skills.summary: A scPathoQuant skill that integrates pathogen UMI counts and per-cell pathogen gene counts back into the 10x cellranger output matrices (filtered_feature_bc_matrix and raw_feature_bc_matrix), so that standard single-cell pipelines such as Seurat can analyze host and pathogen reads together from a single command.

skills.description: Use when 10x Chromium scRNA-seq reads must be counted against competing reference annotations to measure how a modified GFF3 (e.g., extended 3' UTRs) changes per-cell genes and UMI metrics.
skills.name: 10x-chromium-single-cell-read-counting
skills.search_text: 10x-chromium-single-cell-read-counting Use when 10x Chromium scRNA-seq reads must be counted against competing reference annotations to measure how a modified GFF3 (e.g., extended 3' UTRs) changes per-cell genes and UMI metrics. The biological question is UTR identification itself — use peaks2utr on BAM + canonical GFF3 instead of re-running Cell Ranger Reads are not from a 3'-tagged single-cell chemistry (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or full-length protocols) where signal is not concentrated at 3' UTR distal ends http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Re-runs Cell Ranger 6.1.1 count on identical 10x Chromium T. brucei scRNA-seq reads against two GFF3-based references (canonical vs peaks2utr-augmented 3' UTR annotation) to quantify per-cell gains in genes captured and UMIs attributable to extended 3' UTR annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Re-runs Cell Ranger 6.1.1 count on identical 10x Chromium T. brucei scRNA-seq reads against two GFF3-based references (canonical vs peaks2utr-augmented 3' UTR annotation) to quantify per-cell gains in genes captured and UMIs attributable to extended 3' UTR annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological question is UTR identification itself — use peaks2utr on BAM + canonical GFF3 instead of re-running Cell Ranger Reads are not from a 3'-tagged single-cell chemistry (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or full-length protocols) where signal is not concentrated at 3' UTR distal ends

skills.description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices (raw gene-barcode matrices) from multiplexed samples must be read into R and called cells extracted before barcode-swapping or sample-sharing analyses.
skills.name: 10x-count-matrix-handling-with-dropletutils
skills.search_text: 10x-count-matrix-handling-with-dropletutils Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices (raw gene-barcode matrices) from multiplexed samples must be read into R and called cells extracted before barcode-swapping or sample-sharing analyses. Data are plate-based scRNA-seq (e.g. Smart-seq2 plates or the Nestorowa/Richard plate datasets), where barcode swapping is quantified by linear regression on swapped reads rather than droplet barcode sharing The count matrix is already filtered to a final cell set, so emptyDrops cell calling and empty-droplet modelling are not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Load and pre-process 10x Genomics droplet count matrices with the DropletUtils R package in the context of the barcode-swapping study (Griffiths et al. 2018), including emptyDrops cell calling (FDR 0.01, minimum 1000 UMIs) so that per-sample cell-barcode sets can be compared for excess sharing on HiSeq 4000 vs HiSeq 2500 data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Load and pre-process 10x Genomics droplet count matrices with the DropletUtils R package in the context of the barcode-swapping study (Griffiths et al. 2018), including emptyDrops cell calling (FDR 0.01, minimum 1000 UMIs) so that per-sample cell-barcode sets can be compared for excess sharing on HiSeq 4000 vs HiSeq 2500 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are plate-based scRNA-seq (e.g. Smart-seq2 plates or the Nestorowa/Richard plate datasets), where barcode swapping is quantified by linear regression on swapped reads rather than droplet barcode sharing The count matrix is already filtered to a final cell set, so emptyDrops cell calling and empty-droplet modelling are not applicable

skills.description: Use when processing raw 10x Genomics v3 scRNA-seq FASTQ reads (e.g. Arabidopsis root sample GSM4626009 from GSE152766) with scKB/kallisto/bustools and a barcode whitelist is needed for barcode correction and counting.
skills.name: 10x-genomics-barcode-whitelist-processing
skills.search_text: 10x-genomics-barcode-whitelist-processing Use when processing raw 10x Genomics v3 scRNA-seq FASTQ reads (e.g. Arabidopsis root sample GSM4626009 from GSE152766) with scKB/kallisto/bustools and a barcode whitelist is needed for barcode correction and counting. Input is not 10x Genomics v3 chemistry data — the whitelist and -s 10xv3 setting are specific to 10x v3 barcodes A reference-based aligner is required instead of pseudoalignment, since scKB relies on kallisto pseudoalignment rather than full read alignment Data are already processed into count matrices — COPILOT, not scKB, should be applied to existing spliced/unspliced matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Correct and count 10x Genomics v3 cell barcodes during scRNA-seq preprocessing by supplying the 10xv3 barcode whitelist to the bustools step inside the scKB wrapper, enabling spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell count matrix generation from FASTQ reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101729
skills.summary: Correct and count 10x Genomics v3 cell barcodes during scRNA-seq preprocessing by supplying the 10xv3 barcode whitelist to the bustools step inside the scKB wrapper, enabling spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell count matrix generation from FASTQ reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not 10x Genomics v3 chemistry data — the whitelist and -s 10xv3 setting are specific to 10x v3 barcodes A reference-based aligner is required instead of pseudoalignment, since scKB relies on kallisto pseudoalignment rather than full read alignment Data are already processed into count matrices — COPILOT, not scKB, should be applied to existing spliced/unspliced matrices

skills.description: Use when input data comes from a 10x Genomics run consisting of one barcoded BAM plus a barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/, and per-cell BAM files are needed before downstream per-cell analysis.
skills.name: 10x-genomics-output-format-handling
skills.search_text: 10x-genomics-output-format-handling Use when input data comes from a 10x Genomics run consisting of one barcoded BAM plus a barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/, and per-cell BAM files are needed before downstream per-cell analysis. The BAM files are already split by cells (skip 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh as documented). Input is a non-10x scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. E-MTAB-2600-style SMARTer data) that already arrives as one BAM per cell. Handles the standard 10x Genomics output bundle — the single barcoded BAM file and the barcodes.tsv.gz list under outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ — by splitting it into one BAM per cell barcode using SkewC's split step, a prerequisite for per-cell gene body coverage analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.102038
skills.summary: Handles the standard 10x Genomics output bundle — the single barcoded BAM file and the barcodes.tsv.gz list under outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ — by splitting it into one BAM per cell barcode using SkewC's split step, a prerequisite for per-cell gene body coverage analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM files are already split by cells (skip 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh as documented). Input is a non-10x scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. E-MTAB-2600-style SMARTer data) that already arrives as one BAM per cell.

skills.description: Use when raw 10x Genomics Chromium (e.g., 10xv3) scRNA-seq FASTQs must be converted into gene-by-cell spliced/unspliced count matrices quickly, especially for Arabidopsis with a TAIR10-based index.
skills.name: 10x-genomics-read-structure-processing
skills.search_text: 10x-genomics-read-structure-processing Use when raw 10x Genomics Chromium (e.g., 10xv3) scRNA-seq FASTQs must be converted into gene-by-cell spliced/unspliced count matrices quickly, especially for Arabidopsis with a TAIR10-based index. Input reads are not from 10x Genomics Chromium chemistry — the scKB-compatible layout requires barcode/UMI reads separated from cDNA reads in the 10xv3 arrangement A full splice-aware alignment or isoform-level quantification is required — scKB uses kallisto pseudoalignment to produce transcript count matrices, not base-level alignments The goal is quality filtering rather than raw matrix generation — use COPILOT on the scKB-produced raw spliced/unspliced matrices instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Process raw 10x Genomics Chromium scRNA-seq reads (barcode/UMI reads separated from cDNA reads) through the scKB wrapper of kallisto and bustools to rapidly generate gene-by-cell spliced and unspliced UMI count matrices, as demonstrated on the 386-million-read Arabidopsis thaliana col0 dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101729
skills.summary: Process raw 10x Genomics Chromium scRNA-seq reads (barcode/UMI reads separated from cDNA reads) through the scKB wrapper of kallisto and bustools to rapidly generate gene-by-cell spliced and unspliced UMI count matrices, as demonstrated on the 386-million-read Arabidopsis thaliana col0 dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not from 10x Genomics Chromium chemistry — the scKB-compatible layout requires barcode/UMI reads separated from cDNA reads in the 10xv3 arrangement A full splice-aware alignment or isoform-level quantification is required — scKB uses kallisto pseudoalignment to produce transcript count matrices, not base-level alignments The goal is quality filtering rather than raw matrix generation — use COPILOT on the scKB-produced raw spliced/unspliced matrices instead

skills.description: Use when the goal is to predict 21-nt phasiRNAs and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data mapped to cDNA (transcriptome) and/or gDNA (genome) references, e.g. rice SRR5049781 data against oryza_sativa_cdna.fa and oryza_sativa_gdna.fa.
skills.name: 21-nt-phasirna-prediction-configuration
skills.search_text: 21-nt-phasirna-prediction-configuration Use when the goal is to predict 21-nt phasiRNAs and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data mapped to cDNA (transcriptome) and/or gDNA (genome) references, e.g. rice SRR5049781 data against oryza_sativa_cdna.fa and oryza_sativa_gdna.fa. When the aim is 24-nt phasiRNA (reproductive phasiRNA) prediction instead — set -pl 24, this configuration targets 21-nt loci When only one reference is desired, the phase module is designed to integrate multiple reference sequences; using a single -c/-cm or -g/-gm pair discards the multi-reference integration capability When raw sRNA reads have not been preprocessed — the phase module expects .map files and the filtered sRNA fasta, not FASTQ input http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Configure and run PhasiHunter's phase module for 21-nt phasiRNA (phased siRNA) prediction against transcriptome and genome references using both phase score and hypergeometric methods, with the preprocessed sRNA mapping files as input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Configure and run PhasiHunter's phase module for 21-nt phasiRNA (phased siRNA) prediction against transcriptome and genome references using both phase score and hypergeometric methods, with the preprocessed sRNA mapping files as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the aim is 24-nt phasiRNA (reproductive phasiRNA) prediction instead — set -pl 24, this configuration targets 21-nt loci When only one reference is desired, the phase module is designed to integrate multiple reference sequences; using a single -c/-cm or -g/-gm pair discards the multi-reference integration capability When raw sRNA reads have not been preprocessed — the phase module expects .map files and the filtered sRNA fasta, not FASTQ input

skills.description: Use when analyzing a murine embryonic two-cell stage single-cell RNA-Seq dataset where a 2C-like subpopulation must be defined and its differentially expressed transposable elements identified at locus level.
skills.name: 2c-like-cell-identification-zscan4c-tcstv3
skills.search_text: 2c-like-cell-identification-zscan4c-tcstv3 Use when analyzing a murine embryonic two-cell stage single-cell RNA-Seq dataset where a 2C-like subpopulation must be defined and its differentially expressed transposable elements identified at locus level. Input is bulk RNA-Seq or a pre-computed TE expression matrix — SoloTE requires single-cell BAM files with multi-mapped reads retained Analysis targets family-level TE expression only (e.g. scTE metagenes) and does not need locus-specific genomic location The cell type of interest is not a transcriptionally active-TE population (e.g. datasets without known 2C-marker TE activity); STAR multi-mapping alignment overhead may not be justified http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Identifies 2C-like cells in the murine embryonic two-cell stage scRNA-Seq data by Zscan4c/Tcstv3 expression, then recovers differentially expressed marker transposable elements at locus level with SoloTE (106 marker TEs vs 28 with scTE under adjusted P ≤0.05, log2FC ≥1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Identifies 2C-like cells in the murine embryonic two-cell stage scRNA-Seq data by Zscan4c/Tcstv3 expression, then recovers differentially expressed marker transposable elements at locus level with SoloTE (106 marker TEs vs 28 with scTE under adjusted P ≤0.05, log2FC ≥1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-Seq or a pre-computed TE expression matrix — SoloTE requires single-cell BAM files with multi-mapped reads retained Analysis targets family-level TE expression only (e.g. scTE metagenes) and does not need locus-specific genomic location The cell type of interest is not a transcriptionally active-TE population (e.g. datasets without known 2C-marker TE activity); STAR multi-mapping alignment overhead may not be justified

skills.description: Use when analyzing 10x mouse chemical reprogramming scRNA-seq to find a 2CLC population and its defining TE markers using locus-specific TE quantification with MATES.
skills.name: 2clc-population-marker-identification
skills.search_text: 2clc-population-marker-identification Use when analyzing 10x mouse chemical reprogramming scRNA-seq to find a 2CLC population and its defining TE markers using locus-specific TE quantification with MATES. The goal is quantification of long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS that span several thousand bases, exceeding MATES' 2001 bp coverage-vector design TE copies are near-identical with no uniquely mappable flanking regions (e.g., HERVK isoforms), where locus-specific multi-mapping assignment cannot be resolved Input is bulk RNA-seq or an existing gene-expression feature matrix and the question does not require locus-specific TE quantification at single-cell level http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies the 2-cell-like cell (2CLC) subpopulation in mouse chemical reprogramming 10x scRNA-seq by clustering on MATES locus-specific transposable element counts and detecting the signature TE markers MT2_Mm and MERVL-int, which are enriched flanking the Zscan4c/Zscan4d loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Identifies the 2-cell-like cell (2CLC) subpopulation in mouse chemical reprogramming 10x scRNA-seq by clustering on MATES locus-specific transposable element counts and detecting the signature TE markers MT2_Mm and MERVL-int, which are enriched flanking the Zscan4c/Zscan4d loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantification of long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS that span several thousand bases, exceeding MATES' 2001 bp coverage-vector design TE copies are near-identical with no uniquely mappable flanking regions (e.g., HERVK isoforms), where locus-specific multi-mapping assignment cannot be resolved Input is bulk RNA-seq or an existing gene-expression feature matrix and the question does not require locus-specific TE quantification at single-cell level

skills.description: Decision support for judging whether a GraphDDP 2D embedding depends critically on the class-confidence bias - required before trusting layouts built from prior cluster labels.
skills.name: 2d-embedding-stability-assessment
skills.search_text: 2d-embedding-stability-assessment Decision support for judging whether a GraphDDP 2D embedding depends critically on the class-confidence bias - required before trusting layouts built from prior cluster labels. No prior class labels exist for the instances - the confidence bias contracts only same-label edges, so an unlabeled dataset has nothing to sweep Only a single embedding at one parameter setting is needed - a full sweep is unnecessary; just run graph_embed once at the default -c 1.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sweeps the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed class-confidence parameter (-c) across its recommended regimes and verifies that the Kamada-Kawai 2D layout is robust, with same-class instances contracting as C increases (d/(1+C)). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Sweeps the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed class-confidence parameter (-c) across its recommended regimes and verifies that the Kamada-Kawai 2D layout is robust, with same-class instances contracting as C increases (d/(1+C)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior class labels exist for the instances - the confidence bias contracts only same-label edges, so an unlabeled dataset has nothing to sweep Only a single embedding at one parameter setting is needed - a full sweep is unnecessary; just run graph_embed once at the default -c 1.0

skills.description: Use when you have ST data with spot-level gene expression and true 2D coordinates and need to predict 2D locations of scRNA-seq cells or held-out test spots by supervised regression.
skills.name: 2d-location-regression-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: 2d-location-regression-neural-network-training Use when you have ST data with spot-level gene expression and true 2D coordinates and need to predict 2D locations of scRNA-seq cells or held-out test spots by supervised regression. The goal is spatial domain / tissue layer prediction rather than continuous 2D coordinates — that requires the categorical-output spatial domain recovery model instead The target ST platform is a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel; the article notes CeLEry is suboptimal in this setting No spatially variable genes or true spatial locations are available in the training ST data http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train CeLEry's supervised deep neural network to regress 2D spatial coordinates of spots/cells from spatially variable gene expression, using spatial transcriptomics data as training input and optionally VAE-augmented ST replicates to improve robustness. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Train CeLEry's supervised deep neural network to regress 2D spatial coordinates of spots/cells from spatially variable gene expression, using spatial transcriptomics data as training input and optionally VAE-augmented ST replicates to improve robustness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spatial domain / tissue layer prediction rather than continuous 2D coordinates — that requires the categorical-output spatial domain recovery model instead The target ST platform is a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel; the article notes CeLEry is suboptimal in this setting No spatially variable genes or true spatial locations are available in the training ST data

skills.description: Use when validating or reproducing the Forest Fire Clustering benchmarks on ring-shaped, half-moon-shaped, or circular Gaussian-mixture synthetic datasets, where GMM is expected to fail and FFC should achieve top purity.
skills.name: 2d-shape-clustering-reproducibility
skills.search_text: 2d-shape-clustering-reproducibility Use when validating or reproducing the Forest Fire Clustering benchmarks on ring-shaped, half-moon-shaped, or circular Gaussian-mixture synthetic datasets, where GMM is expected to fail and FFC should achieve top purity. Data are real single-cell gene expression matrices requiring preprocessing (zheng17 recipe, 30 principal components) rather than controlled 2D shape benchmarks The goal is quantitative internal validation of FFC results (validate(), entropy(), pval()) rather than cross-method benchmarking on shapes with known ground truth Datasets have intrinsically Gaussian/convex cluster shapes, where distribution-based methods like GMM are expected to work and the ring/moon failure-mode comparison is uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 A reproducibility workflow for benchmarking Forest Fire Clustering against KMeans, GaussianMixture, DBSCAN, OPTICS, and SpectralClustering on non-convex 2D synthetic data (Gaussian mixtures on a unit circle, ring-shaped and half-moon shapes from sklearn), scored by purity against generation labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: A reproducibility workflow for benchmarking Forest Fire Clustering against KMeans, GaussianMixture, DBSCAN, OPTICS, and SpectralClustering on non-convex 2D synthetic data (Gaussian mixtures on a unit circle, ring-shaped and half-moon shapes from sklearn), scored by purity against generation labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real single-cell gene expression matrices requiring preprocessing (zheng17 recipe, 30 principal components) rather than controlled 2D shape benchmarks The goal is quantitative internal validation of FFC results (validate(), entropy(), pval()) rather than cross-method benchmarking on shapes with known ground truth Datasets have intrinsically Gaussian/convex cluster shapes, where distribution-based methods like GMM are expected to work and the ring/moon failure-mode comparison is uninformative

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether cell types or clusters mix less in a 3D embedding (UMAP/tSNE) than in its 2D counterpart, e.g. choosing projection dimensionality for scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: 2d-vs-3d-projection-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: 2d-vs-3d-projection-overlap-analysis Use when you need to quantify whether cell types or clusters mix less in a 3D embedding (UMAP/tSNE) than in its 2D counterpart, e.g. choosing projection dimensionality for scRNA-seq data. Embeddings carry no cell-type/cluster labels — overlap is computed two populations at a time, so unlabeled coordinates cannot be scored. You need overlap measured by convex-hull area rather than entropy — that variant is the separate 2d_vs_3d python code processing ConvexHullGenerator.cs output from CellexalVR. Your goal is in-VR interaction (cell selection, heatmaps, RNA velocity visualization) rather than 2D-vs-3D overlap quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies pairwise cell-type/cluster overlap in 2D versus 3D dimension-reduction embeddings (UMAP, tSNE) using Shannon entropy as a measure of mixing, to test whether 3D projections separate cell populations better than 2D. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Quantifies pairwise cell-type/cluster overlap in 2D versus 3D dimension-reduction embeddings (UMAP, tSNE) using Shannon entropy as a measure of mixing, to test whether 3D projections separate cell populations better than 2D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Embeddings carry no cell-type/cluster labels — overlap is computed two populations at a time, so unlabeled coordinates cannot be scored. You need overlap measured by convex-hull area rather than entropy — that variant is the separate 2d_vs_3d python code processing ConvexHullGenerator.cs output from CellexalVR. Your goal is in-VR interaction (cell selection, heatmaps, RNA velocity visualization) rather than 2D-vs-3D overlap quantification.

skills.description: Use when consecutive ST slices have already been 3D-aligned (e.g., by Scube) and the goal is to model, test, and render per-gene expression as continuous surfaces over the stacked 3D spot/cell coordinates (e.g., STARmap mouse brain).
skills.name: 3d-expression-surface-visualization
skills.search_text: 3d-expression-surface-visualization Use when consecutive ST slices have already been 3D-aligned (e.g., by Scube) and the goal is to model, test, and render per-gene expression as continuous surfaces over the stacked 3D spot/cell coordinates (e.g., STARmap mouse brain). Input data has not been 3D-aligned — Scube's alignment (Scube.alignment.align) must produce stacked 3D coordinates before GPR modeling The goal is 2D spatially variable gene detection on a single slice rather than expression varying along any direction in 3D tissue space Seq-based ST data without a prior Spoint cell-type deconvolution step when downstream modules (e.g., Splane) require cell type composition http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs continuous 3D gene-expression surfaces from Scube-stacked spatial transcriptomics coordinates using a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model, and scores each gene with a Bayes Factor against a no-spatial-structure null so that SPACEL can flag genes varying in any direction within the 3D tissue architecture. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Reconstructs continuous 3D gene-expression surfaces from Scube-stacked spatial transcriptomics coordinates using a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model, and scores each gene with a Bayes Factor against a no-spatial-structure null so that SPACEL can flag genes varying in any direction within the 3D tissue architecture.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been 3D-aligned — Scube's alignment (Scube.alignment.align) must produce stacked 3D coordinates before GPR modeling The goal is 2D spatially variable gene detection on a single slice rather than expression varying along any direction in 3D tissue space Seq-based ST data without a prior Spoint cell-type deconvolution step when downstream modules (e.g., Splane) require cell type composition

skills.description: Use when comparing whether 3D single-cell dimension-reduction projections (UMAP/tSNE) separate annotated cell types or clusters better than 2D, quantified by pairwise Shannon-entropy mixing or convex-hull area overlap across swept viewing angles.
skills.name: 3d-projection-angle-flattening-analysis
skills.search_text: 3d-projection-angle-flattening-analysis Use when comparing whether 3D single-cell dimension-reduction projections (UMAP/tSNE) separate annotated cell types or clusters better than 2D, quantified by pairwise Shannon-entropy mixing or convex-hull area overlap across swept viewing angles. Input is raw scRNA-seq expression counts rather than computed 2D/3D embedding coordinates with cell-type/cluster labels — dimension reduction must be performed first. The goal is interactive, immersive visualization or analysis of the 3D projection; use CellexalVR itself instead of this batch overlap-quantification analysis. You need per-cell differential-expression, heatmap marker, or pseudotime/slingshot trajectory analysis rather than population-overlap quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Quantifies whether 3D single-cell dimension-reduction projections (UMAP/tSNE) separate annotated cell populations better than 2D by systematically rotating the 3D embedding, flattening each rotation to 2D, and scoring pairwise cell-type/cluster overlap with Shannon-entropy mixing or Quickhull convex-hull area. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Quantifies whether 3D single-cell dimension-reduction projections (UMAP/tSNE) separate annotated cell populations better than 2D by systematically rotating the 3D embedding, flattening each rotation to 2D, and scoring pairwise cell-type/cluster overlap with Shannon-entropy mixing or Quickhull convex-hull area.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq expression counts rather than computed 2D/3D embedding coordinates with cell-type/cluster labels — dimension reduction must be performed first. The goal is interactive, immersive visualization or analysis of the 3D projection; use CellexalVR itself instead of this batch overlap-quantification analysis. You need per-cell differential-expression, heatmap marker, or pseudotime/slingshot trajectory analysis rather than population-overlap quantification.

skills.description: Use when you have multiple consecutive ST slices (e.g., 33 MERFISH mouse primary motor cortex slices, Stereo-seq mouse embryo slices) and need to construct a 3D stack by aligning slice coordinate systems.
skills.name: 3d-slice-alignment-and-stacking
skills.search_text: 3d-slice-alignment-and-stacking Use when you have multiple consecutive ST slices (e.g., 33 MERFISH mouse primary motor cortex slices, Stereo-seq mouse embryo slices) and need to construct a 3D stack by aligning slice coordinate systems. You need nonlinear alignment of ST slices: the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment, and no automatic method yet exists for ST data You only have a single ST slice — 3D stacking requires multiple consecutive slices Seq-based ST data (e.g., 10X Visium) without a prior cell type deconvolution step, since Splane requires cell type composition as input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align consecutive spatial transcriptomics slices into a stacked 3D tissue architecture using Scube from SPACEL, which transforms the spatial coordinate systems of adjacent slices based on spatial domains identified by Splane, and benchmark the result against PASTE and STAligner using adjacent-slice SSIM and PCC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Align consecutive spatial transcriptomics slices into a stacked 3D tissue architecture using Scube from SPACEL, which transforms the spatial coordinate systems of adjacent slices based on spatial domains identified by Splane, and benchmark the result against PASTE and STAligner using adjacent-slice SSIM and PCC.

skills.description: Use when consecutive 2D ST slices contain defects (rotation, flip, translation, cropping) and you need to reconstruct or evaluate a stacked 3D tissue architecture against a ground-truth reference.

skills.description: Use when analyzing polyA-captured scRNA-seq data (Sierra or scAPAtrap PACdataset) to detect and visualize 3'UTR shortening/lengthening dynamics across cell states or differentiation trajectories.
skills.name: 3utr-apa-dynamics-analysis
skills.search_text: 3utr-apa-dynamics-analysis Use when analyzing polyA-captured scRNA-seq data (Sierra or scAPAtrap PACdataset) to detect and visualize 3'UTR shortening/lengthening dynamics across cell states or differentiation trajectories. The input is bulk APA data or already-summarized usage tables rather than per-cell poly(A) site counts from polyA-captured scRNA-seq — RUD per-cell gradients require single-cell PACdataset input. The pA sites of interest are not in 3'UTRs — only genes with 3'UTR APA can be used for RUD calculation, so intronic/intergenic events need other analyses. Cell embeddings (UMAP_1/UMAP_2) cannot be computed or cell-type annotations are absent, since vizUMAP overlay and trajectory ordering both depend on per-cell metadata. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify 3'UTR shortening/lengthening dynamics (APA) at single-cell resolution by computing per-gene, per-cell RUD (Relative Usage of Distal poly(A) site) indices on 3'UTR poly(A) sites with vizAPA/movAPA, then visualizing global APA dynamics as RUD-score gradients overlaid on 2D UMAP embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae099
skills.summary: Quantify 3'UTR shortening/lengthening dynamics (APA) at single-cell resolution by computing per-gene, per-cell RUD (Relative Usage of Distal poly(A) site) indices on 3'UTR poly(A) sites with vizAPA/movAPA, then visualizing global APA dynamics as RUD-score gradients overlaid on 2D UMAP embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk APA data or already-summarized usage tables rather than per-cell poly(A) site counts from polyA-captured scRNA-seq — RUD per-cell gradients require single-cell PACdataset input. skills.search_text: abc-score-scaling-of-enhancer-activity Use when scoring enhancer–gene interactions from candidate regions and a chromatin contact map, and you want enhancer activity adapted by enhancer–gene contact counts (adapted ABC), rather than plain activity-by-contact. skills.search_text: ablation-study-model-training Use when a published model is built from multiple interacting components (e.g., ZINB autoencoder + graph convolution + contrastive learning) and you need to isolate each part's contribution to clustering/imputation performance by training and comparing ablation variants. The goal is the full model's benchmark comparison against other imputation methods, not internal component attribution — run the unmodified model instead. skills.when_to_use_negative: Trajectories with cyclic topology (e.g. B cell receptor editing) — absorbing Markov chains cannot represent cyclic trajectories Datasets whose topology is not bifurcation or linear — the destiny-based diffusion map limits trajectory inference to such topologies B cell development data — dandelionR has not yet been applied to B cell development, which involves more complex processes than T cell development

The classifier emits only a single hard label per cell (no ranked scores over Cell Ontology terms), so top-k correctness cannot be computed The task is distinguishing topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings sharing the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — a known OnClass limitation that distorts top-k comparisons The annotation target is free text rather than the controlled Cell Ontology vocabulary (controlled-vocabulary labels assumed; nlp_mapping disabled) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computation of Accuracy@3 and Accuracy@5 to benchmark cell type annotation methods: a prediction counts as correct when the true Cell Ontology label appears among the top-3 or top-5 ranked predicted terms. Used alongside AUROC over unseen terms to compare OnClass against ACTINN, SVM, LR, and reject-option baselines on Muris droplet splits. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Computation of Accuracy@3 and Accuracy@5 to benchmark cell type annotation methods: a prediction counts as correct when the true Cell Ontology label appears among the top-3 or top-5 ranked predicted terms. Used alongside AUROC over unseen terms to compare OnClass against ACTINN, SVM, LR, and reject-option baselines on Muris droplet splits.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods (scKINETICS vs scVelo/VeloVAE/UniTVelo) against a pseudotime-derived transdifferentiation axis in high dimensions, e.g. acute pancreatitis scRNA-seq.
skills.name: acinar-ductal-transdifferentiation-reference-direction-construction
skills.search_text: acinar-ductal-transdifferentiation-reference-direction-construction Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods (scKINETICS vs scVelo/VeloVAE/UniTVelo) against a pseudotime-derived transdifferentiation axis in high dimensions, e.g. acute pancreatitis scRNA-seq. The trajectory of interest is not an acinar-to-ductal or other well-defined pseudotime-resolvable transdifferentiation axis — the reference direction is meaningless without a ductal endpoint anchor. Pseudotime inference cannot be anchored on the differentiation axis (e.g. no clear terminal state), since Palantir anchoring determines the reference directions. Velocity vectors and the pseudotime manifold are computed on different gene sets — angles would not be comparable across methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a per-cell reference direction along the acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) axis from pseudotime-inferred trajectory geometry, enabling angle-based evaluation of RNA velocity vectors against a biologically defined transdifferentiation manifold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Constructs a per-cell reference direction along the acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) axis from pseudotime-inferred trajectory geometry, enabling angle-based evaluation of RNA velocity vectors against a biologically defined transdifferentiation manifold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory of interest is not an acinar-to-ductal or other well-defined pseudotime-resolvable transdifferentiation axis — the reference direction is meaningless without a ductal endpoint anchor. Pseudotime inference cannot be anchored on the differentiation axis (e.g. no clear terminal state), since Palantir anchoring determines the reference directions. Velocity vectors and the pseudotime manifold are computed on different gene sets — angles would not be comparable across methods.

skills.description: Use when a per-plate swapping-fraction estimate has been derived (gradient of swapped reads vs. reads available for swapping) and a single pooled fraction with an uncertainty must be reported for the experiment.
skills.name: across-plate-uncertainty-aggregation
skills.search_text: across-plate-uncertainty-aggregation Use when a per-plate swapping-fraction estimate has been derived (gradient of swapped reads vs. reads available for swapping) and a single pooled fraction with an uncertainty must be reported for the experiment. There is only a single plate or a single library, so no across-plate replicate exists to define a standard deviation The underlying data come from droplet/10x Genomics experiments where swapped molecules are excluded algorithmically rather than estimated by a regression gradient Libraries were sequenced on non-patterned-flow-cell instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where swapping is negligible and the estimate should be near zero http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Aggregates per-plate estimates of the barcode-swapped read fraction by computing the mean and standard deviation of the regression-gradient swapping fractions across plates, yielding a central estimate with an empirical uncertainty (e.g. 2.18 ± 0.08% for Richard et al. libraries sequenced on the HiSeq 4000). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Aggregates per-plate estimates of the barcode-swapped read fraction by computing the mean and standard deviation of the regression-gradient swapping fractions across plates, yielding a central estimate with an empirical uncertainty (e.g. 2.18 ± 0.08% for Richard et al. libraries sequenced on the HiSeq 4000).
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is only a single plate or a single library, so no across-plate replicate exists to define a standard deviation The underlying data come from droplet/10x Genomics experiments where swapped molecules are excluded algorithmically rather than estimated by a regression gradient Libraries were sequenced on non-patterned-flow-cell instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where swapping is negligible and the estimate should be near zero

skills.description: Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM matrices (e.g. TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD, protein-coding and lncRNA genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes prior to building gene co-expression networks.
skills.name: active-gene-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: active-gene-threshold-filtering Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM matrices (e.g. TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD, protein-coding and lncRNA genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes prior to building gene co-expression networks. Data are miRNA expression profiles — the paper reports a much higher pass rate for miRNAs (81% vs ~20% of RNA genes), so the −3.0 zFPKM cutoff is not calibrated for them Input is raw unnormalized counts with no FPKM normalization — zFPKM requires fragments-per-kilobase-million values whose log can be z-scored The goal is differential expression analysis (handled separately in this pipeline with DESeq2), not selection of a common actively expressed background gene set http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects actively expressed RNA-Seq genes by computing zFPKM (z-score of log FPKM, Hart et al. approach) for each gene/sample pair and retaining only genes whose mean zFPKM exceeds −3.0 in both the normal and cancer conditions, discarding background/noisy genes before co-expression network construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Selects actively expressed RNA-Seq genes by computing zFPKM (z-score of log FPKM, Hart et al. approach) for each gene/sample pair and retaining only genes whose mean zFPKM exceeds −3.0 in both the normal and cancer conditions, discarding background/noisy genes before co-expression network construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are miRNA expression profiles — the paper reports a much higher pass rate for miRNAs (81% vs ~20% of RNA genes), so the −3.0 zFPKM cutoff is not calibrated for them Input is raw unnormalized counts with no FPKM normalization — zFPKM requires fragments-per-kilobase-million values whose log can be z-scored The goal is differential expression analysis (handled separately in this pipeline with DESeq2), not selection of a common actively expressed background gene set

skills.search_text: active-learning-benchmarking-single-cell-annotation Use when a single-cell expression dataset has a marker file (author-provided, data-derived, or PanglaoDB top-20) and you need an informative initial 20-cell training set for an active learning annotation loop, benchmarked against random initialization. No marker file exists for the cell types in the dataset and none can be derived or sourced from PanglaoDB — the marker-ranked arm cannot be constructed The task is adaptive reweighting/subsampling of a full dataset for balance (cluster-based leader selection), not choosing a small initial active learning training set The ground-truth cell type labels are unknown or unverifiable, so classifier F1 and uncertainty-based cell selection cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Initializes active learning for single-cell annotation by selecting the first 20 training cells by ranking average cell-type marker gene expression (rather than uniform random sampling), then running the leader/caret active learning loop to measure F1 gain and cell-type coverage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Initializes active learning for single-cell annotation by selecting the first 20 training cells by ranking average cell-type marker gene expression (rather than uniform random sampling), then running the leader/caret active learning loop to measure F1 gain and cell-type coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No marker file exists for the cell types in the dataset and none can be derived or sourced from PanglaoDB — the marker-ranked arm cannot be constructed The task is adaptive reweighting/subsampling of a full dataset for balance (cluster-based leader selection), not choosing a small initial active learning training set The ground-truth cell type labels are unknown or unverifiable, so classifier F1 and uncertainty-based cell selection cannot be computed

skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol for comparing cell selection strategies—active learning (maximum-entropy and lowest-max-probability search), cluster-based and marker-informed adaptive reweighting, and random selection—when constructing training sets for single-cell type annotation classifiers across RNA-Seq and CyTOF datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is self-supervised training-set expansion (pseudo-labeling confident predictions) rather than comparing uncertainty-based active learning against cluster-based and random selection Input is not single-cell expression data (e.g., bulk RNA mixtures or proportional data), since the selection methods operate on individual cell clusters and per-cell marker expression Only one classifier or one dataset will be evaluated, since the skill's conclusion ('no single cell selection method is consistently best') derives from aggregating ranks across 6 datasets and 6 annotation methods

skills.search_text: active-subnetwork-jaccard-similarity-comparison Use when several active subnetworks are recovered from the same seed genes or gene P-values (e.g., on COVID-19 benchmark data) and you need to quantify node-set overlap between methods via pairwise Jaccard similarity. Only a single subnetwork is available (pairwise Jaccard requires at least two method-recovered networks) The comparison should reflect edge-level or causal-structure agreement rather than node-set overlap — Jaccard here is computed on vertex sets only Subnetworks were derived from different seed gene sets or different input data, so overlap reflects differing inputs rather than method behavior http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quantifies how similar active subnetworks recovered by different structure-learning methods are, by converting each undirected perturbed module to a directed tree and computing pairwise Jaccard indices on node sets. In the SEMtree benchmark it distinguishes methods that recover overlapping structures (pathfindR–BioNet and pathfindR–STr2z at Jaccard ≈ 0.3) from those recovering distinct ones. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377

skills.description: Use when a kNN cell graph has been edge-oriented by pseudotime (e.g., DPT rooted at a given iroot) and the N×N adjacency matrix must be confirmed acyclic before Granger causal inference on cell states.
skills.name: acyclicity-verification-of-directed-graphs
skills.search_text: acyclicity-verification-of-directed-graphs Use when a kNN cell graph has been edge-oriented by pseudotime (e.g., DPT rooted at a given iroot) and the N×N adjacency matrix must be confirmed acyclic before Granger causal inference on cell states. The graph is undirected or edge weights have no orientation information — acyclicity is undefined without directed edges. The edge orientations come from cyclic processes with no meaningful pseudotime ordering (e.g., cell-cycle-only data), where forcing a DAG would misrepresent biology rather than merely require cycle-breaking. Verifies that a directed graph over cells—such as the pseudotime-oriented kNN graph used by GrID-Net—is a true directed acyclic graph (DAG) before it is passed to Granger causal inference, since Granger causality on partial orderings relies on the graph having no cycles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Verifies that a directed graph over cells—such as the pseudotime-oriented kNN graph used by GrID-Net—is a true directed acyclic graph (DAG) before it is passed to Granger causal inference, since Granger causality on partial orderings relies on the graph having no cycles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The graph is undirected or edge weights have no orientation information — acyclicity is undefined without directed edges. The edge orientations come from cyclic processes with no meaningful pseudotime ordering (e.g., cell-cycle-only data), where forcing a DAG would misrepresent biology rather than merely require cycle-breaking.

skills.name: adapted-abc-activity-scaling
skills.search_text: adapted-abc-activity-scaling Use when scoring enhancer–gene interactions from activity assays (DNase-seq, H3K27ac/ATAC-seq) plus contact data and you want higher AUPRC than the regular ABC score, or when validating whether a single activity assay suffices. When the goal is de novo enhancer identification from ATAC/ChIP peaks rather than scoring interactions among already-defined candidate enhancers When you cannot supply gene annotation or contact data and the distance-based default c = max{d, 5000}^-1 is unacceptable for your biological question When working with single-cell regulatory-network outputs from GAZE rather than bulk CRISPRi-validated enhancer–gene assignment Score enhancer–gene interactions with the generalized (adapted) ABC model — gene-specific enhancer activity averaged across all annotated TSSs and adapted to each enhancer's contact count — which improved AUPRC by ~0.107 over the regular ABC score on three K562 CRISPRi validation datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Score enhancer–gene interactions with the generalized (adapted) ABC model — gene-specific enhancer activity averaged across all annotated TSSs and adapted to each enhancer's contact count — which improved AUPRC by ~0.107 over the regular ABC score on three K562 CRISPRi validation datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo enhancer identification from ATAC/ChIP peaks rather than scoring interactions among already-defined candidate enhancers When you cannot supply gene annotation or contact data and the distance-based default c = max{d, 5000}^-1 is unacceptable for your biological question When working with single-cell regulatory-network outputs from GAZE rather than bulk CRISPRi-validated enhancer–gene assignment

skills.search_text: adapted-abc-gabc-score-configuration Use when scoring enhancer-gene interactions with STARE and you want the adapted (generalised gABC) variant instead of the regular ABC score — e.g., comparing gABC vs ABC recall against eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs. You chose to run the ABC-scoring without the adapted score — STARE states the adapted activity cannot then be used for scaling Your goal is TF affinity computation or per-gene TF score summarisation rather than enhancer-gene interaction scoring (use STARE's independent affinity task instead) No chromatin contact (Hi-C) data are available, since the Activity-By-Contact model depends on contact matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Configures STARE's adapted Activity-By-Contact (gABC) scoring, which adapts enhancer activity by the number of contacted candidate genes and considers all annotated TSSs of a gene, to produce enhancer-gene interaction scores that outperform the regular ABC score on GTEx eQTL-supported pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062

skills.description: Use when starting from a normalized, log-transformed single-cell expression matrix and you need unsupervised, seed-gene-driven co-expression signatures (ranked gene lists) to drive feature selection for clustering, as in CASCC.
skills.name: adaptive-attractor-co-expression-scanning
skills.search_text: adaptive-attractor-co-expression-scanning Use when starting from a normalized, log-transformed single-cell expression matrix and you need unsupervised, seed-gene-driven co-expression signatures (ranked gene lists) to drive feature selection for clustering, as in CASCC. The input is raw (not normalized/log-transformed) counts — run CASCC's filterGenes/normalization first; findAttractor.adaptive expects well-normalized data You already have a feature table or fixed gene set and only need clustering — go straight to predictClusterK/run.kmeans.fixCenters instead of re-deriving attractors You want differential expression of finished clusters — use Seurat::FindAllMarkers on the feature-selected UMAP object rather than attractor scanning http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs CASCC's unsupervised adaptive attractor algorithm (via findAttractor.adaptive, backed by the cafr package) on a normalized single-cell expression matrix to converge on gene co-expression signatures, each a ranked gene list whose top-ranked genes serve as representative features for downstream clustering/feature selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae283
skills.summary: Runs CASCC's unsupervised adaptive attractor algorithm (via findAttractor.adaptive, backed by the cafr package) on a normalized single-cell expression matrix to converge on gene co-expression signatures, each a ranked gene list whose top-ranked genes serve as representative features for downstream clustering/feature selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw (not normalized/log-transformed) counts — run CASCC's filterGenes/normalization first; findAttractor.adaptive expects well-normalized data You already have a feature table or fixed gene set and only need clustering — go straight to predictClusterK/run.kmeans.fixCenters instead of re-deriving attractors You want differential expression of finished clusters — use Seurat::FindAllMarkers on the feature-selected UMAP object rather than attractor scanning

skills.description: Use when building affinity/transition matrices for diffusion maps or geometry-preserving losses in a TensorFlow GAN pipeline, and gradients must flow through the kernel without saturating.
skills.name: adaptive-bandwidth-inverse-distance-kernel-construction
skills.search_text: adaptive-bandwidth-inverse-distance-kernel-construction Use when building affinity/transition matrices for diffusion maps or geometry-preserving losses in a TensorFlow GAN pipeline, and gradients must flow through the kernel without saturating. Downstream analysis only needs a distance metric and no gradients through the kernel — a Gaussian kernel is simpler and sufficient Input data is not embedded in a continuous ambient space (e.g. already discrete alignment output), where pairwise inverse-distance affinities are not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the pairwise affinity matrix used by scMMGAN's diffusion geometry loss with a gradient-passing inverse-distance kernel k(xi,xj)=max(0,1−||xi−xj||1/σi), where σi is a k-nearest-neighbor adaptive bandwidth, replacing the Gaussian kernel to avoid gradient saturation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Constructs the pairwise affinity matrix used by scMMGAN's diffusion geometry loss with a gradient-passing inverse-distance kernel k(xi,xj)=max(0,1−||xi−xj||1/σi), where σi is a k-nearest-neighbor adaptive bandwidth, replacing the Gaussian kernel to avoid gradient saturation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Downstream analysis only needs a distance metric and no gradients through the kernel — a Gaussian kernel is simpler and sufficient Input data is not embedded in a continuous ambient space (e.g. already discrete alignment output), where pairwise inverse-distance affinities are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when building cell-to-cell affinity matrices from raw or log-normalized scRNAseq count matrices in full dimensionality, and kernel bandwidths must adapt to local density via k-NN scaling rather than fixed global scales.
skills.name: adaptive-bandwidth-kernel-tuning
skills.search_text: adaptive-bandwidth-kernel-tuning Use when building cell-to-cell affinity matrices from raw or log-normalized scRNAseq count matrices in full dimensionality, and kernel bandwidths must adapt to local density via k-NN scaling rather than fixed global scales. Data has already undergone aggressive feature selection, dimensionality reduction, or marker-gene identification — q-diffusion's purpose is to capture high-order gene interactions in full dimensionality, so those stages should be avoided upstream. Analysis requires batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets — the paper explicitly states this was not considered. Datasets are so large that a 20 min to 3 h kernel-evaluation runtime is prohibitive, since the full all-pairs q-diffused kernel evaluation is acknowledged as runtime-suboptimal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tunes the bandwidths of a q-diffused kernel on scRNAseq count data by estimating the inner bandwidth from gene-wise scatter and wrapping the base kernel in an AdaptiveKernel that rescales bandwidth to k-nearest-neighbor distances (PHATE-style adaptive resolution), enabling full-dimensionality cell-to-cell affinity computation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Tunes the bandwidths of a q-diffused kernel on scRNAseq count data by estimating the inner bandwidth from gene-wise scatter and wrapping the base kernel in an AdaptiveKernel that rescales bandwidth to k-nearest-neighbor distances (PHATE-style adaptive resolution), enabling full-dimensionality cell-to-cell affinity computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has already undergone aggressive feature selection, dimensionality reduction, or marker-gene identification — q-diffusion's purpose is to capture high-order gene interactions in full dimensionality, so those stages should be avoided upstream. Analysis requires batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets — the paper explicitly states this was not considered. Datasets are so large that a 20 min to 3 h kernel-evaluation runtime is prohibitive, since the full all-pairs q-diffused kernel evaluation is acknowledged as runtime-suboptimal.

skills.description: Use when a raw or normalized time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g. DREAM 4 In Silico, ~21 samples, 100 genes) must be binned into a limited number of states to make pairwise mutual-information GRN inference tractable.
skills.name: adaptive-binning-discretization-of-expression-data
skills.search_text: adaptive-binning-discretization-of-expression-data Use when a raw or normalized time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g. DREAM 4 In Silico, ~21 samples, 100 genes) must be binned into a limited number of states to make pairwise mutual-information GRN inference tractable. The goal is a refined GRN or Boolean Network: discretization/MI alone only produces the initial (MI-only) network, which the paper shows has low sensitivity (0.38) compared to the refined model (accuracy 0.89) The input is single-cell RNA-Seq data; the paper notes alternative tools (Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, Arboreto) are typically designed for scRNA-Seq, while Augusta targets bulk time-series count tables with few time points Only one or two time points are available: the edge-orientation step relies on the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points and transcriptional time lag, which needs a multi-point time series http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Discretize a normalized RNA-Seq time-series count table into D bins so that pairwise mutual information (MI) can be computed for initial GRN inference in Augusta, keeping the runtime within the paper's O(mn^2 D^2) bound where m is time points and n is genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Discretize a normalized RNA-Seq time-series count table into D bins so that pairwise mutual information (MI) can be computed for initial GRN inference in Augusta, keeping the runtime within the paper's O(mn^2 D^2) bound where m is time points and n is genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a refined GRN or Boolean Network: discretization/MI alone only produces the initial (MI-only) network, which the paper shows has low sensitivity (0.38) compared to the refined model (accuracy 0.89) The input is single-cell RNA-Seq data; the paper notes alternative tools (Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, Arboreto) are typically designed for scRNA-Seq, while Augusta targets bulk time-series count tables with few time points Only one or two time points are available: the edge-orientation step relies on the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points and transcriptional time lag, which needs a multi-point time series

skills.description: Use when running scAce (or benchmarking against it) on scRNA-seq count data and the number of clusters is unknown: after VAE pre-training and cluster initialization, this criterion decides which Leiden-derived or split-derived clusters to merge and when to stop.
skills.name: adaptive-cluster-merging
skills.search_text: adaptive-cluster-merging Use when running scAce (or benchmarking against it) on scRNA-seq count data and the number of clusters is unknown: after VAE pre-training and cluster initialization, this criterion decides which Leiden-derived or split-derived clusters to merge and when to stop. The number of clusters is already known and fixed — merging will alter a user-supplied cluster count rather than preserve it Cell embeddings have not been produced by scAce's VAE pre-training (e.g. embeddings from PCA or another method), since the criterion alternates merging with scAce's own network updates Input is raw counts without the required preprocessing (filtering, normalize_per_cell, log1p, scale) — the ZINB-based embeddings and distance criterion assume the preprocessed space http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 scAce's adaptive cluster merging criterion (Eqs. 7-10): iteratively merge the cluster pair with the smallest size-weighted inter-cluster centroid distance while it is below an adaptive threshold d_bar/2, alternating with VAE network updates, so that a good cluster number is found without pre-estimating it. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546
skills.summary: scAce's adaptive cluster merging criterion (Eqs. 7-10): iteratively merge the cluster pair with the smallest size-weighted inter-cluster centroid distance while it is below an adaptive threshold d_bar/2, alternating with VAE network updates, so that a good cluster number is found without pre-estimating it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters is already known and fixed — merging will alter a user-supplied cluster count rather than preserve it Cell embeddings have not been produced by scAce's VAE pre-training (e.g. embeddings from PCA or another method), since the criterion alternates merging with scAce's own network updates Input is raw counts without the required preprocessing (filtering, normalize_per_cell, log1p, scale) — the ZINB-based embeddings and distance criterion assume the preprocessed space

skills.description: Use when a sample-by-feature single-cell matrix (e.g., PBMC zheng17-preprocessed data, first 30 principal components) must be converted into a KNN-based affinity graph to feed label-propagation clustering, and a full pairwise L2 distance matrix would be computationally expensive (>1 million points).
skills.name: adaptive-kernel-bandwidth-estimation
skills.search_text: adaptive-kernel-bandwidth-estimation Use when a sample-by-feature single-cell matrix (e.g., PBMC zheng17-preprocessed data, first 30 principal components) must be converted into a KNN-based affinity graph to feed label-propagation clustering, and a full pairwise L2 distance matrix would be computationally expensive (>1 million points). Data is in a very high-dimensional representation (beyond the first 30 principal components): the curse of dimensionality makes distances more uniform, degrading KNN-based affinity estimates. Input is already a computed affinity matrix or graph — regenerating affinities from raw features would discard it; the skill applies only when X is a sample-by-feature matrix. The downstream analysis requires nonlinear-dimensionality-reduced embeddings (UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE) rather than PCA-space affinities, which the article states Forest Fire Clustering should be performed with. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 This skill constructs the affinity matrix A for Forest Fire Clustering by approximating the pairwise L2 distance matrix with KNN-to-KNN distances (via scanpy's sc.pp.neighbors) and converting those distances into affinities with an adaptive kernel, avoiding the prohibitive cost of full distance matrices on large single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: This skill constructs the affinity matrix A for Forest Fire Clustering by approximating the pairwise L2 distance matrix with KNN-to-KNN distances (via scanpy's sc.pp.neighbors) and converting those distances into affinities with an adaptive kernel, avoiding the prohibitive cost of full distance matrices on large single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is in a very high-dimensional representation (beyond the first 30 principal components): the curse of dimensionality makes distances more uniform, degrading KNN-based affinity estimates. Input is already a computed affinity matrix or graph — regenerating affinities from raw features would discard it; the skill applies only when X is a sample-by-feature matrix. The downstream analysis requires nonlinear-dimensionality-reduced embeddings (UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE) rather than PCA-space affinities, which the article states Forest Fire Clustering should be performed with.

skills.description: Use when a binary outcome (e.g., invasive vs non-invasive bladder cancer subtype) must be regressed on thousands of molecular variables (e.g., ~8,024 mRNA Z-score entries) where ordinary logistic regression fails and variable selection with correct p-values is needed.
skills.name: adaptive-lasso-logistic-regression
skills.search_text: adaptive-lasso-logistic-regression Use when a binary outcome (e.g., invasive vs non-invasive bladder cancer subtype) must be regressed on thousands of molecular variables (e.g., ~8,024 mRNA Z-score entries) where ordinary logistic regression fails and variable selection with correct p-values is needed. The outcome is a survival time rather than a binary label — use the Cox ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso regression variants instead The data contain variables at the magnitude of a hundred thousand where penalized regression models fall short — FDR screening is recommended, or the problem may be infeasible The covariate set is small and standard (unpenalized) logistic regression with conventional p-values is applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits adaptive Lasso penalized logistic regression (with optional first-step FDR screening) to high-dimensional genomic covariates for a binary outcome, via the HDMAC platform, and computes correct post-selection p-values with selectiveInference. Used to identify candidate genes associated with abnormal expression in TCGA bladder cancer data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60791-z
skills.summary: Fits adaptive Lasso penalized logistic regression (with optional first-step FDR screening) to high-dimensional genomic covariates for a binary outcome, via the HDMAC platform, and computes correct post-selection p-values with selectiveInference. Used to identify candidate genes associated with abnormal expression in TCGA bladder cancer data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The outcome is a survival time rather than a binary label — use the Cox ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso regression variants instead The data contain variables at the magnitude of a hundred thousand where penalized regression models fall short — FDR screening is recommended, or the problem may be infeasible The covariate set is small and standard (unpenalized) logistic regression with conventional p-values is applicable

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF training set is imbalanced (e.g. 450 vs 50 cells or 400 vs 25 per minority type) and you need a cell-selection baseline to rebalance it against active learning or random selection.
skills.name: adaptive-reweighting-cluster-based-cell-selection
skills.search_text: adaptive-reweighting-cluster-based-cell-selection Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF training set is imbalanced (e.g. 450 vs 50 cells or 400 vs 25 per minority type) and you need a cell-selection baseline to rebalance it against active learning or random selection. When ground-truth cell type labels are available for all cells and simple stratified random selection or supervised active learning with uncertainty sampling is feasible and preferred When cells cannot be meaningfully clustered (e.g. very few cells, or clusters do not correspond to cell types), since equal per-cluster sampling assumes cluster structure approximates cell type composition http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A heuristic cell selection procedure that subsamples a single-cell dataset by clustering all cells (e.g. with Seurat) and drawing equal numbers of cells from each cluster, aiming to capture rare cell types and produce more balanced training sets for annotation benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: A heuristic cell selection procedure that subsamples a single-cell dataset by clustering all cells (e.g. with Seurat) and drawing equal numbers of cells from each cluster, aiming to capture rare cell types and produce more balanced training sets for annotation benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth cell type labels are available for all cells and simple stratified random selection or supervised active learning with uncertainty sampling is feasible and preferred When cells cannot be meaningfully clustered (e.g. very few cells, or clusters do not correspond to cell types), since equal per-cluster sampling assumes cluster structure approximates cell type composition

skills.description: Use when a small labeled training set must be constructed from an imbalanced single-cell expression matrix (e.g., snRNA-Seq PDAC SCP1089) and rare cell types should be captured for annotation.
skills.name: adaptive-reweighting-labeling-strategy
skills.search_text: adaptive-reweighting-labeling-strategy Use when a small labeled training set must be constructed from an imbalanced single-cell expression matrix (e.g., snRNA-Seq PDAC SCP1089) and rare cell types should be captured for annotation. When ground-truth labels already exist and a truly stratified balanced split is possible — the paper simulated manual annotation and relied on existing 'ground truth' labels When no processed Seurat object with log-normalized, scaled variable features is available — the input must be normalized and scaled before selection When marker knowledge is unreliable — the paper showed marker files can be corrupted and circular (e.g., cell-line markers derived by differential expression between the same cell lines) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 LEADER adaptive reweighting is a heuristic cell-selection strategy for single-cell data that builds a more balanced labeled subsample by clustering all cells and sampling equal numbers per cluster, optionally assigning putative cell types to clusters from user-supplied marker genes before sampling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: LEADER adaptive reweighting is a heuristic cell-selection strategy for single-cell data that builds a more balanced labeled subsample by clustering all cells and sampling equal numbers per cluster, optionally assigning putative cell types to clusters from user-supplied marker genes before sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth labels already exist and a truly stratified balanced split is possible — the paper simulated manual annotation and relied on existing 'ground truth' labels When no processed Seurat object with log-normalized, scaled variable features is available — the input must be normalized and scaled before selection When marker knowledge is unreliable — the paper showed marker files can be corrupted and circular (e.g., cell-line markers derived by differential expression between the same cell lines)

skills.description: Use when bimodality testing (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test) has confirmed novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data and a non-manual, data-driven cutoff is needed to separate known from unknown cells.
skills.name: adaptive-uncertainty-threshold-estimation
skills.search_text: adaptive-uncertainty-threshold-estimation Use when bimodality testing (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test) has confirmed novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data and a non-manual, data-driven cutoff is needed to separate known from unknown cells. When neither the bimodality coefficient nor Hartigan's dip test indicates a bimodal E-score distribution — then all target cells are defined as the known group and thresholding is skipped When raw source data are available and explicit source-target feature alignment is intended (scEMAIL is designed for source-free adaptation) When the user has already supplied a validated, externally justified cutoff for novel-cell detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derives a data-based threshold (delta) for partitioning scRNA-seq target cells into 'known' vs 'unknown' groups by computing expert-ensemble E-scores of manifold-mixup synthetic pairs, eliminating user-selected thresholds when novel cell types are present in scEMAIL. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Derives a data-based threshold (delta) for partitioning scRNA-seq target cells into 'known' vs 'unknown' groups by computing expert-ensemble E-scores of manifold-mixup synthetic pairs, eliminating user-selected thresholds when novel cell types are present in scEMAIL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When neither the bimodality coefficient nor Hartigan's dip test indicates a bimodal E-score distribution — then all target cells are defined as the known group and thresholding is skipped When raw source data are available and explicit source-target feature alignment is intended (scEMAIL is designed for source-free adaptation) When the user has already supplied a validated, externally justified cutoff for novel-cell detection

skills.description: Use when a custom PPIN adjacency list is needed for a biological process or user-supplied gene set for ORIGINS2 activity() scoring, and only a gene ID list is available from which to subset the full_human_ppin edge list.
skills.name: adjacency-list-construction
skills.search_text: adjacency-list-construction Use when a custom PPIN adjacency list is needed for a biological process or user-supplied gene set for ORIGINS2 activity() scoring, and only a gene ID list is available from which to subset the full_human_ppin edge list. The biological process already ships as a pre-built edges dataset in ORIGINS2 (e.g., differentiation_edges, acute_inflammatory_response_edges, dna_repair_edges) — use the bundled dataset instead of rebuilding. You already hold a normalized expression matrix and want process activity scores — call activity() directly; build_ppin is only the network-construction step. The analysis requires interactions with proteins outside the gene list — build_ppin keeps only edges whose both endpoints are inside the list. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a biological-process-specific protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) adjacency list by overlaying a gene ID list onto the ORIGINS2 full Human PPIN (full_human_ppin) and retaining only edges whose two endpoint genes are both in the list (build_ppin). The resulting edge data frame is the adjacency_edges input for ORIGINS2 activity() scoring of scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Constructs a biological-process-specific protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) adjacency list by overlaying a gene ID list onto the ORIGINS2 full Human PPIN (full_human_ppin) and retaining only edges whose two endpoint genes are both in the list (build_ppin). The resulting edge data frame is the adjacency_edges input for ORIGINS2 activity() scoring of scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process already ships as a pre-built edges dataset in ORIGINS2 (e.g., differentiation_edges, acute_inflammatory_response_edges, dna_repair_edges) — use the bundled dataset instead of rebuilding. You already hold a normalized expression matrix and want process activity scores — call activity() directly; build_ppin is only the network-construction step. The analysis requires interactions with proteins outside the gene list — build_ppin keeps only edges whose both endpoints are inside the list.

skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-recovery-benchmarking Use when comparing dimension-reduction or clustering methods on scRNAseq data that have published ground-truth cell-type annotations, and you need a single reproducible metric (ARI) to rank cluster recovery across datasets. The dataset lacks ground-truth cell-type annotations or the annotations were not independently validated — ARI then measures agreement with a possibly narrow 'reference' rather than true recovery The method's advantages lie in resolving sub-populations or rare cell types that the reference labels do not distinguish; the article notes ARI 'would actually receive a small penalty for differences from "reference"' in such cases The benchmarking goal is complex-tissue cell-type discovery — the article notes high-quality ground-truth datasets are limited to simple pseudo-cell mixtures or pools of distinct cell types and 'do not reflect real-world tissue complexity' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark dimension-reduction methods (e.g., CA vs PCA) for single-cell RNA-seq by clustering cells in the reduced embeddings and scoring cluster assignments against published ground-truth cell-type labels with Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), as done across the SCMixology and Zhengmix benchmark datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Benchmark dimension-reduction methods (e.g., CA vs PCA) for single-cell RNA-seq by clustering cells in the reduced embeddings and scoring cluster assignments against published ground-truth cell-type labels with Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), as done across the SCMixology and Zhengmix benchmark datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks ground-truth cell-type annotations or the annotations were not independently validated — ARI then measures agreement with a possibly narrow 'reference' rather than true recovery The method's advantages lie in resolving sub-populations or rare cell types that the reference labels do not distinguish; the article notes ARI 'would actually receive a small penalty for differences from "reference"' in such cases The benchmarking goal is complex-tissue cell-type discovery — the article notes high-quality ground-truth datasets are limited to simple pseudo-cell mixtures or pools of distinct cell types and 'do not reflect real-world tissue complexity'
