skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-validation Use when assessing whether repeated runs of an unsupervised clustering method (e.g., RCC with ConsensusClusterPlus/k-means base) yield consistent cluster counts and concordant assignments on bulk or single-cell expression matrices. Input lacks a reference clustering or repeat-run assignments, so no concordance measure (ARI) can be computed The goal is supervised subtype classification against known labels rather than unsupervised stability assessment of RCC runs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates the stability and reproducibility of Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) runs by comparing cluster counts and adjusted Rand index (ARI) values across repeated RCC_clus executions on the paper's seven benchmark transcriptome datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Validates the stability and reproducibility of Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) runs by comparing cluster counts and adjusted Rand index (ARI) values across repeated RCC_clus executions on the paper's seven benchmark transcriptome datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a reference clustering or repeat-run assignments, so no concordance measure (ARI) can be computed The goal is supervised subtype classification against known labels rather than unsupervised stability assessment of RCC runs

skills.description: Use when benchmarking clustering or spatial-domain methods against simulations that retain ground-truth cell labels, and you need a chance-corrected agreement score (ARI) per method per dataset, e.g. to reproduce the scSpace Fig. 1d-e comparison.
skills.name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-computation
skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-computation Use when benchmarking clustering or spatial-domain methods against simulations that retain ground-truth cell labels, and you need a chance-corrected agreement score (ARI) per method per dataset, e.g. to reproduce the scSpace Fig. 1d-e comparison. No ground-truth reference labels exist for the cells (ARI requires a reference labeling; it cannot be computed on purely exploratory clusterings of real tissue data) The goal is to assess spatial reconstruction quality (pseudo-space coordinates or pairwise cellular spatial associations) rather than agreement between two label assignments over the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes adjusted Rand index (ARI) between predicted cluster labels and ground-truth subcluster labels to benchmark clustering accuracy, as used to show scSpace outperforms Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, and DR-SC across 140 simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Computes adjusted Rand index (ARI) between predicted cluster labels and ground-truth subcluster labels to benchmark clustering accuracy, as used to show scSpace outperforms Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, and DR-SC across 140 simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth reference labels exist for the cells (ARI requires a reference labeling; it cannot be computed on purely exploratory clusterings of real tissue data) The goal is to assess spatial reconstruction quality (pseudo-space coordinates or pairwise cellular spatial associations) rather than agreement between two label assignments over the same cells

skills.description: Use when a task requires quantifying how well K-means clusters of imputed (or unimputed) log-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrices agree with known cell-type annotations via Adjusted Rand Index.
skills.name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-evaluation Use when a task requires quantifying how well K-means clusters of imputed (or unimputed) log-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrices agree with known cell-type annotations via Adjusted Rand Index. The goal is expression-value recovery or masked-matrix reconstruction rather than clustering accuracy — use an expression recovery test (e.g., AutoImpute's --masked_matrix_test) instead Cell-type annotations are unavailable, so ARI against original labels cannot be computed The data are not log-transformed count matrices (e.g., raw unnormalized counts or other omics), which would break comparability with the paper's Table 1 protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates whether imputation of log2-transformed scRNA-seq dropout improves K-means cell-clustering accuracy by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between K-means labels and original cell-type annotations, as done in the AutoImpute benchmark (Scientific Reports, 2018). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Evaluates whether imputation of log2-transformed scRNA-seq dropout improves K-means cell-clustering accuracy by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between K-means labels and original cell-type annotations, as done in the AutoImpute benchmark (Scientific Reports, 2018).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is expression-value recovery or masked-matrix reconstruction rather than clustering accuracy — use an expression recovery test (e.g., AutoImpute's --masked_matrix_test) instead Cell-type annotations are unavailable, so ARI against original labels cannot be computed The data are not log-transformed count matrices (e.g., raw unnormalized counts or other omics), which would break comparability with the paper's Table 1 protocol

skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single method's clustering is available with no reference labels — ARI cannot be computed without a ground-truth labeling to compare against When the dataset is small enough that all six methods (including SIMLR) run without memory pressure — the SIMLR exclusion rationale (out-of-memory errors on 5,000–30,000-cell Tabula Sapiens datasets) does not apply When the goal is biological interpretation (e.g. attractor co-expression signatures or DEGs) rather than method benchmarking

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type label predictions from multiple reference-mapping or clustering methods against manually curated ground-truth annotations, and you need per-cell-type accuracy plus ARI summary metrics to build a comparison table.
skills.name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-comparison
skills.search_text: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-comparison Use when comparing cell-type label predictions from multiple reference-mapping or clustering methods against manually curated ground-truth annotations, and you need per-cell-type accuracy plus ARI summary metrics to build a comparison table. Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference atlas — projections and transferred labels may be misleading, so unsupervised clustering should be compared to mapping results instead of relying on accuracy/ARI alone Evaluating a single mapping without competing methods or ground-truth annotations — there is nothing to compute ARI against Cross-platform projection scenarios (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) where the paper reports performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth — metrics may not reflect intrinsic method quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill for quantifying agreement between predicted cell-type labels and reference annotations using accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI), as used to compare ProjectSVR against Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs, iNMF, and SCALEX on the DISCO PBMC, MFI, and mTCA reference-mapping tasks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for quantifying agreement between predicted cell-type labels and reference annotations using accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI), as used to compare ProjectSVR against Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs, iNMF, and SCALEX on the DISCO PBMC, MFI, and mTCA reference-mapping tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference atlas — projections and transferred labels may be misleading, so unsupervised clustering should be compared to mapping results instead of relying on accuracy/ARI alone Evaluating a single mapping without competing methods or ground-truth annotations — there is nothing to compute ARI against Cross-platform projection scenarios (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) where the paper reports performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth — metrics may not reflect intrinsic method quality

skills.when_to_use_negative: There are no trusted reference labels (e.g., manual layer annotations) to compare against — ARI requires a ground-truth partition and cannot validate purely exploratory clusterings The goal is SVG detection itself rather than downstream clustering evaluation — use nnSVG ranking on LR_stat instead of ARI comparison Input is a single gene set with no competing feature-selection strategies to compare

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or independently verifying the row-sparse FPS estimation path of SuffPCR (Algorithm 1 with AIRLB plus Algorithm 2 elbow thresholding), or when implementing an ADMM solver for sparse PCA loading matrices whose sparsity must match the suffpcr package.
skills.name: admm-optimization-implementation
skills.search_text: admm-optimization-implementation Use when reconstructing or independently verifying the row-sparse FPS estimation path of SuffPCR (Algorithm 1 with AIRLB plus Algorithm 2 elbow thresholding), or when implementing an ADMM solver for sparse PCA loading matrices whose sparsity must match the suffpcr package. The goal is unsupervised dimension reduction only — SuffPCR is specifically 'row-sparse PCA followed by ordinary least squares or logistic regression', so without a phenotype y to regress there is no sufficient-PC objective to solve. The target subspace need not be row-sparse in features; existing sparse approaches are noted to sometimes 'fail to select the correct features' or 'predict poorly relative to non-sparse alternatives', so non-sparse PCR alternatives are preferable when sparsity assumptions do not hold. The analysis only needs to run the package as-is (out <- suffPCR(...)) rather than independently reconstruct or validate its ADMM/soft-thresholding internals. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reimplementation of the SuffPCR estimation algorithm: an ADMM solver in which the Fantope projection and selection (FPS) problem is solved via truncated eigendecomposition with elementwise soft-thresholding, made row-sparse by hard-thresholding small row norms, with the threshold chosen by an automatic elbow criterion (Algorithm 2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Reimplementation of the SuffPCR estimation algorithm: an ADMM solver in which the Fantope projection and selection (FPS) problem is solved via truncated eigendecomposition with elementwise soft-thresholding, made row-sparse by hard-thresholding small row norms, with the threshold chosen by an automatic elbow criterion (Algorithm 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised dimension reduction only — SuffPCR is specifically 'row-sparse PCA followed by ordinary least squares or logistic regression', so without a phenotype y to regress there is no sufficient-PC objective to solve. The target subspace need not be row-sparse in features; existing sparse approaches are noted to sometimes 'fail to select the correct features' or 'predict poorly relative to non-sparse alternatives', so non-sparse PCR alternatives are preferable when sparsity assumptions do not hold. The analysis only needs to run the package as-is (out <- suffPCR(...)) rather than independently reconstruct or validate its ADMM/soft-thresholding internals.

skills.search_text: admm-optimization-solver-implementation Use when you must estimate a sparse, signed, weighted regulatory matrix from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) moment data — a sample mean vector and covariance matrix — and need a NumPy-only solver for the covariance-restricted L1-regularized regression objective. The data is a true longitudinal time series with linkage across time points, or the goal is a network maintaining a single cell state — COSLIR targets sparse GRNs driving cell-state transitions from TSCS data without pseudo-time inference. Only single-time-point cross-sectional data is available with no consecutive time-point pair, since the method requires first and second moments of two consecutive time points. Pseudo-time trajectory information is already available and a trajectory-dependent GRN inference method is preferred — COSLIR's design bypasses pseudo-time entirely. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements the ADMM solver that COSLIR uses to solve its non-convex, L1-regularized covariance-restricted sparse linear regression objective (Eq. 3), estimating the sparse regulatory matrix A_t from only the first and second moments of two consecutive time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Implements the ADMM solver that COSLIR uses to solve its non-convex, L1-regularized covariance-restricted sparse linear regression objective (Eq. 3), estimating the sparse regulatory matrix A_t from only the first and second moments of two consecutive time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is a true longitudinal time series with linkage across time points, or the goal is a network maintaining a single cell state — COSLIR targets sparse GRNs driving cell-state transitions from TSCS data without pseudo-time inference. Only single-time-point cross-sectional data is available with no consecutive time-point pair, since the method requires first and second moments of two consecutive time points. Pseudo-time trajectory information is already available and a trajectory-dependent GRN inference method is preferred — COSLIR's design bypasses pseudo-time entirely.

skills.description: Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, TEA-seq, ASAP-seq) show ambient antibody noise that masks biologically meaningful populations — e.g., empty-droplet signal correlating with CLR-normalized protein values.
skills.name: adt-ambient-background-normalization
skills.search_text: adt-ambient-background-normalization Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, TEA-seq, ASAP-seq) show ambient antibody noise that masks biologically meaningful populations — e.g., empty-droplet signal correlating with CLR-normalized protein values. When no empty droplets are available and no model-based background can be estimated — use the dsb 'no empty drops' vignette variant (ModelNegativeADTnorm) instead, not the empty-drop background workflow When the protein panel contains proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count <5 across all cells) — these must be removed prior to normalization (e.g., CD34 was removed from two datasets) When the analysis goal is mRNA-only scRNA-seq normalization — dsb targets ADT/protein data specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Normalize and denoise droplet-based ADT (protein) data from CITE-seq/TEA-seq/ASAP-seq using the dsb method, which removes ambient unbound-antibody background estimated from empty droplets plus cell-to-cell technical noise via isotype controls and a per-cell background mean. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Normalize and denoise droplet-based ADT (protein) data from CITE-seq/TEA-seq/ASAP-seq using the dsb method, which removes ambient unbound-antibody background estimated from empty droplets plus cell-to-cell technical noise via isotype controls and a per-cell background mean.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no empty droplets are available and no model-based background can be estimated — use the dsb 'no empty drops' vignette variant (ModelNegativeADTnorm) instead, not the empty-drop background workflow When the protein panel contains proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count <5 across all cells) — these must be removed prior to normalization (e.g., CD34 was removed from two datasets) When the analysis goal is mRNA-only scRNA-seq normalization — dsb targets ADT/protein data specifically

skills.description: Use when a CITE-seq dataset contains ADT counts alongside gene expression and per-cell antibody positivity must be called rather than inferred only from clustering, e.g. surface-marker phenotyping on 10x/cellranger data.
skills.name: adt-background-threshold-positive-cell-calling
skills.search_text: adt-background-threshold-positive-cell-calling Use when a CITE-seq dataset contains ADT counts alongside gene expression and per-cell antibody positivity must be called rather than inferred only from clustering, e.g. surface-marker phenotyping on 10x/cellranger data. The dataset is single-modality scRNA-seq without ADT counts (no antibody expression to threshold). The ADT data has not been filtered to the cells retained by GEX QC, so the two modalities describe different cell sets. The goal is sample hashing deconvolution rather than per-cell antibody positivity assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Part of gExcite's CITE-seq analysis layer, this step applies per-antibody background thresholds to ADT (antibody-derived tag) counts to classify individual cells as antibody-positive, run jointly with gene-plus-antibody (BremSC) clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: Part of gExcite's CITE-seq analysis layer, this step applies per-antibody background thresholds to ADT (antibody-derived tag) counts to classify individual cells as antibody-positive, run jointly with gene-plus-antibody (BremSC) clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is single-modality scRNA-seq without ADT counts (no antibody expression to threshold). The ADT data has not been filtered to the cells retained by GEX QC, so the two modalities describe different cell sets. The goal is sample hashing deconvolution rather than per-cell antibody positivity assignment.

skills.description: Use when processing CITE-Seq, TEA-Seq, or Multiome protein (ADT) counts that must be scaled and clustered on their own terms before multimodal integration with scTriangulate.
skills.name: adt-clr-normalization
skills.search_text: adt-clr-normalization Use when processing CITE-Seq, TEA-Seq, or Multiome protein (ADT) counts that must be scaled and clustered on their own terms before multimodal integration with scTriangulate. Input is RNA or ATAC-seq counts — these use log-CPTT normalization with hypervariable gene/peak selection, not CLR Data already normalized for protein modality (e.g., prior CLR or scaled ADT matrix) — double normalization will distort downstream clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Center log-ratio (CLR) normalization of antibody-derived tag (ADT) CITE-Seq/TEA-Seq counts so protein modality data can be clustered and concatenated with RNA AnnData in the scTriangulate framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Center log-ratio (CLR) normalization of antibody-derived tag (ADT) CITE-Seq/TEA-Seq counts so protein modality data can be clustered and concatenated with RNA AnnData in the scTriangulate framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is RNA or ATAC-seq counts — these use log-CPTT normalization with hypervariable gene/peak selection, not CLR Data already normalized for protein modality (e.g., prior CLR or scaled ADT matrix) — double normalization will distort downstream clustering

skills.description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with a limited number of ADT features (<50) where the ADT modality disproportionately dominates the joint cell-cell distance and masks transcriptomic differences between subsets.
skills.name: adt-distance-sigmoid-filtering
skills.search_text: adt-distance-sigmoid-filtering Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with a limited number of ADT features (<50) where the ADT modality disproportionately dominates the joint cell-cell distance and masks transcriptomic differences between subsets. Datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g., >50, or 228 ADT features on 170K cells) — LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) and failed on massive datasets where Seurat 4 succeeded Analysis goals that are unimodal (RNA-only or ADT-only), where per-modality distances suffice and joint L∞ fusion is unnecessary Datasets already processed into a joint embedding or clustering, where the per-modality pairwise distance matrices required for filtering are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply LinQ-View's elementwise sigmoid filter F(x)=x/(1+e^{-n(x-k)}) with n=10 and k=0.5 to the ADT cell-cell Euclidean distance matrix before L∞-norm fusion with the RNA distance matrix, preventing a single surface marker from dominating the joint distance in CITE-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Apply LinQ-View's elementwise sigmoid filter F(x)=x/(1+e^{-n(x-k)}) with n=10 and k=0.5 to the ADT cell-cell Euclidean distance matrix before L∞-norm fusion with the RNA distance matrix, preventing a single surface marker from dominating the joint distance in CITE-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g., >50, or 228 ADT features on 170K cells) — LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) and failed on massive datasets where Seurat 4 succeeded Analysis goals that are unimodal (RNA-only or ADT-only), where per-modality distances suffice and joint L∞ fusion is unnecessary Datasets already processed into a joint embedding or clustering, where the per-modality pairwise distance matrices required for filtering are unavailable

skills.description: Use when ADT FASTQs from cell-hashing CITE-seq libraries must be organized per sample and converted into a cells-by-hashtags UMI count matrix before sample demultiplexing.
skills.name: adt-fastq-sample-multiplexing-setup
skills.search_text: adt-fastq-sample-multiplexing-setup Use when ADT FASTQs from cell-hashing CITE-seq libraries must be organized per sample and converted into a cells-by-hashtags UMI count matrix before sample demultiplexing. The dataset is not cell-hashed (no hashtag oligonucleotide multiplexing) — this setup and demultiplexing step does not apply. A per-cell hashtag count matrix already exists and you only need downstream demultiplexing rather than recounting ADT FASTQs. You are only processing GEX FASTQs without ADT data — use the gene-expression module instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares hashed ADT FASTQ inputs (I1/R1/R2) in the gExcite-expected folder and naming schema and runs CITE-seq-Count against the hashtag oligo reference to produce per-cell hashtag UMI count matrices, the entry point for hashing demultiplexing in CITE-seq ADT data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: Prepares hashed ADT FASTQ inputs (I1/R1/R2) in the gExcite-expected folder and naming schema and runs CITE-seq-Count against the hashtag oligo reference to produce per-cell hashtag UMI count matrices, the entry point for hashing demultiplexing in CITE-seq ADT data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not cell-hashed (no hashtag oligonucleotide multiplexing) — this setup and demultiplexing step does not apply. A per-cell hashtag count matrix already exists and you only need downstream demultiplexing rather than recounting ADT FASTQs. You are only processing GEX FASTQs without ADT data — use the gene-expression module instead.

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq or REAP-seq ADT/protein count matrices must be converted to relative-abundance training targets for cTP-net, or whenever per-cell protein log-ratios (vs. geometric mean) are needed instead of raw barcode counts.
skills.name: adt-relative-abundance-log-ratio-transformation
skills.search_text: adt-relative-abundance-log-ratio-transformation Use when CITE-seq or REAP-seq ADT/protein count matrices must be converted to relative-abundance training targets for cTP-net, or whenever per-cell protein log-ratios (vs. geometric mean) are needed instead of raw barcode counts. Input RNA is TPM/RPKM rather than UMI-based counts — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input, so paired imputation is out of scope The goal is normalizing the RNA side — that uses SAVER-X denoising followed by Seurat LogNormalize, not the ADT log-ratio transform Imputing proteins for cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the authors state this was not tested http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transforms raw CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein (ADT) barcode counts per cell into relative abundances via the Stoeckius et al. log-ratio transformation, ln(p_ic / geometric mean), producing the response vectors cTP-net trains against. This transformed target yields better prediction accuracy than raw barcode counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Transforms raw CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein (ADT) barcode counts per cell into relative abundances via the Stoeckius et al. log-ratio transformation, ln(p_ic / geometric mean), producing the response vectors cTP-net trains against. This transformed target yields better prediction accuracy than raw barcode counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA is TPM/RPKM rather than UMI-based counts — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input, so paired imputation is out of scope The goal is normalizing the RNA side — that uses SAVER-X denoising followed by Seurat LogNormalize, not the ADT log-ratio transform Imputing proteins for cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the authors state this was not tested

skills.description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches whose embeddings show batch separation: per-cell batch labels are available and a VAE latent space must be made batch-invariant without erasing biological variation.
skills.name: adversarial-batch-classifier-training
skills.search_text: adversarial-batch-classifier-training Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches whose embeddings show batch separation: per-cell batch labels are available and a VAE latent space must be made batch-invariant without erasing biological variation. Batch identity is unknown and cannot be annotated — the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches; unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored The goal is comparing against MNN-based methods (BBKNN, Scanorama, Seurat v3) rather than adversarial deep-learning integration — different tool family with different memory profiles Extremely large batches plus datasets where kBET could not be computed due to computational limitations handling large numbers of cells and batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Adversarially train a feed-forward batch classifier against the scDREAMER encoder (encoder maximizes cross-entropy, classifier minimizes it) so latent embeddings become indistinguishable across batches, enabling batch-invariant single-cell integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Adversarially train a feed-forward batch classifier against the scDREAMER encoder (encoder maximizes cross-entropy, classifier minimizes it) so latent embeddings become indistinguishable across batches, enabling batch-invariant single-cell integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Batch identity is unknown and cannot be annotated — the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches; unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored The goal is comparing against MNN-based methods (BBKNN, Scanorama, Seurat v3) rather than adversarial deep-learning integration — different tool family with different memory profiles Extremely large batches plus datasets where kBET could not be computed due to computational limitations handling large numbers of cells and batches

skills.description: Use when you need to determine whether each adversarial component of an adversarial-VAE integration method (discriminator, batch classifier) contributes to integration, and what each contributes.
skills.name: adversarial-component-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: adversarial-component-ablation-analysis Use when you need to determine whether each adversarial component of an adversarial-VAE integration method (discriminator, batch classifier) contributes to integration, and what each contributes. The goal is to compare scDREAMER against other integration methods (BBKNN, Scanorama, Seurat v3, Harmony, scVI, DESC, iMAP) rather than to dissect scDREAMER's internal components Only a single trained model is available — ablation requires training discriminator-removed and batch-classifier-removed variants from scratch Cell-type labels are unavailable, since bio-conservation attribution to the discriminator relies on NMI, ARI and cell-type ASW http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Ablation-analysis skill for scDREAMER that trains the full adversarial VAE plus variants with the adversarial discriminator or batch classifier removed, then compares bio-conservation and batch-correction metrics to attribute integration performance to each component. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Ablation-analysis skill for scDREAMER that trains the full adversarial VAE plus variants with the adversarial discriminator or batch classifier removed, then compares bio-conservation and batch-correction metrics to attribute integration performance to each component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare scDREAMER against other integration methods (BBKNN, Scanorama, Seurat v3, Harmony, scVI, DESC, iMAP) rather than to dissect scDREAMER's internal components Only a single trained model is available — ablation requires training discriminator-removed and batch-classifier-removed variants from scratch Cell-type labels are unavailable, since bio-conservation attribution to the discriminator relies on NMI, ARI and cell-type ASW

skills.description: Use when training scButterfly-B (or -T/-C) on paired single-cell multi-omics count matrices to align modality-specific VAE latent spaces via translator–discriminator adversarial optimization before cross-modality prediction.
skills.name: adversarial-discriminator-training
skills.search_text: adversarial-discriminator-training Use when training scButterfly-B (or -T/-C) on paired single-cell multi-omics count matrices to align modality-specific VAE latent spaces via translator–discriminator adversarial optimization before cross-modality prediction. When you only need per-modality reconstruction or embedding without cross-modality translation — plain VAE pretraining suffices and adversarial training adds cost When working with modalities not supported by scButterfly (e.g. spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C), which the paper lists as future directions only When no model has been constructed/preprocessed — train_model requires load_data, data_preprocessing, and construct_model to have run first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Trains the scButterfly dual-aligned VAE by jointly optimizing translator and discriminator adversarial losses after per-modality autoencoder pretraining, so that cross-modality translated profiles align in latent space. This adversarial phase is what drives the dual-aligned latent representations used for scRNA-seq ↔ scATAC-seq (and scADT-seq) translation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Trains the scButterfly dual-aligned VAE by jointly optimizing translator and discriminator adversarial losses after per-modality autoencoder pretraining, so that cross-modality translated profiles align in latent space. This adversarial phase is what drives the dual-aligned latent representations used for scRNA-seq ↔ scATAC-seq (and scADT-seq) translation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need per-modality reconstruction or embedding without cross-modality translation — plain VAE pretraining suffices and adversarial training adds cost When working with modalities not supported by scButterfly (e.g. spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C), which the paper lists as future directions only When no model has been constructed/preprocessed — train_model requires load_data, data_preprocessing, and construct_model to have run first

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (Scanpy AnnData) and you need batch-corrected latent embeddings, especially with skewed cell-type distributions, nested batch effects, many batches, or developmental trajectories that must be conserved.
skills.name: adversarial-variational-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: adversarial-variational-autoencoder-training Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (Scanpy AnnData) and you need batch-corrected latent embeddings, especially with skewed cell-type distributions, nested batch effects, many batches, or developmental trajectories that must be conserved. Input is already batch-corrected or is not a raw/normalized count matrix from multiple batches — no batch effect exists to remove The number of batches is unknown and cannot be supplied, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches You need batch information treated unsupervised or to exploit hierarchical batch structure — the paper lists these as unimplemented future directions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains scDREAMER's adversarial variational autoencoder (encoder E, decoder D, discriminator D, batch classifier B) to produce batch-invariant latent embeddings of scRNA-seq data. The VAE maximizes the ELBO (KL terms scaled by beta plus ZINB reconstruction), while the batch classifier is trained adversarially with cross-entropy so the encoder generates embeddings that cannot be differentiated across batches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Trains scDREAMER's adversarial variational autoencoder (encoder E, decoder D, discriminator D, batch classifier B) to produce batch-invariant latent embeddings of scRNA-seq data. The VAE maximizes the ELBO (KL terms scaled by beta plus ZINB reconstruction), while the batch classifier is trained adversarially with cross-entropy so the encoder generates embeddings that cannot be differentiated across batches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already batch-corrected or is not a raw/normalized count matrix from multiple batches — no batch effect exists to remove The number of batches is unknown and cannot be supplied, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches You need batch information treated unsupervised or to exploit hierarchical batch structure — the paper lists these as unimplemented future directions

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple organismal ages and need to identify, per cell type, genes whose expression changes with age to build cell-type-specific senescence signatures.
skills.name: age-dynamic-gene-scoring
skills.search_text: age-dynamic-gene-scoring Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple organismal ages and need to identify, per cell type, genes whose expression changes with age to build cell-type-specific senescence signatures. Your single-cell data contain only one age point or lack replicate age structure, since GAD scoring and the age-label permutation null cannot be computed You only need to score cells for senescence with existing signatures — use senePy's score_hub/load_hubs instead of re-deriving age-dynamic genes Your goal is a universal senescence signature from merged existing hubs (merge_hubs with calculate_thresh=True) rather than de novo per-cell-type gene discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Scores candidate senescence-associated genes for age-dynamic (GAD) behavior within each cell type of a single-cell atlas (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, ages 1–30 months), testing significance against null permutations of age labels so that genes tracking senescence across ages can seed co-positivity hub construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Scores candidate senescence-associated genes for age-dynamic (GAD) behavior within each cell type of a single-cell atlas (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, ages 1–30 months), testing significance against null permutations of age labels so that genes tracking senescence across ages can seed co-positivity hub construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your single-cell data contain only one age point or lack replicate age structure, since GAD scoring and the age-label permutation null cannot be computed You only need to score cells for senescence with existing signatures — use senePy's score_hub/load_hubs instead of re-deriving age-dynamic genes Your goal is a universal senescence signature from merged existing hubs (merge_hubs with calculate_thresh=True) rather than de novo per-cell-type gene discovery

skills.description: Use when single-cell AnnData objects annotated with cell type and age are available and the goal is to compute, per cell type, the fraction of senescence-score-positive cells in young vs old age groups and rank which markers (e.g., CDKN2A, CCL4) are most age-dynamic.
skills.name: age-group-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: age-group-differential-abundance-analysis Use when single-cell AnnData objects annotated with cell type and age are available and the goal is to compute, per cell type, the fraction of senescence-score-positive cells in young vs old age groups and rank which markers (e.g., CDKN2A, CCL4) are most age-dynamic. Input data are bulk transcriptomes or lack per-cell age and cell-type annotations, so positive-cell proportions per cell type per age group cannot be computed. The data matrix is already scaled (z-scored), which would corrupt the binarized score_hub calculation — the README requires data that are 'not scaled'. The goal is scoring senescent cells with in vitro-derived signatures (e.g., SenMayo alone) rather than the in vivo-derived SenePy hubs, which the paper shows better recapitulate in vivo senescence. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies how the proportion of senescence-positive cells (SenePy score binarized per cell) changes with organismal age across cell types in the Tabula Muris Senis mouse atlas (328K cells, 19 tissues, ages 1-30 months) and a human single-cell aging atlas, yielding old/young positive-cell ratios that reveal cell-type-specific marker dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Quantifies how the proportion of senescence-positive cells (SenePy score binarized per cell) changes with organismal age across cell types in the Tabula Muris Senis mouse atlas (328K cells, 19 tissues, ages 1-30 months) and a human single-cell aging atlas, yielding old/young positive-cell ratios that reveal cell-type-specific marker dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are bulk transcriptomes or lack per-cell age and cell-type annotations, so positive-cell proportions per cell type per age group cannot be computed. The data matrix is already scaled (z-scored), which would corrupt the binarized score_hub calculation — the README requires data that are 'not scaled'. The goal is scoring senescent cells with in vitro-derived signatures (e.g., SenMayo alone) rather than the in vivo-derived SenePy hubs, which the paper shows better recapitulate in vivo senescence.

skills.description: Use when scoring cells (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis tongue keratinocytes) with senescence hub signatures and you need to test whether the proportion of senescence-outlier cells increases with organismal age.
skills.name: age-stratified-cell-proportion-analysis
skills.search_text: age-stratified-cell-proportion-analysis Use when scoring cells (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis tongue keratinocytes) with senescence hub signatures and you need to test whether the proportion of senescence-outlier cells increases with organismal age. The goal is identifying which genes are senescence markers rather than testing age-dependent senescent-cell accumulation — use hubs.search_hubs_by_genes or merge_hubs instead The input is bulk transcriptomics or a pre-computed feature table with no per-cell scores and donor-age labels; mu + 3 sigma outlier calling and per-age contingency tables require single-cell scores Data are already scaled — score_hub expects raw or normalized (not scaled) expression since it binarizes by default http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies age-dependent accumulation of senescent cells by scoring single-cell transcriptomes with SenePy cell-type-specific hub signatures, calling outlier cells at mu + 3 sigma, and testing whether the outlier proportion changes across donor ages with a chi-square test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Quantifies age-dependent accumulation of senescent cells by scoring single-cell transcriptomes with SenePy cell-type-specific hub signatures, calling outlier cells at mu + 3 sigma, and testing whether the outlier proportion changes across donor ages with a chi-square test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is identifying which genes are senescence markers rather than testing age-dependent senescent-cell accumulation — use hubs.search_hubs_by_genes or merge_hubs instead The input is bulk transcriptomics or a pre-computed feature table with no per-cell scores and donor-age labels; mu + 3 sigma outlier calling and per-age contingency tables require single-cell scores Data are already scaled — score_hub expects raw or normalized (not scaled) expression since it binarizes by default

skills.description: Use when scDNA-seq cells have copy-number (CNA) profiles but no prior clone labels, and a clone partition is needed as input to RNA-to-clone mapping (e.g., MaCroDNA cell2clone_assignment) or when benchmarking clone definitions across clustering/transformation configurations.
skills.name: agglomerative-clustering-of-copy-number-profiles
skills.search_text: agglomerative-clustering-of-copy-number-profiles Use when scDNA-seq cells have copy-number (CNA) profiles but no prior clone labels, and a clone partition is needed as input to RNA-to-clone mapping (e.g., MaCroDNA cell2clone_assignment) or when benchmarking clone definitions across clustering/transformation configurations. Ground-truth clone labels are already available (e.g., the dna_label 'clone'/'cell' columns from scTrio-seq joint genotyping) — skip clustering and use the labels directly The goal is to evaluate a method on the BE dataset, where no ground truth cell correspondence exists and only resampling/stability analyses apply Comparing against probabilistic assignment methods when confidence measures are required — agglomerative clustering plus MaCroDNA does not provide probabilistic confidence for assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Agglomerative (hierarchical) clustering of scDNA-seq copy-number profiles into clones, applied in the MaCroDNA CRC scTrio-seq benchmark as one of two clone-partitioning strategies (with intNMF) evaluated under both original and log-transformed copy-number values before cell-to-clone assignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Agglomerative (hierarchical) clustering of scDNA-seq copy-number profiles into clones, applied in the MaCroDNA CRC scTrio-seq benchmark as one of two clone-partitioning strategies (with intNMF) evaluated under both original and log-transformed copy-number values before cell-to-clone assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth clone labels are already available (e.g., the dna_label 'clone'/'cell' columns from scTrio-seq joint genotyping) — skip clustering and use the labels directly The goal is to evaluate a method on the BE dataset, where no ground truth cell correspondence exists and only resampling/stability analyses apply Comparing against probabilistic assignment methods when confidence measures are required — agglomerative clustering plus MaCroDNA does not provide probabilistic confidence for assignments

skills.name: aggregated-bloom-comb-tree-construction
skills.search_text: aggregated-bloom-comb-tree-construction Use when many sequence datasets (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip-compressed or not) must be indexed together so later queries can list which datasets share k-mers with a query sequence, especially when index construction time and disk footprint must stay low. The task needs exact (not approximate) membership answers — PAC is an AMQ structure and its Bloom filters admit false positives controlled by the chosen -b bit count The collection is so small that a BLAST-like alignment search is routine and index construction overhead is not justified More files than the chosen encoding allows must be indexed (e.g. >256 files with -e 8); use the default 16-bit or -e 32 instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs a PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) index: an approximate membership query structure that partitions a k-mer set by minimizers into 4^p partition files, each holding aggregated Bloom Comb filters, enabling dataset-membership queries over thousands of FASTA/FASTQ collections with low memory and disk footprint. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Constructs a PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) index: an approximate membership query structure that partitions a k-mer set by minimizers into 4^p partition files, each holding aggregated Bloom Comb filters, enabling dataset-membership queries over thousands of FASTA/FASTQ collections with low memory and disk footprint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task needs exact (not approximate) membership answers — PAC is an AMQ structure and its Bloom filters admit false positives controlled by the chosen -b bit count The collection is so small that a BLAST-like alignment search is routine and index construction overhead is not justified More files than the chosen encoding allows must be indexed (e.g. >256 files with -e 8); use the default 16-bit or -e 32 instead

skills.search_text: aggregated-gradient-heatmap-visualization Use when a trained SpatialDDLS deconvolution model exists and the goal is model interpretation: ranking which genes drive predicted cell type proportions and visualizing top per-cell-type gradient markers as a heatmap. The SpatialDDLS model has not yet been trained (no trainDeconvModel output) — gradients require a fitted neural network over simulated mixed profiles The task is deconvolution itself (predicting cell type proportions from spatial data via deconvSpatialDDLS with spatial regularization) rather than interpreting an already-trained model http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Interprets a trained SpatialDDLS neural network deconvolution model by computing per-gene gradients of predicted class scores (Vanilla Gradient, Simonyan et al. 2014), aggregating them to per-cell-type ranked gene lists, and visualizing the top aggregated gradients as heatmaps (e.g., Cd8/Cd8b1 for CD8 T cells, Foxp3 for Tregs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae072

skills.when_to_use_negative: The SpatialDDLS model has not yet been trained (no trainDeconvModel output) — gradients require a fitted neural network over simulated mixed profiles The task is deconvolution itself (predicting cell type proportions from spatial data via deconvSpatialDDLS with spatial regularization) rather than interpreting an already-trained model

skills.description: Use when you have ScanNeo2 variant_effects.tsv entries plus typed HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and need to rank mutant-vs-wildtype MHC binding predictions into agretopicity-scored neoepitope tables.
skills.name: agretopicity-score-computation
skills.search_text: agretopicity-score-computation Use when you have ScanNeo2 variant_effects.tsv entries plus typed HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and need to rank mutant-vs-wildtype MHC binding predictions into agretopicity-scored neoepitope tables. The prioritization MHC class is not a subset of the detected hlatyping.class (e.g. class I prioritization requested but only HLA-HD class II alleles were typed) — the (allele, length) prediction grid cannot be built. Variants come from outside ScanNeo2's variant_effects.tsv outputs or lack a matched wildtype peptide context, so the mt/wt IC50 pair required for the agretopicity ratio is unavailable. The goal is HLA genotyping itself (yara + Optitype for class I, HLA-HD for class II) rather than peptide-level neoepitope prioritization. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the agretopicity score (mutant affinity / wildtype affinity, i.e. mt_epitope_seq_ic50 / wt_epitope_seq_ic50) for each candidate neoepitope in ScanNeo2's prioritization stage, using netMHCpan and netMHCIIpan binding predictions against the sample's typed HLA alleles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Computes the agretopicity score (mutant affinity / wildtype affinity, i.e. mt_epitope_seq_ic50 / wt_epitope_seq_ic50) for each candidate neoepitope in ScanNeo2's prioritization stage, using netMHCpan and netMHCIIpan binding predictions against the sample's typed HLA alleles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The prioritization MHC class is not a subset of the detected hlatyping.class (e.g. class I prioritization requested but only HLA-HD class II alleles were typed) — the (allele, length) prediction grid cannot be built. Variants come from outside ScanNeo2's variant_effects.tsv outputs or lack a matched wildtype peptide context, so the mt/wt IC50 pair required for the agretopicity ratio is unavailable. The goal is HLA genotyping itself (yara + Optitype for class I, HLA-HD for class II) rather than peptide-level neoepitope prioritization.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. LIGER, LIGER UINMF, fastMNN, SeuratV4, scANVI, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, SAMap) and you need to quantify how much integration blurs distinct cell types, i.e. overcorrection, on integrated embeddings with ground-truth cell type labels.
skills.name: alcs-biology-conservation-metric-implementation
skills.search_text: alcs-biology-conservation-metric-implementation Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. LIGER, LIGER UINMF, fastMNN, SeuratV4, scANVI, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, SAMap) and you need to quantify how much integration blurs distinct cell types, i.e. overcorrection, on integrated embeddings with ground-truth cell type labels. Cell type annotations are untrusted — the metric's quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and confident known cell type homology from literature The desired cell type correspondence across species is non-one-to-one; the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings and valid non-one-to-one mappings are not assessed You need to evaluate species mixing rather than biology conservation — use the paper's species-mixing metrics alongside ALCS http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements ALCS (accuracy loss of cell type self-projection), the BENGAL paper's new biology conservation metric for measuring maintenance of cell type distinguishability after cross-species scRNA-seq integration. It quantifies overcorrection (cell type blending) by comparing an SCCAF self-projection classifier's held-out accuracy on integrated embeddings versus the unintegrated per-species baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Implements ALCS (accuracy loss of cell type self-projection), the BENGAL paper's new biology conservation metric for measuring maintenance of cell type distinguishability after cross-species scRNA-seq integration. It quantifies overcorrection (cell type blending) by comparing an SCCAF self-projection classifier's held-out accuracy on integrated embeddings versus the unintegrated per-species baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type annotations are untrusted — the metric's quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and confident known cell type homology from literature The desired cell type correspondence across species is non-one-to-one; the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings and valid non-one-to-one mappings are not assessed You need to evaluate species mixing rather than biology conservation — use the paper's species-mixing metrics alongside ALCS

skills.description: Use when a paper asserts a time complexity (e.g., Augusta's O(mn²D²) for MI-based GRN inference from RNA-Seq count tables) and you must verify it empirically by timing scaled inputs and fitting runtime to the parameterized model.
skills.name: algorithmic-complexity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: algorithmic-complexity-benchmarking Use when a paper asserts a time complexity (e.g., Augusta's O(mn²D²) for MI-based GRN inference from RNA-Seq count tables) and you must verify it empirically by timing scaled inputs and fitting runtime to the parameterized model. Benchmarking the refinement or BN-conversion stages — the article states the refinement of an initial GRN may be computationally very demanding, so the O(mn²D²) model applies only to the MI-based initial GRN step. Input lacks adjacent time points (e.g., steady-state or single-sample expression matrices) — edge orientation depends on the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points, so the timed workload cannot be reproduced. The aim is to compare network quality rather than runtime scaling — the sensitivity/specificity/accuracy figures here are sanity anchors, not the benchmark target. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Empirically verifies a claimed asymptotic runtime — here Augusta's O(mn²D²) for the mutual-information-based initial GRN inference — by timing the algorithm on progressively scaled time-series count tables, fitting measured seconds to the parameterized model, and anchoring absolute runtime against the paper's 83.07 s DREAM 4 MI-only benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Empirically verifies a claimed asymptotic runtime — here Augusta's O(mn²D²) for the mutual-information-based initial GRN inference — by timing the algorithm on progressively scaled time-series count tables, fitting measured seconds to the parameterized model, and anchoring absolute runtime against the paper's 83.07 s DREAM 4 MI-only benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking the refinement or BN-conversion stages — the article states the refinement of an initial GRN may be computationally very demanding, so the O(mn²D²) model applies only to the MI-based initial GRN step. Input lacks adjacent time points (e.g., steady-state or single-sample expression matrices) — edge orientation depends on the most significant difference (MSD) among adjacent pairs of time points, so the timed workload cannot be reproduced. The aim is to compare network quality rather than runtime scaling — the sensitivity/specificity/accuracy figures here are sanity anchors, not the benchmark target.

skills.description: Use when two aligner runs of scPathoQuant (-align bbmap vs -align bowtie2) have produced per-gene pathogen UMI outputs for the same samples and you need to quantify their per-gene count consistency.
skills.name: aligner-consistency-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: aligner-consistency-correlation-analysis Use when two aligner runs of scPathoQuant (-align bbmap vs -align bowtie2) have produced per-gene pathogen UMI outputs for the same samples and you need to quantify their per-gene count consistency. The scPathoQuant run was performed without a pathogen GTF, so per-gene outputs (pathogen_genes_al_sort_counts.sam) were not produced and only whole-pathogen counts exist The two runs to compare were not performed on the same samples with the same pathogen reference genome, so per-gene vectors are not paired The goal is benchmarking against external tools (ViralTrack, Venus, PathogenTrack) rather than internal aligner consistency http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Validates that scPathoQuant's two alignment backends (bbmap and bowtie2) yield concordant per-gene pathogen UMI quantifications by computing per-sample Pearson correlations of gene-level UMI count vectors across the ten annotated SARS-CoV-2 genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Validates that scPathoQuant's two alignment backends (bbmap and bowtie2) yield concordant per-gene pathogen UMI quantifications by computing per-sample Pearson correlations of gene-level UMI count vectors across the ten annotated SARS-CoV-2 genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scPathoQuant run was performed without a pathogen GTF, so per-gene outputs (pathogen_genes_al_sort_counts.sam) were not produced and only whole-pathogen counts exist The two runs to compare were not performed on the same samples with the same pathogen reference genome, so per-gene vectors are not paired The goal is benchmarking against external tools (ViralTrack, Venus, PathogenTrack) rather than internal aligner consistency

skills.search_text: alignment-distance-and-atc-score-aggregation Use when you need to characterize how a trajectory-tree alignment method's accuracy metrics (e.g., normalized alignment distance, ATC score) degrade as a function of controlled input perturbation such as Gaussian noise. Input datasets have different global topological structure — the paper notes alignment accuracy of CAPITAL degraded in such benchmarking cases The trajectories form complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form deals only with trajectory trees computed from input datasets The goal is biological comparison of authentic datasets rather than controlled robustness/benchmarking of the alignment method itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarking skill from the CAPITAL paper: quantify noise robustness of single-cell trajectory tree alignment by adding Gaussian noise to synthetic trajectory pairs, running the CAPITAL pipeline (preprocessing, trajectory_tree, dpt, tree_alignment, dtw) on each perturbed pair, and aggregating normalized alignment distance and ATC scores by noise level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill from the CAPITAL paper: quantify noise robustness of single-cell trajectory tree alignment by adding Gaussian noise to synthetic trajectory pairs, running the CAPITAL pipeline (preprocessing, trajectory_tree, dpt, tree_alignment, dtw) on each perturbed pair, and aggregating normalized alignment distance and ATC scores by noise level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input datasets have different global topological structure — the paper notes alignment accuracy of CAPITAL degraded in such benchmarking cases The trajectories form complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form deals only with trajectory trees computed from input datasets The goal is biological comparison of authentic datasets rather than controlled robustness/benchmarking of the alignment method itself

skills.description: Use when two domain mappings (e.g. scRNA-seq to spatial transcriptomics) have been generated by GAN-based aligners and you must judge whether target distributions match (MMD) and whether point-wise correspondence with inputs is preserved (MSE).
skills.name: alignment-quality-metric-computation-mmd-mse
skills.search_text: alignment-quality-metric-computation-mmd-mse Use when two domain mappings (e.g. scRNA-seq to spatial transcriptomics) have been generated by GAN-based aligners and you must judge whether target distributions match (MMD) and whether point-wise correspondence with inputs is preserved (MSE). When the two domains share overlapping measurements that can be directly regressed with a supervised model — the adversarial mapping setting is assumed When only distribution-level comparison is needed and point-wise correspondence is not a requirement; MSE against original inputs is meaningless if inputs lack a known alignment When data has not been preprocessed (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50-PC reduction) so MSE comparisons against baselines are not comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify cross-modal alignment quality by computing maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for distribution matching and per-sample mean-squared error (MSE) for point-wise correspondence, as done in the scMMGAN TNBC xenograft evaluation across four scRNA-seq samples (primary tumor, lung, liver, lymph node). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Quantify cross-modal alignment quality by computing maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for distribution matching and per-sample mean-squared error (MSE) for point-wise correspondence, as done in the scMMGAN TNBC xenograft evaluation across four scRNA-seq samples (primary tumor, lung, liver, lymph node).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two domains share overlapping measurements that can be directly regressed with a supervised model — the adversarial mapping setting is assumed When only distribution-level comparison is needed and point-wise correspondence is not a requirement; MSE against original inputs is meaningless if inputs lack a known alignment When data has not been preprocessed (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50-PC reduction) so MSE comparisons against baselines are not comparable

skills.description: Use when pooled protein FASTA files from annotated genomes must be converted into a bitscore-weighted gene similarity network to drive graph-based gene family clustering (e.g., MCL) and downstream absence/presence matrices.
skills.name: all-vs-all-protein-alignment
skills.search_text: all-vs-all-protein-alignment Use when pooled protein FASTA files from annotated genomes must be converted into a bitscore-weighted gene similarity network to drive graph-based gene family clustering (e.g., MCL) and downstream absence/presence matrices. Input is already a gene cluster absence/presence matrix or an MCL-ready network file — proceed directly to lifestyle prediction or MCL instead of re-aligning. Nucleotide-level or genomic alignment is required (e.g., genome-level ANI redundancy reduction) — this skill operates on Prokka-predicted protein sequences only. Ortholog group calling with OrthoFinder is explicitly preferred — the article benchmarks bacLIFE's diamond+MCL clustering against OrthoFinder defaults as an alternative. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generates a weighted similarity network of protein sequences by aligning cluster representatives all-vs-all with diamond (e-value cutoff 1e-5), where the first two columns are gene nodes and the third column is the diamond bitscore. This network is the input required for Markov clustering (MCL) into functional gene clusters in the bacLIFE clustering module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Generates a weighted similarity network of protein sequences by aligning cluster representatives all-vs-all with diamond (e-value cutoff 1e-5), where the first two columns are gene nodes and the third column is the diamond bitscore. This network is the input required for Markov clustering (MCL) into functional gene clusters in the bacLIFE clustering module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene cluster absence/presence matrix or an MCL-ready network file — proceed directly to lifestyle prediction or MCL instead of re-aligning. Nucleotide-level or genomic alignment is required (e.g., genome-level ANI redundancy reduction) — this skill operates on Prokka-predicted protein sequences only. Ortholog group calling with OrthoFinder is explicitly preferred — the article benchmarks bacLIFE's diamond+MCL clustering against OrthoFinder defaults as an alternative.

skills.description: Use when you have vireoSNP clone labels and a set of MQuad ΔBIC-selected mtDNA variants and need to visually confirm clonal discrimination, e.g. reproducing Fig. 4c for MKN-45 scDNA-seq data.
skills.name: allele-frequency-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: allele-frequency-heatmap-visualization Use when you have vireoSNP clone labels and a set of MQuad ΔBIC-selected mtDNA variants and need to visually confirm clonal discrimination, e.g. reproducing Fig. 4c for MKN-45 scDNA-seq data. Input is raw per-cell genotype matrices without prior MQuad variant selection — noisy, non-clonal mtDNA SNVs will dominate the heatmap and obscure clonal structure The task is donor demultiplexing or allele-specific CNV analysis (e.g., with vireo alone, Numbat, XClone); the heatmap is specifically for validating clonal substructure via mitochondrial variants No clone labels exist yet — heatmap requires completed vireoSNP clone assignment; run cellsnp-lite → MQuad → vireoSNP first http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualization step that renders the SNP-by-cell AD/DP pileup from cellsnp-lite, restricted to MQuad-selected clone-discriminative mtDNA variants, as an allele-frequency heatmap across vireoSNP-inferred mitochondrial clones (Fig. 4c), often paired with a CNV-clone vs mtDNA-clone confusion matrix (Fig. 4b). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Visualization step that renders the SNP-by-cell AD/DP pileup from cellsnp-lite, restricted to MQuad-selected clone-discriminative mtDNA variants, as an allele-frequency heatmap across vireoSNP-inferred mitochondrial clones (Fig. 4c), often paired with a CNV-clone vs mtDNA-clone confusion matrix (Fig. 4b).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw per-cell genotype matrices without prior MQuad variant selection — noisy, non-clonal mtDNA SNVs will dominate the heatmap and obscure clonal structure The task is donor demultiplexing or allele-specific CNV analysis (e.g., with vireo alone, Numbat, XClone); the heatmap is specifically for validating clonal substructure via mitochondrial variants No clone labels exist yet — heatmap requires completed vireoSNP clone assignment; run cellsnp-lite → MQuad → vireoSNP first

skills.description: Use when analyzing PTA-amplified high-coverage (>20x) scWGS BAMs with matched bulk WGS, to call small (200 kb–5 Mb) allele-specific CNAs that RDR-only callers miss and to obtain integer copy-number states per allele per cell.
skills.name: allele-specific-cna-detection
skills.search_text: allele-specific-cna-detection Use when analyzing PTA-amplified high-coverage (>20x) scWGS BAMs with matched bulk WGS, to call small (200 kb–5 Mb) allele-specific CNAs that RDR-only callers miss and to obtain integer copy-number states per allele per cell. Data are low-coverage (<0.05x per cell) scWGS from DLP+/10x-style platforms — CHISEL/Alleloscope are designed for that regime and BAF at HiScanner's resolution is unreliable The matched bulk is absent — reference-based phasing and BAF estimation (and SCAN2 germline exclusion) both require bulk WGS The cell is known aneuploid across whole chromosomes and the goal is megabase-scale mosaic CNA prevalence analysis — the article excluded aneuploid neurons from CNA length and prevalence analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect allele-specific (haplotype-specific) copy number alterations in single-cell WGS by jointly modeling read-depth ratios (RDR) and B-allele frequencies (BAF) derived from reference-phased germline heterozygous SNPs, as implemented in HiScanner's standard pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Detect allele-specific (haplotype-specific) copy number alterations in single-cell WGS by jointly modeling read-depth ratios (RDR) and B-allele frequencies (BAF) derived from reference-phased germline heterozygous SNPs, as implemented in HiScanner's standard pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are low-coverage (<0.05x per cell) scWGS from DLP+/10x-style platforms — CHISEL/Alleloscope are designed for that regime and BAF at HiScanner's resolution is unreliable The matched bulk is absent — reference-based phasing and BAF estimation (and SCAN2 germline exclusion) both require bulk WGS The cell is known aneuploid across whole chromosomes and the goal is megabase-scale mosaic CNA prevalence analysis — the article excluded aneuploid neurons from CNA length and prevalence analyses

skills.description: Use when the goal is to infer haplotype-aware CNA states or tumor subclones from single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g., 10x Genomics droplet or Smart-seq2 tumor samples), especially when copy-neutral LOH or low tumor purity challenges expression-only methods.
skills.name: allele-specific-cna-detection-from-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: allele-specific-cna-detection-from-scrnaseq Use when the goal is to infer haplotype-aware CNA states or tumor subclones from single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g., 10x Genomics droplet or Smart-seq2 tumor samples), especially when copy-neutral LOH or low tumor purity challenges expression-only methods. The task only requires expression-level CNA inference and no allelic/LOH information is needed — in that case InferCNV or CopyKAT (which do not model allelic information) may suffice The input is bulk DNA-seq or single-cell DNA-seq data, for which tools like ACT5 or CHISEL are more appropriate Only pseudo-bulk clonal resolution is acceptable and single-cell-level CNA resolution is not required (Numbat-style aggregation) http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect allele- and haplotype-specific copy number alterations in individual cells from low-coverage, sparse scRNA-seq data using XClone, which combines a B-allele frequency (BAF) module and a read-depth ratio (RDR) module, then resolve tumor subclones by clustering the combined CNA states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Detect allele- and haplotype-specific copy number alterations in individual cells from low-coverage, sparse scRNA-seq data using XClone, which combines a B-allele frequency (BAF) module and a read-depth ratio (RDR) module, then resolve tumor subclones by clustering the combined CNA states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task only requires expression-level CNA inference and no allelic/LOH information is needed — in that case InferCNV or CopyKAT (which do not model allelic information) may suffice The input is bulk DNA-seq or single-cell DNA-seq data, for which tools like ACT5 or CHISEL are more appropriate Only pseudo-bulk clonal resolution is acceptable and single-cell-level CNA resolution is not required (Numbat-style aggregation)

skills.description: Use when analyzing high-coverage (>20x) PTA-amplified single-cell WGS data where small (100 kb–Mb scale) somatic CNAs must be called with allele-specific copy states, and paired bulk WGS is available for phasing.
skills.name: allele-specific-copy-number-inference
skills.search_text: allele-specific-copy-number-inference Use when analyzing high-coverage (>20x) PTA-amplified single-cell WGS data where small (100 kb–Mb scale) somatic CNAs must be called with allele-specific copy states, and paired bulk WGS is available for phasing. Low-coverage scWGS data from DLP+ or 10x Genomics — callers like CHISEL or Alleloscope are designed for that regime, not high-coverage allele-specific inference Sex chromosomes — SCAN2 explicitly supports only diploid autosomes 1-22 (analysis is restricted to autosomes) Data lacking matched bulk WGS for germline SNP calling and reference-based phasing, since BAF estimation depends on phased gHETs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Infer integer allele-specific copy number states and cell ploidy from high-coverage scWGS by jointly modeling read depth ratios (RDR) and B-allele frequencies (BAF) at phased germline heterozygous SNPs, as implemented in HiScanner. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Infer integer allele-specific copy number states and cell ploidy from high-coverage scWGS by jointly modeling read depth ratios (RDR) and B-allele frequencies (BAF) at phased germline heterozygous SNPs, as implemented in HiScanner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Low-coverage scWGS data from DLP+ or 10x Genomics — callers like CHISEL or Alleloscope are designed for that regime, not high-coverage allele-specific inference Sex chromosomes — SCAN2 explicitly supports only diploid autosomes 1-22 (analysis is restricted to autosomes) Data lacking matched bulk WGS for germline SNP calling and reference-based phasing, since BAF estimation depends on phased gHETs

skills.description: Use when per-cell copy gain/loss/LOH states must be inferred from raw scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts (10x or Smart-seq2), especially for tumour subclone dissection or when benchmarking XClone against InferCNV/CopyKAT/CaSpER/Numbat with AUROC.
skills.name: allele-specific-copy-number-state-inference
skills.search_text: allele-specific-copy-number-state-inference Use when per-cell copy gain/loss/LOH states must be inferred from raw scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts (10x or Smart-seq2), especially for tumour subclone dissection or when benchmarking XClone against InferCNV/CopyKAT/CaSpER/Numbat with AUROC. Input is already binarized per-gene CNA calls or a processed CNA feature table rather than raw counts — the skill operates on AD/DP and total read depth matrices from raw data Data are single-cell DNA-seq rather than scRNA-seq — methods like ACT5 or CHISEL are designed for single-cell DNA-seq CNA analysis Only expression data are available with no allelic/BAM support and copy-neutral LOH detection is not required — RDR-only callers such as InferCNV or CopyKAT suffice Infer allele- and haplotype-specific copy number states (copy gain, copy loss, LOH) per individual cell from sparse scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data using XClone's combined RDR (read depth ratio) and BAF (B-allele frequency) modules with HMM and KNN graph smoothing, and benchmark against InferCNV, CopyKAT, CaSpER, and Numbat. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Infer allele- and haplotype-specific copy number states (copy gain, copy loss, LOH) per individual cell from sparse scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data using XClone's combined RDR (read depth ratio) and BAF (B-allele frequency) modules with HMM and KNN graph smoothing, and benchmark against InferCNV, CopyKAT, CaSpER, and Numbat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already binarized per-gene CNA calls or a processed CNA feature table rather than raw counts — the skill operates on AD/DP and total read depth matrices from raw data Data are single-cell DNA-seq rather than scRNA-seq — methods like ACT5 or CHISEL are designed for single-cell DNA-seq CNA analysis Only expression data are available with no allelic/BAM support and copy-neutral LOH detection is not required — RDR-only callers such as InferCNV or CopyKAT suffice

skills.description: Use when multi-sample VCF files (GATK HaplotypeCaller output) from RNA-seq of heterozygous individuals are available and the goal is to identify which biallelic SNPs show statistically significant allele-specific expression per tissue.
skills.name: allele-specific-expression-detection
skills.search_text: allele-specific-expression-detection Use when multi-sample VCF files (GATK HaplotypeCaller output) from RNA-seq of heterozygous individuals are available and the goal is to identify which biallelic SNPs show statistically significant allele-specific expression per tissue. VCFs not produced by GATK's HaplotypeCaller — the README warns VCFs from other programs 'could potentially have some bugs' Multiallelic sites or indels, which are removed by design before ASE testing Questions about allele- or isoform-level quantification that require eQTL or phased haplotype data — the article notes ASE-translation associations are speculative 'without eQTL data' http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Detects allele-specific expression (ASE) of biallelic SNPs from RNA-seq VCFs using VADT, which filters variants/samples, runs a per-sample binomial test on raw allele depths, and combines p-values with Fisher's Method plus Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Detects allele-specific expression (ASE) of biallelic SNPs from RNA-seq VCFs using VADT, which filters variants/samples, runs a per-sample binomial test on raw allele depths, and combines p-values with Fisher's Method plus Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: VCFs not produced by GATK's HaplotypeCaller — the README warns VCFs from other programs 'could potentially have some bugs' Multiallelic sites or indels, which are removed by design before ASE testing Questions about allele- or isoform-level quantification that require eQTL or phased haplotype data — the article notes ASE-translation associations are speculative 'without eQTL data'

skills.description: Use when you have VADT sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt call sets for multiple tissues and need gene-level ASE sets, cross-tissue overlap percentages, or a high-ASE-score gene list for pathway analysis.
skills.name: allele-specific-expression-gene-set-compilation
skills.search_text: allele-specific-expression-gene-set-compilation Use when you have VADT sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt call sets for multiple tissues and need gene-level ASE sets, cross-tissue overlap percentages, or a high-ASE-score gene list for pathway analysis. When the input is raw VCF data that has not yet been tested for ASE — run VADT (binomial test + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, cutoff 0.05) first to generate sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt files When SNP-level ASE calls are needed rather than gene-level sets — this skill collapses SNPs to genes and loses per-SNP allele-ratio detail When the organism/annotation differs from Gallus_gallus_5.0 (Ensembl release 86) without re-mapping SNP-to-gene assignments via VEP http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Compiles per-tissue ASE SNP call sets from VADT meta-analysis output into gene-level ASE sets, computes cross-tissue gene overlap and a normalized per-gene ASE score, and prepares a high-confidence gene list (with symbols) for downstream PPI/pathway enrichment in STRING. It converts SNP-level ASE calls into a reusable, validated gene-level resource. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Compiles per-tissue ASE SNP call sets from VADT meta-analysis output into gene-level ASE sets, computes cross-tissue gene overlap and a normalized per-gene ASE score, and prepares a high-confidence gene list (with symbols) for downstream PPI/pathway enrichment in STRING. It converts SNP-level ASE calls into a reusable, validated gene-level resource.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw VCF data that has not yet been tested for ASE — run VADT (binomial test + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, cutoff 0.05) first to generate sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt files When SNP-level ASE calls are needed rather than gene-level sets — this skill collapses SNPs to genes and loses per-SNP allele-ratio detail When the organism/annotation differs from Gallus_gallus_5.0 (Ensembl release 86) without re-mapping SNP-to-gene assignments via VEP
