skills.description: Use when patient-specific HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and per-variant-type variant_effects.tsv files are available and predicted neoantigens must be ranked per allele by MHC binding affinity.
skills.name: allele-specific-peptide-prioritization
skills.search_text: allele-specific-peptide-prioritization Use when patient-specific HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and per-variant-type variant_effects.tsv files are available and predicted neoantigens must be ranked per allele by MHC binding affinity. HLA genotypes have not yet been produced (mhc-i.tsv / mhc-II.tsv missing) — prioritization classes must be a subset of hlatyping.class Only a small set of candidate peptides needs direct affinity checking outside a workflow, with no variant-context wildtype counterparts available for agretopicity computation The goal is de novo peptide discovery from raw sequencing data — this skill only scores peptides already extracted from detected variants http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Prioritization stage of a neoantigen workflow in which variant-derived wildtype and mutant peptide k-mers are scored for binding affinity against the patient's typed HLA class I and II alleles using netMHCpan and netMHCIIpan, yielding a ranked, tab-delimited neoepitope list with agretopicity and immunogenicity metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Prioritization stage of a neoantigen workflow in which variant-derived wildtype and mutant peptide k-mers are scored for binding affinity against the patient's typed HLA class I and II alleles using netMHCpan and netMHCIIpan, yielding a ranked, tab-delimited neoepitope list with agretopicity and immunogenicity metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: HLA genotypes have not yet been produced (mhc-i.tsv / mhc-II.tsv missing) — prioritization classes must be a subset of hlatyping.class Only a small set of candidate peptides needs direct affinity checking outside a workflow, with no variant-context wildtype counterparts available for agretopicity computation The goal is de novo peptide discovery from raw sequencing data — this skill only scores peptides already extracted from detected variants

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a polymorphic F1 cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be converted into per-allele gene counts, and you must decide between unique-read counting and multi-read weighted allocation before allelic classification.
skills.name: allele-specific-read-counting
skills.search_text: allele-specific-read-counting Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a polymorphic F1 cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be converted into per-allele gene counts, and you must decide between unique-read counting and multi-read weighted allocation before allelic classification. The data are bulk RNA-Seq or lack strain-specific polymorphism information, so no phase-known diploid transcriptome can be built Reads are already allele-resolved UMI counts (e.g. Larsson et al. 224-cell UMI data) and multi-read resolution is not the bottleneck You only need total expression per gene, not per-allele proportions, and unique mapping alone would suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Generates allele-specific read count matrices (maternal/paternal per gene per cell) from F1-hybrid single-cell RNA-Seq by aligning to a phase-known diploid transcriptome and resolving multi-mapping reads either by discarding them (unique-reads) or by EM-based weighted allocation, since counting choice drives downstream monoallelic and dynamic expression calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Generates allele-specific read count matrices (maternal/paternal per gene per cell) from F1-hybrid single-cell RNA-Seq by aligning to a phase-known diploid transcriptome and resolving multi-mapping reads either by discarding them (unique-reads) or by EM-based weighted allocation, since counting choice drives downstream monoallelic and dynamic expression calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk RNA-Seq or lack strain-specific polymorphism information, so no phase-known diploid transcriptome can be built Reads are already allele-resolved UMI counts (e.g. Larsson et al. 224-cell UMI data) and multi-read resolution is not the bottleneck You only need total expression per gene, not per-allele proportions, and unique mapping alone would suffice

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from an F1 hybrid cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be assigned to maternal/paternal alleles for allele-specific expression counting, and multi-mapping reads should be retained rather than discarded.
skills.name: allele-specific-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: allele-specific-short-read-alignment Use when scRNA-Seq reads from an F1 hybrid cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be assigned to maternal/paternal alleles for allele-specific expression counting, and multi-mapping reads should be retained rather than discarded. Input reads are not from a cross with known parental variants — there is no SNP/indel basis to build a phase-known diploid transcriptome. UMI-based counting where only unambiguous allelic assignment is acceptable and multi-read resolution is not desired downstream. The goal is whole-genome or splice-aware alignment rather than transcriptome-level allele tagging. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a phase-known diploid (CAST/B6) transcriptome and aligns scRNA-Seq reads against it with bowtie so every read is tagged with parental-origin labels, retaining genomic and allelic multi-reads for downstream allele-specific expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Constructs a phase-known diploid (CAST/B6) transcriptome and aligns scRNA-Seq reads against it with bowtie so every read is tagged with parental-origin labels, retaining genomic and allelic multi-reads for downstream allele-specific expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not from a cross with known parental variants — there is no SNP/indel basis to build a phase-known diploid transcriptome. UMI-based counting where only unambiguous allelic assignment is acceptable and multi-read resolution is not desired downstream. The goal is whole-genome or splice-aware alignment rather than transcriptome-level allele tagging.

skills.description: Use when allele-level UMI counts from single-cell 3' RNA-seq (Cell Ranger output, SNVs called with Freebayes) must be converted into per-cell genotype calls or two-genotype mixture inference, e.g. donor/host chimerism in transplant or mixing datasets.
skills.name: allele-umi-count-analysis
skills.search_text: allele-umi-count-analysis Use when allele-level UMI counts from single-cell 3' RNA-seq (Cell Ranger output, SNVs called with Freebayes) must be converted into per-cell genotype calls or two-genotype mixture inference, e.g. donor/host chimerism in transplant or mixing datasets. The goal is gene-expression analysis (use Seurat on the gene-barcode matrix with the top 1,000 most variable genes instead) Only cell-multiplexing/demultiplexing is needed and prior species/genotype identities are known via the simple SNV-fraction multiplet rule (cells with SNV fraction 0.2-0.8 from either species counted as multiplets) SNVs do not meet the genotype-assignment filters (support from at least two cell barcodes, SNV Qual>=30, base Qual>=1) — downstream mixture fitting will be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 An SNV-based single-cell genotyping method that fits Gibbs-sampled K=1 vs K=2 mixture models to allele-level UMI counts per cell barcodes, enabling de novo donor/host chimerism assignment in single-cell transcriptome data without prior genotype knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: An SNV-based single-cell genotyping method that fits Gibbs-sampled K=1 vs K=2 mixture models to allele-level UMI counts per cell barcodes, enabling de novo donor/host chimerism assignment in single-cell transcriptome data without prior genotype knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-expression analysis (use Seurat on the gene-barcode matrix with the top 1,000 most variable genes instead) Only cell-multiplexing/demultiplexing is needed and prior species/genotype identities are known via the simple SNV-fraction multiplet rule (cells with SNV fraction 0.2-0.8 from either species counted as multiplets) SNVs do not meet the genotype-assignment filters (support from at least two cell barcodes, SNV Qual>=30, base Qual>=1) — downstream mixture fitting will be unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have allele-specific single-cell count matrices and want to test per-gene whether maternal/paternal bursting events are independent (logOR ≈ 0), positively correlated, or anti-correlated, with FDR control.
skills.name: allelic-bursting-independence-testing
skills.search_text: allelic-bursting-independence-testing Use when you have allele-specific single-cell count matrices and want to test per-gene whether maternal/paternal bursting events are independent (logOR ≈ 0), positively correlated, or anti-correlated, with FDR control. Input is raw read alignments rather than scBASE-estimated allelic counts — run the scBASE workflow (unique-read or weighted-allocation counting, beta-binomial P/B/M classification, optional partial pooling) first. The goal is testing differential burst frequency or burst size between two cell populations (e.g., txburstTEST.py), not within-gene allelic burst correlation. Data are bulk or UMI-only without allelic assignment (e.g., Larsson et al. UMI counts without allele-resolved counts), so maternal/paternal bursting cannot be correlated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Fit the SCALE bursting model to scBASE-estimated allele-specific count matrices and compute per-gene burst-correlation log odds ratios (logOR) to test whether maternal and paternal allelic bursting are statistically independent or coordinated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Fit the SCALE bursting model to scBASE-estimated allele-specific count matrices and compute per-gene burst-correlation log odds ratios (logOR) to test whether maternal and paternal allelic bursting are statistically independent or coordinated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read alignments rather than scBASE-estimated allelic counts — run the scBASE workflow (unique-read or weighted-allocation counting, beta-binomial P/B/M classification, optional partial pooling) first. The goal is testing differential burst frequency or burst size between two cell populations (e.g., txburstTEST.py), not within-gene allelic burst correlation. Data are bulk or UMI-only without allelic assignment (e.g., Larsson et al. UMI counts without allele-resolved counts), so maternal/paternal bursting cannot be correlated.

skills.description: Use when starting from cell-barcoded BAM/CRAM files from a scRNA-seq experiment (e.g., 10x Genomics) and you need allele-specific AD/DP matrices to feed haplotype-aware CNA callers such as XClone's BAF module.
skills.name: allelic-count-matrix-generation-from-bam
skills.search_text: allelic-count-matrix-generation-from-bam Use when starting from cell-barcoded BAM/CRAM files from a scRNA-seq experiment (e.g., 10x Genomics) and you need allele-specific AD/DP matrices to feed haplotype-aware CNA callers such as XClone's BAF module. Input is already a processed count/feature matrix (e.g., a cell x gene expression matrix or cell x gene bin counts) with no BAM files available — xcltk needs raw alignments to genotype heterozygous variants. The analysis goal is copy-number calling from single-cell DNA-seq (e.g., using ACT or CHISEL) rather than scRNA-seq-based inference. Allelic information is not needed — RDR-only tools such as InferCNV can run from the expression matrix alone, though they cannot detect copy-neutral LOH. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate the allele-specific AD (alternate-allele depth) and DP (total depth) count matrices from single-cell BAM/CRAM files using xcltk, providing the BAF-signal inputs that XClone needs alongside the RDR read-depth matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Generate the allele-specific AD (alternate-allele depth) and DP (total depth) count matrices from single-cell BAM/CRAM files using xcltk, providing the BAF-signal inputs that XClone needs alongside the RDR read-depth matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed count/feature matrix (e.g., a cell x gene expression matrix or cell x gene bin counts) with no BAM files available — xcltk needs raw alignments to genotype heterozygous variants. The analysis goal is copy-number calling from single-cell DNA-seq (e.g., using ACT or CHISEL) rather than scRNA-seq-based inference. Allelic information is not needed — RDR-only tools such as InferCNV can run from the expression matrix alone, though they cannot detect copy-neutral LOH.

skills.description: Use when merged per-allele inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC for reference and alternative alleles across samples) are available and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR ≤ 10% from replicate or population-scale RNA-seq data.
skills.name: allelic-differential-splicing-statistical-modeling
skills.search_text: allelic-differential-splicing-statistical-modeling Use when merged per-allele inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC for reference and alternative alleles across samples) are available and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR ≤ 10% from replicate or population-scale RNA-seq data. The AS event has no heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon close enough to be detected on the same RNA-seq read — SNPs located within or too distant from alternative exons cannot be analyzed by PAIRADISE with short-read data You need to identify the causal splicing-regulatory SNP — PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs, not causal SNPs located within the alternative exon or nearby intronic regions The goal is sQTL association testing from unpaired genotype-phenotype data (e.g., GLiMMPS-style analysis) rather than allele-specific within-individual splicing comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs the PAIRADISE paired statistical model (R) on allele-stratified exon inclusion/skipping counts to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS), aggregating signal across replicates/individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP and reporting Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-significant AS event-SNP pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Runs the PAIRADISE paired statistical model (R) on allele-stratified exon inclusion/skipping counts to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS), aggregating signal across replicates/individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP and reporting Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-significant AS event-SNP pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AS event has no heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon close enough to be detected on the same RNA-seq read — SNPs located within or too distant from alternative exons cannot be analyzed by PAIRADISE with short-read data You need to identify the causal splicing-regulatory SNP — PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs, not causal SNPs located within the alternative exon or nearby intronic regions The goal is sQTL association testing from unpaired genotype-phenotype data (e.g., GLiMMPS-style analysis) rather than allele-specific within-individual splicing comparison

skills.description: Use when a single-cell WGS CNA analysis must pick a per-dataset bin size that balances CNA detection resolution against amplification noise, e.g. before binning PTA- or MDA-amplified scWGS with HiScanner.
skills.name: allelic-dropout-modeling-single-cell-wgs
skills.search_text: allelic-dropout-modeling-single-cell-wgs Use when a single-cell WGS CNA analysis must pick a per-dataset bin size that balances CNA detection resolution against amplification noise, e.g. before binning PTA- or MDA-amplified scWGS with HiScanner. No phased gHET calls or bulk VAFs are available (e.g., BAF-agnostic RDR-only pipelines or unphased bulk genotypes) — the HMM requires binarized BAF at SHAPEIT2-phased sites with bulk VAF 0.1–0.9 The single-cell library uses a whole-genome amplification assay for which no matched control cells exist to retrain the ADO HMM — dropout size distributions are assay-specific (PTA ~100 kb vs MDA ~10^5 bp-scale) Input is low-coverage scWGS (e.g., DLP+, 10x Genomics) better suited to CHISEL/Alleloscope-style analysis, where dropout-length-based bin size selection at ~100 kb is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fits a two-state Gaussian hidden Markov model ('ADO' vs 'non-ADO') to binarized B-allele frequencies at phased germline heterozygous sites (gHETs) in control single cells, then uses the predicted allelic dropout event size distribution to set the smallest permissible CNA bin size per amplification assay in HiScanner. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Fits a two-state Gaussian hidden Markov model ('ADO' vs 'non-ADO') to binarized B-allele frequencies at phased germline heterozygous sites (gHETs) in control single cells, then uses the predicted allelic dropout event size distribution to set the smallest permissible CNA bin size per amplification assay in HiScanner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No phased gHET calls or bulk VAFs are available (e.g., BAF-agnostic RDR-only pipelines or unphased bulk genotypes) — the HMM requires binarized BAF at SHAPEIT2-phased sites with bulk VAF 0.1–0.9 The single-cell library uses a whole-genome amplification assay for which no matched control cells exist to retrain the ADO HMM — dropout size distributions are assay-specific (PTA ~100 kb vs MDA ~10^5 bp-scale) Input is low-coverage scWGS (e.g., DLP+, 10x Genomics) better suited to CHISEL/Alleloscope-style analysis, where dropout-length-based bin size selection at ~100 kb is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when allelic read counts from single-cell RNA-Seq (e.g., CAST×B6 F1 embryos) need per-cell, per-gene P/B/M state calls, and random monoallelic bursts and sparse coverage make naive read-ratio thresholds unreliable.
skills.name: allelic-expression-state-classification
skills.search_text: allelic-expression-state-classification Use when allelic read counts from single-cell RNA-Seq (e.g., CAST×B6 F1 embryos) need per-cell, per-gene P/B/M state calls, and random monoallelic bursts and sparse coverage make naive read-ratio thresholds unreliable. When reads cannot be assigned allele-of-origin because the organism lacks a phase-known diploid reference (no SNP-split genome such as g2gtools-reconstructed CAST) When bulk (non-single-cell) RNA-Seq allelic proportions are the target — the beta-binomial mixture and partial pooling are designed for extremely low per-cell coverage and cell-to-cell heterogeneity When allele-specific counts are already high-confidence UMI-level per-allele transcript counts requiring burst-kinetics inference (e.g., txburst k_on/k_off/k_syn estimation) rather than state classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Probabilistic classification of each gene in each single cell into paternal monoallelic (P), bi-allelic (B), or maternal monoallelic (M) expression states using scBASE, a hierarchical mixture of beta-binomial distributions (Stan-backed), with optional partial pooling across cells to reduce sampling variability in low-coverage scRNA-Seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Probabilistic classification of each gene in each single cell into paternal monoallelic (P), bi-allelic (B), or maternal monoallelic (M) expression states using scBASE, a hierarchical mixture of beta-binomial distributions (Stan-backed), with optional partial pooling across cells to reduce sampling variability in low-coverage scRNA-Seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads cannot be assigned allele-of-origin because the organism lacks a phase-known diploid reference (no SNP-split genome such as g2gtools-reconstructed CAST) When bulk (non-single-cell) RNA-Seq allelic proportions are the target — the beta-binomial mixture and partial pooling are designed for extremely low per-cell coverage and cell-to-cell heterogeneity When allele-specific counts are already high-confidence UMI-level per-allele transcript counts requiring burst-kinetics inference (e.g., txburst k_on/k_off/k_syn estimation) rather than state classification

skills.description: Use when multiple studies or tissues (e.g., eQTLGen and GTEx whole blood) have summary statistics or individual-level genotypes/phenotypes for the same locus and you need to test whether signals colocalize despite possible multiple causal alleles and LD.
skills.name: allelic-heterogeneity-multi-component-colocalization
skills.search_text: allelic-heterogeneity-multi-component-colocalization Use when multiple studies or tissues (e.g., eQTLGen and GTEx whole blood) have summary statistics or individual-level genotypes/phenotypes for the same locus and you need to test whether signals colocalize despite possible multiple causal alleles and LD. The locus's effects are likely mediated by coding variants that may not show eQTL effects, so cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies have large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The effect-size matrix has missing data, because CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Jointly fine-map and colocalize eQTL signals across multiple tissues/studies with CAFEH, a Bayesian method that models allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) instead of assuming a single shared causal SNP, revealing tissue specificity masked by LD in meta-analytic approaches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Jointly fine-map and colocalize eQTL signals across multiple tissues/studies with CAFEH, a Bayesian method that models allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) instead of assuming a single shared causal SNP, revealing tissue specificity masked by LD in meta-analytic approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus's effects are likely mediated by coding variants that may not show eQTL effects, so cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies have large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The effect-size matrix has missing data, because CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets

skills.description: Use when single-cell allele-specific RNA-Seq read counts are too sparse (e.g. <10 unique reads per gene) for reliable per-cell allelic proportion estimates, and classification of P/B/M expression states is needed.
skills.name: allelic-proportion-partial-pooling
skills.search_text: allelic-proportion-partial-pooling Use when single-cell allele-specific RNA-Seq read counts are too sparse (e.g. <10 unique reads per gene) for reliable per-cell allelic proportion estimates, and classification of P/B/M expression states is needed. When reads are bulk (non-single-cell) allele-specific data — the pooling rationale depends on information across cells sharing an allelic expression state When the goal is bursting-kinetics parameter inference rather than state classification/allelic proportion estimation — use txburst instead When per-gene read coverage is already high and sampling variability is negligible; pooling gains are concentrated at low expression (<10 unique reads per gene) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 scBASE-style estimation of per-cell allelic proportions (maternal:paternal read fractions) that alternates a three-component beta-binomial classification (paternal monoallelic, bi-allelic, maternal monoallelic) with partial pooling — a weighted average of class-specific proportions across cells in the same state — fitted via Stan. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: scBASE-style estimation of per-cell allelic proportions (maternal:paternal read fractions) that alternates a three-component beta-binomial classification (paternal monoallelic, bi-allelic, maternal monoallelic) with partial pooling — a weighted average of class-specific proportions across cells in the same state — fitted via Stan.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are bulk (non-single-cell) allele-specific data — the pooling rationale depends on information across cells sharing an allelic expression state When the goal is bursting-kinetics parameter inference rather than state classification/allelic proportion estimation — use txburst instead When per-gene read coverage is already high and sampling variability is negligible; pooling gains are concentrated at low expression (<10 unique reads per gene)

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads aligned to two haplotype-modified personal genomes must be allele-assigned: filter multi-mapping or between-genome discordant reads, then assign haplotypes by SNP majority voting before ASAS counting.
skills.name: allelic-read-uniqueness-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: allelic-read-uniqueness-qc-filtering Use when RNA-seq reads aligned to two haplotype-modified personal genomes must be allele-assigned: filter multi-mapping or between-genome discordant reads, then assign haplotypes by SNP majority voting before ASAS counting. Reads are aligned to a single unmodified reference genome (e.g., STAR on hg19 only) — uniqueness across both haplotype-modified genomes cannot be assessed and majority voting over phased SNPs is not meaningful No phased per-sample VCF genotype data are available, so haplotype-modified personal genomes cannot be constructed The heterozygous SNPs of interest are inside alternative exons or too distant from the AS event to appear on short RNA-seq reads — reads cannot be allele-assigned for PAIRADISE analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A read-level quality-control and assignment filter from the PAIRADISE/rPGA workflow that retains only RNA-seq reads mapping uniquely to both haplotype-modified personal genomes at the same genomic location, then assigns each retained read to haplotype 1 or 2 by majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs, discarding multi-SNP draws. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: A read-level quality-control and assignment filter from the PAIRADISE/rPGA workflow that retains only RNA-seq reads mapping uniquely to both haplotype-modified personal genomes at the same genomic location, then assigns each retained read to haplotype 1 or 2 by majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs, discarding multi-SNP draws.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are aligned to a single unmodified reference genome (e.g., STAR on hg19 only) — uniqueness across both haplotype-modified genomes cannot be assessed and majority voting over phased SNPs is not meaningful No phased per-sample VCF genotype data are available, so haplotype-modified personal genomes cannot be constructed The heterozygous SNPs of interest are inside alternative exons or too distant from the AS event to appear on short RNA-seq reads — reads cannot be allele-assigned for PAIRADISE analysis

skills.description: Use when validating or benchmarking a cell-type annotation method on external harmonized snRNA-seq query datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas 10x (76,533 nuclei) and Smart-seq (49,495 nuclei) sets.
skills.name: allen-brain-atlas-dataset-handling
skills.search_text: allen-brain-atlas-dataset-handling Use when validating or benchmarking a cell-type annotation method on external harmonized snRNA-seq query datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas 10x (76,533 nuclei) and Smart-seq (49,495 nuclei) sets. Query data are disease snRNA-seq profiles — the paper notes disease expression deviates substantially from normal data and recommends users train on their own disease data rather than the pre-trained atlas models The goal is annotation of non-human species — transfer of SELINA to other species is anticipated but not demonstrated in the paper Cell types of interest have fewer than 1,000 cells in the query dataset, since the benchmark restricts to types with >1,000 cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Workflow for benchmarking cell-type annotation on external harmonized snRNA-seq data from the Allen Brain Atlas: filter to cell types with >1,000 cells, preprocess with SELINA, predict with pre-trained models, and score accuracy/MacroF1 against comparator tools. Used to validate SELINA on data outside its training atlas (93.32% accuracy, MacroF1 0.9336, rank 2 of 9 tools). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Workflow for benchmarking cell-type annotation on external harmonized snRNA-seq data from the Allen Brain Atlas: filter to cell types with >1,000 cells, preprocess with SELINA, predict with pre-trained models, and score accuracy/MacroF1 against comparator tools. Used to validate SELINA on data outside its training atlas (93.32% accuracy, MacroF1 0.9336, rank 2 of 9 tools).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data are disease snRNA-seq profiles — the paper notes disease expression deviates substantially from normal data and recommends users train on their own disease data rather than the pre-trained atlas models The goal is annotation of non-human species — transfer of SELINA to other species is anticipated but not demonstrated in the paper Cell types of interest have fewer than 1,000 cells in the query dataset, since the benchmark restricts to types with >1,000 cells

skills.description: Use when a reference-free or reference-based deconvolution yields an unlabeled cell type whose spatial localization is plausible but whose identity needs independent validation via in situ hybridization gene expression patterns.
skills.name: allen-brain-atlas-ish-cross-validation
skills.search_text: allen-brain-atlas-ish-cross-validation Use when a reference-free or reference-based deconvolution yields an unlabeled cell type whose spatial localization is plausible but whose identity needs independent validation via in situ hybridization gene expression patterns. The cell type's top genes have no in situ hybridization data available in Allen Brain Atlas (e.g. non-brain tissue or poorly characterized genes) The deconvolution produced no spatially coherent cell type, so there is no spatial pattern to compare against ISH anatomy A curated single-cell reference with confident cell-type annotations already exists, making ISH cross-validation redundant for annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Validate a deconvolved cell type by extracting its top upregulated genes (e.g. Sox11, Nrep, Dcx for STdeconvolve MOB cluster X7) and cross-checking their spatial expression against Allen Brain Atlas in situ hybridization images. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Validate a deconvolved cell type by extracting its top upregulated genes (e.g. Sox11, Nrep, Dcx for STdeconvolve MOB cluster X7) and cross-checking their spatial expression against Allen Brain Atlas in situ hybridization images.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell type's top genes have no in situ hybridization data available in Allen Brain Atlas (e.g. non-brain tissue or poorly characterized genes) The deconvolution produced no spatially coherent cell type, so there is no spatial pattern to compare against ISH anatomy A curated single-cell reference with confident cell-type annotations already exists, making ISH cross-validation redundant for annotation

skills.description: Use when evaluating 2D scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., MDS/UMAP/t-SNE of 2000/4000/10000 highly variable genes) for trajectory inference suitability by quantifying cell coverage area as the alpha-convex hull proportion of the minimum enclosing circle (GOF).
skills.name: alpha-convex-hull-density-quantification
skills.search_text: alpha-convex-hull-density-quantification Use when evaluating 2D scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., MDS/UMAP/t-SNE of 2000/4000/10000 highly variable genes) for trajectory inference suitability by quantifying cell coverage area as the alpha-convex hull proportion of the minimum enclosing circle (GOF). The embedding shows newly disconnected clusters — DCcheck classifies it immediately as not recommended, so GOF/density quantification is not the appropriate next step. The trajectory inference approach does not use a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers two-dimensional embeddings. The embedding derives from RNA velocity-based dimension reduction — not yet implemented in Escort's framework. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Escort's GOF component quantifies how densely a 2D single-cell embedding covers its space, computed as the alpha-convex hull area of cells relative to the minimum enclosing circle area. This coverage-area proportion feeds Escort's benchmark score (range −∞ to 2; >0 recommended) for judging embedding suitability for trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Escort's GOF component quantifies how densely a 2D single-cell embedding covers its space, computed as the alpha-convex hull area of cells relative to the minimum enclosing circle area. This coverage-area proportion feeds Escort's benchmark score (range −∞ to 2; >0 recommended) for judging embedding suitability for trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The embedding shows newly disconnected clusters — DCcheck classifies it immediately as not recommended, so GOF/density quantification is not the appropriate next step. The trajectory inference approach does not use a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers two-dimensional embeddings. The embedding derives from RNA velocity-based dimension reduction — not yet implemented in Escort's framework.

skills.description: Use when running cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) on a cell-cell kNN graph and an alpha value weighting attribute similarity must be chosen from multiple candidate partitions.
skills.name: alpha-parameter-optimization-purity-modularity
skills.search_text: alpha-parameter-optimization-purity-modularity Use when running cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) on a cell-cell kNN graph and an alpha value weighting attribute similarity must be chosen from multiple candidate partitions. Cell types are already strongly clustered so attribute-aware weighting adds little; the article notes ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog is more pronounced in studies with weaker clustering structure Single fixed-alpha exploratory clustering where a full 900-run alpha sweep is computationally prohibitive (ELVAR has increased runtimes compared to Milo or the Louvain-analog) The graph lacks a meaningful cell attribute (e.g. no condition/phenotype label), since alpha weighting on a degenerate attribute cannot improve community detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the optimal EVA alpha parameter (weight on cell-attribute similarity in the Extended Louvain objective) by running Eva_partitions over alpha = 0.1–0.9 with ~100 repeats each, then applying SelOptAlpha to pick the alpha whose partitions combine high purity and modularity with a cluster count that departs from the Louvain baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Selects the optimal EVA alpha parameter (weight on cell-attribute similarity in the Extended Louvain objective) by running Eva_partitions over alpha = 0.1–0.9 with ~100 repeats each, then applying SelOptAlpha to pick the alpha whose partitions combine high purity and modularity with a cluster count that departs from the Louvain baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types are already strongly clustered so attribute-aware weighting adds little; the article notes ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog is more pronounced in studies with weaker clustering structure Single fixed-alpha exploratory clustering where a full 900-run alpha sweep is computationally prohibitive (ELVAR has increased runtimes compared to Milo or the Louvain-analog) The graph lacks a meaningful cell attribute (e.g. no condition/phenotype label), since alpha weighting on a degenerate attribute cannot improve community detection

skills.description: Use when you need to choose a maximum α for ClonoCluster hybrid clustering such that cluster number remains comparable to standard transcriptome clustering while still showing significant reorganization.
skills.name: alpha-parameter-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: alpha-parameter-sweep-analysis Use when you need to choose a maximum α for ClonoCluster hybrid clustering such that cluster number remains comparable to standard transcriptome clustering while still showing significant reorganization. When no clone barcode table exists for the cells — α weighting of clone edges is meaningless without barcode assignments When cell fate is largely extrinsically determined (e.g. cardiomyocyte-directed iPSCs or low-dose vemurafenib samples), where clonal information provides limited benefit and marker fidelity can decrease at high α http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A procedure from the ClonoCluster paper for sweeping the hybrid-clustering weighting parameter α over a grid (seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)), plotting the number of clusters returned at each α, and using the inflection point to select a sample-specific 'high α' (with 'low α' set at half of it) that keeps hybrid cluster counts comparable to transcriptome-only clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: A procedure from the ClonoCluster paper for sweeping the hybrid-clustering weighting parameter α over a grid (seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)), plotting the number of clusters returned at each α, and using the inflection point to select a sample-specific 'high α' (with 'low α' set at half of it) that keeps hybrid cluster counts comparable to transcriptome-only clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no clone barcode table exists for the cells — α weighting of clone edges is meaningless without barcode assignments When cell fate is largely extrinsically determined (e.g. cardiomyocyte-directed iPSCs or low-dose vemurafenib samples), where clonal information provides limited benefit and marker fidelity can decrease at high α

skills.description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq) contains abundant false zeros and you need zero-preserving imputation, or when validating imputation against RNA FISH Gini-coefficient correlations.
skills.name: alra-low-rank-imputation
skills.search_text: alra-low-rank-imputation Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq) contains abundant false zeros and you need zero-preserving imputation, or when validating imputation against RNA FISH Gini-coefficient correlations. The input contains no zeros to impute, e.g. it is already a completed or FISH-scale measurement matrix rather than a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix Preserving exact zero values is not required and non-zero-preservation methods such as MAGIC/DCA (which output a matrix in which every gene is expressed in every cell) are acceptable The dataset is so large that runtime matters and rpca-mkl is unavailable; the article notes SAVER and scImpute 'may be extremely slow on scRNA-seq datasets with over 100,000 cells', but very large matrices still benefit from the MKL-accelerated path http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation) imputes technical zeros ('dropouts') in scRNA-seq expression matrices via randomized SVD low-rank approximation while preserving true biological zeros through per-gene adaptive thresholding. This skill applies ALRA to normalized single-cell data and validates imputation quality against orthogonal measurements such as RNA FISH Gini coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation) imputes technical zeros ('dropouts') in scRNA-seq expression matrices via randomized SVD low-rank approximation while preserving true biological zeros through per-gene adaptive thresholding. This skill applies ALRA to normalized single-cell data and validates imputation quality against orthogonal measurements such as RNA FISH Gini coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input contains no zeros to impute, e.g. it is already a completed or FISH-scale measurement matrix rather than a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix Preserving exact zero values is not required and non-zero-preservation methods such as MAGIC/DCA (which output a matrix in which every gene is expressed in every cell) are acceptable The dataset is so large that runtime matters and rpca-mkl is unavailable; the article notes SAVER and scImpute 'may be extremely slow on scRNA-seq datasets with over 100,000 cells', but very large matrices still benefit from the MKL-accelerated path

skills.description: Use when running ALRA (or a similar low-rank scRNA-seq imputation) on a library/log-normalized expression matrix and an automatic, data-driven rank k must be chosen instead of hand-tuning.
skills.name: alra-rank-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: alra-rank-parameter-selection Use when running ALRA (or a similar low-rank scRNA-seq imputation) on a library/log-normalized expression matrix and an automatic, data-driven rank k must be chosen instead of hand-tuning. You already have a biologically justified k for the dataset and want to supply it explicitly to alra(A_norm, k=...) rather than adaptively estimate it The input is raw counts not yet library/log-normalized (normalize_data: 10,000 transcripts per cell, pseudocount 1, log-transform) — choose_k assumes the normalized matrix The dataset's signal spectrum extends beyond the top-100 singular values, since the criterion only examines spacings among the top 100 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 ALRA's automatic selection of its only free parameter, the rank k of the low-rank approximation, via the spacings between the top-100 singular values rather than the spectrum itself. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: ALRA's automatic selection of its only free parameter, the rank k of the low-rank approximation, via the spacings between the top-100 singular values rather than the spectrum itself.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a biologically justified k for the dataset and want to supply it explicitly to alra(A_norm, k=...) rather than adaptively estimate it The input is raw counts not yet library/log-normalized (normalize_data: 10,000 transcripts per cell, pseudocount 1, log-transform) — choose_k assumes the normalized matrix The dataset's signal spectrum extends beyond the top-100 singular values, since the criterion only examines spacings among the top 100

skills.description: Use when novel splice junctions (e.g. novel acceptor/donor events) were detected by a spliced aligner on unmapped reads and you must confirm that an alternative quantifier's refined counts use the identical supporting read set.
skills.name: alt-splicing-event-read-support-verification
skills.search_text: alt-splicing-event-read-support-verification Use when novel splice junctions (e.g. novel acceptor/donor events) were detected by a spliced aligner on unmapped reads and you must confirm that an alternative quantifier's refined counts use the identical supporting read set. When no spliced-aligner realignment of unmapped reads (e.g. STAR star.bam) is available — the --refine step has no novel splice sites to incorporate. When only genome-level alignment counts are needed and no novel or refinement-sensitive splicing events are of interest (a plain align-and-count or fortuna --quant run suffices). http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Verifies that the alignment-free caller fortuna and a spliced aligner (STAR) attribute the exact same set of supporting reads to novel splice-site events, by running fortuna --refine on the STAR realignment of unmapped reads and comparing per-event read support (rebuilding Supplementary Table S4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Verifies that the alignment-free caller fortuna and a spliced aligner (STAR) attribute the exact same set of supporting reads to novel splice-site events, by running fortuna --refine on the STAR realignment of unmapped reads and comparing per-event read support (rebuilding Supplementary Table S4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no spliced-aligner realignment of unmapped reads (e.g. STAR star.bam) is available — the --refine step has no novel splice sites to incorporate. When only genome-level alignment counts are needed and no novel or refinement-sensitive splicing events are of interest (a plain align-and-count or fortuna --quant run suffices).

skills.description: Use when single-cell FASTQ/count data needs gene-expression-defined cell population annotations as one modality-specific clustering input to a mix-and-match integration, prior to NMF splicing subclustering or scTriangulate reconciliation.
skills.name: altanalyze-icgs2-gene-expression-clustering
skills.search_text: altanalyze-icgs2-gene-expression-clustering Use when single-cell FASTQ/count data needs gene-expression-defined cell population annotations as one modality-specific clustering input to a mix-and-match integration, prior to NMF splicing subclustering or scTriangulate reconciliation. When gene-expression population labels already exist (e.g., prior label-transfer annotations) — the ICGS2 clustering step would be redundant and only the decision-level integration applies When the goal is joint embedding-based multimodal integration rather than decision-level mix-and-match — the task card shows Seurat WNN failed to resolve the splicing-defined subpopulations that ICGS2-based populations support When raw counts have not been processed through Cell Ranger to hg19 (or an equivalent genome reference), since ICGS2 expects the aligned expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Defines gene-expression cell populations from single-cell RNA-Seq by running ICGS2 in AltAnalyze with default parameters on Cell Ranger-aligned hg19 count data, producing the RNA-defined annotation layer that downstream decision-level integration (scTriangulate) mixes with splicing-defined subclusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Defines gene-expression cell populations from single-cell RNA-Seq by running ICGS2 in AltAnalyze with default parameters on Cell Ranger-aligned hg19 count data, producing the RNA-defined annotation layer that downstream decision-level integration (scTriangulate) mixes with splicing-defined subclusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene-expression population labels already exist (e.g., prior label-transfer annotations) — the ICGS2 clustering step would be redundant and only the decision-level integration applies When the goal is joint embedding-based multimodal integration rather than decision-level mix-and-match — the task card shows Seurat WNN failed to resolve the splicing-defined subpopulations that ICGS2-based populations support When raw counts have not been processed through Cell Ranger to hg19 (or an equivalent genome reference), since ICGS2 expects the aligned expression matrix

skills.description: Use when factorizing paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g., 10X Multiome RNA/ATAC, CITE-seq ADT) into simplex-constrained dictionaries H(p) and a shared low-dimensional cell embedding W with entropic OT coupling.
skills.name: alternating-dictionary-embedding-minimization
skills.search_text: alternating-dictionary-embedding-minimization Use when factorizing paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g., 10X Multiome RNA/ATAC, CITE-seq ADT) into simplex-constrained dictionaries H(p) and a shared low-dimensional cell embedding W with entropic OT coupling. Data are unpaired (unmatched) multi-omics samples — Mowgli is designed for paired multi-omics integration with any type and number of omics Batch correction across integrated datasets is required — the paper notes Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data GPU resources are unavailable and the dataset is large — OT is inherently expensive to compute compared to Euclidean distance, and GPU availability is required for Mowgli to scale to the larger datasets presented http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Mowgli's core optimization: alternating minimization of the entropic-regularized OT loss (Eq. 5) between modality-specific dictionary matrices H(p) and the shared cell embedding W, solved via L-BFGS on smooth dual problems with softmax recovery of the primal variables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Mowgli's core optimization: alternating minimization of the entropic-regularized OT loss (Eq. 5) between modality-specific dictionary matrices H(p) and the shared cell embedding W, solved via L-BFGS on smooth dual problems with softmax recovery of the primal variables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired (unmatched) multi-omics samples — Mowgli is designed for paired multi-omics integration with any type and number of omics Batch correction across integrated datasets is required — the paper notes Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data GPU resources are unavailable and the dataset is large — OT is inherently expensive to compute compared to Euclidean distance, and GPU availability is required for Mowgli to scale to the larger datasets presented

skills.description: Use when you have scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform count matrices (*.txs.Rds / *.genes.Rds) from 10x 3'-end scRNA-seq data and need to label genes as multi-UTR or IPA and tabulate per-category gene counts.
skills.name: alternative-polyadenylation-gene-classification
skills.search_text: alternative-polyadenylation-gene-classification Use when you have scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform count matrices (*.txs.Rds / *.genes.Rds) from 10x 3'-end scRNA-seq data and need to label genes as multi-UTR or IPA and tabulate per-category gene counts. Input is a gene-level count matrix without 3'UTR isoform resolution — multi-UTR/IPA calls require isoform-fraction quantification from scUTRquant Data are not 3'-end tag-based scRNA-seq libraries compatible with the kallisto-bustools workflow (most 10x reads do not span cleavage sites, so exact de novo CS mapping is not possible) The goal is per-cell-type differential 3'UTR length testing rather than static gene classification — use scUTRboot instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Classifies expressed protein-coding genes as multi-UTR or intronic polyadenylation (IPA) genes by aggregating 3'UTR isoform usage across cell types from scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs and applying a ≥10% isoform-fraction criterion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Classifies expressed protein-coding genes as multi-UTR or intronic polyadenylation (IPA) genes by aggregating 3'UTR isoform usage across cell types from scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs and applying a ≥10% isoform-fraction criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene-level count matrix without 3'UTR isoform resolution — multi-UTR/IPA calls require isoform-fraction quantification from scUTRquant Data are not 3'-end tag-based scRNA-seq libraries compatible with the kallisto-bustools workflow (most 10x reads do not span cleavage sites, so exact de novo CS mapping is not possible) The goal is per-cell-type differential 3'UTR length testing rather than static gene classification — use scUTRboot instead

skills.description: Use when paired-end RNA-Seq from two or more conditions is available and the goal is to detect proximal APA transcripts (shifted/shortened 3' ends) induced by a perturbation, such as knockdown of a polyadenylation factor like CFIm25.
skills.name: alternative-polyadenylation-isoform-comparison
skills.search_text: alternative-polyadenylation-isoform-comparison Use when paired-end RNA-Seq from two or more conditions is available and the goal is to detect proximal APA transcripts (shifted/shortened 3' ends) induced by a perturbation, such as knockdown of a polyadenylation factor like CFIm25. The goal is de novo polyA site prediction without an initial transcriptome: aptardi requires an input transcriptome (GTF/GFF, designed for StringTie output) and only evaluates 3' terminal exons, not intron junctions Only a single condition/sample is available with no comparison transcriptome: isoform-specificity claims from the two-sample comparison cannot be made (use a count threshold filter instead) The question is coding APA within upstream exons: aptardi does not analyze upstream exons, so coding APA cannot be identified http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies sample-specific alternative polyadenylation (APA) transcript isoforms by building sample-specific transcriptomes with aptardi (Mode 1, pre-built model) from HISAT2/SAMtools/StringTie outputs and comparing predicted 3' ends between conditions, e.g. control vs. CFIm25 knockdown HeLa cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Identifies sample-specific alternative polyadenylation (APA) transcript isoforms by building sample-specific transcriptomes with aptardi (Mode 1, pre-built model) from HISAT2/SAMtools/StringTie outputs and comparing predicted 3' ends between conditions, e.g. control vs. CFIm25 knockdown HeLa cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo polyA site prediction without an initial transcriptome: aptardi requires an input transcriptome (GTF/GFF, designed for StringTie output) and only evaluates 3' terminal exons, not intron junctions Only a single condition/sample is available with no comparison transcriptome: isoform-specificity claims from the two-sample comparison cannot be made (use a count threshold filter instead) The question is coding APA within upstream exons: aptardi does not analyze upstream exons, so coding APA cannot be identified

skills.description: Use when RNA-Seq alignments and a reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need to identify expressed polyA sites or refine 3'-terminal exons without 3'-end sequencing data.
skills.name: alternative-polyadenylation-transcript-annotation
skills.search_text: alternative-polyadenylation-transcript-annotation Use when RNA-Seq alignments and a reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need to identify expressed polyA sites or refine 3'-terminal exons without 3'-end sequencing data. You need de novo detection of coding alternative polyadenylation in upstream exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream APA cannot be identified. You require exact single-nucleotide polyA site resolution — aptardi predicts on 100-base bins, though sites wiggle up to ~30 nucleotides. Your input transcriptome has many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and you cannot apply the RSEM-based filtering — aptardi will enumerate redundant aptardi transcripts for each shared isoform. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predict sample-specific polyadenylation (polyA) sites and refine transcript 3'-ends by running aptardi, a supervised machine learning tool that combines RNA-Seq read coverage with genome DNA sequence, and evaluate the predicted bins against polyA-site reference databases (e.g., PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3) with BEDtools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Predict sample-specific polyadenylation (polyA) sites and refine transcript 3'-ends by running aptardi, a supervised machine learning tool that combines RNA-Seq read coverage with genome DNA sequence, and evaluate the predicted bins against polyA-site reference databases (e.g., PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3) with BEDtools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo detection of coding alternative polyadenylation in upstream exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream APA cannot be identified. You require exact single-nucleotide polyA site resolution — aptardi predicts on 100-base bins, though sites wiggle up to ~30 nucleotides. Your input transcriptome has many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and you cannot apply the RSEM-based filtering — aptardi will enumerate redundant aptardi transcripts for each shared isoform.

skills.description: Use when CircAST_result.txt full-length circRNA assemblies exist for an RNase R-treated RNA-seq dataset and you need to count transcripts whose AS events differ from linear cognates or identify novel AS events.
skills.name: alternative-splicing-event-comparison
skills.search_text: alternative-splicing-event-comparison Use when CircAST_result.txt full-length circRNA assemblies exist for an RNase R-treated RNA-seq dataset and you need to count transcripts whose AS events differ from linear cognates or identify novel AS events. Input samples are not RNase R-treated — CircAST applies only to RNase R-treated samples where remnant linear mRNA can generate false circular transcripts, distorting the AS comparison Circular transcripts of interest are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts, so AS comparison against GTF-annotated linear cognates will miss them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Compares alternative splicing (AS) events of CircAST-assembled full-length circular transcripts against their cognate linear transcripts to flag circRNAs whose internal splicing differs, and tallies novel AS events, using the CircAST_result.txt 13-column output. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Compares alternative splicing (AS) events of CircAST-assembled full-length circular transcripts against their cognate linear transcripts to flag circRNAs whose internal splicing differs, and tallies novel AS events, using the CircAST_result.txt 13-column output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are not RNase R-treated — CircAST applies only to RNase R-treated samples where remnant linear mRNA can generate false circular transcripts, distorting the AS comparison Circular transcripts of interest are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts, so AS comparison against GTF-annotated linear cognates will miss them

skills.description: Use when starting from single-cell SMART-seq BAM or junction (SJ.out.tab) files and you need de novo alternative-splicing events and a per-cell AS probability matrix without relying on transcriptome annotation.
skills.name: alternative-splicing-event-identification-from-junction-reads
skills.search_text: alternative-splicing-event-identification-from-junction-reads Use when starting from single-cell SMART-seq BAM or junction (SJ.out.tab) files and you need de novo alternative-splicing events and a per-cell AS probability matrix without relying on transcriptome annotation. You already have an AS probability / feature matrix — instead use the demo intermediate files path (data/junction) or downstream imputation and clustering stages directly Input is bulk RNA-seq or requires annotation-dependent PSI estimation (e.g. rMATS-style exon inclusion) — SCASL targets single-cell SMART-seq junction reads and de novo, annotation-free event definition Cell labels are known and the goal is differential splicing between labeled groups — tools like BRIE, Expedition, rMATS, or MARVEL address differential analysis rather than unsupervised AS-based clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 SCASL's first pipeline stage: Leafcutter-style de novo grouping of splicing schemes sharing a common 5' or 3' splice site into AS events from single-cell SMART-seq junction reads, followed by QC and conversion of split-read counts into a cell-by-site AS probability matrix (normalized_matrix). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: SCASL's first pipeline stage: Leafcutter-style de novo grouping of splicing schemes sharing a common 5' or 3' splice site into AS events from single-cell SMART-seq junction reads, followed by QC and conversion of split-read counts into a cell-by-site AS probability matrix (normalized_matrix).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have an AS probability / feature matrix — instead use the demo intermediate files path (data/junction) or downstream imputation and clustering stages directly Input is bulk RNA-seq or requires annotation-dependent PSI estimation (e.g. rMATS-style exon inclusion) — SCASL targets single-cell SMART-seq junction reads and de novo, annotation-free event definition Cell labels are known and the goal is differential splicing between labeled groups — tools like BRIE, Expedition, rMATS, or MARVEL address differential analysis rather than unsupervised AS-based clustering

skills.description: Use when an sRNA-seq analysis needs to distinguish PHAS loci predicted on transcript isoforms versus genomic sequence, e.g. to detect isoform-specific phasiRNA loss caused by alternative splicing or intron clipping.
skills.name: alternative-splicing-phasirna-isoform-interpretation
skills.search_text: alternative-splicing-phasirna-isoform-interpretation Use when an sRNA-seq analysis needs to distinguish PHAS loci predicted on transcript isoforms versus genomic sequence, e.g. to detect isoform-specific phasiRNA loss caused by alternative splicing or intron clipping. The goal is degradome target or initiator (trigger miRNA) prediction rather than isoform-level phasiRNA interpretation — use phasiHunter target/initiator/deg modules instead The sRNA data are already clean and abundance-filtered with no reference transcriptome available, so isoform-level (cDNA vs gDNA) comparison cannot be made Input is a single-reference workflow where only genome-based PHAS loci are needed and no transcript isoform distinction is sought (integration with -g y would discard only-P results) http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Interprets PhasiHunter's integrated genome- and transcriptome-based phasiRNA predictions to identify phasiRNAs arising specifically through alternative splicing, using the maize gene LOC103650958 as the demonstration case where four transcript isoforms exist but one isoform cannot generate phasiRNAs due to intron clipping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Interprets PhasiHunter's integrated genome- and transcriptome-based phasiRNA predictions to identify phasiRNAs arising specifically through alternative splicing, using the maize gene LOC103650958 as the demonstration case where four transcript isoforms exist but one isoform cannot generate phasiRNAs due to intron clipping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is degradome target or initiator (trigger miRNA) prediction rather than isoform-level phasiRNA interpretation — use phasiHunter target/initiator/deg modules instead The sRNA data are already clean and abundance-filtered with no reference transcriptome available, so isoform-level (cDNA vs gDNA) comparison cannot be made Input is a single-reference workflow where only genome-based PHAS loci are needed and no transcript isoform distinction is sought (integration with -g y would discard only-P results)

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq alignments are available and the neoantigen-prediction goal requires capturing alternative-splicing-derived variants (beyond SNV/indel calling), i.e., when the altsplicing module's activate flag is set in config/config.yml.
skills.name: alternative-splicing-vcf-conversion
skills.search_text: alternative-splicing-vcf-conversion Use when RNA-seq alignments are available and the neoantigen-prediction goal requires capturing alternative-splicing-derived variants (beyond SNV/indel calling), i.e., when the altsplicing module's activate flag is set in config/config.yml. The variant of interest is an exitron-splicing event — use the ScanExitron module (exitrons.vcf.gz) instead of SplAdder conversion Only SNV or short-indel calling is needed — the GATK Mutect2 module on DNA/RNA BAMs covers this without splice-graph conversion RNA-seq data are absent or too low quality to support splice-junction quantification (SplAdder depends on informative alignments) http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts SplAdder splice-graph output from RNA-seq alignments into standardized VCFs of alternative-splicing-derived neoantigen candidates within the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, annotating each record with GRP (group) and SRC (caller source) INFO keys so downstream peptide extraction can trace neoantigen provenance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Converts SplAdder splice-graph output from RNA-seq alignments into standardized VCFs of alternative-splicing-derived neoantigen candidates within the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, annotating each record with GRP (group) and SRC (caller source) INFO keys so downstream peptide extraction can trace neoantigen provenance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant of interest is an exitron-splicing event — use the ScanExitron module (exitrons.vcf.gz) instead of SplAdder conversion Only SNV or short-indel calling is needed — the GATK Mutect2 module on DNA/RNA BAMs covers this without splice-graph conversion RNA-seq data are absent or too low quality to support splice-junction quantification (SplAdder depends on informative alignments)

skills.description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods on a disease dataset and you need biological evidence that one imputed matrix preserves or clarifies disease-relevant DEG patterns and KEGG pathways.
skills.name: alzheimer-disease-pathway-interpretation
skills.search_text: alzheimer-disease-pathway-interpretation Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods on a disease dataset and you need biological evidence that one imputed matrix preserves or clarifies disease-relevant DEG patterns and KEGG pathways. Your goal is a quantitative clustering or imputation-error benchmark rather than biological pathway interpretation of DEGs. The dataset is not a disease-annotated scRNA-seq study (e.g. the AD/adam dataset); KEGG disease-pathway recovery will not be interpretable. You lack imputed variants of the same matrix — the skill requires side-by-side raw vs. imputed DEG comparisons. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Interpret imputation quality biologically by running Wilcoxon differential expression (scanpy rank_genes_groups) on raw, GraphSCI-imputed, and scGCL-imputed Alzheimer's disease (adam) expression matrices, then running KEGG pathway enrichment on each DEG list to see which imputation best recovers disease pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Interpret imputation quality biologically by running Wilcoxon differential expression (scanpy rank_genes_groups) on raw, GraphSCI-imputed, and scGCL-imputed Alzheimer's disease (adam) expression matrices, then running KEGG pathway enrichment on each DEG list to see which imputation best recovers disease pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is a quantitative clustering or imputation-error benchmark rather than biological pathway interpretation of DEGs. The dataset is not a disease-annotated scRNA-seq study (e.g. the AD/adam dataset); KEGG disease-pathway recovery will not be interpretable. You lack imputed variants of the same matrix — the skill requires side-by-side raw vs. imputed DEG comparisons.

skills.description: Use when analyzing two-group (case vs control) single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., late-stage AD vs healthy human brain — to infer differential cell-cell communication networks and rank the most active communicating cell types.
skills.name: alzheimer-disease-scrnaseq-analysis
skills.search_text: alzheimer-disease-scrnaseq-analysis Use when analyzing two-group (case vs control) single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., late-stage AD vs healthy human brain — to infer differential cell-cell communication networks and rank the most active communicating cell types. Input is developmental series scRNA-seq (multiple sequential time points) where the goal is temporal trajectory analysis via developcorrelation and fuzzy clustering rather than a two-group case/control comparison The dataset is not membrane/secreted protein-mediated communication analysis — e.g., intracellular signaling or gene regulatory network inference, since dsCellNet identifies interactions according to protein localizations Only a single condition is available and no control/treatment time-point pair exists for comparednet http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply the dsCellNet R package's two-group comparison (comparednet) to human brain scRNA-seq from six late-stage Alzheimer's disease patients and six healthy controls (GSE174367) to identify which immune cell types drive interactions increased in AD brains. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Apply the dsCellNet R package's two-group comparison (comparednet) to human brain scRNA-seq from six late-stage Alzheimer's disease patients and six healthy controls (GSE174367) to identify which immune cell types drive interactions increased in AD brains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is developmental series scRNA-seq (multiple sequential time points) where the goal is temporal trajectory analysis via developcorrelation and fuzzy clustering rather than a two-group case/control comparison The dataset is not membrane/secreted protein-mediated communication analysis — e.g., intracellular signaling or gene regulatory network inference, since dsCellNet identifies interactions according to protein localizations Only a single condition is available and no control/treatment time-point pair exists for comparednet

skills.description: Use when the task is to identify disease-specific (e.g., Alzheimer's vs normal) biomarkers from brain-region scRNA-seq datasets with scaLR's DNN-based pipeline and validate top-ranked genes against known neurological-disorder marker sets.
skills.name: alzheimer-scrnaseq-dataset-analysis
skills.search_text: alzheimer-scrnaseq-dataset-analysis Use when the task is to identify disease-specific (e.g., Alzheimer's vs normal) biomarkers from brain-region scRNA-seq datasets with scaLR's DNN-based pipeline and validate top-ranked genes against known neurological-disorder marker sets. The analysis goal is cell-type annotation rather than disease-vs-control biomarker discovery (use scaLR's cell-type classification config with target: cell_type instead) The dataset is not a two-class disease-vs-control design — DGE analysis via DgePseudoBulk/DgeLMEM and ClasswisePromoters selection assume distinguishable condition categories Comparison tool outputs lack feature-importance extraction (e.g., scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM), so biomarker ranking cannot be reproduced there http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reproduces scaLR's disease-vs-control biomarker discovery on Alzheimer's disease brain scRNA-seq datasets (human brain superior frontal gyrus, HBSFG, and prefrontal cortex, HBPFC), ranking disease-associated genes and validating the top hits against neurological-disorder gene references from CellMarker2.0. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Reproduces scaLR's disease-vs-control biomarker discovery on Alzheimer's disease brain scRNA-seq datasets (human brain superior frontal gyrus, HBSFG, and prefrontal cortex, HBPFC), ranking disease-associated genes and validating the top hits against neurological-disorder gene references from CellMarker2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is cell-type annotation rather than disease-vs-control biomarker discovery (use scaLR's cell-type classification config with target: cell_type instead) The dataset is not a two-class disease-vs-control design — DGE analysis via DgePseudoBulk/DgeLMEM and ClasswisePromoters selection assume distinguishable condition categories Comparison tool outputs lack feature-importance extraction (e.g., scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM), so biomarker ranking cannot be reproduced there

skills.description: Use when two (or more) independently constructed co-expression networks exist — e.g. 5xFAD vs 3xTg-AD module-assignment tables — and the goal is to flag module pairs with significant gene overlap indicating conserved co-expression.
skills.name: alzheimers-model-network-conservation-analysis
skills.search_text: alzheimers-model-network-conservation-analysis Use when two (or more) independently constructed co-expression networks exist — e.g. 5xFAD vs 3xTg-AD module-assignment tables — and the goal is to flag module pairs with significant gene overlap indicating conserved co-expression. Only one WGCNA network is available and there is no second dataset or external gene list to compare against — module comparison requires two or more objects. You are still constructing the networks themselves (module detection) rather than comparing already-built module assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compare co-expression modules built from two independent WGCNA networks — here the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq datasets — using PyWGCNA's module-comparison routine to detect shared co-expression signatures via Jaccard similarity and Fisher's exact test overlap significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Compare co-expression modules built from two independent WGCNA networks — here the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq datasets — using PyWGCNA's module-comparison routine to detect shared co-expression signatures via Jaccard similarity and Fisher's exact test overlap significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one WGCNA network is available and there is no second dataset or external gene list to compare against — module comparison requires two or more objects. You are still constructing the networks themselves (module detection) rather than comparing already-built module assignments.

skills.description: Use when you have raw ADT/UMI count matrices from both empty droplets and cell-containing droplets (e.g. raw vs filtered Cell Ranger output from a CITE-seq run) and need to characterize or validate ambient, unbound antibody background per protein.
skills.name: ambient-antibody-noise-quantification-from-empty-droplets
skills.search_text: ambient-antibody-noise-quantification-from-empty-droplets Use when you have raw ADT/UMI count matrices from both empty droplets and cell-containing droplets (e.g. raw vs filtered Cell Ranger output from a CITE-seq run) and need to characterize or validate ambient, unbound antibody background per protein. The dataset has no empty droplets available (use the dsb 'no empty drops' strategy / ModelNegativeADTnorm or define background from the modeled negative population instead) The ADT matrix is already dsb-normalized or CLR-normalized — the correlation must be computed on raw counts with log10(count+1) transformation Proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells) — the paper removes such proteins (e.g. CD34) prior to normalization Quantifies protein-specific ambient antibody noise in CITE-seq by computing per-antibody mean log10(count+1) in empty droplets and cell-containing droplets, then correlating the two vectors to demonstrate that background ADT levels in empty droplets closely match levels in cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Quantifies protein-specific ambient antibody noise in CITE-seq by computing per-antibody mean log10(count+1) in empty droplets and cell-containing droplets, then correlating the two vectors to demonstrate that background ADT levels in empty droplets closely match levels in cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no empty droplets available (use the dsb 'no empty drops' strategy / ModelNegativeADTnorm or define background from the modeled negative population instead) The ADT matrix is already dsb-normalized or CLR-normalized — the correlation must be computed on raw counts with log10(count+1) transformation Proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells) — the paper removes such proteins (e.g. CD34) prior to normalization

skills.description: Use when normalizing raw ADT/protein UMI matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq droplet experiments where ambient unbound antibody noise and per-cell technical noise must be removed before clustering.
skills.name: ambient-background-noise-standardization-citeseq-protein-counts
skills.search_text: ambient-background-noise-standardization-citeseq-protein-counts Use when normalizing raw ADT/protein UMI matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq droplet experiments where ambient unbound antibody noise and per-cell technical noise must be removed before clustering. Input is a dataset with no empty droplets available — use the dsb variant without empty drops (vignette 'Using dsb when empty droplets are not available') instead of the standard empty-droplet Step I Datasets lacking isotype control antibody measurements — the technical component definition requires caveats described in the dsb documentation and Supplementary Note Proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells) should be removed prior to normalization rather than passed through the pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Two-step normalization of droplet-based protein (ADT) counts: Step I removes protein-specific ambient antibody noise using empty-droplet statistics, and Step II removes cell-intrinsic technical noise via a Gaussian-mixture-derived technical component regressed out with limma. This is the dsb method (Mulè, Martins & Tsang, Nat Commun 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Two-step normalization of droplet-based protein (ADT) counts: Step I removes protein-specific ambient antibody noise using empty-droplet statistics, and Step II removes cell-intrinsic technical noise via a Gaussian-mixture-derived technical component regressed out with limma. This is the dsb method (Mulè, Martins & Tsang, Nat Commun 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a dataset with no empty droplets available — use the dsb variant without empty drops (vignette 'Using dsb when empty droplets are not available') instead of the standard empty-droplet Step I Datasets lacking isotype control antibody measurements — the technical component definition requires caveats described in the dsb documentation and Supplementary Note Proteins with very low signal (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells) should be removed prior to normalization rather than passed through the pipeline

skills.description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen where ambient (extracellular) gRNA UMIs must be distinguished from endogenous in-cell expression before calling singlets vs multiplets, and per-guide thresholds are preferable to a fixed UMI cutoff.
skills.name: ambient-grna-noise-separation
