skills.search_text: ambient-grna-noise-separation Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen where ambient (extracellular) gRNA UMIs must be distinguished from endogenous in-cell expression before calling singlets vs multiplets, and per-guide thresholds are preferable to a fixed UMI cutoff. When benchmarking against published studies that used ad hoc customized pipelines with fixed thresholds — the article notes such fixed thresholds render head-to-head comparisons unfeasible, so mode choice must match the reference protocol When the input lacks per-cell per-gRNA UMI counts (e.g. only raw FASTQ or expression counts are available) — upstream GiRAFR steps (consensus sequence construction, variant calling) must run first When analyzing CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing in transcriptome data — that is a separate GiRAFR analysis mode, not cell assignment Performs Step 4 of the GiRAFR pipeline — assigning gRNAs to single cells — by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model per gRNA over pooled intact and mutant UMI counts to derive a dynamic per-guide UMI threshold that separates endogenous in-cell UMIs from ambient artifacts, with a fixed min_umi=3 fallback. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Performs Step 4 of the GiRAFR pipeline — assigning gRNAs to single cells — by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model per gRNA over pooled intact and mutant UMI counts to derive a dynamic per-guide UMI threshold that separates endogenous in-cell UMIs from ambient artifacts, with a fixed min_umi=3 fallback.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When benchmarking against published studies that used ad hoc customized pipelines with fixed thresholds — the article notes such fixed thresholds render head-to-head comparisons unfeasible, so mode choice must match the reference protocol When the input lacks per-cell per-gRNA UMI counts (e.g. only raw FASTQ or expression counts are available) — upstream GiRAFR steps (consensus sequence construction, variant calling) must run first When analyzing CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing in transcriptome data — that is a separate GiRAFR analysis mode, not cell assignment

skills.description: Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) show substantial background noise from unbound antibodies and per-cell technical variation, and you need denoised, normalized protein values for downstream clustering or multimodal analysis.
skills.name: ambient-noise-correction-citeseq
skills.search_text: ambient-noise-correction-citeseq Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) show substantial background noise from unbound antibodies and per-cell technical variation, and you need denoised, normalized protein values for downstream clustering or multimodal analysis. The dataset has no empty droplets and no isotype controls — use the 'no_empty_drops' dsb vignette workflow instead, since dsb step I requires a background definition and caveats for missing isotypes are deferred to the Supplementary Note Proteins have very low signal (maximum UMI count < 5 across all cells) and were not pre-filtered — these should be removed before normalization You need raw protein counts or a sample-barcode demultiplexing method (MULTI-seq, demuxlet) rather than ADT noise correction http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Two-step ADT normalization for droplet-based protein data (CITE-seq and related assays): dsb step I removes protein-specific ambient antibody noise using empty droplets, and step II models per-cell background with a Gaussian mixture to remove cell-intrinsic technical noise via a technical component regressed out of the data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Two-step ADT normalization for droplet-based protein data (CITE-seq and related assays): dsb step I removes protein-specific ambient antibody noise using empty droplets, and step II models per-cell background with a Gaussian mixture to remove cell-intrinsic technical noise via a technical component regressed out of the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no empty droplets and no isotype controls — use the 'no_empty_drops' dsb vignette workflow instead, since dsb step I requires a background definition and caveats for missing isotypes are deferred to the Supplementary Note Proteins have very low signal (maximum UMI count < 5 across all cells) and were not pre-filtered — these should be removed before normalization You need raw protein counts or a sample-barcode demultiplexing method (MULTI-seq, demuxlet) rather than ADT noise correction

skills.description: Use when comparing ADT normalization strategies (CLR vs dsb) for residual ambient antibody noise, or when assessing whether a protein cluster's normalized values track empty-droplet background levels.
skills.name: ambient-noise-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: ambient-noise-correlation-analysis Use when comparing ADT normalization strategies (CLR vs dsb) for residual ambient antibody noise, or when assessing whether a protein cluster's normalized values track empty-droplet background levels. Dataset lacks empty droplets or the raw (unfiltered) Cell Ranger output, since the 98th-percentile empty-droplet background estimate cannot be computed Goal is RNA-only analysis with no ADT/protein modality, since ambient antibody noise is specific to ADT counts Data are flow cytometry, bulk, or plate-based where droplet-encapsulated unbound antibody noise does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Quantifies ambient antibody noise retained in CLR-normalized ADT values by correlating per-protein median normalized values of a target WNN cluster against the 98th percentile of empty-droplet expression, demonstrating dsb removes this correlation. Grounded in the CD14+ CD86-high monocyte cluster 3 case study from Kotliarov et al. PBMC CITE-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Quantifies ambient antibody noise retained in CLR-normalized ADT values by correlating per-protein median normalized values of a target WNN cluster against the 98th percentile of empty-droplet expression, demonstrating dsb removes this correlation. Grounded in the CD14+ CD86-high monocyte cluster 3 case study from Kotliarov et al. PBMC CITE-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset lacks empty droplets or the raw (unfiltered) Cell Ranger output, since the 98th-percentile empty-droplet background estimate cannot be computed Goal is RNA-only analysis with no ADT/protein modality, since ambient antibody noise is specific to ADT counts Data are flow cytometry, bulk, or plate-based where droplet-encapsulated unbound antibody noise does not apply

skills.description: Use when filtering a raw 10X droplet count matrix (feature-barcode MTX) for ambient RNA/debris contamination, especially snRNA-seq from frozen tissue, or when comparing DIEM vs EmptyDrops kept-droplet sets using MT% and MALAT1% metrics.
skills.name: ambient-rna-debris-filtering
skills.search_text: ambient-rna-debris-filtering Use when filtering a raw 10X droplet count matrix (feature-barcode MTX) for ambient RNA/debris contamination, especially snRNA-seq from frozen tissue, or when comparing DIEM vs EmptyDrops kept-droplet sets using MT% and MALAT1% metrics. When the input is already a filtered feature table or Seurat object of retained cells — DIEM operates on the full raw droplet matrix during pre-processing When debris-enriched genes are absent (little or no genes increased in the background distribution), the debris score will likely be inaccurate When comparing debris scores across independent samples for integration — scores are normalized within-sample and may not be on the same scale http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Filter debris-contaminated droplets from droplet-based scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data using DIEM's likelihood-based multinomial mixture model with semi-supervised EM, optionally benchmarked against EmptyDrops. DIEM identifies droplets containing extranuclear/ambient RNA that hard UMI cutoffs retain, improving downstream cluster quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Filter debris-contaminated droplets from droplet-based scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data using DIEM's likelihood-based multinomial mixture model with semi-supervised EM, optionally benchmarked against EmptyDrops. DIEM identifies droplets containing extranuclear/ambient RNA that hard UMI cutoffs retain, improving downstream cluster quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a filtered feature table or Seurat object of retained cells — DIEM operates on the full raw droplet matrix during pre-processing When debris-enriched genes are absent (little or no genes increased in the background distribution), the debris score will likely be inaccurate When comparing debris scores across independent samples for integration — scores are normalized within-sample and may not be on the same scale

skills.description: Use when 10x Genomics droplet UMI count matrices (e.g., parsed from molecule information files of HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be separated into real cells versus empty droplets at a specified FDR.
skills.name: ambient-rna-fdr-threshold-testing
skills.search_text: ambient-rna-fdr-threshold-testing Use when 10x Genomics droplet UMI count matrices (e.g., parsed from molecule information files of HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be separated into real cells versus empty droplets at a specified FDR. Input is plate-based scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-seq2 plate datasets such as Nestorowa GSE81682 or the Richard mouse T-cell plates) — there are no empty droplets or ambient profile for emptyDrops to test against. Barcodes shared between samples have not yet been removed from multiplexed HiSeq 4000 10x data — apply cell exclusion first, since swapped molecules can produce artefactual cell libraries that would distort the calls. The input is already a matrix of called cells from a prior cell-calling step — re-running emptyDrops at FDR 0.01 would double-call rather than filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical cell calling for 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq: emptyDrops (DropletUtils) tests each barcode's expression profile for significant deviation from the ambient profile, calling cells at FDR 0.01 with a minimum cell size of 1000 UMIs on the HiSeq 4000-sequenced mouse epithelial samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Statistical cell calling for 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq: emptyDrops (DropletUtils) tests each barcode's expression profile for significant deviation from the ambient profile, calling cells at FDR 0.01 with a minimum cell size of 1000 UMIs on the HiSeq 4000-sequenced mouse epithelial samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is plate-based scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-seq2 plate datasets such as Nestorowa GSE81682 or the Richard mouse T-cell plates) — there are no empty droplets or ambient profile for emptyDrops to test against. Barcodes shared between samples have not yet been removed from multiplexed HiSeq 4000 10x data — apply cell exclusion first, since swapped molecules can produce artefactual cell libraries that would distort the calls. The input is already a matrix of called cells from a prior cell-calling step — re-running emptyDrops at FDR 0.01 would double-call rather than filter.

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., a list of per-donor gene-by-cell count matrices) must be turned into marker-labeled approximated ground-truth cell identities for adjusted-Rand-index clustering benchmarks.
skills.name: ambiguous-cell-removal
skills.search_text: ambiguous-cell-removal Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., a list of per-donor gene-by-cell count matrices) must be turned into marker-labeled approximated ground-truth cell identities for adjusted-Rand-index clustering benchmarks. When the goal is rare cell type identification — the authors note that filtering genes with excessive zeros 'may be problematic for rare cell type identification' When cells already have curated or authoritative ground-truth labels and marker-based approximated labels would only add noise When the input is already a filtered feature table rather than raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Preprocesses real droplet-based scRNA-seq datasets (human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin) by filtering lowly-expressed genes, selecting the top 1000 HVGs, scoring cell-type marker panels, and removing cells whose marker signals do not support an unambiguous type so the surviving cells serve as approximated ground truth for clustering benchmarking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Preprocesses real droplet-based scRNA-seq datasets (human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin) by filtering lowly-expressed genes, selecting the top 1000 HVGs, scoring cell-type marker panels, and removing cells whose marker signals do not support an unambiguous type so the surviving cells serve as approximated ground truth for clustering benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is rare cell type identification — the authors note that filtering genes with excessive zeros 'may be problematic for rare cell type identification' When cells already have curated or authoritative ground-truth labels and marker-based approximated labels would only add noise When the input is already a filtered feature table rather than raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals

skills.description: Use when an Excel-processed gene list contains date-converted symbols Mar-01 or Mar-02 that cannot be uniquely mapped to a single HGNC gene, and MTARC vs MARCHF assignment must be resolved from context.
skills.name: ambiguous-date-term-disambiguation-marchf-mtarc

The date-converted term is not Mar-01 or Mar-02 (e.g. Dec-01, Sep-01..Sep-15) — these have unique HGNC mappings and are auto-corrected without user assignment. The input file has already been processed with Gene Updater and contains only HGNC-approved symbols. The dataset contains no Excel auto-conversion errors, only old-but-valid gene names needing HGNC updates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Resolves the two Excel date-converted gene terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) that each map ambiguously to two HGNC genes (MTARC1/MARCHF1 and MTARC2/MARCHF2), using user-assigned dropdown widgets in the Gene Updater Streamlit app and gene-description matching. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
skills.summary: Resolves the two Excel date-converted gene terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) that each map ambiguously to two HGNC genes (MTARC1/MARCHF1 and MTARC2/MARCHF2), using user-assigned dropdown widgets in the Gene Updater Streamlit app and gene-description matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The date-converted term is not Mar-01 or Mar-02 (e.g. Dec-01, Sep-01..Sep-15) — these have unique HGNC mappings and are auto-corrected without user assignment. skills.search_text: aml-malignant-cell-annotation Use when a cancer (e.g. AML) 10x scRNA-seq sample needs cell-type annotation plus a malignant vs non-malignant call, and bulk SNVs/CNVs must be linked back to individual cell barcodes and clusters. You have no pre-called variant set — VarTrix does not perform variant calling, so the input VCF must already exist (e.g. from Strelka2 or matched WGS) The data are not 10x scRNA-seq with Cell Ranger CB barcode tags and a Cell Ranger barcodes.tsv, since vartrix requires these exact inputs The goal is pure cell-type annotation of healthy tissue without a malignant/non-malignant question — plain ScType marker scoring (sctype_score) suffices without SNV/CopyKAT steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates AML patient scRNA-seq cell types with ScType and separates malignant from non-malignant populations by combining per-cluster single-cell SNV scores (Strelka2/vartrix) with CopyKAT copy-number calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Annotates AML patient scRNA-seq cell types with ScType and separates malignant from non-malignant populations by combining per-cluster single-cell SNV scores (Strelka2/vartrix) with CopyKAT copy-number calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no pre-called variant set — VarTrix does not perform variant calling, so the input VCF must already exist (e.g. from Strelka2 or matched WGS) The data are not 10x scRNA-seq with Cell Ranger CB barcode tags and a Cell Ranger barcodes.tsv, since vartrix requires these exact inputs The goal is pure cell-type annotation of healthy tissue without a malignant/non-malignant question — plain ScType marker scoring (sctype_score) suffices without SNV/CopyKAT steps

skills.description: Use when AML (or other hematopoietic) scRNA-seq count matrices need imputed surface protein levels to assign malignant cells to myeloid differentiation stages or to flag aberrant immunophenotype clusters such as hyper-CD38.
skills.name: aml-patient-immunophenotype-stratification
skills.search_text: aml-patient-immunophenotype-stratification Use when AML (or other hematopoietic) scRNA-seq count matrices need imputed surface protein levels to assign malignant cells to myeloid differentiation stages or to flag aberrant immunophenotype clusters such as hyper-CD38. Input cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage — the article states 'we have not tried to perform imputation of these immune-related markers on cells that are not of the hematopoietic lineage' Expression data are TPM or RPKM metrics rather than UMI-based counts — prediction accuracy is unknown and cTP-net 'can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based)' The input already contains measured (CITE-seq/REAP-seq) surface protein abundances — imputation is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratifies AML patients by the differentiation stage of their malignant cell-of-origin using cTP-net-imputed surface protein abundances (24-immunophenotype panel) from scRNA-seq, reproducing the van Galen myeloid trajectory CD34+ -> CD38+CD123+ -> CD11c+/CD14+ and detecting aberrant clusters such as the hyper-CD38 immunophenotype in the RUNX1/RUNX1T1-fusion sample AML707B. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Stratifies AML patients by the differentiation stage of their malignant cell-of-origin using cTP-net-imputed surface protein abundances (24-immunophenotype panel) from scRNA-seq, reproducing the van Galen myeloid trajectory CD34+ -> CD38+CD123+ -> CD11c+/CD14+ and detecting aberrant clusters such as the hyper-CD38 immunophenotype in the RUNX1/RUNX1T1-fusion sample AML707B.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage — the article states 'we have not tried to perform imputation of these immune-related markers on cells that are not of the hematopoietic lineage' Expression data are TPM or RPKM metrics rather than UMI-based counts — prediction accuracy is unknown and cTP-net 'can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based)' The input already contains measured (CITE-seq/REAP-seq) surface protein abundances — imputation is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., AML CD34+ aligned with Cell Ranger to hg19) must be split into expression-defined populations plus splice-junction PSI subclusters, and decision-level integration is needed to expose splicing-defined disease subtypes.
skills.name: aml-progenitor-single-cell-preprocessing
skills.search_text: aml-progenitor-single-cell-preprocessing Use when scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., AML CD34+ aligned with Cell Ranger to hg19) must be split into expression-defined populations plus splice-junction PSI subclusters, and decision-level integration is needed to expose splicing-defined disease subtypes. When a joint latent-space integration such as Seurat WNN is expected to suffice and no modality-specific (splicing) subtypes are of interest — the paper reports WNN fails to resolve the splicing-defined subpopulations When the input lacks exon-exon junction counts or PSI-quantifiable splicing events (fewer than 25 cells per event, delta-PSI <= 0.1), since the NMF splicing modality cannot be constructed When cells already carry a single trusted annotation and no conflicting clustering solutions need to be reconciled http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocesses pediatric AML CD34+ single-cell data into gene-expression clusters (ICGS2) and splicing-defined subclusters (NMF on PSI values), then reconciles them with scTriangulate to resolve splicing-defined leukemia blood progenitor subpopulations that Seurat WNN cannot resolve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Preprocesses pediatric AML CD34+ single-cell data into gene-expression clusters (ICGS2) and splicing-defined subclusters (NMF on PSI values), then reconciles them with scTriangulate to resolve splicing-defined leukemia blood progenitor subpopulations that Seurat WNN cannot resolve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a joint latent-space integration such as Seurat WNN is expected to suffice and no modality-specific (splicing) subtypes are of interest — the paper reports WNN fails to resolve the splicing-defined subpopulations When the input lacks exon-exon junction counts or PSI-quantifiable splicing events (fewer than 25 cells per event, delta-PSI <= 0.1), since the NMF splicing modality cannot be constructed When cells already carry a single trusted annotation and no conflicting clustering solutions need to be reconciled

skills.description: Use when you have batches of query sequences (e.g., human RefSeq transcripts in FASTA) and a prebuilt AMQ index over thousands of datasets, and you need to list candidate datasets per query while profiling query runtime, CPU usage, and memory footprint.
skills.name: amq-index-sequence-querying
skills.search_text: amq-index-sequence-querying Use when you have batches of query sequences (e.g., human RefSeq transcripts in FASTA) and a prebuilt AMQ index over thousands of datasets, and you need to list candidate datasets per query while profiling query runtime, CPU usage, and memory footprint. When exact alignment or exhaustive similarity search is required — PAC is an approximate membership query structure that only lists datasets that may contain the query, not BLAST-like alignments When no PAC index exists yet — index construction ('./PAC -f fof.txt -d index_test') is a separate workflow step and this skill assumes the index is already built When the query sequences' informative kmers are seen only once in the indexed datasets — PAC's -u construction option filters singletons, so such queries cannot be recalled http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark-style querying of large batches of nucleotide sequences against a prebuilt PAC (Partitioned Aggregated bloom Comb trees) approximate membership query (AMQ) index to identify which indexed datasets share kmers with each query, while recording wall-clock time, CPU time, and peak RAM per batch size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Benchmark-style querying of large batches of nucleotide sequences against a prebuilt PAC (Partitioned Aggregated bloom Comb trees) approximate membership query (AMQ) index to identify which indexed datasets share kmers with each query, while recording wall-clock time, CPU time, and peak RAM per batch size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When exact alignment or exhaustive similarity search is required — PAC is an approximate membership query structure that only lists datasets that may contain the query, not BLAST-like alignments When no PAC index exists yet — index construction ('./PAC -f fof.txt -d index_test') is a separate workflow step and this skill assumes the index is already built When the query sequences' informative kmers are seen only once in the indexed datasets — PAC's -u construction option filters singletons, so such queries cannot be recalled

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-sample or multi-study scRNA-seq data in Seurat where batch correction must preserve cell type structure, especially when partial cell type labels (e.g., scGate CD8_TIL gates) are available to guide anchor finding.
skills.name: anchor-based-integration-execution
skills.search_text: anchor-based-integration-execution Use when integrating multi-sample or multi-study scRNA-seq data in Seurat where batch correction must preserve cell type structure, especially when partial cell type labels (e.g., scGate CD8_TIL gates) are available to guide anchor finding. Input is not raw per-sample scRNA-seq count data (e.g., an already integrated embedding or non-transcriptomic data) — anchors are computed between scRNA-seq datasets. You only need to score an existing integration rather than perform one — use the scIntegrationMetrics/scib-pipeline evaluation tools instead. A single dataset with no batch structure is supplied; there are no inter-dataset anchors to compute. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Executes anchor-based batch correction of scRNA-seq collections using STACAS within Seurat v4, computing inter-dataset anchors, filtering them by pairwise rPCA distance, and integrating data with an optional semisupervised mode that uses prior cell type labels to preserve biological variance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Executes anchor-based batch correction of scRNA-seq collections using STACAS within Seurat v4, computing inter-dataset anchors, filtering them by pairwise rPCA distance, and integrating data with an optional semisupervised mode that uses prior cell type labels to preserve biological variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw per-sample scRNA-seq count data (e.g., an already integrated embedding or non-transcriptomic data) — anchors are computed between scRNA-seq datasets. You only need to score an existing integration rather than perform one — use the scIntegrationMetrics/scib-pipeline evaluation tools instead. A single dataset with no batch structure is supplied; there are no inter-dataset anchors to compute.

skills.description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets affected by batch effects and you need a parsimonious set of representative anchor cells per dataset before building a weighted bipartite graph for one-to-one matching.
skills.name: anchor-cell-identification-in-scrnaseq-partitions
skills.search_text: anchor-cell-identification-in-scrnaseq-partitions Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets affected by batch effects and you need a parsimonious set of representative anchor cells per dataset before building a weighted bipartite graph for one-to-one matching. You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets Input is raw UMI counts without Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing — anchors are identified in log-count space A non-matching-based integration approach is required (e.g. MNN-based tools like MNNcorrect, Scanorama, or Harmony are the alternatives) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify representative anchor cells within each partition of two scRNA-seq datasets (after Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing) to serve as graph nodes for BATMAN's minimum-weight bipartite matching and downstream batch correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Identify representative anchor cells within each partition of two scRNA-seq datasets (after Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing) to serve as graph nodes for BATMAN's minimum-weight bipartite matching and downstream batch correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets Input is raw UMI counts without Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing — anchors are identified in log-count space A non-matching-based integration approach is required (e.g. MNN-based tools like MNNcorrect, Scanorama, or Harmony are the alternatives)

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or validating how STACAS weights integration anchors during batch effect correction, or when you need to reproduce the sample guide tree that determines the order of multi-dataset Seurat integration.
skills.name: anchor-score-weighting-implementation
skills.search_text: anchor-score-weighting-implementation Use when reconstructing or validating how STACAS weights integration anchors during batch effect correction, or when you need to reproduce the sample guide tree that determines the order of multi-dataset Seurat integration. The task is purely unsupervised integration without any cell type annotations — the anchor weighting depends on label probability and label.confidence filtering You only need to evaluate integration quality post hoc (use CiLISI/ASW from carmonalab/scIntegrationMetrics instead of reconstructing anchor weighting) Datasets have only one sample pair where no guide tree ordering decision is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements STACAS's semi-supervised anchor weighting scheme for scRNA-seq integration: anchors are scored from rPCA and SNN similarities via a logistic transform (alpha = 0.8 geometric weighted log-sum), label-inconsistent anchors are rejected, and retained scores are summed into global dataset similarities that drive a ward.D2 guide tree fixing the integration order. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Implements STACAS's semi-supervised anchor weighting scheme for scRNA-seq integration: anchors are scored from rPCA and SNN similarities via a logistic transform (alpha = 0.8 geometric weighted log-sum), label-inconsistent anchors are rejected, and retained scores are summed into global dataset similarities that drive a ward.D2 guide tree fixing the integration order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is purely unsupervised integration without any cell type annotations — the anchor weighting depends on label probability and label.confidence filtering You only need to evaluate integration quality post hoc (use CiLISI/ASW from carmonalab/scIntegrationMetrics instead of reconstructing anchor weighting) Datasets have only one sample pair where no guide tree ordering decision is needed

skills.description: Use when searching for fusions involving one known driver gene (e.g., BCR-ABL1, NSD2-IGH) in paired-end bulk or single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2) where de novo tools miss multi-mapping/homologous or shallow-depth reads.
skills.name: anchored-targeted-read-alignment
skills.search_text: anchored-targeted-read-alignment Use when searching for fusions involving one known driver gene (e.g., BCR-ABL1, NSD2-IGH) in paired-end bulk or single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2) where de novo tools miss multi-mapping/homologous or shallow-depth reads. Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion requires paired-end RNA-seq The fusion of interest does not include the user-provided target gene — only fusions containing the anchored gene are reported A comprehensive de novo fusion discovery is needed rather than a targeted search for a known driver gene http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A targeted fusion-detection strategy from Anchored-fusion that anchors a user-specified gene of interest, maps all paired-end reads to that gene's transcript reference with BWA-MEM, realigns unmapped mates to the whole genome, and uses BLAT local alignment on chimeric reads to pinpoint the fusion breakpoint. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: A targeted fusion-detection strategy from Anchored-fusion that anchors a user-specified gene of interest, maps all paired-end reads to that gene's transcript reference with BWA-MEM, realigns unmapped mates to the whole genome, and uses BLAT local alignment on chimeric reads to pinpoint the fusion breakpoint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion requires paired-end RNA-seq The fusion of interest does not include the user-provided target gene — only fusions containing the anchored gene are reported A comprehensive de novo fusion discovery is needed rather than a targeted search for a known driver gene

skills.search_text: angiogenesis-high-population-identification Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Seurat object or counts matrix from csv/rds/h5/10X) for a pathway signature like angiogenesis to flag which TME cell subpopulations are pathway-high. Input is already an aggregated feature/signature score table rather than per-cell expression data — the skill requires a QC-passed counts matrix or Seurat object The pathway of interest is not represented in MSigDB or an available GMT file and no user-supplied gene set can be prepared The dataset has not passed quality control or cell-type annotation, since angiogenesis-high populations are flagged by per-cell-type aggregation of annotated subpopulations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies angiogenesis-high cell subpopulations in tumor single-cell RNA-seq data by computing per-cell GSVA angiogenesis scores (MSigDB gene sets) with scWizard, then aggregating and ranking cell types by score — as demonstrated on the intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) dataset in the scWizard case study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Identifies angiogenesis-high cell subpopulations in tumor single-cell RNA-seq data by computing per-cell GSVA angiogenesis scores (MSigDB gene sets) with scWizard, then aggregating and ranking cell types by score — as demonstrated on the intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) dataset in the scWizard case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated feature/signature score table rather than per-cell expression data — the skill requires a QC-passed counts matrix or Seurat object The pathway of interest is not represented in MSigDB or an available GMT file and no user-supplied gene set can be prepared The dataset has not passed quality control or cell-type annotation, since angiogenesis-high populations are flagged by per-cell-type aggregation of annotated subpopulations

skills.description: Use when unrolling rolled intestinal tissue imaging data in IntestLine and misprojected points appear in the stretched output after backbone-based projection; the angleCBS parameter is the tool's dedicated control for removing them.
skills.name: anglecbs-projection-filtering
skills.search_text: anglecbs-projection-filtering Use when unrolling rolled intestinal tissue imaging data in IntestLine and misprojected points appear in the stretched output after backbone-based projection; the angleCBS parameter is the tool's dedicated control for removing them. The points to remove are noisy cells or contaminants rather than misprojected projections — use the Z-score filtering instead of angleCBS. The input provides no xy-coordinates or is not imaging data of rolled/Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue, which is outside IntestLine's stated scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies the angleCBS filter inside IntestLine's unroll step to remove misprojected points when mapping Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue images (CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics xy-coordinates) onto a linear structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: Applies the angleCBS filter inside IntestLine's unroll step to remove misprojected points when mapping Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue images (CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics xy-coordinates) onto a linear structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The points to remove are noisy cells or contaminants rather than misprojected projections — use the Z-score filtering instead of angleCBS. The input provides no xy-coordinates or is not imaging data of rolled/Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue, which is outside IntestLine's stated scope.

skills.description: Use when you have a trained mvTCR joint model with specificity annotations and need to quantify each cell's or epitope group's TCR contribution to the shared embedding, or to test whether that contribution tracks TCR sequence similarity.
skills.name: angular-distance-embedding-analysis
skills.search_text: angular-distance-embedding-analysis Use when you have a trained mvTCR joint model with specificity annotations and need to quantify each cell's or epitope group's TCR contribution to the shared embedding, or to test whether that contribution tracks TCR sequence similarity. You only need cell-type or clonotype clustering from the joint embedding without quantifying modality-wise (TCR vs transcriptome) contributions Your data is unpaired or lacks antigen-specificity annotation, so per-specificity averaging and TCRdist group comparisons cannot be performed You want to adjust modality contribution in the model itself — the article notes this requires repeated mvTCR retraining with hyperparameter search, not post-hoc angular-distance analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Quantifies how much TCR sequence information each cell contributes to the mvTCR joint embedding by computing the angular distance between the joint embedding and the TCR-unimodal embedding, then relates per-specificity average contributions to TCRdist sequence similarity (Pearson r = 0.64 in the mvTCR 10x dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how much TCR sequence information each cell contributes to the mvTCR joint embedding by computing the angular distance between the joint embedding and the TCR-unimodal embedding, then relates per-specificity average contributions to TCRdist sequence similarity (Pearson r = 0.64 in the mvTCR 10x dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need cell-type or clonotype clustering from the joint embedding without quantifying modality-wise (TCR vs transcriptome) contributions Your data is unpaired or lacks antigen-specificity annotation, so per-specificity averaging and TCRdist group comparisons cannot be performed You want to adjust modality contribution in the model itself — the article notes this requires repeated mvTCR retraining with hyperparameter search, not post-hoc angular-distance analysis

skills.description: Use when a query AnnData with different or unordered var_names must be passed to TOSICA.pre() alongside a trained reference model, since the reference and query gene sets must match exactly.
skills.name: ann-data-gene-alignment-across-datasets
skills.search_text: ann-data-gene-alignment-across-datasets Use when a query AnnData with different or unordered var_names must be passed to TOSICA.pre() alongside a trained reference model, since the reference and query gene sets must match exactly. The query data is already subset to the reference gene space and var_names order has been verified — re-subsetting is redundant. The query dataset uses a different genome annotation with mostly non-overlapping genes, so subsetting would discard too many features to support meaningful annotation. Input is not scanpy AnnData format (e.g. raw matrix files), which would require a different ingestion pipeline before alignment. Aligns the gene space (var_names) of a query AnnData object to a reference AnnData before label-transfer prediction with TOSICA, ensuring the trained Transformer model receives genes in the identical, same-ordered feature space it was trained on. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Aligns the gene space (var_names) of a query AnnData object to a reference AnnData before label-transfer prediction with TOSICA, ensuring the trained Transformer model receives genes in the identical, same-ordered feature space it was trained on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data is already subset to the reference gene space and var_names order has been verified — re-subsetting is redundant. The query dataset uses a different genome annotation with mostly non-overlapping genes, so subsetting would discard too many features to support meaningful annotation. Input is not scanpy AnnData format (e.g. raw matrix files), which would require a different ingestion pipeline before alignment.

skills.description: Use when a query .h5ad dataset has a different gene set or gene count than the features a SIMS/TabNet reference model was trained on, and label-transfer prediction fails or would fail on feature mismatch.
skills.name: annadata-expression-matrix-subsetting
skills.search_text: annadata-expression-matrix-subsetting Use when a query .h5ad dataset has a different gene set or gene count than the features a SIMS/TabNet reference model was trained on, and label-transfer prediction fails or would fail on feature mismatch. The query dataset's gene panel already matches the model's training features in both identity and order — intersection adds no value Prediction is intended across species (e.g., mouse to human neuronal subtypes); SIMS has only been validated within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species The input is a gene-by-cell matrix or a summary/feature table rather than a cell x gene expression matrix, which SIMS requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aligns a query single-cell AnnData object's gene panel to a trained SIMS/TabNet reference model's feature ordering via set intersection, so label-transfer prediction works across datasets with different numbers of genes (e.g., PBMC68K ~20k genes vs Han landscape ~5k genes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Aligns a query single-cell AnnData object's gene panel to a trained SIMS/TabNet reference model's feature ordering via set intersection, so label-transfer prediction works across datasets with different numbers of genes (e.g., PBMC68K ~20k genes vs Han landscape ~5k genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset's gene panel already matches the model's training features in both identity and order — intersection adds no value Prediction is intended across species (e.g., mouse to human neuronal subtypes); SIMS has only been validated within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species The input is a gene-by-cell matrix or a summary/feature table rather than a cell x gene expression matrix, which SIMS requires

skills.description: Use when a scDEAL single-cell prediction run (e.g. scmodel.py on GSE110894) has finished and the per-cell drug response predictions must be persisted and shared as an AnnData object for evaluation or visualization.

skills.search_text: annadata-h5ad-prediction-export Use when a scDEAL single-cell prediction run (e.g. scmodel.py on GSE110894) has finished and the per-cell drug response predictions must be persisted and shared as an AnnData object for evaluation or visualization. skills.description: Use when a single-cell AnnData/h5ad dataset is too large for memory (e.g. millions of cells) and SQL-based querying, filtering, or aggregation is needed instead of AnnData-backed-mode operations that fail or run ~700x slower.
skills.name: anndata-to-duckdb-database-conversion
skills.search_text: anndata-to-duckdb-database-conversion Use when a single-cell AnnData/h5ad dataset is too large for memory (e.g. millions of cells) and SQL-based querying, filtering, or aggregation is needed instead of AnnData-backed-mode operations that fail or run ~700x slower. Dataset fits comfortably in memory and simple in-memory use suffices — use AnnSQL(adata=adata) directly instead of MakeDb Input is not an AnnData/h5ad object (e.g. raw count matrices or other feature tables) — the database structure mirrors AnnData layers specifically Analysis requires a performance-optimized database schema — the article notes 'The database structure is not optimized for performance' http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts AnnData single-cell objects (.h5ad) into persistent on-disk AnnSQL databases (.asql) backed by an in-process DuckDB engine, where each AnnData layer becomes an individual table. This enables SQL queries on datasets that exceed available memory, such as the 4.4-million-cell Macosko Mouse Atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf105
skills.summary: Converts AnnData single-cell objects (.h5ad) into persistent on-disk AnnSQL databases (.asql) backed by an in-process DuckDB engine, where each AnnData layer becomes an individual table. This enables SQL queries on datasets that exceed available memory, such as the 4.4-million-cell Macosko Mouse Atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset fits comfortably in memory and simple in-memory use suffices — use AnnSQL(adata=adata) directly instead of MakeDb Input is not an AnnData/h5ad object (e.g. raw count matrices or other feature tables) — the database structure mirrors AnnData layers specifically Analysis requires a performance-optimized database schema — the article notes 'The database structure is not optimized for performance'

skills.description: Use when decomposing aggregated spot-level ST expression (e.g. Visium/Slide-seq spots with multiple cells) into per-cell gene expressions given a scRNA-seq reference and a trained conditional score model.
skills.name: annealed-langevin-dynamics-posterior-sampling
skills.search_text: annealed-langevin-dynamics-posterior-sampling Use when decomposing aggregated spot-level ST expression (e.g. Visium/Slide-seq spots with multiple cells) into per-cell gene expressions given a scRNA-seq reference and a trained conditional score model. The goal is only per-spot cell-type proportions — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD suffice without per-cell expression sampling Single-cell resolution spatial data (e.g. MERFISH) already exists; gene imputation rather than spot decomposition is needed No trained conditional score network or scRNA-seq reference is available, since posterior sampling requires s_theta and cell-type means mu_k http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Samples per-cell gene expressions from the posterior p(X_i|y_i,k_i) via annealed Langevin dynamics using a conditional score network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k), enabling SpatialScope to decompose aggregated spot-level expression into single-cell expressions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Samples per-cell gene expressions from the posterior p(X_i|y_i,k_i) via annealed Langevin dynamics using a conditional score network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k), enabling SpatialScope to decompose aggregated spot-level expression into single-cell expressions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only per-spot cell-type proportions — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD suffice without per-cell expression sampling Single-cell resolution spatial data (e.g. MERFISH) already exists; gene imputation rather than spot decomposition is needed No trained conditional score network or scRNA-seq reference is available, since posterior sampling requires s_theta and cell-type means mu_k

skills.description: Use when building an alignment-free splicing quantification pipeline that must first guess novel transcript fragments from a GTF annotation's splice sites, before pseudoaligning reads with kallisto.
skills.name: annotated-splice-site-recombination-fragment-enumeration
skills.search_text: annotated-splice-site-recombination-fragment-enumeration Use when building an alignment-free splicing quantification pipeline that must first guess novel transcript fragments from a GTF annotation's splice sites, before pseudoaligning reads with kallisto. When splice sites not present in the annotation must be included — fortuna's Step A only recombines annotated donor/acceptor sites; novel splice sites from spliced aligners are incorporated only later, from reads unmapped in pseudoalignment step (D) When a full alignment-based quantification is required — this enumeration feeds kallisto pseudoalignment, not align-and-count workflows When the GTF has not been segmented by bin/processGTF.sh — raw unsegmented GTF lacks the NodeId subexon records the enumeration requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Reconstructs fortuna's Step A virtual transcriptome (T^as_g): for each gene, enumerate novel transcript fragments by recombining annotated donor and acceptor splice sites only — implementing exon skipping and exon-boundary modification without ever merging touching exons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Reconstructs fortuna's Step A virtual transcriptome (T^as_g): for each gene, enumerate novel transcript fragments by recombining annotated donor and acceptor splice sites only — implementing exon skipping and exon-boundary modification without ever merging touching exons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When splice sites not present in the annotation must be included — fortuna's Step A only recombines annotated donor/acceptor sites; novel splice sites from spliced aligners are incorporated only later, from reads unmapped in pseudoalignment step (D) When a full alignment-based quantification is required — this enumeration feeds kallisto pseudoalignment, not align-and-count workflows When the GTF has not been segmented by bin/processGTF.sh — raw unsegmented GTF lacks the NodeId subexon records the enumeration requires

skills.description: Use when comparing cell annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with known reference labels — e.g. difficult PBMC splits with p = 10/20/50/80% training proportions or ASD vs control cross-condition directions — to rank methods by accuracy and ARI.
skills.name: annotation-accuracy-ari-evaluation
skills.search_text: annotation-accuracy-ari-evaluation Use when comparing cell annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with known reference labels — e.g. difficult PBMC splits with p = 10/20/50/80% training proportions or ASD vs control cross-condition directions — to rank methods by accuracy and ARI. No true labels are available for the testing data — accuracy and ARI cannot be computed and only qualitative checks (e.g. marker concordance) are possible. The sample may contain unknown or novel cell types absent from the training data — NeuCA's exhaustive assignment is restricted to settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the reference data. Goal is cluster discovery rather than label transfer evaluation — use unsupervised clustering validation metrics, not accuracy against a fixed reference. Evaluate single-cell label assignment by computing annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) of predicted cell labels against published true labels, used in the NeuCA paper to benchmark NeuCA against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH, CellAssign, SCINA, Seurat, and SC3 across intra-study, inter-study, and cross-condition settings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Evaluate single-cell label assignment by computing annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) of predicted cell labels against published true labels, used in the NeuCA paper to benchmark NeuCA against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH, CellAssign, SCINA, Seurat, and SC3 across intra-study, inter-study, and cross-condition settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No true labels are available for the testing data — accuracy and ARI cannot be computed and only qualitative checks (e.g. marker concordance) are possible. The sample may contain unknown or novel cell types absent from the training data — NeuCA's exhaustive assignment is restricted to settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the reference data. Goal is cluster discovery rather than label transfer evaluation — use unsupervised clustering validation metrics, not accuracy against a fixed reference.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how robust an automated cell-type annotation method is to dropout events, by benchmarking accuracy against known labels on simulated scRNA-seq data at graded dropout levels.
skills.name: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how robust an automated cell-type annotation method is to dropout events, by benchmarking accuracy against known labels on simulated scRNA-seq data at graded dropout levels. Your input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without ground-truth cell-type labels — accuracy cannot be computed, so use manual/curation-based validation instead You need dropout correction rather than robustness measurement — the current ScType version does not correct drop-out events (the authors plan to incorporate scDoc) You want to include scCATCH as a comparator on simulated data — its implementation does not allow custom markers http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark automated cell-type annotation accuracy under controlled scRNA-seq dropout stress by simulating 45 Splatter datasets (~50%, ~65%, ~80% dropout) with known labels, running ScType, scSorter, and SCINA on identical marker inputs, and scoring per-dataset accuracy against ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Benchmark automated cell-type annotation accuracy under controlled scRNA-seq dropout stress by simulating 45 Splatter datasets (~50%, ~65%, ~80% dropout) with known labels, running ScType, scSorter, and SCINA on identical marker inputs, and scoring per-dataset accuracy against ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without ground-truth cell-type labels — accuracy cannot be computed, so use manual/curation-based validation instead You need dropout correction rather than robustness measurement — the current ScType version does not correct drop-out events (the authors plan to incorporate scDoc) You want to include scCATCH as a comparator on simulated data — its implementation does not allow custom markers

skills.description: Use when validating an automated cell-annotation model on held-out, independently published cancer scRNA-seq datasets that carry original labeled cell information (e.g., MCC 11,024 cells, CRC 11,717 myeloid cells, LC 45,555 T cells) so predicted labels can be scored against expert ground truth.
skills.name: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking-against-original-labels
skills.search_text: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking-against-original-labels Use when validating an automated cell-annotation model on held-out, independently published cancer scRNA-seq datasets that carry original labeled cell information (e.g., MCC 11,024 cells, CRC 11,717 myeloid cells, LC 45,555 T cells) so predicted labels can be scored against expert ground truth. Targeting tissue-specific cell types outside scWizard's TME scope (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) — the article warns these may not be identified and fall in the Unknown cluster Evaluating on data included in model training rather than independent datasets — accuracy would not be comparable to the reported held-out figures Datasets lacking original expert cell annotations, since the consistent/inconsistent/unknown labeling cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks an automated single-cell annotation method against the original study's expert cell labels on independent cancer scRNA-seq datasets, scoring per-cluster accuracy as the fraction of cells whose predicted label is 'consistent' with the original annotation. Reproduces scWizard's reported accuracies (0.98 major cell types, 0.85 myeloid subtypes, 0.79 T/NK subtypes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Benchmarks an automated single-cell annotation method against the original study's expert cell labels on independent cancer scRNA-seq datasets, scoring per-cluster accuracy as the fraction of cells whose predicted label is 'consistent' with the original annotation. Reproduces scWizard's reported accuracies (0.98 major cell types, 0.85 myeloid subtypes, 0.79 T/NK subtypes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeting tissue-specific cell types outside scWizard's TME scope (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) — the article warns these may not be identified and fall in the Unknown cluster Evaluating on data included in model training rather than independent datasets — accuracy would not be comparable to the reported held-out figures Datasets lacking original expert cell annotations, since the consistent/inconsistent/unknown labeling cannot be computed

skills.search_text: annotation-accuracy-evaluation-against-predefined-labels Use when a new or existing cell type annotation method must be benchmarked for accuracy against predefined labels on scRNA-seq datasets, e.g. reproducing deCS vs. SingleR/CHETAH/scPred/SciBet/Cell BLAST comparisons. skills.description: Use when comparing cluster purity before and after a decomposition/merging step: you have cell type annotations for each cell and two clusterings of the same cells, and need to know if rare types become more dominant within their clusters.
skills.name: annotation-based-cluster-composition-comparison
skills.search_text: annotation-based-cluster-composition-comparison Use when comparing cluster purity before and after a decomposition/merging step: you have cell type annotations for each cell and two clusterings of the same cells, and need to know if rare types become more dominant within their clusters. Input lacks ground-truth cell type annotations, so dominant types and occupy rates P_i cannot be computed You need a single rare-type detection score rather than a purity comparison between two clusterings of the same cells (use scCAD's independence score with threshold I=0.7 instead) The second clustering is an independent re-clustering rather than the decomposition/merging output of the first (M-clusters are derived from I-clusters by iterative decomposition and THM-based merging) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how a cluster-decomposition and merging step (scCAD's I-clusters vs. M-clusters) changes the purity of cell-type composition by computing dominant-type occupy rates P_i = max(N_i,1,...,N_i,t)/N_i per cluster. Demonstrates that decomposition raises the average dominant-type proportion of rare cell types from 0.283 (I-clusters) to 0.704 (M-clusters). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how a cluster-decomposition and merging step (scCAD's I-clusters vs. M-clusters) changes the purity of cell-type composition by computing dominant-type occupy rates P_i = max(N_i,1,...,N_i,t)/N_i per cluster. Demonstrates that decomposition raises the average dominant-type proportion of rare cell types from 0.283 (I-clusters) to 0.704 (M-clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks ground-truth cell type annotations, so dominant types and occupy rates P_i cannot be computed You need a single rare-type detection score rather than a purity comparison between two clusterings of the same cells (use scCAD's independence score with threshold I=0.7 instead) The second clustering is an independent re-clustering rather than the decomposition/merging output of the first (M-clusters are derived from I-clusters by iterative decomposition and THM-based merging)

skills.description: Use when you have binary driver-alteration calls (amplification or mutation) per sample plus continuous pathway activity scores and need to test which alterations activate which pathways.

skills.search_text: anova-statistical-modeling Use when you have binary driver-alteration calls (amplification or mutation) per sample plus continuous pathway activity scores and need to test which alterations activate which pathways. You are scoring pathways by mean expression of pathway gene sets (Gene Ontology or Reactome via GSVA) rather than perturbation-based footprints — the article shows such pathway-expression methods do not detect the strong EGFR-amplification activation that PROGENy does. The outcome is continuous patient survival or drug response rather than binary alteration status — the article uses separate survival and drug-association analyses for those, not ANOVA of alteration status. Samples lack matched tumor/normal or the expression matrix and alteration calls are not from tissue-matched cohorts — the pipeline assumes tissue-matched TCGA cohorts. The cluster of interest is supported by less than 2% of all cells in the experiment — benchmarking showed such clusters produce unstable results and bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types The dataset contains true biological replicates for all conditions — use the replicated Scanpro setting directly rather than bootstrapping-based transformation comparison You lack experimental validation for interpreting bootstrapping results — bootstrapping-derived calls are indications only and require caution http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A Scanpro benchmarking skill that simulates proportion-change datasets with sim_scanpro and compares the accuracy of arcsin versus logit transformations across bootstrapped pseudo-replicate counts, identifying the 5–8 pseudo-replicate accuracy sweet spot on unreplicated data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: A Scanpro benchmarking skill that simulates proportion-change datasets with sim_scanpro and compares the accuracy of arcsin versus logit transformations across bootstrapped pseudo-replicate counts, identifying the 5–8 pseudo-replicate accuracy sweet spot on unreplicated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cluster of interest is supported by less than 2% of all cells in the experiment — benchmarking showed such clusters produce unstable results and bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types The dataset contains true biological replicates for all conditions — use the replicated Scanpro setting directly rather than bootstrapping-based transformation comparison You lack experimental validation for interpreting bootstrapping results — bootstrapping-derived calls are indications only and require caution

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset annotated with cell type clusters (e.g. an AnnData object with cluster/condition/sample columns) must be tested for differential cell-type proportions, especially when replicates are missing or unbalanced across conditions.
skills.name: arcsin-transformed-proportion-testing
skills.search_text: arcsin-transformed-proportion-testing Use when a single-cell dataset annotated with cell type clusters (e.g. an AnnData object with cluster/condition/sample columns) must be tested for differential cell-type proportions, especially when replicates are missing or unbalanced across conditions. When the input is raw cell counts compared directly between clusters — raw counts cannot be compared due to sequencing depth and other technical/biological effects, so transformation and modelling are required instead When the biological question is within-cell-type gene expression change rather than cell-type proportion shift When rare cell types make up less than 2% of all cells and would drive unstable results — merge or interpret such clusters with caution http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Statistical testing of cell-type proportion shifts by applying Scanpro's arcsin (sqrt-linear) transformation to cell type fractions followed by linear modelling (t-test for two conditions, ANOVA for multiple), optionally extended with iteration-based bootstrapping to simulate pseudo-replicates for unreplicated single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Statistical testing of cell-type proportion shifts by applying Scanpro's arcsin (sqrt-linear) transformation to cell type fractions followed by linear modelling (t-test for two conditions, ANOVA for multiple), optionally extended with iteration-based bootstrapping to simulate pseudo-replicates for unreplicated single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw cell counts compared directly between clusters — raw counts cannot be compared due to sequencing depth and other technical/biological effects, so transformation and modelling are required instead When the biological question is within-cell-type gene expression change rather than cell-type proportion shift When rare cell types make up less than 2% of all cells and would drive unstable results — merge or interpret such clusters with caution

skills.description: Use when a batch-corrected expression matrix with per-gene subtype means (cot.df_mean) is available and each gene must be scored and assigned to the subtype whose ideal-marker-gene definition its cross-subtype pattern most closely matches.
skills.name: argmax-subtype-assignment-validation
skills.search_text: argmax-subtype-assignment-validation Use when a batch-corrected expression matrix with per-gene subtype means (cot.df_mean) is available and each gene must be scored and assigned to the subtype whose ideal-marker-gene definition its cross-subtype pattern most closely matches. The input matrix is not batch-corrected — the COT input must be batch-corrected before cosine computation The goal is p-value estimation or marker list extraction rather than cosine scoring/assignment — use cot.estimate_p_values() or cot.obtain_subtype_markers() instead There are too few genes for downstream null-distribution steps (though argmax cosine assignment itself still works, p-values cannot be computed — see Example_GSE28490) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assigns each candidate marker gene to its best-matching subtype by taking the argmax over subtypes of the cosine similarity between the gene's cross-subtype expression vector and each subtype's ideal marker-gene indicator, then validates that every statistic lies in (1/K, 1) and matches the recorded argmax subtype. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: Assigns each candidate marker gene to its best-matching subtype by taking the argmax over subtypes of the cosine similarity between the gene's cross-subtype expression vector and each subtype's ideal marker-gene indicator, then validates that every statistic lies in (1/K, 1) and matches the recorded argmax subtype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is not batch-corrected — the COT input must be batch-corrected before cosine computation The goal is p-value estimation or marker list extraction rather than cosine scoring/assignment — use cot.estimate_p_values() or cot.obtain_subtype_markers() instead There are too few genes for downstream null-distribution steps (though argmax cosine assignment itself still works, p-values cannot be computed — see Example_GSE28490)

skills.description: Use when a per-cell clone labeling from a CNA-inference pipeline must be validated against an existing clone annotation, and a single agreement statistic (ARI) is needed to quantify concordance.
skills.name: ari-clone-label-agreement-evaluation
skills.search_text: ari-clone-label-agreement-evaluation Use when a per-cell clone labeling from a CNA-inference pipeline must be validated against an existing clone annotation, and a single agreement statistic (ARI) is needed to quantify concordance. No independent reference clone annotation exists for the sample — ARI cannot be computed without a second labeling to compare against The goal is de novo clonal reconstruction rather than validation of an existing reconstruction against a benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Evaluates whether a computationally reconstructed subclonal structure (e.g., K-means labels on XClone's flattened CNA probability matrix, stored as XClone_ID) agrees with an independent reference clone annotation (CopyKAT-derived Clone_ID) by computing the adjusted Rand index, with 0.965 as the benchmark concordance for the TNBC1 sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0

skills.search_text: ari-clustering-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing TE quantification methods on scRNA-seq data in terms of downstream cell-clustering fidelity, e.g., testing whether a new method (MATES) beats scTE/SoloTE on ARI against gene-defined clusters. Input is already a feature table or published ARI values — this skill requires raw alignments re-quantified by each competing method The quantification target is long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where MATES coverage-vector flanking context is incomplete The data come from mammalian species for which MATES auto-builds references — this skill targets the non-mammalian (Arabidopsis/Drosophila) extension path requiring custom reference building Benchmark locus-specific single-cell TE quantification methods (MATES, scTE, SoloTE) by clustering cells on TE features and scoring agreement with gene-expression-based reference clustering via Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), with block-permutation empirical p-values and marker-TE recovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Benchmark locus-specific single-cell TE quantification methods (MATES, scTE, SoloTE) by clustering cells on TE features and scoring agreement with gene-expression-based reference clustering via Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), with block-permutation empirical p-values and marker-TE recovery.

skills.description: Use when comparing imputation or preprocessing methods on scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels, so that quality is measured as improvement in k-means clustering accuracy (ARI) rather than direct value error.
skills.name: ari-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: ari-clustering-evaluation Use when comparing imputation or preprocessing methods on scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels, so that quality is measured as improvement in k-means clustering accuracy (ARI) rather than direct value error. Cell-type labels are unknown or unreliable: k cannot be set to the true number of cell types and ARI against ground truth cannot be computed. The analysis goal is per-gene accuracy of recovered expression values rather than downstream clustering quality — masked-value recovery (randomly zeroing 30% of values in 40% of genes) is the paper's separate evaluation design. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates single-cell imputation quality by k-means clustering of imputed (and raw) matrices using the true number of cell types k, then scoring the clustering against known labels with the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI). Used in the scISR paper as the primary metric across 25 real scRNA-seq datasets and 116 Splatter-simulated datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Evaluates single-cell imputation quality by k-means clustering of imputed (and raw) matrices using the true number of cell types k, then scoring the clustering against known labels with the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI). Used in the scISR paper as the primary metric across 25 real scRNA-seq datasets and 116 Splatter-simulated datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are unknown or unreliable: k cannot be set to the true number of cell types and ARI against ground truth cannot be computed. The analysis goal is per-gene accuracy of recovered expression values rather than downstream clustering quality — masked-value recovery (randomly zeroing 30% of values in 40% of genes) is the paper's separate evaluation design.

skills.description: Use when comparing the accuracy or robustness of scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., scAce vs. Leiden) on data with ground-truth cell-type labels, especially across repeated random-cell-subset repeats where median ARI/NMI per method is the target metric.
skills.name: ari-nmi-benchmark-computation
skills.search_text: ari-nmi-benchmark-computation Use when comparing the accuracy or robustness of scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., scAce vs. Leiden) on data with ground-truth cell-type labels, especially across repeated random-cell-subset repeats where median ARI/NMI per method is the target metric. The dataset has no ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI and NMI are external agreement metrics and cannot be computed The goal is clustering-parameter tuning on a single fit rather than cross-method robustness benchmarking over repeats The output needed is an internal clustering-quality score (e.g., silhouette) rather than agreement with reference labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between each clustering method's predicted labels and ground-truth cell-type labels, tabulated across repeated subsampling runs to quantify clustering accuracy and robustness (as in the scAce benchmark). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546
skills.summary: Computes Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between each clustering method's predicted labels and ground-truth cell-type labels, tabulated across repeated subsampling runs to quantify clustering accuracy and robustness (as in the scAce benchmark).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI and NMI are external agreement metrics and cannot be computed The goal is clustering-parameter tuning on a single fit rather than cross-method robustness benchmarking over repeats The output needed is an internal clustering-quality score (e.g., silhouette) rather than agreement with reference labels

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type clustering results against retained ground-truth labels on simulated scRNA-seq data — varying cluster numbers, rare-cell proportions, and dropout — to quantify agreement via ARI, NMI, and silhouette scores.
skills.name: ari-nmi-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: ari-nmi-clustering-accuracy-evaluation Use when comparing cell-type clustering results against retained ground-truth labels on simulated scRNA-seq data — varying cluster numbers, rare-cell proportions, and dropout — to quantify agreement via ARI, NMI, and silhouette scores. The dataset has no retained ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI and NMI require a known reference partition and cannot be computed from clusters alone The analysis goal is rare-cell subcluster discovery on real (unlabeled) data rather than benchmarking clustering accuracy on simulations — use SCISSORS's reclustering workflow directly instead You need to determine the optimal number of robust clusters rather than measure how well an existing partition recapitulates labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates scRNA-seq clustering accuracy by computing Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), and per-cell silhouette scores against retained ground-truth cell-type labels on simulated datasets, then testing SCISSORS against competing clustering methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Evaluates scRNA-seq clustering accuracy by computing Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), and per-cell silhouette scores against retained ground-truth cell-type labels on simulated datasets, then testing SCISSORS against competing clustering methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no retained ground-truth cell-type labels — ARI and NMI require a known reference partition and cannot be computed from clusters alone The analysis goal is rare-cell subcluster discovery on real (unlabeled) data rather than benchmarking clustering accuracy on simulations — use SCISSORS's reclustering workflow directly instead You need to determine the optimal number of robust clusters rather than measure how well an existing partition recapitulates labels

The data lacks ground-truth cell-type labels in the h5 file, since both ARI and NMI require a reference partition Evaluating gene imputation accuracy rather than clustering performance — the paper benchmarks these separately A single unreplicated run when sweeping graph hyperparameters, since averaged ARI/NMI over repeated runs is required for the sweep table http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) between predicted cell clusters and true cell-type labels to benchmark scRNA-seq imputation/clustering methods such as scGCL against baselines (AutoClass, GraphSCI, scTAG, MAGIC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098

skills.description: Use when you have paired per-dataset clustering accuracy scores (e.g. ARI) for a proposed method and one or more baselines over the same dataset set and need non-parametric significance testing.

The ARI vectors are not paired (e.g. baselines were evaluated on different datasets), so the paired signed-rank assumption is violated Only a single clustering result per method is available with no per-dataset score breakdown, leaving nothing to pair across datasets The goal is clustering itself (e.g. running CASCC::run.CASCC or predictClusterK) rather than post-hoc benchmark significance analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing of per-dataset ARI scores to establish whether a clustering method's improvement over baselines is statistically significant, as done for CASCC versus six single-cell clustering methods across the 15-dataset benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae283
skills.summary: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank testing of per-dataset ARI scores to establish whether a clustering method's improvement over baselines is statistically significant, as done for CASCC versus six single-cell clustering methods across the 15-dataset benchmark.

skills.search_text: ari-vs-parameter-curve-visualization Use when you must show that a method's clustering performance (ARI against true labels) remains stable as a hyperparameter is reduced, e.g. subsampling scPLS control genes to q = 10, 20, 30, 40 versus the full 50-gene baseline. You need a single point estimate of performance at a fixed setting rather than a robustness/sensitivity curve across parameter values No ground-truth labels are available, so adjusted Rand index against true cell types cannot be computed The question concerns scPLS performance on downstream analyses other than clustering (e.g. differential expression or lineage reconstruction), which the paper explicitly leaves out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sensitivity-analysis visualization skill: tabulate and plot clustering accuracy (adjusted Rand index, ARI) against a varying method parameter — here the number of control genes q used by scPLS — to demonstrate robustness of confounding removal with reduced inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
