skills.description: Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq training matrix with cell type annotations and need a fast, supervised feature-selection statistic to rank/select cell type-specific genes before training a classifier like SciBet.
skills.name: arithmetic-geometric-mean-dispersion-statistic
skills.search_text: arithmetic-geometric-mean-dispersion-statistic Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq training matrix with cell type annotations and need a fast, supervised feature-selection statistic to rank/select cell type-specific genes before training a classifier like SciBet. The training matrix has no cell type labels — ΔS is a supervised statistic defined over per-cell-type mean expression vectors and cannot be computed without annotations The input is already a reduced/selected feature set or a ranked gene list rather than a per-gene expression matrix requiring feature selection You need unsupervised marker discovery for unannotated data; SciBet itself positions supervised annotation with known labels as the alternative to laborious unsupervised approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 The E-test ΔS statistic from SciBet quantifies per-gene cell-type specificity as the entropy difference between the arithmetic and geometric means of per-cell-type mean expression, ΔS_i = n·(ln AM_i − ln GM_i); genes with larger ΔS are kept as informative features for the multinomial classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: The E-test ΔS statistic from SciBet quantifies per-gene cell-type specificity as the entropy difference between the arithmetic and geometric means of per-cell-type mean expression, ΔS_i = n·(ln AM_i − ln GM_i); genes with larger ΔS are kept as informative features for the multinomial classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training matrix has no cell type labels — ΔS is a supervised statistic defined over per-cell-type mean expression vectors and cannot be computed without annotations The input is already a reduced/selected feature set or a ranked gene list rather than a per-gene expression matrix requiring feature selection You need unsupervised marker discovery for unannotated data; SciBet itself positions supervised annotation with known labels as the alternative to laborious unsupervised approaches

skills.description: Use when building consensus pathway-response signatures from public perturbation data: ArrayExpress series must be searched, pathway-labeled, QC'd, and z-scored per experiment before signature fitting.

skills.search_text: arrayexpress-perturbation-data-curation Use when building consensus pathway-response signatures from public perturbation data: ArrayExpress series must be searched, pathway-labeled, QC'd, and z-scored per experiment before signature fitting. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a z-scored perturbation compendium or a finished pathway signature matrix — curation is complete and this skill would duplicate work The candidate perturbation does not clearly correspond to the pathway phenotype to be observed — the README states such files are excluded rather than curated in Data are observational (e.g., TCGA primary tumors or GDSC cell lines) rather than designed perturbation experiments — those need pathway-scoring methods (PROGENy scores, GSVA, SPIA, Pathifier, PARADIGM), not compendium curation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking bulk tissue cell type deconvolution with a single-cell reference and no gold-standard bulk samples with known cell type proportions are available, as in the Segerstolpe pancreatic islet setup.
skills.name: artificial-bulk-rnaseq-construction
skills.search_text: artificial-bulk-rnaseq-construction Use when benchmarking bulk tissue cell type deconvolution with a single-cell reference and no gold-standard bulk samples with known cell type proportions are available, as in the Segerstolpe pancreatic islet setup. skills.summary: Construct an artificial bulk RNA-seq benchmark by summing scRNA-seq counts per subject (bulk_construct) so that true cell type proportions are known, enabling quantitative evaluation of deconvolution methods like MuSiC, NNLS, and BSEQ-sc.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When real bulk RNA-seq samples with independently measured cell type proportions are available — those are a better benchmark than artificial bulk built from the same study. When input data are normalized values (e.g., TPM) rather than read counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input, so artificial bulk must be built from raw counts.

skills.search_text: artificial-chromosome-genome-construction Use when small RNA-seq reads must be classified as tRNA-derived without ambiguity from non-tRNA loci, requiring a modified reference genome where tRNA regions plus flanks are separated into distinct artificial chromosomes. Input is not a reference genome plus tRNA annotations (e.g. already-aligned BAM or a feature count table) — masking and artificial chromosome construction does not apply The goal is generic small RNA annotation against a standard reference, where exclusive-to-artificial-chromosome mapping is unnecessary Tools must run exclusively on human datasets pre-trained pipelines (e.g. tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) rather than de novo genome construction for plant species http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Builds an artificial genome for unambiguous tncRNA identification by masking genuine tRNA gene regions plus 50 bp flanks in the reference genome (bedtools maskfasta) and appending mature tRNA, 5' leader, and 3' trailer FASTA sequences as artificial chromosomes, then indexing with bowtie-build. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a reference genome plus tRNA annotations (e.g. already-aligned BAM or a feature count table) — masking and artificial chromosome construction does not apply The goal is generic small RNA annotation against a standard reference, where exclusive-to-artificial-chromosome mapping is unnecessary Tools must run exclusively on human datasets pre-trained pipelines (e.g. tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) rather than de novo genome construction for plant species

skills.description: Use when building the real-artificial training set inside the Chord workflow after the overkill filter, i.e. when a prefiltered Seurat object of quality singlets must be converted into simulated doublet profiles to train the GBM/adaboost doublet classifier.
skills.name: artificial-doublet-simulation-from-cell-pairs
skills.search_text: artificial-doublet-simulation-from-cell-pairs Use when building the real-artificial training set inside the Chord workflow after the overkill filter, i.e. when a prefiltered Seurat object of quality singlets must be converted into simulated doublet profiles to train the GBM/adaboost doublet classifier. The condition types under study are strongly correlated and were not converted to a combined condition type (e.g. ctrl_severe) as the article recommends for highly correlated condition types. The goal is evaluating a single method's clustering rather than a controlled batch-removal comparison — ASW-batch here presupposes matched baseline runs (scINSIGHT common factor on the same held-out matrices). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies batch-effect removal in learned latent factors by clustering cells in factor space and computing ARI against ground-truth cell-type labels plus ASW-batch (silhouette width on batch labels), as used to compare scDisInFact's shared/unshared-bio factors against scINSIGHT's common modules in the simulated disentanglement test (Fig. 2d). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Quantifies batch-effect removal in learned latent factors by clustering cells in factor space and computing ARI against ground-truth cell-type labels plus ASW-batch (silhouette width on batch labels), as used to compare scDisInFact's shared/unshared-bio factors against scINSIGHT's common modules in the simulated disentanglement test (Fig. 2d).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition — per the article, 'when each batch of cells is measured under only one condition, there is not enough information to fully disentangle the batch and condition effect', so disentanglement scores on separate shared/unshared factors are not meaningful. skills.summary: Binarizes raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrices and applies scButterfly's ATAC-specific preprocessing (0.5% cell-frequency peak filtering, TF-IDF transformation, [0,1] scaling) so the matrix is suitable for the modality-specific ATAC variational encoder.

skills.search_text: atac-seq-peak-to-tss-annotation Use when building a candidate TF–target GRN mask from ATAC-seq peaks: motif sites in peaks must be mapped to nearby genes and intersected with an expressed-gene set to seed regulatory network inference (e.g., scKINETICS priors). You need distal enhancer–gene links beyond the −500 bp/+3000 bp TSS window — the TSS-anchored annotation will miss long-range peak-to-gene assignments You already have a curated TF–target prior or ChIP-seq-derived regulator set and do not need to derive one from ATAC-seq motifs Your target genes lack expression information in the matched single-cell dataset, since the mask is filtered to expressed genes only http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Constructs a binary candidate TF–target regulatory mask by scanning ATAC-seq peak sequences for TF motifs (MOODS, P < 1e-10) and annotating motif-containing peaks to genes near their transcription start sites (ChIPseeker, −500/+3000 bp TSS window), as used to build scKINETICS' epigenetic prior for the pancreatitis dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Constructs a binary candidate TF–target regulatory mask by scanning ATAC-seq peak sequences for TF motifs (MOODS, P < 1e-10) and annotating motif-containing peaks to genes near their transcription start sites (ChIPseeker, −500/+3000 bp TSS window), as used to build scKINETICS' epigenetic prior for the pancreatitis dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need distal enhancer–gene links beyond the −500 bp/+3000 bp TSS window — the TSS-anchored annotation will miss long-range peak-to-gene assignments You already have a curated TF–target prior or ChIP-seq-derived regulator set and do not need to derive one from ATAC-seq motifs Your target genes lack expression information in the matched single-cell dataset, since the mask is filtered to expressed genes only

skills.search_text: atc-score-paired-statistical-testing Use when comparing trajectory-tree alignment quality (ATC scores) of CAPITAL against integration baselines and you need paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values over many synthetic dataset pairs, e.g. to reproduce the Fig. 4a benchmark. Datasets whose pseudotime trajectories have different global topological structure — the article reports CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in this regime, so a pooled ATC-score win cannot be assumed Trajectory data containing cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL handles only trajectory trees (including single lineages), so ATC scores are undefined for such topologies Score samples that are not paired per dataset pair — the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test used here requires matched CAPITAL/baseline scores for the same pair, not independent samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical benchmarking pattern that compares the ATC (alignment-accuracy of trajectory clusters) scores of CAPITAL's tree alignment against data-integration baselines (Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) across the same 2,278 synthetic dataset pairs, then tests paired score differences with one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Statistical benchmarking pattern that compares the ATC (alignment-accuracy of trajectory clusters) scores of CAPITAL's tree alignment against data-integration baselines (Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) across the same 2,278 synthetic dataset pairs, then tests paired score differences with one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets whose pseudotime trajectories have different global topological structure — the article reports CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in this regime, so a pooled ATC-score win cannot be assumed Trajectory data containing cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL handles only trajectory trees (including single lineages), so ATC scores are undefined for such topologies Score samples that are not paired per dataset pair — the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test used here requires matched CAPITAL/baseline scores for the same pair, not independent samples

skills.search_text: atlas-scale-scrna-seq-data-processing Use when you need clustering-independent DEG/DAF predictions on atlas-level scRNA-seq datasets (h5ad files, up to millions of cells), or to benchmark the continuous v1.0.0+ version against the binary v0.3.4 branch across many datasets. skills.summary: Evaluates predicted miRNA expression (e.g., from miRSCAPE) by computing the auROC of predictions as a score separating experimentally detected (non-zero) miRNAs from undetected miRNAs, averaged across ENCODE cell lines (~0.71) and mouse hematopoietic cell types (~0.67).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions must be validated against continuous measured miRNA abundance correlations (e.g., fold-difference correlation ~0.81) rather than binary detection calls The ground truth lacks detection labels, so no detected/undetected classification can be constructed from measured miRNA values

skills.description: Use when building scTab-style training data from donor- and cell-type-annotated, size-factor-normalized (10000 counts, log1p) scRNA-seq matrices and you need precomputed augmentation vectors for donor-difference data augmentation.
skills.name: augmentation-vector-thresholding-and-clamping
skills.search_text: augmentation-vector-thresholding-and-clamping Use when building scTab-style training data from donor- and cell-type-annotated, size-factor-normalized (10000 counts, log1p) scRNA-seq matrices and you need precomputed augmentation vectors for donor-difference data augmentation. Input data lacks reliable donor identity or cell type labels, so cross-donor difference vectors cannot be computed per cell type The expression matrix has not been size-factor normalized to 10000 counts and log1p transformed, which would make donor-difference vectors incomparable across datasets A cell type is observed in too few donors to reliably estimate mean-expression centroids per donor http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Precomputes scTab's donor-difference augmentation vectors: mean-expression centroids are differenced across donors within each cell type, noise is suppressed by zeroing entries in [-0.25, 0.25], and surviving entries are clamped to [-1.5, 1.5]. Clustering and pooling then yield the augmentation-vector set added to gene expression vectors during model training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Precomputes scTab's donor-difference augmentation vectors: mean-expression centroids are differenced across donors within each cell type, noise is suppressed by zeroing entries in [-0.25, 0.25], and surviving entries are clamped to [-1.5, 1.5]. Clustering and pooling then yield the augmentation-vector set added to gene expression vectors during model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks reliable donor identity or cell type labels, so cross-donor difference vectors cannot be computed per cell type The expression matrix has not been size-factor normalized to 10000 counts and log1p transformed, which would make donor-difference vectors incomparable across datasets A cell type is observed in too few donors to reliably estimate mean-expression centroids per donor

skills.description: Use when evaluating a single-cell cell-type classifier in a cross-dataset or unseen-term setting, where test labels include Cell Ontology terms absent from the training set.
skills.name: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating a single-cell cell-type classifier in a cross-dataset or unseen-term setting, where test labels include Cell Ontology terms absent from the training set. The task is within-dataset cross-validation with no unseen Cell Ontology terms; AUPRC/AUROC over unseen terms is not meaningful when all test labels appear in training (use the run_one_dataset_cross_validation.py path instead) You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — OnClass explicitly cannot do this Your annotation labels are free text and you are not using the provided NLP model to map them to Cell Ontology terms; scores will be invalid until labels are mapped to the controlled vocabulary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking protocol for ontology-based single-cell annotation: train an OnClass model on one dataset (e.g., Lemur 4), test on another (e.g., Lemur 1), and score seen-cell-type predictions with AUPRC and unseen-cell-type predictions with AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for ontology-based single-cell annotation: train an OnClass model on one dataset (e.g., Lemur 4), test on another (e.g., Lemur 1), and score seen-cell-type predictions with AUPRC and unseen-cell-type predictions with AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is within-dataset cross-validation with no unseen Cell Ontology terms; AUPRC/AUROC over unseen terms is not meaningful when all test labels appear in training (use the run_one_dataset_cross_validation.py path instead) You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — OnClass explicitly cannot do this Your annotation labels are free text and you are not using the provided NLP model to map them to Cell Ontology terms; scores will be invalid until labels are mapped to the controlled vocabulary

skills.description: Use when comparing gene co-expression network inference methods on simulated single-cell data with known ground-truth edges (power-law, hub-based, or no-extra-sparsity controls) and quantifying accuracy with AUPRC and AUROC across repeats.
skills.name: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing gene co-expression network inference methods on simulated single-cell data with known ground-truth edges (power-law, hub-based, or no-extra-sparsity controls) and quantifying accuracy with AUPRC and AUROC across repeats. Inferring a network from real single-cell data with no known ground-truth adjacency — AUPRC/AUROC cannot be computed and downstream biological validation is needed instead A single network inference run without method comparison — this skill is specifically for benchmark scoring against known true edges Data with no zero-count sparsity at all (bulk-like expression) — the paper's imputation/simulation discussion notes bulk-data methods behave differently, so the dropout-condition design does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark evaluation of gene co-expression network inference methods (scLink, glasso, glasso-r, glasso-f, PIDC, GENIE3, thresholded Pearson/Spearman) on simulated single-cell expression data with known power-law or hub-based ground-truth topologies, scoring each inferred adjacency against the true connectivity matrix via AUPRC and AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of gene co-expression network inference methods (scLink, glasso, glasso-r, glasso-f, PIDC, GENIE3, thresholded Pearson/Spearman) on simulated single-cell expression data with known power-law or hub-based ground-truth topologies, scoring each inferred adjacency against the true connectivity matrix via AUPRC and AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inferring a network from real single-cell data with no known ground-truth adjacency — AUPRC/AUROC cannot be computed and downstream biological validation is needed instead A single network inference run without method comparison — this skill is specifically for benchmark scoring against known true edges Data with no zero-count sparsity at all (bulk-like expression) — the paper's imputation/simulation discussion notes bulk-data methods behave differently, so the dropout-condition design does not apply

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the predictive accuracy or robustness of inferred cell-lineage-specific GRNs against ground-truth regulatory edges, e.g., testing AUPRC stability after randomly perturbing the prior network's edges.
skills.name: auprc-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: auprc-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking the predictive accuracy or robustness of inferred cell-lineage-specific GRNs against ground-truth regulatory edges, e.g., testing AUPRC stability after randomly perturbing the prior network's edges. No ground-truth regulatory edge set exists for the cell type or lineage — the article notes that label datasets serving as ground-truths are often lacking, so AUPRC cannot be computed. The goal is driver regulator identification or regulon-like gene module (RGM) activity scoring, not GRN prediction-accuracy benchmarking. The input is already a computed AUPRC results table (e.g., an existing perturbed_auprc_results.csv) that only needs comparison or plotting rather than re-inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores CEFCON-inferred cell-lineage-specific GRNs against ground-truth regulatory edges using the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), computed with the PRROC R package, and tests robustness by re-scoring GRNs built from a prior gene interaction network with 20% of its edges randomly shuffled (reported ~10% average AUPRC drop). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Scores CEFCON-inferred cell-lineage-specific GRNs against ground-truth regulatory edges using the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), computed with the PRROC R package, and tests robustness by re-scoring GRNs built from a prior gene interaction network with 20% of its edges randomly shuffled (reported ~10% average AUPRC drop).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth regulatory edge set exists for the cell type or lineage — the article notes that label datasets serving as ground-truths are often lacking, so AUPRC cannot be computed. The goal is driver regulator identification or regulon-like gene module (RGM) activity scoring, not GRN prediction-accuracy benchmarking. The input is already a computed AUPRC results table (e.g., an existing perturbed_auprc_results.csv) that only needs comparison or plotting rather than re-inference.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking GRN reconstruction against a gold-standard interaction network and you need AUPRC distributions under partial-groundtruth train/test splits (e.g. 0.5%-10% gold-standard fractions) rather than a single full-groundtruth AUPRC.
skills.name: auprc-distribution-statistics
skills.search_text: auprc-distribution-statistics Use when benchmarking GRN reconstruction against a gold-standard interaction network and you need AUPRC distributions under partial-groundtruth train/test splits (e.g. 0.5%-10% gold-standard fractions) rather than a single full-groundtruth AUPRC. You only need a single AUPR/AUROC point estimate against a fully available groundtruth — use the au_pr_roc binary instead of the train/test-split ensemble evaluation No gold-standard interaction network exists for your organism — eval_mcpnet's train/test splitting requires a groundtruth, which is why it is 'suitable when full groundtruth is available, hence synthetic expression data' Input is raw expression data not yet converted into candidate method score matrices (MI/MCP scores) — compute those first with the mi/mcp pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes distributions of AUPRC (area under the precision-recall curve) for gene regulatory network reconstruction methods when only a partial groundtruth is available, by splitting the gold-standard network into train/test sets across repeated iterations using MCPNet's eval_mcpnet executable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad373
skills.summary: Computes distributions of AUPRC (area under the precision-recall curve) for gene regulatory network reconstruction methods when only a partial groundtruth is available, by splitting the gold-standard network into train/test sets across repeated iterations using MCPNet's eval_mcpnet executable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single AUPR/AUROC point estimate against a fully available groundtruth — use the au_pr_roc binary instead of the train/test-split ensemble evaluation No gold-standard interaction network exists for your organism — eval_mcpnet's train/test splitting requires a groundtruth, which is why it is 'suitable when full groundtruth is available, hence synthetic expression data' Input is raw expression data not yet converted into candidate method score matrices (MI/MCP scores) — compute those first with the mi/mcp pipeline

skills.description: Use when comparing inferred gene regulatory networks (e.g., from scPRINT, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer, GENIE3) against a binary ground-truth network and you need EPR and AUPRC scores to rank methods.
skills.name: auprc-epr-network-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: auprc-epr-network-metrics-computation Use when comparing inferred gene regulatory networks (e.g., from scPRINT, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer, GENIE3) against a binary ground-truth network and you need EPR and AUPRC scores to rank methods. When no cell-type-specific gold-standard edges exist for the genes in the inferred network — the article notes 'no perfect ground truths exist' and ChIP-seq/perturb-seq ground truths remain scarce and ambiguous. When the ground truth is literature-based rather than ChIP-seq/perturb-seq, if the transposition convention (rows=targets, columns=regulators) specific to ChIP-seq/perturb-seq would then be misapplied. When benchmarking on ODE-generated mock-up expression data rather than real ground truths, which the authors criticize as uninformative. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute EPR (early precision ratio) and AUPRC to benchmark inferred gene networks against ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold-standard directed binary graphs, using the BenGRN/GRnnData packages as done in the scPRINT benchmarks on hESC/mESC datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Compute EPR (early precision ratio) and AUPRC to benchmark inferred gene networks against ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold-standard directed binary graphs, using the BenGRN/GRnnData packages as done in the scPRINT benchmarks on hESC/mESC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no cell-type-specific gold-standard edges exist for the genes in the inferred network — the article notes 'no perfect ground truths exist' and ChIP-seq/perturb-seq ground truths remain scarce and ambiguous. When the ground truth is literature-based rather than ChIP-seq/perturb-seq, if the transposition convention (rows=targets, columns=regulators) specific to ChIP-seq/perturb-seq would then be misapplied. When benchmarking on ODE-generated mock-up expression data rather than real ground truths, which the authors criticize as uninformative.

skills.name: auroc-aupr-network-evaluation
skills.search_text: auroc-aupr-network-evaluation Use when you need to score predicted cell-specific regulatory networks against dyngen ground-truth GRNs, e.g. benchmarking SSN, LIONESS, or pySCENIC on the 42-dataset dyngen CSNI benchmark. You lack cell-specific ground-truth regulatory networks — AUROC/AUPR cannot be computed without known per-cell GRN edges as dyngen provides You are evaluating bulk network inference or non-network tasks (e.g. RNA velocity or trajectory alignment), which the manuscript evaluates with different protocols You need runtime or robustness benchmarks rather than network accuracy against ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantitatively evaluates predicted cell-specific gene regulatory networks (CSNI methods such as SSN) against dyngen's cell-specific ground-truth GRNs by computing per-cell AUROC and AUPR over the top-scored interactions and averaging them per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Quantitatively evaluates predicted cell-specific gene regulatory networks (CSNI methods such as SSN) against dyngen's cell-specific ground-truth GRNs by computing per-cell AUROC and AUPR over the top-scored interactions and averaging them per dataset.

skills.search_text: auroc-auprc-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing GRN inference tools on synthetic or real single-cell datasets where a ground-truth network exists (e.g. BoolODE toggle-switch simulations with known topology), so predicted edges can be scored as AUROC/AUPRC/EPR. The candidate regulators exceed ~5 TFs per target — decoding high-order Boolean logic beyond k=5 suffers overfitting, so benchmark results in that regime are unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark evaluation of single-cell GRN inference tools (e.g. scGATE vs. GRNBOOST2, LEAP, CellOracle) by scoring predicted TF-target edges against a known ground-truth network, reporting AUROC and AUPRC/EPR per tool and per condition on BoolODE-simulated single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of single-cell GRN inference tools (e.g. scGATE vs. GRNBOOST2, LEAP, CellOracle) by scoring predicted TF-target edges against a known ground-truth network, reporting AUROC and AUPRC/EPR per tool and per condition on BoolODE-simulated single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth network is available to score predicted edges against (the article relies on BoolODE simulation ground truth or ChIP-Atlas ChIP-seq-derived GRNs). The goal is large-scale de novo inference from scratch rather than benchmarking — scGATE itself is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with refined candidate TFs. The candidate regulators exceed ~5 TFs per target — decoding high-order Boolean logic beyond k=5 suffers overfitting, so benchmark results in that regime are unreliable.

skills.description: Use when two or more communication-inference methods must be compared fairly on identical ligand-target pairs and expression data, with AUROC/AUPRC ranking of aggregated and per-interaction-pair networks.
skills.name: auroc-auprc-classification-evaluation
skills.search_text: auroc-auprc-classification-evaluation Use when two or more communication-inference methods must be compared fairly on identical ligand-target pairs and expression data, with AUROC/AUPRC ranking of aggregated and per-interaction-pair networks. The methods being compared use different ligand-receptor databases or different preprocessing — AUROC/AUPRC differences would then confound database choice with scoring rule The goal is biological interpretation of a single dataset's communication network rather than method benchmarking — use the standard NeuronChat analysis/visualization workflow instead Network weights are spatially constrained (MERFISH/seqFISH+ spatially constrained networks) rather than the benchmark's thresholded weight aggregation setting Benchmarks cell-cell communication inference methods (NeuronChat vs. reimplemented CellChat and CellPhoneDB) by scoring their inferred networks with AUROC and AUPRC under a single shared computational workflow and ligand-target database, so performance differences reflect scoring rules rather than workflow or database differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks cell-cell communication inference methods (NeuronChat vs. reimplemented CellChat and CellPhoneDB) by scoring their inferred networks with AUROC and AUPRC under a single shared computational workflow and ligand-target database, so performance differences reflect scoring rules rather than workflow or database differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The methods being compared use different ligand-receptor databases or different preprocessing — AUROC/AUPRC differences would then confound database choice with scoring rule The goal is biological interpretation of a single dataset's communication network rather than method benchmarking — use the standard NeuronChat analysis/visualization workflow instead Network weights are spatially constrained (MERFISH/seqFISH+ spatially constrained networks) rather than the benchmark's thresholded weight aggregation setting

skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one cohort is available — there is no independent cohort on which to compute a cross-cohort AUROC The task is cluster-free differential gene expression or pathway/GRN activity inference from GEDI output rather than sample-level classification No trained GEDI model exists (no Qi parameters); cells/genes have not yet been filtered (log10_total_counts > 2.5, log10_total_features_by_counts > 2, subsets_Mito_percent <= 20) and GEDI has not been run

skills.search_text: auroc-benchmark-evaluation Use when quantifying how gene set size or expression variability (CV) affects MetaNeighbor AUROC for cross-dataset cell-type identification, or when validating that a gene set performs above chance (AUROC ~0.5). Cell-type labels are missing or ambiguous across datasets — use unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes instead of the supervised AUROC benchmark. skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are missing or ambiguous across datasets — use unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes instead of the supervised AUROC benchmark. skills.description: Use when validating or reproducing marker gene identification quality for Cell Ontology terms — e.g. checking whether top-20 OnClass-ranked markers recover curated marker sets via AUROC for seen vs unseen cell types in Muris FACS/droplet data.
skills.name: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-against-curated-markers
skills.search_text: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-against-curated-markers Use when validating or reproducing marker gene identification quality for Cell Ontology terms — e.g. checking whether top-20 OnClass-ranked markers recover curated marker sets via AUROC for seen vs unseen cell types in Muris FACS/droplet data. The task is cell type annotation/classification accuracy rather than marker gene validation — use OnClass cross-validation (run_one_dataset_cross_validation.py) or cross-dataset prediction (run_cross_dataset_prediction.py) instead. You have no OnClass prediction matrices (pred_Y_all) — the marker ranking depends on Spearman correlation against each cell type's predicted probability vector, so de novo marker discovery without OnClass outputs is out of scope. You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings sharing the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — OnClass cannot separate them, so per-term AUROCs are uninformative for such pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces OnClass's marker gene identification benchmark: Spearman-rank all genes against each cell type's predicted probability vector in pred_Y_all, take the top 20 markers per Cell Ontology term, and compute AUROC against curated marker gene sets, stratified for seen and unseen terms in Tabula Muris FACS and droplet (0.87–0.97 seen; 0.87 unseen FACS; 0.82 unseen droplet). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Reproduces OnClass's marker gene identification benchmark: Spearman-rank all genes against each cell type's predicted probability vector in pred_Y_all, take the top 20 markers per Cell Ontology term, and compute AUROC against curated marker gene sets, stratified for seen and unseen terms in Tabula Muris FACS and droplet (0.87–0.97 seen; 0.87 unseen FACS; 0.82 unseen droplet).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell type annotation/classification accuracy rather than marker gene validation — use OnClass cross-validation (run_one_dataset_cross_validation.py) or cross-dataset prediction (run_cross_dataset_prediction.py) instead. You have no OnClass prediction matrices (pred_Y_all) — the marker ranking depends on Spearman correlation against each cell type's predicted probability vector, so de novo marker discovery without OnClass outputs is out of scope. You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings sharing the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — OnClass cannot separate them, so per-term AUROCs are uninformative for such pairs.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq cell-calling/filtering method against ground-truth barcode labels (e.g. HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative or demuxlet genetic labels) via AUROC, especially under a hyperparameter sweep.
skills.name: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-of-scrnaseq-barcodes
skills.search_text: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-of-scrnaseq-barcodes Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq cell-calling/filtering method against ground-truth barcode labels (e.g. HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative or demuxlet genetic labels) via AUROC, especially under a hyperparameter sweep. skills.summary: Rank self-signalling (autocrine) ligand–receptor edges from a single-cell atlas by summed specificity, testing whether cognate ligands and receptors are co-expressed within individual cell types. Applied with NATMI on Tabula Muris, it showed autocrine signalling is a major feature of cell-to-cell communication networks (719/2293 connectomeDB2020 pairs co-detected; median 54 co-detected pairs per cell type).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need downstream signalling consequences or pathway inference (NATMI does not predict downstream signalling; use tools like NicheNet/SoptSC) Spatial transcriptomics data where ligand–receiver spatial relationships matter (NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data) Ligand–receptor pairs require heteromeric complex or co-receptor modelling (NATMI does not model heterodimerization or co-receptor requirements)

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (h5ad or CSV/TSV) need denoising/imputation in one step while respecting count overdispersion, sparsity, and dropout.
skills.name: autoencoder-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: autoencoder-architecture-implementation Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (h5ad or CSV/TSV) need denoising/imputation in one step while respecting count overdispersion, sparsity, and dropout. Input is already normalized/log-transformed or not raw counts — the ZINB/NB noise model is defined on sparse count data The analysis requires imputing defined missing values (classical imputation); DCA instead denoises all entries since true and false zero counts cannot be trivially distinguished Datasets too large for memory or when a linear, non-parametric smoothing method is intended — though DCA itself scales linearly, this skill specifically covers the autoencoder architecture setup http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the DCA deep count autoencoder: a fixed network of three hidden layers (64, 32, 64 neurons) with a 32-dimensional bottleneck, ZINB/NB output heads, and a noise-model-likelihood reconstruction loss for denoising scRNA-seq count data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Implements the DCA deep count autoencoder: a fixed network of three hidden layers (64, 32, 64 neurons) with a 32-dimensional bottleneck, ZINB/NB output heads, and a noise-model-likelihood reconstruction loss for denoising scRNA-seq count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/log-transformed or not raw counts — the ZINB/NB noise model is defined on sparse count data The analysis requires imputing defined missing values (classical imputation); DCA instead denoises all entries since true and false zero counts cannot be trivially distinguished Datasets too large for memory or when a linear, non-parametric smoothing method is intended — though DCA itself scales linearly, this skill specifically covers the autoencoder architecture setup

skills.description: Use when highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., >80-95% zeros, masked .hd5 inputs like example.msk90.hd5) need imputation and you must build or reproduce the LATE autoencoder network in TensorFlow 1.x.
skills.name: autoencoder-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: autoencoder-architecture-implementation Use when highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., >80-95% zeros, masked .hd5 inputs like example.msk90.hd5) need imputation and you must build or reproduce the LATE autoencoder network in TensorFlow 1.x. You need to distinguish biological zeros from technical zeros: LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes them with nonzero values You want systematic hyperparameter tuning (as in DCA): LATE hyperparameters were manually tuned only Your environment only supports TensorFlow 2: the implementation requires TensorFlow 1.0-1.4 (or 1.15 in a virtualenv) and is not compatible with TensorFlow 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the LATE autoencoder architecture: an autoencoder with randomly initialized parameters, fully connected hidden layers (e.g., 400 nodes, ReLU), and dropout, trained on log10(count+1)-transformed sparse scRNA-seq data to reconstruct and impute missing (zero) expression values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Implements the LATE autoencoder architecture: an autoencoder with randomly initialized parameters, fully connected hidden layers (e.g., 400 nodes, ReLU), and dropout, trained on log10(count+1)-transformed sparse scRNA-seq data to reconstruct and impute missing (zero) expression values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to distinguish biological zeros from technical zeros: LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes them with nonzero values You want systematic hyperparameter tuning (as in DCA): LATE hyperparameters were manually tuned only Your environment only supports TensorFlow 2: the implementation requires TensorFlow 1.0-1.4 (or 1.15 in a virtualenv) and is not compatible with TensorFlow 2

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy with high dropout and you need a low-dimensional, part-based cell representation to support unsupervised clustering (e.g., ARI benchmarking against SC3, Seurat, CIDR).
skills.name: autoencoder-based-dimension-reduction
skills.search_text: autoencoder-based-dimension-reduction Use when scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy with high dropout and you need a low-dimensional, part-based cell representation to support unsupervised clustering (e.g., ARI benchmarking against SC3, Seurat, CIDR). The analysis goal is differential expression or marker detection on raw counts rather than cell segregation into a low-dimensional latent space The downstream tool requires its own dimensionality reduction (e.g., scVI-based workflows); note scDHA's comparison against scVI is deferred to supplementary material, so claims should not be extended blindly Data are not high-throughput single-cell expression matrices — generalization to other domains (cancer, obesity, aging) is asserted but not demonstrated in the article http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A two-module hierarchical autoencoder pipeline (scDHA) that denoises scRNA-seq data with a non-negative kernel autoencoder and projects cells into a compact low-dimensional space via a stacked Bayesian autoencoder, enabling clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: A two-module hierarchical autoencoder pipeline (scDHA) that denoises scRNA-seq data with a non-negative kernel autoencoder and projects cells into a compact low-dimensional space via a stacked Bayesian autoencoder, enabling clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential expression or marker detection on raw counts rather than cell segregation into a low-dimensional latent space The downstream tool requires its own dimensionality reduction (e.g., scVI-based workflows); note scDHA's comparison against scVI is deferred to supplementary material, so claims should not be extended blindly Data are not high-throughput single-cell expression matrices — generalization to other domains (cancer, obesity, aging) is asserted but not demonstrated in the article

skills.description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) with simulated dropout or low sampling efficiency (e.g., 5–10%) needs a denoised reconstruction before imputation or downstream clustering.
skills.name: autoencoder-based-expression-denoising
skills.search_text: autoencoder-based-expression-denoising Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) with simulated dropout or low sampling efficiency (e.g., 5–10%) needs a denoised reconstruction before imputation or downstream clustering. Small genomic datasets: SERM learns the model from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual distribution and yield inaccurate imputation values Datasets where ROI coverage is too small for the captured data distribution to be representative of the entire expression matrix Data requiring explicit batch-effect correction: SERM's formulation does not consider batch effects explicitly (only a z-score integration step is applied post-hoc) Train a deep autoencoder (as in SERM's first pipeline step) to extract a latent representation from sparse, dropout-affected scRNA-seq data and reconstruct denoised expression values, which then serve as the basis for distribution learning and histogram-equalization imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Train a deep autoencoder (as in SERM's first pipeline step) to extract a latent representation from sparse, dropout-affected scRNA-seq data and reconstruct denoised expression values, which then serve as the basis for distribution learning and histogram-equalization imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Small genomic datasets: SERM learns the model from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual distribution and yield inaccurate imputation values Datasets where ROI coverage is too small for the captured data distribution to be representative of the entire expression matrix Data requiring explicit batch-effect correction: SERM's formulation does not consider batch effects explicitly (only a z-score integration step is applied post-hoc)

skills.description: Use when Smart-seq2 or 10X single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC data must have multi-mapping reads accurately allocated to individual TE loci, rather than collapsed at subfamily level.
skills.name: autoencoder-based-multimapping-rate-regression
skills.search_text: autoencoder-based-multimapping-rate-regression Use when Smart-seq2 or 10X single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC data must have multi-mapping reads accurately allocated to individual TE loci, rather than collapsed at subfamily level. TEs longer than the 2001 bp coverage window (e.g. long autonomously expressed L1HS) — flanking coverage is incomplete and alpha_i estimates unreliable Nearly identical TE copies with no uniquely mappable flanking context (e.g. HERVK isoforms) — the model cannot distinguish loci Input is already a gene expression or feature count table with no alignment-level BAM data to derive coverage vectors from http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 MATES's deep learning core: an AutoEncoder trained on unique-read coverage vectors (Vu, with TE family one-hot encoding) produces latent embeddings that an MLP regressor uses to estimate locus-specific multi-mapping rates (alpha_i), enabling locus-specific TE quantification as URi + ceil(alpha_i x MRi) per cell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: MATES's deep learning core: an AutoEncoder trained on unique-read coverage vectors (Vu, with TE family one-hot encoding) produces latent embeddings that an MLP regressor uses to estimate locus-specific multi-mapping rates (alpha_i), enabling locus-specific TE quantification as URi + ceil(alpha_i x MRi) per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: TEs longer than the 2001 bp coverage window (e.g. long autonomously expressed L1HS) — flanking coverage is incomplete and alpha_i estimates unreliable Nearly identical TE copies with no uniquely mappable flanking context (e.g. HERVK isoforms) — the model cannot distinguish loci Input is already a gene expression or feature count table with no alignment-level BAM data to derive coverage vectors from

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired (non-co-assayed) single-cell modalities such as scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, CyTOF, smFISH, or morphology into a shared low-dimensional latent space for visualization, clustering, and cross-modality imputation.
skills.name: autoencoder-based-single-cell-multimodal-integration
skills.search_text: autoencoder-based-single-cell-multimodal-integration Use when integrating unpaired (non-co-assayed) single-cell modalities such as scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, CyTOF, smFISH, or morphology into a shared low-dimensional latent space for visualization, clustering, and cross-modality imputation. Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections entirely (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since the rIOT alignment relies on connections between features of different modalities Data are paired/co-assayed multimodal, or a mix of paired and unpaired multimodal data must be jointly integrated — scConfluence addresses diagonal integration of unpaired data only The goal requires handling rare cell populations reliably: rare populations are unlikely to be simultaneously sampled from each modality in mini-batches, a stated challenging limitation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Diagonal integration of unpaired single-cell multiomics data by training one uncoupled AutoEncoder per modality to map features into a shared 16-dimensional latent space, aligned with a regularized Inverse Optimal Transport (rIOT) objective computed from weakly connected cross-modality features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Diagonal integration of unpaired single-cell multiomics data by training one uncoupled AutoEncoder per modality to map features into a shared 16-dimensional latent space, aligned with a regularized Inverse Optimal Transport (rIOT) objective computed from weakly connected cross-modality features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections entirely (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since the rIOT alignment relies on connections between features of different modalities Data are paired/co-assayed multimodal, or a mix of paired and unpaired multimodal data must be jointly integrated — scConfluence addresses diagonal integration of unpaired data only The goal requires handling rare cell populations reliably: rare populations are unlikely to be simultaneously sampled from each modality in mini-batches, a stated challenging limitation

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (e.g., genes x cells CSV) contains dropouts and other noise, and a distribution-free deep learning imputation that preserves cell-type signal is needed.
skills.name: autoencoder-classifier-composite-network-implementation
skills.search_text: autoencoder-classifier-composite-network-implementation Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (e.g., genes x cells CSV) contains dropouts and other noise, and a distribution-free deep learning imputation that preserves cell-type signal is needed. When the method's strong distribution assumptions match your data better via alternatives with negative binomial assumptions (SAVER, DCA) or Gaussian/Gamma mixtures (scImpute) — i.e., when you specifically require model-based, distribution-assuming imputation rather than a distribution-agnostic network When input is not a raw count matrix (e.g., already normalized, batch-corrected, or a feature table), since the workflow starts from raw counts normalized via take_norm When TensorFlow (>=2.0) cannot be installed or GPU/NN training is infeasible for the data size http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements AutoClass, a composite deep neural network for scRNA-Seq denoising that couples an autoencoder's bottleneck layer to a classifier branch trained on virtual class labels from K-means pre-clustering, maximizing both noise removal and signal retention without distribution assumptions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Implements AutoClass, a composite deep neural network for scRNA-Seq denoising that couples an autoencoder's bottleneck layer to a classifier branch trained on virtual class labels from K-means pre-clustering, maximizing both noise removal and signal retention without distribution assumptions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the method's strong distribution assumptions match your data better via alternatives with negative binomial assumptions (SAVER, DCA) or Gaussian/Gamma mixtures (scImpute) — i.e., when you specifically require model-based, distribution-assuming imputation rather than a distribution-agnostic network When input is not a raw count matrix (e.g., already normalized, batch-corrected, or a feature table), since the workflow starts from raw counts normalized via take_norm When TensorFlow (>=2.0) cannot be installed or GPU/NN training is infeasible for the data size

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes) is sparse due to dropout/low capture efficiency and you need denoised imputed expression values without training method-specific deep models per dataset.
skills.name: autoencoder-denoising-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: autoencoder-denoising-distribution-fitting Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes) is sparse due to dropout/low capture efficiency and you need denoised imputed expression values without training method-specific deep models per dataset. Small genomic datasets: the paper notes SERM learns from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations Cases where explicit batch-effect correction is required — batch effects are not considered in the SERM formulation Datasets where ROI coverage is too small for the captured ROI distribution to be representative of the entire matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Core SERM mechanism from Islam et al. (Nat Commun 2022): a deep autoencoder first learns the underlying scRNA-seq expression distribution from the sparse observed matrix, then a fitted probability distribution is used for histogram-based imputation of the gene expression matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Core SERM mechanism from Islam et al. (Nat Commun 2022): a deep autoencoder first learns the underlying scRNA-seq expression distribution from the sparse observed matrix, then a fitted probability distribution is used for histogram-based imputation of the gene expression matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Small genomic datasets: the paper notes SERM learns from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations Cases where explicit batch-effect correction is required — batch effects are not considered in the SERM formulation Datasets where ROI coverage is too small for the captured ROI distribution to be representative of the entire matrix

skills.description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix with simulated dropout (low sampling efficiency, e.g. 0.1%–10%) must be denoised before downstream distribution learning or imputation, and you need a latent representation of the noisy data.
skills.name: autoencoder-denoising-of-scrna-seq-expression
skills.search_text: autoencoder-denoising-of-scrna-seq-expression Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix with simulated dropout (low sampling efficiency, e.g. 0.1%–10%) must be denoised before downstream distribution learning or imputation, and you need a latent representation of the noisy data. Input is already a clean, dropout-free reference matrix (e.g. reference data created by choosing cells and genes with high expression) — denoising targets sparse observed data Small genomic datasets, where the distribution learned from a small data subset may diverge from the true data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations Analyses that explicitly require batch-effect modeling — batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a three-layer autoencoder (logistic sigmoid encoder, linear decoder, latent dimension P=2) on a small random subset of a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. data_observed_10perc.mat) to reconstruct denoised expression values (matrix So), the first modeling stage of SERM's gene expression recovery pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Trains a three-layer autoencoder (logistic sigmoid encoder, linear decoder, latent dimension P=2) on a small random subset of a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. data_observed_10perc.mat) to reconstruct denoised expression values (matrix So), the first modeling stage of SERM's gene expression recovery pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a clean, dropout-free reference matrix (e.g. reference data created by choosing cells and genes with high expression) — denoising targets sparse observed data Small genomic datasets, where the distribution learned from a small data subset may diverge from the true data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations Analyses that explicitly require batch-effect modeling — batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking autoencoder-derived latent features of scRNA-seq data against original profiles and correlation-based features (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman) via silhouette values against true cell-type labels.
skills.name: autoencoder-feature-extraction-scrna
skills.search_text: autoencoder-feature-extraction-scrna Use when benchmarking autoencoder-derived latent features of scRNA-seq data against original profiles and correlation-based features (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman) via silhouette values against true cell-type labels. You need a feature construction method guaranteed to improve accordance with true cluster labels — the paper found only the Spearman correlation-based method consistently improved across all five datasets, not the autoencoder. The input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than scRNA-seq expression profiles that need encoding. Working with a very large dataset without an R build linked to an optimized BLAS (ATLAS, MKL) — the sscClust README warns calculations become expensive and recommends Microsoft R Open on Windows. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains an autoencoder on scRNA-seq expression profiles to derive per-cell latent features and scores them by silhouette coefficients against true cell-type labels, as one of the five feature-construction variants (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman, autoencoder) benchmarked in the SSCC framework (Figure 2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: Trains an autoencoder on scRNA-seq expression profiles to derive per-cell latent features and scores them by silhouette coefficients against true cell-type labels, as one of the five feature-construction variants (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman, autoencoder) benchmarked in the SSCC framework (Figure 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a feature construction method guaranteed to improve accordance with true cluster labels — the paper found only the Spearman correlation-based method consistently improved across all five datasets, not the autoencoder. The input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than scRNA-seq expression profiles that need encoding. Working with a very large dataset without an R build linked to an optimized BLAS (ATLAS, MKL) — the sscClust README warns calculations become expensive and recommends Microsoft R Open on Windows.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) is high-dimensional and noisy, and you must remove uninformative genes before training a stacked variational autoencoder or graph-based clustering.
skills.name: autoencoder-feature-selection
skills.search_text: autoencoder-feature-selection Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) is high-dimensional and noisy, and you must remove uninformative genes before training a stacked variational autoencoder or graph-based clustering. The input is already a low-dimensional feature representation or has previously been feature-selected, so a second non-negative-kernel autoencoder pass would be redundant. The analysis goal is supervised marker-gene selection using known cell-type labels rather than unsupervised noise filtering prior to clustering. The dataset is very large (hundreds of thousands to millions of cells, e.g. Brain 1.3M GSE93421) without applying scCAN's Module 3 train/test split — train the autoencoder on the 5000-cell training set and classify remaining cells by k-NN instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Feature-filtering step from scCAN's Module 1: a min-max-scaled, non-negative-kernel autoencoder with a 50-dimension bottleneck ranks genes so that only informative features are carried into downstream dimensionality reduction and clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Feature-filtering step from scCAN's Module 1: a min-max-scaled, non-negative-kernel autoencoder with a 50-dimension bottleneck ranks genes so that only informative features are carried into downstream dimensionality reduction and clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a low-dimensional feature representation or has previously been feature-selected, so a second non-negative-kernel autoencoder pass would be redundant. The analysis goal is supervised marker-gene selection using known cell-type labels rather than unsupervised noise filtering prior to clustering. The dataset is very large (hundreds of thousands to millions of cells, e.g. Brain 1.3M GSE93421) without applying scCAN's Module 3 train/test split — train the autoencoder on the 5000-cell training set and classify remaining cells by k-NN instead.

skills.description: Use when annotating normal (non-disease) scRNA-seq query data with a pre-trained SELINA model and the query distribution differs from the reference, requiring adaptation of pre-trained parameters before label transfer.
skills.name: autoencoder-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: autoencoder-fine-tuning Use when annotating normal (non-disease) scRNA-seq query data with a pre-trained SELINA model and the query distribution differs from the reference, requiring adaptation of pre-trained parameters before label transfer. Query data is a disease dataset (e.g. NSCLC, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's) — use --disease mode, which removes the fine-tuning step since disease expression profiles deviate substantially from normal data No pre-trained model exists yet for the target tissue/reference — selina train must run first to produce pre-trained_params.pt http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fine-tunes SELINA's MADA pre-trained parameters on query data with an autoencoder whose encoder reuses the feature extractor plus cell-type discriminator, so pre-trained reference features adapt to the query data distribution before label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Fine-tunes SELINA's MADA pre-trained parameters on query data with an autoencoder whose encoder reuses the feature extractor plus cell-type discriminator, so pre-trained reference features adapt to the query data distribution before label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data is a disease dataset (e.g. NSCLC, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's) — use --disease mode, which removes the fine-tuning step since disease expression profiles deviate substantially from normal data No pre-trained model exists yet for the target tissue/reference — selina train must run first to produce pre-trained_params.pt

skills.description: Use when running AutoImpute's autoencoder imputation on a scRNA-seq count matrix and per-dataset hyper-parameters (lambda, hidden units, initial learning rate, threshold) must be chosen from Table 2-style settings.
skills.name: autoencoder-hyperparameter-grid-selection
skills.search_text: autoencoder-hyperparameter-grid-selection Use when running AutoImpute's autoencoder imputation on a scRNA-seq count matrix and per-dataset hyper-parameters (lambda, hidden units, initial learning rate, threshold) must be chosen from Table 2-style settings. The input is raw unpre-processed count data in CSV form — it must first be run through the R-script pre-process.R before AutoImpute.py can consume it. The target tool is a matrix-factorization or nuclear-norm imputer rather than the TensorFlow overcomplete autoencoder — its hyper-parameters (lambda_val, hidden_units) do not exist there. Only a single one-shot imputation without repeated initialization is needed — the 10-repeat aggregation is designed to control for random weight initialization and would be unnecessary overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Select per-dataset hyper-parameters (regularization coefficient lambda, hidden/latent layer size, learning rate, convergence threshold) for the AutoImpute overcomplete-autoencoder used to impute sparse scRNA-seq expression matrices, so that imputation quality is tuned per dataset rather than fixed globally. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Select per-dataset hyper-parameters (regularization coefficient lambda, hidden/latent layer size, learning rate, convergence threshold) for the AutoImpute overcomplete-autoencoder used to impute sparse scRNA-seq expression matrices, so that imputation quality is tuned per dataset rather than fixed globally.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unpre-processed count data in CSV form — it must first be run through the R-script pre-process.R before AutoImpute.py can consume it. The target tool is a matrix-factorization or nuclear-norm imputer rather than the TensorFlow overcomplete autoencoder — its hyper-parameters (lambda_val, hidden_units) do not exist there. Only a single one-shot imputation without repeated initialization is needed — the 10-repeat aggregation is designed to control for random weight initialization and would be unnecessary overhead.

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed, log-transformed single-cell count matrix (cells x genes, CSV or .mat) has dropouts or artificially masked non-zero values that need imputation with an overcomplete autoencoder, or when benchmarking imputation recovery error.

skills.summary: Train the AutoImpute overcomplete-autoencoder on sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (CSV/MAT, cells as rows, genes as columns) with TensorFlow/RMSProp, tuning lambda, hidden units, learning rate, and convergence threshold per dataset. Used to impute dropouts or to run masked-matrix recovery benchmarks (NMSE/RMSE/MAE).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix has not been pre-processed/log-transformed — run pre-process.R first rather than feeding raw counts to AutoImpute.py The baseline imputer under comparison is drImpute in a masked-recovery benchmark, since its gene-filtering preprocessing changes matrix dimensions and makes error computation invalid The dataset is very large (e.g. PBMC was excluded from the masked-recovery test due to its size)
