skills.name: autoencoder-latent-vector-extraction
skills.search_text: autoencoder-latent-vector-extraction Use when segmented single-cell masks from multiplexed tissue imaging need quantitative shape descriptors, e.g., feeding cell-shape latent vectors into t-SNE analysis downstream of MIRIAM segmentation. Analysis goal is t-SNE on marker intensities rather than cell shape — the article treats intensity-based t-SNE (Fig. 3A) as a separate input modality No cell segmentation has been performed yet; this skill requires MIRIAM segmented cell masks as input, not raw multiplexed image stacks Latent vectors already exist in latent_vectors.csv for all cells — re-training the autoencoder is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains an autoencoder neural network on binary segmented cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline to produce compact latent-vector encodings of cell shape, implemented in Matlab (Deep Learning Toolbox) or Python (Keras) with 256-unit hidden layers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Trains an autoencoder neural network on binary segmented cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline to produce compact latent-vector encodings of cell shape, implemented in Matlab (Deep Learning Toolbox) or Python (Keras) with 256-unit hidden layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis goal is t-SNE on marker intensities rather than cell shape — the article treats intensity-based t-SNE (Fig. 3A) as a separate input modality No cell segmentation has been performed yet; this skill requires MIRIAM segmented cell masks as input, not raw multiplexed image stacks Latent vectors already exist in latent_vectors.csv for all cells — re-training the autoencoder is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when building or retuning a BEENE get_hybrid_model_1 autoencoder for RNA-seq batch-effect estimation and you must choose λ1/λ2/λ3 and dropout based on feature count, dimensionality reduction, and biological variables.
skills.name: autoencoder-loss-weight-configuration
skills.search_text: autoencoder-loss-weight-configuration Use when building or retuning a BEENE get_hybrid_model_1 autoencoder for RNA-seq batch-effect estimation and you must choose λ1/λ2/λ3 and dropout based on feature count, dimensionality reduction, and biological variables. The downstream goal is batch correction/removal rather than detection and estimation of batch effects — BEENE is an estimation technique whose embedding clusters by batch when batch_weight is high Features are already reduced to a few hundred via a dimensionality-reduction technique but you set λ1=0.001, which the Table 1 guideline reserves for thousands of unreduced features The batch variable has no label information — λ2 requires supervised batch-label prediction to tune the embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Guidance for setting the joint-loss weights (reconstruction_weight λ1, batch_weight λ2, bio_weight λ3) of the BEENE deep autoencoder, plus input-layer dropout, so the learned embedding balances reconstruction quality against batch-effect sensitivity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Guidance for setting the joint-loss weights (reconstruction_weight λ1, batch_weight λ2, bio_weight λ3) of the BEENE deep autoencoder, plus input-layer dropout, so the learned embedding balances reconstruction quality against batch-effect sensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream goal is batch correction/removal rather than detection and estimation of batch effects — BEENE is an estimation technique whose embedding clusters by batch when batch_weight is high Features are already reduced to a few hundred via a dimensionality-reduction technique but you set λ1=0.001, which the Table 1 guideline reserves for thousands of unreduced features The batch variable has no label information — λ2 requires supervised batch-label prediction to tune the embedding

skills.description: Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy or high-dimensional (many cells, high dropout) and a compressed cell embedding is needed before clustering, visualization, cell classification, or pseudo-time inference.
skills.name: autoencoder-low-dimensional-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: autoencoder-low-dimensional-feature-extraction Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy or high-dimensional (many cells, high dropout) and a compressed cell embedding is needed before clustering, visualization, cell classification, or pseudo-time inference. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or compressed feature table — the first module's gene/component filtering based on encoder weight distribution assumes a raw gene-by-cell expression matrix. No labeled training set exists for the target cells — scDHA.class requires train data matrix, train data label and new data matrix, so use the unsupervised path (scDHA + result$cluster) instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts compact, denoised low-dimensional representations of scRNA-seq data with scDHA's hierarchical autoencoder: a non-negative kernel autoencoder first removes insignificant genes/components, then a stacked Bayesian self-learning network compresses cells for clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Extracts compact, denoised low-dimensional representations of scRNA-seq data with scDHA's hierarchical autoencoder: a non-negative kernel autoencoder first removes insignificant genes/components, then a stacked Bayesian self-learning network compresses cells for clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or compressed feature table — the first module's gene/component filtering based on encoder weight distribution assumes a raw gene-by-cell expression matrix. No labeled training set exists for the target cells — scDHA.class requires train data matrix, train data label and new data matrix, so use the unsupervised path (scDHA + result$cluster) instead.

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (cells x top high-dispersion genes, .csv) contains dropout dropouts that must be imputed via overcomplete autoencoder reconstruction, e.g. blakeley.csv.
skills.name: autoencoder-masked-reconstruction-training
skills.search_text: autoencoder-masked-reconstruction-training Use when a preprocessed sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (cells x top high-dispersion genes, .csv) contains dropout dropouts that must be imputed via overcomplete autoencoder reconstruction, e.g. blakeley.csv. The matrix is already dense / free of dropouts — no imputation is needed Only raw unprocessed counts are available and R pre-processing (top-1000 high-dispersion gene selection, log2 transform) via pre-process.R has not been done The goal is de novo gene discovery or differential expression rather than dropout imputation of an existing partially observed matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train AutoImpute, a three-layer fully-connected overcomplete autoencoder (TensorFlow MLP), on a sparse log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrix to reconstruct the complete gene expression matrix, treating dropout imputation as a matrix-completion problem. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Train AutoImpute, a three-layer fully-connected overcomplete autoencoder (TensorFlow MLP), on a sparse log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrix to reconstruct the complete gene expression matrix, treating dropout imputation as a matrix-completion problem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is already dense / free of dropouts — no imputation is needed Only raw unprocessed counts are available and R pre-processing (top-1000 high-dispersion gene selection, log2 transform) via pre-process.R has not been done The goal is de novo gene discovery or differential expression rather than dropout imputation of an existing partially observed matrix

skills.description: Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. top 1000 high-dispersion genes, .csv/.mat) contains dropout zeros and needs imputation before clustering or expression-recovery analysis.
skills.name: autoencoder-matrix-completion
skills.search_text: autoencoder-matrix-completion Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. top 1000 high-dispersion genes, .csv/.mat) contains dropout zeros and needs imputation before clustering or expression-recovery analysis. The matrix has not been R-preprocessed (raw .csv not yet log2-transformed, library-size normalized, and reduced to high-dispersion genes) — run Rscript pre-process.R first The goal is masked-matrix recovery benchmarking rather than genuine dropout imputation — set --masked_matrix_test True only for that evaluation mode The input is already dense/imputed, so training an autoencoder to complete it adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Imputes dropout events in sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices using AutoImpute, a three-layer overcomplete autoencoder (TensorFlow) trained by gradient descent, framing the task as a collaborative-filtering-style matrix completion problem. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Imputes dropout events in sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices using AutoImpute, a three-layer overcomplete autoencoder (TensorFlow) trained by gradient descent, framing the task as a collaborative-filtering-style matrix completion problem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix has not been R-preprocessed (raw .csv not yet log2-transformed, library-size normalized, and reduced to high-dispersion genes) — run Rscript pre-process.R first The goal is masked-matrix recovery benchmarking rather than genuine dropout imputation — set --masked_matrix_test True only for that evaluation mode The input is already dense/imputed, so training an autoencoder to complete it adds no information

skills.description: Use when starting a DESC clustering workflow on preprocessed scRNA-seq data (log1p-transformed, top-1000 HVGs, scaled) and a low-dimensional embedding is needed to initialize cluster centers.
skills.name: autoencoder-pretraining
skills.search_text: autoencoder-pretraining Use when starting a DESC clustering workflow on preprocessed scRNA-seq data (log1p-transformed, top-1000 HVGs, scaled) and a low-dimensional embedding is needed to initialize cluster centers. Input is raw UMI counts that have not undergone cell-level normalization (divide by total UMIs, multiply by 10,000, natural log transform) and gene-level standardization The analysis explicitly requires batch information to be incorporated, as in scVI or BERMUDA, rather than implicit batch-effect removal via iterative self-learning http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pretrain a stacked autoencoder to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the gene expression matrix, serving as parameter initialization for DESC's iterative KL-divergence self-training clustering of scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Pretrain a stacked autoencoder to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the gene expression matrix, serving as parameter initialization for DESC's iterative KL-divergence self-training clustering of scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw UMI counts that have not undergone cell-level normalization (divide by total UMIs, multiply by 10,000, natural log transform) and gene-level standardization The analysis explicitly requires batch information to be incorporated, as in scVI or BERMUDA, rather than implicit batch-effect removal via iterative self-learning

skills.description: Use when quantifying whether an SCA/SSCA latent space (built from TF, miRNA, kinase targets, or immune signatures) reconstructs a given single-cell cluster, or when comparing knowledge-group combinations (e.g., TF+miRNA vs TF alone) by QCM/QCC on a counts table with pre-computed clusters.
skills.name: autoencoder-quality-metric-evaluation-qcm-qcc
skills.search_text: autoencoder-quality-metric-evaluation-qcm-qcc Use when quantifying whether an SCA/SSCA latent space (built from TF, miRNA, kinase targets, or immune signatures) reconstructs a given single-cell cluster, or when comparing knowledge-group combinations (e.g., TF+miRNA vs TF alone) by QCM/QCC on a counts table with pre-computed clusters. Input lacks pre-computed cluster assignments — SCA/QCM/QCC evaluate reconstruction of defined clusters, not perform the initial clustering itself Goal is general-purpose benchmarking of arbitrary (non-knowledge-guided) autoencoders — QCM/QCC are specific to SCA's sparsely-connected, knowledge-derived encoded space Single-cell data exceed ~80% zero counts such that normalization tools like SCnorm cannot converge (per SCnorm README), making upstream counts unreliable for SCA encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Evaluate the quality of Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) cluster reconstruction on scRNAseq data using the two bespoke metrics QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model), with a significance threshold of mean QCM and QCC ≥ 0.5 marking clusters successfully reconstructed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Evaluate the quality of Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) cluster reconstruction on scRNAseq data using the two bespoke metrics QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model), with a significance threshold of mean QCM and QCC ≥ 0.5 marking clusters successfully reconstructed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks pre-computed cluster assignments — SCA/QCM/QCC evaluate reconstruction of defined clusters, not perform the initial clustering itself Goal is general-purpose benchmarking of arbitrary (non-knowledge-guided) autoencoders — QCM/QCC are specific to SCA's sparsely-connected, knowledge-derived encoded space Single-cell data exceed ~80% zero counts such that normalization tools like SCnorm cannot converge (per SCnorm README), making upstream counts unreliable for SCA encoding

skills.description: Use when training the scDHA non-negative kernel autoencoder module on a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq matrix and you need to verify reconstruction-loss convergence before ranking genes by encoder weight variance.
skills.name: autoencoder-training-convergence-monitoring
skills.search_text: autoencoder-training-convergence-monitoring Use when training the scDHA non-negative kernel autoencoder module on a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq matrix and you need to verify reconstruction-loss convergence before ranking genes by encoder weight variance. The goal is the second scDHA module (low-dimensional projection via the Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network/VAE) rather than gene filtering in module 1 The input matrix is already the filtered ~5000-gene set, so re-ranking encoder weights would be redundant The task is downstream pseudotime or classification (scDHA.pt / scDHA.class), which consume the reduced representation rather than train the filtering autoencoder http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains scDHA's first-module non-negative kernel autoencoder — a one-layer network with a 50-node bottleneck on min-max/log2-scaled scRNA-seq count matrices — until reconstruction loss converges, producing a part-based representation whose encoder weight distribution drives gene filtering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Trains scDHA's first-module non-negative kernel autoencoder — a one-layer network with a 50-node bottleneck on min-max/log2-scaled scRNA-seq count matrices — until reconstruction loss converges, producing a part-based representation whose encoder weight distribution drives gene filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is the second scDHA module (low-dimensional projection via the Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network/VAE) rather than gene filtering in module 1 The input matrix is already the filtered ~5000-gene set, so re-ranking encoder weights would be redundant The task is downstream pseudotime or classification (scDHA.pt / scDHA.class), which consume the reduced representation rather than train the filtering autoencoder

skills.description: Use when quantifying transposable elements at locus level in scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq data: multi-mapping reads must be allocated to specific TE loci using unique-read flanking context before counting.
skills.name: autoencoder-training-on-coverage-vectors
skills.search_text: autoencoder-training-on-coverage-vectors Use when quantifying transposable elements at locus level in scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq data: multi-mapping reads must be allocated to specific TE loci using unique-read flanking context before counting. TEs longer than 2001 bp (e.g., L1HS or long autonomously expressed elements) where flanking coverage vectors are incomplete and alpha estimates may be inaccurate Highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, where the AE cannot distinguish loci Datasets without sufficient multi-mapping TE reads or TE families with fewer than 50 training samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a MATES AutoEncoder on unique-mapping-read coverage vectors (Vu) spanning 2001 bp around each TE start, with one-hot TE-family encoding, to learn latent local-read-context embeddings used to predict locus-specific multi-mapping ratios in single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Train a MATES AutoEncoder on unique-mapping-read coverage vectors (Vu) spanning 2001 bp around each TE start, with one-hot TE-family encoding, to learn latent local-read-context embeddings used to predict locus-specific multi-mapping ratios in single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: TEs longer than 2001 bp (e.g., L1HS or long autonomously expressed elements) where flanking coverage vectors are incomplete and alpha estimates may be inaccurate Highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, where the AE cannot distinguish loci Datasets without sufficient multi-mapping TE reads or TE families with fewer than 50 training samples

skills.description: Use when a normalized, log1p-transformed cell-by-gene scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Klein dataset, top 5000 Seurat HVGs) still contains dropouts and you need a statistically grounded imputation via a two-part-generalized-gamma autoencoder.
skills.name: autoencoder-training-on-gene-expression
skills.search_text: autoencoder-training-on-gene-expression Use when a normalized, log1p-transformed cell-by-gene scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Klein dataset, top 5000 Seurat HVGs) still contains dropouts and you need a statistically grounded imputation via a two-part-generalized-gamma autoencoder. The task is dimensionality reduction rather than imputation — for that the README uses the 68K PBMC example and saves adata_filtered.obsm['X_ae_tpgg'] instead of computing the TPGG mean. The input matrix is raw counts that have not been converted to semi-continuous form (normalize_per_cell + log1p), since AE-TPGG is designed for semi-continuous normalized data. The dataset has more than the selected highly variable gene set (e.g. full transcriptome without the Seurat top-5000 HVG filter), which the imputation example does not cover. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the AE-TPGG autoencoder (Keras with TensorFlow backend) on semi-continuous normalized scRNA-seq data to obtain fitted two-part-generalized-gamma parameters, then compute the TPGG mean as a denoised, dropout-free imputed expression matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s11704-022-2011-y
skills.summary: Train the AE-TPGG autoencoder (Keras with TensorFlow backend) on semi-continuous normalized scRNA-seq data to obtain fitted two-part-generalized-gamma parameters, then compute the TPGG mean as a denoised, dropout-free imputed expression matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is dimensionality reduction rather than imputation — for that the README uses the 68K PBMC example and saves adata_filtered.obsm['X_ae_tpgg'] instead of computing the TPGG mean. The input matrix is raw counts that have not been converted to semi-continuous form (normalize_per_cell + log1p), since AE-TPGG is designed for semi-continuous normalized data. The dataset has more than the selected highly variable gene set (e.g. full transcriptome without the Seurat top-5000 HVG filter), which the imputation example does not cover.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data are highly sparse (typically >80-95% zeros) and the goal is to recover true expression behind dropout zeros via autoencoder-based imputation with no reference dataset.
skills.name: autoencoder-training-on-sparse-counts
skills.search_text: autoencoder-training-on-sparse-counts Use when scRNA-seq count data are highly sparse (typically >80-95% zeros) and the goal is to recover true expression behind dropout zeros via autoencoder-based imputation with no reference dataset. When a labeled reference gene expression dataset is available and transfer learning initialization is desired — use TRANSLATE (pre-training + translate steps) instead of de novo LATE When zeros must be distinguished into biological vs technical zeros — LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes zeros with a nonzero value When only TensorFlow 2 is available — LATE is not compatible with TF2 and requires a TensorFlow 1.x (1.0-1.4) environment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train an autoencoder de novo on highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices using LATE (Learning with AuToEncoder), treating zeros as missing values and leveraging gene/cell dependence to impute them. Runs on TensorFlow 1.x with Python 3.5+ and scales to 1M+ cells on a GPU. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Train an autoencoder de novo on highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices using LATE (Learning with AuToEncoder), treating zeros as missing values and leveraging gene/cell dependence to impute them. Runs on TensorFlow 1.x with Python 3.5+ and scales to 1M+ cells on a GPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a labeled reference gene expression dataset is available and transfer learning initialization is desired — use TRANSLATE (pre-training + translate steps) instead of de novo LATE When zeros must be distinguished into biological vs technical zeros — LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes zeros with a nonzero value When only TensorFlow 2 is available — LATE is not compatible with TF2 and requires a TensorFlow 1.x (1.0-1.4) environment

skills.description: Use when you must choose the hidden-layer width of an autoencoder or a dropout-augmentation strength for DCNet by comparing train/test RMSE on log2(x+1)-transformed TCGA expression data.
skills.name: autoencoder-variant-training
skills.search_text: autoencoder-variant-training Use when you must choose the hidden-layer width of an autoencoder or a dropout-augmentation strength for DCNet by comparing train/test RMSE on log2(x+1)-transformed TCGA expression data. Your goal is to run DCNet on new samples for cell-landscape inference using the pretrained parameters rather than retraining/selecting model variants. Your input is not a gene-symbol-by-sample expression matrix (e.g. already a feature/cell-abundance table) or cannot be log2(x+1)-transformed. You need hyperparameter tuning beyond the fixed adam/relu/L2loss, lr 1e-4, 600-iteration, batch-256 CPU recipe; the paper reports no seed or tuning controls. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a sweep of autoencoder variants (AE64–AE4096) and dropout-augmented DCNet variants (D0–D50) on TCGA bulk RNA-seq to select the best model by RMSE, anchoring the DCNet architecture in the AE with the lowest test error (AE2048). transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Trains a sweep of autoencoder variants (AE64–AE4096) and dropout-augmented DCNet variants (D0–D50) on TCGA bulk RNA-seq to select the best model by RMSE, anchoring the DCNet architecture in the AE with the lowest test error (AE2048).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to run DCNet on new samples for cell-landscape inference using the pretrained parameters rather than retraining/selecting model variants. Your input is not a gene-symbol-by-sample expression matrix (e.g. already a feature/cell-abundance table) or cannot be log2(x+1)-transformed. You need hyperparameter tuning beyond the fixed adam/relu/L2loss, lr 1e-4, 600-iteration, batch-256 CPU recipe; the paper reports no seed or tuning controls.

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq dataset has published manual cell-type annotations and you need to check whether an unsupervised annotator (ScType) reproduces them from raw counts alone.
skills.name: automated-cell-type-validation-against-manual-annotations
skills.search_text: automated-cell-type-validation-against-manual-annotations Use when a raw scRNA-seq dataset has published manual cell-type annotations and you need to check whether an unsupervised annotator (ScType) reproduces them from raw counts alone. The dataset has no published manual annotations to validate against, so there is no ground truth for the benchmark. The tissue is not represented in the ScType marker database, so gene_sets_prepare() cannot yield Liver-like gs_positive/gs_negative sets. The input is already an annotated Seurat object and the goal is de novo discovery rather than validating an automated annotator. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark the ScType fully-automated cell-type annotator against the manual annotations of a published atlas, e.g. reproducing the human liver atlas (GSE124395) where 17 Seurat clusters must map to 11 liver cell types, including the CD19/CD20/CD138 split of B-cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Benchmark the ScType fully-automated cell-type annotator against the manual annotations of a published atlas, e.g. reproducing the human liver atlas (GSE124395) where 17 Seurat clusters must map to 11 liver cell types, including the CD19/CD20/CD138 split of B-cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no published manual annotations to validate against, so there is no ground truth for the benchmark. The tissue is not represented in the ScType marker database, so gene_sets_prepare() cannot yield Liver-like gs_positive/gs_negative sets. The input is already an annotated Seurat object and the goal is de novo discovery rather than validating an automated annotator.

skills.description: Use when building a transformer language model whose autoregressive pretraining target is gene expression rankings (not counts) of single-cell transcriptomes, e.g. reproducing tGPT or adapting GPT2LMHeadModel to a gene-token vocabulary.
skills.name: autoregressive-gene-ranking-language-modeling
skills.search_text: autoregressive-gene-ranking-language-modeling Use when building a transformer language model whose autoregressive pretraining target is gene expression rankings (not counts) of single-cell transcriptomes, e.g. reproducing tGPT or adapting GPT2LMHeadModel to a gene-token vocabulary. The goal is modeling actual expression levels or fold changes — tGPT input is gene expression rankings only, so magnitude information is lost The analysis depends on information from low-expressing genes — tGPT uses only top-expressing genes (62 or 126) and may miss signals in low-expressing genes Only raw, unfiltered counts are available — cells must first be filtered (expressed genes <200 or mitochondrial counts >30% removed) and mitochondrial/ribosomal/non-protein-coding genes discarded before rank construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct and pretrain tGPT, a GPT-style autoregressive transformer (8 decoder blocks, 1024 hidden units, 16 attention heads) that generatively models the rankings of top-expressing genes per cell over a 20,706-gene vocabulary, enabling integration of 22.3 million single-cell transcriptomes insensitive to batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Reconstruct and pretrain tGPT, a GPT-style autoregressive transformer (8 decoder blocks, 1024 hidden units, 16 attention heads) that generatively models the rankings of top-expressing genes per cell over a 20,706-gene vocabulary, enabling integration of 22.3 million single-cell transcriptomes insensitive to batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is modeling actual expression levels or fold changes — tGPT input is gene expression rankings only, so magnitude information is lost The analysis depends on information from low-expressing genes — tGPT uses only top-expressing genes (62 or 126) and may miss signals in low-expressing genes Only raw, unfiltered counts are available — cells must first be filtered (expressed genes <200 or mitochondrial counts >30% removed) and mitochondrial/ribosomal/non-protein-coding genes discarded before rank construction

skills.description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells source-free with scEMAIL and you need per-cell uncertainty from the main classifier plus two auxiliary classifiers to later detect novel cell types via E-score bimodality.
skills.name: auxiliary-classifier-ensemble-consistency
skills.search_text: auxiliary-classifier-ensemble-consistency Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells source-free with scEMAIL and you need per-cell uncertainty from the main classifier plus two auxiliary classifiers to later detect novel cell types via E-score bimodality. Source raw data are available, so uncertainty can be derived directly from supervised alignment rather than the source-free expert ensemble You only need a final cell-type label with no novel-cell-type perception — a plain classifier argmax suffices without E-score computation The pre-trained source model lacks the two auxiliary co-training classifiers, so CS cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes a per-cell expert-ensemble E-score for scRNA-seq target cells by combining normalized entropy, confidence, and auxiliary-classifier consistency from a pre-trained source model, quantifying how certain each cell belongs to a known cell type in scEMAIL's novel cell-type perception module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Computes a per-cell expert-ensemble E-score for scRNA-seq target cells by combining normalized entropy, confidence, and auxiliary-classifier consistency from a pre-trained source model, quantifying how certain each cell belongs to a known cell type in scEMAIL's novel cell-type perception module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source raw data are available, so uncertainty can be derived directly from supervised alignment rather than the source-free expert ensemble You only need a final cell-type label with no novel-cell-type perception — a plain classifier argmax suffices without E-score computation The pre-trained source model lacks the two auxiliary co-training classifiers, so CS cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when two single-cell 3′ gene-expression datasets differ by a handling variable (freeze-thaw, library prep) and you must show equivalence of average expression and per-cell sensitivity (genes/UMIs) before downstream cell-type classification.
skills.name: average-gene-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: average-gene-expression-correlation-analysis Use when two single-cell 3′ gene-expression datasets differ by a handling variable (freeze-thaw, library prep) and you must show equivalence of average expression and per-cell sensitivity (genes/UMIs) before downstream cell-type classification. The libraries differ in sequencing depth and you cannot downsample to equal mean reads per cell — depth confounds the correlation and per-cell counts Input is single-cell data from a non-droplet platform whose gene-barcode matrices were not generated by Cell Ranger-style 3′ counting, so sensitivity metrics are not comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how well two scRNA-seq preparations (e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs) match by computing the Pearson correlation of average gene expression across gene-barcode matrices, complemented by t-tests on per-cell genes and UMI counts, to judge whether sample handling compromises profiling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Quantifies how well two scRNA-seq preparations (e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs) match by computing the Pearson correlation of average gene expression across gene-barcode matrices, complemented by t-tests on per-cell genes and UMI counts, to judge whether sample handling compromises profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The libraries differ in sequencing depth and you cannot downsample to equal mean reads per cell — depth confounds the correlation and per-cell counts Input is single-cell data from a non-droplet platform whose gene-barcode matrices were not generated by Cell Ranger-style 3′ counting, so sensitivity metrics are not comparable

skills.description: Use when comparing alternative hierarchical correction algorithms for Cell Ontology-based classification and you need a threshold-free metric (average precision) plus per-cell-type PR curves to establish whether a correction degrades or preserves the baseline.
skills.name: average-precision-benchmarking

skills.description: Use when classifying breast cancer RNA-seq samples into the five intrinsic subtypes (Luminal A/B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like) and the standard median-based PAM50 reference is sensitive to cohort composition or a single-sample, reference-independent caller is needed.
skills.name: awca-reference-construction
skills.search_text: awca-reference-construction Use when classifying breast cancer RNA-seq samples into the five intrinsic subtypes (Luminal A/B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like) and the standard median-based PAM50 reference is sensitive to cohort composition or a single-sample, reference-independent caller is needed. Input profiles are microarray data without appropriate transformation — the article reports AWCA on Affymetrix log2-transformed data (e.g., GSE4922, GSE1456) and the porting workflow assumes comparable RNA-seq profiles The goal is a supervised multi-class learner with gene selection rather than nearest-centroid subtyping — the article's mLR (regularized multiclass logistic regression with Lasso/Ridge and limma50_BWE feature selection) is the alternative single-sample method http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Constructs PAM50 subtype references using the AWCA (average of within-class averages) strategy to mitigate reference-cohort composition bias in breast cancer intrinsic subtyping of RNA-seq profiles, yielding predefined external references usable for single-sample classification with over 90% concordance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Constructs PAM50 subtype references using the AWCA (average of within-class averages) strategy to mitigate reference-cohort composition bias in breast cancer intrinsic subtyping of RNA-seq profiles, yielding predefined external references usable for single-sample classification with over 90% concordance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input profiles are microarray data without appropriate transformation — the article reports AWCA on Affymetrix log2-transformed data (e.g., GSE4922, GSE1456) and the porting workflow assumes comparable RNA-seq profiles The goal is a supervised multi-class learner with gene selection rather than nearest-centroid subtyping — the article's mLR (regularized multiclass logistic regression with Lasso/Ridge and limma50_BWE feature selection) is the alternative single-sample method

skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference atlas annotations exist for the tissue/technology — the agreement assessment requires Azimuth (or equivalent supervised) labels for the same cells When the goal is data-level integration via a joint latent space or geometric graph (e.g., Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) rather than decision-level label reconciliation When reference annotations should be the sole ground truth overwriting all unsupervised solutions — scTriangulate weighs the reference as one player among many, not as an oracle

skills.name: azimuth-reference-based-cell-annotation
skills.search_text: azimuth-reference-based-cell-annotation Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., CD45+ immunotherapy cohorts) lack cell-type labels and downstream differential-state analysis such as scDist requires annotated cluster identities per cell. Input cells are already annotated with trusted cell-type labels and only the perturbation test remains (run scDist directly) The analysis goal is differential abundance (proportion changes between conditions) rather than differential transcriptomic state — tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate alternatives Only raw counts are available and no scTransform/normalized matrix will be produced — scDist cannot be applied directly to raw counts, so annotation alone is insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates cell populations in scRNA-seq data by mapping query cells onto Azimuth reference atlases via the Seurat-based reference mapping workflow, producing per-cell type labels. In the scDist immunotherapy study, these annotations define the cluster labels ('clusters') that scDist subsequently tests for transcriptomic perturbation between responders and non-responders. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Annotates cell populations in scRNA-seq data by mapping query cells onto Azimuth reference atlases via the Seurat-based reference mapping workflow, producing per-cell type labels. In the scDist immunotherapy study, these annotations define the cluster labels ('clusters') that scDist subsequently tests for transcriptomic perturbation between responders and non-responders.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells are already annotated with trusted cell-type labels and only the perturbation test remains (run scDist directly) The analysis goal is differential abundance (proportion changes between conditions) rather than differential transcriptomic state — tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate alternatives Only raw counts are available and no scTransform/normalized matrix will be produced — scDist cannot be applied directly to raw counts, so annotation alone is insufficient

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq-derived Ig transcript contigs (e.g. Trinity-assembled from a BWA/hg38-aligned BAM) need IGHV germline assignment, percent-identity-based SHM calls, and clonotype grouping to classify CLL samples as mCLL/uCLL.
skills.name: b-cell-clonotype-clustering

Input is raw reads or a BAM not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS requires that preprocessed input before this step Goal is full BCR repertoire profiling from single-cell or dedicated AIRR-seq data rather than bulk RNA-seq IGHV SHM-status classification of CLL samples Fewer than 25M sequence reads per sample or non-ribodepleted/polyA-incompatible libraries — README states a minimum of 25M reads for both ribodepleted and polyA selected RNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CRIS's SHM/clonotyping step queries assembled Ig transcripts against IMGT germline V/D/J references with IgBLAST, clusters transcripts sharing the same V-D-J rearrangement into clonotypes ranked by TPM, and calls mutated (mCLL, identity <98%) versus unmutated (uCLL, identity >=98%) IGHV status. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: CRIS's SHM/clonotyping step queries assembled Ig transcripts against IMGT germline V/D/J references with IgBLAST, clusters transcripts sharing the same V-D-J rearrangement into clonotypes ranked by TPM, and calls mutated (mCLL, identity <98%) versus unmutated (uCLL, identity >=98%) IGHV status.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or a BAM not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS requires that preprocessed input before this step Goal is full BCR repertoire profiling from single-cell or dedicated AIRR-seq data rather than bulk RNA-seq IGHV SHM-status classification of CLL samples Fewer than 25M sequence reads per sample or non-ribodepleted/polyA-incompatible libraries — README states a minimum of 25M reads for both ribodepleted and polyA selected RNA-seq

skills.name: b-cell-subset-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: b-cell-subset-cluster-annotation Use when analyzing CITE-seq data from CD19+ B cells where surface protein expression must be integrated with transcriptome to resolve functionally distinct B cell subsets, e.g. spike-specific memory-like clusters in COVID-19 patient PBMC. Datasets with a very high number of ADT features (e.g. >50 ADTs or 228-ADT 170K-cell data) — LinQ-View failed there while Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets too large for quadratic pairwise distance computation, where LinQ-View's time/memory efficiency is limiting Purely unimodal scRNA-seq data without a surface protein (ADT) modality to fuse via the L∞ norm http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Identifies and annotates B cell subsets from CITE-seq data using LinQ-View multimodal clustering, distinguishing naive-like, polyreactive, and antigen-specific memory-like populations in SARS-CoV-2-infected patient samples by fusing transcriptome and ADT pairwise distances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Identifies and annotates B cell subsets from CITE-seq data using LinQ-View multimodal clustering, distinguishing naive-like, polyreactive, and antigen-specific memory-like populations in SARS-CoV-2-infected patient samples by fusing transcriptome and ADT pairwise distances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with a very high number of ADT features (e.g. >50 ADTs or 228-ADT 170K-cell data) — LinQ-View failed there while Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets too large for quadratic pairwise distance computation, where LinQ-View's time/memory efficiency is limiting Purely unimodal scRNA-seq data without a surface protein (ADT) modality to fuse via the L∞ norm

skills.description: Use when you have ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 output plus HISAT2-aligned BAM) and need directly comparable circular vs. linear RNA expression values (FPB and CIRCscore) at shared gene loci.
skills.name: back-splice-junction-fragment-quantification
skills.search_text: back-splice-junction-fragment-quantification Use when you have ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 output plus HISAT2-aligned BAM) and need directly comparable circular vs. linear RNA expression values (FPB and CIRCscore) at shared gene loci. Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ selected — circRNAs are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets, so BSJ fragments will be largely missing Data are poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated — linear RNAs are depleted, making FPBlinear and CIRCscore unreliable Input BAM still contains unmapped reads — hisat_aligned.bam must be mapped-reads-only before circ_quant http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq using the FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) metric computed over fragments mapped to circRNA-specific BSJ sites and linear RNA-specific SJ sites, then computes CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear for direct comparison at the same gene loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Quantifies circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq using the FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) metric computed over fragments mapped to circRNA-specific BSJ sites and linear RNA-specific SJ sites, then computes CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear for direct comparison at the same gene loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ selected — circRNAs are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets, so BSJ fragments will be largely missing Data are poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated — linear RNAs are depleted, making FPBlinear and CIRCscore unreliable Input BAM still contains unmapped reads — hisat_aligned.bam must be mapped-reads-only before circ_quant

skills.description: Use when ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files must be screened for circRNAs via BSJ-spanning fragments, and quantification of circRNA expression relative to cognate linear RNA (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear) is required.
skills.name: back-splicing-junction-circrna-detection
skills.search_text: back-splicing-junction-circrna-detection Use when ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files must be screened for circRNAs via BSJ-spanning fragments, and quantification of circRNA expression relative to cognate linear RNA (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear) is required. Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq or poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated data — polyadenylated linear RNAs are depleted in the latter and CIRCscore evaluation is unsuitable there Goal is only linear gene expression quantification without circRNA/BSJ analysis No bowtie1 (TopHat-Fusion) or HISAT2 index for the target genome is available and none can be built http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Detect and quantify circular RNAs from ribosomal-RNA depleted (ribo−) RNA-seq by identifying RNA-seq fragments spanning back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites, using the CLEAR pipeline's clear_quant (HISAT2 alignment + CIRCexplorer2 ≥2.3.6 fusion junction realignment) to produce per-locus readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Detect and quantify circular RNAs from ribosomal-RNA depleted (ribo−) RNA-seq by identifying RNA-seq fragments spanning back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites, using the CLEAR pipeline's clear_quant (HISAT2 alignment + CIRCexplorer2 ≥2.3.6 fusion junction realignment) to produce per-locus readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq or poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated data — polyadenylated linear RNAs are depleted in the latter and CIRCscore evaluation is unsuitable there Goal is only linear gene expression quantification without circRNA/BSJ analysis No bowtie1 (TopHat-Fusion) or HISAT2 index for the target genome is available and none can be built

skills.description: Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files by detecting fragments spanning back-splicing junction sites, prior to FPB/CIRCscore quantification.
skills.name: back-splicing-junction-read-mapping
skills.search_text: back-splicing-junction-read-mapping Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files by detecting fragments spanning back-splicing junction sites, prior to FPB/CIRCscore quantification. Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making FPBlinear unreliable and precluding valid CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, in which circRNAs are depleted because they lack 3′ poly(A) tails Only linear RNA expression is of interest and no circ/linear comparison is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect and quantify back-splicing junction (BSJ) reads from ribo− RNA-seq by aligning reads with HISAT2 and realigning unmapped/edge reads with TopHat-Fusion (Bowtie1) via CIRCexplorer2, providing the circRNA calls that feed CLEAR's circ_quant for FPBcirc and CIRCscore computation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Detect and quantify back-splicing junction (BSJ) reads from ribo− RNA-seq by aligning reads with HISAT2 and realigning unmapped/edge reads with TopHat-Fusion (Bowtie1) via CIRCexplorer2, providing the circRNA calls that feed CLEAR's circ_quant for FPBcirc and CIRCscore computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making FPBlinear unreliable and precluding valid CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, in which circRNAs are depleted because they lack 3′ poly(A) tails Only linear RNA expression is of interest and no circ/linear comparison is needed

skills.name: backbone-point-selection-center-outward
skills.search_text: backbone-point-selection-center-outward Use when processing imaging data of rolled (Swiss-roll) intestinal tissues — e.g. CODEX-exported .csv files or 10x spatial transcriptomics images providing x and y coordinates — where a curved spiral backbone must be manually defined before unrolling cells onto a line. The input image is of flat, non-rolled tissue with no spiral topology — the center-outward backbone and downstream unrolling are designed for Swiss-rolled intestines The data source does not provide x and y coordinates (IntestLine is only stated to suit CODEX, 10x spatial transcriptomics, or any images providing xy-coordinates) You only need to re-analyze an existing mapped output without redefining the geometry — reuse the previously downloaded backbone file instead of re-selecting points Interactive step in IntestLine (Bioinformatics 2023, btad140) in which the user manually traces a spiral backbone along the edge of a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image, starting from the spiral center and moving outward, to serve as the reference curve for subsequently mapping xy-coordinate cell data onto a linear axis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: Interactive step in IntestLine (Bioinformatics 2023, btad140) in which the user manually traces a spiral backbone along the edge of a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image, starting from the spiral center and moving outward, to serve as the reference curve for subsequently mapping xy-coordinate cell data onto a linear axis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input image is of flat, non-rolled tissue with no spiral topology — the center-outward backbone and downstream unrolling are designed for Swiss-rolled intestines The data source does not provide x and y coordinates (IntestLine is only stated to suit CODEX, 10x spatial transcriptomics, or any images providing xy-coordinates) You only need to re-analyze an existing mapped output without redefining the geometry — reuse the previously downloaded backbone file instead of re-selecting points

skills.description: Use when you are drawing or reusing a backbone over a rolled-intestine ROI (CODEX or 10x xy-coordinate CSV) and must confirm the selection traces a high-quality 3D spiral, starting from the spiral center and going outward, before running the Unroll step.
skills.name: backbone-spiral-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: backbone-spiral-quality-assessment Use when you are drawing or reusing a backbone over a rolled-intestine ROI (CODEX or 10x xy-coordinate CSV) and must confirm the selection traces a high-quality 3D spiral, starting from the spiral center and going outward, before running the Unroll step. The image is not a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue with a spiral structure — there is no center-outward backbone to trace and the linear mapping assumptions do not hold The input provides no per-point xy-coordinates (IntestLine requires 'basically any images providing xy-coordinates') You only need marker-expression visualization along an already validated, downloaded backbone — reuse the existing backbone file instead of redrawing and re-assessing it Quality-control step in the IntestLine workflow that previews whether the user-selected backbone points for a Swiss-rolled intestinal ROI form a high-quality 3D spiral before unrolling. Because cells are assigned to backbone points by a directionally biased outward nearest-neighbor search, a wrongly ordered or deformed backbone corrupts the proximal-distal and serosa-luminal mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140

skills.when_to_use_negative: The image is not a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue with a spiral structure — there is no center-outward backbone to trace and the linear mapping assumptions do not hold The input provides no per-point xy-coordinates (IntestLine requires 'basically any images providing xy-coordinates') You only need marker-expression visualization along an already validated, downloaded backbone — reuse the existing backbone file instead of redrawing and re-assessing it
