skills.name: background-corrected-permutation-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: background-corrected-permutation-pvalue-estimation Use when per-cell TRS or module scores (e.g., Seurat AddModuleScore output) need statistically calibrated significance, because raw module scores lack a null model and cannot be thresholded (e.g., q<0.05) for calling trait-relevant cells. Input is already a calibrated per-cell p-value or q-value vector from scDRS (which uses its own MC null via control gene sets) — re-running this correction would double-correct The gene set is not trait-relevant (no gPAS-derived scGet_PCC prioritization was performed), so background correction would only calibrate an uninterpretable module score Cell-type-level (not single-cell) association testing is the goal — scPagwas uses block bootstrap (200 iterations) over pathway-based genome blocks for that instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A Monte Carlo significance-assessment step in scPagwas that converts raw per-cell trait relevance scores (TRS) into background-corrected p-values by comparing each cell's TRS to an empirical null distribution of control TRSs, generated from matched control gene sets over 100 iterations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: A Monte Carlo significance-assessment step in scPagwas that converts raw per-cell trait relevance scores (TRS) into background-corrected p-values by comparing each cell's TRS to an empirical null distribution of control TRSs, generated from matched control gene sets over 100 iterations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a calibrated per-cell p-value or q-value vector from scDRS (which uses its own MC null via control gene sets) — re-running this correction would double-correct The gene set is not trait-relevant (no gPAS-derived scGet_PCC prioritization was performed), so background correction would only calibrate an uninterpretable module score Cell-type-level (not single-cell) association testing is the goal — scPagwas uses block bootstrap (200 iterations) over pathway-based genome blocks for that instead

skills.description: Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile) shows a bimodal log2 intensity distribution and a background/signal valley must be identified to define a background-subtracted gene set.
skills.name: background-cutoff-histogram-visualization
skills.search_text: background-cutoff-histogram-visualization Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile) shows a bimodal log2 intensity distribution and a background/signal valley must be identified to define a background-subtracted gene set. The input matrix is raw (not yet quantile-normalized by PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command) — normalization must come first. The goal is normalization-method comparison (quantile vs LOESS via MA plots) rather than removing genes below a background threshold. Data are RNA-seq count data rather than microarray intensities from platforms such as Illumina Bead arrays; PIMENTo targets microarray QC and analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A PIMENTo (R) routine that renders full-range and zoomed log2-scale Background Cutoff histograms of quantile-normalized microarray intensities so the valley separating background from signal can be visually located and used to set an intensity cutoff (here 6.1) for background subtraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-9004-7_11
skills.summary: A PIMENTo (R) routine that renders full-range and zoomed log2-scale Background Cutoff histograms of quantile-normalized microarray intensities so the valley separating background from signal can be visually located and used to set an intensity cutoff (here 6.1) for background subtraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is raw (not yet quantile-normalized by PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command) — normalization must come first. The goal is normalization-method comparison (quantile vs LOESS via MA plots) rather than removing genes below a background threshold. Data are RNA-seq count data rather than microarray intensities from platforms such as Illumina Bead arrays; PIMENTo targets microarray QC and analysis.

skills.description: Use when running dsb (DSBNormalizeProtein) on CITE-seq ADT data with both raw and filtered Cell Ranger output available, and a set of empty droplets must be defined to estimate ambient antibody background.
skills.name: background-droplet-definition-barcode-rank
skills.search_text: background-droplet-definition-barcode-rank Use when running dsb (DSBNormalizeProtein) on CITE-seq ADT data with both raw and filtered Cell Ranger output available, and a set of empty droplets must be defined to estimate ambient antibody background. Only the filtered matrix is available and no raw-output barcodes exist to serve as empty droplets — dsb instead offers a workflow 'when empty droplets are not available' (separate vignette). Input data are already dsb-normalized or otherwise background-corrected ADT values; redefining background droplets is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Define the set of empty/background droplets used by dsb's ambient-noise estimation by taking barcodes from the raw Cell Ranger output that are not in the filtered output, using the EmptyDrops/Cell Ranger barcode rank to confirm they are genuine empty droplets (>50,000 in the 10X NextGem ~5K-cell 29-protein dataset). These background droplets provide the per-antibody ambient ADT mean mu_N and SD sigma_N for dsb step I. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Define the set of empty/background droplets used by dsb's ambient-noise estimation by taking barcodes from the raw Cell Ranger output that are not in the filtered output, using the EmptyDrops/Cell Ranger barcode rank to confirm they are genuine empty droplets (>50,000 in the 10X NextGem ~5K-cell 29-protein dataset). These background droplets provide the per-antibody ambient ADT mean mu_N and SD sigma_N for dsb step I.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the filtered matrix is available and no raw-output barcodes exist to serve as empty droplets — dsb instead offers a workflow 'when empty droplets are not available' (separate vignette). Input data are already dsb-normalized or otherwise background-corrected ADT values; redefining background droplets is not applicable.

skills.description: Use when raw CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT count matrices are available together with raw (unfiltered) barcode matrices containing empty droplets, and ambient protein-specific noise must be removed prior to cell-level normalization.
skills.name: background-droplet-standardization
skills.search_text: background-droplet-standardization Use when raw CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT count matrices are available together with raw (unfiltered) barcode matrices containing empty droplets, and ambient protein-specific noise must be removed prior to cell-level normalization. No empty droplets are available (raw/unfiltered matrix missing) — the dsb vignette 'no_empty_drops' workflow or an alternative background definition must be used instead The input is already normalized protein data (e.g., CLR-normalized or dsb step-II output) rather than raw ADT UMI counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 DSB step I: standardize raw ADT (protein) counts in droplet-based single-cell data by log-transforming counts with log(x+10) and then rescaling each protein per cell using the mean (µ_N) and standard deviation (σ_N) of that protein measured in empty (background) droplets. This removes protein-specific ambient noise originating from unbound antibodies encapsulated during droplet generation before any cell-level denoising. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: DSB step I: standardize raw ADT (protein) counts in droplet-based single-cell data by log-transforming counts with log(x+10) and then rescaling each protein per cell using the mean (µ_N) and standard deviation (σ_N) of that protein measured in empty (background) droplets. This removes protein-specific ambient noise originating from unbound antibodies encapsulated during droplet generation before any cell-level denoising.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No empty droplets are available (raw/unfiltered matrix missing) — the dsb vignette 'no_empty_drops' workflow or an alternative background definition must be used instead The input is already normalized protein data (e.g., CLR-normalized or dsb step-II output) rather than raw ADT UMI counts

skills.description: Use when you have a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to enumerate lifestyle-associated genes per group using bacLIFE's 70% prevalence / 2 log2FC rule.
skills.name: bacterial-lifestyle-gene-association-analysis
skills.search_text: bacterial-lifestyle-gene-association-analysis Use when you have a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to enumerate lifestyle-associated genes per group using bacLIFE's 70% prevalence / 2 log2FC rule. You only need the lifestyle prediction itself (bacLIFE machine-learning module), not the gene-level association analysis that follows it You lack the binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix and only have raw genome assemblies — the clustering module must run first You want core-genome identification (genes in >90% of genomes), which is a different filter than the pLAG 70% group-prevalence rule http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Reproduce bacLIFE's analytical-module detection of predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) by running per-lifestyle Fisher's exact tests on a gene cluster absence/presence matrix and filtering with >70% group prevalence and >2 log2 fold change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Reproduce bacLIFE's analytical-module detection of predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) by running per-lifestyle Fisher's exact tests on a gene cluster absence/presence matrix and filtering with >70% group prevalence and >2 log2 fold change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the lifestyle prediction itself (bacLIFE machine-learning module), not the gene-level association analysis that follows it You lack the binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix and only have raw genome assemblies — the clustering module must run first You want core-genome identification (genes in >90% of genomes), which is a different filter than the pLAG 70% group-prevalence rule

skills.description: Use when you have a gene cluster absence/presence matrix for genomes with literature-derived lifestyle labels and need to (a) quantify lifestyle predictability via cross-validated AUC or (b) assign lifestyles to unknown-lifestyle genomes.
skills.name: bacterial-lifestyle-prediction
skills.search_text: bacterial-lifestyle-prediction Use when you have a gene cluster absence/presence matrix for genomes with literature-derived lifestyle labels and need to (a) quantify lifestyle predictability via cross-validated AUC or (b) assign lifestyles to unknown-lifestyle genomes. Input is a raw genome set without a gene cluster absence/presence matrix — run the bacLIFE clustering module (Prokka, linclust/MCL) first Lifestyle labels are not grounded in literature-derived metadata, since the classifiers are binary one-vs-rest models trained per labeled lifestyle group Analysis goal is identifying individual lifestyle-associated genes (LAGs) rather than classifying whole-genome lifestyles — use the pLAG enrichment thresholds (>70% group presence, >2 log2 fold change) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predict bacterial lifestyles (e.g. environmental, opportunistic animal pathogen, plant pathogen) from gene cluster absence/presence matrices using binary random forest classifiers trained per lifestyle, as implemented in the bacLIFE workflow. Assigns lifestyles to unknown genomes via confidence-thresholded adjudication. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Predict bacterial lifestyles (e.g. environmental, opportunistic animal pathogen, plant pathogen) from gene cluster absence/presence matrices using binary random forest classifiers trained per lifestyle, as implemented in the bacLIFE workflow. Assigns lifestyles to unknown genomes via confidence-thresholded adjudication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw genome set without a gene cluster absence/presence matrix — run the bacLIFE clustering module (Prokka, linclust/MCL) first Lifestyle labels are not grounded in literature-derived metadata, since the classifiers are binary one-vs-rest models trained per labeled lifestyle group Analysis goal is identifying individual lifestyle-associated genes (LAGs) rather than classifying whole-genome lifestyles — use the pLAG enrichment thresholds (>70% group presence, >2 log2 fold change) instead

skills.description: Use when single-cell scWGS BAF data must be converted to a clean allelic state matrix at reliable germline SNPs — e.g., before ADO-event HMM decoding or allele-specific CNA calling — and phased gHET calls from SHAPEIT2 (shapeit/phased_hets.vcf) are available.
skills.name: baf-binarization-at-germline-hets
skills.search_text: baf-binarization-at-germline-hets Use when single-cell scWGS BAF data must be converted to a clean allelic state matrix at reliable germline SNPs — e.g., before ADO-event HMM decoding or allele-specific CNA calling — and phased gHET calls from SHAPEIT2 (shapeit/phased_hets.vcf) are available. Input SNPs are somatic rather than germline heterozygous calls — SCAN2 explicitly excludes variants with any read support in matched bulk, and binarization assumes known germline genotypes. The dataset lacks paired bulk WGS for phasing; without SHAPEIT2-phased gHETs (e.g., low-coverage scWGS without bulk), CHISEL-style block phasing should be used instead. Analysis targets sex chromosomes or non-autosomal regions, since HiScanner's analysis is restricted to autosomal chromosomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Prepares the per-cell B-allele-frequency matrix that downstream HiScanner ADO/CNA modeling consumes: only germline heterozygous SNPs phased by SHAPEIT2 with bulk VAF between 0.1 and 0.9 are retained, and each single cell's BAF at these sites is binarized into allele-specific states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Prepares the per-cell B-allele-frequency matrix that downstream HiScanner ADO/CNA modeling consumes: only germline heterozygous SNPs phased by SHAPEIT2 with bulk VAF between 0.1 and 0.9 are retained, and each single cell's BAF at these sites is binarized into allele-specific states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input SNPs are somatic rather than germline heterozygous calls — SCAN2 explicitly excludes variants with any read support in matched bulk, and binarization assumes known germline genotypes. The dataset lacks paired bulk WGS for phasing; without SHAPEIT2-phased gHETs (e.g., low-coverage scWGS without bulk), CHISEL-style block phasing should be used instead. Analysis targets sex chromosomes or non-autosomal regions, since HiScanner's analysis is restricted to autosomal chromosomes.

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell CNA calls from a BAF-agnostic (read-depth-only) caller and phased bulk germline heterozygous SNPs, and you need to quantify how many calls are supported by local allelic (BAF) evidence per cell type.
skills.name: baf-concordance-classification
skills.search_text: baf-concordance-classification Use when you have single-cell CNA calls from a BAF-agnostic (read-depth-only) caller and phased bulk germline heterozygous SNPs, and you need to quantify how many calls are supported by local allelic (BAF) evidence per cell type. When the CNA caller already models BAF and phasing directly (e.g., HiScanner, CHISEL, Alleloscope) — post-hoc BAF validation is redundant and the calls are already allele-specific. When no matched bulk WGS is available to phase gHETs and filter on bulk VAF (0.1–0.9), since local BAF cannot be anchored to a haplotype-phased heterozygous locus. When the target is calling CNVs from scratch rather than auditing the reliability of existing single-cell CNA calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Validates single-cell read-depth-based CNA calls (e.g., from Ginkgo) against local B-allele frequency (BAF) evidence computed from phased gHETs in the same cell's BAM, then quantifies BAF-concordance/discordance fractions per cell type. This tests whether read-depth-only calls are supported by allelic evidence, as read-depth signals alone can be confounded by single-cell whole-genome amplification artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Validates single-cell read-depth-based CNA calls (e.g., from Ginkgo) against local B-allele frequency (BAF) evidence computed from phased gHETs in the same cell's BAM, then quantifies BAF-concordance/discordance fractions per cell type. This tests whether read-depth-only calls are supported by allelic evidence, as read-depth signals alone can be confounded by single-cell whole-genome amplification artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the CNA caller already models BAF and phasing directly (e.g., HiScanner, CHISEL, Alleloscope) — post-hoc BAF validation is redundant and the calls are already allele-specific. When no matched bulk WGS is available to phase gHETs and filter on bulk VAF (0.1–0.9), since local BAF cannot be anchored to a haplotype-phased heterozygous locus. When the target is calling CNVs from scratch rather than auditing the reliability of existing single-cell CNA calls.

skills.description: Use when running XClone's BAF module on phased scRNA-seq allele counts (AD/DP matrices) and the phased mega-gene-level allele states must be projected to per-gene resolution before run_combine merges them with RDR CNA probabilities.
skills.name: baf-gene-scale-mapping
skills.search_text: baf-gene-scale-mapping Use when running XClone's BAF module on phased scRNA-seq allele counts (AD/DP matrices) and the phased mega-gene-level allele states must be projected to per-gene resolution before run_combine merges them with RDR CNA probabilities. Input lacks heterozygous SNP allele counts (AD/DP matrices) — BAF mapping and downstream LOH detection require allelic information, which read-depth-only RDR cannot supply You only need copy gain/loss from read depth and do not intend to combine with the RDR module or detect copy-neutral LOH http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Maps XClone BAF module allele-state results from phased mega-gene (chromosome-arm/gene-bin) scale back to individual gene scale so that BAF-derived LOH/copy states can be combined with the RDR module's genes-by-cells-by-states tensor into the final per-gene-per-cell CNA calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Maps XClone BAF module allele-state results from phased mega-gene (chromosome-arm/gene-bin) scale back to individual gene scale so that BAF-derived LOH/copy states can be combined with the RDR module's genes-by-cells-by-states tensor into the final per-gene-per-cell CNA calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks heterozygous SNP allele counts (AD/DP matrices) — BAF mapping and downstream LOH detection require allelic information, which read-depth-only RDR cannot supply You only need copy gain/loss from read depth and do not intend to combine with the RDR module or detect copy-neutral LOH

skills.description: Use when calling CNV events from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq where expression-based segmentation alone is ambiguous and BAF shift information from mapped reads (no heterozygous variant call set or SNV calls) should be integrated to confirm and consolidate calls at multiple scales.
skills.name: baf-shift-integration-for-cnv-calls
skills.search_text: baf-shift-integration-for-cnv-calls Use when calling CNV events from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq where expression-based segmentation alone is ambiguous and BAF shift information from mapped reads (no heterozygous variant call set or SNV calls) should be integrated to confirm and consolidate calls at multiple scales. 3′-only sequencing protocols (e.g. DropSeq-style 10x data) with sparse variants near gene 3′ ends, where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted and pooling across cells is the only mitigation Analyses lacking BAM files or any variant-containing reads, so no BAF shift can be computed — expression-only CNV inference must be used instead Sample sets where a few cells carry a substantially large number of reads, which may dominate the pooled BAF shift signal and create biases in single-cell mode http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Integrates B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signals (allelic shift measuring LOH) with multiscale HMM segmentation of genome-wide gene expression in CaSpER, so CNV calls are corrected and consolidated across pairwise comparisons of expression and BAF scales before large-scale and gene-based summarization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Integrates B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signals (allelic shift measuring LOH) with multiscale HMM segmentation of genome-wide gene expression in CaSpER, so CNV calls are corrected and consolidated across pairwise comparisons of expression and BAF scales before large-scale and gene-based summarization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: 3′-only sequencing protocols (e.g. DropSeq-style 10x data) with sparse variants near gene 3′ ends, where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted and pooling across cells is the only mitigation Analyses lacking BAM files or any variant-containing reads, so no BAF shift can be computed — expression-only CNV inference must be used instead Sample sets where a few cells carry a substantially large number of reads, which may dominate the pooled BAF shift signal and create biases in single-cell mode

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or single-cell) must be converted into per-sample BAF shift profiles to supply the LOH/allelic-shift input for CaSpER CNV calling.
skills.name: baf-shift-signal-extraction
skills.search_text: baf-shift-signal-extraction Use when RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or single-cell) must be converted into per-sample BAF shift profiles to supply the LOH/allelic-shift input for CaSpER CNV calling. You have only a normalized expression matrix with no BAM files, so no read-level base observations exist from which to compute BAF shifts Your goal is germline SNV genotyping rather than somatic CNV/LOH detection from RNA-seq signal profiles Your data are 3'-only (e.g., DropSeq-style) with very sparse near-3' variants and you cannot pool enough reads to support a usable BAF shift signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signals from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract, the allelic-shift/LOH signal source that CaSpER integrates with multiscale-smoothed expression to call CNV events, without requiring a heterozygous variant call set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Extracts B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signals from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract, the allelic-shift/LOH signal source that CaSpER integrates with multiscale-smoothed expression to call CNV events, without requiring a heterozygous variant call set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a normalized expression matrix with no BAM files, so no read-level base observations exist from which to compute BAF shifts Your goal is germline SNV genotyping rather than somatic CNV/LOH detection from RNA-seq signal profiles Your data are 3'-only (e.g., DropSeq-style) with very sparse near-3' variants and you cannot pool enough reads to support a usable BAF shift signal

skills.description: Use when you have mapped bulk or merged single-cell RNA-seq BAM files and need a genome-wide BAF shift signal to correct/confirm CaSpER CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous SNV call set.
skills.name: baf-shift-signal-generation-from-rnaseq-bam
skills.search_text: baf-shift-signal-generation-from-rnaseq-bam Use when you have mapped bulk or merged single-cell RNA-seq BAM files and need a genome-wide BAF shift signal to correct/confirm CaSpER CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous SNV call set. Input is 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) — the BAF shift signal is degraded because BAF is measured only for variants near the 3' ends of genes Input is already an expression matrix or a feature count table with no BAM — allele frequencies cannot be computed from reads alone You already have high-quality DNA-seq data and a heterozygous variant call set; a DNA-based CNV caller is the more direct route http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift profile directly from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract (no heterozygous variant call set required), then smooths it with CaSpER's recursive per-chromosome median filter across multiscale windows (loh.scale=3) for LOH/CNV correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Generates a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift profile directly from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract (no heterozygous variant call set required), then smooths it with CaSpER's recursive per-chromosome median filter across multiscale windows (loh.scale=3) for LOH/CNV correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) — the BAF shift signal is degraded because BAF is measured only for variants near the 3' ends of genes Input is already an expression matrix or a feature count table with no BAM — allele frequencies cannot be computed from reads alone You already have high-quality DNA-seq data and a heterozygous variant call set; a DNA-based CNV caller is the more direct route

skills.description: Use when candidate m6A site labels are uncertain and inputs are positive/negative bag-level datasets, so instance labels must be inferred via multiple instance learning.
skills.name: bag-level-instance-label-relabeling
skills.search_text: bag-level-instance-label-relabeling Use when candidate m6A site labels are uncertain and inputs are positive/negative bag-level datasets, so instance labels must be inferred via multiple instance learning. Input is already instance-level labeled data where supervised learning is possible rather than a multiple-instance bag problem Bag labels are 0/1-valued rather than +1/-1 — the misvm package notes you will likely get strange results with 0/1 labels You need bag-level-only classifiers (e.g. NSK) where the instancePrediction flag is unavailable and per-instance relabeling via instance predictions is not supported http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a bag-level miSVM/MISVM model with HLMethy's m6A_model_training.py (via the misvm package) to generate scores that relabel hidden-label candidate m6A sites, addressing the partially-labeled positive-bag problem of multiple instance learning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s11103-019-00930-x
skills.summary: Train a bag-level miSVM/MISVM model with HLMethy's m6A_model_training.py (via the misvm package) to generate scores that relabel hidden-label candidate m6A sites, addressing the partially-labeled positive-bag problem of multiple instance learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already instance-level labeled data where supervised learning is possible rather than a multiple-instance bag problem Bag labels are 0/1-valued rather than +1/-1 — the misvm package notes you will likely get strange results with 0/1 labels You need bag-level-only classifiers (e.g. NSK) where the instancePrediction flag is unavailable and per-instance relabeling via instance predictions is not supported

skills.description: Use when a robust GRN is needed from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data and many subsample networks have been built from supercells, so edges recurring across networks must be merged into a consensus before edge pruning.
skills.name: bagged-subsample-network-consensus-merging
skills.search_text: bagged-subsample-network-consensus-merging Use when a robust GRN is needed from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data and many subsample networks have been built from supercells, so edges recurring across networks must be merged into a consensus before edge pruning. The analysis requires explicitly leveraging spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING does not utilize spatial information when building GRNs from spatial transcriptomics The goal is causal or strictly directional regulatory claims — inferred GRN links are not necessarily causal or directional The input is bulk transcriptomics or a pre-computed network rather than single-cell/snRNA-seq data from which supercells and subsample networks can be built A bagging-based consensus step of the SCING pipeline in which many GRNs (100 in the reference workflow) are built in parallel from subsamples of supercell-aggregated single-cell data and merged so that only edges recurring across subsample networks (20% consensus threshold) survive into the final network, which is then pruned with conditional mutual information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: A bagging-based consensus step of the SCING pipeline in which many GRNs (100 in the reference workflow) are built in parallel from subsamples of supercell-aggregated single-cell data and merged so that only edges recurring across subsample networks (20% consensus threshold) survive into the final network, which is then pruned with conditional mutual information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires explicitly leveraging spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING does not utilize spatial information when building GRNs from spatial transcriptomics The goal is causal or strictly directional regulatory claims — inferred GRN links are not necessarily causal or directional The input is bulk transcriptomics or a pre-computed network rather than single-cell/snRNA-seq data from which supercells and subsample networks can be built

skills.description: Use when evaluating an automated cell-type annotation method against curated expert labels on atlas-scale mouse or human tissue datasets, when balanced accuracy and label-similarity metrics must be reproduced from deposited code, or when benchmarking Census against annotators on droplet or FACS.
skills.name: balanced-accuracy-benchmark-computation
skills.search_text: balanced-accuracy-benchmark-computation Use when evaluating an automated cell-type annotation method against curated expert labels on atlas-scale mouse or human tissue datasets, when balanced accuracy and label-similarity metrics must be reproduced from deposited code, or when benchmarking Census against annotators on droplet or FACS. Input is not a Seurat object containing a UMAP dimensionality reduction — census_main requires one Tissue falls outside the 24 Tabula Sapiens organs Census can classify (e.g. tissues not among Bladder, Blood, Bone_Marrow, ... Vasculature) and no custom model has been trained Goal is cancer-of-origin inference rather than normal-tissue annotation benchmarking — that requires the organ-specific cancer models with predict_cancer=T, a different workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce Census's cross-species benchmark on Tabula Muris mouse tissues by annotating droplet and plate-based (FACS) scRNA-seq datasets with the pretrained Census hierarchical model and computing mean balanced accuracy (0.8), label similarity (0.89), and run time (13 s) against expert cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Reproduce Census's cross-species benchmark on Tabula Muris mouse tissues by annotating droplet and plate-based (FACS) scRNA-seq datasets with the pretrained Census hierarchical model and computing mean balanced accuracy (0.8), label similarity (0.89), and run time (13 s) against expert cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a Seurat object containing a UMAP dimensionality reduction — census_main requires one Tissue falls outside the 24 Tabula Sapiens organs Census can classify (e.g. tissues not among Bladder, Blood, Bone_Marrow, ... Input is read-level filtering of FASTQ by k-mer coverage — that is a different task handled by spades-read-filter ('filtering reads with median kmer coverage less than threshold'), not barcode-based contig filtering Contigs lack barcode-to-gene assignments (e.g. assembly of non-barcoded RNA-seq data), so ambiguous vs unique classification is impossible The question is whether a barcode maps to multiple different genes rather than to a single gene multiple times — this skill's ambiguity criterion only covers the latter http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Post-assembly filtering step for cloudrnaSPAdes results that removes contigs whose barcode is assigned to a single gene multiple times (ambiguous assignments), quantifying how many such contigs are removed versus uniquely assigned contigs retained. This reproduces the paper's 'fixed' Table 3 correction, where the barcode filter removes ~15% of ambiguous assignments on real SPIso-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Post-assembly filtering step for cloudrnaSPAdes results that removes contigs whose barcode is assigned to a single gene multiple times (ambiguous assignments), quantifying how many such contigs are removed versus uniquely assigned contigs retained. This reproduces the paper's 'fixed' Table 3 correction, where the barcode filter removes ~15% of ambiguous assignments on real SPIso-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is read-level filtering of FASTQ by k-mer coverage — that is a different task handled by spades-read-filter ('filtering reads with median kmer coverage less than threshold'), not barcode-based contig filtering Contigs lack barcode-to-gene assignments (e.g. assembly of non-barcoded RNA-seq data), so ambiguous vs unique classification is impossible The question is whether a barcode maps to multiple different genes rather than to a single gene multiple times — this skill's ambiguity criterion only covers the latter

skills.description: Use when assembling reference-free isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads: you have a shared SPAdes assembly graph plus per-read barcode tags and need barcode-specific subgraphs for simplification.
skills.name: barcoded-read-cloud-subgraph-extraction
skills.search_text: barcoded-read-cloud-subgraph-extraction Use when assembling reference-free isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads: you have a shared SPAdes assembly graph plus per-read barcode tags and need barcode-specific subgraphs for simplification. Input is standard (non-barcoded) bulk RNA-seq — use rnaSPAdes rather than read-cloud subgraph extraction. Input is WGS isolate or metagenomic data — use the SPAdes/metaSPAdes pipelines; SPAdes is not intended for larger (e.g. mammalian-size) genomes. The goal is to clean the shared assembly graph itself — edges must not be deleted from the base graph because an edge erroneous for one barcode may be correct for another barcode's isoform. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts per-read-cloud (barcode) subgraphs from a shared SPAdes assembly graph during cloudrnaSPAdes isoform assembly, computes barcode-specific edge coverage along sequence-of-edge paths, and simplifies each subgraph (tip clipping, bulge removal, gap closing) without modifying the shared graph. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Extracts per-read-cloud (barcode) subgraphs from a shared SPAdes assembly graph during cloudrnaSPAdes isoform assembly, computes barcode-specific edge coverage along sequence-of-edge paths, and simplifies each subgraph (tip clipping, bulge removal, gap closing) without modifying the shared graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is standard (non-barcoded) bulk RNA-seq — use rnaSPAdes rather than read-cloud subgraph extraction. Input is WGS isolate or metagenomic data — use the SPAdes/metaSPAdes pipelines; SPAdes is not intended for larger (e.g. mammalian-size) genomes. The goal is to clean the shared assembly graph itself — edges must not be deleted from the base graph because an edge erroneous for one barcode may be correct for another barcode's isoform.

skills.description: Use when input is paired-end barcoded RNA-seq FASTQ (e.g. SPIso-seq human brain, ~181.8M read pairs / 584,399 barcodes) and full-length isoform contigs must be assembled without a transcript reference.
skills.name: barcoded-rnaseq-isoform-assembly
skills.search_text: barcoded-rnaseq-isoform-assembly Use when input is paired-end barcoded RNA-seq FASTQ (e.g. SPIso-seq human brain, ~181.8M read pairs / 584,399 barcodes) and full-length isoform contigs must be assembled without a transcript reference. Input is long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq / Oxford Nanopore) transcript data — cloudrnaSPAdes targets barcoded short-read linked RNA-seq, though SPAdes itself can use PacBio CLR and Oxford Nanopore reads only for gap closure and repeat resolution The goal is reference-based transcript quantification or alignment of annotated transcripts rather than reference-free isoform assembly The data are standard short-read RNA-seq without barcodes/linked-read structure, where plain rnaSPAdes rather than the cloudrnaSPAdes barcoded pipeline is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reference-free assembly of full-length isoforms from bulk barcoded (linked-read) Illumina RNA-seq data using cloudrnaSPAdes, a feature release of the SPAdes assembler, followed by contig filtering and IsoQuant-based assignment against a reference annotation (e.g. GENCODE v32 on GRCh38). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Reference-free assembly of full-length isoforms from bulk barcoded (linked-read) Illumina RNA-seq data using cloudrnaSPAdes, a feature release of the SPAdes assembler, followed by contig filtering and IsoQuant-based assignment against a reference annotation (e.g. GENCODE v32 on GRCh38).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq / Oxford Nanopore) transcript data — cloudrnaSPAdes targets barcoded short-read linked RNA-seq, though SPAdes itself can use PacBio CLR and Oxford Nanopore reads only for gap closure and repeat resolution The goal is reference-based transcript quantification or alignment of annotated transcripts rather than reference-free isoform assembly The data are standard short-read RNA-seq without barcodes/linked-read structure, where plain rnaSPAdes rather than the cloudrnaSPAdes barcoded pipeline is appropriate

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic barcoded RNA-seq linked reads from genes with known isoform structure (e.g. GYPC, MAPT, BIN1) to evaluate reference-free isoform assembly and barcode-filtering strategies.
skills.name: barcoded-rnaseq-read-simulation
skills.search_text: barcoded-rnaseq-read-simulation Use when you need synthetic barcoded RNA-seq linked reads from genes with known isoform structure (e.g. GYPC, MAPT, BIN1) to evaluate reference-free isoform assembly and barcode-filtering strategies. The input is real SPIso-seq or other barcoded RNA-seq data — simulation is only needed to establish ground truth for benchmarking assemblers The target gene has a single annotated isoform and no alternative splicing, so isoform recall cannot be meaningfully measured The downstream assembler does not consume barcoded linked reads (e.g. plain short-read genome assemblers) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates barcoded paired-end RNA-seq (SPIso-seq-style) reads from selected gene loci so that barcoded isoform assemblers like cloudrnaSPAdes can be benchmarked against annotated GENCODE isoforms with known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Simulates barcoded paired-end RNA-seq (SPIso-seq-style) reads from selected gene loci so that barcoded isoform assemblers like cloudrnaSPAdes can be benchmarked against annotated GENCODE isoforms with known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real SPIso-seq or other barcoded RNA-seq data — simulation is only needed to establish ground truth for benchmarking assemblers The target gene has a single annotated isoform and no alternative splicing, so isoform recall cannot be meaningfully measured The downstream assembler does not consume barcoded linked reads (e.g. plain short-read genome assemblers)

skills.description: Use when evaluating MaCroDNA cell-to-cell assignments on BE biopsy scDNA-seq/scRNA-seq data in the absence of ground truth, to test statistical significance and quantify assignment stability across resampled runs.
skills.name: barretts-esophagus-biopsy-heterogeneity-assessment
skills.search_text: barretts-esophagus-biopsy-heterogeneity-assessment Use when evaluating MaCroDNA cell-to-cell assignments on BE biopsy scDNA-seq/scRNA-seq data in the absence of ground truth, to test statistical significance and quantify assignment stability across resampled runs. Ground-truth cell correspondence is available (e.g., the CRC scTrio-seq dataset with partially known ground truth) — direct assignment-accuracy evaluation is then the right approach instead of resampling/stability proxies You need probabilistic confidence measures per assignment — MaCroDNA does not provide these (unlike clonealign); only the 'step' column of cell2cell_step offers an ordinal confidence ranking The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g., healthy/NDBE) and the goal is confident cell-to-cell matching — the article notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assess the reliability of MaCroDNA cell assignments on Barrett's esophagus (BE) biopsies — where no ground-truth scRNA-seq to scDNA-seq correspondence exists — via random-assignment null tests and resampling-based stability analyses, and relate stability to biopsy heterogeneity (homogeneous healthy/NDBE vs heterogeneous HGD/EAC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Assess the reliability of MaCroDNA cell assignments on Barrett's esophagus (BE) biopsies — where no ground-truth scRNA-seq to scDNA-seq correspondence exists — via random-assignment null tests and resampling-based stability analyses, and relate stability to biopsy heterogeneity (homogeneous healthy/NDBE vs heterogeneous HGD/EAC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth cell correspondence is available (e.g., the CRC scTrio-seq dataset with partially known ground truth) — direct assignment-accuracy evaluation is then the right approach instead of resampling/stability proxies You need probabilistic confidence measures per assignment — MaCroDNA does not provide these (unlike clonealign); only the 'step' column of cell2cell_step offers an ordinal confidence ranking The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g., healthy/NDBE) and the goal is confident cell-to-cell matching — the article notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples

skills.description: Use when single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression tables from Barrett's esophagus biopsies (NDBE, LGD, HGD, EAC) need cross-modality cell-to-clone assignment and per-gene phylogenetic signal (K*) analysis to test whether genomic mutations drive transcriptomic heterogeneity.
skills.name: barretts-esophagus-multiomic-reanalysis
skills.search_text: barretts-esophagus-multiomic-reanalysis Use when single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression tables from Barrett's esophagus biopsies (NDBE, LGD, HGD, EAC) need cross-modality cell-to-clone assignment and per-gene phylogenetic signal (K*) analysis to test whether genomic mutations drive transcriptomic heterogeneity. The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g. a non-progressing or healthy homogeneous biopsy): the article notes 'matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples', a biologically driven issue for MaCroDNA. Probabilistic confidence measures per assignment are required: MaCroDNA does not provide them, unlike statistical methods such as clonealign. Ground truth cell correspondence is available and accuracy can be measured directly — the BE dataset lacks ground truth, which is why resampling and stability analyses were needed instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reanalysis of Barrett's esophagus progression biopsies using MaCroDNA to assign scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq clones and compute per-gene K* phylogenetic signal, showing that genomic mutations of large effect size increasingly contribute to differential expression as BE progresses to dysplasia and esophageal adenocarcinoma. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Reanalysis of Barrett's esophagus progression biopsies using MaCroDNA to assign scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq clones and compute per-gene K* phylogenetic signal, showing that genomic mutations of large effect size increasingly contribute to differential expression as BE progresses to dysplasia and esophageal adenocarcinoma.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g. a non-progressing or healthy homogeneous biopsy): the article notes 'matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples', a biologically driven issue for MaCroDNA. Probabilistic confidence measures per assignment are required: MaCroDNA does not provide them, unlike statistical methods such as clonealign. Ground truth cell correspondence is available and accuracy can be measured directly — the BE dataset lacks ground truth, which is why resampling and stability analyses were needed instead.

skills.description: Use when preparing scGATE inputs from paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq data: you need a base GRN parquet (e.g. Buenrostro2018_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) of candidate TF–target edges derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF motifs before running scGATE_edge()/scGATE_gate().
skills.name: base-grn-construction-from-scatac-seq
skills.search_text: base-grn-construction-from-scatac-seq Use when preparing scGATE inputs from paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq data: you need a base GRN parquet (e.g. Buenrostro2018_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) of candidate TF–target edges derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF motifs before running scGATE_edge()/scGATE_gate(). You have no paired scATAC-seq data or TF motif annotations and must rely on prior biological knowledge to pre-select TFs — scGATE then runs without a base GRN (base_GRN = NA). You need large-scale network inference from scratch: the article notes scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list derived from external hints. Pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Constructs the per-target-gene candidate TF pool (base GRN) that scGATE consumes by identifying accessible chromatin peaks meeting co-accessibility and TSS-proximity criteria in scATAC-seq data, scanning peak DNA sequences for TF binding motifs, and linking peaks to nearby genes, stored as a parquet TF–target dataframe. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Constructs the per-target-gene candidate TF pool (base GRN) that scGATE consumes by identifying accessible chromatin peaks meeting co-accessibility and TSS-proximity criteria in scATAC-seq data, scanning peak DNA sequences for TF binding motifs, and linking peaks to nearby genes, stored as a parquet TF–target dataframe.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no paired scATAC-seq data or TF motif annotations and must rely on prior biological knowledge to pre-select TFs — scGATE then runs without a base GRN (base_GRN = NA). You need large-scale network inference from scratch: the article notes scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list derived from external hints. Pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data must be combined with a scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN (.parquet) to filter candidate TF-target pairs prior to directed TF-gene network or Boolean logic gate inference with scGATE.
skills.name: base-grn-integration-from-scatac-motif-hints
skills.search_text: base-grn-integration-from-scatac-motif-hints Use when scRNA-seq expression data must be combined with a scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN (.parquet) to filter candidate TF-target pairs prior to directed TF-gene network or Boolean logic gate inference with scGATE. No external scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN exists and the TF set has not been pre-selected from prior biological knowledge — scGATE logic inference is only reliable on a small (<200) gene subset with refined candidate TFs The goal is decoding Boolean logic among more than 5 regulators per target — overfitting is a major concern beyond k=5 candidate TFs The expression data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories or require modeling of temporal delays — scGATE does not handle these http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Integrates a base gene regulatory network derived from external hints (scATAC-seq peak accessibility plus TF DNA binding motifs, supplied as .parquet dataframes) with scRNA-seq data to narrow candidate TFs per target gene before scGATE network inference. This filtering step restricts scGATE to a small pre-selected TF set, which is required for reliable Boolean logic gate inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Integrates a base gene regulatory network derived from external hints (scATAC-seq peak accessibility plus TF DNA binding motifs, supplied as .parquet dataframes) with scRNA-seq data to narrow candidate TFs per target gene before scGATE network inference. This filtering step restricts scGATE to a small pre-selected TF set, which is required for reliable Boolean logic gate inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No external scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN exists and the TF set has not been pre-selected from prior biological knowledge — scGATE logic inference is only reliable on a small (<200) gene subset with refined candidate TFs The goal is decoding Boolean logic among more than 5 regulators per target — overfitting is a major concern beyond k=5 candidate TFs The expression data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories or require modeling of temporal delays — scGATE does not handle these

skills.description: Use when you have a base GRN edge list derived from scATAC-seq (e.g., the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas) plus an scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP) and need cluster-specific pruned GRNs.
skills.name: base-grn-integration-with-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: base-grn-integration-with-scrna-seq Use when you have a base GRN edge list derived from scATAC-seq (e.g., the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas) plus an scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP) and need cluster-specific pruned GRNs. Input is only an scRNA-seq dataset without a prebuilt base GRN — pruning requires epigenome-derived candidate edges; without them use de novo GRN inference instead The goal is perturbation simulation or cell-state transition prediction rather than producing context-dependent GRN configurations Expression matrix contains genes absent from the base GRN edge list and you need to extend the base GRN rather than prune it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Integrates an epigenome-derived base GRN with single-cell RNA-seq expression data using CellOracle to prune inactive TF-target edges and fit cluster-specific, weighted GRN configurations. This converts a static scATAC-seq-based edge list into context-dependent regulatory networks per cell state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Integrates an epigenome-derived base GRN with single-cell RNA-seq expression data using CellOracle to prune inactive TF-target edges and fit cluster-specific, weighted GRN configurations. This converts a static scATAC-seq-based edge list into context-dependent regulatory networks per cell state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only an scRNA-seq dataset without a prebuilt base GRN — pruning requires epigenome-derived candidate edges; without them use de novo GRN inference instead The goal is perturbation simulation or cell-state transition prediction rather than producing context-dependent GRN configurations Expression matrix contains genes absent from the base GRN edge list and you need to extend the base GRN rather than prune it

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq alignment files (BAM) for a sample cohort must be converted to a transcript-independent, base-level coverage matrix for downstream shape-change or structural-variation analysis with SCISSOR.
skills.name: base-level-pileup-processing
skills.search_text: base-level-pileup-processing Use when RNA-seq alignment files (BAM) for a sample cohort must be converted to a transcript-independent, base-level coverage matrix for downstream shape-change or structural-variation analysis with SCISSOR. The goal is isoform-level differential expression from exon-collapsed counts (DEXSeq/SpliceTrap style) rather than base-resolution coverage shape analysis Only junction-spanning read information is needed (transcript-agnostic methods like MISO/rMATS suffice) A cohort is too small for outlier-shape statistics — the authors note ~30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Obtain an uncompressed, base-resolution pileup matrix of RNA-seq coverage per gene (via SCISSOR's build_pileup and get_Ranges) so that structural alterations — splicing, intron retention, deletions, ATS/ATT — can be detected as coverage shape changes across a cohort. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Obtain an uncompressed, base-resolution pileup matrix of RNA-seq coverage per gene (via SCISSOR's build_pileup and get_Ranges) so that structural alterations — splicing, intron retention, deletions, ATS/ATT — can be detected as coverage shape changes across a cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is isoform-level differential expression from exon-collapsed counts (DEXSeq/SpliceTrap style) rather than base-resolution coverage shape analysis Only junction-spanning read information is needed (transcript-agnostic methods like MISO/rMATS suffice) A cohort is too small for outlier-shape statistics — the authors note ~30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully

Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been trimmed with Trimmomatic and mapped with BWA — recalibration operates on aligned BAM data Goal is RNA-Seq gene expression or gene fusion analysis, which TSNAD v2.0 handles with hisat2/Stringtie and STAR/Arriba rather than GATK recalibration http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Recalibrates base quality scores in BWA-mapped WES/WGS BAMs using GATK v4.2.0.0 as part of the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, producing the final BAM that feeds Mutect2 somatic SNV/INDEL calling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Recalibrates base quality scores in BWA-mapped WES/WGS BAMs using GATK v4.2.0.0 as part of the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, producing the final BAM that feeds Mutect2 somatic SNV/INDEL calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads that have not yet been trimmed with Trimmomatic and mapped with BWA — recalibration operates on aligned BAM data Goal is RNA-Seq gene expression or gene fusion analysis, which TSNAD v2.0 handles with hisat2/Stringtie and STAR/Arriba rather than GATK recalibration

skills.name: basecaller-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: basecaller-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating whether a modification-aware basecaller (e.g. NanoSpeech inosine-only or multi-mod models) detects modified bases as accurately as a baseline such as Guppy or Dorado+ModiKit on synthetic or IVT ONT dRNA datasets. Input is already basecalled fasta/fastq without raw signal — modification-aware basecalling from signal cannot be applied The goal is modification detection via re-squiggling with modification-unaware basecallers plus ad hoc models rather than single-step ab initio basecalling Data come from chemistries/kits outside those validated for the available NanoSpeech models http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark modification-aware ONT basecallers (NanoSpeech vs Guppy/Dorado+ModiKit) by basecalling raw dRNA fast5/pod5 reads, aligning with minimap2, extracting per-read and genome-space modification calls, and comparing accuracy, F1, mappability, identity and modification stoichiometry against reported figures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf709
skills.summary: Benchmark modification-aware ONT basecallers (NanoSpeech vs Guppy/Dorado+ModiKit) by basecalling raw dRNA fast5/pod5 reads, aligning with minimap2, extracting per-read and genome-space modification calls, and comparing accuracy, F1, mappability, identity and modification stoichiometry against reported figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled fasta/fastq without raw signal — modification-aware basecalling from signal cannot be applied The goal is modification detection via re-squiggling with modification-unaware basecallers plus ad hoc models rather than single-step ab initio basecalling Data come from chemistries/kits outside those validated for the available NanoSpeech models

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type classifiers on benchmark scRNA-seq data (simulated, PBMC-FACS, AMB2018) to quantify hierarchical F1-scores and unseen-population rejection rates for scHPL's linear vs one-class SVM against CHETAH and SVMrejection.
skills.name: baseline-classifier-comparison-chetah-svmrejection
skills.search_text: baseline-classifier-comparison-chetah-svmrejection Use when comparing cell-type classifiers on benchmark scRNA-seq data (simulated, PBMC-FACS, AMB2018) to quantify hierarchical F1-scores and unseen-population rejection rates for scHPL's linear vs one-class SVM against CHETAH and SVMrejection. skills.search_text: baseline-integration-method-execution Use when benchmarking a new single-cell diagonal-integration method against established baselines on paired-modality datasets (e.g. scRNA-scATAC 10X Multiome or CITE-seq scRNA-surface protein PBMC data) where identical inputs and metrics are required for a fair comparison. The modality pair has no cross-modality feature connections or is not one of the benchmarked pairings (e.g. electrophysiology vs gene expression), since anchor- and feature-based baselines were not evaluated in this setting The goal is paired-multimodal integration, which is out of scope for both scConfluence and these diagonal-integration baselines The dataset contains large modality-specific rare cell populations and a paired method like Seurat anchoring is used, since existing methods struggle with cell types absent in one modality http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run the five state-of-the-art single-cell multimodal integration baselines (Seurat, Liger, MultiMAP, Uniport, scGLUE) with their reference implementations and versions on the same diagonal-integration inputs as scConfluence, so that joint embeddings can be scored head-to-head on gold-standard PBMC 10X Multiome and CITE-seq benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: The modality pair has no cross-modality feature connections or is not one of the benchmarked pairings (e.g. electrophysiology vs gene expression), since anchor- and feature-based baselines were not evaluated in this setting The goal is paired-multimodal integration, which is out of scope for both scConfluence and these diagonal-integration baselines The dataset contains large modality-specific rare cell populations and a paired method like Seurat anchoring is used, since existing methods struggle with cell types absent in one modality

The goal is hyperparameter tuning or performance optimization of a single method — this skill deliberately runs all methods at default parameters for fair baseline comparison The query set contains no novel cell types (all query cell types are present in the reference) — the benchmark design requires held-out novel types such as dendritic cells and megakaryocytes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks novel rare cell detection methods (scNovel vs. scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred, scLearn) on cross-platform PBMCbench settings using default parameters, scoring AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 to quantify robustness to batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Benchmarks novel rare cell detection methods (scNovel vs. scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred, scLearn) on cross-platform PBMCbench settings using default parameters, scoring AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 to quantify robustness to batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is hyperparameter tuning or performance optimization of a single method — this skill deliberately runs all methods at default parameters for fair baseline comparison The query set contains no novel cell types (all query cell types are present in the reference) — the benchmark design requires held-out novel types such as dendritic cells and megakaryocytes

skills.search_text: bash-based-scrna-pipeline-execution Use when raw 10xv3 scRNA-seq FASTQ reads need alignment and quantification into spliced/unspliced count matrices, especially when CellRanger is too slow or RNA velocity / splicing-dynamics downstream analyses are planned. Input is already a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix — scKB operates on raw FASTQ reads, and the matrices should instead be fed directly into COPILOT quality filtering The reads are not from a 10x Genomics v3 chemistry library, since the workflow is parameterized with the 10xv3 index and the 10xv3 whitelist A splice-aware whole-genome alignment is required (e.g. genome browser track generation), as scKB performs pseudoalignment for transcript counting only http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Executes the scKB bash wrapper script, which orchestrates kallisto pseudoalignment against a cDNA+introns index and bustools barcode correction to generate spliced and unspliced gene-by-cell count matrices from 10x Genomics scRNA-seq FASTQs, roughly 30x faster than CellRanger 3.1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101729
skills.summary: Executes the scKB bash wrapper script, which orchestrates kallisto pseudoalignment against a cDNA+introns index and bustools barcode correction to generate spliced and unspliced gene-by-cell count matrices from 10x Genomics scRNA-seq FASTQs, roughly 30x faster than CellRanger 3.1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix — scKB operates on raw FASTQ reads, and the matrices should instead be fed directly into COPILOT quality filtering The reads are not from a 10x Genomics v3 chemistry library, since the workflow is parameterized with the 10xv3 index and the 10xv3 whitelist A splice-aware whole-genome alignment is required (e.g. genome browser track generation), as scKB performs pseudoalignment for transcript counting only

skills.description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple batches where batch effect must be removed jointly with clustering, and no reliable batch annotation is available (DESC does not explicitly require batch information).
skills.name: batch-aware-deep-learning-clustering
skills.search_text: batch-aware-deep-learning-clustering Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple batches where batch effect must be removed jointly with clustering, and no reliable batch annotation is available (DESC does not explicitly require batch information). When batch information is explicit and a batch-supervised method like scVI or BERMUDA is required by the design When technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC removes batch effects only as long as technical differences are smaller than biological variation When reproduction of published results requires tensorflow >= 2.0 with the desc 2.0.3 release — the README states tensorflow must be lower than 2.0 for paper-equivalent results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply DESC, an unsupervised deep embedding algorithm that clusters scRNA-seq data by iteratively optimizing a KL-divergence clustering objective, so that batch effects are gradually removed during clustering without explicitly supplying batch labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Apply DESC, an unsupervised deep embedding algorithm that clusters scRNA-seq data by iteratively optimizing a KL-divergence clustering objective, so that batch effects are gradually removed during clustering without explicitly supplying batch labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When batch information is explicit and a batch-supervised method like scVI or BERMUDA is required by the design When technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC removes batch effects only as long as technical differences are smaller than biological variation When reproduction of published results requires tensorflow >= 2.0 with the desc 2.0.3 release — the README states tensorflow must be lower than 2.0 for paper-equivalent results

skills.description: Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq count matrices from independent studies and you need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding in which batch/study-of-origin effects are removed before clustering or label propagation.
skills.name: batch-corrected-kernel-reduction
skills.search_text: batch-corrected-kernel-reduction Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq count matrices from independent studies and you need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding in which batch/study-of-origin effects are removed before clustering or label propagation. Input is a single homogeneous dataset with no batch/study structure — plain reduce_kernel without correction is sufficient Data have not been filtered and normalized (filter_adata with min_cells_per_feature=0.01, min_features_per_cell=1000, then normalize_total and log1p must precede the reduction) The goal requires preserving batch-specific technical signals rather than removing them (e.g., QC auditing of per-study effects) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Low-rank cell-space reduction (randomized SVD) performed with Harmony-style batch correction so that downstream ACTIONet archetypal analysis and network construction group cells by cell type rather than by study of origin. This is the integration entry point used to merge the Velmeshev, Mathys, and Schirmer human prefrontal cortex datasets (105,099 cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Low-rank cell-space reduction (randomized SVD) performed with Harmony-style batch correction so that downstream ACTIONet archetypal analysis and network construction group cells by cell type rather than by study of origin. This is the integration entry point used to merge the Velmeshev, Mathys, and Schirmer human prefrontal cortex datasets (105,099 cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single homogeneous dataset with no batch/study structure — plain reduce_kernel without correction is sufficient Data have not been filtered and normalized (filter_adata with min_cells_per_feature=0.01, min_features_per_cell=1000, then normalize_total and log1p must precede the reduction) The goal requires preserving batch-specific technical signals rather than removing them (e.g., QC auditing of per-study effects)

skills.description: Use when you have multi-sample/single-batch-annotated scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq embeddings and need a quantitative benchmark of how well alternative embedding/correction methods mix batches while retaining phenotypic information such as diagnosis, sex, or disease stage.

skills.search_text: batch-correction-method-benchmarking Use when you have multi-sample/single-batch-annotated scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq embeddings and need a quantitative benchmark of how well alternative embedding/correction methods mix batches while retaining phenotypic information such as diagnosis, sex, or disease stage. Input is already batch-corrected or has no sample/batch annotation, making the neighborhood-score batch-mixing metric uncomputable The biological question is GRN inference accuracy (e.g. perturbation-target prediction), not embedding-quality comparison across correction methods The dataset lacks a phenotype annotation (diagnosis/sex/stage) needed for the phenotype F1 score http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Quantitatively compares the batch-effect correction and biological signal retention of SCING GRN module AUCell embeddings against dedicated batch correction methods (FastMNN, Harmony, Seurat) using neighborhood scores and phenotype F1 metrics on the Morabito human prefrontal cortex snRNA-seq AD dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Quantitatively compares the batch-effect correction and biological signal retention of SCING GRN module AUCell embeddings against dedicated batch correction methods (FastMNN, Harmony, Seurat) using neighborhood scores and phenotype F1 metrics on the Morabito human prefrontal cortex snRNA-seq AD dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already batch-corrected or has no sample/batch annotation, making the neighborhood-score batch-mixing metric uncomputable The biological question is GRN inference accuracy (e.g. perturbation-target prediction), not embedding-quality comparison across correction methods The dataset lacks a phenotype annotation (diagnosis/sex/stage) needed for the phenotype F1 score
