The input is already a corrected/normalized feature table rather than raw ranked gene-expression data — tGPT expects gene expression rankings, not expression levels Data are from a single batch/donor with no batch variable available, making kBET and batch-correction comparison meaningless (the paper notes batch information is not always available) The analysis targets differential fold-change interpretation, since tGPT's rank-based input neglects fold changes among genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a transformer-pretrained representation (tGPT) against eleven established batch-correction methods (ComBat, MNN, Harmony, Seurat, BBKNN, Scanorama, Pegasus, scVI, scArches, iMAP, DESC) using kBET acceptance rates on the HCA bone-marrow dataset, where tGPT's rank-based input design is expected to confer batch insensitivity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Benchmark a transformer-pretrained representation (tGPT) against eleven established batch-correction methods (ComBat, MNN, Harmony, Seurat, BBKNN, Scanorama, Pegasus, scVI, scArches, iMAP, DESC) using kBET acceptance rates on the HCA bone-marrow dataset, where tGPT's rank-based input design is expected to confer batch insensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a corrected/normalized feature table rather than raw ranked gene-expression data — tGPT expects gene expression rankings, not expression levels Data are from a single batch/donor with no batch variable available, making kBET and batch-correction comparison meaningless (the paper notes batch information is not always available) The analysis targets differential fold-change interpretation, since tGPT's rank-based input neglects fold changes among genes

skills.description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData contain multiple sequencing batches and you need batch-corrected RNA velocities and latent cell states that preserve gene expression dynamics, e.g. with ltv.models.VAE(batch_correction=True, batches=n).
skills.name: batch-correction-model-conditioning
skills.search_text: batch-correction-model-conditioning Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData contain multiple sequencing batches and you need batch-corrected RNA velocities and latent cell states that preserve gene expression dynamics, e.g. with ltv.models.VAE(batch_correction=True, batches=n). The dataset contains a single sequencing batch — batch conditioning adds unnecessary complexity with no correction benefit You need batch correction of static expression embeddings without regard to spliced/unspliced gene dynamics — a dynamics-agnostic autoencoder correction method is the (weaker) alternative the article benchmarks against Cells come from sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — the article notes latent trajectories may then not start from expected initial states http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Enable RNA velocity batch correction in LatentVelo by conditioning the structured latent neural-ODE model on sequencing batch (batch_correction=True with a batches argument in ltv.models.VAE or ltv.models.AnnotVAE), so that the dynamics-based latent space yields batch-corrected cell states and velocities rather than correcting expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Enable RNA velocity batch correction in LatentVelo by conditioning the structured latent neural-ODE model on sequencing batch (batch_correction=True with a batches argument in ltv.models.VAE or ltv.models.AnnotVAE), so that the dynamics-based latent space yields batch-corrected cell states and velocities rather than correcting expression alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains a single sequencing batch — batch conditioning adds unnecessary complexity with no correction benefit You need batch correction of static expression embeddings without regard to spliced/unspliced gene dynamics — a dynamics-agnostic autoencoder correction method is the (weaker) alternative the article benchmarks against Cells come from sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — the article notes latent trajectories may then not start from expected initial states

skills.description: Use when paired multi-omics data (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq via 10X Multiome) are profiled across multiple batches or centers and you need to train, evaluate, and compare batch-corrected versus uncorrected Mowgli embeddings.
skills.name: batch-correction-multiomics-integration
skills.search_text: batch-correction-multiomics-integration Use when paired multi-omics data (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq via 10X Multiome) are profiled across multiple batches or centers and you need to train, evaluate, and compare batch-corrected versus uncorrected Mowgli embeddings. When data come from a single batch/center and no batch effect needs correcting — the uncorrected Mowgli model suffices When the integration is unimodal or unpaired, since Mowgli is designed for paired multi-omics data with any type and number of omics When you need a straightforward way to choose the number of latent dimensions k, which Mowgli does not offer — several values of k must be tested separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A reusable evaluation framework for extending Mowgli with batch correction on paired multi-omics data profiled across centers, leveraging the method's existing embedding and clustering metrics (silhouette score, ARI, purity score). The article explicitly flags batch correction of paired multi-omics integration as an open avenue for future work. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: A reusable evaluation framework for extending Mowgli with batch correction on paired multi-omics data profiled across centers, leveraging the method's existing embedding and clustering metrics (silhouette score, ARI, purity score). The article explicitly flags batch correction of paired multi-omics integration as an open avenue for future work.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When data come from a single batch/center and no batch effect needs correcting — the uncorrected Mowgli model suffices When the integration is unimodal or unpaired, since Mowgli is designed for paired multi-omics data with any type and number of omics When you need a straightforward way to choose the number of latent dimensions k, which Mowgli does not offer — several values of k must be tested separately

skills.description: Use when a cell-attribute-aware DA-testing workflow (e.g. ELVAR/EVA clustering) must be stress-tested for robustness to whether batch correction is applied beforehand, and to quantify how correction shifts significance of DA-test results.
skills.name: batch-correction-scenario-benchmarking
skills.search_text: batch-correction-scenario-benchmarking Use when a cell-attribute-aware DA-testing workflow (e.g. ELVAR/EVA clustering) must be stress-tested for robustness to whether batch correction is applied beforehand, and to quantify how correction shifts significance of DA-test results. When the question is whether batch correction itself changes DA significance for a non-attribute-aware method (e.g. plain Louvain or Milo) — the article's claim that correction is dispensable is specific to cell-attribute aware clustering When cell-type labels or the clustering attribute contain suspected false positives and the goal is annotation-noise robustness rather than batch-correction robustness (that is a separate false-positive-flipping scenario) When the study has very strong clustering structure where ELVAR's advantage over Louvain and its robustness profile are less pronounced http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A robustness benchmarking procedure that re-runs the ELVAR differential abundance pipeline on the same cell-cell kNN graph under multiple preprocessing variants (no batch correction, Harmony-corrected embeddings, Seurat integration-corrected embeddings) and compares DA-detection sensitivity and z-statistic distributions, since attribute-aware clustering may obviate batch correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: A robustness benchmarking procedure that re-runs the ELVAR differential abundance pipeline on the same cell-cell kNN graph under multiple preprocessing variants (no batch correction, Harmony-corrected embeddings, Seurat integration-corrected embeddings) and compares DA-detection sensitivity and z-statistic distributions, since attribute-aware clustering may obviate batch correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is whether batch correction itself changes DA significance for a non-attribute-aware method (e.g. plain Louvain or Milo) — the article's claim that correction is dispensable is specific to cell-attribute aware clustering When cell-type labels or the clustering attribute contain suspected false positives and the goal is annotation-noise robustness rather than batch-correction robustness (that is a separate false-positive-flipping scenario) When the study has very strong clustering structure where ELVAR's advantage over Louvain and its robustness profile are less pronounced

skills.description: Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq count data (e.g., Kolodziejczyk mESC across culture media) must be decomposed so the low-dimensional representation clusters by a known biological variable while dependence on batch is measured and removed.
skills.name: batch-covariate-signal-extraction
skills.search_text: batch-covariate-signal-extraction Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq count data (e.g., Kolodziejczyk mESC across culture media) must be decomposed so the low-dimensional representation clusters by a known biological variable while dependence on batch is measured and removed. Unwanted technical variation is already removed by prior normalization or by including QC measures as cell-level covariates, so a batch-covariate contrast adds no information The goal is supervised differential expression between batches — the article notes this capability is only envisioned for a future zinbwave version There are no known batch or biological group labels, so the batch/cluster silhouette comparison cannot be evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit ZINB-WaVE's zero-inflated negative binomial model with and without batch indicator variables as sample-level covariates (X' matrix) on raw scRNA-seq counts, then compare cluster and batch average silhouette widths to verify the batch covariates remove batch dependence from the low-dimensional W factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Fit ZINB-WaVE's zero-inflated negative binomial model with and without batch indicator variables as sample-level covariates (X' matrix) on raw scRNA-seq counts, then compare cluster and batch average silhouette widths to verify the batch covariates remove batch dependence from the low-dimensional W factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Unwanted technical variation is already removed by prior normalization or by including QC measures as cell-level covariates, so a batch-covariate contrast adds no information The goal is supervised differential expression between batches — the article notes this capability is only envisioned for a future zinbwave version There are no known batch or biological group labels, so the batch/cluster silhouette comparison cannot be evaluated

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq raw count data have technical batches that are partially confounded with biology (e.g., each patient/biological replicate processed in a separate batch) and you must remove batch effects without erasing the biological signal.
skills.name: batch-effect-assessment
skills.search_text: batch-effect-assessment Use when single-cell RNA-seq raw count data have technical batches that are partially confounded with biology (e.g., each patient/biological replicate processed in a separate batch) and you must remove batch effects without erasing the biological signal. When batch and biology are completely confounded and no unconfounded technical covariate (such as detection rate) is available — the batch-indicator covariate model failed to preserve patient separation in this exact setting When the goal is supervised differential expression accounting for zero inflation — the article notes this capability is not yet available and only envisioned for a future zinbwave version When the input is already normalized/transformed expression rather than raw counts — zinbwave is designed to model raw count data directly via its global-scaling intercept http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assess and remove batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq by fitting a ZINB-WaVE zero-inflated negative binomial model in which unwanted variation (e.g., detection rate) enters as a sample-level covariate, so the latent factors W capture only unexplained variation. This enables judging, via PCA of W colored by batch and by biological condition, whether batches mix while biology (e.g., patient effects) is preserved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Assess and remove batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq by fitting a ZINB-WaVE zero-inflated negative binomial model in which unwanted variation (e.g., detection rate) enters as a sample-level covariate, so the latent factors W capture only unexplained variation. This enables judging, via PCA of W colored by batch and by biological condition, whether batches mix while biology (e.g., patient effects) is preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When batch and biology are completely confounded and no unconfounded technical covariate (such as detection rate) is available — the batch-indicator covariate model failed to preserve patient separation in this exact setting When the goal is supervised differential expression accounting for zero inflation — the article notes this capability is not yet available and only envisioned for a future zinbwave version When the input is already normalized/transformed expression rather than raw counts — zinbwave is designed to model raw count data directly via its global-scaling intercept

skills.name: batch-effect-correction-vector-arithmetic
skills.search_text: batch-effect-correction-vector-arithmetic Use when scRNA-seq AnnData objects with a trained GeneVector cell embedding (cell_embed) contain batch/treatment labels (e.g., control vs interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) and batch effects must be removed while retaining stimulus-driven variation for downstream UMAP and silhouette benchmarking. Batches differ strongly in cell type composition — the article notes batch correction is 'challenging in the presence of batch-specific differences in cell type composition' and users must manually verify correction vectors against cell type signatures Input is a raw expression matrix with no trained GeneVector gene/cell embedding — train the embedding (task_001-style workflow) before vector arithmetic correction Goal is gene-level regulatory directionality (activation vs repression) — GeneVector's MI is agnostic to direction of statistical dependency and correction vectors cannot resolve this http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Corrects batch effects in GeneVector cell embeddings by subtracting batch-average gene embeddings from a reference batch (Vcorrection = Vreference − Vbatch) and adding the resulting correction vector to each cell embedding, preserving biological variation (e.g., interferon-stimulated myeloid ISG programs) that Harmony-based alignment removes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Corrects batch effects in GeneVector cell embeddings by subtracting batch-average gene embeddings from a reference batch (Vcorrection = Vreference − Vbatch) and adding the resulting correction vector to each cell embedding, preserving biological variation (e.g., interferon-stimulated myeloid ISG programs) that Harmony-based alignment removes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Batches differ strongly in cell type composition — the article notes batch correction is 'challenging in the presence of batch-specific differences in cell type composition' and users must manually verify correction vectors against cell type signatures Input is a raw expression matrix with no trained GeneVector gene/cell embedding — train the embedding (task_001-style workflow) before vector arithmetic correction Goal is gene-level regulatory directionality (activation vs repression) — GeneVector's MI is agnostic to direction of statistical dependency and correction vectors cannot resolve this

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain multiple batches (e.g., patients or samples, with a metadata CSV batch column such as 'PatientID') and the top PCs must be batch-corrected with Harmony before Louvain clustering in the scDrug/Scanpy pipeline.
skills.name: batch-effect-correction-with-harmony
skills.search_text: batch-effect-correction-with-harmony Use when scRNA-seq data contain multiple batches (e.g., patients or samples, with a metadata CSV batch column such as 'PatientID') and the top PCs must be batch-corrected with Harmony before Louvain clustering in the scDrug/Scanpy pipeline. Input is a single homogeneous sample with no batch column defined — batch correction is applied only 'if needed' and would remove genuine variation The goal is drug response prediction (CaDRReS-Sc IC50 / PRISM AUC) or treatment selection on an already-clustered object — those stages take scanpyobj.h5ad and do not re-correct PCs Cells lack matched batch metadata, since scDrug requires a metadata CSV and a named batch column (e.g., 'PatientID') to run correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Corrects batch effects in scRNA-seq data by adjusting the top principal components with the Harmony algorithm within the scDrug pipeline, so that downstream Louvain clustering and sub-clustering (e.g., of the GSE156625 hepatocellular carcinoma dataset) are not driven by technical or patient-level batch structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Corrects batch effects in scRNA-seq data by adjusting the top principal components with the Harmony algorithm within the scDrug pipeline, so that downstream Louvain clustering and sub-clustering (e.g., of the GSE156625 hepatocellular carcinoma dataset) are not driven by technical or patient-level batch structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single homogeneous sample with no batch column defined — batch correction is applied only 'if needed' and would remove genuine variation The goal is drug response prediction (CaDRReS-Sc IC50 / PRISM AUC) or treatment selection on an already-clustered object — those stages take scanpyobj.h5ad and do not re-correct PCs Cells lack matched batch metadata, since scDrug requires a metadata CSV and a named batch column (e.g., 'PatientID') to run correction

skills.description: Use when multi-individual droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count matrices show batch effects (e.g., same-batch samples clustering together in t-SNE of 50 PCs) and you need corrected/aligned data as input to downstream clustering baselines.
skills.name: batch-effect-correction-with-mnn-and-cca
skills.search_text: batch-effect-correction-with-mnn-and-cca Use when multi-individual droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count matrices show batch effects (e.g., same-batch samples clustering together in t-SNE of 50 PCs) and you need corrected/aligned data as input to downstream clustering baselines. The analysis goal is principled multi-individual clustering of raw UMI counts that accounts for heterogeneity and unbalanced sequencing depth — use a model-based approach like BAMM-SC instead, since naive correction discards information (Cell Ranger downsampling causes 'substantial information loss') Only a single individual/library is present — there is no between-batch effect to correct Genes have not been filtered for excessive zeros; lowly-expressed genes should be removed before correction and clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies mutual nearest neighbors (MNN) batch correction implemented in scran, or CCA-based alignment, to scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple individuals before clustering, as batch-effect-removal baselines against which model-based multi-individual clustering (e.g., BAMM-SC) can be benchmarked via adjusted Rand index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Applies mutual nearest neighbors (MNN) batch correction implemented in scran, or CCA-based alignment, to scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple individuals before clustering, as batch-effect-removal baselines against which model-based multi-individual clustering (e.g., BAMM-SC) can be benchmarked via adjusted Rand index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is principled multi-individual clustering of raw UMI counts that accounts for heterogeneity and unbalanced sequencing depth — use a model-based approach like BAMM-SC instead, since naive correction discards information (Cell Ranger downsampling causes 'substantial information loss') Only a single individual/library is present — there is no between-batch effect to correct Genes have not been filtered for excessive zeros; lowly-expressed genes should be removed before correction and clustering

skills.description: Use when single-cell-derived pseudobulk feature matrices (e.g., scPAFA PAS aggregated per sample) contain clearly known technical batch effects and you need unsupervised factor analysis that separates batch from biological/disease variance.
skills.name: batch-effect-correction-with-mofa-plus
skills.search_text: batch-effect-correction-with-mofa-plus Use when single-cell-derived pseudobulk feature matrices (e.g., scPAFA PAS aggregated per sample) contain clearly known technical batch effects and you need unsupervised factor analysis that separates batch from biological/disease variance. The study has fewer than 15 samples (not cells), since scPAFA requires at least 15 samples to use the MOFA model for identifying multicellular pathway modules Batch effects are unknown or unannotated — the multi-group framework requires clearly known batch effects to declare groups; without labels the single-group framework is the appropriate choice You need causal attribution of pathway-cell type associations — MOFA is linear and the modules are data-driven associations, not biological causal effects http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train a multi-group MOFA+ model on a pseudobulk pathway activity score (PAS) matrix so that known technical batch effects are modeled as groups, allowing latent factors to capture disease-related variance in PAS among samples rather than batch-driven artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Train a multi-group MOFA+ model on a pseudobulk pathway activity score (PAS) matrix so that known technical batch effects are modeled as groups, allowing latent factors to capture disease-related variance in PAS among samples rather than batch-driven artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study has fewer than 15 samples (not cells), since scPAFA requires at least 15 samples to use the MOFA model for identifying multicellular pathway modules Batch effects are unknown or unannotated — the multi-group framework requires clearly known batch effects to declare groups; without labels the single-group framework is the appropriate choice You need causal attribution of pathway-cell type associations — MOFA is linear and the modules are data-driven associations, not biological causal effects

skills.description: Use when normalized microarray intensity data (e.g. quantile- or LOESS-normalized samples from example_unnorm.txt) must be screened for systematic processing artifacts such as date, operator, or reagent lot effects before downstream analysis.
skills.name: batch-effect-detection-in-microarray-samples
skills.search_text: batch-effect-detection-in-microarray-samples Use when normalized microarray intensity data (e.g. quantile- or LOESS-normalized samples from example_unnorm.txt) must be screened for systematic processing artifacts such as date, operator, or reagent lot effects before downstream analysis. Input data is raw and has not been preprocessed/normalized with PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command — the dendrogram should be judged on normalized data (quantile or LOESS) Samples come from a single processing batch with no technical metadata to compare clusters against, so clustering cannot distinguish batch from biological structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects batch effects in microarray expression data by using PIMENTo to generate a dendrogram of all chosen samples based on Euclidean distances with Ward's method, then inspecting whether clusters align with technical variables (date, operator, reagent lot) rather than biological response classes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-9004-7_11
skills.summary: Detects batch effects in microarray expression data by using PIMENTo to generate a dendrogram of all chosen samples based on Euclidean distances with Ward's method, then inspecting whether clusters align with technical variables (date, operator, reagent lot) rather than biological response classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw and has not been preprocessed/normalized with PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command — the dendrogram should be judged on normalized data (quantile or LOESS) Samples come from a single processing batch with no technical metadata to compare clusters against, so clustering cannot distinguish batch from biological structure

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression data are collected across multiple batches or replicates and batch effects must be diagnosed before z-score normalization and clustering.
skills.name: batch-effect-diagnostic-assessment
skills.search_text: batch-effect-diagnostic-assessment Use when scRNA-Seq expression data are collected across multiple batches or replicates and batch effects must be diagnosed before z-score normalization and clustering. When the dataset contains a single batch or replicate, there are no cross-batch distributions to compare and batch.analysis is unnecessary When the goal is downstream cell clustering or gene signature prediction rather than diagnosing confounding batch effects in preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A SINCERA preprocessing skill that uses the batch.analysis function to detect and quantify batch differences in scRNA-Seq expression data by comparing per-cell expression quantiles, MA plots, Q-Q plots, and cell correlation/distance measures across batches before downstream analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: A SINCERA preprocessing skill that uses the batch.analysis function to detect and quantify batch differences in scRNA-Seq expression data by comparing per-cell expression quantiles, MA plots, Q-Q plots, and cell correlation/distance measures across batches before downstream analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset contains a single batch or replicate, there are no cross-batch distributions to compare and batch.analysis is unnecessary When the goal is downstream cell clustering or gene signature prediction rather than diagnosing confounding batch effects in preprocessing

skills.description: Use when integrating multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. DLPFC or seqFISH sections) whose low-dimensional embeddings contain batch effects that must be estimated jointly with spatial clustering.
skills.name: batch-effect-embedding-estimation
skills.search_text: batch-effect-embedding-estimation Use when integrating multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. DLPFC or seqFISH sections) whose low-dimensional embeddings contain batch effects that must be estimated jointly with spatial clustering. Single-sample SRT data with no batch structure — the plain SC.MEB empirical-Bayes hidden-Markov-random-field model suffices instead of the integrated iSC.MEB extension Datasets where only raw counts (not low-dimensional representations) are available and no dimensionality reduction (e.g. runPCA with pca.method = 'APCA', npcs = 15) has been performed yet Analyses needing cell-type annotation of counts rather than joint batch-effect and spatial-domain estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate batch-effect embeddings jointly with spatial cluster labels by fitting the iSC.MEB hidden-Markov-random-field model with empirical Bayes, using the ICM-EM algorithm from the iSC.MEB R package. The batch-related embeddings are updated iteratively against cluster labels so multiple SRT datasets can be integrated despite batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Estimate batch-effect embeddings jointly with spatial cluster labels by fitting the iSC.MEB hidden-Markov-random-field model with empirical Bayes, using the ICM-EM algorithm from the iSC.MEB R package. The batch-related embeddings are updated iteratively against cluster labels so multiple SRT datasets can be integrated despite batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-sample SRT data with no batch structure — the plain SC.MEB empirical-Bayes hidden-Markov-random-field model suffices instead of the integrated iSC.MEB extension Datasets where only raw counts (not low-dimensional representations) are available and no dimensionality reduction (e.g. runPCA with pca.method = 'APCA', npcs = 15) has been performed yet Analyses needing cell-type annotation of counts rather than joint batch-effect and spatial-domain estimation

skills.description: Use when analyzing multiple SRT tissue sections (e.g. six mouse embryo seqFISH sections or twelve human DLPFC sections) where cross-sample batch effects must be estimated simultaneously with spatial domain clustering, and integrated clustering metrics are needed.
skills.name: batch-effect-integration-across-tissue-sections
skills.search_text: batch-effect-integration-across-tissue-sections Use when analyzing multiple SRT tissue sections (e.g. six mouse embryo seqFISH sections or twelve human DLPFC sections) where cross-sample batch effects must be estimated simultaneously with spatial domain clustering, and integrated clustering metrics are needed. Single-section SRT data with no batches to integrate — the SC.MEB model (which iSC.MEB extends) is the appropriate one-sample choice Non-spatial single-cell data without coordinates, since CreateNeighbors requires spatial locations to build the adjacency matrix Benchmarks where only pre-corrected (batch-removed) expression matrices are available, since iSC.MEB is designed to estimate batch effects itself from the multi-section input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Jointly estimate batch effects and perform spatial clustering on low-dimensional representations of multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) sections using iSC.MEB, a hidden Markov random field model fitted with empirical Bayes. It enables domain detection across sections while integrating samples that may share only partially overlapping clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Jointly estimate batch effects and perform spatial clustering on low-dimensional representations of multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) sections using iSC.MEB, a hidden Markov random field model fitted with empirical Bayes. It enables domain detection across sections while integrating samples that may share only partially overlapping clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-section SRT data with no batches to integrate — the SC.MEB model (which iSC.MEB extends) is the appropriate one-sample choice Non-spatial single-cell data without coordinates, since CreateNeighbors requires spatial locations to build the adjacency matrix Benchmarks where only pre-corrected (batch-removed) expression matrices are available, since iSC.MEB is designed to estimate batch effects itself from the multi-section input

skills.description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama) on integrated scRNA-seq datasets and you need a numeric mixing-vs-structure tradeoff score such as mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN.
skills.name: batch-effect-quantification-ilisi
skills.search_text: batch-effect-quantification-ilisi Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama) on integrated scRNA-seq datasets and you need a numeric mixing-vs-structure tradeoff score such as mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN. Integrating more than two datasets with BATMAN itself — the current implementation works only with two datasets (the metric can still be computed, but the correction step cannot) Data that has not been batch-integrated or for which batch labels are unavailable, since iLISI depends on batch composition of neighborhoods Assessing integration of datasets of very different library chemistries where iLISI mixing may be misleading without complementary structure metrics (pair with 50-RNN) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify batch-effect removal quality of single-cell RNA-seq integration by computing mean iLISI (integration Local Inverse Simpson Index) alongside mean 50-RNN (retained neighbor relationships), as benchmarked in the BATMAN paper on 10X Genomics PBMC 8k vs Pan T cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Quantify batch-effect removal quality of single-cell RNA-seq integration by computing mean iLISI (integration Local Inverse Simpson Index) alongside mean 50-RNN (retained neighbor relationships), as benchmarked in the BATMAN paper on 10X Genomics PBMC 8k vs Pan T cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Integrating more than two datasets with BATMAN itself — the current implementation works only with two datasets (the metric can still be computed, but the correction step cannot) Data that has not been batch-integrated or for which batch labels are unavailable, since iLISI depends on batch composition of neighborhoods Assessing integration of datasets of very different library chemistries where iLISI mixing may be misleading without complementary structure metrics (pair with 50-RNN)

skills.description: Use when comparing imputed vs. raw scRNA-Seq matrices for batch correction on datasets with known batch and cell-type annotations (e.g., Villani PBMC GSE80171, Baron pancreatic islet) and numeric batch-merging scores are needed.
skills.name: batch-effect-quantification-scoring
skills.search_text: batch-effect-quantification-scoring Use when comparing imputed vs. raw scRNA-Seq matrices for batch correction on datasets with known batch and cell-type annotations (e.g., Villani PBMC GSE80171, Baron pancreatic islet) and numeric batch-merging scores are needed. Data lack both batch annotations and known cell-type labels, making ASW batch-merging and ARI/NMI/purity scoring undefined Goal is imputation itself (use AutoClassImpute/DCA/SAVER/scImpute/MAGIC directly) rather than scoring their batch-effect removal Evaluating on the simulated Splatter Dataset 1 ground-truth recovery task, where data-recovery correlation rather than batch metrics is the correct criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies batch-effect removal and cell-type separation in scRNA-Seq embeddings by clustering t-SNE coordinates with KMeans (K=8,9,10, random_state=1) and scoring against known labels using average silhouette width (ASW), adjusted Rand index (ARI), normalized mutual information (NMI), and purity score. This skill operationalizes the Fig. 5 / Supplementary Figs. 4-5 evaluation from AutoClass (Li et al., Nat Commun 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Quantifies batch-effect removal and cell-type separation in scRNA-Seq embeddings by clustering t-SNE coordinates with KMeans (K=8,9,10, random_state=1) and scoring against known labels using average silhouette width (ASW), adjusted Rand index (ARI), normalized mutual information (NMI), and purity score. This skill operationalizes the Fig. 5 / Supplementary Figs. 4-5 evaluation from AutoClass (Li et al., Nat Commun 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack both batch annotations and known cell-type labels, making ASW batch-merging and ARI/NMI/purity scoring undefined Goal is imputation itself (use AutoClassImpute/DCA/SAVER/scImpute/MAGIC directly) rather than scoring their batch-effect removal Evaluating on the simulated Splatter Dataset 1 ground-truth recovery task, where data-recovery correlation rather than batch metrics is the correct criterion

skills.description: Use when per-cell batch labels and a low-dimensional representation (e.g., DESC's X_Embeded_z in adata.obsm) or derived quantities such as Monocle3 pseudotime are available, and you need a numeric, distribution-level measure of whether batches are well mixed.
skills.name: batch-effect-quantification-via-kl-divergence
skills.search_text: batch-effect-quantification-via-kl-divergence Use when per-cell batch labels and a low-dimensional representation (e.g., DESC's X_Embeded_z in adata.obsm) or derived quantities such as Monocle3 pseudotime are available, and you need a numeric, distribution-level measure of whether batches are well mixed. Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variation — DESC's iterative self-learning only removes batch effects 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' No per-cell batch labels are available, since the regional batch-mixing KL divergence is computed between batch-specific distributions The corrected embedding order-dependence matters and a non-pairwise evaluation is required on data where pairwise-based correction methods (CCA, MNN, Seurat 3.0, Scanorama) were applied http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies batch effect removal by repeatedly computing regional KL divergence between batch-specific distributions (e.g., pseudotime or embedding neighborhoods) over randomly chosen cells, using K = 5 × number of batches nearest neighbors, and summarizing across 200 iterations as box plots. This is the criterion used in the DESC paper to confirm that the DESC representation removed batch effect in the three-batch 10,878-cell human monocyte dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Quantifies batch effect removal by repeatedly computing regional KL divergence between batch-specific distributions (e.g., pseudotime or embedding neighborhoods) over randomly chosen cells, using K = 5 × number of batches nearest neighbors, and summarizing across 200 iterations as box plots. This is the criterion used in the DESC paper to confirm that the DESC representation removed batch effect in the three-batch 10,878-cell human monocyte dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variation — DESC's iterative self-learning only removes batch effects 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' No per-cell batch labels are available, since the regional batch-mixing KL divergence is computed between batch-specific distributions The corrected embedding order-dependence matters and a non-pairwise evaluation is required on data where pairwise-based correction methods (CCA, MNN, Seurat 3.0, Scanorama) were applied

skills.description: Use when combining scRNA-seq count matrices generated by different library-preparation protocols or batches, and the goal is cell-type clustering with batch effect removed in a single joint analysis (measured by ARI and cell-type classification accuracy).
skills.name: batch-effect-removal-across-protocols
skills.search_text: batch-effect-removal-across-protocols Use when combining scRNA-seq count matrices generated by different library-preparation protocols or batches, and the goal is cell-type clustering with batch effect removed in a single joint analysis (measured by ARI and cell-type classification accuracy). Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC only gradually removes batch effects when technical differences are smaller than biological ones. You have only a single batch/protocol and no batch effect to remove — a simpler clustering approach suffices and the iterative self-training offers no advantage. You require explicitly batch-aware modeling that incorporates batch information as input (e.g., scVI or BERMUDA) — DESC does not explicitly require or consume batch labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Jointly clusters and removes batch effects in multi-protocol scRNA-seq data (e.g., Fluidigm C1, SMART-seq2, CEL-seq, CEL-seq2) using DESC, an unsupervised deep embedding algorithm whose iterative self-learning gradually removes batch effects without requiring explicit batch labels, as long as technical differences are smaller than true biological variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Jointly clusters and removes batch effects in multi-protocol scRNA-seq data (e.g., Fluidigm C1, SMART-seq2, CEL-seq, CEL-seq2) using DESC, an unsupervised deep embedding algorithm whose iterative self-learning gradually removes batch effects without requiring explicit batch labels, as long as technical differences are smaller than true biological variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC only gradually removes batch effects when technical differences are smaller than biological ones. You have only a single batch/protocol and no batch effect to remove — a simpler clustering approach suffices and the iterative self-training offers no advantage. You require explicitly batch-aware modeling that incorporates batch information as input (e.g., scVI or BERMUDA) — DESC does not explicitly require or consume batch labels.

skills.description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq and ST count matrices measured on the same shared gene space from different experiments or patients, and a domain-invariant latent feature is needed before spatial projection or joint clustering.
skills.name: batch-effect-removal-cross-assay
skills.search_text: batch-effect-removal-cross-assay Use when integrating scRNA-seq and ST count matrices measured on the same shared gene space from different experiments or patients, and a domain-invariant latent feature is needed before spatial projection or joint clustering. When the scRNA-seq and ST data do not share a common gene space or are from tissues with low spatial coherence, where scSpace should be applied cautiously (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC evaluated in the paper) When the goal is spatial domain identification of ST data itself rather than cross-assay integration — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC When data come from the same assay with no cross-experiment batch effect to remove http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Removes batch effect between scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data and extracts a shared latent feature space using transfer component analysis (TCA) as implemented in the scSpace workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Removes batch effect between scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data and extracts a shared latent feature space using transfer component analysis (TCA) as implemented in the scSpace workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the scRNA-seq and ST data do not share a common gene space or are from tissues with low spatial coherence, where scSpace should be applied cautiously (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC evaluated in the paper) When the goal is spatial domain identification of ST data itself rather than cross-assay integration — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC When data come from the same assay with no cross-experiment batch effect to remove

skills.search_text: batch-effect-removal-cross-dataset-integration Use when combining two scRNA-Seq datasets generated in different labs/protocols (e.g., Hockley GSE102962 target with Usoskin GSE59739 source) prior to clustering, and you want to test whether batch correction improves cluster recovery. skills.summary: Optional pre-processing step from Mieth et al. skills.when_to_use_negative: When source and target share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only genes present in both datasets can be used When you only have a single dataset with no second dataset to integrate — batch-effect removal for cross-dataset combination is not applicable and plain SC3 clustering suffices When the comparison question is about imputation of zero-inflated values rather than cross-lab technical effects — MAGIC imputation, not Seurat batch removal, is the corresponding condition

skills.search_text: batch-effect-removal-evaluation Use when assessing whether a scRNA-seq clustering method removes batch effects: you have count matrices with multiple batch metadata fields (e.g., donor, region, sample IDs) and reference cell-type labels to score with ARI. The method under test explicitly requires batch information to correct batch effects (e.g., scVI, whose ARI dropped to 0.242 here when batch information was not utilized) No reference cell-type labels are available, so clustering accuracy cannot be scored with ARI http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates whether a clustering pipeline (e.g., DESC) removes batch effects without explicit batch labels by comparing clustering accuracy (ARI against reference cell-type labels) across multiple batch definitions, including the no-batch-information case. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a clustering pipeline (e.g., DESC) removes batch effects without explicit batch labels by comparing clustering accuracy (ARI against reference cell-type labels) across multiple batch definitions, including the no-batch-information case.

skills.name: batch-effect-removal-metric-computation
skills.search_text: batch-effect-removal-metric-computation Use when comparing multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq integration methods on held-out <condition,batch> matrices and you need ARI/ASW-batch values on shared vs condition-specific latent factors to judge batch-removal quality. Each batch is measured under only one condition: the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effect, so metric comparison of shared vs unshared factors is unreliable The goal is key-gene detection or perturbation prediction (predict_counts/extract_gene_scores), not batch-removal quality assessment Input is a single-batch dataset with no batch labels — ASW-batch cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes disentanglement quality metrics (ARI against ground-truth cell types, ASW-batch silhouette on batch labels) on scDisInFact's shared- and unshared-bio factors and on scINSIGHT's common factor, to quantify how well each method separates cell types while removing batch effect (Fig. 2d of the scDisInFact paper). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Computes disentanglement quality metrics (ARI against ground-truth cell types, ASW-batch silhouette on batch labels) on scDisInFact's shared- and unshared-bio factors and on scINSIGHT's common factor, to quantify how well each method separates cell types while removing batch effect (Fig. 2d of the scDisInFact paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition: the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effect, so metric comparison of shared vs unshared factors is unreliable The goal is key-gene detection or perturbation prediction (predict_counts/extract_gene_scores), not batch-removal quality assessment Input is a single-batch dataset with no batch labels — ASW-batch cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Smart-seq2) must be annotated against a clustered reference (e.g. Drop-seq) across technologies with batch effect and strongly imbalanced cell numbers or library sizes per cell.
skills.name: batch-effect-robust-cell-annotation
skills.search_text: batch-effect-robust-cell-annotation Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Smart-seq2) must be annotated against a clustered reference (e.g. Drop-seq) across technologies with batch effect and strongly imbalanced cell numbers or library sizes per cell. When neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types in that case When the target data is highly shallow and imputation of gene expression is required — this is deferred to future work and not implemented or evaluated When log-transformed data is the only available input — scID requires non-log-transformed, library-depth normalized expression http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to reference clusters using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, which exploits cluster-specific gene signatures and is robust to batch effect and imbalance in cell number and library size, as demonstrated on the Drop-seq retinal bipolar reference (~26,800 cells, 15 clusters) mapping to a 288-cell Smart-seq2 target. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to reference clusters using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, which exploits cluster-specific gene signatures and is robust to batch effect and imbalance in cell number and library size, as demonstrated on the Drop-seq retinal bipolar reference (~26,800 cells, 15 clusters) mapping to a 288-cell Smart-seq2 target.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types in that case When the target data is highly shallow and imputation of gene expression is required — this is deferred to future work and not implemented or evaluated When log-transformed data is the only available input — scID requires non-log-transformed, library-depth normalized expression

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods or metrics and you need controlled ground truth where batch effect strength and cell type DE are known by construction (e.g., testing whether iLISI rewards overcorrection).
skills.name: batch-effect-scaling-scenario-design
skills.search_text: batch-effect-scaling-scenario-design Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods or metrics and you need controlled ground truth where batch effect strength and cell type DE are known by construction (e.g., testing whether iLISI rewards overcorrection). Datasets with highly unequal numbers of cells per batch, since LISI and CiLISI remain suboptimal with lopsided cell proportions Cell types present in only one dataset, where CiLISI cannot be calculated Integration of purely technical replicates where no biological variance must be preserved and cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics suffice A simulation-based test design that generates synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with titrated batch effect strengths and biological variance using Splatter, to evaluate how integration metrics (iLISI, CiLISI, ASW) respond to overcorrected vs. variance-preserving integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: A simulation-based test design that generates synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with titrated batch effect strengths and biological variance using Splatter, to evaluate how integration metrics (iLISI, CiLISI, ASW) respond to overcorrected vs. variance-preserving integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with highly unequal numbers of cells per batch, since LISI and CiLISI remain suboptimal with lopsided cell proportions Cell types present in only one dataset, where CiLISI cannot be calculated Integration of purely technical replicates where no biological variance must be preserved and cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics suffice

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is correction of real experimental scRNA-seq data (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 vs. Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 pancreatic datasets) rather than controlled benchmarking of method behavior per distortion mechanism The integration task involves more than two batches/datasets — BATMAN's current implementation supports only two datasets The downstream method requires raw UMI distributions incompatible with the gamma-Poisson Splatter model assumptions

skills.summary: Simulate paired mRNA/ADT CITE-seq datasets with SymSim under controlled clustering-signal, dropout-rate, and batch-effect regimes to benchmark scMDC against competing multimodal clustering methods using ground-truth labels and AMI/NMI/ARI metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real CITE-seq data without ground-truth cell-type labels — AMI/NMI/ARI cannot be computed against simulated labels, so the supervised simulation benchmark design does not apply Single-modality (RNA-only) clustering benchmarks — the simulation pipeline is built around paired mRNA/ADT CITE-seq data with two jointly learned modalities Evaluating method properties other than clustering accuracy (e.g., joint embedding quality or cross-modal generation), which this label-based clustering benchmark does not measure

Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without ground truth — simulation is only for validation where true CKGs and condition effects are known Data lack multiple batches or multiple condition types, so no batch-condition structure can be simulated or disentangled Each batch is measured under only one condition, since there is insufficient information to disentangle batch and condition effects http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate ground-truth multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq datasets with SymSim by simulating a 2-batch × 2-condition-type factorial design (8 count matrices per dataset) and injecting uniform condition effects on condition-associated key genes (CKGs) at controlled perturbation strengths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w

skills.description: Use when a benchmark of batch-correction or multi-source integration methods needs simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known cell-type and batch effect magnitudes instead of real data lacking ground truth.
skills.name: batch-effect-simulation-parameter-design
skills.search_text: batch-effect-simulation-parameter-design Use when a benchmark of batch-correction or multi-source integration methods needs simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known cell-type and batch effect magnitudes instead of real data lacking ground truth. The analysis requires real biological datasets (e.g. TCGA/BRCA multi-omics) rather than synthetic data with known ground truth The benchmark needs more than two batches or a different number of cell types than three, since the grid here fixes 2 batches and 3 cell types Only a single simulation condition is needed — the value of this skill is the crossed 100-condition grid, not one-off simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Designs a controlled grid of synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with the Splatter R package, crossing cell-type effect and batch effect location parameters with balanced/unbalanced cell-type proportions so batch-correction methods can be evaluated under known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Designs a controlled grid of synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with the Splatter R package, crossing cell-type effect and batch effect location parameters with balanced/unbalanced cell-type proportions so batch-correction methods can be evaluated under known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires real biological datasets (e.g. TCGA/BRCA multi-omics) rather than synthetic data with known ground truth The benchmark needs more than two batches or a different number of cell types than three, since the grid here fixes 2 batches and 3 cell types Only a single simulation condition is needed — the value of this skill is the crossed 100-condition grid, not one-off simulation

skills.description: Use when integrating raw scRNA-seq read count matrices across multiple batches or platforms (e.g., GEO datasets like GSE85241 or GSE86473) where cell-type labels are unknown and batch effects and dropout events must be corrected before clustering.
skills.name: batch-effects-correction-single-cell-rna-seq
skills.search_text: batch-effects-correction-single-cell-rna-seq Use when integrating raw scRNA-seq read count matrices across multiple batches or platforms (e.g., GEO datasets like GSE85241 or GSE86473) where cell-type labels are unknown and batch effects and dropout events must be corrected before clustering. The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no method, including BUSseq, is applicable. Cell-type/subtype labels are already known a priori and the data are bulk rather than single-cell — classic methods like ComBat or SVA designed for bulk experiments suffice. All subtypes are guaranteed present in every batch and the goal is only subtype identification — MetaSparseKmeans-style joint clustering may be considered instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply BUSseq, an interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model, to simultaneously correct batch effects, cluster unknown cell types, impute dropout-caused missing data, and detect differentially expressed genes in scRNA-seq count matrices, and benchmark the corrected clustering against competing methods using adjusted Rand index and silhouette coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Apply BUSseq, an interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model, to simultaneously correct batch effects, cluster unknown cell types, impute dropout-caused missing data, and detect differentially expressed genes in scRNA-seq count matrices, and benchmark the corrected clustering against competing methods using adjusted Rand index and silhouette coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no method, including BUSseq, is applicable. Cell-type/subtype labels are already known a priori and the data are bulk rather than single-cell — classic methods like ComBat or SVA designed for bulk experiments suffice. All subtypes are guaranteed present in every batch and the goal is only subtype identification — MetaSparseKmeans-style joint clustering may be considered instead.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multiple scRNA-seq integration/annotation pipelines on batch-involved datasets and you need quantitative batch-mixing and cell-type-structure metrics plus significance testing between pipelines.
skills.name: batch-entropy-mixing-metric-computation
skills.search_text: batch-entropy-mixing-metric-computation Use when benchmarking multiple scRNA-seq integration/annotation pipelines on batch-involved datasets and you need quantitative batch-mixing and cell-type-structure metrics plus significance testing between pipelines. The dataset has no batch structure (single-batch experiment) — batch entropy mixing is not informative The query data contains unseen cell types absent from the reference — MASI alone cannot annotate these; combine with SCCAF instead Only raw counts are available without log-normalization (scale factor 10,000 + log transform) and integrated embeddings — the metrics need annotations and embeddings to be meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the batch entropy mixing score and cell-type silhouette score for each of 16 data-processing pipelines across 6 batch-involved scRNA-seq datasets, then runs paired t-tests (p < 0.05) to test whether pipeline #14 significantly outperforms basic pipelines #1–#7 on integration quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Computes the batch entropy mixing score and cell-type silhouette score for each of 16 data-processing pipelines across 6 batch-involved scRNA-seq datasets, then runs paired t-tests (p < 0.05) to test whether pipeline #14 significantly outperforms basic pipelines #1–#7 on integration quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no batch structure (single-batch experiment) — batch entropy mixing is not informative The query data contains unseen cell types absent from the reference — MASI alone cannot annotate these; combine with SCCAF instead Only raw counts are available without log-normalization (scale factor 10,000 + log transform) and integrated embeddings — the metrics need annotations and embeddings to be meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have latent embeddings from one or more single-cell batch-integration methods plus per-cell batch and cell type labels, and need quantitative ASW scores to rank integration quality.
skills.name: batch-integration-metric-computation
skills.search_text: batch-integration-metric-computation Use when you have latent embeddings from one or more single-cell batch-integration methods plus per-cell batch and cell type labels, and need quantitative ASW scores to rank integration quality. The embeddings have not yet been generated — silhouette scores quantify an existing latent space and cannot be computed from raw counts alone You need scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq peak calling rather than integration benchmarking (e.g. MACS3 is a ChIP-seq peak caller, not a batch-correction scorer) Only a single batch with no batch covariate exists — batch ASW against the joint batch-and-cell-type label is undefined in a meaningful way http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes average silhouette width (ASW) metrics for cell type conservation and batch mixing to benchmark latent-space embeddings from batch-correction methods such as CODAL against baselines like scVI, scANVI, Harmony, and Scanorama on multi-batch single-cell atlases. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Computes average silhouette width (ASW) metrics for cell type conservation and batch mixing to benchmark latent-space embeddings from batch-correction methods such as CODAL against baselines like scVI, scANVI, Harmony, and Scanorama on multi-batch single-cell atlases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The embeddings have not yet been generated — silhouette scores quantify an existing latent space and cannot be computed from raw counts alone You need scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq peak calling rather than integration benchmarking (e.g. MACS3 is a ChIP-seq peak caller, not a batch-correction scorer) Only a single batch with no batch covariate exists — batch ASW against the joint batch-and-cell-type label is undefined in a meaningful way

Single-batch datasets where batch correction metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI) are undefined or uninformative Evaluation questions about trajectory or latent-time accuracy rather than batch integration and velocity consistency across batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify batch correction quality of RNA velocity methods on the two-batch dyngen bifurcation synthetic dataset using scib cell-state integration metrics (kBET, iLISI, cLISI) alongside velocity metrics (CBDir, ICCoh, nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity), to test whether LatentVelo's dynamics-based embedding outperforms gene-space corrected UniTVelo baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581

skills.description: Use when you have one or more scRNA-seq perturbation datasets (e.g. drug-treatment vs control) with ground-truth labels and need to compare ICAT against conventional integration workflows quantitatively by ARI, LISI, and DB.
skills.name: batch-integration-workflow-comparison
skills.search_text: batch-integration-workflow-comparison Use when you have one or more scRNA-seq perturbation datasets (e.g. drug-treatment vs control) with ground-truth labels and need to compare ICAT against conventional integration workflows quantitatively by ARI, LISI, and DB. The goal is only to run ICAT on a new dataset without comparing it to integration baselines — use the standalone ICAT clustering workflow instead. The data contain no perturbation or treatment contrast (single homogeneous condition), so integration-vs-ICAT comparison on treatment mixing is not meaningful. No ground-truth labels exist, making ARI (the primary cluster-quality metric in this benchmark) uncomputable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised clustering against standard integration-plus-Louvain workflows (Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony) on perturbed scRNA-seq datasets using ARI, LISI, and Davies-Bouldin metrics to test whether ICAT resolves perturbation-unique cell states better than batch-correction approaches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Benchmark ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised clustering against standard integration-plus-Louvain workflows (Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony) on perturbed scRNA-seq datasets using ARI, LISI, and Davies-Bouldin metrics to test whether ICAT resolves perturbation-unique cell states better than batch-correction approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only to run ICAT on a new dataset without comparing it to integration baselines — use the standalone ICAT clustering workflow instead. The data contain no perturbation or treatment contrast (single homogeneous condition), so integration-vs-ICAT comparison on treatment mixing is not meaningful. No ground-truth labels exist, making ARI (the primary cluster-quality metric in this benchmark) uncomputable.

skills.description: Use when you have aligned joint embeddings from multiple single-cell modalities (e.g., Full PBMC, Partial PBMC, BM datasets aligned by scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, or SCOTv2) and need to quantify modality mixing for benchmarking.
skills.name: batch-lisi-computation
skills.search_text: batch-lisi-computation Use when you have aligned joint embeddings from multiple single-cell modalities (e.g., Full PBMC, Partial PBMC, BM datasets aligned by scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, or SCOTv2) and need to quantify modality mixing for benchmarking. When cells from the modalities share overlapping features or cells and a supervised/feature-linked integration method is more appropriate — batch LISI is for evaluating unsupervised manifold alignment of non-overlapping modalities When the goal is to evaluate topology preservation of individual-modality low-dimensional representations (e.g., comparing topoAE against Autoencoder, VAE, or UMAP) rather than cross-modality mixing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes the batch Local Inverse Simpson Index (batch LISI) on aligned joint single-cell embeddings to quantify how well modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) mix after manifold alignment; the optimal value is 2, indicating complete modality mixing. It is the key integration metric used to benchmark scTopoGAN against UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Computes the batch Local Inverse Simpson Index (batch LISI) on aligned joint single-cell embeddings to quantify how well modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) mix after manifold alignment; the optimal value is 2, indicating complete modality mixing. It is the key integration metric used to benchmark scTopoGAN against UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cells from the modalities share overlapping features or cells and a supervised/feature-linked integration method is more appropriate — batch LISI is for evaluating unsupervised manifold alignment of non-overlapping modalities When the goal is to evaluate topology preservation of individual-modality low-dimensional representations (e.g., comparing topoAE against Autoencoder, VAE, or UMAP) rather than cross-modality mixing

skills.description: Use when you have embeddings from ≥2 batch integration methods (e.g. JOINTLY, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, LIGER, fastMNN, Seurat, scGPT) run on the same multi-batch sxRNA-seq datasets with cell type labels and need a comparable rank table.
skills.name: batch-mixing-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: batch-mixing-metric-evaluation Use when you have embeddings from ≥2 batch integration methods (e.g. JOINTLY, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, LIGER, fastMNN, Seurat, scGPT) run on the same multi-batch sxRNA-seq datasets with cell type labels and need a comparable rank table. You need to know which genes or features drive integration/clustering — the paper notes such metrics 'do not provide insight into the genes or features driving integration and clustering'; use JOINTLY's interpretable modules/UCell scores instead You are evaluating a single method on a single dataset in isolation — the paper stresses performance varies task-to-task, so single-task ARI is not a defensible ranking on its own The method's output is smoothed/imputed expression (e.g. JOINTLY's H/F-matrix recon_expression values) rather than a clustering-ready embedding; the paper advises using such values only for visualization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark protocol from the JOINTLY paper for scoring batch-integration methods: cluster on each method's embedding and compute ARI/NMI between cell type labels and clusters, plus batch-mixing and cell-type-conservation metrics (iLISI, cLISI, bASW, cASW), then aggregate into per-task ranks across five integration tasks (Lung, Pancreas, Kidney, Liver, PBMC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol from the JOINTLY paper for scoring batch-integration methods: cluster on each method's embedding and compute ARI/NMI between cell type labels and clusters, plus batch-mixing and cell-type-conservation metrics (iLISI, cLISI, bASW, cASW), then aggregate into per-task ranks across five integration tasks (Lung, Pancreas, Kidney, Liver, PBMC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to know which genes or features drive integration/clustering — the paper notes such metrics 'do not provide insight into the genes or features driving integration and clustering'; use JOINTLY's interpretable modules/UCell scores instead You are evaluating a single method on a single dataset in isolation — the paper stresses performance varies task-to-task, so single-task ARI is not a defensible ranking on its own The method's output is smoothed/imputed expression (e.g. JOINTLY's H/F-matrix recon_expression values) rather than a clustering-ready embedding; the paper advises using such values only for visualization

skills.summary: Quantifies how well a dynamics-based latent embedding (e.g. LatentVelo with batch_correction=True) mixes sequencing batches, using kBET batch-mixing scores and nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity across batches, benchmarked against scVI, scANVI, and unintegrated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is a single sequencing batch with no batch_key — kBET batch-mixing scores and cross-batch velocity cosine similarity are undefined Method does not produce a latent embedding or velocity field (e.g. plain clustering pipelines) — there is no batch-corrected latent space to score Sparse cell clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, where the article warns LatentVelo may encounter issues
