skills.description: Use when you need to quantify query scalability of an indexed sequence-collection structure (e.g. PAC) by timing batches of many sequences — from tens to hundreds of thousands — against a fixed index and compiling runtime and memory measurements.
skills.name: batch-query-throughput-benchmarking
skills.search_text: batch-query-throughput-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify query scalability of an indexed sequence-collection structure (e.g. PAC) by timing batches of many sequences — from tens to hundreds of thousands — against a fixed index and compiling runtime and memory measurements. The index does not yet exist — this skill benchmarks querying only; index construction must be done first with './PAC -f fof.txt -d index_test' The goal is exact alignment or similarity scoring (e.g. BLAST-like local alignment) — PAC is an approximate membership query structure that only lists datasets that may contain a query sequence The collection exceeds ~65,536 files without adjusting encoding — by default PAC uses 16-bit integers and indexes up to 65,536 files; use -e 32 for larger collections http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmarks the query throughput of PAC (Partitioned Aggregated bloom Comb trees) by running batches of increasing numbers of human RefSeq transcript queries against a pre-built PAC index, recording wall-clock time, CPU time, and peak RAM per batch size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Benchmarks the query throughput of PAC (Partitioned Aggregated bloom Comb trees) by running batches of increasing numbers of human RefSeq transcript queries against a pre-built PAC index, recording wall-clock time, CPU time, and peak RAM per batch size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The index does not yet exist — this skill benchmarks querying only; index construction must be done first with './PAC -f fof.txt -d index_test' The goal is exact alignment or similarity scoring (e.g. BLAST-like local alignment) — PAC is an approximate membership query structure that only lists datasets that may contain a query sequence The collection exceeds ~65,536 files without adjusting encoding — by default PAC uses 16-bit integers and indexes up to 65,536 files; use -e 32 for larger collections

skills.description: Use when building k-NN graphs over thousands of single cells (or other large point sets) where full pairwise distance computation would exhaust memory, and downstream label propagation must run on the graph.
skills.name: batched-graph-computation
skills.search_text: batched-graph-computation Use when building k-NN graphs over thousands of single cells (or other large point sets) where full pairwise distance computation would exhaust memory, and downstream label propagation must run on the graph. The dataset is small enough that a dense pairwise distance matrix fits comfortably in memory — batching adds complexity without benefit. The goal is the GCN-based consensus model itself rather than the nonparametric neighbor majority baseline on a pre-built k-NN graph. The input is already a graph (e.g., a precomputed adjacency file); only the label propagation, not graph construction, is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Bounded-memory construction and processing of large cell-cell graphs by chunking operations into batches (e.g., 1000 cells at a time) using pytorch-cluster on PCA-reduced scRNA-seq embeddings, as used in scSHARP's nonparametric neighbor majority experiments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Bounded-memory construction and processing of large cell-cell graphs by chunking operations into batches (e.g., 1000 cells at a time) using pytorch-cluster on PCA-reduced scRNA-seq embeddings, as used in scSHARP's nonparametric neighbor majority experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that a dense pairwise distance matrix fits comfortably in memory — batching adds complexity without benefit. The goal is the GCN-based consensus model itself rather than the nonparametric neighbor majority baseline on a pre-built k-NN graph. The input is already a graph (e.g., a precomputed adjacency file); only the label propagation, not graph construction, is needed.

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed scRNA-seq expression (counts rescaled into (0,1)) with a small refined candidate TF set and need a ranked, directed TF-gene edge list or top logic gates per target gene.
skills.name: bayes-factor-based-edge-ranking
skills.search_text: bayes-factor-based-edge-ranking Use when you have preprocessed scRNA-seq expression (counts rescaled into (0,1)) with a small refined candidate TF set and need a ranked, directed TF-gene edge list or top logic gates per target gene. When the target set is large-scale from scratch — scGATE is only applicable to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate TFs from external hints When the regulatory logic involves more than ~5 transcriptional regulators per target, where overfitting is a major concern On pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or with temporal delays, which scGATE does not yet handle http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Ranks inferred TF–target regulatory edges (and Boolean logic gates) by their Bayes Factor (BF), as implemented in scGATE's scGATE_logic()/scGATE_edge() functions, to prioritize the most probable regulatory rules from single-cell expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Ranks inferred TF–target regulatory edges (and Boolean logic gates) by their Bayes Factor (BF), as implemented in scGATE's scGATE_logic()/scGATE_edge() functions, to prioritize the most probable regulatory rules from single-cell expression data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target set is large-scale from scratch — scGATE is only applicable to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate TFs from external hints When the regulatory logic involves more than ~5 transcriptional regulators per target, where overfitting is a major concern On pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or with temporal delays, which scGATE does not yet handle

skills.description: Use when scGATE has fit a zero-inflated mixture likelihood to a target gene's expression and you need a confidence score to select or rank the most probable Boolean logic gate among candidate regulatory TFs.
skills.name: bayes-factor-confidence-scoring
skills.search_text: bayes-factor-confidence-scoring Use when scGATE has fit a zero-inflated mixture likelihood to a target gene's expression and you need a confidence score to select or rank the most probable Boolean logic gate among candidate regulatory TFs. Candidate TF lists per target exceed k=5 regulators (>5 factors) — overfitting makes Bayes-factor ranking unreliable, per the article's discussion You only need a directed TF-target edge network without logic gates — use scGATE_edge() instead of scoring gates The dataset is a large-scale unfiltered GRN inference from scratch — scGATE (and hence BF scoring) is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Ranks inferred Boolean logic gates (TF combinations regulating a target gene) by a Bayes factor BF = L1/L0, where L1 is the mixture-model likelihood under EM-updated priors and L0 is the likelihood under uniform priors w_v = 1/2^k; reported as log10 BF per target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Ranks inferred Boolean logic gates (TF combinations regulating a target gene) by a Bayes factor BF = L1/L0, where L1 is the mixture-model likelihood under EM-updated priors and L0 is the likelihood under uniform priors w_v = 1/2^k; reported as log10 BF per target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate TF lists per target exceed k=5 regulators (>5 factors) — overfitting makes Bayes-factor ranking unreliable, per the article's discussion You only need a directed TF-target edge network without logic gates — use scGATE_edge() instead of scoring gates The dataset is a large-scale unfiltered GRN inference from scratch — scGATE (and hence BF scoring) is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list

skills.description: Use when comparing per-cell gene module variational (GMV) activities inferred by VEGA between two cell groups (or one-vs-rest across annotated cell types) to call significantly activated pathways, TF regulons, or cell type marker sets.
skills.name: bayes-factor-differential-module-testing
skills.search_text: bayes-factor-differential-module-testing Use when comparing per-cell gene module variational (GMV) activities inferred by VEGA between two cell groups (or one-vs-rest across annotated cell types) to call significantly activated pathways, TF regulons, or cell type marker sets. The latent space is not constrained to a priori gene modules (e.g., a standard scVI or scGen model), since GMV posteriors would not map to annotated biological pathways You need to correct or extend the prior gene module annotations at test time — the paper notes hard-coded decoder connections 'do not leave any room for correcting prior knowledge about gene modules when the context requires it' The dataset contains many unannotated genes playing important roles, since prior knowledge from databases like MSigDB can be incomplete or not context-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 VEGA's Bayesian testing procedure that identifies gene modules (GMVs) significantly differentially active between two cell groups by Monte Carlo approximating posterior probabilities of mutually exclusive hypotheses and computing a log Bayes Factor, calling modules significant at |log_e(BF)| > 3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: VEGA's Bayesian testing procedure that identifies gene modules (GMVs) significantly differentially active between two cell groups by Monte Carlo approximating posterior probabilities of mutually exclusive hypotheses and computing a log Bayes Factor, calling modules significant at |log_e(BF)| > 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The latent space is not constrained to a priori gene modules (e.g., a standard scVI or scGen model), since GMV posteriors would not map to annotated biological pathways You need to correct or extend the prior gene module annotations at test time — the paper notes hard-coded decoder connections 'do not leave any room for correcting prior knowledge about gene modules when the context requires it' The dataset contains many unannotated genes playing important roles, since prior knowledge from databases like MSigDB can be incomplete or not context-specific

skills.description: Use when comparing probabilistic phase-inference models (Tempo vs Cyclops, Cyclum, PCA) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, per-cell-type measure of the evidence favoring one model's phase estimates over another's.
skills.name: bayes-factor-model-comparison
skills.search_text: bayes-factor-model-comparison Use when comparing probabilistic phase-inference models (Tempo vs Cyclops, Cyclum, PCA) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, per-cell-type measure of the evidence favoring one model's phase estimates over another's. Input is simulated scRNA-seq data matched to the method's own likelihood model rather than real droplet-based data — the article's motivation is that accuracy must be verified against real 10X Chromium data The methods being compared do not produce per-cell phase point estimates or a probabilistic model of expression over phase, so no Bayes factor can be defined between them The goal is cell-cycle phase ordering rather than circadian phase inference — existing methods were developed for cell cycle analysis and the ~20-gene core clock structure is what distinguishes this setting http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Bayes factor model comparison for circadian phase inference, benchmarking Tempo's Bayesian variational inference against competing unsupervised phase methods (Cyclops, Cyclum, PCA) on droplet-based scRNA-seq data. Bayes factors quantify the evidence that Tempo's phase model explains the data better than alternatives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Bayes factor model comparison for circadian phase inference, benchmarking Tempo's Bayesian variational inference against competing unsupervised phase methods (Cyclops, Cyclum, PCA) on droplet-based scRNA-seq data. Bayes factors quantify the evidence that Tempo's phase model explains the data better than alternatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated scRNA-seq data matched to the method's own likelihood model rather than real droplet-based data — the article's motivation is that accuracy must be verified against real 10X Chromium data The methods being compared do not produce per-cell phase point estimates or a probabilistic model of expression over phase, so no Bayes factor can be defined between them The goal is cell-cycle phase ordering rather than circadian phase inference — existing methods were developed for cell cycle analysis and the ~20-gene core clock structure is what distinguishes this setting

skills.name: bayes-mean-score-computation

Input expression matrix has not been filtered to cycle base genes or is not in log2(TPM+1) scale — reCAT expects get_test_exp-formatted data Cells are synchronized or the goal is bulk RNA-seq/qPCR time-course profiling rather than unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome cycle recovery No consensus-TSP ordIndex has been computed yet — scores are only interpretable along the recovered time-series order http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes the two reCAT cell-cycle stage scoring metrics — Bayes-scores and mean-scores — along the consensus-TSP recovered time-series of unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome data, to discriminate G0/G1/S/G2/M cycle stages before HMM segmentation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression matrix has not been filtered to cycle base genes or is not in log2(TPM+1) scale — reCAT expects get_test_exp-formatted data Cells are synchronized or the goal is bulk RNA-seq/qPCR time-course profiling rather than unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome cycle recovery No consensus-TSP ordIndex has been computed yet — scores are only interpretable along the recovered time-series order

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (e.g. 10x/GemCode 3' gene-barcode matrices from bone marrow mononuclear cells of transplant patients) must be decomposed into host vs donor cell genotypes without a prior known genotype.
skills.name: bayesian-cell-genotype-mixture-assignment
skills.search_text: bayesian-cell-genotype-mixture-assignment Use when scRNA-seq data (e.g. 10x/GemCode 3' gene-barcode matrices from bone marrow mononuclear cells of transplant patients) must be decomposed into host vs donor cell genotypes without a prior known genotype. Samples where a priori donor/host genotypes are already available from conventional genotyping — the method is designed for de novo calls without prior genotype knowledge Detection of very low-level chimerism below ~4% of 6,000 cells, since a K=1 selection only indicates the mixture fraction is below the method's detection level Bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data, as the method requires per-cell barcode-resolved SNV fractions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 A de novo SNV-based Bayesian method that assigns each single cell a host or donor genotype from scRNA-seq transcriptomes, enabling single-cell-resolution chimerism determination in post-transplant bone marrow samples without prior donor/host genotype knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: A de novo SNV-based Bayesian method that assigns each single cell a host or donor genotype from scRNA-seq transcriptomes, enabling single-cell-resolution chimerism determination in post-transplant bone marrow samples without prior donor/host genotype knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples where a priori donor/host genotypes are already available from conventional genotyping — the method is designed for de novo calls without prior genotype knowledge Detection of very low-level chimerism below ~4% of 6,000 cells, since a K=1 selection only indicates the mixture fraction is below the method's detection level Bulk (non-single-cell) sequencing data, as the method requires per-cell barcode-resolved SNV fractions

skills.description: Use when testing whether cis-eQTL signals are shared across tissues (e.g., GTEx v8) and LD inflation from distinct causal variants must be accounted for via Bayesian colocalization.

skills.search_text: bayesian-colocalization-prior-configuration Use when testing whether cis-eQTL signals are shared across tissues (e.g., GTEx v8) and LD inflation from distinct causal variants must be accounted for via Bayesian colocalization. Loci whose disease effects are mediated via coding variants that show no eQTL signal — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences) between cohorts, since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix Situations where the causal variant may be missing from tested datasets, as CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Configure and run Bayesian colocalization methods (COLOC's approximate Bayes approach and CAFEH) on cis-eQTL summary statistics to assess whether causal variants are shared across GTEx tissues, using explicit priors and posterior thresholds rather than LD-blind meta-analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Configure and run Bayesian colocalization methods (COLOC's approximate Bayes approach and CAFEH) on cis-eQTL summary statistics to assess whether causal variants are shared across GTEx tissues, using explicit priors and posterior thresholds rather than LD-blind meta-analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose disease effects are mediated via coding variants that show no eQTL signal — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences) between cohorts, since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix Situations where the causal variant may be missing from tested datasets, as CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix

skills.description: Use when smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from time-course scRNA-seq are available and the goal is a time-resolved gene-gene network plus identification of critical (differentially expressed) genes during differentiation.
skills.name: bayesian-confidence-interval-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-confidence-interval-inference Use when smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from time-course scRNA-seq are available and the goal is a time-resolved gene-gene network plus identification of critical (differentially expressed) genes during differentiation. Input is raw time-course scRNA-seq without prior cell-to-cell lineage alignment (cell_name_traj) and smoothing (smooth_cell_expression) — the functional concurrent model operates on smoothed individual trajectories, not bulk trajectories. The goal is a single bulk population trajectory rather than dynamic pairwise gene-gene relationships at the individual cell level; CellST is designed for the individual-cell case. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs dynamic gene-gene networks from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting functional concurrent linear models and keeping edges whose time-varying coefficient beta(l,s)(t) has a Bayesian confidence interval excluding zero, as implemented in CellST. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: Constructs dynamic gene-gene networks from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting functional concurrent linear models and keeping edges whose time-varying coefficient beta(l,s)(t) has a Bayesian confidence interval excluding zero, as implemented in CellST.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw time-course scRNA-seq without prior cell-to-cell lineage alignment (cell_name_traj) and smoothing (smooth_cell_expression) — the functional concurrent model operates on smoothed individual trajectories, not bulk trajectories. The goal is a single bulk population trajectory rather than dynamic pairwise gene-gene relationships at the individual cell level; CellST is designed for the individual-cell case.

skills.description: Use when after Tempo Step 1 phase inference, you must expand the core-clock cycler set de novo — i.e., classify which currently non-cycling genes from a scRNA-seq anndata matrix are described by 24 h phase variation before refitting the model.
skills.name: bayesian-cycler-gene-threshold-selection
skills.search_text: bayesian-cycler-gene-threshold-selection Use when after Tempo Step 1 phase inference, you must expand the core-clock cycler set de novo — i.e., classify which currently non-cycling genes from a scRNA-seq anndata matrix are described by 24 h phase variation before refitting the model. Genes are already designated cyclers — this module only assesses genes not currently identified as cyclers No Step 1 phase posterior is available yet — the amplitude fit is conditioned on Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, so phase inference must precede this filter The goal is flexible non-sinusoidal waveform detection — the article notes the de novo cycler issue may stem from assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tempo Step 2 module that identifies de novo circadian cycling genes from genes not currently designated as cyclers, by fitting approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions conditioned on the Step 1 cell phase posterior and filtering genes on two statistics: the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and the non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction (Fig. 2c criterion). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Tempo Step 2 module that identifies de novo circadian cycling genes from genes not currently designated as cyclers, by fitting approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions conditioned on the Step 1 cell phase posterior and filtering genes on two statistics: the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and the non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction (Fig. 2c criterion).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes are already designated cyclers — this module only assesses genes not currently identified as cyclers No Step 1 phase posterior is available yet — the amplitude fit is conditioned on Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, so phase inference must precede this filter The goal is flexible non-sinusoidal waveform detection — the article notes the de novo cycler issue may stem from assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means

skills.description: Use when per-sample cell-type counts from scRNA-seq (or similar compositional count data) must be tested for differential abundance across conditions, especially with few replicates.
skills.name: bayesian-dirichlet-multinomial-modeling
skills.search_text: bayesian-dirichlet-multinomial-modeling Use when per-sample cell-type counts from scRNA-seq (or similar compositional count data) must be tested for differential abundance across conditions, especially with few replicates. The goal is to detect heterogeneities between donors/samples in response to treatment — scCODA 'does not model the response variability within a condition' Cell-type clustering is unreliable — scCODA requires pre-specified cell-type definitions which hinge on statistically sound and biologically meaningful clustering assignments The relationship between covariates and abundance is expected to be strongly non-log-linear — scCODA assumes a log-linear relationship which may be mis-specified http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Build and fit scCODA's hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior on cell-type effects, inferred via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, to detect credible compositional changes in single-cell data relative to a fixed reference cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Build and fit scCODA's hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior on cell-type effects, inferred via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, to detect credible compositional changes in single-cell data relative to a fixed reference cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect heterogeneities between donors/samples in response to treatment — scCODA 'does not model the response variability within a condition' Cell-type clustering is unreliable — scCODA requires pre-specified cell-type definitions which hinge on statistically sound and biologically meaningful clustering assignments The relationship between covariates and abundance is expected to be strongly non-log-linear — scCODA assumes a log-linear relationship which may be mis-specified

skills.name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-fitting-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: bayesian-hierarchical-model-fitting-scrnaseq Use when you have per-gene summary statistics (beta and beta variance, or p-values convertible via qnorm) from a scRNA-seq DE tool such as zingeR-DESeq2 and want joint DE + gene set enrichment analysis with permutation-based empirical FDR. When only individual-level scRNA-seq counts are available with no DE summary statistics and no DE tool can be run first — iDEA consumes summary statistics, not raw counts When gene set overlap non-independence must be explicitly modeled rather than handled by gene-label permutation — iDEA does not explicitly account for gene set overlap When DE was performed on inferred cell types that may have inflated test statistics with artificially small standard errors http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Fits the iDEA hierarchical Bayesian model that jointly performs differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis from DE summary statistics (beta coefficients and standard errors) in scRNA-seq studies, improving GSE power and DE consistency over fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA, and Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Fits the iDEA hierarchical Bayesian model that jointly performs differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis from DE summary statistics (beta coefficients and standard errors) in scRNA-seq studies, improving GSE power and DE consistency over fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA, and Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only individual-level scRNA-seq counts are available with no DE summary statistics and no DE tool can be run first — iDEA consumes summary statistics, not raw counts When gene set overlap non-independence must be explicitly modeled rather than handled by gene-label permutation — iDEA does not explicitly account for gene set overlap When DE was performed on inferred cell types that may have inflated test statistics with artificially small standard errors

skills.description: Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq read count matrices contain unknown cell subtypes with batch effects and dropouts, and you need simultaneous batch correction and clustering without prior normalization or subtype labels.
skills.name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-mcmc-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-hierarchical-model-mcmc-inference Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq read count matrices contain unknown cell subtypes with batch effects and dropouts, and you need simultaneous batch correction and clustering without prior normalization or subtype labels. The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1-2 and batch 2 only cell types 3-4) — no method, including BUSseq, is applicable because biological and batch variation cannot be separated Subtype information is already known a priori and only supervised label transfer is needed (bulk-style methods like ComBat/SVA apply, or semi-supervised alternatives such as CellAssign) The input is already normalized or batch-corrected expression data rather than raw read counts, since BUSseq models the count nature, overdispersion, and dropouts of raw scRNA-seq counts directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Fit the BUSseq interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model to multi-batch scRNA-seq read counts via MCMC (BUSseq_MCMC), simultaneously correcting batch effects, clustering unknown cell types, modeling dropouts and overdispersion, and selecting the number of cell types K by comparing BIC values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Fit the BUSseq interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model to multi-batch scRNA-seq read counts via MCMC (BUSseq_MCMC), simultaneously correcting batch effects, clustering unknown cell types, modeling dropouts and overdispersion, and selecting the number of cell types K by comparing BIC values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1-2 and batch 2 only cell types 3-4) — no method, including BUSseq, is applicable because biological and batch variation cannot be separated Subtype information is already known a priori and only supervised label transfer is needed (bulk-style methods like ComBat/SVA apply, or semi-supervised alternatives such as CellAssign) The input is already normalized or batch-corrected expression data rather than raw read counts, since BUSseq models the count nature, overdispersion, and dropouts of raw scRNA-seq counts directly

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted BUSseq model object (e.g., sce_BUSseqfit from BUSseq_MCMC) and need corrected count data free of batch effects and dropout for downstream analysis, cell-type-colored t-SNE, or DE testing.
skills.name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-posterior-use
skills.search_text: bayesian-hierarchical-model-posterior-use Use when you have a fitted BUSseq model object (e.g., sce_BUSseqfit from BUSseq_MCMC) and need corrected count data free of batch effects and dropout for downstream analysis, cell-type-colored t-SNE, or DE testing. The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no batch-correction method is applicable The data are bulk experiments with known subtype information, where classic methods such as ComBat or SVA are the appropriate choice Only imputed (dropout-corrected) values are needed rather than batch-corrected values — use imputed_read_counts(sce_BUSseqfit) instead of corrected_read_counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs BUSseq's quantile-matching module, which uses the fitted Bayesian hierarchical model posterior (cell-type means, batch location effects, cell-specific size factors, overdispersion, and dropout terms) to output batch-effect-corrected read counts usable as if all cells were sequenced in a single batch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Reconstructs BUSseq's quantile-matching module, which uses the fitted Bayesian hierarchical model posterior (cell-type means, batch location effects, cell-specific size factors, overdispersion, and dropout terms) to output batch-effect-corrected read counts usable as if all cells were sequenced in a single batch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no batch-correction method is applicable The data are bulk experiments with known subtype information, where classic methods such as ComBat or SVA are the appropriate choice Only imputed (dropout-corrected) values are needed rather than batch-corrected values — use imputed_read_counts(sce_BUSseqfit) instead of corrected_read_counts

skills.description: Use when base classifiers were built with pre-set, experience-derived hyperparameters and you need to systematically tune them to maximize k-fold cross-validation accuracy before stacking or comparison.
skills.name: bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization
skills.search_text: bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization Use when base classifiers were built with pre-set, experience-derived hyperparameters and you need to systematically tune them to maximize k-fold cross-validation accuracy before stacking or comparison. Input is already an optimized or stacked model (e.g., the logistic-regression meta-model) — the skill targets the individual base classifiers only Goal is prediction on new sequences via the shipped m5C_predict.py script — that uses the fixed trained models, not re-tuning Working on the independent test dataset for final benchmarking — tuning must be driven by 10-fold cross-validation on the training set to avoid test-set leakage Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters for the five Staem5 base classifiers (SVM-RBF, GBDT, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree), selecting settings that maximize 10-fold cross-validation accuracy on the A. thaliana m5C dataset. It replaces experience-based pre-set hyperparameters with a systematic search, yielding the largest gain for SVM (62.40% -> 73.62%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Bayesian optimization of hyperparameters for the five Staem5 base classifiers (SVM-RBF, GBDT, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree), selecting settings that maximize 10-fold cross-validation accuracy on the A. thaliana m5C dataset. It replaces experience-based pre-set hyperparameters with a systematic search, yielding the largest gain for SVM (62.40% -> 73.62%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an optimized or stacked model (e.g., the logistic-regression meta-model) — the skill targets the individual base classifiers only Goal is prediction on new sequences via the shipped m5C_predict.py script — that uses the fixed trained models, not re-tuning Working on the independent test dataset for final benchmarking — tuning must be driven by 10-fold cross-validation on the training set to avoid test-set leakage

skills.description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq UMI read count matrix (e.g. GSE120861 highmoi, Cell Ranger sparse mtx or tsv) and normalized log expression is needed as the basis for Normalisr's downstream association testing.
skills.name: bayesian-log-expression-mmse-estimation
skills.search_text: bayesian-log-expression-mmse-estimation Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq UMI read count matrix (e.g. GSE120861 highmoi, Cell Ranger sparse mtx or tsv) and normalized log expression is needed as the basis for Normalisr's downstream association testing. Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq — Normalisr was validated only on UMI-based datasets, and the nonlinear covariates may need revalidation there You need hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations or causal network reconstruction (v-structures, regularized regression, Granger causality) — Normalisr explicitly does not support these Analysis spans multiple datasets requiring batch-effect correction — integrative studies may need additional consideration for batch effects beyond Normalisr Estimate per-cell, per-gene log relative expression from raw UMI read counts using Normalisr's Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) digamma-based Bayesian posterior estimator — the 'Bayesian log expression' — which recovers pre-measurement mRNA frequencies before nonlinear covariate regression and variance normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Estimate per-cell, per-gene log relative expression from raw UMI read counts using Normalisr's Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) digamma-based Bayesian posterior estimator — the 'Bayesian log expression' — which recovers pre-measurement mRNA frequencies before nonlinear covariate regression and variance normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq — Normalisr was validated only on UMI-based datasets, and the nonlinear covariates may need revalidation there You need hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations or causal network reconstruction (v-structures, regularized regression, Granger causality) — Normalisr explicitly does not support these Analysis spans multiple datasets requiring batch-effect correction — integrative studies may need additional consideration for batch effects beyond Normalisr

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has high dropout (the article notes 40%-90% missing values) and downstream goals are cell clustering, pseudotime/trajectory inference, or visualization that depends on recovering cell-to-cell relationships.
skills.name: bayesian-matrix-factorization-imputation
skills.search_text: bayesian-matrix-factorization-imputation Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has high dropout (the article notes 40%-90% missing values) and downstream goals are cell clustering, pseudotime/trajectory inference, or visualization that depends on recovering cell-to-cell relationships. The count matrix is already normalized/log-transformed without setting normalized=TRUE — Bfimpute would apply CPM and log10(bias 1.01) a second time The goal is a general-purpose best imputer for any dataset: the article's discussion states 'There is no consensus about which imputation method is the best' and it is 'premature to conclude that Bfimpute will achieve better performance across all datasets' False positives in downstream differential expression are unacceptable without tuning — the article notes users 'may constraint parameters to maximize true positives or minimize false positives' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Applies Bfimpute, a full Bayesian probabilistic matrix factorization with Gibbs-sampling MCMC, to impute dropout events in scRNA-seq count matrices by factorizing them into latent gene-specific and cell-specific feature matrices, optionally leveraging cell labels, spectral clustering, or gene/cell side information such as bulk RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Applies Bfimpute, a full Bayesian probabilistic matrix factorization with Gibbs-sampling MCMC, to impute dropout events in scRNA-seq count matrices by factorizing them into latent gene-specific and cell-specific feature matrices, optionally leveraging cell labels, spectral clustering, or gene/cell side information such as bulk RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix is already normalized/log-transformed without setting normalized=TRUE — Bfimpute would apply CPM and log10(bias 1.01) a second time The goal is a general-purpose best imputer for any dataset: the article's discussion states 'There is no consensus about which imputation method is the best' and it is 'premature to conclude that Bfimpute will achieve better performance across all datasets' False positives in downstream differential expression are unacceptable without tuning — the article notes users 'may constraint parameters to maximize true positives or minimize false positives'

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from several individuals (e.g. 10x Genomics Chromium libraries) show batch effects or individual-level heterogeneity and single-individual methods like DIMM-SC or naive merging produce unreliable clusters.
skills.name: bayesian-mixture-model-clustering
skills.search_text: bayesian-mixture-model-clustering Use when raw UMI count matrices from several individuals (e.g. 10x Genomics Chromium libraries) show batch effects or individual-level heterogeneity and single-individual methods like DIMM-SC or naive merging produce unreliable clusters. Single-individual analysis where no cross-individual heterogeneity exists — use DIMMSC (call DIMMSC(X, K) or pass a plain matrix to BAMMSC) Rare cell type discovery, since genes with excessive zeros are filtered out and the supervised strategy for large datasets may potentially miss rare clusters Trajectory, cell-cycle, or developmental-stage interpretation — the model assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities measure clustering uncertainty only Data requiring explicit zero-inflation modeling, which BAMM-SC does not provide http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Clustering droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count data from multiple individuals with BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model that jointly models genes, cell types, and individual-level variability (batch effect, unbalanced sequencing depth) in a unified framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Clustering droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count data from multiple individuals with BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model that jointly models genes, cell types, and individual-level variability (batch effect, unbalanced sequencing depth) in a unified framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-individual analysis where no cross-individual heterogeneity exists — use DIMMSC (call DIMMSC(X, K) or pass a plain matrix to BAMMSC) Rare cell type discovery, since genes with excessive zeros are filtered out and the supervised strategy for large datasets may potentially miss rare clusters Trajectory, cell-cycle, or developmental-stage interpretation — the model assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities measure clustering uncertainty only Data requiring explicit zero-inflation modeling, which BAMM-SC does not provide

skills.description: Use when inferring cell-type-specific TF-gene networks and Boolean logic gates from a small, pre-selected set of TFs and target genes in single-cell expression data, given a candidate base GRN.
skills.name: bayesian-mixture-model-em-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-mixture-model-em-inference Use when inferring cell-type-specific TF-gene networks and Boolean logic gates from a small, pre-selected set of TFs and target genes in single-cell expression data, given a candidate base GRN. The TF set is large (>5 regulators per target) or the gene set exceeds ~200 genes with unrefined candidates — overfitting of high-order Boolean logic is a major concern and scGATE should not be used for large-scale inference from scratch Data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories with temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle temporally ordered single-cell data Only a plain directed TF-gene network is needed with no combinatorial logic — scGATE_edge() is a simpler fit, and other tools may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A Bayesian EM-based procedure used by scGATE to fit zero-inflated mixture likelihoods over Boolean logic combinations (AND/OR/XOR on TF activities) and infer, a posteriori, the most probable logic gate and TF-target edges from continuous scRNA-seq data without binarization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: A Bayesian EM-based procedure used by scGATE to fit zero-inflated mixture likelihoods over Boolean logic combinations (AND/OR/XOR on TF activities) and infer, a posteriori, the most probable logic gate and TF-target edges from continuous scRNA-seq data without binarization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The TF set is large (>5 regulators per target) or the gene set exceeds ~200 genes with unrefined candidates — overfitting of high-order Boolean logic is a major concern and scGATE should not be used for large-scale inference from scratch Data are pseudotime-sorted along differentiation trajectories with temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle temporally ordered single-cell data Only a plain directed TF-gene network is needed with no combinatorial logic — scGATE_edge() is a simpler fit, and other tools may suffice

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq SNV calls yield a per-cell fraction of reads supporting each species/genotype and you must decide if the population is a mixture of two genotypes, assign cells, and quantify multiplets.
skills.name: bayesian-mixture-model-selection
skills.search_text: bayesian-mixture-model-selection Use when single-cell RNA-seq SNV calls yield a per-cell fraction of reads supporting each species/genotype and you must decide if the population is a mixture of two genotypes, assign cells, and quantify multiplets. The dataset is a single-genotype sample where K=1 is expected and the goal is not chimerism/mixture deconvolution (K=1 selection here only means mixture fraction is below the ~4% detection level, not a successful two-genotype assignment) Input is raw gene-barcode count data without SNV calls — this skill requires per-cell SNV fractions, not expression matrices Variants are indels rather than SNVs, since the pipeline explicitly ignores indels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Fit K=1 vs K=2 Bayesian mixture models to per-cell SNV genotype fractions derived from scRNA-seq to decide whether a sample contains two distinct genotypes (e.g., Jurkat vs 293T or host vs donor), classify individual cells, and estimate multiplet rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Fit K=1 vs K=2 Bayesian mixture models to per-cell SNV genotype fractions derived from scRNA-seq to decide whether a sample contains two distinct genotypes (e.g., Jurkat vs 293T or host vs donor), classify individual cells, and estimate multiplet rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single-genotype sample where K=1 is expected and the goal is not chimerism/mixture deconvolution (K=1 selection here only means mixture fraction is below the ~4% detection level, not a successful two-genotype assignment) Input is raw gene-barcode count data without SNV calls — this skill requires per-cell SNV fractions, not expression matrices Variants are indels rather than SNVs, since the pipeline explicitly ignores indels

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, se_beta) are already fitted with iDEA.fit and you want gene-level posterior DE probabilities that exploit consistent DE evidence across overlapping gene sets rather than gene-by-gene testing.
skills.name: bayesian-model-averaging-de-evidence
skills.search_text: bayesian-model-averaging-de-evidence Use when scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, se_beta) are already fitted with iDEA.fit and you want gene-level posterior DE probabilities that exploit consistent DE evidence across overlapping gene sets rather than gene-by-gene testing. Input is raw single-cell count data rather than per-gene DE summary statistics; iDEA works only on summary statistics No fitted iDEA model exists yet — iDEA.BMA must be run after iDEA.fit on a populated iDEA object Individual-level scRNA-seq modeling assumptions or cell-type-level uncertainty must be explicitly modeled, which iDEA's z-score summary-statistic framework does not do http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregate per-gene differential expression evidence across gene sets using iDEA's Bayesian model averaging (iDEA.BMA), which borrows enrichment signals from all fitted gene sets to improve DE power for individual genes in scRNA-seq summary statistics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Aggregate per-gene differential expression evidence across gene sets using iDEA's Bayesian model averaging (iDEA.BMA), which borrows enrichment signals from all fitted gene sets to improve DE power for individual genes in scRNA-seq summary statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-cell count data rather than per-gene DE summary statistics; iDEA works only on summary statistics No fitted iDEA model exists yet — iDEA.BMA must be run after iDEA.fit on a populated iDEA object Individual-level scRNA-seq modeling assumptions or cell-type-level uncertainty must be explicitly modeled, which iDEA's z-score summary-statistic framework does not do

skills.description: Use when gene-level DE summary statistics (beta coefficients and variances) from tools like MAST, edgeR, or zingeR are available and you want to strengthen per-gene DE calls by aggregating evidence across gene set fits rather than testing one gene at a time.
skills.name: bayesian-model-averaging-posterior-inclusion-probability
skills.search_text: bayesian-model-averaging-posterior-inclusion-probability Use when gene-level DE summary statistics (beta coefficients and variances) from tools like MAST, edgeR, or zingeR are available and you want to strengthen per-gene DE calls by aggregating evidence across gene set fits rather than testing one gene at a time. No gene set annotations are available or the coverage rate (annotated genes / tested genes) falls below min_precent_annot=0.0025, so gene sets cannot be fitted Only raw single-cell count matrices are available and no per-gene summary statistics (beta and var(beta)) have been computed by a standalone DE method The analysis goal is gene set enrichment testing alone (use iDEA.fit with iDEA.louis / iDEA.FDR for calibrated gene set p-values rather than BMA gene aggregation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates gene-level differential expression evidence across all gene sets using iDEA's Bayesian model averaging (BMA) approach, which computes posterior inclusion probabilities for genes across fitted gene set models. This augments standalone DE tools (MAST, edgeR, zingeR) by borrowing consistent DE evidence across similar genes in gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Aggregates gene-level differential expression evidence across all gene sets using iDEA's Bayesian model averaging (BMA) approach, which computes posterior inclusion probabilities for genes across fitted gene set models. This augments standalone DE tools (MAST, edgeR, zingeR) by borrowing consistent DE evidence across similar genes in gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No gene set annotations are available or the coverage rate (annotated genes / tested genes) falls below min_precent_annot=0.0025, so gene sets cannot be fitted Only raw single-cell count matrices are available and no per-gene summary statistics (beta and var(beta)) have been computed by a standalone DE method The analysis goal is gene set enrichment testing alone (use iDEA.fit with iDEA.louis / iDEA.FDR for calibrated gene set p-values rather than BMA gene aggregation)

skills.description: Use when a 3D-aligned spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., STARmap mouse brain slices stacked by Scube) is available and you need to flag spatially variable genes by testing directional expression variation in 3D.
skills.name: bayesian-model-comparison-bayes-factor
skills.search_text: bayesian-model-comparison-bayes-factor Use when a 3D-aligned spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., STARmap mouse brain slices stacked by Scube) is available and you need to flag spatially variable genes by testing directional expression variation in 3D. The data are single 2D slices not yet stacked by Scube — no 3D coordinates exist to regress over The goal is 2D spatially variable gene detection on one slice (use spatial-domain tools like Splane/SpaGCN instead of 3D GPR) Input is seq-based ST (e.g., 10X Visium) that first requires Spoint cell type deconvolution and slice alignment before 3D modeling is meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit Gaussian process regression (GPR) models to per-gene expression over Scube's stacked 3D coordinates and score them with a Bayes Factor comparing the optimized kernel length scale against an infinite-length-scale null model, identifying genes whose expression varies significantly along any direction in the 3D tissue architecture. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Fit Gaussian process regression (GPR) models to per-gene expression over Scube's stacked 3D coordinates and score them with a Bayes Factor comparing the optimized kernel length scale against an infinite-length-scale null model, identifying genes whose expression varies significantly along any direction in the 3D tissue architecture.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are single 2D slices not yet stacked by Scube — no 3D coordinates exist to regress over The goal is 2D spatially variable gene detection on one slice (use spatial-domain tools like Splane/SpaGCN instead of 3D GPR) Input is seq-based ST (e.g., 10X Visium) that first requires Spoint cell type deconvolution and slice alignment before 3D modeling is meaningful

skills.description: Use when an unsupervised variational inference loop (e.g., Tempo phase inference) needs a principled termination criterion, or when deciding whether adding de novo detected cycler genes improves or worsens model fit to core clock genes.
skills.name: bayesian-model-evidence-evaluation
skills.search_text: bayesian-model-evidence-evaluation Use when an unsupervised variational inference loop (e.g., Tempo phase inference) needs a principled termination criterion, or when deciding whether adding de novo detected cycler genes improves or worsens model fit to core clock genes. Sample timing is trusted and a time-course design can proxy circadian phase without unsupervised inference from gene expression. The model is a single fixed pass and no iterative gene-set update (Step 2 de novo cycler detection) is performed, so there is no evidence trajectory to evaluate. Bayesian evidence for the current gene set cannot be computed because core clock genes or priors were never supplied. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Iterative Bayesian model comparison used in Tempo's variational inference loop: at each iteration, evaluate Bayesian evidence for user-supplied core clock genes against the prior iteration and a random baseline, and stop when evidence degrades. This criterion controls when the optimized approximate joint posterior q(theta, beta) is considered final. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Iterative Bayesian model comparison used in Tempo's variational inference loop: at each iteration, evaluate Bayesian evidence for user-supplied core clock genes against the prior iteration and a random baseline, and stop when evidence degrades. This criterion controls when the optimized approximate joint posterior q(theta, beta) is considered final.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample timing is trusted and a time-course design can proxy circadian phase without unsupervised inference from gene expression. The model is a single fixed pass and no iterative gene-set update (Step 2 de novo cycler detection) is performed, so there is no evidence trajectory to evaluate. Bayesian evidence for the current gene set cannot be computed because core clock genes or priors were never supplied.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking generative Bayesian-network correction (BNC, URSA) of per-term Cell Ontology classifier probabilities against discriminative baselines (independent classifiers, IR, TPR) on human RNA-seq data.
skills.name: bayesian-network-ontology-correction
skills.search_text: bayesian-network-ontology-correction Use when benchmarking generative Bayesian-network correction (BNC, URSA) of per-term Cell Ontology classifier probabilities against discriminative baselines (independent classifiers, IR, TPR) on human RNA-seq data. You need accurate out-of-the-box cell type annotation: BNC significantly degraded validation-set performance versus independent classifiers, IR, and TPR, so use CellO's default 'IR' algorithm instead of reproducing the BNC comparison. Your data are not human primary cell RNA-seq: CellO's classifiers were trained on human primary bulk RNA-seq from the SRA, and no comprehensive curated mouse training set exists yet. Your goal is calibrated binary yes/no cell type decisions: the paper notes performance with F1-score lags average precision, so average-precision-based ontology-correction comparisons do not certify decision quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Applies the generative Bayesian network correction (BNC, as implemented in URSA) to combine per-cell-type classifier probabilities over the Cell Ontology graph, benchmarked in CellO against independent classifiers and discriminative corrections (IR, TPR). In the CellO validation, BNC significantly degraded average precision, making it chiefly a cautionary baseline showing discriminative ontology correction is preferred. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101913
skills.summary: Applies the generative Bayesian network correction (BNC, as implemented in URSA) to combine per-cell-type classifier probabilities over the Cell Ontology graph, benchmarked in CellO against independent classifiers and discriminative corrections (IR, TPR). In the CellO validation, BNC significantly degraded average precision, making it chiefly a cautionary baseline showing discriminative ontology correction is preferred.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need accurate out-of-the-box cell type annotation: BNC significantly degraded validation-set performance versus independent classifiers, IR, and TPR, so use CellO's default 'IR' algorithm instead of reproducing the BNC comparison. Your data are not human primary cell RNA-seq: CellO's classifiers were trained on human primary bulk RNA-seq from the SRA, and no comprehensive curated mouse training set exists yet. Your goal is calibrated binary yes/no cell type decisions: the paper notes performance with F1-score lags average precision, so average-precision-based ontology-correction comparisons do not certify decision quality.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a novel phase I/II dose-finding design against established Bayesian parametric designs (Thall–Cook P1, Yin et al. P2) in Monte Carlo simulations with a fixed highest acceptable DLT rate phi.
skills.name: bayesian-parametric-comparator-design-implementation
skills.search_text: bayesian-parametric-comparator-design-implementation Use when benchmarking a novel phase I/II dose-finding design against established Bayesian parametric designs (Thall–Cook P1, Yin et al. P2) in Monte Carlo simulations with a fixed highest acceptable DLT rate phi. The response outcome requires long follow-up or is not binary and quickly observable shortly after treatment initiation — the TSNP framework and its comparator setup do not apply The goal is to calibrate or tune the parametric designs themselves rather than to reproduce their published operating characteristics as a benchmark Implements the Bayesian parametric phase I/II comparator designs P1 (Thall et al.) and P2 (Yin et al.) in R so their OBD-selection operating characteristics can be benchmarked against the TSNP design under identical scenarios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Implements the Bayesian parametric phase I/II comparator designs P1 (Thall et al.) and P2 (Yin et al.) in R so their OBD-selection operating characteristics can be benchmarked against the TSNP design under identical scenarios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up or is not binary and quickly observable shortly after treatment initiation — the TSNP framework and its comparator setup do not apply The goal is to calibrate or tune the parametric designs themselves rather than to reproduce their published operating characteristics as a benchmark

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-rescaled scRNA-seq matrix for one cell type/context, a small candidate TF list (k<=5) per target gene, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just directed edges) linking TFs to each target.
skills.name: bayesian-posterior-rule-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-posterior-rule-inference Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-rescaled scRNA-seq matrix for one cell type/context, a small candidate TF list (k<=5) per target gene, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just directed edges) linking TFs to each target. Target genes have a large unrefined candidate TF set (>5 regulators) — the article warns overfitting makes logic inference unreliable beyond ~5 TFs and recommends <5 The goal is only directed TF-gene edges without logic — use scGATE_edge() instead of gate inference The gene set is large-scale (>200 genes) without prior biological knowledge to pre-select TFs — scGATE is stated to be applicable only to a small (<200) subset with refined candidate regulators http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Infer the most probable Boolean logic gate (AND/OR/XOR combinations) governing a target gene from single-cell expression data by EM-updating prior probabilities w_v over 2^k logic combinations under a zero-inflated (dropout + normal) mixture likelihood, then selecting gates by Bayes Factor instead of enumerating per-rule likelihoods. This is the core inference step of scGATE and drastically reduces time complexity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Infer the most probable Boolean logic gate (AND/OR/XOR combinations) governing a target gene from single-cell expression data by EM-updating prior probabilities w_v over 2^k logic combinations under a zero-inflated (dropout + normal) mixture likelihood, then selecting gates by Bayes Factor instead of enumerating per-rule likelihoods. This is the core inference step of scGATE and drastically reduces time complexity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target genes have a large unrefined candidate TF set (>5 regulators) — the article warns overfitting makes logic inference unreliable beyond ~5 TFs and recommends <5 The goal is only directed TF-gene edges without logic — use scGATE_edge() instead of gate inference The gene set is large-scale (>200 genes) without prior biological knowledge to pre-select TFs — scGATE is stated to be applicable only to a small (<200) subset with refined candidate regulators

skills.when_to_use_negative: When genes are known to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime, so posterior interaction calls may not fit the data When the data contain complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath explicitly defers to future work When a standard differential-expression comparison between covariate-positive and covariate-negative cells suffices — benchmarking shows DE-based methods (Limma Voom, DESeq2, MAST, Monocle 2) only match PhenoPath AUC at low interaction fractions (~5-10%)

skills.search_text: bayesian-spike-and-slab-differential-abundance-analysis Use when testing cell-type compositional changes across few biological replicates (e.g. 7 supercentenarian vs 5 control PBMC samples) from an NxK cell-type count matrix with a binary covariate, where univariate tests would inflate false positives. skills.summary: Bayesian differential abundance testing of cell-type proportions using scCODA's hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior, which jointly models all measured cell-type proportions to control false discoveries under compositional bias and low replicates.

skills.search_text: bayesian-spike-and-slab-effect-selection Use when scRNA-seq samples (or other count compositional data) are aggregated per sample into cell-type counts and you need differential abundance testing that controls the FDR, especially with a low number of experimental replicates. skills.summary: Identifies credible cell-type compositional changes by modeling cell-type counts with a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial model and a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior (scCODA), controlling false discoveries even with few replicates. skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq counts (e.g., droplet-based 10X data stored as anndata) must be ordered over the circadian cycle without sample-time labels, and phase point estimates plus uncertainty are needed.
skills.name: bayesian-variational-phase-inference
skills.search_text: bayesian-variational-phase-inference Use when scRNA-seq counts (e.g., droplet-based 10X data stored as anndata) must be ordered over the circadian cycle without sample-time labels, and phase point estimates plus uncertainty are needed. Data were collected as multiple samples over time where explicit modeling of technical effects is necessary — Tempo does not explicitly model these technical effects. The analysis requires cell-type-specific or subpopulation-specific CCG amplitude modeling — Tempo assumes 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means and does not map cell state embeddings to sinusoidal parameters. The goal is rhythmicity detection in bulk time-course data (e.g., JTKCycle on microarray) rather than single-cell circadian phase inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply Tempo, a Bayesian variational inference algorithm, to infer single-cell circadian phase from scRNA-seq count data, incorporating core clock genes or de novo-identified clock-controlled genes (CCGs). It supports unsupervised phase inference for droplet- and plate-based data with calibrated uncertainty quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Apply Tempo, a Bayesian variational inference algorithm, to infer single-cell circadian phase from scRNA-seq count data, incorporating core clock genes or de novo-identified clock-controlled genes (CCGs). It supports unsupervised phase inference for droplet- and plate-based data with calibrated uncertainty quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were collected as multiple samples over time where explicit modeling of technical effects is necessary — Tempo does not explicitly model these technical effects. The goal is rhythmicity detection in bulk time-course data (e.g., JTKCycle on microarray) rather than single-cell circadian phase inference.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare cell-cell communication inference methods (e.g., MDIC3 vs CellChat) on the same scRNA-seq dataset using literature-supported ground truth and AUC, rather than relying on qualitative claims.

skills.search_text: benchmark-auc-comparison Use when you need to quantitatively compare cell-cell communication inference methods (e.g., MDIC3 vs CellChat) on the same scRNA-seq dataset using literature-supported ground truth and AUC, rather than relying on qualitative claims. You lack a curated literature-supported ground truth for the dataset — without it the AUC cannot be computed and the comparison degenerates to counting communications. skills.description: Use when a paper reports headline metrics (e.g. MCC/F1 on named test datasets) and you have access to the model or code deposit, so you can recompute metrics and diff them against the published benchmark values.
skills.name: benchmark-comparison-against-published-metrics
skills.search_text: benchmark-comparison-against-published-metrics Use when a paper reports headline metrics (e.g. MCC/F1 on named test datasets) and you have access to the model or code deposit, so you can recompute metrics and diff them against the published benchmark values. No model artifact or deposit exists and only a web server is available (e.g. LncCat's web server returns results only by email, so exact reproduction is not possible) The target paper omits key settings (e.g. CatBoost/BERT versions, hyperparameters), making a faithful re-run and honest comparison infeasible Your inputs are new or out-of-distribution transcripts rather than the paper's named benchmark test sets — use model evaluation, not published-value comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce a trained model's evaluation on benchmark test sets (long-ORF and sORF) and quantitatively compare computed metrics (PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, AUC) against the values published in the source paper, e.g. LncCat's integrated MCC of 0.9236 and sORF-integrated MCC of 0.8346. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Reproduce a trained model's evaluation on benchmark test sets (long-ORF and sORF) and quantitatively compare computed metrics (PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, AUC) against the values published in the source paper, e.g. LncCat's integrated MCC of 0.9236 and sORF-integrated MCC of 0.8346.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No model artifact or deposit exists and only a web server is available (e.g. LncCat's web server returns results only by email, so exact reproduction is not possible) The target paper omits key settings (e.g. CatBoost/BERT versions, hyperparameters), making a faithful re-run and honest comparison infeasible Your inputs are new or out-of-distribution transcripts rather than the paper's named benchmark test sets — use model evaluation, not published-value comparison

skills.description: Use when a paper reports concrete per-sample quantitative results (e.g., identified-read counts/ratios) on named public datasets (e.g., SAMN accessions) and you must independently reproduce and compare them.
skills.name: benchmark-comparison-against-reported-metrics
skills.search_text: benchmark-comparison-against-reported-metrics Use when a paper reports concrete per-sample quantitative results (e.g., identified-read counts/ratios) on named public datasets (e.g., SAMN accessions) and you must independently reproduce and compare them. Input is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcoded data — the article proposes the fault-tolerant and indel alignment only for SPLiT-seq data, with other platforms stated as potential but not demonstrated No reported quantitative metrics or public raw datasets exist to compare against, so there is nothing to benchmark The goal is biological downstream analysis (e.g., clustering or cell typing) rather than tool reproduction/validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Re-run a published tool (here SCSit, a SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool) on its original public datasets and assemble per-sample metrics into a table alongside the paper's reported values to verify reproduction within a small deviation tolerance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Re-run a published tool (here SCSit, a SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool) on its original public datasets and assemble per-sample metrics into a table alongside the paper's reported values to verify reproduction within a small deviation tolerance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcoded data — the article proposes the fault-tolerant and indel alignment only for SPLiT-seq data, with other platforms stated as potential but not demonstrated No reported quantitative metrics or public raw datasets exist to compare against, so there is nothing to benchmark The goal is biological downstream analysis (e.g., clustering or cell typing) rather than tool reproduction/validation

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare automated cell-type annotation methods on the same clustered scRNA-seq datasets, with controlled marker inputs, accuracy counts, and runtime measurements.
skills.name: benchmark-comparison-of-cell-annotation-methods
skills.search_text: benchmark-comparison-of-cell-annotation-methods Use when you need to quantitatively compare automated cell-type annotation methods on the same clustered scRNA-seq datasets, with controlled marker inputs, accuracy counts, and runtime measurements. When the cell-type labels being evaluated were themselves derived from the annotation method's marker database for that tissue (e.g., brain markers derived from the brain test dataset), since this biases the comparison — the protocol explicitly excludes such self-derived markers When scCATCH must consume custom user-supplied marker sets in the simulated-data comparison, since its implementation does not allow custom markers When the goal is tumor/malignant-cell discrimination rather than healthy tissue annotation — ScType's SNV-calling capability via vartrix is a separate capability outside this benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A systematic benchmarking protocol comparing the fully-automated marker-based method ScType against prior-knowledge methods scSorter, SCINA, and scCATCH for cell-type annotation across six human and mouse scRNA-seq datasets, recording both annotation accuracy and wall-clock runtime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: A systematic benchmarking protocol comparing the fully-automated marker-based method ScType against prior-knowledge methods scSorter, SCINA, and scCATCH for cell-type annotation across six human and mouse scRNA-seq datasets, recording both annotation accuracy and wall-clock runtime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the cell-type labels being evaluated were themselves derived from the annotation method's marker database for that tissue (e.g., brain markers derived from the brain test dataset), since this biases the comparison — the protocol explicitly excludes such self-derived markers When scCATCH must consume custom user-supplied marker sets in the simulated-data comparison, since its implementation does not allow custom markers When the goal is tumor/malignant-cell discrimination rather than healthy tissue annotation — ScType's SNV-calling capability via vartrix is a separate capability outside this benchmark

skills.description: Use when you must validate a temporal differential expression method's detection performance against established DE tools on simulated single-cell counts with a known ground-truth gene set.

skills.search_text: benchmark-comparison-of-de-methods Use when you must validate a temporal differential expression method's detection performance against established DE tools on simulated single-cell counts with a known ground-truth gene set. The goal is differential expression on a single time point / cross-sectional scRNA-seq experiment — plain DESeq2, MAST, or Seurat FindMarkers alone suffices without the temporal simulation benchmark Input lacks a known ground-truth tDEG set (e.g. real data without planted signals) — TDR cannot be computed, so use alternative validation (supplementary ARI comparison, clustering) instead Evaluating cell annotation or novel-cell detection rather than temporal differential expression — those CASi modules (CrossTimeAnnotation, DetectNovelCells) are benchmarked separately (ARI in supplementary Fig 11) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 A benchmarking skill that evaluates CASi's FindTemporalDEGs against conventional differential expression methods (DESeq2, MAST, Seurat Wilcoxon) on simulated longitudinal scRNA-seq data with planted tDEGs, measuring true discovery rate (TDR) across p-value thresholds. It grounds claims of favorable performance in a reproducible simulation-plus-baseline comparison rather than a single method run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that evaluates CASi's FindTemporalDEGs against conventional differential expression methods (DESeq2, MAST, Seurat Wilcoxon) on simulated longitudinal scRNA-seq data with planted tDEGs, measuring true discovery rate (TDR) across p-value thresholds. It grounds claims of favorable performance in a reproducible simulation-plus-baseline comparison rather than a single method run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression on a single time point / cross-sectional scRNA-seq experiment — plain DESeq2, MAST, or Seurat FindMarkers alone suffices without the temporal simulation benchmark Input lacks a known ground-truth tDEG set (e.g. real data without planted signals) — TDR cannot be computed, so use alternative validation (supplementary ARI comparison, clustering) instead Evaluating cell annotation or novel-cell detection rather than temporal differential expression — those CASi modules (CrossTimeAnnotation, DetectNovelCells) are benchmarked separately (ARI in supplementary Fig 11)

skills.description: Use when a new clustering method must be benchmarked against existing ensemble and single-cell baselines across multiple datasets and an ARI/NMI comparison table with per-dataset rankings is the deliverable.

skills.summary: Assembles a method-by-dataset comparison table of clustering performance (ARI and NMI against published cell-type labels) for a proposed method (scEFSC) versus ensemble baselines (SAME-clustering, scCCESS, RSEC) and single-cell clustering algorithms (SHARP, SC3, CIDR, Monocle, RaceID, PhenoGraph, Seurat) on fourteen published scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The evaluation goal is a single method on a single dataset with no baselines to compare — a ranking table has no comparative meaning The reference labels are unavailable or ambiguous (e.g., cells labeled ambiguously as 'abandoned' must first be removed, otherwise ARI/NMI against labels is undefined or biased) The task is biological interpretation (differential expression, GO/KEGG enrichment) rather than quantitative benchmarking

skills.search_text: benchmark-curve-visualization Use when reproducing label-noise robustness curves for (semi)supervised integration methods: you have integration scores at 0–100% shuffled or 0–100% 'unknown' label corruption and need method-comparison curves per task.
