skills.search_text: benchmark-gene-list-mapping Use when you have driver gene prediction lists for multiple tools (e.g. from DriverDBv2) and need to rank them against curated benchmark sets (CGC 616 genes, NCG 711 genes, PMH 501 genes) with an F-measure. The candidate gene list is not a driver-gene prediction set but raw expression or co-expression data — this skill only scores already-predicted gene lists against benchmarks Recall is the priority of the evaluation (beta > 1); the skill's headline metric deliberately weights precision (beta^2 = 0.2), so F0.2 rankings would misrepresent recall-oriented goals No curated benchmark list (CGC/NCG/PMH or equivalent) exists for the cancer type, since TP/FP/FN cannot be defined without a reference gene set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Scores cancer driver gene predictions against curated benchmark gene lists (CGC, NCG, PMH) using precision/recall and the precision-weighted F0.2 measure, then ranks competing tools per benchmark. It grounds tool-performance claims (e.g. WMDS.net vs 11 DriverDBv2 tools) in a reproducible benchmark table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Scores cancer driver gene predictions against curated benchmark gene lists (CGC, NCG, PMH) using precision/recall and the precision-weighted F0.2 measure, then ranks competing tools per benchmark. It grounds tool-performance claims (e.g. WMDS.net vs 11 DriverDBv2 tools) in a reproducible benchmark table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate gene list is not a driver-gene prediction set but raw expression or co-expression data — this skill only scores already-predicted gene lists against benchmarks Recall is the priority of the evaluation (beta > 1); the skill's headline metric deliberately weights precision (beta^2 = 0.2), so F0.2 rankings would misrepresent recall-oriented goals No curated benchmark list (CGC/NCG/PMH or equivalent) exists for the cancer type, since TP/FP/FN cannot be defined without a reference gene set

skills.description: Use when a cell hashing Seurat object and published SNP-based (scSplit) ground-truth labels are both available and you need to correlate hashing singlet groups with genotype clusters to produce validated per-cell sample identity labels.
skills.name: benchmark-ground-truth-label-chaining
skills.search_text: benchmark-ground-truth-label-chaining Use when a cell hashing Seurat object and published SNP-based (scSplit) ground-truth labels are both available and you need to correlate hashing singlet groups with genotype clusters to produce validated per-cell sample identity labels. Samples lack a distinct genetic background (most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies), so SNP-based ground-truth labels cannot be produced for chaining Only cell hashing data is available with no SNP/genotype labels — use HTOreader's standalone HTOClassification cutoff calling instead Input is raw HTO counts that have not yet been demultiplexed by the upstream hashtag step (HTOClassification/PlotHTO cutoff checks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Chains published ground-truth genotype labels (e.g. scSplit labels from the Stoeckius-2018 dataset) with HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function to assign final cell sample identities, using a convergence-score threshold (c_threshold = 0.7, C = N1/(N1+N2)) to decide between merged hashing/genotype labels and cell-hashing fallback labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Chains published ground-truth genotype labels (e.g. scSplit labels from the Stoeckius-2018 dataset) with HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function to assign final cell sample identities, using a convergence-score threshold (c_threshold = 0.7, C = N1/(N1+N2)) to decide between merged hashing/genotype labels and cell-hashing fallback labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack a distinct genetic background (most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies), so SNP-based ground-truth labels cannot be produced for chaining Only cell hashing data is available with no SNP/genotype labels — use HTOreader's standalone HTOClassification cutoff calling instead Input is raw HTO counts that have not yet been demultiplexed by the upstream hashtag step (HTOClassification/PlotHTO cutoff checks)

skills.description: Use when comparing label-transfer methods (e.g., scID vs scmap, CaSTLe, scVI) that map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to clusters of a reference dataset, and you need coverage and accuracy metrics on a common benchmark.
skills.name: benchmark-method-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-accuracy-comparison Use when comparing label-transfer methods (e.g., scID vs scmap, CaSTLe, scVI) that map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to clusters of a reference dataset, and you need coverage and accuracy metrics on a common benchmark. The goal is unsupervised batch integration or correction of datasets rather than benchmarking supervised cell-type label transfer against known labels Neither the reference nor the target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures, so no mapping method produces a meaningful assignment to benchmark Input matrices are already log-transformed, since scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized but non-log-transformed data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks supervised cell-type mapping methods (scID, scmap, CaSTLe, scVI) on the same reference-target scRNA-seq pairs by computing per-method assignment coverage and clustering-accuracy metrics (ARI, VI) against published cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Benchmarks supervised cell-type mapping methods (scID, scmap, CaSTLe, scVI) on the same reference-target scRNA-seq pairs by computing per-method assignment coverage and clustering-accuracy metrics (ARI, VI) against published cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised batch integration or correction of datasets rather than benchmarking supervised cell-type label transfer against known labels Neither the reference nor the target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures, so no mapping method produces a meaningful assignment to benchmark Input matrices are already log-transformed, since scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized but non-log-transformed data

skills.description: Use when multiple active subnetwork detection methods have each recovered a subnetwork from the same seed (disease) genes or gene P-values and you must quantify method-to-method structural overlap via pairwise Jaccard similarity.
skills.name: benchmark-method-agreement-evaluation
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-agreement-evaluation Use when multiple active subnetwork detection methods have each recovered a subnetwork from the same seed (disease) genes or gene P-values and you must quantify method-to-method structural overlap via pairwise Jaccard similarity. You need edge- or topology-level agreement (e.g., graph edit distance) rather than node-set overlap — this skill compares only vertex sets Only one subnetwork has been recovered, so there is no pair against which to compute Jaccard similarity The subnetworks come from heterogeneous benchmark designs (different seeds or reference networks per method), which would confound the overlap interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies agreement among active subnetwork detection methods (pathfindR, BioNet, STr2z, etc.) by computing pairwise Jaccard similarity on the node sets of their recovered benchmark subnetworks, after harmonizing all outputs as directed trees. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement among active subnetwork detection methods (pathfindR, BioNet, STr2z, etc.) by computing pairwise Jaccard similarity on the node sets of their recovered benchmark subnetworks, after harmonizing all outputs as directed trees.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need edge- or topology-level agreement (e.g., graph edit distance) rather than node-set overlap — this skill compares only vertex sets Only one subnetwork has been recovered, so there is no pair against which to compute Jaccard similarity The subnetworks come from heterogeneous benchmark designs (different seeds or reference networks per method), which would confound the overlap interpretation

skills.description: Use when you must objectively compare a new CCI inference method against existing ones (e.g. SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, CellPhoneDB, CellChat, CellCall, CytoTalk, NATMI) on a shared scRNA-seq dataset with a literature-supported ground-truth interaction set.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison Use when you must objectively compare a new CCI inference method against existing ones (e.g. SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, CellPhoneDB, CellChat, CellCall, CytoTalk, NATMI) on a shared scRNA-seq dataset with a literature-supported ground-truth interaction set. You only need to run a single method for exploratory CCI discovery rather than compare methods against a ground truth. No literature-curated ground-truth interaction set exists for the cell-type pair of interest, so AUC/precision cannot be computed. The input is not scRNA-seq expression data with cell-type labels suitable for all compared methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a target CCI prediction method (e.g. DeepCCI) head-to-head against competing methods by running all of them on the same preprocessed scRNA-seq dataset and ranking them with literature-curated ground-truth metrics such as AUC and precision. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: Benchmark a target CCI prediction method (e.g. DeepCCI) head-to-head against competing methods by running all of them on the same preprocessed scRNA-seq dataset and ranking them with literature-curated ground-truth metrics such as AUC and precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to run a single method for exploratory CCI discovery rather than compare methods against a ground truth. No literature-curated ground-truth interaction set exists for the cell-type pair of interest, so AUC/precision cannot be computed. The input is not scRNA-seq expression data with cell-type labels suitable for all compared methods.

skills.description: Use when a new analysis tool claims parity with existing tools and the claim must be validated by running both on identical inputs (e.g. .h5ad AnnData with sample/cluster/condition columns) and comparing per-feature significance calls.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison-across-datasets Use when a new analysis tool claims parity with existing tools and the claim must be validated by running both on identical inputs (e.g. .h5ad AnnData with sample/cluster/condition columns) and comparing per-feature significance calls. Clusters supported by less than 2% of all cells in an experiment — the article's benchmarking found these produce unstable results, so their calls are not a fair basis for method comparison Datasets lacking the metadata needed to define replicates and conditions (sample/cluster/condition columns), since neither the replicated nor the pseudo-replicate comparison design can be set up When the goal is the analysis itself rather than validating tool agreement — for a single dataset with replicates, running one tool (e.g. Scanpro via scanpro()) suffices without benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a new computational method against state-of-the-art alternatives by running all tools on the same replicated and pseudo-replicated single-cell datasets (e.g. Scanpro vs propeller and scCODA on PBMC, heart-development, and COVID-19 BALF AnnData objects) and compiling per-cluster p-values and significance calls into one comparable table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Benchmark a new computational method against state-of-the-art alternatives by running all tools on the same replicated and pseudo-replicated single-cell datasets (e.g. Scanpro vs propeller and scCODA on PBMC, heart-development, and COVID-19 BALF AnnData objects) and compiling per-cluster p-values and significance calls into one comparable table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters supported by less than 2% of all cells in an experiment — the article's benchmarking found these produce unstable results, so their calls are not a fair basis for method comparison Datasets lacking the metadata needed to define replicates and conditions (sample/cluster/condition columns), since neither the replicated nor the pseudo-replicate comparison design can be set up When the goal is the analysis itself rather than validating tool agreement — for a single dataset with replicates, running one tool (e.g. Scanpro via scanpro()) suffices without benchmarking

skills.description: Use when paired scDNA-seq (CNA) and scRNA-seq (gene expression) data from the same cells provide partial ground-truth clone labels, and multiple integration methods must be ranked on cell-to-clone assignment accuracy and clonal prevalence prediction.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison-against-ground-truth
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison-against-ground-truth Use when paired scDNA-seq (CNA) and scRNA-seq (gene expression) data from the same cells provide partial ground-truth clone labels, and multiple integration methods must be ranked on cell-to-clone assignment accuracy and clonal prevalence prediction. No ground truth exists for the cell correspondence (e.g., the BE dataset) — use resampling and stability analyses instead of accuracy benchmarking The goal is probabilistic confidence per assignment — MaCroDNA, unlike clonealign, does not provide probabilistic confidence measures for the assignments Input samples are biologically homogeneous, where matching cells is distinctly challenging and benchmark results may not generalize http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark scRNA-seq–to–scDNA-seq clone-assignment methods (MaCroDNA, clonealign, Seurat) on the CRC scTrio-seq dataset by comparing predicted cell-to-clone assignments and clonal prevalences against ground-truth labels from jointly profiled cells, using true-vs-predicted prevalence scatter plots with a diagonal reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq–to–scDNA-seq clone-assignment methods (MaCroDNA, clonealign, Seurat) on the CRC scTrio-seq dataset by comparing predicted cell-to-clone assignments and clonal prevalences against ground-truth labels from jointly profiled cells, using true-vs-predicted prevalence scatter plots with a diagonal reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground truth exists for the cell correspondence (e.g., the BE dataset) — use resampling and stability analyses instead of accuracy benchmarking The goal is probabilistic confidence per assignment — MaCroDNA, unlike clonealign, does not provide probabilistic confidence measures for the assignments Input samples are biologically homogeneous, where matching cells is distinctly challenging and benchmark results may not generalize

skills.description: Use when a new single-cell fate-mapping method must be validated against a published baseline (e.g., CellRank) by checking whether known terminal states, such as hormone-producing α, β, and ε cells, are consistently recovered.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison-single-cell
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison-single-cell Use when a new single-cell fate-mapping method must be validated against a published baseline (e.g., CellRank) by checking whether known terminal states, such as hormone-producing α, β, and ε cells, are consistently recovered. The dataset is a simulation-only ground truth (e.g., Dyngen) where no published baseline terminal-state calls exist to compare against Only transcription-factor activities are of interest — FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation, not method benchmarking, is the appropriate skill The input adata lacks cell-type annotations or an RNA velocity field, so neither CellRank's velocity kernel nor FateCompass's RNA-velocity-driven mode can be run http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a novel trajectory-inference method (FateCompass) against an established baseline (CellRank) on the same pre-processed scRNA-seq dataset, comparing terminal-fate calls and fate probabilities across kernels and parameters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Benchmark a novel trajectory-inference method (FateCompass) against an established baseline (CellRank) on the same pre-processed scRNA-seq dataset, comparing terminal-fate calls and fate probabilities across kernels and parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a simulation-only ground truth (e.g., Dyngen) where no published baseline terminal-state calls exist to compare against Only transcription-factor activities are of interest — FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation, not method benchmarking, is the appropriate skill The input adata lacks cell-type annotations or an RNA velocity field, so neither CellRank's velocity kernel nor FateCompass's RNA-velocity-driven mode can be run

skills.description: Use when validating a statistical detection method's false discovery rate calibration and power against existing methods using simulated signal spiked into a null dataset with known gold-standard positives.
skills.name: benchmark-method-power-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-power-comparison Use when validating a statistical detection method's false discovery rate calibration and power against existing methods using simulated signal spiked into a null dataset with known gold-standard positives. The analysis goal is applying a single method to real data rather than empirically evaluating FDR calibration and power against alternatives on simulated ground truth. No gold-standard positive gene set or null simulation can be constructed, so real (empirical) FDR cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a differential-expression/pseudotime method against competitors on spike-in simulations built on a null single-cell dataset, comparing real (empirical) FDR versus reported FDR and sensitivity as a function of real FDR (AUC) to demonstrate conservative FDR control and superior power. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Benchmark a differential-expression/pseudotime method against competitors on spike-in simulations built on a null single-cell dataset, comparing real (empirical) FDR versus reported FDR and sensitivity as a function of real FDR (AUC) to demonstrate conservative FDR control and superior power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is applying a single method to real data rather than empirically evaluating FDR calibration and power against alternatives on simulated ground truth. No gold-standard positive gene set or null simulation can be constructed, so real (empirical) FDR cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when a task specifies a published numeric benchmark (e.g. accuracy 0.94, specificity 0.98, sensitivity 0.90 on a 30% held-out test set) that must be verified by re-running the classifier end-to-end.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-reproduction Use when a task specifies a published numeric benchmark (e.g. accuracy 0.94, specificity 0.98, sensitivity 0.90 on a 30% held-out test set) that must be verified by re-running the classifier end-to-end. The classifier inputs are not labeled CD8 T cell profiles (e.g. mixed TIL populations where Treg/CD4T/NKT cells are present and filterCD8T filtering dominates) rather than a defined held-out CD8 TIL test set The goal is classifying new data rather than verifying a published metric — use the classifier directly or its maintained successor (ProjecTILs) instead of benchmark reproduction No reference/ground-truth labels exist for the held-out cells, so accuracy, specificity and sensitivity cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Reproduce a published classification benchmark by re-running a trained predictor (here TILPRED, a multinomial logistic regression CD8 TIL state classifier) on a held-out test split and computing accuracy with 95% CI, mean specificity and mean sensitivity against reported values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Reproduce a published classification benchmark by re-running a trained predictor (here TILPRED, a multinomial logistic regression CD8 TIL state classifier) on a held-out test split and computing accuracy with 95% CI, mean specificity and mean sensitivity against reported values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The classifier inputs are not labeled CD8 T cell profiles (e.g. mixed TIL populations where Treg/CD4T/NKT cells are present and filterCD8T filtering dominates) rather than a defined held-out CD8 TIL test set The goal is classifying new data rather than verifying a published metric — use the classifier directly or its maintained successor (ProjecTILs) instead of benchmark reproduction No reference/ground-truth labels exist for the held-out cells, so accuracy, specificity and sensitivity cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when replicating a published lncRNA-vs-PCT classifier's benchmark table on multi-species transcript datasets to check reported ACC, SEN, SPE, F1, PRE, MCC, and AUC values.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-reproduction-across-species
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-reproduction-across-species Use when replicating a published lncRNA-vs-PCT classifier's benchmark table on multi-species transcript datasets to check reported ACC, SEN, SPE, F1, PRE, MCC, and AUC values. Evaluating on sORF-enriched test sets (human/mouse/zebrafish sORF datasets) — those use a separate protocol with different reported improvement ranges Transcript sets not filtered with CD-HIT at 80% similarity or containing ncRNAs shorter than 200 nt — metric values will not be comparable to the published table Cross-species prediction scenarios — the article reports same-species models perform poorly on wheat (MCC ~0.63-0.67), so cross-species transfers are out of scope for this reproduction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Reproduce published classification benchmarks of LncCat, a CatBoost-based lncRNA identifier with ORF-attention features, on five species datasets (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken) and verify the reported MCC values against the eight competing methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Reproduce published classification benchmarks of LncCat, a CatBoost-based lncRNA identifier with ORF-attention features, on five species datasets (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken) and verify the reported MCC values against the eight competing methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating on sORF-enriched test sets (human/mouse/zebrafish sORF datasets) — those use a separate protocol with different reported improvement ranges Transcript sets not filtered with CD-HIT at 80% similarity or containing ncRNAs shorter than 200 nt — metric values will not be comparable to the published table Cross-species prediction scenarios — the article reports same-species models perform poorly on wheat (MCC ~0.63-0.67), so cross-species transfers are out of scope for this reproduction

skills.description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods (e.g., SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) across pseudotime/trajectory variants on ordered single-cell expression data, scored with AUROC/AUPRC overall and per regulator.
skills.name: benchmark-performance-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: benchmark-performance-comparison-across-methods Use when comparing GRN inference methods (e.g., SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) across pseudotime/trajectory variants on ordered single-cell expression data, scored with AUROC/AUPRC overall and per regulator. The task is to run a single GRN inference method once on a well-ordered pseudotime without any comparative evaluation — no benchmark comparison is needed Input expression data are unordered (no pseudotime or trajectory available), since all three compared methods (SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) require pseudotemporal ordering Only a single-cell count matrix with no ground-truth or reference network and no per-regulator labels, making AUROC/AUPRC evaluation infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Systematic benchmarking of pseudotime-based GRN inference methods (SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) by holding the expression data fixed, varying the pseudotime assignments, and comparing network reconstruction performance with AUROC and AUPRC metrics, both overall and per regulator. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Systematic benchmarking of pseudotime-based GRN inference methods (SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) by holding the expression data fixed, varying the pseudotime assignments, and comparing network reconstruction performance with AUROC and AUPRC metrics, both overall and per regulator.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to run a single GRN inference method once on a well-ordered pseudotime without any comparative evaluation — no benchmark comparison is needed Input expression data are unordered (no pseudotime or trajectory available), since all three compared methods (SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) require pseudotemporal ordering Only a single-cell count matrix with no ground-truth or reference network and no per-regulator labels, making AUROC/AUPRC evaluation infeasible

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation tools across benchmark single-cell datasets with reliable ground truth, to produce a comparable performance/runtime table.
skills.name: benchmark-performance-table-assembly
skills.search_text: benchmark-performance-table-assembly Use when comparing cell-type annotation tools across benchmark single-cell datasets with reliable ground truth, to produce a comparable performance/runtime table. When no datasets with reliable ground-truth annotations are available — the paper notes limited availability of high-quality ground-truth datasets constrains benchmark expansion When comparing against non-marker-based annotation tools — the study explicitly did not conduct a direct comparison with such approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Assembles a per-tool, per-dataset benchmark table of annotation performance (Cell Ontology-based percentage similarity, 0–100) and runtime for the Cell Marker Accordion versus ScType, SCINA, clustifyR, scCATCH and scSorter, quantifying the ~23% average improvement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Assembles a per-tool, per-dataset benchmark table of annotation performance (Cell Ontology-based percentage similarity, 0–100) and runtime for the Cell Marker Accordion versus ScType, SCINA, clustifyR, scCATCH and scSorter, quantifying the ~23% average improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no datasets with reliable ground-truth annotations are available — the paper notes limited availability of high-quality ground-truth datasets constrains benchmark expansion When comparing against non-marker-based annotation tools — the study explicitly did not conduct a direct comparison with such approaches

skills.search_text: benchmark-performance-visualization Use when comparing IPA-detection tools (InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder) on simulated RNA-seq data with known ground-truth polyA sites, and you need sensitivity/precision-vs-coverage figures and IPA-usage error plots. Input is real RNA-seq data without matched ground-truth polyA sites — sensitivity/precision against 'Predefined' sites cannot be computed Goal is 3'UTR-APA quantification only — the compared tools and this benchmark target intronic polyadenylation, and existing APA tools (DaPars, APAtrap, TAPAS) are limited to 3'UTR APA Only one tool's predictions are available — sensitivity, precision, and cumulative |ΔPAU| comparisons require matched predictions from multiple methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarking and visual comparison of intronic polyadenylation (IPA) tools by simulating RNA-seq with Polyester at 10X–50X coverage, scoring predicted sites against predefined polyA sites, and plotting sensitivity/precision curves plus cumulative |ΔPAU| quantification-error distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Benchmarking and visual comparison of intronic polyadenylation (IPA) tools by simulating RNA-seq with Polyester at 10X–50X coverage, scoring predicted sites against predefined polyA sites, and plotting sensitivity/precision curves plus cumulative |ΔPAU| quantification-error distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real RNA-seq data without matched ground-truth polyA sites — sensitivity/precision against 'Predefined' sites cannot be computed Goal is 3'UTR-APA quantification only — the compared tools and this benchmark target intronic polyadenylation, and existing APA tools (DaPars, APAtrap, TAPAS) are limited to 3'UTR APA Only one tool's predictions are available — sensitivity, precision, and cumulative |ΔPAU| comparisons require matched predictions from multiple methods

skills.description: Use when you have ranked driver-regulator lists (with influence scores) from multiple methods and curated ground-truth gene sets (e.g. GO:0045165, GO:0019827, GO:0007492) and need to compute/plot top-k precision curves for benchmarking.
skills.name: benchmark-precision-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: benchmark-precision-curve-visualization Use when you have ranked driver-regulator lists (with influence scores) from multiple methods and curated ground-truth gene sets (e.g. GO:0045165, GO:0019827, GO:0007492) and need to compute/plot top-k precision curves for benchmarking. skills.summary: Reproduce and visualize top-k (k=1–20) precision benchmarks for driver regulator identification, comparing a graph-neural-network method (CEFCON) against baselines such as VIPER, ANANSE, SCENIC, CellRouter, and CellOracle on mESC and hESC scRNA-seq datasets using GO-term ground-truth gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is to run CEFCON itself on a new lineage: CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time and cannot process multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations simultaneously Input is raw scRNA-seq data rather than pre-computed ranked driver-regulator lists with influence scores — use the GRN-inference skill instead No ground-truth gene sets (GO terms or curated driver genes) are available for the cell type or lineage of interest

skills.description: Use when you have per-method activity score matrices from decoupleR benchmark runs (e.g. run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R outputs on Zenodo record 5645208) and need to quantify whether different inference methods produce similar regulator activity estimates.
skills.name: benchmark-result-aggregation-across-omics
skills.search_text: benchmark-result-aggregation-across-omics Use when you have per-method activity score matrices from decoupleR benchmark runs (e.g. run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R outputs on Zenodo record 5645208) and need to quantify whether different inference methods produce similar regulator activity estimates. You are evaluating predictive performance of methods against perturbation ground truth (AUROC/AUPRC with downsampling) — use the decoupleRBench evaluation pipeline instead of agreement aggregation You only have a single method's activity scores and no cross-method panel to compare Input is raw count tables/metadata for the benchmark itself, not the inferred activity score matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates perturbation-benchmark outputs (regulator activity score matrices from 11 inference methods) across transcriptomics and phospho-proteomics collections into cross-method agreement statistics: median pairwise Spearman correlations of activity scores and median Jaccard indexes on top-5% regulator sets, as reported for Fig. 1B of the decoupleR manuscript. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016

skills.summary: Aggregates per-dataset, per-method clustering scores (ARI, AMI, NMI) from the CASCC benchmark into a single score table, enabling direct comparison of CASCC against CIDR, RaceID3, SC3, Seurat V4, SIMLR, and TSCAN on the 15 Krzak et al. 2019 scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The run involves a single clustering method without ground-truth cell-type labels, so no supervised metric like ARI/AMI/NMI can be computed The goal is the CASCC method run itself (attractor feature selection, cluster-k prediction, k-means) rather than cross-method benchmark scoring Input datasets are outside the 15 Krzak et al. 2019 evaluation datasets when the goal is reproducing the published Fig. 1b / Supplementary Table S3 numbers

skills.description: Use when comparing module-detection or sub-network-inference methods on RNA-seq data where ground-truth sub-networks are known or embedded, and sensitivity/robustness must be quantified and statistically compared.
skills.name: benchmark-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: benchmark-sensitivity-analysis Use when comparing module-detection or sub-network-inference methods on RNA-seq data where ground-truth sub-networks are known or embedded, and sensitivity/robustness must be quantified and statistically compared. When no ground-truth (embedded or curated) sub-network is available, since sensitivity against a known target cannot be computed When the goal is detecting modules in a single real dataset rather than comparing competing detection methods on simulated replicates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 A head-to-head benchmarking procedure that measures how sensitively and robustly module-detection methods (fRNC vs WGCNA, LncACT) recover known embedded RBP-ncRNA sub-networks in SimSeq-simulated RNA-seq data, compared via ANOVA and 100-times half-sample resampling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: A head-to-head benchmarking procedure that measures how sensitively and robustly module-detection methods (fRNC vs WGCNA, LncACT) recover known embedded RBP-ncRNA sub-networks in SimSeq-simulated RNA-seq data, compared via ANOVA and 100-times half-sample resampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth (embedded or curated) sub-network is available, since sensitivity against a known target cannot be computed When the goal is detecting modules in a single real dataset rather than comparing competing detection methods on simulated replicates

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is inferring activities on a single new dataset rather than comparing method performance across a perturbation benchmark collection When perturbation ground truth (which regulator was perturbed per experiment) is unavailable, since the response vector depends on perturbation labels When analyzing phospho-proteomic perturbations — that requires the analogous run_php_bench.R pipeline rather than the RNA benchmark

skills.name: benchmark-sensitivity-precision-f1-computation
skills.search_text: benchmark-sensitivity-precision-f1-computation Use when comparing fcircRNA or fusion-junction detection tools against a simulated ground truth and you need sensitivity, precision, and F1 per tool to demonstrate ity (e.g., INTEGRATE-Circ 87.3% sensitivity vs Fcirc 57.1%). skills.summary: Benchmark fcircRNA detection tools on simulated RNA-Seq data by matching each tool's backsplice calls to ground-truth fcircRNAs and computing sensitivity, precision, and F1 per tool across all iterations, as done for INTEGRATE-Circ vs Fcirc/Acfs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real (non-simulated) tumors or cell lines with no ground-truth fcircRNA set — sensitivity and precision cannot be computed without known backsplices; use orthogonal RT-PCR validation instead The goal is detecting fcircRNAs in a new dataset rather than comparing tools' accuracy — run INTEGRATE-Circ directly rather than building a benchmark table Evaluating linear gene-fusion (non-circular) detection only, where fcircRNA-specific backsplice matching to ground truth does not apply

skills.description: Use when a miRNA/small RNA detection method must be benchmarked against a reference truth set (e.g., SRP120169) and you need quantitative sensitivity/specificity, including per-abundance-tier performance.

skills.search_text: benchmark-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation Use when a miRNA/small RNA detection method must be benchmarked against a reference truth set (e.g., SRP120169) and you need quantitative sensitivity/specificity, including per-abundance-tier performance. Input is already a validated detection list with known TP/FP counts — compute metrics directly instead of re-running the pipeline No external reference truth set exists for the samples, making TP/FN (and thus sensitivity) undefined The goal is tool runtime or diversity comparison (e.g., COMPSRA vs exceRpt per-sample minutes or RNA-type counts) rather than detection accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates a small RNA-seq detection pipeline (e.g., COMPSRA) against an external reference dataset by computing sensitivity and specificity of detected miRNAs, both overall and for abundance-restricted subsets such as the top 30% most abundant miRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Validates a small RNA-seq detection pipeline (e.g., COMPSRA) against an external reference dataset by computing sensitivity and specificity of detected miRNAs, both overall and for abundance-restricted subsets such as the top 30% most abundant miRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a validated detection list with known TP/FP counts — compute metrics directly instead of re-running the pipeline No external reference truth set exists for the samples, making TP/FN (and thus sensitivity) undefined The goal is tool runtime or diversity comparison (e.g., COMPSRA vs exceRpt per-sample minutes or RNA-type counts) rather than detection accuracy

skills.description: Use when a paper reports head-to-head quantitative scores (ARI/ASW/kBET) for multiple integration methods on a shared dataset and the goal is to regenerate that table from raw data within rounding tolerance.
skills.name: benchmark-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-table-reproduction Use when a paper reports head-to-head quantitative scores (ARI/ASW/kBET) for multiple integration methods on a shared dataset and the goal is to regenerate that table from raw data within rounding tolerance. The task is a novel benchmark design rather than reproducing a published table — the paper's fixed epochs, seeds, and scripts must be reused, not re-tuned The source datasets lack gold-standard cell-type annotations, since ARI/ASW cannot be computed against 'cell_types' The dataset requires multiple categorical batch variables or multi-omic integration, which the focal model does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduce a published benchmark comparison table (e.g., Supplementary Table 7 of the scETM paper) by retraining the focal method and all competing integrative methods on the same dataset and assembling their clustering and batch-mixing metrics into a single comparison table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Reproduce a published benchmark comparison table (e.g., Supplementary Table 7 of the scETM paper) by retraining the focal method and all competing integrative methods on the same dataset and assembling their clustering and batch-mixing metrics into a single comparison table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a novel benchmark design rather than reproducing a published table — the paper's fixed epochs, seeds, and scripts must be reused, not re-tuned The source datasets lack gold-standard cell-type annotations, since ARI/ASW cannot be computed against 'cell_types' The dataset requires multiple categorical batch variables or multi-omic integration, which the focal model does not support

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix with a known stem/progenitor compartment and need to compare ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR and CytoTRACE scores across cell types to judge which tool identifies stem cells correctly.
skills.name: benchmark-tool-score-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-tool-score-comparison Use when you have an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix with a known stem/progenitor compartment and need to compare ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR and CytoTRACE scores across cell types to judge which tool identifies stem cells correctly. Input scRNA-seq data lacks annotated cell-type labels, so per-type score averages and the stem-cell ranking check cannot be computed The dataset has no stem/progenitor compartment to benchmark against (e.g. purely differentiated tissue), making the 'stem cells rank highest' acceptance check meaningless The goal is trajectory inference from stem-cell origins rather than comparing pluripotency scoring methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark pluripotency/stemness scoring methods (ORIGINS differentiation activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on annotated healthy human scRNA-seq datasets by computing per-cell scores and comparing per-cell-type averages. It exists to verify whether each tool actually ranks the known stem compartment highest. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Benchmark pluripotency/stemness scoring methods (ORIGINS differentiation activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on annotated healthy human scRNA-seq datasets by computing per-cell scores and comparing per-cell-type averages. It exists to verify whether each tool actually ranks the known stem compartment highest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input scRNA-seq data lacks annotated cell-type labels, so per-type score averages and the stem-cell ranking check cannot be computed The dataset has no stem/progenitor compartment to benchmark against (e.g. purely differentiated tissue), making the 'stem cells rank highest' acceptance check meaningless The goal is trajectory inference from stem-cell origins rather than comparing pluripotency scoring methods

skills.description: Use when you have HTO count matrices from multiple published or in-house datasets plus benchmark/simulated references, and need to know if real data quality (component overlap) is comparable to benchmarks or degraded enough that demultiplexing results are method-sensitive.
skills.name: benchmark-versus-real-dataset-comparison
skills.search_text: benchmark-versus-real-dataset-comparison Use when you have HTO count matrices from multiple published or in-house datasets plus benchmark/simulated references, and need to know if real data quality (component overlap) is comparable to benchmarks or degraded enough that demultiplexing results are method-sensitive. The goal is to actually demultiplex droplets into sample assignments rather than to quantify HTO data quality via component overlap. The input lacks HTO count matrices (only the RNA gene-count matrix is available), so no mixture models over HTO counts can be fit. No benchmark or simulated reference datasets are available, so ovs values cannot be placed on a comparative quality scale. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies HTO data quality of real published datasets by fitting demuxmix negative binomial regression mixture models and computing the overlap score (ovs), then comparing those ovs values against benchmark datasets and simulated low-quality levels to judge whether demultiplexing method choice will matter. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Quantifies HTO data quality of real published datasets by fitting demuxmix negative binomial regression mixture models and computing the overlap score (ovs), then comparing those ovs values against benchmark datasets and simulated low-quality levels to judge whether demultiplexing method choice will matter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to actually demultiplex droplets into sample assignments rather than to quantify HTO data quality via component overlap. The input lacks HTO count matrices (only the RNA gene-count matrix is available), so no mixture models over HTO counts can be fit. No benchmark or simulated reference datasets are available, so ovs values cannot be placed on a comparative quality scale.

skills.description: Use when a differential expression meta-analysis yields one combined P value per gene per cell subtype and you must control multiplicity before ranking marker genes (e.g., recovering Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Cck, Htr3a as subtype discriminators).
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when a differential expression meta-analysis yields one combined P value per gene per cell subtype and you must control multiplicity before ranking marker genes (e.g., recovering Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Cck, Htr3a as subtype discriminators). P values are already FDR-adjusted (q-values); re-applying BH would over-correct and shrink the marker list There is no multiple-testing family — e.g., a single pre-specified marker test rather than per-gene P values across the transcriptome per subtype Expression is raw counts or normalized values from non-interneuron datasets where the per-study Wilcoxon + Fisher's meta-analysis design does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to per-gene meta-analysis P values (Fisher's method combined across GSE60361 and GSE71585) from subtype-vs-rest Wilcoxon differential expression tests, retaining genes with FDR < 0.001 and log2FC > 2 to build marker_genes_fdr001.csv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to per-gene meta-analysis P values (Fisher's method combined across GSE60361 and GSE71585) from subtype-vs-rest Wilcoxon differential expression tests, retaining genes with FDR < 0.001 and log2FC > 2 to build marker_genes_fdr001.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: P values are already FDR-adjusted (q-values); re-applying BH would over-correct and shrink the marker list There is no multiple-testing family — e.g., a single pre-specified marker test rather than per-gene P values across the transcriptome per subtype Expression is raw counts or normalized values from non-interneuron datasets where the per-study Wilcoxon + Fisher's meta-analysis design does not apply

skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when many candidate biomarkers (e.g., 16 gene expression programs or transferred qPHATE coordinates) each yield a Cox regression treatment-effect contrast and the family of p-values must be FDR-corrected before declaring significance. When only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested (no multiplicity), where a plain p-value threshold suffices When the goal is family-wise error rate control rather than FDR control (e.g., Bonferroni/Holm is required instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to the family of treatment-effect coefficient-difference tests in the CALGB/SWOG 80405 mCRC analysis, so that multiple Cox-model biomarker contrasts (e.g., qNMF GEPs and qPHATE-derived biomarkers) are assessed at FDR < 0.05 rather than raw p-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to the family of treatment-effect coefficient-difference tests in the CALGB/SWOG 80405 mCRC analysis, so that multiple Cox-model biomarker contrasts (e.g., qNMF GEPs and qPHATE-derived biomarkers) are assessed at FDR < 0.05 rather than raw p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested (no multiplicity), where a plain p-value threshold suffices When the goal is family-wise error rate control rather than FDR control (e.g., Bonferroni/Holm is required instead)

skills.description: Use when you have raw per-gene p-values from a two-group differential expression test (e.g. a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between user-defined cell groups) and need FDR-corrected values before ranking marker genes.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when you have raw per-gene p-values from a two-group differential expression test (e.g. a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between user-defined cell groups) and need FDR-corrected values before ranking marker genes. No multiple testing context exists — e.g. a single pre-specified gene rather than genome/transcriptome-wide testing You only need uncorrected p-values to report the test itself rather than to rank/select marker genes The downstream tool already performs its own multiple-testing correction internally (re-adjusting would double-correct) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment to per-gene p-values from the two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum (Wilcox) test that CellexalVR uses to identify differentially expressed genes for its in-session heatmaps, so marker gene ranking controls the false discovery rate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment to per-gene p-values from the two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum (Wilcox) test that CellexalVR uses to identify differentially expressed genes for its in-session heatmaps, so marker gene ranking controls the false discovery rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No multiple testing context exists — e.g. a single pre-specified gene rather than genome/transcriptome-wide testing You only need uncorrected p-values to report the test itself rather than to rank/select marker genes The downstream tool already performs its own multiple-testing correction internally (re-adjusting would double-correct)

skills.description: Use when you have raw p-values from multiple testing methods (e.g., progressionTest, fateSelectionTest, DAseq, milo) on the same features/genes and need binary differential calls at a controlled false discovery rate of 5% for downstream performance evaluation.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when you have raw p-values from multiple testing methods (e.g., progressionTest, fateSelectionTest, DAseq, milo) on the same features/genes and need binary differential calls at a controlled false discovery rate of 5% for downstream performance evaluation. When a per-test pre-specified significance threshold (e.g., nominal p < 0.05) is required rather than family-wise FDR control across a large gene set When the p-values are not from independent or positively dependent families where BH's assumptions are intended, and stronger (e.g., BY) or weaker correction is explicitly mandated by the protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) multiple-testing correction at a 5% FDR threshold to raw p-values from trajectory-aware tests (condiments progressionTest, fateSelectionTest) and differential abundance methods (DAseq, milo), converting them into binary differential calls for benchmark scoring against dyngen ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) multiple-testing correction at a 5% FDR threshold to raw p-values from trajectory-aware tests (condiments progressionTest, fateSelectionTest) and differential abundance methods (DAseq, milo), converting them into binary differential calls for benchmark scoring against dyngen ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a per-test pre-specified significance threshold (e.g., nominal p < 0.05) is required rather than family-wise FDR control across a large gene set When the p-values are not from independent or positively dependent families where BH's assumptions are intended, and stronger (e.g., BY) or weaker correction is explicitly mandated by the protocol

skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when a gene-list enrichment run (E.PAGE compute/compute_sets over the curated 522-module, 25,789-gene database) produces many raw hypergeometric p-values that must be adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing before filtering significant environmental modules. skills.summary: Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate method to adjust raw Fisher exact (hypergeometric) p-values from E.PAGE environmental gene-module enrichment, yielding p_adj values used to call statistically enriched modules (e.g. infection, cigarette smoking, toxic-chemical categories).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is joint or interaction odds ratios between gene–environment pairs — the article notes these statistical tests are not yet included in E.PAGE Input data are SNPs, copy number variants, or DNA methylations rather than a differentially expressed gene list — E.PAGE's BH-corrected hypergeometric test does not cover these genetic data types Only a single pre-specified gene set/module is tested, so there is no multiple-testing family to correct

skills.description: Use when testing differential regulatory relations between two conditions from paired single-cell data and needing calibrated p-values/FDR for the likelihood ratio statistic, especially when the standard Chi-square null appears anti-conservative.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-estimation
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-estimation Use when testing differential regulatory relations between two conditions from paired single-cell data and needing calibrated p-values/FDR for the likelihood ratio statistic, especially when the standard Chi-square null appears anti-conservative. When testing differential regulation across multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg does not yet accommodate multiple donors per condition When the likelihood ratio statistics are already confirmed to be well calibrated under the asymptotic Chi-square null and no null simulation is available When the analysis is not comparative (single-condition regulatory inference, e.g. the PECA-style context-specific network setting) and no differential-regulation LR statistic exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes p-values and controls false discovery rate for the sc-compReg likelihood ratio statistic that tests differential regulatory relations between two linked subpopulations, comparing a Chi-square (df=3) asymptotic null against an empirically fitted Gamma null with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Computes p-values and controls false discovery rate for the sc-compReg likelihood ratio statistic that tests differential regulatory relations between two linked subpopulations, comparing a Chi-square (df=3) asymptotic null against an empirically fitted Gamma null with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing differential regulation across multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg does not yet accommodate multiple donors per condition When the likelihood ratio statistics are already confirmed to be well calibrated under the asymptotic Chi-square null and no null simulation is available When the analysis is not comparative (single-condition regulatory inference, e.g. the PECA-style context-specific network setting) and no differential-regulation LR statistic exists

skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction Use when many parallel hypothesis tests must be thresholded with false-discovery-rate control — e.g., hundreds of GO over-representation tests on top-ranked communities per donor per time point — and an adjusted-p (BH FDR 0.05) significance call is required. skills.when_to_use_negative: The event table already carries a qval column from a prior BH pass — re-adjusting adjusted values would double-correct and shrink the significant set below 116 (GM12878) / 91-143 (Geuvadis populations) You need family-wise error rate control (e.g., a single genomewide claim) rather than expected-false-discovery control across thousands of ASAS event-SNP pairs P-values come from a method whose assumptions are broken (e.g., the rMATS paired model, where unreliable correlation-parameter estimation can inflate p-values and thus distort the BH ranking)
