skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-adjustment Use when a hypothesis-testing co-expression method (CS-CORE, Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) yields one p-value per gene pair across a p x p matrix, and the network must be thresholded or PR curves computed. No hypothesis test p-values are available (e.g., methods producing only point correlation estimates without inference, or clustering/enrichment steps already operating on a binarized network) A local (per-pair) rather than global FDR control is required, since BH controls the overall false discovery rate across all gene-pair tests jointly http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment applied to the large family of gene-pair p-values produced by co-expression hypothesis tests (e.g., CS-CORE), to control false positives and binarize the inferred co-expression network at a 0.05 threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustment applied to the large family of gene-pair p-values produced by co-expression hypothesis tests (e.g., CS-CORE), to control false positives and binarize the inferred co-expression network at a 0.05 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No hypothesis test p-values are available (e.g., methods producing only point correlation estimates without inference, or clustering/enrichment steps already operating on a binarized network) A local (per-pair) rather than global FDR control is required, since BH controls the overall false discovery rate across all gene-pair tests jointly

skills.description: Use when a single analysis produces many pathway-enrichment p-values (e.g. 100 scETM topics tested against MSigDB Canonical Pathways or PsyGeNET gene sets) and significant topic-pathway associations must be controlled for false discovery.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a single analysis produces many pathway-enrichment p-values (e.g. 100 scETM topics tested against MSigDB Canonical Pathways or PsyGeNET gene sets) and significant topic-pathway associations must be controlled for false discovery. Testing a single pre-specified hypothesis (one topic against one pathway), where no family-wise correction is needed Input p-values are not from an exchangeable permutation structure (e.g. dependent ad-hoc scores without permutation calibration), where BH FDR assumptions are questionable Ranking topics purely exploratorily without making any significance claim — correction would only add conservative distortion http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate correction to the large family of topic-by-pathway p-values produced by permutation-based GSEA of scETM-learned topics, converting raw enrichment p-values into BH-adjusted q-values used to declare biologically meaningful topic-pathway associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate correction to the large family of topic-by-pathway p-values produced by permutation-based GSEA of scETM-learned topics, converting raw enrichment p-values into BH-adjusted q-values used to declare biologically meaningful topic-pathway associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Testing a single pre-specified hypothesis (one topic against one pathway), where no family-wise correction is needed Input p-values are not from an exchangeable permutation structure (e.g. dependent ad-hoc scores without permutation calibration), where BH FDR assumptions are questionable Ranking topics purely exploratorily without making any significance claim — correction would only add conservative distortion

skills.description: Use when a gene-set activity analysis tests many gene sets simultaneously and raw empirical p-values (e.g. ppv L1, ppv Median Exp from rROMA) must be adjusted before classifying modules as significant.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a gene-set activity analysis tests many gene sets simultaneously and raw empirical p-values (e.g. ppv L1, ppv Median Exp from rROMA) must be adjusted before classifying modules as significant. Only a single gene set / single hypothesis is tested, so no multiplicity correction is needed The p-values are not independent or positively correlated in ways violating BH assumptions and FDR control is not the desired error criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply Benjamini and Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to the empirical ppv p-values that rROMA computes for each gene set (overdispersion via L1, shift via Median Exp), yielding q-values that control for the many gene sets tested in parallel (e.g. 50 MSigDB Hallmark sets). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini and Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to the empirical ppv p-values that rROMA computes for each gene set (overdispersion via L1, shift via Median Exp), yielding q-values that control for the many gene sets tested in parallel (e.g. 50 MSigDB Hallmark sets).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single gene set / single hypothesis is tested, so no multiplicity correction is needed The p-values are not independent or positively correlated in ways violating BH assumptions and FDR control is not the desired error criterion

skills.description: Use when many paired statistical tests (e.g., matched perturbed-vs-control Wilcoxon tests over hundreds of TF-gene edges) have been run and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted before calling significant edges.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when many paired statistical tests (e.g., matched perturbed-vs-control Wilcoxon tests over hundreds of TF-gene edges) have been run and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted before calling significant edges. Only a single hypothesis test is being run per comparison (no multiplicity, no correction needed) The goal is per-TF family-wise error control rather than FDR across the full edge set The expression data are not matched perturbed/control samples from the same fixed batch, so paired tests are inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to Wilcoxon test p-values across all TF-gene edges from GRouNdGAN in silico TF knockout experiments, so edge significance (adjusted p < 0.05) can be counted to quantify how much of an imposed GRN is causally enforced in simulated cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to Wilcoxon test p-values across all TF-gene edges from GRouNdGAN in silico TF knockout experiments, so edge significance (adjusted p < 0.05) can be counted to quantify how much of an imposed GRN is causally enforced in simulated cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single hypothesis test is being run per comparison (no multiplicity, no correction needed) The goal is per-TF family-wise error control rather than FDR across the full edge set The expression data are not matched perturbed/control samples from the same fixed batch, so paired tests are inappropriate

skills.description: Use when a gene-wise statistical test (e.g., limma moderated t-statistics across 46 cases and 23 controls) yields thousands of raw P-values that must be FDR-adjusted before ranking seeds or thresholding DEGs.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a gene-wise statistical test (e.g., limma moderated t-statistics across 46 cases and 23 controls) yields thousands of raw P-values that must be FDR-adjusted before ranking seeds or thresholding DEGs. Gene IDs have not yet been normalized/converted (e.g., Entrez to symbols via org.Hs.eg.db) — correct the P-values only after gene-level testing is finalized The analysis requires family-wise error rate control rather than FDR control (BH controls false discovery rate, not per-test or FWER error) P-values come from a small pre-specified hypothesis set (e.g., a handful of pathways) where no genome-wide multiple-testing burden exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Adjust gene-level differential expression P-values for multiple testing with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) so that per-gene results (e.g., from limma empirical Bayes fits of GSE172114 COVID-19 critical vs non-critical RNA-seq) are controlled for false discovery and can serve as seed P-values for downstream active subnetwork detection and SEMtree analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Adjust gene-level differential expression P-values for multiple testing with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) so that per-gene results (e.g., from limma empirical Bayes fits of GSE172114 COVID-19 critical vs non-critical RNA-seq) are controlled for false discovery and can serve as seed P-values for downstream active subnetwork detection and SEMtree analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene IDs have not yet been normalized/converted (e.g., Entrez to symbols via org.Hs.eg.db) — correct the P-values only after gene-level testing is finalized The analysis requires family-wise error rate control rather than FDR control (BH controls false discovery rate, not per-test or FWER error) P-values come from a small pre-specified hypothesis set (e.g., a handful of pathways) where no genome-wide multiple-testing burden exists

skills.description: Use when many gene-set (GO_BP/KEGG) enrichment tests are run in parallel — e.g., one test per detected RGM or SCENIC regulon on the hESC, mESC, or mHSC lineage datasets — and per-module significance must be assessed with a threshold that accounts for multiple testing.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when many gene-set (GO_BP/KEGG) enrichment tests are run in parallel — e.g., one test per detected RGM or SCENIC regulon on the hESC, mESC, or mHSC lineage datasets — and per-module significance must be assessed with a threshold that accounts for multiple testing. Only a single enrichment test is performed — no multiplicity exists, so a plain p-value cutoff suffices. The goal is per-gene differential-expression testing rather than per-module gene-set enrichment significance; other correction contexts may need different family-wise structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate correction to per-module GO_BP and KEGG enrichment p-values when benchmarking regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) against SCENIC regulons, so that significance calls across many tested modules are controlled and enrichment precision (fraction of modules with BH-adjusted p <= 0.05) is computed fairly per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate correction to per-module GO_BP and KEGG enrichment p-values when benchmarking regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) against SCENIC regulons, so that significance calls across many tested modules are controlled and enrichment precision (fraction of modules with BH-adjusted p <= 0.05) is computed fairly per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single enrichment test is performed — no multiplicity exists, so a plain p-value cutoff suffices. The goal is per-gene differential-expression testing rather than per-module gene-set enrichment significance; other correction contexts may need different family-wise structures.

skills.description: Use when you have thousands of per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA) chi-square p-values from a scisorseqr region-vs-region comparison and need FDR-controlled DIE calls with an effect-size (delta-PI) filter.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when you have thousands of per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA) chi-square p-values from a scisorseqr region-vs-region comparison and need FDR-controlled DIE calls with an effect-size (delta-PI) filter. When testing exon-wise inclusion/exclusion, where tests are dependent — use Benjamini–Yekutieli correction instead, as the paper does for the 31-gene exon result When input is raw per-gene isoform counts rather than per-gene chi-square test p-values; the correction operates on the p-value/dPI table, not on the counts directly When only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested and no multiple-testing correction is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction to the per-gene 2x2 chi-square p-values produced by scisorseqr's DiffSplicingAnalysis, then combine FDR <= 0.05 with a delta-PI >= 0.1 effect-size cutoff to call differentially isoform-expressed genes between HIPP and PFC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction to the per-gene 2x2 chi-square p-values produced by scisorseqr's DiffSplicingAnalysis, then combine FDR <= 0.05 with a delta-PI >= 0.1 effect-size cutoff to call differentially isoform-expressed genes between HIPP and PFC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing exon-wise inclusion/exclusion, where tests are dependent — use Benjamini–Yekutieli correction instead, as the paper does for the 31-gene exon result When input is raw per-gene isoform counts rather than per-gene chi-square test p-values; the correction operates on the p-value/dPI table, not on the counts directly When only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested and no multiple-testing correction is needed

skills.description: Use when many hypothesis tests (e.g., GSEA on 22 KEGG-derived LR pathway sets per factor) produce raw P-values per condition, and FDR-controlled adjusted P-values are needed for a factor-by-pathway results table.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when many hypothesis tests (e.g., GSEA on 22 KEGG-derived LR pathway sets per factor) produce raw P-values per condition, and FDR-controlled adjusted P-values are needed for a factor-by-pathway results table. Only one hypothesis test (single pathway set, single factor) is performed — no correction is needed GSEA P-values have already been FDR-adjusted or the GSEA tool already reports q-values you intend to use Input is enrichment scores (NES) without raw P-values — BH correction operates on nominal P-values, not on effect-size statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to raw P-values from pathway-level GSEA of Tensor-cell2cell factor loadings, yielding adjusted P-values that control the expected fraction of false positives across the multiple KEGG-derived LR pathway sets tested per factor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to raw P-values from pathway-level GSEA of Tensor-cell2cell factor loadings, yielding adjusted P-values that control the expected fraction of false positives across the multiple KEGG-derived LR pathway sets tested per factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one hypothesis test (single pathway set, single factor) is performed — no correction is needed GSEA P-values have already been FDR-adjusted or the GSEA tool already reports q-values you intend to use Input is enrichment scores (NES) without raw P-values — BH correction operates on nominal P-values, not on effect-size statistics

skills.description: Use when hundreds of module-vs-term hypergeometric tests are performed (e.g., 137 MCA GEPs against GO/MP gene sets) and enriched terms must be reported with BH-adjusted p-values alongside raw p-values and enrichment ratios.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when hundreds of module-vs-term hypergeometric tests are performed (e.g., 137 MCA GEPs against GO/MP gene sets) and enriched terms must be reported with BH-adjusted p-values alongside raw p-values and enrichment ratios. You are controlling FDR for the SingleCellGGM network edges themselves, where the paper uses the permutation-based fdr_control function on permutated edges rather than BH on enrichment p-values Gene sets are few and pre-specified such that no large family of simultaneous tests exists, making BH adjustment unnecessary or overly conservative Input genes are not Ensembl mouse gene IDs; ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis supports only Ensembl gene IDs unless the symbol-variant GEP file is used Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate adjustment to hypergeometric over-representation p-values when testing many gene co-expression modules (GEPs) against GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) gene sets, so that enriched terms (e.g., 'abnormal NK cell physiology' in GEP M83) are called at a controlled FDR rather than raw p <= 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate adjustment to hypergeometric over-representation p-values when testing many gene co-expression modules (GEPs) against GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) gene sets, so that enriched terms (e.g., 'abnormal NK cell physiology' in GEP M83) are called at a controlled FDR rather than raw p <= 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are controlling FDR for the SingleCellGGM network edges themselves, where the paper uses the permutation-based fdr_control function on permutated edges rather than BH on enrichment p-values Gene sets are few and pre-specified such that no large family of simultaneous tests exists, making BH adjustment unnecessary or overly conservative Input genes are not Ensembl mouse gene IDs; ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis supports only Ensembl gene IDs unless the symbol-variant GEP file is used

skills.description: Use when NeuronChat (or analogous permutation-based cell-cell communication inference) has produced raw per-interaction p-values across many ligand-receptor pairs and you need FDR-controlled significance calls before retaining or zeroing links.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when NeuronChat (or analogous permutation-based cell-cell communication inference) has produced raw per-interaction p-values across many ligand-receptor pairs and you need FDR-controlled significance calls before retaining or zeroing links. The task tests a single hypothesis or very few interactions, where family-wise or uncorrected testing suffices and BH gain is negligible P-values come from a method without a permutation-based null (e.g., spatial proximity enrichment scores already thresholded by spatial proximity, which is a separate NeuronChat filter) The communication strengths need to remain continuous for downstream net_aggregation without thresholding at p<0.05 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction to the p-values from NeuronChat's permutation test so that inferred communication links are called significant at FDR-controlled p<0.05, with non-significant links zeroed out. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction to the p-values from NeuronChat's permutation test so that inferred communication links are called significant at FDR-controlled p<0.05, with non-significant links zeroed out.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task tests a single hypothesis or very few interactions, where family-wise or uncorrected testing suffices and BH gain is negligible P-values come from a method without a permutation-based null (e.g., spatial proximity enrichment scores already thresholded by spatial proximity, which is a separate NeuronChat filter) The communication strengths need to remain continuous for downstream net_aggregation without thresholding at p<0.05

skills.description: Use when a tncRNA count matrix with ≥3 biological replicates per condition is being tested for differential expression across many tncRNA loci and per-locus p-values must be corrected for multiple testing before significance calling.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a tncRNA count matrix with ≥3 biological replicates per condition is being tested for differential expression across many tncRNA loci and per-locus p-values must be corrected for multiple testing before significance calling. Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or a single-hypothesis test (only one locus tested), where correction would be meaningless Sample sets lack at least three biological replicates for both control and treatment, so DESeq2 dispersion estimation is unreliable The goal is tncRNA discovery/quantification from raw sRNA-seq FASTQ rather than differential expression testing of an existing count matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to Wald-test p-values when calling differentially expressed tncRNAs with DESeq2, so that thousands of tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1s, tRNA halves) can be tested simultaneously without inflating false positives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to Wald-test p-values when calling differentially expressed tncRNAs with DESeq2, so that thousands of tRNA-derived non-coding RNAs (tRF-5s, tRF-3s, tRF-1s, tRNA halves) can be tested simultaneously without inflating false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a table of adjusted p-values or a single-hypothesis test (only one locus tested), where correction would be meaningless Sample sets lack at least three biological replicates for both control and treatment, so DESeq2 dispersion estimation is unreliable The goal is tncRNA discovery/quantification from raw sRNA-seq FASTQ rather than differential expression testing of an existing count matrix

skills.description: Use when many parallel significance tests have been run (e.g. one hypergeometric GO over-representation test per bicluster across 151 UniBic biclusters) and enrichment calls must control the false discovery rate before tallying proportions.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when many parallel significance tests have been run (e.g. one hypergeometric GO over-representation test per bicluster across 151 UniBic biclusters) and enrichment calls must control the false discovery rate before tallying proportions. The input is a set of bicluster p-values from a single test per hypothesis already corrected upstream — a second BH pass would over-correct. The analysis goal is bicluster discovery itself (the UniBic LCS/index-matrix steps), not post-hoc enrichment significance calling. Rank-based or resampling FDR methods are specifically required and the BH assumption of valid raw p-values across tests cannot be met. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate adjustment to the per-bicluster GO enrichment p-values computed with the GOstats hypergeometric test, so that UniBic biclusters on the GDS datasets can be called GO-enriched at adjusted p < 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) false-discovery-rate adjustment to the per-bicluster GO enrichment p-values computed with the GOstats hypergeometric test, so that UniBic biclusters on the GDS datasets can be called GO-enriched at adjusted p < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a set of bicluster p-values from a single test per hypothesis already corrected upstream — a second BH pass would over-correct. The analysis goal is bicluster discovery itself (the UniBic LCS/index-matrix steps), not post-hoc enrichment significance calling. Rank-based or resampling FDR methods are specifically required and the BH assumption of valid raw p-values across tests cannot be met.

skills.description: Use when a per-cluster marker gene list has been tested against cell-type gene sets (e.g. easyct with test='fisher') and the family of candidate cell-type p-values within each cluster must be FDR-adjusted before ranking annotations.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-adjustment
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-adjustment Use when a per-cluster marker gene list has been tested against cell-type gene sets (e.g. easyct with test='fisher') and the family of candidate cell-type p-values within each cluster must be FDR-adjusted before ranking annotations. Input is not a family of p-values from a single hypothesis family (e.g. you need per-gene DE q-values rather than per-cell-type overrepresentation p-values) The annotation route is GSEA (easyct with test='gsea'), where ranking comes from enrichment scores rather than Fisher test p-values Adjusting across all clusters pooled together — the correction family is the candidate cell types within one cluster, not the whole marker table http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benjamini–Hochberg multiple-testing correction applied to the modified Fisher's exact test p-values in EasyCellType, computed within each cell cluster across candidate CellMarker cell types, so that overrepresentation calls are ranked by marker expression significance rather than raw overlap size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Benjamini–Hochberg multiple-testing correction applied to the modified Fisher's exact test p-values in EasyCellType, computed within each cell cluster across candidate CellMarker cell types, so that overrepresentation calls are ranked by marker expression significance rather than raw overlap size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a family of p-values from a single hypothesis family (e.g. you need per-gene DE q-values rather than per-cell-type overrepresentation p-values) The annotation route is GSEA (easyct with test='gsea'), where ranking comes from enrichment scores rather than Fisher test p-values Adjusting across all clusters pooled together — the correction family is the candidate cell types within one cluster, not the whole marker table

skills.description: Use when many per-gene hypothesis tests (e.g. Fisher's exact tests on gene-cluster absence/presence per lifestyle) yield a vector of p-values that must be FDR-corrected before ranking candidate lifestyle-associated genes.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-correction Use when many per-gene hypothesis tests (e.g. Fisher's exact tests on gene-cluster absence/presence per lifestyle) yield a vector of p-values that must be FDR-corrected before ranking candidate lifestyle-associated genes. The analysis calls only a handful of pre-specified tests rather than screening all gene clusters genome-wide, where FDR correction is not the intended multiplicity framework The downstream pLAG decision relies solely on the prevalence (>70%) and log2 fold change (>2) thresholds and does not use statistical ranking, making correction unnecessary Input is already a table of adjusted p-values — re-applying p.adjust() would double-correct http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) FDR correction to p-values from per-gene-cluster Fisher's exact tests when detecting lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) with bacLIFE's analytical module, so that thousands of simultaneous gene-cluster tests across lifestyles can be ranked under a controlled false discovery rate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) FDR correction to p-values from per-gene-cluster Fisher's exact tests when detecting lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) with bacLIFE's analytical module, so that thousands of simultaneous gene-cluster tests across lifestyles can be ranked under a controlled false discovery rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis calls only a handful of pre-specified tests rather than screening all gene clusters genome-wide, where FDR correction is not the intended multiplicity framework The downstream pLAG decision relies solely on the prevalence (>70%) and log2 fold change (>2) thresholds and does not use statistical ranking, making correction unnecessary Input is already a table of adjusted p-values — re-applying p.adjust() would double-correct

skills.description: Use when an analysis reduces to binary directional calls per gene or exon — TSS shift direction in pairwise DIE comparisons, or same/opposite delta-PSI between single-cell and spatial measurements — and an exact enrichment p-value against a 50/50 null is required.
skills.name: bernoulli-direction-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: bernoulli-direction-enrichment-testing Use when an analysis reduces to binary directional calls per gene or exon — TSS shift direction in pairwise DIE comparisons, or same/opposite delta-PSI between single-cell and spatial measurements — and an exact enrichment p-value against a 50/50 null is required. When effect magnitudes, not just direction, are the quantity of interest — the Bernoulli test discards delta-PSI magnitude and must be complemented by Pearson correlation of continuous values When the underlying categories are not equiprobable under the null (directions a priori biased, e.g. annotational upstream-TSS preference), so the p = 0.5 binomial assumption is violated When events are independent tests of magnitude rather than binary concordance — use the pairwise DIE fraction framework (deltaPI = 0.1) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 An exact two-sided Bernoulli/binomial test that assesses whether binary directional outcomes in isoform regulation data (e.g. upstream vs downstream TSS shifts, same vs opposite delta-PSI direction) are enriched against a 50% null expectation, as used to validate the CPE upstream-TSS signature (70/93 genes, p = 3e-7) and single-cell-vs-spatial delta-PSI concordance (85% of 40 exons, p <= 3.5e-6). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: An exact two-sided Bernoulli/binomial test that assesses whether binary directional outcomes in isoform regulation data (e.g. upstream vs downstream TSS shifts, same vs opposite delta-PSI direction) are enriched against a 50% null expectation, as used to validate the CPE upstream-TSS signature (70/93 genes, p = 3e-7) and single-cell-vs-spatial delta-PSI concordance (85% of 40 exons, p <= 3.5e-6).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When effect magnitudes, not just direction, are the quantity of interest — the Bernoulli test discards delta-PSI magnitude and must be complemented by Pearson correlation of continuous values When the underlying categories are not equiprobable under the null (directions a priori biased, e.g. annotational upstream-TSS preference), so the p = 0.5 binomial assumption is violated When events are independent tests of magnitude rather than binary concordance — use the pairwise DIE fraction framework (deltaPI = 0.1) instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking single-cell clustering robustness on in silico mixtures (e.g., GM12878/K562) by injecting controlled dropout into expression E and openness O matrices at rates such as 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9.
skills.name: bernoulli-dropout-simulation-single-cell
skills.search_text: bernoulli-dropout-simulation-single-cell Use when benchmarking single-cell clustering robustness on in silico mixtures (e.g., GM12878/K562) by injecting controlled dropout into expression E and openness O matrices at rates such as 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw gene expression matrix that has not yet been converted into RWR diffusion distributions — build the Markov transition matrix and run RWR first. skills.search_text: bhattacharyya-kernel-feature-decomposition Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix with developmental stage labels must be embedded in low dimensions for pseudotime trajectory visualization, e.g. ordering mouse embryo cells across the 1-cell to 64-cell stages. The goal is branch/bifurcation detection rather than dimensionality reduction — use the companion RSKG step (z.get_branches) instead. The input has not been pre-processed into a gene expression matrix (e.g. raw reads or a dataset needing corrupted-gene removal first). Cells lack any ordering or stage information needed to validate the chronological placement of the embedding. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 BKFD is the manifold-learning dimensionality-reduction method at the core of DTFLOW: it represents each cell by a stationary distribution from random walk with restart, forms a Bhattacharyya kernel similarity matrix, and recovers a low-dimensional embedding of single-cell developmental trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is branch/bifurcation detection rather than dimensionality reduction — use the companion RSKG step (z.get_branches) instead. skills.description: Use when single-cell CITE-seq / ADT protein count distributions (after dsb step-I log(pseudocount 10) transformation and empty-droplet standardization) must be modeled with Gaussian mixtures and the number of mixture components needs a principled, per-cell choice.
skills.name: bic-based-model-order-selection
skills.search_text: bic-based-model-order-selection Use when single-cell CITE-seq / ADT protein count distributions (after dsb step-I log(pseudocount 10) transformation and empty-droplet standardization) must be modeled with Gaussian mixtures and the number of mixture components needs a principled, per-cell choice. Input is already fully dsb-denoised residual output (step-II output with technical component regressed out) rather than step-I ambient-corrected values — the mixture model is defined on the step-I transformed count of each cell. No empty droplets are available to define the background mean and standard deviation needed for step-I standardization, unless using the documented no-empty-drops variant. The goal is a single global distribution across cells (e.g., population-level clustering) rather than modeling the within-cell protein count distribution. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the optimal number of Gaussian mixture components (k) for modeling the distribution of dsb step-I ambient-corrected ADT values within each single cell by sweeping G = 1–6 with mclust and comparing BIC values per cell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Selects the optimal number of Gaussian mixture components (k) for modeling the distribution of dsb step-I ambient-corrected ADT values within each single cell by sweeping G = 1–6 with mclust and comparing BIC values per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already fully dsb-denoised residual output (step-II output with technical component regressed out) rather than step-I ambient-corrected values — the mixture model is defined on the step-I transformed count of each cell. No empty droplets are available to define the background mean and standard deviation needed for step-I standardization, unless using the documented no-empty-drops variant. The goal is a single global distribution across cells (e.g., population-level clustering) rather than modeling the within-cell protein count distribution.

skills.description: Use when fitting Gaussian mixture models to principal components of scCRISPR-seq control/perturbation expression data and the number of cell clusters K is unknown and must be chosen objectively.

skills.search_text: bic-cluster-number-selection Use when fitting Gaussian mixture models to principal components of scCRISPR-seq control/perturbation expression data and the number of cell clusters K is unknown and must be chosen objectively. The PC being modeled is unimodal (fails the multimodality/dip-test screen of pc_selection), so a Gaussian mixture with K >= 2 is not warranted. Cell clusters are expected to be so heterogeneous that the GMM assumption and the assumption of similar cellular responses across clusters fail, e.g. intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors. Selects the number of mixture components for the shared-K Gaussian mixture models fitted per infection-biased principal component in scDecouple, using Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) so that the control and perturbation groups are modeled with the same cluster number before EM estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Selects the number of mixture components for the shared-K Gaussian mixture models fitted per infection-biased principal component in scDecouple, using Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) so that the control and perturbation groups are modeled with the same cluster number before EM estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The PC being modeled is unimodal (fails the multimodality/dip-test screen of pc_selection), so a Gaussian mixture with K >= 2 is not warranted. Cell clusters are expected to be so heterogeneous that the GMM assumption and the assumption of similar cellular responses across clusters fail, e.g. intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors.

skills.description: Use when a run of UniBic/runibic has produced trend-preserving biclusters on expression data (e.g. the eight GDS datasets) and you must determine which biclusters are significantly GO-enriched and report their overall proportion.

skills.search_text: bicluster-gene-set-extraction Use when a run of UniBic/runibic has produced trend-preserving biclusters on expression data (e.g. the eight GDS datasets) and you must determine which biclusters are significantly GO-enriched and report their overall proportion. skills.summary: Extracts the gene members of trend-preserving biclusters (e.g. from a UniBic/runibic run) and tests each bicluster for GO over-representation with a hypergeometric test, Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05, to quantify what fraction of discovered biclusters are biologically meaningful.

skills.search_text: bicluster-relevance-recovery-evaluation Use when benchmarking a biclustering algorithm (e.g. UniBic via runibic) on synthetic matrices with implanted ground-truth biclusters and you need quantitative relevance/recovery scores to compare tools. skills.summary: Evaluates biclustering algorithm output by matching discovered biclusters against planted ground-truth biclusters using Jaccard-based relevance S(D,G) and recovery S(G,D) scores, as used to benchmark UniBic on synthetic trend-preserving matrices.

skills.description: Use when a biclustering run (e.g. UniBic on GEO microarray matrices like GDS589) has produced candidate trend-preserving biclusters and only statistically significant ones should be reported or counted downstream.
skills.name: bicluster-significance-filtering
skills.search_text: bicluster-significance-filtering Use when a biclustering run (e.g. UniBic on GEO microarray matrices like GDS589) has produced candidate trend-preserving biclusters and only statistically significant ones should be reported or counted downstream. The input is already a set of statistically validated/filtered biclusters with reported p-values — re-filtering would change reported counts. The goal is to enumerate ALL trend-preserving biclusters regardless of significance (e.g. exploratory seed inspection), not a significance-gated set. The clustering method is not UniBic-style trend-preserving biclustering and its significance model (based on techniques from reference 19 in the paper) does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 A statistical filtering step from the UniBic biclustering workflow that computes significance values for trend-preserving biclusters and retains only those with p-values < 0.05, reporting them in decreasing order of significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: A statistical filtering step from the UniBic biclustering workflow that computes significance values for trend-preserving biclusters and retains only those with p-values < 0.05, reporting them in decreasing order of significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a set of statistically validated/filtered biclusters with reported p-values — re-filtering would change reported counts. The goal is to enumerate ALL trend-preserving biclusters regardless of significance (e.g. exploratory seed inspection), not a significance-gated set. The clustering method is not UniBic-style trend-preserving biclustering and its significance model (based on techniques from reference 19 in the paper) does not apply.

skills.search_text: bilinear-neural-network-training Use when training an OnClass model on annotated scRNA-seq data (h5ad) with Cell Ontology-mapped labels, to obtain a saved model file that supports seen-term classification and unseen Cell Ontology term prediction. You already have a saved/pretrained OnClass model and only need annotations — use ProcessTestFeature with use_pretrain rather than retraining (OnClass ships a pre-trained model that annotates millions of cells in minutes). The target cell types are topologically identical unseen siblings (same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — OnClass explicitly cannot distinguish them. The train/test data have strong batch effects together with a large number of unseen cell types — batch-correction methods for this case are not yet developed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train OnClass's bilinear neural network, which projects single-cell transcriptomes and Cell Ontology terms into the same low-dimensional space so that cells can be scored against all ontology terms, including unseen ones. This is the model-building and training stage of the OnClass scRNA-seq annotation workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Train OnClass's bilinear neural network, which projects single-cell transcriptomes and Cell Ontology terms into the same low-dimensional space so that cells can be scored against all ontology terms, including unseen ones. This is the model-building and training stage of the OnClass scRNA-seq annotation workflow.

The train/test data have strong batch effects together with a large number of unseen cell types — batch-correction methods for this case are not yet developed.

skills.description: Use when a matrix has been imputed patch-wise (e.g., per-ROI histogram equalization in SERM) and the per-window outputs must be merged into a single globally consistent expression matrix before downstream analyses.
skills.name: bilinear-resampling-patch-consistency
skills.search_text: bilinear-resampling-patch-consistency Use when a matrix has been imputed patch-wise (e.g., per-ROI histogram equalization in SERM) and the per-window outputs must be merged into a single globally consistent expression matrix before downstream analyses. The expression matrix has not been divided into at least 4 ROIs and imputed patch-wise, so there are no overlapping ROI histograms to reconcile The observed data are a small genomic dataset where SERM's estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution, making the whole SERM imputation (and hence this final resampling) unreliable The input is already a single fully imputed matrix with consistent expression values across patches http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Final step of the SERM pipeline: after sliding-window histogram-equalization imputation of per-ROI patches, bilinear resampling merges all ROIs into one expression matrix whose values are globally consistent, computed as the average of four diagonal neighbors per element. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Final step of the SERM pipeline: after sliding-window histogram-equalization imputation of per-ROI patches, bilinear resampling merges all ROIs into one expression matrix whose values are globally consistent, computed as the average of four diagonal neighbors per element.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has not been divided into at least 4 ROIs and imputed patch-wise, so there are no overlapping ROI histograms to reconcile The observed data are a small genomic dataset where SERM's estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution, making the whole SERM imputation (and hence this final resampling) unreliable The input is already a single fully imputed matrix with consistent expression values across patches

skills.description: Use when building scFusion's deep-learning artifact-scoring stage: chimeric/fusion candidates extracted from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq alignments must be classified as technical artifacts vs. real fusions before final fusion calls.
skills.name: bilstm-artifact-scoring-model-training
skills.search_text: bilstm-artifact-scoring-model-training Use when building scFusion's deep-learning artifact-scoring stage: chimeric/fusion candidates extracted from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq alignments must be classified as technical artifacts vs. real fusions before final fusion calls. Input data is 10x Genomics rather than Smart-Seq scRNA-seq — scFusion is explicitly built for Smart-Seq data Input is bulk RNA-seq; scFusion's advantage relies on multiple single cells from one sample sharing the same fusion The target fusion is expected at low expression or is a rare fusion in a highly heterogeneous tumor sample, where all RNA-based methods (including scFusion) have reduced sensitivity/power http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Train and validate a bi-directional LSTM (TensorFlow/Keras) model in scFusion that scores scRNA-seq fusion candidates as technical chimeric artifacts, supplementing statistical and ad hoc filters. Trained on six public Smart-Seq datasets, it reaches median ROC AUC 0.884 and median PR AUPR 0.913, and assigns >90% of PCAWG fusions artifact scores <0.5. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Train and validate a bi-directional LSTM (TensorFlow/Keras) model in scFusion that scores scRNA-seq fusion candidates as technical chimeric artifacts, supplementing statistical and ad hoc filters. Trained on six public Smart-Seq datasets, it reaches median ROC AUC 0.884 and median PR AUPR 0.913, and assigns >90% of PCAWG fusions artifact scores <0.5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is 10x Genomics rather than Smart-Seq scRNA-seq — scFusion is explicitly built for Smart-Seq data Input is bulk RNA-seq; scFusion's advantage relies on multiple single cells from one sample sharing the same fusion The target fusion is expected at low expression or is a rare fusion in a highly heterogeneous tumor sample, where all RNA-based methods (including scFusion) have reduced sensitivity/power

skills.description: Use when you need to validate that the top edges (e.g. top 150 filtered edges) of a BoostDiff differential network show condition-specific correlation patterns in the original expression matrix, i.e. bimodal vs unimodal KDE distributions across target conditions.
skills.name: bimodal-distribution-assessment
skills.search_text: bimodal-distribution-assessment Use when you need to validate that the top edges (e.g. top 150 filtered edges) of a BoostDiff differential network show condition-specific correlation patterns in the original expression matrix, i.e. bimodal vs unimodal KDE distributions across target conditions. The network has not yet been filtered for target genes with a more predictive model for the target condition — run filter_network (p=3, n_top_edges=150) first, otherwise the top-edge set is undefined The expression matrices have fewer than ~30 samples per condition, which the BoostDiff README recommends as the minimum per condition for reliable inference and downstream checks The goal is differential expression analysis rather than assessing condition-specific regulator-target correlation patterns of differential network edges http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that top-ranked edges of a BoostDiff differential network are target-condition-specific by computing Pearson correlations of the original expression data per target condition and inspecting the correlation distributions: a bimodal distribution in the target condition (strong positive = activating edges, negative = inhibitory edges) versus a unimodal distribution in the non-target condition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Validates that top-ranked edges of a BoostDiff differential network are target-condition-specific by computing Pearson correlations of the original expression data per target condition and inspecting the correlation distributions: a bimodal distribution in the target condition (strong positive = activating edges, negative = inhibitory edges) versus a unimodal distribution in the non-target condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet been filtered for target genes with a more predictive model for the target condition — run filter_network (p=3, n_top_edges=150) first, otherwise the top-edge set is undefined The expression matrices have fewer than ~30 samples per condition, which the BoostDiff README recommends as the minimum per condition for reliable inference and downstream checks The goal is differential expression analysis rather than assessing condition-specific regulator-target correlation patterns of differential network edges

skills.description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data generated from small pilot sub-samples (384–2304 cells) must be checked against the original data's per-gene distributions, especially to detect missed bimodal gene patterns.
skills.name: bimodal-gene-distribution-visualization
skills.search_text: bimodal-gene-distribution-visualization Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data generated from small pilot sub-samples (384–2304 cells) must be checked against the original data's per-gene distributions, especially to detect missed bimodal gene patterns. The goal is batch-effect assessment or correction — the paper explicitly omitted batch correction, so this skill says nothing about it. Evaluating cluster-level properties (ARI, DBI, cluster proportions) rather than per-gene univariate distributions — those are separate evaluation skills. The input data are not matched original/synthetic pairs from the same gene panel; per-gene MAD comparisons require identical gene sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3368 Reproduce the per-gene univariate distribution evaluation from the scDBM paper by computing per-gene descriptive statistics (median, IQR, CV, zero-count proportion) for original vs. synthetic scRNA-seq data and visualizing exemplary genes such as CD74 to expose the failure of scDBM/scVI to capture bimodal distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Reproduce the per-gene univariate distribution evaluation from the scDBM paper by computing per-gene descriptive statistics (median, IQR, CV, zero-count proportion) for original vs. synthetic scRNA-seq data and visualizing exemplary genes such as CD74 to expose the failure of scDBM/scVI to capture bimodal distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is batch-effect assessment or correction — the paper explicitly omitted batch correction, so this skill says nothing about it. The input data are not matched original/synthetic pairs from the same gene panel; per-gene MAD comparisons require identical gene sets.

skills.description: Use when annotating a target scRNA-seq dataset in open or open-partial settings and you must decide, from the E-score (entropy/confidence/consistency) distribution alone, whether target-private cell types exist before partitioning cells into known vs unknown groups.
skills.name: bimodality-test-interpretation
skills.search_text: bimodality-test-interpretation Use when annotating a target scRNA-seq dataset in open or open-partial settings and you must decide, from the E-score (entropy/confidence/consistency) distribution alone, whether target-private cell types exist before partitioning cells into known vs unknown groups. The setting is closed or partial with no possibility of target-private cell types, so threshold-free novel-type detection is unnecessary The target data contain only one cell type or the E-score distribution is unimodal by design, making bimodality tests uninformative Raw source data are available and you intend to perform explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g. scmap, ItClust-style transfer) rather than source-free adaptation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test to the empirical distribution of scEMAIL's expert-ensemble uncertainty scores (E-scores) to decide whether target scRNA-seq data contain novel cell types, replacing user-defined thresholds with a data-driven decision. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Applies the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test to the empirical distribution of scEMAIL's expert-ensemble uncertainty scores (E-scores) to decide whether target scRNA-seq data contain novel cell types, replacing user-defined thresholds with a data-driven decision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The setting is closed or partial with no possibility of target-private cell types, so threshold-free novel-type detection is unnecessary The target data contain only one cell type or the E-score distribution is unimodal by design, making bimodality tests uninformative Raw source data are available and you intend to perform explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g. scmap, ItClust-style transfer) rather than source-free adaptation

skills.description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a pre-trained source model and you must decide—without manual thresholds or prior information—whether the target contains unseen (novel) cell types based on per-cell uncertainty scores.
skills.name: bimodality-testing-of-uncertainty-scores
skills.search_text: bimodality-testing-of-uncertainty-scores Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a pre-trained source model and you must decide—without manual thresholds or prior information—whether the target contains unseen (novel) cell types based on per-cell uncertainty scores. The target data contain only known cell types already covered by the source label set and no novel-type screening is needed Per-cell uncertainty scores (E-scores) have not yet been computed from the expert ensemble (entropy, confidence, consistency)—run the E-score computation step first A user-supplied novelty threshold already exists and manual thresholding is acceptable—scEMAIL's point is to avoid subjective thresholds http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Decision procedure from scEMAIL that tests the per-cell E-score uncertainty distribution (from entropy, confidence, and consistency in an expert ensemble) for bimodality to automatically judge whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Decision procedure from scEMAIL that tests the per-cell E-score uncertainty distribution (from entropy, confidence, and consistency in an expert ensemble) for bimodality to automatically judge whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target data contain only known cell types already covered by the source label set and no novel-type screening is needed Per-cell uncertainty scores (E-scores) have not yet been computed from the expert ensemble (entropy, confidence, consistency)—run the E-score computation step first A user-supplied novelty threshold already exists and manual thresholding is acceptable—scEMAIL's point is to avoid subjective thresholds

skills.description: Use when configuring scWGS CNA calling resolution: you must choose a bin size for RDR/BAF-based single-cell copy-number analysis or decide if a dataset's coverage (e.g., ~0.5× low-coverage vs >20× PTA-amplified) supports sub-Mb CNA detection.
skills.name: bin-size-optimization-scwgs
skills.search_text: bin-size-optimization-scwgs Use when configuring scWGS CNA calling resolution: you must choose a bin size for RDR/BAF-based single-cell copy-number analysis or decide if a dataset's coverage (e.g., ~0.5× low-coverage vs >20× PTA-amplified) supports sub-Mb CNA detection. Input data are not scWGS with paired bulk for phasing — e.g., bulk-only tumor samples, where bulk callers such as ASCAT or Battenberg are the appropriate choice The amplification assay or coverage regime differs fundamentally from the tested grid (e.g., non-PTA single-cell WGA with severe amplification artifacts), so the simulated optimum may not transfer without re-running the ADO analysis The goal is point-mutation (SNV/indel) calling rather than copy-number detection — use SCAN2 instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A benchmarking protocol that sweeps HiScanner bin sizes (50/100/500 kb) and sequencing depths (0.5×/10×/30×) on SDX-simulated single-cell and paired bulk scWGS data to find the bin-size/coverage combination that best trades precision against sensitivity for CNA detection. It grounds HiScanner's ADO-based bin-size selection in quantitative precision/sensitivity curves per CNA type and size class. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that sweeps HiScanner bin sizes (50/100/500 kb) and sequencing depths (0.5×/10×/30×) on SDX-simulated single-cell and paired bulk scWGS data to find the bin-size/coverage combination that best trades precision against sensitivity for CNA detection. It grounds HiScanner's ADO-based bin-size selection in quantitative precision/sensitivity curves per CNA type and size class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not scWGS with paired bulk for phasing — e.g., bulk-only tumor samples, where bulk callers such as ASCAT or Battenberg are the appropriate choice The amplification assay or coverage regime differs fundamentally from the tested grid (e.g., non-PTA single-cell WGA with severe amplification artifacts), so the simulated optimum may not transfer without re-running the ADO analysis The goal is point-mutation (SNV/indel) calling rather than copy-number detection — use SCAN2 instead

skills.summary: Benchmark lncRNA/mRNA binary classifiers by running each tool with its default prebuilt models on a shared FASTA test set and computing accuracy against known labels, as done when comparing LncDC to CPAT, PLEK, CPC2, CPPred, LncFinder, and COME on the human H-Test dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is lncRNA discovery on unlabeled RNA-Seq transcript assemblies rather than benchmarking classifiers against known labels When classifiers were trained on the same transcripts being evaluated — this skill requires an independent test set to avoid optimistic accuracy When you need multi-class or regression evaluation; this skill covers two-class lncRNA vs mRNA classification only

skills.description: Use when a per-sample binary call (e.g., mCLL vs uCLL from RNA-seq IGHV percent identity) must be compared sample-by-sample against matched clinical gold-standard labels to quantify agreement.
skills.name: binary-classification-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: binary-classification-concordance-analysis Use when a per-sample binary call (e.g., mCLL vs uCLL from RNA-seq IGHV percent identity) must be compared sample-by-sample against matched clinical gold-standard labels to quantify agreement. No matched gold-standard (e.g., PCR-Sanger) labels exist for the samples, so agreement metrics cannot be computed The outcome is not a two-class call — continuous IGHV percent-identity values should be compared directly rather than collapsed to mCLL/uCLL concordance Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted, and indexed, or have far fewer than the required ~25M reads, so the predictions feeding the comparison are invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates a binary classifier (e.g., CRIS IGHV somatic hypermutation status calls, mutated mCLL vs unmutated uCLL) against an independent gold-standard label set (clinical PCR-Sanger classification) by computing per-sample concordance, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity and flagging discordant cases. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Validates a binary classifier (e.g., CRIS IGHV somatic hypermutation status calls, mutated mCLL vs unmutated uCLL) against an independent gold-standard label set (clinical PCR-Sanger classification) by computing per-sample concordance, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity and flagging discordant cases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched gold-standard (e.g., PCR-Sanger) labels exist for the samples, so agreement metrics cannot be computed The outcome is not a two-class call — continuous IGHV percent-identity values should be compared directly rather than collapsed to mCLL/uCLL concordance Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted, and indexed, or have far fewer than the required ~25M reads, so the predictions feeding the comparison are invalid

skills.description: Use when comparing binary RNA-modification classifiers (e.g., m5C predictors on A. thaliana or M. musculus datasets) and you need side-by-side Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, AUC tables from TP/TN/FP/FN counts.

skills.search_text: binary-classification-metric-computation Use when comparing binary RNA-modification classifiers (e.g., m5C predictors on A. thaliana or M. musculus datasets) and you need side-by-side Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, AUC tables from TP/TN/FP/FN counts. The task is multi-class classification or regression — Sn/Sp/MCC formulas here assume a two-class m5C vs non-m5C prediction setting Input is already a metric table (e.g., published Table 3/Table 4 values); recompute only when raw TP/TN/FP/FN counts or predictions are available Datasets are highly imbalanced or species other than those with species-specific Staem5 models ('Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse'), since the article notes no general cross-species model exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Compute Sn, Sp, accuracy, MCC, and AUC from confusion-matrix counts (TP, TN, FP, FN) to benchmark binary m5C site predictors such as Staem5 against iRNA-m5C, m5CPred-SVM, and iRNA-m5C_SVM on identical training and independent test datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Compute Sn, Sp, accuracy, MCC, and AUC from confusion-matrix counts (TP, TN, FP, FN) to benchmark binary m5C site predictors such as Staem5 against iRNA-m5C, m5CPred-SVM, and iRNA-m5C_SVM on identical training and independent test datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is multi-class classification or regression — Sn/Sp/MCC formulas here assume a two-class m5C vs non-m5C prediction setting Input is already a metric table (e.g., published Table 3/Table 4 values); recompute only when raw TP/TN/FP/FN counts or predictions are available Datasets are highly imbalanced or species other than those with species-specific Staem5 models ('Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse'), since the article notes no general cross-species model exists

skills.description: Use when comparing differential detection methods on simulated trajectory data with known ground truth, where each method's per-gene (or per-state) calls must be scored as binary classification metrics.
skills.name: binary-classification-metric-computation
skills.search_text: binary-classification-metric-computation Use when comparing differential detection methods on simulated trajectory data with known ground truth, where each method's per-gene (or per-state) calls must be scored as binary classification metrics. Input is real experimental data without simulation ground truth — TPR/PPV/NPV cannot be computed without known differential labels Methods produce continuous scores without p-values, making BH correction at a common 5% FDR threshold inapplicable Systems are steady-state without a trajectory; the article notes clustering-based differential abundance is the reasonable approach for steady-state systems http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark differential-state/differential-abundance callers (condiments progressionTest, fateSelectionTest, DAseq, milo) as binary classifiers against dyngen simulation ground truth, computing TNR, TPR, PPV, NPV, and F1 on Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p-values at a 5% FDR threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Benchmark differential-state/differential-abundance callers (condiments progressionTest, fateSelectionTest, DAseq, milo) as binary classifiers against dyngen simulation ground truth, computing TNR, TPR, PPV, NPV, and F1 on Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p-values at a 5% FDR threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data without simulation ground truth — TPR/PPV/NPV cannot be computed without known differential labels Methods produce continuous scores without p-values, making BH correction at a common 5% FDR threshold inapplicable Systems are steady-state without a trajectory; the article notes clustering-based differential abundance is the reasonable approach for steady-state systems

skills.description: Use when you have a simulated or labelled scRNA-seq AnnData object with known per-cluster memberships and need to rank enrichment scoring methods by binary classification performance (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) per cluster.
skills.name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: binary-classification-metric-evaluation Use when you have a simulated or labelled scRNA-seq AnnData object with known per-cluster memberships and need to rank enrichment scoring methods by binary classification performance (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) per cluster. The input is raw count data that has not been log-cpm normalised and Leiden-clustered — Cytocipher expects an AnnData object processed per the scanpy standard workflow with tentative cluster labels. The goal is significance testing / cluster merging (cc.tl.merge_clusters) rather than benchmarking scoring methods against known labels. Clusters in the real dataset of interest are not defined by unique gene combinations — the reported method ranking was established on simulated data where clusters are defined by gene combinations rather than single marker genes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks cell-by-cluster enrichment scoring methods (Cytocipher code scoring, coexpr scoring, Giotto PAGE, Scanpy score_genes, and negative-gene-set-subtraction variants Giotto (−) and Scanpy (−)) by converting enrichment scores into per-cluster binary cell-to-cluster assignments and comparing accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. It reproduces the simulated-data ranking from the Cytocipher paper's Fig. 2D benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Benchmarks cell-by-cluster enrichment scoring methods (Cytocipher code scoring, coexpr scoring, Giotto PAGE, Scanpy score_genes, and negative-gene-set-subtraction variants Giotto (−) and Scanpy (−)) by converting enrichment scores into per-cluster binary cell-to-cluster assignments and comparing accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. It reproduces the simulated-data ranking from the Cytocipher paper's Fig. 2D benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw count data that has not been log-cpm normalised and Leiden-clustered — Cytocipher expects an AnnData object processed per the scanpy standard workflow with tentative cluster labels. The goal is significance testing / cluster merging (cc.tl.merge_clusters) rather than benchmarking scoring methods against known labels. skills.description: Use when you need unbiased performance estimates (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy) for a binary classifier fitted on high-dimensional transcriptomic data via nested cross-validation with nestedcv, e.g. to compare against vignette-reported values.
skills.name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: binary-classification-metric-evaluation Use when you need unbiased performance estimates (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy) for a binary classifier fitted on high-dimensional transcriptomic data via nested cross-validation with nestedcv, e.g. to compare against vignette-reported values. The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 split — the article motivates nested CV specifically for small biomedical datasets where P >> n. Feature filtering has already been performed on the whole dataset — filtering on the whole dataset creates a bias when determining accuracy of models. The outcome is multinomial or regression — use family-appropriate metrics (e.g. the iris multinomial glmnet example or BostonHousing2 regression) rather than binary AUC/balanced accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extracts unbiased outer-CV binary classification performance metrics (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy) from nestedcv nested cross-validation runs, computed on concatenated left-out outer-fold test predictions. Used to benchmark nested glmnet models on high-dimensional transcriptomic data such as the R4RA rituximab RNA-seq subset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Extracts unbiased outer-CV binary classification performance metrics (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy) from nestedcv nested cross-validation runs, computed on concatenated left-out outer-fold test predictions. Used to benchmark nested glmnet models on high-dimensional transcriptomic data such as the R4RA rituximab RNA-seq subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 split — the article motivates nested CV specifically for small biomedical datasets where P >> n. Feature filtering has already been performed on the whole dataset — filtering on the whole dataset creates a bias when determining accuracy of models. The outcome is multinomial or regression — use family-appropriate metrics (e.g. the iris multinomial glmnet example or BostonHousing2 regression) rather than binary AUC/balanced accuracy.

skills.search_text: binary-classifier-accuracy-evaluation Use when a binary classifier has produced per-site predictions on a labeled, held-out dataset and you must quantify performance as mean accuracy, AUC, specificity, and precision against gold-standard positives/negatives. skills.search_text: binary-classifier-auc-evaluation Use when benchmarking a trained fusion-read filter (e.g., HVLD retrained per dataset on artificial chimeric negatives and PCAWG positives) and comparing its AUC to competing models on held-out single-cell RNA-seq test samples. skills.summary: Evaluates the HVLD deep learning filter of Anchored-fusion as a binary classifier distinguishing true fusion reads from artificial chimeric reads on scRNA-seq data, reporting AUC on K562 and multiple-myeloma datasets against competitors such as scFusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset provided by the user is too small — the article recommends using the default model parameters provided on GitHub rather than retraining and re-evaluating an HVLD filter Detection on single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion and this evaluation only apply to paired-end RNA-seq The goal is detection of fusion genes not including the user-provided anchored target gene — the anchored search and its filter model cannot score such events

skills.name: binary-classifier-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: binary-classifier-metric-evaluation Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. a Keras/TensorFlow viral-read model) must be scored on a labeled held-out test partition and compared to baselines under identical data. Input sequences come from organisms other than human or virus — the paper states model predictions for such sequences are not defined and models for other organisms are left to future work Reads are not fixed-length 48 bp fragments or have not been mapped/removed against the human genome (hg19) and phiX contaminant first — the model was precomputed for 48 bp reads on unmapped reads Reads are short and detection requires no more than approximately five viral reads — the paper only claims sensitivity if more than five viral reads are present http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluate a binary viral-vs-human read classifier by computing AUROC, AUPRC, accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 on a held-out test set of fixed-length (48 bp) RNA-seq fragments, and compare against baseline classifiers on the identical test set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Evaluate a binary viral-vs-human read classifier by computing AUROC, AUPRC, accuracy, recall, precision, and F1 on a held-out test set of fixed-length (48 bp) RNA-seq fragments, and compare against baseline classifiers on the identical test set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences come from organisms other than human or virus — the paper states model predictions for such sequences are not defined and models for other organisms are left to future work Reads are not fixed-length 48 bp fragments or have not been mapped/removed against the human genome (hg19) and phiX contaminant first — the model was precomputed for 48 bp reads on unmapped reads Reads are short and detection requires no more than approximately five viral reads — the paper only claims sensitivity if more than five viral reads are present

skills.description: Use when several tuned binary classifiers (e.g. LR, DT, SVM, RF, XGBoost) must be ranked on a held-out labeled test set to decide which algorithm a tool should adopt, as in LncDC's five-algorithm selection on H-Test.
skills.name: binary-classifier-performance-metrics
skills.search_text: binary-classifier-performance-metrics Use when several tuned binary classifiers (e.g. LR, DT, SVM, RF, XGBoost) must be ranked on a held-out labeled test set to decide which algorithm a tool should adopt, as in LncDC's five-algorithm selection on H-Test. Input is a feature table still needing model training and SMOTE balancing — the metric evaluation comes after tenfold CV tuning, not before. The task is ranking feature sets or ablation variants (e.g. SIF+PF vs SIF+PF+SSF) on the same model rather than selecting among different algorithms. Predictions are multi-class or the labels are not the binary lncRNA/mRNA classes; MCC and the specificity/sensitivity panel as configured assume a two-class problem. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes and compares a six-metric panel (accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, precision, MCC) for binary lncRNA/mRNA classifiers evaluated on a held-out test set (H-Test), producing the ranked comparison table used to select the final algorithm for LncDC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Computes and compares a six-metric panel (accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, precision, MCC) for binary lncRNA/mRNA classifiers evaluated on a held-out test set (H-Test), producing the ranked comparison table used to select the final algorithm for LncDC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a feature table still needing model training and SMOTE balancing — the metric evaluation comes after tenfold CV tuning, not before. The task is ranking feature sets or ablation variants (e.g. SIF+PF vs SIF+PF+SSF) on the same model rather than selecting among different algorithms. Predictions are multi-class or the labels are not the binary lncRNA/mRNA classes; MCC and the specificity/sensitivity panel as configured assume a two-class problem.
