skills.description: Use when validating whether a trajectory/fate model's predicted fate-bias probabilities match observed clonal outcomes on a held-out progenitor set (e.g. the 335-cell Weinreb day-2 test set), where AUROC, Pearson r, and covered fraction are the acceptance metrics.
skills.name: binary-fate-classification-auroc-evaluation
skills.search_text: binary-fate-classification-auroc-evaluation Use when validating whether a trajectory/fate model's predicted fate-bias probabilities match observed clonal outcomes on a held-out progenitor set (e.g. the 335-cell Weinreb day-2 test set), where AUROC, Pearson r, and covered fraction are the acceptance metrics. The task is interpolation/generation of held-out time points rather than clonal fate-bias classification — the paper separates the Weinreb interpolation task (weinreb-interpolate.sh) from the fate task (weinreb-fate.sh). No lineage-tracing ground truth exists, so observed clonal fate bias cannot be computed and Pearson r/AUROC cannot be validated. The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model assumption the fate-bias comparison rests on. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores predicted clonal fate bias of progenitor cells against held-out lineage-tracing ground truth using Pearson correlation, AUROC for binary fate classification, and the covered fraction of progenitors with a fate call, benchmarking a trajectory model (PRESCIENT) against WOT, FateID, and the clonal upper bound. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Scores predicted clonal fate bias of progenitor cells against held-out lineage-tracing ground truth using Pearson correlation, AUROC for binary fate classification, and the covered fraction of progenitors with a fate call, benchmarking a trajectory model (PRESCIENT) against WOT, FateID, and the clonal upper bound.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is interpolation/generation of held-out time points rather than clonal fate-bias classification — the paper separates the Weinreb interpolation task (weinreb-interpolate.sh) from the fate task (weinreb-fate.sh). No lineage-tracing ground truth exists, so observed clonal fate bias cannot be computed and Pearson r/AUROC cannot be validated. The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model assumption the fate-bias comparison rests on.

skills.description: Use when preparing an expression matrix (e.g. dat.expression, genes x cells) as input to singleCellHaystack's haystack() or DKL computation, which accepts only binary detection data per cell.
skills.name: binary-gene-detection-binarization
skills.search_text: binary-gene-detection-binarization Use when preparing an expression matrix (e.g. dat.expression, genes x cells) as input to singleCellHaystack's haystack() or DKL computation, which accepts only binary detection data per cell. Your analysis depends on expression magnitude, not just detection — two genes with the same detection pattern but ten-fold different levels get identical DKL and p-values under this hard threshold. Your downstream method supports continuous expression (e.g. normalized read counts); the article notes continuous-measure support was planned but not yet available in this implementation. You need p-values corrected for double use of gene expression data (e.g. when coordinates were derived from the same expression data) — singleCellHaystack p-values are known to be inflated in that setting. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Convert a single-cell expression matrix (genes x cells) into a binary gene detection matrix (1 = detected, 0 = not detected), because singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence approach requires binary detection data rather than continuous read counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Convert a single-cell expression matrix (genes x cells) into a binary gene detection matrix (1 = detected, 0 = not detected), because singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence approach requires binary detection data rather than continuous read counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis depends on expression magnitude, not just detection — two genes with the same detection pattern but ten-fold different levels get identical DKL and p-values under this hard threshold. Your downstream method supports continuous expression (e.g. normalized read counts); the article notes continuous-measure support was planned but not yet available in this implementation. You need p-values corrected for double use of gene expression data (e.g. when coordinates were derived from the same expression data) — singleCellHaystack p-values are known to be inflated in that setting.

skills.description: Use when iDEA-based GSE analysis requires pre-defined gene set annotations whose gene identifiers must match the identifier type (gene symbols or MGI IDs) of DE summary statistics.
skills.name: binary-gene-set-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: binary-gene-set-matrix-construction Use when iDEA-based GSE analysis requires pre-defined gene set annotations whose gene identifiers must match the identifier type (gene symbols or MGI IDs) of DE summary statistics. Gene set annotations already exist as an iDEA-compatible binary matrix (e.g. the distributed humanGeneSets.RData / mouseGeneSets.RData files) — load them instead of recompiling Summary statistics use identifiers other than gene symbols or MGI IDs and identifier conversion via biomaRt is not possible The analysis goal is differential expression itself rather than gene set enrichment — gene set annotations are not required as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct binary (0/1) gene-by-gene-set annotation matrices for iDEA's GSE analysis by compiling and pruning human gene sets from seven MSigDB databases (BioCarta, KEGG, GO, PubChem Compound, ImmuneSigDB, PID, Reactome on GRCh37) and mouse GO annotations from MGI GAF 2.0, yielding 12,033 usable human gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Construct binary (0/1) gene-by-gene-set annotation matrices for iDEA's GSE analysis by compiling and pruning human gene sets from seven MSigDB databases (BioCarta, KEGG, GO, PubChem Compound, ImmuneSigDB, PID, Reactome on GRCh37) and mouse GO annotations from MGI GAF 2.0, yielding 12,033 usable human gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene set annotations already exist as an iDEA-compatible binary matrix (e.g. the distributed humanGeneSets.RData / mouseGeneSets.RData files) — load them instead of recompiling Summary statistics use identifiers other than gene symbols or MGI IDs and identifier conversion via biomaRt is not possible The analysis goal is differential expression itself rather than gene set enrichment — gene set annotations are not required as input

skills.description: Use when converting fixed-length nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt RNA 5hmC windows) into numerical feature vectors via position-specific binary occurrence indicators of k-mer and gapped k-mer patterns before classifier training.
skills.name: binary-indicator-vector-construction
skills.search_text: binary-indicator-vector-construction Use when converting fixed-length nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt RNA 5hmC windows) into numerical feature vectors via position-specific binary occurrence indicators of k-mer and gapped k-mer patterns before classifier training. Input sequences have variable length or are not 41-nt windows — the position-specific indicators assume fixed consecutive-residue-group positions Input is already a feature table (e.g., All_Features_Dataset.csv); proceed directly to Model.ipynb training/evaluation instead You need frequency-based gapped k-mer features rather than position-specific binary indicators — the paper shows position-specific features do not combine well with frequency-based counterparts in single models http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Encodes fixed-length (41-nt) RNA sequences into position-specific binary indicator vectors by testing each nucleotide pattern (contiguous or gapped k-mer) against all consecutive-residue-groups along the sequence, then concatenates the pattern blocks with a GC-content feature into a single 19,877-column feature matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: Encodes fixed-length (41-nt) RNA sequences into position-specific binary indicator vectors by testing each nucleotide pattern (contiguous or gapped k-mer) against all consecutive-residue-groups along the sequence, then concatenates the pattern blocks with a GC-content feature into a single 19,877-column feature matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences have variable length or are not 41-nt windows — the position-specific indicators assume fixed consecutive-residue-group positions Input is already a feature table (e.g., All_Features_Dataset.csv); proceed directly to Model.ipynb training/evaluation instead You need frequency-based gapped k-mer features rather than position-specific binary indicators — the paper shows position-specific features do not combine well with frequency-based counterparts in single models

skills.search_text: binary-integer-programming-optimization Use when you have a differential gene co-expression network with per-edge P-values and must select a minimum dominating set of driver nodes, weighting nodes by degree and co-expression difference significance. Input is already a ranked gene list with no underlying network or per-edge P-values — node weights w_i = (Σ −log p_ij)^(−γ) cannot be computed Goal is an unweighted baseline rather than the biologically weighted model — use γ = 0 with w_i = 1 instead of the weighted formulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Formulates driver-node selection on a differential co-expression network as a weighted minimum dominating set binary integer program, solved with MATLAB intlinprog, so that node weights (degree plus differential co-expression significance) guide which genes are selected. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Formulates driver-node selection on a differential co-expression network as a weighted minimum dominating set binary integer program, solved with MATLAB intlinprog, so that node weights (degree plus differential co-expression significance) guide which genes are selected.

skills.search_text: binary-mixed-integer-program-optimization Use when cells measured only by scRNA-seq (expression) must be associated one-to-one with cells measured only by scDNA-seq (CNA), and the matching can be cast as a binary MIP over Pearson-correlation edge weights when |RNA cells| ≤ |DNA cells|. When probabilistic confidence measures for assignments are required — MaCroDNA, unlike statistical methods such as clonealign, provides none (only the step number as a coarse confidence proxy) When the sample is biologically homogeneous — the article notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples When pairing RNA cells to DNA clones rather than individual cells — use the cell2clone_assignment path with an additional dna_label DataFrame ('clone' and 'cell' columns) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Formulates MaCroDNA's maximum weighted bipartite matching between scRNA-seq cells (gene expression) and scDNA-seq cells (copy-number profiles) as a binary mixed-integer program, edge-weighted by per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients, and solves it with Gurobi to recover the one-to-one cell correspondence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3

skills.description: Use when a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. SMARTer-protocol data such as Xin GSE81608) must be converted into a binary low-dimensional cell representation for cell-type clustering, and dropouts should be leveraged as weak signals rather than imputed.
skills.name: binary-pattern-gene-clustering
skills.search_text: binary-pattern-gene-clustering Use when a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. SMARTer-protocol data such as Xin GSE81608) must be converted into a binary low-dimensional cell representation for cell-type clustering, and dropouts should be leveraged as weak signals rather than imputed. The analysis goal is a quantitative (expression-magnitude) representation — use scQA's LC2 module, which clusters genes with quasi-trend-preserved quantitative patterns, instead of LC1 A predetermined number of clusters is required upstream, or the input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than a raw sparse cell × gene matrix Only ~2000 retained HVGs would exclude critical informative genes for the biological question (a limitation the authors note for their own clustering) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1): binarize dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression, cluster genes sharing analogous binary expression patterns via normalized Hamming similarity, and emit a binary low-dimensional cell-landmark matrix (Q1) that treats dropouts as weak signals to be strengthened by gene amalgamation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Implements scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1): binarize dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression, cluster genes sharing analogous binary expression patterns via normalized Hamming similarity, and emit a binary low-dimensional cell-landmark matrix (Q1) that treats dropouts as weak signals to be strengthened by gene amalgamation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a quantitative (expression-magnitude) representation — use scQA's LC2 module, which clusters genes with quasi-trend-preserved quantitative patterns, instead of LC1 A predetermined number of clusters is required upstream, or the input is already a low-dimensional feature/embedding table rather than a raw sparse cell × gene matrix Only ~2000 retained HVGs would exclude critical informative genes for the biological question (a limitation the authors note for their own clustering)

skills.search_text: binding-affinity-mlp-training Use when labeled oligo(dT) priming windows (paired-end alignments indicating primer sites) from scRNA-seq data are available and a sequence-based binding-affinity predictor must be trained or reproduced (e.g. the pa6with1mm model). skills.summary: Implements the co-dependency index (CDI)/nCDI differential expression statistic from scPipeline/scMiko, which scores each gene-cluster pair by a binomial co-occurrence p-value to identify cluster-specific binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) in scRNA-seq data.

skills.search_text: binomial-detection-probability-modeling Use when planning a single-cell RNA-seq experiment to determine the cell number N needed to detect a rare population (e.g., 5% prevalence) while accounting for within-population variability and capture efficiency. The goal is benchmarking clustering, DE, or trajectory-inference method accuracy rather than sizing an experiment to detect a rare population. The population of interest is abundant (not rare), where theoretical binomial sizing alone is adequate without simulating variability. The sequencing protocol and biological system differ substantially from the fitted reference (e.g., non-UMI data where scVI is not applicable to small datasets), so fitted Sigma/alpha parameters would not transfer. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Uses SymSim-based simulation to estimate how many cells must be sequenced to detect a rare subpopulation, comparing empirical detection probabilities across clustering methods with a closed-form binomial theoretical detection curve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w

skills.description: Use when you have cell-attribute-aware clusters (Eva_partitions output over an igraph cell-cell nearest-neighbour graph) and need to flag which communities are significantly enriched for a condition label before downstream DoDA regression.
skills.name: binomial-enrichment-testing-with-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: binomial-enrichment-testing-with-bonferroni-correction Use when you have cell-attribute-aware clusters (Eva_partitions output over an igraph cell-cell nearest-neighbour graph) and need to flag which communities are significantly enriched for a condition label before downstream DoDA regression. You only need DA testing on pre-defined annotated cell types without attribute-aware community detection — Milo or a Louvain-analog (alpha=0) may suffice and avoids the Binomial community-enrichment step. The cell-cell graph contains cells whose attribute labels are unreliable: the paper notes ELVAR is more sensitive to false positives in the clustering attribute (sample/phenotype label), which can degrade enrichment and community quality. The EVA clustering produced strongly Louvain-like partitions (no deviation from alpha=0 cluster count), where attribute enrichment adds little beyond standard Louvain community testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify attribute-enriched cellular communities from EVA partitions in the ELVAR pipeline by testing, for each community, whether the frequency of cells carrying a given vertex attribute (e.g. age, Covid-19 severity, disease stage, smell-loss phenotype) exceeds expectation via a Binomial test with a Bonferroni significance threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Identify attribute-enriched cellular communities from EVA partitions in the ELVAR pipeline by testing, for each community, whether the frequency of cells carrying a given vertex attribute (e.g. age, Covid-19 severity, disease stage, smell-loss phenotype) exceeds expectation via a Binomial test with a Bonferroni significance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need DA testing on pre-defined annotated cell types without attribute-aware community detection — Milo or a Louvain-analog (alpha=0) may suffice and avoids the Binomial community-enrichment step. The cell-cell graph contains cells whose attribute labels are unreliable: the paper notes ELVAR is more sensitive to false positives in the clustering attribute (sample/phenotype label), which can degrade enrichment and community quality. The EVA clustering produced strongly Louvain-like partitions (no deviation from alpha=0 cluster count), where attribute enrichment adds little beyond standard Louvain community testing.

skills.description: Use when single-cell mtDNA AD/DP matrices (from cellsnp-lite or cellSNP) are available and you must distinguish clone-discriminative heteroplasmic variants from noisy, non-inherited SNVs before clonal reconstruction with vireoSNP.
skills.name: binomial-mixture-model-variant-selection
skills.search_text: binomial-mixture-model-variant-selection Use when single-cell mtDNA AD/DP matrices (from cellsnp-lite or cellSNP) are available and you must distinguish clone-discriminative heteroplasmic variants from noisy, non-inherited SNVs before clonal reconstruction with vireoSNP. The input is nuclear genomic SNV data — nuclear SNV callers such as Monovar and Conbase assume a diploid context, which is violated in the mitochondrial genome, and this model is tuned for mtDNA heteroplasmy. The goal is donor deconvolution from common SNPs (use cellSNP/vireo in demultiplexing mode rather than clonal variant selection on somatic mtDNA variants). Data are mtscATAC-seq where mtDNA-specific callers like EMBLEM or mgatk were the primary design target — MQuad was evaluated mainly on scRNA-seq, scDNA-seq and Smart-seq2 protocols. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Selects clonally informative mtDNA variants from single-cell pileup matrices by fitting one- versus two-component binomial mixture models per variant with MQuad and ranking them by ΔBIC = BIC(M0) − BIC(M1), with the selection cutoff taken at the Kneedle knee point. This model-selection approach is more robust than raw allele-frequency filters and reduces false positives, especially in deeply sequenced Smart-seq2 data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Selects clonally informative mtDNA variants from single-cell pileup matrices by fitting one- versus two-component binomial mixture models per variant with MQuad and ranking them by ΔBIC = BIC(M0) − BIC(M1), with the selection cutoff taken at the Kneedle knee point. This model-selection approach is more robust than raw allele-frequency filters and reduces false positives, especially in deeply sequenced Smart-seq2 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is nuclear genomic SNV data — nuclear SNV callers such as Monovar and Conbase assume a diploid context, which is violated in the mitochondrial genome, and this model is tuned for mtDNA heteroplasmy. The goal is donor deconvolution from common SNPs (use cellSNP/vireo in demultiplexing mode rather than clonal variant selection on somatic mtDNA variants). Data are mtscATAC-seq where mtDNA-specific callers like EMBLEM or mgatk were the primary design target — MQuad was evaluated mainly on scRNA-seq, scDNA-seq and Smart-seq2 protocols.

skills.description: Use when you have a SNP-by-cell AD/DP count matrix (e.g. from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP over mtDNA) and need to separate clone-discriminative heteroplasmic mtDNA variants from noisy background variants before clonal assignment.
skills.name: binomial-mixture-variant-scoring
skills.search_text: binomial-mixture-variant-scoring Use when you have a SNP-by-cell AD/DP count matrix (e.g. from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP over mtDNA) and need to separate clone-discriminative heteroplasmic mtDNA variants from noisy background variants before clonal assignment. Variants come from nuclear genome calling where a diploid context holds (e.g. Monovar/Conbase assumptions), not the mitochondrial genome Data are 10x scRNA-seq needing per-UMI genotyping with strict duplicate handling — cellsnp-lite in mode 2 may need tuned read filtering since duplicates are often poorly flagged in CellRanger output The goal is donor demultiplexing from common germline SNPs (vireoSNP donor deconvolution) rather than somatic clonal mtDNA variant discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Score mtDNA variants for clonal informativeness using MQuad's binomial mixture model, which fits one-component vs two-component models per variant and ranks them by ΔBIC, then selects informative variants at a Kneedle knee-point cutoff for downstream clonal reconstruction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Score mtDNA variants for clonal informativeness using MQuad's binomial mixture model, which fits one-component vs two-component models per variant and ranks them by ΔBIC, then selects informative variants at a Kneedle knee-point cutoff for downstream clonal reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants come from nuclear genome calling where a diploid context holds (e.g. Monovar/Conbase assumptions), not the mitochondrial genome Data are 10x scRNA-seq needing per-UMI genotyping with strict duplicate handling — cellsnp-lite in mode 2 may need tuned read filtering since duplicates are often poorly flagged in CellRanger output The goal is donor demultiplexing from common germline SNPs (vireoSNP donor deconvolution) rather than somatic clonal mtDNA variant discovery

skills.description: Use when computing minimizer-sharing thresholds for (w,k)-minimizer queries whose minimizer count varies per read (e.g. m in 15-35), so that random sharing can be separated from true matches at significance level 0.99.
skills.name: binomial-probability-threshold-modeling
skills.search_text: binomial-probability-threshold-modeling Use when computing minimizer-sharing thresholds for (w,k)-minimizer queries whose minimizer count varies per read (e.g. m in 15-35), so that random sharing can be separated from true matches at significance level 0.99. Queries use fixed-length exact k-mer indexing rather than sequence-dependent (w,k)-minimizers, so the minimizer count does not vary per read and a fixed threshold suffices. Raptor's susceptibility to uneven bin sizes or a very high number of bins is the actual bottleneck — threshold modeling will not address these index-level limits. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs Raptor's probabilistic thresholding model (Equations 1-5 and Lemma 2) as a standalone threshold-table generator: a binomial model over the probability that a query minimizer is affected by errors, parameterized by window size w, k-mer size k, number of errors, and the query's minimizer count. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Reconstructs Raptor's probabilistic thresholding model (Equations 1-5 and Lemma 2) as a standalone threshold-table generator: a binomial model over the probability that a query minimizer is affected by errors, parameterized by window size w, k-mer size k, number of errors, and the query's minimizer count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Queries use fixed-length exact k-mer indexing rather than sequence-dependent (w,k)-minimizers, so the minimizer count does not vary per read and a fixed threshold suffices. Raptor's susceptibility to uneven bin sizes or a very high number of bins is the actual bottleneck — threshold modeling will not address these index-level limits.

skills.description: Use when you have a multi-sample VCF with raw allele depths per sample and need to classify biallelic SNPs as showing allele-specific expression versus equal (50/50) allelic balance.
skills.name: binomial-test-allele-count-analysis
skills.search_text: binomial-test-allele-count-analysis Use when you have a multi-sample VCF with raw allele depths per sample and need to classify biallelic SNPs as showing allele-specific expression versus equal (50/50) allelic balance. Input VCF contains multiallelic sites or indels — VADT removes multiallelic SNPs, indels, and SNPs within 75 bp of an indel before testing Per-sample raw allele depths (AD field) are absent or the VCF was not produced by GATK's HaplotypeCaller — VADT may have bugs with other callers' VCF formats The question concerns which samples (not variants) show ASE — then the multi-dimensional p-value adjustment per sample model, not the meta-analysis binomial variant model, is the appropriate analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Per-sample binomial testing of raw allele depths (AD field) from a filtered biallelic VCF, combined across samples per variant with Fisher's Method and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control, to detect allele-specific expression (ASE) SNPs as implemented in VADT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Per-sample binomial testing of raw allele depths (AD field) from a filtered biallelic VCF, combined across samples per variant with Fisher's Method and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control, to detect allele-specific expression (ASE) SNPs as implemented in VADT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input VCF contains multiallelic sites or indels — VADT removes multiallelic SNPs, indels, and SNPs within 75 bp of an indel before testing Per-sample raw allele depths (AD field) are absent or the VCF was not produced by GATK's HaplotypeCaller — VADT may have bugs with other callers' VCF formats The question concerns which samples (not variants) show ASE — then the multi-dimensional p-value adjustment per sample model, not the meta-analysis binomial variant model, is the appropriate analysis

skills.description: Use when evaluating a signal-filtering or cell-cycle-removal method on annotated single-cell data and you need to quantify, alongside a removal score, whether the corrected expression matrix preserves the biology of interest (e.g., subclone structure).
skills.name: bio-conservation-metric-computation
skills.search_text: bio-conservation-metric-computation Use when evaluating a signal-filtering or cell-cycle-removal method on annotated single-cell data and you need to quantify, alongside a removal score, whether the corrected expression matrix preserves the biology of interest (e.g., subclone structure). The task is to remove the unwanted signal itself (cell cycle) rather than to score how well a corrected matrix preserved the biology of interest — use the filtering skill instead. No per-cell annotations exist for either the signal to filter or the biology to conserve, so neither the SiFT kernel nor the conservation metric can be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes biological conservation scores on corrected single-cell expression data so that signal-removal methods (here, six SiFT kernel variants) can be judged not only on how much unwanted variation they remove but on how much of the biological signal of interest (e.g., subclone separability) they retain. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Computes biological conservation scores on corrected single-cell expression data so that signal-removal methods (here, six SiFT kernel variants) can be judged not only on how much unwanted variation they remove but on how much of the biological signal of interest (e.g., subclone separability) they retain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to remove the unwanted signal itself (cell cycle) rather than to score how well a corrected matrix preserved the biology of interest — use the filtering skill instead. No per-cell annotations exist for either the signal to filter or the biology to conserve, so neither the SiFT kernel nor the conservation metric can be defined.

skills.description: Use when BioAnalyzer Expert traces from plate-based scRNA-seq library preparation are available and you need per-sample free-barcode-to-cDNA ratios to test their association with estimated barcode-swapping fractions.
skills.name: bioanalyzer-trace-area-quantification
skills.search_text: bioanalyzer-trace-area-quantification Use when BioAnalyzer Expert traces from plate-based scRNA-seq library preparation are available and you need per-sample free-barcode-to-cDNA ratios to test their association with estimated barcode-swapping fractions. No BioAnalyzer Expert traces exist for the libraries, so free barcode concentration cannot be quantified from trace areas. The sequencing instrument is not a patterned flow-cell machine (e.g. HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq), so free-barcode-driven index swapping is not the expected artifact. The goal is detecting/removing swapped molecules in 10x Genomics droplet data — use the DropletUtils molecule-exclusion algorithm instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify free barcode and sequencable cDNA concentrations from BioAnalyzer Expert electropherogram traces collected during scRNA-seq library preparation, by integrating the area under the curve over defined DNA-length windows (45–70 bp for free barcode, 400–800 bp for cDNA). These per-plate ratios are used to test whether free barcode abundance explains barcode-swapping rates on patterned flow-cell instruments such as the HiSeq 4000. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x

These per-plate ratios are used to test whether free barcode abundance explains barcode-swapping rates on patterned flow-cell instruments such as the HiSeq 4000.

skills.description: Use when you have pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns (CSV) for several pairwise biofilm experimental conditions (e.g. AGXX vs silver vs V2A steel, or sucrose/glucose/lactose/xylitol) and need data-driven, quadrant-grouped identification of extremely changing genes.
skills.name: biofilm-transcriptome-visualization
skills.search_text: biofilm-transcriptome-visualization Use when you have pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns (CSV) for several pairwise biofilm experimental conditions (e.g. AGXX vs silver vs V2A steel, or sucrose/glucose/lactose/xylitol) and need data-driven, quadrant-grouped identification of extremely changing genes. You only have raw reads or unprocessed count matrices — the library expects pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in a CSV, not raw RNA-seq or TRANSIT output that still needs normalization/correction. You need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering or extreme-value regions — the README notes that setting the multiplication factor to 1 produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, and the article's contribution is the significance-filtered, extensible scorecard. Data has not been preprocessed by removing low-expression, noise-prone genes and quality control, as the article's workflow assumes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A scorecard-based visualization skill from the Python 'scorecard' library (Nascimben & Rimondini, Curr Microbiol 2025) that groups bacterial biofilm transcriptome genes into quadrant regions of interest by log2 fold-change thresholds and statistical significance, replacing crowded four-way/volcano plots across multiple pairwise experimental comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: A scorecard-based visualization skill from the Python 'scorecard' library (Nascimben & Rimondini, Curr Microbiol 2025) that groups bacterial biofilm transcriptome genes into quadrant regions of interest by log2 fold-change thresholds and statistical significance, replacing crowded four-way/volcano plots across multiple pairwise experimental comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw reads or unprocessed count matrices — the library expects pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in a CSV, not raw RNA-seq or TRANSIT output that still needs normalization/correction. You need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering or extreme-value regions — the README notes that setting the multiplication factor to 1 produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, and the article's contribution is the significance-filtered, extensible scorecard. Data has not been preprocessed by removing low-expression, noise-prone genes and quality control, as the article's workflow assumes.

skills.description: Use when comparing candidate classifiers (e.g., SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree, GBDT), feature selection methods (F score, MRMD, PCC), or feature dimensions on a balanced sequence classification dataset and you need cross-validated Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC tables.
skills.name: bioinformatics-classifier-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: bioinformatics-classifier-metric-evaluation Use when comparing candidate classifiers (e.g., SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree, GBDT), feature selection methods (F score, MRMD, PCC), or feature dimensions on a balanced sequence classification dataset and you need cross-validated Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC tables. The task is single-classifier deployment/inference on new sequences rather than comparative benchmarking (use the Staem5 m5C_predict.py prediction entry point instead). The dataset is heavily imbalanced or not amenable to 10-fold cross-validation, making Acc/MCC comparison across balanced folds misleading. You need a general cross-species m5C model — the article notes species-specific models are necessary and a general model is difficult to develop. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Systematic 10-fold cross-validation benchmarking of bioinformatics classifiers (base models and stacked ensembles) using Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC, as done in Staem5 for m5C site prediction in M. musculus and A. thaliana. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Systematic 10-fold cross-validation benchmarking of bioinformatics classifiers (base models and stacked ensembles) using Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC, as done in Staem5 for m5C site prediction in M. musculus and A. thaliana.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-classifier deployment/inference on new sequences rather than comparative benchmarking (use the Staem5 m5C_predict.py prediction entry point instead). The dataset is heavily imbalanced or not amenable to 10-fold cross-validation, making Acc/MCC comparison across balanced folds misleading. You need a general cross-species m5C model — the article notes species-specific models are necessary and a general model is difficult to develop.

skills.description: Use when computing per-cell biological-process activities from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must decide which of ORIGINS2's 18 BP adjacency edge sets (or a custom PPIN) to use for a given research question.
skills.name: biological-process-edge-set-selection
skills.search_text: biological-process-edge-set-selection Use when computing per-cell biological-process activities from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must decide which of ORIGINS2's 18 BP adjacency edge sets (or a custom PPIN) to use for a given research question. The analysis target is already a per-cell activity or feature table — edge-set selection is only the precursor to running activity(). skills.summary: Selects the appropriate protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) edge sets — the 18 biological-process adjacency edge sets shipped with the ORIGINS2 R package, or custom PPINs built with build_ppin from full_human_ppin — to serve as input to the activity() function for per-cell BP activity computation in scRNA-seq analysis.

skills.description: Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive the corresponding PPIN edge set (adjacency list) for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2.
skills.name: biological-process-gene-list-curation
skills.search_text: biological-process-gene-list-curation Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive the corresponding PPIN edge set (adjacency list) for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2. The biological process of interest is one of the 18 BP already shipped with the package (e.g. differentiation_edges, acute_inflammatory_response_edges) — use the pre-built adjacency list directly instead. You need to compute network activity scores from an expression matrix — that is the separate activity(expression_matrix, adjacency_edges, normalization) step, not PPIN construction. skills.summary: Curates a custom protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) for an arbitrary biological process or user-supplied gene list by overlaying the gene IDs onto the full Human PPIN adjacency list (full_human_ppin) and keeping only edges whose both endpoints belong to the list, as implemented in the ORIGINS2 build_ppin function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process of interest is one of the 18 BP already shipped with the package (e.g. differentiation_edges, acute_inflammatory_response_edges) — use the pre-built adjacency list directly instead. You need to compute network activity scores from an expression matrix — that is the separate activity(expression_matrix, adjacency_edges, normalization) step, not PPIN construction. Your gene identifiers cannot be matched to the node IDs used in the full_human_ppin edge list.

skills.search_text: biological-process-network-selection Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cells) and need per-cell activity scores for a biological process such as cell differentiation, cell cycle, DNA repair, or immune response, or when you must build a custom PPIN from a gene ID list. skills.search_text: biological-sequence-umap-visualization Use when a trained Keras model (tmpMod./tmpWeight.bin from autoBioSeqpy, parameters.txt) must be inspected by embedding its hidden-layer activations for encoded protein/DNA/RNA test sequences in 2D UMAP space. The model contains layers inside a branch — layerUMAP cannot capture hidden outputs from branched layers; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead No trained model exists yet — use autoBioSeqpy's running.py for training/prediction first, then apply layerUMAP The goal is classification accuracy rather than representation inspection — use the model's test metrics, not UMAP embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 layerUMAP, a command-line tool in autoBioSeqpy, projects hidden-layer activations of trained deep learning models onto 2D UMAP embeddings to visualize and dissect how biological sequence representations organize across model depth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105530
skills.summary: layerUMAP, a command-line tool in autoBioSeqpy, projects hidden-layer activations of trained deep learning models onto 2D UMAP embeddings to visualize and dissect how biological sequence representations organize across model depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model contains layers inside a branch — layerUMAP cannot capture hidden outputs from branched layers; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead No trained model exists yet — use autoBioSeqpy's running.py for training/prediction first, then apply layerUMAP The goal is classification accuracy rather than representation inspection — use the model's test metrics, not UMAP embeddings

skills.description: Use when a low-rank approximation of a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix has been computed and technical zeros must be completed while keeping true biological zeros at exactly zero.
skills.name: biological-zero-symmetry-thresholding
skills.search_text: biological-zero-symmetry-thresholding Use when a low-rank approximation of a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix has been computed and technical zeros must be completed while keeping true biological zeros at exactly zero. The matrix is not a sparse, dropout-heavy scRNA-seq count matrix — if there is little zero-inflation (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already imputed data), the symmetry-at-zero rationale does not apply The input matrix has cells as columns — ALRA requires cells as rows and genes as columns, so transpose first instead of applying the thresholding to the wrong orientation The goal is denoising that outputs a dense matrix treating all zeros as missing (as DCA/MAGIC do) rather than zero-preserving imputation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 ALRA's final step: after computing a rank-k SVD approximation of a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, restore true biological zeros by thresholding each gene row at the magnitude of its most negative value, exploiting the fact that entries at biological-zero positions are symmetrically distributed around zero. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: ALRA's final step: after computing a rank-k SVD approximation of a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, restore true biological zeros by thresholding each gene row at the magnitude of its most negative value, exploiting the fact that entries at biological-zero positions are symmetrically distributed around zero.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is not a sparse, dropout-heavy scRNA-seq count matrix — if there is little zero-inflation (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already imputed data), the symmetry-at-zero rationale does not apply The input matrix has cells as columns — ALRA requires cells as rows and genes as columns, so transpose first instead of applying the thresholding to the wrong orientation The goal is denoising that outputs a dense matrix treating all zeros as missing (as DCA/MAGIC do) rather than zero-preserving imputation

skills.description: Use when implementing, re-implementing, or validating BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions on subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE) and you need per-component loss values and correctness checks.
skills.name: biologically-informed-loss-function-implementation
skills.search_text: biologically-informed-loss-function-implementation Use when implementing, re-implementing, or validating BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions on subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE) and you need per-component loss values and correctness checks. You need to run the full segmentation pipeline end-to-end rather than implement/verify loss functions — use the BIDCell run_pipeline workflow (preprocess, train, predict) instead. Input lacks a single-cell reference or positive/negative marker files, since the marker losses require cell-type-specific markers derived from the highest/lowest 10th expression percentiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Implements and evaluates the six biologically-informed self-supervised loss functions of BIDCell (nuclei encapsulation, cell-calling with eccentricity-driven elongated expansion, over-segmentation, overlap, positive-marker, negative-marker) and their weighted-sum total loss, so that segmentation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data is guided by cell-type and morphology knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Implements and evaluates the six biologically-informed self-supervised loss functions of BIDCell (nuclei encapsulation, cell-calling with eccentricity-driven elongated expansion, over-segmentation, overlap, positive-marker, negative-marker) and their weighted-sum total loss, so that segmentation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data is guided by cell-type and morphology knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to run the full segmentation pipeline end-to-end rather than implement/verify loss functions — use the BIDCell run_pipeline workflow (preprocess, train, predict) instead. Input lacks a single-cell reference or positive/negative marker files, since the marker losses require cell-type-specific markers derived from the highest/lowest 10th expression percentiles.

skills.description: Use when you have joint latent embeddings of two or more species' scRNA-seq data from an integration algorithm (e.g. scVI, scANVI, SeuratV4) and need to score species mixing versus biology conservation in the BENGAL benchmark.
skills.name: biology-conservation-metric-scoring
skills.search_text: biology-conservation-metric-scoring Use when you have joint latent embeddings of two or more species' scRNA-seq data from an integration algorithm (e.g. scVI, scANVI, SeuratV4) and need to score species mixing versus biology conservation in the BENGAL benchmark. The cross-species cell type correspondence involves valid non-one-to-one cell type mappings — the benchmark's quantitative scoring assumes one-to-one cell type mappings and known cell type homology Cell type annotations are unreliable or literature-derived cell type homology is uncertain, since the scoring system assumes accurate annotations and confident homology The task is integrative analysis of a single species' batches rather than cross-species integration — species mixing is undefined in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integrations with the 9 established integration metrics plus a new biology conservation metric that quantifies maintenance of cell type distinguishability, as implemented in the BENGAL benchmarking pipeline. It lets a practitioner judge whether an integration algorithm preserved species-specific biology rather than over-mixing cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Scores cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integrations with the 9 established integration metrics plus a new biology conservation metric that quantifies maintenance of cell type distinguishability, as implemented in the BENGAL benchmarking pipeline. It lets a practitioner judge whether an integration algorithm preserved species-specific biology rather than over-mixing cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cross-species cell type correspondence involves valid non-one-to-one cell type mappings — the benchmark's quantitative scoring assumes one-to-one cell type mappings and known cell type homology Cell type annotations are unreliable or literature-derived cell type homology is uncertain, since the scoring system assumes accurate annotations and confident homology The task is integrative analysis of a single species' batches rather than cross-species integration — species mixing is undefined in that setting

skills.description: Use when two trained cell-annotation models (e.g. scaLR DNN vs CellTypist-Logistic) must be compared on how many literature-validated cell-type biomarkers appear in their top-K ranked feature lists.
skills.name: biomarker-comparison-across-annotation-tools
skills.search_text: biomarker-comparison-across-annotation-tools Use when two trained cell-annotation models (e.g. scaLR DNN vs CellTypist-Logistic) must be compared on how many literature-validated cell-type biomarkers appear in their top-K ranked feature lists. When the comparison tool cannot export feature importance (e.g. scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) — no top-K biomarker ranking can be extracted When the question is differential expression between conditions rather than validated cell-type biomarker recall — use the DGE Pseudo bulk/LMEM modules instead When no curated reference markers exist for the cell types of interest (e.g. condition-specific genes such as COVID-19/normal), recall against CellMarker2.0 is not well defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks annotation/biomarker-discovery platforms by extracting each tool's per-class top-K gene rankings (e.g. top-100) and scoring their overlap with curated literature marker references (CellMarker2.0), summarized as per-cell-type recall counts and gene recall curves. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Benchmarks annotation/biomarker-discovery platforms by extracting each tool's per-class top-K gene rankings (e.g. top-100) and scoring their overlap with curated literature marker references (CellMarker2.0), summarized as per-cell-type recall counts and gene recall curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison tool cannot export feature importance (e.g. scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) — no top-K biomarker ranking can be extracted When the question is differential expression between conditions rather than validated cell-type biomarker recall — use the DGE Pseudo bulk/LMEM modules instead When no curated reference markers exist for the cell types of interest (e.g. condition-specific genes such as COVID-19/normal), recall against CellMarker2.0 is not well defined

skills.description: Use when reproducing a gene-expression signature where the expected direction of change is known (e.g. MCEMP1 up, HLA-DRA down), and you must verify that multiple perturbation conditions (viral proteins vs GFP control) recapitulate that pattern on a majority basis.
skills.name: biomarker-direction-validation
skills.search_text: biomarker-direction-validation Use when reproducing a gene-expression signature where the expected direction of change is known (e.g. MCEMP1 up, HLA-DRA down), and you must verify that multiple perturbation conditions (viral proteins vs GFP control) recapitulate that pattern on a majority basis. When the goal is statistical significance testing (p-values, BH adjustment) rather than sign-of-fold-change concordance — use the severity-vs-mild differential expression analysis from the COVID19-severity app instead When only one condition is being tested (no multiple perturbations to count a majority over), the fraction-based acceptance rule is not meaningful When the expected direction of the biomarker signature has not been established from prior cohorts http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A directional concordance check that validates whether a perturbation experiment reproduces a reported biomarker signature by counting the fraction of conditions showing the expected fold-change direction. Here, MCEMP1 log2FC must be positive and HLA-DRA log2FC negative relative to GFP control for a majority (>50%) of SARS-CoV-2 viral-protein transfection conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: A directional concordance check that validates whether a perturbation experiment reproduces a reported biomarker signature by counting the fraction of conditions showing the expected fold-change direction. Here, MCEMP1 log2FC must be positive and HLA-DRA log2FC negative relative to GFP control for a majority (>50%) of SARS-CoV-2 viral-protein transfection conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is statistical significance testing (p-values, BH adjustment) rather than sign-of-fold-change concordance — use the severity-vs-mild differential expression analysis from the COVID19-severity app instead When only one condition is being tested (no multiple perturbations to count a majority over), the fraction-based acceptance rule is not meaningful When the expected direction of the biomarker signature has not been established from prior cohorts

skills.description: Use when a large network-derived gene community (IC genes) must be reduced to a compact, classification-ready biomarker list and you have per-community gene files plus normal/cancer expression matrices available.
skills.name: biomarker-gene-list-generation
skills.search_text: biomarker-gene-list-generation Use when a large network-derived gene community (IC genes) must be reduced to a compact, classification-ready biomarker list and you have per-community gene files plus normal/cancer expression matrices available. When communities have not yet been extracted: this skill expects 'IC_'+str(tumor)+'.csv' files produced after Gephi modularity community detection on the fused co-expression network When the goal is differential expression-based biomarker identification: the paper treats DE genes as a baseline gene signature to compare against, not as the output of this LASSO-on-communities step When the gene set is already a small, classification-ready signature: re-applying L1 shrinkage would re-reduce an already compact feature list http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Selects a compact representative biomarker list (ICL genes) from each extracted gene community (IC genes) by fitting LASSO (L1-regularized) regression on the community's TCGA expression profiles and keeping only genes with non-zero coefficients, per cancer type, for downstream Random Forest normal/cancer classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Selects a compact representative biomarker list (ICL genes) from each extracted gene community (IC genes) by fitting LASSO (L1-regularized) regression on the community's TCGA expression profiles and keeping only genes with non-zero coefficients, per cancer type, for downstream Random Forest normal/cancer classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When communities have not yet been extracted: this skill expects 'IC_'+str(tumor)+'.csv' files produced after Gephi modularity community detection on the fused co-expression network When the goal is differential expression-based biomarker identification: the paper treats DE genes as a baseline gene signature to compare against, not as the output of this LASSO-on-communities step When the gene set is already a small, classification-ready signature: re-applying L1 shrinkage would re-reduce an already compact feature list

skills.name: biomarker-novelty-classification
skills.search_text: biomarker-novelty-classification Use when IC gene symbol lists from the fused co-expression pipeline must be triaged into drug-actionable versus literature-novel candidate biomarkers per cancer type (KIRC, LIHC, PRAD). The fused co-expression networks have not yet been built and IC gene communities not yet extracted with Gephi (run Pipeline.ipynb first — this skill consumes IC_*.csv lists, not raw TCGA expression or network files) The goal is functional/pathway characterization (g:Profiler GO:BP and KEGG enrichment) rather than drug actionability and literature-novelty classification Genes of interest are differentially expressed (DESeq2) baseline biomarkers rather than IC genes from the fused networks http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 Cross-references IC genes extracted from fused KIRC/LIHC/PRAD co-expression networks against DrugBank pharmacologically-active-target annotations and PubMed literature to label each gene as drug actionable and/or a novel candidate biomarker for its cancer type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: The fused co-expression networks have not yet been built and IC gene communities not yet extracted with Gephi (run Pipeline.ipynb first — this skill consumes IC_*.csv lists, not raw TCGA expression or network files) The goal is functional/pathway characterization (g:Profiler GO:BP and KEGG enrichment) rather than drug actionability and literature-novelty classification Genes of interest are differentially expressed (DESeq2) baseline biomarkers rather than IC genes from the fused networks

skills.description: Use when a clustering method claims to support downstream DEG analysis and you must verify that recovered marker genes match those reported in the paper's supplementary figures.
skills.name: biomarker-recovery-verification-against-supplementary-figures
skills.search_text: biomarker-recovery-verification-against-supplementary-figures Use when a clustering method claims to support downstream DEG analysis and you must verify that recovered marker genes match those reported in the paper's supplementary figures. The analysis goal is evaluating clustering accuracy (NMI/Purity/ARI) rather than verifying that clustering supports downstream DEG recovery Input labels are ground-truth annotations rather than SSRE-inferred cluster labels, so the validation does not test the method's claimed extension to DEG identification The dataset is not the one for which the supplementary marker list was published, since the marker set is figure- and dataset-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates a downstream differential-expression analysis by checking whether a Kruskal-Wallis test on SSRE-inferred cluster labels recovers the marker genes reported in the paper's supplementary figure (Figure S2: NLRP11, NLRP4, CLEC10A, H1FOO, GDF9, OTX2, ACCSL, TUBB8, TUBB4Q on the Yan dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Validates a downstream differential-expression analysis by checking whether a Kruskal-Wallis test on SSRE-inferred cluster labels recovers the marker genes reported in the paper's supplementary figure (Figure S2: NLRP11, NLRP4, CLEC10A, H1FOO, GDF9, OTX2, ACCSL, TUBB8, TUBB4Q on the Yan dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is evaluating clustering accuracy (NMI/Purity/ARI) rather than verifying that clustering supports downstream DEG recovery Input labels are ground-truth annotations rather than SSRE-inferred cluster labels, so the validation does not test the method's claimed extension to DEG identification The dataset is not the one for which the supplementary marker list was published, since the marker set is figure- and dataset-specific

skills.description: Use when evaluating a marker-gene thresholding baseline for cell-type mapping: target cells must be assigned to reference clusters using top cluster markers alone, and the Classified/Ambiguous/Orphan fractions must be quantified.
skills.name: biomarker-threshold-cell-classification
skills.search_text: biomarker-threshold-cell-classification Use when evaluating a marker-gene thresholding baseline for cell-type mapping: target cells must be assigned to reference clusters using top cluster markers alone, and the Classified/Ambiguous/Orphan fractions must be quantified. When the goal is accurate cross-dataset cell-type mapping rather than benchmarking the baseline — the article shows this approach 'does not work effectively owing to the dropout problem', so use scID's full scid_multiclass pipeline instead When data are log-transformed — scID's normalization requires raw or library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized values, not log-transformed data When the reference lacks well-defined cluster-specific gene signatures — scID is 'not a recommended approach' in that case, and the top-two-marker baseline would be even less reliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduces the paper's biomarker-based baseline that assigns target scRNA-seq cells to reference clusters using only the top two marker genes per cluster with per-gene expression thresholds, categorizing cells as Classified, Ambiguous, or Orphan to quantify how dropout limits simple marker-threshold classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Reproduces the paper's biomarker-based baseline that assigns target scRNA-seq cells to reference clusters using only the top two marker genes per cluster with per-gene expression thresholds, categorizing cells as Classified, Ambiguous, or Orphan to quantify how dropout limits simple marker-threshold classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accurate cross-dataset cell-type mapping rather than benchmarking the baseline — the article shows this approach 'does not work effectively owing to the dropout problem', so use scID's full scid_multiclass pipeline instead When data are log-transformed — scID's normalization requires raw or library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized values, not log-transformed data When the reference lacks well-defined cluster-specific gene signatures — scID is 'not a recommended approach' in that case, and the top-two-marker baseline would be even less reliable

skills.description: Use when transcriptomic CSVs contain pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control biomaterial comparisons (e.g., AGXX® vs silver vs V2A steel), and you need quadrant classification plus time-course tracking of extreme genes.
skills.name: biomaterial-exposure-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: biomaterial-exposure-differential-expression-analysis Use when transcriptomic CSVs contain pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control biomaterial comparisons (e.g., AGXX® vs silver vs V2A steel), and you need quadrant classification plus time-course tracking of extreme genes. The CSV does not contain pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns per comparison — raw count matrices must first be processed upstream (e.g., via TRANSIT resampling with beta-geometric normalization for Tn-seq data). You need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering — setting the multiplication factor to 1 produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, so the scorecard quadrant logic should not be applied. The dataset was not preprocessed by removing low-expression, noise-prone genes and quality control, as the scorecard assumes cleaned differential-expression values. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies the Python scorecard library (scorecard_functions) to classify genes into significance/fold-change quadrants across pairwise biomaterial-exposure comparisons, and longitudinally tracks extreme expression changes over time points (e.g., E. faecalis on AGXX®, silver-coated, and uncoated V2A steel). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Applies the Python scorecard library (scorecard_functions) to classify genes into significance/fold-change quadrants across pairwise biomaterial-exposure comparisons, and longitudinally tracks extreme expression changes over time points (e.g., E. faecalis on AGXX®, silver-coated, and uncoated V2A steel).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CSV does not contain pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns per comparison — raw count matrices must first be processed upstream (e.g., via TRANSIT resampling with beta-geometric normalization for Tn-seq data). You need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering — setting the multiplication factor to 1 produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, so the scorecard quadrant logic should not be applied. The dataset was not preprocessed by removing low-expression, noise-prone genes and quality control, as the scorecard assumes cleaned differential-expression values.

skills.description: Use when you have annotated genome assemblies (.gbk) across a genus-scale dataset and need BGC predictions, GCF clustering at a defined distance cutoff, and a binary GCF-by-genome matrix for lifestyle association testing.
skills.name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-prediction
skills.search_text: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-prediction Use when you have annotated genome assemblies (.gbk) across a genus-scale dataset and need BGC predictions, GCF clustering at a defined distance cutoff, and a binary GCF-by-genome matrix for lifestyle association testing. Input is raw reads or unannotated assemblies without a prior gene-annotation step producing .gbk files, since antiSMASH requires .gbk input The analysis goal is lifestyle prediction from gene clusters via machine learning (bacLIFE's lifestyle-prediction module), not secondary-metabolite BGC/GCF analysis Only a small number of genomes is available and a genus-scale comparative BGC matrix is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3314 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Predict and cluster biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) from annotated bacterial genomes into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs) and build a GCF absence/presence matrix, as implemented in the bacLIFE clustering module with antiSMASH 5.1.2 and BiG-SCAPE 1.1.5. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Predict and cluster biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) from annotated bacterial genomes into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs) and build a GCF absence/presence matrix, as implemented in the bacLIFE clustering module with antiSMASH 5.1.2 and BiG-SCAPE 1.1.5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or unannotated assemblies without a prior gene-annotation step producing .gbk files, since antiSMASH requires .gbk input The analysis goal is lifestyle prediction from gene clusters via machine learning (bacLIFE's lifestyle-prediction module), not secondary-metabolite BGC/GCF analysis Only a small number of genomes is available and a genus-scale comparative BGC matrix is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you have K base partitions of a cell-by-feature latent embedding (e.g. from a dual denoising autoencoder) and need a single consensus cell clustering that exploits cell-to-cluster relationships.
skills.name: bipartite-graph-construction-from-clusterings
skills.search_text: bipartite-graph-construction-from-clusterings Use when you have K base partitions of a cell-by-feature latent embedding (e.g. from a dual denoising autoencoder) and need a single consensus cell clustering that exploits cell-to-cluster relationships. Input is raw scRNA-seq count data rather than a learned latent representation from the autoencoder — preprocessing and SDDA must run first You need only a single flat clustering with no ensemble/consensus step — plain K-means on the embedding suffices No MATLAB environment available and no equivalent implementation of the transfer cut generalized eigen-problem is at hand http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a bipartite graph whose nodes are cells and K-means basic clusters (affinity matrix B with bij=1 if cell zi belongs to cluster Cj), then reduces it via the transfer cut criterion to a small cluster-only graph G_R to obtain a graph-based consensus clustering of scRNA-seq latent embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Constructs a bipartite graph whose nodes are cells and K-means basic clusters (affinity matrix B with bij=1 if cell zi belongs to cluster Cj), then reduces it via the transfer cut criterion to a small cluster-only graph G_R to obtain a graph-based consensus clustering of scRNA-seq latent embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq count data rather than a learned latent representation from the autoencoder — preprocessing and SDDA must run first You need only a single flat clustering with no ensemble/consensus step — plain K-means on the embedding suffices No MATLAB environment available and no equivalent implementation of the transfer cut generalized eigen-problem is at hand

skills.description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets via minimum-weight matching: after Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing and anchor identification, a cross-dataset weighted graph must be built before matching.
skills.name: bipartite-graph-construction-with-euclidean-edge-weights
skills.search_text: bipartite-graph-construction-with-euclidean-edge-weights Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets via minimum-weight matching: after Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing and anchor identification, a cross-dataset weighted graph must be built before matching. More than two datasets must be integrated — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets Expression values have not been normalized to log-counts (e.g. raw counts or non-Seurat V3.0 pre-processed matrices), since edge weights are computed in the pre-processed gene space Data are not single-cell expression matrices where cell-to-cell Euclidean distances in gene space are meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs the weighted bipartite anchor graph at the heart of the BATMAN scRNA-seq integration method: one partition per dataset, nodes are representative anchor cells, and edges between cross-dataset anchors are weighted by Euclidean distance in N-dimensional gene (log-count) space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Constructs the weighted bipartite anchor graph at the heart of the BATMAN scRNA-seq integration method: one partition per dataset, nodes are representative anchor cells, and edges between cross-dataset anchors are weighted by Euclidean distance in N-dimensional gene (log-count) space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: More than two datasets must be integrated — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets Expression values have not been normalized to log-counts (e.g. raw counts or non-Seurat V3.0 pre-processed matrices), since edge weights are computed in the pre-processed gene space Data are not single-cell expression matrices where cell-to-cell Euclidean distances in gene space are meaningful

skills.description: Use when you need to visually explore bipartite relationships between two entity types, such as KEGG pathways and the top-ranked eeSNV genes annotated to them, following enrichment analysis.

skills.search_text: bipartite-network-visualization Use when you need to visually explore bipartite relationships between two entity types, such as KEGG pathways and the top-ranked eeSNV genes annotated to them, following enrichment analysis. When relationships are not bipartite (e.g. gene-gene co-expression), a plain force-directed graph without bipartite structure is more appropriate When quantitative enrichment statistics alone suffice and no interactive exploration of gene-pathway membership is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs a bipartite pathway-gene graph (edge: gene annotated to pathway, e.g. from KEGG enrichment via DAVID) and renders it with force-directed graph drawing (spring-like attractive forces, electrical repulsions) in Gephi or Cytoscape to explore the bipartite relationships interactively. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5

skills.description: Use when you need proliferation-rate estimates for single-cell time-series modeling but lack direct lineage-traced descendant counts — e.g. supplying growth weights (data_pt['w']) to PRESCIENT from expression data only.
skills.name: birth-death-score-estimation
skills.search_text: birth-death-score-estimation Use when you need proliferation-rate estimates for single-cell time-series modeling but lack direct lineage-traced descendant counts — e.g. supplying growth weights (data_pt['w']) to PRESCIENT from expression data only. Empirical lineage-traced descendant counts are already available (e.g. the weinreb-interpolate task uses ground truth proliferation rates directly rather than expression-derived estimates). The dataset's lowly-expressed genes critical to the cell-cycle or apoptosis gene sets were dropped during pre-processing — scoring on dropout-heavy expression will be unreliable. The task requires causal attribution of individual genes to fate outcomes rather than an aggregate proliferation score. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Estimates per-cell proliferation (birth–death) rates from normalized scRNA-seq expression alone by scoring KEGG cell-cycle and apoptosis gene sets, smoothing across a k-NN graph in PCA space, and fitting a logistic model to produce growth weights for PRESCIENT training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Estimates per-cell proliferation (birth–death) rates from normalized scRNA-seq expression alone by scoring KEGG cell-cycle and apoptosis gene sets, smoothing across a k-NN graph in PCA space, and fitting a logistic model to produce growth weights for PRESCIENT training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Empirical lineage-traced descendant counts are already available (e.g. the weinreb-interpolate task uses ground truth proliferation rates directly rather than expression-derived estimates). The dataset's lowly-expressed genes critical to the cell-cycle or apoptosis gene sets were dropped during pre-processing — scoring on dropout-heavy expression will be unreliable. skills.description: Use when selecting reliable cycling-gene inputs for DeepCycle: candidate genes from a GOterm cell_cycle list must be checked in unspliced-spliced space (scVelo Ms/Mu layers) for multiple maxima before phase inference.

skills.search_text: bivariate-gaussian-fitting-unspliced-spliced-space Use when selecting reliable cycling-gene inputs for DeepCycle: candidate genes from a GOterm cell_cycle list must be checked in unspliced-spliced space (scVelo Ms/Mu layers) for multiple maxima before phase inference. Genes that show only a single expression state in unspliced-spliced space — the Hotelling filter will correctly exclude them, so do not force them into the reliable-gene list Data lacking scVelo-computed 'Ms' and 'Mu' moment layers — the mixture fit requires the imputed unspliced-spliced reads from pp.moments Datasets where no genes pass the expression threshold and zero cycling genes are found — the paper warns such DeepCycle results will not be reliable and sequencing depth should be increased instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identifies reliably cycling genes for DeepCycle by fitting a two-component bivariate Gaussian mixture to each gene's (spliced, unspliced) read distribution and applying a Hotelling T2 test, retaining genes whose mixture shows at least two distinct expression maxima. This isolates genes with more than one expression state, which underpin robust transcriptional-phase inference (n = 158 such genes for the mESC analysis). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8

skills.search_text: block-permutation-significance-testing Use when a TE-based (or other feature-based) cell clustering must be compared to a reference clustering (e.g., gene-expression-based Leiden/Louvain labels) and a raw ARI alone is insufficient — an empirical significance p-value is needed. No reference clustering exists to compare against (ARI requires two labelings of the same cells). Cells carry no meaningful local neighborhood structure, so block-wise label permutation adds no valid constraint over simple iid permutation. The task is TE quantification itself (read allocation to loci) rather than downstream significance assessment of clustering agreement — use MATES quantification modules instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A statistical validation procedure that assigns empirical p-values to clustering-agreement metrics (e.g., Adjusted Rand Index) by permuting cluster labels in blocks, preserving local neighborhood structure, as used to benchmark MATES versus scTE and SoloTE on Arabidopsis and Drosophila scRNA-seq TE clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7

skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference clustering exists to compare against (ARI requires two labelings of the same cells). Cells carry no meaningful local neighborhood structure, so block-wise label permutation adds no valid constraint over simple iid permutation. The task is TE quantification itself (read allocation to loci) rather than downstream significance assessment of clustering agreement — use MATES quantification modules instead.

The application requires exact (no-false-positive) membership answers — PAC is an AMQ structure, like Cobs and Sequence Bloom Tree tools, that only lists datasets that may contain the query The target collection exceeds the file-count ceiling of the chosen integer width, e.g. more than 256 files with -e 8 or more than 65,636 with the default 16-bit encoding Indexing k-mers seen only once matters, since PAC filters singletons by default in -u mode and the -u option restricts indexing to k-mers seen at least twice http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Encodes the nested series of Bloom filters (Rt⊆…⊆R1) found along the internal nodes of PAC's comb trees as an Aggregated Bloom filter: a t×b matrix of stacked filters compressed into a run-length integer array V of size b, which PAC composes into partitioned aggregated Bloom comb trees for approximate membership queries over dataset collections. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225

skills.description: Use when benchmarking approximate membership query structures (e.g., PAC, Cobs, HowDeSBT) on large collections of FASTA/FASTQ genomes, or when deciding how many Aggregated Bloom Comb trees to enable for sequence search.

skills.search_text: bloom-filter-approximate-membership-query Use when benchmarking approximate membership query structures (e.g., PAC, Cobs, HowDeSBT) on large collections of FASTA/FASTQ genomes, or when deciding how many Aggregated Bloom Comb trees to enable for sequence search. The task requires exact sequence alignment or full BLAST-like sensitivity rather than approximate membership listing of candidate datasets (PAC is an AMQ with Bloom-filter false positives). The index must be queried with a single sequence against a small collection where BLAST-like search is already routine. More than 65,536 files must be indexed without adjusting the -e encoding option, since the default 16-bit integers cap the index at ~65,636 files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb trees), a Bloom-filter-based approximate membership query (AMQ) structure that lists which datasets in a collection may contain a query sequence, comparing index configurations with zero, one, or two Aggregated Bloom Comb trees. Quantifies how aggregated Bloom filters accelerate queries several-fold on dissimilar batches while giving little benefit on highly similar batches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
