skills.description: Use when building a PAC index over a collection of FASTA/FASTQ datasets and you must choose the Bloom filter size (-b) trade-off, e.g. 2^27-bit vs 2^29-bit filters, balancing false positive rate against index size and RAM.
skills.name: bloom-filter-size-parameterization
skills.search_text: bloom-filter-size-parameterization Use when building a PAC index over a collection of FASTA/FASTQ datasets and you must choose the Bloom filter size (-b) trade-off, e.g. 2^27-bit vs 2^29-bit filters, balancing false positive rate against index size and RAM. You are querying or updating an already-built PAC index (-l mode) rather than sizing a new construction — this skill only governs construction-time filter sizing Your application cannot tolerate any false positives: PAC is an approximate membership query (AMQ) structure and Bloom filter sizing only tunes, never eliminates, the FP rate Disk budget is fixed and small: raising -b from 2^27 to 2^29 bits grew the 661k-genome index from 1.4 TB to 2.4 TB, so oversized filters may be infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Sets the PAC indexed Bloom filter size via the -b parameter, where each filter is rounded up to the first power of two above the given value. This is the key trade-off knob: larger filters (e.g. 2^29 vs 2^27 bits) lower the false positive rate but inflate RAM usage during construction and the on-disk index size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225

The sample is expected to have low-level chimerism below the method's detection limit (K=1 selection only indicates mixture fraction below detection, determined at 4% of 6,000 cells in in silico mixing) Clinical chimerism reporting is required for patient management — this method is aspirational ('in the near future') and not yet clinically validated The input is already an annotated feature/cell-type matrix without SNV-level genotype information, so host/donor inference de novo is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A de novo SNV-based single-cell chimerism and cell-type composition workflow that assigns host/donor origin to BMMCs from scRNA-seq transcriptomes (STAR + Cell Ranger + Freebayes 1.0.2 + Seurat) and quantifies subpopulation shifts (erythroid expansion, immature granulocytes, monocytopenia) across pre/post transplant timepoints in AML patients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: A de novo SNV-based single-cell chimerism and cell-type composition workflow that assigns host/donor origin to BMMCs from scRNA-seq transcriptomes (STAR + Cell Ranger + Freebayes 1.0.2 + Seurat) and quantifies subpopulation shifts (erythroid expansion, immature granulocytes, monocytopenia) across pre/post transplant timepoints in AML patients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is expected to have low-level chimerism below the method's detection limit (K=1 selection only indicates mixture fraction below detection, determined at 4% of 6,000 cells in in silico mixing) Clinical chimerism reporting is required for patient management — this method is aspirational ('in the near future') and not yet clinically validated The input is already an annotated feature/cell-type matrix without SNV-level genotype information, so host/donor inference de novo is impossible

skills.description: Use when comparing method runtimes (or similar paired measurements) across multiple dataset sizes — e.g., AnnSQL vs AnnData filter/query timings at 14 simulated cell counts — and per-size significance must be controlled for multiple testing.
skills.name: bonferroni-corrected-paired-t-test-comparison
skills.search_text: bonferroni-corrected-paired-t-test-comparison Use when comparing method runtimes (or similar paired measurements) across multiple dataset sizes — e.g., AnnSQL vs AnnData filter/query timings at 14 simulated cell counts — and per-size significance must be controlled for multiple testing. When only a single runtime measurement per method per dataset size exists — the paired t-test requires repeated paired trials at each size When the goal is a general performance claim rather than a per-dataset-size statistical comparison — a single aggregate runtime plot suffices without correction When the compared runtimes come from different query operations per method (not paired equivalents), since pairing is the basis of the test http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Statistical procedure from the AnnSQL benchmark in which paired t-tests compare runtimes of AnnSQL (in-memory and on-disk) versus AnnData (backed and in-memory) at each simulated dataset size (1,000–250,000 cells × 10,000 genes), with the significance alpha Bonferroni-corrected as 0.05 divided by the number of dataset-size comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbaf105
skills.summary: Statistical procedure from the AnnSQL benchmark in which paired t-tests compare runtimes of AnnSQL (in-memory and on-disk) versus AnnData (backed and in-memory) at each simulated dataset size (1,000–250,000 cells × 10,000 genes), with the significance alpha Bonferroni-corrected as 0.05 divided by the number of dataset-size comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single runtime measurement per method per dataset size exists — the paired t-test requires repeated paired trials at each size When the goal is a general performance claim rather than a per-dataset-size statistical comparison — a single aggregate runtime plot suffices without correction When the compared runtimes come from different query operations per method (not paired equivalents), since pairing is the basis of the test

When only a single filtering step (not multiple) is being compared, so no Bonferroni correction over steps is needed When the positive class is not experimentally planted/tracked per step, so per-step fate of chimeras cannot be recorded http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistical validation procedure from the Bellerophon chimera-removal study: compare per-filter chimera removal percentages against non-chimera removal percentages across replicate spiked assemblies using an unpaired t test followed by Bonferroni correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571

skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a handful of pre-specified genes are tested and a family-wise correction across 11,231 genes would be overly conservative and unnecessary When the goal is FDR control at a desired discovery rate rather than strict family-wise error control, since Bonferroni is the most conservative choice When sample sizes are below ~50 individuals, where the article notes CTMM tests are not reliable and corrected p-values would be untrustworthy

skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when a large family of statistical tests (e.g., 1641 motif enrichment Wilcoxon tests over a gene set) must be jointly thresholded, and raw p-values would otherwise yield inflated false positives. skills.summary: Applies Bonferroni correction to control family-wise error rate when testing many hypotheses simultaneously, as in this workflow where Wilcoxon motif-enrichment p-values are computed across 1641 JASPAR 2020 vertebrate PWMs and corrected before comparing unaugmented versus CODAL-augmented MIRA regulatory potential models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one or very few hypotheses are tested, where the m-fold penalty is unnecessary and only costs power Discovery-oriented analyses where controlling family-wise error rate is too conservative and FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg) control is the appropriate criterion P-values that are not independent or are the result of dependent post-hoc comparisons the correction was not designed to cover

skills.description: Use when testing many source–sink causal paths per subnetwork (SEMace effect='source2sink') or declaring perturbed nodes/edges in SEMtree modules, and family-wise error control at alpha=0.05 is needed.
skills.name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when testing many source–sink causal paths per subnetwork (SEMace effect='source2sink') or declaring perturbed nodes/edges in SEMtree modules, and family-wise error control at alpha=0.05 is needed. When false discovery rate rather than family-wise error control is the target — the paper's own SEMace example uses method = 'BH' (Benjamini–Hochberg), which is the less conservative alternative for exploratory scans. When the family of hypotheses is undefined or tests are not part of a single source–sink enumeration per module, since Bonferroni depends on knowing the exact number of tested paths. When testing a single pre-specified path without a multiplicity burden — correction would only reduce power. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Family-wise multiple-testing correction applied to Average Causal Effect (ACE) P-values over directed source–sink paths (SEMace) and to deconfounding steps (SEMbap) when comparing perturbation across subnetworks. In the SEMtree COVID-19 workflow it controls the 5% error rate when testing many X->Y paths per CAT module, yielding Bonferroni-combined P-values (PVAL(E)) used to rank the seven extracted subnetworks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Family-wise multiple-testing correction applied to Average Causal Effect (ACE) P-values over directed source–sink paths (SEMace) and to deconfounding steps (SEMbap) when comparing perturbation across subnetworks. In the SEMtree COVID-19 workflow it controls the 5% error rate when testing many X->Y paths per CAT module, yielding Bonferroni-combined P-values (PVAL(E)) used to rank the seven extracted subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When false discovery rate rather than family-wise error control is the target — the paper's own SEMace example uses method = 'BH' (Benjamini–Hochberg), which is the less conservative alternative for exploratory scans. When the family of hypotheses is undefined or tests are not part of a single source–sink enumeration per module, since Bonferroni depends on knowing the exact number of tested paths. When testing a single pre-specified path without a multiplicity burden — correction would only reduce power.

skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when a per-gene model (e.g., the negative binomial GLM with Time, Group, and Time-by-Group interaction) yields thousands of raw p-values that must be Bonferroni-adjusted before calling tDEGs at p.cutoff = 0.05. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is expected-discovery (FDR) control rather than family-wise error control — Bonferroni is the strictest adjustment and CASi applies it specifically to support the p.cutoff = 0.05 tDEG criterion When there are no repeated statistical tests to correct (a single model fit), since Bonferroni adjustment requires a defined family of tests

skills.description: Use when many module-level or gene-set-level statistics (e.g., dozens of leiden-derived GRN module scores) are tested against the same phenotype and individual uncorrected p-values would inflate the false positive rate.
skills.name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when many module-level or gene-set-level statistics (e.g., dozens of leiden-derived GRN module scores) are tested against the same phenotype and individual uncorrected p-values would inflate the false positive rate. Only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested, so no multiplicity correction is needed The analysis goal is to control expected false discoveries rather than any false positive occurring (an FDR procedure such as Benjamini-Hochberg is the appropriate choice, not family-wise Bonferroni) Module p-values are not comparable across the same family of tests (e.g., different phenotypes with unrelated nulls) without redefining the correction family http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Bonferroni family-wise correction when testing many SCING GRN modules simultaneously for association with a phenotype (e.g., amyloid beta plaque burden and age in mouse AD Visium data), so that per-module Pearson correlation p-values are judged against the number of modules tested. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Apply Bonferroni family-wise correction when testing many SCING GRN modules simultaneously for association with a phenotype (e.g., amyloid beta plaque burden and age in mouse AD Visium data), so that per-module Pearson correlation p-values are judged against the number of modules tested.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single pre-specified hypothesis is tested, so no multiplicity correction is needed The analysis goal is to control expected false discoveries rather than any false positive occurring (an FDR procedure such as Benjamini-Hochberg is the appropriate choice, not family-wise Bonferroni) Module p-values are not comparable across the same family of tests (e.g., different phenotypes with unrelated nulls) without redefining the correction family

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix and a refined candidate TF list (or base GRN from scATAC-seq + motifs) for <200 target genes, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just TF-target edges) governing each target in a specific cell type or tissue.
skills.name: boolean-logic-gate-inference
skills.search_text: boolean-logic-gate-inference Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix and a refined candidate TF list (or base GRN from scATAC-seq + motifs) for <200 target genes, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just TF-target edges) governing each target in a specific cell type or tissue. Large-scale de novo network inference over many genes: scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list based on external hints Pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or when temporal delays in regulation must be modeled — scGATE does not yet handle this Decoding Boolean logic involving more than 5 transcriptional regulators per target, where overfitting is a major concern http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infers context-specific Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOT combinations) among candidate TFs regulating target genes from scRNA-seq data using scGATE, which fits a zero-inflated mixture likelihood over 2^k logic combinations with EM-updated priors and ranks gates by log10 Bayes Factor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Infers context-specific Boolean logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOT combinations) among candidate TFs regulating target genes from scRNA-seq data using scGATE, which fits a zero-inflated mixture likelihood over 2^k logic combinations with EM-updated priors and ranks gates by log10 Bayes Factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Large-scale de novo network inference over many genes: scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined candidate TF list based on external hints Pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or when temporal delays in regulation must be modeled — scGATE does not yet handle this Decoding Boolean logic involving more than 5 transcriptional regulators per target, where overfitting is a major concern

skills.search_text: boolean-logic-rule-assignment Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix is available and a draft Boolean Network model in SBML-qual format is needed for further manual editing or simulation. The user needs a final, validated Boolean model rather than a first draft — Augusta's BNs 'should be treated with caution as they rather present first drafts than final BNs' No refined GRN exists yet — the conversion stage requires the upstream GRN refinement output, not raw RNA-Seq count tables The organism's curated Boolean models must be fully accurate from the start without manual editing — the draft requires subsequent manual curation in SBML form http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Augusta's conversion of a refined Gene Regulatory Network (adjacency matrix) into a draft Boolean Network by transferring curated Boolean functions from the Cell Collective database where possible and generating generic logical rules (OR for same-sign edges, AND with NOT for mixed-sign edges), exported as an SBML-qual file. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013

skills.when_to_use_negative: The user needs a final, validated Boolean model rather than a first draft — Augusta's BNs 'should be treated with caution as they rather present first drafts than final BNs' No refined GRN exists yet — the conversion stage requires the upstream GRN refinement output, not raw RNA-Seq count tables The organism's curated Boolean models must be fully accurate from the start without manual editing — the draft requires subsequent manual curation in SBML form

skills.description: Use when you have scBONITA-learned Boolean rules for a pathway (e.g., a GRAPHML KEGG topology like hsa00010) plus binarized single-cell expression states and need to map each cell to a characteristic signaling state.
skills.name: boolean-network-attractor-analysis
skills.search_text: boolean-network-attractor-analysis Use when you have scBONITA-learned Boolean rules for a pathway (e.g., a GRAPHML KEGG topology like hsa00010) plus binarized single-cell expression states and need to map each cell to a characteristic signaling state. The analysis goal is differential gene expression or conventional over-representation analysis (ORA) — the article showed ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes, but attractor analysis is also not a DE method No executable Boolean rules have been inferred for the pathway (run Rule_Inference_With_scBONITA first; attractor analysis consumes the learned rules) The expression data are not single-cell states to be mapped — bulk state vectors are not the intended input for per-cell attractor assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates scBONITA-inferred discrete (Boolean) state models of signaling pathways until trajectories fall into steady states (attractors), then assigns each sequenced single cell to its closest attractor via Hamming distance, enabling pathway-based characterization of cellular states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Simulates scBONITA-inferred discrete (Boolean) state models of signaling pathways until trajectories fall into steady states (attractors), then assigns each sequenced single cell to its closest attractor via Hamming distance, enabling pathway-based characterization of cellular states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential gene expression or conventional over-representation analysis (ORA) — the article showed ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes, but attractor analysis is also not a DE method No executable Boolean rules have been inferred for the pathway (run Rule_Inference_With_scBONITA first; attractor analysis consumes the learned rules) The expression data are not single-cell states to be mapped — bulk state vectors are not the intended input for per-cell attractor assignment

skills.description: Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix is available and a draft Boolean model suitable for further manual editing (SBML-qual) is needed, especially for organisms with or without models in the Cell Collective database.
skills.name: boolean-network-inference-from-grn
skills.search_text: boolean-network-inference-from-grn Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix is available and a draft Boolean model suitable for further manual editing (SBML-qual) is needed, especially for organisms with or without models in the Cell Collective database. No GRN has been inferred/refined yet — the conversion expects the refined GRN adjacency matrix, not raw RNA-Seq count tables (use RNASeq_to_BN instead). A final, fully validated Boolean model is required — Augusta BNs are first drafts, not final networks. The goal is dynamic network simulation rather than drafting a logical model (e.g. SQUAD-style GUI simulation). http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Converts a refined Gene Regulatory Network (adjacency matrix) into a draft Boolean Network by transferring curated Boolean functions from the Cell Collective database where target gene and all transcription factors match, and by building generic logical rules (OR for same-sign edges, AND with NOT for mixed-sign edges) for remaining nodes, exported as an SBML-qual file via CellNOpt. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Converts a refined Gene Regulatory Network (adjacency matrix) into a draft Boolean Network by transferring curated Boolean functions from the Cell Collective database where target gene and all transcription factors match, and by building generic logical rules (OR for same-sign edges, AND with NOT for mixed-sign edges) for remaining nodes, exported as an SBML-qual file via CellNOpt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No GRN has been inferred/refined yet — the conversion expects the refined GRN adjacency matrix, not raw RNA-Seq count tables (use RNASeq_to_BN instead). A final, fully validated Boolean model is required — Augusta BNs are first drafts, not final networks. The goal is dynamic network simulation rather than drafting a logical model (e.g. SQUAD-style GUI simulation).

skills.search_text: boolean-rule-inference-evaluation Use when you need to test whether Boolean rule sets inferred from a scRNA-seq cell cluster are stable to the number of training cells, i.e. whether performance degrades below a critical training fraction (e.g. after downsampling to 1%). skills.description: Use when you have BoolODE (or similar) simulated single-cell gene-expression count matrices with known time points and a defined single-gene knockout, and need to benchmark whether a neural ODE forecaster extrapolates to post-perturbation states absent from training.
skills.name: boolode-gene-knockout-simulation-forecasting
skills.search_text: boolode-gene-knockout-simulation-forecasting Use when you have BoolODE (or similar) simulated single-cell gene-expression count matrices with known time points and a defined single-gene knockout, and need to benchmark whether a neural ODE forecaster extrapolates to post-perturbation states absent from training. The unwanted-RNA fasta (fasta_outRNA) is empty in config.yaml — RiboDoc skips the depletion step entirely Splice-aware genome alignment is the goal on its own — RiboDoc pairs Bowtie2 with HISAT2 for the genome/transcriptome alignment step since Bowtie2 is not splice-aware Input is not short reads or not trimmed RPF fragments (e.g. long reads, or raw FastQ still containing adapters) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align short sequencing reads with Bowtie2, as used in the RiboDoc Ribo-seq pipeline to deplete contaminant RNA (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) from adapter-trimmed, RPF-length-selected reads before the double-mapping (HISAT2 + Bowtie2) step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: Align short sequencing reads with Bowtie2, as used in the RiboDoc Ribo-seq pipeline to deplete contaminant RNA (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) from adapter-trimmed, RPF-length-selected reads before the double-mapping (HISAT2 + Bowtie2) step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The unwanted-RNA fasta (fasta_outRNA) is empty in config.yaml — RiboDoc skips the depletion step entirely Splice-aware genome alignment is the goal on its own — RiboDoc pairs Bowtie2 with HISAT2 for the genome/transcriptome alignment step since Bowtie2 is not splice-aware Input is not short reads or not trimmed RPF fragments (e.g. long reads, or raw FastQ still containing adapters)

skills.description: Use when you have replicate-level null statistics (e.g., 1000 random pairwise overlap counts) computed under several permutation backgrounds and need to visually compare their distributions to justify which background a colocalization test should use.
skills.name: boxplot-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: boxplot-comparison-visualization Use when you have replicate-level null statistics (e.g., 1000 random pairwise overlap counts) computed under several permutation backgrounds and need to visually compare their distributions to justify which background a colocalization test should use. You have only a single observed overlap statistic per space (no replicate null counts) — use a permutation test with z-score/p-value instead of a distribution comparison boxplot. The region sets under comparison were generated on different gene backgrounds, making the null distributions non-comparable in one plot. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Assembles replicate-level overlap counts (e.g., 1000 null overlap counts per permutation space) into a table and draws a boxplot comparing null distributions across genome- and transcriptome-based permutation spaces, exposing whether space choice shifts the null. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Assembles replicate-level overlap counts (e.g., 1000 null overlap counts per permutation space) into a table and draws a boxplot comparing null distributions across genome- and transcriptome-based permutation spaces, exposing whether space choice shifts the null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single observed overlap statistic per space (no replicate null counts) — use a permutation test with z-score/p-value instead of a distribution comparison boxplot. The region sets under comparison were generated on different gene backgrounds, making the null distributions non-comparable in one plot.

skills.description: Use when comparing imputation methods on single-cell RNA-seq data by measuring which one reduces gene-wise variability across cells of the same type, replicating the variance-stabilization analysis (Fig. 4) of the AutoImpute paper.
skills.name: boxplot-visualization-of-gene-variability
skills.search_text: boxplot-visualization-of-gene-variability Use when comparing imputation methods on single-cell RNA-seq data by measuring which one reduces gene-wise variability across cells of the same type, replicating the variance-stabilization analysis (Fig. 4) of the AutoImpute paper. The goal is to compare methods on expression recovery from subsampled data or cell-clustering accuracy rather than intra-subpopulation variance stabilization The data are bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated, so there is no intra-subpopulation (cell-to-cell) variance to stabilize Cell-type annotations are unavailable, making it impossible to isolate a single subpopulation for the CV calculation http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies per-gene coefficient of variation (CV) within a single randomly picked cell-type subpopulation and visualizes log-transformed CV distributions as grouped boxplots to compare how well imputation methods (AutoImpute, scImpute, MAGIC, drImpute) stabilize intra-subpopulation variance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Quantifies per-gene coefficient of variation (CV) within a single randomly picked cell-type subpopulation and visualizes log-transformed CV distributions as grouped boxplots to compare how well imputation methods (AutoImpute, scImpute, MAGIC, drImpute) stabilize intra-subpopulation variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare methods on expression recovery from subsampled data or cell-clustering accuracy rather than intra-subpopulation variance stabilization The data are bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated, so there is no intra-subpopulation (cell-to-cell) variance to stabilize Cell-type annotations are unavailable, making it impossible to isolate a single subpopulation for the CV calculation

skills.description: Use when clusters from scCAN (or similar unsupervised clustering) lack true cell type labels and a marker-gene reference table (e.g. PanglaoDB brain cell types) is available to assign each cluster a known cell type.
skills.name: brain-cell-type-annotation-from-markers
skills.search_text: brain-cell-type-annotation-from-markers Use when clusters from scCAN (or similar unsupervised clustering) lack true cell type labels and a marker-gene reference table (e.g. PanglaoDB brain cell types) is available to assign each cluster a known cell type. The dataset already has trusted per-cell type annotations, so validation against marker references would be redundant. You need to determine the number of clusters or perform the clustering itself — use scCAN's eigengap/spectral clustering pipeline first; this skill only annotates pre-existing scCAN cluster assignments. No curated marker reference (e.g. PanglaoDB) exists for the tissue; Jaccard overlap against unavailable marker sets cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Biologically validates unsupervised scCAN clusters on the Brain 1.3M dataset (GSE93421) by matching per-cluster differentially expressed genes against PanglaoDB reference marker sets for 24 neural cell types, yielding a 19x24 Jaccard probability matrix and a cluster-to-cell-type mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Biologically validates unsupervised scCAN clusters on the Brain 1.3M dataset (GSE93421) by matching per-cluster differentially expressed genes against PanglaoDB reference marker sets for 24 neural cell types, yielding a 19x24 Jaccard probability matrix and a cluster-to-cell-type mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has trusted per-cell type annotations, so validation against marker references would be redundant. You need to determine the number of clusters or perform the clustering itself — use scCAN's eigengap/spectral clustering pipeline first; this skill only annotates pre-existing scCAN cluster assignments. No curated marker reference (e.g. PanglaoDB) exists for the tissue; Jaccard overlap against unavailable marker sets cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when a brain RNA-seq WGCNA analysis has produced gene-to-module assignments and you need the biological functions enriched per module plus significant module–trait correlations (e.g., coral module vs. age progression at P < 0.05).
skills.name: brain-rnaseq-module-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: brain-rnaseq-module-functional-annotation Use when a brain RNA-seq WGCNA analysis has produced gene-to-module assignments and you need the biological functions enriched per module plus significant module–trait correlations (e.g., coral module vs. age progression at P < 0.05). Input is raw counts without module assignments — run WGCNA module detection (Quick Start) first before annotating modules. Goal is single-gene differential expression rather than module-level function or eigengene–trait association. Module comparison against an external gene list where network conservation, not functional enrichment, is the question (use the Compare PyWGCNA objects workflow instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 Annotates co-expression modules discovered in brain bulk RNA-seq (e.g., MODEL-AD 5xFAD) with functional meaning by running GO/KEGG/REACTOME enrichment on module gene lists in PyWGCNA and relating module eigengenes to external sample traits such as age progression and brain region. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Annotates co-expression modules discovered in brain bulk RNA-seq (e.g., MODEL-AD 5xFAD) with functional meaning by running GO/KEGG/REACTOME enrichment on module gene lists in PyWGCNA and relating module eigengenes to external sample traits such as age progression and brain region.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts without module assignments — run WGCNA module detection (Quick Start) first before annotating modules. Goal is single-gene differential expression rather than module-level function or eigengene–trait association. Module comparison against an external gene list where network conservation, not functional enrichment, is the question (use the Compare PyWGCNA objects workflow instead).

skills.description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq clusters from brain or nervous-system tissue by querying differential-expression marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers, only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) against CellMarker.
skills.name: brain-tissue-marker-database-querying
skills.search_text: brain-tissue-marker-database-querying Use when annotating scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq clusters from brain or nervous-system tissue by querying differential-expression marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers, only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) against CellMarker. Dataset is from a non-brain tissue — the CellMarker query must be restricted to tissues matching the sample, so a generic brain list would miss the correct cell types Marker lists are to be compared as plain gene-set overlaps without ranking — the article warns that 'simply overlapping the two lists without considering gene ranking might lead to unreliable results', so use GSEA on ranked scores instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotates clusters from brain single-nucleus RNA-seq by ranking Seurat-derived cluster markers (logFC cutoff 0.25) against the CellMarker database restricted to brain tissues, using EasyCellType's GSEA test with graphical dot-plot output. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Annotates clusters from brain single-nucleus RNA-seq by ranking Seurat-derived cluster markers (logFC cutoff 0.25) against the CellMarker database restricted to brain tissues, using EasyCellType's GSEA test with graphical dot-plot output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is from a non-brain tissue — the CellMarker query must be restricted to tissues matching the sample, so a generic brain list would miss the correct cell types Marker lists are to be compared as plain gene-set overlaps without ranking — the article warns that 'simply overlapping the two lists without considering gene ranking might lead to unreliable results', so use GSEA on ranked scores instead

skills.description: Use when an Mpath trajectory contains a branching event and you must isolate which cells commit to each distinct differentiation path, such as muscle versus non-muscle fates in myoblast differentiation.
skills.name: branch-assignment-in-differentiation-trajectories
skills.search_text: branch-assignment-in-differentiation-trajectories Use when an Mpath trajectory contains a branching event and you must isolate which cells commit to each distinct differentiation path, such as muscle versus non-muscle fates in myoblast differentiation. Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell datasets in which specific subset information is not known Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types or FACS-sorted terminal subsets, which Mpath depends on for fate prediction Assigns individual cells to specific branches of an Mpath-constructed multi-branching trajectory (e.g. separating the muscle differentiation path marked by MYOG, MYOD1, MEF2C from the non-muscle branch marked by PDGFRA in primary human myoblast scRNA-seq), enabling fate prediction after a branching event. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Assigns individual cells to specific branches of an Mpath-constructed multi-branching trajectory (e.g. separating the muscle differentiation path marked by MYOG, MYOD1, MEF2C from the non-muscle branch marked by PDGFRA in primary human myoblast scRNA-seq), enabling fate prediction after a branching event.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell datasets in which specific subset information is not known Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types or FACS-sorted terminal subsets, which Mpath depends on for fate prediction

skills.description: Use when a branching single-cell trajectory has been inferred (e.g., STREAM on scRNA-seq) and you need to identify marker genes enriched on each branch to validate the topology or annotate lineage identities.
skills.name: branch-dependent-gene-detection
skills.search_text: branch-dependent-gene-detection Use when a branching single-cell trajectory has been inferred (e.g., STREAM on scRNA-seq) and you need to identify marker genes enriched on each branch to validate the topology or annotate lineage identities. The trajectory is cyclic or disconnected — the article notes further improvement is necessary to adapt STREAM to these more general structures before branch testing is meaningful Data are single-cell chromatin accessibility and the goal is TF binding dynamics rather than gene-expression branch markers — use the scATAC-seq mode/features instead You need to map new cells with potentially different fates onto a precomputed trajectory — the mapping procedure may not be optimal for cells with totally different fates http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect and visualize genes whose expression is significantly enriched on specific branches of a trajectory reconstructed with STREAM, using the branch-specific differential testing built into STREAM (which runs ElPiGraph as its core principal-graph algorithm). This validates lineage branching by confirming that known fate markers (e.g., Gfi1, Irf8, Gata1 in mouse hematopoiesis) localize to the correct inferred branches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Detect and visualize genes whose expression is significantly enriched on specific branches of a trajectory reconstructed with STREAM, using the branch-specific differential testing built into STREAM (which runs ElPiGraph as its core principal-graph algorithm). This validates lineage branching by confirming that known fate markers (e.g., Gfi1, Irf8, Gata1 in mouse hematopoiesis) localize to the correct inferred branches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory is cyclic or disconnected — the article notes further improvement is necessary to adapt STREAM to these more general structures before branch testing is meaningful Data are single-cell chromatin accessibility and the goal is TF binding dynamics rather than gene-expression branch markers — use the scATAC-seq mode/features instead You need to map new cells with potentially different fates onto a precomputed trajectory — the mapping procedure may not be optimal for cells with totally different fates

skills.description: Decision support for selecting a trajectory inference method when a scRNA-seq dataset has known branch structure (e.g., 8 branches in the CMP myeloid progenitor data) and downstream time-series analysis needs single-cell pseudotime.
skills.name: branch-topology-reconstruction-evaluation
skills.search_text: branch-topology-reconstruction-evaluation Decision support for selecting a trajectory inference method when a scRNA-seq dataset has known branch structure (e.g., 8 branches in the CMP myeloid progenitor data) and downstream time-series analysis needs single-cell pseudotime. The dataset has no known reference topology or validated cell-type ordering against which reconstructed branches can be compared You only need branch topology with no downstream need for per-cell pseudotime (in that case Mpath may suffice, unlike scTITANS's asynchrony-correction use case) You already have a completed trajectory and only need DEG/subcluster identification — use scTITANS 'partial' mode instead of re-running the method comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Systematic comparison of trajectory inference (TI) methods on a dataset with known branching structure, evaluating how many and which branches each method reconstructs against known cell-type ordering, and selecting the method that both recovers the topology AND yields per-cell pseudotime for downstream asynchrony correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Systematic comparison of trajectory inference (TI) methods on a dataset with known branching structure, evaluating how many and which branches each method reconstructs against known cell-type ordering, and selecting the method that both recovers the topology AND yields per-cell pseudotime for downstream asynchrony correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known reference topology or validated cell-type ordering against which reconstructed branches can be compared You only need branch topology with no downstream need for per-cell pseudotime (in that case Mpath may suffice, unlike scTITANS's asynchrony-correction use case) You already have a completed trajectory and only need DEG/subcluster identification — use scTITANS 'partial' mode instead of re-running the method comparison

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is suspected to contain a branched developmental trajectory and pseudotime has already been inferred with redPATH's redpath() function, so multiple Hamiltonian path solutions (norm_res_new) are available to combine.
skills.name: branched-cell-fate-trajectory-visualization
skills.search_text: branched-cell-fate-trajectory-visualization Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is suspected to contain a branched developmental trajectory and pseudotime has already been inferred with redPATH's redpath() function, so multiple Hamiltonian path solutions (norm_res_new) are available to combine. When only a single pseudotime ordering is available and no multiple Hamiltonian path solutions (norm_res_new) have been generated by redpath(), since the transition matrix requires multiple path solutions When the underlying pseudotime inference performed poorly — the article notes this approach may fail when pseudotime results are poor When the goal is lineage-internal dynamics such as cell cycle/proliferation visualization, which redPATH handles with plot_cycle_diff_3d/plot_diff_3d on reCAT output instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Visualizes linear or branched developmental trajectories from single-cell RNA-seq by combining multiple Hamiltonian path solutions from redPATH into an N-by-N cell transition probability matrix and embedding it via PCA, exposing binary cell fate decisions such as those in human hematopoietic stem cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Visualizes linear or branched developmental trajectories from single-cell RNA-seq by combining multiple Hamiltonian path solutions from redPATH into an N-by-N cell transition probability matrix and embedding it via PCA, exposing binary cell fate decisions such as those in human hematopoietic stem cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single pseudotime ordering is available and no multiple Hamiltonian path solutions (norm_res_new) have been generated by redpath(), since the transition matrix requires multiple path solutions When the underlying pseudotime inference performed poorly — the article notes this approach may fail when pseudotime results are poor When the goal is lineage-internal dynamics such as cell cycle/proliferation visualization, which redPATH handles with plot_cycle_diff_3d/plot_diff_3d on reCAT output instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a trajectory inference method (e.g. STREAM, Monocle2, TSCAN, DPT) correctly detects known bifurcations and recovers true pseudotime on a synthetic single-cell dataset with ground-truth topology.
skills.name: branching-event-detection-against-gold-standard
skills.search_text: branching-event-detection-against-gold-standard Use when evaluating whether a trajectory inference method (e.g. STREAM, Monocle2, TSCAN, DPT) correctly detects known bifurcations and recovers true pseudotime on a synthetic single-cell dataset with ground-truth topology. The dataset is real experimental data with no known ground-truth branching topology or true pseudotime — correlation metrics cannot be computed against a gold standard. The trajectory of interest is cyclic, disconnected, or has fates absent from a reference structure — the paper notes STREAM requires further adaptation for such general graph topologies. The input is not single-cell omics data (e.g. bulk or spatial data without per-cell ordering), since the compared methods are single-cell trajectory inference tools. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a trajectory inference method's ability to detect branching events and estimate pseudotime by comparing its output against a gold-standard synthetic dataset with known bifurcations, following the STREAM paper's Rizvi et al. benchmark design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Benchmark a trajectory inference method's ability to detect branching events and estimate pseudotime by comparing its output against a gold-standard synthetic dataset with known bifurcations, following the STREAM paper's Rizvi et al. benchmark design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real experimental data with no known ground-truth branching topology or true pseudotime — correlation metrics cannot be computed against a gold standard. The trajectory of interest is cyclic, disconnected, or has fates absent from a reference structure — the paper notes STREAM requires further adaptation for such general graph topologies. The input is not single-cell omics data (e.g. bulk or spatial data without per-cell ordering), since the compared methods are single-cell trajectory inference tools.

skills.description: Use when pseudotime trajectories contain branches (e.g. human vs mouse bone marrow scRNA-seq) and you need to visualize trajectory trees or a globally aligned tree to inspect conserved/divergent lineage marker kinetics.
skills.name: branching-trajectory-visualization
skills.search_text: branching-trajectory-visualization Use when pseudotime trajectories contain branches (e.g. human vs mouse bone marrow scRNA-seq) and you need to visualize trajectory trees or a globally aligned tree to inspect conserved/divergent lineage marker kinetics. The trajectories of interest are graphs with cycles or disconnected components — 'CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees (including single lineages)' You have linear, unbranched lineages that existing linear DTW-based alignment tools already handle, and selecting single paths is not a problem The two datasets have very different global topological structures, where CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render and inspect branched single-cell pseudotime trajectories as minimum-spanning-tree trajectory trees, including cross-dataset tree alignments, using CAPITAL's plotting functions (capital.pl.tree_alignment, capital.pl.gene_expression_trend) on scRNA-seq datasets such as human Velten17 and mouse Paul15 bone marrow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Render and inspect branched single-cell pseudotime trajectories as minimum-spanning-tree trajectory trees, including cross-dataset tree alignments, using CAPITAL's plotting functions (capital.pl.tree_alignment, capital.pl.gene_expression_trend) on scRNA-seq datasets such as human Velten17 and mouse Paul15 bone marrow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectories of interest are graphs with cycles or disconnected components — 'CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees (including single lineages)' You have linear, unbranched lineages that existing linear DTW-based alignment tools already handle, and selecting single paths is not a problem The two datasets have very different global topological structures, where CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in benchmarking

skills.description: Use when single-cell data (transcriptomic or chromatin-accessibility) is expected to contain branching developmental structure, and you need to learn, assign cells to, and visualize a branching trajectory graph with pseudotime.

skills.search_text: branching-trajectory-visualization Use when single-cell data (transcriptomic or chromatin-accessibility) is expected to contain branching developmental structure, and you need to learn, assign cells to, and visualize a branching trajectory graph with pseudotime. skills.summary: Visualize single-cell branching trajectories and pseudotime using STREAM's density-level trajectory plots built on the ElPiGraph principal-graph algorithm, applicable to both scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (k-mer, peak, or motif feature) data.

skills.description: Use when a BRCA (MCF7) GSFM active matrix and drug-induced GSFM matrix are available and the goal is to rank compounds by RSGSFM and confirm a reported top candidate such as WYE-354 against IC50 and FDA-approved/investigational drug benchmarks.
skills.name: brca-drug-repurposing-candidate-confirmation
skills.search_text: brca-drug-repurposing-candidate-confirmation Use when a BRCA (MCF7) GSFM active matrix and drug-induced GSFM matrix are available and the goal is to rank compounds by RSGSFM and confirm a reported top candidate such as WYE-354 against IC50 and FDA-approved/investigational drug benchmarks. Input data are raw gene expression matrices rather than GSFM-transformed functional module active matrices (run the GSFM transformation first) The disease of interest is not BRCA or lacks matched normal samples — the article notes the method may not be applicable to certain rare diseases when normal samples are unavailable Functional modules cannot be reasonably defined for the new dataset without prior knowledge, which the discussion flags as a challenge for applying GSFM http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Confirms WYE-354 (RSGSFM −0.92) as the top-ranked candidate therapeutic agent for breast-invasive carcinoma (BRCA) by computing the RS reversal score on GSFM-transformed drug- and disease-induced functional-module (FM) active matrices and validating retrieval performance with ROC-based cross-validation and IC50-based enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.apsb.2024.08.017

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw gene expression matrices rather than GSFM-transformed functional module active matrices (run the GSFM transformation first) The disease of interest is not BRCA or lacks matched normal samples — the article notes the method may not be applicable to certain rare diseases when normal samples are unavailable Functional modules cannot be reasonably defined for the new dataset without prior knowledge, which the discussion flags as a challenge for applying GSFM

skills.search_text: breakpoint-preservation-qc-in-cnv-matrices Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (after baseline subtraction from confident normal cells) must be denoised before copy number segmentation while retaining breakpoints needed for joint segmentation and clone detection. The tumor has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based smoothing and segmentation assumptions are unsuitable A discretized or already-segmented CNA matrix is provided — smoothing a piecewise-constant input would erode genuine breakpoints Only normal/tumor cell classification is needed with no downstream segmentation, when the smoothing step's main output (breakpoint-preserving profiles) is not required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies SCEVAN's edge-preserving nonlinear diffusion smoothing (total variation with phi(x)=logcosh(x) prior) to the gene-by-cell relative expression matrix so noise is regularized while copy number breakpoints are retained before Mumford-Shah segmentation. skills.when_to_use_negative: The tumor has minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based smoothing and segmentation assumptions are unsuitable A discretized or already-segmented CNA matrix is provided — smoothing a piecewise-constant input would erode genuine breakpoints Only normal/tumor cell classification is needed with no downstream segmentation, when the smoothing step's main output (breakpoint-preserving profiles) is not required

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has cells assigned to mtDNA-defined clones (e.g., TNBC1 T0 vs T1 subclones) and you need to test whether the subclones show detectable transcriptional differences via differential expression.
skills.name: breast-cancer-de-gene-interpretation
skills.search_text: breast-cancer-de-gene-interpretation Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has cells assigned to mtDNA-defined clones (e.g., TNBC1 T0 vs T1 subclones) and you need to test whether the subclones show detectable transcriptional differences via differential expression. Input is bulk RNA-seq or data without clone/subclone assignments — the contrast requires pre-defined mtDNA clone groups (T0 vs T1) The goal is calling clonally informative mtDNA variants themselves (use the cellSNP–MQuad–vireoSNP pipeline instead of nuclear-gene DE) Cells are not tumor cells or the mitochondrial subclones have too few cells per group to support a DESeq2-based two-sided Wald test http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects transcriptional differences between mtDNA-defined tumor subclones in the TNBC1 10x scRNA-seq dataset by running Seurat FindMarkers (DESeq2 model) between the T0 (Tumor & MT0) and T1 (Tumor & MT1) mitochondrial subclones, then interpreting the significant gene set (57 up-regulated genes including SEC61G, RPL39, SETD5) with a volcano plot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Detects transcriptional differences between mtDNA-defined tumor subclones in the TNBC1 10x scRNA-seq dataset by running Seurat FindMarkers (DESeq2 model) between the T0 (Tumor & MT0) and T1 (Tumor & MT1) mitochondrial subclones, then interpreting the significant gene set (57 up-regulated genes including SEC61G, RPL39, SETD5) with a volcano plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or data without clone/subclone assignments — the contrast requires pre-defined mtDNA clone groups (T0 vs T1) The goal is calling clonally informative mtDNA variants themselves (use the cellSNP–MQuad–vireoSNP pipeline instead of nuclear-gene DE) Cells are not tumor cells or the mitochondrial subclones have too few cells per group to support a DESeq2-based two-sided Wald test

skills.description: Use when you have bulk (or single-cell) expression data from a cohort with a binary sample-level covariate (e.g. ER status in TCGA-BRCA) and want to detect covariate–pseudotime interaction genes rather than a single averaged trajectory.

skills.search_text: breast-cancer-er-status-stratified-trajectory-analysis Use when you have bulk (or single-cell) expression data from a cohort with a binary sample-level covariate (e.g. ER status in TCGA-BRCA) and want to detect covariate–pseudotime interaction genes rather than a single averaged trajectory. skills.summary: Fits the PhenoPath Bayesian pseudotime model to bulk TCGA-BRCA log2(TPM+1) expression (4579 highly variable genes, 1135 samples) with estrogen receptor status as a covariate, to identify genes whose trajectory loading is modulated by ER status (1932 genes, 42%, including ESR1 as positive control).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack a sample-level covariate (e.g. ER/mutation/drug status) — PhenoPath's interaction terms require a covariate to perturb the trajectory Nonlinear evolution of features along pseudotime is expected — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime The analysis needs complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath defers to future work

skills.description: Use when classifying breast cancer samples into PAM50 molecular subtypes from gene expression data, especially cross-platform prediction where signature genes are missing or single-sample classification is needed.

skills.search_text: breast-cancer-pam50-subtype-classification Use when classifying breast cancer samples into PAM50 molecular subtypes from gene expression data, especially cross-platform prediction where signature genes are missing or single-sample classification is needed. The task is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised subtype classification — DeepCC was 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' No training labels are available (DeepCC is a supervised framework requiring labels such as PAM50 or CMS) Single-sample microarray prediction without an appropriate reference expression profile and inverseRescale enabled — mixing microarray with TCGA RNA-Seq references is explicitly discouraged http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains a DeepCC artificial neural network on TCGA BRCA RNA-Seq functional spectra with PAM50 labels and applies it to breast cancer validation cohorts (TANSBIG, UNT, UPP, NKI), demonstrating robustness to cross-platform missing genes via random gene-subsampling down to 1000 genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Trains a DeepCC artificial neural network on TCGA BRCA RNA-Seq functional spectra with PAM50 labels and applies it to breast cancer validation cohorts (TANSBIG, UNT, UPP, NKI), demonstrating robustness to cross-platform missing genes via random gene-subsampling down to 1000 genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised subtype classification — DeepCC was 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' No training labels are available (DeepCC is a supervised framework requiring labels such as PAM50 or CMS) Single-sample microarray prediction without an appropriate reference expression profile and inverseRescale enabled — mixing microarray with TCGA RNA-Seq references is explicitly discouraged

skills.search_text: breast-cancer-subtype-classification Use when scRNA-seq tumour biopsies are already annotated as Breast Cancer Cell by the base scATOMIC pan-cancer model and the goal is to assign ER+/HER2+/TN subtype labels per sample, including mixed double-positive calls. Samples not already identified as breast cancer by the base pan-cancer scATOMIC model — the subclassification layer expects Breast Cancer Cell inputs only Whole-cohort classification run on merged multi-patient matrices — the README strongly recommends running scATOMIC on individual patient/biopsy samples because inter-patient cancer-cell effects interfere with signature scoring Normal (non-cancerous) tissue samples — the default scATOMIC model assumes the presence of at least some cancer cells; use the normal_tissue parameter instead Subclassifying cancer types other than breast — future extension of the hierarchy to the other 18 cancer types is not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Applies the pre-trained scATOMIC breast subclassification random forest to pan-cancer-annotated breast cancer cells, resolving them into ER+, HER2+, and triple negative histological subtypes, validated at 97.4% accuracy (37/38 tumours) against immunostaining ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples not already identified as breast cancer by the base pan-cancer scATOMIC model — the subclassification layer expects Breast Cancer Cell inputs only Whole-cohort classification run on merged multi-patient matrices — the README strongly recommends running scATOMIC on individual patient/biopsy samples because inter-patient cancer-cell effects interfere with signature scoring Normal (non-cancerous) tissue samples — the default scATOMIC model assumes the presence of at least some cancer cells; use the normal_tissue parameter instead Subclassifying cancer types other than breast — future extension of the hierarchy to the other 18 cancer types is not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when you have a normalised count matrix plus metadata for TCGA-BRCA (or similar) samples with a SUBTYPE column, and the goal is to find gene–gene interactions whose correlation differs between two phenotypic subgroups.
skills.name: breast-cancer-subtype-group-comparison
skills.search_text: breast-cancer-subtype-group-comparison Use when you have a normalised count matrix plus metadata for TCGA-BRCA (or similar) samples with a SUBTYPE column, and the goal is to find gene–gene interactions whose correlation differs between two phenotypic subgroups. You need to detect non-linear gene–gene associations: DEGGs relies on linear regressions with an interaction term and the authors explicitly state it cannot detect non-linear gene–gene relations The count matrix column names and metadata row names do not align (identical() check fails), since subgroup assignment requires matched samples You are working with multi-omic data (RNAseq + Proteomics/Olink) — the maintained successor multiDEGGs with get_diffNetworks is the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies subgroup-specific gene–gene interaction networks from TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq counts by running DEGGs' robust linear regression with an interaction term across two breast cancer subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and extracting the significantly differential gene–gene pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad192
skills.summary: Identifies subgroup-specific gene–gene interaction networks from TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq counts by running DEGGs' robust linear regression with an interaction term across two breast cancer subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and extracting the significantly differential gene–gene pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect non-linear gene–gene associations: DEGGs relies on linear regressions with an interaction term and the authors explicitly state it cannot detect non-linear gene–gene relations The count matrix column names and metadata row names do not align (identical() check fails), since subgroup assignment requires matched samples You are working with multi-omic data (RNAseq + Proteomics/Olink) — the maintained successor multiDEGGs with get_diffNetworks is the appropriate choice

Input is raw (not normalized) counts — activity() expects a normalized expression matrix The goal is cluster discovery from scratch rather than characterizing already-annotated cell populations (cell labels and UMAP embedding are assumed precomputed) The biological process of interest has no corresponding gene list and no edges exist in full_human_ppin to build a custom PPIN http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates breast epithelial cells (L1, L2, basal) in scRNA-seq data by computing protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) activity scores for biological processes (e.g., GO:0030154 cell differentiation, GO:0008283 cell proliferation) using the ORIGINS2 R package, then overlaying activity distributions on UMAP embeddings and testing them across cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179

skills.description: Use when you have accession-level SNP genotype data (e.g., VCF from Soybase SoySNP50k) plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes per pathogen, and need to rank breeding accessions by predicted resistance.
skills.name: breeding-accession-prioritization
skills.search_text: breeding-accession-prioritization Use when you have accession-level SNP genotype data (e.g., VCF from Soybase SoySNP50k) plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes per pathogen, and need to rank breeding accessions by predicted resistance. The target pathogen is F. graminearum but the genotype matrix is limited to SoySNP50k — no F. graminearum SNPs were found there, so predictions are impossible and the species must be flagged as a no-call instead. You need candidate gene prioritization or coexpression exploration rather than accession ranking — use the SoyFungiGCN network/web app (genes_modules, hubs, mod_enrich) instead of allele-dosage scoring. Phenotypic resistance assay data are available for the accessions — direct phenotypic ranking is more reliable than SNP-allele-based scoring, which only captures known resistance loci. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A marker-based scoring workflow that ranks USDA soybean germplasm accessions by resistance allele dosage at GWAS-derived SNP loci for five fungal pathogens (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi), identifying the top-5 most resistant accessions per pathogen and benchmarking them against the maximum theoretical resistance potential. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x

skills.when_to_use_negative: The target pathogen is F. graminearum but the genotype matrix is limited to SoySNP50k — no F. graminearum SNPs were found there, so predictions are impossible and the species must be flagged as a no-call instead. You need candidate gene prioritization or coexpression exploration rather than accession ranking — use the SoyFungiGCN network/web app (genes_modules, hubs, mod_enrich) instead of allele-dosage scoring. Phenotypic resistance assay data are available for the accessions — direct phenotypic ranking is more reliable than SNP-allele-based scoring, which only captures known resistance loci.

skills.description: Use when training a reference-based identifier on a pre-annotated dataset and applying it to a test dataset whose cell populations include types absent from the reference taxonomy, requiring label harmonization before evaluation of unknown-population rejection.
skills.name: broad-cell-type-taxonomy-renaming
skills.search_text: broad-cell-type-taxonomy-renaming Use when training a reference-based identifier on a pre-annotated dataset and applying it to a test dataset whose cell populations include types absent from the reference taxonomy, requiring label harmonization before evaluation of unknown-population rejection. Reference and test datasets already share an identical, standardized cell-type taxonomy — renaming would destroy informative subtype resolution The goal is fine-grained subtype identification within the same tissue (e.g., distinguishing T cell subtypes), since collapsing to broad types removes those distinctions Marker-based annotation with a curated marker DB (e.g., HiCAT's 3-level taxonomy of tissue/cell_type_major/cell_type_minor/cell_type_subset), where the taxonomy is supplied by the marker file rather than by dataset annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Harmonizes manual cell-type annotations between reference and test single-cell RNA-seq datasets by collapsing fine-grained subtypes into broad cell types (e.g., T cell subtypes mapped to 'T cell'), so that out-of-taxonomy populations (e.g., tumor cells tested against a blood reference) fall outside the reference taxonomy and can be correctly rejected as unknown (CUA) by MarkerCount_Ref. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Harmonizes manual cell-type annotations between reference and test single-cell RNA-seq datasets by collapsing fine-grained subtypes into broad cell types (e.g., T cell subtypes mapped to 'T cell'), so that out-of-taxonomy populations (e.g., tumor cells tested against a blood reference) fall outside the reference taxonomy and can be correctly rejected as unknown (CUA) by MarkerCount_Ref.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference and test datasets already share an identical, standardized cell-type taxonomy — renaming would destroy informative subtype resolution The goal is fine-grained subtype identification within the same tissue (e.g., distinguishing T cell subtypes), since collapsing to broad types removes those distinctions Marker-based annotation with a curated marker DB (e.g., HiCAT's 3-level taxonomy of tissue/cell_type_major/cell_type_minor/cell_type_subset), where the taxonomy is supplied by the marker file rather than by dataset annotations

skills.description: Use when quantifying circRNAs by back-splicing junction (BSJ)-supporting fragment counts from ribo− RNA-seq, or when cross-comparing circRNA call sets from CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR, MapSplice, and DCC under a >= 3 BSJ-fragment filter.
skills.name: bsj-fragment-count-quantification
skills.search_text: bsj-fragment-count-quantification Use when quantifying circRNAs by back-splicing junction (BSJ)-supporting fragment counts from ribo− RNA-seq, or when cross-comparing circRNA call sets from CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR, MapSplice, and DCC under a >= 3 BSJ-fragment filter. Input is poly(A)+ selected RNA-seq: circRNAs lack 3′-end poly(A) tails and are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets, so BSJ-fragment quantification will under-detect. Dataset is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated and a CIRCscore is wanted: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making FPBlinear and CIRCscore unreliable. The BAM handed to DCC or circ_quant still contains unmapped reads: the pipeline requires a mapped-reads-only HISAT2 BAM. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Quantifies circular RNAs by counting RNA-seq fragments mapped to back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites — the readNumber metric of CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR — and cross-compares BSJ-based circRNA calls from CIRCexplorer2, MapSplice, and circtools-embedded DCC on ribo− RNA-seq to expose tool-specific detection inefficiencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Quantifies circular RNAs by counting RNA-seq fragments mapped to back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites — the readNumber metric of CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR — and cross-compares BSJ-based circRNA calls from CIRCexplorer2, MapSplice, and circtools-embedded DCC on ribo− RNA-seq to expose tool-specific detection inefficiencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)+ selected RNA-seq: circRNAs lack 3′-end poly(A) tails and are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets, so BSJ-fragment quantification will under-detect. Dataset is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated and a CIRCscore is wanted: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making FPBlinear and CIRCscore unreliable. The BAM handed to DCC or circ_quant still contains unmapped reads: the pipeline requires a mapped-reads-only HISAT2 BAM.

skills.description: Use when evaluating how overlapping BSJ sites from CircAST output (or similar circRNA lists) affect full-length assembly sensitivity/precision and FPKM/TPM quantification accuracy, e.g. in simulation benchmarking.
skills.name: bsj-overlap-relation-index-computation
skills.search_text: bsj-overlap-relation-index-computation Use when evaluating how overlapping BSJ sites from CircAST output (or similar circRNA lists) affect full-length assembly sensitivity/precision and FPKM/TPM quantification accuracy, e.g. in simulation benchmarking. Input consists of raw FASTQ/back-splice junction reads rather than an assembled circRNA transcript table — RI analysis requires the CircAST output with genomic coordinates and FPKM/TPM columns. The circRNAs under study are intronic or intergenic — the current CircAST pipeline only assembles exon-annotated circular transcripts, so RI stratification of such loci is not supported. Evaluating quantification in non-RNase R-treated samples, where remnant linear mRNA can generate false transcripts and confound the accuracy metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computation of the relation index (RI) — the cardinality of a back-splice junction (BSJ) site's equivalence class under genomic-overlap relations — to stratify CircAST reconstruction and quantification accuracy on simulated circRNA data. It explains why assembly performance degrades when multiple circRNAs share overlapping genomic regions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Computation of the relation index (RI) — the cardinality of a back-splice junction (BSJ) site's equivalence class under genomic-overlap relations — to stratify CircAST reconstruction and quantification accuracy on simulated circRNA data. It explains why assembly performance degrades when multiple circRNAs share overlapping genomic regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw FASTQ/back-splice junction reads rather than an assembled circRNA transcript table — RI analysis requires the CircAST output with genomic coordinates and FPKM/TPM columns. The circRNAs under study are intronic or intergenic — the current CircAST pipeline only assembles exon-annotated circular transcripts, so RI stratification of such loci is not supported. Evaluating quantification in non-RNase R-treated samples, where remnant linear mRNA can generate false transcripts and confound the accuracy metrics.

skills.description: Use when re-implementing or validating singleCellHaystack's per-gene significance pipeline: you have observed D_KL values per gene plus randomized null D_KL replicates and need smoothed p-values via B-splines instead of per-gene empirical tests.
skills.name: bspline-null-statistics-smoothing-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: bspline-null-statistics-smoothing-pvalue-estimation Use when re-implementing or validating singleCellHaystack's per-gene significance pipeline: you have observed D_KL values per gene plus randomized null D_KL replicates and need smoothed p-values via B-splines instead of per-gene empirical tests. Expression data is continuous counts/read counts — the method requires binary detection data (a gene is either detected or not in each cell); continuous-measure support is planned but not available in the described version You need p-values corrected for double use of gene expression data (coordinates derived from the same expression matrix) — the authors note this inflation issue is deferred to future updates http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A statistical sub-step of singleCellHaystack that converts randomized Kullback-Leibler divergence null distributions into per-gene significance by modeling the mean and SD of randomized D_KL as B-spline functions of the observed D_KL, then deriving log p-values from the fitted curves. This enables clustering-independent DEG calling for genes non-randomly positioned in a multidimensional space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: A statistical sub-step of singleCellHaystack that converts randomized Kullback-Leibler divergence null distributions into per-gene significance by modeling the mean and SD of randomized D_KL as B-spline functions of the observed D_KL, then deriving log p-values from the fitted curves. This enables clustering-independent DEG calling for genes non-randomly positioned in a multidimensional space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data is continuous counts/read counts — the method requires binary detection data (a gene is either detected or not in each cell); continuous-measure support is planned but not available in the described version You need p-values corrected for double use of gene expression data (coordinates derived from the same expression matrix) — the authors note this inflation issue is deferred to future updates

skills.description: Use when Nanopore long-read alignments (e.g., minimap2 v2.24 spliced alignments to GRCh38) show inflated PSI or suspected false-positive small internal exons, and you need to quantify the PSI shift from Longcell's consensus correction on bulk isoform quantification.
skills.name: bulk-alternative-splicing-comparison
skills.search_text: bulk-alternative-splicing-comparison Use when Nanopore long-read alignments (e.g., minimap2 v2.24 spliced alignments to GRCh38) show inflated PSI or suspected false-positive small internal exons, and you need to quantify the PSI shift from Longcell's consensus correction on bulk isoform quantification. Input data is not Nanopore long-read spliced alignment output (e.g., Illumina short-read or already consensus-corrected isoform counts) The goal is single-cell or spot-level splicing heterogeneity (phi metrics via genesSitesPhi/phiPlot) rather than bulk exon-level PSI correction comparison Exon read counts are below the constitutive-exon cutoff (> 30), where PSI estimates are noisy and the bulk comparison is unreliable Quantifies bulk percent-spliced-in (PSI) for constitutive internal exons in a Nanopore long-read sample before and after Longcell's UMI-clustering misalignment correction, revealing how mapping errors bias isoform quantification (e.g., CRCLM average PSI shifting from 0.67 to 0.92 and ~20% of VPS28-201 reads wrongly covering its small middle exon). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
