You already have the scCancer2 reference matrix or genes-scRNA-tcga-sorted.txt shipped with the package (system.file('txt', package='scCancer')) — no reconstruction is needed Your goal is cell-subtype annotation with predCellType or runCellSubtypeClassify, which uses marker/submodel paths rather than this TCGA-derived panel You lack malignant/normal bulk sample labels, since the entire panel derives from edgeR contrasts between TCGA malignant and normal samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs scCancer2's bulk+single-cell feature selection: edgeR differential expression between malignant and normal TCGA bulk samples across 14 cancer types is combined with high-variance scRNA-seq genes to produce the 2,756-gene panel used to train the malignant cell classifier on a 466,468-cell reference matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Reconstructs scCancer2's bulk+single-cell feature selection: edgeR differential expression between malignant and normal TCGA bulk samples across 14 cancer types is combined with high-variance scRNA-seq genes to produce the 2,756-gene panel used to train the malignant cell classifier on a 466,468-cell reference matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have the scCancer2 reference matrix or genes-scRNA-tcga-sorted.txt shipped with the package (system.file('txt', package='scCancer')) — no reconstruction is needed Your goal is cell-subtype annotation with predCellType or runCellSubtypeClassify, which uses marker/submodel paths rather than this TCGA-derived panel You lack malignant/normal bulk sample labels, since the entire panel derives from edgeR contrasts between TCGA malignant and normal samples

skills.description: Use when a cluster-specific gene signature (e.g., top 20 DEGs of a scRNA-seq tumor cluster such as Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be translated into a bulk cohort metric to stratify patients for Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival testing.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-activity-score-computation
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-activity-score-computation Use when a cluster-specific gene signature (e.g., top 20 DEGs of a scRNA-seq tumor cluster such as Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be translated into a bulk cohort metric to stratify patients for Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival testing. The input is already per-cluster drug response predictions (IC50/AUC) rather than a gene signature needing bulk-cohort scoring No matched clinical survival data exist for the bulk cohort, so no high/low survival grouping can be tested The cluster signature itself showed no survival significance (as with the prostate cancer tumor clusters, where none reached p < 0.05) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes a per-patient activity score for a cluster-derived gene signature in bulk RNA-seq (e.g., TCGA) by binarizing each signature gene at its median expression (1 if above median, else 0) and summing across genes, enabling stratification of patients into high- vs low-expressing groups for survival analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Computes a per-patient activity score for a cluster-derived gene signature in bulk RNA-seq (e.g., TCGA) by binarizing each signature gene at its median expression (1 if above median, else 0) and summing across genes, enabling stratification of patients into high- vs low-expressing groups for survival analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already per-cluster drug response predictions (IC50/AUC) rather than a gene signature needing bulk-cohort scoring No matched clinical survival data exist for the bulk cohort, so no high/low survival grouping can be tested The cluster signature itself showed no survival significance (as with the prostate cancer tumor clusters, where none reached p < 0.05)

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue must be decomposed into cell-type proportions, especially when single-cell vs bulk technical biases are expected or when only marker genes (not a reference profile) are available.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-decomposition
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-decomposition Use when bulk RNA-seq/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue must be decomposed into cell-type proportions, especially when single-cell vs bulk technical biases are expected or when only marker genes (not a reference profile) are available. When few individuals have single-cell data, since the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable When single-cell-captured cell-type proportions differ significantly from true physiological distributions (e.g., severe underrepresentation of a cell type) When cross-cell-type comparisons of absolute proportions are needed from marker-based mode, since BisqueMarker yields relative abundances that cannot be compared across cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Estimate cell-type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using Bisque, which learns gene-specific transformations between a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference and bulk expression, or BisqueMarker when only marker genes are available. Outperforms CIBERSORT/BSEQ-sc and MuSiC under significant technical variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Estimate cell-type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using Bisque, which learns gene-specific transformations between a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference and bulk expression, or BisqueMarker when only marker genes are available. Outperforms CIBERSORT/BSEQ-sc and MuSiC under significant technical variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When few individuals have single-cell data, since the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable When single-cell-captured cell-type proportions differ significantly from true physiological distributions (e.g., severe underrepresentation of a cell type) When cross-cell-type comparisons of absolute proportions are needed from marker-based mode, since BisqueMarker yields relative abundances that cannot be compared across cell types

skills.description: Use when bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq samples need cell type proportions estimated, and a single-cell reference (real or semi-profiled) is available, or when benchmarking deconvolution methods against ground-truth proportions.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution Use when bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq samples need cell type proportions estimated, and a single-cell reference (real or semi-profiled) is available, or when benchmarking deconvolution methods against ground-truth proportions. No single-cell reference exists — scSemiProfiler's deep generative model enables single-cell level deconvolution only 'provided there is a single-cell reference' Input is already a cell type proportion table rather than bulk/pseudobulk expression data The goal is single-cell resolution downstream analysis other than deconvolution (e.g., UMAP, pseudotime) for which semi-profiling rather than deconvolution benchmarking is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark and apply bulk RNA-seq cell type deconvolution on pseudobulk cohorts (e.g., the 124-sample COVID-19 cohort), comparing scSemiProfiler's single-cell-level deconvolution against CIBERSORTx, Bisque, Scaden, TAPE, EPIC, NNLS, and MuSiC using Lin's CCC, Pearson correlation, and RMSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Benchmark and apply bulk RNA-seq cell type deconvolution on pseudobulk cohorts (e.g., the 124-sample COVID-19 cohort), comparing scSemiProfiler's single-cell-level deconvolution against CIBERSORTx, Bisque, Scaden, TAPE, EPIC, NNLS, and MuSiC using Lin's CCC, Pearson correlation, and RMSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No single-cell reference exists — scSemiProfiler's deep generative model enables single-cell level deconvolution only 'provided there is a single-cell reference' Input is already a cell type proportion table rather than bulk/pseudobulk expression data The goal is single-cell resolution downstream analysis other than deconvolution (e.g., UMAP, pseudotime) for which semi-profiling rather than deconvolution benchmarking is appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrix plus sample metadata and an annotated plant single-cell reference (e.g. Seurat object from Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq), and need cell-type fraction estimates per sample.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrix plus sample metadata and an annotated plant single-cell reference (e.g. Seurat object from Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq), and need cell-type fraction estimates per sample. Input is already a single-cell dataset needing annotation or clustering rather than bulk data — use scPlant's cell-type annotation module instead. No annotated single-cell reference atlas is available for the organism/tissue, since decomposeBulk requires a labeled Seurat reference to estimate fractions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify cell-type composition of bulk RNA-seq samples by deconvolving them against a single-cell reference: scPlant's decomposeBulk function (wrapping RNAMagnet's runCIBERSORT) estimates cell-type fractions from an annotated Seurat single-cell reference, and fractionHmp visualizes them as a per-sample heatmap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Quantify cell-type composition of bulk RNA-seq samples by deconvolving them against a single-cell reference: scPlant's decomposeBulk function (wrapping RNAMagnet's runCIBERSORT) estimates cell-type fractions from an annotated Seurat single-cell reference, and fractionHmp visualizes them as a per-sample heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single-cell dataset needing annotation or clustering rather than bulk data — use scPlant's cell-type annotation module instead. No annotated single-cell reference atlas is available for the organism/tissue, since decomposeBulk requires a labeled Seurat reference to estimate fractions.

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., a 192-sample count/TPM matrix) plus sample trait metadata (age, genotype, tissue, sex) must be partitioned into co-expression modules and those modules related to traits.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-co-expression-network-analysis
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-co-expression-network-analysis Use when a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., a 192-sample count/TPM matrix) plus sample trait metadata (age, genotype, tissue, sex) must be partitioned into co-expression modules and those modules related to traits. Input is single-cell expression data rather than bulk RNA-seq — single-cell data appears in this workflow only as external marker-gene lists for comparison, not as network input The question is differential expression between two conditions, not discovering clusters of co-expressed genes across many samples Input is already a module assignment or eigengene table — use the comparison/enrichment tutorials instead of re-running module detection http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects gene co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq data using PyWGCNA, a Python implementation of weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) that is faster than the R version and adds downstream functional enrichment, PPI, and module-comparison analyses. Applied to the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex-and-hippocampus dataset it recovered 17 modules associated with age, genotype, tissue, and sex. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Detects gene co-expression modules from bulk RNA-seq data using PyWGCNA, a Python implementation of weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) that is faster than the R version and adds downstream functional enrichment, PPI, and module-comparison analyses. Applied to the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex-and-hippocampus dataset it recovered 17 modules associated with age, genotype, tissue, and sex.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell expression data rather than bulk RNA-seq — single-cell data appears in this workflow only as external marker-gene lists for comparison, not as network input The question is differential expression between two conditions, not discovering clusters of co-expressed genes across many samples Input is already a module assignment or eigengene table — use the comparison/enrichment tutorials instead of re-running module detection

skills.description: Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 38 3xTg-AD/WT female hippocampus samples across three ages) must be formatted and cleaned—filtering low-expression genes—before module detection in PyWGCNA.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-count-preprocessing
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-count-preprocessing Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 38 3xTg-AD/WT female hippocampus samples across three ages) must be formatted and cleaned—filtering low-expression genes—before module detection in PyWGCNA. Input is already a filtered expression/feature table rather than raw counts—the Data_format cleaning step would remove signal that was already removed The goal is single-cell co-expression analysis—PyWGCNA is designed for bulk RNA-seq datasets with many samples Only descriptive expression statistics are needed with no co-expression network or module output required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Format, clean, and pre-filter a bulk RNA-seq count matrix so it can be loaded into a PyWGCNA object for weighted co-expression network construction, following the PyWGCNA Data_format and Quick_Start tutorials. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Format, clean, and pre-filter a bulk RNA-seq count matrix so it can be loaded into a PyWGCNA object for weighted co-expression network construction, following the PyWGCNA Data_format and Quick_Start tutorials.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered expression/feature table rather than raw counts—the Data_format cleaning step would remove signal that was already removed The goal is single-cell co-expression analysis—PyWGCNA is designed for bulk RNA-seq datasets with many samples Only descriptive expression statistics are needed with no co-expression network or module output required

skills.description: Use when marker-gene sets must be evaluated for how well they support estimating cell-type proportions from bulk or pseudo-bulk expression mixtures.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-deconvolution
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-deconvolution Use when marker-gene sets must be evaluated for how well they support estimating cell-type proportions from bulk or pseudo-bulk expression mixtures. The goal is selecting markers per individual cell type rather than a globally discriminatory set across all phenotype pairs, which is what deconvolution quality depends on Input is bulk data without any single-cell reference or labeled cell types from which to build a signature matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark marker sets (e.g., G-PC, RankCorr, scGeneFit) for deconvolution of pseudo-bulk RNA-seq mixtures by building cell-type signature matrices, running CIBERSORT linear nu-SVR, and scoring predicted vs. true proportions with Jensen-Shannon divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Benchmark marker sets (e.g., G-PC, RankCorr, scGeneFit) for deconvolution of pseudo-bulk RNA-seq mixtures by building cell-type signature matrices, running CIBERSORT linear nu-SVR, and scoring predicted vs. true proportions with Jensen-Shannon divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is selecting markers per individual cell type rather than a globally discriminatory set across all phenotype pairs, which is what deconvolution quality depends on Input is bulk data without any single-cell reference or labeled cell types from which to build a signature matrix

skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-expression-normalization Use when normalized bulk RNA-seq profiles must be converted into a z-scaled markers_expression matrix as query input for deCS correlation-based cell type annotation (e.g., Figure S12 iPSC-NPC/neuron differentiation-quality assessment). Input is single-cell scRNA-seq clusters requiring deCS.fisher marker-gene enrichment rather than correlation on expression profiles Query profiles are gene lists (marker lists) rather than expression matrices Genes are not human gene symbols (e.g., mouse orthologs or Ensembl IDs without symbol mapping), since deCS example scripts require human gene symbols http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocess bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., hiPSC-NPC and hiPSC-neuron samples from Stertz et al.) into a scaled sample-level expression matrix via log-transformation followed by z-scaling, so that Pearson correlation-based cell type annotation with deCS.correlation operates on comparable profiles with human gene symbols. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Preprocess bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., hiPSC-NPC and hiPSC-neuron samples from Stertz et al.) into a scaled sample-level expression matrix via log-transformation followed by z-scaling, so that Pearson correlation-based cell type annotation with deCS.correlation operates on comparable profiles with human gene symbols.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell scRNA-seq clusters requiring deCS.fisher marker-gene enrichment rather than correlation on expression profiles Query profiles are gene lists (marker lists) rather than expression matrices Genes are not human gene symbols (e.g., mouse orthologs or Ensembl IDs without symbol mapping), since deCS example scripts require human gene symbols

skills.description: Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq (e.g. 298-patient urothelial carcinoma ICB cohort, Mariathasan et al. 2018) needs biologically meaningful latent features derived from a single-cell-trained Miscell model for response association testing.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-latent-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-latent-feature-extraction Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq (e.g. 298-patient urothelial carcinoma ICB cohort, Mariathasan et al. 2018) needs biologically meaningful latent features derived from a single-cell-trained Miscell model for response association testing. Input is raw single-cell data for clustering and marker gene identification — use the standard Miscell scRNA-seq workflow (t-SNE + DBSCAN/Leiden) instead of bulk transfer. The bulk data has batch effects that have not been corrected — Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods and requires batch correction as a preprocessing step. The dataset is very small — Miscell, like other deep-neural-network methods, demands a large sample size to obtain good performance. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transfer a Miscell self-supervised encoder trained on single-cell transcriptomes to bulk tumor RNA-seq by projecting bulk expression profiles through the network to extract 64 latent features, then test each feature's association with clinical phenotypes such as ICB therapy response. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Transfer a Miscell self-supervised encoder trained on single-cell transcriptomes to bulk tumor RNA-seq by projecting bulk expression profiles through the network to extract 64 latent features, then test each feature's association with clinical phenotypes such as ICB therapy response.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-cell data for clustering and marker gene identification — use the standard Miscell scRNA-seq workflow (t-SNE + DBSCAN/Leiden) instead of bulk transfer. The bulk data has batch effects that have not been corrected — Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods and requires batch correction as a preprocessing step. The dataset is very small — Miscell, like other deep-neural-network methods, demands a large sample size to obtain good performance.

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., TCGA LUAD tumor vs normal) must be transformed into per-sample gene-gene association networks to compare pathway connectivity (e.g., EGFR/EGF degrees) at single-sample resolution.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-network-construction
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-network-construction Use when bulk RNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., TCGA LUAD tumor vs normal) must be transformed into per-sample gene-gene association networks to compare pathway connectivity (e.g., EGFR/EGF degrees) at single-sample resolution. The analysis goal is causal network construction or edge direction inference — the authors state c-CSN is not designed for causal networks and 'the directions of the gene associations cannot be obtained'. The question requires group-level differential co-expression only and per-sample resolution is unnecessary — a standard population-level correlation network suffices and avoids the G-fold computational cost of per-sample CCSNs. Input is single-cell scRNA-seq where trajectory/entropy analyses (NFE, CNDM-based clustering) rather than bulk per-sample pathway density is the goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Applies the c-CSN method to bulk RNA-seq data (e.g., TCGA-LUAD tumor and normal samples) to construct a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) per individual sample, enabling per-sample gene-gene association analysis such as EGFR pathway connectivity density comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Applies the c-CSN method to bulk RNA-seq data (e.g., TCGA-LUAD tumor and normal samples) to construct a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) per individual sample, enabling per-sample gene-gene association analysis such as EGFR pathway connectivity density comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is causal network construction or edge direction inference — the authors state c-CSN is not designed for causal networks and 'the directions of the gene associations cannot be obtained'. The question requires group-level differential co-expression only and per-sample resolution is unnecessary — a standard population-level correlation network suffices and avoids the G-fold computational cost of per-sample CCSNs. Input is single-cell scRNA-seq where trajectory/entropy analyses (NFE, CNDM-based clustering) rather than bulk per-sample pathway density is the goal.

skills.description: Use when a paired bulk RNA-seq dataset exists for the same cell-type or condition contrast as scRNA-seq data, and you need to quantify whether imputation improves DE gene-list concordance rather than relying on qualitative checks.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-reference-comparison
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-reference-comparison Use when a paired bulk RNA-seq dataset exists for the same cell-type or condition contrast as scRNA-seq data, and you need to quantify whether imputation improves DE gene-list concordance rather than relying on qualitative checks. No bulk RNA-seq data exist for the same biological contrast, so there is no reference DE gene list to compare against Goal is to evaluate imputation quality for clustering or trajectory inference rather than differential expression accuracy The scRNA-seq data come from a protocol with severely high dropout rates (e.g. droplet microfluidics), where imputation efficiency is a known limitation of scImpute http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scRNA-seq differential expression gene lists (raw vs. imputed by scImpute, MAGIC, SAVER) against bulk RNA-seq DESeq2 results on the same biological comparison, using precision, recall, and F-score to judge imputation quality. In the ESC vs. definitive endoderm case (GSE75748), scImpute-imputed lists gain roughly 10% F-score over raw data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq differential expression gene lists (raw vs. imputed by scImpute, MAGIC, SAVER) against bulk RNA-seq DESeq2 results on the same biological comparison, using precision, recall, and F-score to judge imputation quality. In the ESC vs. definitive endoderm case (GSE75748), scImpute-imputed lists gain roughly 10% F-score over raw data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No bulk RNA-seq data exist for the same biological contrast, so there is no reference DE gene list to compare against Goal is to evaluate imputation quality for clustering or trajectory inference rather than differential expression accuracy The scRNA-seq data come from a protocol with severely high dropout rates (e.g. droplet microfluidics), where imputation efficiency is a known limitation of scImpute

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrices must be classified into known molecular subtypes using single-cell-derived gene signatures, and when subtype survival differences (e.g., basal-like vs. classical in PAAD) need to be quantified.
skills.name: bulk-rna-seq-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: bulk-rna-seq-subtype-classification Use when bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrices must be classified into known molecular subtypes using single-cell-derived gene signatures, and when subtype survival differences (e.g., basal-like vs. classical in PAAD) need to be quantified. The input is single-cell data rather than bulk RNA-seq — SCISSORS' native scope is reclustering single cells within broad Seurat clusters, not scoring bulk samples. Samples already carry trusted subtype labels from the reference schema, making signature-based rescoring redundant. No subtype gene signatures (or no overlap with the Moffitt reference genes) are available to anchor the fold-change-ranked marker lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assigns bulk RNA-seq tumor samples to molecular subtypes by scoring each sample against single-cell-derived (SCISSORS) marker gene signatures and picking the higher-scoring signature, then tests subtype-associated survival with Kaplan-Meier curves and a log-rank test. Validated on TCGA PAAD (150 tumors) against the Moffitt basal-like/classical schema. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Assigns bulk RNA-seq tumor samples to molecular subtypes by scoring each sample against single-cell-derived (SCISSORS) marker gene signatures and picking the higher-scoring signature, then tests subtype-associated survival with Kaplan-Meier curves and a log-rank test. Validated on TCGA PAAD (150 tumors) against the Moffitt basal-like/classical schema.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell data rather than bulk RNA-seq — SCISSORS' native scope is reclustering single cells within broad Seurat clusters, not scoring bulk samples. Samples already carry trusted subtype labels from the reference schema, making signature-based rescoring redundant. No subtype gene signatures (or no overlap with the Moffitt reference genes) are available to anchor the fold-change-ranked marker lists.

skills.description: Use when annotating human primary-cell RNA-seq samples (bulk or single-cell) with Cell Ontology terms, or when auditing whether independent one-vs-rest classifiers produce probabilities inconsistent with the ontology's 'is a' edges.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating human primary-cell RNA-seq samples (bulk or single-cell) with Cell Ontology terms, or when auditing whether independent one-vs-rest classifiers produce probabilities inconsistent with the ontology's 'is a' edges. Input is non-human data (e.g. mouse): the paper notes no comprehensive curated mouse training set exists yet and future work is required Input gene set does not match the classifier's genes and you do not intend to train a new model with the '-t' option — CellO requires input genes to match the trained classifier's genes The goal is calibrated binary yes/no decisions rather than hierarchical probabilities — the discussion notes performance with F1-score lags average precision and better calibration is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate human RNA-seq data against the graph-structured Cell Ontology using CellO's per-term binary classifiers (isotonic regression by default), and quantify logical inconsistencies that arise when classifiers are trained independently of the ontology's 'is a' hierarchy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101913
skills.summary: Annotate human RNA-seq data against the graph-structured Cell Ontology using CellO's per-term binary classifiers (isotonic regression by default), and quantify logical inconsistencies that arise when classifiers are trained independently of the ontology's 'is a' hierarchy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is non-human data (e.g. mouse): the paper notes no comprehensive curated mouse training set exists yet and future work is required Input gene set does not match the classifier's genes and you do not intend to train a new model with the '-t' option — CellO requires input genes to match the trained classifier's genes The goal is calibrated binary yes/no decisions rather than hierarchical probabilities — the discussion notes performance with F1-score lags average precision and better calibration is needed

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq read counts must be deconvolved into cell type proportions using a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, especially for tissues with closely related cell types (e.g., pancreatic islet alpha/beta/delta/gamma, kidney nephron segments).
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution Use when bulk RNA-seq read counts must be deconvolved into cell type proportions using a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, especially for tissues with closely related cell types (e.g., pancreatic islet alpha/beta/delta/gamma, kidney nephron segments). Input expression data are TPM — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input (RPKM is usable only with cell-type-specific total RNA abundance estimates) Bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions differing from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2's iterative algorithm instead Only trends (not absolute proportions) are needed under assumptions A1–A3, or the scRNA-seq reference lacks cross-subject replicates needed for cross-subject weighting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq with MuSiC, a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution method that uses cross-subject single-cell RNA-seq references and weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency, avoiding pre-selected marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq with MuSiC, a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution method that uses cross-subject single-cell RNA-seq references and weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency, avoiding pre-selected marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data are TPM — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input (RPKM is usable only with cell-type-specific total RNA abundance estimates) Bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions differing from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2's iterative algorithm instead Only trends (not absolute proportions) are needed under assumptions A1–A3, or the scRNA-seq reference lacks cross-subject replicates needed for cross-subject weighting

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or pseudo-bulk expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need to estimate abundance of hundreds of cell types for downstream TME clustering or survival analysis.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or pseudo-bulk expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need to estimate abundance of hundreds of cell types for downstream TME clustering or survival analysis. Input is already single-cell data where cell identities are known (DCNet is designed to infer cell content from bulk expression, not to re-classify single cells) Expression matrix uses non-human gene symbols or cannot be matched to the index.pkl gene sets (33 cell types were discarded precisely because no marker genes were detected after ID matching) A reproducible, seed-controlled pipeline with versioned software is required — the paper reports no random seeds, no mxnet/R package versions, and no hardware/runtime specifications http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Infers per-cell-type abundance landscapes from bulk RNA-seq samples using DCNet, an interpretable mxnet-implemented ANN that wires 9078 marker genes to 434 cell types, validated against CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, and xCell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Infers per-cell-type abundance landscapes from bulk RNA-seq samples using DCNet, an interpretable mxnet-implemented ANN that wires 9078 marker genes to 434 cell types, validated against CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, and xCell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already single-cell data where cell identities are known (DCNet is designed to infer cell content from bulk expression, not to re-classify single cells) Expression matrix uses non-human gene symbols or cannot be matched to the index.pkl gene sets (33 cell types were discarded precisely because no marker genes were detected after ID matching) A reproducible, seed-controlled pipeline with versioned software is required — the paper reports no random seeds, no mxnet/R package versions, and no hardware/runtime specifications

skills.description: Use when you have simulated or ground-truth-annotated bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq count matrices plus a known regulator-gene interaction list and need to quantify whether modelled activator/repressor effects manifest as strong expression-accessibility correlations.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-correlation-analysis Use when you have simulated or ground-truth-annotated bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq count matrices plus a known regulator-gene interaction list and need to quantify whether modelled activator/repressor effects manifest as strong expression-accessibility correlations. Data are single-cell (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq): the article specifies Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell regulator-gene validation, not Pearson's on bulk counts. You have no ground-truth or simulated regulator-gene interaction annotation, so activator/repressor/no-effect classes cannot be assigned and the random-pair comparison is meaningless. The goal is differential expression or differential accessibility testing rather than validating whether simulated regulatory interactions manifest as strong correlations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Validation procedure for simulated (or ground-truth-annotated) bulk regulatory networks: compute Pearson correlations between regulator accessibility/activity and gene expression per regulator-gene pair, including lagged correlations, and benchmark them against a null set of 20,000 random feature pairs with no simulated regulatory effect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Validation procedure for simulated (or ground-truth-annotated) bulk regulatory networks: compute Pearson correlations between regulator accessibility/activity and gene expression per regulator-gene pair, including lagged correlations, and benchmark them against a null set of 20,000 random feature pairs with no simulated regulatory effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq): the article specifies Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell regulator-gene validation, not Pearson's on bulk counts. You have no ground-truth or simulated regulator-gene interaction annotation, so activator/repressor/no-effect classes cannot be assigned and the random-pair comparison is meaningless. The goal is differential expression or differential accessibility testing rather than validating whether simulated regulatory interactions manifest as strong correlations.

skills.description: Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GEO GSE23649: 8 DBD EAD vs 8 DBD non-EAD) must be made cross-sample comparable before computing per-sample gene-signature scores for group tests such as EAD vs non-EAD.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-count-normalization
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-count-normalization Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GEO GSE23649: 8 DBD EAD vs 8 DBD non-EAD) must be made cross-sample comparable before computing per-sample gene-signature scores for group tests such as EAD vs non-EAD. Input is already a normalized expression matrix (TPM/log-CPM) or a single-cell Seurat object — median-1000 scaling is meant for raw integer bulk counts only. The goal is differential gene expression calling between conditions; median scaling plus log transform supports signature scoring, not DESeq2/edgeR-style dispersion-based DE testing. Samples lack a two-group design with EAD/non-EAD labels, since the downstream step is a two-sample Welch's t-test comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalizes a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix by scaling each sample to a fixed median of 1000 followed by log transformation, making per-sample gene-signature scores comparable across samples. In this paper it validates the single-cell-defined EAD immune niche (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) on the GSE23649 DBD cohort (8 EAD vs 8 non-EAD). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: Normalizes a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix by scaling each sample to a fixed median of 1000 followed by log transformation, making per-sample gene-signature scores comparable across samples. In this paper it validates the single-cell-defined EAD immune niche (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) on the GSE23649 DBD cohort (8 EAD vs 8 non-EAD).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized expression matrix (TPM/log-CPM) or a single-cell Seurat object — median-1000 scaling is meant for raw integer bulk counts only. The goal is differential gene expression calling between conditions; median scaling plus log transform supports signature scoring, not DESeq2/edgeR-style dispersion-based DE testing. Samples lack a two-group design with EAD/non-EAD labels, since the downstream step is a two-sample Welch's t-test comparison.

skills.description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., DLPFC paired bulk samples) must be converted to Biobase ExpressionSet objects, filtered, and CPM-normalized prior to BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or benchmarking against CIBERSORT/MuSiC/BSEQ-sc.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-cpm-normalization
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-cpm-normalization Use when raw bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., DLPFC paired bulk samples) must be converted to Biobase ExpressionSet objects, filtered, and CPM-normalized prior to BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or benchmarking against CIBERSORT/MuSiC/BSEQ-sc. Expression data are already normalized (e.g., TPM/FPKM or previously CPM-scaled), so applying CountsToCPM would double-normalize and distort proportion estimates There is no paired single-cell/single-nucleus reference to align with (no cellType/SubjectName labels), since this normalization step exists to prepare the bulk eset for overlap-based reference decomposition Too few individuals have single-cell data, in which case the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable regardless of normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Normalize paired bulk RNA-seq count data to counts-per-million (CPM) and filter unexpressed and zero-variance genes with BisqueRNA utilities so the bulk ExpressionSet is comparable across individuals before reference-based cell-type decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Normalize paired bulk RNA-seq count data to counts-per-million (CPM) and filter unexpressed and zero-variance genes with BisqueRNA utilities so the bulk ExpressionSet is comparable across individuals before reference-based cell-type decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are already normalized (e.g., TPM/FPKM or previously CPM-scaled), so applying CountsToCPM would double-normalize and distort proportion estimates There is no paired single-cell/single-nucleus reference to align with (no cellType/SubjectName labels), since this normalization step exists to prepare the bulk eset for overlap-based reference decomposition Too few individuals have single-cell data, in which case the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable regardless of normalization

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq gene-by-sample expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need cell-type composition estimates covering >400 cell types, e.g., to compare TME cell abundance across tumor subtypes.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-interpretation
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-interpretation Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq gene-by-sample expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need cell-type composition estimates covering >400 cell types, e.g., to compare TME cell abundance across tumor subtypes. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — DCNet deconvolves bulk RNA-seq; for scRNA-seq cell landscape validation the paper uses datasets like GSE81861 or GSE75688 rather than applying DCNet inference. You need a limited curated immune panel only — CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, or xCell target fewer cell types and may suffice; DCNet is for broad (>400 cell type) landscapes. Marker genes of interest are absent from the input expression platform — 33 cell types were discarded because none of their marker genes were detected, so such cell types cannot be inferred. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Infers cell-type abundance landscapes from bulk RNA-seq samples using DCNet, an explainable neural network that embeds 434 cell types and 9078 marker genes, and interprets the resulting cell landscapes (e.g., differential abundance between LUAD and LUSC in TCGA). transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Infers cell-type abundance landscapes from bulk RNA-seq samples using DCNet, an explainable neural network that embeds 434 cell types and 9078 marker genes, and interprets the resulting cell landscapes (e.g., differential abundance between LUAD and LUSC in TCGA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — DCNet deconvolves bulk RNA-seq; for scRNA-seq cell landscape validation the paper uses datasets like GSE81861 or GSE75688 rather than applying DCNet inference. You need a limited curated immune panel only — CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, or xCell target fewer cell types and may suffice; DCNet is for broad (>400 cell type) landscapes. Marker genes of interest are absent from the input expression platform — 33 cell types were discarded because none of their marker genes were detected, so such cell types cannot be inferred.

skills.description: Use when estimating cell-type proportions in bulk or simulated bulk RNA-seq samples with a single-cell reference, and when choosing which subsampling/sketching method should build that reference from a large scRNA-seq atlas.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-with-single-cell-references
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-with-single-cell-references Use when estimating cell-type proportions in bulk or simulated bulk RNA-seq samples with a single-cell reference, and when choosing which subsampling/sketching method should build that reference from a large scRNA-seq atlas. The task is cell-type annotation or label transfer of single-cell data rather than estimating proportions in bulk samples — the scValue benchmark's core annotation tasks (PBMC/scANVI, mBrain/scPoli) are a different skill The bulk samples have no ground-truth or reference proportions, so Pearson/RMSE/MAE against truth cannot be computed for method comparison The single-cell reference lacks cell-type labels (cell_type_key column), which MuSiC's reference-based deconvolution requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark cell-type deconvolution of bulk/pseudobulk RNA-seq samples against sketch-based single-cell references using MuSiC, comparing subsampling methods (scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) by Pearson correlation, RMSE and MAE against known true proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-type deconvolution of bulk/pseudobulk RNA-seq samples against sketch-based single-cell references using MuSiC, comparing subsampling methods (scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) by Pearson correlation, RMSE and MAE against known true proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell-type annotation or label transfer of single-cell data rather than estimating proportions in bulk samples — the scValue benchmark's core annotation tasks (PBMC/scANVI, mBrain/scPoli) are a different skill The bulk samples have no ground-truth or reference proportions, so Pearson/RMSE/MAE against truth cannot be computed for method comparison The single-cell reference lacks cell-type labels (cell_type_key column), which MuSiC's reference-based deconvolution requires

skills.description: Use when you have matched scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq counts for the same biological system and want to quantify whether imputation improves differential expression concordance with bulk.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-differential-expression-analysis Use when you have matched scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq counts for the same biological system and want to quantify whether imputation improves differential expression concordance with bulk. No matched bulk RNA-seq data exist for the same system, so no bulk DE reference set can be built The goal is to evaluate imputation quality for clustering, visualization, or pseudotime inference rather than differential expression Cells are unlabeled and the number of clusters is unknown, preventing the labeled or c(7, "Spectrum") Bfimpute configurations used here http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark imputation of scRNA-seq dropout events by measuring how well DE calls agree with a bulk RNA-seq reference: DESeq2 is run on bulk counts to pick the top 200 bulk DE genes, then the raw and six imputed scRNA-seq matrices are re-run through DESeq2 and concordance is summarized as an AUC over FDR thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Benchmark imputation of scRNA-seq dropout events by measuring how well DE calls agree with a bulk RNA-seq reference: DESeq2 is run on bulk counts to pick the top 200 bulk DE genes, then the raw and six imputed scRNA-seq matrices are re-run through DESeq2 and concordance is summarized as an AUC over FDR thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched bulk RNA-seq data exist for the same system, so no bulk DE reference set can be built The goal is to evaluate imputation quality for clustering, visualization, or pseudotime inference rather than differential expression Cells are unlabeled and the number of clusters is unknown, preventing the labeled or c(7, "Spectrum") Bfimpute configurations used here

skills.description: Use when bulk count data must be degraded with simulated scRNA-seq-like dropout (targeting ~80% zero entries) to create a denoising benchmark against the original unperturbed matrix.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-dropout-noise-simulation
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-dropout-noise-simulation Use when bulk count data must be degraded with simulated scRNA-seq-like dropout (targeting ~80% zero entries) to create a denoising benchmark against the original unperturbed matrix. The input is already single-cell data with natural dropouts — the simulation is designed to impose scRNA-seq-like sparsity on bulk data where the true counts are known You need absolute quantification of expression rather than a relative denoiser benchmark — the simulated matrix destroys ~80% of entries and is only meaningful against the retained ground-truth matrix The analysis requires preserving true (celltype-specific) zeros — the paper notes the non-trivial distinction between true and false zero counts makes classical imputation assumptions risky http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates single-cell-like dropout on bulk RNA-seq count data by subtracting gene-wise exponentially distributed values so that a target fraction of entries (80%) become zeros, creating a controlled benchmark on which denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) can be evaluated against the original uncorrupted matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Simulates single-cell-like dropout on bulk RNA-seq count data by subtracting gene-wise exponentially distributed values so that a target fraction of entries (80%) become zeros, creating a controlled benchmark on which denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) can be evaluated against the original uncorrupted matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already single-cell data with natural dropouts — the simulation is designed to impose scRNA-seq-like sparsity on bulk data where the true counts are known You need absolute quantification of expression rather than a relative denoiser benchmark — the simulated matrix destroys ~80% of entries and is only meaningful against the retained ground-truth matrix The analysis requires preserving true (celltype-specific) zeros — the paper notes the non-trivial distinction between true and false zero counts makes classical imputation assumptions risky

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression matrix for a cell population of interest must be reformatted (gene-symbol-indexed) before computing ICELLNET cell-cell communication scores against reference partner cells.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-expression-preprocessing
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-expression-preprocessing Use when a bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression matrix for a cell population of interest must be reformatted (gene-symbol-indexed) before computing ICELLNET cell-cell communication scores against reference partner cells. Input is already single-cell data or a preformatted ICELLNET expression object — use the dedicated scRNA-seq tutorial/workflow instead of re-preprocessing The analysis goal is differential expression within one sample rather than inferring intercellular communication; ICELLNET preprocessing produces scoring inputs, not DE tables Non-human transcriptomes: the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocess bulk RNA-seq expression matrices into the gene-symbol-indexed format required by the ICELLNET communication-scoring framework, so a cell population of interest (e.g. CAF-S1, n=6 and CAF-S4, n=3) can be connected to reference partner transcriptomes such as the Human Primary Cell Atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: Preprocess bulk RNA-seq expression matrices into the gene-symbol-indexed format required by the ICELLNET communication-scoring framework, so a cell population of interest (e.g. CAF-S1, n=6 and CAF-S4, n=3) can be connected to reference partner transcriptomes such as the Human Primary Cell Atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already single-cell data or a preformatted ICELLNET expression object — use the dedicated scRNA-seq tutorial/workflow instead of re-preprocessing The analysis goal is differential expression within one sample rather than inferring intercellular communication; ICELLNET preprocessing produces scoring inputs, not DE tables Non-human transcriptomes: the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies

skills.description: Use when running BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or MarkerBasedDecomposition on bulk RNA-seq counts with a single-cell reference, and the inputs are still raw matrices, Seurat objects, or data frames that must first be cast into Biobase ExpressionSet format.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-expressionset-conversion
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-expressionset-conversion Use when running BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or MarkerBasedDecomposition on bulk RNA-seq counts with a single-cell reference, and the inputs are still raw matrices, Seurat objects, or data frames that must first be cast into Biobase ExpressionSet format. Bisque requires expression data in ExpressionSet format, with SubjectName and cellType phenoData columns on the single-cell object. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Converts bulk RNA-seq count matrices and scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference data (with cell type and individual labels) into Biobase ExpressionSet objects so that BisqueRNA decomposition functions can consume them. Bisque requires expression data in ExpressionSet format, with SubjectName and cellType phenoData columns on the single-cell object.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already in ExpressionSet format — re-conversion is unnecessary; proceed directly to BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition You only intend to run marker-based decomposition and never need subject-level overlap matching — a minimal bulk.eset conversion suffices, but a mislabeled sc.eset with wrong SubjectName parsing would silently break use.overlap

skills.description: Use when a raw bulk expression matrix (e.g., TCGA log2(TPM+1) from GDC) must be reduced to a highly variable gene set before fitting a PhenoPath covariate-pseudotime model.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-highly-variable-gene-selection
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-highly-variable-gene-selection Use when a raw bulk expression matrix (e.g., TCGA log2(TPM+1) from GDC) must be reduced to a highly variable gene set before fitting a PhenoPath covariate-pseudotime model. The input is already a reduced or feature-filtered expression matrix, or a single-cell count object where per-cell HVG selection conventions differ from bulk log2(TPM+1) variance filtering The goal is the downstream ranking of covariate-pathway interactions (interaction_effects / significant_interactions) rather than defining the input feature space for trajectory fitting Data are not bulk gene expression on a log2(TPM+1)-like scale (e.g., already-normalised microarray or proteomics matrices), where TPM-based variance ranking is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepares a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix for PhenoPath covariate-pseudotime modelling by restricting it to the top highly variable genes (e.g., 4579 genes from the TCGA-BRCA log2(TPM+1) matrix across 1135 samples), controlling noise while keeping the variational fit tractable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced or feature-filtered expression matrix, or a single-cell count object where per-cell HVG selection conventions differ from bulk log2(TPM+1) variance filtering The goal is the downstream ranking of covariate-pathway interactions (interaction_effects / significant_interactions) rather than defining the input feature space for trajectory fitting Data are not bulk gene expression on a log2(TPM+1)-like scale (e.g., already-normalised microarray or proteomics matrices), where TPM-based variance ranking is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq normalized expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) needs gene-set/module activity scores, and you must choose or benchmark among rROMA, GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA and z-score for differential pathway activity testing.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-pathway-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-pathway-activity-scoring Use when a bulk RNA-seq normalized expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) needs gene-set/module activity scores, and you must choose or benchmark among rROMA, GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA and z-score for differential pathway activity testing. The expression matrix is not normalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data (cpm/vst), so raw counts must first be normalized The dataset contains unimputed missing values — the authors recommend using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback The goal is a comprehensive view of biological systems with a single small gene-set collection — the README recommends combining multiple databases rather than relying on Hallmark alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmarks rROMA against sample-wise pathway quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) on bulk RNA-seq data (GSE176121, MSigDB Hallmark gene sets), showing rROMA's PC1-based module activity scores most consistently recover expected pathway shifts, e.g. TNFα signaling in IL17+TNFα-treated airway epithelial cultures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks rROMA against sample-wise pathway quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) on bulk RNA-seq data (GSE176121, MSigDB Hallmark gene sets), showing rROMA's PC1-based module activity scores most consistently recover expected pathway shifts, e.g. TNFα signaling in IL17+TNFα-treated airway epithelial cultures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is not normalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data (cpm/vst), so raw counts must first be normalized The dataset contains unimputed missing values — the authors recommend using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback The goal is a comprehensive view of biological systems with a single small gene-set collection — the README recommends combining multiple databases rather than relying on Hallmark alone

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression with binary drug response annotations is available and a drug sensitivity predictor must be trained (or resumed from a checkpoint) before transfer to scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-predictor-training
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-predictor-training Use when bulk RNA-seq expression with binary drug response annotations is available and a drug sensitivity predictor must be trained (or resumed from a checkpoint) before transfer to scRNA-seq data. The goal is already single-cell prediction with a bulk-trained model — use scmodel.py (the transfer step) instead; bulkmodel.py only trains on bulk cell-line data No bulk-level drug response labels or bulk expression matrix are available — the predictor cannot be trained without ALL_expression.csv and ALL_label_binary_wf.csv You need drug response prediction from bulk-only data without any scRNA-seq transfer — scDEAL is designed to augment scRNA-seq analysis with bulk data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train a bulk-level drug sensitivity predictor by fitting a denoising autoencoder (DAE) encoder plus predictor head on bulk RNA-seq expression (ALL_expression.csv) with binary drug-response labels (ALL_label_binary_wf.csv), producing checkpoints that scDEAL later transfers to single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Train a bulk-level drug sensitivity predictor by fitting a denoising autoencoder (DAE) encoder plus predictor head on bulk RNA-seq expression (ALL_expression.csv) with binary drug-response labels (ALL_label_binary_wf.csv), producing checkpoints that scDEAL later transfers to single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is already single-cell prediction with a bulk-trained model — use scmodel.py (the transfer step) instead; bulkmodel.py only trains on bulk cell-line data No bulk-level drug response labels or bulk expression matrix are available — the predictor cannot be trained without ALL_expression.csv and ALL_label_binary_wf.csv You need drug response prediction from bulk-only data without any scRNA-seq transfer — scDEAL is designed to augment scRNA-seq analysis with bulk data

skills.description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. anti-PD-1 vs control CD8 TIL samples from GEO/SRA, such as GSE62771) need QC and trimming before Salmon quasi-mapping quantification.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-read-qc-trimming
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-read-qc-trimming Use when raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. anti-PD-1 vs control CD8 TIL samples from GEO/SRA, such as GSE62771) need QC and trimming before Salmon quasi-mapping quantification. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data (Smart-seq2 plate-based or 10X droplet-based), which follows a different QC/alignment path than bulk FASTQ trimming Data is already quantified transcript-level abundance (e.g. Salmon/Kallisto output) and only needs tximport aggregation and DESeq2 modeling Input is already a gene-level count matrix — trimming has no effect at this stage http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality-control and adapter/low-quality trimming of raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ reads (via Trimmomatic) as the first stage of a pipeline that quantifies CD8 TIL bulk transcriptomes with Salmon and tests EM-like signature enrichment upon anti-PD-1 therapy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Quality-control and adapter/low-quality trimming of raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ reads (via Trimmomatic) as the first stage of a pipeline that quantifies CD8 TIL bulk transcriptomes with Salmon and tests EM-like signature enrichment upon anti-PD-1 therapy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data (Smart-seq2 plate-based or 10X droplet-based), which follows a different QC/alignment path than bulk FASTQ trimming Data is already quantified transcript-level abundance (e.g. Salmon/Kallisto output) and only needs tximport aggregation and DESeq2 modeling Input is already a gene-level count matrix — trimming has no effect at this stage

skills.description: Use when a single-cell pattern/decomposition method (ACTIONet archetypes, cNMF components) must be benchmarked against labeled bulk cell-sorted RNA-seq profiles to test whether learned cell states match known cell-type signatures.
skills.name: bulk-rnaseq-reference-correlation
skills.search_text: bulk-rnaseq-reference-correlation Use when a single-cell pattern/decomposition method (ACTIONet archetypes, cNMF components) must be benchmarked against labeled bulk cell-sorted RNA-seq profiles to test whether learned cell states match known cell-type signatures. No labeled bulk sorted-cell reference profiles exist for the tissue/cell types under study — correlation cannot be interpreted without known ground-truth profiles. skills.summary: Applies a pre-trained Miscell self-supervised encoder (deep neural network latent feature extractor) to TCGA pan-cancer bulk tumor expression data to transfer knowledge learned from single cells into bulk-sample latent features, then tests their association with overall survival (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox proportional hazards).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data without a pre-trained checkpoint — Miscell training requires at least two GPUs and large sample size, and this skill concerns transferring to bulk data Bulk dataset is too small — 'Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance' Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell does not include batch correction, so it must be handled as a preprocessing step before feature extraction

skills.description: Use when a bulk tumour expression matrix (log2(TPM+1), highly variable genes) with a per-sample covariate such as MSI or ER status must be mapped onto a 1D pseudotime and genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions identified.
skills.name: bulk-tumour-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: bulk-tumour-pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when a bulk tumour expression matrix (log2(TPM+1), highly variable genes) with a per-sample covariate such as MSI or ER status must be mapped onto a 1D pseudotime and genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions identified. Features are known to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime No covariate of interest exists and the goal is purely homogeneous trajectory inference, since the covariate-pseudotime interaction machinery is the point of this skill Complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings are needed — the paper explicitly defers this to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers latent pseudotemporal trajectories from bulk tumour expression cohorts (e.g. TCGA-COAD, TCGA-BRCA) with PhenoPath's Bayesian covariate model, so that gene-covariate interactions (e.g. MLH1 with MSI status, ESR1 with ER status) can be ranked along a disease trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Infers latent pseudotemporal trajectories from bulk tumour expression cohorts (e.g. TCGA-COAD, TCGA-BRCA) with PhenoPath's Bayesian covariate model, so that gene-covariate interactions (e.g. MLH1 with MSI status, ESR1 with ER status) can be ranked along a disease trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are known to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime No covariate of interest exists and the goal is purely homogeneous trajectory inference, since the covariate-pseudotime interaction machinery is the point of this skill Complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings are needed — the paper explicitly defers this to future work

skills.name: bursting-kinetics-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: bursting-kinetics-parameter-estimation Use when fitting Canopy2's beta-Poisson bursting model and mutation-specific gene activation/deactivation rates (alpha, beta) must be estimated from single-cell gene expression counts (e.g. featurecounts.qc of GBM10_preproc) before running get_trees(). Alpha and beta are already supplied as 1 x M vectors (e.g. from a prior run or simulation settings like alpha=0.1, beta=1) — re-estimation is unnecessary No single-cell gene expression matrix exists for the mutation-host genes (e.g. bulk DNA-only input), since both BPSC and SCALE require gene expression counts The dataset is very large and a full MCMC-based fit is infeasible without falling back to get_burstiness_scale() — do not default to BPSC when runtime is prohibitive http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Estimates mutation-specific gene activation and deactivation rates (alpha, beta) that parameterize transcriptional bursting in Canopy2's beta-Poisson model, using BPSC (MCMC) or SCALE (moment estimators) fitted to single-cell gene expression counts, independent of the mutational read counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Estimates mutation-specific gene activation and deactivation rates (alpha, beta) that parameterize transcriptional bursting in Canopy2's beta-Poisson model, using BPSC (MCMC) or SCALE (moment estimators) fitted to single-cell gene expression counts, independent of the mutational read counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Alpha and beta are already supplied as 1 x M vectors (e.g. from a prior run or simulation settings like alpha=0.1, beta=1) — re-estimation is unnecessary No single-cell gene expression matrix exists for the mutation-host genes (e.g. bulk DNA-only input), since both BPSC and SCALE require gene expression counts The dataset is very large and a full MCMC-based fit is infeasible without falling back to get_burstiness_scale() — do not default to BPSC when runtime is prohibitive

skills.search_text: ca-biplot-visualization-with-feature-labeling Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., SingleCellExperiment) reduced with standard CA and want a geometric joint display of cells and genes to identify which features (e.g., top 20 by loading L2 norm) drive cell-population separation. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has already been log(x + 1)-transformed to 'logcounts' and reduced with PCA — CA on Pearson residuals expects raw counts, and the biplot interpretation of a PCA solution differs Data come from multiple batches/samples requiring integration — use corralm (multi-table CA) rather than the single-table corral biplot workflow The goal is quantitative clustering-accuracy benchmarking (e.g., ARI) rather than exploratory visualization — the biplot aids cluster interpretation, not performance measurement

skills.description: Use when a GWAS locus has a known/validated target gene or tissue and you need to determine which tissue's eQTL explains the trait association, especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus).
skills.name: cad-gwas-locus-fine-mapping
skills.search_text: cad-gwas-locus-fine-mapping Use when a GWAS locus has a known/validated target gene or tissue and you need to determine which tissue's eQTL explains the trait association, especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus). Loci whose trait effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — the article notes such loci 'cannot be explored with CAFEH' Studies with large LD differences between datasets (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix shared across all studies Datasets with missing entries in the effect size/z-score matrix — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Jointly fine-maps and colocalizes CAD GWAS signals with eQTLs across 49 GTEx tissue studies using CAFEH-S in z-score mode, to prioritize the target tissue at literature-validated CAD loci (LDLR, APOE, APOB, PCSK9, ANGPTL4, LPL, ABCG8, CETP, TWIST1, etc.) and benchmark against single-signal pairwise COLOC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Jointly fine-maps and colocalizes CAD GWAS signals with eQTLs across 49 GTEx tissue studies using CAFEH-S in z-score mode, to prioritize the target tissue at literature-validated CAD loci (LDLR, APOE, APOB, PCSK9, ANGPTL4, LPL, ABCG8, CETP, TWIST1, etc.) and benchmark against single-signal pairwise COLOC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose trait effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — the article notes such loci 'cannot be explored with CAFEH' Studies with large LD differences between datasets (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix shared across all studies Datasets with missing entries in the effect size/z-score matrix — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets

skills.description: Use when individual-level genotype and phenotype matrices are available for multiple eQTL studies or tissues and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization that can resolve multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) that mislead standard colocalization.
skills.name: cafeh-genotype-mode-bayesian-fine-mapping
skills.search_text: cafeh-genotype-mode-bayesian-fine-mapping Use when individual-level genotype and phenotype matrices are available for multiple eQTL studies or tissues and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization that can resolve multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) that mislead standard colocalization. Only summary statistics are available without individual-level genotypes — use CAFEH beta or z mode instead (beta mode needs LD, betas, standard errors, sample sizes; z mode needs LD and z scores). The causal variants may be absent from the tested datasets — CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix and implicitly assumes causal variants are present. Large LD differences between studies (e.g., ancestry differences) are expected, since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix and inference could be impacted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Fit the CAFEH Bayesian model in genotype (individual-level data) mode to jointly fine-map and colocalize genetic association signals across multiple studies/traits, accounting for allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal components per locus). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Fit the CAFEH Bayesian model in genotype (individual-level data) mode to jointly fine-map and colocalize genetic association signals across multiple studies/traits, accounting for allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal components per locus).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only summary statistics are available without individual-level genotypes — use CAFEH beta or z mode instead (beta mode needs LD, betas, standard errors, sample sizes; z mode needs LD and z scores). The causal variants may be absent from the tested datasets — CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix and implicitly assumes causal variants are present. Large LD differences between studies (e.g., ancestry differences) are expected, since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix and inference could be impacted.

skills.description: Use when you have GWAS/eQTL summary statistics (z scores or betas+SEs), a reference LD matrix, and per-study sample sizes, and need joint colocalization/fine-mapping across tens of traits or tissues to prioritize a causal target tissue.

skills.search_text: cafeh-summary-statistic-colocalization Use when you have GWAS/eQTL summary statistics (z scores or betas+SEs), a reference LD matrix, and per-study sample sizes, and need joint colocalization/fine-mapping across tens of traits or tissues to prioritize a causal target tissue. skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have individual-level genotype/phenotype data and no summary statistics — use CAFEH genotype mode (`--mode genotype`) with -X/-Y instead of --mode z The locus's effect is mediated by coding variants without eQTL signal, or there are large LD differences between studies (e.g. ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix and cannot explore such loci Causal variants are missing from some tested datasets — CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix

skills.description: Use when building an enhanced long-read isoform annotation and you need to confirm read 5'/3' ends against CAGE peak (FANTOM, mm10) and polyA site (polyASite 2.0) BED intervals before collapsing novel intron chains.
skills.name: cage-peak-proximal-tss-annotation
skills.search_text: cage-peak-proximal-tss-annotation Use when building an enhanced long-read isoform annotation and you need to confirm read 5'/3' ends against CAGE peak (FANTOM, mm10) and polyA site (polyASite 2.0) BED intervals before collapsing novel intron chains. No external CAGE peak or polyA site reference exists for your genome version, since TSS/polyA assignment depends entirely on proximity to these interval files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Annotates long-read transcript start sites (TSS) and polyA sites by proximity to external FANTOM CAGE peak and polyASite 2.0 interval files, so that only reads with externally confirmed 5' and 3' ends contribute novel intron chains to an enhanced annotation (76 high-confidence novel isoforms in the source study). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Annotates long-read transcript start sites (TSS) and polyA sites by proximity to external FANTOM CAGE peak and polyASite 2.0 interval files, so that only reads with externally confirmed 5' and 3' ends contribute novel intron chains to an enhanced annotation (76 high-confidence novel isoforms in the source study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need gene-level or exon-level quantification from short reads — this skill addresses novel long-read isoform discovery, not bulk expression testing. skills.description: Use when Totem has generated a large set of candidate clusterings (k-medoids/CLARA over many k values) and one must automatically select clustering(s) to feed Slingshot MST construction, using Calinski-Harabasz scores combined with cell connectivity.
skills.name: calinski-harabasz-cluster-ranking
skills.search_text: calinski-harabasz-cluster-ranking Use when Totem has generated a large set of candidate clusterings (k-medoids/CLARA over many k values) and one must automatically select clustering(s) to feed Slingshot MST construction, using Calinski-Harabasz scores combined with cell connectivity.
