skills.name: cancer-associated-fibroblast-subtype-annotation
skills.search_text: cancer-associated-fibroblast-subtype-annotation Use when a scRNA-seq stromal/CAF clustering partition contains low-ROGUE (impure) clusters and finer subtypes — such as myCAF splits or CD74/MHC-II+ apCAFs — must be resolved and annotated. The input partition already consists of high-ROGUE (pure) clusters near the 0.9 purity threshold — no re-clustering is needed. Data are low-quality or continuous/trajectory-like, where the 0.9 ROGUE threshold is not appropriate and the cutoff must instead be determined from global ROGUE values. The goal is to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the paper states ROGUE does not yet support this. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 ROGUE-guided re-clustering of low-purity cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) clusters to resolve purer subtypes (e.g., splitting the myCAF population into RGS5/ACTA2/GPX3 clusters and identifying an antigen-presenting apCAF cluster), then annotating subtypes by marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: ROGUE-guided re-clustering of low-purity cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) clusters to resolve purer subtypes (e.g., splitting the myCAF population into RGS5/ACTA2/GPX3 clusters and identifying an antigen-presenting apCAF cluster), then annotating subtypes by marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input partition already consists of high-ROGUE (pure) clusters near the 0.9 purity threshold — no re-clustering is needed. Data are low-quality or continuous/trajectory-like, where the 0.9 ROGUE threshold is not appropriate and the cutoff must instead be determined from global ROGUE values. The goal is to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the paper states ROGUE does not yet support this.

skills.description: Use when raw TCGA-style RNA-Seq gene count matrices for paired normal vs cancer samples (e.g., KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) must be turned into a differential-expression baseline signature to benchmark other gene sets by classification.
skills.name: cancer-biomarker-signature-generation
skills.search_text: cancer-biomarker-signature-generation Use when raw TCGA-style RNA-Seq gene count matrices for paired normal vs cancer samples (e.g., KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) must be turned into a differential-expression baseline signature to benchmark other gene sets by classification. The goal is the paper's proposed IC gene sets: those are extracted from fused co-expression networks via the disparity filter and the Gephi modularity method, not from DESeq2 - differential expression is only the comparison baseline here Input is already-normalized or filtered expression (e.g., zFPKM-normalized values) rather than raw integer gene counts, since DESeq2's dispersion model requires count data The task is finding survival-associated biomarkers: the article reports only 6 DE genes significantly associated with survival versus 44 IC genes, making the DE baseline the weaker source for that goal http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates the typically-used differential-expression baseline gene signature by running DESeq2 (R/Bioconductor) on TCGA RNA-Seq gene count matrices for normal vs cancer samples of KIRC, LIHC and PRAD, yielding 1059 genes (54 miRNAs), 434 (27) and 218 (24) respectively. These DE sets, reduced via LASSO into DEL sets, benchmark the paper's fused co-expression IC gene sets in normal/cancer classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Generates the typically-used differential-expression baseline gene signature by running DESeq2 (R/Bioconductor) on TCGA RNA-Seq gene count matrices for normal vs cancer samples of KIRC, LIHC and PRAD, yielding 1059 genes (54 miRNAs), 434 (27) and 218 (24) respectively. These DE sets, reduced via LASSO into DEL sets, benchmark the paper's fused co-expression IC gene sets in normal/cancer classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is the paper's proposed IC gene sets: those are extracted from fused co-expression networks via the disparity filter and the Gephi modularity method, not from DESeq2 - differential expression is only the comparison baseline here Input is already-normalized or filtered expression (e.g., zFPKM-normalized values) rather than raw integer gene counts, since DESeq2's dispersion model requires count data The task is finding survival-associated biomarkers: the article reports only 6 DE genes significantly associated with survival versus 44 IC genes, making the DE baseline the weaker source for that goal

skills.description: Use when you have matched gene expression profiles for cancer cell lines plus drug sensitivity (IC50) data (e.g., the GDSC panel) and want to identify which signaling pathway activities explain drug response.
skills.name: cancer-cell-line-drug-response-analysis
skills.search_text: cancer-cell-line-drug-response-analysis Use when you have matched gene expression profiles for cancer cell lines plus drug sensitivity (IC50) data (e.g., the GDSC panel) and want to identify which signaling pathway activities explain drug response. You need pathway activity estimates for pathways outside the 11 PROGENy footprints (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) — no perturbation-based signature exists for them Your drug-sensitivity values are raw dose-response curves rather than processed IC50 values requiring no further curve fitting You require tissue- or context-specific pathway signatures; the article notes consensus PROGENy signatures may be less reflective of activation than tissue-specific ones http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces drug-sensitivity associations by testing whether PROGENy-inferred pathway activity scores explain IC50 values across a cancer cell line panel (GDSC: 265 drugs, 805 cell lines), yielding a drug-pathway association table filtered at 10% FDR. It demonstrates that perturbation-derived pathway footprints provide markers for drug indications. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Reproduces drug-sensitivity associations by testing whether PROGENy-inferred pathway activity scores explain IC50 values across a cancer cell line panel (GDSC: 265 drugs, 805 cell lines), yielding a drug-pathway association table filtered at 10% FDR. It demonstrates that perturbation-derived pathway footprints provide markers for drug indications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need pathway activity estimates for pathways outside the 11 PROGENy footprints (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) — no perturbation-based signature exists for them Your drug-sensitivity values are raw dose-response curves rather than processed IC50 values requiring no further curve fitting You require tissue- or context-specific pathway signatures; the article notes consensus PROGENy signatures may be less reflective of activation than tissue-specific ones

skills.search_text: cancer-cell-of-origin-annotation Use when annotating epithelial cells in a cancer scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., liver, pancreatic, colon, kidney, lung, mammary tumors) to identify malignant cells and infer their cell of origin from a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction. Input tissue is not one of the organs with a pretrained cancer model (only Kidney, Large_Intestine, Liver, Lung, Mammary, Pancreas are supported) — train a custom model instead Input is normal tissue rather than tumor data — use the standard census_main annotation without predict_cancer=T The Seurat object lacks a UMAP dimensionality reduction, which the Census prediction and label-stabilizing steps require http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Apply Census's organ-specific CCLE-trained cancer models to annotate malignant cells in scRNA-seq data and predict their likely cell of origin, using hierarchically organized gradient-boosted decision trees and a UMAP-space label-stabilizing algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Apply Census's organ-specific CCLE-trained cancer models to annotate malignant cells in scRNA-seq data and predict their likely cell of origin, using hierarchically organized gradient-boosted decision trees and a UMAP-space label-stabilizing algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input tissue is not one of the organs with a pretrained cancer model (only Kidney, Large_Intestine, Liver, Lung, Mammary, Pancreas are supported) — train a custom model instead Input is normal tissue rather than tumor data — use the standard census_main annotation without predict_cancer=T The Seurat object lacks a UMAP dimensionality reduction, which the Census prediction and label-stabilizing steps require

skills.description: Use when evaluating a pretrained malignant-cell annotation model (Cancer-Finder, checkpoints/sc_pretrain_article.pkl) against database-curated tumor annotations across many scRNA-seq datasets to test generalization at scale.
skills.name: cancer-database-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: cancer-database-annotation-comparison Use when evaluating a pretrained malignant-cell annotation model (Cancer-Finder, checkpoints/sc_pretrain_article.pkl) against database-curated tumor annotations across many scRNA-seq datasets to test generalization at scale. Input is hematologic tumor scRNA-seq data — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data Evaluating spatial transcriptomic spots rather than single-cell data — ST prediction requires spatial-transcriptomics-trained checkpoints and Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships among spots Only one or a few datasets are available — the correlation-based database-scale validation is designed for many datasets (n = 152 in the reference study), not single-sample spot checks http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Validates Cancer-Finder's malignant cell predictions at database scale by comparing per-dataset malignant percentages predicted on external scRNA-seq databases (e.g., CancerSCEM) against the percentages reported by the database, using a two-tailed Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is hematologic tumor scRNA-seq data — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data Evaluating spatial transcriptomic spots rather than single-cell data — ST prediction requires spatial-transcriptomics-trained checkpoints and Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships among spots Only one or a few datasets are available — the correlation-based database-scale validation is designed for many datasets (n = 152 in the reference study), not single-sample spot checks

skills.description: Use when ranking driver-gene prediction lists (your own or tools like PNC, DawnRank, MutSigCV) against curated CGC, NCG or PMH benchmark gene sets with precision, recall and a precision-weighted F0.2 score across TCGA cancer types.
skills.name: cancer-driver-gene-benchmark-scoring
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-gene-benchmark-scoring Use when ranking driver-gene prediction lists (your own or tools like PNC, DawnRank, MutSigCV) against curated CGC, NCG or PMH benchmark gene sets with precision, recall and a precision-weighted F0.2 score across TCGA cancer types. Input is still raw expression matrices (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal) rather than gene-symbol driver lists — the upstream WMDS.net integer-programming prediction step must run first. The cancer type or study has no meaningful overlap with the CGC, NCG or PMH curated driver sets, so TP/FP/FN counts and F0.2 values would be uninformative. The goal is to run driver discovery itself (constructing Gene_Net / differential co-expression networks and solving the integer program) rather than to score already-produced gene lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores cancer driver gene prediction lists against curated benchmark gene sets — 616-gene CGC (COSMIC), 711-gene NCG and the 501-gene PMH set — computing precision, recall and the precision-weighted F_beta measure (beta^2 = 0.2) per tool and TCGA cancer type, in order to rank predictors such as WMDS.net, WMDS.netP and 11 comparison tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Scores cancer driver gene prediction lists against curated benchmark gene sets — 616-gene CGC (COSMIC), 711-gene NCG and the 501-gene PMH set — computing precision, recall and the precision-weighted F_beta measure (beta^2 = 0.2) per tool and TCGA cancer type, in order to rank predictors such as WMDS.net, WMDS.netP and 11 comparison tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw expression matrices (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal) rather than gene-symbol driver lists — the upstream WMDS.net integer-programming prediction step must run first. The cancer type or study has no meaningful overlap with the CGC, NCG or PMH curated driver sets, so TP/FP/FN counts and F0.2 values would be uninformative. The goal is to run driver discovery itself (constructing Gene_Net / differential co-expression networks and solving the integer program) rather than to score already-produced gene lists.

skills.description: Use when genes must be classified cancer driver vs non-driver from multi-omics features averaged per gene over a directed GRN such as DawnNet, KEGG, or RegNetwork, e.g. to reproduce the DGMP 5-fold cross-validation benchmark.
skills.name: cancer-driver-gene-classification
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-gene-classification Use when genes must be classified cancer driver vs non-driver from multi-omics features averaged per gene over a directed GRN such as DawnNet, KEGG, or RegNetwork, e.g. to reproduce the DGMP 5-fold cross-validation benchmark. The input graph is an undirected PPI network rather than a directed GRN — DGMP's DGCN captures directed regulation information (forward/backward, Zin/Zout) that undirected graphs cannot provide. Per-patient or per-sample predictions are required — DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which the authors note ignores the specific characteristics of individual cancer patients. The goal is recurrent-mutation significance testing (MutSigCV-style) rather than supervised classification from integrated multi-omics features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Trains DGMP — a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) jointed with an MLP, whose three DGCN embeddings (ZF, Zin, Zout) and MLP embedding (ZMLP) are concatenated into a fully connected network — on per-gene 4-omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) over directed GRNs (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) to output per-gene cancer-driver probabilities under 5-fold cross-validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Trains DGMP — a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) jointed with an MLP, whose three DGCN embeddings (ZF, Zin, Zout) and MLP embedding (ZMLP) are concatenated into a fully connected network — on per-gene 4-omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) over directed GRNs (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) to output per-gene cancer-driver probabilities under 5-fold cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input graph is an undirected PPI network rather than a directed GRN — DGMP's DGCN captures directed regulation information (forward/backward, Zin/Zout) that undirected graphs cannot provide. Per-patient or per-sample predictions are required — DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which the authors note ignores the specific characteristics of individual cancer patients. The goal is recurrent-mutation significance testing (MutSigCV-style) rather than supervised classification from integrated multi-omics features.

skills.description: Use when somatic mutation data (e.g. COSMIC MAF-style coding mutations) must be converted into per-gene mutation-type features and genes classified as TSG vs OG, especially to nominate low-frequency candidate drivers among unlabelled genes without background-mutation-rate bias.
skills.name: cancer-driver-gene-classification
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-gene-classification Use when somatic mutation data (e.g. COSMIC MAF-style coding mutations) must be converted into per-gene mutation-type features and genes classified as TSG vs OG, especially to nominate low-frequency candidate drivers among unlabelled genes without background-mutation-rate bias. The input is already a processed feature table or you only need mutation-rate-based driver detection (MutSigCV-style background-rate modelling) rather than TSG/OG functional classification You need tissue-specific predictions from raw per-tissue mutation subsets — use the tissue-specific variant workflow (TSG_OG_tissueAnalysis.py) on tissues with greater than 1000 samples instead of the pan-cancer model Missense/frameshift entropy and frequency features cannot be computed from your mutation data (as with Tokheim et al. data), since the classifier depends on these 37 features http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A pan-cancer random forest workflow (cTaG) that classifies genes as tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) or oncogenes (OGs) using 37 ratio-metric and entropy features derived from COSMIC somatic mutation data, and uses consensus across cross-validation fold models to predict new driver genes among unlabelled genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: A pan-cancer random forest workflow (cTaG) that classifies genes as tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) or oncogenes (OGs) using 37 ratio-metric and entropy features derived from COSMIC somatic mutation data, and uses consensus across cross-validation fold models to predict new driver genes among unlabelled genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table or you only need mutation-rate-based driver detection (MutSigCV-style background-rate modelling) rather than TSG/OG functional classification You need tissue-specific predictions from raw per-tissue mutation subsets — use the tissue-specific variant workflow (TSG_OG_tissueAnalysis.py) on tissues with greater than 1000 samples instead of the pan-cancer model Missense/frameshift entropy and frequency features cannot be computed from your mutation data (as with Tokheim et al. data), since the classifier depends on these 37 features

The goal is training or evaluating DGMP prediction accuracy itself (use 5-fold cross-validation accuracy, 'acc', rather than post-hoc omics-feature comparison) Input is raw sequencing or expression data rather than precomputed per-gene multi-omics alteration matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Rank predicted cancer driver genes from DGMP 'logits' output, partition them into known cancer genes (CGs) and non-probable cancer genes (NPCGs) via NCG annotation, and evaluate whether NPCGs differ from CGs across four multi-omics features using Mann-Whitney U tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004

skills.description: Use when a driver-gene prediction method must be benchmarked for precision against curated reference driver sets (Bailey et al. pan-cancer list or CGC), especially to rank methods like cTaG, TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet on the same evaluation genes.
skills.name: cancer-gene-census-reference-list-validation
skills.search_text: cancer-gene-census-reference-list-validation Use when a driver-gene prediction method must be benchmarked for precision against curated reference driver sets (Bailey et al. pan-cancer list or CGC), especially to rank methods like cTaG, TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet on the same evaluation genes. skills.summary: Validates and compares predicted pan-cancer driver genes by computing precision TP/(TP+FP) against curated reference lists — the Bailey et al. pan-cancer driver list (excluding the 136 TSGs and 76 OGs used for training, leaving a 92-gene evaluation set) and the Cancer Gene Census (CGC) driver gene list — for cTaG, TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The genes under evaluation are part of the 136 TSGs / 76 OGs used to train the cTaG model — these must be excluded from the Bailey et al. evaluation set, so precision on them would be inflated. skills.summary: FeatureCorr-driven pairwise co-expression analysis of cancer gene panels: pairwise_corr computes gene-gene correlations on log2-transformed TCGA Pan-Cancer expression (logTCGA40, 40 genes from >10K samples) and renders a hierarchically clustered correlation heatmap as its default output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is how one prime gene (e.g., RNASEH2A) correlates with many others — use FeatureCorr::primefeature_corr (prime feature correlation) instead of pairwise_corr. Input is single-cell data with non-viable cells and low abundance genes that require read count filtration — the skill targets bulk sequencing/microarray feature tables. skills.summary: Builds a gene-level significance table for differentially mutated genes between two phenotype strata (e.g., hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD) using ARMT's maftools-backed differential mutation analysis, filtered at p < 0.05 and FDR < 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is mutation visualization only (oncoplots, VAF, oncogenic pathway summary) rather than between-group significance testing — use ARMT's Mutant mapping page instead Input mutation data is not a standard .maf file (ARMT requires TCGA-like mutation annotation format for the differential mutation analysis) The comparison involves more than two groups or a continuous association rather than a high-vs-low split of a numeric factor

skills.description: Use when analyzing human breast cancer scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE148093) with GEMLI to discriminate symmetric vs asymmetric DCIS/inv_tumor cell fates and call DEGs marking the onset of invasiveness.
skills.name: cancer-invasiveness-deg-validation
skills.search_text: cancer-invasiveness-deg-validation Use when analyzing human breast cancer scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE148093) with GEMLI to discriminate symmetric vs asymmetric DCIS/inv_tumor cell fates and call DEGs marking the onset of invasiveness. The dataset is not scRNA-seq (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial data without single-cell lineages), since GEMLI predicts lineages solely from single-cell expression memory The cell population contains only distantly related cells, where the paper states GEMLI performs less robustly The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months, which exceeds GEMLI's scope of lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions and requires genetic-mark-based approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the GEMLI breast cancer case study: predicting DCIS-to-invasive (asymmetric) cell lineages from scRNA-seq and calling differentially expressed genes between DCIS cells in symmetric vs asymmetric lineages to uncover invasion markers (CDH2) and novel candidates (DCAF7, LINC01999). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Reproduces the GEMLI breast cancer case study: predicting DCIS-to-invasive (asymmetric) cell lineages from scRNA-seq and calling differentially expressed genes between DCIS cells in symmetric vs asymmetric lineages to uncover invasion markers (CDH2) and novel candidates (DCAF7, LINC01999).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not scRNA-seq (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial data without single-cell lineages), since GEMLI predicts lineages solely from single-cell expression memory The cell population contains only distantly related cells, where the paper states GEMLI performs less robustly The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months, which exceeds GEMLI's scope of lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions and requires genetic-mark-based approaches

skills.description: Use when assigning established molecular subtype labels (e.g., CRCSC CMS, PAM50) to tumor RNA-Seq or microarray samples, especially cross-platform validation where signature-gene classifiers fail due to batch effects or unpaired gene annotation.
skills.name: cancer-molecular-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: cancer-molecular-subtype-classification Use when assigning established molecular subtype labels (e.g., CRCSC CMS, PAM50) to tumor RNA-Seq or microarray samples, especially cross-platform validation where signature-gene classifiers fail due to batch effects or unpaired gene annotation. The goal is de novo discovery/clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' and requires pre-existing subtype labels. Input is not a gene expression matrix with mappable Entrez gene annotation (e.g., mutation, methylation, or imaging data) — functional spectra depend on gene-set enrichment over gene identifiers. The MSigDB gene set database available is not comprehensive — the paper warns that 'the prior knowledge of gene sets needs to be comprehensive to avoid potential bias'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and apply DeepCC, an ANN-based supervised classifier that converts gene expression profiles into pathway-activity 'functional spectra' (MSigDB gene-set enrichment features) to assign cancer molecular subtype labels (e.g., CMS for CRC, PAM50 for breast cancer), platform-independently. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Train and apply DeepCC, an ANN-based supervised classifier that converts gene expression profiles into pathway-activity 'functional spectra' (MSigDB gene-set enrichment features) to assign cancer molecular subtype labels (e.g., CMS for CRC, PAM50 for breast cancer), platform-independently.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery/clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' and requires pre-existing subtype labels. Input is not a gene expression matrix with mappable Entrez gene annotation (e.g., mutation, methylation, or imaging data) — functional spectra depend on gene-set enrichment over gene identifiers. The MSigDB gene set database available is not comprehensive — the paper warns that 'the prior knowledge of gene sets needs to be comprehensive to avoid potential bias'.

skills.description: Use when you need to merge gene alteration, survival, GO-similarity, and protein-RNA binding evidence for candidate RBPs into one feature matrix before unsupervised clustering of circRNA regulators.
skills.name: cancer-multiomics-feature-integration
skills.search_text: cancer-multiomics-feature-integration Use when you need to merge gene alteration, survival, GO-similarity, and protein-RNA binding evidence for candidate RBPs into one feature matrix before unsupervised clustering of circRNA regulators. You already have a merged candidate regulator feature table (MATRIX.txt) and only need downstream clustering or validation steps Your data are not cancer samples with matched TCGA alteration/clinical data and circRNA expression profiles — the article flags generalization to other diseases (e.g., neurodegenerative disease) as untested You need supervised prediction of circRNA-regulating RBPs from known regulators — the article lists this as an unimplemented potential extension, not what this unsupervised pipeline does http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds the CRIT feature matrix by integrating five multi-omics features (ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) for 1344 candidate RBPs across 12 TCGA cancer types and the MiOncoCirc compendium, then clusters them via NMF to surface circRNA-regulator-enriched clusters. It is the core data-integration step that turns heterogeneous genomics, transcriptomics, and protein-RNA interactomics evidence into a single matrix suitable for unsupervised regulator discovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Builds the CRIT feature matrix by integrating five multi-omics features (ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) for 1344 candidate RBPs across 12 TCGA cancer types and the MiOncoCirc compendium, then clusters them via NMF to surface circRNA-regulator-enriched clusters. It is the core data-integration step that turns heterogeneous genomics, transcriptomics, and protein-RNA interactomics evidence into a single matrix suitable for unsupervised regulator discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a merged candidate regulator feature table (MATRIX.txt) and only need downstream clustering or validation steps Your data are not cancer samples with matched TCGA alteration/clinical data and circRNA expression profiles — the article flags generalization to other diseases (e.g., neurodegenerative disease) as untested You need supervised prediction of circRNA-regulating RBPs from known regulators — the article lists this as an unimplemented potential extension, not what this unsupervised pipeline does

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from metastatic tumour biopsies (e.g. breast, kidney, lung, ovarian, skin cancer metastases) lack a known primary and the goal is to infer each sample's cancer tissue of origin at the cancer-cell level.
skills.name: cancer-primary-origin-prediction-from-metastatic-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: cancer-primary-origin-prediction-from-metastatic-scrnaseq Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from metastatic tumour biopsies (e.g. breast, kidney, lung, ovarian, skin cancer metastases) lack a known primary and the goal is to infer each sample's cancer tissue of origin at the cancer-cell level. The sample is normal/non-cancerous tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter instead The primary cancer type is already known — use the known_cancer_type parameter in create_summary_matrix rather than origin prediction Cells have already been QC-filtered by different thresholds (e.g. no cells with pct_mt ≥ 25 or nFeatureRNA ≤ 500 remain), making the mitochondrial/feature-count filtering step redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Predict the primary tissue of origin of cancer cells in metastatic biopsies by running scATOMIC's hierarchical random-forest pan-cancer classifier per sample and taking the majority cancer-cell annotation at the terminal cancer-type layer. Unlike CNV-based malignant-cell identification, this yields a tissue-of-origin call even for unknown primaries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Predict the primary tissue of origin of cancer cells in metastatic biopsies by running scATOMIC's hierarchical random-forest pan-cancer classifier per sample and taking the majority cancer-cell annotation at the terminal cancer-type layer. Unlike CNV-based malignant-cell identification, this yields a tissue-of-origin call even for unknown primaries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is normal/non-cancerous tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter instead The primary cancer type is already known — use the known_cancer_type parameter in create_summary_matrix rather than origin prediction Cells have already been QC-filtered by different thresholds (e.g. no cells with pct_mt ≥ 25 or nFeatureRNA ≤ 500 remain), making the mitochondrial/feature-count filtering step redundant

skills.search_text: cancer-signature-baseline-thresholding Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal training set from scRNA-seq data whose 'Malignant'/'Tumor' labels were assigned by upstream studies of variable quality, and you need to remove mislabeled cells before classifier training. The dataset contains no reliably annotated normal epithelial cells, so the normal-cell AUCell baseline cannot be computed You are annotating malignant cells de novo rather than calibrating pre-existing 'Malignant'/'Tumor' labels for training-set construction (use scMalignantFinder's predict instead) The input is ST data or a cell-type annotation task where the basic cell types have not yet been identified (the method requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Calibrates an initially annotated malignant-cell training set by scoring curated pan-cancer gene signatures (AUCell) and filtering out cells whose signature activity is inconsistent with malignancy, using normal epithelial cells as the baseline. skills.summary: Calibrates an initially annotated malignant-cell training set by scoring curated pan-cancer gene signatures (AUCell) and filtering out cells whose signature activity is inconsistent with malignancy, using normal epithelial cells as the baseline. skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no reliably annotated normal epithelial cells, so the normal-cell AUCell baseline cannot be computed You are annotating malignant cells de novo rather than calibrating pre-existing 'Malignant'/'Tumor' labels for training-set construction (use scMalignantFinder's predict instead) The input is ST data or a cell-type annotation task where the basic cell types have not yet been identified (the method requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types)

skills.description: Use when building a malignant-cell classifier's feature matrix from a multi-dataset calibrated training set: you have malignant/normal-annotated cells (e.g. adata.obs['Raw_annotation'] with 'Malignant'/'Tumor' vs 'Normal') and need union-based DEG feature selection rather than intersection.
skills.name: cancer-signature-calibrated-training-data-handling
skills.search_text: cancer-signature-calibrated-training-data-handling Use when building a malignant-cell classifier's feature matrix from a multi-dataset calibrated training set: you have malignant/normal-annotated cells (e.g. adata.obs['Raw_annotation'] with 'Malignant'/'Tumor' vs 'Normal') and need union-based DEG feature selection rather than intersection. You already have the deposited feature list (ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt from Zenodo record 17888140) and only need to run inference — reuse the pretrained model.joblib instead of re-deriving DEGs. Your goal requires genes consistently differentially expressed across ALL datasets (intersection), which contradicts the union strategy and would lose inter-tumor heterogeneity. Your data contains cells of unknown/controversial origin (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) or is not a cancerous epithelial lineage — scMalignantFinder relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Derives the 2707-gene (1656 upregulated + 1051 downregulated) malignant-vs-normal epithelial feature set by taking the union of per-dataset DEGs from the cancer-signature-calibrated training set (combine_training.h5ad), as done in scMalignantFinder. The union strategy intentionally retains inter-tumor heterogeneous markers that intersection-based feature selection would discard. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Derives the 2707-gene (1656 upregulated + 1051 downregulated) malignant-vs-normal epithelial feature set by taking the union of per-dataset DEGs from the cancer-signature-calibrated training set (combine_training.h5ad), as done in scMalignantFinder. The union strategy intentionally retains inter-tumor heterogeneous markers that intersection-based feature selection would discard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have the deposited feature list (ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt from Zenodo record 17888140) and only need to run inference — reuse the pretrained model.joblib instead of re-deriving DEGs. Your goal requires genes consistently differentially expressed across ALL datasets (intersection), which contradicts the union strategy and would lose inter-tumor heterogeneity. Your data contains cells of unknown/controversial origin (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) or is not a cancerous epithelial lineage — scMalignantFinder relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data from heterogeneous cell populations — use SIMLR's standard single-cell workflow rather than the patient-stratification framing You need supervised subtype classification using known labels — SIMLR is unsupervised and performs de novo discovery, not label-driven prediction You need to rank genes/features for the learned similarities — use SIMLR_Feature_Ranking instead of the stratification workflow

skills.search_text: candidate-k-skewness-selection Use when running GapClust on a scRNA-seq count matrix to flag rare cell clusters (e.g. the 29-cell tuft-cell R2 cluster), and you need the criterion that turns per-k gap statistics into candidate rare clusters. When the goal is to characterise major cell types rather than rare ones — the paper directs that to toolkits such as Seurat or Scater, not GapClust's gap-statistic scan. When clusters are abundant and the between-cluster gap signal is expected to be negligible — the second-order derivative score is designed for minor clusters separated from voluminous neighbours. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 GapClust's candidate-k selection step: scan candidate cluster sizes k using nearest-neighbour distances and a second-order derivative gap score, and accept a k as a rare-cluster candidate only when the skewness<k> statistic exceeds 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: GapClust's candidate-k selection step: scan candidate cluster sizes k using nearest-neighbour distances and a second-order derivative gap score, and accept a k as a rare-cluster candidate only when the skewness<k> statistic exceeds 2.

skills.summary: Reconstructs the iwa-miRNA MiRNA Selection step: two candidate-selection mechanisms — a high-throughput (HT) criteria filter and a one-class SVM classifier — are run in parallel with default parameters on the aggregated miRNA precursor candidate list, and the overlap between the two labelled sets identifies candidates supported by both mechanisms.

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell gene-gene association networks where indirect (non-direct) edges are filtered out via conditional-independence hypothesis tests, e.g. before computing NFE or CNDM-based analyses.
skills.name: ccsn-conditional-independence-network-inference
skills.search_text: ccsn-conditional-independence-network-inference Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell gene-gene association networks where indirect (non-direct) edges are filtered out via conditional-independence hypothesis tests, e.g. before computing NFE or CNDM-based analyses. The analysis goal requires causal (directional) gene regulatory networks — c-CSN is not designed for causal inference and does not orient gene associations Bulk RNA-seq or other data without per-cell resolution, since the method's core output is one direct-association network per individual cell Datasets where pairwise gene expression distributions are too sparse to estimate scatter-diagram neighborhoods reliably in 3D expression space http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for every cell in a scRNA-seq dataset by testing conditional independence of each gene pair given one or more conditional genes, so that only direct gene-gene associations are retained. This per-cell network (or its degree matrix, CNDM) can then feed clustering, dimension reduction, or network flow entropy (NFE) potency estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for every cell in a scRNA-seq dataset by testing conditional independence of each gene pair given one or more conditional genes, so that only direct gene-gene associations are retained. This per-cell network (or its degree matrix, CNDM) can then feed clustering, dimension reduction, or network flow entropy (NFE) potency estimation.

skills.name: cd8-til-state-annotation-from-reference-map
skills.search_text: cd8-til-state-annotation-from-reference-map Use when murine CD8 T cell scRNA-seq data (e.g. Smart-seq2 or 10X counts) must be assigned to reference CD8 TIL states (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naïve) prior to clonotype or state-composition analyses. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a pre-computed cell-type feature table rather than single-cell expression data — the classifier needs per-cell profiles in a SingleCellExperiment object Data are human CD8 T cells without setting the human parameter, or non-T cells dominate the sample — non-CD8 cells are classified into Treg/CD4T/NKT and must be filtered before state prediction A stable, maintained reference-mapping workflow with detection of states deviating from the reference is required — TILPRED is no longer maintained and ProjecTILs is recommended instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Annotates individual CD8 TILs from single-cell RNA-seq with one of the four B16-melanoma reference transcriptomic states — exhausted (Tex), memory-like (Tpex), effector memory-like (EM-like) and naïve — using the TILPRED logistic-regression classifier on a SingleCellExperiment object, enabling downstream clonal-overlap analyses such as Morisita-Horn TCR repertoire comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Annotates individual CD8 TILs from single-cell RNA-seq with one of the four B16-melanoma reference transcriptomic states — exhausted (Tex), memory-like (Tpex), effector memory-like (EM-like) and naïve — using the TILPRED logistic-regression classifier on a SingleCellExperiment object, enabling downstream clonal-overlap analyses such as Morisita-Horn TCR repertoire comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or a pre-computed cell-type feature table rather than single-cell expression data — the classifier needs per-cell profiles in a SingleCellExperiment object Data are human CD8 T cells without setting the human parameter, or non-T cells dominate the sample — non-CD8 cells are classified into Treg/CD4T/NKT and must be filtered before state prediction A stable, maintained reference-mapping workflow with detection of states deviating from the reference is required — TILPRED is no longer maintained and ProjecTILs is recommended instead

skills.description: Use when you have a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cell scRNA-seq profiles (mouse or human) and need to assign each cell a probability of belonging to a reference CD8 TIL state (exhausted, memory-like, naive, EM-like).
skills.name: cd8-til-state-classification
skills.search_text: cd8-til-state-classification Use when you have a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cell scRNA-seq profiles (mouse or human) and need to assign each cell a probability of belonging to a reference CD8 TIL state (exhausted, memory-like, naive, EM-like). TILPRED is explicitly no longer maintained; for new reference-based analyses of non-CD8 or multi-state data prefer its successor ProjecTILs (carmonalab/ProjecTILs) Input cells are not CD8 T lymphocytes or the goal is unbiased de novo clustering rather than mapping to the four reference CD8 TIL states (use unsupervised clustering, e.g. Seurat SNN with silhouette-based K selection) The task is TCR sequence reconstruction rather than state classification (use TraCeR for reconstructing TCR sequences from single-cell RNA-seq) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Classifies single-cell CD8 tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) profiles into four reference transcriptomic states — exhausted, memory-like, naive and effector memory-like (EM-like) — using the TILPRED multinomial logistic regression classifier, which scores each cell via AUCell-based gene-signature enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Classifies single-cell CD8 tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) profiles into four reference transcriptomic states — exhausted, memory-like, naive and effector memory-like (EM-like) — using the TILPRED multinomial logistic regression classifier, which scores each cell via AUCell-based gene-signature enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: TILPRED is explicitly no longer maintained; for new reference-based analyses of non-CD8 or multi-state data prefer its successor ProjecTILs (carmonalab/ProjecTILs) Input cells are not CD8 T lymphocytes or the goal is unbiased de novo clustering rather than mapping to the four reference CD8 TIL states (use unsupervised clustering, e.g. Seurat SNN with silhouette-based K selection) The task is TCR sequence reconstruction rather than state classification (use TraCeR for reconstructing TCR sequences from single-cell RNA-seq)

skills.description: Use when running scISR's data perturbation module on a filtered training gene-by-cell expression matrix and you must decide how many gene-subspace groups to retain before subspace regression imputation.
skills.name: cdf-difference-optimality-assessment
skills.search_text: cdf-difference-optimality-assessment Use when running scISR's data perturbation module on a filtered training gene-by-cell expression matrix and you must decide how many gene-subspace groups to retain before subspace regression imputation. The goal is clustering cells rather than grouping genes into subspaces — scISR's k-means cell clustering with the true number of cell types is a downstream evaluation step, not this skill. The goal is identifying dropout-affected zero entries — that is scISR's first module (hyper-geometric/over- and under-representation testing with significance threshold 0.01), which runs before perturbation clustering. The data have not been filtered and rescaled (log2 transformation for value ranges larger than 100), so perturbation clustering would run on genes expressed in fewer than two cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the optimal number of gene-subspace clusters k in scISR's second module by comparing connectivity matrices of the original versus Gaussian-noise-perturbed training data, and choosing the partition whose cumulative difference distribution (CDF-difference) has maximal area under the curve (AUC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Selects the optimal number of gene-subspace clusters k in scISR's second module by comparing connectivity matrices of the original versus Gaussian-noise-perturbed training data, and choosing the partition whose cumulative difference distribution (CDF-difference) has maximal area under the curve (AUC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering cells rather than grouping genes into subspaces — scISR's k-means cell clustering with the true number of cell types is a downstream evaluation step, not this skill. The goal is identifying dropout-affected zero entries — that is scISR's first module (hyper-geometric/over- and under-representation testing with significance threshold 0.01), which runs before perturbation clustering. The data have not been filtered and rescaled (log2 transformation for value ranges larger than 100), so perturbation clustering would run on genes expressed in fewer than two cells.

skills.description: Use when you have a clustered (or resolution-swept) Seurat scRNA-seq object and need per-cluster top markers ranked by the co-dependency index (CDI) to score cluster specificity or benchmark cluster configurations.
skills.name: cdi-differential-expression-marker-identification
skills.search_text: cdi-differential-expression-marker-identification Use when you have a clustered (or resolution-swept) Seurat scRNA-seq object and need per-cluster top markers ranked by the co-dependency index (CDI) to score cluster specificity or benchmark cluster configurations. Datasets with multiple biological replicates where DE methods must account for replicate variation — the CDI approach does not model this (a stated limitation) Input is raw/unprocessed counts without prior normalization, PCA, and clustering — the CDI marker call operates per-cluster on preprocessed data Artifact genes highly expressed exclusively in a small subset of cells from a single replicate are present and not filtered — they can produce spurious clusters and misleading markers Identifies binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) and the top co-dependency index (CDI) marker for each cell cluster in scRNA-seq data using scMiko's CDI-based differential expression, providing the marker specificity curves that drive resolution optimization in scPipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Identifies binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) and the top co-dependency index (CDI) marker for each cell cluster in scRNA-seq data using scMiko's CDI-based differential expression, providing the marker specificity curves that drive resolution optimization in scPipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with multiple biological replicates where DE methods must account for replicate variation — the CDI approach does not model this (a stated limitation) Input is raw/unprocessed counts without prior normalization, PCA, and clustering — the CDI marker call operates per-cluster on preprocessed data Artifact genes highly expressed exclusively in a small subset of cells from a single replicate are present and not filtered — they can produce spurious clusters and misleading markers

skills.description: Use when validating RiboSeq alignment output (length-selected BAM/BED files) to confirm that ribosome-protected fragments accumulate in coding sequences rather than untranslated regions before downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: cds-versus-utr-read-density-enrichment
skills.search_text: cds-versus-utr-read-density-enrichment Use when validating RiboSeq alignment output (length-selected BAM/BED files) to confirm that ribosome-protected fragments accumulate in coding sequences rather than untranslated regions before downstream statistical analysis. Input is not aligned, length-filtered RPF data (e.g. raw FastQ or contaminant-depleted-but-unaligned reads) — count enrichment is meaningless before mapping The goal is quantifying per-gene expression for differential analysis rather than a qualitative ribosome-activity control The annotation lacks UTR features, making the CDS-versus-UTR comparison undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A ribosome-profiling quality control that counts footprint reads overlapping annotated CDS versus UTR features (e.g. with HTSeq feature counting) and checks that footprints are overrepresented within the CDS, verifying the data correspond to active ribosome footprints. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: A ribosome-profiling quality control that counts footprint reads overlapping annotated CDS versus UTR features (e.g. with HTSeq feature counting) and checks that footprints are overrepresented within the CDS, verifying the data correspond to active ribosome footprints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not aligned, length-filtered RPF data (e.g. raw FastQ or contaminant-depleted-but-unaligned reads) — count enrichment is meaningless before mapping The goal is quantifying per-gene expression for differential analysis rather than a qualitative ribosome-activity control The annotation lacks UTR features, making the CDS-versus-UTR comparison undefined

skills.description: Use when you need to recover 2D spatial coordinates of scRNA-seq cells (or held-out ST spots) by training a supervised model on a reference ST dataset with known locations, e.g. 10x Visium mouse brain sections.
skills.name: celery-2d-location-prediction-training
skills.search_text: celery-2d-location-prediction-training Use when you need to recover 2D spatial coordinates of scRNA-seq cells (or held-out ST spots) by training a supervised model on a reference ST dataset with known locations, e.g. 10x Visium mouse brain sections. The goal is spatial domain/layer prediction rather than 2D coordinates — use the categorical spatial-domain recovery variant instead (Scanpy rank_genes_groups DE genes). Only single-cell-resolution ST data with a small gene panel is available — CeLEry was noted to be suboptimal on single-cell-resolution platforms with small gene panels. No spatial transcriptomics training data with known locations exists to learn from. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Trains a CeLEry supervised deep neural network on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data to predict 2D coordinates of held-out spots/cells in scRNA-seq, using optional VAE-based data augmentation to improve robustness against noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Trains a CeLEry supervised deep neural network on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data to predict 2D coordinates of held-out spots/cells in scRNA-seq, using optional VAE-based data augmentation to improve robustness against noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spatial domain/layer prediction rather than 2D coordinates — use the categorical spatial-domain recovery variant instead (Scanpy rank_genes_groups DE genes). Only single-cell-resolution ST data with a small gene panel is available — CeLEry was noted to be suboptimal on single-cell-resolution platforms with small gene panels. No spatial transcriptomics training data with known locations exists to learn from.

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data, especially when later-timepoint cell types may shift in composition, disappear, or emerge as novel types.
skills.name: cell-annotation-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-annotation-method-benchmarking Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data, especially when later-timepoint cell types may shift in composition, disappear, or emerge as novel types. The task is annotating a single cross-sectional timepoint with no paired t0 training data — CASi's information-borrowing design and the simulation scenarios target multi-timepoint designs The t0 and t1 datasets differ dramatically (e.g., different tissues or platforms), since the neural network would fail to borrow useful information and could not be well trained Only unsupervised clustering on one timepoint is needed without any method comparison against competing supervised annotators http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark supervised cross-timepoint single-cell RNA-seq annotation methods by simulating paired t0/t1 PBMC data under defined composition-change scenarios and comparing per-cell annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) across methods over Monte Carlo repetitions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Benchmark supervised cross-timepoint single-cell RNA-seq annotation methods by simulating paired t0/t1 PBMC data under defined composition-change scenarios and comparing per-cell annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) across methods over Monte Carlo repetitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is annotating a single cross-sectional timepoint with no paired t0 training data — CASi's information-borrowing design and the simulation scenarios target multi-timepoint designs The t0 and t1 datasets differ dramatically (e.g., different tissues or platforms), since the neural network would fail to borrow useful information and could not be well trained Only unsupervised clustering on one timepoint is needed without any method comparison against competing supervised annotators

skills.description: Use when a cell-atlas scRNA-Seq dataset carries multiple conflicting annotation columns (e.g., ICGS2, Seurat3, Monocle3, curated labels) in adata.obs and you need to quantify whether an integrated solution reproduces or refines the reference atlas clusters.
skills.name: cell-atlas-annotation-agreement-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-atlas-annotation-agreement-evaluation Use when a cell-atlas scRNA-Seq dataset carries multiple conflicting annotation columns (e.g., ICGS2, Seurat3, Monocle3, curated labels) in adata.obs and you need to quantify whether an integrated solution reproduces or refines the reference atlas clusters. The dataset has only a single clustering annotation and no reference label set to compare against — there is nothing to mix-and-match or evaluate agreement on You need a modality-specific joint embedding or geometric graph integration (e.g., Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) rather than decision-level reconciliation of existing label assignments The AnnData already holds a final, trusted curated annotation and the goal is only label transfer, not integration or agreement benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluate how well an integrated single-cell clustering solution (e.g., from scTriangulate) agrees with a curated reference cell-atlas annotation, such as the Hay et al. human bone marrow atlas, by tabulating cluster-level agreement between the mix-and-match assignment and each contributing or reference label set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Evaluate how well an integrated single-cell clustering solution (e.g., from scTriangulate) agrees with a curated reference cell-atlas annotation, such as the Hay et al. human bone marrow atlas, by tabulating cluster-level agreement between the mix-and-match assignment and each contributing or reference label set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has only a single clustering annotation and no reference label set to compare against — there is nothing to mix-and-match or evaluate agreement on You need a modality-specific joint embedding or geometric graph integration (e.g., Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) rather than decision-level reconciliation of existing label assignments The AnnData already holds a final, trusted curated annotation and the goal is only label transfer, not integration or agreement benchmarking

skills.description: Use when performing DA-testing of cell-types from scRNA-Seq/snRNA-Seq data where condition labels (age, disease stage, severity, phenotype) exist per cell and standard Louvain, Milo, or DA-seq clustering yields weakly significant composition shifts.
skills.name: cell-attribute-aware-community-detection
skills.search_text: cell-attribute-aware-community-detection Use when performing DA-testing of cell-types from scRNA-Seq/snRNA-Seq data where condition labels (age, disease stage, severity, phenotype) exist per cell and standard Louvain, Milo, or DA-seq clustering yields weakly significant composition shifts. When no per-cell biological condition attribute is available to guide clustering — EVA degenerates to standard Louvain behavior and its advantage disappears When the dataset displays strong clustering structure — the paper reports ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog was less pronounced in such studies When phenotype/sample labels are unreliable — the paper reports ELVAR is more sensitive to false positives in the clustering attribute, which can degrade community quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 ELVAR-style cell-attribute aware community detection adapts the EVA algorithm — a generalization of Louvain — to cluster cells on the single-cell state-manifold by both expression similarity and attribute similarity (e.g. age, disease stage), improving sensitivity of downstream differential abundance (DA) testing of cell-types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: ELVAR-style cell-attribute aware community detection adapts the EVA algorithm — a generalization of Louvain — to cluster cells on the single-cell state-manifold by both expression similarity and attribute similarity (e.g. age, disease stage), improving sensitivity of downstream differential abundance (DA) testing of cell-types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no per-cell biological condition attribute is available to guide clustering — EVA degenerates to standard Louvain behavior and its advantage disappears When the dataset displays strong clustering structure — the paper reports ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog was less pronounced in such studies When phenotype/sample labels are unreliable — the paper reports ELVAR is more sensitive to false positives in the clustering attribute, which can degrade community quality

skills.description: Use when paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. SNARE-seq chromatin + expression) share cell barcodes across modalities, and clusters computed on one modality (here the cell-by-peak chromatin side) must be copied to the other for DE/enrichment.
skills.name: cell-barcode-based-cross-modality-label-transfer
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-based-cross-modality-label-transfer Use when paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. SNARE-seq chromatin + expression) share cell barcodes across modalities, and clusters computed on one modality (here the cell-by-peak chromatin side) must be copied to the other for DE/enrichment. The modalities are not paired — barcodes/cell-IDs differ between datasets (e.g. independent scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq experiments); use embedding/Ingest-style label transfer instead of barcode copying. The expression data is already clustered or annotated — re-transferring chromatin-side clusters would overwrite existing labels for no gain. The input is a cell-by-topic or other reduced matrix rather than raw paired modalities — cisTopic topic discovery and peak-level clustering do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transfers cluster labels between paired single-cell modalities (e.g. SNARE ATAC/RNA from the same cells) by matching shared cell barcodes/IDs, so clusters defined on the chromatin modality annotate the expression modality. In Cellar this underpins joint kidney SNARE-seq analysis, e.g. assigning cluster 1 as Proximal Tubule Cells via SLC5A12 (p-value = 0) and the GO 'Apical Plasma Membrane' term (p value = 1e-4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Transfers cluster labels between paired single-cell modalities (e.g. SNARE ATAC/RNA from the same cells) by matching shared cell barcodes/IDs, so clusters defined on the chromatin modality annotate the expression modality. In Cellar this underpins joint kidney SNARE-seq analysis, e.g. assigning cluster 1 as Proximal Tubule Cells via SLC5A12 (p-value = 0) and the GO 'Apical Plasma Membrane' term (p value = 1e-4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modalities are not paired — barcodes/cell-IDs differ between datasets (e.g. independent scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq experiments); use embedding/Ingest-style label transfer instead of barcode copying. The expression data is already clustered or annotated — re-transferring chromatin-side clusters would overwrite existing labels for no gain. The input is a cell-by-topic or other reduced matrix rather than raw paired modalities — cisTopic topic discovery and peak-level clustering do not apply.

skills.description: Use when raw 3' droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., GemCode/10x data such as SRA SRP073767) must be turned into a cell-filtered gene-barcode UMI matrix, deciding which barcodes represent cells versus empty droplets.
skills.name: cell-barcode-calling-and-filtering
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-calling-and-filtering Use when raw 3' droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., GemCode/10x data such as SRA SRP073767) must be turned into a cell-filtered gene-barcode UMI matrix, deciding which barcodes represent cells versus empty droplets. Input is already a gene-barcode UMI matrix (counting and barcode filtering already performed); this skill operates on raw reads Data lacks droplet cell barcodes and UMIs (e.g., plate-based full-length or bulk RNA-seq), so the barcode-ranking rule and UMI filters cannot apply Earlier libraries documented with 5 nt UMI and 5 bp Read2 (Supplementary Table 1 protocol heterogeneity), where the paper's UMI-quality and read-structure assumptions differ http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts raw 3' droplet scRNA-seq reads into a cell-filtered gene-barcode UMI count matrix by applying the paper's cell-barcode calling rule (order-of-magnitude ranking vs. expected recovered cell count) plus barcode/UMI validity filters (posterior >=0.975 correction, UMI quality >10 non-homopolymer, MAPQ=255 confident mapping) via Cell Ranger. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Converts raw 3' droplet scRNA-seq reads into a cell-filtered gene-barcode UMI count matrix by applying the paper's cell-barcode calling rule (order-of-magnitude ranking vs. expected recovered cell count) plus barcode/UMI validity filters (posterior >=0.975 correction, UMI quality >10 non-homopolymer, MAPQ=255 confident mapping) via Cell Ranger.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-barcode UMI matrix (counting and barcode filtering already performed); this skill operates on raw reads Data lacks droplet cell barcodes and UMIs (e.g., plate-based full-length or bulk RNA-seq), so the barcode-ranking rule and UMI filters cannot apply Earlier libraries documented with 5 nt UMI and 5 bp Read2 (Supplementary Table 1 protocol heterogeneity), where the paper's UMI-quality and read-structure assumptions differ

skills.description: Use when reads are FASTQ/FASTA and a known sequence of interest (barcode, fusion, variant) must be located with tolerated sequencing errors, and reads must be assigned to cell barcodes for single-cell quantification or genotyping.
skills.name: cell-barcode-extraction-from-short-reads
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-extraction-from-short-reads Use when reads are FASTQ/FASTA and a known sequence of interest (barcode, fusion, variant) must be located with tolerated sequencing errors, and reads must be assigned to cell barcodes for single-cell quantification or genotyping. The target sequence can be matched exactly and raw speed on uncompressed text is the only concern — grep (1–2 min) is faster than Flexiplex (~24 min), though it cannot tolerate sequencing errors. The input is already demultiplexed/assigned (e.g. a BAM tagged with cell barcodes and UMIs from a workflow such as epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell) and no sequence search is required. Only flanking sequence is known and the barcode must be discovered de novo from long reads — this is Flexiplex's discovery mode, a different sub-task than known-sequence search in short reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Error-tolerant identification of known target sequences (cell barcodes, fusion junctions such as BCAS4-BCAS3, viral sequences such as Adenovirus E1A, or variants such as rs878887783) in FASTQ/FASTA omics reads using Flexiplex's Levenshtein-distance search, followed by tallying of cell-barcode assignments against the matched reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Error-tolerant identification of known target sequences (cell barcodes, fusion junctions such as BCAS4-BCAS3, viral sequences such as Adenovirus E1A, or variants such as rs878887783) in FASTQ/FASTA omics reads using Flexiplex's Levenshtein-distance search, followed by tallying of cell-barcode assignments against the matched reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target sequence can be matched exactly and raw speed on uncompressed text is the only concern — grep (1–2 min) is faster than Flexiplex (~24 min), though it cannot tolerate sequencing errors. The input is already demultiplexed/assigned (e.g. a BAM tagged with cell barcodes and UMIs from a workflow such as epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell) and no sequence search is required. Only flanking sequence is known and the barcode must be discovered de novo from long reads — this is Flexiplex's discovery mode, a different sub-task than known-sequence search in short reads.

skills.description: Use when processing raw 3'-end tag scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., MCA GSE108097 or HCL GSE134355) where cell barcodes/UMIs must be extracted from merged inserts and corrected against a whitelist before isoform quantification.
skills.name: cell-barcode-extraction-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-extraction-scrna-seq Use when processing raw 3'-end tag scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., MCA GSE108097 or HCL GSE134355) where cell barcodes/UMIs must be extracted from merged inserts and corrected against a whitelist before isoform quantification. Input data are 10x Genomics reads intended for de novo cleavage-site mapping — most 10x reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, so this MWS-based extraction/atlas route is inappropriate Reads have not yet been merged (e.g., raw paired-end inserts whose barcode/UMI segments only reconstruct after PEAR overlap merging) The goal is bulk RNA-seq or full-length transcript analysis where single-cell barcode/UMI recovery does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Recover and validate cell barcodes and UMIs from single-cell RNA-seq reads in the Microwell-seq (MWS) 3'UTR cleavage-site atlas workflow, so that downstream gene and 3'UTR isoform quantification with scUTRquant is attributable to annotated cell types from the Mouse Cell Atlas (MCA) and Human Cell Landscape (HCL). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Recover and validate cell barcodes and UMIs from single-cell RNA-seq reads in the Microwell-seq (MWS) 3'UTR cleavage-site atlas workflow, so that downstream gene and 3'UTR isoform quantification with scUTRquant is attributable to annotated cell types from the Mouse Cell Atlas (MCA) and Human Cell Landscape (HCL).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are 10x Genomics reads intended for de novo cleavage-site mapping — most 10x reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, so this MWS-based extraction/atlas route is inappropriate Reads have not yet been merged (e.g., raw paired-end inserts whose barcode/UMI segments only reconstruct after PEAR overlap merging) The goal is bulk RNA-seq or full-length transcript analysis where single-cell barcode/UMI recovery does not apply

skills.description: Use when raw 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ reads must have their 16 bp cell barcodes error-corrected (or discarded) prior to UMI filtering and building a gene-barcode count matrix.
skills.name: cell-barcode-posterior-error-correction
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-posterior-error-correction Use when raw 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ reads must have their 16 bp cell barcodes error-corrected (or discarded) prior to UMI filtering and building a gene-barcode count matrix. Input is already a filtered gene-cell-barcode count matrix (e.g. a matrix ready for Seurat log-transformation) — barcode correction is a pre-counting step Data were not generated on the 10x Genomics GemCode/droplet 3' counting platform, so barcode structure and error model do not apply Goal is UMI error correction or PCR-duplicate marking rather than cell-barcode error correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Corrects droplet single-cell RNA-seq cell barcodes using a Bayesian posterior-probability rule (threshold ≥0.975) from the 10x Genomics Cell Ranger pipeline, so that sequencing errors in the barcode do not inflate apparent cell counts before UMI collapse and gene-barcode matrix generation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Corrects droplet single-cell RNA-seq cell barcodes using a Bayesian posterior-probability rule (threshold ≥0.975) from the 10x Genomics Cell Ranger pipeline, so that sequencing errors in the barcode do not inflate apparent cell counts before UMI collapse and gene-barcode matrix generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered gene-cell-barcode count matrix (e.g. a matrix ready for Seurat log-transformation) — barcode correction is a pre-counting step Data were not generated on the 10x Genomics GemCode/droplet 3' counting platform, so barcode structure and error model do not apply Goal is UMI error correction or PCR-duplicate marking rather than cell-barcode error correction

skills.description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq samples (e.g. HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be tested pairwise for more shared cell barcodes than expected by chance, to flag barcode-swapping artefacts.
skills.name: cell-barcode-sharing-hypergeometric-testing
skills.search_text: cell-barcode-sharing-hypergeometric-testing Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq samples (e.g. HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be tested pairwise for more shared cell barcodes than expected by chance, to flag barcode-swapping artefacts.
