skills.name: cell-cell-distance-based-communication-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-cell-distance-based-communication-analysis Use when you have non-spatial scRNA-seq data plus a limited spatial measurement of a few genes, and need to infer cell-cell communication or the spatial distance/range of a signaling pathway (e.g. Wg ~100 µm, Dpp ~125 µm). The dataset is excessively large — the article notes 'the computation can become intractable when the dataset is excessively large' because cell-cell distance requires iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs (only landmark-based approximation is available) The signaling pathway's ligand/receptor/downstream genes are unknown — communication inference relies on known genes involved in specific signaling The question requires modeling time delays in communication (ligand diffusion time, intracellular cascade reacting time) — the approach explicitly does not consider them http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers cell-cell communications and spatial signaling ranges by first equipping non-spatial scRNA-seq cells with a spatial cell-cell distance via SpaOTsc structured optimal transport, then optimally transporting ligand-expressing sender cells to receptor-expressing receiver cells and fitting random-forest models over distance neighborhoods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Infers cell-cell communications and spatial signaling ranges by first equipping non-spatial scRNA-seq cells with a spatial cell-cell distance via SpaOTsc structured optimal transport, then optimally transporting ligand-expressing sender cells to receptor-expressing receiver cells and fitting random-forest models over distance neighborhoods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is excessively large — the article notes 'the computation can become intractable when the dataset is excessively large' because cell-cell distance requires iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs (only landmark-based approximation is available) The signaling pathway's ligand/receptor/downstream genes are unknown — communication inference relies on known genes involved in specific signaling The question requires modeling time delays in communication (ligand diffusion time, intracellular cascade reacting time) — the approach explicitly does not consider them

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted SpaOTsc transport plan γ* (n cells × m spatial positions) plus a spatial position distance matrix, and you need a pairwise spatial cell-cell distance matrix for downstream signaling or clustering analyses.
skills.name: cell-cell-distance-inference-from-transport-plan
skills.search_text: cell-cell-distance-inference-from-transport-plan Use when you have a fitted SpaOTsc transport plan γ* (n cells × m spatial positions) plus a spatial position distance matrix, and you need a pairwise spatial cell-cell distance matrix for downstream signaling or clustering analyses. Input is spatial transcriptomics data where true physical cell coordinates are already measured directly — no transport-based distance inference is needed No upstream SpaOTsc transport plan γ* exists yet; transport_plan(cost_matrix) must be run first The goal is time-resolved cell-cell communication, since SpaOTsc does not consider time delay (ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade time) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes a single-cell resolution spatial distance matrix (D_sc_hat) for scRNA-seq cells by evaluating the optimal transport distance between each cell pair's spatial probability distributions derived from the SpaOTsc transport plan γ*, using the POT-wrapped solver and a landmark approximation for tractability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Computes a single-cell resolution spatial distance matrix (D_sc_hat) for scRNA-seq cells by evaluating the optimal transport distance between each cell pair's spatial probability distributions derived from the SpaOTsc transport plan γ*, using the POT-wrapped solver and a landmark approximation for tractability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spatial transcriptomics data where true physical cell coordinates are already measured directly — no transport-based distance inference is needed No upstream SpaOTsc transport plan γ* exists yet; transport_plan(cost_matrix) must be run first The goal is time-resolved cell-cell communication, since SpaOTsc does not consider time delay (ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade time)

skills.description: Use when you have developmental series scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis) with inferred L-R pair expression-change values and need to group interactions by temporal activity to pinpoint key developmental time points.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-expression-profiling
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-expression-profiling Use when you have developmental series scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis) with inferred L-R pair expression-change values and need to group interactions by temporal activity to pinpoint key developmental time points. The data are from a single stationary condition with no time-point information, since dsCellNet's fuzzy clustering leverages developmental series dynamics The goal is only to detect individual L-R pairs in one network (use singlenet), not to profile their expression changes across development Input is already a cluster assignment or enrichment table rather than a raw interaction expression-change matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Profiles the expression dynamics of candidate ligand–receptor (L-R) pairs across developmental series time points and partitions them into soft clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, so that key time points (e.g., E12.5 in corticogenesis) and mediator interactions can be identified. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Profiles the expression dynamics of candidate ligand–receptor (L-R) pairs across developmental series time points and partitions them into soft clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, so that key time points (e.g., E12.5 in corticogenesis) and mediator interactions can be identified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are from a single stationary condition with no time-point information, since dsCellNet's fuzzy clustering leverages developmental series dynamics The goal is only to detect individual L-R pairs in one network (use singlenet), not to profile their expression changes across development Input is already a cluster assignment or enrichment table rather than a raw interaction expression-change matrix

skills.description: Use when training or benchmarking a supervised CCI inference model (e.g., DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) and per-method significant-interaction calls must be merged into a single consensus label set for classification.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-label-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-label-aggregation Use when training or benchmarking a supervised CCI inference model (e.g., DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) and per-method significant-interaction calls must be merged into a single consensus label set for classification. Only one CCI-prediction method is available, so no cross-method vote can be taken — use that method's calls directly instead The goal is unsupervised CCI discovery from a new dataset rather than training/evaluating a supervised interaction model against consensus labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs consensus ground-truth labels (significant vs non-significant) for every ligand-receptor/cell-type pair by majority-voting across multiple constituent CCI-prediction methods, enabling supervised training and cross-validated evaluation of the DeepCCI ResNet+GCN interaction model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: Constructs consensus ground-truth labels (significant vs non-significant) for every ligand-receptor/cell-type pair by majority-voting across multiple constituent CCI-prediction methods, enabling supervised training and cross-validated evaluation of the DeepCCI ResNet+GCN interaction model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one CCI-prediction method is available, so no cross-method vote can be taken — use that method's calls directly instead The goal is unsupervised CCI discovery from a new dataset rather than training/evaluating a supervised interaction model against consensus labels

skills.description: Use when validating AI-inferred single-cell data against a real-profiled ground-truth cohort: you have matched (semi-profiled vs real-profiled) single-cell datasets with shared cell-type annotations and need a quantitative fidelity metric for cell-cell interaction inference.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-network-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-network-comparison Use when validating AI-inferred single-cell data against a real-profiled ground-truth cohort: you have matched (semi-profiled vs real-profiled) single-cell datasets with shared cell-type annotations and need a quantitative fidelity metric for cell-cell interaction inference. The datasets lack a real-profiled counterpart or shared cell-type annotations, since no paired network comparison is possible The goal is single-cell inference itself rather than fidelity evaluation — use the scSemiProfiler semi-profiling or single-cell level deconvolution pipelines instead The input is bulk RNA-seq without a single-cell reference; CellChat requires single-cell-resolution data Compares inferred cell-cell ligand-receptor interaction networks between a semi-profiled (scSemiProfiler-generated) single-cell cohort and its real-profiled counterpart by running CellChat per disease-severity/tissue/condition group on both datasets and computing the Pearson correlation between interaction-strength matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Compares inferred cell-cell ligand-receptor interaction networks between a semi-profiled (scSemiProfiler-generated) single-cell cohort and its real-profiled counterpart by running CellChat per disease-severity/tissue/condition group on both datasets and computing the Pearson correlation between interaction-strength matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets lack a real-profiled counterpart or shared cell-type annotations, since no paired network comparison is possible The goal is single-cell inference itself rather than fidelity evaluation — use the scSemiProfiler semi-profiling or single-cell level deconvolution pipelines instead The input is bulk RNA-seq without a single-cell reference; CellChat requires single-cell-resolution data

skills.description: Use when bulk transcriptome + survival data have been reduced to prognostic immune marker gene pairs (IMGPs) and you need to rank cell types by favorable vs unfavorable prognostic associations via network degree.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-network-degree-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-network-degree-analysis Use when bulk transcriptome + survival data have been reduced to prognostic immune marker gene pairs (IMGPs) and you need to rank cell types by favorable vs unfavorable prognostic associations via network degree. Input lacks matched survival information or has low-quality event/time-to-event data — TimiGP requires large datasets with matched survival to identify prognostic gene pairs The goal is deconvolving absolute cell-type abundances from bulk data (e.g., CIBERSORTx/xCell-style estimation) rather than prognostic cell-cell interaction ranking Cell types of interest have very few marker genes — enrichment-based sensitivity is low and interactions are unlikely to be detected http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds a directed cell-cell interaction network from TimiGP's prognostic marker gene pairs and computes per-cell favorability (out-degree vs in-degree) scores, aggregated across 23 TCGA solid tumor types to reveal consistently favorable (B, cytotoxic) versus unfavorable (neutrophil, Th2) immune cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Builds a directed cell-cell interaction network from TimiGP's prognostic marker gene pairs and computes per-cell favorability (out-degree vs in-degree) scores, aggregated across 23 TCGA solid tumor types to reveal consistently favorable (B, cytotoxic) versus unfavorable (neutrophil, Th2) immune cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks matched survival information or has low-quality event/time-to-event data — TimiGP requires large datasets with matched survival to identify prognostic gene pairs The goal is deconvolving absolute cell-type abundances from bulk data (e.g., CIBERSORTx/xCell-style estimation) rather than prognostic cell-cell interaction ranking Cell types of interest have very few marker genes — enrichment-based sensitivity is low and interactions are unlikely to be detected

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix, cell-type labels, and time-point annotations and need to infer which ligand-receptor interactions connect which sender/receiver cell types at a given time point.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-network-inference
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-network-inference Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix, cell-type labels, and time-point annotations and need to infer which ligand-receptor interactions connect which sender/receiver cell types at a given time point. Your goal is to track dynamic interaction changes across a developmental series or compare two conditions (e.g., AD vs control) — use developcorrelation or comparednet rather than the single-time-point singlenet path. Your interaction of interest is not in dsCellNet's default L-R gene list — the article notes the default list size limits detection of some interactions (e.g., MG–Neurons), and users must supply supplementary L-R genes. You need to distinguish autocrine interactions — the article notes SingleCellSignalR cannot distinguish autocrine interactions with default parameters, and other methods' behaviors differ; verify the chosen method supports your interaction topology. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infer cell-cell communication networks from scRNA-seq by splitting ligand-receptor pairs into membrane-ligand and secreted-ligand classes, computing expression-based edge weights, and retaining only permutation-significant interactions (p < 0.05) for a single time point using the dsCellNet R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Infer cell-cell communication networks from scRNA-seq by splitting ligand-receptor pairs into membrane-ligand and secreted-ligand classes, computing expression-based edge weights, and retaining only permutation-significant interactions (p < 0.05) for a single time point using the dsCellNet R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to track dynamic interaction changes across a developmental series or compare two conditions (e.g., AD vs control) — use developcorrelation or comparednet rather than the single-time-point singlenet path. Your interaction of interest is not in dsCellNet's default L-R gene list — the article notes the default list size limits detection of some interactions (e.g., MG–Neurons), and users must supply supplementary L-R genes. You need to distinguish autocrine interactions — the article notes SingleCellSignalR cannot distinguish autocrine interactions with default parameters, and other methods' behaviors differ; verify the chosen method supports your interaction topology.

skills.description: Use when bulk transcriptomes with matched survival data (e.g., TCGA SKCM06 plus GSE validation cohorts) are available and a prognostic model must aggregate interaction-linked marker gene pairs into one risk score.
skills.name: cell-cell-interaction-risk-score-modeling
skills.search_text: cell-cell-interaction-risk-score-modeling Use when bulk transcriptomes with matched survival data (e.g., TCGA SKCM06 plus GSE validation cohorts) are available and a prognostic model must aggregate interaction-linked marker gene pairs into one risk score. The cohort lacks matched survival information — TimiGP needs a large expression dataset with survival data to identify prognostic gene pairs You need direct cell-type abundance estimation from single-cell-resolution data rather than bulk-inferred interaction/prognosis associations You only need to infer/annotate the interaction network itself (TimiGeneNetwork/TimiEnrich), not turn it into a predictive risk score http://edamontology.org/topic_0634 Builds an interpretable survival risk score (TimiRS-style) from LASSO-penalized Cox regression restricted to cell-cell-interaction-associated marker gene pairs (IMGPs), rather than single interactions, and validates stratification across independent bulk-tumor cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Builds an interpretable survival risk score (TimiRS-style) from LASSO-penalized Cox regression restricted to cell-cell-interaction-associated marker gene pairs (IMGPs), rather than single interactions, and validates stratification across independent bulk-tumor cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort lacks matched survival information — TimiGP needs a large expression dataset with survival data to identify prognostic gene pairs You need direct cell-type abundance estimation from single-cell-resolution data rather than bulk-inferred interaction/prognosis associations You only need to infer/annotate the interaction network itself (TimiGeneNetwork/TimiEnrich), not turn it into a predictive risk score

skills.description: Use when comparing cell–cell signaling between two tissue systems (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData 'ifnb') and you need to rank edges where ligand and receptor are both significantly perturbed, whether concordantly or discordantly.
skills.name: cell-cell-signaling-perturbation-scoring
skills.search_text: cell-cell-signaling-perturbation-scoring Use when comparing cell–cell signaling between two tissue systems (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData 'ifnb') and you need to rank edges where ligand and receptor are both significantly perturbed, whether concordantly or discordantly. You are analyzing a single tissue/condition rather than comparing two systems — use single-connectome functions (FilterConnectome, NetworkPlot, CircosPlot) instead Your goal is to claim actual signal transduction — strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication and requires wet-lab validation Spatial context matters — suspension-based single-cell sequencing does not preserve spatial histologic information, so candidate interactions cannot be verified for spatial proximity http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-edge 'perturbation scores' in a differential connectome — the product of the absolute log-fold changes of the ligand and receptor — to rank strongly perturbed ligand–receptor edges between two conditions (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs), regardless of the direction of change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Compute per-edge 'perturbation scores' in a differential connectome — the product of the absolute log-fold changes of the ligand and receptor — to rank strongly perturbed ligand–receptor edges between two conditions (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs), regardless of the direction of change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are analyzing a single tissue/condition rather than comparing two systems — use single-connectome functions (FilterConnectome, NetworkPlot, CircosPlot) instead Your goal is to claim actual signal transduction — strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication and requires wet-lab validation Spatial context matters — suspension-based single-cell sequencing does not preserve spatial histologic information, so candidate interactions cannot be verified for spatial proximity

skills.description: Use when two cell-level AML/tumor classification labels exist for the same barcodes (e.g., CNA-based CONICSmat clusters vs. SNV/expression-based genotype calls) and you must quantify how well one predicts the other.
skills.name: cell-classification-cross-tabulation
skills.search_text: cell-classification-cross-tabulation Use when two cell-level AML/tumor classification labels exist for the same barcodes (e.g., CNA-based CONICSmat clusters vs. SNV/expression-based genotype calls) and you must quantify how well one predicts the other. The tumor sample has no somatic copy-number alterations (e.g., normal-karyotype AML) and cannot be partitioned by CNA-based clustering, so only the SNV/expression route applies. You need per-cell calls in cells lacking matched tumor/normal eWGS to pre-discover the SNVs or CNA regions used to define the two labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cross-tabulates two independent single-cell tumor-classification schemes — a CNA-based clustering (CONICSmat, k=4 on eWGS-discovered 1p/7q CNA regions) and an SNV/expression-signature-based assignment — and computes directional concordance between them, as benchmarked in AML sample 809653. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Cross-tabulates two independent single-cell tumor-classification schemes — a CNA-based clustering (CONICSmat, k=4 on eWGS-discovered 1p/7q CNA regions) and an SNV/expression-signature-based assignment — and computes directional concordance between them, as benchmarked in AML sample 809653.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tumor sample has no somatic copy-number alterations (e.g., normal-karyotype AML) and cannot be partitioned by CNA-based clustering, so only the SNV/expression route applies. You need per-cell calls in cells lacking matched tumor/normal eWGS to pre-discover the SNVs or CNA regions used to define the two labels.

skills.description: Use when you have a processed scRNA-Seq BAM file and need to find which TEs (at locus resolution) are differentially expressed markers of specific cell clusters, e.g. cancer vs normal cell types.
skills.name: cell-cluster-marker-transposon-identification
skills.search_text: cell-cluster-marker-transposon-identification Use when you have a processed scRNA-Seq BAM file and need to find which TEs (at locus resolution) are differentially expressed markers of specific cell clusters, e.g. cancer vs normal cell types. You only need family-level TE abundance and do not care about the genomic locus — scTE's family-level metagenes may suffice Your reads are 3'-end 10X short reads and the TEs of interest are very young/recently active copies that cannot be uniquely mappable with ~100 nt reads Your expression matrix is already a final gene+TE feature table — this skill covers building that matrix, not consuming it http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies transposable element markers for cell clusters in scRNA-Seq data by building a combined gene+TE expression matrix with SoloTE (locus-level for uniquely mapped reads, family-level for multi-mappers) and running Seurat's FindAllMarkers with adjusted P-value ≤0.05 and average log2(FC) ≥1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Identifies transposable element markers for cell clusters in scRNA-Seq data by building a combined gene+TE expression matrix with SoloTE (locus-level for uniquely mapped reads, family-level for multi-mappers) and running Seurat's FindAllMarkers with adjusted P-value ≤0.05 and average log2(FC) ≥1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need family-level TE abundance and do not care about the genomic locus — scTE's family-level metagenes may suffice Your reads are 3'-end 10X short reads and the TEs of interest are very young/recently active copies that cannot be uniquely mappable with ~100 nt reads Your expression matrix is already a final gene+TE feature table — this skill covers building that matrix, not consuming it

skills.description: Use when you have simulated or labeled scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well a normalization/confounding-removal method (e.g., scPLS) preserves cluster structure via ARI.
skills.name: cell-clustering-ari-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-clustering-ari-evaluation Use when you have simulated or labeled scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well a normalization/confounding-removal method (e.g., scPLS) preserves cluster structure via ARI. The data have no known ground-truth cell-type labels, so no external clustering validation (ARI) is possible The downstream question is not clustering (the paper notes the best confounding-removal method may vary by analysis; scPLS performance was evaluated for clustering, not differential expression or lineage reconstruction) http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates clustering accuracy of confounding-corrected single-cell RNA-seq data by comparing inferred cell clusters against true labels using adjusted Rand index (ARI), as done in the scPLS scenario I sensitivity analysis across reduced control-gene set sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Evaluates clustering accuracy of confounding-corrected single-cell RNA-seq data by comparing inferred cell clusters against true labels using adjusted Rand index (ARI), as done in the scPLS scenario I sensitivity analysis across reduced control-gene set sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have no known ground-truth cell-type labels, so no external clustering validation (ARI) is possible The downstream question is not clustering (the paper notes the best confounding-removal method may vary by analysis; scPLS performance was evaluated for clustering, not differential expression or lineage reconstruction)

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result (e.g., from scSPARKL on a mixed-species sample like the Jurkat–293T mixture) must be checked against known marker genes and a ground-truth cell partition.
skills.name: cell-clustering-validation-with-marker-genes
skills.search_text: cell-clustering-validation-with-marker-genes Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result (e.g., from scSPARKL on a mixed-species sample like the Jurkat–293T mixture) must be checked against known marker genes and a ground-truth cell partition. The dataset is multi-omics (CITE-seq, scATAC-seq, scBS-seq) — no Spark-based pipelines for these exist yet in scSPARKL. You require benchmarked clustering performance against Seurat or Scanpy — the authors explicitly note no such benchmarking was performed. Input is not .csv or .parquet — the pipeline currently supports only these formats. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates Spark-based single-cell clustering output by checking species/cell-type marker gene expression (e.g., CD3D for mouse Jurkat, XIST for human 293T) and computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against the expected partition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: Validates Spark-based single-cell clustering output by checking species/cell-type marker gene expression (e.g., CD3D for mouse Jurkat, XIST for human 293T) and computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against the expected partition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is multi-omics (CITE-seq, scATAC-seq, scBS-seq) — no Spark-based pipelines for these exist yet in scSPARKL. You require benchmarked clustering performance against Seurat or Scanpy — the authors explicitly note no such benchmarking was performed. Input is not .csv or .parquet — the pipeline currently supports only these formats.

skills.description: Use when a refined GRN (adjacency matrix) must be converted into a draft Boolean Network and curated Boolean functions are available in the Cell Collective for the organism under study.
skills.name: cell-collective-database-model-retrieval
skills.search_text: cell-collective-database-model-retrieval Use when a refined GRN (adjacency matrix) must be converted into a draft Boolean Network and curated Boolean functions are available in the Cell Collective for the organism under study. The organism has no curated Boolean models in the Cell Collective database (e.g. many non-model microbes), so only generic Boolean functions will be produced and no curated rules can be transferred. The goal is a final, publication-quality Boolean Network — the article explicitly warns that BNs provided by Augusta are first drafts, not final networks. The upstream GRN has not been refined (no TFBM prediction or curated database interactions incorporated), since this conversion stage expects the refined GRN as input. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Retrieves curated Boolean models for a studied organism from the Cell Collective (CC) database and transfers their Boolean logic rules onto a refined Gene Regulatory Network to construct a draft Boolean Network exported as an SBML-qual file. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Retrieves curated Boolean models for a studied organism from the Cell Collective (CC) database and transfers their Boolean logic rules onto a refined Gene Regulatory Network to construct a draft Boolean Network exported as an SBML-qual file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has no curated Boolean models in the Cell Collective database (e.g. many non-model microbes), so only generic Boolean functions will be produced and no curated rules can be transferred. The goal is a final, publication-quality Boolean Network — the article explicitly warns that BNs provided by Augusta are first drafts, not final networks. The upstream GRN has not been refined (no TFBM prediction or curated database interactions incorporated), since this conversion stage expects the refined GRN as input.

skills.description: Use when an HVG list (e.g. from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, or M3drop on seqFISH+/Seq-Scope data) must be split into communication-related (Y) vs non-related (N) genes via GeneCards/GO labels.
skills.name: cell-communication-gene-labeling
skills.search_text: cell-communication-gene-labeling Use when an HVG list (e.g. from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, or M3drop on seqFISH+/Seq-Scope data) must be split into communication-related (Y) vs non-related (N) genes via GeneCards/GO labels. When the goal is de novo discovery of a communication-gene classification criterion — the article notes existing methods 'lack a standardized classification criterion', and this skill only applies predefined GeneCards/GO labels When gene lists already carry validated communication annotations and only need downstream MIMO network construction (start instead from the directed-graph/MIMO step) When the organism's genes have no GeneCards/GO coverage, since label extraction depends entirely on those databases http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Labels highly variable genes (HVGs) as cell-communication-related or not, by querying GeneCards/Gene Ontology for predefined labels (receptor, ligand, cell–cell adhesion, intercellular interaction) and assigning binary strong_cor values used to filter HVGs in CPPLS-MLP analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Labels highly variable genes (HVGs) as cell-communication-related or not, by querying GeneCards/Gene Ontology for predefined labels (receptor, ligand, cell–cell adhesion, intercellular interaction) and assigning binary strong_cor values used to filter HVGs in CPPLS-MLP analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo discovery of a communication-gene classification criterion — the article notes existing methods 'lack a standardized classification criterion', and this skill only applies predefined GeneCards/GO labels When gene lists already carry validated communication annotations and only need downstream MIMO network construction (start instead from the directed-graph/MIMO step) When the organism's genes have no GeneCards/GO coverage, since label extraction depends entirely on those databases

skills.description: Use when you have a CPM-normalized single-cell expression matrix plus a cell-annotation metafile and want to predict which ligand–receptor pairs mediate communication between annotated cell types.
skills.name: cell-communication-network-extraction
skills.search_text: cell-communication-network-extraction Use when you have a CPM-normalized single-cell expression matrix plus a cell-annotation metafile and want to predict which ligand–receptor pairs mediate communication between annotated cell types. You need downstream signalling consequence prediction (NicheNet, SoptSC) or spatially resolved interaction inference — NATMI is not designed for these Your ligand–receptor pairs require heteromeric complex, heterodimerization, or co-receptor modelling — NATMI does not model them You need binding kinetics or protein-level interaction evidence — predictions rely on mRNA expression and are subject to dropouts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Extract and analyze cell-to-cell communication networks from single-cell (or bulk) expression data by predicting ligand–receptor interactions between cell types using NATMI with the connectomeDB2020 (lrc2p) library of 2,293 literature-supported ligand–receptor pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Extract and analyze cell-to-cell communication networks from single-cell (or bulk) expression data by predicting ligand–receptor interactions between cell types using NATMI with the connectomeDB2020 (lrc2p) library of 2,293 literature-supported ligand–receptor pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need downstream signalling consequence prediction (NicheNet, SoptSC) or spatially resolved interaction inference — NATMI is not designed for these Your ligand–receptor pairs require heteromeric complex, heterodimerization, or co-receptor modelling — NATMI does not model them You need binding kinetics or protein-level interaction evidence — predictions rely on mRNA expression and are subject to dropouts

skills.description: Use when a single-cell atlas (e.g. Tabula Muris, ~117 cell types) has been processed with NATMI and you need organism-wide summary metrics of autocrine signalling, such as the median number of co-detected ligand–receptor pairs per cell type.
skills.name: cell-communication-statistics-summary
skills.search_text: cell-communication-statistics-summary Use when a single-cell atlas (e.g. Tabula Muris, ~117 cell types) has been processed with NATMI and you need organism-wide summary metrics of autocrine signalling, such as the median number of co-detected ligand–receptor pairs per cell type. The goal is spatially-resolved communication inference — NATMI 'has not been specifically designed for spatial data' Downstream signalling consequences or binding kinetics are required — NATMI does not predict these and has 'no estimates of the binding kinetics for each ligand–receptor pair' Ligand–receptor pairs involve heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model heteromeric complexes, heterodimerization or co-receptor requirements http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates NATMI-extracted ligand–receptor edges into summary statistics of autocrine/self-signalling potential — e.g. median co-detected connectomeDB2020 pairs per cell type and the fraction of the 2,293 curated pairs co-detected in at least one cell type — to quantify how much predicted communication occurs within individual cells rather than between them. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Aggregates NATMI-extracted ligand–receptor edges into summary statistics of autocrine/self-signalling potential — e.g. median co-detected connectomeDB2020 pairs per cell type and the fraction of the 2,293 curated pairs co-detected in at least one cell type — to quantify how much predicted communication occurs within individual cells rather than between them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spatially-resolved communication inference — NATMI 'has not been specifically designed for spatial data' Downstream signalling consequences or binding kinetics are required — NATMI does not predict these and has 'no estimates of the binding kinetics for each ligand–receptor pair' Ligand–receptor pairs involve heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model heteromeric complexes, heterodimerization or co-receptor requirements

skills.description: Decision support for detecting condition- or covariate-associated changes in cell abundance/density along a multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectory (Lamian TCD/XCD testing).
skills.name: cell-composition-differential-testing-along-pseudotime
skills.search_text: cell-composition-differential-testing-along-pseudotime Decision support for detecting condition- or covariate-associated changes in cell abundance/density along a multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectory (Lamian TCD/XCD testing). The goal is differential gene expression along pseudotime (TDE/XDE) rather than cell abundance — use lamian_test instead of cellPropTest. The data are single-sample or the question is trajectory topology/branching differences — use Lamian's trajectory inference/uncertainty or differential topology module instead. The input lacks per-sample annotation or a sample-level design matrix, so cross-sample variability cannot be modeled. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Lamian's cellPropTest workflow tests whether cell composition/density along pseudotime differs across sample covariates (TCD: overall change; XCD: covariate-dependent change) by modeling cell counts in 100 equal-length pseudotime intervals while accounting for sample-to-sample variability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Lamian's cellPropTest workflow tests whether cell composition/density along pseudotime differs across sample covariates (TCD: overall change; XCD: covariate-dependent change) by modeling cell counts in 100 equal-length pseudotime intervals while accounting for sample-to-sample variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential gene expression along pseudotime (TDE/XDE) rather than cell abundance — use lamian_test instead of cellPropTest. The data are single-sample or the question is trajectory topology/branching differences — use Lamian's trajectory inference/uncertainty or differential topology module instead. The input lacks per-sample annotation or a sample-level design matrix, so cross-sample variability cannot be modeled.

skills.description: Use when you have a set of minimum spanning trees (one per Totem/CLARA clustering, constructed with Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings and identify likely trajectory leaves and branch points.
skills.name: cell-connectivity-estimation-from-single-cell-data
skills.search_text: cell-connectivity-estimation-from-single-cell-data Use when you have a set of minimum spanning trees (one per Totem/CLARA clustering, constructed with Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings and identify likely trajectory leaves and branch points. The data contain disconnected trajectories or trajectories with cycles — Totem cannot generate these and the connectivity model assumes a tree backbone. The analysis needs correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime, requiring a manual work-around. There is only a single fixed clustering with no set of MSTs to average over, or the k-medoids clustering is unreliable (e.g. extremely rare plus extremely prevalent cell types at the same time). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes Totem's per-cell connectivity from the set of Minimum Spanning Trees built over multiple CLARA k-medoids clusterings: for each MST, per-vertex connectivity combines inverse edge weights with vertex degrees, is scaled to a maximum of 1, and the per-clustering vectors are averaged to rank clusterings and locate leaves and branch points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Computes Totem's per-cell connectivity from the set of Minimum Spanning Trees built over multiple CLARA k-medoids clusterings: for each MST, per-vertex connectivity combines inverse edge weights with vertex degrees, is scaled to a maximum of 1, and the per-clustering vectors are averaged to rank clusterings and locate leaves and branch points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data contain disconnected trajectories or trajectories with cycles — Totem cannot generate these and the connectivity model assumes a tree backbone. The analysis needs correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime, requiring a manual work-around. There is only a single fixed clustering with no set of MSTs to average over, or the k-medoids clustering is unreliable (e.g. extremely rare plus extremely prevalent cell types at the same time).

skills.description: Use when the input is a single-cell expression dataset (SingleCellExperiment) expected to follow a linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating tree trajectory, and you need to rank candidate clusterings and locate trajectory leaves and branch points without a prior clustering.
skills.name: cell-connectivity-profiling
skills.search_text: cell-connectivity-profiling Use when the input is a single-cell expression dataset (SingleCellExperiment) expected to follow a linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating tree trajectory, and you need to rank candidate clusterings and locate trajectory leaves and branch points without a prior clustering. The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The trajectory has multiple roots (converging topology) — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories without manual work-around The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types, where k-medoids may fail and manual cluster merging is required http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Profile single-cell trajectory structure by generating many k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings, building an MST for each with Slingshot, and aggregating them into per-cell connectivity scores that flag likely end points (leaves) and branch points of a tree-shaped trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Profile single-cell trajectory structure by generating many k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings, building an MST for each with Slingshot, and aggregating them into per-cell connectivity scores that flag likely end points (leaves) and branch points of a tree-shaped trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The trajectory has multiple roots (converging topology) — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories without manual work-around The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types, where k-medoids may fail and manual cluster merging is required

skills.description: Use when NATMI ExtractEdges.py output edges exist and the goal is to summarise the entire communication network to show how strongly or specifically each cell type communicates to every other cell type, identifying highly communicating cell-type pairs or communities.
skills.name: cell-connectivity-summary-edge-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-connectivity-summary-edge-aggregation Use when NATMI ExtractEdges.py output edges exist and the goal is to summarise the entire communication network to show how strongly or specifically each cell type communicates to every other cell type, identifying highly communicating cell-type pairs or communities. The goal is per-ligand-receptor edge-level analysis or delta-network comparison between conditions (use VisInteractions.py edge views or DiffEdges.py instead of summary aggregation) Spatially-resolved communication inference is required — NATMI 'has not been specifically designed for spatial data' Heteromeric ligand or receptor complexes must be modelled — 'thus we do not model them in NATMI' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Aggregate NATMI ligand-receptor-specificity edges between the same sending and receiving cell-type pairs into summary cell-connectivity edges whose weights are the sum of per-pair specificity weights, then rank the merged edges to reveal highly communicating cellular communities (e.g. in the Tabula Muris atlas). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Aggregate NATMI ligand-receptor-specificity edges between the same sending and receiving cell-type pairs into summary cell-connectivity edges whose weights are the sum of per-pair specificity weights, then rank the merged edges to reveal highly communicating cellular communities (e.g. in the Tabula Muris atlas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-ligand-receptor edge-level analysis or delta-network comparison between conditions (use VisInteractions.py edge views or DiffEdges.py instead of summary aggregation) Spatially-resolved communication inference is required — NATMI 'has not been specifically designed for spatial data' Heteromeric ligand or receptor complexes must be modelled — 'thus we do not model them in NATMI'

skills.description: Use when a Totem analysis has produced many candidate CLARA clusterings and you must automatically pick which one(s) to feed into Slingshot MST construction based on cell connectivity.
skills.name: cell-connectivity-vector-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-connectivity-vector-analysis Use when a Totem analysis has produced many candidate CLARA clusterings and you must automatically pick which one(s) to feed into Slingshot MST construction based on cell connectivity. You want to score clusterings on the low-dimensional embedding itself (e.g. the 5-dimensional LMDS output) instead of the cell-connectivity vector — Totem's criterion specifically uses the connectivity vector as the data representation. There is no set of candidate clusterings yet (CLARA clustering and min.cluster.size filtering have not been run). The target trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate such trajectories, so selecting a clustering for its tree-shaped MST is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Totem's automatic clustering-selection criterion: compute the Calinski-Harabasz (VRC) score on the one-dimensional cell-connectivity vector rather than the low-dimensional embedding, so the clustering chosen to build the Slingshot MST has cells with coherent connectivity along the tree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Totem's automatic clustering-selection criterion: compute the Calinski-Harabasz (VRC) score on the one-dimensional cell-connectivity vector rather than the low-dimensional embedding, so the clustering chosen to build the Slingshot MST has cells with coherent connectivity along the tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to score clusterings on the low-dimensional embedding itself (e.g. the 5-dimensional LMDS output) instead of the cell-connectivity vector — Totem's criterion specifically uses the connectivity vector as the data representation. There is no set of candidate clusterings yet (CLARA clustering and min.cluster.size filtering have not been run). The target trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate such trajectories, so selecting a clustering for its tree-shaped MST is out of scope.

skills.description: Use when you must show how reconstruction accuracy and sensitivity of a scGRN method depend on the number of input cells, and ground-truth regulatory edges (e.g., SERGIO-simulated 100-gene modules) are available for scoring.
skills.name: cell-count-scaling-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-count-scaling-benchmark-analysis Use when you must show how reconstruction accuracy and sensitivity of a scGRN method depend on the number of input cells, and ground-truth regulatory edges (e.g., SERGIO-simulated 100-gene modules) are available for scoring. Analyzing real scRNA-seq data with no ground-truth regulatory edges available — accuracy/recall against SERGIO truth cannot be computed The goal is detecting differential regulation between two biological conditions rather than benchmarking network construction (use the full scTenifoldNet pipeline with tensorDecomposition and manifoldAlignment instead) Input matrices are already normalized/processed rather than raw counts — scTenifoldNet requires unnormalized input for its main workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmarks GRN construction algorithms (PC regression via scTenifoldNet vs Spearman correlation, mutual information, and GENIE3) across input-cell-number settings by scoring reconstructed scGRNs against SERGIO ground-truth regulatory edges, demonstrating that PC regression yields superior accuracy (specificity) and recall (sensitivity). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Benchmarks GRN construction algorithms (PC regression via scTenifoldNet vs Spearman correlation, mutual information, and GENIE3) across input-cell-number settings by scoring reconstructed scGRNs against SERGIO ground-truth regulatory edges, demonstrating that PC regression yields superior accuracy (specificity) and recall (sensitivity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing real scRNA-seq data with no ground-truth regulatory edges available — accuracy/recall against SERGIO truth cannot be computed The goal is detecting differential regulation between two biological conditions rather than benchmarking network construction (use the full scTenifoldNet pipeline with tensorDecomposition and manifoldAlignment instead) Input matrices are already normalized/processed rather than raw counts — scTenifoldNet requires unnormalized input for its main workflow

skills.description: Use when you must quantify the runtime, memory, and clustering-performance scaling of an integration/clustering method across increasing numbers of cells and compare it with alternatives.
skills.name: cell-count-subsampling-scalability-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-count-subsampling-scalability-analysis Use when you must quantify the runtime, memory, and clustering-performance scaling of an integration/clustering method across increasing numbers of cells and compare it with alternatives. The goal is biological interpretation of learned topics/pathway associations (p-scETM, GSEA) rather than computational scalability measurement. The task is cross-dataset transfer learning (zero-shot transfer or fine-tuning to a target dataset) rather than same-data speed/accuracy benchmarking. The dataset is too small to support meaningful cell-count subsampling (e.g. Mouse Pancreas' 1886 cells alone); use it only for the CPU-vs-GPU timing arm. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks how scETM's wall-clock runtime, peak memory, and clustering accuracy (ARI) scale with cell count against competing single-cell integration methods on merged AD+MDD scRNA-seq data, plus CPU-vs-GPU timing on Mouse Pancreas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks how scETM's wall-clock runtime, peak memory, and clustering accuracy (ARI) scale with cell count against competing single-cell integration methods on merged AD+MDD scRNA-seq data, plus CPU-vs-GPU timing on Mouse Pancreas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological interpretation of learned topics/pathway associations (p-scETM, GSEA) rather than computational scalability measurement. The task is cross-dataset transfer learning (zero-shot transfer or fine-tuning to a target dataset) rather than same-data speed/accuracy benchmarking. The dataset is too small to support meaningful cell-count subsampling (e.g. Mouse Pancreas' 1886 cells alone); use it only for the CPU-vs-GPU timing arm.

skills.description: Use when a VDJ preprocessing or filtering step (e.g. setupVdjPseudobulk) has just been applied and you must quantify and report how many cells were retained versus input, as a baseline check before downstream pseudobulking or trajectory analysis.
skills.name: cell-count-summary-reporting
skills.search_text: cell-count-summary-reporting Use when a VDJ preprocessing or filtering step (e.g. setupVdjPseudobulk) has just been applied and you must quantify and report how many cells were retained versus input, as a baseline check before downstream pseudobulking or trajectory analysis. Input is a pseudobulk or feature-space object (post-vdjPseudobulk); per-cell filtering counts no longer apply The dataset has already been quality-filtered upstream, so an input-vs-retained count would double-report the same filter step Data contains no VDJ information (no paired BCR/TCR contigs), since setupVdjPseudobulk filtering is meaningless there http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Records input and retained cell counts around a filtering/preprocessing step (here, dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk on the Suo et al. fetal-immune scVDJ-seq data, 65102 -> 17308 cells) so that cell loss from non-productive or ambiguous VDJ filtering is explicitly documented and auditable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Records input and retained cell counts around a filtering/preprocessing step (here, dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk on the Suo et al. fetal-immune scVDJ-seq data, 65102 -> 17308 cells) so that cell loss from non-productive or ambiguous VDJ filtering is explicitly documented and auditable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a pseudobulk or feature-space object (post-vdjPseudobulk); per-cell filtering counts no longer apply The dataset has already been quality-filtered upstream, so an input-vs-retained count would double-report the same filter step Data contains no VDJ information (no paired BCR/TCR contigs), since setupVdjPseudobulk filtering is meaningless there

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a low-dimensional embedding of small UMI count matrices suffers from cell crowding at the latent origin, comparing vMF spherical vs Euclidean VAE latents or t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE baselines.
skills.name: cell-crowding-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-crowding-visualization Use when evaluating whether a low-dimensional embedding of small UMI count matrices suffers from cell crowding at the latent origin, comparing vMF spherical vs Euclidean VAE latents or t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE baselines. Datasets with complex multi-level batch factors (e.g. 30 patients x 3 disease statuses x 2 locations as in the IBD colon epithelial data) — that is the batch-correction use case with batch_invariant=False and n_batch=[30, 3, 2], not the crowding demo Hyperbolic trajectory embedding — use latent_dist='wn' (wrapped normal, Lorentz model / Poincaré disk), not the vMF spherical setup compared here Large datasets where crowding is not the question and the goal is reference mapping or batch-invariant embeddings of new individuals http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduces the scPhere demonstration that a hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher prior) VAE latent space resolves the cell-crowding problem that afflicts standard normal-prior (Euclidean) VAEs and tools like t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE on small scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the scPhere demonstration that a hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher prior) VAE latent space resolves the cell-crowding problem that afflicts standard normal-prior (Euclidean) VAEs and tools like t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE on small scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with complex multi-level batch factors (e.g. 30 patients x 3 disease statuses x 2 locations as in the IBD colon epithelial data) — that is the batch-correction use case with batch_invariant=False and n_batch=[30, 3, 2], not the crowding demo Hyperbolic trajectory embedding — use latent_dist='wn' (wrapped normal, Lorentz model / Poincaré disk), not the vMF spherical setup compared here Large datasets where crowding is not the question and the goal is reference mapping or batch-invariant embeddings of new individuals

skills.description: Use when flow-cytometric single-cell data from an unsynchronized, exponentially growing culture must be placed on real cell-cycle time, and no time-resolved sampling exists to calibrate pseudotime directly.
skills.name: cell-cycle-age-distribution-modeling
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-age-distribution-modeling Use when flow-cytometric single-cell data from an unsynchronized, exponentially growing culture must be placed on real cell-cycle time, and no time-resolved sampling exists to calibrate pseudotime directly. When the population is synchronized or otherwise not in exponential growth — the exponential age distribution 2*gamma*exp(-gamma*a) is only valid for unsynchronized populations When the trajectory-inference algorithm's cell order is unreliable — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order When the target real-scale distribution cannot be derived (e.g., stem cell differentiation, where cell death and division rates at every stage would need to be measured) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Models the age distribution of cells in an unsynchronized cell-cycle population as an exponential density (2*gamma*exp(-gamma*a)) and uses it as the true-scale target for MAPiT's measure-preserving transformation, mapping arbitrary pseudotime values onto real cell-cycle time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: Models the age distribution of cells in an unsynchronized cell-cycle population as an exponential density (2*gamma*exp(-gamma*a)) and uses it as the true-scale target for MAPiT's measure-preserving transformation, mapping arbitrary pseudotime values onto real cell-cycle time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the population is synchronized or otherwise not in exponential growth — the exponential age distribution 2*gamma*exp(-gamma*a) is only valid for unsynchronized populations When the trajectory-inference algorithm's cell order is unreliable — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order When the target real-scale distribution cannot be derived (e.g., stem cell differentiation, where cell death and division rates at every stage would need to be measured)

skills.description: Decision support for removing cell-cycle effects from single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices when an annotated set of cell-cycle control genes is available and downstream analyses require corrected expression.
skills.name: cell-cycle-effect-removal
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-effect-removal Decision support for removing cell-cycle effects from single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices when an annotated set of cell-cycle control genes is available and downstream analyses require corrected expression. When the goal is to infer the biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the biological factors, due to model identifiability When downstream evaluation depends on analyses other than those evaluated in the paper (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction), since performance of scPLS in other analysis settings was not evaluated When data are raw counts that require a count-based model — extending the scPLS framework to count data is left as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Removes cell-cycle confounding effects from scRNAseq data by jointly modeling a target gene matrix and an annotated cell-cycle control gene set with scPLS (partial least squares regression), and compares against scLVM, LMM, and PCA using per-gene PVE correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Removes cell-cycle confounding effects from scRNAseq data by jointly modeling a target gene matrix and an annotated cell-cycle control gene set with scPLS (partial least squares regression), and compares against scLVM, LMM, and PCA using per-gene PVE correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to infer the biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the biological factors, due to model identifiability When downstream evaluation depends on analyses other than those evaluated in the paper (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction), since performance of scPLS in other analysis settings was not evaluated When data are raw counts that require a count-based model — extending the scPLS framework to count data is left as future work

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix (log-scaled, gene-by-gene centered) shows within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by annotated cell-cycle genes that obscures clustering of cell types or substructure, and a known cell-cycle gene set can be retrieved.
skills.name: cell-cycle-effect-removal
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-effect-removal Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix (log-scaled, gene-by-gene centered) shows within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by annotated cell-cycle genes that obscures clustering of cell types or substructure, and a known cell-cycle gene set can be retrieved. When the confounder to remove is not the cell cycle — ccRemover does not remove batch effects or other technical effects, as it is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively When the cell-cycle effect influences only a small fraction of control genes (below ~8%), since it may not be captured by the leading principal components and will be missed When the analysis goal requires retaining cell-cycle state information (e.g., studying cell-cycle itself rather than removing it as a bias) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies and removes the cell-cycle effect from single-cell RNA-Seq data using ccRemover, a formal bootstrap-tested PCA-based procedure, so that downstream clustering detects true biological substructure rather than cell-cycle-driven heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Identifies and removes the cell-cycle effect from single-cell RNA-Seq data using ccRemover, a formal bootstrap-tested PCA-based procedure, so that downstream clustering detects true biological substructure rather than cell-cycle-driven heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the confounder to remove is not the cell cycle — ccRemover does not remove batch effects or other technical effects, as it is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively When the cell-cycle effect influences only a small fraction of control genes (below ~8%), since it may not be captured by the leading principal components and will be missed When the analysis goal requires retaining cell-cycle state information (e.g., studying cell-cycle itself rather than removing it as a bias)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain cell-cycle effects confounding subclone or subpopulation delineation, and the goal is to quantify which correction approach (circular vs linear) maximizes subclone separability.
skills.name: cell-cycle-effect-removal-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-effect-removal-method-benchmarking Use when scRNA-seq data contain cell-cycle effects confounding subclone or subpopulation delineation, and the goal is to quantify which correction approach (circular vs linear) maximizes subclone separability. When the goal is predicting discrete cell-cycle phases (G1/S/G2M labels) rather than removing cell-cycle effects — marker-gene scoring (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring) is the appropriate tool instead When the periodic process of interest is the analysis target (pseudo-time inference) rather than a confounder to be removed When the input data are not scRNA-seq expression matrices — the linear regression baselines and circular-manifold projection are defined on gene-by-cell expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking workflow comparing nonlinear circular cell-cycle correction (Cyclum, a sinusoidal autoencoder) against linear regression approaches (Seurat, ccRemover, PC1–5) for how well each restores subclone delineation in scRNA-seq data with perturbed cell-cycle effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow comparing nonlinear circular cell-cycle correction (Cyclum, a sinusoidal autoencoder) against linear regression approaches (Seurat, ccRemover, PC1–5) for how well each restores subclone delineation in scRNA-seq data with perturbed cell-cycle effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is predicting discrete cell-cycle phases (G1/S/G2M labels) rather than removing cell-cycle effects — marker-gene scoring (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring) is the appropriate tool instead When the periodic process of interest is the analysis target (pseudo-time inference) rather than a confounder to be removed When the input data are not scRNA-seq expression matrices — the linear regression baselines and circular-manifold projection are defined on gene-by-cell expression data

skills.description: Use when preparing a gene-by-cell expression matrix for ccRemover: gene names must be mapped to human ('human') or mouse ('mouse') cell-cycle annotations to build the if_cc indicator vector before running ccRemover.
skills.name: cell-cycle-gene-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-gene-annotation-mapping Use when preparing a gene-by-cell expression matrix for ccRemover: gene names must be mapped to human ('human') or mouse ('mouse') cell-cycle annotations to build the if_cc indicator vector before running ccRemover. The dataset's gene identifiers cannot be matched to Biomart or org.Xx.eg.db annotations (e.g. outdated or non-standard symbols), since ccRemover relies on a known set of cell-cycle genes and incomplete annotation mapping will corrupt the control-gene set The analysis goal is removal of non-cell-cycle confounders (batch, technical replicates) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and will not remove these effects No gene-name annotation at all is available (e.g. the matrix lacks gene symbols), making species-level annotation mapping impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Maps a scRNA-Seq dataset's gene identifiers to known cell-cycle annotated genes using annotation databases (Biomart, org.Mm.eg.db, org.Hs.eg.db via the gene_indexer helper), producing the if_cc boolean indicator vector that ccRemover requires to split genes into cell-cycle (XA) and control (XB) sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Maps a scRNA-Seq dataset's gene identifiers to known cell-cycle annotated genes using annotation databases (Biomart, org.Mm.eg.db, org.Hs.eg.db via the gene_indexer helper), producing the if_cc boolean indicator vector that ccRemover requires to split genes into cell-cycle (XA) and control (XB) sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset's gene identifiers cannot be matched to Biomart or org.Xx.eg.db annotations (e.g. outdated or non-standard symbols), since ccRemover relies on a known set of cell-cycle genes and incomplete annotation mapping will corrupt the control-gene set The analysis goal is removal of non-cell-cycle confounders (batch, technical replicates) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and will not remove these effects No gene-name annotation at all is available (e.g. the matrix lacks gene symbols), making species-level annotation mapping impossible

skills.description: Use when preparing DeepCycle inputs: you need an organism-specific cell-cycle gene list, a base cycling gene (Nusap1 for mESCs, MELK for human fibroblasts), and expression/filter thresholds for gene inclusion.
skills.name: cell-cycle-gene-list-curation
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-gene-list-curation Use when preparing DeepCycle inputs: you need an organism-specific cell-cycle gene list, a base cycling gene (Nusap1 for mESCs, MELK for human fibroblasts), and expression/filter thresholds for gene inclusion. No cycling genes are detected after filtering — the article warns results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed rather than further gene-list tuning The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced layers, since expression thresholds are defined on unspliced/spliced reads, not on total counts or feature tables The organism of interest has no available GO cell_cycle (GO:0007049) annotation, so the candidate gene list cannot be assembled http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Curates the candidate cycling gene list (e.g. organism-specific GOterm cell_cycle GO:0007049 annotation) and the base gene used to seed the transcriptional phase, then filters the list by average unspliced/spliced expression and the optional Hotelling filter before DeepCycle inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Curates the candidate cycling gene list (e.g. organism-specific GOterm cell_cycle GO:0007049 annotation) and the base gene used to seed the transcriptional phase, then filters the list by average unspliced/spliced expression and the optional Hotelling filter before DeepCycle inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cycling genes are detected after filtering — the article warns results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed rather than further gene-list tuning The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced layers, since expression thresholds are defined on unspliced/spliced reads, not on total counts or feature tables The organism of interest has no available GO cell_cycle (GO:0007049) annotation, so the candidate gene list cannot be assembled

skills.name: cell-cycle-gene-phase-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-gene-phase-annotation Use when single cells have been reordered along a differentiation trajectory (pseudo-temporal position) and you must cluster gene expression dynamics into temporal waves and check whether cell-cycle gene sets (mitosis vs DNA synthesis) fall into distinct, out-of-phase clusters. Cells have not been reordered along a pseudo-temporal trajectory — GAM fitting requires pseudo-temporal position along a path (e.g. from Mpath cell ordering) Genes are not differentially regulated along the target path — use only the path-specific DEG lists (Supplementary Data 2/3), not the full transcriptome The developmental system starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types or lacks FACS-sorted terminal subsets — Mpath explicitly does not yet support these cases http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotates temporal wave clusters of differentially regulated genes along pseudo-temporally ordered dendritic cell (DC) differentiation paths, specifically identifying mitosis and DNA-synthesis gene sets and verifying they occupy nearly out-of-phase waves. skills.summary: Annotates temporal wave clusters of differentially regulated genes along pseudo-temporally ordered dendritic cell (DC) differentiation paths, specifically identifying mitosis and DNA-synthesis gene sets and verifying they occupy nearly out-of-phase waves. Grounded in Mpath's GAM-based clustering on the cDC2 and cDC1 paths of mouse DC progenitor development.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have not been reordered along a pseudo-temporal trajectory — GAM fitting requires pseudo-temporal position along a path (e.g. from Mpath cell ordering) Genes are not differentially regulated along the target path — use only the path-specific DEG lists (Supplementary Data 2/3), not the full transcriptome The developmental system starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types or lacks FACS-sorted terminal subsets — Mpath explicitly does not yet support these cases

skills.name: cell-cycle-gene-regression-preprocessing
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-gene-regression-preprocessing Use when applying UniTVelo to a pancreas AnnData with spliced/unspliced counts where a known subtle fate transition (e.g., Fev+ to Delta) must be recovered both with and without cell-cycle gene regression, to match a reference fate-mapping result.
