skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a unified latent time across the whole transcriptome — UniTVelo's default Unified-time mode (FIT_OPTION='1') is the appropriate choice, not the Independent mode used here When cell-cycle phase itself is the biological signal of interest (e.g., retina development with a clear cell cycle phase), since regressing out cell-cycle genes would remove the signal under study When input is raw counts without scVelo preprocessing — gene filtering and moment computation must be performed before utv.run_model

skills.description: Use when labeled (Hoechst or equivalent) scRNA-seq or qPCR single-cell data are available and the goal is to quantify how accurately different cell-cycle characterization methods recover cell-cycle phase labels.
skills.name: cell-cycle-gene-set-factor-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-gene-set-factor-analysis Use when labeled (Hoechst or equivalent) scRNA-seq or qPCR single-cell data are available and the goal is to quantify how accurately different cell-cycle characterization methods recover cell-cycle phase labels. The data lack any ground-truth cell-cycle labels (e.g. Hoechst staining), so supervised classification accuracy cannot be computed — use pseudo-time inference alone instead. The goal is removing cell-cycle confounding effects from expression data (Cyclum's deconvolution mode) rather than benchmarking characterization accuracy. The input is already a low-dimensional factor/pseudo-time table; classification against labels can be done directly without re-fitting Cyclum. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark cell-cycle stage characterization from scRNA-seq/qPCR data by fitting Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder and gene-set/linear factor baselines (Slalom/f-scLVM, Cyclone, reCAT, Oscope, Cyclops, PCA) to Hoechst-labeled datasets, then comparing classification accuracy per method per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-cycle stage characterization from scRNA-seq/qPCR data by fitting Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder and gene-set/linear factor baselines (Slalom/f-scLVM, Cyclone, reCAT, Oscope, Cyclops, PCA) to Hoechst-labeled datasets, then comparing classification accuracy per method per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack any ground-truth cell-cycle labels (e.g. Hoechst staining), so supervised classification accuracy cannot be computed — use pseudo-time inference alone instead. The goal is removing cell-cycle confounding effects from expression data (Cyclum's deconvolution mode) rather than benchmarking characterization accuracy. The input is already a low-dimensional factor/pseudo-time table; classification against labels can be done directly without re-fitting Cyclum.

skills.description: Use when you need to show that periodic genes discovered ab initio from a circular manifold (Cyclum pseudo-time) are more enriched for GO:0007049 cell-cycle terms than genes ranked by principal components on scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: cell-cycle-geneset-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-geneset-enrichment-interpretation Use when you need to show that periodic genes discovered ab initio from a circular manifold (Cyclum pseudo-time) are more enriched for GO:0007049 cell-cycle terms than genes ranked by principal components on scRNA-seq data. The biological process is a linear trajectory rather than circular/periodic — Cyclum fits predefined circular manifolds, so pseudo-time and gene rankings are not appropriate You already have validated cell-cycle phase labels and only need to refine them along pseudo-time — use cyclum.postproc.refine_labels instead of an ab-initio ranking + GSEA comparison The analysis relies on marker-gene-based phase scoring (e.g., scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle or Seurat::CellCycleScoring) — Cyclum's methodology relies on the circular manifold instead of the marker genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify whether cell-cycle genes ranked ab initio from a circular manifold (Cyclum) better capture cell-cycle biology than linear PCA rankings, by running GSEA against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set and comparing normalized enrichment scores (Cyclum NES 1.57 vs. PC1 1.07 / PC2 1.06 on mESC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Quantify whether cell-cycle genes ranked ab initio from a circular manifold (Cyclum) better capture cell-cycle biology than linear PCA rankings, by running GSEA against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set and comparing normalized enrichment scores (Cyclum NES 1.57 vs. PC1 1.07 / PC2 1.06 on mESC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process is a linear trajectory rather than circular/periodic — Cyclum fits predefined circular manifolds, so pseudo-time and gene rankings are not appropriate You already have validated cell-cycle phase labels and only need to refine them along pseudo-time — use cyclum.postproc.refine_labels instead of an ab-initio ranking + GSEA comparison The analysis relies on marker-gene-based phase scoring (e.g., scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle or Seurat::CellCycleScoring) — Cyclum's methodology relies on the circular manifold instead of the marker genes

skills.description: Use when a velocity-informed circular trajectory (e.g., Cytopath on the U2OS SMART-Seq2 cell cycle dataset) has been inferred and G1-phase cells must be split into early vs late stages and validated with marker expression tests.
skills.name: cell-cycle-marker-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-marker-expression-analysis Use when a velocity-informed circular trajectory (e.g., Cytopath on the U2OS SMART-Seq2 cell cycle dataset) has been inferred and G1-phase cells must be split into early vs late stages and validated with marker expression tests. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference (and hence G1 partitioning) to be meaningful in that case When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath then When the analysis must rely on expression similarity alone — methods like Angle, ReCAT, and PAGA + velocity pseudotime fail to correctly model the repeating cell-cycle pattern http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Partitions G1-phase cells into early- and late-stage groups using Cytopath pseudotime from an RNA velocity-based circular trajectory, then statistically tests cell cycle marker expression between the groups. This validates that the inferred circular trajectory captures real transcriptional progression through the U2OS cell cycle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Partitions G1-phase cells into early- and late-stage groups using Cytopath pseudotime from an RNA velocity-based circular trajectory, then statistically tests cell cycle marker expression between the groups. This validates that the inferred circular trajectory captures real transcriptional progression through the U2OS cell cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference (and hence G1 partitioning) to be meaningful in that case When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath then When the analysis must rely on expression similarity alone — methods like Angle, ReCAT, and PAGA + velocity pseudotime fail to correctly model the repeating cell-cycle pattern

skills.description: Use when comparing a treated vs. control single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., 10X Chromium hESC, ~12,280 cells) to find genes whose periodic/circular expression kinetics change between conditions.
skills.name: cell-cycle-nicotine-target-nomination
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-nicotine-target-nomination Use when comparing a treated vs. control single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., 10X Chromium hESC, ~12,280 cells) to find genes whose periodic/circular expression kinetics change between conditions. The biological process is non-periodic or linear (Cyclum targets circular manifolds; use linear trajectory methods like Monocle or Wanderlust instead) You only need cell-cycle phase labels from marker genes rather than ab initio circular-pattern inference — Cyclum deliberately relies on the circular manifold, not marker genes Your data is raw unnormalized counts — the log2(x+1), centered (mean=1), scaled (variance=1) preprocessing must be applied first per the Cyclum FAQ http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Nominate condition-responsive (e.g., nicotine target) genes by fitting Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder separately to treated and control scRNA-seq data, quantifying each gene's circular-pattern magnitude per condition, and ranking genes by the treated-minus-control difference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Nominate condition-responsive (e.g., nicotine target) genes by fitting Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder separately to treated and control scRNA-seq data, quantifying each gene's circular-pattern magnitude per condition, and ranking genes by the treated-minus-control difference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process is non-periodic or linear (Cyclum targets circular manifolds; use linear trajectory methods like Monocle or Wanderlust instead) You only need cell-cycle phase labels from marker genes rather than ab initio circular-pattern inference — Cyclum deliberately relies on the circular manifold, not marker genes Your data is raw unnormalized counts — the log2(x+1), centered (mean=1), scaled (variance=1) preprocessing must be applied first per the Cyclum FAQ

skills.description: Use when h5ad data carry a continuous DeepCycle phase annotation (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) with Ms/Mu layers, and you need to quantify how per-cell RNA content (total UMIs) changes around the cell cycle or locate phase transitions.
skills.name: cell-cycle-phase-binning
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-phase-binning Use when h5ad data carry a continuous DeepCycle phase annotation (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) with Ms/Mu layers, and you need to quantify how per-cell RNA content (total UMIs) changes around the cell cycle or locate phase transitions. Input anndata lacks a continuous phase annotation (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) — run DeepCycle first (scvelo.pp.moments preprocessing, base gene Nusap1/MELK, expression threshold ~0.5–1.0) before binning. The population is not asynchronously cycling (e.g. fibroblasts that have exited the cycle into G0) — the UMI-vs-phase doubling profile is only meaningful for cells traversing G1/S/G2/M. DeepCycle found no cycling genes (shallow sequencing, few RNAs per cell) — the README states the results will not be reliable in this case, so downstream phase binning is unfounded. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Bins cells circularly by their DeepCycle transcriptional phase (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) across the full 0–2π cycle and summarizes total RNA (UMI) content per phase bin, enabling quantitative verification that RNA counts per cell approximately double (fold change ~2.0–2.1) before mitosis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Bins cells circularly by their DeepCycle transcriptional phase (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) across the full 0–2π cycle and summarizes total RNA (UMI) content per phase bin, enabling quantitative verification that RNA counts per cell approximately double (fold change ~2.0–2.1) before mitosis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input anndata lacks a continuous phase annotation (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) — run DeepCycle first (scvelo.pp.moments preprocessing, base gene Nusap1/MELK, expression threshold ~0.5–1.0) before binning. The population is not asynchronously cycling (e.g. fibroblasts that have exited the cycle into G0) — the UMI-vs-phase doubling profile is only meaningful for cells traversing G1/S/G2/M. DeepCycle found no cycling genes (shallow sequencing, few RNAs per cell) — the README states the results will not be reliable in this case, so downstream phase binning is unfounded.

skills.description: Use when a processed Seurat object or count matrix from single-cell/spatial RNA-seq needs per-cell cell cycle phase assignment (G0, G1, S, G2M), e.g. to quantify quiescent fractions alongside accordion() cell type annotation.
skills.name: cell-cycle-phase-classification
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-phase-classification Use when a processed Seurat object or count matrix from single-cell/spatial RNA-seq needs per-cell cell cycle phase assignment (G0, G1, S, G2M), e.g. to quantify quiescent fractions alongside accordion() cell type annotation. The goal is annotating cell identities rather than cell cycle staging — use accordion() with the built-in Accordion database instead The goal is scoring a custom pathway or gene signature (e.g. innate immune response via in_im_resp_sig) — use accordion_custom() instead Cell cycle genes have been regressed out or removed from the expression matrix, leaving no signal for the built-in cell cycle marker collection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assigns cell cycle phases (G0, G1, S, G2M) to single-cell or spatial omics datasets using the accordion_cellcycle() function of the cellmarkeraccordion R package and its built-in cell cycle marker collection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Assigns cell cycle phases (G0, G1, S, G2M) to single-cell or spatial omics datasets using the accordion_cellcycle() function of the cellmarkeraccordion R package and its built-in cell cycle marker collection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating cell identities rather than cell cycle staging — use accordion() with the built-in Accordion database instead The goal is scoring a custom pathway or gene signature (e.g. innate immune response via in_im_resp_sig) — use accordion_custom() instead Cell cycle genes have been regressed out or removed from the expression matrix, leaving no signal for the built-in cell cycle marker collection

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell imaging (4i) or single-cell RNA-seq data with a top-k ranked feature subset and ground-truth cell cycle phase labels, and need an accuracy-based comparison of feature selection methods.
skills.name: cell-cycle-phase-classification-svm
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-phase-classification-svm Use when you have single-cell imaging (4i) or single-cell RNA-seq data with a top-k ranked feature subset and ground-truth cell cycle phase labels, and need an accuracy-based comparison of feature selection methods. Ground-truth cell cycle phase annotations (manual gating labels) are unavailable — the classifier is supervised and needs labels_key in adata.obs for cross-validation The goal is unsupervised feature selection or trajectory inference itself rather than evaluating a ranked feature subset's phase-predictive performance Input data lacks an expression matrix of candidate features (e.g. already reduced to a feature table or non-tabular raw microscopy images) Trains support vector machine classifiers with nested 10-fold cross-validation on top-30 feature-selected subsets to predict cell cycle phase labels (G0, G1, S, G2, M) in PDAC 4i protein immunofluorescence data, serving as the classification-accuracy criterion for benchmarking feature selection methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Trains support vector machine classifiers with nested 10-fold cross-validation on top-30 feature-selected subsets to predict cell cycle phase labels (G0, G1, S, G2, M) in PDAC 4i protein immunofluorescence data, serving as the classification-accuracy criterion for benchmarking feature selection methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth cell cycle phase annotations (manual gating labels) are unavailable — the classifier is supervised and needs labels_key in adata.obs for cross-validation The goal is unsupervised feature selection or trajectory inference itself rather than evaluating a ranked feature subset's phase-predictive performance Input data lacks an expression matrix of candidate features (e.g. already reduced to a feature table or non-tabular raw microscopy images)

skills.when_to_use_negative: When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that case When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), which leads to spurious root/terminal inference and meaningless trajectory inference When the dataset is static and not expected to contain a circular/cycling component, so cell cycle phase correlation is not a meaningful validation signal

skills.search_text: cell-cycle-pseudo-time-inference Use when scRNA-seq gene expression is expected to follow a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) and you need ab initio per-cell pseudo-time or phase ordering without prior marker-gene lists. skills.summary: Infers per-cell circular pseudo-time for periodic processes such as the cell cycle from scRNA-seq data using Cyclum, a sinusoidal autoencoder that projects high-dimensional gene expression onto a circular manifold instead of relying on marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The process of interest is linear/non-periodic — existing trajectory methods (e.g., Monocle, Wanderlust) based on linear representations are designed for such data You already have trusted discrete phase labels and only need generic clustering — Cyclum's value is ab initio circular manifold fitting, not marker-gene scoring One pseudo-time value in isolation is needed for interpretation — per the paper, 'one pseudo-time for one cell itself does not make sense'; values are meaningful only as an ordered trajectory

skills.name: cell-cycle-pseudo-time-reconstruction
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-pseudo-time-reconstruction Use when given an unsynchronized scRNA-seq expression matrix (log2 TPM+1) and the goal is to recover cell cycle ordering (G1, S, G2/M) or compare pseudo-time methods such as SCUBA, Monocle, TSCAN, Wishbone, or DPT. When cells were chemically synchronized or the data are bulk (qPCR, microarray, bulk RNA-seq) rather than single-cell — reCAT targets unsynchronized scRNA-seq When the goal is to analyze differentiation or other non-cyclic trajectories — reCAT separates cell cycle analysis from differentiation, which may introduce bias When a data-driven gene selection is required — the method relies on a preselected 378-gene set rather than semi-supervised selection from the data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstruct a high-resolution cell cycle pseudo time-series from unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq data using the reCAT R package, which combines consensus-TSP ordering, Bayes/mean scoring, and HMM-based phase segmentation on cycle base genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Reconstruct a high-resolution cell cycle pseudo time-series from unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq data using the reCAT R package, which combines consensus-TSP ordering, Bayes/mean scoring, and HMM-based phase segmentation on cycle base genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cells were chemically synchronized or the data are bulk (qPCR, microarray, bulk RNA-seq) rather than single-cell — reCAT targets unsynchronized scRNA-seq When the goal is to analyze differentiation or other non-cyclic trajectories — reCAT separates cell cycle analysis from differentiation, which may introduce bias When a data-driven gene selection is required — the method relies on a preselected 378-gene set rather than semi-supervised selection from the data

skills.description: Use when evaluating an ordering/pseudo-time method for cyclic single-cell data against known stage labels (e.g., G1/S/G2/M), by sweeping cluster number k and comparing correlation-score curves between a proposed method and baselines.
skills.name: cell-cycle-pseudotime-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-pseudotime-evaluation Use when evaluating an ordering/pseudo-time method for cyclic single-cell data against known stage labels (e.g., G1/S/G2/M), by sweeping cluster number k and comparing correlation-score curves between a proposed method and baselines. The scRNA-seq data are synchronized along the cycle rather than unsynchronized — reCAT is designed to recover time-series without cell synchronization, so this benchmark is not the right setting There are no experimental cell-cycle stage labels available, since the correlation-score is defined as PCC agreement against known stage labels and cannot be computed The goal is cell-type or differentiation ordering rather than cell cycle ordering — reCAT separates cell cycle analysis from differentiation, which the authors note may introduce bias http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark a cell cycle pseudo time-series method by sweeping cluster numbers k and computing a correlation-score (PCC-based agreement between the generated time-series and experimentally determined cell-cycle stage labels), as reCAT's consensus-TSP was compared against arbitrary-insertion TSP and Oscope on mESC-SMARTer (Fig. 2c). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a cell cycle pseudo time-series method by sweeping cluster numbers k and computing a correlation-score (PCC-based agreement between the generated time-series and experimentally determined cell-cycle stage labels), as reCAT's consensus-TSP was compared against arbitrary-insertion TSP and Oscope on mESC-SMARTer (Fig. 2c).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq data are synchronized along the cycle rather than unsynchronized — reCAT is designed to recover time-series without cell synchronization, so this benchmark is not the right setting There are no experimental cell-cycle stage labels available, since the correlation-score is defined as PCC agreement against known stage labels and cannot be computed The goal is cell-type or differentiation ordering rather than cell cycle ordering — reCAT separates cell cycle analysis from differentiation, which the authors note may introduce bias

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset may contain quiescent G0-like cells that confound pseudotime reconstruction, and cell-cycle scores (e.g. reCAT mean scores) are available to identify and remove them.
skills.name: cell-cycle-score-clustering
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-score-clustering Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset may contain quiescent G0-like cells that confound pseudotime reconstruction, and cell-cycle scores (e.g. reCAT mean scores) are available to identify and remove them. The dataset contains no reCAT (or equivalent) cell-cycle scores, since kmeans_clustering and statistical_test operate on the mean score matrix Trajectory inference is planned on the full proliferative population where G0-like quiescent cells are biologically relevant and should be retained The number of expected cell-cycle states is far from the k = 5 assumption used in the redPATH NSC example http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detects G0-like quiescent cells by k-means clustering (k = 5) of reCAT mean cell-cycle scores followed by a statistical test (threshold = 0.001), so the flagged G0 cluster can be removed before pseudotime inference with redPATH. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Detects G0-like quiescent cells by k-means clustering (k = 5) of reCAT mean cell-cycle scores followed by a statistical test (threshold = 0.001), so the flagged G0 cluster can be removed before pseudotime inference with redPATH.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no reCAT (or equivalent) cell-cycle scores, since kmeans_clustering and statistical_test operate on the mean score matrix Trajectory inference is planned on the full proliferative population where G0-like quiescent cells are biologically relevant and should be retained The number of expected cell-cycle states is far from the k = 5 assumption used in the redPATH NSC example

skills.description: Use when a projected single-cell query contains predicted cycling cells (e.g. Mki67+ exhausted T cells) that need to be quantified and visualized against the projected cell-state labels.
skills.name: cell-cycle-scoring-single-cell
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-scoring-single-cell Use when a projected single-cell query contains predicted cycling cells (e.g. Mki67+ exhausted T cells) that need to be quantified and visualized against the projected cell-state labels. The query has not yet been projected onto a reference map and cell-state labels are unavailable — score cycling only after Run.ProjecTILs so scores can be attributed to subtypes The biological question concerns non-T-cell data or gamma-delta T cells, which are not represented in the ProjecTILs reference atlases Cell-cycle regression rather than visualization/interpretation of cycling states is the goal — the skill provides marker-set scoring, not batch/regression correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Score single-cell transcriptomes for cell-cycle activity using the cell.cycle.obj marker sets shipped with the ProjecTILs R package, and visualize cycling scores alongside a reference-map projection. This separates proliferating cells (e.g. Mki67+ Tex in tumor-specific CD8 TILs) from non-cycling states within the same projected query. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Score single-cell transcriptomes for cell-cycle activity using the cell.cycle.obj marker sets shipped with the ProjecTILs R package, and visualize cycling scores alongside a reference-map projection. This separates proliferating cells (e.g. Mki67+ Tex in tumor-specific CD8 TILs) from non-cycling states within the same projected query.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query has not yet been projected onto a reference map and cell-state labels are unavailable — score cycling only after Run.ProjecTILs so scores can be attributed to subtypes The biological question concerns non-T-cell data or gamma-delta T cells, which are not represented in the ProjecTILs reference atlases Cell-cycle regression rather than visualization/interpretation of cycling states is the goal — the skill provides marker-set scoring, not batch/regression correction

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate or verify that individual cell cycle marker genes cannot classify single cells into cycle stages, motivating a multi-gene, genome-wide approach such as reCAT.
skills.name: cell-cycle-stage-interpretation-of-marker-genes
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-stage-interpretation-of-marker-genes Use when you need to demonstrate or verify that individual cell cycle marker genes cannot classify single cells into cycle stages, motivating a multi-gene, genome-wide approach such as reCAT. You already have reCAT's multi-gene stage assignments and need a stage predictor rather than a demonstration that single markers are insufficient Input data are bulk RNA-seq, qPCR or microarray measurements rather than single-cell expression matrices — the insufficiency argument is specific to single-cell variability The goal is to order cells along the cycle or segment G0/G1/S/G2/M with scores; use reCAT's get_ordIndex/get_score/get_hmm_order workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A diagnostic skill from the reCAT paper showing that expression of single cell cycle marker genes (e.g., Ccne1, Pcna, Cdc6, Hjurp) overlaps strongly across G1, S and G2/M stages in mESC-SMARTer scRNA-seq data, so no single marker can determine a single cell's cycle stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: A diagnostic skill from the reCAT paper showing that expression of single cell cycle marker genes (e.g., Ccne1, Pcna, Cdc6, Hjurp) overlaps strongly across G1, S and G2/M stages in mESC-SMARTer scRNA-seq data, so no single marker can determine a single cell's cycle stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have reCAT's multi-gene stage assignments and need a stage predictor rather than a demonstration that single markers are insufficient Input data are bulk RNA-seq, qPCR or microarray measurements rather than single-cell expression matrices — the insufficiency argument is specific to single-cell variability The goal is to order cells along the cycle or segment G0/G1/S/G2/M with scores; use reCAT's get_ordIndex/get_score/get_hmm_order workflow instead

skills.description: Use when single-cell count matrices show cell-cycle-driven confounding (per-cell cell-cycle scores/phases available) that must be removed while preserving biological signal such as subclone or cell-type separability.
skills.name: cell-cycle-variation-removal
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-variation-removal Use when single-cell count matrices show cell-cycle-driven confounding (per-cell cell-cycle scores/phases available) that must be removed while preserving biological signal such as subclone or cell-type separability. When the goal is batch-effect correction or sample integration rather than removing a biological signal like cell cycle — integration methods (bbknn, Harmony, scVI) operate on joint latent representations instead When no prior knowledge of the signal to filter exists — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal When downstream analysis requires properly log-transformed expression, since SiFT-corrected data is no longer properly log-transformed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Removes cell-cycle-driven unwanted variation from single-cell RNA-seq data by projecting expression onto a cell-cycle signal via a cell-cell similarity kernel (SiFT) and deducting the projection, benchmarked against dedicated cell-cycle removal baselines such as Seurat regression, ccRemover, and Cyclum. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Removes cell-cycle-driven unwanted variation from single-cell RNA-seq data by projecting expression onto a cell-cycle signal via a cell-cell similarity kernel (SiFT) and deducting the projection, benchmarked against dedicated cell-cycle removal baselines such as Seurat regression, ccRemover, and Cyclum.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch-effect correction or sample integration rather than removing a biological signal like cell cycle — integration methods (bbknn, Harmony, scVI) operate on joint latent representations instead When no prior knowledge of the signal to filter exists — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal When downstream analysis requires properly log-transformed expression, since SiFT-corrected data is no longer properly log-transformed

skills.description: Use when evaluating scRNA-seq embeddings for trajectory inference suitability and you need a quantitative cell-density metric: cells should be well-distributed (neither over-clumped nor over-dispersed) in the 2D embedding before fitting pseudotime.
skills.name: cell-density-convex-hull-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-density-convex-hull-coverage-quantification Use when evaluating scRNA-seq embeddings for trajectory inference suitability and you need a quantitative cell-density metric: cells should be well-distributed (neither over-clumped nor over-dispersed) in the 2D embedding before fitting pseudotime. The analysis does not rely on a two-dimensional embedding — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations The embedding has newly disconnected cell clusters — such embeddings are classified immediately as not recommended and excluded from scoring before density evaluation The goal is to evaluate RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction methods — this support is not yet implemented in Escort http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantify cell density in a two-dimensional embedding as the ratio of the alpha-convex hull area (cell coverage area) to the minimum enclosing circle of the cells, using Escort's GOFeval. This coverage-area metric feeds Escort's calcScore, with 0.53 as the scaling cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Quantify cell density in a two-dimensional embedding as the ratio of the alpha-convex hull area (cell coverage area) to the minimum enclosing circle of the cells, using Escort's GOFeval. This coverage-area metric feeds Escort's calcScore, with 0.53 as the scaling cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis does not rely on a two-dimensional embedding — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations The embedding has newly disconnected cell clusters — such embeddings are classified immediately as not recommended and excluded from scoring before density evaluation The goal is to evaluate RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction methods — this support is not yet implemented in Escort

skills.description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq/CyTOF object has been embedded with t-SNE or UMAP and you need to quantify which cell embeddings are dubious vs trustworthy, or to pick hyperparameters (perplexity, min.dist, n.neighbors) by minimizing dubious embeddings.
skills.name: cell-embedding-reliability-classification
skills.search_text: cell-embedding-reliability-classification Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq/CyTOF object has been embedded with t-SNE or UMAP and you need to quantify which cell embeddings are dubious vs trustworthy, or to pick hyperparameters (perplexity, min.dist, n.neighbors) by minimizing dubious embeddings. You need embeddings that guarantee preservation of distances between distant cell clusters — scDEED flags dubious embeddings but cannot guarantee distance preservation across clusters You only need embedding stability assessment, not fidelity to pre-embedding distances — DynamicViz-style stability methods apply, whereas scDEED 'cannot decide if cell embeddings are dubious based on pre-embedding cell distances' alternative is the wrong frame here The dimensionality reduction is neither t-SNE nor UMAP and you are unwilling to adapt the package's reduction hooks http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classify each cell's 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) as dubious, trustworthy, or intermediate using scDEED, which scores reliability by comparing the cell's 2D-embedding neighbors to its pre-embedding (e.g., PCA) neighbors against a permutation null. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Classify each cell's 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) as dubious, trustworthy, or intermediate using scDEED, which scores reliability by comparing the cell's 2D-embedding neighbors to its pre-embedding (e.g., PCA) neighbors against a permutation null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need embeddings that guarantee preservation of distances between distant cell clusters — scDEED flags dubious embeddings but cannot guarantee distance preservation across clusters You only need embedding stability assessment, not fidelity to pre-embedding distances — DynamicViz-style stability methods apply, whereas scDEED 'cannot decide if cell embeddings are dubious based on pre-embedding cell distances' alternative is the wrong frame here The dimensionality reduction is neither t-SNE nor UMAP and you are unwilling to adapt the package's reduction hooks

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells from perturbed (e.g. knockout GMP) populations must be allocated to branches of an already-inferred wild-type branching trajectory to measure fate bias between, e.g., monocyte and granulocyte branches.
skills.name: cell-fate-branch-allocation-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-fate-branch-allocation-quantification Use when scRNA-seq cells from perturbed (e.g. knockout GMP) populations must be allocated to branches of an already-inferred wild-type branching trajectory to measure fate bias between, e.g., monocyte and granulocyte branches. When the new cells have totally different fates compared to the ones present in the reference structure — the mapping procedure may not be optimal in this case When the reference trajectory itself must be inferred or updated (this skill requires a fixed, precomputed STREAM graph); use the full STREAM trajectory inference workflow instead When the underlying topology is cyclic or disconnected — STREAM does not yet properly describe these more general structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how genetically perturbed cells are diverted among the branches of a fixed reference trajectory by projecting them, without re-fitting, onto a precomputed STREAM elastic principal graph and tabulating per-genotype branch fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Quantifies how genetically perturbed cells are diverted among the branches of a fixed reference trajectory by projecting them, without re-fitting, onto a precomputed STREAM elastic principal graph and tabulating per-genotype branch fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the new cells have totally different fates compared to the ones present in the reference structure — the mapping procedure may not be optimal in this case When the reference trajectory itself must be inferred or updated (this skill requires a fixed, precomputed STREAM graph); use the full STREAM trajectory inference workflow instead When the underlying topology is cyclic or disconnected — STREAM does not yet properly describe these more general structures

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-cell rwTPM and DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins, coarse-grained P_ij, soft membership rho*(x)) from MuTrans and need to visualize the manifold, place attractor basins and saddle/transition cells on it, or sanity-check basin structure before lineage (MPPT) or.
skills.name: cell-fate-dynamical-manifold-construction
skills.search_text: cell-fate-dynamical-manifold-construction Use when you have a cell-cell rwTPM and DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins, coarse-grained P_ij, soft membership rho*(x)) from MuTrans and need to visualize the manifold, place attractor basins and saddle/transition cells on it, or sanity-check basin structure before lineage (MPPT) or. Dataset has too few cells (myelopoiesis-scale) for high-resolution transition-cell identification — the paper states special care is needed there before trusting the manifold. Non-stationary dynamics dominated by cell cycle or proliferation effects, which the current MuTrans method does not consider. You only need a static clustering (SC3/SIMLR-style) rather than attractor-basin structure and transition paths — high-accuracy clustering enforces distinct states and loses transient cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Construct and visualize the MuTrans cell-fate dynamical manifold: a Gaussian-mixture landscape fit with attractor centers Yk and per-cell embedding xi(x) in which stable cells reside in attractor basins (E/M/hybrid, Pro-B/Pre-B, etc.) and transition cells are assigned along transition paths between basins. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Construct and visualize the MuTrans cell-fate dynamical manifold: a Gaussian-mixture landscape fit with attractor centers Yk and per-cell embedding xi(x) in which stable cells reside in attractor basins (E/M/hybrid, Pro-B/Pre-B, etc.) and transition cells are assigned along transition paths between basins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset has too few cells (myelopoiesis-scale) for high-resolution transition-cell identification — the paper states special care is needed there before trusting the manifold. Non-stationary dynamics dominated by cell cycle or proliferation effects, which the current MuTrans method does not consider. You only need a static clustering (SC3/SIMLR-style) rather than attractor-basin structure and transition paths — high-accuracy clustering enforces distinct states and loses transient cells.

skills.description: Use when you have simulated single-cell trajectories from a PRESCIENT perturbation run (e.g., TF overexpression/knockdown sweeps) and need to measure how perturbation magnitude shifts fate fractions at the terminal time point, with statistical testing of reciprocal fate changes.
skills.name: cell-fate-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-fate-fraction-quantification Use when you have simulated single-cell trajectories from a PRESCIENT perturbation run (e.g., TF overexpression/knockdown sweeps) and need to measure how perturbation magnitude shifts fate fractions at the terminal time point, with statistical testing of reciprocal fate changes. When association of a gene with a specific fate should be interpreted as causal evidence — the article warns that association does not necessarily imply causality When the analysis goal is trajectory shape or dynamics rather than terminal fate composition (e.g., interpolation of held-out timepoints) When perturbing non-TF targets such as signaling pathway effectors without confirming the model supports them — the paper's perturbation validation was limited to TFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify the fraction of simulated cells assigned to each terminal cell fate (e.g., endocrine vs. exocrine, neutrophil vs. monocyte) at the final time point of PRESCIENT perturbation trajectories, enabling magnitude-dependent assessment of in silico TF perturbation effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Quantify the fraction of simulated cells assigned to each terminal cell fate (e.g., endocrine vs. exocrine, neutrophil vs. monocyte) at the final time point of PRESCIENT perturbation trajectories, enabling magnitude-dependent assessment of in silico TF perturbation effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When association of a gene with a specific fate should be interpreted as causal evidence — the article warns that association does not necessarily imply causality When the analysis goal is trajectory shape or dynamics rather than terminal fate composition (e.g., interpolation of held-out timepoints) When perturbing non-TF targets such as signaling pathway effectors without confirming the model supports them — the paper's perturbation validation was limited to TFs

skills.description: Use when you have GEMLI-predicted lineage assignments plus cell type annotations (e.g., DCIS vs inv_tumor cells from GSE148093 breast cancer biopsies) and need to separate symmetric from asymmetric (mixed-fate) lineages and profile DEGs per fate class.
skills.name: cell-fate-lineage-classification
skills.search_text: cell-fate-lineage-classification Use when you have GEMLI-predicted lineage assignments plus cell type annotations (e.g., DCIS vs inv_tumor cells from GSE148093 breast cancer biopsies) and need to separate symmetric from asymmetric (mixed-fate) lineages and profile DEGs per fate class. The cell population contains only distantly related cells — the article states GEMLI 'will generally perform less robustly' in such populations, so lineage-based fate classification is unreliable The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months — GEMLI's scope is limited to lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions No predicted lineage table or cell type annotation exists yet (e.g., raw count matrix without running predict_lineages and prediction_to_lineage_information first) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classifies GEMLI-predicted lineages from scRNA-seq data into symmetric versus asymmetric cell fates based on cell type composition, then calls differential expression between the fate classes (e.g., DCIS cells in symmetric vs. asymmetric lineages in human breast cancer). This turns lineage predictions into biological insight about recent cell fate switches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Classifies GEMLI-predicted lineages from scRNA-seq data into symmetric versus asymmetric cell fates based on cell type composition, then calls differential expression between the fate classes (e.g., DCIS cells in symmetric vs. asymmetric lineages in human breast cancer). This turns lineage predictions into biological insight about recent cell fate switches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell population contains only distantly related cells — the article states GEMLI 'will generally perform less robustly' in such populations, so lineage-based fate classification is unreliable The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months — GEMLI's scope is limited to lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions No predicted lineage table or cell type annotation exists yet (e.g., raw count matrix without running predict_lineages and prediction_to_lineage_information first)

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq task asks to transfer continuous (non-discrete) annotations such as 7-dimensional cell fate probability vectors between two sequencing runs of the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset, and to rank annotation-transfer methods by JSD.
skills.name: cell-fate-probability-inference
skills.search_text: cell-fate-probability-inference Use when a scRNA-seq task asks to transfer continuous (non-discrete) annotations such as 7-dimensional cell fate probability vectors between two sequencing runs of the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset, and to rank annotation-transfer methods by JSD. The annotation of interest is a discrete cell type label rather than a continuous fate probability distribution — the Cell BLAST ontology-based curation path (BLAST2CO confidence threshold 0.5) targets discrete Cell Ontology terms instead The reference dataset has fewer than ~1000 cells, where the over-parameterized DIRECTi/Cell BLAST neural network is under-trained The goal is mega-scale dataset integration rather than cross-run annotation transfer — over-correcting batches with highly skewed cell-type composition becomes a risk Transfer continuous cell fate probabilities across experimental batches of the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset by treating one sequencing run as reference and the other as query with Cell BLAST, then benchmark accuracy via Jensen–Shannon divergence against scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchors, and scANVI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Transfer continuous cell fate probabilities across experimental batches of the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset by treating one sequencing run as reference and the other as query with Cell BLAST, then benchmark accuracy via Jensen–Shannon divergence against scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchors, and scANVI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation of interest is a discrete cell type label rather than a continuous fate probability distribution — the Cell BLAST ontology-based curation path (BLAST2CO confidence threshold 0.5) targets discrete Cell Ontology terms instead The reference dataset has fewer than ~1000 cells, where the over-parameterized DIRECTi/Cell BLAST neural network is under-trained The goal is mega-scale dataset integration rather than cross-run annotation transfer — over-correcting batches with highly skewed cell-type composition becomes a risk

skills.description: Use when RNA velocity (scvelo spliced/unspliced AnnData) plus Cytopath consensus trajectory steps are available and you need per-cell alignment scores, trajectory assignments, pseudotime, fate probabilities, or differentiation potential per cell.
skills.name: cell-fate-probability-normalization
skills.search_text: cell-fate-probability-normalization Use when RNA velocity (scvelo spliced/unspliced AnnData) plus Cytopath consensus trajectory steps are available and you need per-cell alignment scores, trajectory assignments, pseudotime, fate probabilities, or differentiation potential per cell. When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference (and hence fate scoring) with Cytopath in that setting When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is known to be faulty or based on genes violating scvelo assumptions (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), as spurious endpoints propagate into fate scores Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers or velocity estimates, so static/velocity alignment scores cannot be computed Scores each cell against consensus trajectory steps from Cytopath's simulated, dynamic-time-warping-aligned trajectory ensemble using a velocity-weighted alignment score, then normalizes per-cell scores into fate probabilities that sum to 1 across trajectories. The normalized fate vector additionally yields per-trajectory pseudotime and Shannon-entropy-based differentiation potential. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Scores each cell against consensus trajectory steps from Cytopath's simulated, dynamic-time-warping-aligned trajectory ensemble using a velocity-weighted alignment score, then normalizes per-cell scores into fate probabilities that sum to 1 across trajectories. The normalized fate vector additionally yields per-trajectory pseudotime and Shannon-entropy-based differentiation potential.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference (and hence fate scoring) with Cytopath in that setting When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is known to be faulty or based on genes violating scvelo assumptions (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), as spurious endpoints propagate into fate scores Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers or velocity estimates, so static/velocity alignment scores cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field are available and you need per-cell probabilities of reaching defined terminal fates (e.g., alpha, beta, epsilon) plus aggregate end-fate frequencies from stochastic Markov sampling.
skills.name: cell-fate-probability-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-fate-probability-quantification Use when scRNA-seq data with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field are available and you need per-cell probabilities of reaching defined terminal fates (e.g., alpha, beta, epsilon) plus aggregate end-fate frequencies from stochastic Markov sampling. RNA velocity profiles are not robust and prior biological knowledge for a differentiation potential is unavailable (e.g., cancer studies), since FateCompass depends on one of these two inputs to direct the Markov chain The goal is to infer lineage-specific transcription factor activities rather than fate probabilities — the tf_activities.m and differential_motif_activity_analysis.m steps serve that purpose instead Input data lacks cluster/terminal-state annotations or has not undergone Scanpy-based preprocessing and scVelo velocity estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies end-state probabilities of cell-fate decisions by running stochastic simulations of a discrete Markov chain whose edges are directed by RNA velocity (or differentiation potential), as implemented in FateCompass. Applied to scRNA-seq differentiation systems such as the E15.5 mouse pancreas to obtain per-cell fate probabilities and aggregate end-fate frequencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Quantifies end-state probabilities of cell-fate decisions by running stochastic simulations of a discrete Markov chain whose edges are directed by RNA velocity (or differentiation potential), as implemented in FateCompass. Applied to scRNA-seq differentiation systems such as the E15.5 mouse pancreas to obtain per-cell fate probabilities and aggregate end-fate frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: RNA velocity profiles are not robust and prior biological knowledge for a differentiation potential is unavailable (e.g., cancer studies), since FateCompass depends on one of these two inputs to direct the Markov chain The goal is to infer lineage-specific transcription factor activities rather than fate probabilities — the tf_activities.m and differential_motif_activity_analysis.m steps serve that purpose instead Input data lacks cluster/terminal-state annotations or has not undergone Scanpy-based preprocessing and scVelo velocity estimation

skills.description: Use when simulating cell-fate decisions from a preprocessed pancreatic endocrine AnnData with cluster annotations and differentiation potentials, and RNA velocity is unreliable, so trajectories must be biased by the differentiation-potential gradient toward terminal fates.
skills.name: cell-fate-probability-validation-pancreatic-endocrine
skills.search_text: cell-fate-probability-validation-pancreatic-endocrine Use when simulating cell-fate decisions from a preprocessed pancreatic endocrine AnnData with cluster annotations and differentiation potentials, and RNA velocity is unreliable, so trajectories must be biased by the differentiation-potential gradient toward terminal fates. When RNA velocity profiles are robust for the dataset — FateCompass uses them to direct the edges of the Markov chain instead of differentiation potential When prior biological knowledge defining progenitor sources and terminal fate sinks is unavailable (e.g., cancer studies), since the differentiation-potential mode depends on such input When the data are not a pre-processed AnnData with at least cell-type 'clusters' annotations plus a TF binding-site matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs the FateCompass differentiation-potential-energy transition kernel for the discrete Markov chain in the human in vitro pancreatic β-cell differentiation (Veres) dataset, propagating stochastic trajectories biased by the differentiation-potential gradient to obtain fate probabilities for SC-α, SC-β, and SC-EC terminal fates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Reconstructs the FateCompass differentiation-potential-energy transition kernel for the discrete Markov chain in the human in vitro pancreatic β-cell differentiation (Veres) dataset, propagating stochastic trajectories biased by the differentiation-potential gradient to obtain fate probabilities for SC-α, SC-β, and SC-EC terminal fates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When RNA velocity profiles are robust for the dataset — FateCompass uses them to direct the edges of the Markov chain instead of differentiation potential When prior biological knowledge defining progenitor sources and terminal fate sinks is unavailable (e.g., cancer studies), since the differentiation-potential mode depends on such input When the data are not a pre-processed AnnData with at least cell-type 'clusters' annotations plus a TF binding-site matrix

skills.description: Use when a single-cell trajectory dataset may harbor elusive or low-population terminal fates (e.g., multifurcating, cyclic, or disconnected topologies) and you need automated terminal-state calling plus a quantitative fate-recovery score against known labels.
skills.name: cell-fate-terminal-state-detection-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-fate-terminal-state-detection-evaluation Use when a single-cell trajectory dataset may harbor elusive or low-population terminal fates (e.g., multifurcating, cyclic, or disconnected topologies) and you need automated terminal-state calling plus a quantitative fate-recovery score against known labels. When the goal is only a static cell-type clustering with no trajectory, root, or fate structure — PARC alone or standard clustering suffices When no root/early cell can be proposed and no gold-standard or time-series labels exist, since terminal-state calling depends on pseudotime orientation from a root When the input is a feature/abundance table or bulk data rather than single-cell-level observations, which the cluster-graph random-walk framework requires Detect terminal cell states and rare terminal fates with VIA's lazy-teleporting random-walk lineage inference, and evaluate fate detection against a gold standard using dynverse F1 cell-fate (and branch) metrics. This addresses the documented low sensitivity of Palantir, PAGA, Slingshot, STREAM, and Monocle3 to less populous cell fates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Detect terminal cell states and rare terminal fates with VIA's lazy-teleporting random-walk lineage inference, and evaluate fate detection against a gold standard using dynverse F1 cell-fate (and branch) metrics. This addresses the documented low sensitivity of Palantir, PAGA, Slingshot, STREAM, and Monocle3 to less populous cell fates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only a static cell-type clustering with no trajectory, root, or fate structure — PARC alone or standard clustering suffices When no root/early cell can be proposed and no gold-standard or time-series labels exist, since terminal-state calling depends on pseudotime orientation from a root When the input is a feature/abundance table or bulk data rather than single-cell-level observations, which the cluster-graph random-walk framework requires

skills.description: Use when evaluating RNA velocity or latent-trajectory outputs on a multi-lineage, multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., mouse gastrulation AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers) and you need quantitative transition, batch-mixing, and velocity-consistency scores.
skills.name: cell-fate-transition-scoring
skills.search_text: cell-fate-transition-scoring Use when evaluating RNA velocity or latent-trajectory outputs on a multi-lineage, multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., mouse gastrulation AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers) and you need quantitative transition, batch-mixing, and velocity-consistency scores. The dataset has sparse cell clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, where LatentVelo-inferred trajectories do not start from expected initial states Trajectories must originate from a known, disconnected initial cluster (e.g., dentate gyrus microglia), since LatentVelo assumes a single initial latent state reachable by continuous trajectories Only standard scVI/scANVI latent embeddings without gene expression dynamics are needed — the article shows dynamics-aware embeddings outperform these for batch correction of velocities http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score inferred single-cell fate transitions by computing cross-boundary direction (CBDir) transition scores on RNA-velocity graphs, alongside batch-mixing (kBET) and nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity, to validate that LatentVelo-derived trajectories reproduce known lineage transitions in multi-lineage datasets such as mouse gastrulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Score inferred single-cell fate transitions by computing cross-boundary direction (CBDir) transition scores on RNA-velocity graphs, alongside batch-mixing (kBET) and nearest-neighbor velocity cosine similarity, to validate that LatentVelo-derived trajectories reproduce known lineage transitions in multi-lineage datasets such as mouse gastrulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has sparse cell clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, where LatentVelo-inferred trajectories do not start from expected initial states Trajectories must originate from a known, disconnected initial cluster (e.g., dentate gyrus microglia), since LatentVelo assumes a single initial latent state reachable by continuous trajectories Only standard scVI/scANVI latent embeddings without gene expression dynamics are needed — the article shows dynamics-aware embeddings outperform these for batch correction of velocities

skills.description: Use when a significant directed cell-cell interaction network (e.g., cytotoxic cells → tumor cells) has already been inferred from bulk expression plus survival data with TimiGP and you need per-cell favorable/unfavorable prognostic rankings.
skills.name: cell-favorability-score-computation
skills.search_text: cell-favorability-score-computation Use when a significant directed cell-cell interaction network (e.g., cytotoxic cells → tumor cells) has already been inferred from bulk expression plus survival data with TimiGP and you need per-cell favorable/unfavorable prognostic rankings. The cohort lacks matched survival information or is too small/few events to power the univariate Cox selection of prognostic marker pairs Cell types of interest have very few marker genes, since interaction detection is enrichment-based and such cell types are less likely to yield significant edges The input is already a per-cell abundance/feature table (e.g., CIBERSORTx/xCell output) rather than bulk expression amenable to marker-pair scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-cell favorability scores from a TimiGP-derived directed cell-cell interaction network using TimiFS: an out-degree-based favorable score and an in-degree-based unfavorable score, each normalized across all cell types and scaled by 100. This ranks immune cells by their prognostic impact in the tumor immune microenvironment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Computes per-cell favorability scores from a TimiGP-derived directed cell-cell interaction network using TimiFS: an out-degree-based favorable score and an in-degree-based unfavorable score, each normalized across all cell types and scaled by 100. This ranks immune cells by their prognostic impact in the tumor immune microenvironment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort lacks matched survival information or is too small/few events to power the univariate Cox selection of prognostic marker pairs Cell types of interest have very few marker genes, since interaction detection is enrichment-based and such cell types are less likely to yield significant edges The input is already a per-cell abundance/feature table (e.g., CIBERSORTx/xCell output) rather than bulk expression amenable to marker-pair scoring

skills.description: Use when a BIDCell segmentation mask (pixel values = cell IDs, *_connected.tif) must be converted into a per-cell transcript count matrix (expr_mat.csv) from a transcripts file such as Xenium's transcripts.csv.gz.
skills.name: cell-gene-matrix-extraction-from-segmentation-mask
skills.search_text: cell-gene-matrix-extraction-from-segmentation-mask Use when a BIDCell segmentation mask (pixel values = cell IDs, *_connected.tif) must be converted into a per-cell transcript count matrix (expr_mat.csv) from a transcripts file such as Xenium's transcripts.csv.gz. No segmentation mask exists yet — the matrix can only be built after model.preprocess(), model.train(), and model.predict() have produced the *_connected.tif mask. Transcript data must be assigned without an image-based mask (e.g. segmentation-free, transcript-based approaches such as Baysor), since this skill depends on pixel-level cell IDs. Nuclei images are separated into fields of view (e.g. CosMx) and have not yet been merged with model.stitch_nuclei(), so the mask does not cover the full tissue. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Builds a cell × gene expression matrix by assigning quality-filtered spatial transcripts (e.g. Xenium transcripts.csv.gz) to cells in a BIDCell segmentation mask (_connected.tif, whose pixel values are cell IDs), producing expr_mat.csv for downstream single-cell spatial analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Builds a cell × gene expression matrix by assigning quality-filtered spatial transcripts (e.g. Xenium transcripts.csv.gz) to cells in a BIDCell segmentation mask (_connected.tif, whose pixel values are cell IDs), producing expr_mat.csv for downstream single-cell spatial analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No segmentation mask exists yet — the matrix can only be built after model.preprocess(), model.train(), and model.predict() have produced the *_connected.tif mask. Transcript data must be assigned without an image-based mask (e.g. segmentation-free, transcript-based approaches such as Baysor), since this skill depends on pixel-level cell IDs. Nuclei images are separated into fields of view (e.g. CosMx) and have not yet been merged with model.stitch_nuclei(), so the mask does not cover the full tissue.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix must be embedded in a latent space that preserves inter-cell topological/trajectory structure, not just per-cell features — e.g. clustering and trajectory inference where inter-cluster distances matter.
skills.name: cell-graph-topology-reconstruction
skills.search_text: cell-graph-topology-reconstruction Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix must be embedded in a latent space that preserves inter-cell topological/trajectory structure, not just per-cell features — e.g. clustering and trajectory inference where inter-cluster distances matter. The goal is a direct 2D embedding from the graph autoencoder itself — the paper notes complex data structure is hard to embed directly into two dimensions, so an intermediate dimension plus t-SNE is used instead Input is already an embedded/visualized representation (e.g. a 2D t-SNE or PCA output) rather than a preprocessed count matrix from which a cell graph can be built Cell–cell relationships are irrelevant and only feature-level embedding is needed — a feature-only autoencoder would suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Reconstruct scGAE, a multitask-oriented graph autoencoder that embeds preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices while jointly reconstructing both the feature matrix (counts) and the cell–cell KNN adjacency matrix, preserving topological structure that feature-only deep embeddings ignore. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Reconstruct scGAE, a multitask-oriented graph autoencoder that embeds preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices while jointly reconstructing both the feature matrix (counts) and the cell–cell KNN adjacency matrix, preserving topological structure that feature-only deep embeddings ignore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a direct 2D embedding from the graph autoencoder itself — the paper notes complex data structure is hard to embed directly into two dimensions, so an intermediate dimension plus t-SNE is used instead Input is already an embedded/visualized representation (e.g. a 2D t-SNE or PCA output) rather than a preprocessed count matrix from which a cell graph can be built Cell–cell relationships are irrelevant and only feature-level embedding is needed — a feature-only autoencoder would suffice

skills.description: Use when a single-cell CRISPR screen needs gRNAs assigned to cell barcodes from per-cell UMI counts, especially to separate ambient from endogenously expressed guides and distinguish singlets from multiplets.
skills.name: cell-grna-assignment-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-grna-assignment-annotation Use when a single-cell CRISPR screen needs gRNAs assigned to cell barcodes from per-cell UMI counts, especially to separate ambient from endogenously expressed guides and distinguish singlets from multiplets. Input reads are not yet UMI-collapsed and consensus-called (consensus.sequence.gRNA.variant.txt missing) — run the earlier GiRAFR steps (gRNA bam filtration, consensus sequence construction, variant calling) first. The goal is detecting CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing effects in transcriptome data, which GiRAFR handles in a separate analysis mode rather than via cell assignment. Only mutation patterns in the gRNA library itself need profiling (e.g. profile_MT_pattern.py outputs) without assigning guides to cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Assign CRISPR guide RNAs to single cells from per-cell gRNA UMI counts in a mutation-aware manner, using either a fixed UMI cutoff (min_umi=3) or a two-component Gaussian mixture model to derive a dynamic threshold per gRNA. This is Step 4 of the GiRAFR pipeline and corrects the ambient-UMI-driven misannotation and underestimated multiplet rates seen with default tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Assign CRISPR guide RNAs to single cells from per-cell gRNA UMI counts in a mutation-aware manner, using either a fixed UMI cutoff (min_umi=3) or a two-component Gaussian mixture model to derive a dynamic threshold per gRNA. This is Step 4 of the GiRAFR pipeline and corrects the ambient-UMI-driven misannotation and underestimated multiplet rates seen with default tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not yet UMI-collapsed and consensus-called (consensus.sequence.gRNA.variant.txt missing) — run the earlier GiRAFR steps (gRNA bam filtration, consensus sequence construction, variant calling) first. The goal is detecting CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing effects in transcriptome data, which GiRAFR handles in a separate analysis mode rather than via cell assignment. Only mutation patterns in the gRNA library itself need profiling (e.g. profile_MT_pattern.py outputs) without assigning guides to cells.

skills.description: Use when validating a cell-calling method (e.g., EmptyNN) on a cell hashing dataset by asking whether retained barcodes are transcriptionally closer to confirmed cells than removed barcodes within the same cell type.
skills.name: cell-hashing-data-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-hashing-data-analysis Use when validating a cell-calling method (e.g., EmptyNN) on a cell hashing dataset by asking whether retained barcodes are transcriptionally closer to confirmed cells than removed barcodes within the same cell type. Input is already a filtered/cell-called matrix — partitioning into All-retained/EmptyNN-retained/EmptyNN-removed requires the raw unfiltered matrix Goal is ambient RNA correction of expression profiles — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression; use SoupX instead Analysis targets snRNA-seq or other non-cell-hashing datasets without HTO-derived labels — validation contrasts should be run on the cell hashing ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Analyzes the Stoeckius cell hashing scRNA-seq dataset by partitioning barcodes into All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, and EmptyNN-removed groups and running Seurat differential expression contrasts to test whether EmptyNN-retained barcodes resemble genuine cell-containing barcodes. Validates EmptyNN's cell-calling decisions at the transcriptome level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Analyzes the Stoeckius cell hashing scRNA-seq dataset by partitioning barcodes into All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, and EmptyNN-removed groups and running Seurat differential expression contrasts to test whether EmptyNN-retained barcodes resemble genuine cell-containing barcodes. Validates EmptyNN's cell-calling decisions at the transcriptome level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered/cell-called matrix — partitioning into All-retained/EmptyNN-retained/EmptyNN-removed requires the raw unfiltered matrix Goal is ambient RNA correction of expression profiles — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression; use SoupX instead Analysis targets snRNA-seq or other non-cell-hashing datasets without HTO-derived labels — validation contrasts should be run on the cell hashing ground truth

skills.description: Use when a Seurat object carries an 'HTO' assay from a cell-hashing experiment and per-cell sample identities (singlet/doublet/negative) must be called, especially with many hashtags, imbalanced sample sizes, or degraded hashtag staining.
skills.name: cell-hashing-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: cell-hashing-demultiplexing Use when a Seurat object carries an 'HTO' assay from a cell-hashing experiment and per-cell sample identities (singlet/doublet/negative) must be called, especially with many hashtags, imbalanced sample sizes, or degraded hashtag staining. Samples lack distinct genetic backgrounds and no HTO assay exists (e.g. most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies) — cell hashing cutoff-based demultiplexing requires hashtag-stained cells Input is SNP/genotype-based demultiplexing output rather than an HTO count matrix — that calls for the hybrid strategy (HybridDemultiplexing), not HTOClassification alone The HTO assay shows severely degraded staining for hashtags where even parameter tuning cannot rescue assignment; the article notes tuning only marginally improves performance on such challenging datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns each cell in a pooled multi-sample single-cell experiment to its sample of origin (singlet, doublet, or negative) based on hashtag oligo (HTO) counts, using HTOreader's improved cutoff calling with CLR normalization and comparison against methods such as HTOdemux, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, BFF and DropletUtils. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Assigns each cell in a pooled multi-sample single-cell experiment to its sample of origin (singlet, doublet, or negative) based on hashtag oligo (HTO) counts, using HTOreader's improved cutoff calling with CLR normalization and comparison against methods such as HTOdemux, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, BFF and DropletUtils.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack distinct genetic backgrounds and no HTO assay exists (e.g. most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies) — cell hashing cutoff-based demultiplexing requires hashtag-stained cells Input is SNP/genotype-based demultiplexing output rather than an HTO count matrix — that calls for the hybrid strategy (HybridDemultiplexing), not HTOClassification alone The HTO assay shows severely degraded staining for hashtags where even parameter tuning cannot rescue assignment; the article notes tuning only marginally improves performance on such challenging datasets

skills.description: Use when a dataset has both cell hashing (HTO) demultiplexing labels and SNP/genotype-based demultiplexing labels (e.g. scSplit) and per-cell sample identities must be reconciled into a final assignment.
skills.name: cell-hashing-snp-label-correlation
skills.search_text: cell-hashing-snp-label-correlation Use when a dataset has both cell hashing (HTO) demultiplexing labels and SNP/genotype-based demultiplexing labels (e.g. scSplit) and per-cell sample identities must be reconciled into a final assignment. Samples lack a distinct genetic background (most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies), so SNP-based demultiplexing cannot provide genotype labels to correlate Only cell hashing data is available with no SNP-based demultiplexing result — use HTOClassification cutoff calling instead SNP-based clustering quality is poor (e.g. plasmablast or dying-cell populations with abnormal expression, high true doublet rates), since hybrid performance is largely dependent on SNP clustering quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Correlates cell hashing singlet assignments with SNP-based genotype cluster labels via HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function, computing a per-pair convergence score C = N1/(N1+N2) and resolving disagreeing cells with a 0.7 c_threshold decision and three-case inconsistent-label rules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Correlates cell hashing singlet assignments with SNP-based genotype cluster labels via HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function, computing a per-pair convergence score C = N1/(N1+N2) and resolving disagreeing cells with a 0.7 c_threshold decision and three-case inconsistent-label rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack a distinct genetic background (most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies), so SNP-based demultiplexing cannot provide genotype labels to correlate Only cell hashing data is available with no SNP-based demultiplexing result — use HTOClassification cutoff calling instead SNP-based clustering quality is poor (e.g. plasmablast or dying-cell populations with abnormal expression, high true doublet rates), since hybrid performance is largely dependent on SNP clustering quality

skills.search_text: cell-label-entropy-computation Use when FFC cluster labels exist (fire_temp=100) and you need per-cell label uncertainty — e.g., to flag candidate transition cells along a pseudotime trajectory or to quantify clustering confidence in scRNA-seq data. skills.summary: Computes point-wise label entropies (and posterior exclusion probabilities) for Forest Fire Clustering labels by running parallelized Monte Carlo internal validation, in which seed labels are re-propagated across trials to build an empirical posterior label distribution per cell; high entropy flags transition cells along developmental pseudo-time.

skills.name: cell-line-pharmacogenomic-data-joining
skills.search_text: cell-line-pharmacogenomic-data-joining Use when CMS class labels from CMScaller must be merged with published per-cell-line drug response data (e.g., 5-FU IC50) in MSS colorectal cancer models to test whether subtypes predict drug response. The sample set has a different human stromal component than primary colorectal cancers, e.g., patient biopsies of metastatic CRC — CMScaller in its current implementation is not recommended for such samples. The expression dataset is very small (fewer than about forty samples), where centering and scaling of input gene expression inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty. Input is single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and for which CMScaller is not optimized. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Joins CMScaller-derived CMS subtype labels to published drug response values (e.g., 5-FU IC50) for MSS colorectal cancer cell lines and tests subtype-response associations, showing that CMS4 predicts poor 5-FU response independent of microsatellite instability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Joins CMScaller-derived CMS subtype labels to published drug response values (e.g., 5-FU IC50) for MSS colorectal cancer cell lines and tests subtype-response associations, showing that CMS4 predicts poor 5-FU response independent of microsatellite instability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample set has a different human stromal component than primary colorectal cancers, e.g., patient biopsies of metastatic CRC — CMScaller in its current implementation is not recommended for such samples. The expression dataset is very small (fewer than about forty samples), where centering and scaling of input gene expression inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty. Input is single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and for which CMScaller is not optimized.
