skills.summary: Validates that feature representations learned by tGPT resolve biologically correct developmental branches by constructing diffusion pseudo-time maps with Pegasus (v1.4.3) and visualizing trajectories with force-directed layout embedding (FLE), checking branch structure against known cell type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression counts rather than pretrained-model feature embeddings — extract tGPT features first (rank-based top-expressing gene input, sequence length 64 or 128) The goal is de novo lineage discovery without known cell labels to validate against — alignment to known labels and states is the core validation signal here Batch-effect integration or clustering benchmarking is the goal — use the Scanpy/Pegasus/scVI benchmarking workflow with batch-correction tools instead

skills.name: cell-marker-database-querying
skills.search_text: cell-marker-database-querying Use when you have a per-cluster marker table (Entrez IDs, cluster labels, expression scores such as logFC from Seurat's FindAllMarkers) and need automated cell-type annotations from public marker databases. Input is a raw count matrix or Seurat object without a per-cluster marker table — run clustering and FindAllMarkers first (only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) before querying marker databases The cell type of interest lies outside the tissues covered by CellMarker/PanglaoDB/Clustermole, or the species is not Human/Mouse for the selected database You need to overlap gene lists without ranking information — the article warns this can lead to unreliable annotation results Queries public cell-marker gene databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) with a per-cluster differential marker table to produce ranked cell-type annotation recommendations, using EasyCellType's GSEA or score-weighted modified Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Queries public cell-marker gene databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) with a per-cluster differential marker table to produce ranked cell-type annotation recommendations, using EasyCellType's GSEA or score-weighted modified Fisher's exact test.

skills.description: Use when you have segmented single-cell masks from multiplexed tissue images and need to build the autoencoder cell shape descriptor inputs described by MIRIAM (binarize, rotate major axis horizontal, resize to 128x128).
skills.name: cell-mask-binarization-and-major-axis-alignment
skills.search_text: cell-mask-binarization-and-major-axis-alignment Use when you have segmented single-cell masks from multiplexed tissue images and need to build the autoencoder cell shape descriptor inputs described by MIRIAM (binarize, rotate major axis horizontal, resize to 128x128). Input is already a normalized feature or latent-vector table rather than raw segmented cell masks — go directly to downstream analysis (e.g., t-SNE) instead. Cells lack complete nuclear/membrane segmentation, since the shape descriptor depends on well-defined single-cell masks from the MIRIAM segmentation stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Preprocesses segmented single-cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline into normalized 128x128 binary matrices for training the autoencoder cell shape descriptor. Binarization, major-axis alignment, and fixed-size resizing give every cell a canonical orientation and scale so latent shape vectors are comparable across cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Preprocesses segmented single-cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline into normalized 128x128 binary matrices for training the autoencoder cell shape descriptor. Binarization, major-axis alignment, and fixed-size resizing give every cell a canonical orientation and scale so latent shape vectors are comparable across cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized feature or latent-vector table rather than raw segmented cell masks — go directly to downstream analysis (e.g., t-SNE) instead. skills.name: cell-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-metadata-annotation Use when starting a SingCellaR workflow from a Cell Ranger gene-expression matrix and you need per-cell QC annotation (UMIs, detected genes, mitochondrial percentage) before filtering low-quality cells and doublets. skills.summary: Computes per-cell QC metadata (UMI counts, detected genes, percent mitochondrial expression) for a SingCellaR object and visualizes their relationships, forming the basis for quality-control filtering decisions on individual scRNA-seq samples such as eFL_1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted-sequence reads rather than UMI-based Cell Ranger output — use TargetSeq_process_cells_annotation with min_Reads and ERCC (min_percent_ERCC/max_percent_ERCC) parameters instead The object has already been QC-filtered and normalized; re-annotating would not change thresholds already applied You need interoperable objects for other packages — SingCellaR lacks 'automatic object transformation' to interact with packages such as Seurat

skills.name: cell-metadata-standardization-singlecellexperiment
skills.search_text: cell-metadata-standardization-singlecellexperiment Use when a scRNA-seq SingleCellExperiment (e.g., a Bioconductor ExperimentHub anchor dataset such as EH2259, the Kang PBMC IFN-β data) has heterogeneous or missing cell-level metadata columns and must be harmonized before muscat aggregation/DS analysis. skills.summary: Standardize SingleCellExperiment cell metadata (colData) so that sample_id, group_id, and cluster_id columns are present, uniquely coded, and correctly typed before running muscat pseudobulk differential state analyses.

skills.description: Use when comparing BIDCell vs vendor 10x segmentation masks on Xenium data, or testing cross-replicate concordance of cell morphology, as part of the CellSPA category-A baseline and category agreement metrics.
skills.name: cell-morphology-metric-correlation
skills.search_text: cell-morphology-metric-correlation Use when comparing BIDCell vs vendor 10x segmentation masks on Xenium data, or testing cross-replicate concordance of cell morphology, as part of the CellSPA category-A baseline and category agreement metrics. Input is an already-summarized feature table rather than a pixel-labeled segmentation mask and transcript file — morphology metrics must be derived from *_connected.tif-style cell-ID masks. Nuclei images are split into fields of view (e.g. CosMx) and have not yet been stitched/segmented — run BIDCell's stitch_nuclei and preprocess stages first. Evaluating segmentation quality by a single morphology metric alone — the article notes homogenous cell bodies can result from arbitrary over-segmentation of nuclei, motivating multiple metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-cell morphology metrics (area, elongation, eccentricity, solidity) from cell segmentation masks of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data and correlates them between segmentation methods or between replicate sections, following the CellSPA evaluation framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Computes per-cell morphology metrics (area, elongation, eccentricity, solidity) from cell segmentation masks of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data and correlates them between segmentation methods or between replicate sections, following the CellSPA evaluation framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an already-summarized feature table rather than a pixel-labeled segmentation mask and transcript file — morphology metrics must be derived from *_connected.tif-style cell-ID masks. Nuclei images are split into fields of view (e.g. CosMx) and have not yet been stitched/segmented — run BIDCell's stitch_nuclei and preprocess stages first. Evaluating segmentation quality by a single morphology metric alone — the article notes homogenous cell bodies can result from arbitrary over-segmentation of nuclei, motivating multiple metrics.

skills.description: Use when comparing cluster-purity (ROGUE) values across populations whose cell-type cell counts differ substantially — e.g., aggregated batches vs. individual patient samples in Kang et al. GSE96583 PBMC data — to rule out cell-count confounding.
skills.name: cell-number-down-sampling-equalization
skills.search_text: cell-number-down-sampling-equalization Use when comparing cluster-purity (ROGUE) values across populations whose cell-type cell counts differ substantially — e.g., aggregated batches vs. individual patient samples in Kang et al. GSE96583 PBMC data — to rule out cell-count confounding. When cell-type cell counts are already balanced across the populations being compared, down-sampling adds no information and discards data unnecessarily When the analysis goal is a single population's purity rather than a comparison across populations or batches — there is no confound to equalize When rare cell types would be reduced to too few cells for stable entropy estimation by equalizing to the smallest group http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A confound-removal procedure from the ROGUE cluster-purity workflow: before comparing ROGUE values across populations (e.g., per-patient batches vs. aggregated IFN-stimulated PBMCs), matrices are down-sampled so each cell type contributes an equal cell number, eliminating cell-count differences as a driver of measured purity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: A confound-removal procedure from the ROGUE cluster-purity workflow: before comparing ROGUE values across populations (e.g., per-patient batches vs. aggregated IFN-stimulated PBMCs), matrices are down-sampled so each cell type contributes an equal cell number, eliminating cell-count differences as a driver of measured purity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell-type cell counts are already balanced across the populations being compared, down-sampling adds no information and discards data unnecessarily When the analysis goal is a single population's purity rather than a comparison across populations or batches — there is no confound to equalize When rare cell types would be reduced to too few cells for stable entropy estimation by equalizing to the smallest group

skills.name: cell-ontology-based-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-ontology-based-cell-type-annotation Use when a prepared H5AD study (e.g. the blood_covid AnnData file) needs standardized, ontology-resolved cell type labels per cell — e.g. before cross-study expression comparison in Cellenium — rather than ad hoc cluster labels. skills.summary: Assigns standardized Cell Ontology cell type labels to every individual cell of a prepared single-cell study using CellO's pretrained classifier, as done in Cellenium so that annotations become semantically integratable for cross-study expression comparisons.

skills.description: Use when annotating single-cell data against the Cell Ontology controlled vocabulary, especially when test labels may include unseen cell type terms that have no annotated cells in the training set.
skills.name: cell-ontology-embedding
skills.search_text: cell-ontology-embedding Use when annotating single-cell data against the Cell Ontology controlled vocabulary, especially when test labels may include unseen cell type terms that have no annotated cells in the training set. When labels are not Cell Ontology terms and no controlled-vocabulary mapping is possible (the embedding projects Cell Ontology terms specifically) When the goal is to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot separate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Project cell type terms from the Cell Ontology (cl.obo plus cl.ontology.nlp.emb NLP embeddings) into a low-dimensional, ontology-informed vector space using OnClass's EmbedCellTypes, so that cell types—including terms with no annotated cells in the training data—become classifiable alongside single-cell transcriptomes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Project cell type terms from the Cell Ontology (cl.obo plus cl.ontology.nlp.emb NLP embeddings) into a low-dimensional, ontology-informed vector space using OnClass's EmbedCellTypes, so that cell types—including terms with no annotated cells in the training data—become classifiable alongside single-cell transcriptomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When labels are not Cell Ontology terms and no controlled-vocabulary mapping is possible (the embedding projects Cell Ontology terms specifically) When the goal is to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot separate

skills.name: cell-ontology-graph-score-propagation
skills.search_text: cell-ontology-graph-score-propagation Use when the query dataset may contain cell types absent from the training reference and scores must be produced for all Cell Ontology terms, not just seen training labels. All query cell types have annotated cells in the training set, so extending scores to unseen ontology terms is unnecessary Topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) must be distinguished — OnClass cannot separate them http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Refines per-cell annotation scores by overlaying confidence scores on the Cell Ontology graph and propagating them via random walk with restart (OnClass step 3), so every Cell Ontology term — including unseen terms with no annotated training cells — receives a confidence score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Refines per-cell annotation scores by overlaying confidence scores on the Cell Ontology graph and propagating them via random walk with restart (OnClass step 3), so every Cell Ontology term — including unseen terms with no annotated training cells — receives a confidence score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All query cell types have annotated cells in the training set, so extending scores to unseen ontology terms is unnecessary Topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) must be distinguished — OnClass cannot separate them

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether ontology-defined cell type relatedness (Cell Ontology graph structure) predicts expression-profile or text-description similarity, or to validate ontology-based annotation methods like OnClass.
skills.name: cell-ontology-graph-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: cell-ontology-graph-similarity-computation Use when you need to test whether ontology-defined cell type relatedness (Cell Ontology graph structure) predicts expression-profile or text-description similarity, or to validate ontology-based annotation methods like OnClass. The goal is cell type annotation of a new scRNA-seq dataset rather than characterizing ontology-vs-expression concordance — use the OnClass classification pipeline (ProcessTrainFeature, BuildModel, Train) instead. No Cell Ontology term mapping exists for the cell types in the expression data, so graph-based similarity cannot be traversed. Comparing topologically identical sibling cell types (same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass-related ontology structure cannot distinguish. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Quantify how similar cell types are according to the Cell Ontology graph, text embeddings of cell type definitions (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), and gene expression profiles, by building three pairwise similarity matrices and computing Pearson correlations between them (e.g., 0.65 lung / 0.93 pancreas for expression-vs-ontology). This validates the guilt-by-association principle underlying OnClass. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Quantify how similar cell types are according to the Cell Ontology graph, text embeddings of cell type definitions (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), and gene expression profiles, by building three pairwise similarity matrices and computing Pearson correlations between them (e.g., 0.65 lung / 0.93 pancreas for expression-vs-ontology). This validates the guilt-by-association principle underlying OnClass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell type annotation of a new scRNA-seq dataset rather than characterizing ontology-vs-expression concordance — use the OnClass classification pipeline (ProcessTrainFeature, BuildModel, Train) instead. No Cell Ontology term mapping exists for the cell types in the expression data, so graph-based similarity cannot be traversed. Comparing topologically identical sibling cell types (same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass-related ontology structure cannot distinguish.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a Cell Ontology-based cell type classifier at multiple annotation granularities, or when fine labels must be collapsed into coarser parent classes (e.g. 164 → 31 labels) using ontology-derived information content.
skills.name: cell-ontology-hierarchy-traversal
skills.search_text: cell-ontology-hierarchy-traversal Use when evaluating a Cell Ontology-based cell type classifier at multiple annotation granularities, or when fine labels must be collapsed into coarser parent classes (e.g. 164 → 31 labels) using ontology-derived information content. Cell type labels are not drawn from the Cell Ontology (e.g. free-text or non-CL nomenclature), so subtype/parent relations cannot be resolved Evaluation goal is strict exact-match accuracy only, where ontology-derived partial credit would change the metric definition The cell types of interest are rare types that may not be correctly matched to a corresponding ontology term, making the hierarchy unreliable Traverses the Cell Ontology (CL) child/parent structure — via the child node lookup matrix built in `04_create_hierarchy_matrices.ipynb` — to map the 164 fine-grained cell type labels of scTab to 31 coarse classes using information-content scores, enabling coarse-vs-fine granularity evaluation of macro F1 (0.897 vs 0.830). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Traverses the Cell Ontology (CL) child/parent structure — via the child node lookup matrix built in `04_create_hierarchy_matrices.ipynb` — to map the 164 fine-grained cell type labels of scTab to 31 coarse classes using information-content scores, enabling coarse-vs-fine granularity evaluation of macro F1 (0.897 vs 0.830).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type labels are not drawn from the Cell Ontology (e.g. free-text or non-CL nomenclature), so subtype/parent relations cannot be resolved Evaluation goal is strict exact-match accuracy only, where ontology-derived partial credit would change the metric definition The cell types of interest are rare types that may not be correctly matched to a corresponding ontology term, making the hierarchy unreliable

skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell types of interest are outside the Cell Ontology or are topologically identical siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph, which OnClass cannot distinguish The goal is batch correction of expression data in the presence of many unseen cell types — no such methods are developed here, and Scanorama on expression is the baseline being compared against Input is raw reads or gene expression already organized as an integrated embedding, not scRNA-seq expression matrices to be scored against the ontology

skills.search_text: cell-ontology-term-counting Use when you need to verify or reproduce the dataset-construction statistics of CellO's SRA-derived bulk RNA-seq training set (samples, studies, CL terms, most-specific terms) from the deposited Zenodo package. skills.summary: Reproduces CellO's curated bulk RNA-seq training-set curation statistics — 4,293 samples from 264 studies labeled with 310 Cell Ontology (CL) terms, of which 113 were most-specific cell types — by downloading the Zenodo data package and counting samples, studies, CL terms, and most-specific annotations.

skills.search_text: cell-ontology-term-mapping Use when marker cell-type and tissue labels from heterogeneous marker databases must be harmonized onto Cell Ontology and Uberon terms before computing consistency-weighted marker scores or running accordion() annotation. Input labels are already Cell Ontology / Uberon standardized and need no harmonization before scoring The analysis goal is non-marker-based annotation (e.g., reference-mapping or CNV-based tools like SCEVAN or CopyKAT) where ontology harmonization of marker labels is not the operative step Only a single, internally consistent marker source is used, so cross-source evidence consistency (ECs) cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Standardizes heterogeneous marker gene cell-type labels and tissue names from multiple marker databases (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) onto Cell Ontology (release 2024-08-16) and Uberon (release 2024-09-03) terms so that the Cell Marker Accordion can compute consistent SPs/ECs marker weights. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Standardizes heterogeneous marker gene cell-type labels and tissue names from multiple marker databases (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) onto Cell Ontology (release 2024-08-16) and Uberon (release 2024-09-03) terms so that the Cell Marker Accordion can compute consistent SPs/ECs marker weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input labels are already Cell Ontology / Uberon standardized and need no harmonization before scoring The analysis goal is non-marker-based annotation (e.g., reference-mapping or CNV-based tools like SCEVAN or CopyKAT) where ontology harmonization of marker labels is not the operative step Only a single, internally consistent marker source is used, so cross-source evidence consistency (ECs) cannot be computed

skills.search_text: cell-phase-posterior-conditioned-gene-fitting Use when Step 1 phase posteriors exist for cells in a droplet/plate scRNA-seq dataset and you need to identify de novo circadian cycling genes among currently non-cycling genes before refitting the model. Genes are already designated as cyclers — this skill specifically targets genes not currently identified as cyclers for de novo selection No Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions are available, since the gene fits are conditioned on those phase posteriors Flexible non-sinusoidal waveform modeling is required — the article notes the de novo cycler issue may stem from assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fits approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions for genes not currently designated cyclers, conditioned on Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, and selects de novo cycling genes using the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction criteria (Tempo Step 2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Fits approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions for genes not currently designated cyclers, conditioned on Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, and selects de novo cycling genes using the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction criteria (Tempo Step 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes are already designated as cyclers — this skill specifically targets genes not currently identified as cyclers for de novo selection No Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions are available, since the gene fits are conditioned on those phase posteriors Flexible non-sinusoidal waveform modeling is required — the article notes the de novo cycler issue may stem from assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq UMI count data with high dropout (e.g. PBMC3k 2700 cells x 1158 genes) needs unsupervised dimension reduction to a 2D visualization that distinguishes cell types or resolves sub-populations such as FCGR3A+ vs CD14+ monocytes.
skills.name: cell-population-2d-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-population-2d-visualization Use when scRNA-seq UMI count data with high dropout (e.g. PBMC3k 2700 cells x 1158 genes) needs unsupervised dimension reduction to a 2D visualization that distinguishes cell types or resolves sub-populations such as FCGR3A+ vs CD14+ monocytes. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a feature/marker table rather than a raw or normalized expression matrix — VASC operates on the expression matrix to learn its own nonlinear hierarchical representation The goal is bulk RNA-seq or traditional low-dropout data analysis where conventional dimension reduction (PCA, t-SNE) suffices; VASC is designed for noisy scRNA-seq data with technical dropout events Fast, deterministic 2D coordinates are required for small samples without GPU access — VASC model learning takes several hours on a single-GPU desktop for several-thousand-cell datasets and stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that explicitly models dropout events with a Gumbel distribution, to obtain a 2D latent embedding of scRNA-seq data that separates cell types and sub-populations, as demonstrated on the 10x Genomics PBMC3k dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.08.003
skills.summary: Apply VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that explicitly models dropout events with a Gumbel distribution, to obtain a 2D latent embedding of scRNA-seq data that separates cell types and sub-populations, as demonstrated on the 10x Genomics PBMC3k dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a feature/marker table rather than a raw or normalized expression matrix — VASC operates on the expression matrix to learn its own nonlinear hierarchical representation The goal is bulk RNA-seq or traditional low-dropout data analysis where conventional dimension reduction (PCA, t-SNE) suffices; VASC is designed for noisy scRNA-seq data with technical dropout events Fast, deterministic 2D coordinates are required for small samples without GPU access — VASC model learning takes several hours on a single-GPU desktop for several-thousand-cell datasets and stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation

skills.description: Use when analyzing multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (t0/t1 expression matrices with t0 labels) and you need to display how annotated and novel cell populations evolve, e.g., emerging tumor subclones.
skills.name: cell-population-evolution-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-population-evolution-visualization Use when analyzing multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (t0/t1 expression matrices with t0 labels) and you need to display how annotated and novel cell populations evolve, e.g., emerging tumor subclones. Data come from a single timepoint with no t0/t1 structure to compare, so cross-timepoint population evolution is undefined The follow-up timepoint data differ dramatically from the initial timepoint, so the t0-trained neural network cannot borrow useful information for annotation The goal is temporal differential expression (tDEGs) rather than cell population evolution, which is handled by FindTemporalDEGs instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Visualize how cell populations change across timepoints in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq using CASi's UMAP plots (colored by cell-type-specific correlation and cell labels, via DrawUMAP=TRUE) and fish plots of annotated vs. novel population evolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Visualize how cell populations change across timepoints in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq using CASi's UMAP plots (colored by cell-type-specific correlation and cell labels, via DrawUMAP=TRUE) and fish plots of annotated vs. novel population evolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from a single timepoint with no t0/t1 structure to compare, so cross-timepoint population evolution is undefined The follow-up timepoint data differ dramatically from the initial timepoint, so the t0-trained neural network cannot borrow useful information for annotation The goal is temporal differential expression (tDEGs) rather than cell population evolution, which is handled by FindTemporalDEGs instead

skills.search_text: cell-population-reference-mapping Use when a single-cell AnnData carries multiple conflicting annotation columns (e.g., cellHarmony label transfer to Hay et al. skills.description: Use when training PRESCIENT on longitudinal scRNA-seq (e.g., Weinreb hematopoiesis days 2/4/6) and fate-bias or interpolation predictions must account for cell proliferation via growth weights.
skills.name: cell-proliferation-growth-weight-estimation
skills.search_text: cell-proliferation-growth-weight-estimation Use when training PRESCIENT on longitudinal scRNA-seq (e.g., Weinreb hematopoiesis days 2/4/6) and fate-bias or interpolation predictions must account for cell proliferation via growth weights. The dataset lacks any proliferation information and no lineage-tracing ground truth or cell-cycle-based estimates can be computed (the model then relies on unweighted population dynamics) The task does not require fate-bias or temporal population prediction, e.g., purely exploratory clustering of a single time point The final time point of the dataset is not at steady-state, violating the model's assumption http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell proliferation/growth weights for PRESCIENT training on single-cell time-series data (e.g., the Weinreb et al. mouse hematopoiesis lineage tracing dataset), so the learned differentiation potential accounts for asymmetric cell proliferation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Compute per-cell proliferation/growth weights for PRESCIENT training on single-cell time-series data (e.g., the Weinreb et al. mouse hematopoiesis lineage tracing dataset), so the learned differentiation potential accounts for asymmetric cell proliferation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks any proliferation information and no lineage-tracing ground truth or cell-cycle-based estimates can be computed (the model then relies on unweighted population dynamics) The task does not require fate-bias or temporal population prediction, e.g., purely exploratory clustering of a single time point The final time point of the dataset is not at steady-state, violating the model's assumption

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into pseudo-space via scSpace and clustered, and you must test whether a subpopulation near a reference cell type (e.g., malignant cells) shows a distinct functional signature such as T cell exhaustion.
skills.name: cell-proximity-analysis-in-reconstructed-space
skills.search_text: cell-proximity-analysis-in-reconstructed-space Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into pseudo-space via scSpace and clustered, and you must test whether a subpopulation near a reference cell type (e.g., malignant cells) shows a distinct functional signature such as T cell exhaustion. You want spatial domain identification of ST data itself — scSpace (and this proximity analysis) targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, not SpaGCN/BayesSpace-style ST domain calling The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC), where the article advises applying scSpace cautiously and pseudo-space proximity inference would be unreliable Cells have not yet been projected into pseudo-space coordinates and clustered — proximity and signature comparisons require the space-informed Leiden clusters first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantify pairwise spatial associations between reconstructed cell subpopulations by comparing exhaustion scores and proximity to reference cell types (e.g., malignant cells) in the pseudo-space coordinates produced by scSpace, to identify tissue-infiltrating identities such as tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Quantify pairwise spatial associations between reconstructed cell subpopulations by comparing exhaustion scores and proximity to reference cell types (e.g., malignant cells) in the pseudo-space coordinates produced by scSpace, to identify tissue-infiltrating identities such as tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want spatial domain identification of ST data itself — scSpace (and this proximity analysis) targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, not SpaGCN/BayesSpace-style ST domain calling The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC), where the article advises applying scSpace cautiously and pseudo-space proximity inference would be unreliable Cells have not yet been projected into pseudo-space coordinates and clustered — proximity and signature comparisons require the space-informed Leiden clusters first

skills.description: Use when preparing Tabula Muris or similar scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) as training/testing input for cell-type identification methods, so that low-quality cells and unannotated cells are removed with the paper's exact thresholds.
skills.name: cell-qc-filtering-threshold-application
skills.search_text: cell-qc-filtering-threshold-application Use when preparing Tabula Muris or similar scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) as training/testing input for cell-type identification methods, so that low-quality cells and unannotated cells are removed with the paper's exact thresholds. Input is already a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix (e.g., a processed Seurat object) rather than a raw count matrix The downstream task is marker-based identification (e.g., markersupervised methods like SCSA/SCINA) where cell-level training labels are not required in the same way The analysis goal is de novo clustering without reference labels, since the pipeline requires cells with known cell-type information http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies the paper's standardized single-cell RNA-seq QC filtering thresholds — dropping genes not expressed in any cell, cells with fewer than 200 expressed genes, cells exceeding twice the standard deviation of the mean expressed-gene count, cells with more than 20% mitochondrial reads, and cells lacking manual labels — before automatic cell-type identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Applies the paper's standardized single-cell RNA-seq QC filtering thresholds — dropping genes not expressed in any cell, cells with fewer than 200 expressed genes, cells exceeding twice the standard deviation of the mean expressed-gene count, cells with more than 20% mitochondrial reads, and cells lacking manual labels — before automatic cell-type identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix (e.g., a processed Seurat object) rather than a raw count matrix The downstream task is marker-based identification (e.g., markersupervised methods like SCSA/SCINA) where cell-level training labels are not required in the same way The analysis goal is de novo clustering without reference labels, since the pipeline requires cells with known cell-type information

skills.description: Use when loading high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE, MERFISH, or 10X Xenium cells) or scRNA-seq test data prior to CeLEry training/prediction, and cells with sparse UMIs or few detected genes would otherwise add noise to expression-to-location learning.
skills.name: cell-quality-filtering-umi-counts
skills.search_text: cell-quality-filtering-umi-counts Use when loading high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE, MERFISH, or 10X Xenium cells) or scRNA-seq test data prior to CeLEry training/prediction, and cells with sparse UMIs or few detected genes would otherwise add noise to expression-to-location learning. Data are already spot-level Visium counts with adequate depth per spot — the paper's filtering is described for MERSCOPE, MERFISH, and 10X Xenium cell-level data The downstream method is not CeLEry-style supervised learning, and aggressive cell removal would discard biologically relevant rare or low-UML cells from a descriptive analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quality-control step that eliminates single-cell or spot-level observations with low UMI counts or a small number of expressed genes before downstream normalization and model training. In the CeLEry pipeline this filtering is applied to single-cell-resolution ST platforms (MERSCOPE, MERFISH, 10X Xenium) so that the supervised location-prediction network is not trained on low-information cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Quality-control step that eliminates single-cell or spot-level observations with low UMI counts or a small number of expressed genes before downstream normalization and model training. In the CeLEry pipeline this filtering is applied to single-cell-resolution ST platforms (MERSCOPE, MERFISH, 10X Xenium) so that the supervised location-prediction network is not trained on low-information cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already spot-level Visium counts with adequate depth per spot — the paper's filtering is described for MERSCOPE, MERFISH, and 10X Xenium cell-level data The downstream method is not CeLEry-style supervised learning, and aggressive cell removal would discard biologically relevant rare or low-UML cells from a descriptive analysis

skills.description: Use when mapping per-cell x/y coordinates from a CODEX (or 10x spatial transcriptomics) image of Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue onto a linear backbone, and you must retain radial (thickness) position, not just along-line position.
skills.name: cell-radial-offset-preservation
skills.search_text: cell-radial-offset-preservation Use when mapping per-cell x/y coordinates from a CODEX (or 10x spatial transcriptomics) image of Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue onto a linear backbone, and you must retain radial (thickness) position, not just along-line position. The image data provide no xy-coordinates — IntestLine is suitable for CODEX, 10x spatial transcriptomics, or any images providing xy-coordinates, but nothing else The tissue is already unrolled/linear so there is no spiral backbone and no radial offset to preserve The backbone selection was not drawn from the center outward (e.g. an arbitrary or reversed point order), which would break the directional bias of the nearest-neighbor assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Assigns each cell from a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image to a base-layer (backbone) point using a directionally biased nearest-neighbor match restricted to outward base-layer points, then records each cell's arc position along the line and its residual radial offset. This preserves intestinal-wall thickness and each cell's serosa-luminal position within the wall in the linear map. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: Assigns each cell from a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image to a base-layer (backbone) point using a directionally biased nearest-neighbor match restricted to outward base-layer points, then records each cell's arc position along the line and its residual radial offset. This preserves intestinal-wall thickness and each cell's serosa-luminal position within the wall in the linear map.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The image data provide no xy-coordinates — IntestLine is suitable for CODEX, 10x spatial transcriptomics, or any images providing xy-coordinates, but nothing else The tissue is already unrolled/linear so there is no spiral backbone and no radial offset to preserve The backbone selection was not drawn from the center outward (e.g. an arbitrary or reversed point order), which would break the directional bias of the nearest-neighbor assignment

The data is very large: scLENS's RMT approach requires computing all eigenvalues of the large cell-to-cell similarity matrix, so whole-gene analysis on large data still requires a computer with high specifications You intend to apply imputation or highly-variable-gene feature selection first — imputation risks biasing data and generating false signals, and variance-based gene selection can compromise local structure in low-variance genes A subjective, user-set signal-noise threshold is acceptable or desired; this skill exists specifically to replace manual dimension selection with a data-driven RMT criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Eigendecompose the cell-to-cell similarity matrix G = XX^T/N built from L2-normalized scRNA-seq data, then separate signal from noise by fitting the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) distribution and applying a Tracy-Widom (TW) threshold, as done in scLENS's RMT-based noise filtering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3

skills.description: Use when you have multiple low-dimensional latent representation matrices of single cells (e.g. from a stacked variational autoencoder with latent dimension d = 15) and need to determine cell groups and cluster assignments.
skills.name: cell-similarity-network-construction
skills.search_text: cell-similarity-network-construction Use when you have multiple low-dimensional latent representation matrices of single cells (e.g. from a stacked variational autoencoder with latent dimension d = 15) and need to determine cell groups and cluster assignments. Input is raw high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression data — the non-negative kernel autoencoder feature-filtering module (top 5000 genes by coefficient variance) and VAE dimensionality reduction should run first Data is not normalized and min-max scaled to the 0-1 range per row, which is the required preprocessing before the autoencoder modules The goal is supervised cell-type classification with known labels rather than unsupervised clustering from latent representations http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Constructs cell-similarity networks from low-dimensional latent representations of scRNA-seq data using local Gaussian kernels (k = 30 neighbors), then fuses multiple networks with the SNF-style iterative update and applies spectral clustering to assign cells to clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Constructs cell-similarity networks from low-dimensional latent representations of scRNA-seq data using local Gaussian kernels (k = 30 neighbors), then fuses multiple networks with the SNF-style iterative update and applies spectral clustering to assign cells to clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression data — the non-negative kernel autoencoder feature-filtering module (top 5000 genes by coefficient variance) and VAE dimensionality reduction should run first Data is not normalized and min-max scaled to the 0-1 range per row, which is the required preprocessing before the autoencoder modules The goal is supervised cell-type classification with known labels rather than unsupervised clustering from latent representations

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes × n cells) needs to be transformed into direct gene–gene association networks per cell, or into a CNDM for downstream clustering/dimension reduction.
skills.name: cell-specific-network-construction
skills.search_text: cell-specific-network-construction Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes × n cells) needs to be transformed into direct gene–gene association networks per cell, or into a CNDM for downstream clustering/dimension reduction. Input is not single-cell expression data or already consists of network/association data rather than a gene expression matrix The goal is to infer causal gene association networks or directions of gene regulation — the article states c-CSN is not designed for this and directions cannot be obtained Only a bulk RNA-seq profile with a single sample is available, since CCSNs are constructed per individual cell http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for each single cell from a normalized gene expression matrix by testing conditional independence of gene pairs given top-degree hub genes, then aggregates per-cell CCSNs into an m × n conditional network degree matrix (CNDM) that removes CSN's overestimated indirect associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for each single cell from a normalized gene expression matrix by testing conditional independence of gene pairs given top-degree hub genes, then aggregates per-cell CCSNs into an m × n conditional network degree matrix (CNDM) that removes CSN's overestimated indirect associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not single-cell expression data or already consists of network/association data rather than a gene expression matrix The goal is to infer causal gene association networks or directions of gene regulation — the article states c-CSN is not designed for this and directions cannot be obtained Only a bulk RNA-seq profile with a single sample is available, since CCSNs are constructed per individual cell

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-specific network inference algorithms on single-cell expression data where per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks (or a simulator such as dyngen that provides them) are available for AUROC/AUPR scoring.
skills.name: cell-specific-regulatory-network-inference
skills.search_text: cell-specific-regulatory-network-inference Use when evaluating or comparing cell-specific network inference algorithms on single-cell expression data where per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks (or a simulator such as dyngen that provides them) are available for AUROC/AUPR scoring. No per-cell ground truth exists and no simulator (dyngen or similar) can provide it — the method requires cellwise GRN annotations for AUROC/AUPR scoring The underlying base method requires motif/prior data that is unavailable (e.g. PANDA is inapplicable here because dyngen provides no motif data) Input is bulk or aggregated expression without single-cell resolution, since leave-one-out cell-specific differencing is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3794 Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods — SSN, LIONESS + Pearson, and pySCENIC — against dyngen's cellwise ground-truth GRNs, scoring each method by mean AUROC and mean AUPR averaged over individual cells across 42 simulated datasets (14 backbones × 3 seeds). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods — SSN, LIONESS + Pearson, and pySCENIC — against dyngen's cellwise ground-truth GRNs, scoring each method by mean AUROC and mean AUPR averaged over individual cells across 42 simulated datasets (14 backbones × 3 seeds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No per-cell ground truth exists and no simulator (dyngen or similar) can provide it — the method requires cellwise GRN annotations for AUROC/AUPR scoring The underlying base method requires motif/prior data that is unavailable (e.g. PANDA is inapplicable here because dyngen provides no motif data) Input is bulk or aggregated expression without single-cell resolution, since leave-one-out cell-specific differencing is meaningless

skills.description: Use when query scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10x/hdf5 CD45+ TIL or P14 T cell data) must be assigned reference cell-state labels and subtype frequencies by projecting them onto a curated TIL or viral-infection reference atlas.
skills.name: cell-state-annotation-nearest-neighbor
skills.search_text: cell-state-annotation-nearest-neighbor Use when query scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10x/hdf5 CD45+ TIL or P14 T cell data) must be assigned reference cell-state labels and subtype frequencies by projecting them onto a curated TIL or viral-infection reference atlas. The query needs an independent clustering/annotation because no relevant curated reference atlas exists — e.g. gamma-delta T cells, which are not represented at all in the available reference atlases Only label transfer is desired and the query's own dimensionality reduction must not be modified — use the classifier mode rather than full embedding projection Data are CD4+ TILs or other states under-represented in the reference, since reference atlases do not yet encompass the full diversity of T cell transcriptional states Annotates cell states of new scRNA-seq query data by nearest-neighbor label transfer within the stable coordinate system of a reference T cell atlas (ProjecTILs), preserving the reference embedding rather than rebuilding it. Used to quantify subtype composition shifts and gene-program changes across perturbation conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Annotates cell states of new scRNA-seq query data by nearest-neighbor label transfer within the stable coordinate system of a reference T cell atlas (ProjecTILs), preserving the reference embedding rather than rebuilding it. Used to quantify subtype composition shifts and gene-program changes across perturbation conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query needs an independent clustering/annotation because no relevant curated reference atlas exists — e.g. gamma-delta T cells, which are not represented at all in the available reference atlases Only label transfer is desired and the query's own dimensionality reduction must not be modified — use the classifier mode rather than full embedding projection Data are CD4+ TILs or other states under-represented in the reference, since reference atlases do not yet encompass the full diversity of T cell transcriptional states

skills.description: Use when projecting scRNA-seq query data (e.g., Regnase-1-null vs WT CD8+ TILs) onto a reference atlas and you need cell-state frequency compositions per condition to detect enrichment of subtypes like Tpex or Tex.
skills.name: cell-state-composition-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-state-composition-frequency-analysis Use when projecting scRNA-seq query data (e.g., Regnase-1-null vs WT CD8+ TILs) onto a reference atlas and you need cell-state frequency compositions per condition to detect enrichment of subtypes like Tpex or Tex. The question is whether gene programs within a fixed cell state deviate between conditions rather than whether subtype frequencies change — use find.discriminant.dimensions (PCA/ICA) instead of composition analysis Input data are normalized beyond ProjecTILs' expected raw counts without setting skip.normalize=TRUE, which would double-normalize and distort state label assignment The cell type of interest (e.g., γδ T cells) is not represented in the reference atlas, so predicted state frequencies would be meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies and compares the frequency of predicted reference cell states (e.g., Tpex, Tex in the mouse TIL atlas) between conditions after ProjecTILs projection, revealing whether a perturbation (e.g., Regnase-1 deletion) shifts subtype composition or alters programs within a state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares the frequency of predicted reference cell states (e.g., Tpex, Tex in the mouse TIL atlas) between conditions after ProjecTILs projection, revealing whether a perturbation (e.g., Regnase-1 deletion) shifts subtype composition or alters programs within a state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is whether gene programs within a fixed cell state deviate between conditions rather than whether subtype frequencies change — use find.discriminant.dimensions (PCA/ICA) instead of composition analysis Input data are normalized beyond ProjecTILs' expected raw counts without setting skip.normalize=TRUE, which would double-normalize and distort state label assignment The cell type of interest (e.g., γδ T cells) is not represented in the reference atlas, so predicted state frequencies would be meaningless

skills.description: Use when validating a learned cell-state classifier (e.g., Pollock explain-mode DWGs) against curated marker databases like PanglaoDB, or when asked which cell states' feature scores recover known markers.
skills.name: cell-state-gene-signature-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-state-gene-signature-overlap-analysis Use when validating a learned cell-state classifier (e.g., Pollock explain-mode DWGs) against curated marker databases like PanglaoDB, or when asked which cell states' feature scores recover known markers. The goal is cell type prediction itself (use Pollock predict mode) rather than validating interpretability scores against known markers. The comparison target is not a curated marker database but, e.g., a differential expression analysis; this skill's denominator and mapping assumptions assume PanglaoDB-style marker sets. The pretrained module's classes are non-immune tissue states with no direct or macro-parent match in the PanglaoDB marker files, making the state-to-marker mapping undefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies biological plausibility of Pollock's captum-derived interpretability scores by intersecting the top-100 differentially weighted genes (DWGs) per cell state with PanglaoDB marker gene sets, reporting per-state overlap percentages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Quantifies biological plausibility of Pollock's captum-derived interpretability scores by intersecting the top-100 differentially weighted genes (DWGs) per cell state with PanglaoDB marker gene sets, reporting per-state overlap percentages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell type prediction itself (use Pollock predict mode) rather than validating interpretability scores against known markers. The comparison target is not a curated marker database but, e.g., a differential expression analysis; this skill's denominator and mapping assumptions assume PanglaoDB-style marker sets. The pretrained module's classes are non-immune tissue states with no direct or macro-parent match in the PanglaoDB marker files, making the state-to-marker mapping undefined.

skills.description: Use when analyzing TSCS single-cell RT-PCR or RNA-seq data from two consecutive stages of a cell-state transition (e.g., ICM->EPI, ICM->PE) and needing a directed, weighted, sparse GRN without constructing pseudo-time.
skills.name: cell-state-transition-network-modeling
skills.search_text: cell-state-transition-network-modeling Use when analyzing TSCS single-cell RT-PCR or RNA-seq data from two consecutive stages of a cell-state transition (e.g., ICM->EPI, ICM->PE) and needing a directed, weighted, sparse GRN without constructing pseudo-time. The data are a single cell stage/time point only, where the goal is the dense GRN maintaining the current state rather than the sparse mechanism driving a transition The data constitute a true longitudinal time series with linkage across time points rather than independently sampled, time-stamped cross-sectional batches Accurate pseudo-time trajectories already exist and a pseudo-time-based method (SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) is preferred for the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct directed, sparse gene regulatory networks (GRNs) driving cell fate transitions from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data using COSLIR, which relies only on first and second moments of samples between consecutive time points and avoids pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Reconstruct directed, sparse gene regulatory networks (GRNs) driving cell fate transitions from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data using COSLIR, which relies only on first and second moments of samples between consecutive time points and avoids pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are a single cell stage/time point only, where the goal is the dense GRN maintaining the current state rather than the sparse mechanism driving a transition The data constitute a true longitudinal time series with linkage across time points rather than independently sampled, time-stamped cross-sectional batches Accurate pseudo-time trajectories already exist and a pseudo-time-based method (SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) is preferred for the analysis

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain known or suspected heterogeneous cell populations (e.g., developmental stages E3–E7 or lineage compartments like ICM/PE/EPI vs TE) that should be recovered as separable clusters in a low-dimensional 2D visualization.
skills.name: cell-subpopulation-identification-in-2d-embedding
skills.search_text: cell-subpopulation-identification-in-2d-embedding Use when scRNA-seq data contain known or suspected heterogeneous cell populations (e.g., developmental stages E3–E7 or lineage compartments like ICM/PE/EPI vs TE) that should be recovered as separable clusters in a low-dimensional 2D visualization. The input is bulk RNA-seq or already a low-dimensional feature table — VASC's Gumbel-based dropout modeling targets single-cell data where zero and near-zero dropout events dominate. The goal is a precise, deterministic coordinate output for downstream quantitative comparison rather than exploratory visualization — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation in the dimension reduction. Prior knowledge is too limited to choose the embedding dimension — the determination of the optimal dimension is described as a tricky task without prior knowledge. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Identify and visually validate cell sub-populations and lineages by inspecting the 2D embedding produced by VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models scRNA-seq dropout events (zero and near-zero values) via a Gumbel distribution. The 2D representation recovers known populations more precisely than PCA, ZIFA, and SIMLR and more completely than t-SNE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.08.003
skills.summary: Identify and visually validate cell sub-populations and lineages by inspecting the 2D embedding produced by VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models scRNA-seq dropout events (zero and near-zero values) via a Gumbel distribution. The 2D representation recovers known populations more precisely than PCA, ZIFA, and SIMLR and more completely than t-SNE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq or already a low-dimensional feature table — VASC's Gumbel-based dropout modeling targets single-cell data where zero and near-zero dropout events dominate. The goal is a precise, deterministic coordinate output for downstream quantitative comparison rather than exploratory visualization — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation in the dimension reduction. Prior knowledge is too limited to choose the embedding dimension — the determination of the optimal dimension is described as a tricky task without prior knowledge.

skills.description: Use when you need to test how sensitive CCC inference methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, Connectome, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, Cytotalk via LIANA) are to cell-level noise—reduced cell numbers or erroneous cell-type annotation—in a scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.name: cell-subsampling-and-label-shuffling
skills.search_text: cell-subsampling-and-label-shuffling Use when you need to test how sensitive CCC inference methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, Connectome, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, Cytotalk via LIANA) are to cell-level noise—reduced cell numbers or erroneous cell-type annotation—in a scRNA-seq dataset. Your goal is biological CCC prediction itself, not robustness assessment—this skill only perturbs inputs and re-scores, it does not yield novel interaction calls. You are evaluating methods that additionally infer intracellular processes (NicheNet, Cytotalk's full model, SoptSC), which the paper states are 'not directly comparable' and were excluded from the comparable framework. Your noise concern is in the prior-knowledge resource rather than the data—use the selective/non-selective interaction-replacement ablation instead, which perturbs the resource, not the cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A robustness-to-noise ablation for cell-cell communication (CCC) inference: perturb single-cell RNA-seq inputs by subsampling cells (0-40%) and reshuffling cell-type labels (0-40%), then re-run CCC methods through LIANA and quantify how the top-250 interaction ranking changes relative to the unperturbed baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: A robustness-to-noise ablation for cell-cell communication (CCC) inference: perturb single-cell RNA-seq inputs by subsampling cells (0-40%) and reshuffling cell-type labels (0-40%), then re-run CCC methods through LIANA and quantify how the top-250 interaction ranking changes relative to the unperturbed baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is biological CCC prediction itself, not robustness assessment—this skill only perturbs inputs and re-scores, it does not yield novel interaction calls. You are evaluating methods that additionally infer intracellular processes (NicheNet, Cytotalk's full model, SoptSC), which the paper states are 'not directly comparable' and were excluded from the comparable framework. Your noise concern is in the prior-knowledge resource rather than the data—use the selective/non-selective interaction-replacement ablation instead, which perturbs the resource, not the cells.

skills.description: Use when a heterogeneous PBMC scRNA-seq object has coarse reference-based (SingleR) lineage labels — e.g. a T/NK subset — and the goal is to recluster that subset to expose rare subtypes or doublets hidden by the annotation.
skills.name: cell-subset-filtering-by-reference-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-subset-filtering-by-reference-annotation Use when a heterogeneous PBMC scRNA-seq object has coarse reference-based (SingleR) lineage labels — e.g. a T/NK subset — and the goal is to recluster that subset to expose rare subtypes or doublets hidden by the annotation. The input is already a purified, single-cell-type population with no coarse reference annotation to refine — direct clustering without subsetting is appropriate. The annotation reference panel already contains platelet and RBC transcriptomes, so reference-based labels alone resolve the contaminating cell types (the paper notes mis-classification arose from their absence). The goal is whole-dataset deconvolution rather than deconvolving a pre-annotated subset — run feature selection/clustering on all cells instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Subset a scRNA-seq Seurat object to the cells assigned to a lineage (here the SingleR-annotated T/NK compartment of rheumatoid arthritis PBMCs, 5329 of 8312 cells) so that downstream feature selection and clustering (DUBStepR) can deconvolve substructure — including platelet and RBC 'contaminants' that the reference annotation missed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Subset a scRNA-seq Seurat object to the cells assigned to a lineage (here the SingleR-annotated T/NK compartment of rheumatoid arthritis PBMCs, 5329 of 8312 cells) so that downstream feature selection and clustering (DUBStepR) can deconvolve substructure — including platelet and RBC 'contaminants' that the reference annotation missed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a purified, single-cell-type population with no coarse reference annotation to refine — direct clustering without subsetting is appropriate. The annotation reference panel already contains platelet and RBC transcriptomes, so reference-based labels alone resolve the contaminating cell types (the paper notes mis-classification arose from their absence). The goal is whole-dataset deconvolution rather than deconvolving a pre-annotated subset — run feature selection/clustering on all cells instead.

skills.description: Use when you need to characterize computational scaling (wall-clock time, peak memory) of MaCroDNA, clonealign, or Seurat on patient-stratified scDNA/scRNA data by re-running at controlled sampling rates such as 0.5–1.0.
skills.name: cell-subset-resampling-across-patients
skills.search_text: cell-subset-resampling-across-patients Use when you need to characterize computational scaling (wall-clock time, peak memory) of MaCroDNA, clonealign, or Seurat on patient-stratified scDNA/scRNA data by re-running at controlled sampling rates such as 0.5–1.0. The goal is assignment accuracy rather than computational cost — use the CRC ground-truth cell-to-clone and clonal-prevalence evaluation instead The dataset lacks paired patient-stratified scDNA/scRNA samples, so within-patient stratified subsampling is not meaningful Only probabilistic assignment confidence is of interest — MaCroDNA (and hence this benchmark target) provides no probabilistic confidence measures unlike clonealign http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark how a cross-modality single-cell method's runtime and peak memory scale with input size by repeatedly subsampling paired scRNA-seq/scDNA-seq cells within each patient at fixed fractions and re-running the association step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Benchmark how a cross-modality single-cell method's runtime and peak memory scale with input size by repeatedly subsampling paired scRNA-seq/scDNA-seq cells within each patient at fixed fractions and re-running the association step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assignment accuracy rather than computational cost — use the CRC ground-truth cell-to-clone and clonal-prevalence evaluation instead The dataset lacks paired patient-stratified scDNA/scRNA samples, so within-patient stratified subsampling is not meaningful Only probabilistic assignment confidence is of interest — MaCroDNA (and hence this benchmark target) provides no probabilistic confidence measures unlike clonealign

skills.description: Use when a normalized single-cell tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix needs cell subtype labels beyond the five major TME types, using pretrained subtype templates rather than reference-free clustering.

skills.search_text: cell-subtype-fine-annotation-with-template-classifiers Use when a normalized single-cell tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix needs cell subtype labels beyond the five major TME types, using pretrained subtype templates rather than reference-free clustering. Input is raw (unnormalized) count data — predCellType operates on the LogNormalize-normalized RNA @data matrix, not raw counts Non-tumor scRNA-seq data or cell types outside the TME major types covered by the package-shipped templates (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial) Spatial transcriptomic spots requiring the scCancer2 spatial module rather than single-cell subtype templates http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fine-grained tumor microenvironment cell subtype annotation using scCancer2's two-stage supervised framework: a rough label from predCellType (e.g., five major cell types: T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial) followed by runCellSubtypeClassify, which trains lightweight machine-learning classifiers on package-shipped cellSubtypeTemplates.rds subtype templates and marker files per major type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Fine-grained tumor microenvironment cell subtype annotation using scCancer2's two-stage supervised framework: a rough label from predCellType (e.g., five major cell types: T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial) followed by runCellSubtypeClassify, which trains lightweight machine-learning classifiers on package-shipped cellSubtypeTemplates.rds subtype templates and marker files per major type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unnormalized) count data — predCellType operates on the LogNormalize-normalized RNA @data matrix, not raw counts Non-tumor scRNA-seq data or cell types outside the TME major types covered by the package-shipped templates (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial) Spatial transcriptomic spots requiring the scCancer2 spatial module rather than single-cell subtype templates

skills.name: cell-subtype-similarity-map-construction
skills.search_text: cell-subtype-similarity-map-construction Use when fine cell subtype annotations from different published references must be related quantitatively, or when subtypes from a reference (e.g., the PBMC multimodal reference) must be transferred onto tumor-derived cells and compared across datasets. When only rough level-1 labels are needed and no cross-reference subtype comparison or transfer is intended (predCellType alone suffices) When the input is spatial transcriptomics spots lacking single-cell resolution and no reference subtype map is being evaluated When datasets lack sufficient expressed marker genes to support classifier-based subtype classification, making similarity estimates unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantitative construction of similarity maps between cell subtype labels defined in different published references by testing pretrained classifiers across scRNA-seq datasets (15 datasets, 594 samples in scCancer2), enabling cross-reference label harmonization and reference-based subtype transfer (e.g., mapping Hao et al. 2021 PBMC subtypes onto tumor samples). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028

skills.description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object from tumor tissue needs fine-grained cell subtype labels within the five TME compartments (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial), or when cross-dataset subtype label similarity must be quantified.
skills.name: cell-subtype-supervised-classification
skills.search_text: cell-subtype-supervised-classification Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object from tumor tissue needs fine-grained cell subtype labels within the five TME compartments (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial), or when cross-dataset subtype label similarity must be quantified. The goal is de novo clustering/discovery of novel cell states rather than assigning cells to the five predefined TME compartments with known subtypes The data are spatial transcriptomics spots or bulk RNA-seq samples — use scCancer2's spatial module or the xgboost malignant-cell classifier instead No compatible reference templates or marker files exist for the tissue/cancer type, so the supervised classifiers cannot be trusted without retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A supervised machine-learning framework in scCancer2 that annotates tumor microenvironment (TME) cells to fine subtypes by training multinomial classifiers per compartment across 15 scRNA-seq datasets (594 samples, 1,213,469 cells), and supports cross-dataset label similarity maps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: A supervised machine-learning framework in scCancer2 that annotates tumor microenvironment (TME) cells to fine subtypes by training multinomial classifiers per compartment across 15 scRNA-seq datasets (594 samples, 1,213,469 cells), and supports cross-dataset label similarity maps.
