skills.description: Use when you have SClineager genotype-inference outputs (inferred VAF matrix and covariance from run_sclineager) and need to partition cells into lineages based on similarity of inferred genotypes.
skills.name: cell-to-cell-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-to-cell-correlation-analysis Use when you have SClineager genotype-inference outputs (inferred VAF matrix and covariance from run_sclineager) and need to partition cells into lineages based on similarity of inferred genotypes. The input is raw VAF data before SClineager's Bayesian imputation — expressional drop-outs (low coverage, allelic bias) make raw correlations unreliable; run genotype inference first. You need mutation/variant calling rather than lineage assignment — use the QBRC Somatic Pipeline on scSplitter-split single-cell files instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assigns single cells to evolutionary lineages by computing a cell-to-cell Pearson correlation matrix over SClineager's imputed/inferred VAF genotypes, converting correlations to distances, and detecting lineages via hierarchical clustering. This exploits SClineager's Bayesian MCMC imputation, which mitigates expressional drop-outs before clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108589
skills.summary: Assigns single cells to evolutionary lineages by computing a cell-to-cell Pearson correlation matrix over SClineager's imputed/inferred VAF genotypes, converting correlations to distances, and detecting lineages via hierarchical clustering. This exploits SClineager's Bayesian MCMC imputation, which mitigates expressional drop-outs before clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw VAF data before SClineager's Bayesian imputation — expressional drop-outs (low coverage, allelic bias) make raw correlations unreliable; run genotype inference first. You need mutation/variant calling rather than lineage assignment — use the QBRC Somatic Pipeline on scSplitter-split single-cell files instead.

skills.description: Use when you have imputed (or raw) gene-by-cell count matrices plus cell type labels and need to measure whether dropout recovery improves same-cell-type Pearson correlation and clustering separation without over-homogenizing cell types.
skills.name: cell-to-cell-pearson-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-to-cell-pearson-correlation-analysis Use when you have imputed (or raw) gene-by-cell count matrices plus cell type labels and need to measure whether dropout recovery improves same-cell-type Pearson correlation and clustering separation without over-homogenizing cell types. Input is a bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated expression profile — the same/different-cell-type Pearson comparison requires single-cell matrices with known cell labels No cell type labels or cluster assignments exist — silhouette scoring with true labels is undefined and only unsupervised ARI/Jaccard/NMI/purity workflows apply The goal is differential expression or pseudotime benchmarking rather than assessing cell-to-cell relationship recovery, which the article evaluates separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes same-cell-type versus different-cell-type Pearson correlations of imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (plus silhouette scores with true labels) to quantify whether imputation recovers cell-to-cell relationships, as used to benchmark Bfimpute against scImpute, SAVER, VIPER, DrImpute, MAGIC, PBLR, ALRA, and mcImpute on Chu, Tang, Petropoulos, and Zheng datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Computes same-cell-type versus different-cell-type Pearson correlations of imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (plus silhouette scores with true labels) to quantify whether imputation recovers cell-to-cell relationships, as used to benchmark Bfimpute against scImpute, SAVER, VIPER, DrImpute, MAGIC, PBLR, ALRA, and mcImpute on Chu, Tang, Petropoulos, and Zheng datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated expression profile — the same/different-cell-type Pearson comparison requires single-cell matrices with known cell labels No cell type labels or cluster assignments exist — silhouette scoring with true labels is undefined and only unsupervised ARI/Jaccard/NMI/purity workflows apply The goal is differential expression or pseudotime benchmarking rather than assessing cell-to-cell relationship recovery, which the article evaluates separately

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering pipeline needs a dense, undirected cell-to-cell similarity matrix: the ADMM-learned coefficient matrix is sparse and asymmetric, and zero entries must be imputed (Weighted Adamic/Adar over KNN) before spectral clustering.
skills.name: cell-to-cell-similarity-matrix-symmetrization
skills.search_text: cell-to-cell-similarity-matrix-symmetrization Use when a scRNA-seq clustering pipeline needs a dense, undirected cell-to-cell similarity matrix: the ADMM-learned coefficient matrix is sparse and asymmetric, and zero entries must be imputed (Weighted Adamic/Adar over KNN) before spectral clustering. The input is already a dense, symmetric affinity matrix produced by another framework (e.g., MPSSC's Gaussian-kernel doubly stochastic affinity matrices) — no sparse-subspace learning or symmetrization step is needed. Very large-scale scRNA-seq datasets: SSRE is 'relatively time-consuming in large-scale datasets' and parallel acceleration is only proposed as future work, so runtime may be prohibitive. Single-cell multi-omics integration tasks: the paper only proposes multi-view clustering as a possible future trend, not an implemented capability. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds the SSRE cell-to-cell similarity matrix for scRNA-seq data: the sparse self-expression coefficient matrix learned via ADMM is symmetrized into an undirected sparse similarity (simsparse), then enhanced with Pearson correlation, Jaccard, and cosine similarities plus modified Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation over K-nearest neighbors to recover marked missing entries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Builds the SSRE cell-to-cell similarity matrix for scRNA-seq data: the sparse self-expression coefficient matrix learned via ADMM is symmetrized into an undirected sparse similarity (simsparse), then enhanced with Pearson correlation, Jaccard, and cosine similarities plus modified Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation over K-nearest neighbors to recover marked missing entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a dense, symmetric affinity matrix produced by another framework (e.g., MPSSC's Gaussian-kernel doubly stochastic affinity matrices) — no sparse-subspace learning or symmetrization step is needed. Very large-scale scRNA-seq datasets: SSRE is 'relatively time-consuming in large-scale datasets' and parallel acceleration is only proposed as future work, so runtime may be prohibitive. Single-cell multi-omics integration tasks: the paper only proposes multi-view clustering as a possible future trend, not an implemented capability.

skills.description: Use when you have matched scDNA-seq copy-number data, scRNA-seq gene-expression data, and a clone-label table mapping each DNA cell to a clone id, and you need to predict which clone each RNA cell belongs to.
skills.name: cell-to-clone-assignment
skills.search_text: cell-to-clone-assignment Use when you have matched scDNA-seq copy-number data, scRNA-seq gene-expression data, and a clone-label table mapping each DNA cell to a clone id, and you need to predict which clone each RNA cell belongs to. You only have DNA and RNA data without clone labels and want cell-to-cell rather than cell-to-clone mapping — use MaCroDNA's cell2cell_assignment() instead The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g., healthy or low-grade tissue), where matching cells is distinctively challenging and assignments are unreliable You require probabilistic confidence measures on assignments — MaCroDNA does not provide them, unlike variational methods such as clonealign http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Assign scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq clones by running MaCroDNA's cell2clone_assignment(), which maximizes the sum of per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients between RNA expression and DNA copy-number profiles via a Gurobi-solved weighted bipartite matching. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Assign scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq clones by running MaCroDNA's cell2clone_assignment(), which maximizes the sum of per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients between RNA expression and DNA copy-number profiles via a Gurobi-solved weighted bipartite matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have DNA and RNA data without clone labels and want cell-to-cell rather than cell-to-clone mapping — use MaCroDNA's cell2cell_assignment() instead The sample is biologically homogeneous (e.g., healthy or low-grade tissue), where matching cells is distinctively challenging and assignments are unreliable You require probabilistic confidence measures on assignments — MaCroDNA does not provide them, unlike variational methods such as clonealign

skills.description: Use when a landmark-labeled low-dimensional expression matrix is available and you must quantify neighborhood-based cell state transitions between landmark pairs to build a weighted transition graph.
skills.name: cell-to-landmark-pair-assignment
skills.search_text: cell-to-landmark-pair-assignment Use when a landmark-labeled low-dimensional expression matrix is available and you must quantify neighborhood-based cell state transitions between landmark pairs to build a weighted transition graph. Landmarks or landmark cell definitions have not yet been defined (run the upstream Mpath landmark-definition stage first) Cells are still in high-dimensional raw expression space without the low-dimensional embedding Mpath operates on The analysis starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support such development processes (planned future extension) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Assigns each low-dimensional cell to the pair of Mpath landmark states that are its two nearest landmarks, then counts cells per landmark pair to weight candidate state-transition edges between landmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Assigns each low-dimensional cell to the pair of Mpath landmark states that are its two nearest landmarks, then counts cells per landmark pair to weight candidate state-transition edges between landmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Landmarks or landmark cell definitions have not yet been defined (run the upstream Mpath landmark-definition stage first) Cells are still in high-dimensional raw expression space without the low-dimensional embedding Mpath operates on The analysis starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support such development processes (planned future extension)

skills.description: Use when single-cell coordinates with marker intensities (e.g. MCMICRO-processed CyCIF data in an AnnData object) must be annotated with region labels derived from marker-defined cell populations like SOX10+ tumor cells.
skills.name: cell-to-region-assignment
skills.search_text: cell-to-region-assignment Use when single-cell coordinates with marker intensities (e.g. MCMICRO-processed CyCIF data in an AnnData object) must be annotated with region labels derived from marker-defined cell populations like SOX10+ tumor cells. Data are not spatially resolved single-cell coordinates (e.g. bulk or plate-based readouts with no x/y positions) — boundary construction and point-to-region assignment have no geometric input Cells are already annotated with region labels, so the goal is downstream measurement rather than assignment — go directly to spatialcells.msmt functions like getRegionComposition or getMPI The aim is neighborhood graph analysis of spatial data rather than region delineation — the paper positions Squidpy as the specialized toolkit for neighborhood graph construction and analysis Assigns each of the ~1.1M single cells in an ROI to exactly one named spatial region using SpatialCells' boundary-derived regions (getBoundary/assignPointsToRegions), enabling region-based TME measurements such as area, cell density, region composition, and tumor isolation index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Assigns each of the ~1.1M single cells in an ROI to exactly one named spatial region using SpatialCells' boundary-derived regions (getBoundary/assignPointsToRegions), enabling region-based TME measurements such as area, cell density, region composition, and tumor isolation index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not spatially resolved single-cell coordinates (e.g. bulk or plate-based readouts with no x/y positions) — boundary construction and point-to-region assignment have no geometric input Cells are already annotated with region labels, so the goal is downstream measurement rather than assignment — go directly to spatialcells.msmt functions like getRegionComposition or getMPI The aim is neighborhood graph analysis of spatial data rather than region delineation — the paper positions Squidpy as the specialized toolkit for neighborhood graph construction and analysis

skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on a branching (bifurcating) dataset with close, fine lineages, where purity of cell-to-trajectory assignments and per-path pseudotime accuracy must be quantified.
skills.name: cell-to-trajectory-assignment-entropy-scoring
skills.search_text: cell-to-trajectory-assignment-entropy-scoring Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on a branching (bifurcating) dataset with close, fine lineages, where purity of cell-to-trajectory assignments and per-path pseudotime accuracy must be quantified. The dataset has no branching structure (e.g., linear or cycle trajectories) — entropy scoring after the branching point is undefined or uninformative. No ground-truth trajectory labels are available, since purity of cell-to-trajectory assignments cannot be judged without the simulated truth. You need cluster-level trajectories only (e.g., Directed-PAGA output); entropy scoring is designed for cell-level assignment purity on fine, close lineages. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the normalized average entropy score of cell-to-trajectory assignments after the branching point to quantify how purely a trajectory inference method (CellPath, VeTra, or Slingshot) assigns cells from the same true trajectory to the same inferred path. Used together with per-path Kendall rank correlations of pseudotime to benchmark methods on a dyngen bifurcating dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Computes the normalized average entropy score of cell-to-trajectory assignments after the branching point to quantify how purely a trajectory inference method (CellPath, VeTra, or Slingshot) assigns cells from the same true trajectory to the same inferred path. Used together with per-path Kendall rank correlations of pseudotime to benchmark methods on a dyngen bifurcating dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no branching structure (e.g., linear or cycle trajectories) — entropy scoring after the branching point is undefined or uninformative. No ground-truth trajectory labels are available, since purity of cell-to-trajectory assignments cannot be judged without the simulated truth. You need cluster-level trajectories only (e.g., Directed-PAGA output); entropy scoring is designed for cell-level assignment purity on fine, close lineages.

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples were grown under different differentiation media (e.g. UNC vs SC air-liquid interface cultures) and you need to verify or estimate cell type composition shifts, such as ciliated vs secretory cell abundance, from gene signatures rather than deconvolution tools.
skills.name: cell-type-abundance-comparison-across-culture-media
skills.search_text: cell-type-abundance-comparison-across-culture-media Use when bulk RNA-seq samples were grown under different differentiation media (e.g. UNC vs SC air-liquid interface cultures) and you need to verify or estimate cell type composition shifts, such as ciliated vs secretory cell abundance, from gene signatures rather than deconvolution tools. Input data is single-cell rather than bulk transcriptomics — rROMA cell-type abundance estimation here targets bulk expression matrices The expression matrix is raw counts — rRoma works with normalized data (cpm or vst), so normalization must happen first The goal is pathway activity (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK sets) rather than cell-type composition estimation from signature gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Estimate cell-type abundances in bulk RNA-seq data by running rROMA with cell-type signature gene sets (e.g. Plasschaert and Okuda airway epithelium signatures) and comparing module sample scores between culture-medium groups (UNC vs SC) to confirm expected ciliated/secretory abundance patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Estimate cell-type abundances in bulk RNA-seq data by running rROMA with cell-type signature gene sets (e.g. Plasschaert and Okuda airway epithelium signatures) and comparing module sample scores between culture-medium groups (UNC vs SC) to confirm expected ciliated/secretory abundance patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is single-cell rather than bulk transcriptomics — rROMA cell-type abundance estimation here targets bulk expression matrices The expression matrix is raw counts — rRoma works with normalized data (cpm or vst), so normalization must happen first The goal is pathway activity (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK sets) rather than cell-type composition estimation from signature gene sets

skills.description: Use when building a supervised cell-type annotation model from a reference scRNA-seq matrix whose cell-type counts are imbalanced, and minority types risk being ignored during training.
skills.name: cell-type-abundance-thresholding
skills.search_text: cell-type-abundance-thresholding Use when building a supervised cell-type annotation model from a reference scRNA-seq matrix whose cell-type counts are imbalanced, and minority types risk being ignored during training. Input is a query dataset to be annotated — balancing is applied to the reference data during training, not to query cells Cell-type counts are already balanced or rare types exceed the 1,000-cell cap, so oversampling would add redundant synthetic cells The downstream method does not train a supervised classifier on the reference (e.g., marker-based methods like Garnett or SCINA), where imbalanced abundances matter less http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Flags cell types in a single-cell reference expression matrix as rare based on abundance thresholds (100/500/1000 cells, chosen as a function of Nmax) and oversamples them with SMOTE so classifiers do not ignore minority cell types, as done in SELINA's cell-type balancing step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Flags cell types in a single-cell reference expression matrix as rare based on abundance thresholds (100/500/1000 cells, chosen as a function of Nmax) and oversamples them with SMOTE so classifiers do not ignore minority cell types, as done in SELINA's cell-type balancing step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a query dataset to be annotated — balancing is applied to the reference data during training, not to query cells Cell-type counts are already balanced or rare types exceed the 1,000-cell cap, so oversampling would add redundant synthetic cells The downstream method does not train a supervised classifier on the reference (e.g., marker-based methods like Garnett or SCINA), where imbalanced abundances matter less

skills.description: Use when per-cell pluripotency/differentiation scores from multiple methods (ORIGINS, LandSCENT, CytoTRACE) must be averaged within annotated cell types and their orderings compared for consistency, e.g. on the breast epithelial sample.
skills.name: cell-type-aggregate-score-verification
skills.search_text: cell-type-aggregate-score-verification Use when per-cell pluripotency/differentiation scores from multiple methods (ORIGINS, LandSCENT, CytoTRACE) must be averaged within annotated cell types and their orderings compared for consistency, e.g. on the breast epithelial sample. The expression matrix is not oriented as genes (rows) x cells (columns) or is not normalized — the ORIGINS activity() function expects that layout and the PyOrigins formula normalizes by edge count and mean cell expression The goal is PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — use ORIGINS2 or PyOrigins with a custom PPIN instead of the bundled differentiation_edges Only a single scoring method is used with no cross-method ordering to verify — the skill's core value is comparing rank orderings across ORIGINS, LandSCENT and CytoTRACE http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 A verification procedure that aggregates per-cell pluripotency scores (ORIGINS activity, activity-HVF, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) within annotated cell types of the breast epithelial scRNA-seq dataset (GSE113197) and cross-checks whether the methods produce consistent cell-type orderings, flagging disagreement such as CytoTRACE ranking L1 > L2 > basal while ORIGINS/LandSCENT rank basal highest. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: A verification procedure that aggregates per-cell pluripotency scores (ORIGINS activity, activity-HVF, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) within annotated cell types of the breast epithelial scRNA-seq dataset (GSE113197) and cross-checks whether the methods produce consistent cell-type orderings, flagging disagreement such as CytoTRACE ranking L1 > L2 > basal while ORIGINS/LandSCENT rank basal highest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is not oriented as genes (rows) x cells (columns) or is not normalized — the ORIGINS activity() function expects that layout and the PyOrigins formula normalizes by edge count and mean cell expression The goal is PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — use ORIGINS2 or PyOrigins with a custom PPIN instead of the bundled differentiation_edges Only a single scoring method is used with no cross-method ordering to verify — the skill's core value is comparing rank orderings across ORIGINS, LandSCENT and CytoTRACE

skills.description: Use when per-cell stemness scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) have been computed on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need per-type averages and rankings to benchmark which method correctly identifies stem cells.
skills.name: cell-type-aggregation-of-per-cell-scores
skills.search_text: cell-type-aggregation-of-per-cell-scores Use when per-cell stemness scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) have been computed on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need per-type averages and rankings to benchmark which method correctly identifies stem cells. When no cell-type annotations exist — aggregation requires a prior per-cell type label; use the scores directly or perform clustering/annotation first When the goal is trajectory inference rather than benchmarking — ORIGINS scores are intended to select origin cells, and aggregation into per-type means discards single-cell resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Aggregate per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) into average scores per annotated cell type with dplyr, then rank cell types to assess whether expected stem/progenitor populations attain the highest scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Aggregate per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) into average scores per annotated cell type with dplyr, then rank cell types to assess whether expected stem/progenitor populations attain the highest scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no cell-type annotations exist — aggregation requires a prior per-cell type label; use the scores directly or perform clustering/annotation first When the goal is trajectory inference rather than benchmarking — ORIGINS scores are intended to select origin cells, and aggregation into per-type means discards single-cell resolution

skills.description: Use when a large cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference (.h5ad) must be reduced to a representative sketch to serve as the reference matrix for deconvolution of pseudobulk/bulk RNA-seq samples, and sketch quality must be judged by proportion-estimate accuracy.
skills.name: cell-type-annotated-reference-construction
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotated-reference-construction Use when a large cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference (.h5ad) must be reduced to a representative sketch to serve as the reference matrix for deconvolution of pseudobulk/bulk RNA-seq samples, and sketch quality must be judged by proportion-estimate accuracy. The goal is annotation-quality model training (e.g. scANVI/CellTypist label transfer) rather than serving as a deconvolution reference matrix No cell-type labels are available in the scRNA-seq reference, since MuSiC needs cell-type-stratified reference profiles The input is already a compact reference matrix with no need for subsampling http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds a cell-type-annotated single-cell reference matrix from a sketched scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. a scValue sketch of the two-donor A29/A31 T&ILC reference) and uses it as the reference profile for MuSiC bulk RNA-seq deconvolution, benchmarking subsampling methods by accuracy of inferred cell-type proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Builds a cell-type-annotated single-cell reference matrix from a sketched scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. a scValue sketch of the two-donor A29/A31 T&ILC reference) and uses it as the reference profile for MuSiC bulk RNA-seq deconvolution, benchmarking subsampling methods by accuracy of inferred cell-type proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation-quality model training (e.g. scANVI/CellTypist label transfer) rather than serving as a deconvolution reference matrix No cell-type labels are available in the scRNA-seq reference, since MuSiC needs cell-type-stratified reference profiles The input is already a compact reference matrix with no need for subsampling

skills.description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GEO/E-MTAB pancreas, PBMC) must be used to annotate one or more independent testing studies and per-method annotation accuracy needs to be quantified across all train-test combinations.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-comparison Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GEO/E-MTAB pancreas, PBMC) must be used to annotate one or more independent testing studies and per-method annotation accuracy needs to be quantified across all train-test combinations. The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is restricted to settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest, so a supervised method cannot be trained and unsupervised approaches are the only viable solution The data likely contain rare/unknown or malignant cells that should be removed first (e.g., with inferCNV or copyKAT) before exhaustive label assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark supervised cell-type annotation accuracy across cross-study scRNA-seq train/test scenarios (e.g., the four human pancreas datasets Baron, Muraro, Seg, Xin) by training NeuCA alongside scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, and CHETAH on the same reference and comparing predicted labels to published ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Benchmark supervised cell-type annotation accuracy across cross-study scRNA-seq train/test scenarios (e.g., the four human pancreas datasets Baron, Muraro, Seg, Xin) by training NeuCA alongside scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, and CHETAH on the same reference and comparing predicted labels to published ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is restricted to settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest, so a supervised method cannot be trained and unsupervised approaches are the only viable solution The data likely contain rare/unknown or malignant cells that should be removed first (e.g., with inferCNV or copyKAT) before exhaustive label assignment

skills.description: Use when a trained cell-type annotation model (e.g. a DNN on .h5ad scRNA-seq data) must be scored against ground-truth labels on a held-out test set, or when comparing annotation tools for accuracy and run feasibility on large datasets (>0.6M cells).
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-evaluation Use when a trained cell-type annotation model (e.g. a DNN on .h5ad scRNA-seq data) must be scored against ground-truth labels on a held-out test set, or when comparing annotation tools for accuracy and run feasibility on large datasets (>0.6M cells). The dataset has no ground-truth cell-type labels in adata.obs (no 'target' column), so no held-out test accuracy can be computed. The goal is biomarker/feature discovery rather than annotation accuracy — feature importance extraction is not available for comparison tools (scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, cellPLM), limiting downstream comparability. The input has not been preprocessed to the expected format (log1p normalization, range 0-10); scaLR's performance may vary based on the input data format. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Evaluates trained cell-type annotation models on a held-out test set of scRNA-seq data using precision, recall, f1-score, and accuracy, and benchmarks competing annotation pipelines (e.g. CellTypist, devCellPy, scBalance, cellPLM) under a fixed resource budget such as 128 GB RAM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Evaluates trained cell-type annotation models on a held-out test set of scRNA-seq data using precision, recall, f1-score, and accuracy, and benchmarks competing annotation pipelines (e.g. CellTypist, devCellPy, scBalance, cellPLM) under a fixed resource budget such as 128 GB RAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth cell-type labels in adata.obs (no 'target' column), so no held-out test accuracy can be computed. The goal is biomarker/feature discovery rather than annotation accuracy — feature importance extraction is not available for comparison tools (scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, cellPLM), limiting downstream comparability. The input has not been preprocessed to the expected format (log1p normalization, range 0-10); scaLR's performance may vary based on the input data format.

skills.description: Use when GeneVector phenotype_probability annotations must be trusted before downstream analyses like latent-space arithmetic; trigger when an independent label source (e.g., CellAssign) exists for concordance checking.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-validation
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-validation Use when GeneVector phenotype_probability annotations must be trusted before downstream analyses like latent-space arithmetic; trigger when an independent label source (e.g., CellAssign) exists for concordance checking. No independent label source (e.g., CellAssign output) is available for concordance comparison — validation would be circular Cell type composition differs drastically between batches, making batch correction vectors unreliable and annotations unverifiable against known signatures The goal is metagene discovery or gene similarity ranking rather than assigning cell identity to individual cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates GeneVector latent-space cell type annotations (via CellEmbedding.phenotype_probability with marker gene sets) against independent CellAssign labels, confirming annotation reliability before downstream vector-arithmetic analyses such as the HGSOC adnexa-vs-bowel metagene comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Validates GeneVector latent-space cell type annotations (via CellEmbedding.phenotype_probability with marker gene sets) against independent CellAssign labels, confirming annotation reliability before downstream vector-arithmetic analyses such as the HGSOC adnexa-vs-bowel metagene comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent label source (e.g., CellAssign output) is available for concordance comparison — validation would be circular Cell type composition differs drastically between batches, making batch correction vectors unreliable and annotations unverifiable against known signatures The goal is metagene discovery or gene similarity ranking rather than assigning cell identity to individual cells

skills.description: Use when reproducing Table 1-style accuracy comparisons of cell type annotators across multiple tissue scRNA-seq datasets, or when evaluating how sequencing depth affects single-cell annotation accuracy on a labeled test set.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-benchmarking Use when reproducing Table 1-style accuracy comparisons of cell type annotators across multiple tissue scRNA-seq datasets, or when evaluating how sequencing depth affects single-cell annotation accuracy on a labeled test set. The query involves cancer cells, since deCS is expected to struggle due to expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells The goal is discovering novel cell types, since deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Input cells are not human, as the built-in references (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF) are human-only panels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark deCS cell type annotation against state-of-the-art tools (SingleR, CHETAH, scPred, SciBet, Cell BLAST, etc.) across eight test scRNA-seq datasets and on single-cell-level annotation of the COVID-19 bronchoalveolar immune cell dataset, stratified by sequencing depth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Benchmark deCS cell type annotation against state-of-the-art tools (SingleR, CHETAH, scPred, SciBet, Cell BLAST, etc.) across eight test scRNA-seq datasets and on single-cell-level annotation of the COVID-19 bronchoalveolar immune cell dataset, stratified by sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query involves cancer cells, since deCS is expected to struggle due to expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells The goal is discovering novel cell types, since deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Input cells are not human, as the built-in references (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF) are human-only panels

skills.name: cell-type-annotation-by-gsea
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-by-gsea Use when you have Seurat cluster marker lists (only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) from scRNA-seq data and need automated, database-backed cell-type annotation for each cluster. Input is already a curated cell-type feature/reference table rather than differential-expression marker lists from clustering — no Seurat-derived markers to query Working with species or tissues outside the supported marker databases (EasyCellType/CellMarker coverage is human/mouse-oriented; scCATCH's CellMatch covers human and mouse references) Only a single-cell expression matrix is available with no cluster identities — annotation is per-cluster, so clustering and marker calling must precede this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate scRNA-seq clusters by running EasyCellType's GSEA test on Seurat-derived cluster markers (FindAllMarkers with logfc.threshold=0.25) against the CellMarker database, using gene ranking rather than simple list overlap to recover biologically consistent cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Annotate scRNA-seq clusters by running EasyCellType's GSEA test on Seurat-derived cluster markers (FindAllMarkers with logfc.threshold=0.25) against the CellMarker database, using gene ranking rather than simple list overlap to recover biologically consistent cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated cell-type feature/reference table rather than differential-expression marker lists from clustering — no Seurat-derived markers to query Working with species or tissues outside the supported marker databases (EasyCellType/CellMarker coverage is human/mouse-oriented; scCATCH's CellMatch covers human and mouse references) Only a single-cell expression matrix is available with no cluster identities — annotation is per-cluster, so clustering and marker calling must precede this skill

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cluster assignments produced by an unsupervised method (e.g. scBGEDA) lack cell-type labels and a curated marker database such as CellMark can be matched against per-cluster DEGs.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-from-marker-genes
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-from-marker-genes Use when scRNA-seq cluster assignments produced by an unsupervised method (e.g. scBGEDA) lack cell-type labels and a curated marker database such as CellMark can be matched against per-cluster DEGs. The input data has no cluster labels and clustering itself is the goal — scBGEDA's pipeline (preprocess.py, SDDA.py, BC.m) produces the consensus clusters that this annotation step consumes. The clusters of interest show no overlap with any known markers in the curated database — assignment would be unsupported guesswork. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table without per-cell data — per-cluster Wilcoxon rank-sum testing on cells is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assigns biological cell-type labels to unsupervised scBGEDA clusters by running per-cluster differential expression (Wilcoxon rank-sum, top 20 genes at P<0.05 in scanpy) and matching the nominated marker genes to the CellMark curated marker database (e.g. fibroblast markers Gsn, Col3a1, Col1a2, Mmp2 on the QS_Heart dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Assigns biological cell-type labels to unsupervised scBGEDA clusters by running per-cluster differential expression (Wilcoxon rank-sum, top 20 genes at P<0.05 in scanpy) and matching the nominated marker genes to the CellMark curated marker database (e.g. fibroblast markers Gsn, Col3a1, Col1a2, Mmp2 on the QS_Heart dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data has no cluster labels and clustering itself is the goal — scBGEDA's pipeline (preprocess.py, SDDA.py, BC.m) produces the consensus clusters that this annotation step consumes. The clusters of interest show no overlap with any known markers in the curated database — assignment would be unsupported guesswork. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table without per-cell data — per-cluster Wilcoxon rank-sum testing on cells is not applicable.

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq object (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) needs cell-type labels from lineage signature gene sets rather than marker-gene inspection or reference mapping.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-from-signature-scores
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-from-signature-scores Use when a normalized scRNA-seq object (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) needs cell-type labels from lineage signature gene sets rather than marker-gene inspection or reference mapping. When only 10x Cell Ranger raw outputs are available — the object must already contain normalized UMIs after normalize_UMIs When the biological system lacks relevant curated signatures and customized gene sets would have to be compiled from scratch When reference-based label transfer (e.g., via Seurat interop) is required — SingCellaR lacks automatic object transformation to interact with packages such as Seurat http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assign per-cell lineage labels by computing AUCell enrichment scores for curated signature gene sets (GMT) within SingCellaR, then applying gene-set-specific AUC cutoffs and visualizing the annotations on UMAP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Assign per-cell lineage labels by computing AUCell enrichment scores for curated signature gene sets (GMT) within SingCellaR, then applying gene-set-specific AUC cutoffs and visualizing the annotations on UMAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only 10x Cell Ranger raw outputs are available — the object must already contain normalized UMIs after normalize_UMIs When the biological system lacks relevant curated signatures and customized gene sets would have to be compiled from scratch When reference-based label transfer (e.g., via Seurat interop) is required — SingCellaR lacks automatic object transformation to interact with packages such as Seurat

skills.description: Use when you have a rooted lineage tree in Newick plus per-cell cell-type labels and want to quantify which cell types co-occur within subtrees (e.g., after cutting the LinRace embryo tree at depth 26).
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-mapping Use when you have a rooted lineage tree in Newick plus per-cell cell-type labels and want to quantify which cell types co-occur within subtrees (e.g., after cutting the LinRace embryo tree at depth 26). You need to reconstruct or compare full lineage trees rather than summarize cell-type composition of existing tree subtrees (use tree reconstruction/RF or Nye similarity workflows instead). Cell-type labels are not available for the tree tips, so no per-subtree composition table can be computed. The tree is unrooted or lacks branch-length information, making depth-based cutting ill-defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Maps per-cell annotated cell-type labels onto leaves of a reconstructed lineage tree (e.g., LinRace's mouse embryo tree with 9707 cells and 34 annotated cell types), then tabulates per-subtree cell-type composition to test consistency between transcriptome similarity and barcode similarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Maps per-cell annotated cell-type labels onto leaves of a reconstructed lineage tree (e.g., LinRace's mouse embryo tree with 9707 cells and 34 annotated cell types), then tabulates per-subtree cell-type composition to test consistency between transcriptome similarity and barcode similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to reconstruct or compare full lineage trees rather than summarize cell-type composition of existing tree subtrees (use tree reconstruction/RF or Nye similarity workflows instead). Cell-type labels are not available for the tree tips, so no per-subtree composition table can be computed. The tree is unrooted or lacks branch-length information, making depth-based cutting ill-defined.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (genes x cells) must be paired with a cell-annotation metafile before running NATMI ExtractEdges.py, or when cell-type labels need to be validated so edges are attributed to the right cell types.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-mapping Use when a single-cell expression matrix (genes x cells) must be paired with a cell-annotation metafile before running NATMI ExtractEdges.py, or when cell-type labels need to be validated so edges are attributed to the right cell types. The input is bulk transcriptomics or proteomic data — the cell-labels metafile is required only for single-cell analysis, where cell-to-type mapping applies The expression matrix is spatial-resolved data — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data, so mapping cells to histological locations is out of scope Cell annotations are unavailable or untrustworthy — the paper notes using original authors' annotations 'can potentially affect the accuracy of predicted networks' http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepare the cell-labels metafile that maps each cell barcode in a single-cell expression matrix to a cell-type label, so NATMI's ExtractEdges.py can aggregate expression per cell type and predict cell-to-cell communication edges. Correct barcode-to-label mapping is a prerequisite for computing per-cell-type detection rates, mean-expression weights, and specificity weights. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Prepare the cell-labels metafile that maps each cell barcode in a single-cell expression matrix to a cell-type label, so NATMI's ExtractEdges.py can aggregate expression per cell type and predict cell-to-cell communication edges. Correct barcode-to-label mapping is a prerequisite for computing per-cell-type detection rates, mean-expression weights, and specificity weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk transcriptomics or proteomic data — the cell-labels metafile is required only for single-cell analysis, where cell-to-type mapping applies The expression matrix is spatial-resolved data — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data, so mapping cells to histological locations is out of scope Cell annotations are unavailable or untrustworthy — the paper notes using original authors' annotations 'can potentially affect the accuracy of predicted networks'

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-by-factor or low-dimensional embedding from paired multi-omics data (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq PBMC) and need per-cell type labels grounded in canonical gene/protein markers plus an independent reference annotation.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-marker-genes
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-marker-genes Use when you have a cell-by-factor or low-dimensional embedding from paired multi-omics data (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq PBMC) and need per-cell type labels grounded in canonical gene/protein markers plus an independent reference annotation. Input is raw counts without normalization (RNA should first be normalized to 10,000 counts and log1p-transformed; ADT CLR-normalized via Muon) The goal is de novo marker discovery rather than annotation of known populations against canonical markers and a reference Data lack a credible reference (e.g., non-human PBMC) where Azimuth-based cross-validation of marker-based labels cannot support the assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotates cell types in single-cell embeddings by building a kNN graph, clustering with Leiden, and assigning labels from canonical gene and protein markers, cross-confirmed against an independent reference mapping (e.g., Azimuth PBMC reference). Used in the Mowgli paper to obtain cell-type labels on TEA-seq that enable factor-specificity analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Annotates cell types in single-cell embeddings by building a kNN graph, clustering with Leiden, and assigning labels from canonical gene and protein markers, cross-confirmed against an independent reference mapping (e.g., Azimuth PBMC reference). Used in the Mowgli paper to obtain cell-type labels on TEA-seq that enable factor-specificity analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts without normalization (RNA should first be normalized to 10,000 counts and log1p-transformed; ADT CLR-normalized via Muon) The goal is de novo marker discovery rather than annotation of known populations against canonical markers and a reference Data lack a credible reference (e.g., non-human PBMC) where Azimuth-based cross-validation of marker-based labels cannot support the assignment

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a cell type annotation tool's accuracy on reference-to-query label transfer, or when assessing whether annotation performance depends on expert-knowledge masks vs. parameter-matched random masks.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-model-evaluation Use when benchmarking a cell type annotation tool's accuracy on reference-to-query label transfer, or when assessing whether annotation performance depends on expert-knowledge masks vs. parameter-matched random masks. The input is a single pre-computed accuracy table without per-epoch training curves or dataset metadata, so neither convergence nor correlation analysis can be reproduced The task is to annotate a new query dataset (use TOSICA.pre for prediction, not this evaluation skill) Reference and query var_names are inconsistent or unordered differently — the mask-comparison evaluation would be invalid until genes are aligned http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A reusable evaluation protocol for cell type annotation models (e.g., TOSICA) that reproduces convergence comparisons between knowledge-based and random masks and correlates dataset characteristics (size, cell type count, entropy, DKL) with annotation accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: A reusable evaluation protocol for cell type annotation models (e.g., TOSICA) that reproduces convergence comparisons between knowledge-based and random masks and correlates dataset characteristics (size, cell type count, entropy, DKL) with annotation accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single pre-computed accuracy table without per-epoch training curves or dataset metadata, so neither convergence nor correlation analysis can be reproduced The task is to annotate a new query dataset (use TOSICA.pre for prediction, not this evaluation skill) Reference and query var_names are inconsistent or unordered differently — the mask-comparison evaluation would be invalid until genes are aligned

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how subsampling/sketching (e.g. scValue sketches at 0.02–0.10 fractions) affects supervised cell-type annotation accuracy on .h5ad scRNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth labels.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-model-training
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-model-training Use when benchmarking how subsampling/sketching (e.g. scValue sketches at 0.02–0.10 fractions) affects supervised cell-type annotation accuracy on .h5ad scRNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth labels. The dataset has no original cell-type annotations, so predicted labels cannot be validated against ground truth The goal is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution or cross-study label transfer rather than supervised annotation accuracy benchmarking Input features are raw counts without Scanpy preprocessing (HVG + PCA), which scValue and the annotation models expect http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains/runs dataset-designated automatic cell-type annotation models (scANVI, scPoli, CellTypist, ACTINN) on scRNA-seq references — full data or scValue/baseline sketches at 2%–10% fractions — and scores predicted labels against original annotations to benchmark subsampling impact on downstream ML/DL tasks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Trains/runs dataset-designated automatic cell-type annotation models (scANVI, scPoli, CellTypist, ACTINN) on scRNA-seq references — full data or scValue/baseline sketches at 2%–10% fractions — and scores predicted labels against original annotations to benchmark subsampling impact on downstream ML/DL tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no original cell-type annotations, so predicted labels cannot be validated against ground truth The goal is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution or cross-study label transfer rather than supervised annotation accuracy benchmarking Input features are raw counts without Scanpy preprocessing (HVG + PCA), which scValue and the annotation models expect

skills.description: Use when confident cell type labels from a consensus of annotation tools must be spread to unlabeled cells in scRNA-seq data via a graph convolutional network, or when tuning GCN hyperparameters per dataset.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-model-training
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-model-training Use when confident cell type labels from a consensus of annotation tools must be spread to unlabeled cells in scRNA-seq data via a graph convolutional network, or when tuning GCN hyperparameters per dataset. When no confident labels exist yet — the GCN is semi-supervised and depends on the consensus step producing highly confident label assignments first When a simple nonparametric neighbor majority approach suffices — the paper shows it gives comparable results to the GCN When the input is already processed/normalized embeddings rather than raw counts, since the pipeline expects raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the scSHARP semi-supervised GCN (EdgeConv layers in PyTorch) to propagate confident consensus cell type labels across an scRNA-seq cell-neighbor graph, sweeping batch size b, neighbors k, layer count l, and embedding size e to select the highest-validation-accuracy architecture. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Train the scSHARP semi-supervised GCN (EdgeConv layers in PyTorch) to propagate confident consensus cell type labels across an scRNA-seq cell-neighbor graph, sweeping batch size b, neighbors k, layer count l, and embedding size e to select the highest-validation-accuracy architecture.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no confident labels exist yet — the GCN is semi-supervised and depends on the consensus step producing highly confident label assignments first When a simple nonparametric neighbor majority approach suffices — the paper shows it gives comparable results to the GCN When the input is already processed/normalized embeddings rather than raw counts, since the pipeline expects raw counts

skills.description: Use when you must quantify resource/accuracy trade-offs of cell type annotation pipelines on identical feature subsets of an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., reproducing a Table-3-style comparison of accuracy, memory, and execution time).
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-pipeline-comparison-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-pipeline-comparison-benchmarking Use when you must quantify resource/accuracy trade-offs of cell type annotation pipelines on identical feature subsets of an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., reproducing a Table-3-style comparison of accuracy, memory, and execution time). When the goal is biomarker discovery or DGE analysis (e.g., pseudo bulk / LMEM volcano plots) rather than comparing pipeline accuracy, time, and memory When you need feature importance / top features from the comparison tools themselves — the article notes features cannot be extracted, or there is no explanation of how, from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and CellPLM models When input data is not preprocessed into the expected anndata .h5ad format (log1p-normalized adata.X, cell metadata in adata.obs with a target column) — data-format dependence requires user preprocessing first http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scaLR against alternative single-cell annotation pipelines (scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM, scBalance, CellAssign, etc.) by running each on the same top-3,500 scaLR-extracted features of a scRNA-seq dataset and comparing test accuracy, wall-clock time, and peak memory in a single table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Benchmark scaLR against alternative single-cell annotation pipelines (scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM, scBalance, CellAssign, etc.) by running each on the same top-3,500 scaLR-extracted features of a scRNA-seq dataset and comparing test accuracy, wall-clock time, and peak memory in a single table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biomarker discovery or DGE analysis (e.g., pseudo bulk / LMEM volcano plots) rather than comparing pipeline accuracy, time, and memory When you need feature importance / top features from the comparison tools themselves — the article notes features cannot be extracted, or there is no explanation of how, from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and CellPLM models When input data is not preprocessed into the expected anndata .h5ad format (log1p-normalized adata.X, cell metadata in adata.obs with a target column) — data-format dependence requires user preprocessing first

skills.description: Use when comparing imputed vs. unimputed scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., Jurkat-293T or Zeisel datasets) to assess whether imputation improves clustering of annotated cell-type subpopulations, as in Fig. 5 of the AutoImpute paper.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-plotting
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-plotting Use when comparing imputed vs. unimputed scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., Jurkat-293T or Zeisel datasets) to assess whether imputation improves clustering of annotated cell-type subpopulations, as in Fig. 5 of the AutoImpute paper. The expression matrix has no cell-type annotations, so silhouette scoring against a defined k is impossible. The goal is dropout detection or expression recovery from subsampled data rather than post-imputation cell-type separability assessment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify and visualize cell-type separability in scRNA-seq data by projecting log-transformed expression matrices (before and after imputation) into 2D PCA space colored by cell-type annotations, and computing average silhouette scores to compare imputation methods such as AutoImpute, scImpute, drImpute, and MAGIC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Quantify and visualize cell-type separability in scRNA-seq data by projecting log-transformed expression matrices (before and after imputation) into 2D PCA space colored by cell-type annotations, and computing average silhouette scores to compare imputation methods such as AutoImpute, scImpute, drImpute, and MAGIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has no cell-type annotations, so silhouette scoring against a defined k is impossible. The goal is dropout detection or expression recovery from subsampled data rather than post-imputation cell-type separability assessment.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., from Seurat) need automatic, knowledge-free cell type annotation by scoring cluster marker genes against a tissue-specific cell taxonomy reference database rather than manual marker inspection.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-scoring-against-reference-database
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-scoring-against-reference-database Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., from Seurat) need automatic, knowledge-free cell type annotation by scoring cluster marker genes against a tissue-specific cell taxonomy reference database rather than manual marker inspection. The cell types, species, or tissue of the sample are poorly represented in the CellMatch reference database — the article notes limited reference content can lead to incorrect cell type annotation Clustering itself is inadequate (too many or too few clusters), since clustering errors propagate into annotation The task is cell-level annotation rather than cluster-level annotation, e.g., comparing against cell-based methods like SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, or CHETAH http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate single-cell RNA-seq clusters automatically by identifying cluster marker genes and scoring candidate cell types against the tissue-specific CellMatch taxonomy database (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) with an evidence-based score, assigning the top-1 (highest-scoring) cell type per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell RNA-seq clusters automatically by identifying cluster marker genes and scoring candidate cell types against the tissue-specific CellMatch taxonomy database (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) with an evidence-based score, assigning the top-1 (highest-scoring) cell type per cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell types, species, or tissue of the sample are poorly represented in the CellMatch reference database — the article notes limited reference content can lead to incorrect cell type annotation Clustering itself is inadequate (too many or too few clusters), since clustering errors propagate into annotation The task is cell-level annotation rather than cluster-level annotation, e.g., comparing against cell-based methods like SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, or CHETAH

skills.description: Use when combining scRNA-seq studies whose free-text cell annotations differ, e.g. before rendering a cross-study comparison of expression across aligned cell types in Cellenium (H5AD-imported studies with ontologized metadata).
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-standardization
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-standardization Use when combining scRNA-seq studies whose free-text cell annotations differ, e.g. before rendering a cross-study comparison of expression across aligned cell types in Cellenium (H5AD-imported studies with ontologized metadata). The analysis is within a single study only — Cellenium's per-study features (UMAP exploration, differential expression on annotated clusters) do not require cross-study label alignment. Cell annotations need to be created de novo from plot selections rather than harmonized — use Cellenium's interactive cell annotation feature for adding user-defined cell types instead. Input studies already share one ontologized cell-type vocabulary, so remapping would be a no-op. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aligns heterogeneous cell annotations from different scRNA-seq studies to a shared, standardized cell-type vocabulary — the CellO-predicted ontology used by Cellenium — so that corresponding cell types from different studies map to shared labels and can be compared within one visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Aligns heterogeneous cell annotations from different scRNA-seq studies to a shared, standardized cell-type vocabulary — the CellO-predicted ontology used by Cellenium — so that corresponding cell types from different studies map to shared labels and can be compared within one visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is within a single study only — Cellenium's per-study features (UMAP exploration, differential expression on annotated clusters) do not require cross-study label alignment. Cell annotations need to be created de novo from plot selections rather than harmonized — use Cellenium's interactive cell annotation feature for adding user-defined cell types instead. Input studies already share one ontologized cell-type vocabulary, so remapping would be a no-op.

skills.description: Use when semi-profiled single-cell data (e.g. scSemiProfiler output for a COVID-19 cohort with Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical conditions) is unlabeled, and annotated representative single-cell reference data exists to train a classifier for label transfer.
skills.name: cell-type-annotation-transfer-with-mlp-classifier
skills.search_text: cell-type-annotation-transfer-with-mlp-classifier Use when semi-profiled single-cell data (e.g. scSemiProfiler output for a COVID-19 cohort with Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical conditions) is unlabeled, and annotated representative single-cell reference data exists to train a classifier for label transfer. No annotated single-cell reference is available — scSemiProfiler's deconvolution and classifier-based annotation require a single-cell reference sample Input is already fully annotated bulk deconvolution output where only cell-type-level resolution is needed (conventional methods such as CIBERSORTx or DWLS suffice) Data modalities beyond scRNA-seq (e.g. proteomics) are involved — extension to other modalities is not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Transfers cell-type labels from annotated representative single-cell data to semi-profiled (AI-inferred) single-cell data by training a scikit-learn MLP classifier on the reference annotations, enabling per-sample and per-condition cell-type proportion comparison between semi-profiled and real-profiled cohorts (e.g. COVID-19 severity conditions). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Transfers cell-type labels from annotated representative single-cell data to semi-profiled (AI-inferred) single-cell data by training a scikit-learn MLP classifier on the reference annotations, enabling per-sample and per-condition cell-type proportion comparison between semi-profiled and real-profiled cohorts (e.g. COVID-19 severity conditions).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No annotated single-cell reference is available — scSemiProfiler's deconvolution and classifier-based annotation require a single-cell reference sample Input is already fully annotated bulk deconvolution output where only cell-type-level resolution is needed (conventional methods such as CIBERSORTx or DWLS suffice) Data modalities beyond scRNA-seq (e.g. proteomics) are involved — extension to other modalities is not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. a 428k-cell gut atlas in .h5ad) must be subsampled to a fixed sketch size while preserving cell-type diversity and rare populations for downstream annotation/ML tasks.
skills.name: cell-type-balanced-subset-allocation
skills.search_text: cell-type-balanced-subset-allocation Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. a 428k-cell gut atlas in .h5ad) must be subsampled to a fixed sketch size while preserving cell-type diversity and rare populations for downstream annotation/ML tasks. The AnnData has no cell type labels and no PCA representation (scValue fits the random forest on features from adata.obsm['X_pca'] by default and needs cell_type_key). The goal is geometry/distribution-preserving sketching via distance optimization (GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler maximize distance or structure rather than OOB data value) rather than value-based, cell-type-balanced selection. The input is a small dataset where subsampling is unnecessary — scValue targets datasets scaling from tens of thousands to millions of cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Produces cell-type-balanced sketches of large scRNA-seq AnnData objects by scoring each cell with a random-forest out-of-bag (OOB) 'data value' (DV), allocating sketch size across cell types with DV-weighted weighting, and selecting cells via DV-guided binning. Used to make datasets like the 428k-cell human gut reference tractable for downstream ML tasks such as CellTypist label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Produces cell-type-balanced sketches of large scRNA-seq AnnData objects by scoring each cell with a random-forest out-of-bag (OOB) 'data value' (DV), allocating sketch size across cell types with DV-weighted weighting, and selecting cells via DV-guided binning. Used to make datasets like the 428k-cell human gut reference tractable for downstream ML tasks such as CellTypist label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData has no cell type labels and no PCA representation (scValue fits the random forest on features from adata.obsm['X_pca'] by default and needs cell_type_key). The goal is geometry/distribution-preserving sketching via distance optimization (GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler maximize distance or structure rather than OOB data value) rather than value-based, cell-type-balanced selection. The input is a small dataset where subsampling is unnecessary — scValue targets datasets scaling from tens of thousands to millions of cells.

skills.description: Use when a trained scRNA-seq cell-type classifier (e.g. scaLR DNN on anndata .h5ad data) must be converted into per-class ranked gene lists, or when top-100 biomarkers must be checked for recall against a curated reference like CellMarker2.0.
skills.name: cell-type-biomarker-ranking-extraction
skills.search_text: cell-type-biomarker-ranking-extraction Use when a trained scRNA-seq cell-type classifier (e.g. scaLR DNN on anndata .h5ad data) must be converted into per-class ranked gene lists, or when top-100 biomarkers must be checked for recall against a curated reference like CellMarker2.0. The comparison tool does not expose feature importance — the paper notes features cannot be extracted from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and CellPLM models, so classwise ranking is impossible for those baselines The goal is differential expression between clinical conditions (e.g. COVID-19 vs normal) rather than class-specific markers — use the scaLR DgePseudoBulk or DgeLMEM modules instead Input is raw unnormalized counts or non-anndata formats — the pipeline expects .h5ad with adata.X containing normalized (log1p, 0-10) gene counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract per-cell-type ranked biomarker lists from trained scaLR classifier models using the scalr.feature.selector modules (classwise_abs / abs_mean) over LinearScorer weight matrices, then validate the top-100 markers against CellMarker2.0 reference sets via gene recall curves. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Extract per-cell-type ranked biomarker lists from trained scaLR classifier models using the scalr.feature.selector modules (classwise_abs / abs_mean) over LinearScorer weight matrices, then validate the top-100 markers against CellMarker2.0 reference sets via gene recall curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison tool does not expose feature importance — the paper notes features cannot be extracted from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and CellPLM models, so classwise ranking is impossible for those baselines The goal is differential expression between clinical conditions (e.g. COVID-19 vs normal) rather than class-specific markers — use the scaLR DgePseudoBulk or DgeLMEM modules instead Input is raw unnormalized counts or non-anndata formats — the pipeline expects .h5ad with adata.X containing normalized (log1p, 0-10) gene counts

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics and an annotated single-cell Seurat object are available and the goal is to rank predefined cell types for trait/disease association at FDR < 0.05 (e.g., AD vs. OPCs/microglia, severe COVID-19 vs. PBMC subsets).
skills.name: cell-type-bootstrap-association-testing
skills.search_text: cell-type-bootstrap-association-testing Use when GWAS summary statistics and an annotated single-cell Seurat object are available and the goal is to rank predefined cell types for trait/disease association at FDR < 0.05 (e.g., AD vs. OPCs/microglia, severe COVID-19 vs. PBMC subsets). The scRNA-seq object lacks cell-type annotations or clusters fall below min_clustercells = 10, so cell-type-level t-statistics cannot be estimated The analysis target is single-cell-level p-values or trait-relevant gene prioritization (use scPagwas' singlecell scoring via Get_CorrectBg_p and scGet_PCC instead of the cell-type bootstrap) GWAS and scRNA-seq come from mismatched genome builds without the matching block_annotation (hg37 vs hg38), so SNP-to-gene/pathway block assignment would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scPagwas cell-type-level association testing: after pathway SVD transformation and polygenic regression of GWAS summary statistics against pathway-annotated scRNA-seq data, a block bootstrap over pathway-based genome blocks (200 iterations by default) estimates per-cell-type significance for trait associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: scPagwas cell-type-level association testing: after pathway SVD transformation and polygenic regression of GWAS summary statistics against pathway-annotated scRNA-seq data, a block bootstrap over pathway-based genome blocks (200 iterations by default) estimates per-cell-type significance for trait associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq object lacks cell-type annotations or clusters fall below min_clustercells = 10, so cell-type-level t-statistics cannot be estimated The analysis target is single-cell-level p-values or trait-relevant gene prioritization (use scPagwas' singlecell scoring via Get_CorrectBg_p and scGet_PCC instead of the cell-type bootstrap) GWAS and scRNA-seq come from mismatched genome builds without the matching block_annotation (hg37 vs hg38), so SNP-to-gene/pathway block assignment would be invalid

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been produced and reference cell-type labels exist, and you need ARI plus per-cell-type classification accuracy (e.g., alpha/beta cells) to quantify clustering fidelity.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-accuracy-assessment Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been produced and reference cell-type labels exist, and you need ARI plus per-cell-type classification accuracy (e.g., alpha/beta cells) to quantify clustering fidelity. No reference cell-type labels are available for the dataset, so neither ARI nor classification accuracy can be computed. The method produces hard-only cluster assignments without soft probabilities, precluding high-confidence cell selection via maximum assignment probability. The goal is batch-effect removal or embedding quality assessment (e.g., regional KL divergence of batch mixing) rather than cell-type label recovery. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assesses how accurately a clustering result recovers known cell types by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against reference labels and, using DESC's soft cluster assignment probabilities, the classification accuracy of high-confidence cells for specific cell types (e.g., alpha and beta cells in pancreatic islet data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Assesses how accurately a clustering result recovers known cell types by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against reference labels and, using DESC's soft cluster assignment probabilities, the classification accuracy of high-confidence cells for specific cell types (e.g., alpha and beta cells in pancreatic islet data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference cell-type labels are available for the dataset, so neither ARI nor classification accuracy can be computed. The method produces hard-only cluster assignments without soft probabilities, precluding high-confidence cell selection via maximum assignment probability. The goal is batch-effect removal or embedding quality assessment (e.g., regional KL divergence of batch mixing) rather than cell-type label recovery.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type classifiers on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need repeatable accuracy and balanced-accuracy estimates for SciBet, scmap, and Seurat v3 across many datasets.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-accuracy-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-accuracy-computation Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type classifiers on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need repeatable accuracy and balanced-accuracy estimates for SciBet, scmap, and Seurat v3 across many datasets. Input data lacks curated cell-type labels, so a supervised hold-out benchmark cannot be run Goal is rejecting cells of unknown type rather than measuring classification accuracy — use SciBet's confidence score C (likelihood ratio vs a null dataset, cutoffs 0.001 to 0.5) instead of plain accuracy Input is a small single-dataset query where a full 50-repeat cross-validation benchmark across 14 datasets is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the SciBet-vs-baseline cell-type classification benchmark: 50 repeats of stratified 7:3 hold-out splits on 14 scRNA-seq datasets, E-test feature selection of the top 500 informative genes, and accuracy/balanced-accuracy comparison of SciBet against scmapCluster and Seurat v3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Reproduces the SciBet-vs-baseline cell-type classification benchmark: 50 repeats of stratified 7:3 hold-out splits on 14 scRNA-seq datasets, E-test feature selection of the top 500 informative genes, and accuracy/balanced-accuracy comparison of SciBet against scmapCluster and Seurat v3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks curated cell-type labels, so a supervised hold-out benchmark cannot be run Goal is rejecting cells of unknown type rather than measuring classification accuracy — use SciBet's confidence score C (likelihood ratio vs a null dataset, cutoffs 0.001 to 0.5) instead of plain accuracy Input is a small single-dataset query where a full 50-repeat cross-validation benchmark across 14 datasets is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when a labeled single-cell RNA-seq AnnData (cell x gene, 'class_label' column) needs automated cell-type label transfer with measurable accuracy/F1, including imbalanced, many-class (e.g., 42-type mouse brain) or small-training-set settings.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-evaluation Use when a labeled single-cell RNA-seq AnnData (cell x gene, 'class_label' column) needs automated cell-type label transfer with measurable accuracy/F1, including imbalanced, many-class (e.g., 42-type mouse brain) or small-training-set settings. Trans-species label transfer: the authors limited work to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Completely unlabeled data with no expert annotations: SIMS is supervised and relies on pre-existing normalization, clustering, differential expression, and expert annotation Input matrices in gene x cell orientation, or raw unnormalized counts not log1p-transformed as required by the pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and quantitatively evaluate the SIMS (TabNet-based) single-cell RNA-seq label-transfer classifier on annotated .h5ad datasets, reporting held-out accuracy and Macro F1 under 80/20 splits, trans-sample splits, and training-set ablations (e.g., 7% of cells / 3,285 cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Train and quantitatively evaluate the SIMS (TabNet-based) single-cell RNA-seq label-transfer classifier on annotated .h5ad datasets, reporting held-out accuracy and Macro F1 under 80/20 splits, trans-sample splits, and training-set ablations (e.g., 7% of cells / 3,285 cells).
