skills.when_to_use_negative: Trans-species label transfer: the authors limited work to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Completely unlabeled data with no expert annotations: SIMS is supervised and relies on pre-existing normalization, clustering, differential expression, and expert annotation Input matrices in gene x cell orientation, or raw unnormalized counts not log1p-transformed as required by the pipeline

skills.description: Use when you have a set of k selected marker genes on a labeled scRNA-seq AnnData object and need to quantify how well those markers discriminate cell types via classifier performance.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-evaluation Use when you have a set of k selected marker genes on a labeled scRNA-seq AnnData object and need to quantify how well those markers discriminate cell types via classifier performance. You need to evaluate whole-transcriptome reconstruction quality rather than cell-type discriminative power of a marker subset — MarkerMap also supports reconstruction, but this skill only covers classification metrics. Your data has no cell type labels — supervised evaluation via new_model_metrics requires adata.obs[group_by] annotations. You are comparing marker selection methods at very small k where a simple classifier on k markers is not the paper's evaluation regime (the benchmark is defined over a range of k values, e.g. k=50). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates selected gene marker sets by training simple classifiers (Random Forest / nearest-neighbor) restricted to the k markers and measuring accuracy and weighted F1 on held-out test cells, following the MarkerMap benchmarking protocol for scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Evaluates selected gene marker sets by training simple classifiers (Random Forest / nearest-neighbor) restricted to the k markers and measuring accuracy and weighted F1 on held-out test cells, following the MarkerMap benchmarking protocol for scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to evaluate whole-transcriptome reconstruction quality rather than cell-type discriminative power of a marker subset — MarkerMap also supports reconstruction, but this skill only covers classification metrics. Your data has no cell type labels — supervised evaluation via new_model_metrics requires adata.obs[group_by] annotations. You are comparing marker selection methods at very small k where a simple classifier on k markers is not the paper's evaluation regime (the benchmark is defined over a range of k values, e.g. k=50).

skills.description: Use when comparing cell type annotation models on a held-out test set and you need donor-generalizing performance metrics such as macro F1-score and cross-entropy loss.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-macro-f1-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-macro-f1-evaluation Use when comparing cell type annotation models on a held-out test set and you need donor-generalizing performance metrics such as macro F1-score and cross-entropy loss. Evaluating on a random (cell-level) split where the same donors appear in train and test — this allows donor-level label leakage and inflates scores relative to the unseen-donor protocol Datasets with cell types present in fewer than 30 donors or fewer than 5000 cells, where per-cell-type F1 and donor-generalization cannot be reliably quantified Single-tissue, single-donor benchmarks where cross-tissue macro F1 is not the target of comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates cross-tissue cell type classifiers (e.g., scTab/TabNet vs. a linear reference) on an unseen-donor test set using macro F1-score (per-cell-type F1 averaged over cell types) and cross-entropy loss, following the scTab benchmark protocol on the CELLxGENE-derived corpus. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Evaluates cross-tissue cell type classifiers (e.g., scTab/TabNet vs. a linear reference) on an unseen-donor test set using macro F1-score (per-cell-type F1 averaged over cell types) and cross-entropy loss, following the scTab benchmark protocol on the CELLxGENE-derived corpus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating on a random (cell-level) split where the same donors appear in train and test — this allows donor-level label leakage and inflates scores relative to the unseen-donor protocol Datasets with cell types present in fewer than 30 donors or fewer than 5000 cells, where per-cell-type F1 and donor-generalization cannot be reliably quantified Single-tissue, single-donor benchmarks where cross-tissue macro F1 is not the target of comparison

skills.description: Use when comparing or benchmarking the running time of automatic scRNA-seq cell-type identification methods on subsets of varying training/testing sizes, e.g. reproducing the Fig. 4 speed ranking on the mouse brain dataset GSE116470.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing or benchmarking the running time of automatic scRNA-seq cell-type identification methods on subsets of varying training/testing sizes, e.g. reproducing the Fig. 4 speed ranking on the mouse brain dataset GSE116470. The goal is accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate, or new cell-type identification performance rather than running-time scaling The dataset is not a single scRNA-seq expression matrix with labels (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, proteomics) — cell-type identification classifiers do not apply Only one fixed training/testing size is available, so no runtime scaling curve over dataset sizes can be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark the computation time of automatic cell-type identification methods for scRNA-seq across varying training-set (500–10,000 cells) and testing-set (1,000–50,000 cells) sizes, using the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R wrapper, to rank methods by prediction speed (as in Fig. 4 of the paper). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Benchmark the computation time of automatic cell-type identification methods for scRNA-seq across varying training-set (500–10,000 cells) and testing-set (1,000–50,000 cells) sizes, using the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R wrapper, to rank methods by prediction speed (as in Fig. 4 of the paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate, or new cell-type identification performance rather than running-time scaling The dataset is not a single scRNA-seq expression matrix with labels (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, proteomics) — cell-type identification classifiers do not apply Only one fixed training/testing size is available, so no runtime scaling curve over dataset sizes can be constructed

skills.description: Use when reproducing the LUAD/HCC827-H1975-H2228 scRNA-seq clustering benchmark across three platforms with the 2267 common HVGs, or when comparing ARI of unsupervised batch-correction clustering to published values.
skills.name: cell-type-clustering-ari-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-type-clustering-ari-benchmarking Use when reproducing the LUAD/HCC827-H1975-H2228 scRNA-seq clustering benchmark across three platforms with the 2267 common HVGs, or when comparing ARI of unsupervised batch-correction clustering to published values. The data are bulk RNA-seq where batch correction methods like ComBat and SVA apply, not scRNA-seq counts with unknown subtypes The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures types 3 and 4), where no method is applicable Cell-type labels are fully known a priori and the goal is only correction, not simultaneous clustering of unknown subtypes http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark cell-type clustering accuracy of BUSseq against batch-effect-correction methods (LIGER, MNN, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat, ZINB-WaVE, CellAssign) on the LUAD three-cell-line sc_mixology dataset (CEL-seq2, 10x Chromium, Drop-seq), scoring adjusted Rand index against known cell-line identities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-type clustering accuracy of BUSseq against batch-effect-correction methods (LIGER, MNN, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat, ZINB-WaVE, CellAssign) on the LUAD three-cell-line sc_mixology dataset (CEL-seq2, 10x Chromium, Drop-seq), scoring adjusted Rand index against known cell-line identities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk RNA-seq where batch correction methods like ComBat and SVA apply, not scRNA-seq counts with unknown subtypes The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures types 3 and 4), where no method is applicable Cell-type labels are fully known a priori and the goal is only correction, not simultaneous clustering of unknown subtypes

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-Seq matrix has been corrected for the cell-cycle effect and you must verify that cell-type signal was retained while cell-cycle heterogeneity was removed, comparing original vs corrected matrices.
skills.name: cell-type-clustering-assessment
skills.search_text: cell-type-clustering-assessment Use when an scRNA-Seq matrix has been corrected for the cell-cycle effect and you must verify that cell-type signal was retained while cell-cycle heterogeneity was removed, comparing original vs corrected matrices. The dataset has very low cell-cycle activity, as in the Patel et al. human glioblastoma data, where the article notes the effect is minimal and only a smaller cutoff CΔ = 2 is warranted — assessment of cell-cycle removal is largely moot. The goal is to remove other confounders (batch, mitochondrial, technical effects): ccRemover removes only the cell-cycle effect, so an odds-ratio comparison against it will not diagnose other dominant sources of variation. There are no known cell-type or cell-cycle stage labels, so the hypergeometric odds-ratio / majority-class validation has no ground truth to enrich against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A benchmarking skill for judging whether a cell-cycle correction (ccRemover vs scLVM) preserves or improves cell-type separation in scRNA-Seq data, using matched clustering plus statistical tests (t-test at FDR 0.01, hypergeometric odds ratio) on original and corrected matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for judging whether a cell-cycle correction (ccRemover vs scLVM) preserves or improves cell-type separation in scRNA-Seq data, using matched clustering plus statistical tests (t-test at FDR 0.01, hypergeometric odds ratio) on original and corrected matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has very low cell-cycle activity, as in the Patel et al. human glioblastoma data, where the article notes the effect is minimal and only a smaller cutoff CΔ = 2 is warranted — assessment of cell-cycle removal is largely moot. The goal is to remove other confounders (batch, mitochondrial, technical effects): ccRemover removes only the cell-cycle effect, so an odds-ratio comparison against it will not diagnose other dominant sources of variation. There are no known cell-type or cell-cycle stage labels, so the hypergeometric odds-ratio / majority-class validation has no ground truth to enrich against.

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq read count matrices from multiple batches contain cell types that are unknown a priori, and clustering plus batch-effect correction must be performed jointly without preliminary normalization.
skills.name: cell-type-clustering-unknown-subtypes
skills.search_text: cell-type-clustering-unknown-subtypes Use when raw scRNA-seq read count matrices from multiple batches contain cell types that are unknown a priori, and clustering plus batch-effect correction must be performed jointly without preliminary normalization. Cell-type labels for every cell are already known a priori — methods like ComBat or SVA designed for bulk experiments with subtype information suffice The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g. batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2 while batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no method is applicable All subtypes are known to be present in each batch and a simpler method such as MetaSparseKmeans would apply; BUSseq is aimed at unknown subtypes and designs allowing cell types to be missing from some batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simultaneously cluster scRNA-seq cells into unknown cell types and correct batch effects by fitting BUSseq, an interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model, via multi-core MCMC with K selected by BIC comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Simultaneously cluster scRNA-seq cells into unknown cell types and correct batch effects by fitting BUSseq, an interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model, via multi-core MCMC with K selected by BIC comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels for every cell are already known a priori — methods like ComBat or SVA designed for bulk experiments with subtype information suffice The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g. batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2 while batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no method is applicable All subtypes are known to be present in each batch and a simpler method such as MetaSparseKmeans would apply; BUSseq is aimed at unknown subtypes and designs allowing cell types to be missing from some batches

skills.description: Use when a 2D ivis embedding of scRNA-seq data has been computed and you need to visually validate cell-type segregation and global cluster relationships against published figures.
skills.name: cell-type-colored-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-type-colored-embedding-visualization Use when a 2D ivis embedding of scRNA-seq data has been computed and you need to visually validate cell-type segregation and global cluster relationships against published figures. The embedding has no annotated cell-type labels, so coloring and cluster-segregation validation cannot be performed The goal is quantifying local neighborhood accuracy rather than visual/structural inspection — use the Mantel test or SVM classifier evaluation instead of scatter plots alone t-SNE or other DR outputs with random-noise sensitivity are being interpreted — the paper warns t-SNE 'tends to yield spurious clusters with clean boundaries', so plots should not be assumed structure-preserving without ivis http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates 2D scatter plots of ivis embeddings of scRNA-seq datasets (hippocampus, metastatic melanoma, retinal bipolar) with cells colored by annotated cell type, to verify that cell types form distinct clusters and that global relationships (e.g. hippocampal information flow from dentate gyrus to CA3 and CA1) are preserved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Generates 2D scatter plots of ivis embeddings of scRNA-seq datasets (hippocampus, metastatic melanoma, retinal bipolar) with cells colored by annotated cell type, to verify that cell types form distinct clusters and that global relationships (e.g. hippocampal information flow from dentate gyrus to CA3 and CA1) are preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The embedding has no annotated cell-type labels, so coloring and cluster-segregation validation cannot be performed The goal is quantifying local neighborhood accuracy rather than visual/structural inspection — use the Mantel test or SVM classifier evaluation instead of scatter plots alone t-SNE or other DR outputs with random-noise sensitivity are being interpreted — the paper warns t-SNE 'tends to yield spurious clusters with clean boundaries', so plots should not be assumed structure-preserving without ivis

skills.description: Use when preparing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10X Visium slices such as the 12 human DLPFC slices) for Splane spatial domain identification, which requires per-spot cell type composition rather than gene expression.
skills.name: cell-type-composition-input-construction
skills.search_text: cell-type-composition-input-construction Use when preparing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10X Visium slices such as the 12 human DLPFC slices) for Splane spatial domain identification, which requires per-spot cell type composition rather than gene expression. Input is image-based ST data with single-cell resolution (e.g., MERFISH, STARmap) where per-cell identity is directly observed and no deconvolution step is needed before Splane The goal is to run Splane-single per-slice baselines that explicitly do not use joint cell type composition input A new slice is being added to an already-trained SPACEL model — the entire deep learning model must be retrained from scratch, which may affect computational efficiency Constructs the cell type composition matrix required by Splane by running Spoint deconvolution on 10X Visium slices and attaching the per-spot composition values with Splane.utils.add_cell_type_composition, since Splane's GCN takes cell type composition (not raw gene expression) as input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Constructs the cell type composition matrix required by Splane by running Spoint deconvolution on 10X Visium slices and attaching the per-spot composition values with Splane.utils.add_cell_type_composition, since Splane's GCN takes cell type composition (not raw gene expression) as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is image-based ST data with single-cell resolution (e.g., MERFISH, STARmap) where per-cell identity is directly observed and no deconvolution step is needed before Splane The goal is to run Splane-single per-slice baselines that explicitly do not use joint cell type composition input A new slice is being added to an already-trained SPACEL model — the entire deep learning model must be retrained from scratch, which may affect computational efficiency

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-state or cell-type proportions between conditions (e.g., KO vs WT) in scRNA-seq data where cells have been projected onto a reference atlas and assigned discrete cell-state labels.
skills.name: cell-type-composition-quantification-across-conditions
skills.search_text: cell-type-composition-quantification-across-conditions Use when comparing cell-state or cell-type proportions between conditions (e.g., KO vs WT) in scRNA-seq data where cells have been projected onto a reference atlas and assigned discrete cell-state labels. Data has not been projected onto a reference atlas and has no predicted cell-state labels — quantify composition only after make.projection/cellstate.predict Query cells belong to cell types or states absent from the reference atlas (e.g., γδ T cells, under-represented CD4+ TILs), where frequency estimates would be misleading The goal is de novo clustering and annotation without a reference — use unsupervised Seurat clustering instead of reference-based state frequencies http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Quantifies the frequency of reference-defined cell states in single-cell RNA-seq query datasets (e.g., miR-155 KO vs WT B16 TILs) after projection onto a reference atlas, enabling direct comparison of cell-type composition between biological conditions using ProjecTILs and plot.statepred.composition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Quantifies the frequency of reference-defined cell states in single-cell RNA-seq query datasets (e.g., miR-155 KO vs WT B16 TILs) after projection onto a reference atlas, enabling direct comparison of cell-type composition between biological conditions using ProjecTILs and plot.statepred.composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been projected onto a reference atlas and has no predicted cell-state labels — quantify composition only after make.projection/cellstate.predict Query cells belong to cell types or states absent from the reference atlas (e.g., γδ T cells, under-represented CD4+ TILs), where frequency estimates would be misleading The goal is de novo clustering and annotation without a reference — use unsupervised Seurat clustering instead of reference-based state frequencies

skills.description: Use when a single-cell/nucleus atlas has cell-type or cell-state annotations plus per-donor covariates, and the goal is to test whether cell-type fractions differ across a condition (e.g. obesity, depot) while controlling for covariates.
skills.name: cell-type-composition-regression-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-composition-regression-analysis Use when a single-cell/nucleus atlas has cell-type or cell-state annotations plus per-donor covariates, and the goal is to test whether cell-type fractions differ across a condition (e.g. obesity, depot) while controlling for covariates. Input is a raw count matrix without cell-type/state labels — label the cells first (e.g. with JOINTLY joint clustering or WATLAS transfer learning) before computing fractions The question is about gene expression programs within cell states rather than the fractional composition of cell types across donors Cells would be modeled as independent observations instead of being aggregated to donor-level fractions (pseudoreplication) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Donor-level ordinary linear regression of cell-type/state fractions from the WATLAS white adipose tissue atlas on weight status (lean vs obese), depot and sex, to quantify compositional shifts (Fig. 5C/5G style contrasts). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Donor-level ordinary linear regression of cell-type/state fractions from the WATLAS white adipose tissue atlas on weight status (lean vs obese), depot and sex, to quantify compositional shifts (Fig. 5C/5G style contrasts).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix without cell-type/state labels — label the cells first (e.g. with JOINTLY joint clustering or WATLAS transfer learning) before computing fractions The question is about gene expression programs within cell states rather than the fractional composition of cell types across donors Cells would be modeled as independent observations instead of being aggregated to donor-level fractions (pseudoreplication)

skills.description: Use when evaluating how accurately an automatic cell-type annotation method labels clusters of scRNA-seq data against manually curated cell types, and a comparable consistent-rate table across multiple methods is needed.
skills.name: cell-type-consistency-rate-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-consistency-rate-computation Use when evaluating how accurately an automatic cell-type annotation method labels clusters of scRNA-seq data against manually curated cell types, and a comparable consistent-rate table across multiple methods is needed. The goal is per-cell annotation accuracy rather than cluster-level consistency with manual labels — the scCATCH benchmark scores agreement at the cluster level The datasets or tissue types are not covered by the CellMatch reference database, since scCATCH's performance depends heavily on database coverage and a limited reference can cause incorrect annotation Cluster assignments are themselves unreliable or absent — inadequate clustering analysis introduces errors into cell type annotation per the article's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark methodology from the scCATCH paper for quantifying automatic cell-type annotation accuracy as per-cluster and per-dataset consistent rates, comparing cluster-based scCATCH and Seurat against cell-based methods (CellAssign, SingleR, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Benchmark methodology from the scCATCH paper for quantifying automatic cell-type annotation accuracy as per-cluster and per-dataset consistent rates, comparing cluster-based scCATCH and Seurat against cell-based methods (CellAssign, SingleR, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-cell annotation accuracy rather than cluster-level consistency with manual labels — the scCATCH benchmark scores agreement at the cluster level The datasets or tissue types are not covered by the CellMatch reference database, since scCATCH's performance depends heavily on database coverage and a limited reference can cause incorrect annotation Cluster assignments are themselves unreliable or absent — inadequate clustering analysis introduces errors into cell type annotation per the article's discussion

skills.description: Use when training a supervised single-cell label-assignment model on scRNA-seq data with known cell types and you must decide between a flat vs hierarchical classifier based on how highly correlated the training cell types are.
skills.name: cell-type-correlation-strategy-selection
skills.search_text: cell-type-correlation-strategy-selection Use when training a supervised single-cell label-assignment model on scRNA-seq data with known cell types and you must decide between a flat vs hierarchical classifier based on how highly correlated the training cell types are. The new sample is expected to contain cell types or rare/unknown populations absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training scRNA-seq data exist for the tissue of interest, so an unsupervised clustering approach is required instead of supervised label assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 NeuCA's automatic classifier-strategy selection: compute averaged expression profiles per cell type in the training data, calculate the Pearson correlation matrix across cell types, and if any pairwise off-diagonal correlation exceeds the threshold tau = 0.95, use a cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network (with marker-guided feature selection); otherwise use a single feed-forward neural network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: NeuCA's automatic classifier-strategy selection: compute averaged expression profiles per cell type in the training data, calculate the Pearson correlation matrix across cell types, and if any pairwise off-diagonal correlation exceeds the threshold tau = 0.95, use a cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network (with marker-guided feature selection); otherwise use a single feed-forward neural network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample is expected to contain cell types or rare/unknown populations absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training scRNA-seq data exist for the tissue of interest, so an unsupervised clustering approach is required instead of supervised label assignment

skills.description: Use when visualizing two or more cellular-resolution SRT sections jointly (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl DPI-10 vs DPI-15) and cell-type labels differ across sections, so naive default palettes misalign colors between biologically related or confusable cell types.
skills.name: cell-type-correspondence-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-type-correspondence-mapping Use when visualizing two or more cellular-resolution SRT sections jointly (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl DPI-10 vs DPI-15) and cell-type labels differ across sections, so naive default palettes misalign colors between biologically related or confusable cell types. Only one tissue section is being visualized — single-section colorization needs no cross-section correspondence mapping Cell-type labels are already consistent and identically named across sections and the default Scanpy/Seurat/Squidpy palette suffices Data is not single-cell spatial (SRT) data — e.g., scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates, since the Degree of Interlacement requires spatial relationships between cells Maps cell-type clusters across multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics tissue sections (e.g., Spaco's greedy correspondence mapping over merged cluster-interlacement graphs) so that corresponding cell types receive a shared, contrast-optimized color palette in integrative visualizations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Maps cell-type clusters across multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics tissue sections (e.g., Spaco's greedy correspondence mapping over merged cluster-interlacement graphs) so that corresponding cell types receive a shared, contrast-optimized color palette in integrative visualizations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one tissue section is being visualized — single-section colorization needs no cross-section correspondence mapping Cell-type labels are already consistent and identically named across sections and the default Scanpy/Seurat/Squidpy palette suffices Data is not single-cell spatial (SRT) data — e.g., scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates, since the Degree of Interlacement requires spatial relationships between cells

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-by-feature scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix with per-cell type labels and need across-cell-type expression/accessibility profiles for Spearman/k-medoids clustering or Kendall's Tb correlation validation.
skills.name: cell-type-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-type-count-aggregation Use when you have a cell-by-feature scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix with per-cell type labels and need across-cell-type expression/accessibility profiles for Spearman/k-medoids clustering or Kendall's Tb correlation validation. The data is already bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq or a pre-aggregated cell-type-level table — no per-cell-type averaging is needed The goal is per-cell analysis (clustering single cells rather than comparing across-cell-type feature profiles) The analysis needs spatial or proteomics/metabolomics layers — MOSim's single-cell simulation covers only scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates a simulated (or experimental) single-cell count matrix to the average count per cell type and applies a log(x+1) transformation, producing cell-type-level feature profiles suitable for downstream correlation- and clustering-based validation of multi-omics regulatory simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Aggregates a simulated (or experimental) single-cell count matrix to the average count per cell type and applies a log(x+1) transformation, producing cell-type-level feature profiles suitable for downstream correlation- and clustering-based validation of multi-omics regulatory simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is already bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq or a pre-aggregated cell-type-level table — no per-cell-type averaging is needed The goal is per-cell analysis (clustering single cells rather than comparing across-cell-type feature profiles) The analysis needs spatial or proteomics/metabolomics layers — MOSim's single-cell simulation covers only scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq

skills.description: Use when comparing cell type identification or gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice spatial transcriptomics benchmarks with paired scRNA-seq references and ground-truth per-cell assignments.
skills.name: cell-type-deconvolution-method-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-deconvolution-method-evaluation Use when comparing cell type identification or gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice spatial transcriptomics benchmarks with paired scRNA-seq references and ground-truth per-cell assignments. Input is real (non-simulated) tissue ST data without ground-truth single-cell labels — error-rate and cosine-similarity evaluation is not possible The goal is deconvolving a single new dataset rather than benchmarking methods head-to-head — use a single chosen method instead Data are unpaired, i.e. no scRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue being profiled, since all compared methods are reference-based http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking protocol for evaluating cell type identification and single-cell gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice ST datasets with paired scRNA-seq references, as used to evaluate SpatialScope against Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD and ten deconvolution baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for evaluating cell type identification and single-cell gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice ST datasets with paired scRNA-seq references, as used to evaluate SpatialScope against Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD and ten deconvolution baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) tissue ST data without ground-truth single-cell labels — error-rate and cosine-similarity evaluation is not possible The goal is deconvolving a single new dataset rather than benchmarking methods head-to-head — use a single chosen method instead Data are unpaired, i.e. no scRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue being profiled, since all compared methods are reference-based

skills.description: Use when estimating cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq read counts with a multi-subject single-cell reference, especially for closely related cell types and without pre-selected marker genes.
skills.name: cell-type-deconvolution-wnnls
skills.search_text: cell-type-deconvolution-wnnls Use when estimating cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq read counts with a multi-subject single-cell reference, especially for closely related cell types and without pre-selected marker genes. Bulk input is TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; read counts are required. Bulk data are generated from samples with multiple clinical conditions differing from the single-cell reference — use MuSiC2 instead of the plain W-NNLS fit. No multi-subject scRNA-seq reference with per-subject replication is available — the gene weighting requires cross-subject statistics (M.theta, Sigma). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MuSiC-style cell type deconvolution: a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) estimator that uses cross-subject scRNA-seq statistics to weight genes and estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq read counts, without pre-selected marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: MuSiC-style cell type deconvolution: a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) estimator that uses cross-subject scRNA-seq statistics to weight genes and estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq read counts, without pre-selected marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bulk input is TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; read counts are required. Bulk data are generated from samples with multiple clinical conditions differing from the single-cell reference — use MuSiC2 instead of the plain W-NNLS fit. No multi-subject scRNA-seq reference with per-subject replication is available — the gene weighting requires cross-subject statistics (M.theta, Sigma).

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset contains annotated cell types and two conditions, and you need per-cell-type DE gene counts and magnitudes to rank the biological response across populations.
skills.name: cell-type-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-differential-expression-analysis Use when a single-cell dataset contains annotated cell types and two conditions, and you need per-cell-type DE gene counts and magnitudes to rank the biological response across populations. The data has not been clustered/annotated into cell types — per-cell-type DE requires a prior clustering step (e.g., DESC soft assignments with max.prob) Batch effect has not been assessed: if technical batch dominates true biological variation, DESC's premise that 'technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' fails and DE results may reflect batch, not biology The dataset lacks multiple conditions per cell type (e.g., only one condition present), making within-cell-type control-vs-stimulus DE impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Performs differential expression between conditions (e.g., control vs interferon-beta stimulated) within each annotated cell type of a PBMC scRNA-seq dataset, then ranks cell types by IFN-beta response magnitude to verify that the strongest biological signal lies in CD14+ monocytes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Performs differential expression between conditions (e.g., control vs interferon-beta stimulated) within each annotated cell type of a PBMC scRNA-seq dataset, then ranks cell types by IFN-beta response magnitude to verify that the strongest biological signal lies in CD14+ monocytes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data has not been clustered/annotated into cell types — per-cell-type DE requires a prior clustering step (e.g., DESC soft assignments with max.prob) Batch effect has not been assessed: if technical batch dominates true biological variation, DESC's premise that 'technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' fails and DE results may reflect batch, not biology The dataset lacks multiple conditions per cell type (e.g., only one condition present), making within-cell-type control-vs-stimulus DE impossible

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cross-modality translation methods (e.g., scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq) for generalization to cell types absent from training, mimicking the MB/MCC/MK/PBMC unseen-cell-type evaluation.
skills.name: cell-type-disjoint-cross-validation-splitting
skills.search_text: cell-type-disjoint-cross-validation-splitting Use when benchmarking cross-modality translation methods (e.g., scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq) for generalization to cell types absent from training, mimicking the MB/MCC/MK/PBMC unseen-cell-type evaluation. When the goal is in-distribution translation accuracy on cell types seen during training — a random cell-level split, not a cell-type-disjoint split, is appropriate When the paired dataset has too few cell types to form disjoint folds, making the split ill-defined or folds unrepresentative When evaluating unpaired/diagonal translation or perturbation-response prediction, which use different training and evaluation protocols http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A cross-validation protocol for evaluating single-cell cross-modality translation to novel cell types: partition cell types into folds so training and test sets share no cell type, then measure whether translated profiles preserve cellular heterogeneity on unseen cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: A cross-validation protocol for evaluating single-cell cross-modality translation to novel cell types: partition cell types into folds so training and test sets share no cell type, then measure whether translated profiles preserve cellular heterogeneity on unseen cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is in-distribution translation accuracy on cell types seen during training — a random cell-level split, not a cell-type-disjoint split, is appropriate When the paired dataset has too few cell types to form disjoint folds, making the split ill-defined or folds unrepresentative When evaluating unpaired/diagonal translation or perturbation-response prediction, which use different training and evaluation protocols

skills.description: Use when you need to identify which cell type in an untreated disease scRNA-seq dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, without paired treated/untreated samples.
skills.name: cell-type-drug-response-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-drug-response-ranking Use when you need to identify which cell type in an untreated disease scRNA-seq dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, without paired treated/untreated samples. Only paired pre/post-treatment data with no known drug target gene are available — DEG-count/separability methods like Augur, Wilcoxon, MAST, DESeq2 are more appropriate since scRank relies on prior target knowledge The drug has multiple targets — multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank You need validated agonist-drug modeling — scRank's agonist mode is a simplifying assumption (max-weight out-edges) with only preliminary testing due to limited agonist single-cell data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq data by building a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) with scRank and scoring in silico drug perturbation, combining global manifold-alignment distortion and local 2-hop network diffusion from the drug target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq data by building a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) with scRank and scoring in silico drug perturbation, combining global manifold-alignment distortion and local 2-hop network diffusion from the drug target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only paired pre/post-treatment data with no known drug target gene are available — DEG-count/separability methods like Augur, Wilcoxon, MAST, DESeq2 are more appropriate since scRank relies on prior target knowledge The drug has multiple targets — multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank You need validated agonist-drug modeling — scRank's agonist mode is a simplifying assumption (max-weight out-edges) with only preliminary testing due to limited agonist single-cell data

skills.description: Use when SINCERA hierarchical clustering has produced cell clusters and each cluster must be annotated with a predicted cell type using differentially expressed genes and a Fisher's exact test against the EBI Expression Atlas annotation table.
skills.name: cell-type-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-enrichment-analysis Use when SINCERA hierarchical clustering has produced cell clusters and each cluster must be annotated with a predicted cell type using differentially expressed genes and a Fisher's exact test against the EBI Expression Atlas annotation table. Input lacks cluster-level differentially expressed genes — enrichment requires marker gene sets from cluster.diffgenes, not raw expression matrices The cell types of interest are not represented in the EBI Expression Atlas-derived annotation table (e.g. novel or highly specialized cell types) Cells have not yet been clustered via cluster.assignment; cell type prediction operates on defined clusters, not individual cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assigns a predicted cell type to each SINCERA cluster by testing cluster marker genes for enrichment against a precompiled cell type-gene association table built from EBI Expression Atlas data, then cross-validates assignments with a rank-aggregation-based check. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Assigns a predicted cell type to each SINCERA cluster by testing cluster marker genes for enrichment against a precompiled cell type-gene association table built from EBI Expression Atlas data, then cross-validates assignments with a rank-aggregation-based check.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks cluster-level differentially expressed genes — enrichment requires marker gene sets from cluster.diffgenes, not raw expression matrices The cell types of interest are not represented in the EBI Expression Atlas-derived annotation table (e.g. novel or highly specialized cell types) Cells have not yet been clustered via cluster.assignment; cell type prediction operates on defined clusters, not individual cells

skills.description: Use when comparing segmentation methods on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE melanoma, CosMx lung) where no pixel-level ground truth exists and you need reference-based homogeneity vs cell-size consistency metrics.
skills.name: cell-type-entropy-coefficient-of-variation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cell-type-entropy-coefficient-of-variation-benchmarking Use when comparing segmentation methods on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE melanoma, CosMx lung) where no pixel-level ground truth exists and you need reference-based homogeneity vs cell-size consistency metrics. Datasets with pixel-level ground truth annotations exist — use direct segmentation accuracy metrics instead of entropy/CV surrogates Input is already a cell-by-cell-type annotated matrix with no segmentation step to compare (nothing to benchmark) MERSCOPE tissues dominated by elongated melanocytes/fibroblasts where ~25% of cells lack nuclei — interpret entropy metrics cautiously given the documented morphology caveat http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Benchmark SST segmentation methods on non-Xenium platforms by computing cell-type entropy (homogeneity of per-cell transcriptional composition from single-cell reference annotation) against the coefficient of variation of cell size, plotting the results as the Fig. 4 generalisability panels (e.g., MERSCOPE-Melanoma). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Benchmark SST segmentation methods on non-Xenium platforms by computing cell-type entropy (homogeneity of per-cell transcriptional composition from single-cell reference annotation) against the coefficient of variation of cell size, plotting the results as the Fig. 4 generalisability panels (e.g., MERSCOPE-Melanoma).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with pixel-level ground truth annotations exist — use direct segmentation accuracy metrics instead of entropy/CV surrogates Input is already a cell-by-cell-type annotated matrix with no segmentation step to compare (nothing to benchmark) MERSCOPE tissues dominated by elongated melanocytes/fibroblasts where ~25% of cells lack nuclei — interpret entropy metrics cautiously given the documented morphology caveat

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq study stored as an AnnData/H5AD object must be loaded into a relational sparse expression table and queried for gene-level per-cell-type averages, e.g. to replicate Cellenium's server-side aggregation.
skills.name: cell-type-expression-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-type-expression-aggregation Use when a scRNA-seq study stored as an AnnData/H5AD object must be loaded into a relational sparse expression table and queried for gene-level per-cell-type averages, e.g. to replicate Cellenium's server-side aggregation. The input is already a pre-aggregated gene x cell-type feature table rather than a cells x genes matrix with cell annotations The goal is interactive visual exploration (UMAP plots, violin plots) rather than materializing aggregated expression summaries The study data is not in H5AD/AnnData format with cell-type annotations available, since both the matrix and the annotation are required for the GROUP BY aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs Cellenium's gene-centric sparse storage of single-cell expression data in PostgreSQL and computes per-cell-type expression summaries via SQL aggregation, mirroring how Cellenium implements gene and cell-type-level aggregation as database functions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Reconstructs Cellenium's gene-centric sparse storage of single-cell expression data in PostgreSQL and computes per-cell-type expression summaries via SQL aggregation, mirroring how Cellenium implements gene and cell-type-level aggregation as database functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a pre-aggregated gene x cell-type feature table rather than a cells x genes matrix with cell annotations The goal is interactive visual exploration (UMAP plots, violin plots) rather than materializing aggregated expression summaries The study data is not in H5AD/AnnData format with cell-type annotations available, since both the matrix and the annotation are required for the GROUP BY aggregation

skills.description: Use when a query gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') must be matched to the annotated cell types that specifically express it, within one study or across multiple ingested scRNA-seq studies.
skills.name: cell-type-expression-specificity-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-expression-specificity-ranking Use when a query gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') must be matched to the annotated cell types that specifically express it, within one study or across multiple ingested scRNA-seq studies. The goal is to compute differential expression from raw counts rather than search against precalculated marker statistics — Cellenium relies on DE results already calculated by the study data preparation notebooks The query is for gene–gene correlation or coexpression across pairs of genes, not expression specificity of a single gene per cell type The studies lack annotated cell types/clusters, so no marker statistics per annotated cell type exist to rank http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank annotated cell types within each single-cell study by the specificity of a query gene's expression (e.g. insulin), then aggregate per-study rankings into a cross-study marker search view as demonstrated by Cellenium's use case 3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Rank annotated cell types within each single-cell study by the specificity of a query gene's expression (e.g. insulin), then aggregate per-study rankings into a cross-study marker search view as demonstrated by Cellenium's use case 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compute differential expression from raw counts rather than search against precalculated marker statistics — Cellenium relies on DE results already calculated by the study data preparation notebooks The query is for gene–gene correlation or coexpression across pairs of genes, not expression specificity of a single gene per cell type The studies lack annotated cell types/clusters, so no marker statistics per annotated cell type exist to rank

skills.description: Use when comparing label-transfer accuracy of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq integration methods on cells with held-out ground-truth annotations, especially under varying annotation budgets.
skills.name: cell-type-f1-score-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-f1-score-computation Use when comparing label-transfer accuracy of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq integration methods on cells with held-out ground-truth annotations, especially under varying annotation budgets. Target cells lack held-out ground-truth annotations, so no reference labels exist for F1 computation The task measures joint embedding quality (clustering/visualization) rather than label transfer, where F1 against reference labels is not the appropriate metric http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes average per-cell-type label-transfer F1 scores against held-out target cell annotations to quantitatively compare multi-omics integration methods (e.g., scBridge vs. scJoint), as done in the scBridge benchmark across annotation downsampling fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Computes average per-cell-type label-transfer F1 scores against held-out target cell annotations to quantitatively compare multi-omics integration methods (e.g., scBridge vs. scJoint), as done in the scBridge benchmark across annotation downsampling fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target cells lack held-out ground-truth annotations, so no reference labels exist for F1 computation The task measures joint embedding quality (clustering/visualization) rather than label transfer, where F1 against reference labels is not the appropriate metric

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples have been deconvolved against a single-cell reference (e.g., via scPlant decomposeBulk on an annotated Seurat object) and you need a heatmap of per-sample cell-type fractions to compare compositions across conditions.
skills.name: cell-type-fraction-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-type-fraction-heatmap-visualization Use when bulk RNA-seq samples have been deconvolved against a single-cell reference (e.g., via scPlant decomposeBulk on an annotated Seurat object) and you need a heatmap of per-sample cell-type fractions to compare compositions across conditions. Input is raw single-cell count data that has not been clustered and cell-type annotated — deconvolution signatures require labeled clusters, so run scPlant's QCfun/RunSeurat/annotation steps first The goal is cell-type annotation of the single-cell data itself rather than estimating composition of bulk samples from a reference No bulk RNA-seq matrix or sample metadata is available — decomposeBulk requires both (SeuratObj, exprs, meta) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize scPlant deconvolution results by calling fractionHmp on the decomposeBulk output to draw a heatmap of the estimated fraction of each cell type (e.g., Arabidopsis root vasculature and companion cells) in each bulk RNA-seq sample, enabling comparison of cell-type composition across conditions such as stress treatments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Visualize scPlant deconvolution results by calling fractionHmp on the decomposeBulk output to draw a heatmap of the estimated fraction of each cell type (e.g., Arabidopsis root vasculature and companion cells) in each bulk RNA-seq sample, enabling comparison of cell-type composition across conditions such as stress treatments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-cell count data that has not been clustered and cell-type annotated — deconvolution signatures require labeled clusters, so run scPlant's QCfun/RunSeurat/annotation steps first The goal is cell-type annotation of the single-cell data itself rather than estimating composition of bulk samples from a reference No bulk RNA-seq matrix or sample metadata is available — decomposeBulk requires both (SeuratObj, exprs, meta)

skills.description: Use when an unsupervised clustering (e.g., Leiden) of scRNA-seq data has produced clusters with no labels and you must assign a cell type from the functional enrichment of cluster-specific genes.
skills.name: cell-type-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-type-functional-annotation Use when an unsupervised clustering (e.g., Leiden) of scRNA-seq data has produced clusters with no labels and you must assign a cell type from the functional enrichment of cluster-specific genes. Cells are already annotated (e.g., via SingleR reference-based label transfer or scanpy Ingest from HBMP2-spleen-2 to HBMP3-spleen-CC3) — enrichment would be redundant The input is raw, unclustered, or unfiltered count data — preprocessing (filtering 50–3000 genes/cells, CPM 1e5 normalization, log1p, scaling) and clustering must precede this skill The organism or tissue lacks adequate GO/KEGG/MSigDB gene-set coverage, making enrichment categories uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Annotate single-cell clusters by cell type by running differential expression on one cluster versus the rest (diffxpy), selecting the top 500 DE genes by fold-change, and performing GO/KEGG/MSigDB enrichment with GSEApy (GSEA) to infer function from enriched gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell clusters by cell type by running differential expression on one cluster versus the rest (diffxpy), selecting the top 500 DE genes by fold-change, and performing GO/KEGG/MSigDB enrichment with GSEApy (GSEA) to infer function from enriched gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are already annotated (e.g., via SingleR reference-based label transfer or scanpy Ingest from HBMP2-spleen-2 to HBMP3-spleen-CC3) — enrichment would be redundant The input is raw, unclustered, or unfiltered count data — preprocessing (filtering 50–3000 genes/cells, CPM 1e5 normalization, log1p, scaling) and clustering must precede this skill The organism or tissue lacks adequate GO/KEGG/MSigDB gene-set coverage, making enrichment categories uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when cell types have been annotated across merged datasets (e.g., after Harmony-kernel integration and label propagation) and a unified marker-gene signature per type/subtype is needed, such as neuronal (LINGO2, CUX2, SST) and glial (SLC1A2, MBP, CLDN5) markers.
skills.name: cell-type-gene-signature-definition
skills.search_text: cell-type-gene-signature-definition Use when cell types have been annotated across merged datasets (e.g., after Harmony-kernel integration and label propagation) and a unified marker-gene signature per type/subtype is needed, such as neuronal (LINGO2, CUX2, SST) and glial (SLC1A2, MBP, CLDN5) markers. Cell-type labels have not yet been propagated/integrated across datasets — the signatures are defined on the consensus annotation, not on per-study clusters Input is a single dataset without batch structure to reconcile — the consensus-vocabulary step exists to merge annotations across independent studies The goal is de novo marker discovery from raw counts without an integrated cell-state decomposition (e.g., ACTIONet archetypes/network) in place http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Consolidates network-propagated cell-type annotations from multiple integrated scRNA-seq datasets into a consensus vocabulary and extracts a nonredundant set of gene signatures per cell type/subtype, demonstrated on the ACTIONet joint analysis of 105,099 human prefrontal cortex cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6

skills.name: cell-type-hierarchy-construction
skills.search_text: cell-type-hierarchy-construction Use when training a custom Census cell-type annotation model from a scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Tabula Sapiens plus CCLE) that requires inferring the cell-type hierarchy and fitting node classifiers. The goal is annotating an existing dataset rather than building a model — use the pretrained census_main function with the Tabula Sapiens model instead of training a hierarchy. The reference has too few cell types or unlabelled cells, so pseudo-bulk profiles and a meaningful hierarchy cannot be inferred. Seurat v4 is not available in the environment — Census requires Seurat version 4 and will not run correctly with other versions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds a Census cell-type hierarchy by aggregating single-cell counts into pseudo-bulk profiles per cell type, computing pairwise distances, and applying Ward hierarchical clustering (merging CCLE cancer cell line profiles as extra reference nodes), then training a binary xgboost gradient-boosted decision tree classifier at each internal node. This is how custom Census models are created beyond the pretrained Tabula Sapiens model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Builds a Census cell-type hierarchy by aggregating single-cell counts into pseudo-bulk profiles per cell type, computing pairwise distances, and applying Ward hierarchical clustering (merging CCLE cancer cell line profiles as extra reference nodes), then training a binary xgboost gradient-boosted decision tree classifier at each internal node. This is how custom Census models are created beyond the pretrained Tabula Sapiens model.

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell (not per-spot) discrete cell type labels for ST spots (Visium, Slide-seq), given nucleus segmentation outputs and a labeled scRNA-seq reference, with spatial smoothness enforced.
skills.name: cell-type-identification-potts-model-map-inference
skills.search_text: cell-type-identification-potts-model-map-inference Use when you need per-cell (not per-spot) discrete cell type labels for ST spots (Visium, Slide-seq), given nucleus segmentation outputs and a labeled scRNA-seq reference, with spatial smoothness enforced. Spot-level cell-type proportions suffice and single-cell resolution is not required — deconvolution methods such as RCTD, Cell2location, CARD, or spatialDWLS already estimate proportions per spot. No spatial coordinates for spots/cells are available, since the Potts prior relies on spatial smoothness across neighboring cells/slices. No labeled scRNA-seq reference is available, or platform effects between ST and reference data cannot be corrected. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SpatialScope's cell type identification step assigns a discrete cell type to each nucleus/cell segmented from spatial transcriptomics spots via MAP inference under a Potts (spatial smoothness) model with hyperparameter ν = 10, using a labeled scRNA-seq reference and optionally 3D-aligned adjacent slices for more reliable spatial priors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: SpatialScope's cell type identification step assigns a discrete cell type to each nucleus/cell segmented from spatial transcriptomics spots via MAP inference under a Potts (spatial smoothness) model with hyperparameter ν = 10, using a labeled scRNA-seq reference and optionally 3D-aligned adjacent slices for more reliable spatial priors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spot-level cell-type proportions suffice and single-cell resolution is not required — deconvolution methods such as RCTD, Cell2location, CARD, or spatialDWLS already estimate proportions per spot. No spatial coordinates for spots/cells are available, since the Potts prior relies on spatial smoothness across neighboring cells/slices. No labeled scRNA-seq reference is available, or platform effects between ST and reference data cannot be corrected.

skills.search_text: cell-type-importance-visualization Use when you have dsCellNet-inferred ligand-receptor networks across multiple developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis stages) and need per-cell-type incoming/outgoing/total edge counts to rank the most communicating cell types per stage. skills.summary: Quantifies and visualizes the incoming, outgoing, and total interaction scores of each cell type at each time point in developmental series cell-cell communication networks inferred with dsCellNet, to identify the most communicating sender and receiver cell types (e.g., apical progenitors dominating early mouse corticogenesis, intermediate progenitors dominating the middle stage).

skills.description: Use when gABC/ABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions have been predicted per cell type from snATAC-seq candidate enhancers and you need per-cell-type interaction counts plus cross-cell-type overlap/shared fractions.
skills.name: cell-type-interaction-overlap-statistics
skills.search_text: cell-type-interaction-overlap-statistics Use when gABC/ABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions have been predicted per cell type from snATAC-seq candidate enhancers and you need per-cell-type interaction counts plus cross-cell-type overlap/shared fractions. You only have a single bulk enhancer activity profile with no per-cell-type activity columns — there are no cell-type-specific interaction sets to compare. Your enhancer coordinates and Hi-C contacts are not on the same genome build/window scheme (e.g., hg38 enhancers against the hg19 average Hi-C matrix) — the 5 Mb window and 5000 bp binning would silently mismatch. Your goal is TF affinity summarisation on gene level (GAZE) rather than counting ABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions — the separate ABC-scoring mode and overlap statistics are then the wrong endpoint. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify and compare gABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions predicted per cell type from single-cell ATAC-seq data, measuring how many interactions each cell type shares with all others. This reveals the extent of cell-type specificity in the predicted regulatory landscape (e.g., of the human heart snATAC-seq dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Quantify and compare gABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions predicted per cell type from single-cell ATAC-seq data, measuring how many interactions each cell type shares with all others. skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single bulk enhancer activity profile with no per-cell-type activity columns — there are no cell-type-specific interaction sets to compare. skills.description: Use when annotating cell types in scRNA-seq data without training on the test dataset, or when benchmarking a zero-shot label predictor against supervised classifiers like CellTypist on a multi-batch atlas such as the open-problems pancreas dataset.
skills.name: cell-type-label-prediction
skills.search_text: cell-type-label-prediction Use when annotating cell types in scRNA-seq data without training on the test dataset, or when benchmarking a zero-shot label predictor against supervised classifiers like CellTypist on a multi-batch atlas such as the open-problems pancreas dataset. The task is gene network inference rather than label prediction — scPRINT's headline benchmarking targets GN inference, and this zero-shot annotation skill does not produce gene networks A labeled training split for the target atlas is available and a supervised model can be fine-tuned on it — the zero-shot setup is specifically for predictors that do not train on the test dataset The test data is spatial omics or non-single-cell assay data, which the scPRINT preprocessing explicitly drops http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Zero-shot cell-type label prediction using the pretrained scPRINT foundation model (random gene sampling, 4000-gene context), benchmarked against supervised classifiers such as CellTypist and openproblems logistic regression/XGBoost using accuracy and macro-F1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Zero-shot cell-type label prediction using the pretrained scPRINT foundation model (random gene sampling, 4000-gene context), benchmarked against supervised classifiers such as CellTypist and openproblems logistic regression/XGBoost using accuracy and macro-F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is gene network inference rather than label prediction — scPRINT's headline benchmarking targets GN inference, and this zero-shot annotation skill does not produce gene networks A labeled training split for the target atlas is available and a supervised model can be fine-tuned on it — the zero-shot setup is specifically for predictors that do not train on the test dataset The test data is spatial omics or non-single-cell assay data, which the scPRINT preprocessing explicitly drops

skills.description: Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., three cortex studies totaling ~105,099 cells) are jointly integrated and one or more reference annotations must be propagated to unlabeled cells without re-clustering from scratch.
skills.name: cell-type-label-propagation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: cell-type-label-propagation-across-datasets Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., three cortex studies totaling ~105,099 cells) are jointly integrated and one or more reference annotations must be propagated to unlabeled cells without re-clustering from scratch. Datasets have no shared biological populations or the reference annotations themselves are unreliable — propagation will faithfully transfer wrong labels A single dataset is being analyzed with no cross-study transfer needed; plain ACTIONet clustering and marker discovery suffices without the Harmony-kernel reduction and propagation step Input is already a feature/signature table rather than a raw count matrix — the filter/normalize/log1p/reduce_kernel pipeline is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transfers cell-type and subtype annotations across independent single-cell datasets using ACTIONet's network-based label propagation over a batch-corrected (Harmony-kernel) joint embedding, then consolidates the propagated labels into a consensus vocabulary with nonredundant gene signatures per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Transfers cell-type and subtype annotations across independent single-cell datasets using ACTIONet's network-based label propagation over a batch-corrected (Harmony-kernel) joint embedding, then consolidates the propagated labels into a consensus vocabulary with nonredundant gene signatures per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have no shared biological populations or the reference annotations themselves are unreliable — propagation will faithfully transfer wrong labels A single dataset is being analyzed with no cross-study transfer needed; plain ACTIONet clustering and marker discovery suffices without the Harmony-kernel reduction and propagation step Input is already a feature/signature table rather than a raw count matrix — the filter/normalize/log1p/reduce_kernel pipeline is not applicable

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-type-specific gene network (weighted edge matrix) for one of 26 cell types and need to verify that its node scores recover the correct pangaloDB cell-type markers.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a cell-type-specific gene network (weighted edge matrix) for one of 26 cell types and need to verify that its node scores recover the correct pangaloDB cell-type markers. When the goal is to test whether TFs are hubs or whether TF targets are enriched (use ENCODE-target and TF-enrichment preranks instead) When the network is not cell-type-specific (e.g., a single atlas-level literature-based network), since marker enrichment per cell type is not defined When you need a quantitative significance judgment per cell type rather than the paper's criterion of manual identification of the cell type name in the top 10 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether a cell-type-specific gene network inferred by a method (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, GENIE3, DeepSEM, etc.) is enriched for that cell type's marker genes, using GSEA prerank on network node scores against pangaloDB marker gene sets, aggregated across the 26 cell types benchmarked in the scPRINT paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Tests whether a cell-type-specific gene network inferred by a method (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, GENIE3, DeepSEM, etc.) is enriched for that cell type's marker genes, using GSEA prerank on network node scores against pangaloDB marker gene sets, aggregated across the 26 cell types benchmarked in the scPRINT paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to test whether TFs are hubs or whether TF targets are enriched (use ENCODE-target and TF-enrichment preranks instead) When the network is not cell-type-specific (e.g., a single atlas-level literature-based network), since marker enrichment per cell type is not defined When you need a quantitative significance judgment per cell type rather than the paper's criterion of manual identification of the cell type name in the top 10

skills.description: Use when scQA clustering (labels.txt) has assigned cells to clusters and you must confirm each cluster's key genes overlap known markers, hub genes, and DEGs (e.g., endothelial ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1).
skills.name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-enrichment-annotation Use when scQA clustering (labels.txt) has assigned cells to clusters and you must confirm each cluster's key genes overlap known markers, hub genes, and DEGs (e.g., endothelial ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1). Clustering labels have not yet been generated (labels.txt from scQA is a prerequisite; chain from the clustering task first) The dataset's original publication does not provide marker genes or DEG lists, so no reference sets exist to compute overlap against http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates the biological significance of key genes (landmarks) identified by scQA for each cell-type cluster by computing their overlap and enrichment against reference marker genes and DEGs (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01) from the dataset's original publication. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Validates the biological significance of key genes (landmarks) identified by scQA for each cell-type cluster by computing their overlap and enrichment against reference marker genes and DEGs (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01) from the dataset's original publication.
