skills.description: Use when you have a gene marker list selected from scRNA-seq phenotypes and need to verify it recovers the correct tissues and cell types by enrichment against a curated reference set such as HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-enrichment-interpretation Use when you have a gene marker list selected from scRNA-seq phenotypes and need to verify it recovers the correct tissues and cell types by enrichment against a curated reference set such as HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022. The gene list has not been selected via phenotype cover (G-PC/CEM-PC) at the documented coverage threshold — the coverage-8 extraction rule is specific to this workflow The goal is deconvolution or classification accuracy rather than enrichment-based validation of marker specificity No curated reference gene set matching the tissues/cell types of the dataset exists (the analysis relied on gene marker lists that may be incomplete) http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates a discriminative marker set (e.g., G-PC-selected HCA markers at coverage 8) by gene set enrichment analysis against the HuBMAP ASCT+B marker library via Enrichr/GSEApy, then aggregates adjusted q values at the tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels to compare marker-selection methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Validates a discriminative marker set (e.g., G-PC-selected HCA markers at coverage 8) by gene set enrichment analysis against the HuBMAP ASCT+B marker library via Enrichr/GSEApy, then aggregates adjusted q values at the tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels to compare marker-selection methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list has not been selected via phenotype cover (G-PC/CEM-PC) at the documented coverage threshold — the coverage-8 extraction rule is specific to this workflow The goal is deconvolution or classification accuracy rather than enrichment-based validation of marker specificity No curated reference gene set matching the tissues/cell types of the dataset exists (the analysis relied on gene marker lists that may be incomplete)

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or fine-tuning the DCNet network and you need to wire 9078 marker genes to 434 cell-type hidden neurons via the zero-one relation matrix and align input/output neuron ordering with index.pkl.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-gene-matrix-handling
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-gene-matrix-handling Use when reconstructing or fine-tuning the DCNet network and you need to wire 9078 marker genes to 434 cell-type hidden neurons via the zero-one relation matrix and align input/output neuron ordering with index.pkl. Input gene set does not match the 9078 marker genes in index.pkl (e.g. non-human gene symbols or unaligned identifiers), since the mask connectivity would be meaningless Expression values are not log2(x+1)-transformed — the paper recommends this transformation before feeding the matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Load and apply DCNet's zero-one gene–cell relation matrix (relation_matrix.pkl) and gene-to-neuron index mappings (index.pkl) so that each of the 434 hidden-layer cell-type neurons connects only to its marker-gene input neurons and each of the 21136 output neurons maps to a specific gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Load and apply DCNet's zero-one gene–cell relation matrix (relation_matrix.pkl) and gene-to-neuron index mappings (index.pkl) so that each of the 434 hidden-layer cell-type neurons connects only to its marker-gene input neurons and each of the 21136 output neurons maps to a specific gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene set does not match the 9078 marker genes in index.pkl (e.g. non-human gene symbols or unaligned identifiers), since the mask connectivity would be meaningless Expression values are not log2(x+1)-transformed — the paper recommends this transformation before feeding the matrix

skills.description: Use when you have a raw/normalized scRNA-seq count matrix paired with manually annotated cell-type labels and need a per-cell-type positive marker gene list to drive marker-based or marker-learning cell-type prediction.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-gene-selection
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-gene-selection Use when you have a raw/normalized scRNA-seq count matrix paired with manually annotated cell-type labels and need a per-cell-type positive marker gene list to drive marker-based or marker-learning cell-type prediction. Input is already a curated marker gene table (e.g. downloaded from PanglaoDB or CellMarker) — pass it directly as the marker_list to markersupervised methods instead of re-deriving markers Your target prediction method is eager-supervised or lazy-supervised (e.g. Seurat, CELLBLAST, scmap-cell) since these take train/test count matrices and labels rather than a marker list Training cells lack manually annotated cell-type labels (cells with no cell type information are deleted during preprocessing) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives cell-type-specific differential marker genes from a training scRNA-seq count matrix with manually annotated labels, producing a marker table that seeds marker-learning cell-type identification methods (e.g. SCSA) in the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Derives cell-type-specific differential marker genes from a training scRNA-seq count matrix with manually annotated labels, producing a marker table that seeds marker-learning cell-type identification methods (e.g. SCSA) in the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated marker gene table (e.g. downloaded from PanglaoDB or CellMarker) — pass it directly as the marker_list to markersupervised methods instead of re-deriving markers Your target prediction method is eager-supervised or lazy-supervised (e.g. Seurat, CELLBLAST, scmap-cell) since these take train/test count matrices and labels rather than a marker list Training cells lack manually annotated cell-type labels (cells with no cell type information are deleted during preprocessing)

skills.description: Use when scBridge (or a baseline such as scJoint, Seurat or GLUE) has produced predicted cell-type labels on target scATAC/ADT data and you need marker-based evidence that the predicted populations (e.g. Naive vs Effector CD4+ T cells) are biologically correct.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-gene-validation
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-gene-validation Use when scBridge (or a baseline such as scJoint, Seurat or GLUE) has produced predicted cell-type labels on target scATAC/ADT data and you need marker-based evidence that the predicted populations (e.g. Naive vs Effector CD4+ T cells) are biologically correct. When no marker genes or protein (ADT) measurements are available for the predicted cell types — the check has no biological anchor When the goal is to compare method performance quantitatively (use label transfer accuracy and silhouette score instead) When source annotations themselves are under test (corrupted labels cannot be validated by markers derived from those same annotations) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Biological sanity check of transferred cell-type labels by comparing known marker abundance (e.g. protein/ADT markers such as CD45RA/CCR7 and CD45RO/PLEKHG3 on PBMC CITE-seq/ASAP-seq data) across predicted cell populations. It confirms that label-transfer predictions reflect genuine marker biology rather than integration artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Biological sanity check of transferred cell-type labels by comparing known marker abundance (e.g. protein/ADT markers such as CD45RA/CCR7 and CD45RO/PLEKHG3 on PBMC CITE-seq/ASAP-seq data) across predicted cell populations. It confirms that label-transfer predictions reflect genuine marker biology rather than integration artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no marker genes or protein (ADT) measurements are available for the predicted cell types — the check has no biological anchor When the goal is to compare method performance quantitatively (use label transfer accuracy and silhouette score instead) When source annotations themselves are under test (corrupted labels cannot be validated by markers derived from those same annotations)

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., the Field et al. week-2 cortical organoid data, GEO GSE106245) plus a cell type marker GMT file and want interpretable, module-level per-cell cell type activity rather than opaque clustering.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-gmv-inference
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-gmv-inference Use when you have an annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., the Field et al. week-2 cortical organoid data, GEO GSE106245) plus a cell type marker GMT file and want interpretable, module-level per-cell cell type activity rather than opaque clustering. You need a strong predictive/generative model rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability Your gene modules contain many unannotated genes: hard-coded decoder connections cannot correct incomplete or non-context-specific prior knowledge from databases like MSigDB Input is raw count data that the standard VEGA workflow does not handle — the discussion notes count-data handling would require modifying VEGA following the scVI rationale http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Trains the VEGA variational autoencoder with cell type marker-set gene module variables (GMVs) added to its latent space so that each cell type's marker-set GMV activity segregates the annotated cell populations, enabling interpretable cell type identification in single-cell RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Trains the VEGA variational autoencoder with cell type marker-set gene module variables (GMVs) added to its latent space so that each cell type's marker-set GMV activity segregates the annotated cell populations, enabling interpretable cell type identification in single-cell RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a strong predictive/generative model rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability Your gene modules contain many unannotated genes: hard-coded decoder connections cannot correct incomplete or non-context-specific prior knowledge from databases like MSigDB Input is raw count data that the standard VEGA workflow does not handle — the discussion notes count-data handling would require modifying VEGA following the scVI rationale

skills.description: Use when a single-cell TE matrix (scTE .h5ad output from scRNA-seq or scTEATAC output from scATAC-seq) has been clustered and you must confirm cell-type assignments or marker-TE specificity.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-validation
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-validation Use when a single-cell TE matrix (scTE .h5ad output from scRNA-seq or scTEATAC output from scATAC-seq) has been clustered and you must confirm cell-type assignments or marker-TE specificity. Input is already a gene-level expression matrix without TE quantification — scTE/scTEATAC must first produce the TE-by-cell matrix Bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq data — scTE is designed for single-cell BAM/SAM input with cell barcode and UMI tags (CB/UB or CR/UR) The goal is peak-level enhancer calling from scATAC-seq rather than TE-aggregated accessibility — merging TE data to infer enhancers was described as speculative and not demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that computationally recovered cell identities are supported by cell-type-specific transposable element signals, using scTE/scTEATAC quantifications of TE expression or chromatin accessibility as marker readouts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Validates that computationally recovered cell identities are supported by cell-type-specific transposable element signals, using scTE/scTEATAC quantifications of TE expression or chromatin accessibility as marker readouts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-level expression matrix without TE quantification — scTE/scTEATAC must first produce the TE-by-cell matrix Bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq data — scTE is designed for single-cell BAM/SAM input with cell barcode and UMI tags (CB/UB or CR/UR) The goal is peak-level enhancer calling from scATAC-seq rather than TE-aggregated accessibility — merging TE data to infer enhancers was described as speculative and not demonstrated

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. SingleCellExperiment) has been embedded with correspondence analysis and you want to check whether high-loading genes correspond to known cell-type markers (e.g. GNLY, TYROBP, LYZ, S100A8, CD74, HLA-DRA) and interpret cell-population associations.
skills.name: cell-type-marker-verification-from-loadings
skills.search_text: cell-type-marker-verification-from-loadings Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. SingleCellExperiment) has been embedded with correspondence analysis and you want to check whether high-loading genes correspond to known cell-type markers (e.g. GNLY, TYROBP, LYZ, S100A8, CD74, HLA-DRA) and interpret cell-population associations. The goal is choosing the best dimension-reduction method for downstream clustering accuracy — the article's benchmarks show adapted CA variants (notably CA with Freeman-Tukey residuals) outperform standard CA, which is not the point of marker verification from loadings. The dataset is a complex tissue without well-defined cell clusters — the article notes Zhengmix and SCMixology benchmarks comprise well-defined cell clusters and are simpler than data from complex tissues, so marker recovery expectations differ. Ground-truth cell labels need independent validation — the article cautions benchmark annotations came from original publications and were not independently validated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify and verify known cell-type marker genes in scRNA-seq data by ranking features on the L2 norm of their correspondence analysis (CA) loadings and inspecting the top-weight genes on a first-two-dimension CA biplot, as implemented with the corral R/Bioconductor package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Identify and verify known cell-type marker genes in scRNA-seq data by ranking features on the L2 norm of their correspondence analysis (CA) loadings and inspecting the top-weight genes on a first-two-dimension CA biplot, as implemented with the corral R/Bioconductor package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is choosing the best dimension-reduction method for downstream clustering accuracy — the article's benchmarks show adapted CA variants (notably CA with Freeman-Tukey residuals) outperform standard CA, which is not the point of marker verification from loadings. The dataset is a complex tissue without well-defined cell clusters — the article notes Zhengmix and SCMixology benchmarks comprise well-defined cell clusters and are simpler than data from complex tissues, so marker recovery expectations differ. Ground-truth cell labels need independent validation — the article cautions benchmark annotations came from original publications and were not independently validated.

skills.description: Use when comparing cross-species cell type matching pipelines (e.g., human vs mouse vs marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq) and you need reproducible ADS/recall metrics, including gene-matching ablations that test whether ProtBERT gene matches outperform BLAST matches.
skills.name: cell-type-matching-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-matching-metric-evaluation Use when comparing cross-species cell type matching pipelines (e.g., human vs mouse vs marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq) and you need reproducible ADS/recall metrics, including gene-matching ablations that test whether ProtBERT gene matches outperform BLAST matches. The analysis is within-species only — the skill's ADS/recall evaluation is defined for cross-species cell type matching comparisons (human–mouse–marmoset motor cortex). A final metrics table (e.g., gene_matching_ablation_metrics.csv) already exists and the goal is re-analysis rather than recomputation. The goal is protein/gene sequence similarity computation itself (BLAST or embed_proteins/calc_dist) rather than evaluating downstream cell type matching quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify how well cell types are matched and aligned across species by computing average dimensional score (ADS) and recall for cross-species comparison methods (e.g., TACTiCS vs SAMap), optionally under ablated gene-matching conditions (ProtBERT-derived vs BLAST-derived gene matches). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Quantify how well cell types are matched and aligned across species by computing average dimensional score (ADS) and recall for cross-species comparison methods (e.g., TACTiCS vs SAMap), optionally under ablated gene-matching conditions (ProtBERT-derived vs BLAST-derived gene matches).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is within-species only — the skill's ADS/recall evaluation is defined for cross-species cell type matching comparisons (human–mouse–marmoset motor cortex). A final metrics table (e.g., gene_matching_ablation_metrics.csv) already exists and the goal is re-analysis rather than recomputation. The goal is protein/gene sequence similarity computation itself (BLAST or embed_proteins/calc_dist) rather than evaluating downstream cell type matching quality.

skills.description: Use when preparing labelled scRNA-seq training data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment objects with known cell labels) and you need per-cell-type mean expression profiles plus a cross-cell-type correlation matrix to decide a classifier strategy.
skills.name: cell-type-mean-expression-profile-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-mean-expression-profile-computation Use when preparing labelled scRNA-seq training data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment objects with known cell labels) and you need per-cell-type mean expression profiles plus a cross-cell-type correlation matrix to decide a classifier strategy. The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data You need to detect unknown or novel cell types; NeuCA requires tools like those for rare/unknown cell identification (or inferCNV/copyKAT for malignant cells) as a prior step The input lacks known cell labels, since mean profiles per cell type cannot be computed without labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes a G x K averaged expression profile matrix from labelled scRNA-seq training data (mean expression per cell type) and the K x K Pearson correlation matrix across cell types, which NeuCA uses to select between a feed-forward neural network and a marker-guided hierarchical neural network (threshold tau = 0.95). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Computes a G x K averaged expression profile matrix from labelled scRNA-seq training data (mean expression per cell type) and the K x K Pearson correlation matrix across cell types, which NeuCA uses to select between a feed-forward neural network and a marker-guided hierarchical neural network (threshold tau = 0.95).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data You need to detect unknown or novel cell types; NeuCA requires tools like those for rare/unknown cell identification (or inferCNV/copyKAT for malignant cells) as a prior step The input lacks known cell labels, since mean profiles per cell type cannot be computed without labels

skills.description: Use when single-cell data have been pseudo-spatially mapped onto ST spots (e.g., via STEM's netsc2st mapping) and the goal is to quantify spatial proximity/colocalization between rare cell types such as TSKs, endothelial cells, or pDCs.
skills.name: cell-type-neighborhood-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-neighborhood-enrichment-analysis Use when single-cell data have been pseudo-spatially mapped onto ST spots (e.g., via STEM's netsc2st mapping) and the goal is to quantify spatial proximity/colocalization between rare cell types such as TSKs, endothelial cells, or pDCs. ST data have not been integrated with SC data and only spot-level deconvolution is needed — deconvolution treats a spot as a mixture of a fixed number of cell types and cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level SC and ST data come from different donors; the article notes applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work Input is a spot-level cell-type composition matrix rather than single-cell pseudo-spatial assignments; the enrichment analysis requires per-cell mapped coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes row-normalized neighborhood-enrichment matrices among mapped cell-type subpopulations (e.g., keratinocyte subtypes including tumor-specific keratinocytes) in pseudo-spatial coordinates produced by STEM, to test whether specific cell types colocalize or self-aggregate (e.g., TSKs vs. tumor cycling KCs, TSKs vs. endothelial cells at the tumor leading edge). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Computes row-normalized neighborhood-enrichment matrices among mapped cell-type subpopulations (e.g., keratinocyte subtypes including tumor-specific keratinocytes) in pseudo-spatial coordinates produced by STEM, to test whether specific cell types colocalize or self-aggregate (e.g., TSKs vs. tumor cycling KCs, TSKs vs. endothelial cells at the tumor leading edge).
skills.when_to_use_negative: ST data have not been integrated with SC data and only spot-level deconvolution is needed — deconvolution treats a spot as a mixture of a fixed number of cell types and cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level SC and ST data come from different donors; the article notes applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work Input is a spot-level cell-type composition matrix rather than single-cell pseudo-spatial assignments; the enrichment analysis requires per-cell mapped coordinates

skills.description: Use when combining marker gene sets from multiple published databases or cell-sorting sources whose gene symbols and cell type labels follow non-standard, inconsistent nomenclature, and you need harmonized, comparable sets.
skills.name: cell-type-nomenclature-standardization
skills.search_text: cell-type-nomenclature-standardization Use when combining marker gene sets from multiple published databases or cell-sorting sources whose gene symbols and cell type labels follow non-standard, inconsistent nomenclature, and you need harmonized, comparable sets. The input is already a single, internally consistent marker database that uses standard HGNC/MGI gene symbols and Cell Ontology terms — re-mapping adds no value. The analysis goal is automatic cell type annotation of a single-cell/spatial dataset with the Cell Marker Accordion algorithm (use the accordion() annotation workflow instead of cross-database harmonization). Cell type labels cannot be confidently mapped to Cell Ontology terms (e.g., purely novel or disease-specific aberrant states with no ontology correspondence). http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 Standardizes gene symbols and cell type labels across heterogeneous marker gene databases (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB, cell-sorting collections) using HGNC/MGI for genes and the Cell Ontology for cell types, enabling consistent downstream comparisons such as Jaccard overlap analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Standardizes gene symbols and cell type labels across heterogeneous marker gene databases (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB, cell-sorting collections) using HGNC/MGI for genes and the Cell Ontology for cell types, enabling consistent downstream comparisons such as Jaccard overlap analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a single, internally consistent marker database that uses standard HGNC/MGI gene symbols and Cell Ontology terms — re-mapping adds no value. The analysis goal is automatic cell type annotation of a single-cell/spatial dataset with the Cell Marker Accordion algorithm (use the accordion() annotation workflow instead of cross-database harmonization). Cell type labels cannot be confidently mapped to Cell Ontology terms (e.g., purely novel or disease-specific aberrant states with no ontology correspondence).

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix with per-cell metadata assigning condition, patient, and cluster, and need to identify which predefined cell types are transcriptomically perturbed between two conditions.
skills.name: cell-type-perturbation-detection
skills.search_text: cell-type-perturbation-detection Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix with per-cell metadata assigning condition, patient, and cluster, and need to identify which predefined cell types are transcriptomically perturbed between two conditions. Goal is differential abundance (changing cell-type proportions) rather than differential state — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead Only raw counts are available with no normalized matrix — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts Data are heavily over-clustered, since condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances (false negatives) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect cell types with distinct transcriptomic profiles between conditions (differential state analysis) using scDist, a mixed-effects model that estimates the distance between condition means in gene-expression space while accounting for individual-to-individual and technical variability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Detect cell types with distinct transcriptomic profiles between conditions (differential state analysis) using scDist, a mixed-effects model that estimates the distance between condition means in gene-expression space while accounting for individual-to-individual and technical variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is differential abundance (changing cell-type proportions) rather than differential state — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead Only raw counts are available with no normalized matrix — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts Data are heavily over-clustered, since condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances (false negatives)

skills.description: Use when you have untreated diseased scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and a known drug target gene, and need to identify which cell types are drug-responsive or resistant without paired treated/untreated samples.
skills.name: cell-type-perturbation-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-perturbation-ranking Use when you have untreated diseased scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and a known drug target gene, and need to identify which cell types are drug-responsive or resistant without paired treated/untreated samples. The drug acts as an agonist — scRank primarily focuses on inhibitor drugs due to data availability, and agonist modeling is preliminary only The drug has multiple targets — multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank You need paired disease-treatment datasets analyzed by differential expression or separability-based methods (e.g., Augur) rather than target-informed in silico perturbation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank and infer drug-responsive cell populations from untreated single-cell transcriptomic data by simulating in silico drug perturbation of a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) with scRank, prioritizing cell types most sensitive to perturbing a known drug target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Rank and infer drug-responsive cell populations from untreated single-cell transcriptomic data by simulating in silico drug perturbation of a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) with scRank, prioritizing cell types most sensitive to perturbing a known drug target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts as an agonist — scRank primarily focuses on inhibitor drugs due to data availability, and agonist modeling is preliminary only The drug has multiple targets — multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank You need paired disease-treatment datasets analyzed by differential expression or separability-based methods (e.g., Augur) rather than target-informed in silico perturbation

skills.description: Use when cell-type proportions have been estimated from bulk RNA-seq (via BisqueRNA bulk.props or BisqueMarker) and you need to test associations with phenotypes such as BMI, Matsuda index, or Braak stage, replicating reported cell-composition associations.
skills.name: cell-type-phenotype-association-testing
skills.search_text: cell-type-phenotype-association-testing Use when cell-type proportions have been estimated from bulk RNA-seq (via BisqueRNA bulk.props or BisqueMarker) and you need to test associations with phenotypes such as BMI, Matsuda index, or Braak stage, replicating reported cell-composition associations. Comparing absolute abundance magnitudes across cell types from BisqueMarker output, since marker-based estimates are relative abundances that cannot be compared between cell types Decomposition itself is needed — this skill assumes bulk.props estimates already exist Reference profile or gene-specific transformations are unreliable because too few individuals have single-cell data (a stated Bisque limitation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Tests whether cell-type proportions estimated by Bisque (reference-based) or BisqueMarker (marker-based) decomposition of bulk RNA-seq are significantly associated with measured phenotypes, via linear (mixed) regression with demographic covariates. It is the validation layer that turns decomposition outputs into replicable biological findings, e.g. adipocyte-BMI, macrophage-BMI, T-cell-Matsuda, and microglia-Braak associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Tests whether cell-type proportions estimated by Bisque (reference-based) or BisqueMarker (marker-based) decomposition of bulk RNA-seq are significantly associated with measured phenotypes, via linear (mixed) regression with demographic covariates. It is the validation layer that turns decomposition outputs into replicable biological findings, e.g. adipocyte-BMI, macrophage-BMI, T-cell-Matsuda, and microglia-Braak associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing absolute abundance magnitudes across cell types from BisqueMarker output, since marker-based estimates are relative abundances that cannot be compared between cell types Decomposition itself is needed — this skill assumes bulk.props estimates already exist Reference profile or gene-specific transformations are unreliable because too few individuals have single-cell data (a stated Bisque limitation)

skills.description: Use when single-cell AnnData atlases spanning multiple ages (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, 1-30 months) must be scored for senescence and aggregated into per-cell-type positive-cell proportions or old/young ratios.
skills.name: cell-type-positive-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-type-positive-fraction-quantification Use when single-cell AnnData atlases spanning multiple ages (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, 1-30 months) must be scored for senescence and aggregated into per-cell-type positive-cell proportions or old/young ratios. Data are scaled: score_hub requires non-scaled data ('Just make sure they are not scaled'), so applying the scoring to scaled AnnData matrices is invalid. The goal is single-marker differential expression per se rather than quantifying the proportion of cells positive for senescence signatures across cell types and ages. Input is bulk transcriptomics or lacks cell-type annotations, so positive-cell fractions cannot be aggregated per cell type. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify how the fraction of cells scored positive for cellular senescence signatures (via SenePy hub scoring with binarization and hub-network importance weighting) changes across cell types and age groups in the Tabula Muris Senis mouse atlas and a human aging atlas, recovering marker-specific dynamics such as CDKN2A being dynamic in only ~26% of human and ~32% of mouse cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Quantify how the fraction of cells scored positive for cellular senescence signatures (via SenePy hub scoring with binarization and hub-network importance weighting) changes across cell types and age groups in the Tabula Muris Senis mouse atlas and a human aging atlas, recovering marker-specific dynamics such as CDKN2A being dynamic in only ~26% of human and ~32% of mouse cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are scaled: score_hub requires non-scaled data ('Just make sure they are not scaled'), so applying the scoring to scaled AnnData matrices is invalid. The goal is single-marker differential expression per se rather than quantifying the proportion of cells positive for senescence signatures across cell types and ages. Input is bulk transcriptomics or lacks cell-type annotations, so positive-cell fractions cannot be aggregated per cell type.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq count matrix with malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations is available and the goal is to estimate and rank differentiation potency of cell types without marker genes, feature selection, or training.
skills.name: cell-type-potency-ranking-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-potency-ranking-analysis Use when a scRNA-Seq count matrix with malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations is available and the goal is to estimate and rank differentiation potency of cell types without marker genes, feature selection, or training. The task requires reconstructing developmental trajectories or lineage ordering by expression dynamics — the article notes this insight is not readily obtainable using other algorithms such as Monocle or MPath, but SCENT provides potency ordering, not Monocle-style trajectory fitting. Only network-free transcriptomic entropy is desired (e.g. StemID/SLICE-style measures) — signalling entropy's advantage is driven by a positive correlation between the transcriptome and the connectome, so it requires an interaction network. Marker-gene-based cell identification is sufficient and dropout is not a concern — SCENT's value is potency estimation without prior biological knowledge such as marker expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Compute per-cell signalling entropy (SR) with SCENT's SignallingEntropy routine over a protein interaction network to rank cell types by differentiation potency, e.g. reproducing the Tirosh melanoma result where cancer cells show dramatically higher SR than non-malignant tumour-microenvironment cells (Wilcoxon rank-sum P<1e-500). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Compute per-cell signalling entropy (SR) with SCENT's SignallingEntropy routine over a protein interaction network to rank cell types by differentiation potency, e.g. reproducing the Tirosh melanoma result where cancer cells show dramatically higher SR than non-malignant tumour-microenvironment cells (Wilcoxon rank-sum P<1e-500).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires reconstructing developmental trajectories or lineage ordering by expression dynamics — the article notes this insight is not readily obtainable using other algorithms such as Monocle or MPath, but SCENT provides potency ordering, not Monocle-style trajectory fitting. Only network-free transcriptomic entropy is desired (e.g. StemID/SLICE-style measures) — signalling entropy's advantage is driven by a positive correlation between the transcriptome and the connectome, so it requires an interaction network. Marker-gene-based cell identification is sufficient and dropout is not a concern — SCENT's value is potency estimation without prior biological knowledge such as marker expression.

skills.description: Use when single-cell expression data has a small labeled training set and you need probabilistic cell type predictions plus predictive entropy to guide cell selection or evaluate annotation uncertainty.
skills.name: cell-type-probability-classification
skills.search_text: cell-type-probability-classification Use when single-cell expression data has a small labeled training set and you need probabilistic cell type predictions plus predictive entropy to guide cell selection or evaluate annotation uncertainty. When the goal is de novo clustering rather than supervised probability-based annotation of known or partially known cell types When no ground truth or training labels exist at all — entropy-based novelty detection here still requires a labeled training set to train the classifiers When a cell type is so rare that no cells can be sampled into the 20-cell training set — interpretation of entropy as active-learning signal rather than absence must then be verified http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Train supervised classifiers (random forest and logistic regression via caret) on the first 20 principal components of scaled, centered logcount single-cell expression data to produce per-cell-type probability predictions, whose uncertainty (predictive entropy) can be scored against ground truth labels for active learning evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Train supervised classifiers (random forest and logistic regression via caret) on the first 20 principal components of scaled, centered logcount single-cell expression data to produce per-cell-type probability predictions, whose uncertainty (predictive entropy) can be scored against ground truth labels for active learning evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo clustering rather than supervised probability-based annotation of known or partially known cell types When no ground truth or training labels exist at all — entropy-based novelty detection here still requires a labeled training set to train the classifiers When a cell type is so rare that no cells can be sampled into the 20-cell training set — interpretation of entropy as active-learning signal rather than absence must then be verified

skills.description: Use when ST pixels are cell mixtures and you need to assign reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles to known cell populations and compare them across conditions (e.g., aged vs young) for perturbation-driven gene changes.
skills.name: cell-type-profile-matching
skills.search_text: cell-type-profile-matching Use when ST pixels are cell mixtures and you need to assign reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles to known cell populations and compare them across conditions (e.g., aged vs young) for perturbation-driven gene changes. Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack variability across pixels — STdeconvolve may fail to deconvolve distinct cell types ST data are too sparse with high stochastic drop-out rates, which the LDA model may struggle to separate into co-expressed gene groups The tissue covers only a few pixels (e.g., tissue slivers or thin structures), which challenges deconvolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Matches reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles (beta matrices from STdeconvolve's LDA) to known cell populations, then computes gene-wise log2 fold-changes between deconvolved profiles across conditions (e.g., aged vs young macrophages) to recover perturbation-driven expression changes without a single-cell reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Matches reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles (beta matrices from STdeconvolve's LDA) to known cell populations, then computes gene-wise log2 fold-changes between deconvolved profiles across conditions (e.g., aged vs young macrophages) to recover perturbation-driven expression changes without a single-cell reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack variability across pixels — STdeconvolve may fail to deconvolve distinct cell types ST data are too sparse with high stochastic drop-out rates, which the LDA model may struggle to separate into co-expressed gene groups The tissue covers only a few pixels (e.g., tissue slivers or thin structures), which challenges deconvolution

skills.description: Decision support for validating false-positive control of Scanpro proportion analysis on null simulations, and for choosing pseudo-replicate counts (2–14) based on total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells).
skills.name: cell-type-proportion-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-proportion-accuracy-evaluation Decision support for validating false-positive control of Scanpro proportion analysis on null simulations, and for choosing pseudo-replicate counts (2–14) based on total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells). Datasets where clusters are supported by less than 2% of all cells — the article's benchmarking found such clusters produce unstable results Handling rare cell types — bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types per the benchmarking and real-dataset results Clusters that may be defined by technical parameters (e.g. batch effects from different sequencing machines or timepoints) rather than true cell types — PA interpretation requires care before trusting accuracy estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark approach for evaluating how accurately Scanpro controls false positives in cell-type proportion analysis, using simulated null datasets and bootstrapped pseudo-replicates, and for selecting the optimal pseudo-replicate count as a function of total cells per condition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Benchmark approach for evaluating how accurately Scanpro controls false positives in cell-type proportion analysis, using simulated null datasets and bootstrapped pseudo-replicates, and for selecting the optimal pseudo-replicate count as a function of total cells per condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets where clusters are supported by less than 2% of all cells — the article's benchmarking found such clusters produce unstable results Handling rare cell types — bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types per the benchmarking and real-dataset results Clusters that may be defined by technical parameters (e.g. batch effects from different sequencing machines or timepoints) rather than true cell types — PA interpretation requires care before trusting accuracy estimates

skills.name: cell-type-proportion-computation-per-condition
skills.search_text: cell-type-proportion-computation-per-condition Use when comparing cell-type composition of an AI-generated (semi-profiled) cohort against real-profiled single-cell ground truth across defined conditions, e.g. COVID-19 severity states (Healthy, Asymptomatic, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Critical). You only have bulk data and no single-cell reference or annotated representative samples — scSemiProfiler's single-cell level deconvolution requires a single-cell reference to guide inference and classifier training The goal is generic bulk deconvolution at cell-type resolution without single-cell inference — deconvolution tools like CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, or NNLS are the conventional alternative Input data is already a feature/proportion table with no per-cell annotations — recompute proportions only after cell-type assignment via the trained classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-sample and per-condition cell-type proportion vectors from annotated single-cell data (semi-profiled and real-profiled) using the scSemiProfiler cell-type-proportion utility, then quantifies cohort similarity with per-condition Pearson correlations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Computes per-sample and per-condition cell-type proportion vectors from annotated single-cell data (semi-profiled and real-profiled) using the scSemiProfiler cell-type-proportion utility, then quantifies cohort similarity with per-condition Pearson correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have bulk data and no single-cell reference or annotated representative samples — scSemiProfiler's single-cell level deconvolution requires a single-cell reference to guide inference and classifier training The goal is generic bulk deconvolution at cell-type resolution without single-cell inference — deconvolution tools like CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, or NNLS are the conventional alternative Input data is already a feature/proportion table with no per-cell annotations — recompute proportions only after cell-type assignment via the trained classifier

skills.name: cell-type-proportion-controlled-synthetic-data-generation
skills.search_text: cell-type-proportion-controlled-synthetic-data-generation Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix with known ground-truth cell-type labels and controlled per-type cell numbers — e.g. to benchmark clustering methods on a rare cell type (<5% of cells). You need real, not simulated, single-cell data for your benchmark — this skill produces synthetic counts with ground-truth labels only Your reference data has no cell-type annotations, since scDesign2 must fit per-cell-type marginal parameters You require cluster number to be unknown a priori; here the five ground-truth types are imposed by the simulation design http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates a synthetic scRNA-seq count matrix with scDesign2 by fitting per-cell-type gene marginal and gene-gene correlation parameters to a real reference dataset (10x PBMC, Zheng et al. 2017) and simulating specified cell-type sizes, so rare populations are represented at controlled frequencies for clustering benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic scRNA-seq count matrix with scDesign2 by fitting per-cell-type gene marginal and gene-gene correlation parameters to a real reference dataset (10x PBMC, Zheng et al. 2017) and simulating specified cell-type sizes, so rare populations are represented at controlled frequencies for clustering benchmarks.

skills.search_text: cell-type-proportion-correlation-analysis Use when evaluating SC-ST mapping outputs (SC-ST / ST-SC mapping matrices) against ground-truth ST cell-type labels, to quantify whether each method preserves cell-type composition of spots rather than just coordinate accuracy. Real datasets without ground-truth spot cell-type labels (the paper's PCC metric is computed on semi-simulation E1z2 data where ground truth is known) When the analysis goal is coordinate-level accuracy alone — use MAE between predicted and ground-truth spatial coordinates instead When the goal is neighborhood reconstruction fidelity — use hit-number@K (K=200) against ground-truth adjacency instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks SC-ST mapping methods by comparing per-cell-type proportions predicted from a mapping matrix against ground-truth spot cell-type labels using per-cell-type Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), as done in the STEM paper's semi-simulation E1z2 benchmark alongside MAE and hit-number@K. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1

skills.search_text: cell-type-proportion-correlation-evaluation Use when a decomposition method's estimated cell-type proportions (e.g., BisqueRNA's res$bulk.props) must be scored against known or reference proportions per individual and cell type using Pearson correlation and RMSD. skills.summary: Aggregate per-cell differential abundance (DA) scores from a DA-seq analysis of scMerge2-integrated single-cell data by annotated cell type, yielding the proportion of condition-associated cells within each type — used to rank cell types (e.g. neutrophils) by association with severe COVID-19 outcome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack cell-type annotations, so per-cell DA scores cannot be aggregated into per-type proportions The input expression matrix has not been integrated across samples/studies (dataset variability has not been removed, e.g. with scMerge2), so per-cell abundance differences may reflect batch or study effects rather than condition The analysis goal is joint integration of multiple modalities — the paper's integration was performed within each modality only, deferring multi-modal integration to future work

skills.description: Use when a joint latent embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent in mdata.obsm['latent']) must be quantitatively validated against known cell-type labels, as in diagonal-integration benchmarks or hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps.
skills.name: cell-type-purity-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-purity-evaluation Use when a joint latent embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent in mdata.obsm['latent']) must be quantitatively validated against known cell-type labels, as in diagonal-integration benchmarks or hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps. The data have no reliable cell-type labels (e.g. unannotated modality-specific populations), where label-free metrics like FOSCTTM or graph connectivity are needed instead The goal is to assess cross-modality nearest-neighbor consistency rather than label homogeneity — FOSCTTM is the appropriate metric there Comparing embeddings whose neighborhood-graph construction (k, representation) differs, since purity values are not comparable across different graph settings http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores a shared latent embedding from single-cell multimodal integration by cell-type purity: for each cell, check whether its nearest neighbors in the joint space carry the same cell-type label. It is one of the five benchmark metrics used to show scConfluence outperforms Seurat, Liger, MultiMAP, Uniport and scGLUE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
