skills.description: Use when a scRank analysis has produced a ranked list of drug-responsive cell types (obj@cell_type_rank) and you need to check or display how the ranking distributes across single cells on a dimension-reduction embedding.
skills.name: cell-type-rank-dimension-reduction-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-type-rank-dimension-reduction-visualization Use when a scRank analysis has produced a ranked list of drug-responsive cell types (obj@cell_type_rank) and you need to check or display how the ranking distributes across single cells on a dimension-reduction embedding. The scRank object has not yet been scored with rank_celltype, so no cell-type ranking exists to visualize. The input requires paired disease-vs-treated data or differential expression alone, since scRank is designed for untreated single-cell data only. The drug is an agonist or multi-target compound, where scRank's perturbation model (target-gene node deletion for inhibitors) is only preliminary and the ranking visualization would be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Visualize the scRank drug-responsive cell-type ranking in dimension-reduction space using the plot_dim function, so that per-cell in silico perturbation scores from rank_celltype can be inspected on a UMAP/t-SNE embedding alongside the exported cell_type_rank table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Visualize the scRank drug-responsive cell-type ranking in dimension-reduction space using the plot_dim function, so that per-cell in silico perturbation scores from rank_celltype can be inspected on a UMAP/t-SNE embedding alongside the exported cell_type_rank table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRank object has not yet been scored with rank_celltype, so no cell-type ranking exists to visualize. The input requires paired disease-vs-treated data or differential expression alone, since scRank is designed for untreated single-cell data only. The drug is an agonist or multi-target compound, where scRank's perturbation model (target-gene node deletion for inhibitors) is only preliminary and the ranking visualization would be unreliable.

skills.description: Use when selecting a graining level for metacell construction and you need to check that rare cell populations are not merged into other types, especially in datasets of varying complexity or size.
skills.name: cell-type-recovery-assessment-across-graining-levels
skills.search_text: cell-type-recovery-assessment-across-graining-levels Use when selecting a graining level for metacell construction and you need to check that rare cell populations are not merged into other types, especially in datasets of varying complexity or size. The goal is metacell construction quality (compactness, separation, INV) rather than cell-type recovery — use the QC metric suite instead. Single-cell data lack a cell-type annotation, since purity requires sc_data$celltype to score metacell homogeneity. Data are already at metacell level (e.g. an existing MCView or h5ad metacell model) with no access to the underlying single-cell membership. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A graining-level sweep that builds metacells from single-cell data at multiple coarseness settings and quantifies how well cell types are recovered via metacell purity, revealing when rare populations are merged away in complex datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: A graining-level sweep that builds metacells from single-cell data at multiple coarseness settings and quantifies how well cell types are recovered via metacell purity, revealing when rare populations are merged away in complex datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is metacell construction quality (compactness, separation, INV) rather than cell-type recovery — use the QC metric suite instead. Single-cell data lack a cell-type annotation, since purity requires sc_data$celltype to score metacell homogeneity. Data are already at metacell level (e.g. an existing MCView or h5ad metacell model) with no access to the underlying single-cell membership.

skills.description: Use when comparing pathway activity scoring methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cell labels exist (e.g., SERGIO simulations or annotated datasets), to measure cell-type recovery AUC and accuracy.
skills.name: cell-type-recovery-auc-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-recovery-auc-evaluation Use when comparing pathway activity scoring methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cell labels exist (e.g., SERGIO simulations or annotated datasets), to measure cell-type recovery AUC and accuracy. The data are spatial transcriptomics or trajectory analyses with no ground-truth cell-type labels — use GSDensity's compute.spatial.kld or trajectory workflow instead Only a single method needs to be applied to new data (no benchmarking) — run the GSDensity pipeline directly rather than the comparison harness Data are targeted gene panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity is explicitly unsuitable for such targeted gene data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark framework for evaluating how well gene set/pathway scoring methods (GSDensity vs ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) recover known cell types, quantified as AUC and cell typing accuracy over SERGIO-simulated and real single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Benchmark framework for evaluating how well gene set/pathway scoring methods (GSDensity vs ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) recover known cell types, quantified as AUC and cell typing accuracy over SERGIO-simulated and real single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are spatial transcriptomics or trajectory analyses with no ground-truth cell-type labels — use GSDensity's compute.spatial.kld or trajectory workflow instead Only a single method needs to be applied to new data (no benchmarking) — run the GSDensity pipeline directly rather than the comparison harness Data are targeted gene panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity is explicitly unsuitable for such targeted gene data

skills.description: Use when annotating single-cell RNA-seq cells via marker counting and you must conservatively reject low-confidence assignments (possible unknown cell types) before downstream cluster reassignment.
skills.name: cell-type-rejection-thresholding
skills.search_text: cell-type-rejection-thresholding Use when annotating single-cell RNA-seq cells via marker counting and you must conservatively reject low-confidence assignments (possible unknown cell types) before downstream cluster reassignment. All cell populations are well separated by normalized marker counts alone, so no rejection/reassignment stage is needed (e.g. clearly separable pancreas or blood populations) The task is hierarchical marker-based annotation of immune subtypes — use the successor tool HiCAT instead of the MarkerCount rejection pipeline Cell populations are not well clustered, since cluster-basis reassignment assumes each population forms a coherent cluster http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A conservative rejection-threshold strategy from MarkerCount that labels cells as 'unassigned' when their normalized marker count falls below a cell-type-specific threshold, deferring ambiguous cells to cluster-basis reassignment instead of forcing a wrong annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: A conservative rejection-threshold strategy from MarkerCount that labels cells as 'unassigned' when their normalized marker count falls below a cell-type-specific threshold, deferring ambiguous cells to cluster-basis reassignment instead of forcing a wrong annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All cell populations are well separated by normalized marker counts alone, so no rejection/reassignment stage is needed (e.g. clearly separable pancreas or blood populations) The task is hierarchical marker-based annotation of immune subtypes — use the successor tool HiCAT instead of the MarkerCount rejection pipeline Cell populations are not well clustered, since cluster-basis reassignment assumes each population forms a coherent cluster

skills.description: Use when you need to assess whether a subsampled ('sketched') single-cell dataset preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, by harmonizing labels with CellHint and comparing the inferred relationship tree against a full-data reference tree.
skills.name: cell-type-relationship-tree-inference
skills.search_text: cell-type-relationship-tree-inference Use when you need to assess whether a subsampled ('sketched') single-cell dataset preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, by harmonizing labels with CellHint and comparing the inferred relationship tree against a full-data reference tree. The analysis goal is cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g. CellTypist/scANVI tasks) rather than cross-study label harmonization and subtype relationship structure No cell type labels are available in adata.obs for the dataset or the sketches, since CellHint harmonization and scValue's cell_type_key both require annotations The dataset is small enough to run CellHint directly on all cells, making sketch-based tree comparison unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds a cross-study cell-type subtype relationship tree with CellHint on a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the 200k-cell human Spleen dataset) and compares trees derived from subsampled sketches against the full-data reference tree, here to show that a 10% scValue sketch best preserves fine-grained T-cell subtype relationships. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Builds a cross-study cell-type subtype relationship tree with CellHint on a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the 200k-cell human Spleen dataset) and compares trees derived from subsampled sketches against the full-data reference tree, here to show that a 10% scValue sketch best preserves fine-grained T-cell subtype relationships.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g. CellTypist/scANVI tasks) rather than cross-study label harmonization and subtype relationship structure No cell type labels are available in adata.obs for the dataset or the sketches, since CellHint harmonization and scValue's cell_type_key both require annotations The dataset is small enough to run CellHint directly on all cells, making sketch-based tree comparison unnecessary

skills.description: Use when several pre-computed cell-cell communication (CCI) datasets from different conditions must be compared cell-type-wise, to test whether a cell type (e.g., mast cells or NKT-p) consistently mediates more interactions in one condition.
skills.name: cell-type-relative-interaction-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-type-relative-interaction-quantification Use when several pre-computed cell-cell communication (CCI) datasets from different conditions must be compared cell-type-wise, to test whether a cell type (e.g., mast cells or NKT-p) consistently mediates more interactions in one condition. Only a single condition/dataset is available — the multiple-condition comparison and radar overlays require at least two CCI datasets to contrast The goal is de novo inference of ligand-receptor interactions from a scRNA-seq expression matrix — InterCellar builds on pre-computed, inferred ligand-receptor interactions, not raw counts A tool outside InterCellar's supported set was used to compute the CCI data — input options cover CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET and SingleCellSignalR http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify, for each cell type within a condition, the relative number of predicted ligand-receptor interactions with all other clusters, and overlay profiles across multiple conditions (e.g., control, moderate, and critical COVID-19) using InterCellar's multiple-condition radar plots to reveal condition-specific communication patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Quantify, for each cell type within a condition, the relative number of predicted ligand-receptor interactions with all other clusters, and overlay profiles across multiple conditions (e.g., control, moderate, and critical COVID-19) using InterCellar's multiple-condition radar plots to reveal condition-specific communication patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single condition/dataset is available — the multiple-condition comparison and radar overlays require at least two CCI datasets to contrast The goal is de novo inference of ligand-receptor interactions from a scRNA-seq expression matrix — InterCellar builds on pre-computed, inferred ligand-receptor interactions, not raw counts A tool outside InterCellar's supported set was used to compute the CCI data — input options cover CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET and SingleCellSignalR

skills.description: Use when you must stress-test whether a cross-dataset cell-type identification method still recovers a target type that is rare (1–20% of cells) and only subtly different from the out-group, rather than well-separated abundant types.
skills.name: cell-type-replicability-subsampling-simulation
skills.search_text: cell-type-replicability-subsampling-simulation Use when you must stress-test whether a cross-dataset cell-type identification method still recovers a target type that is rare (1–20% of cells) and only subtly different from the out-group, rather than well-separated abundant types. The question is identifying replicable cell types across datasets at natural abundance — use the unsupervised MetaNeighbor workflow (variableGenes + reciprocal top hits, AUROC ≥ 0.95) instead of subsampling simulation. Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or their gene names do not match the expression-matrix row names, per the README requirements. No cell-type labels exist for the datasets, since the supervised MetaNeighbor analysis requires known corresponding types across datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Empirical robustness test for cross-dataset cell-type identification (Fig. 3b) that subsamples scRNA-seq cells to make a target cell type rare (1–20% incidence) and subtly distinct (up to ~88% subtlety), then measures MetaNeighbor supervised AUROC per condition against random 20-gene controls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Empirical robustness test for cross-dataset cell-type identification (Fig. 3b) that subsamples scRNA-seq cells to make a target cell type rare (1–20% incidence) and subtly distinct (up to ~88% subtlety), then measures MetaNeighbor supervised AUROC per condition against random 20-gene controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is identifying replicable cell types across datasets at natural abundance — use the unsupervised MetaNeighbor workflow (variableGenes + reciprocal top hits, AUROC ≥ 0.95) instead of subsampling simulation. Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or their gene names do not match the expression-matrix row names, per the README requirements. No cell-type labels exist for the datasets, since the supervised MetaNeighbor analysis requires known corresponding types across datasets.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a transcriptomic perturbation score (e.g., number of DEGs, scDist distance) scales with the number of cells per cell type in single-cell RNA-seq data, or when benchmarking speed of differential-state methods.
skills.name: cell-type-scaling-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-scaling-benchmark-analysis Use when evaluating whether a transcriptomic perturbation score (e.g., number of DEGs, scDist distance) scales with the number of cells per cell type in single-cell RNA-seq data, or when benchmarking speed of differential-state methods. Data are raw counts not yet normalized — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts and is sensitive to sub-optimal normalization Cell types are over-clustered or annotation is unreliable — double dipping of expression data for annotation and distance estimation causes over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances The question is differential abundance (changing cell proportions) rather than differential state — DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate tools, not this perturbation-distance benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill that resamples cells per cell type over a controlled grid to test whether a perturbation metric (e.g., nDEG vs. the scDist mixed-model distance) is confounded by cell count, and quantifies speed differences between methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that resamples cells per cell type over a controlled grid to test whether a perturbation metric (e.g., nDEG vs. the scDist mixed-model distance) is confounded by cell count, and quantifies speed differences between methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw counts not yet normalized — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts and is sensitive to sub-optimal normalization Cell types are over-clustered or annotation is unreliable — double dipping of expression data for annotation and distance estimation causes over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances The question is differential abundance (changing cell proportions) rather than differential state — DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate tools, not this perturbation-distance benchmark

skills.description: Use when a small marker-gene panel has been selected and you need a visual check that the reduced-dimensional projection separates known cell type labels into distinct clusters, e.g., reproducing a published t-SNE of cells projected onto 15 markers.
skills.name: cell-type-scatter-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-type-scatter-plot-visualization Use when a small marker-gene panel has been selected and you need a visual check that the reduced-dimensional projection separates known cell type labels into distinct clusters, e.g., reproducing a published t-SNE of cells projected onto 15 markers. Marker selection has not yet been performed and no reduced marker set is available — run scGeneFit marker selection first The goal is quantitative label-recovery accuracy rather than a visual separability check Cell labels are continuous (trajectories, spatial locations) rather than categorical — the paper notes categorical labeling is a current limitation Input is already a 2-D embedding; this skill is about building the embedding from a marker-gene projection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Visualize single cells in a low-dimensional marker space by embedding the reduced marker-gene projection with t-SNE and rendering a 2-D scatter plot colored by cell type label, to verify that the selected marker panel (e.g., scGeneFit's 15 markers on the CBMC dataset) preserves distinctions between cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Visualize single cells in a low-dimensional marker space by embedding the reduced marker-gene projection with t-SNE and rendering a 2-D scatter plot colored by cell type label, to verify that the selected marker panel (e.g., scGeneFit's 15 markers on the CBMC dataset) preserves distinctions between cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Marker selection has not yet been performed and no reduced marker set is available — run scGeneFit marker selection first The goal is quantitative label-recovery accuracy rather than a visual separability check Cell labels are continuous (trajectories, spatial locations) rather than categorical — the paper notes categorical labeling is a current limitation Input is already a 2-D embedding; this skill is about building the embedding from a marker-gene projection

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-type-by-cell score matrix (es.max) from sctype_score() and Seurat cluster identities and must assign a single label per cluster, with an Unknown fallback for low-confidence assignments.
skills.name: cell-type-score-aggregation-across-clusters
skills.search_text: cell-type-score-aggregation-across-clusters Use when you have a cell-type-by-cell score matrix (es.max) from sctype_score() and Seurat cluster identities and must assign a single label per cluster, with an Unknown fallback for low-confidence assignments. The tissue of interest is absent from the ScType database (tissues comprising fewer than 5 cell types were excluded during database construction) Only per-cell scores are needed downstream (e.g. cell-level visualization) and cluster-level summarization would lose resolution A labeled reference dataset is available and a supervised classifier such as CaSTLe or ACTINN is preferred Converts per-cell ScType scores from sctype_score() into one cell-type label per Seurat cluster by aggregating scores (row-sums) per cluster, taking the top-scoring type, and labeling low-confidence clusters 'Unknown' when scores fall below ncells/4 — the decisive step that yields fully-automated cluster annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Converts per-cell ScType scores from sctype_score() into one cell-type label per Seurat cluster by aggregating scores (row-sums) per cluster, taking the top-scoring type, and labeling low-confidence clusters 'Unknown' when scores fall below ncells/4 — the decisive step that yields fully-automated cluster annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue of interest is absent from the ScType database (tissues comprising fewer than 5 cell types were excluded during database construction) Only per-cell scores are needed downstream (e.g. cell-level visualization) and cluster-level summarization would lose resolution A labeled reference dataset is available and a supervised classifier such as CaSTLe or ACTINN is preferred

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis requires scoring cells against known cell-type markers (e.g., producing per-cell scores/labels for MASI-based annotation or for pipeline variants in integration benchmarks).
skills.name: cell-type-score-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-score-computation Use when a scRNA-seq analysis requires scoring cells against known cell-type markers (e.g., producing per-cell scores/labels for MASI-based annotation or for pipeline variants in integration benchmarks). Query data contains unseen cell types not present in the reference — MASI scores alone cannot annotate those; combine MASI with SCCAF to identify subtypes. Reference data quality or resolution does not match the query — MASI annotation accuracy depends on reference quality, so poor reference choice invalidates the scores. Input is raw counts without LogNormalization (scale factor 10,000 + log transform) — the PlinerScore transformation expects normalized expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts a LogNormalized gene expression matrix into a cell-type score matrix using MASI's gene2cell, applying the PlinerScore transformation (TF-IDF normalization plus 0.25-percentile thresholding) and weighted summation of ranked marker genes per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Converts a LogNormalized gene expression matrix into a cell-type score matrix using MASI's gene2cell, applying the PlinerScore transformation (TF-IDF normalization plus 0.25-percentile thresholding) and weighted summation of ranked marker genes per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data contains unseen cell types not present in the reference — MASI scores alone cannot annotate those; combine MASI with SCCAF to identify subtypes. Reference data quality or resolution does not match the query — MASI annotation accuracy depends on reference quality, so poor reference choice invalidates the scores. Input is raw counts without LogNormalization (scale factor 10,000 + log transform) — the PlinerScore transformation expects normalized expression.

skills.description: Use when transferring labels from a reference atlas with MASI and query data may contain cell types not present in the reference: cells whose closest-centroid distance approaches their farthest-centroid distance (ratio near 1, certainty near 0) should be flagged as unassigned.
skills.name: cell-type-score-space-centroid-distance-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-score-space-centroid-distance-analysis Use when transferring labels from a reference atlas with MASI and query data may contain cell types not present in the reference: cells whose closest-centroid distance approaches their farthest-centroid distance (ratio near 1, certainty near 0) should be flagged as unassigned. The query dataset is known to contain only cell types present in the reference — the certainty score only needs to flag unseen types The goal is to discover subtypes within major cell types rather than flag unassigned cells — the article instead recommends combining MASI with SCCAF for that Input is raw counts without LogNormalization — MASI's score conversion expects normalized expression (LogNormalized, 10,000 scale factor followed by log-transformation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Flags cells whose true cell type is absent from the reference by computing MASI's certainty score C = 1 - D1st/DNth — the ratio of each cell's distance to the closest versus least-close reference cell-type centroid in the cell-type score space produced by masi.gene2cell — and labelling cells below a chosen threshold as unassigned. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Flags cells whose true cell type is absent from the reference by computing MASI's certainty score C = 1 - D1st/DNth — the ratio of each cell's distance to the closest versus least-close reference cell-type centroid in the cell-type score space produced by masi.gene2cell — and labelling cells below a chosen threshold as unassigned.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset is known to contain only cell types present in the reference — the certainty score only needs to flag unseen types The goal is to discover subtypes within major cell types rather than flag unassigned cells — the article instead recommends combining MASI with SCCAF for that Input is raw counts without LogNormalization — MASI's score conversion expects normalized expression (LogNormalized, 10,000 scale factor followed by log-transformation)

skills.description: Use when a VEGA (or similar interpretable VAE) model has been trained on single-cell RNA-seq with gene-module-wired latents and you must check that latent dimensions separate annotated cell populations before interpreting module activities.
skills.name: cell-type-separation-visualization
skills.search_text: cell-type-separation-visualization Use when a VEGA (or similar interpretable VAE) model has been trained on single-cell RNA-seq with gene-module-wired latents and you must check that latent dimensions separate annotated cell populations before interpreting module activities. The model is a generic black-box VAE (e.g. plain scVI) whose latent dimensions are not tied to gene modules — separation would not be interpretable per module The input data lacks pre-annotated cell type labels, so separation cannot be assessed against a ground truth Prior gene module knowledge (e.g. MSigDB) is incomplete or not context-specific for the tissue, so GMV wiring may misrepresent the biology http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Visualize the VEGA-trained interpretable latent embedding (e.g. via UMAP) colored by pre-annotated cell types to verify that the GMV-structured latent space disentangles cell type and cell state identity, as demonstrated for the Darmanis GBM single-cell dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Visualize the VEGA-trained interpretable latent embedding (e.g. via UMAP) colored by pre-annotated cell types to verify that the GMV-structured latent space disentangles cell type and cell state identity, as demonstrated for the Darmanis GBM single-cell dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is a generic black-box VAE (e.g. plain scVI) whose latent dimensions are not tied to gene modules — separation would not be interpretable per module The input data lacks pre-annotated cell type labels, so separation cannot be assessed against a ground truth Prior gene module knowledge (e.g. MSigDB) is incomplete or not context-specific for the tissue, so GMV wiring may misrepresent the biology

skills.description: Use when you need to infer relative cell type composition from bulk RNA-seq by scoring curated cell-type gene signatures (GMT module lists) with sample-level PC1 module activity rather than a regression-based deconvolution tool.
skills.name: cell-type-signature-deconvolution
skills.search_text: cell-type-signature-deconvolution Use when you need to infer relative cell type composition from bulk RNA-seq by scoring curated cell-type gene signatures (GMT module lists) with sample-level PC1 module activity rather than a regression-based deconvolution tool. The expression matrix is raw counts — rRoma requires normalized data, so normalization must happen first The goal is testing broad pathway activity databases (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK across a disease contrast) rather than estimating cell type abundance from curated cell-type signatures You need absolute cell fractions from a mixture model — rROMA provides relative module activity scores, not a regression-based deconvolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate cell type abundances from bulk transcriptomic data by running rROMA on normalized gene-by-sample matrices with cell-type gene signature GMT files (e.g. Plasschaert, Okuda airway epithelial signatures), using PC1 sample scores per signature module as abundance proxies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Estimate cell type abundances from bulk transcriptomic data by running rROMA on normalized gene-by-sample matrices with cell-type gene signature GMT files (e.g. Plasschaert, Okuda airway epithelial signatures), using PC1 sample scores per signature module as abundance proxies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw counts — rRoma requires normalized data, so normalization must happen first The goal is testing broad pathway activity databases (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK across a disease contrast) rather than estimating cell type abundance from curated cell-type signatures You need absolute cell fractions from a mixture model — rROMA provides relative module activity scores, not a regression-based deconvolution

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation or integration methods on the same labeled multi-batch scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized scores (silhouette, batch entropy, F1, accuracy) plus statistical significance.
skills.name: cell-type-silhouette-and-batch-entropy-metrics
skills.search_text: cell-type-silhouette-and-batch-entropy-metrics Use when comparing cell-type annotation or integration methods on the same labeled multi-batch scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized scores (silhouette, batch entropy, F1, accuracy) plus statistical significance. Data have no reference cell-type labels — cell-type silhouette, macro F1, and accuracy cannot be computed without ground-truth annotations Data have no batch or condition annotation — batch entropy mixing cannot be defined You need de novo discovery of unseen cell types rather than comparing methods on shared label sets (the MASI paper notes MASI alone cannot annotate unseen cell types; SCCAF is needed for subtypes) Quantitative evaluation suite for scRNA-seq label-transfer/integration benchmarks: compute macro F1, overall accuracy, cell-type silhouette (separation of cell types), and batch entropy (batch mixing) per method, then aggregate into annotation, integration, and overall performance scores and test differences with paired t-tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Quantitative evaluation suite for scRNA-seq label-transfer/integration benchmarks: compute macro F1, overall accuracy, cell-type silhouette (separation of cell types), and batch entropy (batch mixing) per method, then aggregate into annotation, integration, and overall performance scores and test differences with paired t-tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have no reference cell-type labels — cell-type silhouette, macro F1, and accuracy cannot be computed without ground-truth annotations Data have no batch or condition annotation — batch entropy mixing cannot be defined You need de novo discovery of unseen cell types rather than comparing methods on shared label sets (the MASI paper notes MASI alone cannot annotate unseen cell types; SCCAF is needed for subtypes)

skills.description: Use when evaluating BIRD-predicted differential DH between many cell-type pairs and you need to know how prediction–truth correlation (Pearson, all loci vs differential loci) depends on the similarity of the two cell types' DH profiles.
skills.name: cell-type-similarity-quartile-stratification
skills.search_text: cell-type-similarity-quartile-stratification Use when evaluating BIRD-predicted differential DH between many cell-type pairs and you need to know how prediction–truth correlation (Pearson, all loci vs differential loci) depends on the similarity of the two cell types' DH profiles. You need single-sample (not pairwise differential) DH prediction accuracy — use direct per-sample prediction–truth correlation instead Your comparison involves fewer than ~8–10 cell types, where quartile stratification of pairs is unstable You lack a precomputed DH-profile similarity measure and cannot compute a defensible one — arbitrary strata will not reproduce the reported pattern http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Stratifies all pairwise comparisons of BIRD test cell types into quartiles of global DH-profile similarity, then aggregates per-pair differential DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) prediction correlations within each quartile to characterize prediction accuracy as a function of cell-type similarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Stratifies all pairwise comparisons of BIRD test cell types into quartiles of global DH-profile similarity, then aggregates per-pair differential DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) prediction correlations within each quartile to characterize prediction accuracy as a function of cell-type similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need single-sample (not pairwise differential) DH prediction accuracy — use direct per-sample prediction–truth correlation instead Your comparison involves fewer than ~8–10 cell types, where quartile stratification of pairs is unstable You lack a precomputed DH-profile similarity measure and cannot compute a defensible one — arbitrary strata will not reproduce the reported pattern

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into a spatially informed pseudo-space and you need to test whether the spatial proximity between annotated cell types differs between biological conditions (e.g., normal vs. disease).
skills.name: cell-type-spatial-distance-quantification
skills.search_text: cell-type-spatial-distance-quantification Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into a spatially informed pseudo-space and you need to test whether the spatial proximity between annotated cell types differs between biological conditions (e.g., normal vs. disease). When the input is raw ST data rather than projected single-cell coordinates — spatial domain identification methods like SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC target ST data, whereas this skill operates on scRNA-seq cells placed in pseudo-space When tissues have low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), since the reconstruction underlying the distances may be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies pairwise distances between cell types (e.g., myeloid vs. alveolar/airway epithelial cells) in a reconstructed pseudo-space to detect condition-specific spatial reorganization, as demonstrated for COVID-19 immune infiltration using scSpace. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Quantifies pairwise distances between cell types (e.g., myeloid vs. alveolar/airway epithelial cells) in a reconstructed pseudo-space to detect condition-specific spatial reorganization, as demonstrated for COVID-19 immune infiltration using scSpace.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw ST data rather than projected single-cell coordinates — spatial domain identification methods like SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC target ST data, whereas this skill operates on scRNA-seq cells placed in pseudo-space When tissues have low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), since the reconstruction underlying the distances may be unreliable

skills.description: Use when raw UMI-count scRNA-seq data need cell-type-specific co-expression networks, when correlation-based methods give inflated false positives due to sequencing depth confounding, or when differential co-expression between disease groups is sought.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-co-expression-inference
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-co-expression-inference Use when raw UMI-count scRNA-seq data need cell-type-specific co-expression networks, when correlation-based methods give inflated false positives due to sequencing depth confounding, or when differential co-expression between disease groups is sought. When aggregating cells across multiple cell types — CS-CORE is cell-type-specific and applying it to mixed populations confounds co-expression with varying cell-type compositions (Simpson's paradox risk). When the input is already a normalized/transformed expression matrix rather than raw UMI counts, since the measurement model is defined on Poisson UMI counts. When the target is bulk-sample co-expression inference — the article describes integrating bulk with single-cell data as a future opportunity, not an implemented capability. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Infers and tests cell-type-specific gene co-expressions from single-cell RNA-seq data using CS-CORE, which models sequencing depth variations and measurement errors via a Poisson measurement model and an IRLS-based correlation estimator, enabling reproducible co-expression networks and differential co-expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Infers and tests cell-type-specific gene co-expressions from single-cell RNA-seq data using CS-CORE, which models sequencing depth variations and measurement errors via a Poisson measurement model and an IRLS-based correlation estimator, enabling reproducible co-expression networks and differential co-expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When aggregating cells across multiple cell types — CS-CORE is cell-type-specific and applying it to mixed populations confounds co-expression with varying cell-type compositions (Simpson's paradox risk). When the input is already a normalized/transformed expression matrix rather than raw UMI counts, since the measurement model is defined on Poisson UMI counts. When the target is bulk-sample co-expression inference — the article describes integrating bulk with single-cell data as a future opportunity, not an implemented capability.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. BALF or PBMC count matrices from GEO) has been clustered and cell-type-annotated, and the goal is to test candidate genes (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) for differential expression between severity groups per cell type.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-differential-expression-analysis Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. BALF or PBMC count matrices from GEO) has been clustered and cell-type-annotated, and the goal is to test candidate genes (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) for differential expression between severity groups per cell type. Input is bulk RNAseq data rather than single-cell matrices — use the bulk severity database workflow (t-test, BH-adjusted p-values, fold-change per dataset) instead Cell clusters have not yet been defined or annotated — run clustering and annotation first before stratified testing The question requires timing/kinetics of expression rather than severity-group contrasts — longitudinal transcriptomics analysis is needed instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratified differential expression testing on annotated single-cell clusters, comparing disease severity groups (severe vs mild COVID-19) within each cell type using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests in Seurat, to reveal cell-type-resolved gene dysregulation such as HLA-DRA suppression in antigen-presenting cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: Stratified differential expression testing on annotated single-cell clusters, comparing disease severity groups (severe vs mild COVID-19) within each cell type using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests in Seurat, to reveal cell-type-resolved gene dysregulation such as HLA-DRA suppression in antigen-presenting cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNAseq data rather than single-cell matrices — use the bulk severity database workflow (t-test, BH-adjusted p-values, fold-change per dataset) instead Cell clusters have not yet been defined or annotated — run clustering and annotation first before stratified testing The question requires timing/kinetics of expression rather than severity-group contrasts — longitudinal transcriptomics analysis is needed instead

skills.description: Use when running deCS.fisher on a marker gene list or GWAS trait-associated gene list and you must first convert a cell type specificity score panel into discrete per-cell-type gene sets via a score cutoff.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-gene-thresholding
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-gene-thresholding Use when running deCS.fisher on a marker gene list or GWAS trait-associated gene list and you must first convert a cell type specificity score panel into discrete per-cell-type gene sets via a score cutoff. The query input is a gene expression profile rather than a gene list — use deCS.correlation() with the raw specificity score matrix instead of thresholding to CTgenes Novel cell types not represented in the reference panels need annotation — deCS, as a mapping-based toolkit, fails to characterize novel cell types regardless of cutoff Cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences from healthy reference cells can bias thresholded marker sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Defines cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) for each cell type in a deCS reference panel (e.g., BlueprintEncode_main, MonacoImmune_main) by thresholding pre-calculated t-score/z-score specificity matrices at a user-set ratio such as the top 5% highest-scoring genes. These CTgene sets are the overlap universe for deCS.fisher enrichment tests and GWAS trait–cell type association analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Defines cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) for each cell type in a deCS reference panel (e.g., BlueprintEncode_main, MonacoImmune_main) by thresholding pre-calculated t-score/z-score specificity matrices at a user-set ratio such as the top 5% highest-scoring genes. These CTgene sets are the overlap universe for deCS.fisher enrichment tests and GWAS trait–cell type association analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query input is a gene expression profile rather than a gene list — use deCS.correlation() with the raw specificity score matrix instead of thresholding to CTgenes Novel cell types not represented in the reference panels need annotation — deCS, as a mapping-based toolkit, fails to characterize novel cell types regardless of cutoff Cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences from healthy reference cells can bias thresholded marker sets

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq alignments and InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates are available and the goal is to flag IPA events whose usage is restricted to one cell type versus others.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-ipa-usage-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-ipa-usage-comparison Use when single-cell RNA-seq alignments and InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates are available and the goal is to flag IPA events whose usage is restricted to one cell type versus others. The input is bulk RNA-seq from a single condition with no cell-type labels — cell-type-specific comparison is undefined IPA sites have not yet been identified and quantified (no InPACT predict.result.txt or ipa_usage table) — run IPA identification and InPACT_quantify first The goal is 3'UTR APA quantification rather than novel intronic IPA events — tools like DaPars or QAPA target that scope instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Identify cell-type-specific intronic polyadenylation (IPA) events by comparing per-cell IPA usage from InPACT_quantify across cell types in scRNA-seq data, after filtering low-abundance genes with TPM < 1, and test GO enrichment of harboring genes with a hypergeometric test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Identify cell-type-specific intronic polyadenylation (IPA) events by comparing per-cell IPA usage from InPACT_quantify across cell types in scRNA-seq data, after filtering low-abundance genes with TPM < 1, and test GO enrichment of harboring genes with a hypergeometric test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq from a single condition with no cell-type labels — cell-type-specific comparison is undefined IPA sites have not yet been identified and quantified (no InPACT predict.result.txt or ipa_usage table) — run IPA identification and InPACT_quantify first The goal is 3'UTR APA quantification rather than novel intronic IPA events — tools like DaPars or QAPA target that scope instead

skills.description: Use when a model trained on paired bulk omics data (e.g., TCGA miRNA-mRNA) must be validated for cell-type-specific inference against scRNA-seq data with known cell-type miRNA profiles (e.g., Isakova Kidney-Breast-Skin GSE151334).
skills.name: cell-type-specific-model-validation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-model-validation Use when a model trained on paired bulk omics data (e.g., TCGA miRNA-mRNA) must be validated for cell-type-specific inference against scRNA-seq data with known cell-type miRNA profiles (e.g., Isakova Kidney-Breast-Skin GSE151334). When the cellular/tissue context of the application sample does not match the training cohort — miRSCAPE is expected to have slightly reduced accuracy, and a substantive loss in performance is expected when the training context differs substantially (Figure S9) When the scRNA-seq profile is too sparse (large dropout) for a pre-trained model — miRSCAPE needs to be retrained using only genes detected at a reasonable level rather than validated as-is http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Validation skill for assessing whether a bulk-trained regression model (e.g., miRSCAPE XGBoost models trained on TCGA paired miRNA-mRNA data) correctly infers cell-type-specific expression when applied to pooled scRNA-seq profiles, by correlating predicted vs observed fold-differences across cell-type pairs with Spearman rank correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Validation skill for assessing whether a bulk-trained regression model (e.g., miRSCAPE XGBoost models trained on TCGA paired miRNA-mRNA data) correctly infers cell-type-specific expression when applied to pooled scRNA-seq profiles, by correlating predicted vs observed fold-differences across cell-type pairs with Spearman rank correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the cellular/tissue context of the application sample does not match the training cohort — miRSCAPE is expected to have slightly reduced accuracy, and a substantive loss in performance is expected when the training context differs substantially (Figure S9) When the scRNA-seq profile is too sparse (large dropout) for a pre-trained model — miRSCAPE needs to be retrained using only genes detected at a reasonable level rather than validated as-is

skills.description: Use when you have cell-type-specific gene/GRN networks (edge-score matrices per cell type) and need to validate biological relevance via TF, cell-type-marker, and ENCODE TF-target enrichment before benchmarking inference methods.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-network-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-network-annotation Use when you have cell-type-specific gene/GRN networks (edge-score matrices per cell type) and need to validate biological relevance via TF, cell-type-marker, and ENCODE TF-target enrichment before benchmarking inference methods. The input is raw single-cell expression data rather than inferred networks — run network inference (e.g., scPRINT attention-based extraction) first Networks are not cell-type-specific or no marker gene sets (e.g., PanglaoDB) exist for the cell types in question, making the cell-type enrichment criterion inapplicable A validated gold-standard ground-truth network exists for the task — direct benchmarking against ground truth is preferable to enrichment-based annotation, since 'no perfect ground truths exist' is why this indirect validation is used http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotates inferred cell-type-specific gene networks by testing whether their nodes are enriched for transcription factors (hubs), the correct cell type's PanglaoDB markers, and ENCODE-validated TF targets, to demonstrate the networks are biologically meaningful. Used in the scPRINT benchmark to compare scPRINT against scGPT, Geneformer, GENIE3, and DeepSEM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Annotates inferred cell-type-specific gene networks by testing whether their nodes are enriched for transcription factors (hubs), the correct cell type's PanglaoDB markers, and ENCODE-validated TF targets, to demonstrate the networks are biologically meaningful. Used in the scPRINT benchmark to compare scPRINT against scGPT, Geneformer, GENIE3, and DeepSEM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw single-cell expression data rather than inferred networks — run network inference (e.g., scPRINT attention-based extraction) first Networks are not cell-type-specific or no marker gene sets (e.g., PanglaoDB) exist for the cell types in question, making the cell-type enrichment criterion inapplicable A validated gold-standard ground-truth network exists for the task — direct benchmarking against ground truth is preferable to enrichment-based annotation, since 'no perfect ground truths exist' is why this indirect validation is used

skills.description: Use when per-individual, per-cell-type scRNA-seq data must be aggregated into CTP/ctnu/P pseudobulk inputs and fit with CTMM linear mixed models to quantify or test cell type-specific interindividual variance (and its differentiation between cell types/stages).
skills.name: cell-type-specific-pseudobulk-mixed-model-fitting
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-pseudobulk-mixed-model-fitting Use when per-individual, per-cell-type scRNA-seq data must be aggregated into CTP/ctnu/P pseudobulk inputs and fit with CTMM linear mixed models to quantify or test cell type-specific interindividual variance (and its differentiation between cell types/stages). Cohorts with fewer than ~50 individuals: the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable below ~50 sample size Rare cell types or individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells, or very lowly expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian for the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation Continuous cell trajectories that cannot be meaningfully discretized, since CTMM assumes discrete cell types and pseudobulk discards cell-level information http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits CTMM (Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Model) to cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data with hom/iid/free/full models under ML, REML, or HE to estimate and test cell type-specific interindividual variance and inter-stage covariance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fits CTMM (Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Model) to cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data with hom/iid/free/full models under ML, REML, or HE to estimate and test cell type-specific interindividual variance and inter-stage covariance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cohorts with fewer than ~50 individuals: the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable below ~50 sample size Rare cell types or individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells, or very lowly expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian for the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation Continuous cell trajectories that cannot be meaningfully discretized, since CTMM assumes discrete cell types and pseudobulk discards cell-level information

skills.description: Use when predicted and true count matrices must be scored per cell type for multiple prediction scenarios (within-batch/cross-batch, in-sample/out-of-sample) and compared against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-regression-metrics-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-regression-metrics-evaluation Use when predicted and true count matrices must be scored per cell type for multiple prediction scenarios (within-batch/cross-batch, in-sample/out-of-sample) and compared against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN. Input is a matrix of latent embeddings or cluster labels rather than gene count predictions — regression metrics on counts are not meaningful Only one global aggregate metric is required and cell-type stratification is not part of the evaluation design The dataset lacks cell-type annotations in meta_cells, making per-cell-type scoring impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark perturbation-prediction accuracy on scRNA-seq count predictions by computing cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2 between predicted and gold-standard counts, assembling results across scenarios and methods into a CSV comparison table (e.g., prediction_metrics.csv, perturbation_prediction_scores.csv). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Benchmark perturbation-prediction accuracy on scRNA-seq count predictions by computing cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2 between predicted and gold-standard counts, assembling results across scenarios and methods into a CSV comparison table (e.g., prediction_metrics.csv, perturbation_prediction_scores.csv).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a matrix of latent embeddings or cluster labels rather than gene count predictions — regression metrics on counts are not meaningful Only one global aggregate metric is required and cell-type stratification is not part of the evaluation design The dataset lacks cell-type annotations in meta_cells, making per-cell-type scoring impossible

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify genes whose spatial expression varies within a specific cell type — e.g. testing whether imputation of non-MERFISH genes into a MERFISH slice increases detectable cell-type-specific spatially DE genes.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-spatial-de-testing
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-spatial-de-testing Use when the goal is to identify genes whose spatial expression varies within a specific cell type — e.g. testing whether imputation of non-MERFISH genes into a MERFISH slice increases detectable cell-type-specific spatially DE genes. The spatial data already has whole-transcriptome coverage and no imputation is needed — de novo imputation plus DE testing adds a model-generated layer that is inappropriate when measured genes suffice. The question is spot-level deconvolution of cell-type proportions rather than gene-level differential expression testing (use RCTD/CARD/cell2location instead). No cell type labels or paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference exist to define the cell types along which DE is tested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects cell-type-specific spatially differentially expressed genes in a spatial transcriptomics dataset by running C-SIDE (spacexr) and SPARK-X on gene-imputed data, e.g. SpatialScope-imputed MERFISH, and tabulating significant calls at FDR 1% per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Detects cell-type-specific spatially differentially expressed genes in a spatial transcriptomics dataset by running C-SIDE (spacexr) and SPARK-X on gene-imputed data, e.g. SpatialScope-imputed MERFISH, and tabulating significant calls at FDR 1% per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial data already has whole-transcriptome coverage and no imputation is needed — de novo imputation plus DE testing adds a model-generated layer that is inappropriate when measured genes suffice. The question is spot-level deconvolution of cell-type proportions rather than gene-level differential expression testing (use RCTD/CARD/cell2location instead). No cell type labels or paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference exist to define the cell types along which DE is tested.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq counts with cell and individual metadata need to be summarized into cell type-specific pseudobulk and tested for genes with significant cell type-specific interindividual expression variance.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-variance-component-estimation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-variance-component-estimation Use when scRNA-seq counts with cell and individual metadata need to be summarized into cell type-specific pseudobulk and tested for genes with significant cell type-specific interindividual expression variance. Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells or fewer than ~50 individuals, since CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50 and limited to common cell types Genes are very lowly expressed, where severe non-Gaussianity breaks the Gaussian approximation underlying the pseudobulk model Cell types are continuous rather than discrete, since pseudobulk CTP representation requires discretizing them http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit the CTMM (Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Model) Free model with REML and a jackknife-based Wald test to cell type-specific pseudobulk scRNA-seq data in order to detect genes whose interindividual expression variance differs across cell types and to partition variance into cell type-shared (hom2) and cell type-specific (V) components. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fit the CTMM (Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Model) Free model with REML and a jackknife-based Wald test to cell type-specific pseudobulk scRNA-seq data in order to detect genes whose interindividual expression variance differs across cell types and to partition variance into cell type-shared (hom2) and cell type-specific (V) components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells or fewer than ~50 individuals, since CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50 and limited to common cell types Genes are very lowly expressed, where severe non-Gaussianity breaks the Gaussian approximation underlying the pseudobulk model Cell types are continuous rather than discrete, since pseudobulk CTP representation requires discretizing them

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed, z-scored cluster-level marker-gene expression matrix (clusters as columns) needs automatic cell type labels matched against a human cell type reference panel such as MonacoImmune or BlueprintEncode.
skills.name: cell-type-specificity-reference-panel-matching
skills.search_text: cell-type-specificity-reference-panel-matching Use when a preprocessed, z-scored cluster-level marker-gene expression matrix (clusters as columns) needs automatic cell type labels matched against a human cell type reference panel such as MonacoImmune or BlueprintEncode. Query consists of a gene list rather than expression profiles — use the Fisher's exact test mode (deCS.fisher) instead of correlation analysis Goal is characterizing novel cell types or annotating malignant/cancer cells, since deCS is a mapping-based toolkit that fails on novel types and struggles with healthy-vs-malignant expression differences Single-cell-level annotation with tissue-specific context is required — deCS annotates at the cluster level and ignores tissue information (except HCAF), which may bias results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates cell clusters from a scRNA-seq query by computing Pearson correlation coefficients between the query's z-scored marker-gene expression matrix and a built-in cell type specificity score reference panel (e.g., MonacoImmune_main t-score), assigning the top-matching cell type label(s) per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Annotates cell clusters from a scRNA-seq query by computing Pearson correlation coefficients between the query's z-scored marker-gene expression matrix and a built-in cell type specificity score reference panel (e.g., MonacoImmune_main t-score), assigning the top-matching cell type label(s) per cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query consists of a gene list rather than expression profiles — use the Fisher's exact test mode (deCS.fisher) instead of correlation analysis Goal is characterizing novel cell types or annotating malignant/cancer cells, since deCS is a mapping-based toolkit that fails on novel types and struggles with healthy-vs-malignant expression differences Single-cell-level annotation with tissue-specific context is required — deCS annotates at the cluster level and ignores tissue information (except HCAF), which may bias results

skills.description: Use when annotating clusters of a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with scaled matrix) against a tissue-restricted marker database using both positive and negative markers, or when verifying a from-scratch reimplementation of the ScType scoring algorithm.
skills.name: cell-type-specificity-score-implementation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specificity-score-implementation Use when annotating clusters of a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with scaled matrix) against a tissue-restricted marker database using both positive and negative markers, or when verifying a from-scratch reimplementation of the ScType scoring algorithm. The input is raw counts without Seurat normalization, scaling, and clustering — ScType scoring requires a z-scored scale.data matrix and predefined clusters A supervised classifier with a labeled reference dataset is required — ScType is an unsupervised marker-specificity method and was benchmarked against supervised tools like CaSTLe and ACTINN rather than replacing them No marker database covers the tissue of interest — the ScTypeDB restriction to a tissue type is a required input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements the ScType cell-type annotation scoring: z-score transformed gene expression multiplied by a cell-type specificity score S_i^t, combined into positive/negative marker-enrichment scores aggregated to per-cluster ScType scores. Reimplementation of the reference sctype_score_ function from Ianevski et al. 2022 (Nature Communications). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Implements the ScType cell-type annotation scoring: z-score transformed gene expression multiplied by a cell-type specificity score S_i^t, combined into positive/negative marker-enrichment scores aggregated to per-cluster ScType scores. Reimplementation of the reference sctype_score_ function from Ianevski et al. 2022 (Nature Communications).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw counts without Seurat normalization, scaling, and clustering — ScType scoring requires a z-scored scale.data matrix and predefined clusters A supervised classifier with a labeled reference dataset is required — ScType is an unsupervised marker-specificity method and was benchmarked against supervised tools like CaSTLe and ACTINN rather than replacing them No marker database covers the tissue of interest — the ScTypeDB restriction to a tissue type is a required input
