skills.name: cell-type-specificity-tscore-estimation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specificity-tscore-estimation Use when building or verifying deCS CTGene reference panels: you need per-cell-type ranked gene lists derived from bulk (t-score) or single-cell (z-score) specificity scores before annotation or enrichment. You already have a pre-computed deCS reference panel and only need to run deCS.correlation() or deCS.fisher() annotation on a query The query is a raw scRNA-seq matrix needing clustering/normalization first (NormalizeData, FindVariableFeatures, ScaleData, RunPCA, FindNeighbors) rather than reference panel construction You need to discover novel cell types — deCS is a mapping-based toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct deCS cell type specificity (CTGene) reference panels by computing per-gene t-statistics for bulk RNA-seq references (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune) and row-wise z-scores for scRNA-seq references (HCL, HCAF), then retaining the top 5% most specific genes per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Reconstruct deCS cell type specificity (CTGene) reference panels by computing per-gene t-statistics for bulk RNA-seq references (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune) and row-wise z-scores for scRNA-seq references (HCL, HCAF), then retaining the top 5% most specific genes per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a pre-computed deCS reference panel and only need to run deCS.correlation() or deCS.fisher() annotation on a query The query is a raw scRNA-seq matrix needing clustering/normalization first (NormalizeData, FindVariableFeatures, ScaleData, RunPCA, FindNeighbors) rather than reference panel construction You need to discover novel cell types — deCS is a mapping-based toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types

skills.description: Use when you have an integration-adjusted expression matrix plus raw logcounts, consensus cell-type labels and per-sample severity metadata, and need to quantify whether integration improves cell-type-stratified prediction accuracy.
skills.name: cell-type-stratified-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-type-stratified-accuracy-comparison Use when you have an integration-adjusted expression matrix plus raw logcounts, consensus cell-type labels and per-sample severity metadata, and need to quantify whether integration improves cell-type-stratified prediction accuracy. Your integration method returns only a low-dimensional embedding with no adjusted expression matrix — the article notes such embeddings restrict sample-level analysis and interpretable downstream features You want cell-type annotation or clustering quality rather than sample-level prediction performance from pseudo-bulk signatures Data lack per-sample condition/severity labels, so pseudo-replication and class-prediction evaluation cannot be performed Evaluates whether scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression improves downstream prediction compared with raw log-normalised data, by building per-cell-type pseudo-bulk signatures, training RBF-kernel SVMs to predict COVID-19 disease severity (Healthy / Mild-Moderate / Severe-Critical), and comparing per-cell-type cross-validation accuracies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Evaluates whether scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression improves downstream prediction compared with raw log-normalised data, by building per-cell-type pseudo-bulk signatures, training RBF-kernel SVMs to predict COVID-19 disease severity (Healthy / Mild-Moderate / Severe-Critical), and comparing per-cell-type cross-validation accuracies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your integration method returns only a low-dimensional embedding with no adjusted expression matrix — the article notes such embeddings restrict sample-level analysis and interpretable downstream features You want cell-type annotation or clustering quality rather than sample-level prediction performance from pseudo-bulk signatures Data lack per-sample condition/severity labels, so pseudo-replication and class-prediction evaluation cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on datasets with imbalanced cell type proportions, where a cell type-aware batch-mixing metric (rather than plain iLISI) is needed to score batch mixing per cell type.
skills.name: cell-type-stratified-integration-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-stratified-integration-evaluation Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on datasets with imbalanced cell type proportions, where a cell type-aware batch-mixing metric (rather than plain iLISI) is needed to score batch mixing per cell type. Cell type annotations are unavailable — 'One obvious limitation of CiLISI and similar metrics is that it requires cell type annotations.' Evaluating mixing of technical replicates without meaningful cell type structure, where cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics suffice A cell type is present in only one dataset — CiLISI cannot be calculated and that type must be dropped http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates scRNA-seq batch integration quality using CiLISI, a per-cell-type normalized iLISI that measures how well cells of the same type mix across batches, computed with the scIntegrationMetrics R package. It corrects the inadequacy of cell type-agnostic iLISI in integration tasks with cell type imbalance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Evaluates scRNA-seq batch integration quality using CiLISI, a per-cell-type normalized iLISI that measures how well cells of the same type mix across batches, computed with the scIntegrationMetrics R package. It corrects the inadequacy of cell type-agnostic iLISI in integration tasks with cell type imbalance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type annotations are unavailable — 'One obvious limitation of CiLISI and similar metrics is that it requires cell type annotations.' Evaluating mixing of technical replicates without meaningful cell type structure, where cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics suffice A cell type is present in only one dataset — CiLISI cannot be calculated and that type must be dropped

skills.description: Use when predicting held-out condition/batch scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., PW034-705) and you must judge prediction accuracy separately per cell type under both condition-only and condition-plus-batch scenarios.
skills.name: cell-type-stratified-prediction-assessment
skills.search_text: cell-type-stratified-prediction-assessment Use when predicting held-out condition/batch scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., PW034-705) and you must judge prediction accuracy separately per cell type under both condition-only and condition-plus-batch scenarios. Input is a single-batch dataset where each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects, so cross-batch scoring is ill-posed The goal is perturbation prediction on data with no batch variation between input and held-out matrices; scGen/scPreGAN already handle the condition-only task and scDisInFact's main advantage disappears http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores perturbation-prediction outputs per cell type (e.g., Myeloid, Oligodendrocytes, tumor cells) using cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2, comparing scDisInFact against scGen and scPreGAN under within-batch and cross-batch scenarios on GBM scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Scores perturbation-prediction outputs per cell type (e.g., Myeloid, Oligodendrocytes, tumor cells) using cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2, comparing scDisInFact against scGen and scPreGAN under within-batch and cross-batch scenarios on GBM scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-batch dataset where each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects, so cross-batch scoring is ill-posed The goal is perturbation prediction on data with no batch variation between input and held-out matrices; scGen/scPreGAN already handle the condition-only task and scDisInFact's main advantage disappears

skills.description: Use when a per-sample EMBEDR p-value sweep across kEff/perplexity exists for an annotated single-cell dataset and you need to determine whether cell types are embedded at different neighborhood scales.
skills.name: cell-type-stratified-pvalue-aggregation
skills.search_text: cell-type-stratified-pvalue-aggregation Use when a per-sample EMBEDR p-value sweep across kEff/perplexity exists for an annotated single-cell dataset and you need to determine whether cell types are embedded at different neighborhood scales. The dataset has no cell-type annotations to stratify by, so only a global sweep_boxplot/sweep_lineplot summary is possible You need a single global optimal perplexity for the whole dataset rather than cell-wise or population-wise scale comparisons (use the EMBEDR_sweep global summary or fit_samplewise_optimal instead) The input is a non-normalized dataset — EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets per the discussion Stratifies per-sample EMBEDR p-values from a perplexity/kEff sweep by cell-type annotation (e.g., Tabula Muris marrow macrophages, granulocytes, B cells) and computes median and 90th-percentile trajectories per type to reveal that different cell populations have distinct native embedding scales. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Stratifies per-sample EMBEDR p-values from a perplexity/kEff sweep by cell-type annotation (e.g., Tabula Muris marrow macrophages, granulocytes, B cells) and computes median and 90th-percentile trajectories per type to reveal that different cell populations have distinct native embedding scales.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no cell-type annotations to stratify by, so only a global sweep_boxplot/sweep_lineplot summary is possible You need a single global optimal perplexity for the whole dataset rather than cell-wise or population-wise scale comparisons (use the EMBEDR_sweep global summary or fit_samplewise_optimal instead) The input is a non-normalized dataset — EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets per the discussion

skills.description: Use when simulating perturbed trajectories from a differentiation time series and you need fate-outcome shifts computed per starting cell state rather than per whole timepoint.
skills.name: cell-type-subpopulation-stratification
skills.search_text: cell-type-subpopulation-stratification Use when simulating perturbed trajectories from a differentiation time series and you need fate-outcome shifts computed per starting cell state rather than per whole timepoint. The question is about temporal (day 0–6) timing of perturbations rather than starting-population effects — use the day-resolved workflow instead Input scRNA-seq data has not yet been pre-processed with Seurat or scanpy and converted to the data_pt torch object via prescient process_data The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model's constraint and undermining fate-bias interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Stratifies cells from an in vitro β-cell differentiation scRNA-seq time series into labeled starting subpopulations (e.g., SOX2+, NKX6.1+, and neurog3-early/mid/late) so that in silico TF perturbations can be simulated from each population separately, revealing whether perturbation effects depend on developmental stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Stratifies cells from an in vitro β-cell differentiation scRNA-seq time series into labeled starting subpopulations (e.g., SOX2+, NKX6.1+, and neurog3-early/mid/late) so that in silico TF perturbations can be simulated from each population separately, revealing whether perturbation effects depend on developmental stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about temporal (day 0–6) timing of perturbations rather than starting-population effects — use the day-resolved workflow instead Input scRNA-seq data has not yet been pre-processed with Seurat or scanpy and converted to the data_pt torch object via prescient process_data The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model's constraint and undermining fate-bias interpretation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking phase inference on heterogeneous droplet-based scRNA-seq where per-cell-type accuracy (e.g., median phase error per population) must be computed against known sampling times.
skills.name: cell-type-subset-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-subset-analysis Use when benchmarking phase inference on heterogeneous droplet-based scRNA-seq where per-cell-type accuracy (e.g., median phase error per population) must be computed against known sampling times. The dataset lacks cell-type annotations, so no meaningful SMC/fibroblast/endothelial/macrophage subsets can be formed and only whole-population analysis (as done for the hepatocyte time course) is possible The input is plate-based scRNA-seq with a different generative model and the goal is not per-cell-type benchmarking on droplet-based data The analysis goal is a single pooled phase estimate across the entire tissue rather than cell-type-resolved phase errors and Bayes factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratifies droplet-based scRNA-seq data by cell type (e.g., subsetting the 10X Chromium mouse aorta light-dark dataset to SMCs, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and macrophages as anndata objects) so that circadian phase inference methods like Tempo can be benchmarked per population against known sampling-time references. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Stratifies droplet-based scRNA-seq data by cell type (e.g., subsetting the 10X Chromium mouse aorta light-dark dataset to SMCs, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and macrophages as anndata objects) so that circadian phase inference methods like Tempo can be benchmarked per population against known sampling-time references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks cell-type annotations, so no meaningful SMC/fibroblast/endothelial/macrophage subsets can be formed and only whole-population analysis (as done for the hepatocyte time course) is possible The input is plate-based scRNA-seq with a different generative model and the goal is not per-cell-type benchmarking on droplet-based data The analysis goal is a single pooled phase estimate across the entire tissue rather than cell-type-resolved phase errors and Bayes factors

skills.description: Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject single-cell count data where the goal is to test a cell-level predictor (like APOE expression) or subject-level genotype group within one annotated cell type, while accounting for hierarchical subject structure.
skills.name: cell-type-subset-cohort-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-subset-cohort-analysis Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject single-cell count data where the goal is to test a cell-level predictor (like APOE expression) or subject-level genotype group within one annotated cell type, while accounting for hierarchical subject structure. Data are single-subject or non-hierarchical — NEBULA's subject-level overdispersion component requires multiple subjects grouped by sid. The variable of interest is subject-level and the subject count is very small — testing is highly sensitive to subject-level variance component estimation and random-effects distribution assumptions. Genes are very lowly expressed — the co-expression analysis has little statistical power to identify low-expression genes, and no observed correlation does not mean genes are not co-expressed. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Performs cell-level differential or co-expression analysis within a defined cell type (e.g., microglia) across subject genotype groups (e.g., APOE isoform groups e2e3/e3e3/e4+) by fitting a negative binomial gamma mixed model (NBGMM) with NEBULA-LN, which decomposes overdispersion into subject-level and cell-level components for large-scale multi-subject single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Performs cell-level differential or co-expression analysis within a defined cell type (e.g., microglia) across subject genotype groups (e.g., APOE isoform groups e2e3/e3e3/e4+) by fitting a negative binomial gamma mixed model (NBGMM) with NEBULA-LN, which decomposes overdispersion into subject-level and cell-level components for large-scale multi-subject single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-subject or non-hierarchical — NEBULA's subject-level overdispersion component requires multiple subjects grouped by sid. The variable of interest is subject-level and the subject count is very small — testing is highly sensitive to subject-level variance component estimation and random-effects distribution assumptions. Genes are very lowly expressed — the co-expression analysis has little statistical power to identify low-expression genes, and no observed correlation does not mean genes are not co-expressed.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object or raw UMI count matrix contains mixed cell types and the analysis target is cell-type-specific co-expression inference or null-data simulation for one cell type.
skills.name: cell-type-subsetting-from-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: cell-type-subsetting-from-scrna-seq Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object or raw UMI count matrix contains mixed cell types and the analysis target is cell-type-specific co-expression inference or null-data simulation for one cell type. The input is already restricted to a single cell type or is a bulk RNA-seq sample, where cell-type subsetting is meaningless and CS-CORE's cell-type-specific model assumptions do not apply as intended The goal is cross-cell-type or aggregated co-expression; CS-CORE assumes gene expressions from cells of the same cell type follow the same distribution Only normalized/corrected expression matrices (e.g., SCTransform outputs) are available — CS-CORE's Poisson measurement model links latent expression to observed UMI counts, so raw counts must be retained http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts the cells of a single cell type (e.g., B cells or CD14 monocytes from the Wilk PBMC COVID Seurat object, or excitatory neurons from GSE157827) from a raw UMI count matrix so that downstream cell-type-specific co-expression inference with CS-CORE operates on a homogeneous cell population. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Extracts the cells of a single cell type (e.g., B cells or CD14 monocytes from the Wilk PBMC COVID Seurat object, or excitatory neurons from GSE157827) from a raw UMI count matrix so that downstream cell-type-specific co-expression inference with CS-CORE operates on a homogeneous cell population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already restricted to a single cell type or is a bulk RNA-seq sample, where cell-type subsetting is meaningless and CS-CORE's cell-type-specific model assumptions do not apply as intended The goal is cross-cell-type or aggregated co-expression; CS-CORE assumes gene expressions from cells of the same cell type follow the same distribution Only normalized/corrected expression matrices (e.g., SCTransform outputs) are available — CS-CORE's Poisson measurement model links latent expression to observed UMI counts, so raw counts must be retained

skills.description: Use when a labeled .h5ad scRNA-seq dataset needs per-cell informativeness scores (data values) for value-based subsampling, quality assessment, or identifying ambiguous/atypical cells relative to their annotated cell types.
skills.name: cell-type-supervised-classification
skills.search_text: cell-type-supervised-classification Use when a labeled .h5ad scRNA-seq dataset needs per-cell informativeness scores (data values) for value-based subsampling, quality assessment, or identifying ambiguous/atypical cells relative to their annotated cell types. The dataset has no cell-type labels — the random forest is supervised by adata.obs cell-type annotations and cannot compute OOB type-prediction accuracy without them The goal is distance- or distribution-preserving sketching (e.g. GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler, KH) rather than OOB data-value-guided subsampling The input is raw counts without cell-type annotation or a computed feature representation like X_pca http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Trains a supervised random-forest classifier on cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq features (PCA on top 3,000 HVGs) and scores each cell's 'data value' as its out-of-bag prediction accuracy, quantifying how well the cell's type is distinguished by the rest of the data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Trains a supervised random-forest classifier on cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq features (PCA on top 3,000 HVGs) and scores each cell's 'data value' as its out-of-bag prediction accuracy, quantifying how well the cell's type is distinguished by the rest of the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no cell-type labels — the random forest is supervised by adata.obs cell-type annotations and cannot compute OOB type-prediction accuracy without them The goal is distance- or distribution-preserving sketching (e.g. GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler, KH) rather than OOB data-value-guided subsampling The input is raw counts without cell-type annotation or a computed feature representation like X_pca

skills.description: Use when a locus-level TE quantification matrix (cell × TE counts) has been produced by MATES and the goal is to find TEs that mark specific cell populations recovered by clustering or by a gene-expression reference clustering.
skills.name: cell-type-te-marker-identification
skills.search_text: cell-type-te-marker-identification Use when a locus-level TE quantification matrix (cell × TE counts) has been produced by MATES and the goal is to find TEs that mark specific cell populations recovered by clustering or by a gene-expression reference clustering. Only subfamily-level TE counts are available — subfamily-level aggregation cannot resolve individual TE copies (e.g. distinguish the RLTR44B locus from other RLTR44B copies) and reduces marker specificity Identical TE copies such as HERVK isoforms with high sequence similarity and no uniquely mappable flanking regions — MATES cannot reliably distinguish these loci, so locus-specific marker calls are not trustworthy Marker candidate is a long autonomously expressed TE such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases — MATES's coverage-vector design limits accurate quantification of such TEs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies cell-type-specific marker transposable elements from MATES locus-level TE count matrices by clustering cells on TE (optionally gene+TE) expression and testing which TEs are enriched within gene-defined cell populations, e.g. RMER16_Mm/RLTR44B in macrophages and MT2/MERVL-int near Zscan4 genes in 2CLC cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Identifies cell-type-specific marker transposable elements from MATES locus-level TE count matrices by clustering cells on TE (optionally gene+TE) expression and testing which TEs are enriched within gene-defined cell populations, e.g. RMER16_Mm/RLTR44B in macrophages and MT2/MERVL-int near Zscan4 genes in 2CLC cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only subfamily-level TE counts are available — subfamily-level aggregation cannot resolve individual TE copies (e.g. distinguish the RLTR44B locus from other RLTR44B copies) and reduces marker specificity Identical TE copies such as HERVK isoforms with high sequence similarity and no uniquely mappable flanking regions — MATES cannot reliably distinguish these loci, so locus-specific marker calls are not trustworthy Marker candidate is a long autonomously expressed TE such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases — MATES's coverage-vector design limits accurate quantification of such TEs

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets carry heterogeneous free-text cell annotations (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis-style labels) that must be normalized to Cell Ontology terms before ontology-based classification or cross-dataset annotation.
skills.name: cell-type-term-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-type-term-mapping Use when scRNA-seq datasets carry heterogeneous free-text cell annotations (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis-style labels) that must be normalized to Cell Ontology terms before ontology-based classification or cross-dataset annotation. Input cell labels are already valid Cell Ontology term IDs, so no uncontrolled-vocabulary normalization is needed The goal is classifying cells (extending probability scores to unseen cell types via the Cell Ontology graph) rather than normalizing label terminology The task requires distinguishing topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot do http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps uncontrolled free-text cell type labels (with synonyms, misspellings, and abbreviations) onto Cell Ontology terms using OnClass's char-level LSTM siamese network, which embeds cell type descriptions into a low-dimensional space and retrieves the nearest controlled-vocabulary term by text similarity plus maximum-weight bipartite matching. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Maps uncontrolled free-text cell type labels (with synonyms, misspellings, and abbreviations) onto Cell Ontology terms using OnClass's char-level LSTM siamese network, which embeds cell type descriptions into a low-dimensional space and retrieves the nearest controlled-vocabulary term by text similarity plus maximum-weight bipartite matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cell labels are already valid Cell Ontology term IDs, so no uncontrolled-vocabulary normalization is needed The goal is classifying cells (extending probability scores to unseen cell types via the Cell Ontology graph) rather than normalizing label terminology The task requires distinguishing topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot do

skills.description: Use when you have Cell Ontology text embeddings (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), the ontology graph (cl.obo), and per-cell-type expression profiles, and you want to test whether ontology/text/expression similarity agree.
skills.name: cell-type-text-embedding-similarity
skills.search_text: cell-type-text-embedding-similarity Use when you have Cell Ontology text embeddings (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), the ontology graph (cl.obo), and per-cell-type expression profiles, and you want to test whether ontology/text/expression similarity agree. Your goal is to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings sharing the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — both graph-based and text-embedding similarities cannot separate them Your input is free-text cell annotations that first need mapping to Cell Ontology terms — use OnClass's NLP mapping model instead, not similarity analysis You lack text embeddings (cl.ontology.nlp.emb) or ontology structure and only have raw expression clusters — direct expression clustering is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Quantifies how similar cell types are in NLP text-embedding space (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), Cell Ontology graph space, and gene-expression space, by building pairwise similarity matrices and computing Pearson correlations between them. It validates the guilt-by-association principle underlying OnClass. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Quantifies how similar cell types are in NLP text-embedding space (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), Cell Ontology graph space, and gene-expression space, by building pairwise similarity matrices and computing Pearson correlations between them. It validates the guilt-by-association principle underlying OnClass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings sharing the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph) — both graph-based and text-embedding similarities cannot separate them Your input is free-text cell annotations that first need mapping to Cell Ontology terms — use OnClass's NLP mapping model instead, not similarity analysis You lack text embeddings (cl.ontology.nlp.emb) or ontology structure and only have raw expression clusters — direct expression clustering is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when a learned or predicted cell-type hierarchy must be verified against a published cluster-correspondence figure, e.g. checking that AMB2016/AMB2018 visual cortex populations attach to the correct parents.
skills.name: cell-type-tree-comparison-against-published-hierarchy
skills.search_text: cell-type-tree-comparison-against-published-hierarchy Use when a learned or predicted cell-type hierarchy must be verified against a published cluster-correspondence figure, e.g. checking that AMB2016/AMB2018 visual cortex populations attach to the correct parents. Datasets are not yet aligned — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so running tree construction/comparison on unaligned data makes it impossible to tell whether tree mistakes come from erroneous alignment or from scHPL mismatches The cell populations of interest are absent from both the learned tree and any published reference (e.g. many brain cell populations are missing from the Cell Ontology), leaving nothing to compare against Validates a scHPL-constructed hierarchical classification tree of brain cell populations by comparing its learned relationships to a published reference hierarchy (Tasic et al. Extended Data Fig. 6), checking specific parent-child attachments and merges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Validates a scHPL-constructed hierarchical classification tree of brain cell populations by comparing its learned relationships to a published reference hierarchy (Tasic et al. Extended Data Fig. 6), checking specific parent-child attachments and merges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not yet aligned — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so running tree construction/comparison on unaligned data makes it impossible to tell whether tree mistakes come from erroneous alignment or from scHPL mismatches The cell populations of interest are absent from both the learned tree and any published reference (e.g. many brain cell populations are missing from the Cell Ontology), leaving nothing to compare against

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a single-cell diagonal integration method (scRNA with scATAC or surface protein) remains robust as cell populations become unbalanced or absent from one modality.
skills.name: cell-type-unbalancing-simulation
skills.search_text: cell-type-unbalancing-simulation Use when evaluating whether a single-cell diagonal integration method (scRNA with scATAC or surface protein) remains robust as cell populations become unbalanced or absent from one modality. When the integration task is paired/multiomic (same cells measured in both modalities) rather than unpaired diagonal integration When no cross-modality feature connections are available (e.g., integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on weakly connected features for its cost matrix When the goal is detecting rare cell populations rather than stress-testing robustness to population imbalance — the paper notes rare populations are under-represented in mini-batch parameter estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking procedure that subsamples cell populations (e.g., K562 and HCT cell lines in scCATseq scRNA-scATAC data) to create graded unbalanced diagonal-integration scenarios, testing robustness of integration methods when proportions differ across modalities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that subsamples cell populations (e.g., K562 and HCT cell lines in scCATseq scRNA-scATAC data) to create graded unbalanced diagonal-integration scenarios, testing robustness of integration methods when proportions differ across modalities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the integration task is paired/multiomic (same cells measured in both modalities) rather than unpaired diagonal integration When no cross-modality feature connections are available (e.g., integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on weakly connected features for its cost matrix When the goal is detecting rare cell populations rather than stress-testing robustness to population imbalance — the paper notes rare populations are under-represented in mini-batch parameter estimation

skills.description: Use when you have a GEDI model fitted to a multi-sample, condition-contrast scRNA-seq atlas (e.g., Harmony-integrated COVID-19 cohort 1) and need a cluster-free, cell-type-level ranking of response strength to a condition.
skills.name: cell-type-vector-magnitude-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-vector-magnitude-ranking Use when you have a GEDI model fitted to a multi-sample, condition-contrast scRNA-seq atlas (e.g., Harmony-integrated COVID-19 cohort 1) and need a cluster-free, cell-type-level ranking of response strength to a condition. The dataset has no sample-level condition contrast (no healthy-vs-severe or equivalent prior H), so a condition vector field is undefined You need per-gene differential expression rather than a cell-type-level response-magnitude summary — use GEDI's cluster-free DGE (getDiffExp.gedi) instead The embedding has not been produced by GEDI/Harmony; computing raw expression shifts on an unintegrated manifold conflates batch and condition effects, which the article explicitly warns against A GEDI-based analysis step that aggregates per-cell transcriptomic vector field magnitudes (severe-vs-healthy COVID-19) by cell type and ranks cell types by mean magnitude to identify which populations carry the strongest disease-associated transcriptional shift. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: A GEDI-based analysis step that aggregates per-cell transcriptomic vector field magnitudes (severe-vs-healthy COVID-19) by cell type and ranks cell types by mean magnitude to identify which populations carry the strongest disease-associated transcriptional shift.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no sample-level condition contrast (no healthy-vs-severe or equivalent prior H), so a condition vector field is undefined You need per-gene differential expression rather than a cell-type-level response-magnitude summary — use GEDI's cluster-free DGE (getDiffExp.gedi) instead The embedding has not been produced by GEDI/Harmony; computing raw expression shifts on an unintegrated manifold conflates batch and condition effects, which the article explicitly warns against

skills.search_text: cell-variance-estimation-and-variance-normalization Use when preparing scRNA-seq UMI count data for Normalisr association testing and mean-level (lcpm/normcov) normalization is done but per-cell variance effects of library-size covariates still confound expression. skills.summary: Normalisr's variance-level normalization: estimate per-cell variance of the Bayesian log expression, then normalize gene expression variances with normvar to regress out variance-level confounding effects of nonlinear cellular covariates before association testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data comes from full-length (non-UMI) platforms — the nonlinear cellular summary covariates were only validated on UMI-based datasets and 'may benefit from revalidating' there The goal is hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations — 'Normalisr is not designed for hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations' Integrative analysis across multiple datasets requiring explicit batch-effect correction — batch effects are not addressed by Normalisr

skills.search_text: cellmarker-marker-confidence-classification Use when you have a ranked DEG list (e.g. singleCellHaystack log.p.vals from scRNA-seq data) and want to validate biological relevance by checking whether known cell type markers are over-represented among the top ranks rather than uniformly distributed. The gene ranking does not come from a DEG prediction method (e.g. it is an unranked feature table or a clustering result), since the skill depends on partitioning a ranked list into consecutive rank bins. skills.description: Decision support for choosing between NEBULA-LN and NEBULA-HL per gene in multi-subject snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data, when cells-per-subject counts (e.g., CPS ~380–700) may make the large-sample LN approximation unreliable for some genes.
skills.name: cells-per-subject-qc-evaluation
skills.search_text: cells-per-subject-qc-evaluation Decision support for choosing between NEBULA-LN and NEBULA-HL per gene in multi-subject snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data, when cells-per-subject counts (e.g., CPS ~380–700) may make the large-sample LN approximation unreliable for some genes. The data are bulk RNA-seq or single-subject single-cell data with no hierarchical subject structure — the CPS-based dispatch assumes multi-subject droplet-based single-cell data with per-subject cell counts. Every gene will be fit with NEBULA-HL regardless (e.g., very small subjects-per-data-set designs with CPS < 30 genome-wide) — the dispatch rule is then trivial and NEBULA-LN estimates need not be computed first. The task is filtering low-expression genes (cpc=0.005 threshold) or post-fit QC of convergence codes rather than model-choice dispatch between NEBULA-LN and NEBULA-HL. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A decision rule for evaluating cells-per-subject (CPS) adequacy before fitting NEBULA's negative binomial gamma mixed model, dispatching each gene between NEBULA-LN (fast large-sample approximation) and NEBULA-HL (h-likelihood) based on estimated overdispersion components. This preserves the paper's recommended strategy in which ~90% and ~80% of genes (CPC > 0.1%) are resolved by NEBULA-LN alone at CPS ~700 and ~380. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: A decision rule for evaluating cells-per-subject (CPS) adequacy before fitting NEBULA's negative binomial gamma mixed model, dispatching each gene between NEBULA-LN (fast large-sample approximation) and NEBULA-HL (h-likelihood) based on estimated overdispersion components. This preserves the paper's recommended strategy in which ~90% and ~80% of genes (CPC > 0.1%) are resolved by NEBULA-LN alone at CPS ~700 and ~380.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk RNA-seq or single-subject single-cell data with no hierarchical subject structure — the CPS-based dispatch assumes multi-subject droplet-based single-cell data with per-subject cell counts. Every gene will be fit with NEBULA-HL regardless (e.g., very small subjects-per-data-set designs with CPS < 30 genome-wide) — the dispatch rule is then trivial and NEBULA-LN estimates need not be computed first. The task is filtering low-expression genes (cpc=0.005 threshold) or post-fit QC of convergence codes rather than model-choice dispatch between NEBULA-LN and NEBULA-HL.

Input is raw scRNA-seq count data or clustering output without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed, inferred interactions that must be inferred first with a supported tool Interactions were inferred by a tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (only CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR are supported) The goal is de novo prediction of ligand-receptor interactions or statistical inference rather than interactive downstream exploration and visualization of existing CCI results http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize chemokine-mediated cell-cell communication by filtering InterCellar's gene-verse dot plots to selected CXCL ligand-receptor pairs (CXCL1, CXCL3, CXCL6, CXCL16, CXCL17) and specific cluster-pairs, then comparing plots across disease and control conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Visualize chemokine-mediated cell-cell communication by filtering InterCellar's gene-verse dot plots to selected CXCL ligand-receptor pairs (CXCL1, CXCL3, CXCL6, CXCL16, CXCL17) and specific cluster-pairs, then comparing plots across disease and control conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq count data or clustering output without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed, inferred interactions that must be inferred first with a supported tool Interactions were inferred by a tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (only CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR are supported) The goal is de novo prediction of ligand-receptor interactions or statistical inference rather than interactive downstream exploration and visualization of existing CCI results

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell type annotation on scRNA-seq data with a labeled reference/training set, and you need CHETAH as a baseline label-assignment method to compare accuracy against neural-network or scmap-based classifiers.
skills.name: chetah-hierarchical-cell-annotation
skills.search_text: chetah-hierarchical-cell-annotation Use when benchmarking cell type annotation on scRNA-seq data with a labeled reference/training set, and you need CHETAH as a baseline label-assignment method to compare accuracy against neural-network or scmap-based classifiers. When no labeled reference/training data exist for the tissue of interest — supervised reference-based methods including CHETAH are inapplicable and unsupervised clustering (e.g., Seurat, SC3) is the only viable option When the test data contain cell types absent from the reference set, or unknown/rare cells are expected — CHETAH produces an unignorable amount of unassigned/intermediate cell labels in such settings, which is undesirable when exhaustive assignment is required When the goal is clustering de novo rather than transferring known labels to new data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply CHETAH, a correlation/hierarchy-based reference method for cell label assignment, as a competing annotation approach when benchmarking supervised label-assignment methods like NeuCA on scRNA-seq data with labeled training sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Apply CHETAH, a correlation/hierarchy-based reference method for cell label assignment, as a competing annotation approach when benchmarking supervised label-assignment methods like NeuCA on scRNA-seq data with labeled training sets.

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell binary calls (e.g. cells exceeding a hub-score outlier cutoff of mu + 3 sigma) stratified by a categorical variable such as donor age, and you need to test whether the outlier proportion shifts across categories.
skills.name: chi-square-contingency-testing
skills.search_text: chi-square-contingency-testing Use when you have per-cell binary calls (e.g. cells exceeding a hub-score outlier cutoff of mu + 3 sigma) stratified by a categorical variable such as donor age, and you need to test whether the outlier proportion shifts across categories. Your per-cell scores are continuous and you have not yet binarized them into outlier/non-outlier calls at a defined cutoff (e.g. mu + 3 sigma) — chi-square on unthresholded values is inappropriate Expected cell counts in any contingency-table cell are very small (e.g. rare age groups with few cells), where the chi-square approximation breaks down You want to compare mean score distributions rather than proportions of outlier cells — a rank-based or parametric test on continuous scores is the better choice http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply a chi-square test to an outlier/non-outlier contingency table to evaluate age dependence of senescent cell proportions, as done in SenePy to show tongue keratinocyte type-A/type-B hub outlier cells accumulate with organismal age (p = 7.9e-86 and 7.9e-90). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Apply a chi-square test to an outlier/non-outlier contingency table to evaluate age dependence of senescent cell proportions, as done in SenePy to show tongue keratinocyte type-A/type-B hub outlier cells accumulate with organismal age (p = 7.9e-86 and 7.9e-90).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your per-cell scores are continuous and you have not yet binarized them into outlier/non-outlier calls at a defined cutoff (e.g. mu + 3 sigma) — chi-square on unthresholded values is inappropriate Expected cell counts in any contingency-table cell are very small (e.g. rare age groups with few cells), where the chi-square approximation breaks down You want to compare mean score distributions rather than proportions of outlier cells — a rank-based or parametric test on continuous scores is the better choice

skills.description: Use when cell communities (from EVA or Louvain clustering) must be tested for differential enrichment between two conditions (e.g. perturbed vs normal cells), and you need chi-square P-values plus ARI to quantify clustering recovery.
skills.name: chi-square-differential-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: chi-square-differential-abundance-testing Use when cell communities (from EVA or Louvain clustering) must be tested for differential enrichment between two conditions (e.g. perturbed vs normal cells), and you need chi-square P-values plus ARI to quantify clustering recovery. When per-replicate/per-sample differential testing is required: the pooled condition-by-state chi-square ignores replicate structure, whereas the paper's DoDA step explicitly supplies a replicate variable (varREP="mouse") When the goal is DA-testing on real data without attribute information; the paper's advantage over the Louvain-analog was more pronounced only in settings with weaker clustering structure When the input lacks a cell attribute (condition/phenotype label) to attach to the graph vertices — EVA's purity-modularity trade-off cannot be defined without it http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether inferred cell communities are differentially enriched between biological conditions by building condition-by-state contingency tables from the ELVAR/EVA partition of the single-cell state-manifold graph and running chi-square tests, complemented by adjusted Rand Index evaluation against simulated ground-truth labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Tests whether inferred cell communities are differentially enriched between biological conditions by building condition-by-state contingency tables from the ELVAR/EVA partition of the single-cell state-manifold graph and running chi-square tests, complemented by adjusted Rand Index evaluation against simulated ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When per-replicate/per-sample differential testing is required: the pooled condition-by-state chi-square ignores replicate structure, whereas the paper's DoDA step explicitly supplies a replicate variable (varREP="mouse") When the goal is DA-testing on real data without attribute information; the paper's advantage over the Louvain-analog was more pronounced only in settings with weaker clustering structure When the input lacks a cell attribute (condition/phenotype label) to attach to the graph vertices — EVA's purity-modularity trade-off cannot be defined without it

skills.description: Use when comparing overlap of two gene-level hit sets (e.g., DGE calls from Welch t-tests and DUL calls from scUTRboot WUI tests) and you need to test whether their intersection exceeds chance expectation.
skills.name: chi-square-independence-testing
skills.search_text: chi-square-independence-testing Use when comparing overlap of two gene-level hit sets (e.g., DGE calls from Welch t-tests and DUL calls from scUTRboot WUI tests) and you need to test whether their intersection exceeds chance expectation. Gene sets have very small expected cell counts under independence (common for tiny hit sets) where Fisher's exact test is more appropriate than chi-square. The question is effect size or direction concordance of the same genes rather than set membership overlap against a shared background. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Statistical test used to determine whether two gene sets (e.g., differentially expressed genes and differentially 3'UTR-lengthened genes) overlap more than expected by chance across cell-type comparisons, establishing whether DGE and DUL are independent regulatory axes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Statistical test used to determine whether two gene sets (e.g., differentially expressed genes and differentially 3'UTR-lengthened genes) overlap more than expected by chance across cell-type comparisons, establishing whether DGE and DUL are independent regulatory axes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene sets have very small expected cell counts under independence (common for tiny hit sets) where Fisher's exact test is more appropriate than chi-square. The question is effect size or direction concordance of the same genes rather than set membership overlap against a shared background.

skills.description: Use when comparing categorical read-assignment proportions (isoform, TSS, or polyA-site usage) between two biological groups per gene, and you need a gene-level significance call with FDR control and a minimum effect size (delta-PI).
skills.name: chi-square-proportion-testing
skills.search_text: chi-square-proportion-testing Use when comparing categorical read-assignment proportions (isoform, TSS, or polyA-site usage) between two biological groups per gene, and you need a gene-level significance call with FDR control and a minimum effect size (delta-PI). The question is differential gene or exon expression magnitude rather than a shift in isoform/TSS/polyA proportions — use ExonQuant or standard DE tools instead A cell-type-hierarchical comparison is required; the article's non-hierarchical setting (is.hier=FALSE) applies to the bulk two-region test Genes have fewer than minNumReads=25 long reads, where chi-square proportion tests are underpowered/unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Per-gene n x 2 chi-square testing of isoform (and TSS/polyA-site) proportion differences between conditions, implemented via scisorseqr's DiffSplicingAnalysis, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and a delta-PI effect-size filter. This is the statistical core of the HIPP-vs-PFC differential isoform expression (DIE) test in the postnatal mouse brain isoform atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Per-gene n x 2 chi-square testing of isoform (and TSS/polyA-site) proportion differences between conditions, implemented via scisorseqr's DiffSplicingAnalysis, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and a delta-PI effect-size filter. This is the statistical core of the HIPP-vs-PFC differential isoform expression (DIE) test in the postnatal mouse brain isoform atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is differential gene or exon expression magnitude rather than a shift in isoform/TSS/polyA proportions — use ExonQuant or standard DE tools instead A cell-type-hierarchical comparison is required; the article's non-hierarchical setting (is.hier=FALSE) applies to the bulk two-region test Genes have fewer than minNumReads=25 long reads, where chi-square proportion tests are underpowered/unreliable

skills.description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity-built from Illumina RNA-Seq reads) is suspected of containing chimeric or redundant contigs and no reference genome is available to assess assembly quality.
skills.name: chimera-removal-from-de-novo-transcriptomes
skills.search_text: chimera-removal-from-de-novo-transcriptomes Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity-built from Illumina RNA-Seq reads) is suspected of containing chimeric or redundant contigs and no reference genome is available to assess assembly quality. A reference genome is available for assessing assembly quality — TransRate is reference-free, designed for cases where 'there is no reference genome available to assess de novo assembly quality'. Custom ordering of the filtering steps is required — 'Custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version'. The input is already a curated/filtered transcriptome rather than a raw de novo assembly — re-applying the filters may remove alternative-splicing contigs misclassified as chimeras. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A filtering pipeline (Bellerophon) that improves de novo transcriptome assemblies by removing chimeric, lowly expressed, and redundant contigs using TransRate quality assessment, a TPM filter (cut-off 1), CD-HIT-EST (95% identity), and TransRate-C, removing between 40% and 91.9% of chimeras. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571
skills.summary: A filtering pipeline (Bellerophon) that improves de novo transcriptome assemblies by removing chimeric, lowly expressed, and redundant contigs using TransRate quality assessment, a TPM filter (cut-off 1), CD-HIT-EST (95% identity), and TransRate-C, removing between 40% and 91.9% of chimeras.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome is available for assessing assembly quality — TransRate is reference-free, designed for cases where 'there is no reference genome available to assess de novo assembly quality'. skills.description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a tumor sample must be aligned for fusion detection (Arriba) or for RNA-side variant callers (transIndel, ScanExitron) and chimeric events such as gene fusions must not be missed.
skills.name: chimeric-aware-rna-seq-alignment
skills.search_text: chimeric-aware-rna-seq-alignment Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a tumor sample must be aligned for fusion detection (Arriba) or for RNA-side variant callers (transIndel, ScanExitron) and chimeric events such as gene fusions must not be missed. Input is DNA-seq (WES/WGS) — ScanNeo2 aligns DNA-seq read groups directly with BWA-MEM at mapq 30, not with chimeric-aware STAR. Only fusion calling is needed and the STAR parameter --alignIntronMax would have to be reduced — Arriba explicitly avoids this by working on chimeric-aware STAR alignments. Reads are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — the short-read STAR workflow described here is not designed for them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align RNA-seq read groups against the reference genome with STAR run in chimeric-aware mode (chimSegmentMin 20, chimScoreMin 10, chimJunctionOverhangMin 10, chimScoreDropMax 30, chimScoreSeparation 10, matching STAR v2.7.10b) so that split/contiguous alignments spanning gene fusions and structural rearrangements are captured for downstream neoantigen discovery in ScanNeo2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Align RNA-seq read groups against the reference genome with STAR run in chimeric-aware mode (chimSegmentMin 20, chimScoreMin 10, chimJunctionOverhangMin 10, chimScoreDropMax 30, chimScoreSeparation 10, matching STAR v2.7.10b) so that split/contiguous alignments spanning gene fusions and structural rearrangements are captured for downstream neoantigen discovery in ScanNeo2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is DNA-seq (WES/WGS) — ScanNeo2 aligns DNA-seq read groups directly with BWA-MEM at mapq 30, not with chimeric-aware STAR. Only fusion calling is needed and the STAR parameter --alignIntronMax would have to be reduced — Arriba explicitly avoids this by working on chimeric-aware STAR alignments. Reads are long reads (Nanopore/PacBio) — the short-read STAR workflow described here is not designed for them.

skills.description: Use when STAR alignment logs from RNA-seq samples grouped by tissue show anomalous unmapped ('too short') rates and you need to test whether chimeric reads co-occur with unmappable reads, e.g. to diagnose genome-build or annotation-driven mapping failures in one tissue.
skills.name: chimeric-read-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: chimeric-read-correlation-analysis Use when STAR alignment logs from RNA-seq samples grouped by tissue show anomalous unmapped ('too short') rates and you need to test whether chimeric reads co-occur with unmappable reads, e.g. to diagnose genome-build or annotation-driven mapping failures in one tissue. The analysis goal is allele-specific expression detection from VCF files — that is handled by the VADT binomial-test pipeline, not STAR log statistics. Reads are aligned to a different genome build or annotation than Gallus_gallus_5.0 / Ensembl release 86, so the expected per-tissue validation values would not apply. You need per-sample gene-body coverage assessment (RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py) rather than whole-sample mapping-rate summaries. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Extracts per-sample STAR alignment statistics (uniquely mapped, unmapped 'too short', and chimeric read percentages) from two-pass STAR RNA-seq runs, compares them across broiler tissue groups via one-way ANOVA, and fits a linear regression of percent chimeric versus percent unmappable reads in breast muscle to diagnose mapping problems. Quantifies tissue-specific mapping bias in the Gallus_gallus_5.0-based pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Extracts per-sample STAR alignment statistics (uniquely mapped, unmapped 'too short', and chimeric read percentages) from two-pass STAR RNA-seq runs, compares them across broiler tissue groups via one-way ANOVA, and fits a linear regression of percent chimeric versus percent unmappable reads in breast muscle to diagnose mapping problems. Quantifies tissue-specific mapping bias in the Gallus_gallus_5.0-based pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is allele-specific expression detection from VCF files — that is handled by the VADT binomial-test pipeline, not STAR log statistics. skills.search_text: chimeric-read-local-alignment Use when running Anchored-fusion on paired-end RNA-seq (FASTQ) data and you have candidate chimeric reads whose mates fail to map to the anchored target gene, requiring precise fusion-partner localization and breakpoint resolution. The sequencing data is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome data — Anchored-fusion requires paired-end RNA-seq You need to detect fusions that do not include the user-provided target/anchored gene — they will not be reported You only need genome-wide de novo fusion discovery without a gene of interest — use STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, or Arriba instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Local-alignment refinement step of Anchored-fusion in which candidate chimeric read pairs (one mate mapped to the anchored gene, the unmapped mate aligned genome-wide by BWA-MEM) are realigned with BLAT to pinpoint the precise fusion breakpoint. skills.summary: Local-alignment refinement step of Anchored-fusion in which candidate chimeric read pairs (one mate mapped to the anchored gene, the unmapped mate aligned genome-wide by BWA-MEM) are realigned with BLAT to pinpoint the precise fusion breakpoint. skills.name: chimeric-read-splitting
skills.search_text: chimeric-read-splitting Use when demultiplexing long reads (e.g. Ebrahimi et al. 2022 simulated FASTQ) that may contain more than one barcode construct per read, and each detected construct must be reported separately. Reads are short single-end reads where at most one barcode construct is expected, so iterative re-search adds no value Only the flanking sequence is known and barcodes must be discovered de novo rather than matched against a whitelist (Flexiplex's discovery mode handles that separately) The goal is downstream cell-barcode filtering against a whitelist with empty-droplet removal via inflection point — that is flexiplex-filter's role, not chimeric splitting http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Iteratively re-search a read for additional flank/barcode constructs after a first hit, masking each found region so chimeric reads carrying multiple barcode+UMI constructs are split into multiple assignments, mirroring Flexiplex's handling of chimeric long reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Iteratively re-search a read for additional flank/barcode constructs after a first hit, masking each found region so chimeric reads carrying multiple barcode+UMI constructs are split into multiple assignments, mirroring Flexiplex's handling of chimeric long reads.

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) rather than hyb-format hybrid records — hybkit operates on the hyb format defined by the Hyb software package, not on raw reads. skills.search_text: chromatin-3d-model-coordinate-conversion Use when a cudaMMC simulation output file containing 3D coordinates of chromatin beads must be turned into a parseable structural file, particularly for whole-chromosome models whose bead counts exceed legacy PDB format limits. Input is raw ChIA-PET data (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) rather than a cudaMMC model output file — these are simulation inputs, not coordinate structures to convert A downstream tool strictly requires legacy PDB ATOM/PDB format and cannot parse mmCIF — the paper deliberately chose mmCIF because PDB cannot hold the bead counts of whole-chromosome models The structure of interest is an experimental protein/nucleic-acid structure with real atoms, not a bead-based chromatin model from cudaMMC/3D-GNOME http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Converts the 3D bead coordinates of a cudaMMC multiscale Monte Carlo chromatin model into a PDBx/mmCIF structure file (model.cif), where each chromatin bead is written as an atom_site record. mmCIF is chosen over legacy PDB format because it supports a higher number of beads (pseudo-atoms) per structure, which is required for high-resolution whole-chromosome models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Converts the 3D bead coordinates of a cudaMMC multiscale Monte Carlo chromatin model into a PDBx/mmCIF structure file (model.cif), where each chromatin bead is written as an atom_site record. mmCIF is chosen over legacy PDB format because it supports a higher number of beads (pseudo-atoms) per structure, which is required for high-resolution whole-chromosome models.

skills.search_text: chromatin-contact-based-scoring Use when candidate enhancer regions need enhancer-gene interaction scores that incorporate chromatin contact data (e.g. Hi-C maps), such as ranking CRISPRi-validated enhancer-gene pairs on the three validation datasets or comparing against model-based scores like Enformer in-silico mutagenesis. When no chromatin contact data (Hi-C matrix or normalized contact files) is available for the cell type or genome build — the adapted ABC model depends on the contact term When the task is TF affinity or TF-gene scoring rather than enhancer-gene interaction scoring — STARE's TF-affinity part or TEPIC is the appropriate component instead When interactions beyond ~5 MB from the TSS must be considered, since STARE uses a default 5 MB window around the TSS http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Score enhancer-gene interactions with the adapted Activity-By-Contact (ABC) model, which adjusts enhancer activity by the number of chromatin contacts between the enhancer and each candidate target gene and considers all annotated TSSs of a gene. skills.summary: Score enhancer-gene interactions with the adapted Activity-By-Contact (ABC) model, which adjusts enhancer activity by the number of chromatin contacts between the enhancer and each candidate target gene and considers all annotated TSSs of a gene. skills.description: Use when two chromatin modelling tools must be compared for computational performance or run-to-run stability, and per-run execution times are available across repeated simulations on defined chromosomes.

skills.search_text: chromatin-modeling-benchmark-comparison Use when two chromatin modelling tools must be compared for computational performance or run-to-run stability, and per-run execution times are available across repeated simulations on defined chromosomes. The goal is structural accuracy of 3D chromatin models (e.g. contact-map fidelity) rather than computational performance or run-time stability. Only a single simulation run per tool is available, so no run-to-run dispersion (standard deviation) can be computed. The tools are not run on the same workstation and identical chromosome inputs, making timing comparisons confounded by hardware or data differences. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Benchmark and compare execution-time stability of chromatin 3D modelling engines (e.g. cudaMMC vs 3D-GNOME) by computing the coefficient of variation (CoV) of run times over repeated simulation runs on the same chromosomes and workstation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Benchmark and compare execution-time stability of chromatin 3D modelling engines (e.g. cudaMMC vs 3D-GNOME) by computing the coefficient of variation (CoV) of run times over repeated simulation runs on the same chromosomes and workstation.

skills.summary: Reconstruct ensembles of 3D chromatin structures for individual chromosomes from ChIA-PET data (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) using cudaMMC, the GPU-enhanced Multiscale Monte Carlo successor of 3D-GNOME, which enables fast ensemble generation for large chromosomes on GRCh37/human datasets.

skills.description: Use when a fully connected directed graph over measured variables must be collapsed into a single rooted directed tree, and data-driven edge weights (e.g., from bivariate SEM or spline fits) are available or can be estimated per edge.
skills.name: chu-liu-edmonds-arborescence-reconstruction
skills.search_text: chu-liu-edmonds-arborescence-reconstruction Use when a fully connected directed graph over measured variables must be collapsed into a single rooted directed tree, and data-driven edge weights (e.g., from bivariate SEM or spline fits) are available or can be estimated per edge. The input is already a validated DAG from structural learning and no tree-structured summary is needed — CAT collapses a fully connected scored digraph to a tree and discards polytree structure The goal is SEM model improvement with bow-free covariances or latent-variable confounding adjustment (use SEMbap-style steps instead) Edge weights cannot be estimated per directed edge because data are missing or the graph is undirected-only with no bivariate fit possible http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct a directed spanning tree (arborescence) from a weighted digraph by first scoring every directed edge with weights derived from bivariate additive regression fits (penalized regression splines via mgcv::gam, residual-variance-based weights so stronger dependence maps to lower cost), then applying the Chu–Liu–Edmonds algorithm (RBGL::edmondsOptimumBranching) to extract the minimum-weight spanning arborescence, as used in the CAT (causal additive tree) phase of SEMtree(). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Reconstruct a directed spanning tree (arborescence) from a weighted digraph by first scoring every directed edge with weights derived from bivariate additive regression fits (penalized regression splines via mgcv::gam, residual-variance-based weights so stronger dependence maps to lower cost), then applying the Chu–Liu–Edmonds algorithm (RBGL::edmondsOptimumBranching) to extract the minimum-weight spanning arborescence, as used in the CAT (causal additive tree) phase of SEMtree().
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a validated DAG from structural learning and no tree-structured summary is needed — CAT collapses a fully connected scored digraph to a tree and discards polytree structure The goal is SEM model improvement with bow-free covariances or latent-variable confounding adjustment (use SEMbap-style steps instead) Edge weights cannot be estimated per directed edge because data are missing or the graph is undirected-only with no bivariate fit possible

skills.description: Use when fitting scPLS to large scRNAseq count matrices (thousands of cells × tens of thousands of genes) where the naive full-matrix EM becomes CPU-prohibitive and a scalable block-wise EM is needed.

skills.search_text: chunked-estep-vectorized-computation Use when fitting scPLS to large scRNAseq count matrices (thousands of cells × tens of thousands of genes) where the naive full-matrix EM becomes CPU-prohibitive and a scalable block-wise EM is needed.
