skills.search_text: circrna-call-coordinate-intersection Use when you have circRNA call sets from ≥2 detection pipelines on the same ribo− RNA-seq data and need coordinate-based overlaps, Venn counts, or per-circRNA BSJ fragment comparisons. Call sets come from different genome builds or annotations, so coordinate intersection would be spurious Only one circRNA detection tool was run and no cross-tool comparison is possible The goal is quantifying circ vs linear expression (FPB/CIRCscore) rather than comparing detection tools — use the CLEAR quantification workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Intersects circRNA call sets from multiple pipelines (CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR, MapSplice, DCC/circtools) by genomic coordinates (chrom, start, end, strand) to compute pairwise and three-way overlap counts and compare per-tool BSJ fragment support. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Intersects circRNA call sets from multiple pipelines (CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR, MapSplice, DCC/circtools) by genomic coordinates (chrom, start, end, strand) to compute pairwise and three-way overlap counts and compare per-tool BSJ fragment support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Call sets come from different genome builds or annotations, so coordinate intersection would be spurious Only one circRNA detection tool was run and no cross-tool comparison is possible The goal is quantifying circ vs linear expression (FPB/CIRCscore) rather than comparing detection tools — use the CLEAR quantification workflow instead

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ/alignment data from knockdown (shRNA/siRNA) or condition-controlled RNA-seq experiments must be mined for back-splice circRNAs to test whether knocking down a candidate RBP changes global circRNA expression.
skills.name: circrna-detection-from-rnaseq-alignments
skills.search_text: circrna-detection-from-rnaseq-alignments Use when raw FASTQ/alignment data from knockdown (shRNA/siRNA) or condition-controlled RNA-seq experiments must be mined for back-splice circRNAs to test whether knocking down a candidate RBP changes global circRNA expression. Input is already a circRNA count/feature table and no raw alignments are available, so CIRI2/find_circ cannot be re-run from the alignments The goal is RBP-circRNA binding-site prediction or NMF-based regulator discovery (CRIT's features-collecting and cluster-identify stages) rather than validating global circRNA expression change upon knockdown No suitable public knockdown RNA-seq data exist for the RBP of interest — in the source study only 13 of 22 candidate RBPs had suitable knockdown data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect circRNAs directly from raw shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq alignments using two complementary algorithms (CIRI2 and find_circ), then quantify global circRNA burden per sample via the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI) to test whether an RBP regulates circRNA expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Detect circRNAs directly from raw shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq alignments using two complementary algorithms (CIRI2 and find_circ), then quantify global circRNA burden per sample via the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI) to test whether an RBP regulates circRNA expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a circRNA count/feature table and no raw alignments are available, so CIRI2/find_circ cannot be re-run from the alignments The goal is RBP-circRNA binding-site prediction or NMF-based regulator discovery (CRIT's features-collecting and cluster-identify stages) rather than validating global circRNA expression change upon knockdown No suitable public knockdown RNA-seq data exist for the RBP of interest — in the source study only 13 of 22 candidate RBPs had suitable knockdown data

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify circRNA expression and compare it to cognate linear RNA expression from ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files, e.g. to distinguish tumor vs paired-normal circRNA profiles where standard fragment counts fail.
skills.name: circrna-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: circrna-expression-quantification Use when you need to quantify circRNA expression and compare it to cognate linear RNA expression from ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files, e.g. to distinguish tumor vs paired-normal circRNA profiles where standard fragment counts fail. Input RNA-seq is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated: linear RNAs are largely depleted, so accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation is unsuitable Data is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, in which circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3′-end poly(A) tails You only need circRNA discovery/annotation without circular-vs-linear expression comparison (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted (ribo−) RNA-seq using the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline, which reports FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and a CIRCscore (FPBcirc/FPBlinear) per circRNA so circular and linear expression at the same gene loci can be directly compared. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Quantify circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted (ribo−) RNA-seq using the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline, which reports FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and a CIRCscore (FPBcirc/FPBlinear) per circRNA so circular and linear expression at the same gene loci can be directly compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA-seq is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated: linear RNAs are largely depleted, so accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation is unsuitable Data is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, in which circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3′-end poly(A) tails You only need circRNA discovery/annotation without circular-vs-linear expression comparison (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices)

skills.description: Use when paired-end RNA-seq alignments and a back-splice junction list exist and the goal is to reconstruct full-length circular transcript sequences (including isoforms) and estimate FPKM/TPM expression per circRNA locus.
skills.name: circrna-full-length-isoform-assembly
skills.search_text: circrna-full-length-isoform-assembly Use when paired-end RNA-seq alignments and a back-splice junction list exist and the goal is to reconstruct full-length circular transcript sequences (including isoforms) and estimate FPKM/TPM expression per circRNA locus. Samples without RNase R treatment: CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, and remnant linear mRNA can generate false assembled transcripts Goal is intronic or intergenic circRNAs: the current pipeline assembles and quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only a list of back-splice sites is needed: BSJ detectors alone suffice; CircAST is for full-length isoform assembly and quantification, not BSJ discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble full-length alternatively spliced circular RNA isoform sequences and quantify their expression from RNA-seq using CircAST's multiple splice graphs with EM-based maximum-likelihood read allocation, downstream of BSJ detection tools (CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, UROBORUS). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Assemble full-length alternatively spliced circular RNA isoform sequences and quantify their expression from RNA-seq using CircAST's multiple splice graphs with EM-based maximum-likelihood read allocation, downstream of BSJ detection tools (CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, UROBORUS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples without RNase R treatment: CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, and remnant linear mRNA can generate false assembled transcripts Goal is intronic or intergenic circRNAs: the current pipeline assembles and quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only a list of back-splice sites is needed: BSJ detectors alone suffice; CircAST is for full-length isoform assembly and quantification, not BSJ discovery

skills.description: Use when CircAST output tables (per-transcript junction reads, assigned reads, FPKM/TPM) are available for multiple samples and the goal is to characterize how many and how diverse the circular isoforms are across cell lines or tissues.
skills.name: circrna-isoform-distribution-statistics
skills.search_text: circrna-isoform-distribution-statistics Use when CircAST output tables (per-transcript junction reads, assigned reads, FPKM/TPM) are available for multiple samples and the goal is to characterize how many and how diverse the circular isoforms are across cell lines or tissues. The samples were not RNase R-treated — the article states 'CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples', so diversity statistics on non-enriched libraries would be unreliable. The target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the current CircAST pipeline may miss these, so exon-annotated transcript counts and exon-number distributions would be incomplete. The alignment or BSJ detection used a different GTF than CircAST — counts of assembled exonic transcripts would be inconsistent with the junction lists and not comparable across samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Aggregate CircAST per-sample outputs to quantify circRNA isoform diversity: count exonic circular transcripts, examine exon-number and full-length distributions, and compute the fraction of back-splice junctions assigned to more than one isoform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Aggregate CircAST per-sample outputs to quantify circRNA isoform diversity: count exonic circular transcripts, examine exon-number and full-length distributions, and compute the fraction of back-splice junctions assigned to more than one isoform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples were not RNase R-treated — the article states 'CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples', so diversity statistics on non-enriched libraries would be unreliable. The target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the current CircAST pipeline may miss these, so exon-annotated transcript counts and exon-number distributions would be incomplete. The alignment or BSJ detection used a different GTF than CircAST — counts of assembled exonic transcripts would be inconsistent with the junction lists and not comparable across samples.

skills.description: Use when simulated RNA-seq data with known ground-truth circRNA isoforms have been processed by CircAST and you must quantify how BSJ overlap complexity (relation index) affects assembly and quantification accuracy.
skills.name: circrna-isoform-quantification-accuracy-analysis
skills.search_text: circrna-isoform-quantification-accuracy-analysis Use when simulated RNA-seq data with known ground-truth circRNA isoforms have been processed by CircAST and you must quantify how BSJ overlap complexity (relation index) affects assembly and quantification accuracy. Data is real experimental RNA-seq without simulated ground-truth isoforms, so sensitivity/precision against truth cannot be computed Input is not CircAST output — raw FASTQ, SAM/BAM, or upstream BSJ detector output (CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS lists) requires assembly by CircAST first Goal is circRNA detection/BSJ discovery rather than evaluating isoform-level assembly and quantification accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks CircAST's full-length circRNA assembly and isoform quantification on simulated data by stratifying back-splice junction (BSJ) sites by relation index (RI) — the size of the BSJ overlap equivalence class — and computing sensitivity, precision, and theoretical-vs-estimated expression correlation per RI bin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Benchmarks CircAST's full-length circRNA assembly and isoform quantification on simulated data by stratifying back-splice junction (BSJ) sites by relation index (RI) — the size of the BSJ overlap equivalence class — and computing sensitivity, precision, and theoretical-vs-estimated expression correlation per RI bin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is real experimental RNA-seq without simulated ground-truth isoforms, so sensitivity/precision against truth cannot be computed Input is not CircAST output — raw FASTQ, SAM/BAM, or upstream BSJ detector output (CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS lists) requires assembly by CircAST first Goal is circRNA detection/BSJ discovery rather than evaluating isoform-level assembly and quantification accuracy

skills.description: Use when validating circRNA quantification from ribo− RNA-seq against RT-qPCR or existing FPKM/FPM measures, or when reproducing published Pearson correlations (e.g. r=0.92, 0.78, 0.72, 1.00, 0.93) for FPB and CIRCscore values.
skills.name: circrna-linear-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: circrna-linear-expression-correlation-analysis Use when validating circRNA quantification from ribo− RNA-seq against RT-qPCR or existing FPKM/FPM measures, or when reproducing published Pearson correlations (e.g. r=0.92, 0.78, 0.72, 1.00, 0.93) for FPB and CIRCscore values. Input data are poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq data, where circRNAs are depleted and BSJ-based quantification of circRNA expression is unreliable The goal is circRNA discovery/annotation rather than quantification validation — use the base CIRCexplorer2 pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce the CLEAR pipeline's circular vs linear RNA quantification statistics by computing Pearson correlations between FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore values and reference measures (FPKM, FPM, RT-qPCR) on ribo− RNA-seq data, validating the pipeline's quantification against published coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Reproduce the CLEAR pipeline's circular vs linear RNA quantification statistics by computing Pearson correlations between FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore values and reference measures (FPKM, FPM, RT-qPCR) on ribo− RNA-seq data, validating the pipeline's quantification against published coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq data, where circRNAs are depleted and BSJ-based quantification of circRNA expression is unreliable The goal is circRNA discovery/annotation rather than quantification validation — use the base CIRCexplorer2 pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when a CircAST result file (tab-separated, 13 columns ending in junction read counts, FPKM, TPM, assigned reads) must be loaded and structured for downstream RI stratification, isoform comparison, or expression-accuracy analysis.
skills.name: circrna-output-table-parsing
skills.search_text: circrna-output-table-parsing Use when a CircAST result file (tab-separated, 13 columns ending in junction read counts, FPKM, TPM, assigned reads) must be loaded and structured for downstream RI stratification, isoform comparison, or expression-accuracy analysis. Input is a raw circRNA junction list from CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS rather than CircAST's post-assembly output table Analysis requires intronic or intergenic circular transcripts, which the current CircAST pipeline may miss The sample was not RNase R-treated, since CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Parse and structure the tab-separated output table produced by CircAST's full-length circRNA assembly and quantification run, whose 13 columns (bed-like coordinates through FPKM/TPM and assigned read counts) serve as the substrate for downstream analyses such as relation-index (RI) stratification of assembly accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Parse and structure the tab-separated output table produced by CircAST's full-length circRNA assembly and quantification run, whose 13 columns (bed-like coordinates through FPKM/TPM and assigned read counts) serve as the substrate for downstream analyses such as relation-index (RI) stratification of assembly accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw circRNA junction list from CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS rather than CircAST's post-assembly output table Analysis requires intronic or intergenic circular transcripts, which the current CircAST pipeline may miss The sample was not RNase R-treated, since CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples

skills.description: Use when building protein–circRNA interaction counts (C values) from predicted RBP–RNA interactomes plus circRNA annotations, e.g. as an input feature for candidate regulator scoring or clustering.
skills.name: circrna-protein-interaction-mapping
skills.search_text: circrna-protein-interaction-mapping Use when building protein–circRNA interaction counts (C values) from predicted RBP–RNA interactomes plus circRNA annotations, e.g. as an input feature for candidate regulator scoring or clustering. You need experimentally validated (e.g. CLIP-seq) RBP–circRNA interactions rather than catRAPID-predicted scores; CRIT separately validates predictions against CLIP databases. You only have expression or survival data and no interactome plus coordinate annotation files — C values cannot be computed without RNAct, CircBase and GENCODE inputs. Your analysis needs partial-overlap binding-site resolution rather than whole-circRNA containment within the host/associated RNA. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how many circRNAs each protein binds by filtering the RNAct catRAPID human interactome to interaction scores >= 30 and aligning CircBase circRNA coordinates to GENCODE v37 RNA coordinates, yielding the C-value feature used in CRIT's feature matrix for NMF-based circRNA regulator identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Quantifies how many circRNAs each protein binds by filtering the RNAct catRAPID human interactome to interaction scores >= 30 and aligning CircBase circRNA coordinates to GENCODE v37 RNA coordinates, yielding the C-value feature used in CRIT's feature matrix for NMF-based circRNA regulator identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need experimentally validated (e.g. CLIP-seq) RBP–circRNA interactions rather than catRAPID-predicted scores; CRIT separately validates predictions against CLIP databases. You only have expression or survival data and no interactome plus coordinate annotation files — C values cannot be computed without RNAct, CircBase and GENCODE inputs. Your analysis needs partial-overlap binding-site resolution rather than whole-circRNA containment within the host/associated RNA.

skills.description: Use when a list of predicted circRNA regulators (e.g., CRIT NMF cluster output) must be tested for over-representation of circRNA-binding RBPs from CLIP databases (POSTAR3, ENCORI) via one-sided Fisher's exact tests.
skills.name: circrna-regulator-candidate-validation
skills.search_text: circrna-regulator-candidate-validation Use when a list of predicted circRNA regulators (e.g., CRIT NMF cluster output) must be tested for over-representation of circRNA-binding RBPs from CLIP databases (POSTAR3, ENCORI) via one-sided Fisher's exact tests. The goal is to predict or cluster circRNA regulators from omics features (NMF feature collection / cluster identify), rather than to validate an already-defined candidate list. No external circRNA-binding RBP reference list (POSTAR3/ENCORI) is available, so no 2x2 contingency table can be constructed. The question is functional validation (e.g., whether RBP knockdown changes global circRNA expression in shRNA/siRNA RNA-seq datasets), not statistical enrichment against CLIP databases. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reproduces the CLIP-database validation step of the CRIT pipeline: one-sided Fisher's exact tests in R that test whether CRIT's NMF-derived candidate circRNA regulators are over-represented among known circRNA-binding RBPs from POSTAR3 (112 RBPs) and ENCORI (132 down to 27 RBPs stringency sub-lists), against both a 1,344-RBP background and the total gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Reproduces the CLIP-database validation step of the CRIT pipeline: one-sided Fisher's exact tests in R that test whether CRIT's NMF-derived candidate circRNA regulators are over-represented among known circRNA-binding RBPs from POSTAR3 (112 RBPs) and ENCORI (132 down to 27 RBPs stringency sub-lists), against both a 1,344-RBP background and the total gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to predict or cluster circRNA regulators from omics features (NMF feature collection / cluster identify), rather than to validate an already-defined candidate list. No external circRNA-binding RBP reference list (POSTAR3/ENCORI) is available, so no 2x2 contingency table can be constructed. The question is functional validation (e.g., whether RBP knockdown changes global circRNA expression in shRNA/siRNA RNA-seq datasets), not statistical enrichment against CLIP databases.

skills.description: Use when a circRNA junction list from a BSJ detector (CIRCexplorer2 annotated_circ.txt, CIRI2 result.txt, UROBORUS, or any similar tool) must be reshaped into CircAST's circRNA_list.txt (chromosome/start/end) before full-length assembly.
skills.name: circrna-tool-output-format-conversion
skills.search_text: circrna-tool-output-format-conversion Use when a circRNA junction list from a BSJ detector (CIRCexplorer2 annotated_circ.txt, CIRI2 result.txt, UROBORUS, or any similar tool) must be reshaped into CircAST's circRNA_list.txt (chromosome/start/end) before full-length assembly. The upstream tool already emits CircAST-compatible format (CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS annotated_circ.txt, result.txt, or circRNA_list.txt can be passed directly via -J). The goal is linear transcript assembly (e.g., Cufflinks) or de novo BSJ detection itself — this skill only reshapes existing junction lists. The circRNAs of interest are intronic or intergenic, which the current CircAST pipeline cannot assemble (it handles exon-annotated circular transcripts only). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Convert back-splice junction (BSJ) lists produced by upstream circRNA detectors (CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, UROBORUS, or other similar tools) into the CircAST circRNA_list.txt input format (chromosome, start, end columns) so CircAST can assemble full-length circular isoforms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Convert back-splice junction (BSJ) lists produced by upstream circRNA detectors (CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, UROBORUS, or other similar tools) into the CircAST circRNA_list.txt input format (chromosome, start, end columns) so CircAST can assemble full-length circular isoforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The upstream tool already emits CircAST-compatible format (CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS annotated_circ.txt, result.txt, or circRNA_list.txt can be passed directly via -J). The goal is linear transcript assembly (e.g., Cufflinks) or de novo BSJ detection itself — this skill only reshapes existing junction lists. The circRNAs of interest are intronic or intergenic, which the current CircAST pipeline cannot assemble (it handles exon-annotated circular transcripts only).

skills.description: Use when back-spliced junction records (e.g., 2923 Hs68 BSJs from SRA SRR444974 in CircAST junction-list format) must be converted into full circular transcript structures on a UCSC hg19 GTF annotation.
skills.name: circrna-transcript-structure-construction-from-bsj
skills.search_text: circrna-transcript-structure-construction-from-bsj Use when back-spliced junction records (e.g., 2923 Hs68 BSJs from SRA SRR444974 in CircAST junction-list format) must be converted into full circular transcript structures on a UCSC hg19 GTF annotation. The goal is de novo reconstruction of full-length circRNA sequences from reads — use CircAST assembly on splice graphs instead of template-based structure construction The target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only raw FASTQ reads are available without prior BSJ detection by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS or a convertible junction list http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Constructs circular transcript structures from back-spliced junction (BSJ) records by integrating a CircAST-compatible junction list with UCSC hg19 GTF exon annotation, optionally introducing randomly skipped exons to generate isoform variants for simulation ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Constructs circular transcript structures from back-spliced junction (BSJ) records by integrating a CircAST-compatible junction list with UCSC hg19 GTF exon annotation, optionally introducing randomly skipped exons to generate isoform variants for simulation ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo reconstruction of full-length circRNA sequences from reads — use CircAST assembly on splice graphs instead of template-based structure construction The target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only raw FASTQ reads are available without prior BSJ detection by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS or a convertible junction list

skills.description: Use when ribo− RNA-seq data has been mapped (HISAT2 + TopHat-Fusion), circRNAs annotated via CIRCexplorer2, and FPBcirc/FPBlinear values are available per gene locus and a relative circRNA expression level is needed.
skills.name: circscore-computation-from-fpb-ratios
skills.search_text: circscore-computation-from-fpb-ratios Use when ribo− RNA-seq data has been mapped (HISAT2 + TopHat-Fusion), circRNAs annotated via CIRCexplorer2, and FPBcirc/FPBlinear values are available per gene locus and a relative circRNA expression level is needed. Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq data, where circRNAs are depleted and BSJ fragments are not represented The goal is circRNA detection/annotation itself (use CIRCexplorer2); this skill starts from mapped reads/CIRCexplorer2 output and computes relative quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Computation of CIRCscore, the relative circular RNA expression metric defined as FPBcirc divided by FPBlinear, within the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline. Because both circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq are normalized as fragments per billion mapped bases (FPB), their ratio directly compares circRNA abundance against its cognate linear RNA background. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Computation of CIRCscore, the relative circular RNA expression metric defined as FPBcirc divided by FPBlinear, within the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline. Because both circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq are normalized as fragments per billion mapped bases (FPB), their ratio directly compares circRNA abundance against its cognate linear RNA background.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Input is poly(A)+ RNA-seq data, where circRNAs are depleted and BSJ fragments are not represented The goal is circRNA detection/annotation itself (use CIRCexplorer2); this skill starts from mapped reads/CIRCexplorer2 output and computes relative quantification

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain a latent periodic process such as the cell cycle and linear PC-based or regression-based representations cannot accurately represent the circular timing of cells.
skills.name: circular-autoencoder-pseudo-time-inference
skills.search_text: circular-autoencoder-pseudo-time-inference Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain a latent periodic process such as the cell cycle and linear PC-based or regression-based representations cannot accurately represent the circular timing of cells. The latent trajectory is linear/non-periodic (e.g., a differentiation branch) — the article positions Cyclum specifically for nonlinear periodicity that linear pseudo-time methods represent poorly, not for general trajectory inference. The goal is marker-gene-only phase scoring — Cyclum's methodology projects data to a circular manifold 'instead of using marker genes', so marker-based classification is out of scope. The matrix has not been log2(x+1)-transformed, centered to mean = 1 and scaled to variance = 1; feeding raw counts departs from the preprocessing the method was validated on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder to scRNA-seq data to project cells onto a circular manifold, unfold it via least-square embedding into per-cell pseudo-time, and optionally deconvolve the inferred cell-cycle effects. It addresses the failure of linear representations (PCA, regression-based regression of cell-cycle scores) to capture periodic, circular trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Fit Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder to scRNA-seq data to project cells onto a circular manifold, unfold it via least-square embedding into per-cell pseudo-time, and optionally deconvolve the inferred cell-cycle effects. It addresses the failure of linear representations (PCA, regression-based regression of cell-cycle scores) to capture periodic, circular trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The latent trajectory is linear/non-periodic (e.g., a differentiation branch) — the article positions Cyclum specifically for nonlinear periodicity that linear pseudo-time methods represent poorly, not for general trajectory inference. The goal is marker-gene-only phase scoring — Cyclum's methodology projects data to a circular manifold 'instead of using marker genes', so marker-based classification is out of scope. The matrix has not been log2(x+1)-transformed, centered to mean = 1 and scaled to variance = 1; feeding raw counts departs from the preprocessing the method was validated on.

skills.description: Use when single-cell data carry a priori labels along a cyclical process (e.g., G1.S, S, G2, G2.M, M.G1 cell-cycle phase scores) and the goal is a supervised, interpretable circular embedding plus phase-classification accuracy rather than an unbiased clustering.
skills.name: circular-embedding-visualization-of-cell-cycle-phases
skills.search_text: circular-embedding-visualization-of-cell-cycle-phases Use when single-cell data carry a priori labels along a cyclical process (e.g., G1.S, S, G2, G2.M, M.G1 cell-cycle phase scores) and the goal is a supervised, interpretable circular embedding plus phase-classification accuracy rather than an unbiased clustering. Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable (the supervised approach is explicitly inappropriate there) More than 100 feature dimensions, where HSS feature selection is not feasible Large heterogeneity within a class or a large number of populations, where HSS-LDA performance suffers http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Repurposes linear discriminant analysis (LDA) as supervised dimensionality reduction to project single cells onto LD axes built from a priori cell-cycle phase labels, then converts LD1/LD2 coordinates to polar (angle, radius) coordinates to obtain a circular embedding in which cell-cycle phases are ordered cyclically. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Repurposes linear discriminant analysis (LDA) as supervised dimensionality reduction to project single cells onto LD axes built from a priori cell-cycle phase labels, then converts LD1/LD2 coordinates to polar (angle, radius) coordinates to obtain a circular embedding in which cell-cycle phases are ordered cyclically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable (the supervised approach is explicitly inappropriate there) More than 100 feature dimensions, where HSS feature selection is not feasible Large heterogeneity within a class or a large number of populations, where HSS-LDA performance suffers

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be given a continuous circular cell-cycle phase per cell, rather than a discrete marker-based G1/S/G2M label.
skills.name: circular-latent-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: circular-latent-autoencoder-training Use when an scRNA-seq dataset preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be given a continuous circular cell-cycle phase per cell, rather than a discrete marker-based G1/S/G2M label. The dataset has no spliced/unspliced layers and cannot be preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments — DeepCycle requires the RNA velocity moments as input. Few or no genes pass the expression threshold and hotelling filter, indicating no detectable cycling genes — the README states the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed. The goal is a discrete marker-based cell-cycle phase call rather than a continuous circular phase; the paper notes marker-only phase definitions lack generalizability across cellular models. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Two-stage autoencoder training (DeepCycle) that maps imputed unspliced-spliced reads (scVelo Ms/Mu layers) of cell-cycle genes onto a single circular latent variable theta, transformed as (cos(theta), sin(theta)) in the decoder, to assign each single cell a continuous, high-resolution transcriptional cell-cycle phase. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Two-stage autoencoder training (DeepCycle) that maps imputed unspliced-spliced reads (scVelo Ms/Mu layers) of cell-cycle genes onto a single circular latent variable theta, transformed as (cos(theta), sin(theta)) in the decoder, to assign each single cell a continuous, high-resolution transcriptional cell-cycle phase.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no spliced/unspliced layers and cannot be preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments — DeepCycle requires the RNA velocity moments as input. Few or no genes pass the expression threshold and hotelling filter, indicating no detectable cycling genes — the README states the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed. The goal is a discrete marker-based cell-cycle phase call rather than a continuous circular phase; the paper notes marker-only phase definitions lack generalizability across cellular models.

skills.description: Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribo− paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs and comparing it against cognate linear RNA expression at the same gene loci (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear).
skills.name: circular-linear-rna-expression-comparison
skills.search_text: circular-linear-rna-expression-comparison Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribo− paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs and comparing it against cognate linear RNA expression at the same gene loci (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear). Input RNA-seq is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated, because polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Data are poly(A)+ RNA-seq, where circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3′-end poly(A) tails The analysis only needs circRNA detection without a cognate linear RNA expression background (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 A CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline method that quantifies circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq using the FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) metric computed separately at BSJ and SJ sites, and directly compares the two by dividing FPBcirc by FPBlinear to yield a CIRCscore. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: A CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline method that quantifies circular and linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq using the FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) metric computed separately at BSJ and SJ sites, and directly compares the two by dividing FPBcirc by FPBlinear to yield a CIRCscore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA-seq is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated, because polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Data are poly(A)+ RNA-seq, where circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3′-end poly(A) tails The analysis only needs circRNA detection without a cognate linear RNA expression background (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq (or qPCR) expression matrices should be characterized for a periodic/circular latent process (e.g., cell-cycle staging with Hoechst-validated labels), especially where linear methods (PCA, NMF, ICA) or marker-gene methods (Cyclone, reCAT) underperform.
skills.name: circular-manifold-autoencoder-modeling
skills.search_text: circular-manifold-autoencoder-modeling Use when scRNA-seq (or qPCR) expression matrices should be characterized for a periodic/circular latent process (e.g., cell-cycle staging with Hoechst-validated labels), especially where linear methods (PCA, NMF, ICA) or marker-gene methods (Cyclone, reCAT) underperform. The goal is linear trajectory or standard pseudo-time inference (e.g., developmental progression) where a circular manifold is inappropriate; Monocle or Wanderlust-style methods fit better The analysis only needs marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring on already-annotated gene sets without pseudo-time Data cannot be meaningfully log2(x+1)-transformed, centered and scaled, e.g., non-count expression scales the Cyclum transform assumes http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits a sinusoidal autoencoder (Cyclum) to scRNA-seq expression data to project single cells onto a circular manifold, inferring ab initio pseudo-time for periodic processes such as the cell cycle without requiring marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Fits a sinusoidal autoencoder (Cyclum) to scRNA-seq expression data to project single cells onto a circular manifold, inferring ab initio pseudo-time for periodic processes such as the cell cycle without requiring marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is linear trajectory or standard pseudo-time inference (e.g., developmental progression) where a circular manifold is inappropriate; Monocle or Wanderlust-style methods fit better The analysis only needs marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring on already-annotated gene sets without pseudo-time Data cannot be meaningfully log2(x+1)-transformed, centered and scaled, e.g., non-count expression scales the Cyclum transform assumes

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be assigned circular/periodic pseudo-time (e.g., cell-cycle stages) or when periodic-process-associated genes must be identified without marker genes.
skills.name: circular-manifold-pseudotime-inference
skills.search_text: circular-manifold-pseudotime-inference Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be assigned circular/periodic pseudo-time (e.g., cell-cycle stages) or when periodic-process-associated genes must be identified without marker genes. The biological process of interest is non-periodic (e.g., linear differentiation trajectories better served by Monocle or Wanderlust). Only marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring is required and no pseudo-time or periodic-gene ranking is needed. The expression matrix is a model-ready feature table already deconvolved of cell-cycle effects — applying Cyclum again would remove no additional periodic signal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers latent periodic (e.g., cell-cycle) pseudo-time by projecting scRNA-seq gene expression onto a circular manifold with a sinusoidal autoencoder (Cyclum), instead of relying on marker genes or linear trajectory models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Infers latent periodic (e.g., cell-cycle) pseudo-time by projecting scRNA-seq gene expression onto a circular manifold with a sinusoidal autoencoder (Cyclum), instead of relying on marker genes or linear trajectory models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process of interest is non-periodic (e.g., linear differentiation trajectories better served by Monocle or Wanderlust). Only marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring is required and no pseudo-time or periodic-gene ranking is needed. The expression matrix is a model-ready feature table already deconvolved of cell-cycle effects — applying Cyclum again would remove no additional periodic signal.

skills.description: Use when comparing circular cell-cycle phase assignments from two DeepCycle runs (e.g. ablated inputs or replicate fits) to quantify phase consistency or reproduce the Supplementary Fig. S8 inconsistency.
skills.name: circular-phase-variable-comparison
skills.search_text: circular-phase-variable-comparison Use when comparing circular cell-cycle phase assignments from two DeepCycle runs (e.g. ablated inputs or replicate fits) to quantify phase consistency or reproduce the Supplementary Fig. S8 inconsistency. The quantities to compare are linear (e.g. expression levels) rather than angular — a circular embedding or circular statistic is required only for phase angles Only a single DeepCycle run exists and there is no ablated or replicate run to compare against No cycling genes were found in the dataset — per the README, results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing is needed rather than a phase comparison Compares the circular transcriptional phase variable (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) inferred by DeepCycle across two or more runs — e.g. spliced-only vs unspliced-only input ablations — to test whether phase inference depends on both RNA velocity channels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Compares the circular transcriptional phase variable (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) inferred by DeepCycle across two or more runs — e.g. spliced-only vs unspliced-only input ablations — to test whether phase inference depends on both RNA velocity channels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantities to compare are linear (e.g. expression levels) rather than angular — a circular embedding or circular statistic is required only for phase angles Only a single DeepCycle run exists and there is no ablated or replicate run to compare against No cycling genes were found in the dataset — per the README, results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing is needed rather than a phase comparison

skills.description: Use when computing credible intervals or coverage statistics over 24 h circadian phase estimates whose posterior density straddles phase 0/24 (midnight), e.g. validating Tempo's uncertainty calibration on scRNA-seq time-course data.
skills.name: circular-phase-wraparound-handling
skills.search_text: circular-phase-wraparound-handling Use when computing credible intervals or coverage statistics over 24 h circadian phase estimates whose posterior density straddles phase 0/24 (midnight), e.g. validating Tempo's uncertainty calibration on scRNA-seq time-course data. The quantity being interval-estimated is linear/unbounded (not a 24 h circular phase), where wraparound handling would distort interval widths. Only point estimates of circadian phase are needed — the article notes existing methods that do not quantify estimation uncertainty, but this skill specifically requires posterior phase samples. Data were not analyzed with Tempo or lack approximate posterior samples, so HDR credible intervals cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3304 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Treats circadian phase as a circular 24 h quantity when constructing Highest-Density-Region (HDR) credible intervals from Tempo's approximate posterior phase samples, so intervals that cross midnight wrap correctly and calibration coverage is computed without artificially splitting nighttime intervals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Treats circadian phase as a circular 24 h quantity when constructing Highest-Density-Region (HDR) credible intervals from Tempo's approximate posterior phase samples, so intervals that cross midnight wrap correctly and calibration coverage is computed without artificially splitting nighttime intervals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantity being interval-estimated is linear/unbounded (not a 24 h circular phase), where wraparound handling would distort interval widths. Only point estimates of circadian phase are needed — the article notes existing methods that do not quantify estimation uncertainty, but this skill specifically requires posterior phase samples. Data were not analyzed with Tempo or lack approximate posterior samples, so HDR credible intervals cannot be constructed.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells plausibly follow a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) and you need to identify the associated genes ab initio from expression kinetics rather than marker genes, then benchmark the ranking against PCA-based alternatives.
skills.name: circular-pseudotime-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: circular-pseudotime-gene-ranking Use when scRNA-seq cells plausibly follow a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) and you need to identify the associated genes ab initio from expression kinetics rather than marker genes, then benchmark the ranking against PCA-based alternatives. The process of interest is non-periodic/linear (e.g., developmental trajectory) — linear pseudo-time methods like Monocle, not a circular manifold, are appropriate. You already trust marker-gene or label-based cell-cycle scoring (e.g., scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle, Seurat::CellCycleScoring) and only need to refine labels along pseudo-time via cyclum.postproc.refine_labels rather than re-rank genes. Input data cannot support a circular manifold assumption (e.g., asynchronous non-cycling cells), where ab-initio periodicity inference is meaningless. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank genes ab initio by the degree of match between each gene's expression kinetics and a Cyclum-inferred circular pseudo-time, and validate that ranking against PC1/PC2-based rankings using GSEA normalized enrichment scores (NES) against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Rank genes ab initio by the degree of match between each gene's expression kinetics and a Cyclum-inferred circular pseudo-time, and validate that ranking against PC1/PC2-based rankings using GSEA normalized enrichment scores (NES) against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The process of interest is non-periodic/linear (e.g., developmental trajectory) — linear pseudo-time methods like Monocle, not a circular manifold, are appropriate. You already trust marker-gene or label-based cell-cycle scoring (e.g., scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle, Seurat::CellCycleScoring) and only need to refine labels along pseudo-time via cyclum.postproc.refine_labels rather than re-rank genes. Input data cannot support a circular manifold assumption (e.g., asynchronous non-cycling cells), where ab-initio periodicity inference is meaningless.

skills.description: Use when a Cyclum sinusoidal autoencoder has been trained on log2(x+1)-transformed, variance-1-scaled scRNA-seq data and the circular latent stage of each cell must be converted into a wrapped [0, 2π] pseudo-time.
skills.name: circular-pseudotime-wrapping
skills.search_text: circular-pseudotime-wrapping Use when a Cyclum sinusoidal autoencoder has been trained on log2(x+1)-transformed, variance-1-scaled scRNA-seq data and the circular latent stage of each cell must be converted into a wrapped [0, 2π] pseudo-time. The process of interest is non-periodic (a linear or branching trajectory) — use linear pseudo-time methods such as Monocle or Wanderlust, which Cyclum's paper notes are 'not optimal for representing such nonlinear periodicity' The goal is only to remove cell-cycle covariates from an expression matrix without recovering per-cell stages — Cyclum's deconvolution path may be the wrong interface Only marker-gene-based phase scoring (e.g., Cyclone-style PCA/gene-pair scoring) is needed; Cyclum's methodology 'is to rely on the circular manifold, instead of the marker genes' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts the circular latent coordinate inferred by the Cyclum sinusoidal autoencoder and wraps the per-cell pseudo-time into the canonical [0, 2π] interval via the modulus operation, so that stages of a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) are represented on a single continuous circle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Extracts the circular latent coordinate inferred by the Cyclum sinusoidal autoencoder and wraps the per-cell pseudo-time into the canonical [0, 2π] interval via the modulus operation, so that stages of a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) are represented on a single continuous circle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The process of interest is non-periodic (a linear or branching trajectory) — use linear pseudo-time methods such as Monocle or Wanderlust, which Cyclum's paper notes are 'not optimal for representing such nonlinear periodicity' The goal is only to remove cell-cycle covariates from an expression matrix without recovering per-cell stages — Cyclum's deconvolution path may be the wrong interface Only marker-gene-based phase scoring (e.g., Cyclone-style PCA/gene-pair scoring) is needed; Cyclum's methodology 'is to rely on the circular manifold, instead of the marker genes'

skills.description: Use when ribo− depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 circRNA output plus a HISAT2 BAM) needs circRNA quantification per BSJ with readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore per locus.
skills.name: circular-rna-back-splice-junction-quantification
skills.search_text: circular-rna-back-splice-junction-quantification Use when ribo− depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 circRNA output plus a HISAT2 BAM) needs circRNA quantification per BSJ with readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore per locus. Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq, where polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted and accurate linear RNA quantification (and thus CIRCscore) is unsuitable Input is already a CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR quant.txt with FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore fields populated — re-quantification is redundant Only poly(A)+ RNA-seq is available, since circRNAs are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets and BSJ fragments will be underrepresented http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify circular RNA expression from ribo− RNA-seq by counting fragments mapped to back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites with the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline, and express circRNA and cognate linear RNA expression in a common FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) scale so CIRCscore (FPBcirc/FPBlinear) can be computed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Quantify circular RNA expression from ribo− RNA-seq by counting fragments mapped to back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites with the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR pipeline, and express circRNA and cognate linear RNA expression in a common FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) scale so CIRCscore (FPBcirc/FPBlinear) can be computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq, where polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted and accurate linear RNA quantification (and thus CIRCscore) is unsuitable Input is already a CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR quant.txt with FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore fields populated — re-quantification is redundant Only poly(A)+ RNA-seq is available, since circRNAs are depleted in poly(A)+ datasets and BSJ fragments will be underrepresented

skills.description: Use when RNA-Seq BAM reads may contain gene fusions and you need to call the primary fusion junction plus secondary splice-variant/backsplice junctions and fcircRNAs, e.g. sim56-like or TMPRSS2::ERG-style data.
skills.name: circular-rna-backsplice-detection
skills.search_text: circular-rna-backsplice-detection Use when RNA-Seq BAM reads may contain gene fusions and you need to call the primary fusion junction plus secondary splice-variant/backsplice junctions and fcircRNAs, e.g. sim56-like or TMPRSS2::ERG-style data. The question is general (non-fusion-derived) circRNA detection from RNA-Seq alone — INTEGRATE-Circ is a fusion junction detection tool whose fcircRNA calls are tied to identified gene fusion junctions. You lack a reference genome FASTA plus Ensembl annotation, which are the two required input files; the BWT-based workflow cannot run. You only need to quantify expression rather than identify fusion junctions and their isoforms — this skill performs junction/isoform calling, not quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects gene fusion transcripts and their isoforms, including fusion-derived circular RNAs (fcircRNAs), from RNA-Seq data by clustering spanning reads at fusion junctions and classifying secondary clusters relative to the highest-read-support primary junction as alternative-splicing/backsplice junctions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad569
skills.summary: Detects gene fusion transcripts and their isoforms, including fusion-derived circular RNAs (fcircRNAs), from RNA-Seq data by clustering spanning reads at fusion junctions and classifying secondary clusters relative to the highest-read-support primary junction as alternative-splicing/backsplice junctions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is general (non-fusion-derived) circRNA detection from RNA-Seq alone — INTEGRATE-Circ is a fusion junction detection tool whose fcircRNA calls are tied to identified gene fusion junctions. You lack a reference genome FASTA plus Ensembl annotation, which are the two required input files; the BWT-based workflow cannot run. You only need to quantify expression rather than identify fusion junctions and their isoforms — this skill performs junction/isoform calling, not quantification.

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more groups of predicted circadian times (angles on a 0-24 h clock) to formally test whether the angular distributions differ in homogeneity or dispersion, e.g., bootstrapped tauFisher predictions per cell type at each ZT time point.
skills.name: circular-statistics-angular-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: circular-statistics-angular-hypothesis-testing Use when comparing two or more groups of predicted circadian times (angles on a 0-24 h clock) to formally test whether the angular distributions differ in homogeneity or dispersion, e.g., bootstrapped tauFisher predictions per cell type at each ZT time point. The quantities to compare are linear (non-angular) measurements where circular wraparound does not apply — use ordinary dispersion tests instead Predictions are at the single-cell level; tauFisher cannot run on single cells due to high scRNAseq dropout, so pseudobulk replicates must be built first There is only one phase prediction per group per ZT (no bootstrap replicates), leaving insufficient samples for a distributional comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies circular statistical hypothesis tests (Rao's Tests for Homogeneity and the Wallraff Test of Angular Distances) to distributions of bootstrapped circadian-phase predictions (wrapped to the 0-24 h clock) to determine whether predicted phases are significantly more dispersed in one cell type than another. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: Applies circular statistical hypothesis tests (Rao's Tests for Homogeneity and the Wallraff Test of Angular Distances) to distributions of bootstrapped circadian-phase predictions (wrapped to the 0-24 h clock) to determine whether predicted phases are significantly more dispersed in one cell type than another.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantities to compare are linear (non-angular) measurements where circular wraparound does not apply — use ordinary dispersion tests instead Predictions are at the single-cell level; tauFisher cannot run on single cells due to high scRNAseq dropout, so pseudobulk replicates must be built first There is only one phase prediction per group per ZT (no bootstrap replicates), leaving insufficient samples for a distributional comparison

skills.description: Use when recursive neural ODE forecasts (e.g., RNAForecaster 72-step predictions) must be validated for biologically ordered progression along a circular trajectory such as cell-cycle position from tricycle.
skills.name: circular-statistics-ordering-assessment
skills.search_text: circular-statistics-ordering-assessment Use when recursive neural ODE forecasts (e.g., RNAForecaster 72-step predictions) must be validated for biologically ordered progression along a circular trajectory such as cell-cycle position from tricycle. Predictions concern a non-cyclic biological process with no circular embedding available (tricycle scores only make sense for cell-cycle progression) Input is raw counts with no forecast trajectory — there are no sequential hourly states to test for ordering Only a single predicted time point exists, so no per-hour comparison against randomized controls is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores forecast or single-cell expression states on a circular 0–2π coordinate (e.g., tricycle cell-cycle position) and tests whether the temporal ordering of predictions exceeds chance by comparing an ordering metric against randomized controls at each forecast hour. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Scores forecast or single-cell expression states on a circular 0–2π coordinate (e.g., tricycle cell-cycle position) and tests whether the temporal ordering of predictions exceeds chance by comparing an ordering metric against randomized controls at each forecast hour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions concern a non-cyclic biological process with no circular embedding available (tricycle scores only make sense for cell-cycle progression) Input is raw counts with no forecast trajectory — there are no sequential hourly states to test for ordering Only a single predicted time point exists, so no per-hour comparison against randomized controls is possible

skills.description: Use when quantifying run-to-run stability of circular quantities (e.g., circadian phase in hours on a 24 h cycle) by computing per-cell circular standard deviation across five or more replicate runs of a phase-inference method on scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: circular-statistics-standard-deviation-computation
skills.search_text: circular-statistics-standard-deviation-computation Use when quantifying run-to-run stability of circular quantities (e.g., circadian phase in hours on a 24 h cycle) by computing per-cell circular standard deviation across five or more replicate runs of a phase-inference method on scRNA-seq data. The quantity being summarized is linear (not circular/wrapping) — ordinary standard deviation is appropriate and circular SD would distort it Only a single run per method is available — run-to-run circular SD across replicates cannot be computed The goal is phase accuracy against ground truth rather than run-to-run stability of the phase point estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute per-cell circular standard deviations of circadian phase estimates (expressed in hours over the 24 h circadian cycle) across replicate runs of phase-inference methods (Tempo, Cyclops, Cyclum) to quantify run-to-run stability, as in the Tempo paper's Fig. 2f/5d stability analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Compute per-cell circular standard deviations of circadian phase estimates (expressed in hours over the 24 h circadian cycle) across replicate runs of phase-inference methods (Tempo, Cyclops, Cyclum) to quantify run-to-run stability, as in the Tempo paper's Fig. 2f/5d stability analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantity being summarized is linear (not circular/wrapping) — ordinary standard deviation is appropriate and circular SD would distort it Only a single run per method is available — run-to-run circular SD across replicates cannot be computed The goal is phase accuracy against ground truth rather than run-to-run stability of the phase point estimates

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object already carries a continuous circular cell cycle phase (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) and discrete phase assignments plus per-phase fractions are needed for validation against flow cytometry.
skills.name: circular-theta-variable-binning
skills.search_text: circular-theta-variable-binning Use when an AnnData object already carries a continuous circular cell cycle phase (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) and discrete phase assignments plus per-phase fractions are needed for validation against flow cytometry. The input AnnData lacks obs['cell_cycle_theta'] and the scVelo Ms/Mu layers, i.e. DeepCycle has not been run — rerun DeepCycle first with a gene list and base gene (Nusap1 for mESC, MELK for fibroblasts). No cycling genes are detected in the dataset; the README warns the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing is likely needed. Converts DeepCycle's circular transcriptional phase (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) into discrete G1, S, and G2/M cell cycle phase labels by estimating three transition thetas (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) from marker scores and UMI depth, then binning the circular variable to compute per-phase cell fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Converts DeepCycle's circular transcriptional phase (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) into discrete G1, S, and G2/M cell cycle phase labels by estimating three transition thetas (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) from marker scores and UMI depth, then binning the circular variable to compute per-phase cell fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input AnnData lacks obs['cell_cycle_theta'] and the scVelo Ms/Mu layers, i.e. DeepCycle has not been run — rerun DeepCycle first with a gene list and base gene (Nusap1 for mESC, MELK for fibroblasts). No cycling genes are detected in the dataset; the README warns the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing is likely needed. skills.name: circular-trajectory-evaluation
skills.search_text: circular-trajectory-evaluation Use when you have inferred a circular latent time (e.g. adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) from cycling genes in scRNA-seq data and need to verify the fits, phase-transition angles, and agreement with discrete/continuous baseline methods. No cycling genes can be detected in the dataset — the README states results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing (more RNAs per cell) may be needed The input Anndata lacks Mu/Ms moments from scvelo.pp.moments or unspliced/spliced layers, since the circular inference and its evaluation are based on unspliced-spliced reads The cell-cycle signature is being defined from gene markers alone rather than dynamical features — the article notes marker-based phase definition lacks generalizability across cellular models http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A skill for validating circular (1D angular) cell-cycle latent trajectories inferred from scRNA-seq: checking that single-gene unspliced-spliced fits are plausible, that the inferred theta recovers known phase transitions (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1), and comparing against baselines such as scVelo's dynamical model, Cyclum, Cyclone and Revelio. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8

skills.description: Use when cells carry a circular phase annotation (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) from DeepCycle and you must bin, average, or fit quantities (e.g. total UMI counts) across the full cell cycle without breaking the 0/2π wrap-around.

skills.search_text: circular-variable-handling Use when cells carry a circular phase annotation (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) from DeepCycle and you must bin, average, or fit quantities (e.g. total UMI counts) across the full cell cycle without breaking the 0/2π wrap-around. skills.summary: Correctly treat DeepCycle's transcriptional phase (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) as a circular variable on the 0–2π ring rather than a linear quantity, using atan2 initialization, cos/sin encoding, and circular binning across the full cell cycle.

The analysis aims to include trans-eQTL effects — OTTERS only considers cis-eQTL effects and cannot incorporate trans signals Individual-level reference expression and genetic data are available — tools like PrediXcan or FUSION operate directly on individual-level data without this summary-based filtering step The eQTL summary statistics are already clumped/restricted to the target genes' cis-windows and formatted for the PRS tools http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Filter and LD-clump cis-eQTL summary statistics with PLINK 1.9 against an LD reference panel so that SNPs are restricted to each gene's cis-window and formatted as valid inputs for the OTTERS PRS training methods (P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS) before Stage I eQTL weight estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w

skills.name: cis-nat-identification-from-genome-annotation
skills.search_text: cis-nat-identification-from-genome-annotation Use when the task is to comprehensively extract cis-NAT pairs from genome annotation (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns, e.g. from Ensembl) with optional RNA-seq expression profiling (TPM, FPKM, fold_change, padj), and to classify them into EB/FO/HH/TT structural types. Input is raw sequencing data rather than processed gene-level annotation — CCIVR relies on third-party tools (STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression, DESeq2 for statistics) upstream; run those first. The task requires strand-specific RNA-seq error-rate-aware cis-NAT detection from transcriptome assemblies — tools like NASTI-seq (R) or NATpipe (Perl) cover de novo assembled transcriptomes instead. Downstream gene annotation (structure and strand direction) in the database is unknown or unreliable, since CCIVR predictions depend on annotation accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Identify all cis-natural antisense transcript (cis-NAT) pairs — embedded (EB), fully-overlapped (FO), head-to-head (HH), and tail-to-tail (TT) — from a gene annotation CSV, optionally with RNA-seq expression columns, using the CCIVR Python program. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Identify all cis-natural antisense transcript (cis-NAT) pairs — embedded (EB), fully-overlapped (FO), head-to-head (HH), and tail-to-tail (TT) — from a gene annotation CSV, optionally with RNA-seq expression columns, using the CCIVR Python program.

skills.description: Use when a CCIVR run has produced Table.csv with cis-NAT pairs carrying fold_change and padj expression columns, and you need expression-combination counts (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per EB/FO/HH/TT type or a down-up pair set.
skills.name: cis-nat-pair-count-tabulation
skills.search_text: cis-nat-pair-count-tabulation Use when a CCIVR run has produced Table.csv with cis-NAT pairs carrying fold_change and padj expression columns, and you need expression-combination counts (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per EB/FO/HH/TT type or a down-up pair set. The input CSV carries only the five gene annotation columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) with no expression profiling columns (fold_change/padj) — CCIVR will extract structural cis-NATs but no down/up combination classification is possible. You need de novo NAT discovery from unassembled transcriptomes (e.g. NATpipe-style) rather than tabulating pairs already extracted by CCIVR from genome annotation. The cis-NAT pair list was produced by a different tool (e.g. BEDTools annotation-based overlap only) and lacks the CCIVR Table.csv schema with structural types and expression columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Post-processing skill for CCIVR output: parse the ccivr_output/Table.csv of extracted sense-antisense (cis-NAT) pairs, classify each pair by its expression combination (down or up on each strand) using the fold_change and padj columns, and tabulate pair counts per structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT) to surface inversely correlated down-up pairs as in Figure 4B/4D of Ohhata et al. 2022. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Post-processing skill for CCIVR output: parse the ccivr_output/Table.csv of extracted sense-antisense (cis-NAT) pairs, classify each pair by its expression combination (down or up on each strand) using the fold_change and padj columns, and tabulate pair counts per structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT) to surface inversely correlated down-up pairs as in Figure 4B/4D of Ohhata et al. 2022.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input CSV carries only the five gene annotation columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) with no expression profiling columns (fold_change/padj) — CCIVR will extract structural cis-NATs but no down/up combination classification is possible.
