skills.description: Use when you have CCIVR output from an RNA-seq dataset (e.g. Huh-7 cells with TGFβ stimulation) and need to partition differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes by direction (fold_change/padj) into gene lists for enrichment analysis.
skills.name: cis-nat-pair-partner-gene-selection
skills.search_text: cis-nat-pair-partner-gene-selection Use when you have CCIVR output from an RNA-seq dataset (e.g. Huh-7 cells with TGFβ stimulation) and need to partition differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes by direction (fold_change/padj) into gene lists for enrichment analysis. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) — CCIVR relies on processed RNA-seq output from third-party programs (STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression profiling, DESeq2 for statistics), so map and quantify first. You need the total cis-NAT structural catalog (EB/FO/HH/TT counts) without any expression-differential filtering — plain CCIVR Summary.csv analysis suffices and no direction-resolved gene selection applies. No strand-aware or genome-annotated cis-NAT pairs are present in the dataset (CCIVR output contains no differentially expressed pairs), so no partner-gene lists can be formed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the partner genes of differentially expressed cis-NAT pairs from a CCIVR run on Huh-7 TGFβ-stimulated RNA-seq data and prepares up-regulated/down-regulated gene lists for GO (GOTERM_BP_FAT) enrichment in DAVID v6.8. This links CCIVR's Table.csv cis-NAT inventory to functional interpretation of cis-NAT regulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Selects the partner genes of differentially expressed cis-NAT pairs from a CCIVR run on Huh-7 TGFβ-stimulated RNA-seq data and prepares up-regulated/down-regulated gene lists for GO (GOTERM_BP_FAT) enrichment in DAVID v6.8. This links CCIVR's Table.csv cis-NAT inventory to functional interpretation of cis-NAT regulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) — CCIVR relies on processed RNA-seq output from third-party programs (STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression profiling, DESeq2 for statistics), so map and quantify first. You need the total cis-NAT structural catalog (EB/FO/HH/TT counts) without any expression-differential filtering — plain CCIVR Summary.csv analysis suffices and no direction-resolved gene selection applies. No strand-aware or genome-annotated cis-NAT pairs are present in the dataset (CCIVR output contains no differentially expressed pairs), so no partner-gene lists can be formed.

skills.description: Use when genome annotations (e.g. Ensembl GTF releases 105/104 or Ensembl plants/fungi release 52) must be converted and screened with CCIVR to tabulate cis-NAT type counts and percentages per organism.
skills.name: cis-nat-type-frequency-quantification
skills.search_text: cis-nat-type-frequency-quantification Use when genome annotations (e.g. Ensembl GTF releases 105/104 or Ensembl plants/fungi release 52) must be converted and screened with CCIVR to tabulate cis-NAT type counts and percentages per organism. The goal is expression profiling or differential expression of cis-NAT pairs (e.g. TGFβ-stimulated Huh-7 analysis or imprinted KCNQ1/KCNQ1OT1 detection) rather than structural type frequency quantification across species — that requires RNA-seq columns and the CCIVR expression workflow instead Only raw RNA-seq reads are available and the genome annotation has not been converted into CCIVR's CSV format (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End); CCIVR depends on accurate deposited gene annotations and does not perform mapping (third-party programs such as STAR are used for mapping) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify, per species, the absolute number and percentage of genes containing each cis-NAT structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT, and any) using the CCIVR tool on Ensembl-derived gene annotations, to compare cis-NAT prevalence across organisms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Quantify, per species, the absolute number and percentage of genes containing each cis-NAT structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT, and any) using the CCIVR tool on Ensembl-derived gene annotations, to compare cis-NAT prevalence across organisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is expression profiling or differential expression of cis-NAT pairs (e.g. TGFβ-stimulated Huh-7 analysis or imprinted KCNQ1/KCNQ1OT1 detection) rather than structural type frequency quantification across species — that requires RNA-seq columns and the CCIVR expression workflow instead Only raw RNA-seq reads are available and the genome annotation has not been converted into CCIVR's CSV format (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End); CCIVR depends on accurate deposited gene annotations and does not perform mapping (third-party programs such as STAR are used for mapping)

skills.description: Use when preprocessing paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq for cnmf joint clustering and you need a peak-gene coupling matrix that weights open chromatin peaks by distance to genes (d0 = 40 kb decay).
skills.name: cis-regulatory-distance-decay-modeling
skills.search_text: cis-regulatory-distance-decay-modeling Use when preprocessing paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq for cnmf joint clustering and you need a peak-gene coupling matrix that weights open chromatin peaks by distance to genes (d0 = 40 kb decay). You already have consistent cluster assignments for the scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples obtained elsewhere — the cnmf/coupling-matrix route is explicitly optional. The comparison condition has single-donor data processed directly through sc_compreg with clusters supplied by another method that already links subpopulations. The scATAC-seq peak coordinates do not map to one of the supported genome versions (hg19, hg38, mm9, mm10), since cnmf_process_data.sh cannot build the coupling prior. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Links scATAC-seq peaks to putatively regulated co-located genes via a coupling term A_ij = R_ij+ * exp(-d_ij/d0) with distance-decay scale d0 = 40 kb, which feeds the peak-gene coupling matrix D used by the CoupledNMF (cnmf) joint clustering step of sc-compReg. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Links scATAC-seq peaks to putatively regulated co-located genes via a coupling term A_ij = R_ij+ * exp(-d_ij/d0) with distance-decay scale d0 = 40 kb, which feeds the peak-gene coupling matrix D used by the CoupledNMF (cnmf) joint clustering step of sc-compReg.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have consistent cluster assignments for the scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples obtained elsewhere — the cnmf/coupling-matrix route is explicitly optional. The comparison condition has single-donor data processed directly through sc_compreg with clusters supplied by another method that already links subpopulations. The scATAC-seq peak coordinates do not map to one of the supported genome versions (hg19, hg38, mm9, mm10), since cnmf_process_data.sh cannot build the coupling prior.

skills.description: Use when converting co-expression modules into directed gene regulatory networks: after GRNBoost2 proposes candidate TF–TG edges from single-cell expression data, to retain only edges with cis-regulatory motif evidence.
skills.name: cis-regulatory-motif-enrichment-filtering
skills.search_text: cis-regulatory-motif-enrichment-filtering Use when converting co-expression modules into directed gene regulatory networks: after GRNBoost2 proposes candidate TF–TG edges from single-cell expression data, to retain only edges with cis-regulatory motif evidence. The goal is co-expression module detection or hub-gene identification only, with no need for directed TF–TG relationships The candidate edges are not TF–TG pairs (e.g. gene–drug interaction queries, which instead use correlation thresholds such as >= 0.8 in SCANet) Input is already a motif-validated directed GRN; re-running the filter would only remove edges without adding information http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A filter step in SCANet's GCN-to-GRN conversion: RcisTarget validates each candidate TF–target-gene edge proposed by GRNBoost2 by checking whether the TF's regulatory binding motif is significantly enriched at the target's cis-regulatory region, discarding unsupported edges to yield a directed GRN. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: A filter step in SCANet's GCN-to-GRN conversion: RcisTarget validates each candidate TF–target-gene edge proposed by GRNBoost2 by checking whether the TF's regulatory binding motif is significantly enriched at the target's cis-regulatory region, discarding unsupported edges to yield a directed GRN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is co-expression module detection or hub-gene identification only, with no need for directed TF–TG relationships The candidate edges are not TF–TG pairs (e.g. gene–drug interaction queries, which instead use correlation thresholds such as >= 0.8 in SCANet) Input is already a motif-validated directed GRN; re-running the filter would only remove edges without adding information

skills.description: Use when you have a set of ATAC-seq/DNase peak sequences and need TF motif hits to construct a candidate TF–target regulatory mask as a prior for GRN inference.
skills.name: cisbp-motif-database-query
skills.search_text: cisbp-motif-database-query Use when you have a set of ATAC-seq/DNase peak sequences and need TF motif hits to construct a candidate TF–target regulatory mask as a prior for GRN inference. You already possess a TF–target prior mask or ChIP-seq–derived regulatory edges, so motif scanning is redundant. Your peaks lack assignable target genes (e.g., distal peaks with no TSS within the 500 bp upstream / 3000 bp downstream annotation window), since filtering will discard them. You need expression dynamics rather than a static candidate regulator set — that is scKINETICS's EM estimation, not motif querying. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Retrieves CisBP transcription factor position weight matrices and scans them against open chromatin peak sequences (e.g., bulk ATAC-seq peaks from Alonso-Curbelo et al. 2021) with MOODS at a P < 1e-10 significance threshold, to identify candidate TF motif binding sites for building a prior GRN mask. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Retrieves CisBP transcription factor position weight matrices and scans them against open chromatin peak sequences (e.g., bulk ATAC-seq peaks from Alonso-Curbelo et al. 2021) with MOODS at a P < 1e-10 significance threshold, to identify candidate TF motif binding sites for building a prior GRN mask.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already possess a TF–target prior mask or ChIP-seq–derived regulatory edges, so motif scanning is redundant. Your peaks lack assignable target genes (e.g., distal peaks with no TSS within the 500 bp upstream / 3000 bp downstream annotation window), since filtering will discard them. You need expression dynamics rather than a static candidate regulator set — that is scKINETICS's EM estimation, not motif querying.

skills.description: Use when raw ADT/CITE-seq FASTQ files (I1/R1/R2) from hashed samples need to be converted into antibody-by-cell UMI count matrices, optionally after removing index-hopped reads from combined NovaSeq GEX+ADT data.

Data are gene-expression-only with no ADT/CITE-seq library — only the GEX branch of the pipeline is needed Count matrices already exist (pipeline start configured after the resource-intensive cellranger count and CITE-Seq steps — only dummy FASTQ files are then required) GEX and ADT were sequenced separately, not combined on one NovaSeq run — the index-hopping removal step does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Processing of CITE-seq (antibody-derived tag, ADT) libraries in the gExcite Snakemake workflow: per-sample ADT FASTQs are mapped with Cell Ranger count against a feature-barcode reference to yield antibody-by-cell UMI count matrices, with optional index-hopping cleanup (DropletUtils) when GEX and ADT were sequenced together on a NovaSeq run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329

skills.description: Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single-cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) must be normalized and denoised before clustering, or when comparing dsb against CLR normalization for protein-based analyses.
skills.name: cite-seq-adt-normalization
skills.search_text: cite-seq-adt-normalization Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single-cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) must be normalized and denoised before clustering, or when comparing dsb against CLR normalization for protein-based analyses. The dataset has no empty droplets and no isotype controls and the caveats for such cases (deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note/vignettes) have not been considered — use the dedicated no-empty-drops vignette workflow instead of defaulting to the standard recipe The goal is mRNA/counts normalization (e.g., scRNA-seq log-normalization) rather than ADT/protein counts from droplet-based assays Proteins have near-zero signal — those with maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells should be removed prior to normalization rather than normalized http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Normalize and denoise antibody-derived tag (ADT) counts from CITE-seq and related assays with dsb, which removes ambient unbound-antibody noise estimated from empty droplets and cell-to-cell technical noise captured by isotype controls and background protein means, outperforming CLR in downstream WNN clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8

skills.description: Use when preparing paired transcriptome–surface protein (CITE-seq or REAP-seq) data as training targets for cTP-net or comparable protein-imputation models: raw ADT barcode counts must be converted to per-cell relative abundances before model training.
skills.name: cite-seq-adt-relative-abundance-transformation
skills.search_text: cite-seq-adt-relative-abundance-transformation Use when preparing paired transcriptome–surface protein (CITE-seq or REAP-seq) data as training targets for cTP-net or comparable protein-imputation models: raw ADT barcode counts must be converted to per-cell relative abundances before model training. Input scRNA-seq expression is not UMI-based count data (e.g., TPM/RPKM) — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input, so the paired transformation pipeline is not valid The ADT matrix has already been relative-abundance/log-ratio transformed (double transformation would distort the response vectors) No paired protein measurements or trained cTP-net model exist, and the goal is de novo protein abundance estimation rather than transformation of measured ADT counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies the Stoeckius et al. relative abundance transformation (geometric mean log-ratio per cell) to CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein ADT counts, producing the training response vectors for cTP-net. The article reports this transformed relative abundance gives better prediction accuracy than training on raw protein barcode counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Applies the Stoeckius et al. relative abundance transformation (geometric mean log-ratio per cell) to CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein ADT counts, producing the training response vectors for cTP-net. The article reports this transformed relative abundance gives better prediction accuracy than training on raw protein barcode counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input scRNA-seq expression is not UMI-based count data (e.g., TPM/RPKM) — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input, so the paired transformation pipeline is not valid The ADT matrix has already been relative-abundance/log-ratio transformed (double transformation would distort the response vectors) No paired protein measurements or trained cTP-net model exist, and the goal is de novo protein abundance estimation rather than transformation of measured ADT counts

skills.description: Use when clustering cells measured across multiple modalities (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT, or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA+ATAC) and you need integrated unsupervised embeddings comparable to totalVI/MultiVI/MOFA+ methods.
skills.name: cite-seq-atac-seq-multimodal-integration
skills.search_text: cite-seq-atac-seq-multimodal-integration Use when clustering cells measured across multiple modalities (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT, or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA+ATAC) and you need integrated unsupervised embeddings comparable to totalVI/MultiVI/MOFA+ methods. skills.search_text: cite-seq-count-matrix-processing Use when raw ADT/protein UMI count matrices from a CITE-seq experiment are available (e.g., raw and filtered Cell Ranger outputs) and you need to characterize ambient antibody background before normalization, or verify that empty-droplet background reflects protein levels in cells. Input is already normalized/denoised (e.g., dsb DSBNormalizeProtein output) rather than raw UMI counts — the correlation analysis requires raw counts The dataset contains no empty droplets (e.g., sorted-cell experiments) — use the dsb 'no empty drops' mode with ModelNegativeADTnorm instead The goal is full normalization and denoising rather than ambient background characterization — call DSBNormalizeProtein() directly instead of running this diagnostic workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Process raw CITE-seq ADT count matrices by loading cell-containing and empty-droplet UMI matrices, computing per-protein mean log10(count+1) levels, and quantifying the ambient antibody background shared between empty droplets and cells. This characterizes protein-specific noise from unbound antibodies encapsulated during droplet generation, the motivation for dsb normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Process raw CITE-seq ADT count matrices by loading cell-containing and empty-droplet UMI matrices, computing per-protein mean log10(count+1) levels, and quantifying the ambient antibody background shared between empty droplets and cells. skills.search_text: cite-seq-multimodal-embedding-generation Use when CITE-seq or other multimodal single-cell data (same cells measured across modalities, e.g. RNA + ADT matrices) needs integrated embeddings to cluster cells into major and minor cell types. You want a supervised classifier of known cell types rather than an unsupervised clustering framework — SnapCCESS is unsupervised and labels are used only for ARI evaluation. You need recommended hyperparameters out of the box — the README states the tutorial 'doesn't recommend the best parameters for your datasets'; you must consult the paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Generate integrated embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA and ADT) using SnapCCESS, an unsupervised ensemble deep learning framework that creates snapshots of multimodality variational autoencoder embeddings for downstream consensus clustering of cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Generate integrated embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA and ADT) using SnapCCESS, an unsupervised ensemble deep learning framework that creates snapshots of multimodality variational autoencoder embeddings for downstream consensus clustering of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are single-modality (e.g. scRNA-seq only) with no second modality measured across the same cells — SnapCCESS integrates data modalities and is designed for multimodal input. skills.search_text: cite-seq-protein-based-cell-type-annotation Use when a CITE-seq dataset contains cell-surface protein abundance (e.g., PBMC antibody-derived tags) and trusted cell-type labels are needed as reference ground truth for benchmarking clustering or label-validation methods. No CITE-seq/ADT protein measurements are available — constraints must then come from other domain knowledge (e.g., marker genes), not protein distances The downstream method only supports hard-constrained clustering (e.g., COP K-means style); these soft percentile-based constraints are designed for scDCC's loss-augmentation approach Only a small fraction of cells has protein data, so pairwise protein distances are too sparse to yield confident 0.5th/95th percentile pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Converts CITE-seq antibody-derived tag (ADT) protein measurements into soft pairwise constraints (must-link and cannot-link pairs) for scDCC, so that protein-level domain knowledge guides clustering of the matched scRNA-seq data. Rationale: purely unsupervised clustering may yield biologically uninterpretable clusters, and pairwise protein distances at confident extremes encode reliable cell-cell similarity/dissimilarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3

The task is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to binary cancer vs non-cancer calls, so subpopulation-level metrics are out of scope Evaluating on the five training datasets (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC) as unbiased performance — the paper warns training-set performance may be overestimated because those sets were involved in feature selection Input is already a metrics table or the ground-truth annotations for the test cells are unavailable — metrics cannot be computed without reference labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluate a binary cell classifier (PreCanCell) by computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity), and AUROC per dataset, using the original publication's cell annotations as ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Evaluate a binary cell classifier (PreCanCell) by computing accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity), and AUROC per dataset, using the original publication's cell annotations as ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to binary cancer vs non-cancer calls, so subpopulation-level metrics are out of scope Evaluating on the five training datasets (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC) as unbiased performance — the paper warns training-set performance may be overestimated because those sets were involved in feature selection Input is already a metrics table or the ground-truth annotations for the test cells are unavailable — metrics cannot be computed without reference labels

skills.description: Use when you have gold-standard labeled scRNA-seq data (e.g. test_cancerCellLine.h5ad, test_TabulaSapiens.h5ad) and need to quantify a classifier's sensitivity on malignant cells and specificity on normal epithelial cells against published benchmarks.
skills.name: classifier-probability-threshold-evaluation
skills.search_text: classifier-probability-threshold-evaluation Use when you have gold-standard labeled scRNA-seq data (e.g. test_cancerCellLine.h5ad, test_TabulaSapiens.h5ad) and need to quantify a classifier's sensitivity on malignant cells and specificity on normal epithelial cells against published benchmarks. The input is patient tumor data without prerequisite basic cell-type annotation — scMalignantFinder is designed to identify malignant cells only from cancerous lineages, relying on prior identification of basic cell types The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — capabilities are explicitly flagged as requiring further testing The goal is malignant-region calling in spatial transcriptomics rather than per-cell scRNA-seq classification — that requires the multi-feature spatial workflow (image_cal, spatial_nn, region_identification), not this benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a probabilistic binary cell classifier (e.g. scMalignantFinder's malignancy_probability) against gold-standard scRNA-seq labels by computing sensitivity/specificity and comparing to reported baselines (PreCanCell, ikarus, Cancer-Finder, CopyKAT). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Benchmark a probabilistic binary cell classifier (e.g. scMalignantFinder's malignancy_probability) against gold-standard scRNA-seq labels by computing sensitivity/specificity and comparing to reported baselines (PreCanCell, ikarus, Cancer-Finder, CopyKAT).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is patient tumor data without prerequisite basic cell-type annotation — scMalignantFinder is designed to identify malignant cells only from cancerous lineages, relying on prior identification of basic cell types The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — capabilities are explicitly flagged as requiring further testing The goal is malignant-region calling in spatial transcriptomics rather than per-cell scRNA-seq classification — that requires the multi-feature spatial workflow (image_cal, spatial_nn, region_identification), not this benchmark

skills.description: Use when running an active learning loop for single-cell type annotation where you must decide which unlabeled cells (e.g., next 10 of many predicted on first 20 PCs) an expert should label next, using entropy or max-probability uncertainty from caret-trained RF/LR classifiers.
skills.name: classifier-uncertainty-estimation-entropy-maxprob
skills.search_text: classifier-uncertainty-estimation-entropy-maxprob Use when running an active learning loop for single-cell type annotation where you must decide which unlabeled cells (e.g., next 10 of many predicted on first 20 PCs) an expert should label next, using entropy or max-probability uncertainty from caret-trained RF/LR classifiers. The goal is selecting an initial balanced training set before any classifier exists (use leader adaptive reweighting, cluster-based or marker-based, instead of uncertainty ranking) Running self-training, where the most confidently predicted cells (top 10/50/100% by entropy) are pseudo-labeled — that uses low uncertainty, not high uncertainty ranking The expression matrix has no ground-truth labels available to annotate the selected 10 cells at each iteration, since the loop requires labeling with ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Ranks unlabeled single-cell predictions from random forest and logistic regression classifiers by predictive uncertainty (entropy and maximum-probability search) at highest, 95th-percentile, and 75th-percentile thresholds, so that the 10 most uncertain cells per active learning loop iteration are labeled with ground truth and used to retrain the classifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Ranks unlabeled single-cell predictions from random forest and logistic regression classifiers by predictive uncertainty (entropy and maximum-probability search) at highest, 95th-percentile, and 75th-percentile thresholds, so that the 10 most uncertain cells per active learning loop iteration are labeled with ground truth and used to retrain the classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is selecting an initial balanced training set before any classifier exists (use leader adaptive reweighting, cluster-based or marker-based, instead of uncertainty ranking) Running self-training, where the most confidently predicted cells (top 10/50/100% by entropy) are pseudo-labeled — that uses low uncertainty, not high uncertainty ranking The expression matrix has no ground-truth labels available to annotate the selected 10 cells at each iteration, since the loop requires labeling with ground truth

skills.description: Use when you have de novo-called scRNA-seq cleavage site coordinates and need to classify them as GENCODE-validated, externally supported (PolyASite), or novel by genomic interval overlap.
skills.name: cleavage-site-genomic-interval-intersection
skills.search_text: cleavage-site-genomic-interval-intersection Use when you have de novo-called scRNA-seq cleavage site coordinates and need to classify them as GENCODE-validated, externally supported (PolyASite), or novel by genomic interval overlap. Input reads come from 10x Genomics data where most reads do not span cleavage sites, preventing exact de novo CS mapping — use the prebuilt CS atlas as scUTRquant targets instead The CS catalog already exists (e.g. scUTRquant-inputs resources); re-intersection is redundant for isoform quantification You need gene/3'UTR expression quantification rather than CS classification — use scUTRquant directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies candidate mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) de novo-called from Microwell-seq (MWS) data by coordinate-based interval intersection against GENCODE 3' end windows and PolyASite 2.0 clusters, sorting sites into GENCODE-annotated, PolyASite-supported, and novel categories before exporting a CS atlas (mws_cs_annotation.gtf/.bed). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Classifies candidate mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) de novo-called from Microwell-seq (MWS) data by coordinate-based interval intersection against GENCODE 3' end windows and PolyASite 2.0 clusters, sorting sites into GENCODE-annotated, PolyASite-supported, and novel categories before exporting a CS atlas (mws_cs_annotation.gtf/.bed).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads come from 10x Genomics data where most reads do not span cleavage sites, preventing exact de novo CS mapping — use the prebuilt CS atlas as scUTRquant targets instead The CS catalog already exists (e.g. scUTRquant-inputs resources); re-intersection is redundant for isoform quantification You need gene/3'UTR expression quantification rather than CS classification — use scUTRquant directly

skills.description: Use when the goal is to map 3' end cleavage sites de novo from MWS reads spanning the poly(A) tail per cell type, e.g. building a CS atlas from the Mouse Cell Atlas or Human Cell Landscape.
skills.name: cleavage-site-peak-calling-per-cell-type
skills.search_text: cleavage-site-peak-calling-per-cell-type Use when the goal is to map 3' end cleavage sites de novo from MWS reads spanning the poly(A) tail per cell type, e.g. building a CS atlas from the Mouse Cell Atlas or Human Cell Landscape. Input is 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data: most reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, preventing exact de novo CS mapping — use scUTRquant quantification against a fixed CS set instead The CS annotation set already exists and the task is quantification of gene and 3'UTR isoform expression rather than de novo peak discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 De novo mapping of mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) from Microwell-seq (MWS) data across 206 human and mouse primary cell types, producing a coordinate-annotated CS atlas that extends GENCODE annotations by 40%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: De novo mapping of mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) from Microwell-seq (MWS) data across 206 human and mouse primary cell types, producing a coordinate-annotated CS atlas that extends GENCODE annotations by 40%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data: most reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, preventing exact de novo CS mapping — use scUTRquant quantification against a fixed CS set instead The CS annotation set already exists and the task is quantification of gene and 3'UTR isoform expression rather than de novo peak discovery

skills.description: Use when a computational IGHV mutation classifier's calls must be validated against clinical Sanger-based mCLL/uCLL labels, to quantify concordance and correlation of percent-mutation values in a CLL RNA-seq cohort.
skills.name: clinical-concordance-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: clinical-concordance-correlation-analysis Use when a computational IGHV mutation classifier's calls must be validated against clinical Sanger-based mCLL/uCLL labels, to quantify concordance and correlation of percent-mutation values in a CLL RNA-seq cohort. Input BAMs are not aligned to the hg38 (GRCh38) genome build with BWA and coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS calls feeding this comparison would be invalid Samples have fewer than 25M sequence reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for reliable IGHV reconstruction The goal is T-cell receptor (TR) repertoire or non-IGHV mutation analysis rather than CLL IGHV hypermutation status classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compares computationally inferred IGHV somatic hypermutation (mCLL/uCLL) calls from CRIS RNA-seq reconstructions against gold-standard clinical PCR-Sanger classifications, reporting per-sample concordance and Pearson correlation between percent-mutation values (target: 16/16 concordant, r = 0.95 in GSE66228). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Compares computationally inferred IGHV somatic hypermutation (mCLL/uCLL) calls from CRIS RNA-seq reconstructions against gold-standard clinical PCR-Sanger classifications, reporting per-sample concordance and Pearson correlation between percent-mutation values (target: 16/16 concordant, r = 0.95 in GSE66228).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAMs are not aligned to the hg38 (GRCh38) genome build with BWA and coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS calls feeding this comparison would be invalid Samples have fewer than 25M sequence reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for reliable IGHV reconstruction The goal is T-cell receptor (TR) repertoire or non-IGHV mutation analysis rather than CLL IGHV hypermutation status classification

skills.description: Use when associating continuous molecular scores (e.g., PROGENy pathway activity) with patient overall survival time and event status, and confounders such as cohort/study of origin or age must be adjusted for.
skills.name: clinical-covariate-adjustment-regression
skills.search_text: clinical-covariate-adjustment-regression Use when associating continuous molecular scores (e.g., PROGENy pathway activity) with patient overall survival time and event status, and confounders such as cohort/study of origin or age must be adjusted for. The goal is inferring pathway activity scores from expression rather than testing survival associations — use PROGENy/decoupleR scoring instead; this skill consumes already-computed scores. Survival data are missing or the endpoint is not a time-to-event with censoring (e.g., only binary response), where Cox regression is inappropriate. Analysis targets non-clinical associations such as driver-mutation recovery or drug response in GDSC cell lines, where this Cox-survival workflow does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Fit covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models (R survival package, coxph) linking pathway activity scores such as PROGENy signaling footprints to patient overall survival, regressing out confounders like study of origin and age in pan-cancer and per-cancer-type cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Fit covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models (R survival package, coxph) linking pathway activity scores such as PROGENy signaling footprints to patient overall survival, regressing out confounders like study of origin and age in pan-cancer and per-cancer-type cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inferring pathway activity scores from expression rather than testing survival associations — use PROGENy/decoupleR scoring instead; this skill consumes already-computed scores. Survival data are missing or the endpoint is not a time-to-event with censoring (e.g., only binary response), where Cox regression is inappropriate. Analysis targets non-clinical associations such as driver-mutation recovery or drug response in GDSC cell lines, where this Cox-survival workflow does not apply.

skills.description: Use when training data and external validation data come from different transcriptomic platforms (e.g., RNA-seq vs. microarray GEO datasets) and the goal is a clinical outcome prediction model that transfers across platforms.
skills.name: clinical-outcome-prediction-modeling
skills.search_text: clinical-outcome-prediction-modeling Use when training data and external validation data come from different transcriptomic platforms (e.g., RNA-seq vs. microarray GEO datasets) and the goal is a clinical outcome prediction model that transfers across platforms. The training and validation sets share no common genes — Ciclops fails silently, producing train/test split csvs in ./training with only two columns (sample names and labels) and no gene expression columns SHAP biomarker interpretation is needed for the regression models (Gaussian Process Regression or Linear Regression) — SHAP analysis is not implemented for those models Datasets were already jointly normalized during preprocessing — consider the --no_quantile flag rather than applying quantile normalization again http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Build cross-platform clinical outcome prediction models with Ciclops, which performs transfer learning from one transcriptomic platform's samples to another (e.g., training on RNA-seq GSE151189 and testing on microarray GSE59098) using LightGBM as the default model with quantile normalization enabled. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101583
skills.summary: Build cross-platform clinical outcome prediction models with Ciclops, which performs transfer learning from one transcriptomic platform's samples to another (e.g., training on RNA-seq GSE151189 and testing on microarray GSE59098) using LightGBM as the default model with quantile normalization enabled.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training and validation sets share no common genes — Ciclops fails silently, producing train/test split csvs in ./training with only two columns (sample names and labels) and no gene expression columns SHAP biomarker interpretation is needed for the regression models (Gaussian Process Regression or Linear Regression) — SHAP analysis is not implemented for those models Datasets were already jointly normalized during preprocessing — consider the --no_quantile flag rather than applying quantile normalization again

skills.description: Use when a merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN and snRNAseq matrix with per-cell clinical metadata (diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage, sex) are available and the goal is to test which GRN modules are significantly associated with disease traits.
skills.name: clinical-phenotype-association-testing
skills.search_text: clinical-phenotype-association-testing Use when a merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN and snRNAseq matrix with per-cell clinical metadata (diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage, sex) are available and the goal is to test which GRN modules are significantly associated with disease traits. No merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN exists yet — the leiden partitioning and AUCell scoring require the BuildNetwork output as input. Expression data lack per-cell clinical phenotype labels (diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage) or the sex covariate needed for regression adjustment. The goal is causal/directional regulatory inference rather than phenotypic association — inferred GRN links are not necessarily causal or directional. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Associates single-cell GRN module expression scores with clinical traits (e.g., AD diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage) via linear regression with covariate adjustment (sex) and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, then annotates significant modules with pathway enrichment using enrichR against GO biological process, DisGeNET, Reactome, BioCarta, and KEGG. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Associates single-cell GRN module expression scores with clinical traits (e.g., AD diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage) via linear regression with covariate adjustment (sex) and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, then annotates significant modules with pathway enrichment using enrichR against GO biological process, DisGeNET, Reactome, BioCarta, and KEGG.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN exists yet — the leiden partitioning and AUCell scoring require the BuildNetwork output as input. Expression data lack per-cell clinical phenotype labels (diagnosis, plaque stage, tangle stage) or the sex covariate needed for regression adjustment. skills.search_text: clinical-survival-data-integration Use when detected RNCs/modules from tumor expression data (e.g., 161 TCGA ESCA tumors) must be associated with clinical survival outcomes, requiring a per-module Kaplan-Meier log-rank statistic. The cohort or module members lack matched clinical survival metadata (e.g., only the 11 normal ESCA samples), so no KM split/log-rank test can be computed The analysis goal is differential expression scoring (edgeR DEGs / combinp) rather than outcome association of already-detected circuits Modules come from the global runmodule(method='global', FDR=1e-5) case where the target is a single maximum-scoring circuit, not a per-RNC survival screen Links fRNC-detected RBP-ncRNA circuits (RNCs) to patient outcome by joining each module's member expression profiles with tumor clinical data and computing Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank testing per RNC, as demonstrated on the TCGA ESCA case study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035

skills.description: Use when phase I/II trial data contain per-dose binary toxicity (DLT) and efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) plus isotonic DLT rate estimates from PAVA, and closed-form joint response probability estimates are needed to feed a utility-based OBD selection.
skills.name: clinical-trial-binary-outcome-count-analysis
skills.search_text: clinical-trial-binary-outcome-count-analysis Use when phase I/II trial data contain per-dose binary toxicity (DLT) and efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) plus isotonic DLT rate estimates from PAVA, and closed-form joint response probability estimates are needed to feed a utility-based OBD selection. The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the article states the design 'cannot be applied directly to cases in which the response outcome requires a long follow-up time to be assessed' The efficacy outcome is not binary and quickly observable after treatment initiation Drug-combination trials — extending TSNP to identify optimal dose combinations is explicitly future work not yet done http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes closed-form estimates of the joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_jkl for k,l = 0,1) at each dose of the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on the PAVA isotonic DLT rate estimate — no MCMC or numerical optimization required. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Computes closed-form estimates of the joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_jkl for k,l = 0,1) at each dose of the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on the PAVA isotonic DLT rate estimate — no MCMC or numerical optimization required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the article states the design 'cannot be applied directly to cases in which the response outcome requires a long follow-up time to be assessed' The efficacy outcome is not binary and quickly observable after treatment initiation Drug-combination trials — extending TSNP to identify optimal dose combinations is explicitly future work not yet done

skills.search_text: clinical-trial-monte-carlo-simulation Use when estimating operating characteristics — early-termination probability, dose-selection percentages P1/P2 — of the TSNP design for a given toxicity/efficacy scenario, such as the null (all doses overly toxic, φ=0.2) case. The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the TSNP design only handles binary, quickly observable response outcomes The goal is dose-combination trials — extension of TSNP to drug combinations is future work, not implemented A Bayesian parametric phase I/II design simulation is required — this skill specifically simulates the nonparametric TSNP design and its P1/P2 comparators http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Monte Carlo simulation of the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II design's operating characteristics (e.g. early-termination probability under the null scenario with φ changed from 0.3 to 0.2) by replicating thousands of simulated trials in R and aggregating selection percentages into a CSV table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Monte Carlo simulation of the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II design's operating characteristics (e.g. early-termination probability under the null scenario with φ changed from 0.3 to 0.2) by replicating thousands of simulated trials in R and aggregating selection percentages into a CSV table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the TSNP design only handles binary, quickly observable response outcomes The goal is dose-combination trials — extension of TSNP to drug combinations is future work, not implemented A Bayesian parametric phase I/II design simulation is required — this skill specifically simulates the nonparametric TSNP design and its P1/P2 comparators

skills.description: Use when you have per-dose phase I/II toxicity data (patient counts n_j and DLT counts) whose raw proportions p̃_j violate the order constraint p1 ≤ p2 ≤ ... ≤ pJ and you need monotonicity-constrained DLT rate estimates for dose-escalation decisions or utility calculations.
skills.name: clinical-trial-toxicity-data-processing
skills.search_text: clinical-trial-toxicity-data-processing Use when you have per-dose phase I/II toxicity data (patient counts n_j and DLT counts) whose raw proportions p̃_j violate the order constraint p1 ≤ p2 ≤ ... ≤ pJ and you need monotonicity-constrained DLT rate estimates for dose-escalation decisions or utility calculations. The trial outcome requires long follow-up time to assess — the TSNP nonparametric approach 'cannot be applied directly' to such cases The response outcome is not binary and quickly observable after treatment initiation, or the trial involves drug combinations (an untested extension in the TSNP design) Computes per-dose DLT rate estimates that satisfy the monotonic increasing (order) constraint across dose levels by applying the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA) to observed per-dose toxicity data. The resulting isotonic estimates are equivalent to the constrained maximum likelihood estimates of the DLT probabilities used by the TSNP phase I/II design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Computes per-dose DLT rate estimates that satisfy the monotonic increasing (order) constraint across dose levels by applying the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA) to observed per-dose toxicity data. The resulting isotonic estimates are equivalent to the constrained maximum likelihood estimates of the DLT probabilities used by the TSNP phase I/II design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trial outcome requires long follow-up time to assess — the TSNP nonparametric approach 'cannot be applied directly' to such cases The response outcome is not binary and quickly observable after treatment initiation, or the trial involves drug combinations (an untested extension in the TSNP design)

skills.description: Use when you have ClinVar VUSs prioritized by a splicing predictor (e.g., SpliceAI) and per-gene MRSD scores (.results.mrsd.txt) from whole blood, LCL, skeletal muscle, and cultured fibroblast GTEx datasets, and need the fraction of variants in low-MRSD (assayable) genes.
skills.name: clinvar-variant-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: clinvar-variant-gene-mapping Use when you have ClinVar VUSs prioritized by a splicing predictor (e.g., SpliceAI) and per-gene MRSD scores (.results.mrsd.txt) from whole blood, LCL, skeletal muscle, and cultured fibroblast GTEx datasets, and need the fraction of variants in low-MRSD (assayable) genes. The MRSD score tables (.results.mrsd.txt) for the four biosamples have not yet been generated by MRSDexplorer.py from junction counts and sequencing depths — generate scores first.
