skills.name: clonal-variant-caller-benchmarking
skills.search_text: clonal-variant-caller-benchmarking Decision support for choosing an mtDNA variant caller for scRNA-seq clonality analysis, or for reproducing a simulation-based benchmark comparing MQuad, mgatk, and Monovar on ground-truth clonal variants. The goal is calling variants on one real dataset rather than comparing callers on data with known ground-truth clonal variants Input is nuclear-genome scDNA-seq data, where diploid-context callers such as Monovar or Conbase are appropriate (mitochondrial genome violates the diploid assumption) Data are scATAC-seq, for which mtDNA-specific methods like EMBLEM and mgatk were originally designed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark single-cell mtDNA clonal variant callers (MQuad vs mgatk vs Monovar) on simulated Smart-seq2-like mtDNA read data by sweeping each tool's calling threshold to trace PR/ROC curves and report AUPRC/AUROC per simulation setting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell mtDNA clonal variant callers (MQuad vs mgatk vs Monovar) on simulated Smart-seq2-like mtDNA read data by sweeping each tool's calling threshold to trace PR/ROC curves and report AUPRC/AUROC per simulation setting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling variants on one real dataset rather than comparing callers on data with known ground-truth clonal variants Input is nuclear-genome scDNA-seq data, where diploid-context callers such as Monovar or Conbase are appropriate (mitochondrial genome violates the diploid assumption) Data are scATAC-seq, for which mtDNA-specific methods like EMBLEM and mgatk were originally designed

skills.description: Use when single-cell count data have paired clone-barcode assignments (cell ID to barcode table) and the goal is to test how weighting clonal origin reshapes transcriptome-only clusters, e.g. reducing entropy of known cell-type distributions across clusters.
skills.name: clonal-weighted-hybrid-clustering
skills.search_text: clonal-weighted-hybrid-clustering Use when single-cell count data have paired clone-barcode assignments (cell ID to barcode table) and the goal is to test how weighting clonal origin reshapes transcriptome-only clusters, e.g. reducing entropy of known cell-type distributions across clusters. Cells lack clone-barcode information (transcriptome-only data), since α weighting of clone edges requires paired barcode assignments The experimental system's cell fate is determined by extrinsic rather than intrinsic (clonal) factors, where clonal weighting may not be biologically meaningful — no reliable method exists to identify which systems benefit from clonal information Full-lineage-tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) is the input, since the study did not address phylogenetic-distance weighting, though ClonoCluster could be adapted http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates hybrid single-cell clusters by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights using the tunable parameter α (α = 0 purely transcriptome, α = 1 purely clone) via the ClonoCluster R package, then assesses cluster purity/entropy against known cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Generates hybrid single-cell clusters by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights using the tunable parameter α (α = 0 purely transcriptome, α = 1 purely clone) via the ClonoCluster R package, then assesses cluster purity/entropy against known cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack clone-barcode information (transcriptome-only data), since α weighting of clone edges requires paired barcode assignments The experimental system's cell fate is determined by extrinsic rather than intrinsic (clonal) factors, where clonal weighting may not be biologically meaningful — no reliable method exists to identify which systems benefit from clonal information Full-lineage-tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) is the input, since the study did not address phylogenetic-distance weighting, though ClonoCluster could be adapted

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a tumour sample must be partitioned into malignant subclones and normal cells based on copy number alterations, e.g., before clone-stratified differential expression.
skills.name: clone-assignment-cell-grouping
skills.search_text: clone-assignment-cell-grouping Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a tumour sample must be partitioned into malignant subclones and normal cells based on copy number alterations, e.g., before clone-stratified differential expression. Input data lacks heterozygous SNP coverage so BAF signals cannot be computed, and only read-depth-based CNA calling is feasible The task only needs expression clustering without copy-number-aware clone structure — a generic clustering tool would avoid the unnecessary CNA inference The dataset is a pseudo-bulk or bulk sample rather than single-cell data, where XClone's cell-level smoothing and KNN cell-cell graph do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Assign individual cells to clonal subpopulations (e.g., normal, Clone 1, Clone 2 in the TNBC1 sample) by inferring allele- and haplotype-specific copy number states with XClone's combined RDR and BAF modules, storing labels under a Clone_ID cell-annotation key. Accurate clone grouping is the prerequisite for downstream per-clone analyses such as DEG enrichment in LOH regions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Assign individual cells to clonal subpopulations (e.g., normal, Clone 1, Clone 2 in the TNBC1 sample) by inferring allele- and haplotype-specific copy number states with XClone's combined RDR and BAF modules, storing labels under a Clone_ID cell-annotation key. Accurate clone grouping is the prerequisite for downstream per-clone analyses such as DEG enrichment in LOH regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks heterozygous SNP coverage so BAF signals cannot be computed, and only read-depth-based CNA calling is feasible The task only needs expression clustering without copy-number-aware clone structure — a generic clustering tool would avoid the unnecessary CNA inference The dataset is a pseudo-bulk or bulk sample rather than single-cell data, where XClone's cell-level smoothing and KNN cell-cell graph do not apply

skills.description: Use when single-cell count matrices are paired with clone-barcode assignments and you need clusters that weigh clonal origin alongside transcriptomic similarity, plus verification that cluster markers keep ROC AUC fidelity across α levels.
skills.name: clone-barcode-transcriptome-hybrid-clustering
skills.search_text: clone-barcode-transcriptome-hybrid-clustering Use when single-cell count matrices are paired with clone-barcode assignments and you need clusters that weigh clonal origin alongside transcriptomic similarity, plus verification that cluster markers keep ROC AUC fidelity across α levels. Full-lineage tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) — the study did not address these data types, though ClonoCluster could be adapted to weight distances by phylogenetic distance Systems where cell fate is determined extrinsically (e.g. cardiomyocyte-directed iPSCs from Jiang et al., low-dose vemurafenib) — high α reduces marker fidelity here, so clonal weighting is not beneficial Analysis goal is pure transcriptome-defined cell-type discovery with no barcode data available — ClonoCluster requires a table of cell IDs and assigned barcodes http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates hybrid single-cell clusters by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights using ClonoCluster's tunable parameter α (α=0 purely transcriptome, α=1 purely clone), then assesses whether hybrid clusters retain equivalent marker fidelity (median top-marker ROC AUC) versus transcriptome-only clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Generates hybrid single-cell clusters by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights using ClonoCluster's tunable parameter α (α=0 purely transcriptome, α=1 purely clone), then assesses whether hybrid clusters retain equivalent marker fidelity (median top-marker ROC AUC) versus transcriptome-only clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Full-lineage tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) — the study did not address these data types, though ClonoCluster could be adapted to weight distances by phylogenetic distance Systems where cell fate is determined extrinsically (e.g. cardiomyocyte-directed iPSCs from Jiang et al., low-dose vemurafenib) — high α reduces marker fidelity here, so clonal weighting is not beneficial Analysis goal is pure transcriptome-defined cell-type discovery with no barcode data available — ClonoCluster requires a table of cell IDs and assigned barcodes

skills.description: Use when you have a two-column cell-ID-to-barcode table (e.g. columns 'rn' and 'Barcode') and need to convert clonal relationships into normalized edge weights for graph-based single-cell clustering or integration with a transcriptome SNN graph.
skills.name: clone-barcode-weight-matrix-normalization
skills.search_text: clone-barcode-weight-matrix-normalization Use when you have a two-column cell-ID-to-barcode table (e.g. columns 'rn' and 'Barcode') and need to convert clonal relationships into normalized edge weights for graph-based single-cell clustering or integration with a transcriptome SNN graph. Cells have no clone barcode information (clustering must rely on transcriptome-only weights, α = 0) Input is full-lineage tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) — the binary same/different barcode weight does not capture phylogenetic distance, though the authors note ClonoCluster could be adapted for this The barcode table is a gene-by-cell count matrix rather than a cell-ID-to-barcode assignment table http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs the ClonoCluster 'clone weight' edge matrix for a cell-cell network graph: each edge receives a clone weight of 1 or 0 depending on whether two cells share the same barcode, then weights are normalized by the number of cells carrying that barcode, producing the clone modality input to the α-weighted hybrid graph. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Constructs the ClonoCluster 'clone weight' edge matrix for a cell-cell network graph: each edge receives a clone weight of 1 or 0 depending on whether two cells share the same barcode, then weights are normalized by the number of cells carrying that barcode, producing the clone modality input to the α-weighted hybrid graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have no clone barcode information (clustering must rely on transcriptome-only weights, α = 0) Input is full-lineage tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) — the binary same/different barcode weight does not capture phylogenetic distance, though the authors note ClonoCluster could be adapted for this The barcode table is a gene-by-cell count matrix rather than a cell-ID-to-barcode assignment table

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data has paired clone barcode assignments and you want hybrid clusters weighting clonal origin against transcriptomic similarity, e.g. barcoded melanoma/iPSC/HSC datasets.
skills.name: clone-barcode-weighted-louvain-clustering
skills.search_text: clone-barcode-weighted-louvain-clustering Use when single-cell transcriptome data has paired clone barcode assignments and you want hybrid clusters weighting clonal origin against transcriptomic similarity, e.g. barcoded melanoma/iPSC/HSC datasets. No clone barcode data are available for the cells — pure transcriptome tools like Seurat or scanpy remain the appropriate choice. Data are full-lineage tracing (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees); the article notes ClonoCluster was not designed for these, though it could be adapted to weight by phylogenetic distance. You only need 2D visualization rather than clustering — the complementary Warp Factor tool warps UMAPs instead of producing cluster assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 ClonoCluster's method for clustering single-cell profiles by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights via the tunable parameter α (0 = purely transcriptome, 1 = purely clone), followed by Louvain community detection. It is used to generate hybrid clusters that reveal clonally driven transcriptomic reorganization while keeping cluster counts comparable to standard transcriptome-only clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: ClonoCluster's method for clustering single-cell profiles by linearly combining transcriptome nearest-neighbor edge weights with clone-barcode weights via the tunable parameter α (0 = purely transcriptome, 1 = purely clone), followed by Louvain community detection. It is used to generate hybrid clusters that reveal clonally driven transcriptomic reorganization while keeping cluster counts comparable to standard transcriptome-only clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No clone barcode data are available for the cells — pure transcriptome tools like Seurat or scanpy remain the appropriate choice. Data are full-lineage tracing (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees); the article notes ClonoCluster was not designed for these, though it could be adapted to weight by phylogenetic distance. You only need 2D visualization rather than clustering — the complementary Warp Factor tool warps UMAPs instead of producing cluster assignments.

skills.description: Use when you have mtDNA clone assignments (e.g., MQuad/vireoSNP output with cell-level clone labels) plus independent annotations such as CNV subclones or tumor/normal labels, and need to test whether the mitochondrial clones recapitulate or refine the known clonal structure.
skills.name: clone-cnv-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: clone-cnv-concordance-analysis Use when you have mtDNA clone assignments (e.g., MQuad/vireoSNP output with cell-level clone labels) plus independent annotations such as CNV subclones or tumor/normal labels, and need to test whether the mitochondrial clones recapitulate or refine the known clonal structure. The goal is donor deconvolution of multiplexed scRNA-seq from common nuclear SNPs rather than within-sample mtDNA clonal substructure. No independent annotations (CNV subclones or tumor labels) exist, so the concordance/enrichment tests cannot be computed and only clonal assignment is needed. The data are not single-cell (e.g., bulk DNA/RNA), or the assay is scATAC-seq where mtDNA-specific callers like mgatk or EMBLEM were the primary design targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns single cells to mitochondrial clones using the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs, then cross-validates the mtDNA clones against independent tumor cell labels and CNV-defined subclones via two-sided Fisher's exact tests and confusion matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Assigns single cells to mitochondrial clones using the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs, then cross-validates the mtDNA clones against independent tumor cell labels and CNV-defined subclones via two-sided Fisher's exact tests and confusion matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is donor deconvolution of multiplexed scRNA-seq from common nuclear SNPs rather than within-sample mtDNA clonal substructure. No independent annotations (CNV subclones or tumor labels) exist, so the concordance/enrichment tests cannot be computed and only clonal assignment is needed. The data are not single-cell (e.g., bulk DNA/RNA), or the assay is scATAC-seq where mtDNA-specific callers like mgatk or EMBLEM were the primary design targets.

skills.description: Use when you have a PCA (or similar reduced-dimension) matrix plus per-cell clone barcode assignments and want a UMAP-style 2D visualization in which cells sharing a barcode coalesce as a single tunable parameter s increases.
skills.name: clone-informed-pc-warping
skills.search_text: clone-informed-pc-warping Use when you have a PCA (or similar reduced-dimension) matrix plus per-cell clone barcode assignments and want a UMAP-style 2D visualization in which cells sharing a barcode coalesce as a single tunable parameter s increases. You need hybrid clustering assignments rather than a 2D visualization — use ClonoCluster's clonocluster() with tunable alpha instead of PC warping Your input is a raw gene-by-cell count matrix and no PCA has been computed — run irlba_wrap first; the warp operates on PC values, not raw counts Your data have no clone barcode assignments (no clonal origin information to warp toward) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Warp Factor modifies the PCA matrix input to UMAP so that each cell's principal component values approach the mean PC value of its clone (barcode) cluster, controlled by a tunable parameter s from 0 to 10, enabling clonal origin to shape 2D transcriptome visualizations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Warp Factor modifies the PCA matrix input to UMAP so that each cell's principal component values approach the mean PC value of its clone (barcode) cluster, controlled by a tunable parameter s from 0 to 10, enabling clonal origin to shape 2D transcriptome visualizations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need hybrid clustering assignments rather than a 2D visualization — use ClonoCluster's clonocluster() with tunable alpha instead of PC warping Your input is a raw gene-by-cell count matrix and no PCA has been computed — run irlba_wrap first; the warp operates on PC values, not raw counts Your data have no clone barcode assignments (no clonal origin information to warp toward)

skills.description: Use when two lineage barcoding pre-processing pipelines must be cross-validated on identical single-cell amplicon FASTQ data and agreement should be quantified by per-cell annotation overlap and clone-size correlation.
skills.name: clone-size-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: clone-size-correlation-analysis Use when two lineage barcoding pre-processing pipelines must be cross-validated on identical single-cell amplicon FASTQ data and agreement should be quantified by per-cell annotation overlap and clone-size correlation. Input is already a barcode counts/annotation table and no cross-pipeline re-processing of raw FASTQ is required Data are population-level (bulk) barcoding reads rather than single-cell data — the population mode workflow does not involve cell barcode whitelists or PARSE_BARCODES_SC annotation No second pipeline's published annotations exist to compare against, so clone-size correlation has no reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantitative validation of a single-cell lineage barcode annotation pipeline (BARtab) against an existing pipeline (FateMap/Rewind) by comparing per-cell barcode annotations and per-clone sizes on the same FateMap FM0-2 paired-end amplicon FASTQ data, using overlap counts and Pearson clone-size correlations in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Quantitative validation of a single-cell lineage barcode annotation pipeline (BARtab) against an existing pipeline (FateMap/Rewind) by comparing per-cell barcode annotations and per-clone sizes on the same FateMap FM0-2 paired-end amplicon FASTQ data, using overlap counts and Pearson clone-size correlations in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a barcode counts/annotation table and no cross-pipeline re-processing of raw FASTQ is required Data are population-level (bulk) barcoding reads rather than single-cell data — the population mode workflow does not involve cell barcode whitelists or PARSE_BARCODES_SC annotation No second pipeline's published annotations exist to compare against, so clone-size correlation has no reference

skills.description: Use when mining significant higher-order combinations of SNPs (genetic meta-markers) across interacting genes, given binary or additive-encoded marker matrices, phenotype labels, a covariate, and a PPI/pathway/complex prior network.
skills.name: closed-pattern-discovery-in-snp-data
skills.search_text: closed-pattern-discovery-in-snp-data Use when mining significant higher-order combinations of SNPs (genetic meta-markers) across interacting genes, given binary or additive-encoded marker matrices, phenotype labels, a covariate, and a PPI/pathway/complex prior network. You are only testing single SNPs or predefined fixed genomic intervals — FastCMH-style interval search, not higher-order network-guided pattern mining, is the right tool. You have no prior gene-interaction knowledge (PPI network, pathways, complexes) and cannot restrict the search to connected gene subgraphs. Markers are not binary- or additive-encoded; other encodings fall outside HOGImine's supported inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduce HOGImine's breadth-first pattern enumeration with Tarone pruning: the poset of higher-order genetic interaction patterns spanning gene-interaction network cliques is expanded breadth-first, untestable branches are pruned against the updated Tarone significance threshold delta_tar, and only closed patterns are emitted with their CMH p-value, genes, and SNP positions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Reproduce HOGImine's breadth-first pattern enumeration with Tarone pruning: the poset of higher-order genetic interaction patterns spanning gene-interaction network cliques is expanded breadth-first, untestable branches are pruned against the updated Tarone significance threshold delta_tar, and only closed patterns are emitted with their CMH p-value, genes, and SNP positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are only testing single SNPs or predefined fixed genomic intervals — FastCMH-style interval search, not higher-order network-guided pattern mining, is the right tool. You have no prior gene-interaction knowledge (PPI network, pathways, complexes) and cannot restrict the search to connected gene subgraphs. Markers are not binary- or additive-encoded; other encodings fall outside HOGImine's supported inputs.

skills.description: Use when a protein/ADT count matrix from CITE-seq or related assays must be normalized as a baseline (e.g., benchmarking against dsb), by applying CLR across cells.
skills.name: clr-normalization-of-adt-counts
skills.search_text: clr-normalization-of-adt-counts Use when a protein/ADT count matrix from CITE-seq or related assays must be normalized as a baseline (e.g., benchmarking against dsb), by applying CLR across cells. When the goal is to correct ambient background noise and cell-to-cell technical noise, CLR does not model empty-droplet background or isotype-control covariance — use dsb's ambient-correction and denoising steps instead When empty droplets or isotype controls are absent and only a low-level baseline scaling is needed, note that the paper defers caveats for isotype-free usage to the Supplementary Note rather than treating CLR as equivalent When the input is already normalized ADT data (e.g., dsb residuals or clipped values) — applying CLR again would double-normalize Applies centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation to antibody-derived tag (ADT) count matrices across cells as a baseline normalization for CITE-seq protein data, serving here as the comparator to dsb normalization in clustering-coherence and lineage-marker fold-change assessments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Applies centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation to antibody-derived tag (ADT) count matrices across cells as a baseline normalization for CITE-seq protein data, serving here as the comparator to dsb normalization in clustering-coherence and lineage-marker fold-change assessments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to correct ambient background noise and cell-to-cell technical noise, CLR does not model empty-droplet background or isotype-control covariance — use dsb's ambient-correction and denoising steps instead When empty droplets or isotype controls are absent and only a low-level baseline scaling is needed, note that the paper defers caveats for isotype-free usage to the Supplementary Note rather than treating CLR as equivalent When the input is already normalized ADT data (e.g., dsb residuals or clipped values) — applying CLR again would double-normalize

skills.description: Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) counts from CITE-seq/TEA-seq data and you need a standard baseline normalization against which background-corrected methods like dsb can be compared, or when empty-droplet background matrices are not being modeled.
skills.name: clr-protein-count-normalization
skills.search_text: clr-protein-count-normalization Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) counts from CITE-seq/TEA-seq data and you need a standard baseline normalization against which background-corrected methods like dsb can be compared, or when empty-droplet background matrices are not being modeled. When ambient, unbound-antibody background noise must be removed: CLR does not use empty-droplet background and retains correlation with ambient ADT levels (r≈0.8 in TEA-seq), whereas dsb corrects for it When isotype-control-based cell-to-cell technical denoising is needed; CLR performs no per-cell noise modeling (no Gaussian mixture / technical component regression as in dsb) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Centered log-ratio (CLR) normalization of the ADT/protein count matrix, e.g. via Seurat's NormalizeData on the ADT assay, used here as the baseline comparator to dsb normalization in CITE-seq/TEA-seq workflows. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Centered log-ratio (CLR) normalization of the ADT/protein count matrix, e.g. via Seurat's NormalizeData on the ADT assay, used here as the baseline comparator to dsb normalization in CITE-seq/TEA-seq workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ambient, unbound-antibody background noise must be removed: CLR does not use empty-droplet background and retains correlation with ambient ADT levels (r≈0.8 in TEA-seq), whereas dsb corrects for it When isotype-control-based cell-to-cell technical denoising is needed; CLR performs no per-cell noise modeling (no Gaussian mixture / technical component regression as in dsb)

skills.description: Use when you have two or more categorical cell-annotation columns over the same cells (e.g. scTriangulate labels vs. HLCA/CellRef label-transfer results) and need an external-agreement benchmark to compare integration strategies.
skills.name: cluster-agreement-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: cluster-agreement-metrics-computation Use when you have two or more categorical cell-annotation columns over the same cells (e.g. scTriangulate labels vs. HLCA/CellRef label-transfer results) and need an external-agreement benchmark to compare integration strategies. Input is raw counts with no categorical annotation columns — the metrics require a definitive one-annotation-per-cell assignment matrix (binary X of shape I * N) from a prior scTriangulate or label-transfer run. The candidate and reference labels are defined on different cells (no shared base dataset), since Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure need cell-level label pairs. You need to integrate conflicting label sets rather than benchmark an existing one — that is the scTriangulate lazy_run integration step, not the metrics computation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify how well a reconciled cell-population labeling (e.g. a scTriangulate solution, or an ensemble-clustering baseline) agrees with independent reference annotations (Azimuth CellRef 1.0, HLCA) using Homogeneity, Completeness, and V-Measure (sklearn conventions), including subdivided dendritic-cell and macrophage populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Quantify how well a reconciled cell-population labeling (e.g. a scTriangulate solution, or an ensemble-clustering baseline) agrees with independent reference annotations (Azimuth CellRef 1.0, HLCA) using Homogeneity, Completeness, and V-Measure (sklearn conventions), including subdivided dendritic-cell and macrophage populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts with no categorical annotation columns — the metrics require a definitive one-annotation-per-cell assignment matrix (binary X of shape I * N) from a prior scTriangulate or label-transfer run. The candidate and reference labels are defined on different cells (no shared base dataset), since Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure need cell-level label pairs. You need to integrate conflicting label sets rather than benchmark an existing one — that is the scTriangulate lazy_run integration step, not the metrics computation.

skills.description: Use when an RCC (or other unsupervised) clustering result must be cross-tabulated with known sample attributes—such as the Biase dataset's ICM vs. trophectoderm labels—to biologically interpret and validate the clusters.
skills.name: cluster-annotation-against-known-attributes
skills.search_text: cluster-annotation-against-known-attributes Use when an RCC (or other unsupervised) clustering result must be cross-tabulated with known sample attributes—such as the Biase dataset's ICM vs. trophectoderm labels—to biologically interpret and validate the clusters. When the transcriptomic data have no known sample attributes or annotations to compare against — annotation against attributes is meaningless without metadata. When the goal is simply to determine the optimal number of clusters rather than to interpret clusters against known labels; use RCC_clus alone instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate RCC's recursively derived clusters against known sample attributes (e.g., cell type, tissue of origin) using the clusterAnnotation function of the RCC R package, so that discovered subtypes can be interpreted and validated against ground-truth metadata. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Annotate RCC's recursively derived clusters against known sample attributes (e.g., cell type, tissue of origin) using the clusterAnnotation function of the RCC R package, so that discovered subtypes can be interpreted and validated against ground-truth metadata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the transcriptomic data have no known sample attributes or annotations to compare against — annotation against attributes is meaningless without metadata. When the goal is simply to determine the optimal number of clusters rather than to interpret clusters against known labels; use RCC_clus alone instead.

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-wise (sample-wise) optimal EMBEDR embedding plus expert cell-type annotations and need to test whether unsupervised cluster structure in the embedding is biologically concordant with those annotations.
skills.name: cluster-annotation-confusion-analysis
skills.search_text: cluster-annotation-confusion-analysis Use when you have a cell-wise (sample-wise) optimal EMBEDR embedding plus expert cell-type annotations and need to test whether unsupervised cluster structure in the embedding is biologically concordant with those annotations. Input is a raw feature/counts table rather than an already-computed cell-wise optimal EMBEDR embedding — the sweep and fit_samplewise_optimal steps must be completed first The perplexity values of interest were not included in the EMBEDR sweep, since optimal per-cell perplexities can only be selected from those used in the sweep You need a quantitative clustering benchmark with concrete metric values — the article's results only report a template-driven cluster count (print statement), not a validated numeric score http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that clusters found by DBSCAN on the cell-wise optimal t-SNE embedding (built from per-cell EMBEDR-optimal perplexities) correspond to expert cell-type annotations, e.g. the seven bone marrow cell types of the Tabula Muris marrow data, by computing a confusion table of DBSCAN labels versus annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Validates that clusters found by DBSCAN on the cell-wise optimal t-SNE embedding (built from per-cell EMBEDR-optimal perplexities) correspond to expert cell-type annotations, e.g. the seven bone marrow cell types of the Tabula Muris marrow data, by computing a confusion table of DBSCAN labels versus annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw feature/counts table rather than an already-computed cell-wise optimal EMBEDR embedding — the sweep and fit_samplewise_optimal steps must be completed first The perplexity values of interest were not included in the EMBEDR sweep, since optimal per-cell perplexities can only be selected from those used in the sweep You need a quantitative clustering benchmark with concrete metric values — the article's results only report a template-driven cluster count (print statement), not a validated numeric score

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether one-against-all cluster marker gene identification produces pseudo marker genes and how many clusters an automatic annotator (scCATCH/CellMatch) labels consistently with manual ground-truth labels on a clustered scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.name: cluster-annotation-consistency-assessment
skills.search_text: cluster-annotation-consistency-assessment Use when evaluating whether one-against-all cluster marker gene identification produces pseudo marker genes and how many clusters an automatic annotator (scCATCH/CellMatch) labels consistently with manual ground-truth labels on a clustered scRNA-seq dataset. When clusters have already been annotated via a paired-comparison scheme guaranteeing markers upregulated in only one cluster — pseudo marker gene impairment is not expected and consistency assessment adds little When the tissue of interest is poorly covered by the CellMatch reference database, since limited references — not pseudo marker genes — may drive incorrect annotation When the goal is to evaluate cell-based (per-cell) annotation methods such as SingleR or CellAssign rather than cluster-based marker gene annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A method for quantifying how consistently an automatic annotation tool (e.g. scCATCH's findcelltype against CellMatch) recovers manually assigned cell type labels per cluster, and for exposing pseudo marker genes (genes significantly upregulated in at least two clusters) generated by one-against-all marker identification (e.g. Seurat's Wilcoxon rank-sum test) that impair annotation accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: A method for quantifying how consistently an automatic annotation tool (e.g. scCATCH's findcelltype against CellMatch) recovers manually assigned cell type labels per cluster, and for exposing pseudo marker genes (genes significantly upregulated in at least two clusters) generated by one-against-all marker identification (e.g. Seurat's Wilcoxon rank-sum test) that impair annotation accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When clusters have already been annotated via a paired-comparison scheme guaranteeing markers upregulated in only one cluster — pseudo marker gene impairment is not expected and consistency assessment adds little When the tissue of interest is poorly covered by the CellMatch reference database, since limited references — not pseudo marker genes — may drive incorrect annotation When the goal is to evaluate cell-based (per-cell) annotation methods such as SingleR or CellAssign rather than cluster-based marker gene annotation

skills.description: Use when you have simulated single-cell count data with known per-cell-type/DE-group ground-truth labels and need to verify that feature profiles adhere to expected mean cluster profiles before benchmarking downstream methods.
skills.name: cluster-assignment-accuracy-verification
skills.search_text: cluster-assignment-accuracy-verification Use when you have simulated single-cell count data with known per-cell-type/DE-group ground-truth labels and need to verify that feature profiles adhere to expected mean cluster profiles before benchmarking downstream methods. Data are raw single-cell counts that should stay at per-cell resolution — this skill operates on per-cell-type aggregated average profiles Single-cell layers other than scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq are involved, since sc_mosim currently simulates only those two modalities The goal is validating bulk temporal patterns, where the paper instead used k-means clustering of simulated feature profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates that simulated single-cell multi-omics feature profiles (scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq from MOSim's sc_mosim) reproduce the intended co-expression/DE-group structure by clustering across-cell-type profiles with Spearman's distance and k-medoids (k=10) and measuring the rate of incorrect cluster assignment (~3.3% expected). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Validates that simulated single-cell multi-omics feature profiles (scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq from MOSim's sc_mosim) reproduce the intended co-expression/DE-group structure by clustering across-cell-type profiles with Spearman's distance and k-medoids (k=10) and measuring the rate of incorrect cluster assignment (~3.3% expected).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are raw single-cell counts that should stay at per-cell resolution — this skill operates on per-cell-type aggregated average profiles Single-cell layers other than scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq are involved, since sc_mosim currently simulates only those two modalities The goal is validating bulk temporal patterns, where the paper instead used k-means clustering of simulated feature profiles

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-clustering accuracy of methods that assign single cells (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq) to known subpopulations, e.g. testing whether loop data reduces error as dropout increases.
skills.name: cluster-assignment-error-rate-evaluation
skills.search_text: cluster-assignment-error-rate-evaluation Use when comparing cell-clustering accuracy of methods that assign single cells (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq) to known subpopulations, e.g. testing whether loop data reduces error as dropout increases. Ground-truth subpopulation labels are unavailable, so no reference exists against which to compute a classification error rate The task is deconvolution of bulk profiles (accuracy of subpopulation-specific expression/accessibility/loop profiles), not cluster-assignment accuracy of single cells A single deterministic clustering run suffices; the 50-initialization averaging protocol is designed for stochastic NMF-based methods sensitive to initialization http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates clustering quality of single-cell methods (e.g., DC3 vs coupled NMF vs plain NMF) by computing the classification error rate between true subpopulation labels and predicted cluster assignments, averaged across modalities and independent runs. In the DC3 paper this quantifies how bulk HiChIP loop data improves coupled clustering under varying dropout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Evaluates clustering quality of single-cell methods (e.g., DC3 vs coupled NMF vs plain NMF) by computing the classification error rate between true subpopulation labels and predicted cluster assignments, averaged across modalities and independent runs. In the DC3 paper this quantifies how bulk HiChIP loop data improves coupled clustering under varying dropout.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth subpopulation labels are unavailable, so no reference exists against which to compute a classification error rate The task is deconvolution of bulk profiles (accuracy of subpopulation-specific expression/accessibility/loop profiles), not cluster-assignment accuracy of single cells A single deterministic clustering run suffices; the 50-initialization averaging protocol is designed for stochastic NMF-based methods sensitive to initialization

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample cluster assignments plus clinical survival data (survival time and cancer-type attribute) and need to quantify how many cancer types have subtypes with significantly distinct survival profiles.
skills.name: cluster-assignment-survival-association
skills.search_text: cluster-assignment-survival-association Use when you have per-sample cluster assignments plus clinical survival data (survival time and cancer-type attribute) and need to quantify how many cancer types have subtypes with significantly distinct survival profiles. Samples lack survival times or a cancer-type attribute in the clinical info file, so Kaplan-Meier/log-rank testing is undefined The goal is subtype discovery or cluster characterization itself rather than validating clusters against clinical outcome — use RCC clustering or clusterAttr/clusterAnnotation instead Cancer-type/cluster groups are so small that the minSample filter removes them, leaving no powered groups for log-rank comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assess whether cluster assignments (RCC, tSNE+k-means, hclust, Chen et al., Hoadley et al.) produce clinically relevant subtypes by generating Kaplan-Meier curves per cluster within each TCGA pan-cancer type and testing survival differences with log-rank tests at p<0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Assess whether cluster assignments (RCC, tSNE+k-means, hclust, Chen et al., Hoadley et al.) produce clinically relevant subtypes by generating Kaplan-Meier curves per cluster within each TCGA pan-cancer type and testing survival differences with log-rank tests at p<0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack survival times or a cancer-type attribute in the clinical info file, so Kaplan-Meier/log-rank testing is undefined The goal is subtype discovery or cluster characterization itself rather than validating clusters against clinical outcome — use RCC clustering or clusterAttr/clusterAnnotation instead Cancer-type/cluster groups are so small that the minSample filter removes them, leaving no powered groups for log-rank comparison

skills.description: Use when sample-wise tncRNA profiles (Supplementary sheets 5.1–5.4) must be reduced with t-SNE to 2D and each tissue sample assigned to its nearest cluster and logged in a tabular record.
skills.name: cluster-assignment-tabulation
skills.search_text: cluster-assignment-tabulation Use when sample-wise tncRNA profiles (Supplementary sheets 5.1–5.4) must be reduced with t-SNE to 2D and each tissue sample assigned to its nearest cluster and logged in a tabular record. Tissues in the input have fewer than 10 samples — the paper restricts t-SNE matrix generation to tissues with at least 10 samples (Supplementary sheets 5.1–5.4). The question is differential expression or stress-response cataloging of tncRNAs, which relies on abundance/count data rather than binary presence/absence tissue clustering. A 2D embedding or cluster-label table already exists for the samples; re-embedding with t-SNE would reassign labels non-deterministically. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tabulates sample-to-cluster assignments after t-SNE embedding of tissue-wise tncRNA presence/absence profiles, capturing the tissue-specific clustering of plant tncRNAs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) reported in the paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Tabulates sample-to-cluster assignments after t-SNE embedding of tissue-wise tncRNA presence/absence profiles, capturing the tissue-specific clustering of plant tncRNAs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) reported in the paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissues in the input have fewer than 10 samples — the paper restricts t-SNE matrix generation to tissues with at least 10 samples (Supplementary sheets 5.1–5.4). The question is differential expression or stress-response cataloging of tncRNAs, which relies on abundance/count data rather than binary presence/absence tissue clustering. A 2D embedding or cluster-label table already exists for the samples; re-embedding with t-SNE would reassign labels non-deterministically.

skills.description: Use when RCC_clus has produced recursive consensus cluster assignments and you must validate clusters against sample metadata (attribute columns with a minSample cutoff) or assign subtype labels to clusters.
skills.name: cluster-attribute-enrichment-annotation
skills.search_text: cluster-attribute-enrichment-annotation Use when RCC_clus has produced recursive consensus cluster assignments and you must validate clusters against sample metadata (attribute columns with a minSample cutoff) or assign subtype labels to clusters. Clusters have not yet been generated — run RCC_clus with the package config_file first, since clusterAttr and clusterAnnotation operate on RCC cluster assignments. No sample attribute metadata is available for comparison — clusterAttr requires an attribute column in the sample info file and a minSample-filtered category. Input is a small dataset with a known number of clusters where recursive subtype discovery offers no added value over a simpler baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Post-clustering characterization steps of the RCC package (clusterAttr and clusterAnnotation) that compare recursive consensus clusters against known sample attributes and annotate biologically meaningful cluster labels (e.g., CT/PAN proneural subdivision in TCGA glioblastoma). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Post-clustering characterization steps of the RCC package (clusterAttr and clusterAnnotation) that compare recursive consensus clusters against known sample attributes and annotate biologically meaningful cluster labels (e.g., CT/PAN proneural subdivision in TCGA glioblastoma).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters have not yet been generated — run RCC_clus with the package config_file first, since clusterAttr and clusterAnnotation operate on RCC cluster assignments. No sample attribute metadata is available for comparison — clusterAttr requires an attribute column in the sample info file and a minSample-filtered category. Input is a small dataset with a known number of clusters where recursive subtype discovery offers no added value over a simpler baseline.

skills.description: Use when constructing a labeled training set from a single-cell expression dataset (Seurat object with log-normalized expression) where rare cell types must be captured and active learning is impractical or no iterative labeling budget exists.
skills.name: cluster-based-adaptive-reweighting-sampling
skills.search_text: cluster-based-adaptive-reweighting-sampling Use when constructing a labeled training set from a single-cell expression dataset (Seurat object with log-normalized expression) where rare cell types must be captured and active learning is impractical or no iterative labeling budget exists. When an iterative labeling budget exists and active learning (maximum-entropy or lowest-max-probability selection of the 10 most uncertain cells) is feasible — active learning outperformed adaptive reweighting across most datasets in the benchmark When the input Seurat object has not been log-normalized and had variable features scaled — leader requires this preprocessing and unique cell IDs in meta.data When reliable marker knowledge exists and the goal is strictly maximizing accuracy — the article shows prior marker knowledge improves annotation accuracy, so marker-informed strategies may be preferable http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A heuristic cell-selection method (implemented in the leader R package) that clusters all cells with Seurat and samples equal numbers of cells from each cluster to build balanced single-cell training sets, optionally using marker genes to assign clusters to putative cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: A heuristic cell-selection method (implemented in the leader R package) that clusters all cells with Seurat and samples equal numbers of cells from each cluster to build balanced single-cell training sets, optionally using marker genes to assign clusters to putative cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When an iterative labeling budget exists and active learning (maximum-entropy or lowest-max-probability selection of the 10 most uncertain cells) is feasible — active learning outperformed adaptive reweighting across most datasets in the benchmark When the input Seurat object has not been log-normalized and had variable features scaled — leader requires this preprocessing and unique cell IDs in meta.data When reliable marker knowledge exists and the goal is strictly maximizing accuracy — the article shows prior marker knowledge improves annotation accuracy, so marker-informed strategies may be preferable

skills.description: Use when scATOMIC has annotated cells as cancer at the terminal layer but normal cells from the cancer's tissue of origin may be present in the tumour biopsy and must be distinguished from true malignant cells.
skills.name: cluster-based-malignant-cell-refinement
skills.search_text: cluster-based-malignant-cell-refinement Use when scATOMIC has annotated cells as cancer at the terminal layer but normal cells from the cancer's tissue of origin may be present in the tumour biopsy and must be distinguished from true malignant cells. Running on normal (non-cancer) tissue samples — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present in the biopsy; use the normal_tissue parameter instead Datasets pooling cells across multiple patients/biopsies — inter-patient cancer cell-specific effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring module and classification confidence Scoring cells that were not annotated as cancer at the terminal layer — the up-/down-regulated program scoring applies only to cells that received an original cancer-type annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A scATOMIC post-processing module that separates malignant cells from non-malignant tissue-specific cells sharing the same tissue of origin, by scoring cancer-type-specific transcriptional programs and iteratively refining clusters until normal-cell contamination is minimal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: A scATOMIC post-processing module that separates malignant cells from non-malignant tissue-specific cells sharing the same tissue of origin, by scoring cancer-type-specific transcriptional programs and iteratively refining clusters until normal-cell contamination is minimal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running on normal (non-cancer) tissue samples — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present in the biopsy; use the normal_tissue parameter instead Datasets pooling cells across multiple patients/biopsies — inter-patient cancer cell-specific effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring module and classification confidence Scoring cells that were not annotated as cancer at the terminal layer — the up-/down-regulated program scoring applies only to cells that received an original cancer-type annotation

skills.description: Use when you have clustering assignments for single-cell data plus a low-dimensional cell embedding and need to build the tree-shaped trajectory backbone (MST over clusters) for topology estimation, as in Totem's cell-connectivity-guided trajectory inference.
skills.name: cluster-based-minimum-spanning-tree-inference
skills.search_text: cluster-based-minimum-spanning-tree-inference Use when you have clustering assignments for single-cell data plus a low-dimensional cell embedding and need to build the tree-shaped trajectory backbone (MST over clusters) for topology estimation, as in Totem's cell-connectivity-guided trajectory inference. The dataset is expected to contain a disconnected trajectory or trajectories with cycles — Totem (and hence this MST-backbone construction) cannot generate those You need correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime and a manual work-around is required The clustering assignments contain extremely small clusters (below min.cluster.size, default 5 cells); such clusterings should be filtered out before MST construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs the per-clustering minimum spanning tree (MST) module of Totem: each cluster becomes a graph vertex at its centroid, and pairwise between-cluster distances are computed with Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like distance before an MST is estimated over the cluster-vertex distance matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Reconstructs the per-clustering minimum spanning tree (MST) module of Totem: each cluster becomes a graph vertex at its centroid, and pairwise between-cluster distances are computed with Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like distance before an MST is estimated over the cluster-vertex distance matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is expected to contain a disconnected trajectory or trajectories with cycles — Totem (and hence this MST-backbone construction) cannot generate those You need correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime and a manual work-around is required The clustering assignments contain extremely small clusters (below min.cluster.size, default 5 cells); such clusterings should be filtered out before MST construction

skills.description: Use when a marker-count-based identification run leaves many cells unassigned after rejection, and you want to reassign them cluster-wise before finalizing cell type labels.
skills.name: cluster-basis-cell-type-reassignment
skills.search_text: cluster-basis-cell-type-reassignment Use when a marker-count-based identification run leaves many cells unassigned after rejection, and you want to reassign them cluster-wise before finalizing cell type labels. When expression data are not well clustered — the paper notes proper identification requires each cell population to be well clustered, which is not always the case When the goal is plain marker counting without a rejection/reassignment stage (e.g., marker-based HiCAT-style hierarchical annotation), since this skill specifically targets cells left unassigned by the rejection threshold When cell types are not clearly separable sub-populations (e.g., monocytes, macrophage, dendritic cells), which the discussion flags as requiring further study http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 MarkerCount's post-rejection step that reassigns 'unassigned' cells to cell types using similarity within clusters, with a reassignment trigger threshold of 0.8 (portion of unassigned cells), chosen as the best performer over a 0.1–0.9 sweep at 0.1 steps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: MarkerCount's post-rejection step that reassigns 'unassigned' cells to cell types using similarity within clusters, with a reassignment trigger threshold of 0.8 (portion of unassigned cells), chosen as the best performer over a 0.1–0.9 sweep at 0.1 steps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When expression data are not well clustered — the paper notes proper identification requires each cell population to be well clustered, which is not always the case When the goal is plain marker counting without a rejection/reassignment stage (e.g., marker-based HiCAT-style hierarchical annotation), since this skill specifically targets cells left unassigned by the rejection threshold When cell types are not clearly separable sub-populations (e.g., monocytes, macrophage, dendritic cells), which the discussion flags as requiring further study

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq matrix has known cell-type or technical-replicate labels (e.g. LC.PT vs LC.PT_RE) and you need to test whether clusters separate by batch or biology after a correction method (ccRemover, scLVM) has been applied.
skills.name: cluster-celltype-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: cluster-celltype-composition-analysis Use when a scRNA-Seq matrix has known cell-type or technical-replicate labels (e.g. LC.PT vs LC.PT_RE) and you need to test whether clusters separate by batch or biology after a correction method (ccRemover, scLVM) has been applied. The cell-cycle activity is at a very low level (e.g. the Patel et al. glioblastoma data), where ccRemover used a smaller cutoff and clustering may be dominated by other effects The goal is cell-type discovery without reference labels — the skill requires known group labels to interpret cluster composition You want to remove batch effects themselves; ccRemover only removes the cell-cycle effect, so clustering may separate on other confounders that remain http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies k-means clustering (e.g. 4-means on the Kim et al. lung adenocarcinoma scRNA-Seq data) to corrected and uncorrected single-cell expression matrices, then cross-tabulates cluster assignments against known cell-type/technical-replicate labels to reveal batch effects or biological structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Applies k-means clustering (e.g. 4-means on the Kim et al. lung adenocarcinoma scRNA-Seq data) to corrected and uncorrected single-cell expression matrices, then cross-tabulates cluster assignments against known cell-type/technical-replicate labels to reveal batch effects or biological structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell-cycle activity is at a very low level (e.g. the Patel et al. glioblastoma data), where ccRemover used a smaller cutoff and clustering may be dominated by other effects The goal is cell-type discovery without reference labels — the skill requires known group labels to interpret cluster composition You want to remove batch effects themselves; ccRemover only removes the cell-cycle effect, so clustering may separate on other confounders that remain

skills.description: Use when you have an embedded single-cell dataset (e.g., a 20-dim scGAE latent representation) with known cell-type/population labels and need to verify that known transcriptionally related populations (e.g., activated vs quiescent stellate cells, ductal subtypes) remain at short centroid distances.
skills.name: cluster-centroid-distance-analysis
skills.search_text: cluster-centroid-distance-analysis Use when you have an embedded single-cell dataset (e.g., a 20-dim scGAE latent representation) with known cell-type/population labels and need to verify that known transcriptionally related populations (e.g., activated vs quiescent stellate cells, ductal subtypes) remain at short centroid distances. When the goal is only 2D visual inspection of clusters — scGAE embeds to an intermediate dimension and uses tSNE for 2D plots because 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder', so 2D coordinates should not be used for centroid-distance quantification When no reliable population/cluster labels are available — centroids require assigning each cell to a population (e.g., Louvain-derived centers or the 14 known Baron populations) When the embedding method does not claim topology preservation (e.g., PCA/tSNE alone) — the short-distance relationships this analysis checks were demonstrated for scGAE, and competing methods projected ductal subtypes far apart http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify inter-population topological structure preserved by a low-dimensional embedding by computing per-cluster centroids (e.g., the 14 Baron pancreatic cell populations in a 20-dimensional scGAE latent space) and all pairwise Euclidean centroid distances, then checking that transcriptionally similar populations sit at short distances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Quantify inter-population topological structure preserved by a low-dimensional embedding by computing per-cluster centroids (e.g., the 14 Baron pancreatic cell populations in a 20-dimensional scGAE latent space) and all pairwise Euclidean centroid distances, then checking that transcriptionally similar populations sit at short distances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only 2D visual inspection of clusters — scGAE embeds to an intermediate dimension and uses tSNE for 2D plots because 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder', so 2D coordinates should not be used for centroid-distance quantification When no reliable population/cluster labels are available — centroids require assigning each cell to a population (e.g., Louvain-derived centers or the 14 known Baron populations) When the embedding method does not claim topology preservation (e.g., PCA/tSNE alone) — the short-distance relationships this analysis checks were demonstrated for scGAE, and competing methods projected ductal subtypes far apart

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix from a prior clustering step must be paired with per-cell class labels and preprocessed (normalization, correlation transformation, feature selection) before a class-informed 2D embedding.
skills.name: cluster-class-assignment-preprocessing
skills.search_text: cluster-class-assignment-preprocessing Use when a single-cell expression matrix from a prior clustering step must be paired with per-cell class labels and preprocessed (normalization, correlation transformation, feature selection) before a class-informed 2D embedding. When no prior cluster assignment exists — GraphDDP starts from a user-defined cluster assignment and cannot be run without the target CSV When the goal is an unsupervised visualization (plain t-SNE, PCA, MDS) that ignores class information rather than a class-informed embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prepare prior class knowledge (cluster assignments from RaceID3 or similar clustering) and the single-cell expression matrix as CSV inputs for the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed supervised graph-embedding, applying normalization, correlation transformation, and discriminative feature selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Prepare prior class knowledge (cluster assignments from RaceID3 or similar clustering) and the single-cell expression matrix as CSV inputs for the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed supervised graph-embedding, applying normalization, correlation transformation, and discriminative feature selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior cluster assignment exists — GraphDDP starts from a user-defined cluster assignment and cannot be run without the target CSV When the goal is an unsupervised visualization (plain t-SNE, PCA, MDS) that ignores class information rather than a class-informed embedding

skills.description: Use when scoring how reproducibly a reference single-cell cluster is reconstructed across multiple SCA clustering runs, or when validating SCA model stability with QCC/QCM against the 0.5 threshold.
skills.name: cluster-colocalization-quality-scoring
skills.search_text: cluster-colocalization-quality-scoring Use when scoring how reproducibly a reference single-cell cluster is reconstructed across multiple SCA clustering runs, or when validating SCA model stability with QCC/QCM against the 0.5 threshold. Input is a raw UMI count matrix (e.g., an inDrop or Cell Ranger counts table) rather than cluster-assignment labels from SCA runs — filtering/counting steps like filterZeros or lorenzFilter apply first Only a single deterministic clustering result is available, since QCC/QCM require multiple SCA runs to measure co-localization and consistency The goal is functional annotation of clusters (TFs, miRNAs, kinases driving clusterization) rather than quantifying reconstruction robustness http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Implements the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics from the SCA/rCASC paper to quantify how well the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder reconstructs valuable cell clusters and how consistent its neural network results are across runs, with QCC and QCM >= 0.5 defining a cluster explainable by SCA analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Implements the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics from the SCA/rCASC paper to quantify how well the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder reconstructs valuable cell clusters and how consistent its neural network results are across runs, with QCC and QCM >= 0.5 defining a cluster explainable by SCA analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw UMI count matrix (e.g., an inDrop or Cell Ranger counts table) rather than cluster-assignment labels from SCA runs — filtering/counting steps like filterZeros or lorenzFilter apply first Only a single deterministic clustering result is available, since QCC/QCM require multiple SCA runs to measure co-localization and consistency The goal is functional annotation of clusters (TFs, miRNAs, kinases driving clusterization) rather than quantifying reconstruction robustness

skills.description: Use when you must decide whether a dimension-reduced embedding (e.g., UMAP, PCA, t-SNE) is suitable as input to trajectory/pseudotime inference in scRNA-seq data, and specifically need to detect clusters that become disconnected or small clusters that group unexpectedly in the embedding.
skills.name: cluster-connectivity-disconnectedness-evaluation
skills.search_text: cluster-connectivity-disconnectedness-evaluation Use when you must decide whether a dimension-reduced embedding (e.g., UMAP, PCA, t-SNE) is suitable as input to trajectory/pseudotime inference in scRNA-seq data, and specifically need to detect clusters that become disconnected or small clusters that group unexpectedly in the embedding. The downstream trajectory inference method does not operate on two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations, and methods outside this restriction require further evaluation. The goal is to evaluate RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction methods, which are not yet implemented in Escort (future work). An embedding has already passed trajectory-specific scoring and you only need pseudotime ordering (e.g., Slingshot/Monocle3 estimation) rather than connectivity pre-screening. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates whether cell clusters in a 2D embedding (e.g., UMAP of normalized scRNA-seq data) remain connected, using per-cell within/between-cluster Manhattan distance distributions and a Jaccard index test with a 0.3 cutoff, so that embeddings exhibiting disconnected clusters are immediately excluded from trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Evaluates whether cell clusters in a 2D embedding (e.g., UMAP of normalized scRNA-seq data) remain connected, using per-cell within/between-cluster Manhattan distance distributions and a Jaccard index test with a 0.3 cutoff, so that embeddings exhibiting disconnected clusters are immediately excluded from trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream trajectory inference method does not operate on two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations, and methods outside this restriction require further evaluation. The goal is to evaluate RNA velocity-derived dimension reduction methods, which are not yet implemented in Escort (future work). An embedding has already passed trajectory-specific scoring and you only need pseudotime ordering (e.g., Slingshot/Monocle3 estimation) rather than connectivity pre-screening.

skills.description: Use when a cells × genes scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the bundled 1%Jurkat.h5 with 1540 293T + 16 Jurkat cells) is suspected to contain rare cell populations that one-time clustering may overlook, and you need rare sub-cluster labels, independence scores, and candidate DE genes.
skills.name: cluster-decomposition-anomaly-detection
skills.search_text: cluster-decomposition-anomaly-detection Use when a cells × genes scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the bundled 1%Jurkat.h5 with 1540 293T + 16 Jurkat cells) is suspected to contain rare cell populations that one-time clustering may overlook, and you need rare sub-cluster labels, independence scores, and candidate DE genes. The goal is comprehensive annotation of all major cell types — the paper positions scCAD as a specialized rare-cell method complementing comprehensive tools like Seurat, not a replacement. The input is a genes × cells matrix or a precomputed feature/clustering table rather than a cells × genes expression matrix — the README specifies 'genes in columns and cells in rows'. skills.summary: Identifies per-cluster marker gene sets from log-cpm normalised single-cell RNA-seq data with tentative Leiden cluster labels, as the first step of the Cytocipher pipeline for detecting significantly different cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts that have not been log-cpm normalised via the scanpy standard workflow — Cytocipher expects normalised data with tentative cluster labels already present The goal is final cell-type annotation on a well-resolved, non-over-clustered labelling — high-resolution Leiden over-clustering is deliberately preferred as Cytocipher input Data is not scRNA-seq with cluster labels (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a pre-computed feature table), where per-cell code scoring is not applicable
