skills.search_text: cluster-marker-set-interpretation Use when a scdrake pipeline run has produced per-cluster marker-gene tables and you need downstream biological interpretation of those marker sets via gene set enrichment (GO/KEGG) rather than plain marker lists. Your goal is within the standard scdrake scope (QC, filtering, normalization, HVG detection, dimensionality reduction, clustering, cell type annotation, marker detection, contrasts) — these are already provided by the released pipeline without an extension plan Input is not a cluster-level marker-gene set (e.g. you want single-cell-level scoring or differential expression between clusters, i.e. scdrake 'contrasts' — use the built-in contrast module instead) The organism of your data is not covered by the OrgDb configured in the main config (e.g. non-human data with ORGANISM: "human"), making symbol-to-ENTREZ mapping unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets per-cluster marker-gene sets from the scdrake scRNA-seq pipeline by running GO and KEGG over-representation enrichment per cluster and compiling results into a CSV table plus a standalone HTML report styled like scdrake's existing stage reports. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad089
skills.summary: Interprets per-cluster marker-gene sets from the scdrake scRNA-seq pipeline by running GO and KEGG over-representation enrichment per cluster and compiling results into a CSV table plus a standalone HTML report styled like scdrake's existing stage reports.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is within the standard scdrake scope (QC, filtering, normalization, HVG detection, dimensionality reduction, clustering, cell type annotation, marker detection, contrasts) — these are already provided by the released pipeline without an extension plan Input is not a cluster-level marker-gene set (e.g. you want single-cell-level scoring or differential expression between clusters, i.e. scdrake 'contrasts' — use the built-in contrast module instead) The organism of your data is not covered by the OrgDb configured in the main config (e.g. non-human data with ORGANISM: "human"), making symbol-to-ENTREZ mapping unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have a TPM/CPM-normalized reference gene expression matrix with known cluster labels and need cluster-specific marker gene sets (e.g., via find_markers with logFC 0.6) to score or map target cells.
skills.name: cluster-marker-signature-extraction
skills.search_text: cluster-marker-signature-extraction Use when you have a TPM/CPM-normalized reference gene expression matrix with known cluster labels and need cluster-specific marker gene sets (e.g., via find_markers with logFC 0.6) to score or map target cells. Input gene expression is log-transformed rather than TPM/CPM library-depth normalized — the article states this is not compatible with scID marker/weight estimation. The reference dataset is not well clustered and lacks good gene signatures — the paper warns scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types in that case. You only need final target-cell labels via a full one-call mapping; then scid_multiclass(target_gem, reference_gem, reference_clusters, ...) internally handles signature extraction and marker output. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts cluster-specific gene signatures (differentially expressed positive and negative markers) from a clustered reference scRNA-seq gene expression matrix, as the first stage of the scID Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like cell-mapping pipeline. Signatures and their logFC thresholds feed downstream discriminative weight estimation (choose_training_set / scID_weight). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Extracts cluster-specific gene signatures (differentially expressed positive and negative markers) from a clustered reference scRNA-seq gene expression matrix, as the first stage of the scID Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like cell-mapping pipeline. Signatures and their logFC thresholds feed downstream discriminative weight estimation (choose_training_set / scID_weight).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene expression is log-transformed rather than TPM/CPM library-depth normalized — the article states this is not compatible with scID marker/weight estimation. The reference dataset is not well clustered and lacks good gene signatures — the paper warns scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types in that case. You only need final target-cell labels via a full one-call mapping; then scid_multiclass(target_gem, reference_gem, reference_clusters, ...) internally handles signature extraction and marker output.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq (E) and scATAC-seq (O) matrices from the same heterogeneous population already carry cell-cluster labels and a bulk data type (e.g., HiChIP loop counts) must be seeded with per-cluster mean profiles before deconvolution.
skills.name: cluster-mean-subpopulation-profiling
skills.search_text: cluster-mean-subpopulation-profiling Use when scRNA-seq (E) and scATAC-seq (O) matrices from the same heterogeneous population already carry cell-cluster labels and a bulk data type (e.g., HiChIP loop counts) must be seeded with per-cluster mean profiles before deconvolution. Single-cell samples are jointly profiled (e.g., sci-CAR-style multi-ome): the article defers incorporating such data types to future work, so cluster-mean seeding across separate samples is not the right setup No bulk data type is available to deconvolve — if all data types are already at single-cell resolution, per-cluster means are unnecessary and discard single-cell resolution A fully data-driven coupled clustering is required from scratch rather than seeding from pre-assigned cluster labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-subpopulation mean profiles (e.g., expression matrix P1 from scRNA-seq and accessibility matrix P2 from scATAC-seq) by averaging single cells sharing a cluster label, then uses multinomial proportions rho_ijk = sqrt(O_ik * O_jk) / sum_k sqrt(O_ik * O_jk) to initialize latent loop counts for deconvolving bulk HiChIP into subpopulation-specific signals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Computes per-subpopulation mean profiles (e.g., expression matrix P1 from scRNA-seq and accessibility matrix P2 from scATAC-seq) by averaging single cells sharing a cluster label, then uses multinomial proportions rho_ijk = sqrt(O_ik * O_jk) / sum_k sqrt(O_ik * O_jk) to initialize latent loop counts for deconvolving bulk HiChIP into subpopulation-specific signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell samples are jointly profiled (e.g., sci-CAR-style multi-ome): the article defers incorporating such data types to future work, so cluster-mean seeding across separate samples is not the right setup No bulk data type is available to deconvolve — if all data types are already at single-cell resolution, per-cluster means are unnecessary and discard single-cell resolution A fully data-driven coupled clustering is required from scratch rather than seeding from pre-assigned cluster labels

skills.description: Use when a source-regularized NMF has produced soft cluster coefficients W_trg for target cells and the transfer-learning construction of X_trg_new requires hard one-hot cluster memberships per cell.
skills.name: cluster-membership-argmax-thresholding
skills.search_text: cluster-membership-argmax-thresholding Use when a source-regularized NMF has produced soft cluster coefficients W_trg for target cells and the transfer-learning construction of X_trg_new requires hard one-hot cluster memberships per cell. The target coefficient matrix W_trg has not yet been learned against the source dictionary H_src — argmax thresholding presupposes a source-anchored NMF solution, not raw expression data Source and target only share a small set of transcripts: the paper notes 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only the set of genes present in both datasets can be used' You need soft/probabilistic cluster assignments for downstream weighting rather than the hard one-hot memberships required by the X_trg_new convex combination http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts the real-valued NMF coefficient matrix W_trg (k x n_trg) learned for the target scRNA-Seq dataset into a binary cluster-membership matrix W'_trg in {0,1}^(k x n_trg) by placing a single 1 at each column's argmax. This hardened matrix is then mixed back into the target data via X_trg_new = theta * H_src * W'_trg + (1 - theta) * X_trg before SC3 clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Converts the real-valued NMF coefficient matrix W_trg (k x n_trg) learned for the target scRNA-Seq dataset into a binary cluster-membership matrix W'_trg in {0,1}^(k x n_trg) by placing a single 1 at each column's argmax. This hardened matrix is then mixed back into the target data via X_trg_new = theta * H_src * W'_trg + (1 - theta) * X_trg before SC3 clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target coefficient matrix W_trg has not yet been learned against the source dictionary H_src — argmax thresholding presupposes a source-anchored NMF solution, not raw expression data Source and target only share a small set of transcripts: the paper notes 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only the set of genes present in both datasets can be used' You need soft/probabilistic cluster assignments for downstream weighting rather than the hard one-hot memberships required by the X_trg_new convex combination

skills.description: Use when a SINCERA clustering run (hierarchical average/ward linkage, consensus, or tight clustering) on z-scored cell type-selective genes needs a significance check before cell type labels are finalized.
skills.name: cluster-membership-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: cluster-membership-permutation-testing Use when a SINCERA clustering run (hierarchical average/ward linkage, consensus, or tight clustering) on z-scored cell type-selective genes needs a significance check before cell type labels are finalized. Cells have not yet been assigned to clusters — cluster.permutation.analysis operates on an existing cluster.assignment result, so run gene selection (cluster.geneSelection) and cluster.assignment first The expression matrix has not been z-score transformed and filtered for expression selectivity — significance testing on unnormalized or non-selective gene sets conflates clustering quality with preprocessing artifacts Goal is differential expression or gene signature analysis rather than judging cluster quality — SINCERA handles those as separate downstream steps after cell types are defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assess the statistical significance of scRNA-Seq cell clusters produced by SINCERA's cluster.assignment step by permuting cluster memberships, so that a clustering scheme (e.g., average-linkage, ward, consensus, or tight clustering on z-scored cell type-selective genes) is only accepted when permutation analysis supports it. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Assess the statistical significance of scRNA-Seq cell clusters produced by SINCERA's cluster.assignment step by permuting cluster memberships, so that a clustering scheme (e.g., average-linkage, ward, consensus, or tight clustering on z-scored cell type-selective genes) is only accepted when permutation analysis supports it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have not yet been assigned to clusters — cluster.permutation.analysis operates on an existing cluster.assignment result, so run gene selection (cluster.geneSelection) and cluster.assignment first The expression matrix has not been z-score transformed and filtered for expression selectivity — significance testing on unnormalized or non-selective gene sets conflates clustering quality with preprocessing artifacts Goal is differential expression or gene signature analysis rather than judging cluster quality — SINCERA handles those as separate downstream steps after cell types are defined

skills.name: cluster-membership-table-export
skills.search_text: cluster-membership-table-export Use when you have a candidate L-R pair expression-change matrix from dsCellNet's developcorrelation DTW step for a developmental series (e.g. GSE153164 corticogenesis) and need to partition L-R pairs into time-point-specific clusters and write out per-cluster gene lists. Input is a single-time-point expression dataset with no developmental series time information, since DTW-based expression changes and temporal cluster assignment are not applicable You need a single static cell-cell interaction map rather than time-resolved clustering of L-R interactions; dsCellNet is designed for developmental series RNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering on the dsCellNet developmental-series L-R interaction expression-change matrix (eight clusters, fuzzifier estimated with mestimate) and export the full membership/assignment table, e.g. mfuzz_cluster_assignments.csv, so that downstream GO enrichment can be run on per-cluster gene lists such as the E12.5 cluster 1 L-R genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Run Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering on the dsCellNet developmental-series L-R interaction expression-change matrix (eight clusters, fuzzifier estimated with mestimate) and export the full membership/assignment table, e.g. mfuzz_cluster_assignments.csv, so that downstream GO enrichment can be run on per-cluster gene lists such as the E12.5 cluster 1 L-R genes.

skills.name: cluster-membership-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: cluster-membership-threshold-filtering Use when temporal expression changes of candidate interactions (e.g., L-R pairs) must be partitioned into soft clusters and only high-confidence core members of each cluster are needed to call peak time points. When only hard/unique cluster assignment is needed and soft membership values carry no downstream meaning — a standard k-means clustering would suffice instead of Mfuzz fuzzy c-means. When the expression data are from a single stationary condition rather than a developmental series — dynamic time warping and temporal fuzzy clustering in dsCellNet assume ordered time points. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Apply fuzzy c-means clustering (Mfuzz) to standardized developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pairs and retain only core cluster members at a membership >= 0.6 threshold, as used in dsCellNet to resolve temporal clusters across GSE153164 corticogenesis time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Apply fuzzy c-means clustering (Mfuzz) to standardized developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pairs and retain only core cluster members at a membership >= 0.6 threshold, as used in dsCellNet to resolve temporal clusters across GSE153164 corticogenesis time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only hard/unique cluster assignment is needed and soft membership values carry no downstream meaning — a standard k-means clustering would suffice instead of Mfuzz fuzzy c-means. When the expression data are from a single stationary condition rather than a developmental series — dynamic time warping and temporal fuzzy clustering in dsCellNet assume ordered time points.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data is log-cpm normalised with high-resolution Leiden over-clusters and you must decide which clusters are significantly different versus which should be merged.
skills.name: cluster-merge-significance-testing
skills.search_text: cluster-merge-significance-testing Use when scRNA-seq data is log-cpm normalised with high-resolution Leiden over-clusters and you must decide which clusters are significantly different versus which should be merged. Input data lacks tentative cluster labels or has not been log-cpm normalised via the scanpy standard workflow — Cytocipher expects over-clustered, normalised AnnData Clusters are already known to be biologically distinct and no significance testing of merges is needed (the method is for resolving over-clustering, not de novo clustering) The goal is scoring cell-cluster membership alone; use cc.tl.code_enrich / benchmark scoring methods (Giotto PAGE, Scanpy scoring) rather than the merge-testing workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Statistically tests whether over-clustered Leiden groups in scRNA-seq data are significantly different and merges non-significant clusters using Cytocipher, recovering biologically meaningful populations (e.g. CD8+ T cell subtypes, pancreas intermediate states). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Statistically tests whether over-clustered Leiden groups in scRNA-seq data are significantly different and merges non-significant clusters using Cytocipher, recovering biologically meaningful populations (e.g. CD8+ T cell subtypes, pancreas intermediate states).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks tentative cluster labels or has not been log-cpm normalised via the scanpy standard workflow — Cytocipher expects over-clustered, normalised AnnData Clusters are already known to be biologically distinct and no significance testing of merges is needed (the method is for resolving over-clustering, not de novo clustering) The goal is scoring cell-cluster membership alone; use cc.tl.code_enrich / benchmark scoring methods (Giotto PAGE, Scanpy scoring) rather than the merge-testing workflow

skills.name: cluster-metric-computation-ami-ari
skills.search_text: cluster-metric-computation-ami-ari Use when you need to quantify how well predicted single-cell profiles (e.g., ADT from consecutive epigenome→transcriptome→proteome translation) preserve cell-type structure, comparing methods via AMI/ARI/HOM/NMI. You need to generate translated profiles itself — this skill only scores clustering concordance of already-predicted profiles, not the translation (use train_model/train_model_cite/Model.test first). Your evaluation target is per-feature reconstruction accuracy (e.g., correlation of predicted gene/protein values) rather than cell-type clustering concordance. Input profiles span novel cell types or cross-organ settings the article flags as needing improvement — clustering scores there may reflect known scButterfly weaknesses rather than pipeline errors. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores single-cell cross-modality translation quality by computing AMI, ARI, HOM, and NMI clustering concordance of predicted profiles (e.g., ADT translated from scATAC-seq via chained scButterfly translators) against ground-truth cell-type labels and baseline predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data where the true number of cell types is unknown, or when benchmarking how accurately clustering methods (e.g., CASCC vs. SC3) recover K against annotated ground-truth cell-type labels.
skills.name: cluster-number-estimation
skills.search_text: cluster-number-estimation Use when clustering scRNA-seq data where the true number of cell types is unknown, or when benchmarking how accurately clustering methods (e.g., CASCC vs. SC3) recover K against annotated ground-truth cell-type labels. K is already fixed a priori and you only need a final clustering — use kmeansCenterModify / run.kmeans.fixCenters directly instead of predictClusterK Data is raw counts that have not been normalized and log-transformed — CASCC expects 'well-normalized' input for feature selection before K prediction The dataset is so large that dependency methods fail — e.g., SIMLR exited with out-of-memory errors on 5,000–30,000-cell Tabula Sapiens datasets and was excluded from the large-scale comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Estimate the number of cell types (K) in scRNA-seq data by running CASCC's predictClusterK over attractor-based co-expression features (Ward.D2 hierarchical linkage with silhouette index), then quantify estimation accuracy against ground-truth cell-type labels using absolute log-modulus |log2(K_gen/K_true)| and deviation (K_gen - K_true) scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae283
skills.summary: Estimate the number of cell types (K) in scRNA-seq data by running CASCC's predictClusterK over attractor-based co-expression features (Ward.D2 hierarchical linkage with silhouette index), then quantify estimation accuracy against ground-truth cell-type labels using absolute log-modulus |log2(K_gen/K_true)| and deviation (K_gen - K_true) scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: K is already fixed a priori and you only need a final clustering — use kmeansCenterModify / run.kmeans.fixCenters directly instead of predictClusterK Data is raw counts that have not been normalized and log-transformed — CASCC expects 'well-normalized' input for feature selection before K prediction The dataset is so large that dependency methods fail — e.g., SIMLR exited with out-of-memory errors on 5,000–30,000-cell Tabula Sapiens datasets and was excluded from the large-scale comparison

skills.description: Use when tuning the α parameter of hybrid clone/transcriptome clustering (e.g., ClonoCluster) and you need a data-driven cutoff for how much clone information can be injected before cluster number balloons beyond the transcriptome-only baseline.
skills.name: cluster-number-inflection-detection
skills.search_text: cluster-number-inflection-detection Use when tuning the α parameter of hybrid clone/transcriptome clustering (e.g., ClonoCluster) and you need a data-driven cutoff for how much clone information can be injected before cluster number balloons beyond the transcriptome-only baseline. You have no clonal barcode data and are only choosing a Seurat/scanpy resolution — standard resolution tuning applies, not α inflection scanning Your goal is to force a specific number of hybrid clusters regardless of transcriptome-cluster comparability — the inflection rule intentionally caps α to keep cluster counts comparable to transcriptome-only clustering You need full-lineage/phylogenetic weighting (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees), which the paper explicitly did not address http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A calibration procedure from the ClonoCluster paper that determines the maximum ('high') α weighting of clone-versus-transcriptome edges by plotting the number of clusters returned at each α and selecting the value just before cluster counts inflect upward, keeping hybrid clusters comparable to transcriptome-only cluster counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247

skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no clonal barcode data and are only choosing a Seurat/scanpy resolution — standard resolution tuning applies, not α inflection scanning Your goal is to force a specific number of hybrid clusters regardless of transcriptome-cluster comparability — the inflection rule intentionally caps α to keep cluster counts comparable to transcriptome-only clustering You need full-lineage/phylogenetic weighting (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees), which the paper explicitly did not address

skills.description: Use when clustering PCA-reduced single-cell expression data (e.g., scSPARKL-normalized wide-format matrices in Parquet/CSV) and you need to justify k via elbow (WCSS) and silhouette criteria before downstream per-cluster DGE t-tests.
skills.name: cluster-number-selection-elbow-silhouette
skills.search_text: cluster-number-selection-elbow-silhouette Use when clustering PCA-reduced single-cell expression data (e.g., scSPARKL-normalized wide-format matrices in Parquet/CSV) and you need to justify k via elbow (WCSS) and silhouette criteria before downstream per-cluster DGE t-tests. Input is a raw, high-dimensional expression matrix that has not been normalized or PCA-reduced — elbow/silhouette on unnormalized, dropout-heavy scRNA-seq data is unreliable; run scSPARKL normalization and PCA first You need graph/community-based clustering (e.g., Louvain/Leiden as in Seurat or Scanpy) rather than K-means with a globally fixed k The dataset has no plausible range of cluster numbers (e.g., a single homogeneous population), making elbow/silhouette selection meaningless Selects the number of K-means clusters (k) for single-cell RNA-seq data by computing within-cluster sum of squares (elbow plot) and silhouette scores across candidate k values on PCA-reduced data, as implemented in the Spark-based scSPARKL pipeline. Validated on the Jurkat–293T cell mixture where k=2 recovers human vs mouse separation with ARI ≈ 0.90. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: Selects the number of K-means clusters (k) for single-cell RNA-seq data by computing within-cluster sum of squares (elbow plot) and silhouette scores across candidate k values on PCA-reduced data, as implemented in the Spark-based scSPARKL pipeline. Validated on the Jurkat–293T cell mixture where k=2 recovers human vs mouse separation with ARI ≈ 0.90.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw, high-dimensional expression matrix that has not been normalized or PCA-reduced — elbow/silhouette on unnormalized, dropout-heavy scRNA-seq data is unreliable; run scSPARKL normalization and PCA first You need graph/community-based clustering (e.g., Louvain/Leiden as in Seurat or Scanpy) rather than K-means with a globally fixed k The dataset has no plausible range of cluster numbers (e.g., a single homogeneous population), making elbow/silhouette selection meaningless

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters (e.g., Seurat Louvain clusters) and you need per-cluster overexpressed genes to feed NicheNet-style ligand-receptor interaction scoring between sender and receiver clusters.
skills.name: cluster-overexpressed-gene-identification
skills.search_text: cluster-overexpressed-gene-identification Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters (e.g., Seurat Louvain clusters) and you need per-cluster overexpressed genes to feed NicheNet-style ligand-receptor interaction scoring between sender and receiver clusters. The data has not yet been SiFT-filtered against the healthy reference — purity on the original (unfiltered) neighborhood structure fails to expose the relevant cell types and should not be interpreted as informativeness The goal is removal of unwanted variation (e.g. cell cycle, sex, batch) rather than identifying disease-informative cells via a reference trajectory No reference samples or prior mapping exist to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — SiFT filtering and downstream purity classification both depend on it http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classifies individual cells as disease-informative vs non-informative by scoring neighborhood cluster purity on a kNN graph built from SiFT-filtered expression data (healthy reference signal removed) and thresholding purity at tau = 0.55, then aggregating informative labels per annotated cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering partition must be judged for homogeneity — e.g. to decide whether a cluster needs re-clustering, to verify purity of identified subtypes (ROGUE > 0.92 threshold), or to assess purity loss from batch aggregation.
skills.name: cluster-purity-quantification
skills.search_text: cluster-purity-quantification Use when a scRNA-seq clustering partition must be judged for homogeneity — e.g. to decide whether a cluster needs re-clustering, to verify purity of identified subtypes (ROGUE > 0.92 threshold), or to assess purity loss from batch aggregation. Assessing purity of cell populations integrated from different protocols/platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not yet support this Low-quality or continuous datasets where the 0.9 threshold is inappropriate — the threshold must instead be determined from global ROGUE values Selecting rare cell types from raw data alone (use GiniClust-type methods); ROGUE quantifies purity of already-defined clusters rather than performing the initial rare-type detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantify the purity/homogeneity of single-cell clusters using ROGUE (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy), an entropy-based statistic that measures the randomness of gene expression while accounting for technical factors, enabling detection of low-purity clusters and discovery of pure subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Quantify the purity/homogeneity of single-cell clusters using ROGUE (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy), an entropy-based statistic that measures the randomness of gene expression while accounting for technical factors, enabling detection of low-purity clusters and discovery of pure subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assessing purity of cell populations integrated from different protocols/platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not yet support this Low-quality or continuous datasets where the 0.9 threshold is inappropriate — the threshold must instead be determined from global ROGUE values Selecting rare cell types from raw data alone (use GiniClust-type methods); ROGUE quantifies purity of already-defined clusters rather than performing the initial rare-type detection

skills.search_text: cluster-purity-score-computation Use when you have predicted cluster labels plus reference labels used for data generation and need a single score per method to rank clustering performance, e.g., benchmarking on synthetic ring/half-moon data. No reference labels exist (e.g., purely exploratory clustering of new data) — purity is an external metric requiring ground truth; use internal validation like FFC's cluster_obj.validate(), entropy(), or pval() instead Data are in very high dimensions without nonlinear dimensionality reduction — FFC clustering that feeds the labels into purity is limited by the curse of dimensionality and should be performed after UMAP/t-SNE/PHATE The clustering produces only one cluster for the whole dataset — every point receives the same label and purity collapses to the majority-class fraction, carrying no cluster-quality signal Computes purity scores that evaluate predicted cluster labels against a set of reference (ground-truth) labels, the primary external-validation metric used to benchmark Forest Fire Clustering (FFC) against KMeans, GaussianMixture, DBSCAN, OPTICS, and SpectralClustering on synthetic Gaussian-mixture, ring-shaped, and half-moon-shaped datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference labels exist (e.g., purely exploratory clustering of new data) — purity is an external metric requiring ground truth; use internal validation like FFC's cluster_obj.validate(), entropy(), or pval() instead Data are in very high dimensions without nonlinear dimensionality reduction — FFC clustering that feeds the labels into purity is limited by the curse of dimensionality and should be performed after UMAP/t-SNE/PHATE The clustering produces only one cluster for the whole dataset — every point receives the same label and purity collapses to the majority-class fraction, carrying no cluster-quality signal

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq clusters have been produced (e.g., by LinQ-View joint, RNA-only, or ADT-only Louvain clustering) and you need a quantitative purity value per cluster in each modality to compare clustering quality.
skills.name: cluster-purity-score-computation
skills.search_text: cluster-purity-score-computation Use when CITE-seq clusters have been produced (e.g., by LinQ-View joint, RNA-only, or ADT-only Louvain clustering) and you need a quantitative purity value per cluster in each modality to compare clustering quality. The dataset is massive with a high number of ADT features — LinQ-View failed on 170K cells with 228 ADT features where Seurat 4 succeeded; LinQ-View is best for large datasets with <50 ADT features The input is single-modality data (scRNA-seq only or flow-like ADT data only) — the purity score is designed for dual transcriptome/surface-protein CITE-seq modalities You need a definitive answer about whether LinQ-View resolved specific modality-exclusive subsets without also running the unimodal RNA and ADT clusterings as comparators http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute LinQ-View's quantitative purity score for every cluster in both the transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities of CITE-seq data, based on the ROGUE concept of examining whether a cluster is a pure cell population. This metric enables objective assessment of cluster homogeneity that unimodal analyses lack. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Compute LinQ-View's quantitative purity score for every cluster in both the transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities of CITE-seq data, based on the ROGUE concept of examining whether a cluster is a pure cell population. skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is massive with a high number of ADT features — LinQ-View failed on 170K cells with 228 ADT features where Seurat 4 succeeded; LinQ-View is best for large datasets with <50 ADT features The input is single-modality data (scRNA-seq only or flow-like ADT data only) — the purity score is designed for dual transcriptome/surface-protein CITE-seq modalities You need a definitive answer about whether LinQ-View resolved specific modality-exclusive subsets without also running the unimodal RNA and ADT clusterings as comparators

skills.description: Use when you need a quantitative purity score for an identified scRNA-seq cell cluster — e.g. to decide whether to re-cluster — from a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix annotated with a platform (droplet or full-length).
skills.name: cluster-purity-statistic-derivation
skills.search_text: cluster-purity-statistic-derivation Use when you need a quantitative purity score for an identified scRNA-seq cell cluster — e.g. to decide whether to re-cluster — from a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix annotated with a platform (droplet or full-length). Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not support this (proposed as future work) Low-quality or continuous data where the 0.9 purity threshold does not apply without considering global ROGUE values Detecting rare cell types or performing the clustering itself — use methods like GiniClust, GiniClust2, or RaceID3/StemID2 instead; ROGUE quantifies purity of already-identified clusters http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derives the ROGUE (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy) cluster-purity statistic by fitting an entropy-based S-E model (LOESS of ln E(X) vs average expression) to a scRNA-seq expression matrix, extracting per-gene entropy-reduction values (ds), and aggregating them as ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K) to quantify whether a cell cluster is a pure population. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Derives the ROGUE (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy) cluster-purity statistic by fitting an entropy-based S-E model (LOESS of ln E(X) vs average expression) to a scRNA-seq expression matrix, extracting per-gene entropy-reduction values (ds), and aggregating them as ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K) to quantify whether a cell cluster is a pure population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not support this (proposed as future work) Low-quality or continuous data where the 0.9 purity threshold does not apply without considering global ROGUE values Detecting rare cell types or performing the clustering itself — use methods like GiniClust, GiniClust2, or RaceID3/StemID2 instead; ROGUE quantifies purity of already-identified clusters

skills.description: Use when you have run Totem's k-medoids (CLARA) clustering many times (default 10,000 runs, k = 3-20) on a low-dimensional embedding and must drop runs that contain clusters with fewer than five cells.
skills.name: cluster-size-filtering
skills.search_text: cluster-size-filtering Use when you have run Totem's k-medoids (CLARA) clustering many times (default 10,000 runs, k = 3-20) on a low-dimensional embedding and must drop runs that contain clusters with fewer than five cells. The clustering batch was generated on high-dimensional PCA input (e.g., 30 principal components) producing many 1-2 cell clusters — filter alone will not fix the underlying k-medoids instability; switch to a lower-dimensional embedding first The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types and you intend to manually merge clusters — min.cluster.size filtering would discard relevant rare-cell clusterings before you can merge them Input is a single clustering result rather than Totem's large batch of CLARA runs; the size filter is designed for the many-runs stage before MST/cell-connectivity ranking Filter the large batch of CLARA k-medoids clusterings generated by Totem so that only clusterings whose every cluster contains at least five cells (min.cluster.size = 5) are retained for downstream MST construction and cell-connectivity scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Filter the large batch of CLARA k-medoids clusterings generated by Totem so that only clusterings whose every cluster contains at least five cells (min.cluster.size = 5) are retained for downstream MST construction and cell-connectivity scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering batch was generated on high-dimensional PCA input (e.g., 30 principal components) producing many 1-2 cell clusters — filter alone will not fix the underlying k-medoids instability; switch to a lower-dimensional embedding first The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types and you intend to manually merge clusters — min.cluster.size filtering would discard relevant rare-cell clusterings before you can merge them Input is a single clustering result rather than Totem's large batch of CLARA runs; the size filter is designed for the many-runs stage before MST/cell-connectivity ranking

skills.name: cluster-size-read-fraction-statistics
skills.search_text: cluster-size-read-fraction-statistics Use when FASTQ-to-SAM UMI pipelines have produced per-position UMI cluster data for one or more UMI-based RNA-Seq datasets and you need to quantify what proportion of reads fall into size-1 clusters versus mapping-shifted clusters. Input data contains no UMIs — the article states 'In the absence of UMI this artefact is undetectable', so cluster-size statistics are undefined The goal is paired-end or splice-aware transcript-level quantification — the pipeline is designed for single-ended sequencing with STAR specifying no introns You need the true biological distribution of mapping-shift sizes — the article notes the 3 bp collapse threshold is arbitrary and the true distribution is unknown http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes how reads are distributed across UMI-read clusters of different sizes (e.g., fraction of reads in size-one clusters versus shifted clusters) pooled per dataset, quantifying the extent of the UMI mapping-shift artefact for RNA-Seq UMI-counting analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-31064-7
skills.summary: Computes how reads are distributed across UMI-read clusters of different sizes (e.g., fraction of reads in size-one clusters versus shifted clusters) pooled per dataset, quantifying the extent of the UMI mapping-shift artefact for RNA-Seq UMI-counting analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data contains no UMIs — the article states 'In the absence of UMI this artefact is undetectable', so cluster-size statistics are undefined The goal is paired-end or splice-aware transcript-level quantification — the pipeline is designed for single-ended sequencing with STAR specifying no introns You need the true biological distribution of mapping-shift sizes — the article notes the 3 bp collapse threshold is arbitrary and the true distribution is unknown

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset has already been QC-filtered, normalized, scaled, and partitioned into Louvain clusters (e.g. PBMC3k via Seurat/SCALA), and per-cluster marker genes ranked by log2FC are needed.
skills.name: cluster-specific-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: cluster-specific-differential-expression-analysis Use when an scRNA-seq dataset has already been QC-filtered, normalized, scaled, and partitioned into Louvain clusters (e.g. PBMC3k via Seurat/SCALA), and per-cluster marker genes ranked by log2FC are needed. Input is raw counts that have not been QC-filtered, normalized and scaled, or cells are not yet assigned Louvain cluster labels — run QC, normalization, PCA/SVD and clustering first The goal is cell-cell communication or ligand-receptor inference rather than per-cluster marker discovery — use a dedicated framework such as NicheNet instead Analysis is on organisms other than human or mouse — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies marker genes characterizing each Louvain cluster of an scRNA-seq dataset by testing each cluster's cells against all remaining cells using the Wilcoxon rank sum test on normalized expression (with MAST and DESeq2 available in Seurat), as implemented in SCALA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Identifies marker genes characterizing each Louvain cluster of an scRNA-seq dataset by testing each cluster's cells against all remaining cells using the Wilcoxon rank sum test on normalized expression (with MAST and DESeq2 available in Seurat), as implemented in SCALA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts that have not been QC-filtered, normalized and scaled, or cells are not yet assigned Louvain cluster labels — run QC, normalization, PCA/SVD and clustering first The goal is cell-cell communication or ligand-receptor inference rather than per-cluster marker discovery — use a dedicated framework such as NicheNet instead Analysis is on organisms other than human or mouse — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse datasets

skills.description: Use when a library-depth-normalized reference scRNA-seq matrix (genes x cells) with cluster labels is available and you need per-cluster marker gene signatures (e.g. logFC >= 0.6) to feed scid_multiclass for cross-dataset cell type mapping.
skills.name: cluster-specific-gene-signature-extraction
skills.search_text: cluster-specific-gene-signature-extraction Use when a library-depth-normalized reference scRNA-seq matrix (genes x cells) with cluster labels is available and you need per-cluster marker gene signatures (e.g. logFC >= 0.6) to feed scid_multiclass for cross-dataset cell type mapping. The reference data are not well clustered and lack good gene signatures — the article states that in this case scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types The input matrix is already log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalization only You only need single known biomarkers to identify cell types — the paper notes biomarker-based identification works poorly owing to the dropout problem in scRNA-seq data, so full cluster-specific signatures (not individual markers) are required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract cluster-specific gene signatures (differentially expressed gene sets) from a reference scRNA-seq dataset with known cluster labels, as the first stage of the scID pipeline for identifying transcriptionally equivalent cells across datasets with batch effect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Extract cluster-specific gene signatures (differentially expressed gene sets) from a reference scRNA-seq dataset with known cluster labels, as the first stage of the scID pipeline for identifying transcriptionally equivalent cells across datasets with batch effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference data are not well clustered and lack good gene signatures — the article states that in this case scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types The input matrix is already log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalization only You only need single known biomarkers to identify cell types — the paper notes biomarker-based identification works poorly owing to the dropout problem in scRNA-seq data, so full cluster-specific signatures (not individual markers) are required

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed Seurat scRNA-seq object must be clustered at an unknown resolution and you need an objective, marker-specificity-based criterion (rather than eyeballing) to pick the configuration that yields the most specific cluster markers before cell-type annotation.
skills.name: cluster-specificity-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: cluster-specificity-curve-analysis Use when a preprocessed Seurat scRNA-seq object must be clustered at an unknown resolution and you need an objective, marker-specificity-based criterion (rather than eyeballing) to pick the configuration that yields the most specific cluster markers before cell-type annotation. The clustering configuration is already fixed and validated (e.g., a published curated annotation you intend to use as-is) — re-optimization is unnecessary The data is a single-replicate dataset where cluster stability/reproducibility is questionable and spurious clusters from artifact genes cannot be distinguished from real biology The goal is cell-type label assignment rather than resolution selection — use the Miko scoring pipeline or sc-type instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the optimal Louvain clustering resolution by sweeping resolutions and, for each configuration, measuring marker specificity via the co-dependency index (CDI); the resolution maximizing the AUC of the specificity curve (termed 'Speak') is chosen as the starting point for annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Selects the optimal Louvain clustering resolution by sweeping resolutions and, for each configuration, measuring marker specificity via the co-dependency index (CDI); the resolution maximizing the AUC of the specificity curve (termed 'Speak') is chosen as the starting point for annotation.

skills.description: Use when clustering transcriptomic (bulk or single-cell) data with an unknown number of clusters and you must algorithmically determine the optimal k and decide when to stop recursive subdivision.
skills.name: cluster-stability-quantification
skills.search_text: cluster-stability-quantification Use when clustering transcriptomic (bulk or single-cell) data with an unknown number of clusters and you must algorithmically determine the optimal k and decide when to stop recursive subdivision. The number of clusters is known beforehand and the goal is only to partition data, not to discover novel subtypes or select k The analysis goal is supervised classification against known annotations rather than unsupervised subtype discovery; RCC targets data with an unknown number of clusters Datasets with millions of cells — the authors note computational time is a limitation tied to the consensus clustering with k-means base algorithm, and large integrated datasets are still a next step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies cluster stability to select the optimal number of clusters (k) during each parallel consensus clustering run of RCC, using empirical CDF plots from ConsensusClusterPlus plus stability, overlap, and differential-expression quality gates, enabling recursive subdivision of transcriptome data into novel subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Quantifies cluster stability to select the optimal number of clusters (k) during each parallel consensus clustering run of RCC, using empirical CDF plots from ConsensusClusterPlus plus stability, overlap, and differential-expression quality gates, enabling recursive subdivision of transcriptome data into novel subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters is known beforehand and the goal is only to partition data, not to discover novel subtypes or select k The analysis goal is supervised classification against known annotations rather than unsupervised subtype discovery; RCC targets data with an unknown number of clusters Datasets with millions of cells — the authors note computational time is a limitation tied to the consensus clustering with k-means base algorithm, and large integrated datasets are still a next step

skills.description: Use when multiple conflicting cell-cluster annotations (e.g. Leiden at resolutions 1/2/3, Seurat3, Monocle3, ICGS2, cellHarmony, Azimuth label transfer) exist for the same cells and each cluster's stability must be scored before reconciliation.
skills.name: cluster-stability-scoring
skills.search_text: cluster-stability-scoring Use when multiple conflicting cell-cluster annotations (e.g. Leiden at resolutions 1/2/3, Seurat3, Monocle3, ICGS2, cellHarmony, Azimuth label transfer) exist for the same cells and each cluster's stability must be scored before reconciliation. You need a consensus clustering across many (>15) annotation sets and cannot afford Shapley coalitional iteration — scTriangulate automatically substitutes a combined rank-based selection in that regime, changing the stability-selection behavior You want data-level integration via a joint latent space or geometric graph (e.g. Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) rather than decision-level reconciliation of existing cluster labels Your input is raw unnormalized counts without prior clustering — stability scoring requires pre-existing conflicting annotation columns in adata.obs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify the reliability of every cluster produced by conflicting single-cell clustering solutions using scTriangulate's four embedded stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5, TFIDF10, SCCAF), so that a Shapley-value decision engine can mix-and-match clusters from different algorithms, modalities, and resolutions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Quantify the reliability of every cluster produced by conflicting single-cell clustering solutions using scTriangulate's four embedded stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5, TFIDF10, SCCAF), so that a Shapley-value decision engine can mix-and-match clusters from different algorithms, modalities, and resolutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a consensus clustering across many (>15) annotation sets and cannot afford Shapley coalitional iteration — scTriangulate automatically substitutes a combined rank-based selection in that regime, changing the stability-selection behavior You want data-level integration via a joint latent space or geometric graph (e.g. Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) rather than decision-level reconciliation of existing cluster labels Your input is raw unnormalized counts without prior clustering — stability scoring requires pre-existing conflicting annotation columns in adata.obs

skills.description: Use when samples have both an unsupervised grouping (e.g., hierarchical clustering over rROMA pathway activity scores) and independent clinical/molecular subtype labels (e.g., PAM50), and you need to establish or validate the cluster-to-subtype correspondence.

skills.search_text: cluster-subtype-correspondence-mapping Use when samples have both an unsupervised grouping (e.g., hierarchical clustering over rROMA pathway activity scores) and independent clinical/molecular subtype labels (e.g., PAM50), and you need to establish or validate the cluster-to-subtype correspondence. No independent subtype or clinical labels are available — the mapping step cannot be performed and only the unsupervised clustering is meaningful The input is raw/unnormalized count data — rRoma requires normalized matrices (e.g., cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before any clustering Only one or two significant modules are detected, making activity-profile-based clustering unstable or uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps an unsupervised hierarchical clustering of samples, built on rROMA module activity scores, onto clinical molecular subtype labels (e.g., PAM50 breast cancer subtypes) to check whether pathway-activity-based groupings recapitulate known biology, as demonstrated on a 9771-protein × 122-sample breast cancer proteomic dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Maps an unsupervised hierarchical clustering of samples, built on rROMA module activity scores, onto clinical molecular subtype labels (e.g., PAM50 breast cancer subtypes) to check whether pathway-activity-based groupings recapitulate known biology, as demonstrated on a 9771-protein × 122-sample breast cancer proteomic dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent subtype or clinical labels are available — the mapping step cannot be performed and only the unsupervised clustering is meaningful The input is raw/unnormalized count data — rRoma requires normalized matrices (e.g., cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before any clustering Only one or two significant modules are detected, making activity-profile-based clustering unstable or uninformative

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells have not been clustered (the skill requires pre-existing cluster labels such as dropClust R1–R13) No published reference signature exists for the candidate cell sub-types, making differential-gene overlay impossible Goal is to detect rare cells from scratch rather than annotate existing clusters — use FiRE rareness scoring first

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell transcriptomics dataset with cluster labels, a gene-gene regulatory mask (e.g. ATAC-seq-derived), and coexpression/manifold priors, and you need cluster-specific GRN interaction matrices plus per-cell velocity vectors.
skills.name: cluster-wise-dynamical-model-fitting
skills.search_text: cluster-wise-dynamical-model-fitting Use when you have a single-cell transcriptomics dataset with cluster labels, a gene-gene regulatory mask (e.g. ATAC-seq-derived), and coexpression/manifold priors, and you need cluster-specific GRN interaction matrices plus per-cell velocity vectors. Input lacks cluster labels, a regulatory mask, and coexpression/manifold priors — the EM fit depends on these biologically motivated priors. The goal is a global single velocity model over all cells rather than cluster-specific regulatory networks (scKINETICS learns a separate A_c per cluster). The dataset is not single-cell transcriptomics with a definable phenotypic manifold over which future-state constraints can be imposed. Fits the scKINETICS dynamical model separately per Phenograph cluster using an expectation-maximization scheme, jointly learning cluster-specific gene regulatory interaction matrices (A_c) and per-cell transcriptional velocities from scRNA-seq expression plus regulatory and manifold priors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Fits the scKINETICS dynamical model separately per Phenograph cluster using an expectation-maximization scheme, jointly learning cluster-specific gene regulatory interaction matrices (A_c) and per-cell transcriptional velocities from scRNA-seq expression plus regulatory and manifold priors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks cluster labels, a regulatory mask, and coexpression/manifold priors — the EM fit depends on these biologically motivated priors. The goal is a global single velocity model over all cells rather than cluster-specific regulatory networks (scKINETICS learns a separate A_c per cluster). The dataset is not single-cell transcriptomics with a definable phenotypic manifold over which future-state constraints can be imposed.

skills.search_text: clustering-benchmark-evaluation Use when a new clustering method must be rigorously compared to competitors (e.g., PhenoGraph, HDBSCAN, Louvain/Leiden implementations) on simulated or biological datasets where ground-truth labels are available. The dataset has no ground-truth labels and only intrinsic quality measures (e.g., KMD silhouette, DBCV) can be computed — external benchmark metrics like accuracy/NMI/ARI require y_true. The goal is to tune or select hyperparameters (k) rather than compare methods — use the KMD silhouette score scan, not a multi-method benchmark. Evaluating clustering on globular-shaped clusters only, where the standard silhouette score suffices and is biased toward such shapes anyway. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a clustering method against multiple competing general-purpose and domain-specific algorithms on datasets with known ground truth, reporting accuracy, normalized mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI) per method and dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a clustering method against multiple competing general-purpose and domain-specific algorithms on datasets with known ground truth, reporting accuracy, normalized mutual information (NMI) and adjusted Rand index (ARI) per method and dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth labels and only intrinsic quality measures (e.g., KMD silhouette, DBCV) can be computed — external benchmark metrics like accuracy/NMI/ARI require y_true. The goal is to tune or select hyperparameters (k) rather than compare methods — use the KMD silhouette score scan, not a multi-method benchmark. Evaluating clustering on globular-shaped clusters only, where the standard silhouette score suffices and is biased toward such shapes anyway.

skills.description: Use when a clustering method must be validated against baselines on datasets with known ground-truth labels (Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq, synthetic ring/half-moon/Gaussian-mixture shapes), and purity/ARI plus paired significance testing are needed.
skills.name: clustering-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: clustering-benchmark-evaluation Use when a clustering method must be validated against baselines on datasets with known ground-truth labels (Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq, synthetic ring/half-moon/Gaussian-mixture shapes), and purity/ARI plus paired significance testing are needed. Input data has no reference/ground-truth labels for any dataset, so purity and adjusted Rand index cannot be computed — internal validation (FFC.validate/entropy/pval) is the wrong substitute for external benchmarks here. The goal is biological discovery on one real experimental dataset (e.g., PBMC or MCA cell-type assignment), not controlled method comparison against baselines. Data are continuous, unlabeled streams where only label-confidence metrics (posterior significance, entropy) matter and no baseline method comparison is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark a clustering method (e.g., Forest Fire Clustering) against baselines like SC3, Seurat, KMeans, GMM, DBSCAN, OPTICS, and SpectralClustering using purity scores, adjusted Rand index, silhouette scores, and one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on paired per-dataset scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a clustering method (e.g., Forest Fire Clustering) against baselines like SC3, Seurat, KMeans, GMM, DBSCAN, OPTICS, and SpectralClustering using purity scores, adjusted Rand index, silhouette scores, and one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on paired per-dataset scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no reference/ground-truth labels for any dataset, so purity and adjusted Rand index cannot be computed — internal validation (FFC.validate/entropy/pval) is the wrong substitute for external benchmarks here. The goal is biological discovery on one real experimental dataset (e.g., PBMC or MCA cell-type assignment), not controlled method comparison against baselines. Data are continuous, unlabeled streams where only label-confidence metrics (posterior significance, entropy) matter and no baseline method comparison is required.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating the SSRE NMI/ARI clustering benchmark on Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq data, or when comparing a single-cell clustering method against published Tables S1-S2 scores.

skills.search_text: clustering-benchmark-reproduction Use when reproducing or validating the SSRE NMI/ARI clustering benchmark on Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq data, or when comparing a single-cell clustering method against published Tables S1-S2 scores. Input is a real (non-simulated) scRNA-seq dataset without ground-truth labels — the NMI/ARI validation depends on Splatter-simulated true labels; use the paper's separate ten-real-dataset evaluation instead Target datasets are large-scale — SSRE is noted as relatively time-consuming on large-scale datasets, making this benchmark protocol impractical there The goal is applying SSRE for downstream tasks (visualization, differential expression analysis) rather than benchmarking clustering accuracy against Tables S1-S2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark-reproduction protocol for SSRE cell-type detection: simulate five Splatter scRNA-seq datasets spanning 500-1500 cells and sparsity 0.61-0.94, run SSRE (MATLAB/Python, default three-similarity configuration) plus competing clustering methods, and score NMI/ARI against simulated true labels to mirror supplementary Tables S1-S2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Benchmark-reproduction protocol for SSRE cell-type detection: simulate five Splatter scRNA-seq datasets spanning 500-1500 cells and sparsity 0.61-0.94, run SSRE (MATLAB/Python, default three-similarity configuration) plus competing clustering methods, and score NMI/ARI against simulated true labels to mirror supplementary Tables S1-S2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a real (non-simulated) scRNA-seq dataset without ground-truth labels — the NMI/ARI validation depends on Splatter-simulated true labels; use the paper's separate ten-real-dataset evaluation instead Target datasets are large-scale — SSRE is noted as relatively time-consuming on large-scale datasets, making this benchmark protocol impractical there The goal is applying SSRE for downstream tasks (visualization, differential expression analysis) rather than benchmarking clustering accuracy against Tables S1-S2

skills.description: Use when training a deep embedding clustering model (e.g. scMGCA's graph convolutional autoencoder) where the self-optimizing KL clustering stage needs well-initialized cluster centers on latent embeddings of scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: clustering-center-initialization-kmeans-spectral
skills.search_text: clustering-center-initialization-kmeans-spectral Use when training a deep embedding clustering model (e.g. scMGCA's graph convolutional autoencoder) where the self-optimizing KL clustering stage needs well-initialized cluster centers on latent embeddings of scRNA-seq data. When the clustering stage does not rely on initialized centers (e.g. purely KNN-graph-based methods without a KL self-optimization head) When only a small subset of cells is available and K-means alone is already stable — the spectral comparison adds cost with little benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 scMGCA initializes its self-optimized clustering centers by running both K-means and spectral clustering on the latent representation and selecting the best strategy between them, providing a stable starting point for the KL-divergence self-optimization stage of the graph convolutional autoencoder. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: scMGCA initializes its self-optimized clustering centers by running both K-means and spectral clustering on the latent representation and selecting the best strategy between them, providing a stable starting point for the KL-divergence self-optimization stage of the graph convolutional autoencoder.

skills.description: Use when independent cluster assignments of the same cells exist (e.g., CNA-derived and mutation-derived) and an orthogonal-validation metric is needed to confirm a caller's subclone structure.

skills.search_text: clustering-concordance-adjusted-rand-index Use when independent cluster assignments of the same cells exist (e.g., CNA-derived and mutation-derived) and an orthogonal-validation metric is needed to confirm a caller's subclone structure. The two labelings cover different sets of cells — ARI requires paired assignments of the identical cell set (here 179 cells) You only have one clustering and no orthogonal genotype-based labels; ARI is undefined without a second partition to compare against Cluster labels are continuous (e.g., copy-number values) rather than discrete partition assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Validates single-cell CNA-based clustering against an orthogonal somatic-SNV-based clustering by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between the two sets of cell assignments, as done for 179 serial meningioma cells (ARI 0.83). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Validates single-cell CNA-based clustering against an orthogonal somatic-SNV-based clustering by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between the two sets of cell assignments, as done for 179 serial meningioma cells (ARI 0.83).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two labelings cover different sets of cells — ARI requires paired assignments of the identical cell set (here 179 cells) You only have one clustering and no orthogonal genotype-based labels; ARI is undefined without a second partition to compare against Cluster labels are continuous (e.g., copy-number values) rather than discrete partition assignments

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively benchmark whether a feature-quantification method (e.g., MATES vs scTE/SoloTE) yields better downstream cell clustering, given known cell labels and repeated clusterings over multiple seeds.
skills.name: clustering-concordance-metric-computation
skills.search_text: clustering-concordance-metric-computation Use when you need to quantitatively benchmark whether a feature-quantification method (e.g., MATES vs scTE/SoloTE) yields better downstream cell clustering, given known cell labels and repeated clusterings over multiple seeds. Input is a single clustering result with no ground-truth labels — ARI/NMI require reference labels and cannot be computed You need TE locus quantification itself (read assignment/counting), not the downstream evaluation of clusterings built from those counts Only one random seed or one clustering run is available — the skill's t-test over N=10 seeds requires distributional replicates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill for comparing cell-clustering quality across alternative feature matrices (e.g., Gene/Peak+TE, TE-only, Multi-mapping-TE-only produced by MATES, scTE, and SoloTE) using Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) against known cell labels, with statistical comparison via one-sided Student's t-tests over multiple random seeds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing cell-clustering quality across alternative feature matrices (e.g., Gene/Peak+TE, TE-only, Multi-mapping-TE-only produced by MATES, scTE, and SoloTE) using Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) against known cell labels, with statistical comparison via one-sided Student's t-tests over multiple random seeds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single clustering result with no ground-truth labels — ARI/NMI require reference labels and cannot be computed You need TE locus quantification itself (read assignment/counting), not the downstream evaluation of clusterings built from those counts Only one random seed or one clustering run is available — the skill's t-test over N=10 seeds requires distributional replicates

skills.description: Use when an imputation method (e.g., Bfimpute, scImpute, MAGIC, SAVER, VIPER, PBLR, DrImpute) must be benchmarked on data with known cell type labels, such as splatter-simulated matrices or labeled 10x datasets, to quantify clustering recovery.
skills.name: clustering-consistency-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: clustering-consistency-metric-evaluation Use when an imputation method (e.g., Bfimpute, scImpute, MAGIC, SAVER, VIPER, PBLR, DrImpute) must be benchmarked on data with known cell type labels, such as splatter-simulated matrices or labeled 10x datasets, to quantify clustering recovery. No ground-truth cell labels or simulation-known identities exist, making ARI/Jaccard/NMI/purity against truth undefined — use unsupervised metrics instead The goal is differential expression or gene-level recovery accuracy rather than cell-to-cell relationship recovery, where the paper notes prior methods 'were less effective in recovering cell-to-cell relationships' Evaluating pseudotime/trajectory quality alone, where TSCAN POS and Kendall correlation are the appropriate scores rather than label-agreement metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluate how well imputed or raw scRNA-seq expression matrices recover known cell identities by clustering cells and scoring agreement against ground-truth labels with adjusted Rand index, Jaccard index, normalized mutual information, and purity, repeated over random seeds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Evaluate how well imputed or raw scRNA-seq expression matrices recover known cell identities by clustering cells and scoring agreement against ground-truth labels with adjusted Rand index, Jaccard index, normalized mutual information, and purity, repeated over random seeds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth cell labels or simulation-known identities exist, making ARI/Jaccard/NMI/purity against truth undefined — use unsupervised metrics instead The goal is differential expression or gene-level recovery accuracy rather than cell-to-cell relationship recovery, where the paper notes prior methods 'were less effective in recovering cell-to-cell relationships' Evaluating pseudotime/trajectory quality alone, where TSCAN POS and Kendall correlation are the appropriate scores rather than label-agreement metrics

skills.description: Use when combining multiple base clustering solutions (e.g. nine scRNA-seq algorithms on feature-selected scRNA-seq data) and redundant, highly similar label sets must be removed before meta-clustering.
skills.name: clustering-diversity-filtering-with-ari
skills.search_text: clustering-diversity-filtering-with-ari Use when combining multiple base clustering solutions (e.g. nine scRNA-seq algorithms on feature-selected scRNA-seq data) and redundant, highly similar label sets must be removed before meta-clustering. Only a single clustering solution is available, so no pairwise diversity can be assessed Base clusterings are already known to be complementary and the ensemble size is small enough that pruning would discard informative labels The downstream combiner can directly handle redundancy (e.g. weighting schemes that already down-weight correlated clusterings) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A pruning step in the scEFSC ensemble that computes pairwise Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between all base clustering labels and removes labels whose similarity vector has the lowest variance, i.e. the least diverse clusterings, before weighted meta-clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.04.023
skills.summary: A pruning step in the scEFSC ensemble that computes pairwise Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) between all base clustering labels and removes labels whose similarity vector has the lowest variance, i.e. the least diverse clusterings, before weighted meta-clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single clustering solution is available, so no pairwise diversity can be assessed Base clusterings are already known to be complementary and the ensemble size is small enough that pruning would discard informative labels The downstream combiner can directly handle redundancy (e.g. weighting schemes that already down-weight correlated clusterings)

skills.search_text: clustering-enhancement-initialization Use when you already have cluster assignments from another scRNA-seq clustering method (e.g. scDeepCluster, DESC, SCCAF, ADClust) on a preprocessed AnnData object and want scAce to update and enhance those assignments. No prior clustering results exist and a de novo initialization is wanted — scAce then uses Leiden to obtain initial cluster labels instead of the clustering-enhancement path The number of clusters must be known in advance or the goal is purely to reproduce another method's clusters without improvement http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Initializes scAce clustering by applying a cluster splitting approach to pre-existing clustering results from other scRNA-seq methods, producing initial cluster labels that scAce's VAE and adaptive merging then enhance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq cells must be assigned to clusters for cell type identification and no single clustering method can be trusted a priori; run four SINCERA clustering variants on the identical input and pick the scheme supported by permutation tests and selective marker expression.

skills.search_text: clustering-method-variant-comparison Use when scRNA-Seq cells must be assigned to clusters for cell type identification and no single clustering method can be trusted a priori; run four SINCERA clustering variants on the identical input and pick the scheme supported by permutation tests and selective marker expression. The input matrix has not been through SINCERA preprocessing (filtering of low-quality/contaminated cells, gene prefiltering, z-score normalization of cell type-selective genes) — clustering raw or unfiltered data invalidates the comparison. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix has not been through SINCERA preprocessing (filtering of low-quality/contaminated cells, gene prefiltering, z-score normalization of cell type-selective genes) — clustering raw or unfiltered data invalidates the comparison. The analysis goal is downstream gene signature prediction or transcriptional regulatory network construction on already-defined cell types rather than selecting a clustering scheme.
