skills.search_text: coexpression-module-comparison-across-datasets Use when two independently constructed WGCNA networks (or a network and an external gene list) must be compared module-to-module to find shared co-expression signatures, as done for 5xFAD vs 3xTg-AD PyWGCNA objects. You have only one WGCNA network and need within-dataset analyses (module detection, eigengenes, module-trait correlation) rather than cross-dataset module overlap You need functional enrichment of a module (GO/KEGG/REACTOME) rather than conservation between datasets — PyWGCNA's enrichment workflow is the appropriate skill Input is a network and a single external marker-gene list when you want gene-list comparison only; use the 'Compare PyWGCNA objects to gene marker list' workflow instead of full two-network comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify conservation of WGCNA co-expression modules between two datasets (e.g., the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq networks) using PyWGCNA's module-comparison routine, Fisher's exact test, and Jaccard similarity to identify modules with significant overlap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Quantify conservation of WGCNA co-expression modules between two datasets (e.g., the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq networks) using PyWGCNA's module-comparison routine, Fisher's exact test, and Jaccard similarity to identify modules with significant overlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one WGCNA network and need within-dataset analyses (module detection, eigengenes, module-trait correlation) rather than cross-dataset module overlap You need functional enrichment of a module (GO/KEGG/REACTOME) rather than conservation between datasets — PyWGCNA's enrichment workflow is the appropriate skill Input is a network and a single external marker-gene list when you want gene-list comparison only; use the 'Compare PyWGCNA objects to gene marker list' workflow instead of full two-network comparison

skills.description: Use when a trait- or cell-type-specific co-expression module (e.g. M11 or M21 in classical monocytes) has already been inferred and the goal is to identify its transcriptional regulators (TFs) and build a directed TF→TG regulatory graph.
skills.name: coexpression-module-to-grn-conversion
skills.search_text: coexpression-module-to-grn-conversion Use when a trait- or cell-type-specific co-expression module (e.g. M11 or M21 in classical monocytes) has already been inferred and the goal is to identify its transcriptional regulators (TFs) and build a directed TF→TG regulatory graph. No co-expression module gene list exists yet — run SCANet's modified WGCNA GCN inference and module detection (pseudo-bulk aggregation + module selection) first. The goal is co-expression hub detection or drug–gene interaction mining within a GCN rather than TF-to-target regulatory directionality. The dataset has no reliable cis-regulatory motif annotation for the candidate TFs, making RcisTarget motif validation infeasible. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts a co-expression gene module (GCN) inferred by SCANet's modified WGCNA/BioNERO pipeline into a directed transcriptional gene regulatory network (GRN) by identifying transcription factors among the module genes and validating TF–target edges with GRNBoost2 plus RcisTarget motif enrichment, following the pySCENIC workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Converts a co-expression gene module (GCN) inferred by SCANet's modified WGCNA/BioNERO pipeline into a directed transcriptional gene regulatory network (GRN) by identifying transcription factors among the module genes and validating TF–target edges with GRNBoost2 plus RcisTarget motif enrichment, following the pySCENIC workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No co-expression module gene list exists yet — run SCANet's modified WGCNA GCN inference and module detection (pseudo-bulk aggregation + module selection) first. The goal is co-expression hub detection or drug–gene interaction mining within a GCN rather than TF-to-target regulatory directionality. The dataset has no reliable cis-regulatory motif annotation for the candidate TFs, making RcisTarget motif validation infeasible.

skills.description: Use when assessing robustness of scKINETICS-derived velocity estimates and gene regulatory networks to variation in sigma and to noise injected into the coexpression prior A^, holding all other inputs fixed.
skills.name: coexpression-prior-noise-perturbation
skills.search_text: coexpression-prior-noise-perturbation Use when assessing robustness of scKINETICS-derived velocity estimates and gene regulatory networks to variation in sigma and to noise injected into the coexpression prior A^, holding all other inputs fixed. The goal is primary velocity/GRN inference rather than sensitivity analysis — run scKINETICS once with the chosen priors instead of perturbing them. The perturbation target is the epigenetic prior or phenotypic manifold rather than the coexpression prior A^ and sigma; this workflow fixes those inputs unchanged. Reference per-cell velocities from an unperturbed scKINETICS fit are unavailable, so cosine-distance deviation cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A sensitivity-analysis procedure for scKINETICS that perturbs the coexpression prior A^ with successive rounds of Gaussian noise and sweeps the manifold-constraint parameter sigma, quantifying how inferred per-cell velocities and network alignment deviate from a reference fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis procedure for scKINETICS that perturbs the coexpression prior A^ with successive rounds of Gaussian noise and sweeps the manifold-constraint parameter sigma, quantifying how inferred per-cell velocities and network alignment deviate from a reference fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is primary velocity/GRN inference rather than sensitivity analysis — run scKINETICS once with the chosen priors instead of perturbing them. The perturbation target is the epigenetic prior or phenotypic manifold rather than the coexpression prior A^ and sigma; this workflow fixes those inputs unchanged. Reference per-cell velocities from an unperturbed scKINETICS fit are unavailable, so cosine-distance deviation cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell RNA velocity vectors paired with an interpretable gene regulatory network from single-cell transcriptomics, especially when spliced/unspliced-only methods give orthogonal or inconsistent directions relative to a known biological transition axis.
skills.name: coexpression-prior-regularized-dynamics-fitting
skills.search_text: coexpression-prior-regularized-dynamics-fitting Use when you need per-cell RNA velocity vectors paired with an interpretable gene regulatory network from single-cell transcriptomics, especially when spliced/unspliced-only methods give orthogonal or inconsistent directions relative to a known biological transition axis. When you only need fast standard velocity without a mechanistic GRN and spliced/unspliced counts are already adequate for scVelo-style fitting When no gene-gene coexpression prior, epigenetic (ATAC-seq) mask, or cluster structure is available to initialize the priors and manifold constraint When the dataset is too small to support per-cluster EM fitting of a full 15497-gene interaction matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit scKINETICS, a dynamical model of gene expression change that simultaneously learns per-cell transcriptional velocities and a governing gene regulatory network via expectation-maximization, regularized by gene-gene coexpression priors and phenotypic manifold constraints. It yields interpretable, mechanistic velocity vectors where standard approaches (scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) often fail. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Fit scKINETICS, a dynamical model of gene expression change that simultaneously learns per-cell transcriptional velocities and a governing gene regulatory network via expectation-maximization, regularized by gene-gene coexpression priors and phenotypic manifold constraints. It yields interpretable, mechanistic velocity vectors where standard approaches (scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) often fail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need fast standard velocity without a mechanistic GRN and spliced/unspliced counts are already adequate for scVelo-style fitting When no gene-gene coexpression prior, epigenetic (ATAC-seq) mask, or cluster structure is available to initialize the priors and manifold constraint When the dataset is too small to support per-cluster EM fitting of a full 15497-gene interaction matrix

skills.search_text: cohen-kappa-agreement-statistics Use when you need to measure how well clustering assignments (e.g., hybrid ClonoCluster clusters at stepwise α values) agree with a known categorical labeling such as clone barcode membership, especially to characterize transition sharpness across a parameter sweep. skills.summary: Quantifies chance-corrected agreement between hybrid cluster assignments (from ClonoCluster across α = 0 to 1) and clone barcode membership using Cohen's κ, revealing how gradually or abruptly clones conglomerate into hybrid clusters in each single-cell dataset.

skills.description: Use when per-sample circlehunter outputs exist for many ATAC-Seq tumor samples and you need cohort-level counts, ecDNA-positive sample rates, and size/chromosome/segment distributions across cancer types.
skills.name: cohort-ecdna-statistics-aggregation
skills.search_text: cohort-ecdna-statistics-aggregation Use when per-sample circlehunter outputs exist for many ATAC-Seq tumor samples and you need cohort-level counts, ecDNA-positive sample rates, and size/chromosome/segment distributions across cancer types. When analyzing a single sample or cell line rather than a cohort — aggregation statistics require many samples to be meaningful When the per-sample calls have not been generated yet (this skill aggregates circlehunter outputs; run the Snakemake pipeline first) When samples lack cancer type annotations, preventing meaningful per-cancer-type stratification (the article notes the analyzed set was mostly cell lines with skewed cancer type proportions) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Aggregate per-sample circlehunter ecDNA predictions across a curated cohort of public ATAC-Seq tumor samples into cohort-level statistics — total ecDNA count, number and percentage of ecDNA-positive samples, and ecDNA size, chromosome, and segment-count distributions — to quantify the landscape of extrachromosomal circular DNA across cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: When analyzing a single sample or cell line rather than a cohort — aggregation statistics require many samples to be meaningful When the per-sample calls have not been generated yet (this skill aggregates circlehunter outputs; run the Snakemake pipeline first) When samples lack cancer type annotations, preventing meaningful per-cancer-type stratification (the article notes the analyzed set was mostly cell lines with skewed cancer type proportions)

skills.description: Use when a genome-wide shape-change analysis over a base-level pileup matrix must first exclude genes with many non-expressed samples in the cohort, so that downstream on/off artifacts do not masquerade as shape changes.
skills.name: cohort-gene-exclusion-filtering
skills.search_text: cohort-gene-exclusion-filtering Use when a genome-wide shape-change analysis over a base-level pileup matrix must first exclude genes with many non-expressed samples in the cohort, so that downstream on/off artifacts do not masquerade as shape changes. The input is a single-sample pileup with no cohort: the off classification is defined relative to a gene's mean coverage vector across all samples, so a cohort (paper suggests >= 30 samples) is required. The goal is filtering lowly expressed genes by expression magnitude — that step uses percentile cutoffs on median and MAD of normalized RSEM values, not angle-based on/off shape statistics. Severely degraded samples have not yet been removed: on/off fractions computed over the 70 degraded TCGA HNSC cases would be inflated and the 5802-gene result would not reproduce. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SCISSOR's on/off gene filter classifies each sample-gene pair as 'off' using angle-based shape similarity (angle.hy) between the sample's base-level coverage vector and the gene's mean coverage vector, then excludes genes whose fraction of off samples exceeds 20% — removing 5802 genes (~28%) in the 522-sample TCGA HNSC cohort before shape-change analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: SCISSOR's on/off gene filter classifies each sample-gene pair as 'off' using angle-based shape similarity (angle.hy) between the sample's base-level coverage vector and the gene's mean coverage vector, then excludes genes whose fraction of off samples exceeds 20% — removing 5802 genes (~28%) in the 522-sample TCGA HNSC cohort before shape-change analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-sample pileup with no cohort: the off classification is defined relative to a gene's mean coverage vector across all samples, so a cohort (paper suggests >= 30 samples) is required. The goal is filtering lowly expressed genes by expression magnitude — that step uses percentile cutoffs on median and MAD of normalized RSEM values, not angle-based on/off shape statistics. Severely degraded samples have not yet been removed: on/off fractions computed over the 70 degraded TCGA HNSC cases would be inflated and the 5802-gene result would not reproduce.

skills.description: Use when a multi-sample CLL RNA-seq cohort (BAMs aligned to hg38 with BWA) must be run through CRIS one sample at a time to produce cohort-level IGHV mutation-status calls for comparison with clinical Sanger classification.
skills.name: cohort-scale-rnaseq-batch-processing
skills.search_text: cohort-scale-rnaseq-batch-processing Use when a multi-sample CLL RNA-seq cohort (BAMs aligned to hg38 with BWA) must be run through CRIS one sample at a time to produce cohort-level IGHV mutation-status calls for comparison with clinical Sanger classification. Input BAMs are aligned to a genome build other than hg38 (GRCh38) or are not coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS requires hg38 BWA alignments Samples have fewer than 25M sequence reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for ribodepleted or polyA-selected RNA-seq The goal is variant calling outside the immunoglobulin loci or T-cell receptor repertoire analysis — CRIS reconstructs Ig heavy-chain V-D-J specifically http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Batch-apply the CRIS IGHV reconstruction pipeline across every sample of a cohort RNA-seq study (e.g. EGAD00001004046 CLL BAMs) and compile per-sample dominant-clone IGHV gene, percent identity, and mCLL/uCLL calls into one comparison table against clinical classifications. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Batch-apply the CRIS IGHV reconstruction pipeline across every sample of a cohort RNA-seq study (e.g. EGAD00001004046 CLL BAMs) and compile per-sample dominant-clone IGHV gene, percent identity, and mCLL/uCLL calls into one comparison table against clinical classifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAMs are aligned to a genome build other than hg38 (GRCh38) or are not coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS requires hg38 BWA alignments Samples have fewer than 25M sequence reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for ribodepleted or polyA-selected RNA-seq The goal is variant calling outside the immunoglobulin loci or T-cell receptor repertoire analysis — CRIS reconstructs Ig heavy-chain V-D-J specifically

skills.search_text: cohort-size-scaling-analysis Use when choosing a cohort-pooling size or a matrix-factorization method (ICA vs NMF) for a multi-cohort single-cell decomposition pipeline, and you need evidence on how program recovery scales from 5 to 10 to 20 pooled datasets. Input is raw, demultiplexed FASTQ that has not yet been collapsed and aligned — pre-processing/alignment steps come first A per-feature count table already exists and only downstream steps (differential expression, plots) are needed The alignment file targets a reference whose chromosome or feature identifiers do not match the annotation file and cannot be reconciled — tiny-count's identifier matching would silently fail to assign reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Verify that the collapsed SAM alignment file destined for tiny-count is consistent with the reference annotation and selection rules before hierarchical counting, so that miRNA/isomiR assignment by 5' nucleotide, length, and alignment position is computed on a valid input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065

skills.description: Use when you have a CAFEH results table (cafeh.{mode}.results) with pip/top_component/alpha/rank/p_active columns and want to convert top-component sharing across tissues into gene sets for constraint, OMIM, and GO enrichment testing.
skills.name: colocalization-component-based-gene-set-definition
skills.search_text: colocalization-component-based-gene-set-definition Use when you have a CAFEH results table (cafeh.{mode}.results) with pip/top_component/alpha/rank/p_active columns and want to convert top-component sharing across tissues into gene sets for constraint, OMIM, and GO enrichment testing. Loci whose trait effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — the article notes such loci cannot be explored with CAFEH, so no colocalization components exist to stratify Studies with large LD differences between them (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so top_component sharing across such studies is unreliable When the goal is to claim disease-eQTL causality: colocalization does not imply mediation, and colocalizing signals can arise from horizontal pleiotropy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Defines biologically interpretable gene sets from CAFEH colocalization output (top_component, p_active, pip per SNP-study pair) by stratifying genes into highly colocalizing, poorly colocalizing, and background groups based on how many tissues share the CAFEH top component, then tests the sets for constraint (LOEUF, pLI), OMIM disease, and GO enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Defines biologically interpretable gene sets from CAFEH colocalization output (top_component, p_active, pip per SNP-study pair) by stratifying genes into highly colocalizing, poorly colocalizing, and background groups based on how many tissues share the CAFEH top component, then tests the sets for constraint (LOEUF, pLI), OMIM disease, and GO enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose trait effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — the article notes such loci cannot be explored with CAFEH, so no colocalization components exist to stratify Studies with large LD differences between them (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so top_component sharing across such studies is unreliable When the goal is to claim disease-eQTL causality: colocalization does not imply mediation, and colocalizing signals can arise from horizontal pleiotropy

skills.description: Use when spatially resolved data (e.g., Stereo-seq, STARmap, seqFISH, IMC) has many cell types whose default Scanpy/Seurat/Squidpy colors look similar in adjacent regions, causing perceptual ambiguity between biologically distinct neighboring clusters.
skills.name: color-difference-optimization-cielab
skills.search_text: color-difference-optimization-cielab Use when spatially resolved data (e.g., Stereo-seq, STARmap, seqFISH, IMC) has many cell types whose default Scanpy/Seurat/Squidpy colors look similar in adjacent regions, causing perceptual ambiguity between biologically distinct neighboring clusters. skills.search_text: communication-score-robustness-quantification Use when ICELLNET communication scores are computed between clusters of unequal or small cell counts (e.g. lupus nephritis CM3 dendritic cells vs CT0a/CT3b T cells) and you need to assess how score variability depends on cluster cell number before interpreting score differences. skills.search_text: comparative-centrality-analysis Use when signaling networks from two or more conditions or timepoints (e.g., Seurat objects split by an 'injury' variable into Days 0/2/5/7) must be compared to identify which cell types dominate source vs target roles for a signaling family or a single ligand–receptor mechanism. skills.summary: Graph-theoretic centrality comparison across a list of connectomes (e.g., timepoint-specific ligand–receptor networks from Seurat objects) to rank which cell types dominate producing versus receiving a given signaling mode, such as VEGF/Vegfa-mediated signaling during longitudinal tissue remodeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one tissue system/condition is available — use the single-network Centrality function instead of CompareCentrality, which requires a list of connectomes The goal is a direct quantitative edge-by-edge difference between exactly two connectomes requiring identical edge sets — DifferentialConnectome is the appropriate function, not centrality comparison The input lacks ligand–receptor mapping (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated feature table) — CreateConnectome requires a Seurat object with per-cell-type expression

skills.description: Use when a paper claims one method is 'fast' or memory-efficient versus rivals and the runtime/RAM ordering must be reproduced by running each tool on identical ST and scRNA-seq inputs and profiling execution.
skills.name: comparative-method-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: comparative-method-performance-evaluation Use when a paper claims one method is 'fast' or memory-efficient versus rivals and the runtime/RAM ordering must be reproduced by running each tool on identical ST and scRNA-seq inputs and profiling execution. The goal is deconvolution accuracy evaluation (e.g. MAE/MSE per cell type) rather than runtime and RAM benchmarking — use model evaluation metrics like calculateEvalMetrics instead. Only one method is being run, with no competing methods to compare against — there is no comparative ordering to establish. The compared methods are run on different inputs or hardware, making runtime/RAM numbers non-comparable. Benchmarks the computational cost (wall-clock running time and peak RAM consumption) of competing cell type deconvolution methods — here SpatialDDLS, RCTD, and cell2location — on the same spatial transcriptomics inputs, to substantiate claims such as SpatialDDLS being an accurate and fast alternative to state-of-the-art tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae072
skills.summary: Benchmarks the computational cost (wall-clock running time and peak RAM consumption) of competing cell type deconvolution methods — here SpatialDDLS, RCTD, and cell2location — on the same spatial transcriptomics inputs, to substantiate claims such as SpatialDDLS being an accurate and fast alternative to state-of-the-art tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is deconvolution accuracy evaluation (e.g. MAE/MSE per cell type) rather than runtime and RAM benchmarking — use model evaluation metrics like calculateEvalMetrics instead. Only one method is being run, with no competing methods to compare against — there is no comparative ordering to establish. skills.description: Use when you must compare the computational performance (e.g. runtime) of differential expression tools on the same RNA-seq counts matrix, such as testing whether DESeq2 is slower than edgeR and limma.
skills.name: comparative-tool-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: comparative-tool-performance-evaluation Use when you must compare the computational performance (e.g. runtime) of differential expression tools on the same RNA-seq counts matrix, such as testing whether DESeq2 is slower than edgeR and limma. Input is a TPM or log2(TPM+1) matrix rather than raw counts — count-based differential models (edgeR, DESeq2) require the counts matrix, while TPM is used in ARMT only for normalization and GSVA. The goal is to compare DEG result sets (overlapping genes, DEG counts) rather than computational performance — the article notes different tools yield different results on statistical grounds, which is a separate analysis from runtime benchmarking. Only a single differential analysis run is needed and no cross-tool timing comparison is planned. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of RNA-seq differential analysis tools (edgeR, limma, DESeq2) on the identical counts matrix under identical settings, to reproduce ARMT's finding that DESeq2 is significantly slower than edgeR and limma (Fig. 1B). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of RNA-seq differential analysis tools (edgeR, limma, DESeq2) on the identical counts matrix under identical settings, to reproduce ARMT's finding that DESeq2 is significantly slower than edgeR and limma (Fig. 1B).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a TPM or log2(TPM+1) matrix rather than raw counts — count-based differential models (edgeR, DESeq2) require the counts matrix, while TPM is used in ARMT only for normalization and GSVA. The goal is to compare DEG result sets (overlapping genes, DEG counts) rather than computational performance — the article notes different tools yield different results on statistical grounds, which is a separate analysis from runtime benchmarking. Only a single differential analysis run is needed and no cross-tool timing comparison is planned.

skills.description: Use when comparing the statistical power of gene set enrichment methods on identical simulated DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) at a fixed FDR threshold, e.g. to quantify a new method's gain over fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA.

skills.search_text: competitive-gse-method-benchmarking Use when comparing the statistical power of gene set enrichment methods on identical simulated DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) at a fixed FDR threshold, e.g. to quantify a new method's gain over fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA. The goal is to compare DE (per-gene) methods rather than competitive gene set enrichment methods — iDEA's DE-power benchmarking uses a different design (up to 64% gain over existing DE methods). skills.summary: Benchmark gene set enrichment (GSE) methods by simulating gene-level DE summary statistics under an enrichment alternative (tau0=-2, tau1=0.5, CR=10%) and comparing empirical power at a fixed FDR of 5% across iDEA, fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, and GSEA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare DE (per-gene) methods rather than competitive gene set enrichment methods — iDEA's DE-power benchmarking uses a different design (up to 64% gain over existing DE methods). skills.description: Use when the Pearson correlation matrix P over the training data's averaged cell-type profiles has off-diagonal entries >= 0.95, so a single feed-forward network is insufficient and the hierarchical, marker-guided strategy is triggered.
skills.name: complete-linkage-hierarchical-clustering-cell-lineage-tree
skills.search_text: complete-linkage-hierarchical-clustering-cell-lineage-tree Use when the Pearson correlation matrix P over the training data's averaged cell-type profiles has off-diagonal entries >= 0.95, so a single feed-forward network is insufficient and the hierarchical, marker-guided strategy is triggered. All off-diagonal entries of the cell-type correlation matrix P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA instead selects the single feed-forward neural network classifier (model.size = small/medium/big) The new sample may contain unknown, rare, or novel cell types absent from the training reference — NeuCA is designed for well-studied situations where all cell types already exist in the training data; identify such cells first (e.g., inferCNV or copyKAT for malignant cells) before applying NeuCA No labeled training scRNA-seq data exist for the tissue of interest — supervised training is impossible and unsupervised methods are required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds the cell lineage tree used by NeuCA's hierarchical branch: complete-linkage hierarchical clustering on the columns (K cell types) of the averaged G x K gene-expression profile matrix A, defining the tree of binary bifurcations along which neural-network classifiers are trained when cell types are highly correlated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4

skills.when_to_use_negative: All off-diagonal entries of the cell-type correlation matrix P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA instead selects the single feed-forward neural network classifier (model.size = small/medium/big) The new sample may contain unknown, rare, or novel cell types absent from the training reference — NeuCA is designed for well-studied situations where all cell types already exist in the training data; identify such cells first (e.g., inferCNV or copyKAT for malignant cells) before applying NeuCA No labeled training scRNA-seq data exist for the tissue of interest — supervised training is impossible and unsupervised methods are required

skills.description: Use when decomposing a log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix with ICA (n_components=100) and you need IC gene loadings on a comparable scale with consistently oriented (positively skewed) directions before downstream clustering.
skills.name: component-sign-skewness-alignment
skills.search_text: component-sign-skewness-alignment Use when decomposing a log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix with ICA (n_components=100) and you need IC gene loadings on a comparable scale with consistently oriented (positively skewed) directions before downstream clustering. Input is already a normalized loading/signature table or annotated feature set — no decomposition or sign alignment is needed. Goal is annotating new TME cells using MetaTiME's pretrained meta-components (MetaTiME-Annotator projection), not re-learning components from raw data. Expression matrix is not log-transformed single-cell TME data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq), where the ICA-based MetaTiME decomposition does not apply. Normalizes independent component (IC) gene loadings from fastICA decomposition of tumor scRNA-seq expression matrices by z-weight transformation and sign flipping to positive skewness, so that the scales of gene representation scores are comparable among the ~100 components and across datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Normalizes independent component (IC) gene loadings from fastICA decomposition of tumor scRNA-seq expression matrices by z-weight transformation and sign flipping to positive skewness, so that the scales of gene representation scores are comparable among the ~100 components and across datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized loading/signature table or annotated feature set — no decomposition or sign alignment is needed. Goal is annotating new TME cells using MetaTiME's pretrained meta-components (MetaTiME-Annotator projection), not re-learning components from raw data. Expression matrix is not log-transformed single-cell TME data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq), where the ICA-based MetaTiME decomposition does not apply.

skills.summary: Runs a suite of five single-cell classification tools (SCINA, ScType, scSorter, SingleR, scPred) on an RNA gene expression matrix via the R4scSHARP R package, returning per-tool cell-type label predictions in a single consolidated file for downstream consensus aggregation.

skills.description: Use when projecting a clustered target scRNA-seq subpopulation (e.g., a leukemia sub-cluster) onto a reference cell atlas to identify its closest healthy counterpart, especially where single-signature similarity is unreliable due to large leukemia-vs-healthy differences.
skills.name: composite-likelihood-scoring
skills.search_text: composite-likelihood-scoring Use when projecting a clustered target scRNA-seq subpopulation (e.g., a leukemia sub-cluster) onto a reference cell atlas to identify its closest healthy counterpart, especially where single-signature similarity is unreliable due to large leukemia-vs-healthy differences. Target cells are unclustered single cells rather than sub-clusters — CCI projects cell clusters to reference instead of single cells due to prevalent droplets in scRNA-seq No reference normal-cell atlas is available or the target is not carcinoma/leukemia cells being projected onto healthy reference cells The goal is analyzing relationships only among leukemia subpopulations without mapping onto a healthy hematopoietic reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Implements CCI (Counterpart Composite Index), a composite-likelihood framework that combines multiple similarity statistics — expression-level distance, Spearman rank correlation, PCA-space distance, and gene-set-enrichment AUC differences — into a Bayes-factor probability that maps each leukemia cell subpopulation to its healthy counterpart among reference hematopoietic cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41421-020-00223-4
skills.summary: Implements CCI (Counterpart Composite Index), a composite-likelihood framework that combines multiple similarity statistics — expression-level distance, Spearman rank correlation, PCA-space distance, and gene-set-enrichment AUC differences — into a Bayes-factor probability that maps each leukemia cell subpopulation to its healthy counterpart among reference hematopoietic cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target cells are unclustered single cells rather than sub-clusters — CCI projects cell clusters to reference instead of single cells due to prevalent droplets in scRNA-seq No reference normal-cell atlas is available or the target is not carcinoma/leukemia cells being projected onto healthy reference cells The goal is analyzing relationships only among leukemia subpopulations without mapping onto a healthy hematopoietic reference

skills.description: Use when per-sample cell-type counts from scRNA-seq (e.g., BALF donors split into healthy/moderate/severe groups) must be tested for differential abundance across conditions with few replicates, where univariate tests would be inadequate.
skills.name: compositional-data-analysis
skills.search_text: compositional-data-analysis Use when per-sample cell-type counts from scRNA-seq (e.g., BALF donors split into healthy/moderate/severe groups) must be tested for differential abundance across conditions with few replicates, where univariate tests would be inadequate. Standard univariate tests (Poisson regression, Beta-Binomial regression, t tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum) are the goal and the compositional nature of the data is being ignored — these are inadequate because they do not account for compositionality. The analysis requires modeling response variability within a condition or detecting heterogeneities between samples in treatment response or donor variability — scCODA does not model this. Cell-type definitions come from clustering that is not statistically sound or biologically meaningful — scCODA requires pre-specified, reliable cell-type annotations. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Bayesian differential composition analysis of single-cell cell-type counts using scCODA, which models counts with a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial distribution and a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to detect credible cell-type proportion shifts while controlling false discoveries under compositionality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Bayesian differential composition analysis of single-cell cell-type counts using scCODA, which models counts with a hierarchical Dirichlet-Multinomial distribution and a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to detect credible cell-type proportion shifts while controlling false discoveries under compositionality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Standard univariate tests (Poisson regression, Beta-Binomial regression, t tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum) are the goal and the compositional nature of the data is being ignored — these are inadequate because they do not account for compositionality. The analysis requires modeling response variability within a condition or detecting heterogeneities between samples in treatment response or donor variability — scCODA does not model this. Cell-type definitions come from clustering that is not statistically sound or biologically meaningful — scCODA requires pre-specified, reliable cell-type annotations.

When the goal is a causal gene regulatory network: the article states c-CSN cannot obtain directions of gene associations and causal construction is left as future work When no per-cell CSN is available, since importance Dz(k) is defined as the sum of CSN edge weights and requires the baseline CSN first When computational budget is severely limited and datasets are large: the G conditional tests multiply runtime G-fold and the authors note no parallel scheme is provided http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 Selects the top G largest-degree ('importance') genes from each cell's CSN as the conditional gene set used to build conditional cell-specific networks (CCSNs), pruning indirect associations by conditioning on hub genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Selects the top G largest-degree ('importance') genes from each cell's CSN as the conditional gene set used to build conditional cell-specific networks (CCSNs), pruning indirect associations by conditioning on hub genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a causal gene regulatory network: the article states c-CSN cannot obtain directions of gene associations and causal construction is left as future work When no per-cell CSN is available, since importance Dz(k) is defined as the sum of CSN edge weights and requires the baseline CSN first When computational budget is severely limited and datasets are large: the G conditional tests multiply runtime G-fold and the authors note no parallel scheme is provided

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq or RNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes x n cells) must be transformed into per-cell direct gene-gene association networks, e.g. to reproduce CSN/CCSN sparsity, hub genes, or per-sample pathway connectivity.
skills.name: conditional-independence-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: conditional-independence-hypothesis-testing Use when a normalized scRNA-seq or RNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes x n cells) must be transformed into per-cell direct gene-gene association networks, e.g. to reproduce CSN/CCSN sparsity, hub genes, or per-sample pathway connectivity. The goal is to infer causal direction of gene-gene associations — the authors state c-CSN is not designed to construct causal gene association networks and directions cannot be obtained The input is already a network or degree matrix (CNDM); this skill transforms raw/normalized expression matrices into network data Parallel/computationally cheap processing is required for very large cell counts — no parallel computation scheme is provided despite the G-fold computational cost increase http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implementation of the c-CSN statistical procedure, which builds a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for each cell by hypothesis-testing conditional independence of gene pairs given top-degree hub genes, thereby eliminating indirect associations that cause CSN overestimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Implementation of the c-CSN statistical procedure, which builds a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) for each cell by hypothesis-testing conditional independence of gene pairs given top-degree hub genes, thereby eliminating indirect associations that cause CSN overestimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer causal direction of gene-gene associations — the authors state c-CSN is not designed to construct causal gene association networks and directions cannot be obtained The input is already a network or degree matrix (CNDM); this skill transforms raw/normalized expression matrices into network data Parallel/computationally cheap processing is required for very large cell counts — no parallel computation scheme is provided despite the G-fold computational cost increase

skills.description: Use when you have an nx1 pseudotime vector and matched nx1 marker signals from single-cell snapshot data and need marker intensity distributions as a function of pseudotime or a transformed real time/space scale.
skills.name: conditional-marker-density-estimation
skills.search_text: conditional-marker-density-estimation Use when you have an nx1 pseudotime vector and matched nx1 marker signals from single-cell snapshot data and need marker intensity distributions as a function of pseudotime or a transformed real time/space scale. The pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is untrustworthy, since MAPiT relies on the correctness of the provided cell order No knowledge of the real-scale cell density distribution exists for the process of interest (e.g. stem cell differentiation, where target distributions are hard to construct and cell death/division rates are unknown) The analysis goal is trajectory inference itself rather than rescaling an existing pseudotemporal ordering to a meaningful scale http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives conditional marker profiles p(y|x) from the joint density of pseudotime (or true-scale) and marker signal, so that marker trajectories (e.g. geminin, Ki-67, DNA content) can be read as functions of temporal or spatial position from snapshot single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: Derives conditional marker profiles p(y|x) from the joint density of pseudotime (or true-scale) and marker signal, so that marker trajectories (e.g. geminin, Ki-67, DNA content) can be read as functions of temporal or spatial position from snapshot single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is untrustworthy, since MAPiT relies on the correctness of the provided cell order No knowledge of the real-scale cell density distribution exists for the process of interest (e.g. stem cell differentiation, where target distributions are hard to construct and cell death/division rates are unknown) The analysis goal is trajectory inference itself rather than rescaling an existing pseudotemporal ordering to a meaningful scale

skills.description: Use when a merged bagged GRN (e.g., consensus of 100 subsample networks at a 20% consensus threshold) contains indirect or spurious edges that must be pruned before downstream module analysis or disease subnetwork modeling.
skills.name: conditional-mutual-information-edge-pruning
skills.search_text: conditional-mutual-information-edge-pruning Use when a merged bagged GRN (e.g., consensus of 100 subsample networks at a 20% consensus threshold) contains indirect or spurious edges that must be pruned before downstream module analysis or disease subnetwork modeling. Input is a raw count matrix that has not yet been through supercell construction and bagged GBR-based network inference — pruning presupposes an already-built merged network The goal is to leverage spatial information explicitly during network construction — SCING does not currently utilize spatial information of spatial transcriptomics during GRN construction Strict causal/directional regulatory claims are required — pruned SCING links are not necessarily causal or directional http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A SCING edge-filtering step that prunes edges and cycles from a merged, bagged consensus GRN using conditional mutual information and edge importance scoring, removing indirect associations to yield a directed, interpretable gene regulatory network edge list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: A SCING edge-filtering step that prunes edges and cycles from a merged, bagged consensus GRN using conditional mutual information and edge importance scoring, removing indirect associations to yield a directed, interpretable gene regulatory network edge list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix that has not yet been through supercell construction and bagged GBR-based network inference — pruning presupposes an already-built merged network The goal is to leverage spatial information explicitly during network construction — SCING does not currently utilize spatial information of spatial transcriptomics during GRN construction Strict causal/directional regulatory claims are required — pruned SCING links are not necessarily causal or directional

skills.description: Use when comparing ligand–receptor signaling networks between two experimental conditions (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs) and you need to identify and rank strongly perturbed edges, including concordant and discordant ligand/receptor changes.
skills.name: conditional-network-comparison
skills.search_text: conditional-network-comparison Use when comparing ligand–receptor signaling networks between two experimental conditions (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs) and you need to identify and rank strongly perturbed edges, including concordant and discordant ligand/receptor changes. Only a single tissue system/condition is available with no matched comparison connectome — DifferentialConnectome requires exactly the same edges present in both networks, so a single-condition analysis should use CreateConnectome plus FilterConnectome, NetworkPlot, or CircosPlot instead The question is direct evidence of communication or intracellular transduction — paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication, and spatial proximity cannot be verified from suspension-based single-cell sequencing The input data lack a reliable cell-type annotation or a condition subset with fewer than ~75 cells per identity, undermining node definition and edge statistics (article uses min.cells.per.ident = 75) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A differential-connectomics skill for comparing cell–cell signaling networks between two conditions using the Connectome R package: it computes condition-specific connectomes from Seurat objects, derives a differential connectome, and scores each edge with an always-positive 'perturbation score' (product of absolute ligand and receptor log-fold changes) to rank strongly perturbed ligand–receptor edges regardless of direction of change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: A differential-connectomics skill for comparing cell–cell signaling networks between two conditions using the Connectome R package: it computes condition-specific connectomes from Seurat objects, derives a differential connectome, and scores each edge with an always-positive 'perturbation score' (product of absolute ligand and receptor log-fold changes) to rank strongly perturbed ligand–receptor edges regardless of direction of change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single tissue system/condition is available with no matched comparison connectome — DifferentialConnectome requires exactly the same edges present in both networks, so a single-condition analysis should use CreateConnectome plus FilterConnectome, NetworkPlot, or CircosPlot instead The question is direct evidence of communication or intracellular transduction — paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication, and spatial proximity cannot be verified from suspension-based single-cell sequencing The input data lack a reliable cell-type annotation or a condition subset with fewer than ~75 cells per identity, undermining node definition and edge statistics (article uses min.cells.per.ident = 75)

skills.description: Use when you need gene-level co-expression P values or a gene regulatory network from UMI-based scRNA-seq counts, especially when expression-level normalization bias must be avoided so null P values remain uniform across gene expression bins.
skills.name: conditional-pearson-coexpression-testing
skills.search_text: conditional-pearson-coexpression-testing Use when you need gene-level co-expression P values or a gene regulatory network from UMI-based scRNA-seq counts, especially when expression-level normalization bias must be avoided so null P values remain uniform across gene expression bins. You need hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations between genes — Normalisr is explicitly not designed for this You aim to reconstruct causal regulatory networks via v-structures, regularized regression, or Granger causality with longitudinal data Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq, where the nonlinear cellular summary covariates were not validated and may need revalidation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Normalisr's linear-model gene co-expression test that computes conditional Pearson correlation P values between gene pairs on normalized scRNA-seq expression, after nonlinear library-size confounders have been removed at the mean (lcpm, normcov) and variance (compute_var, normvar) levels, yielding exact, unbiased null P values without permutation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Normalisr's linear-model gene co-expression test that computes conditional Pearson correlation P values between gene pairs on normalized scRNA-seq expression, after nonlinear library-size confounders have been removed at the mean (lcpm, normcov) and variance (compute_var, normvar) levels, yielding exact, unbiased null P values without permutation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations between genes — Normalisr is explicitly not designed for this You aim to reconstruct causal regulatory networks via v-structures, regularized regression, or Granger causality with longitudinal data Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq, where the nonlinear cellular summary covariates were not validated and may need revalidation

skills.description: Use when a new paired TCR + transcriptome query dataset must be mapped into an existing T cell reference atlas and labels (e.g., cancer source, tissue type) transferred without retraining the full reference model.
skills.name: conditional-reference-atlas-training
skills.search_text: conditional-reference-atlas-training Use when a new paired TCR + transcriptome query dataset must be mapped into an existing T cell reference atlas and labels (e.g., cancer source, tissue type) transferred without retraining the full reference model. Data lacks paired TCR sequences and gene expression (mvTCR was applied mainly to paired data; partially missing data handling is insufficient) The goal is de novo clustering or specificity prediction rather than mapping queries into an existing reference atlas No GPU/CUDA machine is available — training and scArches fine-tuning require GPU support http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Train a conditional mvTCR multi-view VAE on a large TIL reference atlas (conditioned on study and cell-type annotations), then use scArches architectural surgery to map held-out query studies into the reference latent space for kNN label transfer of cancer source, tissue type, and cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Train a conditional mvTCR multi-view VAE on a large TIL reference atlas (conditioned on study and cell-type annotations), then use scArches architectural surgery to map held-out query studies into the reference latent space for kNN label transfer of cancer source, tissue type, and cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks paired TCR sequences and gene expression (mvTCR was applied mainly to paired data; partially missing data handling is insufficient) The goal is de novo clustering or specificity prediction rather than mapping queries into an existing reference atlas No GPU/CUDA machine is available — training and scArches fine-tuning require GPU support

skills.description: Use when building SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition: a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g. .h5ad) must be converted into a conditional score network usable for posterior sampling of per-cell expressions.
skills.name: conditional-score-function-learning-from-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: conditional-score-function-learning-from-scrna-seq Use when building SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition: a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g. .h5ad) must be converted into a conditional score network usable for posterior sampling of per-cell expressions. The goal is only cell-type proportion estimation per spot without single-cell-resolution expressions — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD estimate proportions only and do not need a score model The task is gene imputation into sparse ST data (e.g. with Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE), which does not require training a generative score function No cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference is available, since the conditional score network requires mu_k per cell type from labeled single-cell data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train SpatialScope's conditional score-based generative network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k) on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference via denoising score matching across multiple Gaussian noise levels, so that annealed Langevin dynamics can later sample per-cell expressions for gene expression decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Train SpatialScope's conditional score-based generative network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k) on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference via denoising score matching across multiple Gaussian noise levels, so that annealed Langevin dynamics can later sample per-cell expressions for gene expression decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only cell-type proportion estimation per spot without single-cell-resolution expressions — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD estimate proportions only and do not need a score model The task is gene imputation into sparse ST data (e.g. with Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE), which does not require training a generative score function No cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference is available, since the conditional score network requires mu_k per cell type from labeled single-cell data

skills.description: Use when an evaluation protocol repeats a clustering/analysis over many independent replications (e.g. 100 simulated datasets) and per-replication scores must be aggregated into means with 95% confidence intervals for method comparison.
skills.name: confidence-interval-aggregation-over-replications
skills.search_text: confidence-interval-aggregation-over-replications Use when an evaluation protocol repeats a clustering/analysis over many independent replications (e.g. 100 simulated datasets) and per-replication scores must be aggregated into means with 95% confidence intervals for method comparison. When only a single dataset replication is available (e.g. the real-data Hockley/Usoskin or Tasic analyses) — no confidence interval over replications can be formed When the goal is method development of TransferCluster itself (NMF, KTA-based theta selection) rather than statistical evaluation of its results Aggregate Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) scores over many independent dataset replications (100 simulated scRNA-Seq sets per overlap setting) and report mean ARI with 95% confidence intervals per method, overlap setting, and target size, enabling statistically grounded comparison of TransferCluster vs TargetCluster vs ConcatenateCluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Aggregate Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) scores over many independent dataset replications (100 simulated scRNA-Seq sets per overlap setting) and report mean ARI with 95% confidence intervals per method, overlap setting, and target size, enabling statistically grounded comparison of TransferCluster vs TargetCluster vs ConcatenateCluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single dataset replication is available (e.g. the real-data Hockley/Usoskin or Tasic analyses) — no confidence interval over replications can be formed When the goal is method development of TransferCluster itself (NMF, KTA-based theta selection) rather than statistical evaluation of its results

skills.description: Use when you have a continuous outcome (e.g., a signature score) and continuous predictors (e.g., reaction fluxes) per sample and need effect-size estimates with 95% CIs rather than only p-values.
skills.name: confidence-interval-estimation
skills.search_text: confidence-interval-estimation Use when you have a continuous outcome (e.g., a signature score) and continuous predictors (e.g., reaction fluxes) per sample and need effect-size estimates with 95% CIs rather than only p-values. The input is already a coefficient/estimate table—no regression needs to be refit. Predictors or the outcome are not continuous per-sample quantities (e.g., single-cell cluster-level data requiring compute_sc_flux instead). The analysis goal is flux computation itself (MRAS/compute_flux) rather than statistical association of precomputed fluxes with a signature. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits an ordinary least squares regression in R and extracts coefficient estimates with 95% confidence intervals (summary() and confint()) to quantify associations—in this case between METAFlux-derived metabolic fluxes (oxygen uptake, glucose uptake, lactate secretion) and Winter hypoxia scores in 676 TCGA pan-cancer tumors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Fits an ordinary least squares regression in R and extracts coefficient estimates with 95% confidence intervals (summary() and confint()) to quantify associations—in this case between METAFlux-derived metabolic fluxes (oxygen uptake, glucose uptake, lactate secretion) and Winter hypoxia scores in 676 TCGA pan-cancer tumors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a coefficient/estimate table—no regression needs to be refit. Predictors or the outcome are not continuous per-sample quantities (e.g., single-cell cluster-level data requiring compute_sc_flux instead). The analysis goal is flux computation itself (MRAS/compute_flux) rather than statistical association of precomputed fluxes with a signature.

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell label predictions from multiple annotation tools and need to separate high-confidence (majority-agreed) from unconfident cells before propagating labels.
skills.name: confidence-threshold-application
skills.search_text: confidence-threshold-application Use when you have per-cell label predictions from multiple annotation tools and need to separate high-confidence (majority-agreed) from unconfident cells before propagating labels. You need the final propagated annotations for all cells — the simple consensus threshold only splits confident vs. unconfident cells and does not label the unconfident ones (use scSHARP's GCN label propagation for that). You have predictions from fewer than three tools, making a 0.51 majority fraction degenerate or unavailable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies a 0.51 simple-majority vote over five scRNA-seq annotation tools (SCINA, ScType, scSorter, SingleR, scPred) to flag cells whose labels are not confidently agreed upon, quantifying the unconfident fraction per dataset. These confident/unconfident labels then feed scSHARP's GCN label propagation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Applies a 0.51 simple-majority vote over five scRNA-seq annotation tools (SCINA, ScType, scSorter, SingleR, scPred) to flag cells whose labels are not confidently agreed upon, quantifying the unconfident fraction per dataset. These confident/unconfident labels then feed scSHARP's GCN label propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the final propagated annotations for all cells — the simple consensus threshold only splits confident vs. unconfident cells and does not label the unconfident ones (use scSHARP's GCN label propagation for that). You have predictions from fewer than three tools, making a 0.51 majority fraction degenerate or unavailable.

skills.description: Use when a trained SIMS/TabNet checkpoint's raw logits must be turned into calibrated per-cell classification probabilities and cells below a confidence cutoff should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a cell-type label.
skills.name: confidence-threshold-unknown-class-assignment
skills.search_text: confidence-threshold-unknown-class-assignment Use when a trained SIMS/TabNet checkpoint's raw logits must be turned into calibrated per-cell classification probabilities and cells below a confidence cutoff should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a cell-type label. When the goal is trans-species label transfer — SIMS calibration has only been validated for samples within the same species When no pre-existing annotations are available for training, since temperature scaling calibrates a supervised model that relies on expert-annotated clusters When raw logit ranks (not calibrated confidences) suffice, e.g. quick top-1 label transfer with no downstream confidence gating http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Post-process a trained SIMS/TabNet single-cell classifier with post-hoc temperature scaling to emit calibrated per-cell cluster probabilities, then apply a user-adjustable confidence threshold so that low-confidence cells are labeled 'unknown' rather than forced into a predicted cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Post-process a trained SIMS/TabNet single-cell classifier with post-hoc temperature scaling to emit calibrated per-cell cluster probabilities, then apply a user-adjustable confidence threshold so that low-confidence cells are labeled 'unknown' rather than forced into a predicted cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is trans-species label transfer — SIMS calibration has only been validated for samples within the same species When no pre-existing annotations are available for training, since temperature scaling calibrates a supervised model that relies on expert-annotated clusters When raw logit ranks (not calibrated confidences) suffice, e.g. quick top-1 label transfer with no downstream confidence gating

skills.description: Use when reconstructing sparse directed GRNs from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell expression data with COSLIR and you must suppress unstable or spurious interaction estimates via bootstrapped confidence and magnitude clipping.
skills.name: confidence-thresholding-interaction-matrix
skills.search_text: confidence-thresholding-interaction-matrix Use when reconstructing sparse directed GRNs from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell expression data with COSLIR and you must suppress unstable or spurious interaction estimates via bootstrapped confidence and magnitude clipping. The goal is to infer the dense GRN maintaining the current cell stage rather than the sparse network driving a transition between consecutive time points. Only a single cell stage/time point is available, so no first and second moments between consecutive time points can be computed. The data are true longitudinal time series with linked cells across time and pseudo-time trajectory methods are appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Stabilizes the COSLIR estimator of the gene-gene interaction matrix by bootstrapping: the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression is refit on resampled cells, coefficients are aggregated into an ensemble, and only entries surviving both a confidence threshold and a small-magnitude clipping threshold are retained as significant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Stabilizes the COSLIR estimator of the gene-gene interaction matrix by bootstrapping: the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression is refit on resampled cells, coefficients are aggregated into an ensemble, and only entries surviving both a confidence threshold and a small-magnitude clipping threshold are retained as significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer the dense GRN maintaining the current cell stage rather than the sparse network driving a transition between consecutive time points. Only a single cell stage/time point is available, so no first and second moments between consecutive time points can be computed. The data are true longitudinal time series with linked cells across time and pseudo-time trajectory methods are appropriate.

skills.description: Use when a supervised 2D embedding must balance cluster separation against trajectory structure: discrete class labels exist per instance and the strength of trust in those labels (clean vs noisy single-cell data) needs an explicit, tunable bias.
skills.name: confidence-weighted-edge-length-contraction
skills.search_text: confidence-weighted-edge-length-contraction Use when a supervised 2D embedding must balance cluster separation against trajectory structure: discrete class labels exist per instance and the strength of trust in those labels (clean vs noisy single-cell data) needs an explicit, tunable bias. Instances lack a discrete class label: GraphEmbed expects 'A discrete label for each instance', so the same-class contraction cannot be applied. The goal is pseudotime ordering on a cluster-level minimum spanning tree rather than an informed 2D layout - TSCAN's cluster-then-MST pipeline is the appropriate tool. A purely unsupervised dimensionality-reduction baseline (PCA, t-SNE, MDS) is required, since injecting class-confidence bias violates the unsupervised setup. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tunes the supervised bias of the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed Kamada-Kawai force layout: desired distances on edges whose endpoints share a class label are contracted to d/(1+C), where C is the class-confidence parameter (-c, default 1.0). This trades off cluster-membership information against density-gradient trajectory information, with C=0.5-1 for clean data and C=5-30 for noisy data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Tunes the supervised bias of the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed Kamada-Kawai force layout: desired distances on edges whose endpoints share a class label are contracted to d/(1+C), where C is the class-confidence parameter (-c, default 1.0). This trades off cluster-membership information against density-gradient trajectory information, with C=0.5-1 for clean data and C=5-30 for noisy data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Instances lack a discrete class label: GraphEmbed expects 'A discrete label for each instance', so the same-class contraction cannot be applied. The goal is pseudotime ordering on a cluster-level minimum spanning tree rather than an informed 2D layout - TSCAN's cluster-then-MST pipeline is the appropriate tool. A purely unsupervised dimensionality-reduction baseline (PCA, t-SNE, MDS) is required, since injecting class-confidence bias violates the unsupervised setup.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking decision-level cluster integration on a simulated dataset with a known ground truth, or when constructing multiple partially matching annotation solutions to test whether a method can reconcile over- and under-clustered inputs.
skills.name: conflicting-annotation-construction
skills.search_text: conflicting-annotation-construction Use when benchmarking decision-level cluster integration on a simulated dataset with a known ground truth, or when constructing multiple partially matching annotation solutions to test whether a method can reconcile over- and under-clustered inputs. Input annotations already agree or are non-conflicting — there is nothing to mix-and-match and ensemble comparison is uninformative No simulated or curated ground truth exists against which Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure can be computed The goal is a production clustering solution rather than a method benchmark, where arbitrarily degraded (over-/under-clustered) inputs would be inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs deliberately conflicting, partially overlapping cell-cluster annotations (e.g., Broad/Median/Fine/Excessive partitions derived from a Splatter-simulated ground truth) so that scTriangulate's mix-and-match integration can be benchmarked against consensus ensemble methods (HGPA, MCLA, HBGF). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Constructs deliberately conflicting, partially overlapping cell-cluster annotations (e.g., Broad/Median/Fine/Excessive partitions derived from a Splatter-simulated ground truth) so that scTriangulate's mix-and-match integration can be benchmarked against consensus ensemble methods (HGPA, MCLA, HBGF).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input annotations already agree or are non-conflicting — there is nothing to mix-and-match and ensemble comparison is uninformative No simulated or curated ground truth exists against which Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure can be computed The goal is a production clustering solution rather than a method benchmark, where arbitrarily degraded (over-/under-clustered) inputs would be inappropriate

skills.description: Use when batch and biology are partially confounded (e.g., each patient processed in a separate batch) and you need to show whether latent factors extracted by ZINB-WaVE capture unwanted technical variation or the biological signal of interest.
skills.name: confounded-model-contrast-analysis
skills.search_text: confounded-model-contrast-analysis Use when batch and biology are partially confounded (e.g., each patient processed in a separate batch) and you need to show whether latent factors extracted by ZINB-WaVE capture unwanted technical variation or the biological signal of interest. Batch and biology are fully crossed (not confounded) — a standard batch-covariate fit directly removes the batch effect and the confounded contrast model is unnecessary. The goal is quantitative DE analysis rather than diagnosing what the latent factors W captured — ZINB-WaVE supervised differential expression was not yet available, only envisioned for a future version. The low-dimensional signal from W is being interpreted as biologically relevant without checking covariates — there is no guarantee the extracted signal is biologically relevant. Fit a deliberately confounded ZINB-WaVE model (sample-level covariate matrix encoding the batch indicator, which is confounded with patient/biology) and contrast its estimated W matrix against the detection-rate-covariate fit, to demonstrate whether the low-dimensional factors capture technical batch effects instead of biology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Fit a deliberately confounded ZINB-WaVE model (sample-level covariate matrix encoding the batch indicator, which is confounded with patient/biology) and contrast its estimated W matrix against the detection-rate-covariate fit, to demonstrate whether the low-dimensional factors capture technical batch effects instead of biology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Batch and biology are fully crossed (not confounded) — a standard batch-covariate fit directly removes the batch effect and the confounded contrast model is unnecessary. The goal is quantitative DE analysis rather than diagnosing what the latent factors W captured — ZINB-WaVE supervised differential expression was not yet available, only envisioned for a future version. The low-dimensional signal from W is being interpreted as biologically relevant without checking covariates — there is no guarantee the extracted signal is biologically relevant.

skills.description: Use when you have donor-aggregated single-cell type/state counts (e.g. WATLAS annotations for 46 donors) and must test whether a condition such as obesity shifts cell-type composition while controlling for covariates like depot and sex.
skills.name: confounder-adjusted-linear-modeling
skills.search_text: confounder-adjusted-linear-modeling Use when you have donor-aggregated single-cell type/state counts (e.g. WATLAS annotations for 46 donors) and must test whether a condition such as obesity shifts cell-type composition while controlling for covariates like depot and sex. Input is raw per-cell data without donor-level aggregation or donor metadata (weight status, depot, sex) — donor-level fractions and covariates are required for the lm() design. The goal is joint clustering or batch integration of single-cell datasets — use JOINTLY for that; this skill only quantifies compositional differences after annotation exists. Multi-condition, multi-sample batch-effect correction is needed at the expression level — the JOINTLY article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY for such datasets, not composition regression. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits per-cell-type ordinary linear regressions of donor-level cell-type/state fractions on disease weight status, depot and sex to quantify compositional changes in the WATLAS white adipose tissue atlas, extracting marginal effect sizes (regression coefficients) with 95% confidence intervals per contrast. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Fits per-cell-type ordinary linear regressions of donor-level cell-type/state fractions on disease weight status, depot and sex to quantify compositional changes in the WATLAS white adipose tissue atlas, extracting marginal effect sizes (regression coefficients) with 95% confidence intervals per contrast.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw per-cell data without donor-level aggregation or donor metadata (weight status, depot, sex) — donor-level fractions and covariates are required for the lm() design. The goal is joint clustering or batch integration of single-cell datasets — use JOINTLY for that; this skill only quantifies compositional differences after annotation exists. Multi-condition, multi-sample batch-effect correction is needed at the expression level — the JOINTLY article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY for such datasets, not composition regression.

skills.name: confusion-matrix-accuracy-auc-evaluation
skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-accuracy-auc-evaluation Use when comparing two or more supervised classifiers on the same held-out test split and you need comparable metrics (confusion matrix, accuracy, AUC) to rank them, e.g. malignant vs nonMalignant cell prediction. When only a single trained model exists and there is no second classifier to rank against — a plain per-model metric report suffices and no comparison table is needed. When the training and validation data share samples (no sample-source split), because leakage would inflate accuracy/AUC and invalidate the comparison. For unsupervised cell clustering or annotation outputs with no ground-truth labels, since confusion matrix, accuracy, and AUC all require reference labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates trained cell-state classifiers (XGBoost, ElasticNet, Neural Network) on a held-out validation split by computing confusion matrices, accuracy, and AUC, enabling head-to-head comparison of malignancy predictors as done in scCancer2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Evaluates trained cell-state classifiers (XGBoost, ElasticNet, Neural Network) on a held-out validation split by computing confusion matrices, accuracy, and AUC, enabling head-to-head comparison of malignancy predictors as done in scCancer2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single trained model exists and there is no second classifier to rank against — a plain per-model metric report suffices and no comparison table is needed. When the training and validation data share samples (no sample-source split), because leakage would inflate accuracy/AUC and invalidate the comparison. For unsupervised cell clustering or annotation outputs with no ground-truth labels, since confusion matrix, accuracy, and AUC all require reference labels.

skills.description: Use when predicted cell type labels from marker-based scoring (e.g., GeneVector phenotype_probability) must be validated against reference annotations via a confusion matrix with per-type accuracy and overall misclassification rate.
skills.name: confusion-matrix-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-accuracy-benchmarking Use when predicted cell type labels from marker-based scoring (e.g., GeneVector phenotype_probability) must be validated against reference annotations via a confusion matrix with per-type accuracy and overall misclassification rate. No reference or ground-truth cell type annotations exist for the dataset — per-type accuracy cannot be computed without a published label to compare against. The goal is assessing clustering or embedding quality rather than label accuracy — the article instead benchmarks those with ARI, kBET, cLISI, and silhouette score (Supplementary Fig. 6A–L). Fine-grained subtype annotation is required — the benchmarked marker sets cover only the three lineage-level categories T cell, B/Plasma, and Myeloid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks marker-based cell type predictions by cross-tabulating GeneVector's argmax 'genevector' labels against CellTypist-derived reference annotations on the TICA subset, producing a confusion matrix with per-type accuracies (97.1% T cell, 95% myeloid, 94.3% B/Plasma) and a 3.977% overall misclassification rate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks marker-based cell type predictions by cross-tabulating GeneVector's argmax 'genevector' labels against CellTypist-derived reference annotations on the TICA subset, producing a confusion matrix with per-type accuracies (97.1% T cell, 95% myeloid, 94.3% B/Plasma) and a 3.977% overall misclassification rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference or ground-truth cell type annotations exist for the dataset — per-type accuracy cannot be computed without a published label to compare against. The goal is assessing clustering or embedding quality rather than label accuracy — the article instead benchmarks those with ARI, kBET, cLISI, and silhouette score (Supplementary Fig. 6A–L). Fine-grained subtype annotation is required — the benchmarked marker sets cover only the three lineage-level categories T cell, B/Plasma, and Myeloid.

skills.description: Use when predicted single-cell clone labels (e.g., from vireoSNP on mtDNA variants) must be validated against ground-truth source/population labels, and a concordance percentage or confusion matrix is the required benchmark output.
