skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-evaluation-against-source-labels Use when predicted single-cell clone labels (e.g., from vireoSNP on mtDNA variants) must be validated against ground-truth source/population labels, and a concordance percentage or confusion matrix is the required benchmark output. No independent ground-truth labels (e.g., source population or donor identity) exist for the cells — concordance cannot be computed and only unsupervised clonal structure can be assessed Predictions come from nuclear SNV/CNV-based methods with different clone definitions that do not correspond one-to-one to mitochondrial clones The goal is caller performance on simulated data without known clone-source structure; use the simulation-specific selection criteria (average depth >50, VAF >1% in >5% of cells) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluates single-cell clonal assignment accuracy by cross-tabulating vireoSNP-predicted mitochondrial clones against known source populations (e.g., PDX pRCC, PDX mRCC, Pt mRCC) and reporting assignment concordance, as done to benchmark MQuad (93% concordance, ~146 variants) versus mgatk (64% concordance, 312 mtSNVs) on the Kim ccRCC Smart-seq2 dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Evaluates single-cell clonal assignment accuracy by cross-tabulating vireoSNP-predicted mitochondrial clones against known source populations (e.g., PDX pRCC, PDX mRCC, Pt mRCC) and reporting assignment concordance, as done to benchmark MQuad (93% concordance, ~146 variants) versus mgatk (64% concordance, 312 mtSNVs) on the Kim ccRCC Smart-seq2 dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent ground-truth labels (e.g., source population or donor identity) exist for the cells — concordance cannot be computed and only unsupervised clonal structure can be assessed Predictions come from nuclear SNV/CNV-based methods with different clone definitions that do not correspond one-to-one to mitochondrial clones The goal is caller performance on simulated data without known clone-source structure; use the simulation-specific selection criteria (average depth >50, VAF >1% in >5% of cells) instead

skills.description: Use when an inferred GRN must be quantitatively scored against an undirected typed gold standard (e.g., DREAM 4) using edge-level confusion-matrix metrics.
skills.name: confusion-matrix-metric-calculation
skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-metric-calculation Use when an inferred GRN must be quantitatively scored against an undirected typed gold standard (e.g., DREAM 4) using edge-level confusion-matrix metrics. The network to evaluate is a directed, signed Boolean model rather than an undirected edge list compared against an undirected typed gold standard — the required simplification (dropping interaction types, making edges positive) is specific to edge-level GRN scoring. The goal is ranking metrics such as AUROC or AUPR on a scored edge list rather than thresholded confusion-matrix proportions (sensitivity/specificity/accuracy). No gold standard network exists for the organism or dataset, so true positives and true negatives cannot be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Evaluates inferred gene regulatory networks by building a confusion matrix of predicted versus true (gold standard) edges and deriving sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, as done for Augusta's DREAM 4 normalization benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Evaluates inferred gene regulatory networks by building a confusion matrix of predicted versus true (gold standard) edges and deriving sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy, as done for Augusta's DREAM 4 normalization benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network to evaluate is a directed, signed Boolean model rather than an undirected edge list compared against an undirected typed gold standard — the required simplification (dropping interaction types, making edges positive) is specific to edge-level GRN scoring. The goal is ranking metrics such as AUROC or AUPR on a scored edge list rather than thresholded confusion-matrix proportions (sensitivity/specificity/accuracy). No gold standard network exists for the organism or dataset, so true positives and true negatives cannot be defined.

skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-normalization-and-binarization Use when two aligned, labeled scRNA-seq datasets (AnnData with label and batch metadata) have been cross-predicted by scHPL classifiers and you must decide which population labels match, merge, split, or are new before updating the classification tree. skills.summary: Performs single-cell drug repurposing by reversing disease differential-expression signatures against LINCS L1000 Level 5 perturbation profiles, ranking FDA-approved drugs per cell cluster with a connectivity/outlier-sum statistic (ASGARD GetDrug), then aggregating into a patient-level multi-cluster drug score (DrugScore).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq data without cell clusters — ASGARD's advantage (multi-cluster drug score) was benchmarked against bulk methods like CLUE and DrInsight precisely for heterogeneous single-cell data Disease is driven by a single cell type and no normal-tissue control exists — the article notes obtaining proper normal samples may not be feasible for some diseases A tissue-specific LINCS L1000 drug reference is unavailable for the target disease, since the reference covers only 98 cell lines

skills.description: Use when you have a set of Minimum Spanning Trees (one per clustering from Totem/Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings or pinpoint trajectory leaves and branching points.
skills.name: connectivity-vector-normalization-and-averaging
skills.search_text: connectivity-vector-normalization-and-averaging Use when you have a set of Minimum Spanning Trees (one per clustering from Totem/Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings or pinpoint trajectory leaves and branching points. Input is a single clustering/trajectory with only one MST — no averaging over L' clusterings is possible and Totem's connectivity ranking is not defined. The dataset contains disconnected components or cycles, since Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories with cycles. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Totem's per-cell connectivity from the set of Minimum Spanning Trees built by Slingshot over CLARA clusterings: for each MST, per-vertex connectivity is derived from inverse edge weights scaled by vertex degree, each clustering's vector is scaled to a maximum of 1, and the L' vectors are averaged arithmetically. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Computes Totem's per-cell connectivity from the set of Minimum Spanning Trees built by Slingshot over CLARA clusterings: for each MST, per-vertex connectivity is derived from inverse edge weights scaled by vertex degree, each clustering's vector is scaled to a maximum of 1, and the L' vectors are averaged arithmetically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single clustering/trajectory with only one MST — no averaging over L' clusterings is possible and Totem's connectivity ranking is not defined. The dataset contains disconnected components or cycles, since Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories with cycles.

skills.description: Use when auditing, extending, or re-deriving Connectome edgeweight attributes (weight_sc vs weight_norm) on a Seurat scRNA-seq object and you must prove how weight_sc is computed from scaled ligand/receptor z-scores.
skills.name: connectome-edge-attribute-validation
skills.search_text: connectome-edge-attribute-validation Use when auditing, extending, or re-deriving Connectome edgeweight attributes (weight_sc vs weight_norm) on a Seurat scRNA-seq object and you must prove how weight_sc is computed from scaled ligand/receptor z-scores. Your goal is downstream signaling analysis (NetworkPlot, Centrality, differential connectomics) rather than validating how the edgeweight itself is defined — use FilterConnectome-style workflows instead Your input is not a Seurat object with identifiable cell-type identities, or you lack a user-supplied/FANTOM5 ligand-receptor reference, so CreateConnectome cannot generate the reference weight_sc column to validate against You expect weightscale to measure absolute raw co-expression strength — it is a system z-score-based specificity metric, not a connectivity metric like weight_norm http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Independently reconstructs Connectome's weightscale (weight_sc) edgeweight — the mean of gene-wise system z-scores (ligand.scale and recept.scale) of the ligand and receptor — and verifies it edge-by-edge against CreateConnectome output, confirming it encodes signal specificity rather than raw connectivity (weight_norm). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Independently reconstructs Connectome's weightscale (weight_sc) edgeweight — the mean of gene-wise system z-scores (ligand.scale and recept.scale) of the ligand and receptor — and verifies it edge-by-edge against CreateConnectome output, confirming it encodes signal specificity rather than raw connectivity (weight_norm).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is downstream signaling analysis (NetworkPlot, Centrality, differential connectomics) rather than validating how the edgeweight itself is defined — use FilterConnectome-style workflows instead Your input is not a Seurat object with identifiable cell-type identities, or you lack a user-supplied/FANTOM5 ligand-receptor reference, so CreateConnectome cannot generate the reference weight_sc column to validate against You expect weightscale to measure absolute raw co-expression strength — it is a system z-score-based specificity metric, not a connectivity metric like weight_norm

skills.description: Use when a CreateConnectome edgelist from single-cell RNA-seq data contains low-confidence ligand-receptor edges (low percent-expressed or weakly scaled expression) that must be pruned before centrality, network plotting, or circos visualization.
skills.name: connectome-edge-filtering-by-expression
skills.search_text: connectome-edge-filtering-by-expression Use when a CreateConnectome edgelist from single-cell RNA-seq data contains low-confidence ligand-receptor edges (low percent-expressed or weakly scaled expression) that must be pruned before centrality, network plotting, or circos visualization. The object is still a raw Seurat object that has not been normalized, scaled on ligand/receptor genes, and converted by CreateConnectome — filtering requires the edgelist with pct.expressing and z-score attributes The goal is differential comparison between two conditions — use DifferentialConnectome on matched connectomes instead of expression-based edge filtering Cell identities (clusters) contain fewer than ~75 cells, so edge statistics are unstable and should be excluded via min.cells.per.ident upstream rather than filtered post hoc http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reduces the large ligand-receptor edgelist produced by CreateConnectome to biologically credible edges by filtering on the fraction of cells expressing ligand and receptor (min.pct), on expression z-scores (min.z), and on minimum cells per cell identity, using the Connectome FilterConnectome function in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Reduces the large ligand-receptor edgelist produced by CreateConnectome to biologically credible edges by filtering on the fraction of cells expressing ligand and receptor (min.pct), on expression z-scores (min.z), and on minimum cells per cell identity, using the Connectome FilterConnectome function in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The object is still a raw Seurat object that has not been normalized, scaled on ligand/receptor genes, and converted by CreateConnectome — filtering requires the edgelist with pct.expressing and z-score attributes The goal is differential comparison between two conditions — use DifferentialConnectome on matched connectomes instead of expression-based edge filtering Cell identities (clusters) contain fewer than ~75 cells, so edge statistics are unstable and should be excluded via min.cells.per.ident upstream rather than filtered post hoc

skills.description: Use when independently reimplementing a Connectome edge statistic (e.g. weight_norm) and needing proof of numerical agreement with CreateConnectome output on a shared edge set.
skills.name: connectome-output-consistency-verification
skills.search_text: connectome-output-consistency-verification Use when independently reimplementing a Connectome edge statistic (e.g. weight_norm) and needing proof of numerical agreement with CreateConnectome output on a shared edge set. When the goal is biological interpretation of the connectome (e.g. filtering with min.pct/min.z or visualization) rather than validating the weight_norm arithmetic When the input object differs from the one fed to CreateConnectome (different normalization, identity slot, or min.cells.per.ident threshold) — edge sets will not match and the comparison is invalid When inferring actual cell–cell communication: the article warns that strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of communication http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A verification skill that reconstructs the Connectome weight_norm (w1) edgeweight — the product of celltype-wise normalized ligand expression in the sender and normalized receptor expression in the receiver — outside the package, then numerically checks it against the weight_norm column emitted by CreateConnectome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: A verification skill that reconstructs the Connectome weight_norm (w1) edgeweight — the product of celltype-wise normalized ligand expression in the sender and normalized receptor expression in the receiver — outside the package, then numerically checks it against the weight_norm column emitted by CreateConnectome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biological interpretation of the connectome (e.g. filtering with min.pct/min.z or visualization) rather than validating the weight_norm arithmetic When the input object differs from the one fed to CreateConnectome (different normalization, identity slot, or min.cells.per.ident threshold) — edge sets will not match and the comparison is invalid When inferring actual cell–cell communication: the article warns that strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of communication

skills.description: Use when you have scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq batch data plus a separate paired scRNA-seq/ADT (CITE-seq) dataset and need to predict protein (ADT) abundance for cells measured only by scATAC-seq, chaining epigenome→transcriptome→proteome inference.
skills.name: consecutive-multi-omics-chain-inference
skills.search_text: consecutive-multi-omics-chain-inference Use when you have scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq batch data plus a separate paired scRNA-seq/ADT (CITE-seq) dataset and need to predict protein (ADT) abundance for cells measured only by scATAC-seq, chaining epigenome→transcriptome→proteome inference. When directly paired multi-omics data covering all target modalities is available — single paired translation between two modalities suffices. When the target modality is spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C — the article names these only as future extensions not yet supported. When only transcriptome-level predictions are needed — the epigenome-to-transcriptome translator alone is sufficient without chaining to the CITE model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Chains two trained scButterfly translators so single-modality scATAC-seq cells can be mapped first to predicted scRNA-seq profiles and then to predicted ADT (protein) profiles, enabling proteome-level analysis from epigenome-only measurements via consecutive translation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Chains two trained scButterfly translators so single-modality scATAC-seq cells can be mapped first to predicted scRNA-seq profiles and then to predicted ADT (protein) profiles, enabling proteome-level analysis from epigenome-only measurements via consecutive translation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When directly paired multi-omics data covering all target modalities is available — single paired translation between two modalities suffices. When the target modality is spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C — the article names these only as future extensions not yet supported. When only transcriptome-level predictions are needed — the epigenome-to-transcriptome translator alone is sufficient without chaining to the CITE model.

skills.description: Use when input is time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data (no true longitudinal linkage) and the goal is a GRN driving cell-state transitions between consecutive time points.
skills.name: consecutive-time-point-pair-grn-modeling
skills.search_text: consecutive-time-point-pair-grn-modeling Use when input is time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data (no true longitudinal linkage) and the goal is a GRN driving cell-state transitions between consecutive time points. The goal is to infer the GRN that maintains a single current cell state/time point rather than the mechanism driving the transition along the cell lineage (most alternative TSCS methods are limited to a single stage) Data are true longitudinal single-cell time series with real temporal linkage of individual cells — COSLIR is designed for TSCS data lacking pseudo-time/real temporal information An accurate pseudo-time trajectory already exists and downstream methods depend on it; COSLIR intentionally bypasses pseudo-time inference rather than refining it http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reconstructs directed, signed, weighted gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cell-state transitions from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell RNA-seq/qPCR data by running COSLIR on each consecutive time-point pair, using only the first and second moments of the samples instead of pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Reconstructs directed, signed, weighted gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cell-state transitions from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell RNA-seq/qPCR data by running COSLIR on each consecutive time-point pair, using only the first and second moments of the samples instead of pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer the GRN that maintains a single current cell state/time point rather than the mechanism driving the transition along the cell lineage (most alternative TSCS methods are limited to a single stage) Data are true longitudinal single-cell time series with real temporal linkage of individual cells — COSLIR is designed for TSCS data lacking pseudo-time/real temporal information An accurate pseudo-time trajectory already exists and downstream methods depend on it; COSLIR intentionally bypasses pseudo-time inference rather than refining it

skills.description: Use when clustering transcriptome data (bulk or single-cell) with an unknown number of clusters and you must algorithmically decide the optimal k and when to stop subdividing clusters, as done inside RCC_clus.
skills.name: consensus-cdf-plateau-analysis
skills.search_text: consensus-cdf-plateau-analysis Use when clustering transcriptome data (bulk or single-cell) with an unknown number of clusters and you must algorithmically decide the optimal k and when to stop subdividing clusters, as done inside RCC_clus. The number of clusters is already known and only needs to be imposed, so no best-k search or CDF plateau analysis is needed Input is not a transcriptomic (bulk or single-cell) expression matrix, since RCC's CDF-based k selection was designed and validated for such data Computational time is a hard constraint on very large datasets, given RCC's stated limitation that its runtime depends on the underlying consensus clustering with k-means base algorithm http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the optimal number of clusters (k) within each parallel run of Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) by reading the cumulative distribution function (CDF) plots generated by ConsensusClusterPlus and applying a plateau criterion, followed by cluster-quality gates (stability, overlap, DE genes) and recursive subdivision termination rules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Selects the optimal number of clusters (k) within each parallel run of Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) by reading the cumulative distribution function (CDF) plots generated by ConsensusClusterPlus and applying a plateau criterion, followed by cluster-quality gates (stability, overlap, DE genes) and recursive subdivision termination rules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters is already known and only needs to be imposed, so no best-k search or CDF plateau analysis is needed Input is not a transcriptomic (bulk or single-cell) expression matrix, since RCC's CDF-based k selection was designed and validated for such data Computational time is a hard constraint on very large datasets, given RCC's stated limitation that its runtime depends on the underlying consensus clustering with k-means base algorithm

skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-combination Use when you have multiple cell embeddings (e.g. VAE snapshot embeddings from CITE-seq or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq modalities) or clusterings over the same cells and need a single consensus cluster label per cell. When you have only a single embedding or a single precomputed clustering of the cells — consensus combination requires multiple clusterings to reconcile When cells differ across embeddings/clustering runs (e.g. different cell subsets), since the consensus loop assumes every clustering covers the same cell set When you need dataset-optimal hyperparameters for a new dataset: the tutorial 'only explains how to use this package; it doesn't recommend the best parameters for your datasets' — parameters must come from analogous published work, not the consensus step itself http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Combines per-embedding clusterings of multimodal single-cell omics data into a single set of consensus cell labels via SnapCCESS's ensemble snapshot approach and the clue cl_consensus fixed-point loop, avoiding the cost of conventional ensemble deep learning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Combines per-embedding clusterings of multimodal single-cell omics data into a single set of consensus cell labels via SnapCCESS's ensemble snapshot approach and the clue cl_consensus fixed-point loop, avoiding the cost of conventional ensemble deep learning.

skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-of-bulk-transcriptomes Use when you have a curated bulk PDAC expression dataset (e.g. TCGA-PAAD whitelisted to 150 PDAC samples) and gene-symbol-level subtype signatures, and you need to assign subtype labels or compare concordance between subtyping schemes. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use the rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas and classifier instead; bulk-consensus subtyping cannot separate cellular populations The dataset is uncurated TCGA-PAAD (all 182 samples) — non-PDAC tumors must be removed via the 'Decision'/'whitelist' filter first or signature derivation/validation is misled You need to interchangeably relabel samples as basal-like, squamous, or QM without measuring overlap — the paper shows the collapsed signatures are not completely redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Derives subtype groups from bulk PDAC expression matrices by restricting to curated subtype gene signatures (Moffitt, Collisson, Bailey) loaded from pdacR and clustering samples with ConsensusClusterPlus, enabling cross-scheme subtype concordance testing (~60% overlap between analogous calls). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Derives subtype groups from bulk PDAC expression matrices by restricting to curated subtype gene signatures (Moffitt, Collisson, Bailey) loaded from pdacR and clustering samples with ConsensusClusterPlus, enabling cross-scheme subtype concordance testing (~60% overlap between analogous calls).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use the rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas and classifier instead; bulk-consensus subtyping cannot separate cellular populations The dataset is uncurated TCGA-PAAD (all 182 samples) — non-PDAC tumors must be removed via the 'Decision'/'whitelist' filter first or signature derivation/validation is misled You need to interchangeably relabel samples as basal-like, squamous, or QM without measuring overlap — the paper shows the collapsed signatures are not completely redundant

skills.description: Use when validating whether a published gene signature is PDAC-specific: cluster genes (not samples) across two or more curated bulk RNAseq datasets and measure cross-signature overlap fractions to expose tissue-nonspecific or contaminant gene subsets.
skills.name: consensus-clustering-of-gene-expression
skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-of-gene-expression Use when validating whether a published gene signature is PDAC-specific: cluster genes (not samples) across two or more curated bulk RNAseq datasets and measure cross-signature overlap fractions to expose tissue-nonspecific or contaminant gene subsets. Input data are single-cell profiles rather than bulk RNAseq — the pdacR platform houses only bulk analyses and cannot fully separate cellular populations Datasets come from mixed platforms (bulk RNA-seq plus microarrays) and you intend to merge them into one clustering input — the authors found aggregation 'introduced more problems than it solved' The analysis goal is clustering samples/patients into subtypes (e.g., basal-like vs classical) rather than decomposing a gene signature at the gene level http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Gene-wise consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus, kmeans, euclidean distance) applied across multiple curated PDAC RNAseq datasets to test whether published subtype signatures like the Bailey ADEX set are confounded by non-PDAC-specific gene subsets, and to quantify gene-set overlaps (e.g., Immunogenic vs pancreatic progenitor and ADEX signatures). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Gene-wise consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus, kmeans, euclidean distance) applied across multiple curated PDAC RNAseq datasets to test whether published subtype signatures like the Bailey ADEX set are confounded by non-PDAC-specific gene subsets, and to quantify gene-set overlaps (e.g., Immunogenic vs pancreatic progenitor and ADEX signatures).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are single-cell profiles rather than bulk RNAseq — the pdacR platform houses only bulk analyses and cannot fully separate cellular populations Datasets come from mixed platforms (bulk RNA-seq plus microarrays) and you intend to merge them into one clustering input — the authors found aggregation 'introduced more problems than it solved' The analysis goal is clustering samples/patients into subtypes (e.g., basal-like vs classical) rather than decomposing a gene signature at the gene level

skills.description: Use when a sample-by-feature landscape (e.g. DCNet-inferred 434-cell-type abundances for ~10,176 TCGA bulk RNA-seq samples) should be partitioned into robust molecular subtypes testable against clinical survival.
skills.name: consensus-clustering-subtype-discovery
skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-subtype-discovery Use when a sample-by-feature landscape (e.g. DCNet-inferred 434-cell-type abundances for ~10,176 TCGA bulk RNA-seq samples) should be partitioned into robust molecular subtypes testable against clinical survival. Input is raw or unnormalized gene expression rather than a DCNet-inferred cell abundance landscape — consensus clustering here is defined on the inferred landscape, not the expression matrix The goal is deconvolution of cell fractions itself; use DCNet (or comparison tools such as CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) first — clustering is a downstream step Samples lack matched clinical survival data, making the IPS/NIPS survival-separation evaluation impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Robust patient stratification by running ConsensusClusterPlus (manhattan distance, PAM clustering, 1000 iterations) on DCNet-inferred cell-type abundance landscapes, yielding two TME subtypes (IPS and NIPS) from 10,176 TCGA tumor samples that differ in overall survival and cell-type composition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Robust patient stratification by running ConsensusClusterPlus (manhattan distance, PAM clustering, 1000 iterations) on DCNet-inferred cell-type abundance landscapes, yielding two TME subtypes (IPS and NIPS) from 10,176 TCGA tumor samples that differ in overall survival and cell-type composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unnormalized gene expression rather than a DCNet-inferred cell abundance landscape — consensus clustering here is defined on the inferred landscape, not the expression matrix The goal is deconvolution of cell fractions itself; use DCNet (or comparison tools such as CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) first — clustering is a downstream step Samples lack matched clinical survival data, making the IPS/NIPS survival-separation evaluation impossible

skills.description: Use when a synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark with planted generative patterns (identity and activity states) is available and you need to quantify whether a decomposition method recovers them better than consensus NMF, LDA, ICA, or Louvain baselines.
skills.name: consensus-decomposition-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: consensus-decomposition-baseline-comparison Use when a synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark with planted generative patterns (identity and activity states) is available and you need to quantify whether a decomposition method recovers them better than consensus NMF, LDA, ICA, or Louvain baselines. Data are real (non-synthetic) cells with no planted generative patterns, since recovery purity cannot be computed by matching to planted patterns. The analysis goal is cell-type discovery on a new dataset rather than benchmarking decomposition methods against each other. Baseline methods require a priori component selection and the planted pattern count is unknown, making the fixed-component comparison invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks ACTIONet's multiresolution archetypal decomposition against consensus baselines (consensus NMF, LDA, ICA, and Louvain clustering) on synthetic scRNA-seq data by measuring pattern-recovery purity for planted identity and activity patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks ACTIONet's multiresolution archetypal decomposition against consensus baselines (consensus NMF, LDA, ICA, and Louvain clustering) on synthetic scRNA-seq data by measuring pattern-recovery purity for planted identity and activity patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real (non-synthetic) cells with no planted generative patterns, since recovery purity cannot be computed by matching to planted patterns. The analysis goal is cell-type discovery on a new dataset rather than benchmarking decomposition methods against each other. Baseline methods require a priori component selection and the planted pattern count is unknown, making the fixed-component comparison invalid.

skills.summary: Compute a single consensus regulator activity score in decoupleR by aggregating multiple methods' activity estimates via a mean z-score per regulator, which the decoupleR benchmark found among the top-performing approaches for predicting perturbed regulators.

skills.description: Use when a single-locus long-read RNA-seq analysis (BAM/GFF3/BED6 input) misses known isoforms under VIsoQLR's default 2% CEC threshold, or when a documented sensitivity/quantification trade-off curve for the threshold is needed before manual curation.
skills.name: consensus-exon-coordinate-threshold-tuning
skills.search_text: consensus-exon-coordinate-threshold-tuning Use when a single-locus long-read RNA-seq analysis (BAM/GFF3/BED6 input) misses known isoforms under VIsoQLR's default 2% CEC threshold, or when a documented sensitivity/quantification trade-off curve for the threshold is needed before manual curation. Goal is whole-transcriptome de novo isoform discovery across many genes — VIsoQLR is designed for close inspection and fine-tuning of one gene at a time in low-throughput splicing assays Input is raw FASTQ with no reference-guided alignment step performed — build the GMAP index and align first, or the CEC proportions among mapped reads cannot be computed All target isoforms have abundances well above the default 2% and quantification already matches the reference — threshold tuning adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sweeps the VIsoQLR 'Read threshold (%)' parameter used to select candidate consensus exon coordinates (CECs) to balance isoform detection sensitivity against quantification accuracy for a single gene. skills.summary: Sweeps the VIsoQLR 'Read threshold (%)' parameter used to select candidate consensus exon coordinates (CECs) to balance isoform detection sensitivity against quantification accuracy for a single gene. skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq gene-by-cell expression data must be ordered along a linear pseudo-developmental time axis without cell type labels, e.g. neural stem cell differentiation.
skills.name: consensus-hamiltonian-path-inference
skills.search_text: consensus-hamiltonian-path-inference Use when single-cell RNA-seq gene-by-cell expression data must be ordered along a linear pseudo-developmental time axis without cell type labels, e.g. neural stem cell differentiation. The developmental trajectory is expected to be branched rather than linear — use the transition-matrix PCA trajectory-detection approach instead of a single cHMT ordering Cell type labels are available and a supervised ordering would suffice, or the input is not a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix The dataset requires removing cycling genes via traditional cell-cycle-effect removal — redPATH instead relies on GO subsetting and dispersion filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 redPATH's consensus Hamiltonian path (cHMT) algorithm reconstructs pseudotime for linear developmental trajectories by merging multiple noisy asymmetric Hamiltonian path solutions over a base path range, using symmetric KL divergence cell-to-cell distances computed via Rcpp. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: redPATH's consensus Hamiltonian path (cHMT) algorithm reconstructs pseudotime for linear developmental trajectories by merging multiple noisy asymmetric Hamiltonian path solutions over a base path range, using symmetric KL divergence cell-to-cell distances computed via Rcpp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The developmental trajectory is expected to be branched rather than linear — use the transition-matrix PCA trajectory-detection approach instead of a single cHMT ordering Cell type labels are available and a supervised ordering would suffice, or the input is not a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix The dataset requires removing cycling genes via traditional cell-cycle-effect removal — redPATH instead relies on GO subsetting and dispersion filtering

The goal is a binary/qualitative representation of cells from dropout-strengthened genes — that is the LC1 module, not LC2 You need final cell cluster labels rather than the quantitative landmark feature matrix — that requires the CC (cluster constructor) and label propagation modules downstream Fewer than ~2000 informative genes or datasets where filtering 2.5%/97.5% and HVG retention would remove the signal under study (article notes HVG retention excluded some informative genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the quantitative low-dimensional landmark representation (LM2) of single-cell RNA-seq data by discretizing expression into k bins, clustering quasi-trend-preserved genes within bin-count groups via Spearman-rank similarity graphs and iterative assignment, and joining retained gene clusters into a cell-by-landmark consensus matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021

skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to identify shared activity GEPs across cell types — cNMF recovered almost no activity programs on MCA (1 of 137) and will underperform versus SingleCellGGM (18 activity GEPs) The dataset has fewer than ~5,000 cells or unfiltered low-expression genes, which prevents reliable matrix factorization and co-expression analysis

skills.description: Use when you have an ensemble of simulated cell state sequences (e.g., from Markov sampling of an RNA-velocity transition matrix) and need a single consensus trajectory per terminal region.
skills.name: consensus-trajectory-averaging
skills.search_text: consensus-trajectory-averaging Use when you have an ensemble of simulated cell state sequences (e.g., from Markov sampling of an RNA-velocity transition matrix) and need a single consensus trajectory per terminal region. The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or root/terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probability with no discernible pattern, as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) Root/terminal state inference is spurious due to violated scvelo assumptions, e.g., features with time-dependent degradation rates as in the simulated erythroid gastrulation case You need a single global trajectory topology upfront — Cytopath imposes no topological constraints, so this skill is inappropriate when a rigid tree/cycle model must be enforced before simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts an ensemble of Markov-sampled differentiation trajectories from the Cytopath simulation engine into a consensus lineage path by aligning simulations that terminate at a common terminal state with dynamic time warping and averaging cell states at every aligned step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Converts an ensemble of Markov-sampled differentiation trajectories from the Cytopath simulation engine into a consensus lineage path by aligning simulations that terminate at a common terminal state with dynamic time warping and averaging cell states at every aligned step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or root/terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probability with no discernible pattern, as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) Root/terminal state inference is spurious due to violated scvelo assumptions, e.g., features with time-dependent degradation rates as in the simulated erythroid gastrulation case You need a single global trajectory topology upfront — Cytopath imposes no topological constraints, so this skill is inappropriate when a rigid tree/cycle model must be enforced before simulation

skills.description: Use when you have log2(TPM+1) scRNA-seq expression filtered to cycle base genes and need to order unsynchronized cells along the cell cycle without synchronization.
skills.name: consensus-traveling-salesman-ordering
skills.search_text: consensus-traveling-salesman-ordering Use when you have log2(TPM+1) scRNA-seq expression filtered to cycle base genes and need to order unsynchronized cells along the cell cycle without synchronization. The data are synchronized bulk or qPCR/microarray measurements rather than unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome data Expression values have not been log2(TPM+1) normalized and filtered to cycle base genes via get_test_exp The goal is assigning cells to discrete G1/S/G2/M phases rather than recovering a continuous time-series ordering (use get_hmm_order/get_start instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Recover the cell-cycle time-series ordering of unsynchronized single cells using reCAT's consensus-TSP heuristic, which merges Traveling Salesman Problem cycles computed across a range of cluster counts k into a robust pseudo-time ordering of cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Recover the cell-cycle time-series ordering of unsynchronized single cells using reCAT's consensus-TSP heuristic, which merges Traveling Salesman Problem cycles computed across a range of cluster counts k into a robust pseudo-time ordering of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are synchronized bulk or qPCR/microarray measurements rather than unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome data Expression values have not been log2(TPM+1) normalized and filtered to cycle base genes via get_test_exp The goal is assigning cells to discrete G1/S/G2/M phases rather than recovering a continuous time-series ordering (use get_hmm_order/get_start instead)

skills.description: Use when an unsynchronized scRNA-seq matrix restricted to cell-cycle base genes (log2(TPM+1) test_exp) must be converted into a cell time-series ordering for downstream G1/S/G2/M segmentation or pseudo-time scoring.
skills.name: consensus-tsp-ordering
skills.search_text: consensus-tsp-ordering Use when an unsynchronized scRNA-seq matrix restricted to cell-cycle base genes (log2(TPM+1) test_exp) must be converted into a cell time-series ordering for downstream G1/S/G2/M segmentation or pseudo-time scoring. Cells are synchronized or already carry trusted experimental time/stage labels — no pseudo-time ordering is needed The goal is a differentiation or developmental trajectory: reCAT separates cell-cycle analysis from differentiation, which the authors note may introduce bias The expression matrix cannot be restricted to cycle base genes (e.g., genes absent from the 378-gene Cyclebase-based ccgene set), leaving the consensus cycle without its expected signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Order unsynchronized single-cell transcriptomes into a cell-cycle pseudo time-series by merging traveling-salesman cycles computed over Gaussian-mixture clusterings at multiple cluster numbers k, as implemented in reCAT's consensus-TSP heuristic. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Order unsynchronized single-cell transcriptomes into a cell-cycle pseudo time-series by merging traveling-salesman cycles computed over Gaussian-mixture clusterings at multiple cluster numbers k, as implemented in reCAT's consensus-TSP heuristic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are synchronized or already carry trusted experimental time/stage labels — no pseudo-time ordering is needed The goal is a differentiation or developmental trajectory: reCAT separates cell-cycle analysis from differentiation, which the authors note may introduce bias The expression matrix cannot be restricted to cycle base genes (e.g., genes absent from the 378-gene Cyclebase-based ccgene set), leaving the consensus cycle without its expected signal

The input is already an annotated feature/cell-type table rather than raw or normalized single-cell expression data A non-marker-based reference-mapping annotation (e.g. reference-based label transfer with a high-quality comprehensive reference) is preferred; the article notes it did not directly compare against non-marker-based tools The tissue or cell type of interest is absent from the Accordion database's 728 cell types / 212 human tissues collection, and no custom marker table is supplied via accordion_custom() http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate single-cell and spatial omics populations using the Cell Marker Accordion's consistency-weighted marker database, in which each marker carries a specificity score (SPs) and an evidence consistency score (ECs) measuring agreement across annotation sources. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell and spatial omics populations using the Cell Marker Accordion's consistency-weighted marker database, in which each marker carries a specificity score (SPs) and an evidence consistency score (ECs) measuring agreement across annotation sources.

skills.description: Use when binary joint toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) are available per dose and closed-form MLEs of π_jkl are needed subject to a monotonicity order constraint on toxicity probabilities.
skills.name: constrained-maximum-likelihood-estimation
skills.search_text: constrained-maximum-likelihood-estimation Use when binary joint toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) are available per dose and closed-form MLEs of π_jkl are needed subject to a monotonicity order constraint on toxicity probabilities. The response outcome requires long follow-up time to assess, since the TSNP design assumes binary, quickly observable response outcomes Toxicity probabilities are not expected to be monotonically increasing with dose, invalidating the order constraint (1) on which the PAVA and conditional MLE rely A Bayesian parametric joint toxicity-efficacy model with prior-based estimation (e.g., via MCMC) is specifically required; this skill is deliberately nonparametric and closed-form http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Derives closed-form nonparametric estimates of joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_jkl) in the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on PAVA-isotonic DLT rate estimates under the monotonic increasing toxicity constraint, avoiding MCMC or numerical optimization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Derives closed-form nonparametric estimates of joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_jkl) in the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on PAVA-isotonic DLT rate estimates under the monotonic increasing toxicity constraint, avoiding MCMC or numerical optimization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up time to assess, since the TSNP design assumes binary, quickly observable response outcomes Toxicity probabilities are not expected to be monotonically increasing with dose, invalidating the order constraint (1) on which the PAVA and conditional MLE rely A Bayesian parametric joint toxicity-efficacy model with prior-based estimation (e.g., via MCMC) is specifically required; this skill is deliberately nonparametric and closed-form

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether integrating partial prior knowledge as soft pairwise constraints into a scRNA-seq deep clustering model improves clustering or marker-gene specificity versus an unsupervised baseline.

skills.search_text: constrained-vs-unconstrained-clustering-comparison Use when evaluating whether integrating partial prior knowledge as soft pairwise constraints into a scRNA-seq deep clustering model improves clustering or marker-gene specificity versus an unsupervised baseline. When no partial prior knowledge or marker information is available to convert into pairwise constraints — scDCC's advantage over unsupervised clustering relies on such constraints. When the input is not scRNA-seq count data with dropout events and high dimensionality, the motivating setting for this comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking skill for scDCC (Single Cell Deep Constrained Clustering) that compares cluster quality when soft pairwise constraints are added versus purely unsupervised clustering, using repeated runs and statistical tests (e.g., one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on marker-gene specificity scores) to quantify whether prior knowledge improves clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3

skills.when_to_use_negative: When no partial prior knowledge or marker information is available to convert into pairwise constraints — scDCC's advantage over unsupervised clustering relies on such constraints. When the goal is hard-constrained clustering — the article explicitly converts prior knowledge into soft pairwise constraints added to the loss, unlike hard-constrained algorithms such as COP K-means. When the input is not scRNA-seq count data with dropout events and high dimensionality, the motivating setting for this comparison.

skills.description: Use when you have expression data from infected vs. mock tissue (e.g. GSE147507, GSE148729) and need to infer metabolic gene essentiality or drug targets via constraint-based modeling of an infected host model.
skills.name: constraint-based-flux-balance-analysis
skills.search_text: constraint-based-flux-balance-analysis Use when you have expression data from infected vs. mock tissue (e.g. GSE147507, GSE148729) and need to infer metabolic gene essentiality or drug targets via constraint-based modeling of an infected host model. The virus must be modeled as an intracellular replicant with a defined VBOF; the drug predictions here rely on network effects on the host metabolome, not direct docking on the viral proteome, so this skill is wrong for virion-assembly or protein-targeting questions Only lung cell lines represented in the datasets (A549, Calu-3, H1299, NHBE) were modeled; applying to unmodeled tissues requires additional validation and other optimization functions If no viral biomass objective function is available for the virus of interest, essentiality of viral-specific genes cannot be assessed this way http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Apply flux balance analysis (FBA) on context-specific genome-scale metabolic models of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung cells (built with rFASTCORMICS and carrying a viral biomass objective function, VBOF) to identify host essential genes and gene pairs whose in silico knockout reduces viral biomass without affecting host biomass. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Apply flux balance analysis (FBA) on context-specific genome-scale metabolic models of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung cells (built with rFASTCORMICS and carrying a viral biomass objective function, VBOF) to identify host essential genes and gene pairs whose in silico knockout reduces viral biomass without affecting host biomass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The virus must be modeled as an intracellular replicant with a defined VBOF; the drug predictions here rely on network effects on the host metabolome, not direct docking on the viral proteome, so this skill is wrong for virion-assembly or protein-targeting questions Only lung cell lines represented in the datasets (A549, Calu-3, H1299, NHBE) were modeled; applying to unmodeled tissues requires additional validation and other optimization functions If no viral biomass objective function is available for the virus of interest, essentiality of viral-specific genes cannot be assessed this way

skills.name: constraint-based-metabolic-modeling
skills.search_text: constraint-based-metabolic-modeling Use when RNA-seq expression data from infected and mock (control) tissue/cell samples must be turned into context-specific metabolic models for knockout-based essentiality prediction and drug-target screening. The goal is direct docking or interaction modeling against the viral proteome — the virus is only represented through its biomass function, so drug targets reflect network effects on the host metabolome Tissue or cell types outside the modeled lung lines (A549, Calu-3, H1299, NHBE) without additional validation Only expression matrices without a consistent genome-scale reconstruction and gene-mapping dictionary are available http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Reconstruct context-specific genome-scale metabolic models from infected-lung expression data (Recon2.04/Recon3D_01 augmented with the viral biomass objective function) and use flux balance analysis in MATLAB/COBRA Toolbox to identify host genes whose knockout reduces viral biomass, enabling drug repositioning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Reconstruct context-specific genome-scale metabolic models from infected-lung expression data (Recon2.04/Recon3D_01 augmented with the viral biomass objective function) and use flux balance analysis in MATLAB/COBRA Toolbox to identify host genes whose knockout reduces viral biomass, enabling drug repositioning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is direct docking or interaction modeling against the viral proteome — the virus is only represented through its biomass function, so drug targets reflect network effects on the host metabolome Tissue or cell types outside the modeled lung lines (A549, Calu-3, H1299, NHBE) without additional validation Only expression matrices without a consistent genome-scale reconstruction and gene-mapping dictionary are available

skills.name: constraint-based-model-statistics-verification

skills.summary: Reconstructs condition-specific metabolic models from infected and mock lung expression data with rFASTCORMICS and verifies their size statistics (metabolite and reaction counts, medians and ranges) against reported values (50 models: 28 infected, 22 mock).

skills.description: Use when a clustering pipeline consumes prior pairwise constraints and you need to verify that noisy or partially incorrect domain knowledge does not hurt performance relative to running the method without constraints.
skills.name: constraint-perturbation-robustness-analysis
skills.search_text: constraint-perturbation-robustness-analysis Use when a clustering pipeline consumes prior pairwise constraints and you need to verify that noisy or partially incorrect domain knowledge does not hurt performance relative to running the method without constraints. The clustering method being tested does not accept pairwise constraints — there is nothing to perturb and the unsupervised baseline alone suffices. The goal is to assess sensitivity to data corruption (e.g., dropout or gene-count noise) rather than corruption of the supervision/constraints themselves. Ground-truth cell type labels are unavailable for the datasets, so clustering performance scores cannot be computed for the comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A robustness-testing skill that quantifies how a constrained-clustering method (e.g., scDCC) degrades when a controlled fraction of pairwise must-link/cannot-link constraints is deliberately mislabeled. It anchors the assessment against a 0-constraint unsupervised baseline across multiple constraint counts and datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3
skills.summary: A robustness-testing skill that quantifies how a constrained-clustering method (e.g., scDCC) degrades when a controlled fraction of pairwise must-link/cannot-link constraints is deliberately mislabeled. It anchors the assessment against a 0-constraint unsupervised baseline across multiple constraint counts and datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering method being tested does not accept pairwise constraints — there is nothing to perturb and the unsupervised baseline alone suffices. The goal is to assess sensitivity to data corruption (e.g., dropout or gene-count noise) rather than corruption of the supervision/constraints themselves. Ground-truth cell type labels are unavailable for the datasets, so clustering performance scores cannot be computed for the comparison.

skills.description: Use when you have gene sets defined by a genomic property (e.g., tissue-specific vs shared CAFEH colocalization) and continuous constraint scores (LOEUF, pLI) per gene, and you need to test whether the sets differ in selective pressure.
skills.name: constraint-score-wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
skills.search_text: constraint-score-wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing Use when you have gene sets defined by a genomic property (e.g., tissue-specific vs shared CAFEH colocalization) and continuous constraint scores (LOEUF, pLI) per gene, and you need to test whether the sets differ in selective pressure. The input is variant-level or SNP-level data rather than per-gene constraint scores — CAFEH-style fine-mapping, not constraint testing, is the right tool You need to test tissue specificity of eQTL effects themselves rather than downstream functional consequences of defined gene sets Colocalizing signals must be interpreted as mediation — the article warns that colocalization does not necessarily suggest mediation and can arise from horizontal pleiotropy http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A statistical procedure for testing whether gene sets defined by eQTL colocalization structure (e.g., CAFEH top-component sharing across tissues) differ in selective constraint, by comparing LOEUF and pLI score distributions with two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests against a background gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: A statistical procedure for testing whether gene sets defined by eQTL colocalization structure (e.g., CAFEH top-component sharing across tissues) differ in selective constraint, by comparing LOEUF and pLI score distributions with two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests against a background gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is variant-level or SNP-level data rather than per-gene constraint scores — CAFEH-style fine-mapping, not constraint testing, is the right tool You need to test tissue specificity of eQTL effects themselves rather than downstream functional consequences of defined gene sets Colocalizing signals must be interpreted as mediation — the article warns that colocalization does not necessarily suggest mediation and can arise from horizontal pleiotropy

skills.description: Use when you have a labeled expression matrix (e.g., the scGeneFit spectral toy dataset) and need to translate pairwise label relationships into linear constraints for a marker-selection LP solved with scipy.optimize.linprog.
skills.name: constraint-set-construction-from-label-pairs
skills.search_text: constraint-set-construction-from-label-pairs Use when you have a labeled expression matrix (e.g., the scGeneFit spectral toy dataset) and need to translate pairwise label relationships into linear constraints for a marker-selection LP solved with scipy.optimize.linprog. The data are unlabeled or lack a categorical cell-type/label partition — scGeneFit's constraint construction requires given labels; placing unlabeled cells on trajectories or in spatial assays is not supported (only envisioned future work) The marker problem needs nonlinear projection or nonlinear dimension reduction — the formulation assumes linear separability and each subspace dimension aligned with a coordinate axis, which the authors plan to relax only in future work Each gene is being tested separately in a one-vs-all manner (e.g., as with COMET) — this skill instead jointly recovers an optimal set of genes via shared constraints http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds the pairwise constraint set Z(D) from the cell/sample label vector for scGeneFit's slack linear program (Eq. 4), forming the vectors z whose squared components z_j^2 enter the linear constraints. This encodes which cell labels must be discriminated so marker selection can be cast as a single tractable LP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Builds the pairwise constraint set Z(D) from the cell/sample label vector for scGeneFit's slack linear program (Eq. 4), forming the vectors z whose squared components z_j^2 enter the linear constraints. This encodes which cell labels must be discriminated so marker selection can be cast as a single tractable LP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are unlabeled or lack a categorical cell-type/label partition — scGeneFit's constraint construction requires given labels; placing unlabeled cells on trajectories or in spatial assays is not supported (only envisioned future work) The marker problem needs nonlinear projection or nonlinear dimension reduction — the formulation assumes linear separability and each subspace dimension aligned with a coordinate axis, which the authors plan to relax only in future work Each gene is being tested separately in a one-vs-all manner (e.g., as with COMET) — this skill instead jointly recovers an optimal set of genes via shared constraints

skills.description: Use when executing the SkewC workflow (0_split10XbyBarcode.sh, 1_geneBodyCoverage.sh, 2_SkewC.sh) on pbmc_8k or other 10x/ E-MTAB-2600 data, especially on systems without admin rights where the R 'stringi'/libicui18n.so.
skills.name: containerized-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: containerized-pipeline-execution Use when executing the SkewC workflow (0_split10XbyBarcode.sh, 1_geneBodyCoverage.sh, 2_SkewC.sh) on pbmc_8k or other 10x/ E-MTAB-2600 data, especially on systems without admin rights where the R 'stringi'/libicui18n.so. You already have a compatible local R/Perl environment that runs the SkewC bash scripts without errors — containerization adds overhead without benefit. Your task is only user-space image handling (e.g. udocker search/pull/export) unrelated to running the SkewC pipeline. BAM files are already split by cells and you only need the R Markdown analysis — the containerized split step (0_split10XbyBarcode.sh) can be skipped per the README. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run the SkewC scRNA-seq quality-control pipeline (splitting 10x barcoded BAMs, geneBodyCoverage.pl, and R Markdown clustering steps) inside a Docker, udocker, or Singularity container so that the R/Perl stack and dependencies are reproducible. The article ships the workflow as a docker/udocker container and a Singularity Image File (SIF) precisely because the R and Perl implementations are fragile to local installation differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.102038
skills.summary: Run the SkewC scRNA-seq quality-control pipeline (splitting 10x barcoded BAMs, geneBodyCoverage.pl, and R Markdown clustering steps) inside a Docker, udocker, or Singularity container so that the R/Perl stack and dependencies are reproducible. The article ships the workflow as a docker/udocker container and a Singularity Image File (SIF) precisely because the R and Perl implementations are fragile to local installation differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a compatible local R/Perl environment that runs the SkewC bash scripts without errors — containerization adds overhead without benefit. Your task is only user-space image handling (e.g. udocker search/pull/export) unrelated to running the SkewC pipeline. BAM files are already split by cells and you only need the R Markdown analysis — the containerized split step (0_split10XbyBarcode.sh) can be skipped per the README.

skills.search_text: contaminant-rna-sequence-filtering Use when processing Ribo-seq FastQ reads after Cutadapt trimming/length filtering and before genome alignment, to remove reads derived from rRNA, tRNA or other contaminant sequences prior to double-mapping. skills.summary: Depletes unwanted RNA contaminants (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) from adapter- and quality-trimmed, RPF-length-selected reads by aligning them with Bowtie2 to a user-provided contaminant index and keeping only unaligned reads, as implemented in the RiboDoc ribosome profiling pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When fasta_outRNA is left empty in config.yaml — RiboDoc skips this step and passes trimmed reads straight to mapping When the input is raw, untrimmed FastQ — trimming and RPF length selection (25-35 nt) must precede depletion When you need multimapper handling or genome alignment — that is the separate downstream HISAT2/Bowtie2 double-mapping step, not contaminant depletion

skills.description: Use when building the SINCERA S4 object from a raw expression matrix (genes x cells, FPKM/TPM) and you suspect mixed-cell wells or droplets, e.g. cells coexpressing markers of two lineages such as Epcam and Pecam1.
skills.name: contaminated-cell-marker-based-detection
skills.search_text: contaminated-cell-marker-based-detection Use when building the SINCERA S4 object from a raw expression matrix (genes x cells, FPKM/TPM) and you suspect mixed-cell wells or droplets, e.g. cells coexpressing markers of two lineages such as Epcam and Pecam1. Input is a normalized matrix that has already passed cell filtering — filterContaminatedCells operates on the SINCERA S4 object during preprocessing, before z-score normalization via normalization.zscore. No lineage-specific marker genes are known for the tissue; the function requires highly specific markers supplied via markers.1 and markers.2 to be meaningful. The analysis goal is clustering or cell type identification itself rather than data filtering — this skill is explicitly a preprocessing step preceding clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Detects and removes potentially contaminated cells from a scRNA-Seq dataset in SINCERA by testing coexpression of known marker genes (e.g., epithelial vs endothelial markers) using the filterContaminatedCells function, as part of the preprocessing stage before clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Detects and removes potentially contaminated cells from a scRNA-Seq dataset in SINCERA by testing coexpression of known marker genes (e.g., epithelial vs endothelial markers) using the filterContaminatedCells function, as part of the preprocessing stage before clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a normalized matrix that has already passed cell filtering — filterContaminatedCells operates on the SINCERA S4 object during preprocessing, before z-score normalization via normalization.zscore. No lineage-specific marker genes are known for the tissue; the function requires highly specific markers supplied via markers.1 and markers.2 to be meaningful. The analysis goal is clustering or cell type identification itself rather than data filtering — this skill is explicitly a preprocessing step preceding clustering.

The goal is direct docking on the viral proteome — the models represent the virus only through its biomass function, so targets are host-metabolome network effects No consistent generic model, dico gene-mapping table, or MATLAB/COBRA Toolbox environment is available The aim is condition-agnostic analysis of a single generic genome-scale model rather than per-sample context-specific pruning http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Reconstruct and analyze context-specific genome-scale metabolic models from RNA-seq expression data using rFASTCORMICS with the COBRA Toolbox V3, then run in silico gene knockouts against a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) to identify host genes whose knockout reduces viral biomass without affecting host biomass. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is direct docking on the viral proteome — the models represent the virus only through its biomass function, so targets are host-metabolome network effects No consistent generic model, dico gene-mapping table, or MATLAB/COBRA Toolbox environment is available The aim is condition-agnostic analysis of a single generic genome-scale model rather than per-sample context-specific pruning

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is plain whole-genome short-read data from a mammalian-size genome — the README states 'SPAdes is not intended for larger genomes (e.g. mammalian size genomes)'; this skill targets barcoded RNA-seq linked-read isoform assembly. skills.name: contig-to-isoform-assignment
skills.search_text: contig-to-isoform-assignment Use when you have assembled isoform contigs from barcoded or bulk RNA-seq (contigs.fasta) and need to quantify which annotated GENCODE isoforms they recover, per gene, with assignment-class statistics. Input is still raw barcoded FASTQ reads rather than assembled contigs — run read error correction (BayesHammer) and cloudrnaSPAdes assembly first The target organism lacks a curated transcript annotation (e.g. no GENCODE GTF), since unique isoform-level assignment depends on a reference transcript set The goal is reference-free isoform assembly itself rather than evaluating assembled contigs against an annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Assign de novo assembled isoform contigs (e.g. contigs.fasta from cloudrnaSPAdes) to annotated reference transcripts using IsoQuant against GENCODE v32 on GRCh38, classifying each contig as unique, minor-difference, ambiguous, inconsistent, or uninformative and computing per-gene isoform precision/recall. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781

skills.description: Use when validating an over-representation claim: a predicted/clustered gene list must be tested for significant overlap with a curated binding list (e.g., 112 POSTAR3 CLIP RBPs or ENCORI stringency sub-lists) against a defined background set.
skills.name: contingency-table-background-selection
skills.search_text: contingency-table-background-selection Use when validating an over-representation claim: a predicted/clustered gene list must be tested for significant overlap with a curated binding list (e.g., 112 POSTAR3 CLIP RBPs or ENCORI stringency sub-lists) against a defined background set. The candidate list has no defined background set (e.g., no RBP_list.RData or all-gene universe) — enrichment cannot be computed without both margins. The validation target is a continuous association (e.g., correlation or interaction score) rather than a categorical overlap between two gene sets — a rank/correlation test, not a Fisher test, is appropriate. You are predicting novel regulators or computing CRIT features (Zp, Zs, Zg, rho_m, C value) rather than validating an already-predicted candidate list against external binding evidence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs 2x2 overlap contingency tables of a candidate regulator list against CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBP lists (POSTAR3, ENCORI) under two backgrounds (1,344 candidate RBPs from RBP_list.RData; all genes) and applies one-sided Fisher's exact tests to quantify enrichment of known circRNA-binding RBPs among CRIT predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Constructs 2x2 overlap contingency tables of a candidate regulator list against CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBP lists (POSTAR3, ENCORI) under two backgrounds (1,344 candidate RBPs from RBP_list.RData; all genes) and applies one-sided Fisher's exact tests to quantify enrichment of known circRNA-binding RBPs among CRIT predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate list has no defined background set (e.g., no RBP_list.RData or all-gene universe) — enrichment cannot be computed without both margins. The validation target is a continuous association (e.g., correlation or interaction score) rather than a categorical overlap between two gene sets — a rank/correlation test, not a Fisher test, is appropriate. You are predicting novel regulators or computing CRIT features (Zp, Zs, Zg, rho_m, C value) rather than validating an already-predicted candidate list against external binding evidence.

skills.description: Use when a survival or group-comparison factor is continuous (e.g. per-sample GSVA scores) and a two-group (high vs low) split is needed for K-M curves or differential analysis in ARMT.

skills.search_text: continuous-variable-sample-dichotomization Use when a survival or group-comparison factor is continuous (e.g. per-sample GSVA scores) and a two-group (high vs low) split is needed for K-M curves or differential analysis in ARMT. skills.description: Use when stabilizing raw hierarchical cell-type predictions on a scRNA-seq dataset where overlapping label regions in UMAP space indicate disputed cells, and an iterative contour-dispute loop is needed to produce converged annotations.
skills.name: contour-overlap-dispute-resolution
skills.search_text: contour-overlap-dispute-resolution Use when stabilizing raw hierarchical cell-type predictions on a scRNA-seq dataset where overlapping label regions in UMAP space indicate disputed cells, and an iterative contour-dispute loop is needed to produce converged annotations. Input cells lack a UMAP dimensionality reduction or SNN clustering — the contours and cluster propagation cannot be computed Predictions are already stabilized/converged (no overlapping contours or label changes) — iterating further is unnecessary You need raw model predictions rather than cluster- and contour-smoothed annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Resolves per-cell label conflicts by fitting MASS-based prediction contours for each candidate label in UMAP space, adjudicating cells falling in overlapping contours, and re-propagating the majority label within UMAP SNN clusters until convergence. This is Census's core label-stabilizing step that counteracts dataset noise and prediction error before descending to the next hierarchy node. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Resolves per-cell label conflicts by fitting MASS-based prediction contours for each candidate label in UMAP space, adjudicating cells falling in overlapping contours, and re-propagating the majority label within UMAP SNN clusters until convergence. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells lack a UMAP dimensionality reduction or SNN clustering — the contours and cluster propagation cannot be computed Predictions are already stabilized/converged (no overlapping contours or label changes) — iterating further is unnecessary You need raw model predictions rather than cluster- and contour-smoothed annotations

skills.description: Use when you have an ST dataset with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']] (AnnData h5ad) and want to reconstruct spatial relationships or neighbor structure of query single-cell RNA-seq data.

skills.search_text: contrastive-learning-training-on-spatial-transcriptomics Use when you have an ST dataset with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']] (AnnData h5ad) and want to reconstruct spatial relationships or neighbor structure of query single-cell RNA-seq data. When the tissue has a high level of repeating elements, which the paper notes 'could pose a challenge for the spatial reconstruction of SC cells' When there is a large gap between query SC data and the ST reference and you require the reference's cell distribution — forced SC assignment 'could introduce more bias'; consider the MDS-based denovo mode instead, accepting that it loses reference pre-knowledge When you need genome-wide spatial resolution directly from ST data rather than transferring spatial information from a reference (CellContrast reconstructs relationships for SC data using an ST reference, not an ST enhancement method) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train CellContrast's encoder-projector model on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data with truth cell locations using infoNCE contrastive learning, so that physically proximate cells show higher cosine similarity in latent space. skills.summary: Train CellContrast's encoder-projector model on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data with truth cell locations using infoNCE contrastive learning, so that physically proximate cells show higher cosine similarity in latent space. At inference the projector is discarded and the encoder representation supports SC-SC neighbor identification and SC-ST spatial mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the tissue has a high level of repeating elements, which the paper notes 'could pose a challenge for the spatial reconstruction of SC cells' When there is a large gap between query SC data and the ST reference and you require the reference's cell distribution — forced SC assignment 'could introduce more bias'; consider the MDS-based denovo mode instead, accepting that it loses reference pre-knowledge When you need genome-wide spatial resolution directly from ST data rather than transferring spatial information from a reference (CellContrast reconstructs relationships for SC data using an ST reference, not an ST enhancement method)
