skills.description: Use when assessing how robust an scPLS confounding-correction workflow is to the number of available control genes, e.g. when only a subset of a full control-gene panel can be measured.
skills.name: control-gene-set-subsampling
skills.search_text: control-gene-set-subsampling Use when assessing how robust an scPLS confounding-correction workflow is to the number of available control genes, e.g. when only a subset of a full control-gene panel can be measured. The analysis goal is inferring the underlying biological factors (u_i) rather than removing confounding effects — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the factors themselves, due to model identifiability. Downstream evaluation is a clustering-external task (e.g. differential expression or lineage reconstruction) — the paper notes scPLS performance in other analysis settings has not been evaluated. The input data are real tissues with no known true cell-type labels, so ARI against ground truth cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A sensitivity-analysis skill for scPLS-based confounding removal in scRNAseq simulations: it subsamples reduced control gene sets (q = 10, 20, 30, 40 from a full 50-gene set) and verifies that adjusted Rand index (ARI) clustering performance is maintained with fewer control genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill for scPLS-based confounding removal in scRNAseq simulations: it subsamples reduced control gene sets (q = 10, 20, 30, 40 from a full 50-gene set) and verifies that adjusted Rand index (ARI) clustering performance is maintained with fewer control genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is inferring the underlying biological factors (u_i) rather than removing confounding effects — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the factors themselves, due to model identifiability. Downstream evaluation is a clustering-external task (e.g. differential expression or lineage reconstruction) — the paper notes scPLS performance in other analysis settings has not been evaluated. The input data are real tissues with no known true cell-type labels, so ARI against ground truth cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq perturbation data (e.g. treatment vs control, gene knock-outs) where the goal is to find perturbation-unique cell states without a priori marker knowledge, and integration approaches would erase treatment-specific signal.
skills.name: control-guided-semi-supervised-clustering
skills.search_text: control-guided-semi-supervised-clustering Use when analyzing scRNA-seq perturbation data (e.g. treatment vs control, gene knock-outs) where the goal is to find perturbation-unique cell states without a priori marker knowledge, and integration approaches would erase treatment-specific signal. When the goal is batch correction or cross-dataset integration of similar conditions — ICAT is designed to preserve perturbation-specific signal that integration workflows like Seurat, Scanorama, or Harmony would remove When treatment labels are unavailable or the dataset has no defined control population to anchor the unsupervised control clustering step When a priori cell states or marker genes are already known and a fully supervised classification approach is preferred over ICAT's unsupervised control-defined states http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised clustering, which first defines cell states by unsupervised Louvain clustering of control cells, weights genes with NCFS, then semi-supervised clusters all cells so control labels stay fixed while perturbed cells join any cluster. It resolves perturbation-unique cell states that integration workflows (Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony) do not. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Runs ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised clustering, which first defines cell states by unsupervised Louvain clustering of control cells, weights genes with NCFS, then semi-supervised clusters all cells so control labels stay fixed while perturbed cells join any cluster. It resolves perturbation-unique cell states that integration workflows (Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony) do not.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch correction or cross-dataset integration of similar conditions — ICAT is designed to preserve perturbation-specific signal that integration workflows like Seurat, Scanorama, or Harmony would remove When treatment labels are unavailable or the dataset has no defined control population to anchor the unsupervised control clustering step When a priori cell states or marker genes are already known and a fully supervised classification approach is preferred over ICAT's unsupervised control-defined states

skills.description: Use when a multi-omics integration method must be benchmarked against a known ground truth, e.g. simulating mixed or rare populations and controlled sparsity (82/90/96%) in paired scRNA/scATAC cell-line data.
skills.name: controlled-single-cell-simulation-generation
skills.search_text: controlled-single-cell-simulation-generation Use when a multi-omics integration method must be benchmarked against a known ground truth, e.g. simulating mixed or rare populations and controlled sparsity (82/90/96%) in paired scRNA/scATAC cell-line data. Datasets lack distinct, known subpopulations to mix or subsample — the simulation needs a clear ground truth The evaluation goal is biological discovery rather than controlled method benchmarking; artificial perturbations would distort real structure Unpaired single-modality data, since the settings exploit jointly profiled RNA and ATAC from the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Constructs controlled benchmark settings from paired single-cell multi-omics data by surgically mixing profiles across cell types and randomly zeroing values to simulate confounding and sparsity, enabling ground-truth evaluation of integration methods on the Liu scCAT-seq RNA/ATAC cell-line dataset (HCT116, HeLa-S3, K562). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Constructs controlled benchmark settings from paired single-cell multi-omics data by surgically mixing profiles across cell types and randomly zeroing values to simulate confounding and sparsity, enabling ground-truth evaluation of integration methods on the Liu scCAT-seq RNA/ATAC cell-line dataset (HCT116, HeLa-S3, K562).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lack distinct, known subpopulations to mix or subsample — the simulation needs a clear ground truth The evaluation goal is biological discovery rather than controlled method benchmarking; artificial perturbations would distort real structure Unpaired single-modality data, since the settings exploit jointly profiled RNA and ATAC from the same cells

skills.search_text: convergence-score-threshold-decision Use when both cell-hashing singlet labels and SNP-based genotype labels (e.g. from scSplit) exist for the same cells and per-cell sample identities must be reconciled via a convergence-score cutoff decision. Samples lack a distinct genetic background (e.g. most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies), so no reliable SNP-based genotype labels exist to correlate with hashing labels SNP-based clustering quality is poor — e.g. plasmablasts or dying cells, high true doublet rates, or poor transcriptome quality — since the hybrid decision is largely dependent on SNP clustering quality Only cell hashing data are available and the goal is per-hashtag cutoff calling; use HTOClassification/HTOcutoff instead of hybrid demultiplexing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Decision logic from HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function that computes a convergence score C = N1/(N1+N2) for each cell-hashing-group/SNP-genotype-cluster pair and merges pairs only when C meets the c_threshold (e.g. 0.7), falling back to cell hashing labels with a warning when the threshold fails. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Decision logic from HTOreader's HybridDemultiplexing function that computes a convergence score C = N1/(N1+N2) for each cell-hashing-group/SNP-genotype-cluster pair and merges pairs only when C meets the c_threshold (e.g. 0.7), falling back to cell hashing labels with a warning when the threshold fails.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data exhibit a convergent differentiation topology (e.g., the 157-cell neonatal mouse inner ear dataset, Burns et al., GSE71982) that violates the topology-related assumptions of tree-based trajectory methods.

skills.search_text: convergent-topology-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq data exhibit a convergent differentiation topology (e.g., the 157-cell neonatal mouse inner ear dataset, Burns et al., GSE71982) that violates the topology-related assumptions of tree-based trajectory methods. When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors state they do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that setting When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — trajectory inference with Cytopath is not expected to be meaningful in that case When the topology can be assumed tree-like and a simpler method such as Slingshot suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct convergent differentiation trajectories and infer pseudotime from scRNA-seq using Cytopath, a simulation-based method that defines a Markov chain model from RNA velocity, simulates an ensemble of trajectories, and builds a consensus trajectory without imposing topological constraints. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Reconstruct convergent differentiation trajectories and infer pseudotime from scRNA-seq using Cytopath, a simulation-based method that defines a Markov chain model from RNA velocity, simulates an ensemble of trajectories, and builds a consensus trajectory without imposing topological constraints.

skills.description: Use when a small target scRNA-Seq dataset must be improved for downstream clustering by mixing in structure learned from a large annotated source dataset via NMF, without concatenating source and target cells.
skills.name: convex-combination-dataset-mixing
skills.search_text: convex-combination-dataset-mixing Use when a small target scRNA-Seq dataset must be improved for downstream clustering by mixing in structure learned from a large annotated source dataset via NMF, without concatenating source and target cells. Source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only genes present in both datasets can be used The goal is to combine cells from source and target into one matrix — this skill explicitly transfers knowledge without concatenating the two datasets No source cluster annotations (labels) are available to initialize/anchor the source NMF, undermining the transfer of source cell-type knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a new target dataset X_trg_new as the convex combination theta * H_src * W'_trg + (1 - theta) * X_trg, blending the source-dictionary reconstruction of the target with the original target expression matrix so knowledge from a large labeled source is mixed in without concatenating the two datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Constructs a new target dataset X_trg_new as the convex combination theta * H_src * W'_trg + (1 - theta) * X_trg, blending the source-dictionary reconstruction of the target with the original target expression matrix so knowledge from a large labeled source is mixed in without concatenating the two datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only genes present in both datasets can be used The goal is to combine cells from source and target into one matrix — this skill explicitly transfers knowledge without concatenating the two datasets No source cluster annotations (labels) are available to initialize/anchor the source NMF, undermining the transfer of source cell-type knowledge

skills.search_text: convex-supervised-unsupervised-loss-balancing Use when training MarkerMap on single-cell (e.g. CITE-seq .h5ad) data and you must choose between supervised, unsupervised, or joint marker selection within one differentiable-sampling VAE model. skills.description: Use when fitting a PhenoPath model to an expression matrix (e.g. 284 TCGA-COAD tumour samples x 4801 highly variable genes, log2(TPM+1)) with a sample-level covariate such as MSI status, and convergence must be checked via the ELBO.
skills.name: coordinate-ascent-variational-bayesian-fitting
skills.search_text: coordinate-ascent-variational-bayesian-fitting Use when fitting a PhenoPath model to an expression matrix (e.g. 284 TCGA-COAD tumour samples x 4801 highly variable genes, log2(TPM+1)) with a sample-level covariate such as MSI status, and convergence must be checked via the ELBO. The scientific question is retrospective association of a pre-computed trajectory with a covariate rather than joint inference of trajectory and covariate effects — the article motivates PhenoPath precisely because factors should be explicitly incorporated, not only examined afterwards. Features are expected to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — the article states an assumption of PhenoPath is that features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime, and model fit checks are required. The covariate structure is a complex mixture of continuous and discrete covariates in a high-dimensional setting — the discussion defers this to future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit PhenoPath's Bayesian pseudotime-covariate model by coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference (CAVI), implemented in Rcpp, which iteratively minimises the KL-divergence between a full-factorised mean-field approximating distribution and the true posterior to infer latent pseudotimes and gene-covariate interactions from bulk or single-cell expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Fit PhenoPath's Bayesian pseudotime-covariate model by coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference (CAVI), implemented in Rcpp, which iteratively minimises the KL-divergence between a full-factorised mean-field approximating distribution and the true posterior to infer latent pseudotimes and gene-covariate interactions from bulk or single-cell expression data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scientific question is retrospective association of a pre-computed trajectory with a covariate rather than joint inference of trajectory and covariate effects — the article motivates PhenoPath precisely because factors should be explicitly incorporated, not only examined afterwards. Features are expected to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — the article states an assumption of PhenoPath is that features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime, and model fit checks are required. The covariate structure is a complex mixture of continuous and discrete covariates in a high-dimensional setting — the discussion defers this to future work.

skills.description: Use when you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization across multiple studies/traits from either individual-level genotype/phenotype data or summary statistics (LD matrix plus effect sizes/SEs or z-scores and sample sizes), especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity.
skills.name: coordinate-ascent-variational-inference-fitting
skills.search_text: coordinate-ascent-variational-inference-fitting Use when you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization across multiple studies/traits from either individual-level genotype/phenotype data or summary statistics (LD matrix plus effect sizes/SEs or z-scores and sample sizes), especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity. The locus's effects are mediated via coding variants that may not show eQTL effects — such loci cannot be explored with CAFEH. Studies have large differences in LD (e.g. ancestry differences), since the current version of CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix. The effect size matrix has missing data, because CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in the tested datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Fits the CAFEH spike-and-slab Bayesian model (CAFEH-G for individual-level genotypes/phenotypes, CAFEH-S for summary statistics) via coordinate-ascent variational inference, jointly fine-mapping causal variants and colocalizing signals across multiple traits while automatically pruning superfluous components. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Fits the CAFEH spike-and-slab Bayesian model (CAFEH-G for individual-level genotypes/phenotypes, CAFEH-S for summary statistics) via coordinate-ascent variational inference, jointly fine-mapping causal variants and colocalizing signals across multiple traits while automatically pruning superfluous components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus's effects are mediated via coding variants that may not show eQTL effects — such loci cannot be explored with CAFEH. Studies have large differences in LD (e.g. ancestry differences), since the current version of CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix. The effect size matrix has missing data, because CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in the tested datasets.

skills.description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group aggregates too many genes across species for gene-level insight and must be split into smaller clusters based on phylogenetic distance.
skills.name: cophenetic-distance-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: cophenetic-distance-matrix-computation Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group aggregates too many genes across species for gene-level insight and must be split into smaller clusters based on phylogenetic distance. The ortholog group is small enough (relative to species count) that gene-level insight is already attainable without splitting The task is standard DE or enrichment analysis on an annotated count table (ExpressAnalystR's normalization/DE modules handle that directly) No multiple sequence alignment or tree can be inferred for the group, so cophenetic distances are undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Computes a cophenetic distance matrix from a phylogenetic dendrogram inferred from a multiple sequence alignment (MAFFT + FastTree) so that genes in an oversized EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (e.g., vitellogenin group s2f_0005567) can be subdivided by k-means into biologically meaningful sub-clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Computes a cophenetic distance matrix from a phylogenetic dendrogram inferred from a multiple sequence alignment (MAFFT + FastTree) so that genes in an oversized EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (e.g., vitellogenin group s2f_0005567) can be subdivided by k-means into biologically meaningful sub-clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ortholog group is small enough (relative to species count) that gene-level insight is already attainable without splitting The task is standard DE or enrichment analysis on an annotated count table (ExpressAnalystR's normalization/DE modules handle that directly) No multiple sequence alignment or tree can be inferred for the group, so cophenetic distances are undefined

skills.description: Use when a breadth-first clustering of leaves over internal nodes of a single-cell phylogeny yields more candidate clusters than the user-defined target (default target := 10) and the count must be reduced while preserving phylogenetic coherence.
skills.name: cophenetic-distance-neighbor-merging
skills.search_text: cophenetic-distance-neighbor-merging Use when a breadth-first clustering of leaves over internal nodes of a single-cell phylogeny yields more candidate clusters than the user-defined target (default target := 10) and the count must be reduced while preserving phylogenetic coherence. The tree is not a single-cell phylogeny with cells as labeled tips (e.g., a species tree) — the breadth-first internal-node grouping assumes cell leaves The number of candidate clusters from the breadth-first search is already at or below the target count — no merging pass is needed Transcriptomic (non-phylogenetic) clustering is intended — this skill groups cells strictly by tree topology and cophenetic distance, not expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 A post-processing step of PhyloVision's Cluster-Phylogeny algorithm: after breadth-first grouping of leaves under internal nodes, surplus clusters are reduced to the target count (default := 10) by iteratively merging the smallest cluster with its phylogenetically nearest cluster as measured by cophenetic distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: A post-processing step of PhyloVision's Cluster-Phylogeny algorithm: after breadth-first grouping of leaves under internal nodes, surplus clusters are reduced to the target count (default := 10) by iteratively merging the smallest cluster with its phylogenetically nearest cluster as measured by cophenetic distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tree is not a single-cell phylogeny with cells as labeled tips (e.g., a species tree) — the breadth-first internal-node grouping assumes cell leaves The number of candidate clusters from the breadth-first search is already at or below the target count — no merging pass is needed Transcriptomic (non-phylogenetic) clustering is intended — this skill groups cells strictly by tree topology and cophenetic distance, not expression

skills.search_text: copy-loss-auroc-benchmarking-across-cna-callers Use when a simulated scRNA-seq dataset has known ground-truth CNA labels (e.g. allele-specific chr3 loss injected across subclones) and you must quantify which caller (XClone, InferCNV, Numbat) recovers the loss via AUROC. skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for comparing allele-specific copy-loss detection accuracy of scRNA-seq CNA callers (XClone, InferCNV, Numbat) on simulated ground-truth data, scored per cell/gene via AUROC against simulator CNA labels.

skills.description: Use when CMScaller CMS subtype assignments exist for a pre-clinical CRC cohort (e.g. Gao PDXs, Fujii organoids) and you need to test whether mutation burden, CNA burden, BRAF mutation status, or MSI is enriched in specific subtypes.
skills.name: copy-number-aberration-burden-analysis
skills.search_text: copy-number-aberration-burden-analysis Use when CMScaller CMS subtype assignments exist for a pre-clinical CRC cohort (e.g. Gao PDXs, Fujii organoids) and you need to test whether mutation burden, CNA burden, BRAF mutation status, or MSI is enriched in specific subtypes. Input samples are primary CRC tumors or metastatic biopsies with a human stromal component — the original CMS classifier, not CMScaller, applies, and CMScaller is explicitly not recommended for metastatic CRC biopsies. Cohort has fewer than approximately forty samples — centered/scaled input introduces prediction uncertainty for such small datasets. Data is single-cell RNA-sequencing — CMScaller is not optimized for such exceedingly noisy data. Statistically associates CMScaller-derived CMS subtypes of pre-clinical colorectal cancer models (PDXs, organoids) with molecular features such as copy number aberration (CNA) burden, total mutation counts, BRAF status, and MSI, using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests and Fisher's exact tests in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Statistically associates CMScaller-derived CMS subtypes of pre-clinical colorectal cancer models (PDXs, organoids) with molecular features such as copy number aberration (CNA) burden, total mutation counts, BRAF status, and MSI, using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests and Fisher's exact tests in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are primary CRC tumors or metastatic biopsies with a human stromal component — the original CMS classifier, not CMScaller, applies, and CMScaller is explicitly not recommended for metastatic CRC biopsies. Cohort has fewer than approximately forty samples — centered/scaled input introduces prediction uncertainty for such small datasets. Data is single-cell RNA-sequencing — CMScaller is not optimized for such exceedingly noisy data.

skills.name: copy-number-expression-correlation-mapping
skills.search_text: copy-number-expression-correlation-mapping Use when you have paired single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) with no direct cell correspondence and need cell-to-cell or cell-to-clone assignment, e.g. to link genomic mutations to transcriptomic states. Samples are biologically homogeneous — the article notes 'matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples' You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — 'unlike statistical methods such as clonealign, MaCroDNA does not provide probabilistic confidence measures' Ground-truth correspondence between cells exists and direct pairing suffices; no cross-modality matching is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Map scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq cells or clones by maximizing summed per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients between RNA expression and DNA copy-number profiles via maximum weighted bipartite matching solved as a binary integer program with Gurobi. Used by MaCroDNA to resolve the cell association problem and downstream K* phylogenetic signal analyses in Barrett's esophagus progression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are biologically homogeneous — the article notes 'matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples' You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — 'unlike statistical methods such as clonealign, MaCroDNA does not provide probabilistic confidence measures' Ground-truth correspondence between cells exists and direct pairing suffices; no cross-modality matching is needed

skills.search_text: copy-number-profile-correlation-with-bulk-truth Use when scRNA-seq copy number inferences (SCEVAN, CopyKAT, inferCNV) need quantitative validation against matched bulk WGS or WES segmented profiles, e.g. for benchmarking tools on GBM or Multiple Myeloma cohorts. skills.summary: Benchmarks copy number profiles inferred from scRNA-seq by SCEVAN, CopyKAT v1.0.5, and inferCNV v1.4.0 against bulk DNA sequencing ground truth by computing Pearson correlations on 1-Mb resampled profiles. skills.when_to_use_negative: Tumors with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based CNA inference is unsuited and correlation with bulk truth is not meaningful No matched bulk WGS/WES ground truth exists for the samples, so the correlation benchmark cannot be computed The goal is cell-level malignant/non-malignant classification accuracy (F1) rather than profile-level agreement with bulk segmentation

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime/efficiency benchmarks of scRNA-seq copy-number (CNV) tools such as SCEVAN, CopyKAT, and inferCNV, or when justifying tool choice on large droplet datasets by measuring per-stage wall-clock runtimes.
skills.name: copy-number-segmentation-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: copy-number-segmentation-runtime-benchmarking Use when reproducing or extending runtime/efficiency benchmarks of scRNA-seq copy-number (CNV) tools such as SCEVAN, CopyKAT, and inferCNV, or when justifying tool choice on large droplet datasets by measuring per-stage wall-clock runtimes. The analysis goal is CNV accuracy (e.g., F1 or segment concordance) rather than computational efficiency — use accuracy benchmarking instead The tumor type has minimal genomic alterations (leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where aneuploidy-based tools including the compared methods are unsuited regardless of runtime The comparison targets bulk or shallow WGS data only, where single-cell CNV pipelines and their classification stages do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill for reproducing per-stage (malignant/non-malignant classification and joint segmentation) runtime comparisons of SCEVAN against CopyKAT v1.0.5, inferCNV v1.4.0, DNAcopy v1.62.0, and CNVkit v0.9.9 on scRNA-seq tumor datasets. It quantifies how SCEVAN's greedy multichannel Mumford–Shah segmentation achieves speedups (e.g., 11× vs inferCNV and 19× vs CopyKAT on the Multiple Myeloma 10X data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for reproducing per-stage (malignant/non-malignant classification and joint segmentation) runtime comparisons of SCEVAN against CopyKAT v1.0.5, inferCNV v1.4.0, DNAcopy v1.62.0, and CNVkit v0.9.9 on scRNA-seq tumor datasets. It quantifies how SCEVAN's greedy multichannel Mumford–Shah segmentation achieves speedups (e.g., 11× vs inferCNV and 19× vs CopyKAT on the Multiple Myeloma 10X data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is CNV accuracy (e.g., F1 or segment concordance) rather than computational efficiency — use accuracy benchmarking instead The tumor type has minimal genomic alterations (leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where aneuploidy-based tools including the compared methods are unsuited regardless of runtime The comparison targets bulk or shallow WGS data only, where single-cell CNV pipelines and their classification stages do not apply

skills.description: Use when a smoothed, gene-coordinate-sorted scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. MGH106 from GSE131928) must be segmented into copy number regions to infer clonal CNA profiles, as in SCEVAN steps D and G.
skills.name: copy-number-segmentation-variational-minimization
skills.search_text: copy-number-segmentation-variational-minimization Use when a smoothed, gene-coordinate-sorted scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. MGH106 from GSE131928) must be segmented into copy number regions to infer clonal CNA profiles, as in SCEVAN steps D and G. The input matrix is a raw count matrix that has not been filtered (cells <200 genes / genes <1% cells), cell-cycle (REACTOME) filtered, normal-cell baseline-subtracted, and TV-smoothed — segmentation on unsmoothed counts produces artificial segments The tumor is expected to have minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemias, pediatric cancers, ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based segmentation assumption is unsuitable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Greedy piecewise-constant Mumford–Shah minimization (exported in SCEVAN as getBreaksVegaMC) that segments a smoothed, chromosome-indexed expression matrix into a copy number matrix, exploiting shared breakpoints across copy number clones via multichannel segmentation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Greedy piecewise-constant Mumford–Shah minimization (exported in SCEVAN as getBreaksVegaMC) that segments a smoothed, chromosome-indexed expression matrix into a copy number matrix, exploiting shared breakpoints across copy number clones via multichannel segmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is a raw count matrix that has not been filtered (cells <200 genes / genes <1% cells), cell-cycle (REACTOME) filtered, normal-cell baseline-subtracted, and TV-smoothed — segmentation on unsmoothed counts produces artificial segments The tumor is expected to have minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemias, pediatric cancers, ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based segmentation assumption is unsuitable

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data from a tumor sample has been segmented (e.g. via getBreaksVegaMC/computeCNAmtx) and each segment must be assigned an integer CNV state label for tumor/normal or clonal analysis.
skills.name: copy-number-state-classification
skills.search_text: copy-number-state-classification Use when scRNA-seq count data from a tumor sample has been segmented (e.g. via getBreaksVegaMC/computeCNAmtx) and each segment must be assigned an integer CNV state label for tumor/normal or clonal analysis. Tumors with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — the aneuploidy-based assumption underlying the five-state model may not be suited in this case Bulk DNA copy number data — CNVkit-style integer cutoffs (-1, -0.25, 0.2, 0.7) apply to bulk segmented log-ratios, not the expression-based five-state mixture used here Input that has not been segmented and baseline-corrected — the mixture model operates on per-cell segment means relative to the confident-normal-cell median, not raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classify each genomic segment of a scRNA-seq sample into one of five copy number states (deletion, loss, neutral, gain, amplification) by fitting a five-component truncated-normal mixture to per-cell segment means via EM, then taking a majority vote across cells to form a consensus per-segment CNV call. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Classify each genomic segment of a scRNA-seq sample into one of five copy number states (deletion, loss, neutral, gain, amplification) by fitting a five-component truncated-normal mixture to per-cell segment means via EM, then taking a majority vote across cells to form a consensus per-segment CNV call.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tumors with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — the aneuploidy-based assumption underlying the five-state model may not be suited in this case Bulk DNA copy number data — CNVkit-style integer cutoffs (-1, -0.25, 0.2, 0.7) apply to bulk segmented log-ratios, not the expression-based five-state mixture used here Input that has not been segmented and baseline-corrected — the mixture model operates on per-cell segment means relative to the confident-normal-cell median, not raw counts

skills.search_text: copynumber-based-malignancy-classification Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix from a tumor biopsy and need automatic malignant/non-malignant cell segregation without manually identifying reference normal cell clusters. skills.search_text: cord-blood-mononuclear-cell-cluster-annotation Use when a CITE-seq dataset of cord blood mononuclear cells needs cluster-level annotation of immune subsets (e.g., NK and CD4+ T cells) and multimodal integration quality must be benchmarked against methods like MOFA2, Seurat 4, and SNF. Datasets with a high number of ADT features or massive cell counts (e.g., 170K cells with 228 ADT features) — LinQ-View's pairwise distance computation scales quadratically and failed there, whereas Seurat 4 succeeded Large datasets with many ADT features where Seurat 4 is the recommended option for both performance and time efficiency Data lacking a surface-protein (ADT) modality, since the L-infinity-norm fusion depends on per-modality distance matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates cell heterogeneity (NK and CD4+ T cell subsets) in the 8,617-cell cord blood mononuclear cell (CBMC) CITE-seq benchmark (GSE100866) by clustering integrated transcriptome and surface-protein modalities at Louvain resolution 0.9 with LinQ-View and comparator multimodal methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056

skills.search_text: correlated-gene-count-comparison-across-methods Use when comparing trajectory-inference methods on identical single-cell RNA-seq input (real or Splatter-simulated) and you need quantitative smoothness metrics — correlated-gene counts and lag-1 autocorrelation — per method. skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectories are not comparable because methods were run on different input datasets or different gene/cell preprocessing — correlated-gene counts are only meaningful on identical matrices A method requires trajectory topology the data do not support (e.g. DPT needs an a priori number of branches; Wishbone allows only a single branch point) — results would reflect the method's structural constraint rather than trajectory quality The goal is real-data biological interpretation (e.g. HSPC lineage discovery) rather than a controlled synthetic-data method benchmark

skills.search_text: correlation-analysis-of-baf-and-expression-signals Use when you have CaSpER outputs from bulk RNA-seq (BAF shift signal from BAFExtract plus multiscale smoothed expression per chromosome arm) and need to quantify whether LOH/bajo-allelic-imbalance arms co-vary with expression loss, e.g. chr1p/chr6q/chr22q in meningioma. 3′-only sequencing data (e.g. DropSeq-style) where the BAF shift signal is degraded because variants are measured only near gene 3′ ends, making BAF-expression correlations unreliable You need focal or gene-level CNV calls (extractSegmentSummary/gene.matrix) rather than arm-level association between allelic imbalance and expression Single-cell samples where a few high-read cells may dominate the pooled BAF shift signal, biasing the correlation http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the relationship between B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signal (allelic imbalance/LOH) and multiscale-smoothed gene expression signal per chromosome arm, as demonstrated with CaSpER on the yale_meningioma bulk RNA-seq dataset (chr1p, chr6q, chr22q Pearson correlations). skills.when_to_use_negative: 3′-only sequencing data (e.g. DropSeq-style) where the BAF shift signal is degraded because variants are measured only near gene 3′ ends, making BAF-expression correlations unreliable You need focal or gene-level CNV calls (extractSegmentSummary/gene.matrix) rather than arm-level association between allelic imbalance and expression Single-cell samples where a few high-read cells may dominate the pooled BAF shift signal, biasing the correlation

The query is a list of marker genes rather than an expression profile — use deCS.fisher() (Fisher's exact test cell type enrichment) instead The goal is to discover or characterize novel cell types — deCS is a mapping-based tool that can only assign labels from the reference panels Annotating malignant/cancer cells, where healthy-reference-based expression profiles differ substantially and bias the annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Annotate single-cell or bulk RNA-seq query clusters by computing Pearson correlation coefficients (PCC) between a z-scored query marker-expression matrix and pre-calculated cell type specificity t-score/z-score reference panels using the deCS.correlation() function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001

skills.description: Use when training a supervised cell-type annotator (NeuCA) on scRNA-seq data with known labels and you must decide whether high inter-cell-type correlations require a hierarchical neural-network strategy instead of a plain feed-forward classifier.
skills.name: correlation-based-classifier-strategy-selection
skills.search_text: correlation-based-classifier-strategy-selection Use when training a supervised cell-type annotator (NeuCA) on scRNA-seq data with known labels and you must decide whether high inter-cell-type correlations require a hierarchical neural-network strategy instead of a plain feed-forward classifier. The new sample may contain cell types or unknown/rare populations absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No training data with known labels exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised methods (e.g., Seurat, SC3) are then the only viable solution Closely correlated cell types are not the concern and a simple correlated-procedure or feed-forward classifier suffices when all off-diagonal correlations are below tau = 0.95 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 NeuCA's automatic decision rule for choosing between a feed-forward neural network and a marker-guided, cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network in supervised scRNA-seq cell annotation. It computes averaged expression profiles per cell type, builds their Pearson correlation matrix, and applies a tau = 0.95 threshold so that closely correlated cell types are classified with hierarchical structure information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: NeuCA's automatic decision rule for choosing between a feed-forward neural network and a marker-guided, cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network in supervised scRNA-seq cell annotation. It computes averaged expression profiles per cell type, builds their Pearson correlation matrix, and applies a tau = 0.95 threshold so that closely correlated cell types are classified with hierarchical structure information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample may contain cell types or unknown/rare populations absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No training data with known labels exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised methods (e.g., Seurat, SC3) are then the only viable solution Closely correlated cell types are not the concern and a simple correlated-procedure or feed-forward classifier suffices when all off-diagonal correlations are below tau = 0.95

skills.description: Use when a bulk expression decomposition run has produced estimated cell proportions (e.g. res$bulk.props) and ground-truth proportions exist (from simulated data with known avg.props) so accuracy can be quantified.
skills.name: correlation-based-decomposition-validation
skills.search_text: correlation-based-decomposition-validation Use when a bulk expression decomposition run has produced estimated cell proportions (e.g. res$bulk.props) and ground-truth proportions exist (from simulated data with known avg.props) so accuracy can be quantified. No ground-truth (or simulated) proportions exist, so correlation with true.props is impossible — use biological/phenotype replication instead (e.g. previously reported cell-proportion–phenotype associations) Evaluating BisqueMarker cross-cell-type accuracy: its estimates are relative abundance differences that cannot be compared across cell types, so raw proportion-level metrics are inappropriate without first scaling the true proportions The single-cell reference proportions are known to differ strongly from true physiological distributions — correlation-based validation would certify a systematically biased estimate Validates cell-type proportion estimates produced by Bisque (or comparator decomposition methods such as CIBERSORT/BSEQ-sc and MuSiC) by correlating estimated proportions against true simulated proportions and reporting R and RMSD metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Validates cell-type proportion estimates produced by Bisque (or comparator decomposition methods such as CIBERSORT/BSEQ-sc and MuSiC) by correlating estimated proportions against true simulated proportions and reporting R and RMSD metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth (or simulated) proportions exist, so correlation with true.props is impossible — use biological/phenotype replication instead (e.g. previously reported cell-proportion–phenotype associations) Evaluating BisqueMarker cross-cell-type accuracy: its estimates are relative abundance differences that cannot be compared across cell types, so raw proportion-level metrics are inappropriate without first scaling the true proportions The single-cell reference proportions are known to differ strongly from true physiological distributions — correlation-based validation would certify a systematically biased estimate

skills.description: Use when a filtered RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., soybean samples across five fungal-pathogen stress conditions) must be converted into a weighted coexpression network whose edges are correlation-based, as a prerequisite for candidate gene or module mining.
skills.name: correlation-based-edge-computation
skills.search_text: correlation-based-edge-computation Use when a filtered RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., soybean samples across five fungal-pathogen stress conditions) must be converted into a weighted coexpression network whose edges are correlation-based, as a prerequisite for candidate gene or module mining. The input is already a coexpression network or edge list rather than a gene-by-sample expression matrix. The analysis requires a signed network that separates positive from negative correlations — this skill explicitly uses absolute correlations in an unsigned network. Data are GWAS SNP summary statistics or germplasm resistance scores rather than RNA-seq expression values; those feed into downstream prioritization, not edge computation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds an unsigned gene coexpression network from soybean fungal-infection RNA-seq expression data by computing pairwise gene-gene Pearson correlations with BioNERO on quantile-normalized, adjusted expression matrices, storing the result as coexpression_network.rds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Builds an unsigned gene coexpression network from soybean fungal-infection RNA-seq expression data by computing pairwise gene-gene Pearson correlations with BioNERO on quantile-normalized, adjusted expression matrices, storing the result as coexpression_network.rds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a coexpression network or edge list rather than a gene-by-sample expression matrix. The analysis requires a signed network that separates positive from negative correlations — this skill explicitly uses absolute correlations in an unsigned network. Data are GWAS SNP summary statistics or germplasm resistance scores rather than RNA-seq expression values; those feed into downstream prioritization, not edge computation.

skills.search_text: cosine-angle-velocity-concordance-analysis Use when benchmarking velocity methods against a known biological axis: you have per-cell velocity vectors, a pseudotime-inferred endpoint, and need to quantify whether vectors align with or are orthogonal to the reference direction. When no biologically grounded reference direction (e.g., pseudotime-derived endpoint) exists — cosine angles to an arbitrary direction are uninterpretable. When velocity vectors and the reference direction are not defined on the same gene set, since per-cell cosine computation requires identical feature spaces. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates RNA velocity methods by computing per-cell cosine angles between inferred velocity vectors and a pseudotime-derived reference direction (e.g., the acinar-to-ductal metaplasia axis in GSE207943 acute pancreatitis data), then aggregating per-method mean angles to test whether velocities point toward the trajectory endpoint. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267

skills.when_to_use_negative: When no biologically grounded reference direction (e.g., pseudotime-derived endpoint) exists — cosine angles to an arbitrary direction are uninterpretable. skills.description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods on the same cell set and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of how well a method's velocity vectors agree with neighbors in the phenotypic manifold.
skills.name: cosine-distance-local-inconsistency-metric
skills.search_text: cosine-distance-local-inconsistency-metric Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods on the same cell set and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of how well a method's velocity vectors agree with neighbors in the phenotypic manifold. You lack velocity vectors for multiple methods over the same cells — the metric is a comparative benchmark, not a stand-alone quality score with an absolute threshold. You want trajectory/pseudotime or downstream fate analysis rather than a velocity-field smoothness comparison across methods. Cell annotations or the underlying shared cell set are inconsistent across methods, which would confound per-cluster aggregation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Quantifies local consistency of single-cell RNA velocity fields by computing, for each cell, the mean cosine distance between its velocity vector and the velocity vectors of its k=30 nearest neighbors, then averaging per cluster and globally. Used in the scKINETICS benchmark to show scKINETICS produces the most locally concordant velocities versus scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Quantifies local consistency of single-cell RNA velocity fields by computing, for each cell, the mean cosine distance between its velocity vector and the velocity vectors of its k=30 nearest neighbors, then averaging per cluster and globally. Used in the scKINETICS benchmark to show scKINETICS produces the most locally concordant velocities versus scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack velocity vectors for multiple methods over the same cells — the metric is a comparative benchmark, not a stand-alone quality score with an absolute threshold. You want trajectory/pseudotime or downstream fate analysis rather than a velocity-field smoothness comparison across methods. Cell annotations or the underlying shared cell set are inconsistent across methods, which would confound per-cluster aggregation.

skills.name: cosine-similarity-expression-reconstruction-assessment
skills.search_text: cosine-similarity-expression-reconstruction-assessment Use when you need to measure how much a GRN inference method (e.g., SCING vs ppcor, PIDC, GRNBOOST2) overfits, by comparing per-gene expression reconstruction quality (cosine similarity) on train vs held-out test cells from snRNA-seq or scRNA-seq data. You lack a held-out test split — training and evaluating the GBR on the same cells only yields train cosine similarity and cannot reveal overfitting You are evaluating perturbation-target prediction (AUROC / TPR at FPR 0.05 from Perturb-seq guides), which is a separate validation scheme in the SCING paper Your network edges are needed as causal/directional regulatory claims — the paper notes links between genes are not necessarily causal or directional, so cosine-similarity reconstruction quality does not establish causality http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A gene-prediction validation protocol that quantifies GRN overfitting: a gradient boosting regressor (GBR) is trained per gene from its parents in a network built on a train split, expression is predicted on the held-out test split, and the cosine similarity to true expression is compared between train and test (test/train ratio). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: A gene-prediction validation protocol that quantifies GRN overfitting: a gradient boosting regressor (GBR) is trained per gene from its parents in a network built on a train split, expression is predicted on the held-out test split, and the cosine similarity to true expression is compared between train and test (test/train ratio).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack a held-out test split — training and evaluating the GBR on the same cells only yields train cosine similarity and cannot reveal overfitting You are evaluating perturbation-target prediction (AUROC / TPR at FPR 0.05 from Perturb-seq guides), which is a separate validation scheme in the SCING paper Your network edges are needed as causal/directional regulatory claims — the paper notes links between genes are not necessarily causal or directional, so cosine-similarity reconstruction quality does not establish causality

skills.description: Use when a batch-corrected multi-subtype expression or proteomics matrix (e.g. FP/FS/NL vascular specimens) must be screened for subtype-specific marker proteins/genes and existing test statistics do not satisfy the MG definition.
skills.name: cosine-similarity-one-sample-testing
skills.search_text: cosine-similarity-one-sample-testing Use when a batch-corrected multi-subtype expression or proteomics matrix (e.g. FP/FS/NL vascular specimens) must be screened for subtype-specific marker proteins/genes and existing test statistics do not satisfy the MG definition. Input data is not batch-corrected — the article explicitly notes 'the input of COT should be batch-corrected', so applying COT to uncorrected batches is invalid. The dataset has too few genes/molecules to support the empirical-null approximation — p-value prediction fails and the marker detection cannot be significance-tested. The goal is clustering or subtype discovery rather than marker detection among already-defined subtypes — COT requires a pre-specified subtype_label and complements rather than replaces existing methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Marker-gene (MG) detection using the Cosine-based One-sample Test (COT), which scores each molecule by the cosine similarity between its cross-subtype expression profile and the exact mathematical definition of an ideal marker gene, then assesses significance against an approximated empirical null distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: Marker-gene (MG) detection using the Cosine-based One-sample Test (COT), which scores each molecule by the cosine similarity between its cross-subtype expression profile and the exact mathematical definition of an ideal marker gene, then assesses significance against an approximated empirical null distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not batch-corrected — the article explicitly notes 'the input of COT should be batch-corrected', so applying COT to uncorrected batches is invalid. The dataset has too few genes/molecules to support the empirical-null approximation — p-value prediction fails and the marker detection cannot be significance-tested. The goal is clustering or subtype discovery rather than marker detection among already-defined subtypes — COT requires a pre-specified subtype_label and complements rather than replaces existing methods.
