skills.name: cosine-similarity-range-validation
skills.search_text: cosine-similarity-range-validation Use when cot.df_cos has been produced by COT's generate_cos_values() (or the XOR-basis SDG variant) and the cosine values must be checked against theoretical bounds before ranking markers or writing sdg_cos_values.csv. cot.df_cos does not yet exist — the cosine statistics must first be computed with generate_cos_values() before ranges can be validated The gene-by-sample matrix is not batch-corrected, since COT's input is explicitly required to be batch-corrected and uncorrected values can distort cosine scores Data are replicate-level samples rather than aggregated subtype means and generate_subtype_means() has not yet been run with the subtype_label mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates that cosine similarity statistics computed by COT's generate_cos_values() lie within their theoretical bounds: cos ≤ 1 with 1 attained by ideal marker genes (MG), and, for the XOR-modified subtype-downregulated gene (SDG) statistic of Eq 7, strictly within (1/(K-1), 1) for K subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: Validates that cosine similarity statistics computed by COT's generate_cos_values() lie within their theoretical bounds: cos ≤ 1 with 1 attained by ideal marker genes (MG), and, for the XOR-modified subtype-downregulated gene (SDG) statistic of Eq 7, strictly within (1/(K-1), 1) for K subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: cot.df_cos does not yet exist — the cosine statistics must first be computed with generate_cos_values() before ranges can be validated The gene-by-sample matrix is not batch-corrected, since COT's input is explicitly required to be batch-corrected and uncorrected values can distort cosine scores Data are replicate-level samples rather than aggregated subtype means and generate_subtype_means() has not yet been run with the subtype_label mapping

skills.description: Use when fitting reference signatures to WGS catalogs from hematological malignancies or other cancers where the default COSMIC signature set contains processes that are biologically implausible for the cohort (e.g., platinum exposure absent) or where genome-wide vs exome context matters.
skills.name: cosmic-signature-reference-curation
skills.search_text: cosmic-signature-reference-curation Use when fitting reference signatures to WGS catalogs from hematological malignancies or other cancers where the default COSMIC signature set contains processes that are biologically implausible for the cohort (e.g., platinum exposure absent) or where genome-wide vs exome context matters. The cohort includes platinum-exposed patients — in that case SBS35 must be kept in the reference (as in the two platinum-exposed t-AML samples) rather than removed. De novo signature extraction is the goal (e.g., NMF on a large cohort) rather than fitting samples against a curated reference set. The mutation catalog comes from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases, where mutational burden is too low for meaningful reference fitting regardless of reference curation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Curates the COSMIC mutational signature reference matrix before fitting by selecting the appropriate reference version (COSMIC v2 vs v3.1), removing context-inappropriate signatures (canonical AID SBS84 for genome-wide analysis, platinum SBS35 when patients are not platinum exposed), and optionally supplementing with cancer-specific signatures such as SBS-MM1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
skills.summary: Curates the COSMIC mutational signature reference matrix before fitting by selecting the appropriate reference version (COSMIC v2 vs v3.1), removing context-inappropriate signatures (canonical AID SBS84 for genome-wide analysis, platinum SBS35 when patients are not platinum exposed), and optionally supplementing with cancer-specific signatures such as SBS-MM1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort includes platinum-exposed patients — in that case SBS35 must be kept in the reference (as in the two platinum-exposed t-AML samples) rather than removed. De novo signature extraction is the goal (e.g., NMF on a large cohort) rather than fitting samples against a curated reference set. The mutation catalog comes from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases, where mutational burden is too low for meaningful reference fitting regardless of reference curation.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a semi-profiling or representative-selection pipeline: you have real-profiled single-cell data for a cohort, inferred or copied data for non-representatives at multiple representative counts, and you need a normalized error vs. cost curve.
skills.name: cost-performance-curve-generation
skills.search_text: cost-performance-curve-generation Use when evaluating a semi-profiling or representative-selection pipeline: you have real-profiled single-cell data for a cohort, inferred or copied data for non-representatives at multiple representative counts, and you need a normalized error vs. cost curve. Input is only bulk data with no real-profiled single-cell ground truth for any samples, since UB/LB normalization and error validation require paired real-profiled reference data The goal is deconvolution from bulk data with an external single-cell reference (the single-cell-level deconvolution scenario), not cohort-level semi-profiling cost-performance evaluation Cell-type proportion comparison or UMAP similarity is the target metric instead of single-cell-level normalized error curves http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates normalized-error-vs-number-of-representatives curves that quantify how well scSemiProfiler's inferred single-cell data approximates real-profiled data as sequencing cost scales, benchmarked against a selection-only baseline that copies representative cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Generates normalized-error-vs-number-of-representatives curves that quantify how well scSemiProfiler's inferred single-cell data approximates real-profiled data as sequencing cost scales, benchmarked against a selection-only baseline that copies representative cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only bulk data with no real-profiled single-cell ground truth for any samples, since UB/LB normalization and error validation require paired real-profiled reference data The goal is deconvolution from bulk data with an external single-cell reference (the single-cell-level deconvolution scenario), not cohort-level semi-profiling cost-performance evaluation Cell-type proportion comparison or UMAP similarity is the target metric instead of single-cell-level normalized error curves

skills.description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq count matrix plus sample metadata with infected vs mock conditions (e.g., GEO GSE147507) and need DEGs for downstream pathway or metabolic model mapping.
skills.name: count-based-statistical-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: count-based-statistical-hypothesis-testing Use when you have a raw RNA-seq count matrix plus sample metadata with infected vs mock conditions (e.g., GEO GSE147507) and need DEGs for downstream pathway or metabolic model mapping. Input is already-normalized expression (FPKM/TPM) rather than raw counts — DESeq2 requires raw counts; FPKM/TPM data is instead the input for rFASTCORMICS model reconstruction. The goal is single-sample context-specific metabolic model reconstruction rather than statistical comparison of conditions. The condition of interest shows no differentially expressed metabolic genes (like A549_0.02), in which case it should be discarded from downstream DEG pathway analysis rather than forced through. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq read counts using DESeq2 negative-binomial testing on the GSE147507 severity study (SARS-CoV-2 infected vs mock lung cells), after low-expression filtering with edgeR's filterByExpr. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Compute differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq read counts using DESeq2 negative-binomial testing on the GSE147507 severity study (SARS-CoV-2 infected vs mock lung cells), after low-expression filtering with edgeR's filterByExpr.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already-normalized expression (FPKM/TPM) rather than raw counts — DESeq2 requires raw counts; FPKM/TPM data is instead the input for rFASTCORMICS model reconstruction. The goal is single-sample context-specific metabolic model reconstruction rather than statistical comparison of conditions. The condition of interest shows no differentially expressed metabolic genes (like A549_0.02), in which case it should be discarded from downstream DEG pathway analysis rather than forced through.

skills.description: Use when an aptardi or StringTie-derived transcriptome has been quantitated with RSEM across multiple samples and a high-quality subset of transcripts is needed before re-quantitation and DESeq2 differential expression testing.
skills.name: count-based-transcript-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: count-based-transcript-quality-filtering Use when an aptardi or StringTie-derived transcriptome has been quantitated with RSEM across multiple samples and a high-quality subset of transcripts is needed before re-quantitation and DESeq2 differential expression testing. Working with a single sample or very few samples, where a 2/3-of-samples count rule is undefined or too strict — a simple expression threshold may be more appropriate The transcriptome has already been filtered and re-quantitated, and the task is downstream DESeq2 testing rather than quality filtering Evaluating raw aptardi polyA-site predictions before any RSEM quantitation, since the filter operates on per-sample counts, not on GTF coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A conservative filtering step that removes transcripts lacking at least 1 count in 2/3 of samples from an RSEM-quantitated (e.g., aptardi-modified) transcriptome, yielding a high-quality transcriptome suitable for downstream differential expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: A conservative filtering step that removes transcripts lacking at least 1 count in 2/3 of samples from an RSEM-quantitated (e.g., aptardi-modified) transcriptome, yielding a high-quality transcriptome suitable for downstream differential expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with a single sample or very few samples, where a 2/3-of-samples count rule is undefined or too strict — a simple expression threshold may be more appropriate The transcriptome has already been filtered and re-quantitated, and the task is downstream DESeq2 testing rather than quality filtering Evaluating raw aptardi polyA-site predictions before any RSEM quantitation, since the filter operates on per-sample counts, not on GTF coordinates

skills.description: Use when two or more barcode pre-processing pipelines have been run on the same FASTQ samples and you need to quantify agreement — overlap of detected barcodes and correlation of counts against a published dataset.
skills.name: count-concordance-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: count-concordance-correlation-analysis Use when two or more barcode pre-processing pipelines have been run on the same FASTQ samples and you need to quantify agreement — overlap of detected barcodes and correlation of counts against a published dataset. No gold-standard dataset with known barcode abundance exists — the article notes benchmarking against similar tools was difficult for this reason, so pure accuracy claims cannot be made, only inter-tool agreement Input is raw FASTQ that has not been processed by at least two comparable pre-processing pipelines to generate count tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark the concordance of barcode pre-processing tools (BARtab, pycashier, TimeMachine) by computing barcode set overlaps with bartools in R and Pearson/Spearman correlations of per-sample barcode counts against a published reference dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Benchmark the concordance of barcode pre-processing tools (BARtab, pycashier, TimeMachine) by computing barcode set overlaps with bartools in R and Pearson/Spearman correlations of per-sample barcode counts against a published reference dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No gold-standard dataset with known barcode abundance exists — the article notes benchmarking against similar tools was difficult for this reason, so pure accuracy claims cannot be made, only inter-tool agreement Input is raw FASTQ that has not been processed by at least two comparable pre-processing pipelines to generate count tables

skills.description: Use when raw simulated count matrices must be transformed before correlation- or clustering-based validation, e.g. prior to Pearson/Kendall Tb regulator-gene correlations, Spearman-distance k-medoids clustering, or PCA in MOSim workflows.
skills.name: count-data-log-transformation
skills.search_text: count-data-log-transformation Use when raw simulated count matrices must be transformed before correlation- or clustering-based validation, e.g. prior to Pearson/Kendall Tb regulator-gene correlations, Spearman-distance k-medoids clustering, or PCA in MOSim workflows. The data are already log-transformed or z-scaled (double transformation would distort the correlations used for validation) Downstream analysis requires raw integer counts (e.g. count-based simulation input such as SPARSim or count-aware DE models) rather than transformed profiles The task is simulation itself (running mosim()/sc_mosim()) rather than post-simulation validation of simulated profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies the log(x+1) transformation to raw simulated omics count matrices (bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq from mosim(), scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq from sc_mosim()) so that downstream Pearson, Kendall Tb, and Spearman-distance analyses on MOSim validation outputs are computed on a variance-stabilized scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Applies the log(x+1) transformation to raw simulated omics count matrices (bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq from mosim(), scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq from sc_mosim()) so that downstream Pearson, Kendall Tb, and Spearman-distance analyses on MOSim validation outputs are computed on a variance-stabilized scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already log-transformed or z-scaled (double transformation would distort the correlations used for validation) Downstream analysis requires raw integer counts (e.g. count-based simulation input such as SPARSim or count-aware DE models) rather than transformed profiles The task is simulation itself (running mosim()/sc_mosim()) rather than post-simulation validation of simulated profiles

skills.description: Explains how to preprocess large count-based single-cell expression matrices (e.g. .mat X with gene_list and regix) before SINGE GLG Granger regression so that glmnet_matlab does not hit memory segmentation violations.
skills.name: count-data-log-transformation-for-glmnet
skills.search_text: count-data-log-transformation-for-glmnet Explains how to preprocess large count-based single-cell expression matrices (e.g. .mat X with gene_list and regix) before SINGE GLG Granger regression so that glmnet_matlab does not hit memory segmentation violations. The expression matrix is already log-transformed or continuous — applying log(1+X) again would distort values; the gaussian family is intended for the count-based setting described in the article The dataset is small enough that glmnet_matlab runs without memory segmentation violations under the poisson family Data lack pseudotime ordering, which SINGE's kernel-based Granger regression requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Log-transform large count-based single-cell expression matrices with X1 = log(1+X) and run SINGE's GLG regression with the --family gaussian setting instead of poisson, because glmnet_matlab encounters memory segmentation violations on large count data with the default family. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Log-transform large count-based single-cell expression matrices with X1 = log(1+X) and run SINGE's GLG regression with the --family gaussian setting instead of poisson, because glmnet_matlab encounters memory segmentation violations on large count data with the default family.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is already log-transformed or continuous — applying log(1+X) again would distort values; the gaussian family is intended for the count-based setting described in the article The dataset is small enough that glmnet_matlab runs without memory segmentation violations under the poisson family Data lack pseudotime ordering, which SINGE's kernel-based Granger regression requires

skills.description: Use when benchmarking detection sensitivity and quantitative linearity of a UMI-based scRNA-seq protocol against ERCC spike-ins with known molecule concentrations loaded into GEMs.
skills.name: count-expected-molecule-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: count-expected-molecule-correlation-analysis Use when benchmarking detection sensitivity and quantitative linearity of a UMI-based scRNA-seq protocol against ERCC spike-ins with known molecule concentrations loaded into GEMs. Input data contain no ERCC spike-ins or no known expected molecule counts, so no expected-vs-observed correlation can be computed Goal is gene-level expression quantification of cellular transcriptomes rather than synthetic-RNA sensitivity benchmarking Reads come from a non-UMI or full-length protocol where molecule counts cannot be de-duplicated via cell barcode + UMI combinations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Quantifies how faithfully a droplet-based scRNA-seq system converts known input synthetic RNA molecules (ERCC spike-ins) into detected UMI counts, reporting inferred cDNA conversion efficiency, Pearson correlation between sequenced UMI counts and expected molecule counts, and CV2 across ERCC experiments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Quantifies how faithfully a droplet-based scRNA-seq system converts known input synthetic RNA molecules (ERCC spike-ins) into detected UMI counts, reporting inferred cDNA conversion efficiency, Pearson correlation between sequenced UMI counts and expected molecule counts, and CV2 across ERCC experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data contain no ERCC spike-ins or no known expected molecule counts, so no expected-vs-observed correlation can be computed Goal is gene-level expression quantification of cellular transcriptomes rather than synthetic-RNA sensitivity benchmarking Reads come from a non-UMI or full-length protocol where molecule counts cannot be de-duplicated via cell barcode + UMI combinations

skills.description: Use when a scisorseqr pipeline has produced LongReadInfo/AllInfo and IsoQuantOutput files and you need a cell_type × isoform count matrix plus a per-read assignment table exported as CSV.
skills.name: count-matrix-construction-and-export
skills.search_text: count-matrix-construction-and-export Use when a scisorseqr pipeline has produced LongReadInfo/AllInfo and IsoQuantOutput files and you need a cell_type × isoform count matrix plus a per-read assignment table exported as CSV. Input is raw fastq.gz files that have not yet been barcode-deconvolved, aligned, and filtered — run GetBarcodes/STARalign/MMalign, MapAndFilter, and InfoPerLongRead first The goal is short-read gene-level quantification rather than cell-type-specific isoform/alternative-splicing counts from long reads Only exon-level usage is needed and IsoQuant outputs would suffice without matrix assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Assembles a per-cell-type isoform (and TSS/PolyA) count matrix from the scisorseqr IsoQuantOutput files and exports it as a CSV alongside the filtered per-read assignment table, so that cell-type-specific isoform abundance can be reused in downstream differential analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Assembles a per-cell-type isoform (and TSS/PolyA) count matrix from the scisorseqr IsoQuantOutput files and exports it as a CSV alongside the filtered per-read assignment table, so that cell-type-specific isoform abundance can be reused in downstream differential analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw fastq.gz files that have not yet been barcode-deconvolved, aligned, and filtered — run GetBarcodes/STARalign/MMalign, MapAndFilter, and InfoPerLongRead first The goal is short-read gene-level quantification rather than cell-type-specific isoform/alternative-splicing counts from long reads Only exon-level usage is needed and IsoQuant outputs would suffice without matrix assembly

skills.description: Use when a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix needs to be represented as a topic model corpus to discover latent biological functions with pLDA.
skills.name: count-matrix-corpus-representation
skills.search_text: count-matrix-corpus-representation Use when a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix needs to be represented as a topic model corpus to discover latent biological functions with pLDA. Input is not raw count data (e.g. normalized/transformed expression values), since LDA treats counts as word frequencies per document The goal is cell-type clustering rather than discovering latent biological-function topics modeled as an LDA corpus http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix onto the Latent Dirichlet Allocation corpus framework — genes as words, cells as documents, latent biological functions as topics — so that a penalized LDA (pLDA) model can extract robust, interpretable topic structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-021-09304-8
skills.summary: Maps a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix onto the Latent Dirichlet Allocation corpus framework — genes as words, cells as documents, latent biological functions as topics — so that a penalized LDA (pLDA) model can extract robust, interpretable topic structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw count data (e.g. normalized/transformed expression values), since LDA treats counts as word frequencies per document The goal is cell-type clustering rather than discovering latent biological-function topics modeled as an LDA corpus

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (h5ad/CSV/TSV) is sparse and dropout-heavy and the goal is a denoised count matrix with the same gene x cell dimensions plus optional 32-dim latent representations.
skills.name: count-matrix-denoising
skills.search_text: count-matrix-denoising Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (h5ad/CSV/TSV) is sparse and dropout-heavy and the goal is a denoised count matrix with the same gene x cell dimensions plus optional 32-dim latent representations. Input is already normalized, log-transformed, or not raw counts — DCA's ZINB/NB loss is defined on sparse count data The goal is classical imputation with explicitly defined missing values — the paper notes the non-trivial distinction between true (celltype-specific) and false (dropout) zero counts makes such approaches unsuitable for scRNA-seq Very small datasets or inadequate hyperparameter choices (e.g., a too low-dimensional bottleneck layer), where overimputation is a risk http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Denoise raw scRNA-seq count matrices with the deep count autoencoder (DCA), which trains an autoencoder under a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB/NB) count loss and outputs the inferred NB mean as the denoised matrix, jointly handling dropout, overdispersion and sparsity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Denoise raw scRNA-seq count matrices with the deep count autoencoder (DCA), which trains an autoencoder under a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB/NB) count loss and outputs the inferred NB mean as the denoised matrix, jointly handling dropout, overdispersion and sparsity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized, log-transformed, or not raw counts — DCA's ZINB/NB loss is defined on sparse count data The goal is classical imputation with explicitly defined missing values — the paper notes the non-trivial distinction between true (celltype-specific) and false (dropout) zero counts makes such approaches unsuitable for scRNA-seq Very small datasets or inadequate hyperparameter choices (e.g., a too low-dimensional bottleneck layer), where overimputation is a risk

skills.description: Use when comparing gene expression between barcode groups of unequal size or total UMI content (e.g., All-retained vs EmptyNN-removed) so that DE results are not biased by depth or cell-number imbalance.
skills.name: count-matrix-downsampling
skills.search_text: count-matrix-downsampling Use when comparing gene expression between barcode groups of unequal size or total UMI content (e.g., All-retained vs EmptyNN-removed) so that DE results are not biased by depth or cell-number imbalance. Input is a single-cell dataset whose groups are already matched in cell number and total UMI counts — downsampling would discard data without benefit The analysis goal is cell calling itself rather than fair post-hoc comparison of barcode groups — use EmptyNN/EmptyDrops directly instead Ambient RNA correction is needed before comparing groups — EmptyNN does not correct expression estimates; apply a tool like SoupX first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Balances UMI counts and cell numbers across barcode groups (e.g., All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, EmptyNN-removed) by downsampling counts and cells before differential expression, removing confounding from unbalanced group sizes in the EmptyNN cell hashing analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Balances UMI counts and cell numbers across barcode groups (e.g., All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, EmptyNN-removed) by downsampling counts and cells before differential expression, removing confounding from unbalanced group sizes in the EmptyNN cell hashing analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-cell dataset whose groups are already matched in cell number and total UMI counts — downsampling would discard data without benefit The analysis goal is cell calling itself rather than fair post-hoc comparison of barcode groups — use EmptyNN/EmptyDrops directly instead Ambient RNA correction is needed before comparing groups — EmptyNN does not correct expression estimates; apply a tool like SoupX first

skills.description: Use when benchmarking read-level bioinformatics tools (UMI deduplication, peak calling, alignment/coverage) needs synthetic scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq reads whose counts are grounded in a fitted synthetic count matrix.
skills.name: count-matrix-driven-read-simulation
skills.search_text: count-matrix-driven-read-simulation Use when benchmarking read-level bioinformatics tools (UMI deduplication, peak calling, alignment/coverage) needs synthetic scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq reads whose counts are grounded in a fitted synthetic count matrix. Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI-count ground truths only, not isoform-level ground truths The count matrix itself is sufficient (count-level simulation alone) and no sequencing reads are needed — use scDesign2 directly instead of the read-level pipeline Multi-sample or multi-condition experiments where only a single BAM file is available — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates realistic synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq sequencing reads by first simulating a synthetic gene- or feature-by-cell count matrix (via scDesign2 trained on real UMI counts) and then using that matrix to guide read generation in BAM/FASTQ, as implemented in scReadSim. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Generates realistic synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq sequencing reads by first simulating a synthetic gene- or feature-by-cell count matrix (via scDesign2 trained on real UMI counts) and then using that matrix to guide read generation in BAM/FASTQ, as implemented in scReadSim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI-count ground truths only, not isoform-level ground truths The count matrix itself is sufficient (count-level simulation alone) and no sequencing reads are needed — use scDesign2 directly instead of the read-level pipeline Multi-sample or multi-condition experiments where only a single BAM file is available — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied

skills.search_text: covariance-spectrum-eigendecomposition-analysis Use when a sparse cell-by-gene expression matrix has been eigendecomposed and you must decide which eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs are noise, sparsity artifacts, or true biological signal — including discarding delocalized eigenvectors whose eigenvalues fall outside the MP bulk. The expression matrix has already been imputed or zero-inflation-corrected (e.g., MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE), since the sparsity-driven localization signal this skill detects depends on the raw sparse structure. The analysis goal is distribution-based noise modeling with explicit i.i.d. expression assumptions, which the paper explicitly avoids because the correct distribution for gene expression is unclear. The input is a small matrix where asymptotic RMT distributions (Marchenko-Pastur, Tracy-Widom) do not provide a reliable null. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Eigendecompose the covariance matrix of a sparse single-cell expression dataset and classify each eigenvalue/eigenvector pair against Random Matrix Theory universality (Marchenko-Pastur bulk) plus eigenvector delocalization tests, so that MP-bulk noise and Gaussian-profile (non-informative) eigenvectors are separated from localized signal-carrying directions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035

skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has already been imputed or zero-inflation-corrected (e.g., MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE), since the sparsity-driven localization signal this skill detects depends on the raw sparse structure. skills.search_text: covariate-encoded-trajectory-modelling Use when a cross-sectional single-cell expression cohort carries a sample-level covariate (stimulant, mutation, drug) that may modulate progression, and pseudotime must be inferred without explicit time-series labels. The population background is homogeneous with no sample-level covariate of interest — existing pseudotime methods that assume homogeneous backgrounds may suffice Features are expected to evolve strongly nonlinearly with pseudotime, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime and nonlinear effects require additional model-fit checks A complex high-dimensional mixture of continuous and discrete covariates is needed — the current PhenoPath defers this to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers pseudotemporal cell trajectories in the presence of heterogeneous backgrounds by explicitly encoding covariates (e.g. LPS vs PAM stimulation status) in PhenoPath, a hybrid regression–latent variable Bayesian model fitted via coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Infers pseudotemporal cell trajectories in the presence of heterogeneous backgrounds by explicitly encoding covariates (e.g. LPS vs PAM stimulation status) in PhenoPath, a hybrid regression–latent variable Bayesian model fitted via coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The population background is homogeneous with no sample-level covariate of interest — existing pseudotime methods that assume homogeneous backgrounds may suffice Features are expected to evolve strongly nonlinearly with pseudotime, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime and nonlinear effects require additional model-fit checks A complex high-dimensional mixture of continuous and discrete covariates is needed — the current PhenoPath defers this to future work

skills.description: Use when a cross-sectional expression cohort (e.g. TCGA-BRCA log2(TPM+1) matrix of 4579 HVGs x 1135 samples) must be ordered along a pseudotemporal trajectory while testing which genes' loadings interact with a sample covariate such as ER status.
skills.name: covariate-gene-interaction-significance-testing
skills.search_text: covariate-gene-interaction-significance-testing Use when a cross-sectional expression cohort (e.g. TCGA-BRCA log2(TPM+1) matrix of 4579 HVGs x 1135 samples) must be ordered along a pseudotemporal trajectory while testing which genes' loadings interact with a sample covariate such as ER status. Features are expected to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly, so strongly nonlinear or branching trajectories are the wrong model The analysis requires complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which the current PhenoPath implementation explicitly defers to future work Only retrospective association testing is needed on a fixed trajectory with no covariate-modulated loadings — a plain pseudotime method (e.g. Monocle 2) suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits PhenoPath's Bayesian covariate-pseudotime model to a bulk/single-cell expression cohort with a sample-level covariate (e.g. TCGA-BRCA ER status), then flags genes whose trajectory loadings significantly interact with that covariate. It turns an implicit homogeneous-trajectory assumption into explicit covariate-modulated pathway inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Fits PhenoPath's Bayesian covariate-pseudotime model to a bulk/single-cell expression cohort with a sample-level covariate (e.g. TCGA-BRCA ER status), then flags genes whose trajectory loadings significantly interact with that covariate. It turns an implicit homogeneous-trajectory assumption into explicit covariate-modulated pathway inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are expected to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly, so strongly nonlinear or branching trajectories are the wrong model The analysis requires complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which the current PhenoPath implementation explicitly defers to future work Only retrospective association testing is needed on a fixed trajectory with no covariate-modulated loadings — a plain pseudotime method (e.g. Monocle 2) suffices

skills.description: Use when a PhenoPath fit is available and the goal is to rank genes by covariate-pseudotime interaction effect size and identify significant interactions (e.g. Shalek LPS/PAM genes, TCGA MSI analysis).
skills.name: covariate-pseudotime-interaction-ranking
skills.search_text: covariate-pseudotime-interaction-ranking Use when a PhenoPath fit is available and the goal is to rank genes by covariate-pseudotime interaction effect size and identify significant interactions (e.g. Shalek LPS/PAM genes, TCGA MSI analysis). The task is plain differential expression between covariate groups without a latent trajectory — the paper shows Limma Voom, DESeq2, MAST and Monocle 2 DE-based interaction tests lose AUC as the interaction fraction exceeds 10%, so only apply this skill when interactions must be modelled jointly with pseudotime. Nonlinear gene dynamics along the trajectory are expected or observed, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with pseudotime and model-fit checks are required. The covariate structure is a complex mixture of continuous and discrete factors in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath cannot handle (deferred to future work). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Ranks gene-covariate interactions from a fitted PhenoPath model by posterior interaction effect size, using the Bayesian decision rule |m_beta|/s_beta > k (via interaction_effects, interaction_sds, significant_interactions) to flag genes whose temporal behaviour is perturbed by a covariate such as LPS vs PAM stimulation or MSI status. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Ranks gene-covariate interactions from a fitted PhenoPath model by posterior interaction effect size, using the Bayesian decision rule |m_beta|/s_beta > k (via interaction_effects, interaction_sds, significant_interactions) to flag genes whose temporal behaviour is perturbed by a covariate such as LPS vs PAM stimulation or MSI status.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is plain differential expression between covariate groups without a latent trajectory — the paper shows Limma Voom, DESeq2, MAST and Monocle 2 DE-based interaction tests lose AUC as the interaction fraction exceeds 10%, so only apply this skill when interactions must be modelled jointly with pseudotime. Nonlinear gene dynamics along the trajectory are expected or observed, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with pseudotime and model-fit checks are required. The covariate structure is a complex mixture of continuous and discrete factors in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath cannot handle (deferred to future work).

skills.description: Use when comparing the wall-clock scalability of nuisance-covariate removal methods (SiFT, scVI, scanpy regress_out) on large scRNA-seq data, e.g. continuous covariates regressed from the expression matrix across subsamples up to ~500,000 cells.
skills.name: covariate-regression-from-gene-expression
skills.search_text: covariate-regression-from-gene-expression Use when comparing the wall-clock scalability of nuisance-covariate removal methods (SiFT, scVI, scanpy regress_out) on large scRNA-seq data, e.g. continuous covariates regressed from the expression matrix across subsamples up to ~500,000 cells. The dataset is too small for a scalability benchmark (runtimes are dominated by overhead rather than scaling to ~500,000 cells), so the SiFT < scVI < regress_out ordering cannot be meaningfully tested The goal is batch-effect integration in a joint latent representation rather than removal of covariates at the gene-expression level — scVI's latent correction, not expression-level regression, is the appropriate target No nuisance covariates or prior knowledge defining the signal-to-filter mapping are available, since SiFT's cell-cell similarity kernel cannot be constructed without such a mapping Benchmarks the runtime scalability of covariate-removal methods that operate directly on the gene expression matrix (SiFT filtering, scanpy regress_out) versus latent-space correction (scVI) on increasingly large subsamples of a single-cell dataset, testing whether the reported SiFT < scVI < regress_out runtime ordering holds on the ~500,000-cell Heart Cell Atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks the runtime scalability of covariate-removal methods that operate directly on the gene expression matrix (SiFT filtering, scanpy regress_out) versus latent-space correction (scVI) on increasingly large subsamples of a single-cell dataset, testing whether the reported SiFT < scVI < regress_out runtime ordering holds on the ~500,000-cell Heart Cell Atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is too small for a scalability benchmark (runtimes are dominated by overhead rather than scaling to ~500,000 cells), so the SiFT < scVI < regress_out ordering cannot be meaningfully tested The goal is batch-effect integration in a joint latent representation rather than removal of covariates at the gene-expression level — scVI's latent correction, not expression-level regression, is the appropriate target No nuisance covariates or prior knowledge defining the signal-to-filter mapping are available, since SiFT's cell-cell similarity kernel cannot be constructed without such a mapping

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model for a multi-sample single-cell dataset (e.g., PBMCsca) and need to visualize sample-level manifold parameters or verify that GEDI disentangled donor from technology effects, as in Fig. 2a/2d UMAPs.
skills.name: covariate-regression-on-sample-parameters
skills.search_text: covariate-regression-on-sample-parameters Use when you have a fitted GEDI model for a multi-sample single-cell dataset (e.g., PBMCsca) and need to visualize sample-level manifold parameters or verify that GEDI disentangled donor from technology effects, as in Fig. 2a/2d UMAPs. You need the GEDI generative model's biological outputs (cluster-free DGE, imputation, pathway/TF activities) rather than post-hoc visualization of sample-level parameters A covariate group has only one sample (e.g., a technology represented by a single donor), since group-wise centering would erase the group entirely — the workflow explicitly restricts to rowSums(donor-by-technology table) > 1 You want to quantify or test the covariate effect itself; regressing it out by centering within groups removes exactly the signal you would be testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Post-hoc procedure from the GEDI manuscript (Nat Commun 2024) that encodes each sample by its GEDI-learned sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi), regresses out a confounding covariate (technology or donor) by group-wise row centering, selects the top 20 most variable parameters, and embeds samples via SVD-based PCA followed by UMAP to test whether samples cluster by the complementary covariate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Post-hoc procedure from the GEDI manuscript (Nat Commun 2024) that encodes each sample by its GEDI-learned sample-specific manifold parameters (Qi), regresses out a confounding covariate (technology or donor) by group-wise row centering, selects the top 20 most variable parameters, and embeds samples via SVD-based PCA followed by UMAP to test whether samples cluster by the complementary covariate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the GEDI generative model's biological outputs (cluster-free DGE, imputation, pathway/TF activities) rather than post-hoc visualization of sample-level parameters A covariate group has only one sample (e.g., a technology represented by a single donor), since group-wise centering would erase the group entirely — the workflow explicitly restricts to rowSums(donor-by-technology table) > 1 You want to quantify or test the covariate effect itself; regressing it out by centering within groups removes exactly the signal you would be testing

skills.description: Use when a per-cell technical covariate (e.g. dsb's PC1 of isotype controls and fitted Gaussian-mixture background means µ1) must be regressed out of normalized protein/ADT values to return denoised residuals.
skills.name: covariate-regression-residualization-limma
skills.search_text: covariate-regression-residualization-limma Use when a per-cell technical covariate (e.g. dsb's PC1 of isotype controls and fitted Gaussian-mixture background means µ1) must be regressed out of normalized protein/ADT values to return denoised residuals. Input is raw uncorrected ADT counts — the limma residualization must be applied to the step-I ambient-noise-corrected values, not raw UMIs Dataset lacks isotype control antibodies and a background-mean estimate; usage of the technical component in experiments without isotype controls requires the dsb documentation / Supplementary Note guidance Goal is removing batch structure across multiple batches — the article notes batch normalization behavior depends on the extent of batch uniformity, so this covariate regression is not a general batch-correction guarantee http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Residualize a per-cell technical noise component out of ambient-corrected ADT values using limma::removeBatchEffect(covariates = technical component), the second-step residualization used by the dsb method for CITE-seq protein data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Residualize a per-cell technical noise component out of ambient-corrected ADT values using limma::removeBatchEffect(covariates = technical component), the second-step residualization used by the dsb method for CITE-seq protein data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw uncorrected ADT counts — the limma residualization must be applied to the step-I ambient-noise-corrected values, not raw UMIs Dataset lacks isotype control antibodies and a background-mean estimate; usage of the technical component in experiments without isotype controls requires the dsb documentation / Supplementary Note guidance Goal is removing batch structure across multiple batches — the article notes batch normalization behavior depends on the extent of batch uniformity, so this covariate regression is not a general batch-correction guarantee

skills.description: Use when assembling isoforms per read cloud (barcode) from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads and the extracted barcode subgraph contains parallel (bulge) paths between the same node pairs that must be resolved using barcode-specific coverage instead of aggregate graph coverage.
skills.name: coverage-based-bulge-removal
skills.search_text: coverage-based-bulge-removal Use when assembling isoforms per read cloud (barcode) from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads and the extracted barcode subgraph contains parallel (bulge) paths between the same node pairs that must be resolved using barcode-specific coverage instead of aggregate graph coverage. The goal is to clean the single shared assembly graph itself — deletions there would remove edges that are correct isoform evidence for other barcodes Input is unbarcoded (standard) RNA-seq or genomic reads, where rnaSPAdes/genomic SPAdes pipelines apply graph simplification to the main graph instead The subgraph contains no parallel edges between the same node pairs (no bulge structure to resolve) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Resolves bulges in each barcode-specific subgraph built from a shared SPAdes assembly graph by comparing barcode-specific coverage of parallel edges connecting the same node pairs, rather than editing the shared graph, so that an edge erroneous for one barcode's isoform can remain available for another barcode's isoform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Resolves bulges in each barcode-specific subgraph built from a shared SPAdes assembly graph by comparing barcode-specific coverage of parallel edges connecting the same node pairs, rather than editing the shared graph, so that an edge erroneous for one barcode's isoform can remain available for another barcode's isoform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to clean the single shared assembly graph itself — deletions there would remove edges that are correct isoform evidence for other barcodes Input is unbarcoded (standard) RNA-seq or genomic reads, where rnaSPAdes/genomic SPAdes pipelines apply graph simplification to the main graph instead The subgraph contains no parallel edges between the same node pairs (no bulge structure to resolve)

skills.search_text: coverage-based-missingness-handling Use when a scRNA-seq mutation (VAF) matrix paired with a per-cell sequencing-coverage matrix must be marked and filtered for low-coverage/unobservable observations before SClineager lineage inference. A valid cleaned.RData already exists for the sample — re-running read_sclineager filtering is redundant and slow; proceed to explore_sclineager or run_sclineager instead. Input is bulk or aggregate sequencing data without per-cell coverage values, where per-cell unobservability percentages are undefined. The goal is lineage/genotype inference itself rather than preprocessing — residual drop-outs are handled by SClineager's Bayesian model, not by harder filtering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Marks and removes low-quality observations from a single-cell RNA-seq variant (VAF) matrix by applying a sequencing-coverage cutoff and unobservability thresholds before SClineager lineage inference. This addresses the inherent scRNA-seq issues of low coverage and allelic bias that would otherwise corrupt genetic lineage reconstruction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108589

This addresses the inherent scRNA-seq issues of low coverage and allelic bias that would otherwise corrupt genetic lineage reconstruction.

skills.search_text: coverage-downsampling-analysis Decision support for choosing bin size and sequencing depth before running a scWGS CNA calling pipeline, especially when balancing detection of small (<500 kb) or single-copy events against per-bin read-depth noise at lower coverage. Data is real tumor/brain scWGS rather than simulated truth-matched data — precision/sensitivity cannot be computed without ground truth The pipeline is allele-specific-only by design (e.g., no phased gHETs or paired bulk available for BAF), so depth effects on BAF-driven performance are not testable Depth is above 30x on PTA-amplified cells where amplification artifacts, not coverage, dominate CNA-detection error http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A benchmarking protocol for quantifying how sequencing depth (0.5x, 10x, 30x) and bin size (50/100/500 kb) jointly affect a single-cell CNA caller's precision and sensitivity, using HiScanner on SDX-simulated scWGS data to identify the optimal parameter combination (100 kb bins at 30x). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5

skills.search_text: coverage-log-transformation-normalization Use when raw base-level coverage pileup matrices (e.g. from build_pileup) must be variance-stabilized and normalized across a cohort prior to SCISSOR global/local shape change detection. The analysis goal is differential gene expression on already-aggregated count/feature tables (e.g. RSEM gene-level values) — this skill requires uncompressed base-level pileup coverage, and SCISSOR itself notes existing methods that collapse reads to exons lose the needed resolution The cohort is smaller than ~30 samples, the smallest cohort the authors report considering successfully The gene has many non-expressed samples that were not first excluded under SCISSOR's 'not expressed' vs 'expressed' per-gene filter http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Preprocessing step of the SCISSOR framework that transforms base-level RNA-seq coverage by a logarithmic transformation with an automatically chosen log shift parameter, followed by base-level normalization, to stabilize variance before shape-change detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3

skills.name: coverage-normalization-and-variance-stabilization
skills.search_text: coverage-normalization-and-variance-stabilization Use when base-level pileup coverage matrices from RNA-seq BAM files must be transformed and normalized before cohort-level outlier or structural-variation analysis, e.g. as the input step to Scissor() shape change detection. skills.description: Use when novel cell subtypes (e.g. the three CD163-high macrophage clusters 3, 5, 12 from the GSE171524 COVID-19 dataset) have been identified and you need to know which GO biological pathways are significantly up- or downregulated in disease vs. control samples.
skills.name: covid-19-differential-gene-interpretation
skills.search_text: covid-19-differential-gene-interpretation Use when novel cell subtypes (e.g. the three CD163-high macrophage clusters 3, 5, 12 from the GSE171524 COVID-19 dataset) have been identified and you need to know which GO biological pathways are significantly up- or downregulated in disease vs. control samples. The goal is discovering the novel rare cell subtypes themselves rather than interpreting their differential genes — use scNovel's novel rare cell detection instead. Input is an unannotated single-cell matrix without prior cluster-level differential expression statistics — the skill operates on DE results of already-identified clusters. The comparison is not between disease and control conditions (e.g. no COVID vs. non-COVID contrast), so directional pathway interpretation is not defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Interprets differential expression of COVID-associated genes in scNovel-discovered novel macrophage subtypes by ranking cluster-level DE statistics and running GO enrichment with gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to identify directionally shifted pathways between COVID and non-COVID samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Interprets differential expression of COVID-associated genes in scNovel-discovered novel macrophage subtypes by ranking cluster-level DE statistics and running GO enrichment with gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to identify directionally shifted pathways between COVID and non-COVID samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovering the novel rare cell subtypes themselves rather than interpreting their differential genes — use scNovel's novel rare cell detection instead. Input is an unannotated single-cell matrix without prior cluster-level differential expression statistics — the skill operates on DE results of already-identified clusters. The comparison is not between disease and control conditions (e.g. no COVID vs. non-COVID contrast), so directional pathway interpretation is not defined.

skills.search_text: covid-19-severity-biomarker-association-analysis Use when whole-blood transcript measurements for candidate severity biomarkers must be aligned sample-wise with clinical/lab variables (CRP, lymphocyte counts, type I IFN score) and tested for Pearson correlation sign and significance. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts from one of the 7 severe-vs-mild comparison datasets with no matched clinical/lab metadata — those support differential expression analysis, not biomarker-clinical correlation.
