skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is microarray data (e.g., GSE4922, GSE1456 Affymetrix) rather than RNA-seq; use the AWCA-based classification route validated on Affymetrix log2-transformed data instead of the RNA-seq cross-cohort porting scheme Only PAM50 gene-panel data (e.g., Nanostring nCounter/Prosigna) is available rather than global RNA-seq expression; use the platform-native assay A reference-free single-sample caller is preferred and no pre-defined external reference exists; consider the regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) models, which reached 90% concordance with PAM50 calls without need of a reference sample

skills.description: Use when you have a trained GEDI model on a multi-sample, multi-condition dataset (e.g., two independent COVID-19 cohorts) and need to predict sample-level disease labels in an unseen cohort from learned parameters.
skills.name: cross-cohort-svm-disease-classification
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-svm-disease-classification Use when you have a trained GEDI model on a multi-sample, multi-condition dataset (e.g., two independent COVID-19 cohorts) and need to predict sample-level disease labels in an unseen cohort from learned parameters. You only have a single cohort with no independent cohort to validate against — the skill's evaluation depends on cross-cohort prediction. Your input is raw single-cell counts without a trained GEDI model; the skill requires the learned sample-specific parameter matrix Q, not per-cell expression data. The prediction target is a per-cell property (e.g., cell-type annotation) rather than a sample-level characteristic; the Q matrix has one column per sample. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains support vector machines on GEDI's sample-specific manifold parameters (model$params$Qi) to predict sample-level disease status (COVID-19 vs. healthy) across independent cohorts, using the top 20 most variable parameters as features and reporting AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Trains support vector machines on GEDI's sample-specific manifold parameters (model$params$Qi) to predict sample-level disease status (COVID-19 vs. healthy) across independent cohorts, using the top 20 most variable parameters as features and reporting AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single cohort with no independent cohort to validate against — the skill's evaluation depends on cross-cohort prediction. Your input is raw single-cell counts without a trained GEDI model; the skill requires the learned sample-specific parameter matrix Q, not per-cell expression data. The prediction target is a per-cell property (e.g., cell-type annotation) rather than a sample-level characteristic; the Q matrix has one column per sample.

skills.description: Use when you have paired bulk mRNA/miRNA expression matrices spanning several TCGA cancer types and need one harmonized pooled cohort (genes/miRNAs as row names, patients as columns) to compare per-miRNA prediction accuracy across methods.
skills.name: cross-cohort-tcga-data-pooling-and-harmonization
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-tcga-data-pooling-and-harmonization Use when you have paired bulk mRNA/miRNA expression matrices spanning several TCGA cancer types and need one harmonized pooled cohort (genes/miRNAs as row names, patients as columns) to compare per-miRNA prediction accuracy across methods. Input is single-cell (scRNA-seq) data stored in a Seurat object — use modifySeuratObject-based scRNA preparation instead of pooling bulk TCGA cohorts The training and application cellular/tissue contexts differ substantially — the article warns miRSCAPE accuracy drops when the application sample does not match the training cohort (Figure S9) Only one cancer type or an unpaired miRNA/mRNA dataset is available, so a pooled pan-cancer accuracy comparison is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Pools paired TCGA bulk mRNA and bulk miRNA expression matrices from multiple cancer types into a single cohort, harmonizes them with miRSCAPE's bulkTransform log-transform (justNorm=TRUE for miRNA, no miRNA scaling), so per-sample miRNA prediction accuracy (e.g. miRSCAPE ~0.86 vs miReact ~0.24 top-50 average) can be benchmarked pan-cancer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Pools paired TCGA bulk mRNA and bulk miRNA expression matrices from multiple cancer types into a single cohort, harmonizes them with miRSCAPE's bulkTransform log-transform (justNorm=TRUE for miRNA, no miRNA scaling), so per-sample miRNA prediction accuracy (e.g. miRSCAPE ~0.86 vs miReact ~0.24 top-50 average) can be benchmarked pan-cancer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (scRNA-seq) data stored in a Seurat object — use modifySeuratObject-based scRNA preparation instead of pooling bulk TCGA cohorts The training and application cellular/tissue contexts differ substantially — the article warns miRSCAPE accuracy drops when the application sample does not match the training cohort (Figure S9) Only one cancer type or an unpaired miRNA/mRNA dataset is available, so a pooled pan-cancer accuracy comparison is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when multiple blood transcriptome cohorts need to be compared at the module-aggregate level using the fixed BloodGen3 repertoire, e.g. to cluster disease states by aggregate activity or reproduce the aggregate abundance heatmap.
skills.name: cross-cohort-transcriptome-clustering-interpretation
skills.search_text: cross-cohort-transcriptome-clustering-interpretation Use when multiple blood transcriptome cohorts need to be compared at the module-aggregate level using the fixed BloodGen3 repertoire, e.g. to cluster disease states by aggregate activity or reproduce the aggregate abundance heatmap. The input data are from tissues or species other than human blood — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood transcriptome data and other contexts would require a separate framework The goal is a per-sample fingerprint rather than a cross-cohort aggregate-level comparison — use Individualcomparison instead of group comparison workflows The expression matrix is already Log2-transformed — the BloodGen3Module functions expect un-Log2-transformed data since they transform internally http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduce and interpret cross-cohort fingerprint heatmaps of the BloodGen3 module repertoire, summarizing the 382 modules into their 27 multi-module aggregates and comparing their activity (percentage of genes increased/decreased) across the 16 reference health states to reveal top-level clustering structure (e.g., acute HIV separating from the remaining states). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24584-w
skills.summary: Reproduce and interpret cross-cohort fingerprint heatmaps of the BloodGen3 module repertoire, summarizing the 382 modules into their 27 multi-module aggregates and comparing their activity (percentage of genes increased/decreased) across the 16 reference health states to reveal top-level clustering structure (e.g., acute HIV separating from the remaining states).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are from tissues or species other than human blood — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood transcriptome data and other contexts would require a separate framework The goal is a per-sample fingerprint rather than a cross-cohort aggregate-level comparison — use Individualcomparison instead of group comparison workflows The expression matrix is already Log2-transformed — the BloodGen3Module functions expect un-Log2-transformed data since they transform internally

skills.description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values spans several pairwise comparisons and you must identify which genes recur across conditions or appear only in one (e.g. VAN-specific Q3 down-regulation).
skills.name: cross-comparison-gene-occurrence-tracking
skills.search_text: cross-comparison-gene-occurrence-tracking Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values spans several pairwise comparisons and you must identify which genes recur across conditions or appear only in one (e.g. VAN-specific Q3 down-regulation). Input is raw sequencing data or raw RNA-seq counts without pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the scorecard expects an already-processed CSV You want a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard: setting 'multiplication factor' to 1 collapses the scorecard into a four-way plot, losing the extreme-value regions Your analysis strategy is experience-driven, targeting a preselected set of gene symbols, rather than the data-driven feature extraction the scorecard is designed for http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A scorecard-based procedure that aggregates statistically significant quadrant entries across multiple pairwise experimental comparisons (e.g. VAN, LZD, CPT conditions of Staphylococcus aureus Dataset 1) and produces total-occurrence reports of common and uncommon genes, enabling tracking of pathway loci such as the Gra/Aps cell-envelope stress genes across antibiotic treatments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: A scorecard-based procedure that aggregates statistically significant quadrant entries across multiple pairwise experimental comparisons (e.g. VAN, LZD, CPT conditions of Staphylococcus aureus Dataset 1) and produces total-occurrence reports of common and uncommon genes, enabling tracking of pathway loci such as the Gra/Aps cell-envelope stress genes across antibiotic treatments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data or raw RNA-seq counts without pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the scorecard expects an already-processed CSV You want a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard: setting 'multiplication factor' to 1 collapses the scorecard into a four-way plot, losing the extreme-value regions Your analysis strategy is experience-driven, targeting a preselected set of gene symbols, rather than the data-driven feature extraction the scorecard is designed for

skills.description: Use when comparing a model's prediction/assignment accuracy across input preprocessing conditions or batch-effect regimes, e.g. testing whether raw scRNA-seq counts outperform normalized inputs for cell type labeling.
skills.name: cross-condition-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-condition-accuracy-comparison Use when comparing a model's prediction/assignment accuracy across input preprocessing conditions or batch-effect regimes, e.g. testing whether raw scRNA-seq counts outperform normalized inputs for cell type labeling. The goal is clustering or metagene discovery rather than quantifying label-assignment accuracy against published annotations The input is not a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already a feature table, bulk RNA-seq, or embedding coordinates) so preprocessing variants are not meaningful Only one input preprocessing condition exists, so no cross-condition accuracy comparison is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks GeneVector cell type prediction accuracy across multiple input preprocessing variants (raw counts, log-transformed, normalized, normalized+log-transformed) on the TICA dataset, optionally with an artificially introduced library-size batch effect, and validates each condition against published TICA annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks GeneVector cell type prediction accuracy across multiple input preprocessing variants (raw counts, log-transformed, normalized, normalized+log-transformed) on the TICA dataset, optionally with an artificially introduced library-size batch effect, and validates each condition against published TICA annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering or metagene discovery rather than quantifying label-assignment accuracy against published annotations The input is not a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already a feature table, bulk RNA-seq, or embedding coordinates) so preprocessing variants are not meaningful Only one input preprocessing condition exists, so no cross-condition accuracy comparison is possible

skills.description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference from one biological condition (e.g., ASD patients) must annotate cells in another condition (e.g., controls), and accuracy/ARI of competing supervised and unsupervised annotators must be benchmarked.
skills.name: cross-condition-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: cross-condition-cell-type-annotation Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference from one biological condition (e.g., ASD patients) must annotate cells in another condition (e.g., controls), and accuracy/ARI of competing supervised and unsupervised annotators must be benchmarked. The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data and does not detect unknown types Deciding whether unknown or novel cell types exist in the data (e.g., tissues from novel conditions) — the article recommends consulting biological/clinical experts instead No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised clustering is then the only viable option http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark protocol for supervised cross-condition cell-type annotation on ASD snRNA-seq data, in which NeuCA (feed-forward or hierarchical neural network selected at a Pearson correlation threshold tau=0.95) is trained on one condition and used to predict labels in the other, against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH, Seurat, and SC3 baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for supervised cross-condition cell-type annotation on ASD snRNA-seq data, in which NeuCA (feed-forward or hierarchical neural network selected at a Pearson correlation threshold tau=0.95) is trained on one condition and used to predict labels in the other, against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH, Seurat, and SC3 baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data and does not detect unknown types Deciding whether unknown or novel cell types exist in the data (e.g., tissues from novel conditions) — the article recommends consulting biological/clinical experts instead No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised clustering is then the only viable option

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data from two or more conditions plus pre-classified cell-type labels, and need to determine which pathway-level dysregulations (not single genes) are shared or specific to a condition within each cell type.
skills.name: cross-condition-cell-type-specific-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-condition-cell-type-specific-comparison Use when you have scRNA-seq data from two or more conditions plus pre-classified cell-type labels, and need to determine which pathway-level dysregulations (not single genes) are shared or specific to a condition within each cell type. Conventional over-representation analysis (ORA) on differential-expression gene lists is the goal — the paper showed ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes such as migration-related pathways Input is bulk RNA-seq without single-cell resolution or without cell-type subpopulation labels, since the comparison must be made within each cell type Only one condition is available and no cross-condition contrast can be defined in the contrast file http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Compares scBONITA-derived dysregulated KEGG pathways across two conditions (e.g., pre- vs 1-year post HIV infection, and AS+ vs AS- PLWH) separately within defined immune cell subpopulations such as cytotoxic T cells and monocytes, to identify shared disease-modulated signaling pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Compares scBONITA-derived dysregulated KEGG pathways across two conditions (e.g., pre- vs 1-year post HIV infection, and AS+ vs AS- PLWH) separately within defined immune cell subpopulations such as cytotoxic T cells and monocytes, to identify shared disease-modulated signaling pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Conventional over-representation analysis (ORA) on differential-expression gene lists is the goal — the paper showed ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes such as migration-related pathways Input is bulk RNA-seq without single-cell resolution or without cell-type subpopulation labels, since the comparison must be made within each cell type Only one condition is available and no cross-condition contrast can be defined in the contrast file

skills.description: Use when the same scRNA-seq communication inference (e.g., MDIC3) has been run on two matched conditions of a dataset (e.g., GEO GSE147424 LS and NL skin) and the goal is to distinguish condition-specific communications from shared ones.
skills.name: cross-condition-communication-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-condition-communication-comparison Use when the same scRNA-seq communication inference (e.g., MDIC3) has been run on two matched conditions of a dataset (e.g., GEO GSE147424 LS and NL skin) and the goal is to distinguish condition-specific communications from shared ones. Only a single condition is available — with no matched second condition there is nothing to compare and per-condition MDIC3 analysis alone suffices The analysis goal is ligand-receptor pair identification within one condition (use the MDIC3 LR_exp / readLRDB workflow instead of cross-condition comparison) The two conditions use different cell-type label schemes or incomparable preprocessing, making heatmap cells non-corresponding http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Jointly compare MDIC3-inferred cell-type communication matrices (celltype_communication.txt) across two biological conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis lesional vs nonlesional skin) to identify both shared and condition-specific cell-cell communications, such as the LS-specific InflameFIB-to-InflameDC signal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Jointly compare MDIC3-inferred cell-type communication matrices (celltype_communication.txt) across two biological conditions (e.g., atopic dermatitis lesional vs nonlesional skin) to identify both shared and condition-specific cell-cell communications, such as the LS-specific InflameFIB-to-InflameDC signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single condition is available — with no matched second condition there is nothing to compare and per-condition MDIC3 analysis alone suffices The analysis goal is ligand-receptor pair identification within one condition (use the MDIC3 LR_exp / readLRDB workflow instead of cross-condition comparison) The two conditions use different cell-type label schemes or incomparable preprocessing, making heatmap cells non-corresponding

skills.description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. anti-CD4-treated vs isotype-control P14 cells in chronic LCMV) must be compared for cell subtype frequencies or gene expression within a defined subtype, using a curated reference atlas as the common coordinate system.
skills.name: cross-condition-gene-expression-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-condition-gene-expression-comparison Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. anti-CD4-treated vs isotype-control P14 cells in chronic LCMV) must be compared for cell subtype frequencies or gene expression within a defined subtype, using a curated reference atlas as the common coordinate system. You need to discover novel cell states absent from the reference — use deviation-aware analyses instead, since subtype assignment is constrained to reference subtypes The query is gamma-delta T cells or under-represented CD4+ TIL states, which the reference atlases do not represent You need accurate cell-cell distances or density estimates from UMAP — the README warns UMAP embeddings are highly distorted and should be used for visual exploration only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares subtype composition and gene expression of query scRNA-seq cells between experimental conditions by projecting each condition onto the same reference atlas with ProjecTILs, so that differences (e.g. SLEC-to-Tpex shifts, Pdcd1 elevation) are measured in a stable, shared coordinate system rather than via de novo clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Compares subtype composition and gene expression of query scRNA-seq cells between experimental conditions by projecting each condition onto the same reference atlas with ProjecTILs, so that differences (e.g. SLEC-to-Tpex shifts, Pdcd1 elevation) are measured in a stable, shared coordinate system rather than via de novo clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to discover novel cell states absent from the reference — use deviation-aware analyses instead, since subtype assignment is constrained to reference subtypes The query is gamma-delta T cells or under-represented CD4+ TIL states, which the reference atlases do not represent You need accurate cell-cell distances or density estimates from UMAP — the README warns UMAP embeddings are highly distorted and should be used for visual exploration only

skills.description: Use when a main folder already holds one sub-directory per pairwise comparison with scorecard outputs, and the goal is to rank genes by total occurrences across all comparisons versus genes found only in isolated conditions.
skills.name: cross-condition-scorecard-aggregation
skills.search_text: cross-condition-scorecard-aggregation Use when a main folder already holds one sub-directory per pairwise comparison with scorecard outputs, and the goal is to rank genes by total occurrences across all comparisons versus genes found only in isolated conditions. Individual scorecards have not yet been reconstructed for each pairwise comparison (reconstruct_scorecard has not been run on the sub-folders) — the aggregation re-uses prior outputs and will fail or be meaningless The analysis goal is a single pairwise comparison; use the single-comparison scorecard workflow instead of cross-condition aggregation You want a radial/visual overview of fold-change magnitudes across comparisons — use scorecard_functions.multiple_view(main_folder) instead, which is only for the scorecard and not the four-way plot http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Merges the pre-computed scorecards from all pairwise experimental comparisons in a main folder into a single per-gene occurrence overview (e.g., SA_RS13430 appearing on 65 scorecards), separating globally altered genes from condition-specific ones. It complements `multiple_view` (radial overview) by providing countable, file-based knowledge extraction across comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Merges the pre-computed scorecards from all pairwise experimental comparisons in a main folder into a single per-gene occurrence overview (e.g., SA_RS13430 appearing on 65 scorecards), separating globally altered genes from condition-specific ones. It complements `multiple_view` (radial overview) by providing countable, file-based knowledge extraction across comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual scorecards have not yet been reconstructed for each pairwise comparison (reconstruct_scorecard has not been run on the sub-folders) — the aggregation re-uses prior outputs and will fail or be meaningless The analysis goal is a single pairwise comparison; use the single-comparison scorecard workflow instead of cross-condition aggregation You want a radial/visual overview of fold-change magnitudes across comparisons — use scorecard_functions.multiple_view(main_folder) instead, which is only for the scorecard and not the four-way plot

skills.description: Use when you have two pre-built CommPath objects from matched scRNA-seq conditions (e.g., tumor vs normal) and need to identify communication chains up- or down-regulated between them.
skills.name: cross-condition-scrnaseq-communication-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-condition-scrnaseq-communication-comparison Use when you have two pre-built CommPath objects from matched scRNA-seq conditions (e.g., tumor vs normal) and need to identify communication chains up- or down-regulated between them. You have only a single condition and want initial LR interaction inference — build objects with createCommPath, findLRmarker, findLRpairs, findLRpath, and scorePath first rather than comparePath Your data are not scRNA-seq expression matrices with cell identity labels (CommPath requires normalized, log-transformed gene x cell matrices and cell.info) Conditions lack matched cell clusters in both objects — comparePath requires comparing the same cluster across the two conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Compares pathway-mediated cell-cell communication between two biological conditions (e.g., HCC tumor vs normal) using CommPath's comparePath, pathPlot.compare, and pathChainPlot.compare functions to detect differentially activated pathways in the same clusters and trace the associated ligand-receptor communication chains. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: Compares pathway-mediated cell-cell communication between two biological conditions (e.g., HCC tumor vs normal) using CommPath's comparePath, pathPlot.compare, and pathChainPlot.compare functions to detect differentially activated pathways in the same clusters and trace the associated ligand-receptor communication chains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single condition and want initial LR interaction inference — build objects with createCommPath, findLRmarker, findLRpairs, findLRpath, and scorePath first rather than comparePath Your data are not scRNA-seq expression matrices with cell identity labels (CommPath requires normalized, log-transformed gene x cell matrices and cell.info) Conditions lack matched cell clusters in both objects — comparePath requires comparing the same cluster across the two conditions

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify or compare annotation accuracy across alternative marker gene databases for a single-cell cluster annotation workflow with known ground-truth cell-type labels.
skills.name: cross-database-annotation-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-database-annotation-accuracy-comparison Use when you need to quantify or compare annotation accuracy across alternative marker gene databases for a single-cell cluster annotation workflow with known ground-truth cell-type labels. You have no ground-truth (simulated or manually curated) cell-type labels, so accuracy cannot be scored per database You only need a single annotation for one database — use the standard easyct annotation workflow instead of a cross-database comparison Input is raw count data rather than a processed marker list from differential expression analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks how the choice of cell marker database (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, or Clustermole) affects EasyCellType annotation accuracy by running easyct with GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test on the same simulated PBMC marker input and scoring results against known labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Benchmarks how the choice of cell marker database (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, or Clustermole) affects EasyCellType annotation accuracy by running easyct with GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test on the same simulated PBMC marker input and scoring results against known labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no ground-truth (simulated or manually curated) cell-type labels, so accuracy cannot be scored per database You only need a single annotation for one database — use the standard easyct annotation workflow instead of a cross-database comparison Input is raw count data rather than a processed marker list from differential expression analysis

skills.description: Use when a combined list of annotated plus newly predicted miRNA precursors must be tallied against miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, and PsRNA to count database-specific overlaps and identify previously unannotated candidates.
skills.name: cross-database-candidate-overlap-counting
skills.search_text: cross-database-candidate-overlap-counting Use when a combined list of annotated plus newly predicted miRNA precursors must be tallied against miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, and PsRNA to count database-specific overlaps and identify previously unannotated candidates. The sRNA-Seq reads derive from a species without a reference genome, since iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Reads do not map to the reference genome — the current version ignores unmapped sequencing reads, so overlap counts would be incomplete The goal is downstream functional analysis of the candidates (e.g., GO annotation or miRNA set enrichment), which the MiRNA Compilation overlap tally does not provide http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Quantifies how many combined miRNA precursor candidates produced by the iwa-miRNA MiRNA Compilation module overlap each of the four source databases (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA), revealing which predictions are novel relative to existing annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Quantifies how many combined miRNA precursor candidates produced by the iwa-miRNA MiRNA Compilation module overlap each of the four source databases (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA), revealing which predictions are novel relative to existing annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sRNA-Seq reads derive from a species without a reference genome, since iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Reads do not map to the reference genome — the current version ignores unmapped sequencing reads, so overlap counts would be incomplete The goal is downstream functional analysis of the candidates (e.g., GO annotation or miRNA set enrichment), which the MiRNA Compilation overlap tally does not provide

skills.description: Use when you have a candidate HVG list (e.g. ~16,000 genes from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, M3drop) and need database-derived communication-relevance labels to retain only genes involved in cell-cell communication.
skills.name: cross-database-gene-label-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-database-gene-label-mapping Use when you have a candidate HVG list (e.g. ~16,000 genes from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, M3drop) and need database-derived communication-relevance labels to retain only genes involved in cell-cell communication. The input is raw expression data or spatial coordinates rather than an already-computed HVG candidate list — labeling presupposes genes from the HVG selection step The organism or gene symbols are absent from GeneCards/GO, since the skill depends entirely on predefined database labels rather than expression-based inference You need de novo identification of communication genes from data; this skill only filters using predefined database annotations, which the article notes lack a standardized classification criterion Labels each HVG as communication-related by cross-referencing GeneCards and Gene Ontology (GO) annotation tags, assigning strong_com, weak_com, or unlabeled classes that are then binarized (1/0) to filter HVGs not involved in cell communication. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Labels each HVG as communication-related by cross-referencing GeneCards and Gene Ontology (GO) annotation tags, assigning strong_com, weak_com, or unlabeled classes that are then binarized (1/0) to filter HVGs not involved in cell communication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw expression data or spatial coordinates rather than an already-computed HVG candidate list — labeling presupposes genes from the HVG selection step The organism or gene symbols are absent from GeneCards/GO, since the skill depends entirely on predefined database labels rather than expression-based inference You need de novo identification of communication genes from data; this skill only filters using predefined database annotations, which the article notes lack a standardized classification criterion

skills.description: Use when you have a FAVA (favapy) predicted protein-pair network with Pearson-correlation confidence scores and need to quantify how many of its high-confidence edges are novel vs. supported by STRING, hu.MAP 2.0, or the IDG Tdark catalogue.
skills.name: cross-database-interaction-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-database-interaction-overlap-analysis Use when you have a FAVA (favapy) predicted protein-pair network with Pearson-correlation confidence scores and need to quantify how many of its high-confidence edges are novel vs. supported by STRING, hu.MAP 2.0, or the IDG Tdark catalogue. You need functional (directional/causal) regulatory edges — FAVA infers functional associations from co-variation in latent space, not pathway mechanisms Your network edges lack a correlation-based confidence score (e.g. edges from STRING or hu.MAP themselves), so the ≥70% cut-off cannot be applied The comparison reference is not STRING v11.5 or hu.MAP 2.0 and its edge identifiers are not mappable to the FAVA protein identifiers http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Validates a FAVA-predicted functional association network by intersecting its ≥70%-confidence edges against reference resources (STRING v11.5, hu.MAP 2.0) and the IDG Tdark understudied-protein set, reporting shared and absent edges/nodes as quantitative overlap counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Validates a FAVA-predicted functional association network by intersecting its ≥70%-confidence edges against reference resources (STRING v11.5, hu.MAP 2.0) and the IDG Tdark understudied-protein set, reporting shared and absent edges/nodes as quantitative overlap counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need functional (directional/causal) regulatory edges — FAVA infers functional associations from co-variation in latent space, not pathway mechanisms Your network edges lack a correlation-based confidence score (e.g. edges from STRING or hu.MAP themselves), so the ≥70% cut-off cannot be applied The comparison reference is not STRING v11.5 or hu.MAP 2.0 and its edge identifiers are not mappable to the FAVA protein identifiers

skills.description: Use when a set of predicted polyA sites or 3'-end bins must be benchmarked against public polyA site annotations (PolyASite, PolyA_DB) instead of a sample-specific gold standard.
skills.name: cross-database-polya-site-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-database-polya-site-comparison Use when a set of predicted polyA sites or 3'-end bins must be benchmarked against public polyA site annotations (PolyASite, PolyA_DB) instead of a sample-specific gold standard. The reference set is sample-specific 3'-end sequencing data (e.g., the HBR PolyA-Seq testing set) rather than an aggregated database — aptardi's own evaluation workflow applies directly instead Input transcripts are not 3' terminal exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so coding (upstream exon) APA events cannot be assessed Bin size was altered from the pre-built model's 100-base bins, making intersections with database sites non-comparable to reported metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Evaluates predicted polyadenylation sites (e.g., aptardi output bins) against independent consolidated polyA site databases such as PolyASite 2.0 and PolyA_DB 3 using BEDtools intersections, and computes precision/recall per reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Evaluates predicted polyadenylation sites (e.g., aptardi output bins) against independent consolidated polyA site databases such as PolyASite 2.0 and PolyA_DB 3 using BEDtools intersections, and computes precision/recall per reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference set is sample-specific 3'-end sequencing data (e.g., the HBR PolyA-Seq testing set) rather than an aggregated database — aptardi's own evaluation workflow applies directly instead Input transcripts are not 3' terminal exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so coding (upstream exon) APA events cannot be assessed Bin size was altered from the pre-built model's 100-base bins, making intersections with database sites non-comparable to reported metrics

skills.description: Use when comparing reference-based cell-type mapping methods across two single-cell datasets with batch effect and strong asymmetry in cell number and library depth (e.g., whole-cell scRNA-seq reference to ultra-sparse snRNA-seq nuclei target).
skills.name: cross-dataset-batch-effect-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-batch-effect-evaluation Use when comparing reference-based cell-type mapping methods across two single-cell datasets with batch effect and strong asymmetry in cell number and library depth (e.g., whole-cell scRNA-seq reference to ultra-sparse snRNA-seq nuclei target). When neither dataset is well clustered and contains good gene signatures — the article states 'If neither of the two data is well clustered and contains good gene signatures, scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types.' When the goal is integration via batch correction of imbalanced datasets — the article notes it is unclear how batch correction methods perform when data are significantly imbalanced in cell number and library size per cell When a biomarker-list-only approach would suffice — biomarker-based identification does not work effectively owing to the dropout problem with scRNA-seq data, so a drop-out-tolerant scorer is needed instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark scID's Fisher's-LDA-based cell mapping against scmap and CaSTLe on a batch-affected scRNA-seq reference-to-target task (E18 mouse brain scRNA-seq vs. snRNA-seq nuclei), measuring assignment coverage plus ARI/VI accuracy against reference-derived ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Benchmark scID's Fisher's-LDA-based cell mapping against scmap and CaSTLe on a batch-affected scRNA-seq reference-to-target task (E18 mouse brain scRNA-seq vs. snRNA-seq nuclei), measuring assignment coverage plus ARI/VI accuracy against reference-derived ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When neither dataset is well clustered and contains good gene signatures — the article states 'If neither of the two data is well clustered and contains good gene signatures, scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types.' When the goal is integration via batch correction of imbalanced datasets — the article notes it is unclear how batch correction methods perform when data are significantly imbalanced in cell number and library size per cell When a biomarker-list-only approach would suffice — biomarker-based identification does not work effectively owing to the dropout problem with scRNA-seq data, so a drop-out-tolerant scorer is needed instead

skills.description: Use when comparing competing feature sets or representations for cell clustering across several scRNA-seq datasets, requiring replicate-level metrics (AMI) against known subpopulation labels to show consistency.
skills.name: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing competing feature sets or representations for cell clustering across several scRNA-seq datasets, requiring replicate-level metrics (AMI) against known subpopulation labels to show consistency. Cells have no known subpopulation labels, so AMI against ground truth cannot be computed The goal is a single-dataset clustering analysis rather than a controlled feature-type comparison across datasets Only raw SNV/GE matrices exist and eeSNV features cannot yet be derived via SSrGE fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark two feature representations (eeSNVs derived by SSrGE vs full gene expression matrices) for scRNA-seq subpopulation identification across multiple GEO datasets and clustering algorithms, quantifying performance with adjusted mutual information (AMI) over 30 bootstrap runs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Benchmark two feature representations (eeSNVs derived by SSrGE vs full gene expression matrices) for scRNA-seq subpopulation identification across multiple GEO datasets and clustering algorithms, quantifying performance with adjusted mutual information (AMI) over 30 bootstrap runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have no known subpopulation labels, so AMI against ground truth cannot be computed The goal is a single-dataset clustering analysis rather than a controlled feature-type comparison across datasets Only raw SNV/GE matrices exist and eeSNV features cannot yet be derived via SSrGE fitting

skills.description: Use when validating an automatic cluster annotation method on several independent published scRNA-seq datasets with known manual annotations, to report per-dataset consistency rates and an overall average.
skills.name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation Use when validating an automatic cluster annotation method on several independent published scRNA-seq datasets with known manual annotations, to report per-dataset consistency rates and an overall average. Evaluating annotation accuracy on a single dataset with no published manual annotations available for comparison The goal is tool-to-tool comparison of annotation methods rather than validating one tool against published manual labels (use the scCATCH_performance_comparison comparison workflow for that) Datasets whose tissues or species are not covered by the CellMatch reference database, since the limited reference database potentially leads to incorrect annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a cell-type annotation tool's accuracy across multiple independent published scRNA-seq datasets by comparing automatic cluster annotations against published manual annotations and computing per-dataset cluster-consistency rates plus an average, as scCATCH did across Enge, Wu, Lindsey, Zheng, Zeisel and Heng (67%-100%, average 83%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Benchmark a cell-type annotation tool's accuracy across multiple independent published scRNA-seq datasets by comparing automatic cluster annotations against published manual annotations and computing per-dataset cluster-consistency rates plus an average, as scCATCH did across Enge, Wu, Lindsey, Zheng, Zeisel and Heng (67%-100%, average 83%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating annotation accuracy on a single dataset with no published manual annotations available for comparison The goal is tool-to-tool comparison of annotation methods rather than validating one tool against published manual labels (use the scCATCH_performance_comparison comparison workflow for that) Datasets whose tissues or species are not covered by the CellMatch reference database, since the limited reference database potentially leads to incorrect annotation

skills.description: Use when a classifier's robustness must be benchmarked across multiple independently sequenced scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 6 cross-platform human pancreas training-test pairs), comparing 2+ annotation methods by mean classification accuracy.
skills.name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation Use when a classifier's robustness must be benchmarked across multiple independently sequenced scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 6 cross-platform human pancreas training-test pairs), comparing 2+ annotation methods by mean classification accuracy. Input is a single dataset with only one train/test split — the multi-pair repeated-splits design and cross-platform comparison cannot be meaningfully applied The question is about SciBet's false-positive control on unseen cell types (GSE108989 T-cell negative-control scenario) rather than method-vs-method accuracy benchmarking Datasets lack authoritative cell type annotations, since supervised training of SciBet, Seurat v3, and scmap all depends on ground-truth labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a cell type classifier across ordered training-test pairs built from independently generated scRNA-seq datasets, comparing against baseline methods via repeated stratified hold-out splits. Used to quantify cross-platform (e.g., full-length-read vs UMI) robustness of annotation methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Benchmark a cell type classifier across ordered training-test pairs built from independently generated scRNA-seq datasets, comparing against baseline methods via repeated stratified hold-out splits. Used to quantify cross-platform (e.g., full-length-read vs UMI) robustness of annotation methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single dataset with only one train/test split — the multi-pair repeated-splits design and cross-platform comparison cannot be meaningfully applied The question is about SciBet's false-positive control on unseen cell types (GSE108989 T-cell negative-control scenario) rather than method-vs-method accuracy benchmarking Datasets lack authoritative cell type annotations, since supervised training of SciBet, Seurat v3, and scmap all depends on ground-truth labels

skills.description: Use when you have 2+ annotated scRNA-seq reference datasets with batch effects and a held-out unlabeled target dataset, and you need cross-dataset cell-type annotation plus an evaluation against known labels.
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-annotation-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-annotation-evaluation Use when you have 2+ annotated scRNA-seq reference datasets with batch effects and a held-out unlabeled target dataset, and you need cross-dataset cell-type annotation plus an evaluation against known labels. Datasets are not yet aligned: scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool and advises alignment (e.g., with Seurat v3, scVI, or scArches) before matching cell populations The analysis requires adding a new dataset to an existing tree without rerunning integration — with current batch correction tools the alignment and scHPL must be rerun The biological system violates hierarchical cell-type relationships, e.g., dedifferentiation states like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train a hierarchical classification tree with scHPL on multiple annotated reference datasets and evaluate it by predicting labels on an independent held-out dataset, using Seurat v3 alignment and a linear SVM classifier. This skill reproduces the PBMC inter-dataset experiment (Fig. 5) where a tree learned from three PBMC datasets annotates PBMC-Bench10Xv3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Train a hierarchical classification tree with scHPL on multiple annotated reference datasets and evaluate it by predicting labels on an independent held-out dataset, using Seurat v3 alignment and a linear SVM classifier. This skill reproduces the PBMC inter-dataset experiment (Fig. 5) where a tree learned from three PBMC datasets annotates PBMC-Bench10Xv3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not yet aligned: scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool and advises alignment (e.g., with Seurat v3, scVI, or scArches) before matching cell populations The analysis requires adding a new dataset to an existing tree without rerunning integration — with current batch correction tools the alignment and scHPL must be rerun The biological system violates hierarchical cell-type relationships, e.g., dedifferentiation states like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets with overlapping cell types must be integrated and you need to quantify dataset mixing vs. cell-type resolution for competing correction methods (e.g., ComBat, MNN, CCA, Harmony, scVI, DIRECTi).
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-embedding-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-embedding-evaluation Use when scRNA-seq datasets with overlapping cell types must be integrated and you need to quantify dataset mixing vs. cell-type resolution for competing correction methods (e.g., ComBat, MNN, CCA, Harmony, scVI, DIRECTi). Datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells, since the over-parameterized neural-network model may suffer from under-training issues (a cell number of 3000 is generally sufficient) Mega-scale dataset integration where highly skewed cell-type composition may lead to over-correcting of batches The goal is cell querying/annotation against a curated reference rather than comparing batch-correction methods' embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks batch-effect correction / integration methods on scRNA-seq dataset combinations by scoring corrected cell embeddings with the Seurat alignment score (batch mixing among matched cell types) and mean average precision (MAP, cell-type relationship preservation), reproducing Cell BLAST's Fig. 2a comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks batch-effect correction / integration methods on scRNA-seq dataset combinations by scoring corrected cell embeddings with the Seurat alignment score (batch mixing among matched cell types) and mean average precision (MAP, cell-type relationship preservation), reproducing Cell BLAST's Fig. 2a comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells, since the over-parameterized neural-network model may suffer from under-training issues (a cell number of 3000 is generally sufficient) Mega-scale dataset integration where highly skewed cell-type composition may lead to over-correcting of batches The goal is cell querying/annotation against a curated reference rather than comparing batch-correction methods' embeddings

skills.description: Use when per-dataset cell subtype fine labels have been produced (fine-labels.RDS per dataset) and you need to reconcile or compare subtype label definitions across published references by constructing a cross-dataset Jaccard similarity matrix.
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-label-integration
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-label-integration Use when per-dataset cell subtype fine labels have been produced (fine-labels.RDS per dataset) and you need to reconcile or compare subtype label definitions across published references by constructing a cross-dataset Jaccard similarity matrix. You only need rough cell-type labels for a single dataset — predCellType alone suffices and the cross-dataset label integration is unnecessary. Your data are spatial transcriptomics or bulk TCGA expression — the label similarity maps were constructed by testing the trained subtype classifiers on the 15 scRNA-seq datasets, not on spatial or bulk inputs. You want de novo clustering-based cell identification rather than preserving original published label definitions across references. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A scCancer2-based workflow that integrates fine-grained cell subtype labels across published scRNA-seq datasets (HCC cohorts Ma2022, Zhang2019, Lu2022, Zheng2017, Sun2021, Liu2023, Losic2020, Ma2021 and four Xue2022 partitions) and quantitatively builds Jaccard similarity maps between subtype labels defined in different references (e.g., NSCLC and BRCA vs. HCC 'Lymphoid-B'). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: A scCancer2-based workflow that integrates fine-grained cell subtype labels across published scRNA-seq datasets (HCC cohorts Ma2022, Zhang2019, Lu2022, Zheng2017, Sun2021, Liu2023, Losic2020, Ma2021 and four Xue2022 partitions) and quantitatively builds Jaccard similarity maps between subtype labels defined in different references (e.g., NSCLC and BRCA vs. HCC 'Lymphoid-B').
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need rough cell-type labels for a single dataset — predCellType alone suffices and the cross-dataset label integration is unnecessary. Your data are spatial transcriptomics or bulk TCGA expression — the label similarity maps were constructed by testing the trained subtype classifiers on the 15 scRNA-seq datasets, not on spatial or bulk inputs. You want de novo clustering-based cell identification rather than preserving original published label definitions across references.

skills.description: Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets (batch-corrected/aligned, e.g. with scVI or Seurat) must have their cell population labels matched and a hierarchical classification tree learned, especially when name-based matching fails (e.g. different labs, resolutions, or nomenclatures).
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-population-matching
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-population-matching Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets (batch-corrected/aligned, e.g. with scVI or Seurat) must have their cell population labels matched and a hierarchical classification tree learned, especially when name-based matching fails (e.g. different labs, resolutions, or nomenclatures). Datasets are not yet batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool and requires alignment (scVI, scArches, Seurat) beforehand Cell populations violate hierarchical/tree relationships, e.g. dedifferentiation cases such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A new dataset is added but rerunning the full alignment is not feasible — with current batch correction tools the alignment and consequently scHPL must be rerun http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A skill for matching cell population labels across scRNA-seq datasets using scHPL's hierarchical progressive learning: cross-predictions between datasets yield confusion matrices from which a matching matrix is built, driving tree updates (match, merge, split, new population) and construction of a hierarchical classification tree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: A skill for matching cell population labels across scRNA-seq datasets using scHPL's hierarchical progressive learning: cross-predictions between datasets yield confusion matrices from which a matching matrix is built, driving tree updates (match, merge, split, new population) and construction of a hierarchical classification tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not yet batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool and requires alignment (scVI, scArches, Seurat) beforehand Cell populations violate hierarchical/tree relationships, e.g. dedifferentiation cases such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A new dataset is added but rerunning the full alignment is not feasible — with current batch correction tools the alignment and consequently scHPL must be rerun

skills.description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset and an unlabeled target dataset (e.g., Drop-seq reference to Smart-seq2 target, or Smart-Seq2 to CEL-Seq pancreas) must be mapped across technologies or batch conditions.
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-type-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-type-mapping Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset and an unlabeled target dataset (e.g., Drop-seq reference to Smart-seq2 target, or Smart-Seq2 to CEL-Seq pancreas) must be mapped across technologies or batch conditions. Neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach' in that case Only top biomarker genes with simple per-gene thresholds are available — dropout makes such marker-threshold baselines assign most cells as Orphans The goal is batch-corrected integration of similarly sized, well-matched datasets where batch-correction methods (e.g., scVI) may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assign cell-type labels to a target scRNA-seq dataset using a labeled reference dataset via scID, a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework that extracts cluster-specific gene signatures, estimates discriminative weights, and assigns target cells with a finite mixture of Gaussians—robust to batch effect and strong imbalance in cell number and library size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Assign cell-type labels to a target scRNA-seq dataset using a labeled reference dataset via scID, a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework that extracts cluster-specific gene signatures, estimates discriminative weights, and assigns target cells with a finite mixture of Gaussians—robust to batch effect and strong imbalance in cell number and library size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach' in that case Only top biomarker genes with simple per-gene thresholds are available — dropout makes such marker-threshold baselines assign most cells as Orphans The goal is batch-corrected integration of similarly sized, well-matched datasets where batch-correction methods (e.g., scVI) may suffice

skills.description: Use when a labeled training scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) must annotate cells from a different dataset — same species or cross-species — where the test set contains cell types with no annotated cells in the training data.

skills.summary: Train an OnClass bilinear neural network on one annotated scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Lemur 4) and predict Cell Ontology cell type labels on a different dataset (e.g., Lemur 1 or Muris FACS to Lemur 2), including unseen cell types, using the Cell Ontology graph to extend scores to terms absent from the training labels.

skills.description: Use when a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., .h5ad from GEO) must be used to label cells in a different test dataset whose taxonomy may contain unseen cell types, and errors from noise/batch effects need suppression.
skills.name: cross-dataset-cell-type-transfer
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-cell-type-transfer Use when a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., .h5ad from GEO) must be used to label cells in a different test dataset whose taxonomy may contain unseen cell types, and errors from noise/batch effects need suppression. Each cell population is not well clustered in the test data — the article notes 'for proper identification, each cell populations should be well clustered, even though this is not always the case' The task requires a standardized, prebuilt cell-type taxonomy — none exists; researchers must prepare their own marker lists and taxonomy The input is already annotated per-cell with a trusted shared taxonomy and no cross-dataset generalization is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transfer cell-type annotations across scRNA-seq datasets using MarkerCount's reference-based mode, which binarizes expression, counts expressed markers instead of using expression levels, and applies a rejection threshold plus cluster-basis reassignment to handle unknown populations and batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Transfer cell-type annotations across scRNA-seq datasets using MarkerCount's reference-based mode, which binarizes expression, counts expressed markers instead of using expression levels, and applies a rejection threshold plus cluster-basis reassignment to handle unknown populations and batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each cell population is not well clustered in the test data — the article notes 'for proper identification, each cell populations should be well clustered, even though this is not always the case' The task requires a standardized, prebuilt cell-type taxonomy — none exists; researchers must prepare their own marker lists and taxonomy The input is already annotated per-cell with a trusted shared taxonomy and no cross-dataset generalization is needed

skills.description: Use when a new cell-annotation or classification method must be compared against established algorithms on the same ground-truth-labeled scRNA-seq test sets with ranked, per-dataset metrics.
skills.name: cross-dataset-classifier-comparison

The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) rather than the binary cancer vs non-cancer task this comparison covers Input is raw counts without library-depth normalization (e.g., TPM/CPM), since PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix The test data were used for feature selection of the candidate method, which would overestimate training-set performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a supervised single-cell classifier (PreCanCell) head-to-head against seven comparators (CHETAH, SciBet, SCINA, scmap-cell, scmap-cluster, SingleR, ikarus) on identical test sets using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, and AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Benchmark a supervised single-cell classifier (PreCanCell) head-to-head against seven comparators (CHETAH, SciBet, SCINA, scmap-cell, scmap-cluster, SingleR, ikarus) on identical test sets using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, and AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) rather than the binary cancer vs non-cancer task this comparison covers Input is raw counts without library-depth normalization (e.g., TPM/CPM), since PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix The test data were used for feature selection of the candidate method, which would overestimate training-set performance

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a clustering model across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and random seeds (e.g. 20 datasets, seeds 1111–10000) and you must assemble per-dataset mean/median ARI comparisons into one table.
skills.name: cross-dataset-clustering-benchmark-aggregation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-clustering-benchmark-aggregation Use when benchmarking a clustering model across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and random seeds (e.g. 20 datasets, seeds 1111–10000) and you must assemble per-dataset mean/median ARI comparisons into one table. You are evaluating a single dataset with a single run — per-seed aggregation and cross-dataset tables are unnecessary overhead No ground-truth cell-type labels exist for the datasets, so ARI (rand_index.m) and NMI (computeNMI.m) cannot be computed You need a novel clustering method itself rather than a benchmark/ablation comparison of existing configurations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates clustering performance (ARI/NMI) across many scRNA-seq datasets, seeds, and model configurations into a single benchmark table, following scBGEDA's protocol of running the dual denoising autoencoder plus bipartite graph ensemble clustering over multiple random seeds per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Aggregates clustering performance (ARI/NMI) across many scRNA-seq datasets, seeds, and model configurations into a single benchmark table, following scBGEDA's protocol of running the dual denoising autoencoder plus bipartite graph ensemble clustering over multiple random seeds per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are evaluating a single dataset with a single run — per-seed aggregation and cross-dataset tables are unnecessary overhead No ground-truth cell-type labels exist for the datasets, so ARI (rand_index.m) and NMI (computeNMI.m) cannot be computed You need a novel clustering method itself rather than a benchmark/ablation comparison of existing configurations

skills.description: Use when you need to compare a scRNA-seq cell clustering method's accuracy (ARI) against published tools across many datasets with known cell type labels, e.g. benchmarking scQA on GEO/ArrayExpress data such as GSE57249 or E-MTAB-5061.
skills.name: cross-dataset-clustering-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-clustering-comparison Use when you need to compare a scRNA-seq cell clustering method's accuracy (ARI) against published tools across many datasets with known cell type labels, e.g. benchmarking scQA on GEO/ArrayExpress data such as GSE57249 or E-MTAB-5061. The input data lacks annotated cell type labels, since the comparison metric (ARI) is computed against known labels and cannot be applied without them The goal is to identify cell type-specific key genes or marker genes for a single dataset rather than to benchmark clustering accuracy across datasets You need de novo clustering of a new dataset rather than a method comparison — use scQA directly instead of the benchmarking workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks a single-cell clustering method (scQA) against nine salient algorithms (SC3, Seurat, CIDR, pcaReduce, SIMLR, TSCAN, RaceID2, scGNN, scHFC) on 20 public scRNA-seq datasets by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against annotated cell type labels, producing a per-dataset, per-method comparison table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Benchmarks a single-cell clustering method (scQA) against nine salient algorithms (SC3, Seurat, CIDR, pcaReduce, SIMLR, TSCAN, RaceID2, scGNN, scHFC) on 20 public scRNA-seq datasets by computing the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) against annotated cell type labels, producing a per-dataset, per-method comparison table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data lacks annotated cell type labels, since the comparison metric (ARI) is computed against known labels and cannot be applied without them The goal is to identify cell type-specific key genes or marker genes for a single dataset rather than to benchmark clustering accuracy across datasets You need de novo clustering of a new dataset rather than a method comparison — use scQA directly instead of the benchmarking workflow

skills.description: Use when multiple methods infer cell-type-specific co-expression from scRNA-seq data and you must test which method's significant gene pairs replicate in an independent dataset.
skills.name: cross-dataset-coexpression-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-coexpression-reproducibility-assessment Use when multiple methods infer cell-type-specific co-expression from scRNA-seq data and you must test which method's significant gene pairs replicate in an independent dataset. Only one scRNA-seq dataset is available with no independent replication dataset, so reproducibility cannot be computed. Cells are aggregated across cell types rather than subset — co-expression inference is then confounded (Simpson's paradox), invalidating any reproducibility comparison. Input is bulk RNA-seq data: inferred networks are confounded by varying cell-type compositions across samples and only give an aggregated view of gene regulations. A benchmarking skill for scRNA-seq co-expression inference: it quantifies whether significant gene co-expressions inferred by a method (e.g., CS-CORE) are recovered in independent datasets, against benchmarks such as rho-sctransform, rho-analytic PR, and SpQN. It was used to show CS-CORE co-expressions in Alzheimer's disease postmortem brain control cells are more reproducible than competitors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for scRNA-seq co-expression inference: it quantifies whether significant gene co-expressions inferred by a method (e.g., CS-CORE) are recovered in independent datasets, against benchmarks such as rho-sctransform, rho-analytic PR, and SpQN. It was used to show CS-CORE co-expressions in Alzheimer's disease postmortem brain control cells are more reproducible than competitors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one scRNA-seq dataset is available with no independent replication dataset, so reproducibility cannot be computed. Cells are aggregated across cell types rather than subset — co-expression inference is then confounded (Simpson's paradox), invalidating any reproducibility comparison. Input is bulk RNA-seq data: inferred networks are confounded by varying cell-type compositions across samples and only give an aggregated view of gene regulations.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify genes consistently dysregulated across several public transcriptomics cohorts (e.g. severe vs mild COVID-19 peripheral blood RNA-seq) instead of relying on a single-dataset DE result.
skills.name: cross-dataset-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-differential-expression-analysis Use when the goal is to identify genes consistently dysregulated across several public transcriptomics cohorts (e.g. severe vs mild COVID-19 peripheral blood RNA-seq) instead of relying on a single-dataset DE result. The analysis is limited to a single dataset with no cross-cohort consistency requirement — a per-dataset DE workflow alone suffices. The data are single-cell RNA-seq PBMC/BALF matrices; the article handles those with a separate subsetting workflow, not this bulk-matrix severity pipeline. The comparison groups are severe vs healthy rather than severe vs mild, unless that contrast is explicitly the intended output. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A skill for re-analysing multiple independent bulk RNA-seq/transcriptomics datasets to rank genes by the consistency of their differential expression between severe and mild COVID-19, rather than in any single cohort. It grounds gene-level calls in per-dataset fold changes and t-test p-values aggregated across 7 public datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: A skill for re-analysing multiple independent bulk RNA-seq/transcriptomics datasets to rank genes by the consistency of their differential expression between severe and mild COVID-19, rather than in any single cohort. It grounds gene-level calls in per-dataset fold changes and t-test p-values aggregated across 7 public datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is limited to a single dataset with no cross-cohort consistency requirement — a per-dataset DE workflow alone suffices. The data are single-cell RNA-seq PBMC/BALF matrices; the article handles those with a separate subsetting workflow, not this bulk-matrix severity pipeline. The comparison groups are severe vs healthy rather than severe vs mild, unless that contrast is explicitly the intended output.

skills.description: Use when drug response data come from datasets with incompatible units (e.g., GDSC IC50 vs PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC) and must be placed on a common sensitivity scale before model training or cross-dataset correlation.
skills.name: cross-dataset-drug-response-scale-transformation
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-drug-response-scale-transformation Use when drug response data come from datasets with incompatible units (e.g., GDSC IC50 vs PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC) and must be placed on a common sensitivity scale before model training or cross-dataset correlation. Both datasets already share one response scale (e.g., all IC50, or all AUC with identical normalization) — re-applying −log(IC50) or D′ = 2.40D − 1.20 would distort the values. Predicting response for a compound absent from the GDSC/PRISM screens — scDrug's prediction is limited to experimentally screened compounds, so no transformed scale exists for it. Single-dataset IC50 prediction with the pretrained GDSC model only (drug_response_prediction.py --model GDSC), where no cross-dataset harmonization is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Harmonizes pharmacological response measurements recorded in different units — GDSC IC50 and PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC — onto a shared sensitivity scale via −log(IC50) and the linear rescaling D′ = 2.40D − 1.20 of 1 − AUC. This makes GDSC-trained and PRISM-trained response models comparable, with an expected cross-dataset Pearson correlation of 0.615. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Harmonizes pharmacological response measurements recorded in different units — GDSC IC50 and PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC — onto a shared sensitivity scale via −log(IC50) and the linear rescaling D′ = 2.40D − 1.20 of 1 − AUC. This makes GDSC-trained and PRISM-trained response models comparable, with an expected cross-dataset Pearson correlation of 0.615.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Both datasets already share one response scale (e.g., all IC50, or all AUC with identical normalization) — re-applying −log(IC50) or D′ = 2.40D − 1.20 would distort the values. Predicting response for a compound absent from the GDSC/PRISM screens — scDrug's prediction is limited to experimentally screened compounds, so no transformed scale exists for it. Single-dataset IC50 prediction with the pretrained GDSC model only (drug_response_prediction.py --model GDSC), where no cross-dataset harmonization is required.

skills.description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data reproduce a protocol-specific expression property (e.g., gene length bias in non-UMI data) by direct comparison against a matched experimental dataset.
skills.name: cross-dataset-expression-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-expression-comparison Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data reproduce a protocol-specific expression property (e.g., gene length bias in non-UMI data) by direct comparison against a matched experimental dataset. Input is already observed UMI count data and the question does not concern protocol-specific technical bias, since UMI data show no gene length bias to compare The reference dataset is not matched to the simulated protocol (e.g., comparing UMI simulations against a non-UMI reference), which invalidates the length-bias comparison You need to simulate batch effects or trajectory/DE ground truth rather than validate technical-variation properties; use DivideBatches or getDEgenes/getTrajectoryGenes instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares simulated SymSim scRNA-seq data with an experimental reference dataset (the Gaublomme Th17 ss2_130cells_counts non-UMI dataset) by plotting gene length versus length-normalized expression to verify that simulated technical variation reproduces gene length bias seen in real full-length protocols. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Compares simulated SymSim scRNA-seq data with an experimental reference dataset (the Gaublomme Th17 ss2_130cells_counts non-UMI dataset) by plotting gene length versus length-normalized expression to verify that simulated technical variation reproduces gene length bias seen in real full-length protocols.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already observed UMI count data and the question does not concern protocol-specific technical bias, since UMI data show no gene length bias to compare The reference dataset is not matched to the simulated protocol (e.g., comparing UMI simulations against a non-UMI reference), which invalidates the length-bias comparison You need to simulate batch effects or trajectory/DE ground truth rather than validate technical-variation properties; use DivideBatches or getDEgenes/getTrajectoryGenes instead

skills.search_text: cross-dataset-expression-correlation-mapping Use when unsupervised BUSseq clusters need biological labels beyond FACS labels — e.g., verifying an intermediate CMP-MEP cluster or mapping a CLP/LMPP-like cluster to Haemopedia progenitor populations. Cells already have trusted FACS or reference-matched labels, so unsupervised cluster-to-reference correlation adds no annotation value The scRNA-seq data are not read counts (e.g., UMI-normalized or TPM matrices), since BUSseq models count data with overdispersion and dropout directly Batches are completely confounded with cell types (e.g., batch 1 has only cell types 1–2, batch 2 only 3–4), where no batch-correction method is applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Annotates clusters discovered by BUSseq in a target scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., the mouse hematopoietic study) by correlating cell-type mean expression profiles with reference cell-type profiles from an external resource (Haemopedia RNA-seq), combined with marker-gene heatmap validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2

skills.name: cross-dataset-gene-clustering
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-gene-clustering Use when a published gene signature (e.g. Bailey ADEX) may be confounded by tissue-nonspecific or non-tumor genes, and you have ≥2 independently parsed bulk RNAseq datasets to test cross-dataset reproducibility of gene groupings. You want to cluster samples (tumors) rather than genes — pdacR's subtyping workflows handle sample-level clustering; this skill operates in gene-wise mode specifically to decompose signatures. skills.summary: Runs gene-wise consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus, kmeans with euclidean distance) independently on multiple PDAC RNAseq datasets to decompose a gene signature into subset-specific components, used to test whether the Bailey ADEX/Immunogenic signatures are confounded by non-PDAC-specific genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to cluster samples (tumors) rather than genes — pdacR's subtyping workflows handle sample-level clustering; this skill operates in gene-wise mode specifically to decompose signatures. skills.name: cross-dataset-gene-set-intersection
skills.search_text: cross-dataset-gene-set-intersection Use when building robust cancer-cell classification features by intersecting malignant-vs-non-malignant DEGs across multiple training scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) rather than relying on a single dataset.
