skills.search_text: cross-method-annotation-comparison Use when a pretrained annotation model (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs) must be validated against baseline annotators (Seurat CIBERSORT-based labeling, SingleR with Human Primary Cell Atlas / Blueprint-ENCODE) on the same held-out scRNA-seq cells. Input data are not tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq — the MetaTiME MeC space was learnt from millions of TME single cells across cancer types and may not transfer outside that domain. You only need one annotation method's output, not a head-to-head resolution comparison across methods on identical cells. Cells have already been manually annotated with curated marker genes and the goal is label merging, not benchmarking automated annotators. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a learned cell-state annotator (MetaTiME's 86 meta-components) against marker/reference-based automated annotators (Seurat CIBERSORT signatures, SingleR) on identical held-out single cells, quantifying the resolution gap in cell-state labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a learned cell-state annotator (MetaTiME's 86 meta-components) against marker/reference-based automated annotators (Seurat CIBERSORT signatures, SingleR) on identical held-out single cells, quantifying the resolution gap in cell-state labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq — the MetaTiME MeC space was learnt from millions of TME single cells across cancer types and may not transfer outside that domain. You only need one annotation method's output, not a head-to-head resolution comparison across methods on identical cells. Cells have already been manually annotated with curated marker genes and the goal is label merging, not benchmarking automated annotators.

skills.description: Use when several prior-knowledge cell-type annotation methods must be compared under identical marker-database perturbations, e.g. quantifying how often each method falsely assigns a removed (unknown) cell type.
skills.name: cross-method-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-annotation-comparison Use when several prior-knowledge cell-type annotation methods must be compared under identical marker-database perturbations, e.g. quantifying how often each method falsely assigns a removed (unknown) cell type. scCATCH must be excluded from this comparison because its implementation does not allow custom marker sets The task is not marker-perturbation sensitivity but general annotation accuracy on fully labeled reference data — supervised methods (CaSTLe, ACTINN) trained on annotated datasets are out of this skill's unsupervised scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark multiple marker-based scRNA-seq cell-type annotation methods (ScType, SCINA, scSorter) side-by-side by re-running each with identical perturbed marker databases on the same datasets and comparing their ability to leave a removed cell type undetected. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple marker-based scRNA-seq cell-type annotation methods (ScType, SCINA, scSorter) side-by-side by re-running each with identical perturbed marker databases on the same datasets and comparing their ability to leave a removed cell type undetected.
skills.when_to_use_negative: scCATCH must be excluded from this comparison because its implementation does not allow custom marker sets The task is not marker-perturbation sensitivity but general annotation accuracy on fully labeled reference data — supervised methods (CaSTLe, ACTINN) trained on annotated datasets are out of this skill's unsupervised scope

skills.description: Use when comparing novel cell detection or open-set cell-type classifiers on scRNA-seq benchmarks where novel-class cells are positives and imbalance makes AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 the appropriate metrics.
skills.name: cross-method-auroc-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-method-auroc-evaluation Use when comparing novel cell detection or open-set cell-type classifiers on scRNA-seq benchmarks where novel-class cells are positives and imbalance makes AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 the appropriate metrics. When the task is generic closed-set cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g., accuracy or macro-F1) rather than novel rare cell detection under class imbalance When only a single method is being run — the evaluation requires side-by-side comparison of scNovel and the four baselines on the same splits When datasets cannot be uniformly preprocessed (normalize_total to target_sum=1e4 + log1p), since metrics are only comparable across methods on identical splits http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark novel rare cell detection methods (scNovel vs scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred, scLearn) on scRNA-seq data by computing AUROC (primary), AUPR, and FPR95 per dataset and per number of novel classes (C^novel = 1–4), then averaging and significance-testing the results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Benchmark novel rare cell detection methods (scNovel vs scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred, scLearn) on scRNA-seq data by computing AUROC (primary), AUPR, and FPR95 per dataset and per number of novel classes (C^novel = 1–4), then averaging and significance-testing the results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is generic closed-set cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g., accuracy or macro-F1) rather than novel rare cell detection under class imbalance When only a single method is being run — the evaluation requires side-by-side comparison of scNovel and the four baselines on the same splits When datasets cannot be uniformly preprocessed (normalize_total to target_sum=1e4 + log1p), since metrics are only comparable across methods on identical splits

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset with a batch/condition covariate (e.g. control vs interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) has cell embeddings from GeneVector and you need to quantify batch alignment versus preservation of treatment-related transcriptional variation across correction methods.
skills.name: cross-method-batch-correction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-method-batch-correction-benchmarking Use when a scRNA-seq dataset with a batch/condition covariate (e.g. control vs interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) has cell embeddings from GeneVector and you need to quantify batch alignment versus preservation of treatment-related transcriptional variation across correction methods. Batches differ substantially in cell type composition — the paper notes batch correction is challenging/unreliable in this setting, and users must manually verify correction vectors against cell type signatures The goal is to remove the biological condition signal itself (e.g. stimulation status) rather than technical batch effects — here the point is to preserve interferon-stimulated variation Input is already a corrected/normalized feature table with no embedding space — vector arithmetic requires GeneVector gene/cell embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks GeneVector embedding-based batch correction against alternative methods (e.g. Harmony) by recomputing UMAPs on corrected and uncorrected cell representations and scoring per-cell-type batch silhouette coefficients, while checking that biological variation such as interferon-stimulated (ISG) programs in myeloid cells is preserved rather than removed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks GeneVector embedding-based batch correction against alternative methods (e.g. Harmony) by recomputing UMAPs on corrected and uncorrected cell representations and scoring per-cell-type batch silhouette coefficients, while checking that biological variation such as interferon-stimulated (ISG) programs in myeloid cells is preserved rather than removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Batches differ substantially in cell type composition — the paper notes batch correction is challenging/unreliable in this setting, and users must manually verify correction vectors against cell type signatures The goal is to remove the biological condition signal itself (e.g. stimulation status) rather than technical batch effects — here the point is to preserve interferon-stimulated variation Input is already a corrected/normalized feature table with no embedding space — vector arithmetic requires GeneVector gene/cell embeddings

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend the scCancer2 Fig. 2B benchmark: comparing cell-type annotation accuracy of scCancer2 against baseline methods across multiple datasets and sequencing technologies.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-accuracy-tabulation
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-accuracy-tabulation Use when you need to reproduce or extend the scCancer2 Fig. 2B benchmark: comparing cell-type annotation accuracy of scCancer2 against baseline methods across multiple datasets and sequencing technologies. The dataset lacks metadata level-1 reference labels, so prediction accuracy cannot be computed against a ground truth The goal is de novo subtype-level annotation of a new tumor microenvironment sample rather than cross-method accuracy benchmarking of the five major cell types The input data is spatial transcriptomics or bulk TCGA data rather than the six scRNA-seq benchmark datasets used in Fig. 2B http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the scCancer2 benchmark by running the scCancer2 annotation framework (predCellType + runCellSubtypeClassify) and eight baselines (scPred, OCLR, multinomial, Scibet, CHETAH, scmap, SingleCellNet, XGBoost) on six scRNA-seq datasets spanning five major cell types and three sequencing technologies, then tabulating prediction accuracy per method per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Reproduces the scCancer2 benchmark by running the scCancer2 annotation framework (predCellType + runCellSubtypeClassify) and eight baselines (scPred, OCLR, multinomial, Scibet, CHETAH, scmap, SingleCellNet, XGBoost) on six scRNA-seq datasets spanning five major cell types and three sequencing technologies, then tabulating prediction accuracy per method per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks metadata level-1 reference labels, so prediction accuracy cannot be computed against a ground truth The goal is de novo subtype-level annotation of a new tumor microenvironment sample rather than cross-method accuracy benchmarking of the five major cell types The input data is spatial transcriptomics or bulk TCGA data rather than the six scRNA-seq benchmark datasets used in Fig. 2B

skills.description: Use when a benchmark must compare pathway-activity/cell-type recovery performance of multiple gene set scoring methods across many simulated or real datasets into one ranked results table.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-aggregation
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-aggregation Use when a benchmark must compare pathway-activity/cell-type recovery performance of multiple gene set scoring methods across many simulated or real datasets into one ranked results table. Input is a spatial transcriptomics dataset where the goal is spatially relevant pathway identification (compute.spatial.kld) rather than cross-method cell-type recovery benchmarking Data are targeted-gene panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity is explicitly not suitable for such data, so a benchmark including it would be invalid The analysis goal is pathway scoring speed comparison rather than cell-type recovery accuracy (the article benchmarks speed separately among GSDensity, CelliD, AUCell, ssGSEA, and VAM) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Aggregates cell-type recovery AUC and cell typing accuracy across seven gene set scoring methods (GSDensity, ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) over 27 SERGIO-simulated and 8 real-world scRNA-seq datasets, producing a single ranked comparison table (benchmark_results.csv) that should reproduce GSDensity first, CelliD typically second. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Aggregates cell-type recovery AUC and cell typing accuracy across seven gene set scoring methods (GSDensity, ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) over 27 SERGIO-simulated and 8 real-world scRNA-seq datasets, producing a single ranked comparison table (benchmark_results.csv) that should reproduce GSDensity first, CelliD typically second.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a spatial transcriptomics dataset where the goal is spatially relevant pathway identification (compute.spatial.kld) rather than cross-method cell-type recovery benchmarking Data are targeted-gene panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity is explicitly not suitable for such data, so a benchmark including it would be invalid The analysis goal is pathway scoring speed comparison rather than cell-type recovery accuracy (the article benchmarks speed separately among GSDensity, CelliD, AUCell, ssGSEA, and VAM)

skills.description: Use when a new clonal-inference method must be evaluated head-to-head against predecessor methods on identical patient datasets, using a shared downstream metric such as cell-to-clone assignment coverage.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a new clonal-inference method must be evaluated head-to-head against predecessor methods on identical patient datasets, using a shared downstream metric such as cell-to-clone assignment coverage. Only one method is runnable — a cross-method comparison requires the same inputs processed by Canopy2, Canopy, and Cardelino The comparison target is a simulated-data accuracy metric rather than real-data unassigned-cell percentages; simulated validation of Canopy2 is a separate skill Input read counts have not passed the pre-processing QC pipeline, so competing methods would be evaluated on inconsistent SNV callsets http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmark a tumor phylogeny method (Canopy2) against competing tools (Canopy, Cardelino) on the same real-data patient inputs by computing a common cell-assignment metric — the percentage of malignant cells left unassigned to subclones — and compiling the results into a comparison table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Benchmark a tumor phylogeny method (Canopy2) against competing tools (Canopy, Cardelino) on the same real-data patient inputs by computing a common cell-assignment metric — the percentage of malignant cells left unassigned to subclones — and compiling the results into a comparison table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one method is runnable — a cross-method comparison requires the same inputs processed by Canopy2, Canopy, and Cardelino The comparison target is a simulated-data accuracy metric rather than real-data unassigned-cell percentages; simulated validation of Canopy2 is a separate skill Input read counts have not passed the pre-processing QC pipeline, so competing methods would be evaluated on inconsistent SNV callsets

skills.description: Use when a new temporal single-cell embedding method must be benchmarked head-to-head against established dimension-reduction tools on the same gene-by-cell count matrices, with a quantitative per-dataset comparison metric and a method-by-dataset results table.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a new temporal single-cell embedding method must be benchmarked head-to-head against established dimension-reduction tools on the same gene-by-cell count matrices, with a quantitative per-dataset comparison metric and a method-by-dataset results table. The datasets lack a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern — TCM explicitly requires a complete, biologically meaningful time index The goal is biological interpretation of cell clusters rather than method comparison — TCM does not provide immediate biological interpretation and further pathway analysis is needed Data are not temporal single-cell expression matrices (no gene-by-cell counts plus cell-by-time-point annotation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking procedure from the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) paper that compares a proposed dimension-reduction method against commonly used tools (t-SNE, diffusion map, diffusion pseudotime, Wishbone, Monocle, TSCAN) on identical temporal single-cell datasets, scoring each by the percent of variance explained by non-temporal factors or by cross-lineage cell separation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05112-9
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure from the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) paper that compares a proposed dimension-reduction method against commonly used tools (t-SNE, diffusion map, diffusion pseudotime, Wishbone, Monocle, TSCAN) on identical temporal single-cell datasets, scoring each by the percent of variance explained by non-temporal factors or by cross-lineage cell separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets lack a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern — TCM explicitly requires a complete, biologically meaningful time index The goal is biological interpretation of cell clusters rather than method comparison — TCM does not provide immediate biological interpretation and further pathway analysis is needed Data are not temporal single-cell expression matrices (no gene-by-cell counts plus cell-by-time-point annotation)

skills.description: Use when a newly proposed sequence-classification method must be validated against a published baseline on shared benchmark splits, and per-tissue metric deltas (e.g., AUC) must be tabulated with significance markers.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a newly proposed sequence-classification method must be validated against a published baseline on shared benchmark splits, and per-tissue metric deltas (e.g., AUC) must be tabulated with significance markers. The input is raw sequencing data needing m6A-site calling rather than benchmark comparison of trained classifiers No shared benchmark datasets or identical splits exist between the new method and the baseline, making AUC deltas incomparable The task targets m6A prediction in species or tissues outside human/mouse/rat brain, liver, kidney, heart, testis coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 A head-to-head benchmarking skill that evaluates a new predictor (im6A-TS-CNN) against an established baseline (iRNA-m6A, SVM-based) on identical tissue-specific m6A datasets, computing per-tissue AUC deltas under both 5-fold cross-validation and independent testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: A head-to-head benchmarking skill that evaluates a new predictor (im6A-TS-CNN) against an established baseline (iRNA-m6A, SVM-based) on identical tissue-specific m6A datasets, computing per-tissue AUC deltas under both 5-fold cross-validation and independent testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing data needing m6A-site calling rather than benchmark comparison of trained classifiers No shared benchmark datasets or identical splits exist between the new method and the baseline, making AUC deltas incomparable The task targets m6A prediction in species or tissues outside human/mouse/rat brain, liver, kidney, heart, testis coverage

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq annotation-transfer method must be compared head-to-head against alternatives on shared reference/query data, using balanced accuracy for cell typing or JSD for continuous-label transfer.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a scRNA-seq annotation-transfer method must be compared head-to-head against alternatives on shared reference/query data, using balanced accuracy for cell typing or JSD for continuous-label transfer. The task is a single-method application with no competing method to compare — run the method directly instead of building a benchmark harness Reference datasets have fewer than ~1000 cells, where the Cell BLAST model itself is under-trained and any benchmark result would reflect under-training rather than method differences http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark Cell BLAST's query-based cell-type transfer against competing methods (scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchor-based mapping, scANVI) on identical reference/query splits, scoring discrete typing by mean balanced accuracy and continuous fate transfer by Jensen–Shannon divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmark Cell BLAST's query-based cell-type transfer against competing methods (scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchor-based mapping, scANVI) on identical reference/query splits, scoring discrete typing by mean balanced accuracy and continuous fate transfer by Jensen–Shannon divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a single-method application with no competing method to compare — run the method directly instead of building a benchmark harness Reference datasets have fewer than ~1000 cells, where the Cell BLAST model itself is under-trained and any benchmark result would reflect under-training rather than method differences

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more count-estimation or preprocessing variants (e.g. unique vs weighted multi-read allocation, with vs without partial pooling) by feeding each through an identical downstream statistical test and reporting matched result counts.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing two or more count-estimation or preprocessing variants (e.g. unique vs weighted multi-read allocation, with vs without partial pooling) by feeding each through an identical downstream statistical test and reporting matched result counts. You only have a single count-estimation method with no alternative variant to compare — there is no benchmark contrast to tabulate The downstream question is differential bursting kinetics between two samples rather than a method-comparison benchmark (use a dedicated differential test instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark multiple allelic count-estimation methods (unique-reads, EMASE weighted allocation, with/without scBASE partial pooling) by running the same downstream test on each and tabulating method-by-method result counts, as done in Choi et al. 2019 where the SCALE bursting model was fit to four scBASE count matrices and independence test outcomes were compared. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple allelic count-estimation methods (unique-reads, EMASE weighted allocation, with/without scBASE partial pooling) by running the same downstream test on each and tabulating method-by-method result counts, as done in Choi et al. 2019 where the SCALE bursting model was fit to four scBASE count matrices and independence test outcomes were compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single count-estimation method with no alternative variant to compare — there is no benchmark contrast to tabulate The downstream question is differential bursting kinetics between two samples rather than a method-comparison benchmark (use a dedicated differential test instead)

skills.description: Use when per-cell stemness/pluripotency score tables (ORIGINS activity, activity-HVF, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) already exist for multiple datasets and the goal is to quantify agreement between scoring methods via mean Pearson correlations.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison-of-pluripotency-tools
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-comparison-of-pluripotency-tools Use when per-cell stemness/pluripotency score tables (ORIGINS activity, activity-HVF, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) already exist for multiple datasets and the goal is to quantify agreement between scoring methods via mean Pearson correlations. When the per-cell pluripotency scores have not yet been computed — this skill correlates existing score tables; score computation itself is done via ORIGINS' activity() function on the expression matrix and differentiation_edges PPIN. When raw count matrices (genes x cells) are the only input and the goal is trajectory inference rather than cross-method agreement — use the ORIGINS workflow to identify stem/progenitor origins instead. When datasets or tool combinations differ from the ORIGINS/LandSCENT/CytoTRACE benchmark, the specific benchmark averages (0.77, 0.44, 0.63, 0.67) are not valid validation targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A reproducible R benchmarking procedure that computes pairwise Pearson correlations between per-cell pluripotency scores from ORIGINS (activity), LandSCENT (SR), and CytoTRACE across four healthy human scRNA-seq datasets (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383) and averages them per score pair to compare methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: A reproducible R benchmarking procedure that computes pairwise Pearson correlations between per-cell pluripotency scores from ORIGINS (activity), LandSCENT (SR), and CytoTRACE across four healthy human scRNA-seq datasets (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383) and averages them per score pair to compare methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the per-cell pluripotency scores have not yet been computed — this skill correlates existing score tables; score computation itself is done via ORIGINS' activity() function on the expression matrix and differentiation_edges PPIN. When raw count matrices (genes x cells) are the only input and the goal is trajectory inference rather than cross-method agreement — use the ORIGINS workflow to identify stem/progenitor origins instead. When datasets or tool combinations differ from the ORIGINS/LandSCENT/CytoTRACE benchmark, the specific benchmark averages (0.77, 0.44, 0.63, 0.67) are not valid validation targets.

skills.description: Use when comparing a new cell-type annotation tool against ready-to-run baselines on a shared single-cell test set, especially when tools use different reference sets and label vocabularies that must be reconciled via an ontology.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing a new cell-type annotation tool against ready-to-run baselines on a shared single-cell test set, especially when tools use different reference sets and label vocabularies that must be reconciled via an ontology. When the goal is to evaluate a single method's absolute accuracy rather than a controlled head-to-head comparison across methods with heterogeneous reference sets When the input data are droplet-based single-cell test sets, which fall outside the non-droplet benchmark scope of this comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A fair-comparison benchmarking procedure for cell type annotation methods: classify the same test set with multiple prepackaged tools (CellO, scMatch, SingleR), project flat labels onto the Cell Ontology, and score each method only over cell types present in its own training set using per-cell-type F1-score and precision. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101913
skills.summary: A fair-comparison benchmarking procedure for cell type annotation methods: classify the same test set with multiple prepackaged tools (CellO, scMatch, SingleR), project flat labels onto the Cell Ontology, and score each method only over cell types present in its own training set using per-cell-type F1-score and precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to evaluate a single method's absolute accuracy rather than a controlled head-to-head comparison across methods with heterogeneous reference sets When the input data are droplet-based single-cell test sets, which fall outside the non-droplet benchmark scope of this comparison

skills.description: Use when multiple GSE or DE methods (e.g., iDEA, fGSEA, GSEA, CAMERA, PAGE) are run on identical DE summary statistics and you need quantitative concordance metrics such as Jaccard overlap to compare their outputs.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-jaccard-overlap
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-jaccard-overlap Use when multiple GSE or DE methods (e.g., iDEA, fGSEA, GSEA, CAMERA, PAGE) are run on identical DE summary statistics and you need quantitative concordance metrics such as Jaccard overlap to compare their outputs. When only one method is applied and there is no second method's gene list to compute a Jaccard overlap against When methods are run on different DE summary statistics or gene universe — the comparison requires all methods to consume identical inputs (same beta/z-score statistics and same gene sets) When the goal is absolute FDR calibration rather than cross-method power/concordance comparison (use permutation-based null calibration via iDEA.fit.null and iDEA.FDR instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking procedure for comparing gene set enrichment and differential expression methods on the same scRNA-seq summary statistics, quantifying agreement via the Jaccard index between method-specific gene lists and recording per-method counts (e.g., enriched gene sets at FDR 5%, genomic-control lambda_gc) in a single results table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure for comparing gene set enrichment and differential expression methods on the same scRNA-seq summary statistics, quantifying agreement via the Jaccard index between method-specific gene lists and recording per-method counts (e.g., enriched gene sets at FDR 5%, genomic-control lambda_gc) in a single results table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one method is applied and there is no second method's gene list to compute a Jaccard overlap against When methods are run on different DE summary statistics or gene universe — the comparison requires all methods to consume identical inputs (same beta/z-score statistics and same gene sets) When the goal is absolute FDR calibration rather than cross-method power/concordance comparison (use permutation-based null calibration via iDEA.fit.null and iDEA.FDR instead)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking several single-cell integration methods on the same dataset collections and you need a reproducible global ranking from batch-mixing and bio-conservation metrics computed on each method's latent embedding.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-ranking-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-ranking-analysis Use when benchmarking several single-cell integration methods on the same dataset collections and you need a reproducible global ranking from batch-mixing and bio-conservation metrics computed on each method's latent embedding. Cell type annotations are unavailable for the datasets, since CiLISI and cell type-aware metrics require cell type labels and cannot be computed for cell types present in only one dataset Datasets have highly unequal numbers of cells, where CiLISI (like LISI) is suboptimal and batch mixing metrics robust to lopsided cell proportions are still lacking Integrating technical replicates where cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics would suffice, making a full semi-supervised benchmark unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks multiple scRNA-seq integration tools on cell type-aware batch mixing (CiLISI) and biological variance preservation (cell type ASW) across multiple dataset collections, using a 50-dimensional latent space per method and a global rank aggregation to identify the best-performing method (here, semi-supervised STACAS). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Ranks multiple scRNA-seq integration tools on cell type-aware batch mixing (CiLISI) and biological variance preservation (cell type ASW) across multiple dataset collections, using a 50-dimensional latent space per method and a global rank aggregation to identify the best-performing method (here, semi-supervised STACAS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type annotations are unavailable for the datasets, since CiLISI and cell type-aware metrics require cell type labels and cannot be computed for cell types present in only one dataset Datasets have highly unequal numbers of cells, where CiLISI (like LISI) is suboptimal and batch mixing metrics robust to lopsided cell proportions are still lacking Integrating technical replicates where cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics would suffice, making a full semi-supervised benchmark unnecessary

skills.description: Use when a claim that 'method A outperforms methods B and C' must be reproduced end-to-end: re-running all quantifiers on the same mapped reads, rebuilding feature matrices under multiple perspectives, and statistically testing the performance gap.
skills.name: cross-method-benchmark-reproduction
skills.search_text: cross-method-benchmark-reproduction Use when a claim that 'method A outperforms methods B and C' must be reproduced end-to-end: re-running all quantifiers on the same mapped reads, rebuilding feature matrices under multiple perspectives, and statistically testing the performance gap. skills.description: Use when evaluating a GRN inference method on time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data against competitors (e.g., SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) using early-precision curves.
skills.name: cross-method-grn-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-method-grn-comparison-analysis Use when evaluating a GRN inference method on time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data against competitors (e.g., SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) using early-precision curves. The dataset is a true longitudinal time series from the same cells rather than time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) data, so pseudo-time-free comparison framing is unnecessary. skills.search_text: cross-method-trajectory-comparison Use when a single-cell pseudotime/branching result from one method (e.g., DTFLOW RSKG) needs to be validated or contextualized against branch assignments from alternative tools such as Scanpy or Monocle2. skills.summary: Reproduces and cross-validates multi-branch trajectory detection by comparing DTFLOW's RSKG branch assignments against branches from Scanpy and Monocle2 on the same single-cell dataset (e.g., the MMP MARS-seq myeloid progenitor data with 2730 cells and 3451 informative genes), exposing method-specific artifacts such as developmentally unreasonable root-cell placement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has only a single developmental path with no branching events, so cross-method branch comparison has no informative signal No trusted reference branching structure or independent method output exists, making agreement checks unfalsifiable Input is raw sequencing data rather than a pre-processed gene expression matrix with pseudotime and branch labels available

skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with simple, well-behaved kinetics where scVelo's default dynamical mode already suffices — the independent mode targets complex, multi-branch or cell-cycle scenarios Analyses requiring a quantitative benchmark with ground-truth cluster edges only — this skill's validation is a qualitative check against published trajectory figures; use utv.evaluate with cluster_edges instead when ground truth is available Datasets lacking spliced/unspliced layer information, since the workflow is built on the spliced/unspliced count matrices

skills.description: Use when a simulated dataset with known pseudotime and branching structure is available and you need to quantify which TI method assigns cells to branches most purely and reconstructs pseudotime most accurately.
skills.name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-method-trajectory-comparison Use when a simulated dataset with known pseudotime and branching structure is available and you need to quantify which TI method assigns cells to branches most purely and reconstructs pseudotime most accurately. The dataset lacks simulated ground-truth pseudotime or branching labels, so neither Kendall correlation nor assignment purity can be computed. The biological system is a single unbranched trajectory, making branch-purity entropy and branching-aware comparison moot. No RNA velocity can be estimated (e.g., no spliced/unspliced counts), since CellPath and VeTra depend on velocity input and the comparison would be confounded. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark trajectory inference methods (CellPath, VeTra, Slingshot) on a simulated branching dataset by comparing per-path Kendall correlations against ground-truth pseudotime and the normalized average entropy score of cell-to-trajectory assignments after the branching point. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Benchmark trajectory inference methods (CellPath, VeTra, Slingshot) on a simulated branching dataset by comparing per-path Kendall correlations against ground-truth pseudotime and the normalized average entropy score of cell-to-trajectory assignments after the branching point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks simulated ground-truth pseudotime or branching labels, so neither Kendall correlation nor assignment purity can be computed. The biological system is a single unbranched trajectory, making branch-purity entropy and branching-aware comparison moot. No RNA velocity can be estimated (e.g., no spliced/unspliced counts), since CellPath and VeTra depend on velocity input and the comparison would be confounded.

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend head-to-head evaluation of lncRNA coding-potential classifiers on sORF-enriched test sets, computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC per species.

skills.search_text: cross-method-transcript-classifier-comparison Use when you need to reproduce or extend head-to-head evaluation of lncRNA coding-potential classifiers on sORF-enriched test sets, computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC per species. The goal is training a new model rather than comparing existing classifiers on held-out test data (use the LncCat training pipeline with CD-HIT 80% redundancy reduction and 70/10/20 split instead) Input transcripts are generic long-ORF benchmark sets from species like wheat or chicken rather than the sORF test sets — different reported MCC ranges (e.g. wheat MCC 0.8672) apply Only one method is being assessed with no competitor baseline, since the skill's core is the eight-method head-to-head comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark LncCat (CatBoost with codon-related, GC-related, sequence-related, peptide-related, and ORF-attention features, cutoff 0.5) against eight lncRNA identification methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) on independent small-ORF (sORF) test datasets from human, mouse, and zebrafish. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Benchmark LncCat (CatBoost with codon-related, GC-related, sequence-related, peptide-related, and ORF-attention features, cutoff 0.5) against eight lncRNA identification methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) on independent small-ORF (sORF) test datasets from human, mouse, and zebrafish.

skills.description: Use when two TWAS frameworks have been run on identical reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=574) and GWAS data and you must count independently significant genes per method and their overlap.

skills.search_text: cross-method-twas-result-comparison Use when two TWAS frameworks have been run on identical reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=574) and GWAS data and you must count independently significant genes per method and their overlap. skills.description: Use when benchmarking two or more RNA velocity methods on the same dataset and you need comparable per-gene metrics (e.g., phase-portrait fitting quality, directional coherence) restricted to commonly modeled genes.
skills.name: cross-method-velocity-metric-computation
skills.search_text: cross-method-velocity-metric-computation Use when benchmarking two or more RNA velocity methods on the same dataset and you need comparable per-gene metrics (e.g., phase-portrait fitting quality, directional coherence) restricted to commonly modeled genes. Only a single velocity method is applied and no cross-method comparison is intended — the metrics are defined relative to multiple methods on commonly modeled genes The dataset contains splicing information that scVelo-style dynamics modeling can fully exploit and no benchmarking against regulation-based fitting is needed Genes modeled by only a subset of methods must be included — restricting to commonly modeled genes is what makes the comparison valid, so partial-coverage genes should be excluded rather than forced in http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes quantitative RNA-velocity evaluation metrics — intra-class distance, inter-class distance, fitting error, CBDir, ICCoh, and velocity consistency — on the genes commonly modeled by all compared methods, to benchmark TFvelo against un/spliced-based baselines (scVelo, Dynamo, UniTVelo, cellDancer) as in Fig. 2d-g and Fig. S5. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Computes quantitative RNA-velocity evaluation metrics — intra-class distance, inter-class distance, fitting error, CBDir, ICCoh, and velocity consistency — on the genes commonly modeled by all compared methods, to benchmark TFvelo against un/spliced-based baselines (scVelo, Dynamo, UniTVelo, cellDancer) as in Fig. 2d-g and Fig. S5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single velocity method is applied and no cross-method comparison is intended — the metrics are defined relative to multiple methods on commonly modeled genes The dataset contains splicing information that scVelo-style dynamics modeling can fully exploit and no benchmarking against regulation-based fitting is needed Genes modeled by only a subset of methods must be included — restricting to commonly modeled genes is what makes the comparison valid, so partial-coverage genes should be excluded rather than forced in

skills.description: Use when you must decide which similarity metric (posterior distance vs. Euclidean) better distinguishes same-type nearest neighbors between query and reference scRNA-seq cells within a fixed embedding space.
skills.name: cross-metric-benchmark-comparison-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: cross-metric-benchmark-comparison-scrna-seq Use when you must decide which similarity metric (posterior distance vs. Euclidean) better distinguishes same-type nearest neighbors between query and reference scRNA-seq cells within a fixed embedding space. The analysis goal is annotating query cells (ontology term transfer) rather than comparing similarity metrics — use Cell BLAST's BLAST2CO curation workflow instead Reference datasets contain fewer than ~1000 cells, since Cell BLAST's neural network model is over-parameterized and under-training would confound the metric comparison You only have a single embedding without a posterior/variational model — NPD requires posterior distributions, so only the Euclidean arm of the comparison is computable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark two cell-to-cell similarity metrics (posterior-based normalized projection distance vs. Euclidean distance) within the same low-dimensional embedding by ROC/AUC analysis of nearest-neighbor cell-type querying, as done in Cell BLAST's Supplementary Figs. 6g-h and 8c. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmark two cell-to-cell similarity metrics (posterior-based normalized projection distance vs. Euclidean distance) within the same low-dimensional embedding by ROC/AUC analysis of nearest-neighbor cell-type querying, as done in Cell BLAST's Supplementary Figs. 6g-h and 8c.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is annotating query cells (ontology term transfer) rather than comparing similarity metrics — use Cell BLAST's BLAST2CO curation workflow instead Reference datasets contain fewer than ~1000 cells, since Cell BLAST's neural network model is over-parameterized and under-training would confound the metric comparison You only have a single embedding without a posterior/variational model — NPD requires posterior distributions, so only the Euclidean arm of the comparison is computable

skills.description: Use when you have per-droplet DIEM debris scores from an snRNA-seq run and a per-droplet contamination proxy (e.g., percent spliced reads) and need to verify the debris score tracks extranuclear RNA contamination.
skills.name: cross-metric-droplet-alignment
skills.search_text: cross-metric-droplet-alignment Use when you have per-droplet DIEM debris scores from an snRNA-seq run and a per-droplet contamination proxy (e.g., percent spliced reads) and need to verify the debris score tracks extranuclear RNA contamination. Data are single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., PBMC scRNA-seq), where the correlation between debris score and spliced-read percent was reported as less successful due to smaller differences between background and cell type profiles Combining debris scores across independent samples for a single pooled correlation, since debris scores cannot be assumed to be on the same scale across experiments The background distribution has few or no genes increased relative to cell types, making the debris score unreliable as the correlation input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aligns per-droplet DIEM debris scores with an independent contamination metric (percent of spliced reads) on shared droplet barcodes and computes their Pearson correlation in R, validating that DIEM's debris score quantifies extranuclear RNA contamination. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Aligns per-droplet DIEM debris scores with an independent contamination metric (percent of spliced reads) on shared droplet barcodes and computes their Pearson correlation in R, validating that DIEM's debris score quantifies extranuclear RNA contamination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., PBMC scRNA-seq), where the correlation between debris score and spliced-read percent was reported as less successful due to smaller differences between background and cell type profiles Combining debris scores across independent samples for a single pooled correlation, since debris scores cannot be assumed to be on the same scale across experiments The background distribution has few or no genes increased relative to cell types, making the debris score unreliable as the correlation input

skills.description: Use when a trained scMM model's latent dimensions need interpretation: sweep each latent dimension independently through the mixture-of-experts decoder to link genes, surface proteins, and chromatin accessibility peaks to individual dimensions.
skills.name: cross-modal-decoder-generation
skills.search_text: cross-modal-decoder-generation Use when a trained scMM model's latent dimensions need interpretation: sweep each latent dimension independently through the mixture-of-experts decoder to link genes, surface proteins, and chromatin accessibility peaks to individual dimensions. The goal is cross-modal prediction between modalities from real cells (e.g. imputing protein from RNA) rather than interpreting what each latent dimension encodes — use scMM's crossmodal generation mode instead No trained scMM decoder is available (e.g. only raw count matrices without a fitted model) — the traversal requires the trained generative model The model is the generic MMVAE on non-single-cell modalities (e.g. MNIST-SVHN, CUB image-caption); this skill's feature extraction and motif enrichment steps are specific to single-cell multiomics data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Generate pseudocells by independently traversing each latent dimension of a trained scMM mixture-of-experts model and decoding each swept value with the multimodal decoder, compensating for the limited interpretability of deep generative latent spaces by associating multimodal features and regulatory programs with individual dimensions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Generate pseudocells by independently traversing each latent dimension of a trained scMM mixture-of-experts model and decoding each swept value with the multimodal decoder, compensating for the limited interpretability of deep generative latent spaces by associating multimodal features and regulatory programs with individual dimensions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cross-modal prediction between modalities from real cells (e.g. imputing protein from RNA) rather than interpreting what each latent dimension encodes — use scMM's crossmodal generation mode instead No trained scMM decoder is available (e.g. only raw count matrices without a fitted model) — the traversal requires the trained generative model The model is the generic MMVAE on non-single-cell modalities (e.g. MNIST-SVHN, CUB image-caption); this skill's feature extraction and motif enrichment steps are specific to single-cell multiomics data

skills.description: Use when two separately measured single-cell modalities of related cells must be aligned or a missing modality predicted — e.g., spatial transcriptomics to scRNA-seq or paired ATAC-seq/RNA-seq — while preserving data geometry.
skills.name: cross-modal-gan-domain-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-modal-gan-domain-mapping Use when two separately measured single-cell modalities of related cells must be aligned or a missing modality predicted — e.g., spatial transcriptomics to scRNA-seq or paired ATAC-seq/RNA-seq — while preserving data geometry. Aligning more than two modalities at once — the number of generators grows quadratically, forcing small or separately trained networks When no meaningful distance metric between data points can be chosen — the geometry-based loss is not completely 'plug-and-play' When only a feature table without underlying data geometry is available, since the method depends on diffusion-geometry correspondence http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train scMMGAN, a multi-modal GAN with a geometry-preserving correspondence loss, to map single-cell measurements (e.g., spatial transcriptomics, scATAC-seq) into a target single-cell modality (e.g., scRNA-seq), generating point-wise aligned synthetic profiles for downstream analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Train scMMGAN, a multi-modal GAN with a geometry-preserving correspondence loss, to map single-cell measurements (e.g., spatial transcriptomics, scATAC-seq) into a target single-cell modality (e.g., scRNA-seq), generating point-wise aligned synthetic profiles for downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Aligning more than two modalities at once — the number of generators grows quadratically, forcing small or separately trained networks When no meaningful distance metric between data points can be chosen — the geometry-based loss is not completely 'plug-and-play' When only a feature table without underlying data geometry is available, since the method depends on diffusion-geometry correspondence

skills.description: Use when a target gene's correlated-gene ranking from original spatial data must be compared against the same ranking computed on a GAN-mapped scRNA-seq output to flag spurious vs. newly discovered candidate associations.
skills.name: cross-modal-gene-list-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-modal-gene-list-comparison Use when a target gene's correlated-gene ranking from original spatial data must be compared against the same ranking computed on a GAN-mapped scRNA-seq output to flag spurious vs. newly discovered candidate associations. The two modalities have not been aligned by a cross-domain mapping (e.g., no scMMGAN `output_fake2` exists), since rankings would come from unrelated feature spaces The datasets have not been preprocessed identically (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50 principal components), making correlation ranks incomparable The goal is differential expression or clustering rather than distinguishing spurious from cross-modal novel gene correlations http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares ranked gene-correlation lists computed independently in two data domains — original spatial transcriptomics and scMMGAN-generated scRNA-seq mapped into the spatial domain — to separate spurious correlations (artifacts of spatial measurement) from novel associations revealed by the cross-modal mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Compares ranked gene-correlation lists computed independently in two data domains — original spatial transcriptomics and scMMGAN-generated scRNA-seq mapped into the spatial domain — to separate spurious correlations (artifacts of spatial measurement) from novel associations revealed by the cross-modal mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two modalities have not been aligned by a cross-domain mapping (e.g., no scMMGAN `output_fake2` exists), since rankings would come from unrelated feature spaces The datasets have not been preprocessed identically (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50 principal components), making correlation ranks incomparable The goal is differential expression or clustering rather than distinguishing spurious from cross-modal novel gene correlations

skills.description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq transcriptome and surface protein counts (RNA_count.mtx/gene.tsv and Protein_count.mtx/protein.tsv with barcode.tsv) and need to predict protein measurements for cells whose protein data is withheld, given transcriptome observations alone.
skills.name: cross-modal-protein-generation-from-transcriptome
skills.search_text: cross-modal-protein-generation-from-transcriptome Use when you have paired CITE-seq transcriptome and surface protein counts (RNA_count.mtx/gene.tsv and Protein_count.mtx/protein.tsv with barcode.tsv) and need to predict protein measurements for cells whose protein data is withheld, given transcriptome observations alone. Data is not paired CITE-seq transcriptome-plus-protein counts (e.g. chromatin accessibility data, which scMM handles under ATAC-seq with peak.tsv, requiring a different crossmodal setup) You need joint latent representations or clustering/interpretability (pseudocell-based multimodal regulatory programs) rather than one-directional protein prediction from transcriptome Only unpaired single-cell transcriptome and protein measurements exist, since the model requires end-to-end training on raw counts of both modalities from the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Predicts CITE-seq surface protein abundances from transcriptome-only observations using scMM's mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder, extracting negative binomial mean parameters as point estimates and validating them by correlation against held-out protein counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Predicts CITE-seq surface protein abundances from transcriptome-only observations using scMM's mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder, extracting negative binomial mean parameters as point estimates and validating them by correlation against held-out protein counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not paired CITE-seq transcriptome-plus-protein counts (e.g. chromatin accessibility data, which scMM handles under ATAC-seq with peak.tsv, requiring a different crossmodal setup) You need joint latent representations or clustering/interpretability (pseudocell-based multimodal regulatory programs) rather than one-directional protein prediction from transcriptome Only unpaired single-cell transcriptome and protein measurements exist, since the model requires end-to-end training on raw counts of both modalities from the same cells

skills.description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/ADT data are available and you must quantify whether a prediction (or RNA signal itself) tracks measured protein levels cell-by-cell — e.g. comparing imputation methods or raw/denoised RNA baselines per protein.
skills.name: cross-modal-rna-protein-correlation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-modal-rna-protein-correlation-benchmarking Use when paired scRNA-seq/ADT data are available and you must quantify whether a prediction (or RNA signal itself) tracks measured protein levels cell-by-cell — e.g. comparing imputation methods or raw/denoised RNA baselines per protein. skills.summary: Benchmarks imputed or RNA-derived estimates of surface protein abundance against measured CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT counts by computing per-protein cross-cell Pearson correlations on held-out cells. It was used to show cTP-net imputation beats raw and SAVER-X-denoised RNA baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input expression data are not UMI-based counts — the article notes cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) input and that accuracy for TPM/RPKM CITE-seq data is untested You want absolute protein quantification — the benchmark evaluates relative surface protein abundances via cross-cell correlation, not absolute concentrations The held-out cells are from cell types unrelated to the training data — generalization was only tested for cell types absent from but related to those in the training data, and not outside the hematopoietic lineage

skills.description: Use when you need to check that structurally-derived relationships (ontology graph distances) are recapitulated by an independent data modality (gene expression or text embeddings) before trusting the structure for downstream inference.
skills.name: cross-modal-similarity-validation
skills.search_text: cross-modal-similarity-validation Use when you need to check that structurally-derived relationships (ontology graph distances) are recapitulated by an independent data modality (gene expression or text embeddings) before trusting the structure for downstream inference. The Cell Ontology was not developed specifically for scRNA-seq and likely misses cell types and cell states, so do not treat expression-vs-ontology correlation as a completeness check of the ontology itself OnClass-style ontology structure cannot distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents), so similarity based purely on graph position will saturate for such siblings regardless of expression data Avoid mixing tissues into a single expression similarity matrix — correlations are computed separately per tissue (lung vs pancreas) because tissue context changes expression profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Quantitatively validates whether two independent representations of the same entities (e.g., Cell Ontology graph structure, NLP text embeddings of cell type definitions, and scRNA-seq expression profiles) agree, by computing per-modality similarity matrices and correlating them with Pearson correlation. As demonstrated in the OnClass paper, this tests the guilt-by-association principle underlying ontology-based cell type classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Quantitatively validates whether two independent representations of the same entities (e.g., Cell Ontology graph structure, NLP text embeddings of cell type definitions, and scRNA-seq expression profiles) agree, by computing per-modality similarity matrices and correlating them with Pearson correlation. As demonstrated in the OnClass paper, this tests the guilt-by-association principle underlying ontology-based cell type classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Cell Ontology was not developed specifically for scRNA-seq and likely misses cell types and cell states, so do not treat expression-vs-ontology correlation as a completeness check of the ontology itself OnClass-style ontology structure cannot distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents), so similarity based purely on graph position will saturate for such siblings regardless of expression data Avoid mixing tissues into a single expression similarity matrix — correlations are computed separately per tissue (lung vs pancreas) because tissue context changes expression profiles

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how robust a cross-modality alignment (e.g. scATAC-to-scRNA via scTopoGAN) is to cell-number imbalance, by generating downsamples from 90% to 10% of cells and measuring alignment quality per fraction.
skills.name: cross-modality-alignment-robustness-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-modality-alignment-robustness-analysis Use when you need to quantify how robust a cross-modality alignment (e.g. scATAC-to-scRNA via scTopoGAN) is to cell-number imbalance, by generating downsamples from 90% to 10% of cells and measuring alignment quality per fraction. When the goal is to benchmark scTopoGAN's baseline alignment against other methods (UnionCom, MMD-MA) on full datasets rather than test downsampling robustness — use the UnionCom.py / manifold_align_mmd_pytorch.py scripts instead. When both modalities have comparable cell counts and no modality-imbalance scenario needs to be evaluated — the robustness curves add no information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Stress-tests an unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment method (scTopoGAN) by downsampling one modality (scATAC-seq) relative to a fixed target modality (scRNA-seq), in stratified and cell-type-specific regimes, and tracking the Celltype matching score as cells are removed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Stress-tests an unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment method (scTopoGAN) by downsampling one modality (scATAC-seq) relative to a fixed target modality (scRNA-seq), in stratified and cell-type-specific regimes, and tracking the Celltype matching score as cells are removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to benchmark scTopoGAN's baseline alignment against other methods (UnionCom, MMD-MA) on full datasets rather than test downsampling robustness — use the UnionCom.py / manifold_align_mmd_pytorch.py scripts instead. When both modalities have comparable cell counts and no modality-imbalance scenario needs to be evaluated — the robustness curves add no information.

skills.description: Use when each single-cell modality (e.g., PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) must be projected to a low-dimensional latent by multiple methods and compared in one table of KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 and Silhouette metrics.
skills.name: cross-modality-benchmark-table-generation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-benchmark-table-generation Use when each single-cell modality (e.g., PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) must be projected to a low-dimensional latent by multiple methods and compared in one table of KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 and Silhouette metrics. Input is raw, unprocessed single-cell data — the benchmark script requires pre-processed data already reduced to 50 components (PCA for RNA, LSI for ATAC) as provided in the Data folder The goal is cross-modality alignment into a common space rather than per-modality projection benchmarking — use run_scTopoGAN instead of the TopoAE_benchmark.py evaluation Only one projection method is of interest and no method comparison table is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates a benchmark table comparing manifold projection methods (topoAE, regular Autoencoder, Variational Autoencoder, UMAP) on single-cell modalities projected to 8-dimensional latents, scoring density preservation with KL divergence at regularization weights 0.01/0.1/1 and cell-class separation with Silhouette scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Generates a benchmark table comparing manifold projection methods (topoAE, regular Autoencoder, Variational Autoencoder, UMAP) on single-cell modalities projected to 8-dimensional latents, scoring density preservation with KL divergence at regularization weights 0.01/0.1/1 and cell-class separation with Silhouette scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unprocessed single-cell data — the benchmark script requires pre-processed data already reduced to 50 components (PCA for RNA, LSI for ATAC) as provided in the Data folder The goal is cross-modality alignment into a common space rather than per-modality projection benchmarking — use run_scTopoGAN instead of the TopoAE_benchmark.py evaluation Only one projection method is of interest and no method comparison table is required

The two modalities already share an identical gene feature space and no feature reconciliation is needed The input is peak-by-cell scATAC-seq data that has not yet been converted to a gene activity matrix (conversion via tools such as Signac must happen first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Intersects the gene features of a scATAC-seq gene activity matrix (h5ad) with the gene features of the scRNA-seq count matrix so that only shared genes are retained, a prerequisite before scBridge ingests both modalities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
