skills.description: Use when two modalities are jointly measured (e.g. DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) and you must score whether a learned cross-domain mapping preserves point-wise correspondence, not just distributional similarity.
skills.name: cross-modality-correlation-metric-computation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-correlation-metric-computation Use when two modalities are jointly measured (e.g. DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) and you must score whether a learned cross-domain mapping preserves point-wise correspondence, not just distributional similarity. The modalities are not jointly measured, so no columns are known to correspond and the correlation metric cannot be meaningfully interpreted. The goal is only distribution-level comparison; CycleGAN/CMAE-style baselines with distribution-level losses alone already answer the question and no correspondence evaluation is needed. The input matrices have not been preprocessed (no MAGIC dropout correction, no zero-centering/unit scaling, not reduced to 50 PCs), violating the [-10, 10] column-range requirement for feeding the network. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes MMD and column-wise correlation between a trained model's cross-domain mappings (e.g. scMMGAN's G(x1) into the proteomic space) and the jointly measured target modality, to quantify how well point-wise correspondence is preserved on jointly measured DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics/proteomics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Computes MMD and column-wise correlation between a trained model's cross-domain mappings (e.g. scMMGAN's G(x1) into the proteomic space) and the jointly measured target modality, to quantify how well point-wise correspondence is preserved on jointly measured DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics/proteomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modalities are not jointly measured, so no columns are known to correspond and the correlation metric cannot be meaningfully interpreted. The goal is only distribution-level comparison; CycleGAN/CMAE-style baselines with distribution-level losses alone already answer the question and no correspondence evaluation is needed. The input matrices have not been preprocessed (no MAGIC dropout correction, no zero-centering/unit scaling, not reduced to 50 PCs), violating the [-10, 10] column-range requirement for feeding the network.

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or surface protein counts) that share only a weak, partial set of features, and a cell-level coupling cost is needed for Optimal Transport-based alignment.
skills.name: cross-modality-cost-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: cross-modality-cost-matrix-construction Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or surface protein counts) that share only a weak, partial set of features, and a cell-level coupling cost is needed for Optimal Transport-based alignment. Modalities share no feature connections at all (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence's alignment relies on cross-modality feature links Data are paired single-cell multiomic profiles of the same cells — paired integration does not require an OT coupling cost inferred from weak feature connections http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs the cell-to-cell coupling cost between modalities from weakly connected features (e.g. genes shared between scRNA and scATAC peaks or surface proteins) using Pearson similarity, so scConfluence's unbalanced Optimal Transport aligns embeddings without converting all modalities to a common feature space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Constructs the cell-to-cell coupling cost between modalities from weakly connected features (e.g. genes shared between scRNA and scATAC peaks or surface proteins) using Pearson similarity, so scConfluence's unbalanced Optimal Transport aligns embeddings without converting all modalities to a common feature space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities share no feature connections at all (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence's alignment relies on cross-modality feature links Data are paired single-cell multiomic profiles of the same cells — paired integration does not require an OT coupling cost inferred from weak feature connections

skills.description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData, rows=cells, columns=peaks) must be converted into a VAE-compatible, [0,1]-scaled matrix before feeding a cross-modality translation model's ATAC encoder.
skills.name: cross-modality-encoder-input-preparation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-encoder-input-preparation Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData, rows=cells, columns=peaks) must be converted into a VAE-compatible, [0,1]-scaled matrix before feeding a cross-modality translation model's ATAC encoder. Input is already TF-IDF-transformed, binarized, or a normalized feature table rather than raw peak counts Preparing scRNA-seq data for the RNA encoder — use RNA_data_preprocessing instead, since ATAC-specific binarization/TF-IDF is modality-specific Unpaired or multi-modal inputs requiring data augmentation or joint MultiVI modeling — this skill covers only per-modality preprocessing prior to augmentation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transforms raw single-cell ATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrices (cells × peaks in AnnData format) into the normalized, value-bounded input required by the scButterfly ATAC variational autoencoder, via binarization, rare-peak filtering, TF-IDF transformation, and [0,1] scaling. This mirrors the modality-specific customary preprocessing applied before scButterfly's encoder/decoder pretraining. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Transforms raw single-cell ATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrices (cells × peaks in AnnData format) into the normalized, value-bounded input required by the scButterfly ATAC variational autoencoder, via binarization, rare-peak filtering, TF-IDF transformation, and [0,1] scaling. This mirrors the modality-specific customary preprocessing applied before scButterfly's encoder/decoder pretraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already TF-IDF-transformed, binarized, or a normalized feature table rather than raw peak counts Preparing scRNA-seq data for the RNA encoder — use RNA_data_preprocessing instead, since ATAC-specific binarization/TF-IDF is modality-specific Unpaired or multi-modal inputs requiring data augmentation or joint MultiVI modeling — this skill covers only per-modality preprocessing prior to augmentation

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with smFISH or scATAC-seq) where features are only weakly connected across modalities and a feature-level cost matrix is needed for rIOT-based alignment.
skills.name: cross-modality-feature-connection-computation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-feature-connection-computation Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with smFISH or scATAC-seq) where features are only weakly connected across modalities and a feature-level cost matrix is needed for rIOT-based alignment. When integrating modality pairs with no cross-modality feature connections at all (e.g. electrophysiology measurements with gene expression), since the method 'relies on connections between features of different modalities'. When data are paired (same cells measured across modalities) rather than unpaired/diagonal integration. When the goal is a modality-specific feature conversion rather than preserving each modality's complete feature set with uncoupled autoencoders. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes the cross-modality distance/cost matrix linking features (e.g. genes) shared between single-cell modalities, which scConfluence uses to align unpaired modalities via regularized Inverse Optimal Transport on weakly connected features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Computes the cross-modality distance/cost matrix linking features (e.g. genes) shared between single-cell modalities, which scConfluence uses to align unpaired modalities via regularized Inverse Optimal Transport on weakly connected features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When integrating modality pairs with no cross-modality feature connections at all (e.g. electrophysiology measurements with gene expression), since the method 'relies on connections between features of different modalities'. When data are paired (same cells measured across modalities) rather than unpaired/diagonal integration. When the goal is a modality-specific feature conversion rather than preserving each modality's complete feature set with uncoupled autoencoders.

skills.description: Use when you have aligned source/target single-cell latent manifolds (e.g. ATAC projected onto RNA space by scTopoGAN) plus cell type labels, and need a metric of alignment quality or a stability check across random GAN initializations.
skills.name: cross-modality-label-matching-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-label-matching-evaluation Use when you have aligned source/target single-cell latent manifolds (e.g. ATAC projected onto RNA space by scTopoGAN) plus cell type labels, and need a metric of alignment quality or a stability check across random GAN initializations. Datasets with overlapping features or cells — standard integration methods that exploit overlap are sufficient, and this unsupervised alignment evaluation is unnecessary Input is raw ATAC/RNA data rather than low-dimensional topoAE latent manifolds — the scores must be computed on aligned embeddings produced by run_scTopoGAN, not unembedded matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies the quality of an unsupervised cross-modality single-cell alignment by computing Celltype and Subcelltype label-matching scores between the aligned source manifold and the target manifold. It also supports correlating those scores with the topology-guided GAN's topological loss (Eq. 2) to verify that low topological loss tracks better alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Quantifies the quality of an unsupervised cross-modality single-cell alignment by computing Celltype and Subcelltype label-matching scores between the aligned source manifold and the target manifold. It also supports correlating those scores with the topology-guided GAN's topological loss (Eq. 2) to verify that low topological loss tracks better alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with overlapping features or cells — standard integration methods that exploit overlap are sufficient, and this unsupervised alignment evaluation is unnecessary Input is raw ATAC/RNA data rather than low-dimensional topoAE latent manifolds — the scores must be computed on aligned embeddings produced by run_scTopoGAN, not unembedded matrices

skills.description: Use when after multi-omic integration you have reclustered cells (e.g. B cells and monocytes at Louvain resolution 0.2) and need statistical evidence that subcluster markers are shared across modalities (scRNA vs scATAC) rather than an alignment artifact.
skills.name: cross-modality-marker-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: cross-modality-marker-enrichment-testing Use when after multi-omic integration you have reclustered cells (e.g. B cells and monocytes at Louvain resolution 0.2) and need statistical evidence that subcluster markers are shared across modalities (scRNA vs scATAC) rather than an alignment artifact. Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections (e.g. integrating electrophysiology measurements with gene expression), so scConfluence embeddings and hence cross-modality marker overlap cannot be computed Cell populations of interest are extremely rare (<0.5% of the dataset); the article notes rare populations are hard to detect and under-represented in parameter estimation, undermining marker reliability Input is paired multimodal data on the same cells, where joint-feature methods rather than diagonal integration plus cross-modality overlap testing are appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validates diagonal integration of unpaired single-cell modalities by testing whether differentially expressed genes of subclusters (e.g. re-annotated B cell and monocyte subclusters from tri-omics PBMC scRNA/scATAC/CyTOF data) significantly overlap across modalities using Fisher's exact tests, confirming biological signal rather than artificial alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Validates diagonal integration of unpaired single-cell modalities by testing whether differentially expressed genes of subclusters (e.g. re-annotated B cell and monocyte subclusters from tri-omics PBMC scRNA/scATAC/CyTOF data) significantly overlap across modalities using Fisher's exact tests, confirming biological signal rather than artificial alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections (e.g. integrating electrophysiology measurements with gene expression), so scConfluence embeddings and hence cross-modality marker overlap cannot be computed Cell populations of interest are extremely rare (<0.5% of the dataset); the article notes rare populations are hard to detect and under-represented in parameter estimation, undermining marker reliability Input is paired multimodal data on the same cells, where joint-feature methods rather than diagonal integration plus cross-modality overlap testing are appropriate

skills.description: Use when a single-modality dataset (e.g., scATAC-seq from BMMC batches) must be translated consecutively to a downstream modality (ADT via CITE_BMMC) and compared head-to-head with alternative translator pipelines under a labeled ground truth.
skills.name: cross-modality-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-modality-method-benchmark-comparison Use when a single-modality dataset (e.g., scATAC-seq from BMMC batches) must be translated consecutively to a downstream modality (ADT via CITE_BMMC) and compared head-to-head with alternative translator pipelines under a labeled ground truth. The target modality is not supported by scButterfly or the baselines, e.g., spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C data, which the article names only as future directions The data to be translated spans cross-cell-type or cross-organ contexts, where the article flags scButterfly performance as still needing improvement via adaptive and interpretable model parameters No ground-truth cell-type labels or baseline predictions are available, so comparative clustering indices (AMI/ARI/HOM/NMI) cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks scButterfly's chained cross-modality translation (scATAC-seq → scRNA-seq → ADT) against combination baselines (BABEL+sciPENN, Polarbear+sciPENN) on BMMC and CITE_BMMC data, using cell-type clustering scores (AMI, ARI, HOM, NMI) as the comparative yardstick. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks scButterfly's chained cross-modality translation (scATAC-seq → scRNA-seq → ADT) against combination baselines (BABEL+sciPENN, Polarbear+sciPENN) on BMMC and CITE_BMMC data, using cell-type clustering scores (AMI, ARI, HOM, NMI) as the comparative yardstick.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target modality is not supported by scButterfly or the baselines, e.g., spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C data, which the article names only as future directions The data to be translated spans cross-cell-type or cross-organ contexts, where the article flags scButterfly performance as still needing improvement via adaptive and interpretable model parameters No ground-truth cell-type labels or baseline predictions are available, so comparative clustering indices (AMI/ARI/HOM/NMI) cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a mosaic multi-omics dataset (e.g. CITE-seq + ASAP-seq batches) has batch–modality slots with no count matrix and you need pseudo-counts for those slots before running scMoMaT first-stage training.
skills.name: cross-modality-pseudo-count-generation
skills.search_text: cross-modality-pseudo-count-generation Use when a mosaic multi-omics dataset (e.g. CITE-seq + ASAP-seq batches) has batch–modality slots with no count matrix and you need pseudo-counts for those slots before running scMoMaT first-stage training. All batch–modality slots already have real count matrices — no pseudo-counts are needed; proceed directly to utils.preprocess() Feature sets are not yet matched across batches — the intersection/remapping step must be done first, since each modality list must share the same feature set Using a baseline method (MultiMap, UINMF, StabMap, MultiMAP, LIGER) that does not consume the scMoMaT counts dictionary or GxR connection matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates pseudo-count matrices for batch–modality slots missing in a mosaic single-cell multi-omics dataset, using a precomputed cross-modality connection matrix (GxR.npz), so that scMoMaT's matrix tri-factorization receives a complete count tensor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Generates pseudo-count matrices for batch–modality slots missing in a mosaic single-cell multi-omics dataset, using a precomputed cross-modality connection matrix (GxR.npz), so that scMoMaT's matrix tri-factorization receives a complete count tensor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All batch–modality slots already have real count matrices — no pseudo-counts are needed; proceed directly to utils.preprocess() Feature sets are not yet matched across batches — the intersection/remapping step must be done first, since each modality list must share the same feature set Using a baseline method (MultiMap, UINMF, StabMap, MultiMAP, LIGER) that does not consume the scMoMaT counts dictionary or GxR connection matrix

skills.description: Use when a segmentation pipeline validated on one multiplexed imaging modality (e.g., MIBI, IMC, imaging mass cytometry) must be evaluated on another platform or marker set to demonstrate cross-tissue/platform transferability.
skills.name: cross-modality-segmentation-transfer
skills.search_text: cross-modality-segmentation-transfer Use when a segmentation pipeline validated on one multiplexed imaging modality (e.g., MIBI, IMC, imaging mass cytometry) must be evaluated on another platform or marker set to demonstrate cross-tissue/platform transferability. Input data is the original multiplexed immunofluorescence colorectal adenoma dataset — that is the primary development/validation use case, not a transfer test. No manually annotated reference segmentation is available, so DSC/JSC cannot be computed to verify transfer quality. The goal is whole-image segmentation benchmarking against Mesmer or Voronoi baselines on a single modality rather than assessing cross-platform generalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Test whether the MIRIAM segmentation pipeline — random forest pixel classification plus membrane extension for internal aberrant membranes — generalizes to a different imaging platform, marker set, and tissue type (breast carcinoma MIBI TMA images) than the multiplexed immunofluorescence colorectal adenoma data it was developed on. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Test whether the MIRIAM segmentation pipeline — random forest pixel classification plus membrane extension for internal aberrant membranes — generalizes to a different imaging platform, marker set, and tissue type (breast carcinoma MIBI TMA images) than the multiplexed immunofluorescence colorectal adenoma data it was developed on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is the original multiplexed immunofluorescence colorectal adenoma dataset — that is the primary development/validation use case, not a transfer test. No manually annotated reference segmentation is available, so DSC/JSC cannot be computed to verify transfer quality. The goal is whole-image segmentation benchmarking against Mesmer or Voronoi baselines on a single modality rather than assessing cross-platform generalization.

skills.name: cross-modality-single-cell-cluster-label-consistency
skills.search_text: cross-modality-single-cell-cluster-label-consistency Use when you have one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq sample from the same heterogeneous population and need linked subpopulations with identical cluster labels across both modalities before comparative gene regulatory analysis. Consistent cluster labels already exist from another source (e.g. known cell-type markers); the README states cnmf is not required, only consistent assignments across scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq Data are unpaired or from more than one donor per condition — the paper notes the approach is for one sample per condition and multi-donor extension is pending http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Joint clustering of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples via CoupledNMF so that cells in both modalities receive a single consistent set of cluster labels, which are then passed as O1.idx/E1.idx/O2.idx/E2.idx to sc_compreg for comparative regulatory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Joint clustering of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples via CoupledNMF so that cells in both modalities receive a single consistent set of cluster labels, which are then passed as O1.idx/E1.idx/O2.idx/E2.idx to sc_compreg for comparative regulatory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Consistent cluster labels already exist from another source (e.g. known cell-type markers); the README states cnmf is not required, only consistent assignments across scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq Data are unpaired or from more than one donor per condition — the paper notes the approach is for one sample per condition and multi-donor extension is pending

skills.description: Use when paired single-cell count matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq genes and scATAC-seq peaks as AnnData) are available and a held-out single-modality profile must be translated into the other modality while preserving cellular heterogeneity.
skills.name: cross-modality-translation-model-training
skills.search_text: cross-modality-translation-model-training Use when paired single-cell count matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq genes and scATAC-seq peaks as AnnData) are available and a held-out single-modality profile must be translated into the other modality while preserving cellular heterogeneity. The two modalities are completely unpaired at the cell level with no paired data available for training — the paired dual-alignment workflow here assumes paired measurements (unpaired/diagonal training is a distinct variant) Input data is already normalized/processed rather than raw count matrices — scButterfly's preprocessing expects raw counts and applies its own RNA normalization and TF-IDF/ATAC handling The goal is translation into a modality beyond scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq pairs such as spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C — the article names these as future directions not yet supported http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a dual-aligned variational autoencoder (scButterfly) that translates single-cell profiles between modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) from raw paired count matrices, with optional data augmentation via cell-type labels (scButterfly-T) or MultiVI cluster labels (scButterfly-C). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Train a dual-aligned variational autoencoder (scButterfly) that translates single-cell profiles between modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) from raw paired count matrices, with optional data augmentation via cell-type labels (scButterfly-T) or MultiVI cluster labels (scButterfly-C).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two modalities are completely unpaired at the cell level with no paired data available for training — the paired dual-alignment workflow here assumes paired measurements (unpaired/diagonal training is a distinct variant) Input data is already normalized/processed rather than raw count matrices — scButterfly's preprocessing expects raw counts and applies its own RNA normalization and TF-IDF/ATAC handling The goal is translation into a modality beyond scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq pairs such as spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C — the article names these as future directions not yet supported

skills.description: Use when paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data are available and ATAC-only profiles must be converted to RNA-like profiles, e.g., to annotate scATAC-seq cell types via translated RNA expression.
skills.name: cross-modality-translation-scrna-scatac
skills.search_text: cross-modality-translation-scrna-scatac Use when paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data are available and ATAC-only profiles must be converted to RNA-like profiles, e.g., to annotate scATAC-seq cell types via translated RNA expression. Data are single-modality with no paired or unpaired counterpart modality available for translator training — scButterfly requires RNA and ATAC (or other modality) inputs Spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C data are the target modalities — the article names these only as future extensions not yet supported The goal is annotating RNA profiles directly; the documented annotation pipeline targets scATAC-seq cell type annotation via translated RNA profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Translate single-cell ATAC-seq profiles into RNA expression using scButterfly's dual-aligned variational autoencoder, enabling downstream tasks such as automatic cell type annotation of scATAC-seq data (e.g., PBMC multiome) without direct RNA measurement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Translate single-cell ATAC-seq profiles into RNA expression using scButterfly's dual-aligned variational autoencoder, enabling downstream tasks such as automatic cell type annotation of scATAC-seq data (e.g., PBMC multiome) without direct RNA measurement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-modality with no paired or unpaired counterpart modality available for translator training — scButterfly requires RNA and ATAC (or other modality) inputs Spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C data are the target modalities — the article names these only as future extensions not yet supported The goal is annotating RNA profiles directly; the documented annotation pipeline targets scATAC-seq cell type annotation via translated RNA profiles

skills.description: Use when multiple virus-read-classification models must be compared fairly on identical RNA-seq fragment data, e.g. to reproduce the finding that viRNAtrap beats baselines on all measures except precision, where DeepVirFinder wins.
skills.name: cross-model-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-model-benchmark-comparison Use when multiple virus-read-classification models must be compared fairly on identical RNA-seq fragment data, e.g. to reproduce the finding that viRNAtrap beats baselines on all measures except precision, where DeepVirFinder wins. The goal is de novo viral discovery or contig assembly from unmapped RNA-seq reads rather than classifier benchmarking (that is viRNAtrap's prediction/assembly pipeline, not this comparison task). Models cannot be retrained on the same fragments — comparing models trained on different training data violates the shared-test-set design and makes the metrics non-comparable. Input reads are not fixed-length 48 bp fragments; the pretrained viRNAtrap model and the benchmark protocol are specific to 48 bp read lengths. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Retrain viRNAtrap and competing virus-identification deep learning models (DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, off-the-shelf Seq2Seq) on the same 48 bp RNA-seq fragments and evaluate them on a shared test set to produce a single head-to-head metrics table (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC), as in the viRNAtrap paper's benchmark comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Retrain viRNAtrap and competing virus-identification deep learning models (DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, off-the-shelf Seq2Seq) on the same 48 bp RNA-seq fragments and evaluate them on a shared test set to produce a single head-to-head metrics table (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC), as in the viRNAtrap paper's benchmark comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo viral discovery or contig assembly from unmapped RNA-seq reads rather than classifier benchmarking (that is viRNAtrap's prediction/assembly pipeline, not this comparison task). Models cannot be retrained on the same fragments — comparing models trained on different training data violates the shared-test-set design and makes the metrics non-comparable. Input reads are not fixed-length 48 bp fragments; the pretrained viRNAtrap model and the benchmark protocol are specific to 48 bp read lengths.

skills.description: Use when comparing prediction accuracy of a new model or aggregation scheme (e.g., cluster/pathway-level) against a baseline model like BIRD at multiple DHS cluster resolutions.
skills.name: cross-model-prediction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-model-prediction-benchmarking Use when comparing prediction accuracy of a new model or aggregation scheme (e.g., cluster/pathway-level) against a baseline model like BIRD at multiple DHS cluster resolutions. You want BIRD to discover new DHS locations not in the training catalog — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs on a new gene expression sample The input expression data uses a platform/gene-id scheme the BIRD model cannot match (e.g., non-ensembl ids without prior matching) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark alternative prediction models (e.g., pathway-level BIR(X-bar, Y-bar) aggregating co-activated DHS clusters vs. locus-level BIRD) by comparing correlation coefficients between predicted and measured DNase I hypersensitivity across genomic resolutions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Benchmark alternative prediction models (e.g., pathway-level BIR(X-bar, Y-bar) aggregating co-activated DHS clusters vs. locus-level BIRD) by comparing correlation coefficients between predicted and measured DNase I hypersensitivity across genomic resolutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want BIRD to discover new DHS locations not in the training catalog — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs on a new gene expression sample The input expression data uses a platform/gene-id scheme the BIRD model cannot match (e.g., non-ensembl ids without prior matching)

skills.description: Use when comparing marker-selection or latent-variable models on their ability to reconstruct full gene expression from a small marker panel (k markers), with per-cell-type and overall reconstruction metrics such as Jaccard Index, Spearman rho, and l2 distance.
skills.name: cross-model-reconstruction-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-model-reconstruction-evaluation Use when comparing marker-selection or latent-variable models on their ability to reconstruct full gene expression from a small marker panel (k markers), with per-cell-type and overall reconstruction metrics such as Jaccard Index, Spearman rho, and l2 distance. The goal is cell-type classification accuracy from markers (use new_model_metrics with a RandomForestClassifier instead of reconstruction metrics) You need to benchmark marker counts over a range of k values rather than compare two models at fixed k The data cannot be converted to a dense numpy array and the models require dense input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking procedure that compares how well different marker-selection models (e.g., unsupervised MarkerMap vs scVI) reconstruct the full transcriptome from only k=50 selected markers, using Jaccard Index, Spearman rho, and l2 distance metrics averaged over 5 random 80/20 splits, as in Table 4 of the MarkerMap paper for the Mouse Brain dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that compares how well different marker-selection models (e.g., unsupervised MarkerMap vs scVI) reconstruct the full transcriptome from only k=50 selected markers, using Jaccard Index, Spearman rho, and l2 distance metrics averaged over 5 random 80/20 splits, as in Table 4 of the MarkerMap paper for the Mouse Brain dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-type classification accuracy from markers (use new_model_metrics with a RandomForestClassifier instead of reconstruction metrics) You need to benchmark marker counts over a range of k values rather than compare two models at fixed k The data cannot be converted to a dense numpy array and the models require dense input

skills.description: Use when comparing synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple deep generative models against an original count matrix to assess per-gene univariate distribution fidelity, including bimodality failures.
skills.name: cross-model-synthetic-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-model-synthetic-quality-evaluation Use when comparing synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple deep generative models against an original count matrix to assess per-gene univariate distribution fidelity, including bimodality failures. When evaluating clustering-level properties (ARI, Davies–Bouldin index, cluster proportions) rather than per-gene univariate distributions When the synthetic data must preserve batch effects — the paper examined all models without batch correction, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects When the input data is not count-level scRNA-seq from the models under comparison (e.g., already-aggregated expression summaries) http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluate how faithfully synthetic scRNA-seq datasets generated by scDBM, scVI (prior), and scVI (posterior) reproduce per-gene univariate distributions of the original data, by comparing medians, interquartile ranges, coefficients of variation, and zero-count proportions across pilot sizes of 384–2304 cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Evaluate how faithfully synthetic scRNA-seq datasets generated by scDBM, scVI (prior), and scVI (posterior) reproduce per-gene univariate distributions of the original data, by comparing medians, interquartile ranges, coefficients of variation, and zero-count proportions across pilot sizes of 384–2304 cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating clustering-level properties (ARI, Davies–Bouldin index, cluster proportions) rather than per-gene univariate distributions When the synthetic data must preserve batch effects — the paper examined all models without batch correction, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects When the input data is not count-level scRNA-seq from the models under comparison (e.g., already-aggregated expression summaries)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq raw count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and the question is how much normalization method (RAW/TC/TMM/FQ) vs. dimensionality-reduction method (PCA/ZIFA/ZINB-WaVE) affects downstream clustering quality.
skills.name: cross-normalization-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-normalization-benchmark-comparison Use when scRNA-seq raw count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and the question is how much normalization method (RAW/TC/TMM/FQ) vs. dimensionality-reduction method (PCA/ZIFA/ZINB-WaVE) affects downstream clustering quality. Input is already normalized or log-transformed (e.g. log2(1 + counts) for ZIFA) and the RAW/TC/TMM/FQ crossing cannot be constructed from raw counts No ground-truth or author-provided cell-type labels exist, so the silhouette criterion cannot be computed The goal is differential expression or batch-effect correction with covariates rather than comparing normalization impact on clustering of labeled cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarking skill that crosses between-sample normalization choices (RAW, TC, TMM, FQ) with dimensionality-reduction methods (PCA, ZIFA, ZINB-WaVE) and scores each representation by the average silhouette width of author-provided cell-type labels, to test whether normalization choice dominates method choice in scRNA-seq signal extraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that crosses between-sample normalization choices (RAW, TC, TMM, FQ) with dimensionality-reduction methods (PCA, ZIFA, ZINB-WaVE) and scores each representation by the average silhouette width of author-provided cell-type labels, to test whether normalization choice dominates method choice in scRNA-seq signal extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or log-transformed (e.g. log2(1 + counts) for ZIFA) and the RAW/TC/TMM/FQ crossing cannot be constructed from raw counts No ground-truth or author-provided cell-type labels exist, so the silhouette criterion cannot be computed The goal is differential expression or batch-effect correction with covariates rather than comparing normalization impact on clustering of labeled cells

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq/ASAP-seq) h5ad data and you need to benchmark label-transfer F1/accuracy under reduced annotations, noisy labels, or novel cell-type discovery.
skills.name: cross-omics-label-transfer-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-omics-label-transfer-benchmarking Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq/ASAP-seq) h5ad data and you need to benchmark label-transfer F1/accuracy under reduced annotations, noisy labels, or novel cell-type discovery. The data are paired multi-omics with cross-omics pairing information, where methods like scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration and clustering instead The target modality is protein abundance rather than scATAC-seq gene activity and no ATAC preprocessing is available to build a gene activity matrix You only need a quick joint visualization without annotations on either modality; scBridge requires annotated scRNA-seq source data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark label transfer from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq data using scBridge against baselines (scJoint, GLUE, Seurat), including annotation-downsampling and label-corruption robustness tests and novel-type discovery via a GMM-based reliability model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Benchmark label transfer from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq data using scBridge against baselines (scJoint, GLUE, Seurat), including annotation-downsampling and label-corruption robustness tests and novel-type discovery via a GMM-based reliability model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are paired multi-omics with cross-omics pairing information, where methods like scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration and clustering instead The target modality is protein abundance rather than scATAC-seq gene activity and no ATAC preprocessing is available to build a gene activity matrix You only need a quick joint visualization without annotations on either modality; scBridge requires annotated scRNA-seq source data

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq data (e.g., CITE-seq source + ASAP-seq target .h5ad) and you need to progressively align modalities without treating all cells homogeneously.
skills.name: cross-omics-prototype-alignment
skills.search_text: cross-omics-prototype-alignment Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq data (e.g., CITE-seq source + ASAP-seq target .h5ad) and you need to progressively align modalities without treating all cells homogeneously. Data is paired multi-omics where cross-omics pairing information is available (e.g., scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration and clustering on such data) Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq data has not yet been transformed into a gene activity matrix — the alignment operates on gene-space representations The integration goal is homogeneous treatment of all cells at once (e.g., scJoint-style semi-supervised training) rather than progressive, heterogeneity-aware integration http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A reliability-weighted prototype alignment step from scBridge's heterogeneous transfer learning loop that narrows the omics gap between annotated scRNA-seq and unlabeled scATAC-seq embeddings by aligning cross-omics cell-type prototypes, prioritizing scATAC-seq cells with smaller omics differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: A reliability-weighted prototype alignment step from scBridge's heterogeneous transfer learning loop that narrows the omics gap between annotated scRNA-seq and unlabeled scATAC-seq embeddings by aligning cross-omics cell-type prototypes, prioritizing scATAC-seq cells with smaller omics differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is paired multi-omics where cross-omics pairing information is available (e.g., scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration and clustering on such data) Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq data has not yet been transformed into a gene activity matrix — the alignment operates on gene-space representations The integration goal is homogeneous treatment of all cells at once (e.g., scJoint-style semi-supervised training) rather than progressive, heterogeneity-aware integration

skills.description: Use when you need to position a new single-cell analysis tool against existing Python ML/DNN pipelines by comparing accuracy, memory usage, and wall-clock execution time on a shared dataset and VM.
skills.name: cross-pipeline-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-pipeline-benchmark-comparison Use when you need to position a new single-cell analysis tool against existing Python ML/DNN pipelines by comparing accuracy, memory usage, and wall-clock execution time on a shared dataset and VM. When you only need to characterize one pipeline's standalone performance without a same-hardware, same-dataset baseline — the comparison is only meaningful under controlled identical conditions When the comparison tools cannot expose needed outputs for fair evaluation — the paper notes top features cannot be extracted from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and cellPLM, limiting biomarker-ranking comparability http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a target single-cell pipeline (e.g. scaLR) against competing frameworks (scVI-tools, SingleCellNet, CellTypist, ACTINN, devCellPy, scBalance, cellPLM) on the same dataset, hardware, and task, recording prediction accuracy, peak memory, and execution time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Benchmark a target single-cell pipeline (e.g. scaLR) against competing frameworks (scVI-tools, SingleCellNet, CellTypist, ACTINN, devCellPy, scBalance, cellPLM) on the same dataset, hardware, and task, recording prediction accuracy, peak memory, and execution time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need to characterize one pipeline's standalone performance without a same-hardware, same-dataset baseline — the comparison is only meaningful under controlled identical conditions When the comparison tools cannot expose needed outputs for fair evaluation — the paper notes top features cannot be extracted from scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, and cellPLM, limiting biomarker-ranking comparability

skills.description: Use when the goal is to validate a barcode annotation pipeline by re-running an alternative published pipeline on the same single-cell amplicon FASTQs and comparing per-cell barcode calls and clone sizes.
skills.name: cross-pipeline-cell-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-pipeline-cell-annotation-comparison Use when the goal is to validate a barcode annotation pipeline by re-running an alternative published pipeline on the same single-cell amplicon FASTQs and comparing per-cell barcode calls and clone sizes. Input is already a cell barcode annotation/counts table rather than raw amplicon FASTQ — barcode extraction and alignment are not needed Data are population-level (bulk) barcoding libraries rather than single-cell data with cell barcodes and UMIs The barcode design lacks a constant flanking region and known reference library, breaking the cutadapt constant-trimming and bowtie-based reference alignment strategy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces and compares single-cell lineage barcode cell annotations generated by two pipelines (BARtab and Rewind/FateMap) on the same FM0-2 amplicon FASTQ data, quantifying annotation overlap and clone-size concordance as a validation of pipeline equivalence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Reproduces and compares single-cell lineage barcode cell annotations generated by two pipelines (BARtab and Rewind/FateMap) on the same FM0-2 amplicon FASTQ data, quantifying annotation overlap and clone-size concordance as a validation of pipeline equivalence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell barcode annotation/counts table rather than raw amplicon FASTQ — barcode extraction and alignment are not needed Data are population-level (bulk) barcoding libraries rather than single-cell data with cell barcodes and UMIs The barcode design lacks a constant flanking region and known reference library, breaking the cutadapt constant-trimming and bowtie-based reference alignment strategy

skills.description: Use when a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq query dataset from one sequencing platform must be labeled using a reference built from other platforms, or when benchmarking annotation tools on externally harmonized datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas.
skills.name: cross-platform-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: cross-platform-cell-type-annotation Use when a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq query dataset from one sequencing platform must be labeled using a reference built from other platforms, or when benchmarking annotation tools on externally harmonized datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas. Query data is from a disease context whose expression profiles deviate strongly from the normal reference — use SELINA's disease mode models or user-supplied disease references instead The species or cell types of interest are outside the human reference atlas coverage (transfer to other species is only anticipated, not demonstrated) A comprehensive, uniformly annotated reference atlas already exists for the exact tissue and the goal is not cross-platform transfer or tool benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate single-cell RNA-seq query data generated on different platforms (e.g., 10x vs. Smart-seq) by transferring labels from a large harmonized reference atlas using SELINA's multi-adversarial domain adaptation workflow, and benchmark against reference-based and marker-based annotation tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell RNA-seq query data generated on different platforms (e.g., 10x vs. Smart-seq) by transferring labels from a large harmonized reference atlas using SELINA's multi-adversarial domain adaptation workflow, and benchmark against reference-based and marker-based annotation tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data is from a disease context whose expression profiles deviate strongly from the normal reference — use SELINA's disease mode models or user-supplied disease references instead The species or cell types of interest are outside the human reference atlas coverage (transfer to other species is only anticipated, not demonstrated) A comprehensive, uniformly annotated reference atlas already exists for the exact tissue and the goal is not cross-platform transfer or tool benchmarking

skills.description: Use when evaluating which automatic cell-type identification method transfers across scRNA-seq platforms: labeled training data from one platform, held-out or cross-platform test data from others, ranked by accuracy, F1 and unlabeling rate.
skills.name: cross-platform-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: cross-platform-cell-type-classification Use when evaluating which automatic cell-type identification method transfers across scRNA-seq platforms: labeled training data from one platform, held-out or cross-platform test data from others, ranked by accuracy, F1 and unlabeling rate. Training and testing cells come from the same platform/dataset — the self-projection evaluation (five-fold cross-validation within one dataset) is the appropriate design instead Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a preprocessed count matrix with gene rows and cell columns; the package expects a count matrix No manually annotated labels or marker sets are available for any platform, so neither supervised nor marker-based interfaces can be trained http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark automatic cell-type identification methods in cross-platform prediction on scRNA-seq data (e.g. PBMC from seven platforms), training on one platform and testing on others, and rank eager, lazy and marker-learning methods by accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Benchmark automatic cell-type identification methods in cross-platform prediction on scRNA-seq data (e.g. PBMC from seven platforms), training on one platform and testing on others, and rank eager, lazy and marker-learning methods by accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training and testing cells come from the same platform/dataset — the self-projection evaluation (five-fold cross-validation within one dataset) is the appropriate design instead Input is raw sequencing reads rather than a preprocessed count matrix with gene rows and cell columns; the package expects a count matrix No manually annotated labels or marker sets are available for any platform, so neither supervised nor marker-based interfaces can be trained

skills.description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic time series with labeled circadian times (microarray or RNAseq) must predict circadian time of samples from a different assay platform, e.g. RNAseq or scRNAseq pseudobulk, and accuracy/RMSE must be reported.
skills.name: cross-platform-circadian-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-platform-circadian-prediction-evaluation Use when a bulk transcriptomic time series with labeled circadian times (microarray or RNAseq) must predict circadian time of samples from a different assay platform, e.g. RNAseq or scRNAseq pseudobulk, and accuracy/RMSE must be reported. You need circadian time at the single-cell level: tauFisher cannot overcome high scRNAseq dropout and predicts only on bulk or pseudobulk samples The test samples are circadian-disturbed or diseased: tauFisher trained on healthy time series cannot project onto a diseased timescale without a diseased training series The predictor genes are absent from the test platform/assay beyond dropout tolerance (only 16 of 18 genes survived in the dermis benchmark; extensive loss would invalidate the model) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark that trains tauFisher on a bulk transcriptomic circadian time series from one assay platform (e.g. GSE38622 mouse skin microarray) and evaluates whether it predicts circadian time of samples measured on another platform (RNAseq or scRNAseq pseudobulk), scored by within-2-hour accuracy and RMSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: Benchmark that trains tauFisher on a bulk transcriptomic circadian time series from one assay platform (e.g. GSE38622 mouse skin microarray) and evaluates whether it predicts circadian time of samples measured on another platform (RNAseq or scRNAseq pseudobulk), scored by within-2-hour accuracy and RMSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need circadian time at the single-cell level: tauFisher cannot overcome high scRNAseq dropout and predicts only on bulk or pseudobulk samples The test samples are circadian-disturbed or diseased: tauFisher trained on healthy time series cannot project onto a diseased timescale without a diseased training series The predictor genes are absent from the test platform/assay beyond dropout tolerance (only 16 of 18 genes survived in the dermis benchmark; extensive loss would invalidate the model)

skills.description: Use when a gene-expression subtype classifier trained on one platform (e.g., TCGA RNA-Seq) must be evaluated on independent cohorts from other platforms, or when robustness to unmatched/missing genes is assessed by random gene subsampling.
skills.name: cross-platform-classifier-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-platform-classifier-benchmarking Use when a gene-expression subtype classifier trained on one platform (e.g., TCGA RNA-Seq) must be evaluated on independent cohorts from other platforms, or when robustness to unmatched/missing genes is assessed by random gene subsampling. The goal is de novo clustering or discovery of new cancer subtypes — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification, not clustering of cancer patients. Input is already a functional-spectra (pathway-activity) feature table rather than a gene-level expression matrix with Entrez identifiers, so gene-level subsampling and spectrum regeneration are impossible. No labeled training cohort exists for the target subtyping system (e.g., PAM50 labels), since DeepCC is a supervised framework. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmarks a DeepCC molecular subtype classifier across platforms: an ANN is trained on functional spectra of TCGA RNA-Seq data (PAM50 labels) and evaluated on independent microarray cohorts, with random gene-subsampling ablation quantifying robustness to cross-platform missing genes (balanced accuracy > 80% at 1000 genes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Benchmarks a DeepCC molecular subtype classifier across platforms: an ANN is trained on functional spectra of TCGA RNA-Seq data (PAM50 labels) and evaluated on independent microarray cohorts, with random gene-subsampling ablation quantifying robustness to cross-platform missing genes (balanced accuracy > 80% at 1000 genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo clustering or discovery of new cancer subtypes — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification, not clustering of cancer patients. Input is already a functional-spectra (pathway-activity) feature table rather than a gene-level expression matrix with Entrez identifiers, so gene-level subsampling and spectrum regeneration are impossible. No labeled training cohort exists for the target subtyping system (e.g., PAM50 labels), since DeepCC is a supervised framework.

skills.description: Use when a newly produced poly(A) site or APA quantification matrix (e.g., polyA_sites.tsv from scAPAtrap on ST-MOB data) must be checked for agreement against a second transcriptomic platform.

skills.summary: Validates poly(A) site-level expression quantification from spatially barcoded ST data by computing Pearson correlations of the site expression table against independently generated datasets from other platforms — here, single-cell MOB (SC-MOB) data and neural bulk 3'-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a quantified poly(A) site or APA usage matrix (e.g., raw FASTQ or a genome alignment BAM) — correlation validation presupposes a site-level expression table The goal is APA site identification from platforms lacking spatial barcodes, e.g., MERFISH or seqFISH — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing scRNA-seq tools such as scAPAtrap or Sierra

skills.description: Use when a cell-gene expression matrix from segmented spatial transcriptomics data needs benchmarking against a matched scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Chromium scFFPE-seq of the same tissue) via expression-profile correlation.
skills.name: cross-platform-gene-expression-correlation
skills.search_text: cross-platform-gene-expression-correlation Use when a cell-gene expression matrix from segmented spatial transcriptomics data needs benchmarking against a matched scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Chromium scFFPE-seq of the same tissue) via expression-profile correlation. The spatial data lack a paired single-cell reference dataset from the same tissue, so no matched average-expression profile can be computed. The task is pure segmentation generation (run_pipeline: preprocess, train, predict) rather than evaluation of an already-produced expression matrix. Cell-type identity annotation (not expression-profile concordance) is the target; neighbour-contamination distance analyses (Fig. 3e) would be more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates a subcellular spatial transcriptomics segmentation (e.g. BIDCell on Xenium-BreastCancer1) by correlating its average cell-gene expression profile with the average expression from a paired Chromium scFFPE-seq single-cell reference, as in Fig. 3a-d of the BIDCell paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Evaluates a subcellular spatial transcriptomics segmentation (e.g. BIDCell on Xenium-BreastCancer1) by correlating its average cell-gene expression profile with the average expression from a paired Chromium scFFPE-seq single-cell reference, as in Fig. 3a-d of the BIDCell paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial data lack a paired single-cell reference dataset from the same tissue, so no matched average-expression profile can be computed. skills.search_text: cross-platform-gene-identifier-harmonization Use when assembling circadian time-course datasets from different GEO platforms (e.g., GSE54651 with Ensembl IDs, GSE54650 raw CEL files) whose identifiers must be unified to uppercase gene names before tauFisher training or cross-method benchmarking. skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset fits comfortably in memory and only one implementation is available, so no cross-method or cross-machine contrast is possible The goal is correctness or biological validation of results rather than runtime/memory benchmarking The operation is a complex machine-learning step (e.g. clustering) where the compared tools implement genuinely different algorithms, making runtimes non-comparable

skills.description: Use when a paired scRNA-seq reference and spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g. ST, Visium, MERFISH) need cell-type deconvolution/label transfer, especially when datasets share only partially overlapping genes or are heterogeneous (e.g. PDAC ST + inDrop scRNA).
skills.name: cross-platform-scrna-st-integration
skills.search_text: cross-platform-scrna-st-integration Use when a paired scRNA-seq reference and spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g. ST, Visium, MERFISH) need cell-type deconvolution/label transfer, especially when datasets share only partially overlapping genes or are heterogeneous (e.g. PDAC ST + inDrop scRNA). When the ST and scRNA data derive from the same cells (paired data) and a vertical-integration approach is needed — use uniPort's mode='v' scenario instead of spatial deconvolution via OT When only common genes exist and dataset-specific gene leverage is unnecessary, the coupled-VAE/UOT machinery with adata_cm is overkill; horizontal integration with common genes alone suffices When memory is constrained: storing the dense global OT plan T 'needs more memory', so save_OT=True is the wrong choice for very large spot-by-cell problems http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrates scRNA-seq reference data with spatial transcriptomics (ST) data via uniPort's coupled-VAE plus Minibatch unbalanced optimal transport (Minibatch-UOT), then deconvolves spot composition using the global OT plan rather than the shared latent space. This enables label transfer and cell-type (or cancer-clone) proportion estimation on heterogeneous spot data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Integrates scRNA-seq reference data with spatial transcriptomics (ST) data via uniPort's coupled-VAE plus Minibatch unbalanced optimal transport (Minibatch-UOT), then deconvolves spot composition using the global OT plan rather than the shared latent space. This enables label transfer and cell-type (or cancer-clone) proportion estimation on heterogeneous spot data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the ST and scRNA data derive from the same cells (paired data) and a vertical-integration approach is needed — use uniPort's mode='v' scenario instead of spatial deconvolution via OT When only common genes exist and dataset-specific gene leverage is unnecessary, the coupled-VAE/UOT machinery with adata_cm is overkill; horizontal integration with common genes alone suffices When memory is constrained: storing the dense global OT plan T 'needs more memory', so save_OT=True is the wrong choice for very large spot-by-cell problems

skills.search_text: cross-platform-scrnaseq-parameter-comparison Use when multiple publicly available scRNA-seq count datasets from different protocols (e.g., UMI-based 10x/droplet vs. plate-based read counts) are available and the goal is to test whether distributional assumptions such as the Tweedie index p differ by platform.
