skills.search_text: cross-species-genome-coordinate-processing Use when building training data for RNA modification site prediction from RMBase v2.0 BED/GTF annotations across multiple species, requiring genome-coordinate extraction of flanking sequence windows. Your input is already extracted, center-aligned RNA fragments rather than genome coordinates Your modification annotations are species-specific with no matching reference genome available (e.g. assemblies other than hg19/mm10/sacCer3) You need modification types other than pseudouridine (Ψ), which this extraction scheme was built around http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Extracts 51-nt RNA fragments centered on experimentally validated Ψ sites from RMBase v2.0 annotations by lifting BED coordinate intervals against species-specific reference genomes (hg19 human, mm10 mouse, sacCer3 yeast) using BEDTools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Extracts 51-nt RNA fragments centered on experimentally validated Ψ sites from RMBase v2.0 annotations by lifting BED coordinate intervals against species-specific reference genomes (hg19 human, mm10 mouse, sacCer3 yeast) using BEDTools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already extracted, center-aligned RNA fragments rather than genome coordinates Your modification annotations are species-specific with no matching reference genome available (e.g. assemblies other than hg19/mm10/sacCer3) You need modification types other than pseudouridine (Ψ), which this extraction scheme was built around

skills.description: Use when you have per-species trained lncRNA classifiers and independent FASTA test sets from multiple species, and need to measure homologous vs. divergent transfer (e.g., animal vs. plant) via an MCC matrix.
skills.name: cross-species-lncrna-model-transfer-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-species-lncrna-model-transfer-evaluation Use when you have per-species trained lncRNA classifiers and independent FASTA test sets from multiple species, and need to measure homologous vs. divergent transfer (e.g., animal vs. plant) via an MCC matrix. You only need same-species benchmark performance (diagonal comparison against CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) rather than transfer analysis No species-specific trained models exist for your taxa — the article notes 'Species may lack annotations, and it is impossible to build models for all species.' Evaluating on sORF test datasets (human/mouse/zebrafish), which is a separate LncCat evaluation task http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies how well species-specific LncCat (CatBoost) lncRNA classifiers transfer across the five-species benchmark (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken) by scoring each trained model against every other species' test set and filling a 5x5 Matthew's Correlation Coefficient (MCC) matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Quantifies how well species-specific LncCat (CatBoost) lncRNA classifiers transfer across the five-species benchmark (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken) by scoring each trained model against every other species' test set and filling a 5x5 Matthew's Correlation Coefficient (MCC) matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need same-species benchmark performance (diagonal comparison against CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) rather than transfer analysis No species-specific trained models exist for your taxa — the article notes 'Species may lack annotations, and it is impossible to build models for all species.' Evaluating on sORF test datasets (human/mouse/zebrafish), which is a separate LncCat evaluation task

skills.description: Use when a human single-cell query must be interpreted against a mouse reference atlas — e.g., projecting human tumor biopsy T cells onto the murine TIL map to test human-mouse T cell subtype conservation.
skills.name: cross-species-ortholog-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-species-ortholog-gene-mapping Use when a human single-cell query must be interpreted against a mouse reference atlas — e.g., projecting human tumor biopsy T cells onto the murine TIL map to test human-mouse T cell subtype conservation. When both query and reference are from the same species and share gene identifiers — no ortholog table is needed When a high-quality human T cell reference atlas covering the desired subtypes exists — direct human-to-human projection avoids ortholog mapping artifacts For gamma-delta T cells or under-represented CD4+ TIL states, which are not (or poorly) represented in the mouse TIL reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Enables projection of human scRNA-seq data onto a murine reference atlas by converting human gene identifiers to mouse orthologs (Hs2Mm.convert.table) and embedding the query in the mouse reference space with make.projection, supporting cross-species meta-analysis of TIL subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Enables projection of human scRNA-seq data onto a murine reference atlas by converting human gene identifiers to mouse orthologs (Hs2Mm.convert.table) and embedding the query in the mouse reference space with make.projection, supporting cross-species meta-analysis of TIL subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When both query and reference are from the same species and share gene identifiers — no ortholog table is needed When a high-quality human T cell reference atlas covering the desired subtypes exists — direct human-to-human projection avoids ortholog mapping artifacts For gamma-delta T cells or under-represented CD4+ TIL states, which are not (or poorly) represented in the mouse TIL reference

skills.description: Use when the query scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq dataset is from a different species than the available reference cell map (e.g., wheat query vs. rice reference) and reference-based annotation is required.
skills.name: cross-species-ortholog-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-species-ortholog-mapping Use when the query scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq dataset is from a different species than the available reference cell map (e.g., wheat query vs. rice reference) and reference-based annotation is required. A same-species reference cell map is available, making within-species annotation more appropriate Only marker-gene databases are available and no single-cell reference exists for label transfer The query and reference gene identifiers cannot be reconciled through orthology, leaving incompatible feature spaces http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Maps query genes to orthologs in a reference species so that reference-based cell-type annotation (e.g., SingleR label transfer via scPlant) can run across species, as demonstrated by annotating hexaploid wheat root cells using a rice reference cell map. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Maps query genes to orthologs in a reference species so that reference-based cell-type annotation (e.g., SingleR label transfer via scPlant) can run across species, as demonstrated by annotating hexaploid wheat root cells using a rice reference cell map.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A same-species reference cell map is available, making within-species annotation more appropriate Only marker-gene databases are available and no single-cell reference exists for label transfer The query and reference gene identifiers cannot be reconciled through orthology, leaving incompatible feature spaces

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing an ortholog database (e.g. EcoOmicsDB) from many species' proteomes, or when non-model-species RNA-seq reads must be quantified against cross-species ortholog groups rather than a reference transcriptome.
skills.name: cross-species-orthology-inference
skills.search_text: cross-species-orthology-inference Use when building or reproducing an ortholog database (e.g. EcoOmicsDB) from many species' proteomes, or when non-model-species RNA-seq reads must be quantified against cross-species ortholog groups rather than a reference transcriptome. The species has a well-annotated reference transcriptome/genome with standard gene IDs — direct annotation and genome alignment is preferable, since many uncharacterized IDs remain even in published reference genomes but mapping through orthologs is unnecessary overhead Reads can be mapped directly to KEGG ortholog (KO) databases with Seq2Fun's translated search — no custom ortholog group construction is needed A single-species analysis where cross-species orthology introduces ambiguity (reads from the same gene may map to similar but different orthologs across species) http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 Bins protein-coding sequences from hundreds of eukaryotic species into ortholog groups (as done to build EcoOmicsDB's ortholog database backing ExpressAnalyst), so that RNA-seq reads from species without a reference transcriptome can be mapped to shared functional units. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Bins protein-coding sequences from hundreds of eukaryotic species into ortholog groups (as done to build EcoOmicsDB's ortholog database backing ExpressAnalyst), so that RNA-seq reads from species without a reference transcriptome can be mapped to shared functional units.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species has a well-annotated reference transcriptome/genome with standard gene IDs — direct annotation and genome alignment is preferable, since many uncharacterized IDs remain even in published reference genomes but mapping through orthologs is unnecessary overhead Reads can be mapped directly to KEGG ortholog (KO) databases with Seq2Fun's translated search — no custom ortholog group construction is needed A single-species analysis where cross-species orthology introduces ambiguity (reads from the same gene may map to similar but different orthologs across species)

skills.description: Use when you have human-trained miRSCAPE models (xgboost-based) and need to test transfer to non-training transcriptomic contexts — e.g. ENCODE cell-line mRNA profiles or mouse scRNA-seq clusters — with binary detectability labels for miRNAs.
skills.name: cross-species-pretrained-model-transfer-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-species-pretrained-model-transfer-evaluation Use when you have human-trained miRSCAPE models (xgboost-based) and need to test transfer to non-training transcriptomic contexts — e.g. ENCODE cell-line mRNA profiles or mouse scRNA-seq clusters — with binary detectability labels for miRNAs. The application sample's cellular/tissue context closely matches an available training cohort — retraining or context-matched models are preferred over cross-context transfer Your scRNA-seq data has severe dropout and no pooling is possible; the article notes a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes may be required You need miRNA expression measurements rather than model-based inference — standard scRNA-seq protocols rely on poly(A) capture which mature miRNAs lack, but this skill produces predictions, not measurements http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluate whether miRSCAPE models pre-trained on human paired miRNA-mRNA bulk cohorts (CCLE, AML-TCGA) transfer across species and contexts by predicting miRNA expression for ENCODE cell lines and Zilionis mouse hematopoietic cell types, and scoring predicted values by auROC for detected vs undetected miRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Evaluate whether miRSCAPE models pre-trained on human paired miRNA-mRNA bulk cohorts (CCLE, AML-TCGA) transfer across species and contexts by predicting miRNA expression for ENCODE cell lines and Zilionis mouse hematopoietic cell types, and scoring predicted values by auROC for detected vs undetected miRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The application sample's cellular/tissue context closely matches an available training cohort — retraining or context-matched models are preferred over cross-context transfer Your scRNA-seq data has severe dropout and no pooling is possible; the article notes a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes may be required You need miRNA expression measurements rather than model-based inference — standard scRNA-seq protocols rely on poly(A) capture which mature miRNAs lack, but this skill produces predictions, not measurements

skills.description: Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g. from csRNA-seq or other nascent-transcription data) for any species and need to detect core promoter elements and assess motif positioning around the TSS.
skills.name: cross-species-promoter-element-profiling
skills.search_text: cross-species-promoter-element-profiling Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g. from csRNA-seq or other nascent-transcription data) for any species and need to detect core promoter elements and assess motif positioning around the TSS. Input is already a set of raw sequences without TSS positions — ElemeNT 2023 expects sequences centered on known TSSs; element detection without a TSS anchor cannot support positional-enrichment validation Goal is de novo motif discovery rather than detection of known core promoter elements — ElemeNT 2023 searches defined core promoter elements (and user-defined motifs), not unmotivated motif discovery The task is only differential expression or peak-calling analysis with no promoter-element interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_3176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Detect and profile core promoter elements around transcription start sites in any sequenced species using the ElemeNT 2023 command-line (Perl) tool, demonstrating that element detection is not limited to D. melanogaster and can be applied to human and mouse TSS datasets such as csRNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Detect and profile core promoter elements around transcription start sites in any sequenced species using the ElemeNT 2023 command-line (Perl) tool, demonstrating that element detection is not limited to D. melanogaster and can be applied to human and mouse TSS datasets such as csRNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of raw sequences without TSS positions — ElemeNT 2023 expects sequences centered on known TSSs; element detection without a TSS anchor cannot support positional-enrichment validation Goal is de novo motif discovery rather than detection of known core promoter elements — ElemeNT 2023 searches defined core promoter elements (and user-defined motifs), not unmotivated motif discovery The task is only differential expression or peak-calling analysis with no promoter-element interpretation

skills.description: Use when integrating single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different tissues or species where a pretrained embedding model (scETM) should be applied to a target AnnData without retraining, and clustering quality (ARI) and batch mixing (kBET) must be benchmarked.
skills.name: cross-species-scrna-seq-integration
skills.search_text: cross-species-scrna-seq-integration Use when integrating single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different tissues or species where a pretrained embedding model (scETM) should be applied to a target AnnData without retraining, and clustering quality (ARI) and batch mixing (kBET) must be benchmarked. Source and target gene sets are unaligned (different/heterologous gene lists) — use prepare_for_transfer plus fine-tuning instead of zero-shot transfer The task requires a single integrated embedding from joint training on all batches rather than transfer of a pretrained encoder The target data require correcting multiple categorical batch variables or numerical covariates like subject age directly — scETM only handles a single categorical batch variable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Zero-shot transfer learning of a pretrained scETM model from a source scRNA-seq dataset to a cross-tissue or cross-species target dataset (e.g. MusMOp→HumM1C brain, TM(FACS)↔MP pancreas), evaluating transferred cell embeddings with ARI and kBET against scVI baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Zero-shot transfer learning of a pretrained scETM model from a source scRNA-seq dataset to a cross-tissue or cross-species target dataset (e.g. MusMOp→HumM1C brain, TM(FACS)↔MP pancreas), evaluating transferred cell embeddings with ARI and kBET against scVI baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target gene sets are unaligned (different/heterologous gene lists) — use prepare_for_transfer plus fine-tuning instead of zero-shot transfer The task requires a single integrated embedding from joint training on all batches rather than transfer of a pretrained encoder The target data require correcting multiple categorical batch variables or numerical covariates like subject age directly — scETM only handles a single categorical batch variable

skills.description: Use when the goal is to derive or validate species-level 'universal' senescence gene panels from SenePy's 72 mouse / 64 human cell-type signatures, or to compare a derived merged panel against the distributed Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt references.
skills.name: cross-species-senescence-signature-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-species-senescence-signature-comparison Use when the goal is to derive or validate species-level 'universal' senescence gene panels from SenePy's 72 mouse / 64 human cell-type signatures, or to compare a derived merged panel against the distributed Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt references. The goal is tissue-specific (e.g., Lung-only) merging with a hard overlap_threshold rather than a species-wide universal panel with a permutation-based threshold. The input is a raw single-cell AnnData to be scored for senescence — use score_hub on an existing signature instead of re-deriving one. Only the gene lists without weights are needed and the distributed Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt files already suffice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces SenePy's universal senescence gene panels by merging all cell-type-specific signatures per species with a permutation-based overrepresentation threshold (FDR p-value < 0.01), yielding 635 universal mouse and 734 universal human genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Reproduces SenePy's universal senescence gene panels by merging all cell-type-specific signatures per species with a permutation-based overrepresentation threshold (FDR p-value < 0.01), yielding 635 universal mouse and 734 universal human genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is tissue-specific (e.g., Lung-only) merging with a hard overlap_threshold rather than a species-wide universal panel with a permutation-based threshold. The input is a raw single-cell AnnData to be scored for senescence — use score_hub on an existing signature instead of re-deriving one. Only the gene lists without weights are needed and the distributed Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt files already suffice.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression matrices from two or more plant species and need to test whether homologous cell types co-embed after integration using orthologous genes as anchors.
skills.name: cross-species-single-cell-integration
skills.search_text: cross-species-single-cell-integration Use when you have scRNA-seq expression matrices from two or more plant species and need to test whether homologous cell types co-embed after integration using orthologous genes as anchors. You are analyzing a single species dataset — crossSpecies_integrate requires multiple species matrices anchored on orthologous genes Your goal is within-species dataset integration/batch correction of replicates rather than cross-species cell-identity comparison You need cell-type-specific gene regulatory network construction or trajectory inference — use scPlant's MINI-EX/pySCENIC or RunMonocle2/RunMonocle3/RunSlingshot modules instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrates plant single-cell transcriptomic datasets from multiple species (e.g., Arabidopsis, rice, maize roots) using scPlant::crossSpecies_integrate, which anchors datasets on one-to-one orthologous genes, SCTransform-normalizes each dataset, and integrates via CCA/RPCA in the Seurat framework to test whether cell identities are preserved across species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Integrates plant single-cell transcriptomic datasets from multiple species (e.g., Arabidopsis, rice, maize roots) using scPlant::crossSpecies_integrate, which anchors datasets on one-to-one orthologous genes, SCTransform-normalizes each dataset, and integrates via CCA/RPCA in the Seurat framework to test whether cell identities are preserved across species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are analyzing a single species dataset — crossSpecies_integrate requires multiple species matrices anchored on orthologous genes Your goal is within-species dataset integration/batch correction of replicates rather than cross-species cell-identity comparison You need cell-type-specific gene regulatory network construction or trajectory inference — use scPlant's MINI-EX/pySCENIC or RunMonocle2/RunMonocle3/RunSlingshot modules instead

skills.description: Use when query scRNA-seq datasets from two or more biological groups (e.g., Ctrl vs RPL decidual immune cells) have been projected onto a shared reference atlas and you need to compare cell-type label composition across groups.
skills.name: cross-study-cell-type-annotation-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-study-cell-type-annotation-comparison Use when query scRNA-seq datasets from two or more biological groups (e.g., Ctrl vs RPL decidual immune cells) have been projected onto a shared reference atlas and you need to compare cell-type label composition across groups. skills.summary: Compares predicted cell-type compositions across conditions (e.g., healthy controls vs RPL patients) after transferring reference labels onto mapped query cells, to test whether a disease state shifts cell population abundances relative to a reference atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel states absent in the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, so unsupervised clustering should be compared to mapping results instead of trusting transferred labels for cross-group comparison The query has not been quality-filtered by mapping metrics — low-quality mapped cells (high mean.knn.dist) will distort compositional comparisons across groups Cross-platform projection where performance declines (e.g., Smart-seq2 to 10x) — transferred labels may be too unreliable for quantitative composition comparison

skills.description: Use when you have expression data from multiple independent studies/cohorts (possibly across species) and need to test whether a shared reference annotation, rather than batch/study/species identity, drives transcriptional clustering.
skills.name: cross-study-clustering-meta-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-study-clustering-meta-analysis Use when you have expression data from multiple independent studies/cohorts (possibly across species) and need to test whether a shared reference annotation, rather than batch/study/species identity, drives transcriptional clustering. The reference atlas does not contain the cell types of interest — e.g. gamma-delta T cells 'were not represented at all' and CD4+ TILs were under-represented compared to CD8+ in the atlases The goal is a de novo unsupervised clustering of the query data without a stable annotated reference system of coordinates You need to alter or re-integrate the reference space with the query rather than embed queries without altering the reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A reference-based meta-analysis strategy in which subtype-study averaged expression profiles from multiple independent scRNA-seq cohorts are projected onto a common reference atlas and clustered, testing whether profiles co-cluster by reference cell subtype rather than by study, cohort, cancer type, or species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: A reference-based meta-analysis strategy in which subtype-study averaged expression profiles from multiple independent scRNA-seq cohorts are projected onto a common reference atlas and clustered, testing whether profiles co-cluster by reference cell subtype rather than by study, cohort, cancer type, or species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference atlas does not contain the cell types of interest — e.g. gamma-delta T cells 'were not represented at all' and CD4+ TILs were under-represented compared to CD8+ in the atlases The goal is a de novo unsupervised clustering of the query data without a stable annotated reference system of coordinates You need to alter or re-integrate the reference space with the query rather than embed queries without altering the reference

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-level collapsed intensity matrix from multiple microarray studies (e.g. GEO-derived 3T3-L1 arrays) and need comparable, log-scale normalized expression across arrays/studies.
skills.name: cross-study-expression-normalization
skills.search_text: cross-study-expression-normalization Use when you have a gene-level collapsed intensity matrix from multiple microarray studies (e.g. GEO-derived 3T3-L1 arrays) and need comparable, log-scale normalized expression across arrays/studies. Input is raw probe-level intensities that have not yet been collapsed to gene symbols (collapseRows must run first) Input is RNA-seq count data (e.g. the curatedAdipoRNA dataset), which follows a different pre-processing workflow Goal is removing known batch effects such as data series or platform — that is a separate downstream step done with sva, not this normalization skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Filters missing/low-intensity genes (< 10) from the collapsed gene-level microarray intensity matrix, log2-transforms the intensities, and normalizes them across arrays and studies with limma so intensity distributions are comparable in the curated 3T3-L1 (curatedAdipoArray) datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Filters missing/low-intensity genes (< 10) from the collapsed gene-level microarray intensity matrix, log2-transforms the intensities, and normalizes them across arrays and studies with limma so intensity distributions are comparable in the curated 3T3-L1 (curatedAdipoArray) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw probe-level intensities that have not yet been collapsed to gene symbols (collapseRows must run first) Input is RNA-seq count data (e.g. the curatedAdipoRNA dataset), which follows a different pre-processing workflow Goal is removing known batch effects such as data series or platform — that is a separate downstream step done with sva, not this normalization skill

skills.description: Use when a classifier trained on one scRNA-seq study must predict labels on an independent dataset (different platform/study), since the two count matrices typically contain different gene sets that must first be normalized and intersected.
skills.name: cross-study-gene-overlap-normalization
skills.search_text: cross-study-gene-overlap-normalization Use when a classifier trained on one scRNA-seq study must predict labels on an independent dataset (different platform/study), since the two count matrices typically contain different gene sets that must first be normalized and intersected. When training and testing data come from the same study with identical gene panels and no cross-platform gene-set mismatch exists When no labeled reference/training data exist — unsupervised approaches are the only viable solution in that setting When the new sample likely contains cell types absent from the reference; NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A preprocessing skill for supervised cross-study scRNA-seq label transfer (e.g., NeuCA on Baron/Muraro/Seg/Xin pancreas data) in which each train/test pair's expression matrices are normalized and both objects subset to the genes shared between studies, so the classifier and the queries live in a common feature space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: A preprocessing skill for supervised cross-study scRNA-seq label transfer (e.g., NeuCA on Baron/Muraro/Seg/Xin pancreas data) in which each train/test pair's expression matrices are normalized and both objects subset to the genes shared between studies, so the classifier and the queries live in a common feature space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When training and testing data come from the same study with identical gene panels and no cross-platform gene-set mismatch exists When no labeled reference/training data exist — unsupervised approaches are the only viable solution in that setting When the new sample likely contains cell types absent from the reference; NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data

skills.description: Use when an interpretable latent-space model (e.g., VEGA) has been trained on one single-cell study and you must quantify generalization to held-out cell types/conditions or to a completely unseen second study.
skills.name: cross-study-generalization-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-study-generalization-evaluation Use when an interpretable latent-space model (e.g., VEGA) has been trained on one single-cell study and you must quantify generalization to held-out cell types/conditions or to a completely unseen second study. The dataset was seen fully during training — this skill only applies to out-of-sample (held-out or unseen-study) inference You need maximal generative/predictive accuracy rather than interpretable module activity: VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices generative capacity for interpretability The gene module annotation (e.g., MSigDB) is unavailable or your genes are largely unannotated, since hard-coded decoder connections cannot correct incomplete prior knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Evaluates whether a VEGA-trained interpretable VAE generalizes out-of-sample by inferring gene module variable (GMV) activities for held-out cell type/condition pairs and for an entirely unseen second PBMC study (Kang vs. Zheng), quantified via top-50 differential GMV overlap and reconstruction R2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a VEGA-trained interpretable VAE generalizes out-of-sample by inferring gene module variable (GMV) activities for held-out cell type/condition pairs and for an entirely unseen second PBMC study (Kang vs. Zheng), quantified via top-50 differential GMV overlap and reconstruction R2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset was seen fully during training — this skill only applies to out-of-sample (held-out or unseen-study) inference You need maximal generative/predictive accuracy rather than interpretable module activity: VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices generative capacity for interpretability The gene module annotation (e.g., MSigDB) is unavailable or your genes are largely unannotated, since hard-coded decoder connections cannot correct incomplete prior knowledge

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a subsampled scRNA-seq sketch (e.g. 10% scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, via CellHint harmonization trees built from .h5ad inputs with X_pca representations.
skills.name: cross-study-label-harmonization-with-cellhint
skills.search_text: cross-study-label-harmonization-with-cellhint Use when evaluating whether a subsampled scRNA-seq sketch (e.g. 10% scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, via CellHint harmonization trees built from .h5ad inputs with X_pca representations. The goal is direct cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g. CellTypist, scANVI, ACTINN cell-type-assignment tasks) rather than preserving inter-study subtype relationship structure — the paper evaluates those as separate benchmark tasks The dataset is small enough to run CellHint on all cells, making sketching unnecessary and the tree-agreement comparison moot Cell type labels lack the fine-grained T-cell subtype structure needed for a meaningful subtype relationship tree (e.g. only a handful of coarse labels) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs CellHint cross-study label harmonization on scRNA-seq sketches (e.g. a 10% scValue sketch of the 200k-cell human Spleen dataset) to build T-cell subtype relationship trees, then compares each method's tree against the full-data reference tree to judge how well a subsampling method preserves fine-grained cell-type structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Runs CellHint cross-study label harmonization on scRNA-seq sketches (e.g. a 10% scValue sketch of the 200k-cell human Spleen dataset) to build T-cell subtype relationship trees, then compares each method's tree against the full-data reference tree to judge how well a subsampling method preserves fine-grained cell-type structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is direct cell-type annotation accuracy (e.g. CellTypist, scANVI, ACTINN cell-type-assignment tasks) rather than preserving inter-study subtype relationship structure — the paper evaluates those as separate benchmark tasks The dataset is small enough to run CellHint on all cells, making sketching unnecessary and the tree-agreement comparison moot Cell type labels lack the fine-grained T-cell subtype structure needed for a meaningful subtype relationship tree (e.g. only a handful of coarse labels)

skills.description: Use when a specific gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') is given and the goal is to find which annotated cell types specifically express it across multiple imported single-cell studies in Cellenium's integrated database.
skills.name: cross-study-marker-gene-search
skills.search_text: cross-study-marker-gene-search Use when a specific gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') is given and the goal is to find which annotated cell types specifically express it across multiple imported single-cell studies in Cellenium's integrated database. The single-cell study lacks precalculated differential expression results per annotated cell cluster — Cellenium requires DE values, a UMAP projection and other study data prepared by the data_import notebooks before ingestion A quantitative cross-study meta-analysis with significance thresholds is required — Cellenium's marker search supports only qualitative cross-study comparison of gene expression Only a single study is involved and a within-study differentially expressed gene lookup suffices, rather than a cross-study marker search http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce Cellenium's cross-study marker gene search: query the PostgreSQL/GraphQL single-cell study backend for a gene of interest (e.g. insulin), rank annotated cell types by differential-expression marker statistics within each study, and aggregate per-study rankings to identify cell types consistently specific for that gene (paper use-case 3 expected result: pancreatic beta-cells for insulin). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Reproduce Cellenium's cross-study marker gene search: query the PostgreSQL/GraphQL single-cell study backend for a gene of interest (e.g. insulin), rank annotated cell types by differential-expression marker statistics within each study, and aggregate per-study rankings to identify cell types consistently specific for that gene (paper use-case 3 expected result: pancreatic beta-cells for insulin).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The single-cell study lacks precalculated differential expression results per annotated cell cluster — Cellenium requires DE values, a UMAP projection and other study data prepared by the data_import notebooks before ingestion A quantitative cross-study meta-analysis with significance thresholds is required — Cellenium's marker search supports only qualitative cross-study comparison of gene expression Only a single study is involved and a within-study differentially expressed gene lookup suffices, rather than a cross-study marker search

skills.description: Use when aggregating metadata from multiple public datasets (e.g., GEO series) whose experimental designs are described inconsistently, and you need a unified vocabulary to compare or pool samples across studies.
skills.name: cross-study-metadata-vocabulary-harmonization
skills.search_text: cross-study-metadata-vocabulary-harmonization Use when aggregating metadata from multiple public datasets (e.g., GEO series) whose experimental designs are described inconsistently, and you need a unified vocabulary to compare or pool samples across studies. The input is a single-study dataset whose metadata already uses consistent terminology — no cross-study harmonization is needed. The input is RNA-seq or ChIP-seq data (e.g., the curatedAdipoRNA or curatedAdipoChIP resources), which follow their own collection and pre-processing pipelines rather than this microarray metadata curation. The task is numerical processing of probe intensities (collapsing, normalization, batch-effect removal) rather than metadata curation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Homogenizes study, series, and sample metadata harvested from multiple public GEO microarray studies (here, 3T3-L1/MDI-induced adipocyte datasets) using a unified vocabulary so samples can be consistently classified as none, genetically modified, or pharmacologically modified. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Homogenizes study, series, and sample metadata harvested from multiple public GEO microarray studies (here, 3T3-L1/MDI-induced adipocyte datasets) using a unified vocabulary so samples can be consistently classified as none, genetically modified, or pharmacologically modified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-study dataset whose metadata already uses consistent terminology — no cross-study harmonization is needed. The input is RNA-seq or ChIP-seq data (e.g., the curatedAdipoRNA or curatedAdipoChIP resources), which follow their own collection and pre-processing pipelines rather than this microarray metadata curation. The task is numerical processing of probe intensities (collapsing, normalization, batch-effect removal) rather than metadata curation.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known labels from one study and need to annotate cells from a different, independently collected study of the same tissue (inter-study annotation), or to benchmark label-assignment methods.
skills.name: cross-study-scrna-seq-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-study-scrna-seq-annotation-benchmarking Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known labels from one study and need to annotate cells from a different, independently collected study of the same tissue (inter-study annotation), or to benchmark label-assignment methods. The new sample contains cell types (e.g., malignant or novel cells) not present in the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue type of interest — unsupervised clustering is the only viable option in that case Unknown cell types are expected but not a priori identifiable — pre-screen with tools for rare/unknown cell identification or expert consultation before applying NeuCA http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark supervised cell label assignment (NeuCA vs scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) on FACS-sorted PBMC datasets by training on one study and testing on an independently collected one, quantifying annotation accuracy per method per train/test combination. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Benchmark supervised cell label assignment (NeuCA vs scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) on FACS-sorted PBMC datasets by training on one study and testing on an independently collected one, quantifying annotation accuracy per method per train/test combination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample contains cell types (e.g., malignant or novel cells) not present in the reference/training data — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue type of interest — unsupervised clustering is the only viable option in that case Unknown cell types are expected but not a priori identifiable — pre-screen with tools for rare/unknown cell identification or expert consultation before applying NeuCA

skills.description: Use when you have a DEGGs subnetworks object built over multiple subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 and BRCA_LumA from TCGA-BRCA) and need each subgroup's network restricted to interactions not significant in all groups.
skills.name: cross-subgroup-network-edge-intersection
skills.search_text: cross-subgroup-network-edge-intersection Use when you have a DEGGs subnetworks object built over multiple subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 and BRCA_LumA from TCGA-BRCA) and need each subgroup's network restricted to interactions not significant in all groups. The analysis goal is the set of interactions shared across all groups (the intersection itself) rather than the group-specific remainder after removing them Data are multi-omic — use the successor multiDEGGs package (get_multiOmics_diffNetworks) instead, since the DEGGs repository is no longer maintained and has been moved and significantly expanded into multiDEGGs Input is raw counts or a single subgroup only — the common-edge removal requires normalised counts and at least two subgroups in the subnetworks_object http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Identifies gene-gene interactions that are significant in every phenotypical subgroup produced by DEGGs' generate_subnetworks and removes them, retaining only group-specific (non-common) links per subgroup. This implements DEGGs' second filtering step, which drops links shared across all user-defined groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad192
skills.summary: Identifies gene-gene interactions that are significant in every phenotypical subgroup produced by DEGGs' generate_subnetworks and removes them, retaining only group-specific (non-common) links per subgroup. This implements DEGGs' second filtering step, which drops links shared across all user-defined groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is the set of interactions shared across all groups (the intersection itself) rather than the group-specific remainder after removing them Data are multi-omic — use the successor multiDEGGs package (get_multiOmics_diffNetworks) instead, since the DEGGs repository is no longer maintained and has been moved and significantly expanded into multiDEGGs Input is raw counts or a single subgroup only — the common-edge removal requires normalised counts and at least two subgroups in the subnetworks_object

skills.description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq cell type proportions with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, and gene weights must reflect cross-subject consistency rather than pre-selected marker genes.
skills.name: cross-subject-gene-weighting
skills.search_text: cross-subject-gene-weighting Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq cell type proportions with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, and gene weights must reflect cross-subject consistency rather than pre-selected marker genes. Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input Only pre-selected marker genes are available or the reference lacks multiple subjects per cell type, so cross-subject variance cannot be estimated Bulk samples come from clinical conditions very different from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2 instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 MuSiC's weighting scheme for weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution, which uses cross-subject variance of cell-type-specific relative gene abundance from a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference to up-weight genes consistent across subjects and down-weight non-informative, highly variable genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: MuSiC's weighting scheme for weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution, which uses cross-subject variance of cell-type-specific relative gene abundance from a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference to up-weight genes consistent across subjects and down-weight non-informative, highly variable genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input Only pre-selected marker genes are available or the reference lacks multiple subjects per cell type, so cross-subject variance cannot be estimated Bulk samples come from clinical conditions very different from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2 instead

skills.description: Use when the same curated PDAC bulk expression samples must be labeled under multiple published subtype schemes (Moffitt, Collisson, Bailey) to measure pairwise overlap between analogous subtypes.
skills.name: cross-subtyping-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-subtyping-concordance-analysis Use when the same curated PDAC bulk expression samples must be labeled under multiple published subtype schemes (Moffitt, Collisson, Bailey) to measure pairwise overlap between analogous subtypes. The goal is single-sample subtype classification rather than comparing schemes across a cohort — use the PurIST classifier instead of re-clustering with ConsensusClusterPlus. The expression matrix contains non-PDAC or low-purity cases that were not filtered (e.g. unfiltered TCGA-PAAD with 182 samples) — subtype signature derivation or validation will be misleading. Input is single-cell data; pdacR datasets are bulk analyses that limit the ability to fully separate cellular populations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives PDAC subtype calls for the same bulk expression samples under the Moffitt (basal-like/classical), Collisson (classical/QM/exocrine), and Bailey (progenitor/squamous/ADEX/immunogenic) schemes, then cross-tabulates analogous subtypes to quantify concordance (~60% overlap between analogous calls). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Derives PDAC subtype calls for the same bulk expression samples under the Moffitt (basal-like/classical), Collisson (classical/QM/exocrine), and Bailey (progenitor/squamous/ADEX/immunogenic) schemes, then cross-tabulates analogous subtypes to quantify concordance (~60% overlap between analogous calls).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-sample subtype classification rather than comparing schemes across a cohort — use the PurIST classifier instead of re-clustering with ConsensusClusterPlus. The expression matrix contains non-PDAC or low-purity cases that were not filtered (e.g. unfiltered TCGA-PAAD with 182 samples) — subtype signature derivation or validation will be misleading. Input is single-cell data; pdacR datasets are bulk analyses that limit the ability to fully separate cellular populations.

skills.description: Use when query scRNA-seq data from multiple sequencing technologies/protocols must be mapped onto a shared reference atlas and you need to quantify batch-effect correction with a cell-type mixing metric such as LISI.
skills.name: cross-technology-scrnaseq-benchmarking
skills.search_text: cross-technology-scrnaseq-benchmarking Use when query scRNA-seq data from multiple sequencing technologies/protocols must be mapped onto a shared reference atlas and you need to quantify batch-effect correction with a cell-type mixing metric such as LISI. The query contains novel cell states absent from the reference — projections from a fixed model may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first The query and reference come from drastically different platforms (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with integration-dependent mappers — ProjectSVR's integration-agnostic formulation is the point of this benchmark, not a generic integration workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 Benchmarks reference mapping of scRNA-seq query cells generated by different 10x protocols (3'v1, 3'v2, 5') onto a pre-built reference atlas, quantifying whether the mapper corrects platform-specific batch effects via LISI before/after projection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Benchmarks reference mapping of scRNA-seq query cells generated by different 10x protocols (3'v1, 3'v2, 5') onto a pre-built reference atlas, quantifying whether the mapper corrects platform-specific batch effects via LISI before/after projection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query contains novel cell states absent from the reference — projections from a fixed model may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first The query and reference come from drastically different platforms (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with integration-dependent mappers — ProjectSVR's integration-agnostic formulation is the point of this benchmark, not a generic integration workflow

skills.description: Use when you have per-subject, per-time-point community label predictions from a MuDCoD fit on donor-specific scRNA-seq networks and need a cross-time module-persistence score per donor, stratified by a donor-level phenotype such as differentiation efficiency.
skills.name: cross-time-module-similarity-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-time-module-similarity-analysis Use when you have per-subject, per-time-point community label predictions from a MuDCoD fit on donor-specific scRNA-seq networks and need a cross-time module-persistence score per donor, stratified by a donor-level phenotype such as differentiation efficiency. You have not yet run MuDCoD fit_predict — no community label vectors exist to compare, so run the community detection skill first. Your networks come from a single subject or a single time point — MuDCoD and this NMI contrast are designed for multi-subject, multi-time-point personalized dynamic networks. You need an exact numeric threshold test against the paper — the paper reports no numeric NMI cutoff, so only the qualitative ordering (low-efficiency > high-efficiency cross-time NMI) is an acceptance criterion, not a score gate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how much a donor's gene co-expression modules persist across time points by computing normalized mutual information (NMI) between the donor's community label vectors at two time points (e.g., day 30 vs day 52) from MuDCoD fit_predict output, then contrasting NMI across donor differentiation-efficiency groups to reproduce the Fig. 5b pattern. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Quantifies how much a donor's gene co-expression modules persist across time points by computing normalized mutual information (NMI) between the donor's community label vectors at two time points (e.g., day 30 vs day 52) from MuDCoD fit_predict output, then contrasting NMI across donor differentiation-efficiency groups to reproduce the Fig. 5b pattern.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet run MuDCoD fit_predict — no community label vectors exist to compare, so run the community detection skill first. Your networks come from a single subject or a single time point — MuDCoD and this NMI contrast are designed for multi-subject, multi-time-point personalized dynamic networks. You need an exact numeric threshold test against the paper — the paper reports no numeric NMI cutoff, so only the qualitative ordering (low-efficiency > high-efficiency cross-time NMI) is an acceptance criterion, not a score gate.

skills.description: Use when you have labeled scRNA-seq data at an initial time point (t0) and unlabeled expression data at a later time point (t1) from the same study, and you need to assign cell-type labels to the t1 cells (e.g., pre- vs post-treatment samples).
skills.name: cross-timepoint-cell-annotation
skills.search_text: cross-timepoint-cell-annotation Use when you have labeled scRNA-seq data at an initial time point (t0) and unlabeled expression data at a later time point (t1) from the same study, and you need to assign cell-type labels to the t1 cells (e.g., pre- vs post-treatment samples). The initial time point's data is dramatically different from the later time point's data — the neural network would fail to borrow useful information and could not be trained well. You only have a single time point (cross-sectional data) with no t0/t1 split — standard supervised annotation tools or unsupervised clustering apply instead. You want to detect cell types absent from the t0 label set as part of annotation — that requires the separate DetectNovelCells pipeline (corr.cutoff=0.4, p.cutoff=0.01), since the classifier only assigns known t0 labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CASi's cross-timepoint cell annotation trains a Keras/TensorFlow neural network on labeled cells from an initial time point (t0) and transfers those labels to scRNA-seq cells from later time points (t1), borrowing information from earlier data in a stepwise fashion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: CASi's cross-timepoint cell annotation trains a Keras/TensorFlow neural network on labeled cells from an initial time point (t0) and transfers those labels to scRNA-seq cells from later time points (t1), borrowing information from earlier data in a stepwise fashion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The initial time point's data is dramatically different from the later time point's data — the neural network would fail to borrow useful information and could not be trained well. You only have a single time point (cross-sectional data) with no t0/t1 split — standard supervised annotation tools or unsupervised clustering apply instead. You want to detect cell types absent from the t0 label set as part of annotation — that requires the separate DetectNovelCells pipeline (corr.cutoff=0.4, p.cutoff=0.01), since the classifier only assigns known t0 labels.

skills.description: Use when you have .results.mrsd.txt scores for multiple GTEx-derived biosamples and a one-per-line gene list (GENCODE v19 symbols/Ensembl IDs), and need to determine which genes/variants are assayable or low-MRSD (≤100 M reads) in at least one tissue.
skills.name: cross-tissue-biosample-suitability-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-tissue-biosample-suitability-analysis Use when you have .results.mrsd.txt scores for multiple GTEx-derived biosamples and a one-per-line gene list (GENCODE v19 symbols/Ensembl IDs), and need to determine which genes/variants are assayable or low-MRSD (≤100 M reads) in at least one tissue. Input RNA-seq uses non-Illumina, non-poly-A-enrichment, long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved protocols — pre-computed MRSD scores are only accurate for similar Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A workflows and no control datasets exist for other modalities The goal is detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the article explicitly states the MRSD model cannot be directly extended to these tasks The disease is associated with widespread transcriptomic change (e.g., interferonopathies, spliceosome disruption) or gene expression is modified by eQTLs/sQTLs — MRSD predictions may not reflect coverage in such genomic backgrounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies whether an RNA-seq biosample (whole blood, LCL, skeletal muscle, or cultured fibroblast) can assay splicing aberrations in a gene of interest, by joining per-gene MRSD scores computed with MRSDexplorer.py against a gene list (e.g., SpliceAI-prioritized ClinVar VUS-harboring genes) and flagging genes with MRSD ≤ 100 million reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Quantifies whether an RNA-seq biosample (whole blood, LCL, skeletal muscle, or cultured fibroblast) can assay splicing aberrations in a gene of interest, by joining per-gene MRSD scores computed with MRSDexplorer.py against a gene list (e.g., SpliceAI-prioritized ClinVar VUS-harboring genes) and flagging genes with MRSD ≤ 100 million reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input RNA-seq uses non-Illumina, non-poly-A-enrichment, long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved protocols — pre-computed MRSD scores are only accurate for similar Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A workflows and no control datasets exist for other modalities The goal is detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the article explicitly states the MRSD model cannot be directly extended to these tasks The disease is associated with widespread transcriptomic change (e.g., interferonopathies, spliceosome disruption) or gene expression is modified by eQTLs/sQTLs — MRSD predictions may not reflect coverage in such genomic backgrounds

skills.description: Use when per-tissue MRSD score tables (*.results.mrsd.txt) are available for two or more biosamples and you must rank tissues by the fraction of low-MRSD genes within a gene panel.
skills.name: cross-tissue-gene-coverage-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-tissue-gene-coverage-comparison Use when per-tissue MRSD score tables (*.results.mrsd.txt) are available for two or more biosamples and you must rank tissues by the fraction of low-MRSD genes within a gene panel. The goal is suitability for differential expression or isoform-imbalance analysis — the article states suitability for these applications is not quantified or proven The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved — the MRSD model is validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment workflows Sample IDs mismatch between the *.junc-counts.txt and *.seq-depths.txt files — such samples are excluded from MRSD calculation, so downstream tissue comparison would be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares per-tissue MRSD scores (in millions of reads) across multiple RNA-seq biosamples to classify genes as low-MRSD (<100 M reads) and select the optimal RNA source per disease gene panel.
