skills.search_text: cross-validation-hyperparameter-stability Use when training a classifier on a small labelled gene set (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs from CGC) where overfitting risk is high and hyper-parameters must be estimated stably before predictions are trusted. When a large labelled training set is available and simple grid-search CV suffices without stability checks When the input is raw somatic mutation data that has not yet been converted into the 37-feature matrix (use feature-matrix construction first) When the goal is driver-gene prediction on unlabelled genes rather than model training and hyper-parameter validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A protocol for avoiding overfitting when training random-forest classifiers on small labelled gene sets (136 TSGs, 76 OGs) by combining fivefold cross-validation with multiple random iterations to identify a stable hyper-parameter set, as used to train the cTaG pan-cancer model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: A protocol for avoiding overfitting when training random-forest classifiers on small labelled gene sets (136 TSGs, 76 OGs) by combining fivefold cross-validation with multiple random iterations to identify a stable hyper-parameter set, as used to train the cTaG pan-cancer model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a large labelled training set is available and simple grid-search CV suffices without stability checks When the input is raw somatic mutation data that has not yet been converted into the 37-feature matrix (use feature-matrix construction first) When the goal is driver-gene prediction on unlabelled genes rather than model training and hyper-parameter validation

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a cancer driver gene prediction model on directed gene regulatory networks (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) with multi-omics gene features and you need 5-fold CV metrics (AUPRC, AUROC, accuracy) comparable to graph-based baselines.
skills.name: cross-validation-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-validation-model-evaluation Use when benchmarking a cancer driver gene prediction model on directed gene regulatory networks (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) with multi-omics gene features and you need 5-fold CV metrics (AUPRC, AUROC, accuracy) comparable to graph-based baselines. The goal is patient-level prediction: DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which the authors note 'will ignore the specific characteristics of individual cancer patients' The GRN is undirected: the DGCN component specifically captures 'the directed information (i.e., regulation information)' from directed gene regulatory networks You need an undirected vanilla GCN baseline only — use EMOGI-style GCN pipelines instead of the DGCN+MLP joint model http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Runs 5-fold cross-validation of the DGMP directed-graph-convolution + MLP cancer driver gene classifier over driver/non-driver gene labels on directed GRNs, reporting per-gene class probabilities and mean CV accuracy for benchmarking against methods like EMOGI, NRFD, DeepWalk+SVM, PageRank, HotNet2, and MutSigCV. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Runs 5-fold cross-validation of the DGMP directed-graph-convolution + MLP cancer driver gene classifier over driver/non-driver gene labels on directed GRNs, reporting per-gene class probabilities and mean CV accuracy for benchmarking against methods like EMOGI, NRFD, DeepWalk+SVM, PageRank, HotNet2, and MutSigCV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is patient-level prediction: DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which the authors note 'will ignore the specific characteristics of individual cancer patients' The GRN is undirected: the DGCN component specifically captures 'the directed information (i.e., regulation information)' from directed gene regulatory networks You need an undirected vanilla GCN baseline only — use EMOGI-style GCN pipelines instead of the DGCN+MLP joint model

skills.description: Use when you need to train or robustness-test EmptyNN's PU-learning classifier over a grid of threshold T (50-400), cross-validation folds k (5-20), and iterations N (5-20) on raw droplet scRNA-seq count matrices.
skills.name: cross-validation-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: cross-validation-neural-network-training Use when you need to train or robustness-test EmptyNN's PU-learning classifier over a grid of threshold T (50-400), cross-validation folds k (5-20), and iterations N (5-20) on raw droplet scRNA-seq count matrices. The data are already filtered cell barcodes rather than a raw unfiltered count matrix — EmptyNN's set P/U logic requires the full droplet distribution You need ambient RNA correction of gene expression estimates — EmptyNN does not correct expression; an external tool such as SoupX is required Cell-containing droplets with very low total counts are expected (the low-count-equals-empty assumption breaks); the T threshold must be manually adjusted and this sweep alone will not resolve the bias Trains EmptyNN's PU-learning neural network (R/keras) over k-fold cross-validation with N repeated iterations to classify cell-free vs. cell-containing droplets, and supports robustness sweeps of threshold T, folds k, and iterations N against ground-truth AUROC benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Trains EmptyNN's PU-learning neural network (R/keras) over k-fold cross-validation with N repeated iterations to classify cell-free vs. cell-containing droplets, and supports robustness sweeps of threshold T, folds k, and iterations N against ground-truth AUROC benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already filtered cell barcodes rather than a raw unfiltered count matrix — EmptyNN's set P/U logic requires the full droplet distribution You need ambient RNA correction of gene expression estimates — EmptyNN does not correct expression; an external tool such as SoupX is required Cell-containing droplets with very low total counts are expected (the low-count-equals-empty assumption breaks); the T threshold must be manually adjusted and this sweep alone will not resolve the bias

The goal is predicting splicing status of scRNA-seq reads (that is the downstream forseti_predictor step, which consumes the fitted model, not builds it) The target model is the oligo(dT) primer binding affinity MLP trained on priming windows, not the fragment length distribution Input reads are single-end or lack empirical paired-end fragment lengths spanning the 1–1000 bp range needed to fit the spline http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Fit and validate the Forseti empirical cDNA fragment length distribution using a cubic spline over paired-end fragment lengths (1–1000 bp), then quantify generalizability via held-out test datasets and 5-fold cross-validation with RMSE metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Fit and validate the Forseti empirical cDNA fragment length distribution using a cubic spline over paired-end fragment lengths (1–1000 bp), then quantify generalizability via held-out test datasets and 5-fold cross-validation with RMSE metrics.

skills.description: Use when fitting FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation on single-cell data and needing to control model complexity via the diffusion step t, which must be tuned by cross-validation rather than set heuristically.
skills.name: cross-validation-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: cross-validation-parameter-selection Use when fitting FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation on single-cell data and needing to control model complexity via the diffusion step t, which must be tuned by cross-validation rather than set heuristically. Working with bulk RNA-seq, where the original ISMARA linear model applies without the single-cell data-diffusion regularization FateCompass adds. The analysis goal is estimating transition probabilities from RNA velocity or differentiation potential — this skill only regularizes the TF-activity linear model step. No expressed-gene/binding-site matrix is available, since the promoter/gene set must be splittable 80/20 for cross-validation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the data-diffusion regularization parameter t in FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation by sweeping candidate diffusion-operator powers, fitting the regularized model on an 80% promoter/gene training split, and choosing the t that minimizes held-out test MSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Selects the data-diffusion regularization parameter t in FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation by sweeping candidate diffusion-operator powers, fitting the regularized model on an 80% promoter/gene training split, and choosing the t that minimizes held-out test MSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with bulk RNA-seq, where the original ISMARA linear model applies without the single-cell data-diffusion regularization FateCompass adds. The analysis goal is estimating transition probabilities from RNA velocity or differentiation potential — this skill only regularizes the TF-activity linear model step. No expressed-gene/binding-site matrix is available, since the promoter/gene set must be splittable 80/20 for cross-validation.

skills.description: Use when you need to identify which sequence-position features (e.g., position-specific gapped k-mer descriptors on 41-nt RNA sequences) are consistently, not just incidentally, predictive across repeated cross-validation resampling.
skills.name: cross-validation-partitioned-feature-selection
skills.search_text: cross-validation-partitioned-feature-selection Use when you need to identify which sequence-position features (e.g., position-specific gapped k-mer descriptors on 41-nt RNA sequences) are consistently, not just incidentally, predictive across repeated cross-validation resampling. You already have a validated small feature subset and only need to train/evaluate the final classifier (use the Model.ipynb workflow instead). The question is predictive performance (accuracy/MCC) rather than feature stability — cross-validation evaluation experiments are the wrong vehicle for ranking consistency analysis. Sequences are not position-aligned (the descriptors are position-specific to the 41-nt window, so shifted or variable-length inputs break the pattern-position annotation). http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A stability-selection skill that trains mode-wise random-forest feature selectors on each training partition of a 5-times 5-fold cross-validation scheme, retains the top 400 position-specific features per selector, and intersects the 25 resulting feature sets to recover only the position-specific gapped k-mer features that are discriminative across every partition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: A stability-selection skill that trains mode-wise random-forest feature selectors on each training partition of a 5-times 5-fold cross-validation scheme, retains the top 400 position-specific features per selector, and intersects the 25 resulting feature sets to recover only the position-specific gapped k-mer features that are discriminative across every partition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a validated small feature subset and only need to train/evaluate the final classifier (use the Model.ipynb workflow instead). The question is predictive performance (accuracy/MCC) rather than feature stability — cross-validation evaluation experiments are the wrong vehicle for ranking consistency analysis. Sequences are not position-aligned (the descriptors are position-specific to the 41-nt window, so shifted or variable-length inputs break the pattern-position annotation).

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking a small-sample gene-classification model (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs labelled from CGC) and you need stable, class-wise performance metrics under k-fold cross-validation rather than a single train/test split.
skills.name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: cross-validation-performance-evaluation Use when reproducing or benchmarking a small-sample gene-classification model (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs labelled from CGC) and you need stable, class-wise performance metrics under k-fold cross-validation rather than a single train/test split. Input is already a model prediction or consensus output (e.g. the classified unlabelled genes) rather than the labelled 37-feature matrix — evaluation metrics cannot be computed without CGC TSG/OG ground-truth labels You are reproducing the Davoli et al. comparison — the paper notes their test set results have not been published, so test-set metric comparison is not possible for that baseline Feature values include Tokheim et al. data — missense and frameshift entropy and frequency features could not be calculated there, so the 37-feature protocol is not fully applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces the cTaG random-forest fivefold cross-validation protocol to estimate per-class accuracy, precision, recall and F1 for tumour suppressor gene (TSG) and oncogene (OG) classification over the 37-feature pan-cancer mutation feature matrix, using iterated hyper-parameter search to avoid overfitting on the small labelled gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Reproduces the cTaG random-forest fivefold cross-validation protocol to estimate per-class accuracy, precision, recall and F1 for tumour suppressor gene (TSG) and oncogene (OG) classification over the 37-feature pan-cancer mutation feature matrix, using iterated hyper-parameter search to avoid overfitting on the small labelled gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a model prediction or consensus output (e.g. the classified unlabelled genes) rather than the labelled 37-feature matrix — evaluation metrics cannot be computed without CGC TSG/OG ground-truth labels You are reproducing the Davoli et al. comparison — the paper notes their test set results have not been published, so test-set metric comparison is not possible for that baseline Feature values include Tokheim et al. data — missense and frameshift entropy and frequency features could not be calculated there, so the 37-feature protocol is not fully applicable

skills.search_text: cross-validation-performance-evaluation Use when validating an m5C site prediction model on a balanced training set (e.g., 5,298 pos/5,298 neg A. thaliana or 4,563 pos/4,563 neg M. musculus 41-bp sequences) and reporting 10-fold cross-validation metrics. Evaluating on the independent A. thaliana test set, where Staem5 was reported to be inferior to iRNA-m5C_SVM and m5CPred-SVM — this skill covers training-set cross-validation only Input is unbalanced or species data other than A. thaliana / M. musculus; the article notes it is difficult to develop a general cross-species model and species-specific models are required The input is already a table of encoded features and cross-validated predictions rather than raw FASTA sequences to be encoded and classified http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Reproduce Staem5's stacked m5C prediction model (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM base classifiers stacked with logistic regression) and evaluate it with 10-fold cross-validation using Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC metrics on the A. thaliana and M. musculus training sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Reproduce Staem5's stacked m5C prediction model (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM base classifiers stacked with logistic regression) and evaluate it with 10-fold cross-validation using Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC metrics on the A. thaliana and M. musculus training sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating on the independent A. thaliana test set, where Staem5 was reported to be inferior to iRNA-m5C_SVM and m5CPred-SVM — this skill covers training-set cross-validation only Input is unbalanced or species data other than A. thaliana / M. musculus; the article notes it is difficult to develop a general cross-species model and species-specific models are required The input is already a table of encoded features and cross-validated predictions rather than raw FASTA sequences to be encoded and classified

skills.search_text: cross-version-runtime-benchmarking Use when an updated tool version must be validated against its predecessor: run both on the same datasets, compare ranked outputs (Spearman of log p-values) and measure runtime savings. skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — singleCellHaystack cannot easily conduct such comparisons The goal is spatial transcriptomics DEG detection where speed is paramount — SPARK-X is the fastest method available and singleCellHaystack has relatively longer runtimes despite better sensitivity Only one tool version exists and no predecessor output is available for pairwise comparison

skills.name: crosslink-induced-truncation-quantification
skills.search_text: crosslink-induced-truncation-quantification Use when starting from eCLIP/STAMP IP and size-matched input BAM files and you need nucleotide-resolution crosslink signal (truncation/mutation events) rather than raw read coverage, e.g. to build Metatruncate objects for metagene plots. When the desired signal is total read-coverage density from BAM alignments rather than crosslink sites — use the metadensity.readdensity module instead of truncation quantification. When a pre-computed WIG signal track already exists, since Metadensity can load it directly to speed up computation instead of re-deriving events from BAMs. When inputs are not CLIP IP/input sequencing data (e.g. already aggregated feature tables); Metadensity expects BAM/BIGWIG CLIP files registered in a dataloader and manifest. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies per-nucleotide crosslink-induced truncations (CITs) and crosslink-induced mutations (CIMs) from CLIP BAM alignments using Metadensity's truncation module, producing a diagnostic-signal table per transcript that can be background-normalized against size-matched inputs for metagene analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac083
skills.summary: Quantifies per-nucleotide crosslink-induced truncations (CITs) and crosslink-induced mutations (CIMs) from CLIP BAM alignments using Metadensity's truncation module, producing a diagnostic-signal table per transcript that can be background-normalized against size-matched inputs for metagene analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the desired signal is total read-coverage density from BAM alignments rather than crosslink sites — use the metadensity.readdensity module instead of truncation quantification. When a pre-computed WIG signal track already exists, since Metadensity can load it directly to speed up computation instead of re-deriving events from BAMs. When inputs are not CLIP IP/input sequencing data (e.g. already aggregated feature tables); Metadensity expects BAM/BIGWIG CLIP files registered in a dataloader and manifest.

skills.name: crossmodal-generation-between-transcriptome-and-accessibility
skills.search_text: crossmodal-generation-between-transcriptome-and-accessibility Use when paired single-cell multiome data (e.g. SHARE-seq RNA + ATAC count matrices) are available and you need to predict gene expression from chromatin accessibility or vice versa, with a quantitative benchmark against GAM-based integration baselines. Data are unpaired single-cell transcriptome and accessibility measurements, so no cell-wise conditioning target exists for crossmodal generation The goal is only clustering or joint latent representation of multimodal data without generating one modality from the other Input is a precomputed gene activity matrix rather than raw per-peak accessibility counts, since the GAM is the baseline being compared against, not the input http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Train scMM, a mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder, on paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq raw counts (e.g. mouse skin SHARE-seq) and use it to bidirectionally generate one modality from the other, benchmarking against the conventional gene activity matrix (+2 kb upstream of TSS) baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Train scMM, a mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder, on paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq raw counts (e.g. mouse skin SHARE-seq) and use it to bidirectionally generate one modality from the other, benchmarking against the conventional gene activity matrix (+2 kb upstream of TSS) baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired single-cell transcriptome and accessibility measurements, so no cell-wise conditioning target exists for crossmodal generation The goal is only clustering or joint latent representation of multimodal data without generating one modality from the other Input is a precomputed gene activity matrix rather than raw per-peak accessibility counts, since the GAM is the baseline being compared against, not the input

skills.search_text: crossmodal-surface-protein-prediction Use when CITE-seq transcriptome counts are available for a new batch (e.g. BMNC) and you must predict surface protein levels for proteins shared with a pretrained scMM model, then compare against a Seurat baseline. skills.summary: Predicts surface protein abundance from transcriptome-only CITE-seq input using the pretrained scMM mixture-of-experts multimodal VAE, and benchmarks prediction quality against a Seurat anchor-based transfer baseline using per-protein Jaccard index (JI).

skills.search_text: cs-catalog-categorization-and-export Use when you have candidate 3' end cleavage site coordinates from scRNA-seq (e.g. Microwell-seq) and need to annotate them against GENCODE 3' ends and PolyASite clusters while removing internal-priming artifacts. Input is 10x Genomics data where most reads do not span the cleavage site — exact de novo CS mapping is not possible and this cataloging approach does not apply You only need gene-level or 3'UTR isoform quantification with an existing CS annotation — use scUTRquant directly rather than rebuilding the catalog Input sites have already been categorized against GENCODE/PolyASite — re-annotating duplicates work http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify de novo mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) called from Microwell-seq (MWS) data into validated/supported/likely categories relative to GENCODE and PolyASite annotations, and export the merged catalog as GTF/BED files that extend GENCODE CS annotations by ~40%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9

skills.description: Use when a per-cell scRNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes x n cells) must be converted to conditional cell-specific networks and a conditional gene set (hub genes) is needed to condition the gene-gene independence tests per cell.
skills.name: csn-hub-gene-selection
skills.search_text: csn-hub-gene-selection Use when a per-cell scRNA-seq gene expression matrix (m genes x n cells) must be converted to conditional cell-specific networks and a conditional gene set (hub genes) is needed to condition the gene-gene independence tests per cell. Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated expression without per-cell vectors — the conditional hub set is defined independently for each cell k The expression matrix is unnormalized/noisy raw counts, since rho_xy is estimated from the scatter of expression values and requires normalization first The goal is a single population-level gene-gene network rather than per-cell conditional networks (a plain CSN suffices, but it overestimates associations by including indirect ones) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the conditional gene set for c-CSN by building each cell's plain CSN with the rho_xy statistic, summing edge weights to each gene z via Equation (8) Dz(k), and taking the top G (G >= 1) largest-'importance' hub genes. These hubs define the conditioning variables under which direct gene-gene associations are tested, filtering indirect associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Selects the conditional gene set for c-CSN by building each cell's plain CSN with the rho_xy statistic, summing edge weights to each gene z via Equation (8) Dz(k), and taking the top G (G >= 1) largest-'importance' hub genes. These hubs define the conditioning variables under which direct gene-gene associations are tested, filtering indirect associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated expression without per-cell vectors — the conditional hub set is defined independently for each cell k The expression matrix is unnormalized/noisy raw counts, since rho_xy is estimated from the scatter of expression values and requires normalization first The goal is a single population-level gene-gene network rather than per-cell conditional networks (a plain CSN suffices, but it overestimates associations by including indirect ones)

skills.search_text: ct-connectivity-table-parsing Use when the available RNA secondary structure file is a CT/connectivity-table file (six columns after one header line) and you need to route it, paired with a Shannon entropy text file, into RSCanner for BPC and entropy scanning. The secondary structure input is a dot-bracket (FASTA) file — RSCanner routes that through RSCanner_dotbracket_shannon.R instead of the CT script. You lack a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list computed from base pairing probabilities; both RSCanner scripts require the structure file to be paired with one. You want a single-command multiple-input pipeline; RSCanner's command-line usage requires one structure file plus one entropy file per run of the appropriate script. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Parses an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) format together with a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list as input to RSCanner's CT-specific command-line script, which computes base pair content (BPC) and smoothed entropy via a centered sliding window. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Parses an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) format together with a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list as input to RSCanner's CT-specific command-line script, which computes base pair content (BPC) and smoothed entropy via a centered sliding window.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The secondary structure input is a dot-bracket (FASTA) file — RSCanner routes that through RSCanner_dotbracket_shannon.R instead of the CT script. You lack a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list computed from base pairing probabilities; both RSCanner scripts require the structure file to be paired with one. skills.description: Use when the input RNA secondary structure is provided in CT format (six columns after one header line) and per-nucleotide Shannon entropy is available as a two-column tab-delimited text file, and structural content visualization is needed.
skills.name: ct-format-file-processing

skills.description: Use when you have a cudaMMC output file (labeled with the -n flag, e.g. 'chr14_test') containing 3D coordinates of beads along the multiscale chromatin chain and need to produce a structural file (model.cif) readable by structure-aware tools.
skills.name: cudammc-simulation-output-parsing
skills.search_text: cudammc-simulation-output-parsing Use when you have a cudaMMC output file (labeled with the -n flag, e.g. 'chr14_test') containing 3D coordinates of beads along the multiscale chromatin chain and need to produce a structural file (model.cif) readable by structure-aware tools. The task requires legacy PDB-format output and the model contains more beads than PDB can represent — mmCIF is chosen precisely because PDB cannot hold the bead count of high-resolution whole chromosome models. The downstream analysis consumes raw ChIA-PET inputs (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) rather than a reconstructed 3D structure — those are cudaMMC inputs, not outputs to convert. You need to modify the simulation itself (e.g. use_motif_orientation, max_pet_length, subanchor heatmap settings) — that is configuration of cudaMMC, not parsing of its output. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parse the 3D bead-coordinate model output produced by a cudaMMC multiscale Monte Carlo simulation run and convert it into PDBx/mmCIF format, chosen over legacy PDB because mmCIF can represent a higher number of beads per structure, which is necessary for high-resolution whole chromosome models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Parse the 3D bead-coordinate model output produced by a cudaMMC multiscale Monte Carlo simulation run and convert it into PDBx/mmCIF format, chosen over legacy PDB because mmCIF can represent a higher number of beads per structure, which is necessary for high-resolution whole chromosome models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires legacy PDB-format output and the model contains more beads than PDB can represent — mmCIF is chosen precisely because PDB cannot hold the bead count of high-resolution whole chromosome models. The downstream analysis consumes raw ChIA-PET inputs (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) rather than a reconstructed 3D structure — those are cudaMMC inputs, not outputs to convert. You need to modify the simulation itself (e.g. use_motif_orientation, max_pet_length, subanchor heatmap settings) — that is configuration of cudaMMC, not parsing of its output.

skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up time to assess — the TSNP design cannot be applied directly in that setting The response outcome is not binary and not observable shortly after treatment initiation — the design is appropriate only for quickly observable binary responses The trial is a drug-combination study seeking an optimal dose combination — extending TSNP to combinations is explicitly future work, not yet done

skills.description: Use when comparing two sample groups' circRNA expression distributions quantified per-circRNA (e.g. FPBcirc or CIRCscore from CLEAR quant.txt outputs) to decide whether one metric better discriminates the groups.
skills.name: cumulative-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: cumulative-distribution-analysis Use when comparing two sample groups' circRNA expression distributions quantified per-circRNA (e.g. FPBcirc or CIRCscore from CLEAR quant.txt outputs) to decide whether one metric better discriminates the groups. Input data are poly(A)-/ribo- or RNase R-treated RNA-seq datasets, where linear RNAs are depleted and CIRCscore cannot be accurately computed The metric of interest is not a per-circRNA continuous quantity (e.g. already-aggregated per-sample summaries or categorical annotations) Only raw junction read counts are available without FPB normalization, since unnormalized counts confound library-size differences http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Builds cumulative distribution curves of circRNA expression metrics (FPBcirc or CIRCscore) across sample groups and applies two-tailed unpaired Student's t-tests to test whether a normalization metric separates conditions, e.g. HCC vs paired-normal liver samples from ribo- RNA-seq quantified with CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Builds cumulative distribution curves of circRNA expression metrics (FPBcirc or CIRCscore) across sample groups and applies two-tailed unpaired Student's t-tests to test whether a normalization metric separates conditions, e.g. HCC vs paired-normal liver samples from ribo- RNA-seq quantified with CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are poly(A)-/ribo- or RNase R-treated RNA-seq datasets, where linear RNAs are depleted and CIRCscore cannot be accurately computed The metric of interest is not a per-circRNA continuous quantity (e.g. already-aggregated per-sample summaries or categorical annotations) Only raw junction read counts are available without FPB normalization, since unnormalized counts confound library-size differences

skills.description: Use when you have an nx1 vector of pseudotime values from a trajectory-inference algorithm (Wanderlust, Diffusion Maps/DPT, Monocle) and independent prior knowledge of the cell density distribution on the desired real scale, and you need to convert pseudotime to true time or distance-from-surface.
skills.name: cumulative-distribution-function-matching
skills.search_text: cumulative-distribution-function-matching Use when you have an nx1 vector of pseudotime values from a trajectory-inference algorithm (Wanderlust, Diffusion Maps/DPT, Monocle) and independent prior knowledge of the cell density distribution on the desired real scale, and you need to convert pseudotime to true time or distance-from-surface. No reliable prior knowledge of the target real-scale distribution exists (e.g. stem-cell differentiation, where cell death and division rates at every stage would need to be measured) — the paper notes constructing such target distributions can be more challenging. The cell order from the trajectory-inference algorithm itself is unreliable — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order. Data are already on a meaningful real-time or real-space scale and do not require rescaling from pseudotime. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 A measure-preserving transformation (MAPiT) that maps arbitrary pseudotime values onto the true temporal or spatial scale by enforcing equality of the area under the density (cumulative distribution) curves at corresponding points, i.e. tau(s) = P_x^{-1}(P_s(s)). It converts abstract pseudotime orderings from trajectory-inference algorithms into interpretable real-scale values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: A measure-preserving transformation (MAPiT) that maps arbitrary pseudotime values onto the true temporal or spatial scale by enforcing equality of the area under the density (cumulative distribution) curves at corresponding points, i.e. tau(s) = P_x^{-1}(P_s(s)). It converts abstract pseudotime orderings from trajectory-inference algorithms into interpretable real-scale values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable prior knowledge of the target real-scale distribution exists (e.g. stem-cell differentiation, where cell death and division rates at every stage would need to be measured) — the paper notes constructing such target distributions can be more challenging. The cell order from the trajectory-inference algorithm itself is unreliable — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order. Data are already on a meaningful real-time or real-space scale and do not require rescaling from pseudotime.

The organism is a non-model microbe absent from OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, and TRRUST — no verified interactions can be retrieved The goal is de novo motif-based refinement only (TFBM discovery with MEME), not database interaction incorporation The input is raw count data rather than an already inferred GRN adjacency matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Refines an MI-inferred GRN by querying manually curated interaction databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) for verified regulatory interactions of the studied organism and merging them into the network with explicit conflict-resolution rules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013

skills.name: curated-pdac-geneset-handling
skills.search_text: curated-pdac-geneset-handling Use when analyzing public PDAC bulk RNA-seq/microarray data with curated subtype signatures (ADEX, Immunogenic, basal-like/classical) and you must avoid contaminating samples (e.g., TCGA-PAAD's 32 non-PDAC cases) or signature non-specificity. skills.description: Use when time-series scRNA-seq cells have been ordered along pseudotime (e.g. by Monocle3) and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose relative abundance changes significantly over the trajectory rather than across discrete time points.
skills.name: curve-fitting-along-pseudotime
skills.search_text: curve-fitting-along-pseudotime Use when time-series scRNA-seq cells have been ordered along pseudotime (e.g. by Monocle3) and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose relative abundance changes significantly over the trajectory rather than across discrete time points. Data are discrete-time-point bulk or pseudobulk comparisons without a trajectory-inferred pseudotime — the time-dependent covariate requires cells ordered along pseudotime Data have not been preprocessed (filtered/normalized) and you cannot run scTITANS 'full' mode with indication 'none' — the statistical test assumes appropriately filtered and scran-normalized expression The scientific question is differential expression between predefined conditions/groups rather than temporal variation along a trajectory — standard DE methods are the wrong model here http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 scTITANS' time-dependent covariate analysis: after Monocle3 pseudotime ordering, fit a curve for each gene's (or subcluster's cell-count) trajectory along pseudotime and test it against a flat-line null with an F statistic, bootstrapped p-values, and Storey-style q-values at FDR 0.01 to call time-varying genes and cell subclusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: scTITANS' time-dependent covariate analysis: after Monocle3 pseudotime ordering, fit a curve for each gene's (or subcluster's cell-count) trajectory along pseudotime and test it against a flat-line null with an F statistic, bootstrapped p-values, and Storey-style q-values at FDR 0.01 to call time-varying genes and cell subclusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are discrete-time-point bulk or pseudobulk comparisons without a trajectory-inferred pseudotime — the time-dependent covariate requires cells ordered along pseudotime Data have not been preprocessed (filtered/normalized) and you cannot run scTITANS 'full' mode with indication 'none' — the statistical test assumes appropriately filtered and scran-normalized expression The scientific question is differential expression between predefined conditions/groups rather than temporal variation along a trajectory — standard DE methods are the wrong model here

skills.description: Use when sequencing a single-cell scRNA-seq library whose barcode/UMI layout is not a default registered chemistry, and you must express the read structure as an explicit geometry string for mapping and quantification.
skills.name: custom-chemistry-geometry-configuration
skills.search_text: custom-chemistry-geometry-configuration Use when sequencing a single-cell scRNA-seq library whose barcode/UMI layout is not a default registered chemistry, and you must express the read structure as an explicit geometry string for mapping and quantification. The data is bulk RNA-seq or scATAC-seq, where piscem map-bulk/map-sc-atac and their barcode flags apply instead of the map-sc chemistry geometry The library is a standard registered chemistry (e.g. 10xv3) and no custom geometry encoding is needed — use the registered name directly rather than hand-writing a geometry string The barcode/UMI read structure is unknown; resolve the library layout first (e.g. via scg_lib_structs documentation) before guessing a geometry string http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configures simpleaf/alevin-fry single-cell quantification for non-default library layouts by supplying a custom barcode/UMI geometry string (e.g. 1{b[16]u[12]x:}2{r:}) or a registered chemistry name such as 10xv3, so piscem map-scrna and alevin-fry parse cell barcodes and UMIs from the correct read positions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad614
skills.summary: Configures simpleaf/alevin-fry single-cell quantification for non-default library layouts by supplying a custom barcode/UMI geometry string (e.g. 1{b[16]u[12]x:}2{r:}) or a registered chemistry name such as 10xv3, so piscem map-scrna and alevin-fry parse cell barcodes and UMIs from the correct read positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is bulk RNA-seq or scATAC-seq, where piscem map-bulk/map-sc-atac and their barcode flags apply instead of the map-sc chemistry geometry The library is a standard registered chemistry (e.g. 10xv3) and no custom geometry encoding is needed — use the registered name directly rather than hand-writing a geometry string The barcode/UMI read structure is unknown; resolve the library layout first (e.g. via scg_lib_structs documentation) before guessing a geometry string

skills.description: Use when FASTQ reads come from a single-cell protocol whose barcode/UMI layout does not fit the mapper's native simple-geometry expectations — e.g. concatenated barcodes, variable-length segments, or segments not at fixed offsets.
skills.name: custom-chemistry-registry-encoding
skills.search_text: custom-chemistry-registry-encoding Use when FASTQ reads come from a single-cell protocol whose barcode/UMI layout does not fit the mapper's native simple-geometry expectations — e.g. concatenated barcodes, variable-length segments, or segments not at fixed offsets. Reads already follow a simple fixed-position geometry natively supported by the alevin-fry mapper — no normalization layer is needed. skills.description: Use when comparing metabolic states of a test cell population against a reference population over experimental time points in single-cell cytometry data, using the TcellHartmann2020_sampleData-style marker set (GLUT1, HK2, GAPDH, LDHA, MCT1, PFKFB4, IDH2, CyclinB1, GLUD12, CS, OGDH, CytC, ATP5A.

Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — this supervised approach is inappropriate in those situations Data has more than 100 dimensions — hybrid subset selection (HSS) is not feasible there, though plain LDA/sda can still be used Large heterogeneity exists within a class (e.g., PBMCs labeled by time point) or a very large number of populations must be separated — HSS-LDA performance suffers Analyzes metabolic marker expression in T cells by training a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) model on CD57low (non-senescent) CyTOF cells across day0–day5 TCR-stimulation time points using the 15 metabolic marker channels (GLUT1 through HIF1A), then projecting unseen CD57high (senescent) cells onto those LD axes with hsslda::makeAxes() to reveal stunted metabolic progression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536

skills.search_text: dag-based-granger-causal-inference Use when you have paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq (multimodal) data from a dynamic biological process and need causal (not merely correlational) peak-gene link inference across cell states. skills.search_text: de-method-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating which DE detection method performs on scRNA-Seq data and a simulator (SymSim) can provide gold-standard differential gene labels and true log fold changes for the comparison. The goal is trajectory inference rather than DE detection — use trajectory evaluation frameworks such as dynwrap/dynmethods with dyneval instead. Only real data with no gold-standard DE labels are available — simulation-based truth (differential EVFs defining DE genes) is required for AUROC and logFC correlation scoring. Data are UMI-based — this benchmark uses nonUMI protocol counts (True2ObservedCounts with protocol='nonUMI'); UMI-based simulation settings are a different configuration. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark differential expression detection methods (edgeR, DESeq2, Wilcoxon rank-sum, t-test) on SymSim-simulated single-cell RNA-Seq data with gold-standard DE labels derived from true transcript counts, scoring each method by AUROC and negative Spearman correlation of p-values against true log fold change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Benchmark differential expression detection methods (edgeR, DESeq2, Wilcoxon rank-sum, t-test) on SymSim-simulated single-cell RNA-Seq data with gold-standard DE labels derived from true transcript counts, scoring each method by AUROC and negative Spearman correlation of p-values against true log fold change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is trajectory inference rather than DE detection — use trajectory evaluation frameworks such as dynwrap/dynmethods with dyneval instead. Only real data with no gold-standard DE labels are available — simulation-based truth (differential EVFs defining DE genes) is required for AUROC and logFC correlation scoring. Data are UMI-based — this benchmark uses nonUMI protocol counts (True2ObservedCounts with protocol='nonUMI'); UMI-based simulation settings are a different configuration.

skills.description: Use when an initial GRN inferred from RNA-Seq time-series data needs refinement with binding motif evidence, and a GenBank genome file with promoter sequences is available.
skills.name: de-novo-tfbm-motif-discovery
skills.search_text: de-novo-tfbm-motif-discovery Use when an initial GRN inferred from RNA-Seq time-series data needs refinement with binding motif evidence, and a GenBank genome file with promoter sequences is available. The organism lacks an annotated genome (GenBank file) for promoter extraction — the article notes refining steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome Only the initial MI-based GRN is needed and computational time is critical — the article reports refinement is computationally very demanding (714.18 s vs 83.07 s without refinement on DREAM 4) Regulons of interest contain fewer than five genes, below the minimum size used for de novo TFBM discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Refines an initial mutual-information-based GRN by discovering transcription factor binding motifs (TFBMs) de novo in promoter sequences of regulated genes using the MEME Suite, then exporting the discovered motifs for downstream motif search and edge re-typing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Refines an initial mutual-information-based GRN by discovering transcription factor binding motifs (TFBMs) de novo in promoter sequences of regulated genes using the MEME Suite, then exporting the discovered motifs for downstream motif search and edge re-typing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism lacks an annotated genome (GenBank file) for promoter extraction — the article notes refining steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome Only the initial MI-based GRN is needed and computational time is critical — the article reports refinement is computationally very demanding (714.18 s vs 83.07 s without refinement on DREAM 4) Regulons of interest contain fewer than five genes, below the minimum size used for de novo TFBM discovery

skills.description: Use when you have Illumina paired-end RNA-Seq reads (FASTQ) and no reference genome, and need a de novo assembled transcriptome (FASTA) to quality-assess with TransRate/BUSCO or to filter with Bellerophon.
skills.name: de-novo-transcriptome-assembly
skills.search_text: de-novo-transcriptome-assembly Use when you have Illumina paired-end RNA-Seq reads (FASTQ) and no reference genome, and need a de novo assembled transcriptome (FASTA) to quality-assess with TransRate/BUSCO or to filter with Bellerophon. A reference genome is available and a genome-guided or reference-based transcript reconstruction would be more appropriate — the paper's scope is de novo assembly when no reference genome exists The input is already an assembled transcriptome FASTA — then skip assembly and go directly to TransRate/BUSCO assessment or Bellerophon filtering The goal is only to remove chimeras from an existing assembly — that is the Bellerophon filtering skill, not the assembly step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Builds a reference-free transcriptome from Illumina RNA-Seq reads with Trinity (e.g., the H. subflexa female pheromone gland assembly, or D. melanogaster reads from SRA BioProject PRJNA527373), discarding contigs supported by fewer than 5 reads, and produces the FASTA assembly that downstream chimera-removal pipelines such as Bellerophon consume. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571
skills.summary: Builds a reference-free transcriptome from Illumina RNA-Seq reads with Trinity (e.g., the H. subflexa female pheromone gland assembly, or D. melanogaster reads from SRA BioProject PRJNA527373), discarding contigs supported by fewer than 5 reads, and produces the FASTA assembly that downstream chimera-removal pipelines such as Bellerophon consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A reference genome is available and a genome-guided or reference-based transcript reconstruction would be more appropriate — the paper's scope is de novo assembly when no reference genome exists The input is already an assembled transcriptome FASTA — then skip assembly and go directly to TransRate/BUSCO assessment or Bellerophon filtering The goal is only to remove chimeras from an existing assembly — that is the Bellerophon filtering skill, not the assembly step

skills.description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly must be filtered and you need to empirically decide which combination and order of TPM, CD-HIT-EST, TransRate-C, and ORF-length filters maximizes quality or chimera removal.
skills.name: de-novo-transcriptome-filtering-order-benchmarking
skills.search_text: de-novo-transcriptome-filtering-order-benchmarking Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly must be filtered and you need to empirically decide which combination and order of TPM, CD-HIT-EST, TransRate-C, and ORF-length filters maximizes quality or chimera removal. Input already has a reference genome/transcriptome — reference-based assessment methods are more appropriate than this reference-free filtering benchmark The assembly has not been quality-scored first with TransRate/BUSCO — Bellerophon requires a ground quality score of the unfiltered assembly before filtering variants can be compared You need custom filter ordering out of the box — the README states custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematically varies the composition and ordering of Bellerophon's filter components (TPM cut-off 1.0, CD-HIT-EST 95% identity, TransRate-C, ORF length 50/100 aa) and scores each variant with TransRate to identify the optimal de novo transcriptome filtering strategy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571
skills.summary: Systematically varies the composition and ordering of Bellerophon's filter components (TPM cut-off 1.0, CD-HIT-EST 95% identity, TransRate-C, ORF length 50/100 aa) and scores each variant with TransRate to identify the optimal de novo transcriptome filtering strategy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input already has a reference genome/transcriptome — reference-based assessment methods are more appropriate than this reference-free filtering benchmark The assembly has not been quality-scored first with TransRate/BUSCO — Bellerophon requires a ground quality score of the unfiltered assembly before filtering variants can be compared You need custom filter ordering out of the box — the README states custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version

skills.description: Use when filtering contaminated (extranuclear RNA) droplets from 10X droplet-based snRNA-seq CellRanger output where hard count/UMI/gene cutoffs or EmptyDrops lose nuclear droplets or retain debris.
skills.name: debris-score-estimation-and-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: debris-score-estimation-and-threshold-filtering Use when filtering contaminated (extranuclear RNA) droplets from 10X droplet-based snRNA-seq CellRanger output where hard count/UMI/gene cutoffs or EmptyDrops lose nuclear droplets or retain debris. Data is single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., PBMCs) where background and cell-type expression profiles differ little and debris-score correlation with contamination is less successful; use the debris-cluster-based call_targets(clusters = "debris") strategy instead of score thresholding. There are no genes increased in the background distribution, so debris-enriched genes cannot be accurately estimated and the resulting debris score will be unreliable. Comparing debris scores across independent samples or integrating multiple samples where the distribution of extranuclear RNA differs, since scores are normalized relative to within-sample cluster means and are not on a common scale. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate per-droplet debris scores with DIEM's semi-supervised multinomial mixture EM and remove background-contaminated droplets by thresholding the debris score, instead of applying hard count cutoffs, in droplet-based snRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Estimate per-droplet debris scores with DIEM's semi-supervised multinomial mixture EM and remove background-contaminated droplets by thresholding the debris score, instead of applying hard count cutoffs, in droplet-based snRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., PBMCs) where background and cell-type expression profiles differ little and debris-score correlation with contamination is less successful; use the debris-cluster-based call_targets(clusters = "debris") strategy instead of score thresholding. There are no genes increased in the background distribution, so debris-enriched genes cannot be accurately estimated and the resulting debris score will be unreliable. Comparing debris scores across independent samples or integrating multiple samples where the distribution of extranuclear RNA differs, since scores are normalized relative to within-sample cluster means and are not on a common scale.

skills.description: Use when a Ctrl-vs-RPL decidual immune query scRNA-seq dataset must be mapped onto the maternal-fetal interface reference to test whether dNK composition shifts (e.g. dNK1 decrease, dNK3 increase) reproduce.
skills.name: decidual-nk-subpopulation-composition-analysis
skills.search_text: decidual-nk-subpopulation-composition-analysis Use when a Ctrl-vs-RPL decidual immune query scRNA-seq dataset must be mapped onto the maternal-fetal interface reference to test whether dNK composition shifts (e.g. dNK1 decrease, dNK3 increase) reproduce. Query cells contain novel states absent from the Vento2018 MFI reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, and unsupervised clustering should be compared against mapping results instead Query data derive from a different platform or UMI distribution than the reference (e.g. Smart-seq2 query vs 10x-based reference), where ProjectSVR projection performance declines The query is not decidual/MFI tissue — use the pre-built models matched to the tissue, e.g. model.disco_pbmc.rds (PBMC), model.Zheng2021.CD8Tcell.rds (pan-cancer T cells), or model.mTCA.rds (testicular germ cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies shifts in decidual NK (dNK) subpopulation composition between healthy controls and recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) patients by projecting Guo2021 decidual immune cells onto the Vento2018 maternal-fetal interface (MFI) reference atlas with ProjectSVR, transferring reference labels, and tabulating per-sample dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 frequencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Quantifies shifts in decidual NK (dNK) subpopulation composition between healthy controls and recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) patients by projecting Guo2021 decidual immune cells onto the Vento2018 maternal-fetal interface (MFI) reference atlas with ProjectSVR, transferring reference labels, and tabulating per-sample dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel states absent from the Vento2018 MFI reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, and unsupervised clustering should be compared against mapping results instead Query data derive from a different platform or UMI distribution than the reference (e.g. Smart-seq2 query vs 10x-based reference), where ProjectSVR projection performance declines The query is not decidual/MFI tissue — use the pre-built models matched to the tissue, e.g. model.disco_pbmc.rds (PBMC), model.Zheng2021.CD8Tcell.rds (pan-cancer T cells), or model.mTCA.rds (testicular germ cells)

skills.description: Use when two or more cluster annotation sets (e.g. RNA Leiden labels and splicing/PSI NMF subclusters, or RNA/ADT/ATAC modalities) disagree per cell and you need a reconciled, stability-scored final assignment rather than a joint-embedding integration.
skills.name: decision-level-multimodal-cluster-integration
skills.search_text: decision-level-multimodal-cluster-integration Use when two or more cluster annotation sets (e.g. RNA Leiden labels and splicing/PSI NMF subclusters, or RNA/ADT/ATAC modalities) disagree per cell and you need a reconciled, stability-scored final assignment rather than a joint-embedding integration. A single consistent clustering already exists and no conflicting annotation sets need reconciliation The goal is a joint latent-space embedding of modalities rather than decision-level assignment — Seurat-WNN or TotalVI are the competing data-level approaches, and scTriangulate deliberately avoids joint embedding More than 15 annotation sets are needed and Shapley runtime is prohibitive — although scTriangulate auto-substitutes rank-based selection, very large sources increase runtime significantly http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Decision-level integration of conflicting single-cell clustering solutions (different modalities, algorithms, resolutions) with scTriangulate, which mixes-and-matches cluster assignments using the Shapley value from coalitional game theory plus stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5/10, SCCAF) instead of building a joint latent space like Seurat WNN or TotalVI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Decision-level integration of conflicting single-cell clustering solutions (different modalities, algorithms, resolutions) with scTriangulate, which mixes-and-matches cluster assignments using the Shapley value from coalitional game theory plus stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5/10, SCCAF) instead of building a joint latent space like Seurat WNN or TotalVI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A single consistent clustering already exists and no conflicting annotation sets need reconciliation The goal is a joint latent-space embedding of modalities rather than decision-level assignment — Seurat-WNN or TotalVI are the competing data-level approaches, and scTriangulate deliberately avoids joint embedding More than 15 annotation sets are needed and Shapley runtime is prohibitive — although scTriangulate auto-substitutes rank-based selection, very large sources increase runtime significantly

skills.description: Use when a malignant epithelial subcluster (e.g. from PDAC scRNA-seq) needs molecular subtype assignment via pathway deconvolution, specifically estimating basal-like vs classical pathway weights, bcRatio, and GATA6 status.
skills.name: decoder-basal-like-weight-estimation
skills.search_text: decoder-basal-like-weight-estimation Use when a malignant epithelial subcluster (e.g. from PDAC scRNA-seq) needs molecular subtype assignment via pathway deconvolution, specifically estimating basal-like vs classical pathway weights, bcRatio, and GATA6 status. The cell population is already unambiguously classified as classical or basal-like and only marker plots are needed — DECODER deconvolution adds nothing over direct marker scoring. The input contains no malignant epithelial cells (e.g. stromal/immune-only clusters); DECODER subtype weights are designed for tumor cell populations, as in the PDAC ductal/PDAC subsetting use case. No subtype gene signatures are available or the dataset is not human PDAC-compatible with the Moffitt/DECODER gene sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies the DECODER deconvolution method (R package 'decoderr') to scRNA-seq tumor subclusters — e.g. PDAC epithelial cells recovered by SCISSORS reclustering — to estimate per-subcluster basal-like and classical pathway weights, compute the bcRatio, and verify GATA6 depletion, thereby assigning molecular subtype identity to rare malignant subpopulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Applies the DECODER deconvolution method (R package 'decoderr') to scRNA-seq tumor subclusters — e.g. PDAC epithelial cells recovered by SCISSORS reclustering — to estimate per-subcluster basal-like and classical pathway weights, compute the bcRatio, and verify GATA6 depletion, thereby assigning molecular subtype identity to rare malignant subpopulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell population is already unambiguously classified as classical or basal-like and only marker plots are needed — DECODER deconvolution adds nothing over direct marker scoring. The input contains no malignant epithelial cells (e.g. stromal/immune-only clusters); DECODER subtype weights are designed for tumor cell populations, as in the PDAC ductal/PDAC subsetting use case. No subtype gene signatures are available or the dataset is not human PDAC-compatible with the Moffitt/DECODER gene sets.

skills.name: decoder-weight-variance-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: decoder-weight-variance-gene-ranking Use when a trained scMGCA (GCN autoencoder) latent embedding is available and the goal is functional interpretation — identifying the pivotal genes the decoder weights encode so they can be tested for pathway/GO enrichment. You want marker genes per cell cluster (p_val_adj <= 0.05, avg_logFC >= 0.5) rather than pivotal genes extracted from autoencoder weight matrices The model is not a GCN-based graph autoencoder (e.g. DCA or scVI without decoder weight matrices) — no W1/W2 weight structure exists to rank You need differential expression across conditions instead of functional interpretation of the compressed transcriptomic space http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks genes by the standard deviation and weight of a trained scMGCA graph-convolutional autoencoder's weight matrices (W1/W2) to extract the top 200 pivotal genes from the compressed transcription space, which are then used for KEGG/GO over-representation analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7

skills.search_text: deep-clustering-model-training Use when you have paired multi-omic count matrices (X1=RNA, X2=ADT or ATAC) in h5 format and want an end-to-end deep clustering with ARI/NMI/AMI evaluation, including multi-batch data needing batch-effect correction. skills.summary: Train the scMDC end-to-end multimodal deep clustering model — a denoising autoencoder with ZINB reconstruction losses on RNA plus a second omic (ADT/ATAC), jointly optimized with a KL loss and deep K-means — to cluster paired CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq cells without requiring labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-modality data only (RNA-only or ATAC-only) — use the single-modality variants scMDC-RNA/-ADT/-ATAC or scDeepCluster instead, which this model significantly outperforms only when both modalities are available The goal is a joint embedding for a purpose other than clustering — the paper notes joint-embedding methods like Cobolt and scMM are not designed and optimized for clustering, and scMDC is purpose-built for clustering, not general embedding tasks No GPU is available and the dataset is large — all experiments in the study were run on an Nvidia Tesla P100 (16 G), so CPU-only reproduction may be infeasible for big multimodal datasets

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a fusion caller or similar ML-assisted pipeline and you must quantify how much a learned filtering component contributes, by comparing full-pipeline precision/recall against a variant with the deep-learning model turned off on the same inputs.
skills.name: deep-learning-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: deep-learning-ablation-analysis Use when benchmarking a fusion caller or similar ML-assisted pipeline and you must quantify how much a learned filtering component contributes, by comparing full-pipeline precision/recall against a variant with the deep-learning model turned off on the same inputs. Input is 10X droplet scRNA-seq data rather than Smart-Seq protocol FASTQ files, since scFusion and this benchmark are designed for Smart-Seq (_1.fastq/_2.fastq, *_1.fq not allowed). No simulation ground truth or known fusion set exists, so precision/recall/F-score deltas between full and ablated runs cannot be computed. The pipeline has no learned/ML component to ablate, so a deep-learning-off comparison is meaningless. Ablation-analysis skill for verifying that a machine-learning component of a bioinformatics pipeline genuinely improves performance: rerun the pipeline with the model disabled on identical inputs and quantify the precision/sensitivity trade-off. In scFusion, this means disabling the tensorflow/keras deep-learning model that filters false-positive fusion candidates in scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6

skills.search_text: deep-learning-based-scrnaseq-imputation Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (CSV, genes x cells) exhibits dropouts/noise and the goal is imputation or improved downstream clustering, with a benchmark against DCA, SAVER, scImpute, or MAGIC. The data are already imputed/denoised or are bulk RNA-Seq rather than single-cell count matrices with dropouts The analysis goal is differential expression or batch-effect-specific correction rather than imputation-benchmarked-by-clustering — AutoClass covers these, but the K-means ARI/JI/NMI/purity evaluation scheme here is clustering-specific TensorFlow >=2.0 and Python 3 cannot be installed in the environment, since AutoClass requires them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Impute and denoise single-cell RNA-Seq count matrices with AutoClass, a TensorFlow >=2.0 deep neural network that integrates an autoencoder and a classifier and is free of distribution assumptions, and benchmark the imputation against controls (DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC) using downstream K-means clustering metrics (ARI, JI, NMI, purity). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Impute and denoise single-cell RNA-Seq count matrices with AutoClass, a TensorFlow >=2.0 deep neural network that integrates an autoencoder and a classifier and is free of distribution assumptions, and benchmark the imputation against controls (DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC) using downstream K-means clustering metrics (ARI, JI, NMI, purity).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already imputed/denoised or are bulk RNA-Seq rather than single-cell count matrices with dropouts The analysis goal is differential expression or batch-effect-specific correction rather than imputation-benchmarked-by-clustering — AutoClass covers these, but the K-means ARI/JI/NMI/purity evaluation scheme here is clustering-specific TensorFlow >=2.0 and Python 3 cannot be installed in the environment, since AutoClass requires them

skills.description: Use when running Anchored-fusion on paired-end RNA-seq data and candidate chimeric reads must be classified as natural chromosome fusions versus artificial cDNA fusions from PCR/sequencing artifacts.
skills.name: deep-learning-false-positive-filtering
skills.search_text: deep-learning-false-positive-filtering Use when running Anchored-fusion on paired-end RNA-seq data and candidate chimeric reads must be classified as natural chromosome fusions versus artificial cDNA fusions from PCR/sequencing artifacts. The sequencing library is single-end RNA-seq or whole-genome/whole-exome data — Anchored-fusion and its HVLD filter operate only on paired-end RNA-seq data You need a quick unfiltered candidate list and cannot spare training time — use '--not_filter_false_positive' instead, accepting more false positives The fusion events of interest do not include the user-provided anchored target gene — the whole anchored-search workflow, including its filter, will not detect them http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and apply the HVLD (hierarchical view learning and distillation) deep-learning module from Anchored-fusion to discard artificial chimeric-fragment false positives generated during sequencing while retaining true fusion gene calls, e.g. NSD2-IGH in multiple myeloma scRNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Train and apply the HVLD (hierarchical view learning and distillation) deep-learning module from Anchored-fusion to discard artificial chimeric-fragment false positives generated during sequencing while retaining true fusion gene calls, e.g. NSD2-IGH in multiple myeloma scRNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing library is single-end RNA-seq or whole-genome/whole-exome data — Anchored-fusion and its HVLD filter operate only on paired-end RNA-seq data You need a quick unfiltered candidate list and cannot spare training time — use '--not_filter_false_positive' instead, accepting more false positives The fusion events of interest do not include the user-provided anchored target gene — the whole anchored-search workflow, including its filter, will not detect them

skills.name: deep-learning-integration-model-training
skills.search_text: deep-learning-integration-model-training Use when multiple scRNA-seq batches (e.g., 16,382 pancreas cells across nine sequencing protocols) must be integrated unsupervised to remove batch effects while conserving biological variation such as skewed or rare cell types. Cell type annotations are available for all cells and supervised integration is desired — use scDREAMER-Sup instead of the unsupervised model The number of batches is unknown and cannot be supplied, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches and unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored A multiomic (e.g., RNA + ATAC) dataset must be integrated, as the multiomic extension is planned but not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train the scDREAMER adversarial variational autoencoder to produce batch-corrected low-dimensional cellular embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq integration, and benchmark it against state-of-the-art unsupervised integration baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Train the scDREAMER adversarial variational autoencoder to produce batch-corrected low-dimensional cellular embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq integration, and benchmark it against state-of-the-art unsupervised integration baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type annotations are available for all cells and supervised integration is desired — use scDREAMER-Sup instead of the unsupervised model The number of batches is unknown and cannot be supplied, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches and unsupervised treatment of batch information is unexplored A multiomic (e.g., RNA + ATAC) dataset must be integrated, as the multiomic extension is planned but not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when a trained Keras deep learning classifier (e.g. RFCN on scRNA-seq data such as the Zheng sorted dataset) must be inspected or diagnosed by visualizing its hidden-layer outputs, or when the sensitivity of the visualization to UMAP parameters (n_neighbors, min_dist) must be assessed.
skills.name: deep-learning-model-representation-visualization
skills.search_text: deep-learning-model-representation-visualization Use when a trained Keras deep learning classifier (e.g. RFCN on scRNA-seq data such as the Zheng sorted dataset) must be inspected or diagnosed by visualizing its hidden-layer outputs, or when the sensitivity of the visualization to UMAP parameters (n_neighbors, min_dist) must be assessed. skills.summary: A skill for inspecting the high-level representations learned by a trained deep learning model — here the RFCN cell-type classifier — by projecting the last hidden layer activations into two-dimensional UMAP space with layerUMAP, including a grid search over UMAP's n_neighbors and min_dist parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model contains branch layers: layerUMAP cannot capture hidden outputs from layers in a branch, so outputs must be captured manually in a Jupyter Notebook instead The goal is quantitative classification accuracy (e.g. RFCN's 98.09% on Zheng sorted) rather than visual inspection of learned representations The exact command-line text is required but unavailable: the article only references commands 1-5 via Figure 2, creating a reproducibility gap

skills.description: Use when unmapped RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be filtered into viral candidates using a pretrained deep learning model, with scores above 0.7 as assembly seeds and average scores below 0.5 as extension stop criteria.
skills.name: deep-learning-read-score-thresholding
skills.search_text: deep-learning-read-score-thresholding Use when unmapped RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be filtered into viral candidates using a pretrained deep learning model, with scores above 0.7 as assembly seeds and average scores below 0.5 as extension stop criteria. Input reads are still mapped/aligned data or raw FASTQ including human-mapped reads — viRNAtrap expects unmapped reads extracted by the user beforehand The goal is read-level viral classification only, not contig assembly — the seed threshold alone suffices but the extension gating and contig output are unnecessary Sequences come from organisms other than human/viral — model predictions for such sequences are not defined per the paper's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Threshold deep-learning model scores assigned to fixed-length (48 bp) RNA-seq reads to select candidate viral reads for assembly seeds, and re-score extended contig regions to gate extension during contig growth in viRNAtrap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Threshold deep-learning model scores assigned to fixed-length (48 bp) RNA-seq reads to select candidate viral reads for assembly seeds, and re-score extended contig regions to gate extension during contig growth in viRNAtrap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are still mapped/aligned data or raw FASTQ including human-mapped reads — viRNAtrap expects unmapped reads extracted by the user beforehand The goal is read-level viral classification only, not contig assembly — the seed threshold alone suffices but the extension gating and contig output are unnecessary Sequences come from organisms other than human/viral — model predictions for such sequences are not defined per the paper's discussion

skills.search_text: deep-neural-network-architecture-implementation Use when building a reference-based single-cell annotation model that must remove batch effects across multiple sequencing platforms in a large reference atlas before transferring labels to a query dataset. Predicting disease datasets where expression profiles deviate substantially from normal data — the fine-tuning step should be removed (--disease) rather than adapted Annotating with an already-published SELINA pre-trained model from SELINA-team/SELINA-reference instead of training a new network on your own reference data Cell-type abundance is already balanced and single-platform reference data is used, removing the need for SMOTE and the multi-adversarial domain adaptation design http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implement and train the deep neural network architecture underlying SELINA: a shared feature extractor with MADA (multi-adversarial domain adaptation) pre-training on multi-platform reference data, followed by autoencoder fine-tuning on query data, implemented in Python/PyTorch and serialized as pre-trained_params.pt with metadata in pre-trained_meta.pkl. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577

Input contains tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) that are outside the 47 TME subtypes — these will land in the 'Unknown' cluster The goal is terminal cell-type assignment without respecting hierarchical major-type/subtype relationships Data is not cancer/TME scRNA-seq and no custom trainset is available for model retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Two-step hierarchical deep neural network annotation (as implemented in scWizard) that classifies cancer scRNA-seq cells into 7 major cell types and 47 tumor-microenvironment (TME) subtypes using a pre-trained reference of 113,976 cells across 13 cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028

skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are not UMI-based counts — the paper states cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based), and TPM/RPKM accuracy is unknown No paired transcriptome–surface protein training data are available and the goal is simply to impute proteins with the pretrained model (use the cTPnet prediction package instead of retraining) Input scRNA-seq has not been quality-filtered and denoised (genes with <10 counts across cells, cells with <200 detected genes removed, SAVER-X denoising)
