skills.name: deep-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: deep-neural-network-training Use when you need to train a fixed-length read classifier (e.g., 48 bp fragments of viral vs. human transcripts) with binary labels, or reproduce viRNAtrap's reported test-set metrics (AUROC 0.81, AUPRC 0.82, accuracy 0.71, recall 0.83, precision 0.67, F1 0.74). Sequences come from organisms other than human or virus — the paper states model predictions for such sequences are not defined and models for other organisms are left to future work Reads are already mapped to the reference human genome — the viRNAtrap workflow applies the model only to unmapped RNAseq reads to reduce running time The task requires alignment-based identification or typing of already-characterized viral genomes — blastn/blastx against curated viral databases is the appropriate step http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a 1D-convolutional deep learning model in Keras/TensorFlow to classify 48 bp RNAseq fragments as viral or human, as done in viRNAtrap, an alignment-free pipeline for identifying viral reads and assembling viral contigs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Train a 1D-convolutional deep learning model in Keras/TensorFlow to classify 48 bp RNAseq fragments as viral or human, as done in viRNAtrap, an alignment-free pipeline for identifying viral reads and assembling viral contigs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences come from organisms other than human or virus — the paper states model predictions for such sequences are not defined and models for other organisms are left to future work Reads are already mapped to the reference human genome — the viRNAtrap workflow applies the model only to unmapped RNAseq reads to reduce running time The task requires alignment-based identification or typing of already-characterized viral genomes — blastn/blastx against curated viral databases is the appropriate step

skills.description: Use when training a supervised cancer subtype classifier from bulk gene expression (RNA-Seq or microarray) with known labels (e.g., PAM50 breast cancer intrinsic subtypes) and when robustness to cross-platform missing genes is required.
skills.name: deep-neural-network-training-on-expression-data
skills.search_text: deep-neural-network-training-on-expression-data Use when training a supervised cancer subtype classifier from bulk gene expression (RNA-Seq or microarray) with known labels (e.g., PAM50 breast cancer intrinsic subtypes) and when robustness to cross-platform missing genes is required. The goal is unsupervised clustering or de novo discovery of cancer patient groups — the article states DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients'. A labeled, well-annotated feature table of pathway scores already exists and only a simple model is needed — DeepCC's value is in the functional spectra transformation, not training on arbitrary precomputed features. The cancer type's characteristic pathways are poorly represented in the MSigDB gene set database — the article warns 'the prior knowledge of gene sets needs to be comprehensive to avoid potential bias'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a DeepCC artificial neural network (ANN) on pathway-level 'functional spectra' derived from tumor gene expression (e.g., TCGA BRCA RNA-Seq with PAM50 labels) to learn a supervised molecular subtype classifier. The deep features overcome platform dependency and batch effects that limit signature-gene classifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Trains a DeepCC artificial neural network (ANN) on pathway-level 'functional spectra' derived from tumor gene expression (e.g., TCGA BRCA RNA-Seq with PAM50 labels) to learn a supervised molecular subtype classifier. The deep features overcome platform dependency and batch effects that limit signature-gene classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised clustering or de novo discovery of cancer patient groups — the article states DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients'. A labeled, well-annotated feature table of pathway scores already exists and only a simple model is needed — DeepCC's value is in the functional spectra transformation, not training on arbitrary precomputed features. The cancer type's characteristic pathways are poorly represented in the MSigDB gene set database — the article warns 'the prior knowledge of gene sets needs to be comprehensive to avoid potential bias'.

skills.description: Use when predicting single-cell drug responses by transferring a bulk-trained model (e.g., I.BET.762 on GSE110894) and you need bulk+scRNA-seq model training with matching hyperparameters.

skills.search_text: deep-transfer-learning-model-training Use when predicting single-cell drug responses by transferring a bulk-trained model (e.g., I.BET.762 on GSE110894) and you need bulk+scRNA-seq model training with matching hyperparameters. Input is bulk data alone with no single-cell dataset to transfer to — bulkmodel.py alone does not produce single-cell predictions The scRNA-seq dataset is from a species other than human without restricting to homologous genes — cross-species transfer (human-trained to mouse data) was only tested by keeping homologous genes and its reliability could not be systematically evaluated No bulk-level drug response data exists for the drug of interest, since prediction accuracy depends on the collection of bulk gene expression of cell lines http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train scDEAL's bulk-level drug-response predictor (bulkmodel.py) and transfer it via a DaNN domain-adaptive network to single-cell data (scmodel.py), enabling drug-sensitivity prediction in scRNA-seq using large-scale bulk GDSC/CCLE training data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Train scDEAL's bulk-level drug-response predictor (bulkmodel.py) and transfer it via a DaNN domain-adaptive network to single-cell data (scmodel.py), enabling drug-sensitivity prediction in scRNA-seq using large-scale bulk GDSC/CCLE training data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk data alone with no single-cell dataset to transfer to — bulkmodel.py alone does not produce single-cell predictions The scRNA-seq dataset is from a species other than human without restricting to homologous genes — cross-species transfer (human-trained to mouse data) was only tested by keeping homologous genes and its reliability could not be systematically evaluated No bulk-level drug response data exists for the drug of interest, since prediction accuracy depends on the collection of bulk gene expression of cell lines

skills.description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model checkpoint exists and you need to identify which genes drive cell type classification (e.g., reproducing Figure 2 gene rankings for testis and PBMC datasets).
skills.name: deeplift-rescale-feature-attribution
skills.search_text: deeplift-rescale-feature-attribution Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model checkpoint exists and you need to identify which genes drive cell type classification (e.g., reproducing Figure 2 gene rankings for testis and PBMC datasets). The GCN has not yet been trained — run the scSHARP consensus label propagation training (task_003 checkpoints) before attempting attribution. You need expression data that is not raw counts; the scSHARP README specifies 'Please input raw counts.' The model is not a graph convolutional network with per-cell-type output neurons — DeepLIFT targets here are the per-tool output neurons of the scSHARP GCN, not generic model heads. Interprets the trained scSHARP graph convolutional network by running DeepLIFT (Rescale rule, via Captum) with a zero reference matrix and per-cell-type target neurons, yielding per-gene importance scores for cell type classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Interprets the trained scSHARP graph convolutional network by running DeepLIFT (Rescale rule, via Captum) with a zero reference matrix and per-cell-type target neurons, yielding per-gene importance scores for cell type classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GCN has not yet been trained — run the scSHARP consensus label propagation training (task_003 checkpoints) before attempting attribution. You need expression data that is not raw counts; the scSHARP README specifies 'Please input raw counts.' The model is not a graph convolutional network with per-cell-type output neurons — DeepLIFT targets here are the per-tool output neurons of the scSHARP GCN, not generic model heads.

skills.search_text: default-configuration-method-execution Use when comparing wall-clock runtime of an imputation method against analytical or deep-learning baselines on the same expression matrix, or when reproducing the reported >=10x efficiency gain of SERM. The goal is imputation accuracy (Pearson coefficient, clustering indices) rather than computational runtime — use the accuracy-benchmarking skill instead Datasets are small enough that all methods complete in comparable time, making the runtime contrast uninformative The target is SERM's internal steps (ROI selection, histogram equalization, bilinear resampling) rather than end-to-end runtime comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark computational runtime of SERM against default-configured imputation baselines (MAGIC, mcImpute, AutoImpute, DeepImpute, SAUCIE) on identical scRNA-seq matrices, timing each run to quantify SERM's >=10x speed advantage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Benchmark computational runtime of SERM against default-configured imputation baselines (MAGIC, mcImpute, AutoImpute, DeepImpute, SAUCIE) on identical scRNA-seq matrices, timing each run to quantify SERM's >=10x speed advantage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is imputation accuracy (Pearson coefficient, clustering indices) rather than computational runtime — use the accuracy-benchmarking skill instead Datasets are small enough that all methods complete in comparable time, making the runtime contrast uninformative The target is SERM's internal steps (ROI selection, histogram equalization, bilinear resampling) rather than end-to-end runtime comparison

skills.description: Use when prioritizing candidate resistance genes around significant SNPs and you need to weight or rank those candidates by defense relevance using annotated defense-related guide genes.
skills.name: defense-gene-guide-selection
skills.search_text: defense-gene-guide-selection Use when prioritizing candidate resistance genes around significant SNPs and you need to weight or rank those candidates by defense relevance using annotated defense-related guide genes. Your goal is de novo functional annotation of genes rather than prioritizing SNP-proximal candidates for a specific pathogen. Your organism or pathogen system lacks defense-related MapMan/PLAZA annotations or a GWAS SNP set, since the guide weighting and SNP-window steps cannot be grounded. You need a web-based interactive exploration of the coexpression network only (use the SoyFungiGCN Shiny app directly instead of rerunning the prioritization). http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Selects defense-related guide genes (via MapMan annotations from PLAZA 3.0 Dicots) to weight candidate soybean resistance genes during prioritization of genes near resistance SNPs, so that candidates are ranked by defense relevance rather than genomic proximity alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Selects defense-related guide genes (via MapMan annotations from PLAZA 3.0 Dicots) to weight candidate soybean resistance genes during prioritization of genes near resistance SNPs, so that candidates are ranked by defense relevance rather than genomic proximity alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo functional annotation of genes rather than prioritizing SNP-proximal candidates for a specific pathogen. Your organism or pathogen system lacks defense-related MapMan/PLAZA annotations or a GWAS SNP set, since the guide weighting and SNP-window steps cannot be grounded. You need a web-based interactive exploration of the coexpression network only (use the SoyFungiGCN Shiny app directly instead of rerunning the prioritization).

skills.description: Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix must be labeled cancer vs non-cancer by a supervised model pre-trained on the five cancer transcriptome datasets with DEG features.
skills.name: deg-feature-based-supervised-classification
skills.search_text: deg-feature-based-supervised-classification Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix must be labeled cancer vs non-cancer by a supervised model pre-trained on the five cancer transcriptome datasets with DEG features. The goal is to annotate non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells only The expression matrix is raw counts and has not been depth-normalized — PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM, CPM) as input No well-annotated training data or DEG feature set is available and only a custom dataset is being used without the Custom_preprocessing()/Custom_classifier() variant http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Supervised ensemble classification of single cells as malignant or non-malignant using k-NN (k=5) base classifiers trained on five cancer scRNA-seq datasets with common DEGs (73 TMGs and 186 NMGs) as features, combined by majority vote. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Supervised ensemble classification of single cells as malignant or non-malignant using k-NN (k=5) base classifiers trained on five cancer scRNA-seq datasets with common DEGs (73 TMGs and 186 NMGs) as features, combined by majority vote.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to annotate non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells only The expression matrix is raw counts and has not been depth-normalized — PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM, CPM) as input No well-annotated training data or DEG feature set is available and only a custom dataset is being used without the Custom_preprocessing()/Custom_classifier() variant

skills.description: Use when a pretrained malignant-cell classifier's feature list must be decomposed into common vs dataset-unique DEGs and their contribution to classification performance (AUROC, balanced accuracy) needs to be quantified.
skills.name: deg-feature-importance-analysis
skills.search_text: deg-feature-importance-analysis Use when a pretrained malignant-cell classifier's feature list must be decomposed into common vs dataset-unique DEGs and their contribution to classification performance (AUROC, balanced accuracy) needs to be quantified. The goal is de novo DEG detection from raw scRNA-seq rather than re-analyzing the precomputed 2707-gene DEG set already deposited on Zenodo. The task is annotating malignant cells in new data (use scMalignantFinder's predict workflow directly) rather than interpreting feature importance of the trained model. The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors), where the DEG features and classifier are untested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts per-gene logistic-regression coefficients from the pretrained scMalignantFinder model (model.joblib, 2707 DEG features) to test whether pan-cancer common DEGs (DE in ≥2 cancer types) carry higher importance than dataset-unique DEGs, and retrains subset models to confirm common-DEG and top-1500-gene models match the full model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Extracts per-gene logistic-regression coefficients from the pretrained scMalignantFinder model (model.joblib, 2707 DEG features) to test whether pan-cancer common DEGs (DE in ≥2 cancer types) carry higher importance than dataset-unique DEGs, and retrains subset models to confirm common-DEG and top-1500-gene models match the full model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo DEG detection from raw scRNA-seq rather than re-analyzing the precomputed 2707-gene DEG set already deposited on Zenodo. The task is annotating malignant cells in new data (use scMalignantFinder's predict workflow directly) rather than interpreting feature importance of the trained model. The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors), where the DEG features and classifier are untested.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or training DEG-combination methods (e.g. Naïve Bayes vote classifiers) and you need simulated count tables paired with known ground-truth DEG labels.
skills.name: deg-ground-truth-label-generation
skills.search_text: deg-ground-truth-label-generation Use when benchmarking or training DEG-combination methods (e.g. Naïve Bayes vote classifiers) and you need simulated count tables paired with known ground-truth DEG labels. You need ground truth for the ERCC spike-in dataset, where truth is defined by spike-in concentrations rather than TCC simulation. You are detecting DEGs on real experimental RNA-seq data (no known labels exist), rather than benchmarking methods on synthetic data. Your input is already a validated count table from a real experiment that should go straight into DEgenes Hunter DEG detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates simulated RNA-seq count matrices together with ground-truth DEG labels using the ExpHunterSuite TCC-based simulation methodology, so that differential expression methods can be benchmarked against known positives. This underpins the suite's Naïve Bayes classifier, which is trained on simulated data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Generates simulated RNA-seq count matrices together with ground-truth DEG labels using the ExpHunterSuite TCC-based simulation methodology, so that differential expression methods can be benchmarked against known positives. This underpins the suite's Naïve Bayes classifier, which is trained on simulated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need ground truth for the ERCC spike-in dataset, where truth is defined by spike-in concentrations rather than TCC simulation. You are detecting DEGs on real experimental RNA-seq data (no known labels exist), rather than benchmarking methods on synthetic data. Your input is already a validated count table from a real experiment that should go straight into DEgenes Hunter DEG detection.

skills.description: Use when you have two or more ranked or unranked gene lists (e.g., Wx DI-ranked UGCBs, edgeR DEGs sorted by adjusted p value, published biomarker signatures) and need to measure their overlap to assess method concordance.
skills.name: deg-list-comparison
skills.search_text: deg-list-comparison Use when you have two or more ranked or unranked gene lists (e.g., Wx DI-ranked UGCBs, edgeR DEGs sorted by adjusted p value, published biomarker signatures) and need to measure their overlap to assess method concordance. You need to compare the classification performance of the gene sets rather than their membership — use LOOCV or a classifier (NN/SVM/XGBoost) comparison instead. The gene lists come from different data sets or different gene identifier schemes without harmonization — symbol-level intersection would be meaningless. You expect functional similarity rather than literal gene overlap — use GO/network analysis (e.g., Metascape on top 50 UGCBs) instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Quantifies the agreement between gene lists produced by different feature-selection or DEG methods (e.g., Wx UGCBs vs. Peng-14, Martinez-7, or edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) by computing set intersections and reporting overlap counts and percentages. This exposes the substantial discrepancy between neural-network-based feature selection and classical DEG ranking on the same TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Quantifies the agreement between gene lists produced by different feature-selection or DEG methods (e.g., Wx UGCBs vs. Peng-14, Martinez-7, or edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) by computing set intersections and reporting overlap counts and percentages. This exposes the substantial discrepancy between neural-network-based feature selection and classical DEG ranking on the same TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to compare the classification performance of the gene sets rather than their membership — use LOOCV or a classifier (NN/SVM/XGBoost) comparison instead. The gene lists come from different data sets or different gene identifier schemes without harmonization — symbol-level intersection would be meaningless. You expect functional similarity rather than literal gene overlap — use GO/network analysis (e.g., Metascape on top 50 UGCBs) instead.

skills.description: Use when a ranked DEG list (e.g., scTITANS output at fdr level 0.01) must be confirmed as biologically meaningful, via literature surveys plus GO BP enrichment of the top genes.
skills.name: deg-literature-validation
skills.search_text: deg-literature-validation Use when a ranked DEG list (e.g., scTITANS output at fdr level 0.01) must be confirmed as biologically meaningful, via literature surveys plus GO BP enrichment of the top genes. The input is raw gene expression data rather than a finalized DEG list — run the upstream differential expression step (e.g., scTITANS_full/scTITANS_partial) first. Cell-level annotation or trajectory analysis is the goal; this skill only validates a gene list, it does not identify genes or subclusters. Enrichment is required for non-GO categories (e.g., pathways, networks) or a different ontology than GO biological process, which the task's ToppGene configuration restricts against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Validates that top differential genes (e.g., scTITANS DEGs at fdr 0.01) are biologically meaningful by combining literature verification with Gene Ontology biological-process enrichment analysis (ToppGene), compiling the results into a structured enrichment table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Validates that top differential genes (e.g., scTITANS DEGs at fdr 0.01) are biologically meaningful by combining literature verification with Gene Ontology biological-process enrichment analysis (ToppGene), compiling the results into a structured enrichment table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw gene expression data rather than a finalized DEG list — run the upstream differential expression step (e.g., scTITANS_full/scTITANS_partial) first. Cell-level annotation or trajectory analysis is the goal; this skill only validates a gene list, it does not identify genes or subclusters. Enrichment is required for non-GO categories (e.g., pathways, networks) or a different ontology than GO biological process, which the task's ToppGene configuration restricts against.

skills.description: Use when a count table must be analyzed for differential expression and robustness matters, or when evaluating which DEG detection method/combination strategy to trust on RNA-seq data.
skills.name: deg-method-consensus-combination
skills.search_text: deg-method-consensus-combination Use when a count table must be analyzed for differential expression and robustness matters, or when evaluating which DEG detection method/combination strategy to trust on RNA-seq data. When the goal is accurate logFC/fold-change estimation for downstream analyses such as GSEA rather than robust DEG calling — the article notes incorrect fold change estimation could lead to poor qPCR target selection, and combination strategies target DEG calls, not logFC quality When blindly extrapolating the spike-in-optimized vote threshold of 2 — the authors state this may differ for other organisms, tissues and experimental designs and they are hesitant to extrapolate a general rule When only a single method's final DEG list exists with no per-method results available to combine http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines per-method DEG calls from DESeq2, limma, and NOISeq (run via the DEgenes Hunter pipeline in ExpHunter Suite) using vote-threshold and combined-FDR consensus strategies plus a Naïve Bayes classifier, because no single method is optimal across datasets. Performance is quantified against known ground truth (spike-in transcripts) using F-measure and logFC correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Combines per-method DEG calls from DESeq2, limma, and NOISeq (run via the DEgenes Hunter pipeline in ExpHunter Suite) using vote-threshold and combined-FDR consensus strategies plus a Naïve Bayes classifier, because no single method is optimal across datasets. Performance is quantified against known ground truth (spike-in transcripts) using F-measure and logFC correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accurate logFC/fold-change estimation for downstream analyses such as GSEA rather than robust DEG calling — the article notes incorrect fold change estimation could lead to poor qPCR target selection, and combination strategies target DEG calls, not logFC quality When blindly extrapolating the spike-in-optimized vote threshold of 2 — the authors state this may differ for other organisms, tissues and experimental designs and they are hesitant to extrapolate a general rule When only a single method's final DEG list exists with no per-method results available to combine

skills.name: deg-method-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: deg-method-performance-evaluation Use when simulated RNA-seq count matrices with known differentially expressed gene labels are available and you need to compare DEG detection methods by AUC, or to benchmark a combined/integrated method against individual tools. When only a real dataset without ground-truth DEG labels is available — AUC against simulated truth cannot be computed, and the article notes vote-threshold optima may not generalize across organisms, tissues and experimental designs When the goal is differential expression calling on a single real dataset rather than benchmarking method performance — use the DEgenes Hunter pipeline directly instead of the simulation-based evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Evaluates the classification performance of individual DEG detection methods (DESeq2, edgeR, limma, NOISeq) and integrated methods (combined-FDR, vote thresholds, Naïve Bayes classifier) by ranking genes and computing AUC against simulated ground-truth labels across varying logFC conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Evaluates the classification performance of individual DEG detection methods (DESeq2, edgeR, limma, NOISeq) and integrated methods (combined-FDR, vote thresholds, Naïve Bayes classifier) by ranking genes and computing AUC against simulated ground-truth labels across varying logFC conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a real dataset without ground-truth DEG labels is available — AUC against simulated truth cannot be computed, and the article notes vote-threshold optima may not generalize across organisms, tissues and experimental designs When the goal is differential expression calling on a single real dataset rather than benchmarking method performance — use the DEgenes Hunter pipeline directly instead of the simulation-based evaluation

skills.description: Use when two DEG-prediction methods (one clustering-independent like singleCellHaystack, one clustering-based like Seurat FindAllMarkers) must be benchmarked on the same scRNA-seq dataset and their top gene lists compared for agreement.
skills.name: deg-method-rank-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: deg-method-rank-overlap-analysis Use when two DEG-prediction methods (one clustering-independent like singleCellHaystack, one clustering-based like Seurat FindAllMarkers) must be benchmarked on the same scRNA-seq dataset and their top gene lists compared for agreement. The goal is method benchmarking on artificial/simulated data with known ground-truth DEGs, where accuracy metrics (not rank agreement) are the appropriate evaluation You need DEG p-values that are not inflated by double use of gene expression data — both approaches here suffer p-value inflation when coordinates/clusters derive from the same expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Head-to-head comparison of clustering-independent DEG prediction (singleCellHaystack, Kullback-Leibler divergence) against clustering-based DEG calling (Seurat FindAllMarkers with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test) by compiling per-gene p-values and quantifying rank overlap of top-scoring genes, as done on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Head-to-head comparison of clustering-independent DEG prediction (singleCellHaystack, Kullback-Leibler divergence) against clustering-based DEG calling (Seurat FindAllMarkers with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test) by compiling per-gene p-values and quantifying rank overlap of top-scoring genes, as done on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is method benchmarking on artificial/simulated data with known ground-truth DEGs, where accuracy metrics (not rank agreement) are the appropriate evaluation You need DEG p-values that are not inflated by double use of gene expression data — both approaches here suffer p-value inflation when coordinates/clusters derive from the same expression matrix

skills.description: Use when you have simulated RNA-seq count data with known DE/non-DE labels and need to choose a consensus combination strategy (vote threshold vs combined-FDR) across DESeq2, NOISeq, and limma results.
skills.name: deg-method-vote-threshold-evaluation
skills.search_text: deg-method-vote-threshold-evaluation Use when you have simulated RNA-seq count data with known DE/non-DE labels and need to choose a consensus combination strategy (vote threshold vs combined-FDR) across DESeq2, NOISeq, and limma results. Data are real experimental datasets (e.g. Lafora or PMM2-CDG) with no ground-truth DE labels, so precision/recall/F-measure cannot be computed You need a final recommendation for a new organism, tissue, or experimental design — the optimal threshold of 2 is data-specific and the authors caution against extrapolating it as a general rule http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates how minimum-vote thresholds (1–4) for combining DEG calls from DESeq2, NOISeq, and limma in the DEgenes Hunter pipeline compare to the combined-FDR data-fusion criterion, using precision, recall, and F-measure against known truth labels on simulated RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Evaluates how minimum-vote thresholds (1–4) for combining DEG calls from DESeq2, NOISeq, and limma in the DEgenes Hunter pipeline compare to the combined-FDR data-fusion criterion, using precision, recall, and F-measure against known truth labels on simulated RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real experimental datasets (e.g. Lafora or PMM2-CDG) with no ground-truth DE labels, so precision/recall/F-measure cannot be computed You need a final recommendation for a new organism, tissue, or experimental design — the optimal threshold of 2 is data-specific and the authors caution against extrapolating it as a general rule

skills.search_text: deg-rank-binning-analysis Use when a ranked DEG list (sorted by p-value, e.g. log.p.vals from show_result_haystack) needs benchmarking against a curated marker database to test whether top hits are enriched for known cell-type markers. skills.when_to_use_negative: No ranked DEG list is available yet — this skill consumes singleCellHaystack output (haystack results sorted by log.p.vals), not raw count matrices or unprocessed scRNA-seq data Continuous expression values are the intended input — the method version described requires binary detection data (a gene is either detected or not in each cell), so continuous normalized counts are not directly supported No curated marker reference (e.g. CellMarker with publication counts) exists for the organism studied, making marker-enrichment validation impossible

skills.description: Use when a haystack run has completed and you need to extract, rank, and export its DEG results ordered by log p-values / D_KL divergence for downstream inspection or verification of the top-ranked gene.
skills.name: deg-result-ranking-and-export
skills.search_text: deg-result-ranking-and-export Use when a haystack run has completed and you need to extract, rank, and export its DEG results ordered by log p-values / D_KL divergence for downstream inspection or verification of the top-ranked gene. Genes detected in very few cells have not yet been filtered (genes with less than 10 cells with non-zero counts should be removed first) The expression data is continuous normalized read counts rather than binary detection data — the original method requires binary detection data (a gene is either detected or not in each cell) You need a newer, generalized version of the method — the default CRAN/GitHub master branch is version 1.0, not the version described in this paper (use the 'binary' branch instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Retrieves and ranks the results of a singleCellHaystack differential expression analysis by log p-values / Kullback-Leibler divergence (D_KL) and exports the ranked gene table (e.g. bone_marrow_deg_table.csv), so the most significant DEG can be verified. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Retrieves and ranks the results of a singleCellHaystack differential expression analysis by log p-values / Kullback-Leibler divergence (D_KL) and exports the ranked gene table (e.g. bone_marrow_deg_table.csv), so the most significant DEG can be verified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes detected in very few cells have not yet been filtered (genes with less than 10 cells with non-zero counts should be removed first) The expression data is continuous normalized read counts rather than binary detection data — the original method requires binary detection data (a gene is either detected or not in each cell) You need a newer, generalized version of the method — the default CRAN/GitHub master branch is version 1.0, not the version described in this paper (use the 'binary' branch instead)

skills.description: Use when you have two DEG result tables from alternative paired linear mixed model fits (e.g. with and without a kinship covariance random effect) and need to quantify how model specification changes detection at a fixed FDR cutoff such as 0.05.

skills.search_text: deg-set-overlap-and-agreement-analysis Use when you have two DEG result tables from alternative paired linear mixed model fits (e.g. with and without a kinship covariance random effect) and need to quantify how model specification changes detection at a fixed FDR cutoff such as 0.05. Barcodes are already known — use known-sequence demultiplexing mode (e.g. 'flexiplex -d 10x3v3 -k barcode_list.txt') instead of discovery mode Input is a gene-by-cell count matrix or already-demultiplexed BAM — there is no barcode discovery left to benchmark Data lack 10x-style cellular-barcode flanking structure, so a flanking-sequence-only discovery mode and inflection-point droplet filtering do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks barcode-discovery and demultiplexing tools (e.g. Flexiplex, BLAZE, scTagger, wf-single-cell) on noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ data by scoring each tool's discovered barcode set for sensitivity and specificity against short-read-derived whitelists treated as withheld truth, alongside wall-clock time and memory measurements. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Benchmarks barcode-discovery and demultiplexing tools (e.g. Flexiplex, BLAZE, scTagger, wf-single-cell) on noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ data by scoring each tool's discovered barcode set for sensitivity and specificity against short-read-derived whitelists treated as withheld truth, alongside wall-clock time and memory measurements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Barcodes are already known — use known-sequence demultiplexing mode (e.g. 'flexiplex -d 10x3v3 -k barcode_list.txt') instead of discovery mode Input is a gene-by-cell count matrix or already-demultiplexed BAM — there is no barcode discovery left to benchmark Data lack 10x-style cellular-barcode flanking structure, so a flanking-sequence-only discovery mode and inflection-point droplet filtering do not apply

skills.description: Use when a multiplexed scRNA-seq dataset has genetically distinct individuals pooled together, and per-barcode genotype-derived labels (singlet/doublet/negative, cell-free versus cell-containing) are needed as ground truth to benchmark cell-calling methods.
skills.name: demuxlet-genotype-based-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: demuxlet-genotype-based-demultiplexing Use when a multiplexed scRNA-seq dataset has genetically distinct individuals pooled together, and per-barcode genotype-derived labels (singlet/doublet/negative, cell-free versus cell-containing) are needed as ground truth to benchmark cell-calling methods. The dataset is not multiplexed across genetically distinct individuals (e.g. a single-donor sample), so genotype-based demultiplexing labels cannot be derived. Only HTO (cell hashing) information is available instead of genotypes; in that case HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative labels provide the ground truth rather than demuxlet. The goal is ambient RNA correction or gene-expression denoising rather than cell-calling benchmark labels; demuxlet does not provide expression correction (tools such as SoupX would be needed). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply demuxlet to a genome-aligned BAM file of a multiplexed PBMC scRNA-seq sample using a merged VCF to infer per-barcode genotype labels and singlet probabilities, providing ground-truth cell-containing versus cell-free labels for benchmarking cell-calling methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Apply demuxlet to a genome-aligned BAM file of a multiplexed PBMC scRNA-seq sample using a merged VCF to infer per-barcode genotype labels and singlet probabilities, providing ground-truth cell-containing versus cell-free labels for benchmarking cell-calling methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not multiplexed across genetically distinct individuals (e.g. a single-donor sample), so genotype-based demultiplexing labels cannot be derived. Only HTO (cell hashing) information is available instead of genotypes; in that case HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative labels provide the ground truth rather than demuxlet. The goal is ambient RNA correction or gene-expression denoising rather than cell-calling benchmark labels; demuxlet does not provide expression correction (tools such as SoupX would be needed).

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing demultiplexing methods (e.g., demuxmix vs HTODemux, hashedDrops, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, DemuxEM) and genotype-derived ground-truth labels from demuxlet are available for the same (HTOs x droplets) count matrix.
skills.name: demuxlet-ground-truth-matching
skills.search_text: demuxlet-ground-truth-matching Use when evaluating or comparing demultiplexing methods (e.g., demuxmix vs HTODemux, hashedDrops, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, DemuxEM) and genotype-derived ground-truth labels from demuxlet are available for the same (HTOs x droplets) count matrix. No genotype data are available to produce demuxlet-based high-confidence SSD ground truth for the same droplets The experiment is not oligonucleotide-barcoded (no HTO count matrix), so there is nothing to demultiplex against SSD labels You need de novo demultiplexing of a new sample rather than method benchmarking/evaluation against known labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark HTO-based demultiplexing methods by treating demuxlet-derived high-confidence singlet/doublet (SSD) genotype calls as ground truth, then scoring each method's droplet assignments with precisionSSD, sensitivitySSD, and F-score on attenuated human brain snRNA-seq HTO data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Benchmark HTO-based demultiplexing methods by treating demuxlet-derived high-confidence singlet/doublet (SSD) genotype calls as ground truth, then scoring each method's droplet assignments with precisionSSD, sensitivitySSD, and F-score on attenuated human brain snRNA-seq HTO data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No genotype data are available to produce demuxlet-based high-confidence SSD ground truth for the same droplets The experiment is not oligonucleotide-barcoded (no HTO count matrix), so there is nothing to demultiplex against SSD labels You need de novo demultiplexing of a new sample rather than method benchmarking/evaluation against known labels

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset of dendritic cell progenitors (CDP through preDC stages) must be checked for a branching event separating cDC1- versus cDC2-committed preDC subsets, and when benchmarking which trajectory method recovers that branch.

skills.search_text: dendritic-cell-progenitor-lineage-branching-analysis Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset of dendritic cell progenitors (CDP through preDC stages) must be checked for a branching event separating cDC1- versus cDC2-committed preDC subsets, and when benchmarking which trajectory method recovers that branch. Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support these (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell datasets in which specific subset information is not known — Mpath depends on signature genes of FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark of trajectory-inference methods (Mpath, SCUBA, monocle, diffusion map, PCA, conventional MST) on the mouse DC progenitor single-cell RNA-seq dataset to test which detects the preDC-stage branching into cDC1- and cDC2-committed subsets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Benchmark of trajectory-inference methods (Mpath, SCUBA, monocle, diffusion map, PCA, conventional MST) on the mouse DC progenitor single-cell RNA-seq dataset to test which detects the preDC-stage branching into cDC1- and cDC2-committed subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support these (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell datasets in which specific subset information is not known — Mpath depends on signature genes of FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction

skills.description: Use when FiRE-scored ~68k human PBMC profiles have yielded a rare-cell subset (~4238 cells) and you need to resolve which Villani dendritic sub-types (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) the rare dendritic clusters correspond to.
skills.name: dendritic-cell-subtype-annotation
skills.search_text: dendritic-cell-subtype-annotation Use when FiRE-scored ~68k human PBMC profiles have yielded a rare-cell subset (~4238 cells) and you need to resolve which Villani dendritic sub-types (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) the rare dendritic clusters correspond to. The goal is doublet detection: the article notes doublet rates vary between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application to doublet detection. The rare-cell pool contains outliers that must be separated from minor cell types: FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types, and outliers get submerged into the minor cell clusters when clustering with dropClust. You need all six Villani DC sub-types resolved: this skill confidently resolves only four (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) out of the six reported sub-types. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Resolves dendritic cell (DC) sub-types within FiRE-detected rare PBMC cells by clustering the rare cells with dropClust, identifying the exclusively dendritic clusters, and matching their differential genes to Villani DC sub-type reference signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Resolves dendritic cell (DC) sub-types within FiRE-detected rare PBMC cells by clustering the rare cells with dropClust, identifying the exclusively dendritic clusters, and matching their differential genes to Villani DC sub-type reference signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is doublet detection: the article notes doublet rates vary between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application to doublet detection. The rare-cell pool contains outliers that must be separated from minor cell types: FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types, and outliers get submerged into the minor cell clusters when clustering with dropClust. You need all six Villani DC sub-types resolved: this skill confidently resolves only four (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) out of the six reported sub-types.

skills.description: Use when a clustering-based trajectory method (e.g. Mpath) requires choosing a dendrogram cut depth and a diversity/aggregation cut, and you must confirm that downstream landmarks, branches, or networks are robust to those parameter choices.
skills.name: dendrogram-cut-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: dendrogram-cut-parameter-tuning Use when a clustering-based trajectory method (e.g. Mpath) requires choosing a dendrogram cut depth and a diversity/aggregation cut, and you must confirm that downstream landmarks, branches, or networks are robust to those parameter choices. The pipeline's conclusions depend on a parameterization that changes qualitatively across cuts — sensitivity analysis alone will not resolve this and the clustering definition must be re-specified. The method does not involve hierarchical clustering or a cut-parameter at all (e.g. data already summarized to fixed cell states) — there is nothing to tune. Development processes start from multiple independent progenitor cell types or subsets are unknown in highly heterogeneous data — Mpath does not yet support these settings, so tuning its cut parameters is moot. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A sensitivity-analysis skill for single-cell clustering pipelines: re-run the clustering/trajectory workflow across multiple dendrogram cut depths and diversity cut thresholds (e.g. 11-13 clusters and diversity cuts 0.5-0.7 in Mpath) to verify that derived landmarks and state transition networks are invariant to these arbitrary parameters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill for single-cell clustering pipelines: re-run the clustering/trajectory workflow across multiple dendrogram cut depths and diversity cut thresholds (e.g. 11-13 clusters and diversity cuts 0.5-0.7 in Mpath) to verify that derived landmarks and state transition networks are invariant to these arbitrary parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline's conclusions depend on a parameterization that changes qualitatively across cuts — sensitivity analysis alone will not resolve this and the clustering definition must be re-specified. The method does not involve hierarchical clustering or a cut-parameter at all (e.g. data already summarized to fixed cell states) — there is nothing to tune. Development processes start from multiple independent progenitor cell types or subsets are unknown in highly heterogeneous data — Mpath does not yet support these settings, so tuning its cut parameters is moot.

skills.description: Use when designating landmark clusters from single-cell expression data by cutting a Ward.D hclust dendrogram at multiple candidate k values and selecting the cut via a purity-versus-number-of-clusters inflection criterion.
skills.name: dendrogram-iterative-cutting
skills.search_text: dendrogram-iterative-cutting Use when designating landmark clusters from single-cell expression data by cutting a Ward.D hclust dendrogram at multiple candidate k values and selecting the cut via a purity-versus-number-of-clusters inflection criterion. The development process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types or the relevant subset information is unknown — Mpath does not yet support these cases No FACS-sort labels or other known subset annotations are available to compute cluster purity for choosing the cut http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Iteratively cut a hierarchical (agglomerative) cell clustering dendrogram over a range of candidate cluster counts to designate landmark clusters in Mpath, choosing the optimal cut where cluster purity (Shannon index of FACS-sort label composition) reaches its inflection point. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Iteratively cut a hierarchical (agglomerative) cell clustering dendrogram over a range of candidate cluster counts to designate landmark clusters in Mpath, choosing the optimal cut where cluster purity (Shannon index of FACS-sort label composition) reaches its inflection point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The development process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types or the relevant subset information is unknown — Mpath does not yet support these cases No FACS-sort labels or other known subset annotations are available to compute cluster purity for choosing the cut

skills.description: Use when you have a symmetric pairwise distance matrix (e.g., scDist distances between cell types) and need to cluster it hierarchically and render a dendrogram to check whether distances recapitulate known biological relationships such as immune cell lineages.
skills.name: dendrogram-visualization
skills.search_text: dendrogram-visualization Use when you have a symmetric pairwise distance matrix (e.g., scDist distances between cell types) and need to cluster it hierarchically and render a dendrogram to check whether distances recapitulate known biological relationships such as immune cell lineages. Distances were computed with a naive approach subject to individual-to-individual/cohort-to-cohort variability (e.g., without a mixed-effects model), since resulting dendrogram topology may reflect false-positive perturbations rather than true lineage structure. Cell-type clusters are over-clustered relative to condition-specific effects — scDist distances decay toward 0 with increasing cluster number, which would compress the dendrogram and mask lineage separation. The goal is differential state testing (which cell types change between conditions) rather than visualizing between-cell-type relationships; use scDist's DistPlot/p-values instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply hierarchical clustering (R stats::hclust, complete linkage) to a symmetric pairwise distance matrix — here the pairwise scDist distances between cell types from the COVID-19 dataset — and render the resulting dendrogram with ggplot2 so cell-type lineage structure (lymphoid vs myeloid grouping) can be visually validated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Apply hierarchical clustering (R stats::hclust, complete linkage) to a symmetric pairwise distance matrix — here the pairwise scDist distances between cell types from the COVID-19 dataset — and render the resulting dendrogram with ggplot2 so cell-type lineage structure (lymphoid vs myeloid grouping) can be visually validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Distances were computed with a naive approach subject to individual-to-individual/cohort-to-cohort variability (e.g., without a mixed-effects model), since resulting dendrogram topology may reflect false-positive perturbations rather than true lineage structure. Cell-type clusters are over-clustered relative to condition-specific effects — scDist distances decay toward 0 with increasing cluster number, which would compress the dendrogram and mask lineage separation. The goal is differential state testing (which cell types change between conditions) rather than visualizing between-cell-type relationships; use scDist's DistPlot/p-values instead.

skills.description: Use when predicting single-cell drug responses from scRNA-seq by transferring a model trained on bulk cell-line drug response data (GDSC/CCLE), e.g. scoring GSE110894 AML cells for I.BET.762 sensitivity.
skills.name: denoising-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: denoising-autoencoder-training Use when predicting single-cell drug responses from scRNA-seq by transferring a model trained on bulk cell-line drug response data (GDSC/CCLE), e.g. scoring GSE110894 AML cells for I.BET.762 sensitivity. Input lacks bulk-level drug response training labels (the transfer relies on GDSC/CCLE-style bulk response annotations); scDEAL cannot be trained without them Task is generic single-cell clustering or dimensionality reduction without a drug-response prediction goal — the DaNN/MMD transfer machinery is unnecessary overhead The scRNA-seq data is mouse and homologous gene mapping was not performed (in the mouse case study only homologous genes were kept before applying the human-trained model) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains scDEAL's denoising-autoencoder (DAE) encoders for bulk and single-cell RNA-seq (encoder hidden dims 256,128; bottleneck 512; dropout 0.1) together with a drug-response predictor, so bulk-trained drug response knowledge can be transferred to scRNA-seq cells via a DaNN/MMD loss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Trains scDEAL's denoising-autoencoder (DAE) encoders for bulk and single-cell RNA-seq (encoder hidden dims 256,128; bottleneck 512; dropout 0.1) together with a drug-response predictor, so bulk-trained drug response knowledge can be transferred to scRNA-seq cells via a DaNN/MMD loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks bulk-level drug response training labels (the transfer relies on GDSC/CCLE-style bulk response annotations); scDEAL cannot be trained without them Task is generic single-cell clustering or dimensionality reduction without a drug-response prediction goal — the DaNN/MMD transfer machinery is unnecessary overhead The scRNA-seq data is mouse and homologous gene mapping was not performed (in the mouse case study only homologous genes were kept before applying the human-trained model)

skills.description: Use when you need a denoised, low-dimensional latent embedding of a scRNA-seq count matrix for downstream cell clustering, especially with dropout-heavy zero-inflated counts.
skills.name: denoising-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: denoising-autoencoder-training Use when you need a denoised, low-dimensional latent embedding of a scRNA-seq count matrix for downstream cell clustering, especially with dropout-heavy zero-inflated counts. Input is not a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already-normalized feature tables or bulk RNA-seq), since the ZINB likelihood models zero-inflated single-cell counts. The goal is consensus clustering itself rather than latent feature learning — use the bipartite graph ensemble clustering module (BC.m/BGEC.m) on the learned embedding instead. Only small numbers of genes are of interest and dimensionality reduction to a compressed latent space is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train scBGEDA's single-cell dual denoising autoencoder (SDDA), which corrupts scRNA-seq counts with Gaussian noise and learns a compressed latent representation via a ZINB master decoder (estimating pi, mu, theta) plus an MSE follower decoder, jointly optimized as lambda*(-log ZINB) + gamma*MSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Train scBGEDA's single-cell dual denoising autoencoder (SDDA), which corrupts scRNA-seq counts with Gaussian noise and learns a compressed latent representation via a ZINB master decoder (estimating pi, mu, theta) plus an MSE follower decoder, jointly optimized as lambda*(-log ZINB) + gamma*MSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. already-normalized feature tables or bulk RNA-seq), since the ZINB likelihood models zero-inflated single-cell counts. The goal is consensus clustering itself rather than latent feature learning — use the bipartite graph ensemble clustering module (BC.m/BGEC.m) on the learned embedding instead. Only small numbers of genes are of interest and dimensionality reduction to a compressed latent space is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you need to compare scRNA-seq denoising/imputation methods (DCA vs MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) on count matrices, either by recovery of a known signal (e.g., time-correlated genes after simulated dropout) or by runtime scaling across downsampled cell counts.
skills.name: denoising-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: denoising-method-benchmarking Use when you need to compare scRNA-seq denoising/imputation methods (DCA vs MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) on count matrices, either by recovery of a known signal (e.g., time-correlated genes after simulated dropout) or by runtime scaling across downsampled cell counts. The input is already a denoised/imputed matrix or normalized expression values — DCA and this benchmark expect raw integer counts so the NB/ZINB noise model applies A reliable ground truth for real single-cell data is required but unavailable — the article notes 'the evaluation of denoising is difficult because the definition of a ground truth can be challenging for real data' You only need imputation of explicitly labeled missing values in a generic (non-count) table — classical imputation methods may be more appropriate since scRNA-seq requires distinguishing true (celltype-specific) from false (dropout) zeros http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill for comparing scRNA-seq denoising/imputation methods — DCA (deep count autoencoder with ZINB/NB loss) against MAGIC, SAVER and scImpute — on quality (recovery of known signal) and runtime scaling, as demonstrated in the DCA paper (Eraslan et al., Nature Communications 2019). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing scRNA-seq denoising/imputation methods — DCA (deep count autoencoder with ZINB/NB loss) against MAGIC, SAVER and scImpute — on quality (recovery of known signal) and runtime scaling, as demonstrated in the DCA paper (Eraslan et al., Nature Communications 2019).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a denoised/imputed matrix or normalized expression values — DCA and this benchmark expect raw integer counts so the NB/ZINB noise model applies A reliable ground truth for real single-cell data is required but unavailable — the article notes 'the evaluation of denoising is difficult because the definition of a ground truth can be challenging for real data' You only need imputation of explicitly labeled missing values in a generic (non-count) table — classical imputation methods may be more appropriate since scRNA-seq requires distinguishing true (celltype-specific) from false (dropout) zeros

skills.description: Use when clustering paired single-cell multimodal data (CITE-seq RNA+ADT or SMAGE-seq RNA+ATAC) with an end-to-end deep model that jointly optimizes reconstruction, KL, and clustering losses.
skills.name: denoising-multimodal-autoencoder-implementation
skills.search_text: denoising-multimodal-autoencoder-implementation Use when clustering paired single-cell multimodal data (CITE-seq RNA+ADT or SMAGE-seq RNA+ATAC) with an end-to-end deep model that jointly optimizes reconstruction, KL, and clustering losses. When a joint embedding suffices without clustering optimization — the article notes joint-embedding methods 'are not designed and optimized for clustering', but if clustering is not the goal, a model like scMM or Cobolt is more appropriate When the number of clusters K is unknown and cannot be estimated by the user — scMDC requires the user to specify K and provides no automatic estimation On single-modal scRNA-seq data where single-omic tools (SC3, Tscan, Specter) are sufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Implement the scMDC denoising multimodal autoencoder in PyTorch: a shared encoder over concatenated modalities, modality-specific decoders, Gaussian corruption, ZINB reconstruction loss, t-distribution KL loss, and a deep K-means head, all optimized end-to-end for single-cell multi-omics clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35031-9
skills.summary: Implement the scMDC denoising multimodal autoencoder in PyTorch: a shared encoder over concatenated modalities, modality-specific decoders, Gaussian corruption, ZINB reconstruction loss, t-distribution KL loss, and a deep K-means head, all optimized end-to-end for single-cell multi-omics clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a joint embedding suffices without clustering optimization — the article notes joint-embedding methods 'are not designed and optimized for clustering', but if clustering is not the goal, a model like scMM or Cobolt is more appropriate When the number of clusters K is unknown and cannot be estimated by the user — scMDC requires the user to specify K and provides no automatic estimation On single-modal scRNA-seq data where single-omic tools (SC3, Tscan, Specter) are sufficient

skills.description: Use when after Tempo Step 1 has produced cell phase posterior distributions for a scRNA-seq dataset, you must expand the circadian cycler set by identifying which previously non-cycling genes are described by phase variation.
skills.name: denovo-ccg-identification
skills.search_text: denovo-ccg-identification Use when after Tempo Step 1 has produced cell phase posterior distributions for a scRNA-seq dataset, you must expand the circadian cycler set by identifying which previously non-cycling genes are described by phase variation. When the goal is to refine phases rather than discover de novo cyclers — this Step 2 module only assesses genes not currently identified as cyclers; already-designated cycling genes are not refiltered here. When Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions are unavailable or unreliable (e.g., poor phase estimates on droplet-based scRNA-seq), since the gene fit is conditioned on the Step 1 phase estimates. When a CCG is expected to have strongly non-sinusoidal expression, since the article notes the de novo cycler identification may be limited by assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tempo's Step 2 module that fits approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions to genes not currently designated as cyclers, conditioned on the Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, and selects de novo clock-controlled genes (CCGs) using the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and the non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction (Fig. 2c). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Tempo's Step 2 module that fits approximate sinusoidal amplitude parameter distributions to genes not currently designated as cyclers, conditioned on the Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions, and selects de novo clock-controlled genes (CCGs) using the MAP amplitude Pearson residual and the non-zero-amplitude MAP fraction (Fig. 2c).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to refine phases rather than discover de novo cyclers — this Step 2 module only assesses genes not currently identified as cyclers; already-designated cycling genes are not refiltered here. When Step 1 cell phase posterior distributions are unavailable or unreliable (e.g., poor phase estimates on droplet-based scRNA-seq), since the gene fit is conditioned on the Step 1 phase estimates. When a CCG is expected to have strongly non-sinusoidal expression, since the article notes the de novo cycler identification may be limited by assuming 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means.

skills.description: Use when you have a subpopulation-specific directed TF-target score matrix (e.g., from DC3 deconvolved expression, ATAC, and HiChIP profiles) and need to identify the densely cross-regulating core regulatory network plus its upstream/downstream effectors.
skills.name: dense-subnetwork-extraction
skills.search_text: dense-subnetwork-extraction Use when you have a subpopulation-specific directed TF-target score matrix (e.g., from DC3 deconvolved expression, ATAC, and HiChIP profiles) and need to identify the densely cross-regulating core regulatory network plus its upstream/downstream effectors. Input is raw scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq/HiChIP data rather than a deconvolved, subpopulation-specific regulatory network — run DC3 deconvolution and coupled clustering first Interaction graph is undirected or lacks TF-target orientation/weights, since the quadratic program requires a directed weighted W_ij The goal is subpopulation identification or clustering rather than distilling regulatory circuitry from an existing subpopulation-specific network http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Extracts a statistically dense subnetwork from each subpopulation-specific TF-gene regulatory network by solving a quadratic program over the directed edge-weight matrix, then partitions it into core, upstream, and downstream TF sets. It distills DC3's deconvolved expression/accessibility/HiChIP profiles into the core regulatory circuitry that maintains each cellular state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Extracts a statistically dense subnetwork from each subpopulation-specific TF-gene regulatory network by solving a quadratic program over the directed edge-weight matrix, then partitions it into core, upstream, and downstream TF sets. It distills DC3's deconvolved expression/accessibility/HiChIP profiles into the core regulatory circuitry that maintains each cellular state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq/HiChIP data rather than a deconvolved, subpopulation-specific regulatory network — run DC3 deconvolution and coupled clustering first Interaction graph is undirected or lacks TF-target orientation/weights, since the quadratic program requires a directed weighted W_ij The goal is subpopulation identification or clustering rather than distilling regulatory circuitry from an existing subpopulation-specific network

skills.description: Use when training a self-supervised feature encoder on a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix of highly variable genes and a DenseNet-based MoCo architecture with contrastive queue settings must be configured.
skills.name: densenet-encoder-architecture-configuration
skills.search_text: densenet-encoder-architecture-configuration Use when training a self-supervised feature encoder on a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix of highly variable genes and a DenseNet-based MoCo architecture with contrastive queue settings must be configured. The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so deep-encoder training is inappropriate for small scRNA-seq datasets Batch effects are present and uncorrected: Miscell does not include batch correction, so the input expression matrix must be batch-corrected beforehand The input is raw unnormalized counts: the README recommends normalizing features before training the model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Configure a DenseNet latent feature encoder (densenet11/21/29/63 variants) with an MLP projection head for MoCo-style self-supervised representation learning on single-cell gene expression matrices, as implemented in Miscell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Configure a DenseNet latent feature encoder (densenet11/21/29/63 variants) with an MLP projection head for MoCo-style self-supervised representation learning on single-cell gene expression matrices, as implemented in Miscell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so deep-encoder training is inappropriate for small scRNA-seq datasets Batch effects are present and uncorrected: Miscell does not include batch correction, so the input expression matrix must be batch-corrected beforehand The input is raw unnormalized counts: the README recommends normalizing features before training the model

skills.description: Use when constructing a single-cell cell–cell network from archetypal/multilevel decomposition outputs (H*) and you need neighborhood sizes to adapt to local density and heterogeneity rather than fixing k in advance.
skills.name: density-adaptive-neighbor-selection
skills.search_text: density-adaptive-neighbor-selection Use when constructing a single-cell cell–cell network from archetypal/multilevel decomposition outputs (H*) and you need neighborhood sizes to adapt to local density and heterogeneity rather than fixing k in advance. Input is raw or preprocessed gene-expression data and no archetypal decomposition (H*) has been computed yet — the k*-NN metric is defined in the archetypal cell space, not gene space You need a standard fixed-k graph (e.g., scRNA kNN used by standard Scanpy clustering) — k*-NN explicitly removes the fixed-neighbor-count assumption Data are chromatin accessibility peaks without prior reduction (LSI/chromVAR/ACTION) — the extremely sparse, high-dimensional peak matrix is not a suitable direct input http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 ACTIONet's k*-NN step builds the cell–cell similarity network by solving a per-node optimal neighbor-selection problem in the archetypal metric space (square-root Jensen–Shannon distances over the normalized multilevel encoding H*), so each cell receives a density-adaptive neighbor count k* instead of a fixed k. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: ACTIONet's k*-NN step builds the cell–cell similarity network by solving a per-node optimal neighbor-selection problem in the archetypal metric space (square-root Jensen–Shannon distances over the normalized multilevel encoding H*), so each cell receives a density-adaptive neighbor count k* instead of a fixed k.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or preprocessed gene-expression data and no archetypal decomposition (H*) has been computed yet — the k*-NN metric is defined in the archetypal cell space, not gene space You need a standard fixed-k graph (e.g., scRNA kNN used by standard Scanpy clustering) — k*-NN explicitly removes the fixed-neighbor-count assumption Data are chromatin accessibility peaks without prior reduction (LSI/chromVAR/ACTION) — the extremely sparse, high-dimensional peak matrix is not a suitable direct input

skills.name: density-based-cluster-seed-selection
skills.search_text: density-based-cluster-seed-selection Use when initializing label-propagation clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data without a predetermined number of cell types, and seed cells must be selected from a directed kNN graph built on a quantitative cell-landmark matrix. Input is a raw gene-by-cell expression matrix that has not yet been preprocessed and converted into the Q1/Q2 cell-landmark representations by scQA's LC1 and LC2 modules You already know the number of cell types and want a method that requires a predetermined cluster count — scQA's seed-based label propagation is designed to avoid specifying the number of cell types in advance The goal is clustering on the raw expression values rather than the landmark-based representation, where higher-density nodes are not meaningful seeds http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A seed-generation step from the scQA CC module that identifies authentic initial cluster cores by grouping cells with identical qualitative (Q1) row vectors, ranking nodes by neighbor-averaged density computed on the quantitative (Q2) matrix, and merging mutually neighboring seed candidates before label propagation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: A seed-generation step from the scQA CC module that identifies authentic initial cluster cores by grouping cells with identical qualitative (Q1) row vectors, ranking nodes by neighbor-averaged density computed on the quantitative (Q2) matrix, and merging mutually neighboring seed candidates before label propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw gene-by-cell expression matrix that has not yet been preprocessed and converted into the Q1/Q2 cell-landmark representations by scQA's LC1 and LC2 modules You already know the number of cell types and want a method that requires a predetermined cluster count — scQA's seed-based label propagation is designed to avoid specifying the number of cell types in advance The goal is clustering on the raw expression values rather than the landmark-based representation, where higher-density nodes are not meaningful seeds

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell expression data with a prior (e.g. RaceID3-derived) cluster assignment and need a 2D embedding whose topology encodes both class separation and density-gradient-based differentiation paths.
skills.name: density-gradient-edge-construction
skills.search_text: density-gradient-edge-construction Use when you have single-cell expression data with a prior (e.g. RaceID3-derived) cluster assignment and need a 2D embedding whose topology encodes both class separation and density-gradient-based differentiation paths. When no prior cluster/class assignment exists — the knn and k_shift edges both depend on discrete labels for each instance When a quantitative pseudotime ordering (rather than a qualitative 2D hierarchy visualization) is the required output — pseudotime methods like TSCAN or Monocle2 are the appropriate alternatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Construction of the two graph edge types used by GraphDDP/GraphEmbed: 'knn' edges linking each instance to its k-th nearest same-class neighbor and 'k_shift' edges linking toward denser instances of a different class, so a force-based (Kamada–Kawai) layout jointly reveals cluster membership and differentiation trajectories in single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Construction of the two graph edge types used by GraphDDP/GraphEmbed: 'knn' edges linking each instance to its k-th nearest same-class neighbor and 'k_shift' edges linking toward denser instances of a different class, so a force-based (Kamada–Kawai) layout jointly reveals cluster membership and differentiation trajectories in single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior cluster/class assignment exists — the knn and k_shift edges both depend on discrete labels for each instance When a quantitative pseudotime ordering (rather than a qualitative 2D hierarchy visualization) is the required output — pseudotime methods like TSCAN or Monocle2 are the appropriate alternatives
