skills.search_text: density-gradient-shift-edge-interpretation Use when a graph-embedding visualization with prior class labels must reveal continuous differentiation orderings between clusters, e.g. resolving meta-cluster C7-C1 in myeloid progenitor single-cell data. When the goal is pseudotime per-cell ordering rather than cluster-level pathway visualization — tools like TSCAN, Monocle2 or Wishbone build MST/pseudotime trajectories instead of shift-edge layouts When no prior class/cluster labels exist for the instances, since both knn and k_shift edges are defined relative to class labels When class hulls are naturally well separated (clean data): the README says values of 0.5-1 for -c suit clean data; forcing -c 5-30 is meant for noisy data needing strong separation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets the k_shift (density-gradient) edges of a GraphDDP/GraphEmbed 2D layout to order classes along differentiation pathways, using cross-class shift-edge counts and ternary confusion scores (e.g. 0.06 for resolved C5-C6-C7 vs 0.72 for unresolved C2-C3-C4) in the Paul et al. myeloid progenitor data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Interprets the k_shift (density-gradient) edges of a GraphDDP/GraphEmbed 2D layout to order classes along differentiation pathways, using cross-class shift-edge counts and ternary confusion scores (e.g. 0.06 for resolved C5-C6-C7 vs 0.72 for unresolved C2-C3-C4) in the Paul et al. myeloid progenitor data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pseudotime per-cell ordering rather than cluster-level pathway visualization — tools like TSCAN, Monocle2 or Wishbone build MST/pseudotime trajectories instead of shift-edge layouts When no prior class/cluster labels exist for the instances, since both knn and k_shift edges are defined relative to class labels When class hulls are naturally well separated (clean data): the README says values of 0.5-1 for -c suit clean data; forcing -c 5-30 is meant for noisy data needing strong separation

skills.description: Use when tuning DUBStepR feature selection on scRNA-seq data without reliable cell type labels: sweeping feature set sizes and needing a label-free criterion whose argmax agrees with the silhouette index.
skills.name: density-index-computation-pc-space
skills.search_text: density-index-computation-pc-space Use when tuning DUBStepR feature selection on scRNA-seq data without reliable cell type labels: sweeping feature set sizes and needing a label-free criterion whose argmax agrees with the silhouette index. Cell type labels are fully trusted and available, making direct silhouette-index maximization feasible without a label-free proxy The pipeline does not use DUBStepR-ordered feature sets or PC-space embeddings (k = 10, num.pcs = 20), since the DI-SI agreement was established in that setting The task is feature ranking itself rather than choosing the feature set size — use DUBStepR's getOptimalFeatureSet/elbow-point machinery instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the Density Index (DI), a label-free measure of clustering inhomogeneity in PCA space, as the root-mean-squared pairwise distance over the mean k-NN distance, and uses its maximum over feature set sizes as a proxy for the silhouette index to select the optimal DUBStepR feature set size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Computes the Density Index (DI), a label-free measure of clustering inhomogeneity in PCA space, as the root-mean-squared pairwise distance over the mean k-NN distance, and uses its maximum over feature set sizes as a proxy for the silhouette index to select the optimal DUBStepR feature set size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type labels are fully trusted and available, making direct silhouette-index maximization feasible without a label-free proxy The pipeline does not use DUBStepR-ordered feature sets or PC-space embeddings (k = 10, num.pcs = 20), since the DI-SI agreement was established in that setting The task is feature ranking itself rather than choosing the feature set size — use DUBStepR's getOptimalFeatureSet/elbow-point machinery instead

skills.description: Use when running DUBStepR with optimise.features = TRUE and you must decide how many correlated feature genes to keep beyond the seed set, e.g. after computing a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix on log-normalized scRNA-seq counts.
skills.name: density-index-optimization
skills.search_text: density-index-optimization Use when running DUBStepR with optimise.features = TRUE and you must decide how many correlated feature genes to keep beyond the seed set, e.g. after computing a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix on log-normalized scRNA-seq counts. The goal is differential expression testing or marker ranking, not choosing a gene subset for cell clustering — the Density Index optimizes cluster separation, not DE significance. Input is already a fixed feature table or a predefined marker list with no need to choose a set size. The dataset lacks cell-type structure where marker-gene correlations are expected (DUBStepR assumes cell-type-specific marker genes are well correlated). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 DUBStepR's feature-set size optimization: expand the minimally redundant stepwise-regression seed genes by guilt-by-association and select the gene set size that maximizes the Density Index as the optimal feature set for clustering single-cell RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: DUBStepR's feature-set size optimization: expand the minimally redundant stepwise-regression seed genes by guilt-by-association and select the gene set size that maximizes the Density Index as the optimal feature set for clustering single-cell RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression testing or marker ranking, not choosing a gene subset for cell clustering — the Density Index optimizes cluster separation, not DE significance. Input is already a fixed feature table or a predefined marker list with no need to choose a set size. The dataset lacks cell-type structure where marker-gene correlations are expected (DUBStepR assumes cell-type-specific marker genes are well correlated).

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq cells genotyped for an expressed somatic SNV (e.g., via cb_sniffer or Vartrix on _counts_UB.tsv data) and want to test which genes track a mutant subclone across the whole sample, including non-genotyped cells.
skills.name: density-regression-gene-expression-association
skills.search_text: density-regression-gene-expression-association Use when you have scRNA-seq cells genotyped for an expressed somatic SNV (e.g., via cb_sniffer or Vartrix on _counts_UB.tsv data) and want to test which genes track a mutant subclone across the whole sample, including non-genotyped cells. The sample lacks expressed somatic SNVs — in AML, CNAs are rare and CNAs rarely reflect the complete clonal architecture, so mutation-based subclone labels require tumor-specific SNVs discovered by eWGS of paired tumor/normal samples. Only genotyped cells are of interest and you do not intend to leverage expression information from the additional, non-genotyped cells in the sample. The goal is variant calling itself rather than expression-phenotype association — Vartrix does not perform variant calling; variants must be pre-called (e.g., from eWGS of tumor/normal pairs). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Regresses single-cell gene expression on a continuous local density of cells expressing a subclonal mutation (e.g., GATA2R361C in AML sample 721214) within the embedded/clustered expression space, controlling for the mutant gene's own expression and covariates, to identify genes whose expression is associated with the subclone (FDR < 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Regresses single-cell gene expression on a continuous local density of cells expressing a subclonal mutation (e.g., GATA2R361C in AML sample 721214) within the embedded/clustered expression space, controlling for the mutant gene's own expression and covariates, to identify genes whose expression is associated with the subclone (FDR < 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample lacks expressed somatic SNVs — in AML, CNAs are rare and CNAs rarely reflect the complete clonal architecture, so mutation-based subclone labels require tumor-specific SNVs discovered by eWGS of paired tumor/normal samples. Only genotyped cells are of interest and you do not intend to leverage expression information from the additional, non-genotyped cells in the sample. The goal is variant calling itself rather than expression-phenotype association — Vartrix does not perform variant calling; variants must be pre-called (e.g., from eWGS of tumor/normal pairs).

skills.search_text: dentate-gyrus-granule-cell-trajectory-analysis Use when applying CellPath to the dentate-gyrus dataset (GSE95753, P12/P35, ~2,930 cells) to extract multiple high-resolution granule-cell trajectories with RNA velocity and quantify DE genes along within-population paths. skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not the dentate-gyrus neurogenesis data or lacks spliced/unspliced layers needed for scVelo velocity estimation The goal is a single fixed-topology trajectory rather than multiple high-resolution paths including within-population sub-flows Velocity should not be estimated (e.g., no velocity desired); CellPath's paths depend on RNA velocity, and its performance is limited by velocity inference accuracy

skills.description: Use when you need to rank or select candidate splitting variables at nodes of a DIPM classification tree or forest for precision-medicine subgroup identification, from fitted dipm tree structures over a covariate dataset.
skills.name: depth-importance-score-computation
skills.search_text: depth-importance-score-computation Use when you need to rank or select candidate splitting variables at nodes of a DIPM classification tree or forest for precision-medicine subgroup identification, from fitted dipm tree structures over a covariate dataset. When the goal is pruning an already-fit DIPM tree rather than ranking splitting variables — use pmprune(tree) instead When the analysis is survival-model subgrouping rather than DIPM classification-tree splitting — spmtree is the sibling method in the package for other tree types When the input is raw unlabeled data with no treatment-assignment outcome to partition — DIPM requires a classification outcome to grow the tree http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the DIPM depth variable importance score (Equation 1), score(T,j) = sum over nodes t split by variable j of 2^{-L(t)} * Gt, which weights each split by the exponentially decaying depth factor 2^{-L(t)} times the split effect statistic Gt, so shallower splits contribute more to variable ranking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: Computes the DIPM depth variable importance score (Equation 1), score(T,j) = sum over nodes t split by variable j of 2^{-L(t)} * Gt, which weights each split by the exponentially decaying depth factor 2^{-L(t)} times the split effect statistic Gt, so shallower splits contribute more to variable ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pruning an already-fit DIPM tree rather than ranking splitting variables — use pmprune(tree) instead When the analysis is survival-model subgrouping rather than DIPM classification-tree splitting — spmtree is the sibling method in the package for other tree types When the input is raw unlabeled data with no treatment-assignment outcome to partition — DIPM requires a classification outcome to grow the tree

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered DESeq2 results data frame (gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj) and defined gene sets (e.g. seed-match targets vs. non-targets, or miRNA predicted targets vs. background) and need to test whether the target set shows a cumulative positive or negative log2FC shift.
skills.name: deseq2-log2foldchange-ecdf-comparison
skills.search_text: deseq2-log2foldchange-ecdf-comparison Use when you have a filtered DESeq2 results data frame (gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj) and defined gene sets (e.g. seed-match targets vs. non-targets, or miRNA predicted targets vs. background) and need to test whether the target set shows a cumulative positive or negative log2FC shift. Input is raw counts or an unfiltered DESeq2 results table that has not been passed through filter_res — the ECDF comparison expects a filtered data frame with gene_id, log2FoldChange, and padj The analysis goal is detecting seed matches in transcript sequences itself rather than testing cumulative expression shifts — use SeedMatchR()/full_search() for sequence search instead Only a single differentially expressed gene is of interest (no gene-set versus background distribution) — a per-gene differential test, not an ECDF shift test, is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compare the empirical cumulative distribution of DESeq2 log2FoldChange values between a seed-target gene set and a background gene set, testing for cumulative differential expression shifts with KS, Wasserstein, DTS, or Wilcoxon statistics via SeedMatchR's deseq_fc_ecdf. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae011
skills.summary: Compare the empirical cumulative distribution of DESeq2 log2FoldChange values between a seed-target gene set and a background gene set, testing for cumulative differential expression shifts with KS, Wasserstein, DTS, or Wilcoxon statistics via SeedMatchR's deseq_fc_ecdf.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or an unfiltered DESeq2 results table that has not been passed through filter_res — the ECDF comparison expects a filtered data frame with gene_id, log2FoldChange, and padj The analysis goal is detecting seed matches in transcript sequences itself rather than testing cumulative expression shifts — use SeedMatchR()/full_search() for sequence search instead Only a single differentially expressed gene is of interest (no gene-set versus background distribution) — a per-gene differential test, not an ECDF shift test, is appropriate

skills.search_text: deseq2-result-filtering Use when a raw DESeq2 results data.frame (e.g., 32883-row Schlegel_2022_Ttr_D1_30mkg output) must be cleaned of NA rows and thresholded on log2FoldChange, padj, and baseMean before seed-match counting or deseq_fc_ecdf. Input is already a filtered, seed-match-annotated results frame — re-filtering would silently discard rows used as ECDF background gene sets The differential expression table lacks gene_id, log2FoldChange, or padj columns, so SeedMatchR()'s res argument cannot map seed counts onto it The analysis targets non-DESeq2 quantification outputs (e.g., raw count matrices) rather than a DESeq2 results object http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filter DESeq2 differential expression results (e.g., the Schlegel_2022_Ttr_* tables from GSE184929) with SeedMatchR::filter_res before seed-match annotation, dropping NA entries and applying log2FoldChange/padj/baseMean cutoffs so downstream ECDF/KS analyses operate on a clean results frame. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae011
skills.summary: Filter DESeq2 differential expression results (e.g., the Schlegel_2022_Ttr_* tables from GSE184929) with SeedMatchR::filter_res before seed-match annotation, dropping NA entries and applying log2FoldChange/padj/baseMean cutoffs so downstream ECDF/KS analyses operate on a clean results frame.

skills.search_text: deseq2-wald-statistic-gene-specificity-scoring Use when you need to quantify how specifically a set of marker genes (e.g., the 55 uniquely assigned human liver marker genes) maps to clusters produced by two or more alternative clustering solutions, and to test whether one solution yields higher marker-gene specificity. skills.search_text: deseq2-wald-test-count-modeling Use when raw UMI count data for single cells are split into two pre-defined clone groups (e.g., by mtDNA variants from MQuad/vireoSNP) and you need a ranked DE gene list with FDR control. skills.summary: Reconstructs the pseudo-temporal ordering of individual cells along the developmental trajectories generated by Mpath, by projecting cells assigned to transitions between neighbouring landmark states onto the edges of the landmark graph. This final Mpath step is what reveals phase-dependent waves of gene regulation and proliferation-to-differentiation switches during development.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development processes start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets where specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to this setting You need trajectory inference without pre-defined landmark states; this skill orders cells on an already-constructed Mpath landmark graph rather than building trajectories from scratch

skills.search_text: developmental-trajectory-visualization Use when you have a dropout-affected scRNA-seq matrix from a differentiating or developing cell population (e.g., zebrafish embryos, embryoid bodies) and need to recover pseudotime ordering and state transitions that imputation may distort. skills.description: Use when you have two competing cell-distance/similarity measures over the same labeled cells and need to quantify and plot which one separates same-type cells more strongly than random expectation (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity vs. HVG+PCA Euclidean distance).

skills.search_text: deviation-distribution-visualization Use when you have two competing cell-distance/similarity measures over the same labeled cells and need to quantify and plot which one separates same-type cells more strongly than random expectation (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity vs. HVG+PCA Euclidean distance). The two distance/similarity methods are not computed on the same set of cells with common cell-type labels — the permutation null must be comparable across methods. skills.summary: Quantifies cell-type abundance shifts between disease conditions by computing per-cell differential abundance (DA-seq) scores over a kNN graph built on a scMerge2-integrated single-cell embedding, then aggregating scores per annotated cell type. skills.name: differential-activity-testing-along-1d-trajectory
skills.search_text: differential-activity-testing-along-1d-trajectory Use when single-cell RNA-seq data have been ordered along a 1D pseudotime trajectory (e.g. monocle3 learn_graph/order_cells from DN to SP thymocytes) and you need genes with biased expression along that axis rather than cluster-marker DEGs. Comparing multiple conditions (e.g. wild-type vs knockout): the authors note such comparisons cannot easily be conducted with singleCellHaystack. You need results integrated into a cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analysis — cluster-based DEG prediction approaches are more straightforward for that. Spatial transcriptomics where raw speed matters most — SPARK-X is faster, though singleCellHaystack is more sensitive. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply singleCellHaystack (R/CRAN or Python) to a single-cell expression matrix with 1D pseudotime coordinates to predict genes (or other features) whose activity is non-randomly positioned along the trajectory, without cluster-based DE comparisons. Top-ranked DEGs can then be partitioned into expression-pattern modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2

Top-ranked DEGs can then be partitioned into expression-pattern modules.

skills.description: Use when a ribosome profiling pipeline has produced a per-transcript count matrix (e.g. from htseq-count) and conditions are defined in config.yaml, and you need DESeq2-based differential calls plus a consolidated HTML report.
skills.name: differential-analysis-html-reporting
skills.search_text: differential-analysis-html-reporting Use when a ribosome profiling pipeline has produced a per-transcript count matrix (e.g. from htseq-count) and conditions are defined in config.yaml, and you need DESeq2-based differential calls plus a consolidated HTML report. Input is already a differential-expression result table or a normalized expression matrix — this skill expects raw per-transcript counts from htseq-count. Samples failed replicate validation (PCA / Spearman correlation) or lack CDS enrichment / metagene periodicity; RiboDoc guidance is to remove low-quality samples and rerun before trusting differential calls. Only P-site offset estimation or read-length QC is needed — use riboWaltz/TRiP-based skills instead of the DESeq2 reporting step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run DESeq2 differential expression on RiboDoc's ribosome profiling count matrix (estimateSizeFactors, estimateDispersions, nbinomWaldTest), apply user-configured p-val and log2FoldChange thresholds, and assemble result tables and QC/diagnostic plots into an HTML report. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: Run DESeq2 differential expression on RiboDoc's ribosome profiling count matrix (estimateSizeFactors, estimateDispersions, nbinomWaldTest), apply user-configured p-val and log2FoldChange thresholds, and assemble result tables and QC/diagnostic plots into an HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a differential-expression result table or a normalized expression matrix — this skill expects raw per-transcript counts from htseq-count. Samples failed replicate validation (PCA / Spearman correlation) or lack CDS enrichment / metagene periodicity; RiboDoc guidance is to remove low-quality samples and rerun before trusting differential calls. Only P-site offset estimation or read-length QC is needed — use riboWaltz/TRiP-based skills instead of the DESeq2 reporting step.

skills.description: Use when you have an imputed 3' UTR RUD (relative usage of distal poly(A) site) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data with layer annotations and need to classify genes with spatial APA usage patterns.
skills.name: differential-apa-usage-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-apa-usage-analysis Use when you have an imputed 3' UTR RUD (relative usage of distal poly(A) site) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data with layer annotations and need to classify genes with spatial APA usage patterns. Input is MERFISH/seqFISH or other non-spatially-barcoded data — APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra The goal is identifying spatial variation in conventional gene expression rather than APA usage variation — use SV gene tools (SPARK, SpatialDE) directly on the expression matrix instead Only a single poly(A) site exists per gene's 3' UTR — only 3' UTR APA genes with at least two poly(A) sites are retained http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify three classes of genes with spatial APA dynamics — DEAPA (layer-to-layer differential APA usage), LSAPA (layer-specific APA), and SVAPA (globally spatially variable APA usage) — from the KNN-imputed RUD matrix using stAPAminer, then merge them with findstAPASet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Identify three classes of genes with spatial APA dynamics — DEAPA (layer-to-layer differential APA usage), LSAPA (layer-specific APA), and SVAPA (globally spatially variable APA usage) — from the KNN-imputed RUD matrix using stAPAminer, then merge them with findstAPASet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is MERFISH/seqFISH or other non-spatially-barcoded data — APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra The goal is identifying spatial variation in conventional gene expression rather than APA usage variation — use SV gene tools (SPARK, SpatialDE) directly on the expression matrix instead Only a single poly(A) site exists per gene's 3' UTR — only 3' UTR APA genes with at least two poly(A) sites are retained

skills.description: Use when a spatially barcoded ST dataset already has poly(A) site annotations and layer labels (e.g., MOB morphological layers), and you need genes with differential or spatially patterned APA usage between those layers.
skills.name: differential-apa-usage-analysis-between-anatomical-layers
skills.search_text: differential-apa-usage-analysis-between-anatomical-layers Use when a spatially barcoded ST dataset already has poly(A) site annotations and layer labels (e.g., MOB morphological layers), and you need genes with differential or spatially patterned APA usage between those layers. Input is raw sequencing reads without poly(A) site annotations — APA sites must first be identified with scAPAtrap/Sierra; stAPAminer starts from a PACdataset APA-spot matrix Data are image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing scRNA-seq tools The question is spatially variable gene expression from a gene count matrix, not APA usage ratios — use SPARK/SpatialDE on gene expression instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA genes whose alternative polyadenylation usage differs across spatially resolved anatomical layers (e.g., MOB GCL, GL, ONL, OPL, MCL) using stAPAminer on an imputed RUD (APA usage) matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Identify DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA genes whose alternative polyadenylation usage differs across spatially resolved anatomical layers (e.g., MOB GCL, GL, ONL, OPL, MCL) using stAPAminer on an imputed RUD (APA usage) matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads without poly(A) site annotations — APA sites must first be identified with scAPAtrap/Sierra; stAPAminer starts from a PACdataset APA-spot matrix Data are image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing scRNA-seq tools The question is spatially variable gene expression from a gene count matrix, not APA usage ratios — use SPARK/SpatialDE on gene expression instead

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-type-by-sample abundance matrix (e.g., DCNet-inferred landscapes from bulk RNA-seq) with two labeled patient subtypes and need to find significantly differentially abundant cell types or build a subtype classifier from them.
skills.name: differential-cell-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-cell-abundance-analysis Use when you have a cell-type-by-sample abundance matrix (e.g., DCNet-inferred landscapes from bulk RNA-seq) with two labeled patient subtypes and need to find significantly differentially abundant cell types or build a subtype classifier from them. You only have raw bulk RNA-seq expression and have not yet run DCNet to infer the cell landscape (this skill operates on the inferred abundance matrix, not on expression directly). Groups are not defined subtypes/labels but continuous phenotypes requiring regression or survival modeling rather than two-group differential testing. The comparison methods' default parameter setting is acceptable only for benchmarking deconvolution accuracy, not for subtype-level differential testing — do not apply this skill when the goal is to benchmark DCNet against CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, or xCell. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Identify cell types whose DCNet-inferred abundances differ significantly between two patient groups (e.g., LUAD vs LUSC in TCGA) using per-cell-type fold change and multiple-testing-adjusted statistical tests, then optionally feed the retained differential cell types into an SVM subtype classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Identify cell types whose DCNet-inferred abundances differ significantly between two patient groups (e.g., LUAD vs LUSC in TCGA) using per-cell-type fold change and multiple-testing-adjusted statistical tests, then optionally feed the retained differential cell types into an SVM subtype classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw bulk RNA-seq expression and have not yet run DCNet to infer the cell landscape (this skill operates on the inferred abundance matrix, not on expression directly). Groups are not defined subtypes/labels but continuous phenotypes requiring regression or survival modeling rather than two-group differential testing. The comparison methods' default parameter setting is acceptable only for benchmarking deconvolution accuracy, not for subtype-level differential testing — do not apply this skill when the goal is to benchmark DCNet against CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, or xCell.

skills.description: Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell data from trajectory inference (e.g., Monocle3) with cluster/cell-type annotations, and need to detect which cell subclusters expand or deplete significantly over pseudotime rather than at discrete time points.
skills.name: differential-cell-subcluster-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-cell-subcluster-abundance-analysis Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell data from trajectory inference (e.g., Monocle3) with cluster/cell-type annotations, and need to detect which cell subclusters expand or deplete significantly over pseudotime rather than at discrete time points. When the goal is differential gene expression without testing cell subcluster abundance dynamics — although scTITANS co-outputs both, the subcluster test requires cell cluster/type annotations in cell_metadata. When no trajectory/pseudotime information exists and none can be inferred — the skill presupposes upstream Monocle3 (or equivalent TI) pseudotime; scTITANS is a trajectory inference-based approach. When subclusters are defined only at discrete sampling timepoints rather than along a continuous pseudotime axis — the method corrects cell asynchrony by introducing a time-dependent covariate along pseudotime, not by per-timepoint comparisons. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Identify cell subclusters whose abundances vary significantly along pseudotime in time-series scRNA-seq data using scTITANS, which fits complete versus flat-line null curves of cell counts across pseudotime bins and calls significance via bootstrap F-statistics with Storey-style q-values at FDR 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Identify cell subclusters whose abundances vary significantly along pseudotime in time-series scRNA-seq data using scTITANS, which fits complete versus flat-line null curves of cell counts across pseudotime bins and calls significance via bootstrap F-statistics with Storey-style q-values at FDR 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential gene expression without testing cell subcluster abundance dynamics — although scTITANS co-outputs both, the subcluster test requires cell cluster/type annotations in cell_metadata. When no trajectory/pseudotime information exists and none can be inferred — the skill presupposes upstream Monocle3 (or equivalent TI) pseudotime; scTITANS is a trajectory inference-based approach. When subclusters are defined only at discrete sampling timepoints rather than along a continuous pseudotime axis — the method corrects cell asynchrony by introducing a time-dependent covariate along pseudotime, not by per-timepoint comparisons.

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) from two conditions and need per-bin-pair differential interaction statistics (pvalue, pvalue.adj.FDR) plus a consensus DCI set.
skills.name: differential-chromatin-interaction-detection
skills.search_text: differential-chromatin-interaction-detection Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) from two conditions and need per-bin-pair differential interaction statistics (pvalue, pvalue.adj.FDR) plus a consensus DCI set. Data are bulk Hi-C contact counts rather than single-cell-level count matrices — scHiCDiff's ZINB zero-inflation model is specifically designed for single-cell interaction comparison Counts are raw/unnormalized — normalize with scHiCDiff.norm (effective length, GC content, mappability) first, since detection functions expect normalized read counts Cells fail QC (< 5000 nondiagonal intra-chromosomal contacts) or bin pairs lie beyond the 0–10 Mb contact-distance range, per the paper's real-data filters http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Detect differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) between two conditions in single-cell Hi-C data using scHiCDiff's four detectors — nonparametric KS and Cramér-von Mises tests and parametric NB/ZINB likelihood-ratio tests — then take the common DCI set with scHiCDiff.common.DCI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Detect differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) between two conditions in single-cell Hi-C data using scHiCDiff's four detectors — nonparametric KS and Cramér-von Mises tests and parametric NB/ZINB likelihood-ratio tests — then take the common DCI set with scHiCDiff.common.DCI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk Hi-C contact counts rather than single-cell-level count matrices — scHiCDiff's ZINB zero-inflation model is specifically designed for single-cell interaction comparison Counts are raw/unnormalized — normalize with scHiCDiff.norm (effective length, GC content, mappability) first, since detection functions expect normalized read counts Cells fail QC (< 5000 nondiagonal intra-chromosomal contacts) or bin pairs lie beyond the 0–10 Mb contact-distance range, per the paper's real-data filters

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell UMI count data with per-cell group labels (e.g. disease status) and per-cell donor/sample labels, and need to test whether gene co-expressions within a specific cell type differ between conditions.
skills.name: differential-co-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-co-expression-analysis Use when you have single-cell UMI count data with per-cell group labels (e.g. disease status) and per-cell donor/sample labels, and need to test whether gene co-expressions within a specific cell type differ between conditions. When the goal is baseline co-expression within one condition rather than a between-group comparison — use the CSCORE estimator directly instead of diff_CSCORE When group labels are at the cell level but samples are single subjects with no donor replication — donor-level permutation cannot be performed and the test is underpowered When input data are normalized/scaled expression values rather than raw UMI counts — CS-CORE's measurement model requires raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify gene pairs whose cell-type-specific co-expression differs between disease and control groups using CS-CORE's diff_CSCORE, which tests differential co-expression from raw UMI counts with donor/sample-level permutations. In the Alzheimer's disease postmortem brain study, this surfaces microglia co-expression changes specific to AD versus controls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Identify gene pairs whose cell-type-specific co-expression differs between disease and control groups using CS-CORE's diff_CSCORE, which tests differential co-expression from raw UMI counts with donor/sample-level permutations. In the Alzheimer's disease postmortem brain study, this surfaces microglia co-expression changes specific to AD versus controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is baseline co-expression within one condition rather than a between-group comparison — use the CSCORE estimator directly instead of diff_CSCORE When group labels are at the cell level but samples are single subjects with no donor replication — donor-level permutation cannot be performed and the test is underpowered When input data are normalized/scaled expression values rather than raw UMI counts — CS-CORE's measurement model requires raw counts

skills.description: Use when you have matched two-condition gene expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample IDs) plus a reference interaction network, and you need driver-node selection by network controllability rather than hub ranking.
skills.name: differential-co-expression-network-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-co-expression-network-analysis Use when you have matched two-condition gene expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample IDs) plus a reference interaction network, and you need driver-node selection by network controllability rather than hub ranking. Only a single condition's expression data is available, so no two-state differential co-expression contrast (ΔZ statistic) can be computed The task is personalized driver discovery in a directed signalling network (e.g. DawnRank-style PageRank) rather than dominating-set controllability on an undirected co-expression network A naive degree-only hub ranking is the intended baseline — the article shows WMDS.net's advantage comes from the MDS formulation plus weights, not degree alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a differential gene co-expression network between two physiological states (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal FPKM matrices) and identifies driver nodes via a weighted minimum dominating set (WMDS.net), solved as a binary integer program in MATLAB intlinprog with node weights w_i = (Σ −log p_ij)^(−γ), γ = 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Builds a differential gene co-expression network between two physiological states (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal FPKM matrices) and identifies driver nodes via a weighted minimum dominating set (WMDS.net), solved as a binary integer program in MATLAB intlinprog with node weights w_i = (Σ −log p_ij)^(−γ), γ = 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single condition's expression data is available, so no two-state differential co-expression contrast (ΔZ statistic) can be computed The task is personalized driver discovery in a directed signalling network (e.g. DawnRank-style PageRank) rather than dominating-set controllability on an undirected co-expression network A naive degree-only hub ranking is the intended baseline — the article shows WMDS.net's advantage comes from the MDS formulation plus weights, not degree alone

skills.description: Use when you have FPKM-normalized expression matrices for two physiological conditions (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal, rows=gene symbols, columns=sample ids) and need to call significant differential co-expression edges on a fixed reference network.
skills.name: differential-coexpression-z-testing
skills.search_text: differential-coexpression-z-testing Use when you have FPKM-normalized expression matrices for two physiological conditions (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal, rows=gene symbols, columns=sample ids) and need to call significant differential co-expression edges on a fixed reference network. The cancer type has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ standard-normal approximation was shown (by Kolmogorov-Smirnov testing) to be reliable only for sample size > 15. You need de novo co-expression edges rather than differential edge calls on a fixed reference network — this skill restricts testing to gene pairs already connected in the Gene_Net reference network. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical testing of differential gene co-expression edges as implemented in WMDS.net: Fisher Z-transform Pearson correlations computed per condition and apply a Z-test on the correlation difference (ΔZ) per reference-network edge, retaining edges with P < 0.05. Also covers the SSN variant that Z-tests the per-patient edge difference Δr_ij between a normal reference network and a tumor-perturbed network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Statistical testing of differential gene co-expression edges as implemented in WMDS.net: Fisher Z-transform Pearson correlations computed per condition and apply a Z-test on the correlation difference (ΔZ) per reference-network edge, retaining edges with P < 0.05. Also covers the SSN variant that Z-tests the per-patient edge difference Δr_ij between a normal reference network and a tumor-perturbed network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cancer type has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ standard-normal approximation was shown (by Kolmogorov-Smirnov testing) to be reliable only for sample size > 15. You need de novo co-expression edges rather than differential edge calls on a fixed reference network — this skill restricts testing to gene pairs already connected in the Gene_Net reference network.

skills.description: Use when testing whether cell-cell communication strength mediated by specific candidate eLR pairs depends on a developmental process, by comparing interaction scores between a perturbed condition (e.g., ZGA-inhibited embryos) and unperturbed time-point conditions.
skills.name: differential-communication-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-communication-analysis Use when testing whether cell-cell communication strength mediated by specific candidate eLR pairs depends on a developmental process, by comparing interaction scores between a perturbed condition (e.g., ZGA-inhibited embryos) and unperturbed time-point conditions. Communication inference between well-defined cell types rather than perturbation-vs-control differential testing — the article notes CellPhoneDB and CellChat are designed for communication between given cell types Studying maternal-embryo interactions — the TimeTalk autocrine assumption in eLR screening precludes this Communication not mediated by ligand-receptor interactions (e.g., extracellular-vesicle-mediated) — the current TimeTalk framework does not account for other communication types http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify how perturbation of a developmental process (e.g., ZGA inhibition by alpha-amanitin) changes the interaction score of embryo-related ligand-receptor pairs (eLRs) across matched developmental stages, using TimeTalk's R analysis scripts on pseudo-bulk per-condition expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Quantify how perturbation of a developmental process (e.g., ZGA inhibition by alpha-amanitin) changes the interaction score of embryo-related ligand-receptor pairs (eLRs) across matched developmental stages, using TimeTalk's R analysis scripts on pseudo-bulk per-condition expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Communication inference between well-defined cell types rather than perturbation-vs-control differential testing — the article notes CellPhoneDB and CellChat are designed for communication between given cell types Studying maternal-embryo interactions — the TimeTalk autocrine assumption in eLR screening precludes this Communication not mediated by ligand-receptor interactions (e.g., extracellular-vesicle-mediated) — the current TimeTalk framework does not account for other communication types

skills.description: Use when two or more single-cell/single-nucleus expression matrices with cell-type annotations from distinct biological conditions (e.g., ASD vs control cortex) must be compared at the level of inferred ligand-receptor communication networks.
skills.name: differential-communication-analysis-between-conditions
skills.search_text: differential-communication-analysis-between-conditions Use when two or more single-cell/single-nucleus expression matrices with cell-type annotations from distinct biological conditions (e.g., ASD vs control cortex) must be compared at the level of inferred ligand-receptor communication networks. Data is spatially resolved transcriptomics where spatially constrained networks and cell-proximity enrichment (400 micron threshold, label permutation) are needed rather than condition comparison The question concerns short-range autocrine/paracrine signaling in non-neural tissue; NeuronChat targets neural-specific communication including long-distance neurotransmitter signaling Only a single condition/dataset exists and no comparative analysis of multiple datasets is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Infers neural cell-cell communication networks separately per condition with NeuronChat (e.g., ASD vs control cortical snRNA-seq), merges them, and compares link counts and communication weights to identify condition-specific signaling such as reduced neuroligin 3 signaling to oligodendrocyte lineage cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Infers neural cell-cell communication networks separately per condition with NeuronChat (e.g., ASD vs control cortical snRNA-seq), merges them, and compares link counts and communication weights to identify condition-specific signaling such as reduced neuroligin 3 signaling to oligodendrocyte lineage cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is spatially resolved transcriptomics where spatially constrained networks and cell-proximity enrichment (400 micron threshold, label permutation) are needed rather than condition comparison The question concerns short-range autocrine/paracrine signaling in non-neural tissue; NeuronChat targets neural-specific communication including long-distance neurotransmitter signaling Only a single condition/dataset exists and no comparative analysis of multiple datasets is intended

skills.description: Use when two single-cell RNA-seq conditions (e.g. ifnb interferon-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData) must be compared at the ligand–receptor level, and each edge needs a magnitude-of-perturbation score that is sign-agnostic for ligand/receptor changes.
skills.name: differential-connectomics-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-connectomics-analysis Use when two single-cell RNA-seq conditions (e.g. ifnb interferon-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData) must be compared at the ligand–receptor level, and each edge needs a magnitude-of-perturbation score that is sign-agnostic for ligand/receptor changes. Only a single tissue system is available with no comparison condition — use CreateConnectome with FilterConnectome, Centrality, or CircosPlot instead of DifferentialConnectome The goal is to claim direct cell–cell communication or intracellular signal transduction — the article states strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of communication and requires wet-lab validation The two connectomes do not contain exactly the same edges — DifferentialConnectome requires identical edge sets so every edge has a reference and test value http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quantitatively compares two cell–cell signaling networks (connectomes) built from single-cell RNA-seq data, e.g. IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs, and scores each differential edge with an always-positive 'perturbation score' (product of the absolute ligand and receptor log-fold changes) so strongly perturbed edges surface regardless of change direction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Quantitatively compares two cell–cell signaling networks (connectomes) built from single-cell RNA-seq data, e.g. IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs, and scores each differential edge with an always-positive 'perturbation score' (product of the absolute ligand and receptor log-fold changes) so strongly perturbed edges surface regardless of change direction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single tissue system is available with no comparison condition — use CreateConnectome with FilterConnectome, Centrality, or CircosPlot instead of DifferentialConnectome The goal is to claim direct cell–cell communication or intracellular signal transduction — the article states strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of communication and requires wet-lab validation The two connectomes do not contain exactly the same edges — DifferentialConnectome requires identical edge sets so every edge has a reference and test value

skills.description: Use when the goal is to detect subpopulation-specific changes in the fraction of cells expressing a gene (differential detection) across conditions from multi-sample scRNA-seq data, e.g. with muscat's pbDD.
skills.name: differential-detection-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-detection-analysis Use when the goal is to detect subpopulation-specific changes in the fraction of cells expressing a gene (differential detection) across conditions from multi-sample scRNA-seq data, e.g. with muscat's pbDD. The analysis goal is differential expression of mean expression levels (DS) rather than the fraction of detecting cells; use standard pbDS on sum-aggregated pseudobulks instead Data lack the multi-sample structure (multiple samples per group) required for sample-level pseudobulk inference; cell-level methods were not designed for the multi-group multi-sample problem and the DD workflow assumes it http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Performs differential detection (DD) analysis in multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq data by testing for shifts in the proportion of cells with detected (nonzero) gene expression across conditions, using muscat's pbDD on num.detected pseudobulks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Performs differential detection (DD) analysis in multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq data by testing for shifts in the proportion of cells with detected (nonzero) gene expression across conditions, using muscat's pbDD on num.detected pseudobulks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential expression of mean expression levels (DS) rather than the fraction of detecting cells; use standard pbDS on sum-aggregated pseudobulks instead Data lack the multi-sample structure (multiple samples per group) required for sample-level pseudobulk inference; cell-level methods were not designed for the multi-group multi-sample problem and the DD workflow assumes it

skills.name: differential-exon-usage-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-exon-usage-analysis Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) FASTQs have short-read cell-type assignments and you need per-exon PSI quantification and HIPP-vs-PFC delta-PSI tests, or single-cell-vs-spatial ΔΨ concordance. skills.summary: Quantifies per-exon inclusion (PSI) from cell-type-assigned long reads and tests for differential exon usage between hippocampus (HIPP) and prefrontal cortex (PFC) at P7, including reproduction of single-cell delta-PSI in spatial long-read data.

skills.description: Use when raw or imputed scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns, e.g. GSE75748 ESC/DEC) need DE gene lists between subpopulations, or when imputation impact on DE accuracy must be benchmarked against a bulk RNA-seq reference.
skills.name: differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-expression-analysis Use when raw or imputed scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns, e.g. GSE75748 ESC/DEC) need DE gene lists between subpopulations, or when imputation impact on DE accuracy must be benchmarked against a bulk RNA-seq reference. Input is bulk RNA-seq data — the dropout phenomenon motivating imputation is a key characteristic of scRNA-seq, not bulk averages across cells The goal is clustering of cell subpopulations or dimension reduction rather than differential expression gene lists Data come from droplet microfluidics with severely high dropout rates, where imputation efficiency degrades and downstream DE lists may be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential gene expression analysis on single-cell RNA-seq count matrices — run before or after dropout imputation (scImpute) to derive DE gene lists between cell populations, and evaluate their concordance with bulk RNA-seq DE references via precision, recall, and F-score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Differential gene expression analysis on single-cell RNA-seq count matrices — run before or after dropout imputation (scImpute) to derive DE gene lists between cell populations, and evaluate their concordance with bulk RNA-seq DE references via precision, recall, and F-score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq data — the dropout phenomenon motivating imputation is a key characteristic of scRNA-seq, not bulk averages across cells The goal is clustering of cell subpopulations or dimension reduction rather than differential expression gene lists Data come from droplet microfluidics with severely high dropout rates, where imputation efficiency degrades and downstream DE lists may be unreliable

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression agreement for a two-population scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. H1 vs DEC), or when benchmarking denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) by bulk-LFC correspondence.
skills.name: differential-expression-analysis-bulk-and-single-cell
skills.search_text: differential-expression-analysis-bulk-and-single-cell Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression agreement for a two-population scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. H1 vs DEC), or when benchmarking denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) by bulk-LFC correspondence. The analysis goal is quantifying denoising quality on datasets without matched bulk samples — correlation with bulk LFC cannot be computed. The comparison requires more than two populations with complex contrasts — the H1 vs DEC two-group DESeq2 design does not directly extend. The input is already a normalized/imputed expression matrix incompatible with DESeq2's raw-count expectation for the raw-data arm of the analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce the DCA paper's Fig. 5 benchmark on the Chu et al. H1 vs definitive endoderm (DEC) data: run DESeq2 log fold change analysis on bulk samples and on raw vs denoised single cells, then bootstrap-correlate single-cell LFCs against bulk LFCs to rank denoising methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Reproduce the DCA paper's Fig. 5 benchmark on the Chu et al. H1 vs definitive endoderm (DEC) data: run DESeq2 log fold change analysis on bulk samples and on raw vs denoised single cells, then bootstrap-correlate single-cell LFCs against bulk LFCs to rank denoising methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is quantifying denoising quality on datasets without matched bulk samples — correlation with bulk LFC cannot be computed. The comparison requires more than two populations with complex contrasts — the H1 vs DEC two-group DESeq2 design does not directly extend. The input is already a normalized/imputed expression matrix incompatible with DESeq2's raw-count expectation for the raw-data arm of the analysis.

When the goal is to detect within-tissue batch effects rather than across-tissue biological signal — use iLISI/cLISI integration scores instead When the input is not endothelial cells from distinct biological conditions (e.g. a single-tissue, single-condition dataset has no across-tissue DE signal to protect) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies differentially expressed genes between pancreas- and lung-derived endothelial cells (3529 genes) using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (wilcoxauc) to assess how well each batch-integration method retains across-tissue biological signal and resists over-correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes between pancreas- and lung-derived endothelial cells (3529 genes) using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (wilcoxauc) to assess how well each batch-integration method retains across-tissue biological signal and resists over-correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to detect within-tissue batch effects rather than across-tissue biological signal — use iLISI/cLISI integration scores instead When the input is not endothelial cells from distinct biological conditions (e.g. a single-tissue, single-condition dataset has no across-tissue DE signal to protect)

skills.description: Use when comparing bulk or single-cell RNA-seq of CD8 TILs between immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) and control conditions, or when scoring an input scRNA-seq dataset for CD8 TIL transcriptomic states to test EM-like signature enrichment.
skills.name: differential-expression-analysis-of-tumor-infiltrating-lymphocytes
skills.search_text: differential-expression-analysis-of-tumor-infiltrating-lymphocytes Use when comparing bulk or single-cell RNA-seq of CD8 TILs between immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) and control conditions, or when scoring an input scRNA-seq dataset for CD8 TIL transcriptomic states to test EM-like signature enrichment. Input is not CD8 T cell transcriptomic data — TILPRED assumes a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cell profiles and needs filterCD8T to handle non-CD8 contamination The goal is general cell-type reference mapping of scRNA-seq beyond TIL state prediction — TILPRED is no longer maintained and the authors recommend ProjecTILs for reference-based projection Tumor antigen specificity of the samples is unknown and the question depends on clone-level specificity — antigen specificity 'is often unknown' for polyclonal CD8 TIL samples, so transcriptome-level DE alone cannot resolve clonal behavior http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies and contrasts transcriptomic profiles of CD8 TILs across anti-PD-1 vs control conditions, using DESeq2/tximport for bulk RNA-seq and TILPRED/AUCell to classify CD8 TIL states (exhausted, memory-like, naive, EM-like), to test whether checkpoint blockade selectively enriches the EM-like CD8 TIL signature. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Quantifies and contrasts transcriptomic profiles of CD8 TILs across anti-PD-1 vs control conditions, using DESeq2/tximport for bulk RNA-seq and TILPRED/AUCell to classify CD8 TIL states (exhausted, memory-like, naive, EM-like), to test whether checkpoint blockade selectively enriches the EM-like CD8 TIL signature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not CD8 T cell transcriptomic data — TILPRED assumes a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cell profiles and needs filterCD8T to handle non-CD8 contamination The goal is general cell-type reference mapping of scRNA-seq beyond TIL state prediction — TILPRED is no longer maintained and the authors recommend ProjecTILs for reference-based projection Tumor antigen specificity of the samples is unknown and the question depends on clone-level specificity — antigen specificity 'is often unknown' for polyclonal CD8 TIL samples, so transcriptome-level DE alone cannot resolve clonal behavior

skills.description: Use when comparing two conditions (e.g., BNLx vs SHR strains) at transcript level after RSEM quantitation, especially to test whether a modified transcriptome changes the DE call set.
skills.name: differential-expression-analysis-with-deseq2
skills.search_text: differential-expression-analysis-with-deseq2 Use when comparing two conditions (e.g., BNLx vs SHR strains) at transcript level after RSEM quantitation, especially to test whether a modified transcriptome changes the DE call set. Quantitation has not been performed with RSEM against a defined transcriptome GTF (DESeq2 needs a count matrix from the filtered high-quality transcriptome). You have fewer than the recommended replicates and no way to apply the 1-count-in-2/3-of-samples filter, since unfiltered aptardi transcriptomes contain redundant false-positive transcripts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run DESeq2 differential expression testing (e.g., BNLx vs SHR rat brain) on RSEM-quantitated, quality-filtered transcriptomes to identify transcripts with p <= 0.001, and compare DE sets between an aptardi-modified and an original StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Run DESeq2 differential expression testing (e.g., BNLx vs SHR rat brain) on RSEM-quantitated, quality-filtered transcriptomes to identify transcripts with p <= 0.001, and compare DE sets between an aptardi-modified and an original StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Quantitation has not been performed with RSEM against a defined transcriptome GTF (DESeq2 needs a count matrix from the filtered high-quality transcriptome). You have fewer than the recommended replicates and no way to apply the 1-count-in-2/3-of-samples filter, since unfiltered aptardi transcriptomes contain redundant false-positive transcripts.

skills.description: Use when evaluating an imputation or preprocessing method's effect on differential expression accuracy in scRNA-seq data where a ground-truth set of DE genes is known, especially as a function of the zero-count (dropout) proportion.
skills.name: differential-expression-aucpr-assessment
skills.search_text: differential-expression-aucpr-assessment Use when evaluating an imputation or preprocessing method's effect on differential expression accuracy in scRNA-seq data where a ground-truth set of DE genes is known, especially as a function of the zero-count (dropout) proportion. No ground-truth DE gene set is available (e.g., real experimental scRNA-seq data without simulated truth) — AUC-PR against truth is undefined Data already contain extremely high dropout rates from droplet-based protocols, where the paper notes imputation efficiency degrades and improved methods remain a future direction The question is imputation fidelity of individual expression values rather than downstream DE accuracy — AUC-PR on DE calls does not measure per-value recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Quantifies how well a scRNA-seq imputation method (e.g., scImpute) supports downstream differential expression (DE) analysis by computing the area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR) of DE calls against a simulated ground truth, across controlled dropout rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Quantifies how well a scRNA-seq imputation method (e.g., scImpute) supports downstream differential expression (DE) analysis by computing the area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR) of DE calls against a simulated ground truth, across controlled dropout rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth DE gene set is available (e.g., real experimental scRNA-seq data without simulated truth) — AUC-PR against truth is undefined Data already contain extremely high dropout rates from droplet-based protocols, where the paper notes imputation efficiency degrades and improved methods remain a future direction The question is imputation fidelity of individual expression values rather than downstream DE accuracy — AUC-PR on DE calls does not measure per-value recovery

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a feature selection algorithm (e.g., DUBStepR vs. HVGDisp, HVGVST, trendVar, devianceFS, HLG, M3Drop/DANB, GiniClust) on scRNA-seq data and you need a DE-detection AUROC against independently ascertained cell type annotations.
skills.name: differential-expression-auroc-assessment
skills.search_text: differential-expression-auroc-assessment Use when benchmarking a feature selection algorithm (e.g., DUBStepR vs. HVGDisp, HVGVST, trendVar, devianceFS, HLG, M3Drop/DANB, GiniClust) on scRNA-seq data and you need a DE-detection AUROC against independently ascertained cell type annotations. Input is already a filtered feature set or DE gene table with no ranked gene list — AUROC needs the full method ranking to score overlap with top-500 positives vs. bottom-500 negatives Datasets lack independent cell type annotations, so the top-500 DE / bottom-500 non-DE gene ground truth cannot be defined The goal is clustering-quality assessment rather than DE-gene detection — the paper pairs this AUROC with the mean scaled silhouette index, which should be computed separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assesses a scRNA-seq feature selection method by how well its ranked gene list separates known differentially expressed (DE) genes from non-DE genes, quantified as AUROC against independently annotated cell types. This mirrors the paper's objective criterion that a good feature selection algorithm selects cell-type-specific DE genes as features and rejects the remaining genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Assesses a scRNA-seq feature selection method by how well its ranked gene list separates known differentially expressed (DE) genes from non-DE genes, quantified as AUROC against independently annotated cell types. This mirrors the paper's objective criterion that a good feature selection algorithm selects cell-type-specific DE genes as features and rejects the remaining genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered feature set or DE gene table with no ranked gene list — AUROC needs the full method ranking to score overlap with top-500 positives vs. bottom-500 negatives Datasets lack independent cell type annotations, so the top-500 DE / bottom-500 non-DE gene ground truth cannot be defined The goal is clustering-quality assessment rather than DE-gene detection — the paper pairs this AUROC with the mean scaled silhouette index, which should be computed separately

skills.description: Use when you have case/control RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. TCGA ESCA tumor vs normal) and need to weight nodes of a CLIP-derived RBP-ncRNA network before running fRNC's global or local module search.
skills.name: differential-expression-based-node-scoring
skills.search_text: differential-expression-based-node-scoring Use when you have case/control RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. TCGA ESCA tumor vs normal) and need to weight nodes of a CLIP-derived RBP-ncRNA network before running fRNC's global or local module search. Expression data are not case/control count matrices but already-processed statistics — skip DEGs and feed existing type/logFC/PValue values directly to combinp (as done for the BRCA case with brca_miRNA_re_se, brca_RNA_re_se, brca_pro_re_se). The goal is protein-level integration without expression weighting — the BRCA protein-level case requires removing RBP mRNA rows (type != "rbp") before combining, so naive rbind of all DE results would double-score RBPs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Convert differential expression results (type, logFC, PValue) for miRNAs, mRNAs and lncRNAs into node weight scores on an RBP-ncRNA interaction network using the fRNC 'combinp' function, so that downstream RNC module searches can rank nodes by expression significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Convert differential expression results (type, logFC, PValue) for miRNAs, mRNAs and lncRNAs into node weight scores on an RBP-ncRNA interaction network using the fRNC 'combinp' function, so that downstream RNC module searches can rank nodes by expression significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are not case/control count matrices but already-processed statistics — skip DEGs and feed existing type/logFC/PValue values directly to combinp (as done for the BRCA case with brca_miRNA_re_se, brca_RNA_re_se, brca_pro_re_se). The goal is protein-level integration without expression weighting — the BRCA protein-level case requires removing RBP mRNA rows (type != "rbp") before combining, so naive rbind of all DE results would double-score RBPs.

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-Seq matrix with a multipotent cell population and competing downstream lineages (e.g. SHARE-Seq hair-follicle TACs vs IRS/HS, or Ranzoni fetal-liver MPPs vs GP/MEMP), and you need to shortlist overexpressed regulatory factors to feed into DICE priming analysis.
skills.name: differential-expression-candidate-regulator-screening
skills.search_text: differential-expression-candidate-regulator-screening Use when you have a scRNA-Seq matrix with a multipotent cell population and competing downstream lineages (e.g. SHARE-Seq hair-follicle TACs vs IRS/HS, or Ranzoni fetal-liver MPPs vs GP/MEMP), and you need to shortlist overexpressed regulatory factors to feed into DICE priming analysis. When the goal is to identify tipping points or bifurcation timing over pseudotime rather than to shortlist candidate priming RFs — use the later DICE workflow steps (CompDICE, CreateDPTbin with minBins=7) instead When the input is already a shortlist of selected RFs (e.g. the top-4 hepatocyte and cholangiocyte TFs NR1I3, NR1I2, FOXA2, TRIM15, LSR, ELF3, IRF6, BGN) — proceed directly to CompDICE When regulatory factors must be validated experimentally; this screen is purely computational and the article notes no experimental work was performed to demonstrate importance of the identified RFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A screening step within the DICE framework that identifies candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in lineage priming by performing differential overexpression analysis of lineage-committed cells versus the multipotent progenitor (MPP) population, then filtering by expression frequency in the MPP population (type1fth='Mean'). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: A screening step within the DICE framework that identifies candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in lineage priming by performing differential overexpression analysis of lineage-committed cells versus the multipotent progenitor (MPP) population, then filtering by expression frequency in the MPP population (type1fth='Mean').
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify tipping points or bifurcation timing over pseudotime rather than to shortlist candidate priming RFs — use the later DICE workflow steps (CompDICE, CreateDPTbin with minBins=7) instead When the input is already a shortlist of selected RFs (e.g. the top-4 hepatocyte and cholangiocyte TFs NR1I3, NR1I2, FOXA2, TRIM15, LSR, ELF3, IRF6, BGN) — proceed directly to CompDICE When regulatory factors must be validated experimentally; this screen is purely computational and the article notes no experimental work was performed to demonstrate importance of the identified RFs

skills.description: Use when RCC (or a consensus clustering run over candidate k values) has produced clusters and you must decide whether each cluster is a genuine subtype before subdividing further, using differential gene expression as the quality gate.
skills.name: differential-expression-cluster-validation
skills.search_text: differential-expression-cluster-validation Use when RCC (or a consensus clustering run over candidate k values) has produced clusters and you must decide whether each cluster is a genuine subtype before subdividing further, using differential gene expression as the quality gate. Clusters already have established biological annotation, so validation by novel DE genes is unnecessary The dataset is not transcriptomic (e.g., no gene-level expression matrix), since RCC is designed for bulk and single-cell transcriptome data A fully exploratory clustering with no interest in subtype validity is desired and stability/overlap/DE gates would over-filter the result http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates clusters/subtypes produced by Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) by checking that each cluster is supported by differentially-expressed genes, computed with the RCC package's geneMarkers interface. This gates whether a subdivision of the data (or a subcluster at a candidate k) is biologically meaningful or whether recursion should stop. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Validates clusters/subtypes produced by Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) by checking that each cluster is supported by differentially-expressed genes, computed with the RCC package's geneMarkers interface. This gates whether a subdivision of the data (or a subcluster at a candidate k) is biologically meaningful or whether recursion should stop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters already have established biological annotation, so validation by novel DE genes is unnecessary The dataset is not transcriptomic (e.g., no gene-level expression matrix), since RCC is designed for bulk and single-cell transcriptome data A fully exploratory clustering with no interest in subtype validity is desired and stability/overlap/DE gates would over-filter the result

skills.description: Use when a simulated bulk multi-omics dataset (e.g. MOSim RNA-seq + miRNA-seq + TF) must yield a defined DEG/regulator feature set with ground-truth regulatory signs (activator vs repressor) for downstream validation.

skills.search_text: differential-expression-feature-extraction Use when a simulated bulk multi-omics dataset (e.g. MOSim RNA-seq + miRNA-seq + TF) must yield a defined DEG/regulator feature set with ground-truth regulatory signs (activator vs repressor) for downstream validation. Input is real (non-simulated) experimental data without ground-truth regulatory signs — this skill's validation relies on MOSim-simulated DE and known activator/repressor effects Simulating single-cell omics layers other than scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and TFs — MOSim's sc_mosim does not support other single-cell modalities The analysis requires spatially resolved GRNs or proteomics/metabolomics regulatory layers — MOSim explicitly does not cover these http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract differentially expressed features (DEGs) and their linked regulators from a simulated multi-omics MOSim object, then transform and validate their group-wise expression profiles against a no-regulation null. Provides ground-truth positive/negative feature sets for benchmarking GRN and multi-omics integration methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Extract differentially expressed features (DEGs) and their linked regulators from a simulated multi-omics MOSim object, then transform and validate their group-wise expression profiles against a no-regulation null. Provides ground-truth positive/negative feature sets for benchmarking GRN and multi-omics integration methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) experimental data without ground-truth regulatory signs — this skill's validation relies on MOSim-simulated DE and known activator/repressor effects Simulating single-cell omics layers other than scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and TFs — MOSim's sc_mosim does not support other single-cell modalities The analysis requires spatially resolved GRNs or proteomics/metabolomics regulatory layers — MOSim explicitly does not cover these

skills.search_text: differential-expression-fold-change-ranking Use when you have differential expression results (gene-level log fold-changes) from perturbed 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data and need a fold-change-ranked gene list as input to clusterProfiler GSEA for GO term enrichment. skills.name: differential-expression-gene-identification
skills.search_text: differential-expression-gene-identification Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices with known rare-cell labels (e.g., artificial splatter data with group.prob = c(0.99, 0.01) or the packaged 1%Jurkat.h5) and need a validated set of DE genes and non-DE background genes for robustness/sensitivity tests. skills.description: Use when a CCIVR Table.csv/Summary.csv of cis-NAT pairs carries RNA-seq expression columns (TPM, fold_change, padj) and the goal is to split partner genes into up/down lists for GO enrichment (e.g., DAVID GOTERM_BP_FAT).
skills.name: differential-expression-gene-list-extraction
skills.search_text: differential-expression-gene-list-extraction Use when a CCIVR Table.csv/Summary.csv of cis-NAT pairs carries RNA-seq expression columns (TPM, fold_change, padj) and the goal is to split partner genes into up/down lists for GO enrichment (e.g., DAVID GOTERM_BP_FAT). Input is raw RNA-seq data (FASTQ) — CCIVR requires processed RNA-seq data produced by third-party programs (STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression profiling, DESeq2 for statistical analysis), so raw reads must be processed first. The analysis goal is only cis-NAT structural characterization (EB/FO/HH/TT counts) without expression profiling — CCIVR handles this directly, and no differential gene lists can be extracted. skills.description: Use when a single common trajectory (e.g., slingshot sds) spans multiple conditions and the goal is to test whether condition-level cell abundance differs between lineages (differential fate selection), after topologyTest has not rejected a common topology.

skills.search_text: differential-fate-selection-testing Use when a single common trajectory (e.g., slingshot sds) spans multiple conditions and the goal is to test whether condition-level cell abundance differs between lineages (differential fate selection), after topologyTest has not rejected a common topology. topologyTest rejects the common-trajectory null and conditions require separate trajectory inferences — fate comparison on a single sds is then inappropriate The expected difference is in pseudotime distributions along a lineage rather than allocation between lineages — progressionTest is the correct test Cells are in a steady-state system with no trajectory structure — differential abundance methods such as DAseq or milo are the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The condiments fateSelectionTest evaluates whether cells from different conditions are differentially allocated to lineages of a common inferred trajectory, using a classifier-based test on lineage weights. skills.summary: The condiments fateSelectionTest evaluates whether cells from different conditions are differentially allocated to lineages of a common inferred trajectory, using a classifier-based test on lineage weights. skills.when_to_use_negative: topologyTest rejects the common-trajectory null and conditions require separate trajectory inferences — fate comparison on a single sds is then inappropriate The expected difference is in pseudotime distributions along a lineage rather than allocation between lineages — progressionTest is the correct test Cells are in a steady-state system with no trajectory structure — differential abundance methods such as DAseq or milo are the appropriate choice
