When only a single method's output is required and dataset properties (e.g. non-model organism count distributions) make one tool clearly appropriate — the multi-method integration adds overhead without benefit in that case When the input is already a DEG result table from all methods and the goal is only result integration (vote thresholds or combined-FDR), not DEG detection itself When the input is a raw FASTQ file — reads must first be converted and mapped to count tables via a clean-and-map program before DEgenes Hunter can run http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Detect differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from an RNA-seq count table by running multiple methods (DESeq2, limma, NOISeq) through the DEgenes Hunter pipeline in ExpHunter Suite and integrating their results via vote thresholds or combined-FDR data fusion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Detect differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from an RNA-seq count table by running multiple methods (DESeq2, limma, NOISeq) through the DEgenes Hunter pipeline in ExpHunter Suite and integrating their results via vote thresholds or combined-FDR data fusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single method's output is required and dataset properties (e.g. non-model organism count distributions) make one tool clearly appropriate — the multi-method integration adds overhead without benefit in that case When the input is already a DEG result table from all methods and the goal is only result integration (vote thresholds or combined-FDR), not DEG detection itself When the input is a raw FASTQ file — reads must first be converted and mapped to count tables via a clean-and-map program before DEgenes Hunter can run

skills.description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object with annotated clusters/subclusters (e.g. PBMC3k) needs cluster-specific marker genes, and genes expressed in any non-target cluster must be excluded from the marker set.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object with annotated clusters/subclusters (e.g. PBMC3k) needs cluster-specific marker genes, and genes expressed in any non-target cluster must be excluded from the marker set. The input is a bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature table rather than a per-cell Seurat object with cluster labels — the method relies on comparing one annotated cluster against background clusters. The goal is differential expression between two defined conditions or groups, not identifying genes specific to a single cluster/subcluster — the specificity filter discards genes expressed in the top percentile of any non-target cluster. Clusters are heterogeneous and have not yet been reclustered (e.g. via SCISSORS silhouette-score-driven reclustering), so the 'target subcluster' is not a valid comparison unit. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Marker gene identification module from the SCISSORS framework: a candidate gene list is generated by one-vs-background differential expression for a target cluster or subcluster, then filtered by expression percentile to retain only genes of high specificity to the target cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Marker gene identification module from the SCISSORS framework: a candidate gene list is generated by one-vs-background differential expression for a target cluster or subcluster, then filtered by expression percentile to retain only genes of high specificity to the target cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature table rather than a per-cell Seurat object with cluster labels — the method relies on comparing one annotated cluster against background clusters. The goal is differential expression between two defined conditions or groups, not identifying genes specific to a single cluster/subcluster — the specificity filter discards genes expressed in the top percentile of any non-target cluster. Clusters are heterogeneous and have not yet been reclustered (e.g. via SCISSORS silhouette-score-driven reclustering), so the 'target subcluster' is not a valid comparison unit.

skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when scRNAseq clusters (e.g., from LCMV1/LCMV2 CD44+ T cell 10X data) already exist and you need genes defining each cluster versus all others, plus subtype label assignment. skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (.h5ad) with cell-type and condition/disease annotations and need per-cell-type DEG calls between conditions (e.g. COVID-19 vs normal, infarct vs control), with ranked gene lists and volcano plots.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (.h5ad) with cell-type and condition/disease annotations and need per-cell-type DEG calls between conditions (e.g. COVID-19 vs normal, infarct vs control), with ranked gene lists and volcano plots. Input lacks per-sample/donor and cell-type annotations required for pseudo-bulk aggregation and the mixed-effects model The goal is feature importance / biomarker ranking from the DNN model — use scaLR's linear_scorer/shap_scorer gene_analysis instead, not DGE Only test-set samples should be analyzed when maximum DEG sensitivity is required — the paper shows full-samples DGE yields substantially more DEGs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 scaLR's differential gene expression (DGE) module identifies condition-associated genes from scRNA-seq data via two complementary approaches — pseudo-bulk aggregation per sample/cell type and per-gene linear mixed-effects models (LMEM) — producing volcano plots and associated DEG gene lists. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: scaLR's differential gene expression (DGE) module identifies condition-associated genes from scRNA-seq data via two complementary approaches — pseudo-bulk aggregation per sample/cell type and per-gene linear mixed-effects models (LMEM) — producing volcano plots and associated DEG gene lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks per-sample/donor and cell-type annotations required for pseudo-bulk aggregation and the mixed-effects model The goal is feature importance / biomarker ranking from the DNN model — use scaLR's linear_scorer/shap_scorer gene_analysis instead, not DGE Only test-set samples should be analyzed when maximum DEG sensitivity is required — the paper shows full-samples DGE yields substantially more DEGs

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell gene expression matrix plus cluster labels (e.g., SSRE-inferred cell type labels) and need to detect marker genes per cluster, expecting recovery of known markers.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when you have a single-cell gene expression matrix plus cluster labels (e.g., SSRE-inferred cell type labels) and need to detect marker genes per cluster, expecting recovery of known markers. You only have raw scRNA-seq counts without any cluster or cell type labels — the test requires a pre-computed grouping factor such as SSRE-inferred labels. The goal is cell type detection itself rather than downstream marker discovery — use SSRE clustering (or SC3/SIMLR) first, then apply this skill to its labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies significantly differentially expressed genes from scRNA-seq data by testing each gene across SSRE-inferred cluster labels, as demonstrated on the Yan dataset with the Kruskal-Wallis rank-sum test at P < 0.01. This extends SSRE's cell type detection output to downstream marker-gene discovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Identifies significantly differentially expressed genes from scRNA-seq data by testing each gene across SSRE-inferred cluster labels, as demonstrated on the Yan dataset with the Kruskal-Wallis rank-sum test at P < 0.01. This extends SSRE's cell type detection output to downstream marker-gene discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw scRNA-seq counts without any cluster or cell type labels — the test requires a pre-computed grouping factor such as SSRE-inferred labels. The goal is cell type detection itself rather than downstream marker discovery — use SSRE clustering (or SC3/SIMLR) first, then apply this skill to its labels.

skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when single-cell RNA-seq case/control data must be reduced to per-cell-cluster DEG profiles before connectivity-based drug repurposing (ASGARD GetDrug/DrugScore), or when benchmarking which scRNA-seq DE method maximizes downstream AUC. When the input is already pseudo-bulk or bulk RNA-seq and the goal is to run the bulk baselines CLUE or DrInsight rather than per-cluster single-cell DE When a cell type has fewer than the minimum of 3 cells in either the case or control group — that cluster's DE contrast should be skipped http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Per-cluster/cell-type differential expression analysis of scRNA-seq case vs. control data (e.g., deceased vs. cured COVID-19 BALF, TNBC patients vs. healthy controls) using limma (Bayes), Seurat Wilcoxon, DESeq2, or edgeR, producing the DEG lists that feed ASGARD's GetDrug and DrugScore repurposing steps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36637-3

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already pseudo-bulk or bulk RNA-seq and the goal is to run the bulk baselines CLUE or DrInsight rather than per-cluster single-cell DE When a cell type has fewer than the minimum of 3 cells in either the case or control group — that cluster's DE contrast should be skipped

skills.description: Use when you have a Seurat object with graph-based clusters (e.g. severe vs healthy COVID-19 bronchoalveolar/peripheral cells) and need DE gene lists plus their enriched environmental/gene modules with padj and fold enrichment.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when you have a Seurat object with graph-based clusters (e.g. severe vs healthy COVID-19 bronchoalveolar/peripheral cells) and need DE gene lists plus their enriched environmental/gene modules with padj and fold enrichment. Input is unclustered raw single-cell data — process_input_seurat() requires a Seurat object with clustering already performed The gene–environment categories of interest fall outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals), since the database is limited to four types of environmental variables The data are genetic variant types (SNPs, CNVs, DNA methylations) — these are not covered by the current E.PAGE statistical tests http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Perform cluster-based differential expression on a clustered single-cell (Seurat) object and statistically enrich the resulting DE gene lists against E.PAGE's curated environmental gene-module database (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals; 522 manually annotated modules, 25,789 genes) using hypergeometric testing with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Perform cluster-based differential expression on a clustered single-cell (Seurat) object and statistically enrich the resulting DE gene lists against E.PAGE's curated environmental gene-module database (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals; 522 manually annotated modules, 25,789 genes) using hypergeometric testing with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unclustered raw single-cell data — process_input_seurat() requires a Seurat object with clustering already performed The gene–environment categories of interest fall outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals), since the database is limited to four types of environmental variables The data are genetic variant types (SNPs, CNVs, DNA methylations) — these are not covered by the current E.PAGE statistical tests

skills.description: Use when building a malignant-vs-normal epithelial classifier feature set from multiple annotated scRNA-seq training datasets, or when you need to combine per-dataset DEG lists into one pan-cancer gene panel.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when building a malignant-vs-normal epithelial classifier feature set from multiple annotated scRNA-seq training datasets, or when you need to combine per-dataset DEG lists into one pan-cancer gene panel. A feature list already exists (e.g., ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt from Zenodo record 17888140) — no need to re-derive DEGs The goal is malignant cell identification from a single already-annotated dataset rather than constructing a pan-cancer training feature set The comparison is between malignant cells and all non-malignant cells rather than their originating normal epithelial counterpart — scMalignantFinder is specifically designed for the latter http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Derives the scMalignantFinder model feature set by running per-dataset differential expression (Seurat FindAllMarkers) between malignant and normal epithelial cells in the signature-calibrated training set, then taking the union (not intersection) of upregulated and downregulated DEG sets into a single 2707-gene feature matrix (1656 up + 1051 down). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Derives the scMalignantFinder model feature set by running per-dataset differential expression (Seurat FindAllMarkers) between malignant and normal epithelial cells in the signature-calibrated training set, then taking the union (not intersection) of upregulated and downregulated DEG sets into a single 2707-gene feature matrix (1656 up + 1051 down).
skills.when_to_use_negative: A feature list already exists (e.g., ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt from Zenodo record 17888140) — no need to re-derive DEGs The goal is malignant cell identification from a single already-annotated dataset rather than constructing a pan-cancer training feature set The comparison is between malignant cells and all non-malignant cells rather than their originating normal epithelial counterpart — scMalignantFinder is specifically designed for the latter

skills.description: Use when validating predicted perturbation-response transcriptomes (e.g., scButterfly-B output on PT_PBMC) by comparing per-cell-type DEG profiles to ground truth with top-100 DEG overlap and R2 metrics.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when validating predicted perturbation-response transcriptomes (e.g., scButterfly-B output on PT_PBMC) by comparing per-cell-type DEG profiles to ground truth with top-100 DEG overlap and R2 metrics. Data is not perturbation-response data (e.g., plain cross-modality scRNA/scATAC translation), where the correct evaluation is translation accuracy rather than DEG overlap Paired ground-truth stimulated profiles are unavailable for the held-out cell types, so no DEG overlap or R2 against truth can be computed Input counts are raw and unnormalized — RNA_data_preprocessing (QC and normalization) must be applied before differential expression http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates predicted single-cell perturbation responses by computing per-cell-type differential expression against ground truth, using top-100 DEG overlap counts and squared Pearson correlation (R2) as metrics. This is the validation scheme used to benchmark scButterfly-B predictions on the PT_PBMC control/stimulated PBMC data against scGen and scPreGAN baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Evaluates predicted single-cell perturbation responses by computing per-cell-type differential expression against ground truth, using top-100 DEG overlap counts and squared Pearson correlation (R2) as metrics. This is the validation scheme used to benchmark scButterfly-B predictions on the PT_PBMC control/stimulated PBMC data against scGen and scPreGAN baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not perturbation-response data (e.g., plain cross-modality scRNA/scATAC translation), where the correct evaluation is translation accuracy rather than DEG overlap Paired ground-truth stimulated profiles are unavailable for the held-out cell types, so no DEG overlap or R2 against truth can be computed Input counts are raw and unnormalized — RNA_data_preprocessing (QC and normalization) must be applied before differential expression

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq expression matrices for two or more FACS-sorted or annotated cell subsets are available and signature genes distinguishing terminal cell types are needed for fate prediction or marker discovery.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when raw scRNA-seq expression matrices for two or more FACS-sorted or annotated cell subsets are available and signature genes distinguishing terminal cell types are needed for fate prediction or marker discovery. Input has no defined subset/group labels or end-stage contrasts, since Mpath depends on signature genes of differentiated cell types for fate prediction The goal is de novo clustering or marker discovery in heterogeneous data where specific subset information is not known, rather than testing pre-specified subset contrasts Temporal ordering of developmental stages is assumed in advance — this method explicitly uses genes only from end-stage contrasts without a priori temporal ordering knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies differentially expressed genes between defined cell subsets (e.g., mature cDC1 versus cDC2 in GSE60782) using ANOVA followed by post-hoc Tukey's test, with Benjamini-Hochberg P-value adjustment. These end-stage contrast genes serve as signature genes for downstream trajectory/fate analyses such as Mpath cell-fate prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes between defined cell subsets (e.g., mature cDC1 versus cDC2 in GSE60782) using ANOVA followed by post-hoc Tukey's test, with Benjamini-Hochberg P-value adjustment. These end-stage contrast genes serve as signature genes for downstream trajectory/fate analyses such as Mpath cell-fate prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has no defined subset/group labels or end-stage contrasts, since Mpath depends on signature genes of differentiated cell types for fate prediction The goal is de novo clustering or marker discovery in heterogeneous data where specific subset information is not known, rather than testing pre-specified subset contrasts Temporal ordering of developmental stages is assumed in advance — this method explicitly uses genes only from end-stage contrasts without a priori temporal ordering knowledge

skills.description: Use when a normalized gene/ortholog expression matrix with sample metadata is available and the goal is a ranked table of DEGs at a defined FDR threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 1.5, or FDR < 0.1 for salamander-style analyses).
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when a normalized gene/ortholog expression matrix with sample metadata is available and the goal is a ranked table of DEGs at a defined FDR threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 1.5, or FDR < 0.1 for salamander-style analyses). Input is already a gene list or pathway membership set rather than an expression matrix — use the enrichment module instead of the DE module The count table has not been normalized and QC'd — run box plot/PCA QC and PerformExpressNormalization (variance filter 15, abundance filter 4) before DE Multiple datasets must be jointly analyzed for batch effects — switch to the meta-analysis branch (SetAnalType("metadata"), PerformDEAnalMeta, batch correction via PlotMetaPCA) instead of single-table limma http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify differentially expressed genes from a normalized RNA-seq or microarray count table using limma (with voom log2 CPM normalization for RNA-seq) as implemented in ExpressAnalyst/ExpressAnalystR, supporting blocking factors, custom contrasts, and FDR-adjusted thresholds matched to the study design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Identify differentially expressed genes from a normalized RNA-seq or microarray count table using limma (with voom log2 CPM normalization for RNA-seq) as implemented in ExpressAnalyst/ExpressAnalystR, supporting blocking factors, custom contrasts, and FDR-adjusted thresholds matched to the study design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene list or pathway membership set rather than an expression matrix — use the enrichment module instead of the DE module The count table has not been normalized and QC'd — run box plot/PCA QC and PerformExpressNormalization (variance filter 15, abundance filter 4) before DE Multiple datasets must be jointly analyzed for batch effects — switch to the meta-analysis branch (SetAnalType("metadata"), PerformDEAnalMeta, batch correction via PlotMetaPCA) instead of single-table limma

skills.description: Use when cells have already been assigned to clusters by SINCERA cluster.assignment and you need per-cluster differentially expressed genes to characterize cell types or build gene signatures.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when cells have already been assigned to clusters by SINCERA cluster.assignment and you need per-cluster differentially expressed genes to characterize cell types or build gene signatures. Cells have not yet been clustered — cluster.diffgenes requires cluster assignments from cluster.assignment; differential testing on unclustered single cells is out of scope The analysis targets single-cell differential expression across conditions (e.g. disease vs control) rather than between cell clusters; tools like SCDE or SAMstrt are referenced for that setting Genes have not passed cluster.geneSelection (specificity threshold 0.7) — unselectively expressed housekeeping genes should be dropped first to avoid non-discriminative signatures http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies differentially expressed genes per cell cluster in SINCERA after clustering, using one-tailed Welch's t test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test with a p-value threshold of 0.05, feeding downstream cell type enrichment analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes per cell cluster in SINCERA after clustering, using one-tailed Welch's t test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test with a p-value threshold of 0.05, feeding downstream cell type enrichment analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have not yet been clustered — cluster.diffgenes requires cluster assignments from cluster.assignment; differential testing on unclustered single cells is out of scope The analysis targets single-cell differential expression across conditions (e.g. disease vs control) rather than between cell clusters; tools like SCDE or SAMstrt are referenced for that setting Genes have not passed cluster.geneSelection (specificity threshold 0.7) — unselectively expressed housekeeping genes should be dropped first to avoid non-discriminative signatures

skills.description: Use when a raw read count matrix plus sample metadata (e.g. GSE147507 severity study) must be tested for infected-vs-mock differential expression under |log2FC|>1 and adj p<0.05 thresholds.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when a raw read count matrix plus sample metadata (e.g. GSE147507 severity study) must be tested for infected-vs-mock differential expression under |log2FC|>1 and adj p<0.05 thresholds. Input is already normalized expression (FPKM/TPM) rather than raw counts — DESeq2 requires raw counts; FPKM/TPM are the input format for rFASTCORMICS, not for this DEG testing step The aim is pathway enrichment on pre-computed gene lists rather than testing for differential expression itself (use Enrichr/GSEApy instead) The contrast involves no biological replicates, so dispersion cannot be estimated for DESeq2 testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SARS-CoV-2-infected and mock lung cell conditions on a raw RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GEO GSE147507) using DESeq2, after filtering low-expression genes with edgeR's filterByExpr, and applies the significance thresholds |log2 fold change| > 1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Computes differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SARS-CoV-2-infected and mock lung cell conditions on a raw RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GEO GSE147507) using DESeq2, after filtering low-expression genes with edgeR's filterByExpr, and applies the significance thresholds |log2 fold change| > 1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized expression (FPKM/TPM) rather than raw counts — DESeq2 requires raw counts; FPKM/TPM are the input format for rFASTCORMICS, not for this DEG testing step The aim is pathway enrichment on pre-computed gene lists rather than testing for differential expression itself (use Enrichr/GSEApy instead) The contrast involves no biological replicates, so dispersion cannot be estimated for DESeq2 testing

skills.description: Use when you have GEMLI-predicted symmetric/asymmetric cell fate lineages with cell type annotations and need to identify DEGs between cells of the same type that followed different fate decisions.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when you have GEMLI-predicted symmetric/asymmetric cell fate lineages with cell type annotations and need to identify DEGs between cells of the same type that followed different fate decisions. Cells lack predicted lineage/fate assignments (no cell_fate_analysis in GEMLI_items), since the contrast groups here are lineage-defined rather than cluster-defined Populations contain only distantly related cells, where GEMLI lineage prediction (and hence fate-based DEG grouping) performs less robustly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Calls differentially expressed genes between cell groups defined by GEMLI-predicted lineage fate (e.g., DCIS cells in symmetric vs. asymmetric lineages from the human breast cancer scRNA-seq dataset), then visualizes them with a volcano plot. This exposes gene expression changes at the onset of cancer invasiveness that are invisible without lineage information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Calls differentially expressed genes between cell groups defined by GEMLI-predicted lineage fate (e.g., DCIS cells in symmetric vs. asymmetric lineages from the human breast cancer scRNA-seq dataset), then visualizes them with a volcano plot. This exposes gene expression changes at the onset of cancer invasiveness that are invisible without lineage information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack predicted lineage/fate assignments (no cell_fate_analysis in GEMLI_items), since the contrast groups here are lineage-defined rather than cluster-defined Populations contain only distantly related cells, where GEMLI lineage prediction (and hence fate-based DEG grouping) performs less robustly

skills.description: Use when rare cells detected from a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. 4238 FiRE-detected PBMC cells) have been clustered and specific clusters must be biologically characterized and assigned to known reference sub-types.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when rare cells detected from a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. 4238 FiRE-detected PBMC cells) have been clustered and specific clusters must be biologically characterized and assigned to known reference sub-types. Input expression profiles have not been through FiRE rareness scoring and dropClust clustering — without FiRE-detected rare cells there are no rare clusters to characterize. The goal is de novo discovery of cell sub-types rather than assigning clusters to an existing reference signature set such as the Villani dendritic sub-types. The target population is an abundant cell type; FiRE scoring is designed for minor subpopulations that require profiling several thousands of cells to capture. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Characterizes FiRE-detected rare dendritic cell clusters from ~68k human PBMC single-cell expression profiles by differential gene expression, overlaying cluster marker genes with Villani dendritic sub-type reference signatures to resolve DC1, DC3, DC4 and DC6 sub-types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Characterizes FiRE-detected rare dendritic cell clusters from ~68k human PBMC single-cell expression profiles by differential gene expression, overlaying cluster marker genes with Villani dendritic sub-type reference signatures to resolve DC1, DC3, DC4 and DC6 sub-types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression profiles have not been through FiRE rareness scoring and dropClust clustering — without FiRE-detected rare cells there are no rare clusters to characterize. The goal is de novo discovery of cell sub-types rather than assigning clusters to an existing reference signature set such as the Villani dendritic sub-types. The target population is an abundant cell type; FiRE scoring is designed for minor subpopulations that require profiling several thousands of cells to capture.

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-cell Smart-seq2 (or comparable) scRNA-seq count matrix is paired with per-cell mtDNA clone/subclone labels and the goal is to test if two subclones are transcriptionally distinct and which Hallmark pathways separate them.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when a gene-by-cell Smart-seq2 (or comparable) scRNA-seq count matrix is paired with per-cell mtDNA clone/subclone labels and the goal is to test if two subclones are transcriptionally distinct and which Hallmark pathways separate them. skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-testing Use when simulated or real single-cell data contain a binary covariate (e.g. stimulant/mutational status) and you need to quantify how well DE-based tests recover genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions versus a dedicated interaction model. skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw or normalized expression matrices but no constructed/aligned gene regulatory networks — run the full scTenifoldNet pipeline (scQC through manifoldAlignment) first You need differential expression at the expression level rather than differential regulation at the network/regulatory level — scTenifoldNet compares constructed scGRNs, not expression fold changes The two samples are highly dissimilar (e.g., different cell types) — the article notes scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type

skills.description: Use when you have scPRINT-derived gene networks (GRnnData objects) for two cell states or conditions — e.g. BPH-associated vs normal prostate fibroblasts — and need to flag genes whose hub status changes between conditions.
skills.name: differential-hub-gene-identification
skills.search_text: differential-hub-gene-identification Use when you have scPRINT-derived gene networks (GRnnData objects) for two cell states or conditions — e.g. BPH-associated vs normal prostate fibroblasts — and need to flag genes whose hub status changes between conditions. You only have raw counts or expression matrices with no inferred gene network — centrality cannot be computed without edges. The task requires causal or directed ground-truth validation; the paper notes 'no perfect ground truths exist' for gene network inference benchmarking, so hub scores are model-derived attention weights, not proven interactions. Networks were built on different gene sets per condition (e.g. different variable-gene sets), making rank comparison across genes ill-defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify cell-type-specific and differential hub genes by computing per-gene centrality (eigenvector centrality plus row-wise target-hub and column-wise regulator-hub edge-score sums) on scPRINT-inferred gene networks and ranking BPH vs normal fibroblast networks against each other. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Identify cell-type-specific and differential hub genes by computing per-gene centrality (eigenvector centrality plus row-wise target-hub and column-wise regulator-hub edge-score sums) on scPRINT-inferred gene networks and ranking BPH vs normal fibroblast networks against each other.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw counts or expression matrices with no inferred gene network — centrality cannot be computed without edges. The task requires causal or directed ground-truth validation; the paper notes 'no perfect ground truths exist' for gene network inference benchmarking, so hub scores are model-derived attention weights, not proven interactions. Networks were built on different gene sets per condition (e.g. different variable-gene sets), making rank comparison across genes ill-defined.

skills.description: Use when you have per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA-site) count tables for two cell types or regions and need to identify genes whose percent-isoform usage shifts significantly between them.
skills.name: differential-isoform-expression-testing
skills.search_text: differential-isoform-expression-testing Use when you have per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA-site) count tables for two cell types or regions and need to identify genes whose percent-isoform usage shifts significantly between them. The input is short-read gene-level expression data without isoform-resolved counts — a standard differential gene expression test, not the chi-square isoform-proportion test, is appropriate You need exon-level usage changes rather than full-isoform proportion shifts — ExonQuant is the alternative, though isoform tests perform better for DIE Comparing more than two conditions at once — DiffSplicingAnalysis as used here requires pairwise comparisons via config rows (e.g. RGL->NIPC, NIPC->GranuleNB, GranuleNB->EN) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Gene-wise differential isoform expression (DIE) testing between two biological conditions (e.g. mouse hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex) using scisorseqr's per-gene n x 2 chi-square tests on isoform (and optionally TSS/polyA-site) proportions, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR <= 0.05 and delta-PI >= 0.1 cutoffs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Gene-wise differential isoform expression (DIE) testing between two biological conditions (e.g. mouse hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex) using scisorseqr's per-gene n x 2 chi-square tests on isoform (and optionally TSS/polyA-site) proportions, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR <= 0.05 and delta-PI >= 0.1 cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is short-read gene-level expression data without isoform-resolved counts — a standard differential gene expression test, not the chi-square isoform-proportion test, is appropriate You need exon-level usage changes rather than full-isoform proportion shifts — ExonQuant is the alternative, though isoform tests perform better for DIE Comparing more than two conditions at once — DiffSplicingAnalysis as used here requires pairwise comparisons via config rows (e.g. RGL->NIPC, NIPC->GranuleNB, GranuleNB->EN)

skills.description: Use when clustering results (e.g. 19 scCAN clusters on the Brain 1.3M dataset, GSE93421) lack true cell type labels and must be biologically validated and mapped to known cell types via marker genes.
skills.name: differential-marker-expression-testing
skills.search_text: differential-marker-expression-testing Use when clustering results (e.g. 19 scCAN clusters on the Brain 1.3M dataset, GSE93421) lack true cell type labels and must be biologically validated and mapped to known cell types via marker genes. When the single-cell dataset already has trusted per-cell cell-type labels — supervised annotation or direct ARI comparison (as in the scCAN README example using adjustedRandIndex) is more appropriate When no curated reference marker set exists for the tissue's expected cell types — Jaccard overlap against an unrelated marker panel would produce meaningless probabilities Before clustering has been performed — this skill validates an existing partition; run scCAN (autoencoder + network fusion + spectral clustering) first to obtain cluster assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies differentially expressed marker genes for each scCAN cluster and validates clusters biologically by computing Jaccard-overlap probabilities against reference marker gene sets (e.g. 24 PanglaoDB brain cell types), producing a cluster-by-cell-type probability matrix and a one-to-one cluster-to-cell-type mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed marker genes for each scCAN cluster and validates clusters biologically by computing Jaccard-overlap probabilities against reference marker gene sets (e.g. 24 PanglaoDB brain cell types), producing a cluster-by-cell-type probability matrix and a one-to-one cluster-to-cell-type mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the single-cell dataset already has trusted per-cell cell-type labels — supervised annotation or direct ARI comparison (as in the scCAN README example using adjustedRandIndex) is more appropriate When no curated reference marker set exists for the tissue's expected cell types — Jaccard overlap against an unrelated marker panel would produce meaningless probabilities Before clustering has been performed — this skill validates an existing partition; run scCAN (autoencoder + network fusion + spectral clustering) first to obtain cluster assignments

skills.description: Use when raw IDAT files plus a sample sheet from an Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array study (e.g. from GEO) need differential methylation calling between groups, and a GUI-driven, reproducible pipeline is acceptable.
skills.name: differential-methylation-calling
skills.search_text: differential-methylation-calling Use when raw IDAT files plus a sample sheet from an Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array study (e.g. from GEO) need differential methylation calling between groups, and a GUI-driven, reproducible pipeline is acceptable. The host is ARM64 (e.g. Apple Silicon) — methylR's Docker container is built for AMD64 and ARM64 is not supported Data are already normalized beta-value tables or precomputed DMC lists — use methylR's downstream accessory modules (MDS/PCA, volcano, enrichment) instead of the ChAMP differential calling module The analysis requires command-line scripting or cluster HPC integration beyond what the Shiny GUI offers — consider running ChAMP or minfi directly in R http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Call differentially methylated CpGs (DMCs) from raw Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array data using the ChAMP analysis module inside the methylR Shiny/Docker pipeline. Validated by reproducing the published full-dataset DMC count (123,510 DMCs) on GEO dataset GSE207426 (glioblastoma). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad184
skills.summary: Call differentially methylated CpGs (DMCs) from raw Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array data using the ChAMP analysis module inside the methylR Shiny/Docker pipeline. Validated by reproducing the published full-dataset DMC count (123,510 DMCs) on GEO dataset GSE207426 (glioblastoma).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The host is ARM64 (e.g. Apple Silicon) — methylR's Docker container is built for AMD64 and ARM64 is not supported Data are already normalized beta-value tables or precomputed DMC lists — use methylR's downstream accessory modules (MDS/PCA, volcano, enrichment) instead of the ChAMP differential calling module The analysis requires command-line scripting or cluster HPC integration beyond what the Shiny GUI offers — consider running ChAMP or minfi directly in R
