skills.description: Use when you have a TCGA-style MAF mutation file and sample groups defined by a continuous factor (e.g. top/bottom hypoxia GSVA score) and need per-gene mutation p-values and FDR between groups.
skills.name: differential-mutation-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-mutation-frequency-analysis Use when you have a TCGA-style MAF mutation file and sample groups defined by a continuous factor (e.g. top/bottom hypoxia GSVA score) and need per-gene mutation p-values and FDR between groups. You only need mutation summary/oncoplot visualization of a single cohort without group comparison — use ARMT's 'Mutant mapping' / maftools Summary mode instead Input is somatic copy-number variation or CNV burden rather than SNV; the validated case study screens SNVs in a standard .maf file Groups cannot be defined through a shared sample column between MAF and phenotype/GSVA data (no common-sample integration possible) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Identify genes whose SNV mutation frequency differs significantly between two sample strata (e.g. hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD) by running ARMT's mutation differential analysis, which wraps maftools on a merged MAF-plus-phenotype dataset and visualizes results as a forest plot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Identify genes whose SNV mutation frequency differs significantly between two sample strata (e.g. hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD) by running ARMT's mutation differential analysis, which wraps maftools on a merged MAF-plus-phenotype dataset and visualizes results as a forest plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need mutation summary/oncoplot visualization of a single cohort without group comparison — use ARMT's 'Mutant mapping' / maftools Summary mode instead Input is somatic copy-number variation or CNV burden rather than SNV; the validated case study screens SNVs in a standard .maf file Groups cannot be defined through a shared sample column between MAF and phenotype/GSVA data (no common-sample integration possible)

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell count matrices from two matched conditions (e.g., 211 normal vs 656 tumor immune cells from GSE114727) and want to detect co-expression edges present in one condition but absent in the other.
skills.name: differential-network-edge-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-network-edge-analysis Use when you have single-cell count matrices from two matched conditions (e.g., 211 normal vs 656 tumor immune cells from GSE114727) and want to detect co-expression edges present in one condition but absent in the other. The analysis goal is directed regulatory relationships — scLink edges are based on statistical dependencies and do not have directions You only have bulk RNA-seq data — imputed single-cell-oriented networks may still be much sparser than bulk data, and bulk-data network methods follow a different workflow Gene set exceeds a few thousand genes without prior correlation analysis — the article advises first using sclink_cor and possibly dividing genes into modules before network inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies condition-specific gene co-expression edges by building separate scLink sparse networks (via sclink_norm and sclink_net with BIC-selected lda) for each condition, then tabulating normal-only vs tumor-only edges with |change in scLink correlation| > 0.5 and bootstrap FDR-adjusted significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Identifies condition-specific gene co-expression edges by building separate scLink sparse networks (via sclink_norm and sclink_net with BIC-selected lda) for each condition, then tabulating normal-only vs tumor-only edges with |change in scLink correlation| > 0.5 and bootstrap FDR-adjusted significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is directed regulatory relationships — scLink edges are based on statistical dependencies and do not have directions You only have bulk RNA-seq data — imputed single-cell-oriented networks may still be much sparser than bulk data, and bulk-data network methods follow a different workflow Gene set exceeds a few thousand genes without prior correlation analysis — the article advises first using sclink_cor and possibly dividing genes into modules before network inference

skills.description: Use when you have two tab-separated gene expression matrices (same genes, rows=genes, columns=samples) from two biological conditions and need a condition-specific differential network for downstream pathway enrichment.
skills.name: differential-network-inference-boosted-trees
skills.search_text: differential-network-inference-boosted-trees Use when you have two tab-separated gene expression matrices (same genes, rows=genes, columns=samples) from two biological conditions and need a condition-specific differential network for downstream pathway enrichment. The two input matrices do not share the same gene/feature set or the first column is not named 'Gene' — BoostDiff requires identical features across conditions Either condition has fewer than ~15 samples per condition (min_samples default) or well below the recommended ~30 samples per condition The goal is a static (single-condition) regulatory network rather than a differential network between two conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infers a differential gene regulatory network between two conditions (e.g., Crohn's disease vs. control colon biopsies) using BoostDiff, a modified AdaBoost ensemble of differential regression trees with differential variance improvement (DVI) as the splitting criterion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Infers a differential gene regulatory network between two conditions (e.g., Crohn's disease vs. control colon biopsies) using BoostDiff, a modified AdaBoost ensemble of differential regression trees with differential variance improvement (DVI) as the splitting criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two input matrices do not share the same gene/feature set or the first column is not named 'Gene' — BoostDiff requires identical features across conditions Either condition has fewer than ~15 samples per condition (min_samples default) or well below the recommended ~30 samples per condition The goal is a static (single-condition) regulatory network rather than a differential network between two conditions

skills.description: Use when two tab-separated gene expression matrices (genes as rows, first column named 'Gene') from two conditions are available and the goal is a condition-specific differential regulatory network with enriched disease-relevant pathways.
skills.name: differential-network-inference-from-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: differential-network-inference-from-transcriptomics Use when two tab-separated gene expression matrices (genes as rows, first column named 'Gene') from two conditions are available and the goal is a condition-specific differential regulatory network with enriched disease-relevant pathways. The inputs are not matched two-condition expression matrices with an identical gene set — BoostDiff simultaneously requires a disease and a control matrix with the same features The goal is single-condition network inference or differential expression alone; BoostDiff targets differential networks and is meant to complement standard differential expression analyses Sample size per condition is below the package minimum (min_samples=15 per condition); the README recommends at least 30 samples per condition as ideal input http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer a differential gene regulatory network discriminating two biological conditions (e.g., disease vs. control) by building modified AdaBoost ensembles of differential regression trees with differential variance improvement (DVI) as the splitting criterion, as implemented in BoostDiff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Infer a differential gene regulatory network discriminating two biological conditions (e.g., disease vs. control) by building modified AdaBoost ensembles of differential regression trees with differential variance improvement (DVI) as the splitting criterion, as implemented in BoostDiff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inputs are not matched two-condition expression matrices with an identical gene set — BoostDiff simultaneously requires a disease and a control matrix with the same features The goal is single-condition network inference or differential expression alone; BoostDiff targets differential networks and is meant to complement standard differential expression analyses Sample size per condition is below the package minimum (min_samples=15 per condition); the README recommends at least 30 samples per condition as ideal input

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters and candidate LR pairs are available and the goal is to determine which intracellular signaling pathways are significantly activated per cluster and which LR interactions are functionally associated with them.
skills.name: differential-pathway-activation-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-pathway-activation-analysis Use when scRNA-seq clusters and candidate LR pairs are available and the goal is to determine which intracellular signaling pathways are significantly activated per cluster and which LR interactions are functionally associated with them. When only intercellular LR pair expression statistics are needed without interpreting downstream pathway activity in receiver cells (e.g. a CellPhoneDB-style first-pass screen). When the expression matrix is raw counts not yet normalized by library-size and log-transformed, since CommPath expects normalized input. When the biological question concerns differential communication between two conditions (tumor vs normal) — use CommPath's comparePath workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A CommPath-based procedure for scoring per-cell signaling pathway activities (GSVA/UCell) and testing which pathways are significantly activated in each cell cluster versus other user-defined clusters, then tying those activated pathways back to ligand-receptor interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: A CommPath-based procedure for scoring per-cell signaling pathway activities (GSVA/UCell) and testing which pathways are significantly activated in each cell cluster versus other user-defined clusters, then tying those activated pathways back to ligand-receptor interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only intercellular LR pair expression statistics are needed without interpreting downstream pathway activity in receiver cells (e.g. a CellPhoneDB-style first-pass screen). When the expression matrix is raw counts not yet normalized by library-size and log-transformed, since CommPath expects normalized input. When the biological question concerns differential communication between two conditions (tumor vs normal) — use CommPath's comparePath workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when you have spot-level (or cell-level) continuous feature values such as Seurat module scores plus 2D/3D spatial coordinates, and you need to rank gene sets or features by how non-randomly their activity is distributed across the tissue.
skills.name: differential-pathway-activity-prediction
skills.search_text: differential-pathway-activity-prediction Use when you have spot-level (or cell-level) continuous feature values such as Seurat module scores plus 2D/3D spatial coordinates, and you need to rank gene sets or features by how non-randomly their activity is distributed across the tissue. Comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type and knockout) — singleCellHaystack cannot easily conduct multi-condition comparisons, per the authors' discussion When the Python implementation is required and hierarchical clustering of gene sets is needed — the Python package lacks the hclust_haystack cluster_genes method When minimal runtime on large spatial data is the priority — SPARK-X is faster, though singleCellHaystack is more sensitive http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predict biological pathways (gene sets) with non-random spatial distributions in Visium spatial transcriptomics data by scoring msigdbr BioCarta gene sets with Seurat AddModuleScore and running singleCellHaystack v1.0.0 KLD-based detection on spot coordinates, without cluster-based comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Predict biological pathways (gene sets) with non-random spatial distributions in Visium spatial transcriptomics data by scoring msigdbr BioCarta gene sets with Seurat AddModuleScore and running singleCellHaystack v1.0.0 KLD-based detection on spot coordinates, without cluster-based comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type and knockout) — singleCellHaystack cannot easily conduct multi-condition comparisons, per the authors' discussion When the Python implementation is required and hierarchical clustering of gene sets is needed — the Python package lacks the hclust_haystack cluster_genes method When minimal runtime on large spatial data is the priority — SPARK-X is faster, though singleCellHaystack is more sensitive

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptomic data has been embedded in VEGA's pathway-informed latent space and you need to test which gene modules differ in activity between defined cell groups or conditions.
skills.name: differential-pathway-activity-testing
skills.search_text: differential-pathway-activity-testing Use when single-cell transcriptomic data has been embedded in VEGA's pathway-informed latent space and you need to test which gene modules differ in activity between defined cell groups or conditions. You need a predictive or strongly generative model rather than an interpretable latent representation — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive/generative performance for interpretability Your gene sets are known to be incomplete or not context-specific and you need to correct prior knowledge during training — VEGA's hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior module membership Input data lacks a GMT gene module definition, so no pathway-wired latent space can be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Identify significantly activated gene module variables (GMVs) by comparing VEGA-inferred pathway activity distributions across cell groups (e.g., interferon-stimulated vs. control PBMCs), leveraging VEGA's interpretable latent space where each latent dimension maps to a biological pathway or gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Identify significantly activated gene module variables (GMVs) by comparing VEGA-inferred pathway activity distributions across cell groups (e.g., interferon-stimulated vs. control PBMCs), leveraging VEGA's interpretable latent space where each latent dimension maps to a biological pathway or gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a predictive or strongly generative model rather than an interpretable latent representation — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive/generative performance for interpretability Your gene sets are known to be incomplete or not context-specific and you need to correct prior knowledge during training — VEGA's hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior module membership Input data lacks a GMT gene module definition, so no pathway-wired latent space can be constructed

skills.description: Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two condition groups (e.g., CF vs non-CF, or treated vs control) needs a benchmarked differential pathway activity comparison across rROMA and sample-wise scoring methods.
skills.name: differential-pathway-activity-testing-between-condition-groups
skills.search_text: differential-pathway-activity-testing-between-condition-groups Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two condition groups (e.g., CF vs non-CF, or treated vs control) needs a benchmarked differential pathway activity comparison across rROMA and sample-wise scoring methods. The expression matrix is raw counts or otherwise not normalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data (e.g., cpm or vst) and will not give valid module statistics on raw input The analysis goal is single-method pathway scoring rather than a cross-method benchmark against expected biology Gene sets outside MSigDB Hallmark-scale references are required without a GMT file — the workflow depends on a GMT module list (SelectFromMSIGdb or ReadGMTFile) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Benchmark workflow that tests differential pathway activity between condition groups by comparing rROMA module statistics against sample-wise quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) on the GSE176121 cystic fibrosis airway epithelial dataset, checking whether each method recovers expected biology (TNFα signaling as top shifted pathway in the IL17+TNFα scenario). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Benchmark workflow that tests differential pathway activity between condition groups by comparing rROMA module statistics against sample-wise quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) on the GSE176121 cystic fibrosis airway epithelial dataset, checking whether each method recovers expected biology (TNFα signaling as top shifted pathway in the IL17+TNFα scenario).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw counts or otherwise not normalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data (e.g., cpm or vst) and will not give valid module statistics on raw input The analysis goal is single-method pathway scoring rather than a cross-method benchmark against expected biology Gene sets outside MSigDB Hallmark-scale references are required without a GMT file — the workflow depends on a GMT module list (SelectFromMSIGdb or ReadGMTFile)

skills.description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency (runtime, memory) and sensitivity of pathway activity scoring / differential pathway methods (scPAFA vs SCPA) on million-cell-scale scRNA-seq data with >1000 pathways, or when assessing whether downsampling-based tools lose disease-relevant pathway.
skills.name: differential-pathway-ranking-comparison
skills.search_text: differential-pathway-ranking-comparison Use when comparing the computational efficiency (runtime, memory) and sensitivity of pathway activity scoring / differential pathway methods (scPAFA vs SCPA) on million-cell-scale scRNA-seq data with >1000 pathways, or when assessing whether downsampling-based tools lose disease-relevant pathway. The goal is multicellular pathway module discovery via factor analysis rather than per-cell-type differential pathway ranking — use scPAFA's MOFA-based steps 2–4 instead Either condition has fewer cells than the SCPA downsampling budget (e.g., <500 cells per condition), making the downsampling comparison uninformative Input is already a pseudobulk/aggregated sample-level matrix rather than a cell-level expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks scPAFA against SCPA for pathway activity scoring (PAS) and per-cell-type differential pathway detection on large single-cell datasets (CRC 108,497-cell subset; lupus 664,214-cell subset), comparing wall-clock runtime and peak memory across SCPA downsampling budgets (500/1000/2000 cells per condition) and validating that interferon-related pathways are consistently ranked as top differential pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks scPAFA against SCPA for pathway activity scoring (PAS) and per-cell-type differential pathway detection on large single-cell datasets (CRC 108,497-cell subset; lupus 664,214-cell subset), comparing wall-clock runtime and peak memory across SCPA downsampling budgets (500/1000/2000 cells per condition) and validating that interferon-related pathways are consistently ranked as top differential pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is multicellular pathway module discovery via factor analysis rather than per-cell-type differential pathway ranking — use scPAFA's MOFA-based steps 2–4 instead Either condition has fewer cells than the SCPA downsampling budget (e.g., <500 cells per condition), making the downsampling comparison uninformative Input is already a pseudobulk/aggregated sample-level matrix rather than a cell-level expression matrix

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq data from two or more conditions share a common trajectory (topologyTest fails to reject it) and the goal is to detect condition-specific shifts in pseudotime distributions along lineages.
skills.name: differential-progression-testing
skills.search_text: differential-progression-testing Use when scRNA-Seq data from two or more conditions share a common trajectory (topologyTest fails to reject it) and the goal is to detect condition-specific shifts in pseudotime distributions along lineages. The topologyTest rejects the common-trajectory null, indicating fundamentally different topologies between conditions rather than a progression shift along a shared path The question is which lineage cells commit to (differential fate selection) rather than how fast they progress; use fateSelectionTest on lineage weights instead Data are steady-state with no trajectory structure; cluster-based differential abundance methods like DAseq or milo are the appropriate family, though the paper's simulations show trajectory-aware tests outperform them when a trajectory exists http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Test whether cells from different conditions progress at different rates along a shared trajectory by comparing per-lineage pseudotime distributions with condiments' progressionTest, typically downstream of slingshot-inferred common trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Test whether cells from different conditions progress at different rates along a shared trajectory by comparing per-lineage pseudotime distributions with condiments' progressionTest, typically downstream of slingshot-inferred common trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The topologyTest rejects the common-trajectory null, indicating fundamentally different topologies between conditions rather than a progression shift along a shared path The question is which lineage cells commit to (differential fate selection) rather than how fast they progress; use fateSelectionTest on lineage weights instead Data are steady-state with no trajectory structure; cluster-based differential abundance methods like DAseq or milo are the appropriate family, though the paper's simulations show trajectory-aware tests outperform them when a trajectory exists

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need differential pseudotime analysis of gene expression, cell abundance, or trajectory topology, and sample-to-sample variation must be modeled to avoid false discoveries.
skills.name: differential-pseudotime-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-pseudotime-analysis Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need differential pseudotime analysis of gene expression, cell abundance, or trajectory topology, and sample-to-sample variation must be modeled to avoid false discoveries. Single-sample scRNA-seq data with no biological replicates per condition — cross-sample variability cannot be modeled (condiments-style one-sample assumption is what Lamian is designed to avoid) Data from Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not natively support these trajectory types Systematic comparison of sample-harmonization methods is needed — this is explicitly beyond the article's scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A multi-sample differential pseudotime analysis workflow implemented in Lamian, which constructs pseudotime (TSCAN cluster-based minimum spanning tree), harmonizes samples with Seurat, and tests for topology, cell density (TCD/XCD), and gene expression (TDE/XDE) changes across conditions while accounting for cross-sample variability via permutation-based likelihood ratio tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: A multi-sample differential pseudotime analysis workflow implemented in Lamian, which constructs pseudotime (TSCAN cluster-based minimum spanning tree), harmonizes samples with Seurat, and tests for topology, cell density (TCD/XCD), and gene expression (TDE/XDE) changes across conditions while accounting for cross-sample variability via permutation-based likelihood ratio tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-sample scRNA-seq data with no biological replicates per condition — cross-sample variability cannot be modeled (condiments-style one-sample assumption is what Lamian is designed to avoid) Data from Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not natively support these trajectory types Systematic comparison of sample-harmonization methods is needed — this is explicitly beyond the article's scope

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-Seq data of a bifurcating multipotent population (e.g. MPPs vs. two downstream lineages) to find which regulatory factors are overexpressed in one lineage's progenitors and may encode primed states prior to computing distance covariance entropy.
skills.name: differential-regulatory-factor-overexpression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-regulatory-factor-overexpression-analysis Use when analyzing scRNA-Seq data of a bifurcating multipotent population (e.g. MPPs vs. two downstream lineages) to find which regulatory factors are overexpressed in one lineage's progenitors and may encode primed states prior to computing distance covariance entropy. The input data already includes matched scATAC-Seq in the same cells (e.g. SHARE-Seq) and the goal is direct epigenomic validation of primed states rather than scRNA-Seq-only candidate RF discovery The population is unipotent or terminally differentiated with no competing downstream lineages, since the differential comparison requires MPPs versus progenitors of each of two lineages The aim is tipping-point/bifurcation-timing detection over pseudotime (use DICE's CreateDPTbin workflow or alternatives like BioTIP/scGET) rather than candidate RF identification in a snapshot population http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in lineage priming by performing differential overexpression analysis of transcription factors and chromatin-state modifiers, comparing one lineage's progenitor population against multipotent progenitors (MPPs) and the competing lineage, then filtering to type-1 (low-frequency, primed-subset) factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Identifies candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in lineage priming by performing differential overexpression analysis of transcription factors and chromatin-state modifiers, comparing one lineage's progenitor population against multipotent progenitors (MPPs) and the competing lineage, then filtering to type-1 (low-frequency, primed-subset) factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data already includes matched scATAC-Seq in the same cells (e.g. SHARE-Seq) and the goal is direct epigenomic validation of primed states rather than scRNA-Seq-only candidate RF discovery The population is unipotent or terminally differentiated with no competing downstream lineages, since the differential comparison requires MPPs versus progenitors of each of two lineages The aim is tipping-point/bifurcation-timing detection over pseudotime (use DICE's CreateDPTbin workflow or alternatives like BioTIP/scGET) rather than candidate RF identification in a snapshot population

skills.description: Use when you have one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq sample from each of two conditions (e.g., a CLL donor vs a healthy control, as log2-transformed O/E matrices with cluster indices) and need subpopulation-specific differential regulatory networks and hub TF rankings.
skills.name: differential-regulatory-network-inference
skills.search_text: differential-regulatory-network-inference Use when you have one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq sample from each of two conditions (e.g., a CLL donor vs a healthy control, as log2-transformed O/E matrices with cluster indices) and need subpopulation-specific differential regulatory networks and hub TF rankings. You have multiple donors per condition — the method was developed for one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq sample per condition, and the authors note that extending to multiple donors is a next step pending data availability. You need to incorporate bulk HiChIP data — sc-compReg does not yet support this type of analysis. Your environment is Windows or lacks Linux Bedtools and Homer — the peak-to-gene and motif preprocessing shell scripts require Bedtools (Linux) and Homer (Linux). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Infers condition-specific gene regulatory networks from paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of two conditions using the sc-compReg comparative model, which links subpopulations across conditions and tests differential regulatory relations to nominate hub TFs (e.g., TOX2 for the CLL tumor-specific B7 B cell subpopulation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Infers condition-specific gene regulatory networks from paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of two conditions using the sc-compReg comparative model, which links subpopulations across conditions and tests differential regulatory relations to nominate hub TFs (e.g., TOX2 for the CLL tumor-specific B7 B cell subpopulation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have multiple donors per condition — the method was developed for one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq sample per condition, and the authors note that extending to multiple donors is a next step pending data availability. You need to incorporate bulk HiChIP data — sc-compReg does not yet support this type of analysis. Your environment is Windows or lacks Linux Bedtools and Homer — the peak-to-gene and motif preprocessing shell scripts require Bedtools (Linux) and Homer (Linux).

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and condition labels (e.g., immunotherapy responder status per patient) must be screened for which annotated cell type shows the largest transcriptomic shift between conditions, accounting for patient/replicate structure.
skills.name: differential-state-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-state-analysis Use when scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and condition labels (e.g., immunotherapy responder status per patient) must be screened for which annotated cell type shows the largest transcriptomic shift between conditions, accounting for patient/replicate structure. The goal is differential abundance (changing cell-type proportions between conditions) — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead; scDist targets differential state of predefined cell types Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to counts and requires normalized data (a future version may adapt this) Data are heavily over-clustered relative to condition-specific effects, which downward-biases estimated distances and can produce false negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects predefined cell types whose transcriptomic profiles differ between conditions (differential state) using scDist, a mixed-effects model that estimates the distance between condition means in gene-expression space while absorbing individual-to-individual and cohort-to-cohort variability. Unlike differential abundance approaches (DA-seq, Milo, Meld), it targets changing expression states rather than changing proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Detects predefined cell types whose transcriptomic profiles differ between conditions (differential state) using scDist, a mixed-effects model that estimates the distance between condition means in gene-expression space while absorbing individual-to-individual and cohort-to-cohort variability. Unlike differential abundance approaches (DA-seq, Milo, Meld), it targets changing expression states rather than changing proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential abundance (changing cell-type proportions between conditions) — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead; scDist targets differential state of predefined cell types Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to counts and requires normalized data (a future version may adapt this) Data are heavily over-clustered relative to condition-specific effects, which downward-biases estimated distances and can produce false negatives

skills.description: Use when building synthetic two-condition, multi-batch single-cell benchmark datasets that require a known set of DS genes with controlled log fold-change and proportion, e.g. to evaluate integration or DS-detection pipelines.
skills.name: differential-state-gene-spiking
skills.search_text: differential-state-gene-spiking Use when building synthetic two-condition, multi-batch single-cell benchmark datasets that require a known set of DS genes with controlled log fold-change and proportion, e.g. to evaluate integration or DS-detection pipelines. The data already contain genuine condition effects you want to quantify — the null permutation step destroys real biology and is only appropriate for constructing controlled benchmark data. You need realistic multi-sample disease signatures rather than a synthetic evaluation set — use the real COVID-19 collection integration workflow instead. Ground truth for differential state is already experimentally available for your dataset, making simulated spiking unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 A benchmarking skill that injects controlled ground-truth differential-state (DS) genes into a real scRNA-seq count matrix (with permuted condition labels and log-normal batch effects) so that DS-detection methods can be evaluated against known positives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that injects controlled ground-truth differential-state (DS) genes into a real scRNA-seq count matrix (with permuted condition labels and log-normal batch effects) so that DS-detection methods can be evaluated against known positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data already contain genuine condition effects you want to quantify — the null permutation step destroys real biology and is only appropriate for constructing controlled benchmark data. You need realistic multi-sample disease signatures rather than a synthetic evaluation set — use the real COVID-19 collection integration workflow instead. Ground truth for differential state is already experimentally available for your dataset, making simulated spiking unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods on multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data and reproducible ground truth (which genes are DS, at what logFC) must be generated by simulation anchored to a real reference.
skills.name: differential-state-ground-truth-design
skills.search_text: differential-state-ground-truth-design Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods on multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data and reproducible ground truth (which genes are DS, at what logFC) must be generated by simulation anchored to a real reference. The goal is to detect DS in real (non-simulated) data rather than to benchmark methods against known truth — use pbDS/mmDS instead The input SingleCellExperiment lacks sample_id/group_id/cluster_id structure, so sample-level multi-group simulation anchoring cannot be defined The benchmark requires an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes, which the paper's simulation framework does not yet accommodate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Designs ground-truth benchmark data for differential state (DS) analysis by generating simulated multi-sample, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq counts with muscat's simulation framework, which is anchored to a reference dataset (e.g., example_sce) and into which DE/DP/DM/DB-type differential state is injected with known gene sets and logFC magnitudes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Designs ground-truth benchmark data for differential state (DS) analysis by generating simulated multi-sample, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq counts with muscat's simulation framework, which is anchored to a reference dataset (e.g., example_sce) and into which DE/DP/DM/DB-type differential state is injected with known gene sets and logFC magnitudes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect DS in real (non-simulated) data rather than to benchmark methods against known truth — use pbDS/mmDS instead The input SingleCellExperiment lacks sample_id/group_id/cluster_id structure, so sample-level multi-group simulation anchoring cannot be defined The benchmark requires an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes, which the paper's simulation framework does not yet accommodate

skills.description: Use when validating scHi-C DCI calls (e.g. from scHiCDiff.ZINB) against orthogonal bulk Hi-C DCI sets and differential topologically associating domain (TAD) regions to assess biological support of single-cell detections.
skills.name: differential-tad-region-enrichment
skills.search_text: differential-tad-region-enrichment Use when validating scHi-C DCI calls (e.g. from scHiCDiff.ZINB) against orthogonal bulk Hi-C DCI sets and differential topologically associating domain (TAD) regions to assess biological support of single-cell detections. Input is a bulk Hi-C dataset rather than single-cell interaction counts — bulk comparisons are only used here as an external validation reference, not as the detection input You need to detect DCIs de novo rather than validate already-called ZINB DCIs against external annotations No differential TAD region or bulk Hi-C DCI reference sets are available for the analyzed conditions, so no supported-fraction can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Annotate ZINB-detected differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) from single-cell Hi-C against bulk Hi-C DCIs and differential TAD regions to validate that a majority of detected DCIs are supported and located within differential TADs, as reported in Supplementary Note 6 of the scHiCDiff evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Annotate ZINB-detected differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) from single-cell Hi-C against bulk Hi-C DCIs and differential TAD regions to validate that a majority of detected DCIs are supported and located within differential TADs, as reported in Supplementary Note 6 of the scHiCDiff evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a bulk Hi-C dataset rather than single-cell interaction counts — bulk comparisons are only used here as an external validation reference, not as the detection input You need to detect DCIs de novo rather than validate already-called ZINB DCIs against external annotations No differential TAD region or bulk Hi-C DCI reference sets are available for the analyzed conditions, so no supported-fraction can be computed

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq BAMs from a branching differentiation system need TE-level quantification and comparison of TE expression between annotated cell-fate branches (e.g., contracting vs non-contractile cardiomyocyte lineages).
skills.name: differential-te-expression-across-cardiac-lineage-branches
skills.search_text: differential-te-expression-across-cardiac-lineage-branches Use when single-cell RNA-seq BAMs from a branching differentiation system need TE-level quantification and comparison of TE expression between annotated cell-fate branches (e.g., contracting vs non-contractile cardiomyocyte lineages). Input is already a gene or TE feature count table (e.g., a matrix from te_counter) rather than aligned BAM/SAM reads — scTE requires alignment files as input. Only bulk RNA-seq data are available; TE heterogeneity between single-cell branches cannot be assessed without single-cell barcoded libraries. The organism/genome is not among the assemblies scTE_build supports (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) and no custom BED/GTF is available. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies single-cell transposable element expression with scTE on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs (E-MTAB-6268 human cardiac differentiation) and contrasts TE expression between NKX2-5+ definitive cardiomyocyte and SPARC+ non-contractile branches, recovering branch-specific TE markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Quantifies single-cell transposable element expression with scTE on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs (E-MTAB-6268 human cardiac differentiation) and contrasts TE expression between NKX2-5+ definitive cardiomyocyte and SPARC+ non-contractile branches, recovering branch-specific TE markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene or TE feature count table (e.g., a matrix from te_counter) rather than aligned BAM/SAM reads — scTE requires alignment files as input. Only bulk RNA-seq data are available; TE heterogeneity between single-cell branches cannot be assessed without single-cell barcoded libraries. The organism/genome is not among the assemblies scTE_build supports (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) and no custom BED/GTF is available.

skills.description: Use when single-cell BAM/SAM files from distinct cell types (e.g. ESCs and MEFs) need per-cell TE counts from scTE and a list of cell-type-specific differentially expressed TEs.
skills.name: differential-te-expression-testing-between-cell-types
skills.search_text: differential-te-expression-testing-between-cell-types Use when single-cell BAM/SAM files from distinct cell types (e.g. ESCs and MEFs) need per-cell TE counts from scTE and a list of cell-type-specific differentially expressed TEs. Input is already a per-cell TE count matrix or a DE results table rather than raw aligned BAM/SAM reads The goal is TE detection from scATAC-seq chromatin accessibility data — use scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build instead of scTE counting Reads overlapping intronic TE loci are expected to be biologically meaningful TE expression rather than background gene signal — the exclusive or inclusive modes may be more appropriate than nointron http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Quantify transposable element (TE) expression per cell with scTE, aggregate the per-cell TE count matrix by cell type (e.g. ESC vs MEF), and test for differentially expressed TEs using a ≥2-fold change with FDR < 0.05, optionally re-testing under the nointron mode to confirm TE specificity is not driven by intronic gene reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Quantify transposable element (TE) expression per cell with scTE, aggregate the per-cell TE count matrix by cell type (e.g. ESC vs MEF), and test for differentially expressed TEs using a ≥2-fold change with FDR < 0.05, optionally re-testing under the nointron mode to confirm TE specificity is not driven by intronic gene reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-cell TE count matrix or a DE results table rather than raw aligned BAM/SAM reads The goal is TE detection from scATAC-seq chromatin accessibility data — use scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build instead of scTE counting Reads overlapping intronic TE loci are expected to be biologically meaningful TE expression rather than background gene signal — the exclusive or inclusive modes may be more appropriate than nointron

skills.description: Use when single-cell full-length scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-Seq2 glioblastoma BAMs) require locus-level TE quantification and downstream clustering/marker testing that subfamily-level TE counts cannot resolve.
skills.name: differential-te-locus-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-te-locus-expression-analysis Use when single-cell full-length scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-Seq2 glioblastoma BAMs) require locus-level TE quantification and downstream clustering/marker testing that subfamily-level TE counts cannot resolve. Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking coverage within the 2001 bp window is incomplete and alpha_i estimates are unreliable Distinguishing highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions Input is already a gene expression feature table with no TE/multi-mapping read context to exploit http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Applies the MATES deep-learning pipeline to quantify locus-specific transposable element (TE) expression in Smart-Seq2 single-cell RNA-seq, then tests whether locus-level TE counts improve cell clustering and reveal marker TE associations with gene markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Applies the MATES deep-learning pipeline to quantify locus-specific transposable element (TE) expression in Smart-Seq2 single-cell RNA-seq, then tests whether locus-level TE counts improve cell clustering and reveal marker TE associations with gene markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking coverage within the 2001 bp window is incomplete and alpha_i estimates are unreliable Distinguishing highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions Input is already a gene expression feature table with no TE/multi-mapping read context to exploit

skills.description: Use when AnnData outputs from a trained scETM model (normalized cell topic mixtures in obsm['theta'], topic embeddings in uns['alpha']) are available with obs metadata labeling disease condition and cell type, and you need to identify which learned topics are differentially enriched between groups.
skills.name: differential-topic-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: differential-topic-abundance-testing Use when AnnData outputs from a trained scETM model (normalized cell topic mixtures in obsm['theta'], topic embeddings in uns['alpha']) are available with obs metadata labeling disease condition and cell type, and you need to identify which learned topics are differentially enriched between groups. The AnnData lacks trained scETM embeddings (no obsm['theta'] / uns['alpha']) or the topic model has not been fit to the cells-by-genes matrix The obs metadata does not contain the categorical group labels (disease condition or cell type) needed to define the tested contrasts The goal is cell-type clustering or batch correction rather than testing topic-level differences between labeled groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistical testing of scETM-learned topic loadings for differential abundance between disease/control conditions and across cell types, using large-scale label permutation and Bonferroni correction, followed by inspection of topic gene loadings (varm['rho']) to assign pathway character. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Statistical testing of scETM-learned topic loadings for differential abundance between disease/control conditions and across cell types, using large-scale label permutation and Bonferroni correction, followed by inspection of topic gene loadings (varm['rho']) to assign pathway character.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData lacks trained scETM embeddings (no obsm['theta'] / uns['alpha']) or the topic model has not been fit to the cells-by-genes matrix The obs metadata does not contain the categorical group labels (disease condition or cell type) needed to define the tested contrasts The goal is cell-type clustering or batch correction rather than testing topic-level differences between labeled groups

skills.description: Use when you have pseudotime trajectories inferred from multiple samples (e.g., 8 HCA-BM donors) and want to know whether covariates change which trajectory branches exist, with uncertainty-aware, sample-level statistical inference.
skills.name: differential-topology-testing
skills.search_text: differential-topology-testing Use when you have pseudotime trajectories inferred from multiple samples (e.g., 8 HCA-BM donors) and want to know whether covariates change which trajectory branches exist, with uncertainty-aware, sample-level statistical inference. Your trajectory inference does not produce a cluster-based tree compatible with Lamian's modules — the article notes Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories You need to compare exactly one sample per condition — the article states condiments assumes each condition has one sample and Lamian instead requires sample-level variation to be estimable across replicates Your question is about gene expression along pseudotime or cell density rather than the branching structure itself (use Lamian's TDE/TCD modules instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Test whether the branching structure (topology) of a pseudotime trajectory differs across sample covariates in multi-sample scRNA-seq data, using Lamian's branch detection-rate uncertainty estimates and branchPropTest binomial logistic regression. The skill was validated on the HCA bone marrow dataset by subsampling myeloid cells and showing controlled type I error with monotone power gains. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Test whether the branching structure (topology) of a pseudotime trajectory differs across sample covariates in multi-sample scRNA-seq data, using Lamian's branch detection-rate uncertainty estimates and branchPropTest binomial logistic regression. The skill was validated on the HCA bone marrow dataset by subsampling myeloid cells and showing controlled type I error with monotone power gains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your trajectory inference does not produce a cluster-based tree compatible with Lamian's modules — the article notes Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories You need to compare exactly one sample per condition — the article states condiments assumes each condition has one sample and Lamian instead requires sample-level variation to be estimable across replicates Your question is about gene expression along pseudotime or cell density rather than the branching structure itself (use Lamian's TDE/TCD modules instead)

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell dynamic processes across conditions and you must first decide whether conditions share a common trajectory topology before testing differential progression, fate selection, or gene expression.
skills.name: differential-topology-testing
skills.search_text: differential-topology-testing Use when comparing single-cell dynamic processes across conditions and you must first decide whether conditions share a common trajectory topology before testing differential progression, fate selection, or gene expression. Cells form a steady-state population rather than a dynamic process — cluster cells and assess differential abundance per cluster instead, since cluster-based approaches ignore continuity of cell-state transitions and trajectory tests assume a trajectory exists Gene-level differences along a lineage are already the target — use tradeSeq fitGAM + conditionTest (Step 3) rather than a topology-level test Differences in cell abundance along a shared trajectory are the target — use progressionTest or fateSelectionTest (Step 2), not a topology test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Step 1 of the condiments workflow: use topologyTest to decide whether cells from different conditions follow a fundamentally different trajectory topology or can be analyzed on a single common trajectory, by permuting condition labels and re-inferring trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Step 1 of the condiments workflow: use topologyTest to decide whether cells from different conditions follow a fundamentally different trajectory topology or can be analyzed on a single common trajectory, by permuting condition labels and re-inferring trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells form a steady-state population rather than a dynamic process — cluster cells and assess differential abundance per cluster instead, since cluster-based approaches ignore continuity of cell-state transitions and trajectory tests assume a trajectory exists Gene-level differences along a lineage are already the target — use tradeSeq fitGAM + conditionTest (Step 3) rather than a topology-level test Differences in cell abundance along a shared trajectory are the target — use progressionTest or fateSelectionTest (Step 2), not a topology test

skills.description: Use when you have multi-sample scRNA-seq (e.g., the 8-donor HCA bone marrow dataset with a sex covariate) and need to test whether trajectory tree topology or branch cell proportions change between conditions.
skills.name: differential-topology-testing-sc-rna-seq
skills.search_text: differential-topology-testing-sc-rna-seq Use when you have multi-sample scRNA-seq (e.g., the 8-donor HCA bone marrow dataset with a sex covariate) and need to test whether trajectory tree topology or branch cell proportions change between conditions. Your data are Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these and tailoring them is deferred to future work. You only need gene expression or cell-density changes along pseudotime rather than branching-structure/topology or branch-proportion differences. Each condition has a single sample with no biological replicates, so cross-sample variability cannot be modeled. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify and test whether pseudotemporal trajectory branching structure (topology) differs across sample covariates in multi-sample scRNA-seq data using Lamian: bootstrapped branch detection rates plus binomial logistic regression of branch cell proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Quantify and test whether pseudotemporal trajectory branching structure (topology) differs across sample covariates in multi-sample scRNA-seq data using Lamian: bootstrapped branch detection rates plus binomial logistic regression of branch cell proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these and tailoring them is deferred to future work. You only need gene expression or cell-density changes along pseudotime rather than branching-structure/topology or branch-proportion differences. Each condition has a single sample with no biological replicates, so cross-sample variability cannot be modeled.

skills.description: Use when you have condition-grouped RNA-seq samples (e.g., 3 control vs 3 LPS-stimulated monocytes from GSE118165) with sample-level IPA usage estimates and need to identify differentially used IPA isoforms between groups.
skills.name: differential-transcript-usage-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-transcript-usage-analysis Use when you have condition-grouped RNA-seq samples (e.g., 3 control vs 3 LPS-stimulated monocytes from GSE118165) with sample-level IPA usage estimates and need to identify differentially used IPA isoforms between groups. You only need to quantify APA usage in annotated 3'UTRs — tools like DaPars, QAPA, or LABRAT suffice, as InPACT/DRIMSeq here targets novel intronic IPA isoforms Your reads are not aligned to a sorted BAM with gene-level grouping feasible, or transcript counts are too low to fit the Dirichlet-multinomial (e.g., genes filtered out by TPM < 1) You lack replication or condition grouping — differential usage testing requires multiple samples per group http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Detect IPA isoforms whose relative usage changes between biological conditions by combining InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates with DRIMSeq's Dirichlet-multinomial differential transcript usage framework, as demonstrated on untreated vs LPS-stimulated human monocyte RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Detect IPA isoforms whose relative usage changes between biological conditions by combining InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates with DRIMSeq's Dirichlet-multinomial differential transcript usage framework, as demonstrated on untreated vs LPS-stimulated human monocyte RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to quantify APA usage in annotated 3'UTRs — tools like DaPars, QAPA, or LABRAT suffice, as InPACT/DRIMSeq here targets novel intronic IPA isoforms Your reads are not aligned to a sorted BAM with gene-level grouping feasible, or transcript counts are too low to fit the Dirichlet-multinomial (e.g., genes filtered out by TPM < 1) You lack replication or condition grouping — differential usage testing requires multiple samples per group

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq differentiation data (adata with cluster annotations and RNA velocity or differentiation potential) must be analyzed to identify time- and fate-specific transcription factor regulators along stochastic trajectories.
skills.name: differential-transcription-factor-activity-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-transcription-factor-activity-analysis Use when single-cell RNA-seq differentiation data (adata with cluster annotations and RNA velocity or differentiation potential) must be analyzed to identify time- and fate-specific transcription factor regulators along stochastic trajectories. Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell transcriptomics — ISMARA/DOROTHEA already handle bulk data and FateCompass targets scRNA-seq trajectories The system lacks robust RNA velocity profiles AND no prior biological knowledge is available to define a differentiation potential gradient (article notes this is difficult in cases such as cancer studies) The goal is exact reconstruction of gene-regulatory interactions, including distal regulatory sites — FateCompass considers only TF-promoter binding sites http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 FateCompass-based differential TF activity analysis that classifies lineage-specific transcription factors during cell-fate decisions using three statistical criteria (Z-score significance, change of regulatory activity, and dynamical correlation of TF activity with TF mRNA level), applied after inferring TF activities with a linear model of gene regulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: FateCompass-based differential TF activity analysis that classifies lineage-specific transcription factors during cell-fate decisions using three statistical criteria (Z-score significance, change of regulatory activity, and dynamical correlation of TF activity with TF mRNA level), applied after inferring TF activities with a linear model of gene regulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell transcriptomics — ISMARA/DOROTHEA already handle bulk data and FateCompass targets scRNA-seq trajectories The system lacks robust RNA velocity profiles AND no prior biological knowledge is available to define a differentiation potential gradient (article notes this is difficult in cases such as cancer studies) The goal is exact reconstruction of gene-regulatory interactions, including distal regulatory sites — FateCompass considers only TF-promoter binding sites

skills.description: Use when you need candidate regulatory factors for bifurcation/priming analysis from scRNA-Seq: e.g. picking top TFs per lineage (retina: 7 neuronal + 7 epithelial; liver: top-4 hepatocyte + top-4 cholangiocyte) before CompDICE.
skills.name: differential-transcription-factor-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-transcription-factor-expression-analysis Use when you need candidate regulatory factors for bifurcation/priming analysis from scRNA-Seq: e.g. picking top TFs per lineage (retina: 7 neuronal + 7 epithelial; liver: top-4 hepatocyte + top-4 cholangiocyte) before CompDICE. skills.search_text: diffusion-geometry-correspondence-loss Use when training a GAN to map between single-cell modalities (e.g. paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq, DBIT-seq transcriptomics/proteomics, or spatial RNA-seq to scRNA-seq) and distribution-matching losses alone leave aligned points uncorrelated with ground truth, i. The geometry-based loss is not completely 'plug-and-play' — it requires choosing a distance between data points — so it is the wrong choice when no meaningful distance metric over the input domain exists or the data cannot be embedded in a metric space You only need distribution-level matching with no point-wise correspondence requirement; a plain CycleGAN or CMAE distribution loss suffices and avoids the extra kernel/eigendecomposition machinery Aligning more than two large modalities where the quadratic growth in required generators would force the networks to be made small or trained separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A geometry-preserving correspondence loss for scMMGAN (TensorFlow) that constrains an over-parameterized GAN by enforcing preservation of diffusion-map geometry across the learned cross-modality mapping, using a new gradient-passing inverse-distance kernel instead of the Gaussian kernel. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577

skills.description: Use when you need a manifold-aware low-dimensional embedding of single-cell (or other high-dimensional) data, or diffusion coordinates to quantify how well a mapping preserves intrinsic geometry.
skills.name: diffusion-map-eigenvector-embedding
skills.search_text: diffusion-map-eigenvector-embedding Use when you need a manifold-aware low-dimensional embedding of single-cell (or other high-dimensional) data, or diffusion coordinates to quantify how well a mapping preserves intrinsic geometry. You only need distributional alignment between modalities without point-wise geometric constraints — a standard adversarial/cycle-consistency loss may suffice The data require a different distance metric — the geometry-based loss is not completely 'plug-and-play' since it still requires a choice of distance between data points http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Computes a diffusion map embedding φ by eigendecomposing a Markov transition matrix built from pairwise affinities, producing low-dimensional diffusion coordinates whose Euclidean distances reflect diffusion distance on the data manifold. skills.description: Use when single cells must be ordered along a differentiation continuum with a diffusion-based method (Scanpy DPT or RWR-based DTFLOW), especially when known developmental stage labels allow scoring by Kendall rank correlation.
skills.name: diffusion-pseudotime-dpt-ordering
skills.search_text: diffusion-pseudotime-dpt-ordering Use when single cells must be ordered along a differentiation continuum with a diffusion-based method (Scanpy DPT or RWR-based DTFLOW), especially when known developmental stage labels allow scoring by Kendall rank correlation. The goal is resolving multiple bifurcation events in a branching trajectory — plain DPT yields a linear ordering only; the article introduces RSKG (Reverse Searching on k-nearest neighbor graph) for multi-branching detection. A restart-augmented diffusion can be tuned instead: the paper reports ordering accuracy is better with p around 0.9, so p=1 DPT may be dominated by the general RWR formulation on the same data. The input is not a cell-level gene expression matrix (e.g., bulk profiles or a metadata table) — the kNN Markov graph and per-cell diffusion distributions require an N x D matrix of single cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Diffusion pseudotime (DPT) ordering of single cells along a differentiation trajectory, framed by the DTFLOW paper as the p=1 special case of random walk with restart (RWR); on the ME mouse-embryo RT-PCR dataset (438 cells, 48 genes) DPT reached Kendall tau 0.796 versus 0.862 for DTFLOW with p=0.9 and 0.761 for Monocle2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Diffusion pseudotime (DPT) ordering of single cells along a differentiation trajectory, framed by the DTFLOW paper as the p=1 special case of random walk with restart (RWR); on the ME mouse-embryo RT-PCR dataset (438 cells, 48 genes) DPT reached Kendall tau 0.796 versus 0.862 for DTFLOW with p=0.9 and 0.761 for Monocle2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is resolving multiple bifurcation events in a branching trajectory — plain DPT yields a linear ordering only; the article introduces RSKG (Reverse Searching on k-nearest neighbor graph) for multi-branching detection. A restart-augmented diffusion can be tuned instead: the paper reports ordering accuracy is better with p around 0.9, so p=1 DPT may be dominated by the general RWR formulation on the same data. The input is not a cell-level gene expression matrix (e.g., bulk profiles or a metadata table) — the kNN Markov graph and per-cell diffusion distributions require an N x D matrix of single cells.

skills.description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g., from GRouNdGAN on the BoneMarrow dataset, Paul et al. 2015, GSE72857) preserves cell trajectories and pseudo-time ordering of a reference dataset, as in Figs. 4-5.

skills.search_text: diffusion-pseudotime-inference Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g., from GRouNdGAN on the BoneMarrow dataset, Paul et al. 2015, GSE72857) preserves cell trajectories and pseudo-time ordering of a reference dataset, as in Figs. 4-5. skills.summary: Jointly embed experimental and GRouNdGAN-simulated single-cell data in scanpy, run PAGA trajectory inference and diffusion pseudotime, then compare marker-gene activation ordering (e.g., Gata2→Gata1→Klf1→Hba-a2 along the erythroid trajectory) between reference and simulated cells to verify pseudo-time and trajectory preservation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: GRouNdGAN only generates library-size normalized expression values across considered genes and TFs, so this validation approach should not assume unnormalized count data are available from the simulator The BoneMarrow dataset is small (~2.7k cells) and simulator performance dropped on the test set, so trajectory concordance on this dataset should not be generalized to larger datasets (e.g., Dahlin, ~45k cells) without re-running the full pipeline This is a validation/similarity skill, not GRN benchmarking — do not use it to evaluate GRN inference method performance; use GRouNdGAN's --benchmark_grn workflow instead

skills.description: Use when you need a controlled benchmark of signature-detection sensitivity/specificity: synthetic 96-channel catalogs with known low-percentage signature contributions are required to compare fitting algorithms' detection thresholds.
skills.name: dilution-catalog-simulation
skills.search_text: dilution-catalog-simulation Use when you need a controlled benchmark of signature-detection sensitivity/specificity: synthetic 96-channel catalogs with known low-percentage signature contributions are required to compare fitting algorithms' detection thresholds. The subnetworks are already directed trees/DAGs and a direction assignment step would only alter the topology The goal is edge-level (not node-level) similarity of already-commensurate network structures The input is a raw expression matrix or gene list rather than a recovered subnetwork — run an active subnetwork detection method first http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Converts undirected perturbed modules produced by active subnetwork detection methods into directed trees using causal additive trees based on Chu–Liu–Edmonds' algorithm, so that heterogeneous methods (pathfindR, BioNet, STr2z, etc.) can be compared on a common directed representation, e.g. via node-set Jaccard similarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Converts undirected perturbed modules produced by active subnetwork detection methods into directed trees using causal additive trees based on Chu–Liu–Edmonds' algorithm, so that heterogeneous methods (pathfindR, BioNet, STr2z, etc.) can be compared on a common directed representation, e.g. via node-set Jaccard similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The subnetworks are already directed trees/DAGs and a direction assignment step would only alter the topology The goal is edge-level (not node-level) similarity of already-commensurate network structures The input is a raw expression matrix or gene list rather than a recovered subnetwork — run an active subnetwork detection method first

skills.search_text: directi-reference-model-training Use when a raw or subsampled scRNA-seq reference dataset (AnnData/h5ad, or legacy h5) must be embedded with DIRECTi before building a Cell BLAST BLAST index for cell querying. Reference datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells, which may suffer from under-training of the over-parameterized neural network model Mega-scale integration where highly skewed cell-type composition risks over-correcting batches When you only need clustering/annotation of a single dataset without querying against a reference — Cell BLAST's similarity metric is designed for cross-dataset cell querying http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train a DIRECTi deep generative model on a scRNA-seq reference dataset to produce unbiased cell embeddings that power Cell BLAST's posterior-distance-based cell querying and downstream annotation transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Train a DIRECTi deep generative model on a scRNA-seq reference dataset to produce unbiased cell embeddings that power Cell BLAST's posterior-distance-based cell querying and downstream annotation transfer.
