skills.description: Use when two orthogonal per-cell label assignments (e.g., copy-number-based vs mutation/expression-based) exist for the same cell barcodes and you need to quantify how well one predicts the other, directionally.
skills.name: directional-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: directional-concordance-analysis Use when two orthogonal per-cell label assignments (e.g., copy-number-based vs mutation/expression-based) exist for the same cell barcodes and you need to quantify how well one predicts the other, directionally. The sample lacks copy-number alterations — CNAs are rare in most AML samples, so the CNA-based reference classification may not be definable The two label sets do not share a common cell-barcode identifier space, making a per-cell contingency table impossible without reconciliation You need variant detection sensitivity, not agreement between existing per-cell classifications — concordance analysis does not address dropout-related sensitivity limits Cross-tabulates two independent single-cell classification schemes — here CNA-based (CONICSmat k=4 clustering on 1p/7q eWGS CNA regions) and SNV/expression-signature-based AML cell calls — and computes directional concordance to benchmark one method against the other in sample 809653. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Cross-tabulates two independent single-cell classification schemes — here CNA-based (CONICSmat k=4 clustering on 1p/7q eWGS CNA regions) and SNV/expression-signature-based AML cell calls — and computes directional concordance to benchmark one method against the other in sample 809653.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample lacks copy-number alterations — CNAs are rare in most AML samples, so the CNA-based reference classification may not be definable The two label sets do not share a common cell-barcode identifier space, making a per-cell contingency table impossible without reconciliation You need variant detection sensitivity, not agreement between existing per-cell classifications — concordance analysis does not address dropout-related sensitivity limits

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq counts from batched experiments (e.g. NEURIPS bone marrow data) need topic compositions and an unconfounded latent representation that separates technical covariates from biological cell states.
skills.name: dirichlet-latent-space-encoding
skills.search_text: dirichlet-latent-space-encoding Use when scRNA-seq counts from batched experiments (e.g. NEURIPS bone marrow data) need topic compositions and an unconfounded latent representation that separates technical covariates from biological cell states. Input is not raw count data — deviance residuals and the Dirichlet-multinomial topic model require unnormalized counts, not already-normalized expression matrices Single-batch data with no technical covariates to disentangle, where standard MIRA topic modeling without the CODAL augmentation suffices Data where batch-confounded cell states cannot be validated with orthogonal biological evidence and under-correction risk is unacceptable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Encodes single-cell RNA-seq counts into an interpretable Dirichlet topic latent space using MIRA's Dirichlet variational encoder (total pseudocount 𝓘=50, Ntopics=22), as extended by CODAL to disentangle technical from biological effects via mutual information regularization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Encodes single-cell RNA-seq counts into an interpretable Dirichlet topic latent space using MIRA's Dirichlet variational encoder (total pseudocount 𝓘=50, Ntopics=22), as extended by CODAL to disentangle technical from biological effects via mutual information regularization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw count data — deviance residuals and the Dirichlet-multinomial topic model require unnormalized counts, not already-normalized expression matrices Single-batch data with no technical covariates to disentangle, where standard MIRA topic modeling without the CODAL augmentation suffices Data where batch-confounded cell states cannot be validated with orthogonal biological evidence and under-correction risk is unacceptable

skills.description: Use when you need controlled simulation benchmarks for multi-individual scRNA-seq clustering: you must vary individual-level heterogeneity and donor count to test whether a method (e.g., BAMM-SC vs SIMLR/SC3/DIMM-SC) benefits from more individuals.
skills.name: dirichlet-multinomial-count-simulation
skills.search_text: dirichlet-multinomial-count-simulation Use when you need controlled simulation benchmarks for multi-individual scRNA-seq clustering: you must vary individual-level heterogeneity and donor count to test whether a method (e.g., BAMM-SC vs SIMLR/SC3/DIMM-SC) benefits from more individuals. You are clustering real droplet scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking — use BAMMSC(X, K) directly on the observed count matrices instead of simulated ones Input is a single individual (a matrix, not a list) — then DIMMSC, not the multi-individual BAMMSC simulation/benchmark path, applies The scientific question concerns zero-inflation patterns or trajectory/developmental-stage assignment, which BAMM-SC's Dirichlet multinomial simulation does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate synthetic droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count matrices by sampling from the Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model (BAMM-SC's generative model), sweeping individual-level heterogeneity (sigma_ik^2) and the number of individuals to benchmark clustering methods by ARI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Generate synthetic droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count matrices by sampling from the Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model (BAMM-SC's generative model), sweeping individual-level heterogeneity (sigma_ik^2) and the number of individuals to benchmark clustering methods by ARI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are clustering real droplet scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking — use BAMMSC(X, K) directly on the observed count matrices instead of simulated ones Input is a single individual (a matrix, not a list) — then DIMMSC, not the multi-individual BAMMSC simulation/benchmark path, applies The scientific question concerns zero-inflation patterns or trajectory/developmental-stage assignment, which BAMM-SC's Dirichlet multinomial simulation does not model

skills.description: Use when converting per-sample cell-cluster count vectors from single-cell AnnData into probability distributions over clusters as input to optimal transport, especially when some samples lack counts for certain clusters and zero probabilities would break downstream distance computations.
skills.name: dirichlet-multinomial-map-estimation
skills.search_text: dirichlet-multinomial-map-estimation Use when converting per-sample cell-cluster count vectors from single-cell AnnData into probability distributions over clusters as input to optimal transport, especially when some samples lack counts for certain clusters and zero probabilities would break downstream distance computations. When the goal is cluster-level or cell-level analysis rather than per-sample distributions — PILOT's downstream steps (Leiden clustering on W, EIPLGraph trajectories) operate on the sample-level distance matrix, not on these distributions directly. When samples come from distinct technologies or cell-isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge and assume uniform collection (similar tissue areas and same technology). When the input is already a normalized probability/feature table per sample rather than raw cell-cluster counts — re-applying pseudo-count smoothing would distort existing proportions. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Robustly estimate each sample's probability distribution over cell clusters via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate, where the Dirichlet prior adds 'pseudo cell counts' weighted by the global cell distribution. This produces the strictly positive per-sample cluster-probability vectors that PILOT feeds into its optimal-transport (Wasserstein distance) module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Robustly estimate each sample's probability distribution over cell clusters via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate, where the Dirichlet prior adds 'pseudo cell counts' weighted by the global cell distribution. This produces the strictly positive per-sample cluster-probability vectors that PILOT feeds into its optimal-transport (Wasserstein distance) module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cluster-level or cell-level analysis rather than per-sample distributions — PILOT's downstream steps (Leiden clustering on W, EIPLGraph trajectories) operate on the sample-level distance matrix, not on these distributions directly. When samples come from distinct technologies or cell-isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge and assume uniform collection (similar tissue areas and same technology). When the input is already a normalized probability/feature table per sample rather than raw cell-cluster counts — re-applying pseudo-count smoothing would distort existing proportions.

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., 10x Chromium droplet scRNA-seq) must be jointly clustered without prior batch correction, and posterior per-cell clustering uncertainty is needed.
skills.name: dirichlet-multinomial-mixture-modeling
skills.search_text: dirichlet-multinomial-mixture-modeling Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., 10x Chromium droplet scRNA-seq) must be jointly clustered without prior batch correction, and posterior per-cell clustering uncertainty is needed. Data are already normalized, batch-corrected, or merged without library adjustment — the model expects raw counts and handles heterogeneity/batch effects itself The goal is trajectory or cell-cycle/developmental-stage analysis — the model assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities measure clustering uncertainty only Identifying very rare cell types — genes with excessive zeros are filtered out, which the authors note may be problematic for rare cell type identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Fit a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model (as implemented in the BAMMSC R package) to cluster droplet-based UMI count data from multiple individuals simultaneously, explicitly modeling variability across genes, cell types, and individuals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Fit a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model (as implemented in the BAMMSC R package) to cluster droplet-based UMI count data from multiple individuals simultaneously, explicitly modeling variability across genes, cell types, and individuals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already normalized, batch-corrected, or merged without library adjustment — the model expects raw counts and handles heterogeneity/batch effects itself The goal is trajectory or cell-cycle/developmental-stage analysis — the model assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities measure clustering uncertainty only Identifying very rare cell types — genes with excessive zeros are filtered out, which the authors note may be problematic for rare cell type identification

skills.description: Use when single-cell data is expected to contain disconnected populations, cyclic/circular processes, or converging multifurcations that tree-only trajectory inference methods would merge or break.
skills.name: disconnected-and-cyclic-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: disconnected-and-cyclic-trajectory-inference Use when single-cell data is expected to contain disconnected populations, cyclic/circular processes, or converging multifurcations that tree-only trajectory inference methods would merge or break. Data is expected to form a simple linear or tree-like topology where tree-based methods (Slingshot, STREAM) suffice and are well-benchmarked Input is already a milestone-network / gold-standard topology rather than single-cell expression data The goal is realistic simulation of synthetic trajectories — use dyngen instead of the simplistic dyntoy model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers non-tree single-cell trajectory topologies — disconnected components, cyclic paths, and hybrid structures — using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks, which tree-based methods like Slingshot and STREAM cannot represent. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Infers non-tree single-cell trajectory topologies — disconnected components, cyclic paths, and hybrid structures — using VIA's lazy-teleporting random walks, which tree-based methods like Slingshot and STREAM cannot represent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is expected to form a simple linear or tree-like topology where tree-based methods (Slingshot, STREAM) suffice and are well-benchmarked Input is already a milestone-network / gold-standard topology rather than single-cell expression data The goal is realistic simulation of synthetic trajectories — use dyngen instead of the simplistic dyntoy model

skills.description: Use when reconstructing ecDNA breakpoints from ATAC-Seq data where junction evidence consists of discordant read pairs with anomalous orientation/insert size and soft-clipped or supplementary-aligned read piles, and realignment is too costly.
skills.name: discordant-read-pair-uniform-likelihood-modeling
skills.search_text: discordant-read-pair-uniform-likelihood-modeling Use when reconstructing ecDNA breakpoints from ATAC-Seq data where junction evidence consists of discordant read pairs with anomalous orientation/insert size and soft-clipped or supplementary-aligned read piles, and realignment is too costly. Input data lacks paired-end junction evidence (no discordant read pairs or clipped reads), e.g. single-end-only ATAC-Seq The target is general structural-variant discovery from WGS depth/copy-number data — use depth-balanced junction graph tools like JaBbA or LINX, or copy-number-based AmpliconArchitect, instead Focal amplifications with misregulated chromatin that are not ecDNA — the accessibility signal may yield false-positive circular calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A Bayesian breakpoint-estimation approach used by circlehunter to pinpoint the exact breakpoints of ecDNA fragments from ATAC-Seq discordant read pair enriched regions without time-consuming read realignment, combining a uniform (German-tank) likelihood over each discordant pair's fragment interval with a Gaussian likelihood on clipped-read offsets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0
skills.summary: A Bayesian breakpoint-estimation approach used by circlehunter to pinpoint the exact breakpoints of ecDNA fragments from ATAC-Seq discordant read pair enriched regions without time-consuming read realignment, combining a uniform (German-tank) likelihood over each discordant pair's fragment interval with a Gaussian likelihood on clipped-read offsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks paired-end junction evidence (no discordant read pairs or clipped reads), e.g. single-end-only ATAC-Seq The target is general structural-variant discovery from WGS depth/copy-number data — use depth-balanced junction graph tools like JaBbA or LINX, or copy-number-based AmpliconArchitect, instead Focal amplifications with misregulated chromatin that are not ecDNA — the accessibility signal may yield false-positive circular calls

skills.description: Use when scATOMIC malignant/non-malignant calls for external tumour biopsies must be cross-checked against CopyKAT aneuploid/diploid ploidy status and discordant biopsies need causal characterization.
skills.name: discordant-sample-characterization
skills.search_text: discordant-sample-characterization Use when scATOMIC malignant/non-malignant calls for external tumour biopsies must be cross-checked against CopyKAT aneuploid/diploid ploidy status and discordant biopsies need causal characterization. Sample is normal (non-cancer) tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes the presence of at least some cancer cells and 'should not be used in normal tissue applications' (use the normal_tissue parameter instead) Analysis pools cells across multiple patients — the authors strongly recommend running scATOMIC only on individual patient/biopsy samples because inter-patient cancer cell effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring Cancer type is already known and CNV-based reconciliation is unnecessary — use the known_cancer_type parameter rather than relying on discordance analysis Reconciles scATOMIC's malignant/non-malignant per-cell predictions against CopyKAT-inferred CNV ploidy (aneuploid vs diploid) per biopsy, computes per-sample agreement rates, and annotates discordant samples with biologically plausible causes such as low CNV burden, sub-clonal CNV heterogeneity, near-diploid cancer cells, or too few reference (normal) cells for CopyKAT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Reconciles scATOMIC's malignant/non-malignant per-cell predictions against CopyKAT-inferred CNV ploidy (aneuploid vs diploid) per biopsy, computes per-sample agreement rates, and annotates discordant samples with biologically plausible causes such as low CNV burden, sub-clonal CNV heterogeneity, near-diploid cancer cells, or too few reference (normal) cells for CopyKAT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample is normal (non-cancer) tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes the presence of at least some cancer cells and 'should not be used in normal tissue applications' (use the normal_tissue parameter instead) Analysis pools cells across multiple patients — the authors strongly recommend running scATOMIC only on individual patient/biopsy samples because inter-patient cancer cell effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring Cancer type is already known and CNV-based reconciliation is unnecessary — use the known_cancer_type parameter rather than relying on discordance analysis

skills.description: Use when building or re-implementing a neural gene/marker selector on scRNA-seq data (e.g. CITE-seq .h5ad) where selecting a discrete subset of k genes must remain differentiable for joint gradient-based optimization with a VAE-style reconstruction or classification objective.
skills.name: discrete-selector-layer-implementation
skills.search_text: discrete-selector-layer-implementation Use when building or re-implementing a neural gene/marker selector on scRNA-seq data (e.g. CITE-seq .h5ad) where selecting a discrete subset of k genes must remain differentiable for joint gradient-based optimization with a VAE-style reconstruction or classification objective. When only a final, non-differentiable discrete marker ranking is needed (e.g. RankCorr- or COSG-style score-and-rank selection) with no joint end-to-end training of the selector When the input is not per-cell gene expression compatible with the MarkerMap VAE pipeline (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables or non-AnnData formats without conversion such as adata.X = adata.X.toarray() for sparse matrices) When the goal is unsupervised-only embedding without marker selection supervision — that is a different loss_tradeoff regime of the same model rather than this selector-layer skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements MarkerMap's differentiable discrete marker-selection layer, where the selection of k genes is performed by sampling from a probabilistic discrete distribution so it can be trained end-to-end with the downstream predictive/reconstruction loss, typically controlled by a temperature parameter τ annealed from a diffuse (τ_init ≥ 2) to a near one-hot (τ_final in (0.001, 0.1)) regime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Implements MarkerMap's differentiable discrete marker-selection layer, where the selection of k genes is performed by sampling from a probabilistic discrete distribution so it can be trained end-to-end with the downstream predictive/reconstruction loss, typically controlled by a temperature parameter τ annealed from a diffuse (τ_init ≥ 2) to a near one-hot (τ_final in (0.001, 0.1)) regime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a final, non-differentiable discrete marker ranking is needed (e.g. RankCorr- or COSG-style score-and-rank selection) with no joint end-to-end training of the selector When the input is not per-cell gene expression compatible with the MarkerMap VAE pipeline (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables or non-AnnData formats without conversion such as adata.X = adata.X.toarray() for sparse matrices) When the goal is unsupervised-only embedding without marker selection supervision — that is a different loss_tradeoff regime of the same model rather than this selector-layer skill

skills.description: Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset lacks cell-type labels while a reference dataset with known clusters exists, especially when the two differ in protocol, batch effect, cell number, or library depth (e.g., Smart-Seq2 reference mapped to CEL-Seq1/CEL-Seq2 targets).
skills.name: discriminant-analysis-cell-classification
skills.search_text: discriminant-analysis-cell-classification Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset lacks cell-type labels while a reference dataset with known clusters exists, especially when the two differ in protocol, batch effect, cell number, or library depth (e.g., Smart-Seq2 reference mapped to CEL-Seq1/CEL-Seq2 targets). Neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types' in that case Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth-normalized (TPM/CPM), non-log data The target dataset is highly shallow and requires imputation — the article defers imputation of gene expression to future work and does not implement or evaluate it http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reference-based cell-type classification across scRNA-seq datasets using scID, a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework that scores target cells on weighted cluster-specific gene signatures and assigns them via a finite mixture of Gaussians, robust to batch effect and imbalanced library sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Reference-based cell-type classification across scRNA-seq datasets using scID, a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework that scores target cells on weighted cluster-specific gene signatures and assigns them via a finite mixture of Gaussians, robust to batch effect and imbalanced library sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Neither dataset is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types' in that case Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth-normalized (TPM/CPM), non-log data The target dataset is highly shallow and requires imputation — the article defers imputation of gene expression to future work and does not implement or evaluate it

skills.description: Use when you need to prioritize genes from high-dimensional RNA-seq data (e.g. TCGA pan-cancer, 20,501 genes) by classification power rather than differential-expression p-values, to build a compact biomarker panel.
skills.name: discriminative-index-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: discriminative-index-gene-ranking Use when you need to prioritize genes from high-dimensional RNA-seq data (e.g. TCGA pan-cancer, 20,501 genes) by classification power rather than differential-expression p-values, to build a compact biomarker panel. The analysis goal is differential-expression testing with statistical significance (adjusted p-values); edgeR is the appropriate DEG tool here, and Wx is positioned as a complement, not a DEG method The dataset has few samples — neural network-based selection needs a large number of samples for good classification or regression performance You need reproducible feature identity across backends/frameworks — selected features can differ depending on which NN backend is used (Keras vs naive TensorFlow) and which algorithm is applied http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Rank genes from a large transcriptomic cohort by their Wx discriminative index (DI) score, computed by iterating a neural network-based feature selection algorithm many times to suppress run-to-run irregularity. The ranked list determines the top gene subsets (e.g. top 14 UGCBs, top 100 genes) used for cancer vs normal classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Rank genes from a large transcriptomic cohort by their Wx discriminative index (DI) score, computed by iterating a neural network-based feature selection algorithm many times to suppress run-to-run irregularity. The ranked list determines the top gene subsets (e.g. top 14 UGCBs, top 100 genes) used for cancer vs normal classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential-expression testing with statistical significance (adjusted p-values); edgeR is the appropriate DEG tool here, and Wx is positioned as a complement, not a DEG method The dataset has few samples — neural network-based selection needs a large number of samples for good classification or regression performance You need reproducible feature identity across backends/frameworks — selected features can differ depending on which NN backend is used (Keras vs naive TensorFlow) and which algorithm is applied

skills.description: Use when ranking genes from high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq/expression matrices by classification power, as an alternative to DEG analysis (e.g., edgeR) for selecting biomarker candidates.
skills.name: discriminative-index-score-computation
skills.search_text: discriminative-index-score-computation Use when ranking genes from high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq/expression matrices by classification power, as an alternative to DEG analysis (e.g., edgeR) for selecting biomarker candidates. Input is already a small curated feature set or gene signature — Wx is designed to rank from thousands of features in high-dimensional NGS data The analysis goal is differential-expression testing with adjusted p-values; edgeR-style DEG analysis is the complementary approach described in the paper Labeled sample groups (e.g., cancer vs normal) are unavailable, since the DI score requires training a supervised softmax classifier on class labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the Wx algorithm's discriminative index (DI) score for every gene by taking inner products of softmax regression parameter vectors with class-average expression vectors, then ranks genes in descending DI-score order. DI score represents classification power for distinguishing given groups (e.g., cancer vs normal) in high-dimensional NGS expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Computes the Wx algorithm's discriminative index (DI) score for every gene by taking inner products of softmax regression parameter vectors with class-average expression vectors, then ranks genes in descending DI-score order. DI score represents classification power for distinguishing given groups (e.g., cancer vs normal) in high-dimensional NGS expression data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small curated feature set or gene signature — Wx is designed to rank from thousands of features in high-dimensional NGS data The analysis goal is differential-expression testing with adjusted p-values; edgeR-style DEG analysis is the complementary approach described in the paper Labeled sample groups (e.g., cancer vs normal) are unavailable, since the DI score requires training a supervised softmax classifier on class labels

skills.description: Use when the input is disease-vs-control scRNA-seq data in .h5ad (anndata) format with a 'disease' target column, and the goal is to rank condition-specific biomarker genes rather than annotate cell types.
skills.name: disease-biomarker-identification
skills.search_text: disease-biomarker-identification Use when the input is disease-vs-control scRNA-seq data in .h5ad (anndata) format with a 'disease' target column, and the goal is to rank condition-specific biomarker genes rather than annotate cell types. The task is cell type annotation/classification on cell_type labels rather than disease-vs-control biomarker discovery (use the cell type classification pipeline instead). Comparison tools such as scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, or CellPLM are used as the model — feature importance cannot be extracted from these, so this top-K biomarker ranking workflow is not applicable. Input data is not in anndata .h5ad format or adata.X is not log1p-normalized in range 0-10; the pipeline expects proper preprocessing and performance may vary with input format. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Identifies disease-vs-control biomarker genes from single-cell RNA-seq using scaLR's low-resource DNN pipeline: train per-condition models, score feature importance (linear weights or SHAP), select top-K genes, and export ranked disease-specific gene lists (top-100 per class) for downstream functional annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Identifies disease-vs-control biomarker genes from single-cell RNA-seq using scaLR's low-resource DNN pipeline: train per-condition models, score feature importance (linear weights or SHAP), select top-K genes, and export ranked disease-specific gene lists (top-100 per class) for downstream functional annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell type annotation/classification on cell_type labels rather than disease-vs-control biomarker discovery (use the cell type classification pipeline instead). Comparison tools such as scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, or CellPLM are used as the model — feature importance cannot be extracted from these, so this top-K biomarker ranking workflow is not applicable. Input data is not in anndata .h5ad format or adata.X is not log1p-normalized in range 0-10; the pipeline expects proper preprocessing and performance may vary with input format.

skills.name: disease-informative-subpopulation-identification-across-cell-types
skills.search_text: disease-informative-subpopulation-identification-across-cell-types Use when case-control single-cell RNA-seq data have a healthy control population usable as a reference trajectory, and the goal is to expose disease-related cells and dynamics masked by healthy shared signal. No healthy reference samples or prior knowledge are available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — SiFT strongly relies on this prior knowledge and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal Downstream analysis strictly requires properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so the filtered data is no longer properly log-transformed The goal is generic batch correction rather than filtering a specific biological (disease) signal; use dedicated integration methods (bbknn, Harmony, scVI) directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies disease-informative subpopulations across annotated cell types by SiFT-filtering the healthy reference signal from case PBMC scRNA-seq data, then classifying cells as disease-informative vs non-informative via neighborhood cluster purity (tau = 0.55). It recovers disease-related dynamics (e.g., interferon-response in monocytes, DCs, HSPC) that the original data fails to expose. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Identifies disease-informative subpopulations across annotated cell types by SiFT-filtering the healthy reference signal from case PBMC scRNA-seq data, then classifying cells as disease-informative vs non-informative via neighborhood cluster purity (tau = 0.55). It recovers disease-related dynamics (e.g., interferon-response in monocytes, DCs, HSPC) that the original data fails to expose.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No healthy reference samples or prior knowledge are available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — SiFT strongly relies on this prior knowledge and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal Downstream analysis strictly requires properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so the filtered data is no longer properly log-transformed The goal is generic batch correction rather than filtering a specific biological (disease) signal; use dedicated integration methods (bbknn, Harmony, scVI) directly instead

skills.description: Use when single-cell data from a diseased tissue (e.g., AML bone marrow) must be screened for aberrant/disease-critical cell populations defined in NCIT, and per-cell disease scores must be compared across conditions such as healthy vs AML or pre- vs post-treatment relapse.
skills.name: disease-marker-based-aberrant-cell-scoring
skills.search_text: disease-marker-based-aberrant-cell-scoring Use when single-cell data from a diseased tissue (e.g., AML bone marrow) must be screened for aberrant/disease-critical cell populations defined in NCIT, and per-cell disease scores must be compared across conditions such as healthy vs AML or pre- vs post-treatment relapse. The goal is annotation of normal/physiological cell types across tissues — use the standard accordion() function with the healthy Accordion database instead of disease scoring The disease cell type of interest is not represented in the NCIT-backed disease Accordion database (728 cell types / 212 human tissues coverage), so no weighted marker set exists Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table with no per-cell resolution, since the method computes per-cell scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Score per-cell enrichment of disease-critical cell types (e.g., Leukemic Hematopoietic Stem Cell, Neoplastic Monocyte) in scRNA-seq data using the accordion_disease() function of the Cell Marker Accordion R package, which exploits the disease Accordion marker database built from consistency-weighted positive and negative markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Score per-cell enrichment of disease-critical cell types (e.g., Leukemic Hematopoietic Stem Cell, Neoplastic Monocyte) in scRNA-seq data using the accordion_disease() function of the Cell Marker Accordion R package, which exploits the disease Accordion marker database built from consistency-weighted positive and negative markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation of normal/physiological cell types across tissues — use the standard accordion() function with the healthy Accordion database instead of disease scoring The disease cell type of interest is not represented in the NCIT-backed disease Accordion database (728 cell types / 212 human tissues coverage), so no weighted marker set exists Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table with no per-cell resolution, since the method computes per-cell scores

skills.description: Use when annotating cell types in a disease scRNA-seq query (e.g., type 2 diabetes, NSCLC, Alzheimer's) against a normal-cell reference where batch/treatment effects make standard label transfer unreliable.
skills.name: disease-scrnaseq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: disease-scrnaseq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating cell types in a disease scRNA-seq query (e.g., type 2 diabetes, NSCLC, Alzheimer's) against a normal-cell reference where batch/treatment effects make standard label transfer unreliable. The query dataset is normal tissue rather than disease — use SELINA's normal mode with the 35-tissue normal models and the fine-tuning step instead No pre-trained disease model exists for the disease condition of interest — the README notes disease datasets are extremely diverse across patients/groups and recommends users train on their own data via 'selina train' The task is de novo clustering or marker-based annotation without a reference atlas — marker-based tools like Garnett or SCINA follow a different paradigm than reference-based label transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate cell types in disease scRNA-seq query datasets (T2D, NSCLC, Alzheimer's) using SELINA's pre-trained disease models in disease mode, which skips fine-tuning because disease expression profiles deviate from normal references, and benchmark against scmap, SingleR, CHETAH, and SingleCellNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Annotate cell types in disease scRNA-seq query datasets (T2D, NSCLC, Alzheimer's) using SELINA's pre-trained disease models in disease mode, which skips fine-tuning because disease expression profiles deviate from normal references, and benchmark against scmap, SingleR, CHETAH, and SingleCellNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset is normal tissue rather than disease — use SELINA's normal mode with the 35-tissue normal models and the fine-tuning step instead No pre-trained disease model exists for the disease condition of interest — the README notes disease datasets are extremely diverse across patients/groups and recommends users train on their own data via 'selina train' The task is de novo clustering or marker-based annotation without a reference atlas — marker-based tools like Garnett or SCINA follow a different paradigm than reference-based label transfer

skills.description: Use when a transcript isoform switching event (e.g. an ENST identifier such as HSPH1-002 / ENST00000380405 in Alzheimer's disease) must be queried in CanIsoNet and its disrupted STRING interactions quantified.
skills.name: disease-specific-dmdt-retrieval
skills.search_text: disease-specific-dmdt-retrieval Use when a transcript isoform switching event (e.g. an ENST identifier such as HSPH1-002 / ENST00000380405 in Alzheimer's disease) must be queried in CanIsoNet and its disrupted STRING interactions quantified. The gene or transcript is outside the 31 disease types covered by CanIsoNet (27 PCAWG cancer types plus OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and Behçet's) — no dMDT annotation exists there The goal is general protein-protein interaction analysis without an isoform switching event — use plain STRING rather than the dMDT/isoform-switching layer You need isoform switching events in diseases not annotated by ClinVar or the loaded RNA-Seq datasets — CanIsoNet covers its indexed disease types only http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Retrieves and annotates disease-type specific dMDTs (disease-specific major disrupted transcripts) and their isoform switching events from CanIsoNet, then characterizes the functional impact of a given dMDT by filtering its STRING interaction network and identifying domain-mediated interactions lost by the switch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Retrieves and annotates disease-type specific dMDTs (disease-specific major disrupted transcripts) and their isoform switching events from CanIsoNet, then characterizes the functional impact of a given dMDT by filtering its STRING interaction network and identifying domain-mediated interactions lost by the switch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene or transcript is outside the 31 disease types covered by CanIsoNet (27 PCAWG cancer types plus OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and Behçet's) — no dMDT annotation exists there The goal is general protein-protein interaction analysis without an isoform switching event — use plain STRING rather than the dMDT/isoform-switching layer You need isoform switching events in diseases not annotated by ClinVar or the loaded RNA-Seq datasets — CanIsoNet covers its indexed disease types only

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq transcriptome data for a disease has yielded isoform switching events / dMDT genes with lost protein domains, and you need to map those domain losses onto a protein interaction network to expose functional disruptions.
skills.name: disease-specific-network-overlay
skills.search_text: disease-specific-network-overlay Use when RNA-seq transcriptome data for a disease has yielded isoform switching events / dMDT genes with lost protein domains, and you need to map those domain losses onto a protein interaction network to expose functional disruptions. The analysis goal is general protein-protein interaction lookup without isoform switching or domain-loss context — a plain STRING query suffices Input transcript data lack isoform-level resolution (e.g., gene-level counts only), since dMDT identification requires isoform switching events per sample Studying non-human/non-mouse species, since the DDI-to-gene mapping described covers human and mouse genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs disease-specific isoform interaction networks by intersecting RNA-seq-derived dMDT gene lists (isoforms losing Pfam domains) with 3did Pfam domain-domain interactions and overlaying the disrupted edges onto STRING protein-protein interaction networks, per disease type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Constructs disease-specific isoform interaction networks by intersecting RNA-seq-derived dMDT gene lists (isoforms losing Pfam domains) with 3did Pfam domain-domain interactions and overlaying the disrupted edges onto STRING protein-protein interaction networks, per disease type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is general protein-protein interaction lookup without isoform switching or domain-loss context — a plain STRING query suffices Input transcript data lack isoform-level resolution (e.g., gene-level counts only), since dMDT identification requires isoform switching events per sample Studying non-human/non-mouse species, since the DDI-to-gene mapping described covers human and mouse genomes

skills.description: Use when a inferred GRN (e.g., from SCING, GRNBOOST2, ppcor, or PIDC) needs biological validation by testing how well it models disease gene subnetworks from DisGeNET versus degree-preserved random network nulls.
skills.name: disease-subnetwork-random-walk-modeling
skills.search_text: disease-subnetwork-random-walk-modeling Use when a inferred GRN (e.g., from SCING, GRNBOOST2, ppcor, or PIDC) needs biological validation by testing how well it models disease gene subnetworks from DisGeNET versus degree-preserved random network nulls. Validation target is perturbation target prediction or network overfitting (use Perturb-seq AUROC/TPR-at-FPR-0.05 or cosine-similarity held-out gene prediction instead) No curated disease gene sets (e.g., DisGeNET categories) are available for the phenotype of interest The network's null comparison requires preserving structure beyond node degree attributes http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Biological validation of inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) using the Huang et al. random walk framework to model DisGeNET disease subnetworks, quantifying the performance gain of a real GRN over degree-preserved random GRNs with similar node attributes. Used in SCING to show SCING outperforms GRNBOOST2, ppcor, and PIDC on Immune, Metabolic, and Neuronal disease gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Biological validation of inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) using the Huang et al. random walk framework to model DisGeNET disease subnetworks, quantifying the performance gain of a real GRN over degree-preserved random GRNs with similar node attributes. Used in SCING to show SCING outperforms GRNBOOST2, ppcor, and PIDC on Immune, Metabolic, and Neuronal disease gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Validation target is perturbation target prediction or network overfitting (use Perturb-seq AUROC/TPR-at-FPR-0.05 or cosine-similarity held-out gene prediction instead) No curated disease gene sets (e.g., DisGeNET categories) are available for the phenotype of interest The network's null comparison requires preserving structure beyond node degree attributes

skills.description: Use when an imputed or latent scRNA-seq expression matrix from a disease dataset (e.g. the adam h5 file) must be checked for AD-versus-control cell separation and clustering quality (ARI/NMI).
skills.name: disease-vs-control-separation-analysis
skills.search_text: disease-vs-control-separation-analysis Use when an imputed or latent scRNA-seq expression matrix from a disease dataset (e.g. the adam h5 file) must be checked for AD-versus-control cell separation and clustering quality (ARI/NMI). The goal is gene-level imputation accuracy (e.g. dropout recovery on simulated data) rather than disease-vs-control cell separation or clustering. The dataset has no true cell labels available to serve as a reference partition for ARI/NMI computation. The input is raw data only and you are not comparing imputed against raw separation — the paper's claim concerns scGCL imputed data separating AD and control cells more efficiently than raw scRNA-seq data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify how well a scRNA-seq representation (raw or imputed) separates disease cells from control cells, visualized as in Supplementary Fig. S3a of the scGCL paper, alongside clustering metrics ARI and NMI on the Alzheimer's disease (adam) dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Quantify how well a scRNA-seq representation (raw or imputed) separates disease cells from control cells, visualized as in Supplementary Fig. S3a of the scGCL paper, alongside clustering metrics ARI and NMI on the Alzheimer's disease (adam) dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-level imputation accuracy (e.g. dropout recovery on simulated data) rather than disease-vs-control cell separation or clustering. The dataset has no true cell labels available to serve as a reference partition for ARI/NMI computation. The input is raw data only and you are not comparing imputed against raw separation — the paper's claim concerns scGCL imputed data separating AD and control cells more efficiently than raw scRNA-seq data.

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 6-patient GBM, DMSO vs panobinostat) must be decomposed into shared vs condition-specific latent factors for batch-effect removal or cell-type/batch-mixing evaluation.
skills.name: disentangled-latent-factor-extraction
skills.search_text: disentangled-latent-factor-extraction Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 6-patient GBM, DMSO vs panobinostat) must be decomposed into shared vs condition-specific latent factors for batch-effect removal or cell-type/batch-mixing evaluation. Each batch is measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effect The goal is a single-task analysis only (e.g., pure batch integration without conditions), where a dedicated batch-removal method suffices Data lacks multiple biological conditions, so unshared-bio factors are undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts disentangled shared-bio factors (condition- and batch-irrelevant) and unshared-bio factors (condition-related) from multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data using scDisInFact's conditional variational autoencoder, and benchmarks them against scINSIGHT's common/condition-specific modules with ASW-batch and ARI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Extracts disentangled shared-bio factors (condition- and batch-irrelevant) and unshared-bio factors (condition-related) from multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data using scDisInFact's conditional variational autoencoder, and benchmarks them against scINSIGHT's common/condition-specific modules with ASW-batch and ARI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effect The goal is a single-task analysis only (e.g., pure batch integration without conditions), where a dedicated batch-removal method suffices Data lacks multiple biological conditions, so unshared-bio factors are undefined

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq model separates cell types while removing batch effect in shared factors, and removes batch effect from condition-specific (unshared-bio) factors.
skills.name: disentanglement-test-holdout-configuration
skills.search_text: disentanglement-test-holdout-configuration Use when benchmarking whether a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq model separates cell types while removing batch effect in shared factors, and removes batch effect from condition-specific (unshared-bio) factors. Each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects in that setting The task is perturbation prediction of held-out matrices (use predict_counts) rather than scoring factor disentanglement quality Input is real data with correlated condition types where the assumption of mutually independent condition types does not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmark configuration for evaluating disentanglement of shared-bio vs unshared-bio latent factors: hold out the <ctrl,severe> batch-1 and <stim,healthy> batch-2 matrices, train scDisInFact and the scINSIGHT NMF baseline, and score cell-type separation (ARI) and batch removal (ASW-batch) as in Fig. 2d. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: A benchmark configuration for evaluating disentanglement of shared-bio vs unshared-bio latent factors: hold out the <ctrl,severe> batch-1 and <stim,healthy> batch-2 matrices, train scDisInFact and the scINSIGHT NMF baseline, and score cell-type separation (ARI) and batch removal (ASW-batch) as in Fig. 2d.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper states there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects in that setting The task is perturbation prediction of held-out matrices (use predict_counts) rather than scoring factor disentanglement quality Input is real data with correlated condition types where the assumption of mutually independent condition types does not hold

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an inferred single-cell GRN captures disease biology: you have one or more inferred networks and want a quantitative, per-disease-category score of how well the network models disease gene subnetworks versus matched random nulls.
skills.name: disgenet-disease-gene-set-mapping
skills.search_text: disgenet-disease-gene-set-mapping Use when evaluating whether an inferred single-cell GRN captures disease biology: you have one or more inferred networks and want a quantitative, per-disease-category score of how well the network models disease gene subnetworks versus matched random nulls. You lack DisGeNET disease gene sets or a mapping between network genes and disease genes — the gain score cannot be computed The network was built on a pre-selected subset of genes or cells rather than a full transcriptome context, so degree-preserved nulls would not be comparable in spirit Your goal is direct perturbation-target validation from Perturb-seq data rather than disease subnetwork modeling — SCING evaluates those as separate benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Biological validation of inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) by modeling disease subnetworks from DisGeNET disease gene sets (Immune, Metabolic, Neuronal categories) with the Huang et al. random walk framework, scoring each GRN by its performance gain over degree-preserved random GRNs with similar node attributes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Biological validation of inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) by modeling disease subnetworks from DisGeNET disease gene sets (Immune, Metabolic, Neuronal categories) with the Huang et al. random walk framework, scoring each GRN by its performance gain over degree-preserved random GRNs with similar node attributes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack DisGeNET disease gene sets or a mapping between network genes and disease genes — the gain score cannot be computed The network was built on a pre-selected subset of genes or cells rather than a full transcriptome context, so degree-preserved nulls would not be comparable in spirit Your goal is direct perturbation-target validation from Perturb-seq data rather than disease subnetwork modeling — SCING evaluates those as separate benchmarks

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank/select genes whose expression correlates with the developmental trajectory, such as markers of transitions between cell states.
skills.name: distance-correlation-statistics
skills.search_text: distance-correlation-statistics Use when you have a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank/select genes whose expression correlates with the developmental trajectory, such as markers of transitions between cell states. When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this approach 'may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly', so validate redpath() output first When the input is already a filtered/subsetted gene matrix — dCor/MIC should be computed on the FULL expression matrix, not the GO-subsetted, dispersion-filtered matrix used for pseudotime inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies redPATH's gene-discovery statistics — distance correlation (dCor) and the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) — between each gene's expression profile and the redPATH-inferred pseudotime to identify genes that change significantly along cell development, e.g. CSF1R in MGH45/MGH107 glioma data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Applies redPATH's gene-discovery statistics — distance correlation (dCor) and the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) — between each gene's expression profile and the redPATH-inferred pseudotime to identify genes that change significantly along cell development, e.g. CSF1R in MGH45/MGH107 glioma data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this approach 'may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly', so validate redpath() output first When the input is already a filtered/subsetted gene matrix — dCor/MIC should be computed on the FULL expression matrix, not the GO-subsetted, dispersion-filtered matrix used for pseudotime inference

skills.description: Use when a multipotent progenitor population (e.g. MPPs, TACs) plus competing downstream lineages are available in log-normalized scRNA-Seq data, and the goal is to quantify priming or locate a bifurcation point by entropy of expression covariation.
skills.name: distance-covariance-entropy-computation
skills.search_text: distance-covariance-entropy-computation Use when a multipotent progenitor population (e.g. MPPs, TACs) plus competing downstream lineages are available in log-normalized scRNA-Seq data, and the goal is to quantify priming or locate a bifurcation point by entropy of expression covariation. When the goal is clustering or cell-type annotation rather than quantifying priming/bifurcation — chromVAR-style motif variability or standard trajectory tools are more appropriate When only a single lineage or no multipotent progenitor population is present, since DICE requires covariation among competing lineage RF sets over a multipotent population When a rigorous variance-based or DNB-based tipping-point analysis is specifically required — the article notes DICE outperformed BioTIP here, but BioTIP may be the mandated comparator http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute the Distance Covariance Entropy (DICE) — the multivariate Gaussian entropy of the double-centered distance-covariance (dCov) matrix of regulatory-factor expression covariation — to quantify priming in multipotent cell populations and pinpoint bifurcation timing from scRNA-Seq data using the DICE R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Compute the Distance Covariance Entropy (DICE) — the multivariate Gaussian entropy of the double-centered distance-covariance (dCov) matrix of regulatory-factor expression covariation — to quantify priming in multipotent cell populations and pinpoint bifurcation timing from scRNA-Seq data using the DICE R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is clustering or cell-type annotation rather than quantifying priming/bifurcation — chromVAR-style motif variability or standard trajectory tools are more appropriate When only a single lineage or no multipotent progenitor population is present, since DICE requires covariation among competing lineage RF sets over a multipotent population When a rigorous variance-based or DNB-based tipping-point analysis is specifically required — the article notes DICE outperformed BioTIP here, but BioTIP may be the mandated comparator

skills.description: Use when region-level TF affinities (TRAP, 818 PFMs from JASPAR 2022 / HOCOMOCO v11 / Kheradpour & Kellis) must be summarised to gene level using a TSS-centred window (default 50 KB gene-window, 5 MB ABC-mode) with activity × exponential distance decay weighting.
skills.name: distance-decay-weighting-of-regulatory-regions
skills.search_text: distance-decay-weighting-of-regulatory-regions Use when region-level TF affinities (TRAP, 818 PFMs from JASPAR 2022 / HOCOMOCO v11 / Kheradpour & Kellis) must be summarised to gene level using a TSS-centred window (default 50 KB gene-window, 5 MB ABC-mode) with activity × exponential distance decay weighting. Promoter-mode runs with no bed-file/activity columns — the scaler is fixed at 1, so no distance decay or activity weighting applies Only the ABC-scored enhancer–gene interactions are of interest — STARE's ABC-scoring part can be called independently and affinity summarisation is unnecessary Regions are already assigned to genes by an external method that does not use the TSS-window or adapted-ABC mapping — the scaler choice (window decay vs adapted activity × contact) would be mismatched http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 STARE's method for scaling per-region TRAP TF affinities by chromatin activity and an exponential distance-to-TSS decay (or by ABC contact-based scaling) before summing them into a per-gene, per-TF affinity matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: STARE's method for scaling per-region TRAP TF affinities by chromatin activity and an exponential distance-to-TSS decay (or by ABC contact-based scaling) before summing them into a per-gene, per-TF affinity matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Promoter-mode runs with no bed-file/activity columns — the scaler is fixed at 1, so no distance decay or activity weighting applies Only the ABC-scored enhancer–gene interactions are of interest — STARE's ABC-scoring part can be called independently and affinity summarisation is unnecessary Regions are already assigned to genes by an external method that does not use the TSS-window or adapted-ABC mapping — the scaler choice (window decay vs adapted activity × contact) would be mismatched

skills.description: Use when fine-mapped noncoding GWAS variants (with posterior probabilities) overlap scATAC-seq peaks and you must assign distal regulatory target genes beyond the nearest gene, accounting for distance-dependent effects.
skills.name: distance-dependent-variant-gene-linking
skills.search_text: distance-dependent-variant-gene-linking Use when fine-mapped noncoding GWAS variants (with posterior probabilities) overlap scATAC-seq peaks and you must assign distal regulatory target genes beyond the nearest gene, accounting for distance-dependent effects. No pseudotemporal/dynamic multiomic context available — GrID-Net requires multiomic single-cell data from a matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation) to orient the cell DAG Only nearest-gene assignment is needed and distal interactions are out of scope, or variants do not overlap any accessible ATAC peaks in the reference dataset Input is already a curated gene list with no variant-level or peak-level resolution to score http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Links fine-mapped GWAS variants to the genes they putatively regulate by combining GrID-Net Granger causal peak-gene scores with a genomic-distance-aware logistic regression, replacing naive nearest-gene assignment. Applied in Wu et al. 2025 to Trubetskoy et al. fine-mapped SCZ variants to yield 132 candidate SCZ genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Links fine-mapped GWAS variants to the genes they putatively regulate by combining GrID-Net Granger causal peak-gene scores with a genomic-distance-aware logistic regression, replacing naive nearest-gene assignment. Applied in Wu et al. 2025 to Trubetskoy et al. fine-mapped SCZ variants to yield 132 candidate SCZ genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No pseudotemporal/dynamic multiomic context available — GrID-Net requires multiomic single-cell data from a matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation) to orient the cell DAG Only nearest-gene assignment is needed and distal interactions are out of scope, or variants do not overlap any accessible ATAC peaks in the reference dataset Input is already a curated gene list with no variant-level or peak-level resolution to score

skills.description: Use when validating per-read barcode calls from SPLiT-seq reads after sliding-window index location: each of the three 8-nt indicator barcodes must satisfy Dist < 2 against its whitelist entry, otherwise the Read2 must be abandoned.
skills.name: distance-function-indicator-sequence-validation
skills.search_text: distance-function-indicator-sequence-validation Use when validating per-read barcode calls from SPLiT-seq reads after sliding-window index location: each of the three 8-nt indicator barcodes must satisfy Dist < 2 against its whitelist entry, otherwise the Read2 must be abandoned. The barcode platform is not SPLiT-seq-style combinatorial 8-nt barcodes — the article states the fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data, and broader application is potential, not demonstrated Reads still need index-region location — this validation step presumes the sliding-window scan has already identified the index positions and extracted the indicator sequences Higher tolerance (>1 mismatch or >1 indel) is required — SCSit's default uses one mismatch and one indel, which increases identified reads only 4–5% while costing 20–40% more runtime http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates the three 8-nt indicator barcodes extracted from each SPLiT-seq Read2 by encoding them via quad-to-decimal conversion (0,1,2,3 = A,T,G,C) and computing the integer distance function Dist(x,y), accepting Read2 only when Dist < 2 for every round. This is the final correctness gate in SCSit's indel-tolerant barcode identification pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Validates the three 8-nt indicator barcodes extracted from each SPLiT-seq Read2 by encoding them via quad-to-decimal conversion (0,1,2,3 = A,T,G,C) and computing the integer distance function Dist(x,y), accepting Read2 only when Dist < 2 for every round. This is the final correctness gate in SCSit's indel-tolerant barcode identification pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The barcode platform is not SPLiT-seq-style combinatorial 8-nt barcodes — the article states the fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data, and broader application is potential, not demonstrated Reads still need index-region location — this validation step presumes the sliding-window scan has already identified the index positions and extracted the indicator sequences Higher tolerance (>1 mismatch or >1 indel) is required — SCSit's default uses one mismatch and one indel, which increases identified reads only 4–5% while costing 20–40% more runtime

skills.search_text: dmap-lineage-label-transfer Use when you need per-cell lineage or cell-type labels from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data without marker genes or supervised training, and a hematopoietic reference profile set (e.g. DMAP) is available for correlation-based matching. skills.search_text: dna-storage-encode-decode-pipeline-implementation Use when implementing or verifying a DNA-based storage system pipeline in simulation: you have a digital file to encode into DNA strands, noisy simulated sequencing reads to decode, and need a fault-injection test bed with round-trip validation. You only need to simulate the synthesis-to-basecalling channel (e.g. nanopore read generation) without an encode/decode pipeline — use the DNArSim channel simulator directly instead. You need a production/archival DNA storage encoder, not a simulation and verification infrastructure; FrameD is a fault-injection test bed for evaluating designs. The input is already decoded strand consensus and the task is downstream statistical analysis only — use the db_gen.py dataframe compilation and notebooks rather than rebuilding the pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Assemble a complete DNA data storage encode/decode pipeline using FrameD's core encoding, decoding, and file-manipulation modules, structuring the encode path as file -> packets -> base-sequences -> DNA strands and the decode path with optional strand clustering + multiple sequence alignment (MSA) or post-inner-code consolidation to resolve errors across the many copies of each strand produced by synthesis and sequencing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Assemble a complete DNA data storage encode/decode pipeline using FrameD's core encoding, decoding, and file-manipulation modules, structuring the encode path as file -> packets -> base-sequences -> DNA strands and the decode path with optional strand clustering + multiple sequence alignment (MSA) or post-inner-code consolidation to resolve errors across the many copies of each strand produced by synthesis and sequencing.

skills.search_text: dna-storage-fault-injection-simulation Use when you need to evaluate a DNA-based data storage pipeline design (encoder/decoder choice) under controlled error injection — e.g. varying fault rates, error distributions, or pipeline stages like multiple sequence alignment — and collect decode-failure and error-location statistics. You only need a single serial encode/decode of a small file with no error injection or parameter sweep — the fault-injection harness and MPI/job-generation machinery add unnecessary overhead You plan to run the full paper-scale sweep (e.g. the 6 .json paper configurations, 240 simulations) on commodity hardware — the README states these are only tractable on HPC systems and, as shipped, require an LSF scheduler You are simulating a nanopore channel yourself from raw sequencer data rather than evaluating a DNA storage pipeline design under injected errors Run FrameD's fault-injection-based test bed to evaluate DNA storage pipeline designs: encode data into oligos, inject sampled errors (i.i.d. or DNArSim nanopore channel model), reconstruct and decode, and aggregate error statistics across parameter sweeps. FrameD's transparent MPI parallelism makes large sweeps (hundreds of fault-injection iterations, many sequencing reads) tractable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Run FrameD's fault-injection-based test bed to evaluate DNA storage pipeline designs: encode data into oligos, inject sampled errors (i.i.d. or DNArSim nanopore channel model), reconstruct and decode, and aggregate error statistics across parameter sweeps. skills.name: domain-generalization-risk-extrapolation-training
skills.search_text: domain-generalization-risk-extrapolation-training Use when training a malignant-cell classifier on multi-tissue scRNA-seq data where the model must generalize to unseen tissue domains — i.e., when optimizing the combined variance-plus-average risk objective over tissue domains is needed. Hematologic tumor data — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumors. Spatial transcriptomics spot annotation with a model trained on single-cell data — ST spot calling requires retraining on spatial transcriptomic training datasets, and the model overlooks spatial relationships among spots. Tasks requiring clonal structure or CNV inference (e.g., CopyKAT-style subclonal copy-number profiles) — this skill only performs binary malignant/non-malignant classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains Cancer-Finder's multi-layer perceptron to generalize across tissues by optimizing the risk-extrapolation objective L(θ) = β·R_var(θ) + R_avg(θ), which penalizes variance of per-domain (per-tissue) cross-entropy risks alongside their average. This is the mechanism that lets a classifier trained on 74 TISCH tumor microenvironment datasets achieve 95.16% average accuracy on held-out malignant/non-malignant cell calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6

This is the mechanism that lets a classifier trained on 74 TISCH tumor microenvironment datasets achieve 95.16% average accuracy on held-out malignant/non-malignant cell calls.

skills.description: Use when FunHoP node-level pathway analysis has been run on RNA-seq data from two independent patient cohorts (e.g. TCGA and Prensner prostate cancer) and you need to verify that dominant genes and very-high/very-low abundance-ratio genes in multi-gene KEGG nodes reproduce across cohorts.
skills.name: dominant-gene-ratio-comparison
skills.search_text: dominant-gene-ratio-comparison Use when FunHoP node-level pathway analysis has been run on RNA-seq data from two independent patient cohorts (e.g. TCGA and Prensner prostate cancer) and you need to verify that dominant genes and very-high/very-low abundance-ratio genes in multi-gene KEGG nodes reproduce across cohorts.
