skills.name: drug-signature-reversal-repurposing
skills.search_text: drug-signature-reversal-repurposing Use when you have case-vs-control scRNA-seq clusters with differential expression profiles and want FDA-approved drug candidates that reverse disease signatures across multiple cell populations, e.g. TNBC, leukemia, or COVID-19 BALF data. You only have bulk RNA-seq or a single homogenous cell population — ASGARD's multi-cluster drug score adds value specifically for heterogeneous multi-cluster scRNA-seq data, and bulk-based methods like CLUE/DrInsight suffice otherwise No reference drug profile exists for the target tissue — the LINCS L1000 reference covers only 98 cell lines and a matching tissue reference may be unavailable No proper normal/control samples are obtainable for the disease, since case-vs-control DE per cluster is a required input http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Ranks repurposing candidates by reversing disease differential-expression signatures against LINCS L1000 perturbational profiles using ASGARD's GetDrug/DrugScore, aggregating per-cell-cluster drug rankings into a multi-cluster drug score that addresses intrapatient cellular heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36637-3
skills.summary: Ranks repurposing candidates by reversing disease differential-expression signatures against LINCS L1000 perturbational profiles using ASGARD's GetDrug/DrugScore, aggregating per-cell-cluster drug rankings into a multi-cluster drug score that addresses intrapatient cellular heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have bulk RNA-seq or a single homogenous cell population — ASGARD's multi-cluster drug score adds value specifically for heterogeneous multi-cluster scRNA-seq data, and bulk-based methods like CLUE/DrInsight suffice otherwise No reference drug profile exists for the target tissue — the LINCS L1000 reference covers only 98 cell lines and a matching tissue reference may be unavailable No proper normal/control samples are obtainable for the disease, since case-vs-control DE per cluster is a required input

skills.description: Use when you have a candidate gene list from a network or biomarker pipeline and need to flag which genes are targets of pharmacologically active drugs (DrugBank) and which lack prior literature links to a disease.
skills.name: drug-target-actionability-annotation
skills.search_text: drug-target-actionability-annotation Use when you have a candidate gene list from a network or biomarker pipeline and need to flag which genes are targets of pharmacologically active drugs (DrugBank) and which lack prior literature links to a disease. The goal is functional or pathway enrichment of gene communities (use g:Profiler GO:BP/KEGG analysis instead), not drug target annotation. No DrugBank pharmacologically-active target file is available and downloading/curating external knowledge bases is out of scope. The input is differential-expression gene counts rather than extracted IC gene symbol lists — drug actionability annotation is only meaningful on curated gene symbol sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Annotates extracted IC gene lists (e.g., from fused KIRC, LIHC, PRAD co-expression networks) as drug actionable by cross-referencing gene symbols against DrugBank pharmacologically-active targets, and combines this with PubMed literature association to flag novel candidate biomarkers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Annotates extracted IC gene lists (e.g., from fused KIRC, LIHC, PRAD co-expression networks) as drug actionable by cross-referencing gene symbols against DrugBank pharmacologically-active targets, and combines this with PubMed literature association to flag novel candidate biomarkers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional or pathway enrichment of gene communities (use g:Profiler GO:BP/KEGG analysis instead), not drug target annotation. No DrugBank pharmacologically-active target file is available and downloading/curating external knowledge bases is out of scope. The input is differential-expression gene counts rather than extracted IC gene symbol lists — drug actionability annotation is only meaningful on curated gene symbol sets.

skills.description: Use when applying scRank to a drug perturbation analysis and only a drug name (not a target gene) is available, or when deciding between antagonist (inhibitor) and agonist MOA settings for CreateScRank.
skills.name: drug-target-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: drug-target-annotation-mapping Use when applying scRank to a drug perturbation analysis and only a drug name (not a target gene) is available, or when deciding between antagonist (inhibitor) and agonist MOA settings for CreateScRank. The drug acts as an agonist and reliable single-cell agonist data are required — scRank's agonist modeling (maximal out-edge weights on the target node) is a simplifying assumption and only preliminary The drug has multiple targets requiring target-to-target interaction modeling — specifically tailored methodologies for multi-target perturbation are not yet developed beyond preliminary results (Figure S17) The analysis needs a standalone drug-target annotation tool — this skill only covers mapping within the scRank tpGRN workflow, not general pharmacological annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Resolves drug names to their canonical targets and mechanism of action (MOA) within the scRank workflow, using the package's `utile_database` so that a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) can be constructed for the correct target gene with the appropriate antagonist (or agonist) perturbation mode. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Resolves drug names to their canonical targets and mechanism of action (MOA) within the scRank workflow, using the package's `utile_database` so that a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) can be constructed for the correct target gene with the appropriate antagonist (or agonist) perturbation mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts as an agonist and reliable single-cell agonist data are required — scRank's agonist modeling (maximal out-edge weights on the target node) is a simplifying assumption and only preliminary The drug has multiple targets requiring target-to-target interaction modeling — specifically tailored methodologies for multi-target perturbation are not yet developed beyond preliminary results (Figure S17) The analysis needs a standalone drug-target annotation tool — this skill only covers mapping within the scRank tpGRN workflow, not general pharmacological annotation

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive vs drug-resistant myeloma samples (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) must be screened to rank combination candidates by subclonal enrichment of specific drug-target genes.
skills.name: drug-target-gene-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: drug-target-gene-enrichment-analysis Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive vs drug-resistant myeloma samples (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) must be screened to rank combination candidates by subclonal enrichment of specific drug-target genes. Input is bulk RNA-seq or bulk pharmacogenomics data — this skill requires single-cell resolution to score per-subclone target-gene enrichment The candidate drug's target gene(s) are not known or not derivable from LINCS, so nothing can be mapped onto clusters The goal is in silico secDrug prediction itself (greedy set cover algorithm on the >70 HMCL pharmacogenomics panel), not single-cell screening of already-predicted combinations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that maps LINCS-derived drug-target genes (e.g., 17-AAG targets HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 and FK866 target NAMPT) onto t-SNE-defined subclonal clusters of myeloma samples to prioritize secDrug combinations by per-cluster target-gene enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41408-022-00636-2
skills.summary: A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that maps LINCS-derived drug-target genes (e.g., 17-AAG targets HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 and FK866 target NAMPT) onto t-SNE-defined subclonal clusters of myeloma samples to prioritize secDrug combinations by per-cluster target-gene enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or bulk pharmacogenomics data — this skill requires single-cell resolution to score per-subclone target-gene enrichment The candidate drug's target gene(s) are not known or not derivable from LINCS, so nothing can be mapped onto clusters The goal is in silico secDrug prediction itself (greedy set cover algorithm on the >70 HMCL pharmacogenomics panel), not single-cell screening of already-predicted combinations

skills.description: Use when scRank has ranked cell types for a drug target (e.g., Smo for vismodegib, SLC6A4 for fluoxetine) and you need to see which perturbed gene modules — especially the target-containing module — differ between top- and bottom-ranked cell types.
skills.name: drug-target-gene-module-visualization
skills.search_text: drug-target-gene-module-visualization Use when scRank has ranked cell types for a drug target (e.g., Smo for vismodegib, SLC6A4 for fluoxetine) and you need to see which perturbed gene modules — especially the target-containing module — differ between top- and bottom-ranked cell types. Only the cell-type ranking is needed — obj@cell_type_rank from rank_celltype() already answers which cell type responds; module inspection adds mechanistic detail, not the ranking itself The drug is an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank's agonist handling is a simplifying assumption (out-edge weights set to maximum) and multi-target perturbation has only preliminary results (Figure S17) No tpGRN exists yet — init_mod requires the gene regulatory network reconstructed by Constr_net() from the expression profiles for the target gene http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Renders scRank's drug-target-gene module views: init_mod modularizes the target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) and plot_net(mode='heatmap') displays perturbed gene module activity per cell type, exposing the transcriptional modules (e.g., Smo-Cnbp in Node_B; module-2 containing SLC6A4 in Ex_9) that underlie in silico drug responsiveness. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Renders scRank's drug-target-gene module views: init_mod modularizes the target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) and plot_net(mode='heatmap') displays perturbed gene module activity per cell type, exposing the transcriptional modules (e.g., Smo-Cnbp in Node_B; module-2 containing SLC6A4 in Ex_9) that underlie in silico drug responsiveness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the cell-type ranking is needed — obj@cell_type_rank from rank_celltype() already answers which cell type responds; module inspection adds mechanistic detail, not the ranking itself The drug is an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank's agonist handling is a simplifying assumption (out-edge weights set to maximum) and multi-target perturbation has only preliminary results (Figure S17) No tpGRN exists yet — init_mod requires the gene regulatory network reconstructed by Constr_net() from the expression profiles for the target gene

skills.description: Use when a drug's direct target is known (or a drug-responsive cell type has been ranked) and you must prioritize additional candidate target genes from the cell-type-specific GRN and confirm them against treated-vs-untreated expression data.
skills.name: drug-target-gene-ranking-and-downregulation-validation
skills.search_text: drug-target-gene-ranking-and-downregulation-validation Use when a drug's direct target is known (or a drug-responsive cell type has been ranked) and you must prioritize additional candidate target genes from the cell-type-specific GRN and confirm them against treated-vs-untreated expression data. The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple/unknown targets requiring tailored multi-target methodology (scRank's agonist handling and multi-target extension are preliminary only). You only have disease-treatment paired data and want simple DEG/separability-based response analysis rather than GRN-based in silico perturbation of untreated samples. Genes already rank highly by simple correlation analysis is sufficient — the paper notes these top targets were not identifiable through simple correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks candidate drug-target genes by scRank perturbation scores within a top-ranked cell-type-specific GRN (e.g., tanshinone IIA targets in the M0-5 macrophage GRN beyond the known direct target Ctsk), then validates targets by significant post-treatment downregulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Ranks candidate drug-target genes by scRank perturbation scores within a top-ranked cell-type-specific GRN (e.g., tanshinone IIA targets in the M0-5 macrophage GRN beyond the known direct target Ctsk), then validates targets by significant post-treatment downregulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple/unknown targets requiring tailored multi-target methodology (scRank's agonist handling and multi-target extension are preliminary only). You only have disease-treatment paired data and want simple DEG/separability-based response analysis rather than GRN-based in silico perturbation of untreated samples. Genes already rank highly by simple correlation analysis is sufficient — the paper notes these top targets were not identifiable through simple correlation.

skills.description: Use when a gene co-expression or regulatory network module has driver/hub genes and you need to retrieve known or experimental drugs targeting them for mechanistic drug repurposing.
skills.name: drug-target-interaction-database-mapping
skills.search_text: drug-target-interaction-database-mapping Use when a gene co-expression or regulatory network module has driver/hub genes and you need to retrieve known or experimental drugs targeting them for mechanistic drug repurposing. The module lacks identified hub/driver genes or the network proteins cannot be mapped to UniProt/Entrez/Ensembl identifiers via Drugst.One. The goal is de novo drug discovery or QSAR modeling rather than lookup of known drug–target interactions in DrugBank/DrugCentral-derived databases. Strict bitwise reproducibility of the drug list is required and no pinned Drugst.One/NeDRex database version can be used, since the databases update weekly. http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 Maps hub-gene proteins from a SCANet-derived co-expression module (e.g. the M4 ISC module of HFHSD obese mice) to drug–target interaction databases via Drugst.One/NeDRex to yield repurposing candidates such as lovastatin, fenofibrate, methyldopa, and warfarin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Maps hub-gene proteins from a SCANet-derived co-expression module (e.g. the M4 ISC module of HFHSD obese mice) to drug–target interaction databases via Drugst.One/NeDRex to yield repurposing candidates such as lovastatin, fenofibrate, methyldopa, and warfarin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The module lacks identified hub/driver genes or the network proteins cannot be mapped to UniProt/Entrez/Ensembl identifiers via Drugst.One. The goal is de novo drug discovery or QSAR modeling rather than lookup of known drug–target interactions in DrugBank/DrugCentral-derived databases. Strict bitwise reproducibility of the drug list is required and no pinned Drugst.One/NeDRex database version can be used, since the databases update weekly.

skills.description: Use when evaluating CaDRReS-Sc drug response predictions trained on GDSC/PRISM cell line data and you need to remove poorly predicted drugs (bottom-quartile drug-wise Spearman correlation) before reporting results.
skills.name: drug-wise-spearman-correlation-filtering
skills.search_text: drug-wise-spearman-correlation-filtering Use when evaluating CaDRReS-Sc drug response predictions trained on GDSC/PRISM cell line data and you need to remove poorly predicted drugs (bottom-quartile drug-wise Spearman correlation) before reporting results. When selecting feature genes for the PRISM kernel — that uses a different filter (8,087 genes with |Pearson correlation| ≥ 0.2 between expression and PRISM AUC), not a drug-wise Spearman quartile filter When the drug set is very small (e.g., a single-drug validation like the idasanutlin 24-cell-line experiment), since dropping the bottom quartile of drugs would remove the drug of interest entirely http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A post-training quality filter used in the scDrug drug response prediction pipeline: after training CaDRReS-Sc models on GDSC (226 drugs, 1074 cell lines) and PRISM (1448 drugs, 480 cell lines) data, drug-wise Spearman correlations between actual and predicted response are computed, and drugs whose coefficient falls below the first-quartile coefficient are dropped before downstream analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: A post-training quality filter used in the scDrug drug response prediction pipeline: after training CaDRReS-Sc models on GDSC (226 drugs, 1074 cell lines) and PRISM (1448 drugs, 480 cell lines) data, drug-wise Spearman correlations between actual and predicted response are computed, and drugs whose coefficient falls below the first-quartile coefficient are dropped before downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When selecting feature genes for the PRISM kernel — that uses a different filter (8,087 genes with |Pearson correlation| ≥ 0.2 between expression and PRISM AUC), not a drug-wise Spearman quartile filter When the drug set is very small (e.g., a single-drug validation like the idasanutlin 24-cell-line experiment), since dropping the bottom quartile of drugs would remove the drug of interest entirely

skills.description: Use when you have a list of disease-specific essential genes/gene pairs from constraint-based knockout analysis and want to identify approved drugs or drug pairs targeting them via DrugBank.
skills.name: drugbank-target-interaction-mapping
skills.search_text: drugbank-target-interaction-mapping Use when you have a list of disease-specific essential genes/gene pairs from constraint-based knockout analysis and want to identify approved drugs or drug pairs targeting them via DrugBank. The virus is being modeled through direct docking on its proteome rather than through a viral biomass objective function — these drug targets derive from network effects on the host metabolome, not from docking No disease-specific essential genes or gene pairs are available yet — the mapping step requires upstream in silico knockout results The drug of interest is not metabolic or not present in DrugBank V5 with target annotations (e.g. nutraceuticals and experimental compounds are explicitly discarded) http://edamontology.org/topic_3332 http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 Maps context-specific essential single genes and gene pairs (from in silico knockout of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung metabolic models) onto DrugBank V5 drug-target interactions to propose FDA-approved single drugs and drug combinations for repositioning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Maps context-specific essential single genes and gene pairs (from in silico knockout of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung metabolic models) onto DrugBank V5 drug-target interactions to propose FDA-approved single drugs and drug combinations for repositioning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The virus is being modeled through direct docking on its proteome rather than through a viral biomass objective function — these drug targets derive from network effects on the host metabolome, not from docking No disease-specific essential genes or gene pairs are available yet — the mapping step requires upstream in silico knockout results The drug of interest is not metabolic or not present in DrugBank V5 with target annotations (e.g. nutraceuticals and experimental compounds are explicitly discarded)

skills.description: Use when building a labeled positive training set of endogenous dsRNA regions from A-to-I RNA editing site annotations, and when structural curation via RNAfold secondary-structure filters is needed before model training.
skills.name: dsrna-positive-training-set-construction
skills.search_text: dsrna-positive-training-set-construction Use when building a labeled positive training set of endogenous dsRNA regions from A-to-I RNA editing site annotations, and when structural curation via RNAfold secondary-structure filters is needed before model training. When constructing the negative (null) dsRNA training set — this skill only defines dsRID_train.tsv positives; dsRID_null.tsv comes from a separate step When the input already contains curated dsRNA predictions (e.g. data/dsRID_novel_dsRNA.bed from a completed dsRID run) rather than raw editing evidence When no A-to-I editing annotation source comparable to REDIportal exists for the organism, since editing enrichment is the sole positive-signal basis http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Defines the positive training regions (dsRID_train.tsv) for the dsRID random-forest model by mining REDIportal A-to-I RNA editing enrichment as evidence of dsRNA structure, then curating candidates with ViennaRNA RNAfold using stem-length, mismatch, and adjusted-MFE thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Defines the positive training regions (dsRID_train.tsv) for the dsRID random-forest model by mining REDIportal A-to-I RNA editing enrichment as evidence of dsRNA structure, then curating candidates with ViennaRNA RNAfold using stem-length, mismatch, and adjusted-MFE thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When constructing the negative (null) dsRNA training set — this skill only defines dsRID_train.tsv positives; dsRID_null.tsv comes from a separate step When the input already contains curated dsRNA predictions (e.g. data/dsRID_novel_dsRNA.bed from a completed dsRID run) rather than raw editing evidence When no A-to-I editing annotation source comparable to REDIportal exists for the organism, since editing enrichment is the sole positive-signal basis

skills.description: Use when you have PacBio long-read RNA-seq (BAM) derived feature tables of candidate dsRNA regions and need to train/validate a classifier, or reproduce reported performance (89% 20-fold CV accuracy) and feature importances (Skip_ratio 75.4%, Len_skip 15.9%).
skills.name: dsrna-region-feature-classification
skills.search_text: dsrna-region-feature-classification Use when you have PacBio long-read RNA-seq (BAM) derived feature tables of candidate dsRNA regions and need to train/validate a classifier, or reproduce reported performance (89% 20-fold CV accuracy) and feature importances (Skip_ratio 75.4%, Len_skip 15.9%). Input is already a whole-genome scan table (dsRID_whole.tsv) and you only want scoring — opt out of training and run extract_whole.py followed by model_predict.py directly instead of re-running dsRID.sh Data are short-read RNA-seq — dsRID is designed to leverage molecular traits of dsRNAs captured by long-read RNA sequencing You lack the paired positive/negative training tables or the packaged Pacbio_AD_data.tsv needed to fit and cross-validate the classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and evaluate a random-forest classifier (dsRID) that discriminates candidate dsRNA regions from null regions using molecular traits extracted from PacBio long-read RNA-seq data, quantifying both cross-validation accuracy and permutation-based feature contributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Train and evaluate a random-forest classifier (dsRID) that discriminates candidate dsRNA regions from null regions using molecular traits extracted from PacBio long-read RNA-seq data, quantifying both cross-validation accuracy and permutation-based feature contributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a whole-genome scan table (dsRID_whole.tsv) and you only want scoring — opt out of training and run extract_whole.py followed by model_predict.py directly instead of re-running dsRID.sh Data are short-read RNA-seq — dsRID is designed to leverage molecular traits of dsRNAs captured by long-read RNA sequencing You lack the paired positive/negative training tables or the packaged Pacbio_AD_data.tsv needed to fit and cross-validate the classifier

skills.description: Use when you need to predict dsRNA regions in silico from PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM files genome-wide, and classify predicted windows into candidate dsRNAs, novel long dsRNAs, and structured RNAs.
skills.name: dsrna-region-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: dsrna-region-threshold-filtering Use when you need to predict dsRNA regions in silico from PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM files genome-wide, and classify predicted windows into candidate dsRNAs, novel long dsRNAs, and structured RNAs. Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM files The goal is de novo training of the dsRID model on new data rather than applying the pre-trained model for prediction (use the full dsRID.sh training pipeline instead) The input regions are already classified structured RNAs and only RNAfold curation is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Applies dsRID, a random-forest machine learning method, to PacBio long-read RNA-seq data to identify and classify candidate double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) regions genome-wide, filtering predictions at a probability threshold of >0.5 and removing overlaps with known EER dsRNAs to define novel long dsRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Applies dsRID, a random-forest machine learning method, to PacBio long-read RNA-seq data to identify and classify candidate double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) regions genome-wide, filtering predictions at a probability threshold of >0.5 and removing overlaps with known EER dsRNAs to define novel long dsRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM files The goal is de novo training of the dsRID model on new data rather than applying the pre-trained model for prediction (use the full dsRID.sh training pipeline instead) The input regions are already classified structured RNAs and only RNAfold curation is needed

skills.description: Use when reproducing or porting the MU-PseUDeep pseudouridine-site classifier: input is paired 51×4 sequence and 51×6 RNAshapes structure one-of-K matrices that must be encoded by separate Conv1D branches and fused in Keras.
skills.name: dual-branch-cnn-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: dual-branch-cnn-architecture-implementation Use when reproducing or porting the MU-PseUDeep pseudouridine-site classifier: input is paired 51×4 sequence and 51×6 RNAshapes structure one-of-K matrices that must be encoded by separate Conv1D branches and fused in Keras. The task requires a sequence-only CNN without secondary-structure context (e.g., replicating the paper's baseline comparison model). Sequences are not fixed-length, uridine-centered 51-nt fragments one-of-K encoded (e.g., variable-length RNAs or protein data). The goal is hyperparameter search over architectures rather than reproducing the fixed MU-PseUDeep topology (use the Hyperas/Hyperopt workflow instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs the MU-PseUDeep dual-input 1D CNN in Keras/TensorFlow: two Conv1D branches encode the 51×4 one-of-K RNA sequence and 51×6 RNAshapes secondary-structure matrices, whose outputs are concatenated into a 512-neuron softplus dense layer and a binary Ψ-site head (661,118 trainable parameters). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Reconstructs the MU-PseUDeep dual-input 1D CNN in Keras/TensorFlow: two Conv1D branches encode the 51×4 one-of-K RNA sequence and 51×6 RNAshapes secondary-structure matrices, whose outputs are concatenated into a 512-neuron softplus dense layer and a binary Ψ-site head (661,118 trainable parameters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires a sequence-only CNN without secondary-structure context (e.g., replicating the paper's baseline comparison model). Sequences are not fixed-length, uridine-centered 51-nt fragments one-of-K encoded (e.g., variable-length RNAs or protein data). The goal is hyperparameter search over architectures rather than reproducing the fixed MU-PseUDeep topology (use the Hyperas/Hyperopt workflow instead).

skills.description: Use when processing Ribo-seq FastQ data that has already passed QC and contaminant removal and must be mapped to a reference genome and transcriptome before CDS-level read counting and differential expression.
skills.name: dual-genome-transcriptome-riboseq-alignment
skills.search_text: dual-genome-transcriptome-riboseq-alignment Use when processing Ribo-seq FastQ data that has already passed QC and contaminant removal and must be mapped to a reference genome and transcriptome before CDS-level read counting and differential expression. Inputs are already alignment files (BAM) or a count matrix — skip re-alignment and start from counting or DESeq2 The study requires ribosome P-site offset estimation on a dataset that does not align enough material — use TRiP instead of riboWaltz, or a dedicated tool outside RiboDoc Analysis of non-RiboSeq RNA-seq data without ribosome footprints, where RPF-specific length selection (25-35 nt) and periodicity QC do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Jointly align ribosome-protected fragments (RPF) to both the genome (HISAT2) and the transcriptome (Bowtie2) within the RiboDoc pipeline, after adapter trimming and rRNA/tRNA contaminant depletion, to produce sorted, indexed BAMs that feed htseq-count CDS quantification and DESeq2 differential translation analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: Jointly align ribosome-protected fragments (RPF) to both the genome (HISAT2) and the transcriptome (Bowtie2) within the RiboDoc pipeline, after adapter trimming and rRNA/tRNA contaminant depletion, to produce sorted, indexed BAMs that feed htseq-count CDS quantification and DESeq2 differential translation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs are already alignment files (BAM) or a count matrix — skip re-alignment and start from counting or DESeq2 The study requires ribosome P-site offset estimation on a dataset that does not align enough material — use TRiP instead of riboWaltz, or a dedicated tool outside RiboDoc Analysis of non-RiboSeq RNA-seq data without ribosome footprints, where RPF-specific length selection (25-35 nt) and periodicity QC do not apply

skills.description: Use when you have 10x cellranger output from infected-cell scRNA-seq and need per-cell pathogen read/UMI counts integrated into filtered_feature_bc_matrix, or when validating an alignment strategy against a combined host+pathogen cellranger reference.
skills.name: dual-reference-viral-read-counting
skills.search_text: dual-reference-viral-read-counting Use when you have 10x cellranger output from infected-cell scRNA-seq and need per-cell pathogen read/UMI counts integrated into filtered_feature_bc_matrix, or when validating an alignment strategy against a combined host+pathogen cellranger reference. Input reads have not first been processed by cellranger count against the host genome — scPathoQuant consumes the 10x output folder, not raw FASTQ Non-10x single-cell platforms whose output scPathoQuant does not consume via the -10x parameter The pathogen genome is already integrated into the host reference used for the primary cellranger run (e.g. hg38 with HIV integrated), leaving no host-unmapped pathogen reads to extract http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Quantifies pathogen (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) reads per cell in 10x scRNA-seq data by running cellranger count against the host genome, then using scPathoQuant to map host-unmapped reads to a pathogen reference with bbmap or bowtie2 and integrate pathogen UMI counts back into the 10x matrix files. Validates the result against a combined GRCh38 + pathogen cellranger run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Quantifies pathogen (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) reads per cell in 10x scRNA-seq data by running cellranger count against the host genome, then using scPathoQuant to map host-unmapped reads to a pathogen reference with bbmap or bowtie2 and integrate pathogen UMI counts back into the 10x matrix files. skills.description: Use when an ensemble of simulated cell state transitions (e.g. from Cytopath Markov sampling) must be converted into per-terminal-region consensus trajectories, or when simulations of unequal length need temporal alignment before averaging.
skills.name: dynamic-time-warping-trajectory-alignment
skills.search_text: dynamic-time-warping-trajectory-alignment Use when an ensemble of simulated cell state transitions (e.g. from Cytopath Markov sampling) must be converted into per-terminal-region consensus trajectories, or when simulations of unequal length need temporal alignment before averaging. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference with Cytopath to be meaningful if velocity itself is unrepresentative of true transcriptional dynamics (e.g. spurious root/terminal states in the erythroid gastrulation dataset) When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that situation When simulations do not share a common terminal state, since DTW alignment in this workflow is applied only within groups of simulations terminating at a common terminal state http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aligns Cytopath's ensemble of Markov-sampled cell state sequences that terminate at a common terminal state using dynamic time warping (fastdtw), then averages cell states at every step of the aligned simulations to construct a consensus trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Aligns Cytopath's ensemble of Markov-sampled cell state sequences that terminate at a common terminal state using dynamic time warping (fastdtw), then averages cell states at every step of the aligned simulations to construct a consensus trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference with Cytopath to be meaningful if velocity itself is unrepresentative of true transcriptional dynamics (e.g. spurious root/terminal states in the erythroid gastrulation dataset) When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that situation When simulations do not share a common terminal state, since DTW alignment in this workflow is applied only within groups of simulations terminating at a common terminal state

skills.name: dynamic-tree-cut-module-detection

skills.name: dyngen-ground-truth-network-comparison
skills.search_text: dyngen-ground-truth-network-comparison Use when a quantitative CSNI benchmark with complete cellwise ground-truth networks is needed and real single-cell data cannot provide that ground truth — i.e. comparing network inference methods on dyngen-simulated transcriptomics. The question concerns trajectory inference, trajectory alignment, or RNA velocity benchmarking — dyngen supports those via different ground-truth layers and workflows (e.g. analysis/usecase_rna_velocity). Only real single-cell data is available and no ground-truth cellwise regulatory network exists — AUROC/AUPR against truth cannot be computed. Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods such as pySCENIC, LIONESS, and SSN against dyngen's simulated cellwise ground-truth regulatory networks, scoring each method with mean AUROC and AUPR across cells on 42 dyngen datasets (14 backbones x 3 seeds). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods such as pySCENIC, LIONESS, and SSN against dyngen's simulated cellwise ground-truth regulatory networks, scoring each method with mean AUROC and AUPR across cells on 42 dyngen datasets (14 backbones x 3 seeds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns trajectory inference, trajectory alignment, or RNA velocity benchmarking — dyngen supports those via different ground-truth layers and workflows (e.g. analysis/usecase_rna_velocity). skills.description: Use when you need synthetic dyngen-simulated trajectory datasets with known ground-truth condition differences to benchmark differential progression, fate selection, or differential abundance methods against simulated reality.
skills.name: dyngen-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: dyngen-trajectory-simulation Use when you need synthetic dyngen-simulated trajectory datasets with known ground-truth condition differences to benchmark differential progression, fate selection, or differential abundance methods against simulated reality. The data are real-world, steady-state samples without a dynamic trajectory structure — the paper notes clustering-based differential abundance is the reasonable approach in steady-state systems You lack simulation ground truth and only need differential calls on one real dataset — this skill is a benchmarking harness, not a per-dataset analysis pipeline The system's trajectory topology itself differs fundamentally between conditions (differential topology), which is tested with topologyTest rather than progression/fate selection tests Benchmark skill for simulating multi-lineage single-cell trajectory datasets with dyngen and using them as ground truth to compare trajectory-aware differential testing (condiments progressionTest/fateSelectionTest) against neighborhood-based differential abundance methods (DAseq, milo), with BH correction at 5% FDR and TNR/TPR/PPV/NPV/F1 scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Benchmark skill for simulating multi-lineage single-cell trajectory datasets with dyngen and using them as ground truth to compare trajectory-aware differential testing (condiments progressionTest/fateSelectionTest) against neighborhood-based differential abundance methods (DAseq, milo), with BH correction at 5% FDR and TNR/TPR/PPV/NPV/F1 scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real-world, steady-state samples without a dynamic trajectory structure — the paper notes clustering-based differential abundance is the reasonable approach in steady-state systems You lack simulation ground truth and only need differential calls on one real dataset — this skill is a benchmarking harness, not a per-dataset analysis pipeline The system's trajectory topology itself differs fundamentally between conditions (differential topology), which is tested with topologyTest rather than progression/fate selection tests

skills.description: Use when inferred trajectories (e.g. from Totem, Slingshot, or TinGa) must be scored against dynverse gold-standard trajectories with known milestone/branch structure, as in the 216 tree-shaped dynverse benchmark or the 10 dynverse Zenodo datasets (doi:10.5281/zenodo.1443566).
skills.name: dynverse-trajectory-scoring
skills.search_text: dynverse-trajectory-scoring Use when inferred trajectories (e.g. from Totem, Slingshot, or TinGa) must be scored against dynverse gold-standard trajectories with known milestone/branch structure, as in the 216 tree-shaped dynverse benchmark or the 10 dynverse Zenodo datasets (doi:10.5281/zenodo.1443566). The data have no gold-standard trajectory (no dynverse milestone/branch ground truth) — the dynverse metrics cannot be computed without a reference to score against The inferred trajectory contains cycles or disconnected components — Totem itself cannot generate such trajectories, so the comparison is out of scope for this pipeline The goal is pseudotime visualization of multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories, so downstream inspection via dynplot is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantitative benchmarking of inferred single-cell trajectories against dynverse gold-standard trajectories, using the four dynverse metrics (correlation of geodesic distances, featureimp correlation, F1 branches, HIM) aggregated into a geometric-mean overall score in the [0, 1] range. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Quantitative benchmarking of inferred single-cell trajectories against dynverse gold-standard trajectories, using the four dynverse metrics (correlation of geodesic distances, featureimp correlation, F1 branches, HIM) aggregated into a geometric-mean overall score in the [0, 1] range.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have no gold-standard trajectory (no dynverse milestone/branch ground truth) — the dynverse metrics cannot be computed without a reference to score against The inferred trajectory contains cycles or disconnected components — Totem itself cannot generate such trajectories, so the comparison is out of scope for this pipeline The goal is pseudotime visualization of multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories, so downstream inspection via dynplot is unreliable

skills.description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a source-free transfer learning model and you need per-cell uncertainty scores to drive downstream novel cell-type detection (bimodality testing) and known/unknown partitioning.
skills.name: e-score-uncertainty-measurement
skills.search_text: e-score-uncertainty-measurement Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a source-free transfer learning model and you need per-cell uncertainty scores to drive downstream novel cell-type detection (bimodality testing) and known/unknown partitioning. Source raw data are fully available and explicit feature alignment between source and target is feasible — standard transfer learning annotation without uncertainty-based novelty perception suffices Target data are known a priori to contain no novel cell types under a closed setting — the E-score/bimodality machinery is unnecessary and closed-set annotation can proceed directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes scEMAIL's expert ensemble score (E-score) that quantifies per-cell annotation uncertainty in target scRNA-seq data by combining three complementary indices — normalized entropy (EN), maximum confidence (CF), and auxiliary-classifier consistency (CS) — as the first step of the novel cell-type perception module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Computes scEMAIL's expert ensemble score (E-score) that quantifies per-cell annotation uncertainty in target scRNA-seq data by combining three complementary indices — normalized entropy (EN), maximum confidence (CF), and auxiliary-classifier consistency (CS) — as the first step of the novel cell-type perception module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source raw data are fully available and explicit feature alignment between source and target is feasible — standard transfer learning annotation without uncertainty-based novelty perception suffices Target data are known a priori to contain no novel cell types under a closed setting — the E-score/bimodality machinery is unnecessary and closed-set annotation can proceed directly

skills.description: Use when building a supervised single-cell classifier from labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a small, cell-type-discriminative gene set before fitting the multinomial model.
skills.name: e-test-gene-feature-selection
skills.search_text: e-test-gene-feature-selection Use when building a supervised single-cell classifier from labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a small, cell-type-discriminative gene set before fitting the multinomial model. The expression matrix has no cell type labels — ΔS is computed from per-cell-type means, so unlabeled data cannot be scored Downstream annotation does not use a multinomial/likelihood model over a compact marker set — genes with high ΔS are tuned to SciBet's classifier, not generic clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SciBet's E-test selects cell type-specific genes by ranking each gene with the entropy-difference statistic ΔS = n·(ln(AM) − ln(GM)) computed over the n cell-type mean expression vectors, retaining the top k (default 500) informative genes for multinomial classifier training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: SciBet's E-test selects cell type-specific genes by ranking each gene with the entropy-difference statistic ΔS = n·(ln(AM) − ln(GM)) computed over the n cell-type mean expression vectors, retaining the top k (default 500) informative genes for multinomial classifier training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has no cell type labels — ΔS is computed from per-cell-type means, so unlabeled data cannot be scored Downstream annotation does not use a multinomial/likelihood model over a compact marker set — genes with high ΔS are tuned to SciBet's classifier, not generic clustering

Input is already a per-sample feature/signature score table with no raw counts to normalize The cohort is single-cell data rather than bulk RNA-seq — use the single-cell niche identification workflow instead Groups have very small and equal variances where a standard t-test rather than Welch's correction is already appropriate and explicitly specified by the study design http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Statistically validates whether the EAD-associated immune niche (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) identified in the single-cell landscape distinguishes EAD from non-EAD samples, by comparing per-sample niche signature scores with Welch's t-test in the independent GSE23649 bulk RNA-seq DBD cohort (8 EAD vs 8 non-EAD). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated comparison result or summary table — apply the test only to per-sample values with known EAD labels The analysis goal is cell-cell communication inference itself (LR-pair enrichment); use scCrossTalk's create_scCrossTalk/find_lrpairs workflow first, then apply this skill only for the non-EAD vs EAD comparison of resulting scores Sample sizes or group structure differ from a two-group (non-EAD vs EAD) within-stage design; the one-sided Welch's test as parameterized here assumes that structure

skills.description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods on time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data where a reference regulatory network (e.g. BEELINE hESC/mESC ground truth) exists and performance at the top of the ranked edge list matters more than full-network accuracy.
skills.name: early-precision-curve-evaluation
skills.search_text: early-precision-curve-evaluation Use when comparing GRN inference methods on time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data where a reference regulatory network (e.g. BEELINE hESC/mESC ground truth) exists and performance at the top of the ranked edge list matters more than full-network accuracy. The data lack a reference/ground-truth regulatory network, so early precision cannot be computed against known edges The goal is to evaluate GRNs that maintain a single cell stage rather than transition mechanisms — the article notes most alternative methods infer networks for a single stage, while early precision here targets sparse transition GRNs between consecutive time points The method requires pseudo-time trajectories as input (e.g. pseudo-time-dependent baselines evaluated on trajectories COSLIR does not use); the evaluation design must instead score networks inferred from the same TSCS time-point pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Evaluates inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) by computing early precision against cell-type-specific or reference ground-truth edges, as used in the COSLIR paper to benchmark COSLIR against SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, and SINGE on TSCS single-cell qPCR and RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Evaluates inferred gene regulatory networks (GRNs) by computing early precision against cell-type-specific or reference ground-truth edges, as used in the COSLIR paper to benchmark COSLIR against SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, and SINGE on TSCS single-cell qPCR and RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack a reference/ground-truth regulatory network, so early precision cannot be computed against known edges The goal is to evaluate GRNs that maintain a single cell stage rather than transition mechanisms — the article notes most alternative methods infer networks for a single stage, while early precision here targets sparse transition GRNs between consecutive time points The method requires pseudo-time trajectories as input (e.g. pseudo-time-dependent baselines evaluated on trajectories COSLIR does not use); the evaluation design must instead score networks inferred from the same TSCS time-point pairs

skills.description: Use when each sample is represented as a vector of cell-cluster (or tissue-structure) proportions and you need a pairwise, unsupervised sample-level distance matrix (e.g. for downstream Leiden clustering or diffusion-map trajectories).
skills.name: earth-mover-distance-solving-single-cell-samples
skills.search_text: earth-mover-distance-solving-single-cell-samples Use when each sample is represented as a vector of cell-cluster (or tissue-structure) proportions and you need a pairwise, unsupervised sample-level distance matrix (e.g. for downstream Leiden clustering or diffusion-map trajectories). Samples have no cluster-level representation (raw per-cell data not yet clustered into cell populations or tissue structures) — cluster proportions are required marginals You need label-supervised sample grouping — prior methods like PhEMD/SCANCell/Multi-scale PHATE require patient labels, but if labels are the analysis goal a supervised approach fits better Data were produced with distinct technologies or cell-isolation methods (e.g. single-nucleus vs single-cell, droplet vs well based) — PILOT assumes samples were collected uniformly and such cross-technology comparison is an open challenge http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute a Wasserstein (earth mover's) distance between two individual single-cell samples by solving an optimal transport problem over their cluster distributions, with a cost matrix built from cosine distances between cluster medians in PCA space. This is the core sample-level distance of PILOT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Compute a Wasserstein (earth mover's) distance between two individual single-cell samples by solving an optimal transport problem over their cluster distributions, with a cost matrix built from cosine distances between cluster medians in PCA space. This is the core sample-level distance of PILOT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples have no cluster-level representation (raw per-cell data not yet clustered into cell populations or tissue structures) — cluster proportions are required marginals You need label-supervised sample grouping — prior methods like PhEMD/SCANCell/Multi-scale PHATE require patient labels, but if labels are the analysis goal a supervised approach fits better Data were produced with distinct technologies or cell-isolation methods (e.g. single-nucleus vs single-cell, droplet vs well based) — PILOT assumes samples were collected uniformly and such cross-technology comparison is an open challenge

skills.description: Use when analyzing a DifferentialConnectome output (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control ifnb PBMCs) and you need a sign-independent per-edge magnitude of perturbation for ranking, filtering, or heatmap/circos visualization of differential ligand–receptor signaling.
skills.name: edge-level-network-score-computation
skills.search_text: edge-level-network-score-computation Use when analyzing a DifferentialConnectome output (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control ifnb PBMCs) and you need a sign-independent per-edge magnitude of perturbation for ranking, filtering, or heatmap/circos visualization of differential ligand–receptor signaling. The input is a single-condition connectome or filtered edgelist (e.g., from FilterConnectome) rather than a differential connectome — there are no test/control log-fold-changes to multiply. You need a signed direction of change per edge rather than a magnitude-only, always-positive perturbation score. You need direct evidence of communication: strongly paired ligand–receptor expression changes are not direct evidence of cell–cell communication, and spatial proximity cannot be verified from suspension scRNA-seq. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Computation of per-edge perturbation scores in a Connectome differential connectome, where each ligand–receptor edge between cell types is scored as the product of the absolute normalized log2 fold-changes of ligand and receptor between test and control conditions, yielding an always-positive magnitude of perturbation from 0 to Infinity regardless of direction of change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Computation of per-edge perturbation scores in a Connectome differential connectome, where each ligand–receptor edge between cell types is scored as the product of the absolute normalized log2 fold-changes of ligand and receptor between test and control conditions, yielding an always-positive magnitude of perturbation from 0 to Infinity regardless of direction of change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single-condition connectome or filtered edgelist (e.g., from FilterConnectome) rather than a differential connectome — there are no test/control log-fold-changes to multiply. You need a signed direction of change per edge rather than a magnitude-only, always-positive perturbation score. You need direct evidence of communication: strongly paired ligand–receptor expression changes are not direct evidence of cell–cell communication, and spatial proximity cannot be verified from suspension scRNA-seq.

The candidate TF set exceeds ~5 regulators — decoding high-order Boolean logic (>5 regulators) is intractable due to overfitting per the article's discussion The task is plain directed TF-gene edge inference without logic gates — use scGATE_edge() instead of the EM logic-combination fitting Data is pseudotime-sorted along a differentiation trajectory — scGATE does not yet handle temporal delays in regulatory logic http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits a zero-inflated mixture distribution over all 2^k Boolean logic combinations of candidate TFs to a target gene's expression profile and uses an expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm to estimate prior weights w_v for each combination, so the Boolean rule can be inferred a posteriori via Bayes factor rather than by fitting a separate likelihood per rule (AND/OR/XOR). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180

Bulk RNA-Seq or other non-single-cell allelic data — the partial-pooling rationale depends on many cells sharing each allelic state and loses its advantage when cell number is small or coverage is high When a preliminary clustering of allelic states already exists and per-cell estimates are adequate without combining information across cells When the goal is burst-kinetic parameter inference (e.g., k_on, k_off, k_syn) rather than allelic state classification — use txburst on allelic UMI counts instead http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run the scBASE classification and partial-pooling steps alternately, each informing the other, until the beta-binomial mixture parameters and per-gene-cell P/B/M state assignments converge. skills.search_text: embedding-connectivity-evaluation Use when candidate 2D embeddings (e.g., PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, diffusion maps of scRNA-seq data) must be screened for disconnected cell clusters before being accepted for trajectory inference scoring in Escort. When the representation is not a two-dimensional embedding — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations, so higher-dimensional or velocity-derived embeddings are out of scope. When the goal is to fit or score the trajectory itself (pseudotime estimation) rather than to gate which embeddings are admissible — this skill is only the connectivity screening step. skills.search_text: embedding-mapping-matrix-construction Use when you have aligned SC and ST embeddings in a shared latent space (e.g. from a trained STEM netE encoder) and need per-cell spatial coordinates or spot-to-cell correspondence probabilities. You only need spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types — the article notes deconvolution cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level, but if that coarse representation suffices, a mapping matrix is unnecessary. The SC and ST embeddings have not been trained/aligned in a shared latent space (e.g. no MMD-based domain alignment was performed) — raw dot-products of unaligned embeddings will not yield meaningful mappings. SC and ST data are from different donors or different disease states — the article flags applying STEM to data from different donors in the same disease state as untested future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs ST-SC and SC-ST mapping matrices by applying F.softmax over the cross dot-product of SC and ST embeddings produced by the STEM encoder, so that probabilities per spot/cell sum to 1. skills.summary: QC-filter, subcluster, and annotate the E14.5 embryonic skin dermal compartment into placode, pre-DC, DC1 and DC2 states so that downstream CellChat communication analysis operates on biologically meaningful cell groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated cell-state annotated object or a CellChat object — re-subclustering would destroy existing group labels Dataset contains only a handful of cells per dermal state, so Louvain subclustering restricted to cell types with abundance > 5% cannot resolve states The goal is de novo tissue annotation of non-skin tissue; the QC thresholds (UMI 2500–50000, mito < 20%) are embryonic-skin specific

skills.description: Use when a merged, cross-study normalized expression matrix (e.g. GEO-derived microarray data collapsed to gene symbols) shows batch structure driven by known covariates such as data series or microarray platform that must be removed before downstream analyses.
skills.name: empirical-bayes-batch-adjustment
skills.search_text: empirical-bayes-batch-adjustment Use when a merged, cross-study normalized expression matrix (e.g. GEO-derived microarray data collapsed to gene symbols) shows batch structure driven by known covariates such as data series or microarray platform that must be removed before downstream analyses. Input is raw probe intensities that have not yet been probe-to-gene collapsed (collapseRows) and cross-study normalized with limma — batch adjustment assumes an already normalized matrix The batch structure is unknown or driven by unmeasured confounders rather than known covariates like data series and platform — a different sva mode (e.g. latent factor estimation) would be needed The dataset comes from a single study/series with no platform variation, so no known batch effect exists to remove http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Remove known batch effects (data series and platform) from a normalized multi-study gene expression matrix using the parametric empirical Bayes adjustment implemented in the sva package (ComBat-style), retaining biological signal so differentiation time-course and perturbation responses are reproduced. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Remove known batch effects (data series and platform) from a normalized multi-study gene expression matrix using the parametric empirical Bayes adjustment implemented in the sva package (ComBat-style), retaining biological signal so differentiation time-course and perturbation responses are reproduced.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw probe intensities that have not yet been probe-to-gene collapsed (collapseRows) and cross-study normalized with limma — batch adjustment assumes an already normalized matrix The batch structure is unknown or driven by unmeasured confounders rather than known covariates like data series and platform — a different sva mode (e.g. latent factor estimation) would be needed The dataset comes from a single study/series with no platform variation, so no known batch effect exists to remove

skills.description: Use when combining multi-study microarray data (e.g. GSE12929 and GSE14004 from curatedAdipoArray) where study of origin or platform confounds the analysis, and you need to verify that a biological variable separates samples after correction.
skills.name: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal
skills.search_text: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal Use when combining multi-study microarray data (e.g. GSE12929 and GSE14004 from curatedAdipoArray) where study of origin or platform confounds the analysis, and you need to verify that a biological variable separates samples after correction. The data come from a single study/series with no known batch variable (data series, platform) to adjust for — ComBat-style removal would remove real signal The matrix is already batch-corrected, or the goal is differential expression or gene set enrichment on the curated data directly without first quantifying batch dominance Working with the RNA-Seq or ChIP-Seq companion datasets (curatedAdipoRNA/curatedAdipoChIP), whose preprocessing pipeline differs from the microarray limma/sva workflow Removes known batch effects (data series and platform) from the curated 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data using sva's empirical Bayes (ComBat-style) adjustment, so that biological variables such as stage of differentiation — rather than study of origin — dominate downstream analyses like PCA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Removes known batch effects (data series and platform) from the curated 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data using sva's empirical Bayes (ComBat-style) adjustment, so that biological variables such as stage of differentiation — rather than study of origin — dominate downstream analyses like PCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data come from a single study/series with no known batch variable (data series, platform) to adjust for — ComBat-style removal would remove real signal The matrix is already batch-corrected, or the goal is differential expression or gene set enrichment on the curated data directly without first quantifying batch dominance Working with the RNA-Seq or ChIP-Seq companion datasets (curatedAdipoRNA/curatedAdipoChIP), whose preprocessing pipeline differs from the microarray limma/sva workflow
