skills.search_text: empirical-cdf-error-visualization Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth circadian phases and multiple phase-inference methods (e.g., Tempo vs Cyclops/Cyclum/PCA) whose point-estimate errors you need to compare across conditions. Real scRNA-seq data without ground-truth or simulated phases, where absolute error against truth cannot be computed The goal is phase point estimation or uncertainty quantification itself (run Tempo) rather than benchmarking/visualizing error distributions across methods Data involve non-circadian oscillations where the 24 h sinusoidal mean assumption of the generative model does not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark circadian phase inference by computing absolute point-estimate phase errors against simulated ground truth and comparing methods via empirical cumulative distribution functions (eCDFs) of these errors, as done to show Tempo's estimates sit near the maximum-likelihood optimum while Cyclops, Cyclum, and PCA degrade. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Benchmark circadian phase inference by computing absolute point-estimate phase errors against simulated ground truth and comparing methods via empirical cumulative distribution functions (eCDFs) of these errors, as done to show Tempo's estimates sit near the maximum-likelihood optimum while Cyclops, Cyclum, and PCA degrade.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scRNA-seq data without ground-truth or simulated phases, where absolute error against truth cannot be computed The goal is phase point estimation or uncertainty quantification itself (run Tempo) rather than benchmarking/visualizing error distributions across methods Data involve non-circadian oscillations where the 24 h sinusoidal mean assumption of the generative model does not hold

skills.description: Use when the sample covariance of a high-dimensional transcriptomic matrix (p >> n, e.g. 116 obs × 6283 genes) is rank deficient and you need a full-rank empirical covariance Φ or a pseudo-true β* to test whether marginal-correlation screening recovers true predictive genes.
skills.name: empirical-covariance-rank-truncation
skills.search_text: empirical-covariance-rank-truncation Use when the sample covariance of a high-dimensional transcriptomic matrix (p >> n, e.g. 116 obs × 6283 genes) is rank deficient and you need a full-rank empirical covariance Φ or a pseudo-true β* to test whether marginal-correlation screening recovers true predictive genes. The dataset has n >= p so the sample covariance is full rank and no truncation is needed The goal is prediction or classification with SuffPCR itself rather than benchmarking marginal-correlation screening against a pseudo-true β* Features are known to be uncorrelated, so marginal screening is expected to work and the counterexample regime does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs a usable empirical covariance from the rank-deficient p>>n sample covariance (e.g. the suffpcr AML data: 116 observations × 6283 genes) by retaining only the top n entries, then combines it with a Graphical-Lasso-estimated sparse precision matrix to form the pseudo-true coefficient vector β* = Σ^-1 Φ used to benchmark marginal-correlation feature screening. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Constructs a usable empirical covariance from the rank-deficient p>>n sample covariance (e.g. the suffpcr AML data: 116 observations × 6283 genes) by retaining only the top n entries, then combines it with a Graphical-Lasso-estimated sparse precision matrix to form the pseudo-true coefficient vector β* = Σ^-1 Φ used to benchmark marginal-correlation feature screening.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has n >= p so the sample covariance is full rank and no truncation is needed The goal is prediction or classification with SuffPCR itself rather than benchmarking marginal-correlation screening against a pseudo-true β* Features are known to be uncorrelated, so marginal screening is expected to work and the counterexample regime does not apply

skills.description: Use when time-course scRNA-seq data sacrifice cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and you need to set up the discrete OT problem for CellST's cell_name_traj lineage alignment.
skills.name: empirical-distribution-estimation-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: empirical-distribution-estimation-scrna-seq Use when time-course scRNA-seq data sacrifice cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and you need to set up the discrete OT problem for CellST's cell_name_traj lineage alignment. When paired correspondence information already exists between the two time points (e.g. longitudinal sampling of the same cells) — the Dirac-mixture OT formulation is designed for sacrificed-cell designs with no correspondence When the goal is a bulk population trajectory rather than individual cell-to-cell lineages — CellST explicitly addresses the case where cells within the same time point are at different developmental stages When the input is not normalized gene expression per cell (e.g. raw counts with unnormalized library sizes), since the squared Euclidean cost assumption requires comparable expression scales http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates empirical gene feature distributions (μt, μt+1) as mixtures of Dirac measures from normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices so that a discrete optimal transport map can align cells between adjacent time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: Estimates empirical gene feature distributions (μt, μt+1) as mixtures of Dirac measures from normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices so that a discrete optimal transport map can align cells between adjacent time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When paired correspondence information already exists between the two time points (e.g. longitudinal sampling of the same cells) — the Dirac-mixture OT formulation is designed for sacrificed-cell designs with no correspondence When the goal is a bulk population trajectory rather than individual cell-to-cell lineages — CellST explicitly addresses the case where cells within the same time point are at different developmental stages When the input is not normalized gene expression per cell (e.g. raw counts with unnormalized library sizes), since the squared Euclidean cost assumption requires comparable expression scales

skills.description: Use when a ground-truth null scRNA-seq read-count matrix is needed to benchmark confounder-detection or normalization methods — specifically a homogeneous, co-expression-free null for testing nonlinear library-size effects in Normalisr.
skills.name: empirical-distribution-sampling
skills.search_text: empirical-distribution-sampling Use when a ground-truth null scRNA-seq read-count matrix is needed to benchmark confounder-detection or normalization methods — specifically a homogeneous, co-expression-free null for testing nonlinear library-size effects in Normalisr. The null hypothesis should contain genuine co-expression (e.g., heterogeneous cell populations or real regulatory signal) — this simulator enforces a co-expression-free homogeneous-cell null by construction. The analysis goal is hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations or causal regulatory network reconstruction — Normalisr itself is not designed for these, and the synthetic null only serves confounder/benchmarking evaluation. Input is already normalized (TPM/log-CPM) rather than raw read counts, since multinomial sampling requires integer read counts and empirical library-size distributions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a synthetic null scRNA-seq dataset by resampling per-cell library sizes and per-gene read proportions from the empirical distributions of a real read-count matrix (e.g., MARS-seq melanoma), then applying log-normal biological variation and multinomial read sampling so the null contains no true co-expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Constructs a synthetic null scRNA-seq dataset by resampling per-cell library sizes and per-gene read proportions from the empirical distributions of a real read-count matrix (e.g., MARS-seq melanoma), then applying log-normal biological variation and multinomial read sampling so the null contains no true co-expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The null hypothesis should contain genuine co-expression (e.g., heterogeneous cell populations or real regulatory signal) — this simulator enforces a co-expression-free homogeneous-cell null by construction. The analysis goal is hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations or causal regulatory network reconstruction — Normalisr itself is not designed for these, and the synthetic null only serves confounder/benchmarking evaluation. Input is already normalized (TPM/log-CPM) rather than raw read counts, since multinomial sampling requires integer read counts and empirical library-size distributions.

skills.description: Use when you must verify that a marker-gene or association test controls type-I error at the nominal 0.05 level across subject-level overdispersion levels — e.g. benchmarking NEBULA against naive glm.nb on unbalanced multi-subject single-cell groupings.
skills.name: empirical-false-positive-rate-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-false-positive-rate-estimation Use when you must verify that a marker-gene or association test controls type-I error at the nominal 0.05 level across subject-level overdispersion levels — e.g. benchmarking NEBULA against naive glm.nb on unbalanced multi-subject single-cell groupings. Input is observed real expression data rather than simulated null counts — this skill estimates type-I error and requires replicates generated under the null model, not real data analysis Cells come from a single subject or the analysis has no multi-subject hierarchical structure, so there is no subject-level overdispersion component to sweep and no naive-vs-mixed-model contrast The goal is power or effect-size estimation under an alternative, not false-positive control under the null http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation-based procedure for measuring the empirical false-positive rate of a regression method under a null mixed model, sweeping subject-level overdispersion to reveal type-I-error inflation. In the NEBULA paper it demonstrates that naive negative binomial regression inflates false positives on unbalanced multi-subject scRNA-seq data while NEBULA's NBGMM keeps FPR near 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: A simulation-based procedure for measuring the empirical false-positive rate of a regression method under a null mixed model, sweeping subject-level overdispersion to reveal type-I-error inflation. In the NEBULA paper it demonstrates that naive negative binomial regression inflates false positives on unbalanced multi-subject scRNA-seq data while NEBULA's NBGMM keeps FPR near 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is observed real expression data rather than simulated null counts — this skill estimates type-I error and requires replicates generated under the null model, not real data analysis Cells come from a single subject or the analysis has no multi-subject hierarchical structure, so there is no subject-level overdispersion component to sweep and no naive-vs-mixed-model contrast The goal is power or effect-size estimation under an alternative, not false-positive control under the null

skills.description: Use when running gene set enrichment on scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (e.g. zingeR-DESeq2 beta/beta-variance) and a calibrated, overlap-aware empirical FDR (e.g. 5% threshold) is needed instead of nominal p-value cutoffs.
skills.name: empirical-fdr-estimation-by-gene-label-permutation
skills.search_text: empirical-fdr-estimation-by-gene-label-permutation Use when running gene set enrichment on scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (e.g. zingeR-DESeq2 beta/beta-variance) and a calibrated, overlap-aware empirical FDR (e.g. 5% threshold) is needed instead of nominal p-value cutoffs. When the input is raw scRNA-seq count data rather than per-gene DE summary statistics — iDEA consumes beta/beta-variance summaries from tools like zingeR-DESeq2, MAST, or SCDE When gene sets are strictly non-overlapping and independent, the permutation-based FDR machinery is unnecessary overhead When performing DE analysis on inferred cell types whose standard errors may be artificially small — iDEA's z-score-based prior can then be mis-calibrated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Estimate empirical gene-set FDR for iDEA by permuting gene labels in gene sets with iDEA.fit.null to build a permuted null distribution of GSE p-values, then computing FDR with iDEA.FDR; this accounts for test non-independence caused by gene set overlap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Estimate empirical gene-set FDR for iDEA by permuting gene labels in gene sets with iDEA.fit.null to build a permuted null distribution of GSE p-values, then computing FDR with iDEA.FDR; this accounts for test non-independence caused by gene set overlap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is raw scRNA-seq count data rather than per-gene DE summary statistics — iDEA consumes beta/beta-variance summaries from tools like zingeR-DESeq2, MAST, or SCDE When gene sets are strictly non-overlapping and independent, the permutation-based FDR machinery is unnecessary overhead When performing DE analysis on inferred cell types whose standard errors may be artificially small — iDEA's z-score-based prior can then be mis-calibrated

skills.description: Use when a t-SNE or UMAP embedding of single-cell omics data (e.g. ~4,800 Tabula Muris marrow cells) must be judged for real vs. algorithm-induced structure, requiring a per-sample significance test rather than a global quality score.
skills.name: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-via-marginal-resampling
skills.search_text: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-via-marginal-resampling Use when a t-SNE or UMAP embedding of single-cell omics data (e.g. ~4,800 Tabula Muris marrow cells) must be judged for real vs. algorithm-induced structure, requiring a per-sample significance test rather than a global quality score. The dataset is not normalized: EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets You need exact tail p-values beyond the empirical null resolution, since no theoretical description of the null distribution tails exists and p-value lower bounds are set by the number of nulls embedded You want a single global DR-quality metric rather than local, per-cell statistical assessment against a null hypothesis A statistical skill from EMBEDR: assess whether a dimensionality-reduction embedding (e.g. t-SNE or UMAP) contains structure more faithful to the high-dimensional data than expected by chance, by generating null datasets via marginal resampling and comparing neighborhood-preservation statistics to obtain a p-value for each sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: A statistical skill from EMBEDR: assess whether a dimensionality-reduction embedding (e.g. t-SNE or UMAP) contains structure more faithful to the high-dimensional data than expected by chance, by generating null datasets via marginal resampling and comparing neighborhood-preservation statistics to obtain a p-value for each sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not normalized: EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets You need exact tail p-values beyond the empirical null resolution, since no theoretical description of the null distribution tails exists and p-value lower bounds are set by the number of nulls embedded You want a single global DR-quality metric rather than local, per-cell statistical assessment against a null hypothesis

skills.description: Use when you need per-sample empirical p values that separate real structure in a DR embedding (t-SNE/UMAP) from algorithm-induced distortions, e.g. on Tabula Muris bone marrow scRNA-seq.
skills.name: empirical-null-pvalue-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-null-pvalue-estimation Use when you need per-sample empirical p values that separate real structure in a DR embedding (t-SNE/UMAP) from algorithm-induced distortions, e.g. on Tabula Muris bone marrow scRNA-seq. Input is a non-normalized dataset — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized data A single global DR-quality estimate suffices and per-cell/local error estimates are unnecessary You need very small p values (below ~1/n_null_embed) — empirical nulls give finite p-value resolution bounded by the number of null embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 EMBEDR-style empirical hypothesis testing for dimensionality reduction: a null distribution of an embedding-quality statistic (EES) is generated by marginal resampling, and each sample receives an empirical p value indicating whether its embedding reflects real high-dimensional structure rather than algorithm-induced noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: EMBEDR-style empirical hypothesis testing for dimensionality reduction: a null distribution of an embedding-quality statistic (EES) is generated by marginal resampling, and each sample receives an empirical p value indicating whether its embedding reflects real high-dimensional structure rather than algorithm-induced noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a non-normalized dataset — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized data A single global DR-quality estimate suffices and per-cell/local error estimates are unnecessary You need very small p values (below ~1/n_null_embed) — empirical nulls give finite p-value resolution bounded by the number of null embeddings

skills.description: Use when testing whether an unsupervised or bulk-derived gene set (e.g., cyclers with q < 0.05) is enriched for a reference set such as circadian clock genes, without a parametric enrichment model.
skills.name: empirical-null-random-gene-set-sampling
skills.search_text: empirical-null-random-gene-set-sampling Use when testing whether an unsupervised or bulk-derived gene set (e.g., cyclers with q < 0.05) is enriched for a reference set such as circadian clock genes, without a parametric enrichment model. When a standard parametric enrichment test (e.g., Fisher's exact test p-value alone) is sufficient and gene-set independence assumptions hold When the gene set of interest comes from a supervised differential-expression contrast rather than an unsupervised de novo call whose overlap with reference sets is the question http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assess whether a gene set (e.g., Tempo's de novo cyclers called unsupervised on scRNA-seq) is enriched for circadian clock genes by comparing the observed overlap statistic to an empirical null built from 1000 randomly sampled gene sets of the same size drawn from the assayed gene universe. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Assess whether a gene set (e.g., Tempo's de novo cyclers called unsupervised on scRNA-seq) is enriched for circadian clock genes by comparing the observed overlap statistic to an empirical null built from 1000 randomly sampled gene sets of the same size drawn from the assayed gene universe.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a standard parametric enrichment test (e.g., Fisher's exact test p-value alone) is sufficient and gene-set independence assumptions hold When the gene set of interest comes from a supervised differential-expression contrast rather than an unsupervised de novo call whose overlap with reference sets is the question

skills.description: Use when comparing detection rates of gene set enrichment methods on simulated summary statistics where the truth (which replicates are enriched) is known and power must be computed at a fixed FDR threshold (e.g. 5%).
skills.name: empirical-power-estimation-at-fixed-fdr
skills.search_text: empirical-power-estimation-at-fixed-fdr Use when comparing detection rates of gene set enrichment methods on simulated summary statistics where the truth (which replicates are enriched) is known and power must be computed at a fixed FDR threshold (e.g. 5%). Input is real scRNA-seq data with no known ground truth about which gene sets are enriched — power cannot be computed and only calibration/replication checks apply. The analysis goal is calibration of gene set p-values or FDR control rather than detection-rate comparison at a fixed FDR. Summary statistics were produced under a different enrichment regime (e.g. different tau1 or coverage rate), so baseline-scenario expected powers (98/26/0/8/26%) do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark empirical gene-set-enrichment power by simulating gene-level DE summary statistics under a known enrichment alternative (tau0=-2, tau1=0.5, CR=10%), running competing GSE methods (iDEA, fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA) on identical replicates, and calling significance at a fixed 5% FDR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Benchmark empirical gene-set-enrichment power by simulating gene-level DE summary statistics under a known enrichment alternative (tau0=-2, tau1=0.5, CR=10%), running competing GSE methods (iDEA, fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA) on identical replicates, and calling significance at a fixed 5% FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-seq data with no known ground truth about which gene sets are enriched — power cannot be computed and only calibration/replication checks apply. The analysis goal is calibration of gene set p-values or FDR control rather than detection-rate comparison at a fixed FDR. Summary statistics were produced under a different enrichment regime (e.g. different tau1 or coverage rate), so baseline-scenario expected powers (98/26/0/8/26%) do not apply.

skills.description: Use when quantifying significance of coordinated gene-set expression in a normalized expression matrix, and needing to classify gene sets as shifted (Median Exp) or overdispersed (L1) against random-set nulls.
skills.name: empirical-pvalue-computation-genesets
skills.search_text: empirical-pvalue-computation-genesets Use when quantifying significance of coordinated gene-set expression in a normalized expression matrix, and needing to classify gene sets as shifted (Median Exp) or overdispersed (L1) against random-set nulls. Input is raw (unnormalized) count data — rRoma requires normalized expression (e.g. edgeR cpm or DESeq2 vst) before PC1 and null-distribution statistics are meaningful The goal is differential expression per gene rather than gene-set/module-level activity quantification — this skill only tests coordinated gene-set behavior Expression data contain unimputed missing values and mice imputation is not desired — README recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 rROMA assesses gene-set activity significance empirically: for each module it computes the L1 statistic (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median of sample projections on PC1) via SVD-based PCA, then compares them against null distributions built from randomly generated gene sets of matched size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: rROMA assesses gene-set activity significance empirically: for each module it computes the L1 statistic (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median of sample projections on PC1) via SVD-based PCA, then compares them against null distributions built from randomly generated gene sets of matched size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unnormalized) count data — rRoma requires normalized expression (e.g. edgeR cpm or DESeq2 vst) before PC1 and null-distribution statistics are meaningful The goal is differential expression per gene rather than gene-set/module-level activity quantification — this skill only tests coordinated gene-set behavior Expression data contain unimputed missing values and mice imputation is not desired — README recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed

skills.description: Use when you have many gene signatures scored for phylogenetic autocorrelation (e.g., Geary's C on a KNN graph of cophenetic distances) and need multiple-testing-corrected significance before reporting which signatures track the phylogeny.
skills.name: empirical-pvalue-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: empirical-pvalue-fdr-correction Use when you have many gene signatures scored for phylogenetic autocorrelation (e.g., Geary's C on a KNN graph of cophenetic distances) and need multiple-testing-corrected significance before reporting which signatures track the phylogeny. skills.search_text: enrichment-odds-ratio-computation Use when testing whether sQTLs alter annotated splice-site strength more frequently or more strongly than non-sQTL variants, via PWM scores of reference vs alternative alleles and a 2×2 odds ratio at FDR 0.05. The question is about variants modifying RNA-binding protein binding motifs rather than splice-site strength — the paper reports these outnumber splice-site sequence changes Variants were never tested by sqtlseeker2-nf, so no sQTL vs non-sQTL partition exists and the 2×2 enrichment is undefined Variants do not overlap annotated donor/acceptor splice-site intervals (e.g. they act through intron retention hotspots or distal mechanisms) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the odds ratio of splice-site strength-altering variants among sQTLs versus non-sQTLs, using PWM-scored donor/acceptor alleles from sqtlseeker2-nf nominal output, to show that sQTLs preferentially modify splice site strength (63% vs 49%, OR = 1.79). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Computes the odds ratio of splice-site strength-altering variants among sQTLs versus non-sQTLs, using PWM-scored donor/acceptor alleles from sqtlseeker2-nf nominal output, to show that sQTLs preferentially modify splice site strength (63% vs 49%, OR = 1.79).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about variants modifying RNA-binding protein binding motifs rather than splice-site strength — the paper reports these outnumber splice-site sequence changes Variants were never tested by sqtlseeker2-nf, so no sQTL vs non-sQTL partition exists and the 2×2 enrichment is undefined Variants do not overlap annotated donor/acceptor splice-site intervals (e.g. they act through intron retention hotspots or distal mechanisms)

skills.description: Use when you have a gene list submitted to an enrichment tool (e.g. Enrichr against GO Biological Processes) and must decide which returned terms are significant, using adjusted p-value < 0.05 rather than raw p-values.
skills.name: enrichment-p-value-multiple-testing-interpretation
skills.search_text: enrichment-p-value-multiple-testing-interpretation Use when you have a gene list submitted to an enrichment tool (e.g. Enrichr against GO Biological Processes) and must decide which returned terms are significant, using adjusted p-value < 0.05 rather than raw p-values. The gene list still contains Excel date terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) or old gene symbols that have not been mapped to HGNC names — pathway databases will not recognize them and enrichment results will be void You need rank-based or set-level statistics (e.g. GSEA permutation testing) rather than over-representation adjusted p-values from Enrichr Raw unadjusted p-values are the quantity of interest for a bespoke sensitivity analysis — this skill deliberately discards them in favor of corrected values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interpret over-representation (pathway enrichment) results from tools like Enrichr by ranking terms on the multiple-testing-corrected p-value and retaining only terms with adjusted p < 0.05. In the Gene Updater study this defined which GO Biological Processes were deemed most affected by Excel date-conversion of gene names. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
skills.summary: Interpret over-representation (pathway enrichment) results from tools like Enrichr by ranking terms on the multiple-testing-corrected p-value and retaining only terms with adjusted p < 0.05. In the Gene Updater study this defined which GO Biological Processes were deemed most affected by Excel date-conversion of gene names.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list still contains Excel date terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) or old gene symbols that have not been mapped to HGNC names — pathway databases will not recognize them and enrichment results will be void You need rank-based or set-level statistics (e.g. GSEA permutation testing) rather than over-representation adjusted p-values from Enrichr Raw unadjusted p-values are the quantity of interest for a bespoke sensitivity analysis — this skill deliberately discards them in favor of corrected values

skills.description: Use when you have top-N gene lists (e.g., top 100 SSrGE-ranked eeSNV genes) from 5+ datasets and need a single cross-dataset pathway enrichment ranking, e.g., to reproduce Fig. 5-style KEGG pathway-gene graphs.
skills.name: enrichment-pvalue-aggregation
skills.search_text: enrichment-pvalue-aggregation Use when you have top-N gene lists (e.g., top 100 SSrGE-ranked eeSNV genes) from 5+ datasets and need a single cross-dataset pathway enrichment ranking, e.g., to reproduce Fig. 5-style KEGG pathway-gene graphs. You only have a single gene list and one enrichment run — a plain DAVID p-value ranking suffices without cross-dataset -log10(p) summation The genes are not derived from SSrGE eeSNV ranking or any ranked feature list (the skill assumes per-dataset top-N ranked genes as input) The annotation resource of interest is not KEGG via DAVID; other databases would need different p-value aggregation provenance Aggregate pathway enrichment evidence across multiple single-cell cancer datasets by submitting top-ranked eeSNV gene lists to DAVID, transforming KEGG p-values via -log10, and summing them per pathway to build a ranked bipartite pathway-gene network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Aggregate pathway enrichment evidence across multiple single-cell cancer datasets by submitting top-ranked eeSNV gene lists to DAVID, transforming KEGG p-values via -log10, and summing them per pathway to build a ranked bipartite pathway-gene network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single gene list and one enrichment run — a plain DAVID p-value ranking suffices without cross-dataset -log10(p) summation The genes are not derived from SSrGE eeSNV ranking or any ranked feature list (the skill assumes per-dataset top-N ranked genes as input) The annotation resource of interest is not KEGG via DAVID; other databases would need different p-value aggregation provenance

skills.description: Use when you have marker gene lists from two or more selection methods and need to determine which method's markers better recover known tissue/cell-type biology via enrichment q values against a reference gene set library.
skills.name: enrichment-result-comparison-across-marker-methods
skills.search_text: enrichment-result-comparison-across-marker-methods Use when you have marker gene lists from two or more selection methods and need to determine which method's markers better recover known tissue/cell-type biology via enrichment q values against a reference gene set library. You have only one marker set and no comparator — there is nothing to compare q values against, so enrichment alone is not this skill's purpose The target phenotypes have no meaningful overlap with the reference library's terms (e.g., mouse datasets like Tabula Muris against a HuBMAP human ASCT+B library) The goal is differential expression or deconvolution accuracy rather than external biological validation of marker discriminative power http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates marker sets selected by different algorithms (e.g., G-PC vs. decision trees) by running gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) against an independent curated gene set library (HuBMAP ASCT+B) and comparing adjusted q values across methods at term, tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Validates marker sets selected by different algorithms (e.g., G-PC vs. decision trees) by running gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) against an independent curated gene set library (HuBMAP ASCT+B) and comparing adjusted q values across methods at term, tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one marker set and no comparator — there is nothing to compare q values against, so enrichment alone is not this skill's purpose The target phenotypes have no meaningful overlap with the reference library's terms (e.g., mouse datasets like Tabula Muris against a HuBMAP human ASCT+B library) The goal is differential expression or deconvolution accuracy rather than external biological validation of marker discriminative power

skills.description: Use when per-cluster up/down-regulated marker gene lists (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon-style testing, e.g. PBMC3k) from SCALA's differential expression step are available and per-cluster GO/KEGG enrichment plus TF activity must be computed and exported as a table.
skills.name: enrichment-results-table-reporting
skills.search_text: enrichment-results-table-reporting Use when per-cluster up/down-regulated marker gene lists (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon-style testing, e.g. PBMC3k) from SCALA's differential expression step are available and per-cluster GO/KEGG enrichment plus TF activity must be computed and exported as a table. The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse for both scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq The input is already an enrichment result table (e.g. a pre-computed term/significance table) rather than marker gene lists, so re-running g:Profiler/FLAME is redundant A non-single-cell bulk expression dataset is provided and cluster-vs-rest marker identification has not been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Produces and reports the per-cluster functional enrichment table downstream of marker-gene identification in SCALA's scRNA-seq pipeline: up/down-regulated marker genes per SF cluster are tested for GO biological process and KEGG enrichment with g:Profiler (gprofiler2), deeper enrichment is run with FLAME, and cluster-level TF activity is scored with decoupleR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Produces and reports the per-cluster functional enrichment table downstream of marker-gene identification in SCALA's scRNA-seq pipeline: up/down-regulated marker genes per SF cluster are tested for GO biological process and KEGG enrichment with g:Profiler (gprofiler2), deeper enrichment is run with FLAME, and cluster-level TF activity is scored with decoupleR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse for both scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq The input is already an enrichment result table (e.g. a pre-computed term/significance table) rather than marker gene lists, so re-running g:Profiler/FLAME is redundant A non-single-cell bulk expression dataset is provided and cluster-vs-rest marker identification has not been performed

skills.description: Use when two gene-selection strategies (e.g., scRNA-seq-only top-1000 vs scRNA-seq+HiChIP Fisher-combined top-1000) must be compared via GO enrichment -log10(p) per subpopulation and term.

skills.search_text: enrichment-score-comparison-across-feature-sets Use when two gene-selection strategies (e.g., scRNA-seq-only top-1000 vs scRNA-seq+HiChIP Fisher-combined top-1000) must be compared via GO enrichment -log10(p) per subpopulation and term. Input lacks matched HiChIP loop data or subpopulation cluster assignments, so only a single gene-selection strategy is possible The question is deconvolution or coupled clustering itself (DC3's core task) rather than downstream GO enrichment comparison of alternative gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Quantitative comparison of GO enrichment significance (-log10 p-values) between gene sets selected by scRNA-seq p-values alone versus gene sets selected by Fisher-combined scRNA-seq + HiChIP p-values, to test whether adding HiChIP loop information improves subpopulation characterization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Quantitative comparison of GO enrichment significance (-log10 p-values) between gene sets selected by scRNA-seq p-values alone versus gene sets selected by Fisher-combined scRNA-seq + HiChIP p-values, to test whether adding HiChIP loop information improves subpopulation characterization.

skills.description: Use when you have two E.PAGE enrichment result objects (results$stats tibbles) from distinct gene lists and need to identify which enriched gene modules are common to both, comparing padj and fold enrichment per module.
skills.name: enrichment-statistics-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: enrichment-statistics-comparison-across-datasets Use when you have two E.PAGE enrichment result objects (results$stats tibbles) from distinct gene lists and need to identify which enriched gene modules are common to both, comparing padj and fold enrichment per module. You have a single gene list and only need per-list enrichment — run E.PAGE compute() directly rather than intersecting two result sets Your input is a Seurat object requiring clustering/differential expression first — use E.PAGE's Seurat input path instead of comparing pre-existing enrichment tables The enrichment outputs come from different annotation/database versions, making module names non-comparable for an inner_join http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Intersects statistically significant enrichment results (FDR-adjusted p-values from E.PAGE) computed for two disease query signatures to identify shared gene modules, as demonstrated for T1D (291 DE genes) and RA (229 DE genes) queries that both enriched infection-associated modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Intersects statistically significant enrichment results (FDR-adjusted p-values from E.PAGE) computed for two disease query signatures to identify shared gene modules, as demonstrated for T1D (291 DE genes) and RA (229 DE genes) queries that both enriched infection-associated modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single gene list and only need per-list enrichment — run E.PAGE compute() directly rather than intersecting two result sets Your input is a Seurat object requiring clustering/differential expression first — use E.PAGE's Seurat input path instead of comparing pre-existing enrichment tables The enrichment outputs come from different annotation/database versions, making module names non-comparable for an inner_join

skills.description: Use when a paper reports GO enrichment as a figure (e.g., GO BP terms among up- vs down-regulated cis-NAT partner genes) and the goal is a reproducible enrichment table rather than just a visual interpretation.
skills.name: enrichment-table-reproduction-from-figure
skills.search_text: enrichment-table-reproduction-from-figure Use when a paper reports GO enrichment as a figure (e.g., GO BP terms among up- vs down-regulated cis-NAT partner genes) and the goal is a reproducible enrichment table rather than just a visual interpretation. The input is not differentially expressed partner genes from a CCIVR-style cis-NAT table but raw RNA-seq counts — first run mapping (STAR), expression profiling (RSEM), and DESeq2 differential analysis to obtain fold_change/padj. The target figure reports non-GO enrichment (e.g., KEGG pathways or motif analysis), since this skill reproduces GOTERM_BP_FAT biological-process terms specifically. No matched background gene set exists; DAVID enrichment requires the Huh-7 dataset genes (or equivalent) as the background universe, and results are not interpretable without it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduce figure-level GO enrichment tables (e.g., Fig. 4C of Ohhata et al. 2022) by submitting gene lists extracted from CCIVR's differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes to DAVID v6.8 GOTERM_BP_FAT with a matched background, and writing a ranked top-15-per-condition CSV. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Reproduce figure-level GO enrichment tables (e.g., Fig. 4C of Ohhata et al. 2022) by submitting gene lists extracted from CCIVR's differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes to DAVID v6.8 GOTERM_BP_FAT with a matched background, and writing a ranked top-15-per-condition CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not differentially expressed partner genes from a CCIVR-style cis-NAT table but raw RNA-seq counts — first run mapping (STAR), expression profiling (RSEM), and DESeq2 differential analysis to obtain fold_change/padj. The target figure reports non-GO enrichment (e.g., KEGG pathways or motif analysis), since this skill reproduces GOTERM_BP_FAT biological-process terms specifically. No matched background gene set exists; DAVID enrichment requires the Huh-7 dataset genes (or equivalent) as the background universe, and results are not interpretable without it.

skills.search_text: enrichr-api-gene-list-query Use when a ranked or selected gene marker list (e.g., G-PC-selected HCA markers at coverage 8) needs external biological validation against a tissue/cell-type marker library such as HuBMAP ASCT+B, with q-value-based comparison to a competing method. The input is a raw expression matrix rather than an already-selected marker gene list; marker selection via GreedyPC at the desired coverage must happen first The validation target is a general functional ontology (e.g., GO/KEGG) rather than a tissue/cell-type marker library like HuBMAP ASCT+B The goal is differential-expression testing per gene rather than gene-set enrichment for a curated marker list http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates discriminative marker gene lists by submitting them to the Enrichr API via GSEApy against the HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022 library, then aggregating adjusted q values at tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels for method comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Validates discriminative marker gene lists by submitting them to the Enrichr API via GSEApy against the HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022 library, then aggregating adjusted q values at tissue, cell-type, and tissue/cell-type-pair levels for method comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw expression matrix rather than an already-selected marker gene list; marker selection via GreedyPC at the desired coverage must happen first The validation target is a general functional ontology (e.g., GO/KEGG) rather than a tissue/cell-type marker library like HuBMAP ASCT+B The goal is differential-expression testing per gene rather than gene-set enrichment for a curated marker list

skills.description: Use when a gene list (e.g. in silico knockout essential genes) must be interpreted for pathway enrichment beyond the metabolic model's own Recon3D_01 subSystems, via Enrichr/KEGG plus FerrDb annotation.
skills.name: enrichr-api-pathway-query
skills.search_text: enrichr-api-pathway-query Use when a gene list (e.g. in silico knockout essential genes) must be interpreted for pathway enrichment beyond the metabolic model's own Recon3D_01 subSystems, via Enrichr/KEGG plus FerrDb annotation. The question is restricted to pathways already captured by the Recon3D_01 subSystems of the context-specific model — the point of this skill is to find enrichment beyond subSystems. The gene list has not been filtered for essentiality or model context (e.g. raw DEG lists), so enrichments would not be attributable to context-specific essential genes. Single-gene 'enrichments' would be the dominant result (very short gene lists), which the workflow explicitly discards. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Submits context-specific essential gene lists (from SKO/DKO in silico knockouts of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung metabolic models) to the Enrichr API against the KEGG pathway library, using Recon3D_01 subSystems as the pathway background, then cross-references hits with FerrDb ferroptosis gene classifications. This surfaces pathways beyond those captured by the metabolic model's subSystems. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Submits context-specific essential gene lists (from SKO/DKO in silico knockouts of SARS-CoV-2-infected lung metabolic models) to the Enrichr API against the KEGG pathway library, using Recon3D_01 subSystems as the pathway background, then cross-references hits with FerrDb ferroptosis gene classifications. This surfaces pathways beyond those captured by the metabolic model's subSystems.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is restricted to pathways already captured by the Recon3D_01 subSystems of the context-specific model — the point of this skill is to find enrichment beyond subSystems. The gene list has not been filtered for essentiality or model context (e.g. raw DEG lists), so enrichments would not be attributable to context-specific essential genes. Single-gene 'enrichments' would be the dominant result (very short gene lists), which the workflow explicitly discards.

skills.description: Use when raw Ensembl GTF annotations must be transformed into CCIVR's required CSV input with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns before running cis-NAT extraction.

skills.search_text: ensembl-gene-annotation-parsing Use when raw Ensembl GTF annotations must be transformed into CCIVR's required CSV input with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns before running cis-NAT extraction. The annotation source is not gene-locational data from Ensembl or a comparable database — CCIVR depends on accurate gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in the databases. The goal is transcript-level or isoform-level cis-NAT analysis requiring assembled transcriptomes, which tools like NATpipe handle rather than gene-annotation-based CCIVR input. The input file already exists in the five-column CCIVR CSV format (e.g. the repository's data/Test_file.csv), so no parsing is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts Ensembl GTF gene annotations (e.g. Ensembl release 105/104, Ensembl plants release 52, Ensembl fungi release 52) into the five-column CSV format required by CCIVR for cis-NAT identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Converts Ensembl GTF gene annotations (e.g. Ensembl release 105/104, Ensembl plants release 52, Ensembl fungi release 52) into the five-column CSV format required by CCIVR for cis-NAT identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation source is not gene-locational data from Ensembl or a comparable database — CCIVR depends on accurate gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in the databases. The goal is transcript-level or isoform-level cis-NAT analysis requiring assembled transcriptomes, which tools like NATpipe handle rather than gene-annotation-based CCIVR input. The input file already exists in the five-column CCIVR CSV format (e.g. the repository's data/Test_file.csv), so no parsing is needed.

The input matrix already carries Ensembl gene IDs (e.g., genes already matched by contains(gene,'ENSMUSG')) — no mapping step is needed The downstream analysis is tool-agnostic with respect to identifier type (e.g., exploratory plotting in Seurat) and does not require Ensembl IDs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps gene names in a single-cell expression matrix to Ensembl gene IDs (e.g., ENSMUSG identifiers for mouse) so downstream tools such as SingleCellGGM and ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis can consume them, since these pipelines require or only support Ensembl gene IDs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813

skills.description: Use when reconstructing a directed, signed GRN from time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data and the raw A_t estimate is unstable because the sample mean and covariance must themselves be estimated.
skills.name: ensemble-aggregation-network-inference
skills.search_text: ensemble-aggregation-network-inference Use when reconstructing a directed, signed GRN from time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data and the raw A_t estimate is unstable because the sample mean and covariance must themselves be estimated. The goal is to infer a network maintaining a single cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition — such dense, single-time-point networks are outside COSLIR's scope. True longitudinal single-cell time series (temporal linkage across time points) is available and pseudo-time inference is not a concern, so moment-based bootstrapped estimation adds unnecessary machinery. Input data are not time-stamped cross-sectional samples from which first and second moments between consecutive time points can be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Stabilizes the COSLIR gene-gene interaction matrix estimator by bootstrapping the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression over resampled single cells, then keeping only entries that survive both a confidence threshold and a small-magnitude clipping threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Stabilizes the COSLIR gene-gene interaction matrix estimator by bootstrapping the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression over resampled single cells, then keeping only entries that survive both a confidence threshold and a small-magnitude clipping threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer a network maintaining a single cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition — such dense, single-time-point networks are outside COSLIR's scope. True longitudinal single-cell time series (temporal linkage across time points) is available and pseudo-time inference is not a concern, so moment-based bootstrapped estimation adds unnecessary machinery. Input data are not time-stamped cross-sectional samples from which first and second moments between consecutive time points can be computed.

skills.summary: Benchmark scTriangulate's decision-level mix-and-match integration against conventional consensus ensemble clustering (HGPA, MCLA, HBGF) using Homogeneity, Completeness, and V-Measure against a known ground truth or reference annotation.

skills.description: Use when you have multiple MCP path-capacity score matrices (2-, 3-, and 4-path) plus partial groundtruth interactions, and want the optimal ensemble weighting that maximizes AUPRC.
skills.name: ensemble-coefficient-grid-search
skills.search_text: ensemble-coefficient-grid-search Use when you have multiple MCP path-capacity score matrices (2-, 3-, and 4-path) plus partial groundtruth interactions, and want the optimal ensemble weighting that maximizes AUPRC.
