skills.search_text: entropy-based-differentiation-potential-quantification Use when you have per-cell alignment scores from Cytopath trajectory inference and need per-cell fate probabilities, differentiation potential, or identification of uncommitted vs. committed cell states. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference (and hence fate scoring) to be meaningful in that case When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probabilities with no discernible pattern), which the authors explicitly do not recommend for Cytopath When no per-cell alignment scores over multiple trajectories exist — entropy over a single-trajectory assignment is degenerate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies each cell's differentiation potential by normalizing Cytopath cell-to-trajectory alignment scores into fate probabilities and computing the Shannon entropy of the fate-probability vector, where low entropy signals a committed fate and high entropy an uncommitted, multi-potent state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Quantifies each cell's differentiation potential by normalizing Cytopath cell-to-trajectory alignment scores into fate probabilities and computing the Shannon entropy of the fate-probability vector, where low entropy signals a committed fate and high entropy an uncommitted, multi-potent state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect trajectory inference (and hence fate scoring) to be meaningful in that case When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probabilities with no discernible pattern), which the authors explicitly do not recommend for Cytopath When no per-cell alignment scores over multiple trajectories exist — entropy over a single-trajectory assignment is degenerate

skills.description: Use when selecting informative/variable genes from raw UMI count matrices (20,000 genes x 2,000 cells scale) prior to clustering, or when benchmarking feature-selection methods against HVG, Gini, M3Drop, SCTransform, Fano, or RaceID3.
skills.name: entropy-based-feature-scoring
skills.search_text: entropy-based-feature-scoring Use when selecting informative/variable genes from raw UMI count matrices (20,000 genes x 2,000 cells scale) prior to clustering, or when benchmarking feature-selection methods against HVG, Gini, M3Drop, SCTransform, Fano, or RaceID3. Gini-based scoring is preferred when the goal is rare cell-type identification; the article notes 'Gini is designed for rare cell-type identification' The 0.9 purity threshold is unsuitable for low-quality or continuous data — ROGUE thresholds must be derived from global ROGUE values instead Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the article lists this as unimplemented future work for ROGUE http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Scores genes for informativeness in scRNA-seq data using an entropy-based model (the S-E model implemented in the ROGUE package), fitting per-gene entropy curves to identify variable genes that enable accurate, sensitive cluster-purity assessment and benchmark-beating feature selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Scores genes for informativeness in scRNA-seq data using an entropy-based model (the S-E model implemented in the ROGUE package), fitting per-gene entropy curves to identify variable genes that enable accurate, sensitive cluster-purity assessment and benchmark-beating feature selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gini-based scoring is preferred when the goal is rare cell-type identification; the article notes 'Gini is designed for rare cell-type identification' The 0.9 purity threshold is unsuitable for low-quality or continuous data — ROGUE thresholds must be derived from global ROGUE values instead Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the article lists this as unimplemented future work for ROGUE

skills.description: Use when a log-normalized cells-by-genes scRNA-seq matrix needs a small set of feature (differentially expressed) genes tied to cell types, alongside dimensionality reduction, rather than generic highly-variable-gene selection.
skills.name: entropy-based-feature-selection
skills.search_text: entropy-based-feature-selection Use when a log-normalized cells-by-genes scRNA-seq matrix needs a small set of feature (differentially expressed) genes tied to cell types, alongside dimensionality reduction, rather than generic highly-variable-gene selection. The input is already a feature/DE gene table or the goal is purely visualization without gene selection — a plain embedding tool (t-SNE, UMAP) alone would suffice The dataset is a Splatter-simulated matrix, where the gene-selection step should use 500 instead of 1000 top variable genes as the restricted input Only global hierarchical structure preservation is required and no cell-type-associated feature genes are needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Select feature genes in scRNA-seq data by ranking genes on their averaged entropy contribution across an ensemble of weak learners run by the EDGE endr function, and apply a μ − 1.5 × σ cutoff on the averaged entropy values to define the feature-gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Select feature genes in scRNA-seq data by ranking genes on their averaged entropy contribution across an ensemble of weak learners run by the EDGE endr function, and apply a μ − 1.5 × σ cutoff on the averaged entropy values to define the feature-gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/DE gene table or the goal is purely visualization without gene selection — a plain embedding tool (t-SNE, UMAP) alone would suffice The dataset is a Splatter-simulated matrix, where the gene-selection step should use 500 instead of 1000 top variable genes as the restricted input Only global hierarchical structure preservation is required and no cell-type-associated feature genes are needed

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq clusters must be assessed for transcriptomic homogeneity, i.e., per-cluster S_RNA values are needed (optionally to be combined with an ADT score via geometric mean) for cluster purity assessment.
skills.name: entropy-based-transcriptome-purity-scoring
skills.search_text: entropy-based-transcriptome-purity-scoring Use when CITE-seq clusters must be assessed for transcriptomic homogeneity, i.e., per-cluster S_RNA values are needed (optionally to be combined with an ADT score via geometric mean) for cluster purity assessment. Datasets are massive with a very high number of ADT features — the article notes LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) and failed on 170K cells with 228 ADT features where Seurat 4 succeeded The K parameter for the ROGUE score cannot be set appropriately for the sequencing technology used, since its value is not specified in the article text Input clusters already come from a unimodal scRNA-seq-only workflow where ADT integration and modality-combined purity are not relevant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes an entropy-based transcriptome purity score (S_RNA) per cell cluster using the ROGUE formula, as implemented in the LinQ-View CITE-seq purity module, to quantify whether a cluster is a uniform single-cell population. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Computes an entropy-based transcriptome purity score (S_RNA) per cell cluster using the ROGUE formula, as implemented in the LinQ-View CITE-seq purity module, to quantify whether a cluster is a uniform single-cell population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are massive with a very high number of ADT features — the article notes LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) and failed on 170K cells with 228 ADT features where Seurat 4 succeeded The K parameter for the ROGUE score cannot be set appropriately for the sequencing technology used, since its value is not specified in the article text Input clusters already come from a unimodal scRNA-seq-only workflow where ADT integration and modality-combined purity are not relevant

skills.description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq target cells with a pre-trained source classifier and you need a per-cell uncertainty score in [0,1] to detect novel cell types without source data.
skills.name: entropy-confidence-classifier-scoring
skills.search_text: entropy-confidence-classifier-scoring Use when annotating scRNA-seq target cells with a pre-trained source classifier and you need a per-cell uncertainty score in [0,1] to detect novel cell types without source data. Source raw data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g., Seurat v3 anchoring or scArches surgery) is preferred over a source-free scheme No pre-trained classifier outputs (main + two auxiliary probability vectors) exist yet — the scoring requires all three classifiers The goal is a final cell-type label rather than an uncertainty score; E-scores are an intermediate signal meant to feed bimodality tests and the manifold-mixup threshold, not a standalone annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes scEMAIL's per-cell E-score by combining three complementary uncertainty indices — entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) — derived from a pre-trained source model's main and two auxiliary classifier outputs, enabling novel cell-type perception in scRNA-seq target data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Computes scEMAIL's per-cell E-score by combining three complementary uncertainty indices — entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) — derived from a pre-trained source model's main and two auxiliary classifier outputs, enabling novel cell-type perception in scRNA-seq target data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source raw data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g., Seurat v3 anchoring or scArches surgery) is preferred over a source-free scheme No pre-trained classifier outputs (main + two auxiliary probability vectors) exist yet — the scoring requires all three classifiers The goal is a final cell-type label rather than an uncertainty score; E-scores are an intermediate signal meant to feed bimodality tests and the manifold-mixup threshold, not a standalone annotation

skills.description: Use when starting from a normalized gene-expression count table (e.g. DREAM 4 time-series, units-to-tens of time points) and you need to rank gene-gene relationships by mutual information to seed GRN inference.
skills.name: entropy-estimation-from-gene-expression
skills.search_text: entropy-estimation-from-gene-expression Use when starting from a normalized gene-expression count table (e.g. DREAM 4 time-series, units-to-tens of time points) and you need to rank gene-gene relationships by mutual information to seed GRN inference. You need the refined, high-confidence GRN: MI-only inference yields low sensitivity (0.38) and requires downstream refinement via TFBM prediction and curated database interactions The organism's genome/GenBank file is unavailable and you require refinement steps, which cannot be performed without additional genome knowledge You must distinguish transcription factor from target gene labels from single-cell data without a time series — the MSD-based time-lag orientation depends on adjacent time points http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Compute gene-wise entropy, joint entropy, and pairwise mutual information over a discretized RNA-Seq count table to propose candidate regulatory edges for an initial GRN, as implemented in Augusta's first inference stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Compute gene-wise entropy, joint entropy, and pairwise mutual information over a discretized RNA-Seq count table to propose candidate regulatory edges for an initial GRN, as implemented in Augusta's first inference stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the refined, high-confidence GRN: MI-only inference yields low sensitivity (0.38) and requires downstream refinement via TFBM prediction and curated database interactions The organism's genome/GenBank file is unavailable and you require refinement steps, which cannot be performed without additional genome knowledge You must distinguish transcription factor from target gene labels from single-cell data without a time series — the MSD-based time-lag orientation depends on adjacent time points

skills.description: Use when raw somatic coding mutation data (e.g. COSMIC v79) must be converted into a per-gene/transcript feature matrix with entropy and frequency statistics for mutation types, for driver gene classification or feature-importance analysis.
skills.name: entropy-feature-computation
skills.search_text: entropy-feature-computation Use when raw somatic coding mutation data (e.g. COSMIC v79) must be converted into a per-gene/transcript feature matrix with entropy and frequency statistics for mutation types, for driver gene classification or feature-importance analysis. A feature matrix already exists (e.g. the published FeatureMat.tsv) and the goal is only to train/predict with cTaG via TSG_OG_Feat_final.py Working with Tokheim et al. data, where missense and frameshift entropy and frequency could not be calculated, limiting comparability The analysis requires background mutation rate methods (e.g. MutSigCV) rather than mutation-type feature profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes entropy and frequency features of different COSMIC mutation types per gene, combined with ratio-metric features (including PolyPhen2 HiFI/MiFI/LoFI missense bins) to build the 37-feature matrix that cTaG uses to classify genes as TSGs or OGs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Computes entropy and frequency features of different COSMIC mutation types per gene, combined with ratio-metric features (including PolyPhen2 HiFI/MiFI/LoFI missense bins) to build the 37-feature matrix that cTaG uses to classify genes as TSGs or OGs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A feature matrix already exists (e.g. the published FeatureMat.tsv) and the goal is only to train/predict with cTaG via TSG_OG_Feat_final.py Working with Tokheim et al. data, where missense and frameshift entropy and frequency could not be calculated, limiting comparability The analysis requires background mutation rate methods (e.g. MutSigCV) rather than mutation-type feature profiles

skills.description: Use when single-cell clustering results must be checked against a developmental trajectory: e.g. testing whether label entropy is high at transition states and decreases with differentiation pseudotime.
skills.name: entropy-pseudotime-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: entropy-pseudotime-correlation-analysis Use when single-cell clustering results must be checked against a developmental trajectory: e.g. testing whether label entropy is high at transition states and decreases with differentiation pseudotime. Data contains only one cluster — Monte Carlo internal validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty when every data point receives one label Clustering was performed on raw high-dimensional features without nonlinear dimensionality reduction (UMAP/t-SNE/PHATE), since the method is sensitive to the curse of dimensionality http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates Forest Fire Clustering's point-wise label entropies as a trajectory read-out by correlating cluster_obj.entropy_list with pseudotime in simulated (Splatter) and PBMC (scanpy diffusion pseudotime) scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Validates Forest Fire Clustering's point-wise label entropies as a trajectory read-out by correlating cluster_obj.entropy_list with pseudotime in simulated (Splatter) and PBMC (scanpy diffusion pseudotime) scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains only one cluster — Monte Carlo internal validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty when every data point receives one label Clustering was performed on raw high-dimensional features without nonlinear dimensionality reduction (UMAP/t-SNE/PHATE), since the method is sensitive to the curse of dimensionality

skills.description: Use when a scHiCDiff DCI results data frame is available (bin_1/bin_2 pairs with pvalue.adj.FDR) and the goal is to characterize detected DCIs by epigenetic mark changes and GO enrichment, e.g. Astro vs Endo.
skills.name: epigenetic-mark-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: epigenetic-mark-enrichment-analysis Use when a scHiCDiff DCI results data frame is available (bin_1/bin_2 pairs with pvalue.adj.FDR) and the goal is to characterize detected DCIs by epigenetic mark changes and GO enrichment, e.g. Astro vs Endo. When no scHiCDiff DCI detection has been performed yet — this skill operates on the DCI results data frame, not raw single-cell Hi-C contact matrices When comparing conditions other than the two-cell-type contrast for which differential epigenetic mark tracks exist (e.g. no Astro/Endo epigenetic data available), since the mark-change test requires matched tracks http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 Downstream functional annotation of differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) detected by scHiCDiff: overlapping significant DCI bins with differential epigenetic mark tracks and running Gene Ontology enrichment on DCI-associated genes, as demonstrated for the Astro vs Endo single-cell Hi-C comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Downstream functional annotation of differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) detected by scHiCDiff: overlapping significant DCI bins with differential epigenetic mark tracks and running Gene Ontology enrichment on DCI-associated genes, as demonstrated for the Astro vs Endo single-cell Hi-C comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no scHiCDiff DCI detection has been performed yet — this skill operates on the DCI results data frame, not raw single-cell Hi-C contact matrices When comparing conditions other than the two-cell-type contrast for which differential epigenetic mark tracks exist (e.g. no Astro/Endo epigenetic data available), since the mark-change test requires matched tracks

skills.description: Use when summarystatistic-level eQTL data (z-scores or betas+SEs) for many tissues, reference LD matrices, and a question of tissue sharing or GWAS target-tissue prioritization are available, especially when loci may harbor multiple causal variants.
skills.name: eqtl-colocalization-analysis
skills.search_text: eqtl-colocalization-analysis Use when summarystatistic-level eQTL data (z-scores or betas+SEs) for many tissues, reference LD matrices, and a question of tissue sharing or GWAS target-tissue prioritization are available, especially when loci may harbor multiple causal variants. Loci whose trait effects are mediated by coding variants without eQTL effects — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences between datasets (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix Effect-size matrices with missing data, as CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Jointly fine-map and colocalize cis-eQTL signals across many tissues using CAFEH, a Bayesian method that accommodates allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) and LD structure, to quantify whether eQTL effects are tissue specific or shared and to prioritize target tissues for GWAS loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Jointly fine-map and colocalize cis-eQTL signals across many tissues using CAFEH, a Bayesian method that accommodates allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) and LD structure, to quantify whether eQTL effects are tissue specific or shared and to prioritize target tissues for GWAS loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose trait effects are mediated by coding variants without eQTL effects — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences between datasets (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix Effect-size matrices with missing data, as CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets

skills.description: Use when a peak-gene (locus-gene) inference method must be quantitatively benchmarked against eQTL-supported ground-truth pairs on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data with multiple samples per dataset.
skills.name: eqtl-groundtruth-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: eqtl-groundtruth-benchmark-evaluation Use when a peak-gene (locus-gene) inference method must be quantitatively benchmarked against eQTL-supported ground-truth pairs on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data with multiple samples per dataset. For pure locus-gene discovery rather than method benchmarking — this skill requires eQTL ground-truth data and is an evaluation, not a discovery, workflow When the input lacks paired single-cell multimodal data from a dynamic process (e.g. differentiation), since pseudotime-oriented DAGs cannot be constructed and Granger causal scores are undefined When only total-variant-to-nearest-gene annotation is needed — distal locus-gene link inference and its benchmarking are unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark protocol for validating inferred noncoding peak-gene links by scoring candidate pairs against significant eQTLs from the eQTL Catalogue and comparing methods via pair-level AUROC across multimodal single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for validating inferred noncoding peak-gene links by scoring candidate pairs against significant eQTLs from the eQTL Catalogue and comparing methods via pair-level AUROC across multimodal single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: For pure locus-gene discovery rather than method benchmarking — this skill requires eQTL ground-truth data and is an evaluation, not a discovery, workflow When the input lacks paired single-cell multimodal data from a dynamic process (e.g. differentiation), since pseudotime-oriented DAGs cannot be constructed and Granger causal scores are undefined When only total-variant-to-nearest-gene annotation is needed — distal locus-gene link inference and its benchmarking are unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether CAFEH fine-mapped credible-set variants are enriched in active regulatory elements (Roadmap chromHMM) and a size-balanced, gene-matched lead-eQTL background is needed for comparison.
skills.name: eqtl-lead-variant-background-matching
skills.search_text: eqtl-lead-variant-background-matching Use when evaluating whether CAFEH fine-mapped credible-set variants are enriched in active regulatory elements (Roadmap chromHMM) and a size-balanced, gene-matched lead-eQTL background is needed for comparison. When LD matrices differ greatly between studies (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so colocalization/fine-mapping inference feeding the credible sets may be biased When loci are likely mediated by coding variants, which may not demonstrate eQTL effects and therefore cannot be explored with CAFEH When the effect-size matrix has missing data — CAFEH does not handle missing data and implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Constructs a matched background set of minimum-p-value lead eQTL variants so that CAFEH credible-set variants can be tested (via Fisher's exact test) for enrichment in Roadmap active regulatory elements, distinguishing causal fine-mapping signal from ordinary top-eQTL association. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Constructs a matched background set of minimum-p-value lead eQTL variants so that CAFEH credible-set variants can be tested (via Fisher's exact test) for enrichment in Roadmap active regulatory elements, distinguishing causal fine-mapping signal from ordinary top-eQTL association.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When LD matrices differ greatly between studies (e.g., ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so colocalization/fine-mapping inference feeding the credible sets may be biased When loci are likely mediated by coding variants, which may not demonstrate eQTL effects and therefore cannot be explored with CAFEH When the effect-size matrix has missing data — CAFEH does not handle missing data and implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets

skills.description: Use when you have SNP genotype data plus RNA-seq counts from (possibly related) individuals across conditions (e.g. infection), and need per-SNP–gene eQTL effect sizes, P-values, and FDR calls rather than plain DEG calls.
skills.name: eqtl-mapping-genotype-expression
skills.search_text: eqtl-mapping-genotype-expression Use when you have SNP genotype data plus RNA-seq counts from (possibly related) individuals across conditions (e.g. infection), and need per-SNP–gene eQTL effect sizes, P-values, and FDR calls rather than plain DEG calls. Your goal is differential expression between conditions without genotype testing — kimma's kmFit, or limma/dream comparisons, cover that instead SNPs cannot be mapped to genes (no dat_map linking genotypeID to geneID), so per-pair eQTL models cannot be constructed Samples are unrelated and no kinship matrix is available, so the kinship-covariance random effect central to this model is not estimable http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps expression quantitative trait loci by fitting each SNP–gene pair with kimma's kmFit_eQTL linear mixed model that includes a genotype-by-infection-condition interaction term and a kinship covariance random effect, then calling pairs significant at FDR < 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Maps expression quantitative trait loci by fitting each SNP–gene pair with kimma's kmFit_eQTL linear mixed model that includes a genotype-by-infection-condition interaction term and a kinship covariance random effect, then calling pairs significant at FDR < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is differential expression between conditions without genotype testing — kimma's kmFit, or limma/dream comparisons, cover that instead SNPs cannot be mapped to genes (no dat_map linking genotypeID to geneID), so per-pair eQTL models cannot be constructed Samples are unrelated and no kinship matrix is available, so the kinship-covariance random effect central to this model is not estimable

skills.description: Use when you have peak-gene scores from one or more causal-inference configurations (GrID-Net, linear Granger, correlational baselines) on the SHARE-seq mouse skin dataset and need a quantitative gold-standard comparison against significant eQTLs from the eQTL Catalogue.
skills.name: eqtl-retrieval-auroc-benchmarking
skills.search_text: eqtl-retrieval-auroc-benchmarking Use when you have peak-gene scores from one or more causal-inference configurations (GrID-Net, linear Granger, correlational baselines) on the SHARE-seq mouse skin dataset and need a quantitative gold-standard comparison against significant eQTLs from the eQTL Catalogue. The dataset has no matching tissue eQTL catalog available to serve as a perturbation-mimicking gold standard (GrID-Net associations are causal hypotheses validated only by such cross-referencing). You want to validate predictions against physical chromatin contacts instead of genetic perturbation evidence — the paper used 5C data for SHARE-seq only because mouse skin Hi-C was unavailable, and that is a different evaluation. The biological system is not a dynamic differentiation process, so no pseudotemporal DAG (and thus no GrID-Net or branch decomposition) can be constructed for the configurations being benchmarked. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark locus-gene causal-scoring methods (e.g., GrID-Net on a cell-state DAG versus linear Granger baselines on full trajectories or individual branches) by how well their scores retrieve significant skin eQTLs (P < 1e-3) from the eQTL Catalogue, evaluated via AUROC of eQTL retrieval using a distance-aware logistic regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Benchmark locus-gene causal-scoring methods (e.g., GrID-Net on a cell-state DAG versus linear Granger baselines on full trajectories or individual branches) by how well their scores retrieve significant skin eQTLs (P < 1e-3) from the eQTL Catalogue, evaluated via AUROC of eQTL retrieval using a distance-aware logistic regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no matching tissue eQTL catalog available to serve as a perturbation-mimicking gold standard (GrID-Net associations are causal hypotheses validated only by such cross-referencing). You want to validate predictions against physical chromatin contacts instead of genetic perturbation evidence — the paper used 5C data for SHARE-seq only because mouse skin Hi-C was unavailable, and that is a different evaluation. The biological system is not a dynamic differentiation process, so no pseudotemporal DAG (and thus no GrID-Net or branch decomposition) can be constructed for the configurations being benchmarked.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking fine-mapping/colocalization methods on summary statistics and you need simulated loci with a controlled number of causal variants and signal strengths.
skills.name: eqtl-summary-statistics-simulation
skills.search_text: eqtl-summary-statistics-simulation Use when benchmarking fine-mapping/colocalization methods on summary statistics and you need simulated loci with a controlled number of causal variants and signal strengths. You have individual-level genotypes/phenotypes rather than summary statistics — CAFEH genotype mode takes -X/-Y directly instead Your loci have large LD differences between studies (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The causal variants may be missing from some tested datasets — CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Simulate multi-trait eQTL summary statistics (LD matrices, effect sizes, standard errors, sample sizes) across allelic-heterogeneity grids to benchmark CAFEH against CAVIAR, FINEMAP, SuSiE, and eCAVIAR on fine-mapping and colocalization power/FDP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Simulate multi-trait eQTL summary statistics (LD matrices, effect sizes, standard errors, sample sizes) across allelic-heterogeneity grids to benchmark CAFEH against CAVIAR, FINEMAP, SuSiE, and eCAVIAR on fine-mapping and colocalization power/FDP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have individual-level genotypes/phenotypes rather than summary statistics — CAFEH genotype mode takes -X/-Y directly instead Your loci have large LD differences between studies (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The causal variants may be missing from some tested datasets — CAFEH does not handle missing data in the effect size matrix

skills.description: Use when GrID-Net Granger scores for peak-gene pairs need distance-aware calibration before linking variants to genes, and an eQTL dataset (e.g., SHARE-seq skin) is available to define positive pairs.
skills.name: eqtl-trained-logistic-model-training
skills.search_text: eqtl-trained-logistic-model-training Use when GrID-Net Granger scores for peak-gene pairs need distance-aware calibration before linking variants to genes, and an eQTL dataset (e.g., SHARE-seq skin) is available to define positive pairs. Peak-gene links are meant to be purely correlational or distance-independent — nearest-gene assignment is adequate and no distal interactions are of interest No eQTL or perturbation-derived positive training set is available for the tissue/assay, since the logistic model requires labeled regulatory pairs to fit Candidate pairs were not filtered by the required thresholds (genes in >= 1% of cells, peaks in >= 0.1% of cells, peaks within the distance window), in which case the training distribution is invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Trains a logistic regression that combines GrID-Net Granger causal scores with log genomic distance to model distance-dependent regulatory effects, using significant SHARE-seq mouse skin eQTL peak-gene pairs (P < 1e-3) as positive training labels; the fitted model is then used to re-rank candidate peak-gene pairs when linking fine-mapped SCZ variants to genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Trains a logistic regression that combines GrID-Net Granger causal scores with log genomic distance to model distance-dependent regulatory effects, using significant SHARE-seq mouse skin eQTL peak-gene pairs (P < 1e-3) as positive training labels; the fitted model is then used to re-rank candidate peak-gene pairs when linking fine-mapped SCZ variants to genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peak-gene links are meant to be purely correlational or distance-independent — nearest-gene assignment is adequate and no distal interactions are of interest No eQTL or perturbation-derived positive training set is available for the tissue/assay, since the logistic model requires labeled regulatory pairs to fit Candidate pairs were not filtered by the required thresholds (genes in >= 1% of cells, peaks in >= 0.1% of cells, peaks within the distance window), in which case the training distribution is invalid

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics and pre-trained eQTL weights (per-gene SNP effect sizes from a reference panel) are available and the goal is to identify genes whose genetically regulated expression associates with a trait.
skills.name: eqtl-weight-based-grex-association-testing
skills.search_text: eqtl-weight-based-grex-association-testing Use when GWAS summary statistics and pre-trained eQTL weights (per-gene SNP effect sizes from a reference panel) are available and the goal is to identify genes whose genetically regulated expression associates with a trait. Only individual-level reference expression data are available and the goal is FUSION-style TWAS with a small reference (OTTERS is designed for summary-level reference data) The aim is to infer the direction of gene-phenotype associations — OTTERS cannot provide direction, only the sign of per-method TWAS Z-scores The question requires trans-eQTL effects — OTTERS only considers cis-eQTL effects http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Performs TWAS Stage II gene-based association testing: impute genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) in GWAS data using trained eQTL weights (from P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS, or FUSION) and test the imputed GReX–phenotype association, with OTTERS aggregating per-method p values into an ACAT-O omnibus test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Performs TWAS Stage II gene-based association testing: impute genetically regulated gene expression (GReX) in GWAS data using trained eQTL weights (from P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS, or FUSION) and test the imputed GReX–phenotype association, with OTTERS aggregating per-method p values into an ACAT-O omnibus test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only individual-level reference expression data are available and the goal is FUSION-style TWAS with a small reference (OTTERS is designed for summary-level reference data) The aim is to infer the direction of gene-phenotype associations — OTTERS cannot provide direction, only the sign of per-method TWAS Z-scores The question requires trans-eQTL effects — OTTERS only considers cis-eQTL effects

skills.description: Use when eQTL summary statistics (CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N) plus an LD reference panel are available but individual-level genotype/expression data are not, and gene-level eQTL weights are needed for TWAS.
skills.name: eqtl-weight-training-from-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: eqtl-weight-training-from-summary-statistics Use when eQTL summary statistics (CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N) plus an LD reference panel are available but individual-level genotype/expression data are not, and gene-level eQTL weights are needed for TWAS. Individual-level reference genotype and expression data are available and desired — the article benchmarks FUSION trained on individual-level data as the alternative baseline Trans-eQTL effects are required — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects Reference data are from a non-European population — available eQTL summary statistics are mainly European, and cross-population TWAS is listed as ongoing work http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 TWAS Stage I skill for training GReX imputation models (eQTL weights) from summary-level eQTL reference data (e.g. eQTLGen, n=31,684) using four summary-data-based PRS methods — P+T with LD clumping, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS — instead of individual-level reference expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: TWAS Stage I skill for training GReX imputation models (eQTL weights) from summary-level eQTL reference data (e.g. eQTLGen, n=31,684) using four summary-data-based PRS methods — P+T with LD clumping, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS — instead of individual-level reference expression data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual-level reference genotype and expression data are available and desired — the article benchmarks FUSION trained on individual-level data as the alternative baseline Trans-eQTL effects are required — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects Reference data are from a non-European population — available eQTL summary statistics are mainly European, and cross-population TWAS is listed as ongoing work

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data and a prior knowledge network (e.g., KEGG pathways like hsa00010/hsa00020) are available and executable Boolean regulatory rules are needed, especially when multiple rule sets can explain the data.
skills.name: equivalent-rule-set-computation
skills.search_text: equivalent-rule-set-computation Use when scRNA-seq data and a prior knowledge network (e.g., KEGG pathways like hsa00010/hsa00020) are available and executable Boolean regulatory rules are needed, especially when multiple rule sets can explain the data. Only a single best-fit rule set is acceptable and rule-set degeneracy cannot be tolerated (the method explicitly returns an ERS because multiple rule sets explain the data equally well) The data are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell — use the original BONITA method, on which scBONITA builds No prior knowledge network topology is available; rule inference is topology-constrained (KEGG or GRAPHML networks are required inputs) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 scBONITA's rule-determination stage: a genetic algorithm finds a minimum-error set of sign-compatible canalyzing Boolean rules per KEGG network node from scRNA-seq data, refined by node-wise local search, yielding an equivalent rule set (ERS) with a per-node uncertainty factor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: scBONITA's rule-determination stage: a genetic algorithm finds a minimum-error set of sign-compatible canalyzing Boolean rules per KEGG network node from scRNA-seq data, refined by node-wise local search, yielding an equivalent rule set (ERS) with a per-node uncertainty factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single best-fit rule set is acceptable and rule-set degeneracy cannot be tolerated (the method explicitly returns an ERS because multiple rule sets explain the data equally well) The data are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell — use the original BONITA method, on which scBONITA builds No prior knowledge network topology is available; rule inference is topology-constrained (KEGG or GRAPHML networks are required inputs)

skills.description: Use when bulk tumour samples (e.g. TCGA-BRCA) have a continuous pseudotime score from PhenoPath plus overall survival time/status and ER status, and the goal is to test pseudotime as an independent survival predictor.
skills.name: er-status-stratified-survival-modeling
skills.search_text: er-status-stratified-survival-modeling Use when bulk tumour samples (e.g. TCGA-BRCA) have a continuous pseudotime score from PhenoPath plus overall survival time/status and ER status, and the goal is to test pseudotime as an independent survival predictor. Pseudotimes were inferred jointly across ER+ and ER− tumours with ER only as a covariate rather than per-stratum trajectories — then a stratified design is not motivated The endpoint is not time-to-event survival data (e.g. only binary responder status) — coxph with Surv() is the wrong model class Input is single-cell data: the article applies PhenoPath pseudotime to bulk TCGA cohorts for survival association, not to individual cells http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Tests whether PhenoPath-inferred pseudotemporal progression (e.g. the TCGA-BRCA angiogenesis trajectory) is prognostic for overall survival using a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by ER status, adjusted for clinical covariates such as stage and age. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Tests whether PhenoPath-inferred pseudotemporal progression (e.g. the TCGA-BRCA angiogenesis trajectory) is prognostic for overall survival using a Cox proportional hazards model stratified by ER status, adjusted for clinical covariates such as stage and age.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pseudotimes were inferred jointly across ER+ and ER− tumours with ER only as a covariate rather than per-stratum trajectories — then a stratified design is not motivated The endpoint is not time-to-event survival data (e.g. only binary responder status) — coxph with Surv() is the wrong model class Input is single-cell data: the article applies PhenoPath pseudotime to bulk TCGA cohorts for survival association, not to individual cells

skills.description: Use when tall-format melted scRNA-seq expression data (CSV or Parquet) has been loaded in Spark and per-cell/per-gene QC metrics — percent ERCC, percent mitochondrial, counts, and dropouts — are needed before filtering.
skills.name: ercc-mitochondrial-fraction-annotation
skills.search_text: ercc-mitochondrial-fraction-annotation Use when tall-format melted scRNA-seq expression data (CSV or Parquet) has been loaded in Spark and per-cell/per-gene QC metrics — percent ERCC, percent mitochondrial, counts, and dropouts — are needed before filtering. Input is raw uncounted sequencing output (e.g. FASTQ or Illumina HiSeq raw data) rather than a melted count matrix — the pipeline expects .csv or .parquet input Data is already in wide matrix form and has not been melted to tall format; data melting must precede quality summary generation The analysis is not scRNA-seq downstream processing (e.g. multi-omics CITE-seq/scATAC-seq) — such Spark-based pipelines are not yet developed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 In scSPARKL's Stage-2 quality control, grouped aggregations over the melted tall-format expression DataFrame derive per-cell (Θ1) and per-gene (Θ2) quality summary matrices, including percent ERCC and percent mitochondrial reads per cell, saved as Parquet files for downstream `data_filter()` thresholding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: In scSPARKL's Stage-2 quality control, grouped aggregations over the melted tall-format expression DataFrame derive per-cell (Θ1) and per-gene (Θ2) quality summary matrices, including percent ERCC and percent mitochondrial reads per cell, saved as Parquet files for downstream `data_filter()` thresholding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw uncounted sequencing output (e.g. FASTQ or Illumina HiSeq raw data) rather than a melted count matrix — the pipeline expects .csv or .parquet input Data is already in wide matrix form and has not been melted to tall format; data melting must precede quality summary generation The analysis is not scRNA-seq downstream processing (e.g. multi-omics CITE-seq/scATAC-seq) — such Spark-based pipelines are not yet developed

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation method (e.g., scImpute on raw read counts with drop_thre = 0.5) recovers true expression levels masked by dropout events, using ERCC spike-ins with known concentrations as ground truth.
skills.name: ercc-spike-in-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: ercc-spike-in-correlation-analysis Use when evaluating whether an imputation method (e.g., scImpute on raw read counts with drop_thre = 0.5) recovers true expression levels masked by dropout events, using ERCC spike-ins with known concentrations as ground truth. The dataset lacks ERCC spike-ins with known concentrations, so no ground-truth correlation can be computed Only a filtered gene subset is available — scImpute recommends applying it to the whole-genome count matrix to ensure robust dropout identification The analysis goal is clustering, differential expression, or time-series analysis downstream of imputation rather than quantifying imputation accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies dropout-recovery quality of scImpute imputation by computing per-cell Pearson correlations between observed ERCC spike-in read counts (57 transcripts in the GSE60361 mouse somatosensory cortex dataset, 3005 cells) and their known concentrations, before vs. after imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Quantifies dropout-recovery quality of scImpute imputation by computing per-cell Pearson correlations between observed ERCC spike-in read counts (57 transcripts in the GSE60361 mouse somatosensory cortex dataset, 3005 cells) and their known concentrations, before vs. after imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks ERCC spike-ins with known concentrations, so no ground-truth correlation can be computed Only a filtered gene subset is available — scImpute recommends applying it to the whole-genome count matrix to ensure robust dropout identification The analysis goal is clustering, differential expression, or time-series analysis downstream of imputation rather than quantifying imputation accuracy

skills.description: Use when benchmarking droplet scRNA-seq conversion efficiency or linearity using ERCC spike-ins: ERCC FASTQ from SRA SRP073767 is available and conversion efficiency, UMI-vs-molecule Pearson r, and CV2 must be recomputed.
skills.name: ercc-spike-in-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: ercc-spike-in-sensitivity-analysis Use when benchmarking droplet scRNA-seq conversion efficiency or linearity using ERCC spike-ins: ERCC FASTQ from SRA SRP073767 is available and conversion efficiency, UMI-vs-molecule Pearson r, and CV2 must be recomputed. Input data are whole-transcriptome cell FASTQs needing genome alignment (hg19/mm10), not ERCC-only spike-in benchmarking runs. The goal is gene expression quantification for biological samples (e.g., 68k PBMC profiling) rather than instrument sensitivity/linearity validation with synthetic RNAs. A gene-barcode UMI count matrix already exists for the ERCC runs and only downstream analysis, not UMI validity filtering and counting, is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies how efficiently the 10x Genomics droplet (GemCode) scRNA-seq system converts ERCC synthetic spike-in RNA molecules into detected UMI counts, by aligning Read1 cDNA inserts to an ERCC-only reference and comparing UMI counts to expected molecule counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Quantifies how efficiently the 10x Genomics droplet (GemCode) scRNA-seq system converts ERCC synthetic spike-in RNA molecules into detected UMI counts, by aligning Read1 cDNA inserts to an ERCC-only reference and comparing UMI counts to expected molecule counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are whole-transcriptome cell FASTQs needing genome alignment (hg19/mm10), not ERCC-only spike-in benchmarking runs. The goal is gene expression quantification for biological samples (e.g., 68k PBMC profiling) rather than instrument sensitivity/linearity validation with synthetic RNAs. A gene-barcode UMI count matrix already exists for the ERCC runs and only downstream analysis, not UMI validity filtering and counting, is required.

skills.description: Use when you need synthetic genotype-phenotype data with known planted higher-order (multi-gene) associations to benchmark network-guided interval miners such as HOGImine against their statistical power and runtime.
skills.name: erdos-renyi-network-simulation
skills.search_text: erdos-renyi-network-simulation Use when you need synthetic genotype-phenotype data with known planted higher-order (multi-gene) associations to benchmark network-guided interval miners such as HOGImine against their statistical power and runtime. The dataset is real (non-simulated) genotype data — this skill only creates synthetic benchmarks and cannot recover ground truth from real cohorts You need a synthetic benchmark for covariate-adjusted single-interval methods like FastCMH — its R generator makefastcmhdata has a different format and only supports K=2 covariate classes You only need to run HOGImine on an existing dataset (e.g. data/mmusculus/BMC.Mode or data/athaliana) rather than generate new synthetic data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates synthetic GWAS datasets with a planted, known ground-truth higher-order association: an Erdos-Renyi gene-interaction network, per-gene SNP intervals, and a causal connected subgraph injected with tunable strength rho, serialized in HOGImine input format. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Generates synthetic GWAS datasets with a planted, known ground-truth higher-order association: an Erdos-Renyi gene-interaction network, per-gene SNP intervals, and a causal connected subgraph injected with tunable strength rho, serialized in HOGImine input format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real (non-simulated) genotype data — this skill only creates synthetic benchmarks and cannot recover ground truth from real cohorts You need a synthetic benchmark for covariate-adjusted single-interval methods like FastCMH — its R generator makefastcmhdata has a different format and only supports K=2 covariate classes You only need to run HOGImine on an existing dataset (e.g. data/mmusculus/BMC.Mode or data/athaliana) rather than generate new synthetic data

skills.description: Use when searching FASTQ/FASTA reads for a known sequence (e.g. a variant, transgene, or fusion junction) where base errors are expected and an exact string matcher would miss true matches.
skills.name: error-tolerant-sequence-search
skills.search_text: error-tolerant-sequence-search Use when searching FASTQ/FASTA reads for a known sequence (e.g. a variant, transgene, or fusion junction) where base errors are expected and an exact string matcher would miss true matches. When reads and targets are error-free such that exact string matching suffices — plain grep/ugrep is 1–2 min versus ~24 min for Flexiplex When no sequence of interest is known and only flanking sequences are available — this is discovery mode, a different Flexiplex use case When the goal is general-purpose single-cell processing (mapping, count matrices) rather than targeted sequence search — a workflow such as epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Use Flexiplex in grep-like known-sequence mode to find reads containing a target sequence of interest while tolerating sequencing errors via Levenshtein-distance matching, where exact-match tools like grep fail on Illumina short-read single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Use Flexiplex in grep-like known-sequence mode to find reads containing a target sequence of interest while tolerating sequencing errors via Levenshtein-distance matching, where exact-match tools like grep fail on Illumina short-read single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads and targets are error-free such that exact string matching suffices — plain grep/ugrep is 1–2 min versus ~24 min for Flexiplex When no sequence of interest is known and only flanking sequences are available — this is discovery mode, a different Flexiplex use case When the goal is general-purpose single-cell processing (mapping, count matrices) rather than targeted sequence search — a workflow such as epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when scBONITA Boolean rules and a GRAPHML pathway topology are available and cells must be mapped to characteristic pathway-specific signaling states via attractor analysis of the learned discrete-state models.
skills.name: ers-rule-sampling-for-network-simulation
skills.search_text: ers-rule-sampling-for-network-simulation Use when scBONITA Boolean rules and a GRAPHML pathway topology are available and cells must be mapped to characteristic pathway-specific signaling states via attractor analysis of the learned discrete-state models. You only need static differential-expression or over-representation analysis — the article showed conventional ORA was inefficacious here, but attractor simulation is the wrong tool if you do not have an executable Boolean model The pathway topology or Boolean rules have not been inferred yet (rule inference with scBONITA must run first) You intend to run attractor analysis on a desktop without the >10G RAM a large scRNA-seq dataset requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Sample alternative rule sets from the ensemble of rule sets (ERS) inferred by scBONITA from scRNA-seq data, simulate the resulting discrete Boolean networks synchronously to convergence, and assign each sequenced cell to its closest steady-state attractor by Hamming distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Sample alternative rule sets from the ensemble of rule sets (ERS) inferred by scBONITA from scRNA-seq data, simulate the resulting discrete Boolean networks synchronously to convergence, and assign each sequenced cell to its closest steady-state attractor by Hamming distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need static differential-expression or over-representation analysis — the article showed conventional ORA was inefficacious here, but attractor simulation is the wrong tool if you do not have an executable Boolean model The pathway topology or Boolean rules have not been inferred yet (rule inference with scBONITA must run first) You intend to run attractor analysis on a desktop without the >10G RAM a large scRNA-seq dataset requires

skills.description: Use when testing the robustness of Boolean rule inference to training-set size: input is a pre-processed scRNA-seq cluster (genes x cells matrix), and the goal is to detect at which training fraction the ERS size degrades.
skills.name: ers-size-quantification
skills.search_text: ers-size-quantification Use when testing the robustness of Boolean rule inference to training-set size: input is a pre-processed scRNA-seq cluster (genes x cells matrix), and the goal is to detect at which training fraction the ERS size degrades. The training fraction is reduced to ~1% of the original cluster — rule determination shows a significant performance decline at this level, so results are not reliable The goal is pathway analysis or attractor analysis rather than assessing rule-inference robustness to training-set size Only network topology is available without scRNA-seq training data for the cluster — rule inference, and hence ERS quantification, cannot be performed Quantifies how the size of a scRNA-seq training cluster affects scBONITA Boolean rule inference by tabulating the size of the inferred ensemble of rules (ERS) across downsampled (1%, 50%), full (100%), and augmented (200%) training fractions of the same cell cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Quantifies how the size of a scRNA-seq training cluster affects scBONITA Boolean rule inference by tabulating the size of the inferred ensemble of rules (ERS) across downsampled (1%, 50%), full (100%), and augmented (200%) training fractions of the same cell cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training fraction is reduced to ~1% of the original cluster — rule determination shows a significant performance decline at this level, so results are not reliable The goal is pathway analysis or attractor analysis rather than assessing rule-inference robustness to training-set size Only network topology is available without scRNA-seq training data for the cluster — rule inference, and hence ERS quantification, cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when a rare-cell analysis of the 68k PBMC dataset has produced a candidate CD34+/megakaryocyte cluster (e.g. ~185 cells) and its reported erythrocyte-marker signature must be verified against remaining CD34+ cells.
skills.name: erythrocyte-marker-expression-profiling
skills.search_text: erythrocyte-marker-expression-profiling Use when a rare-cell analysis of the 68k PBMC dataset has produced a candidate CD34+/megakaryocyte cluster (e.g. ~185 cells) and its reported erythrocyte-marker signature must be verified against remaining CD34+ cells. When the input is a small dataset where exhaustive methods such as RaceID or GiniClust are feasible and the GapClust rare-cluster step is unnecessary When the target population is a major cell type — GapClust and this validation target rare minor clusters, not bulk-type annotation When clusters have already been biologically annotated and no marker-signature verification of the CD34+/megakaryocyte call is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validation skill for rare-cell discoveries in the 68k PBMC dataset: profile erythrocyte-marker expression in the GapClust-detected 185-cell CD34+ megakaryocyte cluster (R2) versus remaining CD34+ cells, replicating the marker pattern reported in Fig. 6a-d of the GapClust paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Validation skill for rare-cell discoveries in the 68k PBMC dataset: profile erythrocyte-marker expression in the GapClust-detected 185-cell CD34+ megakaryocyte cluster (R2) versus remaining CD34+ cells, replicating the marker pattern reported in Fig. 6a-d of the GapClust paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is a small dataset where exhaustive methods such as RaceID or GiniClust are feasible and the GapClust rare-cluster step is unnecessary When the target population is a major cell type — GapClust and this validation target rare minor clusters, not bulk-type annotation When clusters have already been biologically annotated and no marker-signature verification of the CD34+/megakaryocyte call is needed

skills.description: Use when a rare-cell cluster from LSH-based rareness scoring (FiRE) plus dropClust clustering must be assigned a cell-type identity, and candidate marker genes (e.g. erythrocyte markers Alas2, Hba-a1, Hba-a2, Hbb-bt) are available to confirm the assignment.
skills.name: erythrocyte-marker-expression-validation
skills.search_text: erythrocyte-marker-expression-validation Use when a rare-cell cluster from LSH-based rareness scoring (FiRE) plus dropClust clustering must be assigned a cell-type identity, and candidate marker genes (e.g. erythrocyte markers Alas2, Hba-a1, Hba-a2, Hbb-bt) are available to confirm the assignment. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo rare-cell discovery from raw data with no cluster identities yet — first run FiRE scoring and dropClust clustering; marker validation is a downstream confirmation step When testing whether a rare cell is a doublet or technical artifact — the article notes doublet rates vary between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness When the candidate cluster's expected markers are not known in advance; this skill validates a hypothesized identity against specific named markers

skills.description: Decision support for choosing among multiple 2-D embeddings (e.g., MDS, UMAP or t-SNE computed on 2000, 4000 or 10000 highly variable genes) before trajectory inference, when you need a data-driven recommended/not-recommended verdict per embedding.
skills.name: escort-embedding-scoring
skills.search_text: escort-embedding-scoring Decision support for choosing among multiple 2-D embeddings (e.g., MDS, UMAP or t-SNE computed on 2000, 4000 or 10000 highly variable genes) before trajectory inference, when you need a data-driven recommended/not-recommended verdict per embedding. The trajectory inference approach does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort 'only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations' The embedding is derived from RNA velocity-based dimension reduction — this is explicitly not yet implemented and left as future work Every candidate embedding fails DCcheck (newly disconnected clusters) — no scoring is possible, and Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A method for scoring candidate 2-D embeddings of a scRNA-seq dataset with Escort's trajectory-specific metrics (DCcheck connectivity, SimiRetain, GOF coverage area, USHAPE ambiguity) and verifying that the composite score tracks trajectory accuracy (Kendall correlation, MSE) as shown in Figure 4B of Dong et al. 2024. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: A method for scoring candidate 2-D embeddings of a scRNA-seq dataset with Escort's trajectory-specific metrics (DCcheck connectivity, SimiRetain, GOF coverage area, USHAPE ambiguity) and verifying that the composite score tracks trajectory accuracy (Kendall correlation, MSE) as shown in Figure 4B of Dong et al. 2024.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory inference approach does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort 'only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations' The embedding is derived from RNA velocity-based dimension reduction — this is explicitly not yet implemented and left as future work Every candidate embedding fails DCcheck (newly disconnected clusters) — no scoring is possible, and Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices evaluated

skills.description: Use when you have a defined gene list (e.g., TimeTalk's 430 eLR genes) and reference gene sets, and need to test whether the list is significantly enriched/depleted (e.g., essential/ZGA enriched, housekeeping depleted) against a gene-universe background.
skills.name: essential-gene-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: essential-gene-overlap-analysis Use when you have a defined gene list (e.g., TimeTalk's 430 eLR genes) and reference gene sets, and need to test whether the list is significantly enriched/depleted (e.g., essential/ZGA enriched, housekeeping depleted) against a gene-universe background. You need to test regulatory relationships between LR pairs and transcription factors (use Granger causality / RTN master-regulator analysis instead of gene-set overlap). The input is expression data rather than a defined gene list — first reduce to a concrete gene set before applying overlap tests. You need cell-type-specific differential expression, not gene-set-level enrichment against a fixed gene universe. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 One-tailed hypergeometric (Fisher-style) overlap tests that check whether a gene set — such as the 430 early-embryo-development-related ligand-receptor (eLR) genes identified by TimeTalk — is enriched for essential genes (DEG 10), ZGA genes (Table S5, ref. 18), and depleted of housekeeping genes (HRT Atlas v1.0), relative to all-protein-coding and all-LR baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: One-tailed hypergeometric (Fisher-style) overlap tests that check whether a gene set — such as the 430 early-embryo-development-related ligand-receptor (eLR) genes identified by TimeTalk — is enriched for essential genes (DEG 10), ZGA genes (Table S5, ref. 18), and depleted of housekeeping genes (HRT Atlas v1.0), relative to all-protein-coding and all-LR baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to test regulatory relationships between LR pairs and transcription factors (use Granger causality / RTN master-regulator analysis instead of gene-set overlap). The input is expression data rather than a defined gene list — first reduce to a concrete gene set before applying overlap tests. You need cell-type-specific differential expression, not gene-set-level enrichment against a fixed gene universe.

skills.description: Use when you have single-gene deletion results from both infected and mock context-specific models and must rank knockouts on an essentiality-vs-safety plane to select low-toxicity antimetabolic drug targets.
skills.name: essentiality-safety-scatter-visualization
skills.search_text: essentiality-safety-scatter-visualization Use when you have single-gene deletion results from both infected and mock context-specific models and must rank knockouts on an essentiality-vs-safety plane to select low-toxicity antimetabolic drug targets. When only infected models exist without matching mock/healthy controls — safety scores cannot be computed and the scatter's essential-but-safe region is undefined When the goal is direct docking or viral-proteome inhibition — the targets here derive from network effects on the host metabolome, as the virus is only modeled through its biomass function When input is differential expression data alone — deletion simulations require context-specific FBA models, not expression matrices Aggregates in silico single- and double-gene deletion results across mock and SARS-CoV-2-infected context-specific metabolic models into per-gene essentiality and safety scores, and plots them as the Figure 3 essentiality-vs-safety scatter to identify essential-but-safe antiviral drug targets (e.g., GUK1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Aggregates in silico single- and double-gene deletion results across mock and SARS-CoV-2-infected context-specific metabolic models into per-gene essentiality and safety scores, and plots them as the Figure 3 essentiality-vs-safety scatter to identify essential-but-safe antiviral drug targets (e.g., GUK1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only infected models exist without matching mock/healthy controls — safety scores cannot be computed and the scatter's essential-but-safe region is undefined When the goal is direct docking or viral-proteome inhibition — the targets here derive from network effects on the host metabolome, as the virus is only modeled through its biomass function When input is differential expression data alone — deletion simulations require context-specific FBA models, not expression matrices

The current BATMAN implementation only supports integrating two datasets; do not rely on this skill for multi-dataset integration workflows Data are raw counts without Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing; Euclidean distances in raw count space are not what the method assumes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs k-nearest-neighbor graphs weighted by Euclidean distance over cell expression vectors, both as the anchor-matching substrate in BATMAN batch integration and as the basis for the k-RNN (retained nearest neighbors) local-structure metric. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185

skills.description: Use when a cell-by-feature matrix has sparse NA entries (e.g., single-cell AS probability dropouts) and missing values must be imputed before downstream clustering such as spectral clustering.
skills.name: euclidean-distance-neighbor-weighting
skills.search_text: euclidean-distance-neighbor-weighting Use when a cell-by-feature matrix has sparse NA entries (e.g., single-cell AS probability dropouts) and missing values must be imputed before downstream clustering such as spectral clustering. The matrix has no NA entries — imputation would only distort observed AS probabilities. The downstream analysis requires raw unimputed AS probabilities (e.g., differential PSI testing with BRIE or Expedition rather than SCASL clustering). Features are cells rather than sites, i.e., the neighbor search orientation differs from SCASL's cell-to-cell Euclidean KNN scheme. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Iterative distance-weighted KNN imputation of missing values in the single-cell AS probability matrix, as implemented in SCASL: NA entries are first filled with site means, then refreshed over iterations using exponentially distance-weighted averages of the k nearest cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: Iterative distance-weighted KNN imputation of missing values in the single-cell AS probability matrix, as implemented in SCASL: NA entries are first filled with site means, then refreshed over iterations using exponentially distance-weighted averages of the k nearest cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix has no NA entries — imputation would only distort observed AS probabilities. The downstream analysis requires raw unimputed AS probabilities (e.g., differential PSI testing with BRIE or Expedition rather than SCASL clustering). Features are cells rather than sites, i.e., the neighbor search orientation differs from SCASL's cell-to-cell Euclidean KNN scheme.

skills.description: Use when building condition-specific (normal vs cancer) gene co-expression networks from TCGA RNA-Seq expression data and you need a distribution-based, top-percentile sparsification of Euclidean-distance similarity edges before network fusion.
skills.name: euclidean-distance-network-percentile-thresholding
skills.search_text: euclidean-distance-network-percentile-thresholding Use when building condition-specific (normal vs cancer) gene co-expression networks from TCGA RNA-Seq expression data and you need a distribution-based, top-percentile sparsification of Euclidean-distance similarity edges before network fusion. You are filtering Pearson-correlation co-expression networks — these use a permutation test (10 random shuffles) plus a p-value percentile threshold instead of the Euclidean 99th-percentile rule You need the complete dense similarity matrix or a fixed absolute weight cutoff rather than a distribution-relative (top ~1%) edge set Your goal is a single co-expression network rather than multiple similarity-measure networks that will be merged and SNF-fused per cancer type http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters condition-specific Euclidean-distance gene co-expression networks by retaining only edges whose weight exceeds the 99th percentile of the network's edge-weight distribution, producing a sparse per-condition network that is combined with the Pearson-correlation network and fused via SNF for KIRC, LIHC and PRAD. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Filters condition-specific Euclidean-distance gene co-expression networks by retaining only edges whose weight exceeds the 99th percentile of the network's edge-weight distribution, producing a sparse per-condition network that is combined with the Pearson-correlation network and fused via SNF for KIRC, LIHC and PRAD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are filtering Pearson-correlation co-expression networks — these use a permutation test (10 random shuffles) plus a p-value percentile threshold instead of the Euclidean 99th-percentile rule You need the complete dense similarity matrix or a fixed absolute weight cutoff rather than a distribution-relative (top ~1%) edge set Your goal is a single co-expression network rather than multiple similarity-measure networks that will be merged and SNF-fused per cancer type

skills.name: euclidean-minimum-spanning-tree-cell-graph-construction
skills.search_text: euclidean-minimum-spanning-tree-cell-graph-construction Use when benchmarking single-cell trajectory methods on a progenitor dataset with a known branching event (e.g. cDC1 vs cDC2 preDC commitment) and a conventional tree-based baseline is needed to compare against neighborhood-based methods like Mpath. When the expected lineage topology is genuinely multi-branching with multiple cell fates from a single progenitor type — the article showed conventional MST placed cDC1- and cDC2-committed preDCs on the wrong branch, whereas Mpath resolved them When the goal is fate prediction from differentiated-cell signature genes traveling back in time — that requires Mpath's neighborhood-based state-transition framework, not a plain Euclidean MST When the input is already a precomputed cell-cell graph or trajectory object rather than a raw expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Baseline trajectory-inference skill that builds a conventional minimum spanning tree over pairwise Euclidean distances between single cells, used to benchmark whether a tree-based method captures branching events such as the cDC1/cDC2-committed preDC split. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Baseline trajectory-inference skill that builds a conventional minimum spanning tree over pairwise Euclidean distances between single cells, used to benchmark whether a tree-based method captures branching events such as the cDC1/cDC2-committed preDC split.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the expected lineage topology is genuinely multi-branching with multiple cell fates from a single progenitor type — the article showed conventional MST placed cDC1- and cDC2-committed preDCs on the wrong branch, whereas Mpath resolved them When the goal is fate prediction from differentiated-cell signature genes traveling back in time — that requires Mpath's neighborhood-based state-transition framework, not a plain Euclidean MST When the input is already a precomputed cell-cell graph or trajectory object rather than a raw expression matrix

skills.search_text: eukaryotic-protein-sequence-retrieval Use when building or extending a protein ortholog database from KEGG eukaryotic proteomes — i.e., you need per-organism FASTA files for downstream all-vs-all orthology binning. Input is already a per-organism proteome FASTA set or a finished ortholog database — go straight to orthology binning or read-mapping instead You need taxon-specific reference genes absent from KEGG (e.g., vitellogenin, 'a precursor to egg yolk protein formation and a biomarker of interest, is not found in the KO system') Small, taxonomically narrow analyses — mapping against all 687 species risks mapping reads from one gene to similar but different orthologs across distant species http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0157 Bulk-download all protein-coding sequences for eukaryotic organisms from KEGG using KEGGREST, saving one FASTA per species, to construct a protein/ortholog database (the EcoOmicsDB foundation, n = 12,828,537 proteins across 687 species). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Bulk-download all protein-coding sequences for eukaryotic organisms from KEGG using KEGGREST, saving one FASTA per species, to construct a protein/ortholog database (the EcoOmicsDB foundation, n = 12,828,537 proteins across 687 species).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-organism proteome FASTA set or a finished ortholog database — go straight to orthology binning or read-mapping instead You need taxon-specific reference genes absent from KEGG (e.g., vitellogenin, 'a precursor to egg yolk protein formation and a biomarker of interest, is not found in the KO system') Small, taxonomically narrow analyses — mapping against all 687 species risks mapping reads from one gene to similar but different orthologs across distant species

skills.description: Use when running ELVAR/EVA clustering on a cell-cell nearest-neighbor graph with a vertex attribute (age, disease stage/severity) and an optimal alpha balancing attribute-similarity against state-manifold topology must be chosen before downstream DA testing.

skills.search_text: eva-alpha-parameter-optimization Use when running ELVAR/EVA clustering on a cell-cell nearest-neighbor graph with a vertex attribute (age, disease stage/severity) and an optimal alpha balancing attribute-similarity against state-manifold topology must be chosen before downstream DA testing. When no meaningful cell attribute exists to guide clustering — alpha=0 standard Louvain (FindClusters) is the appropriate benchmark instead When the cell-cell graph is disconnected or the vertex attribute has many false positives (ELVAR is more sensitive to FPs in the sample/phenotype label), which degrades inferred communities When data have strong clustering structure, where ELVAR's improvement over Louvain is less noticeable and extra runtime is not justified http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects an optimal alpha parameter for EVA cell-attribute aware community detection by running Eva_partitions 100 times across alpha = 0.1–0.9 and applying SelOptAlpha criteria on purity, modularity, and cluster count. Alpha balances contribution of cell attributes (e.g. disease severity) versus graph topology in the Louvain objective. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Selects an optimal alpha parameter for EVA cell-attribute aware community detection by running Eva_partitions 100 times across alpha = 0.1–0.9 and applying SelOptAlpha criteria on purity, modularity, and cluster count. Alpha balances contribution of cell attributes (e.g. disease severity) versus graph topology in the Louvain objective.

skills.search_text: evidence-based-cell-type-scoring Use when clusters from scRNA-seq data need automatic cell type labels without prior knowledge, and candidate cluster marker genes have been identified and matched against the CellMatch reference database. Marker genes have not yet been identified and matched against CellMatch — run findmarkergene and CellMatch matching first The tissue or cell types of interest are not represented in the CellMatch database, since performance is database-dependent and a limited reference database can lead to incorrect annotation Annotation must be at subtype or custom-taxonomy level not covered by CellMatch's 353 cell types / 686 subtypes, unless a custom cellmatch panel is supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Score candidate cell types for each pre-computed scRNA-seq cluster by counting validated marker genes matched in the CellMatch database plus their supporting literature, then assign the top-1 scoring cell type as the cluster annotation (scCATCH findcelltype step). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
