When comparing methods across different droplet sets — restrict both methods to the identical droplet set (same min_counts) first, or the kept-set differences are confounded When the goal is filtering a single dataset for downstream analysis rather than benchmarking method agreement (use the DIEM filtering skill alone) When the debris score itself needs to be interpreted across independent experiments — debris scores cannot be assumed to be on the same scale across samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks competing droplet-filtering methods (DIEM's debris-cluster removal mode vs. EmptyDrops) on the identical restricted droplet set, comparing uniquely kept droplets by total counts and extranuclear contamination metrics (MT%, MALAT1%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Benchmarks competing droplet-filtering methods (DIEM's debris-cluster removal mode vs. EmptyDrops) on the identical restricted droplet set, comparing uniquely kept droplets by total counts and extranuclear contamination metrics (MT%, MALAT1%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing methods across different droplet sets — restrict both methods to the identical droplet set (same min_counts) first, or the kept-set differences are confounded When the goal is filtering a single dataset for downstream analysis rather than benchmarking method agreement (use the DIEM filtering skill alone) When the debris score itself needs to be interpreted across independent experiments — debris scores cannot be assumed to be on the same scale across samples

skills.description: Use when a pipeline applies an automatic filtering step (e.g., dropping perturbations whose target gene is zero in all cells) and you must determine whether that filter materially alters the final rankings or is a minor edge-case removal.
skills.name: filtering-sensitivity-assessment
skills.search_text: filtering-sensitivity-assessment Use when a pipeline applies an automatic filtering step (e.g., dropping perturbations whose target gene is zero in all cells) and you must determine whether that filter materially alters the final rankings or is a minor edge-case removal. When the filter's removed set is already known to be large (e.g., perturbations with fewer than 30 perturbed cells dominate the screen) — a sensitivity test on rankings is less informative than a direct report of removed perturbations. When the input is not Perturb-seq/CROP-seq single-cell CRISPR screening data with a perturbation annotation per cell, since the ranking comparison target (Rank_overall/Rank_specific) would not exist. When the control sample label cannot be set to 'CTRL', as Input_preprocess requires this label to identify controls. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A validation workflow that quantifies how strongly a candidate data-filtering rule (e.g., MUSIC's zero-expression perturbation filter) changes downstream results, by re-running the full pipeline with and without the filter and comparing perturbation effect rankings via Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: A validation workflow that quantifies how strongly a candidate data-filtering rule (e.g., MUSIC's zero-expression perturbation filter) changes downstream results, by re-running the full pipeline with and without the filter and comparing perturbation effect rankings via Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the filter's removed set is already known to be large (e.g., perturbations with fewer than 30 perturbed cells dominate the screen) — a sensitivity test on rankings is less informative than a direct report of removed perturbations. When the input is not Perturb-seq/CROP-seq single-cell CRISPR screening data with a perturbation annotation per cell, since the ranking comparison target (Rank_overall/Rank_specific) would not exist. When the control sample label cannot be set to 'CTRL', as Input_preprocess requires this label to identify controls.

skills.description: Use when quantifying whether a multi-trait fine-mapping/colocalization method (e.g. CAFEH) improves power or FDP over CAVIAR, eCAVIAR, FINEMAP, or SuSiE under allelic heterogeneity in simulated loci.
skills.name: fine-mapping-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: fine-mapping-method-benchmarking Use when quantifying whether a multi-trait fine-mapping/colocalization method (e.g. CAFEH) improves power or FDP over CAVIAR, eCAVIAR, FINEMAP, or SuSiE under allelic heterogeneity in simulated loci. The loci under study contain variants in nearly perfect or very high LD with each other where distinguishing multiple signals remains difficult even for the best method Studies differ substantially in LD structure (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The goal is inference from individual-level data rather than the summary-statistic simulation benchmark (use CAFEH genotype mode instead of the beta/z benchmark path) http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation-based benchmarking workflow that compares CAFEH's colocalization and fine-mapping performance against CAVIAR, eCAVIAR, FINEMAP, and SuSiE across varying numbers of causal variants (q) and signal strengths (rho), evaluated by false discovery proportion versus power. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: A simulation-based benchmarking workflow that compares CAFEH's colocalization and fine-mapping performance against CAVIAR, eCAVIAR, FINEMAP, and SuSiE across varying numbers of causal variants (q) and signal strengths (rho), evaluated by false discovery proportion versus power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The loci under study contain variants in nearly perfect or very high LD with each other where distinguishing multiple signals remains difficult even for the best method Studies differ substantially in LD structure (e.g. ancestry differences), since CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix The goal is inference from individual-level data rather than the summary-statistic simulation benchmark (use CAFEH genotype mode instead of the beta/z benchmark path)

skills.description: Use when you have a continuous FiRE rareness score for every cell (np.array [nCells]) and need a binary rare-cell annotation per cell, because downstream validation or visualization (e.g., t-SNE overlay of detected rare cells) requires discrete 0/1 calls rather than raw scores.
skills.name: fire-score-thresholding
skills.search_text: fire-score-thresholding Use when you have a continuous FiRE rareness score for every cell (np.array [nCells]) and need a binary rare-cell annotation per cell, because downstream validation or visualization (e.g., t-SNE overlay of detected rare cells) requires discrete 0/1 calls rather than raw scores. Input is already a binary rare/not-rare annotation (e.g., labels from RaceID or GiniClust) rather than a continuous FiRE score vector The analysis goal is only a continuous rareness ranking for visualization (e.g., FiRE score intensity plotted on a t-SNE map) with no need for discrete calls You need to separate technical outliers from cells of genuinely rare cell types — the article notes 'FiRE, in principle, does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types', so this thresholding alone cannot resolve that http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Dichotomizes FiRE's continuous per-cell rareness scores into binary rare/not-rare cell labels using Tukey IQR-based thresholding (score >= q3 + 1.5*IQR), the technique FiRE's authors used to flag rare cells (e.g., 727 rare cells in the mouse brain data and 4238 in the ~68k PBMC data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Dichotomizes FiRE's continuous per-cell rareness scores into binary rare/not-rare cell labels using Tukey IQR-based thresholding (score >= q3 + 1.5*IQR), the technique FiRE's authors used to flag rare cells (e.g., 727 rare cells in the mouse brain data and 4238 in the ~68k PBMC data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binary rare/not-rare annotation (e.g., labels from RaceID or GiniClust) rather than a continuous FiRE score vector The analysis goal is only a continuous rareness ranking for visualization (e.g., FiRE score intensity plotted on a t-SNE map) with no need for discrete calls You need to separate technical outliers from cells of genuinely rare cell types — the article notes 'FiRE, in principle, does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types', so this thresholding alone cannot resolve that

skills.description: Use when per-individual (or per-replicate) ASAS p values must be merged into one event-level p value, or when a non-paired baseline is needed to benchmark a paired differential AS model such as PAIRADISE.
skills.name: fisher-combined-probability-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-combined-probability-testing Use when per-individual (or per-replicate) ASAS p values must be merged into one event-level p value, or when a non-paired baseline is needed to benchmark a paired differential AS model such as PAIRADISE. When the two alleles of an individual can be treated as paired replicates and a paired model (e.g., PAIRADISE or the rMATS paired model) can be fit — Fisher's method forgoes the paired structure and loses power When per-individual p values or allele-specific count data (IJC/SJC) are unavailable for the event being tested When the goal is de novo ASAS detection from raw RNA-seq reads rather than combining already-computed per-individual test results http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fisher's combined probability test aggregates per-individual allele-specific splicing p values for the same event into a single event-level p value. In the PAIRADISE paper it serves as one of four baseline ASAS detection methods benchmarked in the exon-skipping simulation study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Fisher's combined probability test aggregates per-individual allele-specific splicing p values for the same event into a single event-level p value. In the PAIRADISE paper it serves as one of four baseline ASAS detection methods benchmarked in the exon-skipping simulation study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two alleles of an individual can be treated as paired replicates and a paired model (e.g., PAIRADISE or the rMATS paired model) can be fit — Fisher's method forgoes the paired structure and loses power When per-individual p values or allele-specific count data (IJC/SJC) are unavailable for the event being tested When the goal is de novo ASAS detection from raw RNA-seq reads rather than combining already-computed per-individual test results

skills.description: Use when annotating Seurat-derived cluster marker lists (positive markers with avg_log2FC scores, Entrez-mapped) against CellMarker via easyct(test='fisher'), or when comparing Fisher vs GSEA annotation accuracy.
skills.name: fisher-exact-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating Seurat-derived cluster marker lists (positive markers with avg_log2FC scores, Entrez-mapped) against CellMarker via easyct(test='fisher'), or when comparing Fisher vs GSEA annotation accuracy. When the analysis goal is maximum annotation accuracy on larger simulated PBMC datasets — the GSEA variant is preferred (hard GSEA outperformed all four unsupervised tools at 4000 cells, while Fisher exceeded only SCSA and scCATCH at 2400/1600 cells) When markers come from a t-test DE backend — the paper's DE-test comparison found t-test markers give the weakest accuracy and t-test is not recommended for detecting DE genes When you need organism or tissue coverage outside CellMarker's human blood/tissue references; check available db/tissue options first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Annotate scRNA-seq clusters with EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test classifier, which combines gene-set overlap against CellMarker with expression significance (avg_log2FC ranking) rather than raw list overlap alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Annotate scRNA-seq clusters with EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test classifier, which combines gene-set overlap against CellMarker with expression significance (avg_log2FC ranking) rather than raw list overlap alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is maximum annotation accuracy on larger simulated PBMC datasets — the GSEA variant is preferred (hard GSEA outperformed all four unsupervised tools at 4000 cells, while Fisher exceeded only SCSA and scCATCH at 2400/1600 cells) When markers come from a t-test DE backend — the paper's DE-test comparison found t-test markers give the weakest accuracy and t-test is not recommended for detecting DE genes When you need organism or tissue coverage outside CellMarker's human blood/tissue references; check available db/tissue options first

skills.description: Use when the query input is a list of genes rather than an expression matrix — e.g., top-N cluster marker genes from Seurat FindAllMarkers, or trait-associated genes mapped from GWAS SNPs — and cell type membership must be tested for enrichment.
skills.name: fisher-exact-cell-type-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-cell-type-enrichment-analysis Use when the query input is a list of genes rather than an expression matrix — e.g., top-N cluster marker genes from Seurat FindAllMarkers, or trait-associated genes mapped from GWAS SNPs — and cell type membership must be tested for enrichment. The query is a scaled gene expression profile (e.g., pbmc_cluster_marker_z_score) — use deCS.correlation() with PCC instead of the Fisher's exact test The goal is to discover novel cell types not represented in the reference panels — deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Annotating cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells make deCS annotations challenging http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Use deCS.fisher() to test whether a query gene list (e.g., cluster top-10 markers or GWAS trait-associated genes) is disproportionately overlapped in cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) of a deCS reference panel, assigning cell types or trait–cell type associations via Fisher's exact test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Use deCS.fisher() to test whether a query gene list (e.g., cluster top-10 markers or GWAS trait-associated genes) is disproportionately overlapped in cell type-specific genes (CTgenes) of a deCS reference panel, assigning cell types or trait–cell type associations via Fisher's exact test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is a scaled gene expression profile (e.g., pbmc_cluster_marker_z_score) — use deCS.correlation() with PCC instead of the Fisher's exact test The goal is to discover novel cell types not represented in the reference panels — deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Annotating cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells make deCS annotations challenging

skills.description: Use when two binary per-sample viral/infection status calls (e.g., IIV31 positivity and Trichomonas vaginalis positivity in TCGA-UCEC) must be tested for enrichment using an exact 2x2 test.
skills.name: fisher-exact-co-infection-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-co-infection-enrichment-testing Use when two binary per-sample viral/infection status calls (e.g., IIV31 positivity and Trichomonas vaginalis positivity in TCGA-UCEC) must be tested for enrichment using an exact 2x2 test. Per-sample binary viral status is unavailable (no viRNAtrap contig calls or verified TV status), so a 2x2 contingency table cannot be built The comparison involves continuous variables such as TMB, CNA burden, or CIBERSORT CD8+/Treg proportions, where log-rank or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (not Fisher's exact test) are the appropriate procedure Fewer than five viral reads are present in a sample, where viRNAtrap sensitivity is not guaranteed and the resulting positivity call is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Build a 2x2 contingency table of binary per-sample viral status calls (e.g., IIV31-positive vs Trichomonas vaginalis-positive in UCEC) and apply Fisher's exact test to quantify co-infection enrichment, reporting the odds ratio and p-value alongside the log-rank/Wilcoxon statistics of Fig. 4b-e. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Build a 2x2 contingency table of binary per-sample viral status calls (e.g., IIV31-positive vs Trichomonas vaginalis-positive in UCEC) and apply Fisher's exact test to quantify co-infection enrichment, reporting the odds ratio and p-value alongside the log-rank/Wilcoxon statistics of Fig. 4b-e.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-sample binary viral status is unavailable (no viRNAtrap contig calls or verified TV status), so a 2x2 contingency table cannot be built The comparison involves continuous variables such as TMB, CNA burden, or CIBERSORT CD8+/Treg proportions, where log-rank or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (not Fisher's exact test) are the appropriate procedure Fewer than five viral reads are present in a sample, where viRNAtrap sensitivity is not guaranteed and the resulting positivity call is unreliable

skills.description: Use when two WGCNA/PyWGCNA co-expression networks from different datasets must be compared at the module level — i.e., you need to identify which module pairs share significantly more genes than expected by chance.
skills.name: fisher-exact-contingency-table-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-contingency-table-testing Use when two WGCNA/PyWGCNA co-expression networks from different datasets must be compared at the module level — i.e., you need to identify which module pairs share significantly more genes than expected by chance. You only have one WGCNA network — module comparison requires two PyWGCNA objects from different datasets (or one PyWGCNA object plus an external gene/marker list, which is a separate workflow) You need module-level functional interpretation rather than cross-network conservation testing — use PyWGCNA's functional enrichment workflow (GO, KEGG, REACTOME) instead Your input is raw RNA-seq count data that has not yet been through PyWGCNA module construction — build the networks first (Quick Start workflow), then compare them http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Fisher's exact test to module-pair gene-membership contingency tables to detect significant overlap between co-expression networks built from different datasets (e.g., the 5xFAD coral module vs. the 3xTg-AD darkgray module), as implemented in PyWGCNA's module-comparison workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Applies Fisher's exact test to module-pair gene-membership contingency tables to detect significant overlap between co-expression networks built from different datasets (e.g., the 5xFAD coral module vs. the 3xTg-AD darkgray module), as implemented in PyWGCNA's module-comparison workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have one WGCNA network — module comparison requires two PyWGCNA objects from different datasets (or one PyWGCNA object plus an external gene/marker list, which is a separate workflow) You need module-level functional interpretation rather than cross-network conservation testing — use PyWGCNA's functional enrichment workflow (GO, KEGG, REACTOME) instead Your input is raw RNA-seq count data that has not yet been through PyWGCNA module construction — build the networks first (Quick Start workflow), then compare them

skills.description: Use when testing a categorical association between CMScaller CMS class assignments (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2, CMS1 vs non-CMS1) and a binary phenotype (drug responder status, MSI status, BRAF mutation) across PDX, organoid, or cell line cohorts.
skills.name: fisher-exact-contingency-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-contingency-testing Use when testing a categorical association between CMScaller CMS class assignments (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2, CMS1 vs non-CMS1) and a binary phenotype (drug responder status, MSI status, BRAF mutation) across PDX, organoid, or cell line cohorts. Comparing continuous measurements across CMS groups (e.g., total mutation counts or CNA burden in Gao PDXs, reported p=9.9e-4 and p=5.9e-3) — use a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (wilcox.test) instead The exposure variable is already continuous or ordered (e.g., drug IC50 values) rather than a pre-binarized responder/non-responder label The sample-level class labels have not been generated yet — CMScaller classification must be run first on centered and scaled gene expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Apply R's fisher.test() to 2x2 contingency tables to test categorical associations in CMScaller-based pre-clinical CRC analyses — e.g., CMS2 versus non-CMS2 classification against cetuximab responder status, or CMS1-immune prediction against MSI status — reporting exact p-values and odds ratios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Apply R's fisher.test() to 2x2 contingency tables to test categorical associations in CMScaller-based pre-clinical CRC analyses — e.g., CMS2 versus non-CMS2 classification against cetuximab responder status, or CMS1-immune prediction against MSI status — reporting exact p-values and odds ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing continuous measurements across CMS groups (e.g., total mutation counts or CNA burden in Gao PDXs, reported p=9.9e-4 and p=5.9e-3) — use a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (wilcox.test) instead The exposure variable is already continuous or ordered (e.g., drug IC50 values) rather than a pre-binarized responder/non-responder label The sample-level class labels have not been generated yet — CMScaller classification must be run first on centered and scaled gene expression data

skills.description: Use when comparing the composition of ligand-receptor sets from CCC resources against annotation terms (pathways, cancer genes, tissue-enriched proteins), or when testing whether top-ranked CCC interactions overlap significantly with active cytokines.
skills.name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing Use when comparing the composition of ligand-receptor sets from CCC resources against annotation terms (pathways, cancer genes, tissue-enriched proteins), or when testing whether top-ranked CCC interactions overlap significantly with active cytokines. The goal is to score cytokine activities or pathway activities from pseudobulk profiles themselves — use decoupleR's multivariate linear model (mlm) instead of an overlap enrichment test The goal is to compare the magnitude/ranking behaviour of CCC methods against spatial colocalisation or receptor protein abundance — this skill only tests set-overlap enrichment and cannot evaluate score calibration The aim is to infer actual communication events — the article notes such benchmarks 'cannot distinguish simple co-expression from actual CCC events', so odds-ratio enrichment is a compositional, not mechanistic, signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables to quantify whether ligand-receptor interactions from individual CCC resources (or highly ranked interactions from CCC methods) are over- or under-represented in annotation sets, expressed as odds ratios with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Applies Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables to quantify whether ligand-receptor interactions from individual CCC resources (or highly ranked interactions from CCC methods) are over- or under-represented in annotation sets, expressed as odds ratios with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to score cytokine activities or pathway activities from pseudobulk profiles themselves — use decoupleR's multivariate linear model (mlm) instead of an overlap enrichment test The goal is to compare the magnitude/ranking behaviour of CCC methods against spatial colocalisation or receptor protein abundance — this skill only tests set-overlap enrichment and cannot evaluate score calibration The aim is to infer actual communication events — the article notes such benchmarks 'cannot distinguish simple co-expression from actual CCC events', so odds-ratio enrichment is a compositional, not mechanistic, signal

skills.description: Use when validating a predicted gene/RBP set (e.g., an NMF cluster from CRIT's MATRIX.txt features) against a curated reference list such as gold_regulators.xlsx or POSTAR3/ENCORI CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBPs via 2x2 overlap tests.
skills.name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing Use when validating a predicted gene/RBP set (e.g., an NMF cluster from CRIT's MATRIX.txt features) against a curated reference list such as gold_regulators.xlsx or POSTAR3/ENCORI CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBPs via 2x2 overlap tests. The input is already a per-gene statistic table needing multiple-testing correction rather than a set-vs-set overlap test There is no independently curated reference set (gold regulators, circmCherry screen, or CLIP binding lists) to test enrichment against, making the 2x2 table ill-defined The question is a continuous association between gene expression and circRNA levels (use the rho_m Spearman correlation feature) rather than categorical set membership http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A set-overlap validation step of the CRIT pipeline that tests whether NMF-derived RBP clusters and candidate circRNA-regulator lists are significantly enriched for gold-standard regulators and CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBPs, using one-sided Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables computed in R (stats::fisher.test). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: A set-overlap validation step of the CRIT pipeline that tests whether NMF-derived RBP clusters and candidate circRNA-regulator lists are significantly enriched for gold-standard regulators and CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBPs, using one-sided Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables computed in R (stats::fisher.test).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-gene statistic table needing multiple-testing correction rather than a set-vs-set overlap test There is no independently curated reference set (gold regulators, circmCherry screen, or CLIP binding lists) to test enrichment against, making the 2x2 table ill-defined The question is a continuous association between gene expression and circRNA levels (use the rho_m Spearman correlation feature) rather than categorical set membership

skills.description: Use when a fitted SSrGE model must be probed for subgroup-specific genotype markers — e.g., after separating normal vs. cancer cell indices, to find eeSNVs/genes significantly enriched in one subgroup (Fisher's exact test p < 0.05).
skills.name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing Use when a fitted SSrGE model must be probed for subgroup-specific genotype markers — e.g., after separating normal vs. cancer cell indices, to find eeSNVs/genes significantly enriched in one subgroup (Fisher's exact test p < 0.05). You only need a global eeSNV/gene ranking across all cells — use ssrge.rank_eeSNVs() / ssrge.rank_genes() instead of subgroup-specific testing No cell subgroup labels or indices are available (e.g., unsupervised exploration without normal/cancer or subtype assignments) The features matrix is continuous gene expression rather than a binary/encoded SNV presence matrix — subgroup enrichment testing as described operates on eeSNV presence patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Identifies subgroup-specific eeSNVs and genes in single-cell datasets by testing, with Fisher's exact test, whether a given eeSNV (or gene harboring it) is significantly more present among cells of one subgroup (e.g., HCC cells vs. normal hepatocytes) than in the rest, yielding statistically significant features per subgroup. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Identifies subgroup-specific eeSNVs and genes in single-cell datasets by testing, with Fisher's exact test, whether a given eeSNV (or gene harboring it) is significantly more present among cells of one subgroup (e.g., HCC cells vs. normal hepatocytes) than in the rest, yielding statistically significant features per subgroup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a global eeSNV/gene ranking across all cells — use ssrge.rank_eeSNVs() / ssrge.rank_genes() instead of subgroup-specific testing No cell subgroup labels or indices are available (e.g., unsupervised exploration without normal/cancer or subtype assignments) The features matrix is continuous gene expression rather than a binary/encoded SNV presence matrix — subgroup enrichment testing as described operates on eeSNV presence patterns

skills.description: Use when simulating or benchmarking ASAS/differential splicing methods and a simple read-pooled baseline is needed to quantify the power gained by modeling replicates, particularly with injected outlier samples.
skills.name: fisher-exact-pooled-read-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-pooled-read-testing Use when simulating or benchmarking ASAS/differential splicing methods and a simple read-pooled baseline is needed to quantify the power gained by modeling replicates, particularly with injected outlier samples. When analyzing actual replicate RNA-seq data for ASAS detection rather than establishing a benchmark baseline — pooling discards replicate structure and loses robustness to outlier samples When reads cannot be uniquely assigned to alleles, e.g. SNPs located within or too distant from alternative exons, since allele-specific counting is a prerequisite for both pooling and PAIRADISE When the goal is differential AS between conditions rather than allele-specific comparisons within individuals http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 A baseline strategy for allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) detection in which allelic exon inclusion/skipping counts are pooled across replicates and tested with Fisher's exact test, ignoring per-replicate structure. It serves as the comparison benchmark that demonstrates why replicate-aware models like PAIRADISE are more robust, especially under outlier contamination. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: A baseline strategy for allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) detection in which allelic exon inclusion/skipping counts are pooled across replicates and tested with Fisher's exact test, ignoring per-replicate structure. It serves as the comparison benchmark that demonstrates why replicate-aware models like PAIRADISE are more robust, especially under outlier contamination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When analyzing actual replicate RNA-seq data for ASAS detection rather than establishing a benchmark baseline — pooling discards replicate structure and loses robustness to outlier samples When reads cannot be uniquely assigned to alleles, e.g. SNPs located within or too distant from alternative exons, since allele-specific counting is a prerequisite for both pooling and PAIRADISE When the goal is differential AS between conditions rather than allele-specific comparisons within individuals

skills.description: Use when a gene set (e.g., DEGs from rank_genes_groups) must be tested for over-representation within a genomic annotation stratum (e.g., XClone-defined LOH vs non-LOH regions) using proportional counts and an exact test.
skills.name: fisher-exact-proportion-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-proportion-enrichment-testing Use when a gene set (e.g., DEGs from rank_genes_groups) must be tested for over-representation within a genomic annotation stratum (e.g., XClone-defined LOH vs non-LOH regions) using proportional counts and an exact test. InferCNV or CopyKAT outputs are the only CNA annotations available, since both do not consider allelic information and hence cannot detect copy-neutral LOH, making LOH-vs-non-LOH stratification impossible The comparison involves continuous effect sizes rather than counts/proportions in discrete strata — Fisher's exact test requires a 2x2 table of counts, not per-gene expression statistics Strata contain too few genes for a meaningful contingency table (near-zero cell counts), where the exact test loses power http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 Uses Fisher's exact test on 2x2 contingency tables to test whether the proportion of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) is enriched in one genomic stratum (e.g., copy-neutral LOH regions) versus another (non-LOH regions), as applied to XClone CNA states in the TNBC1 triple-negative breast cancer sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Uses Fisher's exact test on 2x2 contingency tables to test whether the proportion of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) is enriched in one genomic stratum (e.g., copy-neutral LOH regions) versus another (non-LOH regions), as applied to XClone CNA states in the TNBC1 triple-negative breast cancer sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: InferCNV or CopyKAT outputs are the only CNA annotations available, since both do not consider allelic information and hence cannot detect copy-neutral LOH, making LOH-vs-non-LOH stratification impossible The comparison involves continuous effect sizes rather than counts/proportions in discrete strata — Fisher's exact test requires a 2x2 table of counts, not per-gene expression statistics Strata contain too few genes for a meaningful contingency table (near-zero cell counts), where the exact test loses power

skills.description: Use when you have imputed surface protein abundances (cTP-net output) that split one cell type into two subgroups, and you need to test whether the genes differential between those subgroups are enriched, e.g. CD56-high/CD16-low vs CD56-low/CD16-high NK cells.
skills.name: fisher-exact-test-differential-gene-enrichment
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-test-differential-gene-enrichment Use when you have imputed surface protein abundances (cTP-net output) that split one cell type into two subgroups, and you need to test whether the genes differential between those subgroups are enriched, e.g. CD56-high/CD16-low vs CD56-low/CD16-high NK cells. Input is raw RNA abundance alone rather than imputed protein space — the CD56/CD16 gradient is not found in the corresponding RNA abundances (F-test p = 0.9377), so enrichment testing there is uninformative for this skill's purpose Expression input is not UMI-based counts — cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based), so TPM/RPKM-style inputs cannot produce the imputed abundances this enrichment test depends on Cells are outside the hematopoietic lineage — the article reports that imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried on non-hematopoietic cells, so subgroup definitions and enrichment results are unvalidated there Applies the Fisher exact test on genes differential between imputed-protein-defined cell subpopulations (e.g., NK cells split by the CD56/CD16 gradient from cTP-net imputation) to test whether the protein-imputed substructure corresponds to distinct transcriptomic programs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Applies the Fisher exact test on genes differential between imputed-protein-defined cell subpopulations (e.g., NK cells split by the CD56/CD16 gradient from cTP-net imputation) to test whether the protein-imputed substructure corresponds to distinct transcriptomic programs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA abundance alone rather than imputed protein space — the CD56/CD16 gradient is not found in the corresponding RNA abundances (F-test p = 0.9377), so enrichment testing there is uninformative for this skill's purpose Expression input is not UMI-based counts — cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based), so TPM/RPKM-style inputs cannot produce the imputed abundances this enrichment test depends on Cells are outside the hematopoietic lineage — the article reports that imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried on non-hematopoietic cells, so subgroup definitions and enrichment results are unvalidated there

skills.description: Use when a per-cluster differential marker list (genes + cluster labels + expression scores such as logFC) needs to be converted into ranked cell-type annotations via overrepresentation testing against a marker database.
skills.name: fisher-exact-test-enrichment
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-test-enrichment Use when a per-cluster differential marker list (genes + cluster labels + expression scores such as logFC) needs to be converted into ranked cell-type annotations via overrepresentation testing against a marker database. The analysis goal is rank-aware enrichment of a full ordered gene list rather than marker overrepresentation testing — EasyCellType's GSEA option (annot.GSEA <- easyct(input.d, db="cellmarker", ...)) is the alternative test in that case. The input is raw counts or an unprocessed Seurat object with no per-cluster marker list — the upstream Seurat workflow (FindAllMarkers, mapIds to Entrez IDs) must run first. Markers come from a tissue with no matching CellMarker tissue subset, since annotation quality depends on tissue-specific marker gene sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test assesses overrepresentation of a cluster's differential marker genes within cell-type marker gene sets (e.g. CellMarker), then ranks passing candidates by the markers' expression significance (e.g. log fold change) rather than raw overlap size, yielding per-cluster cell-type annotation recommendations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test assesses overrepresentation of a cluster's differential marker genes within cell-type marker gene sets (e.g. CellMarker), then ranks passing candidates by the markers' expression significance (e.g. log fold change) rather than raw overlap size, yielding per-cluster cell-type annotation recommendations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is rank-aware enrichment of a full ordered gene list rather than marker overrepresentation testing — EasyCellType's GSEA option (annot.GSEA <- easyct(input.d, db="cellmarker", ...)) is the alternative test in that case. The input is raw counts or an unprocessed Seurat object with no per-cluster marker list — the upstream Seurat workflow (FindAllMarkers, mapIds to Entrez IDs) must run first. Markers come from a tissue with no matching CellMarker tissue subset, since annotation quality depends on tissue-specific marker gene sets.

skills.description: Use when you have a binary gene-cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to find genes significantly enriched in one lifestyle group versus the rest.
skills.name: fisher-exact-test-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-test-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a binary gene-cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to find genes significantly enriched in one lifestyle group versus the rest. Your input is not a binary absence/presence gene-cluster matrix (e.g., raw reads or expression counts) — the enrichment test requires the bacLIFE clustering module's binary matrix Genome lifestyle labels are unavailable or lack the >0.8 random-forest confidence threshold, so group membership cannot be trusted for the 2x2 contingency tables You need genomic regions enriched in virulence factors from pLAG positions rather than per-gene enrichment statistics — that is a separate downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 A per-lifestyle enrichment test that identifies predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) by testing each gene cluster's absence/presence against lifestyle group membership with Fisher's exact test, applying bacLIFE's thresholds of >70% group prevalence and >2 log2 fold change, as used on Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: A per-lifestyle enrichment test that identifies predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) by testing each gene cluster's absence/presence against lifestyle group membership with Fisher's exact test, applying bacLIFE's thresholds of >70% group prevalence and >2 log2 fold change, as used on Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is not a binary absence/presence gene-cluster matrix (e.g., raw reads or expression counts) — the enrichment test requires the bacLIFE clustering module's binary matrix Genome lifestyle labels are unavailable or lack the >0.8 random-forest confidence threshold, so group membership cannot be trusted for the 2x2 contingency tables You need genomic regions enriched in virulence factors from pLAG positions rather than per-gene enrichment statistics — that is a separate downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when the deCS query input is a list of genes — e.g., a top-N cluster marker gene table with 'cluster' and 'gene' columns or trait-associated genes — rather than a gene expression profile matrix.
skills.name: fisher-exact-test-gene-set-enrichment
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-test-gene-set-enrichment Use when the deCS query input is a list of genes — e.g., a top-N cluster marker gene table with 'cluster' and 'gene' columns or trait-associated genes — rather than a gene expression profile matrix. The query is a full gene expression profile or scaled z-score matrix rather than a gene list — use deCS.correlation (Pearson/Spearman correlation) instead The biological sample is malignant/cancer tissue, where expression differences between healthy reference profiles and malignant cells bias the mapping-based annotation The goal is to discover novel cell types not represented in the reference panels, since deCS is a mapping-based toolkit http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 deCS.fisher annotates query gene lists (e.g., cluster marker genes) as cell types by testing enrichment against cell-type-specific genes (CTgenes, top 5% by t-score/z-score) from a reference panel via Fisher's exact test, assigning the cell type with the highest intersection ratio (IR). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: deCS.fisher annotates query gene lists (e.g., cluster marker genes) as cell types by testing enrichment against cell-type-specific genes (CTgenes, top 5% by t-score/z-score) from a reference panel via Fisher's exact test, assigning the cell type with the highest intersection ratio (IR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is a full gene expression profile or scaled z-score matrix rather than a gene list — use deCS.correlation (Pearson/Spearman correlation) instead The biological sample is malignant/cancer tissue, where expression differences between healthy reference profiles and malignant cells bias the mapping-based annotation The goal is to discover novel cell types not represented in the reference panels, since deCS is a mapping-based toolkit

skills.description: Use when running rROMA/Roma PC1-based gene set activity analysis on normalized expression matrices and needing to protect outlier-gene removal (leave-one-out L1 z-scores) from incorrectly excluding genes whose apparent outlier status is not specific to individual gene sets.
skills.name: fisher-exact-test-outlier-filtering
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-test-outlier-filtering Use when running rROMA/Roma PC1-based gene set activity analysis on normalized expression matrices and needing to protect outlier-gene removal (leave-one-out L1 z-scores) from incorrectly excluding genes whose apparent outlier status is not specific to individual gene sets. When genes present in fewer than the defined number of gene sets are at stake — these are exempt and must not be flagged as outliers When data are not normalized — rRoma requires normalized input (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) When you need sample-level filtering rather than gene-level outlier handling — the two-step sample filter (number of detected genes plus PCA projection) is a separate procedure http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A safeguard step of rROMA's outlier-gene filtering that uses a Fisher exact test to compare a gene's outlier proportion across gene set collections to the average proportion of all genes, combined with an exemption for genes present in few gene sets and a cap on the removable fraction per gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: A safeguard step of rROMA's outlier-gene filtering that uses a Fisher exact test to compare a gene's outlier proportion across gene set collections to the average proportion of all genes, combined with an exemption for genes present in few gene sets and a cap on the removable fraction per gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When genes present in fewer than the defined number of gene sets are at stake — these are exempt and must not be flagged as outliers When data are not normalized — rRoma requires normalized input (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) When you need sample-level filtering rather than gene-level outlier handling — the two-step sample filter (number of detected genes plus PCA projection) is a separate procedure

skills.description: Use when implementing or simulating the TSNP two-stage dose-finding design and you must decide which dose levels are sufficiently safe (not overly toxic) to remain candidates for the OBD.
skills.name: fisher-exact-toxicity-admissibility-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-toxicity-admissibility-testing Use when implementing or simulating the TSNP two-stage dose-finding design and you must decide which dose levels are sufficiently safe (not overly toxic) to remain candidates for the OBD. The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is appropriate only for binary outcomes observable shortly after treatment initiation The trial targets drug combinations rather than single-agent dose finding — extending TSNP to combination trials is future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fisher's exact-test admissibility screening from the TSNP phase I/II design: at each dose, test H0: pj <= phi (highest acceptable DLT rate) and exclude doses whose p-value rj falls below the nominal level cT, building the toxicity admissible set used for OBD selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Fisher's exact-test admissibility screening from the TSNP phase I/II design: at each dose, test H0: pj <= phi (highest acceptable DLT rate) and exclude doses whose p-value rj falls below the nominal level cT, building the toxicity admissible set used for OBD selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is appropriate only for binary outcomes observable shortly after treatment initiation The trial targets drug combinations rather than single-agent dose finding — extending TSNP to combination trials is future work

skills.description: Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (Compound Poisson) GLMs to scRNA-seq counts and Wald-type standard errors, p-values, or confidence intervals are needed for regression coefficients after estimating (ϕ, p) by profile likelihood.
skills.name: fisher-information-standard-error-estimation
skills.search_text: fisher-information-standard-error-estimation Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (Compound Poisson) GLMs to scRNA-seq counts and Wald-type standard errors, p-values, or confidence intervals are needed for regression coefficients after estimating (ϕ, p) by profile likelihood. When only point estimates of β are needed (e.g., effect-size exploration) without inference — the full Fisher information computation adds cost without benefit When the goal is zero-inflated (ZICP) model inference, which is instead estimated via Newton-Raphson rather than this Fisher-information-based scoring step When zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes — the paper notes Tweedieverse is not architected for that situation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes standard errors of the Tweedie GLM coefficient vector (β̂) from the observed Fisher information matrix, whose (j,l)-th entry is (1/ϕ)Σ μ_i^(2−p) X_ij X_il, as the final step of the per-gene Tweedieverse fitting procedure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Computes standard errors of the Tweedie GLM coefficient vector (β̂) from the observed Fisher information matrix, whose (j,l)-th entry is (1/ϕ)Σ μ_i^(2−p) X_ij X_il, as the final step of the per-gene Tweedieverse fitting procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only point estimates of β are needed (e.g., effect-size exploration) without inference — the full Fisher information computation adds cost without benefit When the goal is zero-inflated (ZICP) model inference, which is instead estimated via Newton-Raphson rather than this Fisher-information-based scoring step When zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes — the paper notes Tweedieverse is not architected for that situation

skills.description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset has cluster-specific gene signatures and you need to weight those genes by discriminability before scoring target cells, especially with batch effect or imbalanced library sizes.
skills.name: fisher-lda-gene-weight-estimation
skills.search_text: fisher-lda-gene-weight-estimation Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset has cluster-specific gene signatures and you need to weight those genes by discriminability before scoring target cells, especially with batch effect or imbalanced library sizes. Neither the reference nor the target data is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalization, not log-transformed data You need imputation for highly shallow target data — this is deferred to future work and not implemented in scID http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stage 2 of the scID pipeline: estimate discriminative weights for reference-cluster gene signatures using a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, by first selecting putative positive/negative training populations via differential precision-recall (DPR) and then fitting gene weights with scID_weight. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Stage 2 of the scID pipeline: estimate discriminative weights for reference-cluster gene signatures using a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, by first selecting putative positive/negative training populations via differential precision-recall (DPR) and then fitting gene weights with scID_weight.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Neither the reference nor the target data is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — scID is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalization, not log-transformed data You need imputation for highly shallow target data — this is deferred to future work and not implemented in scID

skills.description: Use when a subpopulation-specific gene ranking must integrate expression evidence from scRNA-seq with enhancer-promoter contact evidence from bulk HiChIP loop counts, e.g. to improve GO enrichment of subpopulations at low sequencing depth.
skills.name: fisher-pvalue-combination
skills.search_text: fisher-pvalue-combination Use when a subpopulation-specific gene ranking must integrate expression evidence from scRNA-seq with enhancer-promoter contact evidence from bulk HiChIP loop counts, e.g. to improve GO enrichment of subpopulations at low sequencing depth. No bulk HiChIP (or other enhancer-promoter loop) data are available for the same cell population — only scRNA-seq p-values can be computed, so no combination is possible. Genes are not shared between the expression matrix and the HiChIP interaction file, since the README restricts HiChIP interactions to 'the genes in scRNA-seq data and enhancers in scATAC-seq data'. The goal is deconvolution or coupled clustering itself (DC3's dc3.py step), not downstream gene-set prioritization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Combines per-gene scRNA-seq p-values (one-tailed t-test on the subpopulation-specific expression matrix) with HiChIP enhancer-promoter binomial-test p-values via Fisher's method, so that loop-profile evidence sharpens gene-set selection for subpopulation GO enrichment (Table 2 of DC3). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Combines per-gene scRNA-seq p-values (one-tailed t-test on the subpopulation-specific expression matrix) with HiChIP enhancer-promoter binomial-test p-values via Fisher's method, so that loop-profile evidence sharpens gene-set selection for subpopulation GO enrichment (Table 2 of DC3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No bulk HiChIP (or other enhancer-promoter loop) data are available for the same cell population — only scRNA-seq p-values can be computed, so no combination is possible. Genes are not shared between the expression matrix and the HiChIP interaction file, since the README restricts HiChIP interactions to 'the genes in scRNA-seq data and enhancers in scATAC-seq data'. The goal is deconvolution or coupled clustering itself (DC3's dc3.py step), not downstream gene-set prioritization.

skills.description: Use when a directed/undirected reference network must be re-weighted from case-control high-throughput data (e.g., GSE172114 COVID-19 RNA-seq) so edge costs encode between-group correlation differences prior to Steiner tree or perturbation extraction.
skills.name: fisher-r-to-z-network-weighting
skills.search_text: fisher-r-to-z-network-weighting Use when a directed/undirected reference network must be re-weighted from case-control high-throughput data (e.g., GSE172114 COVID-19 RNA-seq) so edge costs encode between-group correlation differences prior to Steiner tree or perturbation extraction. There is no binary group variable (single-condition data) — Fisher r-to-z tests between-group correlation differences, so it is undefined without two conditions. The input is already an edge-weighted perturbation graph or a precomputed SEM perturbation output rather than raw expression data plus a reference interactome. Data are not approximately continuous/normalizable (e.g., raw counts without the nonparanormal transform), since r-to-z correlation tests assume transformed expression values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Weights edges of a reference interactome (e.g., the KEGG interactome of 5007 nodes / 44755 edges) by testing group differences between correlation coefficients with Fisher's 'r-to-z' method, producing a group-difference weighted graph used to extract perturbed backbones with SEMtree(). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Weights edges of a reference interactome (e.g., the KEGG interactome of 5007 nodes / 44755 edges) by testing group differences between correlation coefficients with Fisher's 'r-to-z' method, producing a group-difference weighted graph used to extract perturbed backbones with SEMtree().
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no binary group variable (single-condition data) — Fisher r-to-z tests between-group correlation differences, so it is undefined without two conditions. The input is already an edge-weighted perturbation graph or a precomputed SEM perturbation output rather than raw expression data plus a reference interactome. Data are not approximately continuous/normalizable (e.g., raw counts without the nonparanormal transform), since r-to-z correlation tests assume transformed expression values.

skills.description: Use when fitting a scDBM or negative-binomial count model to a scRNA-seq UMI count matrix and the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ needs to be estimated or periodically refreshed during training.
skills.name: fisher-scoring-optimization
skills.search_text: fisher-scoring-optimization Use when fitting a scDBM or negative-binomial count model to a scRNA-seq UMI count matrix and the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ needs to be estimated or periodically refreshed during training. Input is not raw UMI counts (e.g., already log-normalized or Smart-seq2-style non-count data), since the negative-binomial variance μ + μ²/θ parametrization assumes count data The goal is batch correction — scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects, and batch correction was outside the paper's scope A benchmarked/validated dispersion estimator is required: the paper describes this Fisher scoring module but reports no separate quantitative benchmark for it http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ of a negative-binomial likelihood in the scDBM generative model via a regularized Fisher scoring update, alternated with stochastic-gradient training. This is the mechanism by which the scDBM adapts deep Boltzmann machines to model scRNA-seq UMI counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Estimates the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ of a negative-binomial likelihood in the scDBM generative model via a regularized Fisher scoring update, alternated with stochastic-gradient training. This is the mechanism by which the scDBM adapts deep Boltzmann machines to model scRNA-seq UMI counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw UMI counts (e.g., already log-normalized or Smart-seq2-style non-count data), since the negative-binomial variance μ + μ²/θ parametrization assumes count data The goal is batch correction — scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects, and batch correction was outside the paper's scope A benchmarked/validated dispersion estimator is required: the paper describes this Fisher scoring module but reports no separate quantitative benchmark for it

skills.description: Use when you have two condition-specific FPKM expression matrices and a fixed reference network, and need to test whether each edge's Pearson correlation differs significantly between conditions.
skills.name: fisher-z-transformation-statistics
skills.search_text: fisher-z-transformation-statistics Use when you have two condition-specific FPKM expression matrices and a fixed reference network, and need to test whether each edge's Pearson correlation differs significantly between conditions. The cancer type (or condition comparison) has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ distribution's standard-normal approximation was validated only for sample size >15 There is no predefined reference network constraining which gene pairs to test — the test is applied only to gene pairs connected in Gene_Net, not genome-wide The expression data are raw counts rather than FPKM-normalized, since Pearson correlations are computed on FPKM-normalized values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies differential co-expression edges between two physiological conditions by Fisher Z-transforming Pearson correlation coefficients and applying a ΔZ Z-test per gene pair, as used in WMDS.net on TCGA RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Quantifies differential co-expression edges between two physiological conditions by Fisher Z-transforming Pearson correlation coefficients and applying a ΔZ Z-test per gene pair, as used in WMDS.net on TCGA RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cancer type (or condition comparison) has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ distribution's standard-normal approximation was validated only for sample size >15 There is no predefined reference network constraining which gene pairs to test — the test is applied only to gene pairs connected in Gene_Net, not genome-wide The expression data are raw counts rather than FPKM-normalized, since Pearson correlations are computed on FPKM-normalized values

skills.description: Use when discrete, mutually exclusive counts form a 2x2 table needing an exact P-value — e.g. insertion-carrying vs wild-type reads split by intronic/exonic class at a SCISSOR-flagged junction, or co-altered gene counts between cohorts.
skills.name: fishers-exact-contingency-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-contingency-testing Use when discrete, mutually exclusive counts form a 2x2 table needing an exact P-value — e.g. insertion-carrying vs wild-type reads split by intronic/exonic class at a SCISSOR-flagged junction, or co-altered gene counts between cohorts. The variable is continuous base-level coverage or pileup intensity rather than discrete counts — SCISSOR's Scissor function on build_pileup output (shape change detection) is the appropriate route, not an exact test on counts. Counts are not independent or marginals are not verified against the extracted read set (e.g. paired reads from one fragment counted twice), which violates the exact test's assumptions. The goal is cohort-level shape outlier discovery rather than testing a pre-specified contingency table of co-altered gene counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Exact test on 2x2 (r x c) contingency tables of discrete counts, used in the SCISSOR framework to test read-level insertion support at a flagged splice junction (intronic vs exonic x insertion present vs absent) and to compare the number of co-altered genes in every pair of cohorts, yielding odds ratios and exact P-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Exact test on 2x2 (r x c) contingency tables of discrete counts, used in the SCISSOR framework to test read-level insertion support at a flagged splice junction (intronic vs exonic x insertion present vs absent) and to compare the number of co-altered genes in every pair of cohorts, yielding odds ratios and exact P-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variable is continuous base-level coverage or pileup intensity rather than discrete counts — SCISSOR's Scissor function on build_pileup output (shape change detection) is the appropriate route, not an exact test on counts. Counts are not independent or marginals are not verified against the extracted read set (e.g. paired reads from one fragment counted twice), which violates the exact test's assumptions. The goal is cohort-level shape outlier discovery rather than testing a pre-specified contingency table of co-altered gene counts.

skills.description: Use when comparing a set of cell-type co-localization pairs detected on reconstructed or predicted spatial coordinates against a reference set of supported co-localizations, to quantify concordance with a p-value.
skills.name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing Use when comparing a set of cell-type co-localization pairs detected on reconstructed or predicted spatial coordinates against a reference set of supported co-localizations, to quantify concordance with a p-value. When ground-truth locations exist (ST data with truth cell locations) — use Moran's R directly on the reference instead of testing reconstructed coordinates against it When query SC data has a large gap or mismatch from the ST reference, where forced SC-to-ST assignment can introduce bias and reconstructed co-localizations may be unreliable When comparing continuous spatial expression gradients rather than discrete binary cell-type occupancy per location http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Uses 2x2 Fisher's exact tests to assess whether cell-type co-localization pairs detected on spatially reconstructed single-cell data (e.g. CellContrast/CeLEry/SageNet coordinates of mouse SC atlas sample S27, E8.5) are enriched among reference co-localizations from SeqFISH ground-truth ST datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Uses 2x2 Fisher's exact tests to assess whether cell-type co-localization pairs detected on spatially reconstructed single-cell data (e.g. CellContrast/CeLEry/SageNet coordinates of mouse SC atlas sample S27, E8.5) are enriched among reference co-localizations from SeqFISH ground-truth ST datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth locations exist (ST data with truth cell locations) — use Moran's R directly on the reference instead of testing reconstructed coordinates against it When query SC data has a large gap or mismatch from the ST reference, where forced SC-to-ST assignment can introduce bias and reconstructed co-localizations may be unreliable When comparing continuous spatial expression gradients rather than discrete binary cell-type occupancy per location

skills.description: Use when two sample groups yield sets of candidate regions (e.g., predicted dsRNA regions per sample) and you need to test whether the shared vs group-specific overlap fractions differ significantly between groups.
skills.name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing Use when two sample groups yield sets of candidate regions (e.g., predicted dsRNA regions per sample) and you need to test whether the shared vs group-specific overlap fractions differ significantly between groups. Input regions have not yet been classified per sample as candidate dsRNA regions — run dsRID prediction first rather than testing raw BAM-derived candidates. The comparison involves more than two groups or paired/clustered region-level counts where a 2x2 contingency test is inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Statistical testing skill for comparing overlap/enrichment of predicted dsRNA regions between sample groups (AD vs control) using Fisher's exact test on overlap contingency counts, with Wilcoxon rank-sum as a complementary test on continuous fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Statistical testing skill for comparing overlap/enrichment of predicted dsRNA regions between sample groups (AD vs control) using Fisher's exact test on overlap contingency counts, with Wilcoxon rank-sum as a complementary test on continuous fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input regions have not yet been classified per sample as candidate dsRNA regions — run dsRID prediction first rather than testing raw BAM-derived candidates. The comparison involves more than two groups or paired/clustered region-level counts where a 2x2 contingency test is inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset has categorical clone assignments (e.g., mitochondrial clones from vireoSNP at probability >0.8) and independent cell labels (tumor vs non-tumor, CNV subclones) and you need to test enrichment of one clone in one label.
skills.name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing Use when a single-cell dataset has categorical clone assignments (e.g., mitochondrial clones from vireoSNP at probability >0.8) and independent cell labels (tumor vs non-tumor, CNV subclones) and you need to test enrichment of one clone in one label. When clone assignments are not confident — cells with vireoSNP assignment probability ≤0.8 should be excluded before testing, not forced into the contingency table When the label is continuous or multi-class without a prespecified contrast — Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 table requires two clones and two label categories When clone-label association is already established by genotype overlap rather than cell-level contingency (e.g., identical variant profiles), a test would be circular http://edamontology.org/topic_3050 A two-sided Fisher's exact test to assess whether a specific mitochondrial clone (e.g., mtDNA clone 1 assigned by MQuad/vireoSNP) is enriched among annotated cells (e.g., tumor cells) relative to another clone, using a 2x2 contingency table of clone-by-label counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: A two-sided Fisher's exact test to assess whether a specific mitochondrial clone (e.g., mtDNA clone 1 assigned by MQuad/vireoSNP) is enriched among annotated cells (e.g., tumor cells) relative to another clone, using a 2x2 contingency table of clone-by-label counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When clone assignments are not confident — cells with vireoSNP assignment probability ≤0.8 should be excluded before testing, not forced into the contingency table When the label is continuous or multi-class without a prespecified contrast — Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 table requires two clones and two label categories When clone-label association is already established by genotype overlap rather than cell-level contingency (e.g., identical variant profiles), a test would be circular

skills.description: Use when testing whether a lead variant set (e.g. sQTLs at FDR < 0.05) is enriched in discrete annotation categories relative to matched non-sQTLs or intron sets, and you need odds ratios with Fisher's exact p-values.
skills.name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing Use when testing whether a lead variant set (e.g. sQTLs at FDR < 0.05) is enriched in discrete annotation categories relative to matched non-sQTLs or intron sets, and you need odds ratios with Fisher's exact p-values. When variants need to be matched on more than location bin and MAF, or when a regression framework accounting for covariates/confounders is required (e.g. fgwas-style functional enrichment modeling) rather than simple 2x2 contingency tests When testing enrichment of continuous or non-categorical scores rather than discrete annotation membership When the variant sets cannot be validly matched/controlled — unbalanced MAF or LD structure between cases and controls can inflate Fisher's exact odds ratios spuriously http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply two-sided Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables to test whether sQTL variants are over-represented in genomic/annotation categories (post-transcriptionally spliced introns, splice donor/acceptor sites, H3K36me3 marks, GWAS LD hits) relative to matched controls, reporting odds ratios and FDR-corrected p-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Apply two-sided Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables to test whether sQTL variants are over-represented in genomic/annotation categories (post-transcriptionally spliced introns, splice donor/acceptor sites, H3K36me3 marks, GWAS LD hits) relative to matched controls, reporting odds ratios and FDR-corrected p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When variants need to be matched on more than location bin and MAF, or when a regression framework accounting for covariates/confounders is required (e.g. fgwas-style functional enrichment modeling) rather than simple 2x2 contingency tests When testing enrichment of continuous or non-categorical scores rather than discrete annotation membership When the variant sets cannot be validly matched/controlled — unbalanced MAF or LD structure between cases and controls can inflate Fisher's exact odds ratios spuriously

skills.description: Use when you have predicted molecular subtype labels (e.g., from a DeepCC model via get_DeepCC_label) plus cohort clinical metadata with ER/PR/HER2 receptor status and survival outcomes, and need to demonstrate clinical relevance.
skills.name: fishers-exact-receptor-association-testing
skills.search_text: fishers-exact-receptor-association-testing Use when you have predicted molecular subtype labels (e.g., from a DeepCC model via get_DeepCC_label) plus cohort clinical metadata with ER/PR/HER2 receptor status and survival outcomes, and need to demonstrate clinical relevance. Your classification scheme cannot resolve Luminal A vs Luminal B (e.g., BluePrint, which 'can only predict Luminal, HER2, and Basal subtypes') — contingency structure will differ from the DeepCC/PAM50 comparison You are using prognostic risk tools like MammaPrint or Oncotype DX, which predict recurrence risk categories rather than biological subtypes, so receptor-association contingency tests are not the appropriate validation Your goal is unsupervised clustering of patients — DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients' http://edamontology.org/topic_3418 Validates that DeepCC-predicted breast cancer subtypes are biologically meaningful by testing associations between predicted Luminal/HER2 calls and ER/PR/HER2 receptor status via Fisher's exact tests in R, benchmarked against PAM50 with Kaplan-Meier disease-free survival and log-rank tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Validates that DeepCC-predicted breast cancer subtypes are biologically meaningful by testing associations between predicted Luminal/HER2 calls and ER/PR/HER2 receptor status via Fisher's exact tests in R, benchmarked against PAM50 with Kaplan-Meier disease-free survival and log-rank tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your classification scheme cannot resolve Luminal A vs Luminal B (e.g., BluePrint, which 'can only predict Luminal, HER2, and Basal subtypes') — contingency structure will differ from the DeepCC/PAM50 comparison You are using prognostic risk tools like MammaPrint or Oncotype DX, which predict recurrence risk categories rather than biological subtypes, so receptor-association contingency tests are not the appropriate validation Your goal is unsupervised clustering of patients — DeepCC is 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients'

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus cell-level categorical metadata and need a per-cell numeric score of plasticity/local state heterogeneity on the tree.
skills.name: fitch-hartigan-small-parsimony-scoring
skills.search_text: fitch-hartigan-small-parsimony-scoring Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus cell-level categorical metadata and need a per-cell numeric score of plasticity/local state heterogeneity on the tree. The metadata of interest is continuous/numeric rather than categorical — Fitch-Hartigan parsimony requires discrete character states There is no cell-resolved phylogeny available (cells as leaves); the score is defined entirely by subtree structure You want relative fitness quantification from the phylogeny — the article explicitly notes such approaches 'are not directly supported within our software' http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Reconstructs PhyloVision's single-cell plasticity analysis, which quantifies how heterogeneous the ancestral neighborhoods of each cell are for a user-provided categorical meta-data column by running Fitch-Hartigan small-parsimony on every internal-node subtree and averaging edge-normalized parsimony scores along root-to-leaf paths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Reconstructs PhyloVision's single-cell plasticity analysis, which quantifies how heterogeneous the ancestral neighborhoods of each cell are for a user-provided categorical meta-data column by running Fitch-Hartigan small-parsimony on every internal-node subtree and averaging edge-normalized parsimony scores along root-to-leaf paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metadata of interest is continuous/numeric rather than categorical — Fitch-Hartigan parsimony requires discrete character states There is no cell-resolved phylogeny available (cells as leaves); the score is defined entirely by subtree structure You want relative fitness quantification from the phylogeny — the article explicitly notes such approaches 'are not directly supported within our software'

skills.description: Use when you have high-dimensional per-cell feature vectors (e.g., Miscell latent features from scRNA-seq data) and need a fast, reproducible 2D t-SNE embedding for visualization and cluster extraction.
skills.name: fitsne-visual-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: fitsne-visual-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have high-dimensional per-cell feature vectors (e.g., Miscell latent features from scRNA-seq data) and need a fast, reproducible 2D t-SNE embedding for visualization and cluster extraction. If the goal is accurate global structure or trajectory inference rather than visualization/density clustering — t-SNE distances are not globally meaningful If batch effects are present, since Miscell/FIt-SNE do not internally batch-correct; correct batch effects before embedding If the dataset is very small, since Miscell (which produces the features) demands a large sample size for good performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Accelerates t-SNE embedding of single-cell latent features (e.g., Miscell-encoded representations) using FFT-accelerated interpolation-based t-SNE (FIt-SNE), producing a 2D embedding suitable for visualization and downstream density clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Accelerates t-SNE embedding of single-cell latent features (e.g., Miscell-encoded representations) using FFT-accelerated interpolation-based t-SNE (FIt-SNE), producing a 2D embedding suitable for visualization and downstream density clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is accurate global structure or trajectory inference rather than visualization/density clustering — t-SNE distances are not globally meaningful If batch effects are present, since Miscell/FIt-SNE do not internally batch-correct; correct batch effects before embedding If the dataset is very small, since Miscell (which produces the features) demands a large sample size for good performance

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how a cross-modality translation model's performance degrades with limited paired training cells, or when testing whether data augmentation compensates for reduced sample size.
skills.name: five-fold-cross-validation-cell-subsampling
skills.search_text: five-fold-cross-validation-cell-subsampling Use when you must quantify how a cross-modality translation model's performance degrades with limited paired training cells, or when testing whether data augmentation compensates for reduced sample size. When abundant paired training cells are available and the goal is not to study limited-sample behavior — a single train/test split suffices. When data are unpaired and no cross-modal correspondence exists for holdout evaluation — the subsampling design requires paired profiles to score held-out cells.
