When the target task is a downstream biological question rather than a benchmark of translation robustness to subsampling. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A benchmarking design that repeatedly holds out paired cells across five cross-validation folds while varying the training fraction (20%–100%) to test whether a method (here, scButterfly variants) retains translation accuracy as paired training cells become limited. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking design that repeatedly holds out paired cells across five cross-validation folds while varying the training fraction (20%–100%) to test whether a method (here, scButterfly variants) retains translation accuracy as paired training cells become limited.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When abundant paired training cells are available and the goal is not to study limited-sample behavior — a single train/test split suffices. When data are unpaired and no cross-modal correspondence exists for holdout evaluation — the subsampling design requires paired profiles to score held-out cells. When the target task is a downstream biological question rather than a benchmark of translation robustness to subsampling.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a graph-based driver-gene predictor (e.g., DGMP on DawnNet/KEGG/RegNetwork) with 5-fold CV and you need per-gene probability logits aggregated into mean±std AUPRC/AUROC across folds.
skills.name: five-fold-cross-validation-metric-computation
skills.search_text: five-fold-cross-validation-metric-computation Use when benchmarking a graph-based driver-gene predictor (e.g., DGMP on DawnNet/KEGG/RegNetwork) with 5-fold CV and you need per-gene probability logits aggregated into mean±std AUPRC/AUROC across folds. The goal is patient-level driver gene prediction rather than per-gene evaluation — averaging omics across all samples ignores individual cancer patient characteristics The network is undirected or lacks a supplied directed GRN, so the DGCN directionality component cannot be exercised as in the DawnNet ablation Only a single train/test split is available and no 5-fold cross-validation logits can be collected, making the fold-aggregated mean ± std comparison impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce DGMP's 5-fold cross-validation evaluation on the DawnNet multi-omics dataset: run ablated variants (DGCN-only, MLP-only, DGCN+MLP) via DGMP.py, collect per-gene driver/non-driver probability logits and mean 5-CV accuracy from './code/result/', and compute AUPRC/AUROC to confirm that jointing DGCN and MLP improves cancer driver gene identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Reproduce DGMP's 5-fold cross-validation evaluation on the DawnNet multi-omics dataset: run ablated variants (DGCN-only, MLP-only, DGCN+MLP) via DGMP.py, collect per-gene driver/non-driver probability logits and mean 5-CV accuracy from './code/result/', and compute AUPRC/AUROC to confirm that jointing DGCN and MLP improves cancer driver gene identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is patient-level driver gene prediction rather than per-gene evaluation — averaging omics across all samples ignores individual cancer patient characteristics The network is undirected or lacks a supplied directed GRN, so the DGCN directionality component cannot be exercised as in the DawnNet ablation Only a single train/test split is available and no 5-fold cross-validation logits can be collected, making the fold-aggregated mean ± std comparison impossible

skills.description: Use when comparing cross-modality translation methods on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq datasets and a by-cell resampling design is needed so per-fold metrics can feed paired statistical tests (one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank).
skills.name: five-fold-cross-validation-partitioning
skills.search_text: five-fold-cross-validation-partitioning Use when comparing cross-modality translation methods on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq datasets and a by-cell resampling design is needed so per-fold metrics can feed paired statistical tests (one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank). Data are unpaired across modalities — use scButterfly's diagonal/unpaired training mode instead of by-cell fold splitting A single train/test split suffices and no paired statistical comparison across folds is intended The evaluation target is perturbation-response prediction or cell-type annotation rather than cross-validation benchmarking of translation methods A benchmarking protocol that partitions each cell into five disjoint folds so that every held-out fold is translated in both directions (RNA→ATAC and ATAC→RNA), yielding 140 paired evaluations (7 datasets × 5 folds × 2 directions) for fair statistical comparison of cross-modality translators such as scButterfly-B/T/C against BABEL, Polarbear, and JAMIE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that partitions each cell into five disjoint folds so that every held-out fold is translated in both directions (RNA→ATAC and ATAC→RNA), yielding 140 paired evaluations (7 datasets × 5 folds × 2 directions) for fair statistical comparison of cross-modality translators such as scButterfly-B/T/C against BABEL, Polarbear, and JAMIE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired across modalities — use scButterfly's diagonal/unpaired training mode instead of by-cell fold splitting A single train/test split suffices and no paired statistical comparison across folds is intended The evaluation target is perturbation-response prediction or cell-type annotation rather than cross-validation benchmarking of translation methods

skills.description: Use when a single labeled scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. PBMC SCP424) must be split into train/test subsets to benchmark supervised cell-type identification methods under self-projection, before computing accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate.
skills.name: five-fold-cross-validation-splitting
skills.search_text: five-fold-cross-validation-splitting Use when a single labeled scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. PBMC SCP424) must be split into train/test subsets to benchmark supervised cell-type identification methods under self-projection, before computing accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate. Cross-platform prediction where training and testing datasets come from different studies (e.g. seven-platform PBMC training vs six-platform testing) — the split is already defined by dataset origin, not by within-dataset folding Datasets already partitioned with caret's createDataPartition (the paper's alternative single-split scheme) or with a predefined train/test division — do not re-fold Datasets with very few cells per cell type, where a fifth of cells held out per fold leaves training folds without representatives of a type http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Partitions a labeled scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. PBMC SCP424 count matrix with manual labels) into five folds with caret's createFolds and runs five rounds of cross-validation (four folds training, one testing) so automatic cell-type identification methods can be compared on accuracy, mean F1-score and unlabeling rate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Partitions a labeled scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. PBMC SCP424 count matrix with manual labels) into five folds with caret's createFolds and runs five rounds of cross-validation (four folds training, one testing) so automatic cell-type identification methods can be compared on accuracy, mean F1-score and unlabeling rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cross-platform prediction where training and testing datasets come from different studies (e.g. seven-platform PBMC training vs six-platform testing) — the split is already defined by dataset origin, not by within-dataset folding Datasets already partitioned with caret's createDataPartition (the paper's alternative single-split scheme) or with a predefined train/test division — do not re-fold Datasets with very few cells per cell type, where a fifth of cells held out per fold leaves training folds without representatives of a type

skills.description: Use when raw nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt m6A positive/negative samples from tissue-specific benchmark datasets like h_b, m_k, r_l) must be encoded as fixed-length numeric matrices before feeding a deep-learning model.
skills.name: fixed-length-feature-vector-construction
skills.search_text: fixed-length-feature-vector-construction Use when raw nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt m6A positive/negative samples from tissue-specific benchmark datasets like h_b, m_k, r_l) must be encoded as fixed-length numeric matrices before feeding a deep-learning model. Input is already a numeric feature table or embedding (e.g., Gene2Vec-style vectors) rather than raw nucleotide sequences Sequences are not composed solely of A/U/C/G (e.g., contain N or lowercase ambiguous codes) and no handling decision has been made The downstream model expects a different sequence representation (e.g., k-mer or SVM-based features as in iRNA-m6A) rather than one-hot CNN input http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Converts variable-text RNA sequences into fixed-length numeric feature vectors via the one-hot scheme used by im6A-TS-CNN: each nucleotide A/U/C/G becomes a 4-dimensional binary vector, so a 41-nt m6A benchmark segment yields a 4 x 41 = 164-dimensional input suitable for CNN training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Converts variable-text RNA sequences into fixed-length numeric feature vectors via the one-hot scheme used by im6A-TS-CNN: each nucleotide A/U/C/G becomes a 4-dimensional binary vector, so a 41-nt m6A benchmark segment yields a 4 x 41 = 164-dimensional input suitable for CNN training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table or embedding (e.g., Gene2Vec-style vectors) rather than raw nucleotide sequences Sequences are not composed solely of A/U/C/G (e.g., contain N or lowercase ambiguous codes) and no handling decision has been made The downstream model expects a different sequence representation (e.g., k-mer or SVM-based features as in iRNA-m6A) rather than one-hot CNN input

skills.description: Use when segmented single-cell masks (e.g. from MIRIAM's membrane-extended segmentation) must be converted into uniform binary matrices to train or apply a deep learning-based cell shape descriptor.
skills.name: fixed-size-cell-shape-resizing-128x128
skills.search_text: fixed-size-cell-shape-resizing-128x128 Use when segmented single-cell masks (e.g. from MIRIAM's membrane-extended segmentation) must be converted into uniform binary matrices to train or apply a deep learning-based cell shape descriptor. Input is already a feature/latent-vector table or marker intensity table — resizing operates on raw cell masks, not on extracted features Cells of interest are not segmented (no membrane-resolved masks); MIRIAM's resizing step assumes the membrane-extension segmentation has already produced single-cell masks The analysis goal is marker intensity quantification over nucleus/membrane/cytoplasm compartments rather than shape characterization Prepares segmented cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline as fixed-size 128x128 binary matrices so they can serve as standardized inputs to the autoencoder neural network used for the cell shape descriptor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Prepares segmented cell masks from the MIRIAM pipeline as fixed-size 128x128 binary matrices so they can serve as standardized inputs to the autoencoder neural network used for the cell shape descriptor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/latent-vector table or marker intensity table — resizing operates on raw cell masks, not on extracted features Cells of interest are not segmented (no membrane-resolved masks); MIRIAM's resizing step assumes the membrane-extension segmentation has already produced single-cell masks The analysis goal is marker intensity quantification over nucleus/membrane/cytoplasm compartments rather than shape characterization

skills.description: Use when a static, unsynchronised flow cytometry dataset of a heterogeneous population (e.g. dissociated HCT116 spheroids stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) must be mapped from pseudotime onto a real spatial (distance-from-surface) or temporal (cell age) scale.
skills.name: flow-cytometry-marker-profile-analysis
skills.search_text: flow-cytometry-marker-profile-analysis Use when a static, unsynchronised flow cytometry dataset of a heterogeneous population (e.g. dissociated HCT116 spheroids stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) must be mapped from pseudotime onto a real spatial (distance-from-surface) or temporal (cell age) scale. No defensible true-scale distribution can be defined — e.g. stem cell differentiation, where the paper notes constructing a target distribution is challenging and would require cell death and division rates at every stage The pseudotemporal cell order from the trajectory-inference algorithm is untrustworthy, since MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order Data are already time-resolved (e.g. single-cell time-lapse microscopy), so no pseudotime-to-real-scale transformation is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Recover marker profiles (Ki-67, p27, DNA, RNA, geminin, forward scatter) on true temporal or spatial scales from static flow cytometric snapshots by transforming single-cell pseudotime with MAPiT, using prior knowledge of the real-scale cell-density distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: Recover marker profiles (Ki-67, p27, DNA, RNA, geminin, forward scatter) on true temporal or spatial scales from static flow cytometric snapshots by transforming single-cell pseudotime with MAPiT, using prior knowledge of the real-scale cell-density distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No defensible true-scale distribution can be defined — e.g. stem cell differentiation, where the paper notes constructing a target distribution is challenging and would require cell death and division rates at every stage The pseudotemporal cell order from the trajectory-inference algorithm is untrustworthy, since MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order Data are already time-resolved (e.g. single-cell time-lapse microscopy), so no pseudotime-to-real-scale transformation is needed

skills.description: Use when raw FCS flow cytometry measurements (e.g. spheroid-derived HCT116 cells stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27 and forward scatter) must be cleaned of doublets, dead cells and outliers before computing pseudotime ordering.
skills.name: flow-cytometry-quality-gating
skills.search_text: flow-cytometry-quality-gating Use when raw FCS flow cytometry measurements (e.g. spheroid-derived HCT116 cells stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27 and forward scatter) must be cleaned of doublets, dead cells and outliers before computing pseudotime ordering. The data are already gated and only pseudotime values are missing (proceed directly to trajectory inference) The input is single-cell imaging or time-lapse microscopy data rather than cytometric FCS measurements The downstream analysis does not require a pseudotemporal ordering (gating quality specifically supports trajectory inference for MAPiT-style transformations) Gates preprocessed single-cell flow cytometry measurements (e.g. DNA/RNA/Ki-67/p27 panels) in MATLAB to remove doublets, dead cells and outlier events before trajectory inference, then subsamples ~10000 gated cells for pseudotime algorithms such as Wanderlust or Diffusion Maps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: Gates preprocessed single-cell flow cytometry measurements (e.g. DNA/RNA/Ki-67/p27 panels) in MATLAB to remove doublets, dead cells and outlier events before trajectory inference, then subsamples ~10000 gated cells for pseudotime algorithms such as Wanderlust or Diffusion Maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already gated and only pseudotime values are missing (proceed directly to trajectory inference) The input is single-cell imaging or time-lapse microscopy data rather than cytometric FCS measurements The downstream analysis does not require a pseudotemporal ordering (gating quality specifically supports trajectory inference for MAPiT-style transformations)

skills.description: Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data span multiple cell states (e.g., HSPC differentiation to erythroid, myeloid, and lymphoid lineages) and you need multi-lineage trajectories between user-chosen source and target subpopulations, plus transition-specific genes and regulators.
skills.name: flow-network-trajectory-reconstruction
skills.search_text: flow-network-trajectory-reconstruction Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data span multiple cell states (e.g., HSPC differentiation to erythroid, myeloid, and lymphoid lineages) and you need multi-lineage trajectories between user-chosen source and target subpopulations, plus transition-specific genes and regulators. The analysis goal is a simple linear pseudotime ordering from a single root to a single endpoint — Waterfall or Monocle 1-style approaches suffice and CellRouter's multi-state machinery is unnecessary. The analysis goal is chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, or mass cytometry trajectory reconstruction — the article only envisions these applications as future work and does not demonstrate them. The goal is generating or functionally validating engraftable HSC-like cells — the article explicitly defers thorough characterization of CellRouter-identified genes for this purpose to future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct high-resolution, multi-state single-cell differentiation trajectories using CellRouter's flow-network algorithm, which is subpopulation-aware and requires no a priori knowledge of the number of branches or cell fates, unlike linear methods (Waterfall, Monocle 1), single-branch methods (Wishbone), or DPT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Reconstruct high-resolution, multi-state single-cell differentiation trajectories using CellRouter's flow-network algorithm, which is subpopulation-aware and requires no a priori knowledge of the number of branches or cell fates, unlike linear methods (Waterfall, Monocle 1), single-branch methods (Wishbone), or DPT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a simple linear pseudotime ordering from a single root to a single endpoint — Waterfall or Monocle 1-style approaches suffice and CellRouter's multi-state machinery is unnecessary. The analysis goal is chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, or mass cytometry trajectory reconstruction — the article only envisions these applications as future work and does not demonstrate them. The goal is generating or functionally validating engraftable HSC-like cells — the article explicitly defers thorough characterization of CellRouter-identified genes for this purpose to future work.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be resolved into distinct lineage trajectories toward rare or underrepresented cell fates, especially when a branching method like Monocle 2 collapses two lineages onto one branch.
skills.name: flow-network-transition-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: flow-network-transition-trajectory-inference Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be resolved into distinct lineage trajectories toward rare or underrepresented cell fates, especially when a branching method like Monocle 2 collapses two lineages onto one branch. Monocle 2/DDRTree alone suffices: only use this skill when trajectories between two chosen cell states (e.g., toward rare megakaryocyte/erythrocyte fates) are needed, since Monocle 2 'is not designed to reconstruct trajectories between any two chosen cell states' CellRouter was tested only on Unix-based systems/Mac and not on Windows, so avoid on Windows environments Analysis goal is differential expression or clustering only, with no cell-state transition or lineage ordering question http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs high-resolution multi-state cell-state transition trajectories between subpopulations (e.g., HSPC progenitors to megakaryocyte vs. erythrocyte fates) using CellRouter's flow network algorithm, which requires no a priori knowledge of the number of branches — unlike Monocle 2's DDRTree branching. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Reconstructs high-resolution multi-state cell-state transition trajectories between subpopulations (e.g., HSPC progenitors to megakaryocyte vs. erythrocyte fates) using CellRouter's flow network algorithm, which requires no a priori knowledge of the number of branches — unlike Monocle 2's DDRTree branching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Monocle 2/DDRTree alone suffices: only use this skill when trajectories between two chosen cell states (e.g., toward rare megakaryocyte/erythrocyte fates) are needed, since Monocle 2 'is not designed to reconstruct trajectories between any two chosen cell states' CellRouter was tested only on Unix-based systems/Mac and not on Windows, so avoid on Windows environments Analysis goal is differential expression or clustering only, with no cell-state transition or lineage ordering question

skills.description: Use when multi-sample IMC/CyTOF protein expression matrices and a manual cell-type annotation are available and you need sample-integrated, annotation-concordant clustering to quantify batch-removal benefit.
skills.name: flowsom-clustering-of-cytof-data
skills.search_text: flowsom-clustering-of-cytof-data Use when multi-sample IMC/CyTOF protein expression matrices and a manual cell-type annotation are available and you need sample-integrated, annotation-concordant clustering to quantify batch-removal benefit. Input is a single-sample, single-condition dataset where batch/sample variability is not a confounder — plain FlowSOM without scMerge2 adjustment suffices Only an embedding (low-dimensional representation) is available and an adjusted expression matrix cannot be produced; embedding-only outputs limit interpretability and downstream sample-level analysis Downstream analysis requires joint use of multi-modal information — scMerge2 integration was performed only within each modality FlowSOM clustering of CyTOF/imaging mass cytometry protein expression, applied here to the COVID-19 IMC dataset (23 samples, 38 protein markers), so that scMerge2-adjusted data yields cluster assignments that concord strongly with manual cell-type annotation (ARI rising from 0.13 to 0.58). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: FlowSOM clustering of CyTOF/imaging mass cytometry protein expression, applied here to the COVID-19 IMC dataset (23 samples, 38 protein markers), so that scMerge2-adjusted data yields cluster assignments that concord strongly with manual cell-type annotation (ARI rising from 0.13 to 0.58).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample, single-condition dataset where batch/sample variability is not a confounder — plain FlowSOM without scMerge2 adjustment suffices Only an embedding (low-dimensional representation) is available and an adjusted expression matrix cannot be produced; embedding-only outputs limit interpretability and downstream sample-level analysis Downstream analysis requires joint use of multi-modal information — scMerge2 integration was performed only within each modality

skills.description: Use when context-specific metabolic models of infected and healthy cells (e.g., rFASTCORMICS models with a VBOF) are available and you need to rank which gene knockouts reduce viral biomass without impairing host biomass.
skills.name: flux-balance-analysis-essentiality-scoring
skills.search_text: flux-balance-analysis-essentiality-scoring Use when context-specific metabolic models of infected and healthy cells (e.g., rFASTCORMICS models with a VBOF) are available and you need to rank which gene knockouts reduce viral biomass without impairing host biomass. When the virus cannot be represented by a biomass objective function (e.g., direct viral-proteome docking is required — the article notes targets come from network effects on the host metabolome, not the virus itself) When models are generic genome-scale reconstructions without context-specific pruning or a VBOF — essentiality calls will not reflect infected-lung conditions When the question is drug-toxicity assessment rather than target essentiality/safety ranking — toxicity here is only inferred from knockout safety scores, not measured http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Scores gene knockouts by running FBA single- and double-gene deletions on context-specific infected (viral biomass objective) and mock (host biomass) metabolic models, aggregating results into an essentiality score (infected models) and a safety score (mock models) to rank toxicity-favorable antiviral targets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Scores gene knockouts by running FBA single- and double-gene deletions on context-specific infected (viral biomass objective) and mock (host biomass) metabolic models, aggregating results into an essentiality score (infected models) and a safety score (mock models) to rank toxicity-favorable antiviral targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the virus cannot be represented by a biomass objective function (e.g., direct viral-proteome docking is required — the article notes targets come from network effects on the host metabolome, not the virus itself) When models are generic genome-scale reconstructions without context-specific pruning or a VBOF — essentiality calls will not reflect infected-lung conditions When the question is drug-toxicity assessment rather than target essentiality/safety ranking — toxicity here is only inferred from knockout safety scores, not measured

skills.description: Use when a generic genome-scale reconstruction (e.g., Recon2.04, Recon3D_01 from VMH) — possibly augmented with a custom biomass reaction such as a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) — must be made flux-consistent before context-specific reconstruction.
skills.name: flux-consistency-analysis
skills.search_text: flux-consistency-analysis Use when a generic genome-scale reconstruction (e.g., Recon2.04, Recon3D_01 from VMH) — possibly augmented with a custom biomass reaction such as a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) — must be made flux-consistent before context-specific reconstruction. The model is already flux-consistent (e.g., a published consistent reconstruction) — re-running FASTCC is redundant and may remove reactions unnecessarily. The goal is a fully unconstrained research model rather than an input to FASTCORMICS-family context-specific reconstruction, where removing reactions could alter the research network. The input is gene expression data rather than a model — consistency pruning operates on the reconstruction, not on expression data (expression enters later via rFASTCORMICS). http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Prunes blocked (flux-inconsistent) reactions from a genome-scale metabolic model using FASTCC in the COBRA Toolbox, as done in DCcov where VBOF-augmented Recon2.04 and Recon3D_01 infected generic models and their mock controls were converted into consistent inputs for rFASTCORMICS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Prunes blocked (flux-inconsistent) reactions from a genome-scale metabolic model using FASTCC in the COBRA Toolbox, as done in DCcov where VBOF-augmented Recon2.04 and Recon3D_01 infected generic models and their mock controls were converted into consistent inputs for rFASTCORMICS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is already flux-consistent (e.g., a published consistent reconstruction) — re-running FASTCC is redundant and may remove reactions unnecessarily. The goal is a fully unconstrained research model rather than an input to FASTCORMICS-family context-specific reconstruction, where removing reactions could alter the research network. The input is gene expression data rather than a model — consistency pruning operates on the reconstruction, not on expression data (expression enters later via rFASTCORMICS).

skills.description: Use when per-sample reaction fluxes (e.g., METAFlux compute_flux output) are available and the goal is to discover metabolically coherent sample subgroups, visualize them in UMAP, and relate them to phenotypes like glucose uptake or survival.
skills.name: flux-profile-clustering-umap-visualization
skills.search_text: flux-profile-clustering-umap-visualization Use when per-sample reaction fluxes (e.g., METAFlux compute_flux output) are available and the goal is to discover metabolically coherent sample subgroups, visualize them in UMAP, and relate them to phenotypes like glucose uptake or survival. When the analysis target is metabolic interaction among cell types within a tumor microenvironment — use METAFlux's single-cell workflow (compute_sc_flux / calculate_avg_exp with Seurat) instead of bulk-sample clustering When samples derive from cell lines rather than human tissue — the medium constraint should be cell_medium, not human_blood, before clustering fluxes When the goal is pathway-level activity summaries only (mean fluxes of reactions per pathway) rather than sample-level subgroup discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster samples on METAFlux-predicted metabolic flux profiles (13,082 Human-GEM reactions) and embed them with UMAP to reveal metabolically distinct subgroups — e.g., a 'LUSC-like' LUAD cluster in TCGA — that expression data alone does not resolve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Cluster samples on METAFlux-predicted metabolic flux profiles (13,082 Human-GEM reactions) and embed them with UMAP to reveal metabolically distinct subgroups — e.g., a 'LUSC-like' LUAD cluster in TCGA — that expression data alone does not resolve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis target is metabolic interaction among cell types within a tumor microenvironment — use METAFlux's single-cell workflow (compute_sc_flux / calculate_avg_exp with Seurat) instead of bulk-sample clustering When samples derive from cell lines rather than human tissue — the medium constraint should be cell_medium, not human_blood, before clustering fluxes When the goal is pathway-level activity summaries only (mean fluxes of reactions per pathway) rather than sample-level subgroup discovery

skills.description: Use when a predicted gene list (e.g., driver genes from WMDS.net) must be quantitatively compared against a benchmark gene set such as the 616-gene CGC list, and a precision-weighted Fβ score is the desired metric.
skills.name: fmeasure-precision-recall-scoring
skills.search_text: fmeasure-precision-recall-scoring Use when a predicted gene list (e.g., driver genes from WMDS.net) must be quantitatively compared against a benchmark gene set such as the 616-gene CGC list, and a precision-weighted Fβ score is the desired metric. When the comparison is against a gold standard that is not a fixed benchmark gene set (e.g., replication across independent cohorts) — precision/recall against CGC is not meaningful there When recall should dominate precision (β² > 1, e.g., β² = 2); this skill fixes β² = 0.2 to privilege precision in driver gene prediction When predictions are ranked scores rather than discrete gene lists — TP/FP counts require a defined predicted set http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Scores predicted driver gene lists against a curated benchmark (the 616-gene CGC set) using precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), and the Fβ-measure with β² = 0.2, weighting recall heavily to emphasize precision. Used to rank WMDS.net against unweighted MDS and degree-only baselines on the TCGA bladder cancer differential co-expression network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Scores predicted driver gene lists against a curated benchmark (the 616-gene CGC set) using precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), and the Fβ-measure with β² = 0.2, weighting recall heavily to emphasize precision. Used to rank WMDS.net against unweighted MDS and degree-only baselines on the TCGA bladder cancer differential co-expression network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison is against a gold standard that is not a fixed benchmark gene set (e.g., replication across independent cohorts) — precision/recall against CGC is not meaningful there When recall should dominate precision (β² > 1, e.g., β² = 2); this skill fixes β² = 0.2 to privilege precision in driver gene prediction When predictions are ranked scores rather than discrete gene lists — TP/FP counts require a defined predicted set

skills.description: Use when two or more single-cell expression quantification tools must be benchmarked on simulated data against a known ground truth of cluster-marker TEs and their log2(FC) values.
skills.name: fold-change-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: fold-change-accuracy-comparison Use when two or more single-cell expression quantification tools must be benchmarked on simulated data against a known ground truth of cluster-marker TEs and their log2(FC) values. Input is real (non-simulated) scRNA-Seq data with no embedded ground-truth marker labels — recovery rates cannot be computed The aim is a marker analysis itself rather than benchmarking a quantification method's accuracy against a known truth The compared tools do not differ in expression summarization granularity (e.g. both locus-level), since the expected underestimation signal arises from family-metagene summarization Benchmark skill for evaluating how accurately a single-cell TE quantification method recovers expected cell-marker transposable elements and reproduces ground-truth average log2(fold change) values from simulated scRNA-Seq matrices, as used to compare SoloTE against scTE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: Benchmark skill for evaluating how accurately a single-cell TE quantification method recovers expected cell-marker transposable elements and reproduces ground-truth average log2(fold change) values from simulated scRNA-Seq matrices, as used to compare SoloTE against scTE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) scRNA-Seq data with no embedded ground-truth marker labels — recovery rates cannot be computed The aim is a marker analysis itself rather than benchmarking a quantification method's accuracy against a known truth The compared tools do not differ in expression summarization granularity (e.g. both locus-level), since the expected underestimation signal arises from family-metagene summarization

skills.description: Use when two or more scRNAseq datasets have been independently clustered (e.g., TIL, dLN, and acute viral Arm CD4+ T cells) and you need to identify which populations share transcriptomic profiles across datasets.
skills.name: fold-change-correlation-between-scrnaseq-clusters
skills.search_text: fold-change-correlation-between-scrnaseq-clusters Use when two or more scRNAseq datasets have been independently clustered (e.g., TIL, dLN, and acute viral Arm CD4+ T cells) and you need to identify which populations share transcriptomic profiles across datasets. Datasets have not been individually clustered and analyzed first — the method reads preclustered datasets and cannot substitute for per-dataset clustering Only a single dataset is available and no cross-dataset population comparison is needed The goal is cell-level integration (e.g., batch-corrected embedding) rather than cluster-level transcriptomic profile comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 A cross-dataset cluster similarity method in robustSingleCell that compares independently clustered scRNAseq datasets by computing fold-change (FC) vectors for each cluster and quantifying similarity between cluster pairs via Pearson correlation, retaining only statistically robust matches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: A cross-dataset cluster similarity method in robustSingleCell that compares independently clustered scRNAseq datasets by computing fold-change (FC) vectors for each cluster and quantifying similarity between cluster pairs via Pearson correlation, retaining only statistically robust matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have not been individually clustered and analyzed first — the method reads preclustered datasets and cannot substitute for per-dataset clustering Only a single dataset is available and no cross-dataset population comparison is needed The goal is cell-level integration (e.g., batch-corrected embedding) rather than cluster-level transcriptomic profile comparison

skills.description: Use when simulating bulk multi-omics count data with MOSim and you need to impose temporal DEG fold-change profiles on negative-binomial counts and couple regulatory-layer features to gene expression patterns.
skills.name: fold-change-count-transformation
skills.search_text: fold-change-count-transformation Use when simulating bulk multi-omics count data with MOSim and you need to impose temporal DEG fold-change profiles on negative-binomial counts and couple regulatory-layer features to gene expression patterns. Single-cell simulation — sc_mosim relies on SPARSim functionality and only supports scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq and TF regulatory layers, not the full bulk regulatory omics set You need regulatory omics layers beyond MOSim's supported set, e.g. proteomics or metabolomics, which the tool explicitly does not cover You only need to transform an existing observed count matrix — this skill generates synthetic counts, not a normalization of real data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MOSim bulk simulation procedure in which negative-binomial RNA-seq counts are modulated by profile-specific fold changes (continuous or transitory induction/repression) and regulator (TF, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, miRNA-seq, Methyl-seq) profiles are derived as same-pattern (activator) or mirrored (repressor) relative to their target genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: MOSim bulk simulation procedure in which negative-binomial RNA-seq counts are modulated by profile-specific fold changes (continuous or transitory induction/repression) and regulator (TF, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, miRNA-seq, Methyl-seq) profiles are derived as same-pattern (activator) or mirrored (repressor) relative to their target genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell simulation — sc_mosim relies on SPARSim functionality and only supports scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq and TF regulatory layers, not the full bulk regulatory omics set You need regulatory omics layers beyond MOSim's supported set, e.g. proteomics or metabolomics, which the tool explicitly does not cover You only need to transform an existing observed count matrix — this skill generates synthetic counts, not a normalization of real data

skills.description: Use when a Leiden/louvain cluster must be annotated by function and you need a compact, high-confidence gene list: rank Welch t-test DE results by log2 fold-change and keep the top 500 genes for enrichment analysis.
skills.name: fold-change-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: fold-change-gene-ranking Use when a Leiden/louvain cluster must be annotated by function and you need a compact, high-confidence gene list: rank Welch t-test DE results by log2 fold-change and keep the top 500 genes for enrichment analysis. Input is already a curated marker gene list or the clusters are already annotated — ranking by fold-change adds nothing before enrichment. Only a handful of genes are differentially expressed (small clusters or weak contrasts), where an arbitrary top-500 cutoff would dilute enrichment with noise. The goal is Kaplan-Meier survival curves for a single factor rather than multi-factor Cox regression effects The factor list contains only non-numeric variables without a defined reference level, making hazard-ratio interpretation ambiguous The data have not been integrated (clinical, GSVA, TPM merged by common samples), so covariates cannot be jointly modeled http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Render Cox proportional-hazards regression coefficients (e.g., GSVA hypoxia and glycolysis scores, gender, stage, age in TCGA-LUAD) as forest plots so that hazard ratios, confidence intervals and independence of prognostic factors can be inspected at a glance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Render Cox proportional-hazards regression coefficients (e.g., GSVA hypoxia and glycolysis scores, gender, stage, age in TCGA-LUAD) as forest plots so that hazard ratios, confidence intervals and independence of prognostic factors can be inspected at a glance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is Kaplan-Meier survival curves for a single factor rather than multi-factor Cox regression effects The factor list contains only non-numeric variables without a defined reference level, making hazard-ratio interpretation ambiguous The data have not been integrated (clinical, GSVA, TPM merged by common samples), so covariates cannot be jointly modeled

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating a published scoring/ranking method: you have the paper's formula definitions, the reference package (e.g. MUSIC's Rank_overall/Rank_specific), and a shared test dataset (e.g. crop_stimulated).
skills.name: formula-verification-against-reference-implementation
skills.search_text: formula-verification-against-reference-implementation Use when reproducing or validating a published scoring/ranking method: you have the paper's formula definitions, the reference package (e.g. MUSIC's Rank_overall/Rank_specific), and a shared test dataset (e.g. crop_stimulated). When the goal is a first-pass analysis of new screening data rather than validating a re-implementation of the scoring formulas When the reference implementation's functions cannot be run on the same intermediate object (e.g. no access to the distri_diff object), since numerical matching is the acceptance criterion When the perturbation-level scoring method differs (e.g. non-topic-model CRISPR screen analysis); this skill is specific to reproducing MUSIC's topic-distribution-based scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Independently re-implements a paper's quantitative scoring formulas (here MUSIC's TPD, TPDS, TPDR, and CS for topic-model-based perturbation ranking) and verifies correctness by numerically matching the re-implementation's values and perturbation orderings against the reference implementation's functions on the same input object. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: Independently re-implements a paper's quantitative scoring formulas (here MUSIC's TPD, TPDS, TPDR, and CS for topic-model-based perturbation ranking) and verifies correctness by numerically matching the re-implementation's values and perturbation orderings against the reference implementation's functions on the same input object.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a first-pass analysis of new screening data rather than validating a re-implementation of the scoring formulas When the reference implementation's functions cannot be run on the same intermediate object (e.g. no access to the distri_diff object), since numerical matching is the acceptance criterion When the perturbation-level scoring method differs (e.g. non-topic-model CRISPR screen analysis); this skill is specific to reproducing MUSIC's topic-distribution-based scores

skills.description: Use when evaluating or tuning a diagonal integration method's shared latent embeddings: FOSCTTM quantifies cross-modality alignment by measuring each cell's nearest-neighbor agreement across modalities, e.g. when sweeping the unbalanced OT parameter m.
skills.name: foscttm-metric-computation
skills.search_text: foscttm-metric-computation Use when evaluating or tuning a diagonal integration method's shared latent embeddings: FOSCTTM quantifies cross-modality alignment by measuring each cell's nearest-neighbor agreement across modalities, e.g. when sweeping the unbalanced OT parameter m. Data are truly paired (multiome/cite-seq) with known cell correspondences — matching-based alignment metrics designed for unpaired diagonal integration are unnecessary Only a single modality is present — no cross-modality nearest-neighbor consistency can be computed No latent embeddings in mdata.obsm['latent'] and no cross-modality cost matrix attached — the metric has no input to score http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute FOSCTTM (Fraction of Samples Closer Than the True Match), a cross-modality nearest-neighbor consistency metric, to score how well scConfluence's shared latent space aligns cells profiled from different modalities. Used here as part of the hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of the unbalanced OT transported-mass parameter m on the cell-line (scCATseq) benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample/per-context LR communication scores from one or more CCC tools (e.g., CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, cell2cell built-in) and need a 4D tensor input for Tensor-cell2cell factorization or cross-tool consistency checks.
skills.name: four-dimensional-communication-tensor-construction
skills.search_text: four-dimensional-communication-tensor-construction Use when you have per-sample/per-context LR communication scores from one or more CCC tools (e.g., CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, cell2cell built-in) and need a 4D tensor input for Tensor-cell2cell factorization or cross-tool consistency checks. Only a single sample/context is available — use regular cell2cell per-context analysis instead of a 4D tensor LR pairs or cell types are missing in some contexts and you need to include all possible communication members — the implemented decomposition is not optimized for missing values, so only shared members can be retained Rare cell types present in only some samples are biologically central — the shared-members filter excludes them from the tensor Construct a 4D communication tensor (LR pairs × sender cell types × receiver cell types × contexts) from per-context cell-cell communication scores so Tensor-cell2cell can deconvolve context-dependent communication patterns. Retaining only LR pairs and cell types shared across all samples makes tensors from different scoring methods directly comparable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Construct a 4D communication tensor (LR pairs × sender cell types × receiver cell types × contexts) from per-context cell-cell communication scores so Tensor-cell2cell can deconvolve context-dependent communication patterns. Retaining only LR pairs and cell types shared across all samples makes tensors from different scoring methods directly comparable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single sample/context is available — use regular cell2cell per-context analysis instead of a 4D tensor LR pairs or cell types are missing in some contexts and you need to include all possible communication members — the implemented decomposition is not optimized for missing values, so only shared members can be retained Rare cell types present in only some samples are biologically central — the shared-members filter excludes them from the tensor

skills.description: Use when fitting Tweedie (CPLM) or zero-inflated Tweedie (ZICP) models to scRNA-seq counts with the index parameter p constrained to (1, 2), where the Tweedie density is semi-continuous with a point mass at zero and its normalizing constant must be computed numerically.
skills.name: fourier-inversion-density-evaluation
skills.search_text: fourier-inversion-density-evaluation Use when fitting Tweedie (CPLM) or zero-inflated Tweedie (ZICP) models to scRNA-seq counts with the index parameter p constrained to (1, 2), where the Tweedie density is semi-continuous with a point mass at zero and its normalizing constant must be computed numerically. The response distribution is not Tweedie with index p in (1, 2) — for special cases with closed-form densities (e.g., Poisson or Gamma limits), numerical Fourier inversion is unnecessary The model requires gene-specific zero-inflation affecting only a subset of genes, which the article states Tweedieverse is not architected for Data are continuous measurements where a non-semi-continuous (non-CPLM) likelihood is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Numerically evaluates the Tweedie density function for 1 < p < 2 via the Fourier inversion strategy implemented in the R package tweedie, because the normalizing constant has no closed form. This is the likelihood-evaluation engine underlying CPLM and ZICP fits in the Tweedieverse framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Numerically evaluates the Tweedie density function for 1 < p < 2 via the Fourier inversion strategy implemented in the R package tweedie, because the normalizing constant has no closed form. This is the likelihood-evaluation engine underlying CPLM and ZICP fits in the Tweedieverse framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response distribution is not Tweedie with index p in (1, 2) — for special cases with closed-form densities (e.g., Poisson or Gamma limits), numerical Fourier inversion is unnecessary The model requires gene-specific zero-inflation affecting only a subset of genes, which the article states Tweedieverse is not architected for Data are continuous measurements where a non-semi-continuous (non-CPLM) likelihood is appropriate

skills.description: Use when quantifying circRNA and cognate linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq so both can be directly compared on a common scale, or when reproducing FPB/CIRCscore-based correlation or tissue-enrichment analyses.
skills.name: fpb-expression-normalization
skills.search_text: fpb-expression-normalization Use when quantifying circRNA and cognate linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq so both can be directly compared on a common scale, or when reproducing FPB/CIRCscore-based correlation or tissue-enrichment analyses. Input is poly(A)-/ribo- or RNase R-treated RNA-seq, where polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making accurate linear RNA quantification and CIRCscore evaluation unsuitable Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ enriched, where circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3' poly(A) tails Goal is de novo circRNA discovery/annotation rather than expression quantification and circ-vs-linear comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Normalize RNA-seq fragments mapped individually to circRNA-specific back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites and linear RNA-specific splicing junction (SJ) sites into FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) values, then divide FPBcirc by FPBlinear to compute a CIRCscore for direct circular-vs-linear expression comparison using CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Normalize RNA-seq fragments mapped individually to circRNA-specific back-splicing junction (BSJ) sites and linear RNA-specific splicing junction (SJ) sites into FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases) values, then divide FPBcirc by FPBlinear to compute a CIRCscore for direct circular-vs-linear expression comparison using CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)-/ribo- or RNase R-treated RNA-seq, where polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, making accurate linear RNA quantification and CIRCscore evaluation unsuitable Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ enriched, where circRNAs are depleted due to their lack of 3' poly(A) tails Goal is de novo circRNA discovery/annotation rather than expression quantification and circ-vs-linear comparison

skills.description: Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM expression matrices (e.g., TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD protein-coding and long non-coding genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes before building co-expression networks.
skills.name: fpkm-to-zfpkm-log-normalization
skills.search_text: fpkm-to-zfpkm-log-normalization Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM expression matrices (e.g., TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD protein-coding and long non-coding genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes before building co-expression networks. Input is raw RNA-Seq counts rather than normalized FPKM values — differential expression in this pipeline uses the DESeq2 R/Bioconductor package, not zFPKM. Data are miRNA expression rather than protein-coding/long non-coding RNA genes — miRNAs are pre-processed separately in this pipeline (on average 81% of miRNAs are extracted) and the zFPKM > −3.0 filter as described applies to RNA genes. The goal is calling differentially expressed genes for a gene signature — use DESeq2 instead; zFPKM filtering only removes background/noisy genes as input selection for network construction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transforms normalized RNA-Seq FPKM gene expression values into zFPKM (z-score of log-FPKM, Hart et al. approach) and filters active genes by keeping only those whose mean zFPKM exceeds −3.0, discarding background/noisy transcripts before gene co-expression network construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Transforms normalized RNA-Seq FPKM gene expression values into zFPKM (z-score of log-FPKM, Hart et al. approach) and filters active genes by keeping only those whose mean zFPKM exceeds −3.0, discarding background/noisy transcripts before gene co-expression network construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA-Seq counts rather than normalized FPKM values — differential expression in this pipeline uses the DESeq2 R/Bioconductor package, not zFPKM. Data are miRNA expression rather than protein-coding/long non-coding RNA genes — miRNAs are pre-processed separately in this pipeline (on average 81% of miRNAs are extracted) and the zFPKM > −3.0 filter as described applies to RNA genes. The goal is calling differentially expressed genes for a gene signature — use DESeq2 instead; zFPKM filtering only removes background/noisy genes as input selection for network construction.

skills.description: Use when single-cell FASTQ reads come from protocols whose barcode/UMI layout is not simple fixed-position (e.g. repeated barcode segments like b[16]...b[4], or 10x-style 1{b[16]u[12]x:}2{r:} geometry strings) and must be normalized before mapping.
skills.name: fragment-geometry-string-parsing
skills.search_text: fragment-geometry-string-parsing Use when single-cell FASTQ reads come from protocols whose barcode/UMI layout is not simple fixed-position (e.g. repeated barcode segments like b[16]...b[4], or 10x-style 1{b[16]u[12]x:}2{r:} geometry strings) and must be normalized before mapping. The protocol already has a simple fixed-position barcode/UMI geometry that the underlying mapper (e.g. piscem map-sc --geometry or alevin-fry) supports directly, so normalization would add overhead without benefit The input is not paired-end reads with an explicit barcode/UMI layout string — e.g. single-end reads with barcodes supplied through a separate file such as piscem map-sc-atac --barcode http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Parses read-pair fragment-geometry specification strings (segment codes b/u/r/x with bracketed lengths and a colon remainder marker) into fixed-position extraction records, so alevin-fry/piscem mappers designed for simple barcodes can handle variable-length or floating-position barcodes without change. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad614
skills.summary: Parses read-pair fragment-geometry specification strings (segment codes b/u/r/x with bracketed lengths and a colon remainder marker) into fixed-position extraction records, so alevin-fry/piscem mappers designed for simple barcodes can handle variable-length or floating-position barcodes without change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The protocol already has a simple fixed-position barcode/UMI geometry that the underlying mapper (e.g. piscem map-sc --geometry or alevin-fry) supports directly, so normalization would add overhead without benefit The input is not paired-end reads with an explicit barcode/UMI layout string — e.g. single-end reads with barcodes supplied through a separate file such as piscem map-sc-atac --barcode

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SingleCellExperiment objects) are overdispersed and you need a chi-squared-residual-based dimension reduction or multi-batch integration embedding that outperforms log-transform PCA.
skills.name: freeman-tukey-residual-count-normalization
skills.search_text: freeman-tukey-residual-count-normalization Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SingleCellExperiment objects) are overdispersed and you need a chi-squared-residual-based dimension reduction or multi-batch integration embedding that outperforms log-transform PCA. The input is not raw count data — CA residual decomposition expects a counts matrix; pre-log-transformed 'logcounts' input defeats the stated advantage of 'avoiding distortive log-transformation'. The benchmark ground truth requires independently validated cell-type labels: the article notes the analyzed datasets 'did not have independently validated cell type annotations, so performance is limited by the original cell type assignments'. The analysis depends on knowing optimal settings a priori from data characteristics — the paper cautions that 'parameters like number of "true" clusters are unknown a priori and depend on the specific research question and context'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute cell embeddings from single-cell RNA-seq count matrices via correspondence analysis using Freeman–Tukey (FT) residuals instead of the standard log(x+1) + PCA transform, implemented in the corral/corralm R/Bioconductor package. FT-residual CA avoids the distortive log-transformation and was the most performant CA variant across diverse datasets in the Hsu & Culhane 2023 benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Compute cell embeddings from single-cell RNA-seq count matrices via correspondence analysis using Freeman–Tukey (FT) residuals instead of the standard log(x+1) + PCA transform, implemented in the corral/corralm R/Bioconductor package. FT-residual CA avoids the distortive log-transformation and was the most performant CA variant across diverse datasets in the Hsu & Culhane 2023 benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not raw count data — CA residual decomposition expects a counts matrix; pre-log-transformed 'logcounts' input defeats the stated advantage of 'avoiding distortive log-transformation'. The benchmark ground truth requires independently validated cell-type labels: the article notes the analyzed datasets 'did not have independently validated cell type annotations, so performance is limited by the original cell type assignments'. The analysis depends on knowing optimal settings a priori from data characteristics — the paper cautions that 'parameters like number of "true" clusters are unknown a priori and depend on the specific research question and context'.

skills.search_text: frequent-gene-feature-selection Use when building an EmptyNN-style classifier on a raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrix and you need a data-driven, ambient-informed gene subset (top frequent genes of empty droplets) instead of the full gene space. skills.search_text: fresh-versus-cryopreserved-sample-comparability-assessment Use when deciding whether cryopreserved (frozen-thawed) PBMC or similar single-cell suspensions can be substituted for fresh specimens in droplet scRNA-seq profiling and cell-type classification, or when comparing two sample preparations for sequencing-depth-matched equivalence. Cell type labels are available and only the supervised silhouette index is needed — the DI sweep is specifically for label-free selection You have not yet produced PC embeddings from DUBStepR-ordered features; the metric requires a PC-space representation per feature set size http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes label-free global distance metrics (e.g., the Density Index) in principal-component space using Frobenius-norm shortcuts for root-mean-squared pairwise distances, as used by DUBStepR to select the optimal feature set size without cell type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Computes label-free global distance metrics (e.g., the Density Index) in principal-component space using Frobenius-norm shortcuts for root-mean-squared pairwise distances, as used by DUBStepR to select the optimal feature set size without cell type labels.

skills.description: Use when you have a weighted cluster interlacement adjacency matrix (CI-graph) from Spaco's DOI modeling plus a selected color palette, and need an optimal cluster-to-color mapping.
skills.name: frobenius-norm-loss-minimization
skills.search_text: frobenius-norm-loss-minimization Use when you have a weighted cluster interlacement adjacency matrix (CI-graph) from Spaco's DOI modeling plus a selected color palette, and need an optimal cluster-to-color mapping. When the user wants colors to follow literature conventions or personal preferences rather than spatial contrast — Spaco enforces a correspondence between color differences and the spatial distribution of cells When hundreds of clusters must be colored or strict color-vision-deficiency support is required, since the achievable visual contrast through color space is limited When only a naive default coloring suffices — this stochastic graph-matching is meant for spatially constrained single-cell-resolution SRT colorization, not generic chart coloring Solves Spaco's cluster-color assignment by stochastically searching for a one-to-one permutation matrix P that minimizes the Frobenius norm loss L(P) = ||P A_CI P^T − A_CD||_F, aligning the cluster interlacement (CI-graph) with the color-difference (CD-graph) so spatially interlaced clusters receive distinct colors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Solves Spaco's cluster-color assignment by stochastically searching for a one-to-one permutation matrix P that minimizes the Frobenius norm loss L(P) = ||P A_CI P^T − A_CD||_F, aligning the cluster interlacement (CI-graph) with the color-difference (CD-graph) so spatially interlaced clusters receive distinct colors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the user wants colors to follow literature conventions or personal preferences rather than spatial contrast — Spaco enforces a correspondence between color differences and the spatial distribution of cells When hundreds of clusters must be colored or strict color-vision-deficiency support is required, since the achievable visual contrast through color space is limited When only a naive default coloring suffices — this stochastic graph-matching is meant for spatially constrained single-cell-resolution SRT colorization, not generic chart coloring

skills.summary: Attaches a single-layer linear classifier to a pretrained Miscell self-supervised encoder with frozen weights, then applies integrated-gradient attribution through the frozen encoder + linear classifier to quantify each gene's influence on cell clusters and identify cluster-specific marker genes.

skills.description: Use when filtering long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments for ScISOrSeq analysis and you need to decide which reads have confirmed transcript boundaries before collapsing novel isoforms.
skills.name: full-length-read-completeness-criteria
skills.search_text: full-length-read-completeness-criteria Use when filtering long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments for ScISOrSeq analysis and you need to decide which reads have confirmed transcript boundaries before collapsing novel isoforms. Reads are short Illumina reads rather than full-length long reads — end-based completeness criteria cannot be applied External CAGE or polyA reference BED files for the organism/genome build (e.g. mm10) are unavailable, so TSS/polyA end assignment cannot be verified The goal is transcript quantification rather than defining high-confidence full-length reads for isoform discovery — use IsoQuant instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Defines how scisorseqr determines which long reads count as full-length and high-confidence: requiring spliced, mapped reads whose 5' start lies within 50 bp of a FANTOM CAGE peak (cp_distance=50) and whose 3' end lies within 50 bp of a polyASite 2.0 site, with truncation-exclusion rules dropping reads lacking both confirmed ends. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Defines how scisorseqr determines which long reads count as full-length and high-confidence: requiring spliced, mapped reads whose 5' start lies within 50 bp of a FANTOM CAGE peak (cp_distance=50) and whose 3' end lies within 50 bp of a polyASite 2.0 site, with truncation-exclusion rules dropping reads lacking both confirmed ends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short Illumina reads rather than full-length long reads — end-based completeness criteria cannot be applied External CAGE or polyA reference BED files for the organism/genome build (e.g. mm10) are unavailable, so TSS/polyA end assignment cannot be verified The goal is transcript quantification rather than defining high-confidence full-length reads for isoform discovery — use IsoQuant instead

skills.description: Use when analyzing full-length Smart-seq2 (or similar plate-based paired-end) scRNA-seq from an organism with an incomplete genome annotation, and you need to detect cell-type-specific unannotated transcripts (uTARs) beyond the reference annotation.
skills.name: full-length-transcript-tar-annotation
skills.search_text: full-length-transcript-tar-annotation Use when analyzing full-length Smart-seq2 (or similar plate-based paired-end) scRNA-seq from an organism with an incomplete genome annotation, and you need to detect cell-type-specific unannotated transcripts (uTARs) beyond the reference annotation. Input is 10x-style 3'-end droplet data already processed by cellranger count — use the from_cellranger droplet workflow instead of the Smart-seq2 paired-end fragment workflow Input is raw FASTQ rather than STAR-aligned BAMs — run the from_fastqs workflow (STAR alignment) first The genome annotation is high quality and complete for the target cell types, so uTAR discovery adds little; standard gene-level scRNA-seq analysis suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extends the gene-annotation-independent TAR-scRNA-seq pipeline to full-length plate-based scRNA-seq (Smart-seq2) data: STAR-aligned paired-end BAMs are converted to bedpe fragments, groHMM calls strand-specific TARs that are labeled aTAR/uTAR against existing annotations, and differential uTAR analysis recovers cell-type-specific unannotated transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Extends the gene-annotation-independent TAR-scRNA-seq pipeline to full-length plate-based scRNA-seq (Smart-seq2) data: STAR-aligned paired-end BAMs are converted to bedpe fragments, groHMM calls strand-specific TARs that are labeled aTAR/uTAR against existing annotations, and differential uTAR analysis recovers cell-type-specific unannotated transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10x-style 3'-end droplet data already processed by cellranger count — use the from_cellranger droplet workflow instead of the Smart-seq2 paired-end fragment workflow Input is raw FASTQ rather than STAR-aligned BAMs — run the from_fastqs workflow (STAR alignment) first The genome annotation is high quality and complete for the target cell types, so uTAR discovery adds little; standard gene-level scRNA-seq analysis suffices

skills.description: Use when you have a CSV gene annotation with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns and need to classify opposite-strand overlaps as fully-overlapped (FO) cis-NAT pairs, e.g. reproducing the Xist/Tsix example.
skills.name: fully-overlapped-antisense-pair-identification
skills.search_text: fully-overlapped-antisense-pair-identification Use when you have a CSV gene annotation with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns and need to classify opposite-strand overlaps as fully-overlapped (FO) cis-NAT pairs, e.g. reproducing the Xist/Tsix example. The annotation lacks reliable strand direction or the five required columns — CCIVR explicitly depends on the accuracy of deposited annotation including strand direction The goal is de novo discovery of NATs from raw RNA-seq reads rather than annotation-based structural classification — annotation-free pipelines like NATpipe or NASTI-seq are the appropriate family You need embedded (EB), head-to-head (HH), or tail-to-tail (TT) classification only; the FO containment criterion is a distinct overlap geometry http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts fully-overlapped (FO) cis-NAT pairs — opposite-strand gene pairs on the same chromosome where one partner's transcribed region completely contains the other's — using the CCIVR 'from-minus-to-plus' FO extraction logic, demonstrated on Ensembl GRCm39 mouse annotation recovering the Xist/Tsix pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Extracts fully-overlapped (FO) cis-NAT pairs — opposite-strand gene pairs on the same chromosome where one partner's transcribed region completely contains the other's — using the CCIVR 'from-minus-to-plus' FO extraction logic, demonstrated on Ensembl GRCm39 mouse annotation recovering the Xist/Tsix pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation lacks reliable strand direction or the five required columns — CCIVR explicitly depends on the accuracy of deposited annotation including strand direction The goal is de novo discovery of NATs from raw RNA-seq reads rather than annotation-based structural classification — annotation-free pipelines like NATpipe or NASTI-seq are the appropriate family You need embedded (EB), head-to-head (HH), or tail-to-tail (TT) classification only; the FO containment criterion is a distinct overlap geometry

skills.search_text: functional-concurrent-gene-network-construction Use when time-course scRNA-seq data have been aligned into individual cell fate trajectories (e.g., via CellST smoothing) and the goal is to infer dynamic gene-gene regulatory relationships and critical genes along differentiation. Data are a single time point or lack cell-to-cell correspondence between time points, so no aligned individual cell fate trajectories exist to fit the functional concurrent models The goal is a single bulk pseudotime trajectory rather than dynamic pairwise gene-gene networks at the individual cell level http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs dynamic gene networks from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting functional concurrent linear models between gene pairs, using Bayesian confidence intervals on the dynamic coefficient beta(l,s)(t) to define edges, and thereby identifies critical genes regulating differentiation (e.g., MYF5, MYOD1, KRT18 in zebrafish embryogenesis). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: Constructs dynamic gene networks from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting functional concurrent linear models between gene pairs, using Bayesian confidence intervals on the dynamic coefficient beta(l,s)(t) to define edges, and thereby identifies critical genes regulating differentiation (e.g., MYF5, MYOD1, KRT18 in zebrafish embryogenesis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are a single time point or lack cell-to-cell correspondence between time points, so no aligned individual cell fate trajectories exist to fit the functional concurrent models The goal is a single bulk pseudotime trajectory rather than dynamic pairwise gene-gene networks at the individual cell level

Input is raw or unsmoothed scRNA-seq expression — this skill expects smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from the CellST smoothing spline step, not bulk or raw count matrices You need a static (single-time-point) gene co-expression network rather than time-resolved dynamic relationships along differentiation Your data are bulk cell trajectories (population mean) rather than individual cell fate trajectories — the article's motivation is that bulk trajectories miss individual differentiation behaviors http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates time-resolved pairwise gene-gene relationships from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting a functional concurrent linear model in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, then builds a dynamic gene network using Bayesian confidence intervals and flags critical genes via FMANOVA with Benjamini & Yekutieli correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: Estimates time-resolved pairwise gene-gene relationships from individual cell fate trajectories by fitting a functional concurrent linear model in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, then builds a dynamic gene network using Bayesian confidence intervals and flags critical genes via FMANOVA with Benjamini & Yekutieli correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unsmoothed scRNA-seq expression — this skill expects smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from the CellST smoothing spline step, not bulk or raw count matrices You need a static (single-time-point) gene co-expression network rather than time-resolved dynamic relationships along differentiation Your data are bulk cell trajectories (population mean) rather than individual cell fate trajectories — the article's motivation is that bulk trajectories miss individual differentiation behaviors

skills.description: Use when computing ligand or target abundance for NeuronChatDB interaction entries (especially non-peptide neurotransmitters like glutamate or GABA) from per-group ensemble-averaged gene expression, when contributing genes must be combined across functional groups.
skills.name: functional-group-geometric-mean-aggregation
skills.search_text: functional-group-geometric-mean-aggregation Use when computing ligand or target abundance for NeuronChatDB interaction entries (especially non-peptide neurotransmitters like glutamate or GABA) from per-group ensemble-averaged gene expression, when contributing genes must be combined across functional groups. When running the CellChat or CellPhoneDB workflow on the same data — their implementation applies AND logic to all contributing genes without functional grouping and can dramatically underestimate small-molecule neurotransmitter ligand abundance When the desired quantity is actual neurotransmitter or receptor protein/metabolite abundance rather than a transcriptomics-based estimate When the interaction is a standard peptide/protein ligand-receptor pair with no functional gene grouping defined in NeuronChatDB http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 NeuronChat's rule for computing ligand (non-peptide neurotransmitter) and receptor/target abundance from grouped gene expression: AND logic (geometric mean) across different functional gene groups (e.g., synthetic enzymes vs. vesicular transporters) and OR logic (arithmetic mean) among redundant genes within a group. This functional grouping is what keeps small-molecule neurotransmitter ligand abundance from being underestimated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: NeuronChat's rule for computing ligand (non-peptide neurotransmitter) and receptor/target abundance from grouped gene expression: AND logic (geometric mean) across different functional gene groups (e.g., synthetic enzymes vs. vesicular transporters) and OR logic (arithmetic mean) among redundant genes within a group. This functional grouping is what keeps small-molecule neurotransmitter ligand abundance from being underestimated.

skills.name: functional-homolog-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: functional-homolog-gene-annotation Use when KEGG KGML pathway files loaded into Cytoscape (KEGGScape) render only the first gene per multi-gene node, and the analysis goal is to surface all functionally homologous genes responsible for enzymatic reactions. The pathway is a glycan-related KEGG pathway (category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism') whose 'line' link nodes cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape, and are hence excluded from FunHoP The pathway already displays all genes per node (e.g. data from tools other than KEGGScape that do not collapse OR groups), so expansion would duplicate nodes The goal is isoform-level enzyme activity analysis, since KEGG does not provide curated enzyme-activity information for isoforms and FunHoP limits analysis to the gene level http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 A KGML-expansion method that rewrites KEGG pathway XML nodes so that every functional homolog gene behind a reaction is displayed in Cytoscape (via KEGGScape/FunHoP), instead of only the first listed gene, recovering hidden enzymes such as the 21 genes behind the PLA2G4B node in hsa00564. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: A KGML-expansion method that rewrites KEGG pathway XML nodes so that every functional homolog gene behind a reaction is displayed in Cytoscape (via KEGGScape/FunHoP), instead of only the first listed gene, recovering hidden enzymes such as the 21 genes behind the PLA2G4B node in hsa00564.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway is a glycan-related KEGG pathway (category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism') whose 'line' link nodes cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape, and are hence excluded from FunHoP The pathway already displays all genes per node (e.g. data from tools other than KEGGScape that do not collapse OR groups), so expansion would duplicate nodes The goal is isoform-level enzyme activity analysis, since KEGG does not provide curated enzyme-activity information for isoforms and FunHoP limits analysis to the gene level
