skills.description: Use when a plant single-cell atlas contains clusters with unknown marker genes or unclear identity and you want to infer their cell type from GO-term enrichment profiles via topic modeling and a functional similarity network.
skills.name: functional-similarity-network-visualization
skills.search_text: functional-similarity-network-visualization Use when a plant single-cell atlas contains clusters with unknown marker genes or unclear identity and you want to infer their cell type from GO-term enrichment profiles via topic modeling and a functional similarity network. Input is non-plant scRNA-seq data without a plant knowledgebase (e.g., TAIR/GO annotations) — scPlant's GSEA pipeline is built around plant genome resources Clusters already have confident marker-based annotations and the goal is marker discovery or trajectory inference rather than functional annotation Input is bulk transcriptomic data — scPlant targets single-cell atlases and uses Seurat/CellFunTopic single-cell objects http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 A scPlant/CellFunTopic-based workflow that annotates cell clusters functionally by combining GO-based GSEA scoring (RunGSEA_plant) with LDA topic modeling (runLDA) to build a cluster-level functional similarity network. Applied to the Arabidopsis thaliana root atlas (Zhang et al., 2019), it places the unannotated cluster 18 adjacent to cortex clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: A scPlant/CellFunTopic-based workflow that annotates cell clusters functionally by combining GO-based GSEA scoring (RunGSEA_plant) with LDA topic modeling (runLDA) to build a cluster-level functional similarity network. Applied to the Arabidopsis thaliana root atlas (Zhang et al., 2019), it places the unannotated cluster 18 adjacent to cortex clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is non-plant scRNA-seq data without a plant knowledgebase (e.g., TAIR/GO annotations) — scPlant's GSEA pipeline is built around plant genome resources Clusters already have confident marker-based annotations and the goal is marker discovery or trajectory inference rather than functional annotation Input is bulk transcriptomic data — scPlant targets single-cell atlases and uses Seurat/CellFunTopic single-cell objects

skills.description: Use when raw gene-level expression matrices (rows = samples, columns = Entrez IDs) must be converted to pathway-activity features before training or applying a DeepCC classifier, or when classifying a single sample that requires a reference expression profile.
skills.name: functional-spectra-computation
skills.search_text: functional-spectra-computation Use when raw gene-level expression matrices (rows = samples, columns = Entrez IDs) must be converted to pathway-activity features before training or applying a DeepCC classifier, or when classifying a single sample that requires a reference expression profile. The input is already a functional spectra matrix — proceed directly to train_DeepCC_model or get_DeepCC_label instead of recomputing spectra. The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised classification — DeepCC and its spectra pipeline are 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients'. Only subtype-defining signature genes (no genome-wide expression matrix) are available — signature gene lists cannot yield the comprehensive gene-set activities the transformation depends on. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transforms gene expression profiles into functional spectra — per-sample quantification of MSigDB gene set (pathway) activities — which serve as the platform-independent feature space that DeepCC trains on, replacing signature-gene inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Transforms gene expression profiles into functional spectra — per-sample quantification of MSigDB gene set (pathway) activities — which serve as the platform-independent feature space that DeepCC trains on, replacing signature-gene inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a functional spectra matrix — proceed directly to train_DeepCC_model or get_DeepCC_label instead of recomputing spectra. The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised classification — DeepCC and its spectra pipeline are 'specifically developed for addressing current challenges in classification but not clustering of cancer patients'. Only subtype-defining signature genes (no genome-wide expression matrix) are available — signature gene lists cannot yield the comprehensive gene-set activities the transformation depends on.

skills.description: Use when a trained DeepCC model's deep features must be validated biologically: samples have CMS (or analogous) labels and you need to show deep-feature space is more compact than signature-gene space and that feature groups map to known subtype characteristics.
skills.name: functional-spectra-interpretation
skills.search_text: functional-spectra-interpretation Use when a trained DeepCC model's deep features must be validated biologically: samples have CMS (or analogous) labels and you need to show deep-feature space is more compact than signature-gene space and that feature groups map to known subtype characteristics. The goal is unsupervised discovery of new subtypes — DeepCC is built for classification, not clustering of cancer patients The model has not been trained and only raw expression is available — this skill interprets deep features of a trained ANN, not raw functional spectra Only a single new sample without a reference expression profile is available (single-sample prediction requires getFunctionalSpectrum with refExp, and has too few samples for silhouette analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Interpret the ten deep features extracted from the last hidden layer of a trained DeepCC ANN by assessing silhouette-based subtype compactness and clustering the absolute Pearson correlation matrix to map feature groups onto subtype biology (MSI, metabolic dysregulation, EMT). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Interpret the ten deep features extracted from the last hidden layer of a trained DeepCC ANN by assessing silhouette-based subtype compactness and clustering the absolute Pearson correlation matrix to map feature groups onto subtype biology (MSI, metabolic dysregulation, EMT).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised discovery of new subtypes — DeepCC is built for classification, not clustering of cancer patients The model has not been trained and only raw expression is available — this skill interprets deep features of a trained ANN, not raw functional spectra Only a single new sample without a reference expression profile is available (single-sample prediction requires getFunctionalSpectrum with refExp, and has too few samples for silhouette analysis)

skills.description: Use when raw gene expression profiles (data.frame with Entrez-ID columns, one row per patient) must be converted into pathway-level feature vectors before training or applying a DeepCC cancer subtype classifier.
skills.name: functional-spectrum-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: functional-spectrum-feature-extraction Use when raw gene expression profiles (data.frame with Entrez-ID columns, one row per patient) must be converted into pathway-level feature vectors before training or applying a DeepCC cancer subtype classifier. The input is already a functional spectra / feature matrix — pass it directly to train_DeepCC_model or get_DeepCC_label instead of re-transforming The goal is clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised classification — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification but not clustering Samples should be assigned labels without transformation when a trained classifier expects raw signature-gene input — DeepCC requires the functional spectra representation, not raw expression, as classifier input http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transforms raw tumor gene expression profiles into DeepCC 'functional spectra' by computing GSEA enrichment scores of every sample against all MSigDB gene sets (e.g., 17,779 gene sets in MSigDB v6.0), yielding a sample-by-gene-set feature matrix used as classifier input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Transforms raw tumor gene expression profiles into DeepCC 'functional spectra' by computing GSEA enrichment scores of every sample against all MSigDB gene sets (e.g., 17,779 gene sets in MSigDB v6.0), yielding a sample-by-gene-set feature matrix used as classifier input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a functional spectra / feature matrix — pass it directly to train_DeepCC_model or get_DeepCC_label instead of re-transforming The goal is clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised classification — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification but not clustering Samples should be assigned labels without transformation when a trained classifier expects raw signature-gene input — DeepCC requires the functional spectra representation, not raw expression, as classifier input

skills.description: Use when interpreting MUSIC topic model output from Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq data: after Get_topics()/Select_topic_number() have fit topics, to assign each topic a functional label via enrichment before computing perturbation impacts.
skills.name: functional-topic-enrichment-annotation
skills.search_text: functional-topic-enrichment-annotation Use when interpreting MUSIC topic model output from Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq data: after Get_topics()/Select_topic_number() have fit topics, to assign each topic a functional label via enrichment before computing perturbation impacts. When the data has not yet been modeled with topics (no Get_topics/Select_topic_number output) — enrichment on raw gene lists misses the topic structure When the organism is not supported by the chosen species annotation (Topic_func_anno invoked with species="Hs" for human; non-human data needs a supported species value) When the goal is perturbation calling rather than functional interpretation — use Rank_overall/Rank_specific outputs instead of re-annotating topics http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotates the biological function of each topic learned by MUSIC's topic model over single-cell CRISPR screening data by performing functional enrichment with clusterProfiler on the genes with the highest occurrence probabilities in each topic, providing the functional interpretation layer for downstream perturbation effect prioritization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: Annotates the biological function of each topic learned by MUSIC's topic model over single-cell CRISPR screening data by performing functional enrichment with clusterProfiler on the genes with the highest occurrence probabilities in each topic, providing the functional interpretation layer for downstream perturbation effect prioritization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data has not yet been modeled with topics (no Get_topics/Select_topic_number output) — enrichment on raw gene lists misses the topic structure When the organism is not supported by the chosen species annotation (Topic_func_anno invoked with species="Hs" for human; non-human data needs a supported species value) When the goal is perturbation calling rather than functional interpretation — use Rank_overall/Rank_specific outputs instead of re-annotating topics

skills.description: Use when Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ files need fusion detection and breakpoint calling, and when fusion-bearing versus fusion-negative cells must be compared for oncogene overexpression (e.g. WHSC1 after IgH-WHSC1).
skills.name: fusion-breakpoint-annotation
skills.search_text: fusion-breakpoint-annotation Use when Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ files need fusion detection and breakpoint calling, and when fusion-bearing versus fusion-negative cells must be compared for oncogene overexpression (e.g. WHSC1 after IgH-WHSC1). Data are 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq full-transcript libraries — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq data, not 10X Input is bulk RNA-seq or an existing fusion call set needing no per-cell resolution FASTQ filenames follow the *_1.fq convention, which scFusion explicitly does not allow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Annotate and validate scRNA-seq-derived gene fusion calls (e.g. IgH-WHSC1 in multiple myeloma) at single-cell resolution using the scFusion pipeline: STAR alignment, chimeric-read extraction, statistical/deep-learning false-positive control, and downstream expression quantification of the fused oncogene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Annotate and validate scRNA-seq-derived gene fusion calls (e.g. IgH-WHSC1 in multiple myeloma) at single-cell resolution using the scFusion pipeline: STAR alignment, chimeric-read extraction, statistical/deep-learning false-positive control, and downstream expression quantification of the fused oncogene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq full-transcript libraries — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq data, not 10X Input is bulk RNA-seq or an existing fusion call set needing no per-cell resolution FASTQ filenames follow the *_1.fq convention, which scFusion explicitly does not allow

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq fusion calls (e.g., from scFusion on Smart-Seq data) need benchmarking against known fusion catalogs (CCLE, TMPRSS2-ERG in prostate cancer) or when fusion positivity must be tested for association with a cell-level phenotype.
skills.name: fusion-call-cross-reference-validation-ccle
skills.search_text: fusion-call-cross-reference-validation-ccle Use when scRNA-seq fusion calls (e.g., from scFusion on Smart-Seq data) need benchmarking against known fusion catalogs (CCLE, TMPRSS2-ERG in prostate cancer) or when fusion positivity must be tested for association with a cell-level phenotype. Input is 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq data — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq only The goal is de novo fusion discovery with no known catalog available for cross-referencing or validation Fusions of interest are very lowly expressed or rare in highly heterogeneous tumors, where all RNA-based methods have reduced sensitivity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Validate scFusion single-cell fusion calls by cross-referencing detected fusions against known catalogs such as CCLE and the known TMPRSS2-ERG fusion, and quantify fusion-associated phenotypes (e.g., enzalutamide response) with Fisher's exact tests on cell-level positivity contingency tables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Validate scFusion single-cell fusion calls by cross-referencing detected fusions against known catalogs such as CCLE and the known TMPRSS2-ERG fusion, and quantify fusion-associated phenotypes (e.g., enzalutamide response) with Fisher's exact tests on cell-level positivity contingency tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq data — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq only The goal is de novo fusion discovery with no known catalog available for cross-referencing or validation Fusions of interest are very lowly expressed or rare in highly heterogeneous tumors, where all RNA-based methods have reduced sensitivity

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing RNA-seq fusion callers on data with known ground-truth fusions, especially simulated single-cell datasets containing technical chimeric reads, to quantify precision/recall/F-score differences.

skills.search_text: fusion-caller-benchmark-evaluation Use when evaluating or comparing RNA-seq fusion callers on data with known ground-truth fusions, especially simulated single-cell datasets containing technical chimeric reads, to quantify precision/recall/F-score differences. Data are bulk RNA-seq without single-cell structure — scFusion's joint analysis across cells and the single-cell simulation design do not apply Input is 10X scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq data — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq FASTQ input only No ground-truth fusion list exists, so precision/recall/F-score against truth cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Benchmark gene fusion detection methods by running them on simulated Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQ data with spiked-in artificial chimeric reads and scoring precision, recall, and F-score against simulation ground truth, as done to compare scFusion against bulk callers (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, EricScript). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Benchmark gene fusion detection methods by running them on simulated Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQ data with spiked-in artificial chimeric reads and scoring precision, recall, and F-score against simulation ground truth, as done to compare scFusion against bulk callers (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, EricScript).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq without single-cell structure — scFusion's joint analysis across cells and the single-cell simulation design do not apply Input is 10X scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq data — scFusion is designed for Smart-Seq FASTQ input only No ground-truth fusion list exists, so precision/recall/F-score against truth cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA/fusion caller against a simulated RNA-Seq truth set, or when estimating a maximum achievable sensitivity ceiling (e.g. Acfs' 86.6% after excluding same-strand, same-chromosome gene-pair backsplices).
skills.name: fusion-caller-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: fusion-caller-performance-evaluation Use when benchmarking a circRNA/fusion caller against a simulated RNA-Seq truth set, or when estimating a maximum achievable sensitivity ceiling (e.g. Acfs' 86.6% after excluding same-strand, same-chromosome gene-pair backsplices). Input is real (non-simulated) RNA-Seq data without a known truth set of backsplices — sensitivity/precision cannot be computed without ground truth. The caller under evaluation does not impose the same-strand, same-chromosome exclusion (the 86.6% ceiling is specific to Acfs' algorithm, not a general benchmark constraint). The goal is visualization rather than performance scoring — use INTEGRATE-Vis with the fcirc.txt output instead of re-running the benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark fcircRNA/gene-fusion callers (e.g. INTEGRATE-Circ vs. Acfs) on simulated RNA-Seq truth sets by computing sensitivity, precision, and accuracy, including caller-specific sensitivity ceilings such as Acfs' exclusion of same-strand, same-chromosome backsplices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad569
skills.summary: Benchmark fcircRNA/gene-fusion callers (e.g. INTEGRATE-Circ vs. Acfs) on simulated RNA-Seq truth sets by computing sensitivity, precision, and accuracy, including caller-specific sensitivity ceilings such as Acfs' exclusion of same-strand, same-chromosome backsplices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) RNA-Seq data without a known truth set of backsplices — sensitivity/precision cannot be computed without ground truth. The caller under evaluation does not impose the same-strand, same-chromosome exclusion (the 86.6% ceiling is specific to Acfs' algorithm, not a general benchmark constraint). The goal is visualization rather than performance scoring — use INTEGRATE-Vis with the fcirc.txt output instead of re-running the benchmark.

skills.description: Use when screening raw STAR chimeric alignments from single-cell Smart-Seq data to remove artifact-driven fusion candidates and retain true fusions such as TCR V(D)J recombinations or recurrent IgH-WHSC1.
skills.name: fusion-candidate-artifact-filtering
skills.search_text: fusion-candidate-artifact-filtering Use when screening raw STAR chimeric alignments from single-cell Smart-Seq data to remove artifact-driven fusion candidates and retain true fusions such as TCR V(D)J recombinations or recurrent IgH-WHSC1. Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data — scFusion is explicitly for single-cell Smart-Seq data rather than 10X or bulk The mappability file is missing and the analysis requires the mappability filter — scFusion will silently turn the filter off, weakening artifact suppression Detecting very rare fusions in highly heterogeneous tumor samples or lowly expressed fusions — detection power is limited and can only be improved by sequencing more/deeper cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A filtering stage of the scFusion pipeline that suppresses amplification-artifact chimeric reads in single-cell fusion calls using a mappability filter, a statistical model, a deep-learning (tensorflow/keras) model, and ad hoc filters. It is essential because the heavy Smart-Seq amplification step generates artificial chimeric reads that appear as false-positive fusion candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: A filtering stage of the scFusion pipeline that suppresses amplification-artifact chimeric reads in single-cell fusion calls using a mappability filter, a statistical model, a deep-learning (tensorflow/keras) model, and ad hoc filters. It is essential because the heavy Smart-Seq amplification step generates artificial chimeric reads that appear as false-positive fusion candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data — scFusion is explicitly for single-cell Smart-Seq data rather than 10X or bulk The mappability file is missing and the analysis requires the mappability filter — scFusion will silently turn the filter off, weakening artifact suppression Detecting very rare fusions in highly heterogeneous tumor samples or lowly expressed fusions — detection power is limited and can only be improved by sequencing more/deeper cells

skills.description: Use when tumor RNA-Seq fastq reads are available as part of a neoantigen prediction workflow and gene fusion candidates must be identified to support downstream fusion-derived neoantigen calling.
skills.name: fusion-candidate-table-generation
skills.search_text: fusion-candidate-table-generation Use when tumor RNA-Seq fastq reads are available as part of a neoantigen prediction workflow and gene fusion candidates must be identified to support downstream fusion-derived neoantigen calling. No RNA-Seq data are provided — per the README, RNA-seq is not necessary to provide, and the fusion module is skipped; WES/WGS-only runs proceed with SNV/INDEL-based neoantigen prediction The goal is quantifying gene expression rather than detecting fusions — TSNAD v2.0 handles expression via a separate RNA-Seq analysis module (StringTie/TPM-based) Fusions are already available from another caller and only peptide prediction is needed — feed fusion-derived peptides directly to the DeepHLApan step instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Detects gene fusion transcripts from tumor RNA-Seq data by aligning reads with STAR (v2.7) and calling fusions with Arriba (v1.1.0), producing a fusions.tsv table that feeds fusion-derived neoantigen prediction in TSNAD v2.0. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Detects gene fusion transcripts from tumor RNA-Seq data by aligning reads with STAR (v2.7) and calling fusions with Arriba (v1.1.0), producing a fusions.tsv table that feeds fusion-derived neoantigen prediction in TSNAD v2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No RNA-Seq data are provided — per the README, RNA-seq is not necessary to provide, and the fusion module is skipped; WES/WGS-only runs proceed with SNV/INDEL-based neoantigen prediction The goal is quantifying gene expression rather than detecting fusions — TSNAD v2.0 handles expression via a separate RNA-Seq analysis module (StringTie/TPM-based) Fusions are already available from another caller and only peptide prediction is needed — feed fusion-derived peptides directly to the DeepHLApan step instead

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ sequencing reads with no fusion-caller output — detection must first be performed with INTEGRATE-Circ before visualization is possible Goal is unbiased fcircRNA detection or quantification rather than visualization/interpretation of already-called junctions Fusion calls cannot be converted to the BEDPE/fcirc.txt junction format expected by INTEGRATE-Vis

skills.description: Use when comparing fusion gene caller sensitivity across simulated or real paired-end RNA-seq data, especially when testing detection limits under progressive subsampling or shallow sequencing depth.

skills.summary: Benchmark targeted fusion gene detection (Anchored-fusion) against de novo callers (STAR-Fusion, FusionInspector, FusionCatcher, Arriba) on simulated, bulk RNA-seq, and subsampled single-cell/bulk data to quantify sensitivity differences at low sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion only supports paired-end RNA-seq The fusions of interest do not include the user-anchored target gene — Anchored-fusion will not report them A de novo (unanchored) survey of all fusions is required — Anchored-fusion is targeted by design

skills.description: Decision support for benchmarking FUSION's individual-level training against summary-level OTTERS/PRS methods, or whenever individual-level genotype and expression reference data are available for TWAS Stage I weight estimation.
skills.name: fusion-individual-level-weight-training
skills.search_text: fusion-individual-level-weight-training Decision support for benchmarking FUSION's individual-level training against summary-level OTTERS/PRS methods, or whenever individual-level genotype and expression reference data are available for TWAS Stage I weight estimation. skills.description: Use when you have a matrix of DTW-computed expression changes for L-R pairs across developmental time points and need to identify which interactions are active at a given stage (e.g., cluster 1 = E12.5 pluripotency-related interactions).
skills.name: fuzzy-c-means-time-series-clustering
skills.search_text: fuzzy-c-means-time-series-clustering Use when you have a matrix of DTW-computed expression changes for L-R pairs across developmental time points and need to identify which interactions are active at a given stage (e.g., cluster 1 = E12.5 pluripotency-related interactions). Input is a single-time-point scRNA-seq dataset with no developmental series — dsCellNet's DTW + fuzzy clustering pipeline requires temporal series data The expression-change matrix has not been pre-filtered for variance (low-variance L-R pairs must be removed via Mfuzz's min.std before clustering) The goal is hard partitioning of stationary-condition L-R gene expression rather than dynamic interaction changes across development http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Partitions expression-change trajectories of candidate ligand-receptor pairs from a developmental series into soft clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, so that interactions peaking at specific developmental time points (e.g., E12.5 during corticogenesis) can be isolated for downstream functional enrichment. Fuzzy membership, rather than hard assignment, captures partial co-regulation of interactions across time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Partitions expression-change trajectories of candidate ligand-receptor pairs from a developmental series into soft clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, so that interactions peaking at specific developmental time points (e.g., E12.5 during corticogenesis) can be isolated for downstream functional enrichment. Fuzzy membership, rather than hard assignment, captures partial co-regulation of interactions across time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-time-point scRNA-seq dataset with no developmental series — dsCellNet's DTW + fuzzy clustering pipeline requires temporal series data The expression-change matrix has not been pre-filtered for variance (low-variance L-R pairs must be removed via Mfuzz's min.std before clustering) The goal is hard partitioning of stationary-condition L-R gene expression rather than dynamic interaction changes across development

skills.description: Use when you have L-R pair (or gene) expression changes across ordered developmental time points and need to group them into temporal expression clusters and identify the peak time point of each cluster.
skills.name: fuzzy-clustering-of-temporal-gene-expression
skills.search_text: fuzzy-clustering-of-temporal-gene-expression Use when you have L-R pair (or gene) expression changes across ordered developmental time points and need to group them into temporal expression clusters and identify the peak time point of each cluster. The expression data are from a single stationary condition rather than an ordered developmental time series — dsCellNet's DTW and fuzzy clustering leverage developmental series information and do not apply. You need a hard (crisp) partition of genes into clusters; fuzzy c-means returns graded membership values requiring a membership threshold (e.g., 0.6) that may be inappropriate for binary assignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering to standardized developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pair genes (e.g., from the GSE153164 corticogenesis dataset processed with dsCellNet) to assign interactions into eight temporal clusters and identify key developmental time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Applies Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering to standardized developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pair genes (e.g., from the GSE153164 corticogenesis dataset processed with dsCellNet) to assign interactions into eight temporal clusters and identify key developmental time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are from a single stationary condition rather than an ordered developmental time series — dsCellNet's DTW and fuzzy clustering leverage developmental series information and do not apply. You need a hard (crisp) partition of genes into clusters; fuzzy c-means returns graded membership values requiring a membership threshold (e.g., 0.6) that may be inappropriate for binary assignments.

The dataset contains no cycling/quiescent heterogeneity and no reCAT cell-cycle scores are available, so k-means on mean scores cannot be computed The goal is to preserve quiescent cells in the trajectory (e.g. a study specifically about quiescence states) rather than removing them before pseudotime inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identification and removal of G0-like quiescent cells from single-cell RNA-seq datasets using reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores, k-means clustering, and pairwise ANOVA testing, as implemented in the redPATH package prior to pseudotime inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014

skills.search_text: g1-fraction-quantification-aging-hsc Use when comparing cell-cycle phase distributions (especially G1 fraction) of stem-cell populations between conditions, e.g., young vs old LT-HSC scRNA-seq data, using unsynchronized single-cell transcriptomes. When the input expression matrix has not been normalized to log2(TPM+1) — reCAT's get_test_exp expects this scale and will not standardize raw counts When cells are synchronized or phase labels are already known experimentally (e.g., FACS-sorted G1/S/G2-M) — reCAT is designed for unsynchronized scRNA-seq data When only a single marker gene is available for phase calling — the paper shows one marker gene is not sufficient to give reliable cell-cycle stage information http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify the proportion of long-term hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs) in the G1 cell-cycle phase between young and old mice by applying reCAT's pseudo-time ordering, Bayes/mean scoring, and HMM phase segmentation to the mHSC SMART-seq dataset, reproducing the paper's 41/167 (young) vs 10/183 (old) G1 fractions (Fig. 4a). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z

Cells have not yet been reordered along a developmental trajectory — Mpath trajectory construction must precede pseudo-temporal GAM fitting The dataset starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types, a case Mpath does not yet support (planned future extension) The analysis is a simple end-stage contrast between subsets rather than temporal dynamics along a path — ANOVA with post-hoc Tukey's test suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits generalized additive models (GAMs) of gene expression as a smooth function of pseudo-temporal position along reordered single-cell developmental trajectories (cDC2 and cDC1 paths), then clusters fitted dynamics into temporal waves of gene regulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988

When the likelihood-ratio statistic's null distribution is already empirically well calibrated (Chi-square empirical FDR tracks nominal FDR), so a Gamma fit adds no benefit When the analysis is not a two-condition differential regulatory test with the sc-compReg LR statistic (e.g. bulk-only differential expression), where this null calibration was not established http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Empirically calibrates the null distribution of the sc-compReg likelihood-ratio statistic for testing differential regulatory relations by fitting a Gamma distribution to simulated null statistics, in place of the asymptotic Chi-square (df=3) null, and validates calibration via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2

skills.description: Use when estimating gene co-expression strength from sparse, zero-inflated single-cell count matrices where excessive zero counts make ordinary Pearson/Spearman correlations unreliable, and you need to separate low-confidence zeros from genuine expression.
skills.name: gamma-normal-mixture-em-estimation
skills.search_text: gamma-normal-mixture-em-estimation Use when estimating gene co-expression strength from sparse, zero-inflated single-cell count matrices where excessive zero counts make ordinary Pearson/Spearman correlations unreliable, and you need to separate low-confidence zeros from genuine expression. The input is already bulk RNA-seq or imputed/low-zero expression data — scLink's zero-filtering targets excess zeros in single-cell data, and imputed data may still be sparser than bulk data so bulk network methods or plain correlations may suffice instead The goal is directed or typed regulatory edges — scLink's edges are undirected statistical dependencies and edge types cannot be distinguished from expression data alone The gene list is very large and unfiltered — the article recommends a gene filtering step by detection rate or mean expression (or filter.genes=TRUE for top-n average expression) and possibly module-wise analysis before applying scLink http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits scLink's per-gene Gamma-Normal mixture model via EM to estimate each cell's non-detection probability d_ij for a gene, so that confidently measured expression values can be distinguished from unreliable zeros before computing robust co-expression. It underpins scLink's robust correlation estimator for sparse, zero-inflated single-cell RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Fits scLink's per-gene Gamma-Normal mixture model via EM to estimate each cell's non-detection probability d_ij for a gene, so that confidently measured expression values can be distinguished from unreliable zeros before computing robust co-expression. It underpins scLink's robust correlation estimator for sparse, zero-inflated single-cell RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already bulk RNA-seq or imputed/low-zero expression data — scLink's zero-filtering targets excess zeros in single-cell data, and imputed data may still be sparser than bulk data so bulk network methods or plain correlations may suffice instead The goal is directed or typed regulatory edges — scLink's edges are undirected statistical dependencies and edge types cannot be distinguished from expression data alone The gene list is very large and unfiltered — the article recommends a gene filtering step by detection rate or mean expression (or filter.genes=TRUE for top-n average expression) and possibly module-wise analysis before applying scLink

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) contains suspected dropout zeros and you need per-entry dropout probabilities to decide which values to impute rather than imputing everything.
skills.name: gamma-normal-mixture-model-fitting
skills.search_text: gamma-normal-mixture-model-fitting Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) contains suspected dropout zeros and you need per-entry dropout probabilities to decide which values to impute rather than imputing everything. The matrix is not a raw whole-genome scRNA-seq count matrix — scImpute recommends whole-genome counts and warns that a gene filtering step is acceptable only if most genes are present, to ensure robust identification of dropouts Dropout rates in the raw data are severely high (e.g. droplet-based technologies), where the article notes imputation efficiency degrades and improvement is a future direction The goal is to alter all gene expression levels (e.g. smoothing all entries as MAGIC/SAVER do) rather than selectively imputing only likely dropouts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit a two-component Gamma–Normal mixture model per gene (within each cell subpopulation) via expectation-maximization to estimate posterior dropout probabilities for every gene–cell pair in an scRNA-seq count matrix, as implemented in scImpute. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Fit a two-component Gamma–Normal mixture model per gene (within each cell subpopulation) via expectation-maximization to estimate posterior dropout probabilities for every gene–cell pair in an scRNA-seq count matrix, as implemented in scImpute.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is not a raw whole-genome scRNA-seq count matrix — scImpute recommends whole-genome counts and warns that a gene filtering step is acceptable only if most genes are present, to ensure robust identification of dropouts Dropout rates in the raw data are severely high (e.g. droplet-based technologies), where the article notes imputation efficiency degrades and improvement is a future direction The goal is to alter all gene expression levels (e.g. smoothing all entries as MAGIC/SAVER do) rather than selectively imputing only likely dropouts

skills.search_text: gamma-poisson-count-modeling Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq batch-integration tools requires synthetic paired-batch count matrices with controlled batch strength, dropout rate, or batch-size imbalance rather than real data. skills.summary: Simulates two-batch scRNA-seq count data with Splatter's gamma-Poisson model to generate controlled batch-effect benchmarks (five scenarios: LB, LB-DR, LB-UB, SB, LB-CT) used to evaluate integration methods such as BATMAN against Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is integrating real experimental datasets (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2, Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2, 10X PBMC 8k) rather than controlled simulation-based benchmarking. skills.description: Use when training a GAN to map between separately measured single-cell modalities and the adversarial loss alone leaves the generator over-parameterized — enforce geometry preservation via the λc-weighted correspondence term.

skills.search_text: gan-generator-loss-regularization Use when training a GAN to map between separately measured single-cell modalities and the adversarial loss alone leaves the generator over-parameterized — enforce geometry preservation via the λc-weighted correspondence term. Modalities are jointly measured on the same cells, so direct pairing supervision exists and diffusion-geometry regularization is unnecessary. You need a fully plug-and-play loss — the geometry-based loss still requires a choice of distance between data points, which may be undefined or ill-suited for the data at hand. Only distribution-level matching matters (e.g., mode coverage only); the correspondence loss constrains point-wise geometry, which adds cost without benefit in that case. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Regularizes a CycleGAN-style generator loss beyond the adversarial term by adding a cycle/reconstruction loss and a diffusion-geometry correspondence loss (Lc) with weights λr=λd=1 and λc=10, constraining an otherwise over-parameterized GAN so the mapping between single-cell modalities preserves data geometry. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Regularizes a CycleGAN-style generator loss beyond the adversarial term by adding a cycle/reconstruction loss and a diffusion-geometry correspondence loss (Lc) with weights λr=λd=1 and λc=10, constraining an otherwise over-parameterized GAN so the mapping between single-cell modalities preserves data geometry.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities are jointly measured on the same cells, so direct pairing supervision exists and diffusion-geometry regularization is unnecessary. Only distribution-level matching matters (e.g., mode coverage only); the correspondence loss constrains point-wise geometry, which adds cost without benefit in that case.

Input is already a dimensionality-reduced feature/cluster table without the per-cell expression profiles GapClust needs for nearest-neighbour distances.
