skills.search_text: gaussian-affinity-estimation Use when you have a high-dimensional data matrix (e.g. mnist2500_X.txt) plus data/null 2D t-SNE or UMAP embeddings and need a local, per-cell measure of how faithfully each cell's neighborhood survives embedding. Input is a non-normalized dataset — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized data You need a single global embedding-quality score rather than local, per-cell estimates — the article's stated objective is a scheme that provides 'local (per cell) estimates of DR-induced error as opposed to a single global estimate' http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes per-cell neighborhood affinity distributions in the high-dimensional data (Gaussian kernel, perplexity-controlled) and in 2D embeddings (Student-t kernel), so their per-cell Kullback-Leibler divergence yields the EMBEDR empirical embedding statistic (EES). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Computes per-cell neighborhood affinity distributions in the high-dimensional data (Gaussian kernel, perplexity-controlled) and in 2D embeddings (Student-t kernel), so their per-cell Kullback-Leibler divergence yields the EMBEDR empirical embedding statistic (EES).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a non-normalized dataset — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized data You need a single global embedding-quality score rather than local, per-cell estimates — the article's stated objective is a scheme that provides 'local (per cell) estimates of DR-induced error as opposed to a single global estimate'

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (N*N dat_HiC) are too sparse for differential testing and a bias-aware normalized count matrix is needed before scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB detection.
skills.name: gaussian-convolution-imputation-for-sparse-contact-maps
skills.search_text: gaussian-convolution-imputation-for-sparse-contact-maps Use when raw single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (N*N dat_HiC) are too sparse for differential testing and a bias-aware normalized count matrix is needed before scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB detection. The count table already contains normalized read counts — the README's detection functions (scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB) expect pre-normalized input, so re-normalizing is unnecessary. No bias feature file (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) is available and it cannot be generated via http://dna.cs.miami.edu/scHiCNorm. The data are bulk Hi-C rather than single-cell Hi-C, since the imputation and ZINB-style zero handling target single-cell-level sparsity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocessing stage of the scHiCDiff pipeline in which a sparse N*N single-cell Hi-C contact matrix is imputed with a Gaussian convolution filter and then normalized by scHiCDiff.norm (scHiCNorm Negative Binomial Hurdle) using local bias features and cell-specific genomic-distance normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Preprocessing stage of the scHiCDiff pipeline in which a sparse N*N single-cell Hi-C contact matrix is imputed with a Gaussian convolution filter and then normalized by scHiCDiff.norm (scHiCNorm Negative Binomial Hurdle) using local bias features and cell-specific genomic-distance normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count table already contains normalized read counts — the README's detection functions (scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB) expect pre-normalized input, so re-normalizing is unnecessary. No bias feature file (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) is available and it cannot be generated via http://dna.cs.miami.edu/scHiCNorm. The data are bulk Hi-C rather than single-cell Hi-C, since the imputation and ZINB-style zero handling target single-cell-level sparsity.

skills.description: Use when a log-normalized single-cell gene expression matrix with >5000 cells needs partial-correlation (GGM) co-expression network inference, or when benchmarking SingleCellGGM against pcor-based methods like ppcor and SILGGM on an identical input matrix.
skills.name: gaussian-graphical-model-inference-large-scale
skills.search_text: gaussian-graphical-model-inference-large-scale Use when a log-normalized single-cell gene expression matrix with >5000 cells needs partial-correlation (GGM) co-expression network inference, or when benchmarking SingleCellGGM against pcor-based methods like ppcor and SILGGM on an identical input matrix. The dataset is small-scale or has fewer than ~5000 cells; existing pcor-based methods (ppcor, SILGGM, scLink) were only tested on small-scale datasets and SingleCellGGM recommends large cell numbers The goal requires modalities beyond transcriptomes (e.g., ATAC-seq or single-cell proteomics); SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data The input matrix has not been log-normalized or low-expression genes have not been filtered, since the algorithm expects a log-normalized matrix with low-expression genes removed first http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers large-scale single-cell gene co-expression networks via the graphical Gaussian model (GGM): SingleCellGGM calculates partial correlation coefficients (pcors) between gene pairs over ~20,000 iterations, and the same log-transformed matrix can be benchmarked against other pcor-based methods (ppcor, SILGGM) to identify gene expression programs (GEPs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Infers large-scale single-cell gene co-expression networks via the graphical Gaussian model (GGM): SingleCellGGM calculates partial correlation coefficients (pcors) between gene pairs over ~20,000 iterations, and the same log-transformed matrix can be benchmarked against other pcor-based methods (ppcor, SILGGM) to identify gene expression programs (GEPs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small-scale or has fewer than ~5000 cells; existing pcor-based methods (ppcor, SILGGM, scLink) were only tested on small-scale datasets and SingleCellGGM recommends large cell numbers The goal requires modalities beyond transcriptomes (e.g., ATAC-seq or single-cell proteomics); SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data The input matrix has not been log-normalized or low-expression genes have not been filtered, since the algorithm expects a log-normalized matrix with low-expression genes removed first

skills.description: Use when a single-cell read-count matrix must be turned into a sparse, undirected gene co-expression network that separates direct gene-gene dependencies from indirect ones, and standard Pearson/Spearman correlations plus plain glasso are unreliable due to excessive zero counts.
skills.name: gaussian-graphical-model-penalized-estimation
skills.search_text: gaussian-graphical-model-penalized-estimation Use when a single-cell read-count matrix must be turned into a sparse, undirected gene co-expression network that separates direct gene-gene dependencies from indirect ones, and standard Pearson/Spearman correlations plus plain glasso are unreliable due to excessive zero counts. The goal is directional regulation or distinguishing regulatory vs co-regulatory vs functionally coordinated edges — expression data alone cannot support this, and scLink edges are undirected Data are bulk expression or already-imputed single-cell data treated as bulk: imputed data may still be much sparser than bulk data, so bulk-data network methods perform poorly and this skill's single-cell robust-correlation rationale does not apply A gene-gene correlation structure survey is all that is needed — use sclink_cor first instead of the full penalized network fit http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers a sparse gene co-expression network from single-cell expression data by adapting the Gaussian graphical model with a penalized likelihood that assigns data-adaptive penalty weights to each edge based on scLink's robust correlation, rather than relying on plain graphical lasso on standard correlations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Infers a sparse gene co-expression network from single-cell expression data by adapting the Gaussian graphical model with a penalized likelihood that assigns data-adaptive penalty weights to each edge based on scLink's robust correlation, rather than relying on plain graphical lasso on standard correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is directional regulation or distinguishing regulatory vs co-regulatory vs functionally coordinated edges — expression data alone cannot support this, and scLink edges are undirected Data are bulk expression or already-imputed single-cell data treated as bulk: imputed data may still be much sparser than bulk data, so bulk-data network methods perform poorly and this skill's single-cell robust-correlation rationale does not apply A gene-gene correlation structure survey is all that is needed — use sclink_cor first instead of the full penalized network fit

skills.description: Use when benchmarking gene co-expression network inference methods on synthetic data where the ground-truth adjacency matrix must be known, especially for sparse scRNA-seq-like data with simulated dropouts.
skills.name: gaussian-graphical-model-simulation
skills.search_text: gaussian-graphical-model-simulation Use when benchmarking gene co-expression network inference methods on synthetic data where the ground-truth adjacency matrix must be known, especially for sparse scRNA-seq-like data with simulated dropouts. The goal is real-data network inference without a known ground-truth adjacency matrix to score against — use the inference skill directly rather than this simulation benchmark The input is a single real expression matrix rather than simulation parameters; this skill generates synthetic data and cannot evaluate methods on data lacking a true network Benchmarking methods designed for time-series or directed regulatory networks — scLink's edges are undirected statistical dependencies, so the simulation only supports undirected co-expression evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates sparse single-cell expression data with known Gaussian graphical model topologies (power-law and hub-based) to benchmark network inference methods such as scLink, glasso, PIDC, GENIE3, and thresholded Pearson/Spearman correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Simulates sparse single-cell expression data with known Gaussian graphical model topologies (power-law and hub-based) to benchmark network inference methods such as scLink, glasso, PIDC, GENIE3, and thresholded Pearson/Spearman correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-data network inference without a known ground-truth adjacency matrix to score against — use the inference skill directly rather than this simulation benchmark The input is a single real expression matrix rather than simulation parameters; this skill generates synthetic data and cannot evaluate methods on data lacking a true network Benchmarking methods designed for time-series or directed regulatory networks — scLink's edges are undirected statistical dependencies, so the simulation only supports undirected co-expression evaluation

skills.description: Use when a single-cell WGS analysis must pick a data-driven bin size before segmentation: specifically, when gHET calls phased by SHAPEIT2 are available and the amplification assay's ADO length distribution must be measured to set the minimum resolvable CNA bin.
skills.name: gaussian-hmm-baum-welch-training
skills.search_text: gaussian-hmm-baum-welch-training Use when a single-cell WGS analysis must pick a data-driven bin size before segmentation: specifically, when gHET calls phased by SHAPEIT2 are available and the amplification assay's ADO length distribution must be measured to set the minimum resolvable CNA bin. The amplification assay is uniform enough that ADO is negligible and a default bin size is acceptable without assay-specific calibration No phased gHET calls exist (phasing pipeline not run), since the HMM operates on phased, bulk-VAF-filtered (0.1–0.9) heterozygous sites Applying this to sex chromosomes or non-autosomal regions, since the analysis is restricted to diploid autosomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fits a two-state Gaussian hidden Markov model ('ADO'/'non-ADO') on binned B-allele frequencies at phased germline heterozygous SNPs using Baum-Welch expectation-maximization, so HiScanner can characterize assay-specific allelic dropout events and derive the smallest permissible bin size (the 95th percentile of predicted dropout event lengths). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Fits a two-state Gaussian hidden Markov model ('ADO'/'non-ADO') on binned B-allele frequencies at phased germline heterozygous SNPs using Baum-Welch expectation-maximization, so HiScanner can characterize assay-specific allelic dropout events and derive the smallest permissible bin size (the 95th percentile of predicted dropout event lengths).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The amplification assay is uniform enough that ADO is negligible and a default bin size is acceptable without assay-specific calibration No phased gHET calls exist (phasing pipeline not run), since the HMM operates on phased, bulk-VAF-filtered (0.1–0.9) heterozygous sites Applying this to sex chromosomes or non-autosomal regions, since the analysis is restricted to diploid autosomes

skills.description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (N cells x D genes) must be converted into a probabilistic neighborhood graph or Markov transition matrix as the substrate for diffusion/random-walk based analyses such as RWR, diffusion pseudotime, or trajectory inference.
skills.name: gaussian-kernel-affinity-computation
skills.search_text: gaussian-kernel-affinity-computation Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (N cells x D genes) must be converted into a probabilistic neighborhood graph or Markov transition matrix as the substrate for diffusion/random-walk based analyses such as RWR, diffusion pseudotime, or trajectory inference. Input data is raw/unnormalized counts rather than a pre-processed gene expression matrix — DTFLOW assumes step A (pre-processing into X_NxD) has already been done The analysis requires a binary adjacency graph without distance-weighted affinities, or needs global (not locally scaled) bandwidths The dataset is so large that the O(N^2) pairwise distance and N x N dense matrices are infeasible (e.g. the MH dataset with 40,210 cells took 3108.35 s) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Transforms pairwise Euclidean distances between single cells into a symmetric Gaussian kernel affinity matrix, with local bandwidth sigma_i set by each cell's distance to its k-th nearest neighbor (k=10 in DTFLOW), then row-normalizes to obtain the Markov transition matrix M used for random walk with restart diffusion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Transforms pairwise Euclidean distances between single cells into a symmetric Gaussian kernel affinity matrix, with local bandwidth sigma_i set by each cell's distance to its k-th nearest neighbor (k=10 in DTFLOW), then row-normalizes to obtain the Markov transition matrix M used for random walk with restart diffusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw/unnormalized counts rather than a pre-processed gene expression matrix — DTFLOW assumes step A (pre-processing into X_NxD) has already been done The analysis requires a binary adjacency graph without distance-weighted affinities, or needs global (not locally scaled) bandwidths The dataset is so large that the O(N^2) pairwise distance and N x N dense matrices are infeasible (e.g. the MH dataset with 40,210 cells took 3108.35 s)

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. 438 cells x 48 genes) must be converted into a Markov transition matrix as input to diffusion-based manifold learning such as BKFD or diffusion pseudotime.
skills.name: gaussian-kernel-nearest-neighbor-graph
skills.search_text: gaussian-kernel-nearest-neighbor-graph Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. 438 cells x 48 genes) must be converted into a Markov transition matrix as input to diffusion-based manifold learning such as BKFD or diffusion pseudotime. The data are already reduced to approximate principal components or another low-dimensional embedding, so a raw-cell k-NN graph adds no diffusion information A branching/pseudotime ordering is needed but no graph-based diffusion representation is acceptable (e.g. when Monocle2-style independent trajectory inference is required for direct comparison) The expression matrix is not pre-processed — the article removes genes with corrupted names (e.g. 10 genes via Scanpy pre-processing) before building the graph http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs a symmetric Gaussian-kernel affinity graph from k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell Euclidean distances and row-normalizes it into a Markov transition matrix, the first step of DTFLOW's BKFD diffusion-propagation pipeline for single-cell pseudotime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Constructs a symmetric Gaussian-kernel affinity graph from k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell Euclidean distances and row-normalizes it into a Markov transition matrix, the first step of DTFLOW's BKFD diffusion-propagation pipeline for single-cell pseudotime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already reduced to approximate principal components or another low-dimensional embedding, so a raw-cell k-NN graph adds no diffusion information A branching/pseudotime ordering is needed but no graph-based diffusion representation is acceptable (e.g. when Monocle2-style independent trajectory inference is required for direct comparison) The expression matrix is not pre-processed — the article removes genes with corrupted names (e.g. 10 genes via Scanpy pre-processing) before building the graph

skills.description: Use when computing per-gene differential expression significance from cell positions in a multidimensional space (t-SNE, PCA, spatial or pseudotime coordinates) without clustering cells.
skills.name: gaussian-kernel-reference-distribution-on-grid
skills.search_text: gaussian-kernel-reference-distribution-on-grid Use when computing per-gene differential expression significance from cell positions in a multidimensional space (t-SNE, PCA, spatial or pseudotime coordinates) without clustering cells. The expression data are continuous and you need differential expression based on expression levels rather than binary detection — the method requires binary detection data as input Two genes share the same detection pattern but different expression magnitudes — the hard detection threshold gives them identical D_KL and p-value, so a level-aware method is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A core computation of singleCellHaystack: a grid is laid over a 2D+ cell space (e.g. t-SNE coordinates) and a Gaussian-kernel reference distribution Q is constructed over grid points, serving as the null density against which each gene's detection distribution is compared via Kullback-Leibler divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: A core computation of singleCellHaystack: a grid is laid over a 2D+ cell space (e.g. t-SNE coordinates) and a Gaussian-kernel reference distribution Q is constructed over grid points, serving as the null density against which each gene's detection distribution is compared via Kullback-Leibler divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are continuous and you need differential expression based on expression levels rather than binary detection — the method requires binary detection data as input Two genes share the same detection pattern but different expression magnitudes — the hard detection threshold gives them identical D_KL and p-value, so a level-aware method is needed

skills.description: Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv from the Figshare deposit DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812) and need the normalized adjacency matrix that serves as STEM's prediction goal for spot-level spatial relationships.
skills.name: gaussian-kernel-spatial-smoothing
skills.search_text: gaussian-kernel-spatial-smoothing Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv from the Figshare deposit DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812) and need the normalized adjacency matrix that serves as STEM's prediction goal for spot-level spatial relationships. When you need the SC-SC pseudo-spatial adjacency between single cells — that is predicted by the trained STEM model from embeddings, not computed from coordinates When constructing the SC-ST or ST-SC mapping matrices (netst2sc / netsc2st) — those come from softmax over dot products of scembedding and stembedding, not from the Gaussian kernel When the ST data has no per-spot spatial coordinates (no spatial metadata CSV), since the kernel requires pairwise Euclidean spot distances http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs the N x N row-normalized ground-truth ST-ST spatial adjacency matrix that supervises STEM's adjacency predictors, by applying a Gaussian kernel (W_ij = exp(-d_ij^2 / (2*sigma^2))) to pairwise Euclidean distances between ST spot coordinates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Constructs the N x N row-normalized ground-truth ST-ST spatial adjacency matrix that supervises STEM's adjacency predictors, by applying a Gaussian kernel (W_ij = exp(-d_ij^2 / (2*sigma^2))) to pairwise Euclidean distances between ST spot coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need the SC-SC pseudo-spatial adjacency between single cells — that is predicted by the trained STEM model from embeddings, not computed from coordinates When constructing the SC-ST or ST-SC mapping matrices (netst2sc / netsc2st) — those come from softmax over dot products of scembedding and stembedding, not from the Gaussian kernel When the ST data has no per-spot spatial coordinates (no spatial metadata CSV), since the kernel requires pairwise Euclidean spot distances

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics clusterings must be ranked without ground-truth labels, e.g. to pick the alpha/beta configuration by the goodness score v(y,Cα) instead of ARI.
skills.name: gaussian-likelihood-scoring-of-clusters
skills.search_text: gaussian-likelihood-scoring-of-clusters Use when spatial transcriptomics clusterings must be ranked without ground-truth labels, e.g. to pick the alpha/beta configuration by the goodness score v(y,Cα) instead of ARI. Ground-truth annotations exist and adjusted Rand index (ARI) can be computed directly, making the annotation-free proxy unnecessary No preprocessed PCs or spot coordinates are available, since both the Gaussian likelihood and the spatial Potts prior require them The clustering is not spatial (no spot neighborhood graph), so the Potts-model term is undefined Computes the ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα) for a spatial-transcriptomics clustering by combining a Gaussian likelihood of the spot PCs, a Potts-model prior on the neighborhood graph, and a quasi-likelihood variance penalty. This lets ScribbleDom select optimal hyperparameters (e.g. alpha/beta options) without manual annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: Computes the ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα) for a spatial-transcriptomics clustering by combining a Gaussian likelihood of the spot PCs, a Potts-model prior on the neighborhood graph, and a quasi-likelihood variance penalty. This lets ScribbleDom select optimal hyperparameters (e.g. alpha/beta options) without manual annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth annotations exist and adjusted Rand index (ARI) can be computed directly, making the annotation-free proxy unnecessary No preprocessed PCs or spot coordinates are available, since both the Gaussian likelihood and the spatial Potts prior require them The clustering is not spatial (no spot neighborhood graph), so the Potts-model term is undefined

skills.description: Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) counts from CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq where ambient unbound-antibody noise and cell-level technical noise must be removed before clustering or differential expression.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-ambient-noise-modeling
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-ambient-noise-modeling Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) counts from CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq where ambient unbound-antibody noise and cell-level technical noise must be removed before clustering or differential expression. Dataset has no empty droplets and no isotype controls — the caveats for such data are deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note and require the alternative no_empty_drops workflow Proteins have very low raw signal (maximum UMI count <5 across all cells, e.g. CD34 in two datasets) — these should be removed before normalization rather than modeled Model per-cell ADT noise in droplet-based protein data by fitting a 2-component Gaussian mixture (via mclust EM) to ambient-corrected counts, then building a technical noise matrix from fitted background means plus isotype controls whose PC1 is regressed out to produce denoised, scaled protein values (dsb step II). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Model per-cell ADT noise in droplet-based protein data by fitting a 2-component Gaussian mixture (via mclust EM) to ambient-corrected counts, then building a technical noise matrix from fitted background means plus isotype controls whose PC1 is regressed out to produce denoised, scaled protein values (dsb step II).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset has no empty droplets and no isotype controls — the caveats for such data are deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note and require the alternative no_empty_drops workflow Proteins have very low raw signal (maximum UMI count <5 across all cells, e.g. CD34 in two datasets) — these should be removed before normalization rather than modeled

skills.description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset with cluster-specific gene signatures and weights (e.g., from scID_weight) is available and unlabeled target cells must be assigned to reference clusters from per-cell signature scores.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-cell-classification
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-cell-classification Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset with cluster-specific gene signatures and weights (e.g., from scID_weight) is available and unlabeled target cells must be assigned to reference clusters from per-cell signature scores. Neither the reference nor the target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures — scID is explicitly not recommended for identifying equivalent cell types in that case The expression matrices are log-transformed rather than library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized The goal is batch correction/integration of two datasets rather than label transfer via reference cluster signatures http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Stage 3 of the scID pipeline: score target cells with weighted cluster-specific gene signatures and assign them to reference clusters by fitting a finite mixture of Gaussian distributions to the score distribution. This converts discriminant scores into hard cell-type labels with conflict resolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Stage 3 of the scID pipeline: score target cells with weighted cluster-specific gene signatures and assign them to reference clusters by fitting a finite mixture of Gaussian distributions to the score distribution. This converts discriminant scores into hard cell-type labels with conflict resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Neither the reference nor the target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures — scID is explicitly not recommended for identifying equivalent cell types in that case The expression matrices are log-transformed rather than library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized The goal is batch correction/integration of two datasets rather than label transfer via reference cluster signatures

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq data provides surface-protein ADT levels for markers (e.g., CD16/CD56) whose RNA is dropout-obscured, and you need protein-derived sub-population labels to quantify or benchmark RNA-based (or denoised) recovery of that structure.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-clustering-of-surface-protein-markers
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-clustering-of-surface-protein-markers Use when CITE-seq data provides surface-protein ADT levels for markers (e.g., CD16/CD56) whose RNA is dropout-obscured, and you need protein-derived sub-population labels to quantify or benchmark RNA-based (or denoised) recovery of that structure. Only scRNA-seq counts are available with no surface-protein ADT measurements — the mixture model needs protein levels because RNA alone is dropout-obscured (silhouette drops to ~0.17 on original RNA) The marker protein distributions are not compatible with a two-component mixture (e.g., continuous gradients rather than CD56bright/CD56dim bimodality) — mclust's G = 2 assumption would be unjustified The goal is denoising itself rather than protein-guided labeling or denoising benchmarking — apply DCA directly instead of this evaluation workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model on CITE-seq antibody-derived tag (ADT) levels of CD16/FCGR3A and CD56/NCAM1 to define CD56bright/CD56dim NK sub-population labels, then benchmarks those labels via average silhouette widths against protein, original RNA, and DCA-denoised RNA expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model on CITE-seq antibody-derived tag (ADT) levels of CD16/FCGR3A and CD56/NCAM1 to define CD56bright/CD56dim NK sub-population labels, then benchmarks those labels via average silhouette widths against protein, original RNA, and DCA-denoised RNA expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only scRNA-seq counts are available with no surface-protein ADT measurements — the mixture model needs protein levels because RNA alone is dropout-obscured (silhouette drops to ~0.17 on original RNA) The marker protein distributions are not compatible with a two-component mixture (e.g., continuous gradients rather than CD56bright/CD56dim bimodality) — mclust's G = 2 assumption would be unjustified The goal is denoising itself rather than protein-guided labeling or denoising benchmarking — apply DCA directly instead of this evaluation workflow

skills.description: Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) data from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq where ambient antibody noise and cell-to-cell technical variation confound protein values and raw/CLR values track empty-droplet signal.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-denoising-of-adt-data
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-denoising-of-adt-data Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) data from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq where ambient antibody noise and cell-to-cell technical variation confound protein values and raw/CLR values track empty-droplet signal. No empty droplets are available and no background matrix can be defined — dsb requires a background definition and 'defining a reasonable subset of barcodes as background droplets still requires care'; use the dedicated no-empty-droplets variant/vignette instead The dataset lacks isotype control antibodies and the workflow has not consulted the Supplementary Note / documentation caveats for the technical component in such experiments The protein is essentially unexpressed in the dataset (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells, e.g. CD34 was removed in two datasets) and should be filtered before normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 dsb's step II denoising: after ambient-noise correction with empty droplets, fit a 2-component Gaussian mixture (mclust EM) to each cell's log-transformed ADT values to extract the background mean µ1, build a noise matrix from µ1 values plus isotype controls, and regress out its PC1 (the dsb technical component) to remove cell-to-cell technical noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: dsb's step II denoising: after ambient-noise correction with empty droplets, fit a 2-component Gaussian mixture (mclust EM) to each cell's log-transformed ADT values to extract the background mean µ1, build a noise matrix from µ1 values plus isotype controls, and regress out its PC1 (the dsb technical component) to remove cell-to-cell technical noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No empty droplets are available and no background matrix can be defined — dsb requires a background definition and 'defining a reasonable subset of barcodes as background droplets still requires care'; use the dedicated no-empty-droplets variant/vignette instead The dataset lacks isotype control antibodies and the workflow has not consulted the Supplementary Note / documentation caveats for the technical component in such experiments The protein is essentially unexpressed in the dataset (maximum raw UMI count < 5 across all cells, e.g. CD34 was removed in two datasets) and should be filtered before normalization

skills.description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq cell-by-gene matrices where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups have differing cluster proportions, so naive fold-change estimation is distorted by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be decoupled.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-em-decoupling
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-em-decoupling Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq cell-by-gene matrices where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups have differing cluster proportions, so naive fold-change estimation is distorted by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be decoupled. Samples where the Gaussian mixture assumption on gene expression distributions does not hold, e.g. intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors Datasets where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, so cell clusters are not shared between NT and perturbation groups Cells with extreme heterogeneity — scDecouple's assumption of similar cellular responses across clusters suits only moderate heterogeneity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit a Gaussian mixture model to perturbed-cell expression profiles and iteratively find the maximum likelihood of cell cluster proportions and the cellular response per gRNA via an EM algorithm, decoupling true perturbation response from infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Fit a Gaussian mixture model to perturbed-cell expression profiles and iteratively find the maximum likelihood of cell cluster proportions and the cellular response per gRNA via an EM algorithm, decoupling true perturbation response from infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples where the Gaussian mixture assumption on gene expression distributions does not hold, e.g. intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors Datasets where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, so cell clusters are not shared between NT and perturbation groups Cells with extreme heterogeneity — scDecouple's assumption of similar cellular responses across clusters suits only moderate heterogeneity

skills.description: Use when quantifying extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in droplet-based snRNA-seq: the percent of reads spliced is bimodal with nuclear and background droplets straddling ~50%, and a sample-specific midpoint separating the two distributions must be estimated per experiment.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-em-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-em-fitting Use when quantifying extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in droplet-based snRNA-seq: the percent of reads spliced is bimodal with nuclear and background droplets straddling ~50%, and a sample-specific midpoint separating the two distributions must be estimated per experiment. Data are single-cell RNA-seq (e.g. PBMCs) where background and cell/nuclear RNA profiles differ little — percent-spliced-based separation was less successful in the PBMC scRNA-seq data. Only the filtered CellRanger matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix) is available — background droplets must be present for the distribution to be bimodal. There are few or no genes increased in the background distribution — the scoring/fitting approach will likely be inaccurate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture (via EM) to the per-droplet percent-spliced-reads distribution of a snRNA-seq experiment, then computes the density-equal midpoint between the nuclear and background components as a sample-specific separation threshold, mirroring DIEM's EM-based two-population debris/cell model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture (via EM) to the per-droplet percent-spliced-reads distribution of a snRNA-seq experiment, then computes the density-equal midpoint between the nuclear and background components as a sample-specific separation threshold, mirroring DIEM's EM-based two-population debris/cell model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell RNA-seq (e.g. PBMCs) where background and cell/nuclear RNA profiles differ little — percent-spliced-based separation was less successful in the PBMC scRNA-seq data. Only the filtered CellRanger matrix (filtered_feature_bc_matrix) is available — background droplets must be present for the distribution to be bimodal. There are few or no genes increased in the background distribution — the scoring/fitting approach will likely be inaccurate.

The goal is genetic-variant-based demultiplexing and samples lack a distinct genetic background (e.g. most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies) — cell hashing cutoff calling is unrelated to SNP clustering needs Cutoffs are already trusted and supplied externally — use HTOClassification's specify_cutoff argument instead of refitting the mixture model Input is not a cell hashing HTO count matrix (e.g. transcriptome gene expression matrix or SNP genotype calls) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture (background vs true positive) to each normalized hashtag oligo (HTO) distribution in cell hashing data to determine per-hashtag classification cutoffs, as implemented in HTOreader. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture (background vs true positive) to each normalized hashtag oligo (HTO) distribution in cell hashing data to determine per-hashtag classification cutoffs, as implemented in HTOreader.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is genetic-variant-based demultiplexing and samples lack a distinct genetic background (e.g. most animal studies or same-donor longitudinal studies) — cell hashing cutoff calling is unrelated to SNP clustering needs Cutoffs are already trusted and supplied externally — use HTOClassification's specify_cutoff argument instead of refitting the mixture model Input is not a cell hashing HTO count matrix (e.g. transcriptome gene expression matrix or SNP genotype calls)

skills.description: Use when expert-provided scribble annotations are unavailable and you need an initial non-spatial domain labeling of Visium or ST spots from principal components of raw gene expression as input to automated scribble generation.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-clustering-of-gene-expression-pcs
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-clustering-of-gene-expression-pcs Use when expert-provided scribble annotations are unavailable and you need an initial non-spatial domain labeling of Visium or ST spots from principal components of raw gene expression as input to automated scribble generation. When expert-generated scribbles are available — use the expert schema (manual_scribble.csv created in Loupe browser) instead of the mclust backbone. When spatially resolved clustering is desired as the final domain calls — mclust here is deliberately non-spatial and only an initialization; AutoScribbleDom's lattice-neighbor consensus filter and the ScribbleDom network supply spatial continuity. When the number of expected domains is unknown — n_cluster_for_auto_scribble must be specified (e.g. 2) for the GMM initialization. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Runs mclust's Gaussian mixture model on spot-level principal components (e.g. n_pcs=15) of spatial transcriptomics data with n_cluster_for_auto_scribble clusters (e.g. 2) to produce an initial non-spatial cluster label per spot, which serves as the backbone for automated scribble generation in AutoScribbleDom. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: Runs mclust's Gaussian mixture model on spot-level principal components (e.g. n_pcs=15) of spatial transcriptomics data with n_cluster_for_auto_scribble clusters (e.g. 2) to produce an initial non-spatial cluster label per spot, which serves as the backbone for automated scribble generation in AutoScribbleDom.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When expert-generated scribbles are available — use the expert schema (manual_scribble.csv created in Loupe browser) instead of the mclust backbone. When spatially resolved clustering is desired as the final domain calls — mclust here is deliberately non-spatial and only an initialization; AutoScribbleDom's lattice-neighbor consensus filter and the ScribbleDom network supply spatial continuity. When the number of expected domains is unknown — n_cluster_for_auto_scribble must be specified (e.g. 2) for the GMM initialization.

skills.description: Use when a user-supplied CSV gene-expression data frame (gene identifiers plus log-fold-change values) must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters using unsupervised, probability-based Gaussian mixture modelling.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting Use when a user-supplied CSV gene-expression data frame (gene identifiers plus log-fold-change values) must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters using unsupervised, probability-based Gaussian mixture modelling. The input is not a properly formatted CSV data frame with gene identifiers and log-fold-change values — the article states the user must ensure the supplied data is in the right format before the pipeline can run The goal is supervised classification with labeled training data — GMMs here are unsupervised and assign cluster memberships probabilistically The analysis targets proteome-level interactome assessment or protein type / cellular location classification rather than expression-pattern clustering of genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a Gaussian mixture model to gene-expression data (gene identifiers with log-fold-change values) using the mclust-based GMM pipeline in the OmicInt R package, assigning each gene to an expression-pattern cluster via probability-based classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2021.100025
skills.summary: Fits a Gaussian mixture model to gene-expression data (gene identifiers with log-fold-change values) using the mclust-based GMM pipeline in the OmicInt R package, assigning each gene to an expression-pattern cluster via probability-based classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a properly formatted CSV data frame with gene identifiers and log-fold-change values — the article states the user must ensure the supplied data is in the right format before the pipeline can run The goal is supervised classification with labeled training data — GMMs here are unsupervised and assign cluster memberships probabilistically The analysis targets proteome-level interactome assessment or protein type / cellular location classification rather than expression-pattern clustering of genes

skills.description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen and per-guide UMI count distributions must be split into endogenous vs ambient components without a user-defined fixed UMI threshold.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen and per-guide UMI count distributions must be split into endogenous vs ambient components without a user-defined fixed UMI threshold. Input is a transcriptome gene-expression matrix rather than gRNA UMI counts from consensus.sequence.gRNA.variant.txt — this model is for CRISPR gRNA capture data only. Per-guide UMI distributions are too sparse to support a two-component fit (e.g., dramatically low average gRNA UMIs across the experiment), in which case ambient-vs-endogenous discrimination is unreliable and the fixed min_umi=3 fallback should be considered. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model per gRNA over pooled intact and mutant UMI counts to derive a dynamic per-guide, per-cell UMI threshold that separates endogenously expressed gRNAs from ambient artifacts, replacing the fixed min_umi=3 cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model per gRNA over pooled intact and mutant UMI counts to derive a dynamic per-guide, per-cell UMI threshold that separates endogenously expressed gRNAs from ambient artifacts, replacing the fixed min_umi=3 cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a transcriptome gene-expression matrix rather than gRNA UMI counts from consensus.sequence.gRNA.variant.txt — this model is for CRISPR gRNA capture data only. Per-guide UMI distributions are too sparse to support a two-component fit (e.g., dramatically low average gRNA UMIs across the experiment), in which case ambient-vs-endogenous discrimination is unreliable and the fixed min_umi=3 fallback should be considered.

skills.description: Use when normalizing CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT data with dsb step II, or when validating that k=2 Gaussian mixtures fit per-cell protein distributions via BIC.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting-per-cell
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting-per-cell Use when normalizing CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT data with dsb step II, or when validating that k=2 Gaussian mixtures fit per-cell protein distributions via BIC. When raw ADT counts have not been ambient-corrected (step I applied): fitting mixtures on unstandardized raw counts conflates protein-specific ambient noise with cell-intrinsic noise When the goal is mRNA expression normalization (e.g., CLR/LogNormalize for gene counts) rather than antibody-derived tag denoising When empty droplets or a background definition are unavailable without careful redefinition — the article notes defining a reasonable background subset 'still requires care' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model (via mclust EM) to the dsb step-I ambient-corrected protein values of each single cell to extract the background mean µ1, which captures cell-intrinsic technical noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture model (via mclust EM) to the dsb step-I ambient-corrected protein values of each single cell to extract the background mean µ1, which captures cell-intrinsic technical noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When raw ADT counts have not been ambient-corrected (step I applied): fitting mixtures on unstandardized raw counts conflates protein-specific ambient noise with cell-intrinsic noise When the goal is mRNA expression normalization (e.g., CLR/LogNormalize for gene counts) rather than antibody-derived tag denoising When empty droplets or a background definition are unavailable without careful redefinition — the article notes defining a reasonable background subset 'still requires care'

skills.description: Use when comparing how accurately different cell-cycle correction methods (Cyclum, Seurat, ccRemover, PC1–5) preserve or recover subclone structure in scRNA-seq data containing two known subpopulations.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-model-subclone-separability
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-model-subclone-separability Use when comparing how accurately different cell-cycle correction methods (Cyclum, Seurat, ccRemover, PC1–5) preserve or recover subclone structure in scRNA-seq data containing two known subpopulations. Data contain more than two subclones or the subclone identity is unknown — the two-component GMM assumes exactly two delineable populations Cell-cycle is not a confounder in the data (e.g., quiescent/post-mitotic cells), so correction and separability benchmarking is unnecessary Only raw, uncorrected expression is of interest — separability on uncorrected data serves only as a baseline, not the target output http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantifies how well two cell subclones can be delineated in cell-cycle-corrected scRNA-seq data by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model (GMM) on leading components and scoring separability, as used to benchmark Cyclum against Seurat, ccRemover, and PC1–5 correction on virtual tumor samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how well two cell subclones can be delineated in cell-cycle-corrected scRNA-seq data by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture model (GMM) on leading components and scoring separability, as used to benchmark Cyclum against Seurat, ccRemover, and PC1–5 correction on virtual tumor samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain more than two subclones or the subclone identity is unknown — the two-component GMM assumes exactly two delineable populations Cell-cycle is not a confounder in the data (e.g., quiescent/post-mitotic cells), so correction and separability benchmarking is unnecessary Only raw, uncorrected expression is of interest — separability on uncorrected data serves only as a baseline, not the target output

skills.description: Use when binarized scRNA-seq marker counts per cell type show a bimodal distribution and a defensible cutoff is needed to label clusters as 'unassigned' (unknown) rather than force an annotation.
skills.name: gaussian-mixture-rejection-threshold-fitting
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-rejection-threshold-fitting Use when binarized scRNA-seq marker counts per cell type show a bimodal distribution and a defensible cutoff is needed to label clusters as 'unassigned' (unknown) rather than force an annotation. Cells cannot be reasonably clustered first — the article notes 'for proper identification, each cell populations should be well clustered, even though this is not always the case' The task is reference-based annotation with a pre-annotated training dataset and no marker count distributions to threshold — use MarkerCount_Ref's reference-based path instead Marker counts per cell type are clearly unimodal, so a k=2 Gaussian mixture would not identify a meaningful separation between target and non-target cells http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits a bimodal (k=2) Gaussian mixture model to per-cell-type normalized marker counts to derive a conservative rejection threshold that separates confidently assigned cells from unknowns in MarkerCount's count-based cell type identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Fits a bimodal (k=2) Gaussian mixture model to per-cell-type normalized marker counts to derive a conservative rejection threshold that separates confidently assigned cells from unknowns in MarkerCount's count-based cell type identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells cannot be reasonably clustered first — the article notes 'for proper identification, each cell populations should be well clustered, even though this is not always the case' The task is reference-based annotation with a pre-annotated training dataset and no marker count distributions to threshold — use MarkerCount_Ref's reference-based path instead Marker counts per cell type are clearly unimodal, so a k=2 Gaussian mixture would not identify a meaningful separation between target and non-target cells

skills.description: Use when transferring labels from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq and you must decide per-cell which target cells can safely be merged into the annotated source during iterative integration.

skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-reliability-modeling Use when transferring labels from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq and you must decide per-cell which target cells can safely be merged into the annotated source during iterative integration. Source and target share the same omics modality (e.g. scRNA-seq to scRNA-seq label transfer), where the cross-omics reliability problem does not arise Paired multi-omics data where joint integration tools such as scAI or MOFA+ can exploit cross-omics pairing information directly You need novel cell-type discovery without any annotated target cells — that requires the separate structure preservation loss (--novel_type) mode rather than plain reliability selection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A scBridge component that models the reliability of scATAC-seq cells with a Gaussian Mixture Model over embedding discriminability and classification confidence, enabling iterative selection of reliable target cells whose omics difference from scRNA-seq is small. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: A scBridge component that models the reliability of scATAC-seq cells with a Gaussian Mixture Model over embedding discriminability and classification confidence, enabling iterative selection of reliable target cells whose omics difference from scRNA-seq is small.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target share the same omics modality (e.g. scRNA-seq to scRNA-seq label transfer), where the cross-omics reliability problem does not arise Paired multi-omics data where joint integration tools such as scAI or MOFA+ can exploit cross-omics pairing information directly You need novel cell-type discovery without any annotated target cells — that requires the separate structure preservation loss (--novel_type) mode rather than plain reliability selection

skills.name: gaussian-mixture-simulation-on-unit-circle
skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-simulation-on-unit-circle Use when benchmarking clustering algorithms on non-convex synthetic shapes (rings, half-moons) where ground-truth labels are available and purity scores against GMM, K-means, DBSCAN, OPTICS, or spectral clustering baselines are required. Data with convex, well-separated Gaussian-shaped clusters where distribution-based methods like GMM suffice — the benchmark exists to expose non-convex failure modes No reference (generation-time) labels exist, since purity scores are computed against the labels used for data generation High-dimensional real data without dimensionality reduction — Forest Fire Clustering is limited by the curse of dimensionality and should be preceded by nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE) http://edamontology.org/topic_3306 Generate reproducible synthetic benchmark datasets — Gaussian mixtures centered on the unit circle (sigma=0.15 and sigma=0.2, n=500 each) plus sklearn ring-shaped and half-moon-shaped data (n=1000 each) — to benchmark clustering methods by purity score against generation-time reference labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Generate reproducible synthetic benchmark datasets — Gaussian mixtures centered on the unit circle (sigma=0.15 and sigma=0.2, n=500 each) plus sklearn ring-shaped and half-moon-shaped data (n=1000 each) — to benchmark clustering methods by purity score against generation-time reference labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with convex, well-separated Gaussian-shaped clusters where distribution-based methods like GMM suffice — the benchmark exists to expose non-convex failure modes No reference (generation-time) labels exist, since purity scores are computed against the labels used for data generation High-dimensional real data without dimensionality reduction — Forest Fire Clustering is limited by the curse of dimensionality and should be preceded by nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE)

skills.search_text: gaussian-mixture-technical-component-denoising Use when ADT/protein counts have already been ambient-corrected against empty droplets and residual cell-to-cell technical noise (correlated with isotype controls and background mean) must be regressed out before clustering or UMAP. The dataset has no isotype control antibody measurements — caveats for this case are deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note and software documentation, and the noise matrix cannot be built as described ADT counts have not yet been background-corrected with empty droplets (step I) — the Gaussian mixture must be fit to the step-I transformed values, not raw counts Input is already dsb-normalized (denoise.counts = FALSE exists for cases where step II should be skipped) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 The dsb step II denoising procedure: fit a 2-component Gaussian mixture per cell to log-transformed ADT values to estimate the background mean µ1, combine µ1 with isotype controls into a noise matrix, take PC1 (via prcomp) as the technical component, and remove it with limma::removeBatchEffect to return denoised residuals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the noise robustness of a single-cell trajectory inference or alignment pipeline by sweeping Gaussian noise levels on synthetic scRNA-seq data and recording performance-metric distributions per noise level.
skills.name: gaussian-noise-perturbation-of-scrnaseq-data
skills.search_text: gaussian-noise-perturbation-of-scrnaseq-data Use when you need to quantify the noise robustness of a single-cell trajectory inference or alignment pipeline by sweeping Gaussian noise levels on synthetic scRNA-seq data and recording performance-metric distributions per noise level. The input is authentic scRNA-seq data (e.g., paul15, setty19, velten17) rather than synthetic trajectory pairs — this sweep is designed for synthetic data where ground-truth trajectory structure is known. You need to compare trajectory data containing cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees, so downstream metric computation would not be valid. Datasets have very different global topological structures — the article reports alignment accuracy of CAPITAL degraded for such datasets, so a noise-robustness curve would not isolate noise effects. A robustness-benchmarking procedure that perturbs synthetic single-cell trajectory datasets with independent Gaussian noise across increasing standard deviations and scores how a trajectory-alignment method (CAPITAL) degrades via normalized alignment distance and ATC score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: A robustness-benchmarking procedure that perturbs synthetic single-cell trajectory datasets with independent Gaussian noise across increasing standard deviations and scores how a trajectory-alignment method (CAPITAL) degrades via normalized alignment distance and ATC score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is authentic scRNA-seq data (e.g., paul15, setty19, velten17) rather than synthetic trajectory pairs — this sweep is designed for synthetic data where ground-truth trajectory structure is known. You need to compare trajectory data containing cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees, so downstream metric computation would not be valid. Datasets have very different global topological structures — the article reports alignment accuracy of CAPITAL degraded for such datasets, so a noise-robustness curve would not isolate noise effects.

No inferred GCN is available yet — the GNIAP inference sub-task must be run first before performance assessment The goal is network inference rather than performance evaluation of an already-inferred GCN http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assess the performance of inferred gene co-expression networks (GCNs) using the GNIAP R package, which combines overlap analysis, topological assessment, and biological assessment of network modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12539-021-00440-9
skills.summary: Assess the performance of inferred gene co-expression networks (GCNs) using the GNIAP R package, which combines overlap analysis, topological assessment, and biological assessment of network modules.
