skills.description: Use when a previously inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) needs its performance measured via topological assessment as part of the GNIAP overlap/topological/biological evaluation pipeline.
skills.name: gcn-topological-assessment
skills.search_text: gcn-topological-assessment Use when a previously inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) needs its performance measured via topological assessment as part of the GNIAP overlap/topological/biological evaluation pipeline. The GCN has not yet been inferred — run the prior GNIAP inference sub-task first, since this skill loads the network produced by that step The question only concerns agreement with reference co-expression edges or biological module relevance in isolation — those are the separate overlap analysis and biological assessment dimensions of the GNIAP workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Assessment stage of the GNIAP R package workflow in which an inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) is evaluated for its network-level topological properties, as one of three combined performance dimensions (overlap analysis, topological assessment, and biological assessment) described in the GNIAP R Package Reproducibility Document. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12539-021-00440-9
skills.summary: Assessment stage of the GNIAP R package workflow in which an inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) is evaluated for its network-level topological properties, as one of three combined performance dimensions (overlap analysis, topological assessment, and biological assessment) described in the GNIAP R Package Reproducibility Document.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GCN has not yet been inferred — run the prior GNIAP inference sub-task first, since this skill loads the network produced by that step The question only concerns agreement with reference co-expression edges or biological module relevance in isolation — those are the separate overlap analysis and biological assessment dimensions of the GNIAP workflow

skills.description: Use when building a pseudoalignment target (UTRome) from a GENCODE or other GTF/GFF annotation and transcripts must be restricted to protein-coding features with verified 3' ends before truncation.
skills.name: gencode-annotation-filtering
skills.search_text: gencode-annotation-filtering Use when building a pseudoalignment target (UTRome) from a GENCODE or other GTF/GFF annotation and transcripts must be restricted to protein-coding features with verified 3' ends before truncation. The goal is comprehensive noncoding RNA or novel-CS annotation — the filter discards lncRNA/noncoding transcripts and unvalidated ends (mRNA_end_NF) by design. The input annotation already encodes only validated protein-coding 3' ends (e.g. the deposited txcutr-db UTRome GTF), in which case re-filtering is redundant. Quantifying full-length transcript abundance (e.g. bulk RNA-seq alignment) rather than 3'-anchored isoform quantification, where 3'-end validation is not the relevant filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 Restrict a GENCODE GTF/GFF transcriptome annotation to protein-coding transcripts with validated 3' ends (excluding mRNA_end_NF-tagged transcripts) so that downstream 3'UTR truncation and quantification targets contain only reliably terminated transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Restrict a GENCODE GTF/GFF transcriptome annotation to protein-coding transcripts with validated 3' ends (excluding mRNA_end_NF-tagged transcripts) so that downstream 3'UTR truncation and quantification targets contain only reliably terminated transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comprehensive noncoding RNA or novel-CS annotation — the filter discards lncRNA/noncoding transcripts and unvalidated ends (mRNA_end_NF) by design. The input annotation already encodes only validated protein-coding 3' ends (e.g. the deposited txcutr-db UTRome GTF), in which case re-filtering is redundant. Quantifying full-length transcript abundance (e.g. bulk RNA-seq alignment) rather than 3'-anchored isoform quantification, where 3'-end validation is not the relevant filter.

skills.description: Use when building or validating a cleavage site (CS) catalog from 3′-end scRNA-seq data and you need GENCODE-annotated transcript 3′ end coordinates as reference intervals for overlap-based classification.
skills.name: gencode-transcript-3prime-end-window-parsing
skills.search_text: gencode-transcript-3prime-end-window-parsing Use when building or validating a cleavage site (CS) catalog from 3′-end scRNA-seq data and you need GENCODE-annotated transcript 3′ end coordinates as reference intervals for overlap-based classification. You need exact 3′ end matching rather than tolerance-window overlap — the 40 nt window deliberately allows coordinate slack around annotated ends Your reference annotation is not GENCODE (e.g., you are validating against PolyASite 2.0, which is a separate downstream overlap step) Input reads are 10x Genomics data that do not span cleavage sites, so exact de novo 3′ end mapping is not possible and window-based validation of de novo CS is inapplicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Parses GENCODE GTF annotations (vM25 mouse, v39 human) to construct 40 nt windows centered on annotated transcript 3′ ends, providing reference coordinate intervals against which candidate Microwell-seq cleavage sites are intersected to classify them as GENCODE-annotated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Parses GENCODE GTF annotations (vM25 mouse, v39 human) to construct 40 nt windows centered on annotated transcript 3′ ends, providing reference coordinate intervals against which candidate Microwell-seq cleavage sites are intersected to classify them as GENCODE-annotated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need exact 3′ end matching rather than tolerance-window overlap — the 40 nt window deliberately allows coordinate slack around annotated ends Your reference annotation is not GENCODE (e.g., you are validating against PolyASite 2.0, which is a separate downstream overlap step) Input reads are 10x Genomics data that do not span cleavage sites, so exact de novo 3′ end mapping is not possible and window-based validation of de novo CS is inapplicable

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo isoform assemblies (e.g. cloudrnaSPAdes, rnaSPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) by counting uniquely assigned GENCODE annotated isoforms per gene from IsoQuant assignment output files.
skills.name: gencode-transcript-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: gencode-transcript-annotation-matching Use when comparing de novo isoform assemblies (e.g. cloudrnaSPAdes, rnaSPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) by counting uniquely assigned GENCODE annotated isoforms per gene from IsoQuant assignment output files. The assembler never produced an assembly (e.g. RNA-Bloom failed at the k-mer counting step) — record it as a pipeline failure, not as zero recovered isoforms. The gene of interest has few or no annotated GENCODE isoforms, so 'unique isoform recovery' is not a discriminative benchmark between assemblers. Assemblies should be assessed on full-length transcript quality metrics rather than annotated-isoform recall — use a dedicated assembly evaluation tool instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Counts how many annotated GENCODE isoforms of a target gene are uniquely recovered by each transcriptome assembler by parsing IsoQuant assignment outputs against the GENCODE v32 GTF, as demonstrated on the ATP6AP2 gene (34 isoforms, chromosome X) from the real SPIso-seq human brain dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Counts how many annotated GENCODE isoforms of a target gene are uniquely recovered by each transcriptome assembler by parsing IsoQuant assignment outputs against the GENCODE v32 GTF, as demonstrated on the ATP6AP2 gene (34 isoforms, chromosome X) from the real SPIso-seq human brain dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assembler never produced an assembly (e.g. RNA-Bloom failed at the k-mer counting step) — record it as a pipeline failure, not as zero recovered isoforms. The gene of interest has few or no annotated GENCODE isoforms, so 'unique isoform recovery' is not a discriminative benchmark between assemblers. Assemblies should be assessed on full-length transcript quality metrics rather than annotated-isoform recall — use a dedicated assembly evaluation tool instead.

skills.description: Use when you have binary gene cluster absence/presence matrices plus literature-based lifestyle labels and need to train lifestyle classifiers or predict lifestyles of genomes from species with no representative in the training set.
skills.name: gene-absence-presence-matrix-modeling
skills.search_text: gene-absence-presence-matrix-modeling Use when you have binary gene cluster absence/presence matrices plus literature-based lifestyle labels and need to train lifestyle classifiers or predict lifestyles of genomes from species with no representative in the training set. Genomes do not meet the CheckM quality thresholds (>90% completeness, <5% contamination) and would inject noise into the feature matrix No lifestyle metadata labels are available for any training genomes, so the supervised random forest cannot be fit The goal is only to detect genes present in >90% of genomes (core-genome analysis) rather than to classify lifestyles from cluster distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train and validate random forest lifestyle classifiers on gene cluster absence/presence matrices from Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas genomes, using chi2 feature selection and tree-vote confidence to predict lifestyles even for species entirely excluded from training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Train and validate random forest lifestyle classifiers on gene cluster absence/presence matrices from Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas genomes, using chi2 feature selection and tree-vote confidence to predict lifestyles even for species entirely excluded from training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genomes do not meet the CheckM quality thresholds (>90% completeness, <5% contamination) and would inject noise into the feature matrix No lifestyle metadata labels are available for any training genomes, so the supervised random forest cannot be fit The goal is only to detect genes present in >90% of genomes (core-genome analysis) rather than to classify lifestyles from cluster distributions

skills.description: Use when matched peak-level scATAC-Seq counts must be summarized to per-gene accessibility (3kb-upstream+gene-body aggregation around RNA-defined marker genes) to validate primed states or compare chromatin opening across cell groups.
skills.name: gene-accessibility-aggregation-from-atac-peaks
skills.search_text: gene-accessibility-aggregation-from-atac-peaks Use when matched peak-level scATAC-Seq counts must be summarized to per-gene accessibility (3kb-upstream+gene-body aggregation around RNA-defined marker genes) to validate primed states or compare chromatin opening across cell groups. The target is per-cell TF motif variability rather than per-gene accessibility - chromVAR computes motif deviations directly from the peak matrix, so aggregating peaks to genes is the wrong operation No marker-gene list or gene-body/TSS annotations are available to anchor peaks, so the 3kb-upstream+gene-body assignment window cannot be defined The scATAC-Seq data are neither matched to the same cells nor represent the same cell-types as the scRNA-Seq priming calls (the paper validated only in the same cells via SHARE-Seq or separate populations of the same cell-types) http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates a gene-level accessibility matrix from peak-level scATAC-Seq data by summing peaks within a region 3kb upstream of each marker gene plus the gene body, then log-normalizes the gene accessible count matrix with Seurat. This converts chromatin peak data into per-gene scores that validate scRNA-Seq-derived DICE primed states in matched or same-cell ATAC profiles (e.g. SHARE-Seq). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Generates a gene-level accessibility matrix from peak-level scATAC-Seq data by summing peaks within a region 3kb upstream of each marker gene plus the gene body, then log-normalizes the gene accessible count matrix with Seurat. This converts chromatin peak data into per-gene scores that validate scRNA-Seq-derived DICE primed states in matched or same-cell ATAC profiles (e.g. SHARE-Seq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is per-cell TF motif variability rather than per-gene accessibility - chromVAR computes motif deviations directly from the peak matrix, so aggregating peaks to genes is the wrong operation No marker-gene list or gene-body/TSS annotations are available to anchor peaks, so the 3kb-upstream+gene-body assignment window cannot be defined The scATAC-Seq data are neither matched to the same cells nor represent the same cell-types as the scRNA-Seq priming calls (the paper validated only in the same cells via SHARE-Seq or separate populations of the same cell-types)

skills.description: Use when snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq come from unpaired samples and you need a shared low-dimensional representation before cell pairing or downstream GRN inference; the ATAC assay must be converted to a gene activity matrix.
skills.name: gene-activity-score-integration
skills.search_text: gene-activity-score-integration Use when snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq come from unpaired samples and you need a shared low-dimensional representation before cell pairing or downstream GRN inference; the ATAC assay must be converted to a gene activity matrix. Data are paired 10x Multiome (pbmc_granulocyte_sorted_10k) measured in the same cells — no unpaired integration or cell pairing is needed. Input is a pre-integrated or already co-embedded multimodal object; re-running CCA co-embedding would be redundant. The goal is single-modality analysis of ATAC peaks without a gene-level feature space; gene activity integration is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 Use ArchR-derived gene activity scores from snATAC-seq as the common feature space for integrating unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq data in scMEGA, enabling CCA co-embedding, Harmony batch correction, and one-to-one cell pairing into a pseudo-multimodal dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Use ArchR-derived gene activity scores from snATAC-seq as the common feature space for integrating unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq data in scMEGA, enabling CCA co-embedding, Harmony batch correction, and one-to-one cell pairing into a pseudo-multimodal dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are paired 10x Multiome (pbmc_granulocyte_sorted_10k) measured in the same cells — no unpaired integration or cell pairing is needed. Input is a pre-integrated or already co-embedded multimodal object; re-running CCA co-embedding would be redundant. The goal is single-modality analysis of ATAC peaks without a gene-level feature space; gene activity integration is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you already have a gene-to-gene-age-class orthomap table for a focal species (e.g. from oggmap of2orthomap on OrthoFinder output) and need per-age-class gene counts for quality checking or downstream plotting.
skills.name: gene-age-class-count-summarization
skills.search_text: gene-age-class-count-summarization Use when you already have a gene-to-gene-age-class orthomap table for a focal species (e.g. from oggmap of2orthomap on OrthoFinder output) and need per-age-class gene counts for quality checking or downstream plotting. You need gene-age-weighted expression per cell or transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) on scRNA objects — that requires oggmap's Scanpy-based downstream steps, not simple per-class counts. The orthogroup-to-age assignments do not yet exist — run oggmap of2orthomap (or eggnog/plaza equivalents) on the gene family results first; this skill only summarizes the finished orthomap. http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregate an extracted orthomap (gene-to-gene-age-class assignments, e.g. danio_rerio_orthomap.tsv produced by oggmap of2orthomap) with pandas to count the number of genes per gene age class, writing a per-class count table such as danio_rerio_age_class_counts.csv. This summarizes the evolutionary age composition of a focal species' gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Aggregate an extracted orthomap (gene-to-gene-age-class assignments, e.g. danio_rerio_orthomap.tsv produced by oggmap of2orthomap) with pandas to count the number of genes per gene age class, writing a per-class count table such as danio_rerio_age_class_counts.csv. This summarizes the evolutionary age composition of a focal species' gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need gene-age-weighted expression per cell or transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) on scRNA objects — that requires oggmap's Scanpy-based downstream steps, not simple per-class counts. The orthogroup-to-age assignments do not yet exist — run oggmap of2orthomap (or eggnog/plaza equivalents) on the gene family results first; this skill only summarizes the finished orthomap.

skills.description: Use when a TEI-annotated AnnData (h5ad) with gene age class annotations is available and you need a table of relative expression shares per gene age class per observation group (cell type, timepoint).
skills.name: gene-age-class-relative-expression-normalization
skills.search_text: gene-age-class-relative-expression-normalization Use when a TEI-annotated AnnData (h5ad) with gene age class annotations is available and you need a table of relative expression shares per gene age class per observation group (cell type, timepoint). The AnnData object lacks gene age class annotations (no orthomap matched to genes yet) — first run the orthomap extraction/matching steps. You need gene age-weighted summary indices such as TEI or partial TEI per cell rather than per-group relative expression per age class. The goal is extracting the orthomap itself (of2orthomap, eggNOG, PLAZA) rather than computing expression per age class. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes relative expression per gene age class in scRNA data using oggmap's get_rematrix, grouping mean expression by an annotated observation (e.g. cell type or sampling timepoint) and normalizing each group's age-class values to shares summing to 1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Computes relative expression per gene age class in scRNA data using oggmap's get_rematrix, grouping mean expression by an annotated observation (e.g. cell type or sampling timepoint) and normalizing each group's age-class values to shares summing to 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData object lacks gene age class annotations (no orthomap matched to genes yet) — first run the orthomap extraction/matching steps. You need gene age-weighted summary indices such as TEI or partial TEI per cell rather than per-group relative expression per age class. The goal is extracting the orthomap itself (of2orthomap, eggNOG, PLAZA) rather than computing expression per age class.

skills.description: Use when an AnnData/scRNA object must be annotated with per-gene evolutionary ages (an orthomap) before computing a transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI), e.g. reproducing hourglass or young-gene-peak patterns across embryo stages.
skills.name: gene-age-orthomap-matching
skills.search_text: gene-age-orthomap-matching Use when an AnnData/scRNA object must be annotated with per-gene evolutionary ages (an orthomap) before computing a transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI), e.g. reproducing hourglass or young-gene-peak patterns across embryo stages. The scRNA object and gene age table are already merged (age classes already present in AnnData var/obs) — re-matching would duplicate annotation effort No orthogroup or gene family resource (OrthoFinder, eggNOG, PLAZA) exists for the query species, so no orthomap can be extracted or sourced The analysis does not involve gene age-weighted or evolutionary indices (e.g. plain differential expression or cell-type annotation), where orthomap matching adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Match gene and transcript identifiers with their orthogroup-derived evolutionary age class (an orthomap from oggmap/OrthoFinder or eggNOG) against the var_names of a Scanpy AnnData single-cell object, so that gene age-weighted indices such as TEI or partial TEI can be computed per cell or per developmental stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Match gene and transcript identifiers with their orthogroup-derived evolutionary age class (an orthomap from oggmap/OrthoFinder or eggNOG) against the var_names of a Scanpy AnnData single-cell object, so that gene age-weighted indices such as TEI or partial TEI can be computed per cell or per developmental stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA object and gene age table are already merged (age classes already present in AnnData var/obs) — re-matching would duplicate annotation effort No orthogroup or gene family resource (OrthoFinder, eggNOG, PLAZA) exists for the query species, so no orthomap can be extracted or sourced The analysis does not involve gene age-weighted or evolutionary indices (e.g. plain differential expression or cell-type annotation), where orthomap matching adds no value

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq AnnData objects need an evolutionary age metric (TEI or partial TEI profiles) per cell, especially for large datasets (~90,000+ up to 1e6 cells) where per-cell computation must stay tractable.
skills.name: gene-age-weighted-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-age-weighted-expression-analysis Use when single-cell RNA-seq AnnData objects need an evolutionary age metric (TEI or partial TEI profiles) per cell, especially for large datasets (~90,000+ up to 1e6 cells) where per-cell computation must stay tractable. Input expression data is dense or not stored as a sparse CSR AnnData matrix — the scalability claim rests on sparse-matrix calculation No gene age / orthomap is available or extractable for the query species (TEI weights require phylostrata per gene) The goal is bulk-RNA stage-level analysis with only a small number of samples rather than per-cell TEI across large scRNA datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Computes the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) — an expression-weighted mean of gene phylostrata per cell following Domazet-Lošo and Tautz 2010 — on single-cell RNA data using oggmap's sparse-matrix get_tei implementation, which scales to millions of cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Computes the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) — an expression-weighted mean of gene phylostrata per cell following Domazet-Lošo and Tautz 2010 — on single-cell RNA data using oggmap's sparse-matrix get_tei implementation, which scales to millions of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data is dense or not stored as a sparse CSR AnnData matrix — the scalability claim rests on sparse-matrix calculation No gene age / orthomap is available or extractable for the query species (TEI weights require phylostrata per gene) The goal is bulk-RNA stage-level analysis with only a small number of samples rather than per-cell TEI across large scRNA datasets

skills.description: Use when building the CRIT feature matrix for candidate genes and you have per-sample TCGA mutation (data_mutations_extended.txt) and CNV (data_CNA.txt) files that must be dichotomized into per-gene alteration proportions and Z-scored.
skills.name: gene-alteration-proportion-zscoring
skills.search_text: gene-alteration-proportion-zscoring Use when building the CRIT feature matrix for candidate genes and you have per-sample TCGA mutation (data_mutations_extended.txt) and CNV (data_CNA.txt) files that must be dichotomized into per-gene alteration proportions and Z-scored. You already have a merged feature table (MATRIX.txt) with Zp columns populated — recompute only when raw TCGA mutation/CNV inputs change You need survival-impact or functional-annotation features (Zs or Zg) — those require the survival log-rank or GoSemSim pipelines, not alteration proportion Your data are non-cancer or lack per-sample mutation/CNV calls, since Zp depends on dichotomized TCGA alteration data across the 19 batches of 12 cancer types http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the CRIT 'Zp' feature: a Z score built from dichotomized TCGA mutation and copy-number (CNV) data that reflects the proportion of gene alterations per sample in each cancer type or batch, quantifying how frequently a candidate RBP gene is altered across 19 batches of 12 cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Computes the CRIT 'Zp' feature: a Z score built from dichotomized TCGA mutation and copy-number (CNV) data that reflects the proportion of gene alterations per sample in each cancer type or batch, quantifying how frequently a candidate RBP gene is altered across 19 batches of 12 cancer types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a merged feature table (MATRIX.txt) with Zp columns populated — recompute only when raw TCGA mutation/CNV inputs change You need survival-impact or functional-annotation features (Zs or Zg) — those require the survival log-rank or GoSemSim pipelines, not alteration proportion Your data are non-cancer or lack per-sample mutation/CNV calls, since Zp depends on dichotomized TCGA alteration data across the 19 batches of 12 cancer types

skills.description: Use when preparing a reference for splicing-status prediction of scRNA-seq reads: you have a gene annotation GTF and matching genome FASTA and need an augmented spliced+unspliced transcriptome (spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, t2g_3col.tsv).
skills.name: gene-annotation-gtf-processing
skills.search_text: gene-annotation-gtf-processing Use when preparing a reference for splicing-status prediction of scRNA-seq reads: you have a gene annotation GTF and matching genome FASTA and need an augmented spliced+unspliced transcriptome (spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, t2g_3col.tsv). You only need a standard spliced transcriptome index (e.g. Salmon/kallisto quantification), not a spliced+unspliced augmented reference for splicing-status prediction. Your GTF and genome FASTA come from different genome builds — the unspliced genomic-span transcripts require consistent coordinates. You already have a completed spliceu index directory containing spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, and t2g_3col.tsv. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the Forseti spliceu augmented gene annotation reference, in which every transcript is represented twice — as a spliced exon concatenation and as an unspliced genomic span — from a standard GTF plus genome FASTA, so downstream alignments gain read compatibility to both splicing states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Constructs the Forseti spliceu augmented gene annotation reference, in which every transcript is represented twice — as a spliced exon concatenation and as an unspliced genomic span — from a standard GTF plus genome FASTA, so downstream alignments gain read compatibility to both splicing states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a standard spliced transcriptome index (e.g. Salmon/kallisto quantification), not a spliced+unspliced augmented reference for splicing-status prediction. Your GTF and genome FASTA come from different genome builds — the unspliced genomic-span transcripts require consistent coordinates. You already have a completed spliceu index directory containing spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, and t2g_3col.tsv.

skills.description: Use when you have groHMM-predicted TAR BED files from scRNA-seq alignments and need to partition them into aTARs vs uTARs relative to a refFlat annotation, or quantify the fraction of reads assigned to uTARs.
skills.name: gene-annotation-overlap-classification-of-tars
skills.search_text: gene-annotation-overlap-classification-of-tars Use when you have groHMM-predicted TAR BED files from scRNA-seq alignments and need to partition them into aTARs vs uTARs relative to a refFlat annotation, or quantify the fraction of reads assigned to uTARs. Starting input is already a cellranger count matrix (use the from_cellranger workflow mode instead of re-annotating from FASTQs) Your analysis goal is annotating uTARs by sequence homology rather than classifying them against an existing annotation Only a high-quality, near-complete annotation is needed and no quantification of transcription outside annotations is desired http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies HMM-derived transcriptionally active regions (TARs) from scRNA-seq data as annotated TARs (aTARs) or unannotated TARs (uTARs) by overlap against refFlat-format gene annotations, quantifying how much transcriptional activity falls outside the current genome annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Classifies HMM-derived transcriptionally active regions (TARs) from scRNA-seq data as annotated TARs (aTARs) or unannotated TARs (uTARs) by overlap against refFlat-format gene annotations, quantifying how much transcriptional activity falls outside the current genome annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Starting input is already a cellranger count matrix (use the from_cellranger workflow mode instead of re-annotating from FASTQs) Your analysis goal is annotating uTARs by sequence homology rather than classifying them against an existing annotation Only a high-quality, near-complete annotation is needed and no quantification of transcription outside annotations is desired

skills.description: Use when per-cell allelic state posteriors (P/B/M) from a beta-binomial mixture on F1-hybrid scRNA-Seq cells are available and genes must be assigned to seven ASE profile classes and validated.
skills.name: gene-ase-profile-class-verification
skills.search_text: gene-ase-profile-class-verification Use when per-cell allelic state posteriors (P/B/M) from a beta-binomial mixture on F1-hybrid scRNA-Seq cells are available and genes must be assigned to seven ASE profile classes and validated. The input is raw allele-specific read counts rather than per-cell P/B/M posterior state classifications — the state classification must be run first via the scBASE beta-binomial mixture model. skills.summary: Classifies genes into scBASE's seven ASE profile classes (P, B, M, PB, BM, MP, PBM) from per-cell P/B/M posterior state assignments, then verifies exemplar gene calls and the blastocyst PBM fraction (56.9%) against the paper.

skills.search_text: gene-embedding-cosine-neighbor-ranking Use when a trained GeneVector embedding (genes.vec) is available and you must rank a query gene's nearest neighbors by cosine similarity to confirm pathway co-membership or seed a metagene. You need the direction of regulation: GeneVector's MI is agnostic to activation vs repression, so cosine neighbors cannot separate co-activation from co-repression. Query or pathway genes were removed by entropy-based QC (entropy_threshold=1.0) or HVG subsetting and are absent from genes.vec — they cannot be ranked. The embedding was trained with target='pearson' and pathway fidelity matters: expected IFIT1 top-16 overlap with Reactome R-HSA-913531 falls to 6/16 vs 12/16 with the MI target. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Rank a query gene's nearest neighbors in a trained GeneVector gene embedding by cosine similarity (compute_similarities on input+output-averaged vectors) to verify that the embedding geometry recovers pathway co-members, e.g., interferon signaling genes around IFIT1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Rank a query gene's nearest neighbors in a trained GeneVector gene embedding by cosine similarity (compute_similarities on input+output-averaged vectors) to verify that the embedding geometry recovers pathway co-members, e.g., interferon signaling genes around IFIT1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the direction of regulation: GeneVector's MI is agnostic to activation vs repression, so cosine neighbors cannot separate co-activation from co-repression. Query or pathway genes were removed by entropy-based QC (entropy_threshold=1.0) or HVG subsetting and are absent from genes.vec — they cannot be ranked. The embedding was trained with target='pearson' and pathway fidelity matters: expected IFIT1 top-16 overlap with Reactome R-HSA-913531 falls to 6/16 vs 12/16 with the MI target.

skills.name: gene-embedding-entropy-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-embedding-entropy-ranking Use when trained graph-embedding outputs (e.g., DGMP logits and ZF, Zin, Zout, ZMLP vectors) are available and you need to isolate genes with dissimilar neighbors to diagnose embedding class separation. When the goal is general cancer driver gene ranking or prioritization by predicted probability — this skill selects by neighborhood entropy, not by driver likelihood When only node-level omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) are available without trained graph embeddings or a GRN to define neighborhoods http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Ranks genes by neighborhood discrete entropy computed on DGMP embedding neighborhoods, then selects the top 50 predicted cancer and top 50 predicted non-cancer driver genes with highest entropy to probe where DGCN embeddings degrade and MLP embeddings compensate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Ranks genes by neighborhood discrete entropy computed on DGMP embedding neighborhoods, then selects the top 50 predicted cancer and top 50 predicted non-cancer driver genes with highest entropy to probe where DGCN embeddings degrade and MLP embeddings compensate.

skills.description: Use when constructing cell-lineage-specific gene embeddings from scRNA-seq data and a prior gene interaction network, e.g. inputs to downstream driver-regulator or RGM analysis.
skills.name: gene-embedding-learning
skills.search_text: gene-embedding-learning Use when constructing cell-lineage-specific gene embeddings from scRNA-seq data and a prior gene interaction network, e.g. inputs to downstream driver-regulator or RGM analysis. The goal is driver-regulator identification or RGM activity scoring alone, without learning new embeddings from a prior network (use cf.driver_regulators / cf.RGM_activity directly on existing results) The data involve multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations or extrinsic factors such as cell–cell communication, which CEFCON explicitly does not handle Ground-truth labels are available and a supervised framework such as GENELink is feasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Learns gene representations by training CEFCON's graph attention network under a deep graph infomax (DGI) contrastive objective on a cell-lineage prior network with scRNA-seq expression and differential-expression encodings; the resulting node embeddings accompany the cell-lineage-specific GRN. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Learns gene representations by training CEFCON's graph attention network under a deep graph infomax (DGI) contrastive objective on a cell-lineage prior network with scRNA-seq expression and differential-expression encodings; the resulting node embeddings accompany the cell-lineage-specific GRN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is driver-regulator identification or RGM activity scoring alone, without learning new embeddings from a prior network (use cf.driver_regulators / cf.RGM_activity directly on existing results) The data involve multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations or extrinsic factors such as cell–cell communication, which CEFCON explicitly does not handle Ground-truth labels are available and a supervised framework such as GENELink is feasible

skills.description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed human genes (from microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or a clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to test which curated environmental gene modules (infection, diet, cigarette smoking, toxic chemicals) are statistically over-represented.
skills.name: gene-environment-module-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-environment-module-annotation Use when you have a list of differentially expressed human genes (from microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or a clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to test which curated environmental gene modules (infection, diet, cigarette smoking, toxic chemicals) are statistically over-represented. The question concerns genetic data types such as SNPs, copy number variants or DNA methylations — E.PAGE does not yet cover these. You need joint odds ratios or interaction odds ratios, which the paper states are not yet included in the statistical tests. The gene list is non-human or the environmental context falls outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Enrich a list of differentially expressed genes against the E.PATH/E.PAGE curated database of 522 manually annotated gene modules (25,789 genes, four environmental factors: cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) using a Fisher exact (hypergeometric) test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to reveal gene–environment associations behind a disease gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Enrich a list of differentially expressed genes against the E.PATH/E.PAGE curated database of 522 manually annotated gene modules (25,789 genes, four environmental factors: cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) using a Fisher exact (hypergeometric) test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, to reveal gene–environment associations behind a disease gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns genetic data types such as SNPs, copy number variants or DNA methylations — E.PAGE does not yet cover these. You need joint odds ratios or interaction odds ratios, which the paper states are not yet included in the statistical tests. The gene list is non-human or the environmental context falls outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether incorporating VDJ features into trajectory inference yields higher fate-prediction accuracy than expression-only trajectory analysis, e.g. on fetal immune atlas DP-to-CD4/CD8 T-cell data.
skills.name: gene-expression-baseline-trajectory-comparison
skills.search_text: gene-expression-baseline-trajectory-comparison Use when benchmarking whether incorporating VDJ features into trajectory inference yields higher fate-prediction accuracy than expression-only trajectory analysis, e.g. on fetal immune atlas DP-to-CD4/CD8 T-cell data. When the input data lacks paired TCR/BCR sequencing (only a gene expression matrix is available) — there is no VDJ arm to compare against When the underlying biology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing) or requires topologies beyond bifurcation/linear — the destiny-based diffusion map and absorbing Markov chain cannot represent them http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs a matched gene-expression-only trajectory baseline (diffusion map + absorbing Markov chain on expression-derived PCs) alongside the VDJ feature space trajectory from dandelionR, to quantify how much VDJ receptor information improves CD4/CD8 fate prediction from double-positive T cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Runs a matched gene-expression-only trajectory baseline (diffusion map + absorbing Markov chain on expression-derived PCs) alongside the VDJ feature space trajectory from dandelionR, to quantify how much VDJ receptor information improves CD4/CD8 fate prediction from double-positive T cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input data lacks paired TCR/BCR sequencing (only a gene expression matrix is available) — there is no VDJ arm to compare against When the underlying biology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing) or requires topologies beyond bifurcation/linear — the destiny-based diffusion map and absorbing Markov chain cannot represent them

skills.description: Use when the input is a continuous (or discretized) gene expression matrix and the goal is to discover overlapping trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters and compare them against planted ground truth or other algorithms.
skills.name: gene-expression-biclustering
skills.search_text: gene-expression-biclustering Use when the input is a continuous (or discretized) gene expression matrix and the goal is to discover overlapping trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters and compare them against planted ground truth or other algorithms. The target biclusters are narrow constant-row/constant-column patterns specifically designed for BicSPAM, which outperformed UniBic on narrow biclusters The data are raw sequencing reads or unmatrixed measurements rather than a rows-by-conditions expression matrix A clustering that partitions all rows into disjoint groups is sufficient — UniBic seeks overlapping local trend-preserving submatrices, not global partitions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects trend-preserving biclusters in gene expression matrices using UniBic, which finds LCS-based seeds between rows of an index matrix, then extends and filters biclusters by significance. The runibic R package provides a parallel C++11 implementation with a Biclust wrapper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: Detects trend-preserving biclusters in gene expression matrices using UniBic, which finds LCS-based seeds between rows of an index matrix, then extends and filters biclusters by significance. The runibic R package provides a parallel C++11 implementation with a Biclust wrapper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target biclusters are narrow constant-row/constant-column patterns specifically designed for BicSPAM, which outperformed UniBic on narrow biclusters The data are raw sequencing reads or unmatrixed measurements rather than a rows-by-conditions expression matrix A clustering that partitions all rows into disjoint groups is sufficient — UniBic seeks overlapping local trend-preserving submatrices, not global partitions

skills.description: Use when preprocessing sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices (e.g. Xin GSE81608) to build a binary low-dimensional representation of cells, where dropouts must be handled as signals rather than imputed away.
skills.name: gene-expression-binarization
skills.search_text: gene-expression-binarization Use when preprocessing sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices (e.g. Xin GSE81608) to build a binary low-dimensional representation of cells, where dropouts must be handled as signals rather than imputed away. Input is already a binary or imputed expression matrix — binarization and dropout-strengthening are designed for sparse, dropout-prone count data The analysis goal is the quantitative (LC2) representation based on quasi-trend-preserved expression patterns, which uses the raw normalized values rather than binary encoding Retaining only 2000 HVGs would discard known informative genes for the study, since the article notes this exclusion as a limitation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Binarizes dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression values (0 if zero, 1 otherwise) as the first step of scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1), treating dropouts as weak signals that are later strengthened by clustering genes with similar binary expression patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Binarizes dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression values (0 if zero, 1 otherwise) as the first step of scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1), treating dropouts as weak signals that are later strengthened by clustering genes with similar binary expression patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binary or imputed expression matrix — binarization and dropout-strengthening are designed for sparse, dropout-prone count data The analysis goal is the quantitative (LC2) representation based on quasi-trend-preserved expression patterns, which uses the raw normalized values rather than binary encoding Retaining only 2000 HVGs would discard known informative genes for the study, since the article notes this exclusion as a limitation

skills.description: Use when you have null (e.g., gRNA-free or split-group) P values from single-cell DE or co-expression testing and need to check P-value uniformity across expression levels via expression-stratified KS tests.
skills.name: gene-expression-binning
skills.search_text: gene-expression-binning Use when you have null (e.g., gRNA-free or split-group) P values from single-cell DE or co-expression testing and need to check P-value uniformity across expression levels via expression-stratified KS tests. The method under evaluation is a generalized linear model or log(CPM+1) normalization known to introduce expression-dependent normalization biases, and the goal is to evaluate its null calibration rather than a covariate-removing method like Normalisr Input P values are not null (e.g., real gRNA perturbation effects or true case–control DE); uniformity is expected only for null P values (guide-unassigned cells or synthetic co-expression-free data) The data are not UMI-based (the article only focused on UMI datasets; full-length platforms were not validated and may need revalidation of covariates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratifies genes into 10 ordered expression-level bins and applies two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests of null P values against the uniform distribution, to verify that a normalization/association method (e.g., Normalisr) yields unbiased P values independent of gene expression level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Stratifies genes into 10 ordered expression-level bins and applies two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests of null P values against the uniform distribution, to verify that a normalization/association method (e.g., Normalisr) yields unbiased P values independent of gene expression level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method under evaluation is a generalized linear model or log(CPM+1) normalization known to introduce expression-dependent normalization biases, and the goal is to evaluate its null calibration rather than a covariate-removing method like Normalisr Input P values are not null (e.g., real gRNA perturbation effects or true case–control DE); uniformity is expected only for null P values (guide-unassigned cells or synthetic co-expression-free data) The data are not UMI-based (the article only focused on UMI datasets; full-length platforms were not validated and may need revalidation of covariates)

skills.description: Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates and a single-cell count matrix are available and you need to partition genes by bulk expression level (true-zero silent genes vs. expressed bins) to test whether an imputation method retains biological zeros while imputing dropouts.
skills.name: gene-expression-binning-from-bulk-replicates
skills.search_text: gene-expression-binning-from-bulk-replicates Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates and a single-cell count matrix are available and you need to partition genes by bulk expression level (true-zero silent genes vs. expressed bins) to test whether an imputation method retains biological zeros while imputing dropouts. No matched bulk replicates exist for the same population — the true-zero (biologically silent) bin cannot be defined without zero-bulk-expression evidence The analysis goal is general imputation accuracy (e.g., masked-value recovery or clustering accuracy) rather than true-zero retention assessment Single-cell data are not preprocessed per the AutoImpute pipeline (gene filter >=3 reads in >=3 cells, median library-size normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion genes, log2 with pseudo-count 1), making zero fractions incomparable to the paper's benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Bins genes by matched bulk RNA-seq median expression (with zero-bulk genes assigned to a biologically-silent true-zero bin) so that zero-retention in imputed single-cell data can be measured per expression level, as done for the Trapnell myoblast data in the AutoImpute paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Bins genes by matched bulk RNA-seq median expression (with zero-bulk genes assigned to a biologically-silent true-zero bin) so that zero-retention in imputed single-cell data can be measured per expression level, as done for the Trapnell myoblast data in the AutoImpute paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched bulk replicates exist for the same population — the true-zero (biologically silent) bin cannot be defined without zero-bulk-expression evidence The analysis goal is general imputation accuracy (e.g., masked-value recovery or clustering accuracy) rather than true-zero retention assessment Single-cell data are not preprocessed per the AutoImpute pipeline (gene filter >=3 reads in >=3 cells, median library-size normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion genes, log2 with pseudo-count 1), making zero fractions incomparable to the paper's benchmark

skills.description: Use when whole-blood gene expression measurements and matched per-sample clinical laboratory values (e.g. CRP, lymphocyte counts, IFN scores) are available and you need to test whether gene abundance is linearly associated with disease-severity markers.
skills.name: gene-expression-clinical-variable-correlation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-clinical-variable-correlation Use when whole-blood gene expression measurements and matched per-sample clinical laboratory values (e.g. CRP, lymphocyte counts, IFN scores) are available and you need to test whether gene abundance is linearly associated with disease-severity markers. The data are group-level differential-expression summaries (p-value, adjusted p-value, fold-change between severe and mild COVID-19, as in the anova folder files) rather than sample-wise matched expression and clinical values, so per-sample correlation is impossible. The relationship between gene and clinical variable is expected to be non-linear or monotonic-only, where a Pearson r would misrepresent the association. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes sample-wise Pearson correlations between focal gene transcript abundances (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1 from the Ong et al. 2021 COVID-19 cohort) and clinical laboratory variables (CRP, lymphocyte counts, 28-gene type I IFN score) to validate that severity-associated transcripts track clinical predictors of severe disease. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: Computes sample-wise Pearson correlations between focal gene transcript abundances (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1 from the Ong et al. 2021 COVID-19 cohort) and clinical laboratory variables (CRP, lymphocyte counts, 28-gene type I IFN score) to validate that severity-associated transcripts track clinical predictors of severe disease.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are group-level differential-expression summaries (p-value, adjusted p-value, fold-change between severe and mild COVID-19, as in the anova folder files) rather than sample-wise matched expression and clinical values, so per-sample correlation is impossible. The relationship between gene and clinical variable is expected to be non-linear or monotonic-only, where a Pearson r would misrepresent the association.

skills.description: Use when a CSV gene-expression data frame with gene identifiers and log-fold-change (LFC) values must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters with per-gene membership probabilities.
skills.name: gene-expression-clustering
skills.search_text: gene-expression-clustering Use when a CSV gene-expression data frame with gene identifiers and log-fold-change (LFC) values must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters with per-gene membership probabilities. The input is raw counts or a feature table lacking log-fold-change (LFC) values — the article states LFC is the key analytical parameter of the machine learning pipeline and exploratory analyses. The goal is protein type and cellular location classification, assessment of gene clusters via known interactors (UniProt/STRINGdb), or epigenomics analysis rather than expression-pattern clustering. Genes are already assigned to expression-pattern clusters and only downstream exploration of a selected pattern is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 OmicInt's mclust-based Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline clusters genes from a CSV expression data frame into distinct expression-pattern types using probability-based classification, retaining per-cluster membership probabilities so a pattern of interest can be selected for downstream exploration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2021.100025
skills.summary: OmicInt's mclust-based Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline clusters genes from a CSV expression data frame into distinct expression-pattern types using probability-based classification, retaining per-cluster membership probabilities so a pattern of interest can be selected for downstream exploration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw counts or a feature table lacking log-fold-change (LFC) values — the article states LFC is the key analytical parameter of the machine learning pipeline and exploratory analyses. The goal is protein type and cellular location classification, assessment of gene clusters via known interactors (UniProt/STRINGdb), or epigenomics analysis rather than expression-pattern clustering. Genes are already assigned to expression-pattern clusters and only downstream exploration of a selected pattern is required.

skills.description: Use when a Lamian lamian_test run has produced significant TDE or XDE genes (FDR.overall < 0.05) and you need to organize them into expression-dynamics clusters and interpret each cluster via GO enrichment.
skills.name: gene-expression-clustering-and-go-enrichment
skills.search_text: gene-expression-clustering-and-go-enrichment Use when a Lamian lamian_test run has produced significant TDE or XDE genes (FDR.overall < 0.05) and you need to organize them into expression-dynamics clusters and interpret each cluster via GO enrichment. Differential testing has not yet been run or no genes pass FDR.overall < 0.05 — clustering needs a validated significant gene set first The data lack a pseudotime trajectory (no TSCAN/Seurat harmonization was performed), so genes have no fitted expression dynamics along a trajectory to cluster http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters significant differentially-expressed (TDE/XDE) genes along pseudotime with Lamian's clusterGene and computes per-cluster GO enrichment, using FDR.overall < 0.05 to call genes and reveal coordinated biological programs (e.g. TBX21/ZEB2 and interferon programs in the COVID-19 CD8 T cell severity analysis). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Clusters significant differentially-expressed (TDE/XDE) genes along pseudotime with Lamian's clusterGene and computes per-cluster GO enrichment, using FDR.overall < 0.05 to call genes and reveal coordinated biological programs (e.g. TBX21/ZEB2 and interferon programs in the COVID-19 CD8 T cell severity analysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Differential testing has not yet been run or no genes pass FDR.overall < 0.05 — clustering needs a validated significant gene set first The data lack a pseudotime trajectory (no TSCAN/Seurat harmonization was performed), so genes have no fitted expression dynamics along a trajectory to cluster

skills.description: Use when building a subtype reference for PAM50-style classification from multiple subtype-labeled RNA-seq cohorts and the goal is a cohort-composition-independent centroid table (e.g. matching Supplementary Material Table S3).
skills.name: gene-expression-cohort-aggregation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-cohort-aggregation Use when building a subtype reference for PAM50-style classification from multiple subtype-labeled RNA-seq cohorts and the goal is a cohort-composition-independent centroid table (e.g. matching Supplementary Material Table S3). The task is single-sample classification without reference construction — use the authors' mLR single-sample caller instead, which reaches 90% concordance with PAM50 without needing a reference sample The input data lacks subtype labels for the training cohorts — the within-class averages require existing PAM50 (or preliminary) subtype assignments per sample The goal is to re-derive the standard cohort-internal PAM50 reference for the dataset under study rather than a fixed external reference http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs an AWCA (average of within-class averages) reference table for PAM50 breast cancer subtyping by aggregating per-gene, per-subtype mean expression across training cohorts, removing the dependence of subtype calls on the arbitrary composition of the reference cohort. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Constructs an AWCA (average of within-class averages) reference table for PAM50 breast cancer subtyping by aggregating per-gene, per-subtype mean expression across training cohorts, removing the dependence of subtype calls on the arbitrary composition of the reference cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is single-sample classification without reference construction — use the authors' mLR single-sample caller instead, which reaches 90% concordance with PAM50 without needing a reference sample The input data lacks subtype labels for the training cohorts — the within-class averages require existing PAM50 (or preliminary) subtype assignments per sample The goal is to re-derive the standard cohort-internal PAM50 reference for the dataset under study rather than a fixed external reference

skills.description: Use when a pooled t-SNE embedding of scRNAseq clusters needs annotation with expression contours of marker genes (e.g. Cd4, Cd8a) to identify compartment or lineage identity of clusters.
skills.name: gene-expression-contour-overlay-on-tsne
skills.search_text: gene-expression-contour-overlay-on-tsne Use when a pooled t-SNE embedding of scRNAseq clusters needs annotation with expression contours of marker genes (e.g. Cd4, Cd8a) to identify compartment or lineage identity of clusters. Datasets have not been individually preclustered — the pooled t-SNE relies on read.preclustered.datasets; run the per-dataset pipeline (read.data, get.variable.genes, PCA, cluster.analysis) first. You need quantitative differential-expression statistics per cluster rather than spatial visualization — use get.robust.markers / summarize differential expression instead. The goal is trajectory (pseudotime) ordering of TIL subpopulations — use Monocle v2.9.0 DDRTree instead of a static t-SNE contour overlay. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A visualization skill that overlays normalized gene-expression contours onto a pooled 2D t-SNE embedding using robustSingleCell's plot_contour_overlay_tSNE, producing flow-cytometry-like contour figures (e.g. CD4.contour.tSNE.png, CD8.contour.tSNE.png) that annotate cell states by marker expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: A visualization skill that overlays normalized gene-expression contours onto a pooled 2D t-SNE embedding using robustSingleCell's plot_contour_overlay_tSNE, producing flow-cytometry-like contour figures (e.g. CD4.contour.tSNE.png, CD8.contour.tSNE.png) that annotate cell states by marker expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have not been individually preclustered — the pooled t-SNE relies on read.preclustered.datasets; run the per-dataset pipeline (read.data, get.variable.genes, PCA, cluster.analysis) first. You need quantitative differential-expression statistics per cluster rather than spatial visualization — use get.robust.markers / summarize differential expression instead. The goal is trajectory (pseudotime) ordering of TIL subpopulations — use Monocle v2.9.0 DDRTree instead of a static t-SNE contour overlay.

skills.description: Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix (imported from H5AD into Cellenium's PostgreSQL backend) is loaded for one study and you need to find all genes whose expression is highly correlated to a query gene, transcriptome-wide, within that study.
skills.name: gene-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-expression-correlation-analysis Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix (imported from H5AD into Cellenium's PostgreSQL backend) is loaded for one study and you need to find all genes whose expression is highly correlated to a query gene, transcriptome-wide, within that study. The goal is cross-study (multi-study) correlation rather than correlation within a single study — Cellenium supports analysis within and across studies, but this skill covers the within-study co-expression view The goal is finding differentially expressed genes based on clusters of annotated cells — that is a separate Cellenium feature, not co-expression correlation The input is not a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or an already-computed feature/summary table); Cellenium imports scRNA expression data and cell annotations in H5AD format http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Within a single single-cell study loaded in Cellenium, compute a transcriptome-wide correlation of every gene's expression vector against a user-selected query gene across all cells, rank genes by correlation coefficient, and expose the pairwise values that drive the gene-pair coexpression (scatter) plot view. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Within a single single-cell study loaded in Cellenium, compute a transcriptome-wide correlation of every gene's expression vector against a user-selected query gene across all cells, rank genes by correlation coefficient, and expose the pairwise values that drive the gene-pair coexpression (scatter) plot view.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cross-study (multi-study) correlation rather than correlation within a single study — Cellenium supports analysis within and across studies, but this skill covers the within-study co-expression view The goal is finding differentially expressed genes based on clusters of annotated cells — that is a separate Cellenium feature, not co-expression correlation The input is not a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or an already-computed feature/summary table); Cellenium imports scRNA expression data and cell annotations in H5AD format

skills.description: Use when a bulk expression matrix (e.g. TCGA AML) and a subclone-associated gene list from scRNA-seq (e.g. GATA2R361C subclone) must be linked to test whether a marker gene like VIM defines a co-expressed regulon.
skills.name: gene-expression-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-expression-correlation-analysis Use when a bulk expression matrix (e.g. TCGA AML) and a subclone-associated gene list from scRNA-seq (e.g. GATA2R361C subclone) must be linked to test whether a marker gene like VIM defines a co-expressed regulon. The correlation anchor gene has near-zero variance across samples, making Pearson coefficients unstable The comparison gene list comes from bulk rather than single-cell subclone assignment — no specific subclone association to test No genome-wide background gene universe is available for the hypergeometric test http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes gene–gene Pearson correlations across bulk expression samples (here, TCGA AML), applies Benjamini-Hochberg correction to retain a high-confidence correlated gene set, and tests its overlap with a single-cell-derived subclone gene list by hypergeometric testing to infer a regulon. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Computes gene–gene Pearson correlations across bulk expression samples (here, TCGA AML), applies Benjamini-Hochberg correction to retain a high-confidence correlated gene set, and tests its overlap with a single-cell-derived subclone gene list by hypergeometric testing to infer a regulon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The correlation anchor gene has near-zero variance across samples, making Pearson coefficients unstable The comparison gene list comes from bulk rather than single-cell subclone assignment — no specific subclone association to test No genome-wide background gene universe is available for the hypergeometric test

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been through the required preprocessing chain (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50-PC reduction) — raw count matrices will yield incomparable correlation rankings across domains The two domains were not aligned by a cross-modality mapping (e.g., scMMGAN), since the spurious-vs-discovered comparison assumes a paired original/mapped pair of domains The goal is differential expression between conditions rather than correlation-landscape comparison against a mapped domain

skills.search_text: gene-expression-correlation-evaluation Use when two gene-matching approaches (e.g. protein-embedding distance and BLAST hits) disagree for a set of ortholog candidates and raw count scRNA-seq data is available to score candidates by expression correlation. ProtBERT and BLAST top-1 matches already agree (13,050/13,935 = 94% of one-to-one human-mouse BLAST matches), so correlation arbitration adds nothing No raw count scRNA-seq expression data is available for the query and candidate genes The goal is cell type matching itself rather than evaluating gene match assignments — use the TACTiCS model directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Resolves disagreements between gene-matching methods (ProtBERT embedding distance vs BLAST alignment) by computing expression correlation of each candidate match against the query gene from scRNA-seq raw count data. In the TACTiCS human–mouse motor cortex analysis, this arbitrates which ortholog assignment better reflects functional gene similarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
