In the TACTiCS human–mouse motor cortex analysis, this arbitrates which ortholog assignment better reflects functional gene similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ProtBERT and BLAST top-1 matches already agree (13,050/13,935 = 94% of one-to-one human-mouse BLAST matches), so correlation arbitration adds nothing No raw count scRNA-seq expression data is available for the query and candidate genes The goal is cell type matching itself rather than evaluating gene match assignments — use the TACTiCS model directly instead

skills.description: Use when preparing cross-platform transcriptome data (e.g., GEO series such as GSE151189 or GSE59098) for ingestion by Ciclops, whose --train_path/--valid_path inputs must be .csv files with sample names as the first column and labels as the last column.
skills.name: gene-expression-csv-formatting
skills.search_text: gene-expression-csv-formatting Use when preparing cross-platform transcriptome data (e.g., GEO series such as GSE151189 or GSE59098) for ingestion by Ciclops, whose --train_path/--valid_path inputs must be .csv files with sample names as the first column and labels as the last column. The dataset is already a preprocessed feature table with the required Ciclops column layout (first column sample names, last column labels) — reformatting risks corrupting columns. The downstream analysis does not use Ciclops or a tool requiring this specific sample-first/label-last .csv convention. Training and validation datasets share no common genes — the formatting step alone will not fix this; Ciclops will fail silently, producing csv splits with only sample names and labels and no gene expression columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Formats GEO transcriptomic datasets (e.g., GSE151189 and GSE59098) into the .csv layout Ciclops requires: sample names in the first column, gene expression values in between, and class labels in the last column. Correct formatting is a prerequisite for the subsequent Ciclops training and transfer-learning pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101583
skills.summary: Formats GEO transcriptomic datasets (e.g., GSE151189 and GSE59098) into the .csv layout Ciclops requires: sample names in the first column, gene expression values in between, and class labels in the last column. Correct formatting is a prerequisite for the subsequent Ciclops training and transfer-learning pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already a preprocessed feature table with the required Ciclops column layout (first column sample names, last column labels) — reformatting risks corrupting columns. The downstream analysis does not use Ciclops or a tool requiring this specific sample-first/label-last .csv convention. Training and validation datasets share no common genes — the formatting step alone will not fix this; Ciclops will fail silently, producing csv splits with only sample names and labels and no gene expression columns.

skills.description: Use when a raw expression matrix from NGS/microarray experiments (e.g., TCGA, GTEx-style gene-by-sample data frames) shows PCR artifacts, heteroskedasticity in high-signal features, or non-normal/multimodal feature distributions before correlation analysis.
skills.name: gene-expression-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: gene-expression-data-preprocessing Use when a raw expression matrix from NGS/microarray experiments (e.g., TCGA, GTEx-style gene-by-sample data frames) shows PCR artifacts, heteroskedasticity in high-signal features, or non-normal/multimodal feature distributions before correlation analysis. The data are already log2-transformed or normalized (e.g., the packaged logTCGA40 used directly in pair_scatter/pairwise_corr) — re-transforming would distort downstream correlations Single-cell data with non-viable cells and low-abundance genes that require read count filtration rather than a simple medianthres filter before transformation The goal is correlation or network analysis itself (primefeature_corr, pair_scatter, pairwise_corr) rather than the preprocessing/normalization step that precedes it http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Preprocessing and normalization of sequencing- or microarray-derived gene expression matrices using FeatureCorr's data_transform function, offering log2 and z-score transformations with median-expression filtering and original-vs-transformed distribution visualizations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: Preprocessing and normalization of sequencing- or microarray-derived gene expression matrices using FeatureCorr's data_transform function, offering log2 and z-score transformations with median-expression filtering and original-vs-transformed distribution visualizations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already log2-transformed or normalized (e.g., the packaged logTCGA40 used directly in pair_scatter/pairwise_corr) — re-transforming would distort downstream correlations Single-cell data with non-viable cells and low-abundance genes that require read count filtration rather than a simple medianthres filter before transformation The goal is correlation or network analysis itself (primefeature_corr, pair_scatter, pairwise_corr) rather than the preprocessing/normalization step that precedes it

skills.description: Use when raw TCGA-style FPKM gene expression matrices must be reduced to actively expressed genes before co-expression network construction, to remove background/noisy genes.
skills.name: gene-expression-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: gene-expression-data-preprocessing Use when raw TCGA-style FPKM gene expression matrices must be reduced to actively expressed genes before co-expression network construction, to remove background/noisy genes. The expression data are already filtered to a curated active-gene or biomarker signature list The analysis requires differential expression (DE) analysis with DESeq2 rather than expression-level filtering for network construction Input data are miRNA expression rather than protein-coding/long non-coding RNA gene expression (a separate 81% miRNA pre-extraction is reported) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocessing step of the GeneNetFusion pipeline that filters TCGA RNA-Seq gene expression matrices to actively expressed genes by computing zFPKM (Hart et al.) and retaining genes whose mean zFPKM is higher than −3.0 in both normal and cancer conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Preprocessing step of the GeneNetFusion pipeline that filters TCGA RNA-Seq gene expression matrices to actively expressed genes by computing zFPKM (Hart et al.) and retaining genes whose mean zFPKM is higher than −3.0 in both normal and cancer conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are already filtered to a curated active-gene or biomarker signature list The analysis requires differential expression (DE) analysis with DESeq2 rather than expression-level filtering for network construction Input data are miRNA expression rather than protein-coding/long non-coding RNA gene expression (a separate 81% miRNA pre-extraction is reported)

skills.description: Use when input is a continuous gene-expression microarray or RNA-seq matrix to be clustered for trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters, and many genes are inactive under some conditions, so raw-value biclustering would be distorted.
skills.name: gene-expression-data-separation-and-granulation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-data-separation-and-granulation Use when input is a continuous gene-expression microarray or RNA-seq matrix to be clustered for trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters, and many genes are inactive under some conditions, so raw-value biclustering would be distorted. Input is already discrete/integer data — use BCUnibicD (parallel UniBic for discrete data) instead of re-granulating The analysis requires preserving expression magnitudes or fold-changes; separation zeroes out all entries within ail±d, discarding value information Dataset has no meaningful up-/down-regulation structure relative to the row middle element, forcing the fallback q = 0.5 setting that bypasses separation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 UniBic's two-stage preprocessing that converts a noisy continuous gene-expression matrix A into an integer index-ready matrix A'' — first zeroing out non-differentially expressed entries (data separation with q = 15/m), then mapping remaining up-/down-regulated entries into r = 15 integer intervals (data granulation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: UniBic's two-stage preprocessing that converts a noisy continuous gene-expression matrix A into an integer index-ready matrix A'' — first zeroing out non-differentially expressed entries (data separation with q = 15/m), then mapping remaining up-/down-regulated entries into r = 15 integer intervals (data granulation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already discrete/integer data — use BCUnibicD (parallel UniBic for discrete data) instead of re-granulating The analysis requires preserving expression magnitudes or fold-changes; separation zeroes out all entries within ail±d, discarding value information Dataset has no meaningful up-/down-regulation structure relative to the row middle element, forcing the fallback q = 0.5 setting that bypasses separation

skills.description: Use when a raw gene-expression matrix (e.g., tab-separated GSE-style text or CSV loaded as a Pandas DataFrame) needs an internal reference gene identified and single-gene normalization to reduce between-group sample variation.
skills.name: gene-expression-dataframe-normalization
skills.search_text: gene-expression-dataframe-normalization Use when a raw gene-expression matrix (e.g., tab-separated GSE-style text or CSV loaded as a Pandas DataFrame) needs an internal reference gene identified and single-gene normalization to reduce between-group sample variation. The input is not a gene-expression DataFrame (FindERG requires its data parameter in DataFrame format), e.g., raw count matrices in other formats not yet loaded as a Pandas DataFrame You need MIQE-compliant normalization: the paper states it is not acceptable to normalize by a single internal reference gene unless invariable expression is clearly demonstrated The dataset is extremely large and a very large computational depth is required — efficiency declines at depth 3 or larger and no result may occur at too large a depth http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 Screen candidate endogenous reference genes from a gene-expression Pandas DataFrame using ERgene's FindERG, then standardize the data with ERgene's normalizationdata using the identified reference gene (e.g., Atp1a3 on the SHED vs salt mouse brain example). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-75586-5
skills.summary: Screen candidate endogenous reference genes from a gene-expression Pandas DataFrame using ERgene's FindERG, then standardize the data with ERgene's normalizationdata using the identified reference gene (e.g., Atp1a3 on the SHED vs salt mouse brain example).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a gene-expression DataFrame (FindERG requires its data parameter in DataFrame format), e.g., raw count matrices in other formats not yet loaded as a Pandas DataFrame You need MIQE-compliant normalization: the paper states it is not acceptable to normalize by a single internal reference gene unless invariable expression is clearly demonstrated The dataset is extremely large and a very large computational depth is required — efficiency declines at depth 3 or larger and no result may occur at too large a depth

skills.description: Use when re-implementing or extending the scGAE decoder stack: you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix plus a KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix and need a single autoencoder that reconstructs both X and A from a shared latent embedding.
skills.name: gene-expression-decoder-implementation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-decoder-implementation Use when re-implementing or extending the scGAE decoder stack: you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix plus a KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix and need a single autoencoder that reconstructs both X and A from a shared latent embedding. You only need a 2D plot: the article notes the graph autoencoder cannot directly embed into two-dimensional space, so a t-SNE step on an intermediate embedding is required rather than this decoder stack. The data is raw/unprocessed counts: scGAE takes preprocessed data as input, so run scTransform (Seurat) preprocessing first. You need only feature-based embedding with no topology preservation — a plain autoencoder or DCA/scVI would avoid the graph construction and edge-decoder overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements the scGAE multitask graph autoencoder's decoding side: a fully connected feature decoder that reconstructs the scRNA-seq count matrix and a graph (edge) decoder that reconstructs the cell–cell adjacency matrix from the latent embedding, jointly trained so one model preserves both feature and topological information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Implements the scGAE multitask graph autoencoder's decoding side: a fully connected feature decoder that reconstructs the scRNA-seq count matrix and a graph (edge) decoder that reconstructs the cell–cell adjacency matrix from the latent embedding, jointly trained so one model preserves both feature and topological information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a 2D plot: the article notes the graph autoencoder cannot directly embed into two-dimensional space, so a t-SNE step on an intermediate embedding is required rather than this decoder stack. The data is raw/unprocessed counts: scGAE takes preprocessed data as input, so run scTransform (Seurat) preprocessing first. You need only feature-based embedding with no topology preservation — a plain autoencoder or DCA/scVI would avoid the graph construction and edge-decoder overhead.

skills.description: Use when connecting an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. zebrafish GSE66688/GSE112294 or Drosophila dge_normalized.txt) to spatial gene measurements and you must supply cost_matrix, sc_dmat, and is_dmat to SpaOTsc.
skills.name: gene-expression-dissimilarity-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: gene-expression-dissimilarity-matrix-computation Use when connecting an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. zebrafish GSE66688/GSE112294 or Drosophila dge_normalized.txt) to spatial gene measurements and you must supply cost_matrix, sc_dmat, and is_dmat to SpaOTsc. The dataset is excessively large, since iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs becomes computationally intractable (approximation via a small number of landmark positions is the fallback) There are no spatial measurements of even a small number of genes to align with the scRNA-seq data, so no meaningful M can be formed The task only needs clustering or downstream spatial-transcriptomic analysis of already spatially resolved data (e.g. seqFISH+) without a scRNA-seq-to-space mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the gene-expression dissimilarity matrix M (cells vs. spatial positions), the cell-cell dissimilarity matrix Dsc, and the spatial distance matrix Dspa that serve as the cost and structured-distance inputs for SpaOTsc's unbalanced structured optimal transport plan. Correct construction of these matrices determines the fidelity of the cell-to-position mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Computes the gene-expression dissimilarity matrix M (cells vs. spatial positions), the cell-cell dissimilarity matrix Dsc, and the spatial distance matrix Dspa that serve as the cost and structured-distance inputs for SpaOTsc's unbalanced structured optimal transport plan. Correct construction of these matrices determines the fidelity of the cell-to-position mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is excessively large, since iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs becomes computationally intractable (approximation via a small number of landmark positions is the fallback) There are no spatial measurements of even a small number of genes to align with the scRNA-seq data, so no meaningful M can be formed The task only needs clustering or downstream spatial-transcriptomic analysis of already spatially resolved data (e.g. seqFISH+) without a scRNA-seq-to-space mapping

skills.description: Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) plus TPM values for the same genes and want to test whether expression level alone predicts required sequencing depth or full-transcript coverage.
skills.name: gene-expression-distribution-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-expression-distribution-overlap-analysis Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) plus TPM values for the same genes and want to test whether expression level alone predicts required sequencing depth or full-transcript coverage. The dataset was generated with long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq, or any workflow other than bulk short-read poly-A enrichment, since MRSD scores were derived from GTEx Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A data and are most accurate only for similar workflows. The goal is to detect allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression, which the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to predict. The gene of interest carries an MRSD score of '-', meaning median splice-junction coverage was 0 reads, so no usable MRSD value exists to correlate or stratify. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether relative gene expression (GTEx TPM) is an adequate proxy for RNA-seq suitability (MRSD scores) across biosamples by computing per-tissue Pearson/Spearman correlations and quantifying TPM distribution overlap between low-MRSD (<100 M reads) and high-MRSD (>=100 M reads) gene groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Tests whether relative gene expression (GTEx TPM) is an adequate proxy for RNA-seq suitability (MRSD scores) across biosamples by computing per-tissue Pearson/Spearman correlations and quantifying TPM distribution overlap between low-MRSD (<100 M reads) and high-MRSD (>=100 M reads) gene groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset was generated with long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq, or any workflow other than bulk short-read poly-A enrichment, since MRSD scores were derived from GTEx Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A data and are most accurate only for similar workflows. The goal is to detect allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression, which the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to predict. The gene of interest carries an MRSD score of '-', meaning median splice-junction coverage was 0 reads, so no usable MRSD value exists to correlate or stratify.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to predict evolutionary targets of gene deletion events ('Redundant' vs 'Unique' classes) from two-species expression data, or to benchmark classifier power across four added-noise SD levels (0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1).
skills.name: gene-expression-feature-classification
skills.search_text: gene-expression-feature-classification Use when the goal is to predict evolutionary targets of gene deletion events ('Redundant' vs 'Unique' classes) from two-species expression data, or to benchmark classifier power across four added-noise SD levels (0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1). The task is predicting continuous evolutionary parameters (theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) rather than discrete 'Redundant'/'Unique' classes — use CLOUDePredictNN/CLOUDePredictXGB/CLOUDePredictRF/CLOUDePredictSVM instead. Expression data are not for deletion events in two species (no derived/survived/lost gene triplet structure), so the 3m-column input format and OU-based class labels do not apply. SVM/RF training workflow is needed as a separate offline step — the README states RF and SVM are trained on-the-fly, so only NN and XGB require prior CV-based training. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies deleted genes as 'Redundant' or 'Unique' from expression features (3m absolute log10(x+1) expression values for derived, survived, and lost genes) using the CLOUDe machine learning suite, including stress-testing classifier power under added Gaussian noise that proxies shallower sequencing depth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Classifies deleted genes as 'Redundant' or 'Unique' from expression features (3m absolute log10(x+1) expression values for derived, survived, and lost genes) using the CLOUDe machine learning suite, including stress-testing classifier power under added Gaussian noise that proxies shallower sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is predicting continuous evolutionary parameters (theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) rather than discrete 'Redundant'/'Unique' classes — use CLOUDePredictNN/CLOUDePredictXGB/CLOUDePredictRF/CLOUDePredictSVM instead. Expression data are not for deletion events in two species (no derived/survived/lost gene triplet structure), so the 3m-column input format and OU-based class labels do not apply. SVM/RF training workflow is needed as a separate offline step — the README states RF and SVM are trained on-the-fly, so only NN and XGB require prior CV-based training.

skills.description: Use when you need to rank/ prioritize genes from a labeled high-dimensional gene-expression matrix (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq) as biomarker candidates, instead of traditional DEG analysis.
skills.name: gene-expression-feature-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-expression-feature-ranking Use when you need to rank/ prioritize genes from a labeled high-dimensional gene-expression matrix (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq) as biomarker candidates, instead of traditional DEG analysis. Input is already a small curated feature/gene panel rather than high-dimensional NGS expression data needing feature selection. The goal is differential expression testing with adjusted p-values rather than classification-power ranking — use a DEG tool like edgeR instead (the paper benchmarks edgeR-14 as the comparison). There are no class labels or group contrast, since the DI score is defined by distinguishing given groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Wx is a neural network (softmax regression)-based feature selection algorithm that ranks genes from high-dimensional NGS transcriptomic data by a discriminative index (DI) score representing classification power for distinguishing groups such as cancer vs. normal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: Wx is a neural network (softmax regression)-based feature selection algorithm that ranks genes from high-dimensional NGS transcriptomic data by a discriminative index (DI) score representing classification power for distinguishing groups such as cancer vs. normal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small curated feature/gene panel rather than high-dimensional NGS expression data needing feature selection. The goal is differential expression testing with adjusted p-values rather than classification-power ranking — use a DEG tool like edgeR instead (the paper benchmarks edgeR-14 as the comparison). There are no class labels or group contrast, since the DI score is defined by distinguishing given groups.

skills.description: Use when the scRNA-seq dataset is too large (e.g. >1 million cells) or resource-limited to train a feature-selection model on all genes at once, and you need an importance-ranked feature set before final classifier training.
skills.name: gene-expression-feature-subsetting
skills.search_text: gene-expression-feature-subsetting Use when the scRNA-seq dataset is too large (e.g. >1 million cells) or resource-limited to train a feature-selection model on all genes at once, and you need an importance-ranked feature set before final classifier training. The input is already a small feature table or a pre-ranked feature-importance file, so subset-wise training adds no value. A SHAP-based feature score is required instead of linear weight magnitudes (scaLR offers shap_scorer for multi-layer models) or the goal is class-wise rather than overall top-K selection (use ClasswiseAbs/ClasswisePromoters instead of AbsMean). The dataset is small enough that a full DNN can be trained on all features without subsetting — the partitioning rationale (low-resource execution) does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A low-resource feature-extraction procedure from scaLR that partitions a single-cell gene expression matrix (.h5ad/anndata) into feature subsets, trains a single-layer DNN on each subset, and aggregates the resulting weight matrices to rank all features for top-K selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: A low-resource feature-extraction procedure from scaLR that partitions a single-cell gene expression matrix (.h5ad/anndata) into feature subsets, trains a single-layer DNN on each subset, and aggregates the resulting weight matrices to rank all features for top-K selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small feature table or a pre-ranked feature-importance file, so subset-wise training adds no value. A SHAP-based feature score is required instead of linear weight magnitudes (scaLR offers shap_scorer for multi-layer models) or the goal is class-wise rather than overall top-K selection (use ClasswiseAbs/ClasswisePromoters instead of AbsMean). The dataset is small enough that a full DNN can be trained on all features without subsetting — the partitioning rationale (low-resource execution) does not apply.

skills.description: Use when training mLR subtype classifiers on whole-transcriptome RNA-seq matrices where a reduced, informative gene space is needed and filter scores or limma DE statistics can define the feature set.
skills.name: gene-expression-filter-based-feature-selection
skills.search_text: gene-expression-filter-based-feature-selection Use when training mLR subtype classifiers on whole-transcriptome RNA-seq matrices where a reduced, informative gene space is needed and filter scores or limma DE statistics can define the feature set. The feature space is already reduced (e.g. the PAM50 gene panel or a predefined signature like limma50_BWE) and no further gene selection is required Labels are not intrinsic subtypes or the data are microarray profiles (e.g. Affymetrix GSE4922/GSE1456), where limma-derived signatures brought less convincing testing performance http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Ranks genes in a TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq expression matrix using univariate filter scores (Fisher, Mutual Information, Chi-squared, Spearman) and limma moderated statistics, then defines top-N gene feature spaces (limmaN, N=10..1000) to improve regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) intrinsic subtyping accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Ranks genes in a TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq expression matrix using univariate filter scores (Fisher, Mutual Information, Chi-squared, Spearman) and limma moderated statistics, then defines top-N gene feature spaces (limmaN, N=10..1000) to improve regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) intrinsic subtyping accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature space is already reduced (e.g. the PAM50 gene panel or a predefined signature like limma50_BWE) and no further gene selection is required Labels are not intrinsic subtypes or the data are microarray profiles (e.g. Affymetrix GSE4922/GSE1456), where limma-derived signatures brought less convincing testing performance

skills.description: Use when raw gene-by-cell UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin 10x Chromium data) must be filtered of lowly-expressed genes and reduced to a top-1000-HVG feature space before clustering or benchmarking.
skills.name: gene-expression-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-expression-filtering Use when raw gene-by-cell UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin 10x Chromium data) must be filtered of lowly-expressed genes and reduced to a top-1000-HVG feature space before clustering or benchmarking. Input matrix has been feature-selected or dimensionality-reduced — the q-diffused framework relies on full transcriptome dimensionality without aggressive feature selection Goal is clustering/cell-type annotation rather than decomposing expression into continuous linear programs — Leiden community detection on the kernel graph is the appropriate alternative Cells lack a meaningful neighborhood structure or the affinity matrix is degenerate, since the kernel regularization constraining GEP weights would be unfounded http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates gene expression programs (GEPs) by kernel-regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (qNMF) constrained by a q-diffused cell graph, representing cells in a small nonnegative basis of interpretable GEPs while lowering the risk of underdetermination relative to plain NMF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w

skills.search_text: gene-expression-tpm-filtering-of-neoantigens Use when TSNAD v2.0 has produced DeepHLApan-scored candidate neoantigens from WES/WGS and matched tumor RNA-Seq is available, so that neoantigens from genes with TPM < 1 must be removed before ranking high-confidence candidates. skills.search_text: gene-homology-mapping Use when preparing single-cell RNA-seq count matrices from two or more species for integration and you must decide which homologous gene sets (O2O vs in-paralog-including HE/SH) define the shared feature space. Genes have no annotated homology and the downstream algorithm cannot exploit unshared features (only LIGER UINMF takes unshared features) The analysis targets within-species batch integration rather than cross-species integration, where orthology-based gene translation is unnecessary Cell type homology rather than gene homology is the mapping target — the article notes flat gene/cell-type mappings do not comprehensively describe cross-species correspondence and needs specialised metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the cross-species gene feature space for scRNA-seq integration by grouping genes into one-to-one orthologs (O2O), one-to-many (HE, in-paralogs) and many-to-many (SH, co-orthologs) homology sets, then subsetting and concatenating raw counts across species. This is the pivotal BENGAL preprocessing step that determines which genes integration algorithms can align across species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Constructs the cross-species gene feature space for scRNA-seq integration by grouping genes into one-to-one orthologs (O2O), one-to-many (HE, in-paralogs) and many-to-many (SH, co-orthologs) homology sets, then subsetting and concatenating raw counts across species. This is the pivotal BENGAL preprocessing step that determines which genes integration algorithms can align across species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes have no annotated homology and the downstream algorithm cannot exploit unshared features (only LIGER UINMF takes unshared features) The analysis targets within-species batch integration rather than cross-species integration, where orthology-based gene translation is unnecessary Cell type homology rather than gene homology is the mapping target — the article notes flat gene/cell-type mappings do not comprehensively describe cross-species correspondence and needs specialised metrics

skills.description: Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive its PPIN adjacency edge list for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2.
skills.name: gene-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-identifier-mapping Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive its PPIN adjacency edge list for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2. The biological process of interest already has a pre-built *_edges dataset bundled with ORIGINS2 (18 BP are included, e.g. differentiation_edges, cell_cycle_edges) — use those directly instead of rebuilding. You need PPIN activity scores rather than a network — call activity(expression_matrix, adjacency_edges, normalization) instead of build_ppin. The gene list is not in the same identifier space as the full_human_ppin adjacency list — mapping/identifier harmonization must be done first, otherwise no or incorrect edges will be retained. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Constructs a custom protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) by overlaying a user-supplied gene ID list onto the full human PPIN and subsetting the edges whose endpoints both belong to the list, as implemented in the ORIGINS2 build_ppin function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Constructs a custom protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) by overlaying a user-supplied gene ID list onto the full human PPIN and subsetting the edges whose endpoints both belong to the list, as implemented in the ORIGINS2 build_ppin function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process of interest already has a pre-built *_edges dataset bundled with ORIGINS2 (18 BP are included, e.g. differentiation_edges, cell_cycle_edges) — use those directly instead of rebuilding. You need PPIN activity scores rather than a network — call activity(expression_matrix, adjacency_edges, normalization) instead of build_ppin. The gene list is not in the same identifier space as the full_human_ppin adjacency list — mapping/identifier harmonization must be done first, otherwise no or incorrect edges will be retained.

skills.description: Use when an RNA-seq counts matrix carries Ensembl gene IDs but downstream GSVA, .gmt gene-set matching, TPM integration, or differential analysis in ARMT requires gene-symbol identifiers.

skills.search_text: gene-identifier-mapping Use when an RNA-seq counts matrix carries Ensembl gene IDs but downstream GSVA, .gmt gene-set matching, TPM integration, or differential analysis in ARMT requires gene-symbol identifiers. The expression matrix already uses gene symbol row names and only needs TPM normalization or GSVA scoring without identifier conversion The input is mutation annotation (.maf) or clinical data, which ARMT consumes directly without gene identifier mapping You need de novo identifier mapping outside ARMT's shiny GUI workflow (e.g. for miRNA or non-Homo sapiens annotations, which the paper's org.Hs.eg.db-based setup does not cover) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps gene identifiers between Ensembl IDs and HGNC gene symbols within the ARMT RNA-seq pipeline, so that raw counts matrices (Ensembl ID rownames) can be normalized to TPM/log2(TPM+1) and matched against gene-set (.gmt) inputs that use gene symbols. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009

skills.description: Use when a trained Cancer-Finder checkpoint exists (e.g., ST model with 5000-gene input) and the goal is to explain malignant-vs-normal spot classification by extracting a ranked, per-gene importance list from spatial transcriptomics slides.
skills.name: gene-importance-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-importance-ranking Use when a trained Cancer-Finder checkpoint exists (e.g., ST model with 5000-gene input) and the goal is to explain malignant-vs-normal spot classification by extracting a ranked, per-gene importance list from spatial transcriptomics slides. No trained Cancer-Finder model or checkpoint is available — the saliency module is gradient-based attribution through the trained feature-extraction and classification layers, not a standalone gene-ranking method. Hematologic tumor data — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data. Analyses requiring spatially aware feature attribution — the paper notes Cancer-Finder overlooks the spatial relationships among spots in ST data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks genes by importance using Cancer-Finder's gradient-based modified saliency-map interpretability module, producing a top-ten gene signature (e.g., the ccRCC signature NDRG1, TAGLN, MALAT1, IGKC, IGHA1, IGHG4, IGLC2, IGHG3, SOD2, KRT19) from malignant-spot predictions on spatial transcriptomics slides. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Ranks genes by importance using Cancer-Finder's gradient-based modified saliency-map interpretability module, producing a top-ten gene signature (e.g., the ccRCC signature NDRG1, TAGLN, MALAT1, IGKC, IGHA1, IGHG4, IGLC2, IGHG3, SOD2, KRT19) from malignant-spot predictions on spatial transcriptomics slides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trained Cancer-Finder model or checkpoint is available — the saliency module is gradient-based attribution through the trained feature-extraction and classification layers, not a standalone gene-ranking method. Hematologic tumor data — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data. Analyses requiring spatially aware feature attribution — the paper notes Cancer-Finder overlooks the spatial relationships among spots in ST data.

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that a trained SIMS/TabNet classifier's sparse gene-selection masks for a specific cell class (e.g., Pvalb+ interneurons) are consistent across independent runs, or to recover an interpretable marker-gene set.
skills.name: gene-importance-stability-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-importance-stability-analysis Use when you need to verify that a trained SIMS/TabNet classifier's sparse gene-selection masks for a specific cell class (e.g., Pvalb+ interneurons) are consistent across independent runs, or to recover an interpretable marker-gene set. Input is already a curated marker-gene/feature table rather than raw cell-by-gene expression requiring model-derived importance You need cross-species label transfer or gene-importance transfer — SIMS has only been validated within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge between species The expression matrices are in gene x cell orientation; SIMS requires cell x gene since training samples are individual transcriptomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies the reproducibility of SIMS/TabNet sparse feature-selection masks by running the explain procedure many times (e.g., 300 runs) for a target cell class and aggregating per-gene explain values, demonstrating stable, concentrated gene selection for Pvalb+ interneurons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Quantifies the reproducibility of SIMS/TabNet sparse feature-selection masks by running the explain procedure many times (e.g., 300 runs) for a target cell class and aggregating per-gene explain values, demonstrating stable, concentrated gene selection for Pvalb+ interneurons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated marker-gene/feature table rather than raw cell-by-gene expression requiring model-derived importance You need cross-species label transfer or gene-importance transfer — SIMS has only been validated within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge between species The expression matrices are in gene x cell orientation; SIMS requires cell x gene since training samples are individual transcriptomes

skills.description: Use when marker genes must be identified for clusters from pretrained deep learning embeddings (e.g., Miscell) and you need per-gene, per-cluster influence scores rather than t-test/Wilcoxon differential expression.

skills.search_text: gene-influence-quantification-per-cluster Use when marker genes must be identified for clusters from pretrained deep learning embeddings (e.g., Miscell) and you need per-gene, per-cluster influence scores rather than t-test/Wilcoxon differential expression. Marker genes outside the highly variable gene set are of interest — the article states 'cluster-specific marker genes may be missed in HVGs' Small datasets — Miscell 'demands a large sample size to obtain good performance' Input lacks batch correction and you expect the method to handle it — batch correction must be done as preprocessing before Miscell http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies each gene's influence on cell-cluster assignments by attaching a 1-layer linear classifier to a frozen Miscell encoder and applying integrated-gradient attribution, yielding cluster-specific marker genes for single-cell transcriptome data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Quantifies each gene's influence on cell-cluster assignments by attaching a 1-layer linear classifier to a frozen Miscell encoder and applying integrated-gradient attribution, yielding cluster-specific marker genes for single-cell transcriptome data.

skills.description: Use when you have a CEFCON-constructed cell-lineage-specific GRN with learned attention coefficients and need to rank MFVS/MDS driver gene candidates by importance to output driver regulators.
skills.name: gene-influence-score-computation
skills.search_text: gene-influence-score-computation Use when you have a CEFCON-constructed cell-lineage-specific GRN with learned attention coefficients and need to rank MFVS/MDS driver gene candidates by importance to output driver regulators. Input is raw scRNA-seq data without a CEFCON-constructed GRN — run data_preparation and GRN construction first The goal is identifying regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) and their activity rather than ranking driver regulators Multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON handles one cell lineage at a time http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Computes a gene influence score from the attention coefficients learned by CEFCON's graph attention network when constructing the cell-lineage-specific GRN; log-transformed, scaled scores (lambda=0.8) rank candidate driver regulators obtained from MFVS and MDS network-control solutions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Computes a gene influence score from the attention coefficients learned by CEFCON's graph attention network when constructing the cell-lineage-specific GRN; log-transformed, scaled scores (lambda=0.8) rank candidate driver regulators obtained from MFVS and MDS network-control solutions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq data without a CEFCON-constructed GRN — run data_preparation and GRN construction first The goal is identifying regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) and their activity rather than ranking driver regulators Multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON handles one cell lineage at a time

skills.description: Use when building a differential co-expression network from TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices and a prior gene-interaction network is available to restrict which gene-pair correlations are computed and tested.
skills.name: gene-interaction-network-subsetting
skills.search_text: gene-interaction-network-subsetting Use when building a differential co-expression network from TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices and a prior gene-interaction network is available to restrict which gene-pair correlations are computed and tested. The expression matrix gene symbols have not been mapped/intersected with the DawnRank interaction network genes — the subgraph only makes sense on the Gene_Net gene space No prior gene-interaction network is available, so an unrestricted all-pairs co-expression analysis is intended The analysis is a single-condition network without a two-condition differential comparison, where the WMDS.net edge-significance framework does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Restricts the DawnRank-derived Gene_Net hub network (intersection of the DawnRank gene-interaction network with TCGA genes) to its largest connected subgraph, defining the candidate gene-pair space on which WMDS.net differential co-expression and SSN analyses are computed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Restricts the DawnRank-derived Gene_Net hub network (intersection of the DawnRank gene-interaction network with TCGA genes) to its largest connected subgraph, defining the candidate gene-pair space on which WMDS.net differential co-expression and SSN analyses are computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix gene symbols have not been mapped/intersected with the DawnRank interaction network genes — the subgraph only makes sense on the Gene_Net gene space No prior gene-interaction network is available, so an unrestricted all-pairs co-expression analysis is intended The analysis is a single-condition network without a two-condition differential comparison, where the WMDS.net edge-significance framework does not apply

skills.name: gene-interaction-table-export
skills.search_text: gene-interaction-table-export Use when a fitted PhenoPath model exists and you must rank genes by |covariate-pseudotime interaction effect|, label interactions of interest, and write the results as a per-gene CSV table. The pseudotime/latent pathway has not yet been fitted — run PhenoPath first, since interactions() requires a converged phenopath_fit object The goal is differential expression along pseudotime without a covariate — a plain pseudotime DE analysis is the wrong tool for covariate-pseudotime interaction effects Features evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime and that nonlinearity is the quantity of interest — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Exports a ranked per-gene table of covariate-pseudotime interaction effect sizes from a fitted PhenoPath model (e.g. the Shalek LPS/PAM dendritic-cell dataset), flagging Bayesian-significant interactions such as Tnf and Mef2c for downstream review or figure reproduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: The pseudotime/latent pathway has not yet been fitted — run PhenoPath first, since interactions() requires a converged phenopath_fit object The goal is differential expression along pseudotime without a covariate — a plain pseudotime DE analysis is the wrong tool for covariate-pseudotime interaction effects Features evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime and that nonlinearity is the quantity of interest — PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime

skills.description: Use when validating that a simulated non-UMI scRNA-seq dataset recapitulates gene length bias, or when contrasting length-biased full-length protocols against UMI-based protocols that lack it.
skills.name: gene-length-bias-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-length-bias-quantification Use when validating that a simulated non-UMI scRNA-seq dataset recapitulates gene length bias, or when contrasting length-biased full-length protocols against UMI-based protocols that lack it. The analysis targets UMI-based data where gene length bias is absent by design (e.g. the Zeisel cortex UMI dataset) Only true transcript counts are of interest and library-preparation/sequencing noise should not be simulated The task requires simulating batch effects rather than length bias — use DivideBatches instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the gene-length dependence of expression seen in non-UMI (full-length) scRNA-seq by running SymSim's True2ObservedCounts with gene length bias (lenslope, nbins) on both non-UMI and UMI protocols, then comparing length-normalized expression against the Gaublomme Th17 reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Reproduces the gene-length dependence of expression seen in non-UMI (full-length) scRNA-seq by running SymSim's True2ObservedCounts with gene length bias (lenslope, nbins) on both non-UMI and UMI protocols, then comparing length-normalized expression against the Gaublomme Th17 reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets UMI-based data where gene length bias is absent by design (e.g. the Zeisel cortex UMI dataset) Only true transcript counts are of interest and library-preparation/sequencing noise should not be simulated The task requires simulating batch effects rather than length bias — use DivideBatches instead

skills.description: Use when raw featureCounts gene-level read counts (TopHat2/hg19 alignments, TCGA or Prensner PCa cohorts) must be corrected for sum-of-exons gene length before FunHoP node aggregation or Voom differential expression.
skills.name: gene-length-read-count-normalization
skills.search_text: gene-length-read-count-normalization Use when raw featureCounts gene-level read counts (TopHat2/hg19 alignments, TCGA or Prensner PCa cohorts) must be corrected for sum-of-exons gene length before FunHoP node aggregation or Voom differential expression. The count matrix is already length-corrected - setting correct=True again in load_countdata applies the sum-of-exons factor twice and distorts node read fractions. Isoform- or transcript-level enzyme activity is the target - KEGG provides no curated isoform activity, so FunHoP limits the analysis to the gene level with a canonical isoform length. The 'expression table' is only a probe-value file used to supply gene names (column 0) - do not length-adjust probe intensities in place of featureCounts read counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scales each gene's raw RNA-seq read counts by its sum-of-exons gene length divided by the average gene length over all genes, so FunHoP can identify the dominant homolog in multi-gene KEGG nodes by true read abundance rather than length bias. The length-adjusted counts feed Voom differential expression and per-node aggregation in the TCGA and Prensner PCa analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Scales each gene's raw RNA-seq read counts by its sum-of-exons gene length divided by the average gene length over all genes, so FunHoP can identify the dominant homolog in multi-gene KEGG nodes by true read abundance rather than length bias. The length-adjusted counts feed Voom differential expression and per-node aggregation in the TCGA and Prensner PCa analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix is already length-corrected - setting correct=True again in load_countdata applies the sum-of-exons factor twice and distorts node read fractions. Isoform- or transcript-level enzyme activity is the target - KEGG provides no curated isoform activity, so FunHoP limits the analysis to the gene level with a canonical isoform length. The 'expression table' is only a probe-value file used to supply gene names (column 0) - do not length-adjust probe intensities in place of featureCounts read counts.

skills.description: Use when a CaSpER run has produced final.objects from runCaSpER and you need gene-level amplification/deletion calls (e.g. to benchmark 69% TPR / 0.3% FPR gene-based deletion detection against a genotyping array gold standard).
skills.name: gene-level-cnv-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: gene-level-cnv-matrix-construction Use when a CaSpER run has produced final.objects from runCaSpER and you need gene-level amplification/deletion calls (e.g. to benchmark 69% TPR / 0.3% FPR gene-based deletion detection against a genotyping array gold standard). You need chromosome-arm-scale events instead — use extractLargeScaleEvents(final.objects, thr=0.75) rather than collapsing to gene resolution. You only have raw expression/BAF signals and have not yet run CreateCasperObject and runCaSpER — the gene matrix requires the harmonized multiscale segment summary as input. The data are 3′-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) where degraded BAF shift signal from variants near 3′ gene ends can bias CNV calls. Constructs the final gene-by-sample CNV matrix in CaSpER by summarizing segment-level HMM+BAF-integrated calls across all N×M expression/BAF scale comparisons, encoding each gene in each sample/cell as 0 (neutral), 1 (amplification), or -1 (deletion). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Constructs the final gene-by-sample CNV matrix in CaSpER by summarizing segment-level HMM+BAF-integrated calls across all N×M expression/BAF scale comparisons, encoding each gene in each sample/cell as 0 (neutral), 1 (amplification), or -1 (deletion).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need chromosome-arm-scale events instead — use extractLargeScaleEvents(final.objects, thr=0.75) rather than collapsing to gene resolution. You only have raw expression/BAF signals and have not yet run CreateCasperObject and runCaSpER — the gene matrix requires the harmonized multiscale segment summary as input. The data are 3′-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) where degraded BAF shift signal from variants near 3′ gene ends can bias CNV calls.

skills.description: Use when a common multi-condition trajectory (slingshot sds) already exists and the goal is to find genes whose expression patterns differ between conditions along its lineages after topology, progression, and fate-selection tests.
skills.name: gene-level-differential-expression-along-lineages
skills.search_text: gene-level-differential-expression-along-lineages Use when a common multi-condition trajectory (slingshot sds) already exists and the goal is to find genes whose expression patterns differ between conditions along its lineages after topology, progression, and fate-selection tests. The topologyTest or trajectory-level tests have not yet been run and differential topology has not been assessed — condiments prescribes ordering DE after the trajectory-level steps The data are not single-cell count data ordered along a trajectory with known condition labels (e.g., already aggregated bulk expression tables) The question is differential abundance of cell populations rather than gene-level expression change along lineages http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Step 3 of the condiments workflow: fit gene-wise negative-binomial GAMs with tradeSeq fitGAM on a slingshot trajectory under multiple conditions and call condition-specific expression changes with conditionTest, selecting genes at FDR 5% (e.g., 1,993 DE genes in the TGF-β EMT case study). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Step 3 of the condiments workflow: fit gene-wise negative-binomial GAMs with tradeSeq fitGAM on a slingshot trajectory under multiple conditions and call condition-specific expression changes with conditionTest, selecting genes at FDR 5% (e.g., 1,993 DE genes in the TGF-β EMT case study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The topologyTest or trajectory-level tests have not yet been run and differential topology has not been assessed — condiments prescribes ordering DE after the trajectory-level steps The data are not single-cell count data ordered along a trajectory with known condition labels (e.g., already aggregated bulk expression tables) The question is differential abundance of cell populations rather than gene-level expression change along lineages

skills.description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a transcriptome-landscape preservation metric — e.g. comparing median gene-level normalized intra dispersion across raw and imputed matrices over multiple datasets.
skills.name: gene-level-dispersion-metric-computation
skills.search_text: gene-level-dispersion-metric-computation Use when benchmarking imputation methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a transcriptome-landscape preservation metric — e.g. comparing median gene-level normalized intra dispersion across raw and imputed matrices over multiple datasets. The analysis goal is clustering-quality comparison (Purity Index / ARI against true labels via k-means) rather than transcriptome-landscape preservation via dispersion. The input matrices have not been pre-filtered (all-zero genes, genes expressed in fewer than two cells, or genes with less than one percent non-zero entries) — filter first, as the dispersion values are otherwise distorted. The data are simulated datasets with different generative parameters than the 25 real scRNA-seq benchmark datasets; the 3.6e-3 reference value applies to the real-dataset benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes gene-level normalized intra dispersion on raw versus imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices to quantify how much of the transcriptome landscape is preserved after imputation. In the scISR benchmark this yields a median gene-level normalized intra dispersion of 3.6e-3 for scISR, compared against raw data and competitor imputation methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Computes gene-level normalized intra dispersion on raw versus imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices to quantify how much of the transcriptome landscape is preserved after imputation. In the scISR benchmark this yields a median gene-level normalized intra dispersion of 3.6e-3 for scISR, compared against raw data and competitor imputation methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is clustering-quality comparison (Purity Index / ARI against true labels via k-means) rather than transcriptome-landscape preservation via dispersion. The input matrices have not been pre-filtered (all-zero genes, genes expressed in fewer than two cells, or genes with less than one percent non-zero entries) — filter first, as the dispersion values are otherwise distorted. The data are simulated datasets with different generative parameters than the 25 real scRNA-seq benchmark datasets; the 3.6e-3 reference value applies to the real-dataset benchmark.

skills.description: Use when a downstream pareg regression call needs a gene-by-pvalue dataframe and you only have raw matched tumor/normal expression data (e.g. GSE62944 TCGA-BRCA) that still requires a differential expression test per gene.
skills.name: gene-level-pvalue-table-preparation
skills.search_text: gene-level-pvalue-table-preparation Use when a downstream pareg regression call needs a gene-by-pvalue dataframe and you only have raw matched tumor/normal expression data (e.g. GSE62944 TCGA-BRCA) that still requires a differential expression test per gene. A gene-level P-value table already exists in pareg's expected format — go directly to the pareg regression call instead of re-running limma. The analysis goal is pathway-level enrichment scoring itself (pareg's regression or enrichmentplot visualization), not producing its gene-level input. The P-values are synthetic (e.g. sampled from Beta/Uniform distributions as in the pareg vignette benchmark) and no real differential expression test is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Produces the gene-level differential expression P-value table that pareg consumes as input, by running a paired limma tumor-vs-normal analysis on TCGA-BRCA (GSE62944) expression data and exporting a two-column gene/pvalue CSV (de_pvalues.csv). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Produces the gene-level differential expression P-value table that pareg consumes as input, by running a paired limma tumor-vs-normal analysis on TCGA-BRCA (GSE62944) expression data and exporting a two-column gene/pvalue CSV (de_pvalues.csv).
skills.when_to_use_negative: A gene-level P-value table already exists in pareg's expected format — go directly to the pareg regression call instead of re-running limma. The analysis goal is pathway-level enrichment scoring itself (pareg's regression or enrichmentplot visualization), not producing its gene-level input. The P-values are synthetic (e.g. sampled from Beta/Uniform distributions as in the pareg vignette benchmark) and no real differential expression test is needed.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw RNA-seq FASTQ files of a patient cohort and per-gene read counts plus DE statistics (P value, regulation direction) are needed as downstream input for node-level pathway aggregation, e.g. FunHoP/KEGG network analysis.
skills.name: gene-level-read-count-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-level-read-count-quantification Use when starting from raw RNA-seq FASTQ files of a patient cohort and per-gene read counts plus DE statistics (P value, regulation direction) are needed as downstream input for node-level pathway aggregation, e.g. FunHoP/KEGG network analysis. Input is already a gene-level count matrix (e.g. TCGA read counts with gene identifiers downloaded directly) — only the voom DE step and gene-length adjustment are needed, not alignment/assignment. The goal is isoform-level or transcript-level quantification — KEGG provides no curated isoform enzyme-activity data, so this skill is deliberately limited to the gene level. Analysis targets KEGG glycan-related pathways (category 1.7, e.g. 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism') — these use 'links' instead of nodes and are excluded from FunHoP. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads into per-gene read counts and per-gene differential expression statistics, following the FunHoP pipeline: TopHat2 splice-aware alignment to hg19, featureCounts assignment (gene length = sum of exons), and voom differential expression between cancer and normal tissue. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003

Query is a scaled gene expression profile (z-score matrix per cluster) — use deCS.correlation, which uses Pearson/Spearman correlation instead of contingency-table overlap The cell type of interest is not represented in any deCS reference panel (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF) or expected to be a novel cell type, since deCS is a mapping-based toolkit Cancer cell annotation, where expression profile differences between healthy reference and malignant cells bias results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Annotate query gene lists (e.g., cluster marker genes) to cell types using deCS.fisher, which tests overlap between the query set and each cell type's top-ranked specific genes (CTgenes, default top 5%) via Fisher's exact test and assigns the cell type with the highest intersection ratio (IR = Q∩R/Q). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001

skills.name: gene-loading-norm-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-loading-norm-ranking Use when you have a CA-embedded scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Zhengmix8eq SingleCellExperiment with corral output) and need to identify which genes carry the highest weight in the first two CA dimensions and interpret their association with cell populations. Input data has already been log(x + 1) transformed for a typical PCA-based workflow — standard CA as implemented in corral decomposes the Pearson chi-squared residual matrix of raw counts and avoids the distortive log-transformation The goal is batch integration across multiple tables — use corralm (multi-table CA) instead of single-table corral for this feature-ranking visualization A different dimension reduction method (PCA, glmPCA, ZINB-WaVE, ZIFA) produced the embeddings, since gene loadings are then not on the CA chi-squared residual geometry http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Ranks genes by the L2 norm of their loadings from a correspondence analysis (CA) solution and renders a CA biplot labeling the top-weighted features, to identify which genes drive cell-population separation in scRNA-seq embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1

Input is not an ICA-derived gene loading matrix — e.g. a cell-by-gene expression matrix that has not been decomposed by fastICA The goal is batch integration across datasets rather than within-dataset component normalization — Harmony or scVI-style joint low-dimensional representations are the alternatives discussed You only need MetaTiME cell-state annotation of new data via the pretrained MeC annotator, which uses published pretrained meta-components rather than re-deriving and re-normalizing loadings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A normalization step from the MetaTiME pipeline that z-score-transforms the gene loading values of each independent component (IC) from fastICA decomposition so that gene representation scores are comparable across the 100 components and across datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8

skills.search_text: gene-locus-isoform-filtering Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblies against a reference annotation and you need per-locus counts of uniquely assigned isoforms, especially for high-isoform-diversity genes like ATP6AP2. The run produced no assignment output at all — record it as a pipeline failure (e.g. RNA-Bloom failing at the k-mer counting step), not as zero uniquely assigned isoforms Assignments are multi-isoform/ambiguous — do not count them toward the unique-isoform total The reference annotation is not the GENCODE version used for the IsoQuant run — restrict matches to isoforms present in that annotation (34 GENCODE v32 ATP6AP2 isoforms) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Parses IsoQuant transcript-to-annotation assignment outputs and filters them to a single gene locus (e.g. ATP6AP2 on chromosome X), counting only unambiguous single-isoform assignments against GENCODE v32 annotations to quantify how many annotated isoforms each assembler recovered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781

skills.search_text: gene-mapping-variance-quantification Use when a trained noise-augmented GAN mapping between transcriptomic and proteomic domains is available and you need to quantify which genes' generated values are stable vs. unstable under stochastic z draws. The GAN was trained without noise augmentation (add_noise disabled), since without the z~N(0,1) input there is no stochastic variation to measure mapping variance The data has not been preprocessed to ensure columns are mostly in the interval [-10, 10] as the README requires for feeding into the neural network Quantifies per-gene uncertainty of scMMGAN cross-modal mapping on DBIT-seq data by repeatedly drawing the isotropic normal noise input z and computing the variance of generated gene values across stochastic mappings, comparing genes with vs. without an analogous proteomic measurement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contains many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes and a single global marker set is needed that distinguishes every phenotype pair, not just markers per individual cell type.
skills.name: gene-marker-selection
skills.search_text: gene-marker-selection Use when scRNA-seq data contains many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes and a single global marker set is needed that distinguishes every phenotype pair, not just markers per individual cell type. When only a small number of distinct groups is present and standard per-group differential expression suffices — PC targets many groups with overlapping DE genes When the goal is an all-relevant feature ranking rather than a minimal globally discriminative cover (e.g., use mRMR, a minimal-optimal alternative) When an optimal (not approximate) solution to the cover is required — G-PC is a polynomial-time approximation and NP-completeness of multiset multicover precludes guaranteed optima http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects a compact, globally discriminative gene marker set for scRNA-seq phenotypes by formulating marker selection as a phenotype cover (PC) problem, equivalent to NP-complete multiset multicover, and approximating it in polynomial time with the extended-greedy G-PC algorithm (or the cross-entropy CEM-PC alternative). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Selects a compact, globally discriminative gene marker set for scRNA-seq phenotypes by formulating marker selection as a phenotype cover (PC) problem, equivalent to NP-complete multiset multicover, and approximating it in polynomial time with the extended-greedy G-PC algorithm (or the cross-entropy CEM-PC alternative).

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix with categorical cell labels (flat or hierarchical) and must design a minimal gene panel that discriminates all labels jointly with high precision.
skills.name: gene-marker-selection
skills.search_text: gene-marker-selection Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix with categorical cell labels (flat or hierarchical) and must design a minimal gene panel that discriminates all labels jointly with high precision. The goal is placing unlabeled cells on trajectories or in spatial assays — scGeneFit only supports categorical labeling, not manifold constraints. Cell type classes are not linearly separable in the reduced space — both scGeneFit and one-vs-all methods assume linear separability, reasonable in high dimensions but possibly violated in low dimensions. A non-linear dimension reduction or feature table unrelated to label discrimination is needed — scGeneFit is built on linear label-aware compressive classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Select a small, non-redundant set of gene markers that jointly optimize recovery of cell type labels from scRNA-seq data, using scGeneFit's label-aware compressive classification rather than per-gene one-vs-all testing. Validated on CBMC CITE-seq data (8.05% vs 9.90% curated vs 30% random classification error) and synthetic 40-class simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Select a small, non-redundant set of gene markers that jointly optimize recovery of cell type labels from scRNA-seq data, using scGeneFit's label-aware compressive classification rather than per-gene one-vs-all testing. Validated on CBMC CITE-seq data (8.05% vs 9.90% curated vs 30% random classification error) and synthetic 40-class simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is placing unlabeled cells on trajectories or in spatial assays — scGeneFit only supports categorical labeling, not manifold constraints. A non-linear dimension reduction or feature table unrelated to label discrimination is needed — scGeneFit is built on linear label-aware compressive classification.

skills.name: gene-membership-table-matching
skills.search_text: gene-membership-table-matching Use when two WGCNA/PyWGCNA networks built from different datasets (e.g., 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD mouse RNA-seq) must be compared module-by-module to find conserved co-expression signatures via significant gene-set overlap. Goal is comparing a PyWGCNA object to an external gene/marker list rather than another co-expression network — PyWGCNA provides a separate 'Compare PyWGCNA objects to gene marker list' workflow Only one dataset's modules exist (single-network module detection or trait correlation), so there is no second network to compare against The two networks were built from non-overlapping gene sets, making membership contingency tables and Jaccard coefficients uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cross-compare co-expression modules from two PyWGCNA networks (here, 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD brain bulk RNA-seq) by building gene-membership contingency tables for every module pair, quantifying Jaccard similarity and overlap counts/proportions, and testing each pair with Fisher's exact test to flag significantly overlapping (conserved) modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Cross-compare co-expression modules from two PyWGCNA networks (here, 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD brain bulk RNA-seq) by building gene-membership contingency tables for every module pair, quantifying Jaccard similarity and overlap counts/proportions, and testing each pair with Fisher's exact test to flag significantly overlapping (conserved) modules.

skills.search_text: gene-module-activity-inference Use when you have a single-cell count matrix (AnnData/scanpy) plus a GMT gene-module file and need per-cell, interpretable activity scores for pathways or marker sets, including out-of-sample inference on unseen cells or studies. skills.search_text: gene-module-annotation-count-audit Use when you have the E.PATH GitHub data files (database and annotations) and need to verify or recompute the reported dataset, gene-module, gene-count, and per-environmental-factor statistics before downstream enrichment work. You need to run enrichment on a gene list of interest (use E.PAGE's process_input_text/process_input_seurat + compute instead of auditing counts) Your goal is annotating new databases or auto-generating GO/KEGG/MeSH annotations via auto_anno, rather than verifying existing counts The environmental factor of interest is outside the four curated categories (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) — the article notes the study is limited to four types of environmental variables http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces the curated E.PATH database's reported scale and composition (237 datasets, 522 gene modules, 25,789 genes across cigarette smoking, diet, infections and toxic chemicals) by importing the GitHub-deposited data files with E.PAGE's import functions and auditing computed counts against the paper's reported figures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Reproduces the curated E.PATH database's reported scale and composition (237 datasets, 522 gene modules, 25,789 genes across cigarette smoking, diet, infections and toxic chemicals) by importing the GitHub-deposited data files with E.PAGE's import functions and auditing computed counts against the paper's reported figures.
