skills.description: Use when the input is a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression networks and detect trait-associated gene modules.
skills.name: gene-module-detection
skills.search_text: gene-module-detection Use when the input is a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression networks and detect trait-associated gene modules. The input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated pseudobulk expression profiles where standard WGCNA applies directly without the single-cell sub-clustering/downsampling step The goal is co-expression on raw unaggregated single-cell counts without the pseudo-bulk pre-processing SCANet expects A causal gene regulatory network is required — GCNs rely on correlation, not causation, and converting GCNs into GRNs may increase the risk of false negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data using a modified version of WGCNA inside SCANet, after reducing single-cell data to pseudo-bulk sub-cluster representatives. This yields trait/cell-type-associated gene modules whose hubs and scale-free topology can be validated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Detect co-expression gene modules from scRNA-seq data using a modified version of WGCNA inside SCANet, after reducing single-cell data to pseudo-bulk sub-cluster representatives. This yields trait/cell-type-associated gene modules whose hubs and scale-free topology can be validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated pseudobulk expression profiles where standard WGCNA applies directly without the single-cell sub-clustering/downsampling step The goal is co-expression on raw unaggregated single-cell counts without the pseudo-bulk pre-processing SCANet expects A causal gene regulatory network is required — GCNs rely on correlation, not causation, and converting GCNs into GRNs may increase the risk of false negatives

skills.description: Use when you have run JOINTLY and need to interpret its learned factors as gene modules — e.g., to annotate cell types, confirm marker genes (DCN for IMR90, CD3B for Jurkat), or discover active biological processes per cluster.
skills.name: gene-module-interpretation-for-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-module-interpretation-for-cell-type-annotation Use when you have run JOINTLY and need to interpret its learned factors as gene modules — e.g., to annotate cell types, confirm marker genes (DCN for IMR90, CD3B for Jurkat), or discover active biological processes per cluster. You only need integration/clustering performance (ARI/NMI) and have no goal of annotating clusters or interpreting factor genes The genes or features driving integration and clustering are already known and validated, so no module interpretation is needed Input is a raw unintegrated clustering result with no JOINTLY factor output — there are no interpretable modules to extract Interprets the gene modules learned by JOINTLY's joint NMF factors to assign biological meaning to clusters and guide cell type annotation, by extracting top genes per factor and scoring them per cell with UCell module scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Interprets the gene modules learned by JOINTLY's joint NMF factors to assign biological meaning to clusters and guide cell type annotation, by extracting top genes per factor and scoring them per cell with UCell module scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need integration/clustering performance (ARI/NMI) and have no goal of annotating clusters or interpreting factor genes The genes or features driving integration and clustering are already known and validated, so no module interpretation is needed Input is a raw unintegrated clustering result with no JOINTLY factor output — there are no interpretable modules to extract

skills.description: Use when applying leave-one-out outlier detection (L1OutExpOut) to gene sets and needing to prevent over-removal of genes, e.g. genes flagged as outliers in many collections or belonging to only a few gene sets.
skills.name: gene-module-membership-outlier-exemption
skills.search_text: gene-module-membership-outlier-exemption Use when applying leave-one-out outlier detection (L1OutExpOut) to gene sets and needing to prevent over-removal of genes, e.g. genes flagged as outliers in many collections or belonging to only a few gene sets. The analysis goal is to remove outlier samples rather than outlier genes — rROMA handles sample filtering separately via detected-gene counts and PCA projection with a distance threshold. The gene set is so small that the maximum removable-outlier proportion cap would invalidate the PC1 computation, or the expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma requires normalized data, e.g. edgeR cpm or DESeq2 vst). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 rROMA's safeguard layer for leave-one-out outlier gene detection: exemptions and caps that prevent legitimate genes from being wrongly excluded when recomputing PC1-explained variance (L1) per gene set. It combines a Fisher test on outlier proportions across gene set collections, a rare-membership exemption, and a per-module cap on removable genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: rROMA's safeguard layer for leave-one-out outlier gene detection: exemptions and caps that prevent legitimate genes from being wrongly excluded when recomputing PC1-explained variance (L1) per gene set. It combines a Fisher test on outlier proportions across gene set collections, a rare-membership exemption, and a per-module cap on removable genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is to remove outlier samples rather than outlier genes — rROMA handles sample filtering separately via detected-gene counts and PCA projection with a distance threshold. The gene set is so small that the maximum removable-outlier proportion cap would invalidate the PC1 computation, or the expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma requires normalized data, e.g. edgeR cpm or DESeq2 vst).

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (AnnData/scanpy) must be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by prior gene annotations (MSigDB, Reactome, GO, cell type markers), e.g. for pathway activity or drug-response interpretation.
skills.name: gene-module-variational-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: gene-module-variational-autoencoder-training Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (AnnData/scanpy) must be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by prior gene annotations (MSigDB, Reactome, GO, cell type markers), e.g. for pathway activity or drug-response interpretation. When no prior biological gene-module annotation (GMT) is available and an unrestricted latent representation suffices — VEGA's latent variables are hard-wired to user-provided gene modules When the priority is generative/predictive performance rather than interpretability — the sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability When the prior knowledge is likely incomplete or not context-specific and needs to be corrected during training — the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Train VEGA (VAE Enhanced by Gene Annotations), a sparse variational autoencoder whose decoder wiring mirrors user-provided gene modules (GMT files), to embed single-cell transcriptomics data into an interpretable latent space of gene module variational activities (GMVs) for pathways, transcription factor regulons, or cell type markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Train VEGA (VAE Enhanced by Gene Annotations), a sparse variational autoencoder whose decoder wiring mirrors user-provided gene modules (GMT files), to embed single-cell transcriptomics data into an interpretable latent space of gene module variational activities (GMVs) for pathways, transcription factor regulons, or cell type markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior biological gene-module annotation (GMT) is available and an unrestricted latent representation suffices — VEGA's latent variables are hard-wired to user-provided gene modules When the priority is generative/predictive performance rather than interpretability — the sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability When the prior knowledge is likely incomplete or not context-specific and needs to be corrected during training — the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge

skills.description: Use when refining an inferred GRN against curated databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) and gene/organism labels from a GenBank file may miss synonyms, causing incomplete interaction retrieval.
skills.name: gene-name-alias-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-name-alias-mapping Use when refining an inferred GRN against curated databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) and gene/organism labels from a GenBank file may miss synonyms, causing incomplete interaction retrieval. The organism or its genes are not represented in curated databases (typical for many non-model microbes), where refinement steps cannot contribute verified interactions The task is Boolean Network conversion from an existing final GRN, which uses the Cell Collective database search rather than alias-based interaction retrieval Only promoter-based de novo TFBM refinement is needed and no database interaction search is planned Expands organism and gene names into scientific and common-name aliases (e.g., via the EcoNameTranslator Python package) before querying curated regulatory databases, so that the maximum number of verified interactions can be retrieved for GRN refinement in Augusta. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Expands organism and gene names into scientific and common-name aliases (e.g., via the EcoNameTranslator Python package) before querying curated regulatory databases, so that the maximum number of verified interactions can be retrieved for GRN refinement in Augusta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism or its genes are not represented in curated databases (typical for many non-model microbes), where refinement steps cannot contribute verified interactions The task is Boolean Network conversion from an existing final GRN, which uses the Cell Collective database search rather than alias-based interaction retrieval Only promoter-based de novo TFBM refinement is needed and no database interaction search is planned

skills.description: Use when comparing gene network inference methods or model variants against a curated directed binary ground truth (e.g. Omnipath) and reporting AUPRC and EPR per cell type or condition.
skills.name: gene-network-benchmarking-metrics
skills.search_text: gene-network-benchmarking-metrics Use when comparing gene network inference methods or model variants against a curated directed binary ground truth (e.g. Omnipath) and reporting AUPRC and EPR per cell type or condition. When no literature or experimental ground truth exists for the gene set of interest — the article notes that no perfect ground truths exist for GN inference benchmarking, so metrics must be interpreted cautiously When comparing methods run on different gene sets or different cell subsets — the benchmark requires identical cells and genes across methods for fair EPR/AUPRC comparison When evaluating causal directionality — Omnipath sources have sparse out-degree, requiring network transposition, so the benchmark is about literature-curated interaction recovery, not causality http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark inferred gene networks (e.g. scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, DeepSEM, GENIE3 variants) against a literature-derived directed ground truth such as Omnipath using prevalence-floored AUPRC and EPR (diagnostic odds ratio at K = number of ground-truth positives), implemented via the BenGRN/GRnnData benchmark suite. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Benchmark inferred gene networks (e.g. scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, DeepSEM, GENIE3 variants) against a literature-derived directed ground truth such as Omnipath using prevalence-floored AUPRC and EPR (diagnostic odds ratio at K = number of ground-truth positives), implemented via the BenGRN/GRnnData benchmark suite.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no literature or experimental ground truth exists for the gene set of interest — the article notes that no perfect ground truths exist for GN inference benchmarking, so metrics must be interpreted cautiously When comparing methods run on different gene sets or different cell subsets — the benchmark requires identical cells and genes across methods for fair EPR/AUPRC comparison When evaluating causal directionality — Omnipath sources have sparse out-degree, requiring network transposition, so the benchmark is about literature-curated interaction recovery, not causality

skills.description: Use when you have weighted, cell-type-specific gene network adjacency matrices (e.g., GRnnData objects from scPRINT) and need to identify differential hub genes or functionally enriched network communities, as done for the BPH fibroblast ion-exchange/senescence module.
skills.name: gene-network-centrality-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-network-centrality-analysis Use when you have weighted, cell-type-specific gene network adjacency matrices (e.g., GRnnData objects from scPRINT) and need to identify differential hub genes or functionally enriched network communities, as done for the BPH fibroblast ion-exchange/senescence module. When the goal is raw edge-level benchmarking against a gold standard (e.g., SERGIO-simulated or gwps perturb-seq edges) rather than node-level hub scoring and enrichment When the network is not weighted/cell-type-specific — hub centrality on binarized, non-specific co-expression matrices loses the per-method edge scores the ranking depends on When you only need pathway enrichment of a predefined gene list; prerank enrichment without a network-derived ranking does not require this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Per-gene hub scoring of cell-type-specific gene networks (e.g., scPRINT-inferred BPH vs normal prostate fibroblast networks) via eigenvector centrality and row/column-wise edge-score sums in GRnnData/NetworkX, followed by Louvain community detection and prerank gene-set enrichment to interpret differential hubs and subnetworks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Per-gene hub scoring of cell-type-specific gene networks (e.g., scPRINT-inferred BPH vs normal prostate fibroblast networks) via eigenvector centrality and row/column-wise edge-score sums in GRnnData/NetworkX, followed by Louvain community detection and prerank gene-set enrichment to interpret differential hubs and subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is raw edge-level benchmarking against a gold standard (e.g., SERGIO-simulated or gwps perturb-seq edges) rather than node-level hub scoring and enrichment When the network is not weighted/cell-type-specific — hub centrality on binarized, non-specific co-expression matrices loses the per-method edge scores the ranking depends on When you only need pathway enrichment of a predefined gene list; prerank enrichment without a network-derived ranking does not require this skill

skills.description: Use when extracting a gene regulatory network from a pretrained transformer's attention matrices and you must decide which attention heads to average, using a literature ground truth such as Omnipath.
skills.name: gene-network-heads-selection
skills.search_text: gene-network-heads-selection Use when extracting a gene regulatory network from a pretrained transformer's attention matrices and you must decide which attention heads to average, using a literature ground truth such as Omnipath. There is no ground-truth edge set (e.g., Omnipath) available to train the RidgeClassifier for head selection — the all-head average or genome-wide variant must be used instead The goal is de novo GRN inference from expression counts alone without a pretrained transformer (use GENIE3 or DeepSEM directly) Benchmarking on ODE-generated mock-up expression data rather than literature-based or experimental ground truths, which the article cautions against http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Select informative transformer attention heads and aggregate them into a gene network using a RidgeClassifier trained on ground-truth edges (e.g., Omnipath), as done for scPRINT's gene network inference benchmark against GENIE3, scGPT, Geneformer, and DeepSEM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Select informative transformer attention heads and aggregate them into a gene network using a RidgeClassifier trained on ground-truth edges (e.g., Omnipath), as done for scPRINT's gene network inference benchmark against GENIE3, scGPT, Geneformer, and DeepSEM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no ground-truth edge set (e.g., Omnipath) available to train the RidgeClassifier for head selection — the all-head average or genome-wide variant must be used instead The goal is de novo GRN inference from expression counts alone without a pretrained transformer (use GENIE3 or DeepSEM directly) Benchmarking on ODE-generated mock-up expression data rather than literature-based or experimental ground truths, which the article cautions against

skills.description: Use when inferring genome-wide gene regulatory networks from a single-cell transformer model's attention matrices and benchmarking against ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold-standard networks with EPR and AUPRC metrics.
skills.name: gene-network-inference-from-attention-matrices
skills.search_text: gene-network-inference-from-attention-matrices Use when inferring genome-wide gene regulatory networks from a single-cell transformer model's attention matrices and benchmarking against ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold-standard networks with EPR and AUPRC metrics. The task only requires zero-shot abilities such as denoising, batch correction, or cell label prediction rather than gene network extraction The expression data are ODE-generated mock-up (e.g., SERGIO-simulated) rather than real single-cell profiles with orthogonal ChIP-seq/perturb-seq ground truths A literature-based aggregate network like Omnipath alone is the intended target, since general collections like Omnipath did not improve performance in most tests http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts gene regulatory networks from transformer foundation-model attention (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer) by averaging Keys/Queries embeddings over cells, and benchmarks them against cell type-specific ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold standards using EPR and AUPRC via the BenGRN/GRnnData packages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Extracts gene regulatory networks from transformer foundation-model attention (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer) by averaging Keys/Queries embeddings over cells, and benchmarks them against cell type-specific ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold standards using EPR and AUPRC via the BenGRN/GRnnData packages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task only requires zero-shot abilities such as denoising, batch correction, or cell label prediction rather than gene network extraction The expression data are ODE-generated mock-up (e.g., SERGIO-simulated) rather than real single-cell profiles with orthogonal ChIP-seq/perturb-seq ground truths A literature-based aggregate network like Omnipath alone is the intended target, since general collections like Omnipath did not improve performance in most tests

skills.description: Use when you have a data frame (CSV format) of significantly changed genes with log-fold-change values from single-cell RNA-seq or proteomics experiments and need per-gene LFC scores for GMM-based gene-network exploration in OmicInt.
skills.name: gene-network-scoring-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-network-scoring-analysis Use when you have a data frame (CSV format) of significantly changed genes with log-fold-change values from single-cell RNA-seq or proteomics experiments and need per-gene LFC scores for GMM-based gene-network exploration in OmicInt. Input data is not a data frame of significantly changed genes with LFC values (e.g. raw counts or unfiltered omics matrices) — OmicInt requires the user to first ensure 'the supplied data is in the right format' The analysis target is epigenomic regulatory-layer exploration, protein type / cellular location classification, or interactome assessment via UniProt/STRINGdb rather than LFC scoring of changed genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the OmicInt LFC-based score — the key analytical parameter of the package's machine learning pipeline — which captures expression and pathology associations for significantly changed genes and feeds the Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline used to explore genes and linked interactome networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2021.100025
skills.summary: Computes the OmicInt LFC-based score — the key analytical parameter of the package's machine learning pipeline — which captures expression and pathology associations for significantly changed genes and feeds the Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline used to explore genes and linked interactome networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not a data frame of significantly changed genes with LFC values (e.g. raw counts or unfiltered omics matrices) — OmicInt requires the user to first ensure 'the supplied data is in the right format' The analysis target is epigenomic regulatory-layer exploration, protein type / cellular location classification, or interactome assessment via UniProt/STRINGdb rather than LFC scoring of changed genes

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or retraining DCNet: you need to wire the 9078x434 zero-one gene-cell matrix into the network's input-to-hidden weights and align input/output neuron ordering with the gene index.
skills.name: gene-neuron-correspondence-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-neuron-correspondence-mapping Use when reconstructing or retraining DCNet: you need to wire the 9078x434 zero-one gene-cell matrix into the network's input-to-hidden weights and align input/output neuron ordering with the gene index. Input expression rows are not human gene symbols or cannot be aligned to the index.pkl gene ordering (e.g. probe IDs, Ensembl IDs without symbol mapping) The analysis targets a different deconvolution method (CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) rather than the DCNet masked-autoencoder architecture Only pre-trained DCNet weights are needed for scoring with no architecture reconstruction or re-masking required http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Map the 9078 marker genes and 434 cell types of DCNet onto input, hidden, and output neurons using the pickled gene-cell relation matrix (rix.pkl/relation_matrix.pkl) and gene-to-neuron index (index.pkl), so each hidden neuron corresponds to one cell type whose incoming weights are masked to its marker genes only. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Map the 9078 marker genes and 434 cell types of DCNet onto input, hidden, and output neurons using the pickled gene-cell relation matrix (rix.pkl/relation_matrix.pkl) and gene-to-neuron index (index.pkl), so each hidden neuron corresponds to one cell type whose incoming weights are masked to its marker genes only.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression rows are not human gene symbols or cannot be aligned to the index.pkl gene ordering (e.g. probe IDs, Ensembl IDs without symbol mapping) The analysis targets a different deconvolution method (CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) rather than the DCNet masked-autoencoder architecture Only pre-trained DCNet weights are needed for scoring with no architecture reconstruction or re-masking required

skills.description: Use when you have mouse gene clusters/modules (e.g., co-expression GEPs) and need to determine which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched, with enrichment ratios and BH-adjusted p-values.
skills.name: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping Use when you have mouse gene clusters/modules (e.g., co-expression GEPs) and need to determine which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched, with enrichment ratios and BH-adjusted p-values. Input gene identifiers are not Ensembl gene IDs (e.g., symbols without prior conversion via Mouse.gene.symbl.txt) — ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis only supports Ensembl gene IDs The gene set is from a non-mouse organism — annotations provided are mouse-specific (Ensembl BioMart GO and MGI MP) You need enrichment for modalities beyond GO/MP term ontology, or brain-focused functional annotation where GO/MP granularity is lacking http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Maps mouse gene sets (e.g., SingleCellGGM-derived GEPs) to GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) terms via over-representation testing with the hypergeometric test and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, using ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis annotation files from Ensembl BioMart and MGI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Maps mouse gene sets (e.g., SingleCellGGM-derived GEPs) to GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) terms via over-representation testing with the hypergeometric test and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, using ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis annotation files from Ensembl BioMart and MGI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene identifiers are not Ensembl gene IDs (e.g., symbols without prior conversion via Mouse.gene.symbl.txt) — ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis only supports Ensembl gene IDs The gene set is from a non-mouse organism — annotations provided are mouse-specific (Ensembl BioMart GO and MGI MP) You need enrichment for modalities beyond GO/MP term ontology, or brain-focused functional annotation where GO/MP granularity is lacking

skills.description: Use when mouse (3T3-L1) differential expression results need to be translated into GO terms — e.g. ranking genes by log fold-change and testing which adipogenic GO categories (BP/CC/MF) are significantly enriched.
skills.name: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping-mouse
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping-mouse Use when mouse (3T3-L1) differential expression results need to be translated into GO terms — e.g. ranking genes by log fold-change and testing which adipogenic GO categories (BP/CC/MF) are significantly enriched. Input is non-mouse (e.g. human) gene expression — Org.Mm.eg.db and the 3T3-L1 curated datasets are mouse-specific Input is raw probe-level intensities rather than gene-collapsed differential expression results — the curatedAdipoArray data are already collapsed to gene symbols using collapsRows The goal is RNA-seq count-level enrichment (curatedAdipoRNA) or ChIP-seq peak enrichment (curatedAdipoChIP) rather than microarray expression ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Maps differentially expressed genes from mouse 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data to Gene Ontology terms and identifies enriched GO categories via clusterProfiler GSEA against BP, CC and MF ontologies, using Org.Mm.eg.db/GO.db annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Maps differentially expressed genes from mouse 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data to Gene Ontology terms and identifies enriched GO categories via clusterProfiler GSEA against BP, CC and MF ontologies, using Org.Mm.eg.db/GO.db annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is non-mouse (e.g. human) gene expression — Org.Mm.eg.db and the 3T3-L1 curated datasets are mouse-specific Input is raw probe-level intensities rather than gene-collapsed differential expression results — the curatedAdipoArray data are already collapsed to gene symbols using collapsRows The goal is RNA-seq count-level enrichment (curatedAdipoRNA) or ChIP-seq peak enrichment (curatedAdipoChIP) rather than microarray expression ranking

skills.description: Use when a pre-computed cell-cell interaction (CCI) dataset of enriched int-pairs must be annotated with Gene Ontology functional terms, as a prerequisite for ranking terms by annotated int-pair occurrence.
skills.name: gene-ontology-annotation-via-biomart
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-annotation-via-biomart Use when a pre-computed cell-cell interaction (CCI) dataset of enriched int-pairs must be annotated with Gene Ontology functional terms, as a prerequisite for ranking terms by annotated int-pair occurrence. The interaction table has not been pre-computed/enriched (InterCellar builds on pre-computed, inferred ligand-receptor interactions uploaded as CCI data). skills.summary: Retrieves Gene Ontology term-gene annotations from Ensembl using the biomaRt R package so that functional terms can be assigned to predicted ligand-receptor interaction pairs (int-pairs) in InterCellar's function-verse.

You need de novo GO enrichment statistics on a plain gene list rather than annotation of already-enriched int-pairs by partner-gene overlap. The analysis goal is pathway-only annotation without Gene Ontology — use the graphite-based pathway resources instead of biomaRt GO queries.

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked or significant gene list (e.g., SigGenes at fdr level 0.01) and need to confirm it is biologically meaningful via GO biological-process term enrichment.
skills.name: gene-ontology-biological-process-enrichment
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-biological-process-enrichment Use when you have a ranked or significant gene list (e.g., SigGenes at fdr level 0.01) and need to confirm it is biologically meaningful via GO biological-process term enrichment. The input is not a gene list but raw scRNA-seq data — run scTITANS first to identify the DEGs before enrichment. skills.description: Use when you must timestamp individual bulk or scRNAseq pseudobulk transcriptomic samples (e.g., microarray or RNAseq) whose circadian phase is unknown and no matched control series exists for cross-sample normalization.
skills.name: gene-pair-difference-normalization
skills.search_text: gene-pair-difference-normalization Use when you must timestamp individual bulk or scRNAseq pseudobulk transcriptomic samples (e.g., microarray or RNAseq) whose circadian phase is unknown and no matched control series exists for cross-sample normalization. Predicting circadian time at single-cell resolution: tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and only works on pseudobulk-aggregated samples Predicting timescales of diseased samples while trained on healthy data: a time series from diseased individuals is required for that projection Datasets where gene-pair differences plausibly depend on factors other than circadian time (e.g., circadian-disturbed/diseased tissue), since the within-sample normalization rests on that unverified assumption http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 tauFisher's within-sample normalization: circadian time is predicted from a single transcriptomic sample by computing and scaling expression differences for each pair of rhythmic predictor genes, then projecting the scaled differences via PCA into a multinomial logistic regression on the first two principal components. This makes the feature vector dependent only on circadian time, not on library size or assay platform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: tauFisher's within-sample normalization: circadian time is predicted from a single transcriptomic sample by computing and scaling expression differences for each pair of rhythmic predictor genes, then projecting the scaled differences via PCA into a multinomial logistic regression on the first two principal components. This makes the feature vector dependent only on circadian time, not on library size or assay platform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting circadian time at single-cell resolution: tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and only works on pseudobulk-aggregated samples Predicting timescales of diseased samples while trained on healthy data: a time series from diseased individuals is required for that projection Datasets where gene-pair differences plausibly depend on factors other than circadian time (e.g., circadian-disturbed/diseased tissue), since the within-sample normalization rests on that unverified assumption

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq/microarray with matched survival data must be tested for whether immune cell types or immune marker genes appear spuriously favorable due to co-infiltration, as in TCGA SKCM06 melanoma.
skills.name: gene-pair-prognostic-association-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-pair-prognostic-association-analysis Use when bulk RNA-seq/microarray with matched survival data must be tested for whether immune cell types or immune marker genes appear spuriously favorable due to co-infiltration, as in TCGA SKCM06 melanoma. Input lacks matched survival information or event/time-to-event fields — TimiGP requires survival data to fit Cox models The cohort is too small: power is determined by sample size, number of events, and quality of survival information The goal is cell-cell interaction inference or immunotherapy response prediction (TimiGP-Response modules) rather than quantifying prognostic bias of cell types/marker genes http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies prognostic bias caused by immune co-infiltration by fitting univariate Cox regressions (survival/TimiCOX, BH-adjusted) on immune cell type scores and immune marker genes in the TCGA SKCM06 metastatic melanoma cohort, then computing the fraction of significant associations (p<0.05) that are favorable (HR<1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Quantifies prognostic bias caused by immune co-infiltration by fitting univariate Cox regressions (survival/TimiCOX, BH-adjusted) on immune cell type scores and immune marker genes in the TCGA SKCM06 metastatic melanoma cohort, then computing the fraction of significant associations (p<0.05) that are favorable (HR<1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks matched survival information or event/time-to-event fields — TimiGP requires survival data to fit Cox models The cohort is too small: power is determined by sample size, number of events, and quality of survival information The goal is cell-cell interaction inference or immunotherapy response prediction (TimiGP-Response modules) rather than quantifying prognostic bias of cell types/marker genes

skills.name: gene-pair-score-computation
skills.search_text: gene-pair-score-computation Use when a bulk transcriptomic cohort has been preprocessed with marker-gene selection and you need a pairwise logical-relational matrix of marker expression comparisons to feed Cox regression or enrichment of cell-cell interactions. Input is single-cell expression data with per-cell resolution where direct cell-type abundance deconvolution methods (xCell, CIBERSORTx) are appropriate The cohort lacks matched survival or response information, since downstream directed IMGP selection relies on Cox regression of the MPS matrix Only a small number of marker genes are available, since enrichment-based interaction sensitivity is affected by marker gene count http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute the binary Marker Pair Score (MPS) matrix used by the TimiGP framework, capturing pairwise logical relations between marker genes (e.g., 1 = gene A expression > gene B) from log-transformed, gene-wise median-normalized bulk expression data, as the basis for inferring prognostic cell-cell interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell expression data with per-cell resolution where direct cell-type abundance deconvolution methods (xCell, CIBERSORTx) are appropriate The cohort lacks matched survival or response information, since downstream directed IMGP selection relies on Cox regression of the MPS matrix Only a small number of marker genes are available, since enrichment-based interaction sensitivity is affected by marker gene count

skills.description: Use when a set of candidate ligand-receptor pairs has been inferred between two cell types and you must determine whether each pair is restricted to that sender-receiver combination or also appears in other cell-type interactions.
skills.name: gene-pair-specificity-evaluation
skills.search_text: gene-pair-specificity-evaluation Use when a set of candidate ligand-receptor pairs has been inferred between two cell types and you must determine whether each pair is restricted to that sender-receiver combination or also appears in other cell-type interactions. When no prior cell-cell interaction inference has been run — specificity evaluation requires precomputed InterCellDB interaction results with confidence from the permutation framework, not raw expression matrices. When the goal is de novo discovery of all interacting pairs rather than assessing the restrictedness of a predefined candidate list — use InterCellDB's full network analysis instead. When pairs are expected to act via non-binding modes (e.g., predicted rather than experiment-validated interactions), since the specificity assessment relies on the interaction database built from STRING protein-protein interactions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates whether candidate ligand-receptor gene pairs (e.g., C3-Itgb2, C3-Itgam, C3-C5ar1, C3-C3ar1) are specific to one sender-receiver cell-type pair or participate in crosstalk elsewhere, using InterCellDB's intercellular analysis on specificity, which evaluates co-occurrences of gene pairs across interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Evaluates whether candidate ligand-receptor gene pairs (e.g., C3-Itgb2, C3-Itgam, C3-C5ar1, C3-C3ar1) are specific to one sender-receiver cell-type pair or participate in crosstalk elsewhere, using InterCellDB's intercellular analysis on specificity, which evaluates co-occurrences of gene pairs across interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior cell-cell interaction inference has been run — specificity evaluation requires precomputed InterCellDB interaction results with confidence from the permutation framework, not raw expression matrices. When the goal is de novo discovery of all interacting pairs rather than assessing the restrictedness of a predefined candidate list — use InterCellDB's full network analysis instead. When pairs are expected to act via non-binding modes (e.g., predicted rather than experiment-validated interactions), since the specificity assessment relies on the interaction database built from STRING protein-protein interactions.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of essential genes and gene pairs (from single-/double-gene knockout analysis, e.g. FBA with a VBOF) and need to convert them into approved single-drug and drug-combination candidates via DrugBank target mapping.
skills.name: gene-pair-to-drug-combination-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-pair-to-drug-combination-mapping Use when you have a list of essential genes and gene pairs (from single-/double-gene knockout analysis, e.g. FBA with a VBOF) and need to convert them into approved single-drug and drug-combination candidates via DrugBank target mapping. When the goal is direct docking or binding-affinity prediction against viral proteins — the identified drugs are based on targets from network effects on the host metabolome (the virus is only modeled via its biomass function), not direct docking When candidate drug pairs must be ranked by measured potency or synergy — no drug response curves, IC-50, or synergy scores are produced by this skill When the gene list is not disease-specific essentiality output (e.g. DEG lists without knockout essentiality scores) — the essentiality-score and gene-pair filters cannot be applied meaningfully http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Maps disease-specific essential genes and gene pairs identified by in silico knockout of context-specific metabolic models onto the DrugBank V5 drug-target network, yielding single-drug and drug-combination repositioning candidates (here: 85 single drugs and 52 combinations for COVID-19). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Maps disease-specific essential genes and gene pairs identified by in silico knockout of context-specific metabolic models onto the DrugBank V5 drug-target network, yielding single-drug and drug-combination repositioning candidates (here: 85 single drugs and 52 combinations for COVID-19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct docking or binding-affinity prediction against viral proteins — the identified drugs are based on targets from network effects on the host metabolome (the virus is only modeled via its biomass function), not direct docking When candidate drug pairs must be ranked by measured potency or synergy — no drug response curves, IC-50, or synergy scores are produced by this skill When the gene list is not disease-specific essentiality output (e.g. DEG lists without knockout essentiality scores) — the essentiality-score and gene-pair filters cannot be applied meaningfully

skills.description: Use when you have a log2-transformed expression matrix (data frame) of multiple genes/features (e.g. 40 genes across ~10K TCGA Pan-Cancer samples) and need a pairwise correlation heatmap ordered by hierarchical clustering into feature clusters.
skills.name: gene-pairwise-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-pairwise-correlation-analysis Use when you have a log2-transformed expression matrix (data frame) of multiple genes/features (e.g. 40 genes across ~10K TCGA Pan-Cancer samples) and need a pairwise correlation heatmap ordered by hierarchical clustering into feature clusters. You want correlation of ONE prime feature (e.g. RNASEH2A) against many features — use primefeature_corr instead of pairwise_corr. You need deep analysis of a single feature pair with regression/density — use pair_scatter (e.g. feature1="RNASEH2A", feature2="PCNA"). Your input data is untransformed/raw sequencing counts and exhibits heteroskedasticity — first apply data_transform with transformation='log2' and a medianthres filter (e.g. medianthres=1) before pairwise_corr. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute and visualize multiple pairwise correlations among a set of genes/features using the FeatureCorr R package's pairwise_corr function, whose default output is a hierarchically clustered correlation heatmap. It is designed for NGS or microarray expression data such as the TCGA Pan-Cancer logTCGA40 dataset (40 genes, >10K samples). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: Compute and visualize multiple pairwise correlations among a set of genes/features using the FeatureCorr R package's pairwise_corr function, whose default output is a hierarchically clustered correlation heatmap. It is designed for NGS or microarray expression data such as the TCGA Pan-Cancer logTCGA40 dataset (40 genes, >10K samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want correlation of ONE prime feature (e.g. RNASEH2A) against many features — use primefeature_corr instead of pairwise_corr. You need deep analysis of a single feature pair with regression/density — use pair_scatter (e.g. feature1="RNASEH2A", feature2="PCNA"). Your input data is untransformed/raw sequencing counts and exhibits heteroskedasticity — first apply data_transform with transformation='log2' and a medianthres filter (e.g. medianthres=1) before pairwise_corr.

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq AnnData has a different gene count or ordering than the SIMS TabNet reference model's training features, and cell-type label prediction must proceed without feature-mismatch errors.
skills.name: gene-panel-intersection-across-datasets
skills.search_text: gene-panel-intersection-across-datasets Use when a query scRNA-seq AnnData has a different gene count or ordering than the SIMS TabNet reference model's training features, and cell-type label prediction must proceed without feature-mismatch errors. The query dataset already contains exactly the reference model's training genes in the same order — no intersection is needed, predict directly Cross-species label transfer is the goal — the article restricts SIMS to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Gene symbols use inconsistent naming conventions across labs — the paper notes lack of naming conventions makes harmonization manually intensive and ontology-based harmonization is only a proposed future direction http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Automated gene-set alignment for cross-dataset label transfer with SIMS/TabNet: the query AnnData's gene panel is intersected with and reordered to match the trained reference model's feature panel, so prediction can run on datasets with a different number of genes (e.g. PBMC68K ~20k vs Han landscape ~5k). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Automated gene-set alignment for cross-dataset label transfer with SIMS/TabNet: the query AnnData's gene panel is intersected with and reordered to match the trained reference model's feature panel, so prediction can run on datasets with a different number of genes (e.g. PBMC68K ~20k vs Han landscape ~5k).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset already contains exactly the reference model's training genes in the same order — no intersection is needed, predict directly Cross-species label transfer is the goal — the article restricts SIMS to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species Gene symbols use inconsistent naming conventions across labs — the paper notes lack of naming conventions makes harmonization manually intensive and ontology-based harmonization is only a proposed future direction

skills.description: Decision support for choosing the RNA-seq biosample for a disease gene panel: you have per-tissue MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) and a panel gene list, and need the tissue minimizing required sequencing depth.
skills.name: gene-panel-tissue-optimality-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-panel-tissue-optimality-analysis Decision support for choosing the RNA-seq biosample for a disease gene panel: you have per-tissue MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) and a panel gene list, and need the tissue minimizing required sequencing depth. The RNA-seq workflow deviates from bulk short-read poly-A enrichment RNA-seq processed with the Cummings-style pipeline — the GTEx-derived MRSD scores are not calibrated for long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq The goal is to predict suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the MRSD model is not validated for these applications Disease involves widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g., interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders) — MRSD predictions may not reflect coverage when genomic background alters expression, and eQTLs/sQTLs are not explicitly modeled http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Rank the four GTEx-derived biosamples (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, fibroblasts) by their proportion of low-MRSD (<100 million reads) genes within each PanelApp disease gene panel, to identify the optimal RNA source per panel. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Rank the four GTEx-derived biosamples (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, fibroblasts) by their proportion of low-MRSD (<100 million reads) genes within each PanelApp disease gene panel, to identify the optimal RNA source per panel.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The RNA-seq workflow deviates from bulk short-read poly-A enrichment RNA-seq processed with the Cummings-style pipeline — the GTEx-derived MRSD scores are not calibrated for long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq The goal is to predict suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the MRSD model is not validated for these applications Disease involves widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g., interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders) — MRSD predictions may not reflect coverage when genomic background alters expression, and eQTLs/sQTLs are not explicitly modeled

skills.name: gene-periodicity-magnitude-quantification
skills.search_text: gene-periodicity-magnitude-quantification Use when you have Cyclum-inferred circular pseudo-time for cells in two or more conditions (e. You only need cell-cycle phase labels or pseudo-time itself, not gene-level periodicity scores — the Cyclum model fitting suffices without the evaluation step The data lack a circular/periodic structure (e.g., linear differentiation trajectories); Cyclum projects data onto a predefined circular manifold and is designed for periodic processes You intend to use marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring, scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle) as the primary quantification — Cyclum explicitly relies on the circular manifold instead of marker genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify each gene's circular-pattern magnitude (degree of match between its expression kinetics and an inferred periodic trajectory) with Cyclum's evaluation module, and compute condition-vs-condition differences in that magnitude to nominate genes associated with a periodic process such as the cell cycle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Quantify each gene's circular-pattern magnitude (degree of match between its expression kinetics and an inferred periodic trajectory) with Cyclum's evaluation module, and compute condition-vs-condition differences in that magnitude to nominate genes associated with a periodic process such as the cell cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need cell-cycle phase labels or pseudo-time itself, not gene-level periodicity scores — the Cyclum model fitting suffices without the evaluation step The data lack a circular/periodic structure (e.g., linear differentiation trajectories); Cyclum projects data onto a predefined circular manifold and is designed for periodic processes You intend to use marker-gene-based cell-cycle scoring (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring, scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle) as the primary quantification — Cyclum explicitly relies on the circular manifold instead of marker genes

skills.search_text: gene-presence-absence-feature-selection Use when building lifestyle or metadata classifiers from a binary gene cluster presence/absence matrix (e. Input is not a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix (e.g. raw gene sequences or annotated GFF files) — clustering into gene clusters must happen first in bacLIFE's clustering module Lifestyle labels are not literature-derived per-genome metadata, so there is no target variable for chi2 scoring and supervised selection The goal is de novo gene clustering or genome annotation rather than lifestyle prediction from an existing cluster matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reduces a high-dimensional gene cluster absence/presence matrix (thousands of MCL-derived gene clusters per genome) to the top 1000 most informative gene-cluster features via chi2 feature selection before training binary random forest lifestyle classifiers. skills.description: Use when preparing a raw scRNA-seq/CITE-seq count matrix (e.g., an AnnData .h5ad loaded with scanpy) for marker selection, and you need to discard genes expressed in too few or too many cells before normalization and z-scaling.
skills.name: gene-presence-fraction-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-presence-fraction-filtering Use when preparing a raw scRNA-seq/CITE-seq count matrix (e.g., an AnnData .h5ad loaded with scanpy) for marker selection, and you need to discard genes expressed in too few or too many cells before normalization and z-scaling. When the input is already a preprocessed/feature-reduced matrix or a marker list rather than raw per-gene counts — re-filtering would discard meaningful genes. When the data is not single-cell gene expression (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial FISH target panels), since the presence/absence fraction logic is calibrated to per-cell expression sparsity. When filtering is the only needed step and no downstream MarkerMap training is planned — a standard scanpy filter may suffice without the dense conversion overhead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A preprocessing filter for single-cell expression matrices that removes housekeeping/general genes and drops genes expressed in too few or too many cells, so that only informative genes survive into normalization, log2(1+x) transformation, and MarkerMap marker selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: A preprocessing filter for single-cell expression matrices that removes housekeeping/general genes and drops genes expressed in too few or too many cells, so that only informative genes survive into normalization, log2(1+x) transformation, and MarkerMap marker selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a preprocessed/feature-reduced matrix or a marker list rather than raw per-gene counts — re-filtering would discard meaningful genes. When the data is not single-cell gene expression (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial FISH target panels), since the presence/absence fraction logic is calibrated to per-cell expression sparsity. When filtering is the only needed step and no downstream MarkerMap training is planned — a standard scanpy filter may suffice without the dense conversion overhead.

skills.description: Use when the goal is unsupervised discovery of gene programs/modules from normalized scRNA-seq data, especially when benchmarking against ICA/NMF or seeking GO-term/PPI-enriched gene modules.
skills.name: gene-program-discovery-network-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-program-discovery-network-analysis Use when the goal is unsupervised discovery of gene programs/modules from normalized scRNA-seq data, especially when benchmarking against ICA/NMF or seeking GO-term/PPI-enriched gene modules. The analysis goal is cell-type annotation or cluster resolution selection rather than gene module discovery — use the Miko scoring or specificity-based resolution workflows instead Data is raw counts without normalization; the SSN pearson-correlation input expects preprocessed expression A supervised or pre-defined gene set scoring task is intended — use mikoScore/sigScore rather than unsupervised SSN discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Discovers unsupervised gene programs from scRNA-seq data by building a scale-free shared nearest neighbor (SSN) network over selected network features, pruning low-connectivity genes, and functionally annotating modules — a graph-based alternative to factorization methods like ICA and NMF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Discovers unsupervised gene programs from scRNA-seq data by building a scale-free shared nearest neighbor (SSN) network over selected network features, pruning low-connectivity genes, and functionally annotating modules — a graph-based alternative to factorization methods like ICA and NMF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is cell-type annotation or cluster resolution selection rather than gene module discovery — use the Miko scoring or specificity-based resolution workflows instead Data is raw counts without normalization; the SSN pearson-correlation input expects preprocessed expression A supervised or pre-defined gene set scoring task is intended — use mikoScore/sigScore rather than unsupervised SSN discovery

skills.description: Use when constructing an intercellular communication database from protein-centric PPI sources (e.g., STRING) that must be expressed as gene pairs to match scRNA-seq gene expression matrices for human or mouse.
skills.name: gene-protein-correspondence-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-protein-correspondence-mapping Use when constructing an intercellular communication database from protein-centric PPI sources (e.g., STRING) that must be expressed as gene pairs to match scRNA-seq gene expression matrices for human or mouse. Input is already a gene expression matrix keyed by gene symbols and no protein-level interaction database needs to be built The target species is neither human nor mouse, since the InterCellDB gene database covers only these two organisms The goal is downstream network inference (e.g., permutation tests on cell-cluster pairs) rather than database construction Builds a gene-coded protein database for InterCellDB by acquiring complete human (127 750) and mouse (21 291) protein data from the Ensembl genomes database and converting proteins into corresponding coding genes via NCBI genomes database references, enabling protein-protein interactions to be expressed as gene-gene pairs for scRNA-seq intercellular analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Builds a gene-coded protein database for InterCellDB by acquiring complete human (127 750) and mouse (21 291) protein data from the Ensembl genomes database and converting proteins into corresponding coding genes via NCBI genomes database references, enabling protein-protein interactions to be expressed as gene-gene pairs for scRNA-seq intercellular analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene expression matrix keyed by gene symbols and no protein-level interaction database needs to be built The target species is neither human nor mouse, since the InterCellDB gene database covers only these two organisms The goal is downstream network inference (e.g., permutation tests on cell-cluster pairs) rather than database construction

skills.description: Use when a labeled single-cell training matrix with cell type annotations needs supervised feature selection before building SciBet (or similar multinomial) classifiers.
skills.name: gene-ranking-and-top-k-selection
skills.search_text: gene-ranking-and-top-k-selection Use when a labeled single-cell training matrix with cell type annotations needs supervised feature selection before building SciBet (or similar multinomial) classifiers. Input is unlabeled data with no cell type annotations — ΔS requires per-cell-type mean expression vectors from a supervised reference You need a full model or predictions rather than a feature ranking — use Learn/Bet or ExportModel instead of SelectGene alone Input is already a reduced feature table of preselected marker genes; re-running ΔS ranking would discard prior curation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements SciBet's E-test feature selection: compute the entropy-based ΔS statistic per gene over cell-type mean expression vectors, then rank genes by ΔS and keep the top 500 as informative genes for the multinomial classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Implements SciBet's E-test feature selection: compute the entropy-based ΔS statistic per gene over cell-type mean expression vectors, then rank genes by ΔS and keep the top 500 as informative genes for the multinomial classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unlabeled data with no cell type annotations — ΔS requires per-cell-type mean expression vectors from a supervised reference You need a full model or predictions rather than a feature ranking — use Learn/Bet or ExportModel instead of SelectGene alone Input is already a reduced feature table of preselected marker genes; re-running ΔS ranking would discard prior curation

skills.description: Use when a normalized UMI matrix from scRNA-seq data (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) must be converted into AUCell rankings to score lineage signature gene sets loaded from a GMT file.
skills.name: gene-ranking-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: gene-ranking-matrix-construction Use when a normalized UMI matrix from scRNA-seq data (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) must be converted into AUCell rankings to score lineage signature gene sets loaded from a GMT file. The signature gene sets for your system are not available or curated — the protocol notes the user would have to compile and curate customized gene sets; only the 75 hematopoiesis sets are provided You only need differential expression between clusters (identifyDifferentialGenes) rather than enrichment-based per-cell signature scoring The object has not yet been normalized (normalize_UMIs not run) — rankings should be built on the normalized UMI matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds per-cell gene ranking matrices for AUCell-based signature scoring within SingCellaR, ranking genes by expression in each cell of the normalized UMI matrix so that gene-set enrichment (AUC) scores can be computed downstream for cell-type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Builds per-cell gene ranking matrices for AUCell-based signature scoring within SingCellaR, ranking genes by expression in each cell of the normalized UMI matrix so that gene-set enrichment (AUC) scores can be computed downstream for cell-type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The signature gene sets for your system are not available or curated — the protocol notes the user would have to compile and curate customized gene sets; only the 75 hematopoiesis sets are provided You only need differential expression between clusters (identifyDifferentialGenes) rather than enrichment-based per-cell signature scoring The object has not yet been normalized (normalize_UMIs not run) — rankings should be built on the normalized UMI matrix

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell-type ranked biomarker lists (e.g. top-100 from scaLR ClasswiseAbs) and a curated cell-type-specific reference marker database, and need to quantify/plot how many validated markers each tool recovers.
skills.name: gene-recall-curve-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-recall-curve-analysis Use when you have per-cell-type ranked biomarker lists (e.g. top-100 from scaLR ClasswiseAbs) and a curated cell-type-specific reference marker database, and need to quantify/plot how many validated markers each tool recovers. skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster labels) requires joint inference of a gene regulatory network and per-cell RNA velocities, especially to resolve directional dynamics like state transdifferentiation that standard methods miss.

skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-inference-via-expectation-maximization Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster labels) requires joint inference of a gene regulatory network and per-cell RNA velocities, especially to resolve directional dynamics like state transdifferentiation that standard methods miss. skills.description: Use when untreated scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue has a known drug target (e.g. Brd4 for BET inhibitors) and you must rank which cell types are most drug-responsive via in silico target perturbation of GRNs.

skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-perturbation-scoring Use when untreated scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue has a known drug target (e.g. Brd4 for BET inhibitors) and you must rank which cell types are most drug-responsive via in silico target perturbation of GRNs. The drug acts as an agonist — scRank primarily focuses on drugs acting as inhibitors, and agonist modeling (setting out-edge weights to their maximum value) is a preliminary simplifying assumption. The drug has multiple targets — multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank. Only treated-vs-untreated differential expression is available and drug target knowledge is not required — DEG-count or separability methods (e.g. Augur) fit that setting instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Generates a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) from cell-type-specific GRNs and scores in silico drug perturbation by combining global manifold-alignment distortion with local n-hop network diffusion, ranking drug-responsive cell types in scRank. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Generates a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) from cell-type-specific GRNs and scores in silico drug perturbation by combining global manifold-alignment distortion with local n-hop network diffusion, ranking drug-responsive cell types in scRank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts as an agonist — scRank primarily focuses on drugs acting as inhibitors, and agonist modeling (setting out-edge weights to their maximum value) is a preliminary simplifying assumption. skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be embedded with prior knowledge from a TF regulatory network (e.g., DoRothEA) so latent variables correspond to TF regulon activities, e.g., to score TF activity per cell or benchmark TF perturbation inference.
skills.name: gene-regulatory-network-prior-integration
skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-prior-integration Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be embedded with prior knowledge from a TF regulatory network (e.g., DoRothEA) so latent variables correspond to TF regulon activities, e.g., to score TF activity per cell or benchmark TF perturbation inference. The goal is a purely data-driven latent embedding without prior knowledge — omit the C prior and use GEDI's standard integration workflow instead. Input is not raw counts from scRNA-seq modeled with GEDI (e.g., pre-normalized feature tables); the prior-subset-then-QR workflow assumes a shared gene-space count matrix matching the DoRothEA network. The regulatory network is unrelated to the measured transcriptome such that after intersecting genes, singular-column removal via QR leaves no usable prior columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrate a TF-gene regulatory network prior (e.g., DoRothEA-derived) into the GEDI latent-variable model so that latent variables encode interpretable transcription factor regulon activities in single cells, validated by correlation of projected TF activity with the decoded abundance of the TF-encoding mRNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Integrate a TF-gene regulatory network prior (e.g., DoRothEA-derived) into the GEDI latent-variable model so that latent variables encode interpretable transcription factor regulon activities in single cells, validated by correlation of projected TF activity with the decoded abundance of the TF-encoding mRNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a purely data-driven latent embedding without prior knowledge — omit the C prior and use GEDI's standard integration workflow instead. skills.description: Use when the input is a directed GRN edge list (e.g. DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) plus a gene feature matrix, and the goal is to capture directed regulation information and second-order neighbor structure as embeddings.

skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-representation-learning Use when the input is a directed GRN edge list (e.g. DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) plus a gene feature matrix, and the goal is to capture directed regulation information and second-order neighbor structure as embeddings. The network is undirected — DGCN's in-/out-degree second-order proximity matrices require directed regulation edges You only need topological structure without gene features — the convolution ZF = sigma(AF X Theta) requires the gene feature matrix X You need patient-specific predictions — DGMP averages the SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression of all samples, ignoring individual cancer patients http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Learns node embeddings on a directed gene regulatory network (GRN) by applying the DGCN module of DGMP, which performs graph convolution with three proximity matrices (first-order AF and second-order in-/out-degree Ain, Aout) over multi-omics gene features to produce ZF, Zin, and Zout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Learns node embeddings on a directed gene regulatory network (GRN) by applying the DGCN module of DGMP, which performs graph convolution with three proximity matrices (first-order AF and second-order in-/out-degree Ain, Aout) over multi-omics gene features to produce ZF, Zin, and Zout.

skills.search_text: gene-scoring-per-cell-type-from-deconvolution-model Use when a trained SpatialDDLS deconvolution model exists and you need to know WHICH genes the network uses to predict each cell type's proportions, e.g. to recover canonical markers (Cd8/Cd8b1, Foxp3) from predicted spot compositions.
