skills.name: gene-set-based-cell-type-identification
skills.search_text: gene-set-based-cell-type-identification Use when the goal is to quantify cross-dataset replicability of known cell-type labels (e.g., neuron vs non-neuron across eight scRNA-seq studies) using gene sets and AUROC, rather than cluster-level unsupervised matching. Cell-type labels are absent, ambiguous, or unmatched across datasets — the supervised MetaNeighbor analysis requires corresponding cell types across datasets; use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS/topHits reciprocal-top-hits workflow instead Gene sets contain a single gene or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — the README states these must hold or MetaNeighbor cannot run Only one dataset is available with no cross-dataset validation possible — leave-one-dataset-out folds are undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A supervised MetaNeighbor workflow that scores how well cell-type labels (e.g., neurons vs non-neuronal cells) replicate across scRNA-seq datasets by neighbor voting on a cell-cell rank correlation network built from functional (e.g., GOmouse) and random gene sets, reporting mean AUROC across leave-one-dataset-out folds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: A supervised MetaNeighbor workflow that scores how well cell-type labels (e.g., neurons vs non-neuronal cells) replicate across scRNA-seq datasets by neighbor voting on a cell-cell rank correlation network built from functional (e.g., GOmouse) and random gene sets, reporting mean AUROC across leave-one-dataset-out folds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are absent, ambiguous, or unmatched across datasets — the supervised MetaNeighbor analysis requires corresponding cell types across datasets; use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS/topHits reciprocal-top-hits workflow instead Gene sets contain a single gene or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — the README states these must hold or MetaNeighbor cannot run Only one dataset is available with no cross-dataset validation possible — leave-one-dataset-out folds are undefined

skills.description: Use when several related (e.g., subtype-level) cell clusters each yield a ranked COVID-vs-healthy biomarker list and you need the gene subset whose expression direction is consistent across all of them.
skills.name: gene-set-consistency-filtering-across-clusters
skills.search_text: gene-set-consistency-filtering-across-clusters Use when several related (e.g., subtype-level) cell clusters each yield a ranked COVID-vs-healthy biomarker list and you need the gene subset whose expression direction is consistent across all of them. Only a single cell cluster is under analysis — the cross-cluster intersection that defines consistency is undefined The goal is pathway or GO enrichment of DE genes rather than identifying genes consistently differentially expressed across related clusters Cell clusters were not detected as related novel subtypes (e.g., they are unrelated reference cell types), so requiring identical expression direction may be biologically inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A downstream differential-expression interpretation step that intersects per-cluster COVID-vs-healthy biomarker lists from scNovel-discovered novel Macrophage clusters to retain only genes with consistent differential expression across all dependent clusters, reproducing the Figure 6H gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: A downstream differential-expression interpretation step that intersects per-cluster COVID-vs-healthy biomarker lists from scNovel-discovered novel Macrophage clusters to retain only genes with consistent differential expression across all dependent clusters, reproducing the Figure 6H gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single cell cluster is under analysis — the cross-cluster intersection that defines consistency is undefined The goal is pathway or GO enrichment of DE genes rather than identifying genes consistently differentially expressed across related clusters Cell clusters were not detected as related novel subtypes (e.g., they are unrelated reference cell types), so requiring identical expression direction may be biologically inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized cell-by-gene scRNA-seq or ST matrix and a list of gene sets, and need to decide which pathways are truly coordinated among cells without clustering, before pathway scoring or binarization.
skills.name: gene-set-coordination-testing
skills.search_text: gene-set-coordination-testing Use when you have a normalized cell-by-gene scRNA-seq or ST matrix and a list of gene sets, and need to decide which pathways are truly coordinated among cells without clustering, before pathway scoring or binarization. Targeted gene panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' If downstream goal is cell-type specificity scoring of already-annotated spots rather than coordination testing — compute.spec is the appropriate tool If pathway activity per cell (not coordination) is already established and only scoring speed matters — AUCell may be faster on small datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster-free statistical test of whether a gene set/pathway is heterogeneous (coordinated) among cells: cells and genes are co-embedded by multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) and the density of pathway genes in the latent space is compared against the all-gene background with KL-divergence and size-matched random-set permutation nulls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Cluster-free statistical test of whether a gene set/pathway is heterogeneous (coordinated) among cells: cells and genes are co-embedded by multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) and the density of pathway genes in the latent space is compared against the all-gene background with KL-divergence and size-matched random-set permutation nulls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeted gene panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' If downstream goal is cell-type specificity scoring of already-annotated spots rather than coordination testing — compute.spec is the appropriate tool If pathway activity per cell (not coordination) is already established and only scoring speed matters — AUCell may be faster on small datasets

skills.description: Use when a list of gene symbols — especially one recovered from Excel date-conversion errors (Mar-01, Mar-02) — must be functionally annotated via GO Biological Processes enrichment, with terms filtered at adjusted p < 0.05.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a list of gene symbols — especially one recovered from Excel date-conversion errors (Mar-01, Mar-02) — must be functionally annotated via GO Biological Processes enrichment, with terms filtered at adjusted p < 0.05. The gene list still contains unresolved Excel date terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) or old gene symbols — run Gene Updater first, since Enrichr requires current gene symbols The input is a full ranked expression matrix rather than a discrete gene list of converted genes (GSEA-style ranking, not over-representation, is indicated) The question targets pathway sets outside GO Biological Processes (e.g. Reactome) without a stated GO BP query http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Over-representation analysis of a gene list (here, Excel date-converted genes such as Mar-01/MARCHF1) against the Gene Ontology Biological Processes database using the Enrichr tool, ranking returned terms by adjusted p-value to identify which biological processes the genes modulate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
skills.summary: Over-representation analysis of a gene list (here, Excel date-converted genes such as Mar-01/MARCHF1) against the Gene Ontology Biological Processes database using the Enrichr tool, ranking returned terms by adjusted p-value to identify which biological processes the genes modulate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list still contains unresolved Excel date terms (Mar-01, Mar-02) or old gene symbols — run Gene Updater first, since Enrichr requires current gene symbols The input is a full ranked expression matrix rather than a discrete gene list of converted genes (GSEA-style ranking, not over-representation, is indicated) The question targets pathway sets outside GO Biological Processes (e.g. Reactome) without a stated GO BP query

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked gene list (e.g. FDR-ranked conditionTest DE genes from a multi-condition trajectory analysis) and need to interpret which biological pathways explain between-condition differences.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a ranked gene list (e.g. FDR-ranked conditionTest DE genes from a multi-condition trajectory analysis) and need to interpret which biological pathways explain between-condition differences. Input is a raw count matrix with no prior gene-level differential expression ranking — run tradeSeq conditionTest first to obtain the ranked DE list The system is steady-state rather than a dynamic trajectory: cluster-based differential abundance methods (milo, DAseq) rather than trajectory-informed DE plus enrichment are the appropriate comparison frame http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run gene-set enrichment (fgsea-style) on the ranked list of condition-specific differentially expressed genes produced by tradeSeq's conditionTest to recover biological processes (e.g. adhesion and locomotion in the TGF-β EMT case study) underlying trajectory-level condition differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Run gene-set enrichment (fgsea-style) on the ranked list of condition-specific differentially expressed genes produced by tradeSeq's conditionTest to recover biological processes (e.g. adhesion and locomotion in the TGF-β EMT case study) underlying trajectory-level condition differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix with no prior gene-level differential expression ranking — run tradeSeq conditionTest first to obtain the ranked DE list The system is steady-state rather than a dynamic trajectory: cluster-based differential abundance methods (milo, DAseq) rather than trajectory-informed DE plus enrichment are the appropriate comparison frame

skills.description: Use when you have differential expression results from the curatedAdipoArray 3T3-L1 microarray data (e.g., Pparg knockdown) and need to rank all genes by decreasing log fold-change to identify significantly enriched GO terms via GSEA rather than overlap-based ORA.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have differential expression results from the curatedAdipoArray 3T3-L1 microarray data (e.g., Pparg knockdown) and need to rank all genes by decreasing log fold-change to identify significantly enriched GO terms via GSEA rather than overlap-based ORA. The input is raw probe intensities or unprocessed microarray data rather than differential expression results — data curation/normalization (limma, sva batch removal) must happen first. The analysis target is the RNA-Seq (curatedAdipoRNA) or ChIP-Seq (curatedAdipoChIP) datasets, whose RangedSummarizedExperiment objects require differential expression/peak-calling before enrichment. You need over-representation analysis (ORA) on a small pre-defined DE gene list rather than GSEA on a full fold-change-ranked list. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Runs Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) on a fold-change-ranked gene list from MDI-induced 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data to detect enriched Gene Ontology terms under perturbation, using clusterProfiler with mouse GO annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Runs Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) on a fold-change-ranked gene list from MDI-induced 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data to detect enriched Gene Ontology terms under perturbation, using clusterProfiler with mouse GO annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw probe intensities or unprocessed microarray data rather than differential expression results — data curation/normalization (limma, sva batch removal) must happen first. The analysis target is the RNA-Seq (curatedAdipoRNA) or ChIP-Seq (curatedAdipoChIP) datasets, whose RangedSummarizedExperiment objects require differential expression/peak-calling before enrichment. You need over-representation analysis (ORA) on a small pre-defined DE gene list rather than GSEA on a full fold-change-ranked list.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (from a text list, microarray study, or clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to find statistically enriched gene modules linked to environmental factors such as cigarette smoking, diet, infections, or toxic chemicals.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (from a text list, microarray study, or clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to find statistically enriched gene modules linked to environmental factors such as cigarette smoking, diet, infections, or toxic chemicals. When the query is not a gene list but raw sequencing reads, SNPs, CNVs or DNA methylation data — E.PAGE does not yet cover these genetic data types When you need environmental associations outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals), unless supplying custom annotations/database When only differential expression between conditions (not enrichment against a curated module set) is the goal — use process_input_seurat/DE tools directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Over-representation enrichment of a query gene list against a curated environmental gene-module database (E.PATH: 4 environmental factors, 522 modules, 25,789 genes), using Fisher exact/hypergeometric tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, implemented in the E.PAGE R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-21988-6
skills.summary: Over-representation enrichment of a query gene list against a curated environmental gene-module database (E.PATH: 4 environmental factors, 522 modules, 25,789 genes), using Fisher exact/hypergeometric tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, implemented in the E.PAGE R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query is not a gene list but raw sequencing reads, SNPs, CNVs or DNA methylation data — E.PAGE does not yet cover these genetic data types When you need environmental associations outside the four curated factors (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals), unless supplying custom annotations/database When only differential expression between conditions (not enrichment against a curated module set) is the goal — use process_input_seurat/DE tools directly instead

skills.description: Use when you have per-factor gene rankings from a trained multi-omics factor model (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq) and need to interpret latent factors biologically by testing their top genes for enrichment against curated gene set databases.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have per-factor gene rankings from a trained multi-omics factor model (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq) and need to interpret latent factors biologically by testing their top genes for enrichment against curated gene set databases. Input is a ranked gene list of arbitrary length rather than the top 150 genes per factor derived from normalized H(rna) rows The factors have not yet been trained (e.g., no Mowgli embedding/loading matrices exist) — factor training must precede enrichment Enrichment is needed for peaks (chromatin accessibility) rather than genes — use Signac's FindMotifs on the top 100 peaks per factor with the JASPAR2022 database instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functional annotation of Mowgli factor loadings: the top 150 genes per latent factor (rows of H(rna) normalized to 1) are submitted as unordered gene lists to the gProfiler API via Scanpy's enrich to identify enriched GO:CC/MF/BP, Azimuth, and Immune SigDB gene sets that give each factor a biological identity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Functional annotation of Mowgli factor loadings: the top 150 genes per latent factor (rows of H(rna) normalized to 1) are submitted as unordered gene lists to the gProfiler API via Scanpy's enrich to identify enriched GO:CC/MF/BP, Azimuth, and Immune SigDB gene sets that give each factor a biological identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a ranked gene list of arbitrary length rather than the top 150 genes per factor derived from normalized H(rna) rows The factors have not yet been trained (e.g., no Mowgli embedding/loading matrices exist) — factor training must precede enrichment Enrichment is needed for peaks (chromatin accessibility) rather than genes — use Signac's FindMotifs on the top 100 peaks per factor with the JASPAR2022 database instead

skills.description: Use when a DMC (differentially methylated CpG) list from a 450K/EPIC Illumina array analysis needs to be translated into enriched biological pathways with per-database enrichment statistics.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a DMC (differentially methylated CpG) list from a 450K/EPIC Illumina array analysis needs to be translated into enriched biological pathways with per-database enrichment statistics. Input is raw IDAT methylation array data — this module operates downstream on an already-derived DMC list, not on raw files Input is a normalized beta value table (testDataFile2), which is intended for MDS/PCA modules rather than pathway enrichment The goal is genomic-feature or GO functional annotation rather than KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation or GSEA http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Perform pathway-level biological interpretation downstream of differential methylation by running over-representation and gene-set enrichment analysis against KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways databases within methylR's shiny GUI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad184
skills.summary: Perform pathway-level biological interpretation downstream of differential methylation by running over-representation and gene-set enrichment analysis against KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways databases within methylR's shiny GUI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw IDAT methylation array data — this module operates downstream on an already-derived DMC list, not on raw files Input is a normalized beta value table (testDataFile2), which is intended for MDS/PCA modules rather than pathway enrichment The goal is genomic-feature or GO functional annotation rather than KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation or GSEA

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq cluster (e.g., a Leiden cluster from Cellar) needs a cell-type label and differential expression has yielded ranked genes that must be interpreted against GO, KEGG, or MSigDB functional gene sets.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq cluster (e.g., a Leiden cluster from Cellar) needs a cell-type label and differential expression has yielded ranked genes that must be interpreted against GO, KEGG, or MSigDB functional gene sets. When differential expression has not yet been performed — the input must already be a ranked list of DE genes, not a raw count matrix or cell-by-gene AnnData object When assigning cell types based on known canonical markers alone (e.g., SLC5A12 for Proximal Tubule), where marker intersection suffices and no functional gene-set testing is needed When cluster labels already exist from reference-based label transfer (e.g., scanpy Ingest) and no functional interpretation of the clusters is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functional enrichment of cluster marker genes to assign cell types: after differential expression with diffxpy, the top 500 DE genes by fold-change are tested against GO, KEGG, and MSigDB gene sets with GSEApy, producing a q-value-sorted enrichment table that supports cell-type annotation of Cellar clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Functional enrichment of cluster marker genes to assign cell types: after differential expression with diffxpy, the top 500 DE genes by fold-change are tested against GO, KEGG, and MSigDB gene sets with GSEApy, producing a q-value-sorted enrichment table that supports cell-type annotation of Cellar clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When differential expression has not yet been performed — the input must already be a ranked list of DE genes, not a raw count matrix or cell-by-gene AnnData object When assigning cell types based on known canonical markers alone (e.g., SLC5A12 for Proximal Tubule), where marker intersection suffices and no functional gene-set testing is needed When cluster labels already exist from reference-based label transfer (e.g., scanpy Ingest) and no functional interpretation of the clusters is required

skills.description: Use when you have a selected gene list (e.g. RMT signal genes from Zeisel mouse cortex or Kang PBMC data) plus a discarded list, and need to test over-representation of biological gene sets against the full gene universe.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a selected gene list (e.g. RMT signal genes from Zeisel mouse cortex or Kang PBMC data) plus a discarded list, and need to test over-representation of biological gene sets against the full gene universe. You only have raw single-cell expression matrices and have not yet run the RMT feature-selection step that separates selected signal genes from discarded genes Your question is about differential expression between cell types rather than over-representation of a fixed gene list against a defined background http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Hypergeometric over-representation analysis that tests whether genes selected by the Randomly RMT feature-selection step enrich for tissue- or phenotype-specific gene sets (GO/Reactome terms) rather than generic ones, reported as p values converted to FDR q values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Hypergeometric over-representation analysis that tests whether genes selected by the Randomly RMT feature-selection step enrich for tissue- or phenotype-specific gene sets (GO/Reactome terms) rather than generic ones, reported as p values converted to FDR q values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw single-cell expression matrices and have not yet run the RMT feature-selection step that separates selected signal genes from discarded genes Your question is about differential expression between cell types rather than over-representation of a fixed gene list against a defined background

skills.description: Use when you have ranked gene-level differential expression statistics (e.g., edgeR log2-fold-changes between two cell clones or conditions) and want to know which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched at FDR < 0.05.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have ranked gene-level differential expression statistics (e.g., edgeR log2-fold-changes between two cell clones or conditions) and want to know which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched at FDR < 0.05. Input is raw counts without a fitted contrast — camera needs ranked gene-level statistics (e.g., edgeR log2-fold-changes) between defined groups, not an unlabeled expression matrix. The goal is calling or genotyping clonal mtDNA variants (MQuad/cellSNP/vireoSNP pipeline), not interpreting downstream pathway biology of an existing DE result. You need genome-wide pathway discovery beyond the 50 Hallmark sets — this skill is scoped to the fixed MSigDB Hallmark collection used in the paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Test curated gene sets for enrichment among differential-expression statistics using the limma camera method, with IHW-based multiple-testing correction. In the MQuad fibroblast case this identifies Hallmark pathways (MYC targets, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, ROS) distinguishing mtDNA-defined subclones MT0 vs MT1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Test curated gene sets for enrichment among differential-expression statistics using the limma camera method, with IHW-based multiple-testing correction. In the MQuad fibroblast case this identifies Hallmark pathways (MYC targets, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, ROS) distinguishing mtDNA-defined subclones MT0 vs MT1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts without a fitted contrast — camera needs ranked gene-level statistics (e.g., edgeR log2-fold-changes) between defined groups, not an unlabeled expression matrix. The goal is calling or genotyping clonal mtDNA variants (MQuad/cellSNP/vireoSNP pipeline), not interpreting downstream pathway biology of an existing DE result. You need genome-wide pathway discovery beyond the 50 Hallmark sets — this skill is scoped to the fixed MSigDB Hallmark collection used in the paper.

skills.description: Use when you have CMScaller-classified (CMS1–CMS4) organoid, PDX or cell-line expression data and need to confirm the subtypes recapitulate known CMS biology (CMS2 HNF4A/MYC/WNT, CMS3 CDX2/metabolic, CMS4 TGFβ/EMT) via gene set enrichment.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have CMScaller-classified (CMS1–CMS4) organoid, PDX or cell-line expression data and need to confirm the subtypes recapitulate known CMS biology (CMS2 HNF4A/MYC/WNT, CMS3 CDX2/metabolic, CMS4 TGFβ/EMT) via gene set enrichment. Samples whose human stromal composition differs from primary CRCs, e.g. metastatic CRC biopsies — CMScaller in its current implementation is not recommended for such samples Datasets with fewer than approximately forty samples — centering/scaling inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty in small datasets Single-cell RNA-seq data — exceedingly noisy and not what CMScaller/CMSgsa is optimized for http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs CMScaller's CMSgsa/Camera gene set analysis — built on the limma camera rotation test — on center-and-scaled expression matrices of CMScaller-classified pre-clinical colorectal cancer models to test enrichment of CMS-informative (cancer cell-intrinsic) gene sets per subtype. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Runs CMScaller's CMSgsa/Camera gene set analysis — built on the limma camera rotation test — on center-and-scaled expression matrices of CMScaller-classified pre-clinical colorectal cancer models to test enrichment of CMS-informative (cancer cell-intrinsic) gene sets per subtype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples whose human stromal composition differs from primary CRCs, e.g. metastatic CRC biopsies — CMScaller in its current implementation is not recommended for such samples Datasets with fewer than approximately forty samples — centering/scaling inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty in small datasets Single-cell RNA-seq data — exceedingly noisy and not what CMScaller/CMSgsa is optimized for

skills.description: Use when a list of discriminatively selected marker genes needs functional/annotation validation against a curated tissue and cell-type gene-set library such as HuBMAP ASCT+B, or when comparing marker-selection methods by enrichment q values.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a list of discriminatively selected marker genes needs functional/annotation validation against a curated tissue and cell-type gene-set library such as HuBMAP ASCT+B, or when comparing marker-selection methods by enrichment q values. Input is raw expression data rather than an already-selected marker gene list — marker selection (e.g., GreedyPC at coverage 8) must be performed first. The target annotation library is not a tissue/cell-type marker set compatible with Enrichr libraries (e.g., no ASCT+B-equivalent terms to aggregate q values over). The goal is deconvolution of pseudo-bulk mixtures rather than annotation-level validation of marker specificity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates G-PC-selected marker genes by submitting the coverage-8 marker list to Enrichr (via GSEApy) against the HuBMAP ASCT+B marker library, then aggregates adjusted q values at tissue/cell-type-pair, tissue, and cell-type levels to benchmark against decision-tree markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Validates G-PC-selected marker genes by submitting the coverage-8 marker list to Enrichr (via GSEApy) against the HuBMAP ASCT+B marker library, then aggregates adjusted q values at tissue/cell-type-pair, tissue, and cell-type levels to benchmark against decision-tree markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw expression data rather than an already-selected marker gene list — marker selection (e.g., GreedyPC at coverage 8) must be performed first. The target annotation library is not a tissue/cell-type marker set compatible with Enrichr libraries (e.g., no ASCT+B-equivalent terms to aggregate q values over). The goal is deconvolution of pseudo-bulk mixtures rather than annotation-level validation of marker specificity.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of mouse gene sets (e.g., co-expression modules or GEPs from SingleCellGGM) and need to test which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched at p <= 0.05.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a list of mouse gene sets (e.g., co-expression modules or GEPs from SingleCellGGM) and need to test which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched at p <= 0.05. Gene IDs are not Ensembl gene IDs and cannot be mapped — ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis states 'Only Ensembl gene IDs are supported.' Analyzing non-mouse gene sets — the bundled GO (Ensembl BioMart) and MP (MGI) annotations are mouse-specific. The task is cell-type annotation or label transfer with the GEPs (use CellGEP/cellgep instead of enrichment testing). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Perform over-representation testing of GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) terms for mouse gene co-expression modules (e.g., SingleCellGGM-derived GEPs) using the ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis R functions, which apply a hypergeometric test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and report enrichment ratios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Perform over-representation testing of GO and Mouse Phenotype (MP) terms for mouse gene co-expression modules (e.g., SingleCellGGM-derived GEPs) using the ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis R functions, which apply a hypergeometric test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and report enrichment ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene IDs are not Ensembl gene IDs and cannot be mapped — ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis states 'Only Ensembl gene IDs are supported.' Analyzing non-mouse gene sets — the bundled GO (Ensembl BioMart) and MP (MGI) annotations are mouse-specific. The task is cell-type annotation or label transfer with the GEPs (use CellGEP/cellgep instead of enrichment testing).

skills.description: Use when genes ranked by an inferred latent process (e.g., Cyclum circular pseudotime match scores, or PCA components 1-2) must be validated against a curated gene set such as GO:0007049 to test whether the ranking captures cell-cycle biology.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-gsea
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-gsea Use when genes ranked by an inferred latent process (e.g., Cyclum circular pseudotime match scores, or PCA components 1-2) must be validated against a curated gene set such as GO:0007049 to test whether the ranking captures cell-cycle biology. The goal is assigning individual cells to cell-cycle phases from marker genes (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring or cyclone-style prediction) rather than validating a discovered gene ranking. The gene ranking comes from a non-periodic (linear) latent variable where a circular-manifold model like Cyclum is not the competing method. No curated gene set database (e.g., GO biological process) is available for enrichment testing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark ab-initio gene rankings from a circular-manifold model (Cyclum) against PCA-based rankings by running GSEA against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set and comparing normalized enrichment scores (NES). This validates that discovered genes capture periodic cell-cycle biology rather than generic linear variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Benchmark ab-initio gene rankings from a circular-manifold model (Cyclum) against PCA-based rankings by running GSEA against the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set and comparing normalized enrichment scores (NES). This validates that discovered genes capture periodic cell-cycle biology rather than generic linear variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assigning individual cells to cell-cycle phases from marker genes (e.g., Seurat::CellCycleScoring or cyclone-style prediction) rather than validating a discovered gene ranking. The gene ranking comes from a non-periodic (linear) latent variable where a circular-manifold model like Cyclum is not the competing method. No curated gene set database (e.g., GO biological process) is available for enrichment testing.

skills.summary: Compute functional spectra by scoring a gene expression profile against MSigDB gene sets (e.g., MSigDB v7 with 22,596 sets), converting gene-level expression into pathway-level enrichment features that feed DeepCC's classifier. This pathway activity transformation underpins platform independence and single-sample prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering of cancer patients rather than supervised classification — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification but not clustering. The input is already a pathway-level/functional spectrum feature table — recomputing enrichment scores would be redundant. Comprehensive gene set prior knowledge (e.g., subtype-characteristic pathways) is unavailable, since biased or incomplete gene sets introduce potential bias.

skills.description: Use when annotating clusters in a Seurat scRNA-seq object against a heterogeneous catalog of variable-sized cell-type marker gene sets, and you need bias-corrected per-cluster enrichment scores with statistical significance calls.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-scoring Use when annotating clusters in a Seurat scRNA-seq object against a heterogeneous catalog of variable-sized cell-type marker gene sets, and you need bias-corrected per-cluster enrichment scores with statistical significance calls. The input is not a clustered single-cell expression object but a bulk or pre-aggregated feature table — Miko scoring operates per cell on scRNA-seq data via Seurat You need fully automated per-cell annotation without a curated marker catalog — marker-based annotations are only as good as the cell-type assigned to the source dataset The marker sets are derived from the same atlas being annotated — the workflow explicitly excludes such sets to avoid circularity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 The Miko scoring pipeline (scMiko) scores single-cell data against cell-type-specific marker gene sets in a three-step workflow — nullScore(), mikoScore(), sigScore() — that corrects for gene set-size bias, then applies hypothesis testing plus coherence and frequent-flier filters to accept or reject candidate cell-type annotations. It benchmarked at AUROC 0.776 against author-curated labels, outperforming GSVA (0.705) and SCINA (0.603). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: The Miko scoring pipeline (scMiko) scores single-cell data against cell-type-specific marker gene sets in a three-step workflow — nullScore(), mikoScore(), sigScore() — that corrects for gene set-size bias, then applies hypothesis testing plus coherence and frequent-flier filters to accept or reject candidate cell-type annotations. It benchmarked at AUROC 0.776 against author-curated labels, outperforming GSVA (0.705) and SCINA (0.603).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a clustered single-cell expression object but a bulk or pre-aggregated feature table — Miko scoring operates per cell on scRNA-seq data via Seurat You need fully automated per-cell annotation without a curated marker catalog — marker-based annotations are only as good as the cell-type assigned to the source dataset The marker sets are derived from the same atlas being annotated — the workflow explicitly excludes such sets to avoid circularity

skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-summary-statistics-testing Use when you have per-gene DE summary statistics (e.g., z-scores from MAST/SCDE/zingeR) plus gene set annotations and need a calibrated p-value testing whether each gene set is enriched in differentially expressed genes. You only have raw scRNA-seq count matrices and no DE summary statistics — iDEA requires summary statistics output from existing DE tools and does not model individual-level data. You need p-values that explicitly account for gene set overlap/non-independence — iDEA does not account for this; use the permutation-based iDEA.fit.null / iDEA.FDR workflow instead for FDR estimation. A gene set is below the coverage threshold (min_precent_annot default 0.0025) or too few DE genes exist (min_degene = 5), making enrichment testing unstable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Calibrated gene set enrichment testing from DE summary statistics using iDEA: an EM-MCMC fit of a hierarchical Bayesian model per gene set, with the Louis missing-information correction to obtain valid enrichment p-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Calibrated gene set enrichment testing from DE summary statistics using iDEA: an EM-MCMC fit of a hierarchical Bayesian model per gene set, with the Louis missing-information correction to obtain valid enrichment p-values.

You need p-values that explicitly account for gene set overlap/non-independence — iDEA does not account for this; use the permutation-based iDEA.fit.null / iDEA.FDR workflow instead for FDR estimation. A gene set is below the coverage threshold (min_precent_annot default 0.0025) or too few DE genes exist (min_degene = 5), making enrichment testing unstable.

skills.description: Use when a fitted topic model (e.g., CODAL/MIRA β matrix) yields a ranked gene list and you need to test overrepresentation of a curated cell-type ontology set — e.g., HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte membership — among the top-ranked genes.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-testing-via-fishers-exact-test
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-testing-via-fishers-exact-test Use when a fitted topic model (e.g., CODAL/MIRA β matrix) yields a ranked gene list and you need to test overrepresentation of a curated cell-type ontology set — e.g., HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte membership — among the top-ranked genes. The gene ranking is not from an interpretable topic/β matrix — e.g., input is already a feature table or differential-expression list where a dedicated overrepresentation tool is more appropriate. The query gene set is not defined against a fixed universe of modeled genes (contingency table requires a well-defined background of all remaining modeled genes). You need batch-corrected latent representations or batch-confounded cell-state detection rather than set-enrichment statistics — use CODAL's disentangling workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether a ranked gene set (e.g., the top 200 genes associated with a CODAL/MIRA topic, ranked by their β-matrix weight) is significantly overrepresented for members of a curated ontology set, using a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 contingency table. Used here to confirm Topic 14 captures the HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte identity program (p = 1.5e-19). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Tests whether a ranked gene set (e.g., the top 200 genes associated with a CODAL/MIRA topic, ranked by their β-matrix weight) is significantly overrepresented for members of a curated ontology set, using a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2x2 contingency table. Used here to confirm Topic 14 captures the HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte identity program (p = 1.5e-19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene ranking is not from an interpretable topic/β matrix — e.g., input is already a feature table or differential-expression list where a dedicated overrepresentation tool is more appropriate. The query gene set is not defined against a fixed universe of modeled genes (contingency table requires a well-defined background of all remaining modeled genes). You need batch-corrected latent representations or batch-confounded cell-state detection rather than set-enrichment statistics — use CODAL's disentangling workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when computing PC1/SVD-based gene set (module) activity from a normalized expression matrix and you must remove aberrant genes that would distort the percentage of variance explained by PC1 (L1) before scoring module activity.

skills.search_text: gene-set-outlier-thresholding Use when computing PC1/SVD-based gene set (module) activity from a normalized expression matrix and you must remove aberrant genes that would distort the percentage of variance explained by PC1 (L1) before scoring module activity. Input data is not yet normalized — rRoma requires normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before filtering The expression matrix contains missing values that have not been imputed — imputation via the mice package / FillNAMethod should happen first, or use datasets with no NAs The analysis goal is sample-level (not gene-level) quality control — sample outlier detection is a separate two-step procedure based on number of detected genes and PCA projection in gene space http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A leave-one-out outlier-gene filtering procedure from rROMA that protects PC1-based gene set activity scores: each gene is temporarily removed, L1 (variance explained by PC1) is recomputed, and genes whose removal abnormally shifts the L1 distribution are flagged via z-score thresholding and excluded with Fisher-test and rarity safeguards. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: A leave-one-out outlier-gene filtering procedure from rROMA that protects PC1-based gene set activity scores: each gene is temporarily removed, L1 (variance explained by PC1) is recomputed, and genes whose removal abnormally shifts the L1 distribution are flagged via z-score thresholding and excluded with Fisher-test and rarity safeguards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not yet normalized — rRoma requires normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before filtering The expression matrix contains missing values that have not been imputed — imputation via the mice package / FillNAMethod should happen first, or use datasets with no NAs The analysis goal is sample-level (not gene-level) quality control — sample outlier detection is a separate two-step procedure based on number of detected genes and PCA projection in gene space

skills.search_text: gene-set-overlap-jaccard-analysis Use when comparing significant gene-set or DE gene call lists from two or more enrichment/DE methods and you need a set-level concordance metric to confirm that a more method's extra hits are consistent with existing calls. When you only have p-value distributions and no discrete call sets — use genomic control (lambda_gc) or FDR curves instead When gene sets have wildly different sizes and overlap is dominated by large annotated sets; the article notes iDEA does not explicitly account for gene set overlap causing non-independence among gene sets When comparing methods run on different inputs or annotations — Jaccard is only interpretable when all methods share the same zingeR summary statistics and gene set universe http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify the pairwise Jaccard overlap between significant gene sets (or DE genes) reported by competing enrichment/DE methods, to measure how concordant their discoveries are. skills.summary: Functional interpretation step of gExcite's GEX analysis layer, in which the embedded scAmpi Snakemake module runs pathway enrichment on the gene expression matrix after QC, normalisation, clustering, cell type classification, and DE analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is ADT/CITE-seq or hashing data only, with no gene expression counts — gExcite routes those samples through the ADT analysis and hashing deconvolution branches instead Clusters and differentially expressed genes have not yet been computed — pathway enrichment in this pipeline depends on the completed scAmpi_basic QC, clustering, and DE analysis steps The workflow cannot run on the target system — gExcite is compatible with and tested on Linux only; other Unix systems including MacOS are not supported
