skills.description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix (RNA-seq cpm/vst or proteomics) plus gene sets (GMT/MSigDB or custom signatures) and need per-sample module activity scores with statistical significance.
skills.name: gene-set-pca-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-set-pca-activity-scoring Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix (RNA-seq cpm/vst or proteomics) plus gene sets (GMT/MSigDB or custom signatures) and need per-sample module activity scores with statistical significance. The expression matrix is raw counts or otherwise unnormalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data before PC1 computation The question is differential expression of individual genes rather than coordinated module/sample-level activity — DE tools like edgeR/DESeq2 testing are the wrong instrument Datasets contain many missing values that have not been pre-imputed — the README recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantify gene-set (module) activity in a normalized omics expression matrix by computing the first principal component (PC1) of each gene set with rROMA, and assess significance of shifted vs over-dispersed modules against random gene-set null distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Quantify gene-set (module) activity in a normalized omics expression matrix by computing the first principal component (PC1) of each gene set with rROMA, and assess significance of shifted vs over-dispersed modules against random gene-set null distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw counts or otherwise unnormalized — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data before PC1 computation The question is differential expression of individual genes rather than coordinated module/sample-level activity — DE tools like edgeR/DESeq2 testing are the wrong instrument Datasets contain many missing values that have not been pre-imputed — the README recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate a gene-set-scoring cell-type annotation pipeline — i.e., measure how annotation accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) degrades as marker sets are corrupted with random genes at increasing replacement rates.
skills.name: gene-set-permutation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gene-set-permutation-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively validate a gene-set-scoring cell-type annotation pipeline — i.e., measure how annotation accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) degrades as marker sets are corrupted with random genes at increasing replacement rates. Your goal is annotating a new dataset with trusted, unmodified marker sets — this skill is a benchmarking exercise with deliberately degraded gene sets, not a production annotation workflow. You lack author-curated (ground-truth) cell-type labels, since benchmarkScores() sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed against reference annotations. The task is comparing alternative automated annotation tools (e.g., ScType) rather than stress-testing the Miko scoring pipeline itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark the sensitivity and specificity of Miko score-based cell-type annotation by degrading cell-type-specific marker gene sets with 0%, 25% and 50% random-gene permutation and comparing called annotations against author-curated labels, as done for the mouse gastrulation dataset (Pijuan-Sala et al.) in scPipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Benchmark the sensitivity and specificity of Miko score-based cell-type annotation by degrading cell-type-specific marker gene sets with 0%, 25% and 50% random-gene permutation and comparing called annotations against author-curated labels, as done for the mouse gastrulation dataset (Pijuan-Sala et al.) in scPipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is annotating a new dataset with trusted, unmodified marker sets — this skill is a benchmarking exercise with deliberately degraded gene sets, not a production annotation workflow. You lack author-curated (ground-truth) cell-type labels, since benchmarkScores() sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed against reference annotations. The task is comparing alternative automated annotation tools (e.g., ScType) rather than stress-testing the Miko scoring pipeline itself.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq expression data with case/control group labels (e.g. GEO GSE172114) must be mapped onto extracted network submodules and compared for perturbation strength via source-sink path ACEs and Bonferroni-combined P-values plus DEG counts.
skills.name: gene-set-perturbation-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-perturbation-analysis Use when RNA-seq expression data with case/control group labels (e.g. GEO GSE172114) must be mapped onto extracted network submodules and compared for perturbation strength via source-sink path ACEs and Bonferroni-combined P-values plus DEG counts. Data are not high-throughput gene expression with a binary case/control grouping — SEMrun/SEMac perturbation testing requires a group vector to contrast conditions The input graph is already a perturbation result table; this skill operates on igraph network modules, not on precomputed pathway enrichment tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies condition-specific perturbation of graph/pathway modules with SEMgraph: SEMace() computes Average Causal Effects (ACEs) over source2sink paths at alpha=0.05, and SEMgsa() ranks perturbed gene sets via 5000-permutation SEM-based testing, yielding ACEs%, PVAL(E)/PVAL(V), and No.DEGs per subnetwork. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Quantifies condition-specific perturbation of graph/pathway modules with SEMgraph: SEMace() computes Average Causal Effects (ACEs) over source2sink paths at alpha=0.05, and SEMgsa() ranks perturbed gene sets via 5000-permutation SEM-based testing, yielding ACEs%, PVAL(E)/PVAL(V), and No.DEGs per subnetwork.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not high-throughput gene expression with a binary case/control grouping — SEMrun/SEMac perturbation testing requires a group vector to contrast conditions The input graph is already a perturbation result table; this skill operates on igraph network modules, not on precomputed pathway enrichment tables

skills.description: Use when building or applying a ProjectSVR reference model: you need a gene-set (signature) score matrix — e.g., from cNMF-derived or overexpression-tested gene sets, top 25 genes per set — as regression input features.
skills.name: gene-set-score-computation
skills.search_text: gene-set-score-computation Use when building or applying a ProjectSVR reference model: you need a gene-set (signature) score matrix — e.g., from cNMF-derived or overexpression-tested gene sets, top 25 genes per set — as regression input features. The downstream task requires differential expression or marker testing itself rather than per-cell signature scoring — use overexpression testing only to define the gene sets, not as the scoring method The analysis goal is unsupervised dimension reduction/clustering rather than supervised reference mapping against a pre-built embedding Only a small number of highly variable genes (not curated gene sets) are intended as model features — ProjectSVR is designed around gene signature score matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell gene signature/activity scores (e.g., with AUCell rank-based scoring) from a gene set matrix so that reference mapping models like ProjectSVR can learn the relationship between signature scores and reference embedding coordinates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Compute per-cell gene signature/activity scores (e.g., with AUCell rank-based scoring) from a gene set matrix so that reference mapping models like ProjectSVR can learn the relationship between signature scores and reference embedding coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream task requires differential expression or marker testing itself rather than per-cell signature scoring — use overexpression testing only to define the gene sets, not as the scoring method The analysis goal is unsupervised dimension reduction/clustering rather than supervised reference mapping against a pre-built embedding Only a small number of highly variable genes (not curated gene sets) are intended as model features — ProjectSVR is designed around gene signature score matrices

skills.description: Use when you have bulk genes-by-samples expression matrices (microarray or RNAseq, e.g. pdacR $ex objects) with sample-level tissue metadata, and you need per-sample gene-set scores to compare signature activity across compartments like normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, and metastases.
skills.name: gene-set-score-computation-across-bulk-transcriptomic-datasets
skills.search_text: gene-set-score-computation-across-bulk-transcriptomic-datasets Use when you have bulk genes-by-samples expression matrices (microarray or RNAseq, e.g. pdacR $ex objects) with sample-level tissue metadata, and you need per-sample gene-set scores to compare signature activity across compartments like normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, and metastases. The goal is tumor-cell-intrinsic subtyping (e.g. PurIST or basal-like/classical classification) rather than attributing signature expression to non-tumor tissue compartments — normal pancreas and CAF contamination will inflate ADEX/Exocrine scores in tumor datasets Input is single-cell data (e.g. the rmoffitt/scOh Seurat .rds atlas) rather than bulk $ex matrices — scoring conventions and grouping by tissue-of-origin tracks do not transfer directly Datasets lack sample-level tissue-of-origin metadata in sampInfo, making the Wilcoxon group comparisons undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-sample gene signature scores (ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) in bulk PDAC expression datasets by z-scoring each gene and averaging across signature members, then testing score differences between tissue-of-origin groups with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to attribute signature expression to specific tissue or cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Computes per-sample gene signature scores (ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) in bulk PDAC expression datasets by z-scoring each gene and averaging across signature members, then testing score differences between tissue-of-origin groups with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to attribute signature expression to specific tissue or cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is tumor-cell-intrinsic subtyping (e.g. PurIST or basal-like/classical classification) rather than attributing signature expression to non-tumor tissue compartments — normal pancreas and CAF contamination will inflate ADEX/Exocrine scores in tumor datasets Input is single-cell data (e.g. the rmoffitt/scOh Seurat .rds atlas) rather than bulk $ex matrices — scoring conventions and grouping by tissue-of-origin tracks do not transfer directly Datasets lack sample-level tissue-of-origin metadata in sampInfo, making the Wilcoxon group comparisons undefined

skills.description: Use when preparing representative single-cell reference data for scSemiProfiler's deep generative model, where raw normalized expression alone under-constrains in silico inference of target samples.
skills.name: gene-set-score-feature-augmentation
skills.search_text: gene-set-score-feature-augmentation Use when preparing representative single-cell reference data for scSemiProfiler's deep generative model, where raw normalized expression alone under-constrains in silico inference of target samples. When running pure bulk deconvolution tools (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS) that only need a signature gene matrix, not augmented single-cell features When no gene set reference collections (MSigDB / Ernst et al.) are available or the data are from a modality (e.g. proteomics) not covered by these gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Augments preprocessed single-cell expression matrices with gene set scores computed from all curated MSigDB and Ernst et al. gene sets, and reweights features by variance, to give the scSemiProfiler VAE-GAN biologically informative inputs beyond raw expression values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Augments preprocessed single-cell expression matrices with gene set scores computed from all curated MSigDB and Ernst et al. gene sets, and reweights features by variance, to give the scSemiProfiler VAE-GAN biologically informative inputs beyond raw expression values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running pure bulk deconvolution tools (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS) that only need a signature gene matrix, not augmented single-cell features When no gene set reference collections (MSigDB / Ernst et al.) are available or the data are from a modality (e.g. proteomics) not covered by these gene sets

skills.description: Use when preparing gene-by-gene-set annotation matrices (e.g. binary 0/1 data.frames from MSigDB or MGI GO GAF 2.0 files) as inputs for iDEA GSE analysis, and sparse sets below the size threshold must be removed first.
skills.name: gene-set-size-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-set-size-filtering Use when preparing gene-by-gene-set annotation matrices (e.g. binary 0/1 data.frames from MSigDB or MGI GO GAF 2.0 files) as inputs for iDEA GSE analysis, and sparse sets below the size threshold must be removed first. Gene set annotations are already provided as iDEA's packaged humanGeneSets/mouseGeneSets objects — do not re-download and re-prune The downstream GSE method expects full unfiltered pathway databases rather than iDEA's curated 12,033 gene sets Summary statistics use identifier types that cannot be mapped to gene symbols or MGI IDs, since pruning plus alignment requires matchable row names Prunes compiled gene-set/pathway annotation matrices (human MSigDB-derived sets and mouse GO annotations) by a minimum gene-set size threshold so that only gene sets large enough to be usable in iDEA's GSE analysis are retained. This prevents sparse, underpowered gene sets from entering downstream enrichment testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Prunes compiled gene-set/pathway annotation matrices (human MSigDB-derived sets and mouse GO annotations) by a minimum gene-set size threshold so that only gene sets large enough to be usable in iDEA's GSE analysis are retained. This prevents sparse, underpowered gene sets from entering downstream enrichment testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene set annotations are already provided as iDEA's packaged humanGeneSets/mouseGeneSets objects — do not re-download and re-prune The downstream GSE method expects full unfiltered pathway databases rather than iDEA's curated 12,033 gene sets Summary statistics use identifier types that cannot be mapped to gene symbols or MGI IDs, since pruning plus alignment requires matchable row names

skills.description: Use when scoring cell-type marker gene sets of widely varying sizes against scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., Miko scoring on a Cell Catalog or permuted marker sets) and raw enrichment scores must be corrected for gene set-size bias before significance calling.
skills.name: gene-set-size-null-model-fitting
skills.search_text: gene-set-size-null-model-fitting Use when scoring cell-type marker gene sets of widely varying sizes against scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., Miko scoring on a Cell Catalog or permuted marker sets) and raw enrichment scores must be corrected for gene set-size bias before significance calling. Input marker gene sets are all of nearly identical size and standardized scoring frameworks (e.g., GSVA, Seurat AddModuleScore) are already appropriate — the size-corrected null is designed for heterogeneous set sizes The goal is clustering or gene program discovery (SSN analysis) rather than marker-based cell-type annotation scoring Gene sets exceed the fitted size range (paper's null was fit for sizes 2–200 genes), so null expectations would be extrapolated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fits a gene set-size-dependent null model (via scMiko's nullScore()) that corrects for the bias whereby larger marker gene sets yield inflated enrichment scores, enabling fair comparison of variable-sized cell-type gene sets prior to Miko scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Fits a gene set-size-dependent null model (via scMiko's nullScore()) that corrects for the bias whereby larger marker gene sets yield inflated enrichment scores, enabling fair comparison of variable-sized cell-type gene sets prior to Miko scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input marker gene sets are all of nearly identical size and standardized scoring frameworks (e.g., GSVA, Seurat AddModuleScore) are already appropriate — the size-corrected null is designed for heterogeneous set sizes The goal is clustering or gene program discovery (SSN analysis) rather than marker-based cell-type annotation scoring Gene sets exceed the fitted size range (paper's null was fit for sizes 2–200 genes), so null expectations would be extrapolated

skills.description: Use when comparing gene-set scoring methods across multiple BP sets and you need overall plus Ngenes-stratified (e.g., Ngenes>200) summary statistics such as mean Pearson correlation.
skills.name: gene-set-size-stratified-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: gene-set-size-stratified-summary-statistics Use when comparing gene-set scoring methods across multiple BP sets and you need overall plus Ngenes-stratified (e.g., Ngenes>200) summary statistics such as mean Pearson correlation. Input is already a summary statistics table with no per-gene-set scores — no stratification can be recomputed Only a single gene set is available, making size-stratified or across-set correlation summaries meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derives summary metrics (e.g., mean Pearson correlations between scoring methods) across biological-process gene sets, and stratifies them by gene-set size (Ngenes), as done when comparing ORIGINS2, AUCell, and Average scores on the 17 BP PPIN sets in the TNBC single-cell sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Derives summary metrics (e.g., mean Pearson correlations between scoring methods) across biological-process gene sets, and stratifies them by gene-set size (Ngenes), as done when comparing ORIGINS2, AUCell, and Average scores on the 17 BP PPIN sets in the TNBC single-cell sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a summary statistics table with no per-gene-set scores — no stratification can be recomputed Only a single gene set is available, making size-stratified or across-set correlation summaries meaningless

skills.description: Use when validating a pathway activity scoring method's ability to detect spatially relevant gene sets, by benchmarking delta-KLD separation between true and random gene sets across simulated ST spatial organization patterns (hotspot, gradient, streak).
skills.name: gene-set-spatial-relevance-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gene-set-spatial-relevance-benchmarking Use when validating a pathway activity scoring method's ability to detect spatially relevant gene sets, by benchmarking delta-KLD separation between true and random gene sets across simulated ST spatial organization patterns (hotspot, gradient, streak). Input is targeted gene-panel ST data with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is explicitly not suitable and imputation of unmeasured genes is suggested but not implemented The goal is detecting coordinated (heterogeneous) gene sets in non-spatial scRNA-seq without a 2D spatial map — use the non-spatial compute.kld workflow instead Simulation of spatial patterns is not possible or no ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets exist to compare against random sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark whether a gene set activity scoring method (GSDensity PAL vs CelliD) can distinguish ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets from matched random gene sets in spatial transcriptomics data, using delta-KLD separation on simulated ST spatial patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Benchmark whether a gene set activity scoring method (GSDensity PAL vs CelliD) can distinguish ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets from matched random gene sets in spatial transcriptomics data, using delta-KLD separation on simulated ST spatial patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is targeted gene-panel ST data with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is explicitly not suitable and imputation of unmeasured genes is suggested but not implemented The goal is detecting coordinated (heterogeneous) gene sets in non-spatial scRNA-seq without a 2D spatial map — use the non-spatial compute.kld workflow instead Simulation of spatial patterns is not possible or no ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets exist to compare against random sets

skills.description: Use when you already have per-cell pathway activity weights (e.g. from run.rwr on an MCA co-embedding) and spot/cell group annotations, and need a numeric JSD-based score of how specific each gene set is to a cluster or anatomical annotation.
skills.name: gene-set-specificity-scoring-jsd
skills.search_text: gene-set-specificity-scoring-jsd Use when you already have per-cell pathway activity weights (e.g. from run.rwr on an MCA co-embedding) and spot/cell group annotations, and need a numeric JSD-based score of how specific each gene set is to a cluster or anatomical annotation. Data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Gene sets have not passed the coordination test (compute.kld adjusted p < 0.05); the article recommends downstream analyses only on coordinated gene sets No cell/cluster or spatial annotations exist to define cell_group, making a JSD specificity score undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify how cluster-restricted each coordinated gene set is using GSDensity's compute.spec, a Jensen-Shannon divergence based specificity score computed on pathway activity labels per cell group; used alongside spatial relevance to find high-order spatial organization that cluster-centric analysis misses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Quantify how cluster-restricted each coordinated gene set is using GSDensity's compute.spec, a Jensen-Shannon divergence based specificity score computed on pathway activity labels per cell group; used alongside spatial relevance to find high-order spatial organization that cluster-centric analysis misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Gene sets have not passed the coordination test (compute.kld adjusted p < 0.05); the article recommends downstream analyses only on coordinated gene sets No cell/cluster or spatial annotations exist to define cell_group, making a JSD specificity score undefined

skills.description: Use when you have gene programs (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs) with gene-level weights and want to identify putative upstream TF regulators by intersecting TF binding/potential scores with the program's TF weights.
skills.name: gene-set-transcription-factor-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-transcription-factor-enrichment-analysis Use when you have gene programs (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs) with gene-level weights and want to identify putative upstream TF regulators by intersecting TF binding/potential scores with the program's TF weights. The gene set has no associated weights, so TF membership cannot be cross-checked against program-level z-weights — plain Lisa regulatory-potential ranking alone can misprioritize (e.g., PPARG in MeC-37). No ChIP-seq data exist for the TF in the relevant cell-state context; binding must then be inferred from other cell lines and treated cautiously (as with GR for CXCL13+ Tfh). Prioritizes transcription factor (TF) regulators of MetaTiME meta-components (MeCs) by comparing Lisa2-predicted ChIP-seq regulatory potentials for the top genes of each MeC against the TF z-weights encoded in the pretrained MeC gene-weight table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Prioritizes transcription factor (TF) regulators of MetaTiME meta-components (MeCs) by comparing Lisa2-predicted ChIP-seq regulatory potentials for the top genes of each MeC against the TF z-weights encoded in the pretrained MeC gene-weight table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene set has no associated weights, so TF membership cannot be cross-checked against program-level z-weights — plain Lisa regulatory-potential ranking alone can misprioritize (e.g., PPARG in MeC-37). No ChIP-seq data exist for the TF in the relevant cell-state context; binding must then be inferred from other cell lines and treated cautiously (as with GR for CXCL13+ Tfh).

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells need pathway-level activity scores (e.g. MSigDB angiogenesis or a user GMT gene set) to flag pathway-high subpopulations within a tumor microenvironment.
skills.name: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring Use when scRNA-seq cells need pathway-level activity scores (e.g. MSigDB angiogenesis or a user GMT gene set) to flag pathway-high subpopulations within a tumor microenvironment. The analysis goal is marker-gene differential expression or cell-type annotation rather than pathway-level activity scoring — use scWizard's Seurat clustering or neural-network annotation modules instead. No predefined gene set exists (no MSigDB set or GMT file) and the pathway signature must be discovered de novo from the data. The input is already a per-cell or per-cluster feature/score table rather than raw or QC-filtered single-cell expression data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Per-cell gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scoring of single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g. the angiogenesis signature computed on the ICC tumor microenvironment dataset in the scWizard case study — to quantify pathway activity and rank cell populations such as Macro_NLRP3, Mono_CD14, and Arteries-like cells as angiogenesis-high. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Per-cell gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scoring of single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g. the angiogenesis signature computed on the ICC tumor microenvironment dataset in the scWizard case study — to quantify pathway activity and rank cell populations such as Macro_NLRP3, Mono_CD14, and Arteries-like cells as angiogenesis-high.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is marker-gene differential expression or cell-type annotation rather than pathway-level activity scoring — use scWizard's Seurat clustering or neural-network annotation modules instead. No predefined gene set exists (no MSigDB set or GMT file) and the pathway signature must be discovered de novo from the data. The input is already a per-cell or per-cluster feature/score table rather than raw or QC-filtered single-cell expression data.

skills.description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, .csv) and want gene-set-level activity scores (e.g. hypoxia/glycolysis) per sample to enable group comparisons, KM/Cox analysis or correlation of pathway activity.
skills.name: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, .csv) and want gene-set-level activity scores (e.g. hypoxia/glycolysis) per sample to enable group comparisons, KM/Cox analysis or correlation of pathway activity. The goal is gene-level differential expression analysis — ARMT uses edgeR on the raw counts matrix for DEGs, not GSVA scores You only need single-gene characteristics (survival, correlation for one gene) and no gene-set/pathway activity summary The expression matrix is already a gene-symbol TPM table and cannot be re-run through ARMT's Ensembl-ID-based normalization path http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-sample gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scores for arbitrary gene sets from RNA-seq expression data, as implemented in ARMT, converting gene sets (e.g. 22-gene glycolysis and 14-gene hypoxia signatures) into continuous per-sample activity values that feed downstream differential, survival and correlation analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Computes per-sample gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scores for arbitrary gene sets from RNA-seq expression data, as implemented in ARMT, converting gene sets (e.g. 22-gene glycolysis and 14-gene hypoxia signatures) into continuous per-sample activity values that feed downstream differential, survival and correlation analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-level differential expression analysis — ARMT uses edgeR on the raw counts matrix for DEGs, not GSVA scores You only need single-gene characteristics (survival, correlation for one gene) and no gene-set/pathway activity summary The expression matrix is already a gene-symbol TPM table and cannot be re-run through ARMT's Ensembl-ID-based normalization path

skills.description: Use when you have a gene set (TMGs/NMGs or other DEG-derived signature) and a matched expression-plus-phenotype matrix (e.g., 962 GDSC cancer cell lines x 265 compound IC50 values) and need a single signature-level score per sample to correlate with the phenotype.
skills.name: gene-signature-aggregate-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-signature-aggregate-scoring Use when you have a gene set (TMGs/NMGs or other DEG-derived signature) and a matched expression-plus-phenotype matrix (e.g., 962 GDSC cancer cell lines x 265 compound IC50 values) and need a single signature-level score per sample to correlate with the phenotype. The task is classifying individual single cells as malignant vs non-malignant — that requires PreCanCell_classifier(), not signature aggregate scoring Gene-level (per-gene) correlation output is required rather than a single signature-level score per sample The expression data are single-cell and unlabeled for cell type — PreCanCell_data()/PreCanCell_classifier() is the intended pipeline, not direct signature scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-sample aggregate expression scores for curated gene signatures (e.g., 73 tumor marker genes and 186 non-tumor marker genes derived as DEGs between malignant and non-malignant cells) and tests them against continuous phenotypes such as GDSC drug IC50 values via Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Computes per-sample aggregate expression scores for curated gene signatures (e.g., 73 tumor marker genes and 186 non-tumor marker genes derived as DEGs between malignant and non-malignant cells) and tests them against continuous phenotypes such as GDSC drug IC50 values via Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is classifying individual single cells as malignant vs non-malignant — that requires PreCanCell_classifier(), not signature aggregate scoring Gene-level (per-gene) correlation output is required rather than a single signature-level score per sample The expression data are single-cell and unlabeled for cell type — PreCanCell_data()/PreCanCell_classifier() is the intended pipeline, not direct signature scoring

skills.description: Use when bulk PDAC expression samples need subtype calls under one or more published signatures, or when concordance between Moffitt, Collisson, and Bailey subtype labels must be quantified per sample.
skills.name: gene-signature-based-sample-annotation
skills.search_text: gene-signature-based-sample-annotation Use when bulk PDAC expression samples need subtype calls under one or more published signatures, or when concordance between Moffitt, Collisson, and Bailey subtype labels must be quantified per sample. When the input is single-cell RNA-seq — use the rmoffitt/scOh atlas and its pretrained RandomForest cell type classifier instead, since pdacR datasets are all bulk analyses When the dataset has not been filtered for non-PDAC or low-purity cases (e.g. full 182-sample TCGA-PAAD), as uncurated samples introduce non-specificity to gene signatures When the goal is to relabel one scheme's calls directly as another (basal-like = squamous = QM); the signatures are not completely redundant and are confounded by purity and tissue-specificity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assign PDAC samples to published molecular subtypes (Moffitt basal-like/classical, Collisson classical/QM/exocrine, Bailey progenitor/squamous/ADEX/immunogenic, or PurIST) by applying curated SYMBOL-level gene signatures to curated bulk expression datasets hosted in pdacR, then cross-tabulating concordance between schemes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Assign PDAC samples to published molecular subtypes (Moffitt basal-like/classical, Collisson classical/QM/exocrine, Bailey progenitor/squamous/ADEX/immunogenic, or PurIST) by applying curated SYMBOL-level gene signatures to curated bulk expression datasets hosted in pdacR, then cross-tabulating concordance between schemes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is single-cell RNA-seq — use the rmoffitt/scOh atlas and its pretrained RandomForest cell type classifier instead, since pdacR datasets are all bulk analyses When the dataset has not been filtered for non-PDAC or low-purity cases (e.g. full 182-sample TCGA-PAAD), as uncurated samples introduce non-specificity to gene signatures When the goal is to relabel one scheme's calls directly as another (basal-like = squamous = QM); the signatures are not completely redundant and are confounded by purity and tissue-specificity

skills.description: Use when building or retraining a malignant-vs-normal scRNA-seq classifier and the initial malignancy labels come from heterogeneous original annotations that may contain mislabeled cells.
skills.name: gene-signature-based-training-label-calibration
skills.search_text: gene-signature-based-training-label-calibration Use when building or retraining a malignant-vs-normal scRNA-seq classifier and the initial malignancy labels come from heterogeneous original annotations that may contain mislabeled cells. When the input training labels are already expert-curated and signature-consistent — the calibration step removes ~2.5% of cells and would discard valid data When the task is unsupervised CNV-based malignancy inference (e.g., CopyKAT/inferCNVpy) rather than supervised classifier training on labeled data When annotating cell types broadly rather than distinguishing malignant from originating normal cells within a cancerous lineage — the method requires prior basic cell-type identification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Refine noisy training labels for malignant-cell classifiers by scoring cells against nine curated pan-cancer cancer gene signatures (e.g., via AUCell on sc_malignant_deg.gmt) and excluding cells that lose their expected signature profile, yielding a signature-calibrated training set that measurably improves downstream supervised classifiers such as Cancer-Finder and ikarus. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Refine noisy training labels for malignant-cell classifiers by scoring cells against nine curated pan-cancer cancer gene signatures (e.g., via AUCell on sc_malignant_deg.gmt) and excluding cells that lose their expected signature profile, yielding a signature-calibrated training set that measurably improves downstream supervised classifiers such as Cancer-Finder and ikarus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input training labels are already expert-curated and signature-consistent — the calibration step removes ~2.5% of cells and would discard valid data When the task is unsupervised CNV-based malignancy inference (e.g., CopyKAT/inferCNVpy) rather than supervised classifier training on labeled data When annotating cell types broadly rather than distinguishing malignant from originating normal cells within a cancerous lineage — the method requires prior basic cell-type identification

skills.description: Use when RCC clusters (e.g. CT/PAN glioblastoma clusters or SKCM subtypes) must be validated against a known transcriptional signature to confirm biologically distinct subtype identity.
skills.name: gene-signature-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-signature-enrichment-scoring Use when RCC clusters (e.g. CT/PAN glioblastoma clusters or SKCM subtypes) must be validated against a known transcriptional signature to confirm biologically distinct subtype identity. Clusters have not yet been generated and annotated — score enrichment only after RCC_clus and clusterAnnotation define the cluster labels The geneSet is undefined or unrelated to the biology of the dataset — enrichment against an arbitrary signature cannot validate subtype identity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify enrichment of a defined gene signature (e.g. the proneural geneSet) across sample groups or clusters using the ssgsea function of the RCC R package, supporting interpretation of recursive consensus clusters as biologically meaningful subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Quantify enrichment of a defined gene signature (e.g. the proneural geneSet) across sample groups or clusters using the ssgsea function of the RCC R package, supporting interpretation of recursive consensus clusters as biologically meaningful subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters have not yet been generated and annotated — score enrichment only after RCC_clus and clusterAnnotation define the cluster labels The geneSet is undefined or unrelated to the biology of the dataset — enrichment against an arbitrary signature cannot validate subtype identity

skills.description: Use when assembling gene signatures for UCell/AddModuleScore_UCell scoring — e.g. building Tcell, Myeloid, NK, Plasma_cell marker lists on a scRNA-seq matrix, marking negative markers with '-', or deciding how absent genes should be treated.
skills.name: gene-signature-geneset-handling
skills.search_text: gene-signature-geneset-handling Use when assembling gene signatures for UCell/AddModuleScore_UCell scoring — e.g. building Tcell, Myeloid, NK, Plasma_cell marker lists on a scRNA-seq matrix, marking negative markers with '-', or deciding how absent genes should be treated. Genes are binned by dataset-wide average expression for normalization (Seurat AddModuleScore-style context) — this skill's rank-based signatures target UCell, which depends only on per-cell relative ranks Input signatures use identifiers incompatible with the dataset gene symbols (e.g. Ensembl IDs) without prior mapping — UCell will treat unmapped genes as missing The task is cell-type classification/purification from markers, not signature scoring — scGate builds on UCell for that purpose instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Defines and formats cell-type gene signatures (named lists of marker genes, optionally with +/- positive/negative members) for UCell scoring, handling absent genes via 'impute' (set to rmax+1) or 'skip' (drop from rank sum). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: Defines and formats cell-type gene signatures (named lists of marker genes, optionally with +/- positive/negative members) for UCell scoring, handling absent genes via 'impute' (set to rmax+1) or 'skip' (drop from rank sum).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes are binned by dataset-wide average expression for normalization (Seurat AddModuleScore-style context) — this skill's rank-based signatures target UCell, which depends only on per-cell relative ranks Input signatures use identifiers incompatible with the dataset gene symbols (e.g. Ensembl IDs) without prior mapping — UCell will treat unmapped genes as missing The task is cell-type classification/purification from markers, not signature scoring — scGate builds on UCell for that purpose instead

skills.description: Use when you have multiple cell-type- or tissue-specific gene signatures (e.g., SenePy hub signatures) and need to derive a consolidated universal or tissue-level signature with statistically filtered, weighted genes.
skills.name: gene-signature-merging
skills.search_text: gene-signature-merging Use when you have multiple cell-type- or tissue-specific gene signatures (e.g., SenePy hub signatures) and need to derive a consolidated universal or tissue-level signature with statistically filtered, weighted genes. You only need the precomputed universal gene lists without importance weights — use the distributed universal_signatures/Universal_mouse.txt or Universal_human.txt files directly instead of merging. You want to score cells with a single existing signature (use sp.score_hub rather than merging). The merge involves only a handful of input signatures and you rely on calculate_thresh — the permutation threshold can drastically reduce the gene set; specify overlap_threshold manually in that case. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Merge multiple cell-type-specific senescence gene signatures from the SenePy hub database into a single universal or tissue-specific signature, using a permutation-based occurrence threshold to retain only statistically overrepresented genes (FDR p-value < 0.01) and importance weights equal to each gene's occurrence count across input signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Merge multiple cell-type-specific senescence gene signatures from the SenePy hub database into a single universal or tissue-specific signature, using a permutation-based occurrence threshold to retain only statistically overrepresented genes (FDR p-value < 0.01) and importance weights equal to each gene's occurrence count across input signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the precomputed universal gene lists without importance weights — use the distributed universal_signatures/Universal_mouse.txt or Universal_human.txt files directly instead of merging. You want to score cells with a single existing signature (use sp.score_hub rather than merging). The merge involves only a handful of input signatures and you rely on calculate_thresh — the permutation threshold can drastically reduce the gene set; specify overlap_threshold manually in that case.

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated Seurat object with condition metadata and want per-cell scores and top genes for a pathway signature (e.g., innate immune response) across conditions and cell types.
skills.name: gene-signature-per-cell-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-signature-per-cell-scoring Use when you have an annotated Seurat object with condition metadata and want per-cell scores and top genes for a pathway signature (e.g., innate immune response) across conditions and cell types. The input is already a summarized per-cluster or bulk feature table rather than per-cell single-cell data No condition/cell-type grouping metadata is available, since accordion_custom requires condition_group_info and celltype_group_info for condition- and cell-type-specific scoring The goal is cell type annotation itself rather than signature scoring — use accordion() or accordion_cellcycle() instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores per-cell activity of a gene signature (e.g., innate immune response) in single-cell data using the Cell Marker Accordion's accordion_custom() on Seurat objects, enabling condition- and cell-type-specific pathway activation comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Scores per-cell activity of a gene signature (e.g., innate immune response) in single-cell data using the Cell Marker Accordion's accordion_custom() on Seurat objects, enabling condition- and cell-type-specific pathway activation comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a summarized per-cluster or bulk feature table rather than per-cell single-cell data No condition/cell-type grouping metadata is available, since accordion_custom requires condition_group_info and celltype_group_info for condition- and cell-type-specific scoring The goal is cell type annotation itself rather than signature scoring — use accordion() or accordion_cellcycle() instead

skills.description: Use when a published nested-CV transcriptomic model reports a final fitted gene signature (ranked nonzero coefficients) and you need to verify your refit retains the same genes in the same order.
skills.name: gene-signature-reproducibility-checking
skills.search_text: gene-signature-reproducibility-checking Use when a published nested-CV transcriptomic model reports a final fitted gene signature (ranked nonzero coefficients) and you need to verify your refit retains the same genes in the same order. You only need unbiased performance estimation — nested CV on held-out folds suffices; do not conflate outer-fold performance with the final refit coefficients used for signature checking. The predictors are low-dimensional with n >> p — nested CV with embedded feature selection is designed for P >> n transcriptomic data. You plan to filter features on the whole dataset before CV — the article shows this biases accuracy estimates; filters must run inside the outer loop. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduce a published glmnet gene signature (e.g. the 22-feature rituximab response model from the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 RNA-Seq cohort) by refitting the final nestcv.glmnet model on the whole dataset and diffing the ranked nonzero coefficients against the published output. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Reproduce a published glmnet gene signature (e.g. the 22-feature rituximab response model from the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 RNA-Seq cohort) by refitting the final nestcv.glmnet model on the whole dataset and diffing the ranked nonzero coefficients against the published output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need unbiased performance estimation — nested CV on held-out folds suffices; do not conflate outer-fold performance with the final refit coefficients used for signature checking. The predictors are low-dimensional with n >> p — nested CV with embedded feature selection is designed for P >> n transcriptomic data. You plan to filter features on the whole dataset before CV — the article shows this biases accuracy estimates; filters must run inside the outer loop.

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus a set of pre-defined gene signatures (.gmt) and want per-cell signature Z-scores and a statistic of whether signature variation tracks a cell similarity structure such as a phylogeny or KNN graph.
skills.name: gene-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: gene-signature-scoring Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus a set of pre-defined gene signatures (.gmt) and want per-cell signature Z-scores and a statistic of whether signature variation tracks a cell similarity structure such as a phylogeny or KNN graph. You want data-driven heritable gene modules rather than testing pre-defined signatures — use PhyloVision's unguided Hotspot module identification instead The input lacks a cell-cell similarity structure (no phylogeny or trajectory/graph); Geary's C phylogenetic autocorrelation is undefined without a cell metric You only need phylogeny visualization with overlays — tools like iTOL or CeLaVi suffice and offer no joint expression/lineage analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Score user-defined gene signatures (e.g., MSigDB Hallmark, C2, C5/BP supplied as .gmt files) per cell and evaluate whether their expression variation agrees with a cell-cell similarity structure, such as a phylogeny, using VISION signature Z-scores and Geary's C autocorrelation. This is the signature-centric analysis that PhyloVision exposes for testing whether gene programs are heritable along a lineage tree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Score user-defined gene signatures (e.g., MSigDB Hallmark, C2, C5/BP supplied as .gmt files) per cell and evaluate whether their expression variation agrees with a cell-cell similarity structure, such as a phylogeny, using VISION signature Z-scores and Geary's C autocorrelation. This is the signature-centric analysis that PhyloVision exposes for testing whether gene programs are heritable along a lineage tree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want data-driven heritable gene modules rather than testing pre-defined signatures — use PhyloVision's unguided Hotspot module identification instead The input lacks a cell-cell similarity structure (no phylogeny or trajectory/graph); Geary's C phylogenetic autocorrelation is undefined without a cell metric You only need phylogeny visualization with overlays — tools like iTOL or CeLaVi suffice and offer no joint expression/lineage analysis

skills.description: Use when a cell population (e.g., 2064 melanoma T cells) has been partitioned into subpopulations (C1–C5) in reconstructed pseudo-space and you must test whether the subpopulation nearest malignant cells carries a higher functional signature score (exhaustion) than a distant one.
skills.name: gene-signature-scoring-for-exhaustion
skills.search_text: gene-signature-scoring-for-exhaustion Use when a cell population (e.g., 2064 melanoma T cells) has been partitioned into subpopulations (C1–C5) in reconstructed pseudo-space and you must test whether the subpopulation nearest malignant cells carries a higher functional signature score (exhaustion) than a distant one. Tissues with low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), where pseudo-space reconstruction—and hence spatially-informed exhaustion comparisons—are unreliable Data that has not been partitioned into spatially informed subpopulations; exhaustion scoring alone cannot establish TIL identity without the spatial proximity context Spatial reference data inappropriate for the target tissue (reference choice directly influences the spatial reconstruction), e.g., a granular DLPFC reference for agranular cortex lacking layer 4 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Score each cell in a pseudo-space-clustered scRNA-seq population against a T-cell exhaustion gene signature using scanpy, then compare scores between spatial subpopulations (e.g., melanoma C5 vs C3) to identify tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) identity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Score each cell in a pseudo-space-clustered scRNA-seq population against a T-cell exhaustion gene signature using scanpy, then compare scores between spatial subpopulations (e.g., melanoma C5 vs C3) to identify tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissues with low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), where pseudo-space reconstruction—and hence spatially-informed exhaustion comparisons—are unreliable Data that has not been partitioned into spatially informed subpopulations; exhaustion scoring alone cannot establish TIL identity without the spatial proximity context Spatial reference data inappropriate for the target tissue (reference choice directly influences the spatial reconstruction), e.g., a granular DLPFC reference for agranular cortex lacking layer 4

skills.description: Use when a single-cell cluster's DEGs (e.g., scanpyobj.h5ad / cluster_DEGs.csv) must be tested against bulk RNA-seq cohorts (e.g., TCGA-LIHC) for prognostic significance via signature scoring and survival analysis.
skills.name: gene-signature-scoring-from-degs
skills.search_text: gene-signature-scoring-from-degs Use when a single-cell cluster's DEGs (e.g., scanpyobj.h5ad / cluster_DEGs.csv) must be tested against bulk RNA-seq cohorts (e.g., TCGA-LIHC) for prognostic significance via signature scoring and survival analysis. Input is already a bulk expression feature table with no cluster-derived DEG signature from scRNA-seq — the scoring relies on cluster-specific DEGs like Cluster 4's PTMA/STMN1 No matched clinical survival data exist for the bulk cohort — the log-rank test and hazard ratio cannot be computed The goal is drug response prediction (IC50/AUC via GDSC or PRISM models) rather than survival stratification — use scDrug's Drug Response Prediction module instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts cluster-specific differentially expressed genes (e.g., the top 20 DEGs of a tumor Cluster 4 from GSE156625 scRNA-seq) into a binary activity score per bulk RNA-seq patient, then stratifies patients into high/low-expressing groups for Kaplan-Meier survival analysis linking scRNA-seq subpopulations to clinical outcome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Converts cluster-specific differentially expressed genes (e.g., the top 20 DEGs of a tumor Cluster 4 from GSE156625 scRNA-seq) into a binary activity score per bulk RNA-seq patient, then stratifies patients into high/low-expressing groups for Kaplan-Meier survival analysis linking scRNA-seq subpopulations to clinical outcome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a bulk expression feature table with no cluster-derived DEG signature from scRNA-seq — the scoring relies on cluster-specific DEGs like Cluster 4's PTMA/STMN1 No matched clinical survival data exist for the bulk cohort — the log-rank test and hazard ratio cannot be computed The goal is drug response prediction (IC50/AUC via GDSC or PRISM models) rather than survival stratification — use scDrug's Drug Response Prediction module instead

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrix plus two competing gene signatures (basal-like vs classical) and need per-sample subtype calls comparable to published schema, followed by survival testing.
skills.name: gene-signature-scoring-pdac-tumors
skills.search_text: gene-signature-scoring-pdac-tumors Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrix plus two competing gene signatures (basal-like vs classical) and need per-sample subtype calls comparable to published schema, followed by survival testing. Input is single-cell data needing subcluster discovery itself — use the full SCISSORS iterative reclustering routine instead of bulk signature scoring. You lack one of the two competing signatures (or only have one subtype's genes), so the higher-score-wins assignment rule cannot be applied. No survival metadata exists, making the Kaplan-Meier/log-rank validation step impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Score bulk RNA-seq tumors (e.g., 150 TCGA PAAD samples) against fold-change-ranked SCISSORS-derived basal-like and classical PDAC gene signatures, assign each tumor the subtype of its higher-scoring signature, and validate calls against the Moffitt schema with Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Score bulk RNA-seq tumors (e.g., 150 TCGA PAAD samples) against fold-change-ranked SCISSORS-derived basal-like and classical PDAC gene signatures, assign each tumor the subtype of its higher-scoring signature, and validate calls against the Moffitt schema with Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data needing subcluster discovery itself — use the full SCISSORS iterative reclustering routine instead of bulk signature scoring. You lack one of the two competing signatures (or only have one subtype's genes), so the higher-score-wins assignment rule cannot be applied. No survival metadata exists, making the Kaplan-Meier/log-rank validation step impossible.

skills.description: Use when a curated gene signature needs to be audited for tissue- or tumor-specificity confounders — e.g., checking if ADEX/Immunogenic genes are driven by non-PDAC or adrenal (ACC) signal before using the signature for subtyping.
skills.name: gene-signature-specificity-partitioning
skills.search_text: gene-signature-specificity-partitioning Use when a curated gene signature needs to be audited for tissue- or tumor-specificity confounders — e.g., checking if ADEX/Immunogenic genes are driven by non-PDAC or adrenal (ACC) signal before using the signature for subtyping. When the goal is sample-level tumor subtyping (e.g., basal-like/classical assignment or PurIST prediction) rather than auditing which genes in a signature are tissue- or tumor-specific When working with single-cell data — the article notes the parsed single-cell atlas (rmoffitt/scOh) lacks a web interface and that bulk datasets, not scRNA, are what pdacR houses for this analysis When datasets are not curated for sample composition; including non-adenocarcinoma cases (e.g., the 32 non-PDAC samples in TCGA-PAAD's 182) would corrupt the specificity clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Tests whether a published PDAC gene signature (e.g., the Bailey ADEX or Immunogenic sets) is confounded by non-PDAC-specific genes by running gene-wise consensus clustering on curated bulk RNA-seq datasets and partitioning signature genes into specificity classes (ACC-specific, pancreas-nonspecific, nonspecific), then quantifying overlap against other signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Tests whether a published PDAC gene signature (e.g., the Bailey ADEX or Immunogenic sets) is confounded by non-PDAC-specific genes by running gene-wise consensus clustering on curated bulk RNA-seq datasets and partitioning signature genes into specificity classes (ACC-specific, pancreas-nonspecific, nonspecific), then quantifying overlap against other signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is sample-level tumor subtyping (e.g., basal-like/classical assignment or PurIST prediction) rather than auditing which genes in a signature are tissue- or tumor-specific When working with single-cell data — the article notes the parsed single-cell atlas (rmoffitt/scOh) lacks a web interface and that bulk datasets, not scRNA, are what pdacR houses for this analysis When datasets are not curated for sample composition; including non-adenocarcinoma cases (e.g., the 32 non-PDAC samples in TCGA-PAAD's 182) would corrupt the specificity clustering

skills.description: Use when mapping target scRNA-seq cells to reference clusters and you need discriminative weights for cluster-specific gene signatures — e.g. before scid_multiclass scoring or when batch effect/strong asymmetry in cell number and library size means weights should come from the target data.
skills.name: gene-signature-weight-estimation
skills.search_text: gene-signature-weight-estimation Use when mapping target scRNA-seq cells to reference clusters and you need discriminative weights for cluster-specific gene signatures — e.g. before scid_multiclass scoring or when batch effect/strong asymmetry in cell number and library size means weights should come from the target data. Input data are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth normalized (TPM/CPM) values, not log-transformed data Neither reference nor target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates discriminative gene weights for reference-cluster signatures using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework: differentially expressed marker genes (logFC >= 0.6) are weighted by their ability to separate putative c+ and c- cells selected via differential precision-recall (DPR), enabling scoring of target cells in cross-dataset mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Estimates discriminative gene weights for reference-cluster signatures using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework: differentially expressed marker genes (logFC >= 0.6) are weighted by their ability to separate putative c+ and c- cells selected via differential precision-recall (DPR), enabling scoring of target cells in cross-dataset mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth normalized (TPM/CPM) values, not log-transformed data Neither reference nor target data are well clustered or contain good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach in that case

skills.description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values for two treatments vs a common control must be partitioned into significance-filtered regions of interest (quadrants A–E, or M/R/S in the full scorecard) by fold-change magnitude.
skills.name: gene-significance-filtering
skills.search_text: gene-significance-filtering Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values for two treatments vs a common control must be partitioned into significance-filtered regions of interest (quadrants A–E, or M/R/S in the full scorecard) by fold-change magnitude. Setting the multiplication factor to 1 — this produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, losing the extreme-vs-moderate partitioning Input lacks adjusted (FDR-corrected) p-values: typical four-way plots are not filtered by statistical significance, but this skill requires significance filtering to assign entries to regions Fold-changes are not pre-computed: the workflow expects log2 fold-change and padj columns in the CSV, not raw count or TPM data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 The Scorecard library assigns statistically significant genes to regions of interest on the Cartesian plane of two treatments' log2 fold-changes versus a common control, using two fold-change thresholds (a standard threshold plus an extreme threshold set via a multiplication factor) and an adjusted p-value filter (e.g. 0.05 or lower). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: The Scorecard library assigns statistically significant genes to regions of interest on the Cartesian plane of two treatments' log2 fold-changes versus a common control, using two fold-change thresholds (a standard threshold plus an extreme threshold set via a multiplication factor) and an adjusted p-value filter (e.g. 0.05 or lower).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Setting the multiplication factor to 1 — this produces a four-way plot, not the scorecard, losing the extreme-vs-moderate partitioning Input lacks adjusted (FDR-corrected) p-values: typical four-way plots are not filtered by statistical significance, but this skill requires significance filtering to assign entries to regions Fold-changes are not pre-computed: the workflow expects log2 fold-change and padj columns in the CSV, not raw count or TPM data

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell expression matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank or filter genes for significance along the trajectory using dCor and MIC statistics.
skills.name: gene-significance-selection-thresholding
skills.search_text: gene-significance-selection-thresholding Use when you have a gene-by-cell expression matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank or filter genes for significance along the trajectory using dCor and MIC statistics. When no pseudotime ordering has been inferred yet — correlations require redpath_pseudotime and 'this approach may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly'. When the input is already a filtered/GO-subset matrix (filtered_GO_data) intended for pseudotime inference, not the full expression matrix that calc_correlation expects. No single-cell reference profile is available and only known marker genes exist — use BisqueMarker (MarkerBasedDecomposition) instead, noting its abundances cannot be compared across cell types Very few individuals have single-cell data, making the reference profile and gene-specific transformations unreliable Known severe bias in the single-cell measurements, e.g. a cell type of interest is severely underrepresented relative to true physiological composition http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Bisque's core statistical step: per-gene regression that learns transformations of the bulk expression scale to correct gene-specific biases between single-cell/nucleus reference profiles and bulk RNA-seq, followed by NNLS decomposition to estimate cell-type proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6

skills.description: Use when the dataset contains complex branching, cycling progenitors, or sparse cell types where a single transcriptome-wide latent time is inappropriate, and per-gene time is needed to recover trajectory structure.

skills.search_text: gene-specific-latent-time-inference Use when the dataset contains complex branching, cycling progenitors, or sparse cell types where a single transcriptome-wide latent time is inappropriate, and per-gene time is needed to recover trajectory structure. Datasets where a single transcriptome-wide ordering suffices and stably, monotonically changed genes dominate — use the Unified-time mode (FIT_OPTION='1') instead Downstream tasks requiring unsupervised selection of dynamically informed genes — the paper states this remains an open challenge Analyses expecting a Bayesian quantification of latent time uncertainty — this is anticipated but not implemented in UniTVelo http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run UniTVelo's Independent mode (FIT_OPTION='2') to assign gene-specific latent time metrics, retaining per-gene time instead of a unified transcriptome-wide time. This is the recommended mode for complex differentiation scenarios such as cell cycles, sparse cell types, and multi-branch trajectories (e.g., retina development with PR, RGC, and AC/HC branches). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7

skills.search_text: gene-specific-length-scale-gaussian-process-modeling Use when identifying spatially variable genes in spatially-resolved transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium DLPFC, ST mouse OB) where genes may have different spatial ranges (length scales) and scalable fitting over thousands of spots is required. The goal is identifying spatial domain marker genes (mean-level changes between domains) rather than genes varying continuously across the tissue or within a priori defined spatial domains Multiple-sample datasets requiring a principled statistical model — nnSVG is developed for a single sample at a time and handles multiple samples only via averaging per-sample ranks Effect sizes must separate technical from biological variance — the prop_sv definition does not make this distinction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit a nearest-neighbor Gaussian process (NNGP) model per gene with a gene-specific length scale parameter to identify and rank spatially variable genes (SVGs) via a likelihood-ratio test, using nnSVG's BRISC-based fitting that scales linearly with the number of spatial locations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z
skills.summary: Fit a nearest-neighbor Gaussian process (NNGP) model per gene with a gene-specific length scale parameter to identify and rank spatially variable genes (SVGs) via a likelihood-ratio test, using nnSVG's BRISC-based fitting that scales linearly with the number of spatial locations.

skills.search_text: gene-subspace-assignment Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq training gene set (genes expressed in at least two cells with at least one percent non-zero entries) must be partitioned into gene subspaces so that dropout-imputation regression can be run within each group. The zero entries have not yet been screened by the hyper-geometric over-/under-representation testing (significance threshold 0.01) — grouping must be run on the training data only, not the whole matrix including imputable entries. Genes expressed in fewer than two cells or with less than one percent non-zero-valued entries have not been filtered out — including them distorts the perturbation clustering. The goal is direct imputation without gene grouping — this skill is an intermediate step of scISR, not a standalone imputer; use scImpute, SAVER, MAGIC, etc. for other imputation paradigms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Groups training genes into co-expression subspaces via scISR's data-perturbation clustering: Gaussian-noise perturbation plus repeated k-means, connectivity matrices, and selection of the partition maximizing the CDF-difference AUC. skills.description: Use when ranking genes by Pearson correlation with a continuous time variable (e.g., a 12-hour C. elegans developmental course) and comparing top-N correlation distributions to score denoising recovery.
skills.name: gene-time-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-time-correlation-analysis Use when ranking genes by Pearson correlation with a continuous time variable (e.g., a 12-hour C. elegans developmental course) and comparing top-N correlation distributions to score denoising recovery. The expression matrix has no continuous, ordered time (or pseudotime) variable — per-gene correlation with time is undefined for unordered conditions or cell-type labels. Only corrupted data with no unperturbed reference is available, since the recovery metric requires original-data correlations as the target. You need an absolute denoising-quality score with ground truth; the article notes that defining a ground truth for real data is challenging, so this comparison is qualitative. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-gene Pearson correlations between expression and developmental time on the Francesconi et al. C. elegans bulk time-course (206 samples spanning 12 hours), and uses the correlation distribution over the top 500 time-correlated genes as a recovery metric to benchmark denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) against a dropout-perturbed (80% zeros) baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Computes per-gene Pearson correlations between expression and developmental time on the Francesconi et al. C. elegans bulk time-course (206 samples spanning 12 hours), and uses the correlation distribution over the top 500 time-correlated genes as a recovery metric to benchmark denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) against a dropout-perturbed (80% zeros) baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has no continuous, ordered time (or pseudotime) variable — per-gene correlation with time is undefined for unordered conditions or cell-type labels. Only corrupted data with no unperturbed reference is available, since the recovery metric requires original-data correlations as the target. You need an absolute denoising-quality score with ground truth; the article notes that defining a ground truth for real data is challenging, so this comparison is qualitative.

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked per-cell-type marker list from reference data and a LogNormalized query/reference expression matrix (AnnData) that must be converted into a per-cell cell-type score matrix for label transfer or integration.
skills.name: gene-to-cell-type-score-conversion
skills.search_text: gene-to-cell-type-score-conversion Use when you have a ranked per-cell-type marker list from reference data and a LogNormalized query/reference expression matrix (AnnData) that must be converted into a per-cell cell-type score matrix for label transfer or integration. When the input is already a cell-type score matrix or a pre-computed feature embedding rather than a gene expression matrix plus marker list When training large model-based annotation methods (scNym, scArches, Symphony) is desired — MASI's marker-based score conversion is a distinct model-free approach and skipping HVG selection is incompatible with methods that need variable genes When the query contains cell types absent from the reference — scores/labels alone will mis-assign them; pair with SCCAF and the certainty-score filter instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MASI's gene2cell step transforms a LogNormalized single-cell gene expression AnnData matrix into a cell-type score matrix by summing ranked, linearly discounted marker-gene expression per cell type, with optional PlinerScore thresholding; this score matrix is the critical input for MASI's downstream annotation and integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: MASI's gene2cell step transforms a LogNormalized single-cell gene expression AnnData matrix into a cell-type score matrix by summing ranked, linearly discounted marker-gene expression per cell type, with optional PlinerScore thresholding; this score matrix is the critical input for MASI's downstream annotation and integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a cell-type score matrix or a pre-computed feature embedding rather than a gene expression matrix plus marker list When training large model-based annotation methods (scNym, scArches, Symphony) is desired — MASI's marker-based score conversion is a distinct model-free approach and skipping HVG selection is incompatible with methods that need variable genes When the query contains cell types absent from the reference — scores/labels alone will mis-assign them; pair with SCCAF and the certainty-score filter instead

skills.search_text: gene-topic-probability-interpretation Use when you have a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix and want to decompose it into latent topics (biological functions) and obtain interpretable per-topic gene-probability distributions. Input is raw sequencing reads or aligned FASTQ/BAM files rather than a cell-by-gene count matrix — pLDA models count data with genes as words Input is already a reduced representation such as a feature/latent table or normalized expression matrix where the gene-count composition has been lost The goal is standard LDA on text documents — pLDA is adapted specifically for scRNA-seq count data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits the penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) model to scRNA-seq count matrices — genes as words, cells as documents, latent biological functions as topics — and extracts the per-topic gene-probability matrix for biological interpretation. skills.summary: Fits the penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) model to scRNA-seq count matrices — genes as words, cells as documents, latent biological functions as topics — and extracts the per-topic gene-probability matrix for biological interpretation. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or aligned FASTQ/BAM files rather than a cell-by-gene count matrix — pLDA models count data with genes as words Input is already a reduced representation such as a feature/latent table or normalized expression matrix where the gene-count composition has been lost The goal is standard LDA on text documents — pLDA is adapted specifically for scRNA-seq count data
