skills.description: Use when csv or .xlsx gene expression files contain gene symbols auto-converted to dates by Excel (e.g. SEPT1, MARC1 becoming date strings, or ambiguous Mar-01/Mar-02 terms) and need to be converted back to HGNC-approved gene names.
skills.name: gene-updater-local-streamlit-deployment
skills.search_text: gene-updater-local-streamlit-deployment Use when csv or .xlsx gene expression files contain gene symbols auto-converted to dates by Excel (e.g. SEPT1, MARC1 becoming date strings, or ambiguous Mar-01/Mar-02 terms) and need to be converted back to HGNC-approved gene names. Input files contain no Excel date-converted gene names and already use current HGNC gene symbols — the tool is designed to rectify date conversions and old names, not general gene expression analysis. Ambiguous Mar-01/Mar-02 terms cannot be resolved because no gene description is provided and the raw dataset cannot disambiguate MTARC1/MARCHF1 from MTARC2/MARCHF2 — manual assignment via the widgets would be guesswork with contrasting biological functions at stake. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Deploy the Gene Updater web tool locally with Streamlit to autocorrect Excel date-converted gene names and update old gene symbols to new HGNC-recommended names, using the date_gene_tool.py script from the kuanrongchan/date-to-gene-converter repository. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-17104-3
skills.summary: Deploy the Gene Updater web tool locally with Streamlit to autocorrect Excel date-converted gene names and update old gene symbols to new HGNC-recommended names, using the date_gene_tool.py script from the kuanrongchan/date-to-gene-converter repository.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input files contain no Excel date-converted gene names and already use current HGNC gene symbols — the tool is designed to rectify date conversions and old names, not general gene expression analysis. Ambiguous Mar-01/Mar-02 terms cannot be resolved because no gene description is provided and the raw dataset cannot disambiguate MTARC1/MARCHF1 from MTARC2/MARCHF2 — manual assignment via the widgets would be guesswork with contrasting biological functions at stake.

skills.description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix (e.g. GSE125792, 1968 genes) and need to screen or rank stable endogenous reference genes for qPCR normalization in Python.
skills.name: gene-variability-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-variability-ranking Use when you have a gene expression matrix (e.g. GSE125792, 1968 genes) and need to screen or rank stable endogenous reference genes for qPCR normalization in Python. Normalization of already-selected reference genes — use ERgene.normalizationdata instead; single gene standardization is not desirable per the literature and MIQE guidance unless invariable expression is clearly demonstrated Computational depth is set too large (3 or larger declines in efficiency; a very large depth may return no result) You need an R or Excel workflow — geNorm (qbase+/Excel 2003) and Normfinder (R/Excel 2003) cover that; ERgene is the Python-specific choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Ranks candidate endogenous reference genes by computing the variance of relative factor change across genes with the ERgene Python library, which inverts the internal-reference method and uses robust matrix block computation (every 1000 genes as a block) to return the top 20 most stable genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-75586-5
skills.summary: Ranks candidate endogenous reference genes by computing the variance of relative factor change across genes with the ERgene Python library, which inverts the internal-reference method and uses robust matrix block computation (every 1000 genes as a block) to return the top 20 most stable genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Normalization of already-selected reference genes — use ERgene.normalizationdata instead; single gene standardization is not desirable per the literature and MIQE guidance unless invariable expression is clearly demonstrated Computational depth is set too large (3 or larger declines in efficiency; a very large depth may return no result) You need an R or Excel workflow — geNorm (qbase+/Excel 2003) and Normfinder (R/Excel 2003) cover that; ERgene is the Python-specific choice

The goal is unsupervised grouping of cancer patients — DeepCC is specifically developed for classification but not clustering of cancer patients The input is already a functional spectra (pathway activity) feature table; subsetting genes applies only at the gene-expression level before getFunctionalSpectra A single sample without matched reference expression profile — single-sample classification requires a reference profile (e.g., refExp = "COADREAD") and does not exercise this subsampling robustness analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 A robustness simulation in which functional spectra for DeepCC are recomputed from random subsets of the most variable genes (e.g., 1000 up to 20,531 genes from TCGA CRC data, n=456) to quantify how classification performance degrades when gene annotation is incomplete across platforms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8

skills.search_text: gene-weight-top-contributor-ranking Use when a rROMA analysis flags a module as over-dispersed or shifted and you need to identify which individual genes carry the largest PC1 weights, e.g. to nominate a lead gene for follow-up in a CF vs healthy comparison. The goal is differential pathway activity (shift testing with 'ppv Median Exp' <= 0.05) rather than identifying individual gene drivers within a module. The expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma requires cpm, vst, or equivalent normalized data). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Ranks the genes driving a rROMA module's PC1 activity by their absolute weights in the first principal component, using the rRoma GetTopContrib function to identify lead drivers such as GSN in the COAGULATION hallmark module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Ranks the genes driving a rROMA module's PC1 activity by their absolute weights in the first principal component, using the rRoma GetTopContrib function to identify lead drivers such as GSN in the COAGULATION hallmark module.

skills.search_text: gene-zweight-averaging-into-mec-profiles Use when a cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight matrix (task_inputs port 'ica_zweight_matrix') is available and the goal is to collapse reproducible ICs into consensus meta-components for tumor microenvironment annotation. Input is raw single-cell expression data rather than a cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight matrix — upstream ICA and reproducibility filtering must be run first (see MetaTiMEpretrain pipeline). The goal is annotating new TME scRNA-seq data with pretrained MeCs; use the MetaTiME-Annotator mapping instead of re-deriving the MeC space. Components are expected to be cohort-specific (e.g. a single-dataset factor analysis) where cross-cohort reproducibility filtering (≥3 datasets Pearson correlation) would incorrectly discard them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Derives MetaTiME meta-components (MeCs) by retaining ICA independent components whose gene z-weight profiles are reproducible across cohorts (minimum Pearson correlation matched in ≥3 datasets), clustering them via Louvain community detection (resolution 1.25, clusters <5 discarded), and averaging within-cluster gene z-weights into MeC profiles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Derives MetaTiME meta-components (MeCs) by retaining ICA independent components whose gene z-weight profiles are reproducible across cohorts (minimum Pearson correlation matched in ≥3 datasets), clustering them via Louvain community detection (resolution 1.25, clusters <5 discarded), and averaging within-cluster gene z-weights into MeC profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-cell expression data rather than a cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight matrix — upstream ICA and reproducibility filtering must be run first (see MetaTiMEpretrain pipeline). skills.description: Use when fitting TF-based gene dynamics and latent times on scRNA-seq data with TFvelo, or when reproducing/tuning the EM optimization loop (weight updates, dynamics updates, time assignment) for RNA velocity without splicing counts.
skills.name: generalized-em-iteration-rna-velocity
skills.search_text: generalized-em-iteration-rna-velocity Use when fitting TF-based gene dynamics and latent times on scRNA-seq data with TFvelo, or when reproducing/tuning the EM optimization loop (weight updates, dynamics updates, time assignment) for RNA velocity without splicing counts. The dataset is very large and runtime matters: the article notes TFvelo time efficiency is lower than scVelo in the same framework, which 'could be a weakness when being applied to the large-scale datasets' Splicing (unspliced/spliced) counts are available and a splicing-based dynamical model such as scVelo is preferred, since TFvelo was designed for datasets without splicing information Only summary/feature tables are available without the gene expression matrix needed for TF-target correlation-based weight initialization http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs TFvelo's generalized EM loop for fitting per-gene dynamics from transcription factor abundance: it alternates a latent-time E-step (grid-search time assignment over n_time_points discrete points) with two M-steps that update TF weights (bounded lsq_linear regression) and the sine-profile dynamics parameters (alpha, beta, theta, gamma). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs TFvelo's generalized EM loop for fitting per-gene dynamics from transcription factor abundance: it alternates a latent-time E-step (grid-search time assignment over n_time_points discrete points) with two M-steps that update TF weights (bounded lsq_linear regression) and the sine-profile dynamics parameters (alpha, beta, theta, gamma).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is very large and runtime matters: the article notes TFvelo time efficiency is lower than scVelo in the same framework, which 'could be a weakness when being applied to the large-scale datasets' Splicing (unspliced/spliced) counts are available and a splicing-based dynamical model such as scVelo is preferred, since TFvelo was designed for datasets without splicing information Only summary/feature tables are available without the gene expression matrix needed for TF-target correlation-based weight initialization

skills.search_text: generalized-linear-model-count-modeling Use when raw single-cell gene count data (e.g. Smart-seq2) has cells assigned to clone/subclone groups and you must test which genes differ between groups while accounting for plate and detection-rate confounders. Input consists of already-normalized values (TPM/CPM/log-expression) instead of raw counts, since edgeR GLMs model raw count dispersion The goal is calling clonally informative mtDNA variants or assigning cells to clones — use the cellSNP-MQuad-vireoSNP pipeline instead Cells lack clone/subclone labels or groups are so small that the edgeR design matrix (detection rate + plate + clone) cannot be estimated http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fits negative-binomial generalized linear models (edgeR quasi-likelihood) to single-cell gene count matrices to test differential expression between mtDNA-defined subclones, with IHW multiple-testing correction and limma camera pathway enrichment on MSigDB Hallmark sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Fits negative-binomial generalized linear models (edgeR quasi-likelihood) to single-cell gene count matrices to test differential expression between mtDNA-defined subclones, with IHW multiple-testing correction and limma camera pathway enrichment on MSigDB Hallmark sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of already-normalized values (TPM/CPM/log-expression) instead of raw counts, since edgeR GLMs model raw count dispersion The goal is calling clonally informative mtDNA variants or assigning cells to clones — use the cellSNP-MQuad-vireoSNP pipeline instead Cells lack clone/subclone labels or groups are so small that the edgeR design matrix (detection rate + plate + clone) cannot be estimated

skills.description: Use when you have cscGAN/scGAN-generated scRNA-seq cells (e.g. .h5ad output for specific PBMC clusters) and need to judge whether they are realistic and indistinguishable from real cells of the target clusters.
skills.name: generated-cell-quality-evaluation-rf-auc-mmd
skills.search_text: generated-cell-quality-evaluation-rf-auc-mmd Use when you have cscGAN/scGAN-generated scRNA-seq cells (e.g. .h5ad output for specific PBMC clusters) and need to judge whether they are realistic and indistinguishable from real cells of the target clusters. You want to evaluate biological utility (e.g. marker gene detection or classifier augmentation gains) rather than realism of the synthetic cells themselves Input data are not single-cell RNA-seq count/expression matrices — the RF and MMD evaluation is calibrated on scRNA-seq representations (e.g. PBMC clusters) No cluster-annotated real cells are available for the target clusters, so the real-vs-synthetic comparison cannot be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantitative realism check for GAN-generated scRNA-seq cells: train a Random Forest classifier to distinguish synthetic from real cells (AUC near 0.5 = hard to distinguish) and compute maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between synthetic and real distributions, complemented by conditional t-SNE inspection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Quantitative realism check for GAN-generated scRNA-seq cells: train a Random Forest classifier to distinguish synthetic from real cells (AUC near 0.5 = hard to distinguish) and compute maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between synthetic and real distributions, complemented by conditional t-SNE inspection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to evaluate biological utility (e.g. marker gene detection or classifier augmentation gains) rather than realism of the synthetic cells themselves Input data are not single-cell RNA-seq count/expression matrices — the RF and MMD evaluation is calibrated on scRNA-seq representations (e.g. PBMC clusters) No cluster-annotated real cells are available for the target clusters, so the real-vs-synthetic comparison cannot be constructed

skills.description: Use when aligning two non-overlapping single-cell modalities (e.g. Full PBMC source/target manifolds) whose topoAE embeddings must be mapped into a common space, especially when GAN-to-GAN variability across initializations is too high.
skills.name: generative-adversarial-network-training
skills.search_text: generative-adversarial-network-training Use when aligning two non-overlapping single-cell modalities (e.g. Full PBMC source/target manifolds) whose topoAE embeddings must be mapped into a common space, especially when GAN-to-GAN variability across initializations is too high. Datasets have overlapping features or cells that standard integration methods can exploit directly — the article notes current integration methods rely on overlap, but this GAN approach is designed for non-overlapping modalities; if overlap exists, simpler methods may suffice The task is only low-dimensional embedding of a single modality, not cross-modality manifold alignment — use the TopoAE step alone (e.g. TopoAE_benchmark.py) instead of the GAN http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains the topology-guided GAN of scTopoGAN to align source and target single-cell manifolds, and extends it by augmenting the GAN's overall loss with the topological loss as a regularization term so the unstable multi-GAN model-selection loop can be removed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Trains the topology-guided GAN of scTopoGAN to align source and target single-cell manifolds, and extends it by augmenting the GAN's overall loss with the topological loss as a regularization term so the unstable multi-GAN model-selection loop can be removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have overlapping features or cells that standard integration methods can exploit directly — the article notes current integration methods rely on overlap, but this GAN approach is designed for non-overlapping modalities; if overlap exists, simpler methods may suffice The task is only low-dimensional embedding of a single modality, not cross-modality manifold alignment — use the TopoAE step alone (e.g. TopoAE_benchmark.py) instead of the GAN

skills.description: Use when the goal is to train a GAN on single-cell RNA-seq data (.h5/.h5ad) so that generated cells are hard to distinguish from real cells by t-SNE embedding, marker-gene correlation, MMD, and classifier AUC.
skills.name: generative-adversarial-network-training
skills.search_text: generative-adversarial-network-training Use when the goal is to train a GAN on single-cell RNA-seq data (.h5/.h5ad) so that generated cells are hard to distinguish from real cells by t-SNE embedding, marker-gene correlation, MMD, and classifier AUC. The task is trajectory inference or manifold visualization rather than cell generation — the companion repos (PAGA, SUGAR) serve other purposes and SUGAR is used here only as a comparison baseline for generation quality Data is not in .h5/.h5ad and there is no plan to convert mtx/tsv first — pre-processing expects these formats You need to condition generation on side information other than cell type (e.g., case/control) — the article leaves this untested for future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Training a single-cell GAN (scGAN or cscGAN) with TensorFlow to generate realistic scRNA-seq cells, validated qualitatively by t-SNE overlap with real validation cells and quantitatively by MMD and AUC metrics against real-data and SUGAR baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Training a single-cell GAN (scGAN or cscGAN) with TensorFlow to generate realistic scRNA-seq cells, validated qualitatively by t-SNE overlap with real validation cells and quantitatively by MMD and AUC metrics against real-data and SUGAR baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is trajectory inference or manifold visualization rather than cell generation — the companion repos (PAGA, SUGAR) serve other purposes and SUGAR is used here only as a comparison baseline for generation quality Data is not in .h5/.h5ad and there is no plan to convert mtx/tsv first — pre-processing expects these formats You need to condition generation on side information other than cell type (e.g., case/control) — the article leaves this untested for future work

skills.description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data from a trained generative model must be quantitatively compared to held-out real cells and rival simulators (e.g., 10x Genomics PBMC-CTL, 1000 generated cells vs 1000 test cells).
skills.name: generative-model-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: generative-model-benchmark-comparison Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data from a trained generative model must be quantitatively compared to held-out real cells and rival simulators (e.g., 10x Genomics PBMC-CTL, 1000 generated cells vs 1000 test cells). The goal is benchmarking GRN inference algorithms rather than simulated-data quality — use GRouNdGAN's --benchmark_grn instead of the resemblance-metric suite. The reference dataset is very small (~2.7k cells, e.g., BoneMarrow): all simulators' performance dropped on the test set, so metric comparisons are unreliable. The input is PBMC-All or another multi-cell-type mixture: the article states benchmarking results there are not conclusive and follow-up studies are required. You need unnormalized count data: GRouNdGAN only generates library-size normalized expression values. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks GRN-guided generative simulators (GRouNdGAN vs scGAN, scDESIGN2, SPARSim) on scRNA-seq realism using a shared resemblance-metric suite (cosine, Euclidean, MMD, RF AUROC, miLISI) against held-out real cells and a real-real control. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks GRN-guided generative simulators (GRouNdGAN vs scGAN, scDESIGN2, SPARSim) on scRNA-seq realism using a shared resemblance-metric suite (cosine, Euclidean, MMD, RF AUROC, miLISI) against held-out real cells and a real-real control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking GRN inference algorithms rather than simulated-data quality — use GRouNdGAN's --benchmark_grn instead of the resemblance-metric suite. The reference dataset is very small (~2.7k cells, e.g., BoneMarrow): all simulators' performance dropped on the test set, so metric comparisons are unreliable. The input is PBMC-All or another multi-cell-type mixture: the article states benchmarking results there are not conclusive and follow-up studies are required. You need unnormalized count data: GRouNdGAN only generates library-size normalized expression values.

skills.description: Use when transferring cell annotations (discrete types or continuous fate probabilities) from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset to an independent query dataset whose batch or distribution differs, e.g. cross-species or cross-platform queries in h5ad format.
skills.name: generative-model-online-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: generative-model-online-fine-tuning Use when transferring cell annotations (discrete types or continuous fate probabilities) from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset to an independent query dataset whose batch or distribution differs, e.g. cross-species or cross-platform queries in h5ad format. Reference datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells, where the over-parameterized neural network may suffer from under-training Queries where labeled reference data are already perfectly matched and batch-corrected, making the online-tuning machinery unnecessary Annotation tasks solvable by simple label voting on identical gene spaces where adversarial batch alignment risks over-correcting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Adapts a pretrained DIRECTi deep generative model (Cell BLAST) to an independent query dataset via online-tuning, so that low-dimensional cell embeddings align across batch/species and annotations can be transferred through a posterior-distribution-based cell-to-cell similarity search. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Adapts a pretrained DIRECTi deep generative model (Cell BLAST) to an independent query dataset via online-tuning, so that low-dimensional cell embeddings align across batch/species and annotations can be transferred through a posterior-distribution-based cell-to-cell similarity search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells, where the over-parameterized neural network may suffer from under-training Queries where labeled reference data are already perfectly matched and batch-corrected, making the online-tuning machinery unnecessary Annotation tasks solvable by simple label voting on identical gene spaces where adversarial batch alignment risks over-correcting

skills.description: Use when you have a reference scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad/AnnData) and need unbiased low-dimensional cell embeddings robust to batch effect, as input for Cell BLAST querying, benchmarking, or annotation transfer.
skills.name: generative-model-training-single-cell
skills.search_text: generative-model-training-single-cell Use when you have a reference scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad/AnnData) and need unbiased low-dimensional cell embeddings robust to batch effect, as input for Cell BLAST querying, benchmarking, or annotation transfer. The reference dataset is very small (fewer than 1000 cells) — the over-parameterized neural network model may suffer from under-training; ~3000 cells is generally sufficient The goal is integrating datasets at mega-scale with highly skewed cell-type composition, where batch over-correction may occur You only need a generic dimension-reduction result (e.g. plain PCA visualization) and will not use the model for cell-to-cell similarity querying or annotation transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Train the DIRECTi deep generative model (Cell BLAST's neural network-based variational model) on a scRNA-seq reference dataset to learn low-dimensional, batch-corrected cell embeddings that support downstream cell-querying and annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Train the DIRECTi deep generative model (Cell BLAST's neural network-based variational model) on a scRNA-seq reference dataset to learn low-dimensional, batch-corrected cell embeddings that support downstream cell-querying and annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference dataset is very small (fewer than 1000 cells) — the over-parameterized neural network model may suffer from under-training; ~3000 cells is generally sufficient The goal is integrating datasets at mega-scale with highly skewed cell-type composition, where batch over-correction may occur You only need a generic dimension-reduction result (e.g. plain PCA visualization) and will not use the model for cell-to-cell similarity querying or annotation transfer

skills.description: Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq cells for membership in a gene signature (e.g. LM22 cell-type sets from a .gmt file) by counting genes expressed above a threshold, especially on sparse pbmc3k-style count matrices where smoothing should boost detection.
skills.name: geneset-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: geneset-overlap-scoring Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq cells for membership in a gene signature (e.g. LM22 cell-type sets from a .gmt file) by counting genes expressed above a threshold, especially on sparse pbmc3k-style count matrices where smoothing should boost detection. Data is already ranked (ranked expression values) — geneset_overlap counts thresholded expression, while rank-based methods like singscore or ssGSEA require ranked data The goal is magnitude-aware pathway activity rather than binary detection of signature genes above a threshold Analysis is on bulk RNA-seq samples with no per-cell nearest-neighbor graph, where mini-pseudobulk smoothing is not defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-cell gene set overlap scores with gssnng's 'geneset_overlap' method, counting (or fractioning) the number of signature genes expressed past a threshold, optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed AnnData to recover signal lost to sparsity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Computes per-cell gene set overlap scores with gssnng's 'geneset_overlap' method, counting (or fractioning) the number of signature genes expressed past a threshold, optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed AnnData to recover signal lost to sparsity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already ranked (ranked expression values) — geneset_overlap counts thresholded expression, while rank-based methods like singscore or ssGSEA require ranked data The goal is magnitude-aware pathway activity rather than binary detection of signature genes above a threshold Analysis is on bulk RNA-seq samples with no per-cell nearest-neighbor graph, where mini-pseudobulk smoothing is not defined

skills.description: Use when per-cell gene set scores from sparse scRNA-seq count matrices are too noisy for downstream tasks (e.g. AUC discrimination of cell types), and you want scores computed on neighbor-smoothed data in a Scanpy AnnData workflow.
skills.name: geneset-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: geneset-signature-scoring Use when per-cell gene set scores from sparse scRNA-seq count matrices are too noisy for downstream tasks (e.g. AUC discrimination of cell types), and you want scores computed on neighbor-smoothed data in a Scanpy AnnData workflow. When smooth_mode='off' is acceptable, i.e. the count matrix is not sparse/noisy and bulk-style scoring without neighborhood smoothing suffices — smoothing changes per-cell values into neighbor-averaged profiles When the input is bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell AnnData; gssnng is built for scRNA-seq and nearest neighbor graphs of cells When using a scoring method that does not match the data mode — e.g. singscore and ssGSEA require ranked data, while mean_z and robust_std recommend unranked counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Score single-cell RNA-seq cells against gene set signatures (e.g. 'B cells naive' from cibersort_lm22.gmt) using gssnng, which smooths counts on the nearest neighbor graph to create mini-pseudobulk profiles before applying bulk-style single-sample scoring methods such as singscore. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Score single-cell RNA-seq cells against gene set signatures (e.g. 'B cells naive' from cibersort_lm22.gmt) using gssnng, which smooths counts on the nearest neighbor graph to create mini-pseudobulk profiles before applying bulk-style single-sample scoring methods such as singscore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When smooth_mode='off' is acceptable, i.e. the count matrix is not sparse/noisy and bulk-style scoring without neighborhood smoothing suffices — smoothing changes per-cell values into neighbor-averaged profiles When the input is bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell AnnData; gssnng is built for scRNA-seq and nearest neighbor graphs of cells When using a scoring method that does not match the data mode — e.g. singscore and ssGSEA require ranked data, while mean_z and robust_std recommend unranked counts

skills.description: Use when per-gene statistics such as CTMM cell type-specificity or mean-difference measures must be related to gene-level annotations like LOEUF, pLI, enhancer domain score (EDS), or enhancer count.
skills.name: genetic-constraint-score-interpretation
skills.search_text: genetic-constraint-score-interpretation Use when per-gene statistics such as CTMM cell type-specificity or mean-difference measures must be related to gene-level annotations like LOEUF, pLI, enhancer domain score (EDS), or enhancer count. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts rather than per-gene CTMM model outputs — this skill operates on fitted cell type-specificity and mean-difference measures, not single-cell data. The goal is assessing calibration or power of CTMM tests (e.g., via simulations) — decile regression against LOEUF/pLI/EDS tests annotation association, not statistical calibration. The gene set lacks constraint/enhancer annotations (LOEUF, pLI, EDS, enhancer count) for all genes, since decile binning and rank regression cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Relates gene-level genetic constraint and enhancer annotations (LOEUF, pLI, enhancer domain score, enhancer count) to CTMM cell type-specific interindividual variance measures via 10 equal-size decile binning and OLS regression on decile ranks, revealing that LOEUF constraint associates in opposite directions with CTMM specificity versus mean-difference cell type-specificity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Relates gene-level genetic constraint and enhancer annotations (LOEUF, pLI, enhancer domain score, enhancer count) to CTMM cell type-specific interindividual variance measures via 10 equal-size decile binning and OLS regression on decile ranks, revealing that LOEUF constraint associates in opposite directions with CTMM specificity versus mean-difference cell type-specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq counts rather than per-gene CTMM model outputs — this skill operates on fitted cell type-specificity and mean-difference measures, not single-cell data. The goal is assessing calibration or power of CTMM tests (e.g., via simulations) — decile regression against LOEUF/pLI/EDS tests annotation association, not statistical calibration. The gene set lacks constraint/enhancer annotations (LOEUF, pLI, EDS, enhancer count) for all genes, since decile binning and rank regression cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when genotype data (SNPs x samples, binary or additive encoding), binary phenotype labels, covariate classes, and a gene-interaction priors file (PPI edges, pathways, complexes) are available, and the goal is to discover higher-order (k>=2) multi-gene meta-markers associated with the phenotype.
skills.name: genetic-interaction-pattern-mining
skills.search_text: genetic-interaction-pattern-mining Use when genotype data (SNPs x samples, binary or additive encoding), binary phenotype labels, covariate classes, and a gene-interaction priors file (PPI edges, pathways, complexes) are available, and the goal is to discover higher-order (k>=2) multi-gene meta-markers associated with the phenotype. The phenotype labels are not binary case/control — HOGImine's CMH test and the -l file require a binary label vector No gene-interaction priors (PPI network, pathways, complexes) are available and the goal is single-SNP or two-locus interval search — FastCMH or SiNIMin are the appropriate baselines instead Only additive-encoded markers are available and the binary-encoding binary (not hogimine_additive) is used — the additive variant must be selected to match the encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Mine higher-order genetic meta-markers with HOGImine: enumerate connected gene-interaction patterns over SNP intervals in a breadth-first branch-and-bound search, test each pattern with the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) statistic, and control FWER at alpha=0.05 using Tarone pruning with optional Westfall-Young permutation testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Mine higher-order genetic meta-markers with HOGImine: enumerate connected gene-interaction patterns over SNP intervals in a breadth-first branch-and-bound search, test each pattern with the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (CMH) statistic, and control FWER at alpha=0.05 using Tarone pruning with optional Westfall-Young permutation testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The phenotype labels are not binary case/control — HOGImine's CMH test and the -l file require a binary label vector No gene-interaction priors (PPI network, pathways, complexes) are available and the goal is single-SNP or two-locus interval search — FastCMH or SiNIMin are the appropriate baselines instead Only additive-encoded markers are available and the binary-encoding binary (not hogimine_additive) is used — the additive variant must be selected to match the encoding

skills.description: Use when benchmarking higher-order genetic meta-marker miners: you need synthetic SNP data (n=3000 samples, per-gene SNP counts U[3,10]) where the true associated connected subgraph of the gene-interaction prior is known.
skills.name: genetic-meta-marker-ground-truth-annotation
skills.search_text: genetic-meta-marker-ground-truth-annotation Use when benchmarking higher-order genetic meta-marker miners: you need synthetic SNP data (n=3000 samples, per-gene SNP counts U[3,10]) where the true associated connected subgraph of the gene-interaction prior is known. The data are real experimental GWAS samples (e.g. the athaliana avrRpm1 or mmusculus BMC.Mode datasets) — no ground-truth meta-marker exists there, so annotation would be fabricated The goal is running HOGImine for discovery rather than validating a miner against known truth; then only the HOGImine file-format skill is needed A FastCMH-style single-interval benchmark is required — that setting uses one significant interval plus a confounded interval, not a connected multi-gene meta-marker Generates synthetic GWAS datasets in HOGImine format with a planted, fully recorded ground-truth meta-marker (a connected gene subgraph with tunable association strength rho), enabling power and FWER validation of meta-marker discovery algorithms such as HOGImine. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Generates synthetic GWAS datasets in HOGImine format with a planted, fully recorded ground-truth meta-marker (a connected gene subgraph with tunable association strength rho), enabling power and FWER validation of meta-marker discovery algorithms such as HOGImine.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real experimental GWAS samples (e.g. the athaliana avrRpm1 or mmusculus BMC.Mode datasets) — no ground-truth meta-marker exists there, so annotation would be fabricated The goal is running HOGImine for discovery rather than validating a miner against known truth; then only the HOGImine file-format skill is needed A FastCMH-style single-interval benchmark is required — that setting uses one significant interval plus a confounded interval, not a connected multi-gene meta-marker

skills.description: Use when a case/control GWAS-style dataset has SNPs mapped to genes plus a gene-interaction prior (PPI edges, 3-cliques, protein complexes) and you need significant multi-gene marker combinations stronger than FastCMH or SiNIMin can find.
skills.name: genetic-meta-marker-pattern-mining
skills.search_text: genetic-meta-marker-pattern-mining Use when a case/control GWAS-style dataset has SNPs mapped to genes plus a gene-interaction prior (PPI edges, 3-cliques, protein complexes) and you need significant multi-gene marker combinations stronger than FastCMH or SiNIMin can find. The analysis goal is finding contiguous significant intervals with covariate conditioning in a single encoding — FastCMH is the appropriate (lower-order) alternative No SNP-to-gene mapping or gene-interaction prior is available, so the network-restricted search space HOGImine exploits cannot be defined The data are already a summarized feature table rather than a per-SNP genotype matrix (n_SNPs x n_samples) with per-sample labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Discover combinations of genetic markers (genetic meta-markers) statistically associated with a binary phenotype using HOGImine, a pattern-mining algorithm that supports higher-order gene interactions (k up to 4), binary and additive encodings, and network-based priors (PPI networks, genetic pathways, protein complexes) while controlling FWER. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Discover combinations of genetic markers (genetic meta-markers) statistically associated with a binary phenotype using HOGImine, a pattern-mining algorithm that supports higher-order gene interactions (k up to 4), binary and additive encodings, and network-based priors (PPI networks, genetic pathways, protein complexes) while controlling FWER.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is finding contiguous significant intervals with covariate conditioning in a single encoding — FastCMH is the appropriate (lower-order) alternative No SNP-to-gene mapping or gene-interaction prior is available, so the network-restricted search space HOGImine exploits cannot be defined The data are already a summarized feature table rather than a per-SNP genotype matrix (n_SNPs x n_samples) with per-sample labels

skills.description: Use when preparing a CSV of genome annotation for cis-NAT identification with CCIVR and you must confirm the required id/Chr/Strand/Start/End columns (and optional expression columns) exist before running.
skills.name: genome-annotation-csv-validation
skills.search_text: genome-annotation-csv-validation Use when preparing a CSV of genome annotation for cis-NAT identification with CCIVR and you must confirm the required id/Chr/Strand/Start/End columns (and optional expression columns) exist before running. The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) or an unmapped BAM — CCIVR expects already processed RNA-seq data and gene annotations, not raw reads; mapping (STAR), expression profiling (RSEM), and statistics (DESeq2) are done by third-party programs upstream. The CSV lacks one of the five required gene annotation columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) and cannot be restructured — CCIVR will not run correctly on it. The analysis goal is de novo transcriptome assembly or cis-NAT discovery without any genome annotation — tools like NATpipe (Perl, de novo assembled transcriptomes) or NASTI-seq (R) are the appropriate alternatives. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validate and prepare the CSV-formatted gene annotation input required by CCIVR, ensuring the five mandatory columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) are present in any order, optionally with RNA-seq expression columns (TPM, FPKM, fold_change, padj). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Validate and prepare the CSV-formatted gene annotation input required by CCIVR, ensuring the five mandatory columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) are present in any order, optionally with RNA-seq expression columns (TPM, FPKM, fold_change, padj).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) or an unmapped BAM — CCIVR expects already processed RNA-seq data and gene annotations, not raw reads; mapping (STAR), expression profiling (RSEM), and statistics (DESeq2) are done by third-party programs upstream. The CSV lacks one of the five required gene annotation columns (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) and cannot be restructured — CCIVR will not run correctly on it. The analysis goal is de novo transcriptome assembly or cis-NAT discovery without any genome annotation — tools like NATpipe (Perl, de novo assembled transcriptomes) or NASTI-seq (R) are the appropriate alternatives.

skills.description: Use when preparing scTE (or scTEATAC) quantification for single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq alignments and a prebuilt index for the genome assembly (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) is not yet available.
skills.name: genome-annotation-index-building
skills.search_text: genome-annotation-index-building Use when preparing scTE (or scTEATAC) quantification for single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq alignments and a prebuilt index for the genome assembly (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) is not yet available. Input is already a TE-by-cell count matrix or .h5ad/.csv from a previous scTE run — no index is needed at that stage. Reads are aligned to a genome assembly version different from the index assembly (e.g. mm9 or hg19 alignments against an mm10/hg38 index), causing coordinate mismatches. The goal is bulk RNA-seq gene/TE counting with te_counter, which builds its own indices via `te_genome` and does not consume scTE index files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds scTE genome indices that map reads to gene metagenes (from a GTF) and TE metagenes (from a RepeatMasker BED/rmsk file), enabling fast quantification of transposable element expression in single-cell data. It is the prerequisite step before running scTE on BAM/SAM alignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Builds scTE genome indices that map reads to gene metagenes (from a GTF) and TE metagenes (from a RepeatMasker BED/rmsk file), enabling fast quantification of transposable element expression in single-cell data. It is the prerequisite step before running scTE on BAM/SAM alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a TE-by-cell count matrix or .h5ad/.csv from a previous scTE run — no index is needed at that stage. Reads are aligned to a genome assembly version different from the index assembly (e.g. mm9 or hg19 alignments against an mm10/hg38 index), causing coordinate mismatches. The goal is bulk RNA-seq gene/TE counting with te_counter, which builds its own indices via `te_genome` and does not consume scTE index files.

skills.description: Use when reproducing a published annotation result (e.g. peaks2utr 3' UTR counts on T. brucei scRNA-seq) and you must confirm your output GFF3/GTF matches reported totals and new/altered/unchanged partitions.
skills.name: genome-annotation-statistics-verification
skills.search_text: genome-annotation-statistics-verification Use when reproducing a published annotation result (e.g. peaks2utr 3' UTR counts on T. brucei scRNA-seq) and you must confirm your output GFF3/GTF matches reported totals and new/altered/unchanged partitions. The goal is de novo gene prediction or annotating features other than 3' UTRs — peaks2utr only annotates 3' untranslated regions from BAM reads against a given canonical annotation. No canonical GFF/GTF annotation is available to serve as the baseline for classifying UTRs as new, altered, or unchanged. The input BAM is not from a protocol where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends (e.g. not 10x Chromium scRNA-seq), since truncation-point pileups driving the counts depend on soft-clipped polyA-tail reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Verify a reproducible genome annotation run by tallying the annotated features (e.g. 3' UTRs emitted by peaks2utr with source=peaks2utr) against published counts, classifying them as new, altered, or unchanged relative to a canonical annotation, and checking gene coverage proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Verify a reproducible genome annotation run by tallying the annotated features (e.g. 3' UTRs emitted by peaks2utr with source=peaks2utr) against published counts, classifying them as new, altered, or unchanged relative to a canonical annotation, and checking gene coverage proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo gene prediction or annotating features other than 3' UTRs — peaks2utr only annotates 3' untranslated regions from BAM reads against a given canonical annotation. No canonical GFF/GTF annotation is available to serve as the baseline for classifying UTRs as new, altered, or unchanged. The input BAM is not from a protocol where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends (e.g. not 10x Chromium scRNA-seq), since truncation-point pileups driving the counts depend on soft-clipped polyA-tail reads.

skills.description: Use when preparing a genome annotation CSV for CCIVR-style cis-NAT extraction and you need to restrict candidate antisense partners to same-chromosome, opposite-strand genes (e.g., selecting the 1,352 minus-strand X-chromosome genes for the Xist/Tsix FO example).
skills.name: genome-annotation-strand-filtering
skills.search_text: genome-annotation-strand-filtering Use when preparing a genome annotation CSV for CCIVR-style cis-NAT extraction and you need to restrict candidate antisense partners to same-chromosome, opposite-strand genes (e.g., selecting the 1,352 minus-strand X-chromosome genes for the Xist/Tsix FO example). The input annotation lacks strand direction or coordinates — CCIVR's predictions depend on the accuracy of gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in databases, so incomplete columns invalidate the filtering The goal is de novo transcriptome-based NAT discovery rather than annotation-based pair extraction (tools like NATpipe or NASTI-seq are designed for assembled transcriptomes or strand-specific read error rates instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A preprocessing step in CCIVR's cis-NAT identification that partitions an Ensembl gene annotation CSV (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) by strand and chromosome, so that opposite-strand interval comparisons (EB, FO, HH, TT) can be performed per chromosome. In the Xist/Tsix example, this reduces 55,146 mouse GRCm39 genes to 1,352 minus-strand genes on the X chromosome before FO extraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: A preprocessing step in CCIVR's cis-NAT identification that partitions an Ensembl gene annotation CSV (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) by strand and chromosome, so that opposite-strand interval comparisons (EB, FO, HH, TT) can be performed per chromosome. In the Xist/Tsix example, this reduces 55,146 mouse GRCm39 genes to 1,352 minus-strand genes on the X chromosome before FO extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input annotation lacks strand direction or coordinates — CCIVR's predictions depend on the accuracy of gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in databases, so incomplete columns invalidate the filtering The goal is de novo transcriptome-based NAT discovery rather than annotation-based pair extraction (tools like NATpipe or NASTI-seq are designed for assembled transcriptomes or strand-specific read error rates instead)

skills.description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads must be visually validated against real reads at the read-sequence level, e.g. comparing coverage tracks of scReadSim BAM output vs minnow/bowtie2-aligned FASTQ over binned genomic windows.
skills.name: genome-browser-coverage-visualization
skills.search_text: genome-browser-coverage-visualization Use when synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads must be visually validated against real reads at the read-sequence level, e.g. comparing coverage tracks of scReadSim BAM output vs minnow/bowtie2-aligned FASTQ over binned genomic windows. The comparison is at the UMI count-matrix level rather than read coverage over genomic coordinates — scReadSim's synthetic gene-by-cell UMI matrix is the appropriate ground truth for count-level benchmarks instead Benchmarking isoform or alternative-splicing tools — scReadSim's current version lacks isoform-level ground truths, so coverage tracks cannot validate isoform resolution The synthetic reads are not aligned to the same reference genome build (mm10) as the real data, making per-window coverage incomparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Renders per-window sequencing read-coverage tracks for real and synthetic single-cell datasets in an IGV-browser-style plot with an inset close-up, enabling visual alongside quantitative (Spearman/Pearson) comparison of read-level fidelity, e.g. scReadSim (Spearman 0.930) vs minnow (0.065) on chromosome 1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Renders per-window sequencing read-coverage tracks for real and synthetic single-cell datasets in an IGV-browser-style plot with an inset close-up, enabling visual alongside quantitative (Spearman/Pearson) comparison of read-level fidelity, e.g. scReadSim (Spearman 0.930) vs minnow (0.065) on chromosome 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison is at the UMI count-matrix level rather than read coverage over genomic coordinates — scReadSim's synthetic gene-by-cell UMI matrix is the appropriate ground truth for count-level benchmarks instead Benchmarking isoform or alternative-splicing tools — scReadSim's current version lacks isoform-level ground truths, so coverage tracks cannot validate isoform resolution The synthetic reads are not aligned to the same reference genome build (mm10) as the real data, making per-window coverage incomparable

skills.description: Use when quantifying transcript abundances from RNA-seq FASTQ files that feed isoform-level analyses (e.g. CanIsoNet), and transcript identifiers must match a specific Ensembl genome build such as human GRCh37.p13.
skills.name: genome-build-version-matching
skills.search_text: genome-build-version-matching Use when quantifying transcript abundances from RNA-seq FASTQ files that feed isoform-level analyses (e.g. CanIsoNet), and transcript identifiers must match a specific Ensembl genome build such as human GRCh37.p13. Input is already a gene-level count or TPM table — quantifying transcript abundances with a genome-build-matched index is unnecessary Downstream analysis uses gene symbols or a different reference (e.g. GRCh38 transcripts) — an index built on GRCh37.p13 isoforms would misalign identifiers The sample is from an organism whose transcriptome build has not been defined (only human GRCh37.p13 and mouse GRCm38.p6 are supported here) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Build the Kallisto transcriptome index from the Ensembl genome-build-specific cDNA (human GRCh37.p13, mouse GRCm38.p6) so that transcript-level TPM quantification of RNA-seq data remains compatible with the transcript isoform definitions used downstream in CanIsoNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Build the Kallisto transcriptome index from the Ensembl genome-build-specific cDNA (human GRCh37.p13, mouse GRCm38.p6) so that transcript-level TPM quantification of RNA-seq data remains compatible with the transcript isoform definitions used downstream in CanIsoNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-level count or TPM table — quantifying transcript abundances with a genome-build-matched index is unnecessary Downstream analysis uses gene symbols or a different reference (e.g. GRCh38 transcripts) — an index built on GRCh37.p13 isoforms would misalign identifiers The sample is from an organism whose transcriptome build has not been defined (only human GRCh37.p13 and mouse GRCm38.p6 are supported here)

skills.description: Use when a collection of FASTA/MultiLine FASTA/FASTQ datasets (gzipped or not) must be indexed so that future sequence queries can list which datasets contain the query, with bounded RAM, disk footprint, and construction time.
skills.name: genome-collection-index-construction
skills.search_text: genome-collection-index-construction Use when a collection of FASTA/MultiLine FASTA/FASTQ datasets (gzipped or not) must be indexed so that future sequence queries can list which datasets contain the query, with bounded RAM, disk footprint, and construction time. When the goal is precise alignment or full similarity search (e.g. BLAST-like scoring) rather than approximate membership listing of candidate datasets — PAC lists datasets that may contain the query. When the collection contains more than 65,536 files and you cannot raise the encoding (PAC defaults to 16-bit integers, indexing up to 65,636 files; use -e 32 or more). When the system cannot open enough files for the chosen partition count — the README warns to check `ulimit -n` (e.g. 5000) when using -p. http://edamontology.org/topic_3277 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Build a scalable approximate membership query (AMQ) index over thousands to hundreds of thousands of genomic datasets using PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb trees), enabling fast identification of which datasets contain a query sequence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Build a scalable approximate membership query (AMQ) index over thousands to hundreds of thousands of genomic datasets using PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb trees), enabling fast identification of which datasets contain a query sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is precise alignment or full similarity search (e.g. BLAST-like scoring) rather than approximate membership listing of candidate datasets — PAC lists datasets that may contain the query. When the collection contains more than 65,536 files and you cannot raise the encoding (PAC defaults to 16-bit integers, indexing up to 65,636 files; use -e 32 or more). When the system cannot open enough files for the chosen partition count — the README warns to check `ulimit -n` (e.g. 5000) when using -p.

skills.description: Use when annotation reference databases or BED/GFF resources are provided in different genome builds (e.g. hg18, hg19, hg38) than the genome used for read alignment, and coordinates must be converted before overlap-based annotation.
skills.name: genome-coordinate-liftover-harmonization
skills.search_text: genome-coordinate-liftover-harmonization Use when annotation reference databases or BED/GFF resources are provided in different genome builds (e.g. hg18, hg19, hg38) than the genome used for read alignment, and coordinates must be converted before overlap-based annotation. All annotation resources are already in the same build as the aligned reads — no LiftOver step is needed The analysis target is non-human reads; COMPSRA's pre-built LiftOver-harmonized annotation databases cover human hg19/hg38 small RNAs, while unmapped reads go to the Microbe module via BLAST against the UCSC nt database Alignment or annotation must be redone from scratch against a custom genome build not among the pre-built hg19/hg38 resources http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconciles heterogeneous reference genome builds (hg18/hg19/hg38) across small RNA annotation databases so that reads mapped to one genome version can be annotated against all pre-built resources, as implemented internally by COMPSRA using UCSC LiftOver. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Reconciles heterogeneous reference genome builds (hg18/hg19/hg38) across small RNA annotation databases so that reads mapped to one genome version can be annotated against all pre-built resources, as implemented internally by COMPSRA using UCSC LiftOver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All annotation resources are already in the same build as the aligned reads — no LiftOver step is needed The analysis target is non-human reads; COMPSRA's pre-built LiftOver-harmonized annotation databases cover human hg19/hg38 small RNAs, while unmapped reads go to the Microbe module via BLAST against the UCSC nt database Alignment or annotation must be redone from scratch against a custom genome build not among the pre-built hg19/hg38 resources

skills.search_text: genome-coordinate-mapping-of-mirna-loci Use when merging miRNA annotations from multiple public databases and sRNA-Seq predictions for a species with a reference genome, and all loci must be expressed in a single uniform genome coordinate system before selection. The species has no reference genome sequence — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Most sequencing reads do not map to the reference genome — unmapped reads are ignored in the current version, so coordinate mapping would drop those candidates Inputs are already in a single uniform coordinate system on the same reference build — re-translation is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Unifies already annotated miRNAs (from miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) and newly predicted sRNA-Seq-derived miRNA precursors into one genomic coordinate system defined by the reference genome, via iwa-miRNA's miRNATranslate step, so that database annotations and de novo predictions can be merged and compared locus-by-locus. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Unifies already annotated miRNAs (from miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) and newly predicted sRNA-Seq-derived miRNA precursors into one genomic coordinate system defined by the reference genome, via iwa-miRNA's miRNATranslate step, so that database annotations and de novo predictions can be merged and compared locus-by-locus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species has no reference genome sequence — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Most sequencing reads do not map to the reference genome — unmapped reads are ignored in the current version, so coordinate mapping would drop those candidates Inputs are already in a single uniform coordinate system on the same reference build — re-translation is unnecessary

skills.name: genome-fasta-preprocessing-and-header-normalization
skills.search_text: genome-fasta-preprocessing-and-header-normalization Use when a plant reference genome FASTA must be fed into the tncRNA Toolkit or any Bowtie-based small-RNA pipeline that requires 'chr'-prefixed headers, masked tRNA loci, and an index under lib/indexes/<species>. The genome FASTA headers already follow the '>chr[Num]'/'>chrMt'/'>chrPt' convention and a compatible Bowtie index exists in lib/indexes/<species> — re-running normalization and index build is redundant The downstream analysis is generic genome annotation or alignment that must retain unmasked tRNA loci in the reference The analysis targets non-plant or organelle-only workflows where the toolkit's nuclear-vs-organellar ('chrMt'/'chrPt') separation does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3489 Preprocesses a reference genome FASTA for the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline: normalizes FASTA headers to the '>chr[Num]' convention (with '>chrMt' and '>chrPt' for organellar sequences), then builds the Bowtie index after masking tRNA genes plus 50 nt flanks and appending tRNA-derived artificial chromosomes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021

skills.search_text: genome-guided-transcriptome-assembly Use when assembling transcripts from RNA-seq reads aligned to a reference genome and single-aligner assemblers (StringTie2, Scallop) miss transcripts because no single alignment covers all splice junctions, or when benchmarking assembler accuracy.
