skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads must be assigned to a specific haplotype (e.g. for allele-specific alternative splicing counting) and per-sample phased VCFs plus a reference FASTA are available.
skills.name: genome-personalization-from-phased-vcf
skills.search_text: genome-personalization-from-phased-vcf Use when RNA-seq reads must be assigned to a specific haplotype (e.g. for allele-specific alternative splicing counting) and per-sample phased VCFs plus a reference FASTA are available. The variant of interest lies within the alternative exon or is too distant from it — PAIRADISE requires a heterozygous SNP outside but close to the AS event so both alleles can be detected on the same short RNA-seq read Genotypes are unphased or only low-confidence calls exist, since haplotype genome construction and SNP voting both depend on phased heterozygous alleles The goal is whole-genome assembly or calling novel variants — this skill only substitutes known phased alleles into a reference and re-assigns reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs two haplotype-modified personal genomes by substituting phased heterozygous alleles from per-chromosome VCFs into hg19.fa, aligns RNA-seq reads to both with STAR, and assigns each uniquely-aligned read to haplotype 1 or 2 via majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs — the rPGA-style personalization used to feed PAIRADISE's allele-specific counting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Constructs two haplotype-modified personal genomes by substituting phased heterozygous alleles from per-chromosome VCFs into hg19.fa, aligns RNA-seq reads to both with STAR, and assigns each uniquely-aligned read to haplotype 1 or 2 via majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs — the rPGA-style personalization used to feed PAIRADISE's allele-specific counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant of interest lies within the alternative exon or is too distant from it — PAIRADISE requires a heterozygous SNP outside but close to the AS event so both alleles can be detected on the same short RNA-seq read Genotypes are unphased or only low-confidence calls exist, since haplotype genome construction and SNP voting both depend on phased heterozygous alleles The goal is whole-genome assembly or calling novel variants — this skill only substitutes known phased alleles into a reference and re-assigns reads

skills.description: Use when transcriptomic data (bulk RNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or cell-cluster expression profiles) must be converted into reaction-level flux distributions under a defined nutrient medium, e.g. nutrient-aware cancer metabolism analysis of TCGA or single-cell TME data.
skills.name: genome-scale-metabolic-modeling
skills.search_text: genome-scale-metabolic-modeling Use when transcriptomic data (bulk RNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or cell-cluster expression profiles) must be converted into reaction-level flux distributions under a defined nutrient medium, e.g. nutrient-aware cancer metabolism analysis of TCGA or single-cell TME data. When the goal is direct measurement of extracellular fluxes or metabolite concentrations — use Seahorse XF analyzer, LC/MS, or MALDI-MS instead of transcriptome-inferred fluxes When input is not gene expression but an already-computed flux or reaction-score table — skip MRAS/GPR mapping and go straight to flux solving When nutrient availability is unknown or the experiment does not fit binary nutrient presence/absence conditions — medium definition is required for uptake-restricted bounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Predict sample- and cell-type-specific metabolic fluxes by constraining a genome-scale metabolic model (Human-GEM, 13,082 reactions / 8,378 metabolites) with gene-expression-derived reaction activity scores and solving a parsimonious convex-QP FBA problem with osqp. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Predict sample- and cell-type-specific metabolic fluxes by constraining a genome-scale metabolic model (Human-GEM, 13,082 reactions / 8,378 metabolites) with gene-expression-derived reaction activity scores and solving a parsimonious convex-QP FBA problem with osqp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct measurement of extracellular fluxes or metabolite concentrations — use Seahorse XF analyzer, LC/MS, or MALDI-MS instead of transcriptome-inferred fluxes When input is not gene expression but an already-computed flux or reaction-score table — skip MRAS/GPR mapping and go straight to flux solving When nutrient availability is unknown or the experiment does not fit binary nutrient presence/absence conditions — medium definition is required for uptake-restricted bounds

skills.description: Use when performing allele-specific expression (ASE) analysis in an F1 hybrid cross (e.g., CAST×B6) and reads must be assigned to parental origin via a strain-specific or diploid reference rather than a single generic reference genome.
skills.name: genome-sequence-reconstruction-with-variant-masking
skills.search_text: genome-sequence-reconstruction-with-variant-masking Use when performing allele-specific expression (ASE) analysis in an F1 hybrid cross (e.g., CAST×B6) and reads must be assigned to parental origin via a strain-specific or diploid reference rather than a single generic reference genome. The analysis discards multi-mapping reads (unique-reads counting); even so a diploid reference may still be needed, but the '--all --best --strata' multi-read retention strategy is wasted effort The cross is not between known, well-annotated strains — without a reliable SNP/indel variant set for the parental strain, reconstruction cannot be performed The data are bulk RNA-Seq or already provide allele-specific alignments from another pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs a strain-specific (CAST/EiJ) genome by incorporating known SNPs and short indels (Sanger REL-1505) into the GRCm38 mouse reference using g2gtools, enabling construction of a phase-known diploid transcriptome for allele-specific read alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Reconstructs a strain-specific (CAST/EiJ) genome by incorporating known SNPs and short indels (Sanger REL-1505) into the GRCm38 mouse reference using g2gtools, enabling construction of a phase-known diploid transcriptome for allele-specific read alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis discards multi-mapping reads (unique-reads counting); even so a diploid reference may still be needed, but the '--all --best --strata' multi-read retention strategy is wasted effort The cross is not between known, well-annotated strains — without a reliable SNP/indel variant set for the parental strain, reconstruction cannot be performed The data are bulk RNA-Seq or already provide allele-specific alignments from another pipeline

skills.description: Use when NanoSpeech basecalled fasta/q read headers carry modification (inosine or multi-mod) indexes and you need them mapped to reference coordinates and aggregated into per-site modification counts/frequencies.
skills.name: genome-space-modification-aggregation
skills.search_text: genome-space-modification-aggregation Use when NanoSpeech basecalled fasta/q read headers carry modification (inosine or multi-mod) indexes and you need them mapped to reference coordinates and aggregated into per-site modification counts/frequencies. Reads were basecalled with a modification-unaware basecaller (standard Guppy/Dorado), so no modification indexes exist in the fasta/q headers for the detector scripts to convert The BAM is not filtered (e.g. secondary/supplementary alignments not removed with 'samtools view -b -F 2304'), sorted, and indexed You need ab initio modification detection from raw currents — that is the basecalling step (NanoSpeech.py / NanoSpeech_multi_mod.py), not this aggregation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Converts per-read modification calls from NanoSpeech modification-aware basecalling into reference-coordinate annotations and aggregated genome/transcriptome-space modification counts and frequencies, using NanoSpeech's accessory detector scripts on sorted, indexed BAM files. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf709
skills.summary: Converts per-read modification calls from NanoSpeech modification-aware basecalling into reference-coordinate annotations and aggregated genome/transcriptome-space modification counts and frequencies, using NanoSpeech's accessory detector scripts on sorted, indexed BAM files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads were basecalled with a modification-unaware basecaller (standard Guppy/Dorado), so no modification indexes exist in the fasta/q headers for the detector scripts to convert The BAM is not filtered (e.g. secondary/supplementary alignments not removed with 'samtools view -b -F 2304'), sorted, and indexed You need ab initio modification detection from raw currents — that is the basecalling step (NanoSpeech.py / NanoSpeech_multi_mod.py), not this aggregation step

skills.description: Use when phasiRNA/siRNA clusters were predicted separately against a reference genome and a reference transcriptome and need to be unified into a single, deduplicated PHAS locus set with gene annotations.
skills.name: genome-transcriptome-coordinate-transform
skills.search_text: genome-transcriptome-coordinate-transform Use when phasiRNA/siRNA clusters were predicted separately against a reference genome and a reference transcriptome and need to be unified into a single, deduplicated PHAS locus set with gene annotations. Predictions were made on only a single reference sequence (no genome/transcriptome duality), so there is nothing to transform or merge — use the phase module outputs directly instead. Input cluster files are not phase module outputs (phase_o.txt/phase_a.txt) or the annotation is not GFF3 format, since the integration module expects these specific file types. The analysis only needs raw phasiRNA cluster prediction with no cross-reference unification or gene annotation — the phase module alone suffices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 PhasiHunter's integration step merges phasiRNA/all-siRNA cluster predictions made independently on cDNA (transcriptome) and gDNA (genome) references by transforming coordinates between the two reference systems with bedtools and a Python3 dictionary data structure, then deduplicating, merging, annotating, and classifying clusters against GFF3 gene annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: PhasiHunter's integration step merges phasiRNA/all-siRNA cluster predictions made independently on cDNA (transcriptome) and gDNA (genome) references by transforming coordinates between the two reference systems with bedtools and a Python3 dictionary data structure, then deduplicating, merging, annotating, and classifying clusters against GFF3 gene annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions were made on only a single reference sequence (no genome/transcriptome duality), so there is nothing to transform or merge — use the phase module outputs directly instead. Input cluster files are not phase module outputs (phase_o.txt/phase_a.txt) or the annotation is not GFF3 format, since the integration module expects these specific file types. The analysis only needs raw phasiRNA cluster prediction with no cross-reference unification or gene annotation — the phase module alone suffices.

skills.description: Use when you have BIRD-predicted DH matrices (log2(x+1)) plus true DNase-seq profiles for multiple cell types and need to quantify prediction accuracy overall, for differential DH, or versus ChromImpute.
skills.name: genome-wide-dh-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: genome-wide-dh-prediction-evaluation Use when you have BIRD-predicted DH matrices (log2(x+1)) plus true DNase-seq profiles for multiple cell types and need to quantify prediction accuracy overall, for differential DH, or versus ChromImpute. You only have a single cell type and no matched true DNase-seq track — there is no ground truth to compute prediction–truth correlations against You want BIRD to discover novel DHS locations not present in the training loci — BIRD will not discover new DHS locations when applied to a new gene expression sample Input expression data is exon array raw CEL output that has not yet been processed by GeneBASE into a gene expression file http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Evaluates BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) profiles against true DNase-seq data by computing per-pair and per-locus Pearson correlations, stratifying cell-type pairs by DH-profile similarity quartiles, and benchmarking against ChromImpute imputation. This quantifies how well gene-expression-based prediction recovers genome-wide regulatory element activity, especially for differential DH between similar cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Evaluates BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) profiles against true DNase-seq data by computing per-pair and per-locus Pearson correlations, stratifying cell-type pairs by DH-profile similarity quartiles, and benchmarking against ChromImpute imputation. This quantifies how well gene-expression-based prediction recovers genome-wide regulatory element activity, especially for differential DH between similar cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single cell type and no matched true DNase-seq track — there is no ground truth to compute prediction–truth correlations against You want BIRD to discover novel DHS locations not present in the training loci — BIRD will not discover new DHS locations when applied to a new gene expression sample Input expression data is exon array raw CEL output that has not yet been processed by GeneBASE into a gene expression file

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample attention-head features from a pretrained tGPT model over tumor bulk transcriptomes and need to link them to mutation, HRD, genome-doubling, TMB, or survival annotations.
skills.name: genomic-alteration-significance-testing
skills.search_text: genomic-alteration-significance-testing Use when you have per-sample attention-head features from a pretrained tGPT model over tumor bulk transcriptomes and need to link them to mutation, HRD, genome-doubling, TMB, or survival annotations. Input is single-cell data for clustering or trajectory tasks — tGPT attention-head alteration testing targets bulk tumor tissue feature patterns You lack per-sample genomic alteration or survival annotations — the regression tests cannot be run on embeddings alone Only actual expression levels (not gene expression rankings) are available and cannot be rank-transformed — tGPT input requires ranked top-expressing genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Tests whether tGPT attention-head entropy/importance features computed from tumor bulk transcriptomes are significantly associated with genomic alteration events (TMB, TP53 mutation, HRD, genome doubling) and overall survival, using regression-based testing per cancer type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Tests whether tGPT attention-head entropy/importance features computed from tumor bulk transcriptomes are significantly associated with genomic alteration events (TMB, TP53 mutation, HRD, genome doubling) and overall survival, using regression-based testing per cancer type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data for clustering or trajectory tasks — tGPT attention-head alteration testing targets bulk tumor tissue feature patterns You lack per-sample genomic alteration or survival annotations — the regression tests cannot be run on embeddings alone Only actual expression levels (not gene expression rankings) are available and cannot be rank-transformed — tGPT input requires ranked top-expressing genes

skills.description: Use when you have a GFF/GTF gene model plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) and need to annotate or refine 3' UTR features at the genome level.
skills.name: genomic-annotation-command-line-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: genomic-annotation-command-line-workflow-execution Use when you have a GFF/GTF gene model plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) and need to annotate or refine 3' UTR features at the genome level. You already have a validated 3' UTR annotation and only need generic GFF format conversion or validation — use GenomeTools alone instead of the peaks2utr pipeline. Input reads lack UTR-distal signal (e.g. not 3' enriched single-cell or similar data), so MACS peak calls will not concentrate at UTR distal ends as the method expects. The task is 5' UTR or CDS annotation rather than 3' UTR annotation from BAM peaks. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run peaks2utr, a Python 3 CLI that annotates 3' UTRs from a canonical GFF/GTF annotation and a BAM of aligned reads, leveraging MACS3-called broad peaks and SPAT truncation points. This skill covers installing the toolchain, invoking the pipeline, and validating its GFF3 output. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Run peaks2utr, a Python 3 CLI that annotates 3' UTRs from a canonical GFF/GTF annotation and a BAM of aligned reads, leveraging MACS3-called broad peaks and SPAT truncation points. This skill covers installing the toolchain, invoking the pipeline, and validating its GFF3 output.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a validated 3' UTR annotation and only need generic GFF format conversion or validation — use GenomeTools alone instead of the peaks2utr pipeline. Input reads lack UTR-distal signal (e.g. not 3' enriched single-cell or similar data), so MACS peak calls will not concentrate at UTR distal ends as the method expects. The task is 5' UTR or CDS annotation rather than 3' UTR annotation from BAM peaks.

skills.description: Use when a set of variants or genes identified by identifiers (GENCODE v19 gene symbols and/or Ensembl gene IDs) must be joined to per-gene quantitative scores (MRSD read depths) across biosamples to yield a per-variant classification and an aggregate fraction.
skills.name: genomic-annotation-cross-referencing
skills.search_text: genomic-annotation-cross-referencing Use when a set of variants or genes identified by identifiers (GENCODE v19 gene symbols and/or Ensembl gene IDs) must be joined to per-gene quantitative scores (MRSD read depths) across biosamples to yield a per-variant classification and an aggregate fraction. The goal is assessment of differential gene expression or allele-specific expression, which the MRSD model was not designed to predict. The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved; MRSD was validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment RNA-seq processed with the Cummings et al. pipeline. Gene identifiers are not GENCODE v19-compatible symbols or Ensembl gene IDs, so they cannot be matched to the .results.mrsd.txt id1/id2 columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Cross-references a variant-anchored gene list (e.g., SpliceAI-prioritized ClinVar VUS-harboring genes) against gene-level MRSD score tables (.results.mrsd.txt) computed for multiple GTEx-derived biosamples, to classify each gene as low- or high-MRSD and quantify the fraction of variants assayable by RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Cross-references a variant-anchored gene list (e.g., SpliceAI-prioritized ClinVar VUS-harboring genes) against gene-level MRSD score tables (.results.mrsd.txt) computed for multiple GTEx-derived biosamples, to classify each gene as low- or high-MRSD and quantify the fraction of variants assayable by RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is assessment of differential gene expression or allele-specific expression, which the MRSD model was not designed to predict. The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved; MRSD was validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment RNA-seq processed with the Cummings et al. pipeline. Gene identifiers are not GENCODE v19-compatible symbols or Ensembl gene IDs, so they cannot be matched to the .results.mrsd.txt id1/id2 columns.

skills.description: Use when raw N*N single-cell Hi-C contact matrices are sparse and biased by local genomic features (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) and must be normalized before DCI testing with scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB.
skills.name: genomic-bias-correction-with-local-features
skills.search_text: genomic-bias-correction-with-local-features Use when raw N*N single-cell Hi-C contact matrices are sparse and biased by local genomic features (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) and must be normalized before DCI testing with scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB. The input count table is already a matrix of normalized scHi-C read counts (as in the sample data sim 1.rds) ready for detection functions — re-normalizing would double-correct the bias. The data is bulk Hi-C interaction counts rather than single-cell contact matrices, since the imputation and cell-specific distance normalization target single-cell sparsity. You lack the bias information file (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) for the bins and cannot generate it, as scHiCDiff.norm requires it as a mandatory input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Normalizes sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices with scHiCDiff by first imputing contacts via a Gaussian convolution filter, then removing systematic biases (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) using the scHiCNorm Negative Binomial Hurdle procedure plus cell-specific genomic-distance normalization, so detection functions receive bias-corrected counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Normalizes sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices with scHiCDiff by first imputing contacts via a Gaussian convolution filter, then removing systematic biases (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) using the scHiCNorm Negative Binomial Hurdle procedure plus cell-specific genomic-distance normalization, so detection functions receive bias-corrected counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input count table is already a matrix of normalized scHi-C read counts (as in the sample data sim 1.rds) ready for detection functions — re-normalizing would double-correct the bias. The data is bulk Hi-C interaction counts rather than single-cell contact matrices, since the imputation and cell-specific distance normalization target single-cell sparsity. You lack the bias information file (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) for the bins and cannot generate it, as scHiCDiff.norm requires it as a mandatory input.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DE or gene set enrichment methods on scRNA-seq summary statistics and you need to check p-value calibration via a genomic control factor (lambda_gc), as in the iDEA paper's Fig. 4 comparison.
skills.name: genomic-control-inflation-assessment-lambda-gc
skills.search_text: genomic-control-inflation-assessment-lambda-gc Use when benchmarking DE or gene set enrichment methods on scRNA-seq summary statistics and you need to check p-value calibration via a genomic control factor (lambda_gc), as in the iDEA paper's Fig. 4 comparison. When the summary statistics come from inferred cell types whose DE test statistics may be inflated with artificially smaller standard errors — inflation may reflect a modeling artifact rather than method miscalibration When you only need enrichment power (gene set counts at FDR 5%) without any p-value calibration assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the lambda_gc genomic control factor from DE or GSE summary statistics to quantify test-statistic inflation when benchmarking scRNA-seq methods such as iDEA, fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA and zingeR on the Chu et al. human ESC (DEC vs EC) dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Computes the lambda_gc genomic control factor from DE or GSE summary statistics to quantify test-statistic inflation when benchmarking scRNA-seq methods such as iDEA, fGSEA, CAMERA, PAGE, GSEA and zingeR on the Chu et al. human ESC (DEC vs EC) dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the summary statistics come from inferred cell types whose DE test statistics may be inflated with artificially smaller standard errors — inflation may reflect a modeling artifact rather than method miscalibration When you only need enrichment power (gene set counts at FDR 5%) without any p-value calibration assessment

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a competitive GSE method (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) yields well-calibrated p-values under null simulations on zero-inflated scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: genomic-control-inflation-factor-estimation
skills.search_text: genomic-control-inflation-factor-estimation Use when benchmarking whether a competitive GSE method (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) yields well-calibrated p-values under null simulations on zero-inflated scRNA-seq data. When simulations embed true DE signal or gene-set enrichment (non-null tau1) — lambda_gc then reflects real signal, not miscalibration When only a handful of gene-set p-values are available; lambda_gc and QQ plots need many p-values aggregated across replicates to be informative http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assess null p-value calibration of gene set enrichment methods by aggregating gene-set p-values per method and coverage rate, computing the genomic-control inflation factor lambda_gc, and drawing observed-vs-expected quantile-quantile plots to detect inflation or over-conservatism. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Assess null p-value calibration of gene set enrichment methods by aggregating gene-set p-values per method and coverage rate, computing the genomic-control inflation factor lambda_gc, and drawing observed-vs-expected quantile-quantile plots to detect inflation or over-conservatism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When simulations embed true DE signal or gene-set enrichment (non-null tau1) — lambda_gc then reflects real signal, not miscalibration When only a handful of gene-set p-values are available; lambda_gc and QQ plots need many p-values aggregated across replicates to be informative

skills.description: Use when two genome-wide DH or regulome track sets (e.g., BIRD predictions and ChromImpute imputations) must be compared across shared loci and cell types, requiring coordinate/locus matching before correlation.
skills.name: genomic-coordinate-alignment-of-prediction-tracks
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-alignment-of-prediction-tracks Use when two genome-wide DH or regulome track sets (e.g., BIRD predictions and ChromImpute imputations) must be compared across shared loci and cell types, requiring coordinate/locus matching before correlation. When only one prediction track exists and no reference (e.g., ChromImpute) track is available for comparison — there is nothing to align against. When the two tracks are on different genome builds (e.g., hg19 vs hg38) and no liftover/reconciliation is possible — coordinate matching would silently fail or mismatch loci. When the goal is de novo DHS discovery rather than comparing existing tracks — BIRD will not discover new DHS locations, so locus-level alignment to new coordinates is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aligns genome-wide prediction tracks (e.g., BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity) against reference imputation tracks (e.g., ChromImpute DH) on shared genomic loci in hg19/hg38 coordinates so that per-cell-type cross-locus and per-locus cross-cell-type agreement can be computed in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Aligns genome-wide prediction tracks (e.g., BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity) against reference imputation tracks (e.g., ChromImpute DH) on shared genomic loci in hg19/hg38 coordinates so that per-cell-type cross-locus and per-locus cross-cell-type agreement can be computed in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one prediction track exists and no reference (e.g., ChromImpute) track is available for comparison — there is nothing to align against. When the two tracks are on different genome builds (e.g., hg19 vs hg38) and no liftover/reconciliation is possible — coordinate matching would silently fail or mismatch loci. When the goal is de novo DHS discovery rather than comparing existing tracks — BIRD will not discover new DHS locations, so locus-level alignment to new coordinates is out of scope.

skills.description: Use when per-nucleotide scores (e.g. RSCanner structure counts) must be aggregated into fixed non-overlapping windows along a transcript to rank regions, e.g. locating high-structure-density segments in a long RNA.
skills.name: genomic-coordinate-binning
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-binning Use when per-nucleotide scores (e.g. RSCanner structure counts) must be aggregated into fixed non-overlapping windows along a transcript to rank regions, e.g. locating high-structure-density segments in a long RNA. When per-nucleotide resolution is required (e.g. mapping individual base-paired positions) — binning to 100-nt windows deliberately aggregates away single-nucleotide detail. When the input is already a binned/region-level table (e.g. an existing ordered_structure_table.csv) rather than per-nucleotide structure counts. When regions of interest have irregular or biologically defined boundaries rather than the fixed non-overlapping windows RSCanner tiles along the RNA. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Tiles a transcript with non-overlapping fixed-length coordinate bins (RSCanner default: 100 nt) and aggregates per-nucleotide structure counts into percent structure content per bin, enabling ranked comparison of sub-regions across an RNA such as the HCV_Jc1 genome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Tiles a transcript with non-overlapping fixed-length coordinate bins (RSCanner default: 100 nt) and aggregates per-nucleotide structure counts into percent structure content per bin, enabling ranked comparison of sub-regions across an RNA such as the HCV_Jc1 genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When per-nucleotide resolution is required (e.g. mapping individual base-paired positions) — binning to 100-nt windows deliberately aggregates away single-nucleotide detail. When the input is already a binned/region-level table (e.g. an existing ordered_structure_table.csv) rather than per-nucleotide structure counts. When regions of interest have irregular or biologically defined boundaries rather than the fixed non-overlapping windows RSCanner tiles along the RNA.

skills.description: Use when merging already annotated miRNAs from heterogeneous databases (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) with novel sRNA-Seq-derived precursor predictions that use inconsistent coordinate representations.
skills.name: genomic-coordinate-format-unification
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-format-unification Use when merging already annotated miRNAs from heterogeneous databases (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) with novel sRNA-Seq-derived precursor predictions that use inconsistent coordinate representations. sRNA-Seq data from species without reference genome sequences — reads that do not map to the reference genome are ignored, so coordinate unification against a genome is impossible Downstream candidate selection — use the miRNASelection / manualCuration modules once the uniform candidate list exists http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Harmonizes miRNA annotations retrieved from multiple public databases and newly predicted precursors into a single uniform genomic coordinate system (GFF3), enabling their merger into one candidate precursor list in iwa-miRNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Harmonizes miRNA annotations retrieved from multiple public databases and newly predicted precursors into a single uniform genomic coordinate system (GFF3), enabling their merger into one candidate precursor list in iwa-miRNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: sRNA-Seq data from species without reference genome sequences — reads that do not map to the reference genome are ignored, so coordinate unification against a genome is impossible Downstream candidate selection — use the miRNASelection / manualCuration modules once the uniform candidate list exists

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted UTR (or other interval) coordinates from multiple tools against a reference annotation and you need a tolerant agreement fraction rather than exact-match counting.
skills.name: genomic-coordinate-overlap-comparison
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-overlap-comparison Use when comparing predicted UTR (or other interval) coordinates from multiple tools against a reference annotation and you need a tolerant agreement fraction rather than exact-match counting. The input is already a summary table of agreement fractions rather than raw coordinate annotations needing comparison. skills.search_text: genomic-sequence-bin-feature-extraction Use when you need per-position (binned) DNA sequence and/or RNA-Seq coverage features over transcript 3' terminal exons from a GTF to feed a sequence+coverage machine-learning model such as aptardi's biLSTM. Your goal is full transcript assembly including intron junctions — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons of the input transcripts and does not evaluate intron junctions You need resolution finer than the bin width for polyA site localization — aptardi annotates only the 3'-most base of a positive 100-base bin, while true sites wiggle up to 30 nucleotides Your input is already a binned feature table or you are using the pre-built HBR model with a non-default bin size — the pre-built model requires 100-base bins http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Builds fixed-width binned feature representations of DNA sequence (and aligned RNA-Seq coverage) over transcript regions, as implemented in aptardi, which bins the genome into 100-base windows spanning the 3' terminal exons of an input transcriptome to train a biLSTM polyadenylation-site classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Builds fixed-width binned feature representations of DNA sequence (and aligned RNA-Seq coverage) over transcript regions, as implemented in aptardi, which bins the genome into 100-base windows spanning the 3' terminal exons of an input transcriptome to train a biLSTM polyadenylation-site classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is full transcript assembly including intron junctions — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons of the input transcripts and does not evaluate intron junctions You need resolution finer than the bin width for polyA site localization — aptardi annotates only the 3'-most base of a positive 100-base bin, while true sites wiggle up to 30 nucleotides Your input is already a binned feature table or you are using the pre-built HBR model with a non-default bin size — the pre-built model requires 100-base bins

skills.description: Use when one or few DNase-seq (or ChIP-seq) replicates are available and a BIRD-predicted DH track can be merged with observed signal on shared genomic bins, then benchmarked against a held-out truth replicate via genome-wide Pearson correlation.
skills.name: genomic-track-alignment-and-integration
skills.search_text: genomic-track-alignment-and-integration Use when one or few DNase-seq (or ChIP-seq) replicates are available and a BIRD-predicted DH track can be merged with observed signal on shared genomic bins, then benchmarked against a held-out truth replicate via genome-wide Pearson correlation. The goal is to discover novel DHS locations — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs, it only predicts activity at ~1M pre-defined genomic loci No held-out replicate is available to validate the combined profile — the acceptance criterion (combined > observed-only Pearson correlation) cannot be evaluated Observed tracks are on a different genome build than the model (e.g. hg38 DNase-seq data with the hg19 model) without lifting coordinates to the model's bin frame http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) tracks with observed ENCODE DNase-seq replicates on the hg19 genomic bin coordinates used by the model, then combines them into a BIRD-augmented pseudo-replicate profile to boost signal in low replicate or low signal-to-noise settings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Aligns BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) tracks with observed ENCODE DNase-seq replicates on the hg19 genomic bin coordinates used by the model, then combines them into a BIRD-augmented pseudo-replicate profile to boost signal in low replicate or low signal-to-noise settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to discover novel DHS locations — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs, it only predicts activity at ~1M pre-defined genomic loci No held-out replicate is available to validate the combined profile — the acceptance criterion (combined > observed-only Pearson correlation) cannot be evaluated Observed tracks are on a different genome build than the model (e.g. hg38 DNase-seq data with the hg19 model) without lifting coordinates to the model's bin frame

skills.description: Use when you have a list of genetic variants (e.g. lead sQTLs from sQTLseekeR2) and two disjoint genomic interval sets, and need to test whether variants are preferentially located in one set (e.g. ps introns) versus the other (cs introns).
skills.name: genomic-variant-interval-overlap
skills.search_text: genomic-variant-interval-overlap Use when you have a list of genetic variants (e.g. lead sQTLs from sQTLseekeR2) and two disjoint genomic interval sets, and need to test whether variants are preferentially located in one set (e.g. ps introns) versus the other (cs introns). When the goal is fine-mapping or colocalization of sQTL/eQTL effects — the article notes available methods are 'not directly applicable within our multivariate, non-parametric framework' and LD confounds paired-effect interpretation When testing enrichment of variant properties (e.g. RBP binding site disruption) rather than overlap with interval sets — this skill only handles counts of variants per interval class When the variant-to-interval statistic should account for LD structure between lead variants — the default pipeline runs with LD-based variant clustering disabled (ld threshold 0) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Intersects mapped sQTL lead variants with curated genomic interval sets — here co- vs post-transcriptionally spliced (cs/ps) introns defined from ENCODE nuclear/cytosolic RNA-seq splicing kinetics — and uses Fisher's exact test to quantify enrichment of variants in one interval class. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Intersects mapped sQTL lead variants with curated genomic interval sets — here co- vs post-transcriptionally spliced (cs/ps) introns defined from ENCODE nuclear/cytosolic RNA-seq splicing kinetics — and uses Fisher's exact test to quantify enrichment of variants in one interval class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is fine-mapping or colocalization of sQTL/eQTL effects — the article notes available methods are 'not directly applicable within our multivariate, non-parametric framework' and LD confounds paired-effect interpretation When testing enrichment of variant properties (e.g. RBP binding site disruption) rather than overlap with interval sets — this skill only handles counts of variants per interval class When the variant-to-interval statistic should account for LD structure between lead variants — the default pipeline runs with LD-based variant clustering disabled (ld threshold 0)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking candidate reference-gene (RG) combinations from a qPCR array (raw CT matrix, e.g. data_GSE78870/data_GSE50013) and you need GeNorm and NormFinder stability measures for each weighted k-gene combination.
skills.name: genorm-normfinder-stability-measure-computation
skills.search_text: genorm-normfinder-stability-measure-computation Use when benchmarking candidate reference-gene (RG) combinations from a qPCR array (raw CT matrix, e.g. data_GSE78870/data_GSE50013) and you need GeNorm and NormFinder stability measures for each weighted k-gene combination. Input is already normalized expression or RNA-seq counts rather than raw CT values from a qPCR array — the pipeline expects CT matrices and normalizes internally with norm_method='high_exp' and norm_method_exp_thr=35. You only need SD/CV stability of combinations — adding algors=c('Genorm','NormFinder') requires building InterOptCuda with nvcc and a CUDA-capable GPU, which is unnecessary overhead otherwise. Candidate miRNAs have missing/high CT values — miRNAs with CT>37 in any sample are excluded by the rowSums(data>37)==0 filter, so datasets dominated by such genes yield too few candidates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes GeNorm and NormFinder stability measures for weighted reference-gene (RG) combinations in qPCR CT data, using InterOpt's run_experiment() with the GPU-accelerated InterOptCuda kernel alongside SD and CV measures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107945
skills.summary: Computes GeNorm and NormFinder stability measures for weighted reference-gene (RG) combinations in qPCR CT data, using InterOpt's run_experiment() with the GPU-accelerated InterOptCuda kernel alongside SD and CV measures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized expression or RNA-seq counts rather than raw CT values from a qPCR array — the pipeline expects CT matrices and normalizes internally with norm_method='high_exp' and norm_method_exp_thr=35. You only need SD/CV stability of combinations — adding algors=c('Genorm','NormFinder') requires building InterOptCuda with nvcc and a CUDA-capable GPU, which is unnecessary overhead otherwise. Candidate miRNAs have missing/high CT values — miRNAs with CT>37 in any sample are excluded by the rowSums(data>37)==0 filter, so datasets dominated by such genes yield too few candidates.

skills.description: Use when you have 10X scRNA-seq data (possorted_genome_bam.bam + barcodes.tsv) from a multi-person blood mixture, with live cells, and need genotype-based single-cell separation of contributors — especially imbalanced mixtures at ratios up to 1:60.
skills.name: genotype-based-single-cell-deconvolution
skills.search_text: genotype-based-single-cell-deconvolution Use when you have 10X scRNA-seq data (possorted_genome_bam.bam + barcodes.tsv) from a multi-person blood mixture, with live cells, and need genotype-based single-cell separation of contributors — especially imbalanced mixtures at ratios up to 1:60. The mixture cells are fixed or non-living — the 10X Genomics platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation, and fixed-cell platforms have not been tested The goal is appearance-trait prediction from the separated contributors — the specific SNPs needed for appearance prediction were not obtained in this approach The mixture is from a non-blood tissue — transferability to biological mixtures other than blood has not yet been demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Separates individuals in multi-person biological mixtures by genotyping each 10X scRNA-seq cell (via freebayes variant calling of expressed SNPs) and clustering cells by genotype with the de-goulash Snakemake pipeline, enabling downstream sex, ancestry, and individual identification of contributors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Separates individuals in multi-person biological mixtures by genotyping each 10X scRNA-seq cell (via freebayes variant calling of expressed SNPs) and clustering cells by genotype with the de-goulash Snakemake pipeline, enabling downstream sex, ancestry, and individual identification of contributors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mixture cells are fixed or non-living — the 10X Genomics platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation, and fixed-cell platforms have not been tested The goal is appearance-trait prediction from the separated contributors — the specific SNPs needed for appearance prediction were not obtained in this approach The mixture is from a non-blood tissue — transferability to biological mixtures other than blood has not yet been demonstrated

skills.description: Use when a raw genotype matrix (columns chr, start, end, snpId; alleles coded 0=REF/REF, 1=REF/ALT, 2=ALT/ALT, -1=missing) must be filtered to well-powered biallelic variants before sQTL association testing.

skills.summary: Preprocesses genotype matrices for sQTL mapping by retaining only biallelic SNPs/indels with minor allele frequency >= 0.01 and sufficient per-genotype-group sample counts, reproducing the sQTLseekeR2 default variant filters applied to GTEx V7 in the sqtlseeker2-nf pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant table is already the filtered sQTLseekeR2 input (e.g. it already contains only the ~3.6M passing biallelic variants) The goal is a single-tissue eQTL/expression analysis where MAF and per-genotype-group counts were set by a different consortium standard (e.g. GTEx V8 eQTL filters) The genotype data are multiallelic or structural variants that must be decomposed/recodeed before dosage-based filtering applies

skills.search_text: geo-dataset-retrieval Use when the goal is to reproduce a published differential methylation analysis from raw array data, and the source dataset (e.g., GSE207426) is available on GEO as IDAT files with a sample sheet. The analysis starts from already normalized beta-value matrices — methylR's ChAMP module expects raw IDAT input, so only downstream modules (Volcano plot, PCA/MDS, enrichment) apply to preprocessed tables. The dataset is not a DNA methylation array study (e.g., WGBS or RNA-seq), since methylR covers 450K and EPIC Illumina arrays only. Only a quick functionality check of the interface is needed — use the bundled methylR test data (testData.zip) instead of downloading a full GEO dataset. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Retrieve a publicly available GEO DNA methylation array dataset (raw IDAT files plus sample sheet) so it can be loaded into an analysis pipeline such as methylR and used to independently reproduce published differential methylation results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad184
skills.summary: Retrieve a publicly available GEO DNA methylation array dataset (raw IDAT files plus sample sheet) so it can be loaded into an analysis pipeline such as methylR and used to independently reproduce published differential methylation results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis starts from already normalized beta-value matrices — methylR's ChAMP module expects raw IDAT input, so only downstream modules (Volcano plot, PCA/MDS, enrichment) apply to preprocessed tables. The dataset is not a DNA methylation array study (e.g., WGBS or RNA-seq), since methylR covers 450K and EPIC Illumina arrays only. Only a quick functionality check of the interface is needed — use the bundled methylR test data (testData.zip) instead of downloading a full GEO dataset.

skills.description: Use when candidate circRNA regulators (e.g. CRIT-predicted RBPs) need experimental validation via reanalysis of public knockdown RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENCODE, with global circRNA abundance compared between knockdown and control conditions.
skills.name: geo-encode-dataset-retrieval-and-reprocessing
skills.search_text: geo-encode-dataset-retrieval-and-reprocessing Use when candidate circRNA regulators (e.g. CRIT-predicted RBPs) need experimental validation via reanalysis of public knockdown RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENCODE, with global circRNA abundance compared between knockdown and control conditions. The goal is de novo discovery of circRNA regulators from MiOncoCirc/TCGA features (rho_m, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) via the CRIT NMF pipeline — that is a separate candidate-prediction skill, not knockdown reanalysis. Only circRNA-RBP interaction evidence is needed (e.g. CLIP database overlap or catRAPID/RNAct binding scores) rather than expression-level validation from knockdown perturbation data. No raw FASTQ data (or suitable knockdown series) exist for the RBP of interest — in the source study, only 22 of the putative regulators had suitable knockdown RNA-seq data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves publicly available shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq datasets from GEO/ENCODE and reprocesses them from raw FASTQ to detect circRNAs (CIRI2, find_circ) and compute the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI), enabling experimental validation of CRIT-predicted circRNA regulators such as SRSF5, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPF, KHSRP, and PSIP1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Retrieves publicly available shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq datasets from GEO/ENCODE and reprocesses them from raw FASTQ to detect circRNAs (CIRI2, find_circ) and compute the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI), enabling experimental validation of CRIT-predicted circRNA regulators such as SRSF5, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPF, KHSRP, and PSIP1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery of circRNA regulators from MiOncoCirc/TCGA features (rho_m, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) via the CRIT NMF pipeline — that is a separate candidate-prediction skill, not knockdown reanalysis. Only circRNA-RBP interaction evidence is needed (e.g. CLIP database overlap or catRAPID/RNAct binding scores) rather than expression-level validation from knockdown perturbation data. No raw FASTQ data (or suitable knockdown series) exist for the RBP of interest — in the source study, only 22 of the putative regulators had suitable knockdown RNA-seq data.

The expression data is not a gene-by-cell matrix from a public repository — e.g., already a processed feature table or spatial transcriptomics object that needs no GEO retrieval Cell labels are unavailable or cannot be matched one-to-one to the expression matrix columns, since MDIC3 requires matching exp.txt and metadata.txt A cell type contains fewer than 10 cells, which the MDIC3 README advises against http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Retrieve scRNA-seq datasets from GEO accessions (e.g., E13.5 and E14.5 mouse skin from GSE122043) and reformat them as MDIC3-compatible gene-by-cell exp.txt and cell-label metadata.txt files so downstream communication inference can run on published data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Retrieve scRNA-seq datasets from GEO accessions (e.g., E13.5 and E14.5 mouse skin from GSE122043) and reformat them as MDIC3-compatible gene-by-cell exp.txt and cell-label metadata.txt files so downstream communication inference can run on published data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data is not a gene-by-cell matrix from a public repository — e.g., already a processed feature table or spatial transcriptomics object that needs no GEO retrieval Cell labels are unavailable or cannot be matched one-to-one to the expression matrix columns, since MDIC3 requires matching exp.txt and metadata.txt A cell type contains fewer than 10 cells, which the MDIC3 README advises against

skills.description: Use when starting from a GEO accession (GSE series) and you need the raw probe-level intensity matrix, its probe annotation table, and per-sample metadata to feed a curation or normalization pipeline.
skills.name: geo-series-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: geo-series-data-retrieval Use when starting from a GEO accession (GSE series) and you need the raw probe-level intensity matrix, its probe annotation table, and per-sample metadata to feed a curation or normalization pipeline. You only need the already-processed gene-level data, which can be fetched as SummarizedExperiment objects via ExperimentHub from curatedAdipoArray The input is sequencing-derived gene counts (e.g., the curatedAdipoRNA RNA-Seq dataset) rather than microarray probe intensities The target GEO study lacks probe annotations or probe intensities — in the curatedAdipoArray curation such studies were excluded outright http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Retrieves probe intensities, probe-to-gene annotation tables, and sample metadata directly from GEO series matrices (e.g., GSE12929) using GEOquery in R/Bioconductor, as the first step of a microarray curation pipeline before probe-to-gene collapsing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Retrieves probe intensities, probe-to-gene annotation tables, and sample metadata directly from GEO series matrices (e.g., GSE12929) using GEOquery in R/Bioconductor, as the first step of a microarray curation pipeline before probe-to-gene collapsing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the already-processed gene-level data, which can be fetched as SummarizedExperiment objects via ExperimentHub from curatedAdipoArray The input is sequencing-derived gene counts (e.g., the curatedAdipoRNA RNA-Seq dataset) rather than microarray probe intensities The target GEO study lacks probe annotations or probe intensities — in the curatedAdipoArray curation such studies were excluded outright

skills.description: Use when a combined multi-study dataset (multiple GEO series merged into one SummarizedExperiment) must be narrowed to specific studies/conditions — e.g. isolating Pparg-knockdown samples across GSE12929 and GSE14004 for batch-removal or variance analyses.
skills.name: geo-series-sample-subsetting
skills.search_text: geo-series-sample-subsetting Use when a combined multi-study dataset (multiple GEO series merged into one SummarizedExperiment) must be narrowed to specific studies/conditions — e.g. isolating Pparg-knockdown samples across GSE12929 and GSE14004 for batch-removal or variance analyses. The analysis requires the full curated panel (all 47 datasets / 43 studies) rather than specific perturbation subsets — subsetting would discard cross-study contrast The target study was excluded during curation for missing probe intensities or probe annotations — it will not be present in the SummarizedExperiment object Working with raw GEO data outside the curated package; use GEOquery directly instead of subsetting the processed object http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Subset a multi-study curated GEO expression resource (e.g. the curatedAdipoArray SummarizedExperiment) down to specific data series of interest — here the two Pparg-knockdown series GSE12929 (n=48) and GSE14004 (n=9) — while retaining stage-of-differentiation metadata for downstream batch-effect and PCA analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Subset a multi-study curated GEO expression resource (e.g. the curatedAdipoArray SummarizedExperiment) down to specific data series of interest — here the two Pparg-knockdown series GSE12929 (n=48) and GSE14004 (n=9) — while retaining stage-of-differentiation metadata for downstream batch-effect and PCA analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires the full curated panel (all 47 datasets / 43 studies) rather than specific perturbation subsets — subsetting would discard cross-study contrast The target study was excluded during curation for missing probe intensities or probe annotations — it will not be present in the SummarizedExperiment object Working with raw GEO data outside the curated package; use GEOquery directly instead of subsetting the processed object

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation methods on the ScType paper datasets, or when standardized GEO/10x scRNA-seq download plus Seurat v4.0 normalization and clustering is needed as input to annotation.
skills.name: geo-single-cell-dataset-acquisition-and-preprocessing
skills.search_text: geo-single-cell-dataset-acquisition-and-preprocessing Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation methods on the ScType paper datasets, or when standardized GEO/10x scRNA-seq download plus Seurat v4.0 normalization and clustering is needed as input to annotation. Input is already a normalized, scaled, and clustered Seurat object — proceed directly to gene_sets_prepare()/sctype_score() or the run_sctype() wrapper The task is malignant vs non-malignant cell discrimination via single-cell SNV calling (vartrix), which is a separate downstream ScType capability, not preprocessing Datasets are not human or mouse scRNA-seq count matrices compatible with Seurat's Read10X/CreateSeuratObject pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Acquire the six human and mouse scRNA-seq benchmark datasets (five from GEO plus the 10x PBMC3k filtered gene-barcode matrices) and preprocess them in Seurat v4.0 with LogNormalize, 2000 variable features, scaling, PCA, and clustering so they are ready for ScType cell-type annotation and method comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Acquire the six human and mouse scRNA-seq benchmark datasets (five from GEO plus the 10x PBMC3k filtered gene-barcode matrices) and preprocess them in Seurat v4.0 with LogNormalize, 2000 variable features, scaling, PCA, and clustering so they are ready for ScType cell-type annotation and method comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized, scaled, and clustered Seurat object — proceed directly to gene_sets_prepare()/sctype_score() or the run_sctype() wrapper The task is malignant vs non-malignant cell discrimination via single-cell SNV calling (vartrix), which is a separate downstream ScType capability, not preprocessing Datasets are not human or mouse scRNA-seq count matrices compatible with Seurat's Read10X/CreateSeuratObject pipeline
