skills.name: geo-transcriptomic-clinical-data-harmonization
skills.search_text: geo-transcriptomic-clinical-data-harmonization Use when a GEO accession (e.g. GSE78220) provides a raw/processed transcriptome matrix plus separate clinical or treatment-response metadata that must be aligned per sample before survival or responder-vs-non-responder analysis. The input is already a harmonized expression-plus-clinical table with gene-symbol rows and sample columns The GEO series lacks paired per-sample clinical/response metadata, so no survival or responder stratification can be performed Analysis targets single-cell data rather than bulk transcriptome matrices (e.g. GSE81861/GSE75688 used only for DCNet validation) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Harmonizes GEO-deposited bulk transcriptome matrices with their paired clinical/response metadata into a sample-by-gene analytical table, as done for the 38 pre-treatment melanoma biopsies of GSE78220 used in the DCNet immunotherapy-response analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Harmonizes GEO-deposited bulk transcriptome matrices with their paired clinical/response metadata into a sample-by-gene analytical table, as done for the 38 pre-treatment melanoma biopsies of GSE78220 used in the DCNet immunotherapy-response analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a harmonized expression-plus-clinical table with gene-symbol rows and sample columns The GEO series lacks paired per-sample clinical/response metadata, so no survival or responder stratification can be performed Analysis targets single-cell data rather than bulk transcriptome matrices (e.g. GSE81861/GSE75688 used only for DCNet validation)

skills.description: Use when a analysis requires raw microarray/RNA-seq expression data hosted on GEO (a GSE accession) and it must be converted into per-condition gene-by-sample tab-separated matrices with a 'Gene' first column before downstream modeling.
skills.name: geo-transcriptomics-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: geo-transcriptomics-data-retrieval Use when a analysis requires raw microarray/RNA-seq expression data hosted on GEO (a GSE accession) and it must be converted into per-condition gene-by-sample tab-separated matrices with a 'Gene' first column before downstream modeling. Expression data is already provided as per-condition tab-separated matrices with gene symbols and a 'Gene' first column (e.g. preprocessed TCGA downloads from xenabrowser.net) The dataset requires no ID mapping or replicate aggregation, i.e. features are already gene-level and sample metadata selection is trivial The goal is raw sequenced-read processing rather than matrix-level retrieval — GEOquery returns processed expression matrices, not FASTQ files http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Retrieve GEO transcriptomics datasets (e.g. GSE27219 B. subtilis stress data, GSE126124 Crohn's disease) using GEOquery, map probe IDs to gene symbols with biomaRt, aggregate replicate probes with dplyr, and export tab-separated disease/control expression matrices ready for differential network tools like BoostDiff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Retrieve GEO transcriptomics datasets (e.g. GSE27219 B. subtilis stress data, GSE126124 Crohn's disease) using GEOquery, map probe IDs to gene symbols with biomaRt, aggregate replicate probes with dplyr, and export tab-separated disease/control expression matrices ready for differential network tools like BoostDiff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data is already provided as per-condition tab-separated matrices with gene symbols and a 'Gene' first column (e.g. preprocessed TCGA downloads from xenabrowser.net) The dataset requires no ID mapping or replicate aggregation, i.e. features are already gene-level and sample metadata selection is trivial The goal is raw sequenced-read processing rather than matrix-level retrieval — GEOquery returns processed expression matrices, not FASTQ files

skills.description: Use when you need a reproducible annotation/inventory table (dataset, type, sample description, sample count, feature count, Used flag) for the thirteen human PDAC expression datasets housed in the pdacR R package, or when verifying curated dataset metadata against a published compendium table.
skills.name: geodb-transcriptomic-dataset-retrieval
skills.search_text: geodb-transcriptomic-dataset-retrieval Use when you need a reproducible annotation/inventory table (dataset, type, sample description, sample count, feature count, Used flag) for the thirteen human PDAC expression datasets housed in the pdacR R package, or when verifying curated dataset metadata against a published compendium table. You need raw sequencing data or the original GEO/TCGA downloads — pdacR houses parsed, annotated datasets rather than raw files You need to merge or aggregate datasets across platforms — the article notes the collection cannot robustly merge datasets and aggregation was removed because it introduced more problems than it solved Your goal is single-cell analysis — use the separate rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas repository; the pdacR GUI/app scope excludes scRNA due to computational burden http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reconstruct the pdacR curated 13-dataset PDAC transcriptomic compendium inventory (Table 1) by installing the pdacR R package, loading its parsed dataset objects, and extracting per-dataset measurement type, sample description, sample count, feature count, and Used flag. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Reconstruct the pdacR curated 13-dataset PDAC transcriptomic compendium inventory (Table 1) by installing the pdacR R package, loading its parsed dataset objects, and extracting per-dataset measurement type, sample description, sample count, feature count, and Used flag.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need raw sequencing data or the original GEO/TCGA downloads — pdacR houses parsed, annotated datasets rather than raw files You need to merge or aggregate datasets across platforms — the article notes the collection cannot robustly merge datasets and aggregation was removed because it introduced more problems than it solved Your goal is single-cell analysis — use the separate rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas repository; the pdacR GUI/app scope excludes scRNA due to computational burden

skills.description: Use when ground-truth (supervised) CCI labels must be constructed for training a cell-cell interaction model: candidates come from a shared LRIDB over clustered scRNA-seq data (e.g. panc8 with Human labels, label_mode True) and no trusted label file exists yet.
skills.name: geometric-mean-expression-scoring
skills.search_text: geometric-mean-expression-scoring Use when ground-truth (supervised) CCI labels must be constructed for training a cell-cell interaction model: candidates come from a shared LRIDB over clustered scRNA-seq data (e.g. panc8 with Human labels, label_mode True) and no trusted label file exists yet. A trusted ground-truth CCI label file already exists — pass it directly with label_mode True rather than re-deriving labels by majority vote. Running DeepCCI in label-free mode (label_mode False) — there are no cluster labels to score interactions against, so supervised label construction is inapplicable. A single-method analysis (e.g. only CellChat) is the goal — this skill specifically aggregates four scorers by majority vote, which requires all benchmark method calls. Score candidate ligand–receptor pairs from a shared LRIDB as the geometric mean of ligand and receptor expression products across cell-cluster pairs, then threshold (LRscore ≥ 0.5 or P-value ≤ 0.01) and majority-vote with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR calls to produce consensus positive/negative CCI labels that supervise DeepCCI's interaction model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: Score candidate ligand–receptor pairs from a shared LRIDB as the geometric mean of ligand and receptor expression products across cell-cluster pairs, then threshold (LRscore ≥ 0.5 or P-value ≤ 0.01) and majority-vote with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR calls to produce consensus positive/negative CCI labels that supervise DeepCCI's interaction model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A trusted ground-truth CCI label file already exists — pass it directly with label_mode True rather than re-deriving labels by majority vote. Running DeepCCI in label-free mode (label_mode False) — there are no cluster labels to score interactions against, so supervised label construction is inapplicable. A single-method analysis (e.g. only CellChat) is the goal — this skill specifically aggregates four scorers by majority vote, which requires all benchmark method calls.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multiple trajectory inference methods (e.g., Totem vs Slingshot vs TinGa) scored with the four dynverse metrics against dynverse gold standards, and a single comparable overall score per method/topology is needed.
skills.name: geometric-mean-score-aggregation
skills.search_text: geometric-mean-score-aggregation Use when benchmarking multiple trajectory inference methods (e.g., Totem vs Slingshot vs TinGa) scored with the four dynverse metrics against dynverse gold standards, and a single comparable overall score per method/topology is needed. Any input metric can be zero or negative, making the geometric mean undefined or uninterpretable Only a single metric is computed, so there is nothing to aggregate into an overall score Metrics are not all on a comparable positive scale and would need normalization before combining http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates the four dynverse trajectory-inference metrics (correlation of geodesic distances, feature-importance correlation, F1 branches, and HIM) into a single geometric-mean overall score per method and topology, then stratifies method rankings by topology (linear vs nonlinear) with paired nonparametric tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Aggregates the four dynverse trajectory-inference metrics (correlation of geodesic distances, feature-importance correlation, F1 branches, and HIM) into a single geometric-mean overall score per method and topology, then stratifies method rankings by topology (linear vs nonlinear) with paired nonparametric tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Any input metric can be zero or negative, making the geometric mean undefined or uninterpretable Only a single metric is computed, so there is nothing to aggregate into an overall score Metrics are not all on a comparable positive scale and would need normalization before combining

skills.description: Use when benchmarking stability of communication-inference or clustering results against reduced cell counts, e.g. re-running CellChat on geometric sketches at 90/80/70% and scoring TPR/FPR/ACC vs full-data predictions.
skills.name: geometric-sketching-subsampling
skills.search_text: geometric-sketching-subsampling Use when benchmarking stability of communication-inference or clustering results against reduced cell counts, e.g. re-running CellChat on geometric sketches at 90/80/70% and scoring TPR/FPR/ACC vs full-data predictions. The dataset lacks cell-cluster labels — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for communication analysis with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR, so sketches of unclustered data cannot be scored You have ground-truth validated interactions — direct evaluation against truth is preferable to self-referential sketch-vs-full-data comparison The tool's predictions depend on absolute cell counts per group rather than relative abundances, making sketch-level comparisons misleading http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Subsample scRNA-seq datasets with geometric sketching at 90%, 80%, and 70% of cells, re-run cell-cell communication inference on each sketch, and score retained interactions against full-data predictions using TPR, FPR, and ACC. Used in the CellChat paper to show that CellChat and CellPhoneDB are relatively robust to subsampling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Subsample scRNA-seq datasets with geometric sketching at 90%, 80%, and 70% of cells, re-run cell-cell communication inference on each sketch, and score retained interactions against full-data predictions using TPR, FPR, and ACC. Used in the CellChat paper to show that CellChat and CellPhoneDB are relatively robust to subsampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks cell-cluster labels — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for communication analysis with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR, so sketches of unclustered data cannot be scored You have ground-truth validated interactions — direct evaluation against truth is preferable to self-referential sketch-vs-full-data comparison The tool's predictions depend on absolute cell counts per group rather than relative abundances, making sketch-level comparisons misleading

skills.description: Use when you need to compare cell-subsampling (sketching) strategies on scRNA-seq data by quantifying how faithfully a sketch of 1%-10% of cells represents the full transcriptomic space or preserves cell-type separability.
skills.name: geometric-versus-spherical-sketch-benchmarking
skills.search_text: geometric-versus-spherical-sketch-benchmarking Use when you need to compare cell-subsampling (sketching) strategies on scRNA-seq data by quantifying how faithfully a sketch of 1%-10% of cells represents the full transcriptomic space or preserves cell-type separability. The input is not a cell-by-feature matrix (e.g., raw FASTQ or unnormalized counts) — Sphetcher expects features such as genes, transcripts, or principal components with rows as samples The goal is only to obtain one sketch without method comparison — running Sphetcher alone suffices and the benchmarking overhead (baseline method, 10 trials, distance computation) is unnecessary The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's model — the article notes the model 'might be less compatible with assumptions made by other algorithms' beyond Louvain and Monocle 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark Sphetcher's spherical sketching (spheres via a thresholding technique) against Hie et al.'s geometric sketching (boxes) on single-cell transcriptomic datasets by measuring robust Hausdorff distances to the full data and downstream Louvain clustering quality (ARI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Benchmark Sphetcher's spherical sketching (spheres via a thresholding technique) against Hie et al.'s geometric sketching (boxes) on single-cell transcriptomic datasets by measuring robust Hausdorff distances to the full data and downstream Louvain clustering quality (ARI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a cell-by-feature matrix (e.g., raw FASTQ or unnormalized counts) — Sphetcher expects features such as genes, transcripts, or principal components with rows as samples The goal is only to obtain one sketch without method comparison — running Sphetcher alone suffices and the benchmarking overhead (baseline method, 10 trials, distance computation) is unnecessary The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's model — the article notes the model 'might be less compatible with assumptions made by other algorithms' beyond Louvain and Monocle 2

skills.description: Use when training a cross-modality GAN (e.g. scMMGAN) where the mapping must keep nearby points nearby across domains — e.g. aligning scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics while preserving manifold structure.
skills.name: geometry-preserving-correspondence-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: geometry-preserving-correspondence-loss-implementation Use when training a cross-modality GAN (e.g. scMMGAN) where the mapping must keep nearby points nearby across domains — e.g. aligning scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics while preserving manifold structure. You only need distributional (adversarial) alignment without point-wise geometric fidelity — plain CycleGAN losses suffice and the eigenvector computation overhead is unnecessary Your data representation lacks a meaningful point-to-point distance metric — the geometry-based loss is not completely plug-and-play and requires a choice of distance between data points You are aligning more than a few modalities — the number of generators grows quadratically with the number of input modalities, forcing small or separately trained networks http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Implements scMMGAN's diffusion-geometry correspondence loss Lc, which penalizes the L2 distance between diffusion-operator eigenvectors of original points and their GAN-mapped counterparts so the learned cross-modality mapping preserves intrinsic data geometry beyond distributional alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Implements scMMGAN's diffusion-geometry correspondence loss Lc, which penalizes the L2 distance between diffusion-operator eigenvectors of original points and their GAN-mapped counterparts so the learned cross-modality mapping preserves intrinsic data geometry beyond distributional alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need distributional (adversarial) alignment without point-wise geometric fidelity — plain CycleGAN losses suffice and the eigenvector computation overhead is unnecessary Your data representation lacks a meaningful point-to-point distance metric — the geometry-based loss is not completely plug-and-play and requires a choice of distance between data points You are aligning more than a few modalities — the number of generators grows quadratically with the number of input modalities, forcing small or separately trained networks

skills.description: Use when starting a scRNA-seq analysis from a public GEO accession (raw UMI count matrix) and a graph-based deep-learning method like scGAE requires scTransform-preprocessed input data.
skills.name: geoscrna-dataset-retrieval-and-preprocessing
skills.search_text: geoscrna-dataset-retrieval-and-preprocessing Use when starting a scRNA-seq analysis from a public GEO accession (raw UMI count matrix) and a graph-based deep-learning method like scGAE requires scTransform-preprocessed input data. The input is already an scTransform-normalized/preprocessed matrix or an embedding — re-running retrieval and preprocessing would discard prior work. The analysis target is not scRNA-seq count data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq, spatial or proteomics data) — scGAE's cell-graph preprocessing assumes single-cell count matrices. You need direct 2D embedding output from the autoencoder — the paper states the complex data structure is hard to embed directly into 2D and instead embeds to an intermediate dimension followed by tSNE. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Retrieves a public scRNA-seq count matrix from GEO (e.g., GSE84133 Baron human pancreas) and preprocesses it with scTransform in the Seurat package so the normalized matrix is in the exact form scGAE expects before KNN graph construction and graph-autoencoder embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Retrieves a public scRNA-seq count matrix from GEO (e.g., GSE84133 Baron human pancreas) and preprocesses it with scTransform in the Seurat package so the normalized matrix is in the exact form scGAE expects before KNN graph construction and graph-autoencoder embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an scTransform-normalized/preprocessed matrix or an embedding — re-running retrieval and preprocessing would discard prior work. The analysis target is not scRNA-seq count data (e.g., bulk RNA-seq, spatial or proteomics data) — scGAE's cell-graph preprocessing assumes single-cell count matrices. You need direct 2D embedding output from the autoencoder — the paper states the complex data structure is hard to embed directly into 2D and instead embeds to an intermediate dimension followed by tSNE.

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptomes (e.g. MCA count matrix) need a low-dimensional, biologically interpretable embedding built from known marker GEPs, and when benchmarking that embedding against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA with clustering metrics.
skills.name: gep-averaging-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: gep-averaging-dimensionality-reduction Use when single-cell transcriptomes (e.g. MCA count matrix) need a low-dimensional, biologically interpretable embedding built from known marker GEPs, and when benchmarking that embedding against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA with clustering metrics. The target cells' types are not covered by the source GEPs (e.g. high-resolution neuronal subtypes absent from MCA GEPs would compromise annotation/averaging precision) The dataset lacks identified GEPs and you only need an off-the-shelf latent-factor reduction with no interpretability requirement — PCA or similar is simpler Gene IDs in the count matrix cannot be matched to the GEP file format (Ensembl vs symbol mismatch would silently average over wrong genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A dimension-reduction method from Xu et al. 2024 that embeds single-cell data by averaging gene expression over SingleCellGGM-derived gene expression programs (GEPs) instead of gene-level latent factors, enhancing the interpretability of single-cell analysis results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: A dimension-reduction method from Xu et al. 2024 that embeds single-cell data by averaging gene expression over SingleCellGGM-derived gene expression programs (GEPs) instead of gene-level latent factors, enhancing the interpretability of single-cell analysis results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target cells' types are not covered by the source GEPs (e.g. high-resolution neuronal subtypes absent from MCA GEPs would compromise annotation/averaging precision) The dataset lacks identified GEPs and you only need an off-the-shelf latent-factor reduction with no interpretability requirement — PCA or similar is simpler Gene IDs in the count matrix cannot be matched to the GEP file format (Ensembl vs symbol mismatch would silently average over wrong genes)

skills.description: Use when a novel single-cell count matrix should be annotated per cell using reference marker GEPs (e.g., mca.marker.geps.txt) instead of clustering, and annotation purity against reference labels must be quantified.
skills.name: gep-based-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: gep-based-cell-type-annotation Use when a novel single-cell count matrix should be annotated per cell using reference marker GEPs (e.g., mca.marker.geps.txt) instead of clustering, and annotation purity against reference labels must be quantified. The target dataset contains cell types absent from the reference GEP set (e.g., TMS cells annotated with MCA GEPs become 'unknown', or high-resolution neuronal subtypes in Mouse Brain not covered by MCA GEPs). A clustering-based annotation or cross-modality (ATAC-seq, proteomics) approach is required — SingleCellGGM/CellGEP relies exclusively on transcriptome data. Gene identifiers in the count matrix do not match the GEP file format (Ensembl vs symbol mismatch). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Direct cell-type annotation of individual single-cell transcriptome cells using pre-identified marker gene expression programs (GEPs), without cell clustering, via the CellGEP R package (cellgep function) with GEP-averaged expression, a dynamic expression cutoff, and KNN neighbor voting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Direct cell-type annotation of individual single-cell transcriptome cells using pre-identified marker gene expression programs (GEPs), without cell clustering, via the CellGEP R package (cellgep function) with GEP-averaged expression, a dynamic expression cutoff, and KNN neighbor voting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target dataset contains cell types absent from the reference GEP set (e.g., TMS cells annotated with MCA GEPs become 'unknown', or high-resolution neuronal subtypes in Mouse Brain not covered by MCA GEPs). A clustering-based annotation or cross-modality (ATAC-seq, proteomics) approach is required — SingleCellGGM/CellGEP relies exclusively on transcriptome data. Gene identifiers in the count matrix do not match the GEP file format (Ensembl vs symbol mismatch).

skills.description: Use when you have gene co-expression modules (GEPs, e.g. MCL clusters of a GGM network) and need per-module GO/MP enrichment significance and a functional category split (identity vs. activity vs. morphogenesis).
skills.name: gep-functional-classification
skills.search_text: gep-functional-classification Use when you have gene co-expression modules (GEPs, e.g. MCL clusters of a GGM network) and need per-module GO/MP enrichment significance and a functional category split (identity vs. activity vs. morphogenesis). The gene set is not mouse, since ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis annotations are mouse-only (Ensembl BioMart GO and MGI MP) and only Ensembl gene IDs are supported Modules have fewer than 10 genes — the article restricts GEPs to modules with ≥10 genes before enrichment You only need cell-type label transfer (CellGEP) rather than functional characterization of the programs themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functionally characterize gene expression programs (GEPs) identified by SingleCellGGM by running GO and MP term enrichment on each module (ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis) and classifying GEPs into cell-identity, activity, and morphogenesis programs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Functionally characterize gene expression programs (GEPs) identified by SingleCellGGM by running GO and MP term enrichment on each module (ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis) and classifying GEPs into cell-identity, activity, and morphogenesis programs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene set is not mouse, since ModuleEnrichmentAnalysis annotations are mouse-only (Ensembl BioMart GO and MGI MP) and only Ensembl gene IDs are supported Modules have fewer than 10 genes — the article restricts GEPs to modules with ≥10 genes before enrichment You only need cell-type label transfer (CellGEP) rather than functional characterization of the programs themselves

skills.description: Use when you have run kernel-regularized NMF (e.g., par_estimate_nmf at rank ~16) on a log-normalized genes x cells matrix and must filter out degenerate gene expression programs before downstream use (e.g., biomarker binarization).
skills.name: gep-sparsity-screening
skills.search_text: gep-sparsity-screening Use when you have run kernel-regularized NMF (e.g., par_estimate_nmf at rank ~16) on a log-normalized genes x cells matrix and must filter out degenerate gene expression programs before downstream use (e.g., biomarker binarization). The weight matrix comes from plain (unregularized) NMF or a method other than the q-diffusion kernel-regularized factorization, so the 5%-95% sparsity heuristic from this paper does not apply The input expression matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — q-diffusion requires the full log-normalized genes x cells matrix The goal is a full-transcriptome embedding (qPHATE) rather than discrete gene expression programs Screens qNMF-estimated gene expression program (GEP) weight matrices for useful sparsity, keeping only programs whose cell weights are between 5% and 95% nonzero — programs that are entirely zero or entirely nonzero carry no discriminative information and signal underdetermined factorization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Screens qNMF-estimated gene expression program (GEP) weight matrices for useful sparsity, keeping only programs whose cell weights are between 5% and 95% nonzero — programs that are entirely zero or entirely nonzero carry no discriminative information and signal underdetermined factorization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The weight matrix comes from plain (unregularized) NMF or a method other than the q-diffusion kernel-regularized factorization, so the 5%-95% sparsity heuristic from this paper does not apply The input expression matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — q-diffusion requires the full log-normalized genes x cells matrix The goal is a full-transcriptome embedding (qPHATE) rather than discrete gene expression programs

skills.description: Use when a germ-cell query dataset (e.g. in vitro induced meiosis, Ythdc2-KO or Zfp541-KO germ cells) must be assigned meiotic stages by mapping onto the mTCA reference, and day-resolved meiotic entry rates or developmental arrest must be quantified.
skills.name: germ-cell-meiosis-stage-annotation
skills.search_text: germ-cell-meiosis-stage-annotation Use when a germ-cell query dataset (e.g. in vitro induced meiosis, Ythdc2-KO or Zfp541-KO germ cells) must be assigned meiotic stages by mapping onto the mTCA reference, and day-resolved meiotic entry rates or developmental arrest must be quantified. Query cells contain novel states absent from the mTCA reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results to detect inconsistencies The task is cross-platform projection (e.g. Smart-seq2 query onto a 10x-built reference), where ProjectSVR performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with ProjectSVR's integration-agnostic gene set activity score approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates germ-cell meiosis stages (e.g. leptotene through pachytene, m11–m15) in a query scRNA-seq dataset by projecting cells onto the mouse testicular cell atlas (mTCA) with ProjectSVR, transferring reference labels, majority-voting them over k-means over-clustering, and assessing meiotic progression by treatment day. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Annotates germ-cell meiosis stages (e.g. leptotene through pachytene, m11–m15) in a query scRNA-seq dataset by projecting cells onto the mouse testicular cell atlas (mTCA) with ProjectSVR, transferring reference labels, majority-voting them over k-means over-clustering, and assessing meiotic progression by treatment day.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel states absent from the mTCA reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results to detect inconsistencies The task is cross-platform projection (e.g. Smart-seq2 query onto a 10x-built reference), where ProjectSVR performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with ProjectSVR's integration-agnostic gene set activity score approach

skills.description: Use when constructing euploid-baseline single-cell inputs for simulated CNA benchmarking (e.g., SDX chrX pooling from male oligodendrocyte BAMs) or when donor cells carry germline CNAs that would confound somatic CNA calling.
skills.name: germline-cna-region-removal
skills.search_text: germline-cna-region-removal Use when constructing euploid-baseline single-cell inputs for simulated CNA benchmarking (e.g., SDX chrX pooling from male oligodendrocyte BAMs) or when donor cells carry germline CNAs that would confound somatic CNA calling. The target analysis is restricted to autosomes from both-sex samples (HiScanner excludes sex chromosomes from its cross-sample workflow; applying chrX-based removal there is out of scope) Input cells are already euploid across the region of interest — removal is unnecessary and discards coverage Germline variant genotyping rather than copy-number analysis is the goal; SCAN2-style workflows explicitly exclude sex chromosomes and matched-bulk-supported calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Excise reads falling in genomic intervals that harbor germline copy-number alterations (e.g., on donor chromosome X) from single-cell BAM files using samtools, so that downstream simulated cells or analyses start from an euploid baseline. This prevents pre-existing aneuploid/germline CN state from contaminating allele-specific CNA benchmarks or scWGS CNA detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Excise reads falling in genomic intervals that harbor germline copy-number alterations (e.g., on donor chromosome X) from single-cell BAM files using samtools, so that downstream simulated cells or analyses start from an euploid baseline. This prevents pre-existing aneuploid/germline CN state from contaminating allele-specific CNA benchmarks or scWGS CNA detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target analysis is restricted to autosomes from both-sex samples (HiScanner excludes sex chromosomes from its cross-sample workflow; applying chrX-based removal there is out of scope) Input cells are already euploid across the region of interest — removal is unnecessary and discards coverage Germline variant genotyping rather than copy-number analysis is the goal; SCAN2-style workflows explicitly exclude sex chromosomes and matched-bulk-supported calls

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ data from wild type and mutant samples (e.g. C. elegans germline, mut-16) must be quantified per-gene by small RNA class defined by length, 5′ nucleotide, and antisense strandedness, with classes resolved from the same loci.
skills.name: germline-sirna-mutant-vs-wildtype-count-comparison
skills.search_text: germline-sirna-mutant-vs-wildtype-count-comparison Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ data from wild type and mutant samples (e.g. C. elegans germline, mut-16) must be quantified per-gene by small RNA class defined by length, 5′ nucleotide, and antisense strandedness, with classes resolved from the same loci. Input is already a counts/feature table rather than raw aligned reads — tiny-count quantifies reads from FASTQ/BAM against reference features, not pre-existing feature tables The small RNA classes of interest cannot be defined by 5′ nucleotide, length, position relative to features, or mismatch number — selection-rule filtering will not separate them _reads are not demultiplexed; the workflow requires demultiplexed FASTQ files per sample http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 A method for hierarchically classifying and quantifying C. elegans small RNA classes (22G-RNAs, 26G-RNAs, unclassified siRNAs) from germline small RNA-seq with tiny-count, using 5′ nucleotide/length/antisense selection rules, and comparing counts between mut-16 mutants and wild type to identify MUT-16-dependent siRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: A method for hierarchically classifying and quantifying C. elegans small RNA classes (22G-RNAs, 26G-RNAs, unclassified siRNAs) from germline small RNA-seq with tiny-count, using 5′ nucleotide/length/antisense selection rules, and comparing counts between mut-16 mutants and wild type to identify MUT-16-dependent siRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a counts/feature table rather than raw aligned reads — tiny-count quantifies reads from FASTQ/BAM against reference features, not pre-existing feature tables The small RNA classes of interest cannot be defined by 5′ nucleotide, length, position relative to features, or mismatch number — selection-rule filtering will not separate them _reads are not demultiplexed; the workflow requires demultiplexed FASTQ files per sample

skills.description: Use when phasiRNA/siRNA cluster predictions exist in multiple coordinate systems (cDNA vs gDNA mapping) and must be merged, deduplicated, and annotated with GFF3 gene features into a unified PHAS loci catalog.
skills.name: gff3-annotation-based-cluster-classification
skills.search_text: gff3-annotation-based-cluster-classification Use when phasiRNA/siRNA cluster predictions exist in multiple coordinate systems (cDNA vs gDNA mapping) and must be merged, deduplicated, and annotated with GFF3 gene features into a unified PHAS loci catalog. Predictions were produced against only a single reference sequence, so no cross-coordinate-system integration is needed. The GFF3 gene annotation for the reference genome is unavailable, since annotation and classification of integrated PHAS loci depend on it. Cluster merging is desired with different thresholds than the phase step without rerunning, e.g. the phase number cutoff 4 or pvalue cutoff 0.001 cannot be re-applied consistently. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Integrates phasiRNA and all-siRNA clusters predicted separately against different reference sequences (transcriptome/cDNA and genome/gDNA) by transforming coordinates with bedtools and python3 dictionaries, then deduplicating, merging, annotating and classifying the merged PHAS loci against a reference GFF3 gene annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Integrates phasiRNA and all-siRNA clusters predicted separately against different reference sequences (transcriptome/cDNA and genome/gDNA) by transforming coordinates with bedtools and python3 dictionaries, then deduplicating, merging, annotating and classifying the merged PHAS loci against a reference GFF3 gene annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions were produced against only a single reference sequence, so no cross-coordinate-system integration is needed. The GFF3 gene annotation for the reference genome is unavailable, since annotation and classification of integrated PHAS loci depend on it. Cluster merging is desired with different thresholds than the phase step without rerunning, e.g. the phase number cutoff 4 or pvalue cutoff 0.001 cannot be re-applied consistently.

skills.description: Use when a workflow requires reading gene models from a GFF3/GTF canonical annotation, merging tool-annotated 3' UTR features (source=peaks2utr) with original features, or comparing predicted UTRs against a canonical GFF truth set.
skills.name: gff3-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: gff3-annotation-parsing Use when a workflow requires reading gene models from a GFF3/GTF canonical annotation, merging tool-annotated 3' UTR features (source=peaks2utr) with original features, or comparing predicted UTRs against a canonical GFF truth set. The annotation is already a peaks2utr output GFF3 with source=peaks2utr 3' UTR features and no further UTR annotation is needed. Input gene models are not in GFF/GTF format (e.g. raw BED or SAM) — convert first or the tool cannot accept them. The task is de novo transcript discovery without a canonical annotation to anchor UTR annotation against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Parse, validate, and manipulate GFF3 (or GTF) gene-model annotations — e.g. canonical annotations like WormBase chrI or T. brucei GFF3 — as both input to and output of peaks2utr-style 3' UTR annotation pipelines, optionally normalizing with GenomeTools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Parse, validate, and manipulate GFF3 (or GTF) gene-model annotations — e.g. canonical annotations like WormBase chrI or T. brucei GFF3 — as both input to and output of peaks2utr-style 3' UTR annotation pipelines, optionally normalizing with GenomeTools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation is already a peaks2utr output GFF3 with source=peaks2utr 3' UTR features and no further UTR annotation is needed. Input gene models are not in GFF/GTF format (e.g. raw BED or SAM) — convert first or the tool cannot accept them. The task is de novo transcript discovery without a canonical annotation to anchor UTR annotation against.

skills.description: Use when supplying reference annotations (GFF3/GFF2/GTF) to tiny-count or tinyRNA for hierarchical small RNA-seq quantification, and feature IDs, Parent relationships, or genome/annotation identifier matching must be validated first.
skills.name: gff3-feature-annotation-handling
skills.search_text: gff3-feature-annotation-handling Use when supplying reference annotations (GFF3/GFF2/GTF) to tiny-count or tinyRNA for hierarchical small RNA-seq quantification, and feature IDs, Parent relationships, or genome/annotation identifier matching must be validated first. Input is already a per-feature count table rather than reference annotations Features lack any `ID`/`gene_id`/`Parent` column-9 tags and cannot be reformatted to satisfy tiny-count's GFF3 requirements `Parent` tags carry multiple values and the annotation cannot be restructured, since multi-value Parent tags are not yet supported http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Prepares and validates GFF3 (or GFF2/GTF) reference annotation files so tiny-count can parse features and assign small RNA-seq reads to them under hierarchical selection rules. Correct column-9 attributes and chromosome identifier consistency are the key failure points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: Prepares and validates GFF3 (or GFF2/GTF) reference annotation files so tiny-count can parse features and assign small RNA-seq reads to them under hierarchical selection rules. Correct column-9 attributes and chromosome identifier consistency are the key failure points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-feature count table rather than reference annotations Features lack any `ID`/`gene_id`/`Parent` column-9 tags and cannot be reformatted to satisfy tiny-count's GFF3 requirements `Parent` tags carry multiple values and the annotation cannot be restructured, since multi-value Parent tags are not yet supported

skills.description: Use when you must write a GFF3 annotation file that preserves existing gene model features and appends newly called 3' UTR features derived from BAM-aligned reads.
skills.name: gff3-genomic-feature-annotation-writing
skills.search_text: gff3-genomic-feature-annotation-writing Use when you must write a GFF3 annotation file that preserves existing gene model features and appends newly called 3' UTR features derived from BAM-aligned reads. Input is not aligned sequencing reads (BAM) or a canonical GFF/GTF annotation — peaks2utr's peak-based 3' UTR inference requires both. You only need to reformat or validate an existing annotation without adding new features; use GenomeTools or a generic GFF3 parser instead. The reads lack 3'-end enrichment (e.g. not from protocols like 10x Chromium where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends), reducing the reliability of called 3' UTR boundaries. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Write augmented GFF3 (or GTF) genomic annotations in which newly inferred 3' UTR features, tagged with source 'peaks2utr', are emitted alongside all original input features, as implemented by the peaks2utr tool. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Write augmented GFF3 (or GTF) genomic annotations in which newly inferred 3' UTR features, tagged with source 'peaks2utr', are emitted alongside all original input features, as implemented by the peaks2utr tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not aligned sequencing reads (BAM) or a canonical GFF/GTF annotation — peaks2utr's peak-based 3' UTR inference requires both. You only need to reformat or validate an existing annotation without adding new features; use GenomeTools or a generic GFF3 parser instead. The reads lack 3'-end enrichment (e.g. not from protocols like 10x Chromium where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends), reducing the reliability of called 3' UTR boundaries.

skills.description: Use when a feature list (e.g., miRNA precursors in table, GFF3/GTF, and FASTA formats) must be mapped to chromosome coordinates or assigned to subgenomes of a polyploid genome such as hexaploid bread wheat.
skills.name: gff3-gtf-genomic-coordinate-parsing
skills.search_text: gff3-gtf-genomic-coordinate-parsing Use when a feature list (e.g., miRNA precursors in table, GFF3/GTF, and FASTA formats) must be mapped to chromosome coordinates or assigned to subgenomes of a polyploid genome such as hexaploid bread wheat. Species without a reference genome or without GFF3/GTF annotations, since iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Precursors whose genomic coordinates are unplaced or ambiguous, which would corrupt subgenome assignment Analyses needing downstream enrichment (GO, miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparison, which the coordinate-parsing step does not provide http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Parses GFF3/GTF genome annotations to assign genomic features (e.g., wheat miRNA precursors from iwa-miRNA) to chromosomes and subgenomes using their coordinate fields, enabling polyploid-specific analyses such as A/B/D homeologous grouping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Parses GFF3/GTF genome annotations to assign genomic features (e.g., wheat miRNA precursors from iwa-miRNA) to chromosomes and subgenomes using their coordinate fields, enabling polyploid-specific analyses such as A/B/D homeologous grouping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Species without a reference genome or without GFF3/GTF annotations, since iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Precursors whose genomic coordinates are unplaced or ambiguous, which would corrupt subgenome assignment Analyses needing downstream enrichment (GO, miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparison, which the coordinate-parsing step does not provide

skills.description: Use when a synthetic single-cell count matrix must be visually validated against a real reference dataset by plotting comparative panels of dispersions, library sizes, fraction of zeros, and sample/feature correlations.
skills.name: ggplot2-comparative-panel-visualization
skills.search_text: ggplot2-comparative-panel-visualization Use when a synthetic single-cell count matrix must be visually validated against a real reference dataset by plotting comparative panels of dispersions, library sizes, fraction of zeros, and sample/feature correlations. The goal is quantitative simulation of dynamic cellular processes rather than visual quality comparison of count-matrix characteristics The two count matrices differ substantially in dimensions (num_cells, num_tfs, num_targets, num_hks not matched to the reference), making dimension-comparison panels uninformative Data are not count matrices amenable to edgeR/DESeq2 dispersion estimation (e.g. already normalised or non-integer data) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Render side-by-side ggplot2 comparison panels that show whether dyngen-simulated single-cell count data match a real reference dataset's characteristics, mirroring the countsimQC-based Supplementary Note 1 result of the dyngen manuscript. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Render side-by-side ggplot2 comparison panels that show whether dyngen-simulated single-cell count data match a real reference dataset's characteristics, mirroring the countsimQC-based Supplementary Note 1 result of the dyngen manuscript.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantitative simulation of dynamic cellular processes rather than visual quality comparison of count-matrix characteristics The two count matrices differ substantially in dimensions (num_cells, num_tfs, num_targets, num_hks not matched to the reference), making dimension-comparison panels uninformative Data are not count matrices amenable to edgeR/DESeq2 dispersion estimation (e.g. already normalised or non-integer data)

skills.description: Use when a per-cell scalar measurement (methylation rate, expression score) must be binned and smoothed along an ordered circular pseudo time-series (ordIndex/HMM phases G1, S, G2/M) and rendered as an annotated curve figure.
skills.name: ggplot2-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: ggplot2-curve-visualization Use when a per-cell scalar measurement (methylation rate, expression score) must be binned and smoothed along an ordered circular pseudo time-series (ordIndex/HMM phases G1, S, G2/M) and rendered as an annotated curve figure. Input cells have not been ordered (no ordIndex/HMM result from reCAT) — plotting raw unordered cells yields a meaningless curve The analysis goal is clustering or reordering of cells (get_ordIndex/get_hmm_order territory), not visualization of an already-ordered scalar profile http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualization skill for drawing smoothed scalar curves (e.g., whole-genome methylation rate) along the reCAT-recovered cell cycle pseudo time-series using ggplot2 in R, as done to reproduce the methylation profile peaking at G1/S (Fig. 4d of the reCAT paper). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Visualization skill for drawing smoothed scalar curves (e.g., whole-genome methylation rate) along the reCAT-recovered cell cycle pseudo time-series using ggplot2 in R, as done to reproduce the methylation profile peaking at G1/S (Fig. 4d of the reCAT paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells have not been ordered (no ordIndex/HMM result from reCAT) — plotting raw unordered cells yields a meaningless curve The analysis goal is clustering or reordering of cells (get_ordIndex/get_hmm_order territory), not visualization of an already-ordered scalar profile

skills.description: Use when clustering droplet-based UMI count matrices from multiple individuals with BAMM-SC and you must run, tune, or validate the MCMC/Gibbs sampler (burn-in, iteration budget, log-likelihood tolerance) behind the hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture.
skills.name: gibbs-sampler-implementation
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-implementation Use when clustering droplet-based UMI count matrices from multiple individuals with BAMM-SC and you must run, tune, or validate the MCMC/Gibbs sampler (burn-in, iteration budget, log-likelihood tolerance) behind the hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture. Input is a single UMI count matrix rather than a list of per-individual matrices — the package then falls back to DIMMSC instead of the multi-individual Gibbs sampler You need explicit modeling of zero inflation or dropouts, which BAMM-SC's multinomial-Dirichlet likelihood does not model You expect posterior probabilities to quantify cell cycle or developmental stage — BAMM-SC assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probability only measures clustering uncertainty http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implements the Gibbs MCMC core of BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model, alternating updates of the Dirichlet concentration parameters alpha_ilk (under a log-normal LN(mu_ik, sigma_ik^2) prior) and cell cluster labels z_jl for multi-individual droplet-based UMI counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Implements the Gibbs MCMC core of BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model, alternating updates of the Dirichlet concentration parameters alpha_ilk (under a log-normal LN(mu_ik, sigma_ik^2) prior) and cell cluster labels z_jl for multi-individual droplet-based UMI counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single UMI count matrix rather than a list of per-individual matrices — the package then falls back to DIMMSC instead of the multi-individual Gibbs sampler You need explicit modeling of zero inflation or dropouts, which BAMM-SC's multinomial-Dirichlet likelihood does not model You expect posterior probabilities to quantify cell cycle or developmental stage — BAMM-SC assumes each cell belongs to one distinct cluster and posterior probability only measures clustering uncertainty

skills.description: Use when single-cell allele-level UMI counts at filtered SNVs are available and the goal is to detect a minor genotype, quantify mixing fraction, or decide K=1 vs K=2 in in silico or wet-lab chimerism mixtures.
skills.name: gibbs-sampler-two-genome-mixture-modeling
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampler-two-genome-mixture-modeling Use when single-cell allele-level UMI counts at filtered SNVs are available and the goal is to detect a minor genotype, quantify mixing fraction, or decide K=1 vs K=2 in in silico or wet-lab chimerism mixtures. Input cells have not been genotyped via SNV calling — the model requires allele-level UMI counts at filtered donor SNVs, not raw expression matrices The mixture fraction is expected far below ~3–4% of profiled cells — K=1 selection would only mean the fraction is below the method's detection level, not that no minor population exists The analysis goal is gene-expression clustering (e.g. Seurat PBMC clustering) rather than genotype-based chimerism assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A Gibbs-sampler-based two-genome (K=1 vs K=2) mixture model that fits per-cell allele-level UMI counts at donor SNVs to detect and quantify minor-genotype populations in chimeric single-cell RNA-seq mixtures, e.g. Donor B/C PBMC mixing experiments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: A Gibbs-sampler-based two-genome (K=1 vs K=2) mixture model that fits per-cell allele-level UMI counts at donor SNVs to detect and quantify minor-genotype populations in chimeric single-cell RNA-seq mixtures, e.g. Donor B/C PBMC mixing experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells have not been genotyped via SNV calling — the model requires allele-level UMI counts at filtered donor SNVs, not raw expression matrices The mixture fraction is expected far below ~3–4% of profiled cells — K=1 selection would only mean the fraction is below the method's detection level, not that no minor population exists The analysis goal is gene-expression clustering (e.g. Seurat PBMC clustering) rather than genotype-based chimerism assignment

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices contain pervasive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and cell-to-cell relationships must be recovered via Bayesian matrix factorization with MCMC, optionally leveraging cell labels or bulk side information.
skills.name: gibbs-sampling-mcmc-implementation
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampling-mcmc-implementation Use when scRNA-seq count matrices contain pervasive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and cell-to-cell relationships must be recovered via Bayesian matrix factorization with MCMC, optionally leveraging cell labels or bulk side information. The counts matrix is already normalized: set normalized=TRUE or Bfimpute will re-run CPM and log10 transform with bias 1.01 (log-transform after normalization is still recommended) A single best imputation is needed universally: the paper notes there is no consensus about which imputation method is the best and performance varies by dataset and downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Bfimpute's computational core: full Bayesian inference over latent gene (G) and cell (C) matrices via a Gibbs-sampling Markov chain Monte Carlo scheme, which factorizes the scRNA-seq count matrix into gene-specific and cell-specific feature matrices to impute dropout events. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Bfimpute's computational core: full Bayesian inference over latent gene (G) and cell (C) matrices via a Gibbs-sampling Markov chain Monte Carlo scheme, which factorizes the scRNA-seq count matrix into gene-specific and cell-specific feature matrices to impute dropout events.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The counts matrix is already normalized: set normalized=TRUE or Bfimpute will re-run CPM and log10 transform with bias 1.01 (log-transform after normalization is still recommended) A single best imputation is needed universally: the paper notes there is no consensus about which imputation method is the best and performance varies by dataset and downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when a trained scDBM (BoltzmannMachines.jl-based model on scRNA-seq count data) must be turned into synthetic observations of a target cell count, and when comparing sampling strategies such as Gibbs sampling against scVI prior/posterior sampling.
skills.name: gibbs-sampling-synthetic-count-generation
skills.search_text: gibbs-sampling-synthetic-count-generation Use when a trained scDBM (BoltzmannMachines.jl-based model on scRNA-seq count data) must be turned into synthetic observations of a target cell count, and when comparing sampling strategies such as Gibbs sampling against scVI prior/posterior sampling. The goal is to reproduce a specific small pilot's cells rather than extrapolate to a larger dataset — scDBM sampling targets study-size generation, not pilot replication Batch effects must be modeled or corrected — scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects and all models were examined without batch-correction capabilities The pilot sample is not representative of the target setting (experimental settings changed) — conclusions from small to larger datasets then violate the paper's stated assumption http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices from a trained single-cell deep Boltzmann machine (scDBM) by Gibbs sampling until the original study's cell count is reached, enabling extrapolation from small pilot studies (e.g. 384–2304 cells from PBMC4k or Segerstolpe) to full study size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Generates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices from a trained single-cell deep Boltzmann machine (scDBM) by Gibbs sampling until the original study's cell count is reached, enabling extrapolation from small pilot studies (e.g. 384–2304 cells from PBMC4k or Segerstolpe) to full study size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to reproduce a specific small pilot's cells rather than extrapolate to a larger dataset — scDBM sampling targets study-size generation, not pilot replication Batch effects must be modeled or corrected — scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects and all models were examined without batch-correction capabilities The pilot sample is not representative of the target setting (experimental settings changed) — conclusions from small to larger datasets then violate the paper's stated assumption

skills.search_text: gini-coefficient-computation Use when you have factor loadings from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition (e.g. rank=10 BALF COVID-19 tensor) and need a scalar inequality statistic per factor to characterize loading concentration across contexts or LR pairs. skills.summary: Computes the Gini coefficient (a measure of loading concentration/inequality) on Tensor-cell2cell factor loadings, e.g. quantifying how concentrated factor-9 loadings are across contexts in the 12x189x6x6 BALF COVID-19 4D-communication tensor, using cell2cell.stats.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tensor contains missing values or cell types not shared across all samples — the article notes the algorithm is not optimized for missing values and the COVID-19/ASD tensors only include cell types shared across all samples You need per-pair communication inference in a single context rather than a concentration statistic on loadings of a multi-context decomposition Loadings are not comparable across contexts (e.g. different normalization or non-converged factorization), which would distort the inequality measure

skills.description: Use when pre-processed SingCellaR objects (e.g. eFL_1, eFL_2) have been QC-filtered and normalized with normalize_UMIs, and a set of highly variable genes is needed before PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering.

skills.search_text: glm-based-variable-gene-selection Use when pre-processed SingCellaR objects (e.g. eFL_1, eFL_2) have been QC-filtered and normalized with normalize_UMIs, and a set of highly variable genes is needed before PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering. Data are not yet normalized (normalize_UMIs has not been run) or still contain unfiltered doublets and low-UMI cells, since GLM mean–CV fits would be distorted by low-quality cells. The goal is a basic variance screen without dispersion modeling — SingCellaR provides get_variable_genes_basic(object, mean_expr_cutoff, max_of_mean_expr_cutoff, cv.max, cv.min) for that simpler case. The object format is not a SingCellaR/SingleCellExperiment object (e.g. a Seurat object), since the function operates on SingCellaR's own object structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies highly variable genes in SingCellaR scRNA-seq objects by fitting a generalized linear model of mean expression versus dispersion, providing data-driven cutoffs for both single-sample and integrative workflows. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Identifies highly variable genes in SingCellaR scRNA-seq objects by fitting a generalized linear model of mean expression versus dispersion, providing data-driven cutoffs for both single-sample and integrative workflows.

skills.search_text: gmm-based-cell-reliability-modeling Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq (source) with unlabeled scATAC-seq gene-activity (target) h5ad data and you must decide per-cell which scATAC-seq cells are trustworthy for label transfer or are candidate novel cell types. skills.summary: Model the reliability of scATAC-seq cells during unpaired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq integration with a two-component Gaussian Mixture Model over embedding discriminability and classification confidence, so that reliable cells are merged into the annotated scRNA-seq data while unreliable cells can be flagged as novel types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are paired across omics (cross-omics pairing information available), where scAI or MOFA+ joint integration is the appropriate choice The scATAC-seq peak data have not been converted into a gene activity matrix with common genes with the scRNA-seq data, so reliability modeling on incomparable features would be meaningless The goal is a single-shot label transfer of all scATAC-seq cells to known types with no need to separate reliable from unreliable cells or detect novel types

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-cycle pseudo-time inference on scRNA-seq data — e.g., five melanoma patient 10X Chromium samples (Mel78–Mel88) — and a model-free GMM baseline ordering is needed for GSEA NES comparison against a circular model such as Cyclum.
skills.name: gmm-based-pseudo-time-reconstruction
skills.search_text: gmm-based-pseudo-time-reconstruction Use when benchmarking cell-cycle pseudo-time inference on scRNA-seq data — e.g., five melanoma patient 10X Chromium samples (Mel78–Mel88) — and a model-free GMM baseline ordering is needed for GSEA NES comparison against a circular model such as Cyclum. The latent process is not circular/periodic — linear-representation trajectory methods or PCA-based orderings, not GMM-based cell-cycle reconstruction, are appropriate for non-periodic pseudo-time Goal is accurate cell-cycle pseudo-time itself rather than benchmarking: the paper's finding is that reCAT constitutes a disadvantage versus Cyclum ('a clear advantage over other model-free approaches, such as reCAT'), so reCAT ordering alone should not be the final result Phase labels already exist from marker-gene scoring (e.g., scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle or Seurat CellCycleScoring) and only need refinement — Cyclum's refine_labels workflow applies instead of re-running GMM reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstruct single-cell cell-cycle pseudo-time with reCAT's Gaussian mixture model (GMM) on log2(x+1) transformed, centered (mean=1), scaled (variance=1) scRNA-seq matrices, and use the resulting orderings as a model-free baseline benchmarked against Cyclum, PC1, and PC2 via GSEA enrichment of the GO cell-cycle gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Reconstruct single-cell cell-cycle pseudo-time with reCAT's Gaussian mixture model (GMM) on log2(x+1) transformed, centered (mean=1), scaled (variance=1) scRNA-seq matrices, and use the resulting orderings as a model-free baseline benchmarked against Cyclum, PC1, and PC2 via GSEA enrichment of the GO cell-cycle gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The latent process is not circular/periodic — linear-representation trajectory methods or PCA-based orderings, not GMM-based cell-cycle reconstruction, are appropriate for non-periodic pseudo-time Goal is accurate cell-cycle pseudo-time itself rather than benchmarking: the paper's finding is that reCAT constitutes a disadvantage versus Cyclum ('a clear advantage over other model-free approaches, such as reCAT'), so reCAT ordering alone should not be the final result Phase labels already exist from marker-gene scoring (e.g., scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle or Seurat CellCycleScoring) and only need refinement — Cyclum's refine_labels workflow applies instead of re-running GMM reconstruction

skills.description: Use when building a VEGA model or similar annotation-guided VAE: you have GMT-format gene set files (e.g., MSigDB) and a Scanpy AnnData matrix, and need the decoder mask linking GMVs to member genes.

skills.search_text: gmt-gene-module-mask-assembly Use when building a VEGA model or similar annotation-guided VAE: you have GMT-format gene set files (e.g., MSigDB) and a Scanpy AnnData matrix, and need the decoder mask linking GMVs to member genes. The analysis goal is a generic, fully expressive generative model with maximal predictive performance rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's hard-coded sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices generative capacity for interpretability. The gene modules are unknown or you expect prior annotations (e.g., MSigDB) to be incomplete or not context-specific and need the model to correct them — the hard-coded connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge. Input is raw unprocessed counts without the recommended preprocessing or a GMT membership file matching the AnnData gene universe. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assembles the binary gene membership mask from GMT gene-module files that wires VEGA's sparse linear decoder, so each latent gene-module variable (GMV) connects only to its annotated member genes in the order of the AnnData expression matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Assembles the binary gene membership mask from GMT gene-module files that wires VEGA's sparse linear decoder, so each latent gene-module variable (GMV) connects only to its annotated member genes in the order of the AnnData expression matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a generic, fully expressive generative model with maximal predictive performance rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's hard-coded sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices generative capacity for interpretability. Input is raw unprocessed counts without the recommended preprocessing or a GMT membership file matching the AnnData gene universe.

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered gene co-expression network (e.g. Normalisr coex edges at Q ≤ 1e-15) and want to test whether genes annotated to the same GO or KEGG pathway are connected more often than expected by chance.
skills.name: go-kegg-edge-over-abundance-testing
skills.search_text: go-kegg-edge-over-abundance-testing Use when you have a filtered gene co-expression network (e.g. Normalisr coex edges at Q ≤ 1e-15) and want to test whether genes annotated to the same GO or KEGG pathway are connected more often than expected by chance. You want to test arbitrary nonlinear gene–gene associations rather than co-expression captured by Normalisr's linear framework — the article states Normalisr is not designed for hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations. The network was built from full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq — the study only focused on UMI-based datasets and did not validate the pipeline on full-length platforms. You need causal regulatory network reconstruction (v-structures, regularized regression, Granger causality) rather than functional enrichment of undirected co-expression edges. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Tests whether gene pairs sharing GO or KEGG pathway annotations are over-represented among edges of a single-cell co-expression network, using GOATOOLS (GO) and BioServices (KEGG) with Bonferroni correction. Applied to the Normalisr-derived dysfunctional CD8+ T cell network, it recovered significant edge over-abundance for 33 GO and 8 KEGG pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Tests whether gene pairs sharing GO or KEGG pathway annotations are over-represented among edges of a single-cell co-expression network, using GOATOOLS (GO) and BioServices (KEGG) with Bonferroni correction. Applied to the Normalisr-derived dysfunctional CD8+ T cell network, it recovered significant edge over-abundance for 33 GO and 8 KEGG pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to test arbitrary nonlinear gene–gene associations rather than co-expression captured by Normalisr's linear framework — the article states Normalisr is not designed for hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations. The network was built from full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq — the study only focused on UMI-based datasets and did not validate the pipeline on full-length platforms. You need causal regulatory network reconstruction (v-structures, regularized regression, Granger causality) rather than functional enrichment of undirected co-expression edges.
