skills.name: go-term-overrepresentation-analysis
skills.search_text: go-term-overrepresentation-analysis Use when you have a CAFEH results table (cafeh.{mode}.results with pip, top_component, alpha, rank, p_active per SNP-study pair) and want to test whether tissue-specific vs shared eQTL regulation differs in constraint, disease association, and functional pathways. No CAFEH results table exists yet — the gene sets depend on top_component sharing across tissues, so colocalization/fine-mapping must be run first Loci whose disease effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — per the paper these 'may not demonstrate eQTL effects and therefore cannot be explored with CAFEH', so no colocalization-based gene sets can be defined You need ranked-list enrichment (e.g., GSEA) rather than binary gene-set overrepresentation — this skill uses Fisher exact tests on dichotomized gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Defines gene sets from CAFEH colocalization results (highly vs poorly colocalizing genes against a background of genes with significant cis-eQTLs in >=20 tissues) and tests them for selective constraint (LOEUF, pLI Wilcoxon tests), OMIM disease-gene enrichment (Fisher exact tests), and GO term overrepresentation with Bonferroni correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Defines gene sets from CAFEH colocalization results (highly vs poorly colocalizing genes against a background of genes with significant cis-eQTLs in >=20 tissues) and tests them for selective constraint (LOEUF, pLI Wilcoxon tests), OMIM disease-gene enrichment (Fisher exact tests), and GO term overrepresentation with Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No CAFEH results table exists yet — the gene sets depend on top_component sharing across tissues, so colocalization/fine-mapping must be run first Loci whose disease effects are mediated via coding variants without eQTL effects — per the paper these 'may not demonstrate eQTL effects and therefore cannot be explored with CAFEH', so no colocalization-based gene sets can be defined You need ranked-list enrichment (e.g., GSEA) rather than binary gene-set overrepresentation — this skill uses Fisher exact tests on dichotomized gene sets

skills.description: Use when comparing unsupervised gene program/module discovery outputs (e.g., SSN gene modules, ICA components, NMF factors) for their ability to recover known functional annotations such as GO terms or PPI enrichments.
skills.name: go-term-recovery-jaccard-scoring
skills.search_text: go-term-recovery-jaccard-scoring Use when comparing unsupervised gene program/module discovery outputs (e.g., SSN gene modules, ICA components, NMF factors) for their ability to recover known functional annotations such as GO terms or PPI enrichments. When scoring cell-type marker sets against clusters for annotation (use the Miko scoring pipeline: nullScore, mikoScore, sigScore — a different, hypothesis-testing workflow) When the input is already an annotated gene set with known GO labels rather than an unsupervised program output to be validated When the goal is per-gene differential expression testing (e.g., CDI-based bDEG identification) rather than gene-set-level recovery benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Benchmarks gene program discovery methods (SSN vs ICA vs NMF) by scoring each program's GO-term recovery as the maximum column-wise Jaccard similarity between the program's gene set and curated GO terms, together with STRING PPI interaction enrichment. This operationalizes the scPipeline/scMiko claim that scale-free SSN programs recover known biology better than factorization-based methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks gene program discovery methods (SSN vs ICA vs NMF) by scoring each program's GO-term recovery as the maximum column-wise Jaccard similarity between the program's gene set and curated GO terms, together with STRING PPI interaction enrichment. This operationalizes the scPipeline/scMiko claim that scale-free SSN programs recover known biology better than factorization-based methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When scoring cell-type marker sets against clusters for annotation (use the Miko scoring pipeline: nullScore, mikoScore, sigScore — a different, hypothesis-testing workflow) When the input is already an annotated gene set with known GO labels rather than an unsupervised program output to be validated When the goal is per-gene differential expression testing (e.g., CDI-based bDEG identification) rather than gene-set-level recovery benchmarking

skills.description: Use when benchmarking batch-correction/integration methods for over-correction risk: you need a known implanted biological signal (GOBP term in one cell type of one batch) that a good integrator must preserve, not erase.
skills.name: gobp-gene-perturbation-simulation
skills.search_text: gobp-gene-perturbation-simulation Use when benchmarking batch-correction/integration methods for over-correction risk: you need a known implanted biological signal (GOBP term in one cell type of one batch) that a good integrator must preserve, not erase. The goal is to measure batch-effect removal strength rather than over-correction risk — an unperturbed benchmark (e.g. scIB metrics on the original data) is the right setup, since the implanted signal here deliberately confounds batch with biology The dataset lacks both cell-type annotations and batch labels, so the perturbation cannot be confined to a specific cell type within a single batch The biological question concerns a real disease/condition contrast (e.g. healthy vs COVID-19 samples) rather than a simulated implanted signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implants a controlled biological signal into a single-cell dataset by increasing expression of genes annotated to a specific GOBP term (e.g. 'Defense response to Virus') in a defined cell type and batch, creating a perturbed dataset to test whether batch-correction methods over-correct real biology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Implants a controlled biological signal into a single-cell dataset by increasing expression of genes annotated to a specific GOBP term (e.g. 'Defense response to Virus') in a defined cell type and batch, creating a perturbed dataset to test whether batch-correction methods over-correct real biology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure batch-effect removal strength rather than over-correction risk — an unperturbed benchmark (e.g. scIB metrics on the original data) is the right setup, since the implanted signal here deliberately confounds batch with biology The dataset lacks both cell-type annotations and batch labels, so the perturbation cannot be confined to a specific cell type within a single batch The biological question concerns a real disease/condition contrast (e.g. healthy vs COVID-19 samples) rather than a simulated implanted signal

skills.description: Use when a ranked GRN prediction (e.g., SINGE_Ranked_Edge_List.txt) must be audited per regulator against a gold standard, to check whether aggregate precision-recall conceals poor performance for individual regulators.
skills.name: gold-standard-interaction-mapping
skills.search_text: gold-standard-interaction-mapping Use when a ranked GRN prediction (e.g., SINGE_Ranked_Edge_List.txt) must be audited per regulator against a gold standard, to check whether aggregate precision-recall conceals poor performance for individual regulators. You only need an overall precision-recall curve for a GRN method and are not investigating regulator-level caveats No gold standard with documented regulator-target edges is available for the dataset (e.g., the ESCAPE evaluated regulators do not cover your system) The prediction is a binary adjacency matrix rather than a ranked edge list — edge ranks for boxplots cannot be formed http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A regulator-specific evaluation skill for GRN inference: map each evaluated regulator's gold-standard edges (e.g., the 12 regulators in the ESCAPE mESC standard such as Dab2, Esrrb) onto SINGE's Borda-aggregated ranked edge list, and render per-regulator boxplots of edge ranks sorted by gold-standard outgoing-edge count to expose regulators whose predictions are poor despite acceptable overall precision-recall performance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: A regulator-specific evaluation skill for GRN inference: map each evaluated regulator's gold-standard edges (e.g., the 12 regulators in the ESCAPE mESC standard such as Dab2, Esrrb) onto SINGE's Borda-aggregated ranked edge list, and render per-regulator boxplots of edge ranks sorted by gold-standard outgoing-edge count to expose regulators whose predictions are poor despite acceptable overall precision-recall performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need an overall precision-recall curve for a GRN method and are not investigating regulator-level caveats No gold standard with documented regulator-target edges is available for the dataset (e.g., the ESCAPE evaluated regulators do not cover your system) The prediction is a binary adjacency matrix rather than a ranked edge list — edge ranks for boxplots cannot be formed

skills.description: Use when training a custom aptardi model (Mode 2) or benchmarking polyA site predictors against 3'-sequencing-derived gold-standard polyA sites that need to be mapped to label columns.
skills.name: gold-standard-polya-site-labeling
skills.search_text: gold-standard-polya-site-labeling Use when training a custom aptardi model (Mode 2) or benchmarking polyA site predictors against 3'-sequencing-derived gold-standard polyA sites that need to be mapped to label columns. You want to run aptardi's canonical Mode 1 with the pre-built HBR model (model.hdf5 and scale.pk), which does not require gold-standard labels The polyA sites are unreliable or unvalidated — Mode 2 explicitly requires 'reliable genomic locations of polyA sites as the gold standard labels to train model' http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Supply reliable gold-standard polyadenylation (polyA) site labels to train a custom aptardi Mode 2 model, using a tab-separated polyA sites file with 0-based chromosome, strand, and site column indices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Supply reliable gold-standard polyadenylation (polyA) site labels to train a custom aptardi Mode 2 model, using a tab-separated polyA sites file with 0-based chromosome, strand, and site column indices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to run aptardi's canonical Mode 1 with the pre-built HBR model (model.hdf5 and scale.pk), which does not require gold-standard labels The polyA sites are unreliable or unvalidated — Mode 2 explicitly requires 'reliable genomic locations of polyA sites as the gold standard labels to train model'

skills.description: Use when a set of candidate RBPs (e.g. CRIT-derived non-physically-associated candidates) must be connected to known circRNA regulators through binding-motif similarity, given circRNA sequences and a gold-regulator motif set.
skills.name: gold-standard-regulator-validation
skills.search_text: gold-standard-regulator-validation Use when a set of candidate RBPs (e.g. CRIT-derived non-physically-associated candidates) must be connected to known circRNA regulators through binding-motif similarity, given circRNA sequences and a gold-regulator motif set. Candidate RBPs already have documented physical interactions with gold regulators — physical interaction, not motif similarity, is the appropriate evidence channel for those candidates CircRNA sequences cannot be mapped to chromosomal positions in CircBase/GENCODE, so candidate RBP–circRNA associations (C value) cannot be established The aim is regulator discovery from expression/alteration data (the CRIT NMF pipeline on ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value features) rather than post-hoc validation of an already-identified candidate set http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Validates candidate circRNA-regulating RBPs that lack physical interactions with gold regulators by testing whether their de novo RNA-binding motifs (discovered with MEME on circRNA sequences) significantly resemble gold-regulator motifs via TOMTOM comparison. This provides an orthogonal, motif-based line of evidence that novel RBPs participate in the circRNA life cycle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Validates candidate circRNA-regulating RBPs that lack physical interactions with gold regulators by testing whether their de novo RNA-binding motifs (discovered with MEME on circRNA sequences) significantly resemble gold-regulator motifs via TOMTOM comparison. This provides an orthogonal, motif-based line of evidence that novel RBPs participate in the circRNA life cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate RBPs already have documented physical interactions with gold regulators — physical interaction, not motif similarity, is the appropriate evidence channel for those candidates CircRNA sequences cannot be mapped to chromosomal positions in CircBase/GENCODE, so candidate RBP–circRNA associations (C value) cannot be established The aim is regulator discovery from expression/alteration data (the CRIT NMF pipeline on ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value features) rather than post-hoc validation of an already-identified candidate set

skills.description: Use when comparing a trajectory inference method's inferred topology, pseudotime, and cell-fate predictions against known synthetic ground truth (e.g., dyntoy multifurcating, cyclic, or disconnected datasets) to quantify accuracy.
skills.name: gold-standard-topology-graph-distance-comparison
skills.search_text: gold-standard-topology-graph-distance-comparison Use when comparing a trajectory inference method's inferred topology, pseudotime, and cell-fate predictions against known synthetic ground truth (e.g., dyntoy multifurcating, cyclic, or disconnected datasets) to quantify accuracy. Input is real biological data without known gold-standard topology/pseudotime — the dynverse metrics require ground-truth milestone networks and fate labels The goal is realistic synthetic data rather than quick topology benchmarking — the dyntoy README notes its model is 'very simplistic (and far from realistic)' and recommends dyngen for more realistic simulations Datasets are atlas-scale (10^5–10^6 cells) where runtime/scalability, not gold-standard topology accuracy, is the evaluation target http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark a trajectory inference method against gold-standard synthetic topologies (dynverse/dyntoy) by scoring inferred trajectories with the five dynverse metrics — graph edit distance, F1-branch, Ipsen-Mikhailov distance, pseudotime correlation, and F1 cell fate — and aggregating them into a composite accuracy ranking, as done for VIA versus Palantir, PAGA, Slingshot, STREAM, and Monocle3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Benchmark a trajectory inference method against gold-standard synthetic topologies (dynverse/dyntoy) by scoring inferred trajectories with the five dynverse metrics — graph edit distance, F1-branch, Ipsen-Mikhailov distance, pseudotime correlation, and F1 cell fate — and aggregating them into a composite accuracy ranking, as done for VIA versus Palantir, PAGA, Slingshot, STREAM, and Monocle3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real biological data without known gold-standard topology/pseudotime — the dynverse metrics require ground-truth milestone networks and fate labels The goal is realistic synthetic data rather than quick topology benchmarking — the dyntoy README notes its model is 'very simplistic (and far from realistic)' and recommends dyngen for more realistic simulations Datasets are atlas-scale (10^5–10^6 cells) where runtime/scalability, not gold-standard topology accuracy, is the evaluation target

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a zero-inflated count model (e.g., ZINB-WaVE on scRNA-seq counts) actually fits observed mean counts, dropout rates, and genewise dispersions better than simpler negative binomial or hurdle alternatives.
skills.name: goodness-of-fit-diagnostic-visualization
skills.search_text: goodness-of-fit-diagnostic-visualization Use when evaluating whether a zero-inflated count model (e.g., ZINB-WaVE on scRNA-seq counts) actually fits observed mean counts, dropout rates, and genewise dispersions better than simpler negative binomial or hurdle alternatives. The goal is low-dimensional signal extraction or dimensionality reduction (ZINB-WaVE's primary use, e.g., vs PCA/ZIFA) rather than goodness-of-fit comparison of count models The data are bulk RNA-seq or already normalized with no dropout structure, so zero-inflated negative binomial vs NB vs hurdle comparison is not meaningful Only one count model can be fit — the skill's core value is the three-way ZINB vs NB (edgeR) vs MAST hurdle comparison and its diagnostic plots http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A diagnostic-comparison skill for single-cell RNA-seq count models: fit a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB-WaVE) model alongside competing count models (edgeR negative binomial, MAST hurdle) and judge fit via estimated-vs-observed mean count, zero probability, and dispersion visualizations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: A diagnostic-comparison skill for single-cell RNA-seq count models: fit a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB-WaVE) model alongside competing count models (edgeR negative binomial, MAST hurdle) and judge fit via estimated-vs-observed mean count, zero probability, and dispersion visualizations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is low-dimensional signal extraction or dimensionality reduction (ZINB-WaVE's primary use, e.g., vs PCA/ZIFA) rather than goodness-of-fit comparison of count models The data are bulk RNA-seq or already normalized with no dropout structure, so zero-inflated negative binomial vs NB vs hurdle comparison is not meaningful Only one count model can be fit — the skill's core value is the three-way ZINB vs NB (edgeR) vs MAST hurdle comparison and its diagnostic plots

skills.description: Use when validating RNA velocity model fits (UniTVelo with spliced/unspliced AnnData) by scoring per-gene R2 goodness-of-fit, e.g. to check that velocity fields and latent time are supported by dynamically informed genes.
skills.name: goodness-of-fit-r2-evaluation-per-gene
skills.search_text: goodness-of-fit-r2-evaluation-per-gene Use when validating RNA velocity model fits (UniTVelo with spliced/unspliced AnnData) by scoring per-gene R2 goodness-of-fit, e.g. to check that velocity fields and latent time are supported by dynamically informed genes. No spliced/unspliced counts are available (e.g. metabolic-labeling information is the required input modality or only a feature table exists) — UniTVelo's phase-portrait-based R2 is undefined The goal is comparing velocity methods against ground-truth cluster edges with directional metrics (e.g. Cross Boundary Direction Correctness via utv.evaluate) rather than per-gene fit quality Genes were not dynamically informed by the fitted model — R2 goodness-of-fit is meaningful for dynamically informed genes, not all genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the coefficient of determination R2 per gene as a goodness-of-fit indicator for UniTVelo RNA velocity fits, reproducing the Fig. 4c histogram on the scEU-seq intestinal organoid dataset to validate dynamical model quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7
skills.summary: Computes the coefficient of determination R2 per gene as a goodness-of-fit indicator for UniTVelo RNA velocity fits, reproducing the Fig. 4c histogram on the scEU-seq intestinal organoid dataset to validate dynamical model quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No spliced/unspliced counts are available (e.g. metabolic-labeling information is the required input modality or only a feature table exists) — UniTVelo's phase-portrait-based R2 is undefined The goal is comparing velocity methods against ground-truth cluster edges with directional metrics (e.g. Cross Boundary Direction Correctness via utv.evaluate) rather than per-gene fit quality Genes were not dynamically informed by the fitted model — R2 goodness-of-fit is meaningful for dynamically informed genes, not all genes

skills.search_text: gpr-based-reaction-activity-scoring Use when you have a bulk gene x sample RNA-seq expression matrix (human gene symbols as row names, non-negative normalized values) and need reaction-level activity scores to feed compute_flux in a METAFlux/Human-GEM workflow. Input is single-cell data — use calculate_avg_exp plus compute_sc_flux instead of bulk MRAS scoring You already have MRAS/reaction scores and only need fluxes — proceed directly to compute_flux with a medium file Expression matrix uses non-human identifiers or contains negative values — it must first be converted to human gene symbols and normalized http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a bulk gene expression matrix by resolving Human-GEM Gene-protein-reaction (GPR) rules, producing the 13082-reaction input required by METAFlux's downstream flux balance analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Computes single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a bulk gene expression matrix by resolving Human-GEM Gene-protein-reaction (GPR) rules, producing the 13082-reaction input required by METAFlux's downstream flux balance analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data — use calculate_avg_exp plus compute_sc_flux instead of bulk MRAS scoring You already have MRAS/reaction scores and only need fluxes — proceed directly to compute_flux with a medium file Expression matrix uses non-human identifiers or contains negative values — it must first be converted to human gene symbols and normalized

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell dataset (e.g. Heart Cell Atlas, ~500,000 cells) must undergo covariate-removal correction via a latent-variable model, or when wall-clock runtimes of scVI vs SiFT vs regress_out must be measured across increasing cell counts.
skills.name: gpu-accelerated-latent-variable-model-training
skills.search_text: gpu-accelerated-latent-variable-model-training Use when a large single-cell dataset (e.g. Heart Cell Atlas, ~500,000 cells) must undergo covariate-removal correction via a latent-variable model, or when wall-clock runtimes of scVI vs SiFT vs regress_out must be measured across increasing cell counts. When the goal is biological signal quality of the correction rather than scalability — the article notes no ground truth reference is available to evaluate computational filtering results, and integration metrics may be application-specific. When the dataset is small (e.g. thousands of cells) such that CPU regression baselines are cheap enough that GPU latent-variable training adds no practical runtime benefit. When the signal to remove requires cell-gene-expression-level correction rather than a joint latent representation — the article notes 'most integration methods, including scVI, provide a correction at the level of a joint latent representation of the cells'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Trains scVI (scverse scvi-tools), a variational latent-variable model operating on a joint latent representation of cells, with GPU acceleration to perform covariate correction at scale — here benchmarked against SiFT (gene-expression-level filtering) and scanpy regress_out on Heart Cell Atlas subsamples up to ~486,134 cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Trains scVI (scverse scvi-tools), a variational latent-variable model operating on a joint latent representation of cells, with GPU acceleration to perform covariate correction at scale — here benchmarked against SiFT (gene-expression-level filtering) and scanpy regress_out on Heart Cell Atlas subsamples up to ~486,134 cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biological signal quality of the correction rather than scalability — the article notes no ground truth reference is available to evaluate computational filtering results, and integration metrics may be application-specific. When the dataset is small (e.g. thousands of cells) such that CPU regression baselines are cheap enough that GPU latent-variable training adds no practical runtime benefit. When the signal to remove requires cell-gene-expression-level correction rather than a joint latent representation — the article notes 'most integration methods, including scVI, provide a correction at the level of a joint latent representation of the cells'.

skills.description: Use when a .h5ad anndata scRNA-seq dataset must be classified (e.g. cell_type or disease target) by a DNN on constrained hardware (e.g. 12GB GPU / 128GB RAM), where memory-heavy pipelines like scVI-tools fail on full feature sets (e.g. 22,858 features).
skills.name: gpu-based-dnn-model-training
skills.search_text: gpu-based-dnn-model-training Use when a .h5ad anndata scRNA-seq dataset must be classified (e.g. cell_type or disease target) by a DNN on constrained hardware (e.g. 12GB GPU / 128GB RAM), where memory-heavy pipelines like scVI-tools fail on full feature sets (e.g. 22,858 features). The goal is unsupervised representation learning or generative modeling (e.g. scVI-style latent embeddings) rather than supervised classification with labeled targets Data is not in anndata .h5ad format with a labeled target column — scaLR requires prior preprocessing into this format Feature importances must be extracted from a comparison model that does not expose them (scBalance, scVI-tools, devCellPy, cellPLM) — biomarker ranking comparability is limited http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a Deep Neural Network (SequentialModel via scaLR) on single-cell expression data in batch-wise, disk-backed reads on GPU ('cuda') or CPU, with early stopping and checkpointing, for cell type/state annotation under low-resource constraints. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Trains a Deep Neural Network (SequentialModel via scaLR) on single-cell expression data in batch-wise, disk-backed reads on GPU ('cuda') or CPU, with early stopping and checkpointing, for cell type/state annotation under low-resource constraints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised representation learning or generative modeling (e.g. scVI-style latent embeddings) rather than supervised classification with labeled targets Data is not in anndata .h5ad format with a labeled target column — scaLR requires prior preprocessing into this format Feature importances must be extracted from a comparison model that does not expose them (scBalance, scVI-tools, devCellPy, cellPLM) — biomarker ranking comparability is limited

skills.description: Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin structures from ChIA-PET anchors, PET clusters, and singletons on an NVIDIA GPU (Pascal or newer, CUDA_ARCH >= 60) and you need warp-parallel per-bead Monte Carlo energy minimization.
skills.name: gpu-bead-chain-energy-minimization
skills.search_text: gpu-bead-chain-energy-minimization Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin structures from ChIA-PET anchors, PET clusters, and singletons on an NVIDIA GPU (Pascal or newer, CUDA_ARCH >= 60) and you need warp-parallel per-bead Monte Carlo energy minimization. Running on GPUs older than Pascal (compute capability < 6.0) — CMake requires CUDA_ARCH >= 60 No GPU available and container-free CPU execution is required — cudaMMC is GPU-enhanced; the CPU-based 3D-GNOME (bitbucket.org/3dome/3dgnome) is the alternative Interpreting finished models rather than generating them — use the 3D-GNOME 3.0 web server analysis features instead of re-running the MC kernel http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Implements cudaMMC's warp-level parallel Simulated Annealing Monte Carlo search, where each 32-thread warp optimizes one chromatin bead by iteratively proposing random displacement moves and reducing to the lowest-energy move without global synchronization. This is the GPU kernel strategy that makes cudaMMC substantially faster and more stable than CPU-based 3D-GNOME for large chromatin model ensembles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Implements cudaMMC's warp-level parallel Simulated Annealing Monte Carlo search, where each 32-thread warp optimizes one chromatin bead by iteratively proposing random displacement moves and reducing to the lowest-energy move without global synchronization. This is the GPU kernel strategy that makes cudaMMC substantially faster and more stable than CPU-based 3D-GNOME for large chromatin model ensembles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running on GPUs older than Pascal (compute capability < 6.0) — CMake requires CUDA_ARCH >= 60 No GPU available and container-free CPU execution is required — cudaMMC is GPU-enhanced; the CPU-based 3D-GNOME (bitbucket.org/3dome/3dgnome) is the alternative Interpreting finished models rather than generating them — use the 3D-GNOME 3.0 web server analysis features instead of re-running the MC kernel

skills.description: Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin models from ChIA-PET anchors/PET clusters/singletons (e.g. GM12878 CTCF GRCh37/GRCh38) for single chromosomes or 100-model ensembles on an NVIDIA GPU (compute capability >= 6.0), especially when CPU 3D-GNOME runtimes (hours to days) are prohibitive.
skills.name: gpu-chromatin-3d-structure-simulation
skills.search_text: gpu-chromatin-3d-structure-simulation Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin models from ChIA-PET anchors/PET clusters/singletons (e.g. GM12878 CTCF GRCh37/GRCh38) for single chromosomes or 100-model ensembles on an NVIDIA GPU (compute capability >= 6.0), especially when CPU 3D-GNOME runtimes (hours to days) are prohibitive. No NVIDIA GPU with Pascal-or-newer architecture (compute capability >= 6.0) is available — the CPU-only 3D-GNOME from the Bitbucket repo should be used instead The task is interactive web-based modelling or promoter-enhancer contact analysis under structural variation — the 3D-GNOME 3.0 web server (https://3dgnome.mini.pw.edu.pl/) is the integrated interface for cudaMMC Input data is not ChIA-PET-style anchors/clusters/singletons (e.g. raw Hi-C contact matrices), which the 3D-GNOME input format does not cover http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generate ensembles of chromatin 3D structures from CTCF ChIA-PET data using cudaMMC, a GPU-enhanced multiscale Monte Carlo (Simulated Annealing) reimplementation of 3D-GNOME that yields 3x-25x speed-ups and order-of-magnitude runtime reductions for large chromosomes while preserving within-ensemble model quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Generate ensembles of chromatin 3D structures from CTCF ChIA-PET data using cudaMMC, a GPU-enhanced multiscale Monte Carlo (Simulated Annealing) reimplementation of 3D-GNOME that yields 3x-25x speed-ups and order-of-magnitude runtime reductions for large chromosomes while preserving within-ensemble model quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No NVIDIA GPU with Pascal-or-newer architecture (compute capability >= 6.0) is available — the CPU-only 3D-GNOME from the Bitbucket repo should be used instead The task is interactive web-based modelling or promoter-enhancer contact analysis under structural variation — the 3D-GNOME 3.0 web server (https://3dgnome.mini.pw.edu.pl/) is the integrated interface for cudaMMC Input data is not ChIA-PET-style anchors/clusters/singletons (e.g. raw Hi-C contact matrices), which the 3D-GNOME input format does not cover

skills.search_text: gpu-cpu-memory-and-runtime-profiling Use when benchmarking scLENS or similar single-cell pipelines for memory footprint and speed on CPU vs. GPU, or when evaluating whether median scaling can replace z-score scaling to cut resource cost. The goal is dimensionality reduction quality alone (e.g. evaluating scLENS against 11 other DR tools) rather than computational cost measurement Input data has already undergone feature selection of highly variable genes, which compromises low-variance local structure and changes the memory profile being measured No CUDA-capable GPU is present and GPU memory savings are the target metric — the package will silently fall back to CPU http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Profiles peak CPU memory, GPU memory, and wall-clock runtime of a Julia-based dimensionality reduction pipeline (scLENS vs. its median-scaling variant scLENS-med) across datasets of varying cell counts, to quantify the computational savings of replacing z-score gene scaling with median scaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: Profiles peak CPU memory, GPU memory, and wall-clock runtime of a Julia-based dimensionality reduction pipeline (scLENS vs. its median-scaling variant scLENS-med) across datasets of varying cell counts, to quantify the computational savings of replacing z-score gene scaling with median scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is dimensionality reduction quality alone (e.g. evaluating scLENS against 11 other DR tools) rather than computational cost measurement Input data has already undergone feature selection of highly variable genes, which compromises low-variance local structure and changes the memory profile being measured No CUDA-capable GPU is present and GPU memory savings are the target metric — the package will silently fall back to CPU

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cudaMMC against 3D-GNOME timing on the same workstation and you have per-run execution times for ≥10 repeated runs per chromosome-method pair, and need a reproducible stability metric (CoV) rather than a single wall-clock time.
skills.name: gpu-cpu-performance-quantification
skills.search_text: gpu-cpu-performance-quantification Use when benchmarking cudaMMC against 3D-GNOME timing on the same workstation and you have per-run execution times for ≥10 repeated runs per chromosome-method pair, and need a reproducible stability metric (CoV) rather than a single wall-clock time. You only have a single timing run per configuration — no variance can be estimated, so a CoV-based stability comparison is meaningless; report absolute run time instead. The goal is comparing structural quality of the generated chromatin models (e.g. enhancer–promoter distances), not execution-time stability. Timing runs were executed on different workstations or under differing GPU/CUDA configurations, so cudaMMC and 3D-GNOME timings are not comparable on the same hardware baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Quantifies and compares run-time stability of the GPU-accelerated cudaMMC engine against the CPU-based 3D-GNOME method by computing coefficients of variation (CoV = std/mean × 100) over repeated modelling runs per chromosome, as reported for chr1, chr14 and chr21 in the cudaMMC paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Quantifies and compares run-time stability of the GPU-accelerated cudaMMC engine against the CPU-based 3D-GNOME method by computing coefficients of variation (CoV = std/mean × 100) over repeated modelling runs per chromosome, as reported for chr1, chr14 and chr21 in the cudaMMC paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single timing run per configuration — no variance can be estimated, so a CoV-based stability comparison is meaningless; report absolute run time instead. The goal is comparing structural quality of the generated chromatin models (e.g. enhancer–promoter distances), not execution-time stability. Timing runs were executed on different workstations or under differing GPU/CUDA configurations, so cudaMMC and 3D-GNOME timings are not comparable on the same hardware baseline.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation pipeline scales to large scRNA-seq datasets: time identical LATE runs on GPU and CPU builds of TensorFlow and compare against other imputation methods' runtimes.
skills.name: gpu-cpu-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gpu-cpu-runtime-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether an imputation pipeline scales to large scRNA-seq datasets: time identical LATE runs on GPU and CPU builds of TensorFlow and compare against other imputation methods' runtimes. The goal is imputation accuracy (e.g., mean squared error against a masked ground truth) rather than runtime scalability — use the LATE imputation/analysis workflow instead The dataset is a small PBMC subset (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) where GPU-vs-CPU differences are unlikely to be meaningful; timing is intended for large (1M+ cell) data The environment only supports TensorFlow 2.x, since LATE is not compatible with TF2 and timing results would be unobtainable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark wall-clock runtime of LATE imputation on GPU versus CPU environments using the 10x Genomics mouse brain scRNA-seq data, to demonstrate scalability (over 1 million cells in a few hours on a GPU) and quantify the GPU speedup relative to CPU. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock runtime of LATE imputation on GPU versus CPU environments using the 10x Genomics mouse brain scRNA-seq data, to demonstrate scalability (over 1 million cells in a few hours on a GPU) and quantify the GPU speedup relative to CPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is imputation accuracy (e.g., mean squared error against a masked ground truth) rather than runtime scalability — use the LATE imputation/analysis workflow instead The dataset is a small PBMC subset (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) where GPU-vs-CPU differences are unlikely to be meaningful; timing is intended for large (1M+ cell) data The environment only supports TensorFlow 2.x, since LATE is not compatible with TF2 and timing results would be unobtainable

skills.name: gpu-deep-learning-training
skills.search_text: gpu-deep-learning-training Use when you must reproduce or adapt scBridge's iterative label transfer from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq (h5ad AnnData) on a single GPU, e.g. the SNARE-seq mouse cortex benchmark. Input is paired (linked) multi-omics data, where paired-integration tools such as scAI or MOFA+ apply instead of scBridge's unpaired transfer learning Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq matrices without a gene activity transformation — peaks must first be converted to a gene activity matrix (e.g. via Signac) Scenarios requiring novel cell-type discovery mode (--novel_type) with its different heuristic stopping rule (>75% scATAC-seq cells annotated), which is outside the standard supervised label-transfer setup http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train scBridge, a PyTorch-based heterogeneous transfer learning model, on a single CUDA-enabled GPU to iteratively integrate annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq data using a Gaussian Mixture reliability model. This skill covers the concrete training loop, hyperparameters, and hardware setup used to reproduce the SNARE-seq mouse cortex label-transfer result (71.95% accuracy). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Train scBridge, a PyTorch-based heterogeneous transfer learning model, on a single CUDA-enabled GPU to iteratively integrate annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq data using a Gaussian Mixture reliability model. This skill covers the concrete training loop, hyperparameters, and hardware setup used to reproduce the SNARE-seq mouse cortex label-transfer result (71.95% accuracy).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is paired (linked) multi-omics data, where paired-integration tools such as scAI or MOFA+ apply instead of scBridge's unpaired transfer learning Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq matrices without a gene activity transformation — peaks must first be converted to a gene activity matrix (e.g. via Signac) Scenarios requiring novel cell-type discovery mode (--novel_type) with its different heuristic stopping rule (>75% scATAC-seq cells annotated), which is outside the standard supervised label-transfer setup

skills.description: Use when a segmentation mask assigning transcripts to individual cells is needed from SST imaging data (e.g., Xenium transcripts.csv.gz + morphology_mip.ome.tif) and a ≥12GB VRAM GPU is available to train the UNet3+ model.
skills.name: gpu-deep-learning-training-and-inference
skills.search_text: gpu-deep-learning-training-and-inference Use when a segmentation mask assigning transcripts to individual cells is needed from SST imaging data (e.g., Xenium transcripts.csv.gz + morphology_mip.ome.tif) and a ≥12GB VRAM GPU is available to train the UNet3+ model. You intend to reuse a model pretrained on other imaging modalities (e.g., Cellpose) directly for SST segmentation without retraining — the article shows such pretrained models do not transfer well to SST images. No GPU with ≥12GB VRAM is available and the full-size dataset is being processed — the deep learning component is strongly GPU-dependent and higher-resolution segmentation needs larger patch sizes and more GPU memory. Nuclei images are separated into fields of view (e.g., CosMx) — model.stitch_nuclei() must be run before training, so plain train/predict alone is insufficient. Train and run inference with BIDCell's biologically-informed UNet3+ segmentation network on GPU to produce cell segmentation masks and cell-gene matrices for subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SST) data such as 10x Genomics Xenium. BIDCell uses self-supervised training with biologically-informed loss functions because manual pixel annotation is unattainable for SST data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Train and run inference with BIDCell's biologically-informed UNet3+ segmentation network on GPU to produce cell segmentation masks and cell-gene matrices for subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SST) data such as 10x Genomics Xenium. BIDCell uses self-supervised training with biologically-informed loss functions because manual pixel annotation is unattainable for SST data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You intend to reuse a model pretrained on other imaging modalities (e.g., Cellpose) directly for SST segmentation without retraining — the article shows such pretrained models do not transfer well to SST images. No GPU with ≥12GB VRAM is available and the full-size dataset is being processed — the deep learning component is strongly GPU-dependent and higher-resolution segmentation needs larger patch sizes and more GPU memory. Nuclei images are separated into fields of view (e.g., CosMx) — model.stitch_nuclei() must be run before training, so plain train/predict alone is insufficient.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a q-diffused or Gaussian kernel over a full n×n cell-pair affinity matrix on a (genes × cells) matrix, and the pairwise gene-to-gene computation is too slow on CPU (the paper reports 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix).
skills.name: gpu-parallel-pairwise-kernel-evaluation
skills.search_text: gpu-parallel-pairwise-kernel-evaluation Use when evaluating a q-diffused or Gaussian kernel over a full n×n cell-pair affinity matrix on a (genes × cells) matrix, and the pairwise gene-to-gene computation is too slow on CPU (the paper reports 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix). No CUDA-enabled GPU is available — omitting cuda_devices delegates to a CPU-bound method, so this skill cannot be applied (expect 20 min–3 h runtime per affinity matrix). The data matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — the kernel design assumes the full log-normalized transcriptome, so GPU-accelerated full-pairwise evaluation would bake in discarded high-order gene interactions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Accelerates evaluation of q-diffused (or Gaussian) kernels between all pairs of scRNAseq cells by delegating cell-by-cell, gene-to-gene computations to CUDA GPUs via the cuda_devices argument in QDiffusion.jl, instead of the CPU-bound default. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Accelerates evaluation of q-diffused (or Gaussian) kernels between all pairs of scRNAseq cells by delegating cell-by-cell, gene-to-gene computations to CUDA GPUs via the cuda_devices argument in QDiffusion.jl, instead of the CPU-bound default.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No CUDA-enabled GPU is available — omitting cuda_devices delegates to a CPU-bound method, so this skill cannot be applied (expect 20 min–3 h runtime per affinity matrix). The data matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — the kernel design assumes the full log-normalized transcriptome, so GPU-accelerated full-pairwise evaluation would bake in discarded high-order gene interactions.

skills.description: Use when the input is a sparsity-filtered single-cell cell-gene expression matrix and the goal is to detect the part of the dataset that behaves like a random matrix by fitting Marchenko-Pastur universality to its covariance eigenvalue spectrum.
skills.name: gradient-descent-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: gradient-descent-distribution-fitting Use when the input is a sparsity-filtered single-cell cell-gene expression matrix and the goal is to detect the part of the dataset that behaves like a random matrix by fitting Marchenko-Pastur universality to its covariance eigenvalue spectrum. Input is the raw, unfiltered sparse expression matrix — sparsity must first be removed by discarding genes causing spurious eigenvector localization in the randomized data, or the covariance spectrum will reflect sparsity-induced effects rather than the random-matrix component. The goal is to extract or interpret the biological (low-rank) signal itself — this skill only characterizes the random-matrix bulk; signal analysis is a separate downstream step. The data is already denoised or reduced to a low-rank representation — the MP fit would be meaningless on a spectrum whose noise bulk has been removed. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits the non-parametric Marchenko-Pastur distribution to the empirical eigenvalue density of the Wishart (sample covariance) matrix of a sparsity-filtered single-cell expression matrix, using gradient descent to locate the MP edge and thereby identify the random-matrix (noise) component of the data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Fits the non-parametric Marchenko-Pastur distribution to the empirical eigenvalue density of the Wishart (sample covariance) matrix of a sparsity-filtered single-cell expression matrix, using gradient descent to locate the MP edge and thereby identify the random-matrix (noise) component of the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is the raw, unfiltered sparse expression matrix — sparsity must first be removed by discarding genes causing spurious eigenvector localization in the randomized data, or the covariance spectrum will reflect sparsity-induced effects rather than the random-matrix component. The goal is to extract or interpret the biological (low-rank) signal itself — this skill only characterizes the random-matrix bulk; signal analysis is a separate downstream step. The data is already denoised or reduced to a low-rank representation — the MP fit would be meaningless on a spectrum whose noise bulk has been removed.

skills.summary: Extracts per-cell-type ranked gene lists from a trained SpatialDDLS neural network using gradient-based interpretation (Vanilla Gradient, Simonyan et al. 2014), computed with respect to either predicted class scores ('class') or the loss ('loss'), to identify which genes drive predicted cell type proportions.

skills.description: Use when inferring causal noncoding locus-gene relationships from paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (or other multimodal single-cell) data undergoing a dynamic process, where a DAG of cell states can be oriented by pseudotime.
skills.name: granger-causal-inference-on-dags
skills.search_text: granger-causal-inference-on-dags Use when inferring causal noncoding locus-gene relationships from paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (or other multimodal single-cell) data undergoing a dynamic process, where a DAG of cell states can be oriented by pseudotime. Data lack a dynamic biological process (e.g., differentiation or disease trajectory), since the method relies on multiomic single-cell data undergoing a dynamic process to provide pseudotemporal context Only a single modality is available, or you need per-locus resolution consolidated into a single per-gene score (MultiVelo-style analysis) rather than pair-level Granger causal tests The question is purely correlational peak-gene association where no causal time-lag modeling is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 GrID-Net (Granger Inference on DAGs) generalizes Granger causality from total orderings to partial orderings via lagged message-passing GNNs, quantifying causal peak-gene links in single-cell multimodal (RNA+ATAC) data on a DAG of cell states. It addresses 'cell-state parallax' — the causal time lag between chromatin accessibility and gene expression that correlational methods miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: GrID-Net (Granger Inference on DAGs) generalizes Granger causality from total orderings to partial orderings via lagged message-passing GNNs, quantifying causal peak-gene links in single-cell multimodal (RNA+ATAC) data on a DAG of cell states. It addresses 'cell-state parallax' — the causal time lag between chromatin accessibility and gene expression that correlational methods miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack a dynamic biological process (e.g., differentiation or disease trajectory), since the method relies on multiomic single-cell data undergoing a dynamic process to provide pseudotemporal context Only a single modality is available, or you need per-locus resolution consolidated into a single per-gene score (MultiVelo-style analysis) rather than pair-level Granger causal tests The question is purely correlational peak-gene association where no causal time-lag modeling is needed

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) from a dynamic process and need causal locus-gene links beyond correlation, or to validate/enrich enhancer-priming annotations of prioritized peak-gene pairs.

skills.summary: Apply GrID-Net, a graph neural network framework for Granger causal inference on DAGs, to paired single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq multimodal data to infer causal noncoding peak-gene regulatory links, exploiting pseudotemporal ordering to resolve the causal time lag ('cell-state parallax') that correlation-based methods miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not paired multimodal single-cell measurements from a dynamic biological process — GrID-Net's DAG construction relies on multimodal Schema integration and diffusion pseudotime over a differentiating trajectory The goal is a purely correlational co-accessibility/co-expression screen without any causal ordering hypothesis, or cells lack a biologically meaningful pseudotemporal axis (e.g. static tissue snapshots) Dataset lacks a credible root cell type/marker gene, since pseudotime orientation of the DAG requires a root (e.g. TOP2A+ cycling progenitors)

skills.description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data from a dynamic process (e.g. 10x Multiome corticogenesis) must be prioritized for causal peak-gene or variant-locus-to-gene links beyond correlation-based proximity.
skills.name: granger-causal-peak-gene-linking
skills.search_text: granger-causal-peak-gene-linking Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data from a dynamic process (e.g. 10x Multiome corticogenesis) must be prioritized for causal peak-gene or variant-locus-to-gene links beyond correlation-based proximity. The input data are not paired multimodal single-cell measurements (RNA + ATAC from the same cells); GrID-Net's DAG-of-cells construction and pseudotime orientation require jointly assayed modalities The tissue is static or lacks a dynamic process (differentiation/disease trajectory), since the method relies on pseudotemporal context from a dynamic biological process Data exceed GPU memory capacity, or a quick exploratory correlation-based peak-gene ranking suffices and causal lag inference is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies GrID-Net, a graph neural network that generalizes Granger causal inference to DAGs of cell states, to identify causal noncoding peak-gene links from paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq multimodal data, exploiting the 'cell-state parallax' time lag between chromatin accessibility and expression that correlation-based methods miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Applies GrID-Net, a graph neural network that generalizes Granger causal inference to DAGs of cell states, to identify causal noncoding peak-gene links from paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq multimodal data, exploiting the 'cell-state parallax' time lag between chromatin accessibility and expression that correlation-based methods miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are not paired multimodal single-cell measurements (RNA + ATAC from the same cells); GrID-Net's DAG-of-cells construction and pseudotime orientation require jointly assayed modalities The tissue is static or lacks a dynamic process (differentiation/disease trajectory), since the method relies on pseudotemporal context from a dynamic biological process Data exceed GPU memory capacity, or a quick exploratory correlation-based peak-gene ranking suffices and causal lag inference is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when constructing a lineage-specific gene regulatory network from scRNA-seq expression (h5ad/csv), a prior interaction network, and differential expression, and benchmarking GRN quality with AUPRC/EPR against ChIP-seq ground truth.
skills.name: graph-attention-model-training
skills.search_text: graph-attention-model-training Use when constructing a lineage-specific gene regulatory network from scRNA-seq expression (h5ad/csv), a prior interaction network, and differential expression, and benchmarking GRN quality with AUPRC/EPR against ChIP-seq ground truth. The goal is to process multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations at once — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time Ground-truth label datasets exist for a supervised approach — supervised frameworks such as GENELink may yield superior results Extrinsic factors (cell–cell communication, spatial location) or epigenetic regulation must be modeled — CEFCON only considers intracellular RNA-seq factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Train CEFCON's two-layer graph attention neural network under a deep graph infomax (DGI) contrastive learning framework to construct a cell-lineage-specific GRN from single-cell RNA-seq data, converting degree-scaled attention coefficients into an edge-weighted network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3

skills.name: graph-attention-network-encoder-implementation
skills.search_text: graph-attention-network-encoder-implementation Use when implementing or reconstructing the scGAE encoder: you have a cells × genes count matrix, a KNN cell graph (default K=35), and need a graph-attention latent embedding Z in TensorFlow/Spektral that supports joint feature and adjacency reconstruction. When the goal is a direct 2D embedding from the graph autoencoder itself — the authors note 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder', so an intermediate dimension plus tSNE is used instead When raw unpreprocessed counts are the only input — scGAE takes preprocessed data (scTransform in Seurat, or Scanpy) as input per the README http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implement the graph attention (GAT) encoder of scGAE that maps a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix X and its KNN cell-graph adjacency A into a low-dimensional latent embedding Z, forming the encoding half of a multitask graph autoencoder that must jointly feed a feature decoder and a graph (edge) decoder. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Implement the graph attention (GAT) encoder of scGAE that maps a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix X and its KNN cell-graph adjacency A into a low-dimensional latent embedding Z, forming the encoding half of a multitask graph autoencoder that must jointly feed a feature decoder and a graph (edge) decoder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a direct 2D embedding from the graph autoencoder itself — the authors note 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder', so an intermediate dimension plus tSNE is used instead When raw unpreprocessed counts are the only input — scGAE takes preprocessed data (scTransform in Seurat, or Scanpy) as input per the README

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be embedded for visualization, clustering, or trajectory inference while preserving inter-cell topological structure (e.g., keeping transcriptionally similar populations close), and deep-learning competitors lose cell-cell relationships.
skills.name: graph-autoencoder-embedding
skills.search_text: graph-autoencoder-embedding Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be embedded for visualization, clustering, or trajectory inference while preserving inter-cell topological structure (e.g., keeping transcriptionally similar populations close), and deep-learning competitors lose cell-cell relationships. When a direct 2D embedding is required without an intermediate step — the paper notes 'A better 2D visualization method is needed to preserve the topological structure' and uses intermediate-dimension-plus-tSNE instead. When input is already a feature/embedding table rather than a raw count matrix requiring scTransform preprocessing and KNN graph construction. When the optimal KNN graph connectivity must be fixed a priori — the article states 'the optimal K varies among different datasets and different parts of a dataset'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A skill for producing topology-preserving low-dimensional embeddings of scRNA-seq data with scGAE: build a KNN cell graph (default K=35), preprocess with scTransform, and train a multitask-oriented graph autoencoder (Spektral/TensorFlow) to embed cells into a 20-dimensional latent space that preserves both topological structure and feature information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: A skill for producing topology-preserving low-dimensional embeddings of scRNA-seq data with scGAE: build a KNN cell graph (default K=35), preprocess with scTransform, and train a multitask-oriented graph autoencoder (Spektral/TensorFlow) to embed cells into a 20-dimensional latent space that preserves both topological structure and feature information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a direct 2D embedding is required without an intermediate step — the paper notes 'A better 2D visualization method is needed to preserve the topological structure' and uses intermediate-dimension-plus-tSNE instead. When input is already a feature/embedding table rather than a raw count matrix requiring scTransform preprocessing and KNN graph construction. skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be embedded in a topology-preserving low-dimensional space with simultaneous cluster assignment, i.e., a cell graph is built and latent features plus cluster labels are learned jointly.
skills.name: graph-autoencoder-model-training
skills.search_text: graph-autoencoder-model-training Use when scRNA-seq count data must be embedded in a topology-preserving low-dimensional space with simultaneous cluster assignment, i.e., a cell graph is built and latent features plus cluster labels are learned jointly. Input is already a low-dimensional feature embedding or a non-single-cell dataset without cell–cell graph structure — the cell graph construction and topology preservation are the core premise Only 2D visualization is needed directly — the graph autoencoder embeds into an intermediate dimension and t-SNE is used for 2D visualization, so a direct 2D method is preferable Trajectory inference is the sole goal and clustering performance is irrelevant — scGAE matches scGNN on trajectory inference but its advantage is clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains the scGAE multitask-oriented graph autoencoder on scRNA-seq data: a pre-training stage minimizing the reconstruction loss L_r on a KNN cell graph, followed by deep-clustering alter-training that jointly minimizes L = L_r + gamma*L_c (gamma=2.5) with Student's-t soft assignment and DEC target distribution to yield a clustering-friendly latent embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional feature embedding or a non-single-cell dataset without cell–cell graph structure — the cell graph construction and topology preservation are the core premise Only 2D visualization is needed directly — the graph autoencoder embeds into an intermediate dimension and t-SNE is used for 2D visualization, so a direct 2D method is preferable Trajectory inference is the sole goal and clustering performance is irrelevant — scGAE matches scGNN on trajectory inference but its advantage is clustering

skills.search_text: graph-autoencoder-training-on-single-cell-rna-seq Use when you have a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq count matrix and need a topology-preserving low-dimensional embedding for cell clustering or trajectory/visualization tasks where deep methods like DCA, scVI, or scDeepCluster lose cell-cell relationships. skills.summary: Compute a 2D embedding of single-cell data via GraphDDP/GraphEmbed, which builds a graph with 'knn' edges (same-label nearest neighbors) and 'k_shift' edges (denser, different-label neighbors) and lays it out with the Kamada-Kawai force algorithm to integrate cluster membership and differentiation pathways in one visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior cluster/class assignment exists for the instances — GraphDDP is supervised and requires a discrete label per instance The goal is pseudotime ordering or trajectory inference alone (e.g. pseudo-time reconstruction) rather than an informed 2D visualization of cluster membership and differentiation pathways The dataset's clusters are naturally well separated and unsupervised methods like t-SNE, PCA, or MDS already suffice — reserve -c values of 5-30 and forced separation for noisy data

skills.description: Use when two networks over the same node set (e.g., denoised scGRNs for samples X and Y) must be aligned so each node's coordinates can be compared across conditions.
skills.name: graph-laplacian-eigendecomposition
skills.search_text: graph-laplacian-eigendecomposition Use when two networks over the same node set (e.g., denoised scGRNs for samples X and Y) must be aligned so each node's coordinates can be compared across conditions. The two networks do not share the same gene set, so cross-condition counterpart ties in the off-diagonal λI blocks cannot be defined Networks are still noisy pre-tensor-decomposition adjacency matrices — the alignment expects the CP tensor-decomposition denoised networks Comparing highly dissimilar samples (e.g., different cell types) rather than two populations of the same type, which scTenifoldNet is more suitable for http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Solves a sparse eigenvalue problem on a joint Laplacian built from two symmetrized gene regulatory networks so that genes from both samples are projected onto a shared low-dimensional manifold, enabling direct gene-by-gene comparison of regulatory positions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Solves a sparse eigenvalue problem on a joint Laplacian built from two symmetrized gene regulatory networks so that genes from both samples are projected onto a shared low-dimensional manifold, enabling direct gene-by-gene comparison of regulatory positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two networks do not share the same gene set, so cross-condition counterpart ties in the off-diagonal λI blocks cannot be defined Networks are still noisy pre-tensor-decomposition adjacency matrices — the alignment expects the CP tensor-decomposition denoised networks Comparing highly dissimilar samples (e.g., different cell types) rather than two populations of the same type, which scTenifoldNet is more suitable for

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a graph neural network (e.g., DGMP vs. MutSigCV, EMOGI, deepDriver) on gene regulatory networks with multi-omics gene features, or when evaluating generalization to an independent driver-gene test set.
skills.name: graph-neural-network-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-model-evaluation Use when benchmarking a graph neural network (e.g., DGMP vs. MutSigCV, EMOGI, deepDriver) on gene regulatory networks with multi-omics gene features, or when evaluating generalization to an independent driver-gene test set. The task requires patient-level predictions — DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which ignores individual cancer patient characteristics. The input is a raw mutation count table without a directed gene-gene interaction network; DGMP requires a GRN for the DGCN graph convolution operation. The goal is to weight the DGCN and MLP embedding contributions differently — DGMP simply concatenates the three DGCN and one MLP embedding vectors without accounting for their differing contributions. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reproducible setup and evaluation of DGMP, a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) jointed with MLP for identifying cancer driver genes from multi-omics data, including independent testing on non-overlapping CancerMine-derived driver genes across DawnNet, KEGG, and RegNetwork GRNs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Reproducible setup and evaluation of DGMP, a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) jointed with MLP for identifying cancer driver genes from multi-omics data, including independent testing on non-overlapping CancerMine-derived driver genes across DawnNet, KEGG, and RegNetwork GRNs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires patient-level predictions — DGMP averages SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, and gene expression across all samples, which ignores individual cancer patient characteristics. The input is a raw mutation count table without a directed gene-gene interaction network; DGMP requires a GRN for the DGCN graph convolution operation. The goal is to weight the DGCN and MLP embedding contributions differently — DGMP simply concatenates the three DGCN and one MLP embedding vectors without accounting for their differing contributions.

skills.description: Use when training a GNN on a directed gene regulatory network with per-gene multi-omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) to predict binary gene labels such as driver/non-driver, or when reproducing ablation studies of DGCN/MLP components.
skills.name: graph-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-training Use when training a GNN on a directed gene regulatory network with per-gene multi-omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) to predict binary gene labels such as driver/non-driver, or when reproducing ablation studies of DGCN/MLP components. The task requires patient-level predictions — DGMP averages omics across all samples, ignoring individual patient-specific characteristics The graph is undirected and topology-free gene features suffice — a plain MLP or non-graph classifier is more appropriate than DGCN Embedding vectors have genuinely different contributions requiring learned weighting — DGMP simply concatenates the three DGCN and one MLP vectors without weighting http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Train and evaluate graph neural network models for gene-level classification by combining a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) operating on a directed gene regulatory network with an MLP branch over multi-omics gene features, as implemented in DGMP for cancer driver gene identification on networks like DawnNet, KEGG, and RegNetwork. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Train and evaluate graph neural network models for gene-level classification by combining a directed graph convolutional network (DGCN) operating on a directed gene regulatory network with an MLP branch over multi-omics gene features, as implemented in DGMP for cancer driver gene identification on networks like DawnNet, KEGG, and RegNetwork.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires patient-level predictions — DGMP averages omics across all samples, ignoring individual patient-specific characteristics The graph is undirected and topology-free gene features suffice — a plain MLP or non-graph classifier is more appropriate than DGCN Embedding vectors have genuinely different contributions requiring learned weighting — DGMP simply concatenates the three DGCN and one MLP vectors without weighting

skills.description: Use when you have paired scATAC-seq peak accessibility (N x C) and scRNA-seq expression (N x T) matrices, a candidate peak-gene pair list, and a cell-state DAG, and need to rank Granger causal links.
skills.name: graph-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-training Use when you have paired scATAC-seq peak accessibility (N x C) and scRNA-seq expression (N x T) matrices, a candidate peak-gene pair list, and a cell-state DAG, and need to rank Granger causal links. Data is static or lacks a dynamic biological process providing pseudotemporal context — GrID-Net relies on multiomic data from matching tissue undergoing a process such as differentiation to orient the DAG. Single-modality data or datasets where scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq are not assayed for the same cells (paired multiomic data is required). Datasets so large that the GNN training exceeds GPU memory capacity, per the paper's stated practical limitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Train lagged message-passing GNNs (reduced and full forecasting models) on a DAG of cell states to score Granger causal peak-gene links from paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data, as implemented in GrID-Net (gridnet.run_gridnet) in PyTorch on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Train lagged message-passing GNNs (reduced and full forecasting models) on a DAG of cell states to score Granger causal peak-gene links from paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data, as implemented in GrID-Net (gridnet.run_gridnet) in PyTorch on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is static or lacks a dynamic biological process providing pseudotemporal context — GrID-Net relies on multiomic data from matching tissue undergoing a process such as differentiation to orient the DAG. Single-modality data or datasets where scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq are not assayed for the same cells (paired multiomic data is required). Datasets so large that the GNN training exceeds GPU memory capacity, per the paper's stated practical limitation.

skills.search_text: graph-neural-network-training Use when constructing a lineage-specific GRN from scRNA-seq data (e.g., h5ad/adata with 1,000 HVGs) given a prior gene interaction network, and downstream driver-regulator analysis requires reliable inferred regulatory edges. No prior gene interaction network is available and the goal is to infer a GRN from scRNA-seq data alone Multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time The analysis requires extrinsic factors such as cell–cell communication, spatial location, or epigenetics, which CEFCON does not model http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains a graph attention neural network under a contrastive learning framework (CEFCON) to infer a cell-lineage-specific gene regulatory network from single-cell RNA-seq expression plus a prior gene interaction network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Trains a graph attention neural network under a contrastive learning framework (CEFCON) to infer a cell-lineage-specific gene regulatory network from single-cell RNA-seq expression plus a prior gene interaction network.

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell data (.h5ad, e.g. scRNA-seq or protein iterative immunofluorescence) plus a small set of dynamic seed features from Step 1 of DELVE, and you need to rank all measured features by their smoothness over the cell trajectory graph.
skills.name: graph-signal-smoothness-analysis
skills.search_text: graph-signal-smoothness-analysis Use when you have single-cell data (.h5ad, e.g. scRNA-seq or protein iterative immunofluorescence) plus a small set of dynamic seed features from Step 1 of DELVE, and you need to rank all measured features by their smoothness over the cell trajectory graph. You lack dynamic seed features from Step 1 of DELVE and would have to build the trajectory graph from the full noisy feature set, the failure mode DELVE's bottom-up approach is designed to avoid Your data have no meaningful cellular trajectory or gradual feature progression (e.g. static, well-separated cell types with no cell-type transitions) You have expensive/laborious manual cell-type annotations available and a supervised feature selection approach is appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Ranks features by Laplacian Score on an approximate cellular trajectory graph built from dynamic seed modules, so that globally smooth features are retained and rapidly oscillating, noisy features are excluded (Step 2 of DELVE, applied to the RPE 4i dataset of 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Ranks features by Laplacian Score on an approximate cellular trajectory graph built from dynamic seed modules, so that globally smooth features are retained and rapidly oscillating, noisy features are excluded (Step 2 of DELVE, applied to the RPE 4i dataset of 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack dynamic seed features from Step 1 of DELVE and would have to build the trajectory graph from the full noisy feature set, the failure mode DELVE's bottom-up approach is designed to avoid Your data have no meaningful cellular trajectory or gradual feature progression (e.g. static, well-separated cell types with no cell-type transitions) You have expensive/laborious manual cell-type annotations available and a supervised feature selection approach is appropriate

skills.name: graph-topology-estimation-from-clustering
skills.search_text: graph-topology-estimation-from-clustering Use when you have a set of cluster assignments for single cells plus a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. LMDS with 5 dimensions) and need a tree-shaped trajectory backbone connecting the clusters. The desired trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles You only have raw expression data with no clustering and no embedding; a clustering must exist before an MST can be estimated per clustering You need correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs a minimum spanning tree (MST) over cluster vertices — as done in Totem's GenerateMST — where each cluster from a k-medoids (CLARA) clustering becomes a vertex at its centroid and edge weights are Slingshot's covariance-based, Mahalanobis-like between-cluster distances. This topology backbone underlies Totem's cell-connectivity-guided trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Reconstructs a minimum spanning tree (MST) over cluster vertices — as done in Totem's GenerateMST — where each cluster from a k-medoids (CLARA) clustering becomes a vertex at its centroid and edge weights are Slingshot's covariance-based, Mahalanobis-like between-cluster distances. This topology backbone underlies Totem's cell-connectivity-guided trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The desired trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles You only have raw expression data with no clustering and no embedding; a clustering must exist before an MST can be estimated per clustering You need correct pseudotime for multi-root (converging) trajectories — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories

Only a single subnetwork is available — pairwise Jaccard requires at least two recovered networks to compare The comparison target is edge-level or topological similarity (path direction, perturbation routes) rather than node membership overlap Vertex identifiers are not harmonized across methods (e.g., mixed Entrez IDs and symbols) — gene ID conversion (e.g., org.Hs.eg.db) must precede the overlap computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0611 Quantifies overlap between subnetworks recovered by different active subnetwork detection methods by computing pairwise Jaccard similarity coefficients on their vertex (node) sets.
