skills.search_text: ground-truth-label-annotation Use when generating synthetic benchmark data (e.g. two-condition, two-batch scRNA-seq simulations) that require known injected signal — DS genes at specified proportions (5%/10%) and logFC ranges — to be written alongside the counts as label annotations. Input is real experimental data without known ground truth — labels must come from a controlled injection, not inferred calls The goal is unsupervised integration only (e.g. standard scMerge2 pseudo-replication) with no downstream DS/differential benchmark to validate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs and stores verifiable ground-truth labels for synthetic single-cell simulations — e.g. differential-state (DS) gene annotations with controlled logFC ranges — so downstream benchmark results can be validated against known truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Constructs and stores verifiable ground-truth labels for synthetic single-cell simulations — e.g. differential-state (DS) gene annotations with controlled logFC ranges — so downstream benchmark results can be validated against known truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data without known ground truth — labels must come from a controlled injection, not inferred calls The goal is unsupervised integration only (e.g. standard scMerge2 pseudo-replication) with no downstream DS/differential benchmark to validate

skills.description: Use when validating GRN inference or denoising methods against a simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known regulatory relationships, e.g., quantifying recall gains from CP tensor denoising of multilayer scGRNs.
skills.name: ground-truth-regulatory-relationship-recovery-evaluation
skills.search_text: ground-truth-regulatory-relationship-recovery-evaluation Use when validating GRN inference or denoising methods against a simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known regulatory relationships, e.g., quantifying recall gains from CP tensor denoising of multilayer scGRNs. Input is real scRNA-seq data with no known ground-truth regulatory relationships — recall cannot be computed and other validation (e.g., functional enrichment of ranked genes) is needed The goal is differential regulation testing between two conditions (manifoldAlignment/dRegulation), not assessing recovery of simulated edges The input is already a denoised network with no matched set of individual (pre-denoising) networks to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how faithfully inferred single-cell GRNs (scGRNs) recover known regulatory relationships from a simulated scRNA-seq ground truth, by computing recall of ground-truth edges before and after CP tensor-denoising of multilayer networks. It provides the validation metric (recall improvement, ~25%) used to justify tensor denoising in the scTenifoldNet workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Quantifies how faithfully inferred single-cell GRNs (scGRNs) recover known regulatory relationships from a simulated scRNA-seq ground truth, by computing recall of ground-truth edges before and after CP tensor-denoising of multilayer networks. It provides the validation metric (recall improvement, ~25%) used to justify tensor denoising in the scTenifoldNet workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-seq data with no known ground-truth regulatory relationships — recall cannot be computed and other validation (e.g., functional enrichment of ranked genes) is needed The goal is differential regulation testing between two conditions (manifoldAlignment/dRegulation), not assessing recovery of simulated edges The input is already a denoised network with no matched set of individual (pre-denoising) networks to compare against

skills.description: Use when benchmarking methods that require known ground truth (RNA velocity via velocity correlation/arrow cosine, trajectory inference, CSNI) on simulated single-cell data where the true trajectory is available by construction.
skills.name: ground-truth-trajectory-extraction
skills.search_text: ground-truth-trajectory-extraction Use when benchmarking methods that require known ground truth (RNA velocity via velocity correlation/arrow cosine, trajectory inference, CSNI) on simulated single-cell data where the true trajectory is available by construction. Working with real experimental single-cell data, where the ground-truth trajectory and velocity are not known and cannot be extracted by construction Benchmarking methods that do not use trajectory information (e.g. clustering or differential expression), for which simulators like Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Extracts per-cell ground-truth trajectories (cell states, progression/pseudotime, and ground-truth RNA velocity vectors) from dyngen single-cell simulations so that computational methods such as RNA velocity, trajectory inference, and trajectory alignment can be quantitatively benchmarked against completely known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Extracts per-cell ground-truth trajectories (cell states, progression/pseudotime, and ground-truth RNA velocity vectors) from dyngen single-cell simulations so that computational methods such as RNA velocity, trajectory inference, and trajectory alignment can be quantitatively benchmarked against completely known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with real experimental single-cell data, where the ground-truth trajectory and velocity are not known and cannot be extracted by construction Benchmarking methods that do not use trajectory information (e.g. clustering or differential expression), for which simulators like Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim may suffice

skills.description: Use when performing XDE (covariate-associated differential expression along pseudotime) on scRNA-seq data with a trajectory method like Monocle2 that lacks native XDE support and needs group-specific intercept/trend tests.
skills.name: group-by-pseudotime-interaction-modeling
skills.search_text: group-by-pseudotime-interaction-modeling Use when performing XDE (covariate-associated differential expression along pseudotime) on scRNA-seq data with a trajectory method like Monocle2 that lacks native XDE support and needs group-specific intercept/trend tests. When the trajectory already comes from a method Lamian modules 1 and 2 directly support — the discussion notes Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not natively interoperate with Monocle2/Monocle3/slingshot and tailoring is deferred to future work, so this adaptation is only needed for such methods When the goal is testing expression changes along pseudotime without a group covariate (plain TDE) — use the null-model-only pseudotime spline test instead of the interaction model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Adapts Monocle2-style generalized additive models to test covariate-associated differential expression along pseudotime (XDE) by fitting a null model g(E(Y)) ~ beta0 + f2(pseudotime) against a full model with a group factor, pseudotime spline, and their interaction, assessed via permutation-based likelihood ratio testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Adapts Monocle2-style generalized additive models to test covariate-associated differential expression along pseudotime (XDE) by fitting a null model g(E(Y)) ~ beta0 + f2(pseudotime) against a full model with a group factor, pseudotime spline, and their interaction, assessed via permutation-based likelihood ratio testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the trajectory already comes from a method Lamian modules 1 and 2 directly support — the discussion notes Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not natively interoperate with Monocle2/Monocle3/slingshot and tailoring is deferred to future work, so this adaptation is only needed for such methods When the goal is testing expression changes along pseudotime without a group covariate (plain TDE) — use the null-model-only pseudotime spline test instead of the interaction model

skills.description: Use when a normalized, non-log2 blood transcriptome matrix (e.g., GSE13015/EH5429 from ExperimentHub) with sample annotation must be compared between two sample groups to get per-module percent-increase/decrease values.
skills.name: group-comparison-differential-expression
skills.search_text: group-comparison-differential-expression Use when a normalized, non-log2 blood transcriptome matrix (e.g., GSE13015/EH5429 from ExperimentHub) with sample annotation must be compared between two sample groups to get per-module percent-increase/decrease values. The expression matrix is already Log2 transformed — the README states data should not be Log2 transformed because the functions transform it internally The goal is single-sample fingerprinting relative to a reference — use the Individualcomparison/Individual_df workflow instead of Groupcomparison The data are not human blood transcriptome profiles — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood and other tissues or species would require a separate framework http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Performs BloodGen3 group comparison analysis by statistically testing every module's constitutive genes between a Test_group and Ref_group, then expressing results at the module level as the percentage of genes increased or decreased. This is the core quantitative step of the fixed-module-repertoire workflow that feeds fingerprint grid visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24584-w
skills.summary: Performs BloodGen3 group comparison analysis by statistically testing every module's constitutive genes between a Test_group and Ref_group, then expressing results at the module level as the percentage of genes increased or decreased. This is the core quantitative step of the fixed-module-repertoire workflow that feeds fingerprint grid visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is already Log2 transformed — the README states data should not be Log2 transformed because the functions transform it internally The goal is single-sample fingerprinting relative to a reference — use the Individualcomparison/Individual_df workflow instead of Groupcomparison The data are not human blood transcriptome profiles — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood and other tissues or species would require a separate framework

skills.description: Use when DEGGs generate_subnetworks has produced per-subgroup significant edge lists (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and you must restrict each network to interactions specific to one group rather than links common to all groups.
skills.name: group-specific-interaction-filtering
skills.search_text: group-specific-interaction-filtering Use when DEGGs generate_subnetworks has produced per-subgroup significant edge lists (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and you must restrict each network to interactions specific to one group rather than links common to all groups. You need interactions significant in all subgroups (common links) rather than group-specific ones — this skill removes exactly those edges You are starting from raw count data rather than a fitted DEGGs subnetworks_object; run generate_subnetworks first Your goal is multi-omic differential networks; the maintained multiDEGGs package (get_diffNetworks) is the successor tool for that scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Post-processing step for DEGGs differential-network results that removes gene-gene interactions significant in every subgroup, leaving only candidate group-specific (differentially expressed) links in each subgroup-annotated network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad192
skills.summary: Post-processing step for DEGGs differential-network results that removes gene-gene interactions significant in every subgroup, leaving only candidate group-specific (differentially expressed) links in each subgroup-annotated network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need interactions significant in all subgroups (common links) rather than group-specific ones — this skill removes exactly those edges You are starting from raw count data rather than a fitted DEGGs subnetworks_object; run generate_subnetworks first Your goal is multi-omic differential networks; the maintained multiDEGGs package (get_diffNetworks) is the successor tool for that scope

skills.search_text: group-wise-median-comparison-across-tools Use when a supplementary table (e.g. Dataset EV2) lists a numeric parameter per study along with the tool that produced it, and the goal is to test whether the parameter differs between tool families. The numeric quantity is already aggregated per tool group (no per-study rows to group by tool annotation) The grouping variable is continuous rather than a categorical tool label, making median-by-group comparison inappropriate Graining-level or dataset-size columns contain unparseable/free-text values that cannot be type-cast without external curation http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistical skill for comparing a numeric parameter (here, metacell graining level) across groups defined by the construction tool used, using medians, ranges, and rank correlation against a covariate such as dataset size, as demonstrated on the article's supplementary Dataset EV2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Statistical skill for comparing a numeric parameter (here, metacell graining level) across groups defined by the construction tool used, using medians, ranges, and rank correlation against a covariate such as dataset size, as demonstrated on the article's supplementary Dataset EV2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The numeric quantity is already aggregated per tool group (no per-study rows to group by tool annotation) The grouping variable is continuous rather than a categorical tool label, making median-by-group comparison inappropriate Graining-level or dataset-size columns contain unparseable/free-text values that cannot be type-cast without external curation

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether a modification to MuDCoD's subject-smoothing term (e.g., replacing the global all-subject mean with group-specific means) improves community recovery, measured by ARI against known true labels on simulated networks.
skills.name: grouped-subject-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: grouped-subject-benchmark-comparison Use when you need to quantify whether a modification to MuDCoD's subject-smoothing term (e.g., replacing the global all-subject mean with group-specific means) improves community recovery, measured by ARI against known true labels on simulated networks. There are no known true community labels (e.g., real scRNA-seq networks without ground truth), since ARI against z_mus_dynamic_true is the sole evaluation signal Subjects have no predefined groupings — the standard MuDCoD β-penalty with global all-subject mean smoothing is already the appropriate model http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking a modified MuDCoD variant against the standard algorithm on simulated multi-subject dynamic networks by comparing adjusted Rand index (ARI) per subject and time point. This isolates the effect of replacing the global β-penalty (all-subject mean smoothing) with group-specific smoothing for case/control-style subject groupings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Benchmarking a modified MuDCoD variant against the standard algorithm on simulated multi-subject dynamic networks by comparing adjusted Rand index (ARI) per subject and time point. This isolates the effect of replacing the global β-penalty (all-subject mean smoothing) with group-specific smoothing for case/control-style subject groupings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There are no known true community labels (e.g., real scRNA-seq networks without ground truth), since ARI against z_mus_dynamic_true is the sole evaluation signal Subjects have no predefined groupings — the standard MuDCoD β-penalty with global all-subject mean smoothing is already the appropriate model

skills.search_text: gsa-rank-based-gene-set-analysis Use when bulk RNA-seq DE contrasts (e.g., 17-AAG-sensitive vs -resistant HMCLs, 17-AAG response, combination response) need to be converted into ranked gene lists and gene-set/upstream-regulator signals to interpret drug-response mechanisms. Input is single-cell RNA-seq or CyTOF data used for combination screening by target-gene enrichment — this skill operates on bulk RNA-seq differential-expression contrasts Input is already a ranked gene list or a gene-set enrichment result with no underlying count matrix or sample grouping available The goal is two-drug combination prediction via the greedy set-cover algorithm rather than post-hoc interpretation of a treatment contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Rank-based Gene Set Analysis (GSA) applied to bulk RNA-seq differential-expression results from 17-AAG / 17-AAG + Ixazomib-treated myeloma cell lines to rank gene sets and identify upstream regulators (e.g., CEBPB, ERBB2, CCND1, let-7) underlying drug-response signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41408-022-00636-2
skills.summary: Rank-based Gene Set Analysis (GSA) applied to bulk RNA-seq differential-expression results from 17-AAG / 17-AAG + Ixazomib-treated myeloma cell lines to rank gene sets and identify upstream regulators (e.g., CEBPB, ERBB2, CCND1, let-7) underlying drug-response signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq or CyTOF data used for combination screening by target-gene enrichment — this skill operates on bulk RNA-seq differential-expression contrasts Input is already a ranked gene list or a gene-set enrichment result with no underlying count matrix or sample grouping available The goal is two-drug combination prediction via the greedy set-cover algorithm rather than post-hoc interpretation of a treatment contrast

skills.search_text: gsea-enrichment-score-calculation Use when a gene expression matrix (samples x genes, Entrez IDs) must be converted into per-sample pathway activity vectors (functional spectra) as classification or visualization features. Input is already a feature/embedding table (e.g. deep features from get_DeepCC_features) rather than raw gene expression The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC's functional spectra pipeline is built for supervised classification, not clustering The gene set database lacks the major characteristic signaling pathways for the cancer subtype, since comprehensive prior knowledge is needed to avoid bias http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Transforms each tumor sample's high-throughput gene expression profile into a functional spectrum by computing GSEA enrichment scores over every gene set in a MSigDB version (e.g. 17,779 sets for MSigDB v6.0), producing the pathway-activity feature vector consumed by the DeepCC classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/embedding table (e.g. deep features from get_DeepCC_features) rather than raw gene expression The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC's functional spectra pipeline is built for supervised classification, not clustering The gene set database lacks the major characteristic signaling pathways for the cancer subtype, since comprehensive prior knowledge is needed to avoid bias

skills.description: Use when a cluster from joint mRNA/protein WNN clustering (e.g., Seurat FindClusters algorithm=3, resolution=2) needs identity confirmation: rank its transcript signature and test enrichment against a curated cell-type gene set (e.g., MAIT-cell signature).
skills.name: gsea-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gsea-gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when a cluster from joint mRNA/protein WNN clustering (e.g., Seurat FindClusters algorithm=3, resolution=2) needs identity confirmation: rank its transcript signature and test enrichment against a curated cell-type gene set (e.g., MAIT-cell signature). When deciding between protein normalization methods itself — use the empty-droplet 98th-percentile correlation diagnostic (CLR r≈0.8 vs dsb r≈0.13) rather than GSEA When no curated gene set signature exists for the candidate cell identity, or the cluster is defined only by protein (ADT) signal with no transcript ranking available When the input is raw, unnormalized ADT counts — GSEA operates on transcript-level enrichment and cannot resolve ambient antibody noise http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) applied to transcripts of a transcriptionally defined cluster to confirm its cell identity via a curated signature. In the TEA-seq case study, GSEA of cluster 14 transcripts against a MAIT-cell signature provides orthogonal validation that dsb normalization unmasks the MAIT population misread as conventional T cells under CLR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) applied to transcripts of a transcriptionally defined cluster to confirm its cell identity via a curated signature. In the TEA-seq case study, GSEA of cluster 14 transcripts against a MAIT-cell signature provides orthogonal validation that dsb normalization unmasks the MAIT population misread as conventional T cells under CLR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When deciding between protein normalization methods itself — use the empty-droplet 98th-percentile correlation diagnostic (CLR r≈0.8 vs dsb r≈0.13) rather than GSEA When no curated gene set signature exists for the candidate cell identity, or the cluster is defined only by protein (ADT) signal with no transcript ranking available When the input is raw, unnormalized ADT counts — GSEA operates on transcript-level enrichment and cannot resolve ambient antibody noise

skills.description: Use when comparing pseudo-time/trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, gene-set-based metric: run GSEA with a cell-cycle gene set on each method's cell ordering and rank methods by NES.
skills.name: gsea-normalized-enrichment-score-benchmarking
skills.search_text: gsea-normalized-enrichment-score-benchmarking Use when comparing pseudo-time/trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, gene-set-based metric: run GSEA with a cell-cycle gene set on each method's cell ordering and rank methods by NES. skills.summary: Benchmark cell-cycle pseudo-time inference methods (Cyclum, reCAT, PC1, PC2) by running GSEA against the GO cell-cycle gene set on the inferred orderings and comparing normalized enrichment scores (NES), mirroring Fig. 4a / Supplementary Table 1 of the Cyclum paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The inferred cell orderings are not continuous pseudo-time values suitable for GSEA continuous phenotypes (e.g., only discrete phase labels) — use Cyclum's label refinement instead The gene set of interest is unrelated to periodic/circular processes; NES benchmarking against the cell-cycle set will not meaningfully distinguish trajectory methods Expression matrices have not been preprocessed with the recommended log2(x+1), centering (mean=1) and scaling (variance=1), which the article states works well for Cyclum-style inference

skills.search_text: gsea-prerank-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a ranked gene list from a differential expression comparison and need per-pathway enrichment FDR values, especially to benchmark model-based module activity tests (e.g., VEGA Bayes Factors) against a standard enrichment method. skills.summary: Run gseapy prerank GSEA on a gene-level differential expression ranking (e.g., stimulated vs control innate immune cells from the Kang et al. PBMC dataset, GEO GSE96583) to obtain per-pathway -log10(FDR) enrichment values. Used in the VEGA paper as the standard-enrichment baseline against which VEGA's Bayesian gene module variable (GMV) Bayes Factor test is compared.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking sample-wise pathway quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) against rROMA module activity on a normalized RNA-seq matrix to test which method recovers an expected treatment- or disease-driven pathway shift.

skills.search_text: gsva-family-sample-level-geneset-scoring Use when benchmarking sample-wise pathway quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) against rROMA module activity on a normalized RNA-seq matrix to test which method recovers an expected treatment- or disease-driven pathway shift. skills.summary: Compute per-sample pathway activity scores for the same 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets using the four sample-wise methods GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA and z-score, so their results can be benchmarked against rROMA's PC1-based module activity on identical normalized expression matrices (edgeR cpm) from the GSE176121 cystic fibrosis dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma/GSVA comparisons assume normalized data such as edgeR cpm or DESeq2 vst) The goal is the rROMA module-activity computation itself rather than benchmarking the GSVA-family sample-wise scoring methods against it The analysis requires a pathway database other than the 50 Hallmark gene sets used in the rROMA benchmark

skills.description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, e.g. TCGA-LUAD) and a curated gene set (e.g. a 14-gene hypoxia or 22-gene glycolysis signature) and need per-sample pathway/hallmark scores for downstream grouping, survival or differential analysis.
skills.name: gsva-geneset-scoring
skills.search_text: gsva-geneset-scoring Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, e.g. TCGA-LUAD) and a curated gene set (e.g. a 14-gene hypoxia or 22-gene glycolysis signature) and need per-sample pathway/hallmark scores for downstream grouping, survival or differential analysis. The input is already a TPM matrix with gene Symbol row names — the Normalization&GSVA module expects a raw counts matrix with Ensembl IDs and would mis-handle pre-normalized symbol-level input. The goal is single-gene differential expression (DEG calling) — that should go through ARMT's differential analysis with edgeR on the counts matrix, not GSVA scoring. The gene set is undefined or you have no .csv/.gmt gene set and no interest in any of the 9 internal MSigDb gene sets — GSVA scoring cannot proceed without a gene set definition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scores per sample for custom or MSigDb gene sets on TCGA-style RNA-seq data, using ARMT's Normalization&GSVA module to transform a raw counts matrix into a log2(TPM + 1) matrix before scoring. Scores then feed survival, Cox, differential and correlation analyses in cancer research. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Compute gene set variation analysis (GSVA) scores per sample for custom or MSigDb gene sets on TCGA-style RNA-seq data, using ARMT's Normalization&GSVA module to transform a raw counts matrix into a log2(TPM + 1) matrix before scoring. Scores then feed survival, Cox, differential and correlation analyses in cancer research.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a TPM matrix with gene Symbol row names — the Normalization&GSVA module expects a raw counts matrix with Ensembl IDs and would mis-handle pre-normalized symbol-level input. skills.description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic cohort (e.g., GSE39582 or TCGA COAD-READ expression matrices) must be scored for a curated pathway list (e.g., high-weight pathways from scPAFA/MOFA modules) to build or validate a disease-status classifier.
skills.name: gsva-pathway-score-computation
skills.search_text: gsva-pathway-score-computation Use when a bulk transcriptomic cohort (e.g., GSE39582 or TCGA COAD-READ expression matrices) must be scored for a curated pathway list (e.g., high-weight pathways from scPAFA/MOFA modules) to build or validate a disease-status classifier. The input is already a single-cell dataset — use scPAFA's 'fast_Ucell' or 'fast_score_genes' for cell-level PAS computation instead of GSVA on pseudobulk data No pathway dictionary or high-weight pathway selection is available — GSVA scores on an arbitrary/unsupervised pathway set will not validate the multicellular modules Fewer than 15 samples (not cells) are available — the MOFA-based module identification that supplies the high-weight pathways requires at least 15 samples Computes GSVA (Gene Set Variation Analysis) pathway scores on bulk RNA expression matrices — here for the 30 highest-MOFA-weight pathways from scPAFA's MMR-related multicellular pathway modules — so they can serve as features for disease-status classifiers such as the L1-regularized SVC predicting MMR/MSI status in CRC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Computes GSVA (Gene Set Variation Analysis) pathway scores on bulk RNA expression matrices — here for the 30 highest-MOFA-weight pathways from scPAFA's MMR-related multicellular pathway modules — so they can serve as features for disease-status classifiers such as the L1-regularized SVC predicting MMR/MSI status in CRC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a single-cell dataset — use scPAFA's 'fast_Ucell' or 'fast_score_genes' for cell-level PAS computation instead of GSVA on pseudobulk data No pathway dictionary or high-weight pathway selection is available — GSVA scores on an arbitrary/unsupervised pathway set will not validate the multicellular modules Fewer than 15 samples (not cells) are available — the MOFA-based module identification that supplies the high-weight pathways requires at least 15 samples

skills.description: Use when a continuous process signature (e.g., hypoxia or glycolysis gene set) must be turned into patient sample groups — e.g., to compare mutation burdens or survival between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD tumors.
skills.name: gsva-score-based-sample-stratification
skills.search_text: gsva-score-based-sample-stratification Use when a continuous process signature (e.g., hypoxia or glycolysis gene set) must be turned into patient sample groups — e.g., to compare mutation burdens or survival between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD tumors. The factor of interest is already a discrete clinical variable (e.g., stage, sex) — no GSVA stratification is needed; group directly. You need gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level sample scoring — use ARMT's edgeR DEG workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Stratifies transcriptome samples into high/low groups of a biological process (e.g., hypoxia) by ranking sample-level GSVA scores computed from a curated gene-set signature in ARMT, enabling downstream differential mutation, survival, and Cox analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Stratifies transcriptome samples into high/low groups of a biological process (e.g., hypoxia) by ranking sample-level GSVA scores computed from a curated gene-set signature in ARMT, enabling downstream differential mutation, survival, and Cox analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The factor of interest is already a discrete clinical variable (e.g., stage, sex) — no GSVA stratification is needed; group directly. You need gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level sample scoring — use ARMT's edgeR DEG workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq gene-set (pathway) activity must be compared between sample groups — e.g. glycolysis GSVA score between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD samples — and the test variable is continuous decimal scores.
skills.name: gsva-score-differential-analysis-limma
skills.search_text: gsva-score-differential-analysis-limma Use when RNA-seq gene-set (pathway) activity must be compared between sample groups — e.g. glycolysis GSVA score between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD samples — and the test variable is continuous decimal scores. Testing differential expression on the raw counts matrix — ARMT uses edgeR for DEGs, not limma-on-GSVA-scores The input is already a per-sample gene-set score table produced elsewhere and no grouping/cut-off step is needed — go straight to statistical testing The question is prognostic (survival/Cox) rather than group comparison — use ARMT's survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression module instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differentially tests gene-set activity between sample groups by first converting gene sets (e.g. 22-gene glycolysis, 14-gene hypoxia signatures) to per-sample GSVA scores, then applying limma on those scores in ARMT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Differentially tests gene-set activity between sample groups by first converting gene sets (e.g. 22-gene glycolysis, 14-gene hypoxia signatures) to per-sample GSVA scores, then applying limma on those scores in ARMT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Testing differential expression on the raw counts matrix — ARMT uses edgeR for DEGs, not limma-on-GSVA-scores The input is already a per-sample gene-set score table produced elsewhere and no grouping/cut-off step is needed — go straight to statistical testing The question is prognostic (survival/Cox) rather than group comparison — use ARMT's survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression module instead

skills.name: gtex-eqtl-finemapped-pair-intersection
skills.search_text: gtex-eqtl-finemapped-pair-intersection Use when validating enhancer-gene interaction predictions against orthogonal genetic evidence: intersect method-ranked enhancer-gene lists with fine-mapped GTEx eQTL credible sets to compute and compare eQTL-pair recall per method and cell type. When the goal is TF-affinity summarisation or gene expression prediction from TF affinities (STARE's GAZE workflow), not enhancer-gene assignment benchmarking When no fine-mapped eQTL credible sets (CAVIAR, CaVEMaN, DAP-G) are available for the tissue or cell types of interest, since recall cannot be computed When comparing methods without a matched scoring scale or ranking depth (e.g. fewer than the top-300,000 interactions retained), which invalidates paired recall comparison Benchmarks enhancer-gene prediction methods (regular ABC, generalized gABC, Cicero co-accessibility) by intersecting their top-scored interactions with high-confidence GTEx eQTL-gene pairs fine-mapped with CAVIAR, CaVEMaN, and DAP-G, and testing recall differences with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Benchmarks enhancer-gene prediction methods (regular ABC, generalized gABC, Cicero co-accessibility) by intersecting their top-scored interactions with high-confidence GTEx eQTL-gene pairs fine-mapped with CAVIAR, CaVEMaN, and DAP-G, and testing recall differences with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is TF-affinity summarisation or gene expression prediction from TF affinities (STARE's GAZE workflow), not enhancer-gene assignment benchmarking When no fine-mapped eQTL credible sets (CAVIAR, CaVEMaN, DAP-G) are available for the tissue or cell types of interest, since recall cannot be computed When comparing methods without a matched scoring scale or ranking depth (e.g. fewer than the top-300,000 interactions retained), which invalidates paired recall comparison

skills.description: Use when GReX imputation weights must be trained from whole-blood eQTL reference data (eQTLGen summary statistics or GTEx individual-level genotypes/expression) and compared by number of valid models (test R2 > 0.01).
skills.name: gtex-expression-reference-modeling
skills.search_text: gtex-expression-reference-modeling Use when GReX imputation weights must be trained from whole-blood eQTL reference data (eQTLGen summary statistics or GTEx individual-level genotypes/expression) and compared by number of valid models (test R2 > 0.01). The available eQTL summary reference is not from individuals of European descent — the article notes available summary-level references are mainly European, limiting cross-population transferability Trans-eQTL effects are needed — OTTERS only considers cis-eQTL effects Only a small individual-level reference is available and summary-level data exist for the tissue — the larger summary-level eQTLGen reference (n=31,684 vs GTEx V6 n=338) is preferred for power http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train GReX imputation (eQTL weight) models for TWAS Stage I from GTEx/eQTLGen reference data — using summary-level eQTLGen data (n=31,684) via P+T, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS, and individual-level GTEx V6 data via FUSION — then benchmark model validity on 315 held-out GTEx V8 whole-blood samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Train GReX imputation (eQTL weight) models for TWAS Stage I from GTEx/eQTLGen reference data — using summary-level eQTLGen data (n=31,684) via P+T, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS, and individual-level GTEx V6 data via FUSION — then benchmark model validity on 315 held-out GTEx V8 whole-blood samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The available eQTL summary reference is not from individuals of European descent — the article notes available summary-level references are mainly European, limiting cross-population transferability Trans-eQTL effects are needed — OTTERS only considers cis-eQTL effects Only a small individual-level reference is available and summary-level data exist for the tissue — the larger summary-level eQTLGen reference (n=31,684 vs GTEx V6 n=338) is preferred for power

skills.description: Use when preparing multi-tissue GTEx transcript expression (TPM) and genotype tables as sqtlseeker2-nf inputs, i.e., when the goal is cis-sQTL mapping and raw tissue, gene, transcript and variant sets must be filtered first.
skills.name: gtex-multitissue-sqtl-preprocessing
skills.search_text: gtex-multitissue-sqtl-preprocessing Use when preparing multi-tissue GTEx transcript expression (TPM) and genotype tables as sqtlseeker2-nf inputs, i.e., when the goal is cis-sQTL mapping and raw tissue, gene, transcript and variant sets must be filtered first. The input is already a filtered sQTLseekeR2-ready expression/genotype set — re-applying the tissue, gene and variant cutoffs would drop further data unnecessarily The goal is univariate eQTL mapping or LeafCutter-based intron excision-ratio analysis rather than multivariate transcript-proportion sQTL mapping, which uses different preprocessing Only a single tissue is analyzed and it has fewer than 70 samples, so the tissue sample-size criterion would remove everything http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocessing skill for GTEx-style multi-tissue sQTL mapping with sQTLseekeR2/sqtlseeker2-nf: retain tissues with >=70 samples, filter genes/transcripts on TPM-based criteria, and restrict variants to biallelic SNPs/indels with MAF >=0.01 and >=10 samples per genotype group. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Preprocessing skill for GTEx-style multi-tissue sQTL mapping with sQTLseekeR2/sqtlseeker2-nf: retain tissues with >=70 samples, filter genes/transcripts on TPM-based criteria, and restrict variants to biallelic SNPs/indels with MAF >=0.01 and >=10 samples per genotype group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered sQTLseekeR2-ready expression/genotype set — re-applying the tissue, gene and variant cutoffs would drop further data unnecessarily The goal is univariate eQTL mapping or LeafCutter-based intron excision-ratio analysis rather than multivariate transcript-proportion sQTL mapping, which uses different preprocessing Only a single tissue is analyzed and it has fewer than 70 samples, so the tissue sample-size criterion would remove everything

skills.summary: Uses GTEx TPM expression values merged with MRSD scores (from *.results.mrsd.txt files) to test whether relative gene expression is an adequate proxy for RNA-seq suitability, via correlation, stratification, and distribution-overlap analyses across four human biosamples.

skills.description: Use when building a per-tissue sQTL catalog from GTEx V7 transcript expression and genotypes, or when reproducing the Garrido-Martín et al. counts of 210,485 cis sQTLs across 6,963 sGenes at 0.05 FDR.
skills.name: gtex-tissue-transcript-expression-preprocessing
skills.search_text: gtex-tissue-transcript-expression-preprocessing Use when building a per-tissue sQTL catalog from GTEx V7 transcript expression and genotypes, or when reproducing the Garrido-Martín et al. counts of 210,485 cis sQTLs across 6,963 sGenes at 0.05 FDR. The analysis goal is univariate gene-expression QTL (eQTL) mapping rather than multivariate splicing phenotype testing — sQTLseekeR2 models vectors of transcript isoform relative abundances. The splicing phenotype is already reduced to LeafCutter intron excision ratios; this skill works on transcript-level expression tables with trId/geneId. Only effect annotation of already-called variants is needed (e.g. LoF prediction via LOFTEE/VEP) — no sQTL association testing is involved. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prepare GTEx V7 tissue-level inputs (coordinate-sorted genotypes, transcript expression with trId/geneId, sample metadata with covariates, gene locations) and run the sqtlseeker2-nf Nextflow pipeline to call cis sQTLs at 0.05 FDR with sQTLseekeR2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Prepare GTEx V7 tissue-level inputs (coordinate-sorted genotypes, transcript expression with trId/geneId, sample metadata with covariates, gene locations) and run the sqtlseeker2-nf Nextflow pipeline to call cis sQTLs at 0.05 FDR with sQTLseekeR2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is univariate gene-expression QTL (eQTL) mapping rather than multivariate splicing phenotype testing — sQTLseekeR2 models vectors of transcript isoform relative abundances. The splicing phenotype is already reduced to LeafCutter intron excision ratios; this skill works on transcript-level expression tables with trId/geneId. Only effect annotation of already-called variants is needed (e.g. LoF prediction via LOFTEE/VEP) — no sQTL association testing is involved.

skills.search_text: gtf-annotation-file-authoring Use when long-read alignments must be converted into novel transcript records in a valid GTF enhanced annotation, with TSS/polyA end-support filtering against external interval BEDs. Input reads are not full-length or not spliced — truncation-exclusion rules would discard most of the data instead of yielding novel isoforms The goal is differential isoform/exon testing rather than annotation extension — use scisorseqr DiffSplicingAnalysis or ExonQuant instead No external CAGE/polyA interval references are available for the genome version, so 5'/3' end assignments cannot be validated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Authoring an enhanced GTF annotation file of novel long-read isoforms by collapsing full-length, spliced ScISOr-Seq reads whose 5' and 3' ends are confirmed against FANTOM CAGE peaks and polyASite 2.0 sites; in this study it yielded exactly 76 high-confidence novel isoform records extending GENCODE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5

skills.description: Use when assembling or correcting isoforms from long-read RNA-seq alignments (e.g. GMAP-aligned PacBio BAM) where a trusted GTF annotation with exon coordinates is available and detection accuracy against known isoforms must be benchmarked.
skills.name: gtf-annotation-guided-splice-correction
skills.search_text: gtf-annotation-guided-splice-correction Use when assembling or correcting isoforms from long-read RNA-seq alignments (e.g. GMAP-aligned PacBio BAM) where a trusted GTF annotation with exon coordinates is available and detection accuracy against known isoforms must be benchmarked. No reference GTF with exon-coordinate evidence exists for the locus or organism being analyzed — de novo isoform discovery methods without annotation guidance are required instead. Input is short-read RNA-seq data — the benchmark and the '-L' long-read mode of StringTie2 are defined for long-read (PacBio/nanopore) alignments. The goal is interactive per-gene fine-tuning of splice sites and read thresholds (e.g. the 2% CEC cutoff) — VIsoQLR's interactive editor, not annotation-guided correction by FLAIR/StringTie2, is the appropriate tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Guides long-read isoform assembly and splice-site correction with a known GTF annotation (e.g. the SIRV GTF with 68 reference isoforms) so that exon coordinates from the annotation, rather than de novo inference alone, define detected transcripts. The VIsoQLR paper benchmarks this approach by running FLAIR (default parameters plus GTF) and StringTie2 ('-L -f 0') on the same GMAP-aligned PacBio BAM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Guides long-read isoform assembly and splice-site correction with a known GTF annotation (e.g. the SIRV GTF with 68 reference isoforms) so that exon coordinates from the annotation, rather than de novo inference alone, define detected transcripts. The VIsoQLR paper benchmarks this approach by running FLAIR (default parameters plus GTF) and StringTie2 ('-L -f 0') on the same GMAP-aligned PacBio BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference GTF with exon-coordinate evidence exists for the locus or organism being analyzed — de novo isoform discovery methods without annotation guidance are required instead. Input is short-read RNA-seq data — the benchmark and the '-L' long-read mode of StringTie2 are defined for long-read (PacBio/nanopore) alignments. The goal is interactive per-gene fine-tuning of splice sites and read thresholds (e.g. the 2% CEC cutoff) — VIsoQLR's interactive editor, not annotation-guided correction by FLAIR/StringTie2, is the appropriate tool.

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is sQTL association mapping itself rather than annotation-based enrichment analysis — run the sqtlseeker2-nf pipeline instead When no intron-level annotation or splicing kinetics data are available, since co- vs post-transcriptional classification cannot be built For gene-expression (eQTL) enrichment, which would require gene expression QTL regions rather than intron classes

skills.search_text: gtf-transcript-annotation-formatting Use when transcript paths recovered from a labeled splice graph (edges labeled 1, 2+, 2-) must be written out as an annotation file, and output candidates need to be filtered by coverage and length thresholds before downstream use. skills.description: Use when a sample-specific GTF/GFF transcriptome (e.g., StringTie output) needs refined 3' ends / expressed polyadenylation sites before quantitation or differential expression analysis.
skills.name: gtf-transcriptome-annotation
skills.search_text: gtf-transcriptome-annotation Use when a sample-specific GTF/GFF transcriptome (e.g., StringTie output) needs refined 3' ends / expressed polyadenylation sites before quantitation or differential expression analysis. The goal is to detect coding (upstream-exon) alternative polyadenylation — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream APA is out of scope The input transcriptome has many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and no post-hoc filtering is planned — redundant false-positive aptardi transcripts will be enumerated The task requires resolving which overlapping transcript isoform truly owns a polyA site — aptardi does not distinguish transcripts overlapping the same genomic region http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Construct a sample-specific transcriptome annotation by running aptardi, which evaluates the 3' terminal exons of input GTF/GFF transcripts with RNA-Seq coverage and DNA sequence via a machine-learning model and outputs a new GTF with aptardi transcripts added on top of the unmodified input transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Construct a sample-specific transcriptome annotation by running aptardi, which evaluates the 3' terminal exons of input GTF/GFF transcripts with RNA-Seq coverage and DNA sequence via a machine-learning model and outputs a new GTF with aptardi transcripts added on top of the unmodified input transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect coding (upstream-exon) alternative polyadenylation — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream APA is out of scope The input transcriptome has many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and no post-hoc filtering is planned — redundant false-positive aptardi transcripts will be enumerated The task requires resolving which overlapping transcript isoform truly owns a polyA site — aptardi does not distinguish transcripts overlapping the same genomic region

skills.description: Use when quantifying imputation accuracy of scRNA-seq methods: comparing MSE/gtMSE against a ground-truth matrix, or evaluating real datasets (e.g. PBMC_G5561, PBMC_G9987) where ground truth is set equal to the input.
skills.name: gtmse-error-metric-computation
skills.search_text: gtmse-error-metric-computation Use when quantifying imputation accuracy of scRNA-seq methods: comparing MSE/gtMSE against a ground-truth matrix, or evaluating real datasets (e.g. PBMC_G5561, PBMC_G9987) where ground truth is set equal to the input. skills.search_text: gumbel-softmax-differentiable-marker-selection Use when selecting a minimal, informative set of k gene markers from single-cell RNA-seq or CITE-seq data (.h5ad AnnData) such that markers are differentiably learned end-to-end and support both cell-type classification and whole-transcriptome reconstruction. skills.search_text: hamming-distance-cell-to-attractor-mapping Use when scBONITA-inferred Boolean rules and binarized single-cell expression states exist and you must map sequenced cells to characteristic signaling states (attractors) of a pathway. You only have raw unbinarized scRNA-seq counts and have not yet run scBONITA rule inference on the pathway topology The pathway's Boolean network does not reach fixed-point attractors (e.g., only cyclic/oscillatory dynamics), so Hamming-distance assignment to steady states is ill-defined Conventional differential expression or over-representation analysis suffices for the question — the article notes such ORA methods were inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes, which is precisely when attractor analysis is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Attractor analysis step of scBONITA that simulates the inferred Boolean network of a signaling pathway (e.g., from a GRAPHML topology) to steady states and assigns each sequenced cell to the attractor closest in Hamming distance, enabling pathway-based characterization of cellular states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Attractor analysis step of scBONITA that simulates the inferred Boolean network of a signaling pathway (e.g., from a GRAPHML topology) to steady states and assigns each sequenced cell to the attractor closest in Hamming distance, enabling pathway-based characterization of cellular states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw unbinarized scRNA-seq counts and have not yet run scBONITA rule inference on the pathway topology The pathway's Boolean network does not reach fixed-point attractors (e.g., only cyclic/oscillatory dynamics), so Hamming-distance assignment to steady states is ill-defined Conventional differential expression or over-representation analysis suffices for the question — the article notes such ORA methods were inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes, which is precisely when attractor analysis is preferred

skills.description: Use when converting a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Xin GSE81608, 2000 highly variable genes, entries in [0,1]) into a binary gene-gene similarity graph to derive qualitative cell landmarks.
skills.name: hamming-similarity-gene-graph-construction
skills.search_text: hamming-similarity-gene-graph-construction Use when converting a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Xin GSE81608, 2000 highly variable genes, entries in [0,1]) into a binary gene-gene similarity graph to derive qualitative cell landmarks. The input is already a qualitative cell-landmark matrix Q1 or a feature table with no raw gene expression values to binarize The analysis goal is the quantitative low-dimensional representation (LC2), which clusters genes with quasi-trend-preserved expression patterns instead of binary patterns Very few genes remain after preprocessing, so the top 1999 gene pairs (one thousandth of all gene pairs) cannot be meaningfully retained as graph edges http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds a binary gene similarity graph inside scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1) by computing normalized Hamming similarity S = 1 − h/n between genes binarized from dropout-prone scRNA-seq data, then retaining the top 1999 gene pairs as edges so genes sharing analogous zero/non-zero expression patterns can be amalgamated into landmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Builds a binary gene similarity graph inside scQA's qualitative landmark constructor (LC1) by computing normalized Hamming similarity S = 1 − h/n between genes binarized from dropout-prone scRNA-seq data, then retaining the top 1999 gene pairs as edges so genes sharing analogous zero/non-zero expression patterns can be amalgamated into landmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a qualitative cell-landmark matrix Q1 or a feature table with no raw gene expression values to binarize The analysis goal is the quantitative low-dimensional representation (LC2), which clusters genes with quasi-trend-preserved expression patterns instead of binary patterns Very few genes remain after preprocessing, so the top 1999 gene pairs (one thousandth of all gene pairs) cannot be meaningfully retained as graph edges

skills.description: Use when building allele-specific CNA calls from scRNA-seq allelic counts (AD/DP matrices) and single-SNP BAF signals are too sparse/noisy, requiring aggregation from SNPs to genes, gene bins, and chromosome arms before HMM smoothing.
skills.name: haplotype-phasing-em-gene-binning
skills.search_text: haplotype-phasing-em-gene-binning Use when building allele-specific CNA calls from scRNA-seq allelic counts (AD/DP matrices) and single-SNP BAF signals are too sparse/noisy, requiring aggregation from SNPs to genes, gene bins, and chromosome arms before HMM smoothing. The analysis goal is read-depth-based CNA calling without allelic information — use the RDR module, since InferCNV/CopyKAT-style RDR approaches cannot detect copy-neutral LOH but this skill targets B-allele imbalance. Only bulk (not single-cell) data or single-cell DNA-seq is available — this skill is built on scRNA-seq allelic UMI counts from platforms such as 10x Genomics and SMART-seq via xcltk preprocessing. Variants are unphased individual SNPs being analyzed independently — the point of this skill is to avoid the high-noise independent-SNP approach used by HoneyBADGER/CaSpER. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 XClone's three-level haplotyping strategy for the BAF module: population-based phasing of individual SNPs to genes, EM-based aggregation of consecutive genes (100 by default) into gene bins, and dynamic-programming aggregation of gene bins to whole chromosome arms, enabling allele-imbalance CNA calling from sparse scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: XClone's three-level haplotyping strategy for the BAF module: population-based phasing of individual SNPs to genes, EM-based aggregation of consecutive genes (100 by default) into gene bins, and dynamic-programming aggregation of gene bins to whole chromosome arms, enabling allele-imbalance CNA calling from sparse scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is read-depth-based CNA calling without allelic information — use the RDR module, since InferCNV/CopyKAT-style RDR approaches cannot detect copy-neutral LOH but this skill targets B-allele imbalance. Only bulk (not single-cell) data or single-cell DNA-seq is available — this skill is built on scRNA-seq allelic UMI counts from platforms such as 10x Genomics and SMART-seq via xcltk preprocessing. Variants are unphased individual SNPs being analyzed independently — the point of this skill is to avoid the high-noise independent-SNP approach used by HoneyBADGER/CaSpER.

skills.search_text: harmonizome-association-enrichment-analysis Use when a list of newly predicted candidate RBPs (e.g., CRIT NMF cluster candidates) must be functionally connected to a gold-standard regulator set via physical interaction, co-expression, or shared transcription factor modulation evidence. Input is not a candidate regulator list but raw omics data (TCGA CNV/mutation/expression, MiOncoCirc, or RNAct files) — run the CRIT feature-collection and NMF.R steps first The goal is direct circRNA-RBP binding validation — use CLIP database analysis or the RNAct/C value feature instead of indirect Harmonizome associations The background distribution cannot be defined (no gene or RBP background lists available) — permutation-based p-values require a defined random-sampling background http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates newly predicted circRNA regulator candidates by testing their biological association with gold-standard regulators using three Harmonizome datasets (Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions, MSigDB Cancer Gene Co-expression Modules, TRANSFAC Curated Transcription Factor Targets) against 10,000 random-sampling permutation controls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Validates newly predicted circRNA regulator candidates by testing their biological association with gold-standard regulators using three Harmonizome datasets (Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions, MSigDB Cancer Gene Co-expression Modules, TRANSFAC Curated Transcription Factor Targets) against 10,000 random-sampling permutation controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a candidate regulator list but raw omics data (TCGA CNV/mutation/expression, MiOncoCirc, or RNAct files) — run the CRIT feature-collection and NMF.R steps first The goal is direct circRNA-RBP binding validation — use CLIP database analysis or the RNAct/C value feature instead of indirect Harmonizome associations The background distribution cannot be defined (no gene or RBP background lists available) — permutation-based p-values require a defined random-sampling background

skills.search_text: harmony-batch-corrected-embedding-evaluation Use when comparing how well alternative single-cell embeddings (TCR-only, RNA-only, Harmony-corrected RNA, mvTCR joint) preserve pMHC antigen specificity, quantified by NMI of Leiden clusters and per-cluster antigen purity. The dataset lacks paired TCR sequences and pMHC specificity annotations, so NMI against specificity labels cannot be computed The goal is general cell-type clustering or batch correction of RNA alone rather than evaluating antigen-specificity preservation across embedding variants Working with B-cell or unpaired data — the article notes mvTCR was applied mainly to paired data with gene expression plus α- and β-CDR3, and no large-scale B-cell specificity benchmark exists http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates whether unimodal (TCR-only, RNA-only), batch-corrected (Harmony-corrected RNA), and multimodal (mvTCR) cell embeddings cluster T cells by pMHC antigen specificity, using Leiden clustering with resolution swept to maximize NMI against specificity labels on the 10x dataset (>60k cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Evaluates whether unimodal (TCR-only, RNA-only), batch-corrected (Harmony-corrected RNA), and multimodal (mvTCR) cell embeddings cluster T cells by pMHC antigen specificity, using Leiden clustering with resolution swept to maximize NMI against specificity labels on the 10x dataset (>60k cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks paired TCR sequences and pMHC specificity annotations, so NMI against specificity labels cannot be computed The goal is general cell-type clustering or batch correction of RNA alone rather than evaluating antigen-specificity preservation across embedding variants Working with B-cell or unpaired data — the article notes mvTCR was applied mainly to paired data with gene expression plus α- and β-CDR3, and no large-scale B-cell specificity benchmark exists

Data are already paired multiome (e.g. 10x multiome) where modalities share cells natively and no cross-modality batch correction is needed A single-modality dataset without batch covariates, where Harmony correction has no group.by.vars to correct http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Applies Harmony batch correction to a co-embedded multi-modal single-cell object (e.g. scMEGA's CCA co-embedding of snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq) so that cells from different donors, regions, and technologies mix in low-dimensional space before clustering, cell pairing, and trajectory/GRN inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already paired multiome (e.g. 10x multiome) where modalities share cells natively and no cross-modality batch correction is needed A single-modality dataset without batch covariates, where Harmony correction has no group.by.vars to correct

skills.search_text: harmony-batch-integration Use when a held-out query dataset from a different technology or batch must be projected into a stable reference embedding built from the other datasets, and the mapping quality must be quantified against a de novo Harmony integration. The goal is de novo discovery of novel cell types in the query — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone, and its mapping metrics are uninformative when a novel population resembles an existing reference population The query dataset lacks comprehensive cell-type coverage in the reference (Condition I), since label transfer and mapping fidelity degrade when reference coverage is incomplete The input is already an integrated embedding and no batch/technology confounder needs to be removed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Build a Harmony-integrated embedding across batches or technologies (here, three 10x PBMC datasets from 3'v1, 3'v2, and 5' chemistry), then compress it into a Symphony reference to map held-out query cells and benchmark the mapping against de novo Harmony integration using LISI, k-NN correlation, and 5-NN label-transfer accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Build a Harmony-integrated embedding across batches or technologies (here, three 10x PBMC datasets from 3'v1, 3'v2, and 5' chemistry), then compress it into a Symphony reference to map held-out query cells and benchmark the mapping against de novo Harmony integration using LISI, k-NN correlation, and 5-NN label-transfer accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery of novel cell types in the query — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone, and its mapping metrics are uninformative when a novel population resembles an existing reference population The query dataset lacks comprehensive cell-type coverage in the reference (Condition I), since label transfer and mapping fidelity degrade when reference coverage is incomplete The input is already an integrated embedding and no batch/technology confounder needs to be removed

skills.name: harmony-batch-integration
skills.search_text: harmony-batch-integration Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GSE149689 PBMCs) pooled from multiple samples/donors shows batch effects that would confound clustering and cell-type annotation prior to differential-expression localisation. Input is bulk RNA-seq or bulk transcriptomic data (e.g. the 7 bulk severe-vs-mild COVID-19 datasets in the COVID19-severity database) — Harmony integration is defined on single-cell embeddings, not bulk samples. The single-cell data already come from a single sample/donor with no batch structure to correct — integration would remove real biological variation for nothing. Cells have already been integrated by another method and you only need cell-type annotation or VlnPlot output. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Harmony-based batch integration of a single-cell PBMC Seurat object on the top-20-PC embedding, so that cells pooled across samples/batches can be jointly clustered and cell-type-resolved. In this paper it enables localisation of MCEMP1 up-regulation and HLA-DRA down-regulation to CD14+ monocytes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ebiom.2023.104472
skills.summary: Harmony-based batch integration of a single-cell PBMC Seurat object on the top-20-PC embedding, so that cells pooled across samples/batches can be jointly clustered and cell-type-resolved. In this paper it enables localisation of MCEMP1 up-regulation and HLA-DRA down-regulation to CD14+ monocytes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or bulk transcriptomic data (e.g. the 7 bulk severe-vs-mild COVID-19 datasets in the COVID19-severity database) — Harmony integration is defined on single-cell embeddings, not bulk samples. The single-cell data already come from a single sample/donor with no batch structure to correct — integration would remove real biological variation for nothing. Cells have already been integrated by another method and you only need cell-type annotation or VlnPlot output.

The task is cell-type annotation itself rather than benchmarking integration — Harmony produces integrated embeddings, not cell-type labels like SELINA's query_predictions.txt Disease-mode SELINA prediction, where fine-tuning is skipped and the paper recommends users rely on their own data rather than a shared integration benchmark Data are not batch-structured (no platform/reference-query grouping variables), making LISI of common vs specific cell groups undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark baseline for batch integration: re-run the same merged single-cell reference/query data through Harmony and compute matching LISI scores so SELINA's MADA and autoencoder-based batch removal can be quantitatively compared against a established integration method (Figures 3D-3F of the SELINA paper). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Benchmark baseline for batch integration: re-run the same merged single-cell reference/query data through Harmony and compute matching LISI scores so SELINA's MADA and autoencoder-based batch removal can be quantitatively compared against a established integration method (Figures 3D-3F of the SELINA paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell-type annotation itself rather than benchmarking integration — Harmony produces integrated embeddings, not cell-type labels like SELINA's query_predictions.txt Disease-mode SELINA prediction, where fine-tuning is skipped and the paper recommends users rely on their own data rather than a shared integration benchmark Data are not batch-structured (no platform/reference-query grouping variables), making LISI of common vs specific cell groups undefined

skills.search_text: hartigan-dip-test-statistics Use when a per-cell uncertainty score distribution (e.g. scEMAIL E-scores from entropy, confidence, consistency) must be tested for bimodality to declare the presence of novel cell types without user-defined thresholds. The E-score distribution is already known to be unimodal and novel cell types have been ruled out or are irrelevant to the analysis goal A novel-cell-type presence decision cannot be reduced to a binary flag — use the downstream adaptive manifold-mixup threshold step instead once bimodality is confirmed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies bimodality statistics — the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test — to the distribution of scEMAIL's expert ensemble (E-score) uncertainty values to decide, via an either-test-positive rule, whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Applies bimodality statistics — the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test — to the distribution of scEMAIL's expert ensemble (E-score) uncertainty values to decide, via an either-test-positive rule, whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The E-score distribution is already known to be unimodal and novel cell types have been ruled out or are irrelevant to the analysis goal A novel-cell-type presence decision cannot be reduced to a binary flag — use the downstream adaptive manifold-mixup threshold step instead once bimodality is confirmed

skills.description: Use when PCA scores from a control-group scCRISPR-seq matrix must be triaged so that only multimodal, high-variance PCs are decoupled for infected proportion bias, while remaining PCs use observed change directly.
skills.name: hartigans-dip-test-multimodality-testing
skills.search_text: hartigans-dip-test-multimodality-testing Use when PCA scores from a control-group scCRISPR-seq matrix must be triaged so that only multimodal, high-variance PCs are decoupled for infected proportion bias, while remaining PCs use observed change directly. When the dataset is expected to be homogeneous such that no cell-cluster proportion differences exist between perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups — no PC will be multimodal and decoupling is unnecessary When the GMM assumption may not hold in intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection, since the article notes these break the method's assumptions When input is raw unnormalized counts — PCA scores and standard deviations must first come from data_preprocessing (log-normalization and highly variable gene detection) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores each principal component of control-group (Z) PCA scores for multimodality using Hartigan's dip test (diptest R package) and combines this with explained-spread ranking to flag PCs suspected of carrying infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq data, as implemented in scDecouple's pc_selection step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Scores each principal component of control-group (Z) PCA scores for multimodality using Hartigan's dip test (diptest R package) and combines this with explained-spread ranking to flag PCs suspected of carrying infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq data, as implemented in scDecouple's pc_selection step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset is expected to be homogeneous such that no cell-cluster proportion differences exist between perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups — no PC will be multimodal and decoupling is unnecessary When the GMM assumption may not hold in intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection, since the article notes these break the method's assumptions When input is raw unnormalized counts — PCA scores and standard deviations must first come from data_preprocessing (log-normalization and highly variable gene detection)

skills.description: Use when you need a fast, method-of-moments cross-check of cell type-specific variance differentiation calls from REML-based LMM fits on scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, e.g. to confirm Bonferroni-significant genes across two independent fitting methods.
skills.name: haseman-elston-regression-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: haseman-elston-regression-scrna-seq Use when you need a fast, method-of-moments cross-check of cell type-specific variance differentiation calls from REML-based LMM fits on scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, e.g. to confirm Bonferroni-significant genes across two independent fitting methods. Sample sizes below ~50 individuals, where CTMM is not reliable and the Free test is slightly inflated Rare cell types that cannot provide >10 cells per individual-cell type pair, since CTMM is limited to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian at available cell counts, violating the Gaussian approximation underlying the pseudobulk LMM http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Fits the Free cell type-specific linear mixed model on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data using Haseman-Elston (HE) regression — a method-of-moments alternative to REML — to obtain an independent set of Wald p-values for differentiation of variance (V) and mean expression (ct_beta) between cell types, used to cross-validate REML-based hits. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fits the Free cell type-specific linear mixed model on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data using Haseman-Elston (HE) regression — a method-of-moments alternative to REML — to obtain an independent set of Wald p-values for differentiation of variance (V) and mean expression (ct_beta) between cell types, used to cross-validate REML-based hits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes below ~50 individuals, where CTMM is not reliable and the Free test is slightly inflated Rare cell types that cannot provide >10 cells per individual-cell type pair, since CTMM is limited to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian at available cell counts, violating the Gaussian approximation underlying the pseudobulk LMM

skills.description: Use when you need cell-to-cell similarity scores from a log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix without full pairwise distance computation, e.g. building the similarity matrix S that feeds EDGE's k-NNG and spectral embedding.
skills.name: hash-based-sketch-vector-construction
skills.search_text: hash-based-sketch-vector-construction Use when you need cell-to-cell similarity scores from a log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix without full pairwise distance computation, e.g. building the similarity matrix S that feeds EDGE's k-NNG and spectral embedding. The goal is a standalone 2-D embedding or clustering — sketch similarity alone is only the front end of EDGE; you still need k-NNG construction, spectral embedding, and SGD optimization. The input matrix is raw counts — gene-specific thresholds and sketching assume log-normalized expression (median-CTP normalized, log2(x+1)). Memory for the hash table is unavailable at the desired H — the article notes large H (optimal 1,017,881) is better but 'large memory will be required'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs binary sketch vectors V ∈ {0,1}^B per cell by thresholding a randomly selected subset of B genes, then maps the inner product V·W via modulo hashing to a predefined hash table so that cell pairs sharing a hash code receive a pairwise similarity score of 1 — the core weak-learner operation inside EDGE's ensemble similarity search. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Constructs binary sketch vectors V ∈ {0,1}^B per cell by thresholding a randomly selected subset of B genes, then maps the inner product V·W via modulo hashing to a predefined hash table so that cell pairs sharing a hash code receive a pairwise similarity score of 1 — the core weak-learner operation inside EDGE's ensemble similarity search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a standalone 2-D embedding or clustering — sketch similarity alone is only the front end of EDGE; you still need k-NNG construction, spectral embedding, and SGD optimization. The input matrix is raw counts — gene-specific thresholds and sketching assume log-normalized expression (median-CTP normalized, log2(x+1)). Memory for the hash table is unavailable at the desired H — the article notes large H (optimal 1,017,881) is better but 'large memory will be required'.

skills.name: hashing-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: hashing-demultiplexing Use when analyzing hashed single-cell multiome data (e.g. cell hashing antibody oligo tags) that requires sample demultiplexing plus combined GEX and ADT/CITE-seq processing from raw FASTQ reads onward.
