skills.description: Use when a Seurat object carries an 'HTO' assay from a cell hashing experiment and per-hashtag cutoffs separating true-positive from background signal are needed to assign singlet/doublet/negative identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes.
skills.name: hashtag-cutoff-calling-for-cell-hashing-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: hashtag-cutoff-calling-for-cell-hashing-demultiplexing Use when a Seurat object carries an 'HTO' assay from a cell hashing experiment and per-hashtag cutoffs separating true-positive from background signal are needed to assign singlet/doublet/negative identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes. No 'HTO' assay is available (e.g. only SNP genotype data or gene expression) — genetic demultiplexing tools such as demuxlet, scSplit, or Vireo are the appropriate choice, and SNP-based methods additionally require distinct genetic backgrounds. The goal is correlating cell hashing labels with SNP clustering results (HybridDemultiplexing) rather than deriving per-hashtag cutoffs from hashtag distributions alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calls per-hashtag classification cutoffs that separate true-positive from background signal in cell hashing (HTO) data by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture to normalized hashtag counts, then labels each cell singlet, doublet, or negative. Designed to improve cutoff accuracy by avoiding dominance of negative signals in experiments with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Calls per-hashtag classification cutoffs that separate true-positive from background signal in cell hashing (HTO) data by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture to normalized hashtag counts, then labels each cell singlet, doublet, or negative. Designed to improve cutoff accuracy by avoiding dominance of negative signals in experiments with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No 'HTO' assay is available (e.g. only SNP genotype data or gene expression) — genetic demultiplexing tools such as demuxlet, scSplit, or Vireo are the appropriate choice, and SNP-based methods additionally require distinct genetic backgrounds. The goal is correlating cell hashing labels with SNP clustering results (HybridDemultiplexing) rather than deriving per-hashtag cutoffs from hashtag distributions alone.

skills.description: Use when a Seurat object with an 'HTO' assay has been demultiplexed (or is about to be) with HTOreader and you need to verify each hashtag's cutoff, especially with imbalanced sample sizes, many hashtags, or suspected poor hashtag staining.
skills.name: hashtag-cutoff-calling-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: hashtag-cutoff-calling-quality-assessment Use when a Seurat object with an 'HTO' assay has been demultiplexed (or is about to be) with HTOreader and you need to verify each hashtag's cutoff, especially with imbalanced sample sizes, many hashtags, or suspected poor hashtag staining. When the samples have distinct genetic backgrounds and SNP-based demultiplexing alone is sufficient — the hybrid strategy, not cutoff inspection, is the article's recommended accuracy booster When the input is not an HTO assay in a Seurat object (e.g. genetic variant data such as VCF/BAM for demuxlet/Vireo) — PlotHTO/HTOClassification do not apply When only global singlet/doublet rate comparisons between methods are needed without diagnosing cutoff placement http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assess and, if needed, manually refine HTOreader's automatic per-hashtag cutoffs by plotting each hashtag's signal distribution with PlotHTO, so that singlet/doublet/negative calls from HTOClassification are not corrupted by poorly called cutoffs (e.g. degraded hashtag staining as in the R125 dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Assess and, if needed, manually refine HTOreader's automatic per-hashtag cutoffs by plotting each hashtag's signal distribution with PlotHTO, so that singlet/doublet/negative calls from HTOClassification are not corrupted by poorly called cutoffs (e.g. degraded hashtag staining as in the R125 dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the samples have distinct genetic backgrounds and SNP-based demultiplexing alone is sufficient — the hybrid strategy, not cutoff inspection, is the article's recommended accuracy booster When the input is not an HTO assay in a Seurat object (e.g. genetic variant data such as VCF/BAM for demuxlet/Vireo) — PlotHTO/HTOClassification do not apply When only global singlet/doublet rate comparisons between methods are needed without diagnosing cutoff placement

skills.description: Use when input contains a cell-hashing (hashtag oligo) ADT count matrix — e.g. CITE-seq-Count output for multiple hashed samples — and each cell barcode must be assigned to a sample, a doublet, or a negative before downstream single-cell analysis.
skills.name: hashtag-demultiplexing-cell-assignment
skills.search_text: hashtag-demultiplexing-cell-assignment Use when input contains a cell-hashing (hashtag oligo) ADT count matrix — e.g. CITE-seq-Count output for multiple hashed samples — and each cell barcode must be assigned to a sample, a doublet, or a negative before downstream single-cell analysis. The input is gene expression (GEX) data only with no hashtag/ADT oligo counts — there is no HTO signal to threshold, so demultiplexing cannot be performed. Sample deconvolution relies on genotype/SNP demultiplexing (e.g. genetic hashing) rather than antibody-derived hashtag oligos; this skill is specific to HTO-count-based Seurat demultiplexing. The cells have already been demultiplexed and a sample-assignment table exists; re-running this step would duplicate the pipeline's doublet/negative removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Assigns individual cells from a multiplexed, cell-hashed experiment back to their source samples using Seurat-based hashtag oligo (HTO) normalization and HTODemux-style demultiplexing, flagging doublets and negatives. In gExcite this step turns the CITE-seq-Count hashtag count matrix into a per-cell sample-assignment table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: Assigns individual cells from a multiplexed, cell-hashed experiment back to their source samples using Seurat-based hashtag oligo (HTO) normalization and HTODemux-style demultiplexing, flagging doublets and negatives. In gExcite this step turns the CITE-seq-Count hashtag count matrix into a per-cell sample-assignment table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is gene expression (GEX) data only with no hashtag/ADT oligo counts — there is no HTO signal to threshold, so demultiplexing cannot be performed. Sample deconvolution relies on genotype/SNP demultiplexing (e.g. genetic hashing) rather than antibody-derived hashtag oligos; this skill is specific to HTO-count-based Seurat demultiplexing. The cells have already been demultiplexed and a sample-assignment table exists; re-running this step would duplicate the pipeline's doublet/negative removal.

skills.search_text: hausdorff-distance-distributional-fidelity-assessment Use when benchmarking single-cell sketching methods and you need a distribution-fidelity metric comparing a subsample's feature distribution (e.g. PCA embeddings in adata.obsm['X_pca']) against the full dataset. The input is already a reduced subsample and no full-data reference distribution exists, since the Hausdorff distance requires comparing sketch and full-data feature distributions.

skills.search_text: hausdorff-distance-simulation-clustering Use when an ensemble of simulated cell-state sequences from the Cytopath Markov sampler must be partitioned into sub-trajectory clusters (per terminal region) before dynamic time warping alignment and consensus averaging. The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the article notes spurious root/terminal inference (e.g., the erythroid gastrulation dataset) makes trajectory inference not meaningful Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this case No ensemble of simulated trajectories or transition probability matrix exists yet (e.g., raw AnnData without scvelo velocity processing) — the clustering operates on simulations, not raw expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Groups Cytopath's simulated Markov-chain differentiation trajectories terminating at the same terminal state by computing pairwise Euclidean Hausdorff distances between simulations and applying Louvain clustering, so that only simulations within a cluster are aligned and averaged into a consensus trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Groups Cytopath's simulated Markov-chain differentiation trajectories terminating at the same terminal state by computing pairwise Euclidean Hausdorff distances between simulations and applying Louvain clustering, so that only simulations within a cluster are aligned and averaged into a consensus trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the article notes spurious root/terminal inference (e.g., the erythroid gastrulation dataset) makes trajectory inference not meaningful Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this case No ensemble of simulated trajectories or transition probability matrix exists yet (e.g., raw AnnData without scvelo velocity processing) — the clustering operates on simulations, not raw expression data

skills.search_text: hdf5-single-cell-matrix-export Use when running scTE on 10x-style or plate-based scRNA-seq BAM files and you need the resulting TE count matrix in anndata-compatible .h5ad format for cell-type-level TE aggregation and marker-TE identification. You need only bulk (non-single-cell) TE counts from a BAM without cell-level resolution — a simpler counter such as te_count from te_counter suffices The downstream pipeline requires plain-text CSV output rather than HDF5/anndata format Input is single-cell ATAC-seq — use the scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build pipeline instead of the scRNA-seq scTE workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Emit scTE's transposable-element-by-cell count matrix as an HDF5 (.h5ad) file instead of CSV by passing --hdf5 True, enabling direct anndata-based loading and downstream aggregation of TE families (e.g., IAP/RLTR45, MER46C, L1ME3D, ETnERV3-int) per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Emit scTE's transposable-element-by-cell count matrix as an HDF5 (.h5ad) file instead of CSV by passing --hdf5 True, enabling direct anndata-based loading and downstream aggregation of TE families (e.g., IAP/RLTR45, MER46C, L1ME3D, ETnERV3-int) per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need only bulk (non-single-cell) TE counts from a BAM without cell-level resolution — a simpler counter such as te_count from te_counter suffices The downstream pipeline requires plain-text CSV output rather than HDF5/anndata format Input is single-cell ATAC-seq — use the scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build pipeline instead of the scRNA-seq scTE workflow

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending the runtime scalability benchmark on the Heart Cell Atlas: measuring how SiFT, scVI, and regress_out runtimes scale with subsample size from 5,000 to ~486,134 cells.
skills.name: heart-cell-atlas-dataset-subsampling
skills.search_text: heart-cell-atlas-dataset-subsampling Use when reproducing or extending the runtime scalability benchmark on the Heart Cell Atlas: measuring how SiFT, scVI, and regress_out runtimes scale with subsample size from 5,000 to ~486,134 cells. The goal is to validate the biological correctness of filtered output rather than runtimes — the article notes no ground truth reference exists to evaluate computational filtering results, so metrics must be application-specific. The dataset is small or unrelated to the Heart Cell Atlas scale; runtime ordering on ~500,000-cell subsamples will not generalize. The task is defining or applying a new filtering signal (kernel choice) rather than benchmarking scalability of existing covariate-removal runs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A runtime scalability benchmark that subsamples the Heart Cell Atlas (~500,000 cells) at 8 increasing sizes (5,000 to 486,134 cells) and measures wall-clock time for removing 10 continuous covariates with SiFT, scVI, and scanpy regress_out, testing the reported ordering SiFT (12 min) < scVI (36 min) < regress_out (1 h 26 min). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: A runtime scalability benchmark that subsamples the Heart Cell Atlas (~500,000 cells) at 8 increasing sizes (5,000 to 486,134 cells) and measures wall-clock time for removing 10 continuous covariates with SiFT, scVI, and scanpy regress_out, testing the reported ordering SiFT (12 min) < scVI (36 min) < regress_out (1 h 26 min).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to validate the biological correctness of filtered output rather than runtimes — the article notes no ground truth reference exists to evaluate computational filtering results, so metrics must be application-specific. The dataset is small or unrelated to the Heart Cell Atlas scale; runtime ordering on ~500,000-cell subsamples will not generalize. The task is defining or applying a new filtering signal (kernel choice) rather than benchmarking scalability of existing covariate-removal runs.

skills.description: Use when you need to cluster a preprocessed sample-by-feature matrix (e.g., PBMC scRNA-seq reduced to 30 PCs) with a method that yields per-point posterior label confidences and works on a KNN affinity graph.
skills.name: heat-based-label-propagation-clustering
skills.search_text: heat-based-label-propagation-clustering Use when you need to cluster a preprocessed sample-by-feature matrix (e.g., PBMC scRNA-seq reduced to 30 PCs) with a method that yields per-point posterior label confidences and works on a KNN affinity graph. Data contains only a single true cluster: Monte Carlo internal validation cannot estimate uncertainty because every point can only receive one type of label Very high-dimensional data without nonlinear dimensionality reduction: the method is sensitive to high dimensionality and limited by the curse of dimensionality Datasets over 1 million points where a full distance matrix is infeasible unless distances are approximated via KNN http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Cluster data by casting labels on seed vertices and propagating 'heat' influence across a KNN affinity graph until equilibrium, as implemented in Forest Fire Clustering (Forest Fire Clustering). Each vertex accepts a seed label when average influence exceeds its acceptance threshold (inverse of vertex degree). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Cluster data by casting labels on seed vertices and propagating 'heat' influence across a KNN affinity graph until equilibrium, as implemented in Forest Fire Clustering (Forest Fire Clustering). Each vertex accepts a seed label when average influence exceeds its acceptance threshold (inverse of vertex degree).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains only a single true cluster: Monte Carlo internal validation cannot estimate uncertainty because every point can only receive one type of label Very high-dimensional data without nonlinear dimensionality reduction: the method is sensitive to high dimensionality and limited by the curse of dimensionality Datasets over 1 million points where a full distance matrix is infeasible unless distances are approximated via KNN

skills.description: Use when you have pre-ranked differential gene tables for every cluster in an integrated scRNA-seq dataset and need to assign cell type identities/states from enrichment of curated signature gene sets (e.g., the 75 hematopoiesis GMT sets).
skills.name: heatmap-visualization-of-enrichment-scores
skills.search_text: heatmap-visualization-of-enrichment-scores Use when you have pre-ranked differential gene tables for every cluster in an integrated scRNA-seq dataset and need to assign cell type identities/states from enrichment of curated signature gene sets (e.g., the 75 hematopoiesis GMT sets). When no curated signature gene sets exist for the biological system — the article notes 'the user would have to compile and curate customized gene sets for the relevant system of interest' When clusters have not yet been defined or differential genes per cluster have not been pre-ranked by log2FC — the fGSEA ranking step requires cluster-level DE tables http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Visualize fgsea-computed normalized enrichment scores (NES) for curated gene sets across all scRNA-seq clusters as a cluster-by-gene-set heatmap, enabling systematic cell type annotation of integrated clusters (e.g., human HSPCs) in SingCellaR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Visualize fgsea-computed normalized enrichment scores (NES) for curated gene sets across all scRNA-seq clusters as a cluster-by-gene-set heatmap, enabling systematic cell type annotation of integrated clusters (e.g., human HSPCs) in SingCellaR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no curated signature gene sets exist for the biological system — the article notes 'the user would have to compile and curate customized gene sets for the relevant system of interest' When clusters have not yet been defined or differential genes per cluster have not been pre-ranked by log2FC — the fGSEA ranking step requires cluster-level DE tables

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a Symphony reference mapping flags query cell populations absent from the reference as novel, or when reproducing the ablation benchmark of per-cell/per-cluster mapping-confidence metrics (AUCs, Supplementary Fig. 9).
skills.name: held-out-cell-type-ablation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: held-out-cell-type-ablation-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a Symphony reference mapping flags query cell populations absent from the reference as novel, or when reproducing the ablation benchmark of per-cell/per-cluster mapping-confidence metrics (AUCs, Supplementary Fig. 9). When the query's novel population is very similar to an existing reference population — the article states the metrics may be less informative in that case When the goal is de novo cell type discovery from the query alone — Symphony does not supplant de novo query-only analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark Symphony's Mahalanobis-distance-based per-cell and per-cluster mapping metrics by ablating (holding out) query cell types and testing whether the metrics flag the missing populations as novel, quantified by AUC against the reference cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Benchmark Symphony's Mahalanobis-distance-based per-cell and per-cluster mapping metrics by ablating (holding out) query cell types and testing whether the metrics flag the missing populations as novel, quantified by AUC against the reference cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query's novel population is very similar to an existing reference population — the article states the metrics may be less informative in that case When the goal is de novo cell type discovery from the query alone — Symphony does not supplant de novo query-only analyses

skills.description: Use when training a custom cTP-net model on paired scRNA-seq/CITE-seq data and you must pick optimal network weights via held-out cells rather than training loss.
skills.name: held-out-cell-validation-model-selection
skills.search_text: held-out-cell-validation-model-selection Use when training a custom cTP-net model on paired scRNA-seq/CITE-seq data and you must pick optimal network weights via held-out cells rather than training loss. Input scRNA-seq is not UMI-based count data — cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based), and TPM/RPKM accuracy is untested Data have not been SAVER-X denoised and LogNormalize-transformed — skipping denoising retracts prediction correlation by 0.02 The goal is out-of-cell-type evaluation — that requires partitioning cells by cell type and iteratively holding out all cells of one type, not a random 10% split http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Randomly reserves 10% of paired transcriptome–protein cells as a testing set, trains the MB-DNN on the remaining 90%, and selects the final cTP-net weights (ctpnet_trained_model.h5) by minimizing testing error. This guards the transcriptome-to-protein model against overfitting before deployment on new scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Randomly reserves 10% of paired transcriptome–protein cells as a testing set, trains the MB-DNN on the remaining 90%, and selects the final cTP-net weights (ctpnet_trained_model.h5) by minimizing testing error. This guards the transcriptome-to-protein model against overfitting before deployment on new scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input scRNA-seq is not UMI-based count data — cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based), and TPM/RPKM accuracy is untested Data have not been SAVER-X denoised and LogNormalize-transformed — skipping denoising retracts prediction correlation by 0.02 The goal is out-of-cell-type evaluation — that requires partitioning cells by cell type and iteratively holding out all cells of one type, not a random 10% split

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a multi-condition scRNA-seq model predicts held-out condition combinations (e.g. <ctrl,severe> cells) correctly, comparing against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN.
skills.name: held-out-condition-splits-evaluation
skills.search_text: held-out-condition-splits-evaluation Use when evaluating whether a multi-condition scRNA-seq model predicts held-out condition combinations (e.g. <ctrl,severe> cells) correctly, comparing against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN. Each batch was measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to disentangle batch and condition effects, so held-out cross-batch condition prediction is ill-posed The task is unsupervised batch correction or key gene detection rather than quantitative evaluation of perturbation prediction against gold-standard counts Datasets contain highly correlated condition types without redefining them as a combined condition type, violating scDisInFact's mutual-independence assumption http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark perturbation-prediction methods by holding out specific condition-effect scenarios (in-sample and out-of-sample, within-batch and cross-batch) and scoring predicted counts against gold standards with cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Benchmark perturbation-prediction methods by holding out specific condition-effect scenarios (in-sample and out-of-sample, within-batch and cross-batch) and scoring predicted counts against gold standards with cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch was measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to disentangle batch and condition effects, so held-out cross-batch condition prediction is ill-posed The task is unsupervised batch correction or key gene detection rather than quantitative evaluation of perturbation prediction against gold-standard counts Datasets contain highly correlated condition types without redefining them as a combined condition type, violating scDisInFact's mutual-independence assumption

skills.description: Use when validating that a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g., Symphony) can transfer annotations (such as surface proteins) to query cells lacking the modality, and you need a donor-level split so query donors are never seen during reference construction.
skills.name: held-out-donor-validation-design
skills.search_text: held-out-donor-validation-design Use when validating that a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g., Symphony) can transfer annotations (such as surface proteins) to query cells lacking the modality, and you need a donor-level split so query donors are never seen during reference construction. When the query cells are annotated from modality-matched data (e.g., mRNA-to-mRNA cell-type label transfer), since protein-inference correlation scoring does not apply When the held-out donors' cells are also included in the reference atlas — this leaks donor identity and invalidates the validation When the reference lacks a second modality (proteins) entirely; there is no ground truth to correlate predictions against http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Design a donor-level held-out validation of reference-mapping-based annotation transfer: split a multimodal CITE-seq memory T-cell atlas into 217 training donors and 54 held-out donors whose mRNA-only data serve as queries, then score surface-protein inference by per-protein Pearson correlation between predicted and measured values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Design a donor-level held-out validation of reference-mapping-based annotation transfer: split a multimodal CITE-seq memory T-cell atlas into 217 training donors and 54 held-out donors whose mRNA-only data serve as queries, then score surface-protein inference by per-protein Pearson correlation between predicted and measured values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query cells are annotated from modality-matched data (e.g., mRNA-to-mRNA cell-type label transfer), since protein-inference correlation scoring does not apply When the held-out donors' cells are also included in the reference atlas — this leaks donor identity and invalidates the validation When the reference lacks a second modality (proteins) entirely; there is no ground truth to correlate predictions against

skills.description: Use when evaluating crossmodal generation quality of scMM (or similar multimodal VAEs) on CITE-seq data: need to quantify how precisely surface protein abundance can be predicted from transcriptome observations in held-out test cells via correlation.
skills.name: held-out-prediction-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: held-out-prediction-correlation-analysis Use when evaluating crossmodal generation quality of scMM (or similar multimodal VAEs) on CITE-seq data: need to quantify how precisely surface protein abundance can be predicted from transcriptome observations in held-out test cells via correlation. The goal is joint representation/clustering of both modalities rather than quantitative prediction accuracy of one modality from the other Data lacks a paired second modality (e.g. transcriptome-only scRNA-seq), so no crossmodal ground truth exists for correlation Modalities are chromatin accessibility rather than surface protein counts and no modality-appropriate likelihood (e.g. scMM's ATAC-seq folder with peak.tsv setup) has been configured http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates a multimodal model's crossmodal generation by withholding one modality (surface proteins) from held-out test cells, generating predictions conditioned only on the transcriptome, and correlating predicted NB mean parameters against original counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Validates a multimodal model's crossmodal generation by withholding one modality (surface proteins) from held-out test cells, generating predictions conditioned only on the transcriptome, and correlating predicted NB mean parameters against original counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is joint representation/clustering of both modalities rather than quantitative prediction accuracy of one modality from the other Data lacks a paired second modality (e.g. transcriptome-only scRNA-seq), so no crossmodal ground truth exists for correlation Modalities are chromatin accessibility rather than surface protein counts and no modality-appropriate likelihood (e.g. scMM's ATAC-seq folder with peak.tsv setup) has been configured

skills.description: Use when a supervised classifier trained with 10-fold stratified CV on the TCGA 19,737-gene training matrix must be assessed for true generalization on unseen held-out TCGA test samples (e.g. confirming mLR's 85% test accuracy).
skills.name: held-out-test-set-generalization-evaluation
skills.search_text: held-out-test-set-generalization-evaluation Use when a supervised classifier trained with 10-fold stratified CV on the TCGA 19,737-gene training matrix must be assessed for true generalization on unseen held-out TCGA test samples (e.g. confirming mLR's 85% test accuracy). Input is a single-sample classification task needing a deployable caller (use the AWCA/mLR subtyping code from the DEIB-GECO repository instead of re-running the survey) Only cross-validated performance is needed and no unseen test partition exists — test-set accuracy cannot be computed and CV accuracy would be a biased substitute Subtype labels themselves were produced by PAM50 on the same gene panel, so accuracy estimates inherit label bias and are not a clean generalization measure http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Evaluates multiclass classifiers for breast cancer intrinsic subtyping (mLR, Decision Forest, Decision Jungle, FFNN, SVM) by refitting the best cross-validated estimator on the 19,737-gene TCGA training set and measuring generalization on a separate held-out TCGA test set, so that reported accuracy is not only cross-validation optimism. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Evaluates multiclass classifiers for breast cancer intrinsic subtyping (mLR, Decision Forest, Decision Jungle, FFNN, SVM) by refitting the best cross-validated estimator on the 19,737-gene TCGA training set and measuring generalization on a separate held-out TCGA test set, so that reported accuracy is not only cross-validation optimism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample classification task needing a deployable caller (use the AWCA/mLR subtyping code from the DEIB-GECO repository instead of re-running the survey) Only cross-validated performance is needed and no unseen test partition exists — test-set accuracy cannot be computed and CV accuracy would be a biased substitute Subtype labels themselves were produced by PAM50 on the same gene panel, so accuracy estimates inherit label bias and are not a clean generalization measure

skills.description: Use when a trained trajectory model must be validated on held-out progenitor states and ranked against existing methods on clonal fate-bias prediction metrics.
skills.name: held-out-timepoint-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: held-out-timepoint-benchmark-comparison Use when a trained trajectory model must be validated on held-out progenitor states and ranked against existing methods on clonal fate-bias prediction metrics. Data is a single time point with no held-out timepoint or clonal labels, so no benchmark against observed fate bias is possible The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model's stated assumption and invalidating a fair fate-bias comparison The task is perturbation simulation or interpolation rather than clonal fate-bias benchmarking against WOT/FateID http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a trajectory/fate-prediction model (PRESCIENT) against external baselines (WOT, FateID) and a held-out clonal upper bound by scoring fate-bias predictions with Pearson r, AUROC, and covered fraction, writing the method-by-method table to fate_bias_metrics.csv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Benchmark a trajectory/fate-prediction model (PRESCIENT) against external baselines (WOT, FateID) and a held-out clonal upper bound by scoring fate-bias predictions with Pearson r, AUROC, and covered fraction, writing the method-by-method table to fate_bias_metrics.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is a single time point with no held-out timepoint or clonal labels, so no benchmark against observed fate bias is possible The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state, violating the model's stated assumption and invalidating a fair fate-bias comparison The task is perturbation simulation or interpolation rather than clonal fate-bias benchmarking against WOT/FateID

skills.description: Use when a longitudinal scRNA-seq dataset has ≥3 time points and you need to test whether a trained trajectory model can generate an unobserved intermediate population, comparing against an optimal-transport baseline.
skills.name: held-out-timepoint-validation
skills.search_text: held-out-timepoint-validation Use when a longitudinal scRNA-seq dataset has ≥3 time points and you need to test whether a trained trajectory model can generate an unobserved intermediate population, comparing against an optimal-transport baseline. The dataset's final time point cannot be assumed to be at steady-state, since the PRESCIENT model requires it as the terminal target The task is fate-bias/clonal prediction rather than interpolation — use the `weinreb-fate.sh`-style setup with estimated proliferation rates instead Reliable proliferation/growth-rate estimates are unavailable, since model performance depends on growth rates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates a PRESCIENT generative model by holding out one time point (day 4 of the Weinreb mouse hematopoiesis lineage tracing dataset), training only on days 2 and 6, simulating the held-out marginal population, and scoring it by Wasserstein distance against both the true held-out cells and a WOT linear-interpolation baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Validates a PRESCIENT generative model by holding out one time point (day 4 of the Weinreb mouse hematopoiesis lineage tracing dataset), training only on days 2 and 6, simulating the held-out marginal population, and scoring it by Wasserstein distance against both the true held-out cells and a WOT linear-interpolation baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset's final time point cannot be assumed to be at steady-state, since the PRESCIENT model requires it as the terminal target The task is fate-bias/clonal prediction rather than interpolation — use the `weinreb-fate.sh`-style setup with estimated proliferation rates instead Reliable proliferation/growth-rate estimates are unavailable, since model performance depends on growth rates

skills.description: Use when clusters from an integrated hematopoietic (e.g. HSPC) scRNA-seq dataset need objective cell-type labels, and a curated GMT of hematopoiesis signature gene sets is available.

skills.search_text: hematopoiesis-gene-set-interpretation Use when clusters from an integrated hematopoietic (e.g. HSPC) scRNA-seq dataset need objective cell-type labels, and a curated GMT of hematopoiesis signature gene sets is available. The tissue or lineage is not hematopoietic — the protocol only provides 75 gene sets curated from previous studies relevant to hematopoiesis, so users must compile and curate customized gene sets for other systems You need fully automatic annotation without curated signature sets — SingCellaR requires signature gene sets to perform the cell type annotation analysis Input is raw unnormalized UMI counts without clusters or differential expression computed — pre-ranked genes per cluster must exist first http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematically annotate cell type identities and cell states for integrated scRNA-seq clusters by running fgSEA with 75 curated hematopoiesis gene sets in SingCellaR and interpreting a cluster-by-gene-set NES heatmap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Systematically annotate cell type identities and cell states for integrated scRNA-seq clusters by running fgSEA with 75 curated hematopoiesis gene sets in SingCellaR and interpreting a cluster-by-gene-set NES heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue or lineage is not hematopoietic — the protocol only provides 75 gene sets curated from previous studies relevant to hematopoiesis, so users must compile and curate customized gene sets for other systems You need fully automatic annotation without curated signature sets — SingCellaR requires signature gene sets to perform the cell type annotation analysis Input is raw unnormalized UMI counts without clusters or differential expression computed — pre-ranked genes per cluster must exist first

skills.description: Use when comparing branching trajectory inference methods on a small single-cell qPCR dataset where sorted population labels can serve as ground truth for lineage-specific marker genes such as Gata1 and Pax5.
skills.name: hematopoiesis-qpcr-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: hematopoiesis-qpcr-trajectory-analysis Use when comparing branching trajectory inference methods on a small single-cell qPCR dataset where sorted population labels can serve as ground truth for lineage-specific marker genes such as Gata1 and Pax5. Input is scATAC-seq data with peaks/k-mers/motifs as features — use the stream_atac conda variant instead of the standard RNA-seq environment The dataset has cyclic or disconnected topology — the article notes STREAM's adaptation to these more general structures requires further improvement Cells may have totally different fates than the reference structure — the mapping procedure is not guaranteed optimal in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark trajectory inference methods (STREAM, Monocle2, ElPiGraph) on the ~270-cell single-cell qPCR hematopoiesis dataset (~170 transcription factors, six sorted populations) by scoring branch assignments for Gata1 and Pax5 lineages with precision, recall, and F1 against sorted-population ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Benchmark trajectory inference methods (STREAM, Monocle2, ElPiGraph) on the ~270-cell single-cell qPCR hematopoiesis dataset (~170 transcription factors, six sorted populations) by scoring branch assignments for Gata1 and Pax5 lineages with precision, recall, and F1 against sorted-population ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scATAC-seq data with peaks/k-mers/motifs as features — use the stream_atac conda variant instead of the standard RNA-seq environment The dataset has cyclic or disconnected topology — the article notes STREAM's adaptation to these more general structures requires further improvement Cells may have totally different fates than the reference structure — the mapping procedure is not guaranteed optimal in that case

skills.description: Use when analyzing large-scale single-cell RNA-seq hematopoiesis data (e.g., human bone marrow from 10X Chromium) where cell-fate dynamics must be reconstructed efficiently and aggregation is needed to make multiscale transition analysis tractable.
skills.name: hematopoiesis-single-cell-data-analysis
skills.search_text: hematopoiesis-single-cell-data-analysis Use when analyzing large-scale single-cell RNA-seq hematopoiesis data (e.g., human bone marrow from 10X Chromium) where cell-fate dynamics must be reconstructed efficiently and aggregation is needed to make multiscale transition analysis tractable. Dataset has relatively few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset studied here) — the paper notes special care is needed to confirm transition-cell analysis in small datasets, and DECLARE aggregation is unnecessary overhead Non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics are central to the question, since these were not considered in the current method The input is already aggregated or is not a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., a feature table or pre-computed pseudotime) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies the MuTrans multi-scale stochastic dynamics framework, with the DECLARE dynamics-preserving aggregation pre-processing module, to the human bone-marrow hematopoiesis (10X Chromium) dataset to reconstruct attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities, and transition path likelihoods while speeding up computation by roughly an order of magnitude. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Applies the MuTrans multi-scale stochastic dynamics framework, with the DECLARE dynamics-preserving aggregation pre-processing module, to the human bone-marrow hematopoiesis (10X Chromium) dataset to reconstruct attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities, and transition path likelihoods while speeding up computation by roughly an order of magnitude.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset has relatively few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset studied here) — the paper notes special care is needed to confirm transition-cell analysis in small datasets, and DECLARE aggregation is unnecessary overhead Non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics are central to the question, since these were not considered in the current method The input is already aggregated or is not a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., a feature table or pre-computed pseudotime)

skills.description: Use when a single-cell hematopoiesis dataset (e.g., Weinreb et al. Kleind2ws murine HSC differentiation data) has ground-truth cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster purity via per-cluster label entropy under different clustering schemes.
skills.name: hematopoietic-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: hematopoietic-cell-type-annotation Use when a single-cell hematopoiesis dataset (e.g., Weinreb et al. Kleind2ws murine HSC differentiation data) has ground-truth cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster purity via per-cluster label entropy under different clustering schemes. The dataset lacks known cell-type labels or ground-truth annotations, so no label-distribution entropy can be computed The data are not hematopoietic/single-cell with clonal barcodes — entropy comparison across α levels presumes hybrid (clonal + transcriptome) clustering The goal is de novo marker discovery or gene set overrepresentation analysis (use Find_Markers_ROC / WebGestaltR workflow instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Annotate and evaluate clustering quality of single-cell hematopoiesis data by cross-tabulating known cell-type labels (basophils, erythroid/megakaryocyte progenitors, mast cells, dendritic cell subsets) against cluster assignments and computing Shannon entropy of the cell-type distribution per cluster. Used in the ClonoCluster paper to show that low-α hybrid clusters reduce entropy (increase purity) relative to transcriptome-only clustering in the in vitro hematopoiesis dataset (Figure S7). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Annotate and evaluate clustering quality of single-cell hematopoiesis data by cross-tabulating known cell-type labels (basophils, erythroid/megakaryocyte progenitors, mast cells, dendritic cell subsets) against cluster assignments and computing Shannon entropy of the cell-type distribution per cluster. Used in the ClonoCluster paper to show that low-α hybrid clusters reduce entropy (increase purity) relative to transcriptome-only clustering in the in vitro hematopoiesis dataset (Figure S7).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks known cell-type labels or ground-truth annotations, so no label-distribution entropy can be computed The data are not hematopoietic/single-cell with clonal barcodes — entropy comparison across α levels presumes hybrid (clonal + transcriptome) clustering The goal is de novo marker discovery or gene set overrepresentation analysis (use Find_Markers_ROC / WebGestaltR workflow instead)

skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a strictly linear pseudotime ordering or a single-branch-point trajectory — Waterfall, Monocle 1, or Wishbone target those cases, and CellRouter's multi-state flow-network design is unnecessary overhead Trajectories must be reconstructed between two pre-specified states using user-defined metadata (e.g., sorted populations) rather than de novo community-detected subpopulations — CellRouter's updated workflow supports user-defined clusters directly instead The data are not single-cell transcriptomics from a hematopoietic context; marker dynamics like Cebpe/Mxd1 and Gata1/Scna are lineage-specific to myelo-erythroid differentiation

skills.description: Use when per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores must be compared across hematopoietic progenitor types (HSC, MPP, GMP, etc.) to check whether a method orders cells according to the classical HSC-first hierarchy.
skills.name: hematopoietic-progenitor-cell-type-ranking
skills.search_text: hematopoietic-progenitor-cell-type-ranking Use when per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores must be compared across hematopoietic progenitor types (HSC, MPP, GMP, etc.) to check whether a method orders cells according to the classical HSC-first hierarchy. The goal is trajectory inference from scratch rather than quantifying pluripotency per cell type — ORIGINS scores are intended to identify stem/progenitor cells as trajectory origins, not to build the trajectory itself. Expression data are not a normalized genes-by-cells matrix; ORIGINS expects a matrix or data frame with genes in rows and cells in columns, and PyOrigins normalizes by edge count and per-cell mean expression before comparing PPINs or samples. The biological process of interest is not cell differentiation — the differentiation PPIN in ORIGINS is specific; use ORIGINS2, which provides PPINs for 18 biological processes and a build_ppin function for custom gene lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Benchmark pluripotency scoring methods (ORIGINS, LandSCENT, CytoTRACE) on the hematopoietic bone marrow scRNA-seq dataset GSE117498 by aggregating per-cell scores over progenitor cell types (HSC, MPP, GMP, etc.) and ranking cell types by average potency to test recovery of the classical hematopoietic hierarchy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Benchmark pluripotency scoring methods (ORIGINS, LandSCENT, CytoTRACE) on the hematopoietic bone marrow scRNA-seq dataset GSE117498 by aggregating per-cell scores over progenitor cell types (HSC, MPP, GMP, etc.) and ranking cell types by average potency to test recovery of the classical hematopoietic hierarchy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is trajectory inference from scratch rather than quantifying pluripotency per cell type — ORIGINS scores are intended to identify stem/progenitor cells as trajectory origins, not to build the trajectory itself. Expression data are not a normalized genes-by-cells matrix; ORIGINS expects a matrix or data frame with genes in rows and cells in columns, and PyOrigins normalizes by edge count and per-cell mean expression before comparing PPINs or samples. The biological process of interest is not cell differentiation — the differentiation PPIN in ORIGINS is specific; use ORIGINS2, which provides PPINs for 18 biological processes and a build_ppin function for custom gene lists.

skills.description: Use when per-sample viral/HERV contig calls from RNAseq (e.g. viRNAtrap FASTA contigs) must be dichotomized into HERV-positive vs HERV-negative groups and tested against TCGA overall survival or somatic driver mutations.

skills.search_text: herv-expression-survival-association Use when per-sample viral/HERV contig calls from RNAseq (e.g. viRNAtrap FASTA contigs) must be dichotomized into HERV-positive vs HERV-negative groups and tested against TCGA overall survival or somatic driver mutations. The input is raw RNAseq FASTQ rather than assembled per-sample contig calls — run viRNAtrap's read-to-contig pipeline first (map to hg19/phiX, then virnatrap-predict) before survival testing. The analysis targets canonical exogenous cancer viruses (e.g. HPV, HBV) rather than endogenous retroviruses; the curated intact-gene HERV database and dichotomization are specific to HERV-K/HERV-H. Cancer types outside the four tested cohorts (COAD, LUSC, LUAD, LIHC) are used without re-validating the survival association, which was reported only for those cohorts. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether the presence of HERV-K/HERV-H transcripts (from viRNAtrap-predicted viral contigs) in TCGA tumor samples is associated with patients' overall survival, and whether HERV-positive samples are enriched among driver-gene mutants. It links the paper's curated functional-HERV database to Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival statistics and hypergeometric mutation-enrichment tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw RNAseq FASTQ rather than assembled per-sample contig calls — run viRNAtrap's read-to-contig pipeline first (map to hg19/phiX, then virnatrap-predict) before survival testing. skills.description: Use when a detected gene co-expression module (GCN) or gene regulatory network (GRN) from scRNA-seq analysis must be linked to repurposable drugs — i.e., after module selection and hub gene detection, when pharmacological targeting of driver mechanisms is the goal.
skills.name: heterogeneous-drug-target-network-construction
skills.search_text: heterogeneous-drug-target-network-construction Use when a detected gene co-expression module (GCN) or gene regulatory network (GRN) from scRNA-seq analysis must be linked to repurposable drugs — i.e., after module selection and hub gene detection, when pharmacological targeting of driver mechanisms is the goal. The linkage is a standard one (single, average, complete, Ward) already implemented efficiently in SciPy's cluster.hierarchy.linkage — the paper notes the python/scipy KMD implementation runs longer than widely used clustering algorithms, so custom code adds cost without benefit. The dataset is at million-object scale and a full dendrogram is required — use the article's sampling-based extension (KMDHierarchicalClustering sub_sample=True) instead, since full-memory KMD linkage is O(n^2). The task is selecting the best k or number of clusters rather than implementing/verifying the linkage algorithm itself — use the KMD silhouette score / DBCV workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implements efficient agglomerative hierarchical clustering with an arbitrary linkage (here KMD linkage) via a heap-based routine that maintains, per pair of clusters, the list of k minimal inter-cluster distances, giving O(nk) linkage updates and O(n^2) memory independent of k. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Implements efficient agglomerative hierarchical clustering with an arbitrary linkage (here KMD linkage) via a heap-based routine that maintains, per pair of clusters, the list of k minimal inter-cluster distances, giving O(nk) linkage updates and O(n^2) memory independent of k.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The linkage is a standard one (single, average, complete, Ward) already implemented efficiently in SciPy's cluster.hierarchy.linkage — the paper notes the python/scipy KMD implementation runs longer than widely used clustering algorithms, so custom code adds cost without benefit. The dataset is at million-object scale and a full dendrogram is required — use the article's sampling-based extension (KMDHierarchicalClustering sub_sample=True) instead, since full-memory KMD linkage is O(n^2). The task is selecting the best k or number of clusters rather than implementing/verifying the linkage algorithm itself — use the KMD silhouette score / DBCV workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing automated cancer scRNA-seq cell-type annotation with a hierarchical deep-learning classifier, or when benchmarking major-type vs subtype annotation accuracy via cross-validation on the scWizard training reference.
skills.name: hierarchical-neural-network-classifier-training
skills.search_text: hierarchical-neural-network-classifier-training Use when building or reproducing automated cancer scRNA-seq cell-type annotation with a hierarchical deep-learning classifier, or when benchmarking major-type vs subtype annotation accuracy via cross-validation on the scWizard training reference. Tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) are the annotation target — the scWizard reference may not identify them and they fall into the Unknown cluster Input data is not cancer scRNA-seq / tumor microenvironment cells, since the reference covers 13 cancer types and 7 TME major types A labeled reference and supervised training are not possible and marker-based or correlation-based annotation tools are preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and cross-validate scWizard's two-step hierarchical deep neural network (ReLU + softmax) that classifies tumor microenvironment cells into 7 major types and 47 subtypes using a built-in reference of 113,976 cells across 13 cancer types, and estimate its accuracy via ten-fold validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Train and cross-validate scWizard's two-step hierarchical deep neural network (ReLU + softmax) that classifies tumor microenvironment cells into 7 major types and 47 subtypes using a built-in reference of 113,976 cells across 13 cancer types, and estimate its accuracy via ten-fold validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) are the annotation target — the scWizard reference may not identify them and they fall into the Unknown cluster Input data is not cancer scRNA-seq / tumor microenvironment cells, since the reference covers 13 cancer types and 7 TME major types A labeled reference and supervised training are not possible and marker-based or correlation-based annotation tools are preferred

skills.description: Use when you need to train a custom Census cell-type classification model from a reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Tabula Sapiens) rather than using the pretrained model, inferring the cell-type hierarchy from the reference and fitting one binary classifier per node.
skills.name: hierarchical-node-classifier-training
skills.search_text: hierarchical-node-classifier-training Use when you need to train a custom Census cell-type classification model from a reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Tabula Sapiens) rather than using the pretrained model, inferring the cell-type hierarchy from the reference and fitting one binary classifier per node. The goal is annotating a new dataset with normal/cancer cell types and cell of origin using the pretrained Tabula Sapiens/CCLE model — use the census_main prediction workflow instead of retraining The input is a single Seurat object needing annotation rather than a labeled reference dataset from which a hierarchy and node models can be trained The reference lacks multiple cell types sufficient to define nodal cell-type relationships for successive root-to-terminal classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a Census-style collection of hierarchically organized binary xgboost gradient-boosted decision tree classifiers, one per internal node of a cell-type hierarchy inferred from pseudo-bulk reference profiles (Tabula Sapiens plus CCLE), yielding a serialized node model collection used for successive root-to-terminal cell-type classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Train a Census-style collection of hierarchically organized binary xgboost gradient-boosted decision tree classifiers, one per internal node of a cell-type hierarchy inferred from pseudo-bulk reference profiles (Tabula Sapiens plus CCLE), yielding a serialized node model collection used for successive root-to-terminal cell-type classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating a new dataset with normal/cancer cell types and cell of origin using the pretrained Tabula Sapiens/CCLE model — use the census_main prediction workflow instead of retraining The input is a single Seurat object needing annotation rather than a labeled reference dataset from which a hierarchy and node models can be trained The reference lacks multiple cell types sufficient to define nodal cell-type relationships for successive root-to-terminal classification

skills.description: Use when pathway module scores (e.g., Seurat AddModuleScore over msigdbr BioCarta gene sets with >=10 genes) have already been scored per spot and ranked by singleCellHaystack KLD-based FDR in 2D spatial data, and the top pathways (e.g., top 25) need to be grouped by spatial-pattern similarity.
skills.name: hierarchical-pathway-clustering
skills.search_text: hierarchical-pathway-clustering Use when pathway module scores (e.g., Seurat AddModuleScore over msigdbr BioCarta gene sets with >=10 genes) have already been scored per spot and ranked by singleCellHaystack KLD-based FDR in 2D spatial data, and the top pathways (e.g., top 25) need to be grouped by spatial-pattern similarity. You are using the Python singleCellHaystack package (v0.0.5 beta): the README lists 'Hierarchical clustering method for cluster_genes' among its missing features, so use the R package instead. You need to compare pathway activity across multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout); the article states such comparisons cannot easily be conducted. The feature matrix is still raw or binary detection data rather than the rescaled continuous module scores the updated method expects. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Groups top-ranked differentially active pathways by similarity of their spatial activity patterns using singleCellHaystack's hierarchical clustering method (hclust_haystack / cluster_genes), as in the BioCarta module-score analysis of Visium datasets (Fig. 5). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Groups top-ranked differentially active pathways by similarity of their spatial activity patterns using singleCellHaystack's hierarchical clustering method (hclust_haystack / cluster_genes), as in the BioCarta module-score analysis of Visium datasets (Fig. 5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are using the Python singleCellHaystack package (v0.0.5 beta): the README lists 'Hierarchical clustering method for cluster_genes' among its missing features, so use the R package instead. You need to compare pathway activity across multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout); the article states such comparisons cannot easily be conducted. The feature matrix is still raw or binary detection data rather than the rescaled continuous module scores the updated method expects.

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g. AnnData of normalized, log-transformed cells) where some or all cell type annotations are available and a supervised/semi-supervised latent space with label prediction is desired.
skills.name: hierarchical-prior-conditioning-on-cell-type-labels
skills.search_text: hierarchical-prior-conditioning-on-cell-type-labels Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g. AnnData of normalized, log-transformed cells) where some or all cell type annotations are available and a supervised/semi-supervised latent space with label prediction is desired. No cell type annotations exist at all and a purely unsupervised integration is required — use plain scDREAMER instead, since the classifier C and label-conditioned y-prior need annotations to train Annotations are used only for downstream evaluation and should not influence the latent space — conditioning the prior on labels would leak supervision into the embedding The task requires handling unknown batch structure, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches scDREAMER-Sup extends the adversarial VAE backbone of scDREAMER with an additional variational autoencoder AY and a feed-forward cell type classifier C, conditioning the latent prior on available cell type annotations so that supervised or semi-supervised (10/20/50% labeled) integration yields annotation-guided latent embeddings and predicted labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: scDREAMER-Sup extends the adversarial VAE backbone of scDREAMER with an additional variational autoencoder AY and a feed-forward cell type classifier C, conditioning the latent prior on available cell type annotations so that supervised or semi-supervised (10/20/50% labeled) integration yields annotation-guided latent embeddings and predicted labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell type annotations exist at all and a purely unsupervised integration is required — use plain scDREAMER instead, since the classifier C and label-conditioned y-prior need annotations to train Annotations are used only for downstream evaluation and should not influence the latent space — conditioning the prior on labels would leak supervision into the embedding The task requires handling unknown batch structure, since the model assumes prior knowledge of the number of batches

skills.description: Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices from individual tumour biopsies need pan-cancer TME cell-type labels, including malignant cells and their tissue of origin across 19 cancer types.
skills.name: hierarchical-random-forest-tme-annotation
skills.search_text: hierarchical-random-forest-tme-annotation Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices from individual tumour biopsies need pan-cancer TME cell-type labels, including malignant cells and their tissue of origin across 19 cancer types. The input is a normal (non-tumour) tissue sample: the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter of create_summary_matrix instead. The input is a pooled matrix spanning multiple patients: inter-patient cancer-cell-specific effects interfere with cancer signature scoring and classification confidence, so run scATOMIC per biopsy only. The sample is a cancer type not in the validated reference (e.g. bile duct, bone, endometrial, esophageal, gallbladder, gastric), which may be misclassified as related cancers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate single cells in tumour microenvironments pan-cancer using scATOMIC, which trains hierarchically organized random forest models with elimination processes on >300,000 cancer, immune and stromal cells covering 19 common cancers, using MAGIC-imputed signatures and EM-fitted confidence cutoffs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Annotate single cells in tumour microenvironments pan-cancer using scATOMIC, which trains hierarchically organized random forest models with elimination processes on >300,000 cancer, immune and stromal cells covering 19 common cancers, using MAGIC-imputed signatures and EM-fitted confidence cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a normal (non-tumour) tissue sample: the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter of create_summary_matrix instead. The input is a pooled matrix spanning multiple patients: inter-patient cancer-cell-specific effects interfere with cancer signature scoring and classification confidence, so run scATOMIC per biopsy only. The sample is a cancer type not in the validated reference (e.g. bile duct, bone, endometrial, esophageal, gallbladder, gastric), which may be misclassified as related cancers.

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized barcode counts table (samples x barcodes) and need to test whether samples group by treatment condition based on overall clonal composition rather than single-clone abundance.
skills.name: hierarchical-sample-clustering-by-barcode-composition
skills.search_text: hierarchical-sample-clustering-by-barcode-composition Use when you have a normalized barcode counts table (samples x barcodes) and need to test whether samples group by treatment condition based on overall clonal composition rather than single-clone abundance. Input is raw (unnormalized) barcode counts — composition-based correlation will be dominated by sequencing depth rather than clonal structure The goal is pre-processing or barcode extraction from FASTQ — that is BARtab's pipeline (SOFTWARE_CHECK through counts table generation), not downstream clustering Lineage reconstruction from single-cell phylogenetic data is required — tools like Cassiopeia or LinRace are the appropriate choice per the article's discussion Clusters biological samples based on similarity of their synthetic barcode abundance profiles using hierarchical clustering on correlation-based dissimilarity, to reveal whether treatment groups (e.g., AraC IC90 vs. gradual dose-escalation DMSO/IBET-151 samples) occupy distinct clonal-composition states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Clusters biological samples based on similarity of their synthetic barcode abundance profiles using hierarchical clustering on correlation-based dissimilarity, to reveal whether treatment groups (e.g., AraC IC90 vs. gradual dose-escalation DMSO/IBET-151 samples) occupy distinct clonal-composition states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unnormalized) barcode counts — composition-based correlation will be dominated by sequencing depth rather than clonal structure The goal is pre-processing or barcode extraction from FASTQ — that is BARtab's pipeline (SOFTWARE_CHECK through counts table generation), not downstream clustering Lineage reconstruction from single-cell phylogenetic data is required — tools like Cassiopeia or LinRace are the appropriate choice per the article's discussion

skills.description: Use when unsupervised transcriptomic data (bulk or single-cell RNA-seq) has an unknown number of clusters and the goal is to discover and verify novel, biologically meaningful subtypes without manual k selection.
skills.name: hierarchical-subtype-discovery-verification
skills.search_text: hierarchical-subtype-discovery-verification Use when unsupervised transcriptomic data (bulk or single-cell RNA-seq) has an unknown number of clusters and the goal is to discover and verify novel, biologically meaningful subtypes without manual k selection. The number of clusters is already known and only a single fixed-k partition is needed — RCC is designed for datasets with an unknown number of clusters and hierarchical subdivision Manual, annotation-driven cluster identification via known sample labels and visualization is acceptable — RCC targets novel subtype discovery without requiring computational expertise or known annotations Large integrated datasets with millions of cells — the paper notes computational time is a limitation and that analysis of millions-of-cell integrated datasets is still 'the next step', not yet demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduces and verifies novel hierarchical subtype structures in transcriptomic datasets using the RCC (Recursive Consensus Clustering) R package, which recursively applies ConsensusClusterPlus with k-means to determine optimal cluster numbers and subdivides clusters level by level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Reproduces and verifies novel hierarchical subtype structures in transcriptomic datasets using the RCC (Recursive Consensus Clustering) R package, which recursively applies ConsensusClusterPlus with k-means to determine optimal cluster numbers and subdivides clusters level by level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters is already known and only a single fixed-k partition is needed — RCC is designed for datasets with an unknown number of clusters and hierarchical subdivision Manual, annotation-driven cluster identification via known sample labels and visualization is acceptable — RCC targets novel subtype discovery without requiring computational expertise or known annotations Large integrated datasets with millions of cells — the paper notes computational time is a limitation and that analysis of millions-of-cell integrated datasets is still 'the next step', not yet demonstrated

skills.description: Use when a new labeled scRNA-seq dataset (AnnData with cell population labels and batch indicators) must be progressively integrated into an existing scHPL classification tree, and you need to determine which populations match, merge, split, or are new.
skills.name: hierarchical-tree-split-merge-update
skills.search_text: hierarchical-tree-split-merge-update Use when a new labeled scRNA-seq dataset (AnnData with cell population labels and batch indicators) must be progressively integrated into an existing scHPL classification tree, and you need to determine which populations match, merge, split, or are new. Datasets are not yet aligned in a shared latent space — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so matching must not be run on raw counts You only need to predict labels of an unlabeled dataset using an existing tree (use scHPL's predict mode instead of progressive tree updating) Cell-type relationships are known to violate a tree structure, e.g. dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs scHPL's reciprocal label-matching and tree-updating procedure: cross-predict populations between two aligned datasets, build a matching matrix from binarized confusion matrices, and update the hierarchical classification tree via match, merge, split, or new-population operations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Reconstructs scHPL's reciprocal label-matching and tree-updating procedure: cross-predict populations between two aligned datasets, build a matching matrix from binarized confusion matrices, and update the hierarchical classification tree via match, merge, split, or new-population operations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not yet aligned in a shared latent space — scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so matching must not be run on raw counts You only need to predict labels of an unlabeled dataset using an existing tree (use scHPL's predict mode instead of progressive tree updating) Cell-type relationships are known to violate a tree structure, e.g. dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes

skills.description: Use when annotating unlabeled cancer scRNA-seq cells against the tumor microenvironment reference (113,976 cells, 13 cancer types) — e.g., MCC/CRC/LC datasets — and when major-type and subtype labels are both needed.
skills.name: hierarchical-two-step-cell-annotation
skills.search_text: hierarchical-two-step-cell-annotation Use when annotating unlabeled cancer scRNA-seq cells against the tumor microenvironment reference (113,976 cells, 13 cancer types) — e.g., MCC/CRC/LC datasets — and when major-type and subtype labels are both needed. Tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) are expected — scWizard may assign them to the Unknown cluster; a tissue-specific annotation method is preferable. Input data has not been quality-controlled — scWizard's default QC (<200 genes, >10,000 genes, >5% mitochondrial reads) should be applied or data checked with 'view quality' before annotation. The analysis goal is clustering or differential expression alone rather than cell-type classification — the Seurat-based Clustering module or 11 downstream analyses apply instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Two-step hierarchical cell-type annotation from scWizard: a deep neural network (ReLU/softmax, PCA on combined training+prediction data) first assigns each cell to one of 7 major tumor-microenvironment cell types, then Seurat subclustering plus a second DNN with majority-vote assignment refines cells into 47 subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Two-step hierarchical cell-type annotation from scWizard: a deep neural network (ReLU/softmax, PCA on combined training+prediction data) first assigns each cell to one of 7 major tumor-microenvironment cell types, then Seurat subclustering plus a second DNN with majority-vote assignment refines cells into 47 subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) are expected — scWizard may assign them to the Unknown cluster; a tissue-specific annotation method is preferable. Input data has not been quality-controlled — scWizard's default QC (<200 genes, >10,000 genes, >5% mitochondrial reads) should be applied or data checked with 'view quality' before annotation. The analysis goal is clustering or differential expression alone rather than cell-type classification — the Seurat-based Clustering module or 11 downstream analyses apply instead.

skills.description: Use when a classification tree (e.g. scHPL trained on multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets) has predicted labels for a held-out dataset and you need to quantify which cross-node and within-subtree misclassifications occur, as in the PBMC Bench10Xv3 evaluation.
skills.name: hierarchy-aware-confusion-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: hierarchy-aware-confusion-matrix-analysis Use when a classification tree (e.g. scHPL trained on multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets) has predicted labels for a held-out dataset and you need to quantify which cross-node and within-subtree misclassifications occur, as in the PBMC Bench10Xv3 evaluation. scHPL has not yet been applied — this skill evaluates tree predictions and requires an already-trained classification tree and predicted labels Datasets are not batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL requires datasets to be aligned (e.g. via Seurat v3, scVI, or scArches) before learning and prediction, so evaluation would be confounded by batch effects The task is a flat (non-hierarchical) cell-type classification where per-population confusions have no tree structure to exploit Evaluate cell-identity predictions from a hierarchical classifier (scHPL) by constructing a confusion matrix whose misclassification counts respect the tree's hierarchy boundaries, rather than treating all cell-population confusions as equally severe errors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Evaluate cell-identity predictions from a hierarchical classifier (scHPL) by constructing a confusion matrix whose misclassification counts respect the tree's hierarchy boundaries, rather than treating all cell-population confusions as equally severe errors.

skills.description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix (e.g., mouse olfactory bulb HDST from the Broad Single Cell Portal, SCP420) with 2D spatial coordinates and need to detect spatially variable genes or reconcile rank disagreements between SVG callers.
skills.name: high-definition-spatial-transcriptomics-analysis
skills.search_text: high-definition-spatial-transcriptomics-analysis Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix (e.g., mouse olfactory bulb HDST from the Broad Single Cell Portal, SCP420) with 2D spatial coordinates and need to detect spatially variable genes or reconcile rank disagreements between SVG callers. Comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type and knockout) are needed — singleCellHaystack cannot easily conduct multi-condition comparisons Results must integrate with cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analysis — singleCellHaystack output is not straightforward to incorporate into cluster-based DEG workflows Input genes are expected to be identified by cluster-vs-cluster differential expression rather than non-random spatial patterning of activity http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A workflow for identifying and cross-validating spatially variable genes (SVGs) in high-definition spatial transcriptomics data by running singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X on the same count matrix and 2D spatial coordinates, then comparing per-gene ranks and p-values side by side. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: A workflow for identifying and cross-validating spatially variable genes (SVGs) in high-definition spatial transcriptomics data by running singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X on the same count matrix and 2D spatial coordinates, then comparing per-gene ranks and p-values side by side.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type and knockout) are needed — singleCellHaystack cannot easily conduct multi-condition comparisons Results must integrate with cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analysis — singleCellHaystack output is not straightforward to incorporate into cluster-based DEG workflows Input genes are expected to be identified by cluster-vs-cluster differential expression rather than non-random spatial patterning of activity

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed, normalized scRNA-seq HVG expression matrix must be converted into a cell-to-cell graph (one node per cell, kNN edges) as input to graph-based contrastive learning or downstream imputation.
skills.name: high-dimensional-expression-matrix-neighborhood-search
skills.search_text: high-dimensional-expression-matrix-neighborhood-search Use when a pre-processed, normalized scRNA-seq HVG expression matrix must be converted into a cell-to-cell graph (one node per cell, kNN edges) as input to graph-based contrastive learning or downstream imputation. The expression matrix has not yet been normalized and restricted to highly variable genes — build it from the pre-processing filter output first The downstream method does not consume graph/topological structure over cells, so a kNN graph adds no benefit Only global cell-level statistics are needed (e.g. distribution fitting without graph contrastive learning); a full pairwise kNN graph is unnecessary overhead Constructs the cell graph for scGCL's graph contrastive learning by searching for k=15 nearest neighbors over the normalized HVG expression matrix using cosine distances. This preserves cell-to-cell topological relationships that existing scRNA-seq imputation methods ignore. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Constructs the cell graph for scGCL's graph contrastive learning by searching for k=15 nearest neighbors over the normalized HVG expression matrix using cosine distances. This preserves cell-to-cell topological relationships that existing scRNA-seq imputation methods ignore.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has not yet been normalized and restricted to highly variable genes — build it from the pre-processing filter output first The downstream method does not consume graph/topological structure over cells, so a kNN graph adds no benefit Only global cell-level statistics are needed (e.g. distribution fitting without graph contrastive learning); a full pairwise kNN graph is unnecessary overhead
