skills.search_text: hla-allele-typing-from-wes-reads Use when raw WES/WGS FASTQ reads of a tumor-normal pair must be typed for HLA class I alleles as a prerequisite step before peptide-MHC binding prediction (e.g., DeepHLApan) in a neoantigen discovery workflow. Input is already a sorted BAM/VCF or an annotated variant list with HLA types provided clinically (e.g., the TESLA clinical-grade HLA typing) — typing from reads is redundant Only HLA class II typing is needed — OptiType identifies HLA class I alleles Input is RNA-Seq-only without WES/WGS data and no support for the TSNAD WES/WGS mutation-calling modules is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Identify the HLA alleles of a patient from WES/WGS reads (with optional tumor RNA-Seq support) using OptiType 1.3.5 embedded in the TSNAD v2.0 one-stop pipeline, producing the patient-specific pMHC typing required for downstream neoantigen prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Identify the HLA alleles of a patient from WES/WGS reads (with optional tumor RNA-Seq support) using OptiType 1.3.5 embedded in the TSNAD v2.0 one-stop pipeline, producing the patient-specific pMHC typing required for downstream neoantigen prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a sorted BAM/VCF or an annotated variant list with HLA types provided clinically (e.g., the TESLA clinical-grade HLA typing) — typing from reads is redundant Only HLA class II typing is needed — OptiType identifies HLA class I alleles Input is RNA-Seq-only without WES/WGS data and no support for the TSNAD WES/WGS mutation-calling modules is intended

skills.description: Use when tumor-normal WES/WGS or RNA-Seq fastq files require patient-specific HLA class I genotyping as a prerequisite for neoantigen/pMHC binding prediction.
skills.name: hla-class-i-allele-typing
skills.search_text: hla-class-i-allele-typing Use when tumor-normal WES/WGS or RNA-Seq fastq files require patient-specific HLA class I genotyping as a prerequisite for neoantigen/pMHC binding prediction. Clinical-grade HLA typing is already available (as with the TESLA Synapse syn21048999 dataset), so in-pipeline OptiType typing is redundant The goal is HLA class II (e.g. HLA-DR/DQ/DP) typing — OptiType in TSNAD covers only HLA class I alleles The task is peptide-MHC binding/immunogenicity scoring rather than genotype determination — that is handled by the DeepHLApan module, not this typing step http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3120 Identify 4-digit HLA class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) alleles from tumor-normal sequencing reads using OptiType v1.3.5, as embedded in the TSNAD v2.0.1 neoantigen prediction pipeline, so that downstream DeepHLApan peptide-MHC predictions use patient-specific HLA genotypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Identify 4-digit HLA class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) alleles from tumor-normal sequencing reads using OptiType v1.3.5, as embedded in the TSNAD v2.0.1 neoantigen prediction pipeline, so that downstream DeepHLApan peptide-MHC predictions use patient-specific HLA genotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clinical-grade HLA typing is already available (as with the TESLA Synapse syn21048999 dataset), so in-pipeline OptiType typing is redundant The goal is HLA class II (e.g. HLA-DR/DQ/DP) typing — OptiType in TSNAD covers only HLA class I alleles The task is peptide-MHC binding/immunogenicity scoring rather than genotype determination — that is handled by the DeepHLApan module, not this typing step

skills.description: Use when running ScanNeo2's prioritization stage: before submitting peptide-binding prediction jobs, confirm the requested MHC class(es) and allele lists match the HLA genotyping results (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv).
skills.name: hla-genotype-subset-validation
skills.search_text: hla-genotype-subset-validation Use when running ScanNeo2's prioritization stage: before submitting peptide-binding prediction jobs, confirm the requested MHC class(es) and allele lists match the HLA genotyping results (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv). No HLA genotyping results exist yet for the sample — run Optitype/HLA-HD typing first; this skill only validates an already-typed allele set. You intend to predict binding for HLA alleles outside the patient's typed genotype (e.g. a fixed allele panel) — ScanNeo2's prioritization explicitly restricts prediction to hlatyping.class outputs. You need MHC-II epitope lengths beyond the implemented 13–15-mers (the article describes 13–25-mers for MHC class II, but the workflow restricts extraction to 13,14,15). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A guard step in ScanNeo2's prioritization stage that verifies the configured prediction MHC classes (and every submitted HLA allele) are a strict subset of the alleles actually typed by Optitype (class I) and HLA-HD (class II), before any netMHCpan/netMHCIIpan jobs are launched. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: A guard step in ScanNeo2's prioritization stage that verifies the configured prediction MHC classes (and every submitted HLA allele) are a strict subset of the alleles actually typed by Optitype (class I) and HLA-HD (class II), before any netMHCpan/netMHCIIpan jobs are launched.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No HLA genotyping results exist yet for the sample — run Optitype/HLA-HD typing first; this skill only validates an already-typed allele set. You intend to predict binding for HLA alleles outside the patient's typed genotype (e.g. a fixed allele panel) — ScanNeo2's prioritization explicitly restricts prediction to hlatyping.class outputs. You need MHC-II epitope lengths beyond the implemented 13–15-mers (the article describes 13–25-mers for MHC class II, but the workflow restricts extraction to 13,14,15).

skills.description: Use when a neoantigen workflow must genotype HLA alleles from tumor samples using one or more read sources (DNA-seq, RNA-seq, or user-supplied allele files), with class-specific tool dispatch and merged multi-source allele output.
skills.name: hla-read-source-mode-merging
skills.search_text: hla-read-source-mode-merging Use when a neoantigen workflow must genotype HLA alleles from tumor samples using one or more read sources (DNA-seq, RNA-seq, or user-supplied allele files), with class-specific tool dispatch and merged multi-source allele output. Normal-sample rows should not be fed into HLA typing — the workflow excludes rows with type 'normal' by design. If HLA alleles are already known and provided as custom files only, running read-based DNA/RNA genotyping (yara/OptiType/HLA-HD) is unnecessary overhead. Do not attempt class II genotyping from DNA or RNA reads when the HLA-HD reference data (freq_data, split, dict) or hlahd.sh is missing — the workflow emits a '[config error]' at load time instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configures and merges HLA genotyping results across multiple read sources (DNA, RNA, custom allele files) in ScanNeo2, dispatching class I typing to OptiType (yara-filtered reads) and class II typing to HLA-HD, and writing per-source allele rows to mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Configures and merges HLA genotyping results across multiple read sources (DNA, RNA, custom allele files) in ScanNeo2, dispatching class I typing to OptiType (yara-filtered reads) and class II typing to HLA-HD, and writing per-source allele rows to mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Normal-sample rows should not be fed into HLA typing — the workflow excludes rows with type 'normal' by design. If HLA alleles are already known and provided as custom files only, running read-based DNA/RNA genotyping (yara/OptiType/HLA-HD) is unnecessary overhead. Do not attempt class II genotyping from DNA or RNA reads when the HLA-HD reference data (freq_data, split, dict) or hlahd.sh is missing — the workflow emits a '[config error]' at load time instead.

skills.description: Use when tumor SNV/INDEL calls (e.g., from GATK Mutect2) and patient WES/RNA-Seq data are available and HLA-typed peptide-MHC immunogenicity prediction is needed.
skills.name: hla-typed-peptide-prediction
skills.search_text: hla-typed-peptide-prediction Use when tumor SNV/INDEL calls (e.g., from GATK Mutect2) and patient WES/RNA-Seq data are available and HLA-typed peptide-MHC immunogenicity prediction is needed. Input lacks patient HLA typing — OptiType alleles are required to pair peptides with MHC Goal is TCR-pMHC interaction prediction — the article notes TCR-pMHC binding prediction is a planned future feature, not included Variants lie in unexpressed genes — the expression filter removes neoantigens from genes with TPM < 1, so RNA-Seq expression data should be available http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Predict candidate neoantigenic peptide-MHC pairs by combining patient HLA alleles (OptiType) with mutant peptides extracted after VEP annotation, scored by DeepHLApan for both binding and immunogenicity within TSNAD v2.0. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Predict candidate neoantigenic peptide-MHC pairs by combining patient HLA alleles (OptiType) with mutant peptides extracted after VEP annotation, scored by DeepHLApan for both binding and immunogenicity within TSNAD v2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks patient HLA typing — OptiType alleles are required to pair peptides with MHC Goal is TCR-pMHC interaction prediction — the article notes TCR-pMHC binding prediction is a planned future feature, not included Variants lie in unexpressed genes — the expression filter removes neoantigens from genes with TPM < 1, so RNA-Seq expression data should be available

skills.description: Use when a compositional scRNA-seq dataset (cell counts per sample) has been set up with sccoda's CompositionalAnalysis model and credible cell-type abundance effects must be estimated via posterior inference with sample_hmc().
skills.name: hmc-posterior-sampling
skills.search_text: hmc-posterior-sampling Use when a compositional scRNA-seq dataset (cell counts per sample) has been set up with sccoda's CompositionalAnalysis model and credible cell-type abundance effects must be estimated via posterior inference with sample_hmc(). When the data are not compositional per-sample cell counts, e.g. already summarized feature tables without a sample-level covariate design When sample-level response variability or donor heterogeneity must be modeled — scCODA does not model response variability within a condition and cannot detect heterogeneities between samples When the log-linear relationship between covariates and cell abundance is likely mis-specified for the system under study http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) posterior inference step of the scCODA Bayesian compositional model, which samples the posterior of the Dirichlet-Multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to estimate covariate effects on cell-type proportions from scRNA-seq cell counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) posterior inference step of the scCODA Bayesian compositional model, which samples the posterior of the Dirichlet-Multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to estimate covariate effects on cell-type proportions from scRNA-seq cell counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are not compositional per-sample cell counts, e.g. already summarized feature tables without a sample-level covariate design When sample-level response variability or donor heterogeneity must be modeled — scCODA does not model response variability within a condition and cannot detect heterogeneities between samples When the log-linear relationship between covariates and cell abundance is likely mis-specified for the system under study

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive vs drug-resistant HMCL pairs (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) must be screened for subclonal enrichment of drug-target genes to prioritize combination therapy candidates.
skills.name: hmcl-drug-resistance-expression-profiling
skills.search_text: hmcl-drug-resistance-expression-profiling Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive vs drug-resistant HMCL pairs (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) must be screened for subclonal enrichment of drug-target genes to prioritize combination therapy candidates. The goal is in silico prediction of secDrug candidates from pharmacogenomics data via the greedy set cover algorithm, not single-cell target-gene screening of a predicted combination. Input is bulk RNA-seq transcriptome data rather than single-cell count matrices; subclonal cluster-level enrichment cannot be computed. Validation requires functional/ex vivo assays (CRISPR editing, CyTOF on primary bone marrow cells) — this skill only screens candidate combinations, it does not confirm efficacy. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that profiles drug-target gene enrichment across subclonal clusters of human myeloma cell lines (HMCLs) to prioritize secDrug combination candidates such as 17-AAG + FK866. It translates target-gene expression (HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 for 17-AAG, NAMPT for FK866) into ranked combination evidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41408-022-00636-2
skills.summary: A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that profiles drug-target gene enrichment across subclonal clusters of human myeloma cell lines (HMCLs) to prioritize secDrug combination candidates such as 17-AAG + FK866. It translates target-gene expression (HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 for 17-AAG, NAMPT for FK866) into ranked combination evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is in silico prediction of secDrug candidates from pharmacogenomics data via the greedy set cover algorithm, not single-cell target-gene screening of a predicted combination. Input is bulk RNA-seq transcriptome data rather than single-cell count matrices; subclonal cluster-level enrichment cannot be computed. Validation requires functional/ex vivo assays (CRISPR editing, CyTOF on primary bone marrow cells) — this skill only screens candidate combinations, it does not confirm efficacy.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to infer CNV/LOH events from raw RNA-seq signal profiles (bulk or single-cell) without a high-quality heterozygous SNV call set, e.g., tumor scRNA-seq clonal architecture questions.
skills.name: hmm-based-copy-number-segmentation
skills.search_text: hmm-based-copy-number-segmentation Use when the goal is to infer CNV/LOH events from raw RNA-seq signal profiles (bulk or single-cell) without a high-quality heterozygous SNV call set, e.g., tumor scRNA-seq clonal architecture questions. The goal is transcriptomic analysis only and no CNV/LOH inference is needed — the skill probes the genomic landscape, not expression signatures per se. Input data are already curated CNV calls or a feature table of copy numbers rather than raw RNA-seq signal profiles needing segmentation. Only 3′-end (e.g., DropSeq-style) data with very sparse variants are available and no pooling is possible, since BAF shift signal may be adversely impacted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Segment genome-wide RNA-seq signal into copy-number states with CaSpER's Hidden Markov Model, which runs on all multiscale-smoothed expression scales and integrates BAF allele-shift states to call focal and large-scale CNVs from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Segment genome-wide RNA-seq signal into copy-number states with CaSpER's Hidden Markov Model, which runs on all multiscale-smoothed expression scales and integrates BAF allele-shift states to call focal and large-scale CNVs from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is transcriptomic analysis only and no CNV/LOH inference is needed — the skill probes the genomic landscape, not expression signatures per se. Input data are already curated CNV calls or a feature table of copy numbers rather than raw RNA-seq signal profiles needing segmentation. Only 3′-end (e.g., DropSeq-style) data with very sparse variants are available and no pooling is possible, since BAF shift signal may be adversely impacted.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq must be analyzed without a high-quality gene annotation: STAR- or CellRanger-aligned read alignments are available and genome-wide transcribed regions (TARs) must be predicted de novo from read coverage.
skills.name: hmm-based-transcribed-region-prediction
skills.search_text: hmm-based-transcribed-region-prediction Use when scRNA-seq must be analyzed without a high-quality gene annotation: STAR- or CellRanger-aligned read alignments are available and genome-wide transcribed regions (TARs) must be predicted de novo from read coverage. A high-quality genome annotation already exists and the analysis only needs standard gene-level quantification — the TAR-discovery stage is designed for annotation-independent analysis Input is a single-cell expression matrix rather than a genome alignment; groHMM requires per-bin read coverage along the genome, so re-running this skill on a matrix is meaningless Per-cell resolution is required at this stage — this step intentionally discards cell barcodes to build a combined genome-level track http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotation-free identification of transcriptionally active regions (TARs) from scRNA-seq alignments using groHMM's two-state hidden Markov model (transcribed vs. untranscribed), followed by merging, coverage filtering, and refFlat output for downstream single-cell TAR expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Annotation-free identification of transcriptionally active regions (TARs) from scRNA-seq alignments using groHMM's two-state hidden Markov model (transcribed vs. untranscribed), followed by merging, coverage filtering, and refFlat output for downstream single-cell TAR expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A high-quality genome annotation already exists and the analysis only needs standard gene-level quantification — the TAR-discovery stage is designed for annotation-independent analysis Input is a single-cell expression matrix rather than a genome alignment; groHMM requires per-bin read coverage along the genome, so re-running this skill on a matrix is meaningless Per-cell resolution is required at this stage — this step intentionally discards cell barcodes to build a combined genome-level track

skills.description: Use when you have an ordered single-cell pseudo time-series (e.g., reCAT ordIndex from consensus-TSP) with Bayes/mean scores and need to assign each cell to a cell cycle stage such as G1, S, or G2/M.
skills.name: hmm-cell-cycle-phase-segmentation
skills.search_text: hmm-cell-cycle-phase-segmentation Use when you have an ordered single-cell pseudo time-series (e.g., reCAT ordIndex from consensus-TSP) with Bayes/mean scores and need to assign each cell to a cell cycle stage such as G1, S, or G2/M. The goal is de novo trajectory inference on non-cyclic processes (e.g. differentiation ordering) where methods like Monocle, TSCAN, Wanderlust/Wishbone, SCUBA or DPT are the appropriate baselines Expression values are not on the log2(TPM+1) scale and have not been filtered to cell-cycle base genes, since get_hmm_order requires the standard reCAT input Only a single marker gene is available to call cell cycle stage, which the paper shows is insufficient to give reliable stage information in scRNA-seq data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Segments unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq data into cell cycle phases (G1, S, G2/M, or G0/G1/S/G2/M) using reCAT's hidden Markov model driven by two scores — Bayes-scores and mean-scores — computed along the recovered pseudo time-series order. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Segments unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq data into cell cycle phases (G1, S, G2/M, or G0/G1/S/G2/M) using reCAT's hidden Markov model driven by two scores — Bayes-scores and mean-scores — computed along the recovered pseudo time-series order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo trajectory inference on non-cyclic processes (e.g. differentiation ordering) where methods like Monocle, TSCAN, Wanderlust/Wishbone, SCUBA or DPT are the appropriate baselines Expression values are not on the log2(TPM+1) scale and have not been filtered to cell-cycle base genes, since get_hmm_order requires the standard reCAT input Only a single marker gene is available to call cell cycle stage, which the paper shows is insufficient to give reliable stage information in scRNA-seq data

skills.description: Use when calling per-gene, per-cell copy-number states from sparse, low-coverage scRNA-seq read-depth (RDR) or B-allele-frequency (BAF) matrices where raw signals are too noisy and need smoothing on gene-coordinate and cell-neighborhood graphs.
skills.name: hmm-knn-cna-state-smoothing
skills.search_text: hmm-knn-cna-state-smoothing Use when calling per-gene, per-cell copy-number states from sparse, low-coverage scRNA-seq read-depth (RDR) or B-allele-frequency (BAF) matrices where raw signals are too noisy and need smoothing on gene-coordinate and cell-neighborhood graphs. Input is already a smoothed CNA probability tensor or combined XClone output (combine_Xdata.h5ad) — re-smoothing would double-count neighborhood information Data are bulk or pseudo-bulk (e.g., Numbat-style aggregated clones) where single-cell KNN smoothing over cells is not applicable No reference/normal cells are available to anchor the RDR normalization (ref_celltype undefined) http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 XClone's orthogonal smoothing strategy for CNA-state inference from scRNA-seq: hidden Markov model smoothing along genome coordinates (horizontal) combined with KNN cell-cell connectivity graph smoothing (vertical), applied to both the RDR and BAF modules to strengthen noisy read-depth and allelic-imbalance signals before combining them into haplotype-aware CNA calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: XClone's orthogonal smoothing strategy for CNA-state inference from scRNA-seq: hidden Markov model smoothing along genome coordinates (horizontal) combined with KNN cell-cell connectivity graph smoothing (vertical), applied to both the RDR and BAF modules to strengthen noisy read-depth and allelic-imbalance signals before combining them into haplotype-aware CNA calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a smoothed CNA probability tensor or combined XClone output (combine_Xdata.h5ad) — re-smoothing would double-count neighborhood information Data are bulk or pseudo-bulk (e.g., Numbat-style aggregated clones) where single-cell KNN smoothing over cells is not applicable No reference/normal cells are available to anchor the RDR normalization (ref_celltype undefined)

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQs must be analyzed without relying on a complete gene annotation — e.g., to quantify reads falling outside GENCODE/refFlat gene bodies in less-studied organisms (lemur, mole rat, sea urchin).
skills.name: hmm-transcribed-region-calling-from-sc-rna-seq
skills.search_text: hmm-transcribed-region-calling-from-sc-rna-seq Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQs must be analyzed without relying on a complete gene annotation — e.g., to quantify reads falling outside GENCODE/refFlat gene bodies in less-studied organisms (lemur, mole rat, sea urchin). Input is already aligned — use the from_cellranger workflow (cellranger count output) instead of re-running from FASTQs The organism has a high-quality, complete annotation and the goal is standard gene-level quantification rather than discovery of transcription outside annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Call transcriptionally active regions (TARs) genome-wide from scRNA-seq data using a groHMM hidden Markov model that classifies the genome into transcribed and untranscribed states, then split TARs into annotated (aTARs) and unannotated (uTARs) against refFlat annotations to quantify transcriptional dark matter. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Call transcriptionally active regions (TARs) genome-wide from scRNA-seq data using a groHMM hidden Markov model that classifies the genome into transcribed and untranscribed states, then split TARs into annotated (aTARs) and unannotated (uTARs) against refFlat annotations to quantify transcriptional dark matter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aligned — use the from_cellranger workflow (cellranger count output) instead of re-running from FASTQs The organism has a high-quality, complete annotation and the goal is standard gene-level quantification rather than discovery of transcription outside annotation

skills.description: Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics sections (e.g. Visium DLPFC or seqFISH embryo sections) need joint spatial-domain clustering with simultaneous batch-effect estimation over a grid of cluster numbers K.
skills.name: hmrf-spatial-clustering-model-fitting
skills.search_text: hmrf-spatial-clustering-model-fitting Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics sections (e.g. Visium DLPFC or seqFISH embryo sections) need joint spatial-domain clustering with simultaneous batch-effect estimation over a grid of cluster numbers K. Data are not spatially resolved or no spot/cell adjacency can be defined (CreateNeighbors cannot be applied), since the model is a hidden Markov random field over spatial neighborhoods. Only a single sample with no batch structure is being analyzed — the single-sample empirical-Bayes HMRF predecessor SC.MEB is the appropriate tool. Input is raw count matrices without dimensionality reduction; the model requires low-dimensional representations (e.g. npcs=15 ACA/APCA embeddings), not full-gene expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a hidden-Markov-random-field spatial clustering model with empirical Bayes (iSC.MEB) to jointly estimate cluster labels and batch-related embeddings across multiple SRT sections, using ICM-EM inference and MBIC cluster-number selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Fits a hidden-Markov-random-field spatial clustering model with empirical Bayes (iSC.MEB) to jointly estimate cluster labels and batch-related embeddings across multiple SRT sections, using ICM-EM inference and MBIC cluster-number selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not spatially resolved or no spot/cell adjacency can be defined (CreateNeighbors cannot be applied), since the model is a hidden Markov random field over spatial neighborhoods. Only a single sample with no batch structure is being analyzed — the single-sample empirical-Bayes HMRF predecessor SC.MEB is the appropriate tool. Input is raw count matrices without dimensionality reduction; the model requires low-dimensional representations (e.g. npcs=15 ACA/APCA embeddings), not full-gene expression.

skills.description: Use when training or validating the Forseti oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP on labeled priming windows and you need held-out generalization accuracies on training, hold-out, and test scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.name: hold-out-classification-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: hold-out-classification-accuracy-evaluation Use when training or validating the Forseti oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP on labeled priming windows and you need held-out generalization accuracies on training, hold-out, and test scRNA-seq datasets. The goal is predicting splicing status of scRNA-seq reads on a new dataset rather than training/evaluating the binding-affinity model — use the full Forseti prediction workflow (spliceu index, STAR alignment, forseti_predictor) instead Primed transcripts lack labeled priming windows with a valid adenine single-nucleotide repeat of length >= 6, so no valid training or hold-out windows can be extracted You need splicing-status prediction quality metrics (e.g., AUC on simulated or experimental reads) rather than binding-affinity classification accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains the Forseti oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP on labeled priming windows from scRNA-seq training datasets and evaluates generalization via per-dataset 1000-example hold-out sets and two held-out test datasets, reporting mean classification accuracies (~0.83 train, ~0.84 hold-out, ~0.89 test). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Trains the Forseti oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP on labeled priming windows from scRNA-seq training datasets and evaluates generalization via per-dataset 1000-example hold-out sets and two held-out test datasets, reporting mean classification accuracies (~0.83 train, ~0.84 hold-out, ~0.89 test).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is predicting splicing status of scRNA-seq reads on a new dataset rather than training/evaluating the binding-affinity model — use the full Forseti prediction workflow (spliceu index, STAR alignment, forseti_predictor) instead Primed transcripts lack labeled priming windows with a valid adenine single-nucleotide repeat of length >= 6, so no valid training or hold-out windows can be extracted You need splicing-status prediction quality metrics (e.g., AUC on simulated or experimental reads) rather than binding-affinity classification accuracy

skills.description: Use when ground-truth cell-type labels are available for only a fraction of cells in an scRNA-seq dataset and you want to convert them into soft pairwise constraints for semi-supervised clustering with scDCC.
skills.name: hold-out-label-sampling
skills.search_text: hold-out-label-sampling Use when ground-truth cell-type labels are available for only a fraction of cells in an scRNA-seq dataset and you want to convert them into soft pairwise constraints for semi-supervised clustering with scDCC. No partial labels or prior cell-type knowledge exist for the dataset, since the constraints must be derived from a labeled hold-out set Prior knowledge is limited to marker genes and predefined cell types — the paper notes CellAssign/SCINA-style marker-based approaches are a different paradigm than soft pairwise constraints Hard-constrained clustering is required (e.g., COP-K-means-style guarantees); scDCC deliberately treats constraints as soft penalty terms http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Sample must-link and cannot-link pairwise constraints from a small labeled hold-out set (10% of cells) to inject partial domain knowledge into scDCC's constrained clustering loss on scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3
skills.summary: Sample must-link and cannot-link pairwise constraints from a small labeled hold-out set (10% of cells) to inject partial domain knowledge into scDCC's constrained clustering loss on scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No partial labels or prior cell-type knowledge exist for the dataset, since the constraints must be derived from a labeled hold-out set Prior knowledge is limited to marker genes and predefined cell types — the paper notes CellAssign/SCINA-style marker-based approaches are a different paradigm than soft pairwise constraints Hard-constrained clustering is required (e.g., COP-K-means-style guarantees); scDCC deliberately treats constraints as soft penalty terms

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset has one matrix held out as a test set and you must compare methods that predict the unseen condition/batch combination using per-cell-type prediction accuracy.
skills.name: holdout-batch-prediction-scoring
skills.search_text: holdout-batch-prediction-scoring Use when a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset has one matrix held out as a test set and you must compare methods that predict the unseen condition/batch combination using per-cell-type prediction accuracy. Each batch of cells was measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to fully disentangle the batch and condition effect, so held-out batch predictions are not well-posed The goal is batch effect removal or condition-associated key gene detection rather than perturbation prediction accuracy comparison against baselines Baselines cannot be trained on identical training matrices, so the accuracy comparison would not be fair http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A benchmarking skill for perturbation prediction on multi-batch scRNA-seq data: hold out one count matrix (e.g., GBM matrix PW034-705), train scDisInFact against scGen and scPreGAN baselines, and score held-out condition/batch predictions with cell-type-specific accuracy metrics (MSE, Pearson, R2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for perturbation prediction on multi-batch scRNA-seq data: hold out one count matrix (e.g., GBM matrix PW034-705), train scDisInFact against scGen and scPreGAN baselines, and score held-out condition/batch predictions with cell-type-specific accuracy metrics (MSE, Pearson, R2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch of cells was measured under only one condition — there is not enough information to fully disentangle the batch and condition effect, so held-out batch predictions are not well-posed The goal is batch effect removal or condition-associated key gene detection rather than perturbation prediction accuracy comparison against baselines Baselines cannot be trained on identical training matrices, so the accuracy comparison would not be fair

skills.description: Use when quantifying whether adding supervision (pairwise must-link/cannot-link constraints from a labeled hold-out) consistently improves scRNA-seq clustering across incrementally varied parameter levels.
skills.name: holdout-benchmark-repetition
skills.search_text: holdout-benchmark-repetition Use when quantifying whether adding supervision (pairwise must-link/cannot-link constraints from a labeled hold-out) consistently improves scRNA-seq clustering across incrementally varied parameter levels. The dataset has no partial cell-type labels from which must-link/cannot-link constraints can be built The goal is purely unsupervised clustering without evaluating the benefit of integrating prior/domain knowledge Only a single training run per setting is affordable — single-run scores are unreliable versus the ten-repeat mean protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a clustering method by holding out a labeled fraction of cells to generate supervision signals, sweeping a parameter (e.g., number of pairwise constraints from 0 to 6000) and repeating over ten random splits to report mean NMI, CA, and ARI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3
skills.summary: Benchmark a clustering method by holding out a labeled fraction of cells to generate supervision signals, sweeping a parameter (e.g., number of pairwise constraints from 0 to 6000) and repeating over ten random splits to report mean NMI, CA, and ARI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no partial cell-type labels from which must-link/cannot-link constraints can be built The goal is purely unsupervised clustering without evaluating the benefit of integrating prior/domain knowledge Only a single training run per setting is affordable — single-run scores are unreliable versus the ten-repeat mean protocol

skills.description: Use when a trained ProjectSVR ensemble SVR model (m=8000 subsample, t=10 median-aggregated models) must be validated before release or reuse, by scoring held-out reference cells and checking prediction accuracy against reference embeddings.
skills.name: holdout-embedding-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: holdout-embedding-accuracy-evaluation Use when a trained ProjectSVR ensemble SVR model (m=8000 subsample, t=10 median-aggregated models) must be validated before release or reuse, by scoring held-out reference cells and checking prediction accuracy against reference embeddings. Evaluating projection of query cells whose gene expression comes from a different platform (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) — performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth Query data may contain novel cell states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, so compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results instead The task is cell-type annotation rather than embedding accuracy — use ProjectSVR's ensemble SVM classifier (LabelTransfer) instead of SVR coordinate regression http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates a ProjectSVR ensemble-SVR reference mapping model by predicting low-dimensional reference embeddings (e.g. UMAP_1/2) for held-out reference cells and comparing predicted vs. reference coordinates, to confirm the gene-set-score-to-embedding regression recovers the reference structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Evaluates a ProjectSVR ensemble-SVR reference mapping model by predicting low-dimensional reference embeddings (e.g. UMAP_1/2) for held-out reference cells and comparing predicted vs. reference coordinates, to confirm the gene-set-score-to-embedding regression recovers the reference structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating projection of query cells whose gene expression comes from a different platform (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) — performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth Query data may contain novel cell states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, so compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results instead The task is cell-type annotation rather than embedding accuracy — use ProjectSVR's ensemble SVM classifier (LabelTransfer) instead of SVR coordinate regression

skills.description: Use when benchmarking protein-imputation from paired CITE-seq RNA/ADT data requires a random cell-level train/test split, with model selection on testing error and per-protein correlation reporting.
skills.name: holdout-train-test-split-validation
skills.search_text: holdout-train-test-split-validation Use when benchmarking protein-imputation from paired CITE-seq RNA/ADT data requires a random cell-level train/test split, with model selection on testing error and per-protein correlation reporting. Prediction for cell types absent from training data — use the out-of-cell-type scheme that partitions cells by cell type and holds out all cells of one type instead of a random split Non-UMI expression input such as TPM or RPKM — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input Cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the paper states imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried there http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates surface-protein imputation methods by randomly holding out 10% of cells as a testing set and training on the remaining 90%, then comparing per-protein Pearson correlations of imputed abundances against raw and SAVER-X-denoised RNA baselines. This is the paper's 90/10 random holdout scheme for validating cTP-net on CITE-seq PBMC data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Evaluates surface-protein imputation methods by randomly holding out 10% of cells as a testing set and training on the remaining 90%, then comparing per-protein Pearson correlations of imputed abundances against raw and SAVER-X-denoised RNA baselines. This is the paper's 90/10 random holdout scheme for validating cTP-net on CITE-seq PBMC data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prediction for cell types absent from training data — use the out-of-cell-type scheme that partitions cells by cell type and holds out all cells of one type instead of a random split Non-UMI expression input such as TPM or RPKM — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) expression input Cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the paper states imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried there

skills.description: Use when two paired single-cell count matrices (t=0/t=1, genes-as-rows) are available and a neural ODE forecaster must be quantitatively compared to an MLP baseline via held-out MSE at t=1 and recursive multi-step forecasts.
skills.name: holdout-validation-mse-benchmarking
skills.search_text: holdout-validation-mse-benchmarking Use when two paired single-cell count matrices (t=0/t=1, genes-as-rows) are available and a neural ODE forecaster must be quantitatively compared to an MLP baseline via held-out MSE at t=1 and recursive multi-step forecasts. No paired two-time-point counts for the same cells exist — standard scRNA-seq protocols destroy the cell, so RNAForecaster training and this benchmark cannot be applied Goal is purely cell ordering or embedding-space trajectory inference rather than gene-dimensional forward forecasting with an accuracy benchmark Only one trained model is of interest and no baseline comparison is needed — a single-model validation does not require this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a neural ODE forecaster (RNAForecaster) against a five-hidden-layer MLP by comparing held-out validation MSE at the trained time step (t=1) and over 50 recursive future prediction steps, using paired two-time-point BoolODE simulated single-cell count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Benchmark a neural ODE forecaster (RNAForecaster) against a five-hidden-layer MLP by comparing held-out validation MSE at the trained time step (t=1) and over 50 recursive future prediction steps, using paired two-time-point BoolODE simulated single-cell count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired two-time-point counts for the same cells exist — standard scRNA-seq protocols destroy the cell, so RNAForecaster training and this benchmark cannot be applied Goal is purely cell ordering or embedding-space trajectory inference rather than gene-dimensional forward forecasting with an accuracy benchmark Only one trained model is of interest and no baseline comparison is needed — a single-model validation does not require this skill

skills.search_text: homogeneity-completeness-vmeasure-computation Use when a partitioned clustering solution must be scored against a known ground-truth labeling (e.g. Splatter-simulated c1–c5 populations), and per-method Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure comparisons across competing methods are needed. No ground-truth labeling exists — Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure are external metrics requiring a reference partition; use internal stability scores (reassign, TFIDF5/TFIDF10, SCCAF) instead Comparing soft/probabilistic cluster assignments rather than one definitive label per cell (the binary assignment matrix X of shape I * N assumption does not hold) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes external clustering validity metrics — Homogeneity (H(C|K)), Completeness (H(K|C)), and their harmonic mean (V-Measure) — to benchmark a reconciliation method (scTriangulate) against ensemble clustering baselines (HGPA, MCLA, HBGF) on a simulated ground-truth clustering (Splatter clusters c1–c5). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y

skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth labeling exists — Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure are external metrics requiring a reference partition; use internal stability scores (reassign, TFIDF5/TFIDF10, SCCAF) instead Comparing soft/probabilistic cluster assignments rather than one definitive label per cell (the binary assignment matrix X of shape I * N assumption does not hold)

skills.description: Use when per-orthogroup gene trees and species-membership tables are available and you need to screen orthogroups for lineage gaps between the LCA gene age class and the focal species, i.e. candidate HGT.
skills.name: horizontal-gene-transfer-flagging
skills.search_text: horizontal-gene-transfer-flagging Use when per-orthogroup gene trees and species-membership tables are available and you need to screen orthogroups for lineage gaps between the LCA gene age class and the focal species, i.e. candidate HGT. You only need the gene age (LCA) assignment itself — use oggmap's of2orthomap orthomap extraction rather than the continuity/HGT screen Orthogroup gene trees or per-orthogroup species-membership tables are unavailable, so intermediate-node completeness cannot be evaluated The query species has no LCA-to-focal-species path resolvable in the NCBI taxonomy lineage (e.g. unresolved lineage), making node-wise completeness undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Computes an optional per-orthogroup continuity score quantifying species completeness along tree nodes from the LCA to the focal species (e.g. Danio rerio), so that intermediate nodes lacking detectable orthologs can be flagged as candidate horizontal gene transfer events. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Computes an optional per-orthogroup continuity score quantifying species completeness along tree nodes from the LCA to the focal species (e.g. Danio rerio), so that intermediate nodes lacking detectable orthologs can be flagged as candidate horizontal gene transfer events.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the gene age (LCA) assignment itself — use oggmap's of2orthomap orthomap extraction rather than the continuity/HGT screen Orthogroup gene trees or per-orthogroup species-membership tables are unavailable, so intermediate-node completeness cannot be evaluated The query species has no LCA-to-focal-species path resolvable in the NCBI taxonomy lineage (e.g. unresolved lineage), making node-wise completeness undefined

skills.description: Use when assessing whether TWAS test statistics at tagging genes are inflated by horizontal pleiotropy through linkage, or when building a null ensemble of TWAS Z-scores/p-values under a model where GWAS effects are independent of eQTLs.
skills.name: horizontal-pleiotropy-gwas-effect-simulation
skills.search_text: horizontal-pleiotropy-gwas-effect-simulation Use when assessing whether TWAS test statistics at tagging genes are inflated by horizontal pleiotropy through linkage, or when building a null ensemble of TWAS Z-scores/p-values under a model where GWAS effects are independent of eQTLs. The goal is power analysis under the causal TWAS model where expression mediates the trait (alpha != 0) — use the causal simulation mode instead of --indep-gwas, since --indep-gwas generates GWAS effects independently of eQTLs by design Input is real GWAS summary statistics rather than simulated genotypes/traits — twas_sim simulates from PLINK reference genotypes and cannot ingest existing GWAS results Evaluating prediction-weight accuracy of eQTL models (LASSO, ENet, GBLUP, SuSiE) rather than null-model FWER calibration — the pleiotropy mode conflates tagging-gene tests and is not a clean comparison of weight quality http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Simulate GWAS effect sizes independently of eQTL effects using twas_sim's --indep-gwas mode, which models horizontal pleiotropy through linkage and is used to quantify FWER inflation at tagging genes in TWAS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad288
skills.summary: Simulate GWAS effect sizes independently of eQTL effects using twas_sim's --indep-gwas mode, which models horizontal pleiotropy through linkage and is used to quantify FWER inflation at tagging genes in TWAS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is power analysis under the causal TWAS model where expression mediates the trait (alpha != 0) — use the causal simulation mode instead of --indep-gwas, since --indep-gwas generates GWAS effects independently of eQTLs by design Input is real GWAS summary statistics rather than simulated genotypes/traits — twas_sim simulates from PLINK reference genotypes and cannot ingest existing GWAS results Evaluating prediction-weight accuracy of eQTL models (LASSO, ENet, GBLUP, SuSiE) rather than null-model FWER calibration — the pleiotropy mode conflates tagging-gene tests and is not a clean comparison of weight quality

skills.description: Use when you have context-specific host metabolic models with a viral biomass reaction and need to find gene knockouts that reduce viral growth (grRatio < 0.2) without compromising host biomass.
skills.name: host-pathogen-essential-gene-identification
skills.search_text: host-pathogen-essential-gene-identification Use when you have context-specific host metabolic models with a viral biomass reaction and need to find gene knockouts that reduce viral growth (grRatio < 0.2) without compromising host biomass. You only have the generic reconstruction (Recon2.04/Recon3D_01) without expression data — context-specific models built with rFASTCORMICS are required for cell-line-relevant essentiality calls The models lack a viral biomass objective function — knockout of host genes against a host-only biomass objective identifies host-essential rather than viral-specific targets The goal is direct antiviral docking against the viral proteome — this approach models the virus only through its biomass function, so targets arise from host metabolome network effects http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Identifies host genes essential for viral biomass production in SARS-CoV-2-infected lung cells by running in silico single-gene deletion (FBA) on context-specific metabolic models reconstructed with rFASTCORMICS and carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Identifies host genes essential for viral biomass production in SARS-CoV-2-infected lung cells by running in silico single-gene deletion (FBA) on context-specific metabolic models reconstructed with rFASTCORMICS and carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have the generic reconstruction (Recon2.04/Recon3D_01) without expression data — context-specific models built with rFASTCORMICS are required for cell-line-relevant essentiality calls The models lack a viral biomass objective function — knockout of host genes against a host-only biomass objective identifies host-essential rather than viral-specific targets The goal is direct antiviral docking against the viral proteome — this approach models the virus only through its biomass function, so targets arise from host metabolome network effects

skills.name: host-read-filtering
skills.search_text: host-read-filtering Use when RNA-seq reads (e.g., TCGA tumor BAMs) must be stripped of host and contaminant signal before viral read detection, i.e., when you need *_unmapped.fastq inputs for an alignment-free viral caller like viRNAtrap. skills.summary: Extract unmapped RNA-seq reads by aligning paired-end reads from TCGA/GDC BAM files against the hg19 human reference and the phiX phage (NC_001422) contaminant reference using Bowtie2, producing combined *_unmapped.fastq files that serve as the input to viRNAtrap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a *_unmapped.fastq file produced by an upstream host-alignment step — do not re-filter, just pass it to viRNAtrap RNA-seq data from organisms other than human — the filtering pipeline and viRNAtrap models are built around human reads, and model predictions for other organisms are undefined Analysis goal requires mapped host reads (e.g., host expression quantification) — this skill deliberately discards everything aligning to hg19

skills.name: hotelling-t2-significance-testing
skills.search_text: hotelling-t2-significance-testing Use when preprocessing AnnData (Ms/Mu layers from scvelo.pp.moments) before running DeepCycle and you need to select a trustworthy base gene or restrict inference to genes showing at least two distinct expression states in unspliced-spliced space. If no cycling genes are found after filtering, DeepCycle results will not be reliable — likely the data need deeper sequencing and more RNAs per cell rather than further filtering If you only need a cell-cycle phase annotation and already have a validated base gene, the optional Hotelling filter is not required for the DeepCycle run When the organism of interest has no curated GOterm cell_cycle gene list to restrict candidates, the filter has no defined candidate set to operate on http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A gene-filtering skill for DeepCycle that identifies reliably cycling genes by fitting a two-component bivariate Gaussian mixture to each gene's (spliced, unspliced) reads and retaining genes whose fitted mixture shows more than one expression state, validated with the Hotelling filter on n=158 cycling genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: If no cycling genes are found after filtering, DeepCycle results will not be reliable — likely the data need deeper sequencing and more RNAs per cell rather than further filtering If you only need a cell-cycle phase annotation and already have a validated base gene, the optional Hotelling filter is not required for the DeepCycle run When the organism of interest has no curated GOterm cell_cycle gene list to restrict candidates, the filter has no defined candidate set to operate on

skills.description: Use when you have CRISPR-lineage-traced single-cell expression data plus a Cassiopeia-reconstructed phylogeny and want de novo, signature-free detection of gene programs whose variation is heritable across the lineage.
skills.name: hotspot-gene-module-identification
skills.search_text: hotspot-gene-module-identification Use when you have CRISPR-lineage-traced single-cell expression data plus a Cassiopeia-reconstructed phylogeny and want de novo, signature-free detection of gene programs whose variation is heritable across the lineage. When no lineage/phylogeny is available — Hotspot would need a spatial or transcriptional (PCA) metric and would identify spatially varying or transcriptional modules, not heritable ones When the goal is guided signature scoring rather than de novo module discovery — use createGeneSignature with user-provided sigData instead When clone size is far below the min_gene_threshold=70 genes per module or the tree is unresolved (unifurcations not collapsed), making module grouping unstable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 De novo identification of heritable gene modules by applying Hotspot's phylogenetic autocorrelation analysis within the PhyloVision pipeline, using a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny (rather than PCA space) as the cell-similarity metric so that genes whose expression is concordant with lineage structure are grouped into modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: De novo identification of heritable gene modules by applying Hotspot's phylogenetic autocorrelation analysis within the PhyloVision pipeline, using a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny (rather than PCA space) as the cell-similarity metric so that genes whose expression is concordant with lineage structure are grouped into modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no lineage/phylogeny is available — Hotspot would need a spatial or transcriptional (PCA) metric and would identify spatially varying or transcriptional modules, not heritable ones When the goal is guided signature scoring rather than de novo module discovery — use createGeneSignature with user-provided sigData instead When clone size is far below the min_gene_threshold=70 genes per module or the tree is unresolved (unifurcations not collapsed), making module grouping unstable

Input is a raw expression matrix or unclustered tree with no Hotspot modules computed — module identification (runHotspot, compute_local_correlations) must precede annotation The goal is joint analysis of lineage and expression de novo rather than annotating existing modules against signatures — tools like iTOL or CeLaVi are explicitly noted as lacking automated interpretation, but this skill is only the reporting/annotation stage http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Within the PhyloVision web report, Hotspot-derived heritable gene modules are annotated against user-provided gene signatures (e.g., MSigDB) via a hypergeometric enrichment test and rendered as collapsible module tables alongside the radial/linear phylogeny and UMAP/tSNE overlays, making phylogeny-associated expression programs interpretable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw expression matrix or unclustered tree with no Hotspot modules computed — module identification (runHotspot, compute_local_correlations) must precede annotation The goal is joint analysis of lineage and expression de novo rather than annotating existing modules against signatures — tools like iTOL or CeLaVi are explicitly noted as lacking automated interpretation, but this skill is only the reporting/annotation stage

skills.description: Use when validating that a candidate ligand-receptor-derived gene set (e.g., eLRs) behaves like developmentally-required genes — enriched for essential/ZGA genes, depleted of housekeeping genes — relative to protein-coding and LR-pair baselines.
skills.name: housekeeping-gene-reference-set-mapping
skills.search_text: housekeeping-gene-reference-set-mapping Use when validating that a candidate ligand-receptor-derived gene set (e.g., eLRs) behaves like developmentally-required genes — enriched for essential/ZGA genes, depleted of housekeeping genes — relative to protein-coding and LR-pair baselines. The input is per-cell or pseudo-bulk expression data rather than a curated gene list to test for set-level overlap enrichment. The question is which LR pairs exist or are co-varying (use TimeTalk's |PCC|=0.1/SCC=0.2 and Granger cutoffs instead), not whether an already-identified gene set is enriched for functional categories. The target gene set is unrelated to early embryo development, so the expected essential/ZGA-enriched, housekeeping-depleted signature provides no meaningful validation. Maps a candidate gene list (e.g., the 430 TimeTalk eLR genes) against the HRT Atlas v1.0 housekeeping gene set, DEG 10 essential genes, and ZGA gene sets using one-tailed hypergeometric tests, expecting enrichment for essential/ZGA genes and depletion of housekeeping genes to support a role in organism fitness and early embryo development. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Maps a candidate gene list (e.g., the 430 TimeTalk eLR genes) against the HRT Atlas v1.0 housekeeping gene set, DEG 10 essential genes, and ZGA gene sets using one-tailed hypergeometric tests, expecting enrichment for essential/ZGA genes and depletion of housekeeping genes to support a role in organism fitness and early embryo development.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is per-cell or pseudo-bulk expression data rather than a curated gene list to test for set-level overlap enrichment. The question is which LR pairs exist or are co-varying (use TimeTalk's |PCC|=0.1/SCC=0.2 and Granger cutoffs instead), not whether an already-identified gene set is enriched for functional categories. The target gene set is unrelated to early embryo development, so the expected essential/ZGA-enriched, housekeeping-depleted signature provides no meaningful validation.

skills.description: Use when a simulation pipeline (e.g., fault-injection over many sequencing reads) must be shown to scale on HPC: serial baseline timing is available and speedup must be measured at increasing MPI rank counts.
skills.name: hpc-scaling-benchmarking
skills.search_text: hpc-scaling-benchmarking Use when a simulation pipeline (e.g., fault-injection over many sequencing reads) must be shown to scale on HPC: serial baseline timing is available and speedup must be measured at increasing MPI rank counts. The pipeline or hardware lacks an MPI implementation, or the workflow needs an unsupported scheduler (e.g., SLURM/Cobalt) without extending the TcshJob class in tools/lsf/submit.py — the README states the infrastructure assumes an IBM LSF managed platform The configuration is a small non-HPC test: use the background sub-shell examples in examples/small instead of full rank-scaling runs The analysis goal is fault-injection accuracy (error rate / MSA choice) rather than performance — scaling benchmarks answer nothing about whether multiple sequence alignment is beneficial Benchmark wall-clock scaling of a fault-injection simulation pipeline under transparent MPI parallelism, computing speedup factors (T_serial / T_parallel) as MPI rank count increases. Applied here to FrameD's RS(9,47) DNA storage pipeline to demonstrate scalability from 1 core to 92 ranks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock scaling of a fault-injection simulation pipeline under transparent MPI parallelism, computing speedup factors (T_serial / T_parallel) as MPI rank count increases. Applied here to FrameD's RS(9,47) DNA storage pipeline to demonstrate scalability from 1 core to 92 ranks.

skills.search_text: hto-count-normalization-clr-log Use when a pooled multi-sample single-cell experiment has raw HTO (hashtag) counts loaded as a Seurat object and cells must be normalized (CLR or log) and demultiplexed into singlet/doublet/negative hashtag identities. skills.search_text: hyperparameter-grid-configuration Use when preparing a hyperparameter file for SINGE's GLG tests on pseudotemporal single-cell expression data, choosing lambda, dT, num-lags, kernel-width, family, and replicate settings for the ensemble. skills.search_text: hyperparameter-optimization-deep-learning Use when training a Keras CNN (e.g., for RNA modification site prediction) and you need to search dropout rates, kernel regularizer weights, optimizer choice, and learning rate to maximize validation F1-score. skills.description: Use when a model's default hyperparameter (e.g. the unbalanced OT transported mass m=0.5 in scConfluence) lacks justification for your dataset and you need to demonstrate that embeddings are insensitive to its choice across progressively unbalanced modality scenarios.
skills.name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when a model's default hyperparameter (e.g. the unbalanced OT transported mass m=0.5 in scConfluence) lacks justification for your dataset and you need to demonstrate that embeddings are insensitive to its choice across progressively unbalanced modality scenarios. skills.summary: Systematic robustness test that retrains AutoClass (TensorFlow >=2.0) across a hyperparameter grid — bottleneck layer size, pre-clustering number K, classifier weight, and loss exponent p — on simulated Splatter dropout data, and compares metric stability against DCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-Seq data without a simulated ground-truth count matrix — MSE and dropout0/true0 zero-recovery ratios cannot be computed and the robustness claim cannot be validated Goal is to evaluate a method other than AutoClass or DCA (e.g., SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC) whose hyperparameter grids and loss structures differ and are not covered by this paper's grid You only need a single default AutoClass run — sweeping the grid is unnecessary when hyperparameter stability is not the question

skills.search_text: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when you must quantify how sensitive integration performance (e.g. scMoMaT's NMI/ARI/GC on the human PBMC dataset) is to choices like latent dimension d, lambda, KNN neighborhood size k, or radius r. The analysis goal is a single default-parameter integration run rather than robustness characterization (README recommends K = 30, n_neighbors = 30, resolution = 0.9 as defaults). The dataset has no reference cell type labels, since NMI/ARI cannot be computed without them. The aim is cross-method benchmarking against LIGER, Seurat, MultiVI, etc. — that requires a comparison harness, not a within-method sensitivity sweep. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Systematic grid sweep of an integration pipeline's key hyper-parameters (latent dimension d, regularization lambda, neighborhood size k, radius r) with clustering metrics (NMI, ARI) computed per setting, to establish robustness or plateau behavior of the method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Systematic grid sweep of an integration pipeline's key hyper-parameters (latent dimension d, regularization lambda, neighborhood size k, radius r) with clustering metrics (NMI, ARI) computed per setting, to establish robustness or plateau behavior of the method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a single default-parameter integration run rather than robustness characterization (README recommends K = 30, n_neighbors = 30, resolution = 0.9 as defaults). The dataset has no reference cell type labels, since NMI/ARI cannot be computed without them. The aim is cross-method benchmarking against LIGER, Seurat, MultiVI, etc. — that requires a comparison harness, not a within-method sensitivity sweep.

skills.search_text: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when a pipeline contains a tunable clustering/embedding parameter (e.g. Leiden resolution) whose default needs empirical justification across multiple benchmark datasets via ARI/NMI sweeps. skills.description: Use when a marker-selection pipeline (e.g. scGeneFit) exposes a tunable separation parameter Delta that controls how closely same-label samples must sit in the selected-marker subspace, and you must locate the Delta maximizing label-recovery accuracy.
skills.name: hyperparameter-tuning-for-marker-selection
skills.search_text: hyperparameter-tuning-for-marker-selection Use when a marker-selection pipeline (e.g. scGeneFit) exposes a tunable separation parameter Delta that controls how closely same-label samples must sit in the selected-marker subspace, and you must locate the Delta maximizing label-recovery accuracy. The marker-selection method has no tunable separation parameter and marker set size alone fully specifies the search (e.g. scGeneFit's spectral toy model where any target marker set size ≥ 2 recovers circle-coordinate labels deterministically). Cell-type classes are not linearly separable in the low-dimensional selected-marker space — scGeneFit assumes linear separability, so an LP-evaluated Delta objective would be mis-specified. Labels are continuous or manifold-valued (e.g. trajectory time points or spatial locations); the approach presumes categorical cell labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs a dual-annealing hyperparameter search over the target separation Delta for marker selection, scoring candidate Delta values by classifier label-recovery accuracy computed through a linear-program solver backend. It serializes the best Delta with metadata so scGeneFit-style marker selection can be reused on arbitrary train/test/classifier splits. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs a dual-annealing hyperparameter search over the target separation Delta for marker selection, scoring candidate Delta values by classifier label-recovery accuracy computed through a linear-program solver backend. It serializes the best Delta with metadata so scGeneFit-style marker selection can be reused on arbitrary train/test/classifier splits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The marker-selection method has no tunable separation parameter and marker set size alone fully specifies the search (e.g. scGeneFit's spectral toy model where any target marker set size ≥ 2 recovers circle-coordinate labels deterministically). Cell-type classes are not linearly separable in the low-dimensional selected-marker space — scGeneFit assumes linear separability, so an LP-evaluated Delta objective would be mis-specified. Labels are continuous or manifold-valued (e.g. trajectory time points or spatial locations); the approach presumes categorical cell labels.

skills.description: Decision support for validating or reimplementing VAE training objectives where latent variables are vMF-distributed on a unit hypersphere and the KL term to a uniform hyperspherical prior must be computed in closed form.
skills.name: hyperspherical-kl-divergence-computation
skills.search_text: hyperspherical-kl-divergence-computation Decision support for validating or reimplementing VAE training objectives where latent variables are vMF-distributed on a unit hypersphere and the KL term to a uniform hyperspherical prior must be computed in closed form. Latent space is hyperbolic (Lorentz model / Poincaré disk) — scPhere uses a wrapped normal ('wn') latent distribution there, not a vMF posterior with hyperspherical KL Input is raw UMI counts needing preprocessing or batch correction by an external method rather than reimplementing/verifying the vMF-VAE objective itself Standard Euclidean VAE (Gaussian latent prior) is sufficient — the hyperspherical KL machinery addresses the specific crowding distortion of normal priors on sparse droplet scRNA-seq data http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs and numerically verifies the von Mises–Fisher (vMF) latent machinery of scPhere: rejection-sampled vMF posterior, the closed-form KL divergence between the vMF posterior and the uniform prior on the unit hypersphere, and the softmax-parameterized negative-binomial decoder that together replace the Gaussian/Euclidean VAE objective. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs and numerically verifies the von Mises–Fisher (vMF) latent machinery of scPhere: rejection-sampled vMF posterior, the closed-form KL divergence between the vMF posterior and the uniform prior on the unit hypersphere, and the softmax-parameterized negative-binomial decoder that together replace the Gaussian/Euclidean VAE objective.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Latent space is hyperbolic (Lorentz model / Poincaré disk) — scPhere uses a wrapped normal ('wn') latent distribution there, not a vMF posterior with hyperspherical KL Input is raw UMI counts needing preprocessing or batch correction by an external method rather than reimplementing/verifying the vMF-VAE objective itself Standard Euclidean VAE (Gaussian latent prior) is sufficient — the hyperspherical KL machinery addresses the specific crowding distortion of normal priors on sparse droplet scRNA-seq data

skills.search_text: hypoxia-signature-sample-stratification Use when a counts matrix of tumor RNA-seq samples (e.g., TCGA-LUAD from GDC) must be split into hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low groups before differential expression or survival analysis, using a gene-set score rather than a single marker gene. skills.search_text: ic50-based-compound-efficacy-labeling Use when a drug retrieval evaluation needs binary efficacy ground truth per compound — e.g., computing ROC AUC and PR AUC for GSFM reversal scores against CMap/XSum/ZhangScore/RS baselines.
