skills.name: ic50-to-cell-death-efficacy-conversion
skills.search_text: ic50-to-cell-death-efficacy-conversion Use when you have per-cell or cluster-level IC50 predictions from CaDRReS-Sc GDSC pre-trained model and need to express drug kill efficacy as cell death percentages per cluster and drug. You want PRISM-based drug sensitivity predictions (AUC) rather than IC50/kill efficacy — use --model PRISM, which outputs AUC_prediction.csv instead Input is raw 10x mtx or CSV rather than a processed AnnData object from Single-Cell Data Analysis — cluster-wise IC50 requires the clustered scanpyobj.h5ad The compounds of interest were not experimentally screened in GDSC; scDrug drug response prediction is limited to experimentally screened compounds http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts predicted cluster-wise IC50 values (estimated via CaDRReS-Sc on scRNA-seq clusters) into cell death percentages that scDrug reports as drug kill efficacy for each predicted GDSC drug on each Louvain cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Converts predicted cluster-wise IC50 values (estimated via CaDRReS-Sc on scRNA-seq clusters) into cell death percentages that scDrug reports as drug kill efficacy for each predicted GDSC drug on each Louvain cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want PRISM-based drug sensitivity predictions (AUC) rather than IC50/kill efficacy — use --model PRISM, which outputs AUC_prediction.csv instead Input is raw 10x mtx or CSV rather than a processed AnnData object from Single-Cell Data Analysis — cluster-wise IC50 requires the clustered scanpyobj.h5ad The compounds of interest were not experimentally screened in GDSC; scDrug drug response prediction is limited to experimentally screened compounds

skills.description: Use when you have gene z-weight vectors for independent components derived from multiple tumor scRNA-seq cohorts and must keep only cross-cohort-reproducible components before building consensus meta-components.
skills.name: ica-component-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: ica-component-reproducibility-assessment Use when you have gene z-weight vectors for independent components derived from multiple tumor scRNA-seq cohorts and must keep only cross-cohort-reproducible components before building consensus meta-components. The input is single-cell data from only one cohort — no cross-cohort IC matching is possible, so the ≥3-dataset Pearson correlation filter is undefined. The goal is annotating new TME scRNA-seq data with the pretrained MeC space (use the MetaTiME-Annotator) rather than re-deriving the meta-components themselves. The input is already a consensus MeC gene-weight profile table (e.g. mec_profiles.csv); this skill produces that table, not one that consumes it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters independent components (ICs) learned by ICA across multiple tumor single-cell cohorts so that only transcriptional programs reproducible across datasets (minimum Pearson correlation with a matching component in ≥3 datasets) are retained, then merges them into consensus meta-components (MeCs) via Louvain clustering of the component similarity graph. This is how MetaTiME ensures its MeC space reflects shared, not cohort-specific, gene-expression variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Filters independent components (ICs) learned by ICA across multiple tumor single-cell cohorts so that only transcriptional programs reproducible across datasets (minimum Pearson correlation with a matching component in ≥3 datasets) are retained, then merges them into consensus meta-components (MeCs) via Louvain clustering of the component similarity graph. This is how MetaTiME ensures its MeC space reflects shared, not cohort-specific, gene-expression variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell data from only one cohort — no cross-cohort IC matching is possible, so the ≥3-dataset Pearson correlation filter is undefined. The goal is annotating new TME scRNA-seq data with the pretrained MeC space (use the MetaTiME-Annotator) rather than re-deriving the meta-components themselves. The input is already a consensus MeC gene-weight profile table (e.g. mec_profiles.csv); this skill produces that table, not one that consumes it.

skills.description: Use when you have a single log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix and need reproducible, independent transcriptional directions (meta-components) rather than manual marker-based cell labeling.
skills.name: ica-decomposition-of-scrna-seq-expression
skills.search_text: ica-decomposition-of-scrna-seq-expression Use when you have a single log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix and need reproducible, independent transcriptional directions (meta-components) rather than manual marker-based cell labeling. The goal is annotating cells against already-trained meta-components rather than re-deriving components — use the MetaTiME annotator projection workflow instead The input is not a single log-transformed expression matrix (e.g., it is already a feature/embedding table or multi-dataset joint matrix) You need to align datasets into a joint low-dimensional representation across cohorts — the paper contrasts this with Harmony and scVI/scArches integration approaches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Decompose a log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix into ~100 maximally independent gene-expression components via fastICA, then z-weight normalize and skewness-align the IC loading vectors so gene representation scores are comparable across components, yielding normalized IC loadings for downstream MeC clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Decompose a log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix into ~100 maximally independent gene-expression components via fastICA, then z-weight normalize and skewness-align the IC loading vectors so gene representation scores are comparable across components, yielding normalized IC loadings for downstream MeC clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating cells against already-trained meta-components rather than re-deriving components — use the MetaTiME annotator projection workflow instead The input is not a single log-transformed expression matrix (e.g., it is already a feature/embedding table or multi-dataset joint matrix) You need to align datasets into a joint low-dimensional representation across cohorts — the paper contrasts this with Harmony and scVI/scArches integration approaches

skills.description: Use when comparing two projected query conditions (e.g., knockout vs WT) on a shared reference atlas and you need to find which latent dimensions/gene programs shift, beyond changes in cell-state composition.
skills.name: ica-discriminant-dimension-analysis
skills.search_text: ica-discriminant-dimension-analysis Use when comparing two projected query conditions (e.g., knockout vs WT) on a shared reference atlas and you need to find which latent dimensions/gene programs shift, beyond changes in cell-state composition. The query has not yet been projected onto a reference atlas — run make.projection/Run.ProjecTILs first, since discriminant dimensions require query and control in a shared embedding space The goal is only to quantify cell-state composition differences between conditions — plot.statepred.composition alone suffices without ICA dimension ranking The input is raw unprojected counts without a reference map; ProjecTILs performs cell-state quantification in the reference PCA latent space, and UMAP should be used for visual exploration only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Uses the ProjecTILs function find.discriminant.dimensions with ICA as the reduction to rank low-dimensional components where a projected query population (e.g., Regnase-1-null Tex CD8+ TILs) deviates most from a control (WT), then inspects the top components' driving genes for altered gene programs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Uses the ProjecTILs function find.discriminant.dimensions with ICA as the reduction to rank low-dimensional components where a projected query population (e.g., Regnase-1-null Tex CD8+ TILs) deviates most from a control (WT), then inspects the top components' driving genes for altered gene programs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query has not yet been projected onto a reference atlas — run make.projection/Run.ProjecTILs first, since discriminant dimensions require query and control in a shared embedding space The goal is only to quantify cell-state composition differences between conditions — plot.statepred.composition alone suffices without ICA dimension ranking The input is raw unprojected counts without a reference map; ProjecTILs performs cell-state quantification in the reference PCA latent space, and UMAP should be used for visual exploration only

skills.description: Use when you have a large pan-cancer tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. thousands to millions of cells across many cohorts) and want reproducible, low-dimensional gene programs for cell-state annotation rather than marker-based manual labelling.
skills.name: ica-meta-component-decomposition-single-cell
skills.search_text: ica-meta-component-decomposition-single-cell Use when you have a large pan-cancer tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. thousands to millions of cells across many cohorts) and want reproducible, low-dimensional gene programs for cell-state annotation rather than marker-based manual labelling. Input is already a projected cell-state annotation or feature-signature table rather than raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression data — the ICA decomposition requires expression matrices. The goal is joint low-dimensional integration of a small set of query datasets via methods like Harmony or scArches; MetaTiME MeC learning instead trains a reusable component space from a large aggregated corpus and maps new data onto it. The data are not tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq; the MeC space is trained on TME single cells and its cell-type/state interpretation is TME-specific. Learns data-driven, interpretable meta-components (MeCs) of the tumor immune microenvironment by running ICA-based decomposition over millions of TME single-cell gene expression profiles, yielding ~86 transcriptional directions that encode independent gene-expression variation across cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38333-8
skills.summary: Learns data-driven, interpretable meta-components (MeCs) of the tumor immune microenvironment by running ICA-based decomposition over millions of TME single-cell gene expression profiles, yielding ~86 transcriptional directions that encode independent gene-expression variation across cancer types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a projected cell-state annotation or feature-signature table rather than raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression data — the ICA decomposition requires expression matrices. The goal is joint low-dimensional integration of a small set of query datasets via methods like Harmony or scArches; MetaTiME MeC learning instead trains a reusable component space from a large aggregated corpus and maps new data onto it. The data are not tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq; the MeC space is trained on TME single cells and its cell-type/state interpretation is TME-specific.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq gene programs must be discovered by independent component analysis or NMF — e.g., as ICA/NMF comparators in a benchmark against SSN gene programs scored by GO and PPI enrichment.
skills.name: ica-nmf-factor-decomposition
skills.search_text: ica-nmf-factor-decomposition Use when scRNA-seq gene programs must be discovered by independent component analysis or NMF — e.g., as ICA/NMF comparators in a benchmark against SSN gene programs scored by GO and PPI enrichment. The goal is cell-type annotation rather than gene program discovery — the Miko scoring pipeline or sc-type are the paper's annotation tools, not ICA/NMF factorization. The input is already a set of gene programs; this skill generates programs from expression data and cannot recover GO/PPI statistics for externally supplied gene sets without the getAnnotationPathways enrichment step. The expected best-performing method is needed for program discovery — the paper's finding is that scale-free SSN achieves superior GO-term recovery and STRING PPI enrichment compared to ICA and NMF, so factorization is primarily a baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Discovers gene programs from scRNA-seq data by ICA and NMF factorization (scMiko getICAGenes/getNMFGenes, with consolidateNMF to merge redundant NMF factors), and evaluates program quality by GO-term recovery and STRING PPI enrichment as comparator methods to scale-free SSN analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Discovers gene programs from scRNA-seq data by ICA and NMF factorization (scMiko getICAGenes/getNMFGenes, with consolidateNMF to merge redundant NMF factors), and evaluates program quality by GO-term recovery and STRING PPI enrichment as comparator methods to scale-free SSN analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-type annotation rather than gene program discovery — the Miko scoring pipeline or sc-type are the paper's annotation tools, not ICA/NMF factorization. The input is already a set of gene programs; this skill generates programs from expression data and cannot recover GO/PPI statistics for externally supplied gene sets without the getAnnotationPathways enrichment step. The expected best-performing method is needed for program discovery — the paper's finding is that scale-free SSN achieves superior GO-term recovery and STRING PPI enrichment compared to ICA and NMF, so factorization is primarily a baseline.

skills.description: Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData (obsm['X_icat'] upweighted matrix, ICAT gene list, 'control' vs 'perturbed' treatment labels) and need to test whether ICAT-selected marker genes are differentially expressed between treatments.
skills.name: icat-upweighted-gene-space-analysis
skills.search_text: icat-upweighted-gene-space-analysis Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData (obsm['X_icat'] upweighted matrix, ICAT gene list, 'control' vs 'perturbed' treatment labels) and need to test whether ICAT-selected marker genes are differentially expressed between treatments. You have raw, unclustered single-cell counts with no ICAT weighting (no obsm['X_icat'] or NCFS gene list) — run the upstream ICAT clustering/weighting workflow first Your goal is de novo differential-expression discovery across all genes rather than validating stability of a pre-selected ICAT marker set The AnnData lacks treatment labels or contains only one condition, so control-vs-perturbed MAST contrast is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential-expression stability testing of ICAT-weighted marker genes using MAST hurdle models, as in the ICAT paper's PMC (primary mesenchyme cell) analysis where control cells were compared against MK-886-treated cells to test the paper's latent assumption that ICAT-selected marker genes remain stable across treatment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Differential-expression stability testing of ICAT-weighted marker genes using MAST hurdle models, as in the ICAT paper's PMC (primary mesenchyme cell) analysis where control cells were compared against MK-886-treated cells to test the paper's latent assumption that ICAT-selected marker genes remain stable across treatment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw, unclustered single-cell counts with no ICAT weighting (no obsm['X_icat'] or NCFS gene list) — run the upstream ICAT clustering/weighting workflow first Your goal is de novo differential-expression discovery across all genes rather than validating stability of a pre-selected ICAT marker set The AnnData lacks treatment labels or contains only one condition, so control-vs-perturbed MAST contrast is impossible

skills.description: Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq profiles from ICB-treated patients have been projected through a single-cell-trained encoder and latent features must be tested for responder/non-responder association and biologically interpreted.
skills.name: icb-response-immune-signature-interpretation
skills.search_text: icb-response-immune-signature-interpretation Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq profiles from ICB-treated patients have been projected through a single-cell-trained encoder and latent features must be tested for responder/non-responder association and biologically interpreted. Input data is single-cell expression data rather than bulk tumor RNA-seq — Miscell's primary use is single-cell clustering and marker identification, not ICB response testing The encoder has not been trained on single-cell data, since the method's premise is transferring knowledge learned from single-cells to bulk tumor expression data Patient response labels are unavailable, since the Wilcoxon rank-sum test requires responder/non-responder grouping http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets clinically significant Miscell latent features extracted from bulk tumor RNA-seq by testing their association with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response and characterizing significant features via an immune signature (IFNG, IL12B, CXCR3, CD19). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Interprets clinically significant Miscell latent features extracted from bulk tumor RNA-seq by testing their association with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response and characterizing significant features via an immune signature (IFNG, IL12B, CXCR3, CD19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is single-cell expression data rather than bulk tumor RNA-seq — Miscell's primary use is single-cell clustering and marker identification, not ICB response testing The encoder has not been trained on single-cell data, since the method's premise is transferring knowledge learned from single-cells to bulk tumor expression data Patient response labels are unavailable, since the Wilcoxon rank-sum test requires responder/non-responder grouping

skills.description: Use when a task requires paired-sample analysis of the ICGC PACA-AU cohort (primary vs metastatic vs derived cell line comparisons) across both RNAseq and microarray platforms using pdacR-parsed objects.
skills.name: icgc-paca-au-sample-metadata-handling
skills.search_text: icgc-paca-au-sample-metadata-handling Use when a task requires paired-sample analysis of the ICGC PACA-AU cohort (primary vs metastatic vs derived cell line comparisons) across both RNAseq and microarray platforms using pdacR-parsed objects. When the analysis does not require pairing (e.g., cohort-level subtype classification or survival analysis on TCGA-PAAD), plain pdacR dataset loading and filtering suffices When the input data are un-parsed raw ICGC downloads rather than pdacR-parsed .rds objects, since the sampInfo structure and ICGC_PARSE_Nones flags will not exist When you need to merge samples across RNAseq and microarray into a single expression matrix, since pdacR explicitly warns it cannot robustly merge datasets across platforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Method for loading and joining the paired ICGC PACA-AU RNAseq and microarray expression matrices with their sampInfo metadata tables to identify matched primary, metastatic, and cell-line samples while excluding samples flagged by ICGC_PARSE_Nones, enabling paired analyses such as signature-loss testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Method for loading and joining the paired ICGC PACA-AU RNAseq and microarray expression matrices with their sampInfo metadata tables to identify matched primary, metastatic, and cell-line samples while excluding samples flagged by ICGC_PARSE_Nones, enabling paired analyses such as signature-loss testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis does not require pairing (e.g., cohort-level subtype classification or survival analysis on TCGA-PAAD), plain pdacR dataset loading and filtering suffices When the input data are un-parsed raw ICGC downloads rather than pdacR-parsed .rds objects, since the sampInfo structure and ICGC_PARSE_Nones flags will not exist When you need to merge samples across RNAseq and microarray into a single expression matrix, since pdacR explicitly warns it cannot robustly merge datasets across platforms

skills.description: Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. Visium or seqFISH sections) have APCA low-dimensional embeddings and spatial adjacency matrices already built, and you need joint spatial clustering with batch-effect estimation and a data-driven choice of cluster number.
skills.name: icm-em-algorithm-execution
skills.search_text: icm-em-algorithm-execution Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. Visium or seqFISH sections) have APCA low-dimensional embeddings and spatial adjacency matrices already built, and you need joint spatial clustering with batch-effect estimation and a data-driven choice of cluster number. You have a single SRT sample with no batch structure — the simpler SC.MEB empirical Bayes model is the predecessor designed for that setting Input data has not yet been reduced to low-dimensional embeddings and spatial neighbors (no APCA/PCA representation or adjacency matrix) — the model operates on these, not raw counts You need marker-gene differential expression rather than clustering; those come after integration via doDEG on the IntegrateSpaData output http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit the iSC.MEB hidden-Markov-random-field model with empirical Bayes over a grid of candidate cluster numbers, using ICM-EM inference that alternates cluster-label and batch-embedding posterior updates, then select K by MBIC. This estimates spatial cluster labels while simultaneously correcting batch effects across multiple SRT samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Fit the iSC.MEB hidden-Markov-random-field model with empirical Bayes over a grid of candidate cluster numbers, using ICM-EM inference that alternates cluster-label and batch-embedding posterior updates, then select K by MBIC. This estimates spatial cluster labels while simultaneously correcting batch effects across multiple SRT samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single SRT sample with no batch structure — the simpler SC.MEB empirical Bayes model is the predecessor designed for that setting Input data has not yet been reduced to low-dimensional embeddings and spatial neighbors (no APCA/PCA representation or adjacency matrix) — the model operates on these, not raw counts You need marker-gene differential expression rather than clustering; those come after integration via doDEG on the IntegrateSpaData output

skills.description: Use when hyb-format records from miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. CLASH/qCLASH) need segment-type classification from segment reference identifiers, or when miRNA_seg flags ('N','5p','3p','B','U') must be set for downstream analysis.
skills.name: identifier-based-sequence-classification
skills.search_text: identifier-based-sequence-classification Use when hyb-format records from miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. CLASH/qCLASH) need segment-type classification from segment reference identifiers, or when miRNA_seg flags ('N','5p','3p','B','U') must be set for downstream analysis. Input is not in the hyb file format defined by the Hyb software package (e.g. raw FASTQ or unaligned chimera reads) — records must already be parsed into hyb records The goal is subsetting rather than typing: use hyb_filter (e.g. --filter any_seg_contains kshv) instead of eval-based classification Segment reference identifiers do not conform to conventions the identifier-based criteria can resolve, so typing would rely on unsupported inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assigns segment types (e.g. 'miRNA', 'mRNA', 'lncRNA') and miRNA flags to hybrid RNA records in the 'hyb' file format using identifier-based criteria, as implemented by hybkit's HybRecord.eval_types and eval_mirna methods and the hyb_eval command-line utility. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad721
skills.summary: Assigns segment types (e.g. 'miRNA', 'mRNA', 'lncRNA') and miRNA flags to hybrid RNA records in the 'hyb' file format using identifier-based criteria, as implemented by hybkit's HybRecord.eval_types and eval_mirna methods and the hyb_eval command-line utility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not in the hyb file format defined by the Hyb software package (e.g. raw FASTQ or unaligned chimera reads) — records must already be parsed into hyb records The goal is subsetting rather than typing: use hyb_filter (e.g. --filter any_seg_contains kshv) instead of eval-based classification Segment reference identifiers do not conform to conventions the identifier-based criteria can resolve, so typing would rely on unsupported inference

skills.description: Use when comparing GEP-identification methods on a single-cell dataset with known cell-type labels, specifically to quantify how many programs are cell-type-specific identity programs versus shared activity programs across cell types.
skills.name: identity-versus-activity-gep-classification
skills.search_text: identity-versus-activity-gep-classification Use when comparing GEP-identification methods on a single-cell dataset with known cell-type labels, specifically to quantify how many programs are cell-type-specific identity programs versus shared activity programs across cell types. When cell-type labels are unavailable, since the identity-versus-activity classification depends on associating program usage with known cell-type annotations. When the goal is to annotate cells in a novel dataset rather than benchmark GEP-identification methods — use CellGEP label transfer instead. When the dataset has fewer than ~5000 cells or high-expression noise, which SingleCellGGM's README warns against for its pcor-based network construction. Classifies gene expression programs (GEPs) identified on a single-cell dataset as cell-type-specific identity programs versus shared-usage activity GEPs, and benchmarks alternative GEP-identification methods (e.g., cNMF with fixed k against SingleCellGGM) on the same dataset for their ability to recover shared activity programs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Classifies gene expression programs (GEPs) identified on a single-cell dataset as cell-type-specific identity programs versus shared-usage activity GEPs, and benchmarks alternative GEP-identification methods (e.g., cNMF with fixed k against SingleCellGGM) on the same dataset for their ability to recover shared activity programs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell-type labels are unavailable, since the identity-versus-activity classification depends on associating program usage with known cell-type annotations. When the goal is to annotate cells in a novel dataset rather than benchmark GEP-identification methods — use CellGEP label transfer instead. When the dataset has fewer than ~5000 cells or high-expression noise, which SingleCellGGM's README warns against for its pcor-based network construction.

skills.description: Use when paired scRNA-seq + TCR data from patients with known epitope exposure (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 PBMCs) and donor HLA types are available, and clusters in a mvTCR joint embedding must be labeled antigen-specific vs bystander.
skills.name: iedb-antigen-specificity-annotation
skills.search_text: iedb-antigen-specificity-annotation Use when paired scRNA-seq + TCR data from patients with known epitope exposure (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 PBMCs) and donor HLA types are available, and clusters in a mvTCR joint embedding must be labeled antigen-specific vs bystander. TCR sequences are unpaired or partially missing (mvTCR was applied mainly to fully paired α/β-CDR3 + gene expression data) Donor HLA types are unavailable, so MHCFlurry donor-specific binding filtering cannot be performed Data are BCR/antibody repertoires — the paper notes no in-depth benchmark exists for B-cell receptors due to lack of large-scale B cell datasets with specificity annotation Labels T cell clusters as antigen-specific or bystander by querying TCR sequences against IEDB for epitope pairings and retaining only hits whose restricting epitope is predicted (MHCFlurry) to bind the donor's HLAs, then validating labels via differential gene expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Labels T cell clusters as antigen-specific or bystander by querying TCR sequences against IEDB for epitope pairings and retaining only hits whose restricting epitope is predicted (MHCFlurry) to bind the donor's HLAs, then validating labels via differential gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: TCR sequences are unpaired or partially missing (mvTCR was applied mainly to fully paired α/β-CDR3 + gene expression data) Donor HLA types are unavailable, so MHCFlurry donor-specific binding filtering cannot be performed Data are BCR/antibody repertoires — the paper notes no in-depth benchmark exists for B-cell receptors due to lack of large-scale B cell datasets with specificity annotation

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq case-control data has been signal-filtered (e.g., SiFT healthy-trajectory removal) and you need a gene-set readout to confirm which cell types carry the recovered disease signal.
skills.name: ifn-response-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: ifn-response-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when scRNA-seq case-control data has been signal-filtered (e.g., SiFT healthy-trajectory removal) and you need a gene-set readout to confirm which cell types carry the recovered disease signal. The data are raw unfiltered counts where the healthy signal has not been removed — the paper reports the same analysis on the original data failed to expose the relevant cell types. The biological question targets a pathway other than interferon response, with no prior knowledge linking it to the filtered signal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores interferon (IFN)-response gene-set enrichment in SiFT-filtered COVID-19 PBMC scRNA-seq data to verify that filtering the healthy reference signal exposes disease-related dynamics in innate immune cell types (monocytes, DCs, HSPC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Scores interferon (IFN)-response gene-set enrichment in SiFT-filtered COVID-19 PBMC scRNA-seq data to verify that filtering the healthy reference signal exposes disease-related dynamics in innate immune cell types (monocytes, DCs, HSPC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw unfiltered counts where the healthy signal has not been removed — the paper reports the same analysis on the original data failed to expose the relevant cell types. The biological question targets a pathway other than interferon response, with no prior knowledge linking it to the filtered signal.

skills.description: Use when starting from a BWA-aligned, coordinate-sorted, indexed hg38 RNA-seq BAM (e.g. ribodepleted or polyA-selected, ≥25M reads) and you need Ig-locus reads extracted and assembled into IGHV-D-J transcript contigs before SHM/IGHV mutation-status analysis.
skills.name: ig-locus-read-extraction-from-bam
skills.search_text: ig-locus-read-extraction-from-bam Use when starting from a BWA-aligned, coordinate-sorted, indexed hg38 RNA-seq BAM (e.g. ribodepleted or polyA-selected, ≥25M reads) and you need Ig-locus reads extracted and assembled into IGHV-D-J transcript contigs before SHM/IGHV mutation-status analysis. Input is not a BAM aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS explicitly requires this pre-processing The goal is BCR repertoire inference from only a portion of the IGHV gene segment rather than de novo reconstruction of full IGHV-D-J transcripts RNA-seq data has fewer than 25M reads per sample, below CRIS's stated minimum http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts RNA-seq read pairs aligned to putative immunoglobulin gene loci from a coordinate-sorted, indexed hg38 BAM using sambamba, converts them to paired-end FASTQ with Picard SamToFastq, and de novo assembles Ig transcript contigs with Trinity (v2.1.1) as the first stage of the CRIS IGHV-D-J reconstruction pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Extracts RNA-seq read pairs aligned to putative immunoglobulin gene loci from a coordinate-sorted, indexed hg38 BAM using sambamba, converts them to paired-end FASTQ with Picard SamToFastq, and de novo assembles Ig transcript contigs with Trinity (v2.1.1) as the first stage of the CRIS IGHV-D-J reconstruction pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a BAM aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS explicitly requires this pre-processing The goal is BCR repertoire inference from only a portion of the IGHV gene segment rather than de novo reconstruction of full IGHV-D-J transcripts RNA-seq data has fewer than 25M reads per sample, below CRIS's stated minimum

skills.description: Use when a CRIS run has produced Ig-transcript outputs (.ig-transcripts.sortedbyTPM.txt/.fasta and .IgBLAST_out.txt) and the top-expressed contig must be selected and assigned to a germline IGHV gene (e.g. IGHV3-74) for percent-identity comparison.
skills.name: ig-transcript-tpm-sorted-contig-selection
skills.search_text: ig-transcript-tpm-sorted-contig-selection Use when a CRIS run has produced Ig-transcript outputs (.ig-transcripts.sortedbyTPM.txt/.fasta and .IgBLAST_out.txt) and the top-expressed contig must be selected and assigned to a germline IGHV gene (e.g. IGHV3-74) for percent-identity comparison. Input is a raw RNA-seq BAM or FASTQ that has not been processed by CRIS — no TPM-sorted Ig-transcript files exist yet, so run CRIS first (requires ≥25M reads, ≥16GB RAM, 4 threads). The goal is bulk B-cell receptor repertoire profiling of many clonotypes rather than selecting a single top-expressed IGHV transcript for hypermutation status classification. The BAM is not aligned to the hg38 (GRCh38) genome build with BWA and coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS extraction of Ig-locus reads and downstream TPM ranking are not valid on other builds. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Identifies the top-expressed immunoglobulin transcript contig from CRIS output by ranking Ig-transcript FASTA sequences by TPM expression values, then assigning the selected contig to its germline IGHV gene via BLAST/IgBLAST alignment. This selection step is what determines the IGHV sequence used for downstream percent-identity and SHM classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Identifies the top-expressed immunoglobulin transcript contig from CRIS output by ranking Ig-transcript FASTA sequences by TPM expression values, then assigning the selected contig to its germline IGHV gene via BLAST/IgBLAST alignment. This selection step is what determines the IGHV sequence used for downstream percent-identity and SHM classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw RNA-seq BAM or FASTQ that has not been processed by CRIS — no TPM-sorted Ig-transcript files exist yet, so run CRIS first (requires ≥25M reads, ≥16GB RAM, 4 threads). The goal is bulk B-cell receptor repertoire profiling of many clonotypes rather than selecting a single top-expressed IGHV transcript for hypermutation status classification. The BAM is not aligned to the hg38 (GRCh38) genome build with BWA and coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS extraction of Ig-locus reads and downstream TPM ranking are not valid on other builds.

skills.description: Use when you have RNA-seq-derived Ig transcript FASTAs (TPM-ranked) or contigs from a BCR/CLL sample and need to assign a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity, and call mCLL/uCLL SHM status.
skills.name: igblast-germline-vdj-alignment
skills.search_text: igblast-germline-vdj-alignment Use when you have RNA-seq-derived Ig transcript FASTAs (TPM-ranked) or contigs from a BCR/CLL sample and need to assign a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity, and call mCLL/uCLL SHM status. The input is raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads or an unprocessed whole-transcriptome BAM — Ig transcripts must first be extracted from Ig gene loci and de novo assembled (CRIS steps 1–2) before IgBLAST alignment is meaningful The BAM is not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS will not accept it and the germline-alignment step cannot be validated The goal is to infer the B-cell receptor repertoire from only a portion of the IGHV gene segment — CRIS deliberately improves on such tools by reconstructing the entire IGHV segment via de novo assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 Aligns de novo-assembled Ig transcripts (or contigs) against the IMGT germline V, D and J reference database with IgBLAST to recover the top germline IGHV hit, its percent identity, somatic hypermutations, and clonotype groupings — the mutation-calling core of the CRIS CLL IGHV classification pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Aligns de novo-assembled Ig transcripts (or contigs) against the IMGT germline V, D and J reference database with IgBLAST to recover the top germline IGHV hit, its percent identity, somatic hypermutations, and clonotype groupings — the mutation-calling core of the CRIS CLL IGHV classification pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads or an unprocessed whole-transcriptome BAM — Ig transcripts must first be extracted from Ig gene loci and de novo assembled (CRIS steps 1–2) before IgBLAST alignment is meaningful The BAM is not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS will not accept it and the germline-alignment step cannot be validated The goal is to infer the B-cell receptor repertoire from only a portion of the IGHV gene segment — CRIS deliberately improves on such tools by reconstructing the entire IGHV segment via de novo assembly

skills.summary: Benchmarks BCR/IGHV reconstruction tools (CRIS, V'DJer, TRUST, MiXCR) on CLL RNA-seq samples by tabulating the percent of the full IGHV gene each tool assembles and their wall-clock runtimes under identical thread settings.

skills.description: Use when you have de novo assembled Ig-transcript contigs from RNA-seq and need to assign each contig to a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity to the germline allele, or benchmark whether reconstruction length affects reported identity.
skills.name: ighv-germline-alignment-percent-identity-computation
skills.search_text: ighv-germline-alignment-percent-identity-computation Use when you have de novo assembled Ig-transcript contigs from RNA-seq and need to assign each contig to a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity to the germline allele, or benchmark whether reconstruction length affects reported identity. Input is raw reads rather than assembled Ig-transcript contigs — the identity computation requires de novo assembly output (e.g. CRIS/trinity contigs) first BAM is aligned to a build other than hg38 (GRCh38) or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed Sample RNA-seq has fewer than 25M reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for reliable reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3396 Assigns reconstructed Ig-transcript contigs to their germline IGHV gene (e.g. IGHV3-74*03) by aligning to germline Ig references with BLAST/IgBLAST and computes reconstruction length and percent identity, the metric CRIS uses for SHM status and the benchmark used to show full-length versus partial IGHV reconstruction changes identity (295/296 bp at 91.2% vs 226 bp at 89.4%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Assigns reconstructed Ig-transcript contigs to their germline IGHV gene (e.g. IGHV3-74*03) by aligning to germline Ig references with BLAST/IgBLAST and computes reconstruction length and percent identity, the metric CRIS uses for SHM status and the benchmark used to show full-length versus partial IGHV reconstruction changes identity (295/296 bp at 91.2% vs 226 bp at 89.4%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads rather than assembled Ig-transcript contigs — the identity computation requires de novo assembly output (e.g. CRIS/trinity contigs) first BAM is aligned to a build other than hg38 (GRCh38) or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed Sample RNA-seq has fewer than 25M reads, below CRIS's stated minimum for reliable reconstruction

skills.description: Use when you have de novo-assembled transcript contigs (e.g., Trinity FASTA) and need to find which contigs are immunoglobulin IGHV-derived and which expressed Ig transcript is the dominant clone by TPM.
skills.name: ighv-germline-homology-search
skills.search_text: ighv-germline-homology-search Use when you have de novo-assembled transcript contigs (e.g., Trinity FASTA) and need to find which contigs are immunoglobulin IGHV-derived and which expressed Ig transcript is the dominant clone by TPM. Input reads have not been assembled — this step operates on Trinity-assembled contigs, not raw FASTQ or BAM alignments You need full IGHV-D-J reconstruction or SHM classification itself; this skill only performs germline homology identification and TPM-based dominance ranking (downstream steps use IgBLAST v1.14.0) http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Identify immunoglobulin transcripts among Trinity-assembled contigs by blastn against a custom IMGT IGHV reference database (BLAST v2.9.0, E-value cutoff 20), then quantify the retained Ig transcripts with Salmon (v0.8.1, k-mer 31) and rank by TPM to flag the dominant clone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Identify immunoglobulin transcripts among Trinity-assembled contigs by blastn against a custom IMGT IGHV reference database (BLAST v2.9.0, E-value cutoff 20), then quantify the retained Ig transcripts with Salmon (v0.8.1, k-mer 31) and rank by TPM to flag the dominant clone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads have not been assembled — this step operates on Trinity-assembled contigs, not raw FASTQ or BAM alignments You need full IGHV-D-J reconstruction or SHM classification itself; this skill only performs germline homology identification and TPM-based dominance ranking (downstream steps use IgBLAST v1.14.0)

skills.description: Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs (≥25M reads, ribodepleted or polyA) aligned to hg38/GRCh38 with BWA need an IGHV mutation status call, and clinical Sanger genotyping is unavailable or should be cross-checked from transcriptome data.
skills.name: ighv-mutation-status-classification
skills.search_text: ighv-mutation-status-classification Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs (≥25M reads, ribodepleted or polyA) aligned to hg38/GRCh38 with BWA need an IGHV mutation status call, and clinical Sanger genotyping is unavailable or should be cross-checked from transcriptome data. Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) — CRIS requires BWA-aligned hg38, coordinate-sorted BAMs; other builds or unsorted files are unsupported Samples have fewer than 25M RNA-seq reads per sample, insufficient for de novo assembly of the IGHV transcript Goal is full B-cell receptor repertoire profiling from mixed samples rather than CLL IGHV hypermutation status per patient http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classify chronic lymphocytic leukemia samples as mutated (mCLL) or unmutated (uCLL) by de novo assembling IGHV transcripts from RNA-seq BAMs with CRIS and comparing the dominant clone's IGHV sequence to its top germline hit. Validated against clinical PCR-Sanger IGHV classification with high concordance across three CLL cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Classify chronic lymphocytic leukemia samples as mutated (mCLL) or unmutated (uCLL) by de novo assembling IGHV transcripts from RNA-seq BAMs with CRIS and comparing the dominant clone's IGHV sequence to its top germline hit. Validated against clinical PCR-Sanger IGHV classification with high concordance across three CLL cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) — CRIS requires BWA-aligned hg38, coordinate-sorted BAMs; other builds or unsorted files are unsupported Samples have fewer than 25M RNA-seq reads per sample, insufficient for de novo assembly of the IGHV transcript Goal is full B-cell receptor repertoire profiling from mixed samples rather than CLL IGHV hypermutation status per patient

skills.description: Use when you need a quantitative batch-mixing score (complementary to kBET rejection rates) for comparing embeddings such as BEENE vs. PCA on batch-corrected vs. uncorrected scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: ilisi-batch-mixing-metric-computation
skills.search_text: ilisi-batch-mixing-metric-computation Use when you need a quantitative batch-mixing score (complementary to kBET rejection rates) for comparing embeddings such as BEENE vs. PCA on batch-corrected vs. uncorrected scRNA-seq data. When the goal is a statistical significance test of batch-label mixing rather than a local mixing index — kBET (R-only, run via rpy2) returns average test rejection rates via Pearson's chi-square and is the complementary metric When labels cannot be formatted per the API contract: batch_var must be a 1D 0/1 array for two categories and a dense one-hot matrix for more; a string label vector without encoding is invalid input When interpreting mixing alone would be misleading — iLISI should be compared across embeddings/corrections on the same data, not treated as an absolute batch-effect-free threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the inverse Local Inverse Simpson's Index (iLISI) to quantify batch mixing on a learned embedding (e.g., BEENE), where higher iLISI indicates better mixing of batch labels among neighboring cells. In the BEENE workflow, iLISI is calculated on held-out test samples via beene_model.evaluate_batch_iLisi after a seeded train/validation/test split. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Computes the inverse Local Inverse Simpson's Index (iLISI) to quantify batch mixing on a learned embedding (e.g., BEENE), where higher iLISI indicates better mixing of batch labels among neighboring cells. In the BEENE workflow, iLISI is calculated on held-out test samples via beene_model.evaluate_batch_iLisi after a seeded train/validation/test split.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a statistical significance test of batch-label mixing rather than a local mixing index — kBET (R-only, run via rpy2) returns average test rejection rates via Pearson's chi-square and is the complementary metric When labels cannot be formatted per the API contract: batch_var must be a 1D 0/1 array for two categories and a dense one-hot matrix for more; a string label vector without encoding is invalid input When interpreting mixing alone would be misleading — iLISI should be compared across embeddings/corrections on the same data, not treated as an absolute batch-effect-free threshold

skills.description: Use when two preprocessed scRNA-seq datasets have been integrated (e.g., by BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, or Scanorama) and you need quantitative batch-mixing (iLISI) and cell-type-consistency (cLISI) scores to compare correction methods.
skills.name: ilisi-clisi-metric-computation
skills.search_text: ilisi-clisi-metric-computation Use when two preprocessed scRNA-seq datasets have been integrated (e.g., by BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, or Scanorama) and you need quantitative batch-mixing (iLISI) and cell-type-consistency (cLISI) scores to compare correction methods. Integrating more than two datasets — the BATMAN implementation whose outputs these metrics benchmark supports only two datasets per run Single-dataset input with no batch structure to integrate — iLISI is undefined without batch labels Unintegrated, raw concatenated data being treated as corrected output — the paper keeps an explicit 'Original' (no-correction) baseline rather than scoring raw counts as if corrected http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computation of mean iLISI (integration Local Inverse Simpson Index) and mean cLISI on integrated single-cell RNA-seq data to quantify batch mixing versus cell-type purity, as used to benchmark BATMAN against Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Computation of mean iLISI (integration Local Inverse Simpson Index) and mean cLISI on integrated single-cell RNA-seq data to quantify batch mixing versus cell-type purity, as used to benchmark BATMAN against Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Integrating more than two datasets — the BATMAN implementation whose outputs these metrics benchmark supports only two datasets per run Single-dataset input with no batch structure to integrate — iLISI is undefined without batch labels Unintegrated, raw concatenated data being treated as corrected output — the paper keeps an explicit 'Original' (no-correction) baseline rather than scoring raw counts as if corrected

skills.description: Use when comparing robustness of signal-removal methods (SiFT, regress_out, scVI) to partial or noisy marker gene priors, with iLISI percentage degradation as the metric on single-cell RNA-seq data.
skills.name: ilisi-degradation-metric-computation
skills.search_text: ilisi-degradation-metric-computation Use when comparing robustness of signal-removal methods (SiFT, regress_out, scVI) to partial or noisy marker gene priors, with iLISI percentage degradation as the metric on single-cell RNA-seq data. No cell annotations or label sets exist to compute iLISI, so degradation cannot be evaluated (the article notes SiFT 'suffers from the general challenge of any computational method which lacks a ground truth reference'). The goal is batch correction with known discrete batch labels rather than robustness testing of continuous biological-signal filtering under a partially corrupted marker prior. Downstream analysis requires properly log-transformed expression, since filtered/corrected gene expression is no longer properly log-transformed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking procedure that quantifies how much each single-cell signal-filtering method's label-mixing performance (iLISI) degrades when prior marker knowledge is weakened, used to show SiFT's robustness versus regress_out and scVI on Drosophila wing disc cell cycle/sex filtering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that quantifies how much each single-cell signal-filtering method's label-mixing performance (iLISI) degrades when prior marker knowledge is weakened, used to show SiFT's robustness versus regress_out and scVI on Drosophila wing disc cell cycle/sex filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell annotations or label sets exist to compute iLISI, so degradation cannot be evaluated (the article notes SiFT 'suffers from the general challenge of any computational method which lacks a ground truth reference'). The goal is batch correction with known discrete batch labels rather than robustness testing of continuous biological-signal filtering under a partially corrupted marker prior. Downstream analysis requires properly log-transformed expression, since filtered/corrected gene expression is no longer properly log-transformed.

skills.description: Use when you have integrated (batch-corrected) single-cell expression or PCA-space embeddings from ≥2 batches and need quantitative iLISI/RNN scores plus runtime to compare integration methods.
skills.name: ilisi-rnn-integration-metric-computation
skills.search_text: ilisi-rnn-integration-metric-computation Use when you have integrated (batch-corrected) single-cell expression or PCA-space embeddings from ≥2 batches and need quantitative iLISI/RNN scores plus runtime to compare integration methods. The current BATMAN implementation only integrates two datasets, so this skill cannot score a single multi-batch BATMAN run across more than two inputs Only uncorrected, concatenated count matrices are available and no integration has been performed yet — iLISI/RNN evaluate corrected output, not raw data The goal is de novo batch correction rather than benchmarking; use the integration skill itself instead of the metric-computation skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies batch-effect removal and local-structure preservation after scRNA-seq integration by computing mean iLISI (inverted Local Inverse Simpson Index) and RNN (retained-neighbor-neighbor, e.g. 50-RNN or 10-RNN) scores for each integration tool. Used in the BATMAN paper to rank BATMAN against Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama, and Harmony on simulated (Splatter) and real (Muraro/Segerstolpe pancreas, 10X PBMC 8k + Pan T cells) datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Quantifies batch-effect removal and local-structure preservation after scRNA-seq integration by computing mean iLISI (inverted Local Inverse Simpson Index) and RNN (retained-neighbor-neighbor, e.g. 50-RNN or 10-RNN) scores for each integration tool. Used in the BATMAN paper to rank BATMAN against Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama, and Harmony on simulated (Splatter) and real (Muraro/Segerstolpe pancreas, 10X PBMC 8k + Pan T cells) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The current BATMAN implementation only integrates two datasets, so this skill cannot score a single multi-batch BATMAN run across more than two inputs Only uncorrected, concatenated count matrices are available and no integration has been performed yet — iLISI/RNN evaluate corrected output, not raw data The goal is de novo batch correction rather than benchmarking; use the integration skill itself instead of the metric-computation skill

skills.description: Use when validating Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification after adaptive UMI cluster pruning (e.g., Longcell step 4) by checking that pruned cluster-size distributions reproduce a matched short-read Illumina reference distribution.
skills.name: illumina-nanopore-cross-platform-umi-comparison
skills.search_text: illumina-nanopore-cross-platform-umi-comparison Use when validating Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification after adaptive UMI cluster pruning (e.g., Longcell step 4) by checking that pruned cluster-size distributions reproduce a matched short-read Illumina reference distribution. The sample lacks a matched Illumina (short-read) dataset for the same gene/cell population, so no reference UMI cluster-size distribution exists for comparison The gene under inspection has multiple isoforms, making it impossible to attribute Nanopore UMI clusters cleanly to a single isoform as the Fig. 1C comparison requires Quantification was produced by fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing (e.g., Sicelore2 or FLAMES) rather than Longcell's adaptive pruning, in which case distributions reflect error-inflated UMI counts Validation skill for Longcell's UMI-scatter-reduction pruning: compare the pruned Nanopore UMI cluster-size distribution of a single-isoform gene against the matched Illumina UMI cluster-size distribution to confirm that error-driven small clusters were correctly removed rather than true transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Validation skill for Longcell's UMI-scatter-reduction pruning: compare the pruned Nanopore UMI cluster-size distribution of a single-isoform gene against the matched Illumina UMI cluster-size distribution to confirm that error-driven small clusters were correctly removed rather than true transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample lacks a matched Illumina (short-read) dataset for the same gene/cell population, so no reference UMI cluster-size distribution exists for comparison The gene under inspection has multiple isoforms, making it impossible to attribute Nanopore UMI clusters cleanly to a single isoform as the Fig. 1C comparison requires Quantification was produced by fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing (e.g., Sicelore2 or FLAMES) rather than Longcell's adaptive pruning, in which case distributions reflect error-inflated UMI counts

skills.search_text: image-based-palette-extraction Use when the goal is to adopt a coloring theme from a publication figure or cover image and apply it to spatial transcriptomics cell-type plots while keeping palette discernibility comparable to standard palettes like matplotlib tab20. When the palette is already predefined (e.g., matplotlib tab20 or ggplot2 defaults) and only cluster-to-color assignment needs spatial optimization — use Spaco's graph-guided colorization instead of palette extraction When user-specified cell types must retain fixed colors per literature conventions — Spaco's enforcement of color-difference/spatial-distribution correspondence may not match such preferences http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Extract a coloring palette from a theme image (e.g., a journal cover) using Spaco's image-guided palette extraction, which bins colors by frequency in CIELab space, updates frequencies with the CIEDE2000 color-difference metric, and refines with farthest point sampling so the theme color is preserved while color differentiation is maximized. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-sample CyTOF/imaging mass cytometry protein-expression data (e.g. 23-sample COVID-19 IMC with 38 protein markers) to remove sample/dataset variability before clustering against manual cell-type labels.
skills.name: imaging-mass-cytometry-data-integration
skills.search_text: imaging-mass-cytometry-data-integration Use when integrating multi-sample CyTOF/imaging mass cytometry protein-expression data (e.g. 23-sample COVID-19 IMC with 38 protein markers) to remove sample/dataset variability before clustering against manual cell-type labels.
