Input is already a per-sample cell-type composition/feature table rather than raw count matrices with per-cell annotations The goal is ligand-receptor cell-cell communication inference (use the scCrossTalk find_lrpairs/get_top_lrpairs workflow instead) Data lacks cell-type annotations for MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, and S100A12+ neutrophils, so the three niche populations cannot be identified http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies per-sample proportions of specific immune cell populations (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) from annotated scRNA-seq data and aggregates them into an EAD-associated immune niche score for group comparison in liver transplantation samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: Quantifies per-sample proportions of specific immune cell populations (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) from annotated scRNA-seq data and aggregates them into an EAD-associated immune niche score for group comparison in liver transplantation samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-sample cell-type composition/feature table rather than raw count matrices with per-cell annotations The goal is ligand-receptor cell-cell communication inference (use the scCrossTalk find_lrpairs/get_top_lrpairs workflow instead) Data lacks cell-type annotations for MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, and S100A12+ neutrophils, so the three niche populations cannot be identified

skills.description: Use when a bulk-tumor transcriptome cohort has RECIST/ICB response annotations and you want to test whether pretrained tGPT attention-head entropy differs between responders (CR/PR) and non-responders (SD/PD).
skills.name: immune-checkpoint-blockade-response-group-comparison
skills.search_text: immune-checkpoint-blockade-response-group-comparison Use when a bulk-tumor transcriptome cohort has RECIST/ICB response annotations and you want to test whether pretrained tGPT attention-head entropy differs between responders (CR/PR) and non-responders (SD/PD). Input is single-cell data without bulk-tumor ICB response annotations — tGPT attention-response association was established on bulk tumor tissues You need actual expression-level modeling: tGPT uses expression rankings only, so fold changes among genes are neglected and are not recoverable from this skill The cohort lacks outcome/RECIST labels, leaving no groups to compare entropy against http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Compares tGPT-derived attention-head entropy/importance patterns computed from bulk tumor transcriptomes across RECIST response groups (CR, PR, SD, PD) in an immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) cohort, to identify heads associated with therapy response. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Compares tGPT-derived attention-head entropy/importance patterns computed from bulk tumor transcriptomes across RECIST response groups (CR, PR, SD, PD) in an immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) cohort, to identify heads associated with therapy response.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data without bulk-tumor ICB response annotations — tGPT attention-response association was established on bulk tumor tissues You need actual expression-level modeling: tGPT uses expression rankings only, so fold changes among genes are neglected and are not recoverable from this skill The cohort lacks outcome/RECIST labels, leaving no groups to compare entropy against

skills.description: Use when annotating clusters from Seurat WNN joint mRNA+ADT analysis of PBMC CITE-seq data by matching protein markers (CD14, CD86) to immune cell identities and confirming phenotypes with differential gene expression.
skills.name: immune-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: immune-cluster-annotation Use when annotating clusters from Seurat WNN joint mRNA+ADT analysis of PBMC CITE-seq data by matching protein markers (CD14, CD86) to immune cell identities and confirming phenotypes with differential gene expression. Data are mRNA-only scRNA-seq with no ADT/protein modality, so clusters cannot be anchored by canonical surface-protein markers Protein normalization has not yet been performed — dsb requires cells and background droplets defined from Cell Ranger filtered/raw outputs before WNN clustering and annotation Datasets lacking isotype control antibody measurements without consulting the dsb Supplementary Note guidance on defining the technical component http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Annotate immune cell populations from joint mRNA-protein (CITE-seq) clustering by identifying clusters via canonical marker proteins (e.g., CD14+ monocytes with high CD86) and validating their biological identity with differential transcript expression, as demonstrated for the CD86-high monocyte cluster 3 in the dsb Nature Communications study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Annotate immune cell populations from joint mRNA-protein (CITE-seq) clustering by identifying clusters via canonical marker proteins (e.g., CD14+ monocytes with high CD86) and validating their biological identity with differential transcript expression, as demonstrated for the CD86-high monocyte cluster 3 in the dsb Nature Communications study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are mRNA-only scRNA-seq with no ADT/protein modality, so clusters cannot be anchored by canonical surface-protein markers Protein normalization has not yet been performed — dsb requires cells and background droplets defined from Cell Ranger filtered/raw outputs before WNN clustering and annotation Datasets lacking isotype control antibody measurements without consulting the dsb Supplementary Note guidance on defining the technical component

skills.description: Use when WGCNA module eigengenes (or DEG lists) from a rare-disease RNA-seq experiment correlate with a phenotypic trait and you must translate the module gene lists into GO Biological Process terms to confirm immune/infiltration biology or nominate targets.
skills.name: immune-inflammatory-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: immune-inflammatory-enrichment-interpretation Use when WGCNA module eigengenes (or DEG lists) from a rare-disease RNA-seq experiment correlate with a phenotypic trait and you must translate the module gene lists into GO Biological Process terms to confirm immune/infiltration biology or nominate targets. Input is raw reads or FASTQ that has not been converted to a count table — the workflow requires count tables as the starting point for DEgenes Hunter The modules of interest do not correlate with the disease phenotypic trait — enrichment of uncorrelated modules will not support the immune/inflammatory phenotype interpretation The organism/annotation has no orthologous translation to supported databases — the article's functional analysis depends on orthologous annotation; non-model organisms without this support will yield empty enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets co-expression modules correlated with a disease phenotype (e.g. mutant animals in the Lafora disease RNA-seq dataset) by running functional enrichment on module gene lists with multiple annotation databases and checking for immune/inflammatory GO Biological Process terms, confirming known biology and surfacing candidate therapeutic targets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Interprets co-expression modules correlated with a disease phenotype (e.g. mutant animals in the Lafora disease RNA-seq dataset) by running functional enrichment on module gene lists with multiple annotation databases and checking for immune/inflammatory GO Biological Process terms, confirming known biology and surfacing candidate therapeutic targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads or FASTQ that has not been converted to a count table — the workflow requires count tables as the starting point for DEgenes Hunter The modules of interest do not correlate with the disease phenotypic trait — enrichment of uncorrelated modules will not support the immune/inflammatory phenotype interpretation The organism/annotation has no orthologous translation to supported databases — the article's functional analysis depends on orthologous annotation; non-model organisms without this support will yield empty enrichment

skills.description: Use when an independent bulk RNA-seq (e.g. GSE23649) or scRNA-seq cohort (e.g. SRP313633) of liver transplant recipients with EAD vs non-EAD labels must be scored for the niche cell populations and tested for association with EAD occurrence.
skills.name: immune-niche-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: immune-niche-signature-scoring Use when an independent bulk RNA-seq (e.g. GSE23649) or scRNA-seq cohort (e.g. SRP313633) of liver transplant recipients with EAD vs non-EAD labels must be scored for the niche cell populations and tested for association with EAD occurrence. The goal is to infer ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communications from scRNA-seq data — use the scCrossTalk find_lrpairs/enrichment workflow instead of signature scoring. The cohort lacks EAD vs non-EAD clinical labels or lacks Sample A (pre-cold-perfusion) / Sample B (2h post-portal-reperfusion) stage metadata, so the niche-occurrence association cannot be tested. Input is already a processed niche score table or feature-level summary rather than a count matrix or annotated single-cell object. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes a per-sample score reflecting the abundance of the EAD-associated immune niche identified in the single-cell landscape of human transplanted livers (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) and tests whether it discriminates EAD from non-EAD samples in independent validation cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: Computes a per-sample score reflecting the abundance of the EAD-associated immune niche identified in the single-cell landscape of human transplanted livers (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) and tests whether it discriminates EAD from non-EAD samples in independent validation cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communications from scRNA-seq data — use the scCrossTalk find_lrpairs/enrichment workflow instead of signature scoring. The cohort lacks EAD vs non-EAD clinical labels or lacks Sample A (pre-cold-perfusion) / Sample B (2h post-portal-reperfusion) stage metadata, so the niche-occurrence association cannot be tested. Input is already a processed niche score table or feature-level summary rather than a count matrix or annotated single-cell object.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., PBMC 3k with 9 Seurat clusters) need automatic cell type labels against a curated human immune reference panel, or when comparing concordance of correlation- vs enrichment-based annotation approaches.
skills.name: immune-reference-panel-matching
skills.search_text: immune-reference-panel-matching Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., PBMC 3k with 9 Seurat clusters) need automatic cell type labels against a curated human immune reference panel, or when comparing concordance of correlation- vs enrichment-based annotation approaches. The query contains novel cell types absent from the reference panels — deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Annotating cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells make deCS challenging Tissue-specific annotation is required — deCS does not take tissue information (except HCAF) into account, which may bias results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Annotates scRNA-seq cell clusters by matching cluster-level marker expression (z-scores) or top marker gene lists against pre-calculated immune reference panels such as MonacoImmune (10 main / 29 fine cell types), using deCS's two statistical approaches: Pearson correlation (PCC) and Fisher's exact test enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Annotates scRNA-seq cell clusters by matching cluster-level marker expression (z-scores) or top marker gene lists against pre-calculated immune reference panels such as MonacoImmune (10 main / 29 fine cell types), using deCS's two statistical approaches: Pearson correlation (PCC) and Fisher's exact test enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query contains novel cell types absent from the reference panels — deCS is a mapping-based annotation toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types Annotating cancer/malignant cells, where expression profile differences between healthy and malignant cells make deCS challenging Tissue-specific annotation is required — deCS does not take tissue information (except HCAF) into account, which may bias results

skills.description: Use when analyzing paired scRNA-seq + single-cell VDJ-seq data (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas T cells) to reconstruct T or B cell differentiation trajectories and assign per-cell pseudotime and branch fate probabilities.
skills.name: immune-repertoire-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: immune-repertoire-trajectory-analysis Use when analyzing paired scRNA-seq + single-cell VDJ-seq data (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas T cells) to reconstruct T or B cell differentiation trajectories and assign per-cell pseudotime and branch fate probabilities. Data lacks paired single-cell VDJ (BCR/TCR) sequencing — the workflow requires complete TCR/BCR information for filtering and pseudobulking The trajectory topology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains The dataset has too few relevant cells (e.g. only ~972 healthy B cells in Tonglin et al.), likely insufficient for miloR neighbourhood construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 A single-cell immune repertoire (scVDJ-seq) trajectory analysis workflow that constructs a VDJ feature space, infers pseudotime and branching probabilities via diffusion maps and absorbing Markov chains, and projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results back to individual cells. Implemented in R via dandelionR, replicating the Python Dandelion workflow with miloR pseudobulking and scRepertoire interoperability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: A single-cell immune repertoire (scVDJ-seq) trajectory analysis workflow that constructs a VDJ feature space, infers pseudotime and branching probabilities via diffusion maps and absorbing Markov chains, and projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results back to individual cells. Implemented in R via dandelionR, replicating the Python Dandelion workflow with miloR pseudobulking and scRepertoire interoperability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks paired single-cell VDJ (BCR/TCR) sequencing — the workflow requires complete TCR/BCR information for filtering and pseudobulking The trajectory topology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains The dataset has too few relevant cells (e.g. only ~972 healthy B cells in Tonglin et al.), likely insufficient for miloR neighbourhood construction

skills.description: Use when you need intercellular interaction predictions tied to a specific biological function (e.g., immune response GO: 0006955) on scRNA-seq data, rather than the fixed built-in criteria of tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat.
skills.name: immune-response-gene-restriction-analysis
skills.search_text: immune-response-gene-restriction-analysis Use when you need intercellular interaction predictions tied to a specific biological function (e.g., immune response GO: 0006955) on scRNA-seq data, rather than the fixed built-in criteria of tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat. When the goal is unbiased, function-agnostic interaction discovery rather than interactions tied to a specific GO biological process — the log2FC > 0.25 and GO: 0006955 restriction deliberately narrows the candidate set When you require downstream signal transduction prediction inside receiving cells — the paper notes NicheNet offers this and InterCellDB does not target it When datasets are outside human or mouse — InterCellDB covers only human and mouse databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A user-defined InterCellDB analysis that restricts cell–cell interaction inference to differentially expressed genes belonging to a specific GO biological process (here immune response, GO: 0006955), enabling function-focused intercellular network analysis and accuracy benchmarking against other tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: A user-defined InterCellDB analysis that restricts cell–cell interaction inference to differentially expressed genes belonging to a specific GO biological process (here immune response, GO: 0006955), enabling function-focused intercellular network analysis and accuracy benchmarking against other tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is unbiased, function-agnostic interaction discovery rather than interactions tied to a specific GO biological process — the log2FC > 0.25 and GO: 0006955 restriction deliberately narrows the candidate set When you require downstream signal transduction prediction inside receiving cells — the paper notes NicheNet offers this and InterCellDB does not target it When datasets are outside human or mouse — InterCellDB covers only human and mouse databases

skills.description: Use when single-cell clusters (e.g., setA clusters 4 NK cells and 5 naïve T cells) must be confirmed as supported by a cancer-immune-signature encoded space, requiring QCM/QCC > 0.5 and COMET p-values for signature/KEGG enrichment.
skills.name: immune-signature-cluster-validation
skills.search_text: immune-signature-cluster-validation Use when single-cell clusters (e.g., setA clusters 4 NK cells and 5 naïve T cells) must be confirmed as supported by a cancer-immune-signature encoded space, requiring QCM/QCC > 0.5 and COMET p-values for signature/KEGG enrichment. Clusters other than the reference immune clusters (e.g., setA clusters 1 and 2, B cells and monocytes) for which no immune-signature support claim is being tested The goal is de novo clustering or cell type discovery rather than validating previously defined clusters against the signature encoding space No curated latent space (TF/miRNA/kinase/immune signatures) is available — SCA relies on experimentally validated data for its encoded space http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Validates that specific scRNAseq cell clusters are functionally supported by a manually curated cancer-immune-signature latent space, using the SCA autoencoder's QCM/QCC reconstruction metrics (both must exceed 0.5) plus COMET (cometsc) gene-set enrichment of cluster-specific genes against immune-signature and KEGG gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Validates that specific scRNAseq cell clusters are functionally supported by a manually curated cancer-immune-signature latent space, using the SCA autoencoder's QCM/QCC reconstruction metrics (both must exceed 0.5) plus COMET (cometsc) gene-set enrichment of cluster-specific genes against immune-signature and KEGG gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters other than the reference immune clusters (e.g., setA clusters 1 and 2, B cells and monocytes) for which no immune-signature support claim is being tested The goal is de novo clustering or cell type discovery rather than validating previously defined clusters against the signature encoding space No curated latent space (TF/miRNA/kinase/immune signatures) is available — SCA relies on experimentally validated data for its encoded space

skills.description: Use when analyzing Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. myeloma, T cells) to detect recurrent gene fusions per cell and test whether fusion carriage drives target-gene overexpression.
skills.name: immunoglobulin-fusion-classification
skills.search_text: immunoglobulin-fusion-classification Use when analyzing Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. myeloma, T cells) to detect recurrent gene fusions per cell and test whether fusion carriage drives target-gene overexpression. Data are 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq single-cell libraries — scFusion is built 'for Smart-Seq data rather than 10X'. Fusions of interest are rare in highly heterogeneous tumor samples or have very low expression, where scFusion's detection power is limited. Only bulk RNA-seq data are available; scFusion is designed for scRNA-seq and jointly leverages multiple single cells from a sample. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A single-cell fusion-detection skill using scFusion (STAR chimeric reads + statistical/deep-learning models) to identify recurrent immunoglobulin gene fusions such as IgH-WHSC1 in Smart-Seq scRNA-seq and link them to oncogene overexpression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: A single-cell fusion-detection skill using scFusion (STAR chimeric reads + statistical/deep-learning models) to identify recurrent immunoglobulin gene fusions such as IgH-WHSC1 in Smart-Seq scRNA-seq and link them to oncogene overexpression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq single-cell libraries — scFusion is built 'for Smart-Seq data rather than 10X'. Fusions of interest are rare in highly heterogeneous tumor samples or have very low expression, where scFusion's detection power is limited. Only bulk RNA-seq data are available; scFusion is designed for scRNA-seq and jointly leverages multiple single cells from a sample.

skills.description: Use when starting from a bulk RNA-seq BAM aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, coordinate-sorted and indexed, and the goal is to subset reads from putative Ig loci and de novo assemble IGHV-D-J transcript contigs prior to SHM analysis.
skills.name: immunoglobulin-heavy-chain-locus-subsetting
skills.search_text: immunoglobulin-heavy-chain-locus-subsetting Use when starting from a bulk RNA-seq BAM aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, coordinate-sorted and indexed, and the goal is to subset reads from putative Ig loci and de novo assemble IGHV-D-J transcript contigs prior to SHM analysis. The input BAM is not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS will not operate correctly on such files The data is targeted/amplicon B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing (Ig-seq) rather than bulk RNA-seq (ribodepleted or polyA selected, >=25M reads per sample) — de novo locus subsetting from a whole-transcriptome alignment is unnecessary You already have assembled Ig transcript contigs and only need downstream SHM classification or contig-to-reference Ig alignment steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts RNA-seq reads aligned to the putative immunoglobulin gene loci from a hg38-aligned, coordinate-sorted BAM using sambamba, converts them to paired-end FASTQ with Picard SamToFastq, and de novo assembles the subset into Ig transcripts with Trinity — the read-extraction and assembly front end of the CRIS IGHV-D-J reconstruction pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Extracts RNA-seq reads aligned to the putative immunoglobulin gene loci from a hg38-aligned, coordinate-sorted BAM using sambamba, converts them to paired-end FASTQ with Picard SamToFastq, and de novo assembles the subset into Ig transcripts with Trinity — the read-extraction and assembly front end of the CRIS IGHV-D-J reconstruction pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input BAM is not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, or is not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS will not operate correctly on such files The data is targeted/amplicon B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing (Ig-seq) rather than bulk RNA-seq (ribodepleted or polyA selected, >=25M reads per sample) — de novo locus subsetting from a whole-transcriptome alignment is unnecessary You already have assembled Ig transcript contigs and only need downstream SHM classification or contig-to-reference Ig alignment steps

skills.description: Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) must yield the dominant IGHV gene, its percent identity to the germline, and mCLL/uCLL status, and partial-IGHV tools (e.g. V'DJer) are insufficient.
skills.name: immunoglobulin-transcript-de-novo-assembly
skills.search_text: immunoglobulin-transcript-de-novo-assembly Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) must yield the dominant IGHV gene, its percent identity to the germline, and mCLL/uCLL status, and partial-IGHV tools (e.g. V'DJer) are insufficient. The BAM is not aligned to hg38 or is not coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS requires this exact input state The goal is only a partial-IGHV repertoire sketch rather than full-length IGHV reconstruction and SHM classification Samples have far fewer than 25M reads, insufficient for de novo assembly of Ig transcripts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 A CRIS-pipeline skill that extracts RNA-seq reads aligned to Ig gene loci from a hg38-aligned BAM, assembles Ig transcripts de novo with Trinity, and aligns contigs to reference Ig sequences with BLAST/IgBLAST to reconstruct the full IGHV region and classify somatic hypermutation status. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021

skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM is not aligned to hg38 or is not coordinate-sorted/indexed — CRIS requires this exact input state The goal is only a partial-IGHV repertoire sketch rather than full-length IGHV reconstruction and SHM classification Samples have far fewer than 25M reads, insufficient for de novo assembly of Ig transcripts

skills.description: Use when you have pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq from immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) patients with survival and clinical response metadata, and need to test whether a published gene-signature risk score separates responders from non-responders.
skills.name: immunotherapy-response-stratification
skills.search_text: immunotherapy-response-stratification Use when you have pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq from immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) patients with survival and clinical response metadata, and need to test whether a published gene-signature risk score separates responders from non-responders. The dataset has no paired clinical survival or treatment-response metadata, so neither the Kaplan-Meier split nor the responder/non-responder Wilcoxon comparison can be evaluated The goal is deconvolving cell-type abundances from bulk RNA-seq (that is DCNet's own task), not scoring a gene signature for patient stratification Expression values are already log-transformed by the provider — a second log2(x+1) transformation would distort the risk-score terms http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Stratifies pre-treatment melanoma patients into anti-PD-1 responder-relevant high- and low-risk groups by scoring a 33-gene prognostic signature (log10 hazard ratio × log2(x+1) expression) on bulk RNA-seq and testing Kaplan-Meier survival and response-group differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Stratifies pre-treatment melanoma patients into anti-PD-1 responder-relevant high- and low-risk groups by scoring a 33-gene prognostic signature (log10 hazard ratio × log2(x+1) expression) on bulk RNA-seq and testing Kaplan-Meier survival and response-group differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no paired clinical survival or treatment-response metadata, so neither the Kaplan-Meier split nor the responder/non-responder Wilcoxon comparison can be evaluated The goal is deconvolving cell-type abundances from bulk RNA-seq (that is DCNet's own task), not scoring a gene signature for patient stratification Expression values are already log-transformed by the provider — a second log2(x+1) transformation would distort the risk-score terms

skills.description: Use when comparing sensitivity of single-cell pathway analysis methods against a ground-truth perturbation, i.e. the analysis goal is a controlled simulation where the true significant pathway is known by construction.

skills.search_text: implanted-pathway-benchmark-design Use when comparing sensitivity of single-cell pathway analysis methods against a ground-truth perturbation, i.e. the analysis goal is a controlled simulation where the true significant pathway is known by construction. skills.summary: Design a Splatter-based sensitivity benchmark in which a 200-gene target pathway is implanted into simulated single-cell populations over a panel of ~17,000 background genes, then measure how often SCPA and competitor tools (fGSEA, iDEA, GSVA, AUCell, Vision, ssGSEA) recover the implanted pathway.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological interpretation of a real dataset (e.g. T cell activation dynamics) rather than method-level sensitivity benchmarking — use SCPA's compare_pathways directly on the data instead of simulating No ground truth exists for the significant pathway, as in a purely exploratory analysis where sensitivity cannot be computed

skills.name: impossible-barcode-combination-quantification
skills.search_text: impossible-barcode-combination-quantification Use when a plate-prepared scRNA-seq library was sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and you need to estimate the sample index swapping fraction from the raw FASTQ/BCL data. Data were generated on non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g., HiSeq 2500), where index swapping is negligible and the regression would mostly measure noise Droplet-based (e.g., 10x Genomics) data where swapped molecules should instead be removed by the UMI/cell-barcode/gene molecule-exclusion algorithm rather than quantified by impossible-combination regression Only processed count matrices are available; the method requires raw reads and sample barcodes to detect impossible combinations during demultiplexing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies the fraction of barcode-swapped reads in plate-based scRNA-seq data (e.g., the Richard et al. mouse T-cell plates sequenced on HiSeq 4000) by demultiplexing to retain 'impossible' sample-barcode combinations and regressing their library sizes on the reads available for swapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of barcode-swapped reads in plate-based scRNA-seq data (e.g., the Richard et al. mouse T-cell plates sequenced on HiSeq 4000) by demultiplexing to retain 'impossible' sample-barcode combinations and regressing their library sizes on the reads available for swapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were generated on non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g., HiSeq 2500), where index swapping is negligible and the regression would mostly measure noise Droplet-based (e.g., 10x Genomics) data where swapped molecules should instead be removed by the UMI/cell-barcode/gene molecule-exclusion algorithm rather than quantified by impossible-combination regression Only processed count matrices are available; the method requires raw reads and sample barcodes to detect impossible combinations during demultiplexing

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq data from parthenogenetic (pESC) and androgenetic (aESC) embryonic stem cells (or other allele-biased expression settings) must be screened to confirm a known imprinted cis-NAT pair is identified and expressed from opposite parental alleles.
skills.name: imprinted-locus-verification
skills.search_text: imprinted-locus-verification Use when RNA-seq data from parthenogenetic (pESC) and androgenetic (aESC) embryonic stem cells (or other allele-biased expression settings) must be screened to confirm a known imprinted cis-NAT pair is identified and expressed from opposite parental alleles. Raw (unprocessed) FASTQ data — CCIVR requires RNA-seq data already processed by third-party programs such as STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression profiling, and DESeq2 for statistics Inputs lacking strand-direction or accurate gene annotation, since CCIVR's prediction depends on annotation accuracy of structure and strand direction deposited in databases Strand-specific novel transcript discovery without a genome annotation — tools like NASTI-seq or NATpipe are designed for de novo or strand-error-aware detection instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Verifies that a known imprinted cis-NAT pair (e.g. KCNQ1OT1/KCNQ1) is recovered from RNA-seq of parthenogenetic and androgenetic embryonic stem cells by running CCIVR, computing sense–antisense expression correlations from DEG columns, and confirming the pair falls in the negatively correlated set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Verifies that a known imprinted cis-NAT pair (e.g. KCNQ1OT1/KCNQ1) is recovered from RNA-seq of parthenogenetic and androgenetic embryonic stem cells by running CCIVR, computing sense–antisense expression correlations from DEG columns, and confirming the pair falls in the negatively correlated set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw (unprocessed) FASTQ data — CCIVR requires RNA-seq data already processed by third-party programs such as STAR for mapping, RSEM for expression profiling, and DESeq2 for statistics Inputs lacking strand-direction or accurate gene annotation, since CCIVR's prediction depends on annotation accuracy of structure and strand direction deposited in databases Strand-specific novel transcript discovery without a genome annotation — tools like NASTI-seq or NATpipe are designed for de novo or strand-error-aware detection instead

skills.description: Use when an imputed hd5 matrix (e.g. step2/imputation.step2.hd5) and a ground-truth matrix (e.g. example.hd5) with a masked input (e.g. example.msk90.hd5) are available and entrywise imputation accuracy must be quantified and decomposed by zero class.
skills.name: imputation-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: imputation-accuracy-evaluation Use when an imputed hd5 matrix (e.g. step2/imputation.step2.hd5) and a ground-truth matrix (e.g. example.hd5) with a masked input (e.g. example.msk90.hd5) are available and entrywise imputation accuracy must be quantified and decomposed by zero class. No true ground truth exists and it is set to be the same as the input (as in the mouse brain 10x example) — error metrics against the input are not meaningful imputation accuracy. Only zero-classification behavior (not accuracy) is of interest — the article itself notes LATE/TRANSLATE never distinguish biological from technical zeros when imputing. The step2/ folder with imputation.step2.hd5 has not been generated by a LATE or TRANSLATE run yet. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Decomposes the overall imputation error gtMSEall of an LATE/TRANSLATE-imputed single-cell RNA-seq matrix into entry-class errors gtMSEnz, gtMSEbiol, and gtMSEtech on the log10(count+1) scale, and verifies the weighted decomposition with the zero proportions p0 and q0. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Decomposes the overall imputation error gtMSEall of an LATE/TRANSLATE-imputed single-cell RNA-seq matrix into entry-class errors gtMSEnz, gtMSEbiol, and gtMSEtech on the log10(count+1) scale, and verifies the weighted decomposition with the zero proportions p0 and q0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No true ground truth exists and it is set to be the same as the input (as in the mouse brain 10x example) — error metrics against the input are not meaningful imputation accuracy. Only zero-classification behavior (not accuracy) is of interest — the article itself notes LATE/TRANSLATE never distinguish biological from technical zeros when imputing. The step2/ folder with imputation.step2.hd5 has not been generated by a LATE or TRANSLATE run yet.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing an imputation method to fill missing ctp/ctnu entries (individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells, set to missing via preprocess.pseudobulk with ct_cut=10) before fitting CTMM to pseudobulk data.
skills.name: imputation-accuracy-evaluation-correlation-mse
skills.search_text: imputation-accuracy-evaluation-correlation-mse Decision support for choosing an imputation method to fill missing ctp/ctnu entries (individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells, set to missing via preprocess.pseudobulk with ct_cut=10) before fitting CTMM to pseudobulk data. The data has no missing ctp/ctnu entries (e.g. all individual-cell type pairs exceed the 10-cell threshold), so no imputation or accuracy evaluation is needed The goal is imputing raw single-cell counts or per-cell expression rather than individual-level pseudobulk (ctp) and noise variance (ctnu) matrices used as CTMM input Benchmark matrix-completion imputation of cell type-specific pseudobulk (ctp) and cell type-specific noise variance (ctnu) matrices by holding out masked entries as ground truth and scoring transcriptome-wide softImpute against alternatives using Pearson correlation and mean squared error. This establishes that transcriptome-wide softImpute is the imputation approach used to fill individual-cell type pair entries with <=10 cells before CTMM fitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Benchmark matrix-completion imputation of cell type-specific pseudobulk (ctp) and cell type-specific noise variance (ctnu) matrices by holding out masked entries as ground truth and scoring transcriptome-wide softImpute against alternatives using Pearson correlation and mean squared error. This establishes that transcriptome-wide softImpute is the imputation approach used to fill individual-cell type pair entries with <=10 cells before CTMM fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data has no missing ctp/ctnu entries (e.g. all individual-cell type pairs exceed the 10-cell threshold), so no imputation or accuracy evaluation is needed The goal is imputing raw single-cell counts or per-cell expression rather than individual-level pseudobulk (ctp) and noise variance (ctnu) matrices used as CTMM input

skills.description: Use when you have an imputed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus the original values and a known synthetic-dropout mask, and need per-method accuracy scores (median L1, RMSE, cosine similarity) at each dropout rate.
skills.name: imputation-accuracy-metric-computation
skills.search_text: imputation-accuracy-metric-computation Use when you have an imputed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus the original values and a known synthetic-dropout mask, and need per-method accuracy scores (median L1, RMSE, cosine similarity) at each dropout rate. Evaluating imputation of naturally missing values, where no ground-truth true values exist — this skill requires known true values retained from synthetic masking Benchmarking clustering performance of imputation methods instead of gene-imputation accuracy — scGCL also supports clustering tasks (node, clustering, similarity) that need different metrics The input matrix has no non-zero entries to mask, or the data is not scRNA-seq expression in the h5 format scGCL expects http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes median L1 distance, RMSE and cosine similarity between imputed and true values on synthetically masked scRNA-seq entries (10%, 30% and 50% scVI-style dropout) to benchmark imputation methods such as scGCL against AutoClass, GraphSCI and MAGIC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Computes median L1 distance, RMSE and cosine similarity between imputed and true values on synthetically masked scRNA-seq entries (10%, 30% and 50% scVI-style dropout) to benchmark imputation methods such as scGCL against AutoClass, GraphSCI and MAGIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating imputation of naturally missing values, where no ground-truth true values exist — this skill requires known true values retained from synthetic masking Benchmarking clustering performance of imputation methods instead of gene-imputation accuracy — scGCL also supports clustering tasks (node, clustering, similarity) that need different metrics The input matrix has no non-zero entries to mask, or the data is not scRNA-seq expression in the h5 format scGCL expects

skills.description: Use when comparing TWAS weight-training methods (summary-level PRS methods vs FUSION) by imputation accuracy, and a held-out individual-level genotype+expression reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=315) is available to compute per-gene test R2.
skills.name: imputation-accuracy-r2-evaluation
skills.search_text: imputation-accuracy-r2-evaluation Use when comparing TWAS weight-training methods (summary-level PRS methods vs FUSION) by imputation accuracy, and a held-out individual-level genotype+expression reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=315) is available to compute per-gene test R2. No held-out individual-level genotype and expression data exist for the target tissue — per-gene test R2 cannot be computed and only out-of-sample TWAS associations (Stage II) are possible The goal is the Stage II gene-phenotype association test itself, not the benchmarking of weight-training methods; use the omnibus ACAT-O TWAS workflow instead Working in non-European populations — eQTLGen-derived weights and their R2 benchmarks reflect individuals of European descent and may not transfer Benchmark protocol for TWAS Stage I GReX imputation models: trained eQTL weights (from P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS on eQTLGen summary data, or FUSION on individual-level GTEx V6) are evaluated by predicting expression in 315 held-out GTEx V8 whole-blood samples and computing per-gene test R2, counting 'valid' models at R2 > 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for TWAS Stage I GReX imputation models: trained eQTL weights (from P+T, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS on eQTLGen summary data, or FUSION on individual-level GTEx V6) are evaluated by predicting expression in 315 held-out GTEx V8 whole-blood samples and computing per-gene test R2, counting 'valid' models at R2 > 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No held-out individual-level genotype and expression data exist for the target tissue — per-gene test R2 cannot be computed and only out-of-sample TWAS associations (Stage II) are possible The goal is the Stage II gene-phenotype association test itself, not the benchmarking of weight-training methods; use the omnibus ACAT-O TWAS workflow instead Working in non-European populations — eQTLGen-derived weights and their R2 benchmarks reflect individuals of European descent and may not transfer

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare gene expression imputation accuracy across multiple ST integration methods by holding out measured genes and computing MAE against ground truth.
skills.name: imputation-baseline-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: imputation-baseline-method-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively compare gene expression imputation accuracy across multiple ST integration methods by holding out measured genes and computing MAE against ground truth. Your spatial data already covers the whole transcriptome (e.g. Visium or Slide-seq with full coverage), so there are no unmeasured genes to impute You lack a paired scRNA-seq reference annotated for cell types — all seven benchmarked imputation methods are reference-based You need cell-type proportion deconvolution per spot rather than whole-transcriptome imputation at single-cell resolution (use RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Benchmarks SpatialScope against seven existing gene imputation methods (Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE, SpaOTsc, novoSpaRc, stPlus, Seurat) using leave-one-out cortical layer marker genes in the MERFISH MOp dataset, quantifying imputation accuracy via mean absolute error (MAE). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks SpatialScope against seven existing gene imputation methods (Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE, SpaOTsc, novoSpaRc, stPlus, Seurat) using leave-one-out cortical layer marker genes in the MERFISH MOp dataset, quantifying imputation accuracy via mean absolute error (MAE).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your spatial data already covers the whole transcriptome (e.g. Visium or Slide-seq with full coverage), so there are no unmeasured genes to impute You lack a paired scRNA-seq reference annotated for cell types — all seven benchmarked imputation methods are reference-based You need cell-type proportion deconvolution per spot rather than whole-transcriptome imputation at single-cell resolution (use RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD instead)

skills.description: Use when a dropout-affected scRNA-seq matrix and its dropout-free reference counterpart are available, and you need to rank competing imputation techniques by recovery accuracy and computational efficiency.
skills.name: imputation-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: imputation-benchmark-comparison Use when a dropout-affected scRNA-seq matrix and its dropout-free reference counterpart are available, and you need to rank competing imputation techniques by recovery accuracy and computational efficiency. The dataset is a small genomic dataset, where SERM's distribution estimated from a small data fraction may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputation (per the paper's discussion) Only a single noisy matrix without a dropout-free reference or simulated-dropout ground truth exists, making Pearson-recovery evaluation impossible The observed matrix contains experimentally observed dropouts rather than simulated sampling-efficiency loss, breaking the reference-vs-observed benchmark design used in this paper http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods (e.g., SERM against MAGIC, mcImpute, AutoImpute, DeepImpute, SAUCIE) on the same dropout-affected matrices, comparing recovery accuracy (Pearson coefficients, cluster quality indices) and wall-clock runtime against the reference data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods (e.g., SERM against MAGIC, mcImpute, AutoImpute, DeepImpute, SAUCIE) on the same dropout-affected matrices, comparing recovery accuracy (Pearson coefficients, cluster quality indices) and wall-clock runtime against the reference data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a small genomic dataset, where SERM's distribution estimated from a small data fraction may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputation (per the paper's discussion) Only a single noisy matrix without a dropout-free reference or simulated-dropout ground truth exists, making Pearson-recovery evaluation impossible The observed matrix contains experimentally observed dropouts rather than simulated sampling-efficiency loss, breaking the reference-vs-observed benchmark design used in this paper

skills.description: Use when a new or existing scRNA-seq imputation method needs head-to-head evaluation against published imputers on simulated or real developmental datasets, scored by downstream pseudotime, clustering, or correlation metrics.
skills.name: imputation-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: imputation-benchmark-comparison Use when a new or existing scRNA-seq imputation method needs head-to-head evaluation against published imputers on simulated or real developmental datasets, scored by downstream pseudotime, clustering, or correlation metrics. The goal is a single-dataset method application rather than a comparative benchmark — no competitor imputers or ground-truth labels/time orderings are available Input data lacks QC or cell-type/trajectory ground truth, making POS/Kendall or clustering-based evaluation meaningless Generalizing conclusions beyond benchmarked datasets is desired — the paper cautions it is premature to conclude Bfimpute will outperform across all datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark a scRNA-seq imputation method (e.g., Bfimpute) against competing imputers (scImpute, DrImpute, SCRABBLE, netNMF-sc) on raw and imputed count matrices using downstream tasks such as pseudotime inference (POS, Kendall's tau), PCA clustering, and cell-to-cell correlation, as done in the Bfimpute paper (Cell Reports Methods 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Benchmark a scRNA-seq imputation method (e.g., Bfimpute) against competing imputers (scImpute, DrImpute, SCRABBLE, netNMF-sc) on raw and imputed count matrices using downstream tasks such as pseudotime inference (POS, Kendall's tau), PCA clustering, and cell-to-cell correlation, as done in the Bfimpute paper (Cell Reports Methods 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single-dataset method application rather than a comparative benchmark — no competitor imputers or ground-truth labels/time orderings are available Input data lacks QC or cell-type/trajectory ground truth, making POS/Kendall or clustering-based evaluation meaningless Generalizing conclusions beyond benchmarked datasets is desired — the paper cautions it is premature to conclude Bfimpute will outperform across all datasets

skills.description: Use when training and test single-cell multi-omic data are not perfectly cell-type aligned or come from different tissues/protocols (PBMC vs CBMC, CITE-seq vs REAP-seq), and per-protein imputation accuracy must be quantified against measured protein levels.
skills.name: imputation-correlation-analysis-vs-measured-proteins
skills.search_text: imputation-correlation-analysis-vs-measured-proteins Use when training and test single-cell multi-omic data are not perfectly cell-type aligned or come from different tissues/protocols (PBMC vs CBMC, CITE-seq vs REAP-seq), and per-protein imputation accuracy must be quantified against measured protein levels. Input expression is TPM or RPKM rather than UMI-based counts — cTP-net only applies to count-based (UMI) expression input, and accuracy for TPM/RPKM data is untested Target cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage — generalization of these immune-marker imputations outside hematopoietic cells was not evaluated No measured protein (ADT) data are available for the test set, since this skill's evaluation requires computing correlations against measured protein abundances http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Cross-cell Pearson correlation benchmarking of cTP-net-imputed surface protein abundances against measured CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT counts, specifically to test generalization when the test tissue or protocol differs from training (e.g., train CITE-CBMC → test CITE-PBMC, train CITE-seq → test REAP-seq). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Cross-cell Pearson correlation benchmarking of cTP-net-imputed surface protein abundances against measured CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT counts, specifically to test generalization when the test tissue or protocol differs from training (e.g., train CITE-CBMC → test CITE-PBMC, train CITE-seq → test REAP-seq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression is TPM or RPKM rather than UMI-based counts — cTP-net only applies to count-based (UMI) expression input, and accuracy for TPM/RPKM data is untested Target cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage — generalization of these immune-marker imputations outside hematopoietic cells was not evaluated No measured protein (ADT) data are available for the test set, since this skill's evaluation requires computing correlations against measured protein abundances

skills.description: Use when comparing how much different imputation strategies (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) improve cell-type clustering of sparse scRNA-seq count matrices, measured by ARI against original cell annotations.
skills.name: imputation-method-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: imputation-method-benchmark-comparison Use when comparing how much different imputation strategies (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) improve cell-type clustering of sparse scRNA-seq count matrices, measured by ARI against original cell annotations. Datasets so large that third-party imputers exhaust system memory (in the paper, scImpute/drImpute/MAGIC could not be run on ~68,000 PBMC cells, so only AutoImpute was evaluated there) — restrict the comparison accordingly. Raw (non-log-transformed, non-preprocessed) count matrices — AutoImpute.py expects a pre-processed count single-cell matrix; raw data must first pass through the R pre-processing pipeline. Evaluating imputation quality by expression-value recovery on masked entries rather than downstream clustering — this skill scores ARI of K-means clustering only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks single-cell RNA-seq dropout imputation methods (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) against a no-imputation baseline by running K-means on log2-transformed expression matrices and scoring cell-clustering accuracy with Adjusted Rand Index, exactly as in the AutoImpute paper's Table 1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-cell RNA-seq dropout imputation methods (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) against a no-imputation baseline by running K-means on log2-transformed expression matrices and scoring cell-clustering accuracy with Adjusted Rand Index, exactly as in the AutoImpute paper's Table 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets so large that third-party imputers exhaust system memory (in the paper, scImpute/drImpute/MAGIC could not be run on ~68,000 PBMC cells, so only AutoImpute was evaluated there) — restrict the comparison accordingly. Raw (non-log-transformed, non-preprocessed) count matrices — AutoImpute.py expects a pre-processed count single-cell matrix; raw data must first pass through the R pre-processing pipeline. Evaluating imputation quality by expression-value recovery on masked entries rather than downstream clustering — this skill scores ARI of K-means clustering only.

skills.description: Use when comparing whether an imputation method improves downstream clustering quality over raw data and competitor imputers on real scRNA-seq datasets, using clustering-quality indices and significance tests.
skills.name: imputation-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: imputation-method-benchmarking Use when comparing whether an imputation method improves downstream clustering quality over raw data and competitor imputers on real scRNA-seq datasets, using clustering-quality indices and significance tests. The goal is imputation accuracy on masked entries rather than downstream clustering quality (use the 30%-masked-genes simulation protocol instead) The dataset lacks known cell-type labels, since k requires the true number of cell types and ARI-based PI requires reference labels Input is bulk RNA-seq or non-single-cell data, which cannot measure cell-to-cell heterogeneity as described http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods (scISR, scImpute, SAVER, MAGIC, DrImpute, scScope, DCA, DeepImpute, BISCUIT) against raw data by clustering imputed matrices with k-means and scoring cluster quality, following the scISR evaluation protocol. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods (scISR, scImpute, SAVER, MAGIC, DrImpute, scScope, DCA, DeepImpute, BISCUIT) against raw data by clustering imputed matrices with k-means and scoring cluster quality, following the scISR evaluation protocol.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is imputation accuracy on masked entries rather than downstream clustering quality (use the 30%-masked-genes simulation protocol instead) The dataset lacks known cell-type labels, since k requires the true number of cell types and ARI-based PI requires reference labels Input is bulk RNA-seq or non-single-cell data, which cannot measure cell-to-cell heterogeneity as described

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and you need to quantify whether imputation improves downstream clustering versus raw data and control methods.

skills.search_text: imputation-method-benchmarking-across-datasets Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and you need to quantify whether imputation improves downstream clustering versus raw data and control methods. skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-Seq imputation methods (AutoClass vs DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC) by K-means clustering real count matrices and comparing ARI, JI, NMI, and purity against known cell-type labels, as in Table 1 of the AutoClass paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are simulated with known true counts, where direct data-recovery metrics (e.g., correlation to truecounts.csv) are more appropriate than clustering benchmarks The dataset lacks trusted cell-type labels, so ARI/JI/NMI/purity cannot be computed against ground truth The goal is differential expression analysis or batch effect removal rather than clustering-based imputation benchmarking

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime/scaling of scRNA-seq imputation methods on large datasets (tens of thousands of cells), e.g. to decide which imputer is tractable for >10,000-cell matrices on a single core.
skills.name: imputation-method-comparison
skills.search_text: imputation-method-comparison Use when comparing runtime/scaling of scRNA-seq imputation methods on large datasets (tens of thousands of cells), e.g. to decide which imputer is tractable for >10,000-cell matrices on a single core. When the goal is to evaluate imputation accuracy (e.g., preserving true biological zeros) rather than computational runtime — ALRA's thresholding-based zero preservation is a separate capability not measured here When the dataset is small (fewer than ~10,000 cells) — all five methods are tractable, so runtime benchmarking does not discriminate between them When the input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix — DCA and MAGIC treat all zeros as 'missing data' and densify the matrix, which is irrelevant for non-count data Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime and scaling behavior of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, scImpute, SAVER) on progressively larger cell-count subsets, using the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex dataset as the testbed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime and scaling behavior of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, scImpute, SAVER) on progressively larger cell-count subsets, using the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex dataset as the testbed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to evaluate imputation accuracy (e.g., preserving true biological zeros) rather than computational runtime — ALRA's thresholding-based zero preservation is a separate capability not measured here When the dataset is small (fewer than ~10,000 cells) — all five methods are tractable, so runtime benchmarking does not discriminate between them When the input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix — DCA and MAGIC treat all zeros as 'missing data' and densify the matrix, which is irrelevant for non-count data

skills.description: Use when you have imputed scRNA-seq matrices from multiple methods on log10(count+1) scale plus ground truth, and need to visually compare which methods recover nonlinear gene-gene patterns for selected gene pairs.
skills.name: imputation-method-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: imputation-method-comparison-across-datasets Use when you have imputed scRNA-seq matrices from multiple methods on log10(count+1) scale plus ground truth, and need to visually compare which methods recover nonlinear gene-gene patterns for selected gene pairs. skills.search_text: in-silico-single-cell-mixture-construction Use when benchmarking deconvolution or coupled clustering of bulk/single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and HiChIP data and true subpopulation-specific profiles are needed as ground truth for computing PCC against predicted profiles. skills.summary: Generate realistic synthetic scRNA-seq data by training GRouNdGAN, a GRN-guided causal implicit GAN, on a preprocessed experimental reference dataset and a GRNBoost2-inferred causal gene regulatory network, then sampling cells in silico.

skills.description: Use when you have context-specific genome-scale metabolic models (e.g. built with rFASTCORMICS on Recon2.04/Recon3D_01) with a VBOF and need to find genes essential to viral biomass but not host growth.

skills.search_text: in-silico-single-gene-deletion-analysis Use when you have context-specific genome-scale metabolic models (e.g. built with rFASTCORMICS on Recon2.04/Recon3D_01) with a VBOF and need to find genes essential to viral biomass but not host growth. You need synergistic gene-pair effects (essential + non-essential combinations) — use double gene deletion (doubleGeneDeletion) instead, as single deletion alone cannot capture pair synergy The model is a generic reconstruction without the VBOF or without a host biomass reaction to constrain — knockout effects would not be attributable to viral replication The question is drug repositioning or pathway enrichment rather than essentiality calling — those downstream steps require the essential gene list as input but use different tools (DrugBank mapping, KEGG/Enrichr) http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Systematic single-gene deletion via flux balance analysis on context-specific infected-lung metabolic models carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF), to identify host genes whose knockout abolishes viral biomass production while preserving host biomass maintenance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331

skills.when_to_use_negative: You need synergistic gene-pair effects (essential + non-essential combinations) — use double gene deletion (doubleGeneDeletion) instead, as single deletion alone cannot capture pair synergy The model is a generic reconstruction without the VBOF or without a host biomass reaction to constrain — knockout effects would not be attributable to viral replication The question is drug repositioning or pathway enrichment rather than essentiality calling — those downstream steps require the essential gene list as input but use different tools (DrugBank mapping, KEGG/Enrichr)

skills.description: Use when you have a trained GRouNdGAN checkpoint and an imposed (e.g., GRNBoost2- or PPCOR-derived) bipartite TF-gene GRN, and you want to test whether knocking out each TF significantly alters its target genes in simulated cells.
skills.name: in-silico-tf-knockout-simulation
skills.search_text: in-silico-tf-knockout-simulation Use when you have a trained GRouNdGAN checkpoint and an imposed (e.g., GRNBoost2- or PPCOR-derived) bipartite TF-gene GRN, and you want to test whether knocking out each TF significantly alters its target genes in simulated cells. The goal is to predict real experimental TF knockout outcomes in biological cells — GRouNdGAN is a generative simulator, not a predictive model, and outcome prediction would require a high-quality GRN plus additional data modalities such as (sc)ATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq The GRN contains multi-layer or TF-gene-phenotype edges — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN The model checkpoint was trained on a different reference dataset — GRouNdGAN must be retrained for a new dataset rather than perturbed out of context http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Use GRouNdGAN, a causal-implicit GAN, to sample from interventional distributions in which a transcription factor is knocked out, then quantify the effect of the knockout on each TF-gene edge in the imposed GRN via matched Wilcoxon testing with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. skills.summary: Use GRouNdGAN, a causal-implicit GAN, to sample from interventional distributions in which a transcription factor is knocked out, then quantify the effect of the knockout on each TF-gene edge in the imposed GRN via matched Wilcoxon testing with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to predict real experimental TF knockout outcomes in biological cells — GRouNdGAN is a generative simulator, not a predictive model, and outcome prediction would require a high-quality GRN plus additional data modalities such as (sc)ATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq The GRN contains multi-layer or TF-gene-phenotype edges — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN The model checkpoint was trained on a different reference dataset — GRouNdGAN must be retrained for a new dataset rather than perturbed out of context

skills.description: Use when CellOracle in silico TF perturbation simulations must be converted into quantitative perturbation scores to rank candidate regulators (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) for experimental validation.

skills.search_text: in-silico-transcription-factor-perturbation-simulation Use when CellOracle in silico TF perturbation simulations must be converted into quantitative perturbation scores to rank candidate regulators (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) for experimental validation. The goal is GRN inference or network-topology analysis from scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data rather than scoring perturbation effects against a reference trajectory No pseudotime-derived differentiation gradient or reference trajectory exists for the system, so simulated transitions cannot be compared to a reference vector field The candidates of interest are not transcription factors; the study scope was mainly focused on TFs associated with installing new cell identities (KO or overexpression) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies CellOracle in silico TF perturbation simulations by converting simulated cell-state transitions into the same 2D grid vector-field format as the pseudotime-derived differentiation gradient and taking their per-grid-point inner product. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is GRN inference or network-topology analysis from scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data rather than scoring perturbation effects against a reference trajectory No pseudotime-derived differentiation gradient or reference trajectory exists for the system, so simulated transitions cannot be compared to a reference vector field The candidates of interest are not transcription factors; the study scope was mainly focused on TFs associated with installing new cell identities (KO or overexpression)

skills.description: Use when two FateCompass differential TF activity result sets exist (e.g. mouse in vivo E15.5 and human in vitro beta differentiation) and the goal is to quantify shared versus system-specific beta-cell regulators.

skills.name: independent-component-analysis-decomposition
skills.search_text: independent-component-analysis-decomposition Use when a single-dataset TME scRNA-seq expression matrix must be decomposed into independent gene-expression programs (MeCs), or when benchmarking ICA vs NMF recovery of known gene expression programs across pooled cohorts. The goal is joint multi-dataset integration/batch correction via shared latent representations (Harmony, scArches, scVI) rather than decomposing a single expression matrix into independent components. A supervised annotation against curated reference cell-type definitions (CIBERSORT, Azimuth, Human Primary Cell Atlas) is sufficient and the user does not need data-learnt programs. The input is not a raw/normalized expression matrix but an already-decomposed latent space or precomputed component table. skills.description: Use when a trained model (e.g., im6A-TS-CNN on 41-nt RNA sequences) must be evaluated on a separate benchmark test set, and per-dataset Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC values must be compared against cross-validation results.
skills.name: independent-dataset-testing
skills.search_text: independent-dataset-testing Use when a trained model (e.g., im6A-TS-CNN on 41-nt RNA sequences) must be evaluated on a separate benchmark test set, and per-dataset Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC values must be compared against cross-validation results. You only need within-training-set performance — 5-fold cross-validation on the training set already covers this; the independent test is a separate held-out evaluation. Your sequences have pairwise similarity ≥80% — the article used CD-HIT to make sure sequence similarity of the dataset was less than 80%, so unfiltered test sets could inflate independent-test metrics through train/test leakage. The task requires cross-species or cross-tissue generalization (training on one tissue, testing on another) — the article handles that under a separate cross-species and cross-tissue validation step, not the standard independent dataset test. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Held-out (independent) dataset evaluation of a trained tissue-specific m6A classifier, recording Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC per species-tissue dataset (e.g., h_b, m_k, r_k) alongside 5-fold cross-validation results to demonstrate model stability and generalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Held-out (independent) dataset evaluation of a trained tissue-specific m6A classifier, recording Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC per species-tissue dataset (e.g., h_b, m_k, r_k) alongside 5-fold cross-validation results to demonstrate model stability and generalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need within-training-set performance — 5-fold cross-validation on the training set already covers this; the independent test is a separate held-out evaluation. Your sequences have pairwise similarity ≥80% — the article used CD-HIT to make sure sequence similarity of the dataset was less than 80%, so unfiltered test sets could inflate independent-test metrics through train/test leakage. The task requires cross-species or cross-tissue generalization (training on one tissue, testing on another) — the article handles that under a separate cross-species and cross-tissue validation step, not the standard independent dataset test.

skills.description: Use when you have a large family of test p-values (e.g., ~20k genes from edgeR or 50 camera gene-set tests) plus an independent continuous covariate like average expression, and you need FDR-controlled calls (FDR < 0.1 or < 0.05) with maximal power.
skills.name: independent-hypothesis-weighting-multiple-testing
skills.search_text: independent-hypothesis-weighting-multiple-testing Use when you have a large family of test p-values (e.g., ~20k genes from edgeR or 50 camera gene-set tests) plus an independent continuous covariate like average expression, and you need FDR-controlled calls (FDR < 0.1 or < 0.05) with maximal power. No independent covariate is available for the tested hypotheses (IHW's power gain depends on an informative, null-independent covariate such as average gene expression) The p-value family is small or has a simple flat structure where plain Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control is sufficient The covariate is not independent of the test statistic under the null hypothesis (e.g., it is derived from the same counts driving the p-values directly) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Independent Hypothesis Weighting (IHW) to control FDR with improved power by exploiting a continuous independent covariate (here, average gene expression) when correcting gene-level and gene-set p-values from single-cell clonal differential expression analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0

skills.description: Use when a controlled induction experiment (e.g. doxycycline-inducible miRNA in scRNA-seq) yields induced vs uninduced cell profiles and you must quantify whether a miRNA-inference method recovers the induction as logFC with significance.
skills.name: induced-vs-uninduced-logfc-comparison
skills.search_text: induced-vs-uninduced-logfc-comparison Use when a controlled induction experiment (e.g. doxycycline-inducible miRNA in scRNA-seq) yields induced vs uninduced cell profiles and you must quantify whether a miRNA-inference method recovers the induction as logFC with significance. The goal is target-based miRNA activity scoring without a benchmark induction signal — miReact-style cross-gene-correlation methods are the appropriate control, not this logFC verification The pre-trained model's training context differs substantially from the application context and no matched cohort is available, since performance loss is expected (Figure S9) Profiles are so sparse that the pre-trained model fails and no retraining on detected genes is feasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Compares predicted miRNA expression between experimentally induced and uninduced single-cell samples by computing induced-vs-uninduced log-fold changes and Wilcoxon p-values, used to verify that miRSCAPE recapitulates miR-199a-5p/3p induction in scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962

skills.description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups show differing cell-cluster proportions, so naive fold-change / observed-change (OC) estimates of perturbation effect are contaminated by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be recovered.
skills.name: infected-proportion-bias-decoupling
skills.search_text: infected-proportion-bias-decoupling Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups show differing cell-cluster proportions, so naive fold-change / observed-change (OC) estimates of perturbation effect are contaminated by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be recovered. Data from intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors, where the GMM assumption on expression distributions may not hold Extreme cases where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, violating the shared-cluster assumption between NT and perturbation groups Samples with strong heterogeneity, since the similar-cellular-response assumption limits scDecouple to cells with moderate heterogeneity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A maximum-likelihood decoupling method (scDecouple) that separates the true cellular response to CRISPR perturbation from 'infected proportion bias' — the distortion caused when cell-cluster proportions differ between the perturbation group Y and control group Z in scCRISPR-seq. It uses a Gaussian mixture model with EM, applied on principal components of the control group, outperforming naive observed-change/fold-change estimates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: A maximum-likelihood decoupling method (scDecouple) that separates the true cellular response to CRISPR perturbation from 'infected proportion bias' — the distortion caused when cell-cluster proportions differ between the perturbation group Y and control group Z in scCRISPR-seq. It uses a Gaussian mixture model with EM, applied on principal components of the control group, outperforming naive observed-change/fold-change estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data from intricate systems or disease tissues such as tumors, where the GMM assumption on expression distributions may not hold Extreme cases where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, violating the shared-cluster assumption between NT and perturbation groups Samples with strong heterogeneity, since the similar-cellular-response assumption limits scDecouple to cells with moderate heterogeneity

skills.description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq perturbation vs. control data where cluster proportions differ between groups, and you need to measure or validate how much fold-change estimates are contaminated by infected proportion bias.

skills.search_text: infection-proportion-bias-quantification Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq perturbation vs. control data where cluster proportions differ between groups, and you need to measure or validate how much fold-change estimates are contaminated by infected proportion bias. When cell cluster proportions are identical between perturbation and control groups — there is no infected proportion bias to quantify When the data violate scDecouple's assumptions: non-Gaussian-mixture expression distributions (e.g. tumor tissues) or rare cell types completely absent from infection http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Quantifies the infected proportion bias that distorts perturbation effect estimates in scCRISPR-seq, including validating its linear dependence on cluster distance d and ratio change r (Equations 14-15) in synthetic two-cluster scenarios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Quantifies the infected proportion bias that distorts perturbation effect estimates in scCRISPR-seq, including validating its linear dependence on cluster distance d and ratio change r (Equations 14-15) in synthetic two-cluster scenarios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell cluster proportions are identical between perturbation and control groups — there is no infected proportion bias to quantify When the data violate scDecouple's assumptions: non-Gaussian-mixture expression distributions (e.g. tumor tissues) or rare cell types completely absent from infection
