skills.name: inference-difficulty-benchmarking
skills.search_text: inference-difficulty-benchmarking Use when a cohort bulk dataset has candidate representative-selection strategies and you must quantify which strategy yields lower single-cell inference difficulty at a fixed representative budget. The task is cell-type-level bulk deconvolution rather than comparing representative-selection strategies — conventional deconvolution methods (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC) are constrained to cell-type-level resolution and cannot assess single-cell inference difficulty. Only one selection strategy is available, so no active-vs-passive comparison curve can be produced at matched representative counts. No single-cell reference or representative data exist at all — the tool requires a single-cell reference to perform single-cell-level decomposition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmarks representative-selection strategies (type-II active learning vs passive uncertainty-style selection) by measuring in silico single-cell inference difficulty — the average Euclidean distance between representative cells and their nearest neighbors in target samples — across representative counts using scSemiProfiler. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Benchmarks representative-selection strategies (type-II active learning vs passive uncertainty-style selection) by measuring in silico single-cell inference difficulty — the average Euclidean distance between representative cells and their nearest neighbors in target samples — across representative counts using scSemiProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell-type-level bulk deconvolution rather than comparing representative-selection strategies — conventional deconvolution methods (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC) are constrained to cell-type-level resolution and cannot assess single-cell inference difficulty. Only one selection strategy is available, so no active-vs-passive comparison curve can be produced at matched representative counts. No single-cell reference or representative data exist at all — the tool requires a single-cell reference to perform single-cell-level decomposition.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing a single-cell trajectory that needs discrete cell-state landmarks, and the number of clusters k must be chosen objectively from clustering-purity or landmark-count curves (e.g. FACS-label-guided cuts of hclust dendrograms).
skills.name: inflection-point-based-cluster-set-selection
skills.search_text: inflection-point-based-cluster-set-selection Use when reconstructing a single-cell trajectory that needs discrete cell-state landmarks, and the number of clusters k must be chosen objectively from clustering-purity or landmark-count curves (e.g. FACS-label-guided cuts of hclust dendrograms). The starting cell types are multiple independent progenitor populations — Mpath is designed for processes stemming from a single progenitor cell type and does not yet support this (planned future extension). Specific subset information is unknown and no FACS-sorted terminal subsets or signature genes from end-stage contrasts are available — landmark designation and fate prediction depend on them. Mpath's landmark designation procedure: agglomerative clustering (Ward.D) of single-cell expression data, iterative cutting of the dendrogram, and selection of the optimal cluster set at the inflexion point of landmarks-versus-clusters (or purity) curves, yielding discrete cell-state landmark clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Mpath's landmark designation procedure: agglomerative clustering (Ward.D) of single-cell expression data, iterative cutting of the dendrogram, and selection of the optimal cluster set at the inflexion point of landmarks-versus-clusters (or purity) curves, yielding discrete cell-state landmark clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The starting cell types are multiple independent progenitor populations — Mpath is designed for processes stemming from a single progenitor cell type and does not yet support this (planned future extension). Specific subset information is unknown and no FACS-sorted terminal subsets or signature genes from end-stage contrasts are available — landmark designation and fate prediction depend on them.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a cell type classifier on a label hierarchy — e.g. mapping ~164 Cell Ontology fine labels to ~31 coarse classes via information content and comparing macro F1 across granularity levels.
skills.name: information-content-label-coarsening
skills.search_text: information-content-label-coarsening Use when evaluating a cell type classifier on a label hierarchy — e.g. mapping ~164 Cell Ontology fine labels to ~31 coarse classes via information content and comparing macro F1 across granularity levels. Cell type labels are free-text annotations not resolvable to Cell Ontology terms — the subtype/parent grading requires a valid CL hierarchy The analysis goal is fine-grained subtype discrimination only and granularity relaxation would mask real errors (e.g. coarse labels like 'native cell' being predicted) Predictions and ground truth come from a flat label set with no ontology-defined parent–child relations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A granularity-aware evaluation method from the scTab paper that maps 164 fine-grained Cell Ontology cell type labels to 31 coarse classes using information content (IC ≤ 60) and computes ontology-aware macro F1 at both levels. It quantifies how much a cross-tissue classifier (scTab) gains when annotation tolerance is relaxed from fine subtypes to parent cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: A granularity-aware evaluation method from the scTab paper that maps 164 fine-grained Cell Ontology cell type labels to 31 coarse classes using information content (IC ≤ 60) and computes ontology-aware macro F1 at both levels. It quantifies how much a cross-tissue classifier (scTab) gains when annotation tolerance is relaxed from fine subtypes to parent cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type labels are free-text annotations not resolvable to Cell Ontology terms — the subtype/parent grading requires a valid CL hierarchy The analysis goal is fine-grained subtype discrimination only and granularity relaxation would mask real errors (e.g. coarse labels like 'native cell' being predicted) Predictions and ground truth come from a flat label set with no ontology-defined parent–child relations

skills.search_text: information-flow-distance-profiling Use when scRNA-seq data has been equipped with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell affects which gene in a neighboring cell, and at which spatial range. Input lacks any spatial measurements or a cell–cell distance matrix — the η-neighborhoods cannot be built without spatial context The dataset is excessively large: the article notes 'the computation can become intractable when the dataset is excessively large' and recommends landmark approximations instead The question concerns time-resolved signaling cascades — the approach does not consider time delay (ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade reacting time) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Profiles intercellular gene–gene regulatory information flow as a function of spatial distance between cells, using partial information decomposition on scRNA-seq data paired with SpaOTsc-derived cell–cell distances (e.g. Twist→Snail in the Drosophila embryo peaking at ~25 µm). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Profiles intercellular gene–gene regulatory information flow as a function of spatial distance between cells, using partial information decomposition on scRNA-seq data paired with SpaOTsc-derived cell–cell distances (e.g. Twist→Snail in the Drosophila embryo peaking at ~25 µm).

skills.description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. lesional vs nonlesional AD skin, E13.5 vs E14.5 embryonic skin) each have a CellChat object and you need to rank which signaling pathways change their information flow between conditions.
skills.name: information-flow-quantification-of-signaling-pathways
skills.search_text: information-flow-quantification-of-signaling-pathways Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. lesional vs nonlesional AD skin, E13.5 vs E14.5 embryonic skin) each have a CellChat object and you need to rank which signaling pathways change their information flow between conditions. You have only one condition — information-flow contrasts require at least two CellChat objects to merge; use single-dataset centrality analysis instead Cell groups are not shared/matched across conditions and there are fewer than the common populations needed for joint manifold learning (e.g. the E13.5/E14.5 comparison relies on 11 common cell populations) The question is about spatially proximal communication at single-cell resolution — use CellChat v3 (SpatialCellChat) rather than this condition-contrast workflow Quantify and compare signaling-pathway information flow between conditions by aggregating CellChat-inferred ligand-receptor communications to the pathway level, merging condition-specific CellChat objects, and ranking up/down-regulated pathways via differential interaction counts/strength and joint manifold learning (SNN smoothing + UMAP). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Quantify and compare signaling-pathway information flow between conditions by aggregating CellChat-inferred ligand-receptor communications to the pathway level, merging condition-specific CellChat objects, and ranking up/down-regulated pathways via differential interaction counts/strength and joint manifold learning (SNN smoothing + UMAP).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one condition — information-flow contrasts require at least two CellChat objects to merge; use single-dataset centrality analysis instead Cell groups are not shared/matched across conditions and there are fewer than the common populations needed for joint manifold learning (e.g. the E13.5/E14.5 comparison relies on 11 common cell populations) The question is about spatially proximal communication at single-cell resolution — use CellChat v3 (SpatialCellChat) rather than this condition-contrast workflow

skills.search_text: information-flow-ranking-of-interaction-pairs Use when a NeuronChat run has produced per-interaction communication networks and you need to rank all significant interaction pairs by information flow (weight and/or count) to report the top-ranked neuron-neuron signaling interactions. skills.description: Use when building predictive models on high-dimensional data (P >> n) where univariate feature filters like ttest_filter are applied inside nested cross-validation and unbiased outer-fold accuracy is required.
skills.name: information-leakage-avoidance-in-cv
skills.search_text: information-leakage-avoidance-in-cv Use when building predictive models on high-dimensional data (P >> n) where univariate feature filters like ttest_filter are applied inside nested cross-validation and unbiased outer-fold accuracy is required. You only need a filter ranking for descriptive/exploratory statistics on the full dataset and no CV performance estimate — running ttest_filter on all data is fine outside CV, but never feed those rankings into CV accuracy measurement Predictor count is modest relative to sample size and no feature selection step is embedded in the CV loop — leakage avoidance machinery is unnecessary Your workflow already pre-specifies the feature set a priori (e.g. force_vars only) so no data-driven filtering occurs within folds http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Applies univariate feature-selection filters (ttest_filter and related nestedcv filters) independently within each outer CV fold so hold-out test rows never influence feature selection, avoiding the accuracy bias from filtering on the whole dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Applies univariate feature-selection filters (ttest_filter and related nestedcv filters) independently within each outer CV fold so hold-out test rows never influence feature selection, avoiding the accuracy bias from filtering on the whole dataset.

skills.search_text: information-theoretic-correlation-transformation Use when you must quantify association strength between continuous/ordinal features and a response, and overlapping information between feature pairs, from Spearman rank correlations without expensive mutual-information density estimation. When features are inherently discrete and a mutual-information toolbox is appropriate — FEAST expects discrete inputs and continuous values must be discretised (e.g., 10 equal-width bins) before use When you need a full probabilistic mutual-information estimate rather than a correlation-based surrogate — the transformation is a heuristic nonlinear mapping of rank correlations, not proper MI density estimation When the analysis goal is not ranking/selecting features from a data matrix plus response (RRCT is designed specifically as an off-the-shelf filter feature-selection step) http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 A nonlinear, information-theoretic transformation of Spearman rank correlation coefficients that quantifies feature-response relevance and feature-pair redundancy, and, together with partial correlations, the complementarity term used in the RRCT feature-selection criterion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100471

skills.description: Use when preparing a normalized scRNA-seq reference matrix for supervised cell-type classification (e.g., SciBet Learn/Bet) and a compact marker gene set is needed to discriminate close subtypes or rare populations.
skills.name: informative-gene-selection
skills.search_text: informative-gene-selection Use when preparing a normalized scRNA-seq reference matrix for supervised cell-type classification (e.g., SciBet Learn/Bet) and a compact marker gene set is needed to discriminate close subtypes or rare populations. Input is raw UMI counts that have not yet been normalized (TPM+log or Seurat v3-style size-factor 10,000 normalization), since ΔS ranking assumes log-scale expression. The goal is unsupervised clustering or marker discovery on unlabeled cells — E-test ΔS requires pre-annotated cell group labels. Genes are already fixed by the experimental design (e.g., a targeted panel or a HomoloGene one-to-one orthologue gene space); selection would be redundant or invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks genes by the ΔS entropy statistic (E-test) and retains the top 500 informative genes per cell-type reference, providing the compact feature space on which SciBet's multinomial maximum-likelihood classifier operates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Ranks genes by the ΔS entropy statistic (E-test) and retains the top 500 informative genes per cell-type reference, providing the compact feature space on which SciBet's multinomial maximum-likelihood classifier operates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw UMI counts that have not yet been normalized (TPM+log or Seurat v3-style size-factor 10,000 normalization), since ΔS ranking assumes log-scale expression. The goal is unsupervised clustering or marker discovery on unlabeled cells — E-test ΔS requires pre-annotated cell group labels. Genes are already fixed by the experimental design (e.g., a targeted panel or a HomoloGene one-to-one orthologue gene space); selection would be redundant or invalid.

skills.description: Use when constructing a DeformedKernel/AdaptiveKernel affinity matrix on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix and a data-driven inner bandwidth is needed instead of hand-tuning φ.

skills.search_text: inner-bandwidth-estimation-from-gene-scatter Use when constructing a DeformedKernel/AdaptiveKernel affinity matrix on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix and a data-driven inner bandwidth is needed instead of hand-tuning φ. The input is not a (genes x cells) expression matrix — e.g. already dimensionality-reduced embeddings or PCA scores — since the heuristic relies on per-gene pairwise squared distances on the same matrix passed to the kernel The data is raw counts or otherwise not log-normalized, which the authors' study pipeline assumes before kernel construction Batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets is needed upstream, which the paper explicitly did not consider http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Heuristic estimation of the inner bandwidth (φ) parameter of the q-diffused kernel by computing the median (50% quantile) of per-gene scatters on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix, via QDiffusion.jl's estimate_inner_bandwidth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a (genes x cells) expression matrix — e.g. already dimensionality-reduced embeddings or PCA scores — since the heuristic relies on per-gene pairwise squared distances on the same matrix passed to the kernel The data is raw counts or otherwise not log-normalized, which the authors' study pipeline assumes before kernel construction Batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets is needed upstream, which the paper explicitly did not consider

skills.search_text: inner-product-perturbation-scoring Use when scoring systematic in silico KO/overexpression simulations (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) against a reference differentiation trajectory to prioritize TF regulators for validation. skills.description: Use when you need to test whether DeepCycle's accurate transcriptional phase inference depends on training with both the spliced (Ms) and unspliced (Mu) scVelo moment layers, by ablating one input channel and comparing the resulting cell_cycle_theta values between single-channel runs.
skills.name: input-channel-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: input-channel-ablation-analysis Use when you need to test whether DeepCycle's accurate transcriptional phase inference depends on training with both the spliced (Ms) and unspliced (Mu) scVelo moment layers, by ablating one input channel and comparing the resulting cell_cycle_theta values between single-channel runs. You want the full published DeepCycle result on both channels — DeepCycle.py has no CLI flag for removing a channel, so this skill requires modifying the autoencoder input and is not a drop-in rerun of the README command The dataset contains no cycling genes (e.g. insufficient sequencing depth), since results will not be reliable regardless of channel configuration Your goal is phase-transition (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) estimation via estimate_cell_cycle_transitions.py rather than ablation of the input channels http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces DeepCycle's input-channel ablation: retrain the autoencoder on the mESC Anndata with either the spliced or the unspliced channel removed from the autoencoder input, then compare the inferred circular phases (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) to show phase inconsistency, as reported in Supplementary Fig. S8. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Reproduces DeepCycle's input-channel ablation: retrain the autoencoder on the mESC Anndata with either the spliced or the unspliced channel removed from the autoencoder input, then compare the inferred circular phases (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) to show phase inconsistency, as reported in Supplementary Fig. S8.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want the full published DeepCycle result on both channels — DeepCycle.py has no CLI flag for removing a channel, so this skill requires modifying the autoencoder input and is not a drop-in rerun of the README command The dataset contains no cycling genes (e.g. insufficient sequencing depth), since results will not be reliable regardless of channel configuration Your goal is phase-transition (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) estimation via estimate_cell_cycle_transitions.py rather than ablation of the input channels

skills.description: Use when evaluating how input matrix preprocessing (raw vs log1p vs size-factor normalized variants) affects a downstream embedding or cell type annotation pipeline, or when validating that a method's raw-count requirement holds under batch perturbation.
skills.name: input-preprocessing-benchmark-design
skills.search_text: input-preprocessing-benchmark-design Use when evaluating how input matrix preprocessing (raw vs log1p vs size-factor normalized variants) affects a downstream embedding or cell type annotation pipeline, or when validating that a method's raw-count requirement holds under batch perturbation. When the downstream method explicitly requires log-normalized or scaled inputs (e.g. methods built on Gaussian assumptions) — this benchmark specifically tests the raw-count regime of GeneVector's MI-based discretization. When the research goal is real batch-effect removal rather than benchmarking preprocessing sensitivity — use GeneVector's batch_correct workflow instead. When the dataset lacks published reference cell type annotations, since the acceptance criterion requires comparing predictions to ground-truth labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Design and execute a controlled benchmark comparing GeneVector cell type prediction accuracy across input preprocessing variants (raw counts, log-transformed, normalized, normalized+log-transformed) on the TICA scRNA-seq dataset, including subsets with an artificially generated library-size batch effect. This demonstrates that the entropy-based mutual information framework performs best on untransformed raw counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Design and execute a controlled benchmark comparing GeneVector cell type prediction accuracy across input preprocessing variants (raw counts, log-transformed, normalized, normalized+log-transformed) on the TICA scRNA-seq dataset, including subsets with an artificially generated library-size batch effect. This demonstrates that the entropy-based mutual information framework performs best on untransformed raw counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the downstream method explicitly requires log-normalized or scaled inputs (e.g. methods built on Gaussian assumptions) — this benchmark specifically tests the raw-count regime of GeneVector's MI-based discretization. When the research goal is real batch-effect removal rather than benchmarking preprocessing sensitivity — use GeneVector's batch_correct workflow instead. When the dataset lacks published reference cell type annotations, since the acceptance criterion requires comparing predictions to ground-truth labels.

The task is CCI inference itself — InterCellar builds on pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions and does not predict them Data are bulk RNA-seq-derived interactions (e.g., CCCExplorer territory), which lack a straightforward scRNA-seq application in InterCellar The CCI input was generated by a tool InterCellar does not support; supported inputs are limited to CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, and SingleCellSignalR http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Defines int-pair modules — groups of predicted ligand-receptor interactions with similar functional patterns — by embedding enriched interaction pairs via UMAP and grouping them with hierarchical clustering inside InterCellar's data-driven analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Defines int-pair modules — groups of predicted ligand-receptor interactions with similar functional patterns — by embedding enriched interaction pairs via UMAP and grouping them with hierarchical clustering inside InterCellar's data-driven analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is CCI inference itself — InterCellar builds on pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions and does not predict them Data are bulk RNA-seq-derived interactions (e.g., CCCExplorer territory), which lack a straightforward scRNA-seq application in InterCellar The CCI input was generated by a tool InterCellar does not support; supported inputs are limited to CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, and SingleCellSignalR

skills.description: Use when a directed gene regulatory network must be reduced to control-theoretic driver-node candidates, i.e., an MFVS that breaks all directed cycles and an MDS that covers every node are needed as optimization problems.
skills.name: integer-linear-programming-formulation
skills.search_text: integer-linear-programming-formulation Use when a directed gene regulatory network must be reduced to control-theoretic driver-node candidates, i.e., an MFVS that breaks all directed cycles and an MDS that covers every node are needed as optimization problems. The input graph is already acyclic (DAG), making the MFVS formulation trivial/unnecessary The GRN has not yet been constructed — CEFCON must first build the cell-lineage-specific GRN with the graph attention network before control-based candidate extraction The analysis targets multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations at once — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time Within CEFCON's driver-regulator module, network-control candidate sets are obtained by formulating and solving the minimum feedback vertex set (MFVS) and minimum dominating set (MDS) problems on the directed cell-lineage-specific GRN as integer linear programs (ILPs) with gurobipy/cvxpy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Within CEFCON's driver-regulator module, network-control candidate sets are obtained by formulating and solving the minimum feedback vertex set (MFVS) and minimum dominating set (MDS) problems on the directed cell-lineage-specific GRN as integer linear programs (ILPs) with gurobipy/cvxpy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input graph is already acyclic (DAG), making the MFVS formulation trivial/unnecessary The GRN has not yet been constructed — CEFCON must first build the cell-lineage-specific GRN with the graph attention network before control-based candidate extraction The analysis targets multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations at once — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time

skills.description: Use when cluster-specific marker genes must be recovered from a trained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (e.g., Miscell latent features) and attributed to individual genes via an attribution method.
skills.name: integrated-gradient-attribution-scoring
skills.search_text: integrated-gradient-attribution-scoring Use when cluster-specific marker genes must be recovered from a trained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (e.g., Miscell latent features) and attributed to individual genes via an attribution method. The gene of interest is not among the highly variable genes, since Miscell's marker identification is limited to HVGs and may miss cluster-specific markers outside them The dataset is too small, because Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance Batch effects have not been corrected beforehand, since Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction method http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Identifies cluster-specific marker genes from a pretrained Miscell encoder by attaching a 1-layer linear classifier to the frozen encoder and computing integrated-gradient attribution scores that quantify each gene's influence on each cell cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Identifies cluster-specific marker genes from a pretrained Miscell encoder by attaching a 1-layer linear classifier to the frozen encoder and computing integrated-gradient attribution scores that quantify each gene's influence on each cell cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene of interest is not among the highly variable genes, since Miscell's marker identification is limited to HVGs and may miss cluster-specific markers outside them The dataset is too small, because Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance Batch effects have not been corrected beforehand, since Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction method

skills.description: Use when a trained STEM model and spatial trajectory (e.g., the 11-segment E1z2 spinal-cord pseudo-spatial coordinates) are available and you need to identify which genes determine individual cells' spatial locations, beyond expression-based DEGs.
skills.name: integrated-gradient-gene-attribution
skills.search_text: integrated-gradient-gene-attribution Use when a trained STEM model and spatial trajectory (e.g., the 11-segment E1z2 spinal-cord pseudo-spatial coordinates) are available and you need to identify which genes determine individual cells' spatial locations, beyond expression-based DEGs. The STEM model has not been trained or is still in training mode — attributions require the converged checkpoint switched to evaluation via modeleval. The goal is differential expression along a trajectory rather than identifying genes driving spatial localization — expression-based DEGs (218 here) are the comparison set, not the attribution product. The dataset is not the E1z2 SeqFISH/spatial-trajectory setting and no ground-truth pseudo time exists for validating SDG expression trends. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Runs integrated gradient attribution through the trained STEM model's spatial adjacency-embedding-gene path (PyTorch) to rank genes by their contribution to each cell's spatial placement along a trajectory, calling spatially dominant genes (SDGs) at FDR < 0.05 via Benjamini-Hochberg correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Runs integrated gradient attribution through the trained STEM model's spatial adjacency-embedding-gene path (PyTorch) to rank genes by their contribution to each cell's spatial placement along a trajectory, calling spatially dominant genes (SDGs) at FDR < 0.05 via Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The STEM model has not been trained or is still in training mode — attributions require the converged checkpoint switched to evaluation via modeleval. The goal is differential expression along a trajectory rather than identifying genes driving spatial localization — expression-based DEGs (218 here) are the comparison set, not the attribution product. The dataset is not the E1z2 SeqFISH/spatial-trajectory setting and no ground-truth pseudo time exists for validating SDG expression trends.

skills.description: Use when a trained Pollock cell-type/state model needs interpretable gene-level attributions — e.g. to identify driving genes (DWGs) for predicted immune cell states on held-out annotated cells.
skills.name: integrated-gradients-feature-attribution
skills.search_text: integrated-gradients-feature-attribution Use when a trained Pollock cell-type/state model needs interpretable gene-level attributions — e.g. to identify driving genes (DWGs) for predicted immune cell states on held-out annotated cells. Input expression matrices are normalized rather than raw counts — explain mode requires unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts The goal is cell type prediction only (use Pollock predict mode; explanation is not needed and adds substantial runtime) Very large numbers of cells without downsampling — explain mode has excessive runtimes and cells should be downsampled (e.g. ~100 cells ≈ 15 minutes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes Captum Integrated Gradients feature attributions through Pollock's VAE-classifier to rank genes that drive cell type/state predictions, producing per-state DWG (differentially weight gene) rankings that recover known markers such as FOXP3 in Tregs and LAG3/PDCD1 in exhausted T cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Computes Captum Integrated Gradients feature attributions through Pollock's VAE-classifier to rank genes that drive cell type/state predictions, producing per-state DWG (differentially weight gene) rankings that recover known markers such as FOXP3 in Tregs and LAG3/PDCD1 in exhausted T cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression matrices are normalized rather than raw counts — explain mode requires unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts The goal is cell type prediction only (use Pollock predict mode; explanation is not needed and adds substantial runtime) Very large numbers of cells without downsampling — explain mode has excessive runtimes and cells should be downsampled (e.g. ~100 cells ≈ 15 minutes)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a clustering/integration method resolves perturbation-unique cell states in control/perturbed single-cell transcriptome data with known ground-truth labels, across perturbation-severity, marker-gene, and cell-proportion conditions.
skills.name: integration-baseline-pipeline-comparison
skills.search_text: integration-baseline-pipeline-comparison Use when benchmarking whether a clustering/integration method resolves perturbation-unique cell states in control/perturbed single-cell transcriptome data with known ground-truth labels, across perturbation-severity, marker-gene, and cell-proportion conditions. The dataset is a single condition with no control/perturbed treatment labels — ICAT's semi-supervised clustering requires control-defined cell states to anchor the sslouvain step, so no comparison arm can be run No ground-truth population labels exist, so agreement metrics (ARI, F1, LISI against truth) cannot be computed and the benchmark cannot be scored The goal is batch-effect removal for downstream visualization rather than testing whether integration workflows miss perturbation-unique cell states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Head-to-head benchmarking of ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised Louvain clustering against Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony, and no-integration Louvain baselines on simulated control/perturbed scRNA-seq datasets, scoring cluster recovery (ARI, LISI, F1) against ground-truth population labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Head-to-head benchmarking of ICAT's control-guided semi-supervised Louvain clustering against Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony, and no-integration Louvain baselines on simulated control/perturbed scRNA-seq datasets, scoring cluster recovery (ARI, LISI, F1) against ground-truth population labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single condition with no control/perturbed treatment labels — ICAT's semi-supervised clustering requires control-defined cell states to anchor the sslouvain step, so no comparison arm can be run No ground-truth population labels exist, so agreement metrics (ARI, F1, LISI against truth) cannot be computed and the benchmark cannot be scored The goal is batch-effect removal for downstream visualization rather than testing whether integration workflows miss perturbation-unique cell states

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell diagonal integration methods (e.g. scRNA-scATAC or scRNA-surface protein) on unpaired data and you need quantitative, per-method performance scores to produce a ranked benchmark table.
skills.name: integration-benchmark-metric-computation
skills.search_text: integration-benchmark-metric-computation Use when comparing single-cell diagonal integration methods (e.g. scRNA-scATAC or scRNA-surface protein) on unpaired data and you need quantitative, per-method performance scores to produce a ranked benchmark table. When integrating paired (multiome-like) data where cells are matched across modalities — the paper's benchmark targets unpaired diagonal integration settings When cross-modality feature connections are unavailable (e.g. integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since the embedding pipeline these metrics evaluate depends on such features When the goal is single-modality clustering or batch correction rather than cross-modality integration benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking procedure from the scConfluence paper (Nat Commun 2024) that scores diagonal integration methods (scConfluence, Seurat, Liger, MultiMAP, Uniport, scGLUE) on unpaired single-cell multimodal tasks using four quantitative metrics — cell-type purity, label-transfer accuracy, connectivity of the latent embedding, and FOSCTTM — across balanced and unbalanced population scenarios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure from the scConfluence paper (Nat Commun 2024) that scores diagonal integration methods (scConfluence, Seurat, Liger, MultiMAP, Uniport, scGLUE) on unpaired single-cell multimodal tasks using four quantitative metrics — cell-type purity, label-transfer accuracy, connectivity of the latent embedding, and FOSCTTM — across balanced and unbalanced population scenarios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When integrating paired (multiome-like) data where cells are matched across modalities — the paper's benchmark targets unpaired diagonal integration settings When cross-modality feature connections are unavailable (e.g. integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since the embedding pipeline these metrics evaluate depends on such features When the goal is single-modality clustering or batch correction rather than cross-modality integration benchmarking

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple single-cell batch-integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI, Harmony, Seurat v3) on the same AnnData embedding and you need quantitative, composite-scored benchmark metrics.
skills.name: integration-benchmark-metric-computation
skills.search_text: integration-benchmark-metric-computation Use when comparing multiple single-cell batch-integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI, Harmony, Seurat v3) on the same AnnData embedding and you need quantitative, composite-scored benchmark metrics. You only have raw count matrices with no integrated embeddings — this skill evaluates integration results, it does not produce them You need a metric that requires full kBET on a very large, many-batch dataset (e.g., the 147-batch heart atlas), where kBET computation fails due to memory/time limits and must be excluded http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes single-cell integration benchmark metrics — biological conservation (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW), batch correction (batch ASW, PCR batch, graph connectivity, kBET with k=50), and min-max normalized composite scores — to compare integration methods on a shared dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Computes single-cell integration benchmark metrics — biological conservation (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW), batch correction (batch ASW, PCR batch, graph connectivity, kBET with k=50), and min-max normalized composite scores — to compare integration methods on a shared dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw count matrices with no integrated embeddings — this skill evaluates integration results, it does not produce them You need a metric that requires full kBET on a very large, many-batch dataset (e.g., the 147-batch heart atlas), where kBET computation fails due to memory/time limits and must be excluded

skills.description: Use when evaluating or visualizing how well integrated scRNA-seq embeddings mix batches while preserving cell types, especially to detect overcorrection where batch mixing destroys biological structure.
skills.name: integration-benchmark-metric-visualization
skills.search_text: integration-benchmark-metric-visualization Use when evaluating or visualizing how well integrated scRNA-seq embeddings mix batches while preserving cell types, especially to detect overcorrection where batch mixing destroys biological structure. Cell type annotations are unavailable — CiLISI and similar cell type-aware metrics require cell type labels and cannot be computed without them Cell types are present in only one dataset (e.g., a dataset with a unique cell type), where CiLISI cannot be calculated Datasets have highly unequal numbers of cells per batch — LISI/CiLISI are suboptimal and batch-mixing scores can be misleading with lopsided cell proportions http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark single-cell RNA-seq data integration by computing batch-mixing and cell-type-preservation metrics (iLISI, CiLISI, ASW, normalized cLISI) on integrated embeddings using the scIntegrationMetrics R package, with STACAS as the integration method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell RNA-seq data integration by computing batch-mixing and cell-type-preservation metrics (iLISI, CiLISI, ASW, normalized cLISI) on integrated embeddings using the scIntegrationMetrics R package, with STACAS as the integration method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell type annotations are unavailable — CiLISI and similar cell type-aware metrics require cell type labels and cannot be computed without them Cell types are present in only one dataset (e.g., a dataset with a unique cell type), where CiLISI cannot be calculated Datasets have highly unequal numbers of cells per batch — LISI/CiLISI are suboptimal and batch-mixing scores can be misleading with lopsided cell proportions

skills.search_text: integration-method-benchmarking Use when two or more single-cell datasets (scRNA-seq batches or spatial/scRNA pairs) must be integrated and a defensible choice among integration methods is needed, measured by batch-removal vs biological-conservation metrics. When reference and query datasets originate from different tissue types or lack similar cell types — the article notes label transfer requires same-tissue or similar-cell-type reference/query For CITE-seq or other modalities with only a few hundred protein features, where the article notes it is challenging to identify shared features and optimize the shared-encoder model When the goal is single-dataset analysis without batch structure — no integration benchmark is meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmark single-cell data integration methods (scCobra vs Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) on batch-effect removal and biological conservation using the scIB metric pipeline, as done for scRNA-seq atlases (lung, immune, pancreas) and MERFISH–scRNA-seq hypothalamus integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell data integration methods (scCobra vs Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) on batch-effect removal and biological conservation using the scIB metric pipeline, as done for scRNA-seq atlases (lung, immune, pancreas) and MERFISH–scRNA-seq hypothalamus integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reference and query datasets originate from different tissue types or lack similar cell types — the article notes label transfer requires same-tissue or similar-cell-type reference/query For CITE-seq or other modalities with only a few hundred protein features, where the article notes it is challenging to identify shared features and optimize the shared-encoder model When the goal is single-dataset analysis without batch structure — no integration benchmark is meaningful

skills.description: Use when comparing how robust filtering/integration methods are to incomplete prior knowledge (e.g., a partial cell-cycle marker gene set), quantified as mean percentage degradation of iLISI across repeated runs.
skills.name: integration-method-benchmarking-across-repetitions
skills.search_text: integration-method-benchmarking-across-repetitions Use when comparing how robust filtering/integration methods are to incomplete prior knowledge (e.g., a partial cell-cycle marker gene set), quantified as mean percentage degradation of iLISI across repeated runs. When the goal is absolute integration performance on a full, high-quality marker set rather than sensitivity to a weakened prior — a direct iLISI comparison without the degradation calculation is more appropriate When no annotated attributes (cell cycle, sex labels) exist to compute iLISI, since degradation cannot be quantified without them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark single-cell filtering/integration methods (SiFT, scanpy regress_out, scVI) for robustness to a weakened prior-knowledge marker set by repeating each method 10 times on Drosophila wing disc data and averaging the percentage degradation of iLISI scores per attribute (cell cycle, cell cycle + sex). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell filtering/integration methods (SiFT, scanpy regress_out, scVI) for robustness to a weakened prior-knowledge marker set by repeating each method 10 times on Drosophila wing disc data and averaging the percentage degradation of iLISI scores per attribute (cell cycle, cell cycle + sex).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is absolute integration performance on a full, high-quality marker set rather than sensitivity to a weakened prior — a direct iLISI comparison without the degradation calculation is more appropriate When no annotated attributes (cell cycle, sex labels) exist to compute iLISI, since degradation cannot be quantified without them

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple single-cell integration methods on the same dataset and you need a reproducible multi-metric ranking (batch/cell-type ARI and ASW) summarised into a single benchmark table.

skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell data integration methods (e.g. scMerge2, scMerge2-h vs Seurat, Scanorama, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, scANVI, DESC) by computing batch-ARI, cell-type-ARI, batch-ASW and cell-type-ASW on each corrected embedding and aggregating them into an overall per-method ranking table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single integration result for downstream analysis rather than a comparative benchmark across methods — running scMerge2 alone suffices Your data are already integrated or you lack per-cell batch and cell-type labels, since ARI/ASW computation requires both batch labels and cell-type annotations as references

skills.name: integration-metric-scoring
skills.search_text: integration-metric-scoring Use when benchmarking whether an integration method (e.g. GEDI) removes technical/batch effects while preserving biological variability against competitors across multiple datasets and latent-dimension settings. When the goal is evaluating a single method's biological discovery (e.g. cluster-free DGE, pathway activity, or vector field analysis) rather than comparative benchmarking of integration performance When the input embedding was not produced on the same QC-filtered data and latent-factor range as the competitors, since score comparisons across method-dataset-K combinations would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Scores single-cell data-integration methods (GEDI, Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) across datasets and latent-factor counts using Luecken-style metrics that quantify batch removal and cell-type conservation, aggregating them into an overall ranking written to integration_benchmark_scores.csv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Scores single-cell data-integration methods (GEDI, Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) across datasets and latent-factor counts using Luecken-style metrics that quantify batch removal and cell-type conservation, aggregating them into an overall ranking written to integration_benchmark_scores.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is evaluating a single method's biological discovery (e.g. cluster-free DGE, pathway activity, or vector field analysis) rather than comparative benchmarking of integration performance When the input embedding was not produced on the same QC-filtered data and latent-factor range as the competitors, since score comparisons across method-dataset-K combinations would be invalid

skills.description: Use when per-cell UMAP embeddings from several integration methods are available together with batch and cell-type annotations, and you need to objectively compare how well each method mixes batches while preserving AUCell-derived cell types.
skills.name: integration-metric-visualization-across-methods
skills.search_text: integration-metric-visualization-across-methods Use when per-cell UMAP embeddings from several integration methods are available together with batch and cell-type annotations, and you need to objectively compare how well each method mixes batches while preserving AUCell-derived cell types. Input lacks per-cell batch and cell-type annotations, since LISI and kBET both require labels for covariates (batch/donor) and cell types to score Only one integration embedding exists and no cross-method comparison is intended; single-method scores cannot be ranked against alternatives Cell-type labels are not trusted/conserved (e.g., random labels), making cLISI close to 1 unattainable and the batch-mixing vs. conservation trade-off uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies and visualizes single-cell data integration quality by computing per-cell iLISI (batch mixing) and cLISI (cell-type conservation) scores plus kBET acceptance rates across multiple integration embeddings (e.g., Supervised Harmony, Harmony, Seurat RPCA, Scanorama, Limma), then aggregating them into comparison boxplots (Figure 3B/3C style). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Quantifies and visualizes single-cell data integration quality by computing per-cell iLISI (batch mixing) and cLISI (cell-type conservation) scores plus kBET acceptance rates across multiple integration embeddings (e.g., Supervised Harmony, Harmony, Seurat RPCA, Scanorama, Limma), then aggregating them into comparison boxplots (Figure 3B/3C style).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks per-cell batch and cell-type annotations, since LISI and kBET both require labels for covariates (batch/donor) and cell types to score Only one integration embedding exists and no cross-method comparison is intended; single-method scores cannot be ranked against alternatives Cell-type labels are not trusted/conserved (e.g., random labels), making cLISI close to 1 unattainable and the batch-mixing vs. conservation trade-off uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when you have latent embeddings from integrating scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq (e.g. uniPort coupled-VAE + Minibatch-UOT output) and must quantify alignment via Silhouette, FOSCTTM, and ARI/NMI/F1.
skills.name: integration-quality-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: integration-quality-metric-evaluation Use when you have latent embeddings from integrating scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq (e.g. uniPort coupled-VAE + Minibatch-UOT output) and must quantify alignment via Silhouette, FOSCTTM, and ARI/NMI/F1. Input is raw unnormalized count matrices rather than trained latent embeddings — metrics must be computed on post-uniport.Run embeddings The datasets share no meaningful cell-type annotation for the reference modality, making kNN-based ARI/NMI/F1 label transfer inapplicable Storing a dense global OT plan (save_OT=True) when memory capacity is insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates single-cell multi-omics integration quality by computing Silhouette coefficient, average FOSCTTM, and ARI/NMI/F1 label-transfer scores on uniPort latent embeddings, benchmarked against baselines like GLUE on the 10x paired PBMC scATAC/scRNA dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Evaluates single-cell multi-omics integration quality by computing Silhouette coefficient, average FOSCTTM, and ARI/NMI/F1 label-transfer scores on uniPort latent embeddings, benchmarked against baselines like GLUE on the 10x paired PBMC scATAC/scRNA dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unnormalized count matrices rather than trained latent embeddings — metrics must be computed on post-uniport.Run embeddings The datasets share no meaningful cell-type annotation for the reference modality, making kNN-based ARI/NMI/F1 label transfer inapplicable Storing a dense global OT plan (save_OT=True) when memory capacity is insufficient

skills.name: inter-gene-feature-segmentation
skills.search_text: inter-gene-feature-segmentation Use when building scReadSim's feature space from a scRNA-seq BAM file and a GTF annotation (e.g. gencode.vM10.annotation.gtf), and you need non-overlapping gene and inter-gene regions to construct gene-by-cell and inter-gene-by-cell count matrices. The goal is scATAC-seq feature generation — use Utility.scATAC_CreateFeatureSets instead Input is already a feature BED / count matrix from a prior segmentation run — skip directly to count-matrix construction You need isoform-level ground truths (isoform abundance, alternative splicing events), which the current scReadSim version does not generate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A genome-segmentation skill from scReadSim that partitions the reference genome into gene-region foreground features and complementary inter-gene background features, so that synthetic scRNA-seq reads can be simulated for both annotated genes and the genomic background. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scATAC-seq feature generation — use Utility.scATAC_CreateFeatureSets instead Input is already a feature BED / count matrix from a prior segmentation run — skip directly to count-matrix construction You need isoform-level ground truths (isoform abundance, alternative splicing events), which the current scReadSim version does not generate

skills.description: Use when building or filtering a protein–protein interaction database for intercellular communication analysis and you must separate STRING interactions by evidence channel (experiments > 0, database > 0, predicted low-evidence sources) with credibility/action annotations.
skills.name: interaction-evidence-channel-filtering
skills.search_text: interaction-evidence-channel-filtering Use when building or filtering a protein–protein interaction database for intercellular communication analysis and you must separate STRING interactions by evidence channel (experiments > 0, database > 0, predicted low-evidence sources) with credibility/action annotations. When you need a pre-curated ligand–receptor complex resource (CellPhoneDB-style) rather than user-defined filtering of genome-wide STRING evidence channels When the filtering question is about subcellular plausibility of a pair (COMPARTMENTS localization cut-off) rather than evidence provenance — that is a separate localization filter with a user-adjustable cut-off When predicting downstream signal transduction inside receiver cells (NicheNet-style), which InterCellDB's interaction evidence channels do not model http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Partitions genome-wide STRING v11 protein–protein interactions into three evidence-channel sub-libraries — experiment validated (InterCellDB.exp), pathway curated (InterCellDB.know), and predicted (InterCellDB.pred) — and annotates every pair with a credibility score, action mode, and action effect to form the user-filterable interaction backbone of InterCellDB. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Partitions genome-wide STRING v11 protein–protein interactions into three evidence-channel sub-libraries — experiment validated (InterCellDB.exp), pathway curated (InterCellDB.know), and predicted (InterCellDB.pred) — and annotates every pair with a credibility score, action mode, and action effect to form the user-filterable interaction backbone of InterCellDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need a pre-curated ligand–receptor complex resource (CellPhoneDB-style) rather than user-defined filtering of genome-wide STRING evidence channels When the filtering question is about subcellular plausibility of a pair (COMPARTMENTS localization cut-off) rather than evidence provenance — that is a separate localization filter with a user-adjustable cut-off When predicting downstream signal transduction inside receiver cells (NicheNet-style), which InterCellDB's interaction evidence channels do not model

skills.description: Use when building or auditing a cell-cell communication database and you must confirm that curated ligand-receptor interactions are complete, counted correctly, and classified into the expected molecular families before running inference.
skills.name: interaction-family-classification-verification
skills.search_text: interaction-family-classification-verification Use when building or auditing a cell-cell communication database and you must confirm that curated ligand-receptor interactions are complete, counted correctly, and classified into the expected molecular families before running inference. The input database is already a scored communication matrix rather than a raw curated interaction list — validation counts would be meaningless You are using ICELLNET v2 with the extended database (1669 interactions); the expected counts of 380 interactions / 194 cytokine-receptor interactions apply only to the original curated database from Supplementary Data 1 You need de novo prediction of ligand-receptor pairs; this skill only verifies existing expert curation and family assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Validates an expert-curated ligand-receptor interaction database (e.g. the ICELLNET database in Supplementary Data 1) by loading it in R, counting curated interactions, and verifying that every interaction is assigned to one of the defined molecular families (Growth factors, Cytokines, Chemokines, Immune Checkpoints, Notch signaling, Antigen binding/other). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: Validates an expert-curated ligand-receptor interaction database (e.g. the ICELLNET database in Supplementary Data 1) by loading it in R, counting curated interactions, and verifying that every interaction is assigned to one of the defined molecular families (Growth factors, Cytokines, Chemokines, Immune Checkpoints, Notch signaling, Antigen binding/other).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input database is already a scored communication matrix rather than a raw curated interaction list — validation counts would be meaningless You are using ICELLNET v2 with the extended database (1669 interactions); the expected counts of 380 interactions / 194 cytokine-receptor interactions apply only to the original curated database from Supplementary Data 1 You need de novo prediction of ligand-receptor pairs; this skill only verifies existing expert curation and family assignment

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters (e.g., Seurat Louvain clusters) and the goal is to score, rank, and visualize bona fide ligand-receptor interactions between a sender and a receiver population.
skills.name: interaction-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: interaction-heatmap-visualization Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters (e.g., Seurat Louvain clusters) and the goal is to score, rank, and visualize bona fide ligand-receptor interactions between a sender and a receiver population. The input lacks cell-type/cluster annotations, so sender and receiver populations cannot be defined for scoring interactions. The goal is scATAC-seq-only regulatory analysis (e.g., GRN/chromVAR motif enrichment) rather than intercellular communication scoring. The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse, since SCALA's analysis of only human and mouse datasets is currently supported. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Renders ligand-receptor interactions between annotated single-cell clusters as a scored, ranked heatmap, as implemented in SCALA's ligand-receptor layer built on the nichenetr (NicheNet) framework. Interactions are filtered by expression prevalence (percentage of expression > 10% in clusters of interest) and ranked by the 'prior interaction potential' score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Renders ligand-receptor interactions between annotated single-cell clusters as a scored, ranked heatmap, as implemented in SCALA's ligand-receptor layer built on the nichenetr (NicheNet) framework. Interactions are filtered by expression prevalence (percentage of expression > 10% in clusters of interest) and ranked by the 'prior interaction potential' score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks cell-type/cluster annotations, so sender and receiver populations cannot be defined for scoring interactions. The goal is scATAC-seq-only regulatory analysis (e.g., GRN/chromVAR motif enrichment) rather than intercellular communication scoring. The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse, since SCALA's analysis of only human and mouse datasets is currently supported.

skills.description: Use when an analyzed PhyloVision/VISION object must be delivered as an interactive HTML+JSON web report, or when a previously rendered report's saved state (differential expression cache, selections) must be restored before serving.
skills.name: interactive-report-state-save-restore
skills.search_text: interactive-report-state-save-restore Use when an analyzed PhyloVision/VISION object must be delivered as an interactive HTML+JSON web report, or when a previously rendered report's saved state (differential expression cache, selections) must be restored before serving. No analysis has been run yet — the object must already contain computed signature/Hotspot module results before a report can be viewed Static figures or publication plots are the goal rather than interactive exploration of phylogeny, module tables, and UMAP/tSNE overlays The analysis lives in Python-only tooling; the article notes the R implementation may challenge use of separate Python software like Cassiopeia at report-serving time Generate and re-serve the feature-rich, interactive web-based report of an analyzed PhyloVision (VISION) single-cell lineage-tracing object, optionally restoring previously saved differential-expression and cell-selection state so that hosted reports remain fully explorable locally or on a remote server. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Generate and re-serve the feature-rich, interactive web-based report of an analyzed PhyloVision (VISION) single-cell lineage-tracing object, optionally restoring previously saved differential-expression and cell-selection state so that hosted reports remain fully explorable locally or on a remote server.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No analysis has been run yet — the object must already contain computed signature/Hotspot module results before a report can be viewed Static figures or publication plots are the goal rather than interactive exploration of phylogeny, module tables, and UMAP/tSNE overlays The analysis lives in Python-only tooling; the article notes the R implementation may challenge use of separate Python software like Cassiopeia at report-serving time

skills.description: Use when a gene cluster table of significantly changed genes with LFC values needs interactome-level assessment of key interactors, e.g. to characterize cellular perturbation events or prioritize network targets.
skills.name: interactome-complexity-quantification
skills.search_text: interactome-complexity-quantification Use when a gene cluster table of significantly changed genes with LFC values needs interactome-level assessment of key interactors, e.g. to characterize cellular perturbation events or prioritize network targets. Input is not significantly changed genes with LFC values — the score is defined on LFC-based significance, so unfiltered or raw expression data is out of scope The goal is de novo prediction of physical interactions rather than assessment of known interactors from STRING/UniProt resources http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Quantifies predicted interactome complexity for significantly changed genes by combining known protein-protein interactors (STRING v11 via STRINGdb, UniProt) with log-fold-change (LFC) values, as implemented in the OmicInt R package for exploring gene networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2021.100025
skills.summary: Quantifies predicted interactome complexity for significantly changed genes by combining known protein-protein interactors (STRING v11 via STRINGdb, UniProt) with log-fold-change (LFC) values, as implemented in the OmicInt R package for exploring gene networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not significantly changed genes with LFC values — the score is defined on LFC-based significance, so unfiltered or raw expression data is out of scope The goal is de novo prediction of physical interactions rather than assessment of known interactors from STRING/UniProt resources

skills.description: Use when a completed interactome/GMM analysis has produced a list of key interactor genes/proteins and you need to annotate each interactor with protein type and subcellular location to interpret the cluster biologically.
skills.name: interactor-function-assessment
skills.search_text: interactor-function-assessment Use when a completed interactome/GMM analysis has produced a list of key interactor genes/proteins and you need to annotate each interactor with protein type and subcellular location to interpret the cluster biologically. You want to cluster or score the genes themselves (use OmicInt's Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline on expression/LFC data instead) The proteins of interest are not key interactors from the interactome assessment and you need de novo subcellular localisation prediction rather than retrieval of known UniProt annotations The input is not a properly formatted CSV data frame of identifiers (the README stresses the user must ensure the supplied data is in the right format) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A classification step of the OmicInt R package that labels key interactor proteins with their protein type and cellular compartment by retrieving known UniProt-based annotations, extending the interactome assessment into a functional annotation table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2021.100025
skills.summary: A classification step of the OmicInt R package that labels key interactor proteins with their protein type and cellular compartment by retrieving known UniProt-based annotations, extending the interactome assessment into a functional annotation table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to cluster or score the genes themselves (use OmicInt's Gaussian mixture modelling pipeline on expression/LFC data instead) The proteins of interest are not key interactors from the interactome assessment and you need de novo subcellular localisation prediction rather than retrieval of known UniProt annotations The input is not a properly formatted CSV data frame of identifiers (the README stresses the user must ensure the supplied data is in the right format)

skills.description: Use when the goal is to infer and benchmark intercellular/ligand–receptor interactions between annotated cell clusters from scRNA-seq count matrices, especially with user-defined gene filters such as GO terms or subcellular location cutoffs.
skills.name: intercellular-communication-inference
skills.search_text: intercellular-communication-inference Use when the goal is to infer and benchmark intercellular/ligand–receptor interactions between annotated cell clusters from scRNA-seq count matrices, especially with user-defined gene filters such as GO terms or subcellular location cutoffs. The question is about downstream signal transduction inside the receiving cell rather than intercellular interaction inference — the article notes 'the NicheNet offers a solution to predict the downstream signal transduction in the receiving cells' Only ligand–receptor interactions from a fixed built-in database are needed without user-defined gene/pair filters — other tools like CellPhoneDB may suffice; InterCellDB's value is user-defined analysis Input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated expression without single-cell cluster annotations, since the analysis targets interactions between defined cell clusters http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer cell–cell communication from scRNA-seq data using InterCellDB, a user-defined R package that matches statistically significant gene pairs to a curated protein–protein interaction database annotated with cellular localization (COMPARTMENTS), functional classification (UniProt, GO), and interaction type/direction/effect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Infer cell–cell communication from scRNA-seq data using InterCellDB, a user-defined R package that matches statistically significant gene pairs to a curated protein–protein interaction database annotated with cellular localization (COMPARTMENTS), functional classification (UniProt, GO), and interaction type/direction/effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about downstream signal transduction inside the receiving cell rather than intercellular interaction inference — the article notes 'the NicheNet offers a solution to predict the downstream signal transduction in the receiving cells' Only ligand–receptor interactions from a fixed built-in database are needed without user-defined gene/pair filters — other tools like CellPhoneDB may suffice; InterCellDB's value is user-defined analysis Input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated expression without single-cell cluster annotations, since the analysis targets interactions between defined cell clusters

skills.description: Use when validating that an integration method (e.g. JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI) resists over-correction: score a biologically meaningful module, such as interferon signalling, on cells from different conditions and check whether condition-specific signal remains separable after integration.
skills.name: interferon-gene-module-scoring
skills.search_text: interferon-gene-module-scoring Use when validating that an integration method (e.g. JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI) resists over-correction: score a biologically meaningful module, such as interferon signalling, on cells from different conditions and check whether condition-specific signal remains separable after integration. When the goal is only to quantify batch removal (iLISI/cLISI, ARI/NMI) rather than retention of condition-specific biology — module scoring addresses over-correction, not mixing When the integrated object lacks a biologically validated gene set (e.g. the interferon-signalling module) or cell type labels, since score interpretation depends on known across-condition biology Scores an interferon-signalling gene module on individual cells (notably endothelial cells in a merged pancreas-lung mixture) with AddModuleScore_UCell to test whether a batch-integration method retains across-tissue biological signal while removing batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Scores an interferon-signalling gene module on individual cells (notably endothelial cells in a merged pancreas-lung mixture) with AddModuleScore_UCell to test whether a batch-integration method retains across-tissue biological signal while removing batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only to quantify batch removal (iLISI/cLISI, ARI/NMI) rather than retention of condition-specific biology — module scoring addresses over-correction, not mixing When the integrated object lacks a biologically validated gene set (e.g. the interferon-signalling module) or cell type labels, since score interpretation depends on known across-condition biology

skills.description: Use when the goal is to detect individual subjects with increased abundance of interferon (A28) modules in blood expression matrices, especially when group-mean comparisons show no significant overall change.
skills.name: interferon-module-subject-stratification
skills.search_text: interferon-module-subject-stratification Use when the goal is to detect individual subjects with increased abundance of interferon (A28) modules in blood expression matrices, especially when group-mean comparisons show no significant overall change. Input expression data is already Log2-transformed — the functions expect non-Log2 data and perform the transformation themselves The analysis targets non-blood tissues or non-human species — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood transcriptome data The question is whether a cohort differs on average from controls — use Groupcomparison/Groupcomparisonlimma and gridplot instead of individual stratification http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Performs individual-level (single-sample) blood transcriptome fingerprinting restricted to the A28 interferon module aggregate using the BloodGen3Module R package, to identify subjects carrying interferon signatures in cohorts where group-level comparisons detect no overall change (e.g., 3/22 melanoma and 11/40 JDM subjects). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24584-w
skills.summary: Performs individual-level (single-sample) blood transcriptome fingerprinting restricted to the A28 interferon module aggregate using the BloodGen3Module R package, to identify subjects carrying interferon signatures in cohorts where group-level comparisons detect no overall change (e.g., 3/22 melanoma and 11/40 JDM subjects).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data is already Log2-transformed — the functions expect non-Log2 data and perform the transformation themselves The analysis targets non-blood tissues or non-human species — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood transcriptome data The question is whether a cohort differs on average from controls — use Groupcomparison/Groupcomparisonlimma and gridplot instead of individual stratification

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data contain control vs interferon-beta-stimulated cells and you need to rank cell types by IFN-beta response magnitude while verifying batch effects were removed without erasing true biological variation.
skills.name: interferon-response-quantification
skills.search_text: interferon-response-quantification Use when scRNA-seq count data contain control vs interferon-beta-stimulated cells and you need to rank cell types by IFN-beta response magnitude while verifying batch effects were removed without erasing true biological variation. When technical batch differences are larger than true biological variation — DESC removes batch effects only 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' When the design requires explicitly providing batch labels to the batch-correction method — DESC does not require batch information, and this workflow deliberately trains desc.train without batch labels When cells have already been cluster-annotated and only a bulk-style DE test is needed — the DESC clustering pipeline is unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies cell-type-specific interferon-beta response in single-cell RNA-seq by clustering cells (e.g., with DESC on the Kang et al. lupus PBMC data), annotating clusters to PBMC cell types, and running per-cell-type differential expression between control and stimulated conditions, ranking cell types by response magnitude. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Quantifies cell-type-specific interferon-beta response in single-cell RNA-seq by clustering cells (e.g., with DESC on the Kang et al. lupus PBMC data), annotating clusters to PBMC cell types, and running per-cell-type differential expression between control and stimulated conditions, ranking cell types by response magnitude.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When technical batch differences are larger than true biological variation — DESC removes batch effects only 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' When the design requires explicitly providing batch labels to the batch-correction method — DESC does not require batch information, and this workflow deliberately trains desc.train without batch labels When cells have already been cluster-annotated and only a bulk-style DE test is needed — the DESC clustering pipeline is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when evaluating or annotating a gene embedding learned from interferon-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq data against the Reactome Interferon Signaling pathway R-HSA-913531 or MSigDB C8 co-membership, e.g. comparing MI vs Pearson training objectives.
skills.name: interferon-signaling-pathway-geneset-annotation
skills.search_text: interferon-signaling-pathway-geneset-annotation Use when evaluating or annotating a gene embedding learned from interferon-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq data against the Reactome Interferon Signaling pathway R-HSA-913531 or MSigDB C8 co-membership, e.g. comparing MI vs Pearson training objectives.
