skills.summary: Annotates GeneVector gene embeddings against the Reactome Interferon Signaling pathway (R-HSA-913531) plus MSigDB C8 co-membership by comparing embedding cosine similarities to binary pathway membership, quantifying how well MI-trained vectors capture interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) relationships in the PBMC interferon-beta dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to determine direction of regulation — GeneVector builds MI that is agnostic to whether a dependency is activation or repression The input is not interferon-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq (e.g. TICA, HGSOC, or TNBC PDX datasets) and the pathway of interest is not interferon signaling / ISG expression Genes have not passed quality control (e.g. entropy_threshold=1.0 filtering); sparse, low-entropy genes will degrade MI estimation

skills.description: Use when analyzing interferon beta-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq (or a similar perturbation dataset) and you need to extract a co-regulated gene program and verify it is not confounded by cell type composition.
skills.name: interferon-stimulated-gene-program-interpretation
skills.search_text: interferon-stimulated-gene-program-interpretation Use when analyzing interferon beta-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq (or a similar perturbation dataset) and you need to extract a co-regulated gene program and verify it is not confounded by cell type composition. The question is about repression or mutually exclusive expression — GeneVector's signed MI cannot discern activation from repression direction. The dataset lacks both stimulated and control conditions or cell type annotations, making the cell-type-independent expression check infeasible. The goal is generic dimensionality reduction rather than testing whether a gene program is confounded by cell type — plain PCA/LDVAE alone would suffice for the former. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies a cell-type-independent interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) metagene in interferon beta-stimulated PBMCs using GeneVector gene embeddings, and demonstrates that PCA/LDVAE loadings conflate ISGs with cell-type markers while GeneVector does not. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Identifies a cell-type-independent interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) metagene in interferon beta-stimulated PBMCs using GeneVector gene embeddings, and demonstrates that PCA/LDVAE loadings conflate ISGs with cell-type markers while GeneVector does not.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about repression or mutually exclusive expression — GeneVector's signed MI cannot discern activation from repression direction. The dataset lacks both stimulated and control conditions or cell type annotations, making the cell-type-independent expression check infeasible. The goal is generic dimensionality reduction rather than testing whether a gene program is confounded by cell type — plain PCA/LDVAE alone would suffice for the former.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span ordered cell types or stages and the goal is to test whether interindividual expression correlations between adjacent stages exceed those between more distant stages.
skills.name: interindividual-covariance-partitioning-across-differentiation-stages
skills.search_text: interindividual-covariance-partitioning-across-differentiation-stages Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span ordered cell types or stages and the goal is to test whether interindividual expression correlations between adjacent stages exceed those between more distant stages. Sample size is below ~50 individuals — CTMM is not reliable at this scale and the Free test is slightly inflated Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells — CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and such pairs are filtered out (ct_cut=10), limiting it to common cell types Cell types are continuous rather than discrete — they can only be expressed in pseudobulk by discretizing them, which this workflow assumes has already happened http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits the CTMM Full model by REML on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data to partition interindividual covariance between ordered differentiation stages (here the 4 day-stages of the Cuomo et al. 2020 iPSC-to-endoderm trajectory), then converts the partitioned stage-specific covariance (V) into a stage-by-stage correlation matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fits the CTMM Full model by REML on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data to partition interindividual covariance between ordered differentiation stages (here the 4 day-stages of the Cuomo et al. 2020 iPSC-to-endoderm trajectory), then converts the partitioned stage-specific covariance (V) into a stage-by-stage correlation matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample size is below ~50 individuals — CTMM is not reliable at this scale and the Free test is slightly inflated Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells — CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and such pairs are filtered out (ct_cut=10), limiting it to common cell types Cell types are continuous rather than discrete — they can only be expressed in pseudobulk by discretizing them, which this workflow assumes has already happened

The reference collection has severely uneven bin sizes or a very high number of bins, where Raptor's authors note susceptibility to uneven bin sizes and a moderate slowdown when processing several ten thousand bins Exact full-text search or edit-distance-aware mapping results are required directly — the IBF is a pre-filter whose assignments must be verified by a downstream mapper An existing index was built with a Raptor version older than 2.0.0 and cannot be reused; it must be rebuilt http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Build and query compressed, partitioned Interleaved Bloom Filter (IBF) binning directories over large nucleotide sequence collections using Raptor's winnowing minimizers and probabilistic thresholding, enabling fast approximate sequence search as a pre-filter for tools like DREAM-Yara. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782

skills.description: Use when multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images yield watershed cell labels that are bisected by internal membrane segments (e.g., columnar epithelial or Mucin 2+ goblet cells) and need resegmentation into single objects.
skills.name: internal-membrane-detection
skills.search_text: internal-membrane-detection Use when multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images yield watershed cell labels that are bisected by internal membrane segments (e.g., columnar epithelial or Mucin 2+ goblet cells) and need resegmentation into single objects. Cells already correctly segmented by the initial watershed step — only cells with >10% internal membrane area (or goblet cells) are candidates, so applying extension to unflagged cells risks altering valid boundaries Segmentation problems caused by poor nuclei seeds rather than internal membranes — the article notes deep learning nuclei detection was not implemented here and may be a better remedy for seed errors Non-tissue, isolated single-cell images without tissue-scale membrane architecture where internal aberrant membranes do not occur http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 MIRIAM's method for detecting and resegmenting cells whose watershed segmentation was incorrectly split by internal (aberrant) membranes in multiplexed tissue images, by 'connecting the dots' — extending incomplete membrane segments from their endpoints until they meet the cell border or another extension. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: MIRIAM's method for detecting and resegmenting cells whose watershed segmentation was incorrectly split by internal (aberrant) membranes in multiplexed tissue images, by 'connecting the dots' — extending incomplete membrane segments from their endpoints until they meet the cell border or another extension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells already correctly segmented by the initial watershed step — only cells with >10% internal membrane area (or goblet cells) are candidates, so applying extension to unflagged cells risks altering valid boundaries Segmentation problems caused by poor nuclei seeds rather than internal membranes — the article notes deep learning nuclei detection was not implemented here and may be a better remedy for seed errors Non-tissue, isolated single-cell images without tissue-scale membrane architecture where internal aberrant membranes do not occur

skills.name: internal-priming-artifact-filtering
skills.search_text: internal-priming-artifact-filtering Use when building or curating a candidate cleavage-site catalog from 3'-tag scRNA-seq data (e.g. Microwell-seq) where genomic A-rich stretches downstream of a candidate site could indicate internal priming rather than a genuine polyadenylation event. Input reads are full-length or otherwise span the actual mRNA 3' end cleavage site, so de novo 3' end mapping does not rely on local sequence context (the paper notes most 10x reads do NOT span CS, which is the motivating condition) Candidate sites are already annotated as internal priming artifacts in an existing resource such as PolyASite, making re-scoring redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Removes mis-called mRNA 3' end cleavage sites caused by internal oligo-dT priming during scRNA-seq library construction, by scoring local nucleotide context around candidate sites (e.g. with cleanUpdTSeq) and dropping high-scoring artifacts from the Microwell-seq-derived CS atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Removes mis-called mRNA 3' end cleavage sites caused by internal oligo-dT priming during scRNA-seq library construction, by scoring local nucleotide context around candidate sites (e.g. with cleanUpdTSeq) and dropping high-scoring artifacts from the Microwell-seq-derived CS atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are full-length or otherwise span the actual mRNA 3' end cleavage site, so de novo 3' end mapping does not rely on local sequence context (the paper notes most 10x reads do NOT span CS, which is the motivating condition) Candidate sites are already annotated as internal priming artifacts in an existing resource such as PolyASite, making re-scoring redundant

skills.description: Use when interval-overlap queries (features overlapping an alignment/read interval) are a measured bottleneck in a Python counting pipeline, and the stock container (e.g., HTSeq StepVector) creates excessive intermediate objects per query.
skills.name: interval-data-structure-implementation
skills.search_text: interval-data-structure-implementation Use when interval-overlap queries (features overlapping an alignment/read interval) are a measured bottleneck in a Python counting pipeline, and the stock container (e.g., HTSeq StepVector) creates excessive intermediate objects per query. The task requires only exact feature matching with no interval-overlap logic, so a simple lookup suffices and a custom interval structure adds unwarranted complexity. Any tolerance for differing query results is acceptable — this skill is only valid when returned feature sets must match HTSeq StepVector exactly, feature-for-feature, for every query interval. The pipeline already delegates interval queries to a faster indexed structure (e.g., an interval tree or genome index), making a StepVector replacement redundant. Reimplement a piecewise-constant interval data structure (HTSeq StepVector replacement) in Cython to eliminate iteration inefficiencies and intermediate object creation when resolving features that overlap an alignment interval, then prove output equivalence and benchmark the speedup. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: Reimplement a piecewise-constant interval data structure (HTSeq StepVector replacement) in Cython to eliminate iteration inefficiencies and intermediate object creation when resolving features that overlap an alignment interval, then prove output equivalence and benchmark the speedup.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires only exact feature matching with no interval-overlap logic, so a simple lookup suffices and a custom interval structure adds unwarranted complexity. Any tolerance for differing query results is acceptable — this skill is only valid when returned feature sets must match HTSeq StepVector exactly, feature-for-feature, for every query interval. The pipeline already delegates interval queries to a faster indexed structure (e.g., an interval tree or genome index), making a StepVector replacement redundant.

skills.description: Use when a Python interval/feature data structure (e.g. HTSeq StepVector) is a measured bottleneck in read-to-feature assignment and a compiled (Cython) replacement must be proven query-equivalent before adoption.
skills.name: interval-overlap-equivalence-testing
skills.search_text: interval-overlap-equivalence-testing Use when a Python interval/feature data structure (e.g. HTSeq StepVector) is a measured bottleneck in read-to-feature assignment and a compiled (Cython) replacement must be proven query-equivalent before adoption. You are changing query semantics (e.g. different overlap rules or returned feature sets) — equivalence testing asserts exact matching against HTSeq StepVector behavior, not redesigned behavior The interval data structure is not on the measured critical path — the skill justifies a Cython rewrite only via a demonstrated average runtime reduction on the read-assignment workload Features are already a pre-built count matrix; this skill operates on interval-overlap resolution, not downstream counting outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A validation and benchmarking method for a custom Cython piecewise-constant StepVector that replaces HTSeq's StepVector for resolving features overlapping an alignment interval in tiny-count. It establishes output equivalence via identical interval-overlap query results and quantifies the runtime gain (~30% average reduction) against the HTSeq baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: A validation and benchmarking method for a custom Cython piecewise-constant StepVector that replaces HTSeq's StepVector for resolving features overlapping an alignment interval in tiny-count. It establishes output equivalence via identical interval-overlap query results and quantifies the runtime gain (~30% average reduction) against the HTSeq baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are changing query semantics (e.g. different overlap rules or returned feature sets) — equivalence testing asserts exact matching against HTSeq StepVector behavior, not redesigned behavior The interval data structure is not on the measured critical path — the skill justifies a Cython rewrite only via a demonstrated average runtime reduction on the read-assignment workload Features are already a pre-built count matrix; this skill operates on interval-overlap resolution, not downstream counting outputs

skills.description: Use when a CODEX-exported .csv of per-cell x/y coordinates from rolled (spiral/Swiss-roll) intestinal tissue needs to be unrolled onto a line so cell types and markers can be assessed along proximal–distal and serosa-luminal axes.
skills.name: intestinal-tissue-linearization
skills.search_text: intestinal-tissue-linearization Use when a CODEX-exported .csv of per-cell x/y coordinates from rolled (spiral/Swiss-roll) intestinal tissue needs to be unrolled onto a line so cell types and markers can be assessed along proximal–distal and serosa-luminal axes. The input image is an unrolled/flat tissue section rather than a Swiss-rolled spiral, so there is no spiral backbone to trace from center outward The data provide no x/y coordinates (e.g. an expression matrix without spatial positions) — IntestLine requires images providing xy-coordinates A large dataset must be processed quickly on the FASTGenomics deployment, whose server is limited (2 vCPUs @2.1GHz, 16 GB RAM) — unrolling 150k cells takes on the order of minutes http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps per-cell x/y coordinates from Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue images (e.g. CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics exports) onto a one-dimensional line, preserving proximal–distal position along the organ and serosa-luminal position within the intestinal wall. Implemented as the IntestLine Shiny application. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: Maps per-cell x/y coordinates from Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue images (e.g. CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics exports) onto a one-dimensional line, preserving proximal–distal position along the organ and serosa-luminal position within the intestinal wall. Implemented as the IntestLine Shiny application.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input image is an unrolled/flat tissue section rather than a Swiss-rolled spiral, so there is no spiral backbone to trace from center outward The data provide no x/y coordinates (e.g. an expression matrix without spatial positions) — IntestLine requires images providing xy-coordinates A large dataset must be processed quickly on the FASTGenomics deployment, whose server is limited (2 vCPUs @2.1GHz, 16 GB RAM) — unrolling 150k cells takes on the order of minutes

skills.search_text: intnmf-copy-number-clustering Use when scDNA-seq copy-number data must be partitioned into clones (clone labels for DNA cells) before evaluating or running cell-to-clone assignment of scRNA-seq cells, and multiple clustering algorithms/transformations should be compared. Ground-truth clone labels already exist for the DNA cells — clustering would only add a confound; use the known labels directly as dna_label. The goal is cell-to-cell (not cell-to-clone) mapping, which needs only dna_df and rna_df and no clone partition. The sample is biologically homogeneous — the article notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Cluster scDNA-seq copy-number profiles with intNMF (and agglomerative clustering as a comparator) to define DNA clones, then use the resulting clone labels as inputs for cell-to-clone assignment benchmarking of MaCroDNA, clonealign, and Seurat on the Bian et al. CRC scTrio-seq dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3

CRC scTrio-seq dataset.

skills.description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference in which closely related cell types cause collinearity (e.g., 13 mouse kidney cell types), so proportions must be resolved hierarchically rather than in a single NNLS fit.
skills.name: intra-cluster-gene-selection
skills.search_text: intra-cluster-gene-selection Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference in which closely related cell types cause collinearity (e.g., 13 mouse kidney cell types), so proportions must be resolved hierarchically rather than in a single NNLS fit. When cell types are well separated and not collinear, a single-stage music_prop W-NNLS fit without clustering is sufficient When the input is TPM-normalized expression — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input When no intra-cluster differential expression markers or scRNA-seq reference with replicate subjects are available for the tissue http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 MuSiC's tree-guided recursive two-stage deconvolution resolves collinear, closely related cell types (e.g., PT vs DCT in the mouse kidney) by first clustering cell types and estimating cluster proportions with cluster-consistent genes / group markers, then estimating within-cluster cell type proportions via W-NNLS constrained by the stage-1 cluster proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: MuSiC's tree-guided recursive two-stage deconvolution resolves collinear, closely related cell types (e.g., PT vs DCT in the mouse kidney) by first clustering cell types and estimating cluster proportions with cluster-consistent genes / group markers, then estimating within-cluster cell type proportions via W-NNLS constrained by the stage-1 cluster proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell types are well separated and not collinear, a single-stage music_prop W-NNLS fit without clustering is sufficient When the input is TPM-normalized expression — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input When no intra-cluster differential expression markers or scRNA-seq reference with replicate subjects are available for the tissue

skills.description: Use when analyzing coordinate-sorted RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or SMART-seq2 single-cell) to discover novel skipped or composite IPA events, reconstruct IPA isoforms, and estimate per-site PAU usage not present in the RefSeq annotation.
skills.name: intronic-polyadenylation-site-identification
skills.search_text: intronic-polyadenylation-site-identification Use when analyzing coordinate-sorted RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or SMART-seq2 single-cell) to discover novel skipped or composite IPA events, reconstruct IPA isoforms, and estimate per-site PAU usage not present in the RefSeq annotation. The goal is only 3'UTR alternative polyadenylation quantification in annotated regions — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap, TAPAS, QAPA, or LABRAT cover that scope; InPACT targets intronic polyadenylation and novel IPA isoform discovery Only 3'-end sequencing (3P-seq, polyA-seq) data are available and no conventional RNA-seq alignments exist, since InPACT is designed for standard RNA-seq BAM inputs Sequencing depth is very low — the read thresholds (>=5 spliced reads for skipped, >=10 spanning reads for composite) may be unattainable, mirroring the coverage-dependence criticism raised against IPAFinder http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Identify and quantify novel intronic polyadenylation (IPA) sites and isoforms from conventional RNA-seq using InPACT, which combines a CNN sequence module scoring candidate polyA sites (InPACT_polyAsites.hg38.saf for GRCh38) with a random-forest read module operating on sorted BAM alignments against a RefSeq GTF annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Identify and quantify novel intronic polyadenylation (IPA) sites and isoforms from conventional RNA-seq using InPACT, which combines a CNN sequence module scoring candidate polyA sites (InPACT_polyAsites.hg38.saf for GRCh38) with a random-forest read module operating on sorted BAM alignments against a RefSeq GTF annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only 3'UTR alternative polyadenylation quantification in annotated regions — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap, TAPAS, QAPA, or LABRAT cover that scope; InPACT targets intronic polyadenylation and novel IPA isoform discovery Only 3'-end sequencing (3P-seq, polyA-seq) data are available and no conventional RNA-seq alignments exist, since InPACT is designed for standard RNA-seq BAM inputs Sequencing depth is very low — the read thresholds (>=5 spliced reads for skipped, >=10 spanning reads for composite) may be unattainable, mirroring the coverage-dependence criticism raised against IPAFinder

skills.description: Use when you have lead sQTL variants mapped with sQTLseekeR2 plus an intron annotation, and need to test whether splicing QTLs localize preferentially in post-transcriptionally vs co-transcriptionally spliced introns.
skills.name: intronic-splicing-kinetics-classification
skills.search_text: intronic-splicing-kinetics-classification Use when you have lead sQTL variants mapped with sQTLseekeR2 plus an intron annotation, and need to test whether splicing QTLs localize preferentially in post-transcriptionally vs co-transcriptionally spliced introns. Intron set or cell lines with no matched nuclear/cytosolic ENCODE RNA-seq, since the ps/cs classification depends on that splicing-kinetics data Questions about exon-centric splicing events or junction-level LeafCutter clusters rather than intron-centered sQTL localization Variant-level effect annotation (e.g. splice-site disruption prediction with LOFTEE) rather than enrichment testing of mapped sQTL lead variants http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Classify annotated introns as co-transcriptionally spliced (cs) versus post-transcriptionally spliced (ps) using ENCODE nuclear/cytosolic RNA-seq splicing kinetics across 13 cell lines, then test whether sQTLs are enriched in ps introns by Fisher's exact test. This reproduces the paper's finding that splicing-regulatory variants concentrate in introns spliced after transcript release. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Classify annotated introns as co-transcriptionally spliced (cs) versus post-transcriptionally spliced (ps) using ENCODE nuclear/cytosolic RNA-seq splicing kinetics across 13 cell lines, then test whether sQTLs are enriched in ps introns by Fisher's exact test. This reproduces the paper's finding that splicing-regulatory variants concentrate in introns spliced after transcript release.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Intron set or cell lines with no matched nuclear/cytosolic ENCODE RNA-seq, since the ps/cs classification depends on that splicing-kinetics data Questions about exon-centric splicing events or junction-level LeafCutter clusters rather than intron-centered sQTL localization Variant-level effect annotation (e.g. splice-site disruption prediction with LOFTEE) rather than enrichment testing of mapped sQTL lead variants

skills.description: Use when you must identify previously unannotated intronic terminal exons / IPA sites from a standard RNA-seq BAM aligned to GRCh38 with RefSeq annotation, and need sample-specific classification of skipped vs composite candidates.
skills.name: intronic-terminal-exon-classification
skills.search_text: intronic-terminal-exon-classification Use when you must identify previously unannotated intronic terminal exons / IPA sites from a standard RNA-seq BAM aligned to GRCh38 with RefSeq annotation, and need sample-specific classification of skipped vs composite candidates. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 3'-end sequencing, A-seq/3P-seq or long-read data — use dedicated benchmarking/comparison workflows rather than the read-module classifier Goal is only quantifying already-annotated 3'UTR APA events, which tools like DaPars or QAPA handle without novel terminal exon classification The sample lacks sufficient depth for the default read thresholds (5 spliced reads for skipped, 10 spanning reads for composite candidates)

skills.name: inverse-dispersion-fisher-scoring-estimation
skills.search_text: inverse-dispersion-fisher-scoring-estimation Use when training scDBM (BoltzmannMachines.jl) on scRNA-seq count matrices where the negative-binomial likelihood's inverse dispersion must be re-estimated during training rather than fixed, e.g. to support Gibbs sampling of synthetic cells. Input is not raw count data from a negative-binomial-generating process (e.g. already-normalized or batch-corrected expression matrices), where dispersion estimation assumptions break down Data contain strong batch effects, since scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects and all models were examined without batch correction capabilities A fixed dispersion suffices for the analysis and re-estimation every five epochs adds unnecessary complexity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Within scDBM training, the inverse dispersion parameter of the negative-binomial observation model is estimated via a regularized Fisher-scoring update, refined every five epochs to keep the dispersion estimate aligned with the evolving hidden representation. This stabilizes synthetic count generation for scRNA-seq data with gene-specific overdispersion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Within scDBM training, the inverse dispersion parameter of the negative-binomial observation model is estimated via a regularized Fisher-scoring update, refined every five epochs to keep the dispersion estimate aligned with the evolving hidden representation. This stabilizes synthetic count generation for scRNA-seq data with gene-specific overdispersion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw count data from a negative-binomial-generating process (e.g. already-normalized or batch-corrected expression matrices), where dispersion estimation assumptions break down Data contain strong batch effects, since scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects and all models were examined without batch correction capabilities A fixed dispersion suffices for the analysis and re-estimation every five epochs adds unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when preparing inputs for scMMGAN's geometry-preserving correspondence loss: pairwise L1 distances on preprocessed modality matrices (MAGIC-corrected, zero-centered/unit-scaled, 50 principal components) must be converted to affinities via the inverse-distance kernel with adaptive kNN bandwidth.
skills.name: inverse-distance-kernel-affinity-construction
skills.search_text: inverse-distance-kernel-affinity-construction Use when preparing inputs for scMMGAN's geometry-preserving correspondence loss: pairwise L1 distances on preprocessed modality matrices (MAGIC-corrected, zero-centered/unit-scaled, 50 principal components) must be converted to affinities via the inverse-distance kernel with adaptive kNN bandwidth. If no meaningful choice of distance between data points exists for the modality at hand — the article notes the geometry-based loss 'is not completely plug-and-play' and requires a distance metric If the input is already an affinity or transition-probability matrix, in which case kernel construction would double-transform the data If the data have not been preprocessed (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50-PC reduction) — raw columns can fall outside the [-10, 10] interval the README says gives best results Constructs pairwise affinity matrices for scMMGAN's diffusion-geometry correspondence loss by applying the inverse-distance kernel k(xi,xj)=max(0,1−||xi−xj||1/σi) with a k-nearest-neighbor adaptive bandwidth σi, then row-normalizing the affinities into Markov transition probability matrices used for diffusion-coordinate extraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Constructs pairwise affinity matrices for scMMGAN's diffusion-geometry correspondence loss by applying the inverse-distance kernel k(xi,xj)=max(0,1−||xi−xj||1/σi) with a k-nearest-neighbor adaptive bandwidth σi, then row-normalizing the affinities into Markov transition probability matrices used for diffusion-coordinate extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If no meaningful choice of distance between data points exists for the modality at hand — the article notes the geometry-based loss 'is not completely plug-and-play' and requires a distance metric If the input is already an affinity or transition-probability matrix, in which case kernel construction would double-transform the data If the data have not been preprocessed (MAGIC dropout correction, zero-centering/unit scaling, 50-PC reduction) — raw columns can fall outside the [-10, 10] interval the README says gives best results

skills.description: Use when a miloR neighbourhood object holds per-cell data and a pseudobulk milo object (pb.milo) carries pseudotime/branch probabilities in colData, and you need cell-level trajectory values.
skills.name: inverse-pseudobulk-size-weighted-averaging
skills.search_text: inverse-pseudobulk-size-weighted-averaging Use when a miloR neighbourhood object holds per-cell data and a pseudobulk milo object (pb.milo) carries pseudotime/branch probabilities in colData, and you need cell-level trajectory values. The pseudobulk object already contains cell-level (not pseudobulk) trajectory values — no projection/weighting step is needed The trajectory topology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which absorbing-Markov-chain-based pseudotime cannot represent The dataset is too small for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. Tonglin et al.'s 972 healthy B cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branching probabilities from the miloR pb.milo object) back to individual cells in dandelionR via projectPseudotimeToCell, weighting each pseudobulk's contribution by the inverse of its pseudobulk size and dropping cells not assigned to any neighbourhood. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branching probabilities from the miloR pb.milo object) back to individual cells in dandelionR via projectPseudotimeToCell, weighting each pseudobulk's contribution by the inverse of its pseudobulk size and dropping cells not assigned to any neighbourhood.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pseudobulk object already contains cell-level (not pseudobulk) trajectory values — no projection/weighting step is needed The trajectory topology is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which absorbing-Markov-chain-based pseudotime cannot represent The dataset is too small for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. Tonglin et al.'s 972 healthy B cells)

skills.description: Reference for when CCIVR Table.csv contains fold_change and padj columns for both strands and you need to classify cis-NAT pairs into expression combinations and visualize the down-up subset as a heatmap.
skills.name: inversely-correlated-pair-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: inversely-correlated-pair-heatmap-visualization Reference for when CCIVR Table.csv contains fold_change and padj columns for both strands and you need to classify cis-NAT pairs into expression combinations and visualize the down-up subset as a heatmap. Input is raw RNA-seq reads rather than processed expression-profiled gene annotation data — CCIVR expects a CSV with gene locational information, not FASTQ (upstream STAR/RSEM/DESeq2 processing is required first). Gene annotation lacks strand direction or Start/End coordinates — CCIVR's prediction depends on the accuracy of gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in databases. Goal is identification of cis-NATs themselves rather than visualization of expression combinations of already-extracted pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Skill for tabulating sense–antisense cis-NAT pairs by expression combination (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) from CCIVR's Table.csv and visualizing the inversely correlated (down-up) pairs as a heatmap reproducing Figure 4D of the TGFβ-stimulated Huh-7 analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Skill for tabulating sense–antisense cis-NAT pairs by expression combination (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) from CCIVR's Table.csv and visualizing the inversely correlated (down-up) pairs as a heatmap reproducing Figure 4D of the TGFβ-stimulated Huh-7 analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA-seq reads rather than processed expression-profiled gene annotation data — CCIVR expects a CSV with gene locational information, not FASTQ (upstream STAR/RSEM/DESeq2 processing is required first). Gene annotation lacks strand direction or Start/End coordinates — CCIVR's prediction depends on the accuracy of gene annotation including structure and strand direction deposited in databases. Goal is identification of cis-NATs themselves rather than visualization of expression combinations of already-extracted pairs.

skills.name: ipa-isoform-assembly-annotation
skills.search_text: ipa-isoform-assembly-annotation Use when sorted RNA-seq or scRNA-seq BAM alignments (BAM against GRCh38 with RefSeq GTF) have yielded InPACT-predicted novel IPA terminal exons and you need assembled isoform GTFs plus per-site IPA usage values. The goal is only 3'UTR alternative polyadenylation quantification without novel intronic IPA isoform discovery — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap, or TAPAS address that narrower scope Input alignments are unsorted or contain secondary alignments — InPACT requires coordinate-sorted BAMs and the workflow removes secondary alignments with SAMtools first The genome/annotation is not human GRCh38 with a precomputed InPACT_polyAsites SAF, since the provided candidate-site file is hg38-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assemble novel intronic polyadenylation (IPA) isoforms identified by InPACT into an augmented transcript annotation, then quantify transcript-level abundance with Salmon/gffread to compute IPA usage (PAU) per site. This extends IPA site detection from a coordinate list to full isoforms with measurable relative usage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Assemble novel intronic polyadenylation (IPA) isoforms identified by InPACT into an augmented transcript annotation, then quantify transcript-level abundance with Salmon/gffread to compute IPA usage (PAU) per site. This extends IPA site detection from a coordinate list to full isoforms with measurable relative usage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only 3'UTR alternative polyadenylation quantification without novel intronic IPA isoform discovery — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap, or TAPAS address that narrower scope Input alignments are unsorted or contain secondary alignments — InPACT requires coordinate-sorted BAMs and the workflow removes secondary alignments with SAMtools first The genome/annotation is not human GRCh38 with a precomputed InPACT_polyAsites SAF, since the provided candidate-site file is hg38-specific

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq-derived IPA site predictions from multiple tools need accuracy assessment against experimentally determined polyA site coordinates, or when deciding which IPA caller to adopt.
skills.name: ipa-site-benchmarking-against-3p-end-sequencing
skills.search_text: ipa-site-benchmarking-against-3p-end-sequencing Use when RNA-seq-derived IPA site predictions from multiple tools need accuracy assessment against experimentally determined polyA site coordinates, or when deciding which IPA caller to adopt. When the goal is quantification of already-annotated 3'UTR APA usage rather than identification of novel intronic IPA sites (tools like DaPars, QAPA, LABRAT are limited to 3'UTR APA or quantification only) When no experimental ground truth (3'-end sequencing or Iso-seq data) is available for the evaluated cell type or tissue When sequencing depth is very low — IPAFinder depends on read coverage fluctuations requiring adequate depth, distorting benchmark comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill for evaluating intronic polyadenylation (IPA) site prediction accuracy by comparing tool outputs (InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder) against ground-truth polyA sites from 3'-end sequencing (A-seq, 3P-seq, polyA-seq) and long-read Iso-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for evaluating intronic polyadenylation (IPA) site prediction accuracy by comparing tool outputs (InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder) against ground-truth polyA sites from 3'-end sequencing (A-seq, 3P-seq, polyA-seq) and long-read Iso-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is quantification of already-annotated 3'UTR APA usage rather than identification of novel intronic IPA sites (tools like DaPars, QAPA, LABRAT are limited to 3'UTR APA or quantification only) When no experimental ground truth (3'-end sequencing or Iso-seq data) is available for the evaluated cell type or tissue When sequencing depth is very low — IPAFinder depends on read coverage fluctuations requiring adequate depth, distorting benchmark comparisons

skills.description: Use when comparing RNA-seq-based IPA site prediction tools for sensitivity, precision, and IPA-usage quantification accuracy, especially when ground-truth polyA sites are known and simulated reads at controlled coverage (10X–50X) are feasible.
skills.name: ipa-site-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: ipa-site-prediction-evaluation Use when comparing RNA-seq-based IPA site prediction tools for sensitivity, precision, and IPA-usage quantification accuracy, especially when ground-truth polyA sites are known and simulated reads at controlled coverage (10X–50X) are feasible. Ground truth consists only of 3'UTR APA events rather than intronic polyadenylation — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap and TAPAS cover 3'UTR APA, but this benchmark targets IPA specifically No predefined/known polyA sites or ground-truth relative usage are available, so TP/FP classification and |ΔPAU| error cannot be computed The goal is novel IPA discovery in real biological samples (e.g. monocyte activation, scRNA-seq) rather than controlled tool benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark computational IPA (intronic polyadenylation) site identification and quantification tools — InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder — on simulated RNA-seq data generated with Polyester at 10X–50X coverage, scoring sensitivity, precision, and per-site quantification error (|ΔPAU|). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Benchmark computational IPA (intronic polyadenylation) site identification and quantification tools — InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder — on simulated RNA-seq data generated with Polyester at 10X–50X coverage, scoring sensitivity, precision, and per-site quantification error (|ΔPAU|).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground truth consists only of 3'UTR APA events rather than intronic polyadenylation — tools like DaPars, Aptardi, APAtrap and TAPAS cover 3'UTR APA, but this benchmark targets IPA specifically No predefined/known polyA sites or ground-truth relative usage are available, so TP/FP classification and |ΔPAU| error cannot be computed The goal is novel IPA discovery in real biological samples (e.g. monocyte activation, scRNA-seq) rather than controlled tool benchmarking

skills.description: Decision support for choosing an IPA quantification method: you have simulated RNA-seq (Polyester, 10X–50X coverage, ≥5 replicates) with predefined polyA sites and known ground-truth relative usage, and need to compare tools' quantification error via |ΔPAU| distributions.
skills.name: ipa-usage-error-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: ipa-usage-error-distribution-analysis Decision support for choosing an IPA quantification method: you have simulated RNA-seq (Polyester, 10X–50X coverage, ≥5 replicates) with predefined polyA sites and known ground-truth relative usage, and need to compare tools' quantification error via |ΔPAU| distributions. Input is real RNA-seq data without known ground-truth relative usage — |ΔPAU| cannot be computed, so use Iso-seq or 3'-end sequencing validation instead The question is IPA site identification accuracy only (sensitivity/precision of site calls), not quantification error of usage values The comparison is between general APA/3'UTR-APA quantification tools (MISO, QAPA, LABRAT, DaPars), which are limited to 3'UTR APA and cannot identify novel IPA isoforms http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark how accurately IPA tools (InPACT, IPAFinder, APAIQ) quantify relative usage of intronic polyadenylation sites by computing per-site absolute PAU error (|ΔPAU|) against ground-truth relative usage on Polyester-simulated RNA-seq data, then visualizing cumulative error distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Benchmark how accurately IPA tools (InPACT, IPAFinder, APAIQ) quantify relative usage of intronic polyadenylation sites by computing per-site absolute PAU error (|ΔPAU|) against ground-truth relative usage on Polyester-simulated RNA-seq data, then visualizing cumulative error distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real RNA-seq data without known ground-truth relative usage — |ΔPAU| cannot be computed, so use Iso-seq or 3'-end sequencing validation instead The question is IPA site identification accuracy only (sensitivity/precision of site calls), not quantification error of usage values The comparison is between general APA/3'UTR-APA quantification tools (MISO, QAPA, LABRAT, DaPars), which are limited to 3'UTR APA and cannot identify novel IPA isoforms

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq profiles of iPSC-derived cells (e.g., hiPSC-NPC n=13, hiPSC-neuron n=11) need cell type assignment to judge whether differentiation toward a target lineage succeeded or stalled.
skills.name: ipsc-differentiation-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: ipsc-differentiation-quality-assessment Use when bulk RNA-seq profiles of iPSC-derived cells (e.g., hiPSC-NPC n=13, hiPSC-neuron n=11) need cell type assignment to judge whether differentiation toward a target lineage succeeded or stalled. Query cells are malignant/cancer cells, since deCS 'might be challenging for cancer cell annotations due to the expression profile difference between healthy and malignant cells' The goal is to discover novel cell types, as deCS is a mapping-based toolkit that 'fails to characterize novel cell types' Input is raw single-cell data without prior normalization, scaling, and clustering to produce a markers_expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assesses the differentiation quality of iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and neurons by annotating normalized bulk RNA-seq sample profiles against human cell type reference panels using deCS correlation analysis, verifying that NPCs map to fetal progenitor/hESC-like types and neurons to neuronal types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Assesses the differentiation quality of iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and neurons by annotating normalized bulk RNA-seq sample profiles against human cell type reference panels using deCS correlation analysis, verifying that NPCs map to fetal progenitor/hESC-like types and neurons to neuronal types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells are malignant/cancer cells, since deCS 'might be challenging for cancer cell annotations due to the expression profile difference between healthy and malignant cells' The goal is to discover novel cell types, as deCS is a mapping-based toolkit that 'fails to characterize novel cell types' Input is raw single-cell data without prior normalization, scaling, and clustering to produce a markers_expression matrix

skills.description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix may contain outlier cells that should be flagged and removed before dropout imputation, based on their distance to the nearest neighboring cell in PC space.
skills.name: iqr-based-anomaly-thresholding
skills.search_text: iqr-based-anomaly-thresholding Use when a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix may contain outlier cells that should be flagged and removed before dropout imputation, based on their distance to the nearest neighboring cell in PC space. The input is not a raw gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. already normalized or imputed data) — scImpute is meant to be applied to the raw read count matrix before downstream analyses such as dimension reduction, normalization, clustering, or differential expression analysis. The analysis goal is to impute dropouts for every cell in a dataset with known, legitimate rare subpopulations — outlier exclusion would remove those cells from imputation rather than correct them. The task is clustering or annotating cell types (e.g. with SNN-Cliq, CIDR, or Seurat) rather than screening cells prior to dropout imputation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects outlier cells in a raw scRNA-seq count matrix by measuring each cell's nearest-neighbor Euclidean distance in a PCA-reduced space and thresholding at the Tukey bound Q3 + 1.5*(Q3 - Q1), so that scImpute can exclude these cells from dropout imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Detects outlier cells in a raw scRNA-seq count matrix by measuring each cell's nearest-neighbor Euclidean distance in a PCA-reduced space and thresholding at the Tukey bound Q3 + 1.5*(Q3 - Q1), so that scImpute can exclude these cells from dropout imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a raw gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. already normalized or imputed data) — scImpute is meant to be applied to the raw read count matrix before downstream analyses such as dimension reduction, normalization, clustering, or differential expression analysis. The analysis goal is to impute dropouts for every cell in a dataset with known, legitimate rare subpopulations — outlier exclusion would remove those cells from imputation rather than correct them. The task is clustering or annotating cell types (e.g. with SNN-Cliq, CIDR, or Seurat) rather than screening cells prior to dropout imputation.

skills.description: Use when initializing demuxmix model fitting on an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and a per-droplet detected-gene vector, and droplets with extreme HTO counts or abnormally many detected genes must be flagged as outliers before mixture fitting.
skills.name: iqr-based-outlier-flagging-of-count-data
skills.search_text: iqr-based-outlier-flagging-of-count-data Use when initializing demuxmix model fitting on an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and a per-droplet detected-gene vector, and droplets with extreme HTO counts or abnormally many detected genes must be flagged as outliers before mixture fitting. Input is not oligonucleotide-labeled scRNA-seq demultiplexing data (no HTO count matrix and no per-droplet detected-genes metric) The goal is downstream classification filtering by assignment error probability — that is the post-fitting step of discarding uncertain droplets, not this pre-fitting outlier flagging Droplets that fail the thresholds should be dropped entirely rather than retained for classification; demuxmix flags outliers as excluded from fitting but still classified Rule-based outlier flagging used in demuxmix preprocessing: k-means (k=2) on log-transformed HTO counts yields initial positive/negative droplet classes, then droplets exceeding Q3 + 1.5*IQR on HTO counts or detected genes are flagged as outliers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Rule-based outlier flagging used in demuxmix preprocessing: k-means (k=2) on log-transformed HTO counts yields initial positive/negative droplet classes, then droplets exceeding Q3 + 1.5*IQR on HTO counts or detected genes are flagged as outliers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not oligonucleotide-labeled scRNA-seq demultiplexing data (no HTO count matrix and no per-droplet detected-genes metric) The goal is downstream classification filtering by assignment error probability — that is the post-fitting step of discarding uncertain droplets, not this pre-fitting outlier flagging Droplets that fail the thresholds should be dropped entirely rather than retained for classification; demuxmix flags outliers as excluded from fitting but still classified

skills.description: Use when you have a per-cell continuous FiRE rareness score vector and need to convert it to binary rare-cell calls via a distribution-based IQR cutoff.
skills.name: iqr-outlier-detection
skills.search_text: iqr-outlier-detection Use when you have a per-cell continuous FiRE rareness score vector and need to convert it to binary rare-cell calls via a distribution-based IQR cutoff. Input is already a binary rare/abundant label table (e.g., RaceID or GiniClust output) — no thresholding needed The score distribution is not the FiRE rareness score (e.g., expression matrix or cluster IDs); IQR fence cutoffs are not meaningful there A fixed expected rare-fraction is required instead of a distribution-derived cutoff — the IQR fence yields data-dependent rare-cell counts (4238/68k in the PBMC analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Dichotomizes continuous FiRE rareness scores into binary rare/not-rare cell labels using Tukey-style IQR thresholding (score >= q3 + 1.5*IQR), as used in the FiRE paper to flag rare cells (e.g., 727 in mouse brain, 4238 in ~68k PBMC data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Dichotomizes continuous FiRE rareness scores into binary rare/not-rare cell labels using Tukey-style IQR thresholding (score >= q3 + 1.5*IQR), as used in the FiRE paper to flag rare cells (e.g., 727 in mouse brain, 4238 in ~68k PBMC data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binary rare/abundant label table (e.g., RaceID or GiniClust output) — no thresholding needed The score distribution is not the FiRE rareness score (e.g., expression matrix or cluster IDs); IQR fence cutoffs are not meaningful there A fixed expected rare-fraction is required instead of a distribution-derived cutoff — the IQR fence yields data-dependent rare-cell counts (4238/68k in the PBMC analysis)

skills.description: Use when you have a continuous rareness score per cell (FiRE, LOF) and need binary rare/non-rare calls for a scRNA-seq dataset, or must compare against binary predictors like RaceID and GiniClust.
skills.name: iqr-threshold-dichotomization
skills.search_text: iqr-threshold-dichotomization Use when you have a continuous rareness score per cell (FiRE, LOF) and need binary rare/non-rare calls for a scRNA-seq dataset, or must compare against binary predictors like RaceID and GiniClust. When the rare population is expected to be far below the ~2.3% implied by a Q3 + 1.5×IQR cutoff — the article separately inspects the top 0.25% of scores to resolve a 0.3% megakaryocyte cluster When you need to separate outlier cells from cells of genuine minor cell types — FiRE (and hence its thresholded calls) does not discriminate between the two When doublets are the target: doublet rates vary 1–30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness captured by this cutoff Dichotomize continuous rareness scores (e.g., FiRE scores per cell) into rare vs non-rare calls by thresholding at the third quartile plus 1.5×IQR (th = Q3 + 1.5×IQR), so that score-based and binary methods can be compared and rare cells isolated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Dichotomize continuous rareness scores (e.g., FiRE scores per cell) into rare vs non-rare calls by thresholding at the third quartile plus 1.5×IQR (th = Q3 + 1.5×IQR), so that score-based and binary methods can be compared and rare cells isolated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the rare population is expected to be far below the ~2.3% implied by a Q3 + 1.5×IQR cutoff — the article separately inspects the top 0.25% of scores to resolve a 0.3% megakaryocyte cluster When you need to separate outlier cells from cells of genuine minor cell types — FiRE (and hence its thresholded calls) does not discriminate between the two When doublets are the target: doublet rates vary 1–30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness captured by this cutoff

skills.description: Use when FiRE (or an equivalent LSH-based density estimator) has produced a per-cell rareness score array and a binary rare/abundant cell label is needed for downstream clustering of candidate rare subpopulations.
skills.name: iqr-threshold-rare-cell-selection
skills.search_text: iqr-threshold-rare-cell-selection Use when FiRE (or an equivalent LSH-based density estimator) has produced a per-cell rareness score array and a binary rare/abundant cell label is needed for downstream clustering of candidate rare subpopulations. Input is raw or unnormalized counts — FiRE scores must be computed on the log2-transformed ranger_preprocess output before IQR thresholding is meaningful The goal is doublet detection — the article notes doublet rate varies between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness Rare and outlier cells must be distinguished — FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types, and outlier cells may get submerged into minor cell clusters when the selected cells are clustered http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects rare cells from a scRNA-seq dataset by thresholding per-cell FiRE rareness scores with the IQR rule (score >= Q3 + 1.5*IQR), converting continuous rareness scores into a binary rare-cell call. In the Arc-ME mouse brain application this retained 727 rare cells that were subsequently clustered into R1-R12 subpopulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Selects rare cells from a scRNA-seq dataset by thresholding per-cell FiRE rareness scores with the IQR rule (score >= Q3 + 1.5*IQR), converting continuous rareness scores into a binary rare-cell call. In the Arc-ME mouse brain application this retained 727 rare cells that were subsequently clustered into R1-R12 subpopulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unnormalized counts — FiRE scores must be computed on the log2-transformed ranger_preprocess output before IQR thresholding is meaningful The goal is doublet detection — the article notes doublet rate varies between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness Rare and outlier cells must be distinguished — FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types, and outlier cells may get submerged into minor cell clusters when the selected cells are clustered

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a rare-cell or doublet detection method whose outlier-calling threshold is adjustable (e.g. FiRE's default vs relaxed IQR threshold) and you need to show the comparison is not an artifact of a single cutoff choice.
skills.name: iqr-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: iqr-threshold-sensitivity-analysis Use when benchmarking a rare-cell or doublet detection method whose outlier-calling threshold is adjustable (e.g. FiRE's default vs relaxed IQR threshold) and you need to show the comparison is not an artifact of a single cutoff choice. The method under comparison has no adjustable outlier threshold, so a single default run suffices Evaluating GapClust itself under alternative cutoffs — its candidate k is fixed by the rule skewness > 2, not an IQR-style threshold A benchmarking sensitivity analysis that evaluates a rare-cell detection method (FiRE) under both its default outlier threshold and a relaxed IQR threshold, scoring each setting by precision, recall, and F1 against ground-truth rare-cell labels on subsampled 68k PBMC datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking sensitivity analysis that evaluates a rare-cell detection method (FiRE) under both its default outlier threshold and a relaxed IQR threshold, scoring each setting by precision, recall, and F1 against ground-truth rare-cell labels on subsampled 68k PBMC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method under comparison has no adjustable outlier threshold, so a single default run suffices Evaluating GapClust itself under alternative cutoffs — its candidate k is fixed by the rule skewness > 2, not an IQR-style threshold

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell count matrix (e.g., 1500 features x >20,000 cells) needs fast, scalable dimension reduction or when comparing wall-clock runtime of CA against glmPCA on benchmark datasets.
skills.name: irlba-partial-svd-computation
skills.search_text: irlba-partial-svd-computation Use when a large single-cell count matrix (e.g., 1500 features x >20,000 cells) needs fast, scalable dimension reduction or when comparing wall-clock runtime of CA against glmPCA on benchmark datasets. The goal is integrating multiple tables or batches — use corralm for multi-table alignment instead of single-table corral The analysis requires model-based factorization that explicitly handles overdispersion (e.g., glmPCA-style negative binomial modeling) rather than fast chi-squared residual decomposition http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes correspondence analysis embeddings for scRNAseq count matrices by partial SVD of the chi-squared residual matrix using irlba, as implemented in the corral R/Bioconductor package. This keeps runtime under a minute even for ~22,000-cell datasets, where glmPCA requires over an hour. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Computes correspondence analysis embeddings for scRNAseq count matrices by partial SVD of the chi-squared residual matrix using irlba, as implemented in the corral R/Bioconductor package. This keeps runtime under a minute even for ~22,000-cell datasets, where glmPCA requires over an hour.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is integrating multiple tables or batches — use corralm for multi-table alignment instead of single-table corral The analysis requires model-based factorization that explicitly handles overdispersion (e.g., glmPCA-style negative binomial modeling) rather than fast chi-squared residual decomposition

skills.description: Use when after applying BUSseq to multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., the four human pancreas datasets), you need a heat-map view of corrected counts over intrinsic genes to confirm that islet and non-islet cell populations separate cleanly rather than clustering by batch.
skills.name: islet-non-islet-separation-visualization
skills.search_text: islet-non-islet-separation-visualization Use when after applying BUSseq to multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., the four human pancreas datasets), you need a heat-map view of corrected counts over intrinsic genes to confirm that islet and non-islet cell populations separate cleanly rather than clustering by batch. Data have not been batch-corrected by BUSseq — plotting raw counts would confound islet/non-islet separation with batch effects The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1-2, batch 2 only types 3-4), where no batch-correction method is applicable The goal is a quantitative clustering metric (ARI, silhouette) rather than a visual separation check — compute those separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize the separation of islet versus non-islet cells on BUSseq-corrected pancreas scRNA-seq counts using heatmap_data_BUSseq with the intrinsic gene set, serving as a qualitative check that batch correction preserved biological cell-type structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Visualize the separation of islet versus non-islet cells on BUSseq-corrected pancreas scRNA-seq counts using heatmap_data_BUSseq with the intrinsic gene set, serving as a qualitative check that batch correction preserved biological cell-type structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have not been batch-corrected by BUSseq — plotting raw counts would confound islet/non-islet separation with batch effects The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1-2, batch 2 only types 3-4), where no batch-correction method is applicable The goal is a quantitative clustering metric (ARI, silhouette) rather than a visual separation check — compute those separately

skills.description: Use when you need to infer TF motif activity trajectories across single-cell cell-cycle phases from unspliced scRNA-seq counts and promoter-annotated motif binding sites.
skills.name: ismara-linear-motif-activity-inference
skills.search_text: ismara-linear-motif-activity-inference Use when you need to infer TF motif activity trajectories across single-cell cell-cycle phases from unspliced scRNA-seq counts and promoter-annotated motif binding sites. Input counts are spliced-only (Ms layer): the model is fit on unspliced 'Mu' counts to capture transcriptional dynamics No cycling genes/patterns are found in the dataset — DeepCycle results would be unreliable and downstream motif activity correlations meaningless No Motevo/Swiss Regulon motif annotation GFF is available for the organism — the promoter-by-motif matrix cannot be constructed Reproduces ISMARA-style transcription factor motif activity estimation by fitting a ridge-regularized linear model on scVelo 'Mu' (unspliced) read counts aggregated over Motevo-predicted promoter binding sites, enabling motif activity dynamics across the cell cycle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Reproduces ISMARA-style transcription factor motif activity estimation by fitting a ridge-regularized linear model on scVelo 'Mu' (unspliced) read counts aggregated over Motevo-predicted promoter binding sites, enabling motif activity dynamics across the cell cycle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input counts are spliced-only (Ms layer): the model is fit on unspliced 'Mu' counts to capture transcriptional dynamics No cycling genes/patterns are found in the dataset — DeepCycle results would be unreliable and downstream motif activity correlations meaningless No Motevo/Swiss Regulon motif annotation GFF is available for the organism — the promoter-by-motif matrix cannot be constructed

skills.description: Use when scoring cross-species scRNA-seq integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL outputs) for biology conservation, specifically to detect overcorrection where nearest-neighbour methods merge cell types present in only a few species datasets.
skills.name: iso-f1-biology-conservation-scoring
skills.search_text: iso-f1-biology-conservation-scoring Use when scoring cross-species scRNA-seq integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL outputs) for biology conservation, specifically to detect overcorrection where nearest-neighbour methods merge cell types present in only a few species datasets. Input is raw un-integrated scRNA-seq data rather than per-strategy integrated embeddings — run an integration algorithm first via the BENGAL pipeline Cell type homology across species is non-one-to-one — the article's quantitative scoring is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings Cell type annotations are uncurated or homology relationships are uncertain — the scoring explicitly assumes accurate annotations and confident literature-supported homology http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the isolated-label F1 (iso_F1) biology-conservation score from cross-species integrated embeddings to test whether cell types found in only a few datasets (species-restricted cell types) remain distinguishable after integration. This is the article's new biology conservation metric addressing maintenance of cell type distinguishability alongside 9 established metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Computes the isolated-label F1 (iso_F1) biology-conservation score from cross-species integrated embeddings to test whether cell types found in only a few datasets (species-restricted cell types) remain distinguishable after integration. This is the article's new biology conservation metric addressing maintenance of cell type distinguishability alongside 9 established metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw un-integrated scRNA-seq data rather than per-strategy integrated embeddings — run an integration algorithm first via the BENGAL pipeline Cell type homology across species is non-one-to-one — the article's quantitative scoring is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings Cell type annotations are uncurated or homology relationships are uncertain — the scoring explicitly assumes accurate annotations and confident literature-supported homology

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq data contain circRNA back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS and you need isoform-level relative expression (read counts, FPKM, TPM) rather than locus-level junction counts.
skills.name: isoform-abundance-assignment
skills.search_text: isoform-abundance-assignment Use when RNA-seq data contain circRNA back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS and you need isoform-level relative expression (read counts, FPKM, TPM) rather than locus-level junction counts. Samples were not RNase R-treated (article states CircAST applies only to RNase R-treated samples; remnant linear mRNA causes false transcripts) The circRNAs of interest are intronic or intergenic — the current pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only locus-level junction counting is needed, e.g. for differential BSJ testing, where full isoform assembly adds unnecessary complexity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Assigns paired-end RNA-seq reads to specific circular RNA isoforms using CircAST's multiple splice graphs and maximum likelihood (EMPC) algorithm, yielding per-isoform junction read counts, FPKM and TPM estimates. It addresses the fact that circRNAs at one locus can have multiple alternatively spliced isoforms sharing the same back-spliced junction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Assigns paired-end RNA-seq reads to specific circular RNA isoforms using CircAST's multiple splice graphs and maximum likelihood (EMPC) algorithm, yielding per-isoform junction read counts, FPKM and TPM estimates. It addresses the fact that circRNAs at one locus can have multiple alternatively spliced isoforms sharing the same back-spliced junction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples were not RNase R-treated (article states CircAST applies only to RNase R-treated samples; remnant linear mRNA causes false transcripts) The circRNAs of interest are intronic or intergenic — the current pipeline assembles only exon-annotated circular transcripts Only locus-level junction counting is needed, e.g. for differential BSJ testing, where full isoform assembly adds unnecessary complexity
