skills.search_text: isoform-abundance-cosine-similarity-comparison Use when benchmarking isoform detection and quantification accuracy of long-read transcript tools against a set of known reference isoforms (e.g. SIRV spike-ins with PacBio data), needing detection counts plus cosine similarity of abundance profiles. The dataset has no known reference isoforms or expected abundances to compare against (no ground truth for exact matching or cosine similarity) Input is short-read sequencing data — this skill is grounded in long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq, ONT) isoform analysis with GMAP alignments The goal is de novo transcriptome discovery/annotation genome-wide (e.g. a bambu/SQANTI3 reference-guided workflow) rather than per-gene or spike-in benchmarking against a known isoform panel Benchmarks long-read isoform detection/quantification tools (VIsoQLR, FLAIR, StringTie2) by comparing each tool's assembled isoform set against known reference isoforms and computing the cosine similarity between predicted and reference isoform abundance profiles, as done on SIRV spike-ins with GMAP-aligned PacBio Iso-Seq reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks long-read isoform detection/quantification tools (VIsoQLR, FLAIR, StringTie2) by comparing each tool's assembled isoform set against known reference isoforms and computing the cosine similarity between predicted and reference isoform abundance profiles, as done on SIRV spike-ins with GMAP-aligned PacBio Iso-Seq reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known reference isoforms or expected abundances to compare against (no ground truth for exact matching or cosine similarity) Input is short-read sequencing data — this skill is grounded in long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq, ONT) isoform analysis with GMAP alignments The goal is de novo transcriptome discovery/annotation genome-wide (e.g. a bambu/SQANTI3 reference-guided workflow) rather than per-gene or spike-in benchmarking against a known isoform panel

skills.description: Use when a GMAP- or minimap2-aligned BAM from long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT) data needs per-isoform abundance quantification for a single gene/locus, and the read-threshold parameter must be tuned or its sensitivity characterized against a known isoform profile.
skills.name: isoform-abundance-quantification
skills.search_text: isoform-abundance-quantification Use when a GMAP- or minimap2-aligned BAM from long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT) data needs per-isoform abundance quantification for a single gene/locus, and the read-threshold parameter must be tuned or its sensitivity characterized against a known isoform profile. The goal is whole-transcriptome annotation rather than close inspection and fine-tuning of one gene at a time — VIsoQLR is explicitly designed for single-locus, low-throughput splicing assays. Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been aligned (GMAP/minimap2 alignment must precede isoform identification and quantification). Isoform quantification accuracy must be judged by exon-coordinate correctness alone (e.g. the SIRV benchmark's 99% exon-coordinate accuracy) rather than by abundance-profile similarity, which this skill measures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify isoform abundances from long-read sequencing alignments of a target gene using VIsoQLR's CEC-based isoform identification, testing how the 'Read threshold (%)' parameter trades off isoform sensitivity against quantification accuracy (cosine similarity to a reference abundance profile). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Quantify isoform abundances from long-read sequencing alignments of a target gene using VIsoQLR's CEC-based isoform identification, testing how the 'Read threshold (%)' parameter trades off isoform sensitivity against quantification accuracy (cosine similarity to a reference abundance profile).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is whole-transcriptome annotation rather than close inspection and fine-tuning of one gene at a time — VIsoQLR is explicitly designed for single-locus, low-throughput splicing assays. Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been aligned (GMAP/minimap2 alignment must precede isoform identification and quantification). Isoform quantification accuracy must be judged by exon-coordinate correctness alone (e.g. the SIRV benchmark's 99% exon-coordinate accuracy) rather than by abundance-profile similarity, which this skill measures.

skills.description: Use when region sets are defined only by genomic positions without clear isoform association (e.g., POSTAR3/RBP or RNA modification sites) and you need transcriptome-level association testing against picked regions like 5'UTR, CDS, or stop codons.
skills.name: isoform-ambiguity-aware-colocalization-analysis
skills.search_text: isoform-ambiguity-aware-colocalization-analysis Use when region sets are defined only by genomic positions without clear isoform association (e.g., POSTAR3/RBP or RNA modification sites) and you need transcriptome-level association testing against picked regions like 5'UTR, CDS, or stop codons. Region sets already have clear transcript/isoform association and standard region-region permutation suffices — use permTestTx or permTestTx_customPick instead The analysis target is genome-based colocalization without transcriptome context — existing genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, BEDTools, regioneR) are the appropriate comparison point, and RgnTX's transcriptome null model would not match Input is a feature table without genomic coordinates, so sites cannot be projected onto isoforms http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Performs colocalization analysis of transcriptome elements (e.g., RNA modification sites like m7G or m6A with unknown isoform origin) against regions of interest (e.g., 5'UTR, CDS, stop codons) using RgnTX's IA-mode permutation tests, which explicitly model isoform ambiguity and alternative splicing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Performs colocalization analysis of transcriptome elements (e.g., RNA modification sites like m7G or m6A with unknown isoform origin) against regions of interest (e.g., 5'UTR, CDS, stop codons) using RgnTX's IA-mode permutation tests, which explicitly model isoform ambiguity and alternative splicing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Region sets already have clear transcript/isoform association and standard region-region permutation suffices — use permTestTx or permTestTx_customPick instead The analysis target is genome-based colocalization without transcriptome context — existing genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, BEDTools, regioneR) are the appropriate comparison point, and RgnTX's transcriptome null model would not match Input is a feature table without genomic coordinates, so sites cannot be projected onto isoforms

skills.description: Use when a region set (e.g. m6A sites from POSTAR3/miCLIP-seq) has genomic positions but no known transcript isoform association, and you need an overlap score or permutation test against transcriptome regions of interest such as stop codons.
skills.name: isoform-ambiguity-fractional-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: isoform-ambiguity-fractional-overlap-scoring Use when a region set (e.g. m6A sites from POSTAR3/miCLIP-seq) has genomic positions but no known transcript isoform association, and you need an overlap score or permutation test against transcriptome regions of interest such as stop codons. The region set already has clear isoform association (each element maps to a known transcript) — use permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead. The analysis target is genome-based colocalization of genomic region sets where transcriptome heterogeneity is irrelevant (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks vs genome intervals via LOLA/GREAT/BEDTools). http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute colocalization overlap scores for transcriptome features that carry isoform ambiguity by summing per-feature fractional contributions c(i)/n(i), where c(i) is the count of overlaps with the transcriptome ROIs and n(i) is the number of isoform transcripts the feature can be aligned to, as implemented in RgnTX's overlapCountsTxIA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Compute colocalization overlap scores for transcriptome features that carry isoform ambiguity by summing per-feature fractional contributions c(i)/n(i), where c(i) is the count of overlaps with the transcriptome ROIs and n(i) is the number of isoform transcripts the feature can be aligned to, as implemented in RgnTX's overlapCountsTxIA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The region set already has clear isoform association (each element maps to a known transcript) — use permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick with overlapCountsTx instead. The analysis target is genome-based colocalization of genomic region sets where transcriptome heterogeneity is irrelevant (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks vs genome intervals via LOLA/GREAT/BEDTools).

skills.description: Use when transcriptome elements (e.g. POSTAR3 RBP sites or miCLIP-seq m6A sites) have known genomic positions but no clear isoform association, and a permutation-based colocalization test at the transcriptome level is required.
skills.name: isoform-ambiguity-handling
skills.search_text: isoform-ambiguity-handling Use when transcriptome elements (e.g. POSTAR3 RBP sites or miCLIP-seq m6A sites) have known genomic positions but no clear isoform association, and a permutation-based colocalization test at the transcriptome level is required. Features already have a clear isoform association — use randomizeTx/permTestTx with overlapCountsTx on specified transcript IDs instead The analysis is purely genome-based with no transcriptome annotation involved — existing genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, regioneR) are the appropriate choice The input is not region data but, e.g., an expression matrix or feature table with no genomic coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Handles transcriptome elements with unknown isoform association in RgnTX colocalization analysis by projecting features to the genome, collecting all overlapping isoform transcripts, and permuting each feature only over those permitted transcripts while preserving feature width. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Handles transcriptome elements with unknown isoform association in RgnTX colocalization analysis by projecting features to the genome, collecting all overlapping isoform transcripts, and permuting each feature only over those permitted transcripts while preserving feature width.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features already have a clear isoform association — use randomizeTx/permTestTx with overlapCountsTx on specified transcript IDs instead The analysis is purely genome-based with no transcriptome annotation involved — existing genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, regioneR) are the appropriate choice The input is not region data but, e.g., an expression matrix or feature table with no genomic coordinates

skills.summary: Reproduces the barcode-based post-assembly filtering step from cloudrnaSPAdes, which removes contigs whose barcode is assigned to a single gene multiple times, and quantifies how much of the ambiguous-assignment fraction this removes (~15% difference between the '1' and '1-fixed' Table 3 rows) on real SPIso-seq contigs assembled by cloudrnaSPAdes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already-filtered ('1-fixed') output — reapplying the duplicate-barcode filter would double-remove and inflate the removal rate beyond the ~15% Table 3 difference Data are the simulated human data sets or the SPAdes toy data set (first 1000 bp of E. coli) rather than the real SPIso-seq contigs the Table 3 fixed rows refer to The goal is read-level filtering before assembly (e.g. median k-mer coverage filtering with spades-read-filter) rather than post-assembly contig filtering

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers by counting uniquely assigned reference isoforms from IsoQuant assignment output files against a GENCODE annotation for a specific gene locus.
skills.name: isoform-assignment-parsing-from-alignment-tools
skills.search_text: isoform-assignment-parsing-from-alignment-tools Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers by counting uniquely assigned reference isoforms from IsoQuant assignment output files against a GENCODE annotation for a specific gene locus. No IsoQuant assignment output files exist and only raw read alignments are available — counts must come from IsoQuant assignments, not from re-annotating BAMs. The assembler failed mid-pipeline (e.g. RNA-Bloom at the k-mer counting step) — record it as a failure status rather than running the counter on empty outputs and reporting zero isoforms. The reference annotation is not GENCODE v32 (or the locus's isoform set differs) — the counts are defined against the 34 annotated ATP6AP2 isoforms and are not comparable across annotation versions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Parse IsoQuant transcript-assignment output files generated for multiple de novo transcriptome assemblies and count how many annotated GENCODE isoforms of a target gene locus (e.g. ATP6AP2 on chromosome X, 34 GENCODE v32 isoforms) received a unique, unambiguous assignment per assembler. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: Parse IsoQuant transcript-assignment output files generated for multiple de novo transcriptome assemblies and count how many annotated GENCODE isoforms of a target gene locus (e.g. ATP6AP2 on chromosome X, 34 GENCODE v32 isoforms) received a unique, unambiguous assignment per assembler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No IsoQuant assignment output files exist and only raw read alignments are available — counts must come from IsoQuant assignments, not from re-annotating BAMs. The assembler failed mid-pipeline (e.g. RNA-Bloom at the k-mer counting step) — record it as a failure status rather than running the counter on empty outputs and reporting zero isoforms. The reference annotation is not GENCODE v32 (or the locus's isoform set differs) — the counts are defined against the 34 annotated ATP6AP2 isoforms and are not comparable across annotation versions.

skills.search_text: isoform-switch-interaction-loss-assessment Use when a dMDT or isoform switching event (e.g. transcript ENST00000380405) is identified and you need to determine which high-confidence STRING interactions are lost because the switched isoform lacks domains mediating them. skills.search_text: iterative-reliable-cell-selection Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq (source) with unlabeled scATAC-seq (target) h5ad data and cell heterogeneity means some target cells are easy to bridge while others differ strongly across omics. Data are paired multi-omics (same cells profiled in both omics) — scAI/MOFA+ style joint integration with pairing information applies instead The goal is novel cell-type discovery without the structure preservation loss enabled; the reliability loop as described assumes all target cells belong to known source types The target is not scATAC-seq gene-activity data derived from peaks (peak-by-cell matrices must first be transformed into an activity matrix, e.g., with Signac) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 The scBridge loop that progressively identifies reliable scATAC-seq cells (via GMM-modeled reliability over embedding discriminability and classification confidence) and merges them into the annotated scRNA-seq set, integrating cells from-easy-to-hard to narrow the omics gap without treating all cells homogeneously. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: The scBridge loop that progressively identifies reliable scATAC-seq cells (via GMM-modeled reliability over embedding discriminability and classification confidence) and merges them into the annotated scRNA-seq set, integrating cells from-easy-to-hard to narrow the omics gap without treating all cells homogeneously.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are paired multi-omics (same cells profiled in both omics) — scAI/MOFA+ style joint integration with pairing information applies instead The goal is novel cell-type discovery without the structure preservation loss enabled; the reliability loop as described assumes all target cells belong to known source types The target is not scATAC-seq gene-activity data derived from peaks (peak-by-cell matrices must first be transformed into an activity matrix, e.g., with Signac)

skills.search_text: iterative-subnetwork-module-mining Use when building a fixed blood transcriptome module repertoire from multiple GEO cohort expression datasets: transcripts must be grouped by co-clustering across cohorts and mined from a weighted graph into stable modules and aggregates. skills.summary: Constructs the BloodGen3 fixed module repertoire by co-clustering transcripts across 16 blood transcriptome datasets (985 unique profiles), converting cross-cohort co-clustering frequencies into a weighted co-expression graph, and iteratively mining sub-networks until segmentation stabilizes into 382 modules covering 14,168 transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing tissues other than blood or non-human species — the BloodGen3 repertoire is specifically designed for human blood transcriptome profiling data, and other contexts require separate frameworks Performing group comparison or individual fingerprint analysis on an already-built repertoire — use the BloodGen3Module Groupcomparison/Individualcomparison/gridplot functions instead of re-mining the network Input expression data are already summarized into fixed gene sets/modules — this skill only applies when constructing a new repertoire from raw cohort-level expression profiles

skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional dataset (e.g. single-cell expression, CyTOF, or synthetic benchmarks with redundant polynomial features) must be embedded in 2–3 dimensions while preserving global cluster shapes and relative locations, or when t-SNE's spurious clustering is a concern.
skills.name: ivis-siamese-embedding
skills.search_text: ivis-siamese-embedding Use when a high-dimensional dataset (e.g. single-cell expression, CyTOF, or synthetic benchmarks with redundant polynomial features) must be embedded in 2–3 dimensions while preserving global cluster shapes and relative locations, or when t-SNE's spurious clustering is a concern. When the goal is strictly local structure at the expense of global geometry, or when a well-validated non-neural method is mandated — the paper shows t-SNE and related pairwise-(dis)similarity methods (e.g. LargeVis) tend to yield spurious clusters, but they remain standard for other goals When data cannot be scaled to [0, 1] or the analysis requires interpretability of the original feature axes rather than an embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional datasets with ivis, a siamese neural network trained with a triplet loss, which preserves both local and global structure in low-dimensional embeddings — unlike t-SNE, which forms spurious compact clusters in the presence of uniform random noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional datasets with ivis, a siamese neural network trained with a triplet loss, which preserves both local and global structure in low-dimensional embeddings — unlike t-SNE, which forms spurious compact clusters in the presence of uniform random noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is strictly local structure at the expense of global geometry, or when a well-validated non-neural method is mandated — the paper shows t-SNE and related pairwise-(dis)similarity methods (e.g. LargeVis) tend to yield spurious clusters, but they remain standard for other goals When data cannot be scaled to [0, 1] or the analysis requires interpretability of the original feature axes rather than an embedding

skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional single-cell expression matrix (e.g. melanoma 4,645 x 23,686 from SCP11, hippocampus, retinal bipolar) needs a 2D embedding that preserves both local cell-type clusters and global inter-cluster relationships.
skills.name: ivis-triplet-loss-embedding-training
skills.search_text: ivis-triplet-loss-embedding-training Use when a high-dimensional single-cell expression matrix (e.g. melanoma 4,645 x 23,686 from SCP11, hippocampus, retinal bipolar) needs a 2D embedding that preserves both local cell-type clusters and global inter-cluster relationships. Data is low-dimensional or already an embedding — ivis is designed for high-dimensional single-cell expression matrices You need annotated spurious-cluster behavior analysis with clean boundaries — t-SNE/SIMLR comparisons are separate skills; ivis is chosen to avoid spurious clusters under random noise Dataset exceeds the validated hyperparameter regime (>500,000 observations) without adjusting the recommended k/model settings http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train the ivis siamese neural network with a triplet-loss function to produce 2D structure-preserving embeddings of high-dimensional scRNA-seq (and CyTOF) datasets, using MinMaxScaler [0,1] scaling and PCA-50 reduction as preprocessing and k=15, model='maaten' for datasets under 500,000 observations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Train the ivis siamese neural network with a triplet-loss function to produce 2D structure-preserving embeddings of high-dimensional scRNA-seq (and CyTOF) datasets, using MinMaxScaler [0,1] scaling and PCA-50 reduction as preprocessing and k=15, model='maaten' for datasets under 500,000 observations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is low-dimensional or already an embedding — ivis is designed for high-dimensional single-cell expression matrices You need annotated spurious-cluster behavior analysis with clean boundaries — t-SNE/SIMLR comparisons are separate skills; ivis is chosen to avoid spurious clusters under random noise Dataset exceeds the validated hyperparameter regime (>500,000 observations) without adjusting the recommended k/model settings

skills.name: jaccard-ari-shifting-distance-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-ari-shifting-distance-computation Use when comparing spatial domain labels against layer annotations on multi-slice ST data (e.g., 12 DLPFC Visium slices) to quantify accuracy via JI, median ARI, and average shifting distance. skills.summary: Benchmarking metric suite for spatial domain identification on human DLPFC Visium slices: compute the Jaccard index (JI) between predicted domains and annotated cortical layers, the median adjusted Rand index (ARI) across slices, and the average shifting distance, to compare joint vs single-slice analyses (e.g., Splane vs Splane-single).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue has no ground-truth layer/domain annotations (e.g., a breast cancer Visium dataset), so JI against annotated cortical layers and shifting distance cannot be computed. The data are single slices with no joint vs single comparison to make — ARI/JI benchmarking of multi-slice integration is not the goal.

skills.description: Decision support for judging whether a 2D embedding (e.g. PCA, UMAP, t-SNE of normalized scRNA-seq data) is suitable for trajectory inference, by detecting disconnected cell clusters or homogeneous cells lacking a trajectory signal before fitting a trajectory.
skills.name: jaccard-index-cluster-distance-assessment
skills.search_text: jaccard-index-cluster-distance-assessment Decision support for judging whether a 2D embedding (e.g. PCA, UMAP, t-SNE of normalized scRNA-seq data) is suitable for trajectory inference, by detecting disconnected cell clusters or homogeneous cells lacking a trajectory signal before fitting a trajectory. The trajectory inference method of interest does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches using two-dimensional representations The dimension reduction is derived from RNA velocity — Escort has not yet implemented support for velocity-derived dimension reduction methods You need a guaranteed recommendation — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the evaluated choices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Escort's connectivity check for single-cell embeddings: computes Manhattan distance-based within- vs between-cluster distance distributions, derives Jaccard index scores per cell, and declares clusters disconnected (immediately disqualifying the embedding for trajectory inference) when connectivity fails the 0.3 cutoff in >10 cells per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Escort's connectivity check for single-cell embeddings: computes Manhattan distance-based within- vs between-cluster distance distributions, derives Jaccard index scores per cell, and declares clusters disconnected (immediately disqualifying the embedding for trajectory inference) when connectivity fails the 0.3 cutoff in >10 cells per cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory inference method of interest does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches using two-dimensional representations The dimension reduction is derived from RNA velocity — Escort has not yet implemented support for velocity-derived dimension reduction methods You need a guaranteed recommendation — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the evaluated choices

skills.name: jaccard-similarity-analysis-of-regulon-rankings
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-analysis-of-regulon-rankings Use when two gene regulatory network inference tools (e.g., MINI-EX and SCENIC) have produced per-cell-type regulons and you need to quantify their overlap per cluster and validate specific regulon TF calls. Only one regulon set is available — Jaccard similarity requires two tools' regulon predictions to compare The dataset is not plant scRNA-seq with defined cell-type annotations, since MINI-EX/scPlant regulon inference and the bZIP44/ANAC030 reference calls are plant-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Quantifies agreement between cell-type-specific regulons inferred by MINI-EX and SCENIC on the Arabidopsis root single-cell atlas by computing Jaccard similarity of the top 30 regulons per cell cluster, verifying cross-tool consistency (bZIP44 in companion cells, ANAC030 in xylem) and the higher signal-to-noise ratio of MINI-EX. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between cell-type-specific regulons inferred by MINI-EX and SCENIC on the Arabidopsis root single-cell atlas by computing Jaccard similarity of the top 30 regulons per cell cluster, verifying cross-tool consistency (bZIP44 in companion cells, ANAC030 in xylem) and the higher signal-to-noise ratio of MINI-EX.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one regulon set is available — Jaccard similarity requires two tools' regulon predictions to compare The dataset is not plant scRNA-seq with defined cell-type annotations, since MINI-EX/scPlant regulon inference and the bZIP44/ANAC030 reference calls are plant-specific

skills.description: Use when comparing which interactions are shared versus distinct across CCC inference methods, resources, or datasets — e.g., to measure how much top-ranked predictions from CellChat vs NATMI (or CellChatDB vs Ramilowski) overlap.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-computation Use when comparing which interactions are shared versus distinct across CCC inference methods, resources, or datasets — e.g., to measure how much top-ranked predictions from CellChat vs NATMI (or CellChatDB vs Ramilowski) overlap. When a gold-standard comparison of prediction accuracy is needed — no gold standard for CCC exists, so Jaccard overlap only measures agreement, not correctness When methods infer intracellular processes (NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC) that are not directly comparable to ligand-receptor methods When interactions should not be decomplexified (comparing complex-level rather than subunit-level resource contents) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies overlap between sets of cell-cell communication interactions (or resource contents) by building presence-absence matrices and computing pairwise Jaccard indices, used in Dimitrov et al. 2022 to show that both CCC methods and prior-knowledge resources strongly influence predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Quantifies overlap between sets of cell-cell communication interactions (or resource contents) by building presence-absence matrices and computing pairwise Jaccard indices, used in Dimitrov et al. 2022 to show that both CCC methods and prior-knowledge resources strongly influence predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a gold-standard comparison of prediction accuracy is needed — no gold standard for CCC exists, so Jaccard overlap only measures agreement, not correctness When methods infer intracellular processes (NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC) that are not directly comparable to ligand-receptor methods When interactions should not be decomplexified (comparing complex-level rather than subunit-level resource contents)

skills.name: jaccard-similarity-computation
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-computation Use when quantifying overlap between marker gene sets for the same cell types across multiple marker databases or cell-sorting marker collections to assess database consistency. When the goal is cell type annotation of single-cell data rather than quantifying marker database overlap — use the Cell Marker Accordion accordion() function instead When cell type labels between sources cannot be reconciled (e.g., no mapping to a shared ontology), since Jaccard on non-common cell types is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Computes pairwise Jaccard similarity (intersection/union of marker gene sets) between cell-type marker databases such as CellMarker2.0 and PanglaoDB to quantify marker-set consistency, as done in the Cell Marker Accordion paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Computes pairwise Jaccard similarity (intersection/union of marker gene sets) between cell-type marker databases such as CellMarker2.0 and PanglaoDB to quantify marker-set consistency, as done in the Cell Marker Accordion paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cell type annotation of single-cell data rather than quantifying marker database overlap — use the Cell Marker Accordion accordion() function instead When cell type labels between sources cannot be reconciled (e.g., no mapping to a shared ontology), since Jaccard on non-common cell types is meaningless

skills.description: Use when a pathway enrichment analysis needs inter-pathway dependencies quantified from gene set overlaps — e.g. before fitting pareg with network regularization, or for rendering a pathway network view — and the input is a term-to-gene mapping (df_terms) such as GO BP terms of size 50-500.
skills.name: jaccard-similarity-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-matrix-construction Use when a pathway enrichment analysis needs inter-pathway dependencies quantified from gene set overlaps — e.g. before fitting pareg with network regularization, or for rendering a pathway network view — and the input is a term-to-gene mapping (df_terms) such as GO BP terms of size 50-500. The analysis does not model inter-pathway dependencies — e.g. running plain over-representation analysis or pareg's no-regularization variant (pareg_noterms) requires no term similarity matrix. The pathway database is so small or non-redundant that pathway overlap carries no useful signal; Jaccard similarity is only meaningful when pathways share genes. You need semantic (ontology-based) pathway similarity rather than gene-set-overlap similarity; the article compares similarity measures on GO Biological Process because they can differ substantially. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Construct a pairwise pathway similarity matrix from a pathway database (gene set annotations) using pareg's compute_term_similarities helper with the Jaccard similarity function; this matrix supplies the network regularization (term_network) input to pareg's regularized GLM and enables pathway-network visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Construct a pairwise pathway similarity matrix from a pathway database (gene set annotations) using pareg's compute_term_similarities helper with the Jaccard similarity function; this matrix supplies the network regularization (term_network) input to pareg's regularized GLM and enables pathway-network visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis does not model inter-pathway dependencies — e.g. running plain over-representation analysis or pareg's no-regularization variant (pareg_noterms) requires no term similarity matrix. The pathway database is so small or non-redundant that pathway overlap carries no useful signal; Jaccard similarity is only meaningful when pathways share genes. You need semantic (ontology-based) pathway similarity rather than gene-set-overlap similarity; the article compares similarity measures on GO Biological Process because they can differ substantially.

skills.description: Use when comparing label vocabularies across published single-cell references (e.g. is HCC 'Lymphoid-B' closer to naive or memory B cells?) or harmonizing subtype annotations from multiple atlases.

skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-matrix-construction Use when comparing label vocabularies across published single-cell references (e.g. is HCC 'Lymphoid-B' closer to naive or memory B cells?) or harmonizing subtype annotations from multiple atlases. When only a single dataset is available — the similarity matrix requires cross-reference testing across multiple labeled datasets. When the goal is malignant cell identification or spatial transcriptome analysis, which are separate scCancer2 modules, not label similarity mapping. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Quantitatively maps the similarity between cell subtype labels defined in different scRNA-seq references by training subtype classifiers, testing them across datasets, and computing a Jaccard similarity matrix (e.g. scCancer2's similarityCalculation over integrated fine labels). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Quantitatively maps the similarity between cell subtype labels defined in different scRNA-seq references by training subtype classifiers, testing them across datasets, and computing a Jaccard similarity matrix (e.g. scCancer2's similarityCalculation over integrated fine labels).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single dataset is available — the similarity matrix requires cross-reference testing across multiple labeled datasets. When the goal is malignant cell identification or spatial transcriptome analysis, which are separate scCancer2 modules, not label similarity mapping.

skills.name: jaccard-similarity-module-overlap-quantification
skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-module-overlap-quantification Use when two PyWGCNA objects (e.g., the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD networks) have been built with module assignments and you need to find which module pairs significantly overlap, indicating conserved co-expression signatures across datasets. Only one network exists — comparing a PyWGCNA object to an external gene marker list uses the Comparison_PyWGCNA_geneMarker workflow instead You need to compare more than two PyWGCNA objects — the article provides a separate multi-comparison tutorial (Comparison_multi_PyWGCNAs.ipynb) Your goal is functional enrichment (GO, KEGG, REACTOME) or PPI (STRING) analysis of a single module rather than cross-dataset module overlap http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies co-expression module overlap between two WGCNA networks (here the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq networks) using Jaccard similarity, gene-membership contingency tables, and Fisher's exact test P-values to identify modules with significant overlap conserved across datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Quantifies co-expression module overlap between two WGCNA networks (here the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD brain bulk RNA-seq networks) using Jaccard similarity, gene-membership contingency tables, and Fisher's exact test P-values to identify modules with significant overlap conserved across datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one network exists — comparing a PyWGCNA object to an external gene marker list uses the Comparison_PyWGCNA_geneMarker workflow instead You need to compare more than two PyWGCNA objects — the article provides a separate multi-comparison tutorial (Comparison_multi_PyWGCNAs.ipynb) Your goal is functional enrichment (GO, KEGG, REACTOME) or PPI (STRING) analysis of a single module rather than cross-dataset module overlap

skills.search_text: jaccard-similarity-of-top-ranked-regulators Use when comparing activity-inference methods (e.g. the 11 decoupleR methods) on the same omics benchmark to measure whether methods nominate the same top regulators, complementing median Spearman correlation of activity scores. skills.summary: Quantifies cross-method agreement among decoupleR activity-inference methods by ranking regulators by inferred activity score, retaining the top 5% per method, and computing pairwise Jaccard indexes on those top-regulator sets (median reported: 0.23 for transcriptomics, 0.21 for phospho-proteomics).

Comparing regulator rankings across different prior-knowledge resources rather than across inference methods within one resource.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data have been summarized to CTP/ctnu/P inputs and you need per-gene p-values for cell type-specific interindividual variance differentiation that are robust at modest sample sizes.
skills.name: jackknife-based-wald-testing
skills.search_text: jackknife-based-wald-testing Use when scRNA-seq data have been summarized to CTP/ctnu/P inputs and you need per-gene p-values for cell type-specific interindividual variance differentiation that are robust at modest sample sizes. Sample sizes below ~50 individuals, where the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable Rare cell types: CTMM requires >10 cells per individual-cell type pair, limiting it to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes, which can be severely non-Gaussian and violate the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit the CTMM Free model on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data with REML and enable the jackknife-based Wald test to obtain calibrated gene-level p-values for differentiation of expression variance (V) and mean expression (ct_beta) across cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fit the CTMM Free model on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data with REML and enable the jackknife-based Wald test to obtain calibrated gene-level p-values for differentiation of expression variance (V) and mean expression (ct_beta) across cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes below ~50 individuals, where the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable Rare cell types: CTMM requires >10 cells per individual-cell type pair, limiting it to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes, which can be severely non-Gaussian and violate the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation

skills.description: Use when fitting per-gene PLS1 regression models on multi-omics GRN data (e.g., voom-transformed RNA-seq response against miRNA-seq and TF predictor layers) and you need to separate regulations stable across resampled fits from spurious single-fit associations.
skills.name: jackknife-model-stability-assessment
skills.search_text: jackknife-model-stability-assessment Use when fitting per-gene PLS1 regression models on multi-omics GRN data (e.g., voom-transformed RNA-seq response against miRNA-seq and TF predictor layers) and you need to separate regulations stable across resampled fits from spurious single-fit associations. Single-cell data: MOSim validates single-cell gene-regulator relationships with Kendall's Tb correlation, not Pearson on bulk profiles, so a bulk PLS1 + Pearson stability workflow is the wrong template Data simulated from omics layers MOSim does not cover (proteomics, metabolomics, spatially resolved GRNs), where no ground-truth regulatory network exists for stability-based inference Datasets without a two-group simulated design or ground-truth regulatory pairs — Jack-Knife stability can flag coefficients, but sensitivity/F1 benchmarking against random feature pairs requires the simulated true positives/negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Per-gene regression models (PLS1 in the MORE GRN-inference benchmark) are refitted under Jack-Knife resampling so that regulator coefficients surviving resampling are called stable/significant regulations rather than artifacts of a single fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Per-gene regression models (PLS1 in the MORE GRN-inference benchmark) are refitted under Jack-Knife resampling so that regulator coefficients surviving resampling are called stable/significant regulations rather than artifacts of a single fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell data: MOSim validates single-cell gene-regulator relationships with Kendall's Tb correlation, not Pearson on bulk profiles, so a bulk PLS1 + Pearson stability workflow is the wrong template Data simulated from omics layers MOSim does not cover (proteomics, metabolomics, spatially resolved GRNs), where no ground-truth regulatory network exists for stability-based inference Datasets without a two-group simulated design or ground-truth regulatory pairs — Jack-Knife stability can flag coefficients, but sensitivity/F1 benchmarking against random feature pairs requires the simulated true positives/negatives

skills.description: Use when you must choose how many PCs to retain in a scRNA-seq PCA objectively (jackstraw p-values), or quantify whether imputation/denoising preserved the signal subspace via subspace angles.
skills.name: jackstraw-pc-significance-testing
skills.search_text: jackstraw-pc-significance-testing Use when you must choose how many PCs to retain in a scRNA-seq PCA objectively (jackstraw p-values), or quantify whether imputation/denoising preserved the signal subspace via subspace angles. The input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix but already a dimensionality-reduced embedding or feature table — jackstraw significance testing requires raw gene-level PCA. The question is whether ALRA's imputed values match held-out entries directly (use the out-of-bag-error skill instead of subspace-angle comparison). Datasets have no downsampled counterpart, since the angle-reduction validation (e.g., Baron 0.34->0.25) is defined only for original/downsampled pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the number of signal-bearing principal components from scRNA-seq PCA using Seurat's jackstraw permutation-based significance testing (retaining PCs with p-value ≤ 1e-5), then measures subspace agreement between PC bases of original, downsampled, and ALRA-imputed matrices with pracma's subspace function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Selects the number of signal-bearing principal components from scRNA-seq PCA using Seurat's jackstraw permutation-based significance testing (retaining PCs with p-value ≤ 1e-5), then measures subspace agreement between PC bases of original, downsampled, and ALRA-imputed matrices with pracma's subspace function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix but already a dimensionality-reduced embedding or feature table — jackstraw significance testing requires raw gene-level PCA. The question is whether ALRA's imputed values match held-out entries directly (use the out-of-bag-error skill instead of subspace-angle comparison). Datasets have no downsampled counterpart, since the angle-reduction validation (e.g., Baron 0.34->0.25) is defined only for original/downsampled pairs.

skills.description: Use when evaluating spatial reconstruction of single-cell data (e.g., CellContrast on SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections) and you need to score whether reconstructed neighbors reproduce the reference local cell-type composition.
skills.name: jensen-shannon-cell-type-distribution-comparison
skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-cell-type-distribution-comparison Use when evaluating spatial reconstruction of single-cell data (e.g., CellContrast on SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections) and you need to score whether reconstructed neighbors reproduce the reference local cell-type composition. When the goal is global spatial alignment rather than local neighborhood composition — use SC-ST mapping plus Spearman's rank correlation of pairwise distances instead When truth cell-type annotations or truth coordinates (.obs[['x','y']]) are unavailable for the test section, since JSD cannot be computed without a reference composition http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark metric for spatial reconstruction methods that compares predicted versus true cell-type proportions among the k=20 nearest neighbors of each cell using the Jensen-Shannon distance (Scipy jensenshannon), quantifying how well local cell-type composition is preserved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Benchmark metric for spatial reconstruction methods that compares predicted versus true cell-type proportions among the k=20 nearest neighbors of each cell using the Jensen-Shannon distance (Scipy jensenshannon), quantifying how well local cell-type composition is preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is global spatial alignment rather than local neighborhood composition — use SC-ST mapping plus Spearman's rank correlation of pairwise distances instead When truth cell-type annotations or truth coordinates (.obs[['x','y']]) are unavailable for the test section, since JSD cannot be computed without a reference composition

skills.description: Use when constructing a cell-cell similarity network from ACTIONet multilevel decomposition outputs: cells are represented as convex archetype-mixing weight vectors and a distribution-aware, bounded distance is needed for density-dependent k*-NN edge selection.
skills.name: jensen-shannon-distance-computation
skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-distance-computation Use when constructing a cell-cell similarity network from ACTIONet multilevel decomposition outputs: cells are represented as convex archetype-mixing weight vectors and a distribution-aware, bounded distance is needed for density-dependent k*-NN edge selection. Input is raw or only library-size-normalized gene expression (not the reduced H* archetype-weight space) — distances should be computed after an.pp.reduce_kernel, not directly on counts The goal is a fixed-k nearest-neighbor graph (e.g. standard scanpy neighbors) rather than ACTIONet's density-adaptive k*-NN multiresolution network Cell representations are not nonnegative mixture weights over archetypes, since Jensen-Shannon divergence presumes probability-like distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute pairwise square-root Jensen-Shannon distances between cells in ACTIONet's reduced archetypal metric space (the normalized multilevel encoding H*) so that the subsequent density-adaptive k*-NN network is built on a bounded, probability-simplex-aware metric rather than Euclidean distance in gene space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Compute pairwise square-root Jensen-Shannon distances between cells in ACTIONet's reduced archetypal metric space (the normalized multilevel encoding H*) so that the subsequent density-adaptive k*-NN network is built on a bounded, probability-simplex-aware metric rather than Euclidean distance in gene space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or only library-size-normalized gene expression (not the reduced H* archetype-weight space) — distances should be computed after an.pp.reduce_kernel, not directly on counts The goal is a fixed-k nearest-neighbor graph (e.g. standard scanpy neighbors) rather than ACTIONet's density-adaptive k*-NN multiresolution network Cell representations are not nonnegative mixture weights over archetypes, since Jensen-Shannon divergence presumes probability-like distributions

skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-divergence-benchmarking Use when transferring continuous annotations (e.g. 7-dimensional cell fate probabilities) between batches or datasets and you need a distribution-level metric to rank annotation-transfer methods. The annotation to transfer is a discrete cell-type label rather than a continuous probability distribution — label-accuracy metrics would be more appropriate The query and reference datasets have fewer than ~1000 cells, since the DIRECTi model may suffer under-training issues http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark annotation-transfer methods by measuring Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD) between transferred and reference cell fate probability distributions, as done to compare Cell BLAST against scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchor-based mapping, and scANVI on the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmark annotation-transfer methods by measuring Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD) between transferred and reference cell fate probability distributions, as done to compare Cell BLAST against scmap, CellFishing.jl, CCA anchor-based mapping, and scANVI on the Tusi hematopoietic progenitor dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation to transfer is a discrete cell-type label rather than a continuous probability distribution — label-accuracy metrics would be more appropriate The query and reference datasets have fewer than ~1000 cells, since the DIRECTi model may suffer under-training issues

skills.description: Use when you have deconvolution-predicted cell-type proportions (e.g., from CIBERSORT nu-SVR runs) and known true proportions for pseudo-bulk mixtures, and need a single distributional metric to rank marker sets.
skills.name: jensen-shannon-divergence-proportion-evaluation
skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-divergence-proportion-evaluation Use when you have deconvolution-predicted cell-type proportions (e.g., from CIBERSORT nu-SVR runs) and known true proportions for pseudo-bulk mixtures, and need a single distributional metric to rank marker sets. You lack ground-truth cell-type proportions for the mixtures — JS comparison against true proportions is impossible and a different validation strategy is needed You need to select markers rather than evaluate an already-selected marker set — use the phenotype cover / G-PC selection skill instead Predictions are continuous labels or class scores rather than compositional proportion vectors — JS divergence over cell-type fractions is the wrong metric http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates deconvolution-derived cell-type proportion estimates against known ground-truth proportions by computing the Jensen-Shannon divergence per pseudo-bulk mixture and averaging per marker-selection method, as done for CIBERSORT runs on IPF, MC, and HCA scRNA-seq pseudo-bulk mixtures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Evaluates deconvolution-derived cell-type proportion estimates against known ground-truth proportions by computing the Jensen-Shannon divergence per pseudo-bulk mixture and averaging per marker-selection method, as done for CIBERSORT runs on IPF, MC, and HCA scRNA-seq pseudo-bulk mixtures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack ground-truth cell-type proportions for the mixtures — JS comparison against true proportions is impossible and a different validation strategy is needed You need to select markers rather than evaluate an already-selected marker set — use the phenotype cover / G-PC selection skill instead Predictions are continuous labels or class scores rather than compositional proportion vectors — JS divergence over cell-type fractions is the wrong metric

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a cell-similarity measure captures same-type cell similarity more strongly than a baseline such as HVG+PCA Euclidean distance, with permutation-labeled null models on PBMC data.
skills.name: jensen-shannon-divergence-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-divergence-similarity-scoring Use when benchmarking whether a cell-similarity measure captures same-type cell similarity more strongly than a baseline such as HVG+PCA Euclidean distance, with permutation-labeled null models on PBMC data. You only need a single-cell embedding or visualization rather than a quantitative similarity benchmark against a permutation null The dataset lacks a marker panel or reliable cell-type labels, so same-type groupings needed for intra-type similarity scoring cannot be defined Cells are already represented by archetype weights or a precomputed metric space and no comparative baseline evaluation is requested http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Scores intra-cell-type similarity using ACTIONet's Jensen-Shannon-divergence-based cell distances in the archetypal metric cell space, and validates them against a permutation null, demonstrating a larger deviation from random expectation than Seurat-style HVG+PCA Euclidean distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Scores intra-cell-type similarity using ACTIONet's Jensen-Shannon-divergence-based cell distances in the archetypal metric cell space, and validates them against a permutation null, demonstrating a larger deviation from random expectation than Seurat-style HVG+PCA Euclidean distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single-cell embedding or visualization rather than a quantitative similarity benchmark against a permutation null The dataset lacks a marker panel or reliable cell-type labels, so same-type groupings needed for intra-type similarity scoring cannot be defined Cells are already represented by archetype weights or a precomputed metric space and no comparative baseline evaluation is requested

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a spatial reconstruction method for single-cell data: a predicted neighbor structure exists for query cells with known truth locations, and you need a local, neighborhood-composition quality metric beyond raw neighbor hits.
skills.name: jensen-shannon-neighborhood-divergence-analysis
skills.search_text: jensen-shannon-neighborhood-divergence-analysis Use when benchmarking a spatial reconstruction method for single-cell data: a predicted neighbor structure exists for query cells with known truth locations, and you need a local, neighborhood-composition quality metric beyond raw neighbor hits. You lack cell-type annotations for the query cells, so neighborhood cell-type distributions cannot be formed. You only need global reconstruction fidelity — Spearman's rank correlation of global distances is the appropriate metric, not neighborhood JSD. The test data has no truth locations, so no reference neighborhood composition exists to compare against. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluation skill that scores spatial reconstruction quality by comparing cell-type composition of k-nearest-neighborhoods between predicted and true spatial layouts using Jensen-Shannon distance, as implemented in CellContrast's eval module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Evaluation skill that scores spatial reconstruction quality by comparing cell-type composition of k-nearest-neighborhoods between predicted and true spatial layouts using Jensen-Shannon distance, as implemented in CellContrast's eval module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack cell-type annotations for the query cells, so neighborhood cell-type distributions cannot be formed. You only need global reconstruction fidelity — Spearman's rank correlation of global distances is the appropriate metric, not neighborhood JSD. The test data has no truth locations, so no reference neighborhood composition exists to compare against.

skills.description: Use when multi-source or multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices need batch-effect correction with preservation of cell-type signal, or when benchmarking JIVE against Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, and ComBat-seq under balanced versus unbalanced batch conditions.
skills.name: jive-joint-individual-variation-decomposition-scrna
skills.search_text: jive-joint-individual-variation-decomposition-scrna Use when multi-source or multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices need batch-effect correction with preservation of cell-type signal, or when benchmarking JIVE against Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, and ComBat-seq under balanced versus unbalanced batch conditions. Data is a single batch/source with no multi-source structure to decompose — the joint/individual decomposition has no batch effect to correct The analysis targets bulk multi-omics integration where original r.jive is appropriate; the article notes original JIVE 'is computationally infeasible for large-scale single-cell sequencing datasets' without the scJIVE enhancements http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply scJIVE (enhanced JIVE for single-cell data) to decompose multi-source scRNA-seq datasets into a joint structure capturing shared biological variability and individual structures capturing batch-level technical variability, and benchmark the corrected embeddings against Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, and ComBat-seq using PVCA, kBET, ASW, and LISI metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Apply scJIVE (enhanced JIVE for single-cell data) to decompose multi-source scRNA-seq datasets into a joint structure capturing shared biological variability and individual structures capturing batch-level technical variability, and benchmark the corrected embeddings against Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, and ComBat-seq using PVCA, kBET, ASW, and LISI metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is a single batch/source with no multi-source structure to decompose — the joint/individual decomposition has no batch effect to correct The analysis targets bulk multi-omics integration where original r.jive is appropriate; the article notes original JIVE 'is computationally infeasible for large-scale single-cell sequencing datasets' without the scJIVE enhancements

skills.description: Use when you have two or more data matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq batches, or matched gene expression/methylation/miRNA sources like BRCA TCGA data) sharing samples/cells and need to separate shared signal from batch-specific variation.
skills.name: jive-multi-source-decomposition
skills.search_text: jive-multi-source-decomposition Use when you have two or more data matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq batches, or matched gene expression/methylation/miRNA sources like BRCA TCGA data) sharing samples/cells and need to separate shared signal from batch-specific variation. When the data are a single matrix with no multi-source/multi-batch structure — there is no joint-vs-individual decomposition to estimate When the goal is a benchmarked batch-correction comparison against methods like Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, or ComBat-seq on metrics such as kBET, ASW, and LISI — JIVE is one candidate but the skill alone does not cover those comparators' workflows For very large scRNA-seq datasets when restricted to the original r.jive implementation, which was designed for bulk sequencing data and is computationally infeasible at single-cell scale — use the enhanced scJIVE implementation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Decompose multi-source (multi-batch or multi-omics) matrices into a joint structure capturing shared biological variability plus per-source individual structures capturing technical/batch variation, using the JIVE method via the scJIVE R implementation for computationally efficient application to large single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Decompose multi-source (multi-batch or multi-omics) matrices into a joint structure capturing shared biological variability plus per-source individual structures capturing technical/batch variation, using the JIVE method via the scJIVE R implementation for computationally efficient application to large single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data are a single matrix with no multi-source/multi-batch structure — there is no joint-vs-individual decomposition to estimate When the goal is a benchmarked batch-correction comparison against methods like Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, or ComBat-seq on metrics such as kBET, ASW, and LISI — JIVE is one candidate but the skill alone does not cover those comparators' workflows For very large scRNA-seq datasets when restricted to the original r.jive implementation, which was designed for bulk sequencing data and is computationally infeasible at single-cell scale — use the enhanced scJIVE implementation instead

skills.description: Use when you have multiple matched data matrices (e.g. BRCA gene expression, methylation, miRNA) and must decide the joint rank and per-source individual ranks before interpreting a JIVE decomposition.
skills.name: jive-multi-source-rank-selection
skills.search_text: jive-multi-source-rank-selection Use when you have multiple matched data matrices (e.g. BRCA gene expression, methylation, miRNA) and must decide the joint rank and per-source individual ranks before interpreting a JIVE decomposition. Data are large-scale single-cell scRNA-seq batches — the original r.jive implementation was designed for bulk sequencing data and is computationally infeasible there; use scJIVE instead Runtime and peak memory are tightly constrained and a Python AJIVE (mvdr) implementation is acceptable — AJIVE fitted the same scenario in ~18 s / 601 MB vs ~2 h / 1180 MB for jive() Data sources are not matched across samples/rows, since JIVE requires jointly decomposable multi-source matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the joint and individual ranks for a JIVE decomposition of multi-source data using r.jive's two built-in approaches: a permutation-based test (jive.perm) described by Lock et al. and a BIC-motivated criterion (bic.jive). Correct rank selection is what determines how much variation is attributed to shared vs. batch-specific structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Selects the joint and individual ranks for a JIVE decomposition of multi-source data using r.jive's two built-in approaches: a permutation-based test (jive.perm) described by Lock et al. and a BIC-motivated criterion (bic.jive). Correct rank selection is what determines how much variation is attributed to shared vs. batch-specific structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are large-scale single-cell scRNA-seq batches — the original r.jive implementation was designed for bulk sequencing data and is computationally infeasible there; use scJIVE instead Runtime and peak memory are tightly constrained and a Python AJIVE (mvdr) implementation is acceptable — AJIVE fitted the same scenario in ~18 s / 601 MB vs ~2 h / 1180 MB for jive() Data sources are not matched across samples/rows, since JIVE requires jointly decomposable multi-source matrices

skills.description: Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell dataset needs marker trajectories expressed on a real time or spatial scale, and a prior cell-density distribution on that true scale is available.
skills.name: joint-density-change-of-variables
skills.search_text: joint-density-change-of-variables Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell dataset needs marker trajectories expressed on a real time or spatial scale, and a prior cell-density distribution on that true scale is available. No prior knowledge of the real-scale cell-density distribution is available (e.g. stem cell differentiation, where the paper notes constructing a target distribution is challenging) Sources and sinks such as cell death or cell division rates along the process are unknown, since these are critical for obtaining the correct real-time distribution The pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is unreliable, as MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 MAPiT applies a measure-preserving nonlinear change of variables (transformation tau from preMAPiT.m) to the joint density p_s(s,y) computed on the pseudotime scale, yielding p_x(x,y) on the real temporal or spatial scale so that conditional marker profiles p_x(y|x) can be recovered from snapshot single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: MAPiT applies a measure-preserving nonlinear change of variables (transformation tau from preMAPiT.m) to the joint density p_s(s,y) computed on the pseudotime scale, yielding p_x(x,y) on the real temporal or spatial scale so that conditional marker profiles p_x(y|x) can be recovered from snapshot single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior knowledge of the real-scale cell-density distribution is available (e.g. stem cell differentiation, where the paper notes constructing a target distribution is challenging) Sources and sinks such as cell death or cell division rates along the process are unknown, since these are critical for obtaining the correct real-time distribution The pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is unreliable, as MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order

skills.description: Use when a hashed PBMC-style CITE-seq dataset has passed GEX QC and cellranger/CITE-Seq preprocessing, and you need joint gene-plus-antibody clustering, UMAP embeddings per modality, and antibody-positive cell calls.
skills.name: joint-gene-antibody-clustering
skills.search_text: joint-gene-antibody-clustering Use when a hashed PBMC-style CITE-seq dataset has passed GEX QC and cellranger/CITE-Seq preprocessing, and you need joint gene-plus-antibody clustering, UMAP embeddings per modality, and antibody-positive cell calls. The dataset contains only gene expression (no ADT/CITE-seq library), so no antibody modality exists to combine for joint clustering The goal is hashing deconvolution or upstream cellranger count / FASTQ processing rather than the CITE-seq analysis layer's clustering and positive-cell calling The ADT data has not been filtered to GEX-QC-retained cells, so joint analysis would mix mismatched cell sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CITE-seq analysis step of the gExcite Snakemake workflow that computes UMAP embeddings from gene expression, antibody (ADT) expression, or both modalities combined, and runs joint gene-plus-antibody (BremSC) clustering to assess cell similarity across data types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: CITE-seq analysis step of the gExcite Snakemake workflow that computes UMAP embeddings from gene expression, antibody (ADT) expression, or both modalities combined, and runs joint gene-plus-antibody (BremSC) clustering to assess cell similarity across data types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains only gene expression (no ADT/CITE-seq library), so no antibody modality exists to combine for joint clustering The goal is hashing deconvolution or upstream cellranger count / FASTQ processing rather than the CITE-seq analysis layer's clustering and positive-cell calling The ADT data has not been filtered to GEX-QC-retained cells, so joint analysis would mix mismatched cell sets

skills.description: Use when per-slide clustering of spatial transcriptomics data hides a global migratory/regenerative subpopulation behind local spatial neighborhoods, and you need clusters comparable across multiple APAP-injury slides (GSE223561).
skills.name: joint-leiden-clustering-across-spatial-slides
skills.search_text: joint-leiden-clustering-across-spatial-slides Use when per-slide clustering of spatial transcriptomics data hides a global migratory/regenerative subpopulation behind local spatial neighborhoods, and you need clusters comparable across multiple APAP-injury slides (GSE223561). The analysis goal is to study local spatial niches or zonation patterns themselves — filtering the spatial-coordinate signal with SiFT removes exactly the signal of interest in that case. The slides have not been SiFT-filtered with a spatial-coordinate kernel and you are clustering raw per-slide data: cluster identities will then reflect local neighborhoods and batch effects and will not be comparable across slides. There is no prior spatial or coordinate information available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — SiFT 'strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell–cell similarity kernel' and an inaccurate kernel can cause signal loss. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Joint Leiden clustering of SiFT-filtered APAP-injury spatial transcriptomics slides: the per-slide SiFT-filtered AnnData objects (filtered with a KnnKernel over spatial coordinates) are concatenated, embedded via PCA plus a neighbor graph, and Leiden-clustered across samples so that clusters correspond to global subpopulations (e.g., the ANXA2+ migratory hepatocytes) rather than slide-local spatial niches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Joint Leiden clustering of SiFT-filtered APAP-injury spatial transcriptomics slides: the per-slide SiFT-filtered AnnData objects (filtered with a KnnKernel over spatial coordinates) are concatenated, embedded via PCA plus a neighbor graph, and Leiden-clustered across samples so that clusters correspond to global subpopulations (e.g., the ANXA2+ migratory hepatocytes) rather than slide-local spatial niches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is to study local spatial niches or zonation patterns themselves — filtering the spatial-coordinate signal with SiFT removes exactly the signal of interest in that case. The slides have not been SiFT-filtered with a spatial-coordinate kernel and you are clustering raw per-slide data: cluster identities will then reflect local neighborhoods and batch effects and will not be comparable across slides. There is no prior spatial or coordinate information available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — SiFT 'strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell–cell similarity kernel' and an inaccurate kernel can cause signal loss.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending scGAE: a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq must simultaneously reconstruct the expression count matrix and the KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix in a single multitask loss.
skills.name: joint-reconstruction-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: joint-reconstruction-loss-implementation Use when reproducing or extending scGAE: a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq must simultaneously reconstruct the expression count matrix and the KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix in a single multitask loss. The model must output a direct 2D embedding — scGAE embeds to an intermediate dimension and relies on tSNE for 2D visualization because 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder' Only feature reconstruction is needed (e.g. plain denoising autoencoders like DCA) — the joint loss adds the topology term L_A, which is only meaningful when a cell-graph adjacency matrix is supplied No cell–cell graph can be constructed (e.g. spatially unstructured data without a meaningful neighborhood definition) — the adjacency-based decoder has no input to reconstruct http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implement scGAE's joint reconstruction objective L = L_X + lambda·L_A (lambda = 0.6), which combines a feature decoder that reconstructs the count matrix with a graph decoder that reconstructs the cell–cell adjacency from the latent embedding Z, so the model preserves both feature and topological structure information in scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Implement scGAE's joint reconstruction objective L = L_X + lambda·L_A (lambda = 0.6), which combines a feature decoder that reconstructs the count matrix with a graph decoder that reconstructs the cell–cell adjacency from the latent embedding Z, so the model preserves both feature and topological structure information in scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model must output a direct 2D embedding — scGAE embeds to an intermediate dimension and relies on tSNE for 2D visualization because 'the complex data structure is hard to be directly embedded into two-dimensional space by graph autoencoder' Only feature reconstruction is needed (e.g. plain denoising autoencoders like DCA) — the joint loss adds the topology term L_A, which is only meaningful when a cell-graph adjacency matrix is supplied No cell–cell graph can be constructed (e.g. spatially unstructured data without a meaningful neighborhood definition) — the adjacency-based decoder has no input to reconstruct

skills.description: Use when dose-finding trial data contain per-dose bivariate toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) and monotone-constrained joint response probability estimates are needed to feed a utility-based OBD selection.
skills.name: joint-toxicity-efficacy-probability-derivation
skills.search_text: joint-toxicity-efficacy-probability-derivation Use when dose-finding trial data contain per-dose bivariate toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) and monotone-constrained joint response probability estimates are needed to feed a utility-based OBD selection. The response outcome requires long follow-up time to be assessed — the TSNP design cannot be applied directly in this case The response outcome is not binary and observable shortly after treatment initiation The trial is a drug-combination study — extending TSNP to identify the optimal dose combination is future work, not yet done http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Derives closed-form nonparametric estimates of the joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_j00, π_j01, π_j10, π_j11) at each dose in the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on the isotonic (PAVA) DLT rate estimate — no MCMC or numerical optimization required. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Derives closed-form nonparametric estimates of the joint toxicity-efficacy response probabilities (π_j00, π_j01, π_j10, π_j11) at each dose in the TSNP phase I/II design, by conditioning the likelihood on the isotonic (PAVA) DLT rate estimate — no MCMC or numerical optimization required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up time to be assessed — the TSNP design cannot be applied directly in this case The response outcome is not binary and observable shortly after treatment initiation The trial is a drug-combination study — extending TSNP to identify the optimal dose combination is future work, not yet done

skills.description: Use when you have CoupledNMF H matrices (cnmf.output$H1, cnmf.output$H2) from a paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq run and need a joint embedding plot to check cluster coherence and cross-modality integration.
skills.name: joint-tsne-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: joint-tsne-embedding-visualization Use when you have CoupledNMF H matrices (cnmf.output$H1, cnmf.output$H2) from a paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq run and need a joint embedding plot to check cluster coherence and cross-modality integration. skills.search_text: k-means-cell-clustering Use when you need to quantify whether an imputation method (e.g. scISR vs MAGIC, scImpute, SAVER, scScope, scGNN or raw data) improved cell-type clustering of an scRNA-seq dataset with known cell-type labels, measured by ARI. The number of true cell types k is unknown — the benchmark protocol requires k to be set to the true number of cell types, so an unsupervised k must be estimated by other means The goal is to evaluate imputation itself on dropout-free or labeled-truth-free data — k-means/ARI validation needs ground-truth cell labels and is meaningless for purely exploratory clustering Evaluating raw (unimputed) data as the final answer — the article shows raw-data ARI is systematically lower (e.g. Goolam 0.533 raw vs 0.641 scISR), so clustering raw data without an imputed comparison understates the achievable quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices with k-means (k set to the true number of cell types) on 50-component PCA embeddings to benchmark imputation quality via Adjusted Rand Index against known cell labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Clusters single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices with k-means (k set to the true number of cell types) on 50-component PCA embeddings to benchmark imputation quality via Adjusted Rand Index against known cell labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of true cell types k is unknown — the benchmark protocol requires k to be set to the true number of cell types, so an unsupervised k must be estimated by other means The goal is to evaluate imputation itself on dropout-free or labeled-truth-free data — k-means/ARI validation needs ground-truth cell labels and is meaningless for purely exploratory clustering Evaluating raw (unimputed) data as the final answer — the article shows raw-data ARI is systematically lower (e.g. Goolam 0.533 raw vs 0.641 scISR), so clustering raw data without an imputed comparison understates the achievable quality

skills.search_text: k-means-clustering-of-scrna-data Use when simulating artificial doublets from quality singlets after an overkill/filter step, and cells must be grouped so sampled pairs come from transcriptionally similar cells to make realistic training doublets. The input is raw droplet data that has not yet passed Chord's overkill step — clustering should be run on the prefiltered/remaining quality singlet data, not before doublet filtering. The goal is biological cell-type annotation rather than simulating doublet training profiles — k=20 here is a simulation-granularity parameter, not a cell-type resolution choice. The data are not cell-level expression profiles (e.g. already a feature table or aggregated counts), since within-cluster cell-pair averaging of expression profiles is the core operation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Partition cells of a prefiltered Seurat object into k-means clusters (k=20) on a PC1-30 embedding so that artificial doublets can be simulated from within-cluster cell-pair averages when building Chord's GBM training set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Partition cells of a prefiltered Seurat object into k-means clusters (k=20) on a PC1-30 embedding so that artificial doublets can be simulated from within-cluster cell-pair averages when building Chord's GBM training set.
