skills.description: Use when training miRSCAPE on paired bulk miRNA–mRNA matrices spanning thousands of tumor and normal samples and you need a compact, representative training set (k-means medoids) before xgboost model fitting.
skills.name: k-means-medoid-sample-selection
skills.search_text: k-means-medoid-sample-selection Use when training miRSCAPE on paired bulk miRNA–mRNA matrices spanning thousands of tumor and normal samples and you need a compact, representative training set (k-means medoids) before xgboost model fitting. The training cohort is already small (e.g. the pdac_mirna/pdac_mrna example data) — medoid subsampling is meant for ~10,000-sample compendia and would discard data unnecessarily The application scRNA-seq context differs strongly from the training tissues — miRSCAPE accuracy drops when training and application contexts do not match, so a medoid-selected multi-tissue model may not be the right training set You need per-sample (not pooled) predictions and cannot afford any loss of cohort granularity from collapsing clusters to medoids http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Reduces a large paired bulk miRNA–mRNA training compendium (e.g. ~10,000 TCGA/GTEx/CCLE tumor and normal samples across 10 tissues) to ~1,000 representative samples chosen as k-means medoids, so the miRSCAPE xgboost model can be trained efficiently without losing cohort diversity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Reduces a large paired bulk miRNA–mRNA training compendium (e.g. ~10,000 TCGA/GTEx/CCLE tumor and normal samples across 10 tissues) to ~1,000 representative samples chosen as k-means medoids, so the miRSCAPE xgboost model can be trained efficiently without losing cohort diversity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The training cohort is already small (e.g. the pdac_mirna/pdac_mrna example data) — medoid subsampling is meant for ~10,000-sample compendia and would discard data unnecessarily The application scRNA-seq context differs strongly from the training tissues — miRSCAPE accuracy drops when training and application contexts do not match, so a medoid-selected multi-tissue model may not be the right training set You need per-sample (not pooled) predictions and cannot afford any loss of cohort granularity from collapsing clusters to medoids

skills.search_text: k-medoids-clustering-generation Use when building tree-shaped trajectory inference from single-cell data and you need many alternative clusterings (rather than one) to explore topologies, e.g. linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating trajectories in a SingleCellExperiment object. skills.summary: Generate a large ensemble of k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings over a range of k values on a low-dimensional single-cell embedding, so that many candidate clusterings exist for topology estimation and cell-connectivity-based trajectory selection with Totem.

Input embedding is a high-dimensional PCA representation (e.g. 30 principal components) where k-medoids produces degenerate 1–2 cell clusters.

skills.search_text: k-medoids-clustering-of-pathway-curves Use when a set of coordinated pathways has per-cell PAL scores along a trajectory (pseudotime) and you want to discover shared stage-activity patterns, e.g. developmental stage-specific pathway modules. Gene sets have not passed the coordination test (compute.kld adjusted p >= 0.05) — noise curves would dominate clusters Data is not ordered along a trajectory (no pseudotime), e.g. dissociated static samples — curve fitting is meaningless without an ordering Spatial transcriptomics data where the goal is spatial relevance testing (compute.spatial.kld) rather than trajectory-stage patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Groups fitted pathway activity level (PAL) curves along pseudotime into stage-pattern clusters using k-medoids (pam), as done to organize 97 KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways active across E17.5 mouse cortex development into 8 clusters in the GSDensity mouse brain development analysis (Fig. 4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Groups fitted pathway activity level (PAL) curves along pseudotime into stage-pattern clusters using k-medoids (pam), as done to organize 97 KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways active across E17.5 mouse cortex development into 8 clusters in the GSDensity mouse brain development analysis (Fig. 4).

skills.description: Use when comparing normalization strategies (e.g., dsb vs CLR) on protein-only ADT data via clustering coherence, or when selecting the number of protein-defined clusters in a PBMC CITE-seq matrix.
skills.name: k-medoids-clustering-with-gap-statistic
skills.search_text: k-medoids-clustering-with-gap-statistic Use when comparing normalization strategies (e.g., dsb vs CLR) on protein-only ADT data via clustering coherence, or when selecting the number of protein-defined clusters in a PBMC CITE-seq matrix. Input is raw ADT UMI counts without prior normalization — clustering coherence would reflect noise rather than normalization quality (low-signal proteins with max UMI < 5 must first be removed and data dsb/CLR normalized). The goal is joint mRNA+protein clustering (WNN) — this skill deliberately clusters on protein expression data alone; multimodal WNN analysis combining 30 mRNA PCs is a different workflow. Datasets without empty-droplet background or isotype controls — dsb normalization prerequisites may be missing, invalidating the dsb-vs-CLR comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies k-medoids clustering to normalized ADT (protein) matrices from CITE-seq data for k = 1..20 and computes the Gap-Statistic — a measure of within-cluster coherence — to compare how well normalization methods (dsb vs CLR) unmask biologically meaningful cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Applies k-medoids clustering to normalized ADT (protein) matrices from CITE-seq data for k = 1..20 and computes the Gap-Statistic — a measure of within-cluster coherence — to compare how well normalization methods (dsb vs CLR) unmask biologically meaningful cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ADT UMI counts without prior normalization — clustering coherence would reflect noise rather than normalization quality (low-signal proteins with max UMI < 5 must first be removed and data dsb/CLR normalized). The goal is joint mRNA+protein clustering (WNN) — this skill deliberately clusters on protein expression data alone; multimodal WNN analysis combining 30 mRNA PCs is a different workflow. Datasets without empty-droplet background or isotype controls — dsb normalization prerequisites may be missing, invalidating the dsb-vs-CLR comparison.

A complete, high-quality reference genome is available and gene-expression feature matrices are already suitable for the classifier The input is already a cell feature table (e.g., precomputed CKG or gene-expression matrix) — skip directly to the classification module http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates compressed k-mer group (CKG) features for scRNA-seq cells by selecting informative k-mers and simhashing k-mer vectors into fingerprints, producing a CKG look-up table that transforms raw-read k-mer abundances into reference-free cell features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102855

skills.description: Use when implementing hierarchical clustering with an arbitrary linkage function (e.g., KMD linkage), where naive agglomerative recomputation is impractical and you need linear-time linkage updates and k-independent memory.
skills.name: k-minimal-distance-cluster-pair-tracking
skills.search_text: k-minimal-distance-cluster-pair-tracking Use when implementing hierarchical clustering with an arbitrary linkage function (e.g., KMD linkage), where naive agglomerative recomputation is impractical and you need linear-time linkage updates and k-independent memory. When a standard linkage (single, average, complete, Ward) suffices — those run directly via SciPy's cluster.hierarchy.linkage and KMD's k-list bookkeeping only adds overhead When n is in the millions: the O(n^2) memory implementation is infeasible; the paper's sampling-based extension is the appropriate route instead When you only need cluster labels rather than the full dendrogram and cannot afford KMD's inherently slower per-run cost of maintaining k-distance lists for each cluster pair http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Efficiently implements KMD (k-minimal distances) linkage for agglomerative hierarchical clustering by maintaining, for each pair of clusters, a heap of the k smallest inter-cluster distances, merging sorted distance lists in O(k) per pair to achieve O(nk) linkage updates with O(n^2) memory independent of k. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Efficiently implements KMD (k-minimal distances) linkage for agglomerative hierarchical clustering by maintaining, for each pair of clusters, a heap of the k smallest inter-cluster distances, merging sorted distance lists in O(k) per pair to achieve O(nk) linkage updates with O(n^2) memory independent of k.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a standard linkage (single, average, complete, Ward) suffices — those run directly via SciPy's cluster.hierarchy.linkage and KMD's k-list bookkeeping only adds overhead When n is in the millions: the O(n^2) memory implementation is infeasible; the paper's sampling-based extension is the appropriate route instead When you only need cluster labels rather than the full dendrogram and cannot afford KMD's inherently slower per-run cost of maintaining k-distance lists for each cluster pair

skills.description: Use when clustering with KMDHierarchicalClustering and k is unknown: fit across a k_scan_range, compute KMD silhouette per k, and verify the silhouette is predictive of accuracy/NMI/ARI against ground-truth labels.
skills.name: k-scan-silhouette-evaluation
skills.search_text: k-scan-silhouette-evaluation Use when clustering with KMDHierarchicalClustering and k is unknown: fit across a k_scan_range, compute KMD silhouette per k, and verify the silhouette is predictive of accuracy/NMI/ARI against ground-truth labels. skills.search_text: kallisto-transcriptome-index-construction Use when building a kallisto index for scRNA-seq that must distinguish spliced (cDNA) from intronic (unspliced) reads — e.g., before running scKB to emit spliced and unspliced count matrices for COPILOT or RNA velocity analysis. skills.summary: Builds a combined cDNA+intron kallisto pseudoalignment index (cDNA_introns_10xv3.idx) from the TAIR10 GTF and the TAIR9 BSgenome sequence via BUSpaRse::get_velocity_files, so scKB/kallisto can split scRNA-seq reads into spliced and unspliced count matrices.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from unsynchronized cells needs a denoised, phase-resolved (G1/S/G2/M) expression time-series along a TSP-recovered cell-cycle order, e.g., to surface cycle genes missing from curated bases like Cyclebase.
skills.name: kalman-smoothing-pseudotime-expression
skills.search_text: kalman-smoothing-pseudotime-expression Use when scRNA-seq data from unsynchronized cells needs a denoised, phase-resolved (G1/S/G2/M) expression time-series along a TSP-recovered cell-cycle order, e.g., to surface cycle genes missing from curated bases like Cyclebase. Cells are chemically synchronized, since reCAT is designed to recover the cycle without synchronization-induced perturbation The expression matrix has not been preprocessed to log2(TPM+1) and filtered to the cell-cycle base genes expected by get_test_exp The goal is to model multiple processes (e.g., differentiation alongside cell cycle) simultaneously — reCAT separates cell cycle analysis from differentiation and may introduce bias http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply reCAT's HMM-based segmentation plus Kalman smoother to estimate smoothed gene-expression profiles along a recovered cell-cycle pseudo time-series from unsynchronized single-cell RNA-seq data, enabling downstream ranking of candidate cell-cycle-regulated genes (e.g., Ncapd2) by dCor and KNN-MI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z

skills.search_text: kaplan-meier-cohort-survival-estimation Use when DeepCC subtype labels exist for validation cohorts (TANSBIG, UNT, UPP, NKI) with clinical metadata containing disease-free survival outcomes, and you need to show the classification has prognostic value. You want to discover patient groups by clustering — DeepCC is a supervised classifier, not a clustering method ('not clustering of cancer patients'). The cohorts lack time-to-event or censoring information, so KM estimation and log-rank tests are impossible. skills.search_text: kaplan-meier-survival-estimation Use when a per-sample continuous score (e.g., ssGSEA enrichment of a gene signature in TCGA bulk RNA-seq) must be validated as a prognostic indicator against patient overall-survival metadata. Cancer-Finder is not recommended for hematologic tumor data, so signature/score derivation from such datasets should not feed this survival workflow Input lacks per-patient survival time/event metadata or the sample set is too small for a two-group median-split comparison The goal is classifying malignant cells rather than validating a score's prognostic association (use Cancer-Finder/CopyKAT-style annotation instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of a continuous molecular score (here the 10-gene ccRCC signature ssGSEA score) split at the median into high/low groups, tested with a two-sided log-rank test, to establish prognostic significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of a continuous molecular score (here the 10-gene ccRCC signature ssGSEA score) split at the median into high/low groups, tested with a two-sided log-rank test, to establish prognostic significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cancer-Finder is not recommended for hematologic tumor data, so signature/score derivation from such datasets should not feed this survival workflow Input lacks per-patient survival time/event metadata or the sample set is too small for a two-group median-split comparison The goal is classifying malignant cells rather than validating a score's prognostic association (use Cancer-Finder/CopyKAT-style annotation instead)

skills.description: Use when a per-patient prognostic risk score (e.g., TimiRS from LASSO Cox-selected marker pairs) must be validated by showing overall survival separation between high- and low-risk groups in one or more cohorts with survival endpoints.
skills.name: kaplan-meier-survival-stratification
skills.search_text: kaplan-meier-survival-stratification Use when a per-patient prognostic risk score (e.g., TimiRS from LASSO Cox-selected marker pairs) must be validated by showing overall survival separation between high- and low-risk groups in one or more cohorts with survival endpoints. Clinical data lack reliable event and time-to-event information (TimiCheckEvent filters out low-quality survival info, so stratification would be unpowered) The goal is response prediction to immunotherapy rather than overall-survival stratification from bulk transcriptomics plus survival data Cohorts are too small for adequate log-rank power — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to identify prognostic pairs effectively http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Stratifies patients into high- and low-risk groups (median split of a risk score such as TimiRS) per cohort and assesses survival separation with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests, used in TimiGP to validate that inferred cell-cell interactions carry prognostic signal across independent melanoma cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Stratifies patients into high- and low-risk groups (median split of a risk score such as TimiRS) per cohort and assesses survival separation with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests, used in TimiGP to validate that inferred cell-cell interactions carry prognostic signal across independent melanoma cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clinical data lack reliable event and time-to-event information (TimiCheckEvent filters out low-quality survival info, so stratification would be unpowered) The goal is response prediction to immunotherapy rather than overall-survival stratification from bulk transcriptomics plus survival data Cohorts are too small for adequate log-rank power — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to identify prognostic pairs effectively

skills.description: Use when preprocessing single-cell RNA-seq FASTQs with kallisto|bustools (kb-python/cellatlas) and a seqspec spec.yaml is available but the kb technology/chemistry string is unknown or must be reproduced programmatically.
skills.name: kb-technology-string-generation
skills.search_text: kb-technology-string-generation Use when preprocessing single-cell RNA-seq FASTQs with kallisto|bustools (kb-python/cellatlas) and a seqspec spec.yaml is available but the kb technology/chemistry string is unknown or must be reproduced programmatically. The input is not a seqspec YAML specification (e.g. only raw FASTQs with no assay annotation) — seqspec index has no library structure to index The target tool is not kallisto|bustools-compatible preprocessing (e.g. building an mx matrix QC workflow on an existing count matrix) — use mx subcommands instead The assay modality requested (e.g. rna) is not present or not annotated with barcode/UMI/cDNA regions in the spec http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generates the kallisto|bustools technology string from a seqspec YAML assay specification using `seqspec index`, so preprocessing tools like kb-python/cellatlas know where barcode, UMI, and cDNA regions sit in each FASTQ read. It removes the need for hand-written, assay-specific chemistry strings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae168
skills.summary: Generates the kallisto|bustools technology string from a seqspec YAML assay specification using `seqspec index`, so preprocessing tools like kb-python/cellatlas know where barcode, UMI, and cDNA regions sit in each FASTQ read. It removes the need for hand-written, assay-specific chemistry strings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a seqspec YAML specification (e.g. only raw FASTQs with no assay annotation) — seqspec index has no library structure to index The target tool is not kallisto|bustools-compatible preprocessing (e.g. building an mx matrix QC workflow on an existing count matrix) — use mx subcommands instead The assay modality requested (e.g. rna) is not present or not annotated with barcode/UMI/cDNA regions in the spec

skills.description: Use when comparing how well cell embeddings (e.g., tGPT mean-pooled hidden states) mix cells across donor/batch labels against batch-corrected baselines, or when verifying that a representation is insensitive to batch effect on a multi-donor dataset.
skills.name: kbet-acceptance-rate-computation
skills.search_text: kbet-acceptance-rate-computation Use when comparing how well cell embeddings (e.g., tGPT mean-pooled hidden states) mix cells across donor/batch labels against batch-corrected baselines, or when verifying that a representation is insensitive to batch effect on a multi-donor dataset. The dataset has no batch or donor labels, so kBET cannot define a batch variable to test against You need biological cell-type interpretation rather than batch-mixing assessment — kBET acceptance rewards mixing and can be misleading when cell-type composition genuinely differs across batches Input is already an expression matrix without per-cell gene rankings and you cannot extract tGPT embeddings (the comparison requires embeddings from each method on the same cells) Quantifies batch mixing by computing kBET acceptance rates on cell embeddings, as done to show tGPT's rank-based embeddings reach a kBET acceptance rate of ~0.87 on the HCA bone-marrow dataset, comparable to eleven batch-correction methods (ComBat, MNN, Harmony, Seurat, BBKNN, Scanorama, Pegasus, scVI, scArches, iMAP, DESC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Quantifies batch mixing by computing kBET acceptance rates on cell embeddings, as done to show tGPT's rank-based embeddings reach a kBET acceptance rate of ~0.87 on the HCA bone-marrow dataset, comparable to eleven batch-correction methods (ComBat, MNN, Harmony, Seurat, BBKNN, Scanorama, Pegasus, scVI, scArches, iMAP, DESC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no batch or donor labels, so kBET cannot define a batch variable to test against You need biological cell-type interpretation rather than batch-mixing assessment — kBET acceptance rewards mixing and can be misleading when cell-type composition genuinely differs across batches Input is already an expression matrix without per-cell gene rankings and you cannot extract tGPT embeddings (the comparison requires embeddings from each method on the same cells)

skills.description: Use when integrating public scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. GSE38495 MII-oocyte, GSE45719 E1–E4.0) with low-input bulk RNA-seq and you need to quantify pseudo-bulk vs bulk agreement and batch mixing before downstream communication analysis.
skills.name: kbet-batch-effect-quantification-in-pca-space
skills.search_text: kbet-batch-effect-quantification-in-pca-space Use when integrating public scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. GSE38495 MII-oocyte, GSE45719 E1–E4.0) with low-input bulk RNA-seq and you need to quantify pseudo-bulk vs bulk agreement and batch mixing before downstream communication analysis. Your data have no batch labels or only a single batch — kBET requires multiple batches to test neighborhood mixing. The goal is inferring ligand–receptor cell-cell communication (use TimeTalk, CellChat, or CellPhoneDB), not validating the quality of curated expression profiles. No stage-matched bulk RNA-seq profiles exist — the correlation component cannot be computed and only the kBET batch test applies. http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 A QC validation skill from the TimeTalk workflow: it checks that curated early-embryo scRNA-seq pseudo-bulk profiles agree with stage-matched low-input bulk RNA-seq (Pearson correlation, e.g. 0.91 at the late 2-cell stage) and that batches are well-mixed in PCA space using kBET with a fixed neighborhood size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: A QC validation skill from the TimeTalk workflow: it checks that curated early-embryo scRNA-seq pseudo-bulk profiles agree with stage-matched low-input bulk RNA-seq (Pearson correlation, e.g. 0.91 at the late 2-cell stage) and that batches are well-mixed in PCA space using kBET with a fixed neighborhood size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data have no batch labels or only a single batch — kBET requires multiple batches to test neighborhood mixing. The goal is inferring ligand–receptor cell-cell communication (use TimeTalk, CellChat, or CellPhoneDB), not validating the quality of curated expression profiles. No stage-matched bulk RNA-seq profiles exist — the correlation component cannot be computed and only the kBET batch test applies.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking batch-correction or integration methods on scRNA-seq embeddings and you need a quantitative batch-mixing score (kBET acceptance rate) to accompany cell-type clustering metrics like ARI/NMI/ASW.
skills.name: kbet-batch-mixing-assessment
skills.search_text: kbet-batch-mixing-assessment Use when benchmarking batch-correction or integration methods on scRNA-seq embeddings and you need a quantitative batch-mixing score (kBET acceptance rate) to accompany cell-type clustering metrics like ARI/NMI/ASW. Input has only one batch (no batch_indices variable) — kBET cannot measure mixing without batch labels You only need clustering accuracy and have no batch-effect concern — ARI/NMI alone suffices and kBET adds no signal Evaluating embeddings whose biological structure is unknown — kBET alone rewards over-correction and must be paired with ASW-beta/ARI as in the HP beta-cell-removal test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies batch mixing in single-cell integration embeddings using kBET acceptance rates, so that batch-effect correction (e.g. scETM, Harmony, LIGER, Scanorama) can be benchmarked alongside clustering metrics such as ARI/NMI rather than judged on clustering alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Quantifies batch mixing in single-cell integration embeddings using kBET acceptance rates, so that batch-effect correction (e.g. scETM, Harmony, LIGER, Scanorama) can be benchmarked alongside clustering metrics such as ARI/NMI rather than judged on clustering alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has only one batch (no batch_indices variable) — kBET cannot measure mixing without batch labels You only need clustering accuracy and have no batch-effect concern — ARI/NMI alone suffices and kBET adds no signal Evaluating embeddings whose biological structure is unknown — kBET alone rewards over-correction and must be paired with ASW-beta/ARI as in the HP beta-cell-removal test

skills.description: Use when two gene-by-barcode matrices (e.g., a Chromium reference GBM and a platform-specific GBM) have been integrated and you need quantitative metrics of batch-effect removal and cluster separation.
skills.name: kbet-integration-quality-evaluation
skills.search_text: kbet-integration-quality-evaluation Use when two gene-by-barcode matrices (e.g., a Chromium reference GBM and a platform-specific GBM) have been integrated and you need quantitative metrics of batch-effect removal and cluster separation. When the two GBMs have not yet been harmonised to matching barcodes and genes, since kBET and Silhouette require comparable cell and gene sets When comparing within-platform replicates where no batch effect is expected, making kBET acceptance rates uninformative When the goal is direct GBM agreement (Pearson correlation) or clustering concordance (ARI) rather than integration quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates the quality of single-cell data integration between a reference and a comparison dataset (e.g., Chromium vs SmartSeq2 GBMs integrated with Seurat) by computing kBET batch-effect acceptance rates and Silhouette scores, as done in the UniverSC paper to compare cross-platform processing pipelines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Evaluates the quality of single-cell data integration between a reference and a comparison dataset (e.g., Chromium vs SmartSeq2 GBMs integrated with Seurat) by computing kBET batch-effect acceptance rates and Silhouette scores, as done in the UniverSC paper to compare cross-platform processing pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two GBMs have not yet been harmonised to matching barcodes and genes, since kBET and Silhouette require comparable cell and gene sets When comparing within-platform replicates where no batch effect is expected, making kBET acceptance rates uninformative When the goal is direct GBM agreement (Pearson correlation) or clustering concordance (ARI) rather than integration quality

skills.description: Use when filtering mtDNA variant candidates from MQuad binomial mixture output — i.e., when a ΔBIC distribution over SNPs must be converted into an informative-variant list via an objective, data-driven knee-point cutoff (kneed v0.7.0).
skills.name: kbic-knee-point-cutoff-selection
skills.search_text: kbic-knee-point-cutoff-selection Use when filtering mtDNA variant candidates from MQuad binomial mixture output — i.e., when a ΔBIC distribution over SNPs must be converted into an informative-variant list via an objective, data-driven knee-point cutoff (kneed v0.7.0). The input is nuclear SNV calls or a diploid-context variant set — the ΔBIC mixture model assumes mitochondrial heteroplasmy, which nuclear SNV callers like Monovar and Conbase do not model Only a handful of candidate variants exist, so the ΔBIC distribution is too sparse to define a meaningful Kneedle knee point The goal is donor demultiplexing with known common germline SNPs (cellSNP+vireo mode), not somatic mtDNA clone discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Selects clonally informative mitochondrial SNPs by computing ΔBIC = BIC(M0) − BIC(M1) from MQuad's one- versus two-component binomial mixture model fits, then choosing an objective ΔBIC cutoff at the Kneedle knee point instead of a hand-picked threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Selects clonally informative mitochondrial SNPs by computing ΔBIC = BIC(M0) − BIC(M1) from MQuad's one- versus two-component binomial mixture model fits, then choosing an objective ΔBIC cutoff at the Kneedle knee point instead of a hand-picked threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is nuclear SNV calls or a diploid-context variant set — the ΔBIC mixture model assumes mitochondrial heteroplasmy, which nuclear SNV callers like Monovar and Conbase do not model Only a handful of candidate variants exist, so the ΔBIC distribution is too sparse to define a meaningful Kneedle knee point The goal is donor demultiplexing with known common germline SNPs (cellSNP+vireo mode), not somatic mtDNA clone discovery

skills.description: Use when benchmarking spatially aware colorization (e.g., Spaco vs. baseline palettes) on simulated 2D cluster pairs and you need a density-overlap color-difference score that is expected to be zero for spatially non-overlapping cluster pairs.
skills.name: kde-jaccard-color-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: kde-jaccard-color-similarity-scoring Use when benchmarking spatially aware colorization (e.g., Spaco vs. baseline palettes) on simulated 2D cluster pairs and you need a density-overlap color-difference score that is expected to be zero for spatially non-overlapping cluster pairs. When you need to distinguish isolated from distantly isolated cluster pairs or grade differences by spatial distance — KDE-Jaccard scored zero for all non-overlapping pairs, whereas DOI and LISI successfully distinguished the two isolated cases from the non-isolated ones When evaluating single-cell spatial colorization of 3D SRT data, where the paper notes fine-tuning of parameters is crucial to differentiate 'sparse' from 'dense' cell types When measuring batch correction or label mixing quality in scRNA-seq integration — use LISI via scPOP in its native context instead of this color-overlap scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A benchmark metric from the Spaco paper that scores color similarity between two spatial cluster pairs by estimating each cluster's 2D density (scikit-image density estimation) and computing the Jaccard overlap of the resulting density regions, used alongside DOI, Wasserstein distance, and LISI to evaluate colorization quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: A benchmark metric from the Spaco paper that scores color similarity between two spatial cluster pairs by estimating each cluster's 2D density (scikit-image density estimation) and computing the Jaccard overlap of the resulting density regions, used alongside DOI, Wasserstein distance, and LISI to evaluate colorization quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need to distinguish isolated from distantly isolated cluster pairs or grade differences by spatial distance — KDE-Jaccard scored zero for all non-overlapping pairs, whereas DOI and LISI successfully distinguished the two isolated cases from the non-isolated ones When evaluating single-cell spatial colorization of 3D SRT data, where the paper notes fine-tuning of parameters is crucial to differentiate 'sparse' from 'dense' cell types When measuring batch correction or label mixing quality in scRNA-seq integration — use LISI via scPOP in its native context instead of this color-overlap scoring

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked list of predicted protein interactions from omics data (scRNA-seq or bulk proteomics) and need to quantify its accuracy against a KEGG gold-standard functional association set, or to compare predictors like FAVA vs plain PCC.
skills.name: kegg-benchmark-evaluation-of-predicted-interactions
skills.search_text: kegg-benchmark-evaluation-of-predicted-interactions Use when you have a ranked list of predicted protein interactions from omics data (scRNA-seq or bulk proteomics) and need to quantify its accuracy against a KEGG gold-standard functional association set, or to compare predictors like FAVA vs plain PCC. The input is not a ranked predicted interaction list but raw expression data — run the predictor (favapy or PCC) first before benchmarking You need a physical protein-protein interaction (PPI) gold standard rather than functional association networks — KEGG functional associations are the benchmark used here, not binary PPIs The organism/pathway scope of your proteins is not covered by KEGG, making the benchmark reference inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Benchmark ranked predicted protein-protein interactions (e.g. from FAVA or a PCC baseline) against KEGG functional associations by computing precision curves over the ranking, verifying that the scRNA-seq-derived FAVA network yields >5000 true positives with <500 false positives (>90% precision) and outperforms PCC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Benchmark ranked predicted protein-protein interactions (e.g. from FAVA or a PCC baseline) against KEGG functional associations by computing precision curves over the ranking, verifying that the scRNA-seq-derived FAVA network yields >5000 true positives with <500 false positives (>90% precision) and outperforms PCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a ranked predicted interaction list but raw expression data — run the predictor (favapy or PCC) first before benchmarking You need a physical protein-protein interaction (PPI) gold standard rather than functional association networks — KEGG functional associations are the benchmark used here, not binary PPIs The organism/pathway scope of your proteins is not covered by KEGG, making the benchmark reference inappropriate

skills.search_text: kegg-go-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a trained single-cell graph-embedding autoencoder (e.g., scMGCA on 'Qx Limb Muscle' or PDAC scRNA-seq data) and need to interpret its compressed transcriptomic space by identifying biological functions of its top pivotal genes. The analysis goal is cell clustering or batch-effect correction rather than functional interpretation of the autoencoder's latent space The input is already a candidate gene list not derived from an autoencoder weight matrix (the ranking pipeline W2 → W1 → r2 would not apply) The data are bulk transcriptomics rather than single-cell data from the compressed transcription space of a scRNA-seq model http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functional-genomics interpretation of a deep single-cell model (scMGCA) by ranking pivotal genes from the graph-embedding autoencoder's weight matrices and running KEGG/GO over-representation analysis on the top 200 with ClusterProfiler at pvalueCutoff=0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7

skills.name: kegg-kgml-xml-parsing
skills.search_text: kegg-kgml-xml-parsing Use when KEGG KGML pathway XMLs must be inspected or rewritten in Cytoscape so that multi-gene nodes (functional homolog / OR groups) show all responsible genes, not just the first listed gene that KEGGScape renders by default. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'line' link nodes instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or coloured in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP The goal is only the baseline KEGGScape rendering showing the first listed gene per node — no XML rewriting is needed in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Parse KEGG KGML XML pathway files with Python's ElementTree API to identify nodes whose name strings contain multiple functional homolog genes, and rewrite the XML so every gene in a multi-gene node is represented as a child element grouped under the original node while preserving node coordinates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Parse KEGG KGML XML pathway files with Python's ElementTree API to identify nodes whose name strings contain multiple functional homolog genes, and rewrite the XML so every gene in a multi-gene node is represented as a child element grouped under the original node while preserving node coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'line' link nodes instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or coloured in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP The goal is only the baseline KEGGScape rendering showing the first listed gene per node — no XML rewriting is needed in that case

skills.search_text: kegg-network-topology-parsing Use when a rule-inference or dynamic-modeling pipeline needs pathway topology scaffolds and the source is KEGG (organism code + pathway IDs), or when non-KEGG networks must be loaded in GRAPHML format for downstream Boolean rule inference. skills.description: Use when you have ranked gene lists (e.g., SSrGE rank_genes() output) from multiple scRNA-seq datasets and need to test which KEGG pathways are over-represented among top-ranked genes and combine evidence across datasets.
skills.name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: kegg-pathway-enrichment-analysis Use when you have ranked gene lists (e.g., SSrGE rank_genes() output) from multiple scRNA-seq datasets and need to test which KEGG pathways are over-represented among top-ranked genes and combine evidence across datasets. Input genes are an unranked or unfiltered gene list rather than top-ranked SSrGE eeSNV genes — enrichment would not reflect genotype-phenotype linkage. skills.when_to_use_negative: Real data with no ground-truth latent ordering exists — Kendall-tau against simulated z cannot be computed, so use qualitative validation (e.g. checks that PhenoPath model fits are consistent with the data) instead Branching or cyclic trajectories where a single one-dimensional latent z is not the correct reference ordering Evaluating a method specifically designed for covariate-modulated trajectories on data with zero interaction genes, where 'de-only' simulation regimes make all methods roughly comparable and the benchmark is uninformative

skills.description: Use when implementing ivis-style or other triplet-loss siamese models in TensorFlow/Keras and you need weight-shared anchor/positive/negative branches built from a shared base encoder.
skills.name: keras-model-assembly
skills.search_text: keras-model-assembly Use when implementing ivis-style or other triplet-loss siamese models in TensorFlow/Keras and you need weight-shared anchor/positive/negative branches built from a shared base encoder. Task is unsupervised embedding with a non-triplet objective (e.g. plain autoencoder or PCA reduction such as the article's PCA to n=50 for Melanoma features) — weight-shared triplet branches are unnecessary. Data is not scaled suitably for SELU-based dense networks; ivis workflows scale inputs to [0,1] with MinMaxScaler first, so raw unnormalised features may train poorly. Only a single-input encoder is needed (no anchor/positive/negative triplet structure), e.g. a supervised classifier head. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assembles a siamese neural network in Keras by instantiating three weight-shared replicas of a dense base network ('szubert': 3×128-neuron SELU layers with LeCun normal init, plus a linear-activation embedding layer with Glorot uniform init sized to embedding_dims), so anchor, positive, and negative inputs pass through identical weights for triplet-loss training as used in ivis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Assembles a siamese neural network in Keras by instantiating three weight-shared replicas of a dense base network ('szubert': 3×128-neuron SELU layers with LeCun normal init, plus a linear-activation embedding layer with Glorot uniform init sized to embedding_dims), so anchor, positive, and negative inputs pass through identical weights for triplet-loss training as used in ivis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Task is unsupervised embedding with a non-triplet objective (e.g. plain autoencoder or PCA reduction such as the article's PCA to n=50 for Melanoma features) — weight-shared triplet branches are unnecessary. Data is not scaled suitably for SELU-based dense networks; ivis workflows scale inputs to [0,1] with MinMaxScaler first, so raw unnormalised features may train poorly. Only a single-input encoder is needed (no anchor/positive/negative triplet structure), e.g. a supervised classifier head.

skills.search_text: keras-model-definition-and-persistence Use when a circular (periodic) pseudo-time model must be defined as a Keras autoencoder with cos/sin decoder activations, trained on preprocessed scRNA-seq data, and saved as a loadable .h5 artifact. The trajectory in the data is linear rather than periodic — Cyclum's circular manifold and sinusoidal decoder are designed for latent periodic processes (e.g., cell cycle), not linear pseudo-time. skills.description: Use when you need to encode a known biological signal (cell-cycle labels, spatial coordinates, zonation gene scores, or a cell-to-reference mapping) as a cell–cell similarity kernel before projecting and removing that signal from scRNA-seq expression data with SiFT.
skills.name: kernel-based-cell-similarity-construction
skills.search_text: kernel-based-cell-similarity-construction Use when you need to encode a known biological signal (cell-cycle labels, spatial coordinates, zonation gene scores, or a cell-to-reference mapping) as a cell–cell similarity kernel before projecting and removing that signal from scRNA-seq expression data with SiFT. No prior knowledge exists about the signal to filter — SiFT strongly relies on prior knowledge to define the cell–cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to loss of signal. The goal is batch-effect integration at the latent-representation level (e.g., bbknn, Harmony, scVI) rather than gene-expression-level filtering of a defined biological signal. Data are already filtered/corrected and downstream work only requires log-transformed expression — SiFT output is no longer properly log-transformed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a probabilistic cell–cell similarity kernel capturing similarity with respect to a biological signal (e.g., cell cycle phase, spatial zonation, a reference mapping) as the first step of SiFT signal filtering. The kernel choice (mapping, knn, RBF/Laplacian distance) determines how the signal to be filtered is encoded. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Constructs a probabilistic cell–cell similarity kernel capturing similarity with respect to a biological signal (e.g., cell cycle phase, spatial zonation, a reference mapping) as the first step of SiFT signal filtering. The kernel choice (mapping, knn, RBF/Laplacian distance) determines how the signal to be filtered is encoded.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior knowledge exists about the signal to filter — SiFT strongly relies on prior knowledge to define the cell–cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to loss of signal. skills.description: Use when a known nuisance signal (cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, batch) encoded in marker genes or cell attributes must be removed from single-cell RNA-seq expression while preserving the biological structure of interest.
skills.name: kernel-based-expression-projection
skills.search_text: kernel-based-expression-projection Use when a known nuisance signal (cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, batch) encoded in marker genes or cell attributes must be removed from single-cell RNA-seq expression while preserving the biological structure of interest. No reliable prior knowledge exists for the signal to filter — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell–cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to loss of signal Downstream tasks require properly log-transformed data — filtering modifies gene expression so the output is no longer properly log-transformed The goal is batch-effect integration via a joint latent representation rather than gene-expression-level correction (methods like scVI or Harmony operate in latent space instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 SiFT's core operation: define a probabilistic cell–cell similarity kernel capturing the biological signal to remove, project the gene expression count matrix onto that signal via matrix multiplication, and deduct the projection to obtain a filtered expression matrix that preserves other biological attributes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: SiFT's core operation: define a probabilistic cell–cell similarity kernel capturing the biological signal to remove, project the gene expression count matrix onto that signal via matrix multiplication, and deduct the projection to obtain a filtered expression matrix that preserves other biological attributes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable prior knowledge exists for the signal to filter — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell–cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to loss of signal Downstream tasks require properly log-transformed data — filtering modifies gene expression so the output is no longer properly log-transformed The goal is batch-effect integration via a joint latent representation rather than gene-expression-level correction (methods like scVI or Harmony operate in latent space instead)

skills.summary: Constructs a Bhattacharyya kernel matrix from RWR diffusion distributions and derives a low-dimensional cell embedding via SVD of its element-wise logarithm, as implemented in the BKFD step of DTFLOW for single-cell pseudotime visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression without an RWR diffusion distribution step — the Bhattacharyya kernel requires per-cell probability distribution vectors, not raw counts or normalized expression The goal is branch detection or pseudotime ordering itself — this skill only produces the BKFD embedding; use RSKG branch detection and root-cell-based ordering downstream instead Downstream method requires a Euclidean distance on expression space (e.g., PCA on expression) rather than a kernel-induced embedding on diffusion distributions

skills.description: Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell gene expression (sparse matrix X plus ptime, optional regix/branches in a .mat file) and need to infer a ranked directed regulator-target network with Granger causality ensembling.
skills.name: kernel-granger-causality-ensembling
skills.search_text: kernel-granger-causality-ensembling Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell gene expression (sparse matrix X plus ptime, optional regix/branches in a .mat file) and need to infer a ranked directed regulator-target network with Granger causality ensembling. Data are unordered bulk time series or lack pseudotime values — Granger regression here requires pseudotemporal ordering of single-cell expression You need a fully dense (complete) weighted graph: lambda=0 produces a non-sparse solution and is avoided because it is impractical and raises segmentation-violation risk on large datasets A single, non-ensemble Granger regression is sufficient and the ensemble/aggregation overhead is unwarranted http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporal single-cell expression data by running an ensemble of kernel-based Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) tests across hyperparameters and subsampled replicates, then compiling the partial networks into a ranked regulator-target list via modified Borda aggregation (SINGE). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Infers gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporal single-cell expression data by running an ensemble of kernel-based Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) tests across hyperparameters and subsampled replicates, then compiling the partial networks into a ranked regulator-target list via modified Borda aggregation (SINGE).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unordered bulk time series or lack pseudotime values — Granger regression here requires pseudotemporal ordering of single-cell expression You need a fully dense (complete) weighted graph: lambda=0 produces a non-sparse solution and is avoided because it is impractical and raises segmentation-violation risk on large datasets A single, non-ensemble Granger regression is sufficient and the ensemble/aggregation overhead is unwarranted

skills.description: Use when a downstream step (e.g., DELVE Step 1 module discovery) needs a distribution-preserving subsample of a large .h5ad single-cell dataset, or when per-sample sketches must retain cell-type frequencies.
skills.name: kernel-herding-distribution-sketching
skills.search_text: kernel-herding-distribution-sketching Use when a downstream step (e.g., DELVE Step 1 module discovery) needs a distribution-preserving subsample of a large .h5ad single-cell dataset, or when per-sample sketches must retain cell-type frequencies. The analysis goal is exhaustive per-cell inference (e.g., diffusion pseudotime regression over all 500 selected genes) rather than distribution-level subsampling — sketching discards cells The dataset is a small .h5ad where the full distribution is already computationally tractable and subsampling would add no benefit No meaningful sample-set structure or feature space exists on which the Gaussian kernel and random Fourier features can be computed (e.g., raw unnormalized counts lacking preprocessing) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Subsamples a small, representative set of cells (or prototypical cellular neighborhoods) from a preprocessed single-cell dataset via Kernel Herding, preserving cell-type frequencies and the spectral properties of the original data. In DELVE, it supplies the ~1000-neighborhood subsample on which dynamic feature-module discovery is performed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Subsamples a small, representative set of cells (or prototypical cellular neighborhoods) from a preprocessed single-cell dataset via Kernel Herding, preserving cell-type frequencies and the spectral properties of the original data. In DELVE, it supplies the ~1000-neighborhood subsample on which dynamic feature-module discovery is performed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is exhaustive per-cell inference (e.g., diffusion pseudotime regression over all 500 selected genes) rather than distribution-level subsampling — sketching discards cells The dataset is a small .h5ad where the full distribution is already computationally tractable and subsampling would add no benefit No meaningful sample-set structure or feature space exists on which the Gaussian kernel and random Fourier features can be computed (e.g., raw unnormalized counts lacking preprocessing)

skills.description: Use when input is pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data (e.g., a .mat file with sparse matrix X and ptime) and the goal is to infer directed regulator-target interactions via kernel-smoothed Lasso Granger regression.
skills.name: kernel-lasso-granger-regression
skills.search_text: kernel-lasso-granger-regression Use when input is pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data (e.g., a .mat file with sparse matrix X and ptime) and the goal is to infer directed regulator-target interactions via kernel-smoothed Lasso Granger regression. Data lack pseudotemporal ordering or the pseudotimes are uninformative — the article warns SINGE performs poorly with uninformative pseudotimes You need branch-specific networks but did not separate per-branch GLG outputs before calling Aggregate on a branching trajectory lambda=0 is selected — the GLG test becomes non-sparse and no network edge ranking is produced http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SINGE's Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) regression performs kernel-weighted, sparsity-controlled Granger causality testing on pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data, using Gaussian kernel smoothing over irregular pseudotimes and glmnet_matlab Lasso regression with per-gene subsampling across replicates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: SINGE's Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) regression performs kernel-weighted, sparsity-controlled Granger causality testing on pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data, using Gaussian kernel smoothing over irregular pseudotimes and glmnet_matlab Lasso regression with per-gene subsampling across replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack pseudotemporal ordering or the pseudotimes are uninformative — the article warns SINGE performs poorly with uninformative pseudotimes You need branch-specific networks but did not separate per-branch GLG outputs before calling Aggregate on a branching trajectory lambda=0 is selected — the GLG test becomes non-sparse and no network edge ranking is produced

skills.description: Use when 3D-aligned spot/cell coordinates and per-gene expression from consecutive ST slices (e.g., STARmap mouse brain) are available and genes whose expression varies significantly along any direction in 3D tissue must be identified.
skills.name: kernel-length-scale-hyperparameter-grid-search
skills.search_text: kernel-length-scale-hyperparameter-grid-search Use when 3D-aligned spot/cell coordinates and per-gene expression from consecutive ST slices (e.g., STARmap mouse brain) are available and genes whose expression varies significantly along any direction in 3D tissue must be identified. The data are a single 2D ST slice without stacked 3D coordinates — Spoint/Splane tasks, not Scube's 3D GPR module, apply The dataset is seq-based (e.g., 10X Visium) and has not yet been processed by Spoint deconvolution and Splane domain identification, which Scube's alignment depends on The goal is nonlinear slice alignment rather than 3D expression modeling — the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Grid-searches the Gaussian process kernel length scale when fitting Scube's GPRmodel to per-gene expression over stacked 3D spatial-transcriptomics coordinates, then scores each gene by the Bayes Factor of the optimized model versus an infinite-length-scale (no spatial structure) null. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Grid-searches the Gaussian process kernel length scale when fitting Scube's GPRmodel to per-gene expression over stacked 3D spatial-transcriptomics coordinates, then scores each gene by the Bayes Factor of the optimized model versus an infinite-length-scale (no spatial structure) null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are a single 2D ST slice without stacked 3D coordinates — Spoint/Splane tasks, not Scube's 3D GPR module, apply The dataset is seq-based (e.g., 10X Visium) and has not yet been processed by Spoint deconvolution and Splane domain identification, which Scube's alignment depends on The goal is nonlinear slice alignment rather than 3D expression modeling — the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment

skills.description: Use when decomposing a log-normalized single-cell RNA-seq matrix into nonnegative gene expression programs while regularizing cell GEP weights toward similarity to nearby cells in a q-diffused graph.
skills.name: kernel-regularized-nmf-factorization
skills.search_text: kernel-regularized-nmf-factorization Use when decomposing a log-normalized single-cell RNA-seq matrix into nonnegative gene expression programs while regularizing cell GEP weights toward similarity to nearby cells in a q-diffused graph. When the input matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — qNMF is designed to work on the full log-normalized gene library (*.normalized element) When batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets is required — the paper notes this was not considered and pre-existing tools must be coopted upstream When a fast runtime is essential — q-diffused kernel evaluation across all cell pairs takes 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Kernel-regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (qNMF) estimates gene expression programs (GEPs) by constraining NMF cell weights with a q-diffused cell affinity matrix, reducing underdetermination of the factorization. It is implemented in QDiffusion.jl via par_estimate_nmf on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Kernel-regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (qNMF) estimates gene expression programs (GEPs) by constraining NMF cell weights with a q-diffused cell affinity matrix, reducing underdetermination of the factorization. It is implemented in QDiffusion.jl via par_estimate_nmf on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input matrix has already undergone feature selection or dimensionality reduction — qNMF is designed to work on the full log-normalized gene library (*.normalized element) When batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets is required — the paper notes this was not considered and pre-existing tools must be coopted upstream When a fast runtime is essential — q-diffused kernel evaluation across all cell pairs takes 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix

skills.description: Use when input is a raw single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix from heterogeneous samples and a cell-to-cell similarity measure is needed before clustering, t-SNE-style visualization, or estimating the number of clusters C.
skills.name: kernel-similarity-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: kernel-similarity-matrix-construction Use when input is a raw single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix from heterogeneous samples and a cell-to-cell similarity measure is needed before clustering, t-SNE-style visualization, or estimating the number of clusters C. Input is already a cell-to-cell similarity/adjacency matrix rather than an expression matrix. The data are not heterogeneous single-cell samples and standard metrics (e.g., Euclidean/PCA) are known to suffice; SIMLR targets scRNA-seq noise and dropout structure. Only gene importance is needed without a similarity model — use SIMLR_Feature_Ranking on an already learned similarity instead of re-learning kernels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs a cell-to-cell (sample-to-sample) similarity matrix from single-cell RNA-seq expression data by learning a convex combination of multiple kernels, so the metric fits the data's statistical structure despite large noise and dropout. This similarity structure underpins SIMLR's dimension reduction, clustering, visualization, and cluster-number estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: Constructs a cell-to-cell (sample-to-sample) similarity matrix from single-cell RNA-seq expression data by learning a convex combination of multiple kernels, so the metric fits the data's statistical structure despite large noise and dropout. This similarity structure underpins SIMLR's dimension reduction, clustering, visualization, and cluster-number estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-to-cell similarity/adjacency matrix rather than an expression matrix. The data are not heterogeneous single-cell samples and standard metrics (e.g., Euclidean/PCA) are known to suffice; SIMLR targets scRNA-seq noise and dropout structure. Only gene importance is needed without a similarity model — use SIMLR_Feature_Ranking on an already learned similarity instead of re-learning kernels.

skills.description: Use when a target scRNA-Seq dataset has been reconstructed via the source dictionary H_src (X_trg_new = theta*H_src*W'trg + (1-theta)*X_trg) and you need to choose theta without ground-truth labels.
skills.name: kernel-target-alignment-parameter-selection
skills.search_text: kernel-target-alignment-parameter-selection Use when a target scRNA-Seq dataset has been reconstructed via the source dictionary H_src (X_trg_new = theta*H_src*W'trg + (1-theta)*X_trg) and you need to choose theta without ground-truth labels. Ground-truth labels for the target cells are available and supervised tuning of theta (e.g. by maximizing ARI) is feasible — the paper's KTA route is specifically the unsupervised option The source and target share no (or an extremely small) gene set — the article notes loss of vital information is inevitable when only shared transcripts can be used, making the reconstructed target unreliable for KTA scoring The downstream analysis is not clustering-derived (KTA assesses cluster-structure alignment, so the score is not meaningful for other objectives) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Automatic unsupervised selection of the mixture parameter theta for NMF-based transfer learning in scRNA-Seq clustering, by scoring Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) over a pre-specified range of convex-combination weights instead of hand-tuning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Automatic unsupervised selection of the mixture parameter theta for NMF-based transfer learning in scRNA-Seq clustering, by scoring Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) over a pre-specified range of convex-combination weights instead of hand-tuning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth labels for the target cells are available and supervised tuning of theta (e.g. by maximizing ARI) is feasible — the paper's KTA route is specifically the unsupervised option The source and target share no (or an extremely small) gene set — the article notes loss of vital information is inevitable when only shared transcripts can be used, making the reconstructed target unreliable for KTA scoring The downstream analysis is not clustering-derived (KTA assesses cluster-structure alignment, so the score is not meaningful for other objectives)

skills.description: Use when you must choose the transfer learning mixture parameter theta in [0,1] for a modified target dataset Xtrg_new without ground-truth labels, or when validating that unsupervised KTA-based theta selection tracks supervised ARI across overlap settings.
skills.name: kernel-target-alignment-scoring
skills.search_text: kernel-target-alignment-scoring Use when you must choose the transfer learning mixture parameter theta in [0,1] for a modified target dataset Xtrg_new without ground-truth labels, or when validating that unsupervised KTA-based theta selection tracks supervised ARI across overlap settings. When ground-truth labels are available and a directly supervised selection of theta (via ARI) is preferred — KTA is the unsupervised surrogate. When the goal is plain SC3 clustering of the original target data without transfer learning — no theta sweep or KTA scoring is needed. When source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the article notes a loss of vital information is inevitable since only shared genes can be used. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores between the linear kernel of a transfer-modified scRNA-Seq target dataset and the linear kernel of SC3-predicted cell-type labels, providing an unsupervised criterion for automatically selecting the mixture parameter theta. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Computes Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores between the linear kernel of a transfer-modified scRNA-Seq target dataset and the linear kernel of SC3-predicted cell-type labels, providing an unsupervised criterion for automatically selecting the mixture parameter theta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ground-truth labels are available and a directly supervised selection of theta (via ARI) is preferred — KTA is the unsupervised surrogate. When the goal is plain SC3 clustering of the original target data without transfer learning — no theta sweep or KTA scoring is needed. When source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the article notes a loss of vital information is inevitable since only shared genes can be used.

skills.description: Use when the analysis must compare spatial regions (rexels) or cell groups as transcriptome distributions rather than individual cells — e.g. segmenting MERFISH cortical tissue via LDS.
skills.name: kernel-two-sample-distance-computation
skills.search_text: kernel-two-sample-distance-computation Use when the analysis must compare spatial regions (rexels) or cell groups as transcriptome distributions rather than individual cells — e.g. segmenting MERFISH cortical tissue via LDS. The data is a plain single-cell expression matrix needing standard dimensionality reduction or clustering without a spatial/distributional comparison — use qPHATE or ordinary Leiden clustering instead. You need batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets first — the paper explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction upstream of this analysis. The sample size per region is too small for stable within-set kernel averaging — q-diffusion also makes parametric assumptions that may be restrictive for some use cases. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes pairwise distances between sets of cells (rexels or spatial regions) as distributional two-sample comparisons via maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) with a q-diffused kernel (or plain Gaussian baseline), enabling local distributional segmentation of spatial scRNAseq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Computes pairwise distances between sets of cells (rexels or spatial regions) as distributional two-sample comparisons via maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) with a q-diffused kernel (or plain Gaussian baseline), enabling local distributional segmentation of spatial scRNAseq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is a plain single-cell expression matrix needing standard dimensionality reduction or clustering without a spatial/distributional comparison — use qPHATE or ordinary Leiden clustering instead. You need batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets first — the paper explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction upstream of this analysis. The sample size per region is too small for stable within-set kernel averaging — q-diffusion also makes parametric assumptions that may be restrictive for some use cases.

skills.search_text: kernel-weighted-lasso-regression-ensembling Use when you have single-cell gene expression data ordered along pseudotime (a .mat file with matrix X, ptime array, gene list) and need to reconstruct a gene regulatory network as ranked transcription-regulator-to-target interactions. Data are not ordered along a meaningful pseudotime — the paper warns of poor performance for uninformative pseudotimes The trajectory branches but you want branch-specific networks without splitting GLG results per branch (branch results are combined by default in SINGE v0.5.0) Expression data are not count-based and you plan to log-transform anyway — the --family gaussian + log-transform recommendation targets count data with glmnet_matlab memory issues http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs the SINGE workflow: kernel-based Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) regression on pseudotime-ordered single-cell expression data, followed by modified Borda aggregation of an ensemble of subsampled GLG networks into a ranked regulator-target edge list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Runs the SINGE workflow: kernel-based Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) regression on pseudotime-ordered single-cell expression data, followed by modified Borda aggregation of an ensemble of subsampled GLG networks into a ranked regulator-target edge list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not ordered along a meaningful pseudotime — the paper warns of poor performance for uninformative pseudotimes The trajectory branches but you want branch-specific networks without splitting GLG results per branch (branch results are combined by default in SINGE v0.5.0) Expression data are not count-based and you plan to log-transform anyway — the --family gaussian + log-transform recommendation targets count data with glmnet_matlab memory issues

skills.summary: Recovers the key genes (landmark genes) defining each scQA cluster and validates their biological significance against published marker genes, hub genes, and differentially expressed genes (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p-value < 0.01) from the dataset's original publication.

skills.search_text: kinase-substrate-network-activity-inference Use when evaluating which biological activity inference methods recover perturbed regulators (kinases) from phospho-proteomics perturbation experiments using a kinase-substrate network. skills.description: Use when modeling RNA-seq counts from paired-sample designs of genetically related individuals and you need to incorporate pairwise kinship covariance, assess its impact on model fit (delta AIC), or on DEG detection at FDR < 0.05.

skills.search_text: kinship-mixed-effects-modeling Use when modeling RNA-seq counts from paired-sample designs of genetically related individuals and you need to incorporate pairwise kinship covariance, assess its impact on model fit (delta AIC), or on DEG detection at FDR < 0.05. Samples are unrelated or no pairwise kinship matrix is available — use kimma_lm/kimma_lme fits without run_lmerel The goal is SNP–gene eQTL interaction testing — that is handled by kmFit_eQTL with dat_snp and dat_map rather than the kinship random-effect workflow Unpaired single-time-point designs where a simple limma-style lm fit suffices and kinship covariance adds no modeling information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit linear mixed effects models for RNA-seq data that include a pairwise genetic kinship covariance matrix as a random effect, using the kimma R package (which delegates kinship-capable fits to lme4qtl::relmatLmer), and compare kinship vs. non-kinship model fit per gene via AIC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279

skills.description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or manifold-projection methods on single-cell modalities and you need quantitative metrics of how well low-dimensional embeddings preserve high-dimensional pairwise-distance distributions.

skills.search_text: kl-density-preservation-scoring Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or manifold-projection methods on single-cell modalities and you need quantitative metrics of how well low-dimensional embeddings preserve high-dimensional pairwise-distance distributions. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is manifold alignment between two modalities into a shared space — use scTopoGAN's run_scTopoGAN instead of per-modality projection scoring.
