skills.name: kl-divergence-based-spatial-deg-ranking
skills.search_text: kl-divergence-based-spatial-deg-ranking Use when you have spatial transcriptomics counts plus per-spot 2D tissue coordinates (e.g., a 10x Visium Seurat object) and want to identify spatially regulated genes without defining spatial clusters or bins. Your coordinates are a dimensionality-reduction embedding (t-SNE/UMAP/PCA) rather than physical spot positions — this skill specifically requires the actual 2D coordinates of spots inside the tissue You need continuous expression values for DEG testing — the current implementation requires binary detection data and genes with different expression levels but the same detection pattern receive identical D_KL and p-values Genes are detected in fewer than 10 spots/cells — the article's filter removes these very lowly expressed genes before running haystack http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Ranks spatially differentially expressed genes by applying singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence-based haystack() to the actual 2D tissue spot coordinates of a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., 10x Visium), rather than a dimensionality-reduction embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Ranks spatially differentially expressed genes by applying singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence-based haystack() to the actual 2D tissue spot coordinates of a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., 10x Visium), rather than a dimensionality-reduction embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your coordinates are a dimensionality-reduction embedding (t-SNE/UMAP/PCA) rather than physical spot positions — this skill specifically requires the actual 2D coordinates of spots inside the tissue You need continuous expression values for DEG testing — the current implementation requires binary detection data and genes with different expression levels but the same detection pattern receive identical D_KL and p-values Genes are detected in fewer than 10 spots/cells — the article's filter removes these very lowly expressed genes before running haystack

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. GO-subset, dispersion-filtered) must be converted into cell-to-cell edge weights for redPATH's cHMT pseudotime or Hamiltonian path trajectory reconstruction.
skills.name: kl-divergence-cell-distance-computation
skills.search_text: kl-divergence-cell-distance-computation Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. GO-subset, dispersion-filtered) must be converted into cell-to-cell edge weights for redPATH's cHMT pseudotime or Hamiltonian path trajectory reconstruction. The input matrix has not been GO-subset and dispersion-filtered — raw noisy expression inflates KL divergence between same-type cells The goal is clustering/cell-type assignment rather than ordering cells along a linear or branching developmental trajectory Pseudotime results perform poorly (per the article, downstream approaches that skip cell-type labeling may fail in this case) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute pairwise cell-to-cell edge weights for redPATH's Hamiltonian path formulation using the symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence, implemented in C++ via Rcpp/RcppArmadillo. This probabilistic distance matrix is the input edge weighting from which multiple noisy Hamiltonian path solutions are derived. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Compute pairwise cell-to-cell edge weights for redPATH's Hamiltonian path formulation using the symmetric Kullback-Leibler divergence, implemented in C++ via Rcpp/RcppArmadillo. This probabilistic distance matrix is the input edge weighting from which multiple noisy Hamiltonian path solutions are derived.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix has not been GO-subset and dispersion-filtered — raw noisy expression inflates KL divergence between same-type cells The goal is clustering/cell-type assignment rather than ordering cells along a linear or branching developmental trajectory Pseudotime results perform poorly (per the article, downstream approaches that skip cell-type labeling may fail in this case)

skills.description: Use when compressing high-dimensional, sparse omics data (e.g., protein abundances scaled 0-1) into a low-dimensional latent space with a VAE, and you need an explicitly regularized Gaussian latent representation to avoid sparseness/redundancy artifacts before computing protein associations.
skills.name: kl-divergence-loss-weighting-regularization
skills.search_text: kl-divergence-loss-weighting-regularization Use when compressing high-dimensional, sparse omics data (e.g., protein abundances scaled 0-1) into a low-dimensional latent space with a VAE, and you need an explicitly regularized Gaussian latent representation to avoid sparseness/redundancy artifacts before computing protein associations. The input data are already low-dimensional or dense — FAVA's motivation is compressing high-dimensional data where co-expression analysis fails due to sparseness and redundancy You need to reconstruct inputs rather than produce a regularized latent embedding — the 0.1 KL weight intentionally trades reconstruction fidelity for prior-constrained latent structure Downstream analysis requires a non-Gaussian latent prior — the KL term is defined against a N(1, 0.1) normal prior specific to this implementation http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 A VAE training scheme from FAVA that combines reconstruction error and KL-divergence regularization in a 0.9/0.1 weighted sum, regularizing the latent space toward a Gaussian prior N(1, 0.1) so that high-dimensional proteomics/scRNA-seq data are compressed into a dense, low-dimensional latent space suitable for downstream correlation-based network inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: A VAE training scheme from FAVA that combines reconstruction error and KL-divergence regularization in a 0.9/0.1 weighted sum, regularizing the latent space toward a Gaussian prior N(1, 0.1) so that high-dimensional proteomics/scRNA-seq data are compressed into a dense, low-dimensional latent space suitable for downstream correlation-based network inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already low-dimensional or dense — FAVA's motivation is compressing high-dimensional data where co-expression analysis fails due to sparseness and redundancy You need to reconstruct inputs rather than produce a regularized latent embedding — the 0.1 KL weight intentionally trades reconstruction fidelity for prior-constrained latent structure Downstream analysis requires a non-Gaussian latent prior — the KL term is defined against a N(1, 0.1) normal prior specific to this implementation

skills.description: Use when you must test whether a gene set/pathway is truly coordinated (heterogeneous) among cells in scRNA-seq data without pre-clustering, e.g. validating marker, mixed, or random gene sets across datasets.
skills.name: kl-divergence-null-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: kl-divergence-null-hypothesis-testing Use when you must test whether a gene set/pathway is truly coordinated (heterogeneous) among cells in scRNA-seq data without pre-clustering, e.g. validating marker, mixed, or random gene sets across datasets. Data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' per the discussion You need cluster/annotation-free per-cell pathway activity scores rather than a gene set coordination p-value — use run.rwr/compute.cell.label instead Input gene sets are smaller than gene.set.cutoff = 3 genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 GSDensity's cluster-free gene set coordination test: co-embed cells and genes via MCA, compute the KL-divergence (KLD) between a gene set's density and the background density in the latent space, and calibrate significance against size-matched random gene sets (n.times = 100) with adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: GSDensity's cluster-free gene set coordination test: co-embed cells and genes via MCA, compute the KL-divergence (KLD) between a gene set's density and the background density in the latent space, and calibrate significance against size-matched random gene sets (n.times = 100) with adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' per the discussion You need cluster/annotation-free per-cell pathway activity scores rather than a gene set coordination p-value — use run.rwr/compute.cell.label instead Input gene sets are smaller than gene.set.cutoff = 3 genes

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with a pretrained deep embedding (e.g., stacked autoencoder bottleneck features) and you need to iteratively refine soft cluster assignments until the fraction of cells changing clusters falls below a tolerance.
skills.name: kl-divergence-self-training-optimization
skills.search_text: kl-divergence-self-training-optimization Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with a pretrained deep embedding (e.g., stacked autoencoder bottleneck features) and you need to iteratively refine soft cluster assignments until the fraction of cells changing clusters falls below a tolerance. Technical batch differences are larger than true biological variations — DESC's gradual batch-effect removal only holds when 'technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations'. You need hard, non-iterative clustering without a pretrained embedding — alternative methods such as SC3 consensus clustering or pairwise batch-correction tools (Seurat 3.0 CCA/MNN, Scanorama) address different setups. Input is raw UMI counts without the required cell-level (counts/total × 10,000, log1p) and gene-level standardization preprocessing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Iterative self-training scheme from DESC that refines cluster assignments by minimizing the Kullback–Leibler divergence between a soft assignment distribution Q (Student's t-kernel over embedded cells and centroids) and an auxiliary target distribution P, learning cluster-specific representations while ignoring irrelevant signals such as batch effect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Iterative self-training scheme from DESC that refines cluster assignments by minimizing the Kullback–Leibler divergence between a soft assignment distribution Q (Student's t-kernel over embedded cells and centroids) and an auxiliary target distribution P, learning cluster-specific representations while ignoring irrelevant signals such as batch effect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Technical batch differences are larger than true biological variations — DESC's gradual batch-effect removal only holds when 'technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations'. You need hard, non-iterative clustering without a pretrained embedding — alternative methods such as SC3 consensus clustering or pairwise batch-correction tools (Seurat 3.0 CCA/MNN, Scanorama) address different setups. Input is raw UMI counts without the required cell-level (counts/total × 10,000, log1p) and gene-level standardization preprocessing.

skills.description: Use when fitting KMD clustering to a biological dataset (mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, or simulated data) and you need to set KMDClustering hyperparameters — especially whether to let k be auto-computed via KMD silhouette or fixed, and how to configure sub-sampling for large datasets.
skills.name: kmd-clustering-hyperparameter-configuration
skills.search_text: kmd-clustering-hyperparameter-configuration Use when fitting KMD clustering to a biological dataset (mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, or simulated data) and you need to set KMDClustering hyperparameters — especially whether to let k be auto-computed via KMD silhouette or fixed, and how to configure sub-sampling for large datasets. When the goal is de novo estimation of the number of clusters — the article notes DBCV-based cluster number estimation is only preliminary and 'further research is needed' When compute time is critical — automatic k selection requires scanning many k values and the python/scipy implementation has longer running times than optimized implementations When the dataset contains very small clusters that a sub-sampled fit may miss because they are not sampled well http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Configuration guide for KMDHierarchicalClustering's KMDClustering class: choosing k, min_cluster_size, affinity, certainty, and k_scan_range so the KMD silhouette score selects the optimal k automatically and outlier-aware partitioning is applied correctly. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Configuration guide for KMDHierarchicalClustering's KMDClustering class: choosing k, min_cluster_size, affinity, certainty, and k_scan_range so the KMD silhouette score selects the optimal k automatically and outlier-aware partitioning is applied correctly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo estimation of the number of clusters — the article notes DBCV-based cluster number estimation is only preliminary and 'further research is needed' When compute time is critical — automatic k selection requires scanning many k values and the python/scipy implementation has longer running times than optimized implementations When the dataset contains very small clusters that a sub-sampled fit may miss because they are not sampled well

skills.description: Use when clustering simulated, mass cytometry, or scRNA-seq data where general-purpose methods fail on non-globular or noisy clusters and you want automatic k selection rather than user-specified cryptic hyperparameters.
skills.name: kmd-hierarchical-clustering
skills.search_text: kmd-hierarchical-clustering Use when clustering simulated, mass cytometry, or scRNA-seq data where general-purpose methods fail on non-globular or noisy clusters and you want automatic k selection rather than user-specified cryptic hyperparameters. Runtime is critical: a single KMD run maintains lists of k minimal distances for each pair of clusters and the python/scipy implementation is slower than optimized non-interpreted implementations of widely used clustering algorithms The data contain very small clusters that a sampling-based subsample would not represent — the sampling extension may miss clusters that are not sampled well The standard silhouette is sufficient: KMD silhouette computation requires scanning a range of k values (k < 100 in all paper cases), consuming more computational resources than a single fixed-k run http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Apply KMD (k-minimal distances) clustering — a generalization of single and average linkage hierarchical clustering — to datasets with known or unknown cluster structure, using the KMD silhouette to auto-select the hyperparameter k, an outlier-aware partitioning scheme, and optional DBCV-based cluster-number estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Apply KMD (k-minimal distances) clustering — a generalization of single and average linkage hierarchical clustering — to datasets with known or unknown cluster structure, using the KMD silhouette to auto-select the hyperparameter k, an outlier-aware partitioning scheme, and optional DBCV-based cluster-number estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Runtime is critical: a single KMD run maintains lists of k minimal distances for each pair of clusters and the python/scipy implementation is slower than optimized non-interpreted implementations of widely used clustering algorithms The data contain very small clusters that a sampling-based subsample would not represent — the sampling extension may miss clusters that are not sampled well The standard silhouette is sufficient: KMD silhouette computation requires scanning a range of k values (k < 100 in all paper cases), consuming more computational resources than a single fixed-k run

skills.description: Use when fitting KMDClustering without an a priori k: ground-truth labels are unavailable, the number of neighbors driving the KMD linkage is unknown, and the user wants k selected intrinsically via the KMD silhouette instead of manual tuning.
skills.name: kmd-silhouette-k-selection
skills.search_text: kmd-silhouette-k-selection Use when fitting KMDClustering without an a priori k: ground-truth labels are unavailable, the number of neighbors driving the KMD linkage is unknown, and the user wants k selected intrinsically via the KMD silhouette instead of manual tuning. When k is already known or scientifically motivated — the scan runs clustering repeatedly over many k values and requires substantially more computational resources When cluster shape is strongly non-globular and an intrinsic criterion is needed — the silhouette score is biased towards globular cluster shapes; prefer DBCV-based validation instead When using the sampled KMD extension on datasets with very small clusters — sampling may miss small clusters regardless of the selected k http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Automatic elimination of the cryptic hyperparameter k in KMD clustering by running the clustering in parallel over a range of k values (e.g. k_scan_range=(1,100,3)) and selecting the k whose solution has the highest generalized KMD silhouette score, rather than requiring the user to guess k a priori. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Automatic elimination of the cryptic hyperparameter k in KMD clustering by running the clustering in parallel over a range of k values (e.g. k_scan_range=(1,100,3)) and selecting the k whose solution has the highest generalized KMD silhouette score, rather than requiring the user to guess k a priori.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When k is already known or scientifically motivated — the scan runs clustering repeatedly over many k values and requires substantially more computational resources When cluster shape is strongly non-globular and an intrinsic criterion is needed — the silhouette score is biased towards globular cluster shapes; prefer DBCV-based validation instead When using the sampled KMD extension on datasets with very small clusters — sampling may miss small clusters regardless of the selected k

skills.description: Use when you need to create diverse base partitions on an embedded scRNA-seq representation (e.g. latent matrix from SDDA.py) before building a bipartite graph for consensus clustering of cell types.
skills.name: kmeans-base-clustering-ensemble
skills.search_text: kmeans-base-clustering-ensemble Use when you need to create diverse base partitions on an embedded scRNA-seq representation (e.g. latent matrix from SDDA.py) before building a bipartite graph for consensus clustering of cell types. Input is raw gene expression counts rather than a learned latent representation — scBGEDA generates basic clusterings on the compressed low-dimensional space from the dual denoising autoencoder, not on raw scRNA-seq data. You need a single fixed-k clustering with no ensemble aggregation — this skill's purpose is to create many partitions of varying k for a graph-based consensus function, not a final partition itself. The downstream goal is direct clustering of cells without consensus assembly — this skill feeds BC.m/BGEC.m and the transfer cut step; running K-means alone is the wrong granularity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates a large ensemble of K-means basic clusterings (K=100 base partitions, each with a random k drawn between kmin and kmax) on the latent representation Z learned by the single-cell dual denoising autoencoder, to serve as the diversity-producing front end of bipartite graph ensemble clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Generates a large ensemble of K-means basic clusterings (K=100 base partitions, each with a random k drawn between kmin and kmax) on the latent representation Z learned by the single-cell dual denoising autoencoder, to serve as the diversity-producing front end of bipartite graph ensemble clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression counts rather than a learned latent representation — scBGEDA generates basic clusterings on the compressed low-dimensional space from the dual denoising autoencoder, not on raw scRNA-seq data. You need a single fixed-k clustering with no ensemble aggregation — this skill's purpose is to create many partitions of varying k for a graph-based consensus function, not a final partition itself. The downstream goal is direct clustering of cells without consensus assembly — this skill feeds BC.m/BGEC.m and the transfer cut step; running K-means alone is the wrong granularity.

skills.description: Use when you have pre-processed, log2-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrices (cells as rows, genes as columns) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify whether imputation improves clustering accuracy.
skills.name: kmeans-cell-type-clustering
skills.search_text: kmeans-cell-type-clustering Use when you have pre-processed, log2-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrices (cells as rows, genes as columns) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify whether imputation improves clustering accuracy. Input matrices are raw counts rather than log2-transformed expression, since the comparison protocol assumes log-transformed data Cell-type labels are unavailable, since the ARI cannot be computed against original annotations Datasets small enough that alternative clustering evaluation (e.g. silhouette) is desired and no ground-truth annotations exist to justify ARI http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark cell-type recovery on log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrices by running scikit-learn K-means (K = number of unique cell types per dataset) on raw and imputed data (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) and scoring each clustering with the Adjusted Rand Index against original cell annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-type recovery on log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrices by running scikit-learn K-means (K = number of unique cell types per dataset) on raw and imputed data (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) and scoring each clustering with the Adjusted Rand Index against original cell annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices are raw counts rather than log2-transformed expression, since the comparison protocol assumes log-transformed data Cell-type labels are unavailable, since the ARI cannot be computed against original annotations Datasets small enough that alternative clustering evaluation (e.g. silhouette) is desired and no ground-truth annotations exist to justify ARI

skills.description: Use when a cohort of bulk RNA-seq samples must be distilled into representatives for single-cell sequencing in one batch, and multi-round active learning is impractical or risks introducing batch effects across sequencing rounds.
skills.name: kmeans-centroid-based-sample-selection
skills.search_text: kmeans-centroid-based-sample-selection Use when a cohort of bulk RNA-seq samples must be distilled into representatives for single-cell sequencing in one batch, and multi-round active learning is impractical or risks introducing batch effects across sequencing rounds. When iterative active learning is feasible and preferred, since active learning can incrementally refine representative selection and global mode was reported as comparable but slightly inferior (Supplementary Fig. S8) When deconvolving a single target sample with a single-cell reference rather than selecting representatives from a cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects all representative cohort samples in a single round by K-Means clustering of PCA-reduced bulk RNA-seq data, designating the sample closest to each cluster centroid as the representative — the 'global mode' of scSemiProfiler that avoids multi-round active learning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Selects all representative cohort samples in a single round by K-Means clustering of PCA-reduced bulk RNA-seq data, designating the sample closest to each cluster centroid as the representative — the 'global mode' of scSemiProfiler that avoids multi-round active learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When iterative active learning is feasible and preferred, since active learning can incrementally refine representative selection and global mode was reported as comparable but slightly inferior (Supplementary Fig. S8) When deconvolving a single target sample with a single-cell reference rather than selecting representatives from a cohort

skills.description: Use when reducing high-dimensional gene expression (scRNA-seq or TCGA-style) matrices to a low-dimensional cell-cell similarity representation via CCSF, specifically for the centroid-localization step that defines P cell groups.
skills.name: kmeans-centroid-optimization
skills.search_text: kmeans-centroid-optimization Use when reducing high-dimensional gene expression (scRNA-seq or TCGA-style) matrices to a low-dimensional cell-cell similarity representation via CCSF, specifically for the centroid-localization step that defines P cell groups. The dataset contains data points from only one class (no contrast between data points): CCSF then behaves like kernel PCA and offers only linearization and speed benefits over PCA Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or spatial coordinate table rather than a gene expression matrix The analysis goal is spatial reconstruction with marker genes or a reference atlas — novoSpaRc alone is the appropriate route, not CCSF centroid optimization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Stage 2 of the CCSF framework: locate P class centroids by minimizing the distance between centroids and all data points using k-means++ optimization, then compute the cell-centroid similarity matrix that seeds the Gram-matrix and class-discriminative optimization stages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100840
skills.summary: Stage 2 of the CCSF framework: locate P class centroids by minimizing the distance between centroids and all data points using k-means++ optimization, then compute the cell-centroid similarity matrix that seeds the Gram-matrix and class-discriminative optimization stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains data points from only one class (no contrast between data points): CCSF then behaves like kernel PCA and offers only linearization and speed benefits over PCA Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or spatial coordinate table rather than a gene expression matrix The analysis goal is spatial reconstruction with marker genes or a reference atlas — novoSpaRc alone is the appropriate route, not CCSF centroid optimization

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq expression data is accompanied by reCAT mean cell-cycle scores and quiescent/G0-like cells must be removed before pseudotime reconstruction, or when no cell-type labels are available for gating non-cycling cells.
skills.name: kmeans-cluster-identification
skills.search_text: kmeans-cluster-identification Use when single-cell RNA-seq expression data is accompanied by reCAT mean cell-cycle scores and quiescent/G0-like cells must be removed before pseudotime reconstruction, or when no cell-type labels are available for gating non-cycling cells. No reCAT (or equivalent) cell-cycle score matrix exists for the dataset — the clustering operates on mean phase scores, not expression values The goal is to study cycling/proliferating subpopulations rather than remove quiescent cells before trajectory inference Cell-cycle scores are unreliable or the pseudotime/phase decomposition performs poorly, which the paper notes can make this labeling approach fail http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify G0-like (quiescent) cells by running k-means (k = 5) on reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) and flagging the cluster that is significantly lowest (pairwise ANOVA, P < 0.001) across all six phase scores. This is the redPATH approach for detecting quiescent cells prior to trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Identify G0-like (quiescent) cells by running k-means (k = 5) on reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) and flagging the cluster that is significantly lowest (pairwise ANOVA, P < 0.001) across all six phase scores. This is the redPATH approach for detecting quiescent cells prior to trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reCAT (or equivalent) cell-cycle score matrix exists for the dataset — the clustering operates on mean phase scores, not expression values The goal is to study cycling/proliferating subpopulations rather than remove quiescent cells before trajectory inference Cell-cycle scores are unreliable or the pseudotime/phase decomposition performs poorly, which the paper notes can make this labeling approach fail

skills.description: Use when constructing scTab-style data augmentation: you already have donor-difference vectors per cell type (noise-zeroed, clamped to [-1.5, 1.5]) and need to consolidate them into a compact augmentation-vector set via k-means clustering with cluster-support filtering.
skills.name: kmeans-cluster-support-filtering
skills.search_text: kmeans-cluster-support-filtering Use when constructing scTab-style data augmentation: you already have donor-difference vectors per cell type (noise-zeroed, clamped to [-1.5, 1.5]) and need to consolidate them into a compact augmentation-vector set via k-means clustering with cluster-support filtering. The input is raw single-cell expression vectors rather than donor-difference centroid vectors — clustering cells directly does not yield the donor-shift directions this skill extracts. The dataset lacks donor stratification (cell types not observed across multiple donors), so donor-difference centroids and the resulting difference vectors cannot be reliably computed. A precomputed augmentation_vectors.parquet from the scTab release already exists and does not need to be regenerated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Distills scTab's donor-difference augmentation vectors into a reusable set of cell-type-independent augmentation directions by k-means clustering (k=50) followed by a support filter that retains only clusters containing >2000 vectors. The pooled vectors are serialized to augmentation_vectors.parquet for use during model training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Distills scTab's donor-difference augmentation vectors into a reusable set of cell-type-independent augmentation directions by k-means clustering (k=50) followed by a support filter that retains only clusters containing >2000 vectors. The pooled vectors are serialized to augmentation_vectors.parquet for use during model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw single-cell expression vectors rather than donor-difference centroid vectors — clustering cells directly does not yield the donor-shift directions this skill extracts. The dataset lacks donor stratification (cell types not observed across multiple donors), so donor-difference centroids and the resulting difference vectors cannot be reliably computed. A precomputed augmentation_vectors.parquet from the scTab release already exists and does not need to be regenerated.

skills.description: Use when you need to ask 'which indexed dataset(s) may contain this sequence?' over thousands of FASTA/FASTQ files and exact per-k-mer counts matter less than scalable, low-footprint membership queries.
skills.name: kmer-dataset-membership-indexing
skills.search_text: kmer-dataset-membership-indexing Use when you need to ask 'which indexed dataset(s) may contain this sequence?' over thousands of FASTA/FASTQ files and exact per-k-mer counts matter less than scalable, low-footprint membership queries. The goal is exact (false-negative-free) sequence search or alignment scoring — PAC is an approximate membership query structure like Cobs or HowDeSBT, not a BLAST-like aligner Only a handful of small genomes are involved and a simple all-against-all search suffices; the comb-tree/partition machinery targets collections of thousands of datasets Per-k-mer provenance must be exact with zero false positives — larger Bloom filters reduce but never eliminate the false positive rate http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds an approximate membership query index that maps k-mers (e.g. 21-mers) to the datasets containing them, using PAC's Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb Trees so thousands of FASTA/FASTQ files can be queried for sequence membership with low memory and disk footprint. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Builds an approximate membership query index that maps k-mers (e.g. 21-mers) to the datasets containing them, using PAC's Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb Trees so thousands of FASTA/FASTQ files can be queried for sequence membership with low memory and disk footprint.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is exact (false-negative-free) sequence search or alignment scoring — PAC is an approximate membership query structure like Cobs or HowDeSBT, not a BLAST-like aligner Only a handful of small genomes are involved and a simple all-against-all search suffices; the comb-tree/partition machinery targets collections of thousands of datasets Per-k-mer provenance must be exact with zero false positives — larger Bloom filters reduce but never eliminate the false positive rate

skills.description: Use when running PAC queries against an index of thousands of datasets and you need to turn the raw per-line kmer-sharing counts (e.g. '29719 50 701') into a ranked list of datasets that may contain the query sequence.
skills.name: kmer-sharing-count-interpretation
skills.search_text: kmer-sharing-count-interpretation Use when running PAC queries against an index of thousands of datasets and you need to turn the raw per-line kmer-sharing counts (e.g. '29719 50 701') into a ranked list of datasets that may contain the query sequence. You need exact containment calls rather than an approximate membership query — PAC lists datasets that may contain a query and can return false positives. You are indexing a single dataset or a handful of files where a direct containment test is cheaper than building an index. Queries are raw reads with many single-occurrence kmers and you did not build the index with the -u option, which filters kmers seen only once — shared-count signal will be diluted by error kmers. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Interpret PAC query output lines, which report per-query kmer-sharing counts between a query sequence and each indexed dataset (e.g. '29719 50 701'), to decide which indexed datasets plausibly contain the query. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Interpret PAC query output lines, which report per-query kmer-sharing counts between a query sequence and each indexed dataset (e.g. '29719 50 701'), to decide which indexed datasets plausibly contain the query.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need exact containment calls rather than an approximate membership query — PAC lists datasets that may contain a query and can return false positives. You are indexing a single dataset or a handful of files where a direct containment test is cheaper than building an index. Queries are raw reads with many single-occurrence kmers and you did not build the index with the -u option, which filters kmers seen only once — shared-count signal will be diluted by error kmers.

skills.description: Use when building or benchmarking approximate sequence search pre-filters over many bins of nucleotide sequences, and you must choose k (e.g. k=19), minimizer/threshold settings, and evaluate sensitivity (false positives) against known bin memberships.

skills.search_text: kmer-threshold-parameterization Use when building or benchmarking approximate sequence search pre-filters over many bins of nucleotide sequences, and you must choose k (e.g. k=19), minimizer/threshold settings, and evaluate sensitivity (false positives) against known bin memberships. The reference collection has highly uneven bin sizes or a very high number of bins, since Raptor's method is susceptible to uneven bin sizes and slows down moderately at several ten thousand bins You need edit-distance-sensitive full-text search rather than approximate k-mer membership pre-filtering, where word-based indices are inappropriate but FM-index-based approaches are required Only one tool is being evaluated — the skill's core value is the controlled cross-tool comparison against known bin memberships http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Parameterizes k-mer based search indices (Raptor's binning directory with winnowing minimizers, interleaved Bloom filters, and probabilistic thresholding; COBS with a 53% k-mer-lemma threshold; Mantis) and benchmark-tunes these settings so construction time, search time, memory/disk usage, and false positives can be compared fairly against a known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Parameterizes k-mer based search indices (Raptor's binning directory with winnowing minimizers, interleaved Bloom filters, and probabilistic thresholding; COBS with a 53% k-mer-lemma threshold; Mantis) and benchmark-tunes these settings so construction time, search time, memory/disk usage, and false positives can be compared fairly against a known ground truth.

skills.search_text: kmer-uniqueness-analysis-across-binnings Use when evaluating or reproducing Raptor's minimizer-based representative k-mer statistics (Table 8), e.g. to check how quickly r(k) collapses toward 1.00 as k grows for a given number of bins. The goal is running actual sequence queries or read mapping with Raptor/DREAM-Yara rather than characterizing index k-mer statistics Bins have highly uneven sizes — the paper notes Raptor's main limiting factor is 'its susceptibility to uneven bin sizes as well as a high number of bins', which distorts minimizer behavior Comparing against Raptor indices built with an older version, since indices built before version 2.0.0 are incompatible Computes Raptor's effective text ratios r(k), the size of the winnowing-minimizer representative k-mer set relative to the original text length, for a dataset partitioned into 64 and 1,024 bins across k-mer sizes k=12..20. This quantifies how many distinct k-mers actually index a binning, explaining Raptor's space/accuracy trade-off. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Computes Raptor's effective text ratios r(k), the size of the winnowing-minimizer representative k-mer set relative to the original text length, for a dataset partitioned into 64 and 1,024 bins across k-mer sizes k=12..20. This quantifies how many distinct k-mers actually index a binning, explaining Raptor's space/accuracy trade-off.

skills.summary: Select informative DNA k-mer accessibility features from raw single-cell ATAC-seq count matrices (z-score deviation computation plus PCA-based filtering) so that branching trajectories can be reconstructed and lineage-driving transcription factors identified via k-mer-to-motif mapping.

skills.description: Use when a scATAC-seq trajectory has been reconstructed with STREAM using k-mer features and you need to identify which transcription factors drive each detected branch.

skills.search_text: kmert-to-transcription-factor-mapping Use when a scATAC-seq trajectory has been reconstructed with STREAM using k-mer features and you need to identify which transcription factors drive each detected branch. skills.description: Use when calling clonally informative mtDNA variants from single-cell genotyping matrices (e.g., cellsnp-lite AD/DP) and you need an objective, unsupervised ΔBIC cutoff instead of raw allele frequency thresholds.
skills.name: knee-point-threshold-selection-delta-bic
skills.search_text: knee-point-threshold-selection-delta-bic Use when calling clonally informative mtDNA variants from single-cell genotyping matrices (e.g., cellsnp-lite AD/DP) and you need an objective, unsupervised ΔBIC cutoff instead of raw allele frequency thresholds. skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already processed by mgatk or another mtDNA variant caller with its own quality cutoffs (e.g., log10(VMR) ≥ −2 and strand correlation ≥ 0.65) — do not double-filter with the ΔBIC knee. skills.search_text: knn-cell-type-classification Use when clustering very large scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., tens of thousands of cells like the 49,300-cell Macosko retina set) where clustering all cells is too expensive, so labels must be propagated from a subsample (e.g., 5% or 10%) to the rest via k-NN. Dataset is small enough that direct clustering of all cells (e.g., ssc.run with subsampling=F) is computationally feasible — subsampling plus k-NN adds unnecessary indirection. You need cluster labels only for the subsampled cells, not for the full cell population. You lack a reliable reference clustering on the subsample: k-NN classification propagates whatever bias the subsample clustering introduces. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 The classification step of the subsampling-clustering-classification (SCC/SSCC) strategy: k-means clusters are learned on a random cell subsample, then k-nearest-neighbor classification transfers those labels to all remaining cells, reducing complexity from O(n^2) to O(n). Within SSCC, k-NN operates on a Spearman-correlation feature space after random projection, which also improves cross-scheme consistency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: The classification step of the subsampling-clustering-classification (SCC/SSCC) strategy: k-means clusters are learned on a random cell subsample, then k-nearest-neighbor classification transfers those labels to all remaining cells, reducing complexity from O(n^2) to O(n). Within SSCC, k-NN operates on a Spearman-correlation feature space after random projection, which also improves cross-scheme consistency.

When the reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage (Condition I), since equivalence with de novo Harmony integration is then not expected. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assess the fidelity of query-cell reference mapping (e.g., Symphony-mapped PBMCs) by computing per-cell k-NN correlation between the mapped query embedding and a gold-standard de novo reference embedding (calcknncorr at k=500), and report the fraction of query cells with correlation > 0.4 against a PCA-only baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Assess the fidelity of query-cell reference mapping (e.g., Symphony-mapped PBMCs) by computing per-cell k-NN correlation between the mapped query embedding and a gold-standard de novo reference embedding (calcknncorr at k=500), and report the fraction of query cells with correlation > 0.4 against a PCA-only baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query contains a genuinely novel cell population absent from the reference — the article notes mapping metrics may be less informative when the novel population is very similar to an existing reference population, and Symphony does not supplant de novo query-only analysis for novel cell type discovery. When the reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage (Condition I), since equivalence with de novo Harmony integration is then not expected.

skills.description: Use when you have a low-dimensional cell embedding (e.g., scPhere 'wn' latent coordinates) plus per-cell labels such as embryo collection time, and need a quantitative time-continuity comparison across embedding methods.
skills.name: knn-cross-validated-classification-benchmark
skills.search_text: knn-cross-validated-classification-benchmark Use when you have a low-dimensional cell embedding (e.g., scPhere 'wn' latent coordinates) plus per-cell labels such as embryo collection time, and need a quantitative time-continuity comparison across embedding methods. Input is raw UMI counts or a feature table rather than an existing cell embedding — scPhere must be trained first The dataset has real batch vectors (e.g., patient/health/location like the UC epi example with n_batch=[30, 3, 2]) — use batch-aware scPhere, not the n_batch=0 artificial-batch setup Labels are discrete cell types on a sphere ('vmf') rather than a continuous time course suited to the hyperbolic 'wn' latent space http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Tenfold-cross-validated k-nearest-neighbor classification of embryo time points on a scPhere hyperbolic (Poincaré disk) embedding, benchmarked against t-SNE, UMAP, and PHATE, to test whether the embedding preserves time-continuity structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Tenfold-cross-validated k-nearest-neighbor classification of embryo time points on a scPhere hyperbolic (Poincaré disk) embedding, benchmarked against t-SNE, UMAP, and PHATE, to test whether the embedding preserves time-continuity structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw UMI counts or a feature table rather than an existing cell embedding — scPhere must be trained first The dataset has real batch vectors (e.g., patient/health/location like the UC epi example with n_batch=[30, 3, 2]) — use batch-aware scPhere, not the n_batch=0 artificial-batch setup Labels are discrete cell types on a sphere ('vmf') rather than a continuous time course suited to the hyperbolic 'wn' latent space

skills.description: Use when you must benchmark the k-NN (k = 5) DEG-feature classifier's malignant vs non-malignant performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, AUROC) within the five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets under 10-fold cross-validation.
skills.name: knn-cross-validation-classification
skills.search_text: knn-cross-validation-classification Use when you must benchmark the k-NN (k = 5) DEG-feature classifier's malignant vs non-malignant performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, AUROC) within the five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets under 10-fold cross-validation. Predicting labels for a new (test) single-cell dataset rather than measuring training-set performance — use the standard majority-vote PreCanCell_classifier() prediction workflow instead. Input is raw unnormalized counts or a matrix without gene rownames — PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix (any library-depth normalization such as TPM or CPM) with rownames being genes and colnames being cells. The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cross-validates PreCanCell's k-NN (k = 5) malignant vs non-malignant classifier within each of the five cancer training scRNA-seq datasets (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC), using the shared DEGs (73 TMGs and 186 NMGs) as [0,1]-min-max-scaled features. Reports 10-fold cross-validated accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, and AUROC, all expected to exceed 0.90 per training dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Cross-validates PreCanCell's k-NN (k = 5) malignant vs non-malignant classifier within each of the five cancer training scRNA-seq datasets (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC), using the shared DEGs (73 TMGs and 186 NMGs) as [0,1]-min-max-scaled features. Reports 10-fold cross-validated accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, and AUROC, all expected to exceed 0.90 per training dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting labels for a new (test) single-cell dataset rather than measuring training-set performance — use the standard majority-vote PreCanCell_classifier() prediction workflow instead. Input is raw unnormalized counts or a matrix without gene rownames — PreCanCell_data() requires a normalized expression matrix (any library-depth normalization such as TPM or CPM) with rownames being genes and colnames being cells. The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells.

skills.description: Use when projected query cells (e.g. PBMC query mapped onto the DISCO PBMC reference via ProjectNewdata) need a statistical per-cell mapping-quality score before downstream label transfer or filtering.
skills.name: knn-distance-null-distribution-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: knn-distance-null-distribution-permutation-testing Use when projected query cells (e.g. PBMC query mapped onto the DISCO PBMC reference via ProjectNewdata) need a statistical per-cell mapping-quality score before downstream label transfer or filtering. The query has not yet been projected into the reference UMAP space (AddProjQual operates on projected cells, not raw counts) Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — a low quality score there reflects reference incompleteness, not necessarily bad mapping Cross-platform projection with severe depth mismatch (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) — the article reports performance declines in this regime, so distance-based quality metrics may be miscalibrated http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 ProjectSVR's mapping-quality assessment (AddProjQual) scores each projected query cell by its mean k-nearest-neighbour distance (mean.knn.dist, k=20) in the reference UMAP space, builds a null distribution by repeatedly computing the mean distance of K randomly selected cells (repeats = 1e4), and derives empirical p-values with Benjamini–Hochberg correction (mapQ.p.val, mapQ.p.adj) to flag poorly mapped cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: ProjectSVR's mapping-quality assessment (AddProjQual) scores each projected query cell by its mean k-nearest-neighbour distance (mean.knn.dist, k=20) in the reference UMAP space, builds a null distribution by repeatedly computing the mean distance of K randomly selected cells (repeats = 1e4), and derives empirical p-values with Benjamini–Hochberg correction (mapQ.p.val, mapQ.p.adj) to flag poorly mapped cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query has not yet been projected into the reference UMAP space (AddProjQual operates on projected cells, not raw counts) Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — a low quality score there reflects reference incompleteness, not necessarily bad mapping Cross-platform projection with severe depth mismatch (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x) — the article reports performance declines in this regime, so distance-based quality metrics may be miscalibrated

skills.description: Use when you need to label individual cells in a normalized scRNA-seq matrix (genes as rownames, cells as colnames) as malignant or non-malignant, especially when you have no annotated training cohort of your own, since five pretrained k-NN (k = 5) classifiers are shipped.
skills.name: knn-ensemble-cell-classification
skills.search_text: knn-ensemble-cell-classification Use when you need to label individual cells in a normalized scRNA-seq matrix (genes as rownames, cells as colnames) as malignant or non-malignant, especially when you have no annotated training cohort of your own, since five pretrained k-NN (k = 5) classifiers are shipped. The goal is fine-grained annotation of non-malignant subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial cell types) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells and is not designed for identifying non-cancer subpopulations. The input matrix is raw counts that have not been library-depth normalized — PreCanCell_data() expects normalized expression values (e.g., TPM, CPM). The input is bulk RNA-seq (e.g., TCGA/CCLE/GDSC expression profiles) — the k-NN classifiers are trained on single-cell transcriptomes and target per-cell annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Ensemble binary cell-state classification from single-cell transcriptomes (PreCanCell): a normalized expression matrix is restricted to the shared DEG set (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) from five cancer training datasets, min-max scaled to [0,1], and each cell is labeled cancer/non_cancer by the majority vote of five k-NN (k = 5) classifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Ensemble binary cell-state classification from single-cell transcriptomes (PreCanCell): a normalized expression matrix is restricted to the shared DEG set (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) from five cancer training datasets, min-max scaled to [0,1], and each cell is labeled cancer/non_cancer by the majority vote of five k-NN (k = 5) classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is fine-grained annotation of non-malignant subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial cell types) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells and is not designed for identifying non-cancer subpopulations. The input matrix is raw counts that have not been library-depth normalized — PreCanCell_data() expects normalized expression values (e.g., TPM, CPM). The input is bulk RNA-seq (e.g., TCGA/CCLE/GDSC expression profiles) — the k-NN classifiers are trained on single-cell transcriptomes and target per-cell annotation.

skills.description: Use when classifying cells from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) as cancer vs non-cancer, and per-cell voting frequencies (freq_cancer/freq_non_cancer) are needed for downstream accuracy/sensitivity/AUROC evaluation.
skills.name: knn-ensemble-majority-voting
skills.search_text: knn-ensemble-majority-voting Use when classifying cells from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) as cancer vs non-cancer, and per-cell voting frequencies (freq_cancer/freq_non_cancer) are needed for downstream accuracy/sensitivity/AUROC evaluation. The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells only The input is raw counts rather than a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM/CPM) — PreCanCell_data() expects depth-normalized values Training-set performance is claimed as unbiased — the reported training-set accuracy is overestimated because the predicted sets were involved in feature selection (DEG identification) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 An ensemble classification skill (from PreCanCell) that labels single cells as malignant or non-malignant by running k-NN (k=5) five times — once per cancer training dataset (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC) — over a 259-gene DEG panel (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) and taking the majority vote. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: An ensemble classification skill (from PreCanCell) that labels single cells as malignant or non-malignant by running k-NN (k=5) five times — once per cancer training dataset (T1_RCC, T2_HNSCC, T3_Melanoma, T4_LUAD, T5_BC) — over a 259-gene DEG panel (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) and taking the majority vote.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — the algorithm is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells only The input is raw counts rather than a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM/CPM) — PreCanCell_data() expects depth-normalized values Training-set performance is claimed as unbiased — the reported training-set accuracy is overestimated because the predicted sets were involved in feature selection (DEG identification)

skills.description: Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix must be classified as malignant vs non-malignant using PreCanCell's five-dataset k-NN (k=5) ensemble with majority vote over common DEG features.
skills.name: knn-ensemble-model-training
skills.search_text: knn-ensemble-model-training Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix must be classified as malignant vs non-malignant using PreCanCell's five-dataset k-NN (k=5) ensemble with majority vote over common DEG features. The goal is to identify subpopulations of non-cancer cells (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells You want to train custom models on your own labeled data — use the package's Custom_preprocessing()/Custom_classifier() path with a CustomDataList instead of the five-dataset ensemble The input matrix is raw counts, not library-depth normalized (TPM/CPM) — PreCanCell_data() expects a normalized expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reconstructs PreCanCell's ensemble classifier: train one k-NN (k=5) base classifier on each of five cancer single-cell transcriptome training datasets (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) using the common DEGs (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) as features, then assign a malignant/non-malignant label by majority vote of the five base results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Reconstructs PreCanCell's ensemble classifier: train one k-NN (k=5) base classifier on each of five cancer single-cell transcriptome training datasets (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) using the common DEGs (73 TMGs + 186 NMGs) as features, then assign a malignant/non-malignant label by majority vote of the five base results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify subpopulations of non-cancer cells (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells You want to train custom models on your own labeled data — use the package's Custom_preprocessing()/Custom_classifier() path with a CustomDataList instead of the five-dataset ensemble The input matrix is raw counts, not library-depth normalized (TPM/CPM) — PreCanCell_data() expects a normalized expression matrix

skills.description: Use when deconvolving spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium spots) with a trained SpatialDDLS model and you want neighbor-aware, spatially regularized cell type proportions for each spot.
skills.name: knn-extrinsic-profile-simulation
skills.search_text: knn-extrinsic-profile-simulation Use when deconvolving spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium spots) with a trained SpatialDDLS model and you want neighbor-aware, spatially regularized cell type proportions for each spot. Datasets where the spatial continuity assumption does not hold (e.g. disorganized or dissociated spatial architecture) — spatial regularization is optional and may mislead Deconvolution tasks on bulk RNA-seq or non-spatial single-cell data with no spot coordinates, since no k-nearest spots exist When only unregularized intrinsic per-spot predictions are desired, extrinsic simulation adds unnecessary computation Simulates extrinsic transcriptional profiles for each spatial transcriptomics spot from its k-nearest neighbouring spots (k.spots = 6) and uses a trained SpatialDDLS neural network to predict extrinsic cell type proportions, which then spatially regularize the intrinsic per-spot predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae072
skills.summary: Simulates extrinsic transcriptional profiles for each spatial transcriptomics spot from its k-nearest neighbouring spots (k.spots = 6) and uses a trained SpatialDDLS neural network to predict extrinsic cell type proportions, which then spatially regularize the intrinsic per-spot predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets where the spatial continuity assumption does not hold (e.g. disorganized or dissociated spatial architecture) — spatial regularization is optional and may mislead Deconvolution tasks on bulk RNA-seq or non-spatial single-cell data with no spot coordinates, since no k-nearest spots exist When only unregularized intrinsic per-spot predictions are desired, extrinsic simulation adds unnecessary computation

skills.description: Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell trajectory (e.g., DTFLOW pseudotime with root cell indices) must be split into sub-branches at bifurcation points, and existing tools detect only a single bifurcation.
skills.name: knn-graph-branch-detection
skills.search_text: knn-graph-branch-detection Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell trajectory (e.g., DTFLOW pseudotime with root cell indices) must be split into sub-branches at bifurcation points, and existing tools detect only a single bifurcation. When only a single bifurcation point is expected and a simpler branching method suffices — RSKG targets multi-branching processes with multiple bifurcation events When the data are already a completed, independently validated branch/cluster assignment table rather than a pseudotime-ordered trajectory requiring branch discovery When no defensible root cell or root list can be supplied, since RSKG reverse-searches the kNN graph in decreasing pseudotime order anchored at root cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Implements DTFLOW's Reverse Searching on the k-nearest neighbor graph (RSKG) to identify multi-branching processes of cellular differentiation, including multiple bifurcation events, along a pseudotime trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Implements DTFLOW's Reverse Searching on the k-nearest neighbor graph (RSKG) to identify multi-branching processes of cellular differentiation, including multiple bifurcation events, along a pseudotime trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single bifurcation point is expected and a simpler branching method suffices — RSKG targets multi-branching processes with multiple bifurcation events When the data are already a completed, independently validated branch/cluster assignment table rather than a pseudotime-ordered trajectory requiring branch discovery When no defensible root cell or root list can be supplied, since RSKG reverse-searches the kNN graph in decreasing pseudotime order anchored at root cells

skills.description: Use when you need to test how sensitive an automated terminal-state/fate-detection method (VIA) is to graph parameters (KNN, ncomps) on a small annotated scRNA-seq hematopoiesis dataset, or to recover rare dendritic lineages and validate them by marker gene trends.
skills.name: knn-graph-clustering-hematopoiesis-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: knn-graph-clustering-hematopoiesis-scrna-seq Use when you need to test how sensitive an automated terminal-state/fate-detection method (VIA) is to graph parameters (KNN, ncomps) on a small annotated scRNA-seq hematopoiesis dataset, or to recover rare dendritic lineages and validate them by marker gene trends. Input is not an annotated single-cell dataset with a known root population — the F1 benchmarking requires ground-truth lineage labels and a valid early start cell. Trajectory topology is disconnected or cyclic and needs multiple roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected with preserve_disconnected=True instead of the standard wrapper. Dataset is large (10^5-10^6+ cells) where the goal is scalability rather than rare-lineage recovery on a small 5800-cell benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark robustness of VIA's automated terminal-state detection on the Setty 5800-cell human CD34+ hematopoiesis scRNA-seq dataset by sweeping KNN neighborhood size and number of PCs, scoring per-lineage F1 against ground-truth annotations (cDC, pDC, megakaryocyte, erythroid, monocyte, B-cell), and validating rare DC lineages with IRF8, CSF1R and CD123 marker-pseudotime trends. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Benchmark robustness of VIA's automated terminal-state detection on the Setty 5800-cell human CD34+ hematopoiesis scRNA-seq dataset by sweeping KNN neighborhood size and number of PCs, scoring per-lineage F1 against ground-truth annotations (cDC, pDC, megakaryocyte, erythroid, monocyte, B-cell), and validating rare DC lineages with IRF8, CSF1R and CD123 marker-pseudotime trends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not an annotated single-cell dataset with a known root population — the F1 benchmarking requires ground-truth lineage labels and a valid early start cell. Trajectory topology is disconnected or cyclic and needs multiple roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected with preserve_disconnected=True instead of the standard wrapper. Dataset is large (10^5-10^6+ cells) where the goal is scalability rather than rare-lineage recovery on a small 5800-cell benchmark.

skills.description: Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g., scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on local smoothness of their velocity fields, or when a kNN neighborhood structure over cells is needed for neighborhood-aggregated metrics.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g., scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on local smoothness of their velocity fields, or when a kNN neighborhood structure over cells is needed for neighborhood-aggregated metrics. The task is to infer velocities from spliced/unspliced counts rather than to evaluate already-inferred velocity fields. The comparison target is a global trajectory metric rather than neighborhood-level velocity concordance among cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct a k-nearest-neighbor graph (k=30) over single-cell transcriptomic embeddings with scanpy, then score each cell's velocity local inconsistency as the mean cosine distance between its velocity vector and those of its 30 nearest neighbors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Construct a k-nearest-neighbor graph (k=30) over single-cell transcriptomic embeddings with scanpy, then score each cell's velocity local inconsistency as the mean cosine distance between its velocity vector and those of its 30 nearest neighbors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to infer velocities from spliced/unspliced counts rather than to evaluate already-inferred velocity fields. The comparison target is a global trajectory metric rather than neighborhood-level velocity concordance among cells.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF expression matrix exceeds ~100k cells (e.g. 1.3M-cell 10X mouse brain data) and a neighbourhood structure is needed for triplet-based dimensionality reduction where scikit-learn Barnes-Hut t-SNE would not finish within 24 hours.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-for-million-scale-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-for-million-scale-scrnaseq Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF expression matrix exceeds ~100k cells (e.g. 1.3M-cell 10X mouse brain data) and a neighbourhood structure is needed for triplet-based dimensionality reduction where scikit-learn Barnes-Hut t-SNE would not finish within 24 hours. Dataset is already a low-dimensional embedding or a precomputed distance/similarity matrix rather than a raw single-cell expression matrix Small datasets (e.g. iris, MNIST 70k, or Levine 265k CyTOF cells) where standard ivis k values suffice and million-scale hyperparameters (k=15–150) are unnecessary The goal is supervised classification of cell populations rather than scalable neighbourhood graph construction for unsupervised dimensionality reduction http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a k-nearest-neighbour neighbourhood graph over a million-scale single-cell expression matrix (e.g. the 1.3M-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain dataset) to drive ivis triplet sampling, where positives are drawn from the KNN vector and negatives from outside it, enabling linearly-scaling dimensionality reduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Constructs a k-nearest-neighbour neighbourhood graph over a million-scale single-cell expression matrix (e.g. the 1.3M-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain dataset) to drive ivis triplet sampling, where positives are drawn from the KNN vector and negatives from outside it, enabling linearly-scaling dimensionality reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is already a low-dimensional embedding or a precomputed distance/similarity matrix rather than a raw single-cell expression matrix Small datasets (e.g. iris, MNIST 70k, or Levine 265k CyTOF cells) where standard ivis k values suffice and million-scale hyperparameters (k=15–150) are unnecessary The goal is supervised classification of cell populations rather than scalable neighbourhood graph construction for unsupervised dimensionality reduction

skills.description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data need a cell-state DAG (not just a clustering or trajectory) so that Granger causal locus-gene inference can be run over an acyclic cell ordering.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-from-cell-embeddings
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-from-cell-embeddings Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data need a cell-state DAG (not just a clustering or trajectory) so that Granger causal locus-gene inference can be run over an acyclic cell ordering. The data are not paired multimodal single-cell observations from a dynamic process (e.g. differentiation or disease) — pseudotime orientation requires a dynamic biological process to provide temporal context You only need cell clustering or visualization, not a directed acyclic structure for causal inference — a plain undirected kNN graph suffices Cells lack a biologically meaningful root cell type, making diffusion pseudotime rooting and edge orientation unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of cell states by building a k-nearest-neighbor graph over Schema-derived joint RNA+ATAC cell embeddings and orienting each edge by diffusion pseudotime, providing the DAG structure GrID-Net requires for Granger causal inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Constructs a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of cell states by building a k-nearest-neighbor graph over Schema-derived joint RNA+ATAC cell embeddings and orienting each edge by diffusion pseudotime, providing the DAG structure GrID-Net requires for Granger causal inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not paired multimodal single-cell observations from a dynamic process (e.g. differentiation or disease) — pseudotime orientation requires a dynamic biological process to provide temporal context You only need cell clustering or visualization, not a directed acyclic structure for causal inference — a plain undirected kNN graph suffices Cells lack a biologically meaningful root cell type, making diffusion pseudotime rooting and edge orientation unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (e.g., Cassiopeia Newick with cells as leaves) plus expression data and need a cell-neighborhood metric for phylogenetic autocorrelation with Hotspot.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-from-cophenetic-distances
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-from-cophenetic-distances Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (e.g., Cassiopeia Newick with cells as leaves) plus expression data and need a cell-neighborhood metric for phylogenetic autocorrelation with Hotspot. No reliable lineage/phylogeny exists for the cells — a transcriptional latent space (e.g., PCA) or spatial coordinates should define the cell metric instead The tree has not been pruned to the analyzed clone and unifurcations collapsed (collapse.singles), so cophenetic distances would be distorted or leaf names would not match expression barcodes The goal is signature-level enrichment scoring only (VISION-style Geary's C on user signatures) rather than de novo Hotspot gene module discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds the cell-similarity graph that Hotspot uses for heritable gene module detection by computing a K-nearest-neighbor graph (n_neighbors=30, unweighted) from cophenetic distances on a Cassiopeia-reconstructed phylogeny, after pruning cells and collapsing unifurcations with collapse.singles (R ape). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Builds the cell-similarity graph that Hotspot uses for heritable gene module detection by computing a K-nearest-neighbor graph (n_neighbors=30, unweighted) from cophenetic distances on a Cassiopeia-reconstructed phylogeny, after pruning cells and collapsing unifurcations with collapse.singles (R ape).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable lineage/phylogeny exists for the cells — a transcriptional latent space (e.g., PCA) or spatial coordinates should define the cell metric instead The tree has not been pruned to the analyzed clone and unifurcations collapsed (collapse.singles), so cophenetic distances would be distorted or leaf names would not match expression barcodes The goal is signature-level enrichment scoring only (VISION-style Geary's C on user signatures) rather than de novo Hotspot gene module discovery

skills.description: Use when you need a subpopulation-aware network over single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., hematopoietic progenitor snapshots) so that trajectory search between any chosen source and target subpopulations, including rare cell types, can be performed.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-from-embeddings
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-from-embeddings Use when you need a subpopulation-aware network over single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., hematopoietic progenitor snapshots) so that trajectory search between any chosen source and target subpopulations, including rare cell types, can be performed. The goal is a simple linear pseudotime ordering of cells (e.g., Monocle 1 / Waterfall-style) rather than multi-state transitions between chosen subpopulations Only a single branch point needs to be identified and the number of fates is known a priori (Wishbone/DPT-style analyses) The analysis goal is pseudotemporal ordering via diffusion pseudotime as in the theislab/scAnalysisTutorial, not subpopulation-aware flow-network trajectories http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Build a k-nearest-neighbor graph over dimensionality-reduced single-cell embeddings, convert kNN edges into Jaccard similarity-weighted igraph edges, and use community detection on this graph to define subpopulations that CellRouter's flow-network trajectory search operates on. This graph representation is what enables trajectory reconstruction between any two subpopulations, including rare or intermediate cell states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Build a k-nearest-neighbor graph over dimensionality-reduced single-cell embeddings, convert kNN edges into Jaccard similarity-weighted igraph edges, and use community detection on this graph to define subpopulations that CellRouter's flow-network trajectory search operates on. This graph representation is what enables trajectory reconstruction between any two subpopulations, including rare or intermediate cell states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a simple linear pseudotime ordering of cells (e.g., Monocle 1 / Waterfall-style) rather than multi-state transitions between chosen subpopulations Only a single branch point needs to be identified and the number of fates is known a priori (Wishbone/DPT-style analyses) The analysis goal is pseudotemporal ordering via diffusion pseudotime as in the theislab/scAnalysisTutorial, not subpopulation-aware flow-network trajectories

skills.description: Use when you need a cell-cell similarity graph for label propagation or GNN classification on scRNA-seq data, and cells are represented as PCA-reduced expression embeddings.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-from-pca-embeddings
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-from-pca-embeddings Use when you need a cell-cell similarity graph for label propagation or GNN classification on scRNA-seq data, and cells are represented as PCA-reduced expression embeddings. Input is raw counts without a dimensionality-reduction step — the README instructs users to 'input raw counts' to scSHARP, which computes its own embeddings; feeding a pre-built unrelated graph bypasses this pipeline. The goal is the GCN consensus model itself rather than the nonparametric neighbor-majority baseline or graph construction for it. Single-cell data is not expression-based (e.g. image or spatial-only modalities) where PCA over transcriptomic profiles is not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a k-nearest-neighbor graph over single-cell PCA embeddings using pytorch-cluster, with batched processing to keep memory bounded, as the graph substrate for neighbor-majority label propagation and GCN-based cell type annotation in scSHARP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Builds a k-nearest-neighbor graph over single-cell PCA embeddings using pytorch-cluster, with batched processing to keep memory bounded, as the graph substrate for neighbor-majority label propagation and GCN-based cell type annotation in scSHARP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts without a dimensionality-reduction step — the README instructs users to 'input raw counts' to scSHARP, which computes its own embeddings; feeding a pre-built unrelated graph bypasses this pipeline. The goal is the GCN consensus model itself rather than the nonparametric neighbor-majority baseline or graph construction for it. Single-cell data is not expression-based (e.g. image or spatial-only modalities) where PCA over transcriptomic profiles is not meaningful.

skills.description: Use when a precomputed cell-by-cell similarity matrix (e.g., EDGE's averaged weak-learner matrix S) must be converted into a k-NNG before spectral embedding or graph-based dimensionality reduction.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-from-similarity-matrix
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-from-similarity-matrix Use when a precomputed cell-by-cell similarity matrix (e.g., EDGE's averaged weak-learner matrix S) must be converted into a k-NNG before spectral embedding or graph-based dimensionality reduction. Input is raw or unnormalized counts rather than the log2-transformed normalized expression matrix and ensemble similarity matrix — EDGE's similarity learning and graph construction assume normalized data The goal is embedding directly from raw expression profiles without a cell-to-cell similarity structure (e.g., running UMAP or t-SNE from scratch on dat_log instead of graphing S) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds a k-nearest-neighbor graph from EDGE's ensemble similarity matrix S, using the top-n_neigs weighted neighbors per cell, to serve as the substrate for spectral embedding of scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Builds a k-nearest-neighbor graph from EDGE's ensemble similarity matrix S, using the top-n_neigs weighted neighbors per cell, to serve as the substrate for spectral embedding of scRNA-seq data.
