skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw or unnormalized counts rather than the log2-transformed normalized expression matrix and ensemble similarity matrix — EDGE's similarity learning and graph construction assume normalized data The goal is embedding directly from raw expression profiles without a cell-to-cell similarity structure (e.g., running UMAP or t-SNE from scratch on dat_log instead of graphing S)

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-processed N-cell × D-gene expression matrix and need a cell-to-cell transition probability graph (Markov matrix) as input to random walk or diffusion-based trajectory methods.
skills.name: knn-graph-construction-on-single-cell-data
skills.search_text: knn-graph-construction-on-single-cell-data Use when you have a pre-processed N-cell × D-gene expression matrix and need a cell-to-cell transition probability graph (Markov matrix) as input to random walk or diffusion-based trajectory methods. The data are raw counts that have not been pre-processed into a filtered expression matrix (DTFLOW requires a pre-processed X with N cells and D genes first) The downstream task needs gene-level features rather than cell-to-cell transition probabilities (this skill discards gene dimensions by design) You need trajectory branch detection directly (RSKG branch detection via z.get_branches(Num) is a separate skill step, not part of kNN graph construction) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a k-nearest neighbor graph over single cells and converts it into a row-normalized Markov transition matrix (DTFLOW's get_transition_matrix), the substrate for RWR diffusion distributions in pseudotime inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Builds a k-nearest neighbor graph over single cells and converts it into a row-normalized Markov transition matrix (DTFLOW's get_transition_matrix), the substrate for RWR diffusion distributions in pseudotime inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw counts that have not been pre-processed into a filtered expression matrix (DTFLOW requires a pre-processed X with N cells and D genes first) The downstream task needs gene-level features rather than cell-to-cell transition probabilities (this skill discards gene dimensions by design) You need trajectory branch detection directly (RSKG branch detection via z.get_branches(Num) is a separate skill step, not part of kNN graph construction)

skills.description: Use when a labeled single-cell or feature matrix must be turned into a graph whose edges capture both same-class proximity and cross-class density-gradient transitions prior to force-based 2D embedding.
skills.name: knn-graph-edge-construction
skills.search_text: knn-graph-edge-construction Use when a labeled single-cell or feature matrix must be turned into a graph whose edges capture both same-class proximity and cross-class density-gradient transitions prior to force-based 2D embedding. When no prior cluster/class labels are available — both edge types depend on a user-defined label per instance When a continuous pseudotime ordering (not a class-informed trajectory graph) is the primary goal — pseudotime methods like TSCAN or Monocle2 target that directly When instance labels are noisy and compact per-class layouts cannot be forced — the -c separation strength (0.5-30) assumes labels are at least partially trusted http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the two edge types ('knn' and 'k_shift') used by GraphDDP/GraphEmbed to encode cluster membership and density-gradient differentiation pathways in a graph that is then laid out with the Kamada-Kawai force algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Constructs the two edge types ('knn' and 'k_shift') used by GraphDDP/GraphEmbed to encode cluster membership and density-gradient differentiation pathways in a graph that is then laid out with the Kamada-Kawai force algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior cluster/class labels are available — both edge types depend on a user-defined label per instance When a continuous pseudotime ordering (not a class-informed trajectory graph) is the primary goal — pseudotime methods like TSCAN or Monocle2 target that directly When instance labels are noisy and compact per-class layouts cannot be forced — the -c separation strength (0.5-30) assumes labels are at least partially trusted

skills.description: Use when you need a class-label-agnostic baseline visualization of single-cell expression data that mixes clusters, to contrast with class-informed graph embeddings like GraphDDP.
skills.name: knn-graph-layout-visualization
skills.search_text: knn-graph-layout-visualization Use when you need a class-label-agnostic baseline visualization of single-cell expression data that mixes clusters, to contrast with class-informed graph embeddings like GraphDDP. The goal is trajectory/pseudotime ordering rather than a 2D layout baseline — a pseudotime method like TSCAN or Monocle2 is the appropriate comparison Data are raw reads or lack per-cell class labels, since the graph construction expects a discrete label per instance and a data matrix in CSV format http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds SPRING-style k-nearest-neighbor force layouts on single-cell expression data, with and without a class-contraction prior, to serve as the baseline against which GraphDDP's informed 2D embedding is judged. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Builds SPRING-style k-nearest-neighbor force layouts on single-cell expression data, with and without a class-contraction prior, to serve as the baseline against which GraphDDP's informed 2D embedding is judged.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is trajectory/pseudotime ordering rather than a 2D layout baseline — a pseudotime method like TSCAN or Monocle2 is the appropriate comparison Data are raw reads or lack per-cell class labels, since the graph construction expects a discrete label per instance and a data matrix in CSV format

skills.description: Use when cell/gene feature embeddings (e.g. from tGPT) must be clustered into groups and quantitatively compared with known cell type annotations using NMI, ARI, and FMI metrics.
skills.name: knn-graph-leiden-clustering
skills.search_text: knn-graph-leiden-clustering Use when cell/gene feature embeddings (e.g. from tGPT) must be clustered into groups and quantitatively compared with known cell type annotations using NMI, ARI, and FMI metrics. Input is already a cluster assignment or metric table — no feature extraction or graph clustering is needed Data has not been reduced to top-expressing gene rankings (tGPT takes expression rankings of top-expressing genes, not raw counts or normalized expression levels) No ground-truth cell type labels exist — external metrics NMI/ARI/FMI cannot be computed, so the grid-search evaluation component is inapplicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a KNN neighbor graph on tGPT feature representations and clusters cells with Leiden, evaluating NMI/ARI/FMI against ground-truth cell type labels. It reproduces the clustering-performance evaluation of the tGPT transformer model across single-cell and bulk tissue datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Builds a KNN neighbor graph on tGPT feature representations and clusters cells with Leiden, evaluating NMI/ARI/FMI against ground-truth cell type labels. It reproduces the clustering-performance evaluation of the tGPT transformer model across single-cell and bulk tissue datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cluster assignment or metric table — no feature extraction or graph clustering is needed Data has not been reduced to top-expressing gene rankings (tGPT takes expression rankings of top-expressing genes, not raw counts or normalized expression levels) No ground-truth cell type labels exist — external metrics NMI/ARI/FMI cannot be computed, so the grid-search evaluation component is inapplicable

skills.description: Use when you have extracted per-cell latent factors from a multi-omics integration model (e.g. scMoMaT extract_cell_factors) and need discrete cluster labels plus a 2D UMAP visualization to interpret populations.
skills.name: knn-graph-leiden-clustering-single-cell
skills.search_text: knn-graph-leiden-clustering-single-cell Use when you have extracted per-cell latent factors from a multi-omics integration model (e.g. scMoMaT extract_cell_factors) and need discrete cluster labels plus a 2D UMAP visualization to interpret populations. Cells do not come from a shared integrated embedding — clustering raw per-batch count matrices will not remove batch effects The analysis goal is sub-clustering within already-annotated cell types at finer resolution than 0.9 provides, without re-tuning resolution Input is already a cluster label table or annotation (no embedding to graph-ify) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds a shared k-nearest-neighbor graph from integrated single-cell embeddings (e.g. scMoMaT cell factors) and clusters it with the Leiden algorithm to obtain cell populations for downstream annotation and marker-based interpretation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Builds a shared k-nearest-neighbor graph from integrated single-cell embeddings (e.g. scMoMaT cell factors) and clusters it with the Leiden algorithm to obtain cell populations for downstream annotation and marker-based interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells do not come from a shared integrated embedding — clustering raw per-batch count matrices will not remove batch effects The analysis goal is sub-clustering within already-annotated cell types at finer resolution than 0.9 provides, without re-tuning resolution Input is already a cluster label table or annotation (no embedding to graph-ify)

skills.description: Use when you have extracted cell factors (zs) from a first-stage scMoMaT model and need a KNN graph plus Leiden cluster labels for benchmarking (NMI/ARI/GC) or for second-stage retraining.
skills.name: knn-graph-post-processing
skills.search_text: knn-graph-post-processing Use when you have extracted cell factors (zs) from a first-stage scMoMaT model and need a KNN graph plus Leiden cluster labels for benchmarking (NMI/ARI/GC) or for second-stage retraining. The goal is to obtain cluster-specific biomarkers — that requires the second-stage scmomat_retrain step with labels and extract_feature_factors(), not the KNN post-processing alone. The input is a precomputed distance or adjacency graph rather than raw cell factor embeddings — post_process expects the zs cell factors directly. The analysis needs cross-batch cell factor alignment rather than neighborhood construction (e.g. consider alternative alignment methods such as LIGER's centroidAlign). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Post-process scMoMaT first-stage cell factors into a shared-neighbor KNN graph and Leiden-cluster it to obtain cell labels. This step converts the latent embedding (zs) into discrete clustering labels that are evaluated with NMI, ARI, and graph connectivity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Post-process scMoMaT first-stage cell factors into a shared-neighbor KNN graph and Leiden-cluster it to obtain cell labels. This step converts the latent embedding (zs) into discrete clustering labels that are evaluated with NMI, ARI, and graph connectivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to obtain cluster-specific biomarkers — that requires the second-stage scmomat_retrain step with labels and extract_feature_factors(), not the KNN post-processing alone. The input is a precomputed distance or adjacency graph rather than raw cell factor embeddings — post_process expects the zs cell factors directly. The analysis needs cross-batch cell factor alignment rather than neighborhood construction (e.g. consider alternative alignment methods such as LIGER's centroidAlign).

skills.description: Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (with scVelo/velocyto spliced-unspliced velocity) contains multiple or branching trajectories whose direction and topology cannot be resolved by expression-only TI methods.
skills.name: knn-graph-trajectory-path-finding
skills.search_text: knn-graph-trajectory-path-finding Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (with scVelo/velocyto spliced-unspliced velocity) contains multiple or branching trajectories whose direction and topology cannot be resolved by expression-only TI methods. Velocity estimates are unreliable or unavailable — the paper notes all RNA velocity-based methods are limited by the accuracy of RNA velocity inference Only a single pre-defined linear backbone is needed and expression-based methods (e.g., Slingshot, PAGA) suffice A cluster-level global trajectory graph is sufficient; Directed-PAGA-style outputs are more appropriate than high-resolution local paths http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs k-nearest-neighbor graphs on smoothed meta-cells derived from scRNA-seq counts and RNA velocity, then enumerates and greedily selects major trajectories to infer high-resolution, directed cell paths with pseudotime — the core trajectory inference engine of CellPath. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Constructs k-nearest-neighbor graphs on smoothed meta-cells derived from scRNA-seq counts and RNA velocity, then enumerates and greedily selects major trajectories to infer high-resolution, directed cell paths with pseudotime — the core trajectory inference engine of CellPath.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Velocity estimates are unreliable or unavailable — the paper notes all RNA velocity-based methods are limited by the accuracy of RNA velocity inference Only a single pre-defined linear backbone is needed and expression-based methods (e.g., Slingshot, PAGA) suffice A cluster-level global trajectory graph is sufficient; Directed-PAGA-style outputs are more appropriate than high-resolution local paths

skills.description: Use when comparing imputation methods for highly sparse APA ratio (RUD) matrices from spatially barcoded ST data, e.g. deciding whether stAPAminer's k-nearest-neighbor imputation or scDaPars better recovers APA signals.
skills.name: knn-imputation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: knn-imputation-benchmarking Use when comparing imputation methods for highly sparse APA ratio (RUD) matrices from spatially barcoded ST data, e.g. deciding whether stAPAminer's k-nearest-neighbor imputation or scDaPars better recovers APA signals. Input is already an imputed or dense APA ratio matrix — benchmarking only makes sense on the raw, sparse RUD matrix prior to imputation Data are non-spatial single-cell or image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools such as scAPAtrap or Sierra The goal is APA site discovery rather than imputation benchmarking — use the upstream scAPAtrap/Sierra PA-extraction pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks stAPAminer's KNN-based imputation of sparse spatial APA usage (RUD) matrices against scDaPars imputation on mouse olfactory bulb (MOB) ST data, scoring both by within-layer spot correlations and Seurat-based clustering quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Benchmarks stAPAminer's KNN-based imputation of sparse spatial APA usage (RUD) matrices against scDaPars imputation on mouse olfactory bulb (MOB) ST data, scoring both by within-layer spot correlations and Seurat-based clustering quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an imputed or dense APA ratio matrix — benchmarking only makes sense on the raw, sparse RUD matrix prior to imputation Data are non-spatial single-cell or image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools such as scAPAtrap or Sierra The goal is APA site discovery rather than imputation benchmarking — use the upstream scAPAtrap/Sierra PA-extraction pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset contains unwanted biological variation (e.g., cell cycle, sex) that can be encoded by curated marker gene lists, and you need a cell-cell similarity kernel for SiFT gene-level filtering or covariate scores for regress_out/scVI baselines.
skills.name: knn-kernel-construction-from-marker-genes
skills.search_text: knn-kernel-construction-from-marker-genes Use when a scRNA-seq dataset contains unwanted biological variation (e.g., cell cycle, sex) that can be encoded by curated marker gene lists, and you need a cell-cell similarity kernel for SiFT gene-level filtering or covariate scores for regress_out/scVI baselines. The signal to filter cannot be encoded by prior-knowledge marker genes or a known mapping — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal. You only need latent-space batch integration without gene-level correction — scVI-style joint latent representation may be more appropriate since most integration methods correct at the latent level. Downstream analysis strictly requires properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so data is no longer properly log-transformed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a probabilistic k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell similarity kernel using marker gene lists (e.g., cell-cycle and sex markers) as the signal encoding, for use as the kernel argument in SiFT's projection-based filtering of unwanted variation from scRNA-seq count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Constructs a probabilistic k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell similarity kernel using marker gene lists (e.g., cell-cycle and sex markers) as the signal encoding, for use as the kernel argument in SiFT's projection-based filtering of unwanted variation from scRNA-seq count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The signal to filter cannot be encoded by prior-knowledge marker genes or a known mapping — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal. You only need latent-space batch integration without gene-level correction — scVI-style joint latent representation may be more appropriate since most integration methods correct at the latent level. Downstream analysis strictly requires properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so data is no longer properly log-transformed.

skills.description: Use when filtering a biological signal from scRNA-seq data via reference mapping — i.e., disease cells must be linked to their nearest healthy reference cells before projection-and-subtraction with SiFT.
skills.name: knn-kernel-construction-in-harmonized-pca-space
skills.search_text: knn-kernel-construction-in-harmonized-pca-space Use when filtering a biological signal from scRNA-seq data via reference mapping — i.e., disease cells must be linked to their nearest healthy reference cells before projection-and-subtraction with SiFT. Disease and healthy cells have not been integrated/batch-corrected into a joint latent space — a coarse or biased mapping may lead to loss of the disease signal No reference population exists that represents the signal to remove (SiFT strongly relies on prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel) The signal of interest is defined by gene attributes rather than cell-cell reference mapping (use distance/RBF/Laplacian kernels or gene kernels instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Construct a k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell similarity kernel in a batch-corrected joint PCA latent space so that query cells (e.g., COVID-19 patient PBMCs) map to reference cells (healthy control PBMCs), encoding the signal to be filtered out by SiFT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Construct a k-nearest-neighbor cell-cell similarity kernel in a batch-corrected joint PCA latent space so that query cells (e.g., COVID-19 patient PBMCs) map to reference cells (healthy control PBMCs), encoding the signal to be filtered out by SiFT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Disease and healthy cells have not been integrated/batch-corrected into a joint latent space — a coarse or biased mapping may lead to loss of the disease signal No reference population exists that represents the signal to remove (SiFT strongly relies on prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel) The signal of interest is defined by gene attributes rather than cell-cell reference mapping (use distance/RBF/Laplacian kernels or gene kernels instead)

skills.description: Use when clusters or labels have been assigned only to a sketched subset of cells (e.g., Sphetcher spherical or geometric sketch) and you need to infer labels for all cells of the original expression/PCA matrix.
skills.name: knn-label-propagation-to-full-dataset
skills.search_text: knn-label-propagation-to-full-dataset Use when clusters or labels have been assigned only to a sketched subset of cells (e.g., Sphetcher spherical or geometric sketch) and you need to infer labels for all cells of the original expression/PCA matrix. Labels already exist for every cell (no sketch-based subsampling was performed), so propagation would only add classifier noise. The sketch labels come from a method whose distance metric is incompatible with the features used for kNN (the paper notes the interplay of sketching distance metric with downstream algorithms was not systematically addressed). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Extends cluster labels computed on a cell sketch (e.g., Louvain communities on Sphetcher's spherical sketch) back to every cell of the original scRNA-seq dataset by training a k-nearest-neighbor classifier on the sketched cells' features, enabling whole-dataset evaluation of sketch quality via Adjusted Rand Index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Extends cluster labels computed on a cell sketch (e.g., Louvain communities on Sphetcher's spherical sketch) back to every cell of the original scRNA-seq dataset by training a k-nearest-neighbor classifier on the sketched cells' features, enabling whole-dataset evaluation of sketch quality via Adjusted Rand Index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels already exist for every cell (no sketch-based subsampling was performed), so propagation would only add classifier noise. The sketch labels come from a method whose distance metric is incompatible with the features used for kNN (the paper notes the interplay of sketching distance metric with downstream algorithms was not systematically addressed).

skills.description: Use when comparing reference mapping methods (e.g. ProjectSVR, Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs) on reference/query pairs where query cells have manually curated labels and you need accuracy/ARI benchmark numbers.
skills.name: knn-label-transfer-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: knn-label-transfer-annotation-accuracy-evaluation Use when comparing reference mapping methods (e.g. ProjectSVR, Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs) on reference/query pairs where query cells have manually curated labels and you need accuracy/ARI benchmark numbers. Query cells lack manually curated ground-truth annotations, so accuracy and ARI against curated labels cannot be computed Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — projections may be misleading and label-transfer accuracy would be artificially low The goal is reference-model construction or gene-set scoring rather than post-mapping evaluation of label transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates reference-mapping methods by transferring cell-type labels from the reference to mapped query cells via k-NN (k=10) and scoring per-cell-type annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) against manually curated query annotations, as done in the ProjectSVR benchmark (Table 2, Fig. 3). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Evaluates reference-mapping methods by transferring cell-type labels from the reference to mapped query cells via k-NN (k=10) and scoring per-cell-type annotation accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI) against manually curated query annotations, as done in the ProjectSVR benchmark (Table 2, Fig. 3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells lack manually curated ground-truth annotations, so accuracy and ARI against curated labels cannot be computed Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — projections may be misleading and label-transfer accuracy would be artificially low The goal is reference-model construction or gene-set scoring rather than post-mapping evaluation of label transfer

skills.description: Use when you have uniPort latent embeddings from two heterogeneous single-cell datasets (e.g. scATAC gene activity vs scRNA) and need quantitative ARI+NMI+F1 and Silhouette metrics to judge integration quality, including unbalanced-matching cases where cell types are missing from one modality.
skills.name: knn-label-transfer-evaluation
skills.search_text: knn-label-transfer-evaluation Use when you have uniPort latent embeddings from two heterogeneous single-cell datasets (e.g. scATAC gene activity vs scRNA) and need quantitative ARI+NMI+F1 and Silhouette metrics to judge integration quality, including unbalanced-matching cases where cell types are missing from one modality. Input data are already paired/vertical integration of the same cells, where label transfer via UOT mapping is unnecessary The goal is deconvolution of spatial transcriptomic data using the OT plan itself rather than embedding-space label transfer metrics Reference cell-type annotations are absent, since the kNN classifier requires labeled reference cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluate uniPort-integrated single-cell multi-omics embeddings by training a k-Nearest-Neighbor classifier (sklearn.neighbors.KNeighborsClassifier) on reference cell-type annotations and UMAP coordinates, then computing ARI, NMI, and F1 label-transfer scores plus Silhouette coefficients on the shared latent space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Evaluate uniPort-integrated single-cell multi-omics embeddings by training a k-Nearest-Neighbor classifier (sklearn.neighbors.KNeighborsClassifier) on reference cell-type annotations and UMAP coordinates, then computing ARI, NMI, and F1 label-transfer scores plus Silhouette coefficients on the shared latent space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already paired/vertical integration of the same cells, where label transfer via UOT mapping is unnecessary The goal is deconvolution of spatial transcriptomic data using the OT plan itself rather than embedding-space label transfer metrics Reference cell-type annotations are absent, since the kNN classifier requires labeled reference cells

skills.description: Use when paired TCR+transcriptome query single-cell studies must be annotated by mapping them into a pre-trained mvTCR reference embedding, and accuracy of kNN label transfer for metadata labels (e.g. cancer source, tissue type) must be quantified against a baseline projection.
skills.name: knn-label-transfer-evaluation
skills.search_text: knn-label-transfer-evaluation Use when paired TCR+transcriptome query single-cell studies must be annotated by mapping them into a pre-trained mvTCR reference embedding, and accuracy of kNN label transfer for metadata labels (e.g. cancer source, tissue type) must be quantified against a baseline projection. Data is unimodal (gene expression or TCR only) — mvTCR's benefit is fusing both modalities; use a unimodal label-transfer tool instead No pre-annotated reference atlas exists — there is no labeled reference embedding to transfer labels from Goal is predicting antigen specificity from specificity annotations rather than transferring metadata labels via reference mapping (use tutorials/03_training_prediction.ipynb instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates whether a conditional mvTCR model combined with scArches architectural surgery improves k-nearest-neighbor label transfer (cancer source, tissue type, cell type) of query cells mapped into a large TIL reference atlas, compared to a non-conditional projection baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a conditional mvTCR model combined with scArches architectural surgery improves k-nearest-neighbor label transfer (cancer source, tissue type, cell type) of query cells mapped into a large TIL reference atlas, compared to a non-conditional projection baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is unimodal (gene expression or TCR only) — mvTCR's benefit is fusing both modalities; use a unimodal label-transfer tool instead No pre-annotated reference atlas exists — there is no labeled reference embedding to transfer labels from Goal is predicting antigen specificity from specificity annotations rather than transferring metadata labels via reference mapping (use tutorials/03_training_prediction.ipynb instead)

skills.description: Use when the scRNA-seq matrix exceeds scCAN's 5,000-cell training threshold and full network fusion on all cells is impractical, but per-cell cluster assignments are still needed for every cell.
skills.name: knn-label-transfer-large-dataset
skills.search_text: knn-label-transfer-large-dataset Use when the scRNA-seq matrix exceeds scCAN's 5,000-cell training threshold and full network fusion on all cells is impractical, but per-cell cluster assignments are still needed for every cell. Dataset has 5,000 or fewer cells — scCAN clusters the full matrix directly without the train/test split (Module 3 is unnecessary) A pre-trained reference annotation exists and only label propagation to a query set is needed — this skill's k-NN step transfers labels only from scCAN's own training-subsample clusters, not from an external reference atlas http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ScCAN's big-data strategy (Module 3): cluster only a random training subsample with network fusion and spectral clustering, then transfer labels to all remaining cells with a k-NN classifier, making autoencoder+SNF clustering tractable for datasets far above the 5,000-cell threshold (e.g. Zilionis, 34,558 cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: ScCAN's big-data strategy (Module 3): cluster only a random training subsample with network fusion and spectral clustering, then transfer labels to all remaining cells with a k-NN classifier, making autoencoder+SNF clustering tractable for datasets far above the 5,000-cell threshold (e.g. Zilionis, 34,558 cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset has 5,000 or fewer cells — scCAN clusters the full matrix directly without the train/test split (Module 3 is unnecessary) A pre-trained reference annotation exists and only label propagation to a query set is needed — this skill's k-NN step transfers labels only from scCAN's own training-subsample clusters, not from an external reference atlas

skills.description: Use when new query datasets have been integrated onto an annotated reference (e.g., a STACAS seed map) and cell subtype labels must be propagated to unlabeled cells using nearest-neighbor voting in the shared embedding.
skills.name: knn-label-transfer-to-reference-atlas
skills.search_text: knn-label-transfer-to-reference-atlas Use when new query datasets have been integrated onto an annotated reference (e.g., a STACAS seed map) and cell subtype labels must be propagated to unlabeled cells using nearest-neighbor voting in the shared embedding. The query data have not been batch-corrected into a shared embedding with the reference — nearest-neighbor voting on uncorrected spaces reflects batch, not biology No trustworthy cell type annotations exist on the reference — the article notes CiLISI-type and label-based approaches require annotations, and semi-supervised STACAS presumes prior labels Cell types of interest are absent from the reference — neighbor voting cannot assign labels for types not represented in the seed map http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Transfers cell subtype annotations from an annotated seed/reference map to newly integrated single-cell datasets by K-nearest-neighbor classification in the integrated embedding (annotate.by.neighbors), enabling label propagation at atlas scale while preserving biological subtype structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Transfers cell subtype annotations from an annotated seed/reference map to newly integrated single-cell datasets by K-nearest-neighbor classification in the integrated embedding (annotate.by.neighbors), enabling label propagation at atlas scale while preserving biological subtype structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data have not been batch-corrected into a shared embedding with the reference — nearest-neighbor voting on uncorrected spaces reflects batch, not biology No trustworthy cell type annotations exist on the reference — the article notes CiLISI-type and label-based approaches require annotations, and semi-supervised STACAS presumes prior labels Cell types of interest are absent from the reference — neighbor voting cannot assign labels for types not represented in the seed map

skills.description: Use when a spot-by-poly(A)-site RUD (relative usage difference) matrix derived from spatially barcoded ST data is too sparse for downstream clustering or spatial-pattern tests, and a companion gene-spot count matrix is available to define spot neighborhoods.
skills.name: knn-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: knn-missing-value-imputation Use when a spot-by-poly(A)-site RUD (relative usage difference) matrix derived from spatially barcoded ST data is too sparse for downstream clustering or spatial-pattern tests, and a companion gene-spot count matrix is available to define spot neighborhoods. Input is image-based ST data (MERFISH/seqFISH): APA sites can currently only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using scRNA-seq tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra There is no companion gene expression count matrix, since spot–spot distances are computed from the expression profile The RUD matrix is already dense, or zero vs. truly missing entries cannot be distinguished — the authors note there is no method to determine whether an entry is truly missing before imputation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 KNN-based imputation of sparse APA usage (RUD) matrices in stAPAminer: spot–spot distances are inferred from the spatial gene expression profile, and missing RUD entries are filled iteratively by borrowing APA usage values from the k nearest spots (default k=10). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: KNN-based imputation of sparse APA usage (RUD) matrices in stAPAminer: spot–spot distances are inferred from the spatial gene expression profile, and missing RUD entries are filled iteratively by borrowing APA usage values from the k nearest spots (default k=10).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is image-based ST data (MERFISH/seqFISH): APA sites can currently only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using scRNA-seq tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra There is no companion gene expression count matrix, since spot–spot distances are computed from the expression profile The RUD matrix is already dense, or zero vs. truly missing entries cannot be distinguished — the authors note there is no method to determine whether an entry is truly missing before imputation

skills.description: Use when quantifying how closely inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data matches real-profiled ground truth across representative counts, e.g. benchmarking scSemiProfiler against a selection-only baseline that merely copies each representative's cells.
skills.name: knn-nearest-neighbor-distance-calculation
skills.search_text: knn-nearest-neighbor-distance-calculation Use when quantifying how closely inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data matches real-profiled ground truth across representative counts, e.g. benchmarking scSemiProfiler against a selection-only baseline that merely copies each representative's cells. Input is bulk-only with no single-cell reference: the per-cell K=1 distance is undefined, and the paper notes the tool's single-cell level deconvolution requires a single-cell reference You only have cell-type-level deconvolution output (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS, EPIC, Scaden, TAPE) - the paper states conventional methods are constrained to cell type level resolution, so per-cell distance cannot be computed Datasets are not cohort-paired (no target-sample-to-representative correspondence), since the random-pairing UB and random-half LB normalization is defined over paired cohort samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Scores single-cell-level agreement between semi-profiled and real-profiled datasets by averaging each cell's Euclidean distance to its K=1 nearest neighbor in a 100-principal-component space (Scikit-learn PCA), then normalizing as EN = (mean_difference - LB) / (UB - LB) with a random-pairing upper bound (UB) and a random-half lower bound (LB). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Scores single-cell-level agreement between semi-profiled and real-profiled datasets by averaging each cell's Euclidean distance to its K=1 nearest neighbor in a 100-principal-component space (Scikit-learn PCA), then normalizing as EN = (mean_difference - LB) / (UB - LB) with a random-pairing upper bound (UB) and a random-half lower bound (LB).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk-only with no single-cell reference: the per-cell K=1 distance is undefined, and the paper notes the tool's single-cell level deconvolution requires a single-cell reference You only have cell-type-level deconvolution output (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS, EPIC, Scaden, TAPE) - the paper states conventional methods are constrained to cell type level resolution, so per-cell distance cannot be computed Datasets are not cohort-paired (no target-sample-to-representative correspondence), since the random-pairing UB and random-half LB normalization is defined over paired cohort samples

skills.description: Use when a velocity or trajectory pipeline needs a cell-neighborhood graph over preprocessed scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. after scvelo pp.filter_and_normalize with top-2000 highly variable genes) to support moment smoothing or local averaging.
skills.name: knn-neighbor-graph-construction
skills.search_text: knn-neighbor-graph-construction Use when a velocity or trajectory pipeline needs a cell-neighborhood graph over preprocessed scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. after scvelo pp.filter_and_normalize with top-2000 highly variable genes) to support moment smoothing or local averaging. The count matrix has not yet been filtered and normalized (scvelo pp.filter_and_normalize is a prerequisite; building the graph on raw counts gives unreliable neighborhoods) The analysis needs splicing-based RNA velocity dynamics rather than a cell graph for TF-expression smoothing — TFvelo's graph step exists to support TF-based dynamics without relying on unspliced/spliced kinetics The input is not a single-cell count AnnData (e.g. bulk or already-aggregated expression tables have no meaningful per-cell neighborhoods) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a k-nearest-neighbor cell graph on filtered/normalized scRNA-seq counts with scvelo pp.neighbors (n_neighbors=30 in TFvelo), providing the connectivity structure over which scvelo pp.moments smooths total (unspliced+spliced) mRNA counts before TF-model fitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Constructs a k-nearest-neighbor cell graph on filtered/normalized scRNA-seq counts with scvelo pp.neighbors (n_neighbors=30 in TFvelo), providing the connectivity structure over which scvelo pp.moments smooths total (unspliced+spliced) mRNA counts before TF-model fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix has not yet been filtered and normalized (scvelo pp.filter_and_normalize is a prerequisite; building the graph on raw counts gives unreliable neighborhoods) The analysis needs splicing-based RNA velocity dynamics rather than a cell graph for TF-expression smoothing — TFvelo's graph step exists to support TF-based dynamics without relying on unspliced/spliced kinetics The input is not a single-cell count AnnData (e.g. bulk or already-aggregated expression tables have no meaningful per-cell neighborhoods)

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix yields a sparse cell-to-cell similarity (e.g., from ADMM-solved sparse subspace representation) whose zero entries must be imputed within K-nearest-neighbor neighborhoods to obtain a dense similarity for spectral clustering.
skills.name: knn-neighbor-graph-construction-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: knn-neighbor-graph-construction-scrna-seq Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix yields a sparse cell-to-cell similarity (e.g., from ADMM-solved sparse subspace representation) whose zero entries must be imputed within K-nearest-neighbor neighborhoods to obtain a dense similarity for spectral clustering. The input similarity matrix is already dense and contains no missing/zero entries to impute The data are very large-scale, since SSRE is reported to be relatively time-consuming on large datasets The task requires single-cell multi-omics integration, which the authors only propose as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs an enhanced cell-to-cell similarity matrix for scRNA-seq clustering by restricting each cell to its K-nearest neighbors in a sparse subspace-representation similarity (simsparse) and imputing missing (zero) entries with the modified Weighted Adamic/Adar index over common neighbors, then symmetrizing with the three classical pairwise similarities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Constructs an enhanced cell-to-cell similarity matrix for scRNA-seq clustering by restricting each cell to its K-nearest neighbors in a sparse subspace-representation similarity (simsparse) and imputing missing (zero) entries with the modified Weighted Adamic/Adar index over common neighbors, then symmetrizing with the three classical pairwise similarities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input similarity matrix is already dense and contains no missing/zero entries to impute The data are very large-scale, since SSRE is reported to be relatively time-consuming on large datasets The task requires single-cell multi-omics integration, which the authors only propose as future work

skills.description: Use when annotating individual cells directly from marker GEPs (no clustering) and you need to smooth/consolidate per-cell GEP assignments using a precomputed KNN neighbor index.
skills.name: knn-neighbor-voting-label-propagation
skills.search_text: knn-neighbor-voting-label-propagation Use when annotating individual cells directly from marker GEPs (no clustering) and you need to smooth/consolidate per-cell GEP assignments using a precomputed KNN neighbor index. The target dataset contains cell types absent from the reference GEP set (e.g., TMS cells annotated with MCA GEPs can only be labeled 'unknown') High-resolution neuronal subtypes are needed but the reference (MCA) lacks them — MCA GEPs would compromise Mouse Brain neuron annotation precision You only need GEP-averaged expression for dimension reduction, not per-cell categorical annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A step inside CellGEP in which each cell's marker-GEP annotation is consolidated by k-nearest-neighbor voting: after the highest-expressed GEP is assigned per cell, the labels of the cell's stored Seurat neighbors are used to propagate and stabilize cell-type labels without clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: A step inside CellGEP in which each cell's marker-GEP annotation is consolidated by k-nearest-neighbor voting: after the highest-expressed GEP is assigned per cell, the labels of the cell's stored Seurat neighbors are used to propagate and stabilize cell-type labels without clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target dataset contains cell types absent from the reference GEP set (e.g., TMS cells annotated with MCA GEPs can only be labeled 'unknown') High-resolution neuronal subtypes are needed but the reference (MCA) lacks them — MCA GEPs would compromise Mouse Brain neuron annotation precision You only need GEP-averaged expression for dimension reduction, not per-cell categorical annotation

skills.description: Use when comparing two embedding configurations (e.g., t-SNE perplexity 100 from scDEED vs 1000 from EMBEDR) by measuring retention of pre-embedding neighbor structure.
skills.name: knn-neighborhood-preservation-assessment
skills.search_text: knn-neighborhood-preservation-assessment Use when comparing two embedding configurations (e.g., t-SNE perplexity 100 from scDEED vs 1000 from EMBEDR) by measuring retention of pre-embedding neighbor structure. When the pre-embedding space itself is under evaluation (e.g., comparing alternative dimensionality reductions rather than a given PCA reference) When the goal is hyperparameter optimization per se rather than post-hoc evaluation of an already-selected embedding; use scDEED's dubious-embedding minimization instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies how faithfully a 2D embedding (e.g., t-SNE at a chosen perplexity) preserves local neighborhood structure from the pre-embedding space (e.g., PCA) using KNN and KNC preservation metrics, and tests differences across datasets with paired t-tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Quantifies how faithfully a 2D embedding (e.g., t-SNE at a chosen perplexity) preserves local neighborhood structure from the pre-embedding space (e.g., PCA) using KNN and KNC preservation metrics, and tests differences across datasets with paired t-tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the pre-embedding space itself is under evaluation (e.g., comparing alternative dimensionality reductions rather than a given PCA reference) When the goal is hyperparameter optimization per se rather than post-hoc evaluation of an already-selected embedding; use scDEED's dubious-embedding minimization instead

skills.description: Use when comparing embedding methods on a multi-sample single-cell dataset for batch-effect correction versus biological signal retention, e.g. scoring SCING module AUCell embeddings against FastMNN/Harmony/Seurat on snRNA-seq cell annotations.
skills.name: knn-neighborhood-score-computation
skills.search_text: knn-neighborhood-score-computation Use when comparing embedding methods on a multi-sample single-cell dataset for batch-effect correction versus biological signal retention, e.g. scoring SCING module AUCell embeddings against FastMNN/Harmony/Seurat on snRNA-seq cell annotations. Input data has no batch/sample covariate or no cell-level phenotype annotations, so neither mixing nor signal retention can be scored You only need standard clustering quality metrics (silhouette, ARI) rather than an explicit batch-mixing versus biological-retention trade-off The embedding space was already produced by a dedicated batch-correction method and the goal is correction itself, not comparison of correction quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A KNN-based neighborhood score (Equation 1) that quantifies how well a cell-embedding space mixes cells across batches/samples while retaining biological annotations (diagnosis, sex, tangle/plaque stage), used in the SCING paper to benchmark GRN module AUCell embeddings against FastMNN, Harmony, and Seurat batch correction (Figure S6). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: A KNN-based neighborhood score (Equation 1) that quantifies how well a cell-embedding space mixes cells across batches/samples while retaining biological annotations (diagnosis, sex, tangle/plaque stage), used in the SCING paper to benchmark GRN module AUCell embeddings against FastMNN, Harmony, and Seurat batch correction (Figure S6).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no batch/sample covariate or no cell-level phenotype annotations, so neither mixing nor signal retention can be scored You only need standard clustering quality metrics (silhouette, ARI) rather than an explicit batch-mixing versus biological-retention trade-off The embedding space was already produced by a dedicated batch-correction method and the goal is correction itself, not comparison of correction quality

skills.description: Use when validating that a graph-based trajectory-inference result is robust to the KNN hyperparameter on time-labeled single-cell data (e.g., ~90K-cell CyTOF panels with day annotations) by correlating inferred pseudotime against known sampling days across a KNN sweep.
skills.name: knn-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: knn-parameter-sensitivity-analysis Use when validating that a graph-based trajectory-inference result is robust to the KNN hyperparameter on time-labeled single-cell data (e.g., ~90K-cell CyTOF panels with day annotations) by correlating inferred pseudotime against known sampling days across a KNN sweep. The dataset has no annotated time-point/sampling-day labels, so no pseudotime-vs-day Pearson correlation can serve as the accuracy metric The goal is lineage/fate discovery on a new dataset rather than validating robustness of an existing TI run to the KNN hyperparameter The candidate method requires dimensionality reduction (UMAP/t-SNE) before trajectory parsing, which the paper shows makes results susceptible to user-defined input parameters and confounds a KNN-sensitivity comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Sweep K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) settings around the VIA default (knn=30, HNSWlib graph) on the mESC CyTOF time-series data to quantify how pseudotime accuracy (Pearson correlation vs. annotated sampling days) changes with KNN, comparing full VIA, the no-lazy-teleporting ablation (memory=1), and baselines (Slingshot, Palantir, STREAM, PAGA). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Sweep K-nearest-neighbor (KNN) settings around the VIA default (knn=30, HNSWlib graph) on the mESC CyTOF time-series data to quantify how pseudotime accuracy (Pearson correlation vs. annotated sampling days) changes with KNN, comparing full VIA, the no-lazy-teleporting ablation (memory=1), and baselines (Slingshot, Palantir, STREAM, PAGA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no annotated time-point/sampling-day labels, so no pseudotime-vs-day Pearson correlation can serve as the accuracy metric The goal is lineage/fate discovery on a new dataset rather than validating robustness of an existing TI run to the KNN hyperparameter The candidate method requires dimensionality reduction (UMAP/t-SNE) before trajectory parsing, which the paper shows makes results susceptible to user-defined input parameters and confounds a KNN-sensitivity comparison

skills.description: Use when a query dataset measures only mRNA (no CITE-seq ADT counts) but you need surface protein levels, and a multimodal CITE-seq reference atlas with a joint mRNA/protein embedding is available.
skills.name: knn-protein-abundance-inference
skills.search_text: knn-protein-abundance-inference Use when a query dataset measures only mRNA (no CITE-seq ADT counts) but you need surface protein levels, and a multimodal CITE-seq reference atlas with a joint mRNA/protein embedding is available. The query already contains measured ADT/surface protein counts, so direct measurement rather than KNN prediction should be used Novel cell populations or cell types absent from the reference are expected — Symphony mapping metrics are less informative and it 'does not entirely supplant the need for users interested in novel cell type discovery to conduct de novo analyses of the query alone' No multimodal (mRNA + protein) reference embedding exists; protein inference from an mRNA-only PCA reference degrades correlations substantially (baseline r 0.65-0.97 vs 0.88-0.99) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Infers per-cell surface protein abundance for mRNA-only query cells by predicting protein levels from the k nearest reference neighbors (k=50) in a Symphony-harmonized multimodal CITE-seq embedding, enabling annotation transfer beyond cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Infers per-cell surface protein abundance for mRNA-only query cells by predicting protein levels from the k nearest reference neighbors (k=50) in a Symphony-harmonized multimodal CITE-seq embedding, enabling annotation transfer beyond cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query already contains measured ADT/surface protein counts, so direct measurement rather than KNN prediction should be used Novel cell populations or cell types absent from the reference are expected — Symphony mapping metrics are less informative and it 'does not entirely supplant the need for users interested in novel cell type discovery to conduct de novo analyses of the query alone' No multimodal (mRNA + protein) reference embedding exists; protein inference from an mRNA-only PCA reference degrades correlations substantially (baseline r 0.65-0.97 vs 0.88-0.99)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods (e.g. Monocle, Slingshot, dynverse MST) on simulated continuous single-cell populations where gold-standard branch labels are available and ordering-only metrics are insufficient.
skills.name: knn-purity-assessment
skills.search_text: knn-purity-assessment Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods (e.g. Monocle, Slingshot, dynverse MST) on simulated continuous single-cell populations where gold-standard branch labels are available and ordering-only metrics are insufficient. The task is clustering or differential expression benchmarking rather than trajectory/branching assessment — the article evaluates those tasks with other metrics such as AUROC No gold-standard branch labels exist for the cells, so neighbor purity against true branches cannot be computed Data are UMI-based and the trajectory question concerns discrete populations rather than continuous EVF trajectories http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assess trajectory inference quality by computing k-nearest-neighbor purity (cal_KNNP): the fraction of each cell's k nearest neighbors in the inferred pseudotime embedding that belong to the same gold-standard branch as the cell. It complements Spearman pseudotime correlation by capturing branch-assignment fidelity rather than ordering fidelity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Assess trajectory inference quality by computing k-nearest-neighbor purity (cal_KNNP): the fraction of each cell's k nearest neighbors in the inferred pseudotime embedding that belong to the same gold-standard branch as the cell. It complements Spearman pseudotime correlation by capturing branch-assignment fidelity rather than ordering fidelity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is clustering or differential expression benchmarking rather than trajectory/branching assessment — the article evaluates those tasks with other metrics such as AUROC No gold-standard branch labels exist for the cells, so neighbor purity against true branches cannot be computed Data are UMI-based and the trajectory question concerns discrete populations rather than continuous EVF trajectories

skills.description: Use when preparing single-cell RNA-Seq data (e.g. a Seurat object) as an undirected kNN graph input for EVA/ELVAR community detection and DA testing, or when reproducing the paper's lungCD4T or Tabula Muris Senis pipelines.
skills.name: knn-state-manifold-graph-construction
skills.search_text: knn-state-manifold-graph-construction Use when preparing single-cell RNA-Seq data (e.g. a Seurat object) as an undirected kNN graph input for EVA/ELVAR community detection and DA testing, or when reproducing the paper's lungCD4T or Tabula Muris Senis pipelines. Input is already a cell-cell graph or ELVAR-compatible igraph object — rebuilding the kNN graph would discard existing neighborhood structure The goal is generic clustering/visualization (FindClusters/RunTSNE) without downstream attribute-aware DA testing Data is single-cell ATAC-Seq or another modality where a gene-expression PCA state-space is not the appropriate manifold http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds a cell-cell kNN graph (the 'state-manifold') from PCA-reduced scRNA-Seq data using Seurat's FindNeighbors, which ELVAR then consumes for cell-attribute aware community detection and differential abundance testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Builds a cell-cell kNN graph (the 'state-manifold') from PCA-reduced scRNA-Seq data using Seurat's FindNeighbors, which ELVAR then consumes for cell-attribute aware community detection and differential abundance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-cell graph or ELVAR-compatible igraph object — rebuilding the kNN graph would discard existing neighborhood structure The goal is generic clustering/visualization (FindClusters/RunTSNE) without downstream attribute-aware DA testing Data is single-cell ATAC-Seq or another modality where a gene-expression PCA state-space is not the appropriate manifold

skills.description: Use when candidate RBPs (e.g., from CRIT NMF clusters) need experimental validation via public shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq data: detect circRNAs per dataset, compute per-sample mCRI, and run group t tests knockdown vs control.
skills.name: knockdown-perturbation-differential-testing
skills.search_text: knockdown-perturbation-differential-testing Use when candidate RBPs (e.g., from CRIT NMF clusters) need experimental validation via public shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq data: detect circRNAs per dataset, compute per-sample mCRI, and run group t tests knockdown vs control. The input is not perturbation RNA-seq but observational expression data (e.g., TCGA/MiOncoCirc correlation or NMF feature matrices) — use the CRIT feature-collecting scripts instead Only one circRNA-detecting tool can be run, since the validation requires concordance between CIRI2 and find_circ calls No knockdown and matched control samples exist for the RBP of interest (only 22 of the CRIT candidates had suitable knockdown RNA-seq data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 A validation skill that tests whether candidate circRNA-regulating RBPs affect global circRNA expression upon shRNA/siRNA knockdown, by reanalyzing public knockdown RNA-seq datasets with two circRNA-detecting tools (CIRI2 and find_circ) and computing the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI) per knockdown/control pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: A validation skill that tests whether candidate circRNA-regulating RBPs affect global circRNA expression upon shRNA/siRNA knockdown, by reanalyzing public knockdown RNA-seq datasets with two circRNA-detecting tools (CIRI2 and find_circ) and computing the normalized modified circRNA index (mCRI) per knockdown/control pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not perturbation RNA-seq but observational expression data (e.g., TCGA/MiOncoCirc correlation or NMF feature matrices) — use the CRIT feature-collecting scripts instead Only one circRNA-detecting tool can be run, since the validation requires concordance between CIRI2 and find_circ calls No knockdown and matched control samples exist for the RBP of interest (only 22 of the CRIT candidates had suitable knockdown RNA-seq data)

skills.description: Use when contrasting two small RNA-seq conditions (e.g., wild-type control vs ZSWIM8-knockout human cell lines) and the goal is a filtered differential expression table of miRNA/isomiR features, starting from FASTQ reads plus GFF3 miRNA reference annotations.
skills.name: knockout-vs-control-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: knockout-vs-control-differential-expression-testing Use when contrasting two small RNA-seq conditions (e.g., wild-type control vs ZSWIM8-knockout human cell lines) and the goal is a filtered differential expression table of miRNA/isomiR features, starting from FASTQ reads plus GFF3 miRNA reference annotations. Input is already a feature count table produced by another quantifier — the tiny-count hierarchical classification step (5′ nucleotide, length, position, mismatch filters) is the basis of the contrast and would be bypassed. The goal is to resolve distinct small RNA classes (e.g., piRNAs vs siRNAs) produced from a single locus rather than to test abundance differences between knockout and control conditions. skills.search_text: krnn-nearest-neighbor-retention-metric-computation Use when evaluating scRNA-seq integration quality beyond batch mixing: you have matched pre- and post-integration log-count matrices and need to quantify how many of each cell's original top-k neighbors survive correction. skills.description: Use when you need to train a neural autoencoder on preprocessed (log2(x+1), variance=1, mean=1) single-cell expression data to infer circular/periodic pseudo-time, and MSE+L2 regularization is the fitting objective.
skills.name: l2-regularized-neural-network-training
skills.search_text: l2-regularized-neural-network-training Use when you need to train a neural autoencoder on preprocessed (log2(x+1), variance=1, mean=1) single-cell expression data to infer circular/periodic pseudo-time, and MSE+L2 regularization is the fitting objective. The process is non-periodic / linear (e.g. a developmental trajectory), where linear pseudo-time methods such as Monocle or Wanderlust — not a circular-manifold autoencoder — are appropriate; Cyclum targets 'latent periodic' processes You need marker-gene-based cell-cycle phase scoring (e.g. Cyclone or scanpy/Seurat CellCycleScoring style); Cyclum's methodology explicitly relies on the circular manifold instead of marker genes, though it can refine external phase labels afterwards Input data is raw/unnormalized counts: the least-square fit assumes the log2(x+1) transform with variance = 1, mean = 1 scaling, so training directly on raw counts violates the model's expectations http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Trains Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder — a tanh-activated MLP encoder whose output feeds a cosine/sine decoder layer mapped linearly back to gene space — with a mean-squared-error objective plus L2 weight regularization, implemented in Keras with TensorFlow, to embed scRNA-seq cells on a circular manifold and recover periodic pseudo-time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Trains Cyclum's sinusoidal autoencoder — a tanh-activated MLP encoder whose output feeds a cosine/sine decoder layer mapped linearly back to gene space — with a mean-squared-error objective plus L2 weight regularization, implemented in Keras with TensorFlow, to embed scRNA-seq cells on a circular manifold and recover periodic pseudo-time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The process is non-periodic / linear (e.g. a developmental trajectory), where linear pseudo-time methods such as Monocle or Wanderlust — not a circular-manifold autoencoder — are appropriate; Cyclum targets 'latent periodic' processes You need marker-gene-based cell-cycle phase scoring (e.g. Cyclone or scanpy/Seurat CellCycleScoring style); Cyclum's methodology explicitly relies on the circular manifold instead of marker genes, though it can refine external phase labels afterwards Input data is raw/unnormalized counts: the least-square fit assumes the log2(x+1) transform with variance = 1, mean = 1 scaling, so training directly on raw counts violates the model's expectations
