skills.search_text: label-transfer-method-comparison Use when evaluating which supervised cell-type annotation method (SciBet, Seurat v3, scmap) transfers labels across scRNA-seq datasets generated by distinct sequencing technologies. The task is cell-type discovery or clustering of an unlabeled dataset rather than benchmarking supervised annotation methods against known labels Only one dataset is available with no cross-platform or cross-dataset generalization question — SciBet alone on a single train/test split suffices Test data contains cell types absent from the reference and false-positive rejection via the null-dataset confidence score is the goal — that requires SciBet's conf_score/null-dataset workflow, not plain accuracy comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark supervised single-cell cell-type label transfer by running SciBet, Seurat v3 (FindTransferAnchors/TransferData), and scmapCluster side-by-side on repeated stratified train/test splits and comparing mean classification accuracy, as in the SciBet cross-platform pancreas evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Benchmark supervised single-cell cell-type label transfer by running SciBet, Seurat v3 (FindTransferAnchors/TransferData), and scmapCluster side-by-side on repeated stratified train/test splits and comparing mean classification accuracy, as in the SciBet cross-platform pancreas evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is cell-type discovery or clustering of an unlabeled dataset rather than benchmarking supervised annotation methods against known labels Only one dataset is available with no cross-platform or cross-dataset generalization question — SciBet alone on a single train/test split suffices Test data contains cell types absent from the reference and false-positive rejection via the null-dataset confidence score is the goal — that requires SciBet's conf_score/null-dataset workflow, not plain accuracy comparison

skills.description: Use when the scRNA-seq count matrix comes with trusted cell type labels (e.g., a published dataset like GSE118068 with annotations) and you want group-wise dropout imputation instead of unsupervised spectral clustering.
skills.name: labeled-cell-type-guided-imputation
skills.search_text: labeled-cell-type-guided-imputation Use when the scRNA-seq count matrix comes with trusted cell type labels (e.g., a published dataset like GSE118068 with annotations) and you want group-wise dropout imputation instead of unsupervised spectral clustering. No reliable cell type labels exist — then supply a cluster count and method (e.g., c(7,"Spectrum") or c(7,"specc")) or a custom ccluster function instead of "labeled" Counts are already normalized — set normalized=TRUE to avoid double CPM/log10 transformation (though log-transform after normalization is still recommended) You need a single universally best imputation method — the authors caution no consensus exists and it is premature to conclude Bfimpute wins on all datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run Bfimpute in labeled mode, supplying ground-truth cell type labels via ccluster="labeled" and label= so imputation is performed within each known cell group rather than via clustering. This leverages similar-cell information from verified annotations to recover dropouts more accurately. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Run Bfimpute in labeled mode, supplying ground-truth cell type labels via ccluster="labeled" and label= so imputation is performed within each known cell group rather than via clustering. This leverages similar-cell information from verified annotations to recover dropouts more accurately.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable cell type labels exist — then supply a cluster count and method (e.g., c(7,"Spectrum") or c(7,"specc")) or a custom ccluster function instead of "labeled" Counts are already normalized — set normalized=TRUE to avoid double CPM/log10 transformation (though log-transform after normalization is still recommended) You need a single universally best imputation method — the authors caution no consensus exists and it is premature to conclude Bfimpute wins on all datasets

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq reads are spliced-aligned to a reference genome with more than one aligner (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) and a full-length transcript assembly (GTF) is needed that recovers transcripts missed by single-aligner assemblers like StringTie2 or Scallop.
skills.name: labeled-splice-graph-transcript-assembly
skills.search_text: labeled-splice-graph-transcript-assembly Use when RNA-seq reads are spliced-aligned to a reference genome with more than one aligner (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) and a full-length transcript assembly (GTF) is needed that recovers transcripts missed by single-aligner assemblers like StringTie2 or Scallop. Only one aligner's alignments are available and a standard assembler suffices — Tiglon's advantage comes from integrating Hisat2 and STAR mappings, and it accepts only Hisat(2)/Star BAM files Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets Annotation-guided assembly is required — the current Tiglon version has no option for using known transcript annotations to guide assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Genome-guided transcriptome assembly via Tiglon's labeled splice graph: integrate BAM alignments from multiple aligners (Hisat2 and Star), label splice-junction edges by which aligner captured them, and recover transcripts with a label-based dynamic path extension algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Genome-guided transcriptome assembly via Tiglon's labeled splice graph: integrate BAM alignments from multiple aligners (Hisat2 and Star), label splice-junction edges by which aligner captured them, and recover transcripts with a label-based dynamic path extension algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one aligner's alignments are available and a standard assembler suffices — Tiglon's advantage comes from integrating Hisat2 and STAR mappings, and it accepts only Hisat(2)/Star BAM files Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets Annotation-guided assembly is required — the current Tiglon version has no option for using known transcript annotations to guide assembly

skills.description: Use when comparing pseudotime orderings produced by multiple trajectory-inference algorithms on the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GSE72857 myeloid progenitors or Splatter simulations) and you need a quantitative smoothness score per algorithm.
skills.name: lag-1-autocorrelation-computation-along-pseudotime
skills.search_text: lag-1-autocorrelation-computation-along-pseudotime Use when comparing pseudotime orderings produced by multiple trajectory-inference algorithms on the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GSE72857 myeloid progenitors or Splatter simulations) and you need a quantitative smoothness score per algorithm. When the goal is to reconstruct a trajectory itself (e.g., subpopulation-aware flow-network reconstruction with CellRouter) rather than to score the smoothness of orderings already produced by one or more algorithms. When cells lack a single pseudotime ordering (e.g., unconnected subpopulations or no trajectory spanning the cell states of interest), since lag-1 autocorrelation requires a successive ordering of cells. When the input is bulk RNA-seq or otherwise lacks per-cell expression and per-cell pseudotime values. A trajectory-smoothness metric that correlates gene expression between successive cells along a reconstructed pseudotime ordering, used in the CellRouter paper to quantify whether trajectories (e.g., CellRouter vs. Monocle 2, DPT, Wishbone, Waterfall) have smoother, more autocorrelated gene expression dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: A trajectory-smoothness metric that correlates gene expression between successive cells along a reconstructed pseudotime ordering, used in the CellRouter paper to quantify whether trajectories (e.g., CellRouter vs. Monocle 2, DPT, Wishbone, Waterfall) have smoother, more autocorrelated gene expression dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to reconstruct a trajectory itself (e.g., subpopulation-aware flow-network reconstruction with CellRouter) rather than to score the smoothness of orderings already produced by one or more algorithms. When cells lack a single pseudotime ordering (e.g., unconnected subpopulations or no trajectory spanning the cell states of interest), since lag-1 autocorrelation requires a successive ordering of cells. When the input is bulk RNA-seq or otherwise lacks per-cell expression and per-cell pseudotime values.

skills.description: Use when building reference cell-type markers from multiple DE tests and you need a significance-driven consensus (p-value combination) rather than rank-only aggregation of top-N markers.
skills.name: lancaster-p-value-combination
skills.search_text: lancaster-p-value-combination Use when building reference cell-type markers from multiple DE tests and you need a significance-driven consensus (p-value combination) rather than rank-only aggregation of top-N markers. When only the top-N markers per DE test are needed and rank-only robust rank aggregation (marker_identification_fast) suffices without p-value combination When the reference data lacks cell-type labels or the DE tests do not produce p-values suitable for Lancaster combination When the goal is annotating unseen cell types absent from the reference — MASI must be combined with SCCAF for that http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 MASI's ensemble marker-identification path that aggregates statistically significant markers from N differential expression tests into a single final ranked cell-type marker list using Lancaster's method for combining p-values, implemented as marker_identification_LC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: MASI's ensemble marker-identification path that aggregates statistically significant markers from N differential expression tests into a single final ranked cell-type marker list using Lancaster's method for combining p-values, implemented as marker_identification_LC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only the top-N markers per DE test are needed and rank-only robust rank aggregation (marker_identification_fast) suffices without p-value combination When the reference data lacks cell-type labels or the DE tests do not produce p-values suitable for Lancaster combination When the goal is annotating unseen cell types absent from the reference — MASI must be combined with SCCAF for that

skills.description: Use when the scRNA-seq dataset has many cells so that solving the optimal transport problem (Eq. 2) for every cell pair over all m spatial positions is computationally intractable, and an approximate n x n spatial distance matrix is acceptable.
skills.name: landmark-based-approximation
skills.search_text: landmark-based-approximation Use when the scRNA-seq dataset has many cells so that solving the optimal transport problem (Eq. 2) for every cell pair over all m spatial positions is computationally intractable, and an approximate n x n spatial distance matrix is acceptable. The dataset is small enough that the exact pairwise optimal transport over all m spatial positions is computationally feasible, so the exact Eq. (2) distances can be used instead of the landmark approximation No upstream cell–position transport plan gamma* exists yet — the approximation requires the SpaOTsc mapping to be solved first The analysis requires modeling time delay in cell–cell communication (e.g. ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade times), which SpaOTsc's distance-based approach does not consider http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Approximates the n x n spatial cell–cell distance matrix in SpaOTsc by restricting the pairwise optimal transport computation over spatial locations to a small set of landmark positions, because the full cell-pair-wise OT computation becomes intractable for excessively large datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Approximates the n x n spatial cell–cell distance matrix in SpaOTsc by restricting the pairwise optimal transport computation over spatial locations to a small set of landmark positions, because the full cell-pair-wise OT computation becomes intractable for excessively large datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that the exact pairwise optimal transport over all m spatial positions is computationally feasible, so the exact Eq. (2) distances can be used instead of the landmark approximation No upstream cell–position transport plan gamma* exists yet — the approximation requires the SpaOTsc mapping to be solved first The analysis requires modeling time delay in cell–cell communication (e.g. ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade times), which SpaOTsc's distance-based approach does not consider

skills.description: Use when an LDA (or HSS-LDA) embedding orders cells along a known biological axis (e.g., villus zone labels) and you must validate or interpret the axis using marker genes with distinct spatial or temporal expression patterns.
skills.name: landmark-gene-expression-annotation
skills.search_text: landmark-gene-expression-annotation Use when an LDA (or HSS-LDA) embedding orders cells along a known biological axis (e.g., villus zone labels) and you must validate or interpret the axis using marker genes with distinct spatial or temporal expression patterns. Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the article notes 'This supervised approach is inappropriate in situations in which labels are unknown, or in which an unbiased view of the data is preferable.' Input data have more than ~100 dimensions and HSS feature selection is required — 'in situations in which HSS is not feasible (>100 dimensions) or desirable, LDA and sda still provide useful plots', so use PCs or run LDA without HSS as in this skill The goal is to resolve non-linear structure — 'LDA does not capture non-linear relationships, which may limit its performance on some datasets.' Annotates an LDA-ordered single-cell trajectory by coloring cells on linear discriminant axes with landmark gene expression (e.g., ADA at the villus tip, SLC2A2 in the mid-villus), verifying that biologically relevant spatial expression patterns are preserved by supervised dimensionality reduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Annotates an LDA-ordered single-cell trajectory by coloring cells on linear discriminant axes with landmark gene expression (e.g., ADA at the villus tip, SLC2A2 in the mid-villus), verifying that biologically relevant spatial expression patterns are preserved by supervised dimensionality reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the article notes 'This supervised approach is inappropriate in situations in which labels are unknown, or in which an unbiased view of the data is preferable.' Input data have more than ~100 dimensions and HSS feature selection is required — 'in situations in which HSS is not feasible (>100 dimensions) or desirable, LDA and sda still provide useful plots', so use PCs or run LDA without HSS as in this skill The goal is to resolve non-linear structure — 'LDA does not capture non-linear relationships, which may limit its performance on some datasets.'

skills.description: Use when an Mpath trajectory analysis on single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. mouse DC progenitors) needs its landmark clusters and branching topology checked for robustness to clustering/cut parameters before downstream interpretation.
skills.name: landmark-set-reproducibility-assessment
skills.search_text: landmark-set-reproducibility-assessment Use when an Mpath trajectory analysis on single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. mouse DC progenitors) needs its landmark clusters and branching topology checked for robustness to clustering/cut parameters before downstream interpretation. Trajectories expected to start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets where specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to such data Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets — Mpath depends on end-stage contrasts for fate prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A sensitivity-analysis skill for the Mpath trajectory pipeline that re-runs landmark-cluster designation and neighborhood-based state transition network construction across diversity cuts (0.5, 0.6, 0.7) and dendrogram cut depths (11-13 initial clusters) to verify the reconstructed DC progenitor cascade is parameter-invariant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill for the Mpath trajectory pipeline that re-runs landmark-cluster designation and neighborhood-based state transition network construction across diversity cuts (0.5, 0.6, 0.7) and dendrogram cut depths (11-13 initial clusters) to verify the reconstructed DC progenitor cascade is parameter-invariant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Trajectories expected to start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets where specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to such data Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets — Mpath depends on end-stage contrasts for fate prediction

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count/normalized expression matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) need per-cell stemness/pluripotency ranking, e.g. to select stem/progenitor origins for trajectory inference or to benchmark against ORIGINS activity scores.
skills.name: landscent-signal-rank-computation
skills.search_text: landscent-signal-rank-computation Use when scRNA-seq count/normalized expression matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) need per-cell stemness/pluripotency ranking, e.g. to select stem/progenitor origins for trajectory inference or to benchmark against ORIGINS activity scores. When the goal is to score PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — the extended ORIGINS2 package or PyOrigins with a custom build_ppin network is the appropriate tool When RAM memory is severely constrained: the article reports ORIGINS requires less RAM memory than LandSCENT and CytoTRACE When only a highly-variable-feature (HVF)-derived network is available as scaffold — this comparator failed to order lung cell types by expected pluripotency http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes LandSCENT Signal Rank (SR) pluripotency scores per cell from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix, as benchmarked in Senra et al. (2022) against ORIGINS differentiation activity and CytoTRACE on breast, colon, hematopoietic (GSE117498) and lung (GSE161383) datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Computes LandSCENT Signal Rank (SR) pluripotency scores per cell from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix, as benchmarked in Senra et al. (2022) against ORIGINS differentiation activity and CytoTRACE on breast, colon, hematopoietic (GSE117498) and lung (GSE161383) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to score PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — the extended ORIGINS2 package or PyOrigins with a custom build_ppin network is the appropriate tool When RAM memory is severely constrained: the article reports ORIGINS requires less RAM memory than LandSCENT and CytoTRACE When only a highly-variable-feature (HVF)-derived network is available as scaffold — this comparator failed to order lung cell types by expected pluripotency

skills.description: Use when training a multinomial cell-type classifier on single-cell expression data and zero mean expression for some genes would otherwise yield zero likelihood; i.e., building a SciBet Learn model from log-normalized counts.
skills.name: laplace-smoothing-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: laplace-smoothing-parameter-estimation Use when training a multinomial cell-type classifier on single-cell expression data and zero mean expression for some genes would otherwise yield zero likelihood; i.e., building a SciBet Learn model from log-normalized counts. The query data contains cell types absent from the training reference — SciBet's confidence score C (likelihood ratio vs. a null dataset, cutoffs 0.001–0.5) exists precisely to flag such cells, and a plain smoothed multinomial will still force a label. The expression matrix has not been log-normalized consistently with the training data (TPM-log for full-length, Seurat v3 size-factor-10,000 for UMI), since p_ij estimation and likelihood comparison assume matched scales. Feature selection has not been performed — the article fits parameters on the top-500 ΔS informative genes, not the full transcriptome. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate per-cell-type multinomial parameters (p_ij) in SciBet by normalizing the mean expression vector across genes and applying Laplace smoothing (adding one), so that maximum-likelihood classification over the top-500 informative genes never encounters zero probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Estimate per-cell-type multinomial parameters (p_ij) in SciBet by normalizing the mean expression vector across genes and applying Laplace smoothing (adding one), so that maximum-likelihood classification over the top-500 informative genes never encounters zero probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data contains cell types absent from the training reference — SciBet's confidence score C (likelihood ratio vs. a null dataset, cutoffs 0.001–0.5) exists precisely to flag such cells, and a plain smoothed multinomial will still force a label. The expression matrix has not been log-normalized consistently with the training data (TPM-log for full-length, Seurat v3 size-factor-10,000 for UMI), since p_ij estimation and likelihood comparison assume matched scales. Feature selection has not been performed — the article fits parameters on the top-500 ΔS informative genes, not the full transcriptome.

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed single-cell dataset (e.g. .h5ad from scRNA-seq or 4i imaging) already has dynamic seed features and you need to rank all features by trajectory smoothness before trajectory inference.
skills.name: laplacian-score-feature-ranking
skills.search_text: laplacian-score-feature-ranking Use when a preprocessed single-cell dataset (e.g. .h5ad from scRNA-seq or 4i imaging) already has dynamic seed features and you need to rank all features by trajectory smoothness before trajectory inference. No dynamic seed features exist yet — DELVE Step 1 must first identify dynamic modules from core regulatory complexes before the seed graph can be built Data are single-cell images or raw counts that have not been preprocessed/normalized into a cells x features matrix suitable for graph construction The goal is clustering or differential expression rather than selecting features that preserve cellular trajectories — variance-based or other selection may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 DELVE Step 2: rank all measured features by Laplacian Score on an affinity graph built from the Step-1 dynamic seed modules, retaining globally smooth features that vary slowly among neighboring cells and excluding noisy, rapidly oscillating features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: DELVE Step 2: rank all measured features by Laplacian Score on an affinity graph built from the Step-1 dynamic seed modules, retaining globally smooth features that vary slowly among neighboring cells and excluding noisy, rapidly oscillating features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No dynamic seed features exist yet — DELVE Step 1 must first identify dynamic modules from core regulatory complexes before the seed graph can be built Data are single-cell images or raw counts that have not been preprocessed/normalized into a cells x features matrix suitable for graph construction The goal is clustering or differential expression rather than selecting features that preserve cellular trajectories — variance-based or other selection may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when a clustering task involves very large datasets (e.g. 100k-1M cells/objects, such as mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) where full-dataset KMD clustering is computationally infeasible, and the number of populations is known.
skills.name: large-dataset-subsampled-clustering
skills.search_text: large-dataset-subsampled-clustering Use when a clustering task involves very large datasets (e.g. 100k-1M cells/objects, such as mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) where full-dataset KMD clustering is computationally infeasible, and the number of populations is known. Dataset is small enough to cluster directly without subsampling (the repo recommends sub_sample only on large datasets) The number of clusters is unknown — the sampling scheme was demonstrated with n_clusters set to the known number of populations, and de novo cluster number estimation via DBCV is only preliminary Very small clusters are expected that may not be captured by a small random sample (a stated limitation of the sampling approach) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Scales KMD hierarchical clustering (KMD linkage + KMD silhouette + outlier-aware partitioning) to million-object datasets by clustering a small random subsample and post-hoc assigning remaining objects via the outlier classification scheme. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Scales KMD hierarchical clustering (KMD linkage + KMD silhouette + outlier-aware partitioning) to million-object datasets by clustering a small random subsample and post-hoc assigning remaining objects via the outlier classification scheme.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is small enough to cluster directly without subsampling (the repo recommends sub_sample only on large datasets) The number of clusters is unknown — the sampling scheme was demonstrated with n_clusters set to the known number of populations, and de novo cluster number estimation via DBCV is only preliminary Very small clusters are expected that may not be captured by a small random sample (a stated limitation of the sampling approach)

skills.description: Use when building interactive selection over dense 3D/2D scatter plots of single-cell DR coordinates (>30k points) where per-cell colliders would be too slow and freehand per-cell capture is required.
skills.name: large-point-cloud-selection-scaling
skills.search_text: large-point-cloud-selection-scaling Use when building interactive selection over dense 3D/2D scatter plots of single-cell DR coordinates (>30k points) where per-cell colliders would be too slow and freehand per-cell capture is required. Point clouds are small enough that native per-object Unity colliders incur no performance cost — the custom system is unnecessary overhead The goal is aggregate (group/cluster-level) selection rather than per-cell freehand selection; CellexalVR's other selection modes may suffice The rendering environment is not Unity/VR (e.g. flat-screen 2D plotting libraries), where raycast-based octree traversal does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A technique for making every cell in a dense VR dimension-reduction plot (tens of thousands of points) individually selectable by replacing per-object Unity colliders with a custom-engineered collision detection system built to accommodate a large number of points, as implemented in CellexalVR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: A technique for making every cell in a dense VR dimension-reduction plot (tens of thousands of points) individually selectable by replacing per-object Unity colliders with a custom-engineered collision detection system built to accommodate a large number of points, as implemented in CellexalVR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Point clouds are small enough that native per-object Unity colliders incur no performance cost — the custom system is unnecessary overhead The goal is aggregate (group/cluster-level) selection rather than per-cell freehand selection; CellexalVR's other selection modes may suffice The rendering environment is not Unity/VR (e.g. flat-screen 2D plotting libraries), where raycast-based octree traversal does not apply

skills.description: Use when sketching or sampling cells from an expression matrix with >1 million cells (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) and you need cell-cell distances or a timing comparison of the distance-computation stage.
skills.name: large-scale-cell-distance-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: large-scale-cell-distance-matrix-computation Use when sketching or sampling cells from an expression matrix with >1 million cells (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) and you need cell-cell distances or a timing comparison of the distance-computation stage. The dataset is small enough that sketching is unnecessary and a full-dataset analysis (e.g., SC3 consensus clustering, Monocle 2 trajectory inference) is tractable directly The input is not a cell-by-feature matrix with rows as cells (e.g., already a precomputed sketch or a pairwise distance file), since Sphetcher expects CSV expression matrices The goal is unbiased uniform downsampling rather than data-dependent coverage of transcriptomic space, since uniform subsampling ignores similarity between gene expression patterns and risks overlooking rare cell states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute all-pairs cell-cell distances (e.g., Pearson correlation) over a multi-million-cell single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix as the expensive distance-computation stage of Sphetcher-H, so that runtime can be benchmarked against geometric sketching on the 2,026,641-cell MOCA dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Compute all-pairs cell-cell distances (e.g., Pearson correlation) over a multi-million-cell single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix as the expensive distance-computation stage of Sphetcher-H, so that runtime can be benchmarked against geometric sketching on the 2,026,641-cell MOCA dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that sketching is unnecessary and a full-dataset analysis (e.g., SC3 consensus clustering, Monocle 2 trajectory inference) is tractable directly The input is not a cell-by-feature matrix with rows as cells (e.g., already a precomputed sketch or a pairwise distance file), since Sphetcher expects CSV expression matrices The goal is unbiased uniform downsampling rather than data-dependent coverage of transcriptomic space, since uniform subsampling ignores similarity between gene expression patterns and risks overlooking rare cell states

skills.description: Use when benchmarking inference time or memory of scRNA-seq annotation tools on matrices ranging from 100 to 1,000,000 cells, and you need to isolate file-parsing overhead from model runtime.
skills.name: large-scale-count-matrix-io-optimization
skills.search_text: large-scale-count-matrix-io-optimization Use when benchmarking inference time or memory of scRNA-seq annotation tools on matrices ranging from 100 to 1,000,000 cells, and you need to isolate file-parsing overhead from model runtime. Data are hematologic tumor samples — Cancer-Finder is explicitly not recommended there The analysis goal is annotation accuracy rather than runtime/memory scalability Datasets are small (<1,000 cells) where csv-parsing overhead is negligible and binary storage adds no measurable benefit A benchmarking skill that quantifies how text-format (tsv/csv) parsing dominates wall-clock inference time for malignant cell annotation tools at 10^2–10^6 cell scale, and uses binary-stored matrices to separate parsing overhead from model compute. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that quantifies how text-format (tsv/csv) parsing dominates wall-clock inference time for malignant cell annotation tools at 10^2–10^6 cell scale, and uses binary-stored matrices to separate parsing overhead from model compute.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are hematologic tumor samples — Cancer-Finder is explicitly not recommended there The analysis goal is annotation accuracy rather than runtime/memory scalability Datasets are small (<1,000 cells) where csv-parsing overhead is negligible and binary storage adds no measurable benefit

skills.name: large-scale-dataset-downsampling
skills.search_text: large-scale-dataset-downsampling Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method's runtime and memory footprint across dataset sizes (e.g., 10k → 100k → 1M cells) on a single large source dataset. The dataset is already small (e.g., the 10X Genomics pbmc_1k_v2 PBMC dataset used for the clustering-accuracy benchmarks) — scaling behavior cannot be assessed without a large source dataset The analysis goal is clustering accuracy or silhouette-index comparison rather than runtime/memory scalability Only a downsampled subset exists and the full-scale point (over a million cells) cannot be run, invalidating the scaling comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates multi-scale (10k, 100k, ~1M cell) downsamplings of the Cao et al. mouse organogenesis scRNA-seq dataset (GEO GSE119945) to profile how a feature selection method's runtime and peak memory scale with cell count, as in the DUBStepR scalability benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Generates multi-scale (10k, 100k, ~1M cell) downsamplings of the Cao et al. mouse organogenesis scRNA-seq dataset (GEO GSE119945) to profile how a feature selection method's runtime and peak memory scale with cell count, as in the DUBStepR scalability benchmark.

skills.search_text: latent-embedding-decoding-for-scrna-seq Use when decoding a latent cell embedding back to gene space for scRNA-seq count data where dropout-heavy zeros must be accounted for by explicit Bernoulli dropout probabilities instead of ZINB modeling. When the analysis goal explicitly requires a zero-inflated negative binomial decoder — DCA and scDeepCluster-style ZINB losses are the appropriate alternative, and scMGCA deliberately departs from that modeling choice When the input is not raw-ish count data (e.g., already log-transformed or TPM-normalized continuous values), since the multinomial likelihood and dropout estimation are defined on count matrices When only cell clustering is needed without denoising/gene-space reconstruction — the KL-divergence self-optimized clustering on Z alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs the scMGCA decoder as a three-layer fully connected network (128→256→512) with softmax output that maps latent embeddings Z to multinomial gene probabilities, combined with Bernoulli dropout variables so that single-cell count data are modeled by a multinomial distribution with dropout compensation rather than a zero-inflated distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs the scMGCA decoder as a three-layer fully connected network (128→256→512) with softmax output that maps latent embeddings Z to multinomial gene probabilities, combined with Bernoulli dropout variables so that single-cell count data are modeled by a multinomial distribution with dropout compensation rather than a zero-inflated distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal explicitly requires a zero-inflated negative binomial decoder — DCA and scDeepCluster-style ZINB losses are the appropriate alternative, and scMGCA deliberately departs from that modeling choice When the input is not raw-ish count data (e.g., already log-transformed or TPM-normalized continuous values), since the multinomial likelihood and dropout estimation are defined on count matrices When only cell clustering is needed without denoising/gene-space reconstruction — the KL-divergence self-optimized clustering on Z alone suffices

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices must be compressed into a low-dimensional feature representation for downstream clustering, explicitly modeling zero inflation via a ZINB likelihood.
skills.name: latent-embedding-extraction
skills.search_text: latent-embedding-extraction Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices must be compressed into a low-dimensional feature representation for downstream clustering, explicitly modeling zero inflation via a ZINB likelihood. The goal is only preprocessing or quality control of raw counts — that belongs to the first module (preprocess.py), not the autoencoder A consensus clustering of existing embeddings is already available and only the third module (BC.m / BGEC.m) is needed The data lack the excess zeros characteristic of scRNA-seq, making ZINB modeling inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains the single-cell Dual Denoising Autoencoder (SDDA) of scBGEDA — a Gaussian-noise-corrupted encoder with a ZINB master decoder and an MSE follower decoder — to produce a 32-dimensional latent embedding of scRNA-seq count data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Trains the single-cell Dual Denoising Autoencoder (SDDA) of scBGEDA — a Gaussian-noise-corrupted encoder with a ZINB master decoder and an MSE follower decoder — to produce a 32-dimensional latent embedding of scRNA-seq count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only preprocessing or quality control of raw counts — that belongs to the first module (preprocess.py), not the autoencoder A consensus clustering of existing embeddings is already available and only the third module (BC.m / BGEC.m) is needed The data lack the excess zeros characteristic of scRNA-seq, making ZINB modeling inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you have log1p-normalized, multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches; 2000 highly variable genes with batch labels) and need harmonized latent embeddings plus corrected outputs in original gene space.
skills.name: latent-embedding-extraction-from-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: latent-embedding-extraction-from-scrnaseq Use when you have log1p-normalized, multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches; 2000 highly variable genes with batch labels) and need harmonized latent embeddings plus corrected outputs in original gene space. Input is single-batch scRNA-seq with no batch effects to mitigate — the domain discriminator and DSBN machinery target cross-batch harmonization Multi-omic integration where modalities share very few features, e.g., CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features, which makes it challenging to identify shared features and optimize the model Online label transfer where the reference and query datasets come from different tissue types — scCobra requires the same tissue type or similar cell types for optimal performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts batch-corrected cell embeddings by training scCobra, a contrastive VAE-GAN whose encoder maps multi-batch scRNA-seq into a unified low-dimensional latent space and whose DSBN-equipped decoder (BN1) reconstructs outputs in the original gene space, without assuming a gene expression distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Extracts batch-corrected cell embeddings by training scCobra, a contrastive VAE-GAN whose encoder maps multi-batch scRNA-seq into a unified low-dimensional latent space and whose DSBN-equipped decoder (BN1) reconstructs outputs in the original gene space, without assuming a gene expression distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-batch scRNA-seq with no batch effects to mitigate — the domain discriminator and DSBN machinery target cross-batch harmonization Multi-omic integration where modalities share very few features, e.g., CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features, which makes it challenging to identify shared features and optimize the model Online label transfer where the reference and query datasets come from different tissue types — scCobra requires the same tissue type or similar cell types for optimal performance

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell latent feature vectors (e.g. 64-dim Miscell/MoCo embeddings) and need a 2D t-SNE visualization plus clustering assignments for a large scRNA-seq dataset such as the 43,095-cell 10x PBMC data.
skills.name: latent-embedding-tsne-visualization
skills.search_text: latent-embedding-tsne-visualization Use when you have per-cell latent feature vectors (e.g. 64-dim Miscell/MoCo embeddings) and need a 2D t-SNE visualization plus clustering assignments for a large scRNA-seq dataset such as the 43,095-cell 10x PBMC data. Input is raw gene expression or already-processed Scanpy/Seurat PCA embeddings rather than Miscell latent features — the article benchmarks Miscell against those pipelines instead of reusing them The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so t-SNE on its latent features is not the right choice for small cohorts Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell includes no internal batch correction, so embedding uncorrected features is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Embed cell latent features learned by a self-supervised model (Miscell) into a 2D FIt-SNE visualization and cluster the embedding with DBSCAN or a Scanpy Leiden graph, enabling visual delineation of single-cell clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Embed cell latent features learned by a self-supervised model (Miscell) into a 2D FIt-SNE visualization and cluster the embedding with DBSCAN or a Scanpy Leiden graph, enabling visual delineation of single-cell clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression or already-processed Scanpy/Seurat PCA embeddings rather than Miscell latent features — the article benchmarks Miscell against those pipelines instead of reusing them The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so t-SNE on its latent features is not the right choice for small cohorts Batch effects are present and uncorrected — Miscell includes no internal batch correction, so embedding uncorrected features is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data contain suspected unmeasured technical or cell-cycle confounders and a set of control genes is available; goal is confounder estimation and corrected expression for downstream clustering.
skills.name: latent-factor-inference-via-partial-least-squares
skills.search_text: latent-factor-inference-via-partial-least-squares Use when scRNA-seq expression data contain suspected unmeasured technical or cell-cycle confounders and a set of control genes is available; goal is confounder estimation and corrected expression for downstream clustering. You need to infer the biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, due to model identifiability Your data are raw counts and you require a count-based model — extending the framework to modeling count data is left as future work The downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction) — performance of scPLS in other analysis settings has not been evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer and remove hidden confounding factors in single-cell RNA-seq data with scPLS, which jointly models a control gene set and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, bridging PCA/LMM-type and RUV/scLVM-type methods. Implemented in the Citrus R package with an Rcpp/RcppArmadillo block-wise EM algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Infer and remove hidden confounding factors in single-cell RNA-seq data with scPLS, which jointly models a control gene set and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, bridging PCA/LMM-type and RUV/scLVM-type methods. Implemented in the Citrus R package with an Rcpp/RcppArmadillo block-wise EM algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to infer the biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, due to model identifiability Your data are raw counts and you require a count-based model — extending the framework to modeling count data is left as future work The downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction) — performance of scPLS in other analysis settings has not been evaluated

skills.description: Use when assessing how sensitive a ZINB-WaVE fit is to choosing the wrong number of latent factors K or omitting the gene-level intercept in V, e.g. before trusting low-dimensional outputs from scRNA-seq counts.
skills.name: latent-factor-misspecification-analysis
skills.search_text: latent-factor-misspecification-analysis Use when assessing how sensitive a ZINB-WaVE fit is to choosing the wrong number of latent factors K or omitting the gene-level intercept in V, e.g. before trusting low-dimensional outputs from scRNA-seq counts. The goal is comparing dimensionality-reduction methods (e.g. ZINB-WaVE vs PCA vs ZIFA) on real data rather than auditing estimator bias under model misspecification The data are already normalized/log-transformed and you do not intend to model raw counts with the ZINB likelihood — the skill's simulation refits require count data and genewise dispersion You lack the fitted-model parameters (true ln(mu), pi) needed to define bias and MSE, e.g. when only raw unmodelled data are available http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 A simulation-based robustness assessment for ZINB-WaVE that quantifies bias and MSE of ln(mu) and pi estimates when the number of latent factors K, the gene-level covariate matrix V, or the dispersion specification are misspecified. It grounds the paper's claim that ZINB-WaVE yields robust, unbiased estimators of underlying biological signals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: A simulation-based robustness assessment for ZINB-WaVE that quantifies bias and MSE of ln(mu) and pi estimates when the number of latent factors K, the gene-level covariate matrix V, or the dispersion specification are misspecified. It grounds the paper's claim that ZINB-WaVE yields robust, unbiased estimators of underlying biological signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparing dimensionality-reduction methods (e.g. ZINB-WaVE vs PCA vs ZIFA) on real data rather than auditing estimator bias under model misspecification The data are already normalized/log-transformed and you do not intend to model raw counts with the ZINB likelihood — the skill's simulation refits require count data and genewise dispersion You lack the fitted-model parameters (true ln(mu), pi) needed to define bias and MSE, e.g. when only raw unmodelled data are available

skills.description: Use when a normalized log-transformed scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows within-cell-type heterogeneity suspected to arise from cell-cycle effects, and a known cell-cycle gene annotation set is available to guide removal before clustering.
skills.name: latent-factor-removal-from-expression-matrices
skills.search_text: latent-factor-removal-from-expression-matrices Use when a normalized log-transformed scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows within-cell-type heterogeneity suspected to arise from cell-cycle effects, and a known cell-cycle gene annotation set is available to guide removal before clustering. When the goal is to remove non-cell-cycle latent confounders (e.g. batch or mitochondrial effects) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively When cell-cycle activity is very low and few control genes are influenced (below ~8% affected), the effect may not be captured by the principal components and may be missed When no reliable cell-cycle gene annotation set is available for the species http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies and removes unwanted latent factors (specifically the cell-cycle effect) from single-cell RNA-Seq expression matrices using ccRemover's PCA-based iterative loop, preserving other biological signals of interest. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Identifies and removes unwanted latent factors (specifically the cell-cycle effect) from single-cell RNA-Seq expression matrices using ccRemover's PCA-based iterative loop, preserving other biological signals of interest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to remove non-cell-cycle latent confounders (e.g. batch or mitochondrial effects) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively When cell-cycle activity is very low and few control genes are influenced (below ~8% affected), the effect may not be captured by the principal components and may be missed When no reliable cell-cycle gene annotation set is available for the species

skills.description: Reference for removing dominant latent factors (e.g. cell cycle) from log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrices via scLVM's Python script, choosing K = 1 or the scree-plot value, and comparing corrected vs. original data.
skills.name: latent-factor-removal-sclvm
skills.search_text: latent-factor-removal-sclvm Reference for removing dominant latent factors (e.g. cell cycle) from log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrices via scLVM's Python script, choosing K = 1 or the scree-plot value, and comparing corrected vs. original data. When the leading factor's identity must be statistically verified before removal — scLVM 'does not inspect whether a leading factor represents the cell cycle' and risks removing biological components of interest such as cell-type signal (K = 1 on simulated data removed the cell-type effect). When the goal is to remove only the cell-cycle effect while preserving cell-type separation and the data contain strong competing latent structure — ccRemover is the article's purpose-built alternative with a formal bootstrap t-test on the loading difference Δj. When a versioned, packaged R workflow is required — the article applies scLVM via a Python script from its GitHub page with no version number or explicit repository URL recorded. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply scLVM to remove latent factors (primarily the cell-cycle effect) from single-cell RNA-Seq data by fitting a latent variable model with a user-chosen number K of leading factors, then assess downstream clustering/enrichment on the corrected matrix. In the source article scLVM is used as the comparison baseline against ccRemover on simulated data, T-helper cells, mESC, and glioblastoma datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Apply scLVM to remove latent factors (primarily the cell-cycle effect) from single-cell RNA-Seq data by fitting a latent variable model with a user-chosen number K of leading factors, then assess downstream clustering/enrichment on the corrected matrix. In the source article scLVM is used as the comparison baseline against ccRemover on simulated data, T-helper cells, mESC, and glioblastoma datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the leading factor's identity must be statistically verified before removal — scLVM 'does not inspect whether a leading factor represents the cell cycle' and risks removing biological components of interest such as cell-type signal (K = 1 on simulated data removed the cell-type effect). When the goal is to remove only the cell-cycle effect while preserving cell-type separation and the data contain strong competing latent structure — ccRemover is the article's purpose-built alternative with a formal bootstrap t-test on the loading difference Δj. When a versioned, packaged R workflow is required — the article applies scLVM via a Python script from its GitHub page with no version number or explicit repository URL recorded.

skills.description: Use when a multi-sample single-cell integration method must be shown competitive against alternatives (Seurat, Harmony, LIGER, scVI, Scanorama, BBKNN, CSS) across datasets while sweeping the number of latent factors K.
skills.name: latent-factor-sweep-benchmarking
skills.search_text: latent-factor-sweep-benchmarking Use when a multi-sample single-cell integration method must be shown competitive against alternatives (Seurat, Harmony, LIGER, scVI, Scanorama, BBKNN, CSS) across datasets while sweeping the number of latent factors K. When analyzing a single already-fitted GEDI model for downstream tasks (cluster-free DGE, pathway/TF activity) rather than comparing methods — this skill is only for integration benchmarking When the goal is to evaluate GEDI's gene-level expression imputations against other imputation methods — the article states this comparison 'remains to be tested' and is out of scope here When the input is not raw per-cell counts needing inter-sample harmonization (e.g., data already integrated or ratio-based splicing/stability modalities handled by GEDI's other modes) Benchmarks GEDI's cross-sample integration against competing single-cell integration methods (Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) while sweeping the number of latent factors (e.g., K = 5 to 40), scoring batch removal and biological conservation with Luecken-style metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Benchmarks GEDI's cross-sample integration against competing single-cell integration methods (Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) while sweeping the number of latent factors (e.g., K = 5 to 40), scoring batch removal and biological conservation with Luecken-style metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When analyzing a single already-fitted GEDI model for downstream tasks (cluster-free DGE, pathway/TF activity) rather than comparing methods — this skill is only for integration benchmarking When the goal is to evaluate GEDI's gene-level expression imputations against other imputation methods — the article states this comparison 'remains to be tested' and is out of scope here When the input is not raw per-cell counts needing inter-sample harmonization (e.g., data already integrated or ratio-based splicing/stability modalities handled by GEDI's other modes)

skills.description: Use when a spliced/unspliced AnnData (h5ad) needs directional developmental trajectories or latent-time ordering, especially with multiple lineages, time-dependent rates, or batch effects that break linear RNA velocity.
skills.name: latent-ode-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: latent-ode-trajectory-inference Use when a spliced/unspliced AnnData (h5ad) needs directional developmental trajectories or latent-time ordering, especially with multiple lineages, time-dependent rates, or batch effects that break linear RNA velocity. Data lacks an unspliced layer, since LatentVelo requires both spliced and unspliced count layers in AnnData Cells are unlikely to be reachable from a single initial state by continuous trajectories, e.g. disconnected populations like the microglia cluster in the dentate gyrus dataset Only steady-state, single-lineage velocity estimates are needed, where simpler linear methods such as scVelo stochastic mode may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer developmental cell trajectories with LatentVelo by embedding cells in a VAE latent space and modeling differentiation dynamics with neural ODEs, so that individual cells get inferred developmental paths (z_traj with times) rather than only local RNA velocity vectors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Infer developmental cell trajectories with LatentVelo by embedding cells in a VAE latent space and modeling differentiation dynamics with neural ODEs, so that individual cells get inferred developmental paths (z_traj with times) rather than only local RNA velocity vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks an unspliced layer, since LatentVelo requires both spliced and unspliced count layers in AnnData Cells are unlikely to be reachable from a single initial state by continuous trajectories, e.g. disconnected populations like the microglia cluster in the dentate gyrus dataset Only steady-state, single-lineage velocity estimates are needed, where simpler linear methods such as scVelo stochastic mode may suffice

skills.description: Use when a LatentVelo model with zr_dim > 0 has been trained on spliced/unspliced AnnData and you need to test whether the latent regulatory state predicts divergent cell fates or lineage outcomes.
skills.name: latent-regulatory-state-analysis
skills.search_text: latent-regulatory-state-analysis Use when a LatentVelo model with zr_dim > 0 has been trained on spliced/unspliced AnnData and you need to test whether the latent regulatory state predicts divergent cell fates or lineage outcomes. The dataset has a single continuous lineage with no divergent fates — zr separation analysis is uninformative without distinct outcome groups A celltype-annotated model is required (use ltv.models.AnnotVAE with ltv.utils.anvi_clean_recipe and a celltype_key instead of the standard VAE/zr workflow) Cells form sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, where LatentVelo's latent trajectories may not start from expected initial states http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Analyzes the latent regulatory state (zr) inferred by LatentVelo's VAE to determine whether it separates cells into distinct dynamics regimes (e.g., reprogrammed vs. dead-end fates in the Biddy et al. fibroblast reprogramming dataset), using visualization on the latent UMAP and a logistic regression classifier with ROC evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Analyzes the latent regulatory state (zr) inferred by LatentVelo's VAE to determine whether it separates cells into distinct dynamics regimes (e.g., reprogrammed vs. dead-end fates in the Biddy et al. fibroblast reprogramming dataset), using visualization on the latent UMAP and a logistic regression classifier with ROC evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has a single continuous lineage with no divergent fates — zr separation analysis is uninformative without distinct outcome groups A celltype-annotated model is required (use ltv.models.AnnotVAE with ltv.utils.anvi_clean_recipe and a celltype_key instead of the standard VAE/zr workflow) Cells form sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, where LatentVelo's latent trajectories may not start from expected initial states

skills.description: Use when building an RNA velocity model that must capture lineage-dependent or time-dependent kinetics on single-cell spliced/unspliced data, e.g. bifurcating developmental systems where steady-state or linear dynamical models fail.
skills.name: latent-regulatory-state-structured-dynamics
skills.search_text: latent-regulatory-state-structured-dynamics Use when building an RNA velocity model that must capture lineage-dependent or time-dependent kinetics on single-cell spliced/unspliced data, e.g. bifurcating developmental systems where steady-state or linear dynamical models fail. The dataset has a single dominant lineage with simple time-independent kinetics, where linear methods like scVelo's dynamical model already suffice Data lacks both spliced and unspliced count layers in AnnData, since LatentVelo requires these two layers Sparse cell clusters have very few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — latent trajectories may not start from expected initial states in such cases http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implement LatentVelo's structured latent dynamics VAE, which embeds spliced/unspliced counts into latent states (zu, zs, zr) whose dynamics are integrated as neural ODEs, with a latent regulatory state zr and conditioning variable h enabling lineage-dependent dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Implement LatentVelo's structured latent dynamics VAE, which embeds spliced/unspliced counts into latent states (zu, zs, zr) whose dynamics are integrated as neural ODEs, with a latent regulatory state zr and conditioning variable h enabling lineage-dependent dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has a single dominant lineage with simple time-independent kinetics, where linear methods like scVelo's dynamical model already suffice Data lacks both spliced and unspliced count layers in AnnData, since LatentVelo requires these two layers Sparse cell clusters have very few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — latent trajectories may not start from expected initial states in such cases

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch single-cell dataset has been integrated with a disentangling model (e.g., CODAL) and you need to judge whether the new latent space corrects technical batch effects while preserving or improving biological cell-type separation, relative to a baseline latent space.
skills.name: latent-space-integration-benchmarking
skills.search_text: latent-space-integration-benchmarking Use when a multi-batch single-cell dataset has been integrated with a disentangling model (e.g., CODAL) and you need to judge whether the new latent space corrects technical batch effects while preserving or improving biological cell-type separation, relative to a baseline latent space. Single-batch datasets with no technical covariates to disentangle — there is no batch mixing to benchmark against a baseline. Datasets where cell states are not batch-confounded and standard scanpy PCA already separates cell types cleanly, so a disentangling model adds no benchmark value. Benchmarking against feature tables or precomputed embeddings that cannot be re-clustered; the comparison requires raw counts refit through both the model and the baseline pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarking a batch-corrected latent space (e.g., CODAL topic-model latent variables) against a baseline latent space (e.g., scanpy PCA) by visual inspection of UMAPs and comparison of batch mixing versus cell-type discrimination, as demonstrated on the Pijuan-Sala mouse gastrulation atlas with Tal1-/- chimeras. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Benchmarking a batch-corrected latent space (e.g., CODAL topic-model latent variables) against a baseline latent space (e.g., scanpy PCA) by visual inspection of UMAPs and comparison of batch mixing versus cell-type discrimination, as demonstrated on the Pijuan-Sala mouse gastrulation atlas with Tal1-/- chimeras.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-batch datasets with no technical covariates to disentangle — there is no batch mixing to benchmark against a baseline. Datasets where cell states are not batch-confounded and standard scanpy PCA already separates cell types cleanly, so a disentangling model adds no benchmark value. Benchmarking against feature tables or precomputed embeddings that cannot be re-clustered; the comparison requires raw counts refit through both the model and the baseline pipeline.

skills.search_text: latent-space-structural-validation Use when a fitted TCM model (from tcm(X, time.table)) must be verified against a simulated or real temporal scRNA-seq dataset before exporting or interpreting its 2D latent space and prototype layout. The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern (TCM's stated prerequisite) The goal is direct biological interpretation of cell clusters or trajectories — TCM output requires further pathway analysis and does not provide it immediately Input is a single time point or an atemporal population with no time.table, since the temporal convolving landscape cannot be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Structurally validates the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) temporal latent space: each time-point-specific subspace must contain the full H = R×S prototype grid, and the convolved global space must place early developmental stages near the center and later stages at the periphery. This checks that the prototype-based generative model reconstructed the expected radial temporal topology before the embedding is trusted. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05112-9
skills.summary: Structurally validates the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) temporal latent space: each time-point-specific subspace must contain the full H = R×S prototype grid, and the convolved global space must place early developmental stages near the center and later stages at the periphery. This checks that the prototype-based generative model reconstructed the expected radial temporal topology before the embedding is trusted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern (TCM's stated prerequisite) The goal is direct biological interpretation of cell clusters or trajectories — TCM output requires further pathway analysis and does not provide it immediately Input is a single time point or an atemporal population with no time.table, since the temporal convolving landscape cannot be constructed

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks ground-truth cluster edges / cell-type labels, so direction correctness cannot be assessed against expected maturation ordering The analysis needs gene-specific time on complex branching data better served by the independent FIT_OPTION='2' mode rather than a single unified latent time Only chromatin-accessibility-integrated velocity (e.g., MultiVelo-style) is required; UniTVelo models spliced/unspliced RNA only

When runtime is constrained — this method costs ~24 h versus ~3 min for the simple plug-in method When single-cell data type profiles cannot be treated as known (this inference assumes scRNA-seq E and scATAC-seq O profiles are available and fixed) When no HiChIP data linking enhancers to target genes exists and only coupled clustering of single cells is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 A Poisson model-based iterative MAP inference approach within DC3 that deconvolves bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loop counts into subpopulation-specific profiles by treating single-cell scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles as known and estimating the latent loop-count variable M_ij conditional on all other latent variables until convergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1

skills.description: Use when you have a layer-annotated stAPAminer object built from an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix and need to detect DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA gene sets, e.g. for ST-MOB replicates or merging into stAPA sets.
skills.name: layer-specific-apa-marker-detection
skills.search_text: layer-specific-apa-marker-detection Use when you have a layer-annotated stAPAminer object built from an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix and need to detect DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA gene sets, e.g. for ST-MOB replicates or merging into stAPA sets. Input is raw spatially barcoded reads without prior poly(A) site identification (scAPAtrap/Sierra) and imputation — the RUD matrix and layer annotations must already exist Data are single-cell scRNA-seq or image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH): APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing scRNA-seq tools The goal is spatially variable gene detection from the gene expression matrix alone — that is plain SPARK SV analysis, not spatial APA usage mining http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 This skill reproduces the stAPAminer workflow that identifies three classes of genes with spatial APA dynamics — DEAPA genes (differential APA usage between MOB morphological layers), LSAPA genes (layer-specific APA markers), and SVAPA genes (global spatial APA usage patterns) — from the kNN-imputed RUD (relative usage degree) matrix of spatially barcoded ST data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: This skill reproduces the stAPAminer workflow that identifies three classes of genes with spatial APA dynamics — DEAPA genes (differential APA usage between MOB morphological layers), LSAPA genes (layer-specific APA markers), and SVAPA genes (global spatial APA usage patterns) — from the kNN-imputed RUD (relative usage degree) matrix of spatially barcoded ST data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw spatially barcoded reads without prior poly(A) site identification (scAPAtrap/Sierra) and imputation — the RUD matrix and layer annotations must already exist Data are single-cell scRNA-seq or image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH): APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing scRNA-seq tools The goal is spatially variable gene detection from the gene expression matrix alone — that is plain SPARK SV analysis, not spatial APA usage mining

Direction of the gene-phenotype association is required from training alone — OTTERS cannot provide direction; only the sign of the per-method TWAS Z-score is available.

skills.summary: Computes linkage disequilibrium (r2) between significant ASAS SNPs and GWAS-catalog SNPs using 1000 Genomes phase 3 haplotypes, then tests enrichment of ASAS–GWAS linked pairs against ±1,000 bp random control SNPs via 10,000 permutations. skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to identify the causal SNP affecting splicing — LD tagging only surfaces tagging SNPs, not causal variants, which may lie within alternative exons or nearby intronic regions and are not tested by PAIRADISE Your SNPs are not covered by 1000 Genomes phase 3 haplotypes or lack nearby GWAS-catalog entries, making r2 computation or the enrichment null meaningless You need per-SNP association testing rather than a set-level enrichment test against a randomized ±1,000 bp control expectation

skills.description: Use when fitting LDA on single-cell data with known a priori labels (e.g., day0–day5 CyTOF markers) and you need to score candidate feature subsets to pick the subset with the class separation.

skills.search_text: lda-class-separation-scoring Use when fitting LDA on single-cell data with known a priori labels (e.g., day0–day5 CyTOF markers) and you need to score candidate feature subsets to pick the subset with the class separation. Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — supervised separation scoring is inappropriate in these situations. The dataset has more than ~100 dimensions, where HSS-based subset scoring is not computationally feasible. A large degree of heterogeneity exists within a class or there are many populations — separation-score-based subset selection will perform poorly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Scores candidate marker subsets produced by hybrid subset selection (HSS) with a selectable class-separation metric (euclidean, silhouette, pixel.entropy, pixel.density, or a custom function) so the feature set fed to LDA best separates a priori labels in single-cell data. It replaces manual, user-intensive tuning of the LDA input feature set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536

It replaces manual, user-intensive tuning of the LDA input feature set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — supervised separation scoring is inappropriate in these situations. skills.description: Use when single-cell clusters contain unannotated populations with unknown marker genes and you need functional annotation from GO enrichment signatures plus topic-model-based similarity, especially for plant scRNA-seq.
skills.name: lda-topic-modeling-on-single-cell-clusters
skills.search_text: lda-topic-modeling-on-single-cell-clusters Use when single-cell clusters contain unannotated populations with unknown marker genes and you need functional annotation from GO enrichment signatures plus topic-model-based similarity, especially for plant scRNA-seq. All clusters are already confidently annotated by marker genes or reference-based methods, so functional topic modeling adds no identity information The input is not a cluster-level pathway/functional signature matrix (e.g., raw counts or a feature table) — first run GSEA scoring with RunGSEA_plant The organism lacks a compatible plant GO knowledgebase mapping for the gene ID type (e.g., non-TAIR identifiers without conversion) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit an LDA topic model with CellFunTopic's runLDA on a cluster-by-GO-pathway matrix (built from scPlant's RunGSEA_plant output) to derive functional profiles of cell clusters and identify the identity of unannotated clusters via functional similarity networks, as demonstrated on Zhang et al. (2019) Arabidopsis root data where cluster 18 grouped with cortex clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Fit an LDA topic model with CellFunTopic's runLDA on a cluster-by-GO-pathway matrix (built from scPlant's RunGSEA_plant output) to derive functional profiles of cell clusters and identify the identity of unannotated clusters via functional similarity networks, as demonstrated on Zhang et al. (2019) Arabidopsis root data where cluster 18 grouped with cortex clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All clusters are already confidently annotated by marker genes or reference-based methods, so functional topic modeling adds no identity information The input is not a cluster-level pathway/functional signature matrix (e.g., raw counts or a feature table) — first run GSEA scoring with RunGSEA_plant The organism lacks a compatible plant GO knowledgebase mapping for the gene ID type (e.g., non-TAIR identifiers without conversion)

skills.description: Use when a pipeline includes data-driven steps such as feature ranking, selection, or scaling that must be re-fit inside every CV fold to avoid information leaking from held-out data into the model.
skills.name: leakage-free-cross-validation-fitting
skills.search_text: leakage-free-cross-validation-fitting Use when a pipeline includes data-driven steps such as feature ranking, selection, or scaling that must be re-fit inside every CV fold to avoid information leaking from held-out data into the model. Input is already a reduced/cleaned feature table with no data-dependent selection step remaining — a single global fit is then acceptable and per-fold refitting adds no protection You need a single fixed feature panel to deploy (e.g., for the iRNA5hmC-PS webserver); per-fold selectors differ across folds and are intended for unbiased performance estimation, not a final feature list The model itself performs embedded feature selection (e.g., L1-regularized logistic regression) inside the CV loop, making a separate Random Forest selector redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Fits data-dependent preprocessing/feature-selection steps (here, group-wise RandomForestClassifier Gini-importance selection for iRNA5hmC-PS) strictly on the training partition of each cross-validation fold, so that held-out folds remain untouched and performance estimates are unbiased. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: Fits data-dependent preprocessing/feature-selection steps (here, group-wise RandomForestClassifier Gini-importance selection for iRNA5hmC-PS) strictly on the training partition of each cross-validation fold, so that held-out folds remain untouched and performance estimates are unbiased.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced/cleaned feature table with no data-dependent selection step remaining — a single global fit is then acceptable and per-fold refitting adds no protection You need a single fixed feature panel to deploy (e.g., for the iRNA5hmC-PS webserver); per-fold selectors differ across folds and are intended for unbiased performance estimation, not a final feature list The model itself performs embedded feature selection (e.g., L1-regularized logistic regression) inside the CV loop, making a separate Random Forest selector redundant

Input is a query dataset for prediction only — use TOSICA.pre with an already-trained weight file instead of running an ablation The goal is simply to annotate cells rather than to evaluate whether expert-knowledge masks causally contribute to accuracy The reference dataset lacks a reliable label column in ref_adata.obs, since convergence curves require supervised validation accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains TOSICA models under multiple mask conditions (knowledge-based GMT masks vs parameter-matched random masks) and tracks per-epoch validation accuracy to determine epochs-to-convergence and converged accuracy, testing whether expert-knowledge masks are required for annotation performance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Trains TOSICA models under multiple mask conditions (knowledge-based GMT masks vs parameter-matched random masks) and tracks per-epoch validation accuracy to determine epochs-to-convergence and converged accuracy, testing whether expert-knowledge masks are required for annotation performance.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending the SnapCCESS hyperparameter sensitivity diagnostics — specifically when testing how the initial learning rate of the variational-autoencoder embedding step affects clustering performance on a multimodal single-cell omics dataset such as Swanson TEA-seq (GSE158013).

skills.search_text: learning-rate-sensitivity-analysis-of-embeddings Use when reproducing or extending the SnapCCESS hyperparameter sensitivity diagnostics — specifically when testing how the initial learning rate of the variational-autoencoder embedding step affects clustering performance on a multimodal single-cell omics dataset such as Swanson TEA-seq (GSE158013).
