The goal is standard SnapCCESS embedding generation and consensus clustering at fixed settings, not a sensitivity analysis of hyperparameters. The dataset is unimodal or lacks paired RNA/ADT modalities measured across the same cells, so the multimodal variational-autoencoder embedding step cannot be run as specified. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A diagnostic procedure for quantifying how sensitive SnapCCESS snapshot variational-autoencoder embedding quality and downstream consensus clustering are to the initial learning rate, by rerunning embedding generation at multiple learning rates and comparing adjusted Rand index (ARI) against reference cell-type labels, as reported in Supplementary Fig. S2a of the SnapCCESS paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: A diagnostic procedure for quantifying how sensitive SnapCCESS snapshot variational-autoencoder embedding quality and downstream consensus clustering are to the initial learning rate, by rerunning embedding generation at multiple learning rates and comparing adjusted Rand index (ARI) against reference cell-type labels, as reported in Supplementary Fig. S2a of the SnapCCESS paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tutorial/package explicitly does not recommend best parameters for new datasets — do not treat the 0.02-vs-0.2 comparison as a parameter recommendation for a different dataset without consulting the paper or tuning empirically. The goal is standard SnapCCESS embedding generation and consensus clustering at fixed settings, not a sensitivity analysis of hyperparameters. The dataset is unimodal or lacks paired RNA/ADT modalities measured across the same cells, so the multimodal variational-autoencoder embedding step cannot be run as specified.

skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset was part of the reference integration — sample-level split is required, so self-referential evaluation would inflate accuracy The biological goal is exploring a new query in the reference space rather than benchmarking mapping accuracy — use Run.ProjecTILs in standard mode instead The cell types of interest are absent from the reference atlas (e.g. γδ T cells, which were not represented at all) — classification benchmarks would be meaningless

skills.description: Use when assessing whether a cell type replicates across two or more scRNA-seq datasets: you have labeled cells per dataset, a gene set (e.g. GOmouse), and need an AUROC that reflects cross-dataset identity recovery rather than within-study clustering.

skills.search_text: leave-one-dataset-out-cross-validation Use when assessing whether a cell type replicates across two or more scRNA-seq datasets: you have labeled cells per dataset, a gene set (e.g. GOmouse), and need an AUROC that reflects cross-dataset identity recovery rather than within-study clustering. You lack corresponding cell-type labels across datasets — the supervised variant requires known correspondence; use unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with high-variance genes (variableGenes) instead All cells come from a single dataset — leave-one-dataset-out folds are undefined; there is no cross-dataset test set to hide The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than scoring replication of already-defined cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cross-dataset validation scheme in which all cell-type labels are hidden for one dataset at a time (the test set) and a neighbor-voting predictor on a Spearman rank-correlation cell network predicts the held-out identities, with recovery measured as AUROC and averaged across folds per gene set-by-cell-type pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack corresponding cell-type labels across datasets — the supervised variant requires known correspondence; use unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with high-variance genes (variableGenes) instead All cells come from a single dataset — leave-one-dataset-out folds are undefined; there is no cross-dataset test set to hide The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than scoring replication of already-defined cell types

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a trained single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet checkpoint) can distinguish seen from unseen cell types, or when calibrating per-cell probabilities and flagging low-confidence cells as 'unknown' before label transfer.

skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cell-type-generalization-evaluation Use when evaluating whether a trained single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet checkpoint) can distinguish seen from unseen cell types, or when calibrating per-cell probabilities and flagging low-confidence cells as 'unknown' before label transfer. skills.description: Use when comparing cancer-vs-normal classification accuracy of alternative gene sets (e.g., Wx-14 vs Peng-14 UGCBs) on a small-to-moderate TCGA expression matrix, where every sample must serve as a validation case to estimate generalization performance.
skills.name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cross-validation Use when comparing cancer-vs-normal classification accuracy of alternative gene sets (e.g., Wx-14 vs Peng-14 UGCBs) on a small-to-moderate TCGA expression matrix, where every sample must serve as a validation case to estimate generalization performance. The dataset is large enough for k-fold splits (e.g., GEO validation sets GSE72056/GSE40419/GSE103322, where the authors used 5-fold cross validation on train/dev/test splits instead of LOOCV) The goal is feature selection rather than evaluation — use the Wx discriminative-index (DI) ranking (iterated 10,000 times) to pick genes; LOOCV only scores a fixed, already-selected gene set Input is raw TCGA downloads — the samples must first be preprocessed into the TCGA_DATAS expression matrix before LOOCV can be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Leave-one-out cross validation (LOOCV) estimates the generalization performance of a classifier by training on n-1 samples and validating on the single held-out sample, repeated over every sample. skills.description: Use when you have a spatial dataset measuring a small panel of genes (e.g. bdtnp.txt in situ values at 3039 Drosophila embryo positions) and a matched scRNA-seq matrix, and you need to quantify how accurately an optimal-transport mapping reconstructs spatial expression of held-out genes.
skills.name: leave-one-out-cross-validation-evaluation
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cross-validation-evaluation Use when you have a spatial dataset measuring a small panel of genes (e.g. bdtnp.txt in situ values at 3039 Drosophila embryo positions) and a matched scRNA-seq matrix, and you need to quantify how accurately an optimal-transport mapping reconstructs spatial expression of held-out genes. No spatial reference measurements of even a small gene panel exist — the optimal transport mapping and its cross-validation require spatial values at known positions. The scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large, where per the article the computation can become intractable and one must approximate with a small number of landmark positions. The task is cell-cell communication or signaling-range inference (spsc.spatial_signaling_ot / infer_signal_range_ml) rather than spatial gene-expression reconstruction scoring. Evaluates SpaOTsc spatial gene-expression prediction by leave-one-out cross-validation over measured spatial genes: hold out one in situ gene, predict it at all spatial positions via the transport-plan-weighted cell average, and score against measured values with AUC, Spearman correlation (RS), and RMSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Evaluates SpaOTsc spatial gene-expression prediction by leave-one-out cross-validation over measured spatial genes: hold out one in situ gene, predict it at all spatial positions via the transport-plan-weighted cell average, and score against measured values with AUC, Spearman correlation (RS), and RMSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No spatial reference measurements of even a small gene panel exist — the optimal transport mapping and its cross-validation require spatial values at known positions. The scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large, where per the article the computation can become intractable and one must approximate with a small number of landmark positions. The task is cell-cell communication or signaling-range inference (spsc.spatial_signaling_ot / infer_signal_range_ml) rather than spatial gene-expression reconstruction scoring.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data are being mapped onto a spatial reference map of a small number of measured genes (e.g. 64-position in situ hybridization maps) and an unbiased estimate of spatial gene-expression reconstruction quality is needed.

skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cross-validation-of-spatial-gene-expression Use when scRNA-seq data are being mapped onto a spatial reference map of a small number of measured genes (e.g. 64-position in situ hybridization maps) and an unbiased estimate of spatial gene-expression reconstruction quality is needed. The dataset has no spatially measured reference genes or positions, so held-out spatial patterns cannot be scored (e.g. purely non-spatial scRNA-seq without an in situ map) The dataset is excessively large, since the article notes the optimal-transport computation 'can become intractable when the dataset is excessively large' — use landmark-position approximation instead of full LOOCV over all cell pairs Spatial measurements are live spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. seqFISH+, Slide-seq) where the goal is direct integration rather than reconstruction validated against a small gene panel http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates an scRNA-seq-to-spatial mapping produced by SpaOTsc by holding out each spatially measured gene, re-deriving the optimal transport plan, predicting the held-out gene's spatial pattern at each position, and scoring predictions with AUC, Spearman rank correlation (RS), and RMSE against the in situ reference map (e.g. the 64-position/47-gene zebrafish reference). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Validates an scRNA-seq-to-spatial mapping produced by SpaOTsc by holding out each spatially measured gene, re-deriving the optimal transport plan, predicting the held-out gene's spatial pattern at each position, and scoring predictions with AUC, Spearman rank correlation (RS), and RMSE against the in situ reference map (e.g. the 64-position/47-gene zebrafish reference).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no spatially measured reference genes or positions, so held-out spatial patterns cannot be scored (e.g. purely non-spatial scRNA-seq without an in situ map) The dataset is excessively large, since the article notes the optimal-transport computation 'can become intractable when the dataset is excessively large' — use landmark-position approximation instead of full LOOCV over all cell pairs Spatial measurements are live spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. seqFISH+, Slide-seq) where the goal is direct integration rather than reconstruction validated against a small gene panel

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq snapshot contains a multipotent population (e.g. MPPs) with competing downstream lineages, candidate priming RFs have already been filtered (type-1, low MPP-expression frequency), and you must prioritize which RFs and RF pairs define the primed state.
skills.name: leave-one-out-entropy-perturbation-ranking
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-entropy-perturbation-ranking Use when a scRNA-Seq snapshot contains a multipotent population (e.g. MPPs) with competing downstream lineages, candidate priming RFs have already been filtered (type-1, low MPP-expression frequency), and you must prioritize which RFs and RF pairs define the primed state. When only a single terminal lineage exists with no competing lineage or multipotent population — LOO entropy covariation is defined over competing lineage priming within a multipotent pool When candidate RFs have not been pre-filtered (e.g. type-1 low-frequency-in-MPP factors) — ranking the full RF set by LOO perturbation will be dominated by lineage-marker noise rather than priming factors When the goal is pseudotime-based tipping-point detection along a trajectory rather than snapshot priming detection; the article recommends trajectory tools like Palantir or other tipping-point methods (BioTIP, scGET) for that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in multipotent-cell priming by measuring how much the Distance Covariance Entropy (DICE) statistic degrades when each RF is removed (leave-one-out), and rank RF pairs by Spearman correlation of their expression covariation over the multipotent progenitor cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Rank candidate regulatory factors (RFs) implicated in multipotent-cell priming by measuring how much the Distance Covariance Entropy (DICE) statistic degrades when each RF is removed (leave-one-out), and rank RF pairs by Spearman correlation of their expression covariation over the multipotent progenitor cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single terminal lineage exists with no competing lineage or multipotent population — LOO entropy covariation is defined over competing lineage priming within a multipotent pool When candidate RFs have not been pre-filtered (e.g. type-1 low-frequency-in-MPP factors) — ranking the full RF set by LOO perturbation will be dominated by lineage-marker noise rather than priming factors When the goal is pseudotime-based tipping-point detection along a trajectory rather than snapshot priming detection; the article recommends trajectory tools like Palantir or other tipping-point methods (BioTIP, scGET) for that setting

The target genes have no measured ground-truth expression in the ST data, so MAE against measured values cannot be computed The ST data is seq-based (e.g. Visium) with spot-level mixtures rather than single-cell image-based data where leave-one-out on a gene panel is defined The reference scRNA-seq does not cover the held-out genes, leaving no basis for the generative model to impute them http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark spatial gene-expression imputation accuracy by removing known cortical layer marker genes (Cux2, Otof, Rorb, Rspo1, Sulf2, Fezf2, Osr1) from a MERFISH panel, imputing each held-out gene with SpatialScope and baseline methods, and scoring predictions by mean absolute error (MAE). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w

skills.description: Use when a MAPiT (or other measure-preserving pseudotime) reconstruction must be shown to be robust to the choice of markers fed into the pseudotime algorithm — e.g. spheroid flow cytometry data with multiple stains where input-marker bias is a concern.
skills.name: leave-one-out-marker-subset-cross-validation
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-marker-subset-cross-validation Use when a MAPiT (or other measure-preserving pseudotime) reconstruction must be shown to be robust to the choice of markers fed into the pseudotime algorithm — e.g. spheroid flow cytometry data with multiple stains where input-marker bias is a concern. The true-scale target distribution cannot be derived theoretically — e.g. stem cell differentiation, where cell death and cell division rates at every stage are not measured The goal is real-time (temporal) rather than spatial reconstruction — the cell-density-versus-distance-from-surface distribution used here applies only to the spheroid spatial scale A pseudotime ordering whose cell order cannot be trusted is the input — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order, so LOOCV on a bad ordering will not rescue it A robustness validation scheme for MAPiT spatial reconstruction: pseudotime trajectories are recomputed with each leave-one-out subset of the measured markers (DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) as input, transformed to the distance-from-spheroid-surface scale, and the resulting marker distance profiles are checked against the full-marker-set profiles and microscopic Ki-67 cross-sections. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: A robustness validation scheme for MAPiT spatial reconstruction: pseudotime trajectories are recomputed with each leave-one-out subset of the measured markers (DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) as input, transformed to the distance-from-spheroid-surface scale, and the resulting marker distance profiles are checked against the full-marker-set profiles and microscopic Ki-67 cross-sections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The true-scale target distribution cannot be derived theoretically — e.g. stem cell differentiation, where cell death and cell division rates at every stage are not measured The goal is real-time (temporal) rather than spatial reconstruction — the cell-density-versus-distance-from-surface distribution used here applies only to the spheroid spatial scale A pseudotime ordering whose cell order cannot be trusted is the input — MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order, so LOOCV on a bad ordering will not rescue it

skills.description: Use when validating a PROGENy model built from the 11-pathway perturbation compendium (208 ArrayExpress submissions, 580 experiments): you need evidence that pathway scores recover the perturbed pathway for experiments not seen during model construction.
skills.name: leave-one-out-model-validation
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-model-validation Use when validating a PROGENy model built from the 11-pathway perturbation compendium (208 ArrayExpress submissions, 580 experiments): you need evidence that pathway scores recover the perturbed pathway for experiments not seen during model construction. When the goal is benchmarking PROGENy against other pathway methods (GSVA, SPIA, Pathifier, PARADIGM) on fixed data — use the full perturbation-recall comparison instead When the pathway under study is not among the 11 perturbation pathways (e.g. pathway lacks sufficient ArrayExpress perturbation experiments to fit a leave-one-out model) When the expression data are not z-scored relative to proper controls — the regression is defined on per-experiment z-scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluates whether PROGENy pathway-activity scores generalize to perturbation experiments excluded from model building. skills.summary: Evaluates whether PROGENy pathway-activity scores generalize to perturbation experiments excluded from model building. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is benchmarking PROGENy against other pathway methods (GSVA, SPIA, Pathifier, PARADIGM) on fixed data — use the full perturbation-recall comparison instead When the pathway under study is not among the 11 perturbation pathways (e.g. pathway lacks sufficient ArrayExpress perturbation experiments to fit a leave-one-out model) When the expression data are not z-scored relative to proper controls — the regression is defined on per-experiment z-scores

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS, SSN) against known per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks generated by dyngen, using AUROC/AUPR.
skills.name: leave-one-out-network-differencing
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-network-differencing Use when benchmarking cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS, SSN) against known per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks generated by dyngen, using AUROC/AUPR. When no per-cell ground-truth regulatory network is available for quantitative AUROC/AUPR evaluation, since quantitative assessment of CSNI performance was previously lacking for exactly this reason When the goal is aggregate (pooled) network inference rather than cell-specific network inference across individual cells When sensitivity to noise is critical — leave-one-out correlation differencing yields correlation differences that are mostly noise (SSN performed worse than LIONESS and pySCENIC) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A cell-specific network inference (CSNI) strategy that predicts a per-cell gene regulatory network by subtracting the leave-one-out (aggregate-of-all-other-cells) network from the whole-dataset network, as implemented by LIONESS and SSN. Applied on dyngen's 42 simulated single-cell datasets to quantitatively benchmark against cell-specific ground-truth GRNs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: A cell-specific network inference (CSNI) strategy that predicts a per-cell gene regulatory network by subtracting the leave-one-out (aggregate-of-all-other-cells) network from the whole-dataset network, as implemented by LIONESS and SSN. Applied on dyngen's 42 simulated single-cell datasets to quantitatively benchmark against cell-specific ground-truth GRNs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no per-cell ground-truth regulatory network is available for quantitative AUROC/AUPR evaluation, since quantitative assessment of CSNI performance was previously lacking for exactly this reason When the goal is aggregate (pooled) network inference rather than cell-specific network inference across individual cells When sensitivity to noise is critical — leave-one-out correlation differencing yields correlation differences that are mostly noise (SSN performed worse than LIONESS and pySCENIC)

skills.description: Use when computing PC1-based gene set activity scores (e.g. rROMA on MSigDB Hallmark sets) and genes within a set distort the one-dimensional variance, so aberrant genes must be excluded before scoring.
skills.name: leave-one-out-pc1-variance-outlier-scoring
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-pc1-variance-outlier-scoring Use when computing PC1-based gene set activity scores (e.g. rROMA on MSigDB Hallmark sets) and genes within a set distort the one-dimensional variance, so aberrant genes must be excluded before scoring. Genes already belong to fewer than the OutlierRarelyFoundThr number of gene sets (e.g. <~2 of 50 Hallmark sets) — the article states such genes are exempt and not considered outliers The goal is outlier detection of samples, not genes — the article uses a separate two-step sample filtering based on detected-gene counts and PCA projection in gene space with a distance threshold Data are raw counts — rRoma requires normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before any PC1 computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 rROMA's outlier gene detection procedure: for each gene in a gene set, recompute the percentage of variance explained by PC1 (L1) with that gene removed (leave-one-out), z-score normalize the resulting L1 distribution, and flag genes whose removal abnormally changes L1 as outliers, with Fisher-test and rare-gene safeguards. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: rROMA's outlier gene detection procedure: for each gene in a gene set, recompute the percentage of variance explained by PC1 (L1) with that gene removed (leave-one-out), z-score normalize the resulting L1 distribution, and flag genes whose removal abnormally changes L1 as outliers, with Fisher-test and rare-gene safeguards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes already belong to fewer than the OutlierRarelyFoundThr number of gene sets (e.g. <~2 of 50 Hallmark sets) — the article states such genes are exempt and not considered outliers The goal is outlier detection of samples, not genes — the article uses a separate two-step sample filtering based on detected-gene counts and PCA projection in gene space with a distance threshold Data are raw counts — rRoma requires normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) before any PC1 computation

skills.search_text: leave-one-out-resampling-robustness-analysis Use when a learned representation (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs trained on multi-cohort single-cell data) must be shown to be robust to the removal of any single training cohort before it is reused for annotation. skills.description: Use when you have embeddings from single-cell manifold-alignment methods on datasets with known cell-type labels (e.g. Full PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) and need to quantify unsupervised structure recovery via ARI.

skills.search_text: leiden-clustering-of-aligned-single-cell-embeddings Use when you have embeddings from single-cell manifold-alignment methods on datasets with known cell-type labels (e.g. Full PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) and need to quantify unsupervised structure recovery via ARI. The data are raw expression/count matrices that have not yet been aligned into a common embedding space — this skill presupposes post-alignment embeddings from methods such as scTopoGAN, UnionCom, or MMD-MA. The datasets have no known cell-type labels, so the ARI between Leiden assignments and ground-truth labels cannot be computed. The goal is alignment method development (e.g. obtaining embeddings via get_TopoAE_Embeddings/run_scTopoGAN) rather than downstream evaluation of existing aligned embeddings. Evaluates whether aligned single-cell embeddings (e.g. from scTopoGAN, topoAE, UnionCom, MMD-MA, UMAP) preserve biological structure by running Leiden clustering at a resolution matched to the number of known cell classes and scoring cluster-label agreement with the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Evaluates whether aligned single-cell embeddings (e.g. from scTopoGAN, topoAE, UnionCom, MMD-MA, UMAP) preserve biological structure by running Leiden clustering at a resolution matched to the number of known cell classes and scoring cluster-label agreement with the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw expression/count matrices that have not yet been aligned into a common embedding space — this skill presupposes post-alignment embeddings from methods such as scTopoGAN, UnionCom, or MMD-MA. The datasets have no known cell-type labels, so the ARI between Leiden assignments and ground-truth labels cannot be computed. The goal is alignment method development (e.g. obtaining embeddings via get_TopoAE_Embeddings/run_scTopoGAN) rather than downstream evaluation of existing aligned embeddings.

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell integration or batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra vs. Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) and you need resolution-robust ARI/NMI/ASW metrics on each method's embedding.
skills.name: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep
skills.search_text: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep Use when comparing single-cell integration or batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra vs. Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) and you need resolution-robust ARI/NMI/ASW metrics on each method's embedding. The goal is routine cell-type annotation or downstream biological interpretation of a single embedding, not a method benchmark — a single fixed Leiden resolution is sufficient and the sweep adds no information. You need distribution-free or full-dimensional evaluation: the scCobra paper notes scores were derived from two-dimensional UMAP embeddings following SCALEX, so results are dependent on that UMAP projection. No ground-truth cell-type labels or batch labels are available for the cells, since ARI, NMI, CellType ASW, and batch-removal metrics all require them. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks integrated single-cell embeddings by running Leiden clustering over a resolution sweep (0.1–2.0 in 0.1 increments) via the scIB pipeline, so batch-removal and biological-conservation metrics (ARI, NMI, Batch ASW, CellType ASW, Graph Connectivity) are not artifacts of a single clustering granularity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks integrated single-cell embeddings by running Leiden clustering over a resolution sweep (0.1–2.0 in 0.1 increments) via the scIB pipeline, so batch-removal and biological-conservation metrics (ARI, NMI, Batch ASW, CellType ASW, Graph Connectivity) are not artifacts of a single clustering granularity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is routine cell-type annotation or downstream biological interpretation of a single embedding, not a method benchmark — a single fixed Leiden resolution is sufficient and the sweep adds no information. You need distribution-free or full-dimensional evaluation: the scCobra paper notes scores were derived from two-dimensional UMAP embeddings following SCALEX, so results are dependent on that UMAP projection. No ground-truth cell-type labels or batch labels are available for the cells, since ARI, NMI, CellType ASW, and batch-removal metrics all require them.

skills.search_text: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep Use when you have QC-filtered multimodal single-cell data (RNA, ATAC, ADT/CITE-Seq) and need per-modality Leiden annotations at multiple resolutions as players for downstream decision-level integration (scTriangulate) or ensemble clustering. If you already have a curated, low-resolution cell-type annotation and only want to refine specific subpopulations — Cytocipher's merge strategy expects deliberate over-clustering, not near-final labels If the data has not been processed with the scanpy standard workflow to log-cpm normalised values — Cytocipher's code enrichment and merging assume that normalisation state http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Deliberately over-cluster log-cpm normalised scRNA-seq data with Leiden at high resolution to generate tentative cluster labels, which Cytocipher then statistically tests and merges into significantly different cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Deliberately over-cluster log-cpm normalised scRNA-seq data with Leiden at high resolution to generate tentative cluster labels, which Cytocipher then statistically tests and merges into significantly different cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you already have a curated, low-resolution cell-type annotation and only want to refine specific subpopulations — Cytocipher's merge strategy expects deliberate over-clustering, not near-final labels If the data has not been processed with the scanpy standard workflow to log-cpm normalised values — Cytocipher's code enrichment and merging assume that normalisation state

skills.description: Use when a multiresolution archetypal decomposition (e.g., ACTIONet run_ACTIONet output) yields many overlapping archetypes across resolutions and you need a nonredundant set of cell-state patterns for downstream comparison or annotation.
skills.name: leiden-pattern-graph-pruning
skills.search_text: leiden-pattern-graph-pruning Use when a multiresolution archetypal decomposition (e.g., ACTIONet run_ACTIONet output) yields many overlapping archetypes across resolutions and you need a nonredundant set of cell-state patterns for downstream comparison or annotation. When patterns come from a fixed-k decomposition (e.g., cNMF with a priori k=12) that already produces a single nonredundant set rather than a multiresolution stack of redundant archetypes. When the input is a clustering of cells rather than archetypal patterns — Leiden here is applied over the pattern graph, not the cell-cell graph used for cell clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A network-based feature-selection step from ACTIONet that removes redundant archetypal patterns from a multiresolution decomposition: the Leiden graph-clustering algorithm is run over the pattern graph to define equivalent pattern classes, and one nonredundant representative pattern is kept per class. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: A network-based feature-selection step from ACTIONet that removes redundant archetypal patterns from a multiresolution decomposition: the Leiden graph-clustering algorithm is run over the pattern graph to define equivalent pattern classes, and one nonredundant representative pattern is kept per class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When patterns come from a fixed-k decomposition (e.g., cNMF with a priori k=12) that already produces a single nonredundant set rather than a multiresolution stack of redundant archetypes. When the input is a clustering of cells rather than archetypal patterns — Leiden here is applied over the pattern graph, not the cell-cell graph used for cell clustering.

skills.description: Use when you have a numeric cell-embedding matrix (e.g. from Mowgli, MOFA+, or integrative NMF) and need clusterings at multiple granularities to compute resolution-dependent clustering metrics such as ARI.
skills.name: leiden-resolution-sweep-clustering
skills.search_text: leiden-resolution-sweep-clustering Use when you have a numeric cell-embedding matrix (e.g. from Mowgli, MOFA+, or integrative NMF) and need clusterings at multiple granularities to compute resolution-dependent clustering metrics such as ARI. The input comes from Seurat v4 WNN, which provides no cell embedding and no silhouette score — cluster with Seurat's FindClusters instead The data are raw counts or preprocessed Muon objects rather than a fitted embedding — run the integration method (Mowgli, MOFA+, etc.) first Only a single fixed cluster granularity is needed with no resolution-dependent metric — a single Leiden call suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters cell embeddings by building a kNN graph (k=20, Euclidean distance) with Scanpy and running Leiden across a sweep of resolutions so that benchmark metrics like ARI can be computed across cluster granularities, as done in the Mowgli vs. state-of-the-art benchmark on paired single-cell multi-omics datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Clusters cell embeddings by building a kNN graph (k=20, Euclidean distance) with Scanpy and running Leiden across a sweep of resolutions so that benchmark metrics like ARI can be computed across cluster granularities, as done in the Mowgli vs. state-of-the-art benchmark on paired single-cell multi-omics datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input comes from Seurat v4 WNN, which provides no cell embedding and no silhouette score — cluster with Seurat's FindClusters instead The data are raw counts or preprocessed Muon objects rather than a fitted embedding — run the integration method (Mowgli, MOFA+, etc.) first Only a single fixed cluster granularity is needed with no resolution-dependent metric — a single Leiden call suffices

skills.description: Use when you have a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., PILOT's Wasserstein W over scRNA-seq samples in an AnnData with patient/disease columns) and need to detect unsupervised patient sub-groups and pick the Leiden resolution.
skills.name: leiden-sample-level-clustering-silhouette-selection
skills.search_text: leiden-sample-level-clustering-silhouette-selection Use when you have a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., PILOT's Wasserstein W over scRNA-seq samples in an AnnData with patient/disease columns) and need to detect unsupervised patient sub-groups and pick the Leiden resolution. Samples already carry labels or a known trajectory — PILOT's unsupervised clustering is intended for unlabeled sample-level comparison; prior label-based methods (PhEMD, SCANCell, Multi-scale PHATE) 'require labels of patients for their analysis and cannot be used in the unsupervised analysis'. The data mix distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — the article flags cross-technology analysis as 'still an open challenge', and PILOT assumes uniformly collected tissue samples. The goal is cell-level rather than sample-level clustering — this skill operates on the sample distance matrix W, not on individual cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Unsupervised Leiden clustering of single-cell samples on PILOT's Wasserstein-distance matrix (W), with the Leiden resolution chosen by maximizing the Silhouette Score via PILOT's select_best_sil plot, to detect patient-level subgroups such as the PDAC 11-control/14-Tumor1/10-Tumor2 split. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Unsupervised Leiden clustering of single-cell samples on PILOT's Wasserstein-distance matrix (W), with the Leiden resolution chosen by maximizing the Silhouette Score via PILOT's select_best_sil plot, to detect patient-level subgroups such as the PDAC 11-control/14-Tumor1/10-Tumor2 split.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples already carry labels or a known trajectory — PILOT's unsupervised clustering is intended for unlabeled sample-level comparison; prior label-based methods (PhEMD, SCANCell, Multi-scale PHATE) 'require labels of patients for their analysis and cannot be used in the unsupervised analysis'. The data mix distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — the article flags cross-technology analysis as 'still an open challenge', and PILOT assumes uniformly collected tissue samples. The goal is cell-level rather than sample-level clustering — this skill operates on the sample distance matrix W, not on individual cells.

skills.description: Use when a batch-integrated single-cell atlas (e.g. wild-type + Tal1-/- chimeric E6.5-E8.5 embryos in a CODAL topic latent space) contains a coarse Leiden cluster enriched for hemato-endothelial progenitors that must be split into finer perturbation-affected subtypes.
skills.name: leiden-subclustering-of-hematopoietic-progenitors
skills.search_text: leiden-subclustering-of-hematopoietic-progenitors Use when a batch-integrated single-cell atlas (e.g. wild-type + Tal1-/- chimeric E6.5-E8.5 embryos in a CODAL topic latent space) contains a coarse Leiden cluster enriched for hemato-endothelial progenitors that must be split into finer perturbation-affected subtypes. skills.summary: High-resolution Leiden subclustering of hemato-endothelial progenitor (HE-prog) cells within the CODAL topic-model latent space of the mouse gastrulation atlas, isolating perturbation-induced Tal1-/- subclusters (A-E) and annotating them by mesodermal marker gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been batch-integrated — subclustering raw scanpy PCA space will confound batch effects with cell state when chimeric status is batch-confounded The dataset is a single-batch atlas without a perturbation or batch-confounded cell states, so CODAL integration and chimera-vs-wildtype subclustering add no value The target cluster is already well resolved at coarse resolution and contains no rare or perturbation-induced populations to discover

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a leukemia (or carcinoma) cell subpopulation must be projected onto a healthy reference atlas to identify its healthy counterpart, subtype, and lineage/developmental stage.
skills.name: leukemia-counterpart-mapping-onto-hematopoietic-reference
skills.search_text: leukemia-counterpart-mapping-onto-hematopoietic-reference Use when scRNA-seq data from a leukemia (or carcinoma) cell subpopulation must be projected onto a healthy reference atlas to identify its healthy counterpart, subtype, and lineage/developmental stage. Goal is to analyze relationships only among leukemia subpopulations without a healthy reference — the paper notes such studies 'lost the whole picture of leukemogenesis' Target cells are unclustered single cells: CCI projects cell clusters to the reference rather than single cells, so cells must be properly clustered first No healthy reference atlas is available or the reference files cannot be formatted as the required four-file toy-data format (expression matrix, gene list, cell types, cell identity) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Applies the CCI (counterpart composite index) tool, which integrates multiple statistics (expression level, co-expression, and dimension-reduction embedding space) in a composite likelihood/Bayes-factor framework, to map a leukemia cell subpopulation onto a healthy hematopoietic reference atlas and assign it a healthy counterpart. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41421-020-00223-4
skills.summary: Applies the CCI (counterpart composite index) tool, which integrates multiple statistics (expression level, co-expression, and dimension-reduction embedding space) in a composite likelihood/Bayes-factor framework, to map a leukemia cell subpopulation onto a healthy hematopoietic reference atlas and assign it a healthy counterpart.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is to analyze relationships only among leukemia subpopulations without a healthy reference — the paper notes such studies 'lost the whole picture of leukemogenesis' Target cells are unclustered single cells: CCI projects cell clusters to the reference rather than single cells, so cells must be properly clustered first No healthy reference atlas is available or the reference files cannot be formatted as the required four-file toy-data format (expression matrix, gene list, cell types, cell identity)

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing long-read (FASTQ/FASTA) data against a known barcode whitelist and you need edit-distance-tolerant barcode matching with a unique--match assignment rule.
skills.name: levenshtein-barcode-matching
skills.search_text: levenshtein-barcode-matching Use when demultiplexing long-read (FASTQ/FASTA) data against a known barcode whitelist and you need edit-distance-tolerant barcode matching with a unique--match assignment rule. Only flanking sequences are known and the barcode itself must be discovered (Flexiplex's discovery mode is a different workflow). The task is filtering an existing barcode-count table against a whitelist or removing empty droplets — use flexiplex-filter's inflection-point method instead. Input is aligned BAM/single-cell count matrices rather than raw FASTQ/FASTA reads (e.g. downstream steps of epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reimplements Flexiplex's barcode-assignment logic: extract the barcode+UMI region between error-tolerant flank hits, then match the extracted barcode to a whitelist using Levenshtein distance, reporting an assignment only when the minimal edit distance is attained by exactly one barcode. This reproduces Flexiplex's accuracy (Fig. 1D) on simulated long-read data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102
skills.summary: Reimplements Flexiplex's barcode-assignment logic: extract the barcode+UMI region between error-tolerant flank hits, then match the extracted barcode to a whitelist using Levenshtein distance, reporting an assignment only when the minimal edit distance is attained by exactly one barcode. This reproduces Flexiplex's accuracy (Fig. 1D) on simulated long-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only flanking sequences are known and the barcode itself must be discovered (Flexiplex's discovery mode is a different workflow). The task is filtering an existing barcode-count table against a whitelist or removing empty droplets — use flexiplex-filter's inflection-point method instead. skills.description: Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq counts with scVI (e.g. from a PBMC4k pilot with 4182 cells and 1000 HVGs) and you must decide whether library-size factors come from the per-cell posterior or from the Normal(l_mu, 1) prior variant.
skills.name: library-size-factor-modeling
skills.search_text: library-size-factor-modeling Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq counts with scVI (e.g. from a PBMC4k pilot with 4182 cells and 1000 HVGs) and you must decide whether library-size factors come from the per-cell posterior or from the Normal(l_mu, 1) prior variant. You need synthetic data faithful to individual pilot observations — the posterior-sampling variant (the standard approach) is designed for that, and the prior variant explicitly avoids copies of the original observations. Your dataset requires batch correction — the paper examined all models without using potentially available batch correction capabilities, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 In the scVI generative pipeline from Treppner et al. (2021), library-size factors are modeled probabilistically so that synthetic UMI counts have realistic per-cell sequencing depth. In the prior-sampling variant, library sizes are drawn from Normal(l_mu, 1) — where l_mu is the learned library-size mean — instead of from the inferred per-cell library-size posterior. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: In the scVI generative pipeline from Treppner et al. (2021), library-size factors are modeled probabilistically so that synthetic UMI counts have realistic per-cell sequencing depth. In the prior-sampling variant, library sizes are drawn from Normal(l_mu, 1) — where l_mu is the learned library-size mean — instead of from the inferred per-cell library-size posterior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need synthetic data faithful to individual pilot observations — the posterior-sampling variant (the standard approach) is designed for that, and the prior variant explicitly avoids copies of the original observations. Your dataset requires batch correction — the paper examined all models without using potentially available batch correction capabilities, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects.

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv, cells as rows, genes as columns) must be library-size normalized with median-of-totals scaling to make counts comparable across cells prior to imputation or downstream analysis.

skills.search_text: library-size-median-normalization Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv, cells as rows, genes as columns) must be library-size normalized with median-of-totals scaling to make counts comparable across cells prior to imputation or downstream analysis. The matrix is already pre-processed and stored in the <dataset_name>.{mat, csv} format consumed by AutoImpute.py — re-normalizing would double-scale the counts. The analysis requires per-gene rather than per-cell normalization, or a normalization scheme incompatible with feeding AutoImpute (e.g. SCTransform-style variance stabilization on raw counts). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalizes a raw scRNA-seq count matrix by dividing each read count by its cell's total counts and scaling by the median of total read counts across cells, as implemented in the AutoImpute pre-processing pipeline before autoencoder imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Normalizes a raw scRNA-seq count matrix by dividing each read count by its cell's total counts and scaling by the median of total read counts across cells, as implemented in the AutoImpute pre-processing pipeline before autoencoder imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is already pre-processed and stored in the <dataset_name>.{mat, csv} format consumed by AutoImpute.py — re-normalizing would double-scale the counts. The analysis requires per-gene rather than per-cell normalization, or a normalization scheme incompatible with feeding AutoImpute (e.g. SCTransform-style variance stabilization on raw counts).
