skills.name: library-size-normalization-cp10k
skills.search_text: library-size-normalization-cp10k Use when raw scRNAseq UMI counts must be summed over cells of each annotated cell type per sample/circadian time point and scaled to CP10K before running JTK_Cycle on pseudobulk series. Input is already normalized expression (e.g., SCTransform-normalized or log-transformed matrices) rather than raw UMI counts — CP10K re-scaling of normalized values double-corrects library size Data is a single-cell-level prediction task — the article notes tauFisher 'cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and thus cannot predict circadian time at a single cell level', so pseudobulk aggregation is required first No cell-type annotations or circadian time points are available to define pseudobulk aggregation groups Aggregates raw UMI counts to per-cell-type pseudobulk matrices per circadian time point and library-size normalizes each pseudobulk sample to counts per 10,000 (CP10K), preparing scRNAseq-derived series for JTK_Cycle rhythm detection with MetaCycle via tauFisher. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: Aggregates raw UMI counts to per-cell-type pseudobulk matrices per circadian time point and library-size normalizes each pseudobulk sample to counts per 10,000 (CP10K), preparing scRNAseq-derived series for JTK_Cycle rhythm detection with MetaCycle via tauFisher.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized expression (e.g., SCTransform-normalized or log-transformed matrices) rather than raw UMI counts — CP10K re-scaling of normalized values double-corrects library size Data is a single-cell-level prediction task — the article notes tauFisher 'cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and thus cannot predict circadian time at a single cell level', so pseudobulk aggregation is required first No cell-type annotations or circadian time points are available to define pseudobulk aggregation groups

skills.description: Use when fitting per-gene/per-feature GLMs (e.g., Tweedie CPLM/ZICP) to raw scRNA-seq counts or semi-continuous omics data with unequal sequencing depth, so that differences in depth are absorbed by an offset log(S) rather than by transforming counts.
skills.name: library-size-offset-estimation
skills.search_text: library-size-offset-estimation Use when fitting per-gene/per-feature GLMs (e.g., Tweedie CPLM/ZICP) to raw scRNA-seq counts or semi-continuous omics data with unequal sequencing depth, so that differences in depth are absorbed by an offset log(S) rather than by transforming counts. Input is already normalized or transformed (e.g., log-CPM, TPM, relative abundances that already absorbed depth) — the offset would double-correct for sequencing depth Zero-inflation is a property of only a subset of genes — the paper notes Tweedieverse is not architected for gene-specific zero-inflation affecting a gene subset Data are continuous quantities unrelated to sequencing depth where a size-factor offset has no sampling-depth interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates per-cell (or per-sample) library sizes/normalization factors and enters them as a log-scale offset in per-feature regression models, avoiding ad hoc normalization or transformation prior to differential testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Estimates per-cell (or per-sample) library sizes/normalization factors and enters them as a log-scale offset in per-feature regression models, avoiding ad hoc normalization or transformation prior to differential testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or transformed (e.g., log-CPM, TPM, relative abundances that already absorbed depth) — the offset would double-correct for sequencing depth Zero-inflation is a property of only a subset of genes — the paper notes Tweedieverse is not architected for gene-specific zero-inflation affecting a gene subset Data are continuous quantities unrelated to sequencing depth where a size-factor offset has no sampling-depth interpretation

skills.description: Use when a BiG-SCAPE GCF absence/presence matrix at 0.70 distance is available together with lifestyle metadata per genome, and the goal is to rank GCF families significantly enriched in one lifestyle group (e.g., plant pathogens vs non-plant-pathogens).
skills.name: lifestyle-associated-bgc-identification
skills.search_text: lifestyle-associated-bgc-identification Use when a BiG-SCAPE GCF absence/presence matrix at 0.70 distance is available together with lifestyle metadata per genome, and the goal is to rank GCF families significantly enriched in one lifestyle group (e.g., plant pathogens vs non-plant-pathogens). The input is a gene-cluster (homolog) absence/presence matrix rather than a BiG-SCAPE GCF matrix — use the gene-level lifestyle-associated gene (LAG) analysis with 70% group presence and >2 log2 fold change thresholds instead. GCFs are not yet clustered (only raw antiSMASH BGC annotations exist) — run BiG-SCAPE at 0.70 distance to build the absence/presence matrix first. The analysis goal is lifestyle prediction/classification via the random forest model rather than identification of associated BGCs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Identifies biosynthetic gene cluster families (GCFs) statistically associated with a bacterial lifestyle (e.g., plant pathogenicity) by applying Fisher's exact tests to a BiG-SCAPE GCF absence/presence matrix with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, as done in bacLIFE for Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Identifies biosynthetic gene cluster families (GCFs) statistically associated with a bacterial lifestyle (e.g., plant pathogenicity) by applying Fisher's exact tests to a BiG-SCAPE GCF absence/presence matrix with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, as done in bacLIFE for Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia and Pseudomonas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a gene-cluster (homolog) absence/presence matrix rather than a BiG-SCAPE GCF matrix — use the gene-level lifestyle-associated gene (LAG) analysis with 70% group presence and >2 log2 fold change thresholds instead. GCFs are not yet clustered (only raw antiSMASH BGC annotations exist) — run BiG-SCAPE at 0.70 distance to build the absence/presence matrix first. The analysis goal is lifestyle prediction/classification via the random forest model rather than identification of associated BGCs.

skills.description: Use when you have clustered scRNA-seq data (discrete cell groups or pseudotime-ordered continuous states) and need to predict significant ligand-receptor interactions and signaling pathways between cell populations.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-communication-inference
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-communication-inference Use when you have clustered scRNA-seq data (discrete cell groups or pseudotime-ordered continuous states) and need to predict significant ligand-receptor interactions and signaling pathways between cell populations. Input data has not been cell-clustered — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis Input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell-resolution inference — use CellChat v3 (SpatialCellChat) instead You need validated ground-truth communication interactions — systematic evaluation of predicted networks is challenging due to the lack of ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infer, filter, and analyze cell-cell ligand-receptor communication networks from scRNA-seq using CellChat's mass-action/Hill-function model with the curated CellChatDB, then quantify signaling roles via centrality metrics and pattern recognition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Infer, filter, and analyze cell-cell ligand-receptor communication networks from scRNA-seq using CellChat's mass-action/Hill-function model with the curated CellChatDB, then quantify signaling roles via centrality metrics and pattern recognition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been cell-clustered — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis Input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell-resolution inference — use CellChat v3 (SpatialCellChat) instead You need validated ground-truth communication interactions — systematic evaluation of predicted networks is challenging due to the lack of ground truth

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq from developmental systems (e.g. EPI/PE lineages of blastoids or blastocysts) to infer autocrine/paracrine LR signaling dynamics and LR-to-TF causal relationships along pseudotime trajectories.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-communication-inference-early-embryo
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-communication-inference-early-embryo Use when analyzing scRNA-seq from developmental systems (e.g. EPI/PE lineages of blastoids or blastocysts) to infer autocrine/paracrine LR signaling dynamics and LR-to-TF causal relationships along pseudotime trajectories. Communication is not mediated by ligand-receptor interactions (e.g. EV-mediated communication) — the framework does not account for other communication types Goal is maternal-embryo interaction analysis — the autocrine hypothesis in eLR screening precludes this Cell types are already definitive and static (e.g. mature tissue) — tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat designed for communication between given cell types may suffice; TimeTalk targets temporal developmental data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 TimeTalk-based inference of ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communication from pseudotime-ordered scRNA-seq trajectories, testing LR-to-TF causal relationships via cellAlign trajectory alignment and Granger causality. Designed for early embryo development where definitive cell types emerge late. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: TimeTalk-based inference of ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communication from pseudotime-ordered scRNA-seq trajectories, testing LR-to-TF causal relationships via cellAlign trajectory alignment and Granger causality. Designed for early embryo development where definitive cell types emerge late.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Communication is not mediated by ligand-receptor interactions (e.g. EV-mediated communication) — the framework does not account for other communication types Goal is maternal-embryo interaction analysis — the autocrine hypothesis in eLR screening precludes this Cell types are already definitive and static (e.g. mature tissue) — tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat designed for communication between given cell types may suffice; TimeTalk targets temporal developmental data

skills.description: Use when you need to load, audit, or validate a manually curated ligand–receptor interaction database (e.g. ICELLNET Supplementary Data 1) before using it for cell–cell communication scoring, or when reproducing its family-level and subfamily-level interaction counts.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-database-curation-validation
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-database-curation-validation Use when you need to load, audit, or validate a manually curated ligand–receptor interaction database (e.g. ICELLNET Supplementary Data 1) before using it for cell–cell communication scoring, or when reproducing its family-level and subfamily-level interaction counts. You are using ICELLNET v2 (1669 interactions) rather than the v1 database of the 2021 paper — expected counts of 380/194 will fail and the database has a new structure You want to score communication between transcriptomic samples — use the ICELLNET communication-score quantification workflow instead, which consumes this validated database as input You need a non-human, non-expert-curated interaction set — ICELLNET's database is curated exclusively from human studies and is deliberately smaller than other databases (e.g. CellPhoneDB) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Reproduce and validate the ICELLNET expert-curated ligand–receptor interaction database (380 curated interactions across 6 families: Growth factors, Cytokines, Chemokines, Immune Checkpoints, Notch signaling, Antigen binding/other), including the 194 cytokine-receptor interactions across 7 subfamilies, by loading Supplementary Data 1 from the soumelis-lab/ICELLNET repository and comparing observed counts against expected values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: Reproduce and validate the ICELLNET expert-curated ligand–receptor interaction database (380 curated interactions across 6 families: Growth factors, Cytokines, Chemokines, Immune Checkpoints, Notch signaling, Antigen binding/other), including the 194 cytokine-receptor interactions across 7 subfamilies, by loading Supplementary Data 1 from the soumelis-lab/ICELLNET repository and comparing observed counts against expected values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are using ICELLNET v2 (1669 interactions) rather than the v1 database of the 2021 paper — expected counts of 380/194 will fail and the database has a new structure You want to score communication between transcriptomic samples — use the ICELLNET communication-score quantification workflow instead, which consumes this validated database as input You need a non-human, non-expert-curated interaction set — ICELLNET's database is curated exclusively from human studies and is deliberately smaller than other databases (e.g. CellPhoneDB)

skills.description: Use when inferring cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq and interactions must be restricted to literature-supported ligand-receptor pairs, or when comparing tools whose one-ligand/one-receptor assumptions mis-handle multi-subunit receptor complexes.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-database-mapping
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-database-mapping Use when inferring cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq and interactions must be restricted to literature-supported ligand-receptor pairs, or when comparing tools whose one-ligand/one-receptor assumptions mis-handle multi-subunit receptor complexes. The goal is discovering novel, uncurated interactions — CellChatDB mapping only recovers literature-supported pairs, so de novo interaction discovery is out of scope The analysis requires protein-level validation — mRNA levels are only used to approximate protein levels, and single-cell proteomic information is not capturable at present Ground-truth evaluation of predicted networks is needed — no ground truth exists for systematic evaluation of predicted cell-cell communication networks http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Map predicted cell-cell signaling interactions to a curated ligand-receptor database (CellChatDB, built on KEGG) that accounts for multi-subunit receptor complexes and cofactors, enabling principled pathway-level classification and cross-tool benchmarking of communication inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Map predicted cell-cell signaling interactions to a curated ligand-receptor database (CellChatDB, built on KEGG) that accounts for multi-subunit receptor complexes and cofactors, enabling principled pathway-level classification and cross-tool benchmarking of communication inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovering novel, uncurated interactions — CellChatDB mapping only recovers literature-supported pairs, so de novo interaction discovery is out of scope The analysis requires protein-level validation — mRNA levels are only used to approximate protein levels, and single-cell proteomic information is not capturable at present Ground-truth evaluation of predicted networks is needed — no ground truth exists for systematic evaluation of predicted cell-cell communication networks

skills.description: Use when inferring neural-specific ligand-receptor communication from human single-nucleus/single-cell RNA-seq of brain tissue (e.g., cortical ASD vs control) and you must pick the correct species-specific interaction DB.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-database-usage-human-brain
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-database-usage-human-brain Use when inferring neural-specific ligand-receptor communication from human single-nucleus/single-cell RNA-seq of brain tissue (e.g., cortical ASD vs control) and you must pick the correct species-specific interaction DB. Input data are from mouse — use DB='mouse' (183 entries) instead of DB='human' The analysis requires small-molecule neurotransmitter signaling under non-neural, protein-only ligand-receptor databases such as CellChat or CellPhoneDB, which exclude glutamate and GABA and underestimate their ligand abundance The task is spatial proximity modeling without expression matrices — spatially constrained workflows need centroid metadata and proximity thresholds, not just the interaction DB http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Select and apply NeuronChat's curated human neural interaction database (NeuronChatDB, 190 human entries of 373 total) when inferring cell-cell communication from human brain snRNA-seq data, e.g., ASD vs control cortical comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Select and apply NeuronChat's curated human neural interaction database (NeuronChatDB, 190 human entries of 373 total) when inferring cell-cell communication from human brain snRNA-seq data, e.g., ASD vs control cortical comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are from mouse — use DB='mouse' (183 entries) instead of DB='human' The analysis requires small-molecule neurotransmitter signaling under non-neural, protein-only ligand-receptor databases such as CellChat or CellPhoneDB, which exclude glutamate and GABA and underestimate their ligand abundance The task is spatial proximity modeling without expression matrices — spatially constrained workflows need centroid metadata and proximity thresholds, not just the interaction DB

skills.description: Use when a signaling pathway's spatial range must be estimated from scRNA-seq data and the canonical ligand, receptor, and downstream target genes for that pathway are known and can be listed explicitly.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-downstream-gene-selection
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-downstream-gene-selection Use when a signaling pathway's spatial range must be estimated from scRNA-seq data and the canonical ligand, receptor, and downstream target genes for that pathway are known and can be listed explicitly. The ligand/receptor/downstream genes for the pathway of interest are unknown — the article notes that 'cell–cell communication inference relies on known genes involved in specific signaling' You only have a cell–cell communication score requirement without spatial range estimation; spatial_signaling_ot alone suffices and gene-list-based range inference is unnecessary No spatial cell–cell distance matrix exists yet (run the transport_plan and cell_cell_distance steps first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the known ligand, receptor, and downstream target genes that define a signaling system of interest so SpaOTsc can infer its spatial signaling range. This curated gene triple (e.g. Wnt5/fz with CycD and dpp as downstream genes) supplies both the random-forest features and the sample weights for range estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Selects the known ligand, receptor, and downstream target genes that define a signaling system of interest so SpaOTsc can infer its spatial signaling range. This curated gene triple (e.g. Wnt5/fz with CycD and dpp as downstream genes) supplies both the random-forest features and the sample weights for range estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ligand/receptor/downstream genes for the pathway of interest are unknown — the article notes that 'cell–cell communication inference relies on known genes involved in specific signaling' You only have a cell–cell communication score requirement without spatial range estimation; spatial_signaling_ot alone suffices and gene-list-based range inference is unnecessary No spatial cell–cell distance matrix exists yet (run the transport_plan and cell_cell_distance steps first)

skills.description: Use when constructing or reproducing ligand-receptor edge weights from a normalised single-cell expression matrix plus cell-type annotations, e.g. to validate NATMI's ExtractEdges.py weighting scheme or recompute edge_weights.csv independently.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-edge-quantification
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-edge-quantification Use when constructing or reproducing ligand-receptor edge weights from a normalised single-cell expression matrix plus cell-type annotations, e.g. to validate NATMI's ExtractEdges.py weighting scheme or recompute edge_weights.csv independently. You need heteromeric ligand/receptor complexes, co-receptor requirements, downstream signalling consequences (NicheNet/SoptSC), or spatial context — NATMI models only simple binary ligand-receptor pairs from mRNA abundance You need absolute binding kinetics or protein-level concentrations — the weights are mRNA-based and subject to dropouts, not protein measurements The input is raw, unnormalised counts — weights are only comparable if profiles are first normalised per total UMI and rescaled ×1,000,000 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Quantify cell-to-cell communication edges as two NATMI weights: a mean-expression weight (mean ligand in sender × mean receptor in receiver) and a specificity weight (product of cell-type-normalised expression fractions, 0–1), after filtering edges through the >20% detection-rate rule on connectomeDB2020 (lrc2p) ligand-receptor pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Quantify cell-to-cell communication edges as two NATMI weights: a mean-expression weight (mean ligand in sender × mean receptor in receiver) and a specificity weight (product of cell-type-normalised expression fractions, 0–1), after filtering edges through the >20% detection-rate rule on connectomeDB2020 (lrc2p) ligand-receptor pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need heteromeric ligand/receptor complexes, co-receptor requirements, downstream signalling consequences (NicheNet/SoptSC), or spatial context — NATMI models only simple binary ligand-receptor pairs from mRNA abundance You need absolute binding kinetics or protein-level concentrations — the weights are mRNA-based and subject to dropouts, not protein measurements The input is raw, unnormalised counts — weights are only comparable if profiles are first normalised per total UMI and rescaled ×1,000,000

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce, verify, or interpret the edge attributes Connectome emits for every celltype-to-celltype ligand–receptor mechanism, or when you must compute normalized-slot (w1) vs z-score-based (w2) weights independently from Seurat-normalized data.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-edge-weight-computation
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-edge-weight-computation Use when you need to reproduce, verify, or interpret the edge attributes Connectome emits for every celltype-to-celltype ligand–receptor mechanism, or when you must compute normalized-slot (w1) vs z-score-based (w2) weights independently from Seurat-normalized data. You need statistical confidence calls per edge — pass p.values = TRUE to CreateConnectome instead of computing only w1/w2 point estimates. Strongly paired ligand–receptor expression is being treated as direct evidence of cell–cell communication; the article explicitly states it is not, and suspension-based scRNAseq does not preserve spatial proximity. Downstream differential connectomics (DifferentialConnectome) is the goal and a completed connectome edgelist already exists — use filtering/differential functions rather than recomputing raw edgeweights. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct how Connectome assigns edgeweights to ligand–receptor edges: weightnorm (w1), the product of celltype-wise normalized ligand and receptor expression, and weightscale (w2), the mean of gene-wise system z-scores which encodes signal specificity across the whole tissue system. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Reconstruct how Connectome assigns edgeweights to ligand–receptor edges: weightnorm (w1), the product of celltype-wise normalized ligand and receptor expression, and weightscale (w2), the mean of gene-wise system z-scores which encodes signal specificity across the whole tissue system.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need statistical confidence calls per edge — pass p.values = TRUE to CreateConnectome instead of computing only w1/w2 point estimates. Strongly paired ligand–receptor expression is being treated as direct evidence of cell–cell communication; the article explicitly states it is not, and suspension-based scRNAseq does not preserve spatial proximity. Downstream differential connectomics (DifferentialConnectome) is the goal and a completed connectome edgelist already exists — use filtering/differential functions rather than recomputing raw edgeweights.

skills.description: Use when building ligand–receptor communication edges from single-cell expression data and you need to decide which genes count as 'expressed' per cell type before edge extraction.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-expression-filtering
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-expression-filtering Use when building ligand–receptor communication edges from single-cell expression data and you need to decide which genes count as 'expressed' per cell type before edge extraction. Input data are not normalised to counts per million — detection/expression thresholds assume CPM-scaled values, so apply NATMI's normalisation (divide by total UMIs/reads, multiply by 1,000,000) first You need heteromeric complex modelling or co-receptor requirements — NATMI does not model these, so filtering simple pairs is the wrong fit You need spatially resolved communication predictions — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 NATMI-style filtering that declares a ligand or receptor 'expressed' in a cell type only when detected in more than 20% of that cell type's cells and optionally requires mean expression above 10 counts-per-million, yielding a per-cell-type detection/expression summary used to gate predicted communication edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: NATMI-style filtering that declares a ligand or receptor 'expressed' in a cell type only when detected in more than 20% of that cell type's cells and optionally requires mean expression above 10 counts-per-million, yielding a per-cell-type detection/expression summary used to gate predicted communication edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not normalised to counts per million — detection/expression thresholds assume CPM-scaled values, so apply NATMI's normalisation (divide by total UMIs/reads, multiply by 1,000,000) first You need heteromeric complex modelling or co-receptor requirements — NATMI does not model these, so filtering simple pairs is the wrong fit You need spatially resolved communication predictions — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data

skills.description: Use when preparing a gene-by-cell-population expression matrix (microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or scRNA-seq) for ICELLNET communication scoring, so that highly expressed molecules like chemokines do not dominate interaction scores.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-gene-normalization
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-gene-normalization Use when preparing a gene-by-cell-population expression matrix (microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or scRNA-seq) for ICELLNET communication scoring, so that highly expressed molecules like chemokines do not dominate interaction scores. The expression data are non-human: the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies The data have already been max-scaled to the 0-10 range; reapplying the scaling would distort values The goal is differential expression or clustering rather than ligand-receptor communication scoring, where max-scaling would erase absolute-expression information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ICELLNET's scaling procedure for ligand/receptor gene expression: each gene is divided by its maximum value (computed as the mean of the top 5% highest expression values) and multiplied by 10, so values fall in a bounded 0-10 range before computing ligand-receptor interaction and global communication scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: ICELLNET's scaling procedure for ligand/receptor gene expression: each gene is divided by its maximum value (computed as the mean of the top 5% highest expression values) and multiplied by 10, so values fall in a bounded 0-10 range before computing ligand-receptor interaction and global communication scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are non-human: the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies The data have already been max-scaled to the 0-10 range; reapplying the scaling would distort values The goal is differential expression or clustering rather than ligand-receptor communication scoring, where max-scaling would erase absolute-expression information

skills.description: Use when validating that an identified set of ligand-receptor genes (e.g. eLRs) is enriched or depleted for reference gene sets, and you need a defensible background universe — all protein-coding genes and/or an all-known-LR baseline.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-gene-pair-background-definition
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-gene-pair-background-definition Use when validating that an identified set of ligand-receptor genes (e.g. eLRs) is enriched or depleted for reference gene sets, and you need a defensible background universe — all protein-coding genes and/or an all-known-LR baseline. The query set is not composed of ligand-receptor genes — the LR-baseline correction is meaningless for unrelated gene panels. Reference gene sets or the protein-coding universe are unavailable or incompatible in gene identifier space, so overlap counts would be spuriously small. The goal is differential expression rather than set-overreach testing; hypergeometric background definition does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Defines the statistical universes (all-protein-coding genes and all known mouse ligand-receptor genes from CellTalkDB, 2034 pairs) against which the 430 TimeTalk eLR genes are tested for enrichment/depletion, using one-tailed hypergeometric tests in R. Proper background choice distinguishes LR-specific biology (e.g. essential-gene enrichment surviving LR-baseline correction) from genome-wide artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Defines the statistical universes (all-protein-coding genes and all known mouse ligand-receptor genes from CellTalkDB, 2034 pairs) against which the 430 TimeTalk eLR genes are tested for enrichment/depletion, using one-tailed hypergeometric tests in R. Proper background choice distinguishes LR-specific biology (e.g. essential-gene enrichment surviving LR-baseline correction) from genome-wide artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query set is not composed of ligand-receptor genes — the LR-baseline correction is meaningless for unrelated gene panels. Reference gene sets or the protein-coding universe are unavailable or incompatible in gene identifier space, so overlap counts would be spuriously small. The goal is differential expression rather than set-overreach testing; hypergeometric background definition does not apply.

skills.description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for Connectome ligand-receptor mapping: the expression matrix must be subset to the union of ligand and receptor genes from ncomms8866_mouse/human before NormalizeData/ScaleData and CreateConnectome.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-gene-subsetting-against-fantom5
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-gene-subsetting-against-fantom5 Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for Connectome ligand-receptor mapping: the expression matrix must be subset to the union of ligand and receptor genes from ncomms8866_mouse/human before NormalizeData/ScaleData and CreateConnectome. The goal is unbiased gene-level analysis (e.g. FindMarkers differential expression on all genes) rather than ligand-receptor network construction — subsetting would discard non-connectome genes A researcher-hypothesized mechanism is not in FANTOM5 — the database must be customized, since extraneous or missing connections are bounded by the ground-truth list The dataset is already an edgelist/connectome output; this step operates upstream on raw expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Restricts a single-cell expression matrix to the union of ligand and receptor approved symbols drawn from the FANTOM5-derived ligand-receptor database (ncomms8866_mouse/human in the Connectome package) so that downstream CreateConnectome calls compute signaling edgelists only over known ligand-receptor mechanisms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Restricts a single-cell expression matrix to the union of ligand and receptor approved symbols drawn from the FANTOM5-derived ligand-receptor database (ncomms8866_mouse/human in the Connectome package) so that downstream CreateConnectome calls compute signaling edgelists only over known ligand-receptor mechanisms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unbiased gene-level analysis (e.g. FindMarkers differential expression on all genes) rather than ligand-receptor network construction — subsetting would discard non-connectome genes A researcher-hypothesized mechanism is not in FANTOM5 — the database must be customized, since extraneous or missing connections are bounded by the ground-truth list The dataset is already an edgelist/connectome output; this step operates upstream on raw expression data

skills.description: Use when you have expression values for retained L-R pairs across ordered developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 E12.5–E17.5 corticogenesis) and need to identify which interactions peak at which stage.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-gene-time-series-profiling
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-gene-time-series-profiling Use when you have expression values for retained L-R pairs across ordered developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 E12.5–E17.5 corticogenesis) and need to identify which interactions peak at which stage. Data are from a single stationary condition with no developmental-series time points — dsCellNet's DTW and fuzzy clustering leverage temporal information and a single time-point map cannot capture dynamic interaction changes Input is a cell-cell interaction network table rather than per-time-point gene expression of L-R pairs — clustering operates on standardized expression changes of the L-R pairs, not on network edges You only need a single-time-point cell-cell interaction network; use dsCellNet's singlenet workflow instead of the developmental clustering step http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Profiles the temporal expression trajectories of ligand-receptor (L-R) pair genes across developmental-series time points and groups them with Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering into temporal clusters that pinpoint key time points of interaction activity during corticogenesis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Profiles the temporal expression trajectories of ligand-receptor (L-R) pair genes across developmental-series time points and groups them with Mfuzz fuzzy c-means clustering into temporal clusters that pinpoint key time points of interaction activity during corticogenesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from a single stationary condition with no developmental-series time points — dsCellNet's DTW and fuzzy clustering leverage temporal information and a single time-point map cannot capture dynamic interaction changes Input is a cell-cell interaction network table rather than per-time-point gene expression of L-R pairs — clustering operates on standardized expression changes of the L-R pairs, not on network edges You only need a single-time-point cell-cell interaction network; use dsCellNet's singlenet workflow instead of the developmental clustering step

skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-curation Use when building or updating a curated ligand-receptor pair list from existing resources (CellPhoneDB, RNA-Magnet, SingleCellSignalR/LRdb, ICELLNET) and prior connectomes, requiring PubMedID-level literature verification before network inference. skills.summary: Curate a literature-supported ligand-receptor interaction database (connectomeDB2020, 2,293 human pairs) by merging and manually validating pairs from CellPhoneDB v2.0, RNA-Magnet, SingleCellSignalR LRdb, ICELLNET, a prior 2015 resource, and new manual curation, for use as NATMI's '--interDB' input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need heteromeric ligand or receptor complexes or co-receptor requirements modeled — these are excluded during curation and not modeled in NATMI You need predicted interactions without literature support, downstream signaling consequences (e.g. NicheNet-style), or spatially resolved interaction inference You only need to run NATMI on an existing database — connectomeDB2020 ships precompiled with NATMI and its Docker image

skills.description: Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) have been resolved to single-cell resolution via SpatialScope decomposition and you need to identify significant ligand-receptor pairs between spatially co-located cell types, such as EC–SMC signaling in a vascular region of interest.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-interaction-detection-in-spatial-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-detection-in-spatial-transcriptomics Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) have been resolved to single-cell resolution via SpatialScope decomposition and you need to identify significant ligand-receptor pairs between spatially co-located cell types, such as EC–SMC signaling in a vascular region of interest. The ST data are still at spot level (Visium ~55 μm spots containing multiple cells) without prior single-cell decomposition, since communication analysis on mixed spots is unreliable You only need spot-level cell-type proportions (deconvolution); RCTD/Cell2location/CARD suffice and no ligand-receptor testing is required Image-based ST data already at single-cell resolution but with only a few hundred genes, where the whole-transcriptome ligand-receptor database cannot be evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect significant ligand-receptor signaling pairs between cell types located in a spatial transcriptomics dataset by running Giotto's spatCellCellcom on SpatialScope single-cell-resolution output, using a Delaunay-triangulation spatial network and strict significance/expression filters. This makes spot-level Visium data usable for cell-cell communication analysis that the original ~55 μm spot resolution cannot support. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Detect significant ligand-receptor signaling pairs between cell types located in a spatial transcriptomics dataset by running Giotto's spatCellCellcom on SpatialScope single-cell-resolution output, using a Delaunay-triangulation spatial network and strict significance/expression filters. This makes spot-level Visium data usable for cell-cell communication analysis that the original ~55 μm spot resolution cannot support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ST data are still at spot level (Visium ~55 μm spots containing multiple cells) without prior single-cell decomposition, since communication analysis on mixed spots is unreliable You only need spot-level cell-type proportions (deconvolution); RCTD/Cell2location/CARD suffice and no ligand-receptor testing is required Image-based ST data already at single-cell resolution but with only a few hundred genes, where the whole-transcriptome ligand-receptor database cannot be evaluated

skills.description: Use when you have multiple ligand-receptor interaction resources and want to detect over-/underrepresentation of pathway, cancer, or tissue-enriched protein annotations in each resource relative to a pooled background.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-interaction-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-enrichment-analysis Use when you have multiple ligand-receptor interaction resources and want to detect over-/underrepresentation of pathway, cancer, or tissue-enriched protein annotations in each resource relative to a pooled background. When the goal is benchmarking CCC inference methods against expression data (spatial colocalisation, cytokine activities, receptor protein abundance) rather than characterizing annotation bias of the resources themselves When quantifying raw resource overlap (number of unique or shared interactions) rather than testing enrichment against a pooled background When no pooled multi-resource background is available, since Fisher's exact test requires the 2x2 contingency of resource vs pooled background membership http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether individual cell-cell communication (CCC) ligand-receptor resources are biased toward specific biological annotations (SignaLink/NetPath pathways, CancerSEA cancer gene sets, Human Protein Atlas tissue-enriched proteins, DisGeNet) using Fisher's exact tests against the pooled collection of all 16 resources, with odds ratios summarized in a heatmap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Tests whether individual cell-cell communication (CCC) ligand-receptor resources are biased toward specific biological annotations (SignaLink/NetPath pathways, CancerSEA cancer gene sets, Human Protein Atlas tissue-enriched proteins, DisGeNet) using Fisher's exact tests against the pooled collection of all 16 resources, with odds ratios summarized in a heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is benchmarking CCC inference methods against expression data (spatial colocalisation, cytokine activities, receptor protein abundance) rather than characterizing annotation bias of the resources themselves When quantifying raw resource overlap (number of unique or shared interactions) rather than testing enrichment against a pooled background When no pooled multi-resource background is available, since Fisher's exact test requires the 2x2 contingency of resource vs pooled background membership

skills.description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor CCI data (e.g. from CellChat on scRNA-seq) subset to a specific viewpoint such as directed outgoing interactions of one cell cluster, and you need to annotate enriched interaction pairs by biological function before grouping them into modules.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-interaction-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-functional-annotation Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor CCI data (e.g. from CellChat on scRNA-seq) subset to a specific viewpoint such as directed outgoing interactions of one cell cluster, and you need to annotate enriched interaction pairs by biological function before grouping them into modules. You need to predict ligand-receptor interactions from raw scRNA-seq expression — InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed, inferred ligand−receptor interactions and does not perform the prediction itself The CCI data come from a tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR); the article notes extension to other published tools is planned future work You require a command-line, scripted, or remotely hosted analysis — InterCellar is an interactive local Shiny app, and remote web-based tools raise data privacy issues for unpublished patient data http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Functional annotation of enriched ligand-receptor interaction pairs in InterCellar's function-verse, linking predicted CCI pairs to Gene Ontology and pathway resources so that groups of interactions with similar functional patterns (int-pair modules) can be defined. This is the step that turns raw predicted interactions into biologically interpretable modules, e.g. ECM/integrin signaling or ANXA1–FPR signaling in melanoma. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Functional annotation of enriched ligand-receptor interaction pairs in InterCellar's function-verse, linking predicted CCI pairs to Gene Ontology and pathway resources so that groups of interactions with similar functional patterns (int-pair modules) can be defined. This is the step that turns raw predicted interactions into biologically interpretable modules, e.g. ECM/integrin signaling or ANXA1–FPR signaling in melanoma.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to predict ligand-receptor interactions from raw scRNA-seq expression — InterCellar's workflow builds upon pre-computed, inferred ligand−receptor interactions and does not perform the prediction itself The CCI data come from a tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR); the article notes extension to other published tools is planned future work You require a command-line, scripted, or remotely hosted analysis — InterCellar is an interactive local Shiny app, and remote web-based tools raise data privacy issues for unpublished patient data

skills.description: Use when a developmental-series scRNA-seq dataset (expression matrix + cell-type labels + time-point annotations) needs cell-cell interaction inference that distinguishes membrane- from secreted-ligand signaling and tracks dynamic interaction changes across time points.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference Use when a developmental-series scRNA-seq dataset (expression matrix + cell-type labels + time-point annotations) needs cell-cell interaction inference that distinguishes membrane- from secreted-ligand signaling and tracks dynamic interaction changes across time points. The dataset is a single stationary time point with no developmental series information — the DTW reinforcement and fuzzy clustering across time points, dsCellNet's key advantage, cannot be exploited The signaling of interest is absent from the default 5,744-pair L-R list (e.g. reported missing MG–Neurons interactions) and no supplementary L-R gene list can be provided A per-method runtime or accuracy benchmark against NATMI, CellPhoneDB or SingleCellSignalR is the goal rather than interaction inference itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Infer cell–cell communication networks from developmental-series scRNA-seq with dsCellNet, which scores membrane- and secreted-ligand interactions separately against a 5,744-pair L-R database, then reinforces interactions with dynamic time warping and fuzzy clustering to recover key time points and mediator cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Infer cell–cell communication networks from developmental-series scRNA-seq with dsCellNet, which scores membrane- and secreted-ligand interactions separately against a 5,744-pair L-R database, then reinforces interactions with dynamic time warping and fuzzy clustering to recover key time points and mediator cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a single stationary time point with no developmental series information — the DTW reinforcement and fuzzy clustering across time points, dsCellNet's key advantage, cannot be exploited The signaling of interest is absent from the default 5,744-pair L-R list (e.g. reported missing MG–Neurons interactions) and no supplementary L-R gene list can be provided A per-method runtime or accuracy benchmark against NATMI, CellPhoneDB or SingleCellSignalR is the goal rather than interaction inference itself

skills.description: Use when analyzing cell-cell communication in SC data lacking native spatial coordinates but with a matched ST reference (e.g., Stereo-seq E9.5), to compare gene-expression-only vs spatially-informed LRI detection.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference Use when analyzing cell-cell communication in SC data lacking native spatial coordinates but with a matched ST reference (e.g., Stereo-seq E9.5), to compare gene-expression-only vs spatially-informed LRI detection. Query SC data and ST reference have a large gap/mismatch — forcing SC assignment to resemble the ST can introduce bias, and MDS-based mapping loses the reference's cell-distribution pre-knowledge Target tissues have a high level of repeating elements, which poses a challenge for spatial reconstruction of SC cells You need a strict gold-standard CCC validation — the reference CCCs here were identified through the same spatially-reconstructed approach, introducing circularity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Infers ligand-receptor interactions (LRIs) and local cell-cell communications from single-cell RNA-seq data by incorporating CellContrast-reconstructed spatial locations, using CellChat for gene-expression-only global inference and spatialDM for spatially-informed detection, thereby reducing false positives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Infers ligand-receptor interactions (LRIs) and local cell-cell communications from single-cell RNA-seq data by incorporating CellContrast-reconstructed spatial locations, using CellChat for gene-expression-only global inference and spatialDM for spatially-informed detection, thereby reducing false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query SC data and ST reference have a large gap/mismatch — forcing SC assignment to resemble the ST can introduce bias, and MDS-based mapping loses the reference's cell-distribution pre-knowledge Target tissues have a high level of repeating elements, which poses a challenge for spatial reconstruction of SC cells You need a strict gold-standard CCC validation — the reference CCCs here were identified through the same spatially-reconstructed approach, introducing circularity

skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw counts and has not been normalized by library size and log-transformed, since CommPath expects normalized expression values The goal is intercellular signaling inference only, without examining activated pathways in receiver cells or downstream communication chains, where lighter tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat suffice The organism is not among the species for which CommPath provides LR and pathway databases (human, mouse, rat, zebrafish, fruitfly, worm)
