skills.summary: Infer and visualise cell-to-cell communication networks from single-cell gene expression data using NATMI, which scores ligand-receptor edges from connectomeDB2020 by expression detection rates and dataset-specific summed-specificity weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Spatial transcriptomics data — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data Questions requiring downstream signalling consequence prediction or ligand-receptor binding kinetics — NATMI does not model these Interactions requiring heteromeric complexes, heterodimerization or co-receptors — NATMI does not model them

skills.description: Use when you have a heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq dataset with cell-type annotations and want to infer cell–cell communication as ligand–receptor edges (e.g., VEGF, PDGF, DLL3-NOTCH signaling) between cell identities.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-network-mapping
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-network-mapping Use when you have a heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq dataset with cell-type annotations and want to infer cell–cell communication as ligand–receptor edges (e.g., VEGF, PDGF, DLL3-NOTCH signaling) between cell identities. Strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication; do not treat mapped edges as confirmed signaling without follow-up validation Suspension-based single-cell sequencing does not preserve spatial histologic information, so the method cannot verify spatial proximity of candidate interactions Output quality is bounded by the ground-truth ligand–receptor database; do not use for mechanisms absent from the reference list unless a user-provided database is supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Maps ligand–receptor signaling edges between cell types in a Seurat single-cell RNA-seq object using the Connectome R package against the FANTOM5-derived ncomms8866 database (or a user-supplied mechanism list), producing a weighted, directional edgelist of cell-type-to-cell-type signaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Maps ligand–receptor signaling edges between cell types in a Seurat single-cell RNA-seq object using the Connectome R package against the FANTOM5-derived ncomms8866 database (or a user-supplied mechanism list), producing a weighted, directional edgelist of cell-type-to-cell-type signaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Strongly paired ligand and receptor expression is not direct evidence of cell–cell communication; do not treat mapped edges as confirmed signaling without follow-up validation Suspension-based single-cell sequencing does not preserve spatial histologic information, so the method cannot verify spatial proximity of candidate interactions Output quality is bounded by the ground-truth ligand–receptor database; do not use for mechanisms absent from the reference list unless a user-provided database is supplied

skills.description: Use when building a cell-cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you must split a curated L-R pair database into membrane-ligand, secreted-ligand, and membrane-receptor classes before computing interaction weights.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-classification
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-classification Use when building a cell-cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you must split a curated L-R pair database into membrane-ligand, secreted-ligand, and membrane-receptor classes before computing interaction weights. Published methods' single undistinguished L-R list is sufficient — i.e., you do not need to separate membrane-ligand from secreted-ligand significance calculations Your organism is not supported by the homologene human/mouse homolog database and you cannot provide custom gene-identifier mappings You only have a single stationary-condition expression map and no cell-type structure — the localization-aware split and downstream per-cell-type weighting require cell-type labeled data http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classify known ligand-receptor pairs into membrane-ligand, secreted-ligand and membrane-receptor categories using protein localization information and multi-species homology mapping, as done in dsCellNet to enable separate significance calculation for membrane vs secreted ligand-mediated interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Classify known ligand-receptor pairs into membrane-ligand, secreted-ligand and membrane-receptor categories using protein localization information and multi-species homology mapping, as done in dsCellNet to enable separate significance calculation for membrane vs secreted ligand-mediated interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Published methods' single undistinguished L-R list is sufficient — i.e., you do not need to separate membrane-ligand from secreted-ligand significance calculations Your organism is not supported by the homologene human/mouse homolog database and you cannot provide custom gene-identifier mappings You only have a single stationary-condition expression map and no cell-type structure — the localization-aware split and downstream per-cell-type weighting require cell-type labeled data

skills.description: Use when building or rebuilding the reference LR interaction database needed for cell-cell communication inference (e.g., CommPath, CellPhoneDB-style pipelines) from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 resources.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-database-curation
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-database-curation Use when building or rebuilding the reference LR interaction database needed for cell-cell communication inference (e.g., CommPath, CellPhoneDB-style pipelines) from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 resources. The goal is downstream LR inference itself (findLRpairs, filterLR) rather than building the reference database — those steps require the curated database plus scRNA-seq expression data as input. Curating signaling pathway databases (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, GO) for pathway activation scoring — that is a separate CommPath curation task. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Curates a ligand-receptor (LR) pair reference database by merging interactions from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 into a standardized (ligand, receptor) gene-pair table that serves as CommPath's reference for inferring potential LR associations between cell clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: Curates a ligand-receptor (LR) pair reference database by merging interactions from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 into a standardized (ligand, receptor) gene-pair table that serves as CommPath's reference for inferring potential LR associations between cell clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is downstream LR inference itself (findLRpairs, filterLR) rather than building the reference database — those steps require the curated database plus scRNA-seq expression data as input. Curating signaling pathway databases (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, GO) for pathway activation scoring — that is a separate CommPath curation task.

skills.description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-type annotations and need to infer, rank, or visualize ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communication between annotated cell populations.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-enrichment
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-enrichment Use when you have an scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-type annotations and need to infer, rank, or visualize ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communication between annotated cell populations. Input is not single-cell transcriptomic data with cell-type labels (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed communication matrix) Species lacks CellTalkDB coverage or no suitable lrpairs data.frame is available for the organism The goal is pathway-level transcriptome enrichment (e.g. GSEA of DEGs) rather than pairwise ligand-receptor communication inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Enrich highly expressed ligand-receptor pairs from single-cell RNA-seq data using scCrossTalk, which tests CellTalkDB-derived LR pairs with the Z-test statistical method to infer and rank cell-cell communications (e.g., hepatocyte SAA1-FPR1 signaling to S100A12+ neutrophils in liver transplantation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: Enrich highly expressed ligand-receptor pairs from single-cell RNA-seq data using scCrossTalk, which tests CellTalkDB-derived LR pairs with the Z-test statistical method to infer and rank cell-cell communications (e.g., hepatocyte SAA1-FPR1 signaling to S100A12+ neutrophils in liver transplantation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not single-cell transcriptomic data with cell-type labels (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed communication matrix) Species lacks CellTalkDB coverage or no suitable lrpairs data.frame is available for the organism The goal is pathway-level transcriptome enrichment (e.g. GSEA of DEGs) rather than pairwise ligand-receptor communication inference

skills.description: Use when building a multi-method or multi-context cell-cell communication tensor and you must restrict inputs to LR pairs and cell types shared across all samples, e.g. the 172 shared LR pairs common to all five scoring methods on the BALF COVID-19 data.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-filtering
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-filtering Use when building a multi-method or multi-context cell-cell communication tensor and you must restrict inputs to LR pairs and cell types shared across all samples, e.g. the 172 shared LR pairs common to all five scoring methods on the BALF COVID-19 data. The analysis targets a single context/sample, where per-tool output already defines the LR space and no cross-method intersection is needed The tensor decomposition implementation supports missing values, so dropping LR pairs or cell types absent in some contexts is unnecessary (the implemented Tensor-cell2cell algorithm is not optimized for missing values, but future variants may be) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filter and harmonize ligand-receptor (LR) pair inventories so that communication tensors built from multiple scoring methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, Tensor-cell2cell built-in) share a common LR and cell-type space before tensor decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Filter and harmonize ligand-receptor (LR) pair inventories so that communication tensors built from multiple scoring methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, Tensor-cell2cell built-in) share a common LR and cell-type space before tensor decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a single context/sample, where per-tool output already defines the LR space and no cross-method intersection is needed The tensor decomposition implementation supports missing values, so dropping LR pairs or cell types absent in some contexts is unnecessary (the implemented Tensor-cell2cell algorithm is not optimized for missing values, but future variants may be)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) with cell-type labels must be converted into a ligand-receptor pair graph so a GCN model (e.g. DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) can classify significant CCIs.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-graph-construction
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-graph-construction Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) with cell-type labels must be converted into a ligand-receptor pair graph so a GCN model (e.g. DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) can classify significant CCIs. When the goal is cell clustering rather than interaction inference — that requires the separate Cluster_model pipeline (preprocess.py + Cluster.py), not the interaction-model pair graph When cells lack reliable type labels and no downstream CCI classifier is needed — Feature.py with --label_mode False is a different mode than the labeled supervision path this skill describes When data are bulk RNA-seq or non-scRNA-seq expression data; the pair-graph construction presumes scRNA-seq with sparse, heterogeneous single-cell profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a ligand-receptor pair graph for DeepCCI's GCN-based interaction model by preprocessing scRNA-seq data into processed ligand-receptor pair features (with SVD dimensionality reduction) via Feature.py, aggregating consensus significant-interaction labels by majority vote across CCI methods, and linking similar pairs with similarity threshold tau=0.95. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: Constructs a ligand-receptor pair graph for DeepCCI's GCN-based interaction model by preprocessing scRNA-seq data into processed ligand-receptor pair features (with SVD dimensionality reduction) via Feature.py, aggregating consensus significant-interaction labels by majority vote across CCI methods, and linking similar pairs with similarity threshold tau=0.95.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cell clustering rather than interaction inference — that requires the separate Cluster_model pipeline (preprocess.py + Cluster.py), not the interaction-model pair graph When cells lack reliable type labels and no downstream CCI classifier is needed — Feature.py with --label_mode False is a different mode than the labeled supervision path this skill describes When data are bulk RNA-seq or non-scRNA-seq expression data; the pair-graph construction presumes scRNA-seq with sparse, heterogeneous single-cell profiles

skills.description: Use when MDIC3 has produced celltype_communication.txt / cellular_communication.txt outputs and you need the specific L-R pairs (e.g., Cx3cl1-Cx3cr1, Apoe-Lrp1, CCL2-CCR2, SST-SSTR2) supporting each sender-receiver communication.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-mapping
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-mapping Use when MDIC3 has produced celltype_communication.txt / cellular_communication.txt outputs and you need the specific L-R pairs (e.g., Cx3cl1-Cx3cr1, Apoe-Lrp1, CCL2-CCR2, SST-SSTR2) supporting each sender-receiver communication. As the primary inference step when the species lacks curated L-R annotations — MDIC3's communication inference is independent of prior L-R knowledge and should run first; L-R mapping is only interpretive. When the goal is to detect communications involving undiscovered or orphan interactions (e.g., orphan receptors DR6/TNFRSF21, RELT, TROY, NGFR) — these are absent from L-R databases and cannot be recovered by L-R mapping. When no MDIC3 communication output exists — this skill interprets MDIC3 results and is not a standalone communication-inference method. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Post-hoc extraction of ligand-receptor pairs underlying cell-cell communications inferred by MDIC3, using the CellChatDB-derived L-R database and Bonferroni-corrected significance testing (corrected p < 0.01) to interpret matrix-decomposition communication scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Post-hoc extraction of ligand-receptor pairs underlying cell-cell communications inferred by MDIC3, using the CellChatDB-derived L-R database and Bonferroni-corrected significance testing (corrected p < 0.01) to interpret matrix-decomposition communication scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: As the primary inference step when the species lacks curated L-R annotations — MDIC3's communication inference is independent of prior L-R knowledge and should run first; L-R mapping is only interpretive. When the goal is to detect communications involving undiscovered or orphan interactions (e.g., orphan receptors DR6/TNFRSF21, RELT, TROY, NGFR) — these are absent from L-R databases and cannot be recovered by L-R mapping. When no MDIC3 communication output exists — this skill interprets MDIC3 results and is not a standalone communication-inference method.

skills.description: Use when you have cluster-annotated scRNA-seq data (human or mouse) and need to infer candidate protein pairs mediating communication between two specific cell types, e.g. CAF1–myeloid interactions in melanoma.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-prediction
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-prediction Use when you have cluster-annotated scRNA-seq data (human or mouse) and need to infer candidate protein pairs mediating communication between two specific cell types, e.g. CAF1–myeloid interactions in melanoma. When the goal is downstream signal transduction prediction inside the receiver cells rather than intercellular pair prediction — NicheNet is designed for that purpose When genes lack subcellular-localization or GO annotation, since the COMPARTMENTS/UniProt/GO filtering is central to excluding biologically unlikely interactions When you need interactions for a non-human/non-mouse organism — InterCellDB covers only human (18,990 genes) and mouse (20,938 genes) Predict candidate intercellular protein pairs (ligand–receptor, receptor–receptor, ECM–receptor) between two scRNA-seq cell clusters using InterCellDB: statistically significant differentially expressed gene pairs are matched against a curated protein–protein interaction database annotated with subcellular localization (COMPARTMENTS), action mode, effect, and GO functional classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Predict candidate intercellular protein pairs (ligand–receptor, receptor–receptor, ECM–receptor) between two scRNA-seq cell clusters using InterCellDB: statistically significant differentially expressed gene pairs are matched against a curated protein–protein interaction database annotated with subcellular localization (COMPARTMENTS), action mode, effect, and GO functional classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is downstream signal transduction prediction inside the receiver cells rather than intercellular pair prediction — NicheNet is designed for that purpose When genes lack subcellular-localization or GO annotation, since the COMPARTMENTS/UniProt/GO filtering is central to excluding biologically unlikely interactions When you need interactions for a non-human/non-mouse organism — InterCellDB covers only human (18,990 genes) and mouse (20,938 genes)

skills.description: Use when you have factor loadings for ligand-receptor pairs from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition and need to rank them (descending by loading value) to identify top communication pairs or feed factor-specific pre-ranked lists into GSEA.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-ranking
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-ranking Use when you have factor loadings for ligand-receptor pairs from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition and need to rank them (descending by loading value) to identify top communication pairs or feed factor-specific pre-ranked lists into GSEA. The input is raw per-context communication scores not yet factorized — build and decompose the 4D-communication tensor with Tensor-cell2cell first You need pathway-level scores rather than LR-pair rankings — tools like CellChat generate scores at the signaling pathway level instead of LR pairs Ranks ligand-receptor pairs by their loadings from Tensor-cell2cell factor decompositions (e.g., the 6-factor ASD or 10-factor BALF COVID-19 decompositions) to produce pre-ranked lists for downstream analyses such as factor-specific PreRanked GSEA against KEGG-derived LR pathway sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Ranks ligand-receptor pairs by their loadings from Tensor-cell2cell factor decompositions (e.g., the 6-factor ASD or 10-factor BALF COVID-19 decompositions) to produce pre-ranked lists for downstream analyses such as factor-specific PreRanked GSEA against KEGG-derived LR pathway sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw per-context communication scores not yet factorized — build and decompose the 4D-communication tensor with Tensor-cell2cell first You need pathway-level scores rather than LR-pair rankings — tools like CellChat generate scores at the signaling pathway level instead of LR pairs

skills.description: Use when analyzing time-course scRNA-seq with a reconstructed trajectory (e.g. monocle3 pseudotime) and a ligand-receptor database to identify which LR pairs co-vary along development.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-pair-screening
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-pair-screening Use when analyzing time-course scRNA-seq with a reconstructed trajectory (e.g. monocle3 pseudotime) and a ligand-receptor database to identify which LR pairs co-vary along development. The goal is communication between pre-defined, stable cell types (e.g. mature tissue labels) — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting, whereas this temporal co-variation screen targets developmental time series where definitive cell types do not yet exist Input lacks a trajectory/pseudotime ordering or is bulk bulk-only data without single-cell temporal structure Analysis targets maternal-embryo or extracellular-vesicle-mediated communication, which the autocrine ligand-receptor assumption of TimeTalk explicitly does not cover Screen a ligand-receptor database against pseudotime-ordered single-cell expression series to find co-varying LR pairs, as in TimeTalk's use of 2034 CellTalkDB mouse pairs with |PCC| = 0.1 (or SCC = 0.2) correlation filtering on interpolated time series. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Screen a ligand-receptor database against pseudotime-ordered single-cell expression series to find co-varying LR pairs, as in TimeTalk's use of 2034 CellTalkDB mouse pairs with |PCC| = 0.1 (or SCC = 0.2) correlation filtering on interpolated time series.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is communication between pre-defined, stable cell types (e.g. mature tissue labels) — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting, whereas this temporal co-variation screen targets developmental time series where definitive cell types do not yet exist Input lacks a trajectory/pseudotime ordering or is bulk bulk-only data without single-cell temporal structure Analysis targets maternal-embryo or extracellular-vesicle-mediated communication, which the autocrine ligand-receptor assumption of TimeTalk explicitly does not cover

skills.description: Use when comparing two Seurat/Connectome connectomes (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs control PBMCs) and you need a sign-agnostic per-edge magnitude of perturbation from ligand.norm.lfc and recept.norm.lfc values.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-perturbation-scoring
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-perturbation-scoring Use when comparing two Seurat/Connectome connectomes (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs control PBMCs) and you need a sign-agnostic per-edge magnitude of perturbation from ligand.norm.lfc and recept.norm.lfc values. You only have a single condition/connectome with no paired test-and-control edge set — DifferentialConnectome requires exactly the same edges present in both connectomes You need the direction (up vs down) of the perturbation, not just its magnitude — the perturbation score is always positive and discards sign Either the ligand or receptor log2 fold-change is missing/NA for an edge, since the score is a product of both and cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes Connectome's per-edge 'perturbation score' for a differential connectome as the product of the absolute normalized log2 fold-changes of the ligand and receptor between test and control conditions, yielding an always-positive magnitude of perturbation ranging from 0 to Infinity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Computes Connectome's per-edge 'perturbation score' for a differential connectome as the product of the absolute normalized log2 fold-changes of the ligand and receptor between test and control conditions, yielding an always-positive magnitude of perturbation ranging from 0 to Infinity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single condition/connectome with no paired test-and-control edge set — DifferentialConnectome requires exactly the same edges present in both connectomes You need the direction (up vs down) of the perturbation, not just its magnitude — the perturbation score is always positive and discards sign Either the ligand or receptor log2 fold-change is missing/NA for an edge, since the score is a product of both and cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when an analysis needs to enumerate, compare, or overlap multiple CCC ligand-receptor resources (e.g., CellChatDB, CellPhoneDB, Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, LRdb) before downstream inference or benchmarking.
skills.name: ligand-receptor-resource-loading
skills.search_text: ligand-receptor-resource-loading Use when an analysis needs to enumerate, compare, or overlap multiple CCC ligand-receptor resources (e.g., CellChatDB, CellPhoneDB, Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, LRdb) before downstream inference or benchmarking. When only a single, already-chosen resource is needed for one CCC inference run — decomplexification and cross-resource uniqueness statistics are unnecessary When comparing CCC inference METHODS rather than resources — method comparison requires applying scoring schemes to expression data, not loading resource databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Loads and harmonizes the 16 curated cell-cell communication ligand-receptor resources via liana::select_resource in LIANA (backed by OmnipathR) so their unique interactions, receivers, and transmitters can be quantified and cross-compared. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Loads and harmonizes the 16 curated cell-cell communication ligand-receptor resources via liana::select_resource in LIANA (backed by OmnipathR) so their unique interactions, receivers, and transmitters can be quantified and cross-compared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single, already-chosen resource is needed for one CCC inference run — decomplexification and cross-resource uniqueness statistics are unnecessary When comparing CCC inference METHODS rather than resources — method comparison requires applying scoring schemes to expression data, not loading resource databases

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing NeuronChat's ligand/target abundance and communication-strength computation for small-molecule neurotransmitter signaling from single-cell expression data.
skills.name: ligand-target-communication-strength-computation
skills.search_text: ligand-target-communication-strength-computation Use when reproducing or auditing NeuronChat's ligand/target abundance and communication-strength computation for small-molecule neurotransmitter signaling from single-cell expression data. Input is protein-based ligand-receptor signaling (e.g., peptide ligands handled by CellChat/CellPhoneDB) — the AND/OR functional-grouping logic here is specific to non-peptide small-molecule neurotransmitters. You only need the aggregated, downstream network-level summary and don't need to reconstruct/verify how ligand/target abundance or communication strength is derived. Spatial data requiring the spatial proximity enrichment score / spatially constrained network filtering — that is a separate, additional step beyond the basic ligand-target computation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Reconstructs how NeuronChat computes non-peptide neurotransmitter ligand abundance and receptor/target abundance from scRNA-seq expression (AND logic as geometric mean across functional gene groups, OR logic as arithmetic mean within redundant groups) and derives communication strength as the ligand-target product for each sender-receiver cell-group pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Reconstructs how NeuronChat computes non-peptide neurotransmitter ligand abundance and receptor/target abundance from scRNA-seq expression (AND logic as geometric mean across functional gene groups, OR logic as arithmetic mean within redundant groups) and derives communication strength as the ligand-target product for each sender-receiver cell-group pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is protein-based ligand-receptor signaling (e.g., peptide ligands handled by CellChat/CellPhoneDB) — the AND/OR functional-grouping logic here is specific to non-peptide small-molecule neurotransmitters. You only need the aggregated, downstream network-level summary and don't need to reconstruct/verify how ligand/target abundance or communication strength is derived. Spatial data requiring the spatial proximity enrichment score / spatially constrained network filtering — that is a separate, additional step beyond the basic ligand-target computation.

skills.description: Use when comparing gene regulatory networks between two conditions from paired single-cell data (one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq per condition) and you need subpopulation-specific differential regulation testing with p-values and FDR control.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-differential-regulation-testing
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-differential-regulation-testing Use when comparing gene regulatory networks between two conditions from paired single-cell data (one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq per condition) and you need subpopulation-specific differential regulation testing with p-values and FDR control. Conditions comprise multiple donors per condition — the method does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition Only scRNA-seq data are available without paired scATAC-seq — use the scRNA-only baseline instead (its AUC is lower, 0.7561 vs 0.9157, but sc-compReg requires accessibility data) The goal is de novo network inference from expression alone rather than testing differential regulation — alternative pipelines (GENIE3/PIDC crossed with diffK/diffRank) may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 sc-compReg's statistical test for differential TF-TG regulatory relations between two linked subpopulations: it computes cell-specific transcription factor regulatory potential (TFRP), fits a linear regression of TFRP on target gene expression per condition, and uses a likelihood-ratio statistic with p-value computation and FDR control to detect edges whose regulation changed between conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: sc-compReg's statistical test for differential TF-TG regulatory relations between two linked subpopulations: it computes cell-specific transcription factor regulatory potential (TFRP), fits a linear regression of TFRP on target gene expression per condition, and uses a likelihood-ratio statistic with p-value computation and FDR control to detect edges whose regulation changed between conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Conditions comprise multiple donors per condition — the method does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition Only scRNA-seq data are available without paired scATAC-seq — use the scRNA-only baseline instead (its AUC is lower, 0.7561 vs 0.9157, but sc-compReg requires accessibility data) The goal is de novo network inference from expression alone rather than testing differential regulation — alternative pipelines (GENIE3/PIDC crossed with diffK/diffRank) may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when separated cell clusters from a mixed scRNA-seq sample must be attributed to specific contributors by matching cluster SNP profiles against WES reference VCFs, yielding a likelihood ratio per contributor.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-forensic-identification
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-forensic-identification Use when separated cell clusters from a mixed scRNA-seq sample must be attributed to specific contributors by matching cluster SNP profiles against WES reference VCFs, yielding a likelihood ratio per contributor. When no reference dataset (WES or transcriptome sequencing) exists for candidate contributors — the approach does not use universal identity SNPs, so references must contain as many SNPs as possible When cell clusters contain too few cells: sensitivity analysis showed matching SNPs stay above 90% only for sampled points with more than 20 cells, and the 10E+9 LR threshold is exceeded at 100-200 cells When the goal is appearance-trait prediction — the required specific SNPs were not obtained and this extension was not performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Computes forensic likelihood ratios by matching identity SNPs from deconvoluted single-cell clusters against a de-novo whole-exome sequencing (WES) reference profile, using de-goulash's statistical analysis step with 1000G population data. Establishes individual identification of mixture contributors with court-acceptable statistical certainty (LR > 10E+9). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Computes forensic likelihood ratios by matching identity SNPs from deconvoluted single-cell clusters against a de-novo whole-exome sequencing (WES) reference profile, using de-goulash's statistical analysis step with 1000G population data. Establishes individual identification of mixture contributors with court-acceptable statistical certainty (LR > 10E+9).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference dataset (WES or transcriptome sequencing) exists for candidate contributors — the approach does not use universal identity SNPs, so references must contain as many SNPs as possible When cell clusters contain too few cells: sensitivity analysis showed matching SNPs stay above 90% only for sampled points with more than 20 cells, and the 10E+9 LR threshold is exceeded at 100-200 cells When the goal is appearance-trait prediction — the required specific SNPs were not obtained and this extension was not performed

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between NB and ZINB noise models before running DCA on a scRNA-seq count matrix, when you need to test whether a zero-inflation component is statistically justified.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-model-selection
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-model-selection Decision support for choosing between NB and ZINB noise models before running DCA on a scRNA-seq count matrix, when you need to test whether a zero-inflation component is statistically justified. The count matrix has not been preprocessed (zero-expression cells and genes not yet removed), since the mean/dropout dependence would be distorted You are not deciding between nested NB and ZINB noise models — a likelihood-ratio test is only valid for nested model comparison The dataset is so small or sparse that gene-wise mean and empirical dropout-rate estimates are too unstable to fit a mean-dropout dependence http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A statistical model-selection procedure for DCA denoising that fits both negative binomial (NB) and zero-inflated NB (ZINB) noise models to the gene-wise mean-vs-dropout-rate dependence and uses a log-likelihood-ratio test on the nested fits to decide whether zero-inflation is required for a given scRNA-seq dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: A statistical model-selection procedure for DCA denoising that fits both negative binomial (NB) and zero-inflated NB (ZINB) noise models to the gene-wise mean-vs-dropout-rate dependence and uses a log-likelihood-ratio test on the nested fits to decide whether zero-inflation is required for a given scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix has not been preprocessed (zero-expression cells and genes not yet removed), since the mean/dropout dependence would be distorted You are not deciding between nested NB and ZINB noise models — a likelihood-ratio test is only valid for nested model comparison The dataset is so small or sparse that gene-wise mean and empirical dropout-rate estimates are too unstable to fit a mean-dropout dependence

skills.description: Use when computing p-values/FDR for likelihood ratio statistics from a differential regulatory relation test between two linked subpopulations, and the standard Chi-square null is suspected to be anti-conservative or miscalibrated.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-statistic-null-calibration
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-statistic-null-calibration Use when computing p-values/FDR for likelihood ratio statistics from a differential regulatory relation test between two linked subpopulations, and the standard Chi-square null is suspected to be anti-conservative or miscalibrated. Input is raw scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices rather than computed LR statistics — run sc_compreg first to obtain the differential regulation likelihood ratios The LR statistic already has a validated asymptotic null distribution for the statistic at hand and no calibration check is needed Analysis involves more than two conditions or multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each of the two conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Calibrates the null distribution of the sc-compReg likelihood ratio (LR) statistic testing differential TF-TG regulatory relations by fitting a Gamma distribution to the lower 10 empirical quantiles of the null LR scores, replacing the miscalibrated asymptotic Chi-square (df=3) null for p-value and FDR computation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Calibrates the null distribution of the sc-compReg likelihood ratio (LR) statistic testing differential TF-TG regulatory relations by fitting a Gamma distribution to the lower 10 empirical quantiles of the null LR scores, replacing the miscalibrated asymptotic Chi-square (df=3) null for p-value and FDR computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices rather than computed LR statistics — run sc_compreg first to obtain the differential regulation likelihood ratios The LR statistic already has a validated asymptotic null distribution for the statistic at hand and no calibration check is needed Analysis involves more than two conditions or multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each of the two conditions

skills.summary: Fits a maximum-likelihood likelihood-ratio-test (LRT) classifier on the same class-balanced Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-simulated expression test data used by CLOUDe, providing the classical statistical baseline against which the NN, XGB, RF, and SVM classifiers are benchmarked.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is predicting continuous evolutionary parameters (theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) rather than discrete 'Redundant'/'Unique' classes — the LRT here serves only the classification benchmark When input expression data are not from two species with derived, survived, and lost gene columns (the 3m-column eD/eS/eL layout required by CLOUDe)

skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a different human stromal component than primary CRCs, e.g. metastatic CRC biopsies — CMScaller is not recommended there Very small datasets (fewer than ~40 samples), where centering/scaling inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty Single-cell RNA-seq data, which is exceedingly noisy and for which CMScaller is not optimized

skills.description: Use when training a NeuCA cell-type classifier on scRNA-seq data whose cell-type Pearson correlation matrix contains off-diagonal entries at or above tau = 0.95, requiring the marker-guided hierarchical neural-network route.
skills.name: limma-differential-expression-bifurcation-feature-selection
skills.search_text: limma-differential-expression-bifurcation-feature-selection Use when training a NeuCA cell-type classifier on scRNA-seq data whose cell-type Pearson correlation matrix contains off-diagonal entries at or above tau = 0.95, requiring the marker-guided hierarchical neural-network route. All off-diagonal cell-type Pearson correlations in P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA then uses a single feed-forward neural network instead of the hierarchical route The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is restricted to exhaustive assignment of known types; identify unknown/rare cells first with other tools Good candidate marker genes are unavailable and supervised training labels are missing — supervised annotation is not applicable without training data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects bifurcation-specific marker genes with limma differential analysis at each node of a cell lineage tree, then trains binary feed-forward neural networks at each bifurcation — the hierarchical branch of NeuCA for highly correlated cell types (off-diagonal Pearson correlations ≥ 0.95). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Selects bifurcation-specific marker genes with limma differential analysis at each node of a cell lineage tree, then trains binary feed-forward neural networks at each bifurcation — the hierarchical branch of NeuCA for highly correlated cell types (off-diagonal Pearson correlations ≥ 0.95).
skills.when_to_use_negative: All off-diagonal cell-type Pearson correlations in P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA then uses a single feed-forward neural network instead of the hierarchical route The new sample may contain cell types absent from the reference/training data — NeuCA is restricted to exhaustive assignment of known types; identify unknown/rare cells first with other tools Good candidate marker genes are unavailable and supervised training labels are missing — supervised annotation is not applicable without training data

skills.description: Use when you have normalized bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated with a two-group design) and need a DEG call to define true positives for benchmarking or to feed downstream GRN/regulator modeling.
skills.name: limma-differential-expression-calling
skills.search_text: limma-differential-expression-calling Use when you have normalized bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated with a two-group design) and need a DEG call to define true positives for benchmarking or to feed downstream GRN/regulator modeling. Single-cell simulation output (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq from sc_mosim) — the MOSim paper uses Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell data and this bulk voom/limma workflow is not designed for it Data already summarized as DEG lists or feature tables with no raw/normalized count matrix to fit linear models on When the goal is to validate the simulator's temporal or regulatory behavior rather than to define a DEG set (use correlation-based validation against 20,000 random feature pairs instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calls differentially expressed genes between experimental groups on bulk RNA-seq count data using limma linear modeling after voom transformation, as done in the MOSim/MORE benchmark where limma was applied to MOSim-simulated STATegra-configured data to identify the DEG set that seeds downstream GRN inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Calls differentially expressed genes between experimental groups on bulk RNA-seq count data using limma linear modeling after voom transformation, as done in the MOSim/MORE benchmark where limma was applied to MOSim-simulated STATegra-configured data to identify the DEG set that seeds downstream GRN inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell simulation output (scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq from sc_mosim) — the MOSim paper uses Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell data and this bulk voom/limma workflow is not designed for it Data already summarized as DEG lists or feature tables with no raw/normalized count matrix to fit linear models on When the goal is to validate the simulator's temporal or regulatory behavior rather than to define a DEG set (use correlation-based validation against 20,000 random feature pairs instead)

skills.description: Use when the analysis target is a GSVA score matrix (samples x genesets) and the goal is testing differential gene-set activity between two sample groups in RNA-seq/cancer data.
skills.name: limma-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: limma-differential-expression-testing Use when the analysis target is a GSVA score matrix (samples x genesets) and the goal is testing differential gene-set activity between two sample groups in RNA-seq/cancer data. The input is a raw counts matrix for gene-level differential expression (DEG) — ARMT uses edgeR for that case, not limma-on-GSVA. The difference factor is a non-numeric variable — instead select two explicit values to group samples into experiment and control groups. No gene-set-level (GSVA) scores exist and the question concerns single-gene expression or mutation differences rather than pathway activity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Differential testing of gene-set-level GSVA scores with limma, as implemented in ARMT: samples are grouped high/low by a GSVA score and limma linear models test score differences between groups, with results filtered by logFC, p-value, and FDR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Differential testing of gene-set-level GSVA scores with limma, as implemented in ARMT: samples are grouped high/low by a GSVA score and limma linear models test score differences between groups, with results filtered by logFC, p-value, and FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw counts matrix for gene-level differential expression (DEG) — ARMT uses edgeR for that case, not limma-on-GSVA. The difference factor is a non-numeric variable — instead select two explicit values to group samples into experiment and control groups. No gene-set-level (GSVA) scores exist and the question concerns single-gene expression or mutation differences rather than pathway activity.

skills.description: Use when PILOT has detected sample-level sub-groups (e.g. 3 PDAC clusters at resolution 0.3) and you need cell-type-specific genes distinguishing one cluster from the others, as a gene-level follow-up to proportion testing.
skills.name: limma-empirical-bayes-differential-expression
skills.search_text: limma-empirical-bayes-differential-expression Use when PILOT has detected sample-level sub-groups (e.g. 3 PDAC clusters at resolution 0.3) and you need cell-type-specific genes distinguishing one cluster from the others, as a gene-level follow-up to proportion testing. You need a trajectory (pseudotime) analysis rather than cluster contrasts — PILOT uses Wald statistics on fitted curves along diffusion-map/EIPLGraph pseudotime for that setting Input is pathomics/tissue-structure data with no gene-expression matrix, so limma gene contrasts are not applicable You have not yet validated the sample clustering (e.g. the 11/14/10 patient split at resolution 0.3) — DE on unstable clusters is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 PILOT's marker-gene step: after Leiden clustering of samples on the Wasserstein-distance matrix, limma's empirical-Bayes framework (Ritchie et al, 2015) is used to contrast gene expression of a chosen cell type in one patient cluster against all other clusters. In the PDAC case study this yields gene-level statistics for ductal cell 2 and stellate cells across the 3 clusters found at Leiden resolution 0.3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: PILOT's marker-gene step: after Leiden clustering of samples on the Wasserstein-distance matrix, limma's empirical-Bayes framework (Ritchie et al, 2015) is used to contrast gene expression of a chosen cell type in one patient cluster against all other clusters. In the PDAC case study this yields gene-level statistics for ductal cell 2 and stellate cells across the 3 clusters found at Leiden resolution 0.3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a trajectory (pseudotime) analysis rather than cluster contrasts — PILOT uses Wald statistics on fitted curves along diffusion-map/EIPLGraph pseudotime for that setting Input is pathomics/tissue-structure data with no gene-expression matrix, so limma gene contrasts are not applicable You have not yet validated the sample clustering (e.g. the 11/14/10 patient split at resolution 0.3) — DE on unstable clusters is meaningless

skills.description: Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two-group labels (e.g., 46 critical vs 23 non-critical COVID-19 samples from GSE172114) needs gene-level DEG P-values to seed active subnetwork detection or SEMtree perturbation analysis.
skills.name: limma-empirical-bayes-linear-modeling
skills.search_text: limma-empirical-bayes-linear-modeling Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two-group labels (e.g., 46 critical vs 23 non-critical COVID-19 samples from GSE172114) needs gene-level DEG P-values to seed active subnetwork detection or SEMtree perturbation analysis. The input is raw (unnormalized) counts or single-sample data with no group design — limma's linear model requires a normalized matrix and a defined contrast between groups The goal is pathway-level or network-level perturbation testing (use SEMrun/SEMpath node, edge, or path perturbation models instead of gene-level DE testing) The downstream method needs seed genes only (a curated disease-gene list) rather than genome-wide P-values http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute gene-level differential expression P-values on the GSE172114 COVID-19 RNA-seq benchmark (46 critical vs 23 non-critical cases) using limma's empirical Bayes moderated linear models with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment; the resulting per-gene table supplies the P-values/seeds consumed by SEMtree's active subnetwork detection and downstream SEM analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Compute gene-level differential expression P-values on the GSE172114 COVID-19 RNA-seq benchmark (46 critical vs 23 non-critical cases) using limma's empirical Bayes moderated linear models with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment; the resulting per-gene table supplies the P-values/seeds consumed by SEMtree's active subnetwork detection and downstream SEM analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw (unnormalized) counts or single-sample data with no group design — limma's linear model requires a normalized matrix and a defined contrast between groups The goal is pathway-level or network-level perturbation testing (use SEMrun/SEMpath node, edge, or path perturbation models instead of gene-level DE testing) The downstream method needs seed genes only (a curated disease-gene list) rather than genome-wide P-values

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw probe-level microarray data straight from GEO — the pipeline must first collapse probes to gene symbols and remove missing/low-intensity genes before fitting the model Input is RNA-Seq count data (curatedAdipoRNA RangedSummarizedExperiment) or ChIP-Seq peak counts (curatedAdipoChIP), where a count-based model rather than this microarray-intensity limma workflow applies Goal is gene set enrichment or batch-effect exploration rather than a two-group differential expression contrast

skills.search_text: limma-voom-count-normalization Use when the input is a raw RNA-seq gene/ortholog count matrix (e.g., salamander samples SRR7499348–SRR7499365) and the goal is DE analysis with a primary factor plus a blocking factor at a defined FDR threshold. skills.description: Use when preparing the regulatory-factor input for DICE/CompDICE bifurcation-timing analysis: after differential expression between terminal cells of competing lineages, to pick an equal number of antagonistic lineage-specific TFs per branch.
skills.name: lineage-antagonistic-tf-selection
skills.search_text: lineage-antagonistic-tf-selection Use when preparing the regulatory-factor input for DICE/CompDICE bifurcation-timing analysis: after differential expression between terminal cells of competing lineages, to pick an equal number of antagonistic lineage-specific TFs per branch. When the goal is trajectory inference or pseudotime estimation itself — use Palantir instead; DICE-based TF selection quantifies bifurcation timing, not cell orderings. When candidate regulatory factors have not yet been filtered by differential overexpression between lineages — applying entropy computation to an unbalanced or arbitrary TF set can bias the inferred transition point toward one lineage. skills.description: Use when validating that a neural ODE forecaster trained on paired time points of a bifurcating single-cell simulation reproduces lineage commitment, or when testing how far before a fate switch training data stays predictive.
skills.name: lineage-differentiation-verification
skills.search_text: lineage-differentiation-verification Use when validating that a neural ODE forecaster trained on paired time points of a bifurcating single-cell simulation reproduces lineage commitment, or when testing how far before a fate switch training data stays predictive. Training time points sit well before the fate switch (e.g., BoolODE time points 250/251): recursive forecasts break down at the bifurcation and form a new cluster absent from the simulation, so this skill cannot certify long-horizon fate prediction. Input is standard scRNA-seq without temporally paired measurements of the same cells; RNAForecaster requires paired time-point data that only simulations or metabolic labeling protocols provide. The analysis goal is only ordering cells along a trajectory (pseudotime); trajectory inference methods, not forecasting, are the appropriate choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Verifies that RNAForecaster neural ODE forecasts reproduce a bifurcating lineage split by training on two adjacent BoolODE simulated time points immediately before the bifurcation and recursively forecasting 100 steps, contrasted with training well before the split to expose the limited prediction horizon. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Verifies that RNAForecaster neural ODE forecasts reproduce a bifurcating lineage split by training on two adjacent BoolODE simulated time points immediately before the bifurcation and recursively forecasting 100 steps, contrasted with training well before the split to expose the limited prediction horizon.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq of progenitor populations plus FACS-sorted mature/differentiated subsets from which end-stage signature genes can be derived, and the goal is to assign individual progenitor cells to lineage-committed branches of a branching trajectory.
skills.name: lineage-fate-prediction-from-signature-genes
skills.search_text: lineage-fate-prediction-from-signature-genes Use when you have scRNA-seq of progenitor populations plus FACS-sorted mature/differentiated subsets from which end-stage signature genes can be derived, and the goal is to assign individual progenitor cells to lineage-committed branches of a branching trajectory. The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension). The single-cell data set is highly heterogeneous with no known subset information, or no signature genes from FACS-sorted terminal subsets are available — Mpath depends on signature genes of differentiated cell types and end-stage contrasts for fate prediction. The goal is a linear, non-branching ordering — other tools (e.g. SCUBA-based clustering, used in this article's supplementary analyses) may be more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Mpath-based prediction of individual cell fate along a multi-branching single-cell trajectory: the algorithm travels back in time from differentiated cell subsets (e.g. mature cDC1 and cDC2) using their signature genes to map each progenitor cell onto a lineage-committed branch. This reveals branching events such as the preDC-stage split into cDC1- versus cDC2-exclusive preDC subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension). skills.search_text: lineage-marker-dynamics-analysis Use when you have CellRouter subpopulations and reconstructed trajectories (e.g., from subpopulation 20 HSCs to neutrophil/erythroid) and need to score marker genes or regulators along each trajectory to confirm lineage identity and transition-specific dynamics. skills.search_text: lineage-marker-gene-activation-comparison Use when validating simulated scRNA-seq data against a reference for trajectory preservation, e.g. hematopoietic differentiation (BoneMarrow, GSE72857), by checking that marker gene sets activate sequentially along PAGA-inferred branches and pseudo-time ordering is concordant. skills.description: Use when you have CAFEH per-(SNP, tissue) results (pip, p_active, top_component, rank, pi) across many tissues and traits, and need to quantify whether tissue-restricted eQTL components are enriched for activity in GWAS loci.

skills.search_text: linear-mixed-model-association-testing Use when you have CAFEH per-(SNP, tissue) results (pip, p_active, top_component, rank, pi) across many tissues and traits, and need to quantify whether tissue-restricted eQTL components are enriched for activity in GWAS loci. Loci with large LD differences between studies (e.g., ancestry differences): CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so cross-study inference may be biased before any mixed-model aggregation is attempted. skills.search_text: linear-regression-correlation-analysis Use when you need to estimate a per-sample swapped-read fraction from count data via regression gradients, or test whether a swapping rate correlates with a covariate such as free library barcode concentration across plates. skills.summary: Fits simple linear models in R to quantify barcode swapping: regressing observed swapped reads on reads available for swapping (taking the gradient as the swapping fraction), and regressing per-plate swapping fractions against free-barcode-to-cDNA ratios to test for correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are droplet-based (10x Genomics) and the goal is to remove swapped molecules rather than estimate plate-level swapping rates — use the DropletUtils molecule-exclusion algorithm instead The sequencing instrument is not a patterned flow-cell platform (e.g. libraries were run only on HiSeq 2500), where swapping at the ~2.5% HiSeq 4000 level is not expected The design is a simple two-group comparison where a correlation/regression of swapping fraction against a covariate is not the question being asked

skills.search_text: linear-regression-modeling Use when you have a merged per-sample table of continuous predictors and a continuous response (e.g., 676 TCGA tumors with METAFlux flux features and Winter hypoxia scores) and need coefficient estimates, standard errors, p-values, and 95% CIs to test metabolic reprogramming associations. skills.search_text: linear-regression-of-cell-proportions-on-clinical-trait Use when estimated cell type proportions from deconvolution (e.g., MuSiC music_prop output) must be tested for association with a clinical trait such as HbA1c via single-variable linear regression. skills.description: Use when a base-level RNA-seq coverage dataset shows systematic 3'-end coverage decline per sample, and you need per-sample decay rates to identify degraded cases before shape change detection.
skills.name: linear-regression-of-log-coverage-vs-base-position
skills.search_text: linear-regression-of-log-coverage-vs-base-position Use when a base-level RNA-seq coverage dataset shows systematic 3'-end coverage decline per sample, and you need per-sample decay rates to identify degraded cases before shape change detection. Input is only gene-level expression counts (e.g. RSEM gene summaries) rather than base-level pileup coverage — slopes across base position cannot be computed Goal is detection of splicing/deletion shape changes rather than sample-level degradation screening — use SCISSOR's GSC/LSC detection on non-degraded samples instead Genes with many non-expressed samples (e.g. the 5802 genes ~28% excluded in HNSC) are retained — coverage-fitting on non-expressed genes yields unreliable decay rates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies sample-level RNA degradation by regressing mean-centered, log-transformed base-level pileup coverage on scaled base position; the per-sample slope (decay rate) captures 3'-to-5' coverage decline and is used to flag severely degraded samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Quantifies sample-level RNA degradation by regressing mean-centered, log-transformed base-level pileup coverage on scaled base position; the per-sample slope (decay rate) captures 3'-to-5' coverage decline and is used to flag severely degraded samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only gene-level expression counts (e.g. RSEM gene summaries) rather than base-level pileup coverage — slopes across base position cannot be computed Goal is detection of splicing/deletion shape changes rather than sample-level degradation screening — use SCISSOR's GSC/LSC detection on non-degraded samples instead Genes with many non-expressed samples (e.g. the 5802 genes ~28% excluded in HNSC) are retained — coverage-fitting on non-expressed genes yields unreliable decay rates

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether cell-type proportions shift between conditions in single-cell resolution data (.h5ad/AnnData), including unreplicated datasets where standard regression approaches fail.
skills.name: linear-regression-proportion-testing
skills.search_text: linear-regression-proportion-testing Use when you need to test whether cell-type proportions shift between conditions in single-cell resolution data (.h5ad/AnnData), including unreplicated datasets where standard regression approaches fail. The dataset contains rare cell types / clusters under ~2% of all cells, where bootstrapping has limited benefits and results are unstable You intend to compare raw cell counts directly between clusters, which is invalid due to sequencing depth and other technical and biological effects Clusters do not reflect real cell types but are defined by technical parameters (e.g. Leiden resolution) — clustering parameters must be validated first http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fits propeller-style linear regressions of per-cluster cell proportions on condition for differential compositional analysis of single-cell data, extending the regression approach with iteration-based bootstrapping to simulate pseudo-replicates when samples lack biological replicates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Fits propeller-style linear regressions of per-cluster cell proportions on condition for differential compositional analysis of single-cell data, extending the regression approach with iteration-based bootstrapping to simulate pseudo-replicates when samples lack biological replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains rare cell types / clusters under ~2% of all cells, where bootstrapping has limited benefits and results are unstable You intend to compare raw cell counts directly between clusters, which is invalid due to sequencing depth and other technical and biological effects Clusters do not reflect real cell types but are defined by technical parameters (e.g. Leiden resolution) — clustering parameters must be validated first

skills.description: Use when comparing the computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as input size scales, and you need a quantitative extrapolation beyond measured cell counts.
skills.name: linear-regression-runtime-extrapolation
skills.search_text: linear-regression-runtime-extrapolation Use when comparing the computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as input size scales, and you need a quantitative extrapolation beyond measured cell counts. You need accuracy/assignment-quality comparisons rather than computational cost scaling (use cell-to-clone assignment accuracy evaluation instead). Input data has no per-patient structure or you cannot preserve it during subsampling, since the benchmark subsamples RNA and DNA cells within each patient. Runtime is not dominated by a deterministic solver step, so a linear extrapolation of solve time to larger sizes is not justified. Benchmarks wall-clock runtime and peak memory of MaCroDNA against clonealign and Seurat by subsampling cells at fixed rates, fitting a linear regression to the measured runtimes, and extrapolating to a larger cell count. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks wall-clock runtime and peak memory of MaCroDNA against clonealign and Seurat by subsampling cells at fixed rates, fitting a linear regression to the measured runtimes, and extrapolating to a larger cell count.

Input data has no per-patient structure or you cannot preserve it during subsampling, since the benchmark subsamples RNA and DNA cells within each patient. Runtime is not dominated by a deterministic solver step, so a linear extrapolation of solve time to larger sizes is not justified.

Libraries sequenced exclusively on non-patterned-flowcell instruments such as the HiSeq 2500, where barcode swapping is negligible and the regression signal would be near zero Droplet-based 10x Genomics data where the goal is molecule-level exclusion (shared UMI, cell barcode, gene) rather than estimating a plate-level swapping fraction — use the DropletUtils exclusion algorithm instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates the fraction of barcode-swapped reads in plate-prepared scRNA-seq data sequenced on patterned-flowcell instruments (HiSeq 4000) by regressing observed swapped reads in 'impossible' barcode combinations against reads available for swapping; the fitted gradient is the swapping fraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x

skills.description: Use when you have paired labeled/unlabeled/total count matrices from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (e.g., scEU-seq 4sU-treated cells) and need per-gene degradation rates to estimate pre-labeling expression.
skills.name: linear-regression-transcript-counts
skills.search_text: linear-regression-transcript-counts Use when you have paired labeled/unlabeled/total count matrices from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (e.g., scEU-seq 4sU-treated cells) and need per-gene degradation rates to estimate pre-labeling expression. Input is standard scRNA-seq without metabolic labeling — no labeled/unlabeled split exists, so degradation rates cannot be estimated and paired time-point data required by RNAForecaster are unavailable Cells have heterogeneous labeling times — subset to a common labeling time (e.g., 60 min 4sU) first, as the degradation calculation assumes equal labeling duration The goal is forecasting future states from already-paired time-course data rather than constructing a t=0 matrix from labeling data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Estimates per-gene RNA degradation rates from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq) by fitting a linear regression of labeled counts against total counts across cells, then computing the rate as -log(1 - slope); these rates enable construction of the t=0 input matrix for RNAForecaster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Estimates per-gene RNA degradation rates from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq) by fitting a linear regression of labeled counts against total counts across cells, then computing the rate as -log(1 - slope); these rates enable construction of the t=0 input matrix for RNAForecaster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is standard scRNA-seq without metabolic labeling — no labeled/unlabeled split exists, so degradation rates cannot be estimated and paired time-point data required by RNAForecaster are unavailable Cells have heterogeneous labeling times — subset to a common labeling time (e.g., 60 min 4sU) first, as the degradation calculation assumes equal labeling duration The goal is forecasting future states from already-paired time-course data rather than constructing a t=0 matrix from labeling data

skills.search_text: linear-runtime-scaling-analysis Use when estimating or validating SkewC gene body coverage compute cost for a 10x Genomics barcoded BAM (e.g. pbmc_8k), or when planning how many cells can be processed in a given time budget. skills.search_text: linear-scaling-regression-analysis Use when a method's scalability claim (e.g., 'linear running time') must be verified empirically: you can generate or obtain datasets at multiple sizes and record wall-clock runtime per size for regression. skills.search_text: linear-svm-hierarchical-classification Use when you have multiple aligned (batch-corrected), annotated scRNA-seq datasets with high-dimensional integrated expression matrices and need to construct or extend a hierarchical cell-population classification tree with per-node linear SVMs. Input datasets are not aligned — scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool, so unaligned datasets must first be corrected (e.g., with Seurat, scVI, or scArches) You only need to annotate an unlabeled dataset against an existing reference without discovering relationships between populations Cell populations are expected to violate strict hierarchical relationships (e.g., dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a hierarchical classification tree with a linear SVM at each node using scHPL, so that cell populations annotated at different resolutions (e.g., Seurat-aligned AMB2016 vs AMB2018 mouse visual cortex) are automatically related and new populations can be attached at the correct tree position. The linear SVM is the advised classifier for integrated data that retains many dimensions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Train a hierarchical classification tree with a linear SVM at each node using scHPL, so that cell populations annotated at different resolutions (e.g., Seurat-aligned AMB2016 vs AMB2018 mouse visual cortex) are automatically related and new populations can be attached at the correct tree position. The linear SVM is the advised classifier for integrated data that retains many dimensions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input datasets are not aligned — scHPL is explicitly not a batch correction tool, so unaligned datasets must first be corrected (e.g., with Seurat, scVI, or scArches) You only need to annotate an unlabeled dataset against an existing reference without discovering relationships between populations Cell populations are expected to violate strict hierarchical relationships (e.g., dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes)

skills.description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with RNA and surface-protein (ADT) modalities where modality fusion by L∞ norm of pairwise cell-cell distances is needed, especially with routine numbers of ADT features (<50).
skills.name: linf-norm-joint-distance-fusion
skills.search_text: linf-norm-joint-distance-fusion Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with RNA and surface-protein (ADT) modalities where modality fusion by L∞ norm of pairwise cell-cell distances is needed, especially with routine numbers of ADT features (<50). Massive CITE-seq datasets with many ADT features (e.g. 170K cells with 228 ADT features): pairwise distance computation grows quadratically with cell number, LinQ-View failed where Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g. ≥50): LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) Analyses where batch effects between multiple runs are uncorrected: negative-control runs without Seurat 3 batch correction over-split cell groups (24 vs 21 groups on PBMC 1K + PBMC 10K) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Fuse per-modality cell-cell pairwise distance matrices from CITE-seq RNA and ADT data into a single joint distance using the LinQ-View L∞ norm model, optionally applying a sigmoid filter to the ADT distances so no single surface protein dominates the integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Fuse per-modality cell-cell pairwise distance matrices from CITE-seq RNA and ADT data into a single joint distance using the LinQ-View L∞ norm model, optionally applying a sigmoid filter to the ADT distances so no single surface protein dominates the integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Massive CITE-seq datasets with many ADT features (e.g. 170K cells with 228 ADT features): pairwise distance computation grows quadratically with cell number, LinQ-View failed where Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g. ≥50): LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) Analyses where batch effects between multiple runs are uncorrected: negative-control runs without Seurat 3 batch correction over-split cell groups (24 vs 21 groups on PBMC 1K + PBMC 10K)

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq data with both transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities has been preprocessed and per-modality cell-cell distance matrices must be fused for joint Louvain clustering or dimensionality reduction.
skills.name: linfinity-distance-matrix-fusion
skills.search_text: linfinity-distance-matrix-fusion Use when CITE-seq data with both transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities has been preprocessed and per-modality cell-cell distance matrices must be fused for joint Louvain clustering or dimensionality reduction. Datasets with a very large number of ADT features (>50) or massive cell counts (e.g. 170K cells with 228 ADT features), where Seurat 4 is the better option and LinQ-View failed Unimodal scRNA-seq data with no surface-protein modality, since there is no second distance matrix to fuse Cases where a feature-level integration (e.g. Seurat 4 WNN) is preferred over distance-matrix-level fusion http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 LinQ-View's method for combining per-modality cell-cell pairwise distance matrices from CITE-seq mRNA and surface-protein (ADT) data into a single joint distance matrix, using a sigmoid filter on ADT distances, linear alpha-rescaling, and an elementwise L-infinity (maximum) fusion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: LinQ-View's method for combining per-modality cell-cell pairwise distance matrices from CITE-seq mRNA and surface-protein (ADT) data into a single joint distance matrix, using a sigmoid filter on ADT distances, linear alpha-rescaling, and an elementwise L-infinity (maximum) fusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with a very large number of ADT features (>50) or massive cell counts (e.g. 170K cells with 228 ADT features), where Seurat 4 is the better option and LinQ-View failed Unimodal scRNA-seq data with no surface-protein modality, since there is no second distance matrix to fuse Cases where a feature-level integration (e.g. Seurat 4 WNN) is preferred over distance-matrix-level fusion

skills.search_text: linked-read-isoform-assembly Use when input is barcoded bulk RNA-seq (e.g. SPIso-seq-style linked reads in FASTQ) and the goal is de novo full-length isoform reconstruction, especially for highly alternatively spliced genes such as GYPC, MAPT, or BIN1.
