skills.description: Use when evaluating imputation accuracy on masked scRNA-seq data and you need to attribute ground-truth MSE to nonzero entries, biological zeros (true zeros), and technical zeros (masked nonzero values).
skills.name: log-transformed-count-error-metrics
skills.search_text: log-transformed-count-error-metrics Use when evaluating imputation accuracy on masked scRNA-seq data and you need to attribute ground-truth MSE to nonzero entries, biological zeros (true zeros), and technical zeros (masked nonzero values). No ground truth matrix exists (e.g., the mouse brain example where the ground truth is set to the same as the input) — error decomposition against true values is then meaningless. The data have not been log10(count+1) transformed — the imputed output and error metrics are defined on that scale, so raw-count comparisons would be inconsistent. You need to distinguish biological from technical zeros at imputation time — LATE/TRANSLATE assume all zeros are missing values and always impute zeros with a nonzero value; this decomposition only evaluates results post hoc. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Decompose the overall imputation error gtMSEall between an imputed scRNA-seq matrix and the ground truth on the log10(count+1) scale into component mean squared errors gtMSEnz, gtMSEbiol, and gtMSEtech attributable to nonzero, biological-zero, and technical-zero entry classes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Decompose the overall imputation error gtMSEall between an imputed scRNA-seq matrix and the ground truth on the log10(count+1) scale into component mean squared errors gtMSEnz, gtMSEbiol, and gtMSEtech attributable to nonzero, biological-zero, and technical-zero entry classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground truth matrix exists (e.g., the mouse brain example where the ground truth is set to the same as the input) — error decomposition against true values is then meaningless. The data have not been log10(count+1) transformed — the imputed output and error metrics are defined on that scale, so raw-count comparisons would be inconsistent. You need to distinguish biological from technical zeros at imputation time — LATE/TRANSLATE assume all zeros are missing values and always impute zeros with a nonzero value; this decomposition only evaluates results post hoc.

skills.summary: Normalizes raw scRNA-seq counts by each cell's library size and applies a log10 transformation, producing the expression matrix on which scImpute's Gamma-Normal mixture model is fit to estimate dropout probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or log-transformed expression data rather than a raw count matrix The counts have not been generated genome-wide — a heavy prior gene filtering removes most genes, undermining robust dropout identification

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., FPKM/RPKM/CPM values from plate-based protocols like SUPeR-seq or Smart-Seq2) has a value range larger than 100 and will feed into subspace-regression imputation of dropout-affected zero entries.
skills.name: log2-expression-rescaling
skills.search_text: log2-expression-rescaling Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., FPKM/RPKM/CPM values from plate-based protocols like SUPeR-seq or Smart-Seq2) has a value range larger than 100 and will feed into subspace-regression imputation of dropout-affected zero entries. The expression matrix already has a value range of 100 or below (scISR applies the log2 transformation only for datasets with a value range larger than 100). Values are already log-scale normalized (e.g., log-transformed RPKM/CPM), in which case re-applying log2 would distort the scale. The goal is downstream cluster assessment of the raw data rather than scISR imputation — the README's k-means/ARI evaluation operates on the raw or fully imputed matrix, not on the intermediate rescaled matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A preprocessing step in the scISR imputation workflow that rescales a single-cell gene-by-cell expression matrix using a base-2 log transformation whenever the value range exceeds 100, so that downstream generalized linear regression (stats::lm) in the subspace-regression imputation module operates on a comparable numeric scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: A preprocessing step in the scISR imputation workflow that rescales a single-cell gene-by-cell expression matrix using a base-2 log transformation whenever the value range exceeds 100, so that downstream generalized linear regression (stats::lm) in the subspace-regression imputation module operates on a comparable numeric scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix already has a value range of 100 or below (scISR applies the log2 transformation only for datasets with a value range larger than 100). Values are already log-scale normalized (e.g., log-transformed RPKM/CPM), in which case re-applying log2 would distort the scale. The goal is downstream cluster assessment of the raw data rather than scISR imputation — the README's k-means/ARI evaluation operates on the raw or fully imputed matrix, not on the intermediate rescaled matrix.

skills.search_text: log2-fold-change-differential-expression-analysis Use when two deconvolved or reference-free cell-type transcriptional profiles (beta matrices) from different biological conditions (e.g., aged vs young pseudo-pixels) must be compared gene-by-gene to validate recovered perturbation signatures. skills.summary: Computes gene-by-gene log2 fold-changes between two condition-matched transcriptional profiles — here, STdeconvolve LDA-derived cell-type beta profiles (e.g., aged vs young macrophages) — to recover perturbation-driven, cell-type-specific expression changes from deconvolved spatial transcriptomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw pixel-level ST counts rather than deconvolved, cell-type-matched transcriptional profiles — the comparison requires condition-matched beta profiles, not mixtures The ST data are too sparse with high stochastic drop-out rates or cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels, so STdeconvolve itself fails to recover distinct cell-type profiles to compare Sub-cellular pixel-resolution ST data, for which the paper states STdeconvolve may not be best suited

skills.name: log2-fold-change-prevalence-filtering
skills.search_text: log2-fold-change-prevalence-filtering Use when given a gene cluster absence/presence matrix and per-genome lifestyle labels, you must identify lifestyle-enriched gene clusters using prevalence and log2 fold-change thresholds plus Fisher's exact test. You only need core-genome identification — bacLIFE uses a separate >90% of genomes threshold for core genes, not the pLAG rule Your input is already a ranked feature-importance list from the Chi2 machine learning step (top 1000 features) rather than a presence/absence matrix The dataset lacks lifestyle labels for genomes (bacLIFE lifestyle prediction requires a >0.8 random forest confidence value before labels can be used) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 bacLIFE's pLAG detection rule: classify gene clusters as predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) when present in >70% of genomes of a lifestyle group AND showing >2 log2 fold change in presence versus remaining bacteria, ranked by Fisher's exact test p-value with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: bacLIFE's pLAG detection rule: classify gene clusters as predicted lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs) when present in >70% of genomes of a lifestyle group AND showing >2 log2 fold change in presence versus remaining bacteria, ranked by Fisher's exact test p-value with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need core-genome identification — bacLIFE uses a separate >90% of genomes threshold for core genes, not the pLAG rule Your input is already a ranked feature-importance list from the Chi2 machine learning step (top 1000 features) rather than a presence/absence matrix The dataset lacks lifestyle labels for genomes (bacLIFE lifestyle prediction requires a >0.8 random forest confidence value before labels can be used)

The input is raw sequencing data or a count matrix without pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the CSV must already contain these as columns (e.g. 'Treatment1vsCtrl_Log2FoldChange', 'Treatment1vsCtrl_padj') The analysis is experience-driven tracking of a preselected set of symbols rather than data-driven feature extraction — the article's goal is explicitly to bypass gene preselection 'multiplication factor' is set to 1, which produces a plain four-way plot rather than the scorecard's extreme-region regions of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A data-driven screening step that classifies genes as extreme or moderately changing by applying joint log2 fold-change thresholds (with a multiplication factor for extreme regions) and adjusted-p significance cut-offs, as implemented in the Scorecard Python library for bacterial biofilm transcriptomics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3

skills.search_text: long-read-demultiplexing Use when noisy ONT long-read FASTQ/FASTA single-cell data needs cell-barcode demultiplexing or barcode discovery, e.g. 10x Chromium libraries where barcodes contain sequencing errors and a whitelist may or may not be known. skills.summary: Error-tolerant demultiplexing of cellular barcodes from noisy long-read (ONT) single-cell RNA-seq data using Flexiplex, including barcode discovery, whitelist filtering, and empty-droplet removal, benchmarked against scTagger and FLAMES.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads already carry trusted cell-barcode tags and the task is downstream counting/UMI collapse (e.g. building gene x cell matrices, as in epi2me-labs/wf-single-cell), not barcode assignment When an exact, error-free pattern search is needed and fuzzy Levenshtein matching would introduce false positives; Flexiplex's error tolerance is designed for noisy barcodes When compute memory is severely constrained but wall-clock time is not, and exact-match approaches like scTagger's lower-memory profile are acceptable

skills.description: Use when you need to validate or benchmark a short-read single-cell TE quantification method and matched long-read data (nanopore scNanoRNAseq or PacBio) from the same sample exists to serve as ground truth at the TE subfamily level.
skills.name: long-read-ground-truth-validation
skills.search_text: long-read-ground-truth-validation Use when you need to validate or benchmark a short-read single-cell TE quantification method and matched long-read data (nanopore scNanoRNAseq or PacBio) from the same sample exists to serve as ground truth at the TE subfamily level. When no matched long-read (nanopore or PacBio) dataset from the same sample exists — there is no independent ground truth to correlate against When quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, since MATES's 2001 bp coverage vector and multi-mapping rate estimation are inaccurate for TEs longer than 2001 bp When the goal is locus-level resolution for highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark short-read single-cell TE quantification methods (MATES, scTE, SoloTE) against nanopore and PacBio long-read sequencing from the same cells, using subfamily-level R² against long-read counts as ground truth. This validates that MATES's deep-learning multi-mapping read allocation genuinely improves TE quantification accuracy on real short-read data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Benchmark short-read single-cell TE quantification methods (MATES, scTE, SoloTE) against nanopore and PacBio long-read sequencing from the same cells, using subfamily-level R² against long-read counts as ground truth. This validates that MATES's deep-learning multi-mapping read allocation genuinely improves TE quantification accuracy on real short-read data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no matched long-read (nanopore or PacBio) dataset from the same sample exists — there is no independent ground truth to correlate against When quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, since MATES's 2001 bp coverage vector and multi-mapping rate estimation are inaccurate for TEs longer than 2001 bp When the goal is locus-level resolution for highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions

skills.description: Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial long reads are grouped into UMI clusters and you must fix misalignment or end truncation before isoform quantification, e.g. false-positive small internal exons or truncated read ends from high sequencing error.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-consensus-repair
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-consensus-repair Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial long reads are grouped into UMI clusters and you must fix misalignment or end truncation before isoform quantification, e.g. false-positive small internal exons or truncated read ends from high sequencing error. Reads lack UMI/PCR-duplicate structure (no clusters to take a consensus over), e.g. bulk long-read data without cellular barcodes You are doing downstream alternative-splicing statistics (phi/psi heterogeneity analysis) rather than pre-processing — Longcell steps 3–4 upstream outputs should already exist UMI collapsing with fixed edit distance is already trusted (e.g. Sicelore2/FLAMES output) and no misalignment/truncation correction is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Longcell's UMI-cluster consensus correction (workflow step 3): within each UMI-based read cluster of Nanopore long reads, collapse PCR-duplicate reads into a consensus alignment that repairs truncated ends and mis-mapped isoforms, retaining the majority-vote isoform as the cluster representative. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Longcell's UMI-cluster consensus correction (workflow step 3): within each UMI-based read cluster of Nanopore long reads, collapse PCR-duplicate reads into a consensus alignment that repairs truncated ends and mis-mapped isoforms, retaining the majority-vote isoform as the cluster representative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads lack UMI/PCR-duplicate structure (no clusters to take a consensus over), e.g. bulk long-read data without cellular barcodes You are doing downstream alternative-splicing statistics (phi/psi heterogeneity analysis) rather than pre-processing — Longcell steps 3–4 upstream outputs should already exist UMI collapsing with fixed edit distance is already trusted (e.g. Sicelore2/FLAMES output) and no misalignment/truncation correction is needed

skills.description: Use when BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of long reads (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT cDNA/direct RNA) from a targeted gene, minigene, or SIRV spike-in must be resolved into isoforms and quantified without prior splice-site annotation.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-detection
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-detection Use when BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of long reads (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT cDNA/direct RNA) from a targeted gene, minigene, or SIRV spike-in must be resolved into isoforms and quantified without prior splice-site annotation. Input is raw short-read RNA-seq or Sanger/capillary electropherograms — the tool is designed for long-read sequencing data Whole-transcriptome high-throughput annotation where a batch pipeline such as wf-transcriptomes (bambu/SQANTI3) is more appropriate; VIsoQLR is tailored to low-throughput, one-gene-at-a-time inspection and manual fine-tuning The alignment already exists but Minimap2 was used on data with small exons — re-align with GMAP first http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0108 Detect and quantify isoforms from long-read sequencing (LRS) alignments of a single locus or spike-in set using VIsoQLR's consensus exon coordinate (CEC) approach, benchmarked against StringTie2 and FLAIR on SIRV and PAX6 minigene data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Detect and quantify isoforms from long-read sequencing (LRS) alignments of a single locus or spike-in set using VIsoQLR's consensus exon coordinate (CEC) approach, benchmarked against StringTie2 and FLAIR on SIRV and PAX6 minigene data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw short-read RNA-seq or Sanger/capillary electropherograms — the tool is designed for long-read sequencing data Whole-transcriptome high-throughput annotation where a batch pipeline such as wf-transcriptomes (bambu/SQANTI3) is more appropriate; VIsoQLR is tailored to low-throughput, one-gene-at-a-time inspection and manual fine-tuning The alignment already exists but Minimap2 was used on data with small exons — re-align with GMAP first

skills.description: Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial FASTQ reads (e.g., Jurkat GSP-targeted, MOB Visium, CRCLM) must be turned into cell-by-isoform count matrices, or when benchmarking isoform quantification methods against Illumina or PacBio IsoSeq gold standards.
skills.name: long-read-isoform-quantification
skills.search_text: long-read-isoform-quantification Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial FASTQ reads (e.g., Jurkat GSP-targeted, MOB Visium, CRCLM) must be turned into cell-by-isoform count matrices, or when benchmarking isoform quantification methods against Illumina or PacBio IsoSeq gold standards. Input reads are already a processed cell-by-isoform feature table — use downstream splicing analysis (Splice object, phi estimation) instead of re-quantifying Data are short-read Illumina sequences with no cell barcode/UMI error problem — Longcell's denoising rationale (85–99% Nanopore per-base error) does not apply Goal is de-novo isoform discovery without a cell/spatial barcode structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A pipeline skill for converting single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long-read FASTQ into a cell-by-isoform count matrix, built around Longcell's barcode/UMI recovery, consensus error correction, and UMI-clustered isoform quantification, with benchmarking against Illumina- or PacBio-supervised ground truth via per-cell Spearman correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: A pipeline skill for converting single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long-read FASTQ into a cell-by-isoform count matrix, built around Longcell's barcode/UMI recovery, consensus error correction, and UMI-clustered isoform quantification, with benchmarking against Illumina- or PacBio-supervised ground truth via per-cell Spearman correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already a processed cell-by-isoform feature table — use downstream splicing analysis (Splice object, phi estimation) instead of re-quantifying Data are short-read Illumina sequences with no cell barcode/UMI error problem — Longcell's denoising rationale (85–99% Nanopore per-base error) does not apply Goal is de-novo isoform discovery without a cell/spatial barcode structure

skills.description: Use when benchmarking computationally predicted IPA/polyA sites from conventional RNA-seq (e.g., InPACT, IPAFinder) against long-read Iso-seq isoform annotations to obtain validation rates for a dataset such as GSE167486 small airway epithelial cells.
skills.name: long-read-isoseq-validation-analysis
skills.search_text: long-read-isoseq-validation-analysis Use when benchmarking computationally predicted IPA/polyA sites from conventional RNA-seq (e.g., InPACT, IPAFinder) against long-read Iso-seq isoform annotations to obtain validation rates for a dataset such as GSE167486 small airway epithelial cells. No long-read Iso-seq data or isoform annotation is available for the same sample/dataset — use 3'-end sequencing ground truth (3P-seq, A-seq, polyA-seq) instead Goal is quantifying IPA usage (PAU) rather than validating site identification — use Salmon-based quantification and |ΔPAU| error metrics instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Validates RNA-seq-derived IPA site predictions against long-read Iso-seq isoform annotations by matching predicted polyA sites to Iso-seq-extracted polyA sites and computing Iso-seq validation rates, as done in the InPACT benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Validates RNA-seq-derived IPA site predictions against long-read Iso-seq isoform annotations by matching predicted polyA sites to Iso-seq-extracted polyA sites and computing Iso-seq validation rates, as done in the InPACT benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No long-read Iso-seq data or isoform annotation is available for the same sample/dataset — use 3'-end sequencing ground truth (3P-seq, A-seq, polyA-seq) instead Goal is quantifying IPA usage (PAU) rather than validating site identification — use Salmon-based quantification and |ΔPAU| error metrics instead

skills.description: Use when you have raw long-read RNA FASTQ data (PacBio Iso-Seq, ONT) and unspliced reference sequences (FASTA) and need spliced alignments (BAM+BAI) as input for VIsoQLR isoform analysis.
skills.name: long-read-rna-seq-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-rna-seq-alignment Use when you have raw long-read RNA FASTQ data (PacBio Iso-Seq, ONT) and unspliced reference sequences (FASTA) and need spliced alignments (BAM+BAI) as input for VIsoQLR isoform analysis. Reads are already aligned and you have a BAM file — proceed directly to VIsoQLR's main analysis view instead of re-aligning Reference annotation is a genome + GTF and you need a genome-guided pipeline like StringTie2/bambu; VIsoQLR's GMAP panel expects unspliced FASTA reference sequences Short-read data where spliced alignment to a genome with a standard spliced short-read aligner is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align long-read RNA sequencing reads (e.g., PacBio UHR Iso-Seq FASTQ) to a reference using GMAP inside the VIsoQLR Docker container, producing a mapped BAM file plus BAI index suitable for downstream isoform detection and quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Align long-read RNA sequencing reads (e.g., PacBio UHR Iso-Seq FASTQ) to a reference using GMAP inside the VIsoQLR Docker container, producing a mapped BAM file plus BAI index suitable for downstream isoform detection and quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already aligned and you have a BAM file — proceed directly to VIsoQLR's main analysis view instead of re-aligning Reference annotation is a genome + GTF and you need a genome-guided pipeline like StringTie2/bambu; VIsoQLR's GMAP panel expects unspliced FASTA reference sequences Short-read data where spliced alignment to a genome with a standard spliced short-read aligner is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when a trained random forest model (e.g., dsRID trained on /data/Pacbio_AD_data.tsv) needs feature-level interpretation, specifically to rank features like Skip_ratio and Len_skip by permutation contribution score.
skills.name: long-read-rna-seq-feature-analysis
skills.search_text: long-read-rna-seq-feature-analysis Use when a trained random forest model (e.g., dsRID trained on /data/Pacbio_AD_data.tsv) needs feature-level interpretation, specifically to rank features like Skip_ratio and Len_skip by permutation contribution score. You have raw PacBio BAM alignments rather than an extracted feature table — run extract_whole.py first to produce dsRID_whole.tsv before feature contribution analysis. You want to train a new model rather than interpret an existing one — use the full dsRID.sh training workflow instead of the opt-out prediction path. Your data are short-read RNA-seq — dsRID is designed for long-read RNA-seq data such as PacBio. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies which molecular features of candidate dsRNA regions drive the dsRID random forest predictions, using permutation-based feature contribution analysis on PacBio long-read RNA-seq-derived features such as skipping ratio (Skip_ratio) and length of skipping (Len_skip). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Quantifies which molecular features of candidate dsRNA regions drive the dsRID random forest predictions, using permutation-based feature contribution analysis on PacBio long-read RNA-seq-derived features such as skipping ratio (Skip_ratio) and length of skipping (Len_skip).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw PacBio BAM alignments rather than an extracted feature table — run extract_whole.py first to produce dsRID_whole.tsv before feature contribution analysis. You want to train a new model rather than interpret an existing one — use the full dsRID.sh training workflow instead of the opt-out prediction path. Your data are short-read RNA-seq — dsRID is designed for long-read RNA-seq data such as PacBio.

skills.description: Use when the input is PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM alignments and the goal is a genome-wide scan for candidate endogenous dsRNA regions that feed into novel-long-dsRNA and structured-RNA classification (e.g. reproducing dsRID Fig. 3A counts).
skills.name: long-read-rnaseq-window-scanning
skills.search_text: long-read-rnaseq-window-scanning Use when the input is PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM alignments and the goal is a genome-wide scan for candidate endogenous dsRNA regions that feed into novel-long-dsRNA and structured-RNA classification (e.g. reproducing dsRID Fig. 3A counts). Input is short-read (e.g. Illumina) RNA-seq rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM data — skipping-read evidence and the pre-trained model were built for long reads from AD brain You want to retrain the random-forest model rather than reuse the pre-trained one — use the full bash dsRID.sh training pipeline instead of the extract_whole.py/model_predict.py prediction-only path The goal is variant calling or transcript isoform reconstruction from the BAM, not genome-wide dsRNA region prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Genome-wide window scanning of PacBio long-read RNA-seq alignments with dsRID's extract_whole.py followed by random-forest scoring via model_predict.py, to nominate candidate double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) regions in silico and classify them into novel long dsRNAs and structured RNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Genome-wide window scanning of PacBio long-read RNA-seq alignments with dsRID's extract_whole.py followed by random-forest scoring via model_predict.py, to nominate candidate double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) regions in silico and classify them into novel long dsRNAs and structured RNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read (e.g. Illumina) RNA-seq rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM data — skipping-read evidence and the pre-trained model were built for long reads from AD brain You want to retrain the random-forest model rather than reuse the pre-trained one — use the full bash dsRID.sh training pipeline instead of the extract_whole.py/model_predict.py prediction-only path The goal is variant calling or transcript isoform reconstruction from the BAM, not genome-wide dsRNA region prediction

skills.description: Reference for defining consensus exon coordinates (splice start/end positions) from long-read BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments when splice sites are unknown a priori, e.g. SIRV or minigene splicing assays analyzed one gene at a time.
skills.name: long-read-splice-site-merging
skills.search_text: long-read-splice-site-merging Reference for defining consensus exon coordinates (splice start/end positions) from long-read BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments when splice sites are unknown a priori, e.g. SIRV or minigene splicing assays analyzed one gene at a time. The analysis goal is automated transcriptome-wide discovery with a supplied genome and annotation rather than interactive, single-gene curation (VIsoQLR is tailored to low-throughput splicing assays, one gene at a time) Known isoforms from another method (e.g. StringTie2 or FLAIR output) are being imported as references for comparison, so splice sites need not be re-derived from reads Reads are unaligned FASTQ; CEC detection requires mapped reads — align first with GMAP or Minimap2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 VIsoQLR's consensus exon coordinate (CEC) detection: splice-site coordinates are extracted from aligned long reads, filtered by read frequency (default 2%), and low-frequency or nearby coordinates are merged via padding (5 nt) and close-splice-site (3 nt) rules to define consensus splice sites per gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: VIsoQLR's consensus exon coordinate (CEC) detection: splice-site coordinates are extracted from aligned long reads, filtered by read frequency (default 2%), and low-frequency or nearby coordinates are merged via padding (5 nt) and close-splice-site (3 nt) rules to define consensus splice sites per gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is automated transcriptome-wide discovery with a supplied genome and annotation rather than interactive, single-gene curation (VIsoQLR is tailored to low-throughput splicing assays, one gene at a time) Known isoforms from another method (e.g. StringTie2 or FLAIR output) are being imported as references for comparison, so splice sites need not be re-derived from reads Reads are unaligned FASTQ; CEC detection requires mapped reads — align first with GMAP or Minimap2

skills.description: Use when long-read transcript sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. PacBio HiFi or ONT) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome (FASTA) before isoform detection or benchmarking of tools such as VIsoQLR, FLAIR or StringTie2.
skills.name: long-read-spliced-read-alignment
skills.search_text: long-read-spliced-read-alignment Use when long-read transcript sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. PacBio HiFi or ONT) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome (FASTA) before isoform detection or benchmarking of tools such as VIsoQLR, FLAIR or StringTie2. Input reads are short reads — the article's workflow and the splice:hq preset target long-read sequencing data; short-read aligners should be used instead A reference-guided annotation-first transcriptome workflow (e.g. epi2me-labs/wf-transcriptomes with bambu and a supplied ref_annotation GTF) is preferred over mapper-agnostic isoform calling from a fresh BAM Only a pre-existing alignment is available — VIsoQLR accepts GFF3, BED6, or BAM inputs directly, so re-alignment with this skill is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns long-read cDNA/RNA sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio Iso-Seq SIRV reads) to a reference genome using splice-aware mappers — Minimap2 with the high-quality splice preset '-ax splice:hq -uf --secondary=no', or GMAP from within the VIsoQLR Docker container — to produce spliced BAM alignments that downstream isoform detection tools (VIsoQLR, FLAIR, StringTie2) consume. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Aligns long-read cDNA/RNA sequencing reads (e.g. PacBio Iso-Seq SIRV reads) to a reference genome using splice-aware mappers — Minimap2 with the high-quality splice preset '-ax splice:hq -uf --secondary=no', or GMAP from within the VIsoQLR Docker container — to produce spliced BAM alignments that downstream isoform detection tools (VIsoQLR, FLAIR, StringTie2) consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short reads — the article's workflow and the splice:hq preset target long-read sequencing data; short-read aligners should be used instead A reference-guided annotation-first transcriptome workflow (e.g. epi2me-labs/wf-transcriptomes with bambu and a supplied ref_annotation GTF) is preferred over mapper-agnostic isoform calling from a fresh BAM Only a pre-existing alignment is available — VIsoQLR accepts GFF3, BED6, or BAM inputs directly, so re-alignment with this skill is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when raw PacBio/ONT FASTQ reads with single-cell barcodes must be splice-aligned to a reference genome and filtered to high-confidence full-length spliced isoforms before per-cell-type isoform quantification.
skills.name: long-read-transcript-alignment-filtering
skills.search_text: long-read-transcript-alignment-filtering Use when raw PacBio/ONT FASTQ reads with single-cell barcodes must be splice-aligned to a reference genome and filtered to high-confidence full-length spliced isoforms before per-cell-type isoform quantification. Input reads are short Illumina paired-end reads — minimap2/STARlong presets and MapAndFilter full-length criteria target long noisy reads Goal is genome-free transcript quantification directly from FASTQ without a reference genome and annotation Reads lack single-cell barcodes and only bulk transcriptome alignment (no cell-type deconvolution) is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Align barcoded long-read (PacBio/ONT) isoform reads to the mm10 genome with STARlong or Minimap2 and retain only mapped, full-length, spliced, poly-exonic reads via scisorseqr MapAndFilter, using GENCODE annotation, FANTOM CAGE and polyASite 2.0 interval files (cp_distance=50). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Align barcoded long-read (PacBio/ONT) isoform reads to the mm10 genome with STARlong or Minimap2 and retain only mapped, full-length, spliced, poly-exonic reads via scisorseqr MapAndFilter, using GENCODE annotation, FANTOM CAGE and polyASite 2.0 interval files (cp_distance=50).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina paired-end reads — minimap2/STARlong presets and MapAndFilter full-length criteria target long noisy reads Goal is genome-free transcript quantification directly from FASTQ without a reference genome and annotation Reads lack single-cell barcodes and only bulk transcriptome alignment (no cell-type deconvolution) is needed

skills.description: Use when analyzing long-read RNA-seq (nanopore or PacBio Iso-Seq) BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of selected genes or spike-ins (e.g., SIRVs) to identify and quantify known or novel isoforms and tune detection thresholds.
skills.name: long-read-transcriptome-isoform-detection
skills.search_text: long-read-transcriptome-isoform-detection Use when analyzing long-read RNA-seq (nanopore or PacBio Iso-Seq) BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of selected genes or spike-ins (e.g., SIRVs) to identify and quantify known or novel isoforms and tune detection thresholds. Input is raw FASTQ with no reference index and no intention to use the GMAP alignment panel — align reads first (GMAP or Minimap2) before isoform detection The goal is whole-transcriptome de-novo discovery across many samples — VIsoQLR is designed for close inspection and fine-tuning of one gene at a time in low-throughput splicing assays Isoform abundances are very small (e.g., ~1.7–4%), where LRS may overrepresent them and they are hardly distinguishable from noise in electropherograms http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect, quantify, and fine-tune isoforms from long-read sequencing data using VIsoQLR, an interactive Docker-based analyzer that defines consensus splice sites per gene and quantifies isoforms, with tunable CEC read thresholds for sensitivity analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Detect, quantify, and fine-tune isoforms from long-read sequencing data using VIsoQLR, an interactive Docker-based analyzer that defines consensus splice sites per gene and quantifies isoforms, with tunable CEC read thresholds for sensitivity analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ with no reference index and no intention to use the GMAP alignment panel — align reads first (GMAP or Minimap2) before isoform detection The goal is whole-transcriptome de-novo discovery across many samples — VIsoQLR is designed for close inspection and fine-tuning of one gene at a time in low-throughput splicing assays Isoform abundances are very small (e.g., ~1.7–4%), where LRS may overrepresent them and they are hardly distinguishable from noise in electropherograms

skills.description: Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes for TCGA cancer types (e.g., BLCA, BRCA, COAD, HNSC, KICH, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUAD, LUSC, PRAD, STAD, THCA, UCEC) and GDC somatic SNV data, and need to classify drivers as low- vs high-frequency mutations.
skills.name: long-tail-low-frequency-driver-detection
skills.search_text: long-tail-low-frequency-driver-detection Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes for TCGA cancer types (e.g., BLCA, BRCA, COAD, HNSC, KICH, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUAD, LUSC, PRAD, STAD, THCA, UCEC) and GDC somatic SNV data, and need to classify drivers as low- vs high-frequency mutations. skills.summary: Quantifies how many network-predicted cancer driver genes (intersected with the COSMIC Cancer Gene Census, CGC, 616 genes) are rarely mutated in TCGA somatic SNV data, splitting them into low-frequency (<0.05) versus high-frequency (>0.05) classes per cancer type to demonstrate detection of long-tail drivers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When your aim is discovery of the driver genes themselves from RNA-seq (use the WMDS.net network-control prediction step instead; this skill only evaluates mutation frequency of already-predicted drivers). skills.name: longest-common-subsequence-seed-detection
skills.search_text: longest-common-subsequence-seed-detection Use when clustering continuous gene expression microarray or RNA-seq matrix data to discover trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters hidden in complex, noisy data, e.g. GEO GDS datasets or BicatYeast. The goal is to find narrow biclusters specifically — the article reports BicSPAM was somewhat better at that task The input data are already discretized/integer-level and the target is not trend (order) preservation — other biclustering formulations may be more appropriate Only a single row (not a pair of rows of an index matrix) can be compared — the LCS seeding framework requires row-pair subsequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Locates trend-preserving bicluster seeds in a gene expression matrix by applying the longest common subsequence (LCS) algorithm to selected pairs of rows of an index matrix derived from the input data, as implemented in the UniBic algorithm and its parallel runibic package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: Locates trend-preserving bicluster seeds in a gene expression matrix by applying the longest common subsequence (LCS) algorithm to selected pairs of rows of an index matrix derived from the input data, as implemented in the UniBic algorithm and its parallel runibic package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to find narrow biclusters specifically — the article reports BicSPAM was somewhat better at that task The input data are already discretized/integer-level and the target is not trend (order) preservation — other biclustering formulations may be more appropriate Only a single row (not a pair of rows of an index matrix) can be compared — the LCS seeding framework requires row-pair subsequences

skills.search_text: longitudinal-gene-expression-tracking Use when pairwise differential-expression comparisons form a time course or experimental series (e.g., log2 fold-change and padj CSVs at t=3–90 min) and you need to confirm which scorecard-identified genes stay stable or shift over time. Only a single pairwise comparison exists — there is no time course or experiment series to track across count_frequencies/common_entries have not yet been run on the comparison sub-folders, so track_over_exper lacks its required pre-computed inputs Data are raw counts or lack pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns; the scorecard library expects log2 fold changes and padj as CSV columns http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A scorecard-based workflow that tracks how gene expression changes across time points or sequential experiments, using scorecard_functions.track_over_exper over sub-folders of pre-computed comparisons (e.g., Enterococcus faecalis on AGXX/Ag/V2A steel at t=3, 6, 12, 24, 60, 90 minutes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: A scorecard-based workflow that tracks how gene expression changes across time points or sequential experiments, using scorecard_functions.track_over_exper over sub-folders of pre-computed comparisons (e.g., Enterococcus faecalis on AGXX/Ag/V2A steel at t=3, 6, 12, 24, 60, 90 minutes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single pairwise comparison exists — there is no time course or experiment series to track across count_frequencies/common_entries have not yet been run on the comparison sub-folders, so track_over_exper lacks its required pre-computed inputs Data are raw counts or lack pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns; the scorecard library expects log2 fold changes and padj as CSV columns

skills.description: Use when a method for multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (cross-timepoint annotation, novel-cell detection, or tDEG calling) needs a ground-truth benchmark with controlled temporal effects, since no real dataset has fully known labels/DEG truth.
skills.name: longitudinal-scrna-seq-simulation
skills.search_text: longitudinal-scrna-seq-simulation Use when a method for multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (cross-timepoint annotation, novel-cell detection, or tDEG calling) needs a ground-truth benchmark with controlled temporal effects, since no real dataset has fully known labels/DEG truth. The real dataset already carries validated ground truth (e.g., MCL pre/post labels, accuracy, and ARI) — benchmark directly on it instead of simulating The question is about nonlinear time effects or time×condition interactions — the GLM-based tDEG framework underpinning this benchmark can only detect linear effects, so a linear-effect simulation would not exercise the failure mode The goal is a one-off descriptive analysis of an existing longitudinal dataset rather than method comparison against planted ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates multi-timepoint single-cell RNA-seq data by sampling real reference cells (e.g., public PBMC monocytes) and planting controlled temporal effects (novel cell types, cell-type-specific tDEGs at graded strengths) so that cross-timepoint methods like CASi can be benchmarked against DESeq2, MAST, Seurat Wilcoxon, CHETAH, scPred, and scmap with known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Simulates multi-timepoint single-cell RNA-seq data by sampling real reference cells (e.g., public PBMC monocytes) and planting controlled temporal effects (novel cell types, cell-type-specific tDEGs at graded strengths) so that cross-timepoint methods like CASi can be benchmarked against DESeq2, MAST, Seurat Wilcoxon, CHETAH, scPred, and scmap with known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The real dataset already carries validated ground truth (e.g., MCL pre/post labels, accuracy, and ARI) — benchmark directly on it instead of simulating The question is about nonlinear time effects or time×condition interactions — the GLM-based tDEG framework underpinning this benchmark can only detect linear effects, so a linear-effect simulation would not exercise the failure mode The goal is a one-off descriptive analysis of an existing longitudinal dataset rather than method comparison against planted ground truth

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more timepoints, a metadata table with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and you need genes whose expression trends over time differ between strata (tDEGs).
skills.name: longitudinal-scrnaseq-differential-expression
skills.search_text: longitudinal-scrnaseq-differential-expression Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more timepoints, a metadata table with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and you need genes whose expression trends over time differ between strata (tDEGs). You expect nonlinear temporal changes in expression — the article states 'the current GLM framework can only detect linear effect, i.e., the linear change of gene expression by time or the interaction of time and condition' The data are cross-sectional (a single time point) with no Time-by-strata structure to test — use standard DE methods like DESeq2 or MAST instead The Group variable is multi-class rather than the binary strata factor the metadata check requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies temporal differentially expressed genes (tDEGs) in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data by fitting a per-gene negative binomial GLM (log link) with Time, Group, and Time-by-Group interaction covariates, followed by Bonferroni correction. This is CASi's FindTemporalDEGs mechanism for detecting genes with divergent time-trending behavior across strata. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Identifies temporal differentially expressed genes (tDEGs) in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data by fitting a per-gene negative binomial GLM (log link) with Time, Group, and Time-by-Group interaction covariates, followed by Bonferroni correction. This is CASi's FindTemporalDEGs mechanism for detecting genes with divergent time-trending behavior across strata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You expect nonlinear temporal changes in expression — the article states 'the current GLM framework can only detect linear effect, i.e., the linear change of gene expression by time or the interaction of time and condition' The data are cross-sectional (a single time point) with no Time-by-strata structure to test — use standard DE methods like DESeq2 or MAST instead The Group variable is multi-class rather than the binary strata factor the metadata check requires

skills.description: Use when a model's training objective combines multiple loss terms (e.g. scBGEDA's zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss plus an MSE denoising reconstruction loss) and you need to isolate whether a specific term improves downstream performance such as cell-type clustering ARI.
skills.name: loss-ablation-study-design
skills.search_text: loss-ablation-study-design Use when a model's training objective combines multiple loss terms (e.g. scBGEDA's zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss plus an MSE denoising reconstruction loss) and you need to isolate whether a specific term improves downstream performance such as cell-type clustering ARI. When the model's objective has only a single loss term — there is no component to ablate and the comparison degenerates to the full model against itself. When the question is whether the overall method beats baselines (state-of-the-art comparison experiments) rather than attributing performance to a specific loss component. When computational budget does not permit retraining all configurations across the ten seeds with identical hyperparameters — an uncontrolled ablation with differing seeds or parameters confounds the loss-term effect. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Design and execute a loss-term ablation for a multi-component training objective — here, removing the MSE follower-decoder denoising term from scBGEDA's dual ZINB+MSE loss — and compare clustering performance (ARI) across datasets and seeds to quantify each loss term's contribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Design and execute a loss-term ablation for a multi-component training objective — here, removing the MSE follower-decoder denoising term from scBGEDA's dual ZINB+MSE loss — and compare clustering performance (ARI) across datasets and seeds to quantify each loss term's contribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the model's objective has only a single loss term — there is no component to ablate and the comparison degenerates to the full model against itself. When the question is whether the overall method beats baselines (state-of-the-art comparison experiments) rather than attributing performance to a specific loss component. When computational budget does not permit retraining all configurations across the ten seeds with identical hyperparameters — an uncontrolled ablation with differing seeds or parameters confounds the loss-term effect.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how individual biologically-informed loss components of BIDCell contribute to segmentation performance, e.g. reproducing the ablation trends of Supplementary Figs. 4-5 on Xenium breast cancer data.
skills.name: loss-weight-ablation-study-design
skills.search_text: loss-weight-ablation-study-design Use when benchmarking how individual biologically-informed loss components of BIDCell contribute to segmentation performance, e.g. reproducing the ablation trends of Supplementary Figs. 4-5 on Xenium breast cancer data. You want to benchmark BIDCell against external segmentation methods (Cellpose, Baysor, StereoCell) rather than dissect its own loss terms — use the full CellSPA benchmarking comparison instead. Your data are not from an SST platform with a xenium/cosmx/merscope/stereoseq example configuration available and you lack the single-cell reference needed for preannotate. You only need a single full-model segmentation result (run model.run_pipeline() directly rather than a loss-weight sweep). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Designs and executes a loss-weight ablation study for BIDCell on the Xenium-BreastCancer1 dataset: each biologically-informed loss weight (lambda) in the xenium .yaml configuration is zeroed one at a time, segmentation is retrained, and performance is quantified to show the synergistic contribution of each loss component. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Designs and executes a loss-weight ablation study for BIDCell on the Xenium-BreastCancer1 dataset: each biologically-informed loss weight (lambda) in the xenium .yaml configuration is zeroed one at a time, segmentation is retrained, and performance is quantified to show the synergistic contribution of each loss component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to benchmark BIDCell against external segmentation methods (Cellpose, Baysor, StereoCell) rather than dissect its own loss terms — use the full CellSPA benchmarking comparison instead. Your data are not from an SST platform with a xenium/cosmx/merscope/stereoseq example configuration available and you lack the single-cell reference needed for preannotate. You only need a single full-model segmentation result (run model.run_pipeline() directly rather than a loss-weight sweep).

skills.description: Use when testing whether a gene set is enriched in differentially expressed genes from scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) after fitting iDEA with iDEA.fit, and a properly calibrated enrichment p-value is required.
skills.name: louis-method-pvalue-calibration
skills.search_text: louis-method-pvalue-calibration Use when testing whether a gene set is enriched in differentially expressed genes from scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) after fitting iDEA with iDEA.fit, and a properly calibrated enrichment p-value is required. Summary statistics are not gene-level DE effect sizes (beta, beta_var) from scRNA-seq DE tools, so the iDEA hierarchical model does not apply Gene set coverage rate is below the min_precent_annot threshold (default 0.0025) or fewer than min_degene = 5 DE genes are detected Only an uncalibrated nominal p-value is acceptable and the computational cost of MCMC (mcmc_iter = 1000) plus the Louis information correction is prohibitive http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes calibrated gene-set enrichment p-values in iDEA by applying the Louis missing-information correction to the observed Fisher information after EM-MCMC fitting, correcting the underestimation of variance that arises because latent gene DE indicators are not directly observed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Computes calibrated gene-set enrichment p-values in iDEA by applying the Louis missing-information correction to the observed Fisher information after EM-MCMC fitting, correcting the underestimation of variance that arises because latent gene DE indicators are not directly observed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Summary statistics are not gene-level DE effect sizes (beta, beta_var) from scRNA-seq DE tools, so the iDEA hierarchical model does not apply Gene set coverage rate is below the min_precent_annot threshold (default 0.0025) or fewer than min_degene = 5 DE genes are detected Only an uncalibrated nominal p-value is acceptable and the computational cost of MCMC (mcmc_iter = 1000) plus the Louis information correction is prohibitive

skills.description: Use when you must quantify whether cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) attains stronger significance for a known simulated or real DA shift than standard Louvain clustering on the same single-cell graph.
skills.name: louvain-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: louvain-benchmark-comparison Use when you must quantify whether cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) attains stronger significance for a known simulated or real DA shift than standard Louvain clustering on the same single-cell graph. The input is already a feature/abundance table without single-cell counts and no cell-cell nearest-neighbour graph can be built The study displays strong clustering structure — the article notes ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog was 'more pronounced in studies displaying weaker clustering structure', so the benchmark may show negligible gain on strongly structured data You only need a single clustering result without replicates — the comparison requires distributions of DA P-values over repeated runs to be meaningful Benchmark differential-abundance testing pipelines that differ only in clustering strategy — cell-attribute aware EVA (ELVAR) versus deterministic (sequential) and non-sequential (stochastic) Louvain analogs — by comparing negative-binomial-regression DA-test P-value distributions over repeated runs with one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Benchmark differential-abundance testing pipelines that differ only in clustering strategy — cell-attribute aware EVA (ELVAR) versus deterministic (sequential) and non-sequential (stochastic) Louvain analogs — by comparing negative-binomial-regression DA-test P-value distributions over repeated runs with one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/abundance table without single-cell counts and no cell-cell nearest-neighbour graph can be built The study displays strong clustering structure — the article notes ELVAR's improvement over the Louvain-analog was 'more pronounced in studies displaying weaker clustering structure', so the benchmark may show negligible gain on strongly structured data You only need a single clustering result without replicates — the comparison requires distributions of DA P-values over repeated runs to be meaningful

skills.search_text: louvain-cell-type-clustering Use when training scDesign2 in scReadSim on a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix whose cells lack predefined cell labels (no celllabel_file), since scDesign2 requires discrete cell types. Cells follow continuous trajectories or spatial locations rather than discrete clusters — use scDesign3 instead of scDesign2 with Louvain labels A predefined celllabel_file is already available, making re-clustering redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pre-clusters cells of a real scRNA-seq UMI count matrix with Louvain clustering (Seurat R package) so that discrete cell-type labels are available to train scDesign2 inside scReadSim's synthetic count generation step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Pre-clusters cells of a real scRNA-seq UMI count matrix with Louvain clustering (Seurat R package) so that discrete cell-type labels are available to train scDesign2 inside scReadSim's synthetic count generation step.

skills.description: Use when training a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq cell clustering (e.g. scGAE) and initial cluster centers are needed before soft-assignment/KL clustering training; also relevant to any DEC-style pipeline requiring centroid initialization.
skills.name: louvain-centroid-initialization
skills.search_text: louvain-centroid-initialization Use when training a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq cell clustering (e.g. scGAE) and initial cluster centers are needed before soft-assignment/KL clustering training; also relevant to any DEC-style pipeline requiring centroid initialization. Input data has not been pre-trained/embedded yet — Louvain should be run on the embedded data, not the raw high-dimensional count matrix. The analysis goal is pure visualization/trajectory inference without clustering; the clustering-training stage (and its centroid initialization) is optional in scGAE. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Obtains initial cluster centroids for scGAE's deep-clustering stage by running Louvain clustering on the pre-trained autoencoder's embedded data, which are then used to initialize the DEC-style KL-loss clustering training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Obtains initial cluster centroids for scGAE's deep-clustering stage by running Louvain clustering on the pre-trained autoencoder's embedded data, which are then used to initialize the DEC-style KL-loss clustering training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been pre-trained/embedded yet — Louvain should be run on the embedded data, not the raw high-dimensional count matrix. The analysis goal is pure visualization/trajectory inference without clustering; the clustering-training stage (and its centroid initialization) is optional in scGAE.

skills.description: Use when a simulated or ground-truth-labelled scRNA-Seq dataset is available and you need to quantify whether cell-attribute aware EVA community detection recovers known labels better than a Louvain-analog, via ARI and chi-square DA statistics.
skills.name: louvain-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-benchmarking Use when a simulated or ground-truth-labelled scRNA-Seq dataset is available and you need to quantify whether cell-attribute aware EVA community detection recovers known labels better than a Louvain-analog, via ARI and chi-square DA statistics. Datasets with strong clustering structure — the article notes ELVAR's improvement over its Louvain-analog was more pronounced in studies with weaker clustering structure and less noticeable in stronger ones Input is a real dataset with no simulated or trusted ground-truth labels, making adjusted Rand Index against truth impossible to compute Purity parameter (alpha) cannot be varied — EVA only outperformed Louvain at larger purity parameter values in the benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks EVA (cell-attribute aware, Extended Louvain) clustering against the standard Louvain baseline on a simulated 200-cell Tabula Muris Senis monocyte scRNA-Seq dataset, quantifying recovery of simulated perturbation labels via adjusted Rand Index and chi-square differential-abundance tests across the alpha purity-parameter grid (0.1–0.9). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks EVA (cell-attribute aware, Extended Louvain) clustering against the standard Louvain baseline on a simulated 200-cell Tabula Muris Senis monocyte scRNA-Seq dataset, quantifying recovery of simulated perturbation labels via adjusted Rand Index and chi-square differential-abundance tests across the alpha purity-parameter grid (0.1–0.9).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with strong clustering structure — the article notes ELVAR's improvement over its Louvain-analog was more pronounced in studies with weaker clustering structure and less noticeable in stronger ones Input is a real dataset with no simulated or trusted ground-truth labels, making adjusted Rand Index against truth impossible to compute Purity parameter (alpha) cannot be varied — EVA only outperformed Louvain at larger purity parameter values in the benchmark

skills.description: Use when comparing the output embeddings of multiple scRNA-seq integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER, scVI, Harmony) and you need standardized, composite bio-conservation and batch-correction scores to rank them.
skills.name: louvain-clustering-bio-conservation-scoring
skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-bio-conservation-scoring Use when comparing the output embeddings of multiple scRNA-seq integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER, scVI, Harmony) and you need standardized, composite bio-conservation and batch-correction scores to rank them. Evaluating a single integration output with no competing methods — min-max normalization across methods is required for the composite scores and is undefined for a lone method Clustering raw counts or non-integrated embeddings to measure biological structure alone — this skill is specifically for scoring batch-corrected integrated embeddings against cell-type ground truth Datasets lacking cell-type annotations, since NMI, ARI, and cell-type ASW all require ground-truth labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking skill for evaluating single-cell data integration methods: it Louvain-clusters each integrated embedding at the resolution that maximizes NMI, computes biological conservation metrics (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW) alongside batch-correction metrics (ASW batch, PCR batch, graph connectivity, kBET), and aggregates min-max normalized values into composite scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for evaluating single-cell data integration methods: it Louvain-clusters each integrated embedding at the resolution that maximizes NMI, computes biological conservation metrics (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW) alongside batch-correction metrics (ASW batch, PCR batch, graph connectivity, kBET), and aggregates min-max normalized values into composite scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating a single integration output with no competing methods — min-max normalization across methods is required for the composite scores and is undefined for a lone method Clustering raw counts or non-integrated embeddings to measure biological structure alone — this skill is specifically for scoring batch-corrected integrated embeddings against cell-type ground truth Datasets lacking cell-type annotations, since NMI, ARI, and cell-type ASW all require ground-truth labels

skills.description: Use when evaluating integrated scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI/Scanorama/Harmony baselines) and you need per-method cluster assignments that are resolution-optimized before computing NMI, ARI, or ASW metrics.
skills.name: louvain-clustering-nmi-optimization
skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-nmi-optimization Use when evaluating integrated scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI/Scanorama/Harmony baselines) and you need per-method cluster assignments that are resolution-optimized before computing NMI, ARI, or ASW metrics. When the goal is batch-correction-only assessment (batch ASW, PCR batch, kBET, graph connectivity) that does not require cluster assignments When no ground-truth cell-type labels exist to compute NMI, since the resolution cannot be selected by NMI maximization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters each integrated single-cell embedding with the Louvain algorithm, sweeping resolution to find the value that maximizes NMI against ground-truth cell-type labels, so downstream bio-conservation metrics (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW) are computed on a fair, optimized clustering per method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Clusters each integrated single-cell embedding with the Louvain algorithm, sweeping resolution to find the value that maximizes NMI against ground-truth cell-type labels, so downstream bio-conservation metrics (NMI, ARI, cell-type ASW) are computed on a fair, optimized clustering per method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch-correction-only assessment (batch ASW, PCR batch, kBET, graph connectivity) that does not require cluster assignments When no ground-truth cell-type labels exist to compute NMI, since the resolution cannot be selected by NMI maximization

skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-of-control-cells Use when a perturbation scRNAseq analysis requires reference cell-state labels from the control condition alone (scanpy neighbors + Louvain on control cells) before NCFS feature weighting and semi-supervised clustering. When the goal is de novo clustering of the full perturbed-plus-control dataset without control-guided anchoring — ICAT's sslouvain, not plain Louvain on controls, is the appropriate step When cell states or marker genes are already known a priori and supervised label transfer would be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Unsupervised Louvain clustering of control-arm single-cell data to define control-defined cell states whose labels anchor ICAT's downstream semi-supervised clustering of perturbed cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278

skills.description: Use when a cell-level embedding matrix (e.g., scGAE latent representation of Splatter-simulated scenario3/4 scRNA-seq data) is available and discrete cell clusters must be recovered and scored by NMI.
skills.name: louvain-clustering-of-embeddings
skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-of-embeddings Use when a cell-level embedding matrix (e.g., scGAE latent representation of Splatter-simulated scenario3/4 scRNA-seq data) is available and discrete cell clusters must be recovered and scored by NMI. No low-dimensional embedding exists yet — raw count matrices should first be preprocessed (scTransform) and embedded (e.g., via scGAE's KNN graph, K=35, and graph autoencoder) before Louvain is applied. The goal is trajectory inference or 2D visualization rather than discrete cluster recovery — the paper evaluates clustering via NMI separately from trajectory tasks where scGAE and scGNN perform similarly. A direct 2D layout is the only representation available — the article notes the complex data structure is hard to embed directly into two dimensions by a graph autoencoder, so clustering should use the intermediate-dimension embedding rather than a distorted 2D projection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Louvain community detection to low-dimensional single-cell embeddings (e.g., from scGAE's multitask-oriented graph autoencoder) to obtain predicted cell clusters and initial centroids, evaluated by NMI against ground-truth labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Applies Louvain community detection to low-dimensional single-cell embeddings (e.g., from scGAE's multitask-oriented graph autoencoder) to obtain predicted cell clusters and initial centroids, evaluated by NMI against ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No low-dimensional embedding exists yet — raw count matrices should first be preprocessed (scTransform) and embedded (e.g., via scGAE's KNN graph, K=35, and graph autoencoder) before Louvain is applied. The goal is trajectory inference or 2D visualization rather than discrete cluster recovery — the paper evaluates clustering via NMI separately from trajectory tasks where scGAE and scGNN perform similarly. A direct 2D layout is the only representation available — the article notes the complex data structure is hard to embed directly into two dimensions by a graph autoencoder, so clustering should use the intermediate-dimension embedding rather than a distorted 2D projection.

skills.description: Use when an ensemble of simulated differentiation trajectories (from RNA-velocity Markov sampling) must be partitioned into sub-trajectory groups within each terminal state before DTW alignment and consensus construction.
skills.name: louvain-clustering-of-simulated-trajectories
skills.search_text: louvain-clustering-of-simulated-trajectories Use when an ensemble of simulated differentiation trajectories (from RNA-velocity Markov sampling) must be partitioned into sub-trajectory groups within each terminal state before DTW alignment and consensus construction. The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or root/terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in these cases (e.g. the hepatocyte zonation dataset showed fuzzy, patternless root-cell probabilities) Input is a pre-clustered downstream analysis problem unrelated to trajectory simulation ensembles — Louvain clustering here operates specifically on Hausdorff distances between simulated trajectories within a common terminal region Cell cycling with overlapping start/end regions when terminal supervision is absent — convergence/cycle handling requires the simulation-ensemble machinery, not plain cell clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Within the Cytopath pipeline, simulated Markov-chain cell-state sequences that terminate at a common terminal region are compared via pairwise Euclidean Hausdorff distances and grouped by Louvain clustering into sub-trajectory clusters prior to dynamic-time-warping alignment and consensus averaging. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Within the Cytopath pipeline, simulated Markov-chain cell-state sequences that terminate at a common terminal region are compared via pairwise Euclidean Hausdorff distances and grouped by Louvain clustering into sub-trajectory clusters prior to dynamic-time-warping alignment and consensus averaging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty or root/terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in these cases (e.g. the hepatocyte zonation dataset showed fuzzy, patternless root-cell probabilities) Input is a pre-clustered downstream analysis problem unrelated to trajectory simulation ensembles — Louvain clustering here operates specifically on Hausdorff distances between simulated trajectories within a common terminal region Cell cycling with overlapping start/end regions when terminal supervision is absent — convergence/cycle handling requires the simulation-ensemble machinery, not plain cell clustering

skills.description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrix (h5 or mtx) has been filtered by a total-count cutoff and you suspect real low-count cells (e.g., platelets) were discarded.

skills.search_text: low-count-barcodes-recovery-filtering Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrix (h5 or mtx) has been filtered by a total-count cutoff and you suspect real low-count cells (e.g., platelets) were discarded. The count matrix is already filtered or only contains barcodes passing the original threshold — recovered below-threshold barcodes cannot be extracted without raw unfiltered data You need ambient RNA-corrected expression values — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression profiles; tools like SoupX are required for that Barcodes have total counts <= 10 — these are excluded from the EmptyNN analysis by design http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Recover and validate genuine cell-containing barcodes that fall below an original study's total-count filtering threshold (e.g., Cell Ranger v.2-style cutoff of 200) using EmptyNN's positive-unlabeled neural network, then characterize the recovered low-count cells with Seurat clustering and reference-dataset correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Recover and validate genuine cell-containing barcodes that fall below an original study's total-count filtering threshold (e.g., Cell Ranger v.2-style cutoff of 200) using EmptyNN's positive-unlabeled neural network, then characterize the recovered low-count cells with Seurat clustering and reference-dataset correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix is already filtered or only contains barcodes passing the original threshold — recovered below-threshold barcodes cannot be extracted without raw unfiltered data You need ambient RNA-corrected expression values — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression profiles; tools like SoupX are required for that Barcodes have total counts <= 10 — these are excluded from the EmptyNN analysis by design

skills.summary: A preprocessing step for singleCellHaystack analyses that removes very lowly expressed genes — genes with non-zero counts in fewer than 10 cells (or spots) — to reduce computation and noise before Kullback-Leibler divergence-based DEG prediction.

skills.name: low-dimensional-embedding-cell-ordering
skills.search_text: low-dimensional-embedding-cell-ordering Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g. mouse embryo datasets Yan, Goolam, Deng) already have a scDHA low-dimensional representation and the goal is a developmental pseudo-time ordering whose accuracy can be scored as R-squared against known capture/stage time. The data have no scDHA low-dimensional embedding — scDHA.pt's input is the dimension reduction output, so raw counts must first be embedded via scDHA The analysis stack is scVI alone: 'The scVI package itself is not capable of clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference' There is no reference time/stage information and the goal is only qualitative trajectory visualization rather than an R-squared-scored ordering Infers single-cell pseudo-time by ordering cells along a trajectory in a scDHA low-dimensional embedding (via scDHA.pt), and benchmarks the ordering against state-of-the-art trajectory tools (Monocle, TSCAN, Slingshot, SCANPY) using R-squared against known embryonic capture stages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Infers single-cell pseudo-time by ordering cells along a trajectory in a scDHA low-dimensional embedding (via scDHA.pt), and benchmarks the ordering against state-of-the-art trajectory tools (Monocle, TSCAN, Slingshot, SCANPY) using R-squared against known embryonic capture stages.
