skills.description: Use when two denoised, same-gene-set GRN adjacency matrices (e.g., sparse dgCMatrix networks X and Y from CP tensor decomposition) must be aligned into a shared low-dimensional space to compare each gene's regulatory positions across conditions.
skills.name: low-dimensional-embedding-construction
skills.search_text: low-dimensional-embedding-construction Use when two denoised, same-gene-set GRN adjacency matrices (e.g., sparse dgCMatrix networks X and Y from CP tensor decomposition) must be aligned into a shared low-dimensional space to compare each gene's regulatory positions across conditions. Input networks come from different gene sets or have not been denoised — the joint Laplacian requires symmetric Wx and Wy over the same gene set The goal is comparing highly dissimilar samples — scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type A ranked gene list is needed without per-gene cross-condition coordinates — the downstream dRegulation step alone may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a shared low-dimensional embedding of two denoised single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) by solving an eigenvalue problem on a joint Laplacian, so each gene from both samples receives coordinates on a common manifold that can be directly compared. This is the manifold-alignment step (manifoldAlignment) of the scTenifoldNet workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Constructs a shared low-dimensional embedding of two denoised single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) by solving an eigenvalue problem on a joint Laplacian, so each gene from both samples receives coordinates on a common manifold that can be directly compared. This is the manifold-alignment step (manifoldAlignment) of the scTenifoldNet workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input networks come from different gene sets or have not been denoised — the joint Laplacian requires symmetric Wx and Wy over the same gene set The goal is comparing highly dissimilar samples — scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type A ranked gene list is needed without per-gene cross-condition coordinates — the downstream dRegulation step alone may suffice

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple processing batches and you need pseudotime/trajectory inference on an embedding that suppresses technical batch differences (e.g. DESC X_Embeded_z feeding Monocle3).
skills.name: low-dimensional-embedding-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: low-dimensional-embedding-trajectory-analysis Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple processing batches and you need pseudotime/trajectory inference on an embedding that suppresses technical batch differences (e.g. DESC X_Embeded_z feeding Monocle3). When technical batch differences are larger than true biological variation — DESC only removes batch effects when technical differences are smaller than biological ones When the goal is clustering accuracy assessment alone (use ARI against reference labels) rather than pseudotemporal/trajectory reconstruction When no per-cell batch labels are available, since batch-mixing KL divergence cannot be computed to validate the trajectory http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds trajectory/pseudotime reconstructions (e.g. Monocle3) on a deep-learning low-dimensional embedding such as DESC's X_Embeded_z representation, so that pseudotemporal structure is revealed while batch effects are removed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Builds trajectory/pseudotime reconstructions (e.g. Monocle3) on a deep-learning low-dimensional embedding such as DESC's X_Embeded_z representation, so that pseudotemporal structure is revealed while batch effects are removed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When technical batch differences are larger than true biological variation — DESC only removes batch effects when technical differences are smaller than biological ones When the goal is clustering accuracy assessment alone (use ARI against reference labels) rather than pseudotemporal/trajectory reconstruction When no per-cell batch labels are available, since batch-mixing KL divergence cannot be computed to validate the trajectory

skills.description: Use when comparing 2D embeddings of scRNA-seq count matrices across methods (EDGE vs UMAP vs t-SNE), especially to assess separation of rare cell types against dominant populations.
skills.name: low-dimensional-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: low-dimensional-embedding-visualization Use when comparing 2D embeddings of scRNA-seq count matrices across methods (EDGE vs UMAP vs t-SNE), especially to assess separation of rare cell types against dominant populations. The goal is feature gene identification rather than embedding — EDGE's gene-selection output, not the 2D plot, is the deliverable in that case Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a normalized/log-transformed matrix for which library-size normalization should not be re-applied Global hierarchical structure recovery is the primary goal and only t-SNE is considered — the article notes t-SNE 'may suffer from losing the global geometry pattern/property of the data' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Produce side-by-side two-dimensional scatter plot embeddings of single-cell RNA-seq data using EDGE, UMAP, and t-SNE with matched seeds and neighborhood sizes, so that rare cell type separation can be visually and quantitatively compared (e.g., via silhouette index). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature gene identification rather than embedding — EDGE's gene-selection output, not the 2D plot, is the deliverable in that case Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or a normalized/log-transformed matrix for which library-size normalization should not be re-applied Global hierarchical structure recovery is the primary goal and only t-SNE is considered — the article notes t-SNE 'may suffer from losing the global geometry pattern/property of the data'

skills.description: Use when high-dimensional raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) with technical noise and dropout need to be compressed into a low-dimensional cell representation for clustering, visualization, classification, or trajectory analysis.
skills.name: low-dimensional-representation-learning
skills.search_text: low-dimensional-representation-learning Use when high-dimensional raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) with technical noise and dropout need to be compressed into a low-dimensional cell representation for clustering, visualization, classification, or trajectory analysis. The scVI package alone may be preferable if only variational-inference dimension reduction is needed without integrated clustering/visualization/classification/pseudo-time (though scVI itself is not capable of these four tasks). Input is not single-cell high-throughput data with dropout/noise issues; the article's rationale targets scRNA-seq noise and dropout challenges. Only a standalone imputation-based clustering is needed — CIDR handles dropouts via implicit imputation rather than autoencoder representation learning. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Learn a compact, denoised low-dimensional representation of scRNA-seq data using scDHA's hierarchical autoencoder: a non-negative kernel autoencoder filters insignificant genes/components, and a stacked Bayesian autoencoder (built on a modified VAE) projects cells into a compressed space suitable for clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Learn a compact, denoised low-dimensional representation of scRNA-seq data using scDHA's hierarchical autoencoder: a non-negative kernel autoencoder filters insignificant genes/components, and a stacked Bayesian autoencoder (built on a modified VAE) projects cells into a compressed space suitable for clustering, visualization, classification, and pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scVI package alone may be preferable if only variational-inference dimension reduction is needed without integrated clustering/visualization/classification/pseudo-time (though scVI itself is not capable of these four tasks). Input is not single-cell high-throughput data with dropout/noise issues; the article's rationale targets scRNA-seq noise and dropout challenges. Only a standalone imputation-based clustering is needed — CIDR handles dropouts via implicit imputation rather than autoencoder representation learning.

Input is already a filtered, normalized feature matrix or a cell-by-gene count table in formats like .h5ad rather than a raw FPKM/TPM gene-by-cell matrix The goal is to filter low-quality or contaminated cells rather than genes — that is handled by filterLowQualityCells and filterContaminatedCells, not prefilterGenes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Removes non- or low-expressed genes from an scRNA-Seq expression matrix using SINCERA's prefilterGenes function, then floors residual FPKM/TPM values with expr.minimum, as the gene-level half of SINCERA's preprocessing stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered, normalized feature matrix or a cell-by-gene count table in formats like .h5ad rather than a raw FPKM/TPM gene-by-cell matrix The goal is to filter low-quality or contaminated cells rather than genes — that is handled by filterLowQualityCells and filterContaminatedCells, not prefilterGenes

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a genome-guided transcriptome assembler (e.g. Tiglon vs StringTie2/Scallop) on RNA-seq alignments and you must show whether gains come specifically from recovering lowly expressed reference transcripts.
skills.name: low-expression-transcript-recovery-analysis
skills.search_text: low-expression-transcript-recovery-analysis Use when benchmarking a genome-guided transcriptome assembler (e.g. Tiglon vs StringTie2/Scallop) on RNA-seq alignments and you must show whether gains come specifically from recovering lowly expressed reference transcripts. Input data is long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets The analysis goal is annotation-guided assembly — the current Tiglon version has no option for using known transcript annotations to guide assembly Only a single aligner's BAM is available — Tiglon is designed to integrate alignments of different mapping tools (Hisat2 and Star), so single-aligner input forfeits the labeled-splice-graph advantage being evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantify how many lowly expressed reference transcripts an assembler recovers by stratifying Cuffcompare evaluation results against the reference annotation (e.g. mm10.ncbiRefSeq.gtf or hg38.ncbiRefSeq.gtf) by expression level. In the Tiglon paper this analysis is what reveals Tiglon's key advantage: it is 'significantly powerful in recovering lowly expressed transcripts' compared with StringTie2, Scallop, and StringTie2-Merge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Quantify how many lowly expressed reference transcripts an assembler recovers by stratifying Cuffcompare evaluation results against the reference annotation (e.g. mm10.ncbiRefSeq.gtf or hg38.ncbiRefSeq.gtf) by expression level. In the Tiglon paper this analysis is what reveals Tiglon's key advantage: it is 'significantly powerful in recovering lowly expressed transcripts' compared with StringTie2, Scallop, and StringTie2-Merge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets The analysis goal is annotation-guided assembly — the current Tiglon version has no option for using known transcript annotations to guide assembly Only a single aligner's BAM is available — Tiglon is designed to integrate alignments of different mapping tools (Hisat2 and Star), so single-aligner input forfeits the labeled-splice-graph advantage being evaluated

skills.description: Use when quantifying mutant gRNA molecule fractions in a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library and sequencing-error-derived molecules must be excluded before variant calling.
skills.name: low-read-support-umi-filtering
skills.search_text: low-read-support-umi-filtering Use when quantifying mutant gRNA molecule fractions in a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library and sequencing-error-derived molecules must be excluded before variant calling. You want to profile ambient or very-low-abundance gRNA capture rather than remove low-support UMIs — dropping UMIs below min_reads biases the measured molecule pool toward well-supported sequences The goal is assigning gRNAs to cells (assign_gRNA.assign_gRNA_to_cell with min_umi, default 3), which is a distinct downstream step rather than molecule-level error filtering Detecting CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing effects in transcriptome data, which uses GiRAFR's separate editing-effect analysis mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Discard sequencing-error-derived gRNA molecules by filtering UMI-cell barcode consensus sequences with fewer than a minimum read count (GiRAFR's min_reads parameter), before calling gRNA mutations; for the in-house CROP-seq library this still left 28.4% of molecules mutant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Discard sequencing-error-derived gRNA molecules by filtering UMI-cell barcode consensus sequences with fewer than a minimum read count (GiRAFR's min_reads parameter), before calling gRNA mutations; for the in-house CROP-seq library this still left 28.4% of molecules mutant.

skills.description: Use when quantifying how a fusion caller's sensitivity degrades with shallower bulk or single-cell RNA-seq depth, e.g. testing detection limits on CCLE bRNA-seq subsampled below 1 million read pairs.
skills.name: low-sequencing-depth-sensitivity-analysis
skills.search_text: low-sequencing-depth-sensitivity-analysis Use when quantifying how a fusion caller's sensitivity degrades with shallower bulk or single-cell RNA-seq depth, e.g. testing detection limits on CCLE bRNA-seq subsampled below 1 million read pairs. Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion only supports paired-end RNA-seq The goal is discovery of fusions not involving a known target gene — Anchored-fusion only reports fusions including the anchored gene of interest The question is fusion-call accuracy at full depth rather than sensitivity decay across depths (use standard de novo callers directly instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks fusion-gene detection sensitivity as sequencing depth is progressively reduced by repeated random subsampling of paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files, verifying whether an ultra-sensitive caller (Anchored-fusion) still detects known fusions where standard tools fail below 1 M read pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Benchmarks fusion-gene detection sensitivity as sequencing depth is progressively reduced by repeated random subsampling of paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files, verifying whether an ultra-sensitive caller (Anchored-fusion) still detects known fusions where standard tools fail below 1 M read pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion only supports paired-end RNA-seq The goal is discovery of fusions not involving a known target gene — Anchored-fusion only reports fusions including the anchored gene of interest The question is fusion-call accuracy at full depth rather than sensitivity decay across depths (use standard de novo callers directly instead)

skills.description: Use when preparing gene-by-sample expression matrices for differential network inference and the feature space is large relative to sample size — filter by per-gene variance (here a cutoff of 0.4) before running BoostDiff or similar tree-based methods.
skills.name: low-variance-gene-filtering
skills.search_text: low-variance-gene-filtering Use when preparing gene-by-sample expression matrices for differential network inference and the feature space is large relative to sample size — filter by per-gene variance (here a cutoff of 0.4) before running BoostDiff or similar tree-based methods. The dataset has already been preprocessed and feature-selected (e.g. TCGA or COVID-19 matrices from the tutorial/preprocessing scripts) — re-filtering could remove disease-relevant genes. The downstream tool does not require a reduced feature space and sample sizes are ample (>= 30 per condition), making aggressive variance pruning unnecessary or harmful. Genes of low variance are themselves the object of study (e.g. housekeeping-gene control analysis) rather than input to differential network inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A preprocessing step that removes genes below a variance cutoff (e.g. 0.4 in the GSE27219 B. subtilis stress dataset) before differential network inference, shrinking the feature space so BoostDiff models focus on genes whose expression actually varies across conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: A preprocessing step that removes genes below a variance cutoff (e.g. 0.4 in the GSE27219 B. subtilis stress dataset) before differential network inference, shrinking the feature space so BoostDiff models focus on genes whose expression actually varies across conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has already been preprocessed and feature-selected (e.g. TCGA or COVID-19 matrices from the tutorial/preprocessing scripts) — re-filtering could remove disease-relevant genes. The downstream tool does not require a reduced feature space and sample sizes are ample (>= 30 per condition), making aggressive variance pruning unnecessary or harmful. Genes of low variance are themselves the object of study (e.g. housekeeping-gene control analysis) rather than input to differential network inference.

skills.description: Use when screening ligand-receptor pairs from a curated LR database against pseudotime-ordered scRNA-seq trajectories to identify co-varying LR pairs in temporal developmental data.
skills.name: lr-pair-database-mapping
skills.search_text: lr-pair-database-mapping Use when screening ligand-receptor pairs from a curated LR database against pseudotime-ordered scRNA-seq trajectories to identify co-varying LR pairs in temporal developmental data. Input data has no temporal/trajectory ordering — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for communication between given cell types and would be more appropriate for static cell-type comparisons Goal is to call active (not merely co-varying) LR pairs — the |PCC| = 0.1 filter is only the first screen; candidate eLR and active LR require Granger causality (p < 0.01) and SCC_ens > 0.8 or < -0.8 Interest is in maternal-embryo or EV-mediated communication — the TimeTalk autocrine/eLR screening assumption precludes maternal-embryo interactions and other non-LR-mediated communication types http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps curated ligand-receptor database pairs (e.g. the CellTalkDB-derived Mouse-2020-Shao-LR-pairs.txt, 2034 mouse LR pairs) onto time-course single-cell expression data and retains co-varying LR pairs by computing Pearson correlation coefficients on pseudotime-ordered series with a |PCC| >= 0.1 cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Maps curated ligand-receptor database pairs (e.g. the CellTalkDB-derived Mouse-2020-Shao-LR-pairs.txt, 2034 mouse LR pairs) onto time-course single-cell expression data and retains co-varying LR pairs by computing Pearson correlation coefficients on pseudotime-ordered series with a |PCC| >= 0.1 cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no temporal/trajectory ordering — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for communication between given cell types and would be more appropriate for static cell-type comparisons Goal is to call active (not merely co-varying) LR pairs — the |PCC| = 0.1 filter is only the first screen; candidate eLR and active LR require Granger causality (p < 0.01) and SCC_ens > 0.8 or < -0.8 Interest is in maternal-embryo or EV-mediated communication — the TimeTalk autocrine/eLR screening assumption precludes maternal-embryo interactions and other non-LR-mediated communication types

skills.description: Use when scMDC (or a similar pretrained deep clustering model) has produced cluster assignments on single-cell multi-omics data and you need per-cluster marker genes or pathway-level enrichment from a directed gene rank.
skills.name: lrp-based-differential-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: lrp-based-differential-gene-ranking Use when scMDC (or a similar pretrained deep clustering model) has produced cluster assignments on single-cell multi-omics data and you need per-cluster marker genes or pathway-level enrichment from a directed gene rank. skills.summary: Evaluates how added noise in test expression data (proxying shallower sequencing depth) degrades CLOUDe's classification power between 'Redundant' and 'Unique' classes, comparing NN, XGB, RF, and SVM architectures across four noise SD scenarios (0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1).

skills.search_text: machine-learning-prediction-pipeline-execution Use when a BAM file from PacBio long-read RNA-seq must be converted into predicted dsRNA regions with per-region probabilities, or when reproducing feature-importance (Skip_ratio 75.4%, Len_skip 15.9%) and cv_scores from the AD-trained model. You already have dsRID_whole.tsv or a dsRID feature table and only need model scoring — in that case run model_predict.py directly rather than re-running the dsRID.sh training process. Your input is short-read RNA-seq rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM data, since dsRID is designed to leverage long-read sequencing. You need calibrated per-base dsRNA annotations rather than region-level predicted probabilities from the random-forest model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Executes the dsRID machine-learning prediction pipeline, which trains a random-forest model on PacBio long-read RNA-seq-derived dsRNA features and applies it to score candidate dsRNA regions genome-wide, yielding feature importance and cross-validation outputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad649
skills.summary: Executes the dsRID machine-learning prediction pipeline, which trains a random-forest model on PacBio long-read RNA-seq-derived dsRNA features and applies it to score candidate dsRNA regions genome-wide, yielding feature importance and cross-validation outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have dsRID_whole.tsv or a dsRID feature table and only need model scoring — in that case run model_predict.py directly rather than re-running the dsRID.sh training process. Your input is short-read RNA-seq rather than PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM data, since dsRID is designed to leverage long-read sequencing. You need calibrated per-base dsRNA annotations rather than region-level predicted probabilities from the random-forest model.

skills.description: Use when expression data for deletion events (3m-column absolute log10(x+1) format) is available and per-event continuous evolutionary parameters must be estimated and compared across multiple machine learning regressors rather than classified.
skills.name: machine-learning-regression-across-architectures
skills.search_text: machine-learning-regression-across-architectures Use when expression data for deletion events (3m-column absolute log10(x+1) format) is available and per-event continuous evolutionary parameters must be estimated and compared across multiple machine learning regressors rather than classified. The goal is classifying deleted genes as 'redundant' vs 'unique' rather than estimating continuous parameters — use the CLOUDeClassify* functions instead. The input is not expression data for deletion events in the 3m-column derived/survived/lost gene format (e.g. raw count matrices or unrelated omics features). Only a single estimator (e.g. the LRT) is required with no cross-architecture comparison of estimation precision. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains four CLOUDe regression architectures (multi-layer neural network, extreme gradient boosting, random forest, support vector machine) to predict the 3m evolutionary parameters theta1, theta2, and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) per deletion event, then compares their estimation accuracy and precision against each other and an LRT-based estimate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Trains four CLOUDe regression architectures (multi-layer neural network, extreme gradient boosting, random forest, support vector machine) to predict the 3m evolutionary parameters theta1, theta2, and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) per deletion event, then compares their estimation accuracy and precision against each other and an LRT-based estimate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classifying deleted genes as 'redundant' vs 'unique' rather than estimating continuous parameters — use the CLOUDeClassify* functions instead. skills.search_text: macro-f1-and-accuracy-evaluation Use when comparing cell-type label-transfer or integration methods on scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative annotation metrics (macro F1, accuracy) plus integration metrics (silhouette, batch entropy) with statistical significance testing. This is the metric framework used to show MASI outperforms SVM, scNym, scArches scANVI, and Symphony across six mixed-batch scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of cell-type annotation and integration methods using macro F1, overall accuracy, cell-type silhouette, and batch entropy mixing, aggregated into annotation, integration, and overall performance scores and compared with paired t-tests. This is the metric framework used to show MASI outperforms SVM, scNym, scArches scANVI, and Symphony across six mixed-batch scRNA-seq datasets.

skills.search_text: macro-f1-class-imbalance-evaluation Use when scoring cell type annotation predictions on heavily class-imbalanced single-cell datasets (e.g. 164 cell types, 22.19M cells) where accuracy would be dominated by abundant types and ontology subtypes should count as correct. skills.search_text: macro-f1-multiclass-classification-evaluation Use when a semi-supervised single-cell label-prediction experiment has trained cell-type classifiers on partially annotated data and you need a balanced metric that weights rare and abundant cell types equally. skills.search_text: macs2-broad-peak-calling Use when the analysis goal is to identify regions of significant read enrichment from BAM-format aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium 3' end-enriched signal) as candidate features, prior to downstream filtering or annotation. The goal is narrow punctate peak detection (e.g. TF binding sites) rather than broad regions of enriched coverage — peaks2utr explicitly calls broad peaks Reads are not 3' end-enriched; the approach favours signal concentrated at UTR distal ends such as 10x Chromium runs Downstream UTR designation is already done — this stage produces raw candidate regions only, with no gene-search or UTR annotation applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calls broad 'peaks' of significant read coverage in an aligned BAM file using MACS (MACS3 from PyPI), producing per-strand broadPeak intervals that peaks2utr uses as candidate regions for annotating novel 3' UTRs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Calls broad 'peaks' of significant read coverage in an aligned BAM file using MACS (MACS3 from PyPI), producing per-strand broadPeak intervals that peaks2utr uses as candidate regions for annotating novel 3' UTRs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is narrow punctate peak detection (e.g. TF binding sites) rather than broad regions of enriched coverage — peaks2utr explicitly calls broad peaks Reads are not 3' end-enriched; the approach favours signal concentrated at UTR distal ends such as 10x Chromium runs Downstream UTR designation is already done — this stage produces raw candidate regions only, with no gene-search or UTR annotation applied

skills.search_text: macs3-peak-calling-qvalue-thresholding Use when constructing a trustworthy feature space (peaks and non-peaks) from a scATAC-seq BAM file, or when peaks of differing confidence are needed for count-matrix construction or simulator training. When the goal is scRNA-seq feature definition — this skill applies only to ATAC-seq open-chromatin peaks; scRNA-seq uses gene/inter-gene features via Utility.scRNA_CreateFeatureSets instead. When only a single peak confidence level is needed and the paired stringent/relaxed complement design is not required — a single MACS3 call at one threshold suffices. When input is already a peak BED or feature table — peak calling has already been done; proceed directly to count matrix construction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Call scATAC-seq peaks with MACS3 at two q-value thresholds — 0.01 for trustworthy peaks and 0.1 for the relaxed set whose complement defines trustworthy non-peaks — as done in the scReadSim sci-ATAC-seq benchmarking workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Call scATAC-seq peaks with MACS3 at two q-value thresholds — 0.01 for trustworthy peaks and 0.1 for the relaxed set whose complement defines trustworthy non-peaks — as done in the scReadSim sci-ATAC-seq benchmarking workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is scRNA-seq feature definition — this skill applies only to ATAC-seq open-chromatin peaks; scRNA-seq uses gene/inter-gene features via Utility.scRNA_CreateFeatureSets instead. When only a single peak confidence level is needed and the paired stringent/relaxed complement design is not required — a single MACS3 call at one threshold suffices. When input is already a peak BED or feature table — peak calling has already been done; proceed directly to count matrix construction.

skills.description: Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq reference datasets sequenced on different platforms and batch effects must be removed before training a cell-type annotation model or fine-tuning on query data.
skills.name: mada-domain-adaptation-pretraining
skills.search_text: mada-domain-adaptation-pretraining Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq reference datasets sequenced on different platforms and batch effects must be removed before training a cell-type annotation model or fine-tuning on query data. Query data is from a disease context — the fine-tuning step is removed in disease mode ('--disease') since disease expression profiles deviate substantially from normal references Reference consists of a single dataset with no batch/platform structure to remove — MADA domain adaptation needs multiple domains Input is raw unprocessed counts without normalization and gene-symbol conversion to hg38 via 'selina preprocess' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pre-train SELINA's multi-adversarial domain adaptation (MADA) network on a merged multi-dataset reference (e.g., five liver datasets) so the feature extractor and cell-type discriminator remove platform batch effects, evaluated with LISI scores before label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Pre-train SELINA's multi-adversarial domain adaptation (MADA) network on a merged multi-dataset reference (e.g., five liver datasets) so the feature extractor and cell-type discriminator remove platform batch effects, evaluated with LISI scores before label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data is from a disease context — the fine-tuning step is removed in disease mode ('--disease') since disease expression profiles deviate substantially from normal references Reference consists of a single dataset with no batch/platform structure to remove — MADA domain adaptation needs multiple domains Input is raw unprocessed counts without normalization and gene-symbol conversion to hg38 via 'selina preprocess'

skills.description: Use when you have simulated technical dropouts (e.g., UMIs of marker genes subsampled to 50/100/200 counts) plus un-subsampled ground-truth expression, and you need to quantify and compare how well correction methods (e.g., SpatialScope vs Tangram) recover the true spatial expression profiles.
skills.name: mae-pcc-correction-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: mae-pcc-correction-accuracy-evaluation Use when you have simulated technical dropouts (e.g., UMIs of marker genes subsampled to 50/100/200 counts) plus un-subsampled ground-truth expression, and you need to quantify and compare how well correction methods (e.g., SpatialScope vs Tangram) recover the true spatial expression profiles. There is no ground-truth (un-subsampled) expression reference — MAE and PCC cannot be computed without true values The goal is deconvolving cell-type proportions per spot (use RCTD/Cell2location/CARD) rather than evaluating gene-expression recovery accuracy Data are already measured at single-cell resolution with a predefined panel (e.g., MERFISH); no dropout-correction benchmark on seq-based ST data is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks dropout-correction / gene-expression-imputation performance by computing mean absolute error (MAE) and Pearson's correlation (PCC) of corrected versus ground-truth expression across simulated subsampling settings, as done to compare SpatialScope against Tangram on Slide-seq V2 cerebellum data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks dropout-correction / gene-expression-imputation performance by computing mean absolute error (MAE) and Pearson's correlation (PCC) of corrected versus ground-truth expression across simulated subsampling settings, as done to compare SpatialScope against Tangram on Slide-seq V2 cerebellum data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no ground-truth (un-subsampled) expression reference — MAE and PCC cannot be computed without true values The goal is deconvolving cell-type proportions per spot (use RCTD/Cell2location/CARD) rather than evaluating gene-expression recovery accuracy Data are already measured at single-cell resolution with a predefined panel (e.g., MERFISH); no dropout-correction benchmark on seq-based ST data is needed

skills.description: Use when mutation information is provided as a standard .maf file (e.g., TCGA LUAD) and you need per-gene mutation significance between groups (p-value, FDR) or mutation visualization such as forest plots and oncoplots.
skills.name: maf-file-processing-with-maftools
skills.search_text: maf-file-processing-with-maftools Use when mutation information is provided as a standard .maf file (e.g., TCGA LUAD) and you need per-gene mutation significance between groups (p-value, FDR) or mutation visualization such as forest plots and oncoplots. Mutation data is not in standard .maf format — ARMT explicitly requires 'standard .maf file like the mutation annotation format file in TCGA' The goal is differential gene expression or GSVA score analysis rather than somatic mutation analysis (use the differential analysis of gene expression or GSVA instead) Samples cannot be integrated across clinical, GSVA, TPM and mutation data through common samples http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Process and visualize somatic mutation data in standard .maf format (e.g., TCGA mutation annotation files) through maftools as integrated into ARMT, supporting mutation summary plots, oncoplots, and differential gene mutation analysis between sample groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Process and visualize somatic mutation data in standard .maf format (e.g., TCGA mutation annotation files) through maftools as integrated into ARMT, supporting mutation summary plots, oncoplots, and differential gene mutation analysis between sample groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mutation data is not in standard .maf format — ARMT explicitly requires 'standard .maf file like the mutation annotation format file in TCGA' The goal is differential gene expression or GSVA score analysis rather than somatic mutation analysis (use the differential analysis of gene expression or GSVA instead) Samples cannot be integrated across clinical, GSVA, TPM and mutation data through common samples

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics count matrices contain dropout artifacts and must be smoothed prior to GAN-based cross-domain alignment or clustering pipelines.

skills.search_text: magic-dropout-correction-preprocessing Use when raw scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics count matrices contain dropout artifacts and must be smoothed prior to GAN-based cross-domain alignment or clustering pipelines. Data is already imputed or the analysis does not rely on diffusion-geometry preservation (e.g., downstream methods sensitive to over-smoothed expression) Input is already a PCA-reduced feature table or a pre-aligned embedding rather than a gene-by-cell count matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies MAGIC manifold smoothing to correct dropout in single-cell datasets (e.g., MDA-MB-231 xenograft scRNA-seq and TNBC spatial transcriptomics) before zero-centering, unit scaling, 50-component PCA reduction, and downstream scMMGAN alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Applies MAGIC manifold smoothing to correct dropout in single-cell datasets (e.g., MDA-MB-231 xenograft scRNA-seq and TNBC spatial transcriptomics) before zero-centering, unit scaling, 50-component PCA reduction, and downstream scMMGAN alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already imputed or the analysis does not rely on diffusion-geometry preservation (e.g., downstream methods sensitive to over-smoothed expression) Input is already a PCA-reduced feature table or a pre-aligned embedding rather than a gene-by-cell count matrix

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix fed into the scDrug pipeline is too sparse/noisy for reliable clustering and the analyst opts into imputation via the --impute flag; default behavior is no imputation.
skills.name: magic-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: magic-missing-value-imputation Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix fed into the scDrug pipeline is too sparse/noisy for reliable clustering and the analyst opts into imputation via the --impute flag; default behavior is no imputation. When the count matrix is dense enough for the 20-PC neighborhood graph — the scDrug default is 'do imputation. default: no', so imputation should not be applied reflexively When the goal is only drug response prediction from an already-clustered scanpyobj.h5ad (drug_response_prediction.py takes the h5ad directly) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Optional MAGIC-based imputation step inside the scDrug Single-Cell Data Analysis module, which fills missing values in scRNA-seq count matrices (10x mtx or CSV input) after Scanpy preprocessing so downstream PCA, Harmony correction, and Louvain clustering operate on a denser expression object. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Optional MAGIC-based imputation step inside the scDrug Single-Cell Data Analysis module, which fills missing values in scRNA-seq count matrices (10x mtx or CSV input) after Scanpy preprocessing so downstream PCA, Harmony correction, and Louvain clustering operate on a denser expression object.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the count matrix is dense enough for the 20-PC neighborhood graph — the scDrug default is 'do imputation. default: no', so imputation should not be applied reflexively When the goal is only drug response prediction from an already-clustered scanpyobj.h5ad (drug_response_prediction.py takes the h5ad directly)

skills.description: Use when a marker-count-based annotation leaves cells 'unassigned' by a rejection threshold, and you want to recover labels by exploiting clustering structure (PCA + GMM clusters) with within-cluster expression similarity.
skills.name: mahalanobis-distance-cluster-reassignment
skills.search_text: mahalanobis-distance-cluster-reassignment Use when a marker-count-based annotation leaves cells 'unassigned' by a rejection threshold, and you want to recover labels by exploiting clustering structure (PCA + GMM clusters) with within-cluster expression similarity. Clusters where 80% or more of cells are unassigned — reassignment is deliberately not applied there, since the cluster likely represents an unknown cell type Input lacks a prior marker-count assignment with rejection thresholds tm, so there is no 'unassigned' population to reassign Cell populations are poorly clustered (MarkerCount's discussion notes each population should be well clustered for proper identification) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 MarkerCount's cluster-basis reassignment step: after a conservative marker-count rejection leaves cells 'unassigned', unassigned cells inside well-populated clusters are relabeled using weighted Mahalanobis distances to the centroids of partially occupying cell types, minimizing unnecessarily unassigned cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: MarkerCount's cluster-basis reassignment step: after a conservative marker-count rejection leaves cells 'unassigned', unassigned cells inside well-populated clusters are relabeled using weighted Mahalanobis distances to the centroids of partially occupying cell types, minimizing unnecessarily unassigned cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters where 80% or more of cells are unassigned — reassignment is deliberately not applied there, since the cluster likely represents an unknown cell type Input lacks a prior marker-count assignment with rejection thresholds tm, so there is no 'unassigned' population to reassign Cell populations are poorly clustered (MarkerCount's discussion notes each population should be well clustered for proper identification)

skills.description: Use when a Symphony-mapped query may contain cell types missing from the reference and you need quantitative per-cell or per-cluster scores (with AUC evaluation) to flag unmapped/novel populations.
skills.name: mahalanobis-distance-mapping-metrics
skills.search_text: mahalanobis-distance-mapping-metrics Use when a Symphony-mapped query may contain cell types missing from the reference and you need quantitative per-cell or per-cluster scores (with AUC evaluation) to flag unmapped/novel populations. When the novel query population is expected to be very similar to an existing reference population — the article notes these metrics may be less informative in that case When the goal is de novo cell type discovery from the query alone rather than flagging cells that failed to map to a reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Uses Symphony's per-cell and per-cluster Mahalanobis-distance-based mapping metrics to flag query cell types that are absent from the reference, quantifying detection performance as AUC for held-out cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Uses Symphony's per-cell and per-cluster Mahalanobis-distance-based mapping metrics to flag query cell types that are absent from the reference, quantifying detection performance as AUC for held-out cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the novel query population is expected to be very similar to an existing reference population — the article notes these metrics may be less informative in that case When the goal is de novo cell type discovery from the query alone rather than flagging cells that failed to map to a reference

skills.description: Use when you have cell-to-cluster assignments plus a low-dimensional SingleCellExperiment embedding and need between-cluster distances that account for within-cluster covariance, to build an MST cluster topology.
skills.name: mahalanobis-like-between-cluster-distance-computation
skills.search_text: mahalanobis-like-between-cluster-distance-computation Use when you have cell-to-cluster assignments plus a low-dimensional SingleCellExperiment embedding and need between-cluster distances that account for within-cluster covariance, to build an MST cluster topology. The clustering contains clusters smaller than the min.cluster.size threshold (default 5 cells) — such clusterings are filtered out before MST construction because covariance estimates on tiny clusters are unreliable You need trajectories with cycles or disconnected components — Totem's MST backbone cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The embedding is high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components) where k-medoids clustering itself is unstable, producing 1-2 cell clusters that make between-cluster distance/MST construction meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes pairwise distances between cluster centroids in a low-dimensional cell embedding using Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like distance, which accounts for the shape and spread of cells within each cluster, and uses these distances to construct a minimum spanning tree (MST) over cluster vertices — the backbone of Totem's topology estimation for each clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Computes pairwise distances between cluster centroids in a low-dimensional cell embedding using Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like distance, which accounts for the shape and spread of cells within each cluster, and uses these distances to construct a minimum spanning tree (MST) over cluster vertices — the backbone of Totem's topology estimation for each clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering contains clusters smaller than the min.cluster.size threshold (default 5 cells) — such clusterings are filtered out before MST construction because covariance estimates on tiny clusters are unreliable You need trajectories with cycles or disconnected components — Totem's MST backbone cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The embedding is high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components) where k-medoids clustering itself is unstable, producing 1-2 cell clusters that make between-cluster distance/MST construction meaningless

skills.description: Use when visualizing consensus clustering results on a CITE-seq embedding to highlight a specific minor cell population (e.g. MAIT-NKT cells) and reproduce the paper's Figure 3 / Supplementary Fig. S3.
skills.name: mait-nkt-cell-population-visualization
skills.search_text: mait-nkt-cell-population-visualization Use when visualizing consensus clustering results on a CITE-seq embedding to highlight a specific minor cell population (e.g. MAIT-NKT cells) and reproduce the paper's Figure 3 / Supplementary Fig. S3. The input is single-modality scRNA-seq with no second data modality, since SnapCCESS integrates multiple modalities of the same cells (e.g. RNA + ADT from CITE-seq) You need ready-made best hyperparameters for a new dataset — the tutorial only explains package usage and states it 'doesn't recommend the best parameters for your datasets'; those are in the paper The goal is supervised cell-type classification rather than unsupervised consensus clustering and embedding visualization http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Reproduce the Ramaswamy CITE-seq consensus-clustering embedding visualization from SnapCCESS (Figure 3 and Supplementary Fig. S3) by highlighting the MAIT-NKT cell population identified via ensemble clustering of multimodal RNA/ADT embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Reproduce the Ramaswamy CITE-seq consensus-clustering embedding visualization from SnapCCESS (Figure 3 and Supplementary Fig. S3) by highlighting the MAIT-NKT cell population identified via ensemble clustering of multimodal RNA/ADT embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-modality scRNA-seq with no second data modality, since SnapCCESS integrates multiple modalities of the same cells (e.g. RNA + ADT from CITE-seq) You need ready-made best hyperparameters for a new dataset — the tutorial only explains package usage and states it 'doesn't recommend the best parameters for your datasets'; those are in the paper The goal is supervised cell-type classification rather than unsupervised consensus clustering and embedding visualization

skills.search_text: major-minor-cell-type-label-splitting Use when benchmarking a single-cell clustering method against curated cell-type annotations and you need to assess performance at both coarse (major) and fine-grained (minor) label granularity, e.g. resolving rare populations like MAIT-NKT cells. The dataset has only a single flat annotation level with no coarse/fine hierarchy to split The goal is clustering itself rather than evaluating clustering quality against reference labels Labels are continuous scores or predicted probabilities rather than discrete categorical cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Splits each dataset's cell-type annotations into two hierarchical label sets — coarse major cell types and fine-grained minor cell types — so clustering performance can be evaluated separately at both resolutions, as done in the SnapCCESS evaluation on six multimodal single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Splits each dataset's cell-type annotations into two hierarchical label sets — coarse major cell types and fine-grained minor cell types — so clustering performance can be evaluated separately at both resolutions, as done in the SnapCCESS evaluation on six multimodal single-cell datasets.

skills.description: Use when a single cell must be labeled malignant vs non-malignant from scRNA-seq expression and multiple base classifiers (one per training dataset) have produced per-cell predictions that need to be combined into a final consensus label.
skills.name: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation
skills.search_text: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation Use when a single cell must be labeled malignant vs non-malignant from scRNA-seq expression and multiple base classifiers (one per training dataset) have produced per-cell predictions that need to be combined into a final consensus label. The goal is annotating subpopulations of non-cancer cells (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to cancer vs non-cancer annotation only Only a single training dataset or single base classifier is available, so no vote aggregation is possible Input expression values have not been normalized (e.g. raw counts); PreCanCell_data() expects any library-depth-normalized matrix (TPM, CPM) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Aggregates the outputs of five k-NN (k=5) base classifiers — one trained per cancer scRNA-seq training dataset (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) on the common DEG features — into a single malignant/non-malignant call per cell via majority vote, as implemented in PreCanCell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Aggregates the outputs of five k-NN (k=5) base classifiers — one trained per cancer scRNA-seq training dataset (RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) on the common DEG features — into a single malignant/non-malignant call per cell via majority vote, as implemented in PreCanCell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating subpopulations of non-cancer cells (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to cancer vs non-cancer annotation only Only a single training dataset or single base classifier is available, so no vote aggregation is possible Input expression values have not been normalized (e.g. raw counts); PreCanCell_data() expects any library-depth-normalized matrix (TPM, CPM)

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell classification predictions across a sample and need a single sample-level call (e.g. predicted primary origin of a metastatic biopsy) from the majority cancer-cell annotation.
skills.name: majority-vote-sample-level-label-aggregation
skills.search_text: majority-vote-sample-level-label-aggregation Use when you have per-cell classification predictions across a sample and need a single sample-level call (e.g. predicted primary origin of a metastatic biopsy) from the majority cancer-cell annotation. Samples expected to be normal/non-cancerous tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes presence of at least some cancer cells and should not be used on normal tissue Cases where a per-cell heterogeneous mixture must be preserved (e.g. TME composition analysis) rather than collapsed to a single sample-level label When the cancer type is already known — create_summary_matrix() has a known_cancer_type parameter instead of majority-vote inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derives a sample-level label by taking the majority annotation among cells classified as a class of interest (e.g. cancer cells) after running a per-cell classifier like scATOMIC, used to predict the primary tissue of origin of each metastatic biopsy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Derives a sample-level label by taking the majority annotation among cells classified as a class of interest (e.g. cancer cells) after running a per-cell classifier like scATOMIC, used to predict the primary tissue of origin of each metastatic biopsy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples expected to be normal/non-cancerous tissue — the default scATOMIC model assumes presence of at least some cancer cells and should not be used on normal tissue Cases where a per-cell heterogeneous mixture must be preserved (e.g. TME composition analysis) rather than collapsed to a single sample-level label When the cancer type is already known — create_summary_matrix() has a known_cancer_type parameter instead of majority-vote inference

skills.description: Use when you have staged scRNA-seq expression matrices (.h5ad) from a cancerous epithelial lineage and want to test whether predicted malignancy increases with progression stage, rather than performing a one-off malignant/normal classification.

skills.search_text: malignancy-probability-interpretation Use when you have staged scRNA-seq expression matrices (.h5ad) from a cancerous epithelial lineage and want to test whether predicted malignancy increases with progression stage, rather than performing a one-off malignant/normal classification. The input is a cancer type with unknown or controversial cellular origin (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the classifier's capabilities are untested The dataset lacks prerequisite basic cell-type annotation or you need to classify non-epithelial lineages, since the method identifies malignant cells only from cancerous lineages The goal is de novo malignant-cell discovery without any stage/condition contrast — a single binary classification run suffices and per-stage trend interpretation adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets scMalignantFinder's malignancy_probability output and Normal/Malignant predictions to quantify how the malignant fraction of epithelial cells changes across carcinogenesis stages (e.g., normal mucosa → CAG/IM → gastric cancer, or normal mucosa → polyp → colorectal tumor), using probability as a dynamic readout of tumor progression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a cancer type with unknown or controversial cellular origin (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the classifier's capabilities are untested The dataset lacks prerequisite basic cell-type annotation or you need to classify non-epithelial lineages, since the method identifies malignant cells only from cancerous lineages The goal is de novo malignant-cell discovery without any stage/condition contrast — a single binary classification run suffices and per-stage trend interpretation adds no value

skills.description: Use when computing per-cell gene signature scores from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (sparse matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or Seurat object) via rank-based Mann-Whitney U statistics, or when reimplementing/porting UCell's scoring mechanism.

skills.search_text: mann-whitney-u-statistic-computation Use when computing per-cell gene signature scores from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (sparse matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or Seurat object) via rank-based Mann-Whitney U statistics, or when reimplementing/porting UCell's scoring mechanism. You need scores that depend on dataset-wide normalization — UCell ranks are purely per-cell relative expression, unlike Seurat's AddModuleScore, which bins genes by average expression across the whole dataset and yields composition-dependent results. You want to compare absolute expression levels of genes across cells rather than within-cell relative ordering. Your reference UCell version differs in normalization (pre- vs post-2.7.6 U_max definition) — mixing the two normalizations will produce systematically offset scores for large gene sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reconstructs UCell's rank-based gene signature scoring: per-cell gene ranks are capped at maxRank (default 1500), the Mann-Whitney U statistic is computed from signature-gene rank sums, and the score is normalized to [0,1]. This enables faithful reimplementation or cross-validation of UCell scoring (data_to_ranks + u_stat) in R or Python (pyUCell). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: Reconstructs UCell's rank-based gene signature scoring: per-cell gene ranks are capped at maxRank (default 1500), the Mann-Whitney U statistic is computed from signature-gene rank sums, and the score is normalized to [0,1]. This enables faithful reimplementation or cross-validation of UCell scoring (data_to_ranks + u_stat) in R or Python (pyUCell).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need scores that depend on dataset-wide normalization — UCell ranks are purely per-cell relative expression, unlike Seurat's AddModuleScore, which bins genes by average expression across the whole dataset and yields composition-dependent results. You want to compare absolute expression levels of genes across cells rather than within-cell relative ordering. Your reference UCell version differs in normalization (pre- vs post-2.7.6 U_max definition) — mixing the two normalizations will produce systematically offset scores for large gene sets.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count data (log normalization with L=1, gene scaling, L2 normalization) and needing a data-driven signal/noise threshold from the eigenvalue spectrum of the cell similarity matrix, without subjective dimension selection.

skills.search_text: marchenko-pastur-distribution-fitting Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count data (log normalization with L=1, gene scaling, L2 normalization) and needing a data-driven signal/noise threshold from the eigenvalue spectrum of the cell similarity matrix, without subjective dimension selection. Input is a similarity matrix whose dimensions do not match the random-matrix regime assumptions (e.g. extremely few cells relative to genes may destabilize the MP fit) The user has already fixed signal dimensions subjectively or uses a tool requiring manual threshold input — RMT filtering exists precisely to avoid such user discretion Data have not been L2-normalized after log normalization: log normalization alone on TGC-biased sparse matrices produces ~400 artificial signals that would be falsely passed downstream http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 RMT-based noise filtering for single-cell similarity matrices: eigenvalues of G = XX^T/N that conform to the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) distribution are classified as noise, while eigenvalues deviating from MP and surpassing a Tracy-Widom (TW) threshold (0.05 probability cutoff) are retained as biological signals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: RMT-based noise filtering for single-cell similarity matrices: eigenvalues of G = XX^T/N that conform to the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) distribution are classified as noise, while eigenvalues deviating from MP and surpassing a Tracy-Widom (TW) threshold (0.05 probability cutoff) are retained as biological signals.

skills.description: Use when you need a biologically realistic null expectation for embedding quality (EMBEDR p-values) from single-cell omics data such as Tabula Muris scRNA-seq, before fitting data and null embeddings with a DRA like t-SNE or UMAP.
skills.name: marginal-resampling-null-embedding
skills.search_text: marginal-resampling-null-embedding Use when you need a biologically realistic null expectation for embedding quality (EMBEDR p-values) from single-cell omics data such as Tabula Muris scRNA-seq, before fitting data and null embeddings with a DRA like t-SNE or UMAP. The dataset is non-normalized — the article states EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets The analysis requires preserving inter-gene (joint/correlation) structure in the null — marginal resampling deliberately destroys it You need parametric or theoretical null distributions — the article notes no theoretical description of the null tails or principled parameterization exists Generates data-driven null datasets for EMBEDR by marginal resampling — each gene's expression values are independently drawn with replacement from that gene's empirical distribution — preserving per-gene marginals while destroying inter-gene correlations, so embedding quality can be hypothesis-tested against signal-less data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Generates data-driven null datasets for EMBEDR by marginal resampling — each gene's expression values are independently drawn with replacement from that gene's empirical distribution — preserving per-gene marginals while destroying inter-gene correlations, so embedding quality can be hypothesis-tested against signal-less data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is non-normalized — the article states EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets The analysis requires preserving inter-gene (joint/correlation) structure in the null — marginal resampling deliberately destroys it You need parametric or theoretical null distributions — the article notes no theoretical description of the null tails or principled parameterization exists

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix and a marker gene list (gene, cluster, optional fold-change weight) per cell type, but no scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference profile to decompose cell-type composition trends.
skills.name: marker-based-bulk-decomposition
skills.search_text: marker-based-bulk-decomposition Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix and a marker gene list (gene, cluster, optional fold-change weight) per cell type, but no scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference profile to decompose cell-type composition trends. A snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference profile with matched cell type and individual labels IS available — use reference-based decomposition (BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition) instead, which learns gene-specific transformations and yields more accurate estimates You need absolute cell-type proportions comparable across cell types — BisqueMarker estimates relative differences in abundance across individuals only, not proportions Bulk and single-cell data come from different tissues, violating the same-tissue assumption of decomposition http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 BisqueMarker (BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition) is the semi-supervised mode of Bisque that extracts relative cell-type abundance trends from normalized bulk RNA-seq expression using only cell-specific marker genes, for cases where no single-cell reference profile is available. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: BisqueMarker (BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition) is the semi-supervised mode of Bisque that extracts relative cell-type abundance trends from normalized bulk RNA-seq expression using only cell-specific marker genes, for cases where no single-cell reference profile is available.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference profile with matched cell type and individual labels IS available — use reference-based decomposition (BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition) instead, which learns gene-specific transformations and yields more accurate estimates You need absolute cell-type proportions comparable across cell types — BisqueMarker estimates relative differences in abundance across individuals only, not proportions Bulk and single-cell data come from different tissues, violating the same-tissue assumption of decomposition

skills.name: marker-based-cell-type-abundance-estimation
skills.search_text: marker-based-cell-type-abundance-estimation Use when bulk RNA-seq samples need cell-type proportion/abundance estimates but no matched scRNA/snRNA-seq reference exists, and a validated marker gene list for the tissue's cell types is available. A matched single-cell/snRNA-seq reference with overlapping individuals is available — use Bisque's reference-based decomposition instead, which was the only method yielding the significant microglia–Braak association (p = 0.001) The goal is absolute cell proportions that can be compared across different cell types — marker-based estimates are relative abundances within a cell type and cannot be compared between cell types No validated cell-type marker genes exist for the tissue http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Estimate cell-type abundance in bulk RNA-seq with BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition when a matched single-cell reference profile is unavailable, using only a set of known cell-type-specific marker genes to extract relative abundance trends across individuals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Estimate cell-type abundance in bulk RNA-seq with BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition when a matched single-cell reference profile is unavailable, using only a set of known cell-type-specific marker genes to extract relative abundance trends across individuals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A matched single-cell/snRNA-seq reference with overlapping individuals is available — use Bisque's reference-based decomposition instead, which was the only method yielding the significant microglia–Braak association (p = 0.001) The goal is absolute cell proportions that can be compared across different cell types — marker-based estimates are relative abundances within a cell type and cannot be compared between cell types No validated cell-type marker genes exist for the tissue

skills.description: Use when annotating a scRNA-seq count matrix from a marker gene list — top 5 or 15 genes per cell type derived with Seurat, or canonical markers from PanglaoDB/CellMarker/CancerSEA — and no labeled training expression matrix is used.
skills.name: marker-based-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: marker-based-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating a scRNA-seq count matrix from a marker gene list — top 5 or 15 genes per cell type derived with Seurat, or canonical markers from PanglaoDB/CellMarker/CancerSEA — and no labeled training expression matrix is used. Only a labeled training expression matrix plus testing matrix is available — the eagersupervised/lazysupervised wrappers (e.g. Seurat, SingleR, CELLBLAST) consume train/test expression data, whereas markersupervised consumes marker lists instead of expression matrices. No marker list exists and none can be derived (no labels for Seurat FindAllMarkers, no canonical/resource markers) — marker-learning wrappers cannot train from expression alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assigns cell types to scRNA-seq cells from per-cell-type marker gene lists rather than labeled training expression matrices, using the markersupervised wrapper (scTyper, Markercount, SCSA, DigitalCellSorter, SCINA) of the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package or MarkerCount's marker-based mode. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Assigns cell types to scRNA-seq cells from per-cell-type marker gene lists rather than labeled training expression matrices, using the markersupervised wrapper (scTyper, Markercount, SCSA, DigitalCellSorter, SCINA) of the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package or MarkerCount's marker-based mode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a labeled training expression matrix plus testing matrix is available — the eagersupervised/lazysupervised wrappers (e.g. Seurat, SingleR, CELLBLAST) consume train/test expression data, whereas markersupervised consumes marker lists instead of expression matrices. No marker list exists and none can be derived (no labels for Seurat FindAllMarkers, no canonical/resource markers) — marker-learning wrappers cannot train from expression alone.

skills.description: Use when you have a log-normalized Seurat object of single-cell (snRNA-seq/RNA-seq) expression, a YAML marker file, and need a balanced subsample of cell IDs for manual or classifier labeling.

No prior marker knowledge is available — use mode = 'cluster_based' instead, sampling equal cells per Seurat cluster The goal is differential expression or cell-type discovery rather than creating a balanced labeled training subsample Cells lack unique cell IDs in the meta.data slot, since IDs are what LEADER outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Marker-informed adaptive reweighting (LEADER): assign each cluster of single-cell expression data a putative cell type by comparing average positive vs negative marker gene expression, then sample cells equally per putative type to build a balanced labeled training set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Marker-informed adaptive reweighting (LEADER): assign each cluster of single-cell expression data a putative cell type by comparing average positive vs negative marker gene expression, then sample cells equally per putative type to build a balanced labeled training set.

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq cohort needs cell-type proportion estimates but no matched single-cell reference profile exists and only cell-specific marker genes (with weights such as avg_logFC) are available.

skills.when_to_use_negative: A matched single-cell/snRNA-seq reference profile is available for the same tissue — use reference-based decomposition (ReferenceBasedDecomposition) instead, which is more accurate with snRNA-seq data Absolute proportions comparable across cell types are required — BisqueMarker estimates relative abundance differences that cannot be compared between cell types The bulk and single-cell data come from different tissues — the README assumes single-cell and bulk counts are measured from the same tissue

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that MAPiT-transformed distance profiles of flow cytometry markers (e.g. DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) are robust to which markers are fed to the pseudotime algorithm, or when validating pseudotime-derived spatial arrangements against microscopy cross-sections.
skills.name: marker-distance-profile-comparison
skills.search_text: marker-distance-profile-comparison Use when you need to verify that MAPiT-transformed distance profiles of flow cytometry markers (e.g. DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) are robust to which markers are fed to the pseudotime algorithm, or when validating pseudotime-derived spatial arrangements against microscopy cross-sections. The target true-scale distribution cannot be derived or measured — e.g. stem cell differentiation processes where cell death and division rates at every stage are unknown The pseudotemporal cell order is not trustworthy, since MAPiT is reliant on the correctness of the provided cell order from the trajectory inference algorithm The data are already spatially resolved (e.g. imaging cross-sections); profiles can be compared directly without a pseudotime-to-space transformation http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Validates MAPiT's spatial reconstruction of spheroid marker profiles by comparing distance-from-surface profiles across leave-one-out marker subsets (Wanderlust/DPT pseudotime inputs) against full-marker-set profiles and microscopically quantified Ki-67 spheroid cross-sections. skills.summary: Validates MAPiT's spatial reconstruction of spheroid marker profiles by comparing distance-from-surface profiles across leave-one-out marker subsets (Wanderlust/DPT pseudotime inputs) against full-marker-set profiles and microscopically quantified Ki-67 spheroid cross-sections. Demonstrates the reconstruction is robust to the choice of markers used as pseudotime-algorithm input.
