skills.description: Use when you have a ranked DEG list from scRNA-seq analysis and need to assess whether top-ranked genes are biologically meaningful by testing enrichment of known cell type marker genes by rank position.
skills.name: marker-enrichment-validation
skills.search_text: marker-enrichment-validation Use when you have a ranked DEG list from scRNA-seq analysis and need to assess whether top-ranked genes are biologically meaningful by testing enrichment of known cell type marker genes by rank position. The input is an unranked gene set or cluster assignment rather than a gene list ordered by statistical significance (e.g. p-value), since the method relies on rank-bin partitioning No cell type marker reference database is available for the organism or tissue under study, so enrichment cannot be computed against a marker gold standard http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates a ranked DEG list (e.g. from singleCellHaystack's haystack function sorted by log.p.vals) by quantifying enrichment of known cell type markers across rank bins, using the CellMarker mouse database stratified by publication count into high- (>=5 publications) and low-confidence (1-4 publications) marker classes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Validates a ranked DEG list (e.g. from singleCellHaystack's haystack function sorted by log.p.vals) by quantifying enrichment of known cell type markers across rank bins, using the CellMarker mouse database stratified by publication count into high- (>=5 publications) and low-confidence (1-4 publications) marker classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is an unranked gene set or cluster assignment rather than a gene list ordered by statistical significance (e.g. p-value), since the method relies on rank-bin partitioning No cell type marker reference database is available for the organism or tissue under study, so enrichment cannot be computed against a marker gold standard

skills.description: Use when building the initial training set for active learning cell type annotation and a marker file (author-provided, data-derived, or PanglaoDB-derived) is available; especially beneficial when few cells will be labeled initially.
skills.name: marker-expression-based-cell-selection
skills.search_text: marker-expression-based-cell-selection Use when building the initial training set for active learning cell type annotation and a marker file (author-provided, data-derived, or PanglaoDB-derived) is available; especially beneficial when few cells will be labeled initially. No prior marker knowledge exists for the expected cell types — the article's adaptive reweighting without markers (cluster-based mode, Seurat clustering with equal per-cluster sampling) is the intended fallback Markers are unreliable or highly circular (e.g. cell line datasets where markers are derived by differential expression between the very cell lines being annotated) The task is balanced subsampling of an already-annotated dataset rather than selecting an initial annotation training set http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the initial labeled training set for active learning single-cell annotation by ranking candidate cells on average marker gene expression per expected cell type (positive and negative markers), rather than random selection, so that more ground-truth cell types are represented in the first 20 labeled cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Selects the initial labeled training set for active learning single-cell annotation by ranking candidate cells on average marker gene expression per expected cell type (positive and negative markers), rather than random selection, so that more ground-truth cell types are represented in the first 20 labeled cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior marker knowledge exists for the expected cell types — the article's adaptive reweighting without markers (cluster-based mode, Seurat clustering with equal per-cluster sampling) is the intended fallback Markers are unreliable or highly circular (e.g. cell line datasets where markers are derived by differential expression between the very cell lines being annotated) The task is balanced subsampling of an already-annotated dataset rather than selecting an initial annotation training set

skills.description: Use when validating a completed integration of CyTOF or similar single-cell datasets: you need to confirm dataset effects are removed by checking that per-marker density curves overlap across datasets while cell-type-specific marker expression is preserved.
skills.name: marker-expression-density-profiling
skills.search_text: marker-expression-density-profiling Use when validating a completed integration of CyTOF or similar single-cell datasets: you need to confirm dataset effects are removed by checking that per-marker density curves overlap across datasets while cell-type-specific marker expression is preserved. Integration has not yet been performed — density profiling of raw, unadjusted CyTOF matrices will show residual dataset effects and cannot validate the integration Datasets lack shared markers or harmonized cell-type annotations, so density curves cannot be meaningfully overlaid per marker or per cell type The goal is quantitative batch-effect metrics (e.g., kBET, LISI) rather than marker-level distributional inspection — use a dedicated metric workflow instead Overlay per-marker expression density distributions across datasets after single-cell integration (e.g., CyTOF integration via scMerge2) to visually and quantitatively confirm that dataset-level unwanted variation has been removed while biological structure is retained. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39923-2
skills.summary: Overlay per-marker expression density distributions across datasets after single-cell integration (e.g., CyTOF integration via scMerge2) to visually and quantitatively confirm that dataset-level unwanted variation has been removed while biological structure is retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Integration has not yet been performed — density profiling of raw, unadjusted CyTOF matrices will show residual dataset effects and cannot validate the integration Datasets lack shared markers or harmonized cell-type annotations, so density curves cannot be meaningfully overlaid per marker or per cell type The goal is quantitative batch-effect metrics (e.g., kBET, LISI) rather than marker-level distributional inspection — use a dedicated metric workflow instead

skills.description: Use when a spatial single-cell dataset (e.g., CODEX-exported .csv with x,y coordinates) has already been unrolled onto a linear structure and you need to visualize marker expression along organ length and wall thickness.
skills.name: marker-expression-overlay-visualization
skills.search_text: marker-expression-overlay-visualization Use when a spatial single-cell dataset (e.g., CODEX-exported .csv with x,y coordinates) has already been unrolled onto a linear structure and you need to visualize marker expression along organ length and wall thickness. Input is raw rolled intestinal tissue imaging data that has not yet been uploaded, ROI-selected, backbone-traced, and unrolled in IntestLine — the overlay requires a completed linear mapping. Data lacks xy-coordinates — IntestLine is suitable only for images providing xy-coordinates (e.g. CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics), not other imaging modalities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 A visualization step in the IntestLine Shiny app that overlays marker expression onto the linearly unrolled intestinal tissue, enabling assessment of location-specific cell types and markers along the proximal–distal and serosa-luminal axes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: A visualization step in the IntestLine Shiny app that overlays marker expression onto the linearly unrolled intestinal tissue, enabling assessment of location-specific cell types and markers along the proximal–distal and serosa-luminal axes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw rolled intestinal tissue imaging data that has not yet been uploaded, ROI-selected, backbone-traced, and unrolled in IntestLine — the overlay requires a completed linear mapping. Data lacks xy-coordinates — IntestLine is suitable only for images providing xy-coordinates (e.g. CODEX or 10x spatial transcriptomics), not other imaging modalities.

skills.description: Use when converting per-cluster differential marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers output with Entrez IDs and scores) into ranked cell-type annotations, where significance-adjusted candidates must be ordered by marker expression significance.
skills.name: marker-expression-score-ranking
skills.search_text: marker-expression-score-ranking Use when converting per-cluster differential marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers output with Entrez IDs and scores) into ranked cell-type annotations, where significance-adjusted candidates must be ordered by marker expression significance. When the marker list has no expression score / ranking information (e.g. only an unranked overlap gene list) — the article warns that ignoring gene ranking leads to unreliable results When a full GSEA-based ranked-test annotation is required instead of the Fisher-test-plus-ranking approach (EasyCellType offers both GSEA and the modified Fisher's exact test) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Rank cell-type candidates for each cluster by the markers' expression score (e.g. log fold change) rather than raw overlap size, so that the top-ranked marker–label associations become the hard (top-1) and soft (top-5) annotation recommendations in EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Rank cell-type candidates for each cluster by the markers' expression score (e.g. log fold change) rather than raw overlap size, so that the top-ranked marker–label associations become the hard (top-1) and soft (top-5) annotation recommendations in EasyCellType's modified Fisher's exact test workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the marker list has no expression score / ranking information (e.g. only an unranked overlap gene list) — the article warns that ignoring gene ranking leads to unreliable results When a full GSEA-based ranked-test annotation is required instead of the Fisher-test-plus-ranking approach (EasyCellType offers both GSEA and the modified Fisher's exact test)

skills.description: Use when you have hybrid cluster assignments from ClonoCluster at multiple α values and need to verify that cluster markers keep equivalent fidelity (median top-marker AUC) versus the α = 0 transcriptome-only baseline.
skills.name: marker-fidelity-roc-analysis
skills.search_text: marker-fidelity-roc-analysis Use when you have hybrid cluster assignments from ClonoCluster at multiple α values and need to verify that cluster markers keep equivalent fidelity (median top-marker AUC) versus the α = 0 transcriptome-only baseline. You only need standard transcriptome-only cluster markers with no clonal barcode data or α comparison — use Seurat/scanpy marker finding directly. Your goal is to identify reorganization markers between paired transcriptome and hybrid clusters (a different analysis computed as *_auc_barcodes.txt), not top-marker AUC fidelity. Cell fate is not barcoded and no clone weight information exists, so hybrid clustering at varying α cannot be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantifies whether top markers of ClonoCluster hybrid clusters retain the sensitivity/specificity (ROC AUC) of transcriptome-only cluster markers as α shifts weight toward clonal origin, using Find_Markers_ROC and ROCR across α = 0 to 1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Quantifies whether top markers of ClonoCluster hybrid clusters retain the sensitivity/specificity (ROC AUC) of transcriptome-only cluster markers as α shifts weight toward clonal origin, using Find_Markers_ROC and ROCR across α = 0 to 1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need standard transcriptome-only cluster markers with no clonal barcode data or α comparison — use Seurat/scanpy marker finding directly. Your goal is to identify reorganization markers between paired transcriptome and hybrid clusters (a different analysis computed as *_auc_barcodes.txt), not top-marker AUC fidelity. Cell fate is not barcoded and no clone weight information exists, so hybrid clustering at varying α cannot be defined.

skills.description: Use when running marker-aware cell selection or active-learning initialization on scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq/CyTOF data and a marker gene set per expected cell type must be sourced, formatted, or validated.
skills.name: marker-file-preparation-panglaodb
skills.search_text: marker-file-preparation-panglaodb Use when running marker-aware cell selection or active-learning initialization on scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq/CyTOF data and a marker gene set per expected cell type must be sourced, formatted, or validated. No prior knowledge of expected cell types exists and no marker resource covers the tissue — cluster-based leader mode or purely random initialization is the appropriate choice instead The downstream tool does not accept the YAML marker structure (positive/negative lists) and reformatted marker tables are not available http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepare cell-type marker gene files (YAML for the leader package or marker tables) from author-provided knowledge, differential expression, or the 20 most sensitive PanglaoDB markers, so that marker-ranked cell selection can be applied to single-cell expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Prepare cell-type marker gene files (YAML for the leader package or marker tables) from author-provided knowledge, differential expression, or the 20 most sensitive PanglaoDB markers, so that marker-ranked cell selection can be applied to single-cell expression data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior knowledge of expected cell types exists and no marker resource covers the tissue — cluster-based leader mode or purely random initialization is the appropriate choice instead The downstream tool does not accept the YAML marker structure (positive/negative lists) and reformatted marker tables are not available

skills.description: Use when the input is per-cell x/y coordinates plus multi-marker intensity values (e.g., MCMICRO output from a CyCIF whole-slide image in an AnnData object) and the analysis goal is to label each cell by marker-defined type (e.g., SOX10+ tumor cells) before spatial/region analyses.
skills.name: marker-gated-cell-phenotyping
skills.search_text: marker-gated-cell-phenotyping Use when the input is per-cell x/y coordinates plus multi-marker intensity values (e.g., MCMICRO output from a CyCIF whole-slide image in an AnnData object) and the analysis goal is to label each cell by marker-defined type (e.g., SOX10+ tumor cells) before spatial/region analyses. Input is spot-level or bulk data rather than per-cell multiplexed imaging intensities — e.g., the Visium lymph node dataset, which the paper deconvolutes with Cell2location before SpatialCells analysis rather than gating single-cell markers The task is spatial region delineation or per-cell region assignment, not phenotype calling — those are handled by getBoundary and assignPointsToRegions, which require already-gated cell-type labels No marker-intensity data are available (e.g., only pre-computed cell labels or morphology-only segmentation), since gating requires raw per-cell intensity values Defines per-cell phenotype labels on multiplexed single-cell data by applying user-specified marker-intensity gates with SpatialCells' setGates/setGate (e.g., calling SOX10+ tumor cells and Ki67+/SOX10+ proliferating cells in 30-marker CyCIF data), giving downstream region-based TME analyses a marker-defined cell-type basis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Defines per-cell phenotype labels on multiplexed single-cell data by applying user-specified marker-intensity gates with SpatialCells' setGates/setGate (e.g., calling SOX10+ tumor cells and Ki67+/SOX10+ proliferating cells in 30-marker CyCIF data), giving downstream region-based TME analyses a marker-defined cell-type basis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spot-level or bulk data rather than per-cell multiplexed imaging intensities — e.g., the Visium lymph node dataset, which the paper deconvolutes with Cell2location before SpatialCells analysis rather than gating single-cell markers The task is spatial region delineation or per-cell region assignment, not phenotype calling — those are handled by getBoundary and assignPointsToRegions, which require already-gated cell-type labels No marker-intensity data are available (e.g., only pre-computed cell labels or morphology-only segmentation), since gating requires raw per-cell intensity values

skills.description: Use when re-clustered scRNA-seq subpopulations must be biologically labeled by signature genes and their purity quantified with a quantitative statistic such as ROGUE before being trusted as subtypes.
skills.name: marker-gene-annotation-of-cell-subclusters
skills.search_text: marker-gene-annotation-of-cell-subclusters Use when re-clustered scRNA-seq subpopulations must be biologically labeled by signature genes and their purity quantified with a quantitative statistic such as ROGUE before being trusted as subtypes. When the goal is to detect rare cell types within a large population rather than verify purity of existing subclusters — GiniClust/GiniClust2 or RaceID3 are designed for rare-type detection, not purity assessment When clusters contain continuously varying trajectories or low-quality data where the fixed 0.9 threshold is inappropriate — the authors note the threshold must be determined from global ROGUE values in such cases When measuring purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the authors state current ROGUE does not yet support this http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotates re-clustered single-cell subpopulations by checking per-cluster marker gene signatures, then verifies each cluster is a pure subtype using the ROGUE entropy statistic. In the ROGUE-guided B-cell analysis, five of seven subclusters passed the ROGUE > 0.92 purity bar while doublet-like and germinal-center clusters failed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Annotates re-clustered single-cell subpopulations by checking per-cluster marker gene signatures, then verifies each cluster is a pure subtype using the ROGUE entropy statistic. In the ROGUE-guided B-cell analysis, five of seven subclusters passed the ROGUE > 0.92 purity bar while doublet-like and germinal-center clusters failed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to detect rare cell types within a large population rather than verify purity of existing subclusters — GiniClust/GiniClust2 or RaceID3 are designed for rare-type detection, not purity assessment When clusters contain continuously varying trajectories or low-quality data where the fixed 0.9 threshold is inappropriate — the authors note the threshold must be determined from global ROGUE values in such cases When measuring purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the authors state current ROGUE does not yet support this

skills.description: Use when a single-cell integrated/clustering result has interpretable gene modules (e.g. JOINTLY factors) and you need to test if module genes are more cell-type-specific than conventional marker genes, or to guide cell type annotation.
skills.name: marker-gene-auc-specificity-comparison
skills.search_text: marker-gene-auc-specificity-comparison Use when a single-cell integrated/clustering result has interpretable gene modules (e.g. JOINTLY factors) and you need to test if module genes are more cell-type-specific than conventional marker genes, or to guide cell type annotation. The object has no interpretable gene modules or factor gene sets — the comparison is specifically between JOINTLY module genes and traditional markers, so without modules only generic marker ranking is possible Cell type labels are unreliable or missing — wilcoxauc group_by = 'celltype' and the AUC comparison depend on trustworthy per-cell-type groups (the vignette subsets to named cell types with more than 10 cells) Complex multi-condition, multi-sample datasets where the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY over consensus PCA, since module interpretation quality degrades otherwise http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies whether genes belonging to JOINTLY's interpretable factor modules are more cell-type-discriminative than traditional marker genes by scoring modules per cell (UCell), ranking genes per cell type with a Wilcoxon rank-sum AUC (presto::wilcoxauc), and comparing mean AUC of module genes versus non-module marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Quantifies whether genes belonging to JOINTLY's interpretable factor modules are more cell-type-discriminative than traditional marker genes by scoring modules per cell (UCell), ranking genes per cell type with a Wilcoxon rank-sum AUC (presto::wilcoxauc), and comparing mean AUC of module genes versus non-module marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The object has no interpretable gene modules or factor gene sets — the comparison is specifically between JOINTLY module genes and traditional markers, so without modules only generic marker ranking is possible Cell type labels are unreliable or missing — wilcoxauc group_by = 'celltype' and the AUC comparison depend on trustworthy per-cell-type groups (the vignette subsets to named cell types with more than 10 cells) Complex multi-condition, multi-sample datasets where the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY over consensus PCA, since module interpretation quality degrades otherwise

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., T/NK cells from BRCA/KIRC or myeloid cells from PAAD) needs cell-type/subtype annotation via a canonical marker-gene set, or when marker-based tools must be benchmarked against a learned classifier.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., T/NK cells from BRCA/KIRC or myeloid cells from PAAD) needs cell-type/subtype annotation via a canonical marker-gene set, or when marker-based tools must be benchmarked against a learned classifier. Tissue-specific cell types without canonical marker gene sets (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers), which marker-based tools may fail to identify and leave in an Unknown cluster When the goal is to leverage hierarchical major-type-to-subtype relationships learned from a large reference — a trained classifier like scWizard (113,976-cell reference) is the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Classifies scRNA-seq cells by matching a marker-gene panel (e.g., classical T/NK subtype markers or Wilcoxon-derived myeloid DE genes from Table S3) against the expression matrix using tools such as CellAssign and SCSA, and scores the predictions as accuracy/F1 baselines against deep-learning annotation methods like scWizard. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Classifies scRNA-seq cells by matching a marker-gene panel (e.g., classical T/NK subtype markers or Wilcoxon-derived myeloid DE genes from Table S3) against the expression matrix using tools such as CellAssign and SCSA, and scores the predictions as accuracy/F1 baselines against deep-learning annotation methods like scWizard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissue-specific cell types without canonical marker gene sets (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers), which marker-based tools may fail to identify and leave in an Unknown cluster When the goal is to leverage hierarchical major-type-to-subtype relationships learned from a large reference — a trained classifier like scWizard (113,976-cell reference) is the appropriate choice

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been identified (e.g., via robustSingleCell PCA/clustering on LCMV1/LCMV2 10X data) and need to be assigned biologically interpretable cell-type labels from a curated marker-gene panel.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been identified (e.g., via robustSingleCell PCA/clustering on LCMV1/LCMV2 10X data) and need to be assigned biologically interpretable cell-type labels from a curated marker-gene panel. Clusters have not yet been defined — marker annotation requires completed PCA/clustering and summarize differential expression output Data are not murine T cell scRNA-seq where the curated markers (Tcf7, Cxcr5, Bcl6, Foxp3, Mki67, etc.) are expected to discriminate subtypes; the marker panel must be adapted to the user's own data as the README states The goal is cross-dataset cluster integration/similarity rather than labeling — use assess.cluster.similarity / get.robust.cluster.similarity instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates scRNA-seq clusters with curated T cell subtype names (Tfh, Th1, Tcmp, Treg, Tmem, CD8, CD4, Cycle) by testing curated marker genes against cluster differential expression statistics from robustSingleCell's limma-based summarize step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: Annotates scRNA-seq clusters with curated T cell subtype names (Tfh, Th1, Tcmp, Treg, Tmem, CD8, CD4, Cycle) by testing curated marker genes against cluster differential expression statistics from robustSingleCell's limma-based summarize step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters have not yet been defined — marker annotation requires completed PCA/clustering and summarize differential expression output Data are not murine T cell scRNA-seq where the curated markers (Tcf7, Cxcr5, Bcl6, Foxp3, Mki67, etc.) are expected to discriminate subtypes; the marker panel must be adapted to the user's own data as the README states The goal is cross-dataset cluster integration/similarity rather than labeling — use assess.cluster.similarity / get.robust.cluster.similarity instead

skills.description: Use when IA-SVA (or similar SV analysis) has identified outlier cells via a surrogate variable, but standard all-gene visualizations (PCA, USVA, tSNE) fail to clearly separate those outlier cells in the embedding.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-cell-visualization
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-cell-visualization Use when IA-SVA (or similar SV analysis) has identified outlier cells via a surrogate variable, but standard all-gene visualizations (PCA, USVA, tSNE) fail to clearly separate those outlier cells in the embedding. When the surrogate-variable marker set has not yet been computed — this skill depends on an upstream find_markers step with the p-value and R-squared cutoffs already applied When the goal is de novo clustering or cell-type discovery rather than visualizing cells already flagged by a surrogate variable When the analysis target is differential expression or factor testing rather than 2D embedding comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds 2D tSNE embeddings from log-transformed IA-SVA-derived marker gene counts (adjusted p-value < 0.05, R-squared > 0.3) to make hidden heterogeneity — e.g. outlier alpha cells flagged by SV1 — visually separable where all-gene PCA/tSNE projections fail. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: Builds 2D tSNE embeddings from log-transformed IA-SVA-derived marker gene counts (adjusted p-value < 0.05, R-squared > 0.3) to make hidden heterogeneity — e.g. outlier alpha cells flagged by SV1 — visually separable where all-gene PCA/tSNE projections fail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the surrogate-variable marker set has not yet been computed — this skill depends on an upstream find_markers step with the p-value and R-squared cutoffs already applied When the goal is de novo clustering or cell-type discovery rather than visualizing cells already flagged by a surrogate variable When the analysis target is differential expression or factor testing rather than 2D embedding comparison

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-type label prediction on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, specifically to compare a marker/reference-database classifier such as CellTypist against zero-shot predictors using accuracy and macro-F1.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-classification
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-classification Use when benchmarking cell-type label prediction on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, specifically to compare a marker/reference-database classifier such as CellTypist against zero-shot predictors using accuracy and macro-F1. The task is gene network inference or denoising rather than cell-type label prediction — scPRINT's primary purpose is GN inference and classification is only a zero-shot side evaluation No tissue-matched CellTypist reference database exists, so the marker-based baseline would cover only a small fraction of test-set cell types (e.g. a ceiling of 4 of 14 database cell types covering ~70% of cells) and the comparison is unfair The dataset is spatial omics or non-single-cell — excluded from this benchmarking scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs marker-gene-referenced cell-type classification (CellTypist with a curated marker/reference database) as a supervised baseline against zero-shot foundation-model label predictors such as scPRINT, on batch-split scRNA-seq benchmarks like the open-problems human pancreas dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Runs marker-gene-referenced cell-type classification (CellTypist with a curated marker/reference database) as a supervised baseline against zero-shot foundation-model label predictors such as scPRINT, on batch-split scRNA-seq benchmarks like the open-problems human pancreas dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is gene network inference or denoising rather than cell-type label prediction — scPRINT's primary purpose is GN inference and classification is only a zero-shot side evaluation No tissue-matched CellTypist reference database exists, so the marker-based baseline would cover only a small fraction of test-set cell types (e.g. a ceiling of 4 of 14 database cell types covering ~70% of cells) and the comparison is unfair The dataset is spatial omics or non-single-cell — excluded from this benchmarking scope

skills.description: Use when a re-clustering or clustering partition of scRNA-seq data (e.g. low-purity fibroblast clusters split by ROGUE) needs biological labels, and marker genes distinguishing subtypes such as myCAFs or antigen-presenting CAFs can be evaluated from the expression matrix.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-cluster-interpretation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-cluster-interpretation Use when a re-clustering or clustering partition of scRNA-seq data (e.g. low-purity fibroblast clusters split by ROGUE) needs biological labels, and marker genes distinguishing subtypes such as myCAFs or antigen-presenting CAFs can be evaluated from the expression matrix. Clusters whose ROGUE purity is below the data-appropriate threshold and have no coherent marker signature — re-cluster further before annotating Low-quality or continuous datasets where the 0.9 purity threshold does not apply and thresholds must be set from global ROGUE values Integrated populations from different protocols/platforms, which ROGUE does not yet assess for purity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate single-cell clusters by their signature marker genes after ROGUE-guided re-clustering, e.g. labeling lung-tumor CAF subtypes as myCAF (RGS5/ACTA2/GPX3) or apCAF (CD74/MHC-II) to translate a purer clustering partition into biological subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell clusters by their signature marker genes after ROGUE-guided re-clustering, e.g. labeling lung-tumor CAF subtypes as myCAF (RGS5/ACTA2/GPX3) or apCAF (CD74/MHC-II) to translate a purer clustering partition into biological subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters whose ROGUE purity is below the data-appropriate threshold and have no coherent marker signature — re-cluster further before annotating Low-quality or continuous datasets where the 0.9 purity threshold does not apply and thresholds must be set from global ROGUE values Integrated populations from different protocols/platforms, which ROGUE does not yet assess for purity

skills.description: Use when building a labeled reference scRNA-seq training set for supervised TME cell subtype annotation and you need to filter cells down to those confidently belonging to T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, or Endothelial compartments.
skills.name: marker-gene-based-confident-cell-selection
skills.search_text: marker-gene-based-confident-cell-selection Use when building a labeled reference scRNA-seq training set for supervised TME cell subtype annotation and you need to filter cells down to those confidently belonging to T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, or Endothelial compartments.
