skills.search_text: marker-gene-expression-visualization Use when scRNA-Seq clusters or predicted cell type-specific signatures need quality assessment via known marker gene expression patterns, e.g. after cluster.assignment or signature.prediction in SINCERA. Input is a raw count matrix that has not yet been filtered, normalized, or z-score transformed — preprocessing must precede clustering and marker visualization No known marker genes are available for the tissue or cell types, so plotMarkers cannot discriminate cluster quality The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than visual quality assessment of existing SINCERA cluster assignments or signatures http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A SINCERA-based visualization skill that renders expression patterns of known marker genes across cell clusters (plotMarkers) and predicted cell type-specific signature genes across cell types (plotHeatmap), using the visual pattern of selective versus scattered expression to accept or reject clustering and signature results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: A SINCERA-based visualization skill that renders expression patterns of known marker genes across cell clusters (plotMarkers) and predicted cell type-specific signature genes across cell types (plotHeatmap), using the visual pattern of selective versus scattered expression to accept or reject clustering and signature results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix that has not yet been filtered, normalized, or z-score transformed — preprocessing must precede clustering and marker visualization No known marker genes are available for the tissue or cell types, so plotMarkers cannot discriminate cluster quality The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than visual quality assessment of existing SINCERA cluster assignments or signatures

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices (raw vs imputed) must be compared at the cluster level by coloring t-SNE plots by cell type and overlaying curated marker genes (e.g., S100A8, FCER1A) to confirm subpopulation separation.
skills.name: marker-gene-expression-visualization-across-clusters
skills.search_text: marker-gene-expression-visualization-across-clusters Use when scRNA-seq count matrices (raw vs imputed) must be compared at the cluster level by coloring t-SNE plots by cell type and overlaying curated marker genes (e.g., S100A8, FCER1A) to confirm subpopulation separation. The analysis goal is a numeric clustering benchmark (e.g., ARI) rather than the qualitative t-SNE/marker validation reported in this paper, which explicitly states 'no numeric threshold reported in the paper'. The input is bulk RNA-seq data, which 'does not allow people to study cell-to-cell variation' and therefore has no cell clusters or marker overlays to visualize. Gene-level filtering has already removed most genes; scImpute's README recommends applying it to the whole-genome count matrix 'to ensure robust identification of dropouts', which this visualization workflow depends on. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Overlay known marker genes (e.g., S100A8, FCER1A for monocyte/dendritic clusters) and cell-type colors onto t-SNE embeddings computed separately from raw and scImpute-imputed scRNA-seq count matrices, to qualitatively verify whether imputation resolves subpopulation structure that dropout obscures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Overlay known marker genes (e.g., S100A8, FCER1A for monocyte/dendritic clusters) and cell-type colors onto t-SNE embeddings computed separately from raw and scImpute-imputed scRNA-seq count matrices, to qualitatively verify whether imputation resolves subpopulation structure that dropout obscures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a numeric clustering benchmark (e.g., ARI) rather than the qualitative t-SNE/marker validation reported in this paper, which explicitly states 'no numeric threshold reported in the paper'. The input is bulk RNA-seq data, which 'does not allow people to study cell-to-cell variation' and therefore has no cell clusters or marker overlays to visualize. Gene-level filtering has already removed most genes; scImpute's README recommends applying it to the whole-genome count matrix 'to ensure robust identification of dropouts', which this visualization workflow depends on.

skills.description: Use when you need marker gene sets for Cell Ontology cell types — including types with no annotated cells in training data — from OnClass prediction matrices and single-cell expression data such as Tabula Muris Senis FACS.
skills.name: marker-gene-identification
skills.search_text: marker-gene-identification Use when you need marker gene sets for Cell Ontology cell types — including types with no annotated cells in training data — from OnClass prediction matrices and single-cell expression data such as Tabula Muris Senis FACS. You only need cell type label annotation from expression data and do not need per-term gene rankings — use OnClass classification (e.g., run_OnClass_example.py) instead. The cell types of interest are topologically identical siblings in the Cell Ontology graph, which OnClass cannot distinguish, making per-term marker gene identity unreliable. Your reference lacks annotated cells and you require experimentally curated marker associations rather than correlation-derived markers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify marker genes for every Cell Ontology term (seen or unseen) by ranking genes per cell type via Spearman correlation between OnClass predicted cell-type probability vectors and gene expression profiles, then validate them by marker-gene-based prediction AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Identify marker genes for every Cell Ontology term (seen or unseen) by ranking genes per cell type via Spearman correlation between OnClass predicted cell-type probability vectors and gene expression profiles, then validate them by marker-gene-based prediction AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need cell type label annotation from expression data and do not need per-term gene rankings — use OnClass classification (e.g., run_OnClass_example.py) instead. The cell types of interest are topologically identical siblings in the Cell Ontology graph, which OnClass cannot distinguish, making per-term marker gene identity unreliable. Your reference lacks annotated cells and you require experimentally curated marker associations rather than correlation-derived markers.

skills.description: Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq matrix and need cluster-level marker genes free of pseudo markers (upregulated in multiple clusters) before automatic cell type annotation.
skills.name: marker-gene-identification-across-clusters
skills.search_text: marker-gene-identification-across-clusters Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq matrix and need cluster-level marker genes free of pseudo markers (upregulated in multiple clusters) before automatic cell type annotation. The goal is cell-level (not cluster-based) annotation — cell-based methods like SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, or CHETAH are the appropriate comparison class The reference database (CellMatch) does not cover the tissue/cell types of interest — scCATCH performance majorly depends on the reference database and a limited one may cause incorrect annotation Clustering itself is inadequate (too many or too few clusters), which would introduce errors regardless of marker quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies potential marker genes for each cell cluster by paired one-against-all comparison across clusters (scCATCH findmarkergene), filtering for genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster (log10 fold change ≥0.25, p < 0.05) and expressed in ≥25% of cells, as the basis for downstream cluster annotation against CellMatch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Identifies potential marker genes for each cell cluster by paired one-against-all comparison across clusters (scCATCH findmarkergene), filtering for genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster (log10 fold change ≥0.25, p < 0.05) and expressed in ≥25% of cells, as the basis for downstream cluster annotation against CellMatch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-level (not cluster-based) annotation — cell-based methods like SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, or CHETAH are the appropriate comparison class The reference database (CellMatch) does not cover the tissue/cell types of interest — scCATCH performance majorly depends on the reference database and a limited one may cause incorrect annotation Clustering itself is inadequate (too many or too few clusters), which would introduce errors regardless of marker quality

skills.description: Use when an unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data (e.g., k-means on PCs of PBMCs) yields clusters whose biological identities must be determined from cluster-enriched genes such as CD3D, NKG7, CD79A, S100A8/S100A9, PF4, FCER1A.
skills.name: marker-gene-identification-for-immune-cell-populations
skills.search_text: marker-gene-identification-for-immune-cell-populations Use when an unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data (e.g., k-means on PCs of PBMCs) yields clusters whose biological identities must be determined from cluster-enriched genes such as CD3D, NKG7, CD79A, S100A8/S100A9, PF4, FCER1A. When cell populations are already annotated by orthogonal methods (e.g., flow cytometry panels or cell-type correlation assignment to purified reference populations) — marker discovery adds no identity information. When the tissue is not blood/immune-derived (e.g., tumor or solid-tissue scRNA-seq), since the canonical PBMC marker set (CD3D, CD79A, S100A8/S100A9, PF4, FCER1A) will not map onto the relevant populations. When the input is raw sequencing data needing barcode processing first — Cell Ranger demultiplexing/counting must be completed before marker gene identification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Identify cluster-specific marker genes from single-cell 3′ counting data of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (e.g., the 68k PBMC dataset) to assign canonical immune cell identities (T cells, NK cells, B cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, megakaryocytes/platelets) to unsupervised clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Identify cluster-specific marker genes from single-cell 3′ counting data of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (e.g., the 68k PBMC dataset) to assign canonical immune cell identities (T cells, NK cells, B cells, monocytes, dendritic cells, megakaryocytes/platelets) to unsupervised clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell populations are already annotated by orthogonal methods (e.g., flow cytometry panels or cell-type correlation assignment to purified reference populations) — marker discovery adds no identity information. When the tissue is not blood/immune-derived (e.g., tumor or solid-tissue scRNA-seq), since the canonical PBMC marker set (CD3D, CD79A, S100A8/S100A9, PF4, FCER1A) will not map onto the relevant populations. When the input is raw sequencing data needing barcode processing first — Cell Ranger demultiplexing/counting must be completed before marker gene identification.

skills.description: Use when an IA-SVA run has produced a significant surrogate variable (e.g., SV1 for 101 human alpha cells) and you need the marker genes driving that hidden factor for downstream interpretation.
skills.name: marker-gene-identification-via-rsq-regression
skills.search_text: marker-gene-identification-via-rsq-regression Use when an IA-SVA run has produced a significant surrogate variable (e.g., SV1 for 101 human alpha cells) and you need the marker genes driving that hidden factor for downstream interpretation. No surrogate variable has been estimated yet — run IA-SVA first (e.g., fast_iasva) to obtain the SV to which genes are regressed The putative 'markers' may stem from compromised/doublet cells or contamination (e.g., fibroblast genes in alpha cells) — such cells should be excluded from downstream analyses rather than treated as biological signal The hidden factor was not significant by IA-SVA's permutation-based significance index — an SV that does not explain meaningful variation will yield no reliable marker set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies the set of genes significantly associated with a hidden factor captured by an IA-SVA surrogate variable by regressing each gene's expression on the SV with the find_markers() function of the iasva R package and retaining genes passing multiple-testing-adjusted p-value < 0.05 and R-squared > 0.3 thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: Identifies the set of genes significantly associated with a hidden factor captured by an IA-SVA surrogate variable by regressing each gene's expression on the SV with the find_markers() function of the iasva R package and retaining genes passing multiple-testing-adjusted p-value < 0.05 and R-squared > 0.3 thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No surrogate variable has been estimated yet — run IA-SVA first (e.g., fast_iasva) to obtain the SV to which genes are regressed The putative 'markers' may stem from compromised/doublet cells or contamination (e.g., fibroblast genes in alpha cells) — such cells should be excluded from downstream analyses rather than treated as biological signal The hidden factor was not significant by IA-SVA's permutation-based significance index — an SV that does not explain meaningful variation will yield no reliable marker set

skills.description: Use when a dimensionality-reduction/feature-selection method produces a ranked gene list that must be checked for biological plausibility against known cell-type markers before downstream use.
skills.name: marker-gene-list-validation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-list-validation Use when a dimensionality-reduction/feature-selection method produces a ranked gene list that must be checked for biological plausibility against known cell-type markers before downstream use. Input is simulated scRNA-seq data without known cell-type markers — the validation relies on curated marker references for real datasets only The gene list is a raw variable-feature list (e.g., Seurat FindVariableFeatures output) rather than the post-cutoff EDGE feature gene set — the μ − 1.5 × σ step must run first The dataset was restricted to fewer than 1000 top variable genes, which would change the candidate pool and invalidate the expected list sizes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates a computationally derived feature gene list (e.g., from EDGE's μ − 1.5 × σ entropy cutoff) by cross-referencing it against a curated marker reference and checking that known cell-type markers (e.g., PBMC markers PPBP, LYZ, CST3, NKG7, S100A9) and expected list sizes (17, 35, 43 genes for Jurkat, PBMC, mouse brain) are recovered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Validates a computationally derived feature gene list (e.g., from EDGE's μ − 1.5 × σ entropy cutoff) by cross-referencing it against a curated marker reference and checking that known cell-type markers (e.g., PBMC markers PPBP, LYZ, CST3, NKG7, S100A9) and expected list sizes (17, 35, 43 genes for Jurkat, PBMC, mouse brain) are recovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated scRNA-seq data without known cell-type markers — the validation relies on curated marker references for real datasets only The gene list is a raw variable-feature list (e.g., Seurat FindVariableFeatures output) rather than the post-cutoff EDGE feature gene set — the μ − 1.5 × σ step must run first The dataset was restricted to fewer than 1000 top variable genes, which would change the candidate pool and invalidate the expected list sizes

skills.description: Use when a clustering method outputs per-cluster key genes and you must verify they are biologically meaningful by testing overlap with published cell-type markers and DEGs (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01).
skills.name: marker-gene-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: marker-gene-overlap-analysis Use when a clustering method outputs per-cluster key genes and you must verify they are biologically meaningful by testing overlap with published cell-type markers and DEGs (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01). The clustering outputs are not scQA landmark/key genes (e.g., you only have cluster labels without the key genes defining each cluster) — there is nothing to validate against the marker/DEG references. The dataset's original publication does not provide marker or DEG gene sets to serve as reference, leaving no external ground truth for overlap testing. You need to identify cell types or cluster cells de novo — use the upstream scQA clustering pipeline (pre-processing, LC1/LC2, CC modules) instead of the downstream validation step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates scQA key genes (landmark genes) per cluster by computing overlap and enrichment statistics against marker genes and DEGs compiled from the dataset's original publication, confirming biological significance as in the Camp2 endothelial case (ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Validates scQA key genes (landmark genes) per cluster by computing overlap and enrichment statistics against marker genes and DEGs compiled from the dataset's original publication, confirming biological significance as in the Camp2 endothelial case (ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering outputs are not scQA landmark/key genes (e.g., you only have cluster labels without the key genes defining each cluster) — there is nothing to validate against the marker/DEG references. The dataset's original publication does not provide marker or DEG gene sets to serve as reference, leaving no external ground truth for overlap testing. You need to identify cell types or cluster cells de novo — use the upstream scQA clustering pipeline (pre-processing, LC1/LC2, CC modules) instead of the downstream validation step.

skills.description: Use when you have bulk transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq or microarray) with matched survival information and a cell-type marker set, and need to identify prognostic marker gene pairs as the basis for inferring cell-cell interactions in the tumor immune microenvironment.
skills.name: marker-gene-pair-cox-survival-regression
skills.search_text: marker-gene-pair-cox-survival-regression Use when you have bulk transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq or microarray) with matched survival information and a cell-type marker set, and need to identify prognostic marker gene pairs as the basis for inferring cell-cell interactions in the tumor immune microenvironment. The dataset is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to effectively identify prognostic gene pairs The clinical survival information is low quality (few events or poor time-to-event data), since the power of the survival analysis is determined by sample size, number of events, and quality of survival information The goal is immunotherapy response rather than prognosis — use the TimiGP-Response module (e.g. TimiFisher) instead of the Cox-based Prognosis Module http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A TimiGP workflow step that converts cell-type marker expression into a binary Marker Pair Score (MPS) matrix, fits univariate Cox regression on each marker pair against survival data, and selects directed pairs associated with favorable prognosis for downstream cell-cell interaction network inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: A TimiGP workflow step that converts cell-type marker expression into a binary Marker Pair Score (MPS) matrix, fits univariate Cox regression on each marker pair against survival data, and selects directed pairs associated with favorable prognosis for downstream cell-cell interaction network inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to effectively identify prognostic gene pairs The clinical survival information is low quality (few events or poor time-to-event data), since the power of the survival analysis is determined by sample size, number of events, and quality of survival information The goal is immunotherapy response rather than prognosis — use the TimiGP-Response module (e.g. TimiFisher) instead of the Cox-based Prognosis Module

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk transcriptomic profile (RNA-seq or microarray) plus a cell-type marker annotation and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to prognostic gene-pair analysis.
skills.name: marker-gene-pair-score-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: marker-gene-pair-score-matrix-construction Use when you have a bulk transcriptomic profile (RNA-seq or microarray) plus a cell-type marker annotation and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to prognostic gene-pair analysis. Input expression data has not been preprocessed (no log transformation or gene-wise median normalization) — run TimiPrePropress first, since unnormalized values distort the pairwise comparisons The goal is estimating absolute cell-type abundance proportions (e.g., deconvolution with CIBERSORTx or xCell) rather than pairwise expression relations for prognostic network analysis No cell-type marker annotation is available to define the gene pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 TimiGP's Marker Pair Score (MPS) construction step: convert a bulk transcriptomic profile and a cell-type marker set into a binary pairwise-comparison matrix where each marker pair (gene A vs gene B) scores 1 when gene A expression exceeds gene B in a sample. This MPS is the substrate for downstream univariate Cox selection and cell-cell interaction inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: TimiGP's Marker Pair Score (MPS) construction step: convert a bulk transcriptomic profile and a cell-type marker set into a binary pairwise-comparison matrix where each marker pair (gene A vs gene B) scores 1 when gene A expression exceeds gene B in a sample. This MPS is the substrate for downstream univariate Cox selection and cell-cell interaction inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data has not been preprocessed (no log transformation or gene-wise median normalization) — run TimiPrePropress first, since unnormalized values distort the pairwise comparisons The goal is estimating absolute cell-type abundance proportions (e.g., deconvolution with CIBERSORTx or xCell) rather than pairwise expression relations for prognostic network analysis No cell-type marker annotation is available to define the gene pairs

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-type marker gene list (e.g., scRNA-seq-derived T cell subtype markers) plus bulk RNA-seq/microarray data and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to survival modeling.
skills.name: marker-gene-pairwise-comparison
skills.search_text: marker-gene-pairwise-comparison Use when you have a cell-type marker gene list (e.g., scRNA-seq-derived T cell subtype markers) plus bulk RNA-seq/microarray data and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to survival modeling. Input is single-cell expression data where direct cell-cell communication tools (e.g., scSeqComm) can be applied instead of bulk-inferred gene pairs No matched survival/clinical outcome information is available, since prognostic gene-pair selection via TimiCOX cannot be powered The gene set of interest is continuous dosage data rather than marker dichotomies and cont=TRUE behavior has not been validated for the cohort http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates a Marker Pair Score (MPS) matrix from a cell-type marker gene list and a bulk transcriptomic profile by logical pairwise comparison of marker expression within each sample, the first analytical step of the TimiGP framework that enables downstream Cox-based prognostic ranking of gene pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Generates a Marker Pair Score (MPS) matrix from a cell-type marker gene list and a bulk transcriptomic profile by logical pairwise comparison of marker expression within each sample, the first analytical step of the TimiGP framework that enables downstream Cox-based prognostic ranking of gene pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell expression data where direct cell-cell communication tools (e.g., scSeqComm) can be applied instead of bulk-inferred gene pairs No matched survival/clinical outcome information is available, since prognostic gene-pair selection via TimiCOX cannot be powered The gene set of interest is continuous dosage data rather than marker dichotomies and cont=TRUE behavior has not been validated for the cohort

skills.description: Use when validating scRNA-seq imputation on marker genes: you have a cell-by-gene normalized matrix (and optionally its imputed counterpart), cell-type labels, and need per-type percent-expressing fractions for genes like NCAM1 or CR2.
skills.name: marker-gene-percent-expressing-aggregation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-percent-expressing-aggregation Use when validating scRNA-seq imputation on marker genes: you have a cell-by-gene normalized matrix (and optionally its imputed counterpart), cell-type labels, and need per-type percent-expressing fractions for genes like NCAM1 or CR2. The input matrix is raw counts that have not been library/log normalized — percent-expressing comparisons against ALRA output require matching normalized scales The goal is differential expression testing between cell types rather than verification that biological zeros were preserved/completed by imputation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies, for chosen marker genes (e.g. NCAM1, CR2) in a scRNA-seq matrix, the percentage of cells with non-zero expression per cell type, before and after imputation, to verify that ALRA recovers biological-zero marker expression in the B/NK PBMC data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Quantifies, for chosen marker genes (e.g. NCAM1, CR2) in a scRNA-seq matrix, the percentage of cells with non-zero expression per cell type, before and after imputation, to verify that ALRA recovers biological-zero marker expression in the B/NK PBMC data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is raw counts that have not been library/log normalized — percent-expressing comparisons against ALRA output require matching normalized scales The goal is differential expression testing between cell types rather than verification that biological zeros were preserved/completed by imputation

skills.description: Use when preparing positive/negative marker files for BIDCell training on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Xenium breast cancer), or when defining cell-type markers by expression percentile cutoffs from a single-cell reference.
skills.name: marker-gene-percentile-selection
skills.search_text: marker-gene-percentile-selection Use when preparing positive/negative marker files for BIDCell training on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Xenium breast cancer), or when defining cell-type markers by expression percentile cutoffs from a single-cell reference. The spatial dataset already ships with curated marker files (manual curation is an accepted alternative, so re-deriving percentiles may be unnecessary). The tissue of interest has no matching single-cell reference in repositories such as TISCH2, Allen Brain Map, or the Human Cell Atlas, so percentile ranking cannot be grounded in cell-type-specific expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Derives positive and negative cell-type marker gene lists from a single-cell reference by selecting genes with expression in the highest and lowest 10 percentile per cell type, then removing positive markers shared by at least a third of cell types. These marker files drive BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions and enable expression-purity/neighbour-contamination evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Derives positive and negative cell-type marker gene lists from a single-cell reference by selecting genes with expression in the highest and lowest 10 percentile per cell type, then removing positive markers shared by at least a third of cell types. These marker files drive BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions and enable expression-purity/neighbour-contamination evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial dataset already ships with curated marker files (manual curation is an accepted alternative, so re-deriving percentiles may be unnecessary). The tissue of interest has no matching single-cell reference in repositories such as TISCH2, Allen Brain Map, or the Human Cell Atlas, so percentile ranking cannot be grounded in cell-type-specific expression.

skills.description: Use when Louvain/SNN cluster labels exist per cell and you must characterize each cluster by its top differentially expressed genes, e.g. to reproduce per-cluster marker depictions like the paper's Fig. 2E.
skills.name: marker-gene-ranking-by-log2fc
skills.search_text: marker-gene-ranking-by-log2fc Use when Louvain/SNN cluster labels exist per cell and you must characterize each cluster by its top differentially expressed genes, e.g. to reproduce per-cluster marker depictions like the paper's Fig. 2E. Cells are not yet clustered — marker testing requires pre-existing cluster labels from a prior Louvain/SNN step The goal is annotating clusters against reference signatures (e.g. CIPR-style Cluster Identity Prediction) rather than de novo one-vs-rest marker discovery Input is scATAC-seq accessibility data, for which gene-expression DE tests like Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2 do not directly apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify and rank cluster-defining marker genes from scRNA-seq data by running one-vs-rest differential expression (Wilcoxon rank sum test, with MAST and DESeq2 as alternatives in SCALA) and ranking genes per cluster by Log2FC, as demonstrated on the PBMC3k dataset in SCALA (Seurat-based pipeline). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Identify and rank cluster-defining marker genes from scRNA-seq data by running one-vs-rest differential expression (Wilcoxon rank sum test, with MAST and DESeq2 as alternatives in SCALA) and ranking genes per cluster by Log2FC, as demonstrated on the PBMC3k dataset in SCALA (Seurat-based pipeline).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are not yet clustered — marker testing requires pre-existing cluster labels from a prior Louvain/SNN step The goal is annotating clusters against reference signatures (e.g. CIPR-style Cluster Identity Prediction) rather than de novo one-vs-rest marker discovery Input is scATAC-seq accessibility data, for which gene-expression DE tests like Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2 do not directly apply

skills.description: Use when a redPATH pseudotime ordering exists for single-cell RNA-seq data and the goal is to discover and validate genes whose expression significantly associates with both cell proliferation and differentiation along the trajectory.
skills.name: marker-gene-recovery-validation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-recovery-validation Use when a redPATH pseudotime ordering exists for single-cell RNA-seq data and the goal is to discover and validate genes whose expression significantly associates with both cell proliferation and differentiation along the trajectory. When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this gene discovery approach may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly. When the goal is to simultaneously model the coupling between proliferation and differentiation with an integrative model rather than discover individual correlated genes. When the input expression matrix has not been GO-subsetted and dispersion-filtered; redPATH's preprocessing expects genes reduced via Gene Ontology and a simple dispersion threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Recovers proliferation/differentiation-coupled marker genes (Foxm1, Tubb5, Nek2) and marker genes (Dcx, Sp9) by applying distance correlation (dCor) and Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) statistics to redPATH pseudotime on the NSC-Llorens neural stem cell dataset, then validating the recovered genes against published results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Recovers proliferation/differentiation-coupled marker genes (Foxm1, Tubb5, Nek2) and marker genes (Dcx, Sp9) by applying distance correlation (dCor) and Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) statistics to redPATH pseudotime on the NSC-Llorens neural stem cell dataset, then validating the recovered genes against published results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this gene discovery approach may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly. When the goal is to simultaneously model the coupling between proliferation and differentiation with an integrative model rather than discover individual correlated genes. When the input expression matrix has not been GO-subsetted and dispersion-filtered; redPATH's preprocessing expects genes reduced via Gene Ontology and a simple dispersion threshold.

skills.description: Use when an AnnData annotated with DeepCycle's obs['cell_cycle_theta'] needs marker-gene-derived phase-transition landmarks (Cyclin E peak, G2M-vs-S crossover) to assign cells to G1, S, or G2/M.
skills.name: marker-gene-score-computation-from-rna-velocity-layers
skills.search_text: marker-gene-score-computation-from-rna-velocity-layers Use when an AnnData annotated with DeepCycle's obs['cell_cycle_theta'] needs marker-gene-derived phase-transition landmarks (Cyclin E peak, G2M-vs-S crossover) to assign cells to G1, S, or G2/M. When defining cell cycle phases from scratch without a continuous phase variable — the article warns that 'defining the cell cycle phases in RNA data based solely on gene markers lacks generalizability', so scores are only used to landmark the DeepCycle theta, not to replace it When the AnnData lacks scVelo Ms/Mu layers or obs['cell_cycle_theta'] (e.g. raw unpreprocessed count matrices not run through scvelo.pp.moments and DeepCycle) When no cycling genes were found in the dataset — the README states 'If you do not find any cycling genes the results will not be reliable' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute Cyclin E, S-phase, and G2/M marker gene scores per cell from the scVelo 'Ms' (spliced) and 'Mu' (unspliced) imputed layers of an AnnData object so that cell cycle phase transitions (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) can be located along the DeepCycle-inferred circular transcriptional phase theta. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Compute Cyclin E, S-phase, and G2/M marker gene scores per cell from the scVelo 'Ms' (spliced) and 'Mu' (unspliced) imputed layers of an AnnData object so that cell cycle phase transitions (G1/S, S/G2, M/G1) can be located along the DeepCycle-inferred circular transcriptional phase theta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When defining cell cycle phases from scratch without a continuous phase variable — the article warns that 'defining the cell cycle phases in RNA data based solely on gene markers lacks generalizability', so scores are only used to landmark the DeepCycle theta, not to replace it When the AnnData lacks scVelo Ms/Mu layers or obs['cell_cycle_theta'] (e.g. raw unpreprocessed count matrices not run through scvelo.pp.moments and DeepCycle) When no cycling genes were found in the dataset — the README states 'If you do not find any cycling genes the results will not be reliable'

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset and need to learn cell-type marker lists (with rejection thresholds) for downstream reference-based cell type identification instead of using a curated marker DB.
skills.name: marker-gene-selection-per-cell-type
skills.search_text: marker-gene-selection-per-cell-type Use when you have a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset and need to learn cell-type marker lists (with rejection thresholds) for downstream reference-based cell type identification instead of using a curated marker DB. You already have a curated marker list/database (e.g. Panglao DB or CellMarker DB) and want marker-based identification — use MarkerCount() marker-based mode or HiCAT instead of training from a reference No cell type annotations are available for the input dataset — this skill requires a pre-annotated reference to compute the gene-cell type association score The goal is test-phase cell identification of new cells rather than constructing the reference training model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Derives per-cell-type marker gene sets from a pre-annotated single-cell RNA-seq reference by binarizing expression, computing MarkerCount's gene-cell type association score, and selecting the top N=18 markers per type. This training step replaces curated marker databases with data-driven markers before test-phase identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Derives per-cell-type marker gene sets from a pre-annotated single-cell RNA-seq reference by binarizing expression, computing MarkerCount's gene-cell type association score, and selecting the top N=18 markers per type. This training step replaces curated marker databases with data-driven markers before test-phase identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a curated marker list/database (e.g. Panglao DB or CellMarker DB) and want marker-based identification — use MarkerCount() marker-based mode or HiCAT instead of training from a reference No cell type annotations are available for the input dataset — this skill requires a pre-annotated reference to compute the gene-cell type association score The goal is test-phase cell identification of new cells rather than constructing the reference training model

skills.description: Use when NeuCA's hierarchical branch is triggered — off-diagonal Pearson correlations among cell-type mean profiles exceed tau = 0.95 — and test cells must be pre-assigned from highly sensitive markers before tree traversal.
skills.name: marker-gene-sensitivity-scoring
skills.search_text: marker-gene-sensitivity-scoring Use when NeuCA's hierarchical branch is triggered — off-diagonal Pearson correlations among cell-type mean profiles exceed tau = 0.95 — and test cells must be pre-assigned from highly sensitive markers before tree traversal. All off-diagonal elements of the cell-type correlation matrix P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA switches to a single feed-forward network and the marker-guided hierarchical branch is not used The test sample may contain novel or unknown cell types not present in the training reference — NeuCA assumes every test cell belongs to one of the K training-defined types No labeled training data exist for the tissue — supervised pre-assignment cannot be performed and unsupervised methods are required http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores cell-type-specific marker genes by sensitivity (Sen_gk > 0.95, i.e. expressed in >95% of cells of that type) from the averaged expression profile, and uses markers to pre-assign test cells before NeuCA's lineage-tree bifurcation classification, improving accuracy for closely correlated cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Scores cell-type-specific marker genes by sensitivity (Sen_gk > 0.95, i.e. expressed in >95% of cells of that type) from the averaged expression profile, and uses markers to pre-assign test cells before NeuCA's lineage-tree bifurcation classification, improving accuracy for closely correlated cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All off-diagonal elements of the cell-type correlation matrix P are below tau = 0.95 — NeuCA switches to a single feed-forward network and the marker-guided hierarchical branch is not used The test sample may contain novel or unknown cell types not present in the training reference — NeuCA assumes every test cell belongs to one of the K training-defined types No labeled training data exist for the tissue — supervised pre-assignment cannot be performed and unsupervised methods are required

skills.description: Use when you need cell-type marker gene sets (positive and negative) from the ScTypeDB database restricted to a specific tissue type (e.g. 'Immune system', 'Liver', 'Eye', 'Brain') before running sctype_score or comparable marker-based annotation methods.
skills.name: marker-gene-set-preparation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-set-preparation Use when you need cell-type marker gene sets (positive and negative) from the ScTypeDB database restricted to a specific tissue type (e.g. 'Immune system', 'Liver', 'Eye', 'Brain') before running sctype_score or comparable marker-based annotation methods. The expression dataset's tissue has no matching tissueType entry in the ScTypeDB (fewer than 5 cell types were excluded from the database), so no candidate gene sets can be prepared Gene identifiers in the expression matrix are not approved gene symbols and cannot be converted, since the database was standardized to approved gene symbols You need de novo marker discovery without prior marker knowledge — ScType requires a marker database as background information http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares tissue-restricted positive and negative marker gene sets for ScType cell-type annotation by reading the ScTypeDB XLSX marker database (tissueType, cellName, geneSymbolmore1, geneSymbolmore2 columns) through the gene_sets_prepare() function, producing gs_positive and gs_negative lists per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Prepares tissue-restricted positive and negative marker gene sets for ScType cell-type annotation by reading the ScTypeDB XLSX marker database (tissueType, cellName, geneSymbolmore1, geneSymbolmore2 columns) through the gene_sets_prepare() function, producing gs_positive and gs_negative lists per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression dataset's tissue has no matching tissueType entry in the ScTypeDB (fewer than 5 cell types were excluded from the database), so no candidate gene sets can be prepared Gene identifiers in the expression matrix are not approved gene symbols and cannot be converted, since the database was standardized to approved gene symbols You need de novo marker discovery without prior marker knowledge — ScType requires a marker database as background information

skills.description: Use when harmonizing cell-type marker genes from multiple annotation sources (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need consistent, evidence-weighted marker scores for downstream cell type annotation.
skills.name: marker-gene-specificity-scoring
skills.search_text: marker-gene-specificity-scoring Use when harmonizing cell-type marker genes from multiple annotation sources (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need consistent, evidence-weighted marker scores for downstream cell type annotation. You need to annotate cells directly from raw counts without a pre-built or user-provided weighted marker database — use the accordion() annotation workflow instead Your markers come from a single source with no conflicting annotations, so evidence consistency (ECs) provides no discriminative signal Input is already a weighted signature/marker score table and does not require integration across heterogeneous marker databases http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Weights marker genes from the Cell Marker Accordion database by combining a specificity score (SPs) and an evidence consistency score (ECs) so that annotation sources with heterogeneous marker sets are harmonized into a single interpretable weight per gene-cell type pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Weights marker genes from the Cell Marker Accordion database by combining a specificity score (SPs) and an evidence consistency score (ECs) so that annotation sources with heterogeneous marker sets are harmonized into a single interpretable weight per gene-cell type pair.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to annotate cells directly from raw counts without a pre-built or user-provided weighted marker database — use the accordion() annotation workflow instead Your markers come from a single source with no conflicting annotations, so evidence consistency (ECs) provides no discriminative signal Input is already a weighted signature/marker score table and does not require integration across heterogeneous marker databases

skills.description: Use when you have a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix with subtype labels and need to score genes by how closely their cross-subtype pattern matches an ideal marker gene (or an XOR-defined subtype-downregulated gene) profile.
skills.name: marker-gene-test-statistic-implementation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-test-statistic-implementation Use when you have a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix with subtype labels and need to score genes by how closely their cross-subtype pattern matches an ideal marker gene (or an XOR-defined subtype-downregulated gene) profile. Input data is not batch-corrected — COT expects batch-corrected input and the statistic will be distorted otherwise The goal is differential expression between exactly two conditions rather than marker detection among many subtypes Too few genes are provided to approximate the empirical null distribution — p-values cannot be computed reliably (see the Example_GSE28490 vignette) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Implement the COT Cosine-based One-sample Test statistic: the cosine similarity between a molecule's cross-subtype expression profile and the exact mathematical definition of an ideal marker gene (and its XOR-based extension for subtype-downregulated genes), used to detect marker genes among many subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: Implement the COT Cosine-based One-sample Test statistic: the cosine similarity between a molecule's cross-subtype expression profile and the exact mathematical definition of an ideal marker gene (and its XOR-based extension for subtype-downregulated genes), used to detect marker genes among many subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not batch-corrected — COT expects batch-corrected input and the statistic will be distorted otherwise The goal is differential expression between exactly two conditions rather than marker detection among many subtypes Too few genes are provided to approximate the empirical null distribution — p-values cannot be computed reliably (see the Example_GSE28490 vignette)

skills.description: Use when interpreting a trained single-cell classifier (e.g., scSHARP GCN) with DeepLIFT and you need to confirm the per-gene importance rankings recover known cell-type markers.
skills.name: marker-gene-top-rank-validation
skills.search_text: marker-gene-top-rank-validation Use when interpreting a trained single-cell classifier (e.g., scSHARP GCN) with DeepLIFT and you need to confirm the per-gene importance rankings recover known cell-type markers. You only need cell type labels and not model interpretability — run the scSHARP consensus/GCN classification pipeline instead of attribution. The trained model or its checkpoints are unavailable; DeepLIFT attributions require the fitted GCN, not just predictions. Input expression data is not raw counts; the scSHARP README explicitly instructs to 'Please input raw counts.' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validate GCN feature attributions by checking whether biologically canonical marker genes rank at the top of per-cell-type gene importance scores (e.g., CD8B for CD8 T cells, Tnp1/Ldhc for testis), reproducing Figure 2 of the scSHARP paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Validate GCN feature attributions by checking whether biologically canonical marker genes rank at the top of per-cell-type gene importance scores (e.g., CD8B for CD8 T cells, Tnp1/Ldhc for testis), reproducing Figure 2 of the scSHARP paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need cell type labels and not model interpretability — run the scSHARP consensus/GCN classification pipeline instead of attribution. The trained model or its checkpoints are unavailable; DeepLIFT attributions require the fitted GCN, not just predictions. Input expression data is not raw counts; the scSHARP README explicitly instructs to 'Please input raw counts.'

skills.description: Use when you have an upstream ranked marker list (e.g., MASI's marker_identification output) per cell type and need rank-discounted marker weights before computing a cell-type score matrix for annotation or integration.
skills.name: marker-gene-weight-assignment
skills.search_text: marker-gene-weight-assignment Use when you have an upstream ranked marker list (e.g., MASI's marker_identification output) per cell type and need rank-discounted marker weights before computing a cell-type score matrix for annotation or integration. Input is an unranked or significant-marker-only marker set with no per-cell-type rank ordering, since the linear discount is defined over rank position N Query data contains cell types absent from the reference; MASI weighting cannot annotate unseen cell types (combine MASI with SCCAF instead) The reference data are low quality or poorly resolved — annotation accuracy depends critically on reference quality and resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns linearly discounted weights to a ranked cell-type marker list following MASI's weighing scheme, where the 1st-ranked marker contributes 100% and the Nth-ranked marker contributes 50% of its expression to the cell-type score. These weighted markers drive MASI's conversion of the gene expression matrix into the cell-type score matrix used for annotation and integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Assigns linearly discounted weights to a ranked cell-type marker list following MASI's weighing scheme, where the 1st-ranked marker contributes 100% and the Nth-ranked marker contributes 50% of its expression to the cell-type score. These weighted markers drive MASI's conversion of the gene expression matrix into the cell-type score matrix used for annotation and integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unranked or significant-marker-only marker set with no per-cell-type rank ordering, since the linear discount is defined over rank position N Query data contains cell types absent from the reference; MASI weighting cannot annotate unseen cell types (combine MASI with SCCAF instead) The reference data are low quality or poorly resolved — annotation accuracy depends critically on reference quality and resolution

skills.description: Use when the analysis goal is to visualize spatial expression of specific marker gene sets at native sub-micrometer barcode resolution (e.g., Seq-Scope data with >1M barcodes/mm²), and you have an unaggregated digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates.
skills.name: marker-geneset-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: marker-geneset-expression-quantification Use when the analysis goal is to visualize spatial expression of specific marker gene sets at native sub-micrometer barcode resolution (e.g., Seq-Scope data with >1M barcodes/mm²), and you have an unaggregated digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates. Input DGE has already been collapsed into grid-level Seurat objects (Step C1/C2 output), destroying the per-barcode spatial resolution needed for subcellular visualization The goal is cell-type clustering or reference mapping rather than marker geneset visualization — use STtools Steps C1–C3/V2 with the sliding window strategy instead Analysis is at VISIUM (~120 barcodes/mm²) or Slide-seq resolution where per-barcode RGB rendering is unnecessary; lower-resolution feature plotting suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify user-selected marker gene sets in spatial transcriptomics data and encode their aggregate expression into R/G/B image channels rendered at <1 μm²/pixel, enabling STtools RGB plots that resolve cell-type (periportal vs. pericentral hepatocytes, macrophages) and subcellular (nucleus vs. mitochondria) patterns in Seq-Scope mouse liver data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Quantify user-selected marker gene sets in spatial transcriptomics data and encode their aggregate expression into R/G/B image channels rendered at <1 μm²/pixel, enabling STtools RGB plots that resolve cell-type (periportal vs. pericentral hepatocytes, macrophages) and subcellular (nucleus vs. mitochondria) patterns in Seq-Scope mouse liver data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input DGE has already been collapsed into grid-level Seurat objects (Step C1/C2 output), destroying the per-barcode spatial resolution needed for subcellular visualization The goal is cell-type clustering or reference mapping rather than marker geneset visualization — use STtools Steps C1–C3/V2 with the sliding window strategy instead Analysis is at VISIUM (~120 barcodes/mm²) or Slide-seq resolution where per-barcode RGB rendering is unnecessary; lower-resolution feature plotting suffices

skills.description: Use when annotating cells in a novel single-cell dataset (e.g. TMS FACS) using pre-identified marker GEPs from a reference dataset (e.g. MCA) without cell clustering.
skills.name: marker-gep-based-cell-label-transfer
skills.search_text: marker-gep-based-cell-label-transfer Use when annotating cells in a novel single-cell dataset (e.g. TMS FACS) using pre-identified marker GEPs from a reference dataset (e.g. MCA) without cell clustering. The source dataset's cell-type coverage is insufficient for the target (e.g. annotating the Mouse Brain dataset with MCA GEPs, where high-resolution neuronal subtypes are absent) The reference marker GEPs were not generated via SingleCellGGM co-expression analysis and thus lack cell-type-specific expression structure Gene IDs in the novel dataset's count matrix cannot be matched to the GEP gene ID format (Ensembl vs symbol) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CellGEP-based transfer of cell-type labels across single-cell datasets using marker gene expression programs (GEPs) identified in a reference study, enabling annotation of individual cells without clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: CellGEP-based transfer of cell-type labels across single-cell datasets using marker gene expression programs (GEPs) identified in a reference study, enabling annotation of individual cells without clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source dataset's cell-type coverage is insufficient for the target (e.g. annotating the Mouse Brain dataset with MCA GEPs, where high-resolution neuronal subtypes are absent) The reference marker GEPs were not generated via SingleCellGGM co-expression analysis and thus lack cell-type-specific expression structure Gene IDs in the novel dataset's count matrix cannot be matched to the GEP gene ID format (Ensembl vs symbol)

skills.description: Use when building a labeled training set for single-cell annotation without active learning, but prior knowledge of cell type marker genes (e.g. PanglaoDB markers) is available to guide sampling.
skills.name: marker-informed-training-set-construction
skills.search_text: marker-informed-training-set-construction Use when building a labeled training set for single-cell annotation without active learning, but prior knowledge of cell type marker genes (e.g. PanglaoDB markers) is available to guide sampling. No prior marker knowledge exists for the expected cell types — use cluster-based adaptive reweighting or active learning instead The marker file is circular or unreliable, e.g. cell-line markers derived by differential expression between the very cell lines being annotated The goal is to benchmark annotation tools themselves rather than to construct a training set http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs balanced single-cell training sets by clustering all cells (Seurat), assigning each cluster to an expected cell type via user-provided marker genes, and sampling equal numbers of cells per putatively assigned cluster — an adaptive reweighting alternative to active learning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Constructs balanced single-cell training sets by clustering all cells (Seurat), assigning each cluster to an expected cell type via user-provided marker genes, and sampling equal numbers of cells per putatively assigned cluster — an adaptive reweighting alternative to active learning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior marker knowledge exists for the expected cell types — use cluster-based adaptive reweighting or active learning instead The marker file is circular or unreliable, e.g. cell-line markers derived by differential expression between the very cell lines being annotated The goal is to benchmark annotation tools themselves rather than to construct a training set

skills.description: Use when per-cell shape descriptors (autoencoder latent vectors) and per-cell marker quantifications from MIRIAM segmentation must be aligned cell-by-cell and tested for association, e.g. after t-SNE shows no obvious shape-marker patterns.
skills.name: marker-intensity-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: marker-intensity-correlation-analysis Use when per-cell shape descriptors (autoencoder latent vectors) and per-cell marker quantifications from MIRIAM segmentation must be aligned cell-by-cell and tested for association, e.g. after t-SNE shows no obvious shape-marker patterns. Input is only raw image stacks with no MIRIAM segmentation/quantification output yet — run MIRIAM's segmentation, per-cell marker quantification, and autoencoder shape characterization first The goal is shape-based clustering or population discovery itself (t-SNE on latent vectors) rather than statistical testing of shape-marker association Marker and shape tables come from different segmentation runs and cannot be aligned cell-by-cell — correlations would be spurious http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistically tests whether cell shape (encoded as MIRIAM autoencoder latent vectors) corresponds to per-cell marker signal intensity in multiplexed imaging data, via Spearman rank correlation across every latent-dimension x marker pair with multiple-testing correction. Mirrors the MIRIAM paper's negative result for colonic adenoma t-SNE shape analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Statistically tests whether cell shape (encoded as MIRIAM autoencoder latent vectors) corresponds to per-cell marker signal intensity in multiplexed imaging data, via Spearman rank correlation across every latent-dimension x marker pair with multiple-testing correction. Mirrors the MIRIAM paper's negative result for colonic adenoma t-SNE shape analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only raw image stacks with no MIRIAM segmentation/quantification output yet — run MIRIAM's segmentation, per-cell marker quantification, and autoencoder shape characterization first The goal is shape-based clustering or population discovery itself (t-SNE on latent vectors) rather than statistical testing of shape-marker association Marker and shape tables come from different segmentation runs and cannot be aligned cell-by-cell — correlations would be spurious

skills.description: Use when running marker-based cell type identification without a pre-annotated reference dataset and you must assemble cell-type marker lists from Panglao DB or CellMarker DB, choosing how many markers per type.
skills.name: marker-list-curation-from-public-databases
skills.search_text: marker-list-curation-from-public-databases Use when running marker-based cell type identification without a pre-annotated reference dataset and you must assemble cell-type marker lists from Panglao DB or CellMarker DB, choosing how many markers per type. A pre-annotated reference dataset is available and reference-based MarkerCount_Ref() can derive markers via marker score sm,j instead of database curation Cell types of interest are not covered by Panglao DB or CellMarker DB and no expert-curated markers exist (the paper notes taxonomy is not standardized and researchers must prepare their own lists) The analysis uses HiCAT's hierarchical taxonomy directly against its bundled R&D Systems-derived marker file (cell_markers_rndsystems_rev.tsv), which already provides curated markers http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Curate per-cell-type marker gene lists from public marker databases (Panglao DB, CellMarker DB), sized around ~18 markers per cell type, for use in marker-based cell type identification with MarkerCount. List size is a sensitivity-relevant hyper-parameter since MarkerCount fixes N=18 as the marker count per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Curate per-cell-type marker gene lists from public marker databases (Panglao DB, CellMarker DB), sized around ~18 markers per cell type, for use in marker-based cell type identification with MarkerCount. List size is a sensitivity-relevant hyper-parameter since MarkerCount fixes N=18 as the marker count per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A pre-annotated reference dataset is available and reference-based MarkerCount_Ref() can derive markers via marker score sm,j instead of database curation Cell types of interest are not covered by Panglao DB or CellMarker DB and no expert-curated markers exist (the paper notes taxonomy is not standardized and researchers must prepare their own lists) The analysis uses HiCAT's hierarchical taxonomy directly against its bundled R&D Systems-derived marker file (cell_markers_rndsystems_rev.tsv), which already provides curated markers

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or microarray profile with matched survival (event + time-to-event) info and a cell-type marker geneset, and you need directed cell-cell interactions (FDR<0.05) plus per-cell prognostic favorability scores.
skills.name: marker-pair-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: marker-pair-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or microarray profile with matched survival (event + time-to-event) info and a cell-type marker geneset, and you need directed cell-cell interactions (FDR<0.05) plus per-cell prognostic favorability scores. The expression dataset is small or lacks high-quality matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival data to identify prognostic pairs The cell types of interest have very few marker genes — sensitivity to identify a specific interaction is affected by the number of corresponding marker genes The goal is direct ligand-receptor communication from single-cell data rather than prognostic association inferred from bulk co-expression with survival http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 TimiGP's enrichment-based procedure that converts prognostic marker gene pairs (IMGPs) from univariate Cox screening into directed cell-cell interaction calls and per-cell favorability scores, using hypergeometric enrichment plus permutation-based FDR on bulk transcriptomes with matched survival data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: TimiGP's enrichment-based procedure that converts prognostic marker gene pairs (IMGPs) from univariate Cox screening into directed cell-cell interaction calls and per-cell favorability scores, using hypergeometric enrichment plus permutation-based FDR on bulk transcriptomes with matched survival data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression dataset is small or lacks high-quality matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival data to identify prognostic pairs The cell types of interest have very few marker genes — sensitivity to identify a specific interaction is affected by the number of corresponding marker genes The goal is direct ligand-receptor communication from single-cell data rather than prognostic association inferred from bulk co-expression with survival

skills.description: Use when single-cell gene expression data (e.g. scRNA-seq, synthetic multimodal simulations) comes with cell type labels and the goal is to test whether jointly optimized marker panels recover labels better than one-vs-all gene-by-gene scoring.
skills.name: marker-panel-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: marker-panel-benchmark-analysis Use when single-cell gene expression data (e.g. scRNA-seq, synthetic multimodal simulations) comes with cell type labels and the goal is to test whether jointly optimized marker panels recover labels better than one-vs-all gene-by-gene scoring. The data lack categorical cell labels or the goal is to place unlabeled cells on trajectories or spatial locations — scGeneFit only supports categorical labeling. Cell type classes are expected to be non-linearly separable in the low-dimensional marker space; the method assumes linear separability, which is reasonable in high dimensions but may not hold otherwise. Input is already a reduced feature table or a fixed marker panel — the skill benchmarks marker selection on the full gene-by-cell expression matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark scGeneFit's label-aware joint marker selection against one-vs-all marker selection (the strategy used by methods such as COMET) on gene expression data with cellular labels, quantifying per-label classification error and f1 across increasing marker-set sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Benchmark scGeneFit's label-aware joint marker selection against one-vs-all marker selection (the strategy used by methods such as COMET) on gene expression data with cellular labels, quantifying per-label classification error and f1 across increasing marker-set sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack categorical cell labels or the goal is to place unlabeled cells on trajectories or spatial locations — scGeneFit only supports categorical labeling. Cell type classes are expected to be non-linearly separable in the low-dimensional marker space; the method assumes linear separability, which is reasonable in high dimensions but may not hold otherwise. Input is already a reduced feature table or a fixed marker panel — the skill benchmarks marker selection on the full gene-by-cell expression matrix.

skills.description: Use when constructing an initial 10–40 cell training set for single-cell cell-type annotation and a marker gene file (positive/negative markers per expected cell type) is available to guide cell selection.
skills.name: marker-ranked-cell-sampling
skills.search_text: marker-ranked-cell-sampling Use when constructing an initial 10–40 cell training set for single-cell cell-type annotation and a marker gene file (positive/negative markers per expected cell type) is available to guide cell selection. No marker file is available for the expected cell types (e.g. snRNA-Seq markers must come from author communication or PanglaoDB) — use cluster_based mode instead Markers are unreliable or circular, e.g. derived from differential expression between the same cell lines being annotated, or missing due to single-cell dropout Input is a marker-corruption scenario where markers are replaced by random highly expressed genes — accuracy degrades by design http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Marker-aware adaptive reweighting: cluster a single-cell expression dataset, putatively assign each cluster to a known cell type via average marker-gene expression, and sample equal numbers of cells per cluster to build a balanced initial active-learning training set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Marker-aware adaptive reweighting: cluster a single-cell expression dataset, putatively assign each cluster to a known cell type via average marker-gene expression, and sample equal numbers of cells per cluster to build a balanced initial active-learning training set.

skills.description: Use when comparing DE methods (e.g., CDI vs Wilcoxon) for cell-type-specific binary DEGs across scRNA-seq datasets, and you need DEG counts plus per-marker cluster-discriminating sensitivity/specificity benchmarking.
skills.name: marker-sensitivity-specificity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: marker-sensitivity-specificity-benchmarking Use when comparing DE methods (e.g., CDI vs Wilcoxon) for cell-type-specific binary DEGs across scRNA-seq datasets, and you need DEG counts plus per-marker cluster-discriminating sensitivity/specificity benchmarking. Datasets with multiple biological replicates where DE methods that model replicate variation are required — CDI, like other scRNA-seq DE methods, does not account for variation in biological replicates. Single-replicate datasets where clusters may be unstable or spurious (artifact genes in a small subset of cells from one replicate can create distinct clusters), undermining specificity estimates as a benchmark signal. Analysis goals beyond binary cell-type-specific DEG identification (e.g., graded, non-binary differential expression) since CDI is validated specifically for binary DEGs (bDEGs). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks the CDI differential expression method against Wilcoxon for identifying cell-type-specific binary DEGs in scRNA-seq, comparing DEG counts at FDR < 0.05 and top-50 marker cluster specificity via per-marker sensitivity/specificity indices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks the CDI differential expression method against Wilcoxon for identifying cell-type-specific binary DEGs in scRNA-seq, comparing DEG counts at FDR < 0.05 and top-50 marker cluster specificity via per-marker sensitivity/specificity indices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with multiple biological replicates where DE methods that model replicate variation are required — CDI, like other scRNA-seq DE methods, does not account for variation in biological replicates. Analysis goals beyond binary cell-type-specific DEG identification (e.g., graded, non-binary differential expression) since CDI is validated specifically for binary DEGs (bDEGs).

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data from a mixture of two genotypically distinguishable cell populations and need to assign each cell to its genotype from transcriptome SNVs, then validate those assignments against marker-based cell classification.

skills.search_text: marker-vs-genotype-assignment-concordance-analysis Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data from a mixture of two genotypically distinguishable cell populations and need to assign each cell to its genotype from transcriptome SNVs, then validate those assignments against marker-based cell classification.
