skills.description: Use when a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix must be reduced from cell-level random-walk dynamics to attractor-level (cluster-cluster) transition probabilities and soft membership assignments to quantify cell-fate transitions.
skills.name: markov-chain-coarse-graining
skills.search_text: markov-chain-coarse-graining Use when a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix must be reduced from cell-level random-walk dynamics to attractor-level (cluster-cluster) transition probabilities and soft membership assignments to quantify cell-fate transitions. The dataset has very few cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis dataset) and only coarse attractor structure is needed — the article notes special care is required to confirm transition-cell analysis when cell numbers are small The system is strongly non-stationary due to cell-cycle or proliferation dynamics, which MuTrans's stationary, detailed-balance-assuming Markov model does not consider The goal is plain hard clustering without transition dynamics — high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR enforce distinct cell states and are a simpler choice when transient/hybrid cells are not of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Coarse-grain a cell-cell scale random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) into cluster-cluster dynamics by optimizing attractor basins and inter-attractor transition probabilities, then refining soft cell-cluster memberships, as implemented in MuTrans's multi-scale analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Coarse-grain a cell-cell scale random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) into cluster-cluster dynamics by optimizing attractor basins and inter-attractor transition probabilities, then refining soft cell-cluster memberships, as implemented in MuTrans's multi-scale analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has very few cells (e.g. the myelopoiesis dataset) and only coarse attractor structure is needed — the article notes special care is required to confirm transition-cell analysis when cell numbers are small The system is strongly non-stationary due to cell-cycle or proliferation dynamics, which MuTrans's stationary, detailed-balance-assuming Markov model does not consider The goal is plain hard clustering without transition dynamics — high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR enforce distinct cell states and are a simpler choice when transient/hybrid cells are not of interest

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g., a Scanpy/scVelo-preprocessed AnnData with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field) must be converted into stochastic trajectories and fate probabilities toward defined terminal states.
skills.name: markov-chain-trajectory-sampling
skills.search_text: markov-chain-trajectory-sampling Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g., a Scanpy/scVelo-preprocessed AnnData with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field) must be converted into stochastic trajectories and fate probabilities toward defined terminal states. RNA velocity profiles are unreliable or absent and no prior biological knowledge is available to define a differentiation potential (the alternative mode requires prior knowledge, which is difficult to provide e.g. in cancer studies) The goal is transcription factor activity estimation rather than trajectory sampling — that is handled by the downstream tf_activities/linear gene regulation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Samples stochastic cell differentiation trajectories by running a discrete Markov chain on a nearest-neighbor graph whose edges are directed by RNA velocity vectors, yielding fate probabilities and end-fate frequencies from progenitor to terminal cell states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Samples stochastic cell differentiation trajectories by running a discrete Markov chain on a nearest-neighbor graph whose edges are directed by RNA velocity vectors, yielding fate probabilities and end-fate frequencies from progenitor to terminal cell states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: RNA velocity profiles are unreliable or absent and no prior biological knowledge is available to define a differentiation potential (the alternative mode requires prior knowledge, which is difficult to provide e.g. in cancer studies) The goal is transcription factor activity estimation rather than trajectory sampling — that is handled by the downstream tf_activities/linear gene regulation step

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data has reliable spliced/unspliced velocity estimates and the goal is trajectory inference across linear, circular, bifurcated, tree-like, or convergent topologies, especially where static-expression methods fail (e.g., cyclical cell-cycle patterns).
skills.name: markov-chain-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: markov-chain-trajectory-simulation Use when scRNA-seq data has reliable spliced/unspliced velocity estimates and the goal is trajectory inference across linear, circular, bifurcated, tree-like, or convergent topologies, especially where static-expression methods fail (e.g., cyclical cell-cycle patterns). When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that case When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or unrepresentative (e.g., time-dependent degradation rates, single-regime assumption violations), as spurious root/terminal states will be inferred When the input lacks spliced/unspliced layers and no velocity field can be estimated with scvelo http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Cytopath's simulation-based trajectory inference engine: define a Markov chain model from scvelo-derived RNA velocity transition probabilities, simulate an ensemble of differentiation trajectories initialized at root states, and collapse simulations into consensus trajectories via dynamic time warping and per-step averaging. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Cytopath's simulation-based trajectory inference engine: define a Markov chain model from scvelo-derived RNA velocity transition probabilities, simulate an ensemble of differentiation trajectories initialized at root states, and collapse simulations into consensus trajectories via dynamic time warping and per-step averaging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that case When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or unrepresentative (e.g., time-dependent degradation rates, single-regime assumption violations), as spurious root/terminal states will be inferred When the input lacks spliced/unspliced layers and no velocity field can be estimated with scvelo

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be converted into stochastic differentiation trajectories and per-cell fate probabilities, especially when RNA velocity is noisy and a progenitor-defined differentiation potential gradient is available.
skills.name: markov-chain-transition-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: markov-chain-transition-probability-estimation Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be converted into stochastic differentiation trajectories and per-cell fate probabilities, especially when RNA velocity is noisy and a progenitor-defined differentiation potential gradient is available. Data lack cell-type annotations or any basis (robust RNA velocity or prior biological knowledge of progenitors) for defining trajectory direction — differentiation-potential mode depends on prior knowledge that is hard to supply in some cases such as cancer studies The goal is TF activity or differential TF analysis rather than trajectory/fate-probability estimation — the downstream linear model of gene regulation and differential_motif_activity_analysis.m are separate steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Estimate cell-fate transition probabilities by directing the edges of a discrete Markov process on a nearest-neighbor network with RNA velocities or, when velocities are inconclusive, the gradient of differentiation potential from annotated progenitors, producing fate-probability distributions per cell for downstream TF activity inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Estimate cell-fate transition probabilities by directing the edges of a discrete Markov process on a nearest-neighbor network with RNA velocities or, when velocities are inconclusive, the gradient of differentiation potential from annotated progenitors, producing fate-probability distributions per cell for downstream TF activity inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack cell-type annotations or any basis (robust RNA velocity or prior biological knowledge of progenitors) for defining trajectory direction — differentiation-potential mode depends on prior knowledge that is hard to supply in some cases such as cancer studies The goal is TF activity or differential TF analysis rather than trajectory/fate-probability estimation — the downstream linear model of gene regulation and differential_motif_activity_analysis.m are separate steps

skills.description: Use when a weighted gene co-expression or GGM network (e.g., SingleCellGGM SigEdges from the MCA matrix) must be partitioned into gene modules/GEPs under the same MCL parameters across methods for fair comparison.
skills.name: markov-clustering-coexpression-modules
skills.search_text: markov-clustering-coexpression-modules Use when a weighted gene co-expression or GGM network (e.g., SingleCellGGM SigEdges from the MCA matrix) must be partitioned into gene modules/GEPs under the same MCL parameters across methods for fair comparison. The analysis goal is cell-type annotation or label transfer with pre-existing marker GEPs (use CellGEP's average_by_gep/cellgep instead of re-clustering a network) Comparing methods on datasets where each method's clustering parameters differ, making module counts non-comparable The network is a bulk-transcriptome rgsGGM network rather than a single-cell co-expression network under test http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Clusters gene co-expression networks (e.g., the SingleCellGGM GGM network and ppcor/SILGGM benchmark networks built from the MCA dataset) into gene modules via Markov clustering (MCL), treating the modules as gene expression programs (GEPs) that are subsequently scored for gene count and GO enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Clusters gene co-expression networks (e.g., the SingleCellGGM GGM network and ppcor/SILGGM benchmark networks built from the MCA dataset) into gene modules via Markov clustering (MCL), treating the modules as gene expression programs (GEPs) that are subsequently scored for gene count and GO enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is cell-type annotation or label transfer with pre-existing marker GEPs (use CellGEP's average_by_gep/cellgep instead of re-clustering a network) Comparing methods on datasets where each method's clustering parameters differ, making module counts non-comparable The network is a bulk-transcriptome rgsGGM network rather than a single-cell co-expression network under test

skills.description: Use when a large multi-genome protein set (e.g., Prokka-predicted proteins from thousands of RefSeq genomes) must be reduced to functionally coherent gene clusters and an absence/presence matrix for downstream comparative or machine-learning analyses.
skills.name: markov-clustering-gene-family-inference
skills.search_text: markov-clustering-gene-family-inference Use when a large multi-genome protein set (e.g., Prokka-predicted proteins from thousands of RefSeq genomes) must be reduced to functionally coherent gene clusters and an absence/presence matrix for downstream comparative or machine-learning analyses. Input is a small set of genomes where a single-genome orthology tool (e.g., OrthoFinder defaults) is sufficient without linclust pre-clustering Genomes have not passed quality filtering (>90% completeness, <5% contamination by CheckM) and 0.99 ANI redundancy reduction, as redundancy inflates cluster counts The goal is nucleotide-level or strain-level typing rather than protein functional clustering for absence/presence modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Infers functional gene families from pooled protein FASTA files by pre-clustering with MMseqs2 linclust (>90% identity, 80% coverage), aligning cluster representatives all-vs-all with diamond (e-value 1e-5), and running Markov clustering (MCL, inflation 3.0) on the resulting bitscore network, as implemented in the bacLIFE clustering module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Infers functional gene families from pooled protein FASTA files by pre-clustering with MMseqs2 linclust (>90% identity, 80% coverage), aligning cluster representatives all-vs-all with diamond (e-value 1e-5), and running Markov clustering (MCL, inflation 3.0) on the resulting bitscore network, as implemented in the bacLIFE clustering module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a small set of genomes where a single-genome orthology tool (e.g., OrthoFinder defaults) is sufficient without linclust pre-clustering Genomes have not passed quality filtering (>90% completeness, <5% contamination by CheckM) and 0.99 ANI redundancy reduction, as redundancy inflates cluster counts The goal is nucleotide-level or strain-level typing rather than protein functional clustering for absence/presence modeling

skills.description: Use when an scvelo-processed AnnData object with spliced/unspliced counts and a velocity field is available and root/terminal cell states must be identified (or supplied in supervised mode) before running Cytopath trajectory simulations.
skills.name: markov-random-walk-transition-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: markov-random-walk-transition-matrix-construction Use when an scvelo-processed AnnData object with spliced/unspliced counts and a velocity field is available and root/terminal cell states must be identified (or supplied in supervised mode) before running Cytopath trajectory simulations. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect Cytopath trajectory inference to be meaningful, and showed spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset and a simulated dataset with time-dependent degradation rates When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this situation (e.g. hepatocyte zonation, where root cell probability appeared fuzzy with no discernible pattern) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the cell-to-cell transition probability matrix from an RNA velocity field and performs absorbing-state (stationary-state) estimation following La Manno et al. to derive root cell probability (Pr) and terminal cell probability (Pt) for Cytopath's Markov-chain trajectory simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Constructs the cell-to-cell transition probability matrix from an RNA velocity field and performs absorbing-state (stationary-state) estimation following La Manno et al. to derive root cell probability (Pr) and terminal cell probability (Pt) for Cytopath's Markov-chain trajectory simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors do not expect Cytopath trajectory inference to be meaningful, and showed spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset and a simulated dataset with time-dependent degradation rates When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this situation (e.g. hepatocyte zonation, where root cell probability appeared fuzzy with no discernible pattern)

skills.description: Use when a pairwise affinity/similarity matrix over data points must be converted into a diffusion (random-walk) operator, e.g. before eigendecomposition for diffusion map coordinates in a geometry-preserving loss.
skills.name: markov-transition-matrix-normalization
skills.search_text: markov-transition-matrix-normalization Use when a pairwise affinity/similarity matrix over data points must be converted into a diffusion (random-walk) operator, e.g. before eigendecomposition for diffusion map coordinates in a geometry-preserving loss. Input is a raw distance/similarity matrix not yet converted to kernel affinities — the kernel construction (adaptive bandwidth, gradient-passing kernel) must precede normalization The analysis requires a symmetric graph Laplacian (e.g. spectral clustering with normalized cuts) rather than an asymmetric row-stochastic random-walk operator Data points are not samples on a shared manifold (e.g. feature-by-feature tables without meaningful pairwise geometry), since diffusion probabilities would be meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Row-normalizes a pairwise affinity matrix (e.g. the gradient-passing inverse-distance kernel used in scMMGAN) into a Markov chain transition probability matrix P, whose powers Pt model forward diffusion steps on the data manifold for diffusion map embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Row-normalizes a pairwise affinity matrix (e.g. the gradient-passing inverse-distance kernel used in scMMGAN) into a Markov chain transition probability matrix P, whose powers Pt model forward diffusion steps on the data manifold for diffusion map embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw distance/similarity matrix not yet converted to kernel affinities — the kernel construction (adaptive bandwidth, gradient-passing kernel) must precede normalization The analysis requires a symmetric graph Laplacian (e.g. spectral clustering with normalized cuts) rather than an asymmetric row-stochastic random-walk operator Data points are not samples on a shared manifold (e.g. feature-by-feature tables without meaningful pairwise geometry), since diffusion probabilities would be meaningless

skills.description: Use when a raw single-cell gene-count dataset (e.g., MARS-seq myeloid progenitor data with corrupted gene names) must be cleaned and shaped into an N×D expression matrix before DTFLOW trajectory or branch analysis.
skills.name: mars-seq-gene-expression-preprocessing
skills.search_text: mars-seq-gene-expression-preprocessing Use when a raw single-cell gene-count dataset (e.g., MARS-seq myeloid progenitor data with corrupted gene names) must be cleaned and shaped into an N×D expression matrix before DTFLOW trajectory or branch analysis. The input is already a pre-processed gene expression matrix with no corrupted gene names — re-running Scanpy pre-processing and gene removal would be redundant The downstream goal is pseudotime or branch detection itself rather than data preparation — use the DTFLOW transition-matrix, RWR-diffusion, and RSKG branch-detection steps instead The dataset is not a gene-level single-cell expression table (e.g., already PCA-reduced embeddings), since the DTFLOW constructor expects raw_df as an N cells × D genes count matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepares a raw MARS-seq single-cell count dataset (e.g., the mouse myeloid progenitor dataset of 2730 cells × 3451 informative genes) into a cleaned cells×genes expression matrix by applying Scanpy pre-processing, including removal of the 10 genes with corrupted names, as the entry step of the DTFLOW pseudotime workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Prepares a raw MARS-seq single-cell count dataset (e.g., the mouse myeloid progenitor dataset of 2730 cells × 3451 informative genes) into a cleaned cells×genes expression matrix by applying Scanpy pre-processing, including removal of the 10 genes with corrupted names, as the entry step of the DTFLOW pseudotime workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a pre-processed gene expression matrix with no corrupted gene names — re-running Scanpy pre-processing and gene removal would be redundant The downstream goal is pseudotime or branch detection itself rather than data preparation — use the DTFLOW transition-matrix, RWR-diffusion, and RSKG branch-detection steps instead The dataset is not a gene-level single-cell expression table (e.g., already PCA-reduced embeddings), since the DTFLOW constructor expects raw_df as an N cells × D genes count matrix

skills.description: Use when comparing imputation methods (LATE, TRANSLATE, DCA, scVI, SAVER, MAGIC, ALRA, scImpute) on masked scRNA-seq data (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) with an unmasked ground truth available for error quantification.
skills.name: masked-data-ground-truth-mse-evaluation
skills.search_text: masked-data-ground-truth-mse-evaluation Use when comparing imputation methods (LATE, TRANSLATE, DCA, scVI, SAVER, MAGIC, ALRA, scImpute) on masked scRNA-seq data (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) with an unmasked ground truth available for error quantification. The goal is cell-type separation quality (BCSS/WCSS after t-SNE on labeled data like PBMC_G949_10K) rather than imputation accuracy against a ground truth The imputed matrix is not on the same log10(count+1) scale as the ground truth, since MSE values are not comparable across scales Only one imputation method is available and no baseline comparison (DCA, scVI, SAVER, MAGIC, ALRA, scImpute) is possible http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation accuracy by computing mean squared error (MSE) of imputed matrices against ground truth on masked datasets, and gtMSE on real datasets without ground truth, following the LATE/TRANSLATE paper's Supplementary Table S3 design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation accuracy by computing mean squared error (MSE) of imputed matrices against ground truth on masked datasets, and gtMSE on real datasets without ground truth, following the LATE/TRANSLATE paper's Supplementary Table S3 design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-type separation quality (BCSS/WCSS after t-SNE on labeled data like PBMC_G949_10K) rather than imputation accuracy against a ground truth The imputed matrix is not on the same log10(count+1) scale as the ground truth, since MSE values are not comparable across scales Only one imputation method is available and no baseline comparison (DCA, scVI, SAVER, MAGIC, ALRA, scImpute) is possible

skills.description: Use when building the GRouNdGAN/CausalGAN generator stack — instantiating per-target-gene masked generators from a pickled causal graph and pretraining the controller before the 1,000,000-step Wasserstein GAN training run.
skills.name: masked-fully-connected-generator-construction
skills.search_text: masked-fully-connected-generator-construction Use when building the GRouNdGAN/CausalGAN generator stack — instantiating per-target-gene masked generators from a pickled causal graph and pretraining the controller before the 1,000,000-step Wasserstein GAN training run. The GRN you want to impose is multi-layer (TF-gene-phenotype causal graph) — the current version only supports bipartite GRNs You need unnormalized count data — the model currently only generates library-size normalized expression values You need a predictive model of knockout outcomes for a new dataset rather than a generative model — GRouNdGAN must be retrained for new data and is not predictive http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs the causal core of GRouNdGAN: a causal controller plus one fully connected target generator per target gene, whose input connectivity is masked by a user-provided causal GRN so simulated scRNA-seq expression obeys the imposed TF-gene regulatory structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Constructs the causal core of GRouNdGAN: a causal controller plus one fully connected target generator per target gene, whose input connectivity is masked by a user-provided causal GRN so simulated scRNA-seq expression obeys the imposed TF-gene regulatory structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GRN you want to impose is multi-layer (TF-gene-phenotype causal graph) — the current version only supports bipartite GRNs You need unnormalized count data — the model currently only generates library-size normalized expression values You need a predictive model of knockout outcomes for a new dataset rather than a generative model — GRouNdGAN must be retrained for new data and is not predictive

skills.description: Use when building an interpretable Transformer-based cell-type annotation model where input genes must be grouped into biologically relevant pathway tokens (from .gmt files such as GO_bp.gmt or reactome.gmt) before self-attention.
skills.name: masked-gene-to-pathway-embedding
skills.search_text: masked-gene-to-pathway-embedding Use when building an interpretable Transformer-based cell-type annotation model where input genes must be grouped into biologically relevant pathway tokens (from .gmt files such as GO_bp.gmt or reactome.gmt) before self-attention. Query and reference AnnData var_names differ or are not in the same order — the embedding assumes identical gene ordering (use query_adata = query_adata[:, ref_adata.var_names] first). You need a dimensionality-reducing autoencoder latent space; TOSICA deliberately avoids dimensionality reduction to keep attention traceable. No biologically relevant gene-set resource (.gmt mask) is available for the species or feature space of the data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Embed the expression of n input genes into k pathway tokens via a masked linear transformation (W' = W*M), where the mask matrix is derived from a GSEA .gmt gene-set file, as the first layer of TOSICA's Transformer cell-type annotation model. This keeps every attention layer traceable to original gene features, enabling interpretable annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Embed the expression of n input genes into k pathway tokens via a masked linear transformation (W' = W*M), where the mask matrix is derived from a GSEA .gmt gene-set file, as the first layer of TOSICA's Transformer cell-type annotation model. This keeps every attention layer traceable to original gene features, enabling interpretable annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query and reference AnnData var_names differ or are not in the same order — the embedding assumes identical gene ordering (use query_adata = query_adata[:, ref_adata.var_names] first). You need a dimensionality-reducing autoencoder latent space; TOSICA deliberately avoids dimensionality reduction to keep attention traceable. No biologically relevant gene-set resource (.gmt mask) is available for the species or feature space of the data.

skills.description: Use when constructing the basic scButterfly-B encoder/decoder stack for paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq translation and dropout noise must be denoised without data augmentation.
skills.name: masked-input-encoder-construction
skills.search_text: masked-input-encoder-construction Use when constructing the basic scButterfly-B encoder/decoder stack for paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq translation and dropout noise must be denoised without data augmentation. The goal is scButterfly-T or scButterfly-C, which rely on cell-type or MultiVI data augmentation rather than the basic masked-encoder architecture (aug_type must be None for scButterfly-B). Training on unpaired data with diagonal strategies, which requires the scButterfly extension for unpaired training rather than the standard paired-input masked encoders. Modalities other than RNA/ATAC/ADT single-cell count matrices, e.g., spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C, which are named as future directions not yet supported. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Build the fixed seven-module scButterfly-B network whose variational encoders apply modality-specific random input masking (50% for RNA, 30% for ATAC) to alleviate dropout-driven false zeros while keeping the model parameter-efficient via pruned inter-chromosomal ATAC connections. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Build the fixed seven-module scButterfly-B network whose variational encoders apply modality-specific random input masking (50% for RNA, 30% for ATAC) to alleviate dropout-driven false zeros while keeping the model parameter-efficient via pruned inter-chromosomal ATAC connections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is scButterfly-T or scButterfly-C, which rely on cell-type or MultiVI data augmentation rather than the basic masked-encoder architecture (aug_type must be None for scButterfly-B). Training on unpaired data with diagonal strategies, which requires the scButterfly extension for unpaired training rather than the standard paired-input masked encoders. Modalities other than RNA/ATAC/ADT single-cell count matrices, e.g., spatial transcriptomics or single-cell Hi-C, which are named as future directions not yet supported.

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) must be deconvolved into >400 cell-type abundances and an interpretable, marker-gene-masked network is needed instead of black-box deconvolution methods.
skills.name: masked-neural-network-architecture-construction
skills.search_text: masked-neural-network-architecture-construction Use when bulk RNA-seq samples (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) must be deconvolved into >400 cell-type abundances and an interpretable, marker-gene-masked network is needed instead of black-box deconvolution methods. The goal is estimating a small predefined panel of cell types (e.g. 6–7 immune subsets) where CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER or xCell already suffice Input expression rows are not human gene symbols or the matrix cannot be aligned to the 9078 marker-gene index in index.pkl No gene–cell relation matrix is available, since masking each hidden neuron to its marker genes is the core interpretability mechanism http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Constructs DCNet, an explainable three-layer mxnet/gluon neural network (9078 input genes → 434 cell-type hidden neurons → 21136 output genes) whose input-to-hidden weights are element-wise masked by a gene–cell zero-one relation matrix, so the latent layer's activation directly encodes 434 cell-type abundances from bulk RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Constructs DCNet, an explainable three-layer mxnet/gluon neural network (9078 input genes → 434 cell-type hidden neurons → 21136 output genes) whose input-to-hidden weights are element-wise masked by a gene–cell zero-one relation matrix, so the latent layer's activation directly encodes 434 cell-type abundances from bulk RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is estimating a small predefined panel of cell types (e.g. 6–7 immune subsets) where CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER or xCell already suffice Input expression rows are not human gene symbols or the matrix cannot be aligned to the 9078 marker-gene index in index.pkl No gene–cell relation matrix is available, since masking each hidden neuron to its marker genes is the core interpretability mechanism

skills.description: Use when inferring cell-state specific communication probabilities from scRNA-seq cell groups or continuous pseudotime states (e.g., E14.5 embryonic skin) and statistically testing which L-R pairs are significant.
skills.name: mass-action-signaling-probability-modeling
skills.search_text: mass-action-signaling-probability-modeling Use when inferring cell-state specific communication probabilities from scRNA-seq cell groups or continuous pseudotime states (e.g., E14.5 embryonic skin) and statistically testing which L-R pairs are significant. Input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell resolution communication — use Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) instead No cell clustering or pseudotime state labels exist yet — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis The target signaling events depend on protein-level abundance rather than mRNA proxies — CellChat approximates protein level with mRNA http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 Model ligand-receptor mediated signaling in CellChat using a Hill function under the law of mass action, with trimean-based ensemble average expression and a permutation test (M=100, p<0.05) to call significant cell-cell communications. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Model ligand-receptor mediated signaling in CellChat using a Hill function under the law of mass action, with trimean-based ensemble average expression and a permutation test (M=100, p<0.05) to call significant cell-cell communications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell resolution communication — use Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) instead No cell clustering or pseudotime state labels exist yet — cell clustering is a pre-requisite for CellChat analysis The target signaling events depend on protein-level abundance rather than mRNA proxies — CellChat approximates protein level with mRNA

skills.description: Use when evaluating a clustering algorithm on mass cytometry data with known cell-type ground truth, or when comparing a new method to specialized cytometry clustering tools on the Levine15_13/Levine15_32/Samusik16 benchmarks.
skills.name: mass-cytometry-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: mass-cytometry-clustering-benchmarking Use when evaluating a clustering algorithm on mass cytometry data with known cell-type ground truth, or when comparing a new method to specialized cytometry clustering tools on the Levine15_13/Levine15_32/Samusik16 benchmarks. Input is unlabeled data with no ground-truth population annotations — accuracy/NMI/ARI against y_true cannot be computed Data is scRNA-seq rather than mass cytometry — use the paper's scRNA-seq benchmarks (Li17, Lawlor17, Zeisel15) and their preprocessing/filtering instead Dataset is too large to run 10 resamples of 20,000 cells and full k scanning — the sampling-based extension with smaller cores (e.g. 5,000 cells) is the appropriate approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Benchmarks a general-purpose clustering method (e.g. KMD clustering) against specialized mass cytometry algorithms (Xshift, DEPECHE, Accense, FlowSOM) and general-purpose ones (kmeans, PhenoGraph) on the Levine15_13, Levine15_32 and Samusik16 bone marrow datasets, scoring accuracy, NMI and ARI against ground-truth cell-population labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks a general-purpose clustering method (e.g. KMD clustering) against specialized mass cytometry algorithms (Xshift, DEPECHE, Accense, FlowSOM) and general-purpose ones (kmeans, PhenoGraph) on the Levine15_13, Levine15_32 and Samusik16 bone marrow datasets, scoring accuracy, NMI and ARI against ground-truth cell-population labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unlabeled data with no ground-truth population annotations — accuracy/NMI/ARI against y_true cannot be computed Data is scRNA-seq rather than mass cytometry — use the paper's scRNA-seq benchmarks (Li17, Lawlor17, Zeisel15) and their preprocessing/filtering instead Dataset is too large to run 10 resamples of 20,000 cells and full k scanning — the sampling-based extension with smaller cores (e.g. 5,000 cells) is the appropriate approach

skills.description: Use when a proteomic (CyTOF/mass cytometry) time-series single-cell dataset annotated with sampling-day labels needs pseudotime ordering, or when benchmarking whether lazy-teleporting MCMC (memory) improves pseudotime over TI baselines.
skills.name: mass-cytometry-pseudotime-inference
skills.search_text: mass-cytometry-pseudotime-inference Use when a proteomic (CyTOF/mass cytometry) time-series single-cell dataset annotated with sampling-day labels needs pseudotime ordering, or when benchmarking whether lazy-teleporting MCMC (memory) improves pseudotime over TI baselines. Input is scRNA-seq or an already-computed pseudotime; this skill targets proteomic CyTOF data with true day labels The goal is topology/lineage discovery without any time-point labels to validate against — the Pearson-vs-days metric cannot be computed Data requires no ablation question (i.e., you are not testing the lazy-teleporting MCMC's contribution against memory=1 or TI baselines) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers developmental pseudotime on mass cytometry (CyTOF) time-series data using VIA's lazy-teleporting MCMC random walks, and quantifies accuracy by Pearson correlation of inferred pseudotime against annotated sampling days (~0.88 on mESC CyTOF). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Infers developmental pseudotime on mass cytometry (CyTOF) time-series data using VIA's lazy-teleporting MCMC random walks, and quantifies accuracy by Pearson correlation of inferred pseudotime against annotated sampling days (~0.88 on mESC CyTOF).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scRNA-seq or an already-computed pseudotime; this skill targets proteomic CyTOF data with true day labels The goal is topology/lineage discovery without any time-point labels to validate against — the Pearson-vs-days metric cannot be computed Data requires no ablation question (i.e., you are not testing the lazy-teleporting MCMC's contribution against memory=1 or TI baselines)

skills.description: Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData with an ICAT-upweighted matrix (adata.obsm['X_icat']) and need to verify which weighted marker genes are differentially expressed between treatment groups.
skills.name: mast-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: mast-differential-expression-analysis Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData with an ICAT-upweighted matrix (adata.obsm['X_icat']) and need to verify which weighted marker genes are differentially expressed between treatment groups. Input data has not been processed by ICAT and no weighted gene list exists — DE on unweighted genes does not test the marker-stability assumption The goal is de novo cell-state discovery rather than validating differential expression of a predefined gene set — use the ICAT clustering workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit MAST hurdle models to test ICAT-weighted marker genes for differential expression between control and perturbed (MK-886) treatments, testing the assumption that ICAT-selected marker genes remain stably expressed across conditions. Outputs a DE results table used to validate marker gene stability against Supplementary Fig. S12. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Fit MAST hurdle models to test ICAT-weighted marker genes for differential expression between control and perturbed (MK-886) treatments, testing the assumption that ICAT-selected marker genes remain stably expressed across conditions. Outputs a DE results table used to validate marker gene stability against Supplementary Fig. S12.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been processed by ICAT and no weighted gene list exists — DE on unweighted genes does not test the marker-stability assumption The goal is de novo cell-state discovery rather than validating differential expression of a predefined gene set — use the ICAT clustering workflow instead

skills.name: master-regulator-analysis-with-rtn
skills.search_text: master-regulator-analysis-with-rtn Use when you need cell-type-specific master regulators (tTFs) from time-course scRNA-seq — e.g., to pair TF activity with inferred ligand-receptor signaling along an early-embryo developmental trajectory. Your goal is cell-cell communication between definitive cell types rather than temporal TF identification — TimeTalk's downstream RunTimeTalk / CellPhoneDB / CellChat-style analysis is the wrong fit here and vice versa: MRA alone does not infer ligand-receptor interactions You lack cell-type/cluster identities or a reconstructed trajectory: the workflow depends on per-cell-type TRNs and trajectory-variable genes (monocle2 differentialGeneTest qval = 0.01) as the MRA phenotype Your expression matrix is raw counts without per-stage/pseudo-bulk processing compatible with the RTN 'tni' object built from log10(RPKM + 1)-normalized data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies temporal transcription factors (tTFs) from integrated pre-implantation scRNA-seq by running RTN master regulator analysis (tna.mra) on cell-type-specific transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), then hierarchically clustering regulators (ward.D2, six clusters C1–C6). In TimeTalk this is the by-product step that links eLR signaling to TF activity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2

skills.description: Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available for the same cell population and the goal is to test whether bulk signalling entropy exceeds what random single-cell sampling would explain, i.e. regulated heterogeneity.
skills.name: matched-bulk-single-cell-comparison
skills.search_text: matched-bulk-single-cell-comparison Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available for the same cell population and the goal is to test whether bulk signalling entropy exceeds what random single-cell sampling would explain, i.e. regulated heterogeneity. Only a bulk-average profile is available with no matched single cells — the bulk-average control itself is expected to be non-significant (P approximately 0.30), so MRH significance cannot be assessed The goal is ordering cells by differentiation potency in pseudo-time; SCENT alone (or alternatives like Monocle, MPath, StemID, SLICE) is the appropriate framing rather than a bulk-vs-single-cell MRH test Single-cell and bulk data are not matched to the same cell population, since the z-score is defined against the matched population's single-cell SR distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies regulated single-cell expression heterogeneity (the measure of regulated heterogeneity, MRH) by testing whether the SCENT signalling entropy (SR) of a bulk RNA-Seq sample deviates significantly above the single-cell SR distribution computed from matched individual cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Quantifies regulated single-cell expression heterogeneity (the measure of regulated heterogeneity, MRH) by testing whether the SCENT signalling entropy (SR) of a bulk RNA-Seq sample deviates significantly above the single-cell SR distribution computed from matched individual cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a bulk-average profile is available with no matched single cells — the bulk-average control itself is expected to be non-significant (P approximately 0.30), so MRH significance cannot be assessed The goal is ordering cells by differentiation potency in pseudo-time; SCENT alone (or alternatives like Monocle, MPath, StemID, SLICE) is the appropriate framing rather than a bulk-vs-single-cell MRH test Single-cell and bulk data are not matched to the same cell population, since the z-score is defined against the matched population's single-cell SR distribution

skills.description: Use when you need to test, edge by edge, whether knocking out a regulating TF via GRouNdGAN's --perturb mode significantly changes the expression of each gene it regulates in an imposed GRN.
skills.name: matched-case-control-expression-testing
skills.search_text: matched-case-control-expression-testing Use when you need to test, edge by edge, whether knocking out a regulating TF via GRouNdGAN's --perturb mode significantly changes the expression of each gene it regulates in an imposed GRN. You want to predict TF knockout outcomes in real (non-simulated) cells — the paper notes this would require a high-quality GRN plus additional data modalities such as (sc)ATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq Your imposed GRN is multi-layer or includes TF-gene-phenotype edges — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN The task is quality assessment of simulated data or GRN-inference benchmarking rather than interventional significance testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies whether in silico TF knockout in GRouNdGAN-simulated cells significantly alters target gene expression, by comparing matched perturbed vs. unperturbed cells with two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction over TF-gene edges. It validates that the user-imposed causal GRN is actually realized in the simulated data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Quantifies whether in silico TF knockout in GRouNdGAN-simulated cells significantly alters target gene expression, by comparing matched perturbed vs. unperturbed cells with two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction over TF-gene edges. It validates that the user-imposed causal GRN is actually realized in the simulated data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to predict TF knockout outcomes in real (non-simulated) cells — the paper notes this would require a high-quality GRN plus additional data modalities such as (sc)ATAC-seq or TF ChIP-seq Your imposed GRN is multi-layer or includes TF-gene-phenotype edges — the current GRouNdGAN version only supports imposing a bipartite GRN The task is quality assessment of simulated data or GRN-inference benchmarking rather than interventional significance testing

skills.description: Use when a subset of individuals has both bulk RNA-seq and single-cell/scRNA-seq measurements (use.overlap=TRUE), so gene-specific bulk transformations can be learned from matched pairs before decomposition.
skills.name: matched-pairs-linear-regression
skills.search_text: matched-pairs-linear-regression Use when a subset of individuals has both bulk RNA-seq and single-cell/scRNA-seq measurements (use.overlap=TRUE), so gene-specific bulk transformations can be learned from matched pairs before decomposition. No individuals have matched bulk and single-cell measurements — use the semisupervised shrinkage-variance transform (SemisupervisedTransformBulk, use.overlap=FALSE) instead of the supervised fit. Only a set of known marker genes is available and no single-cell reference exists — use marker-based decomposition (BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition) instead. Very few individuals have single-cell data — the article warns the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Per-gene supervised linear regression on matched bulk/single-cell samples: regress bulk gene expression on single-cell-derived cell-type proportions across the overlapping individuals to learn gene-specific coefficients that map the single-cell reference profile to the bulk expression scale, correcting technical biases between the two technologies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Per-gene supervised linear regression on matched bulk/single-cell samples: regress bulk gene expression on single-cell-derived cell-type proportions across the overlapping individuals to learn gene-specific coefficients that map the single-cell reference profile to the bulk expression scale, correcting technical biases between the two technologies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No individuals have matched bulk and single-cell measurements — use the semisupervised shrinkage-variance transform (SemisupervisedTransformBulk, use.overlap=FALSE) instead of the supervised fit. Only a set of known marker genes is available and no single-cell reference exists — use marker-based decomposition (BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition) instead. Very few individuals have single-cell data — the article warns the reference profile and gene-specific transformations may become unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a pipeline has dual implementations (e.g., Matlab and Python) and you must verify they yield similar segmentations on identical image inputs before deploying either version for downstream quantification.
skills.name: matlab-python-pipeline-equivalence-testing
skills.search_text: matlab-python-pipeline-equivalence-testing Use when a pipeline has dual implementations (e.g., Matlab and Python) and you must verify they yield similar segmentations on identical image inputs before deploying either version for downstream quantification. Input is a single-implementation pipeline with no second codebase to compare against — there is nothing to test equivalence on. The goal is validating segmentation accuracy against ground-truth annotations (accuracy benchmarking, e.g., MIRIAM vs. Mesmer vs. Voronoi DSC of 0.65/0.59/0.32), not inter-implementation agreement. Image stacks differ between the two runs (different TMA cores or markers) — equivalence testing requires identical inputs for both implementations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Cross-implementation equivalence testing of a segmentation pipeline: running both the Matlab and Python implementations of MIRIAM on identical manually annotated multiplexed immunofluorescence TMA core image stacks and quantifying membrane segmentation agreement with Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Cross-implementation equivalence testing of a segmentation pipeline: running both the Matlab and Python implementations of MIRIAM on identical manually annotated multiplexed immunofluorescence TMA core image stacks and quantifying membrane segmentation agreement with Dice (DSC) and Jaccard (JSC) similarity coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-implementation pipeline with no second codebase to compare against — there is nothing to test equivalence on. The goal is validating segmentation accuracy against ground-truth annotations (accuracy benchmarking, e.g., MIRIAM vs. Mesmer vs. Voronoi DSC of 0.65/0.59/0.32), not inter-implementation agreement. Image stacks differ between the two runs (different TMA cores or markers) — equivalence testing requires identical inputs for both implementations.

skills.description: Use when screening endogenous reference genes over a large gene expression matrix (thousands of genes, e.g. GSE125792) and full-matrix pairwise computation would be too slow or depth-3+ screening risks no result.
skills.name: matrix-block-computation
skills.search_text: matrix-block-computation Use when screening endogenous reference genes over a large gene expression matrix (thousands of genes, e.g. GSE125792) and full-matrix pairwise computation would be too slow or depth-3+ screening risks no result. Normalization of a specific known gene is the goal — use ERgene.normalizationdata instead; single-gene standardization is documented as undesirable and should be used with caution per MIQE guidance The expression matrix is small enough that full-matrix screening is fast — blocking adds no benefit and depth 3+ already declines in efficiency Computational depth is set too large — the paper warns there may be no result at all http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 ERgene's robust matrix block operation partitions large gene expression DataFrames into blocks of 1000 genes so the inverse internal-reference screening (variance of relative factor change) stays computationally efficient. It is the mechanism that lets FindERG screen datasets like GSE125792 (1968 genes) in seconds at computational depth 2 or 3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-75586-5

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (exp.txt gene-by-cell matrix plus metadata.txt cell labels) for cell-cell communication in species beyond human/mouse, or when no prior L-R database should constrain the inference.
skills.name: matrix-decomposition-cell-cell-communication-inference
skills.search_text: matrix-decomposition-cell-cell-communication-inference Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (exp.txt gene-by-cell matrix plus metadata.txt cell labels) for cell-cell communication in species beyond human/mouse, or when no prior L-R database should constrain the inference. The input lacks existing cell classification labels (MDIC3 infers communication from individual cells to cell types based on existing labels; users are also advised to include at least 10 cells). The analysis must be grounded in a curated ligand-receptor database as the primary evidence; in that case L-R-coexpression methods such as CellChat, CellPhoneDB, or iTALK are the appropriate choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 MDIC3 infers cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq by factorizing the gene expression matrix A into R*Sigma*W, where R is a gene regulatory network (GRN) adjacency matrix computed with GNIPLR, and interpreting W's elements as directed communication strengths — independent of ligand-receptor databases and applicable to any species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: MDIC3 infers cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq by factorizing the gene expression matrix A into R*Sigma*W, where R is a gene regulatory network (GRN) adjacency matrix computed with GNIPLR, and interpreting W's elements as directed communication strengths — independent of ligand-receptor databases and applicable to any species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks existing cell classification labels (MDIC3 infers communication from individual cells to cell types based on existing labels; users are also advised to include at least 10 cells). The analysis must be grounded in a curated ligand-receptor database as the primary evidence; in that case L-R-coexpression methods such as CellChat, CellPhoneDB, or iTALK are the appropriate choice.

skills.description: Use when comparing the runtime of dense matrix multiplication across R backends (%*%, RcppArmadillo, RcppEigen) with varying OpenMP core counts, or when justifying a faster backend for a computationally heavy R linear-algebra routine.
skills.name: matrix-multiplication-benchmarking
skills.search_text: matrix-multiplication-benchmarking Use when comparing the runtime of dense matrix multiplication across R backends (%*%, RcppArmadillo, RcppEigen) with varying OpenMP core counts, or when justifying a faster backend for a computationally heavy R linear-algebra routine. The analysis goal is batch-effect correction or decomposition of scRNA-seq data (e.g., running jive/bic.jive with cores set for the JIVE estimator) rather than timing a linear-algebra kernel itself. The matrices are not dense matrix multiplication workloads (e.g., I/O-bound tasks or sparse operations), where the %*%-vs-C++ speedup metric is not meaningful. OpenMP is unavailable, so the 1/2/4/8-core parallel configurations cannot be compiled or evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A reproducible R benchmarking procedure that times R's built-in %*% operator against RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen matrix-multiplication backends compiled via Rcpp with OpenMP at 1, 2, 4, and 8 cores, quantifying percentage speedup over the single-threaded baseline. This is the kind of computational-efficiency validation used to justify fast C++ backends for heavy linear algebra such as the JIVE decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: A reproducible R benchmarking procedure that times R's built-in %*% operator against RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen matrix-multiplication backends compiled via Rcpp with OpenMP at 1, 2, 4, and 8 cores, quantifying percentage speedup over the single-threaded baseline. This is the kind of computational-efficiency validation used to justify fast C++ backends for heavy linear algebra such as the JIVE decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is batch-effect correction or decomposition of scRNA-seq data (e.g., running jive/bic.jive with cores set for the JIVE estimator) rather than timing a linear-algebra kernel itself. The matrices are not dense matrix multiplication workloads (e.g., I/O-bound tasks or sparse operations), where the %*%-vs-C++ speedup metric is not meaningful. OpenMP is unavailable, so the 1/2/4/8-core parallel configurations cannot be compiled or evaluated.

Downstream tasks require properly log-transformed expression data — SiFT's correction modifies gene expression so the data is no longer properly log-transformed No reliable prior knowledge or annotation exists to define the cell–cell similarity kernel — an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal The goal is integration or correction at a joint latent representation level (e.g., scVI-style models) rather than correction at the gene expression level http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Kernel-based projection filtering for single-cell gene expression data: a cell–cell similarity kernel encoding the signal to remove is built with SiFT, the count matrix is projected onto it, and the projection is deducted (X~ = X − K·X) with a pseudocount correction, filtering unwanted variation at the gene expression level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7

skills.description: Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv) and need the normalized ground-truth adjacency matrix that STEM's predictors are trained to reconstruct from embeddings.
skills.name: matrix-row-normalization
skills.search_text: matrix-row-normalization Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv) and need the normalized ground-truth adjacency matrix that STEM's predictors are trained to reconstruct from embeddings. You need the SC-ST or ST-SC mapping matrices rather than the ground-truth spot adjacency — those come from softmax over embedding dot products (netst2sc/netsc2sc), not from coordinates. The spot coordinates are unavailable or unreliable (e.g. you only have expression matrices) — the Gaussian kernel requires true spatial coordinates. Constructs the row-normalized N x N spatial adjacency matrix that serves as STEM's ground-truth prediction target, by applying a Gaussian kernel exp(-d_ij^2/(2*sigma^2)) to pairwise Euclidean distances between ST spot coordinates. Row-normalization makes each spot's adjacency weights sum to 1 so they act as probability distributions supervising STEM's adjacency predictors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Constructs the row-normalized N x N spatial adjacency matrix that serves as STEM's ground-truth prediction target, by applying a Gaussian kernel exp(-d_ij^2/(2*sigma^2)) to pairwise Euclidean distances between ST spot coordinates. Row-normalization makes each spot's adjacency weights sum to 1 so they act as probability distributions supervising STEM's adjacency predictors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the SC-ST or ST-SC mapping matrices rather than the ground-truth spot adjacency — those come from softmax over embedding dot products (netst2sc/netsc2sc), not from coordinates. skills.name: matrix-singularity-removal
skills.search_text: matrix-singularity-removal Use when supplying a gene-by-geneset or TF-gene prior matrix (e.g., 'C_dorothea_tf_human.refined.rds') to a model like GEDI that requires a full-rank C, and singularity must be eliminated before model fitting. The prior matrix is already full rank (QR rank equals column count) — truncation is a no-op and reordering may be unnecessary The downstream method accepts rank-deficient priors or uses regularization that handles collinearity without requiring full rank http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Removes linearly dependent (singular) columns from a prior knowledge matrix (e.g., the DoRothEA-derived TF-gene matrix C used in GEDI) via QR decomposition so downstream latent-variable models can be fitted without numerical failure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Removes linearly dependent (singular) columns from a prior knowledge matrix (e.g., the DoRothEA-derived TF-gene matrix C used in GEDI) via QR decomposition so downstream latent-variable models can be fitted without numerical failure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The prior matrix is already full rank (QR rank equals column count) — truncation is a no-op and reordering may be unnecessary The downstream method accepts rank-deficient priors or uses regularization that handles collinearity without requiring full rank

skills.description: Use when you need to transform a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix into a pathway-by-cell activity score matrix via SVD (PC1 per pathway) and empirically verify that the pathway-level representation is less sparse than the gene-level matrix.
skills.name: matrix-sparsity-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: matrix-sparsity-comparison-analysis Use when you need to transform a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix into a pathway-by-cell activity score matrix via SVD (PC1 per pathway) and empirically verify that the pathway-level representation is less sparse than the gene-level matrix. The goal is per-gene differential expression or gene-level trait association rather than pathway-level activity summarization — the SVD PC1 collapse discards individual gene resolution. The scRNA-seq matrix is raw/unnormalized counts — the SVD-based PAS computation assumes LogNormalize normalization with scale.factor = 10000 has been applied first. Pathway definitions other than KEGG are required and cannot be recast into the 5–300 gene size range expected by min.pathway.size/max.pathway.size filtering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Reconstructs scPagwas's pathway activation transformation — computing the SVD-based first principal component (PAS) of each KEGG pathway's gene-by-cell sub-matrix — and quantitatively compares zero-entry fractions between the normalized gene-level matrix and the resulting pathway-by-cell PAS matrix to demonstrate reduced sparsity and technical noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Reconstructs scPagwas's pathway activation transformation — computing the SVD-based first principal component (PAS) of each KEGG pathway's gene-by-cell sub-matrix — and quantitatively compares zero-entry fractions between the normalized gene-level matrix and the resulting pathway-by-cell PAS matrix to demonstrate reduced sparsity and technical noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-gene differential expression or gene-level trait association rather than pathway-level activity summarization — the SVD PC1 collapse discards individual gene resolution. The scRNA-seq matrix is raw/unnormalized counts — the SVD-based PAS computation assumes LogNormalize normalization with scale.factor = 10000 has been applied first. Pathway definitions other than KEGG are required and cannot be recast into the 5–300 gene size range expected by min.pathway.size/max.pathway.size filtering.

skills.description: Use when Leiden cluster labels are already available from the first-stage scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph and you need per-cluster, per-modality marker scores (genes, ATAC regions, proteins) to annotate cell types.
skills.name: matrix-tri-factorization-retraining
skills.search_text: matrix-tri-factorization-retraining Use when Leiden cluster labels are already available from the first-stage scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph and you need per-cluster, per-modality marker scores (genes, ATAC regions, proteins) to annotate cell types. Clusters have not yet been computed — this skill requires labels_leiden from the first-stage KNN graph and Leiden clustering; without them there are no fixed cell factors to condition retraining on. Only an integrated cell embedding is needed — first-stage training and extract_cell_factors() alone suffice; retraining is required specifically for cluster-specific feature scoring. The counts matrices have not been preprocessed with utils.preprocess() or features have not been matched across batches (gene intersection / peak remapping) — retraining assumes aligned feature sets per modality. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Second-stage scMoMaT retraining that encodes Leiden cluster labels as fixed binary cell factors and re-optimizes feature factors and association matrices via matrix tri-factorization, yielding per-cluster multi-modal bio-marker score matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Second-stage scMoMaT retraining that encodes Leiden cluster labels as fixed binary cell factors and re-optimizes feature factors and association matrices via matrix tri-factorization, yielding per-cluster multi-modal bio-marker score matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters have not yet been computed — this skill requires labels_leiden from the first-stage KNN graph and Leiden clustering; without them there are no fixed cell factors to condition retraining on. Only an integrated cell embedding is needed — first-stage training and extract_cell_factors() alone suffice; retraining is required specifically for cluster-specific feature scoring. The counts matrices have not been preprocessed with utils.preprocess() or features have not been matched across batches (gene intersection / peak remapping) — retraining assumes aligned feature sets per modality.

skills.description: Use when integrating multiple single-cell batches with partially missing modalities (mosaic scenario, e.g. scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq/protein with None placeholders) and you need a joint low-dimensional cell representation before clustering.
skills.name: matrix-trifactorization-cell-factor-training
skills.search_text: matrix-trifactorization-cell-factor-training Use when integrating multiple single-cell batches with partially missing modalities (mosaic scenario, e.g. scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq/protein with None placeholders) and you need a joint low-dimensional cell representation before clustering. When the task is horizontal/diagonal/vertical integration already handled by LIGER, Seurat v3/v4, CoupleNMF, MMD-MA, scDART, scAI, or MultiVI rather than a mosaic scenario with missing modalities When only a single batch/modality is available and no mosaic integration is needed When feature sets cannot be matched across batches (no gene intersection and no peak remapping possible), since each modality must share the same features per modality http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 First-stage training of the scMoMaT matrix tri-factorization model to learn unified cell factors from mosaic single-cell multi-omics counts (e.g. the MOp_5batches dataset), producing a cell embedding for downstream KNN/Leiden clustering and marker detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: First-stage training of the scMoMaT matrix tri-factorization model to learn unified cell factors from mosaic single-cell multi-omics counts (e.g. the MOp_5batches dataset), producing a cell embedding for downstream KNN/Leiden clustering and marker detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is horizontal/diagonal/vertical integration already handled by LIGER, Seurat v3/v4, CoupleNMF, MMD-MA, scDART, scAI, or MultiVI rather than a mosaic scenario with missing modalities When only a single batch/modality is available and no mosaic integration is needed When feature sets cannot be matched across batches (no gene intersection and no peak remapping possible), since each modality must share the same features per modality
