skills.description: Use when you have per-cell gene set scores for two experimental conditions and want a simple median cut point to quantify whether a smoothing or scoring change improves binary label prediction.
skills.name: median-threshold-binary-classification
skills.search_text: median-threshold-binary-classification Use when you have per-cell gene set scores for two experimental conditions and want a simple median cut point to quantify whether a smoothing or scoring change improves binary label prediction. The goal is multiclass or probabilistic classification — a single median cut point only supports binary label assignment at one threshold. Gene set scores have not yet been computed for both the unsmoothed and smoothed conditions, so no comparison of smoothing benefit is possible. The condition labels are continuous rather than binary, making a median threshold cut point inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A validation skill that binarizes per-cell gene set scores (e.g. gssnng summed_up scores) at their median to predict a binary condition label (LPS treatment status), then computes classification accuracy to test whether nearest neighbor smoothing improves separation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: A validation skill that binarizes per-cell gene set scores (e.g. gssnng summed_up scores) at their median to predict a binary condition label (LPS treatment status), then computes classification accuracy to test whether nearest neighbor smoothing improves separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is multiclass or probabilistic classification — a single median cut point only supports binary label assignment at one threshold. Gene set scores have not yet been computed for both the unsmoothed and smoothed conditions, so no comparison of smoothing benefit is possible. The condition labels are continuous rather than binary, making a median threshold cut point inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when a sequencing (NGS/RNA-seq) or microarray expression data frame contains low-abundance or background-noise features that would distort correlation analysis, and you need to filter them by median expression (e.g. medianthres=1) prior to transformation.
skills.name: median-threshold-feature-filtering
skills.search_text: median-threshold-feature-filtering Use when a sequencing (NGS/RNA-seq) or microarray expression data frame contains low-abundance or background-noise features that would distort correlation analysis, and you need to filter them by median expression (e.g. medianthres=1) prior to transformation. Single-cell data where the article notes non-viable cells and low-abundance genes require read count filtration as a separate step rather than a simple median threshold Data already transformed and normalized — re-filtering a transformed table would discard legitimately transformed low-scale values Features are methylation or transcription data mixed in one data frame; the article suggests grouping with featuregroup (e.g. grepl) instead of threshold filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A preprocessing skill from FeatureCorr that removes low-abundance features by applying a median expression threshold (medianthres) before data transformation, so that downstream correlation analysis (log2/z-score, pairwise or prime-feature) is computed only on features with sufficient signal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: A preprocessing skill from FeatureCorr that removes low-abundance features by applying a median expression threshold (medianthres) before data transformation, so that downstream correlation analysis (log2/z-score, pairwise or prime-feature) is computed only on features with sufficient signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell data where the article notes non-viable cells and low-abundance genes require read count filtration as a separate step rather than a simple median threshold Data already transformed and normalized — re-filtering a transformed table would discard legitimately transformed low-scale values Features are methylation or transcription data mixed in one data frame; the article suggests grouping with featuregroup (e.g. grepl) instead of threshold filtering

skills.description: Use when running METAFlux FBA on bulk RNA-seq MRAS scores and you must choose between cell_medium, human_blood, a custom-edited medium file, or a no-medium free-exchange control (known to yield only ρ=0.15 on NCI-60).
skills.name: medium-constraint-customization
skills.search_text: medium-constraint-customization Use when running METAFlux FBA on bulk RNA-seq MRAS scores and you must choose between cell_medium, human_blood, a custom-edited medium file, or a no-medium free-exchange control (known to yield only ρ=0.15 on NCI-60). Input is already solved flux data or metabolite abundance measurements rather than gene-expression-derived MRAS scores Single-cell community fluxes, where compute_sc_flux handles medium differently via cell-type fractions When the goal is medium-agnostic uptake/excretion inference — note the paper's control shows this condition alone yields poor correlation with measured fluxes (ρ=0.15 on NCI-60) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Configure the nutrient exchange medium (or deliberately remove it) in METAFlux's compute_flux step to control which of the 1,648 nutrient exchange reactions are open for uptake/excretion, since medium constraints directly determine predicted flux accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Configure the nutrient exchange medium (or deliberately remove it) in METAFlux's compute_flux step to control which of the 1,648 nutrient exchange reactions are open for uptake/excretion, since medium constraints directly determine predicted flux accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already solved flux data or metabolite abundance measurements rather than gene-expression-derived MRAS scores Single-cell community fluxes, where compute_sc_flux handles medium differently via cell-type fractions When the goal is medium-agnostic uptake/excretion inference — note the paper's control shows this condition alone yields poor correlation with measured fluxes (ρ=0.15 on NCI-60)

skills.description: Use when running METAFlux on bulk or single-cell RNA-seq data and the model must be constrained to a defined nutrient environment (cell culture vs. human-derived samples), or when customizing which nutrients are available for uptake.
skills.name: medium-exchange-reaction-configuration
skills.search_text: medium-exchange-reaction-configuration Use when running METAFlux on bulk or single-cell RNA-seq data and the model must be constrained to a defined nutrient environment (cell culture vs. human-derived samples), or when customizing which nutrients are available for uptake. The analysis goal is unconstrained FBA where all exchange reactions are open — the medium file deliberately restricts uptake. Only one model should be run per analysis; choosing both cell_medium and human_blood is explicitly not supported — pick the one matching the sample type. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Configure the nutrient medium file (e.g. human_blood or cell_medium) so that METAFlux's FBA only permits uptake of medium metabolites through their exchange reactions, making flux predictions nutrient-aware. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Configure the nutrient medium file (e.g. human_blood or cell_medium) so that METAFlux's FBA only permits uptake of medium metabolites through their exchange reactions, making flux predictions nutrient-aware.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is unconstrained FBA where all exchange reactions are open — the medium file deliberately restricts uptake. Only one model should be run per analysis; choosing both cell_medium and human_blood is explicitly not supported — pick the one matching the sample type.

skills.description: Use when testing drug-resistance program mutual exclusivity in melanoma scRNA-seq, especially in proliferating samples where cell-cycle signal masks the AXL–MITF anticorrelation (e.g., reproducing Mel78 R = -0.02 → -0.43 shift).
skills.name: melanoma-axl-mitf-state-marker-analysis
skills.search_text: melanoma-axl-mitf-state-marker-analysis Use when testing drug-resistance program mutual exclusivity in melanoma scRNA-seq, especially in proliferating samples where cell-cycle signal masks the AXL–MITF anticorrelation (e.g., reproducing Mel78 R = -0.02 → -0.43 shift). The sample is quiescent rather than actively proliferating — cell-cycle correction is not needed to unmask the AXL–MITF anticorrelation. The goal is to infer circular pseudo-time or cell-cycle stage itself, rather than to use Cyclum as a confounder-removal step before program-score correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes AXL-high and MITF-high melanoma cell-state program scores (mean expression of published gene sets) on raw and cell-cycle-corrected scRNA-seq matrices, then tests whether Cyclum correction unmasks the expected mutual exclusivity (negative AXL–MITF correlation) in actively proliferating melanoma samples like Mel78. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Computes AXL-high and MITF-high melanoma cell-state program scores (mean expression of published gene sets) on raw and cell-cycle-corrected scRNA-seq matrices, then tests whether Cyclum correction unmasks the expected mutual exclusivity (negative AXL–MITF correlation) in actively proliferating melanoma samples like Mel78.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is quiescent rather than actively proliferating — cell-cycle correction is not needed to unmask the AXL–MITF anticorrelation. The goal is to infer circular pseudo-time or cell-cycle stage itself, rather than to use Cyclum as a confounder-removal step before program-score correlation.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-Seq count matrix has malignant vs non-malignant (and cell-type) annotations and you need to test whether cancer cells show higher differentiation potency/signalling entropy than microenvironment cells, without feature selection or training.
skills.name: melanoma-cancer-vs-normal-cell-entropy-contrast
skills.search_text: melanoma-cancer-vs-normal-cell-entropy-contrast Use when a single-cell RNA-Seq count matrix has malignant vs non-malignant (and cell-type) annotations and you need to test whether cancer cells show higher differentiation potency/signalling entropy than microenvironment cells, without feature selection or training. When the analysis goal requires ordering cells along a trajectory in pseudo-time using pseudotime algorithms such as Monocle or MPath — the article notes this potency insight is not readily obtainable with those tools, but they serve a different purpose When only transcriptomic entropy without network information is acceptable (e.g. StemID- or SLICE-style measures) — this skill specifically requires the interaction-network-context SR computation When the input lacks malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations, since the contrast and potency-graded ordering cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Computes per-cell signalling entropy (SR) with the SCENT SignallingEntropy routine on the Tirosh melanoma scRNA-Seq data (3,256 non-malignant and 1,257 cancer cells across 12 patients) and contrasts cancer-cell entropy against each non-malignant tumour-microenvironment cell type using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Computes per-cell signalling entropy (SR) with the SCENT SignallingEntropy routine on the Tirosh melanoma scRNA-Seq data (3,256 non-malignant and 1,257 cancer cells across 12 patients) and contrasts cancer-cell entropy against each non-malignant tumour-microenvironment cell type using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal requires ordering cells along a trajectory in pseudo-time using pseudotime algorithms such as Monocle or MPath — the article notes this potency insight is not readily obtainable with those tools, but they serve a different purpose When only transcriptomic entropy without network information is acceptable (e.g. StemID- or SLICE-style measures) — this skill specifically requires the interaction-network-context SR computation When the input lacks malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations, since the contrast and potency-graded ordering cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when bulk transcriptomic data with matched survival (e.g., TCGA SKCM06) must be dissected at T cell-subpopulation resolution using scRNA-seq-derived markers to compare prognostic associations of Tex subtypes.
skills.name: melanoma-prognostic-t-cell-subpopulation-analysis
skills.search_text: melanoma-prognostic-t-cell-subpopulation-analysis Use when bulk transcriptomic data with matched survival (e.g., TCGA SKCM06) must be dissected at T cell-subpopulation resolution using scRNA-seq-derived markers to compare prognostic associations of Tex subtypes. The bulk cohort is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival data to identify prognostic gene pairs. The goal is immunotherapy response prediction rather than prognosis — use the TimiGP-Response module instead of the prognosis workflow. High-resolution single-cell data are already available — direct scRNA-seq analysis or dedicated interaction tools (e.g., scSeqComm) may be more appropriate than marker-pair inference from bulk data. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A TimiGP-based workflow that applies scRNA-seq-derived T cell-subpopulation markers to bulk metastatic melanoma data (TCGA SKCM06) to resolve prognostic heterogeneity among CD8+ exhausted T cell (Tex) subtypes, showing CD8+ GZMK+ Tex has a less favorable prognostic association than CD8+ TCF7+ Tex. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: A TimiGP-based workflow that applies scRNA-seq-derived T cell-subpopulation markers to bulk metastatic melanoma data (TCGA SKCM06) to resolve prognostic heterogeneity among CD8+ exhausted T cell (Tex) subtypes, showing CD8+ GZMK+ Tex has a less favorable prognostic association than CD8+ TCF7+ Tex.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The bulk cohort is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival data to identify prognostic gene pairs. The goal is immunotherapy response prediction rather than prognosis — use the TimiGP-Response module instead of the prognosis workflow. High-resolution single-cell data are already available — direct scRNA-seq analysis or dedicated interaction tools (e.g., scSeqComm) may be more appropriate than marker-pair inference from bulk data.

skills.description: Use when per-cell MPI labels for MEL1 tumor cells (from a getMPI reconstruction) are available and the goal is the overall proliferating (MPI = 1) tumor-cell fraction to verify against the reported 7.4%.
skills.name: melanoma-tumor-cell-fraction-analysis
skills.search_text: melanoma-tumor-cell-fraction-analysis Use when per-cell MPI labels for MEL1 tumor cells (from a getMPI reconstruction) are available and the goal is the overall proliferating (MPI = 1) tumor-cell fraction to verify against the reported 7.4%. Input is raw multiplexed image data or MCMICRO output that has not yet been gated/phenotyped and passed through getMPI — no per-cell MPI labels exist to count The analysis goal is region-level composition (e.g., proportion of MPI = 1 cells within immune-rich vs. immune-isolated subregions) rather than the overall sample-level fraction Computes the overall percentage of proliferating tumor cells (MPI = 1) among all tumor cells in the MEL1 cutaneous melanoma CyCIF sample using SpatialCells' multivariate proliferation index, yielding the paper's reference value of 7.4%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Computes the overall percentage of proliferating tumor cells (MPI = 1) among all tumor cells in the MEL1 cutaneous melanoma CyCIF sample using SpatialCells' multivariate proliferation index, yielding the paper's reference value of 7.4%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multiplexed image data or MCMICRO output that has not yet been gated/phenotyped and passed through getMPI — no per-cell MPI labels exist to count The analysis goal is region-level composition (e.g., proportion of MPI = 1 cells within immune-rich vs. immune-isolated subregions) rather than the overall sample-level fraction

skills.description: Use when benchmarking condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection on multi-condition scRNA-seq data and a baseline ranking from an NMF-based method with known condition-specific modules is needed, or when ground-truth CKG labels allow AUPRC/early-precision comparison.
skills.name: membership-matrix-variance-scoring
skills.search_text: membership-matrix-variance-scoring Use when benchmarking condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection on multi-condition scRNA-seq data and a baseline ranking from an NMF-based method with known condition-specific modules is needed, or when ground-truth CKG labels allow AUPRC/early-precision comparison. When batch effects are confounded with condition effects and no batch-aware disentanglement is possible — scINSIGHT factorizes expression matrices without explicit batch-effect modeling When no ground-truth or validation set exists to compare the resulting gene ranking against an alternative method's scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A baseline gene-ranking method that uses scINSIGHT's non-negative matrix factorization to identify condition-specific gene modules, then scores each gene by the variance of its membership (loadings) across those modules. It serves as the baseline against which scDisInFact's per-gene CKG scores are benchmarked by AUPRC on simulated data with known ground-truth condition-associated key genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: A baseline gene-ranking method that uses scINSIGHT's non-negative matrix factorization to identify condition-specific gene modules, then scores each gene by the variance of its membership (loadings) across those modules. It serves as the baseline against which scDisInFact's per-gene CKG scores are benchmarked by AUPRC on simulated data with known ground-truth condition-associated key genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When batch effects are confounded with condition effects and no batch-aware disentanglement is possible — scINSIGHT factorizes expression matrices without explicit batch-effect modeling When no ground-truth or validation set exists to compare the resulting gene ranking against an alternative method's scores

skills.description: Use when segmenting single cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., multiplexed immunofluorescence of colorectal adenomas or MIBI breast carcinoma TMAs) where cells have internal or incomplete membranes that defeat dilation- or Voronoi-based segmentation.
skills.name: membrane-extension-cell-separation
skills.search_text: membrane-extension-cell-separation Use when segmenting single cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., multiplexed immunofluorescence of colorectal adenomas or MIBI breast carcinoma TMAs) where cells have internal or incomplete membranes that defeat dilation- or Voronoi-based segmentation. Input consists of single-cell suspension images or dissociated cells without tissue architecture and aberrant internal membranes — the membrane-extension logic targets in-tissue, membrane-incomplete cells. Input is already a per-cell feature/intensity table; this skill operates on raw multiplexed image stacks before quantification. Only a single nuclear channel is available with no membrane markers — pixel classification cannot label the membrane compartment that drives the extension step. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 MIRIAM's novel membrane-extension method identifies and separates cells with internal aberrant membranes in multiplexed tissue images, extending incomplete cell membranes to produce per-cell segmentation masks with per-compartment (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm) marker quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: MIRIAM's novel membrane-extension method identifies and separates cells with internal aberrant membranes in multiplexed tissue images, extending incomplete cell membranes to produce per-cell segmentation masks with per-compartment (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm) marker quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of single-cell suspension images or dissociated cells without tissue architecture and aberrant internal membranes — the membrane-extension logic targets in-tissue, membrane-incomplete cells. Input is already a per-cell feature/intensity table; this skill operates on raw multiplexed image stacks before quantification. Only a single nuclear channel is available with no membrane markers — pixel classification cannot label the membrane compartment that drives the extension step.

skills.description: Use when watershed or pixel-classification-based cell segmentation has split columnar epithelial cells along internal membrane segments, and cells need re-segmentation by extending incomplete membranes geometrically.
skills.name: membrane-extension-geometry
skills.search_text: membrane-extension-geometry Use when watershed or pixel-classification-based cell segmentation has split columnar epithelial cells along internal membrane segments, and cells need re-segmentation by extending incomplete membranes geometrically. Cells have no internal membrane segments exceeding 10% of cell area — the initial watershed segmentation is retained as-is Segmentation targets round, regular cells (e.g., isolated nuclei) where Voronoi or dilation from nuclei suffices; MIRIAM targets irregular columnar epithelial morphologies No pixel-classification probability maps or watershed label mask are available — this skill is a downstream resegmentation step, not a stand-alone segmenter http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 MIRIAM's geometric membrane-extension routine that re-segments cells whose initial watershed segmentation was split by internal (aberrant) membranes, by extending internal membrane segments from their endpoints until they meet the cell border or another extension. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: MIRIAM's geometric membrane-extension routine that re-segments cells whose initial watershed segmentation was split by internal (aberrant) membranes, by extending internal membrane segments from their endpoints until they meet the cell border or another extension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have no internal membrane segments exceeding 10% of cell area — the initial watershed segmentation is retained as-is Segmentation targets round, regular cells (e.g., isolated nuclei) where Voronoi or dilation from nuclei suffices; MIRIAM targets irregular columnar epithelial morphologies No pixel-classification probability maps or watershed label mask are available — this skill is a downstream resegmentation step, not a stand-alone segmenter

skills.description: Use when two segmentation algorithms or two implementations of the same pipeline have been run on identical multiplexed imaging data and you need a numeric overlap metric (DSC/JSC) to demonstrate cross-implementation reproducibility of membrane masks.
skills.name: membrane-mask-overlap-metric-computation
skills.search_text: membrane-mask-overlap-metric-computation Use when two segmentation algorithms or two implementations of the same pipeline have been run on identical multiplexed imaging data and you need a numeric overlap metric (DSC/JSC) to demonstrate cross-implementation reproducibility of membrane masks. You only have a single segmentation output and no paired masks from a second implementation or method to compare against. The comparison target is a manual ground-truth annotation for benchmarking segmentation accuracy (e.g., MIRIAM vs. hand-drawn membranes, DSC 0.65 ± 0.08), not cross-implementation consistency. The masks are nucleus or cytoplasm compartment masks rather than the membrane masks the pipeline is designed to resegment. Quantifies agreement between membrane segmentation masks produced by two implementations (Matlab and Python) of the MIRIAM pipeline, using per-sub-image Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Jaccard similarity coefficient (JSC) aggregated as mean ± standard deviation. skills.description: Use when a single-cell Nanopore isoform quantification (Splice object from sc_iso_count.rds) contains multiple alternative exons or splice sites per gene, and downstream Beta-Binomial inter-cell heterogeneity (phi) estimation requires them merged into meta-splicing sites.
skills.name: meta-splice-site-merging
skills.search_text: meta-splice-site-merging Use when a single-cell Nanopore isoform quantification (Splice object from sc_iso_count.rds) contains multiple alternative exons or splice sites per gene, and downstream Beta-Binomial inter-cell heterogeneity (phi) estimation requires them merged into meta-splicing sites. The gene strand annotation (gene_bed.rds) is unavailable, since gene strand information is necessary to build meta splicing sites The Splice object has not been filtered with HighExprsGene, so low-expression genes with too few junction reads would produce unstable meta-sites The goal is per-exon psi visualization on a single well-defined site (psiHist/psiCellPlot) rather than gene-level heterogeneity modeling, where merging is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Merges coexisting or mutually exclusive alternative splicing sites of the same gene into meta-splicing sites using Longcell's geneSiteTable (eps = 0.05), so that downstream Beta-Binomial psi/phi heterogeneity estimation operates on well-supported, non-redundant splicing units. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Merges coexisting or mutually exclusive alternative splicing sites of the same gene into meta-splicing sites using Longcell's geneSiteTable (eps = 0.05), so that downstream Beta-Binomial psi/phi heterogeneity estimation operates on well-supported, non-redundant splicing units.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene strand annotation (gene_bed.rds) is unavailable, since gene strand information is necessary to build meta splicing sites The Splice object has not been filtered with HighExprsGene, so low-expression genes with too few junction reads would produce unstable meta-sites The goal is per-exon psi visualization on a single well-defined site (psiHist/psiCellPlot) rather than gene-level heterogeneity modeling, where merging is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you have a gene x sample RNA-seq matrix (human gene symbols as row names, normalized, non-negative) and need nutrient-aware metabolic flux estimates for 13082 reactions, e.g., glucose uptake (HMR_9034), pathway activity, or TME cell-type community fluxes.
skills.name: metabolic-flux-balance-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolic-flux-balance-analysis Use when you have a gene x sample RNA-seq matrix (human gene symbols as row names, normalized, non-negative) and need nutrient-aware metabolic flux estimates for 13082 reactions, e.g., glucose uptake (HMR_9034), pathway activity, or TME cell-type community fluxes. You need absolute quantitative flux measurements rather than relative flux scores — use Seahorse XF extracellular flux analysis or LC/MS metabolomics instead Input expression data is negative or not normalized (METAFlux requires non-negative, normalized gene x sample matrices) You need a full in-depth comparison with Compass beyond what the paper's Supplementary Note provides, or a specific METAFlux version — no version numbers or changelog are documented http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Infer metabolic fluxes from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq data using METAFlux, which combines Human-GEM (13082 reactions, 8378 metabolites) gene-protein-reaction mapping with flux balance analysis under medium constraints. It enables nutrient-aware flux prediction for cancer metabolism studies, NCI-60 benchmarking, and TCGA subgroup/survival analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Infer metabolic fluxes from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq data using METAFlux, which combines Human-GEM (13082 reactions, 8378 metabolites) gene-protein-reaction mapping with flux balance analysis under medium constraints. It enables nutrient-aware flux prediction for cancer metabolism studies, NCI-60 benchmarking, and TCGA subgroup/survival analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need absolute quantitative flux measurements rather than relative flux scores — use Seahorse XF extracellular flux analysis or LC/MS metabolomics instead Input expression data is negative or not normalized (METAFlux requires non-negative, normalized gene x sample matrices) You need a full in-depth comparison with Compass beyond what the paper's Supplementary Note provides, or a specific METAFlux version — no version numbers or changelog are documented

skills.search_text: metabolic-flux-interpretation-from-gene-expression Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g. the 21-gene PLA2G4B node) and you need to identify the dominant enzyme, node-level regulation, and net metabolic flux from RNA-seq data. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP Non-human pathways — the current FunHoP version supports only human metabolic pathways found in KEGG (excluding glycan-related pathways) Analyses requiring isoform- or enzyme-kinetics-level activity, since KEGG provides no curated isoform enzyme-activity data and kinetics data are usually unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Interprets overall metabolic node regulation and inferred substrate flux direction in KEGG metabolic pathways by collapsing multi-gene functionally homologous nodes into single read-count-based measurements, assuming reaction activity depends mainly on the gene with the highest number of RNA-seq reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003

skills.search_text: metabolic-gene-set-curation-and-application Use when analyzing metabolic pathway activity in single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., across T cell activation time points or pseudotime trajectory nodes — where combined metabolic gene sets and distribution-based qvals are needed rather than simple enrichment. When the question is gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level distribution change across populations When the input is already a scored pathway activity matrix (e.g., from AUCell/GSVA) rather than single-cell expression data with population metadata When judging results solely by fold change/enrichment — SCPA pathways can show large qvals without enrichment, so enrichment-only workflows will misinterpret results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Curate and apply metabolic pathway gene sets (Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome from MSigDB) with SCPA's compare_pathways to quantify metabolic reprogramming across single-cell populations or pseudotime milestones, using the qval as the primary statistic and fold change/enrichment only as secondary evidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Curate and apply metabolic pathway gene sets (Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome from MSigDB) with SCPA's compare_pathways to quantify metabolic reprogramming across single-cell populations or pseudotime milestones, using the qval as the primary statistic and fold change/enrichment only as secondary evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level distribution change across populations When the input is already a scored pathway activity matrix (e.g., from AUCell/GSVA) rather than single-cell expression data with population metadata When judging results solely by fold change/enrichment — SCPA pathways can show large qvals without enrichment, so enrichment-only workflows will misinterpret results

skills.description: Use when input is metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (scEU-seq h5ad like rpeLabeling.h5ad) with labeled/total/unlabeled counts and a labeling time, and you must prepare paired t0/t1 matrices for RNAForecaster forecasting.
skills.name: metabolic-labeling-scrnaseq-data-processing
skills.search_text: metabolic-labeling-scrnaseq-data-processing Use when input is metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (scEU-seq h5ad like rpeLabeling.h5ad) with labeled/total/unlabeled counts and a labeling time, and you must prepare paired t0/t1 matrices for RNAForecaster forecasting. Data come from standard scRNA-seq protocols, which destroy cells to measure them and therefore cannot provide paired time-point measurements of the same cell required by RNAForecaster In vivo samples without metabolic labeling, since these protocols are currently largely confined to in vitro studies The data are already log-normalized and variance-filtered paired t0/t1 matrices ready for trainRNAForecaster — applying redundant filtering could remove signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocessing pipeline for metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq 4sU uridine labeling) to produce log-normalized, sparsity- and variance-filtered paired time-point matrices suitable for RNAForecaster neural ODE training, including degradation rate estimation via estimateT0LabelingData. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from standard scRNA-seq protocols, which destroy cells to measure them and therefore cannot provide paired time-point measurements of the same cell required by RNAForecaster In vivo samples without metabolic labeling, since these protocols are currently largely confined to in vitro studies The data are already log-normalized and variance-filtered paired t0/t1 matrices ready for trainRNAForecaster — applying redundant filtering could remove signal

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data come from a metabolic labeling assay (e.g., scEU-seq) with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices, and you need a t=0 expression estimate to train RNAForecaster on paired time points.
skills.name: metabolic-labeling-t0-estimation
skills.search_text: metabolic-labeling-t0-estimation Use when scRNA-seq data come from a metabolic labeling assay (e.g., scEU-seq) with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices, and you need a t=0 expression estimate to train RNAForecaster on paired time points. Input is standard scRNA-seq without labeled/unlabeled count matrices — the same cell cannot be measured at two time points, so no t=0 estimate can be constructed Data come from trajectory-inference or RNA velocity settings where only spliced/unspliced counts are available rather than metabolic labeling counts A t0Estimate matrix has already been produced and validated; re-running estimation would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs the t=0 total-expression input matrix for RNAForecaster from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq) by estimating per-gene degradation rates from labeled-vs-total count regressions and adding estimated degraded transcripts to the unlabeled counts matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Constructs the t=0 total-expression input matrix for RNAForecaster from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq) by estimating per-gene degradation rates from labeled-vs-total count regressions and adding estimated degraded transcripts to the unlabeled counts matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is standard scRNA-seq without labeled/unlabeled count matrices — the same cell cannot be measured at two time points, so no t=0 estimate can be constructed Data come from trajectory-inference or RNA velocity settings where only spliced/unspliced counts are available rather than metabolic labeling counts A t0Estimate matrix has already been produced and validated; re-running estimation would be redundant

skills.description: Use when you have context-specific metabolic models of infected vs. mock tissue (built via rFASTCORMICS from GEO datasets such as GSE147507/GSE148729) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic double-knockout gene pairs to prioritize drug targets.
skills.name: metabolic-model-essentiality-analysis
skills.search_text: metabolic-model-essentiality-analysis Use when you have context-specific metabolic models of infected vs. mock tissue (built via rFASTCORMICS from GEO datasets such as GSE147507/GSE148729) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic double-knockout gene pairs to prioritize drug targets. When the goal is directly docking drugs on the viral proteome — DCcov notes identified targets come from 'network effects on the host metabolome (as the virus is only modeled through its biomass function) rather than direct docking' When input models lack the viral biomass objective function or are mock (uninfected) models, since essentiality is scored against viral biomass production When only differential expression is needed — use DESeq2 (|log2FC| > 1, adjusted p < 0.05) instead of knockout simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Systematic in silico single- and double-gene deletion on context-specific genome-scale metabolic models carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) to identify essential genes and synergistic gene pairs whose knockout reduces viral biomass production without affecting host biomass maintenance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331
skills.summary: Systematic in silico single- and double-gene deletion on context-specific genome-scale metabolic models carrying a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) to identify essential genes and synergistic gene pairs whose knockout reduces viral biomass production without affecting host biomass maintenance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is directly docking drugs on the viral proteome — DCcov notes identified targets come from 'network effects on the host metabolome (as the virus is only modeled through its biomass function) rather than direct docking' When input models lack the viral biomass objective function or are mock (uninfected) models, since essentiality is scored against viral biomass production When only differential expression is needed — use DESeq2 (|log2FC| > 1, adjusted p < 0.05) instead of knockout simulation

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized, non-negative gene x sample bulk RNA-seq matrix (or bootstrapped single-cell average-expression profiles per cell type) with human gene symbols as row names, and need reaction-level activity scores before flux estimation.
skills.name: metabolic-reaction-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: metabolic-reaction-activity-scoring Use when you have a normalized, non-negative gene x sample bulk RNA-seq matrix (or bootstrapped single-cell average-expression profiles per cell type) with human gene symbols as row names, and need reaction-level activity scores before flux estimation. Input is proteomics or metabolomics abundance data (e.g. LC/MS metabolite concentrations) rather than RNA-seq gene expression — GPR-based MRAS requires gene-level signal Row names of the expression matrix are not human gene symbols (e.g. Ensembl IDs, probe IDs, or non-human orthologs), since the GPR rules map HGNC symbols You need per-reaction fluxes under a specific nutrient condition — MRAS alone is an activity score; fluxes require a subsequent medium-constrained compute_flux/compute_sc_flux step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a gene x sample expression matrix by aggregating gene expression through Human-GEM Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) rules, producing scores for the 13,082 metabolic reactions in Human-GEM. skills.summary: Compute single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a gene x sample expression matrix by aggregating gene expression through Human-GEM Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) rules, producing scores for the 13,082 metabolic reactions in Human-GEM. This is the input layer that METAFlux's compute_flux and compute_sc_flux consume to solve flux balance problems.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is proteomics or metabolomics abundance data (e.g. LC/MS metabolite concentrations) rather than RNA-seq gene expression — GPR-based MRAS requires gene-level signal Row names of the expression matrix are not human gene symbols (e.g. Ensembl IDs, probe IDs, or non-human orthologs), since the GPR rules map HGNC symbols You need per-reaction fluxes under a specific nutrient condition — MRAS alone is an activity score; fluxes require a subsequent medium-constrained compute_flux/compute_sc_flux step

The VBOF and the target reconstruction already share the same metabolite identifier namespace, so no cross-namespace mapping is needed The goal is building context-specific (sample-level) models from RNA-seq/expression data — that is the rFASTCORMICS step that consumes the outputs of this skill, not this skill itself The target model is not a consistent COBRA-format genome-scale reconstruction (e.g. a small cell-line model or non-metabolic network), since the workflow is defined for Recon2.04/Recon3D_01-style inputs This skill merges an external biomass reaction (the SARS-CoV-2 viral biomass objective function, VBOF, from BioModels MODEL2003020001) into generic genome-scale reconstructions (Recon2.04, Recon3D_01) in MATLAB with the COBRA Toolbox V3, by reconciling the VBOF metabolite namespace with the BiGG/VMH identifiers of each reconstruction so the augmented models are consistent and usable as rFASTCORMICS inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103331

skills.description: Use when building metacells and you must choose a graining level: sweep the graining parameter across a dataset and measure purity/cell-type recovery to pick a level that preserves rare populations without fragmenting the analysis.
skills.name: metacell-construction-graining-level-sweep
skills.search_text: metacell-construction-graining-level-sweep Use when building metacells and you must choose a graining level: sweep the graining parameter across a dataset and measure purity/cell-type recovery to pick a level that preserves rare populations without fragmenting the analysis. The input is a single fixed-resolution metacell model and no re-construction at different graining levels is possible (e.g. a pre-built .h5ad metacell model loaded only for interactive exploration in MCView). The goal is a cell-type atlas projection against a reference (metacell projection/atlas mapping) rather than choosing construction granularity. The dataset has no ground-truth celltype annotations, since purity (proportion of the most abundant cell type within the metacell) cannot be computed without them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A systematic scan of metacell graining levels (coarse-to-fine average metacell sizes) that quantifies how well cell types are recovered at each level, using metacell purity and the number of distinct cell types represented per graining level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: A systematic scan of metacell graining levels (coarse-to-fine average metacell sizes) that quantifies how well cell types are recovered at each level, using metacell purity and the number of distinct cell types represented per graining level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single fixed-resolution metacell model and no re-construction at different graining levels is possible (e.g. a pre-built .h5ad metacell model loaded only for interactive exploration in MCView). The goal is a cell-type atlas projection against a reference (metacell projection/atlas mapping) rather than choosing construction granularity. The dataset has no ground-truth celltype annotations, since purity (proportion of the most abundant cell type within the metacell) cannot be computed without them.

skills.when_to_use_negative: You are building metacells for a new dataset rather than surveying how published studies sized their metacells — use the MetacellAnalysisToolkit pipeline instead. Your input is raw scRNA-seq count data rather than the curated study-level Dataset EV2 table. skills.name: metacell-level-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: metacell-level-differential-abundance-analysis Use when comparing cell-type abundance or gene mean expression between conditions using aggregated metacell profiles, and you must ensure metacell size weights are applied to avoid inflated type I/II errors. Your analysis operates directly on the single-cell expression matrix — metacell aggregation and weighting are not needed and add unnecessary indirection You are building or quality-controlling metacells themselves (purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than using pre-built metacells for downstream comparison Metacells in your dataset are highly homogeneous in size (uniform cell counts), where weighting has little effect and single-cell-level analysis may be simpler http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Perform differential abundance and differential expression at the metacell level with Seurat, running each test in two modes — unweighted and weighted by metacell size (number of constituent single cells) — and compare both against single-cell-level reference results to expose type I/II artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Perform differential abundance and differential expression at the metacell level with Seurat, running each test in two modes — unweighted and weighted by metacell size (number of constituent single cells) — and compare both against single-cell-level reference results to expose type I/II artifacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your analysis operates directly on the single-cell expression matrix — metacell aggregation and weighting are not needed and add unnecessary indirection You are building or quality-controlling metacells themselves (purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than using pre-built metacells for downstream comparison Metacells in your dataset are highly homogeneous in size (uniform cell counts), where weighting has little effect and single-cell-level analysis may be simpler

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large or sparse for robust per-cell statistics and you need disjoint groups of cells of the same biological state as input for downstream analyses (trajectories, cell typing, differential analysis at the metacell level).
skills.name: metacell-partitioning-from-cell-similarity-graph
skills.search_text: metacell-partitioning-from-cell-similarity-graph Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large or sparse for robust per-cell statistics and you need disjoint groups of cells of the same biological state as input for downstream analyses (trajectories, cell typing, differential analysis at the metacell level). The input is already aggregated at the metacell level or is a feature table — no per-cell profiles exist to partition. The analysis goal requires single-cell resolution (e.g. rare-state detection where each individual profile matters) — the article outlines how and when metacells should or should not be used. The data has not been pruned of technical artifacts (doublets, ruptured cells) and excluded-gene/cell lists have not been specified — the metacells package warns these decisions are crucial for high-quality metacells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Partitions highly similar single cells into disjoint metacells using MC2, SuperCell, or SEACells, based on a cell similarity space defined by PCA of a normalized, variable-feature-selected scRNA-seq dataset, then aggregates raw counts into metacell profiles. Metacells reduce data size and complexity while preserving biologically relevant information and improving interpretability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Partitions highly similar single cells into disjoint metacells using MC2, SuperCell, or SEACells, based on a cell similarity space defined by PCA of a normalized, variable-feature-selected scRNA-seq dataset, then aggregates raw counts into metacell profiles. Metacells reduce data size and complexity while preserving biologically relevant information and improving interpretability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already aggregated at the metacell level or is a feature table — no per-cell profiles exist to partition. The analysis goal requires single-cell resolution (e.g. rare-state detection where each individual profile matters) — the article outlines how and when metacells should or should not be used. The data has not been pruned of technical artifacts (doublets, ruptured cells) and excluded-gene/cell lists have not been specified — the metacells package warns these decisions are crucial for high-quality metacells.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large for standard metacell construction (time/memory limits at hundreds of thousands of cells), or when built metacells must be projected onto a single-cell UMAP/embedding for visualization and QC.
skills.name: metacell-projection-based-reduction
skills.search_text: metacell-projection-based-reduction Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large for standard metacell construction (time/memory limits at hundreds of thousands of cells), or when built metacells must be projected onto a single-cell UMAP/embedding for visualization and QC. The dataset is small enough that standard direct metacell construction (MC2, SuperCell, SEACells) is already tractable — the projection variant is specifically motivated by scaling limits on large data Per-cell resolution is required for the downstream analysis (metacells deliberately aggregate profiles of the same biological state, reducing ~100-fold) The goal is interactive exploration/annotation of an already-built metacell model — MCView (shiny-app) is the appropriate tool rather than re-running projection http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reduces large single-cell RNA-seq datasets to metacell level using projection-based approaches (e.g. the projection-based SuperCell variant) and maps the resulting metacells back onto single-cell embeddings such as UMAP via mc_projection(). This strategy is what allows metacell construction to scale to very large atlases (e.g. the 900k-cell MOCA subsets) where direct construction is time- and memory-consuming. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Reduces large single-cell RNA-seq datasets to metacell level using projection-based approaches (e.g. the projection-based SuperCell variant) and maps the resulting metacells back onto single-cell embeddings such as UMAP via mc_projection(). This strategy is what allows metacell construction to scale to very large atlases (e.g. the 900k-cell MOCA subsets) where direct construction is time- and memory-consuming.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that standard direct metacell construction (MC2, SuperCell, SEACells) is already tractable — the projection variant is specifically motivated by scaling limits on large data Per-cell resolution is required for the downstream analysis (metacells deliberately aggregate profiles of the same biological state, reducing ~100-fold) The goal is interactive exploration/annotation of an already-built metacell model — MCView (shiny-app) is the appropriate tool rather than re-running projection

skills.description: Use when metacells have been constructed (SuperCell/SEACells backends) and you need to check whether each metacell corresponds to a single cell type, e.g. when tuning graining level or comparing datasets of differing complexity.
skills.name: metacell-purity-quantification
skills.search_text: metacell-purity-quantification Use when metacells have been constructed (SuperCell/SEACells backends) and you need to check whether each metacell corresponds to a single cell type, e.g. when tuning graining level or comparing datasets of differing complexity. Before metacells are actually constructed — purity requires a cell-to-metacell membership mapping, not just a PCA/UMAP embedding When no per-cell type annotations exist for the dataset, since purity is computed against an annotation vector such as sc_data$celltype http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies metacell purity — the proportion of the most abundant cell type within each metacell — using the MetacellAnalysisToolkit mc_purity function, to evaluate how faithfully metacells preserve cell-type identity (e.g., rare populations lost at coarse graining levels). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Quantifies metacell purity — the proportion of the most abundant cell type within each metacell — using the MetacellAnalysisToolkit mc_purity function, to evaluate how faithfully metacells preserve cell-type identity (e.g., rare populations lost at coarse graining levels).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Before metacells are actually constructed — purity requires a cell-to-metacell membership mapping, not just a PCA/UMAP embedding When no per-cell type annotations exist for the dataset, since purity is computed against an annotation vector such as sc_data$celltype

skills.description: Use when a constructed metacell partition must be quantitatively assessed for quality, especially when no cell-type annotations are available and a latent-space-independent metric (INV) is needed.
skills.name: metacell-quality-metric-computation
skills.search_text: metacell-quality-metric-computation Use when a constructed metacell partition must be quantitatively assessed for quality, especially when no cell-type annotations are available and a latent-space-independent metric (INV) is needed. The goal is to compare metacells against an annotated atlas or project metacells onto a single-cell UMAP — use mc_projection() instead of the QC metric functions. Cell-type annotations are unavailable and a supervised metric like purity is requested — purity requires an annotation vector; only INV is annotation-free. The task is interactive exploration of an already-built metacell model rather than metric computation — MCView shiny-app exploration is the wrong tool here. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute four per-metacell quality metrics — purity, compactness, separation, and inner normalized variance (INV) — using MetacellAnalysisToolkit functions on packaged metacell/single-cell objects, and visualize them with qc_boxplot(). The key insight is that INV is the only metric requiring no cell-type annotation or latent-space embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Compute four per-metacell quality metrics — purity, compactness, separation, and inner normalized variance (INV) — using MetacellAnalysisToolkit functions on packaged metacell/single-cell objects, and visualize them with qc_boxplot(). The key insight is that INV is the only metric requiring no cell-type annotation or latent-space embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare metacells against an annotated atlas or project metacells onto a single-cell UMAP — use mc_projection() instead of the QC metric functions. Cell-type annotations are unavailable and a supervised metric like purity is requested — purity requires an annotation vector; only INV is annotation-free. The task is interactive exploration of an already-built metacell model rather than metric computation — MCView shiny-app exploration is the wrong tool here.

skills.description: Use when a trained GeneVector embedding must be turned into interpretable gene modules and ranked against a directional vector (e.g., Vadnexa − Vbowel in HGSOC cancer cells) to identify Hallmark-enriched programs.
skills.name: metagene-clustering-and-hallmark-enrichment
skills.search_text: metagene-clustering-and-hallmark-enrichment Use when a trained GeneVector embedding must be turned into interpretable gene modules and ranked against a directional vector (e.g., Vadnexa − Vbowel in HGSOC cancer cells) to identify Hallmark-enriched programs. The goal is to infer directed regulatory relationships (activation vs. repression) — GeneVector's mutual-information target is agnostic to the direction of statistical dependency, so metagenes cannot distinguish these. Batches differ substantially in cell type composition, since batch correction vectors and downstream metagene interpretation become unreliable and must be manually verified against cell type signatures. Input is not a raw-count AnnData or no trained gene embedding exists — clustering metagenes presumes a completed GeneVector training run producing genes.vec. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Decomposes a trained GeneVector gene embedding (genes.vec) into unsupervised metagenes by clustering the gene co-expression graph at a fixed Leiden resolution, then scores metagenes against a condition-direction vector to surface Hallmark-enriched transcriptional programs (e.g., EMT gain, MHC-I loss). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Decomposes a trained GeneVector gene embedding (genes.vec) into unsupervised metagenes by clustering the gene co-expression graph at a fixed Leiden resolution, then scores metagenes against a condition-direction vector to surface Hallmark-enriched transcriptional programs (e.g., EMT gain, MHC-I loss).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to infer directed regulatory relationships (activation vs. repression) — GeneVector's mutual-information target is agnostic to the direction of statistical dependency, so metagenes cannot distinguish these. Batches differ substantially in cell type composition, since batch correction vectors and downstream metagene interpretation become unreliable and must be manually verified against cell type signatures. Input is not a raw-count AnnData or no trained gene embedding exists — clustering metagenes presumes a completed GeneVector training run producing genes.vec.

skills.description: Use when you have a trained GeneVector embedding (genes.vec) from scRNA-seq AnnData and need to discover co-regulated gene modules (metagenes) and test whether their per-cell module scores change across conditions or treatment timepoints.
skills.name: metagene-clustering-from-gene-vectors
skills.search_text: metagene-clustering-from-gene-vectors Use when you have a trained GeneVector embedding (genes.vec) from scRNA-seq AnnData and need to discover co-regulated gene modules (metagenes) and test whether their per-cell module scores change across conditions or treatment timepoints. The goal is distinguishing activation from repression or identifying negative regulation — GeneVector's MI target cannot discern the direction of statistical dependency. Batches differ strongly in cell type composition and you intend to interpret correction vectors as transcriptional signatures without manual verification against cell type signatures. The input is not single-cell expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table); the embedding requires per-cell expression sparsity structure in AnnData .X. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster trained GeneVector gene embeddings into metagenes (unsupervised transcriptional programs) and score them per cell to detect context- or treatment-specific programs, e.g. the TGF-beta metagene 24 in cisplatin-treated TNBC PDXs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Cluster trained GeneVector gene embeddings into metagenes (unsupervised transcriptional programs) and score them per cell to detect context- or treatment-specific programs, e.g. the TGF-beta metagene 24 in cisplatin-treated TNBC PDXs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is distinguishing activation from repression or identifying negative regulation — GeneVector's MI target cannot discern the direction of statistical dependency. Batches differ strongly in cell type composition and you intend to interpret correction vectors as transcriptional signatures without manual verification against cell type signatures. The input is not single-cell expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table); the embedding requires per-cell expression sparsity structure in AnnData .X.

skills.description: Use when length-selected Ribo-seq alignments (e.g. 25-35 nt RPF BAM/BED files) and a GFF3 annotation are available and you must verify footprints reflect active ribosomes before differential analysis.
skills.name: metagene-periodicity-qc-around-start-stop-codons
skills.search_text: metagene-periodicity-qc-around-start-stop-codons Use when length-selected Ribo-seq alignments (e.g. 25-35 nt RPF BAM/BED files) and a GFF3 annotation are available and you must verify footprints reflect active ribosomes before differential analysis. The input dataset does not align enough material for the riboWaltz pipeline — in that case RiboDoc should be run with TRiP selected instead (as noted for the GEO GSE173856 example dataset) The goal is differential expression or quantification rather than qualitative footprint validation — use the DESeq2 step of RiboDoc instead Input is raw FastQ; adapter trimming, rRNA/tRNA contaminant removal with Bowtie2, and alignment with HISAT2/Bowtie2 must precede this QC http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0623 A qualitative quality-control module of the RiboDoc pipeline that pools all annotated CDS into a metagene and verifies that ribosome footprints show 3-nt periodicity and CDS-anchored phasing, confirming the data correspond to active ribosome-protected fragments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: A qualitative quality-control module of the RiboDoc pipeline that pools all annotated CDS into a metagene and verifies that ribosome footprints show 3-nt periodicity and CDS-anchored phasing, confirming the data correspond to active ribosome-protected fragments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input dataset does not align enough material for the riboWaltz pipeline — in that case RiboDoc should be run with TRiP selected instead (as noted for the GEO GSE173856 example dataset) The goal is differential expression or quantification rather than qualitative footprint validation — use the DESeq2 step of RiboDoc instead Input is raw FastQ; adapter trimming, rRNA/tRNA contaminant removal with Bowtie2, and alignment with HISAT2/Bowtie2 must precede this QC

skills.description: Use when you must compare the robustness of two cell-cycle/pseudo-time methods by down-sampling an annotated scRNA-seq matrix to fewer cells (e.g. n=10, n=30) or fewer genes and plotting median accuracy against sample size.
skills.name: method-accuracy-benchmark-visualization
skills.search_text: method-accuracy-benchmark-visualization Use when you must compare the robustness of two cell-cycle/pseudo-time methods by down-sampling an annotated scRNA-seq matrix to fewer cells (e.g. n=10, n=30) or fewer genes and plotting median accuracy against sample size. The question is method development or pseudo-time inference quality itself, not a head-to-head accuracy robustness comparison under down-sampling The dataset lacks annotated cell-cycle stage labels, so stratified cell down-sampling and stage-prediction accuracy cannot be computed Both candidate methods require full-scale data (e.g. reCAT fails below 5000 genes), making down-sampled comparisons uninformative for that method http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark and visualize classification accuracy of competing methods (here Cyclum vs. reCAT on mESC scRNA-seq) under controlled down-sampling of cells and genes, producing accuracy tables and accuracy-vs-sample-size curves that expose robustness differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Benchmark and visualize classification accuracy of competing methods (here Cyclum vs. reCAT on mESC scRNA-seq) under controlled down-sampling of cells and genes, producing accuracy tables and accuracy-vs-sample-size curves that expose robustness differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is method development or pseudo-time inference quality itself, not a head-to-head accuracy robustness comparison under down-sampling The dataset lacks annotated cell-cycle stage labels, so stratified cell down-sampling and stage-prediction accuracy cannot be computed Both candidate methods require full-scale data (e.g. reCAT fails below 5000 genes), making down-sampled comparisons uninformative for that method

skills.description: Use when two methods were compared on differently sized datasets and you must re-run both on the same cell count subsets to isolate true performance differences from dataset-size effects.
skills.name: method-benchmark-comparison-across-datasets
skills.search_text: method-benchmark-comparison-across-datasets Use when two methods were compared on differently sized datasets and you must re-run both on the same cell count subsets to isolate true performance differences from dataset-size effects. When the research question concerns absolute accuracy on the full datasets rather than a size-controlled head-to-head comparison — the 50k subsets deliberately trade performance for comparability. When species other than human, mouse, or marmoset motor cortex are involved — the 50k subset resource on Zenodo covers only these three motor cortex datasets. When a species pair includes a cell type with fewer than 50 cells — subset construction requires a minimum of 50 cells per included type. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Benchmark two cross-species cell type matching methods (TACTiCS vs SAMap) on identical equal-sized 50k-cells-per-species subsets of the human, mouse, and marmoset motor cortex scRNA-seq data, to control for dataset size differences when judging relative performance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Benchmark two cross-species cell type matching methods (TACTiCS vs SAMap) on identical equal-sized 50k-cells-per-species subsets of the human, mouse, and marmoset motor cortex scRNA-seq data, to control for dataset size differences when judging relative performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the research question concerns absolute accuracy on the full datasets rather than a size-controlled head-to-head comparison — the 50k subsets deliberately trade performance for comparability. When species other than human, mouse, or marmoset motor cortex are involved — the 50k subset resource on Zenodo covers only these three motor cortex datasets. When a species pair includes a cell type with fewer than 50 cells — subset construction requires a minimum of 50 cells per included type.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods for multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data against simulated ground truth, especially to compare FDR/TPR under local (per-subpopulation) vs. global BH p-value adjustment.
skills.name: method-benchmark-fdr-tpr-evaluation
skills.search_text: method-benchmark-fdr-tpr-evaluation Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods for multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data against simulated ground truth, especially to compare FDR/TPR under local (per-subpopulation) vs. global BH p-value adjustment. The task is applying a single DS method to real scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking multiple methods against simulated ground truth with known DS genes. There is no sample-level replication (one sample per condition) — sample-level FDR/TPR evaluation and pseudobulk testing across samples require multiple samples per group. The SingleCellExperiment lacks sample_id, group_id, and cluster_id metadata columns required by aggregateData/pbDS/mmDS. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark 16 differential state (DS) analysis methods on muscat-simulated multi-sample multi-condition scRNA-seq data, computing false discovery rate (FDR) and true positive rate (TPR) per method against simulated ground truth, stratified by DS type (DE, DP, DM, DB) and by locally vs. globally Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Benchmark 16 differential state (DS) analysis methods on muscat-simulated multi-sample multi-condition scRNA-seq data, computing false discovery rate (FDR) and true positive rate (TPR) per method against simulated ground truth, stratified by DS type (DE, DP, DM, DB) and by locally vs. globally Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is applying a single DS method to real scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking multiple methods against simulated ground truth with known DS genes. There is no sample-level replication (one sample per condition) — sample-level FDR/TPR evaluation and pseudobulk testing across samples require multiple samples per group. The SingleCellExperiment lacks sample_id, group_id, and cluster_id metadata columns required by aggregateData/pbDS/mmDS.

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell, pathway-level estimates of genetic association from GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object, e.g. to compute scPagwas.gPAS.score for trait-relevant cell identification.
skills.name: method-of-moments-polygenic-regression
skills.search_text: method-of-moments-polygenic-regression Use when you need per-cell, pathway-level estimates of genetic association from GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object, e.g. to compute scPagwas.gPAS.score for trait-relevant cell identification. When the goal is cell-type-level (not single-cell) enrichment — use the block-bootstrap celltype branch or tools like LDSC-SEG/EPIC instead When disease-specific gene prioritization via MAGMA gene-based tests (as in scDRS) is preferred over pathway-based regression When the single-cell data are not normalized or pathway sizes fall outside 5-300 genes, since the SVD-based PAS and pathway filtering assumptions are violated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Per-pathway polygenic regression from scPagwas that links SVD-derived pathway activity scores (PAS) of single cells to GWAS summary statistics, estimating each pathway's genetically associated polygenic score (gPAS) per cell via a method-of-moments regression on SNP-pathway LD blocks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Per-pathway polygenic regression from scPagwas that links SVD-derived pathway activity scores (PAS) of single cells to GWAS summary statistics, estimating each pathway's genetically associated polygenic score (gPAS) per cell via a method-of-moments regression on SNP-pathway LD blocks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cell-type-level (not single-cell) enrichment — use the block-bootstrap celltype branch or tools like LDSC-SEG/EPIC instead When disease-specific gene prioritization via MAGMA gene-based tests (as in scDRS) is preferred over pathway-based regression When the single-cell data are not normalized or pathway sizes fall outside 5-300 genes, since the SVD-based PAS and pathway filtering assumptions are violated

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how a DEG prediction method's detection accuracy and computational cost scale with dataset size, using artificial single-cell datasets with known planted DEGs as ground truth.
skills.name: method-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: method-runtime-profiling Use when you need to quantify how a DEG prediction method's detection accuracy and computational cost scale with dataset size, using artificial single-cell datasets with known planted DEGs as ground truth. The analysis goal is DEG discovery on a real biological dataset rather than method benchmarking against known ground-truth labels. The input data lacks planted or otherwise known true DEG labels, so ROC AUC of DEG detection cannot be computed. Only one method and one dataset size are of interest — runtime/accuracy scaling comparisons across methods are the point of this skill. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark the accuracy (AUC of DEG detection ROC) and elapsed runtime of singleCellHaystack against competing DEG prediction methods (DEsingle, EMDomics, scDD, edgeR, monocle 2, Seurat FindAllMarkers) on artificial scRNA-seq datasets of increasing size (1,000–10,000 cells), aggregating medians per method and dataset size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy (AUC of DEG detection ROC) and elapsed runtime of singleCellHaystack against competing DEG prediction methods (DEsingle, EMDomics, scDD, edgeR, monocle 2, Seurat FindAllMarkers) on artificial scRNA-seq datasets of increasing size (1,000–10,000 cells), aggregating medians per method and dataset size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is DEG discovery on a real biological dataset rather than method benchmarking against known ground-truth labels. The input data lacks planted or otherwise known true DEG labels, so ROC AUC of DEG detection cannot be computed. Only one method and one dataset size are of interest — runtime/accuracy scaling comparisons across methods are the point of this skill.

skills.search_text: methylation-pipeline-runtime-comparison Use when estimating or reproducing the computational cost of methylR's ChAMP or minfi methylation array pipelines on the paper's test dataset under stated hardware constraints, e.g. to plan capacity or validate the tool.
