skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell methylation and transcriptome data and want to map methylation rates onto an independently recovered cell cycle ordering, or reproduce Fig. 4d-style methylation curves along G1/S/G2-M.
skills.name: methylation-to-pseudotime-assignment
skills.search_text: methylation-to-pseudotime-assignment Use when you have paired single-cell methylation and transcriptome data and want to map methylation rates onto an independently recovered cell cycle ordering, or reproduce Fig. 4d-style methylation curves along G1/S/G2-M. Methylation and transcriptome data come from different cells or unsynchronized samples without matched pairing, since each cell's methylation must be placed at its own pseudo-time position The goal is cell cycle ordering itself from methylation data alone — reCAT recovers order from transcriptome data, not from methylation profiles Only a few cells are available: binning methylation rates in sliding windows along the cycle requires enough cells per window for a stable smoothed curve http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Projects single-cell bisulfite methylation profiles onto a reCAT-recovered cell cycle pseudo time-series derived from matched scRNA-seq data, to reveal whole-genome methylation variation along the cycle (e.g., higher methylation at G1/S in mESC-MT, Fig. 4d). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Projects single-cell bisulfite methylation profiles onto a reCAT-recovered cell cycle pseudo time-series derived from matched scRNA-seq data, to reveal whole-genome methylation variation along the cycle (e.g., higher methylation at G1/S in mESC-MT, Fig. 4d).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Methylation and transcriptome data come from different cells or unsynchronized samples without matched pairing, since each cell's methylation must be placed at its own pseudo-time position The goal is cell cycle ordering itself from methylation data alone — reCAT recovers order from transcriptome data, not from methylation profiles Only a few cells are available: binning methylation rates in sliding windows along the cycle requires enough cells per window for a stable smoothed curve

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes/PCs) is too large for downstream clustering, trajectory inference, or visualization, and a fixed-size representative subset that preserves rare cell states is needed.
skills.name: metric-space-distance-thresholding
skills.search_text: metric-space-distance-thresholding Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes/PCs) is too large for downstream clustering, trajectory inference, or visualization, and a fixed-size representative subset that preserves rare cell states is needed. When the dataset is already small enough that current computational analysis methods handle routine tasks (clustering, trajectory inference, visualization) without sketching. When a uniform random subsample is acceptable and similarity/dissimilarity between gene expression patterns need not be preserved — though note uniform subsampling risks overlooking rare cell states. When downstream algorithm assumptions are incompatible with a metric-sphere model; the article notes Sphetcher's model might be less compatible with algorithms other than Louvain community detection and Monocle 2. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sketching of large single-cell RNA-seq datasets by selecting representative cells within covering spheres using thresholding over sphere radii combined with greedy set cover, as implemented in Sphetcher. Produces a fixed-size subset ('spherical sketch') that evenly covers the transcriptomic space better than uniform or box-based (geometric) sketches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Sketching of large single-cell RNA-seq datasets by selecting representative cells within covering spheres using thresholding over sphere radii combined with greedy set cover, as implemented in Sphetcher. Produces a fixed-size subset ('spherical sketch') that evenly covers the transcriptomic space better than uniform or box-based (geometric) sketches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset is already small enough that current computational analysis methods handle routine tasks (clustering, trajectory inference, visualization) without sketching. When a uniform random subsample is acceptable and similarity/dissimilarity between gene expression patterns need not be preserved — though note uniform subsampling risks overlooking rare cell states. When downstream algorithm assumptions are incompatible with a metric-sphere model; the article notes Sphetcher's model might be less compatible with algorithms other than Louvain community detection and Monocle 2.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq trajectories must be inferred beyond RNA velocity, e.g. propagating fates from progenitor (NEUROG3) clusters to terminal fates (SC-α, SC-β, SC-EC) using a potential-energy-biased Markov chain.
skills.name: metropolis-monte-carlo-trajectory-sampling
skills.search_text: metropolis-monte-carlo-trajectory-sampling Use when scRNA-seq trajectories must be inferred beyond RNA velocity, e.g. propagating fates from progenitor (NEUROG3) clusters to terminal fates (SC-α, SC-β, SC-EC) using a potential-energy-biased Markov chain. RNA velocity profiles are robust and available — FateCompass then uses velocity to direct the Markov-chain edges instead of the potential-energy bias No prior biological knowledge of progenitor/sink states is available (e.g. cancer studies), since the differentiation-potential mode depends on such annotations The goal is TF-activity inference (linear model / differential motif activity) rather than fate-probability estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs stochastic cell-fate trajectories by sampling Markov-chain transitions whose transition kernel is biased by a differentiation-potential energy landscape, accepting or rejecting proposed moves with a Metropolis-style criterion (Equations 5-8 of FateCompass). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Reconstructs stochastic cell-fate trajectories by sampling Markov-chain transitions whose transition kernel is biased by a differentiation-potential energy landscape, accepting or rejecting proposed moves with a Metropolis-style criterion (Equations 5-8 of FateCompass).
skills.when_to_use_negative: RNA velocity profiles are robust and available — FateCompass then uses velocity to direct the Markov-chain edges instead of the potential-energy bias No prior biological knowledge of progenitor/sink states is available (e.g. cancer studies), since the differentiation-potential mode depends on such annotations The goal is TF-activity inference (linear model / differential motif activity) rather than fate-probability estimation

skills.description: Use when jointly inferring tumor phylogeny from bulk DNA-seq and scRNA-seq SNV read counts and the joint posterior over Z, P^s, P^b admits no closed form, requiring iterative full-conditional MCMC sampling.
skills.name: metropolis-within-gibbs-posterior-sampling
skills.search_text: metropolis-within-gibbs-posterior-sampling Use when jointly inferring tumor phylogeny from bulk DNA-seq and scRNA-seq SNV read counts and the joint posterior over Z, P^s, P^b admits no closed form, requiring iterative full-conditional MCMC sampling. Input lacks single-cell RNA-seq read counts (Rs/Xs), so the beta-binomial bursting-likelihood component of the joint posterior cannot be formed — the predecessor Canopy, which uses bulk DNA alone, is the appropriate choice. Mutations have zero alternative read counts across all cells (or cells have zero total counts), so mutation-specific bursting rates alpha and beta cannot be estimated and the mutations should be filtered out before sampling. The goal is point-estimate inference where a closed-form posterior exists and MCMC sampling (with its convergence bottleneck) is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Canopy2's Bayesian sampling engine: because the joint posterior over clonal configuration Z, single-cell assignment P^s, and bulk composition P^b has no closed form, Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC repeatedly samples each parameter from its full conditional, mixing a binomial likelihood (bulk DNA WES) with beta-binomial likelihoods (scRNA-seq). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Canopy2's Bayesian sampling engine: because the joint posterior over clonal configuration Z, single-cell assignment P^s, and bulk composition P^b has no closed form, Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC repeatedly samples each parameter from its full conditional, mixing a binomial likelihood (bulk DNA WES) with beta-binomial likelihoods (scRNA-seq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks single-cell RNA-seq read counts (Rs/Xs), so the beta-binomial bursting-likelihood component of the joint posterior cannot be formed — the predecessor Canopy, which uses bulk DNA alone, is the appropriate choice. Mutations have zero alternative read counts across all cells (or cells have zero total counts), so mutation-specific bursting rates alpha and beta cannot be estimated and the mutations should be filtered out before sampling. The goal is point-estimate inference where a closed-form posterior exists and MCMC sampling (with its convergence bottleneck) is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking mtDNA variant callers on single-cell data, or when comparing an mgatk-based clone-assignment workflow against MQuad-based selection using concordance to known source labels.
skills.name: mgatk-vmr-strand-correlation-variant-calling
skills.search_text: mgatk-vmr-strand-correlation-variant-calling Use when benchmarking mtDNA variant callers on single-cell data, or when comparing an mgatk-based clone-assignment workflow against MQuad-based selection using concordance to known source labels. When the goal is to identify informative mtDNA variants for clonal substructure in conventional scRNA-seq — the article states mgatk was 'designed primarily for single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (scATAC-seq)', so use MQuad instead When input is raw FASTQ — alignment (STAR) and duplicate removal (Picard MarkDuplicates) must be done upstream first http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call mtDNA variants from single-cell data with mgatk using its suggested quality cutoffs — log10(VMR) ≥ −2 and strand correlation coefficient ≥ 0.65 — and feed the resulting mtSNVs to vireoSNP for clonal assignment. In this article it serves as the benchmark comparator against the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline on the Kim ccRCC Smart-seq2 scRNA-seq dataset (mgatk: 312 mtSNVs, 64% concordance vs MQuad: ~146 variants, 93%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Call mtDNA variants from single-cell data with mgatk using its suggested quality cutoffs — log10(VMR) ≥ −2 and strand correlation coefficient ≥ 0.65 — and feed the resulting mtSNVs to vireoSNP for clonal assignment. In this article it serves as the benchmark comparator against the cellSNP-MQuad-VireoSNP pipeline on the Kim ccRCC Smart-seq2 scRNA-seq dataset (mgatk: 312 mtSNVs, 64% concordance vs MQuad: ~146 variants, 93%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify informative mtDNA variants for clonal substructure in conventional scRNA-seq — the article states mgatk was 'designed primarily for single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (scATAC-seq)', so use MQuad instead When input is raw FASTQ — alignment (STAR) and duplicate removal (Picard MarkDuplicates) must be done upstream first

skills.description: Use when tumor FASTQ/BAM reads (DNA-seq or RNA-seq) need HLA class I genotyping to constrain MHC-I peptide binding predictions, or when custom allele files must be merged into typed allele sets.
skills.name: mhc-class-i-allele-typing-with-optitype
skills.search_text: mhc-class-i-allele-typing-with-optitype Use when tumor FASTQ/BAM reads (DNA-seq or RNA-seq) need HLA class I genotyping to constrain MHC-I peptide binding predictions, or when custom allele files must be merged into typed allele sets. The goal is HLA class II genotyping — OptiType covers class I only; HLA-HD (hlahd.sh with freqdata, split, dict reference data) is the class II path in ScanNeo2 Reads are from normal samples — rows with type 'normal' in samples.tsv are excluded from HLA typing Already curated allele lists exist per sample — use the custom mode instead of re-running read-based yara+OptiType typing http://edamontology.org/topic_3337 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Determines patient HLA class I alleles as required downstream by ScanNeo2's neoantigen prediction, by filtering tumor DNA-seq/RNA-seq reads for HLA reads with yara and aligning them against a panel of HLA class I alleles with OptiType, with per-source allele outputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Determines patient HLA class I alleles as required downstream by ScanNeo2's neoantigen prediction, by filtering tumor DNA-seq/RNA-seq reads for HLA reads with yara and aligning them against a panel of HLA class I alleles with OptiType, with per-source allele outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is HLA class II genotyping — OptiType covers class I only; HLA-HD (hlahd.sh with freqdata, split, dict reference data) is the class II path in ScanNeo2 Reads are from normal samples — rows with type 'normal' in samples.tsv are excluded from HLA typing Already curated allele lists exist per sample — use the custom mode instead of re-running read-based yara+OptiType typing

skills.description: Use when TCR repertoires (paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq, e.g. PBMCs from SARS-CoV-2 patients) are clustered and clusters must be annotated as antigen-specific vs bystander using epitope database hits filtered by donor HLA binding.
skills.name: mhc-peptide-binding-prediction-filtering
skills.search_text: mhc-peptide-binding-prediction-filtering Use when TCR repertoires (paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq, e.g. PBMCs from SARS-CoV-2 patients) are clustered and clusters must be annotated as antigen-specific vs bystander using epitope database hits filtered by donor HLA binding. Specificity annotations already exist (e.g. training mvTCR's prediction task with known specificity labels via tutorials/03_training_prediction.ipynb) — no IEDB/HLA filtering needed Donor HLA types are unknown, since MHCFlurry filtering cannot be applied and IEDB hits cannot be narrowed to patient-specific binders Data are unpaired or lack CDR3 sequences, since mvTCR is mainly applied to paired data with gene expression plus alpha- and beta-CDR3 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Labels T-cell clusters as antigen-specific or bystander by querying TCRs against IEDB for epitope pairings and retaining only hits whose peptide is predicted (e.g. with MHCFlurry) to bind the donor's HLAs. This HLA-aware filtering converts generic epitope matches into patient-specific specificity annotations for downstream mvTCR cluster interpretation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Labels T-cell clusters as antigen-specific or bystander by querying TCRs against IEDB for epitope pairings and retaining only hits whose peptide is predicted (e.g. with MHCFlurry) to bind the donor's HLAs. This HLA-aware filtering converts generic epitope matches into patient-specific specificity annotations for downstream mvTCR cluster interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Specificity annotations already exist (e.g. training mvTCR's prediction task with known specificity labels via tutorials/03_training_prediction.ipynb) — no IEDB/HLA filtering needed Donor HLA types are unknown, since MHCFlurry filtering cannot be applied and IEDB hits cannot be narrowed to patient-specific binders Data are unpaired or lack CDR3 sequences, since mvTCR is mainly applied to paired data with gene expression plus alpha- and beta-CDR3

skills.name: mhc-region-exclusion
skills.search_text: mhc-region-exclusion Use when preprocessing GWAS summary statistics (e.g. via scPagwas::GWAS_summary_input) before SNP-to-pathway linking, to drop SNPs in the MHC region that exhibit extensive LD and would bias pathway association estimates. When the trait of interest is explicitly MHC-mediated (e.g. autoimmune H loci) and the MHC signal is biologically central rather than a confounder When the input is not raw GWAS summary statistics but an already preprocessed Pagwas object in which MHC filtering has already been applied When using LDSC-SEG, RolyPoly, or EPIC-style pipelines whose own annotation/filtering scheme differs from scPagwas's 20 kb proximal window and KEGG pathway framework http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 During scPagwas GWAS preprocessing, SNPs located in the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region on chromosome 6 (25–35 Mbp) are removed because extensive linkage disequilibrium in this region confounds pathway-based polygenic regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383

skills.description: Use when training a topic/VAE model on multi-batch single-cell counts where cell states may be batch-confounded, and you must quantify or penalize the dependence between expression-rate predictions and batch covariates.
skills.name: mi-lower-bound-estimation-mine
skills.search_text: mi-lower-bound-estimation-mine Use when training a topic/VAE model on multi-batch single-cell counts where cell states may be batch-confounded, and you must quantify or penalize the dependence between expression-rate predictions and batch covariates. Data has no batch structure or technical covariates — the MI regularization target is absent, so the ELBO-only objective suffices Cell states are not batch-confounded (standard batch-correction methods like Seurat v3, FastMNN, Scanorama, or Harmony are appropriate) Input is continuous/normalized expression rather than raw counts — the count-based topic model assumption is violated Estimate the mutual information between a topic model's predicted expression and technical-effect predictions using the MINE neural-network lower bound, so the estimate can be used as a regularizer (CODAL objective) that disentangles biological from technical effects in batched single-cell count data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Estimate the mutual information between a topic model's predicted expression and technical-effect predictions using the MINE neural-network lower bound, so the estimate can be used as a regularizer (CODAL objective) that disentangles biological from technical effects in batched single-cell count data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has no batch structure or technical covariates — the MI regularization target is absent, so the ELBO-only objective suffices Cell states are not batch-confounded (standard batch-correction methods like Seurat v3, FastMNN, Scanorama, or Harmony are appropriate) Input is continuous/normalized expression rather than raw counts — the count-based topic model assumption is violated

skills.description: Use when segmenting single cells in MIBI or other multiplexed tissue imaging data (e.g., breast carcinoma TMA images) where cells have internal aberrant or incomplete membranes that defeat standard segmentation approaches.
skills.name: mibi-image-single-cell-segmentation
skills.search_text: mibi-image-single-cell-segmentation Use when segmenting single cells in MIBI or other multiplexed tissue imaging data (e.g., breast carcinoma TMA images) where cells have internal aberrant or incomplete membranes that defeat standard segmentation approaches. The input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table and no segmentation masks are needed The images are simple, uniformly shaped cells without internal or incomplete membranes, where simpler methods (dilation from nuclei, Voronoi tessellation) suffice — though note the article shows Voronoi undersegments cells towards the lumen The task is generic deep-learning segmentation rather than reproducing MIRIAM's membrane-extension approach (e.g., Mesmer alone, which MIRIAM outperformed: DSC 0.65 ± 0.08 vs 0.59 ± 0.10) http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Applies the MIRIAM pipeline (Matlab or Python implementation) to Multiplexed Ion Beam Imaging (MIBI) breast carcinoma tissue images to produce single-cell segmentation masks, demonstrating cross-platform transfer from multiplexed immunofluorescence to a different modality and marker set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/cyto.a.24541
skills.summary: Applies the MIRIAM pipeline (Matlab or Python implementation) to Multiplexed Ion Beam Imaging (MIBI) breast carcinoma tissue images to produce single-cell segmentation masks, demonstrating cross-platform transfer from multiplexed immunofluorescence to a different modality and marker set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-cell feature/quantification table and no segmentation masks are needed The images are simple, uniformly shaped cells without internal or incomplete membranes, where simpler methods (dilation from nuclei, Voronoi tessellation) suffice — though note the article shows Voronoi undersegments cells towards the lumen The task is generic deep-learning segmentation rather than reproducing MIRIAM's membrane-extension approach (e.g., Mesmer alone, which MIRIAM outperformed: DSC 0.65 ± 0.08 vs 0.59 ± 0.10)

skills.description: Use when a per-cell assignment (e.g., inferred spatial layer L1-L6 for 15413 scRNA-seq cells) must be scored against ground-truth multiclass labels and compared to a chance/majority baseline.
skills.name: micro-f1-multiclass-evaluation
skills.search_text: micro-f1-multiclass-evaluation Use when a per-cell assignment (e.g., inferred spatial layer L1-L6 for 15413 scRNA-seq cells) must be scored against ground-truth multiclass labels and compared to a chance/majority baseline. Input predictions have no per-cell ground-truth labels — micro F1 cannot be computed without paired reference labels The evaluation target is continuous (e.g., reconstructed spatial gene expression values) rather than categorical class membership Only 2 of 1020 STARmap genes or unaligned cell sets are available, so predicted and truth label vectors have different lengths/indices Evaluates per-cell label assignments (e.g., SpaOTsc's L1-L6 spatial-origin assignment of mouse visual cortex scRNA-seq cells) as a multiclass classification problem using scikit-learn's micro-averaged F1 score, benchmarked against a majority-population baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Evaluates per-cell label assignments (e.g., SpaOTsc's L1-L6 spatial-origin assignment of mouse visual cortex scRNA-seq cells) as a multiclass classification problem using scikit-learn's micro-averaged F1 score, benchmarked against a majority-population baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input predictions have no per-cell ground-truth labels — micro F1 cannot be computed without paired reference labels The evaluation target is continuous (e.g., reconstructed spatial gene expression values) rather than categorical class membership Only 2 of 1020 STARmap genes or unaligned cell sets are available, so predicted and truth label vectors have different lengths/indices

skills.description: Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile from a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt) shows a distinct low-intensity background peak in its log2 histogram that must be filtered out before downstream expression analysis.
skills.name: microarray-background-subtraction
skills.search_text: microarray-background-subtraction Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile from a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt) shows a distinct low-intensity background peak in its log2 histogram that must be filtered out before downstream expression analysis. Input is RNA-seq count data rather than microarray intensity values — the cutoff is defined on normalized array log-intensities, not read counts Data has not yet been normalized — run the PIMENTo Preprocess Data step (quantile or LOESS normalization) first, since the cutoff is chosen on the quantile-normalized histogram The intensity distribution shows no separable background population in the [5,7] log2 zoomed histogram, so no defensible valley/inflection point exists to set the cutoff http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies a background-vs-signal intensity cutoff from a PIMENTo-rendered Background Cutoff histogram of quantile-normalized microarray data, then removes all genes whose maximal intensity does not exceed that cutoff (6.1 on the log2 scale for the example data) to yield a background-subtracted matrix for downstream analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-9004-7_11
skills.summary: Identifies a background-vs-signal intensity cutoff from a PIMENTo-rendered Background Cutoff histogram of quantile-normalized microarray data, then removes all genes whose maximal intensity does not exceed that cutoff (6.1 on the log2 scale for the example data) to yield a background-subtracted matrix for downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is RNA-seq count data rather than microarray intensity values — the cutoff is defined on normalized array log-intensities, not read counts Data has not yet been normalized — run the PIMENTo Preprocess Data step (quantile or LOESS normalization) first, since the cutoff is chosen on the quantile-normalized histogram The intensity distribution shows no separable background population in the [5,7] log2 zoomed histogram, so no defensible valley/inflection point exists to set the cutoff

skills.search_text: microarray-batch-effect-removal Use when a normalized gene-level expression matrix aggregated across multiple GEO studies or platforms shows study-of-origin batch structure, and downstream comparison requires homogenized batch distributions while preserving perturbation/differentiation signal. When the data come from a single study/series and platform, so no known batch covariate exists to adjust When only raw probe intensities are available — missing/low-intensity filtering, probe-to-gene-symbol collapsing (collapseRows) and limma normalization must be done first When the goal is to quantify, not remove, batch structure; this skill applies a known-covariate adjustment, not de novo latent-factor discovery (e.g. sva's surrogate variable estimation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Removes known batch effects (data series and platform) from a normalized merged microarray expression matrix using the parametric empirical Bayes adjustment implemented in sva, so that multi-study gene-expression data (e.g. the curated 3T3-L1 adipocyte datasets) can be compared while retaining biological signal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Removes known batch effects (data series and platform) from a normalized merged microarray expression matrix using the parametric empirical Bayes adjustment implemented in sva, so that multi-study gene-expression data (e.g. the curated 3T3-L1 adipocyte datasets) can be compared while retaining biological signal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the data come from a single study/series and platform, so no known batch covariate exists to adjust When only raw probe intensities are available — missing/low-intensity filtering, probe-to-gene-symbol collapsing (collapseRows) and limma normalization must be done first When the goal is to quantify, not remove, batch structure; this skill applies a known-covariate adjustment, not de novo latent-factor discovery (e.g. sva's surrogate variable estimation)

skills.search_text: microarray-data-normalization Use when raw microarray intensity data (e.g., a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt with gene IDs, symbols, and per-sample intensity columns) must be normalized before differential expression or background subtraction. The input is RNA-seq count data rather than microarray intensities — PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command expects microarray intensity columns The data have already been normalized; re-running quantile or LOESS normalization would distort downstream QC interpretations The goal is significance testing only — that is carried out separately with the 'samr' package, not during normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Normalizes microarray intensity data using PIMENTo, which implements quantile normalization (via the 'limma' package) and LOESS normalization (via the 'affy' package), then judges the better method by inspecting MA plots and dendrograms for batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-9004-7_11

skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-network-trimming Use when a complete weighted graph over cell states (landmarks) has been built from transitional-cell counts and must be reduced to a sparse, connected multi-branching trajectory network retaining only maximum-support edges. Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — the article states Mpath does not yet support this and lists it as a planned future extension Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets in which specific subset information is not known — the article notes Mpath is not yet extended to this setting Graphs whose nodes are not biologically meaningful landmark states with transitional-cell support, since the −w(e) MST heuristic presumes edge weights are cell counts http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Trims a complete landmark-to-landmark graph by computing a minimum spanning tree over edge distances defined as the negative count of transitional cells (−w(e)), so that only the highest-support edges survive. This is the graph-pruning step of Mpath that converts neighborhood-based cell state transition counts into a connected, multi-branching developmental skeleton. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Trims a complete landmark-to-landmark graph by computing a minimum spanning tree over edge distances defined as the negative count of transitional cells (−w(e)), so that only the highest-support edges survive. This is the graph-pruning step of Mpath that converts neighborhood-based cell state transition counts into a connected, multi-branching developmental skeleton.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development processes starting from multiple independent progenitor cell types — the article states Mpath does not yet support this and lists it as a planned future extension Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets in which specific subset information is not known — the article notes Mpath is not yet extended to this setting Graphs whose nodes are not biologically meaningful landmark states with transitional-cell support, since the −w(e) MST heuristic presumes edge weights are cell counts

skills.description: Use when inferring tree-shaped trajectories from single-cell expression data where a good clustering must be found automatically and cell connectivity should guide selection of end points (leaves) and branch points.
skills.name: minimum-spanning-tree-topology-estimation
skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-topology-estimation Use when inferring tree-shaped trajectories from single-cell expression data where a good clustering must be found automatically and cell connectivity should guide selection of end points (leaves) and branch points. The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The trajectory is multi-root/converging — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories without a manual work-around The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types — k-medoids may not work properly, requiring manual cluster merging Estimates a tree-shaped single-cell trajectory (linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating) by generating many k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings, constructing a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) backbone for each via Slingshot, and using cell connectivity plus the Calinski-Harabasz score to select the clustering/topology that best matches the data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Estimates a tree-shaped single-cell trajectory (linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating) by generating many k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings, constructing a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) backbone for each via Slingshot, and using cell connectivity plus the Calinski-Harabasz score to select the clustering/topology that best matches the data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles The trajectory is multi-root/converging — dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories without a manual work-around The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types — k-medoids may not work properly, requiring manual cluster merging

skills.description: Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories that include branches across two or more scRNA-seq datasets, and a tree-structured cell-state transition map (rather than a single linear path) is needed before trajectory tree alignment.
skills.name: minimum-spanning-tree-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: minimum-spanning-tree-trajectory-inference Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories that include branches across two or more scRNA-seq datasets, and a tree-structured cell-state transition map (rather than a single linear path) is needed before trajectory tree alignment. The input trajectories are single linear lineages where simpler DTW-based linear alignment suffices (existing tools mainly focus on linear alignment of single-cell trajectories). The trajectory structure contains complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees. The two datasets have very different global topological structures, since CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded for such datasets in the benchmarking test. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers branched single-cell pseudotime trajectories by building a minimum-spanning-tree over clusters (capital.tl.trajectory_tree) with pseudotime from diffusion pseudotime (capital.tl.dpt), enabling downstream tree alignment of scRNA-seq datasets in CAPITAL. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Infers branched single-cell pseudotime trajectories by building a minimum-spanning-tree over clusters (capital.tl.trajectory_tree) with pseudotime from diffusion pseudotime (capital.tl.dpt), enabling downstream tree alignment of scRNA-seq datasets in CAPITAL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input trajectories are single linear lineages where simpler DTW-based linear alignment suffices (existing tools mainly focus on linear alignment of single-cell trajectories). The trajectory structure contains complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL in its present form can deal only with trajectory trees. The two datasets have very different global topological structures, since CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded for such datasets in the benchmarking test.

skills.description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., log-count matrices pre-processed with Seurat V3.0) where batch correction must preserve local cell-to-cell structure, and a one-to-one matching of representative anchor cells across datasets is needed.
skills.name: minimum-weight-bipartite-matching
skills.search_text: minimum-weight-bipartite-matching Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., log-count matrices pre-processed with Seurat V3.0) where batch correction must preserve local cell-to-cell structure, and a one-to-one matching of representative anchor cells across datasets is needed. You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle'). You have extra-large datasets where exact blossom matching would be too slow — prefer the -greedy heuristic, or a different method if even greedy matching is infeasible. Your goal requires matching cell types absent from one dataset (e.g., alpha cells held out of CEL-Seq2) — the matching leaves such cells unmatched by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Core algorithmic step of BATMAN for scRNA-seq batch integration: anchors identified in each of two datasets are connected in a weighted bipartite graph (edges weighted by Euclidean distance), and a parsimonious one-to-one minimum-weight matching is found either exactly (blossom-based) or via a greedy approximation with ratio 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Core algorithmic step of BATMAN for scRNA-seq batch integration: anchors identified in each of two datasets are connected in a weighted bipartite graph (edges weighted by Euclidean distance), and a parsimonious one-to-one minimum-weight matching is found either exactly (blossom-based) or via a greedy approximation with ratio 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle'). You have extra-large datasets where exact blossom matching would be too slow — prefer the -greedy heuristic, or a different method if even greedy matching is infeasible. Your goal requires matching cell types absent from one dataset (e.g., alpha cells held out of CEL-Seq2) — the matching leaves such cells unmatched by design.

skills.description: Use when integrating exactly two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 10X PBMC 8k vs Pan T cells, or Splatter-simulated pairs) in gene or PCA space, prioritizing both batch mixing (iLISI) and local structure retention (RNN) over batch-effect removal alone.
skills.name: minimum-weight-matching-batch-correction
skills.search_text: minimum-weight-matching-batch-correction Use when integrating exactly two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 10X PBMC 8k vs Pan T cells, or Splatter-simulated pairs) in gene or PCA space, prioritizing both batch mixing (iLISI) and local structure retention (RNN) over batch-effect removal alone. You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') Input is raw counts that have not gone through Seurat V3.0 pre-processing to log-counts, or datasets lacking a comparable feature/PCA space across batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 BATMAN-style batch correction for two single-cell RNA-seq datasets: after Seurat V3.0 preprocessing to log-counts, a minimum-weight matching of anchor cells between datasets is used to derive local shifting vectors and apply the minimal total correction needed to align the query to the reference while preserving local structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: BATMAN-style batch correction for two single-cell RNA-seq datasets: after Seurat V3.0 preprocessing to log-counts, a minimum-weight matching of anchor cells between datasets is used to derive local shifting vectors and apply the minimal total correction needed to align the query to the reference while preserving local structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') Input is raw counts that have not gone through Seurat V3.0 pre-processing to log-counts, or datasets lacking a comparable feature/PCA space across batches

skills.description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq batches via BATMAN: anchors have been identified per dataset and a globally minimal one-to-one cell-to-cell correspondence (not mutual-nearest-neighbor) is needed to derive local shifting vectors for batch correction.
skills.name: minimum-weight-matching-blossom-algorithm
skills.search_text: minimum-weight-matching-blossom-algorithm Use when integrating two scRNA-seq batches via BATMAN: anchors have been identified per dataset and a globally minimal one-to-one cell-to-cell correspondence (not mutual-nearest-neighbor) is needed to derive local shifting vectors for batch correction. The task requires integrating more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation only works with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') The goal is a many-to-many or mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment rather than a strict one-to-one parsimonious matching of representative cells The input is a single dataset or the batches have no shared biological cell types, so meaningful cross-dataset anchor pairs cannot be identified http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes a parsimonious one-to-one minimum-weight matching between representative anchor cells of two scRNA-seq datasets on a weighted bipartite graph, as the core of the BATMAN batch integration method. Edge weights are Euclidean distances between cells in N-dimensional gene (log-count) space, and the exact blossom-based algorithm can be swapped for a greedy 2-approximation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Computes a parsimonious one-to-one minimum-weight matching between representative anchor cells of two scRNA-seq datasets on a weighted bipartite graph, as the core of the BATMAN batch integration method. Edge weights are Euclidean distances between cells in N-dimensional gene (log-count) space, and the exact blossom-based algorithm can be swapped for a greedy 2-approximation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires integrating more than two datasets — the current BATMAN implementation only works with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') The goal is a many-to-many or mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment rather than a strict one-to-one parsimonious matching of representative cells The input is a single dataset or the batches have no shared biological cell types, so meaningful cross-dataset anchor pairs cannot be identified

skills.description: Use when integrating exactly two single-cell RNA-seq batches (e.g. CEL-Seq2 vs Smart-Seq2 count matrices) where you need batch correction that maintains cell-to-cell (local) structure, and MNN-based tools underperform on iLISI/50-RNN.
skills.name: minimum-weight-matching-on-cell-graphs
skills.search_text: minimum-weight-matching-on-cell-graphs Use when integrating exactly two single-cell RNA-seq batches (e.g. CEL-Seq2 vs Smart-Seq2 count matrices) where you need batch correction that maintains cell-to-cell (local) structure, and MNN-based tools underperform on iLISI/50-RNN. You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current implementation of BATMAN works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') Your data is not single-cell expression matrices (e.g. already-integrated embeddings, bulk RNA-seq, or feature tables) You require mutually-nearest-neighbor semantics or multi-dataset harmonization pipelines like Harmony/Scanorama by design http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Core algorithmic skill of BATMAN: build a weighted bipartite graph between two scRNA-seq batches (partitions = datasets, edge weights = Euclidean distance between cells in N-dimensional gene space) and solve a minimum-weight one-to-one matching to derive local shifting vectors for batch correction. It preserves local dataset structure while using the minimal total correction necessary. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Core algorithmic skill of BATMAN: build a weighted bipartite graph between two scRNA-seq batches (partitions = datasets, edge weights = Euclidean distance between cells in N-dimensional gene space) and solve a minimum-weight one-to-one matching to derive local shifting vectors for batch correction. It preserves local dataset structure while using the minimal total correction necessary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to integrate more than two datasets — the current implementation of BATMAN works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is possible only 'in principle') Your data is not single-cell expression matrices (e.g. already-integrated embeddings, bulk RNA-seq, or feature tables) You require mutually-nearest-neighbor semantics or multi-dataset harmonization pipelines like Harmony/Scanorama by design

skills.description: Use when building an RBP-ncRNA edge list (e.g. from ENCORI/starBase CLIP data for human or mouse) whose nodes mix gene/lncRNA symbols, mature miRNA names, and circRNA IDs and must be converted to Ensembl, MIMAT*, and circBase identifiers.
skills.name: mirbase-accession-mapping
skills.search_text: mirbase-accession-mapping Use when building an RBP-ncRNA edge list (e.g. from ENCORI/starBase CLIP data for human or mouse) whose nodes mix gene/lncRNA symbols, mature miRNA names, and circRNA IDs and must be converted to Ensembl, MIMAT*, and circBase identifiers. Expression or differential-analysis data already keyed by Ensembl/MIMAT identifiers where no symbol-to-accession mapping is needed (e.g. the pre-processed brca_miRNA_re_se / brca_RNA_re_se internal fRNC datasets) Interaction sources other than ENCORI/starBase that use different identifier vocabularies incompatible with the package's ID mapping resources http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Standardizes identifiers when assembling the fRNC RBP-ncRNA network from ENCORI-derived interactions: lncRNA/gene symbols are mapped to Ensembl gene IDs, miRNA names to miRBase accession numbers of mature miRNAs (MIMAT*), and circRNAs to circBase IDs, so network edges use consistent, resolvable node identifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Standardizes identifiers when assembling the fRNC RBP-ncRNA network from ENCORI-derived interactions: lncRNA/gene symbols are mapped to Ensembl gene IDs, miRNA names to miRBase accession numbers of mature miRNAs (MIMAT*), and circRNAs to circBase IDs, so network edges use consistent, resolvable node identifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression or differential-analysis data already keyed by Ensembl/MIMAT identifiers where no symbol-to-accession mapping is needed (e.g. the pre-processed brca_miRNA_re_se / brca_RNA_re_se internal fRNC datasets) Interaction sources other than ENCORI/starBase that use different identifier vocabularies incompatible with the package's ID mapping resources

skills.name: mirna-annotation-against-mirbase
skills.search_text: mirna-annotation-against-mirbase Use when small RNA-seq reads (e.g., 50 nt serum FASTQ with 3' adapter TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG) have been STAR-aligned to hg19/hg38 and must be quantified against miRBase miRNAs to build a miRNA-by-sample count matrix. Reads have not yet been adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered by the COMPSRA QC module (e.g., raw FASTQ still containing the TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG adapter and random ligation bases) The goal is non-miRNA small RNA annotation (piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, circRNA) or microbial profiling — use the corresponding databases or the COMPSRA Microbe/BLAST module instead The data are not human (hg19/hg38); COMPSRA's prebuilt miRBase databases also cover rat (rno5/rno6), but other organisms require different resources http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Annotate STAR-mapped small RNA-seq reads to miRBase miRNAs using the COMPSRA Annotation module, producing per-sample miRNA read counts suitable for downstream aggregation and benchmarking against reference miRNA sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Annotate STAR-mapped small RNA-seq reads to miRBase miRNAs using the COMPSRA Annotation module, producing per-sample miRNA read counts suitable for downstream aggregation and benchmarking against reference miRNA sets.

skills.description: Use when annotating miRNAs in a plant species with a reference genome and you need a consolidated candidate precursor list combining public database annotations with novel sRNA-Seq-based predictions.
skills.name: mirna-database-aggregation
skills.search_text: mirna-database-aggregation Use when annotating miRNAs in a plant species with a reference genome and you need a consolidated candidate precursor list combining public database annotations with novel sRNA-Seq-based predictions. The species has no reference genome sequence — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences and ignores reads that do not map to the reference You need a curated, false-positive-free miRNA annotation set — the aggregated candidate list certainly contains false positive hits and requires downstream selection and wet-lab validation You only need annotations from a single database rather than a cross-database consolidated candidate list http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Aggregate already annotated plant miRNA precursors from four representative databases (miRBase v22.1, PmiREN v1.0, sRNAanno v1.0, PsRNA v1.0) using the iwa-miRNA miRNARetrival tool, then merge them with newly predicted precursors into a uniform genomic coordinate system to produce a comprehensive candidate list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Aggregate already annotated plant miRNA precursors from four representative databases (miRBase v22.1, PmiREN v1.0, sRNAanno v1.0, PsRNA v1.0) using the iwa-miRNA miRNARetrival tool, then merge them with newly predicted precursors into a uniform genomic coordinate system to produce a comprehensive candidate list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species has no reference genome sequence — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences and ignores reads that do not map to the reference You need a curated, false-positive-free miRNA annotation set — the aggregated candidate list certainly contains false positive hits and requires downstream selection and wet-lab validation You only need annotations from a single database rather than a cross-database consolidated candidate list

skills.description: Use when two small RNA-seq miRNA identification pipelines (e.g. COMPSRA and exceRpt) have been run on identical FASTQ inputs and you need to quantify detection overlap and independently validate tool-unique miRNA calls.
skills.name: mirna-detection-comparison-across-pipelines
skills.search_text: mirna-detection-comparison-across-pipelines Use when two small RNA-seq miRNA identification pipelines (e.g. COMPSRA and exceRpt) have been run on identical FASTQ inputs and you need to quantify detection overlap and independently validate tool-unique miRNA calls. The analysis goal is profiling non-miRNA small RNA classes (piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, circRNA) or microbial content rather than comparing miRNA detection between pipelines The two tools being compared were run on different samples or with mismatched parameters, making the overlap analysis invalid No independent external dataset is available to validate tool-unique miRNA calls http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces a head-to-head comparison of miRNA detection between the COMPSRA stand-alone pipeline and the web-based exceRpt pipeline on the same 12 serum small RNA-seq FASTQ samples, quantifying shared vs. tool-unique miRNA calls and validating unique calls against an external dataset (SRP120169). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Reproduces a head-to-head comparison of miRNA detection between the COMPSRA stand-alone pipeline and the web-based exceRpt pipeline on the same 12 serum small RNA-seq FASTQ samples, quantifying shared vs. tool-unique miRNA calls and validating unique calls against an external dataset (SRP120169).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is profiling non-miRNA small RNA classes (piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, circRNA) or microbial content rather than comparing miRNA detection between pipelines The two tools being compared were run on different samples or with mismatched parameters, making the overlap analysis invalid No independent external dataset is available to validate tool-unique miRNA calls

skills.description: Use when manually curating candidate plant miRNAs and needing to inspect arm-specific expression and 5p/3p arm-switching events of a selected precursor across available sRNA-Seq samples, as part of the manualCuration HTML report.
skills.name: mirna-expression-arm-selection-boxplotting
skills.search_text: mirna-expression-arm-selection-boxplotting Use when manually curating candidate plant miRNAs and needing to inspect arm-specific expression and 5p/3p arm-switching events of a selected precursor across available sRNA-Seq samples, as part of the manualCuration HTML report. The sRNA-Seq data come from a species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA ignores reads that do not map to the reference genome and cannot handle such data. The goal is downstream enrichment or cross-species comparative analysis of curated miRNAs — the article notes iwa-miRNA has limited ability for such downstream analysis. The candidate precursor has no supporting sRNA-Seq samples, so no arm expression/arm-selection events can be visualized. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates the expression-pattern panel of an iwa-miRNA manualCuration report: a boxplot of miRNA arm expression across sRNA-Seq samples that visualizes miRNA arm selection (5p vs 3p) events, rendered via Rmarkdown into the per-miRNA interactive HTML page. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Generates the expression-pattern panel of an iwa-miRNA manualCuration report: a boxplot of miRNA arm expression across sRNA-Seq samples that visualizes miRNA arm selection (5p vs 3p) events, rendered via Rmarkdown into the per-miRNA interactive HTML page.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sRNA-Seq data come from a species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA ignores reads that do not map to the reference genome and cannot handle such data. The goal is downstream enrichment or cross-species comparative analysis of curated miRNAs — the article notes iwa-miRNA has limited ability for such downstream analysis. The candidate precursor has no supporting sRNA-Seq samples, so no arm expression/arm-selection events can be visualized.

skills.description: Use when you have paired bulk mRNA and miRNA expression matrices (genes as rows, samples as columns) and want to predict miRNA expression in samples or pooled single-cell clusters lacking direct miRNA measurement.
skills.name: mirna-expression-prediction-from-bulk-mrna
skills.search_text: mirna-expression-prediction-from-bulk-mrna Use when you have paired bulk mRNA and miRNA expression matrices (genes as rows, samples as columns) and want to predict miRNA expression in samples or pooled single-cell clusters lacking direct miRNA measurement. The query sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the training cohort — accuracy loss is expected (quantified in Figure S9) scRNA-seq data has severe dropout such that detected genes are too sparse — a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes is required instead You need paired miRNA-protein prediction: large cohorts of paired miRNA-protein expression data are not available to train such a model http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Train and apply miRSCAPE, an XGBoost-based machine learning tool that predicts miRNA expression from paired bulk mRNA-miRNA cohorts (TCGA, GTEx, CCLE) and infers miRNA expression in single-cell clusters from scRNA-seq profiles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Train and apply miRSCAPE, an XGBoost-based machine learning tool that predicts miRNA expression from paired bulk mRNA-miRNA cohorts (TCGA, GTEx, CCLE) and infers miRNA expression in single-cell clusters from scRNA-seq profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the training cohort — accuracy loss is expected (quantified in Figure S9) scRNA-seq data has severe dropout such that detected genes are too sparse — a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes is required instead You need paired miRNA-protein prediction: large cohorts of paired miRNA-protein expression data are not available to train such a model

skills.description: Use when you have demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads plus miRNA reference annotations (GFF3/GTF) and need to distinguish miRNAs from isomiRs at single-nucleotide resolution and test their abundance between conditions (e.g. control vs knockout).
skills.name: mirna-isomir-hierarchical-read-counting
skills.search_text: mirna-isomir-hierarchical-read-counting Use when you have demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads plus miRNA reference annotations (GFF3/GTF) and need to distinguish miRNAs from isomiRs at single-nucleotide resolution and test their abundance between conditions (e.g. control vs knockout). skills.summary: Classify and quantify small RNA-seq reads as miRNAs/isomiRs (or piRNAs, siRNAs, tRNA/rRNA fragments) with single-nucleotide precision using tiny-count's hierarchical selection rules, then feed the per-sample counts matrix into tinyRNA's R-based differential expression step to detect condition-specific isomiRs.

skills.description: Use when scRNAseq clusters must be functionally annotated with miRNA markers via a miRNA-target autoencoder latent space, and you need to know whether normalization of the input counts table changes which markers/scores emerge.
skills.name: mirna-marker-ranking-across-normalizations

skills.description: Decision support for choosing SCSit's mismatch/indel tolerance parameters when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data and questioning whether the default one-mismatch/one-indel setting sacrifices too many reads.

skills.search_text: mismatch-indel-tolerant-read2-index-alignment Decision support for choosing SCSit's mismatch/indel tolerance parameters when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data and questioning whether the default one-mismatch/one-indel setting sacrifices too many reads. Input data is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcode data; SCSit's fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq, and support for other platforms is only potential, not demonstrated You need a tool that supports other single-cell sequencing platforms out of the box — SCSit states it 'will be updated and improved in time' for more platforms, so this is not yet available You only need the default preprocessing result and have no question about the tolerance trade-off; the paper already concludes the default one-mismatch/one-indel setting is optimal http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking skill for SCSit that evaluates whether relaxing the default Read2 index/indicator-sequence identification tolerance (one mismatch and one indel) to more than one mismatch and one indel is worthwhile. The paper found this yields only ~4–5% more identified reads at 20–40% more runtime (Table S4), so the default setting is retained. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for SCSit that evaluates whether relaxing the default Read2 index/indicator-sequence identification tolerance (one mismatch and one indel) to more than one mismatch and one indel is worthwhile. The paper found this yields only ~4–5% more identified reads at 20–40% more runtime (Table S4), so the default setting is retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcode data; SCSit's fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq, and support for other platforms is only potential, not demonstrated You need a tool that supports other single-cell sequencing platforms out of the box — SCSit states it 'will be updated and improved in time' for more platforms, so this is not yet available You only need the default preprocessing result and have no question about the tolerance trade-off; the paper already concludes the default one-mismatch/one-indel setting is optimal

skills.description: Use when evaluating robustness of a 101-base-window RNA editing classifier to missing RNAseq coverage — e.g. quantifying FP/FN rates after randomly swapping RNAseq nucleotide frequencies for genomic reference frequencies in >30% of flanking positions.

Input is real RNAseq data whose 101-base windows are already fully covered — perturbation would misrepresent actual missing-data behavior You need to impute missing values in production inference rather than measure robustness — REDInet_Inference.py already ships reference-genome imputation as a BETA FEATURE, so use that instead of a simulation harness Ground truth labels are unavailable — FP/FN rates cannot be computed against unlabeled predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Stress-test the REDInet A-to-I RNA editing classifier by simulating missing RNAseq coverage: RNAseq-derived nucleotide frequencies are randomly replaced with genomic reference frequencies across flanking positions of 8×101 feature matrices, and false-positive/false-negative rates are measured on the degraded inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf107

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real RNAseq data whose 101-base windows are already fully covered — perturbation would misrepresent actual missing-data behavior You need to impute missing values in production inference rather than measure robustness — REDInet_Inference.py already ships reference-genome imputation as a BETA FEATURE, so use that instead of a simulation harness Ground truth labels are unavailable — FP/FN rates cannot be computed against unlabeled predictions

skills.description: Use when comparing isoform call sets from StringTie2 and VIsoQLR on long-read RNA-seq (e.g., SIRV or minigene assays) and you need to identify missed-exon isoforms and distinguish genuine boundary extensions from tool artifacts.
skills.name: missing-exon-isoform-detection
skills.search_text: missing-exon-isoform-detection Use when comparing isoform call sets from StringTie2 and VIsoQLR on long-read RNA-seq (e.g., SIRV or minigene assays) and you need to identify missed-exon isoforms and distinguish genuine boundary extensions from tool artifacts. Input is a single tool's isoform set with no second call set to compare against — boundary-extension and missed-exon behaviors are defined relative to the VIsoQLR consensus. Data are short-read or Sanger/capillary electrophoresis based — the article states these traditional techniques have drawbacks across the full spectrum of splicing events and this skill is built on long-read sequencing isoform calls. The goal is de novo transcriptome-wide discovery (e.g., with epi2me-labs wf-transcriptomes/bambu) rather than focused one-gene fine-tuning of splicing-assay isoforms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematic cross-tool comparison of StringTie2- and VIsoQLR-called isoforms on long-read sequencing data to flag isoforms with missing central exons that StringTie2 fails to call (or calls with extra exons), and to annotate StringTie2 outer-boundary extensions as artifacts by cross-checking against shared BAM alignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Systematic cross-tool comparison of StringTie2- and VIsoQLR-called isoforms on long-read sequencing data to flag isoforms with missing central exons that StringTie2 fails to call (or calls with extra exons), and to annotate StringTie2 outer-boundary extensions as artifacts by cross-checking against shared BAM alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single tool's isoform set with no second call set to compare against — boundary-extension and missed-exon behaviors are defined relative to the VIsoQLR consensus. Data are short-read or Sanger/capillary electrophoresis based — the article states these traditional techniques have drawbacks across the full spectrum of splicing events and this skill is built on long-read sequencing isoform calls. The goal is de novo transcriptome-wide discovery (e.g., with epi2me-labs wf-transcriptomes/bambu) rather than focused one-gene fine-tuning of splicing-assay isoforms.

skills.name: missingness-indicator-matrix-encoding
skills.search_text: missingness-indicator-matrix-encoding Use when a sparse single-cell AS probability (PSI) matrix contains NA entries from dropouts and the downstream step (e.g. spectral clustering in SCASL) requires a complete feature matrix that also preserves original missingness information. The AS probability matrix is already complete (no NA entries) — the imputation loop and indicator rows add no information. Downstream clustering operates directly on the raw junction-read count matrix (junc_matrix.csv) rather than the AS probability matrix. The goal is differential splicing analysis with known cell labels (e.g. BRIE18 or Expedition19 style), for which unsupervised imputation-then-clustering is not the intended workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Impute missing AS probabilities in a single-cell alternative splicing matrix with an iterative distance-weighted KNN procedure, then vertically concatenate the imputed matrix with a binary NA-indicator matrix so that downstream clustering sees both imputed values and original missingness patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: Impute missing AS probabilities in a single-cell alternative splicing matrix with an iterative distance-weighted KNN procedure, then vertically concatenate the imputed matrix with a binary NA-indicator matrix so that downstream clustering sees both imputed values and original missingness patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AS probability matrix is already complete (no NA entries) — the imputation loop and indicator rows add no information. Downstream clustering operates directly on the raw junction-read count matrix (junc_matrix.csv) rather than the AS probability matrix. The goal is differential splicing analysis with known cell labels (e.g. BRIE18 or Expedition19 style), for which unsupervised imputation-then-clustering is not the intended workflow.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing a SpatialExperiment gene-by-spot count matrix (e.g. Visium human DLPFC) before fitting nnSVG, where mitochondrial genes and genes with low UMI counts or detection in too few spots must be dropped to reduce runtime and improve p-value calibration.
skills.name: mitochondrial-gene-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: mitochondrial-gene-qc-filtering Use when preprocessing a SpatialExperiment gene-by-spot count matrix (e.g. Visium human DLPFC) before fitting nnSVG, where mitochondrial genes and genes with low UMI counts or detection in too few spots must be dropped to reduce runtime and improve p-value calibration. If the goal is spatial-domain marker genes (mean-level changes between domains) rather than continuous SVGs, this filtering context from the nnSVG SVG-detection workflow is not the right framework If counts are already normalized logcounts without a raw counts assay — filter_genes operates on the raw count matrix with UMI-count and percent-of-spots thresholds If downstream analysis requires mitochondrial genes retained (e.g. QC metric computation itself), since filter_mito removes them outright http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Removes mitochondrial genes (and optionally low-expressed genes) from a spatially-resolved transcriptomics count matrix using the nnSVG Bioconductor package's filter_genes module before SVG detection. On the Visium human DLPFC tutorial dataset with default parameters it removed 13 mitochondrial genes and 30216 of 33525 low-expression genes, retaining 3396 of 21803 genes in the paper's reported run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z
skills.summary: Removes mitochondrial genes (and optionally low-expressed genes) from a spatially-resolved transcriptomics count matrix using the nnSVG Bioconductor package's filter_genes module before SVG detection. skills.description: Use when quantifying per-droplet contamination features (e.g., percent spliced reads, debris scores) in droplet snRNA-seq, where mitochondrial reads must be excluded so the metric reflects splicing status rather than extranuclear debris content.
skills.name: mitochondrial-read-exclusion
skills.search_text: mitochondrial-read-exclusion Use when quantifying per-droplet contamination features (e.g., percent spliced reads, debris scores) in droplet snRNA-seq, where mitochondrial reads must be excluded so the metric reflects splicing status rather than extranuclear debris content. When the goal is to measure mitochondrial contamination itself (e.g., plotting pct.mt vs. debris score) — mito reads must be counted there, not excluded When input is already a filtered feature/barcode matrix without gene-level mapping, since mito genes can no longer be identified and excluded by pattern For scRNA-seq filtering with EmptyDrops-style assumptions, where mito-based debris scoring behaves differently than in snRNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Excludes reads mapping to mitochondrial genes when computing per-droplet metrics such as percent-spliced-reads for snRNA-seq contamination quantification, because mito-encoded genes are the canonical debris-upregulated markers and their inclusion conflates the debris signal with the nuclear/background separation metric. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Excludes reads mapping to mitochondrial genes when computing per-droplet metrics such as percent-spliced-reads for snRNA-seq contamination quantification, because mito-encoded genes are the canonical debris-upregulated markers and their inclusion conflates the debris signal with the nuclear/background separation metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to measure mitochondrial contamination itself (e.g., plotting pct.mt vs. debris score) — mito reads must be counted there, not excluded When input is already a filtered feature/barcode matrix without gene-level mapping, since mito genes can no longer be identified and excluded by pattern For scRNA-seq filtering with EmptyDrops-style assumptions, where mito-based debris scoring behaves differently than in snRNA-seq

skills.description: Use when raw 10X droplet counts are loaded (sparse Matrix / SCE object) and you need per-droplet MT% or MALAT1% to assess extranuclear RNA contamination, tune debris-score filtering, or benchmark which droplets a filter (DIEM, EmptyDrops, hard cutoffs) retains.
skills.name: mitochondrial-read-fraction-qc
skills.search_text: mitochondrial-read-fraction-qc Use when raw 10X droplet counts are loaded (sparse Matrix / SCE object) and you need per-droplet MT% or MALAT1% to assess extranuclear RNA contamination, tune debris-score filtering, or benchmark which droplets a filter (DIEM, EmptyDrops, hard cutoffs) retains. The data is not droplet-based 10X output or lacks mitochondrial/MALAT1 gene annotations matching '^mt-' / '^malat1$', since get_gene_pct relies on these gene-name patterns The goal is to replace DIEM's expression-based debris scoring entirely — MT% cutoffs are described as ad hoc and hard cutoffs can retain debris droplets and drop nuclear droplets in snRNA-seq Comparing debris scores or MT% thresholds across independent samples for integration — the paper warns the debris score 'cannot be assumed to exist on the same scale in independent experiments' http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute per-droplet mitochondrial read fraction (pct.mt) and MALAT1% from a 10X feature-barcode matrix using the diem package's get_gene_pct, using these extranuclear-contamination metrics as QC covariates for droplet filtering decisions (e.g. DIEM vs EmptyDrops comparison). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Compute per-droplet mitochondrial read fraction (pct.mt) and MALAT1% from a 10X feature-barcode matrix using the diem package's get_gene_pct, using these extranuclear-contamination metrics as QC covariates for droplet filtering decisions (e.g. DIEM vs EmptyDrops comparison).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data is not droplet-based 10X output or lacks mitochondrial/MALAT1 gene annotations matching '^mt-' / '^malat1$', since get_gene_pct relies on these gene-name patterns The goal is to replace DIEM's expression-based debris scoring entirely — MT% cutoffs are described as ad hoc and hard cutoffs can retain debris droplets and drop nuclear droplets in snRNA-seq Comparing debris scores or MT% thresholds across independent samples for integration — the paper warns the debris score 'cannot be assumed to exist on the same scale in independent experiments'

skills.description: Use when detecting differentially perturbed cell types in scRNA-seq with patient replicates, especially when naive methods (Augur AUC, nDEG counts) risk false positives from individual-to-individual variability or cell-count confounding.

skills.search_text: mixed-effects-distance-estimation Use when detecting differentially perturbed cell types in scRNA-seq with patient replicates, especially when naive methods (Augur AUC, nDEG counts) risk false positives from individual-to-individual variability or cell-count confounding. Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to counts and requires normalized data Data are heavily over-clustered or clustering/annotation was informed by the same expression data (double dipping), which biases estimated distances downward toward false negatives Goal is differential abundance (changing cell proportions) rather than differential state — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate transcriptomic distances between cell-type populations across conditions using scDist's linear mixed-effects model on PC scores, correcting for individual-to-individual variability while controlling false positives. Provides a statistically rigorous, >60x faster alternative to gene-wise nDEG counting, which is confounded by cells-per-cell-type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Estimate transcriptomic distances between cell-type populations across conditions using scDist's linear mixed-effects model on PC scores, correcting for individual-to-individual variability while controlling false positives. skills.search_text: mixed-model-differential-state-testing Use when analyzing scRNA-seq with multiple samples, groups, and cell subpopulations and cell-level (mixed-model) DS testing is preferred over pseudobulk aggregation, e.g. to compare mmDS against pbDS or when per-cell modeling is desired. skills.description: Use when compressing a Harmony-integrated reference atlas into a portable Symphony reference or when mapping query cells into that reference's embedding via soft cluster assignment.
skills.name: mixture-model-soft-clustering
skills.search_text: mixture-model-soft-clustering Use when compressing a Harmony-integrated reference atlas into a portable Symphony reference or when mapping query cells into that reference's embedding via soft cluster assignment. The goal is discovering novel cell types absent from the reference — Symphony's mapping metrics may be uninformative when a novel population closely resembles an existing reference population, and de novo analysis of the query alone is needed The reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage (Condition I), where soft-cluster-based mapping is less flexible than de novo Harmony integration The analysis requires de novo integration of all datasets together rather than reference-based mapping (e.g. BBKNN, Seurat anchors, or Harmony on the full combined data) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Symphony compresses a Harmony-integrated single-cell reference by fitting a mixture model with soft cluster assignments and centroids, then reuses the stored mixture components to softly assign query cells to reference clusters during mapping. This soft-clustering step is what makes million-cell references mappable in seconds without access to raw per-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x

skills.name: mixture-of-experts-batch-correction

You need novel cell type discovery — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone, and mapping metrics are less informative when a novel population closely resembles an existing reference population The reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage for the query context (Condition I), limiting equivalence with de novo Harmony integration Reference and query datasets use different feature sets with no defined optimal selection (e.g. scATAC-seq peaks), where mapping is not immediately clear how to optimally perform http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Symphony's query-mapping step that softly assigns query cells to reference mixture-model components and regresses out query batch effects using stored reference parameters, placing cells in the reference's harmonized low-dimensional embedding.
