skills.description: Use when you need to infer a joint latent representation from paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein counts) with modality-specific encoders and a mixture-of-experts posterior.
skills.name: mixture-of-experts-variational-posterior-implementation
skills.search_text: mixture-of-experts-variational-posterior-implementation Use when you need to infer a joint latent representation from paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein counts) with modality-specific encoders and a mixture-of-experts posterior. Input data are already normalized values rather than raw counts — scMM is designed for end-to-end learning by modeling raw count data with different probability distributions (e.g. negative binomial likelihoods). The task is generic multimodal VAE modeling on non-single-cell paired data (e.g. MNIST-SVHN images or CUB image-caption pairs) — use the upstream iffsid/mmvae repository directly instead. Only a single modality is available with no prospect of joint inference — the MoE posterior provides no benefit over a unimodal VAE. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements scMM's mixture-of-experts multimodal VAE, in which each modality's encoder estimates its own recognition posterior and the experts are mixed with equal weights to infer a joint latent representation from single-cell multiomics counts. Rationale: MoE factorization lets scMM handle missing/complex modalities while achieving end-to-end learning on raw counts via modality-specific likelihoods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Implements scMM's mixture-of-experts multimodal VAE, in which each modality's encoder estimates its own recognition posterior and the experts are mixed with equal weights to infer a joint latent representation from single-cell multiomics counts. Rationale: MoE factorization lets scMM handle missing/complex modalities while achieving end-to-end learning on raw counts via modality-specific likelihoods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already normalized values rather than raw counts — scMM is designed for end-to-end learning by modeling raw count data with different probability distributions (e.g. negative binomial likelihoods). The task is generic multimodal VAE modeling on non-single-cell paired data (e.g. MNIST-SVHN images or CUB image-caption pairs) — use the upstream iffsid/mmvae repository directly instead. Only a single modality is available with no prospect of joint inference — the MoE posterior provides no benefit over a unimodal VAE.

skills.name: mixture-parameter-selection-via-kta
skills.search_text: mixture-parameter-selection-via-kta Use when applying TransferCluster to a small scRNA-Seq target dataset: after learning Wtrg against the source NMF dictionary Hsrc, theta must be chosen without ground-truth labels to construct Xtrg_new = theta*Hsrc*W'trg + (1-theta)*Xtrg. No source reference dataset is available, so there is no Hsrc/W'trg reconstruction to mix — plain TargetCluster (SC3 on the target alone) is the correct route Ground-truth target labels exist and a supervised criterion could be used directly; KTA is an unsupervised substitute for cases without labels Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes only the shared gene set can be used and calls this loss of vital information a deferred open problem http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Unsupervised selection of the mixture parameter theta that balances the reconstructed target dataset against the original target data in the scRNA transfer learning framework, using Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores as a label-free cluster-quality proxy before SC3 clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Unsupervised selection of the mixture parameter theta that balances the reconstructed target dataset against the original target data in the scRNA transfer learning framework, using Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores as a label-free cluster-quality proxy before SC3 clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No source reference dataset is available, so there is no Hsrc/W'trg reconstruction to mix — plain TargetCluster (SC3 on the target alone) is the correct route Ground-truth target labels exist and a supervised criterion could be used directly; KTA is an unsupervised substitute for cases without labels Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes only the shared gene set can be used and calls this loss of vital information a deferred open problem

skills.description: Use when transferring knowledge from a source scRNA-Seq dataset to a smaller target and needing to choose the convex-combination mixture parameter theta without ground-truth labels, or when validating that unsupervised KTA-based theta selection tracks supervised ARI.
skills.name: mixture-parameter-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: mixture-parameter-sweep-analysis Use when transferring knowledge from a source scRNA-Seq dataset to a smaller target and needing to choose the convex-combination mixture parameter theta without ground-truth labels, or when validating that unsupervised KTA-based theta selection tracks supervised ARI. Source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes a loss of vital information is inevitable since only shared genes can be used, and handling differing gene sets is deferred to future work Ground-truth target labels are available and a supervised criterion (ARI) can be optimized directly, making unsupervised KTA selection unnecessary The downstream task is not clustering of the modified target dataset (the paper's downstream anchor is SC3; other analyses are untested in this workflow) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sweeps the transfer-learning mixture parameter theta over [0,1] and selects its value automatically via unsupervised Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores computed on SC3 clusterings of the modified target dataset, optionally correlating KTA against supervised ARI to validate the selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Sweeps the transfer-learning mixture parameter theta over [0,1] and selects its value automatically via unsupervised Kernel Target Alignment (KTA) scores computed on SC3 clusterings of the modified target dataset, optionally correlating KTA against supervised ARI to validate the selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target datasets share only a small set of transcripts — the paper notes a loss of vital information is inevitable since only shared genes can be used, and handling differing gene sets is deferred to future work Ground-truth target labels are available and a supervised criterion (ARI) can be optimized directly, making unsupervised KTA selection unnecessary The downstream task is not clustering of the modified target dataset (the paper's downstream anchor is SC3; other analyses are untested in this workflow)

skills.search_text: mlp-baseline-model-comparison Use when evaluating whether a neural ODE transcriptomic forecaster genuinely outperforms a standard multi-layer MLP on paired two-time-point single-cell data, i.e., a controlled prediction-accuracy (MSE) ablation on held-out cells is needed. Input is unpaired standard scRNA-seq with no two-time-point measurements of the same cell population, since neither the neural ODE nor the paired benchmark can be trained on t=0 -> t=1 transitions The goal is mechanistic gene regulatory network inference rather than forecasting accuracy; the article states network inference from RNAForecaster remains future work Predictions must extend beyond short time scales without validation data; the article has not evaluated limits of predictability over diverse timescales and biological conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmarking procedure in which the RNAForecaster neural ODE (trained with Flux.jl/DiffEqFlux.jl via the Tsit5 solver) is compared against a five-hidden-layer MLP baseline on matched training/validation splits, using validation-set MSE at t=1 and across recursive future predictions to quantify the accuracy benefit of the neural ODE formulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793

skills.name: mlp-gene-classification
skills.search_text: mlp-gene-classification Use when spatial transcriptomics HVGs (e.g. top 2000 from Seurat FindVariableFeatures()) restricted to a MIMO cell-communication network must be assigned binary communication-relevance labels and scored, in the CPPLS-MLP pipeline after network construction. No MIMO communication network has been constructed yet — the CPPLS regression and MIMO-graph step (upstream in the CPPLS-MLP pipeline) must run first, since classification is restricted to network-involved HVGs The analysis goal is constructing the cell-cell communication network itself (CPPLS regression on RMD files), not classifying genes against that network The classification criterion must be based on something other than GeneCards/GO strong-communication database labels — the article notes these methods 'lack a standardized classification criterion' beyond such database labeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains an MLP neural network (Python >= 3.7) on HVGs from the CPPLS-MLP MIMO communication network, using GeneCards/GO strong-communication labels ('receptor', 'ligand', 'cell-cell adhesion', 'intercellular interaction') as binary targets, to classify top-2000 HVGs as cell-communication-related on spatial transcriptomics datasets such as seqFISH+ mouse cortex and Seq-Scope mouse colon. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Trains an MLP neural network (Python >= 3.7) on HVGs from the CPPLS-MLP MIMO communication network, using GeneCards/GO strong-communication labels ('receptor', 'ligand', 'cell-cell adhesion', 'intercellular interaction') as binary targets, to classify top-2000 HVGs as cell-communication-related on spatial transcriptomics datasets such as seqFISH+ mouse cortex and Seq-Scope mouse colon.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No MIMO communication network has been constructed yet — the CPPLS regression and MIMO-graph step (upstream in the CPPLS-MLP pipeline) must run first, since classification is restricted to network-involved HVGs The analysis goal is constructing the cell-cell communication network itself (CPPLS regression on RMD files), not classifying genes against that network The classification criterion must be based on something other than GeneCards/GO strong-communication database labels — the article notes these methods 'lack a standardized classification criterion' beyond such database labeling

Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases — the 2001-bp coverage window gives incomplete flanking coverage and inaccurate α estimates Distinguishing identical TE copies such as HERVK isoforms that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions Data without sufficient multi-mapping TE reads is better handled by MATES v0.1.8's simple mode rather than full α regression http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Trains a multilayer perceptron regressor on AutoEncoder-encoded unique-read coverage vectors (Vu), combined with TE family one-hot embeddings, to predict a locus-specific multi-mapping ratio (α) used by MATES to probabilistically allocate multi-mapping reads to specific TE loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7

skills.description: Use when a cudaMMC (or 3D-GNOME-style) chromatin simulation has produced a bead-coordinate model file that must be converted into a parseable PDBx/mmCIF structure, especially when bead counts exceed legacy PDB limits.
skills.name: mmcif-structure-file-generation
skills.search_text: mmcif-structure-file-generation Use when a cudaMMC (or 3D-GNOME-style) chromatin simulation has produced a bead-coordinate model file that must be converted into a parseable PDBx/mmCIF structure, especially when bead counts exceed legacy PDB limits. The downstream tool only consumes legacy PDB format and the model has few enough beads to fit PDB limits (mmCIF is chosen specifically because PDB cannot represent high bead counts). The goal is to inspect or post-process raw cudaMMC simulation data (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) rather than convert a finished 3D model to a structure file. http://edamontology.org/topic_3176 Convert cudaMMC multiscale chromatin 3D model output into PDBx/mmCIF format by writing each bead of the modeled chromatin chain as an atom_site coordinate record. mmCIF is chosen over legacy PDB because it supports a higher number of beads per structure, required for high-resolution whole chromosome models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad588
skills.summary: Convert cudaMMC multiscale chromatin 3D model output into PDBx/mmCIF format by writing each bead of the modeled chromatin chain as an atom_site coordinate record. mmCIF is chosen over legacy PDB because it supports a higher number of beads per structure, required for high-resolution whole chromosome models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream tool only consumes legacy PDB format and the model has few enough beads to fit PDB limits (mmCIF is chosen specifically because PDB cannot represent high bead counts). The goal is to inspect or post-process raw cudaMMC simulation data (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) rather than convert a finished 3D model to a structure file.

skills.description: Use when you have trained a cross-modality mapping model (e.g. scMMGAN) between two domains and need to quantify both distributional fidelity (MMD) and point-wise correspondence preservation (correlation of columns known to correspond).
skills.name: mmd-distribution-distance-evaluation
skills.search_text: mmd-distribution-distance-evaluation Use when you have trained a cross-modality mapping model (e.g. scMMGAN) between two domains and need to quantify both distributional fidelity (MMD) and point-wise correspondence preservation (correlation of columns known to correspond). You have not yet trained a mapping model — MMD/correlation require generated G(x1) and G(x2) outputs; they cannot evaluate a single-domain dataset alone. Your two input domains were preprocessed with different pipelines (e.g. only one MAGIC-corrected or scaled to a different interval than [-10, 10]) — the distribution- and correlation-based metrics become incomparable across models. You only need to measure distributional similarity and do not care about point-wise correspondence — in that case MMD alone suffices, since all models achieve similarly low MMDs and correlation adds the discriminating signal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark cross-modality GAN mappings (scMMGAN vs CycleGAN vs CMAE) by computing maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) and correlation between generated mappings G(x1)/G(x2) and the opposite modality, as demonstrated on DBIT-seq mouse embryo spatial transcriptomics/proteomics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Benchmark cross-modality GAN mappings (scMMGAN vs CycleGAN vs CMAE) by computing maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) and correlation between generated mappings G(x1)/G(x2) and the opposite modality, as demonstrated on DBIT-seq mouse embryo spatial transcriptomics/proteomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet trained a mapping model — MMD/correlation require generated G(x1) and G(x2) outputs; they cannot evaluate a single-domain dataset alone. Your two input domains were preprocessed with different pipelines (e.g. only one MAGIC-corrected or scaled to a different interval than [-10, 10]) — the distribution- and correlation-based metrics become incomparable across models. You only need to measure distributional similarity and do not care about point-wise correspondence — in that case MMD alone suffices, since all models achieve similarly low MMDs and correlation adds the discriminating signal.

skills.description: Use when you need to align single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics count data into a unified embedding space via deep transfer learning — e.g., before computing SC-ST mapping matrices or pseudo-spatial adjacency for single-cell spatial landscapes.
skills.name: mmd-loss-transfer-learning-model-training
skills.search_text: mmd-loss-transfer-learning-model-training Use when you need to align single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics count data into a unified embedding space via deep transfer learning — e.g., before computing SC-ST mapping matrices or pseudo-spatial adjacency for single-cell spatial landscapes. Input matrices have not been normalize_total + log1p transformed — the encoder and dropout-rate correction assume this preprocessing ST and SC data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work The goal is deconvolving spots into a fixed number of cell types rather than single-cell mapping — the article notes such deconvolution cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train the STEM transfer learning model (SOmodel in PyTorch) that encodes SC and ST count matrices into a shared 128-d latent space by combining a spatial Gaussian loss with an MMD (maximum mean discrepancy) loss that eliminates the SC-ST domain gap. This produces the encoder (netE) whose embeddings are later used to build SC-ST mapping matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Train the STEM transfer learning model (SOmodel in PyTorch) that encodes SC and ST count matrices into a shared 128-d latent space by combining a spatial Gaussian loss with an MMD (maximum mean discrepancy) loss that eliminates the SC-ST domain gap. This produces the encoder (netE) whose embeddings are later used to build SC-ST mapping matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices have not been normalize_total + log1p transformed — the encoder and dropout-rate correction assume this preprocessing ST and SC data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work The goal is deconvolving spots into a fixed number of cell types rather than single-cell mapping — the article notes such deconvolution cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparing DGMP against external baselines rather than decomposing its own components — use a state-of-the-art comparison benchmark instead The task uses undirected PPI networks or patient-level features rather than the directed GRN with sample-averaged multi-omics gene features Only a single model configuration is available with no code path to toggle components (DGCN/MLP/directionality), making true ablation infeasible

skills.search_text: model-ensemble-distribution-comparison-across-methods Use when porting or re-implementing a stochastic 3D chromatin modelling tool and you need to demonstrate the new version produces statistically equivalent ensembles, by comparing within-ensemble similarity distributions. Input is a single 3D model per method — this skill requires an ensemble of ~100 models per method to form a within-ensemble similarity distribution The goal is a runtime/performance benchmark rather than model-quality equivalence — use timing benchmarks instead, since cudaMMC's headline advantage is speed Comparing models from different chromosomes or non-equivalent settings — the ensembles must be chr21 (or the same locus) with matched simulation parameters Validates that a rewritten or ported structure-modelling engine (e.g. cudaMMC vs. its predecessor 3D-GNOME) preserves model quality by comparing within-ensemble similarity distributions of two ensembles of 100 chromatin models for the same locus (chr21). It quantifies method equivalence as a difference in distribution medians of less than 1%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single 3D model per method — this skill requires an ensemble of ~100 models per method to form a within-ensemble similarity distribution The goal is a runtime/performance benchmark rather than model-quality equivalence — use timing benchmarks instead, since cudaMMC's headline advantage is speed Comparing models from different chromosomes or non-equivalent settings — the ensembles must be chr21 (or the same locus) with matched simulation parameters

skills.description: Use when a paired/repeated-measure RNA-seq differential expression analysis needs per-gene fit metrics (AIC/BIC) to compare mixed-effects models, since kimma is the only tool among limma/dream that reports AIC for its models.
skills.name: model-fit-metrics-extraction-aic
skills.search_text: model-fit-metrics-extraction-aic Use when a paired/repeated-measure RNA-seq differential expression analysis needs per-gene fit metrics (AIC/BIC) to compare mixed-effects models, since kimma is the only tool among limma/dream that reports AIC for its models. The design is unpaired with no random effect or kinship to compare — kimma_lm (fixed-effect lm) models suffice and mixed-model AIC is not the target quantity. The goal is genotype/eQTL association modeling (kmFit_eQTL with dat_snp/dat_map), which is a separate kimma workflow rather than per-gene fit-metric extraction. The model must include a genetic kinship covariance matrix (kimma_lmerel with kin_subset); plain kimma_lme fit metrics do not capture kinship's effect on model fit. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract per-gene model fit metrics (AIC/BIC) from kimma's kmFit linear mixed effects runs, which fit RNA-seq paired designs via lme4::lmer and uniquely report fit metrics alongside fixed-effect estimates and P-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Extract per-gene model fit metrics (AIC/BIC) from kimma's kmFit linear mixed effects runs, which fit RNA-seq paired designs via lme4::lmer and uniquely report fit metrics alongside fixed-effect estimates and P-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The design is unpaired with no random effect or kinship to compare — kimma_lm (fixed-effect lm) models suffice and mixed-model AIC is not the target quantity. The goal is genotype/eQTL association modeling (kmFit_eQTL with dat_snp/dat_map), which is a separate kimma workflow rather than per-gene fit-metric extraction. The model must include a genetic kinship covariance matrix (kimma_lmerel with kin_subset); plain kimma_lme fit metrics do not capture kinship's effect on model fit.

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is same-species benchmarking only — the diagonal entries of the matrix duplicate standard held-out test evaluation (e.g., human 0.9503, mouse 0.9219) Species lack annotations or sufficient data to train species-specific models, making a cross-species matrix impossible to populate (noted as a limitation in the article discussion) Comparing feature-engineering-based classifiers (like LncCat) with deep-learning predictors (e.g., RNAsamba, mRNN) on general coding-potential tasks rather than assessing transfer of a fixed set of trained models

skills.search_text: modified-base-vocabulary-design Use when building or adapting a deep-learning basecaller for ONT direct RNA data and the goal is single-step detection of modified bases (e.g. m6A, m1A, inosine) rather than modification-unaware basecalling followed by re-squiggling. The downstream pipeline already performs modification-unaware basecalling followed by re-squiggling with modification-specific models (e.g. Dorado plus modification models) — the expanded vocabulary is meant to replace that multi-step workflow Only canonical bases are needed and no modified-base calling is required — a standard four-base vocabulary suffices and avoids training-data burden The target modifications are highly similar chemical structures — streamlined NanoSpeech models for these are still under investigation and development http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Designs an expanded output-token vocabulary (canonical bases A, C, G, U plus modification tokens such as inosine, encoded as N1..Nn, together with boundary and gap symbols) so a transformer basecaller can ab initio call modified bases in a single pass instead of requiring separate basecalling, re-squiggling, and modification-detection models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf709
skills.summary: Designs an expanded output-token vocabulary (canonical bases A, C, G, U plus modification tokens such as inosine, encoded as N1..Nn, together with boundary and gap symbols) so a transformer basecaller can ab initio call modified bases in a single pass instead of requiring separate basecalling, re-squiggling, and modification-detection models.

skills.description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell trait labels (outcome, condition, cell type) and you have detected co-expression modules and need to know which modules associate with which trait.
skills.name: module-trait-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: module-trait-correlation-analysis Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell trait labels (outcome, condition, cell type) and you have detected co-expression modules and need to know which modules associate with which trait. The input is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated expression profiles that lack single-cell metadata — SCANet's pseudo-bulking of neighboring cells and trait-association workflow assumes per-cell trait labels. The goal is causal inference of regulatory relationships: GCNs rely on correlation, not causation, so module–trait correlations can yield false positives and should not be read as mechanistic direction without downstream GRN validation (e.g. GRNBoost2 + RcisTarget). Trait labels are missing or ambiguous — the module–trait correlation step requires cell-level metadata (outcome, condition, cell type) to correlate against. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Correlates single-cell-derived gene co-expression modules (inferred with SCANet's modified WGCNA/BioNERO framework) against cell-level trait metadata such as patient outcome or diet condition, to identify modules tracking a phenotype (e.g. M11 with deceased patients, M21 with survivors). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Correlates single-cell-derived gene co-expression modules (inferred with SCANet's modified WGCNA/BioNERO framework) against cell-level trait metadata such as patient outcome or diet condition, to identify modules tracking a phenotype (e.g. M11 with deceased patients, M21 with survivors).

skills.description: Use when estimating cell-cell similarity for scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (e.g. EDGE) without full pairwise distance computation, by hashing binary gene-expression sketches from many weak learners.
skills.name: modulo-hashing-similarity-estimation
skills.search_text: modulo-hashing-similarity-estimation Use when estimating cell-cell similarity for scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (e.g. EDGE) without full pairwise distance computation, by hashing binary gene-expression sketches from many weak learners. Input is raw counts or unnormalized expression — sketch thresholds require log-normalized values (e.g. log2 of counts scaled to the median library size). Exact pairwise distances are required rather than hash-collision-based similarities, or the dataset's memory budget cannot accommodate the chosen hash table size H. The goal is direct embedding/visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) rather than building a similarity matrix for downstream k-NNG and spectral embedding. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Ensemble weak-learner similarity search from the EDGE method: each of many weak learners sketches cells into binary bit vectors, applies modulo hashing to map sketch dot-products to hash codes, and cell pairs sharing a hash code receive similarity score 1; final similarities are averaged across all learners. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Ensemble weak-learner similarity search from the EDGE method: each of many weak learners sketches cells into binary bit vectors, applies modulo hashing to map sketch dot-products to hash codes, and cell pairs sharing a hash code receive similarity score 1; final similarities are averaged across all learners.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or unnormalized expression — sketch thresholds require log-normalized values (e.g. log2 of counts scaled to the median library size). Exact pairwise distances are required rather than hash-collision-based similarities, or the dataset's memory budget cannot accommodate the chosen hash table size H. The goal is direct embedding/visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) rather than building a similarity matrix for downstream k-NNG and spectral embedding.

skills.description: Use when calling somatic SNVs from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq BAMs (e.g., with cb_sniffer) and per-cell variant read counts must be deduplicated at the molecule level using the UB_tag before computing per-site false-positive rates.

The scRNA-seq data come from full-length plate-based platforms (e.g., Fluidigm C1/SMART-seq) that lack 10x Chromium UB_tag molecular barcodes, so molecule-level deduplication is not possible. The goal is de novo variant discovery from the RNA data itself — this skill only genotypes pre-called somatic variants; discovery is done upstream with eWGS of paired tumor/normal samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Collapses PCR duplicates in 10x Chromium single-cell data by counting reads per Chromium molecular barcode (UB_tag), so that variant-supporting evidence in each cell reflects unique molecules rather than PCR amplification artifacts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Collapses PCR duplicates in 10x Chromium single-cell data by counting reads per Chromium molecular barcode (UB_tag), so that variant-supporting evidence in each cell reflects unique molecules rather than PCR amplification artifacts.

skills.search_text: molecule-information-to-count-matrix-parsing Use when starting from 10x Genomics droplet molecule information (raw per-molecule records with cell barcode, UMI, gene) and you need per-sample UMI count matrices for cell calling or barcode-swapping exclusion. Input is already a gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. a 10x matrix.mtx/h5 bundle); skip parsing and go directly to cell calling or exclusion. Data are plate-based (e.g. Smart-seq2 mouse T-cell plates from E-MTAB-6843); molecule information parsing for 10x droplet data does not apply. The analysis target is whole-transcript coverage outside exonic regions; the pipeline here counts only read pairs mapping to the exonic region of each gene. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Parse 10x Genomics molecule information files into per-sample UMI count matrices as the first step of droplet-based scRNA-seq processing, enabling downstream cell calling with emptyDrops. In this study it prepares the droplet-prepared mouse epithelial libraries (ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854, sequenced on HiSeq 2500 and HiSeq 4000) for barcode-swapping and cell-calling analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x

skills.description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X, NovaSeq) contain multiplexed samples and artefactual swapped cell libraries are suspected.
skills.name: molecule-level-barcode-swapping-exclusion
skills.search_text: molecule-level-barcode-swapping-exclusion Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X, NovaSeq) contain multiplexed samples and artefactual swapped cell libraries are suspected. Data were sequenced on non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500), where the swapping fraction is negligible The dataset is plate-based (Smart-seq2) rather than droplet-based; the plate-data regression approach for estimating swapping fraction is the appropriate method there Only one sample is present, so cross-sample UMI/cell-barcode/gene sharing cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A computational method to exclude individual molecules that have swapped between samples in 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq experiments by removing molecules sharing the same UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene combination across samples, then re-calling cells with emptyDrops. It addresses artefactual swapped cell libraries generated by barcode swapping on patterned flow-cell sequencers such as the HiSeq 4000 (~2.5% swapped reads). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: A computational method to exclude individual molecules that have swapped between samples in 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq experiments by removing molecules sharing the same UMI, cell barcode, and aligned gene combination across samples, then re-calling cells with emptyDrops. It addresses artefactual swapped cell libraries generated by barcode swapping on patterned flow-cell sequencers such as the HiSeq 4000 (~2.5% swapped reads).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were sequenced on non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500), where the swapping fraction is negligible The dataset is plate-based (Smart-seq2) rather than droplet-based; the plate-data regression approach for estimating swapping fraction is the appropriate method there Only one sample is present, so cross-sample UMI/cell-barcode/gene sharing cannot be assessed

skills.description: Use when learning latent representations from a normalized highly-variable-gene scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. .npz of HVG profiles) via self-supervised momentum contrast instead of deep generative reconstruction.
skills.name: momentum-contrast-queue-management
skills.search_text: momentum-contrast-queue-management Use when learning latent representations from a normalized highly-variable-gene scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. .npz of HVG profiles) via self-supervised momentum contrast instead of deep generative reconstruction. The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, analogous to other deep-neural-network methods Batch effects are present and uncorrected: Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods, so batch correction must be done beforehand A decoder/reconstruction objective is required (e.g. denoising or imputation tasks), where deep generative approaches like scVI are the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A MoCo-style self-supervised training scheme in which a DenseNet latent feature encoder for single-cell gene expression is trained against a momentum-updated key encoder and a contrastive queue, minimizing an InfoNCE loss between original and augmented (gene-zeroed/shuffled) expression profiles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
