When all cell types in the new sample are not represented in the reference/training data — NeuCA and this exhaustive-annotation benchmark assume no unknown cell types When a fixed, pre-specified train/test split already exists and repeated random resampling would not answer the question When the goal is de novo clustering without any labeled training data (unsupervised-only setting) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark protocol from the NeuCA paper that generates Monte Carlo train/test splits of the FACS-sorted 10X Genomics PBMC dataset (Zheng_8ct_PBMC) to evaluate cell annotation methods by accurately assigned rate and ARI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol from the NeuCA paper that generates Monte Carlo train/test splits of the FACS-sorted 10X Genomics PBMC dataset (Zheng_8ct_PBMC) to evaluate cell annotation methods by accurately assigned rate and ARI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all cell types in the new sample are not represented in the reference/training data — NeuCA and this exhaustive-annotation benchmark assume no unknown cell types When a fixed, pre-specified train/test split already exists and repeated random resampling would not answer the question When the goal is de novo clustering without any labeled training data (unsupervised-only setting)

skills.description: Use when you need p-values (not just effect sizes) for per-cell-type between-condition transcriptomic distances from scDist mixed-model output, especially with few patients per group where MLE-based tests would be biased.
skills.name: monte-carlo-wald-p-value-estimation
skills.search_text: monte-carlo-wald-p-value-estimation Use when you need p-values (not just effect sizes) for per-cell-type between-condition transcriptomic distances from scDist mixed-model output, especially with few patients per group where MLE-based tests would be biased. Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist requires normalized expression and cannot currently be applied directly to counts The question is differential abundance (proportion changes) rather than differential state — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead Data are over-clustered — condition-specific effects can cause downward bias and false negatives as the number of clusters increases http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scDist's inference core: after shrinkage of squared PC loadings toward zero, the distance D_K is estimated from posterior samples and its null significance is obtained as an empirical Monte Carlo p-value computed from draws of the sum of Wald statistics, with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom from lmerTest. This provides statistically rigorous significance calls on cell-type transcriptomic distances despite small patient numbers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: scDist's inference core: after shrinkage of squared PC loadings toward zero, the distance D_K is estimated from posterior samples and its null significance is obtained as an empirical Monte Carlo p-value computed from draws of the sum of Wald statistics, with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom from lmerTest. This provides statistically rigorous significance calls on cell-type transcriptomic distances despite small patient numbers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist requires normalized expression and cannot currently be applied directly to counts The question is differential abundance (proportion changes) rather than differential state — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead Data are over-clustered — condition-specific effects can cause downward bias and false negatives as the number of clusters increases

skills.description: Use when you have scored spots or cells (e.g., SenePy hub scores) on spatially resolved data and need to test whether the score is spatially clustered or colocalized with a marker-defined region such as Col1a1+ fibrosis.
skills.name: morans-i-spatial-autocorrelation-testing
skills.search_text: morans-i-spatial-autocorrelation-testing Use when you have scored spots or cells (e.g., SenePy hub scores) on spatially resolved data and need to test whether the score is spatially clustered or colocalized with a marker-defined region such as Col1a1+ fibrosis. Data are non-spatial single-cell suspensions — sp.score_hub applies, but Moran's I spatial autocorrelation and fibrosis colocalization testing are not meaningful without spatial coordinates The AnnData expression matrix is already scaled — SenePy scoring assumes raw or normalized (not scaled) data because score_hub binarizes by default Species is human — this workflow retrieves the 8 mouse heart hub signatures and would need the corresponding human hubs instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether a per-spot composite senescence score derived from SenePy hub signatures on Visium myocardial-infarction sections exhibits significant spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I), and quantifies colocalization of senescence-outlier spots with Col1a1-expressing fibrotic regions across the post-MI time course. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Tests whether a per-spot composite senescence score derived from SenePy hub signatures on Visium myocardial-infarction sections exhibits significant spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I), and quantifies colocalization of senescence-outlier spots with Col1a1-expressing fibrotic regions across the post-MI time course.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are non-spatial single-cell suspensions — sp.score_hub applies, but Moran's I spatial autocorrelation and fibrosis colocalization testing are not meaningful without spatial coordinates The AnnData expression matrix is already scaled — SenePy scoring assumes raw or normalized (not scaled) data because score_hub binarizes by default Species is human — this workflow retrieves the 8 mouse heart hub signatures and would need the corresponding human hubs instead

skills.description: Use when you have spatially reconstructed (or truth) single-cell coordinates with cell-type annotations and need to detect which cell-type pairs are significantly co-localized, e.g. after CellContrast spatial inference.
skills.name: morans-r-colocalization-analysis
skills.search_text: morans-r-colocalization-analysis Use when you have spatially reconstructed (or truth) single-cell coordinates with cell-type annotations and need to detect which cell-type pairs are significantly co-localized, e.g. after CellContrast spatial inference. Input SC data has no reconstructed or reference spatial coordinates — Moran's R requires locations, so use a spatial reconstruction skill first Tissue has a high level of repeating elements or a large gap between SC and ST reference, where spatial reconstruction itself is unreliable and co-localization calls would inherit the bias You only need cell-cell communication inference rather than cell-type spatial co-localization patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detects cell-type co-localization pairs from reconstructed spatial locations using SpatialDM Moran's R spatial autocorrelation, encoding binary cell-type occupancy per location and calling significant pairs at p<=0.05 for downstream Fisher's exact comparison against reference patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Detects cell-type co-localization pairs from reconstructed spatial locations using SpatialDM Moran's R spatial autocorrelation, encoding binary cell-type occupancy per location and calling significant pairs at p<=0.05 for downstream Fisher's exact comparison against reference patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input SC data has no reconstructed or reference spatial coordinates — Moran's R requires locations, so use a spatial reconstruction skill first Tissue has a high level of repeating elements or a large gap between SC and ST reference, where spatial reconstruction itself is unreliable and co-localization calls would inherit the bias You only need cell-cell communication inference rather than cell-type spatial co-localization patterns

skills.description: Use when paired single-cell RNA-seq with full-length TCR sequencing is available (e.g. plate-based smart-seq2, >3500 CD8 TILs) and you must test whether annotated CD8 TIL states share overlapping TCR clonotypes within a sample.
skills.name: morisita-horn-repertoire-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: morisita-horn-repertoire-overlap-analysis Use when paired single-cell RNA-seq with full-length TCR sequencing is available (e.g. plate-based smart-seq2, >3500 CD8 TILs) and you must test whether annotated CD8 TIL states share overlapping TCR clonotypes within a sample. Single-cell data lacking TCR sequences — clonotype reconstruction and Morisita-Horn overlap cannot be computed Bulk TCR repertoire data without per-cell transcriptomic state annotations — states to compare cannot be defined Comparing repertoires across different mice/samples — clonotypes must be grouped separately per mouse before computing overlap http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify clonal relatedness between annotated single-cell T cell transcriptomic states by reconstructing TCR clonotypes from paired scRNA/TCR-seq and computing pairwise Morisita-Horn overlap indices between state repertoires (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like) within each biological replicate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Quantify clonal relatedness between annotated single-cell T cell transcriptomic states by reconstructing TCR clonotypes from paired scRNA/TCR-seq and computing pairwise Morisita-Horn overlap indices between state repertoires (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like) within each biological replicate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell data lacking TCR sequences — clonotype reconstruction and Morisita-Horn overlap cannot be computed Bulk TCR repertoire data without per-cell transcriptomic state annotations — states to compare cannot be defined Comparing repertoires across different mice/samples — clonotypes must be grouped separately per mouse before computing overlap

skills.description: Use when re-annotated cell labels from an integration method (e.g., scMoMaT Leiden labels at resolution 0.9) must be compared against a paper's original published labels on the same mosaic dataset to argue annotation quality.
skills.name: mosaic-dataset-label-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: mosaic-dataset-label-annotation-matching Use when re-annotated cell labels from an integration method (e.g., scMoMaT Leiden labels at resolution 0.9) must be compared against a paper's original published labels on the same mosaic dataset to argue annotation quality. When the two label sets come from different cell sets or batches that cannot be aligned cell-for-cell — kNN agreement requires labels defined on identical cells When the goal is quantitative correspondence to a ground-truth cell type annotation rather than agreement with local per-matrix neighborhood structure (this metric measures self-consistency, not external accuracy) When a modality lacks a usable low-dimensional representation (e.g., too few features after peak remapping) — agreement must be computed per modality, so dropping modality averages silently changes the metric http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates whether cell type labels produced by a mosaic-integration method (e.g., scMoMaT Leiden clusters) agree with per-batch cell–cell variation better than originally published labels, by computing kNN agreement in each input data matrix's own reduced space (PCA for scRNA/protein, LSI for scATAC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Evaluates whether cell type labels produced by a mosaic-integration method (e.g., scMoMaT Leiden clusters) agree with per-batch cell–cell variation better than originally published labels, by computing kNN agreement in each input data matrix's own reduced space (PCA for scRNA/protein, LSI for scATAC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the two label sets come from different cell sets or batches that cannot be aligned cell-for-cell — kNN agreement requires labels defined on identical cells When the goal is quantitative correspondence to a ground-truth cell type annotation rather than agreement with local per-matrix neighborhood structure (this metric measures self-consistency, not external accuracy) When a modality lacks a usable low-dimensional representation (e.g., too few features after peak remapping) — agreement must be computed per modality, so dropping modality averages silently changes the metric

skills.description: Use when a mosaic scMultiome layout contains batches lacking a modality (e.g., no scRNA-seq or CITE-seq protein counts) and feature entities such as peaks and genes cannot be connected by the available input data matrices.
skills.name: mosaic-missing-modality-imputation
skills.search_text: mosaic-missing-modality-imputation Use when a mosaic scMultiome layout contains batches lacking a modality (e.g., no scRNA-seq or CITE-seq protein counts) and feature entities such as peaks and genes cannot be connected by the available input data matrices. All modalities are jointly profiled in every batch (vertical integration), so measured counts exist and no pseudo-count substitution is needed No region-to-gene connection matrix (GxR.npz) is available for the genome build/peak set, since the gene-activity aggregation depends on it The missing modality has no 1:1 protein-gene mapping or gene-body/TSS annotation (e.g., non-transcriptomic modalities like motif deviation matrices), which the pseudo-count procedure does not cover http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates pseudo-count matrices to fill modalities missing from mosaic single-cell multi-omics batches in scMoMaT: a binarized pseudo-scRNA-seq (gene activity) matrix derived from scATAC-seq peaks via a region-to-gene connection matrix, and pseudo-protein counts projected from scRNA-seq via a 1:1 protein-gene mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Generates pseudo-count matrices to fill modalities missing from mosaic single-cell multi-omics batches in scMoMaT: a binarized pseudo-scRNA-seq (gene activity) matrix derived from scATAC-seq peaks via a region-to-gene connection matrix, and pseudo-protein counts projected from scRNA-seq via a 1:1 protein-gene mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All modalities are jointly profiled in every batch (vertical integration), so measured counts exist and no pseudo-count substitution is needed No region-to-gene connection matrix (GxR.npz) is available for the genome build/peak set, since the gene-activity aggregation depends on it The missing modality has no 1:1 protein-gene mapping or gene-body/TSS annotation (e.g., non-transcriptomic modalities like motif deviation matrices), which the pseudo-count procedure does not cover

skills.description: Use when you already have Leiden cluster labels from scMoMaT's post-processed cell-factor KNN graph and need cluster-specific marker genes, marker regions, or marker proteins (e.g. from ASAP-PBMC RNA/ATAC/protein counts) to annotate clusters.
skills.name: mosaic-multiomics-data-handling
skills.search_text: mosaic-multiomics-data-handling Use when you already have Leiden cluster labels from scMoMaT's post-processed cell-factor KNN graph and need cluster-specific marker genes, marker regions, or marker proteins (e.g. from ASAP-PBMC RNA/ATAC/protein counts) to annotate clusters. You have not yet run first-stage cell-factor training and post-processing/clustering (scmomat.post_process + leiden_cluster) — retraining requires cluster labels as fixed binary cell factors Your goal is only cell embedding/batch integration without cluster-specific bio-markers — the first-stage model's extract_cell_factors() alone suffices Batches lack matched feature sets per modality (genes intersected or peaks remapped) — the counts dictionary requires identical features within each modality before retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Post-clustering retraining stage of scMoMaT: after Leiden clustering of the integrated cell embedding, the matrix tri-factorization model is retrained with cluster labels encoded as fixed binary cell factors so that feature factors and association matrices yield per-cluster, multi-modal bio-marker score matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Post-clustering retraining stage of scMoMaT: after Leiden clustering of the integrated cell embedding, the matrix tri-factorization model is retrained with cluster labels encoded as fixed binary cell factors so that feature factors and association matrices yield per-cluster, multi-modal bio-marker score matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet run first-stage cell-factor training and post-processing/clustering (scmomat.post_process + leiden_cluster) — retraining requires cluster labels as fixed binary cell factors Your goal is only cell embedding/batch integration without cluster-specific bio-markers — the first-stage model's extract_cell_factors() alone suffices Batches lack matched feature sets per modality (genes intersected or peaks remapped) — the counts dictionary requires identical features within each modality before retraining

skills.description: Use when after MuTrans dynamical_analysis has identified attractor basins in a single-cell dataset and you need to infer the most probable transition trajectories between a starting state si and a final state sf for lineage reconstruction.
skills.name: most-probable-path-tree-lineage-inference
skills.search_text: most-probable-path-tree-lineage-inference Use when after MuTrans dynamical_analysis has identified attractor basins in a single-cell dataset and you need to infer the most probable transition trajectories between a starting state si and a final state sf for lineage reconstruction. When dynamical_analysis has not yet been run — InferLineage requires the attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities and membership assignment as input When the goal is pseudo-time ordering alone (e.g., DPT, Slingshot, Monocle) rather than stochastic transition-path lineage on an attractor landscape When the dataset is too small for reliable multi-scale dynamics — e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset, where the paper notes 'special care is needed' to confirm transition-cell analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer and overlay cell lineage on the MuTrans cell-fate dynamical manifold using the Most Probable Path Tree (MPPT) or Maximum Probability Flow Tree (MPFT) approach, tracing most-likely transition trajectories from a root attractor (e.g., lymphoid progenitor) to target attractors (e.g., Pro-B/Pre-B states). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Infer and overlay cell lineage on the MuTrans cell-fate dynamical manifold using the Most Probable Path Tree (MPPT) or Maximum Probability Flow Tree (MPFT) approach, tracing most-likely transition trajectories from a root attractor (e.g., lymphoid progenitor) to target attractors (e.g., Pro-B/Pre-B states).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When dynamical_analysis has not yet been run — InferLineage requires the attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities and membership assignment as input When the goal is pseudo-time ordering alone (e.g., DPT, Slingshot, Monocle) rather than stochastic transition-path lineage on an attractor landscape When the dataset is too small for reliable multi-scale dynamics — e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset, where the paper notes 'special care is needed' to confirm transition-cell analyses

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating CellO's bulk RNA-seq training set curation counts (samples, studies, CL terms, most-specific terms) or when analyzing most-specific cell type annotations against the Cell Ontology hierarchy.
skills.name: most-specific-cell-type-annotation-analysis
skills.search_text: most-specific-cell-type-annotation-analysis Use when reproducing or validating CellO's bulk RNA-seq training set curation counts (samples, studies, CL terms, most-specific terms) or when analyzing most-specific cell type annotations against the Cell Ontology hierarchy. Input samples are non-human (e.g., mouse): CellO's training set covers only human primary cell bulk RNA-seq data from the SRA, and no curated mouse training set exists yet The goal is de novo clustering or marker-gene-based annotation: this skill audits ontology-based hierarchical annotation statistics, not marker gene or flat-classifier workflows The input already contains curated cell type labels and the task is not ontology-based re-annotation or training-set statistics reproduction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Reproduces CellO's curated bulk RNA-seq training-set curation statistics (4,293 samples, 264 studies, 310 Cell Ontology terms, 113 most-specific cell types) by auditing the deposited sample metadata and per-sample CL annotations, grounding the most-specific cell type annotation task CellO performs against the Cell Ontology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101913
skills.summary: Reproduces CellO's curated bulk RNA-seq training-set curation statistics (4,293 samples, 264 studies, 310 Cell Ontology terms, 113 most-specific cell types) by auditing the deposited sample metadata and per-sample CL annotations, grounding the most-specific cell type annotation task CellO performs against the Cell Ontology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are non-human (e.g., mouse): CellO's training set covers only human primary cell bulk RNA-seq data from the SRA, and no curated mouse training set exists yet The goal is de novo clustering or marker-gene-based annotation: this skill audits ontology-based hierarchical annotation statistics, not marker gene or flat-classifier workflows The input already contains curated cell type labels and the task is not ontology-based re-annotation or training-set statistics reproduction

skills.description: Use when you need to infer TF motif activities from scRNA-seq unspliced promoter counts and test whether a TF's motif activity tracks its own mRNA level across cell cycle phases.
skills.name: motif-activity-mrna-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: motif-activity-mrna-correlation-analysis Use when you need to infer TF motif activities from scRNA-seq unspliced promoter counts and test whether a TF's motif activity tracks its own mRNA level across cell cycle phases. The dataset lacks an unspliced layer — the model is fit on unspliced (Mu) counts, so spliced-only matrices cannot support motif activity inference No motif/PWM site annotations (e.g. Swiss Regulon GFF) exist for the organism, so the promoter-by-motif matrix cannot be built The population is not cycling — if no cycling genes are found, DeepCycle theta and downstream motif-activity dynamics will not be reliable http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces an ISMARA-like transcription factor motif activity analysis on single-cell RNA-seq unspliced counts and quantifies the correlation between a TF's motif activity and its mRNA abundance across the cell cycle (e.g. Ybx1 in ductal cell progenitors, r = 0.91, p = 4e-19). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Reproduces an ISMARA-like transcription factor motif activity analysis on single-cell RNA-seq unspliced counts and quantifies the correlation between a TF's motif activity and its mRNA abundance across the cell cycle (e.g. Ybx1 in ductal cell progenitors, r = 0.91, p = 4e-19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks an unspliced layer — the model is fit on unspliced (Mu) counts, so spliced-only matrices cannot support motif activity inference No motif/PWM site annotations (e.g. Swiss Regulon GFF) exist for the organism, so the promoter-by-motif matrix cannot be built The population is not cycling — if no cycling genes are found, DeepCycle theta and downstream motif-activity dynamics will not be reliable

skills.description: Use when you have differentially active TF sets from two or more FateCompass (or similar motif-activity) runs and need to quantify their intersection and partition factors into shared vs. system-specific groups.
skills.name: motif-activity-result-integration
skills.search_text: motif-activity-result-integration Use when you have differentially active TF sets from two or more FateCompass (or similar motif-activity) runs and need to quantify their intersection and partition factors into shared vs. system-specific groups. You have raw scRNA-seq counts and have not yet run the FateCompass TF activity estimation and differential motif activity analysis — integrate only finished differentially active TF sets The datasets being compared lack comparable TF binding-site matrices or lineage annotations (e.g. cancer studies where prior biological knowledge for differentiation-potential mode is unavailable) The goal is method validation on simulated data rather than cross-system comparison — use the Dyngen ground-truth workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrates differentially active motif/TF activity outputs from FateCompass across multiple datasets (here, mouse E15.5 in vivo and human in vitro pancreatic endocrine differentiation) to quantify cross-system overlap of lineage-specific transcription factors and classify species- or system-specific factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Integrates differentially active motif/TF activity outputs from FateCompass across multiple datasets (here, mouse E15.5 in vivo and human in vitro pancreatic endocrine differentiation) to quantify cross-system overlap of lineage-specific transcription factors and classify species- or system-specific factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have raw scRNA-seq counts and have not yet run the FateCompass TF activity estimation and differential motif activity analysis — integrate only finished differentially active TF sets The datasets being compared lack comparable TF binding-site matrices or lineage annotations (e.g. cancer studies where prior biological knowledge for differentiation-potential mode is unavailable) The goal is method validation on simulated data rather than cross-system comparison — use the Dyngen ground-truth workflow instead

skills.description: Use when a set of fine-mapped GWAS variants (e.g. linked to target genes via GrID-Net peak-gene links) needs to be prioritized by predicted TF binding disruption, using PWM-based motif scanning of alternate vs. reference alleles.
skills.name: motif-disruption-quantification
skills.search_text: motif-disruption-quantification Use when a set of fine-mapped GWAS variants (e.g. linked to target genes via GrID-Net peak-gene links) needs to be prioritized by predicted TF binding disruption, using PWM-based motif scanning of alternate vs. reference alleles. Variants have not been linked to target genes (e.g. via GrID-Net peak-gene scores), so there is no prioritized variant set to annotate with motif disruptions The goal is direct experimental measurement of binding (e.g. ChIP-seq/EMSA) rather than PWM-based in silico prediction of affinity changes Input is protein-level or expression-level data with no variant coordinates on GRCh38/hg38 from which allele-flanked sequences can be extracted http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantify how variant alleles alter predicted transcription-factor binding affinity by scanning reference- and risk-allele flanked sequences (±20 bp, GRCh38/hg38) with FIMO against PWM collections (HOCOMOCO v11 Full Collection, JASPAR CORE Non-Redundant v2, CIS-BP v2) and computing per-variant, per-TF fold changes. Used here to identify GrID-Net-linked SCZ variants causing ≥20-fold binding affinity disruptions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Quantify how variant alleles alter predicted transcription-factor binding affinity by scanning reference- and risk-allele flanked sequences (±20 bp, GRCh38/hg38) with FIMO against PWM collections (HOCOMOCO v11 Full Collection, JASPAR CORE Non-Redundant v2, CIS-BP v2) and computing per-variant, per-TF fold changes. Used here to identify GrID-Net-linked SCZ variants causing ≥20-fold binding affinity disruptions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Variants have not been linked to target genes (e.g. via GrID-Net peak-gene scores), so there is no prioritized variant set to annotate with motif disruptions The goal is direct experimental measurement of binding (e.g. ChIP-seq/EMSA) rather than PWM-based in silico prediction of affinity changes Input is protein-level or expression-level data with no variant coordinates on GRCh38/hg38 from which allele-flanked sequences can be extracted

skills.description: Use when you have raw PMET paired-motif enrichment output (output/output.txt) from a plant scRNA-seq cluster analysis and need to identify and visualize cluster-specific enriched TF motif pairs as heatmaps and network plots.
skills.name: motif-enrichment-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: motif-enrichment-heatmap-visualization Use when you have raw PMET paired-motif enrichment output (output/output.txt) from a plant scRNA-seq cluster analysis and need to identify and visualize cluster-specific enriched TF motif pairs as heatmaps and network plots. Input is not PMET paired-motif output (e.g. single-motif cisTarget/SCENIC rankings or JASPAR/PlantTFDB motif collections alone) — processPMET expects the PMET output table format You need to run the enrichment test itself rather than visualize it — use RunPMET.sh (with samtools, bedtools, meme, parallel dependencies) instead of the visualization functions The organism is not one of the supported species databases (e.g. not At, Osa, or Zma with prepared scPlantData/PMET resources) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Visualize paired motif enrichment test (PMET) results from plant single-cell regulon analysis using scPlant's processPMET, PMEThmp, triHmp and topPairsNet functions to reproduce cluster-specific motif-pair enrichments such as the TCP14/TCP15 and ABI5-ABF pairings in the Arabidopsis root atlas photosynthetic cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Visualize paired motif enrichment test (PMET) results from plant single-cell regulon analysis using scPlant's processPMET, PMEThmp, triHmp and topPairsNet functions to reproduce cluster-specific motif-pair enrichments such as the TCP14/TCP15 and ABI5-ABF pairings in the Arabidopsis root atlas photosynthetic cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not PMET paired-motif output (e.g. single-motif cisTarget/SCENIC rankings or JASPAR/PlantTFDB motif collections alone) — processPMET expects the PMET output table format You need to run the enrichment test itself rather than visualize it — use RunPMET.sh (with samtools, bedtools, meme, parallel dependencies) instead of the visualization functions The organism is not one of the supported species databases (e.g. not At, Osa, or Zma with prepared scPlantData/PMET resources)

skills.description: Use when you need to identify which TF binding motifs are enriched among an upregulated gene set (e.g., the top 200 topic-4 proerythroblast genes), especially when motif signal may be masked by technical batch effects.
skills.name: motif-enrichment-testing-with-pwm-collection
skills.search_text: motif-enrichment-testing-with-pwm-collection Use when you need to identify which TF binding motifs are enriched among an upregulated gene set (e.g., the top 200 topic-4 proerythroblast genes), especially when motif signal may be masked by technical batch effects. When the analysis goal is de novo motif discovery rather than testing a curated PWM collection — in silico deletion only scores pre-defined JASPAR motifs When no scATAC-seq accessibility data are available, since regulatory potential and peak masking depend on accessible peaks linked to UCSC TSS annotations When technical-effect correction is irrelevant (e.g., single-batch data), where the CODAL-augmented model adds no value over the unaugmented regulatory potential model Tests transcription factor motif enrichment among a target gene set by scoring motif-gene associations over a curated PWM collection (here, the 1641 JASPAR 2020 vertebrate PWMs) via probabilistic in silico deletion on a MIRA regulatory potential model, then comparing score distributions with a Wilcoxon test and Bonferroni correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Tests transcription factor motif enrichment among a target gene set by scoring motif-gene associations over a curated PWM collection (here, the 1641 JASPAR 2020 vertebrate PWMs) via probabilistic in silico deletion on a MIRA regulatory potential model, then comparing score distributions with a Wilcoxon test and Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is de novo motif discovery rather than testing a curated PWM collection — in silico deletion only scores pre-defined JASPAR motifs When no scATAC-seq accessibility data are available, since regulatory potential and peak masking depend on accessible peaks linked to UCSC TSS annotations When technical-effect correction is irrelevant (e.g., single-batch data), where the CODAL-augmented model adds no value over the unaugmented regulatory potential model

skills.description: Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g., HOMER-called csRNA-seq peaks, EPDnew/CAGE, RAMPAGE annotations) and need to quantify whether core promoter elements show preferential positional enrichment around the TSS.
skills.name: motif-position-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: motif-position-distribution-analysis Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g., HOMER-called csRNA-seq peaks, EPDnew/CAGE, RAMPAGE annotations) and need to quantify whether core promoter elements show preferential positional enrichment around the TSS. Input sequences have no TSS-centered coordinate frame — ElemeNT positional stringency interpretation requires motifs scored relative to an annotated TSS The goal is general de novo motif discovery in arbitrary DNA rather than detection and positioning of known core promoter elements (TATA, dInr, PB, DPE) The TSS source is low-quality or unvalidated — the article positions this skill specifically for evaluating the quality of high-throughput TSS datasets, not for raw unfiltered peak lists http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Analyzes the position and score distributions of core promoter motifs (TATA, dInr, PB, DPE) relative to annotated TSSs using ElemeNT 2023, enabling dataset-quality assessment and cross-species comparison of promoter element positioning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Analyzes the position and score distributions of core promoter motifs (TATA, dInr, PB, DPE) relative to annotated TSSs using ElemeNT 2023, enabling dataset-quality assessment and cross-species comparison of promoter element positioning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences have no TSS-centered coordinate frame — ElemeNT positional stringency interpretation requires motifs scored relative to an annotated TSS The goal is general de novo motif discovery in arbitrary DNA rather than detection and positioning of known core promoter elements (TATA, dInr, PB, DPE) The TSS source is low-quality or unvalidated — the article positions this skill specifically for evaluating the quality of high-throughput TSS datasets, not for raw unfiltered peak lists

skills.description: Use when candidate RBPs lack physical interactions with gold regulators and you must test whether their circRNA-derived binding motifs statistically resemble known regulator motifs (E-value cutoff E < 0.01).
skills.name: motif-similarity-comparison-tomtom
skills.search_text: motif-similarity-comparison-tomtom Use when candidate RBPs lack physical interactions with gold regulators and you must test whether their circRNA-derived binding motifs statistically resemble known regulator motifs (E-value cutoff E < 0.01). Candidate RBPs already have physical interactions (protein-protein or protein-RNA) with gold regulators — motif similarity is used here specifically for non-physically-associated candidates De novo motifs have not yet been discovered — run MEME on circRNA sequences first; TOMTOM requires query motifs in MEME format Comparing motifs without a GC-matched background model — significance of TOMTOM matches would not be comparable to the article's E < 0.01 results http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compares de novo RNA-binding motifs discovered by MEME for candidate circRNA regulators against a gold-regulator motif set using TOMTOM with a GC-matched background, to show non-physically-associated RBPs are functionally connected to known circRNA regulators via similar binding motifs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Compares de novo RNA-binding motifs discovered by MEME for candidate circRNA regulators against a gold-regulator motif set using TOMTOM with a GC-matched background, to show non-physically-associated RBPs are functionally connected to known circRNA regulators via similar binding motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Candidate RBPs already have physical interactions (protein-protein or protein-RNA) with gold regulators — motif similarity is used here specifically for non-physically-associated candidates De novo motifs have not yet been discovered — run MEME on circRNA sequences first; TOMTOM requires query motifs in MEME format Comparing motifs without a GC-matched background model — significance of TOMTOM matches would not be comparable to the article's E < 0.01 results

skills.description: Use when denoising a sparse single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3,005-cell mouse cortex from Zeisel et al.) with known cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster resolution via mean silhouette score after RMT feature selection versus baseline denoising methods.
skills.name: mouse-cortex-cell-type-grouping-analysis
skills.search_text: mouse-cortex-cell-type-grouping-analysis Use when denoising a sparse single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3,005-cell mouse cortex from Zeisel et al.) with known cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster resolution via mean silhouette score after RMT feature selection versus baseline denoising methods. The dataset has no known phenotype/cell-type labels, so silhouette scores against marked populations cannot be computed. The input matrix is already a denoised or low-rank feature embedding rather than a raw sparse cell-gene count matrix. The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than benchmarking denoising methods against known marked cell populations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces the silhouette-score benchmark from Aparicio et al. (Patterns, 2020) in which RMT-based denoising of the 3,005-cell mouse cortex dataset (Zeisel et al.) is compared against imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning baselines by computing mean silhouette scores of known phenotype groupings (7, 15, and 26 groups) in latent spaces of varying dimension. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Reproduces the silhouette-score benchmark from Aparicio et al. (Patterns, 2020) in which RMT-based denoising of the 3,005-cell mouse cortex dataset (Zeisel et al.) is compared against imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning baselines by computing mean silhouette scores of known phenotype groupings (7, 15, and 26 groups) in latent spaces of varying dimension.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no known phenotype/cell-type labels, so silhouette scores against marked populations cannot be computed. The input matrix is already a denoised or low-rank feature embedding rather than a raw sparse cell-gene count matrix. The goal is de novo cluster discovery rather than benchmarking denoising methods against known marked cell populations.

skills.description: Use when running trajectory inference on a ~1.3-million-cell single-cell atlas (e.g., MOCA) and needing to confirm scalable runtime (~40 min) plus globally connected, multi-branch topology robustness across PC counts.
skills.name: mouse-organogenesis-atlas-analysis
skills.search_text: mouse-organogenesis-atlas-analysis Use when running trajectory inference on a ~1.3-million-cell single-cell atlas (e.g., MOCA) and needing to confirm scalable runtime (~40 min) plus globally connected, multi-branch topology robustness across PC counts. Input is a small (~10^2-10^3 cell) simulated or toy dataset — dyntoy/dyngen simulations are for prototyping TI methods, not for this million-cell scalability benchmark The goal is topology discovery on data where UMAP/t-SNE pre-embedding suffices — the article notes methods requiring UMAP (or t-SNE) before parsing MOCA are highly susceptible to user-defined input parameters Data are disconnected trajectories needing multiple roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected instead of the standard atlas-scale connected workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark and reproduce VIA's million-cell-scale trajectory inference on the 1.3-million-cell MOCA mouse organogenesis atlas, measuring runtime against PAGA, Palantir, STREAM and Monocle3 while verifying that the cluster-graph preserves global connectivity across choices of input principal components. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Benchmark and reproduce VIA's million-cell-scale trajectory inference on the 1.3-million-cell MOCA mouse organogenesis atlas, measuring runtime against PAGA, Palantir, STREAM and Monocle3 while verifying that the cluster-graph preserves global connectivity across choices of input principal components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a small (~10^2-10^3 cell) simulated or toy dataset — dyntoy/dyngen simulations are for prototyping TI methods, not for this million-cell scalability benchmark The goal is topology discovery on data where UMAP/t-SNE pre-embedding suffices — the article notes methods requiring UMAP (or t-SNE) before parsing MOCA are highly susceptible to user-defined input parameters Data are disconnected trajectories needing multiple roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected instead of the standard atlas-scale connected workflow

skills.description: Use when analyzing drug-treated mouse scRNA-seq (e.g., Mus musculus AML cells, GSE110894, I-BET-762) with a human-trained scDEAL model, or when correlating predicted response probabilities with Monocle3 pseudotime.
skills.name: mouse-scrna-seq-aml-data-analysis
skills.search_text: mouse-scrna-seq-aml-data-analysis Use when analyzing drug-treated mouse scRNA-seq (e.g., Mus musculus AML cells, GSE110894, I-BET-762) with a human-trained scDEAL model, or when correlating predicted response probabilities with Monocle3 pseudotime. Data is human scRNA-seq (Datasets 1-5, e.g., GSE117872/GSE112274) rather than mouse AML — no homologous-gene restriction is needed and other case-study workflows apply Goal is bulk-level drug response prediction from cell-line data (GDSC/CCLE) rather than single-cell trajectory analysis of a treated mouse dataset No pretrained AnnData or scDEAL model checkpoint for GSE110894 is available and the user is not prepared to run bulkmodel.py/scmodel.py training first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Case-study skill for analyzing the mouse AML scRNA-seq dataset (Data 6, GSE110894, I-BET-762, 1419 cells) with scDEAL, including trans-species prediction on homologous genes and pseudotime correlation of predicted response probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Case-study skill for analyzing the mouse AML scRNA-seq dataset (Data 6, GSE110894, I-BET-762, 1419 cells) with scDEAL, including trans-species prediction on homologous genes and pseudotime correlation of predicted response probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is human scRNA-seq (Datasets 1-5, e.g., GSE117872/GSE112274) rather than mouse AML — no homologous-gene restriction is needed and other case-study workflows apply Goal is bulk-level drug response prediction from cell-line data (GDSC/CCLE) rather than single-cell trajectory analysis of a treated mouse dataset No pretrained AnnData or scDEAL model checkpoint for GSE110894 is available and the user is not prepared to run bulkmodel.py/scmodel.py training first

skills.description: Use when a FrameD fault-injection configuration must be benchmarked for parallel scalability, i.e. when evaluating whether FrameD delivers measurable speedups from 1 core to 32 and 92 MPI ranks on the identical pipeline settings.
skills.name: mpi-parallel-benchmark-execution
skills.search_text: mpi-parallel-benchmark-execution Use when a FrameD fault-injection configuration must be benchmarked for parallel scalability, i.e. when evaluating whether FrameD delivers measurable speedups from 1 core to 32 and 92 MPI ranks on the identical pipeline settings. Running on commodity hardware without an HPC scheduler/MPI — FrameD's batch-level parallelism assumes an IBM LSF managed platform, and the full 368-simulation configuration is only tractable on HPC systems The analysis goal is fault-injection accuracy (e.g. whether multiple sequence alignment helps at a given error rate), not runtime scalability — benchmark timings alone cannot answer error-rate questions The pipeline configuration differs between the serial and parallel runs (different code, read depth, fault rate, or number of simulations) — speedup ratios are then not comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Measures wall-clock scalability of FrameD's fault-injection simulation pipeline under its transparent MPI parallelism, comparing serial runtime against multi-rank runs to compute speedup factors for a fixed DNA storage pipeline configuration (e.g. RS(9,47) code, 25x read depth, 10% fault rate, 368 simulations). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Measures wall-clock scalability of FrameD's fault-injection simulation pipeline under its transparent MPI parallelism, comparing serial runtime against multi-rank runs to compute speedup factors for a fixed DNA storage pipeline configuration (e.g. RS(9,47) code, 25x read depth, 10% fault rate, 368 simulations).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running on commodity hardware without an HPC scheduler/MPI — FrameD's batch-level parallelism assumes an IBM LSF managed platform, and the full 368-simulation configuration is only tractable on HPC systems The analysis goal is fault-injection accuracy (e.g. whether multiple sequence alignment helps at a given error rate), not runtime scalability — benchmark timings alone cannot answer error-rate questions The pipeline configuration differs between the serial and parallel runs (different code, read depth, fault rate, or number of simulations) — speedup ratios are then not comparable

skills.description: Use when you have sorted, indexed BAM files (bulk DNA WES and single-cell or bulk RNA-seq) plus a finalized, QC-passed SNV callset and need per-locus allele read counts to feed Canopy2 or a similar joint bulk/scDNA-scRNA clonal-inference model.
skills.name: mpileup-allele-read-count-extraction
skills.search_text: mpileup-allele-read-count-extraction Use when you have sorted, indexed BAM files (bulk DNA WES and single-cell or bulk RNA-seq) plus a finalized, QC-passed SNV callset and need per-locus allele read counts to feed Canopy2 or a similar joint bulk/scDNA-scRNA clonal-inference model. The SNV callset has not yet passed the pipeline QC filters (variants failing FilterMutectCalls PASS, with non-0/0 normal genotypes, multiple alternative alleles, or < 20 total reads in the normal) — counts should be extracted only at finalized loci The task is germline heterozygous locus calling in single-cell data; the paper provides a separate germline variant calling pipeline for that purpose You already have Rs/Xs/Rb/Xb matrices — this skill is the pre-processing step, not Canopy2 inference itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Extracts alternative (mutated-locus) and total (mutated plus benign-locus) read counts at finalized somatic SNV loci using SAMtools mpileup in force-calling mode, and assembles them into the R^s/X^s (mutation-by-single-cell) and R^b/X^b (mutation-by-bulk) matrices required by Canopy2, saved as read_count_matrices.rda. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Extracts alternative (mutated-locus) and total (mutated plus benign-locus) read counts at finalized somatic SNV loci using SAMtools mpileup in force-calling mode, and assembles them into the R^s/X^s (mutation-by-single-cell) and R^b/X^b (mutation-by-bulk) matrices required by Canopy2, saved as read_count_matrices.rda.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SNV callset has not yet passed the pipeline QC filters (variants failing FilterMutectCalls PASS, with non-0/0 normal genotypes, multiple alternative alleles, or < 20 total reads in the normal) — counts should be extracted only at finalized loci The task is germline heterozygous locus calling in single-cell data; the paper provides a separate germline variant calling pipeline for that purpose You already have Rs/Xs/Rb/Xb matrices — this skill is the pre-processing step, not Canopy2 inference itself

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized, non-negative bulk gene x sample expression matrix with human gene symbols as row names and need reaction-level activity scores as the input to metabolic flux prediction (FBA) rather than gene-level expression.
skills.name: mras-reaction-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: mras-reaction-activity-scoring Use when you have a normalized, non-negative bulk gene x sample expression matrix with human gene symbols as row names and need reaction-level activity scores as the input to metabolic flux prediction (FBA) rather than gene-level expression. Input is already a reaction-level flux matrix or pathway activity table (scoring would be redundant) Expression matrix uses probe IDs, Ensembl IDs, or non-human gene identifiers without first mapping to human gene symbols Working with single-cell data where you need cluster-averaged profiles via calculate_avg_exp and compute_sc_flux instead of bulk per-sample MRAS http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Computes single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a gene x sample bulk RNA-seq matrix by collapsing gene expression onto 13,082 Human-GEM reactions via Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) rules, producing the MRAS input required by METAFlux's compute_flux step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Computes single-sample normalized Metabolic Reaction Activity Scores (MRAS) from a gene x sample bulk RNA-seq matrix by collapsing gene expression onto 13,082 Human-GEM reactions via Gene-Protein-Reaction (GPR) rules, producing the MRAS input required by METAFlux's compute_flux step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reaction-level flux matrix or pathway activity table (scoring would be redundant) Expression matrix uses probe IDs, Ensembl IDs, or non-human gene identifiers without first mapping to human gene symbols Working with single-cell data where you need cluster-averaged profiles via calculate_avg_exp and compute_sc_flux instead of bulk per-sample MRAS

skills.description: Use when benchmarking marker-selection runtimes or ranking features on phenotype×feature score matrices, e.g. when reproducing Table 2 of the multiset multicover marker-selection paper on the IPF, MC, or HCA scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.name: mrmr-feature-ranking
skills.search_text: mrmr-feature-ranking Use when benchmarking marker-selection runtimes or ranking features on phenotype×feature score matrices, e.g. when reproducing Table 2 of the multiset multicover marker-selection paper on the IPF, MC, or HCA scRNA-seq datasets. The goal is a globally discriminative marker set covering every phenotype pair (use GreedyPC/CEMPC from phenotype-cover instead of mRMR). The target variable is a ranking of already-scored features rather than a supervised selection problem. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without conversion to a feature matrix; log-transform or preprocess before mrmr_classif/mrmr_regression. mRMR (minimum Redundancy - Maximum Relevance) feature ranking, used in Hasanaj et al. 2022 as a competitor marker-selection method benchmarked against G-PC/CEM-PC on IPF, MC, and HCA scRNA-seq datasets, including the Table 2 runtime comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: mRMR (minimum Redundancy - Maximum Relevance) feature ranking, used in Hasanaj et al. 2022 as a competitor marker-selection method benchmarked against G-PC/CEM-PC on IPF, MC, and HCA scRNA-seq datasets, including the Table 2 runtime comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a globally discriminative marker set covering every phenotype pair (use GreedyPC/CEMPC from phenotype-cover instead of mRMR). The target variable is a ranking of already-scored features rather than a supervised selection problem. Input is raw scRNA-seq counts without conversion to a feature matrix; log-transform or preprocess before mrmr_classif/mrmr_regression.

skills.description: Use when validating scRNA-seq denoising/imputation against an orthogonal per-cell protein measurement (CITE-seq ADT), by comparing mRNA detection rates against protein-positivity as ground truth.
skills.name: mrna-detection-fraction-quantification-against-protein-ground-truth
skills.search_text: mrna-detection-fraction-quantification-against-protein-ground-truth Use when validating scRNA-seq denoising/imputation against an orthogonal per-cell protein measurement (CITE-seq ADT), by comparing mRNA detection rates against protein-positivity as ground truth. No orthogonal per-cell protein measurements (e.g., CITE-seq ADT tags) are available to serve as ground truth for the mRNA The goal is bulk RNA-seq or full-length scRNA-seq where dropout-driven false zeros are not the dominant detection limitation The dataset lacks a defined positive cell population (e.g., T cells for CD3E), making the protein-based ground-truth comparison uninterpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantifies the fraction of cells in which an mRNA (e.g., CD3E) is detected (non-zero counts) before and after DCA denoising, using CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein measurements (e.g., CD3) as ground truth to validate that denoising recovers biologically true expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of cells in which an mRNA (e.g., CD3E) is detected (non-zero counts) before and after DCA denoising, using CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein measurements (e.g., CD3) as ground truth to validate that denoising recovers biologically true expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No orthogonal per-cell protein measurements (e.g., CITE-seq ADT tags) are available to serve as ground truth for the mRNA The goal is bulk RNA-seq or full-length scRNA-seq where dropout-driven false zeros are not the dominant detection limitation The dataset lacks a defined positive cell population (e.g., T cells for CD3E), making the protein-based ground-truth comparison uninterpretable

skills.description: Use when raw TCGA mRNA expression matrices must be reduced to abnormal-expression entries before FDR screening or Ridge/Lasso/adaptive-Lasso penalized regression in HDMAC.
skills.name: mrna-zscore-abnormality-scoring
skills.search_text: mrna-zscore-abnormality-scoring Use when raw TCGA mRNA expression matrices must be reduced to abnormal-expression entries before FDR screening or Ridge/Lasso/adaptive-Lasso penalized regression in HDMAC. Data are mutation calls rather than mRNA expression — the article applies a 1%-mutation frequency screen for mutations, not the 2% mRNA abnormal-expression Z-score rule The covariate count is modest and penalized regression or abnormality pre-screening is unnecessary Clinical variables (gender, age) alone are the analysis target, not high-dimensional molecular entries http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pre-screening step from the HDMAC workflow that converts TCGA mRNA expression values into Z-scores, flags entries as abnormally expressed when Z > 2 or Z < -2, and retains only entries abnormal in at least 2% of patients (8,024 entries for bladder, 9,548 for ovarian cancer) before penalized regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60791-z
skills.summary: Pre-screening step from the HDMAC workflow that converts TCGA mRNA expression values into Z-scores, flags entries as abnormally expressed when Z > 2 or Z < -2, and retains only entries abnormal in at least 2% of patients (8,024 entries for bladder, 9,548 for ovarian cancer) before penalized regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are mutation calls rather than mRNA expression — the article applies a 1%-mutation frequency screen for mutations, not the 2% mRNA abnormal-expression Z-score rule The covariate count is modest and penalized regression or abnormality pre-screening is unnecessary Clinical variables (gender, age) alone are the analysis target, not high-dimensional molecular entries

skills.description: Use when you need gene- or transcript-specific predictions of RNA-seq depth required to survey splice junctions (e.g. low-MRSD <100 M reads classification) from bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq reference datasets.
skills.name: mrsd-score-calculation
skills.search_text: mrsd-score-calculation Use when you need gene- or transcript-specific predictions of RNA-seq depth required to survey splice junctions (e.g. low-MRSD <100 M reads classification) from bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq reference datasets. Your sequencing workflow is long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq, or total-RNA/other library prep — appropriate control datasets to develop corresponding MRSD models are not yet available You need suitability predictions for allele-specific expression, differential gene expression, or isoform imbalance — the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these Patient disorders involve widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g. interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders, spliceosome disruption) — MRSD predictions may not accurately reflect coverage in such genomic backgrounds http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Calculate Minimum Required Sequencing Depth (MRSD) scores that quantify, in millions of reads, the RNA-seq depth needed to cover a user-specified proportion of splice junctions for genes or transcripts of interest, stratified by control biosample (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, fibroblasts from GTEx). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Calculate Minimum Required Sequencing Depth (MRSD) scores that quantify, in millions of reads, the RNA-seq depth needed to cover a user-specified proportion of splice junctions for genes or transcripts of interest, stratified by control biosample (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, fibroblasts from GTEx).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your sequencing workflow is long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq, or total-RNA/other library prep — appropriate control datasets to develop corresponding MRSD models are not yet available You need suitability predictions for allele-specific expression, differential gene expression, or isoform imbalance — the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these Patient disorders involve widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g. interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders, spliceosome disruption) — MRSD predictions may not accurately reflect coverage in such genomic backgrounds

skills.description: Use when planning bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq for splice-junction surveillance of Mendelian disease genes and you need to know how many reads (e.g. --number_reads 8 over --sj_prop 0.75 junctions) a given tissue requires.
skills.name: mrsd-sequencing-depth-prediction
skills.search_text: mrsd-sequencing-depth-prediction Use when planning bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq for splice-junction surveillance of Mendelian disease genes and you need to know how many reads (e.g. --number_reads 8 over --sj_prop 0.75 junctions) a given tissue requires. The dataset is long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq — no appropriate control datasets exist yet, and MRSD is validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment data processed with the specified pipeline The goal is to predict suitability for allele-specific expression, differential gene expression, or isoform imbalance analysis — the article states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these The patient's disorder involves widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g. interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders, spliceosome disruption) or strong eQTL/sQTL effects, which the current model does not account for http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply the MRSD (Minimum Required Sequencing Depth) framework via MRSDexplorer to predict, per gene/transcript and per tissue dataset, the RNA-seq depth needed to achieve a user-specified splice-junction coverage level, and validate predictions with PPV/NPV. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Apply the MRSD (Minimum Required Sequencing Depth) framework via MRSDexplorer to predict, per gene/transcript and per tissue dataset, the RNA-seq depth needed to achieve a user-specified splice-junction coverage level, and validate predictions with PPV/NPV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq — no appropriate control datasets exist yet, and MRSD is validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment data processed with the specified pipeline The goal is to predict suitability for allele-specific expression, differential gene expression, or isoform imbalance analysis — the article states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to these The patient's disorder involves widespread transcriptomic changes (e.g. interferonopathies, chromatin structure disorders, spliceosome disruption) or strong eQTL/sQTL effects, which the current model does not account for

skills.description: Use when deciding whether MSA belongs in a DNA storage pipeline: you must compare HEDGES-MSA vs MSA-only configurations across error rates and error types to see where MSA helps or hurts.
skills.name: msa-inclusion-tradeoff-analysis
skills.search_text: msa-inclusion-tradeoff-analysis Use when deciding whether MSA belongs in a DNA storage pipeline: you must compare HEDGES-MSA vs MSA-only configurations across error rates and error types to see where MSA helps or hurts. Only a single error rate or a single error type is tested — the tradeoff cannot be characterized, since MSA inclusion 'is dependent on the error rate and the type of errors being injected' The goal is functional encoding/decoding testing of a pipeline rather than a design decision about whether the MSA stage is worth its density cost The error model does not represent the deployment channel (e.g. conclusions drawn only under i.i.d. errors will not transfer to nanopore's burst-error profile) Evaluates whether multiple sequence alignment (MSA) should be included in a DNA storage pipeline by running FrameD fault-injection simulations across error-rate settings and error types (i.i.d. vs DNArSim nanopore), then checking whether MSA-only configurations survive on the cross-pipeline read/write density Pareto frontier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Evaluates whether multiple sequence alignment (MSA) should be included in a DNA storage pipeline by running FrameD fault-injection simulations across error-rate settings and error types (i.i.d. vs DNArSim nanopore), then checking whether MSA-only configurations survive on the cross-pipeline read/write density Pareto frontier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single error rate or a single error type is tested — the tradeoff cannot be characterized, since MSA inclusion 'is dependent on the error rate and the type of errors being injected' The goal is functional encoding/decoding testing of a pipeline rather than a design decision about whether the MSA stage is worth its density cost The error model does not represent the deployment channel (e.g. conclusions drawn only under i.i.d. errors will not transfer to nanopore's burst-error profile)

skills.search_text: mse-loss-regressor-validation Use when single-cell latent features (e.g. TCA characteristic matrices) must be projected into spatial coordinates by regression against a spatial transcriptomics reference, and per-cell coordinate outputs need validation. Input is raw gene expression rather than TCA-extracted shared characteristic matrices — the MLP operates on the latent features scSpace extracts via transfer component analysis The goal is spatial domain identification of ST data itself (e.g. with SpaGCN, BayesSpace, DR-SC) rather than reconstructing pseudo-space for scRNA-seq cells The tissue has low spatial coherence or the spatial reference is anatomically mismatched to the scRNA-seq tissue (e.g. agranular dACC vs granular DLPFC), which undermines reconstruction accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains and validates a multi-layer perceptron regressor that maps shared latent features to spatial coordinates, using Adam with mean squared error loss, as done in scSpace's pseudo-space reconstruction of scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4

Calling nuclear SNVs, where diploid assumptions hold — use nuclear SNV callers such as Monovar or Conbase, since the mitochondrial genome violates diploidy scATAC-seq data processed without NUMT masking — the article masks NUMT regions from the standard hg19 reference before CellRanger-ATAC, and mtDNA-specific methods like mgatk/EMBLEM were designed primarily for scATAC-seq quality scDNA-seq data below ~3,000 mitochondrial reads per cell, where downsampling shows a linear drop in assignable cells, informative variants detected, and clonal assignment concordance http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Detect clonally informative mitochondrial DNA variants in single-cell omics data by first piling up mtDNA reads into SNP-by-cell AD/DP matrices with cellsnp-lite/cellSNP, then separating informative heteroplasmic variants from noise with MQuad's binomial mixture model and a ΔBIC knee-point cutoff. skills.summary: Detect clonally informative mitochondrial DNA variants in single-cell omics data by first piling up mtDNA reads into SNP-by-cell AD/DP matrices with cellsnp-lite/cellSNP, then separating informative heteroplasmic variants from noise with MQuad's binomial mixture model and a ΔBIC knee-point cutoff. This mtDNA-specific approach avoids the diploid assumption that breaks nuclear SNV callers on the mitochondrial genome.

skills.summary: Integrates multiple enhancer-activity assays (DNase-seq, ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq) with chromatin-contact matrices to score enhancer-gene interactions using the ABC and adapted (gABC) Activity-By-Contact models via STARE, and benchmarks them against CRISPRi perturbation labels using AUPRC.

skills.name: multi-batch-classification-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-batch-classification-benchmarking Use when comparing a pretrained zero-shot label predictor (e.g. scPRINT) against supervised classifiers (CellTypist, openproblems logistic regression/xgboost) on multi-batch single-cell data where the test set comes from held-out batches. The goal is gene network inference benchmarking (use scPRINT's BenGRN/GRnnData suite instead of label prediction metrics). Fine-tuning on the target dataset is allowed — the headline comparison here rests on scPRINT being a zero-shot predictor that does not train on the test dataset. The dataset has a single batch, so a train-test split by batch (and the batch-effect challenge) cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark cell-type label prediction methods head-to-head on a multi-batch scRNAseq dataset by splitting train-test by batch, running zero-shot and supervised classifiers, and computing accuracy and macro-F1 at multiple label granularities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-type label prediction methods head-to-head on a multi-batch scRNAseq dataset by splitting train-test by batch, running zero-shot and supervised classifiers, and computing accuracy and macro-F1 at multiple label granularities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene network inference benchmarking (use scPRINT's BenGRN/GRnnData suite instead of label prediction metrics). The dataset has a single batch, so a train-test split by batch (and the batch-effect challenge) cannot be constructed.

skills.summary: Jointly clusters paired multimodal single-cell data across batches (e.g. multi-batch SMAGE-seq PBMC13K RNA+ATAC) using scMDC's conditional autoencoder, which corrects batch effects while learning a shared latent embedding, followed by deep K-means clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is single-modal (RNA-only or ADT-only) — scMDC is designed for paired multimodal inputs; use single-modal deep clustering instead Only a joint embedding is needed (not clustering) — the paper notes methods 'focusing on joint embedding are not designed and optimized for clustering', and conversely scMDC targets clustering Only CPU hardware is available and runtime is critical — all experiments were conducted on an Nvidia Tesla P100 (16 G) GPU

skills.name: multi-biosample-depth-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-biosample-depth-comparison-analysis Use when you need per-gene, per-tissue predicted RNA-seq depths (MRSD scores) for splice-junction coverage of a disease gene panel across several control biosample datasets. When assessing suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the article states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to those tasks When the planned data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq — no appropriate control datasets yet exist to develop corresponding MRSD models When sequencing workflows differ substantially from Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A enrichment, unless you regenerate your own MRSD scores for that methodology http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Generates MRSD (Minimum Required Sequencing Depth) scores in millions of reads for a list of genes across multiple GTEx control biosamples (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, cultured fibroblasts) using the MRSDexplorer toolkit, so the depth needed to cover splice junctions can be compared per tissue. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Generates MRSD (Minimum Required Sequencing Depth) scores in millions of reads for a list of genes across multiple GTEx control biosamples (whole blood, LCLs, skeletal muscle, cultured fibroblasts) using the MRSDexplorer toolkit, so the depth needed to cover splice junctions can be compared per tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When assessing suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression — the article states the MRSD model cannot directly be extended to those tasks When the planned data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq — no appropriate control datasets yet exist to develop corresponding MRSD models When sequencing workflows differ substantially from Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A enrichment, unless you regenerate your own MRSD scores for that methodology

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein measurements and need to train a transcriptome-to-protein mapping model rather than apply the pre-trained cTP-net model.
skills.name: multi-branch-network-architecture-implementation
skills.search_text: multi-branch-network-architecture-implementation Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein measurements and need to train a transcriptome-to-protein mapping model rather than apply the pre-trained cTP-net model. Input expression is TPM/RPKM or otherwise non-UMI: 'cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based)' You only want to impute surface proteins with the published model — use the cTPnet R/Python package inference pipeline instead of retraining Target cell types are outside the hematopoietic lineage, which was not tested for generalization http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implement and train cTP-net's multiple-branch deep neural network (MB-DNN) that maps a cell's SAVER-X denoised, LogNormalize-normalized transcriptome to relative abundances of surface proteins, with a 128-node bottleneck feeding protein-specific 64-node branches. The shared training script (training_05152020.py) enables retraining on new paired transcriptome-protein datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Implement and train cTP-net's multiple-branch deep neural network (MB-DNN) that maps a cell's SAVER-X denoised, LogNormalize-normalized transcriptome to relative abundances of surface proteins, with a 128-node bottleneck feeding protein-specific 64-node branches. The shared training script (training_05152020.py) enables retraining on new paired transcriptome-protein datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression is TPM/RPKM or otherwise non-UMI: 'cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based)' You only want to impute surface proteins with the published model — use the cTPnet R/Python package inference pipeline instead of retraining Target cell types are outside the hematopoietic lineage, which was not tested for generalization

skills.description: Use when a locus may harbor multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) across many tissues or studies and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization rather than single-causal-variant meta-analysis.
skills.name: multi-causal-variant-fine-mapping
skills.search_text: multi-causal-variant-fine-mapping Use when a locus may harbor multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) across many tissues or studies and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization rather than single-causal-variant meta-analysis. Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants with no eQTL signal — CAFEH cannot explore them Studies with large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences) from the single LD matrix CAFEH relies on, or datasets with missing entries in the effect size matrix When distinguishing multiple signals among variants in nearly perfect LD is required — CAFEH struggles in very high LD http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Jointly fine-map causal regulatory variants and assess colocalization across multiple tissues/studies using CAFEH, a Bayesian method that accounts for allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) that confounds traditional meta-analytic tissue-sharing estimates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Jointly fine-map causal regulatory variants and assess colocalization across multiple tissues/studies using CAFEH, a Bayesian method that accounts for allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus) that confounds traditional meta-analytic tissue-sharing estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants with no eQTL signal — CAFEH cannot explore them Studies with large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences) from the single LD matrix CAFEH relies on, or datasets with missing entries in the effect size matrix When distinguishing multiple signals among variants in nearly perfect LD is required — CAFEH struggles in very high LD

skills.description: Use when several candidate classifiers must be evaluated on identical training/test feature files, and you need to tabulate classification power (accuracy) per method, optionally across graded noise levels proxying shallower sequencing depth.

skills.search_text: multi-classifier-performance-comparison Use when several candidate classifiers must be evaluated on identical training/test feature files, and you need to tabulate classification power (accuracy) per method, optionally across graded noise levels proxying shallower sequencing depth. The goal is predicting continuous evolutionary parameters (theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) rather than class discrimination — use CLOUDePredictNN/CLOUDePredictXGB/CLOUDePredictRF/CLOUDePredictSVM instead of the classify functions Only a single classifier is being applied and no head-to-head or noise-robustness comparison is required Input expression data are raw counts not yet transformed to absolute log10(x+1) values in the required 3m-column deletion-event format http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks multiple machine learning classifiers (neural network, extreme gradient boosting, random forest, SVM) on the same classification task — here CLOUDe's 'Redundant' vs 'Unique' gene-deletion classes — including under controlled noise perturbation, to identify the best-performing architecture. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
