skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is predicting continuous evolutionary parameters (theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) rather than class discrimination — use CLOUDePredictNN/CLOUDePredictXGB/CLOUDePredictRF/CLOUDePredictSVM instead of the classify functions Only a single classifier is being applied and no head-to-head or noise-robustness comparison is required Input expression data are raw counts not yet transformed to absolute log10(x+1) values in the required 3m-column deletion-event format

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell-type drug rankings from ASGARD GetDrug across multiple clusters of a patient's scRNA-seq data and need a single patient-level drug recommendation that accounts for heterogeneous cell populations.
skills.name: multi-cluster-drug-score-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-cluster-drug-score-aggregation Use when you have per-cell-type drug rankings from ASGARD GetDrug across multiple clusters of a patient's scRNA-seq data and need a single patient-level drug recommendation that accounts for heterogeneous cell populations. When the disease is driven by a single homogeneous cell population — per-cluster predictions alone may suffice, though the paper still reports multi-cluster AUC superiority When no normal-tissue control samples exist to compute case-vs-control differential signatures (the article notes substitutes are needed until normal tissue data are available) When the drug reference lacks a proper tissue-matched cell-line panel — the reference is limited to 98 LINCS L1000 cell lines http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Aggregates ASGARD per-cluster drug repurposing rankings into a patient-level drug therapeutic score (DrugScore) that considers all diseased cell clusters, addressing intratumoral cellular heterogeneity before TopDrug selects significant FDA-approved candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36637-3
skills.summary: Aggregates ASGARD per-cluster drug repurposing rankings into a patient-level drug therapeutic score (DrugScore) that considers all diseased cell clusters, addressing intratumoral cellular heterogeneity before TopDrug selects significant FDA-approved candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the disease is driven by a single homogeneous cell population — per-cluster predictions alone may suffice, though the paper still reports multi-cluster AUC superiority When no normal-tissue control samples exist to compute case-vs-control differential signatures (the article notes substitutes are needed until normal tissue data are available) When the drug reference lacks a proper tissue-matched cell-line panel — the reference is limited to 98 LINCS L1000 cell lines

skills.search_text: multi-comparison-gene-occurrence-counting Use when you have one sub-directory per pairwise experimental comparison, each with scorecard outputs, and you need a per-gene tally of how many scorecards/quadrants of interest each gene appears in across comparisons. Only a single pairwise comparison is being analyzed (no multi-comparison folder structure exists), so occurrence counting across experiments is meaningless You need the four-way plot variant, since multiple_view/overview functions apply only to the scorecard, not the four-way plot Input CSV has not yet been processed into per-quadrant scorecard outcomes — run scorecard_functions.scorecard and reconstruct_scorecard per comparison first http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Merges pre-computed scorecard outputs from all pairwise experimental comparisons in a main folder into a per-gene occurrence report, distinguishing genes consistently altered across experiments (e.g., SA_RS13430 appearing on 65 scorecards) from isolated, condition-specific modifications. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Merges pre-computed scorecard outputs from all pairwise experimental comparisons in a main folder into a per-gene occurrence report, distinguishing genes consistently altered across experiments (e.g., SA_RS13430 appearing on 65 scorecards) from isolated, condition-specific modifications.

skills.description: Use when two or more pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB- or CellChat-derived) covering distinct biological conditions are available and the goal is to identify cell types or int-pairs whose communication is condition-specific, such as gain of interactions in critical vs moderate COVID-19.
skills.name: multi-condition-cci-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-condition-cci-comparison Use when two or more pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB- or CellChat-derived) covering distinct biological conditions are available and the goal is to identify cell types or int-pairs whose communication is condition-specific, such as gain of interactions in critical vs moderate COVID-19. You only have a single condition/dataset and no multi-condition comparison is intended — InterCellar's comparison module requires multiple datasets to extract condition-unique patterns. Raw scRNA-seq count matrices without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar builds on pre-computed, inferred interactions and does not infer CCI itself. The input CCI data was generated by a tool outside InterCellar's supported set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) — the article notes extension to other published tools is planned future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Compares pre-computed ligand-receptor cell-cell interaction (CCI) datasets across multiple conditions (e.g., control, moderate, critical COVID-19) in InterCellar's multiple-conditions module to highlight per-cell-type and per-interaction-pair patterns uniquely found in each condition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Compares pre-computed ligand-receptor cell-cell interaction (CCI) datasets across multiple conditions (e.g., control, moderate, critical COVID-19) in InterCellar's multiple-conditions module to highlight per-cell-type and per-interaction-pair patterns uniquely found in each condition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single condition/dataset and no multi-condition comparison is intended — InterCellar's comparison module requires multiple datasets to extract condition-unique patterns. Raw scRNA-seq count matrices without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar builds on pre-computed, inferred interactions and does not infer CCI itself. The input CCI data was generated by a tool outside InterCellar's supported set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) — the article notes extension to other published tools is planned future work.

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix plus meta_cells must yield predicted counts for held-out or out-of-sample condition combinations, with per-cell-type accuracy metrics.
skills.name: multi-condition-count-matrix-prediction
skills.search_text: multi-condition-count-matrix-prediction Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix plus meta_cells must yield predicted counts for held-out or out-of-sample condition combinations, with per-cell-type accuracy metrics. Each batch is measured under only one condition, so there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects The task is batch effect removal or condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection only — use extract_gene_scores or the integration task instead Condition types are strongly correlated in real data; combine them into a single combined condition type (e.g. stim1_stim2, ctrl1_ctrl2) before training rather than modeling them as independent http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predicts cell-type-specific perturbed scRNA-seq count matrices for unseen condition-batch combinations (e.g. <ctrl, healthy, batch 0> from <stim, severe, batch 1> input) using scDisInFact's disentangled shared-bio and unshared-bio latent factors, and benchmarks predictions against scGen and scPreGAN using MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Predicts cell-type-specific perturbed scRNA-seq count matrices for unseen condition-batch combinations (e.g. <ctrl, healthy, batch 0> from <stim, severe, batch 1> input) using scDisInFact's disentangled shared-bio and unshared-bio latent factors, and benchmarks predictions against scGen and scPreGAN using MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition, so there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects The task is batch effect removal or condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection only — use extract_gene_scores or the integration task instead Condition types are strongly correlated in real data; combine them into a single combined condition type (e.g. stim1_stim2, ctrl1_ctrl2) before training rather than modeling them as independent

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA-seq mixtures (e.g., different tissues from multiple donors) where batch effects within conditions must be removed without erasing across-condition biological differences.
skills.name: multi-condition-dataset-merging
skills.search_text: multi-condition-dataset-merging Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA-seq mixtures (e.g., different tissues from multiple donors) where batch effects within conditions must be removed without erasing across-condition biological differences. Simple single-tissue, multi-sample integration where all samples share the same axes of variation — consensus PCA in JOINTLY may be acceptable there, and the over-correction test is not the goal Datasets lacking a batch/condition metadata variable (batch_label), since jointly() requires batch.var to define batches Reproducing analyses with pyJOINTLY expecting identical results — the README states the R and Python versions do not produce identical results and all manuscript analyses used the R version http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Merges multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Lung and Pancreas benchmarks from Zenodo record 8298157) into a single mixture object with a batch_label variable, then integrates them with JOINTLY in regular PCA mode to remove within-tissue batch effects while retaining across-tissue biological variability (over-correction robustness test). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Merges multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Lung and Pancreas benchmarks from Zenodo record 8298157) into a single mixture object with a batch_label variable, then integrates them with JOINTLY in regular PCA mode to remove within-tissue batch effects while retaining across-tissue biological variability (over-correction robustness test).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Simple single-tissue, multi-sample integration where all samples share the same axes of variation — consensus PCA in JOINTLY may be acceptable there, and the over-correction test is not the goal Datasets lacking a batch/condition metadata variable (batch_label), since jointly() requires batch.var to define batches Reproducing analyses with pyJOINTLY expecting identical results — the README states the R and Python versions do not produce identical results and all manuscript analyses used the R version

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-level metadata with >=1 condition columns and a batch/study ID column, and you need to train scDisInFact or run cross-batch perturbation prediction.
skills.name: multi-condition-multi-batch-dataset-construction
skills.search_text: multi-condition-multi-batch-dataset-construction Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-level metadata with >=1 condition columns and a batch/study ID column, and you need to train scDisInFact or run cross-batch perturbation prediction. Each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper notes there is then not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects Only a single condition type exists and no batch structure needs modeling — task-specific perturbation methods like scGen/scPreGAN may suffice Condition types are strongly correlated and cannot be assumed mutually independent — combine them into one condition type rather than passing them as separate condition_keys http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a scdisinfact dataset object from a count matrix and cell metadata for multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq integration, explicitly encoding multiple condition types (e.g., age and disease severity) and a batch key so batch and condition effects can be disentangled downstream. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Constructs a scdisinfact dataset object from a count matrix and cell metadata for multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq integration, explicitly encoding multiple condition types (e.g., age and disease severity) and a batch key so batch and condition effects can be disentangled downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition — the paper notes there is then not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects Only a single condition type exists and no batch structure needs modeling — task-specific perturbation methods like scGen/scPreGAN may suffice Condition types are strongly correlated and cannot be assumed mutually independent — combine them into one condition type rather than passing them as separate condition_keys

skills.description: Use when a CSV of gene IDs with log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control comparisons must be screened for extreme or moderate expression variations across several experimental conditions (e.g., antibiotic, adjuvant, and co-treatment RNA-seq).
skills.name: multi-condition-transcriptome-scorecard-visualization
skills.search_text: multi-condition-transcriptome-scorecard-visualization Use when a CSV of gene IDs with log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control comparisons must be screened for extreme or moderate expression variations across several experimental conditions (e.g., antibiotic, adjuvant, and co-treatment RNA-seq). skills.summary: A Python scorecard library that groups genes from pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value tables into significance-filtered quadrants across multiple pairwise wet-lab comparisons, overcoming the limits of four-way plots and volcano plots in multi-condition differential-expression analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks pre-computed fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the CSV must already contain these; the library does not compute differential expression from raw counts Only a single pairwise comparison is needed and a standard volcano plot suffices — note that volcano plots get crowded with large samples and show one condition per graph Setting 'multiplication factor' to 1 degrades the scorecard into a plain four-way plot, which the library is designed to improve upon

skills.description: Use when FASTQ small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to hg19/hg38 with STAR and you need to classify and count reads into multiple small RNA classes (miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA) in one pass rather than running separate single-class tools.
skills.name: multi-database-small-rna-annotation
skills.search_text: multi-database-small-rna-annotation Use when FASTQ small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to hg19/hg38 with STAR and you need to classify and count reads into multiple small RNA classes (miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA) in one pass rather than running separate single-class tools. Pathways in KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP Single-gene nodes with no homologs to collapse (aggregation is unnecessary; x = 1 nodes need no read-count weighting) Non-human species or pathway databases (Reactome, Panther) outside the current FunHoP KEGG human-metabolism scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 FunHoP-style aggregation that collapses all functionally homologous genes in a multi-gene KEGG network node into a single node-level RNA-seq expression value, weighting reads by gene length and the dominant gene's read ratio, so differential expression can be computed per node rather than per gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: FunHoP-style aggregation that collapses all functionally homologous genes in a multi-gene KEGG network node into a single node-level RNA-seq expression value, weighting reads by gene length and the dominant gene's read ratio, so differential expression can be computed per node rather than per gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways in KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP Single-gene nodes with no homologs to collapse (aggregation is unnecessary; x = 1 nodes need no read-count weighting) Non-human species or pathway databases (Reactome, Panther) outside the current FunHoP KEGG human-metabolism scope

skills.description: Use when single-cell PAS matrices from multiple samples/donors and cell types must be integrated into low-dimensional factors that stratify clinical groups (e.g., MMRd vs MMRp) while correcting for known technical batch effects.
skills.name: multi-group-factor-analysis-training
skills.search_text: multi-group-factor-analysis-training Use when single-cell PAS matrices from multiple samples/donors and cell types must be integrated into low-dimensional factors that stratify clinical groups (e.g., MMRd vs MMRp) while correcting for known technical batch effects. The study contains fewer than 15 samples (not cells) — scPAFA notes MOFA requires at least 15 samples for multicellular pathway module identification. No known technical batch structure exists and a single-group design suffices — the multi-group framework is specifically recommended for correcting clearly known batch effects. The goal is pairwise cross-condition differential pathway activity per cell type rather than data-driven low-dimensional modules (MOFA factors are data-driven associations, not causal effects). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a multi-group MOFA+ model (mofapy2) on pseudobulk-averaged pathway activity scores (PAS) computed by scPAFA's fast_Ucell, using technical batch as group, to extract disease-related multicellular pathway modules (latent factors and pathway-by-cell-type weights). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Train a multi-group MOFA+ model (mofapy2) on pseudobulk-averaged pathway activity scores (PAS) computed by scPAFA's fast_Ucell, using technical batch as group, to extract disease-related multicellular pathway modules (latent factors and pathway-by-cell-type weights).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study contains fewer than 15 samples (not cells) — scPAFA notes MOFA requires at least 15 samples for multicellular pathway module identification. No known technical batch structure exists and a single-group design suffices — the multi-group framework is specifically recommended for correcting clearly known batch effects. The goal is pairwise cross-condition differential pathway activity per cell type rather than data-driven low-dimensional modules (MOFA factors are data-driven associations, not causal effects).

skills.description: Use when you must compare clustering accuracy across methods on multi-individual droplet scRNA-seq simulations (e.g., varying number of individuals, sigma_ik^2 heterogeneity, or Splatter group/batch-effect levels) and quantify results with ARI.
skills.name: multi-individual-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-individual-clustering-benchmarking Use when you must compare clustering accuracy across methods on multi-individual droplet scRNA-seq simulations (e.g., varying number of individuals, sigma_ik^2 heterogeneity, or Splatter group/batch-effect levels) and quantify results with ARI. Input is a single individual's data or a single matrix — BAMMSC then falls back to DIMMSC, so multi-individual benchmarking claims do not apply Input data are already normalized or reduced features rather than raw UMI counts — BAMM-SC is designed to take raw count data as input The goal is trajectory/developmental-stage analysis, which the authors explicitly defer to future papers rather than address with this clustering benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model for clustering droplet-based scRNA-seq data from multiple individuals, against competing clustering methods on simulated multi-individual UMI count data, scoring clustering accuracy with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) via mclust. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Benchmark BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model for clustering droplet-based scRNA-seq data from multiple individuals, against competing clustering methods on simulated multi-individual UMI count data, scoring clustering accuracy with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) via mclust.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single individual's data or a single matrix — BAMMSC then falls back to DIMMSC, so multi-individual benchmarking claims do not apply Input data are already normalized or reduced features rather than raw UMI counts — BAMM-SC is designed to take raw count data as input The goal is trajectory/developmental-stage analysis, which the authors explicitly defer to future papers rather than address with this clustering benchmark

skills.name: multi-input-combination-optimization-config
skills.search_text: multi-input-combination-optimization-config Use when reproducing DC3's Table 1 benchmark: an in silico GM12878/K562 mixture with scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and bulk HiChIP data must be deconvolved under four input-combination settings to compare PCC scores. Input data types are not among the supported combinations of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq and bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq/HiChIP from the same heterogeneous population (e.g., jointly-profiled sci-CAR data, which the authors deferred to future work) The analysis goal is only single-cell clustering without bulk deconvolution — the coupled NMF method of Duren et al. alone may suffice HiChIP interactions have not been restricted to genes present in the scRNA-seq data and enhancers in the scATAC-seq data, as the preprocessing requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Configure DC3 (De-Convolution and Coupled-Clustering) to run under different combinations of single-cell (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq) and bulk (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, HiChIP) inputs, switching alpha/beta/gamma indicators to test each input-combination setting and benchmark deconvolution accuracy across settings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Configure DC3 (De-Convolution and Coupled-Clustering) to run under different combinations of single-cell (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq) and bulk (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, HiChIP) inputs, switching alpha/beta/gamma indicators to test each input-combination setting and benchmark deconvolution accuracy across settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data types are not among the supported combinations of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq and bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq/HiChIP from the same heterogeneous population (e.g., jointly-profiled sci-CAR data, which the authors deferred to future work) The analysis goal is only single-cell clustering without bulk deconvolution — the coupled NMF method of Duren et al. alone may suffice HiChIP interactions have not been restricted to genes present in the scRNA-seq data and enhancers in the scATAC-seq data, as the preprocessing requires

When input is not a raw expression matrix but an already-computed similarity/feature table — SIMLR learns its own multi-kernel metric from expression data and is unsupervised, so precomputed distances bypass its core step When clusters or cell types are already known and labeled — a supervised classification approach is more appropriate than SIMLR's de novo discovery When the dataset is very large-scale and standard SIMLR is too slow — use the SIMLR_Large_Scale variant instead of the standard implementation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Learn a sample-to-sample similarity measure by combining multiple kernels, as implemented in SIMLR, to cluster heterogeneous samples (single cells or tumor cohorts) and estimate the number of populations directly from expression data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: Learn a sample-to-sample similarity measure by combining multiple kernels, as implemented in SIMLR, to cluster heterogeneous samples (single cells or tumor cohorts) and estimate the number of populations directly from expression data.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., .RData workspace like Test_1_mECS.RData) must be converted into a cell-to-cell similarity matrix for clustering, dimension reduction, or visualization, especially under high noise and dropout.
skills.name: multi-kernel-distance-metric-optimization
skills.search_text: multi-kernel-distance-metric-optimization Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., .RData workspace like Test_1_mECS.RData) must be converted into a cell-to-cell similarity matrix for clustering, dimension reduction, or visualization, especially under high noise and dropout. The samples are not single-cell expression data and a standard distance metric or linear method such as PCA already fits the data's statistical assumptions A gene subset with known function has been pre-selected and a supervised or feature-restricted analysis is required — SIMLR is unsupervised and allows only de novo discovery The goal is ranking features rather than learning sample-to-sample similarities — use SIMLR_Feature_Ranking instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 SIMLR's similarity-learning procedure combines multiple Gaussian kernels of cell-to-cell distances into a single learned sample-to-sample distance metric via an iterative optimization with a rank constraint, then applies graph diffusion to repair weak similarities caused by noise and dropout events in single-cell RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: SIMLR's similarity-learning procedure combines multiple Gaussian kernels of cell-to-cell distances into a single learned sample-to-sample distance metric via an iterative optimization with a rank constraint, then applies graph diffusion to repair weak similarities caused by noise and dropout events in single-cell RNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples are not single-cell expression data and a standard distance metric or linear method such as PCA already fits the data's statistical assumptions A gene subset with known function has been pre-selected and a supervised or feature-restricted analysis is required — SIMLR is unsupervised and allows only de novo discovery The goal is ranking features rather than learning sample-to-sample similarities — use SIMLR_Feature_Ranking instead

skills.description: Use when input is a single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix with high noise and dropout events, and the goal is de novo, unsupervised clustering or 2-D/3-D visualization of cell subpopulations.
skills.name: multi-kernel-similarity-learning
skills.search_text: multi-kernel-similarity-learning Use when input is a single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix with high noise and dropout events, and the goal is de novo, unsupervised clustering or 2-D/3-D visualization of cell subpopulations. Input data are provided purely as examples in the repository and should not be used in place of the ones from the respective publications. The analysis requires supervised classification using pre-selected gene subsets of known function — SIMLR is deliberately unsupervised for de novo discovery. Data fit the statistical assumptions of standard dimension reduction algorithms and lack the noise/dropout structure SIMLR is designed to address. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Learn a cell-to-cell similarity measure from single-cell RNA-seq data by combining multiple kernels and applying graph diffusion, as implemented in SIMLR, to support dimension reduction, clustering, and visualization of heterogeneous cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pmic.201700232
skills.summary: Learn a cell-to-cell similarity measure from single-cell RNA-seq data by combining multiple kernels and applying graph diffusion, as implemented in SIMLR, to support dimension reduction, clustering, and visualization of heterogeneous cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are provided purely as examples in the repository and should not be used in place of the ones from the respective publications. The analysis requires supervised classification using pre-selected gene subsets of known function — SIMLR is deliberately unsupervised for de novo discovery. Data fit the statistical assumptions of standard dimension reduction algorithms and lack the noise/dropout structure SIMLR is designed to address.

skills.description: Use when cells have two or more a priori labels capturing distinct biological variance (e.g., cell-cycle phase and cell line) and you want a single supervised-then-unsupervised embedding that preserves all label relationships.
skills.name: multi-label-lda-axis-merging
skills.search_text: multi-label-lda-axis-merging Use when cells have two or more a priori labels capturing distinct biological variance (e.g., cell-cycle phase and cell line) and you want a single supervised-then-unsupervised embedding that preserves all label relationships. Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — this supervised approach is inappropriate in those situations A label has a large degree of heterogeneity within a class or many populations, where HSS-LDA performance suffers More than 100 dimensions, where HSS feature selection is not feasible http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Runs separate HSS-LDA analyses on multiple class labels (e.g., cell-cycle phase and cell line in CyTOF data), then merges the resulting HSS-LD axis projections into a single feature set for unsupervised embedding (UMAP), capturing several known sources of variance in one plot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Runs separate HSS-LDA analyses on multiple class labels (e.g., cell-cycle phase and cell line in CyTOF data), then merges the resulting HSS-LD axis projections into a single feature set for unsupervised embedding (UMAP), capturing several known sources of variance in one plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — this supervised approach is inappropriate in those situations A label has a large degree of heterogeneity within a class or many populations, where HSS-LDA performance suffers More than 100 dimensions, where HSS feature selection is not feasible

skills.description: Use when reconstructing cell pseudo-space from scRNA-seq data: TCA characteristic matrices for ST reference and scRNA-seq exist, plus ST spot x-y coordinates, and per-cell spatial coordinates must be predicted.
skills.name: multi-layer-perceptron-coordinate-regression-training
skills.search_text: multi-layer-perceptron-coordinate-regression-training Use when reconstructing cell pseudo-space from scRNA-seq data: TCA characteristic matrices for ST reference and scRNA-seq exist, plus ST spot x-y coordinates, and per-cell spatial coordinates must be predicted. The goal is spatial domain identification of ST data itself (e.g., SpaGCN, BayesSpace, DR-SC territory) rather than projecting scRNA-seq cells into a pseudo space The tissue reference has low spatial coherence or differs architecturally from the scRNA-seq tissue (e.g., dACC lacking cortical layer 4) without an appropriateness assessment or pre-processing of the spatial reference Input data are raw expression matrices rather than TCA-extracted shared latent characteristic matrices — the transfer component analysis step must come first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains a two-layer fully connected MLP in PyTorch that regresses spatial x-y coordinates from TCA-extracted latent features of a spatial transcriptomics reference, then applies the trained model to scRNA-seq latent features to project single cells into a pseudo space (scSpace). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Trains a two-layer fully connected MLP in PyTorch that regresses spatial x-y coordinates from TCA-extracted latent features of a spatial transcriptomics reference, then applies the trained model to scRNA-seq latent features to project single cells into a pseudo space (scSpace).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spatial domain identification of ST data itself (e.g., SpaGCN, BayesSpace, DR-SC territory) rather than projecting scRNA-seq cells into a pseudo space The tissue reference has low spatial coherence or differs architecturally from the scRNA-seq tissue (e.g., dACC lacking cortical layer 4) without an appropriateness assessment or pre-processing of the spatial reference Input data are raw expression matrices rather than TCA-extracted shared latent characteristic matrices — the transfer component analysis step must come first

skills.name: multi-mapped-read-filtering
skills.search_text: multi-mapped-read-filtering Use when assigning small RNA-seq FASTQ reads to tRNA-derived loci (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, tRH, tRNA halves) and ambiguous reads from repetitive tRNA-flanking regions or paralogous tRNA genes must be excluded before subtype classification. Reads are long paired-end or whole-transcript RNA-seq data rather than 14–50 nt small RNAs; the '--norc -v 0 -m 50' realignment to the plus strand is calibrated for short sRNA reads The goal is quantification of tncRNAs expressed from multi-copy tRNA families where keeping multi-mapped reads (scaled or probabilistic assignment) is the desired behavior instead of discarding them Existing human tncRNA tools (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) are adequate — they are trained and tested on human datasets, not plant genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A read-mapping filter strategy for plant sRNA-seq tncRNA detection that keeps only error-tolerant, uniquely mapping reads: alignment to an artificial genome with bowtie '-v 2 --best', followed by realignment of uniquely mapped reads (SAM flags 0/16) to the plus strand with '-m 50' suppression of multi-mappers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: A read-mapping filter strategy for plant sRNA-seq tncRNA detection that keeps only error-tolerant, uniquely mapping reads: alignment to an artificial genome with bowtie '-v 2 --best', followed by realignment of uniquely mapped reads (SAM flags 0/16) to the plus strand with '-m 50' suppression of multi-mappers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are long paired-end or whole-transcript RNA-seq data rather than 14–50 nt small RNAs; the '--norc -v 0 -m 50' realignment to the plus strand is calibrated for short sRNA reads The goal is quantification of tncRNAs expressed from multi-copy tRNA families where keeping multi-mapped reads (scaled or probabilistic assignment) is the desired behavior instead of discarding them Existing human tncRNA tools (tDRmapper, MINTmap, tRF2Cancer) are adequate — they are trained and tested on human datasets, not plant genomes

skills.description: Use when benchmarking single-cell TE quantification methods that must resolve multi-mapping reads (e.g., Alu subfamilies, HERVK isoforms) across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or long-read datasets, using ARI/NMI clustering or simulation ground-truth accuracy as the comparison metric.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-allocation-benchmarking Use when benchmarking single-cell TE quantification methods that must resolve multi-mapping reads (e.g., Alu subfamilies, HERVK isoforms) across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or long-read datasets, using ARI/NMI clustering or simulation ground-truth accuracy as the comparison metric. Input is already a quantified TE feature/count table — this skill benchmarks read-allocation from aligned BAMs, not downstream matrix analysis Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements like L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where MATES coverage-vector context is incomplete and estimated multi-mapping rates may be inaccurate The task requires distinguishing nearly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, which all compared methods handle poorly http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark locus-specific allocation of multi-mapping reads to transposable elements (TEs) in single-cell data, comparing MATES against alignment-based methods (scTE, SoloTE) via cell-clustering metrics (ARI/NMI) and simulation-grounded quantification accuracy (R2, percent reads recaptured). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Benchmark locus-specific allocation of multi-mapping reads to transposable elements (TEs) in single-cell data, comparing MATES against alignment-based methods (scTE, SoloTE) via cell-clustering metrics (ARI/NMI) and simulation-grounded quantification accuracy (R2, percent reads recaptured).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantified TE feature/count table — this skill benchmarks read-allocation from aligned BAMs, not downstream matrix analysis Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements like L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where MATES coverage-vector context is incomplete and estimated multi-mapping rates may be inaccurate The task requires distinguishing nearly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, which all compared methods handle poorly

skills.description: Use when quantifying transposable element expression at individual locus resolution in single-cell scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data where repetitive TE sequences generate multi-mapping reads that alignment-only tools (scTE, SoloTE, Telescope) cannot resolve per-locus.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-neural-network
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-allocation-neural-network Use when quantifying transposable element expression at individual locus resolution in single-cell scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data where repetitive TE sequences generate multi-mapping reads that alignment-only tools (scTE, SoloTE, Telescope) cannot resolve per-locus. Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking context within the 2001 bp window is incomplete and αi estimates become inaccurate Distinguishing highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions — the model cannot separate these loci When computational resources lack GPUs: MATES typically requires more resources such as GPUs than scTE or SoloTE http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 A deep learning skill (MATES) that probabilistically allocates multi-mapping reads to specific transposable element loci in single-cell data by learning locus-specific multi-mapping rates from unique-read coverage context flanking each TE start, rather than assigning reads to best- or random-mapped loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: A deep learning skill (MATES) that probabilistically allocates multi-mapping reads to specific transposable element loci in single-cell data by learning locus-specific multi-mapping rates from unique-read coverage context flanking each TE start, rather than assigning reads to best- or random-mapped loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking context within the 2001 bp window is incomplete and αi estimates become inaccurate Distinguishing highly identical TE copies (e.g., HERVK isoforms) that lack uniquely mappable flanking regions — the model cannot separate these loci When computational resources lack GPUs: MATES typically requires more resources such as GPUs than scTE or SoloTE

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq or scATAC-seq alignments contain multi-mapping reads over repetitive TE loci and locus-specific (not subfamily-level) TE quantification or marker discovery is the goal.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-to-te-loci
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-allocation-to-te-loci Use when single-cell RNA-seq or scATAC-seq alignments contain multi-mapping reads over repetitive TE loci and locus-specific (not subfamily-level) TE quantification or marker discovery is the goal. The TE of interest is a long autonomously expressed element such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking unique-read coverage within the 2001 bp window is incomplete The TE copies are near-identical (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, so αi estimation cannot distinguish loci Quantification at the subfamily level is sufficient and GPU resources are constrained, since MATES requires more compute (GPUs) than scTE or SoloTE http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 MATES-based allocation of multi-mapping reads to specific transposable element loci in single-cell data, using unique-read coverage context flanking each TE start to train an AutoEncoder + MLP that estimates a locus-specific multi-mapping rate αi, yielding locus-level TE counts URi + ⌈αi × MRi⌉ per cell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: MATES-based allocation of multi-mapping reads to specific transposable element loci in single-cell data, using unique-read coverage context flanking each TE start to train an AutoEncoder + MLP that estimates a locus-specific multi-mapping rate αi, yielding locus-level TE counts URi + ⌈αi × MRi⌉ per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The TE of interest is a long autonomously expressed element such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where flanking unique-read coverage within the 2001 bp window is incomplete The TE copies are near-identical (e.g., HERVK isoforms) lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions, so αi estimation cannot distinguish loci Quantification at the subfamily level is sufficient and GPU resources are constrained, since MATES requires more compute (GPUs) than scTE or SoloTE

skills.description: Use when quantifying small RNA-seq reads (miRNA/piRNA/tRNA/snRNA/snoRNA/circRNA) where reads map to multiple loci of one RNA or shared sequences create cross-RNA-type ambiguity and per-RNA read counts are the output.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-count-disambiguation
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-count-disambiguation Use when quantifying small RNA-seq reads (miRNA/piRNA/tRNA/snRNA/snoRNA/circRNA) where reads map to multiple loci of one RNA or shared sequences create cross-RNA-type ambiguity and per-RNA read counts are the output. You need a single exclusive RNA-type assignment per read (this scheme deliberately assigns one count to each overlapping RNA, not a unique best annotation) Quantifying RNA classes outside COMPSRA's supported set (miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA, microbial RNA) or non-human genomes other than the supported human hg19/hg38 and rat rno5/rno6 references You require partial-overlap annotations — the default Rolp = 1 (-aol 1.0) demands the read lie completely within the annotated gene region http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 COMPSRA's Annotation module rule for counting small RNA-seq reads without double-counting: a read mapping to multiple genomic loci of the same RNA contributes one count to that RNA, while a read sharing sequence with distinct RNAs (e.g. let-7a-5p vs piR_008113) contributes one count to each overlapping RNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: COMPSRA's Annotation module rule for counting small RNA-seq reads without double-counting: a read mapping to multiple genomic loci of the same RNA contributes one count to that RNA, while a read sharing sequence with distinct RNAs (e.g. let-7a-5p vs piR_008113) contributes one count to each overlapping RNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a single exclusive RNA-type assignment per read (this scheme deliberately assigns one count to each overlapping RNA, not a unique best annotation) Quantifying RNA classes outside COMPSRA's supported set (miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA, microbial RNA) or non-human genomes other than the supported human hg19/hg38 and rat rno5/rno6 references You require partial-overlap annotations — the default Rolp = 1 (-aol 1.0) demands the read lie completely within the annotated gene region

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell BAM files with multi-mapping reads to repetitive TE loci and need per-cell, per-locus coverage vectors and unique/multi read segregation before training a MATES model.
skills.name: multi-mapping-read-segregation-from-bam
skills.search_text: multi-mapping-read-segregation-from-bam Use when you have single-cell BAM files with multi-mapping reads to repetitive TE loci and need per-cell, per-locus coverage vectors and unique/multi read segregation before training a MATES model. Input is already a feature-count matrix or h5ad gene expression table — segregation requires alignment-level BAM input Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases — the 2001-bp window centered on the TE start yields incomplete flanking coverage TE loci (e.g., HERVK isoforms) with high sequence similarity and no uniquely mappable flanking regions — flanking context carries no signal for segregation http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Segregate reads from a sorted single-cell BAM (mapped by STAR/STARsolo) into unique-mapping and multi-mapping sets per cell, then build per-locus 2001-bp coverage vectors (Vu for unique reads, Vm for multi-mapping reads) centered on TE start positions, binning them as U-bin or M-bin — the preprocessing substrate for MATES locus-specific TE quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Segregate reads from a sorted single-cell BAM (mapped by STAR/STARsolo) into unique-mapping and multi-mapping sets per cell, then build per-locus 2001-bp coverage vectors (Vu for unique reads, Vm for multi-mapping reads) centered on TE start positions, binning them as U-bin or M-bin — the preprocessing substrate for MATES locus-specific TE quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature-count matrix or h5ad gene expression table — segregation requires alignment-level BAM input Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases — the 2001-bp window centered on the TE start yields incomplete flanking coverage TE loci (e.g., HERVK isoforms) with high sequence similarity and no uniquely mappable flanking regions — flanking context carries no signal for segregation

skills.search_text: multi-method-annotation-comparison-across-datasets Use when evaluating whether a cluster-based annotation method (scCATCH) outperforms cell-based annotation tools on benchmark scRNA-seq datasets with published cluster assignments and manually assigned cell types. You need to annotate clusters without a reference comparison — scCATCH's performance depends on the CellMatch reference database, and a limited database can lead to incorrect annotation Your goal is annotating individual cells rather than clusters — the cell-based baselines (SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) operate per cell and face the challenge that multiple cell types may be present in one cluster The dataset has no published cluster assignments or manually assigned ground-truth cell types, since the consistent-rate metric requires cluster-level agreement with manual annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks automatic cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq clusters by comparing scCATCH's cluster-based approach against Seurat's one-against-all marker method and cell-based methods (CellAssign, SingleR, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn datasets, scoring each method by per-cluster and per-dataset consistent rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Benchmarks automatic cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq clusters by comparing scCATCH's cluster-based approach against Seurat's one-against-all marker method and cell-based methods (CellAssign, SingleR, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn datasets, scoring each method by per-cluster and per-dataset consistent rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to annotate clusters without a reference comparison — scCATCH's performance depends on the CellMatch reference database, and a limited database can lead to incorrect annotation Your goal is annotating individual cells rather than clusters — the cell-based baselines (SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH) operate per cell and face the challenge that multiple cell types may be present in one cluster The dataset has no published cluster assignments or manually assigned ground-truth cell types, since the consistent-rate metric requires cluster-level agreement with manual annotation

skills.description: Use when you need reliable positive/negative labels for candidate L-R interactions between cell clusters from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. panc8) to supervise a deep-learning CCI model, and no single statistical method's calls should be trusted alone.
skills.name: multi-method-cci-consensus-voting
skills.search_text: multi-method-cci-consensus-voting Use when you need reliable positive/negative labels for candidate L-R interactions between cell clusters from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. panc8) to supervise a deep-learning CCI model, and no single statistical method's calls should be trusted alone. You only have one statistical method available (e.g. CellChat alone) — the skill requires a majority vote across CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR plus geometric-mean scoring, so a single method cannot produce consensus labels. Your goal is the final CCI prediction rather than training labels — use DeepCCI's Interaction_inference.py on a trained model instead, with these labels serving only as supervision. Data is not scRNA-seq gene-expression with assignable cell clusters, so ligand/receptor expression products over the LRIDB cannot be computed per cluster pair. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns positive/negative ground-truth labels to candidate ligand–receptor-mediated cell–cell interactions by thresholding calls from CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR (plus DeepCCI's geometric-mean scoring over a shared LRIDB) and taking a majority vote across methods. These consensus labels then supervise DeepCCI's GCN-based interaction model training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: Assigns positive/negative ground-truth labels to candidate ligand–receptor-mediated cell–cell interactions by thresholding calls from CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR (plus DeepCCI's geometric-mean scoring over a shared LRIDB) and taking a majority vote across methods. These consensus labels then supervise DeepCCI's GCN-based interaction model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have one statistical method available (e.g. CellChat alone) — the skill requires a majority vote across CellChat, CellPhoneDB, and SingleCellSignalR plus geometric-mean scoring, so a single method cannot produce consensus labels. Your goal is the final CCI prediction rather than training labels — use DeepCCI's Interaction_inference.py on a trained model instead, with these labels serving only as supervision. Data is not scRNA-seq gene-expression with assignable cell clusters, so ligand/receptor expression products over the LRIDB cannot be computed per cluster pair.

skills.search_text: multi-method-cell-cell-communication-benchmarking Use when comparing performance of cell-cell communication inference tools (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK, SingleCellSignalR) on identical scRNA-seq datasets to quantify false-positive rates and robustness to cell subsampling. skills.when_to_use_negative: When a ground-truth set of validated cell-cell interactions is available — overlap-based comparison assumes similar methods generate similar results regardless of accuracy, so it is not a true accuracy measure When comparing tools that use different ligand-receptor databases if database choice alone is not the variable under study, since differing databases could contribute to the variety of predicted interactions and confound the comparison When the input lacks cell clustering labels, which are a pre-requisite for CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR

skills.search_text: multi-method-cell-type-benchmarking Use when you have single-cell count matrices with manually annotated labels and need to quantitatively compare which automatic cell-type identification methods (eager, lazy or marker-based) perform , e.g. across platforms or tissues. The task is a single-method prediction on a new dataset rather than a comparative benchmark against manual labels — use one method directly instead of the full evaluation harness Only marker lists and no labeled reference/training data are available — markersupervised interfaces cover this, but accuracy/F1-score against manual labels cannot be computed The training and testing data are not cell-type-labeled count matrices (e.g. already-annotated feature tables or non scRNA-seq data) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark multiple automatic cell-type identification methods for scRNA-seq data (e.g. clustifyr, scLearn, scHPL, SciBet, SingleR) by running them through the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package on shared train/test splits and comparing accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate. It exists because manual annotation is time-consuming and knowledge-dependent, while automatic methods vary in performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a single-method prediction on a new dataset rather than a comparative benchmark against manual labels — use one method directly instead of the full evaluation harness Only marker lists and no labeled reference/training data are available — markersupervised interfaces cover this, but accuracy/F1-score against manual labels cannot be computed The training and testing data are not cell-type-labeled count matrices (e.g. already-annotated feature tables or non scRNA-seq data)

Input is already a normalized expression matrix or a pre-computed DEG list rather than a raw count table produced from initial RNA-seq analysis A ground-truth spike-in setting is being used: the optimum vote threshold there was 2 by F-measure, so the strict all-methods (3-vote) cut-off would under-call true positives Only one method's output is available or the analysis design does not permit running multiple DEG methods, since the vote threshold requires at least the chosen minimum number of method calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines differential expression calls from multiple DEG detection methods (DESeq2, edgeR, NOISeq, limma) run inside DEgenes Hunter by a minimum vote threshold, because individual methods behave inconsistently across datasets. skills.summary: Combines differential expression calls from multiple DEG detection methods (DESeq2, edgeR, NOISeq, limma) run inside DEgenes Hunter by a minimum vote threshold, because individual methods behave inconsistently across datasets. Produces a per-gene consensus table with per-method calls, vote counts, and estimated logFC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized expression matrix or a pre-computed DEG list rather than a raw count table produced from initial RNA-seq analysis A ground-truth spike-in setting is being used: the optimum vote threshold there was 2 by F-measure, so the strict all-methods (3-vote) cut-off would under-call true positives Only one method's output is available or the analysis design does not permit running multiple DEG methods, since the vote threshold requires at least the chosen minimum number of method calls

skills.summary: Builds a benchmark comparison table of Kendall-tau correlation values for trajectory inference across multiple scRNA-seq dimensionality-reduction methods (scGAE, DCA, scVI, PHATE, SAUCIE, scGNN, ZINB-WaVE, Ivis) on simulated lineage datasets, mirroring the scGAE paper's Fig. 3a,b evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is clustering performance comparison rather than trajectory recovery — the paper notes scGAE and scGNN have similar trajectory performance but differ on clustering, so Kendall tau alone would not separate them there. skills.description: Use when comparing pseudotime/TI methods on datasets with known ground-truth cell ordering (e.g., VeloSim-simulated cycle-tree data), or when needing a per-path Kendall rank correlation benchmark against baseline velocity-based and expression-based methods.
skills.name: multi-method-trajectory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-method-trajectory-benchmarking Use when comparing pseudotime/TI methods on datasets with known ground-truth cell ordering (e.g., VeloSim-simulated cycle-tree data), or when needing a per-path Kendall rank correlation benchmark against baseline velocity-based and expression-based methods. The dataset has no ground-truth pseudotime or simulated trajectory structure, so Kendall correlation against truth cannot be computed. The goal is applying a single TI method to a new real dataset (e.g., hematopoiesis, dentate gyrus, pancreatic endocrinogenesis, forebrain) rather than head-to-head method benchmarking. The analysis requires only cluster-level trajectory topology without pseudotime ordering comparison (e.g., Directed-PAGA output). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark trajectory inference (TI) methods — CellPath, CellRank+DPT, VeTra, Vdpt, Slingshot — on simulated VeloSim cycle-tree datasets by scoring each method's pseudotime against ground truth with Kendall rank correlation. It quantifies how accurately each method recovers cell ordering, following the Figure 5G-style evaluation of the CellPath paper (Zhang & Zhang, 2021). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Benchmark trajectory inference (TI) methods — CellPath, CellRank+DPT, VeTra, Vdpt, Slingshot — on simulated VeloSim cycle-tree datasets by scoring each method's pseudotime against ground truth with Kendall rank correlation. It quantifies how accurately each method recovers cell ordering, following the Figure 5G-style evaluation of the CellPath paper (Zhang & Zhang, 2021).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth pseudotime or simulated trajectory structure, so Kendall correlation against truth cannot be computed. skills.search_text: multi-objective-loss-optimization Use when a graph autoencoder latent embedding must be refined for clustering: after pre-training on reconstruction loss alone, when initial cluster centroids (e.g. from Louvain on embedded data) are available and soft-assignment KL refinement is needed. skills.description: Use when evaluating multi-omic single-cell integration output (e.g., MaCroDNA assignments on scRNA-seq/scDNA-seq pairs) in the absence of ground truth, to quantify statistical significance and assignment stability via resampling.

skills.search_text: multi-omic-resampling-stability-analysis Use when evaluating multi-omic single-cell integration output (e.g., MaCroDNA assignments on scRNA-seq/scDNA-seq pairs) in the absence of ground truth, to quantify statistical significance and assignment stability via resampling. A partially known ground-truth correspondence between scRNA-seq and scDNA-seq cells exists (e.g., scTrio-seq CRC data) — direct assignment-accuracy evaluation against ground truth is the appropriate skill instead. The method being evaluated provides only clustering labels and no cell embedding (e.g. Seurat v4), so silhouette score cannot be computed for it and must be omitted Data are unpaired single-cell multi-omics batches requiring batch correction — the article notes Mowgli does not handle batch correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark paired single-cell multi-omics integration methods (Mowgli, Seurat v4 WNN, MOFA+, integrative NMF, Cobolt, Multigrate) on embedding and clustering performance using silhouette score, ARI across Leiden resolutions, and kNN purity score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Benchmark paired single-cell multi-omics integration methods (Mowgli, Seurat v4 WNN, MOFA+, integrative NMF, Cobolt, Multigrate) on embedding and clustering performance using silhouette score, ARI across Leiden resolutions, and kNN purity score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method being evaluated provides only clustering labels and no cell embedding (e.g. Seurat v4), so silhouette score cannot be computed for it and must be omitted Data are unpaired single-cell multi-omics batches requiring batch correction — the article notes Mowgli does not handle batch correction

skills.description: Use when Leiden clusters from the post-processed scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph are available and cluster-specific bio-markers across RNA/ATAC/protein modalities are needed to interpret and annotate clusters.
skills.name: multi-omics-marker-score-extraction
skills.search_text: multi-omics-marker-score-extraction Use when Leiden clusters from the post-processed scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph are available and cluster-specific bio-markers across RNA/ATAC/protein modalities are needed to interpret and annotate clusters. Cross-modality feature relationships are the primary goal — the paper defers learning cross-modality relationships via feature representations to future work Batches lack matched feature sets per modality (features must first be matched via gene intersection or peak remapping) You need integration metrics only (e.g., batch mixing) without cell-type interpretation — the first-stage cell factors suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Retrains the scMoMaT matrix tri-factorization model with Leiden cluster labels held fixed as binary cell factors, then extracts per-cluster feature scoring matrices (marker genes, marker regions/motifs, marker proteins) across modalities for cell-type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Retrains the scMoMaT matrix tri-factorization model with Leiden cluster labels held fixed as binary cell factors, then extracts per-cluster feature scoring matrices (marker genes, marker regions/motifs, marker proteins) across modalities for cell-type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cross-modality feature relationships are the primary goal — the paper defers learning cross-modality relationships via feature representations to future work Batches lack matched feature sets per modality (features must first be matched via gene intersection or peak remapping) You need integration metrics only (e.g., batch mixing) without cell-type interpretation — the first-stage cell factors suffice

skills.description: Use when two or more FAVA-scored PCC networks (e.g., scRNA-seq and bulk proteomics tsv inputs) need to be converted to calibrated posterior probabilities and merged into one combined functional association network with STRING-style confidence cutoffs.
skills.name: multi-omics-network-union-integration
skills.search_text: multi-omics-network-union-integration Use when two or more FAVA-scored PCC networks (e.g., scRNA-seq and bulk proteomics tsv inputs) need to be converted to calibrated posterior probabilities and merged into one combined functional association network with STRING-style confidence cutoffs. The input is raw scRNA-seq or proteomics data rather than already FAVA-scored PCC networks — run the FAVA VAE dimensionality-reduction and correlation step first. Only one data type's network is available — the union integration requires at least two calibrated networks (e.g., HPA and PRIDE) to merge. No benchmark of known associations (e.g., KEGG) is available — without it, the local precision estimates needed to fit the calibration function cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calibrates FAVA-scored PCC networks from two omics data types (Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics) into STRING-style posterior probabilities on the KEGG benchmark, then merges them into a single combined functional association network by union and extracts subnetworks at 15%, 40%, and 70% confidence cutoffs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Calibrates FAVA-scored PCC networks from two omics data types (Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics) into STRING-style posterior probabilities on the KEGG benchmark, then merges them into a single combined functional association network by union and extracts subnetworks at 15%, 40%, and 70% confidence cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw scRNA-seq or proteomics data rather than already FAVA-scored PCC networks — run the FAVA VAE dimensionality-reduction and correlation step first. Only one data type's network is available — the union integration requires at least two calibrated networks (e.g., HPA and PRIDE) to merge. No benchmark of known associations (e.g., KEGG) is available — without it, the local precision estimates needed to fit the calibration function cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when fine-tuning a source-pretrained scRNA-seq annotation encoder on target data without source access and you need a self-supervised neighbor-based affinity loss on 'known' cells.
skills.name: multi-order-local-affinity-loss-implementation
skills.search_text: multi-order-local-affinity-loss-implementation Use when fine-tuning a source-pretrained scRNA-seq annotation encoder on target data without source access and you need a self-supervised neighbor-based affinity loss on 'known' cells. Source data are still available — explicit feature alignment between source and target is possible, so source-free affinity regularization is unnecessary. The known/unknown partition of target cells has not yet been established — unknown neighbors must be excluded, so applying L_nbht without the adaptive manifold-mixup threshold risks noisy supervision. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements scEMAIL's multi-order local affinity loss (L_nbht), which retrieves bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional neighbors of each target cell from offline memory banks and imposes weighted affinity regularizations on 'known' target cells during source-free model adaptation, mitigating batch effect via reliable self-supervised neighbor information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Implements scEMAIL's multi-order local affinity loss (L_nbht), which retrieves bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional neighbors of each target cell from offline memory banks and imposes weighted affinity regularizations on 'known' target cells during source-free model adaptation, mitigating batch effect via reliable self-supervised neighbor information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source data are still available — explicit feature alignment between source and target is possible, so source-free affinity regularization is unnecessary. The known/unknown partition of target cells has not yet been established — unknown neighbors must be excluded, so applying L_nbht without the adaptive manifold-mixup threshold risks noisy supervision.

skills.description: Use when adapting a pre-trained single-cell classifier to a target scRNA-seq/CITE-seq/scATAC-seq dataset with no access to source data, and batch effect must be mitigated self-supervised from target neighborhoods.
skills.name: multi-order-neighbor-affinity-optimization
skills.search_text: multi-order-neighbor-affinity-optimization Use when adapting a pre-trained single-cell classifier to a target scRNA-seq/CITE-seq/scATAC-seq dataset with no access to source data, and batch effect must be mitigated self-supervised from target neighborhoods. Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g. scArches-style surgery) is possible — scEMAIL's adaptation is designed for the source-free setting where privacy or storage prevents sharing raw source data. Target data have no novel cell types and no source-target batch effect — the local affinity regularization and the D/Dt machinery add unnecessary complexity. Labels are unavailable even in a source dataset (this is a transfer/annotation method that requires a trained source classifier, not a de novo clustering method). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A source-free model-adaptation step from scEMAIL that fine-tunes only the ZINB autoencoder encoder h (classifier weights fixed) by minimizing target ZINB denoising NLL plus a local affinity loss built from bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional nearest neighbors, to implicitly mitigate source-target batch effect without raw source data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: A source-free model-adaptation step from scEMAIL that fine-tunes only the ZINB autoencoder encoder h (classifier weights fixed) by minimizing target ZINB denoising NLL plus a local affinity loss built from bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional nearest neighbors, to implicitly mitigate source-target batch effect without raw source data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g. scArches-style surgery) is possible — scEMAIL's adaptation is designed for the source-free setting where privacy or storage prevents sharing raw source data. Target data have no novel cell types and no source-target batch effect — the local affinity regularization and the D/Dt machinery add unnecessary complexity. Labels are unavailable even in a source dataset (this is a transfer/annotation method that requires a trained source classifier, not a de novo clustering method).
