skills.description: Use when a repeated cross-validation feature-selection experiment (e.g., 5-times 5-fold, 25 partitions) must be reduced to the features selected in every partition, to expose partition-invariant discriminative sequence patterns.
skills.name: multi-partition-feature-set-intersection-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-partition-feature-set-intersection-analysis Use when a repeated cross-validation feature-selection experiment (e.g., 5-times 5-fold, 25 partitions) must be reduced to the features selected in every partition, to expose partition-invariant discriminative sequence patterns. When the goal is to rank or score features by importance rather than find features consistently selected across all partitions (use the selector's feature_importances_ directly instead) When input is already a reduced, curated feature table and no cross-validation feature-selection runs exist to intersect When combining position-specific features with frequency-based features in single models — the authors found these do not work well together and deferred that to a future feature-subspace ensemble approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Recovers the discriminative position-specific gapped k-mer patterns for RNA 5hmC prediction by intersecting the mode-wise RF-selected feature sets (top 400 per selector) from all 25 training partitions of the 5-times 5-fold cross-validation, yielding 34 features consistently selected in every partition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: Recovers the discriminative position-specific gapped k-mer patterns for RNA 5hmC prediction by intersecting the mode-wise RF-selected feature sets (top 400 per selector) from all 25 training partitions of the 5-times 5-fold cross-validation, yielding 34 features consistently selected in every partition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to rank or score features by importance rather than find features consistently selected across all partitions (use the selector's feature_importances_ directly instead) When input is already a reduced, curated feature table and no cross-validation feature-selection runs exist to intersect When combining position-specific features with frequency-based features in single models — the authors found these do not work well together and deferred that to a future feature-subspace ensemble approach

skills.description: Use when a cell-level trajectory inference output (e.g. cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) assigns cells to more than one path and you need a per-dataset statistic of pseudotime agreement across those paths.
skills.name: multi-path-cell-consistency-quantification
skills.search_text: multi-path-cell-consistency-quantification Use when a cell-level trajectory inference output (e.g. cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) assigns cells to more than one path and you need a per-dataset statistic of pseudotime agreement across those paths. Cells assigned to only a single CellPath trajectory path — Diffpst across paths is undefined for them You need a global alignment of locally detected paths rather than a per-cell pseudotime consistency statistic — the article lists global path alignment as a not-yet-implemented future direction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies whether CellPath-assigned pseudotimes are consistent for cells that belong to multiple trajectory paths, by computing Diffpst (mean absolute deviation of path-percentile positions) per dataset, as in the CellPath paper's Figure S4G consistency analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Quantifies whether CellPath-assigned pseudotimes are consistent for cells that belong to multiple trajectory paths, by computing Diffpst (mean absolute deviation of path-percentile positions) per dataset, as in the CellPath paper's Figure S4G consistency analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells assigned to only a single CellPath trajectory path — Diffpst across paths is undefined for them You need a global alignment of locally detected paths rather than a per-cell pseudotime consistency statistic — the article lists global path alignment as a not-yet-implemented future direction

skills.description: Use when a binary/additive-encoded SNP x sample matrix with case/control labels, covariate classes, and a PPI/gene-interaction prior is available and the goal is to discover higher-order gene meta-markers associated with multiple phenotypes beyond single-interval methods like FastCMH or SiNIMin.
skills.name: multi-phenotype-gwas-pattern-scan
skills.search_text: multi-phenotype-gwas-pattern-scan Use when a binary/additive-encoded SNP x sample matrix with case/control labels, covariate classes, and a PPI/gene-interaction prior is available and the goal is to discover higher-order gene meta-markers associated with multiple phenotypes beyond single-interval methods like FastCMH or SiNIMin. When the goal is to test single genomic intervals conditioned on a covariate only — FastCMH (R package or C code) is the appropriate tool, not higher-order meta-marker mining When no prior biological knowledge of gene interactions (PPI network, pathways, complexes) is available or the features cannot be mapped to genes/nodes in such a network When labels are not binary case/control; HOGImine expects a binary labels matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Run HOGImine (hogimine_additive) over each phenotype of a GWAS dataset (e.g. Atwell et al. 2010 A. thaliana) to mine significant gene-interaction meta-markers, using network priors up to k=4 interacting genes and Westfall-Young permutation testing to control family-wise error rate at 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Run HOGImine (hogimine_additive) over each phenotype of a GWAS dataset (e.g. Atwell et al. 2010 A. thaliana) to mine significant gene-interaction meta-markers, using network priors up to k=4 interacting genes and Westfall-Young permutation testing to control family-wise error rate at 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to test single genomic intervals conditioned on a covariate only — FastCMH (R package or C code) is the appropriate tool, not higher-order meta-marker mining When no prior biological knowledge of gene interactions (PPI network, pathways, complexes) is available or the features cannot be mapped to genes/nodes in such a network When labels are not binary case/control; HOGImine expects a binary labels matrix

skills.description: Use when automatically classifying malignant vs non-malignant cells from raw scRNA-seq count matrices spanning different cancer types and sequencing platforms (Smart-seq2 vs 10X Chromium), and when benchmarking that classification against CopyKAT using per-sample F1 scores.
skills.name: multi-platform-scrna-dataset-harmonization
skills.search_text: multi-platform-scrna-dataset-harmonization Use when automatically classifying malignant vs non-malignant cells from raw scRNA-seq count matrices spanning different cancer types and sequencing platforms (Smart-seq2 vs 10X Chromium), and when benchmarking that classification against CopyKAT using per-sample F1 scores. The sample is expected to contain only malignant cells with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — aneuploidy-based classification is unsuitable there You already have manually identified reference normal-cell clusters and want a supervised inferCNV-style analysis rather than fully automatic end-to-end classification The goal is clonal substructure and phylogeny rather than pure malignant/non-malignant classification (then set SUBCLONES = TRUE, outside this skill's scope) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Run SCEVAN's fully automatic malignant/non-malignant cell classification across 106 real scRNA-seq samples from multiple cancer types (GBM, HNSCC, colorectal) and platforms (Smart-seq2 and 10X Chromium), benchmarking per-sample F1 against CopyKAT v1.0.5 (SCEVAN 0.90 vs CopyKAT 0.63, winning in 63% of samples). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Run SCEVAN's fully automatic malignant/non-malignant cell classification across 106 real scRNA-seq samples from multiple cancer types (GBM, HNSCC, colorectal) and platforms (Smart-seq2 and 10X Chromium), benchmarking per-sample F1 against CopyKAT v1.0.5 (SCEVAN 0.90 vs CopyKAT 0.63, winning in 63% of samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is expected to contain only malignant cells with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — aneuploidy-based classification is unsuitable there You already have manually identified reference normal-cell clusters and want a supervised inferCNV-style analysis rather than fully automatic end-to-end classification The goal is clonal substructure and phylogeny rather than pure malignant/non-malignant classification (then set SUBCLONES = TRUE, outside this skill's scope)

skills.description: Use when raw read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches or platforms must be integrated while cell-type labels are unknown, and batch effects, overdispersion, dropout events, and cell-specific sequencing depth need joint correction.
skills.name: multi-platform-scrna-seq-data-integration
skills.search_text: multi-platform-scrna-seq-data-integration Use when raw read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches or platforms must be integrated while cell-type labels are unknown, and batch effects, overdispersion, dropout events, and cell-specific sequencing depth need joint correction. The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 only cell types 3 and 4) — the article states no method, including BUSseq, is applicable The design violates the conditions of the completely randomized, reference panel, or chain-type designs under which biological variability can be separated from batch effects Input is already normalized/transformed expression data — BUSseq takes raw read counts and models count nature, overdispersion, and dropouts itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrate read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches or platforms (e.g., CEL-seq2, Drop-seq, 10X Chromium) using BUSseq, a Bayesian hierarchical model (Batch Effects Correction with Unknown Subtypes) that simultaneously corrects batch effects, clusters cell types, imputes dropouts, and identifies intrinsic genes without preliminary normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Integrate read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches or platforms (e.g., CEL-seq2, Drop-seq, 10X Chromium) using BUSseq, a Bayesian hierarchical model (Batch Effects Correction with Unknown Subtypes) that simultaneously corrects batch effects, clusters cell types, imputes dropouts, and identifies intrinsic genes without preliminary normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures only cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 only cell types 3 and 4) — the article states no method, including BUSseq, is applicable The design violates the conditions of the completely randomized, reference panel, or chain-type designs under which biological variability can be separated from batch effects Input is already normalized/transformed expression data — BUSseq takes raw read counts and models count nature, overdispersion, and dropouts itself

skills.description: Use when evaluating reference-free cell-type deconvolution on multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data from multiple platforms (Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) and checking that known marker genes are recovered.
skills.name: multi-platform-st-dataset-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-platform-st-dataset-benchmarking Use when evaluating reference-free cell-type deconvolution on multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data from multiple platforms (Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) and checking that known marker genes are recovered. Data are sub-cellular pixel-resolution ST, where the authors state new methods specifically suited for that resolution will be needed Tissue slivers or thin structures covering only a few pixels, which the discussion flags as challenging for deconvolution by STdeconvolve Gene expression is too sparse with high stochastic drop-out rates or cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels, where LDA may fail to identify distinct groups of co-expressed genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark STdeconvolve, a reference-free LDA-based cell-type deconvolution, across real high-resolution multi-cellular ST datasets from diverse technologies (10X Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) at pre-specified numbers of cell types K, verifying that deconvolved transcriptional profiles recover expected marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Benchmark STdeconvolve, a reference-free LDA-based cell-type deconvolution, across real high-resolution multi-cellular ST datasets from diverse technologies (10X Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) at pre-specified numbers of cell types K, verifying that deconvolved transcriptional profiles recover expected marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are sub-cellular pixel-resolution ST, where the authors state new methods specifically suited for that resolution will be needed Tissue slivers or thin structures covering only a few pixels, which the discussion flags as challenging for deconvolution by STdeconvolve Gene expression is too sparse with high stochastic drop-out rates or cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels, where LDA may fail to identify distinct groups of co-expressed genes

skills.description: Use when you have a probe-level microarray intensity matrix (e.g. a GEO series matrix) whose annotation table maps multiple probes to the same gene symbol, and you need one row per gene for downstream analysis.
skills.name: multi-probe-gene-collapsing-maxmean
skills.search_text: multi-probe-gene-collapsing-maxmean Use when you have a probe-level microarray intensity matrix (e.g. a GEO series matrix) whose annotation table maps multiple probes to the same gene symbol, and you need one row per gene for downstream analysis. The data are already gene-level (e.g. RNA-seq counts like the curatedAdipoRNA adipo_counts matrix) — no probe collapsing is needed The dataset lacks a probe-to-gene annotation table — in the source study, datasets missing probe annotations were excluded rather than collapsed Collapses a probe-level microarray intensity matrix to a gene-level matrix by mapping probe IDs to mouse gene symbols and, for genes with multiple probes, applying the 'MaxMean' rule of the collapseRows function to retain the probe with the highest mean expression across samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/21623945.2020.1829852
skills.summary: Collapses a probe-level microarray intensity matrix to a gene-level matrix by mapping probe IDs to mouse gene symbols and, for genes with multiple probes, applying the 'MaxMean' rule of the collapseRows function to retain the probe with the highest mean expression across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already gene-level (e.g. RNA-seq counts like the curatedAdipoRNA adipo_counts matrix) — no probe collapsing is needed The dataset lacks a probe-to-gene annotation table — in the source study, datasets missing probe annotations were excluded rather than collapsed

skills.summary: Reconstructs deCS cell type-specific gene (CTGene) reference panels by scoring every gene's cell type specificity — t-statistics for bulk RNA-seq references (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune) and z-scores for scRNA-seq references (HCL, HCAF) — and retaining the top 5% genes per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is annotating a query scRNA-seq dataset against an already-built reference panel rather than reconstructing the panels themselves The query input is a marker gene list to be tested with deCS.fisher against existing CTgene panels rather than deriving new panels Novel/uncharacterized cell types are expected — deCS is a mapping-based toolkit and fails to characterize novel cell types

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single query dataset already paired with a single matching reference — standard single-reference annotation tools suffice Predicting on disease query data where no suitable disease model exists — the paper notes it is 'difficult to build a comprehensive database for disease scRNA-seq data' and recommends users train on their own disease data The query data are non-human scRNA-seq — transfer to other species is anticipated but not demonstrated

skills.description: Use when predicting tumor neoantigens from WES/WGS plus optional RNA-Seq of matched tumor-normal pairs and you need to test or control for reference genome build (GRCh37 vs GRCh38) effects on variant calling and downstream pMHC predictions.
skills.name: multi-reference-genome-pipeline-configuration
skills.search_text: multi-reference-genome-pipeline-configuration Use when predicting tumor neoantigens from WES/WGS plus optional RNA-Seq of matched tumor-normal pairs and you need to test or control for reference genome build (GRCh37 vs GRCh38) effects on variant calling and downstream pMHC predictions. The analysis requires TCR sequencing integration or TCR-pMHC binding prediction — the article states this is future work and not yet part of the TSNAD pipeline Input data is not paired WES/WGS (e.g., already-variant-called VCFs only) and you need the full raw-read-to-neoantigen one-stop workflow with its specific depth requirements (minimum 15x WGS / 50x WES) A single reference genome is fixed and re-running both builds is unnecessary — TSNAD v1.0 users, who support only GRCh37, cannot benefit from the GRCh38 branch http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run the TSNAD v2.0 one-stop neoantigen prediction pipeline twice, once against GRCh37 and once against GRCh38, using the -V genome-build flag of the Dockerized pipeline to assess how reference genome choice affects neoantigen calls on the TESLA dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Run the TSNAD v2.0 one-stop neoantigen prediction pipeline twice, once against GRCh37 and once against GRCh38, using the -V genome-build flag of the Dockerized pipeline to assess how reference genome choice affects neoantigen calls on the TESLA dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires TCR sequencing integration or TCR-pMHC binding prediction — the article states this is future work and not yet part of the TSNAD pipeline Input data is not paired WES/WGS (e.g., already-variant-called VCFs only) and you need the full raw-read-to-neoantigen one-stop workflow with its specific depth requirements (minimum 15x WGS / 50x WES) A single reference genome is fixed and re-running both builds is unnecessary — TSNAD v1.0 users, who support only GRCh37, cannot benefit from the GRCh38 branch

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq query matrix needs cell-type labels transferred from multiple heterogeneous reference datasets, especially with imbalanced/rare cell types or batch effects between reference and query.
skills.name: multi-reference-label-transfer
skills.search_text: multi-reference-label-transfer Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq query matrix needs cell-type labels transferred from multiple heterogeneous reference datasets, especially with imbalanced/rare cell types or batch effects between reference and query. The query is non-human scRNA-seq — SELINA's reference atlas covers 230 distinct human cell types, with transfer to other species only anticipated, not demonstrated Only a single small marker list is available with no reference expression data — marker-based tools like Garnett or SCINA fit that scenario instead The query is a disease dataset run without the --disease flag, where fine-tuning against normal references would be inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate human scRNA-seq query cells using SELINA, a deep-learning framework that jointly leverages multiple pre-curated reference datasets (1.7 million cells, 230 human cell types) via SMOTE cell-type balancing, multi-adversarial domain adaptation (MADA) pre-training, and autoencoder fine-tuning before label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Annotate human scRNA-seq query cells using SELINA, a deep-learning framework that jointly leverages multiple pre-curated reference datasets (1.7 million cells, 230 human cell types) via SMOTE cell-type balancing, multi-adversarial domain adaptation (MADA) pre-training, and autoencoder fine-tuning before label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is non-human scRNA-seq — SELINA's reference atlas covers 230 distinct human cell types, with transfer to other species only anticipated, not demonstrated Only a single small marker list is available with no reference expression data — marker-based tools like Garnett or SCINA fit that scenario instead The query is a disease dataset run without the --disease flag, where fine-tuning against normal references would be inappropriate

skills.description: Use when sRNA-seq data must be mined for phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters against both a genome and a transcriptome reference, and when integrated multi-reference PHAS loci sets or alternative-splicing-derived phasiRNAs are the target output.
skills.name: multi-reference-phas-loci-integration
skills.search_text: multi-reference-phas-loci-integration Use when sRNA-seq data must be mined for phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters against both a genome and a transcriptome reference, and when integrated multi-reference PHAS loci sets or alternative-splicing-derived phasiRNAs are the target output. Only one reference sequence (single transcriptome or single genome) is available and no integration of multi-reference results is intended — run phasiHunter phase alone instead. The goal is degradome-based target verification or initiator (trigger) miRNA prediction rather than PHAS loci discovery and integration — use the target/initiator/deg submodules instead. Input sRNA reads are already mapped (no preprocess step needed) and no PHAS loci prediction is requested. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predict PHAS loci independently against multiple reference sequences (transcriptome cDNA and genome gDNA) with PhasiHunter's phase module, then merge the results with the integration module to recover PHAS genes missed by single-reference tools, including phasiRNAs arising from alternative splicing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Predict PHAS loci independently against multiple reference sequences (transcriptome cDNA and genome gDNA) with PhasiHunter's phase module, then merge the results with the integration module to recover PHAS genes missed by single-reference tools, including phasiRNAs arising from alternative splicing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one reference sequence (single transcriptome or single genome) is available and no integration of multi-reference results is intended — run phasiHunter phase alone instead. The goal is degradome-based target verification or initiator (trigger) miRNA prediction rather than PHAS loci discovery and integration — use the target/initiator/deg submodules instead. Input sRNA reads are already mapped (no preprocess step needed) and no PHAS loci prediction is requested.

skills.description: Use when phasiRNA predictions have been run separately against cDNA, gdna, and/or flnc references (phase_a.txt/phase_o.txt outputs) and the goal is to merge them into one annotation-anchored result and quantify reference-specific loci.
skills.name: multi-reference-result-integration
skills.search_text: multi-reference-result-integration Use when phasiRNA predictions have been run separately against cDNA, gdna, and/or flnc references (phase_a.txt/phase_o.txt outputs) and the goal is to merge them into one annotation-anchored result and quantify reference-specific loci. Only a single reference sequence was used, so there are no multi-reference phase outputs to integrate — run the phase module alone instead The goal is initiator/target prediction or differential expression of phasiRNAs (use the 'target'/'initiator' or 'deg' modules), not merging multi-reference PHAS loci No genome gff3 annotation is available and genomic anchoring of integrated loci is required but impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS loci predictions generated against multiple reference sequences (transcriptome, genome, full-length transcriptome) with the PhasiHunter integration module, then computes reference-unique PHAS gene sets and classifies them by exon/intron structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS loci predictions generated against multiple reference sequences (transcriptome, genome, full-length transcriptome) with the PhasiHunter integration module, then computes reference-unique PHAS gene sets and classifies them by exon/intron structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single reference sequence was used, so there are no multi-reference phase outputs to integrate — run the phase module alone instead The goal is initiator/target prediction or differential expression of phasiRNAs (use the 'target'/'initiator' or 'deg' modules), not merging multi-reference PHAS loci No genome gff3 annotation is available and genomic anchoring of integrated loci is required but impossible

skills.description: Use when DA-testing from scRNA-Seq data involves biological replicates (e.g. several mice per age group), where inter-mouse variability must be separated from the condition-specific cell-state frequency shift.
skills.name: multi-replicates-mouse-cohort-design
skills.search_text: multi-replicates-mouse-cohort-design Use when DA-testing from scRNA-Seq data involves biological replicates (e.g. several mice per age group), where inter-mouse variability must be separated from the condition-specific cell-state frequency shift. Data come from a single sample per condition with no replicate structure — there is no varREP covariate to model and inter-subject variance cannot be estimated The goal is plain clustering or cell-type annotation rather than condition-associated differential abundance of cell states Cell attribute labels (sample/phenotype annotation) carry many false positives, since ELVAR was reported to be more sensitive to FPs in the clustering attribute than in cell-type annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Design and analyze a multi-mouse scRNA-Seq cohort in which biological replicate structure (multiple mice per age group) is carried through the ELVAR differential-abundance pipeline, with mouse replicate modeled explicitly as a variance covariate (varREP) in the negative-binomial regression step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Design and analyze a multi-mouse scRNA-Seq cohort in which biological replicate structure (multiple mice per age group) is carried through the ELVAR differential-abundance pipeline, with mouse replicate modeled explicitly as a variance covariate (varREP) in the negative-binomial regression step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from a single sample per condition with no replicate structure — there is no varREP covariate to model and inter-subject variance cannot be estimated The goal is plain clustering or cell-type annotation rather than condition-associated differential abundance of cell states Cell attribute labels (sample/phenotype annotation) carry many false positives, since ELVAR was reported to be more sensitive to FPs in the clustering attribute than in cell-type annotation

skills.description: Use when a stochastic trajectory or pseudotime method (e.g. Cytopath on RNA velocity fields) is rerun across independent runs and stability or median performance across runs must be reported, e.g. Pearson correlation with elapsed stimulation time (0–120 min).
skills.name: multi-run-repeatability-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-run-repeatability-analysis Use when a stochastic trajectory or pseudotime method (e.g. Cytopath on RNA velocity fields) is rerun across independent runs and stability or median performance across runs must be reported, e.g. Pearson correlation with elapsed stimulation time (0–120 min). The trajectory method is deterministic (no stochastic simulation), so repeated runs would be identical and repeatability analysis is uninformative. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable or the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the article does not recommend performing Cytopath trajectory inference in these cases, so run-level correlation summaries would be meaningless. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies run-to-run stability of stochastic trajectory inference by repeating Cytopath's Markov-chain pseudotime inference over multiple independent runs (e.g. 10) and summarizing per-run metrics such as Pearson correlation with the scNT-seq stimulation-duration internal clock. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Quantifies run-to-run stability of stochastic trajectory inference by repeating Cytopath's Markov-chain pseudotime inference over multiple independent runs (e.g. 10) and summarizing per-run metrics such as Pearson correlation with the scNT-seq stimulation-duration internal clock.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory method is deterministic (no stochastic simulation), so repeated runs would be identical and repeatability analysis is uninformative. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable or the underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the article does not recommend performing Cytopath trajectory inference in these cases, so run-level correlation summaries would be meaningless.

skills.description: Use when you have ≥2 SRT sections (e.g. the 12-sample DLPFC 10x Visium set) with batch/individual effects and need joint spatial domain detection or cross-sample integrated clustering.
skills.name: multi-sample-batch-effect-integration
skills.search_text: multi-sample-batch-effect-integration Use when you have ≥2 SRT sections (e.g. the 12-sample DLPFC 10x Visium set) with batch/individual effects and need joint spatial domain detection or cross-sample integrated clustering. You have a single SRT section only — the predecessor SC.MEB fits one sample and iSC.MEB's batch-effect estimation is unnecessary Your datasets have no (fully) shared cell/domain clusters and you are not comparing across batches, individuals, or conditions — integration machinery is not the right fit Input is already batch-corrected/integrated features rather than per-sample raw count Seurat objects requiring CreateiSCMEBObject http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrates multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) samples by fitting the iSC.MEB hidden Markov random field empirical Bayes model, which simultaneously estimates batch effects and performs spatial clustering on shared low-dimensional representations, then exports an integrated Seurat object via IntegrateSpaData. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Integrates multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) samples by fitting the iSC.MEB hidden Markov random field empirical Bayes model, which simultaneously estimates batch effects and performs spatial clustering on shared low-dimensional representations, then exports an integrated Seurat object via IntegrateSpaData.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single SRT section only — the predecessor SC.MEB fits one sample and iSC.MEB's batch-effect estimation is unnecessary Your datasets have no (fully) shared cell/domain clusters and you are not comparing across batches, individuals, or conditions — integration machinery is not the right fit Input is already batch-corrected/integrated features rather than per-sample raw count Seurat objects requiring CreateiSCMEBObject

skills.description: Use when you need to remove technical/sample effects from multi-sample single-cell RNA-seq data while preserving cell-type variability, and to quantify how GEDI compares with other integration methods across datasets and latent-factor settings.
skills.name: multi-sample-batch-integration
skills.search_text: multi-sample-batch-integration Use when you need to remove technical/sample effects from multi-sample single-cell RNA-seq data while preserving cell-type variability, and to quantify how GEDI compares with other integration methods across datasets and latent-factor settings. Data are single-sample with no inter-sample technical variability to harmonize — GEDI's integration objective is unnecessary The modality is ratio-based (splicing/stability) or the goal is cluster-free differential expression, pathway, or TF activity analysis rather than cross-method integration benchmarking Only gene-level imputation quality is of interest — the article notes GEDI's imputations have not been benchmarked against existing imputation methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark GEDI, a generative Bayesian framework that unifies inter-sample integration, denoising, and low-dimensional embedding, against state-of-the-art single-cell integration methods (Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) across PBMC, pancreas, and Tabula Muris datasets, scoring batch removal and biological conservation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Benchmark GEDI, a generative Bayesian framework that unifies inter-sample integration, denoising, and low-dimensional embedding, against state-of-the-art single-cell integration methods (Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, BBKNN, scVI, Scanorama, CSS, PCA) across PBMC, pancreas, and Tabula Muris datasets, scoring batch removal and biological conservation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-sample with no inter-sample technical variability to harmonize — GEDI's integration objective is unnecessary The modality is ratio-based (splicing/stability) or the goal is cluster-free differential expression, pathway, or TF activity analysis rather than cross-method integration benchmarking Only gene-level imputation quality is of interest — the article notes GEDI's imputations have not been benchmarked against existing imputation methods

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data span multiple biological samples and experimental groups (e.g., vehicle vs LPS-treated mice) and the goal is cell-subpopulation-level differential state inference rather than across-cell comparisons.
skills.name: multi-sample-multi-condition-scrna-seq-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-sample-multi-condition-scrna-seq-analysis Use when scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data span multiple biological samples and experimental groups (e.g., vehicle vs LPS-treated mice) and the goal is cell-subpopulation-level differential state inference rather than across-cell comparisons. Data are single-sample or single-group per condition such that sample-level inference (replicates) is impossible; pseudobulk DS requires multiple samples per group. The question is differential detection (DD) per cell rather than differential state across conditions; use muscat's pbDD / fun='num.detected' workflow instead. Cell-level mixed-model flexibility (mmDS with e.g. dream) is required despite higher cost; the aggregation-based pbDS route assumes pseudobulk sums are the appropriate unit of inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Pseudobulk differential state (DS) analysis of multi-sample, multi-condition, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data using muscat: single-cell counts are aggregated to pseudobulk sums per sample-by-subpopulation and tested with bulk RNA-seq engines such as edgeR to identify subpopulation-specific state transitions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Pseudobulk differential state (DS) analysis of multi-sample, multi-condition, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data using muscat: single-cell counts are aggregated to pseudobulk sums per sample-by-subpopulation and tested with bulk RNA-seq engines such as edgeR to identify subpopulation-specific state transitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-sample or single-group per condition such that sample-level inference (replicates) is impossible; pseudobulk DS requires multiple samples per group. The question is differential detection (DD) per cell rather than differential state across conditions; use muscat's pbDD / fun='num.detected' workflow instead. Cell-level mixed-model flexibility (mmDS with e.g. dream) is required despite higher cost; the aggregation-based pbDS route assumes pseudobulk sums are the appropriate unit of inference.

skills.description: Use when evaluating a new SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original barcode/UMI filtering baseline across five or more samples, and you need per-sample identified-read overlap and 96-97% consistency rates as validation.
skills.name: multi-sample-preprocessing-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-sample-preprocessing-benchmarking Use when evaluating a new SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original barcode/UMI filtering baseline across five or more samples, and you need per-sample identified-read overlap and 96-97% consistency rates as validation. Input data is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial barcoding reads; the fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data in this study The goal is read mapping or genome alignment quantification rather than barcode/UMI identification benchmarking; use STAR-based mapping assessment instead Only a single sample is available and per-sample cross-method consistency across five samples cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark a preprocessing tool (e.g., SCSit) against a baseline method (original SPLiT-seq filtering) across multiple samples by intersecting identified reads and computing per-sample consistency percentages of identified reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Benchmark a preprocessing tool (e.g., SCSit) against a baseline method (original SPLiT-seq filtering) across multiple samples by intersecting identified reads and computing per-sample consistency percentages of identified reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial barcoding reads; the fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data in this study The goal is read mapping or genome alignment quantification rather than barcode/UMI identification benchmarking; use STAR-based mapping assessment instead Only a single sample is available and per-sample cross-method consistency across five samples cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when analyzing multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectories to identify genes whose expression along pseudotime differs across a covariate (e.g. sex, disease severity) while adjusting for batch effects.
skills.name: multi-sample-pseudotime-xde-testing
skills.search_text: multi-sample-pseudotime-xde-testing Use when analyzing multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectories to identify genes whose expression along pseudotime differs across a covariate (e.g. sex, disease severity) while adjusting for batch effects. Data are from a single biological sample or lack multiple replicates per condition — Lamian's cross-sample variability inference and XDE testing require multiple samples per condition The trajectory was inferred with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot and you need Lamian modules 1 and 2 (topology/branch analysis), which do not support those trajectories You only need pseudotime trajectory construction or topology testing, not differential expression along pseudotime across covariates http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run Lamian's differential pseudotime gene-expression (XDE) testing across multiple scRNA-seq samples while adjusting for batch effects, using permutation-based likelihood ratio tests and sample-level variability modeling to detect covariate-associated changes in expression along pseudotime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Run Lamian's differential pseudotime gene-expression (XDE) testing across multiple scRNA-seq samples while adjusting for batch effects, using permutation-based likelihood ratio tests and sample-level variability modeling to detect covariate-associated changes in expression along pseudotime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from a single biological sample or lack multiple replicates per condition — Lamian's cross-sample variability inference and XDE testing require multiple samples per condition The trajectory was inferred with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot and you need Lamian modules 1 and 2 (topology/branch analysis), which do not support those trajectories You only need pseudotime trajectory construction or topology testing, not differential expression along pseudotime across covariates

skills.description: Use when preparing multi-sample scRNA-seq expression, pseudotime, and sample-covariate data for differential pseudotime (XDE/TDE) testing, or when a Monocle2 trajectory must be retrofitted for covariate-associated differential expression tests.
skills.name: multi-sample-scrna-seq-data-preparation
skills.search_text: multi-sample-scrna-seq-data-preparation Use when preparing multi-sample scRNA-seq expression, pseudotime, and sample-covariate data for differential pseudotime (XDE/TDE) testing, or when a Monocle2 trajectory must be retrofitted for covariate-associated differential expression tests. Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories, so this skill cannot seamlessly plug those reconstructed trajectories into topology or trajectory-inference modules Single-sample scRNA-seq data without sample-level covariates or replicates — Lamian's cross-sample variability accounting and the group covariate require multiple samples per condition Systematic comparison of sample harmonization/embedding methods, which the article explicitly states is beyond the study's scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A preparation and benchmarking workflow for multi-sample scRNA-seq differential pseudotime analysis, including the Monocle2 adaptation monocle2TrajTestCorr that tests group-specific intercept and trend differences along pseudotime for XDE detection as a baseline against Lamian. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: A preparation and benchmarking workflow for multi-sample scRNA-seq differential pseudotime analysis, including the Monocle2 adaptation monocle2TrajTestCorr that tests group-specific intercept and trend differences along pseudotime for XDE detection as a baseline against Lamian.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories, so this skill cannot seamlessly plug those reconstructed trajectories into topology or trajectory-inference modules Single-sample scRNA-seq data without sample-level covariates or replicates — Lamian's cross-sample variability accounting and the group covariate require multiple samples per condition Systematic comparison of sample harmonization/embedding methods, which the article explicitly states is beyond the study's scope

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples with covariates (e.g. sex, disease status) and a reconstructed pseudotime trajectory, and you need to test which genes or density patterns change along pseudotime in association with those covariates.
skills.name: multi-sample-scrna-seq-differential-pseudotime-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-sample-scrna-seq-differential-pseudotime-analysis Use when you have scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples with covariates (e.g. sex, disease status) and a reconstructed pseudotime trajectory, and you need to test which genes or density patterns change along pseudotime in association with those covariates. You have only one biological sample per condition and cannot estimate sample-level variance — Lamian's FDR control relies on cross-sample variability (as with condiments' limitation). You need topology/differential-trajectory modules compatible with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these. Your goal is a systematic comparison of sample-harmonization methods, which is explicitly beyond the paper's scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A statistically-rigorous framework (Lamian) for detecting differences in gene expression (TDE/XDE), cell density (TCD/XCD), and trajectory topology along pseudotime across multiple scRNA-seq samples, accounting for cross-sample variability to control FDR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: A statistically-rigorous framework (Lamian) for detecting differences in gene expression (TDE/XDE), cell density (TCD/XCD), and trajectory topology along pseudotime across multiple scRNA-seq samples, accounting for cross-sample variability to control FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one biological sample per condition and cannot estimate sample-level variance — Lamian's FDR control relies on cross-sample variability (as with condiments' limitation). You need topology/differential-trajectory modules compatible with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these. Your goal is a systematic comparison of sample-harmonization methods, which is explicitly beyond the paper's scope.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential state analysis methods on scRNA-seq data, or when ground-truth multi-sample multi-subpopulation counts with known DS genes/logFCs are needed.
skills.name: multi-sample-scrnaseq-data-simulation
skills.search_text: multi-sample-scrnaseq-data-simulation Use when benchmarking differential state analysis methods on scRNA-seq data, or when ground-truth multi-sample multi-subpopulation counts with known DS genes/logFCs are needed. The goal is analyzing a real experimental dataset for DS hits — no ground-truth simulation is needed; use muscat's pbDS/mmDS analysis workflow instead The reference data lack the required colData columns (sample_id, group_id, cluster_id) that simData needs to estimate subpopulation- and sample-specific parameters You need simulations with an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the article notes the simulation framework does not yet accommodate these http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulate multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq count data anchored to a real reference dataset using muscat's simData framework, with injected differential state (DE, DP, DM, DB) genes of known truth for benchmarking DS methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Simulate multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq count data anchored to a real reference dataset using muscat's simData framework, with injected differential state (DE, DP, DM, DB) genes of known truth for benchmarking DS methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analyzing a real experimental dataset for DS hits — no ground-truth simulation is needed; use muscat's pbDS/mmDS analysis workflow instead The reference data lack the required colData columns (sample_id, group_id, cluster_id) that simData needs to estimate subpopulation- and sample-specific parameters You need simulations with an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the article notes the simulation framework does not yet accommodate these

skills.description: Use when two or more SRT sections (e.g. Visium DLPFC sections or seqFISH mouse embryo sections) across batches, individuals, or conditions must be jointly clustered while correcting batch effects.
skills.name: multi-sample-srt-data-integration
skills.search_text: multi-sample-srt-data-integration Use when two or more SRT sections (e.g. Visium DLPFC sections or seqFISH mouse embryo sections) across batches, individuals, or conditions must be jointly clustered while correcting batch effects. Only a single SRT section is available — the predecessor SC.MEB covers single-sample empirical-Bayes spatial clustering Input is already-integrated expression matrices without spatial coordinates, since adjacency matrices from spot positions are required Datasets have no shared cell/domain clusters at all, outside the 'partially shared clusters' context the package targets http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Integrate multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) datasets with iSC.MEB, which simultaneously estimates batch effects and performs spatial clustering via a hidden Markov random field fitted with empirical Bayes on low-dimensional representations of each sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Integrate multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) datasets with iSC.MEB, which simultaneously estimates batch effects and performs spatial clustering via a hidden Markov random field fitted with empirical Bayes on low-dimensional representations of each sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single SRT section is available — the predecessor SC.MEB covers single-sample empirical-Bayes spatial clustering Input is already-integrated expression matrices without spatial coordinates, since adjacency matrices from spot positions are required Datasets have no shared cell/domain clusters at all, outside the 'partially shared clusters' context the package targets

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need pseudotemporal trajectory comparison across covariates (e.g. mild vs moderate COVID-19), and naive single-sample pseudotime methods would ignore sample-to-sample variation.
skills.name: multi-sample-trajectory-statistical-modeling
skills.search_text: multi-sample-trajectory-statistical-modeling Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need pseudotemporal trajectory comparison across covariates (e.g. mild vs moderate COVID-19), and naive single-sample pseudotime methods would ignore sample-to-sample variation. Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — the pipeline assumes TSCAN pseudotime; tailoring to those methods is deferred to future work. Single-sample pseudotime analyses where cross-sample variability cannot be modeled — Lamian's key advantage (sample-level inference) does not apply. Data types outside gene expression, e.g. single-cell ATAC-seq — the statistical model extension is explicitly future research. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Apply the Lamian statistical framework for differential multi-sample pseudotime analysis of scRNA-seq data: after sample harmonization with Seurat and pseudotime construction with TSCAN's cluster-based minimum spanning tree, test for topology, cell abundance (TCD/XCD), and gene expression (TDE/XDE) changes across sample covariates such as disease severity while accounting for cross-sample variability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Apply the Lamian statistical framework for differential multi-sample pseudotime analysis of scRNA-seq data: after sample harmonization with Seurat and pseudotime construction with TSCAN's cluster-based minimum spanning tree, test for topology, cell abundance (TCD/XCD), and gene expression (TDE/XDE) changes across sample covariates such as disease severity while accounting for cross-sample variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot trajectories — the pipeline assumes TSCAN pseudotime; tailoring to those methods is deferred to future work. Single-sample pseudotime analyses where cross-sample variability cannot be modeled — Lamian's key advantage (sample-level inference) does not apply. Data types outside gene expression, e.g. single-cell ATAC-seq — the statistical model extension is explicitly future research.

skills.description: Use when analyzing Seq-Scope/Slide-seq DGEs with spatial coordinates where simple square-grid aggregation is too coarse to resolve cell-type boundaries and finer, overlapping-bin clustering is desired.
skills.name: multi-scale-sliding-window-binning
skills.search_text: multi-scale-sliding-window-binning Use when analyzing Seq-Scope/Slide-seq DGEs with spatial coordinates where simple square-grid aggregation is too coarse to resolve cell-type boundaries and finer, overlapping-bin clustering is desired. The dataset is already high enough resolution that simple square aggregation suffices, e.g. VISIUM spot data (~120 barcodes/mm²) where overlapping bins add no resolution benefit The goal is subcellular analysis: spatial segments must remain larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so MSSW cannot be pushed to subcellular scale The platform resolution is too low for overlapping-bin benefits to be visible, as shown for Slide-seq where the MSSW benefit at 100 μm² was not visually pronounced versus 2500 μm² simple aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Implements STtools' multiscale sliding window (MSSW) aggregation, which collapses an ultra-high-resolution spatial DGE into overlapping square bins (e.g. ~100 μm² at ~4 μm² steps for Seq-Scope) instead of non-overlapping simple square grids, enabling several-folds-higher-resolution cell-type cluster maps after label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Implements STtools' multiscale sliding window (MSSW) aggregation, which collapses an ultra-high-resolution spatial DGE into overlapping square bins (e.g. ~100 μm² at ~4 μm² steps for Seq-Scope) instead of non-overlapping simple square grids, enabling several-folds-higher-resolution cell-type cluster maps after label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already high enough resolution that simple square aggregation suffices, e.g. VISIUM spot data (~120 barcodes/mm²) where overlapping bins add no resolution benefit The goal is subcellular analysis: spatial segments must remain larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so MSSW cannot be pushed to subcellular scale The platform resolution is too low for overlapping-bin benefits to be visible, as shown for Slide-seq where the MSSW benefit at 100 μm² was not visually pronounced versus 2500 μm² simple aggregation

skills.description: Use when raw nucleotide sequence segments (e.g., 41-bp windows centered on candidate m5C sites in FASTA format) must be converted into informative numeric features to train or apply site-prediction classifiers.
skills.name: multi-scheme-sequence-feature-encoding
skills.search_text: multi-scheme-sequence-feature-encoding Use when raw nucleotide sequence segments (e.g., 41-bp windows centered on candidate m5C sites in FASTA format) must be converted into informative numeric features to train or apply site-prediction classifiers. Input is already a numeric feature table or embedding — encoding raw sequences again is unnecessary The task requires cross-species generalization with a single model: the article notes it 'could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction, and it is necessary to set up species-specific models' Sequence segments shorter than the 41-bp window used by Staem5, since PSP and PCPseDNC assume the fixed local window structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Encode 41-bp RNA sequence segments by fusing four feature schemes — position-specific propensity (PSP), k-mer (k=1,2,3), PCPseDNC, and PseEIIP — into a single numeric feature vector, then reduce dimension with F-score-based selection (step of 5) for machine learning classifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Encode 41-bp RNA sequence segments by fusing four feature schemes — position-specific propensity (PSP), k-mer (k=1,2,3), PCPseDNC, and PseEIIP — into a single numeric feature vector, then reduce dimension with F-score-based selection (step of 5) for machine learning classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table or embedding — encoding raw sequences again is unnecessary The task requires cross-species generalization with a single model: the article notes it 'could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction, and it is necessary to set up species-specific models' Sequence segments shorter than the 41-bp window used by Staem5, since PSP and PCPseDNC assume the fixed local window structure

skills.description: Use when a new scRNA-seq clustering method must be validated against baselines across multiple real datasets, and clustering quality must be measured as NMI/ARI averaged over repeated random-seed runs.
skills.name: multi-seed-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-seed-clustering-benchmarking Use when a new scRNA-seq clustering method must be validated against baselines across multiple real datasets, and clustering quality must be measured as NMI/ARI averaged over repeated random-seed runs. The goal is to tune a single clustering run on one dataset rather than to compare methods fairly across datasets — seeding and benchmarking overhead is unnecessary there The data are not scRNA-seq count matrices from single-cell transcriptome profiles (the method assumes zero-inflated scRNA-seq data with highly variable gene selection) Only one clustering metric is required per single run — this skill is specifically about multi-seed, multi-method, multi-dataset NMI/ARI benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a single-cell clustering method against state-of-the-art competitors by running every method on the same scRNA-seq datasets under 10 fixed random seeds (1111–10000) and comparing averaged NMI and ARI, as done for scBGEDA versus SHARP, CIDR, SOUP, Seurat, SC3, Scanpy, PCA, DCA, scDeepCluster, scziDesk and DESC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Benchmark a single-cell clustering method against state-of-the-art competitors by running every method on the same scRNA-seq datasets under 10 fixed random seeds (1111–10000) and comparing averaged NMI and ARI, as done for scBGEDA versus SHARP, CIDR, SOUP, Seurat, SC3, Scanpy, PCA, DCA, scDeepCluster, scziDesk and DESC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to tune a single clustering run on one dataset rather than to compare methods fairly across datasets — seeding and benchmarking overhead is unnecessary there The data are not scRNA-seq count matrices from single-cell transcriptome profiles (the method assumes zero-inflated scRNA-seq data with highly variable gene selection) Only one clustering metric is required per single run — this skill is specifically about multi-seed, multi-method, multi-dataset NMI/ARI benchmarking

skills.description: Use when benchmarking stochastic batch-correction/integration methods whose embeddings or scores vary run-to-run, and you need seed-averaged metrics (e.g. over-correction scores) comparable to a reference figure such as Fig. 3c.
skills.name: multi-seed-stochastic-evaluation-averaging
skills.search_text: multi-seed-stochastic-evaluation-averaging Use when benchmarking stochastic batch-correction/integration methods whose embeddings or scores vary run-to-run, and you need seed-averaged metrics (e.g. over-correction scores) comparable to a reference figure such as Fig. 3c. When the method being benchmarked is deterministic (e.g. fully reproducible runs give identical embeddings), seed averaging adds no information. When the evaluation metric is computed on a fixed pre-computed embedding rather than on stochastic integration runs you execute yourself. When comparing methods you have tuned per-method rather than run with default parameters — seed averaging will not fix a comparability bias from unequal tuning. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Protocol for benchmarking stochastic single-cell integration methods (scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) by repeating each run over 5 random seeds, computing over-correction scores per seed from 2D UMAP embeddings, then normalizing and averaging across seeds to obtain stable scores comparable to published values (e.g. scCobra 0.043 vs scVI 0.086 on the perturbed GSE149614 immune dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Protocol for benchmarking stochastic single-cell integration methods (scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) by repeating each run over 5 random seeds, computing over-correction scores per seed from 2D UMAP embeddings, then normalizing and averaging across seeds to obtain stable scores comparable to published values (e.g. scCobra 0.043 vs scVI 0.086 on the perturbed GSE149614 immune dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the method being benchmarked is deterministic (e.g. fully reproducible runs give identical embeddings), seed averaging adds no information. When the evaluation metric is computed on a fixed pre-computed embedding rather than on stochastic integration runs you execute yourself. When comparing methods you have tuned per-method rather than run with default parameters — seed averaging will not fix a comparability bias from unequal tuning.

skills.description: Use when multiple adjacent or replicated ST slices (e.g., simulated Visium Datasets 5-6) with paired scRNA-seq references are available and you need to decide whether analyzing slices jointly improves cell type labeling accuracy versus slice-by-slice analysis.
skills.name: multi-slice-spatial-alignment-evaluation
skills.search_text: multi-slice-spatial-alignment-evaluation Use when multiple adjacent or replicated ST slices (e.g., simulated Visium Datasets 5-6) with paired scRNA-seq references are available and you need to decide whether analyzing slices jointly improves cell type labeling accuracy versus slice-by-slice analysis. Only a single ST slice is available, so the joint-vs-individual comparison is undefined No ground-truth single-cell labels exist, making single-cell-level error-rate scoring impossible (use deconvolution proportion metrics instead) The goal is gene expression imputation or decomposition rather than discrete cell type label assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks single-cell cell type identification on multiple spatial transcriptomics slices by running methods (SpatialScope, Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD) per-slice and jointly on all slices, then scoring single-cell-level error rates against ground-truth labels to test whether joint multi-slice inference improves accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-cell cell type identification on multiple spatial transcriptomics slices by running methods (SpatialScope, Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD) per-slice and jointly on all slices, then scoring single-cell-level error rates against ground-truth labels to test whether joint multi-slice inference improves accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single ST slice is available, so the joint-vs-individual comparison is undefined No ground-truth single-cell labels exist, making single-cell-level error-rate scoring impossible (use deconvolution proportion metrics instead) The goal is gene expression imputation or decomposition rather than discrete cell type label assignment

skills.description: Use when analyzing multiple ST slices (e.g., 11 breast cancer 10X Visium slices or 33 MERFISH MOp slices) and you need a single set of spatial domain labels (D1–D9) shared across slices rather than per-slice clusters.
skills.name: multi-slice-spatial-domain-identification
skills.search_text: multi-slice-spatial-domain-identification Use when analyzing multiple ST slices (e.g., 11 breast cancer 10X Visium slices or 33 MERFISH MOp slices) and you need a single set of spatial domain labels (D1–D9) shared across slices rather than per-slice clusters. Single-slice spatial clustering where no cross-slice uniform domain labels are needed — Splane's adversarial training is designed for multi-slice joint analysis Raw seq-based ST data without deconvolution — Splane needs cell type composition input, so Spoint (or equivalent) must be run first on 10X Visium-like data Constructing 3D tissue alignment itself — that is Scube's role (Scube.alignment.align), which consumes Splane's domains rather than producing them http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify uniform spatial domains that are transcriptomically and spatially coherent across multiple spatial transcriptomics slices using Splane's graph convolutional network with adversarial learning, taking per-spot cell type composition (e.g., from Spoint deconvolution) and spatial coordinates as input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Identify uniform spatial domains that are transcriptomically and spatially coherent across multiple spatial transcriptomics slices using Splane's graph convolutional network with adversarial learning, taking per-spot cell type composition (e.g., from Spoint deconvolution) and spatial coordinates as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-slice spatial clustering where no cross-slice uniform domain labels are needed — Splane's adversarial training is designed for multi-slice joint analysis Raw seq-based ST data without deconvolution — Splane needs cell type composition input, so Spoint (or equivalent) must be run first on 10X Visium-like data Constructing 3D tissue alignment itself — that is Scube's role (Scube.alignment.align), which consumes Splane's domains rather than producing them

skills.description: Use when you have multiple ST slices of the same tissue (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) and need unified spatial domain labels across slices rather than independent per-slice clustering.
skills.name: multi-slice-spatial-transcriptomics-integration
skills.search_text: multi-slice-spatial-transcriptomics-integration Use when you have multiple ST slices of the same tissue (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) and need unified spatial domain labels across slices rather than independent per-slice clustering. You only have a single ST slice and no cross-slice batch effects to mitigate — joint training adds no benefit over per-slice analysis You are working with image-based ST data with single-cell resolution where Spoint deconvolution is unnecessary; check whether the module workflow still applies You need nonlinear slice alignment rather than domain identification — the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment (unlike STAligner and PASTE) http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Jointly analyze multiple spatial transcriptomics (ST) slices with Splane, a graph convolutional network with adversarial learning, to identify spatial domains that are coherent across slices while minimizing batch effects. Joint modeling outperforms per-slice analysis on 12 human DLPFC Visium slices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Jointly analyze multiple spatial transcriptomics (ST) slices with Splane, a graph convolutional network with adversarial learning, to identify spatial domains that are coherent across slices while minimizing batch effects. Joint modeling outperforms per-slice analysis on 12 human DLPFC Visium slices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single ST slice and no cross-slice batch effects to mitigate — joint training adds no benefit over per-slice analysis You are working with image-based ST data with single-cell resolution where Spoint deconvolution is unnecessary; check whether the module workflow still applies You need nonlinear slice alignment rather than domain identification — the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment (unlike STAligner and PASTE)

skills.description: Use when integrating marker gene sets from multiple published databases (e.g. CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need to quantify and reconcile source agreement/conflict to weight markers for cell type annotation.
skills.name: multi-source-evidence-consistency-scoring
skills.search_text: multi-source-evidence-consistency-scoring Use when integrating marker gene sets from multiple published databases (e.g. CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need to quantify and reconcile source agreement/conflict to weight markers for cell type annotation. You have a single authoritative marker source with no cross-source agreement to measure — SPs/ECs weighting adds no consistency information Input is expression data without a marker gene database — use annotation directly (accordion()) rather than rebuilding weights Non-marker-based annotation is required (e.g. reference-mapping tools); the article notes no direct comparison was conducted with annotation tools that do not rely on marker genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Weights marker genes from multiple heterogeneous annotation sources by combining a specificity score (SPs = 1/number of cell types a gene marks) with an evidence consistency score (ECs = number of sources defining the gene as a marker), regularized via log10 transforms, to ensure consistency-weighted cell type annotation in the Cell Marker Accordion database. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Weights marker genes from multiple heterogeneous annotation sources by combining a specificity score (SPs = 1/number of cell types a gene marks) with an evidence consistency score (ECs = number of sources defining the gene as a marker), regularized via log10 transforms, to ensure consistency-weighted cell type annotation in the Cell Marker Accordion database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single authoritative marker source with no cross-source agreement to measure — SPs/ECs weighting adds no consistency information Input is expression data without a marker gene database — use annotation directly (accordion()) rather than rebuilding weights Non-marker-based annotation is required (e.g. reference-mapping tools); the article notes no direct comparison was conducted with annotation tools that do not rely on marker genes

skills.description: Use when a curated list must be assembled by unioning multiple published source databases and removing duplicate entries across sources, e.g. building a default L-R interaction database for cell-cell communication inference.
skills.name: multi-source-list-merging-deduplication
skills.search_text: multi-source-list-merging-deduplication Use when a curated list must be assembled by unioning multiple published source databases and removing duplicate entries across sources, e.g. building a default L-R interaction database for cell-cell communication inference. The user already supplies a curated L-R list — dsCellNet explicitly allows users to support their own L-R genes as supplementary when the default list's size is limiting The task requires distinguishing membrane-ligand vs secreted-ligand mediated interactions at the pair level, which the published sources merged here do not resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Merge several published ligand-receptor pair databases (Ramilowski et al. 2015, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR) into a single non-redundant, multi-species supported membrane-or-secreted L-R database, as done to build dsCellNet's default L-R pair list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Merge several published ligand-receptor pair databases (Ramilowski et al. 2015, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR) into a single non-redundant, multi-species supported membrane-or-secreted L-R database, as done to build dsCellNet's default L-R pair list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user already supplies a curated L-R list — dsCellNet explicitly allows users to support their own L-R genes as supplementary when the default list's size is limiting The task requires distinguishing membrane-ligand vs secreted-ligand mediated interactions at the pair level, which the published sources merged here do not resolve

skills.description: Use when building a ligand-receptor reference by integrating multiple external LR resources (CellPhoneDB, FANTOM5) into one standardized, deduplicated, species-mapped table for cell-cell communication inference.
skills.name: multi-source-reference-integration
skills.search_text: multi-source-reference-integration Use when building a ligand-receptor reference by integrating multiple external LR resources (CellPhoneDB, FANTOM5) into one standardized, deduplicated, species-mapped table for cell-cell communication inference. You need signaling pathway gene sets (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, GO) for pathway scoring rather than the LR pair reference — those are separate CommPath databases You already have a valid LR reference and want to infer statistically significant LR associations from scRNA-seq expression data — that is CommPath's findLRpairs step, not reference curation Your species is outside the six CommPath-supported species (hsapiens, mmusculus, rnorvegicus, drerio, dmelanogaster, celegans), since ortholog mapping is only defined for these http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs CommPath's curated ligand-receptor reference database by merging and standardizing LR interactions from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 into a single deduplicated, provenance-tagged table for six supported species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: Constructs CommPath's curated ligand-receptor reference database by merging and standardizing LR interactions from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 into a single deduplicated, provenance-tagged table for six supported species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need signaling pathway gene sets (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, GO) for pathway scoring rather than the LR pair reference — those are separate CommPath databases You already have a valid LR reference and want to infer statistically significant LR associations from scRNA-seq expression data — that is CommPath's findLRpairs step, not reference curation Your species is outside the six CommPath-supported species (hsapiens, mmusculus, rnorvegicus, drerio, dmelanogaster, celegans), since ortholog mapping is only defined for these

skills.description: Use when a multi-donor or cross-species scRNA-seq query (e.g. inDrop human+mouse islets) must be mapped onto an existing human pancreatic islet reference and its cell types annotated via reference-label transfer.
skills.name: multi-species-pancreatic-islet-annotation-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-species-pancreatic-islet-annotation-analysis Use when a multi-donor or cross-species scRNA-seq query (e.g. inDrop human+mouse islets) must be mapped onto an existing human pancreatic islet reference and its cell types annotated via reference-label transfer. The goal is discovering novel query cell types absent from the reference — Symphony requires comprehensive cell type coverage in the reference and does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone The query contains a novel population very similar to an existing reference population, where mapping metrics may be less informative Reference and query are scATAC-seq peak matrices analyzed with different peak sets, where optimal feature selection for mapping is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the Symphony-based mapping of a multi-donor, multi-species (human+mouse) inDrop pancreatic islet query onto a human islet reference, benchmarking integration (donor LISI) and cell-type transfer accuracy (F1) against Seurat and scArches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Reproduces the Symphony-based mapping of a multi-donor, multi-species (human+mouse) inDrop pancreatic islet query onto a human islet reference, benchmarking integration (donor LISI) and cell-type transfer accuracy (F1) against Seurat and scArches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovering novel query cell types absent from the reference — Symphony requires comprehensive cell type coverage in the reference and does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone The query contains a novel population very similar to an existing reference population, where mapping metrics may be less informative Reference and query are scATAC-seq peak matrices analyzed with different peak sets, where optimal feature selection for mapping is undefined

skills.search_text: multi-species-transcript-feature-engineering Use when raw transcript sequences (FASTA, >=200 nt, CD-HIT filtered at 80%) from one or more species must be converted into a numeric feature matrix for coding-potential classification, especially when sORF-containing lncRNAs must be distinguished from PCTs. skills.summary: Encoding transcript FASTA sequences from multiple species (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken) into five fused feature types — codon-related, GC-related, sequence-related, peptide-related, and ORF-attention features — to build CatBoost-based lncRNA/PCT classifiers like LncCat.
