skills.name: multi-strategy-performance-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-strategy-performance-comparison Use when several integration algorithms (SAMap, fastMNN, Harmony, LIGER, LIGER UINMF, Scanorama, SeuratV4, scVI, scANVI) must be compared on identical cross-species scRNA-seq inputs with a common scoring scheme. When the goal is a single best integration of one species pair rather than a benchmark — a comparator tuned to the setting (e.g. scANVI, scVI or SeuratV4 for balanced mixing/conservation) may suffice When ground-truth cell type annotations or confident known cell type homology are unavailable — the paper states quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and known homology When non-one-to-one cell type mappings across species must be assessed — the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark multiple cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integration strategies head-to-head under the BENGAL pipeline, scoring each with the same metrics (e.g. alignment score as the average percentage of cross-species kNN neighbours, plus biology-conservation metrics such as trajectory conservation) on a shared task like the Embryo_xt_dr xenopus–zebrafish whole-body atlas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Benchmark multiple cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integration strategies head-to-head under the BENGAL pipeline, scoring each with the same metrics (e.g. alignment score as the average percentage of cross-species kNN neighbours, plus biology-conservation metrics such as trajectory conservation) on a shared task like the Embryo_xt_dr xenopus–zebrafish whole-body atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single best integration of one species pair rather than a benchmark — a comparator tuned to the setting (e.g. scANVI, scVI or SeuratV4 for balanced mixing/conservation) may suffice When ground-truth cell type annotations or confident known cell type homology are unavailable — the paper states quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and known homology When non-one-to-one cell type mappings across species must be assessed — the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings

skills.description: Use when benchmarking multi-subject dynamic community detection (e.g., MuDCoD vs PisCES/static spectral clustering/Betzel-2019) or when ground-truth subject x time x node labels are needed for ARI evaluation on simulated S x T x n x n adjacency tensors.
skills.name: multi-subject-dynamic-network-simulation
skills.search_text: multi-subject-dynamic-network-simulation Use when benchmarking multi-subject dynamic community detection (e.g., MuDCoD vs PisCES/static spectral clustering/Betzel-2019) or when ground-truth subject x time x node labels are needed for ARI evaluation on simulated S x T x n x n adjacency tensors. Your data are real single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices rather than simulated networks — use Dozer to filter genes and construct personalized co-expression networks instead You need community detection on a single network with no subject or time dimension — the multi-subject dynamic simulator's S x T layout does not apply You lack ground-truth label requirements and only need clustering of observed networks without benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate multi-subject dynamic gene co-expression networks with ground-truth communities using the MuSDynamicDCBM model, in SSoT and SSoS variants, to benchmark MuDCoD against baseline community-detection methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Simulate multi-subject dynamic gene co-expression networks with ground-truth communities using the MuSDynamicDCBM model, in SSoT and SSoS variants, to benchmark MuDCoD against baseline community-detection methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are real single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices rather than simulated networks — use Dozer to filter genes and construct personalized co-expression networks instead You need community detection on a single network with no subject or time dimension — the multi-subject dynamic simulator's S x T layout does not apply You lack ground-truth label requirements and only need clustering of observed networks without benchmarking

skills.description: Use when preparing adjacency matrices from multiple subjects sampled across multiple time points for MuDCoD fit_predict — input must be a numpy tensor with subject as the first dimension and time point as the second.
skills.name: multi-subject-network-tensor-formatting
skills.search_text: multi-subject-network-tensor-formatting Use when preparing adjacency matrices from multiple subjects sampled across multiple time points for MuDCoD fit_predict — input must be a numpy tensor with subject as the first dimension and time point as the second. Input is a single network or single-subject time series — MuDCoD's tensor format assumes networks from multiple subjects and multiple time points simultaneously, which no pre-existing community detection setting included Raw scRNA-seq count data that has not yet been filtered and turned into gene co-expression networks by Dozer — tensor assembly presumes per-subject adjacency matrices already exist Data stored in non-numpy structures (e.g., a list of R matrices) — must be converted to numpy arrays before MuDCoD, which takes multi-dimensional numpy arrays as the input network argument http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Formats multi-subject dynamic networks (e.g., simulated via MuSDynamicDCBM or built from scRNA-seq gene co-expression networks) into the multi-dimensional numpy adjacency tensor (S x T x n) that MuDCoD requires as input for community detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Formats multi-subject dynamic networks (e.g., simulated via MuSDynamicDCBM or built from scRNA-seq gene co-expression networks) into the multi-dimensional numpy adjacency tensor (S x T x n) that MuDCoD requires as input for community detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single network or single-subject time series — MuDCoD's tensor format assumes networks from multiple subjects and multiple time points simultaneously, which no pre-existing community detection setting included Raw scRNA-seq count data that has not yet been filtered and turned into gene co-expression networks by Dozer — tensor assembly presumes per-subject adjacency matrices already exist Data stored in non-numpy structures (e.g., a list of R matrices) — must be converted to numpy arrays before MuDCoD, which takes multi-dimensional numpy arrays as the input network argument

skills.description: Use when benchmarking ligand-receptor inference tools on scRNA-seq data and you need to measure how often a tool predicts single-gene interactions for receptors that are known heteromeric complexes, or when choosing a database that accounts for multimeric receptor structure.
skills.name: multi-subunit-complex-false-positive-assessment
skills.search_text: multi-subunit-complex-false-positive-assessment Use when benchmarking ligand-receptor inference tools on scRNA-seq data and you need to measure how often a tool predicts single-gene interactions for receptors that are known heteromeric complexes, or when choosing a database that accounts for multimeric receptor structure. The tool under test already supports multi-subunit receptor complexes (e.g., CellChat with CellChatDB), so the single-ligand/single-receptor restriction itself would not yield a meaningful false-positive measurement The scRNA-seq data are not yet cell-clustered — clustering is a pre-requisite for communication analysis with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR The task is validating biological ground truth of communications rather than comparing tool behavior; the article notes systematic evaluation is challenging due to the lack of ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies the false-positive rate incurred by cell-cell communication tools that model only one-ligand/one-receptor gene pairs, by flagging predicted interactions whose receptors are actually multi-subunit complexes. CellChat reports 10.6% (SingleCellSignalR) and 14.3% (iTALK) of such mispredictions on mouse skin scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Quantifies the false-positive rate incurred by cell-cell communication tools that model only one-ligand/one-receptor gene pairs, by flagging predicted interactions whose receptors are actually multi-subunit complexes. CellChat reports 10.6% (SingleCellSignalR) and 14.3% (iTALK) of such mispredictions on mouse skin scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tool under test already supports multi-subunit receptor complexes (e.g., CellChat with CellChatDB), so the single-ligand/single-receptor restriction itself would not yield a meaningful false-positive measurement The scRNA-seq data are not yet cell-clustered — clustering is a pre-requisite for communication analysis with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR The task is validating biological ground truth of communications rather than comparing tool behavior; the article notes systematic evaluation is challenging due to the lack of ground truth

skills.description: Use when transferring bulk-level GDSC/CCLE drug response labels to scRNA-seq data with scDEAL, i.e. when training Eb, Es, and P simultaneously so single-cell and bulk embeddings are harmonized (MMD) while prediction accuracy is supervised.
skills.name: multi-task-loss-optimization
skills.search_text: multi-task-loss-optimization Use when transferring bulk-level GDSC/CCLE drug response labels to scRNA-seq data with scDEAL, i.e. when training Eb, Es, and P simultaneously so single-cell and bulk embeddings are harmonized (MMD) while prediction accuracy is supervised. Only bulk RNA-seq drug response data is available with no scRNA-seq target dataset — the MMD/harmonization term has no single-cell domain to align to; use bulkmodel.py training alone A converged single-cell checkpoint already exists and the task is only per-cell prediction/application — skip joint re-optimization and run scmodel.py with --checkpoint The drug response labels are continuous IC50 values rather than the binary sensitivity/resistance labels the cross-entropy loss requires http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Jointly optimizes scDEAL's bulk encoder (Eb), single-cell encoder (Es), and drug-response predictor (P) in PyTorch by combining a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD/DaNN) transfer loss between bulk and single-cell embeddings with cross-entropy loss on predicted bulk drug responses, plus per-epoch cell-type label regularization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Jointly optimizes scDEAL's bulk encoder (Eb), single-cell encoder (Es), and drug-response predictor (P) in PyTorch by combining a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD/DaNN) transfer loss between bulk and single-cell embeddings with cross-entropy loss on predicted bulk drug responses, plus per-epoch cell-type label regularization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only bulk RNA-seq drug response data is available with no scRNA-seq target dataset — the MMD/harmonization term has no single-cell domain to align to; use bulkmodel.py training alone A converged single-cell checkpoint already exists and the task is only per-cell prediction/application — skip joint re-optimization and run scmodel.py with --checkpoint The drug response labels are continuous IC50 values rather than the binary sensitivity/resistance labels the cross-entropy loss requires

skills.description: Use when direct TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize, but an inferred fibroblast GRN edge list with target genes is available and TF regulome spatial patterns must be compared across tissue regions.
skills.name: multi-tf-regulome-gradient-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-tf-regulome-gradient-comparison Use when direct TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize, but an inferred fibroblast GRN edge list with target genes is available and TF regulome spatial patterns must be compared across tissue regions. Direct TF expression in the spatial spots is sufficiently abundant to plot and interpret without target-gene aggregation. No GRN edge list linking TFs to target genes is available — the regulome scores depend entirely on the inferred target-gene sets. The tissue of interest lacks defined spatial regions or fibrotic markers (COL1A1/POSTN/FN1) to anchor the gradient comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Spatially maps and compares transcription factor regulomes by aggregating mean expression of each TF's GRN target genes per spatial transcriptomics spot, enabling delineation of TF activity gradients (e.g. NR3C2 vs RUNX1 in fibrotic myocardial infarction regions) when direct TF expression is too sparse to detect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Spatially maps and compares transcription factor regulomes by aggregating mean expression of each TF's GRN target genes per spatial transcriptomics spot, enabling delineation of TF activity gradients (e.g. NR3C2 vs RUNX1 in fibrotic myocardial infarction regions) when direct TF expression is too sparse to detect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Direct TF expression in the spatial spots is sufficiently abundant to plot and interpret without target-gene aggregation. No GRN edge list linking TFs to target genes is available — the regulome scores depend entirely on the inferred target-gene sets. The tissue of interest lacks defined spatial regions or fibrotic markers (COL1A1/POSTN/FN1) to anchor the gradient comparison.

skills.description: Use when you have absolute log10(x+1) expression values for gene deletion events across m conditions (e.g., 6 Drosophila tissues) and must build the EmpiricalData.data-style input required by CLOUDe's GenerateTrainingData, CLOUDeClassifyNN, and CLOUDePredictNN functions.
skills.name: multi-tissue-expression-data-parsing
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-expression-data-parsing Use when you have absolute log10(x+1) expression values for gene deletion events across m conditions (e.g., 6 Drosophila tissues) and must build the EmpiricalData.data-style input required by CLOUDe's GenerateTrainingData, CLOUDeClassifyNN, and CLOUDePredictNN functions. Expression data are raw counts or non-log-transformed values — the format requires absolute log10(x+1) expression values, so transformation must precede this skill Data are single-species gene expression profiles without paired derived/survived/lost genes — the 3m column layout presumes two-species deletion events http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Formats and validates multi-tissue expression data into CLOUDe's space-delimited input structure (N+1 rows by 3m columns with derived/survived/lost gene blocks) so deletion events can be classified and their evolutionary parameters predicted with the CLOUDe R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Formats and validates multi-tissue expression data into CLOUDe's space-delimited input structure (N+1 rows by 3m columns with derived/survived/lost gene blocks) so deletion events can be classified and their evolutionary parameters predicted with the CLOUDe R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are raw counts or non-log-transformed values — the format requires absolute log10(x+1) expression values, so transformation must precede this skill Data are single-species gene expression profiles without paired derived/survived/lost genes — the 3m column layout presumes two-species deletion events

skills.description: Use when multiple ribo− RNA-seq samples have been quantified with CLEAR (FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore) and the goal is cross-tissue comparison, per-tissue summary statistics, or reproducing tissue-enrichment patterns like Figure 5A.
skills.name: multi-tissue-expression-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-expression-summary-statistics Use when multiple ribo− RNA-seq samples have been quantified with CLEAR (FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore) and the goal is cross-tissue comparison, per-tissue summary statistics, or reproducing tissue-enrichment patterns like Figure 5A. Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: the article notes polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Only a single sample/tissue is available and no cross-tissue comparison or summary is intended The quant outputs have not been produced by CLEAR/circ_quant (no FPBcirc, FPBlinear, or CIRCscore columns) — e.g. raw CIRCexplorer2 back-splicing calls without quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Aggregates per-sample CLEAR quant.txt outputs (readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, CIRCscore) across multiple tissues into a consolidated summary table, reproducing tissue-enrichment patterns such as brain-enriched circRNAs from the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR ENCODE 12-tissue analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample CLEAR quant.txt outputs (readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, CIRCscore) across multiple tissues into a consolidated summary table, reproducing tissue-enrichment patterns such as brain-enriched circRNAs from the CIRCexplorer3-CLEAR ENCODE 12-tissue analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: the article notes polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted, which is unsuitable for accurate linear RNA quantification and subsequent CIRCscore evaluation Only a single sample/tissue is available and no cross-tissue comparison or summary is intended The quant outputs have not been produced by CLEAR/circ_quant (no FPBcirc, FPBlinear, or CIRCscore columns) — e.g. raw CIRCexplorer2 back-splicing calls without quantification

skills.description: Use when MRSD-predicted sequencing depths must be validated on independent RNA-seq cohorts: you have paired junction-count and sequencing-depth files for control biosamples and need PPV/NPV per parameter combination.
skills.name: multi-tissue-rna-seq-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-rna-seq-benchmark-evaluation Use when MRSD-predicted sequencing depths must be validated on independent RNA-seq cohorts: you have paired junction-count and sequencing-depth files for control biosamples and need PPV/NPV per parameter combination. The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved: no appropriate control datasets exist yet to develop corresponding MRSD models The goal is predicting suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression: the MRSD model cannot be directly extended to these Sequencing methodology differs from Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A enrichment (e.g. total RNA, ribo-depletion): pre-computed GTEx-derived MRSDs are most accurate only for similar workflows, so scores must be regenerated rather than benchmarked as-is http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark evaluation of MRSD splice-junction coverage predictions against independent RNA-seq validation samples by sweeping the MRSDexplorer parameter grid (--number_reads, --sj_prop, --mrsd_param, --read_type) and computing per-combination PPV/NPV over 68 biosamples (12 blood, 4 LCL, 52 muscle). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of MRSD splice-junction coverage predictions against independent RNA-seq validation samples by sweeping the MRSDexplorer parameter grid (--number_reads, --sj_prop, --mrsd_param, --read_type) and computing per-combination PPV/NPV over 68 biosamples (12 blood, 4 LCL, 52 muscle).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The RNA-seq data are long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved: no appropriate control datasets exist yet to develop corresponding MRSD models The goal is predicting suitability for detecting allele-specific expression biases or differential gene expression: the MRSD model cannot be directly extended to these Sequencing methodology differs from Illumina 75 bp paired-end poly-A enrichment (e.g. total RNA, ribo-depletion): pre-computed GTEx-derived MRSDs are most accurate only for similar workflows, so scores must be regenerated rather than benchmarked as-is

skills.description: Use when you have Scanpro proportion-analysis results for several tissue subsets (e.g. heart, intestine, skeletal muscle) and need to verify that significant cell-type proportion shifts agree between the replicated design and the non-replicated bootstrapping mode.
skills.name: multi-tissue-significance-pattern-comparison
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-significance-pattern-comparison Use when you have Scanpro proportion-analysis results for several tissue subsets (e.g. heart, intestine, skeletal muscle) and need to verify that significant cell-type proportion shifts agree between the replicated design and the non-replicated bootstrapping mode. The input AnnData has no prior cell clustering/cell-type annotation — proportion analysis requires clustering into cell types before it can run The question is differential gene expression within individual subpopulations rather than shifts in the proportions of cell types Clusters of interest contain less than 2% of all cells — benchmarking showed such rare clusters produce unstable results and bootstrapping has limited benefit there http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A validation-style skill for cell-type proportion analysis in which significance calls from Scanpro are extracted per tissue and cross-compared between replicated runs and bootstrapped (pseudo-replicate) runs, checking that tissue-specialized cell types are consistently flagged and shared/ubiquitous cell types consistently not flagged. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: A validation-style skill for cell-type proportion analysis in which significance calls from Scanpro are extracted per tissue and cross-compared between replicated runs and bootstrapped (pseudo-replicate) runs, checking that tissue-specialized cell types are consistently flagged and shared/ubiquitous cell types consistently not flagged.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input AnnData has no prior cell clustering/cell-type annotation — proportion analysis requires clustering into cell types before it can run The question is differential gene expression within individual subpopulations rather than shifts in the proportions of cell types Clusters of interest contain less than 2% of all cells — benchmarking showed such rare clusters produce unstable results and bootstrapping has limited benefit there

skills.description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL result tables (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv) from GTEx or another multi-tissue cohort and want to measure cross-tissue sQTL sharing and cluster tissues by splicing-effect similarity.
skills.name: multi-tissue-sqtl-sharing-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-tissue-sqtl-sharing-analysis Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL result tables (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv) from GTEx or another multi-tissue cohort and want to measure cross-tissue sQTL sharing and cluster tissues by splicing-effect similarity. You need to determine whether paired sQTL/eQTL effects come from the same variant or two variants in LD — the article explicitly states co-localization and fine-mapping methods are not applicable within this multivariate framework You lack per-tissue significant sQTL call sets with MD effect sizes and only have raw splicing phenotype matrices (map sQTLs first with sqtlseeker2-nf) You want a specific statistical test of tissue-specific heteropleiotropic effects — the authors note no such test exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the extent to which sQTLs discovered by sQTLseekeR2 across GTEx tissues are shared, by correlating MD effect sizes of significant variant-gene pairs between tissue pairs and applying hierarchical clustering to the tissue-by-tissue correlation matrix. It reveals whether brain tissues form a distinct sQTL-sharing cluster from non-brain tissues. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Quantifies the extent to which sQTLs discovered by sQTLseekeR2 across GTEx tissues are shared, by correlating MD effect sizes of significant variant-gene pairs between tissue pairs and applying hierarchical clustering to the tissue-by-tissue correlation matrix. It reveals whether brain tissues form a distinct sQTL-sharing cluster from non-brain tissues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to determine whether paired sQTL/eQTL effects come from the same variant or two variants in LD — the article explicitly states co-localization and fine-mapping methods are not applicable within this multivariate framework You lack per-tissue significant sQTL call sets with MD effect sizes and only have raw splicing phenotype matrices (map sQTLs first with sqtlseeker2-nf) You want a specific statistical test of tissue-specific heteropleiotropic effects — the authors note no such test exists

skills.description: Use when comparing a new single-cell clustering method's accuracy against established tools on datasets with known cell-type labels, using ARI as the external validation metric.
skills.name: multi-tool-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-tool-clustering-benchmarking Use when comparing a new single-cell clustering method's accuracy against established tools on datasets with known cell-type labels, using ARI as the external validation metric. Datasets lack ground-truth cell-type annotations, so ARI cannot be computed and external validation is impossible The goal is clustering a single dataset rather than comparing methods across many datasets Input is already a preprocessed/normalized feature table — rerunning the 2.5%–97.5% gene filter and 2000-HVG selection would discard different genes than intended http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark scQA against nine clustering algorithms (SC3, Seurat, CIDR, pcaReduce, SIMLR, TSCAN, RaceID2, scGNN, scHFC) on 20 public scRNA-seq datasets with annotated cell types, scoring each with Adjusted Rand Index (ARI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Benchmark scQA against nine clustering algorithms (SC3, Seurat, CIDR, pcaReduce, SIMLR, TSCAN, RaceID2, scGNN, scHFC) on 20 public scRNA-seq datasets with annotated cell types, scoring each with Adjusted Rand Index (ARI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lack ground-truth cell-type annotations, so ARI cannot be computed and external validation is impossible The goal is clustering a single dataset rather than comparing methods across many datasets Input is already a preprocessed/normalized feature table — rerunning the 2.5%–97.5% gene filter and 2000-HVG selection would discard different genes than intended

skills.description: Use when comparing execution time of phasiRNA prediction tools on the same sRNA library and reference sequences, and you need an apples-to-apples runtime comparison that isolates the prediction step from shared preprocessing.
skills.name: multi-tool-comparative-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-tool-comparative-benchmarking Use when comparing execution time of phasiRNA prediction tools on the same sRNA library and reference sequences, and you need an apples-to-apples runtime comparison that isolates the prediction step from shared preprocessing. When the goal is to compare prediction accuracy or sensitivity (the sets of predicted phasiRNAs/PHAS loci) rather than wall-clock runtime — this skill only benchmarks execution time. When timing the full end-to-end pipeline: the benchmark deliberately excludes the shared bowtie index preparation and sRNA mapping step, so it is the wrong method for measuring preprocess-inclusive cost. When input is raw FASTQ data from your own library rather than the preprocessed test_osa .map files — you would first need phasiHunter preprocess and would be timing a different workflow. Benchmark runtime of PhasiHunter against unitas, PhaseTank, and PhasiRNAnalyzer for 21-nt phasiRNA prediction on transcriptome (cDNA) and genome (gDNA) references, excluding the shared bowtie indexing/mapping step from all timings, and quantify multithreaded speedup (-j 4 to ~45 min). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Benchmark runtime of PhasiHunter against unitas, PhaseTank, and PhasiRNAnalyzer for 21-nt phasiRNA prediction on transcriptome (cDNA) and genome (gDNA) references, excluding the shared bowtie indexing/mapping step from all timings, and quantify multithreaded speedup (-j 4 to ~45 min).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare prediction accuracy or sensitivity (the sets of predicted phasiRNAs/PHAS loci) rather than wall-clock runtime — this skill only benchmarks execution time. When timing the full end-to-end pipeline: the benchmark deliberately excludes the shared bowtie index preparation and sRNA mapping step, so it is the wrong method for measuring preprocess-inclusive cost. When input is raw FASTQ data from your own library rather than the preprocessed test_osa .map files — you would first need phasiHunter preprocess and would be timing a different workflow.

skills.description: Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools have each produced per-cell label predictions on the same dataset and you need a consensus confidence mask separating confidently labeled cells from unconfident ones.
skills.name: multi-tool-consensus-voting
skills.search_text: multi-tool-consensus-voting Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools have each produced per-cell label predictions on the same dataset and you need a consensus confidence mask separating confidently labeled cells from unconfident ones. You need higher annotation accuracy than simple majority voting provides — the paper shows its GCN label propagation method 'improves accuracy over a simple consensus algorithm' You have only one annotator tool's predictions, since a majority vote over a single labeler is degenerate Input is not a raw-count single-cell expression matrix (the README instructs 'Please input raw counts') http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregate per-cell cell-type predictions from five independent single-cell annotation tools (SCINA, ScType, scSorter, SingleR, scPred) via simple majority voting, marking cells as unconfident when fewer than a 0.51 fraction of tools agree, to quantify how many cells can be confidently labeled before downstream label propagation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Aggregate per-cell cell-type predictions from five independent single-cell annotation tools (SCINA, ScType, scSorter, SingleR, scPred) via simple majority voting, marking cells as unconfident when fewer than a 0.51 fraction of tools agree, to quantify how many cells can be confidently labeled before downstream label propagation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need higher annotation accuracy than simple majority voting provides — the paper shows its GCN label propagation method 'improves accuracy over a simple consensus algorithm' You have only one annotator tool's predictions, since a majority vote over a single labeler is degenerate Input is not a raw-count single-cell expression matrix (the README instructs 'Please input raw counts')

skills.description: Use when benchmarking circRNA/BSJ detection tools on identical ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ inputs and you need pairwise/three-way call-set overlaps plus per-tool BSJ fragment counts to expose sensitivity differences such as DCC misses.
skills.name: multi-tool-detection-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: multi-tool-detection-overlap-analysis Use when benchmarking circRNA/BSJ detection tools on identical ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ inputs and you need pairwise/three-way call-set overlaps plus per-tool BSJ fragment counts to expose sensitivity differences such as DCC misses. You only need to quantify circular vs. linear expression per locus (FPB/CIRCscore) rather than compare detection sensitivity across tools — use CLEAR's circ_quant directly instead Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ rather than ribo−-depleted, since circRNA/BSJ detection pipelines like CLEAR are designed for ribo− data You lack the raw FASTQ or a clean HISAT2 BAM (DCC requires a BAM without unmapped reads, so read-mapping-only comparisons cannot be performed) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs three circRNA detection pipelines (CLEAR-embedded CIRCexplorer2, MapSplice, and circtools-embedded DCC) on the same PA1 ribo− RNA-seq data, filters each call set to ≥3 BSJ-supporting fragments, and intersects them by genomic coordinates to quantify tool agreement, including circRNAs missed by DCC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Runs three circRNA detection pipelines (CLEAR-embedded CIRCexplorer2, MapSplice, and circtools-embedded DCC) on the same PA1 ribo− RNA-seq data, filters each call set to ≥3 BSJ-supporting fragments, and intersects them by genomic coordinates to quantify tool agreement, including circRNAs missed by DCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to quantify circular vs. linear expression per locus (FPB/CIRCscore) rather than compare detection sensitivity across tools — use CLEAR's circ_quant directly instead Input RNA-seq is poly(A)+ rather than ribo−-depleted, since circRNA/BSJ detection pipelines like CLEAR are designed for ribo− data You lack the raw FASTQ or a clean HISAT2 BAM (DCC requires a BAM without unmapped reads, so read-mapping-only comparisons cannot be performed)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking fusion gene callers on the same input datasets under graded conditions (e.g., successive read subsampling) and you need a unified detection matrix to compare which tool calls which fusions at which depth.

skills.description: Use when clusters from single-cell expression data must be tested for transitional relationships — e.g. estimating per-cell class probabilities and pairwise confusion scores to build ternary plots between putatively connected classes.
skills.name: multiclass-logistic-regression-cross-validation
skills.search_text: multiclass-logistic-regression-cross-validation Use when clusters from single-cell expression data must be tested for transitional relationships — e.g. estimating per-cell class probabilities and pairwise confusion scores to build ternary plots between putatively connected classes. When the goal is visualization of the embedding itself rather than testing transitional relationships between classes — plain graph_embed without the cross-validation/confusion-score analysis suffices. When classes are so few (< 3) that no class triple exists to score in a ternary plot. When the data matrix has already been correlation-transformed downstream, applying --correlation_transformation again would double-transform the profiles. Fits a one-vs-rest multiclass logistic regression (liblinear solver) on cell/cluster profiles and uses 5-fold cross-validated multiclass error estimates, symmetrized per class pair, to compute confusion scores for every cluster triple. These scores (0–1) drive ternary (simplex) plots that reveal whether a cluster represents a transitional state in a differentiation pathway. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Fits a one-vs-rest multiclass logistic regression (liblinear solver) on cell/cluster profiles and uses 5-fold cross-validated multiclass error estimates, symmetrized per class pair, to compute confusion scores for every cluster triple. These scores (0–1) drive ternary (simplex) plots that reveal whether a cluster represents a transitional state in a differentiation pathway.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is visualization of the embedding itself rather than testing transitional relationships between classes — plain graph_embed without the cross-validation/confusion-score analysis suffices. skills.description: Use when a compute-bound step (matrix multiplication, JIVE decomposition/rank estimation via bic.jive or jive.perm with a cores argument) dominates runtime and you need to quantify speedup across core counts 1/2/4/8 against a single-threaded baseline.

skills.search_text: multicore-parallel-scaling-analysis Use when a compute-bound step (matrix multiplication, JIVE decomposition/rank estimation via bic.jive or jive.perm with a cores argument) dominates runtime and you need to quantify speedup across core counts 1/2/4/8 against a single-threaded baseline. skills.search_text: multilevel-batch-vector-specification Use when scRNA-seq data have several batch covariates at once (e.g., 30 patients, 3 disease statuses, 2 locations) and single-factor methods like Harmony, LIGER, or Seurat3 CCA are insufficient. The dataset has only a single batch factor or no batch vectors — use n_batch=0 with an artificial all -1 batch vector instead of a multi-level specification The goal is mapping new, unseen patients without their batch annotations — set batch_invariant=True rather than batch_invariant=False Latent structure is hierarchical or branched developmental trajectory, where the hyperbolic 'wn' latent_dist is preferable to the spherical 'vmf' setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Specifies multiple simultaneous technical and biological batch factors (e.g., patient, health status, tissue location) in a scPhere VAE by passing a list of batch counts to n_batch, enabling batch correction for datasets where existing methods handle only a single batch variable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4

skills.name: multimapping-read-family-level-aggregation
skills.search_text: multimapping-read-family-level-aggregation Use when building a locus-specific TE expression matrix from scRNA-Seq BAMs (CellRanger/STAR) and reads overlap multiple TE copies, so locus-level counts would be unreliable for multi-mappers. The input is already a gene/TE feature count matrix — no read-level MAPQ partitioning is needed. The goal is bulk RNA-Seq TE analysis with EM-based multi-mapper resolution (e.g., Telescope/SQuIRE style), not single-cell locus-level summarization. The analysis requires TE-derived isoform detection or reads from TE-derived alternative transcription start sites, which SoloTE's 3'-biased 10X workflow cannot detect. A read-assignment strategy from SoloTE that assigns uniquely mapped reads (MAPQ >= user-defined threshold, default 255) to individual TE loci, while multi-mapping reads — which cannot be placed at a single genomic copy — are aggregated at the TE family level to preserve repetitive-element signal without false locus calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04020-5
skills.summary: A read-assignment strategy from SoloTE that assigns uniquely mapped reads (MAPQ >= user-defined threshold, default 255) to individual TE loci, while multi-mapping reads — which cannot be placed at a single genomic copy — are aggregated at the TE family level to preserve repetitive-element signal without false locus calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene/TE feature count matrix — no read-level MAPQ partitioning is needed. skills.search_text: multimeric-complex-subunit-minimum-rule Use when a curated ligand-receptor pair list annotates protein complexes (e.g. Human-2020-Jin-LR-pairs.csv from LewisLabUCSD/Ligand-Receptor-Pairs) and per-pair ligand/receptor scores must be computed from single-cell expression of individual subunits. skills.description: Use when you have multimodal single-cell omics data (RNA/ADT/ATAC measured on the same cells) and want to cluster cells by integrating modalities via ensemble VAE embeddings rather than clustering from any single modality alone.
skills.name: multimodal-embedding-snapshot-training
skills.search_text: multimodal-embedding-snapshot-training Use when you have multimodal single-cell omics data (RNA/ADT/ATAC measured on the same cells) and want to cluster cells by integrating modalities via ensemble VAE embeddings rather than clustering from any single modality alone. You only have a single modality — the integration benefit (better ARI/NMI than unimodality clustering) only arises when multiple modalities measured on the same cells are combined. You need a prescribed optimal hyperparameter set for a new dataset — the tutorial explicitly does not recommend best parameters; for datasets other than those in the paper, parameters must be determined separately. You need supervised cell-type annotation — SnapCCESS is an unsupervised clustering/embedding framework, not a classifier. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train SnapCCESS, an unsupervised ensemble deep learning framework that creates snapshots of multimodal variational autoencoder embeddings from single-cell omics data (e.g. RNA, ADT, ATAC), then couple the ensemble embedding with k-means to generate consensus cell clusters evaluated by ARI/NMI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Train SnapCCESS, an unsupervised ensemble deep learning framework that creates snapshots of multimodal variational autoencoder embeddings from single-cell omics data (e.g. RNA, ADT, ATAC), then couple the ensemble embedding with k-means to generate consensus cell clusters evaluated by ARI/NMI.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single modality — the integration benefit (better ARI/NMI than unimodality clustering) only arises when multiple modalities measured on the same cells are combined. You need a prescribed optimal hyperparameter set for a new dataset — the tutorial explicitly does not recommend best parameters; for datasets other than those in the paper, parameters must be determined separately. You need supervised cell-type annotation — SnapCCESS is an unsupervised clustering/embedding framework, not a classifier.

skills.description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data where both RNA and surface protein modalities must be integrated — e.g., fusing pairwise distance matrices, clustering mixed modalities, or computing a quantitative cluster purity score.
skills.name: multimodal-single-cell-distance-integration
skills.search_text: multimodal-single-cell-distance-integration Use when analyzing CITE-seq data where both RNA and surface protein modalities must be integrated — e.g., fusing pairwise distance matrices, clustering mixed modalities, or computing a quantitative cluster purity score. Massive datasets such as 170K cells with 228 ADT features — LinQ-View failed on this scale whereas Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets with a high number of ADT features (≥50) — LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (e.g., <50) Unimodal data with no surface protein modality — the L∞ norm fusion and ADT sigmoid filter require both mRNA and protein distances http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Integrates single-cell transcriptome and surface protein (ADT) expression by computing per-modality cell-cell pairwise distances, applying a sigmoid filter to ADT distances, and fusing them with an L∞ norm, then deriving a quantitative purity score for cluster purity assessment in CITE-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Integrates single-cell transcriptome and surface protein (ADT) expression by computing per-modality cell-cell pairwise distances, applying a sigmoid filter to ADT distances, and fusing them with an L∞ norm, then deriving a quantitative purity score for cluster purity assessment in CITE-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Massive datasets such as 170K cells with 228 ADT features — LinQ-View failed on this scale whereas Seurat 4 succeeded Datasets with a high number of ADT features (≥50) — LinQ-View is best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (e.g., <50) Unimodal data with no surface protein modality — the L∞ norm fusion and ADT sigmoid filter require both mRNA and protein distances

skills.description: Use when the input is multimodal single-cell omics count data (RNA plus ADT or ATAC measured on the same cells) and the goal is an unsupervised shared latent space for clustering cells.

skills.search_text: multimodal-single-cell-embedding-generation Use when the input is multimodal single-cell omics count data (RNA plus ADT or ATAC measured on the same cells) and the goal is an unsupervised shared latent space for clustering cells. The tutorial only explains package usage and does not recommend best parameters, so do not rely on tutorial defaults when reproducing paper benchmarks — use dataset-specific parameters from the paper instead Data are unimodal (a single feature table with no second modality); the framework concatenates modality-specific encoders and expects a list of modalities across the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates cell embeddings from multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA/ADT, SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA/ATAC) by creating snapshots of multimodality variational autoencoder embeddings, which are then coupled with clustering algorithms to produce consensus cell clusterings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Generates cell embeddings from multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA/ADT, SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA/ATAC) by creating snapshots of multimodality variational autoencoder embeddings, which are then coupled with clustering algorithms to produce consensus cell clusterings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tutorial only explains package usage and does not recommend best parameters, so do not rely on tutorial defaults when reproducing paper benchmarks — use dataset-specific parameters from the paper instead Data are unimodal (a single feature table with no second modality); the framework concatenates modality-specific encoders and expects a list of modalities across the same cells

skills.search_text: multimodal-single-cell-omics-clustering Use when you have multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA + ADT matrices over the same cells) with no labels, and the goal is unsupervised consensus cell-type clustering via deep-learning embeddings. skills.summary: Unsupervised ensemble deep learning (SnapCCESS) for clustering multimodal single-cell omics data: it creates snapshots of multimodality variational autoencoder embeddings and couples them with clustering algorithms to generate consensus clusters, achieving performance comparable to conventional VAE ensembles at far lower training cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-modality only, or modalities are not measured across the same cells (SnapCCESS expects a list of modalities over the same cells, e.g. RNA + ADT) A supervised cell-type classifier is needed: SnapCCESS is an unsupervised framework for consensus clustering, not label-based classification You need dataset-specific optimal hyperparameters from the package alone — the tutorial explicitly does not recommend best parameters; those must come from the paper

skills.description: Use when analyzing paired multi-omic SNARE-seq data where cells have both a chromatin (cell-by-peak) and expression modality, and cluster-level cell-type annotation must be supported by marker genes and GO enrichment.
skills.name: multimodal-snare-seq-data-harmonization
skills.search_text: multimodal-snare-seq-data-harmonization Use when analyzing paired multi-omic SNARE-seq data where cells have both a chromatin (cell-by-peak) and expression modality, and cluster-level cell-type annotation must be supported by marker genes and GO enrichment. Data are unpaired (e.g., separate scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq experiments) — label transfer relies on matching cell barcodes between modalities profiled from the same cells The goal is purely RNA-based clustering — this skill's clustering operates on the chromatin modality's cell-by-topic matrix, not gene expression Cellar's reference-annotation mode suffices — for datasets with HuBMAP annotated references, direct reference-based label transfer (e.g., scanpy Ingest) may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Jointly cluster paired ATAC/RNA SNARE-seq data by clustering the chromatin modality (cisTopic topics) and transferring cluster labels to the paired expression modality via shared cell barcodes, then annotating clusters with marker and GO enrichment evidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Jointly cluster paired ATAC/RNA SNARE-seq data by clustering the chromatin modality (cisTopic topics) and transferring cluster labels to the paired expression modality via shared cell barcodes, then annotating clusters with marker and GO enrichment evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired (e.g., separate scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq experiments) — label transfer relies on matching cell barcodes between modalities profiled from the same cells The goal is purely RNA-based clustering — this skill's clustering operates on the chromatin modality's cell-by-topic matrix, not gene expression Cellar's reference-annotation mode suffices — for datasets with HuBMAP annotated references, direct reference-based label transfer (e.g., scanpy Ingest) may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and TCR sequencing data (with cell type, clonotype, or antigen specificity annotations) and need a joint cell-level embedding for clustering, antigen specificity prediction, or atlas-query label transfer.
skills.name: multimodal-tcr-transcriptome-model-training
skills.search_text: multimodal-tcr-transcriptome-model-training Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and TCR sequencing data (with cell type, clonotype, or antigen specificity annotations) and need a joint cell-level embedding for clustering, antigen specificity prediction, or atlas-query label transfer. Data are unimodal (TCR-only or expression-only) — mvTCR requires both modalities, and the paper notes it was mainly applied to fully paired data with alpha- and beta-CDR3 plus gene expression Only a small exploratory dataset without GPU access — a machine with GPU- and CUDA-support is heavily encouraged and training is impractical on CPU-only hardware The goal is TCR sequence-only specificity prediction with pretrained TCR embeddings or VDJ-gene encoding — the paper states these are not yet incorporated; only the CDR3 sequence is currently used http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Train mvTCR, a multi-view Variational Autoencoder, to fuse modality-specific transcriptome and TCR (CDR3 sequence) information into a shared cell-level embedding for antigen specificity prediction, clustering, and reference mapping of single-cell immune profiling data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Train mvTCR, a multi-view Variational Autoencoder, to fuse modality-specific transcriptome and TCR (CDR3 sequence) information into a shared cell-level embedding for antigen specificity prediction, clustering, and reference mapping of single-cell immune profiling data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unimodal (TCR-only or expression-only) — mvTCR requires both modalities, and the paper notes it was mainly applied to fully paired data with alpha- and beta-CDR3 plus gene expression Only a small exploratory dataset without GPU access — a machine with GPU- and CUDA-support is heavily encouraged and training is impractical on CPU-only hardware The goal is TCR sequence-only specificity prediction with pretrained TCR embeddings or VDJ-gene encoding — the paper states these are not yet incorporated; only the CDR3 sequence is currently used

skills.description: Use when fitting reference signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1) to individual hematological cancer genomes with ≥500 mutations and you need contribution estimates with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and error suppression.
skills.name: multinomial-bootstrap-signature-fitting
skills.search_text: multinomial-bootstrap-signature-fitting Use when fitting reference signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1) to individual hematological cancer genomes with ≥500 mutations and you need contribution estimates with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and error suppression. Targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases yield too low mutational burdens for meaningful per-patient signature fitting. The goal is de novo discovery of novel signatures — this skill fits a fixed reference set (e.g. COSMIC v3.1) rather than extracting new signatures by NMF. Catalogs with fewer than ~500 mutations, where fitting accuracy (including APOBEC SBS2/SBS13 discrimination) degrades. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit reference mutational signatures (e.g. COSMIC SBS signatures) to a tumor's 96-channel trinucleotide catalog with mmsig's expectation-maximization fitting plus bootstrapping to obtain 95% confidence intervals for each signature's contribution, supporting presence/absence calls via non-zero CIs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
skills.summary: Fit reference mutational signatures (e.g. COSMIC SBS signatures) to a tumor's 96-channel trinucleotide catalog with mmsig's expectation-maximization fitting plus bootstrapping to obtain 95% confidence intervals for each signature's contribution, supporting presence/absence calls via non-zero CIs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases yield too low mutational burdens for meaningful per-patient signature fitting. The goal is de novo discovery of novel signatures — this skill fits a fixed reference set (e.g. COSMIC v3.1) rather than extracting new signatures by NMF. Catalogs with fewer than ~500 mutations, where fitting accuracy (including APOBEC SBS2/SBS13 discrimination) degrades.

skills.description: Use when rebuilding or adapting the scMGCA decoder to model scRNA-seq count matrices with a multinomial likelihood plus Bernoulli dropout simulation instead of a zero-inflated (ZINB/NB) distribution, e.g. in TensorFlow re-implementations of the autoencoder.
skills.name: multinomial-decoder-network-implementation
skills.search_text: multinomial-decoder-network-implementation Use when rebuilding or adapting the scMGCA decoder to model scRNA-seq count matrices with a multinomial likelihood plus Bernoulli dropout simulation instead of a zero-inflated (ZINB/NB) distribution, e.g. in TensorFlow re-implementations of the autoencoder. If the goal is denoising with a zero-inflated negative binomial loss (e.g. reproducing DCA) or model-based deep embedding clustering under ZINB (e.g. scDeepCluster) — those methods intentionally model the data with ZINB, which this multinomial decoder replaces. If the input is already a latent embedding with no accompanying count matrix — the multinomial NLL requires the per-cell count vector to evaluate gene probabilities. If the input is TPM/CPM-normalized continuous values rather than counts — multinomial likelihood evaluation on non-count data is not supported by this formulation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder's decoder as a three-layer fully connected network (128→256→512) with a softmax final activation that maps the latent representation Z to a multinomial parameter matrix M over genes, combined with Bernoulli dropout probabilities for zero-count entries. This replaces the zero-inflated negative binomial likelihood used by methods like DCA and scDeepCluster because single-cell count matrices largely follow a multinomial distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: Reconstructs the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder's decoder as a three-layer fully connected network (128→256→512) with a softmax final activation that maps the latent representation Z to a multinomial parameter matrix M over genes, combined with Bernoulli dropout probabilities for zero-count entries. This replaces the zero-inflated negative binomial likelihood used by methods like DCA and scDeepCluster because single-cell count matrices largely follow a multinomial distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is denoising with a zero-inflated negative binomial loss (e.g. reproducing DCA) or model-based deep embedding clustering under ZINB (e.g. scDeepCluster) — those methods intentionally model the data with ZINB, which this multinomial decoder replaces. If the input is already a latent embedding with no accompanying count matrix — the multinomial NLL requires the per-cell count vector to evaluate gene probabilities. If the input is TPM/CPM-normalized continuous values rather than counts — multinomial likelihood evaluation on non-count data is not supported by this formulation.

skills.description: Use when annotating newly sequenced single-cell RNA-seq cells (or clusters) against labeled reference data — including cross-species queries mapped to one-to-one orthologues — and a fast, portable supervised classifier is needed.
skills.name: multinomial-likelihood-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: multinomial-likelihood-cell-type-classification Use when annotating newly sequenced single-cell RNA-seq cells (or clusters) against labeled reference data — including cross-species queries mapped to one-to-one orthologues — and a fast, portable supervised classifier is needed. Cell types in the query data are not represented in the reference and no null dataset is available — SciBet's low false-positive rate relies on setting a null dataset as the alternate reference for uncovered types The query and reference gene spaces cannot be reconciled (e.g., cross-species work without one-to-one orthologues in HomoloGene) Labels are unknown in the training data — this is a supervised method requiring annotated reference cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 SciBet-style supervised cell-type annotation that models each training cell type as a multinomial distribution over informative genes and assigns an unknown cell to the type with maximum multinomial likelihood (equivalently, minimal Kullback–Leibler divergence). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: SciBet-style supervised cell-type annotation that models each training cell type as a multinomial distribution over informative genes and assigns an unknown cell to the type with maximum multinomial likelihood (equivalently, minimal Kullback–Leibler divergence).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types in the query data are not represented in the reference and no null dataset is available — SciBet's low false-positive rate relies on setting a null dataset as the alternate reference for uncovered types The query and reference gene spaces cannot be reconciled (e.g., cross-species work without one-to-one orthologues in HomoloGene) Labels are unknown in the training data — this is a supervised method requiring annotated reference cells

skills.description: Use when predicting the circadian time of a single transcriptomic sample (bulk or pseudobulk) after training on a paired-expression/timepoint time series, with rhythmic genes as platform-agnostic features.
skills.name: multinomial-logistic-timepoint-classification
skills.search_text: multinomial-logistic-timepoint-classification Use when predicting the circadian time of a single transcriptomic sample (bulk or pseudobulk) after training on a paired-expression/timepoint time series, with rhythmic genes as platform-agnostic features. Predicting circadian time of individual cells — tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and only works on bulk or pseudobulk data You need uncertainty quantification or confidence scores — tauFisher does not output them; consider Tempo for uncertainty estimates in single-cell data Projecting test data onto the timescale of diseased samples — a time series from diseased individuals is required, which a model trained on healthy data cannot provide http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 tauFisher's timepoint classifier: pairwise expression differences of rhythmic predictor genes are PCA-embedded and a multinomial logistic regression (nnet::multinom) on the first two principal components predicts the circadian time (CT) of a single transcriptomic sample, independent of assay platform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: tauFisher's timepoint classifier: pairwise expression differences of rhythmic predictor genes are PCA-embedded and a multinomial logistic regression (nnet::multinom) on the first two principal components predicts the circadian time (CT) of a single transcriptomic sample, independent of assay platform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting circadian time of individual cells — tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and only works on bulk or pseudobulk data You need uncertainty quantification or confidence scores — tauFisher does not output them; consider Tempo for uncertainty estimates in single-cell data Projecting test data onto the timescale of diseased samples — a time series from diseased individuals is required, which a model trained on healthy data cannot provide

skills.description: Use when you have bulk HiChIP loop counts (gene-enhancer pairs) plus scRNA-seq (E) and scATAC-seq (O) matrices with cluster labels from the same heterogeneous population, and you want subpopulation-specific HiChIP profiles with better interpretation than the plug-in baseline.
skills.name: multinomial-loop-count-allocation
skills.search_text: multinomial-loop-count-allocation Use when you have bulk HiChIP loop counts (gene-enhancer pairs) plus scRNA-seq (E) and scATAC-seq (O) matrices with cluster labels from the same heterogeneous population, and you want subpopulation-specific HiChIP profiles with better interpretation than the plug-in baseline. When wall-clock runtime matters (~3 min) or a first-pass result suffices — the simple plug-in baseline achieves comparable PCC at a fraction of the ~24 h cost When the HiChIP profile for each subpopulation can be measured directly, e.g. on FACS-isolated marker-positive cells When scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples do not come from the same cell population, since cluster-mean profiles P1/P2 from these samples anchor the multinomial proportions Model-based inference that decomposes bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loop counts into subpopulation-specific loop counts by initializing latent counts C_ijk via multinomial allocation and iteratively refining them with MAP estimation under a Poisson gene-expression likelihood, as an alternative to DC3's simple plug-in method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Model-based inference that decomposes bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loop counts into subpopulation-specific loop counts by initializing latent counts C_ijk via multinomial allocation and iteratively refining them with MAP estimation under a Poisson gene-expression likelihood, as an alternative to DC3's simple plug-in method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When wall-clock runtime matters (~3 min) or a first-pass result suffices — the simple plug-in baseline achieves comparable PCC at a fraction of the ~24 h cost When the HiChIP profile for each subpopulation can be measured directly, e.g. on FACS-isolated marker-positive cells When scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples do not come from the same cell population, since cluster-mean profiles P1/P2 from these samples anchor the multinomial proportions

skills.description: Use when building a co-expression-free null read-count matrix with known ground-truth log expression proportions, e.g. to calibrate or benchmark detection of nonlinear library-size confounders in scRNA-seq association testing.
skills.name: multinomial-read-sampling
skills.search_text: multinomial-read-sampling Use when building a co-expression-free null read-count matrix with known ground-truth log expression proportions, e.g. to calibrate or benchmark detection of nonlinear library-size confounders in scRNA-seq association testing. When the goal is a null with preserved gene-gene correlations — the multinomial sampling construction explicitly produces no true co-expression When analyzing full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq platforms: Normalisr only focused on UMI-based datasets, and read-count distributions may differ and require revalidation When input is already a normalized/feature-table expression matrix — sampling must start from raw read counts to estimate empirical library sizes and proportions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates a synthetic null scRNA-seq read-count matrix (e.g. homogeneous gRNA-free K562-like cells) by combining log-normal biological variation on gene expression proportions with multinomial read sampling of per-cell library sizes, yielding a null that mimics real cells but contains no true co-expression. It is used by Normalisr to detect nonlinear technical confounders arising from library size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic null scRNA-seq read-count matrix (e.g. homogeneous gRNA-free K562-like cells) by combining log-normal biological variation on gene expression proportions with multinomial read sampling of per-cell library sizes, yielding a null that mimics real cells but contains no true co-expression. It is used by Normalisr to detect nonlinear technical confounders arising from library size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a null with preserved gene-gene correlations — the multinomial sampling construction explicitly produces no true co-expression When analyzing full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq platforms: Normalisr only focused on UMI-based datasets, and read-count distributions may differ and require revalidation When input is already a normalized/feature-table expression matrix — sampling must start from raw read counts to estimate empirical library sizes and proportions

skills.search_text: multiomic-coembedded-data-handling Use when single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq from the same tissue (e.g. human heart post-myocardial infarction) are stored in separate Seurat objects and must be co-embedded, batch-corrected, and cell-paired before trajectory or GRN analysis. Data are already natively paired 10x Multiome with matched barcodes per cell — PairCells-based cross-modality matching is unnecessary for such objects Only one modality is available (e.g. snRNA-seq alone), so no co-embedding or enhancer-to-gene linking across modalities is possible Input is bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq rather than single-cell/nucleus data, where Seurat/ArchR cell-level co-embedding does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Handles the integration stage of the scMEGA workflow: co-embedding unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq cells into a common low-dimensional space with Seurat's CCA, batch-correcting with Harmony, sub-clustering, and pairing cells across modalities so enhancer-based GRN inference can proceed on a paired Seurat object. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Handles the integration stage of the scMEGA workflow: co-embedding unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq cells into a common low-dimensional space with Seurat's CCA, batch-correcting with Harmony, sub-clustering, and pairing cells across modalities so enhancer-based GRN inference can proceed on a paired Seurat object.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already natively paired 10x Multiome with matched barcodes per cell — PairCells-based cross-modality matching is unnecessary for such objects Only one modality is available (e.g. snRNA-seq alone), so no co-embedding or enhancer-to-gene linking across modalities is possible Input is bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq rather than single-cell/nucleus data, where Seurat/ArchR cell-level co-embedding does not apply
