Input is raw CITE-seq counts that have not yet been encoded by scMM into a joint latent representation Single-modality data (RNA-only or ATAC-only) where surface-protein marker panels cannot be computed Aims requiring only coarse cell-type labels rather than high-resolution (~54-cluster) interpretable characterization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate and interpret high-resolution clusters from scMM's joint transcriptome–surface-protein latent space by building side-by-side z-scored marker heatmaps (pheatmap) of genes and proteins per Rphenograph cluster, as demonstrated on PBMC CITE-seq data (~54 clusters). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Annotate and interpret high-resolution clusters from scMM's joint transcriptome–surface-protein latent space by building side-by-side z-scored marker heatmaps (pheatmap) of genes and proteins per Rphenograph cluster, as demonstrated on PBMC CITE-seq data (~54 clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw CITE-seq counts that have not yet been encoded by scMM into a joint latent representation Single-modality data (RNA-only or ATAC-only) where surface-protein marker panels cannot be computed Aims requiring only coarse cell-type labels rather than high-resolution (~54-cluster) interpretable characterization

skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell multi-omics data (e.g., a Muon object with RNA, ATAC and/or protein modalities) and need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding with interpretable factors, as in the Mowgli workflow.
skills.name: multiomics-nmf-embedding-training
skills.search_text: multiomics-nmf-embedding-training Use when you have paired single-cell multi-omics data (e.g., a Muon object with RNA, ATAC and/or protein modalities) and need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding with interpretable factors, as in the Mowgli workflow. Unpaired or non-paired single-cell data where cell-level correspondence between modalities is unavailable When the number of latent dimensions k must be set automatically — Mowgli does not offer a straightforward approach to defining k, so avoid expecting auto-selection Datasets that require batch correction across centers — Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data Train the Mowgli model, which decomposes paired multi-omics matrices (scRNA, scATAC, ADT) via integrative Nonnegative Matrix Factorization combined with entropic-regularized Optimal Transport to yield modality-specific dictionaries H(p) and a shared cell embedding W. This skill covers building the cosine ground cost, running Sinkhorn-based OT, and alternating L-BFGS optimization on the dual problems. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Train the Mowgli model, which decomposes paired multi-omics matrices (scRNA, scATAC, ADT) via integrative Nonnegative Matrix Factorization combined with entropic-regularized Optimal Transport to yield modality-specific dictionaries H(p) and a shared cell embedding W. This skill covers building the cosine ground cost, running Sinkhorn-based OT, and alternating L-BFGS optimization on the dual problems.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Unpaired or non-paired single-cell data where cell-level correspondence between modalities is unavailable When the number of latent dimensions k must be set automatically — Mowgli does not offer a straightforward approach to defining k, so avoid expecting auto-selection Datasets that require batch correction across centers — Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data

skills.description: Use when you have run JOINTLY and scored cells with AddModuleScore_UCell and need to visualize factor activity per cell type or per covariate (e.g. factor 10 insulin-signalling boxplots by status and sex), or build module/marker AUC comparison panels.
skills.name: multipanel-figure-generation-from-module-scores
skills.search_text: multipanel-figure-generation-from-module-scores Use when you have run JOINTLY and scored cells with AddModuleScore_UCell and need to visualize factor activity per cell type or per covariate (e.g. factor 10 insulin-signalling boxplots by status and sex), or build module/marker AUC comparison panels. No interpretable modules have been learned yet — JOINTLY must be run first (e.g. jointly(obj, batch.var = "batch_label")) before scores exist to plot Expression values are batch-smoothed/imputed from the JOINTLY H and F matrices — the authors advise these are for visualization with caution only, not for quantitative score comparisons The question is which integration method to choose — integration metrics such as ARI/NMI do not reveal the genes or features driving clustering, which is what this visualization skill targets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates publication figures (module-by-cell-type heatmaps, UMAP feature plots, and boxplots of JOINTLY factor module scores split by covariates such as insulin-signalling status and sex) from JOINTLY's interpretable gene modules and UCell scores, as done for Fig. 4A-H of the adipose analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Generates publication figures (module-by-cell-type heatmaps, UMAP feature plots, and boxplots of JOINTLY factor module scores split by covariates such as insulin-signalling status and sex) from JOINTLY's interpretable gene modules and UCell scores, as done for Fig. 4A-H of the adipose analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No interpretable modules have been learned yet — JOINTLY must be run first (e.g. jointly(obj, batch.var = "batch_label")) before scores exist to plot Expression values are batch-smoothed/imputed from the JOINTLY H and F matrices — the authors advise these are for visualization with caution only, not for quantitative score comparisons The question is which integration method to choose — integration metrics such as ARI/NMI do not reveal the genes or features driving clustering, which is what this visualization skill targets

skills.description: Use when you have two disjoint gene lists (algorithm-selected vs discarded genes) plus gene set annotations and need over-representation p values converted to FDR q values to validate that selection enriches specific biology.
skills.name: multiple-hypothesis-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-hypothesis-fdr-correction Use when you have two disjoint gene lists (algorithm-selected vs discarded genes) plus gene set annotations and need over-representation p values converted to FDR q values to validate that selection enriches specific biology. You need enrichment of a single pre-specified hypothesis gene set without multiple-testing burden — an uncorrected hypergeometric p value suffices and FDR correction is unnecessary You lack a defined background universe (full gene list of the dataset), making hypergeometric over-representation testing invalid Your goal is denoising or feature selection itself (Randomly's RMT eigenvalue/eigenvector analysis) rather than downstream validation of selected genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Hypergeometric over-representation testing of RMT-selected signal genes against gene set annotations (GO/Reactome-style terms), with Benjamini-Hochberg-style FDR q-value correction across all tested gene sets, to show that Randomly-selected genes enrich for tissue-specific processes (e.g. chemical synaptic transmission, Neural system in mouse cortex) rather than generic ones. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Hypergeometric over-representation testing of RMT-selected signal genes against gene set annotations (GO/Reactome-style terms), with Benjamini-Hochberg-style FDR q-value correction across all tested gene sets, to show that Randomly-selected genes enrich for tissue-specific processes (e.g. chemical synaptic transmission, Neural system in mouse cortex) rather than generic ones.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need enrichment of a single pre-specified hypothesis gene set without multiple-testing burden — an uncorrected hypergeometric p value suffices and FDR correction is unnecessary You lack a defined background universe (full gene list of the dataset), making hypergeometric over-representation testing invalid Your goal is denoising or feature selection itself (Randomly's RMT eigenvalue/eigenvector analysis) rather than downstream validation of selected genes

skills.description: Use when a large set of per-feature association tests (e.g., one Fisher's exact test per GCF in an absence/presence matrix) produces raw p-values that must be BH-corrected before ranking significant hits.
skills.name: multiple-hypothesis-pvalue-adjustment
skills.search_text: multiple-hypothesis-pvalue-adjustment Use when a large set of per-feature association tests (e.g., one Fisher's exact test per GCF in an absence/presence matrix) produces raw p-values that must be BH-corrected before ranking significant hits. Input is a single pre-computed p-value or a small pre-planned hypothesis set with no multiplicity — BH correction would needlessly inflate the threshold The enrichment features are individual genes (pLAGs) rather than GCFs; bacLIFE uses different thresholds for genes (>70% group presence, >2 log2 fold change) and applies machine learning instead of per-GCF Fisher tests GCFs below the >15% group presence threshold — sparse clusters are excluded before testing rather than corrected after http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Corrects per-feature enrichment p-values (e.g., per-GCF Fisher's exact tests) for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg via base R p.adjust(), so that lifestyle-associated biosynthetic gene cluster families can be flagged at a controlled significance threshold (P < 0.01 in bacLIFE). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Corrects per-feature enrichment p-values (e.g., per-GCF Fisher's exact tests) for multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg via base R p.adjust(), so that lifestyle-associated biosynthetic gene cluster families can be flagged at a controlled significance threshold (P < 0.01 in bacLIFE).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single pre-computed p-value or a small pre-planned hypothesis set with no multiplicity — BH correction would needlessly inflate the threshold The enrichment features are individual genes (pLAGs) rather than GCFs; bacLIFE uses different thresholds for genes (>70% group presence, >2 log2 fold change) and applies machine learning instead of per-GCF Fisher tests GCFs below the >15% group presence threshold — sparse clusters are excluded before testing rather than corrected after

skills.description: Use when a family of m raw p-values (e.g. from RgnTX permutation tests over m6A site groups) must be FDR-adjusted before declaring colocalization significant at alpha=0.05.
skills.name: multiple-hypothesis-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-hypothesis-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction Use when a family of m raw p-values (e.g. from RgnTX permutation tests over m6A site groups) must be FDR-adjusted before declaring colocalization significant at alpha=0.05. Only a single hypothesis test is present — no family of m p-values to correct, so FDR adjustment is inappropriate The input is already an adjusted p-value vector or a q-value/FDR table rather than raw p-values The analysis requires family-wise error rate control (e.g. Bonferroni guarantees) rather than FDR control http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up FDR procedure to adjust raw permutation p-values (e.g. from RgnTX colocalization tests), computing adjusted p-values via pFDR(i)=p(i)*m/i with backward min-accumulation and rejecting the largest k with p(k) <= k*alpha/m to control false positives across many tested region-set pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Applies the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up FDR procedure to adjust raw permutation p-values (e.g. from RgnTX colocalization tests), computing adjusted p-values via pFDR(i)=p(i)*m/i with backward min-accumulation and rejecting the largest k with p(k) <= k*alpha/m to control false positives across many tested region-set pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single hypothesis test is present — no family of m p-values to correct, so FDR adjustment is inappropriate The input is already an adjusted p-value vector or a q-value/FDR table rather than raw p-values The analysis requires family-wise error rate control (e.g. Bonferroni guarantees) rather than FDR control

skills.description: Use when you have ARI results from clustering methods evaluated across a SymSim parameter grid (N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, rare-population proportion) and need to attribute performance variation to individual simulation factors.
skills.name: multiple-linear-regression-of-parameters-versus-ari
skills.search_text: multiple-linear-regression-of-parameters-versus-ari Use when you have ARI results from clustering methods evaluated across a SymSim parameter grid (N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, rare-population proportion) and need to attribute performance variation to individual simulation factors. The data are real experimental counts rather than SymSim simulations with known ground-truth parameters, so there is no parameter grid to regress against You only have ARI for a single parameter setting (no variation in N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, or Prop), leaving the regression with no explanatory variation The goal is to rank clustering methods rather than attribute ARI variation to simulation factors — a direct comparison of ARI curves (Fig. 5b-c) is more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a multiple linear regression of clustering adjusted Rand index (ARI) on the SymSim simulation parameters (N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, Prop) and extracts standardized coefficients to quantify which factors drive rare-population detection performance, reproducing the Fig. 5a coefficient bar plot of the Zhang et al. 2019 SymSim paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Fits a multiple linear regression of clustering adjusted Rand index (ARI) on the SymSim simulation parameters (N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, Prop) and extracts standardized coefficients to quantify which factors drive rare-population detection performance, reproducing the Fig. 5a coefficient bar plot of the Zhang et al. 2019 SymSim paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real experimental counts rather than SymSim simulations with known ground-truth parameters, so there is no parameter grid to regress against You only have ARI for a single parameter setting (no variation in N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, or Prop), leaving the regression with no explanatory variation The goal is to rank clustering methods rather than attribute ARI variation to simulation factors — a direct comparison of ARI curves (Fig. 5b-c) is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads in FrameD and multiple noisy copies per strand must be consolidated before inner-code reversal, especially under fault injection.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-decode-integration
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-decode-integration Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads in FrameD and multiple noisy copies per strand must be consolidated before inner-code reversal, especially under fault injection. Error profile has low error rate or error types for which MSA is not beneficial — the paper states MSA inclusion depends on error rate and error type and is not always beneficial Each strand exists as only a single read, so there are no redundant copies to cluster or align You need to consolidate strands after the inner code instead — FrameD provides an alternative decode mode for post-inner-code consolidation Integrates strand clustering (MinHash/edit-distance) and multiple sequence alignment (e.g. Muscle) into the FrameD decode pipeline before reversing the inner code, so multiple sequenced copies of each encoded strand are aggregated toward a consensus base-sequence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Integrates strand clustering (MinHash/edit-distance) and multiple sequence alignment (e.g. Muscle) into the FrameD decode pipeline before reversing the inner code, so multiple sequenced copies of each encoded strand are aggregated toward a consensus base-sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Error profile has low error rate or error types for which MSA is not beneficial — the paper states MSA inclusion depends on error rate and error type and is not always beneficial Each strand exists as only a single read, so there are no redundant copies to cluster or align You need to consolidate strands after the inner code instead — FrameD provides an alternative decode mode for post-inner-code consolidation

skills.description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (like Seq2Fun 's2f_' groups) aggregates too many genes across species to allow gene-level insights, and the protein sequences plus species labels need alignment before clustering.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-protein-sequences
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-protein-sequences Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (like Seq2Fun 's2f_' groups) aggregates too many genes across species to allow gene-level insights, and the protein sequences plus species labels need alignment before clustering. Input is raw RNA-seq reads rather than protein sequences of a defined ortholog group — use Seq2Fun read-to-KO mapping instead of ortholog splitting. The goal is KO-based functional annotation; note vitellogenin is not found in the KO system, which is precisely why ortholog-level splitting is needed for such biomarkers. The ortholog group is already small enough to permit gene-level insights without splitting. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Builds a MAFFT multiple sequence alignment of all protein sequences in an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (e.g. vitellogenin group s2f_0005567), preserving each sequence's species assignment, so that phylogenetic structure within oversized ortholog groups can be quantified for ortholog splitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Builds a MAFFT multiple sequence alignment of all protein sequences in an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (e.g. vitellogenin group s2f_0005567), preserving each sequence's species assignment, so that phylogenetic structure within oversized ortholog groups can be quantified for ortholog splitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA-seq reads rather than protein sequences of a defined ortholog group — use Seq2Fun read-to-KO mapping instead of ortholog splitting. The goal is KO-based functional annotation; note vitellogenin is not found in the KO system, which is precisely why ortholog-level splitting is needed for such biomarkers. The ortholog group is already small enough to permit gene-level insights without splitting.

skills.description: Use when constructing a curated database of potentially functional HERVs: genomic loci must be translated, screened against retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV), and filtered to retain only sequences with detectable homology.
skills.name: multiple-sequence-alignment-profiling
skills.search_text: multiple-sequence-alignment-profiling Use when constructing a curated database of potentially functional HERVs: genomic loci must be translated, screened against retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV), and filtered to retain only sequences with detectable homology. When the target is exogenous (non-human) viral identification from RNAseq reads — that is handled by the viRNAtrap deep learning pipeline, not HERV database curation. When HERV sequences have already been annotated as functional/intact (e.g., via an existing curated database) and only expression quantification is needed. When loci lack any detectable POL/RT, GAG, or ENV motif after blastx/MAFFT-profiling — these fail the filter and should not be retained in the database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds a POL protein profile by aligning candidate reverse transcriptase sequences with MAFFT, then screening HERV candidate sequences against it (alongside blastx hits) to retain HERVs with retroviral POL/RT, GAG, or ENV motifs for a curated, potentially-functional HERV database. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Builds a POL protein profile by aligning candidate reverse transcriptase sequences with MAFFT, then screening HERV candidate sequences against it (alongside blastx hits) to retain HERVs with retroviral POL/RT, GAG, or ENV motifs for a curated, potentially-functional HERV database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target is exogenous (non-human) viral identification from RNAseq reads — that is handled by the viRNAtrap deep learning pipeline, not HERV database curation. When HERV sequences have already been annotated as functional/intact (e.g., via an existing curated database) and only expression quantification is needed. When loci lack any detectable POL/RT, GAG, or ENV motif after blastx/MAFFT-profiling — these fail the filter and should not be retained in the database.

skills.description: Use when you have computed thousands of per-gene statistics in parallel (e.g., a Pearson correlation p-value for every gene vs. a marker gene like VIM) and must select a FDR-controlled gene set before overlap or enrichment testing.
skills.name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction Use when you have computed thousands of per-gene statistics in parallel (e.g., a Pearson correlation p-value for every gene vs. a marker gene like VIM) and must select a FDR-controlled gene set before overlap or enrichment testing. You are testing a single pre-specified hypothesis (no family of thousands of parallel tests), so correction is unnecessary. The statistic is not a p-value (e.g., raw fold-changes or correlation coefficients without assigned p-values); compute p-values first. Your downstream test already internally controls family-wise error (e.g., an enrichment tool that estimates its own null), making a second correction layer inappropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to per-gene statistics (e.g., Pearson correlation p-values against VIM across TCGA AML samples) computed in a python3 workflow, converting raw p-values into q-values so that only genes passing a strict significance threshold (q < 0.001) are carried forward as a gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to per-gene statistics (e.g., Pearson correlation p-values against VIM across TCGA AML samples) computed in a python3 workflow, converting raw p-values into q-values so that only genes passing a strict significance threshold (q < 0.001) are carried forward as a gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are testing a single pre-specified hypothesis (no family of thousands of parallel tests), so correction is unnecessary. The statistic is not a p-value (e.g., raw fold-changes or correlation coefficients without assigned p-values); compute p-values first. Your downstream test already internally controls family-wise error (e.g., an enrichment tool that estimates its own null), making a second correction layer inappropriate.

skills.description: Use when many topics/features are tested per contrast (e.g. scETM topic abundance across disease vs control or cell types) and a family-wise-error-controlled significance call is needed.
skills.name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction Use when many topics/features are tested per contrast (e.g. scETM topic abundance across disease vs control or cell types) and a family-wise-error-controlled significance call is needed. When the goal is controlling the false discovery rate rather than family-wise error (Bonferroni is the most conservative choice and may miss weaker but real topics) When only one hypothesis is tested per contrast, where no correction is needed When corrected tests span multiple different contrasts that should each have their own family of hypotheses (correction is applied over all tested topics within each contrast, not pooled across contrasts) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A conservative multiple-testing correction applied to per-topic permutation p-values in scETM differential topic-abundance analysis, so that significantly differential topics (e.g. AD topics 12 and 58) are called within each tested contrast. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: A conservative multiple-testing correction applied to per-topic permutation p-values in scETM differential topic-abundance analysis, so that significantly differential topics (e.g. AD topics 12 and 58) are called within each tested contrast.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is controlling the false discovery rate rather than family-wise error (Bonferroni is the most conservative choice and may miss weaker but real topics) When only one hypothesis is tested per contrast, where no correction is needed When corrected tests span multiple different contrasts that should each have their own family of hypotheses (correction is applied over all tested topics within each contrast, not pooled across contrasts)

skills.description: Use when calling significant hits across thousands of parallel gene-level tests (DGE or DUL) in scRNA-seq pseudobulk comparisons, or when testing set overlaps (chi-square independence) where unadjusted p-values would inflate false positives.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when calling significant hits across thousands of parallel gene-level tests (DGE or DUL) in scRNA-seq pseudobulk comparisons, or when testing set overlaps (chi-square independence) where unadjusted p-values would inflate false positives. When only a small predefined number of hypotheses is tested (e.g., a single gene of interest), where an FDR correction over thousands of tests is unnecessary and over-conservative When the goal is exploratory ranking of genes by raw effect size rather than defining significant hit sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistical practice of correcting p-values for many simultaneous hypothesis tests (e.g., thousands of genes tested per cell-type pair), so that significant hits are called at a controlled false-discovery rate rather than by raw p-value cutoffs. In this workflow it is applied to both differential gene expression (Welch t-tests) and differential 3'UTR usage (scUTRboot WUI tests) before downstream overlap analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Statistical practice of correcting p-values for many simultaneous hypothesis tests (e.g., thousands of genes tested per cell-type pair), so that significant hits are called at a controlled false-discovery rate rather than by raw p-value cutoffs. In this workflow it is applied to both differential gene expression (Welch t-tests) and differential 3'UTR usage (scUTRboot WUI tests) before downstream overlap analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a small predefined number of hypotheses is tested (e.g., a single gene of interest), where an FDR correction over thousands of tests is unnecessary and over-conservative When the goal is exploratory ranking of genes by raw effect size rather than defining significant hit sets

skills.description: Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously (e.g., normal-vs-cancer DESeq2 tests on KIRC, LIHC, PRAD TCGA count matrices) and raw p-values must be converted into adjusted p-values before thresholding DE gene sets.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously (e.g., normal-vs-cancer DESeq2 tests on KIRC, LIHC, PRAD TCGA count matrices) and raw p-values must be converted into adjusted p-values before thresholding DE gene sets. The tests are not simultaneous genome/transcriptome-wide tests (e.g., a single pre-specified gene set) where FDR correction is overly conservative The downstream consumer requires family-wise error rate control (e.g., Bonferroni) rather than FDR control, or the effect-size criterion |log2FC| > 2.0 is inappropriate for the biology of the comparison Input expression data are already normalized and significance-tested (e.g., an existing DE results table with padj) — correction would double-adjust the values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Controls the false discovery rate when selecting thousands of genes (and miRNAs) from differential expression tests, using the Benjamini-Hochberg method so that DE genes are called at adjusted p-value < 0.05 combined with a |log2 fold change| > 2.0 cutoff. In the GeneNetFusion pipeline this corrected selection defines the differential-expression baseline signature per TCGA cancer type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Controls the false discovery rate when selecting thousands of genes (and miRNAs) from differential expression tests, using the Benjamini-Hochberg method so that DE genes are called at adjusted p-value < 0.05 combined with a |log2 fold change| > 2.0 cutoff. In the GeneNetFusion pipeline this corrected selection defines the differential-expression baseline signature per TCGA cancer type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tests are not simultaneous genome/transcriptome-wide tests (e.g., a single pre-specified gene set) where FDR correction is overly conservative The downstream consumer requires family-wise error rate control (e.g., Bonferroni) rather than FDR control, or the effect-size criterion |log2FC| > 2.0 is inappropriate for the biology of the comparison Input expression data are already normalized and significance-tested (e.g., an existing DE results table with padj) — correction would double-adjust the values

skills.description: Use when performing many parallel statistical tests (e.g., one t test per feature across a multi-feature matrix) and you need adjusted p-values to identify which features genuinely differ between groups.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when performing many parallel statistical tests (e.g., one t test per feature across a multi-feature matrix) and you need adjusted p-values to identify which features genuinely differ between groups. skills.search_text: multiscale-cnv-call-harmonization Use when CaSpER (runCaSpER, method="iterative") has produced CNV calls from multiple smoothed expression scales paired with BAF shift evidence, and you must collapse N×M scale-wise calls into a single consistent set of chromosome-arm, segment, or gene-level CNV calls. 3′-only sequencing data (e.g., DropSeq) where the BAF shift signal is sparse because variants are measured only near gene 3′ ends — the BAF-evidence gating of HMM states 2/4 will be unreliable Inputs lacking any BAF/allelic shift signal (expression-only matrices), since the harmonization relies on BAF-shift confirmation of intermediate HMM states Single-sample analyses needing no consensus, where only one scale is used and there is no N×M pairwise comparison to harmonize http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Harmonize and summarize CNV calls that CaSpER produces from N×M pairwise comparisons of multi-scale smoothed expression signals and BAF shift signals, yielding consistent chromosome-arm, segment-level, and gene-level copy-number calls from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Harmonize and summarize CNV calls that CaSpER produces from N×M pairwise comparisons of multi-scale smoothed expression signals and BAF shift signals, yielding consistent chromosome-arm, segment-level, and gene-level copy-number calls from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq.
skills.when_to_use_negative: 3′-only sequencing data (e.g., DropSeq) where the BAF shift signal is sparse because variants are measured only near gene 3′ ends — the BAF-evidence gating of HMM states 2/4 will be unreliable Inputs lacking any BAF/allelic shift signal (expression-only matrices), since the harmonization relies on BAF-shift confirmation of intermediate HMM states Single-sample analyses needing no consensus, where only one scale is used and there is no N×M pairwise comparison to harmonize

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be decomposed into attractor basins and transition cells via stochastic dynamics — e.g., recovering EMT epithelial/mesenchymal/hybrid states or bifurcating iPSC lineages from a processed gene expression matrix.
skills.name: multiscale-coarse-graining-attractor-identification
skills.search_text: multiscale-coarse-graining-attractor-identification Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be decomposed into attractor basins and transition cells via stochastic dynamics — e.g., recovering EMT epithelial/mesenchymal/hybrid states or bifurcating iPSC lineages from a processed gene expression matrix. The dataset has very few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where transition-cell identification requires special care and confirmation The goal is static clustering of distinct states only — high-accuracy clusterers like SC3 or SIMLR enforce distinct states and do not model transient cells Root cell state detection via RNA velocity or entropy methods is required, which MuTrans does not currently integrate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs MuTrans' multi-scale analysis of the cell-cell random-walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) to coarse-grain single-cell transcriptome dynamics into K attractor basins with soft cell membership, recovering meta-stable states and transition cells. Validated on EMT (Smart-Seq2, K=5) and iPSC induction (single-cell RT-qPCR, K=9) datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Runs MuTrans' multi-scale analysis of the cell-cell random-walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) to coarse-grain single-cell transcriptome dynamics into K attractor basins with soft cell membership, recovering meta-stable states and transition cells. Validated on EMT (Smart-Seq2, K=5) and iPSC induction (single-cell RT-qPCR, K=9) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has very few cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 dataset), where transition-cell identification requires special care and confirmation The goal is static clustering of distinct states only — high-accuracy clusterers like SC3 or SIMLR enforce distinct states and do not model transient cells Root cell state detection via RNA velocity or entropy methods is required, which MuTrans does not currently integrate

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data (e.g., an Anndata object or N_cells x N_genes expression matrix) must be dissected into meta-stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells via stochastic dynamics rather than hard clustering.
skills.name: multiscale-coarse-graining-of-stochastic-dynamics
skills.search_text: multiscale-coarse-graining-of-stochastic-dynamics Use when single-cell transcriptome data (e.g., an Anndata object or N_cells x N_genes expression matrix) must be dissected into meta-stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells via stochastic dynamics rather than hard clustering. When a static clustering/pseudo-time result suffices and transition cells need not be separated — methods like SC3, SIMLR, DPT, Slingshot, Monocle enforce distinct cell states or orderings without identifying transient cells When the dataset has very few cells (e.g., the small myelopoiesis dataset), since high-resolution transition-cell identification requires a sufficiently large cell number When non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or proliferation dynamics dominate, which the current method does not consider http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Multi-scale reduction of the cell-cell scale random-walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) as implemented in MuTrans, which coarse-grains stochastic dynamics to recover attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities, and per-cell soft membership rho*(x) on a cell-fate dynamical manifold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Multi-scale reduction of the cell-cell scale random-walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) as implemented in MuTrans, which coarse-grains stochastic dynamics to recover attractor basins, coarse-grained transition probabilities, and per-cell soft membership rho*(x) on a cell-fate dynamical manifold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a static clustering/pseudo-time result suffices and transition cells need not be separated — methods like SC3, SIMLR, DPT, Slingshot, Monocle enforce distinct cell states or orderings without identifying transient cells When the dataset has very few cells (e.g., the small myelopoiesis dataset), since high-resolution transition-cell identification requires a sufficiently large cell number When non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or proliferation dynamics dominate, which the current method does not consider

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample RNA-seq matrix (e.g. TCGA-GBM bulk or single-cell GBM) and need to detect both focal CNVs (e.g. PDGFRA amplification) and large-scale chromosome-arm events from expression alone.
skills.name: multiscale-expression-signal-smoothing
skills.search_text: multiscale-expression-signal-smoothing Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample RNA-seq matrix (e.g. TCGA-GBM bulk or single-cell GBM) and need to detect both focal CNVs (e.g. PDGFRA amplification) and large-scale chromosome-arm events from expression alone. You only need transcriptomic analysis (differential expression, clustering) without probing the CNV landscape — multiscale smoothing is specific to CNV event recovery You require an exact ground-truth SNV/heterozygous variant call set workflow — CaSpER deliberately avoids needing a high-quality heterozygous variant call set, so tools built around such call sets are a different fit Data are 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted because shifts are measured only for variants near 3' ends of genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 A signal-processing skill from CaSpER that smooths genome-wide RNA-seq expression signals at multiple scales (median/mean filtering) so that focal CNV events are recovered at small scales and broad arm-level CNV events at larger scales, prior to HMM segmentation and CNV calling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: A signal-processing skill from CaSpER that smooths genome-wide RNA-seq expression signals at multiple scales (median/mean filtering) so that focal CNV events are recovered at small scales and broad arm-level CNV events at larger scales, prior to HMM segmentation and CNV calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need transcriptomic analysis (differential expression, clustering) without probing the CNV landscape — multiscale smoothing is specific to CNV event recovery You require an exact ground-truth SNV/heterozygous variant call set workflow — CaSpER deliberately avoids needing a high-quality heterozygous variant call set, so tools built around such call sets are a different fit Data are 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted because shifts are measured only for variants near 3' ends of genes

skills.description: Use when you have mapped RNA-seq BAM files and need an allelic shift (BAF/LOH) signal profile to correct or integrate with expression-based CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous variant call set.
skills.name: multiscale-median-filtering-of-allelic-signals
skills.search_text: multiscale-median-filtering-of-allelic-signals Use when you have mapped RNA-seq BAM files and need an allelic shift (BAF/LOH) signal profile to correct or integrate with expression-based CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous variant call set. 3′-only sequencing data (e.g. DropSeq-style 3′ assays): the BAF shift signal may be adversely impacted because BAF shift will be measured for only variants close to the 3′ ends of genes You already have a high-quality heterozygous variant call set or SNV VCFs and need direct genotyping rather than BAF-shift estimation from reads alone Your aligner's MAPQ scale makes a minimum mapping quality of 50 filter out all reads — recalibrate the MAPQ cutoff before pileup generation http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Generate a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signal directly from mapped RNA-seq reads with BAFExtract, then smooth it with recursive per-chromosome median filtering across multiple scales (loh.scale=3) so allelic shift (LOH) information can be integrated with expression-based CNV calling in CaSpER. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Generate a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signal directly from mapped RNA-seq reads with BAFExtract, then smooth it with recursive per-chromosome median filtering across multiple scales (loh.scale=3) so allelic shift (LOH) information can be integrated with expression-based CNV calling in CaSpER.
skills.when_to_use_negative: 3′-only sequencing data (e.g. DropSeq-style 3′ assays): the BAF shift signal may be adversely impacted because BAF shift will be measured for only variants close to the 3′ ends of genes You already have a high-quality heterozygous variant call set or SNV VCFs and need direct genotyping rather than BAF-shift estimation from reads alone Your aligner's MAPQ scale makes a minimum mapping quality of 50 filter out all reads — recalibrate the MAPQ cutoff before pileup generation

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq or similar dataset has many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes, and a global marker set is needed that discriminates every phenotype pair at least K times.
skills.name: multiset-multicover-approximation
skills.search_text: multiset-multicover-approximation Use when a scRNA-seq or similar dataset has many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes, and a global marker set is needed that discriminates every phenotype pair at least K times. When only a small number of distinct groups is present and standard per-group differential-expression marker selection suffices (the paper notes DE-based selection breaks down with many groups with overlapping DE genes) When a provably optimal minimum marker set is required — G-PC is a polynomial-time approximation and does not provide an optimal solution When the goal is all-relevant feature identification rather than a minimal-optimal discriminative subset (e.g., Boruta-style tasks) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Approximates the phenotype cover (PC) marker-selection problem — shown to be equivalent to the NP-complete multiset multicover problem — using polynomial-time algorithms: G-PC (extended greedy set cover) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy method), to select a small feature set that distinguishes every phenotype pair to a desired coverage K. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Approximates the phenotype cover (PC) marker-selection problem — shown to be equivalent to the NP-complete multiset multicover problem — using polynomial-time algorithms: G-PC (extended greedy set cover) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy method), to select a small feature set that distinguishes every phenotype pair to a desired coverage K.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a small number of distinct groups is present and standard per-group differential-expression marker selection suffices (the paper notes DE-based selection breaks down with many groups with overlapping DE genes) When a provably optimal minimum marker set is required — G-PC is a polynomial-time approximation and does not provide an optimal solution When the goal is all-relevant feature identification rather than a minimal-optimal discriminative subset (e.g., Boruta-style tasks)

skills.description: Use when computing pairwise ligand-receptor communication scores between cell populations from scRNAseq, bulk RNAseq, microarray, or spatial transcriptomic profiles in which ligands or receptors (e.g. checkpoint, chemokine, cytokine complexes) have multiple subunits requiring co-expression logic.
skills.name: multisubunit-complex-coexpression-logic
skills.search_text: multisubunit-complex-coexpression-logic Use when computing pairwise ligand-receptor communication scores between cell populations from scRNAseq, bulk RNAseq, microarray, or spatial transcriptomic profiles in which ligands or receptors (e.g. checkpoint, chemokine, cytokine complexes) have multiple subunits requiring co-expression logic. The input already contains pre-computed interaction scores or a feature table that bypasses expression-level scoring The study requires non-human ligand-receptor curation — the ICELLNET database is curated exclusively from human studies Downstream intracellular signaling effectors must be modeled; the paper states downstream effectors were deliberately not integrated in ICELLNET http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ICEllNET's rule set for scoring ligand-receptor communication from transcriptomic profiles while enforcing logical co-expression of the multiple protein subunits that make up multimeric ligand and receptor complexes, so that non-functional partial expression of a complex contributes nothing to the communication score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: ICEllNET's rule set for scoring ligand-receptor communication from transcriptomic profiles while enforcing logical co-expression of the multiple protein subunits that make up multimeric ligand and receptor complexes, so that non-functional partial expression of a complex contributes nothing to the communication score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input already contains pre-computed interaction scores or a feature table that bypasses expression-level scoring The study requires non-human ligand-receptor curation — the ICELLNET database is curated exclusively from human studies Downstream intracellular signaling effectors must be modeled; the paper states downstream effectors were deliberately not integrated in ICELLNET

skills.description: Use when computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities with CellChatDB and a ligand or receptor in the interaction is annotated as a multi-subunit complex whose subunits each have per-cell-group expression values.
skills.name: multisubunit-complex-geometric-mean-aggregation
skills.search_text: multisubunit-complex-geometric-mean-aggregation Use when computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities with CellChatDB and a ligand or receptor in the interaction is annotated as a multi-subunit complex whose subunits each have per-cell-group expression values. The interaction involves only single-gene ligands and single-chain receptors with no heteromeric annotation in CellChatDB — no aggregation is needed Analyzing secreted signaling described only at pathway level (computeCommunProbPathway aggregation), where per-subunit complex composition is not the target quantity The expression matrix is raw counts without per-cell-group normalization; trimean aggregation on unnormalized counts will not match CellChat's probabilities http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 CellChat represents multi-subunit ligand and receptor heteromeric complexes by aggregating the expression of their subunit genes via a geometric mean, so that complex-level abundance feeds the law-of-mass-action communication probability model rather than a single-gene proxy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: CellChat represents multi-subunit ligand and receptor heteromeric complexes by aggregating the expression of their subunit genes via a geometric mean, so that complex-level abundance feeds the law-of-mass-action communication probability model rather than a single-gene proxy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The interaction involves only single-gene ligands and single-chain receptors with no heteromeric annotation in CellChatDB — no aggregation is needed Analyzing secreted signaling described only at pathway level (computeCommunProbPathway aggregation), where per-subunit complex composition is not the target quantity The expression matrix is raw counts without per-cell-group normalization; trimean aggregation on unnormalized counts will not match CellChat's probabilities

skills.description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ reads that require combinatorial barcode/UMI identification and the serial BLAST-based original method is too slow or CPU-bound; especially when runtime must be under 10% of the original.
skills.name: multithreaded-fastq-preprocessing
skills.search_text: multithreaded-fastq-preprocessing Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ reads that require combinatorial barcode/UMI identification and the serial BLAST-based original method is too slow or CPU-bound; especially when runtime must be under 10% of the original. The data are not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcode single-cell reads — fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data; other platforms are stated as potential future support, not yet available Barcodes are too short for a general aligner such as BWA (8 bp) and the task is generic alignment rather than SPLiT-seq barcode/UMI identification Tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel is required — SCSit's default setting restricts to one mismatch and one indel; loosening yields only 4–5% more identified reads at 20–40% more runtime (Table S4) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Speed up preprocessing of paired-end SPLiT-seq FASTQ data by running SCSit, a C program that identifies the three rounds of combinatorial barcodes and UMI directly with multithreaded parallel processing, instead of serial single-core BLAST (blastn-short) alignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Speed up preprocessing of paired-end SPLiT-seq FASTQ data by running SCSit, a C program that identifies the three rounds of combinatorial barcodes and UMI directly with multithreaded parallel processing, instead of serial single-core BLAST (blastn-short) alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcode single-cell reads — fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data; other platforms are stated as potential future support, not yet available Barcodes are too short for a general aligner such as BWA (8 bp) and the task is generic alignment rather than SPLiT-seq barcode/UMI identification Tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel is required — SCSit's default setting restricts to one mismatch and one indel; loosening yields only 4–5% more identified reads at 20–40% more runtime (Table S4)

skills.description: Use when ranked gene sets (e.g., IC genes from fused co-expression networks) must be validated against patient survival endpoints, comparing their Cox hazard ratios and Concordance statistics to a DE-gene baseline.
skills.name: multivariate-cox-model-concordance-evaluation
skills.search_text: multivariate-cox-model-concordance-evaluation Use when ranked gene sets (e.g., IC genes from fused co-expression networks) must be validated against patient survival endpoints, comparing their Cox hazard ratios and Concordance statistics to a DE-gene baseline. No patient survival metadata (vital status, days to death/follow-up) is available for the cohort. skills.summary: Prognostic evaluation of fused-network-derived IC genes against DESeq2-derived DE genes using univariate and multivariate Cox proportional-hazards models on TCGA KIRC, LIHC and PRAD patients, comparing Concordance statistics to show IC genes better fit patient overall survival.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is normal/cancer classification or network construction (use the repository's extraction_classification.py / Pipeline.ipynb workflow instead of survival modelling). No patient survival metadata (vital status, days to death/follow-up) is available for the cohort. Gene lists are not derived from fused co-expression networks or a comparable ranked signature and no DE baseline exists for fair comparison.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify randomness of expression covariation between candidate regulatory factors (TFs and chromatin-state modifiers) across cells of a multipotent population, e.g. to detect priming toward a lineage in scRNA-Seq data.
skills.name: multivariate-gaussian-entropy-estimation
skills.search_text: multivariate-gaussian-entropy-estimation Use when you need to quantify randomness of expression covariation between candidate regulatory factors (TFs and chromatin-state modifiers) across cells of a multipotent population, e.g. to detect priming toward a lineage in scRNA-Seq data. The goal is inferring cell-fate probabilities or trajectory/pseudotime rather than quantifying covariation entropy in a snapshot multipotent population — use a trajectory algorithm such as Palantir instead. The input is scATAC-Seq peak/accessibility data rather than scRNA-Seq expression covariation; the DICE metric as described is applied to log-normalized scRNA-Seq matrices. The candidate RF set has not been filtered (e.g. by frequency of expression in the MPP population via FindCandidateFactors / type1fth='Mean'), so the dCov matrix would be dominated by sparsely expressed factors. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Estimate the entropy of expression covariation among regulatory factors as a multivariate Gaussian entropy H = 0.5 * sum(log(eigenvalues)) of a double-centered distance covariance (dCov) matrix — the core DICE metric for quantifying priming in multipotent cell populations from scRNA-Seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Estimate the entropy of expression covariation among regulatory factors as a multivariate Gaussian entropy H = 0.5 * sum(log(eigenvalues)) of a double-centered distance covariance (dCov) matrix — the core DICE metric for quantifying priming in multipotent cell populations from scRNA-Seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inferring cell-fate probabilities or trajectory/pseudotime rather than quantifying covariation entropy in a snapshot multipotent population — use a trajectory algorithm such as Palantir instead. The input is scATAC-Seq peak/accessibility data rather than scRNA-Seq expression covariation; the DICE metric as described is applied to log-normalized scRNA-Seq matrices. The candidate RF set has not been filtered (e.g. by frequency of expression in the MPP population via FindCandidateFactors / type1fth='Mean'), so the dCov matrix would be dominated by sparsely expressed factors.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq transcript expression (transcript usage ratios) and genotypes from the same individuals are available and the goal is to identify genetic variants affecting alternative splicing genome-wide, e.g. GTEx V7 tissue-by-tissue sQTL catalogs.
skills.name: multivariate-sqtl-mapping
skills.search_text: multivariate-sqtl-mapping Use when RNA-seq transcript expression (transcript usage ratios) and genotypes from the same individuals are available and the goal is to identify genetic variants affecting alternative splicing genome-wide, e.g. GTEx V7 tissue-by-tissue sQTL catalogs. The aim is univariate splicing-event QTL mapping (e.g. intron excision ratios from LeafCutter) rather than testing multivariate shifts in a gene's transcript isoform proportions Only gene-level expression is available with no transcript-level expression file (trId/geneId), so splicing ratios cannot be computed The goal is annotating coding variant consequences (LoF/splice-site effects), which is the role of tools like LOFTEE, not sQTL mapping http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Map splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTLs) by testing variants against a vector of transcript isoform relative abundances per gene, using sQTLseekeR2 via the sqtlseeker2-nf Nextflow/Docker pipeline, rather than treating each splicing event as a univariate phenotype. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Map splicing quantitative trait loci (sQTLs) by testing variants against a vector of transcript isoform relative abundances per gene, using sQTLseekeR2 via the sqtlseeker2-nf Nextflow/Docker pipeline, rather than treating each splicing event as a univariate phenotype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The aim is univariate splicing-event QTL mapping (e.g. intron excision ratios from LeafCutter) rather than testing multivariate shifts in a gene's transcript isoform proportions Only gene-level expression is available with no transcript-level expression file (trId/geneId), so splicing ratios cannot be computed The goal is annotating coding variant consequences (LoF/splice-site effects), which is the role of tools like LOFTEE, not sQTL mapping

skills.description: Use when you must segment a chromosome-ordered smoothed scRNA-seq expression matrix into copy number regions, exploiting shared breakpoints across cells/clones via multichannel Mumford–Shah minimization.
skills.name: mumford-shah-piecewise-constant-optimization
skills.search_text: mumford-shah-piecewise-constant-optimization Use when you must segment a chromosome-ordered smoothed scRNA-seq expression matrix into copy number regions, exploiting shared breakpoints across cells/clones via multichannel Mumford–Shah minimization. Tumors with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemias, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based segmentation assumption is unsuited Unsorted gene expression matrices without genomic coordinate annotation, since the algorithm merges only adjacent regions along the genome Normal/tumor classification only, with no need for clonal copy number segmentation http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Greedy piecewise-constant minimization of the Mumford–Shah energy from Computer Vision, used in SCEVAN as the joint multichannel segmentation step that converts the smoothed per-cell expression matrix into a copy number matrix with shared breakpoints across clonal subpopulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Greedy piecewise-constant minimization of the Mumford–Shah energy from Computer Vision, used in SCEVAN as the joint multichannel segmentation step that converts the smoothed per-cell expression matrix into a copy number matrix with shared breakpoints across clonal subpopulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tumors with minimal genomic alterations (e.g. leukemias, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas), where the aneuploidy-based segmentation assumption is unsuited Unsorted gene expression matrices without genomic coordinate annotation, since the algorithm merges only adjacent regions along the genome Normal/tumor classification only, with no need for clonal copy number segmentation

skills.description: Use when a per-cell somatic SNV genotype matrix from 10x scRNA-seq data must be summarized into per-variant mutation frequencies and benchmarked against bulk VAFs (eWGS or RNA-seq) to assess single-cell detection sensitivity.
skills.name: mutant-cell-fraction-estimation
skills.search_text: mutant-cell-fraction-estimation Use when a per-cell somatic SNV genotype matrix from 10x scRNA-seq data must be summarized into per-variant mutation frequencies and benchmarked against bulk VAFs (eWGS or RNA-seq) to assess single-cell detection sensitivity. When no eWGS or bulk RNA-seq VAF calls exist for the same variants, since the correlation-based validation cannot be performed When the goal is de novo variant calling from scRNA-seq data — VarTrix and cb_sniffer require pre-called variant sets and noise from reverse transcription makes RNA-seq variant calling error-prone When variants lie outside regions covered by end-biased 10x Chromium transcripts, since coverage drops non-linearly across transcript length and detection is unreliable there http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Compute read-based and cell-based mutation detection metrics — single-cell VAF (scVAF), Mutant Cell Fraction (MCF), and Mutant Cell Detection Rate (MCDR) — from a per-cell scRNA-seq genotype matrix and validate them by Pearson correlation against eWGS and bulk RNA-seq variant allele fractions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Compute read-based and cell-based mutation detection metrics — single-cell VAF (scVAF), Mutant Cell Fraction (MCF), and Mutant Cell Detection Rate (MCDR) — from a per-cell scRNA-seq genotype matrix and validate them by Pearson correlation against eWGS and bulk RNA-seq variant allele fractions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no eWGS or bulk RNA-seq VAF calls exist for the same variants, since the correlation-based validation cannot be performed When the goal is de novo variant calling from scRNA-seq data — VarTrix and cb_sniffer require pre-called variant sets and noise from reverse transcription makes RNA-seq variant calling error-prone When variants lie outside regions covered by end-biased 10x Chromium transcripts, since coverage drops non-linearly across transcript length and detection is unreliable there

skills.name: mutant-cell-overlay-on-cluster-space

skills.summary: Overlays cells genotyped as expressing a somatic mutation (e.g. GATA2R361C) as a binary/graded label onto the t-SNE/cluster space of the full sample and computes a local mutant-cell density per cell, enabling genotype-to-phenotype association for non-genotyped cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-cell genotype certainty: dropout makes it impossible to call a cell truly wild-type, so treat unmutated labels as 'not detected' rather than confirmed wild-type Mutations lie in transcript regions with poor coverage on end-biased Chromium platforms, where detection sensitivity is limited and the overlay label will be sparse The sample's tumor type is a low-mutation-burden cancer like AML where few expressed SNVs are available to define a subclone

skills.description: Use when you need to estimate the fraction of mutant gRNA molecules in a CROP-seq/gRNA library BAM after consensus filtering that removes sequencing-error UMIs (min_reads threshold), to profile library quality or mutation-aware gRNA annotation.

skills.search_text: mutant-grna-fraction-quantification Use when you need to estimate the fraction of mutant gRNA molecules in a CROP-seq/gRNA library BAM after consensus filtering that removes sequencing-error UMIs (min_reads threshold), to profile library quality or mutation-aware gRNA annotation. You only need cell-level gRNA-to-cell assignment counts — use assign_gRNA.assign_gRNA_to_cell with min_umi (default 3) instead of molecule-level mutant fraction quantification. Your goal is detecting CRISPR-Cas9 editing effects in the transcriptome (cutsite-spanning deletions), a separate GiRAFR analysis mode. You want to detect mutations in raw reads without consensus/error filtering — that inflates the mutant fraction with sequencing errors that min_reads=2 is designed to remove. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Quantifies the fraction of mutant gRNA molecules in a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library that remain after UMI consensus-sequence filtering (min_reads=2), using GiRAFR's bam filtering, consensus-sequence construction, and variant-calling modules. skills.description: Use when VEP-annotated somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g. from GATK Mutect2) must be converted into amino-acid-level mutant peptide sequences for downstream neoantigen prediction.
skills.name: mutant-peptide-extraction-from-variants
skills.search_text: mutant-peptide-extraction-from-variants Use when VEP-annotated somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g. from GATK Mutect2) must be converted into amino-acid-level mutant peptide sequences for downstream neoantigen prediction. Mutations come from gene fusions or RNA-Seq-only analyses — TSNAD v2.0 handles fusion-derived neoantigens via STAR/Arriba in a separate module, not via this SNV/INDEL peptide extraction. Genes carrying the mutations are not expressed (TPM < 1) — the expression filter from module 4 removes neoantigens from unexpressed genes before prediction is useful. A standalone MHC-I binding predictor is needed without immunogenicity scoring — DeepHLApan replaced NetMHCpan specifically to add immunogenicity; NetMHCpan is no longer used in this pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Converts VEP-annotated SNV/INDEL calls into a list of mutant peptides spanning each mutation, with peptide lengths from 8 to 11 amino acids, to feed pMHC binding/immunogenicity prediction (DeepHLApan in TSNAD v2.0). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Converts VEP-annotated SNV/INDEL calls into a list of mutant peptides spanning each mutation, with peptide lengths from 8 to 11 amino acids, to feed pMHC binding/immunogenicity prediction (DeepHLApan in TSNAD v2.0).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mutations come from gene fusions or RNA-Seq-only analyses — TSNAD v2.0 handles fusion-derived neoantigens via STAR/Arriba in a separate module, not via this SNV/INDEL peptide extraction. Genes carrying the mutations are not expressed (TPM < 1) — the expression filter from module 4 removes neoantigens from unexpressed genes before prediction is useful. A standalone MHC-I binding predictor is needed without immunogenicity scoring — DeepHLApan replaced NetMHCpan specifically to add immunogenicity; NetMHCpan is no longer used in this pipeline.

skills.search_text: mutation-aware-grna-annotation-classification Use when analyzing CROP-seq / single-cell CRISPR screen data where gRNAs must be assigned to cell barcodes in a mutation-aware manner, e.g. to verify that spacer- or scaffold-mutant gRNAs are dysfunctional rather than mislabeled as intact. skills.summary: Mutation-aware assignment of intact vs mutant (spacer- or scaffold-mutant) gRNAs to single-cell CRISPR screen cells using GiRAFR, followed by functional validation that mutant gRNAs fail to downregulate their target genes via Welch t-tests on expression counts.

skills.description: Use when analyzing CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library alignments (BAM) where mutant gRNAs need to be detected and assigned to cells, e.g. quantifying cells lacking a gRNA call under standard feature barcoding pipelines.
skills.name: mutation-aware-grna-variant-calling
skills.search_text: mutation-aware-grna-variant-calling Use when analyzing CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library alignments (BAM) where mutant gRNAs need to be detected and assigned to cells, e.g. quantifying cells lacking a gRNA call under standard feature barcoding pipelines. The goal is detecting CRISPR-Cas9 editing effects in transcriptome data — GiRAFR exposes this in a separate analysis mode (gRNA_mutation mode is for gRNA library mutation profiling) Cell barcodes have not been corrected/produced by Cell Ranger, so the filtered_barcode input cannot be supplied Only intact gRNA identity per cell is needed and mutation-awareness is irrelevant — a simpler Cell Ranger feature-counting approach may suffice, at the cost of missing mutant gRNAs http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Calling intact and mutant gRNA sequences in single-cell CRISPR screens by building per-UMI consensus sequences from the gRNA library BAM and comparing them to the designed oligo pool reference, then assigning gRNAs to cells with a mutation-aware UMI threshold. This catches mutant gRNAs that Cell Ranger feature barcoding misses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Calling intact and mutant gRNA sequences in single-cell CRISPR screens by building per-UMI consensus sequences from the gRNA library BAM and comparing them to the designed oligo pool reference, then assigning gRNAs to cells with a mutation-aware UMI threshold. This catches mutant gRNAs that Cell Ranger feature barcoding misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting CRISPR-Cas9 editing effects in transcriptome data — GiRAFR exposes this in a separate analysis mode (gRNA_mutation mode is for gRNA library mutation profiling) Cell barcodes have not been corrected/produced by Cell Ranger, so the filtered_barcode input cannot be supplied Only intact gRNA identity per cell is needed and mutation-awareness is irrelevant — a simpler Cell Ranger feature-counting approach may suffice, at the cost of missing mutant gRNAs

skills.description: Use when you have GDSC IC50 drug-sensitivity data plus cell-line mutation calls and gene expression, and you want to know whether pathway activity scores stratify drug response within mutant or wild-type sub-populations.
skills.name: mutation-based-cell-line-stratification
skills.search_text: mutation-based-cell-line-stratification Use when you have GDSC IC50 drug-sensitivity data plus cell-line mutation calls and gene expression, and you want to know whether pathway activity scores stratify drug response within mutant or wild-type sub-populations. Data are mouse or non-human cell lines without confirming PROGENy applicability (the package notes the original release was developed for human data) The question is only mutation-vs-drug association without expression data — no pathway scores can be computed Analysis targets primary tumors with tissue-matched normals for SPIA/Pathifier-style comparisons rather than GDSC cell-line drug response http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Stratify GDSC cancer cell lines by MAPK-pathway driver mutation status (BRAF/KRAS/NRAS) with TP53 tracked, then further partition each stratum by PROGENy MAPK pathway-score quartile to test whether expression-derived pathway activity adds drug-sensitivity resolution beyond mutation calls alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Stratify GDSC cancer cell lines by MAPK-pathway driver mutation status (BRAF/KRAS/NRAS) with TP53 tracked, then further partition each stratum by PROGENy MAPK pathway-score quartile to test whether expression-derived pathway activity adds drug-sensitivity resolution beyond mutation calls alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are mouse or non-human cell lines without confirming PROGENy applicability (the package notes the original release was developed for human data) The question is only mutation-vs-drug association without expression data — no pathway scores can be computed Analysis targets primary tumors with tissue-matched normals for SPIA/Pathifier-style comparisons rather than GDSC cell-line drug response

Samples have not been assigned CMS subtypes by CMScaller — subtype-comparison tests require per-sample predictions as the grouping variable Data are single-cell RNA-seq or primary tumor biopsies with human stromal content, where CMScaller predictions are not recommended The dataset is small (fewer than ~40 samples) where CMScaller's centered-and-scaled input introduces prediction uncertainty, weakening subtype grouping for burden tests http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compares genomic alteration burden (total mutation counts, copy number aberration counts, BRAF mutation status) across CMScaller consensus molecular subtype groups in pre-clinical colorectal cancer models, using Mann-Whitney U and Fisher's exact tests in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x

skills.search_text: mutation-rate-parameter-sweep Use when validating lineage-reconstruction tools on real expression data paired with simulated barcodes, and you need robustness evidence across mutation rates (e.g., mu in 0.025/0.05/0.075) and dropout settings. You have real, experimentally acquired lineage barcodes of known diversity — sweep simulation parameters like mu only apply when barcodes are simulated on a known ground-truth tree The ground-truth lineage tree is unknown, since RF distance, Nye similarity, and CID all require comparing against a reference tree Evaluating a method on a single fixed mutation rate without robustness claims — the sweep's value is demonstrating consistent outperformance across rates and dropout conditions Benchmark lineage-reconstruction methods by simulating lineage barcodes on a known true tree (TedSim SimulateCIFs) while sweeping CRISPR mutation rates and dropout conditions, then scoring every reconstructed tree against ground truth with RF distance, Nye similarity, and CID. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Benchmark lineage-reconstruction methods by simulating lineage barcodes on a known true tree (TedSim SimulateCIFs) while sweeping CRISPR mutation rates and dropout conditions, then scoring every reconstructed tree against ground truth with RF distance, Nye similarity, and CID.

skills.description: Use when assigning reference mutational signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1 SBS1, SBS2, SBS5, SBS8, SBS9, SBS13, SBS18, SBS-MM1) to whole-genome or whole-exome SNV catalogs from hematological malignancies and deciding signature presence/absence without hard contribution thresholds.
skills.name: mutational-signature-fitting
skills.search_text: mutational-signature-fitting Use when assigning reference mutational signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1 SBS1, SBS2, SBS5, SBS8, SBS9, SBS13, SBS18, SBS-MM1) to whole-genome or whole-exome SNV catalogs from hematological malignancies and deciding signature presence/absence without hard contribution thresholds. Mutational catalogs from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases, which often yield too low mutational burdens for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting Fitting with a flat signature that mmsig may falsely remove because all its mutations can be re-classified to another signature at a relatively low cosine similarity threshold De novo signature extraction — this skill assumes a curated reference matrix; de novo extraction (e.g. NMF) is a separate preceding step http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit an input 96-channel SNV catalog against a fixed reference signature matrix (COSMIC v3.1) using mmsig's expectation-maximization fitting with dynamic cosine-similarity error suppression, bootstrapped 95% CIs, and transcriptional strand-bias testing to decide which signatures are truly present. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
