skills.name: mutual-information-network-inference
skills.search_text: mutual-information-network-inference Use when you have a raw or normalized RNA-Seq time-series count table (e.g., DREAM 4 100 genes x 21 samples, B. subtilis 3997 genes x 7 samples) and need a first-pass directed, signed GRN before TFBM/database refinement. Data are single-cell RNA-Seq — the article notes alternative tools (Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, Arboreto) are typically designed for scRNA-Seq, while Augusta targets bulk time-series count tables You need a fully refined network with verified interactions — MI-only inference must be followed by de novo TFBM discovery (MEME Suite) and curated database search (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) Only a single time point or non-time-series expression data are available — edge orientation/sign relies on the most significant difference among adjacent pairs of time points http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Augusta's core initial gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from RNA-Seq time-series count tables via pairwise mutual information (MI) with binning D = min(n/5, 10), edge direction/sign from the most significant difference (MSD) between adjacent time points, at O(mn²D²) complexity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Augusta's core initial gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from RNA-Seq time-series count tables via pairwise mutual information (MI) with binning D = min(n/5, 10), edge direction/sign from the most significant difference (MSD) between adjacent time points, at O(mn²D²) complexity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell RNA-Seq — the article notes alternative tools (Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, Arboreto) are typically designed for scRNA-Seq, while Augusta targets bulk time-series count tables You need a fully refined network with verified interactions — MI-only inference must be followed by de novo TFBM discovery (MEME Suite) and curated database search (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) Only a single time point or non-time-series expression data are available — edge orientation/sign relies on the most significant difference among adjacent pairs of time points

skills.description: Use when training a topic model/VAE on multi-batch scRNA-seq (or multiome) data where cell states are batch-confounded and ELBO-only training entangles predicted expression rates with technical effect estimates.
skills.name: mutual-information-regularized-training
skills.search_text: mutual-information-regularized-training Use when training a topic model/VAE on multi-batch scRNA-seq (or multiome) data where cell states are batch-confounded and ELBO-only training entangles predicted expression rates with technical effect estimates. Data come from a single batch with no technical covariates to encode — the disentanglement objective has nothing to regularize against The goal is de novo ChIP-seq peak calling (MACS is an unrelated tool surfaced in the same repositories) rather than multi-batch expression disentanglement Cell states are not batch-confounded and a standard integration method (scVI, Harmony, Seurat v3) is known to suffice — the authors position CODAL specifically for batch-confounded comparative atlases http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a CODAL topic-model VAE using an objective that augments the standard ELBO with a differentiable MINE mutual-information regularizer, explicitly disentangling technical (batch) effects from biological expression-rate effects in multi-batch single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Train a CODAL topic-model VAE using an objective that augments the standard ELBO with a differentiable MINE mutual-information regularizer, explicitly disentangling technical (batch) effects from biological expression-rate effects in multi-batch single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from a single batch with no technical covariates to encode — the disentanglement objective has nothing to regularize against The goal is de novo ChIP-seq peak calling (MACS is an unrelated tool surfaced in the same repositories) rather than multi-batch expression disentanglement Cell states are not batch-confounded and a standard integration method (scVI, Harmony, Seurat v3) is known to suffice — the authors position CODAL specifically for batch-confounded comparative atlases

skills.description: Use when extending cluster labels from an FFC-trained dataset to newly arriving (out-of-sample or streaming) test batches that show batch effects relative to the training data, prior to computing the joint affinity matrix.
skills.name: mutual-nearest-neighbor-batch-correction
skills.search_text: mutual-nearest-neighbor-batch-correction Use when extending cluster labels from an FFC-trained dataset to newly arriving (out-of-sample or streaming) test batches that show batch effects relative to the training data, prior to computing the joint affinity matrix. Training and testing data are already in the same batch condition — MNN correction is only needed to correct batch effects between training and testing data. Only a single in-sample cluster exists in the data — the article notes every data point can only receive one label in that case, and Monte Carlo validation cannot estimate uncertainty. High-dimensional raw input without nonlinear dimensionality reduction — the method should be performed with nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE) because it mimics a low-dimensional fire propagation process. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies mutual nearest neighbor (MNN) batch correction between a Forest Fire Clustering training dataset and incoming out-of-sample testing data, so that the joint affinity matrix used for online label propagation is computed on comparably aligned feature spaces. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Applies mutual nearest neighbor (MNN) batch correction between a Forest Fire Clustering training dataset and incoming out-of-sample testing data, so that the joint affinity matrix used for online label propagation is computed on comparably aligned feature spaces.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training and testing data are already in the same batch condition — MNN correction is only needed to correct batch effects between training and testing data. Only a single in-sample cluster exists in the data — the article notes every data point can only receive one label in that case, and Monte Carlo validation cannot estimate uncertainty. High-dimensional raw input without nonlinear dimensionality reduction — the method should be performed with nonlinear dimensionality reduction (e.g., UMAP, t-SNE, PHATE) because it mimics a low-dimensional fire propagation process.

skills.description: Use when combining scRNA-seq matrices from different batches (e.g., GSE70630 MGH53 & MGH54) and you need to detect which of the ~50 PCA subspaces carry batch effect before removal.
skills.name: mutual-nearest-neighbor-pair-identification
skills.search_text: mutual-nearest-neighbor-pair-identification Use when combining scRNA-seq matrices from different batches (e.g., GSE70630 MGH53 & MGH54) and you need to detect which of the ~50 PCA subspaces carry batch effect before removal. Data has not been quality-controlled (low-quality cells/genes not removed) — the README requires basic QC before BEER Input is gene-centric scaled data rather than raw counts (UMI, FPKM, RPKM, TPM, PKM), which BEER explicitly does not accept Cells of a given type exist in only one batch with no cross-batch analogues, so mutual nearest pairs cannot anchor correlation estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies mutual nearest (MN) cell pairs across batches within grouped cells, then scores each PCA subspace by rank and linear correlation of MN pair positions to flag sub-spaces with latent high batch effect, as implemented in BEER. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41421-019-0114-x
skills.summary: Identifies mutual nearest (MN) cell pairs across batches within grouped cells, then scores each PCA subspace by rank and linear correlation of MN pair positions to flag sub-spaces with latent high batch effect, as implemented in BEER.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been quality-controlled (low-quality cells/genes not removed) — the README requires basic QC before BEER Input is gene-centric scaled data rather than raw counts (UMI, FPKM, RPKM, TPM, PKM), which BEER explicitly does not accept Cells of a given type exist in only one batch with no cross-batch analogues, so mutual nearest pairs cannot anchor correlation estimates

skills.description: Use when adapting a source-trained single-cell classifier to unlabeled target cells without raw source data and you need reliable self-supervised neighborhood structure for affinity regularization.
skills.name: mutual-neighbor-graph-construction
skills.search_text: mutual-neighbor-graph-construction Use when adapting a source-trained single-cell classifier to unlabeled target cells without raw source data and you need reliable self-supervised neighborhood structure for affinity regularization. Raw source data are available, so explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g., scArches-style surgery or direct joint training) can be used instead of source-free neighbor-based regularization No pre-trained source model exists, so soft label bank S from predicted probabilities cannot be constructed The goal is de novo clustering of target data rather than regularizing annotation of an already source-trained classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs multi-order neighbor sets (bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional) for each scRNA-seq target cell by cosine-similarity top-M retrieval over an offline representation bank, as used by scEMAIL to impose local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Constructs multi-order neighbor sets (bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional) for each scRNA-seq target cell by cosine-similarity top-M retrieval over an offline representation bank, as used by scEMAIL to impose local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw source data are available, so explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g., scArches-style surgery or direct joint training) can be used instead of source-free neighbor-based regularization No pre-trained source model exists, so soft label bank S from predicted probabilities cannot be constructed The goal is de novo clustering of target data rather than regularizing annotation of an already source-trained classifier

skills.description: Use when building an 'explainable' neural deconvolution model in mxnet where each hidden neuron must map to a defined biological entity (cell type) via a masked gene–cell relation matrix, trained with adam/ReLU/L2loss on bulk RNA-seq.
skills.name: mxnet-symbolic-model-definition
skills.search_text: mxnet-symbolic-model-definition Use when building an 'explainable' neural deconvolution model in mxnet where each hidden neuron must map to a defined biological entity (cell type) via a masked gene–cell relation matrix, trained with adam/ReLU/L2loss on bulk RNA-seq. The input is not bulk RNA-seq gene expression (e.g. already a per-cell single-cell matrix or a precomputed cell abundance table) — DCNet is designed to deconvolve bulk samples into cell-type content A non-transparent, freely learned network is acceptable and the masked, biologically constrained connectivity is not needed — the mask is the core interpretability mechanism here Marker genes and cell types are not from the human CellMarker landscape (9078 genes / 434 cells) and the gene-to-neuron index mappings cannot be reused http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Define an interpretable three-layer mxnet (gluon) neural network with a 9078–434–21136 topology whose hidden-layer neurons correspond one-to-one to 434 cell types, embedding the gene–cell marker relation matrix as a mask on the input-to-hidden weights so latent activations are directly interpretable as cell abundances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Define an interpretable three-layer mxnet (gluon) neural network with a 9078–434–21136 topology whose hidden-layer neurons correspond one-to-one to 434 cell types, embedding the gene–cell marker relation matrix as a mask on the input-to-hidden weights so latent activations are directly interpretable as cell abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not bulk RNA-seq gene expression (e.g. already a per-cell single-cell matrix or a precomputed cell abundance table) — DCNet is designed to deconvolve bulk samples into cell-type content A non-transparent, freely learned network is acceptable and the masked, biologically constrained connectivity is not needed — the mask is the core interpretability mechanism here Marker genes and cell types are not from the human CellMarker landscape (9078 genes / 434 cells) and the gene-to-neuron index mappings cannot be reused

skills.description: Use when analyzing ATAC-Seq samples from SCLC (or similar cancer) cell lines to determine whether MYC resides on ecDNA and whether that ecMYC status elevates MYC copy number and expression.
skills.name: myc-copy-number-amplification-analysis
skills.search_text: myc-copy-number-amplification-analysis Use when analyzing ATAC-Seq samples from SCLC (or similar cancer) cell lines to determine whether MYC resides on ecDNA and whether that ecMYC status elevates MYC copy number and expression. Input data is whole-genome sequencing rather than ATAC-Seq; tools like AmpliconArchitect, which use copy number variation from WGS, are the appropriate alternative Focal amplifications other than ecDNA (e.g. complex structural variants) are the target — circlehunter's benchmarking cannot guarantee accuracy for all focal amplification classes Single-cell ATAC-Seq data — application of circlehunter to single-cell data has yet to be explored http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduce circlehunter-based detection of ecDNA carrying MYC (ecMYC) in SCLC cell-line ATAC-Seq data and verify that ecMYC status drives elevated MYC copy number (P = 1.425e-4, ANOVA) and expression (P = 2.327e-3) with a NEUROD1-high (SCLC-N) expression pattern. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0
skills.summary: Reproduce circlehunter-based detection of ecDNA carrying MYC (ecMYC) in SCLC cell-line ATAC-Seq data and verify that ecMYC status drives elevated MYC copy number (P = 1.425e-4, ANOVA) and expression (P = 2.327e-3) with a NEUROD1-high (SCLC-N) expression pattern.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is whole-genome sequencing rather than ATAC-Seq; tools like AmpliconArchitect, which use copy number variation from WGS, are the appropriate alternative Focal amplifications other than ecDNA (e.g. complex structural variants) are the target — circlehunter's benchmarking cannot guarantee accuracy for all focal amplification classes Single-cell ATAC-Seq data — application of circlehunter to single-cell data has yet to be explored

skills.description: Use when primary AML scRNA-seq samples need a cell-of-origin differentiation-stage call from imputed surface protein levels rather than transcriptome clustering alone.
skills.name: myeloid-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: myeloid-differentiation-trajectory-analysis Use when primary AML scRNA-seq samples need a cell-of-origin differentiation-stage call from imputed surface protein levels rather than transcriptome clustering alone. Input expression is not UMI-based count data — cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based) Cells are outside the hematopoietic lineage — the article notes imputation of these immune-related markers was not tested on non-hematopoietic cells Goal is protein prediction from TPM/RPKM expression metrics — prediction accuracy is unknown as no such CITE-seq data were available for testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Characterizes the myeloid differentiation stage of malignant AML cells by running cTP-net on SAVER-X-denoised, LogNormalize-transformed scRNA-seq data to impute a 24-protein immunophenotype panel, then ordering cells along the CD34+ -> CD38+CD123+ -> CD11c+/CD14+ trajectory and assigning each patient a differentiation-stage category. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0

skills.description: Use when a batch-corrected scRNA-seq embedding (e.g., interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) must be checked for whether treatment-related variation in myeloid cells survives correction, or when comparing GeneVector batch correction against Harmony using silhouette scores and ISG program scoring.
skills.name: myeloid-isg-variation-preservation-assessment
skills.search_text: myeloid-isg-variation-preservation-assessment Use when a batch-corrected scRNA-seq embedding (e.g., interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) must be checked for whether treatment-related variation in myeloid cells survives correction, or when comparing GeneVector batch correction against Harmony using silhouette scores and ISG program scoring. Batches differ substantially in cell type composition — the article warns batch correction is challenging in the presence of batch-specific differences in cell type composition, so correction vectors can conflate batch and cell-type signals and must be manually verified against cell type signatures first The goal is to infer directionality of regulation (activation vs. repression) — GeneVector's mutual information is agnostic to the direction of the statistical dependency No cell-type annotations or stimulation labels are available, since per-cell-type silhouette coefficients and ISG program scoring cannot be computed without them http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmarks whether a batch-corrected single-cell embedding preserves interferon-stimulated (ISG) transcriptional variation within myeloid cells, using per-cell-type batch silhouette coefficients (CD14+ Monocytes expected largest after GeneVector correction) and stimulation-program scoring to contrast GeneVector vector-arithmetic correction against Harmony, which removes treatment-related variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks whether a batch-corrected single-cell embedding preserves interferon-stimulated (ISG) transcriptional variation within myeloid cells, using per-cell-type batch silhouette coefficients (CD14+ Monocytes expected largest after GeneVector correction) and stimulation-program scoring to contrast GeneVector vector-arithmetic correction against Harmony, which removes treatment-related variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Batches differ substantially in cell type composition — the article warns batch correction is challenging in the presence of batch-specific differences in cell type composition, so correction vectors can conflate batch and cell-type signals and must be manually verified against cell type signatures first The goal is to infer directionality of regulation (activation vs. repression) — GeneVector's mutual information is agnostic to the direction of the statistical dependency No cell-type annotations or stimulation labels are available, since per-cell-type silhouette coefficients and ISG program scoring cannot be computed without them

skills.description: Use when CellPath has resolved parallel monocyte differentiation paths in the 6,555 day-4 in vivo mouse hematopoiesis cells and marker genes distinguishing each route must be recovered and verified via per-trajectory DE analysis.
skills.name: myeloid-lineage-marker-validation
skills.search_text: myeloid-lineage-marker-validation Use when CellPath has resolved parallel monocyte differentiation paths in the 6,555 day-4 in vivo mouse hematopoiesis cells and marker genes distinguishing each route must be recovered and verified via per-trajectory DE analysis. The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced counts, so scVelo cannot estimate RNA velocity and CellPath's velocity-based trajectories are not applicable The goal is trajectory inference alone on a simple topology dataset — traditional TI methods (e.g., Slingshot, Monocle-style backbone-constrained methods) suffice and per-trajectory DE validation is unnecessary The biological question concerns non-myeloid lineages where the expected markers (Elane, Mpo, Cd74) provide no validation signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates myeloid lineage markers on CellPath-resolved parallel monocyte routes: after RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference on the mouse hematopoiesis data, per-trajectory differentially expressed gene analysis recovers Elane/Mpo for the Neu-like monocyte route and Cd74 for the DC-like route. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Validates myeloid lineage markers on CellPath-resolved parallel monocyte routes: after RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference on the mouse hematopoiesis data, per-trajectory differentially expressed gene analysis recovers Elane/Mpo for the Neu-like monocyte route and Cd74 for the DC-like route.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced counts, so scVelo cannot estimate RNA velocity and CellPath's velocity-based trajectories are not applicable The goal is trajectory inference alone on a simple topology dataset — traditional TI methods (e.g., Slingshot, Monocle-style backbone-constrained methods) suffice and per-trajectory DE validation is unnecessary The biological question concerns non-myeloid lineages where the expected markers (Elane, Mpo, Cd74) provide no validation signal

skills.description: Use when untreated-vs-treated bulk RNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive and drug-resistant HMCLs (e.g. 0.5 µM 17-AAG ± 15 nM Ixazomib at 24 h) must be converted into per-contrast DEG counts and ranked gene lists.
skills.name: myeloma-drug-response-genomics
skills.search_text: myeloma-drug-response-genomics Use when untreated-vs-treated bulk RNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive and drug-resistant HMCLs (e.g. 0.5 µM 17-AAG ± 15 nM Ixazomib at 24 h) must be converted into per-contrast DEG counts and ranked gene lists. The analysis goal is single-cell (scRNAseq or CyTOF) target-enrichment screening rather than bulk differential-expression signatures The input is already a summarized DEG table or ranked list, i.e. differential expression has already been fit and thresholds applied The pipeline question is secDrug combination prediction via the greedy set cover algorithm on pharmacogenomics data, not validation of a specific treatment contrast by RNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce bulk RNA-seq differential-expression signatures of drug (combination) response in the secDrug myeloma pipeline, e.g. 17-AAG and 17-AAG + Ixazomib in human myeloma cell lines (HMCLs), using DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models, GSA/limma ranked gene lists, and explicit significance cutoffs (p < 0.05; |fold-change| > 2 with FDR < 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41408-022-00636-2
skills.summary: Reproduce bulk RNA-seq differential-expression signatures of drug (combination) response in the secDrug myeloma pipeline, e.g. 17-AAG and 17-AAG + Ixazomib in human myeloma cell lines (HMCLs), using DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial models, GSA/limma ranked gene lists, and explicit significance cutoffs (p < 0.05; |fold-change| > 2 with FDR < 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is single-cell (scRNAseq or CyTOF) target-enrichment screening rather than bulk differential-expression signatures The input is already a summarized DEG table or ranked list, i.e. differential expression has already been fit and thresholds applied The pipeline question is secDrug combination prediction via the greedy set cover algorithm on pharmacogenomics data, not validation of a specific treatment contrast by RNA-seq

skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on the Trapnell HSMM myoblast dataset, or when assessing pseudotime accuracy via correlations with differentiation marker genes (ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2) as in STREAM Fig. 5c-d.
skills.name: myoblast-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: myoblast-differentiation-trajectory-analysis Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on the Trapnell HSMM myoblast dataset, or when assessing pseudotime accuracy via correlations with differentiation marker genes (ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2) as in STREAM Fig. 5c-d. The dataset is scATAC-seq or another epigenomic modality where marker-gene expression correlations are not defined; use STREAM's ATAC workflow (peaks/k-mers/motifs features) instead. The trajectory topology is not a bifurcation (e.g., multifurcation, cyclic, or disconnected graphs), since restricting to 'the correctly inferred bifurcation' is part of this protocol. No marker genes with known differentiation ordering are available for the system, so pseudotime accuracy cannot be assessed by correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Reproduces the STREAM paper's myoblast differentiation (HSMM) trajectory benchmark: infer trajectories on the human skeletal muscle myoblast scRNA-seq dataset with STREAM/ElPiGraph and comparison methods such as Monocle2, extract rank- and distance-based pseudotime, and quantify pseudotime accuracy by correlating with marker genes ENO3, MEF2C, and MYH2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the STREAM paper's myoblast differentiation (HSMM) trajectory benchmark: infer trajectories on the human skeletal muscle myoblast scRNA-seq dataset with STREAM/ElPiGraph and comparison methods such as Monocle2, extract rank- and distance-based pseudotime, and quantify pseudotime accuracy by correlating with marker genes ENO3, MEF2C, and MYH2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is scATAC-seq or another epigenomic modality where marker-gene expression correlations are not defined; use STREAM's ATAC workflow (peaks/k-mers/motifs features) instead. The trajectory topology is not a bifurcation (e.g., multifurcation, cyclic, or disconnected graphs), since restricting to 'the correctly inferred bifurcation' is part of this protocol. No marker genes with known differentiation ordering are available for the system, so pseudotime accuracy cannot be assessed by correlation.

skills.summary: Train a Naïve Bayes classifier that integrates per-gene p-values from multiple DEG detection methods into DEG/non-DEG calls, following the ExpHunter Suite approach of learning from simulated RNA-seq data that mimics the target dataset's characteristics.

skills.description: Use when a merged allele-specific splicing count table with IJC/SJC inclusion and skipping junction counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) is available and naive per-allele PSI (IncLevel) values are needed for quality filtering prior to ASAS testing.
skills.name: naive-psi-estimation-from-inclusion-skipping-counts
skills.search_text: naive-psi-estimation-from-inclusion-skipping-counts Use when a merged allele-specific splicing count table with IJC/SJC inclusion and skipping junction counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) is available and naive per-allele PSI (IncLevel) values are needed for quality filtering prior to ASAS testing. Input lacks per-allele IJC/SJC junction counts or effective isoform lengths (incLen/skpLen), so the length-adjusted inclusion ratio cannot be computed The analysis goal is differential splicing between experimental conditions rather than allele-specific alternative splicing within individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP The event's heterozygous SNP lies within or too distant from the alternative exon, so allele-specific read assignment on RNA-seq reads is not possible http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Computes per-allele naive exon inclusion levels (PSI) as effective-length-adjusted inclusion ratios from PAIRADISE IJC/SJC count data, along with average total read counts, to enable exclusion of unreliable exon skipping events before PAIRADISE's Step 5 ASAS statistical test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks per-allele IJC/SJC junction counts or effective isoform lengths (incLen/skpLen), so the length-adjusted inclusion ratio cannot be computed The analysis goal is differential splicing between experimental conditions rather than allele-specific alternative splicing within individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP The event's heterozygous SNP lies within or too distant from the alternative exon, so allele-specific read assignment on RNA-seq reads is not possible

skills.description: Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads from 10x 3'/5' or Visium-barcoded libraries need cell-barcode/UMI extraction and error-robust UMI deduplication before isoform or gene quantification.
skills.name: nanopore-cell-barcode-umi-recovery
skills.search_text: nanopore-cell-barcode-umi-recovery Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads from 10x 3'/5' or Visium-barcoded libraries need cell-barcode/UMI extraction and error-robust UMI deduplication before isoform or gene quantification. Input reads are short Illumina reads with high per-base accuracy, where simple exact or fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing suffices and UMI scattering is minimal The library has no cell-barcode/UMI structure (e.g. bulk long-read cDNA), so barcode recovery is meaningless Only downstream alternative-splicing statistics are needed and Longcell-pre barcode/UMI outputs already exist — use the Longcell analysis package instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Longcell's preprocessing module for recovering cell barcodes and UMIs from noisy Nanopore single-cell/spatial long reads: sliding-window adapter search, k-mer dictionary barcode matching (edit-distance cutoff 3), Needleman-Wunsch-based UMI clustering with Louvain, and error-driven scatter pruning. It exists because Nanopore per-base accuracy (85–99%) makes whitelist-exact and fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing unreliable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Longcell's preprocessing module for recovering cell barcodes and UMIs from noisy Nanopore single-cell/spatial long reads: sliding-window adapter search, k-mer dictionary barcode matching (edit-distance cutoff 3), Needleman-Wunsch-based UMI clustering with Louvain, and error-driven scatter pruning. It exists because Nanopore per-base accuracy (85–99%) makes whitelist-exact and fixed-edit-distance UMI collapsing unreliable.

skills.summary: Fits gene-specific nearest-neighbor Gaussian process (NNGP) models to spatially-resolved transcriptomics data via the BRISC algorithm to identify and rank spatially variable genes (SVGs) using likelihood-ratio (LR) tests, with runtime scaling linearly in the number of spatial locations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify spatial domain marker genes (mean-level changes between domains) rather than SVGs with continuous spatial variation Grouping SVGs into gene groups or metagenes is required — nnSVG identifies individual SVGs but does not group them A principled multi-sample statistical model is needed — nnSVG is developed for a single sample at a time and handles multiple samples only by rank averaging

skills.description: Use when you need a cell-cell similarity network whose neighbor count adapts to local neighborhood density and heterogeneity (e.g., after computing multilevel archetype encodings H*), without pre-specifying k.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-graph-construction
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-graph-construction Use when you need a cell-cell similarity network whose neighbor count adapts to local neighborhood density and heterogeneity (e.g., after computing multilevel archetype encodings H*), without pre-specifying k. You need a fixed-k nearest-neighbor graph with a uniform neighbor count for all cells — the density-adaptive k* deliberately varies neighbor counts per cell. The data has not been reduced to the archetypal (H*) space yet — distances should be computed in that space, not on raw or merely PCA-reduced expression. You are clustering expression directly without ACTIONet's multilevel archetypal decomposition; k*-NN here presupposes the ACTION/decomposition outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the ACTIONet cell–cell similarity network with a density-dependent adaptive nearest-neighbor algorithm (k*-NN), where each cell's neighbor count k* is solved from a sparsity parameter (kappa) rather than fixed in advance, over square-root Jensen–Shannon distances in the reduced archetypal (H*) space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Constructs the ACTIONet cell–cell similarity network with a density-dependent adaptive nearest-neighbor algorithm (k*-NN), where each cell's neighbor count k* is solved from a sparsity parameter (kappa) rather than fixed in advance, over square-root Jensen–Shannon distances in the reduced archetypal (H*) space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a fixed-k nearest-neighbor graph with a uniform neighbor count for all cells — the density-adaptive k* deliberately varies neighbor counts per cell. The data has not been reduced to the archetypal (H*) space yet — distances should be computed in that space, not on raw or merely PCA-reduced expression. You are clustering expression directly without ACTIONet's multilevel archetypal decomposition; k*-NN here presupposes the ACTION/decomposition outputs.

skills.description: Use when scoring sparse, noisy scRNA-seq count data with bulk-style gene set methods (e.g. singscore, ssGSEA, summed_up) and per-cell signal is too weak — e.g. signature genes missed or AUC degraded by downsampling.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-graph-smoothing
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-graph-smoothing Use when scoring sparse, noisy scRNA-seq count data with bulk-style gene set methods (e.g. singscore, ssGSEA, summed_up) and per-cell signal is too weak — e.g. signature genes missed or AUC degraded by downsampling. smooth_mode='off' is the explicit bypass: when the analysis requires the original unsmoothed counts (e.g. as the no-smoothing baseline condition), do not apply the graph multiplication Scoring bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated pseudobulk profiles, where per-cell sparsity is not the limiting issue and smoothing offers no benefit When the analysis requires cell-level resolution of raw counts rather than neighbor-averaged profiles (smoothing shares gene measure information across a transcriptomic neighborhood) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Builds a nearest neighbor graph of cells within user-defined groups and computes the smoothed expression matrix M = A·X, where A is a binary adjacency or weighted connectivity matrix, producing mini-pseudobulk profiles per cell that reduce single-cell sparsity and technical noise before gene set scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Builds a nearest neighbor graph of cells within user-defined groups and computes the smoothed expression matrix M = A·X, where A is a binary adjacency or weighted connectivity matrix, producing mini-pseudobulk profiles per cell that reduce single-cell sparsity and technical noise before gene set scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: smooth_mode='off' is the explicit bypass: when the analysis requires the original unsmoothed counts (e.g. as the no-smoothing baseline condition), do not apply the graph multiplication Scoring bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated pseudobulk profiles, where per-cell sparsity is not the limiting issue and smoothing offers no benefit When the analysis requires cell-level resolution of raw counts rather than neighbor-averaged profiles (smoothing shares gene measure information across a transcriptomic neighborhood)

skills.description: Use when you need a per-feature ranking by discriminative power from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Zeisel et al. mouse cortex) to serve as a baseline against combinatorial marker-selection methods like phenotype cover.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-hit-miss-weighting
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-hit-miss-weighting Use when you need a per-feature ranking by discriminative power from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Zeisel et al. mouse cortex) to serve as a baseline against combinatorial marker-selection methods like phenotype cover. The goal is a globally discriminative marker set covering every phenotype pair (the phenotype cover problem) — ReliefF scores features individually and does not guarantee pairwise coverage; use GreedyPC/CEMPC instead. A minimal-optimal subset of features is required rather than a full ranking of all features (e.g. the mRMR setting described in the smazzanti/mrmr README). The data are raw counts that have not been preprocessed/log-transformed, so distances used for neighbor retrieval would be dominated by count scale. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 ReliefF-style per-feature weighting that retrieves 30 approximate nearest neighbors per sample with a faiss index and scores each feature by contrasting its values among same-label neighbors (hits) versus different-label neighbors (misses). Used in the marker-selection study as a neighbor-based baseline ranking against phenotype-cover methods (G-PC, CEM-PC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: ReliefF-style per-feature weighting that retrieves 30 approximate nearest neighbors per sample with a faiss index and scores each feature by contrasting its values among same-label neighbors (hits) versus different-label neighbors (misses). Used in the marker-selection study as a neighbor-based baseline ranking against phenotype-cover methods (G-PC, CEM-PC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a globally discriminative marker set covering every phenotype pair (the phenotype cover problem) — ReliefF scores features individually and does not guarantee pairwise coverage; use GreedyPC/CEMPC instead. A minimal-optimal subset of features is required rather than a full ranking of all features (e.g. the mRMR setting described in the smazzanti/mrmr README). The data are raw counts that have not been preprocessed/log-transformed, so distances used for neighbor retrieval would be dominated by count scale.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g., 10x Chromium barcoded cells in _counts_UB.tsv) need lineage or cell-type labels without marker genes or supervised training labels, and a suitable reference expression profile set exists.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-reference-profile-matching
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-reference-profile-matching Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g., 10x Chromium barcoded cells in _counts_UB.tsv) need lineage or cell-type labels without marker genes or supervised training labels, and a suitable reference expression profile set exists. The goal is variant/genotype calling per cell (e.g., expressed somatic SNVs) — use the mutation barcode caller instead, not expression-profile matching. No reference expression profiles are available for the expected cell types of the sample, so nearest-neighbor matching would assign arbitrary labels. Marker genes or supervised cell-type labels are already available and a supervised classifier is preferred. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Unsupervised, marker-free cell-type assignment in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data: each cell's expression profile is matched to hematopoietic reference profiles (e.g., DMAP lineages such as RBC, HSC, CMP, MEP, monocyte, T-cell, B-cell) using Spearman rank correlation as the similarity measure, and a nearest-neighbor classifier assigns the most-correlated lineage label. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Unsupervised, marker-free cell-type assignment in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data: each cell's expression profile is matched to hematopoietic reference profiles (e.g., DMAP lineages such as RBC, HSC, CMP, MEP, monocyte, T-cell, B-cell) using Spearman rank correlation as the similarity measure, and a nearest-neighbor classifier assigns the most-correlated lineage label.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is variant/genotype calling per cell (e.g., expressed somatic SNVs) — use the mutation barcode caller instead, not expression-profile matching. No reference expression profiles are available for the expected cell types of the sample, so nearest-neighbor matching would assign arbitrary labels. Marker genes or supervised cell-type labels are already available and a supervised classifier is preferred.

skills.description: Use when adapting a source-free scRNA-seq annotation model (e.g., scEMAIL) and you need globally-scoped neighborhood structure — bidirectional (mutual nearest), unidirectional, and extensional (neighbors-of-neighbors) sets — to regularize 'known' target cells.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-retrieval-cosine-similarity
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-retrieval-cosine-similarity Use when adapting a source-free scRNA-seq annotation model (e.g., scEMAIL) and you need globally-scoped neighborhood structure — bidirectional (mutual nearest), unidirectional, and extensional (neighbors-of-neighbors) sets — to regularize 'known' target cells. Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment between source and target is possible — scEMAIL's neighborhood scheme is designed for the source-free setting The target cells belong to the 'unknown' (novel cell type) group — their neighbors are deliberately excluded from the affinity computation to avoid noisy supervision No pre-trained source model / representation bank exists yet; neighbor retrieval operates on encoder embeddings, not raw count matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves each target cell's M nearest neighbors in global scope via cosine similarity over an offline representation bank, as used by scEMAIL to gather bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional neighbors for multi-order local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Retrieves each target cell's M nearest neighbors in global scope via cosine similarity over an offline representation bank, as used by scEMAIL to gather bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional neighbors for multi-order local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment between source and target is possible — scEMAIL's neighborhood scheme is designed for the source-free setting The target cells belong to the 'unknown' (novel cell type) group — their neighbors are deliberately excluded from the affinity computation to avoid noisy supervision No pre-trained source model / representation bank exists yet; neighbor retrieval operates on encoder embeddings, not raw count matrices

skills.description: Use when a single-cell analysis pipeline needs a neighbors graph over cell embeddings (PCA/UMAP/cell-by-gene or protein matrices) as input for Leiden clustering, and dataset size makes exact kNN too slow.
skills.name: nearest-neighbors-graph-construction
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbors-graph-construction Use when a single-cell analysis pipeline needs a neighbors graph over cell embeddings (PCA/UMAP/cell-by-gene or protein matrices) as input for Leiden clustering, and dataset size makes exact kNN too slow. The input is already a neighbors graph or precomputed cluster labels — rebuilding a kNN graph would discard the prior representation. The embedding is small enough that exact kNN is tractable and approximate search overhead offers no benefit. The task requires spatial-image-based co-localization scoring directly, which in the article is a separate downstream step applied to the spatial CODEX tile, not part of graph construction. Constructs an approximate nearest-neighbors graph over cell embeddings (e.g., UMAP or PCA reductions of single-cell data) using faiss with 15 neighbors, to feed downstream Leiden community-detection clustering in the Cellar pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Constructs an approximate nearest-neighbors graph over cell embeddings (e.g., UMAP or PCA reductions of single-cell data) using faiss with 15 neighbors, to feed downstream Leiden community-detection clustering in the Cellar pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a neighbors graph or precomputed cluster labels — rebuilding a kNN graph would discard the prior representation. The embedding is small enough that exact kNN is tractable and approximate search overhead offers no benefit. The task requires spatial-image-based co-localization scoring directly, which in the article is a separate downstream step applied to the spatial CODEX tile, not part of graph construction.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a batch-integration embedding (e.g., JOINTLY on a multi-donor scRNA-seq dataset) is robust to dropping input batches — subsample the donors and compare neighbour structure and metrics to the full reference.
skills.name: nearest-neighbour-conservation-analysis
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbour-conservation-analysis Use when evaluating whether a batch-integration embedding (e.g., JOINTLY on a multi-donor scRNA-seq dataset) is robust to dropping input batches — subsample the donors and compare neighbour structure and metrics to the full reference. The dataset is a complex multi-condition, multi-sample dataset where samples do not share the same axes of variation — the paper advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than consensus PCA there, so neighbour-conservation relative to a consensus-PCA reference is not the right robustness check The goal is comparing JOINTLY against other integration methods (Harmony, scVI, fastMNN) rather than testing dependence on the number of input samples http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies how many nearest neighbours each cell retains in a JOINTLY embedding built from a subsampled batch set compared with the full-dataset embedding, to test whether integration performance depends on the number of input samples. Used with ARI/LISI/ASW metrics to reproduce the liver subsampling robustness results (Fig. 2D-I). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Quantifies how many nearest neighbours each cell retains in a JOINTLY embedding built from a subsampled batch set compared with the full-dataset embedding, to test whether integration performance depends on the number of input samples. Used with ARI/LISI/ASW metrics to reproduce the liver subsampling robustness results (Fig. 2D-I).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a complex multi-condition, multi-sample dataset where samples do not share the same axes of variation — the paper advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than consensus PCA there, so neighbour-conservation relative to a consensus-PCA reference is not the right robustness check The goal is comparing JOINTLY against other integration methods (Harmony, scVI, fastMNN) rather than testing dependence on the number of input samples

skills.search_text: nearest-template-prediction Use when you need to classify pre-clinical colorectal cancer models (cell lines, patient-derived organoids, xenografts) into CMS1–CMS4 subtypes from a gene expression matrix, since the original CMS classifier fails on these stroma-free samples. When a well-defined ground truth or well-calibrated denoising objective is required for real data: the article notes it may be difficult to determine when denoising improves scRNA-seq data and that ground truth definition is challenging When overimputation is unacceptable without careful model selection: inadequate hyperparameter choices such as a too-low-dimensional bottleneck layer can cause overimputation When hyperparameters were tuned on downstream analyses: the authors warn that hyperparameters were not fine-tuned for any analysis in the manuscript, so blindly tuning may inflate apparent gains http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Denoise single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with a deep count autoencoder (DCA) that uses a negative binomial (or zero-inflated NB) loss so the reconstruction error is the likelihood of a count noise model, imputing dropouts while preserving overdispersion and gene-gene dependencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2

skills.search_text: negative-binomial-count-simulation Use when building a bulk RNA-seq simulator with realistic count distributions: you need NB draws per gene, time point and replicate, plus controlled DEG profiles (induction, repression, transitory, flat) and coupled regulator profiles. The goal is single-cell multi-omics simulation — use the sc_mosim module, which relies on SPARSim functionality rather than this bulk mosim NB workflow. The input data is real experimental RNA-seq to be analyzed rather than a seed sample for parameter estimation in a simulation. Simulation requires spatial resolution or omics layers like proteomics and metabolomics, which MOSim does not support. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simulates bulk RNA-seq count matrices by drawing negative-binomial counts from per-gene mean and dispersion parameters estimated on a seed RNA-seq sample (SPARSim-style parameterization), then applying profile-specific fold changes for DEG patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Simulates bulk RNA-seq count matrices by drawing negative-binomial counts from per-gene mean and dispersion parameters estimated on a seed RNA-seq sample (SPARSim-style parameterization), then applying profile-specific fold changes for DEG patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-cell multi-omics simulation — use the sc_mosim module, which relies on SPARSim functionality rather than this bulk mosim NB workflow. Simulation requires spatial resolution or omics layers like proteomics and metabolomics, which MOSim does not support.

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices show noisy gene-gene relationships (e.g., low marker co-expression correlations) and a trained batch-invariant scPhere model is available whose decoder can impute denoised negative-binomial mean expression values.
skills.name: negative-binomial-decoder-reconstruction
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-decoder-reconstruction Use when raw UMI count matrices show noisy gene-gene relationships (e.g., low marker co-expression correlations) and a trained batch-invariant scPhere model is available whose decoder can impute denoised negative-binomial mean expression values. No trained scPhere model exists for the dataset — the decoder cannot reconstruct meaningful expression without a fitted model The task is batch correction or latent-space embedding rather than expression imputation/denoising (use model.encode / Trainer instead) Ambient RNA contamination removal is the goal — the paper explicitly states this remains an unvalidated future direction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs denoised per-cell gene expression by feeding UMI count vectors through the scPhere decoder, which outputs a negative-binomial mean ('nb' observation_dist) count vector per input cell, enabling imputation and denoising of scRNA-seq data (e.g., raising CD8A–CD8B correlation from 0.27 to 0.81 in UC CD8+ T cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs denoised per-cell gene expression by feeding UMI count vectors through the scPhere decoder, which outputs a negative-binomial mean ('nb' observation_dist) count vector per input cell, enabling imputation and denoising of scRNA-seq data (e.g., raising CD8A–CD8B correlation from 0.27 to 0.81 in UC CD8+ T cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trained scPhere model exists for the dataset — the decoder cannot reconstruct meaningful expression without a fitted model The task is batch correction or latent-space embedding rather than expression imputation/denoising (use model.encode / Trainer instead) Ambient RNA contamination removal is the goal — the paper explicitly states this remains an unvalidated future direction

skills.description: Use when synthetic single-cell count data must be generated without relying on copies of the original cells — e.g., enlarging a small pilot scRNA-seq dataset (such as PBMC4k, 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) after a VAE like scVI has been trained on it.
skills.name: negative-binomial-decoder-simulation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-decoder-simulation Use when synthetic single-cell count data must be generated without relying on copies of the original cells — e.g., enlarging a small pilot scRNA-seq dataset (such as PBMC4k, 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) after a VAE like scVI has been trained on it. When the goal is to faithfully reproduce the original pilot cells' clustering structure — the paper's scVI (posterior) variant is the standard approach for conditioning on observations, and posterior-vs-prior quality trade-offs should be compared rather than assuming the prior variant suffices. When batch effects must be modeled: the paper examined all models without batch correction capabilities and notes batch correction methods were outside its scope. When the target technology is highly sparse 10x Genomics data with very small pilot sizes — the paper found inference from small to larger datasets more challenging for sparser 10x datasets than Smart-seq2. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A scVI-based generative variant for scRNA-seq that draws latent variables directly from the prior Normal(0,1) instead of the posterior p(z|x), and library sizes from Normal(l_mu, 1), then passes them through the gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder to synthesize UMI counts. It serves as a fully generative alternative to the posterior-sampling variant, which still relies on copies of original observations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: A scVI-based generative variant for scRNA-seq that draws latent variables directly from the prior Normal(0,1) instead of the posterior p(z|x), and library sizes from Normal(l_mu, 1), then passes them through the gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder to synthesize UMI counts. It serves as a fully generative alternative to the posterior-sampling variant, which still relies on copies of original observations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to faithfully reproduce the original pilot cells' clustering structure — the paper's scVI (posterior) variant is the standard approach for conditioning on observations, and posterior-vs-prior quality trade-offs should be compared rather than assuming the prior variant suffices. When batch effects must be modeled: the paper examined all models without batch correction capabilities and notes batch correction methods were outside its scope. When the target technology is highly sparse 10x Genomics data with very small pilot sizes — the paper found inference from small to larger datasets more challenging for sparser 10x datasets than Smart-seq2.

skills.description: Use when you need to generate synthetic scRNA-seq count data from a small pilot dataset (a few hundred to ~2300 cells) with a generative model that avoids the posterior-sampling bias amplification seen in scVI, e.g. for pilot-study-based power analysis.
skills.name: negative-binomial-deep-boltzmann-machine-training
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-deep-boltzmann-machine-training Use when you need to generate synthetic scRNA-seq count data from a small pilot dataset (a few hundred to ~2300 cells) with a generative model that avoids the posterior-sampling bias amplification seen in scVI, e.g. for pilot-study-based power analysis. Data contains batch effects that need correction — the study examined all models without batch correction capabilities, and batch effects currently cannot be learned with scDBMs. The goal is dimensionality reduction or batch integration of existing cells (use scvi-tools for those tasks) rather than generating novel synthetic observations from a pilot study. The pilot sample may not be representative of the target population (e.g. experimental settings will change), since extrapolation from small to larger datasets relies on that assumption. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a single-cell deep Boltzmann machine (scDBM) with negative binomial likelihood on small pilot scRNA-seq sub-samples (384–2304 cells) using scDBM.jl / BoltzmannMachines.jl in Julia, then generate synthetic counts via Gibbs sampling up to the original study size to support experimental design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Train a single-cell deep Boltzmann machine (scDBM) with negative binomial likelihood on small pilot scRNA-seq sub-samples (384–2304 cells) using scDBM.jl / BoltzmannMachines.jl in Julia, then generate synthetic counts via Gibbs sampling up to the original study size to support experimental design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contains batch effects that need correction — the study examined all models without batch correction capabilities, and batch effects currently cannot be learned with scDBMs. The goal is dimensionality reduction or batch integration of existing cells (use scvi-tools for those tasks) rather than generating novel synthetic observations from a pilot study. The pilot sample may not be representative of the target population (e.g. experimental settings will change), since extrapolation from small to larger datasets relies on that assumption.

skills.description: Use when training scDBM or similar NB-based generative models on scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) and per-gene inverse dispersion (θ) estimates are needed for the negative-binomial likelihood.
skills.name: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation Use when training scDBM or similar NB-based generative models on scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) and per-gene inverse dispersion (θ) estimates are needed for the negative-binomial likelihood. Input is normalized, log-transformed, or otherwise non-count data — the NB likelihood and Fisher information are derived for raw UMI counts Batch correction is required — the paper states batch effects cannot currently be learned with scDBMs and models were examined without batch correction capabilities A separately validated or benchmarked dispersion estimator is needed — the paper describes this mechanism but does not separately benchmark it http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter (θ) of a negative-binomial likelihood fitted to scRNA-seq UMI counts using a regularized Fisher scoring algorithm inside the scDBM training loop, as proposed in the scDBM paper (Treppner et al. 2021). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Estimates the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter (θ) of a negative-binomial likelihood fitted to scRNA-seq UMI counts using a regularized Fisher scoring algorithm inside the scDBM training loop, as proposed in the scDBM paper (Treppner et al. 2021).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is normalized, log-transformed, or otherwise non-count data — the NB likelihood and Fisher information are derived for raw UMI counts Batch correction is required — the paper states batch effects cannot currently be learned with scDBMs and models were examined without batch correction capabilities A separately validated or benchmarked dispersion estimator is needed — the paper describes this mechanism but does not separately benchmark it

skills.description: Use when modeling scRNA-seq count data requires comparing goodness-of-fit of zero-inflated NB vs negative binomial (edgeR) vs hurdle (MAST) models in terms of mean count, zero (dropout) probability, and dispersion estimation.
skills.name: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation Use when modeling scRNA-seq count data requires comparing goodness-of-fit of zero-inflated NB vs negative binomial (edgeR) vs hurdle (MAST) models in terms of mean count, zero (dropout) probability, and dispersion estimation. Input data are already normalized low-dimensional embeddings or transformed expressions where count-based dispersion estimation is not meaningful (ZINB-WaVE's cell-level intercept global-scaling normalization is intended for raw count data) The analysis goal is supervised differential expression — this capability was not yet available and only envisioned for a future zinbwave version Bulk RNA-seq data without zero inflation/dropouts, where a plain negative binomial model (e.g., edgeR/DESeq2) alone is sufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit and compare count-model dispersion and zero-inflation estimates for single-cell RNA-seq data using a zero-inflated negative binomial model (ZINB-WaVE zinbFit), a gene-by-gene negative binomial model (edgeR), and a MAST hurdle model, benchmarking estimated mean counts, zero probabilities, and genewise dispersions against observed values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Fit and compare count-model dispersion and zero-inflation estimates for single-cell RNA-seq data using a zero-inflated negative binomial model (ZINB-WaVE zinbFit), a gene-by-gene negative binomial model (edgeR), and a MAST hurdle model, benchmarking estimated mean counts, zero probabilities, and genewise dispersions against observed values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already normalized low-dimensional embeddings or transformed expressions where count-based dispersion estimation is not meaningful (ZINB-WaVE's cell-level intercept global-scaling normalization is intended for raw count data) The analysis goal is supervised differential expression — this capability was not yet available and only envisioned for a future zinbwave version Bulk RNA-seq data without zero inflation/dropouts, where a plain negative binomial model (e.g., edgeR/DESeq2) alone is sufficient

skills.description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking gene co-expression estimators (CS-CORE, rho-sctransform, locCSN, etc.) on synthetic UMI counts where a known true latent correlation must be held fixed across a grid of expression levels.
skills.name: negative-binomial-gaussian-copula-count-simulation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-gaussian-copula-count-simulation Use when evaluating or benchmarking gene co-expression estimators (CS-CORE, rho-sctransform, locCSN, etc.) on synthetic UMI counts where a known true latent correlation must be held fixed across a grid of expression levels. When the goal is differential co-expression testing on real data rather than estimator benchmarking under known ground truth When the underlying generative model must differ from the Poisson measurement process, since the paper's measurement model uses only a Poisson distribution and defers negative-binomial count modeling to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A scRNA-seq simulation scheme that generates synthetic gene-pair UMI counts with negative-binomial marginals and a Gaussian-copula latent correlation (e.g., rho = 0.5), used to benchmark co-expression estimators for mean-correlation bias and MSE against CS-CORE-style ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: A scRNA-seq simulation scheme that generates synthetic gene-pair UMI counts with negative-binomial marginals and a Gaussian-copula latent correlation (e.g., rho = 0.5), used to benchmark co-expression estimators for mean-correlation bias and MSE against CS-CORE-style ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential co-expression testing on real data rather than estimator benchmarking under known ground truth When the underlying generative model must differ from the Poisson measurement process, since the paper's measurement model uses only a Poisson distribution and defers negative-binomial count modeling to future work

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a co-expression estimator applied to log-normalized scRNA-seq UMI counts produces false positives: simulate counts for an independent gene pair under a negative-binomial model with zero true co-expression and measure the spurious correlation each method reports.
skills.name: negative-binomial-gene-count-simulation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-gene-count-simulation Use when evaluating whether a co-expression estimator applied to log-normalized scRNA-seq UMI counts produces false positives: simulate counts for an independent gene pair under a negative-binomial model with zero true co-expression and measure the spurious correlation each method reports. The goal is co-expression inference on real scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking estimator false-positive behavior on simulated independent genes The simulated pair is intended to have true co-expression — this skill's design requires zero true co-expression so any nonzero estimate is a false positive The data are not UMI counts with sequencing-depth variation (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or already-normalized expression matrices), since the spurious-correlation phenomenon being probed arises from log-normalizing variable-depth UMI counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking simulation that generates UMI counts for a truly independent (non-co-expressed) gene pair from a negative-binomial model calibrated to single-cell expression levels, then runs co-expression estimators on log-normalized counts to quantify spurious (false-positive) co-expression. It exposes the inflated false positives of log-normalization-based methods that motivate CS-CORE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: A benchmarking simulation that generates UMI counts for a truly independent (non-co-expressed) gene pair from a negative-binomial model calibrated to single-cell expression levels, then runs co-expression estimators on log-normalized counts to quantify spurious (false-positive) co-expression. It exposes the inflated false positives of log-normalization-based methods that motivate CS-CORE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is co-expression inference on real scRNA-seq data rather than benchmarking estimator false-positive behavior on simulated independent genes The simulated pair is intended to have true co-expression — this skill's design requires zero true co-expression so any nonzero estimate is a false positive The data are not UMI counts with sequencing-depth variation (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or already-normalized expression matrices), since the spurious-correlation phenomenon being probed arises from log-normalizing variable-depth UMI counts

skills.description: Use when benchmarking circadian phase-inference methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when choosing a count likelihood distribution for unsupervised phase inference from droplet scRNA-seq (e.g. 10X Genomics Chromium) data.
skills.name: negative-binomial-generative-modeling
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-generative-modeling Use when benchmarking circadian phase-inference methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when choosing a count likelihood distribution for unsupervised phase inference from droplet scRNA-seq (e.g. 10X Genomics Chromium) data. Analysis requires explicitly modeling technical/batch effects for data collected as multiple samples over time — Tempo's model does not incorporate these The biology demands subpopulation-specific gene amplitude variation or non-sinusoidal CCG waveforms, since Tempo assumes 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means The task is cell-cycle phase inference with existing tools on plate-based data (e.g. Fluidigm C1) rather than circadian phase inference from droplet-based data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Use Tempo's Negative Binomial generative model of droplet-based scRNA-seq counts to simulate datasets with known ground-truth circadian phases, so that phase-estimation accuracy can be benchmarked against a theoretical optimum. This addresses the core limitation that existing unsupervised phase methods assume likelihood distributions that poorly approximate true droplet count generation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: Use Tempo's Negative Binomial generative model of droplet-based scRNA-seq counts to simulate datasets with known ground-truth circadian phases, so that phase-estimation accuracy can be benchmarked against a theoretical optimum. This addresses the core limitation that existing unsupervised phase methods assume likelihood distributions that poorly approximate true droplet count generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis requires explicitly modeling technical/batch effects for data collected as multiple samples over time — Tempo's model does not incorporate these The biology demands subpopulation-specific gene amplitude variation or non-sinusoidal CCG waveforms, since Tempo assumes 24 h sinusoidal CCG expression means The task is cell-cycle phase inference with existing tools on plate-based data (e.g. Fluidigm C1) rather than circadian phase inference from droplet-based data

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI/read counts must be transformed into copy-number states (loss/neutral/gain) per gene and cell via negative-binomial statistical modeling with HMM smoothing.
skills.name: negative-binomial-glm-copy-number-fitting
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-glm-copy-number-fitting Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI/read counts must be transformed into copy-number states (loss/neutral/gain) per gene and cell via negative-binomial statistical modeling with HMM smoothing. The goal is copy-neutral LOH or allele-specific calls, which the RDR read-depth module alone cannot resolve — the BAF module and combine step are required. Input is already a CNA state matrix or per-gene-per-cell copy-number call table rather than raw read/UMI counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit a negative-binomial GLM to the gene-by-cell expression read-count matrix of XClone's RDR module, estimating library size, dispersions, and copy loss/neutral/gain ratios to convert read depth into per-gene, per-cell CNA-state probabilities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Fit a negative-binomial GLM to the gene-by-cell expression read-count matrix of XClone's RDR module, estimating library size, dispersions, and copy loss/neutral/gain ratios to convert read depth into per-gene, per-cell CNA-state probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is copy-neutral LOH or allele-specific calls, which the RDR read-depth module alone cannot resolve — the BAF module and combine step are required. Input is already a CNA state matrix or per-gene-per-cell copy-number call table rather than raw read/UMI counts.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple time points plus metadata with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and need to detect genes whose expression trends over time differ between conditions (tDEGs).
skills.name: negative-binomial-glm-fitting
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-glm-fitting Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple time points plus metadata with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and need to detect genes whose expression trends over time differ between conditions (tDEGs). When the hypothesis involves nonlinear temporal changes in gene expression — the GLM can only detect linear effects (linear change by time or by the time-by-condition interaction) When the input is normalized continuous expression rather than counts — the negative binomial model assumes raw count data When samples across time points are not relatable (e.g., no shared subject/annotation structure), since CASi's cross-timepoint design assumes information borrowing from earlier time points http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fits per-gene negative binomial GLMs with a log link to identify temporal differentially expressed genes (tDEGs) in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data, as implemented in CASi's FindTemporalDEGs. The interaction term between time and condition captures genes with divergent time-trending behavior across strata. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Fits per-gene negative binomial GLMs with a log link to identify temporal differentially expressed genes (tDEGs) in multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data, as implemented in CASi's FindTemporalDEGs. The interaction term between time and condition captures genes with divergent time-trending behavior across strata.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the hypothesis involves nonlinear temporal changes in gene expression — the GLM can only detect linear effects (linear change by time or by the time-by-condition interaction) When the input is normalized continuous expression rather than counts — the negative binomial model assumes raw count data When samples across time points are not relatable (e.g., no shared subject/annotation structure), since CASi's cross-timepoint design assumes information borrowing from earlier time points

skills.description: Use when comparing two single-cell Hi-C conditions (e.g., mouse oocyte vs zygote, Astro vs Endo) at bin-pair resolution from a normalized count table, and per-bin-pair differential interaction calls with raw and BH-adjusted p-values are needed.
skills.name: negative-binomial-likelihood-ratio-testing
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-likelihood-ratio-testing Use when comparing two single-cell Hi-C conditions (e.g., mouse oocyte vs zygote, Astro vs Endo) at bin-pair resolution from a normalized count table, and per-bin-pair differential interaction calls with raw and BH-adjusted p-values are needed. The data are bulk Hi-C contact matrices without single-cell-level sparsity structure — the article positions the ZINB regression specially for the excessive zeros of single-cell interaction comparison Only non-negative KS/CVM results and pvalue.adj columns are available; scHiCDiff.NB/ZINB require a normalized count.table and produce the parametric (mu/theta/pi, chi2LR1) statistics The count table has not been normalized (e.g., with scHiCDiff.norm using effective length, GC content, mappability), since the detection functions expect normalized scHi-C read counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Parametric detection of differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) in single-cell Hi-C via scHiCDiff's Negative Binomial (scHiCDiff.NB) and Zero-inflated Negative Binomial (scHiCDiff.ZINB) likelihood-ratio tests, which fit (mu, theta, pi) per condition and test the null with a chi2LR1 statistic. The ZINB option is specifically designed for single-cell counts by accounting for excessive zeros. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Parametric detection of differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) in single-cell Hi-C via scHiCDiff's Negative Binomial (scHiCDiff.NB) and Zero-inflated Negative Binomial (scHiCDiff.ZINB) likelihood-ratio tests, which fit (mu, theta, pi) per condition and test the null with a chi2LR1 statistic. The ZINB option is specifically designed for single-cell counts by accounting for excessive zeros.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk Hi-C contact matrices without single-cell-level sparsity structure — the article positions the ZINB regression specially for the excessive zeros of single-cell interaction comparison Only non-negative KS/CVM results and pvalue.adj columns are available; scHiCDiff.NB/ZINB require a normalized count.table and produce the parametric (mu/theta/pi, chi2LR1) statistics The count table has not been normalized (e.g., with scHiCDiff.norm using effective length, GC content, mappability), since the detection functions expect normalized scHi-C read counts

skills.description: Use when scMM has been trained on transcriptome + surface-protein CITE-seq counts and you must score held-out transcriptome-to-protein crossmodal generation via NB mean-parameter correlations.
skills.name: negative-binomial-mean-extraction
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-mean-extraction Use when scMM has been trained on transcriptome + surface-protein CITE-seq counts and you must score held-out transcriptome-to-protein crossmodal generation via NB mean-parameter correlations. Input modalities are not raw counts (e.g. normalized or log-transformed expression), since scMM models raw count data with modality-specific likelihoods including the negative binomial for proteins The target modality is chromatin accessibility rather than surface proteins, where the count distribution and feature files (peak.tsv, ATAC-seq folder) differ from the CITE-seq protein setup http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts the negative binomial (NB) mean parameters from scMM's crossmodally generated protein-count distributions as point estimates of surface protein abundance, then validates them by correlating against original counts for held-out CITE-seq cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Extracts the negative binomial (NB) mean parameters from scMM's crossmodally generated protein-count distributions as point estimates of surface protein abundance, then validates them by correlating against original counts for held-out CITE-seq cells.
