skills.description: Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., thousands of cells across dozens of subjects) where per-gene tests must account for hierarchical overdispersion, or when glmer.nb-style NB mixed models are too slow for genome-scale testing (~16,000 genes).
skills.name: negative-binomial-mixed-model-fitting
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-mixed-model-fitting Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., thousands of cells across dozens of subjects) where per-gene tests must account for hierarchical overdispersion, or when glmer.nb-style NB mixed models are too slow for genome-scale testing (~16,000 genes). Input is already aggregated to pseudo-bulk/bulk per-subject profiles where subject-level random effects are not needed — a standard bulk negative binomial model suffices Data are single-subject or lack a multi-subject hierarchical structure, so the subject/cell overdispersion decomposition of the NBMM is unnecessary The gene set consists of very lowly expressed genes (counts per cell far below the cpc=0.005 cutoff), which the co-expression analysis has little statistical power to test http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) per gene to multi-subject single-cell count data using NEBULA, which decomposes overdispersion into subject-level (sigma^2) and cell-level (phi^-1) components, enabling fast differential expression, marker-gene, and cell-level co-expression testing across tens of thousands of cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Fit negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) per gene to multi-subject single-cell count data using NEBULA, which decomposes overdispersion into subject-level (sigma^2) and cell-level (phi^-1) components, enabling fast differential expression, marker-gene, and cell-level co-expression testing across tens of thousands of cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aggregated to pseudo-bulk/bulk per-subject profiles where subject-level random effects are not needed — a standard bulk negative binomial model suffices Data are single-subject or lack a multi-subject hierarchical structure, so the subject/cell overdispersion decomposition of the NBMM is unnecessary The gene set consists of very lowly expressed genes (counts per cell far below the cpc=0.005 cutoff), which the co-expression analysis has little statistical power to test

skills.description: Use when analyzing large-scale multi-subject droplet scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count data (e.g., human frontal cortex snRNA-seq, PBMCs) where hierarchical overdispersion must be decomposed into between-subject and within-subject components per gene.
skills.name: negative-binomial-mixed-model-overdispersion-estimation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-mixed-model-overdispersion-estimation Use when analyzing large-scale multi-subject droplet scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count data (e.g., human frontal cortex snRNA-seq, PBMCs) where hierarchical overdispersion must be decomposed into between-subject and within-subject components per gene. Bulk RNA-seq or small-sample-size data with few subjects, where conventional transcriptomics methods are adequate and large-sample approximations do not hold Data where cells cannot be grouped by subject (no multi-subject structure), since the NBMM between-subject component is undefined Genes with estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 (for ≥50 cells per subject) or subject-level overdispersion > 1 when testing subject-level variables — these should be removed or interpreted cautiously rather than modeled http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit per-gene negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) with NEBULA to decompose overdispersion in multi-subject single-cell data into subject-level (σ²) and cell-level (φ⁻¹) components, choosing between the fast large-sample-approximation algorithm (NEBULA-LN) and the h-likelihood algorithm (NEBULA-HL). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Fit per-gene negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) with NEBULA to decompose overdispersion in multi-subject single-cell data into subject-level (σ²) and cell-level (φ⁻¹) components, choosing between the fast large-sample-approximation algorithm (NEBULA-LN) and the h-likelihood algorithm (NEBULA-HL).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bulk RNA-seq or small-sample-size data with few subjects, where conventional transcriptomics methods are adequate and large-sample approximations do not hold Data where cells cannot be grouped by subject (no multi-subject structure), since the NBMM between-subject component is undefined Genes with estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 (for ≥50 cells per subject) or subject-level overdispersion > 1 when testing subject-level variables — these should be removed or interpreted cautiously rather than modeled

skills.description: Use when demultiplexing a cell hashing experiment with more than 4 hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes, where negative-signal dominance degrades cutoff accuracy in HTOreader's HTOcutoff step.
skills.name: negative-signal-subsampling-in-multi-hashtag-experiments
skills.search_text: negative-signal-subsampling-in-multi-hashtag-experiments Use when demultiplexing a cell hashing experiment with more than 4 hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes, where negative-signal dominance degrades cutoff accuracy in HTOreader's HTOcutoff step. Experiments with 4 or fewer hashtags, where the subsampling trigger (N > 4) does not apply and negative signals are less likely to dominate Datasets without an 'HTO' assay loadable as a Seurat object (e.g. raw FASTQ or non-hashing samples) Samples being demultiplexed by SNP/genetic-variation methods alone (e.g. demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo), which do not use hashtag distributions A cutoff-calling refinement in HTOreader that subsamples the negative-signal population when a cell hashing experiment uses many hashtags (N > 4), using an empirical CLR cutoff of 1.5 (3 for the log method) and a stride of floor(N/2) so background cells do not dominate the Gaussian mixture fit and skew per-hashtag cutoffs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: A cutoff-calling refinement in HTOreader that subsamples the negative-signal population when a cell hashing experiment uses many hashtags (N > 4), using an empirical CLR cutoff of 1.5 (3 for the log method) and a stride of floor(N/2) so background cells do not dominate the Gaussian mixture fit and skew per-hashtag cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Experiments with 4 or fewer hashtags, where the subsampling trigger (N > 4) does not apply and negative signals are less likely to dominate Datasets without an 'HTO' assay loadable as a Seurat object (e.g. raw FASTQ or non-hashing samples) Samples being demultiplexed by SNP/genetic-variation methods alone (e.g. demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo), which do not use hashtag distributions

skills.description: Use when building cell-cell communication networks from single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., seqFISH+ mouse cortex, Seq-Scope mouse colon) where a coordinate matrix and cell type label vector are available and neighbor exposure scores must precede regression modeling.
skills.name: neighbor-cell-type-score-computation
skills.search_text: neighbor-cell-type-score-computation Use when building cell-cell communication networks from single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., seqFISH+ mouse cortex, Seq-Scope mouse colon) where a coordinate matrix and cell type label vector are available and neighbor exposure scores must precede regression modeling. Data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., spot-level or bulk data) — the log10(distance/dist0) decay requires per-cell positions The goal is ligand-receptor-based communication inference (e.g., CellPhoneDB-style) rather than spatial neighbor-effect regression on HVG expression Cell type labels have not yet been assigned to individual cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes raw adjacent cell type scores that quantify how strongly each cell is exposed to neighboring cell types, using spatial coordinates and cell type labels, then z-score normalizes them per cell type. These scores are the independent variables (B matrix) for downstream CPPLS regression modeling of cell-cell communication effects on HVG expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Computes raw adjacent cell type scores that quantify how strongly each cell is exposed to neighboring cell types, using spatial coordinates and cell type labels, then z-score normalizes them per cell type. These scores are the independent variables (B matrix) for downstream CPPLS regression modeling of cell-cell communication effects on HVG expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., spot-level or bulk data) — the log10(distance/dist0) decay requires per-cell positions The goal is ligand-receptor-based communication inference (e.g., CellPhoneDB-style) rather than spatial neighbor-effect regression on HVG expression Cell type labels have not yet been assigned to individual cells

Cells do not share an identical barcode group and fine-scale subtree resolution is not needed (barcode data alone already resolves them) Barcode data quality is too low (short barcodes, dropout, non-optimal mutation rates) such that Hamming distances are uninformative — the article notes these challenges degrade lineage inference You only need the final ML-refined tree and no initial-tree control; use the full NJ_asym_Dif pipeline instead of running NJ manually http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Initializes a candidate cell lineage tree for LinRace by computing pairwise Hamming distances on transformed lineage barcode characters and running Neighbor Joining, providing a starting tree that the rSS maximum-likelihood local search subsequently refines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Initializes a candidate cell lineage tree for LinRace by computing pairwise Hamming distances on transformed lineage barcode characters and running Neighbor Joining, providing a starting tree that the rSS maximum-likelihood local search subsequently refines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells do not share an identical barcode group and fine-scale subtree resolution is not needed (barcode data alone already resolves them) Barcode data quality is too low (short barcodes, dropout, non-optimal mutation rates) such that Hamming distances are uninformative — the article notes these challenges degrade lineage inference You only need the final ML-refined tree and no initial-tree control; use the full NJ_asym_Dif pipeline instead of running NJ manually

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a semi-supervised scRNA-seq label propagation model (e.g. scSHARP's GCN) against a simple nonparametric neighbor-voting baseline on PCA-embedded cells with reference labels.
skills.name: neighbor-majority-label-propagation
skills.search_text: neighbor-majority-label-propagation Use when benchmarking a semi-supervised scRNA-seq label propagation model (e.g. scSHARP's GCN) against a simple nonparametric neighbor-voting baseline on PCA-embedded cells with reference labels. The goal is feature interpretation or identifying important genes for classification — the neighbor-majority baseline offers no interpretability, unlike the GCN method. The task is to improve accuracy over the consensus of component tools rather than to benchmark against a simple baseline — use the scSHARP GCN label propagation instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A nonparametric baseline for scRNA-seq cell type annotation that assigns each cell the majority label of its k nearest PCA-embedding neighbors, iterated to convergence. It benchmarks the scSHARP GCN label propagation model and shows comparable accuracy on simulated and real datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: A nonparametric baseline for scRNA-seq cell type annotation that assigns each cell the majority label of its k nearest PCA-embedding neighbors, iterated to convergence. It benchmarks the scSHARP GCN label propagation model and shows comparable accuracy on simulated and real datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature interpretation or identifying important genes for classification — the neighbor-majority baseline offers no interpretability, unlike the GCN method. The task is to improve accuracy over the consensus of component tools rather than to benchmark against a simple baseline — use the scSHARP GCN label propagation instead.

skills.description: Use when comparing cell types across two or more scRNA-seq datasets without shared labels, to identify reciprocal matches (AUROC >= 0.95) and assess how well novel subtypes replicate across studies.
skills.name: neighbor-voting-cell-type-identification
skills.search_text: neighbor-voting-cell-type-identification Use when comparing cell types across two or more scRNA-seq datasets without shared labels, to identify reciprocal matches (AUROC >= 0.95) and assess how well novel subtypes replicate across studies. Corresponding cell type labels are already known across datasets — use the fully supervised MetaNeighbor mode instead of the unsupervised AUROC-matrix workflow The question is de novo clustering of cells within a single dataset rather than cross-dataset replication of pre-defined cell type labels Gene names in the gene sets do not match the expression matrix row names, or gene sets contain only one gene — MetaNeighbor will not run correctly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 MetaNeighbor-based quantification of cell type replicability across scRNA-seq datasets via neighbor voting, producing cell type-by-cell type mean AUROC scores from highly variable gene sets to identify replicated subtypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: MetaNeighbor-based quantification of cell type replicability across scRNA-seq datasets via neighbor voting, producing cell type-by-cell type mean AUROC scores from highly variable gene sets to identify replicated subtypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Corresponding cell type labels are already known across datasets — use the fully supervised MetaNeighbor mode instead of the unsupervised AUROC-matrix workflow The question is de novo clustering of cells within a single dataset rather than cross-dataset replication of pre-defined cell type labels Gene names in the gene sets do not match the expression matrix row names, or gene sets contain only one gene — MetaNeighbor will not run correctly

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how well cell-type labels replicate across two or more scRNA-seq datasets by predicting labels for cells from one held-out dataset based on their similarity to labeled cells in training datasets.
skills.name: neighbor-voting-label-prediction
skills.search_text: neighbor-voting-label-prediction Use when you need to quantify how well cell-type labels replicate across two or more scRNA-seq datasets by predicting labels for cells from one held-out dataset based on their similarity to labeled cells in training datasets. Cell-type labels are ambiguous or missing across datasets — use the unsupervised variant (MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes and topHits) instead of the fully supervised neighbor-voting pipeline. There is only one dataset of origin, since cross-dataset validation requires hiding labels for one dataset at a time and scoring recovery on held-out data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting algorithm predicts held-out cell-type identities across scRNA-seq datasets by building a cell-cell Spearman rank correlation network for a gene set and voting with labeled training cells, scoring recovery with mean AUROC under leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting algorithm predicts held-out cell-type identities across scRNA-seq datasets by building a cell-cell Spearman rank correlation network for a gene set and voting with labeled training cells, scoring recovery with mean AUROC under leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are ambiguous or missing across datasets — use the unsupervised variant (MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes and topHits) instead of the fully supervised neighbor-voting pipeline. There is only one dataset of origin, since cross-dataset validation requires hiding labels for one dataset at a time and scoring recovery on held-out data.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing multi-branching developmental trajectories from scRNA-seq (e.g. FACS-sorted progenitor populations like MDP/CDP/preDC or time-course myoblast data) where branching points and cell fates must be inferred without known temporal ordering.
skills.name: neighborhood-based-cell-state-transition-mapping
skills.search_text: neighborhood-based-cell-state-transition-mapping Use when reconstructing multi-branching developmental trajectories from scRNA-seq (e.g. FACS-sorted progenitor populations like MDP/CDP/preDC or time-course myoblast data) where branching points and cell fates must be inferred without known temporal ordering. The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types - Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension). The dataset is highly heterogeneous with unknown specific subset information - Mpath currently relies on signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction. A priori temporal ordering of developmental subsets is already known and a linear ordering method suffices - Mpath's value is resolving nonlinear multi-branching trajectories without temporal prior knowledge. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Mpath's core operation: aggregate single-cell RNA-seq cells by counting neighbouring cells to estimate potential state transitions, building a multi-branching aggregation tree that maps progenitor progression and branching events without a priori temporal ordering of developmental subsets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Mpath's core operation: aggregate single-cell RNA-seq cells by counting neighbouring cells to estimate potential state transitions, building a multi-branching aggregation tree that maps progenitor progression and branching events without a priori temporal ordering of developmental subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types - Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension). The dataset is highly heterogeneous with unknown specific subset information - Mpath currently relies on signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction. A priori temporal ordering of developmental subsets is already known and a linear ordering method suffices - Mpath's value is resolving nonlinear multi-branching trajectories without temporal prior knowledge.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing cell-state transition graphs from landmark- or cluster-labeled single-cell data, where edge support should be quantified by counting cells whose two nearest landmark states define each candidate edge.
skills.name: neighborhood-based-transition-edge-weighting
skills.search_text: neighborhood-based-transition-edge-weighting Use when reconstructing cell-state transition graphs from landmark- or cluster-labeled single-cell data, where edge support should be quantified by counting cells whose two nearest landmark states define each candidate edge. The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this and the authors list it as a planned future extension. Specific subset information is unknown in a highly heterogeneous dataset — the article notes Mpath is not yet extended to such settings. Terminal differentiated subsets or end-stage contrast signature genes are unavailable, since Mpath relies on them to predict individual cell fate via travelling back in time. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Mpath's method for building a landmark state-transition network: each pooled cell is assigned to the pair of its two nearest landmarks, and the number of cells supporting each landmark pair becomes that edge's weight; a minimum spanning tree over -w(e) then trims the complete weighted graph to a multi-branching skeleton. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Mpath's method for building a landmark state-transition network: each pooled cell is assigned to the pair of its two nearest landmarks, and the number of cells supporting each landmark pair becomes that edge's weight; a minimum spanning tree over -w(e) then trims the complete weighted graph to a multi-branching skeleton.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The developmental process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this and the authors list it as a planned future extension. Specific subset information is unknown in a highly heterogeneous dataset — the article notes Mpath is not yet extended to such settings. Terminal differentiated subsets or end-stage contrast signature genes are unavailable, since Mpath relies on them to predict individual cell fate via travelling back in time.

skills.description: Use when clustering single-cell perturbation data where control-defined cell states are already labeled, and non-explanatory gene variance must be down-weighted before assigning perturbed cells to states.
skills.name: neighborhood-component-feature-selection-gene-weighting

skills.summary: Sparse gene-weighting step of ICAT that uses Neighborhood Component Feature Selection (NCFS) to highly weight genes predictive of control-defined cell states while removing variance from non-explanatory genes, producing an upweighted matrix for semi-supervised clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No control-defined cell-state labels exist yet — NCFS is supervised by control Louvain clusters, so run optimize_louvain/clustering first Data are not in a scanpy AnnData structure with log1p normalization applied — ICAT makes heavy use of the scanpy library and AnnData data structure The goal is integration across treatments rather than identifying perturbation-unique cell states — the paper reports integration workflows behave differently from ICAT

skills.description: Use when you need to statistically judge whether local structures in a t-SNE/UMAP embedding reflect real high-dimensional signal rather than stochastic DR distortion, e.g. to color cells by embedding quality or pick DR hyperparameters.
skills.name: neighborhood-correspondence-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: neighborhood-correspondence-statistical-testing Use when you need to statistically judge whether local structures in a t-SNE/UMAP embedding reflect real high-dimensional signal rather than stochastic DR distortion, e.g. to color cells by embedding quality or pick DR hyperparameters. Datasets that are not normalized — the article notes 'EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets', so quality analyses of entire unnormalized pipelines are out of scope When you need very small p values with high resolution — p values have finite empirical resolution bounded by the number of null embeddings, so the number of nulls you can afford sets the lower bound on p http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Performs an empirical hypothesis test on dimensionally-reduced embeddings by comparing each sample's neighborhood correspondence between the high-dimensional space and its projection against a null distribution generated via marginal resampling, yielding per-sample EMBEDR p values that separate real structure from algorithm-induced noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Performs an empirical hypothesis test on dimensionally-reduced embeddings by comparing each sample's neighborhood correspondence between the high-dimensional space and its projection against a null distribution generated via marginal resampling, yielding per-sample EMBEDR p values that separate real structure from algorithm-induced noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets that are not normalized — the article notes 'EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets', so quality analyses of entire unnormalized pipelines are out of scope When you need very small p values with high resolution — p values have finite empirical resolution bounded by the number of null embeddings, so the number of nulls you can afford sets the lower bound on p

skills.description: Use when building a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) from a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix and you must estimate rho_xy|z(k) via scatter-diagram neighborhood counts given a conditional gene z.
skills.name: neighborhood-count-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: neighborhood-count-probability-estimation Use when building a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) from a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix and you must estimate rho_xy|z(k) via scatter-diagram neighborhood counts given a conditional gene z. The goal is a plain (unconditioned) CSN of gene-gene associations without filtering indirect associations — no conditional gene z is involved The input is already a network/degree matrix (e.g., a CNDM) rather than raw normalized gene expression values, so no scatter diagram can be constructed Causal gene association networks with directed edges are required — c-CSN explicitly does not obtain directions of gene associations http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Numerically estimates the conditional co-expression statistic rho_xy|z(k) for the c-CSN method by counting scatter-diagram neighborhood points in 3D gene expression space (genes x, y, conditional gene z) for each cell k, then normalizing it for the conditional-independence hypothesis test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Numerically estimates the conditional co-expression statistic rho_xy|z(k) for the c-CSN method by counting scatter-diagram neighborhood points in 3D gene expression space (genes x, y, conditional gene z) for each cell k, then normalizing it for the conditional-independence hypothesis test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a plain (unconditioned) CSN of gene-gene associations without filtering indirect associations — no conditional gene z is involved The input is already a network/degree matrix (e.g., a CNDM) rather than raw normalized gene expression values, so no scatter diagram can be constructed Causal gene association networks with directed edges are required — c-CSN explicitly does not obtain directions of gene associations

skills.description: Use when adapting a pre-trained source classifier to unlabeled scRNA-seq target data source-free, and you need self-supervised regularization on 'known' cells using neighborhood structure to counter batch effect.

skills.search_text: neighborhood-regularization-in-transfer-learning Use when adapting a pre-trained source classifier to unlabeled scRNA-seq target data source-free, and you need self-supervised regularization on 'known' cells using neighborhood structure to counter batch effect. When raw source data are available and explicit source-target feature alignment can be performed directly (scEMAIL is designed for the source-free setting) When the target cell has been assigned to the 'unknown' group — affinity constraints are imposed only on 'known' cells to avoid noisy supervision http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A source-free transfer-learning regularization technique from scEMAIL that gathers multi-order neighbors (bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional) of each target cell in global scope and imposes weighted local affinity constraints on 'known' cells, mitigating batch effect without accessing raw source data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: A source-free transfer-learning regularization technique from scEMAIL that gathers multi-order neighbors (bidirectional, unidirectional, and extensional) of each target cell in global scope and imposes weighted local affinity constraints on 'known' cells, mitigating batch effect without accessing raw source data.

skills.description: Use when fitting lasso/elastic-net or caret-based models on high-dimensional data (e.g. RNA-seq with far more predictors than samples) and you need unbiased performance estimates plus feature selection without information leakage.
skills.name: nested-cross-validation-model-fitting
skills.search_text: nested-cross-validation-model-fitting Use when fitting lasso/elastic-net or caret-based models on high-dimensional data (e.g. RNA-seq with far more predictors than samples) and you need unbiased performance estimates plus feature selection without information leakage. Dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3–1/3 train/test split — nested CV's main rationale is biomedical data too small for a fixed split, where the left-out test set is too small for reliable accuracy determination Predictors have already been filtered on the whole dataset before cross-validation — this reintroduces the selection bias the skill is designed to avoid; filters must be nested within the outer CV loop The goal is unsupervised analysis or simple univariate testing rather than supervised predictive model fitting and performance estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit predictive models with fully nested k × l-fold cross-validation using the nestedcv R package, tuning hyperparameters (e.g. glmnet lambda and alpha) on inner folds and estimating unbiased performance on left-out outer folds, with feature-selection filters nested inside the outer loop. Designed for high-dimensional biomedical data (P ≫ n) where a single train/test split is unreliable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Fit predictive models with fully nested k × l-fold cross-validation using the nestedcv R package, tuning hyperparameters (e.g. glmnet lambda and alpha) on inner folds and estimating unbiased performance on left-out outer folds, with feature-selection filters nested inside the outer loop. Designed for high-dimensional biomedical data (P ≫ n) where a single train/test split is unreliable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3–1/3 train/test split — nested CV's main rationale is biomedical data too small for a fixed split, where the left-out test set is too small for reliable accuracy determination Predictors have already been filtered on the whole dataset before cross-validation — this reintroduces the selection bias the skill is designed to avoid; filters must be nested within the outer CV loop The goal is unsupervised analysis or simple univariate testing rather than supervised predictive model fitting and performance estimation

skills.description: Use when a small-n, high-predictor-count (P >> n) dataset needs unbiased model accuracy (e.g. ROC AUC) while feature selection or class balancing must be embedded inside the CV loop to avoid information leakage.
skills.name: nested-cross-validation-performance-estimation
skills.search_text: nested-cross-validation-performance-estimation Use when a small-n, high-predictor-count (P >> n) dataset needs unbiased model accuracy (e.g. ROC AUC) while feature selection or class balancing must be embedded inside the CV loop to avoid information leakage. The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split without severe small-test-set inaccuracy — nested CV is motivated by biomedical datasets too small for this split The goal is feature ranking or biological interpretation rather than unbiased accuracy estimation of a final fitted model Predictor count is modest relative to sample size and no embedded feature selection or hyperparameter tuning is needed, making simple k-fold CV sufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Unbiased estimation of predictive model performance in high-dimensional (P >> n) settings using fully nested k x l-fold cross-validation via the nestedcv R package, with hyperparameter tuning on inner folds and unbiased performance measured on concatenated left-out outer-fold test predictions. Prevents the overoptimistic ROC AUC bias caused by whole-dataset feature filtering or balancing done outside the CV loop. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Unbiased estimation of predictive model performance in high-dimensional (P >> n) settings using fully nested k x l-fold cross-validation via the nestedcv R package, with hyperparameter tuning on inner folds and unbiased performance measured on concatenated left-out outer-fold test predictions. Prevents the overoptimistic ROC AUC bias caused by whole-dataset feature filtering or balancing done outside the CV loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split without severe small-test-set inaccuracy — nested CV is motivated by biomedical datasets too small for this split The goal is feature ranking or biological interpretation rather than unbiased accuracy estimation of a final fitted model Predictor count is modest relative to sample size and no embedded feature selection or hyperparameter tuning is needed, making simple k-fold CV sufficient

skills.description: Use when testing whether adding a sample covariate (group, condition) or its interaction with pseudotime significantly improves a gene-level generalized model, e.g., to call XDE/TDE genes.
skills.name: nested-model-likelihood-ratio-testing
skills.search_text: nested-model-likelihood-ratio-testing Use when testing whether adding a sample covariate (group, condition) or its interaction with pseudotime significantly improves a gene-level generalized model, e.g., to call XDE/TDE genes. When the compared models are not nested (the likelihood-ratio statistic is only valid between nested null and full models). When the goal is trajectory inference itself (Monocle/TSCAN/Slingshot) rather than testing covariate-associated expression differences along pseudotime. When sample-level variability must be modeled natively by Lamian's multi-sample framework — this skill's Monocle2 adaptation (monocle2TrajTestCorr) exists because Monocle2 does not natively support XDE analysis and Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support Monocle2/3 or Slingshot trajectories. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Hypothesis-testing strategy used by Lamian (and its Monocle2 adaptation monocle2TrajTestCorr) in which a null generalized model is nested within a full model and a permutation-based likelihood ratio test assesses whether the added covariate terms (e.g., group, group-by-pseudotime interaction) significantly improve fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Hypothesis-testing strategy used by Lamian (and its Monocle2 adaptation monocle2TrajTestCorr) in which a null generalized model is nested within a full model and a permutation-based likelihood ratio test assesses whether the added covariate terms (e.g., group, group-by-pseudotime interaction) significantly improve fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the compared models are not nested (the likelihood-ratio statistic is only valid between nested null and full models). When the goal is trajectory inference itself (Monocle/TSCAN/Slingshot) rather than testing covariate-associated expression differences along pseudotime. skills.description: Use when a trait- or cell-type-associated co-expression module or GRN has already been inferred (e.g. SCANet WGCNA modules like M11/M4) and you need mechanistic drug repurposing candidates targeting its hub/key-driver genes.
skills.name: network-based-drug-repurposing
skills.search_text: network-based-drug-repurposing Use when a trait- or cell-type-associated co-expression module or GRN has already been inferred (e.g. SCANet WGCNA modules like M11/M4) and you need mechanistic drug repurposing candidates targeting its hub/key-driver genes. You have no network module yet — run SCANet's upstream steps first (pseudo-bulk aggregation, modified WGCNA GCN inference, module selection, GCN→GRN conversion) before drug repurposing; the module/trait association must already be established (e.g. M11 highest positive correlation with deceased patients). The gene list is not from human tissue/cells — Drugst.One maps to the human interactome and human-focused drug–target databases, so non-human networks need prior orthology mapping. Strict bit-for-bit reproducibility across runs is required — Drugst.One drug–target databases update weekly, so result sets may drift across database versions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify repurposable drugs by mapping a trait-associated gene co-expression network (GCN) or gene regulatory network (GRN) — e.g. the M11 classical monocyte module from deceased COVID-19 patients or the M4 ISC module from obese mice — onto drug–target databases via SCANet and Drugst.One, using NeDRex (DrugBank + DrugCentral) as the default interaction source. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Identify repurposable drugs by mapping a trait-associated gene co-expression network (GCN) or gene regulatory network (GRN) — e.g. the M11 classical monocyte module from deceased COVID-19 patients or the M4 ISC module from obese mice — onto drug–target databases via SCANet and Drugst.One, using NeDRex (DrugBank + DrugCentral) as the default interaction source.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no network module yet — run SCANet's upstream steps first (pseudo-bulk aggregation, modified WGCNA GCN inference, module selection, GCN→GRN conversion) before drug repurposing; the module/trait association must already be established (e.g. M11 highest positive correlation with deceased patients). The gene list is not from human tissue/cells — Drugst.One maps to the human interactome and human-focused drug–target databases, so non-human networks need prior orthology mapping. Strict bit-for-bit reproducibility across runs is required — Drugst.One drug–target databases update weekly, so result sets may drift across database versions.

skills.name: network-benchmark-auc-evaluation
skills.search_text: network-benchmark-auc-evaluation Use when a directed TF-target network (e.g. from scGATE, CellOracle, Loregic) must be quantitatively scored against a known ground-truth GRN to reproduce or report AUROC/AUPRC benchmark performance. No ground-truth GRN is available for the tissue/cell type (no deposited GRN and no qualifying ChIP-seq data — remember the <50 peaks and non-physiological-condition exclusions) The network output is an unranked binary edge list with no confidence scores (e.g. log10 Bayes Factor), since AUROC/AUPRC require ranked predictions The goal is to validate Boolean logic gate structure against curated relationships rather than edge-level network benchmarking; scGATE itself notes that directed networks do not convey combinatorial relationships among regulating factors http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark an inferred directed TF-gene regulatory network against a deposited ground-truth GRN by computing AUROC and AUPRC over Bayes-Factor-ranked edges, as done for scGATE on the mouse haematopoiesis, Tabula Muris, Cusanovich scATAC-seq, and Buenrostro human haematopoiesis datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Benchmark an inferred directed TF-gene regulatory network against a deposited ground-truth GRN by computing AUROC and AUPRC over Bayes-Factor-ranked edges, as done for scGATE on the mouse haematopoiesis, Tabula Muris, Cusanovich scATAC-seq, and Buenrostro human haematopoiesis datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth GRN is available for the tissue/cell type (no deposited GRN and no qualifying ChIP-seq data — remember the <50 peaks and non-physiological-condition exclusions) The network output is an unranked binary edge list with no confidence scores (e.g. log10 Bayes Factor), since AUROC/AUPRC require ranked predictions The goal is to validate Boolean logic gate structure against curated relationships rather than edge-level network benchmarking; scGATE itself notes that directed networks do not convey combinatorial relationships among regulating factors

skills.description: Use when you need to show that SR-based potency discrimination (e.g. pluripotent vs non-pluripotent cells) or its monotonic decrease with developmental stage collapses when expression values are reshuffled over the PPI network — i.
skills.name: network-constrained-expression-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: network-constrained-expression-permutation-testing Use when you need to show that SR-based potency discrimination (e.g. pluripotent vs non-pluripotent cells) or its monotonic decrease with developmental stage collapses when expression values are reshuffled over the PPI network — i. When the goal is simply to estimate differentiation potency of cells — use SCENT's standard SR estimation workflow on the unpermuted expression matrix instead. When the expression matrix has no mapping onto the PPI network — unrestricted (non-network-constrained) permutation destroys the very network-dependence this ablation is designed to test. When the claim to validate involves transcriptomic entropy measures that do not use network information (e.g. those used in StemID and SLICE) — this skill tests network-constrained signalling entropy, not those measures. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A network-reshuffling null ablation that randomly permutes gene expression values over a fixed PPI network (preserving network structure) to test whether signalling entropy (SR), as computed by SCENT, depends on network-constrained expression patterns rather than expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: A network-reshuffling null ablation that randomly permutes gene expression values over a fixed PPI network (preserving network structure) to test whether signalling entropy (SR), as computed by SCENT, depends on network-constrained expression patterns rather than expression alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is simply to estimate differentiation potency of cells — use SCENT's standard SR estimation workflow on the unpermuted expression matrix instead. When the expression matrix has no mapping onto the PPI network — unrestricted (non-network-constrained) permutation destroys the very network-dependence this ablation is designed to test. When the claim to validate involves transcriptomic entropy measures that do not use network information (e.g. those used in StemID and SLICE) — this skill tests network-constrained signalling entropy, not those measures.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data along a single developmental lineage plus a prior gene interaction network are available and the goal is to identify the driver regulators (e.g., top-20 per lineage) steering that cell fate trajectory.
skills.name: network-control-theory-driver-regulator-identification
skills.search_text: network-control-theory-driver-regulator-identification Use when scRNA-seq data along a single developmental lineage plus a prior gene interaction network are available and the goal is to identify the driver regulators (e.g., top-20 per lineage) steering that cell fate trajectory. The trajectory contains multiple fate branches or bifurcations that need simultaneous analysis — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time The question involves extrinsic control such as cell–cell communication, spatial location, or epigenetic regulation — CEFCON models only intracellular RNA-level factors Supervised training labels (ground-truth GRN edges) are available for the cell type — a supervised framework such as GENELink may yield superior results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Identifies driver regulators controlling cell fate decisions by modeling cell fate dynamics with network control theory on a cell-lineage-specific GRN inferred by CEFCON's graph attention network, combining control-based methods with an influence score to rank candidate driver regulators per lineage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Identifies driver regulators controlling cell fate decisions by modeling cell fate dynamics with network control theory on a cell-lineage-specific GRN inferred by CEFCON's graph attention network, combining control-based methods with an influence score to rank candidate driver regulators per lineage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory contains multiple fate branches or bifurcations that need simultaneous analysis — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time The question involves extrinsic control such as cell–cell communication, spatial location, or epigenetic regulation — CEFCON models only intracellular RNA-level factors Supervised training labels (ground-truth GRN edges) are available for the cell type — a supervised framework such as GENELink may yield superior results

skills.description: Use when fitting MuDCoD (or similar smoothed spectral community detection) to multi-subject dynamic networks and the eigenvector-smoothing penalty strengths alpha (over time points) and beta (across subjects) must be tuned rather than guessed.
skills.name: network-cross-validation-hyperparameter-tuning
skills.search_text: network-cross-validation-hyperparameter-tuning Use when fitting MuDCoD (or similar smoothed spectral community detection) to multi-subject dynamic networks and the eigenvector-smoothing penalty strengths alpha (over time points) and beta (across subjects) must be tuned rather than guessed. The number of communities K is not determined by this procedure — K is selected via the eigengap of the degree-normalized Laplacian within MuDCoD (opt_K/max_K parameters), so do not use cross-validation to pick K. Input is a single-subject or single-time-point network: alpha (temporal smoothness) and beta (subject smoothness) penalties are undefined without multiple time points and multiple subjects. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 A re-sampling network cross-validation procedure (Li et al. 2020, as used in MuDCoD's examples/cross_validation.py) that grid-searches the smoothing hyper-parameters alpha and beta by selecting the pair that maximizes the degree-corrected block model (DCBM) likelihood on held-out network data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: A re-sampling network cross-validation procedure (Li et al. 2020, as used in MuDCoD's examples/cross_validation.py) that grid-searches the smoothing hyper-parameters alpha and beta by selecting the pair that maximizes the degree-corrected block model (DCBM) likelihood on held-out network data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of communities K is not determined by this procedure — K is selected via the eigengap of the degree-normalized Laplacian within MuDCoD (opt_K/max_K parameters), so do not use cross-validation to pick K. Input is a single-subject or single-time-point network: alpha (temporal smoothness) and beta (subject smoothness) penalties are undefined without multiple time points and multiple subjects.

skills.description: Use when scLink networks have been inferred for multiple conditions or time points and you need to identify genes whose connectivity (hub status) changes, e.g., 0 h vs 96 h of DE differentiation.
skills.name: network-degree-hub-identification
skills.search_text: network-degree-hub-identification Use when scLink networks have been inferred for multiple conditions or time points and you need to identify genes whose connectivity (hub status) changes, e.g., 0 h vs 96 h of DE differentiation. skills.search_text: network-sparsity-comparison Use when comparing per-cell edge counts of CSN versus CCSN built from a normalized scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., Buettner mESC) to verify that conditional independence testing yields sparser, direct-association-only gene–gene networks. The goal is a denser co-expression network that includes indirect associations — CSN alone is intended for that, and CCSN filtering would remove them by design Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated gene–gene association matrix — CCSN construction is defined per single cell and requires per-cell expression vectors The analysis requires causal/directed gene interactions — the paper states directions of gene associations cannot be obtained with c-CSN http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the c-CSN paper's finding that conditional cell-specific networks (CCSNs) are much sparser per cell than baseline CSNs, because conditional independence testing filters out indirect gene–gene associations that cause CSN's overestimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Reproduces the c-CSN paper's finding that conditional cell-specific networks (CCSNs) are much sparser per cell than baseline CSNs, because conditional independence testing filters out indirect gene–gene associations that cause CSN's overestimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a denser co-expression network that includes indirect associations — CSN alone is intended for that, and CCSN filtering would remove them by design Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated gene–gene association matrix — CCSN construction is defined per single cell and requires per-cell expression vectors The analysis requires causal/directed gene interactions — the paper states directions of gene associations cannot be obtained with c-CSN

skills.description: Use when a task asks you to reproduce, verify, or cross-check reported network statistics (e.g. '16 of 90 genes with correlation >= 0.9', 'GRN regulators GATA2, MAFF, FOSB', Table 2 / Fig. 3B / Fig. 3D values) from a co-expression or regulatory network analysis.
skills.name: network-statistics-reproduction
skills.search_text: network-statistics-reproduction Use when a task asks you to reproduce, verify, or cross-check reported network statistics (e.g. '16 of 90 genes with correlation >= 0.9', 'GRN regulators GATA2, MAFF, FOSB', Table 2 / Fig. 3B / Fig. 3D values) from a co-expression or regulatory network analysis. The goal is de novo discovery of regulators or modules rather than checking previously reported statistics — use the upstream GCN/GRN inference skill instead Input data is not the classical monocyte population or the module gene lists were not retained from a prior GCN run, making the reported correlation counts (16/90, 11/137) unreproducible Only correlation-based GCN statistics are needed and no GRN conversion is in scope; GRNBoost2/RcisTarget overhead is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A validation skill for reproducing published gene co-expression network (GCN) and gene regulatory network (GRN) statistics — per-module correlation-count thresholds and transcription factor regulator identities — so that a re-run pipeline can be checked against reported values such as SCANet's M11/M21 monocyte modules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: A validation skill for reproducing published gene co-expression network (GCN) and gene regulatory network (GRN) statistics — per-module correlation-count thresholds and transcription factor regulator identities — so that a re-run pipeline can be checked against reported values such as SCANet's M11/M21 monocyte modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery of regulators or modules rather than checking previously reported statistics — use the upstream GCN/GRN inference skill instead Input data is not the classical monocyte population or the module gene lists were not retained from a prior GCN run, making the reported correlation counts (16/90, 11/137) unreproducible Only correlation-based GCN statistics are needed and no GRN conversion is in scope; GRNBoost2/RcisTarget overhead is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple GRN inference methods on single-cell expression data and you need quantitative, method-agnostic topology and reproducibility metrics (scale-free fit, edge counts, betweenness variance, edge overlap) to judge which method's networks are structurally most plausible.
skills.name: network-topology-metric-computation
skills.search_text: network-topology-metric-computation Use when comparing multiple GRN inference methods on single-cell expression data and you need quantitative, method-agnostic topology and reproducibility metrics (scale-free fit, edge counts, betweenness variance, edge overlap) to judge which method's networks are structurally most plausible. The network has not yet been inferred — this skill evaluates existing GRNs and cannot substitute for running SCING, ppcor, PIDC, or GRNBOOST2 on the expression data You need perturbation-based accuracy validation (e.g., perturb-seq target prediction or cosine-similarity held-out expression tests) rather than structural topology comparison The network was built from spatial transcriptomics where spatial information should be leveraged during construction — SCING itself does not use spatial coordinates in GRN construction, so topology metrics alone will not capture spatial specificity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute structural topology metrics on inferred gene regulatory networks — scale-free degree-distribution fit R-squared, edge/gene counts, betweenness centrality variance, and normalized edge overlap between independently built networks — to benchmark GRN inference methods such as SCING, ppcor, PIDC, and GRNBOOST2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Compute structural topology metrics on inferred gene regulatory networks — scale-free degree-distribution fit R-squared, edge/gene counts, betweenness centrality variance, and normalized edge overlap between independently built networks — to benchmark GRN inference methods such as SCING, ppcor, PIDC, and GRNBOOST2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet been inferred — this skill evaluates existing GRNs and cannot substitute for running SCING, ppcor, PIDC, or GRNBOOST2 on the expression data You need perturbation-based accuracy validation (e.g., perturb-seq target prediction or cosine-similarity held-out expression tests) rather than structural topology comparison The network was built from spatial transcriptomics where spatial information should be leveraged during construction — SCING itself does not use spatial coordinates in GRN construction, so topology metrics alone will not capture spatial specificity

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted gene networks from attention- or regression-based inference methods to a directed source-to-target ground truth (e.g., Omnipath) whose regulators have sparse out-degree, so predicted edge matrices must be transposed to align regulator/target conventions.
skills.name: network-transpose-normalization
skills.search_text: network-transpose-normalization Use when comparing predicted gene networks from attention- or regression-based inference methods to a directed source-to-target ground truth (e.g., Omnipath) whose regulators have sparse out-degree, so predicted edge matrices must be transposed to align regulator/target conventions. The predicted network and the ground-truth database already share the same regulator/target axis convention — transposing would corrupt the comparison The ground truth is undirected (e.g., literature co-mention networks) where orientation is meaningless The inference method already outputs edges in the source-to-target convention of the benchmark (e.g., methods explicitly trained to predict regulators of targets) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalizes the orientation of inferred gene regulatory networks (regulators vs. targets) before benchmarking against a directed ground-truth database such as Omnipath, by taking the transpose of predicted networks when the ground truth's edge direction convention (sparse out-degree of sources) differs from the inference method's convention. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Normalizes the orientation of inferred gene regulatory networks (regulators vs. targets) before benchmarking against a directed ground-truth database such as Omnipath, by taking the transpose of predicted networks when the ground truth's edge direction convention (sparse out-degree of sources) differs from the inference method's convention.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The predicted network and the ground-truth database already share the same regulator/target axis convention — transposing would corrupt the comparison The ground truth is undirected (e.g., literature co-mention networks) where orientation is meaningless The inference method already outputs edges in the source-to-target convention of the benchmark (e.g., methods explicitly trained to predict regulators of targets)

skills.description: Use when you have a predicted protein interaction network with confidence scores (e.g. FAVA output filtered at ≥70% Pearson correlation confidence) and must quantify its novelty and agreement against STRING or hu.MAP 2.0.
skills.name: network-validation-against-reference-databases
skills.search_text: network-validation-against-reference-databases Use when you have a predicted protein interaction network with confidence scores (e.g. FAVA output filtered at ≥70% Pearson correlation confidence) and must quantify its novelty and agreement against STRING or hu.MAP 2.0. The input is not a functional association network with per-edge confidence scores (e.g. it is raw scRNA-seq expression data or a proteomics feature table — run FAVA inference first). The goal is to infer a new network from omics data rather than to validate or benchmark an existing predicted network against STRING or hu.MAP 2.0. No suitable reference database (STRING, hu.MAP, or an equivalent curated interaction set) exists for the organism being analyzed, making the overlap counts uninformative. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Validation workflow that quantifies how a FAVA-predicted functional association network agrees with (or extends beyond) established protein-network references, using STRING v11.5 and hu.MAP 2.0 as ground-truth databases and reporting overlaps for understudied (IDG Tdark) proteins. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Validation workflow that quantifies how a FAVA-predicted functional association network agrees with (or extends beyond) established protein-network references, using STRING v11.5 and hu.MAP 2.0 as ground-truth databases and reporting overlaps for understudied (IDG Tdark) proteins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a functional association network with per-edge confidence scores (e.g. it is raw scRNA-seq expression data or a proteomics feature table — run FAVA inference first). The goal is to infer a new network from omics data rather than to validate or benchmark an existing predicted network against STRING or hu.MAP 2.0. No suitable reference database (STRING, hu.MAP, or an equivalent curated interaction set) exists for the organism being analyzed, making the overlap counts uninformative.

skills.description: Use when comparing enrichment/activity-inference methods that differ only in whether they leverage interaction weights, or when validating that weight-aware decoupleR methods outperform their weight-ignoring counterparts on perturbed-regulator prediction.
skills.name: network-weight-leveraging-method-comparison
skills.search_text: network-weight-leveraging-method-comparison Use when comparing enrichment/activity-inference methods that differ only in whether they leverage interaction weights, or when validating that weight-aware decoupleR methods outperform their weight-ignoring counterparts on perturbed-regulator prediction. When comparing methods that differ in more than weight handling (e.g. different network resources or statistics entirely) — this skill tests the specific with-weights vs. without-weights contrast for paired method counterparts. When no perturbation ground truth (perturbed regulators) is available for AUROC/AUPRC evaluation, since decoupleRBench requires a response vector of perturbed vs. non-perturbed regulators. When the network interactions carry no sign or weight information, since the contrast being tested does not exist. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Reproduces the decoupleR benchmark analysis testing whether regulator-activity inference methods perform better when the sign/weight of prior-knowledge network interactions is taken into account versus ignored, using paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank testing across dataset/regulator combinations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Reproduces the decoupleR benchmark analysis testing whether regulator-activity inference methods perform better when the sign/weight of prior-knowledge network interactions is taken into account versus ignored, using paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank testing across dataset/regulator combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing methods that differ in more than weight handling (e.g. different network resources or statistics entirely) — this skill tests the specific with-weights vs. without-weights contrast for paired method counterparts. When no perturbation ground truth (perturbed regulators) is available for AUROC/AUPRC evaluation, since decoupleRBench requires a response vector of perturbed vs. non-perturbed regulators. When the network interactions carry no sign or weight information, since the contrast being tested does not exist.

skills.description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN cell-type classifier needs feature interpretation — i.e., you must rank genes by DeepLIFT attribution per cell type and/or validate those attributions against differential expression marker lists.
skills.name: neural-attribution-gene-ranking-interpretation
skills.search_text: neural-attribution-gene-ranking-interpretation Use when a trained scSHARP GCN cell-type classifier needs feature interpretation — i.e., you must rank genes by DeepLIFT attribution per cell type and/or validate those attributions against differential expression marker lists. You need a standalone marker-gene discovery pipeline with no trained GCN — the attributions are only defined relative to the scSHARP GCN classifier You expect DeepLIFT attributions to replace differential expression: the paper found many genes not jointly identified by both methods, so it serves as a complementary analysis, not a substitute Input is not raw single-cell counts — the scSHARP tooling explicitly requests raw counts ('Please input raw counts.') Extracts per-cell-type gene importance scores from a trained scSHARP GCN using DeepLIFT (via the scSHARP.interpret module), then compares the top-ten attributed genes with Wilcoxon differential-expression rankings to assess whether network attributions identify cell type marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad360
skills.summary: Extracts per-cell-type gene importance scores from a trained scSHARP GCN using DeepLIFT (via the scSHARP.interpret module), then compares the top-ten attributed genes with Wilcoxon differential-expression rankings to assess whether network attributions identify cell type marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a standalone marker-gene discovery pipeline with no trained GCN — the attributions are only defined relative to the scSHARP GCN classifier You expect DeepLIFT attributions to replace differential expression: the paper found many genes not jointly identified by both methods, so it serves as a complementary analysis, not a substitute Input is not raw single-cell counts — the scSHARP tooling explicitly requests raw counts ('Please input raw counts.')

skills.description: Use when training DCNet (or a similar gene-embedded ANN) on bulk RNA-seq data and you need to test whether zero-fill input perturbation improves generalization, or when comparing autoencoder sizes vs. dropout variants by RMSE.
skills.name: neural-network-dropout-perturbation
skills.search_text: neural-network-dropout-perturbation Use when training DCNet (or a similar gene-embedded ANN) on bulk RNA-seq data and you need to test whether zero-fill input perturbation improves generalization, or when comparing autoencoder sizes vs. dropout variants by RMSE. Input is already a deconvolved cell-abundance/feature table rather than a gene-by-sample bulk RNA-seq matrix The marker-gene index files (index.pkl, relation_matrix.pkl) cannot be matched to the input gene symbols, so the neuron-gene embedding cannot be constructed The goal is deconvolution with other tools (CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) run under default parameters rather than training the DCNet architecture itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Augment DCNet training by randomly deleting input gene-expression values with probability 0.1, 0.3, or 0.5 (zero fill), then compare RMSE of the dropout variants (DCNet-D0–D50) against AE64–AE4096 autoencoders on the TCGA 80/20 split and the independent CRC set (GSE81861) to select the best model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662

skills.description: Use when training the DCA autoencoder (64-32-64 hidden layers, 32-dim bottleneck, ZINB loss) on raw scRNA-seq counts and you need a validation-driven early-stopping and learning-rate-reduction schedule.
skills.name: neural-network-early-stopping-training
skills.search_text: neural-network-early-stopping-training Use when training the DCA autoencoder (64-32-64 hidden layers, 32-dim bottleneck, ZINB loss) on raw scRNA-seq counts and you need a validation-driven early-stopping and learning-rate-reduction schedule. Input is not raw counts (e.g., log-normalized or batch-corrected data), since the ZINB/NB noise-model likelihood assumes a sparse count structure You only need a fixed, pre-trained transformation rather than fitting an autoencoder to a new dataset Denoising with simpler methods is sufficient and the count structure/overdispersion does not need modeling http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Training-protocol skill for the DCA deep count autoencoder: train the ZINB/NB-loss autoencoder with RMSProp (learning rate 0.001), halve the learning rate by 0.1 after 20 stagnant epochs, and terminate via early stopping after 25 epochs without validation-loss improvement to prevent overfitting/overimputation of scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2

skills.search_text: neural-network-embedding-training Use when a high-dimensional single-cell (scRNA-seq or CyTOF) expression matrix must be reduced to a low-dimensional embedding at scale — especially >100k cells where t-SNE is too slow. The goal is strict local-structure visualization of a small dataset (<100k cells) where standard Barnes-Hut t-SNE completes in reasonable time The input is a low-dimensional toy dataset with few features where the siamese network's overhead offers no benefit (though ivis still works, e.g. iris) Random-noise robustness patterns matter: t-SNE yields spurious clean-boundary clusters under noise, so comparative interpretation of cluster boundaries requires care http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains a siamese neural network with a triplet loss function (via the ivis algorithm) to produce low-dimensional embeddings of high-dimensional single-cell expression data, preserving both local and global structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0

skills.description: Use when you must rank/select genes from a high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal) and DEG analysis alone cannot pick an optimal biomarker combination.
skills.name: neural-network-feature-selection
skills.search_text: neural-network-feature-selection Use when you must rank/select genes from a high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal) and DEG analysis alone cannot pick an optimal biomarker combination. The analysis goal is differential-expression p-value ranking (e.g., edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) rather than classification-power ranking of genes. Only a small sample size is available, since neural network-based approaches need a large number of samples to achieve good classification performance. A single-run ranking suffices without validation — Wx selected features vary between runs/algorithms, so unstable one-shot output is a known failure mode, not a use case. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The Wx algorithm ranks genes from high-dimensional NGS expression matrices by a discriminative index (DI) score derived from softmax regression parameters and class-average expression vectors, to select universal cancer-vs-normal biomarker candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-47016-8
skills.summary: The Wx algorithm ranks genes from high-dimensional NGS expression matrices by a discriminative index (DI) score derived from softmax regression parameters and class-average expression vectors, to select universal cancer-vs-normal biomarker candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential-expression p-value ranking (e.g., edgeR DEG-14-UGCB) rather than classification-power ranking of genes. Only a small sample size is available, since neural network-based approaches need a large number of samples to achieve good classification performance. A single-run ranking suffices without validation — Wx selected features vary between runs/algorithms, so unstable one-shot output is a known failure mode, not a use case.

skills.description: Use when two species' scRNA-seq datasets must be matched at the cell type level: gene identities differ across species, so a cross-species gene similarity distance matrix (e.g. from ProtBERT protein embeddings) is available and a confusion-matrix-style label transfer is the goal.
skills.name: neural-network-transfer-learning-training
skills.search_text: neural-network-transfer-learning-training Use when two species' scRNA-seq datasets must be matched at the cell type level: gene identities differ across species, so a cross-species gene similarity distance matrix (e.g. from ProtBERT protein embeddings) is available and a confusion-matrix-style label transfer is the goal. The analysis is single-species cell type classification only — TACTiCS explicitly requires two scRNA-seq datasets and a cross-species gene similarity distance matrix as input. A gene-similarity matrix cannot be computed (no protein sequences or embeddings available for the genes in the two datasets), since the alignment loss depends on it. The user expects one-to-one ortholog gene mapping rather than embedding-based matching — the paper's finding is that ProtBERT-based gene matching, not BLAST, drives TACTiCS's cell type matches. Trains TACTiCS, a PyTorch model with two linear embedding layers and species-specific softmax classifiers, to match cell types across species from scRNA-seq data using protein-embedding-derived gene similarity as an alignment constraint. The trained classifiers are swapped to propagate cell type labels between species via transfer learning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Trains TACTiCS, a PyTorch model with two linear embedding layers and species-specific softmax classifiers, to match cell types across species from scRNA-seq data using protein-embedding-derived gene similarity as an alignment constraint. skills.description: Use when inferring neuron-neuron communication strength from scRNA-seq for neurotransmitter-type entries (glutamate, GABA, etc.) whose 'ligand' is a small molecule synthesized and vesicularly transported by the sender group, and you must convert gene expression into a ligand abundance score.

skills.search_text: neurotransmitter-ligand-abundance-scoring Use when inferring neuron-neuron communication strength from scRNA-seq for neurotransmitter-type entries (glutamate, GABA, etc.) whose 'ligand' is a small molecule synthesized and vesicularly transported by the sender group, and you must convert gene expression into a ligand abundance score. The interaction entry is a peptide/protein ligand-receptor pair where the ligand abundance is directly the ensemble expression of one gene, so no functional-group AND/OR logic is needed The interaction database lacks curated functional grouping of contributing genes (synthetic enzymes vs. vesicular transporters), forcing a degenerate AND-only computation known to underestimate neurotransmitter ligand abundance Abundance estimates must reflect actual metabolite levels: the article warns transcriptomic ligand scores can be inconsistent with protein or metabolite levels, so single-cell proteomics/metabolomics is the wrong substrate here http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes non-peptide neurotransmitter ligand abundance from single-cell expression by grouping contributing genes (e.g., synthetic enzymes, vesicular transporters) into functional categories and combining them with AND logic (geometric mean) across groups and OR logic (arithmetic mean) within redundant groups. This avoids the dramatic underestimation of small-molecule ligand abundance that generic AND-only ligand-receptor rules produce. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Computes non-peptide neurotransmitter ligand abundance from single-cell expression by grouping contributing genes (e.g., synthetic enzymes, vesicular transporters) into functional categories and combining them with AND logic (geometric mean) across groups and OR logic (arithmetic mean) within redundant groups. This avoids the dramatic underestimation of small-molecule ligand abundance that generic AND-only ligand-receptor rules produce.
