When the target cell types are closely related and collinear (e.g., PT and DCT in mouse kidney); use the tree-guided two-stage music_prop.cluster instead, since plain NNLS has limited power to resolve similar cell types When the input bulk matrix is TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input When the goal is deconvolution of multi-condition bulk data whose clinical conditions differ from the scRNA-seq reference; MuSiC2 is the indicated iterative method http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq by ordinary (all-gene) non-negative least squares against a design matrix built from a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference; in MuSiC it is the baseline estimator returned by music_prop (Est.prop.allgene) and the initialization step for the gene-weighted W-NNLS procedure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Estimates cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq by ordinary (all-gene) non-negative least squares against a design matrix built from a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference; in MuSiC it is the baseline estimator returned by music_prop (Est.prop.allgene) and the initialization step for the gene-weighted W-NNLS procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target cell types are closely related and collinear (e.g., PT and DCT in mouse kidney); use the tree-guided two-stage music_prop.cluster instead, since plain NNLS has limited power to resolve similar cell types When the input bulk matrix is TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input When the goal is deconvolution of multi-condition bulk data whose clinical conditions differ from the scRNA-seq reference; MuSiC2 is the indicated iterative method

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting predictor from the Methods: you have a cell-cell similarity network plus a binary cell-type membership vector and need degree-normalized vote scores per cell for downstream AUROC computation.
skills.name: node-degree-null-standardization
skills.search_text: node-degree-null-standardization Use when reconstructing or reimplementing MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting predictor from the Methods: you have a cell-cell similarity network plus a binary cell-type membership vector and need degree-normalized vote scores per cell for downstream AUROC computation. Cell-type labels for the query dataset are already known and you only want a similarity map — use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS/topHits route with variableGenes instead of supervised voting Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — the predictor cannot run (README states both are critical requirements) The goal is de novo clustering rather than scoring replicability against existing labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Core MetaNeighbor scoring step: build a Spearman rank-correlation cell-cell network for a gene set, re-rank and standardize all network values to lie between 0 and 1, then compute each cell's vote as (standardized network x binary cell-type membership vector) divided by the null predictor (node degree), yielding the fraction of a cell's neighbors (including itself) in a given cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Core MetaNeighbor scoring step: build a Spearman rank-correlation cell-cell network for a gene set, re-rank and standardize all network values to lie between 0 and 1, then compute each cell's vote as (standardized network x binary cell-type membership vector) divided by the null predictor (node degree), yielding the fraction of a cell's neighbors (including itself) in a given cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels for the query dataset are already known and you only want a similarity map — use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS/topHits route with variableGenes instead of supervised voting Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — the predictor cannot run (README states both are critical requirements) The goal is de novo clustering rather than scoring replicability against existing labels

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq read-count data must be analyzed per KEGG pathway node containing multiple functionally homologous genes, to identify which homolog dominates enzymatic activity and the node's overall up/down regulation (e.g., the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564).
skills.name: node-level-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: node-level-differential-expression-analysis Use when RNA-seq read-count data must be analyzed per KEGG pathway node containing multiple functionally homologous genes, to identify which homolog dominates enzymatic activity and the node's overall up/down regulation (e.g., the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564). Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP Gene-level analysis where each node already contains a single gene and no homolog collapsing is needed Non-KEGG pathway sources lacking KGML node definitions or multi-gene homolog groups http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 FunHoP's approach of running differential expression on aggregated KEGG network nodes rather than individual genes: multi-gene nodes are collapsed using RNA-seq read counts (weighted by gene length and ratio), then Voom is applied at the node level with P < 0.05 cutoff and a log2(P)-transformed value scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: FunHoP's approach of running differential expression on aggregated KEGG network nodes rather than individual genes: multi-gene nodes are collapsed using RNA-seq read counts (weighted by gene length and ratio), then Voom is applied at the node level with P < 0.05 cutoff and a log2(P)-transformed value scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP Gene-level analysis where each node already contains a single gene and no homolog collapsing is needed Non-KEGG pathway sources lacking KGML node definitions or multi-gene homolog groups

skills.name: node-level-read-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: node-level-read-count-aggregation Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes contain multiple functionally homologous genes catalyzing the same reaction and you need a single node-level RNA-seq read-count value plus identification of the dominant (most-expressed) gene per node. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP Count data already corrected for gene length — set 'correct' to False rather than re-correcting in load_countdata Pathway databases other than human KEGG metabolic pathways — the current FunHoP version supports only KEGG human metabolic pathways (excluding glycan-related ones) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates RNA-seq read counts across all functionally homologous genes in a multi-gene KEGG pathway node into a single node-level expression value, weighting reads by gene length and per-gene abundance ratio, as implemented in FunHoP for prostate cancer RNA-seq data analyzed in Cytoscape. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Aggregates RNA-seq read counts across all functionally homologous genes in a multi-gene KEGG pathway node into a single node-level expression value, weighting reads by gene length and per-gene abundance ratio, as implemented in FunHoP for prostate cancer RNA-seq data analyzed in Cytoscape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP Count data already corrected for gene length — set 'correct' to False rather than re-correcting in load_countdata Pathway databases other than human KEGG metabolic pathways — the current FunHoP version supports only KEGG human metabolic pathways (excluding glycan-related ones)

skills.description: Use when training a cross-modal single-cell GAN where you need stochastic generator outputs to estimate mapping uncertainty, e.g. comparing per-gene variance for genes with vs without an analogous measured modality.
skills.name: noise-augmented-gan-generator-training
skills.search_text: noise-augmented-gan-generator-training Use when training a cross-modal single-cell GAN where you need stochastic generator outputs to estimate mapping uncertainty, e.g. comparing per-gene variance for genes with vs without an analogous measured modality. When a deterministic cross-modal mapping suffices and no uncertainty quantification is needed — the noise input makes outputs stochastic and adds variance that must be averaged over draws When the input columns are not approximately in [-10, 10] after preprocessing — per the README, further preprocessing is necessary before feeding data into the network When you have a large number of input modalities to align, since the number of required generators grows quadratically and networks must be made small or separately trained http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains scMMGAN with a noise-augmented generator G(xi;z), where a draw z from an isotropic N(0,1) is concatenated to the original input, so that repeated stochastic mappings can be used to quantify per-gene mapping uncertainty (e.g., variance of 0.026 for genes with an analogous proteomic measurement vs 1.419 without). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Trains scMMGAN with a noise-augmented generator G(xi;z), where a draw z from an isotropic N(0,1) is concatenated to the original input, so that repeated stochastic mappings can be used to quantify per-gene mapping uncertainty (e.g., variance of 0.026 for genes with an analogous proteomic measurement vs 1.419 without).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a deterministic cross-modal mapping suffices and no uncertainty quantification is needed — the noise input makes outputs stochastic and adds variance that must be averaged over draws When the input columns are not approximately in [-10, 10] after preprocessing — per the README, further preprocessing is necessary before feeding data into the network When you have a large number of input modalities to align, since the number of required generators grows quadratically and networks must be made small or separately trained

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating the dsb noise model on a droplet CITE-seq dataset: you have raw+filtered Cell Ranger ADT matrices, empty droplets, and want to confirm the µ1–isotype (Cor 1) and µ1–library-size (Cor 2) correlations across single cells.
skills.name: noise-correlation-assessment-single-cell
skills.search_text: noise-correlation-assessment-single-cell Use when reproducing or validating the dsb noise model on a droplet CITE-seq dataset: you have raw+filtered Cell Ranger ADT matrices, empty droplets, and want to confirm the µ1–isotype (Cor 1) and µ1–library-size (Cor 2) correlations across single cells. The dataset has no isotype control antibodies — the article defers the caveats for dsb without isotype measurements to the Supplementary Note, so Cor 1 cannot be assessed ADT data are already normalized (e.g. CLR-normalized) — µ1 must be fitted on the dsb log-transformed, background-standardized values, not pre-normalized matrices Only filtered ADT counts are available with no raw matrix — empty droplets needed to estimate the ambient background and define µ1 cannot be obtained http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validates the two noise-model assumptions underlying dsb ADT normalization by fitting a k=2 Gaussian mixture per cell to extract the background mean µ1, then computing cross-single-cell correlations of µ1 with isotype controls (Cor 1) and with protein library size λ (Cor 2), replicating Fig. 2i of Mulè, Martins & Tsang (2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Validates the two noise-model assumptions underlying dsb ADT normalization by fitting a k=2 Gaussian mixture per cell to extract the background mean µ1, then computing cross-single-cell correlations of µ1 with isotype controls (Cor 1) and with protein library size λ (Cor 2), replicating Fig. 2i of Mulè, Martins & Tsang (2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no isotype control antibodies — the article defers the caveats for dsb without isotype measurements to the Supplementary Note, so Cor 1 cannot be assessed ADT data are already normalized (e.g. CLR-normalized) — µ1 must be fitted on the dsb log-transformed, background-standardized values, not pre-normalized matrices Only filtered ADT counts are available with no raw matrix — empty droplets needed to estimate the ambient background and define µ1 cannot be obtained

skills.description: Use when a simulated tensor with known embedded patterns (e.g., 4 temporal patterns across 3 cell types, 300 LR pairs, 12 contexts) must be shown recoverable, or when rank selection must be stress-tested against measurement noise.
skills.name: noise-perturbation-robustness-evaluation
skills.search_text: noise-perturbation-robustness-evaluation Use when a simulated tensor with known embedded patterns (e.g., 4 temporal patterns across 3 cell types, 300 LR pairs, 12 contexts) must be shown recoverable, or when rank selection must be stress-tested against measurement noise. The tensor contains missing values: the article notes 'the implemented tensor decomposition algorithm is not optimized' for missing values, so noise-robustness conclusions would not transfer There is no ground truth (e.g., real biological tensors): the article stresses that 'benchmarking CCC prediction tools is challenging due to the lack of a ground truth', so pattern-recovery accuracy cannot be judged The communication matrix is a single context (2D), where context-aware TCA and its rank-robustness analysis do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluate whether a decomposition (e.g., Tensor-cell2cell non-negative TCA on a 4D communication tensor) recovers the true latent structure by adding Gaussian noise to simulated scores and re-running the rank scan. It grounds confidence in the selected rank and factor loadings before applying the method to real biological contexts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Evaluate whether a decomposition (e.g., Tensor-cell2cell non-negative TCA on a 4D communication tensor) recovers the true latent structure by adding Gaussian noise to simulated scores and re-running the rank scan. It grounds confidence in the selected rank and factor loadings before applying the method to real biological contexts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tensor contains missing values: the article notes 'the implemented tensor decomposition algorithm is not optimized' for missing values, so noise-robustness conclusions would not transfer There is no ground truth (e.g., real biological tensors): the article stresses that 'benchmarking CCC prediction tools is challenging due to the lack of a ground truth', so pattern-recovery accuracy cannot be judged The communication matrix is a single context (2D), where context-aware TCA and its rank-robustness analysis do not apply

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how noise-tolerant a decomposition/clustering method is on scRNA-seq data: you have synthetic instances with known planted identity/activity patterns (e.g., 20 instances, 14 planted patterns, 3 noise levels) and want pattern-recovery purity per noise level.
skills.name: noise-robustness-assessment-across-instances
skills.search_text: noise-robustness-assessment-across-instances Use when you need to quantify how noise-tolerant a decomposition/clustering method is on scRNA-seq data: you have synthetic instances with known planted identity/activity patterns (e.g., 20 instances, 14 planted patterns, 3 noise levels) and want pattern-recovery purity per noise level. Input is real experimental data without planted ground-truth patterns — purity matching to generative patterns is undefined; use cell-type annotation or pathway validation instead. You only need a single-run application of ACTIONet to one dataset (e.g., the pbmc_10k_v3.h5 PBMC workflow) rather than a multi-instance noise sweep. The method under test requires a fixed optimal number of clusters and cannot accept the reference number of components set to the planted pattern count for fair baseline comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a cell-state decomposition or clustering method's robustness to noise by running it over multiple synthetic scRNA-seq instances at several noise levels and scoring pattern-recovery purity against planted generative patterns, as done for ACTIONet versus cNMF, cLDA, cICA, and Louvain baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Benchmark a cell-state decomposition or clustering method's robustness to noise by running it over multiple synthetic scRNA-seq instances at several noise levels and scoring pattern-recovery purity against planted generative patterns, as done for ACTIONet versus cNMF, cLDA, cICA, and Louvain baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data without planted ground-truth patterns — purity matching to generative patterns is undefined; use cell-type annotation or pathway validation instead. You only need a single-run application of ACTIONet to one dataset (e.g., the pbmc_10k_v3.h5 PBMC workflow) rather than a multi-instance noise sweep. The method under test requires a fixed optimal number of clusters and cannot accept the reference number of components set to the planted pattern count for fair baseline comparison.

skills.description: Use when you must choose the rank k of a randomized-SVD low-rank approximation of a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and cannot identify the 'beginning of noise' by eye from the spectrum; 50–300 chars ok.
skills.name: noise-spacing-statistical-thresholding
skills.search_text: noise-spacing-statistical-thresholding Use when you must choose the rank k of a randomized-SVD low-rank approximation of a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and cannot identify the 'beginning of noise' by eye from the spectrum; 50–300 chars ok. You already have a biologically justified fixed rank for the SVD (e.g. replicating a paper's reported k) and do not need automatic selection You have fewer than 100 singular values or want k near or above 100 — the criterion is defined only on the top-100 spectrum with the upper bound k < 100 You are thresholding the completed matrix entries themselves (ALRA's per-gene magnitude thresholding step), not selecting the SVD rank Automatically selects the rank k for ALRA's low-rank approximation by testing the spacings between the top 100 singular values against a statistical threshold: the largest spacing exceeding mu + 6*sigma, where mu and sigma are estimated from the tail (s80–s100) noise spacings. This replaces visual inspection of the singular-value spectrum with a data-driven cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Automatically selects the rank k for ALRA's low-rank approximation by testing the spacings between the top 100 singular values against a statistical threshold: the largest spacing exceeding mu + 6*sigma, where mu and sigma are estimated from the tail (s80–s100) noise spacings. This replaces visual inspection of the singular-value spectrum with a data-driven cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a biologically justified fixed rank for the SVD (e.g. replicating a paper's reported k) and do not need automatic selection You have fewer than 100 singular values or want k near or above 100 — the criterion is defined only on the top-100 spectrum with the upper bound k < 100 You are thresholding the completed matrix entries themselves (ALRA's per-gene magnitude thresholding step), not selecting the SVD rank

skills.description: Use when benchmarking supervised/semi-supervised single-cell integration methods that consume cell type labels, and you must quantify degradation under incomplete or imprecise annotations rather than only testing on curated ground truth.
skills.name: noisy-celltype-label-perturbation
skills.search_text: noisy-celltype-label-perturbation Use when benchmarking supervised/semi-supervised single-cell integration methods that consume cell type labels, and you must quantify degradation under incomplete or imprecise annotations rather than only testing on curated ground truth. When the integration methods under test do not consume cell type labels (e.g., unsupervised Harmony, FastMNN, Seurat v4, scVI, Scanorama baselines) — label perturbation has no effect on their behavior. When cell type annotations are missing entirely or too incomplete for CiLISI, since the evaluation metric requires cell type annotations and cannot be computed for cell types present in only one dataset. When the goal is final atlas construction with high-quality curated labels (e.g., the CD8 TIL atlas) rather than robustness benchmarking — do not corrupt the labels used for semi-supervised integration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking procedure from Andreatta et al. (Nat Commun 2024) that deliberately corrupts input cell type annotations — masking a fraction as 'unknown' and shuffling a fraction of the rest — to measure how robust semi-supervised integration methods (ssSTACAS, scANVI, scGen) are to noisy labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure from Andreatta et al. (Nat Commun 2024) that deliberately corrupts input cell type annotations — masking a fraction as 'unknown' and shuffling a fraction of the rest — to measure how robust semi-supervised integration methods (ssSTACAS, scANVI, scGen) are to noisy labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the integration methods under test do not consume cell type labels (e.g., unsupervised Harmony, FastMNN, Seurat v4, scVI, Scanorama baselines) — label perturbation has no effect on their behavior. When cell type annotations are missing entirely or too incomplete for CiLISI, since the evaluation metric requires cell type annotations and cannot be computed for cell types present in only one dataset. When the goal is final atlas construction with high-quality curated labels (e.g., the CD8 TIL atlas) rather than robustness benchmarking — do not corrupt the labels used for semi-supervised integration.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a GRN inference method (e.g., scKINETICS EM fitting) can recover a known ground-truth regulatory matrix A from simulated expression trajectories with added noise.
skills.name: noisy-single-cell-count-simulation
skills.search_text: noisy-single-cell-count-simulation Use when benchmarking whether a GRN inference method (e.g., scKINETICS EM fitting) can recover a known ground-truth regulatory matrix A from simulated expression trajectories with added noise. You already have real single-cell expression data with a validated ground-truth network — simulate only when a true A is needed for controlled recovery benchmarks You need velocity or manifold-constrained inference on observed data rather than a linear-systems simulation study — use the scKINETICS fitting workflow directly instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates noisy single-cell expression data by propagating sampled starting cell states through linear GRN dynamics x(t)=e^{At}x(0) and adding Gaussian noise (SD=5), enabling benchmarking of GRN recovery accuracy for methods like scKINETICS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Simulates noisy single-cell expression data by propagating sampled starting cell states through linear GRN dynamics x(t)=e^{At}x(0) and adding Gaussian noise (SD=5), enabling benchmarking of GRN recovery accuracy for methods like scKINETICS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real single-cell expression data with a validated ground-truth network — simulate only when a true A is needed for controlled recovery benchmarks You need velocity or manifold-constrained inference on observed data rather than a linear-systems simulation study — use the scKINETICS fitting workflow directly instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scLENS on real or simulated scRNA-seq datasets and you need to quantify the amount of non-binary (graded, non-zero-count) signal the embedding retains, e.g. to relate performance gains to dataset sparsity.
skills.name: non-binary-information-quantification-delta-sil-shuffle
skills.search_text: non-binary-information-quantification-delta-sil-shuffle Use when benchmarking scLENS on real or simulated scRNA-seq datasets and you need to quantify the amount of non-binary (graded, non-zero-count) signal the embedding retains, e.g. to relate performance gains to dataset sparsity. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or cluster assignment rather than a raw count matrix, since the test requires re-running scLENS on both the original and the non-zero-shuffled matrix. The dataset contains essentially no non-zero structure worth testing (near-binary data), making SILp indistinguishable from SIL and Delta-SIL uninformative. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A permutation-based diagnostic that quantifies how much non-binary (graded expression) information scLENS captures from a scRNA-seq dataset: non-zero values are shuffled, scLENS is re-run on the permuted matrix, and Delta-SIL = SIL - SILp measures the silhouette loss caused by destroying non-binary structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: A permutation-based diagnostic that quantifies how much non-binary (graded expression) information scLENS captures from a scRNA-seq dataset: non-zero values are shuffled, scLENS is re-run on the permuted matrix, and Delta-SIL = SIL - SILp measures the silhouette loss caused by destroying non-binary structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or cluster assignment rather than a raw count matrix, since the test requires re-running scLENS on both the original and the non-zero-shuffled matrix. The dataset contains essentially no non-zero structure worth testing (near-binary data), making SILp indistinguishable from SIL and Delta-SIL uninformative.

skills.description: Use when TE quantification must be benchmarked or applied on non-mammalian scRNA-seq data (e.g., Arabidopsis or Drosophila 10X alignments) and you need ARI-based comparison of TE-derived versus gene-derived cell clustering across MATES, scTE, and SoloTE.
skills.name: non-mammalian-scrnaseq-processing
skills.search_text: non-mammalian-scrnaseq-processing Use when TE quantification must be benchmarked or applied on non-mammalian scRNA-seq data (e.g., Arabidopsis or Drosophila 10X alignments) and you need ARI-based comparison of TE-derived versus gene-derived cell clustering across MATES, scTE, and SoloTE. Input data is human or mouse scRNA/scATAC — the standard MATES build_reference.py pipeline applies and this non-mammalian benchmarking extension is unnecessary You only need bulk-level TE quantification — bulk methods (Squire, TEtranscripts, Telescope) exist for that and single-cell clustering agreement is not the goal Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements (e.g., L1HS-like, several thousand bases) where MATES's 2001 bp coverage vectors yield unreliable multi-mapping rate estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Benchmarking locus-specific TE quantification from non-mammalian (Arabidopsis thaliana and Drosophila melanogaster) scRNA-seq by comparing MATES against scTE and SoloTE via cell-clustering agreement (ARI) with gene-expression reference clustering. Demonstrates that MATES's deep-learning multi-mapping read allocation extends beyond human/mouse to plant and fly single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Benchmarking locus-specific TE quantification from non-mammalian (Arabidopsis thaliana and Drosophila melanogaster) scRNA-seq by comparing MATES against scTE and SoloTE via cell-clustering agreement (ARI) with gene-expression reference clustering. Demonstrates that MATES's deep-learning multi-mapping read allocation extends beyond human/mouse to plant and fly single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is human or mouse scRNA/scATAC — the standard MATES build_reference.py pipeline applies and this non-mammalian benchmarking extension is unnecessary You only need bulk-level TE quantification — bulk methods (Squire, TEtranscripts, Telescope) exist for that and single-cell clustering agreement is not the goal Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements (e.g., L1HS-like, several thousand bases) where MATES's 2001 bp coverage vectors yield unreliable multi-mapping rate estimates

skills.description: Use when the input gene IDs or RNA-seq reads come from a non-model eukaryotic species (e.g. salamander) and downstream KEGG/GO pathway analysis requires mapping those IDs to model-organism orthologs or KEGG ortholog (KO) IDs.
skills.name: non-model-species-ortholog-annotation
skills.search_text: non-model-species-ortholog-annotation Use when the input gene IDs or RNA-seq reads come from a non-model eukaryotic species (e.g. salamander) and downstream KEGG/GO pathway analysis requires mapping those IDs to model-organism orthologs or KEGG ortholog (KO) IDs. The species already has a well-annotated reference genome/transcriptome and IDs can be mapped directly — direct annotation will outperform ortholog transfer The analysis requires gene-level resolution for proteins absent from the KO system (e.g. vitellogenin is not found in the KO system) Reads are from a taxonomic group with no suitable EcoOmicsDB sub-group database — mapping to an improper sub-group will miss key functional groups http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate non-model species gene/transcript identifiers by mapping them to orthologs in model organisms using ExpressAnalyst's integrated EcoOmicsDB ortholog database, enabling functional (KEGG, GO) analysis for eukaryotes without a reference transcriptome. This replaces de novo transcript assembly plus BLAST-based 'annotation transfer' with direct ortholog-level mapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Annotate non-model species gene/transcript identifiers by mapping them to orthologs in model organisms using ExpressAnalyst's integrated EcoOmicsDB ortholog database, enabling functional (KEGG, GO) analysis for eukaryotes without a reference transcriptome. This replaces de novo transcript assembly plus BLAST-based 'annotation transfer' with direct ortholog-level mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species already has a well-annotated reference genome/transcriptome and IDs can be mapped directly — direct annotation will outperform ortholog transfer The analysis requires gene-level resolution for proteins absent from the KO system (e.g. vitellogenin is not found in the KO system) Reads are from a taxonomic group with no suitable EcoOmicsDB sub-group database — mapping to an improper sub-group will miss key functional groups

skills.description: Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a non-model eukaryotic species (no reference transcriptome needed) and the goal is a KO-level ortholog count matrix for downstream statistical analysis.
skills.name: non-model-species-rnaseq-functional-profiling
skills.search_text: non-model-species-rnaseq-functional-profiling Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a non-model eukaryotic species (no reference transcriptome needed) and the goal is a KO-level ortholog count matrix for downstream statistical analysis. Input is already a count table or gene expression matrix — use the ExpressAnalyst/ExpressAnalystR statistical, normalization, and enrichment modules instead of re-quantifying reads. The analysis targets specific protein-coding genes absent from the KO system (e.g., vitellogenin is not found in the KO system) or requires full transcriptome-level coverage; KO-based annotation covers only ~76% of human and ~61% of zebrafish protein-coding genes. The sample's taxonomy is distant from the selected database sub-group (e.g., mapping protist reads to the 'fishes' database) — key functional groups may be missed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantify raw RNA-seq reads from non-model species directly into KEGG ortholog (KO) count tables by mapping translated reads against an EcoOmicsDB taxonomic sub-group database with Seq2Fun 2.0 via ExpressAnalyst, bypassing transcript assembly and annotation. This yields functionally coherent, reproducible gene-level features for downstream differential expression and pathway analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Quantify raw RNA-seq reads from non-model species directly into KEGG ortholog (KO) count tables by mapping translated reads against an EcoOmicsDB taxonomic sub-group database with Seq2Fun 2.0 via ExpressAnalyst, bypassing transcript assembly and annotation. This yields functionally coherent, reproducible gene-level features for downstream differential expression and pathway analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a count table or gene expression matrix — use the ExpressAnalyst/ExpressAnalystR statistical, normalization, and enrichment modules instead of re-quantifying reads. The analysis targets specific protein-coding genes absent from the KO system (e.g., vitellogenin is not found in the KO system) or requires full transcriptome-level coverage; KO-based annotation covers only ~76% of human and ~61% of zebrafish protein-coding genes. The sample's taxonomy is distant from the selected database sub-group (e.g., mapping protist reads to the 'fishes' database) — key functional groups may be missed.

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) must be filtered to an informative gene set and compressed to a ~50-dimensional representation before clustering, visualization, or classification with scDHA.
skills.name: non-negative-autoencoder-implementation
skills.search_text: non-negative-autoencoder-implementation Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) must be filtered to an informative gene set and compressed to a ~50-dimensional representation before clustering, visualization, or classification with scDHA. When the input is already a reduced feature table or a low-dimensional embedding rather than a raw genes-by-cells count matrix — scDHA's main function expects a matrix with rows as samples and columns as genes. When the goal is dropout imputation via heavy statistical modelling (e.g. CIDR's implicit imputation) rather than part-based gene filtering through a non-negative autoencoder. When downstream analysis requires trajectory or pseudotime inference directly — that is handled by scDHA's second module (stacked Bayesian autoencoder / VAE) and scDHA.pt, not this first-module filter. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Implement the first module of scDHA as a one-layer non-negative kernel autoencoder with a 50-node bottleneck that produces a part-based representation of scRNA-seq data, then use the encoder weight distribution to remove genes or components with insignificant contributions. This gene filtering step yields a compact, denoised input for downstream clustering and dimension reduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Implement the first module of scDHA as a one-layer non-negative kernel autoencoder with a 50-node bottleneck that produces a part-based representation of scRNA-seq data, then use the encoder weight distribution to remove genes or components with insignificant contributions. This gene filtering step yields a compact, denoised input for downstream clustering and dimension reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a reduced feature table or a low-dimensional embedding rather than a raw genes-by-cells count matrix — scDHA's main function expects a matrix with rows as samples and columns as genes. When the goal is dropout imputation via heavy statistical modelling (e.g. CIDR's implicit imputation) rather than part-based gene filtering through a non-negative autoencoder. When downstream analysis requires trajectory or pseudotime inference directly — that is handled by scDHA's second module (stacked Bayesian autoencoder / VAE) and scDHA.pt, not this first-module filter.

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq (ExpressionSet) and single-cell/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue are available — including overlapping individuals — and cell-type proportions must be estimated while correcting single-cell technical biases.
skills.name: non-negative-least-squares-decomposition
skills.search_text: non-negative-least-squares-decomposition Use when bulk RNA-seq (ExpressionSet) and single-cell/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue are available — including overlapping individuals — and cell-type proportions must be estimated while correcting single-cell technical biases. No single-cell reference is available and only marker genes are known — use the marker-based mode, whose relative abundances cannot be compared across cell types. The single-cell data's cell-type composition is known to deviate strongly from physiological proportions (e.g. severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest), since estimates reflect the single-cell technology's reported proportions. Very few individuals have single-cell data, making the reference profile and gene-specific transformations unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Reference-based decomposition of bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions using Bisque: build a single-cell reference profile, learn gene-specific bulk transformations, then solve a non-negative least-squares (NNLS) regression per bulk sample with non-negativity and sum-to-one constraints. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Reference-based decomposition of bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions using Bisque: build a single-cell reference profile, learn gene-specific bulk transformations, then solve a non-negative least-squares (NNLS) regression per bulk sample with non-negativity and sum-to-one constraints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No single-cell reference is available and only marker genes are known — use the marker-based mode, whose relative abundances cannot be compared across cell types. The single-cell data's cell-type composition is known to deviate strongly from physiological proportions (e.g. severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest), since estimates reflect the single-cell technology's reported proportions. Very few individuals have single-cell data, making the reference profile and gene-specific transformations unreliable.

skills.description: Use when clustering a small target scRNA-Seq dataset where a large well-annotated source dataset (shared gene space, non-negative counts) is available and rare cell types are hard to resolve with SC3 alone.
skills.name: non-negative-matrix-factorization-transfer-learning
skills.search_text: non-negative-matrix-factorization-transfer-learning Use when clustering a small target scRNA-Seq dataset where a large well-annotated source dataset (shared gene space, non-negative counts) is available and rare cell types are hard to resolve with SC3 alone. Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — vital information is lost since only genes present in both datasets can be used No labeled/annotated source dataset with overlapping cell types is available (e.g. a no-overlap setting), where transfer can degrade clustering relative to TargetCluster The expression matrix is not non-negative count-level scRNA-Seq data (NMF requires non-negativity), or the goal is batch correction/imputation rather than clustering improvement http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 An NMF-based transfer learning method that adjusts a small target scRNA-Seq dataset using a dictionary learned from a large, annotated source dataset, then feeds the modified target (X_trg_new) to SC3 for improved clustering without concatenating source and target cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: An NMF-based transfer learning method that adjusts a small target scRNA-Seq dataset using a dictionary learned from a large, annotated source dataset, then feeds the modified target (X_trg_new) to SC3 for improved clustering without concatenating source and target cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — vital information is lost since only genes present in both datasets can be used No labeled/annotated source dataset with overlapping cell types is available (e.g. a no-overlap setting), where transfer can degrade clustering relative to TargetCluster The expression matrix is not non-negative count-level scRNA-Seq data (NMF requires non-negativity), or the goal is batch correction/imputation rather than clustering improvement

skills.description: Use when a trajectory method uses RNA velocity and you need to quantify its contribution by ablating velocity (distance-only variant) and comparing pseudotime against an elapsed-time or known-ordering reference.
skills.name: non-velocity-ablation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: non-velocity-ablation-benchmarking Use when a trajectory method uses RNA velocity and you need to quantify its contribution by ablating velocity (distance-only variant) and comparing pseudotime against an elapsed-time or known-ordering reference. The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case, so the ablation comparison would test against a broken baseline. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable; the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that setting. No external reference of elapsed process time or known cell ordering exists to serve as the ground-truth clock for correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks velocity-based Cytopath pseudotime against a velocity-ablated (Cytopath-Euclidean) variant by correlating each with an external ground-truth clock (stimulation duration), quantifying how much RNA velocity contributes to pseudotime accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Benchmarks velocity-based Cytopath pseudotime against a velocity-ablated (Cytopath-Euclidean) variant by correlating each with an external ground-truth clock (stimulation duration), quantifying how much RNA velocity contributes to pseudotime accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty — the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case, so the ablation comparison would test against a broken baseline. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable; the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in that setting. No external reference of elapsed process time or known cell ordering exists to serve as the ground-truth clock for correlation.

skills.description: Use when fine-mapped noncoding GWAS variants (e.g., SCZ variants linked to genes by GrID-Net) need functional annotation of allele-specific TF binding disruption in accessible regulatory peaks.

skills.search_text: nonlinear-embedding-based-batch-quantification Use when detecting or quantifying the extent of batch effects introduced by technical non-biological factors in RNA-seq data, especially when existing PCA-based estimation may fail to capture non-linear batch effects. skills.search_text: nonlinear-manifold-network-alignment Use when two condition-specific scGRNs (e.g., mock vs morphine-treated neurons) have been denoised by CP tensor decomposition and you need a common embedding to quantify gene-wise regulatory differences. Input networks have not been denoised by CP tensor decomposition — raw subsampled pcNet networks are too noisy for meaningful alignment The two samples are highly dissimilar populations (e.g., different cell types) — the article notes scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples such as two populations of cells of the same type The goal is de novo network construction from expression data rather than comparison of already-built networks http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Aligns two denoised single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) into a shared low-dimensional latent space using nonlinear manifold alignment, so that per-gene coordinate shifts between conditions can be measured for differential regulation testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139

Input already contains fewer than ~5000 informative genes, or genes have already been pre-selected — the autoencoder cut of exactly 5000 genes would discard usable signal or add nothing The goal is supervised marker-gene discovery rather than unsupervised preprocessing — this filter uses no label information by design Data are raw counts that must not be log2-transformed (e.g., downstream tools requiring raw UMI counts) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A dimensionality-reduction pre-selection step from scEFSC that uses a single-layer non-negative kernel autoencoder to retain the 5000 most significant genes from a log2-normalized scRNA-seq matrix before downstream unsupervised feature selection and ensemble clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.04.023

skills.search_text: nonnegative-matrix-factorization-decomposition Use when comparing factorization choices for single-cell program recovery (NMF vs ICA), or when decomposing nonnegative scRNA count matrices into latent gene expression programs against simulation ground truth. skills.summary: Applying NMF-based matrix factorization to decompose pooled single-cell expression matrices into nonnegative gene expression programs (GEPs), used in the MetaTiME work as the comparator to ICA for recovering pre-embedded transcriptional programs in simulated multi-cohort data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices contain negative values (NMF requires nonnegative factorization inputs). The goal is joint low-dimensional representation across already-collected real cohorts rather than program recovery benchmarking — the article's discussion points to integration algorithms such as Harmony and scArches for that setting. Independent-component structure among programs is the explicit objective — MetaTiME used ICA 'to optimize information independence among components', and ICA slightly outperformed NMF at recovering pre-embedded GEPs in simulation.

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C interaction counts between two conditions on a bin-pair-by-cell normalized count matrix and you want DCI calls that make no assumption on the data distribution.
skills.name: nonparametric-goodness-of-fit-testing
skills.search_text: nonparametric-goodness-of-fit-testing Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C interaction counts between two conditions on a bin-pair-by-cell normalized count matrix and you want DCI calls that make no assumption on the data distribution. If you can justify a parametric count model and want maximum sensitivity: the article's simulation benchmark shows the parametric NB and especially the zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) likelihood-ratio tests outperform KS and CVM in all simulation settings (cell num=50, fold change=5, 200kb resolution). If the input is raw (not normalized) scHi-C counts: the detection functions expect a matrix of scHi-C normalized read counts, so scHiCDiff.norm should be applied first using local bias features (effective length, GC content, mappability).
