skills.search_text: novel-cell-detection-mode-ablation Use when benchmarking or configuring scNovel for novel rare cell-type discovery and you must choose among its four detection score modes (S^MSP, S^ODIN, S^SEQ, S^SIM) using AUROC/AUPR/FPR95. The task is generic cell-type annotation of query cells matching known reference types, not detecting novel/rare cell types absent from the reference You need only run scNovel's default annotation pipeline rather than compare or tune its four detection score modes Your goal is comparing scNovel against other novel cell detection methods (e.g. scLearn, scPred) rather than ablating scNovel's internal score modes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 An ablation protocol for scNovel's four novel cell detection score modes — S^MSP (maximum prediction probability), S^ODIN, S^SEQ (sequential barcode preprocessing), and S^SIM (simultaneous barcode preprocessing) — to determine which mode best detects novel rare cell types in scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: An ablation protocol for scNovel's four novel cell detection score modes — S^MSP (maximum prediction probability), S^ODIN, S^SEQ (sequential barcode preprocessing), and S^SIM (simultaneous barcode preprocessing) — to determine which mode best detects novel rare cell types in scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is generic cell-type annotation of query cells matching known reference types, not detecting novel/rare cell types absent from the reference You need only run scNovel's default annotation pipeline rather than compare or tune its four detection score modes Your goal is comparing scNovel against other novel cell detection methods (e.g. scLearn, scPred) rather than ablating scNovel's internal score modes

skills.description: Use when a pre-trained source model must annotate target scRNA-seq cells without access to source data, and the target may contain cell types absent from the source label set, with no user-specified threshold allowed.
skills.name: novel-cell-type-detection
skills.search_text: novel-cell-type-detection Use when a pre-trained source model must annotate target scRNA-seq cells without access to source data, and the target may contain cell types absent from the source label set, with no user-specified threshold allowed. The target data are known to contain only cell types present in the source label set and a bimodality test of the E-score distribution is not triggered — then all cells belong to the known group and no thresholding is needed Raw source data are available and you want explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g. ItClust-style transfer) instead of source-free adaptation Input is not single-cell omics data with a pre-trained source classifier providing soft probability vectors (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or feature tables without per-cell predictions) Detect novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data source-free by scoring each cell with an expert-ensemble E-score (entropy, confidence, consistency), testing the E-score distribution for bimodality, and partitioning cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups via an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold. This is scEMAIL's novel cell-type perception module (Wan et al., GPB 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Detect novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data source-free by scoring each cell with an expert-ensemble E-score (entropy, confidence, consistency), testing the E-score distribution for bimodality, and partitioning cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups via an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold. This is scEMAIL's novel cell-type perception module (Wan et al., GPB 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target data are known to contain only cell types present in the source label set and a bimodality test of the E-score distribution is not triggered — then all cells belong to the known group and no thresholding is needed Raw source data are available and you want explicit source-target feature alignment (e.g. ItClust-style transfer) instead of source-free adaptation Input is not single-cell omics data with a pre-trained source classifier providing soft probability vectors (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or feature tables without per-cell predictions)

skills.description: Use when a labeled t0 scRNA-seq matrix has been cross-timepoint-annotated onto a t1 matrix (CrossTimeAnnotation) and you need to flag emerged/novel cell types or tumor subclones rather than force-assigning them known labels.
skills.name: novel-cell-type-detection
skills.search_text: novel-cell-type-detection Use when a labeled t0 scRNA-seq matrix has been cross-timepoint-annotated onto a t1 matrix (CrossTimeAnnotation) and you need to flag emerged/novel cell types or tumor subclones rather than force-assigning them known labels. The novel population of interest is transcriptomically very similar to a known cell type — the article notes the detection framework 'may not work well' in that case The t0 data differ dramatically from later timepoints, so the neural-network annotation step that feeds this skill cannot be well trained You need de novo unsupervised clustering of a single-timepoint dataset with no labeled reference — this skill assumes labeled t0 cells and prior cross-timepoint annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detect cell populations at later timepoints (t1) that do not correspond to any known initial-timepoint (t0) cell type, using CASi's DetectNovelCells: UMAP-based cell-type-specific correlations, iterative Louvain two-cluster bisection, and a two-sample t-test with corr.cutoff=0.4 and p.cutoff=0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Detect cell populations at later timepoints (t1) that do not correspond to any known initial-timepoint (t0) cell type, using CASi's DetectNovelCells: UMAP-based cell-type-specific correlations, iterative Louvain two-cluster bisection, and a two-sample t-test with corr.cutoff=0.4 and p.cutoff=0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The novel population of interest is transcriptomically very similar to a known cell type — the article notes the detection framework 'may not work well' in that case The t0 data differ dramatically from later timepoints, so the neural-network annotation step that feeds this skill cannot be well trained You need de novo unsupervised clustering of a single-timepoint dataset with no labeled reference — this skill assumes labeled t0 cells and prior cross-timepoint annotation

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq (h5ad, gene activity matrices) and you suspect the target data contains cell types missing from the source annotations.
skills.name: novel-cell-type-discovery-in-cross-omics-integration
skills.search_text: novel-cell-type-discovery-in-cross-omics-integration Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq (h5ad, gene activity matrices) and you suspect the target data contains cell types missing from the source annotations. Source and target datasets are known to share all cell types — use standard scBridge label transfer without --novel_type instead Data are paired multi-omics (e.g., CITE-seq/ASAP-seq from the same cells) — scAI, MOFA+, or scJoint's paired modes are the appropriate integrators Target data are raw scATAC-seq peak matrices not yet converted to a gene activity matrix — convert with Signac first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Discovery of scATAC-seq cells from cell types absent in annotated scRNA-seq data using scBridge's structure preservation loss: unreliable target cells receive low confidence scores, are modeled with a two-component Gaussian M Model, and are predicted as a novel type. Validated by recovering scATAC-seq-only Myeloid cells in the human myocardial infarction dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Discovery of scATAC-seq cells from cell types absent in annotated scRNA-seq data using scBridge's structure preservation loss: unreliable target cells receive low confidence scores, are modeled with a two-component Gaussian M Model, and are predicted as a novel type. Validated by recovering scATAC-seq-only Myeloid cells in the human myocardial infarction dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target datasets are known to share all cell types — use standard scBridge label transfer without --novel_type instead Data are paired multi-omics (e.g., CITE-seq/ASAP-seq from the same cells) — scAI, MOFA+, or scJoint's paired modes are the appropriate integrators Target data are raw scATAC-seq peak matrices not yet converted to a gene activity matrix — convert with Signac first

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) may contain cell types absent from the curated reference, and you want annotation transfer to correctly reject those cells so the unassigned cluster can be characterized by marker genes.
skills.name: novel-cell-type-rejection-analysis
skills.search_text: novel-cell-type-rejection-analysis Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) may contain cell types absent from the curated reference, and you want annotation transfer to correctly reject those cells so the unassigned cluster can be characterized by marker genes. The reference dataset already contains the cell type of interest — annotations will simply be transferred and no novel-type rejection can occur The query dataset has fewer than ~1000 cells — DIRECTi is over-parameterized and small datasets may suffer from under-training issues The goal is mega-scale dataset integration with highly skewed cell-type composition, which the authors note risks over-correcting batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detects putative novel cell types by querying a dataset against a reference that excludes the candidate type: Cell BLAST's DIRECTi model and cell-to-cell similarity metric leave cells of the missing type unassigned ('rejected'), and differential expression on the rejected cluster confirms its identity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Detects putative novel cell types by querying a dataset against a reference that excludes the candidate type: Cell BLAST's DIRECTi model and cell-to-cell similarity metric leave cells of the missing type unassigned ('rejected'), and differential expression on the rejected cluster confirms its identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference dataset already contains the cell type of interest — annotations will simply be transferred and no novel-type rejection can occur The query dataset has fewer than ~1000 cells — DIRECTi is over-parameterized and small datasets may suffer from under-training issues The goal is mega-scale dataset integration with highly skewed cell-type composition, which the authors note risks over-correcting batches

skills.description: Use when long-read BAM/FASTQ alignments plus a reference annotation (e.g. GENCODE mm10 GTF) are available and the goal is to discover novel isoforms by requiring end-support from CAGE TSS and polyA site references before collapsing intron chains.
skills.name: novel-intron-chain-isoform-reconstruction
skills.search_text: novel-intron-chain-isoform-reconstruction Use when long-read BAM/FASTQ alignments plus a reference annotation (e.g. GENCODE mm10 GTF) are available and the goal is to discover novel isoforms by requiring end-support from CAGE TSS and polyA site references before collapsing intron chains. Reads are short-read-only (e.g. bulk Illumina junctions alone) and cannot support full-length isoform reconstruction with confirmed 5'/3' ends The goal is differential isoform expression testing among already-annotated isoforms (use DiffSplicingAnalysis/ExonQuant instead) No external TSS/polyA reference (FANTOM CAGE, polyASite) is available for the genome version, so end-based confidence filtering cannot be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct high-confidence novel isoforms by collapsing full-length, spliced long reads (ScISOr-Seq) whose 5' and 3' ends are independently validated against FANTOM CAGE peaks and polyASite 2.0 sites, yielding an enhanced GTF of novel intron-chain records (76 novel isoforms in the mouse P7 brain study). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Reconstruct high-confidence novel isoforms by collapsing full-length, spliced long reads (ScISOr-Seq) whose 5' and 3' ends are independently validated against FANTOM CAGE peaks and polyASite 2.0 sites, yielding an enhanced GTF of novel intron-chain records (76 novel isoforms in the mouse P7 brain study).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are short-read-only (e.g. bulk Illumina junctions alone) and cannot support full-length isoform reconstruction with confirmed 5'/3' ends The goal is differential isoform expression testing among already-annotated isoforms (use DiffSplicingAnalysis/ExonQuant instead) No external TSS/polyA reference (FANTOM CAGE, polyASite) is available for the genome version, so end-based confidence filtering cannot be applied

skills.description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference exists but the query set may contain cell types absent from the reference, or when comparing novel-cell-detection methods (scNovel vs scmap/scPred/scLearn) with AUROC, AUPR and FPR95 across C^novel = 1–4 settings.
skills.name: novel-rare-cell-detection-benchmarking
skills.search_text: novel-rare-cell-detection-benchmarking Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference exists but the query set may contain cell types absent from the reference, or when comparing novel-cell-detection methods (scNovel vs scmap/scPred/scLearn) with AUROC, AUPR and FPR95 across C^novel = 1–4 settings. There is no labeled reference set of known cell types — scNovel's training stage requires a reference with cross-entropy-trained cell-type labels The goal is generic auto-annotation of cell types already present in the reference, not identifying novel/rare types absent from the reference (the article notes prior annotation tools 'paid little attention to novel rare cell discovery') The data are single-cell chromatin accessibility or other non-transcriptomic modalities — the paper states the current method does not incorporate such biology information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark novel rare cell detection in single-cell transcriptomics by running scNovel (a deep neural network with barcode preprocessing) against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred and scLearn, scoring AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 with novel cells as positives across datasets of different scales and sequencing protocols. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Benchmark novel rare cell detection in single-cell transcriptomics by running scNovel (a deep neural network with barcode preprocessing) against scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred and scLearn, scoring AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 with novel cells as positives across datasets of different scales and sequencing protocols.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no labeled reference set of known cell types — scNovel's training stage requires a reference with cross-entropy-trained cell-type labels The goal is generic auto-annotation of cell types already present in the reference, not identifying novel/rare types absent from the reference (the article notes prior annotation tools 'paid little attention to novel rare cell discovery') The data are single-cell chromatin accessibility or other non-transcriptomic modalities — the paper states the current method does not incorporate such biology information

skills.description: Use when quantifying reads on novel splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE) without a spliced aligner: you have a genome FASTA, a GTF annotation, and a known read length.
skills.name: novel-splice-site-fragment-indexing
skills.search_text: novel-splice-site-fragment-indexing Use when quantifying reads on novel splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE) without a spliced aligner: you have a genome FASTA, a GTF annotation, and a known read length. Input is already a fortuna index or a pre-built H. sapiens index for the matching read length (75/100/150bp) — download it rather than rebuilding The annotation is not in GTF format or has not been segmented by bin/processGTF.sh — fortuna --index requires the preprocessed .rg.gtf Goal is full spliced alignment (e.g. building a genome BAM of spliced reads) — use a spliced aligner like STAR instead; fortuna optionally refines with its output http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Build a kallisto index over sequence fragments of annotated and 'guessed' novel transcripts — combinations of annotated splice sites — so that alignment-free pseudoalignment can count reads supporting novel splicing events. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Build a kallisto index over sequence fragments of annotated and 'guessed' novel transcripts — combinations of annotated splice sites — so that alignment-free pseudoalignment can count reads supporting novel splicing events.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fortuna index or a pre-built H. sapiens index for the matching read length (75/100/150bp) — download it rather than rebuilding The annotation is not in GTF format or has not been segmented by bin/processGTF.sh — fortuna --index requires the preprocessed .rg.gtf Goal is full spliced alignment (e.g. building a genome BAM of spliced reads) — use a spliced aligner like STAR instead; fortuna optionally refines with its output

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be quantified against a GTF annotation while simultaneously detecting unannotated splicing events (exon skipping, intron retention, alternative donor/acceptor) with per-event read counts, without a spliced aligner.
skills.name: novel-splicing-event-annotation
skills.search_text: novel-splicing-event-annotation Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be quantified against a GTF annotation while simultaneously detecting unannotated splicing events (exon skipping, intron retention, alternative donor/acceptor) with per-event read counts, without a spliced aligner. The task requires full spliced genome alignment of all reads rather than counting reads supporting annotated-splice-site-combination events (use STAR or another aligner as the primary tool, at most via fortuna --refine) Read length does not match the -rl read length used to build the fortuna index (a separate index per read length, e.g. 75/100/150 bp, is required) Novel events must include splice sites absent from the annotation and no spliced-aligner BAM is available for --refine refinement http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotation-free-of-alignment detection and counting of novel splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE, XX) using fortuna: it guesses novel combinations of annotated splice sites, builds a kallisto fragment index, pseudoaligns reads, and emits per-event supporting read counts (alt.tsv) alongside elementary signature counts (cnt.tsv). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Annotation-free-of-alignment detection and counting of novel splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE, XX) using fortuna: it guesses novel combinations of annotated splice sites, builds a kallisto fragment index, pseudoaligns reads, and emits per-event supporting read counts (alt.tsv) alongside elementary signature counts (cnt.tsv).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires full spliced genome alignment of all reads rather than counting reads supporting annotated-splice-site-combination events (use STAR or another aligner as the primary tool, at most via fortuna --refine) Read length does not match the -rl read length used to build the fortuna index (a separate index per read length, e.g. 75/100/150 bp, is required) Novel events must include splice sites absent from the annotation and no spliced-aligner BAM is available for --refine refinement

skills.description: Use when deconvolving pseudo-bulk or bulk RNA-seq mixtures with a signature matrix (e.g., built from G-PC/RankCorr/scGeneFit markers) and you need to fit cell-type fractions with CIBERSORT's linear nu-SVR approach.
skills.name: nu-svr-regression-tuning
skills.search_text: nu-svr-regression-tuning Use when deconvolving pseudo-bulk or bulk RNA-seq mixtures with a signature matrix (e.g., built from G-PC/RankCorr/scGeneFit markers) and you need to fit cell-type fractions with CIBERSORT's linear nu-SVR approach. Input is single-cell expression data that has not yet been aggregated into pseudo-bulk mixtures with known proportions The task is marker selection itself (use phenotype-cover/GreedyPC rather than deconvolution); this skill assumes a marker set already exists No ground-truth cell-type proportions are available, so JS divergence between predicted and true proportions cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tunes linear nu-SVR for CIBERSORT-style cell-type proportion deconvolution by initializing three nu-SVR instances with nu in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} and keeping the model with the lowest root-mean-square error, then scoring predicted vs. true proportions with Jensen-Shannon divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Tunes linear nu-SVR for CIBERSORT-style cell-type proportion deconvolution by initializing three nu-SVR instances with nu in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} and keeping the model with the lowest root-mean-square error, then scoring predicted vs. true proportions with Jensen-Shannon divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell expression data that has not yet been aggregated into pseudo-bulk mixtures with known proportions The task is marker selection itself (use phenotype-cover/GreedyPC rather than deconvolution); this skill assumes a marker set already exists No ground-truth cell-type proportions are available, so JS divergence between predicted and true proportions cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) that has a paired H&E image (~10000x10000 pixels) and you need per-spot cell counts and cell centroid locations before single-cell resolution reconstruction.
skills.name: nuclei-segmentation-from-he-histology-images
skills.search_text: nuclei-segmentation-from-he-histology-images Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) that has a paired H&E image (~10000x10000 pixels) and you need per-spot cell counts and cell centroid locations before single-cell resolution reconstruction. No histological (or single-channel nuclear, e.g. DAPI) image is available — alternative image types or no images complicate cell count estimation and a different strategy is needed Data are spot-level but image-free such as Slide-seq — SpatialScope replaces nucleus segmentation with singlet/doublet classification instead Goal is pure downstream deconvolution of proportions per spot (e.g. RCTD/Cell2location/CARD alone) without single-cell resolution reconstruction — segmentation-based cell counts are not required http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 Segment nuclei in H&E-stained histology images (e.g. StarDist as used inside SpatialScope) to count cells per spatial transcriptomics spot, producing per-spot cell counts and single-cell spatial locations that feed downstream cell-type identification and expression decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Segment nuclei in H&E-stained histology images (e.g. StarDist as used inside SpatialScope) to count cells per spatial transcriptomics spot, producing per-spot cell counts and single-cell spatial locations that feed downstream cell-type identification and expression decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No histological (or single-channel nuclear, e.g. DAPI) image is available — alternative image types or no images complicate cell count estimation and a different strategy is needed Data are spot-level but image-free such as Slide-seq — SpatialScope replaces nucleus segmentation with singlet/doublet classification instead Goal is pure downstream deconvolution of proportions per spot (e.g. RCTD/Cell2location/CARD alone) without single-cell resolution reconstruction — segmentation-based cell counts are not required

skills.description: Use when stress-testing a sequence-window classifier (e.g. REDInet) for robustness to incomplete RNAseq coverage, by injecting reference-genome substitutions into feature matrices and re-scoring predictions against ground truth.
skills.name: nucleotide-frequency-feature-matrix-perturbation
skills.search_text: nucleotide-frequency-feature-matrix-perturbation Use when stress-testing a sequence-window classifier (e.g. REDInet) for robustness to incomplete RNAseq coverage, by injecting reference-genome substitutions into feature matrices and re-scoring predictions against ground truth. Feature matrices already contain imputed/genomic values or are known to be fully covered — perturbation would not represent genuine missing-data conditions Evaluating REDInet on unperturbed benchmark performance (A549, HEK293T KO-WT/KO-OE ground truth sets) rather than robustness to missing flanking data Input is raw BAM/REDItools outTable rather than precomputed 8x101 feature matrices — run the REDInet pipeline first to generate feature vectors http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Simulates missing RNAseq coverage in 8x101 nucleotide-frequency feature matrices by replacing RNAseq-derived frequencies with corresponding genomic reference frequencies at >30% of the 101 flanking positions, then re-runs REDInet inference to quantify false-positive/false-negative rates under degraded input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf107
skills.summary: Simulates missing RNAseq coverage in 8x101 nucleotide-frequency feature matrices by replacing RNAseq-derived frequencies with corresponding genomic reference frequencies at >30% of the 101 flanking positions, then re-runs REDInet inference to quantify false-positive/false-negative rates under degraded input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Feature matrices already contain imputed/genomic values or are known to be fully covered — perturbation would not represent genuine missing-data conditions Evaluating REDInet on unperturbed benchmark performance (A549, HEK293T KO-WT/KO-OE ground truth sets) rather than robustness to missing flanking data Input is raw BAM/REDItools outTable rather than precomputed 8x101 feature matrices — run the REDInet pipeline first to generate feature vectors

skills.description: Use when you have balanced positive/negative sequence fragments centered on a candidate site and need to visualize per-position nucleotide enrichment or depletion between the two classes.
skills.name: nucleotide-frequency-logo-analysis
skills.search_text: nucleotide-frequency-logo-analysis Use when you have balanced positive/negative sequence fragments centered on a candidate site and need to visualize per-position nucleotide enrichment or depletion between the two classes. The goal is building or evaluating a predictive model (e.g., Staem5 stacking classifier) rather than qualitative motif inspection — use feature encoding such as PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, or PseEIIP instead Input sequences are not aligned with a common reference position (candidate site centered), since Two Sample Logo requires per-position correspondence between classes Positive and negative sets are highly imbalanced, which can distort per-position frequency comparisons without correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Two Sample Logo analysis that compares per-position nucleotide frequencies between m5C-positive and m5C-negative RNA fragments to reveal whether cytosine methylation sites carry distinctive sequence motifs. Applied in Staem5 to 41-bp A. thaliana and M. musculus fragments with the candidate cytosine centered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Two Sample Logo analysis that compares per-position nucleotide frequencies between m5C-positive and m5C-negative RNA fragments to reveal whether cytosine methylation sites carry distinctive sequence motifs. Applied in Staem5 to 41-bp A. thaliana and M. musculus fragments with the candidate cytosine centered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is building or evaluating a predictive model (e.g., Staem5 stacking classifier) rather than qualitative motif inspection — use feature encoding such as PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, or PseEIIP instead Input sequences are not aligned with a common reference position (candidate site centered), since Two Sample Logo requires per-position correspondence between classes Positive and negative sets are highly imbalanced, which can distort per-position frequency comparisons without correction

skills.description: Use when converting tabix-indexed REDItools outTables into TCN input feature vectors for A-to-I RNA editing classification, i.e. when putative editing sites need 101-nt window encoding of reference base identity and RNAseq nucleotide frequencies.
skills.name: nucleotide-one-hot-sequence-encoding
skills.search_text: nucleotide-one-hot-sequence-encoding Use when converting tabix-indexed REDItools outTables into TCN input feature vectors for A-to-I RNA editing classification, i.e. when putative editing sites need 101-nt window encoding of reference base identity and RNAseq nucleotide frequencies. The REDItools outTable is not yet bgzip-compressed and tabix-indexed — run 'bgzip' and 'tabix -s 1 -b 2 -e 2 -c R' first, since REDInet requires tabix-indexed input The downstream model does not consume 8 x 101 window matrices (e.g. RED-ML or RDDpred, which expect raw BAMs and use their own feature representations) Only raw RNA editing detection without prior REDItools pileup tables is needed — this skill encodes pre-computed REDItools output, it does not generate pileups http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encode 101-base RNAseq windows centered on putative A-to-I editing sites as 8 x 101 feature matrices — 4 one-hot channels for the reference base plus 4 channels of log2-transformed, pseudocount-normalized RNAseq nucleotide pileup frequencies — as the input format for the REDInet temporal convolutional network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf107
skills.summary: Encode 101-base RNAseq windows centered on putative A-to-I editing sites as 8 x 101 feature matrices — 4 one-hot channels for the reference base plus 4 channels of log2-transformed, pseudocount-normalized RNAseq nucleotide pileup frequencies — as the input format for the REDInet temporal convolutional network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The REDItools outTable is not yet bgzip-compressed and tabix-indexed — run 'bgzip' and 'tabix -s 1 -b 2 -e 2 -c R' first, since REDInet requires tabix-indexed input The downstream model does not consume 8 x 101 window matrices (e.g. RED-ML or RDDpred, which expect raw BAMs and use their own feature representations) Only raw RNA editing detection without prior REDItools pileup tables is needed — this skill encodes pre-computed REDItools output, it does not generate pileups

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a minimizer-based pre-filter/read mapper against a k-mer baseline, or when validating that smaller interleaved Bloom filters (e.g., 15.2 GiB vs 16 GiB at 64 bins) do not cost mapping sensitivity.
skills.name: nucleotide-read-mapping-benchmarking
skills.search_text: nucleotide-read-mapping-benchmarking Use when benchmarking a minimizer-based pre-filter/read mapper against a k-mer baseline, or when validating that smaller interleaved Bloom filters (e.g., 15.2 GiB vs 16 GiB at 64 bins) do not cost mapping sensitivity. The goal is biological mapping of new reads rather than benchmarking memory/time/sensitivity trade-offs of IBF-based pre-filters Raptor indices were built with an older version — 'Indices built with an older version of raptor cannot be used with version 2.0.0.' Bin sizes are highly uneven, since the paper notes 'The main limiting factor of our method is its susceptibility to uneven bin sizes as well as a high number of bins.' http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmark protocol for the Raptor-based DREAM-Yara re-implementation, comparing IBF build time, mapping time, peak RAM, and unmapped-read counts between the original 19-mer index and (23,19)/(31,19)-minimizer indices on clustered NCBI RefSeq bin sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for the Raptor-based DREAM-Yara re-implementation, comparing IBF build time, mapping time, peak RAM, and unmapped-read counts between the original 19-mer index and (23,19)/(31,19)-minimizer indices on clustered NCBI RefSeq bin sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological mapping of new reads rather than benchmarking memory/time/sensitivity trade-offs of IBF-based pre-filters Raptor indices were built with an older version — 'Indices built with an older version of raptor cannot be used with version 2.0.0.' Bin sizes are highly uneven, since the paper notes 'The main limiting factor of our method is its susceptibility to uneven bin sizes as well as a high number of bins.'

skills.description: Use when benchmarking false discovery control of XDE/pseudotime methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq: you hold samples with no true condition differences (built via random partitioning) and must count FDR-cutoff false positives.
skills.name: null-dataset-simulation-via-sample-partitioning
skills.search_text: null-dataset-simulation-via-sample-partitioning Use when benchmarking false discovery control of XDE/pseudotime methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq: you hold samples with no true condition differences (built via random partitioning) and must count FDR-cutoff false positives. The dataset contains genuine between-condition differences you want to detect — random partitioning and removal of group effects would erase the signal under study. Each condition has only one biological sample — the article notes condiments assumes one sample per condition, while this null requires multiple samples per pseudo-condition to expose sample-variability-driven false discoveries. Benchmarking topology or cell-density modules (differential branching, cell abundance changes) rather than gene-expression XDE false-positive control. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a false-positive benchmark for cross-sample differential expression (XDE) methods by randomly partitioning the 8 HCA-BM healthy donors into two pseudo-condition groups and removing group differences so no gene is truly differential, then counts significant calls per method at the 5% FDR cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Constructs a false-positive benchmark for cross-sample differential expression (XDE) methods by randomly partitioning the 8 HCA-BM healthy donors into two pseudo-condition groups and removing group differences so no gene is truly differential, then counts significant calls per method at the 5% FDR cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains genuine between-condition differences you want to detect — random partitioning and removal of group effects would erase the signal under study. Each condition has only one biological sample — the article notes condiments assumes one sample per condition, while this null requires multiple samples per pseudo-condition to expose sample-variability-driven false discoveries. Benchmarking topology or cell-density modules (differential branching, cell abundance changes) rather than gene-expression XDE false-positive control.

skills.description: Reference for building an empirical null distribution from shuffled/permuted single-cell data to classify embeddings or statistics (e.g., scDEED dubious vs trustworthy cells at dubious_cutoff=0.05 and trustworthy_cutoff=0.95).
skills.name: null-distribution-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: null-distribution-permutation-testing Reference for building an empirical null distribution from shuffled/permuted single-cell data to classify embeddings or statistics (e.g., scDEED dubious vs trustworthy cells at dubious_cutoff=0.05 and trustworthy_cutoff=0.95). The analysis goal is hyperparameter search itself rather than significance classification — use the full scDEED optimize() grid search instead of a single permuted-vs-original comparison The input is raw count data that has not been normalized and scaled, since Permuted() shuffles rows of the scale.data slot and requires a completed Seurat preprocessing pipeline A parametric or theoretical null is appropriate and empirical marginal resampling would be too costly (scDEED's permuted runs double the embedding computations, and the joint UMAP grid search is already computationally expensive) http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a signalless null distribution by permuting (marginal resampling) the input data, then classifies per-cell embedding reliability scores against the null's 5th/95th percentiles. In the scDEED context, the Permuted() function shuffles each row of the Seurat scale.data slot so that the reliability scores of real cell embeddings can be compared to those expected by chance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Constructs a signalless null distribution by permuting (marginal resampling) the input data, then classifies per-cell embedding reliability scores against the null's 5th/95th percentiles. In the scDEED context, the Permuted() function shuffles each row of the Seurat scale.data slot so that the reliability scores of real cell embeddings can be compared to those expected by chance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is hyperparameter search itself rather than significance classification — use the full scDEED optimize() grid search instead of a single permuted-vs-original comparison The input is raw count data that has not been normalized and scaled, since Permuted() shuffles rows of the scale.data slot and requires a completed Seurat preprocessing pipeline A parametric or theoretical null is appropriate and empirical marginal resampling would be too costly (scDEED's permuted runs double the embedding computations, and the joint UMAP grid search is already computationally expensive)

skills.name: null-hypothesis-dataset-construction-for-embedding-quality
skills.search_text: null-hypothesis-dataset-construction-for-embedding-quality Use when establishing the null expectation for embedding quality of scRNA-seq (e.g., Tabula Muris bone marrow) data: you need signalless data with preserved per-gene marginals to compute EMBEDR p-values. Input is non-normalized data — the paper states EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets The goal is to test differential-expression or co-expression signals directly; marginal resampling destroys joint gene correlations by design, so the null is only appropriate for embedding-quality hypothesis testing You need exact tail probabilities rather than empirical estimates — null distributions are computed empirically, giving p-values of finite resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs data-driven null datasets for EMBEDR's empirical hypothesis test by marginal resampling: each gene's expression values are independently drawn with replacement from that gene's empirical distribution, producing a null matrix of the same shape whose per-gene marginals match the real data while inter-gene correlations are destroyed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Constructs data-driven null datasets for EMBEDR's empirical hypothesis test by marginal resampling: each gene's expression values are independently drawn with replacement from that gene's empirical distribution, producing a null matrix of the same shape whose per-gene marginals match the real data while inter-gene correlations are destroyed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is non-normalized data — the paper states EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets The goal is to test differential-expression or co-expression signals directly; marginal resampling destroys joint gene correlations by design, so the null is only appropriate for embedding-quality hypothesis testing You need exact tail probabilities rather than empirical estimates — null distributions are computed empirically, giving p-values of finite resolution

When the goal is detecting real perturbations in data with a genuine between-condition effect (beta != 0), not benchmarking false-positive control When comparing methods for differential abundance (e.g., DA-seq, Milo, Meld) on cell-type proportions rather than differential transcriptomic state When data cannot be normalized to Pearson residuals via scTransform — scDist is not designed for raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate null-condition simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets (no true between-condition effect, beta=0) using the scDist simData utility with varied patient-level variability (tau^2), plus random 3-vs-3 partitions of a COVID-19 blood Seurat object, to benchmark whether differential-state tools like Augur and scDist falsely flag perturbed cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3

skills.description: Use when solving the COSLIR Eq. 3 objective from only the first and second moments (sample mean vectors and covariance matrices) of two consecutive TSCS time points, and you must demonstrate numerically that the ADMM iteration converged before trusting the sparse A_t estimate.
skills.name: numerical-convergence-testing
skills.search_text: numerical-convergence-testing Use when solving the COSLIR Eq. 3 objective from only the first and second moments (sample mean vectors and covariance matrices) of two consecutive TSCS time points, and you must demonstrate numerically that the ADMM iteration converged before trusting the sparse A_t estimate. Input is true longitudinal single-cell data where the same cells are linked across time points — COSLIR is designed for time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) data with no linkage across time, so moment-based inference is unnecessary. The goal is to infer the dense GRN that maintains a single cell state at one time point — COSLIR targets the sparse GRN driving cell state transitions between consecutive time points, not single-stage networks. Per-cell expression profiles or a constructed pseudo-time trajectory are available and preferred — the ADMM moment-based solver intentionally bypasses single-cell temporal ordering and cannot exploit per-cell linkage information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Verifies that the ADMM solver for COSLIR's non-convex, L1-regularized covariance-restricted sparse linear regression (Eq. 3) converges by monitoring primal and dual residuals across the closed-form A, B, C subproblem updates, yielding a defensible estimate of the sparse regulatory matrix A_t. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Verifies that the ADMM solver for COSLIR's non-convex, L1-regularized covariance-restricted sparse linear regression (Eq. 3) converges by monitoring primal and dual residuals across the closed-form A, B, C subproblem updates, yielding a defensible estimate of the sparse regulatory matrix A_t.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is true longitudinal single-cell data where the same cells are linked across time points — COSLIR is designed for time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) data with no linkage across time, so moment-based inference is unnecessary. The goal is to infer the dense GRN that maintains a single cell state at one time point — COSLIR targets the sparse GRN driving cell state transitions between consecutive time points, not single-stage networks. Per-cell expression profiles or a constructed pseudo-time trajectory are available and preferred — the ADMM moment-based solver intentionally bypasses single-cell temporal ordering and cannot exploit per-cell linkage information.

skills.when_to_use_negative: The formulas are already provided by a tested library (e.g. Seurat 4's WNN integration) and no re-implementation is needed The dataset is massive (e.g. >100K cells with many ADT features) — LinQ-View's quadratic pairwise-distance computation fails on such data, so validating its formulas offers no benefit over Seurat 4 The goal is statistical validation on real data rather than correctness of formula implementation on synthetic inputs

skills.search_text: numerical-invariant-verification Use when a SiFT-filtered single-cell expression matrix (X~ = X − K·X with pseudocount α = min(X~)) must be algebraically validated before saving to .h5ad or feeding downstream analysis. Filtering used a non-row-stochastic kernel or a non-SiFT method, so variance preservation after K·X projection does not hold by construction and the invariants would give misleading pass/fail signals The goal is biological (not algebraic) correctness of the filtering — the article notes SiFT 'suffers from the general challenge of any computational method which lacks a ground truth reference', so invariant checks cannot substitute for biological validation The matrix has been re-normalized or log-transformed after SiFT's α shift, since SiFT's corrected expression 'is no longer properly log-transformed' and comparisons to the original counts are then invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Post-hoc numerical validation of the SiFT filtering output: after computing the filtered matrix X~ = X − K·X with the pseudocount correction α = min(X~), verify that total variance is preserved and pairwise gene differences are unchanged, before persisting results as filtered_expression.h5ad and a sift_invariants_report. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7

skills.search_text: numerical-threshold-table-generation Use when you need minimizer-sharing thresholds for a pre-filter query whose threshold must depend on w, k, the error budget, and the per-read minimizer count m (e.g. 15-35), rather than a fixed fraction of shared k-mers. skills.summary: Reconstructs Raptor's probabilistic thresholding model (Equations 1-5 and Lemma 2) as a standalone generator of minimizer-sharing thresholds, combining a binomial model of errors affecting (w,k)-minimizers with Monte Carlo estimation of indirectly affected minimizers P(Cn), and tabulates thresholds over the (w, k, errors, m) parameter grid.

skills.description: Use when comparing a binary biomarker/class label (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2 from CMScaller) against a binary drug-response annotation in PDX or cell line cohorts, and you need per-cohort p-values and odds ratios to quantify the association.
skills.name: odds-ratio-effect-size-estimation
skills.search_text: odds-ratio-effect-size-estimation Use when comparing a binary biomarker/class label (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2 from CMScaller) against a binary drug-response annotation in PDX or cell line cohorts, and you need per-cohort p-values and odds ratios to quantify the association. The outcome or the class variable is not binary (e.g., continuous drug-response metrics such as IC50) — Fisher's exact test and odds ratios require 2x2 contingency tables Expected cell counts are large enough that a chi-square test is appropriate and the rarity assumption underlying odds ratios does not hold The class labels come from samples with a human stromal component unlike primary CRCs (e.g., metastatic biopsies), where CMScaller predictions are unreliable and any downstream association is confounded http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Estimates the strength of association between a binary classification (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2 in pre-clinical colorectal cancer models) and a binary outcome (e.g., cetuximab responder vs non-responder) by building 2x2 contingency tables and applying Fisher's exact test in R, reporting p-values and odds ratios per cohort and subset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Estimates the strength of association between a binary classification (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2 in pre-clinical colorectal cancer models) and a binary outcome (e.g., cetuximab responder vs non-responder) by building 2x2 contingency tables and applying Fisher's exact test in R, reporting p-values and odds ratios per cohort and subset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The outcome or the class variable is not binary (e.g., continuous drug-response metrics such as IC50) — Fisher's exact test and odds ratios require 2x2 contingency tables Expected cell counts are large enough that a chi-square test is appropriate and the rarity assumption underlying odds ratios does not hold The class labels come from samples with a human stromal component unlike primary CRCs (e.g., metastatic biopsies), where CMScaller predictions are unreliable and any downstream association is confounded

skills.description: Use when ranked ligand-receptor predictions from scRNA-seq must be validated against spatial transcriptomics: Visium spots with cell-type deconvolution, or seqFISH/merFISH cell-type maps, to test adjacency preference.

skills.search_text: odds-ratio-enrichment-of-ranked-lr-interactions Use when ranked ligand-receptor predictions from scRNA-seq must be validated against spatial transcriptomics: Visium spots with cell-type deconvolution, or seqFISH/merFISH cell-type maps, to test adjacency preference. No spatial information is available (pure dissociated scRNA-seq) — adjacency cannot be defined and the odds ratio is not computable The goal is comparing method/resource combinations on expression grounds alone; this skill is a downstream spatial-agreement check, not a benchmarking oracle (no gold standard exists) The CCC analysis infers intracellular signal propagation (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC); these are not directly comparable to ligand-receptor ranking and cannot be validated this way http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies whether top-ranked ligand-receptor interactions inferred by CCC methods (via LIANA) are preferentially found between spatially adjacent or colocalized cell-type pairs, expressed as odds ratios with a label-permutation null. It serves as an orthogonal spatial-validation layer for CCC predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No spatial information is available (pure dissociated scRNA-seq) — adjacency cannot be defined and the odds ratio is not computable The goal is comparing method/resource combinations on expression grounds alone; this skill is a downstream spatial-agreement check, not a benchmarking oracle (no gold standard exists) The CCC analysis infers intracellular signal propagation (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC); these are not directly comparable to ligand-receptor ranking and cannot be validated this way

skills.search_text: odds-ratio-heatmap-visualization Use when comparing a ligand-receptor resource's membership in biological annotation terms (pathways, cancer gene sets, tissue-enriched proteins) against a pooled background to expose enrichment bias. skills.search_text: ols-meta-regression-analysis Use when per-gene model measures (e.g., CTMM cell type-specificity, mean-difference) must be related to gene-level annotations such as EDS, enhancer count, LOEUF, or pLI via decile-binned regression.
