skills.name: optimal-transport-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-baseline-comparison Use when a generative model of single-cell time series is trained with an intermediate time point held out and you need to compare its simulated marginal against baselines (e.g., WOT linear interpolation) via Wasserstein distance. The task is clonal fate bias prediction rather than temporal interpolation — the prescient-analysis repo uses a separate workflow (weinreb-fate.sh, 03*-weinreb2020-fate-* notebooks) with all time points and estimated proliferation rates The dataset lacks a time point that can serve as a steady-state terminal target, since the model requires the final time point to be at steady-state http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a learned single-cell time-series model against a WOT (optimal transport) interpolation baseline by computing Wasserstein distances between simulated and held-out populations, as done for PRESCIENT on the Weinreb hematopoiesis day-2/4/6 interpolation task. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Benchmark a learned single-cell time-series model against a WOT (optimal transport) interpolation baseline by computing Wasserstein distances between simulated and held-out populations, as done for PRESCIENT on the Weinreb hematopoiesis day-2/4/6 interpolation task.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is clonal fate bias prediction rather than temporal interpolation — the prescient-analysis repo uses a separate workflow (weinreb-fate.sh, 03*-weinreb2020-fate-* notebooks) with all time points and estimated proliferation rates The dataset lacks a time point that can serve as a steady-state terminal target, since the model requires the final time point to be at steady-state

skills.description: Use when a time-course scRNA-seq matrix sacrifices cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and individual cell lineage paths between adjacent time points are needed before smoothing, fate prediction, or dynamic gene network construction.
skills.name: optimal-transport-cell-lineage-alignment
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-cell-lineage-alignment Use when a time-course scRNA-seq matrix sacrifices cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and individual cell lineage paths between adjacent time points are needed before smoothing, fate prediction, or dynamic gene network construction. Only a single-time-point scRNA-seq dataset is available — adjacent time points are required for the optimal transport coupling A bulk population-average trajectory across time is sufficient for the analysis, e.g. bulk pseudotime ordering without per-cell lineage resolution Ground-truth cell-to-cell correspondence already exists between time points, making transport-based estimation unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aligns individual cells between adjacent time points of a time-course scRNA-seq experiment by solving a discrete Monge optimal transport problem (Earth mover's distance, squared Euclidean cost, alpha=2), yielding unique cell-to-cell trajectories that no bulk pseudotime method provides. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ailsci.2023.100068
skills.summary: Aligns individual cells between adjacent time points of a time-course scRNA-seq experiment by solving a discrete Monge optimal transport problem (Earth mover's distance, squared Euclidean cost, alpha=2), yielding unique cell-to-cell trajectories that no bulk pseudotime method provides.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single-time-point scRNA-seq dataset is available — adjacent time points are required for the optimal transport coupling A bulk population-average trajectory across time is sufficient for the analysis, e.g. bulk pseudotime ordering without per-cell lineage resolution Ground-truth cell-to-cell correspondence already exists between time points, making transport-based estimation unnecessary

skills.description: Use when control and perturbed single-cell RNA-seq profiles are unpaired (no per-cell ground-truth pairing) and a translator must be trained to predict stimulated-expression profiles, especially with held-out cell types.
skills.name: optimal-transport-cell-matching
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-cell-matching Use when control and perturbed single-cell RNA-seq profiles are unpaired (no per-cell ground-truth pairing) and a translator must be trained to predict stimulated-expression profiles, especially with held-out cell types. Control and perturbed cells are already paired per cell, in which case augmentation matching is unnecessary overhead and basic training may suffice. The target data lacks cell_type annotations and cannot be confidently clustered, making cell_type_augmentation inapplicable (MultiVI_augmentation or scButterfly-B would be required instead). The task is standard paired scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq/scADT-seq cross-modality translation rather than unpaired perturbation-response prediction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies scButterfly's data augmentation with per-cell-type optimal transport matching (scButterfly-T) to construct paired training samples from unpaired single-cell datasets, enabling perturbation-response prediction on data such as the PT_PBMC control/stimulated PBMC cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Applies scButterfly's data augmentation with per-cell-type optimal transport matching (scButterfly-T) to construct paired training samples from unpaired single-cell datasets, enabling perturbation-response prediction on data such as the PT_PBMC control/stimulated PBMC cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Control and perturbed cells are already paired per cell, in which case augmentation matching is unnecessary overhead and basic training may suffice. The target data lacks cell_type annotations and cannot be confidently clustered, making cell_type_augmentation inapplicable (MultiVI_augmentation or scButterfly-B would be required instead). The task is standard paired scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq/scADT-seq cross-modality translation rather than unpaired perturbation-response prediction.

skills.description: Use when a non-spatial scRNA-seq dataset must be linked to spatial measurements of a small set of genes (e.g., seqFISH/in situ reference maps) to predict spatial expression patterns or assign cells to spatial regions.
skills.name: optimal-transport-cell-to-position-mapping
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-cell-to-position-mapping Use when a non-spatial scRNA-seq dataset must be linked to spatial measurements of a small set of genes (e.g., seqFISH/in situ reference maps) to predict spatial expression patterns or assign cells to spatial regions. When the scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large, where the article notes computation can become intractable due to iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs When spatial data lacks shared genes with the scRNA-seq data and no low-dimensional common space (e.g., via Seurat cca) can be established When the goal is time-resolved signaling inference — the approach does not consider time delay in cell-cell communication http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Maps individual scRNA-seq cells to spatial positions of a reference spatial transcriptomics dataset by solving a structured/unbalanced optimal transport problem in SpaOTsc, yielding a transport plan that supports spatial gene expression prediction, cell-origin assignment, and downstream cell-cell distance inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Maps individual scRNA-seq cells to spatial positions of a reference spatial transcriptomics dataset by solving a structured/unbalanced optimal transport problem in SpaOTsc, yielding a transport plan that supports spatial gene expression prediction, cell-origin assignment, and downstream cell-cell distance inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large, where the article notes computation can become intractable due to iterative optimal transport over all cell pairs When spatial data lacks shared genes with the scRNA-seq data and no low-dimensional common space (e.g., via Seurat cca) can be established When the goal is time-resolved signaling inference — the approach does not consider time delay in cell-cell communication

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, morphology, or CyTOF) where cross-modality feature connections are weak, and a modality-mixed latent embedding is the desired output.
skills.name: optimal-transport-embedding-alignment
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-embedding-alignment Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, morphology, or CyTOF) where cross-modality feature connections are weak, and a modality-mixed latent embedding is the desired output. Modalities lack any cross-modality feature connections (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities Data are paired (same cells measured in all modalities) — diagonal integration is designed for unpaired cells from the same biological condition Goal is detecting very rare cell populations, which are hard to align because they are rarely co-sampled from each modality in mini-batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align unpaired single-cell modalities into a shared 16-dimensional latent space by back-propagating the IOT loss and unbalanced Sinkhorn divergence regularization from an unbalanced Optimal Transport plan computed on weakly connected cross-modality features, as implemented in scConfluence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Align unpaired single-cell modalities into a shared 16-dimensional latent space by back-propagating the IOT loss and unbalanced Sinkhorn divergence regularization from an unbalanced Optimal Transport plan computed on weakly connected cross-modality features, as implemented in scConfluence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities lack any cross-modality feature connections (e.g. electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities Data are paired (same cells measured in all modalities) — diagonal integration is designed for unpaired cells from the same biological condition Goal is detecting very rare cell populations, which are hard to align because they are rarely co-sampled from each modality in mini-batches

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell datasets with both common and dataset-specific HVGs — e.g., scATAC gene activity matrices vs scRNA counts with unmatched cell types — and you need latent embeddings plus robustness metrics.
skills.name: optimal-transport-latent-embedding
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-latent-embedding Use when integrating unpaired single-cell datasets with both common and dataset-specific HVGs — e.g., scATAC gene activity matrices vs scRNA counts with unmatched cell types — and you need latent embeddings plus robustness metrics. Datasets are already paired cell-by-cell (vertical integration of the same cells profiled with multiple modalities is a different mode; default mode='h' assumes horizontal integration with common genes) The task is spatial transcriptomics deconvolution via the OT plan rather than latent embedding — uniPort's label transfer for spatial data uses the optimal transport plan 'instead of embedding latent space' Only batch-effect correction of a single modality is needed (methods like scMC or SCALEX target batch correction, not cross-modal integration) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Integrate heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics datasets (e.g., mouse spleen scATAC gene activity and scRNA data) by training uniPort's coupled-VAE with Minibatch Unbalanced Optimal Transport to jointly embed both modalities in a shared latent space, then evaluate integration quality with label-transfer metrics (ARI, NMI, F1) and Silhouette coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Integrate heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics datasets (e.g., mouse spleen scATAC gene activity and scRNA data) by training uniPort's coupled-VAE with Minibatch Unbalanced Optimal Transport to jointly embed both modalities in a shared latent space, then evaluate integration quality with label-transfer metrics (ARI, NMI, F1) and Silhouette coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are already paired cell-by-cell (vertical integration of the same cells profiled with multiple modalities is a different mode; default mode='h' assumes horizontal integration with common genes) The task is spatial transcriptomics deconvolution via the OT plan rather than latent embedding — uniPort's label transfer for spatial data uses the optimal transport plan 'instead of embedding latent space' Only batch-effect correction of a single modality is needed (methods like scMC or SCALEX target batch correction, not cross-modal integration)

skills.description: Use when training scConfluence on unpaired single-cell multiomics data (e.g., scRNA-scATAC MuData objects) and the latent embeddings must be checked for modality mixing versus cell-type structure before benchmarking or downstream clustering.
skills.name: optimal-transport-latent-space-tuning
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-latent-space-tuning Use when training scConfluence on unpaired single-cell multiomics data (e.g., scRNA-scATAC MuData objects) and the latent embeddings must be checked for modality mixing versus cell-type structure before benchmarking or downstream clustering. No cross-modality feature connections are available (e.g., integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities Data is paired multimodal (same cells profiled in both modalities) — scConfluence targets diagonal integration of unpaired data and does not yet jointly integrate paired and unpaired data The target population is extremely rare, since rare populations are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches, degrading both scConfluence and state-of-the-art methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Tuning the unbalanced optimal-transport hyperparameters of scConfluence (sinkhorn_loss_weight and reach, with partial transported mass m=0.5) during model training so that the shared latent space both mixes modalities and preserves biological structure in diagonal integration tasks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Tuning the unbalanced optimal-transport hyperparameters of scConfluence (sinkhorn_loss_weight and reach, with partial transported mass m=0.5) during model training so that the shared latent space both mixes modalities and preserves biological structure in diagonal integration tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cross-modality feature connections are available (e.g., integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities Data is paired multimodal (same cells profiled in both modalities) — scConfluence targets diagonal integration of unpaired data and does not yet jointly integrate paired and unpaired data The target population is extremely rare, since rare populations are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches, degrading both scConfluence and state-of-the-art methods

skills.description: Use when you have paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. scRNA+scATAC from scCAT-seq or 10X Multiome, CITE-seq, or tri-omic TEA-seq Muon objects) and need a joint cell embedding with interpretable, cell-type-specific factors.
skills.name: optimal-transport-matrix-factorization
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-matrix-factorization Use when you have paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. scRNA+scATAC from scCAT-seq or 10X Multiome, CITE-seq, or tri-omic TEA-seq Muon objects) and need a joint cell embedding with interpretable, cell-type-specific factors. Data are unpaired multi-omics or require batch correction across batches — the paper states Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data You need a principled, data-driven choice of the number of latent dimensions — Mowgli does not offer a straightforward way to define k, so several values must be tested No GPU is available for very large datasets — optimal transport is inherently expensive to compute compared to the Euclidean distance, and GPU availability is required to scale http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrate paired single-cell multi-omics data with Mowgli, which combines integrative Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with entropic-regularized Optimal Transport (solved via GPU-enabled Sinkhorn) to produce cell embeddings that improve both clustering and factor interpretability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43019-2
skills.summary: Integrate paired single-cell multi-omics data with Mowgli, which combines integrative Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with entropic-regularized Optimal Transport (solved via GPU-enabled Sinkhorn) to produce cell embeddings that improve both clustering and factor interpretability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired multi-omics or require batch correction across batches — the paper states Mowgli does not handle batch correction when integrating paired multi-omics data You need a principled, data-driven choice of the number of latent dimensions — Mowgli does not offer a straightforward way to define k, so several values must be tested No GPU is available for very large datasets — optimal transport is inherently expensive to compute compared to the Euclidean distance, and GPU availability is required to scale

skills.description: Use when integrating non-spatial scRNA-seq data with spatial transcriptomics (e.g., in situ hybridization, seqFISH+) and a cell-to-position mapping is needed to recover spatial properties of single cells.
skills.name: optimal-transport-plan-computation
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-plan-computation Use when integrating non-spatial scRNA-seq data with spatial transcriptomics (e.g., in situ hybridization, seqFISH+) and a cell-to-position mapping is needed to recover spatial properties of single cells. Input is a purely spatial single-cell dataset with coordinates for every cell already — SpaOTsc-integration or direct spatial analysis is more appropriate than solving the cross-modality transport problem The scRNA-seq and spatial datasets share no genes or measurable expression similarity, since the cost matrix M cannot be constructed Very large datasets where the iterative transport computation becomes intractable without landmark approximation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Computes the unbalanced, structured optimal transport plan γ* that maps scRNA-seq cells to spatial measurement positions in SpaOTsc, forming the foundation for deriving spatial cell-cell distances and downstream signaling analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Computes the unbalanced, structured optimal transport plan γ* that maps scRNA-seq cells to spatial measurement positions in SpaOTsc, forming the foundation for deriving spatial cell-cell distances and downstream signaling analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a purely spatial single-cell dataset with coordinates for every cell already — SpaOTsc-integration or direct spatial analysis is more appropriate than solving the cross-modality transport problem The scRNA-seq and spatial datasets share no genes or measurable expression similarity, since the cost matrix M cannot be constructed Very large datasets where the iterative transport computation becomes intractable without landmark approximation

skills.description: Use when you have multiple single-cell/pathomics samples (.h5ad with per-cell cluster labels and sample IDs) and need an unsupervised, sample-level distance matrix to cluster patients or infer disease trajectories.
skills.name: optimal-transport-sample-distance-estimation
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-sample-distance-estimation Use when you have multiple single-cell/pathomics samples (.h5ad with per-cell cluster labels and sample IDs) and need an unsupervised, sample-level distance matrix to cluster patients or infer disease trajectories. When the input is already a sample-level feature/summary table rather than per-cell annotated data — no cluster distributions exist to define transport marginals When samples come from distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge for cross-technology comparison When labeled, supervised patient stratification is required — competing approaches needing patient labels are out of PILOT's unsupervised scope http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 PILOT-style computation of patient-level Wasserstein distances between single-cell or pathomics samples using optimal transport over cell-cluster distributions, with the cost matrix derived from cosine distances between cluster medians in PCA space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: PILOT-style computation of patient-level Wasserstein distances between single-cell or pathomics samples using optimal transport over cell-cluster distributions, with the cost matrix derived from cosine distances between cluster medians in PCA space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a sample-level feature/summary table rather than per-cell annotated data — no cluster distributions exist to define transport marginals When samples come from distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge for cross-technology comparison When labeled, supervised patient stratification is required — competing approaches needing patient labels are out of PILOT's unsupervised scope

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities whose cell populations are unequally represented, and you need to verify that the chosen unbalanced-OT relaxation (transported mass m) yields robust, biologically meaningful embeddings.
skills.name: optimal-transport-unbalancedness-tuning
skills.search_text: optimal-transport-unbalancedness-tuning Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities whose cell populations are unequally represented, and you need to verify that the chosen unbalanced-OT relaxation (transported mass m) yields robust, biologically meaningful embeddings. When prior information about the level of unbalanceness of the data is available — in that case m can be set directly rather than swept When modalities are fully paired or population proportions are balanced, where the unbalanced OT relaxation and its m parameter add unnecessary complexity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Sensitivity analysis of the unbalanced-OT transported-mass parameter m in scConfluence, sweeping m around the default 0.5 on progressively more unbalanced cell-line scenarios and scoring the shared latent space with cell-type purity, FOSCTTM, and graph connectivity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Sensitivity analysis of the unbalanced-OT transported-mass parameter m in scConfluence, sweeping m around the default 0.5 on progressively more unbalanced cell-line scenarios and scoring the shared latent space with cell-type purity, FOSCTTM, and graph connectivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When prior information about the level of unbalanceness of the data is available — in that case m can be set directly rather than swept When modalities are fully paired or population proportions are balanced, where the unbalanced OT relaxation and its m parameter add unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when the goal is to find trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters in noisy, complex gene expression microarray data, where rows share a consistent upward/downward trend rather than identical absolute values.
skills.name: order-preserving-biclustering
skills.search_text: order-preserving-biclustering Use when the goal is to find trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters in noisy, complex gene expression microarray data, where rows share a consistent upward/downward trend rather than identical absolute values. The analysis goal is finding biclusters with constant or additive/multiplicative coherent values rather than consistent row-wise ordering/trends The input is already a discrete or binary matrix — in that case use BCUnibicD (the discrete-data variant) instead of the continuous-data path with separation/granulation preprocessing Narrow biclusters are the primary target — BicSPAM was reported to be somewhat better at finding narrow biclusters, the task for which it was specifically designed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 UniBic-style trend-preserving biclustering: preprocess a gene expression matrix (data separation + granulation), build a row-wise index matrix, seed biclusters via longest common subsequences between row pairs, and extend seeds into approximately trend-preserving biclusters with significance filtering (p < 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: UniBic-style trend-preserving biclustering: preprocess a gene expression matrix (data separation + granulation), build a row-wise index matrix, seed biclusters via longest common subsequences between row pairs, and extend seeds into approximately trend-preserving biclusters with significance filtering (p < 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is finding biclusters with constant or additive/multiplicative coherent values rather than consistent row-wise ordering/trends The input is already a discrete or binary matrix — in that case use BCUnibicD (the discrete-data variant) instead of the continuous-data path with separation/granulation preprocessing Narrow biclusters are the primary target — BicSPAM was reported to be somewhat better at finding narrow biclusters, the task for which it was specifically designed

skills.description: Use when transcript sequences (e.g. CD-HIT-reduced lncRNA/PCT FASTA from RefSeq, Ensembl, or GENCODE) must be scanned for ORFs to compute ORF-derived coding-potential features or ORF-attention encodings.
skills.name: orf-extraction-with-orfipy
skills.search_text: orf-extraction-with-orfipy Use when transcript sequences (e.g. CD-HIT-reduced lncRNA/PCT FASTA from RefSeq, Ensembl, or GENCODE) must be scanned for ORFs to compute ORF-derived coding-potential features or ORF-attention encodings. Input is already a feature table or precomputed coding-potential scores — ORF extraction would be redundant Sequences are raw genomic DNA rather than mature transcript sequences, since ORF coverage and dominance are defined relative to transcript length Datasets are not redundancy-reduced (CD-HIT 80%) or contain ncRNAs shorter than 200 nt, which LncCat's pipeline explicitly filters out http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Extracts open reading frames (ORFs) from transcript FASTA sequences using Orfipy under the Standard Code (transl_table=1), retaining the top three longest ORFs per transcript as the basis for LncCat's ORF-related and ORF-attention features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012

skills.description: Use when building a feature matrix from FASTA transcripts (e.g. H-Train mRNA/CDS/lncRNA files) for coding-potential classification and you need ORF-derived features beyond the single longest-ORF convention.
skills.name: orf-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: orf-feature-extraction Use when building a feature matrix from FASTA transcripts (e.g. H-Train mRNA/CDS/lncRNA files) for coding-potential classification and you need ORF-derived features beyond the single longest-ORF convention. Input is already an imputed/scaled feature matrix or a prediction output csv — this skill operates on raw transcript FASTA sequences Only the single longest ORF is desired (e.g. when replicating a longest-ORF tool like CPC-style pipelines) rather than LncDC's four flexible ORF types You need secondary structure features (SSFs) — those require separate RNAfold folding and k-mer scoring, not ORF feature extraction http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Extract ORF-associated coding-potential features from RNA transcripts following LncDC's four FEELnc-style ORF types (type 0-3), computing maximum ORF length, ORF coverage, ORF hexamer score, and relative codon bias (RCB) per ORF category as part of the sequence intrinsic features (SIFs) feeding the XGBoost lncRNA/mRNA classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Extract ORF-associated coding-potential features from RNA transcripts following LncDC's four FEELnc-style ORF types (type 0-3), computing maximum ORF length, ORF coverage, ORF hexamer score, and relative codon bias (RCB) per ORF category as part of the sequence intrinsic features (SIFs) feeding the XGBoost lncRNA/mRNA classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an imputed/scaled feature matrix or a prediction output csv — this skill operates on raw transcript FASTA sequences Only the single longest ORF is desired (e.g. when replicating a longest-ORF tool like CPC-style pipelines) rather than LncDC's four flexible ORF types You need secondary structure features (SSFs) — those require separate RNAfold folding and k-mer scoring, not ORF feature extraction

skills.name: orf-length-based-transcript-filtering
skills.search_text: orf-length-based-transcript-filtering Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity FASTA contigs) must be filtered for likely non-coding or fragmented transcripts by predicted ORF length, as part of chimera-removal or assembly-cleanup filtering. When maximizing TransRate score is the only goal: the CD-HIT-EST-only filter scored highest (0.319) and ORF-length filtering removed too many transcripts, so it is suboptimal for that objective When the current Bellerophon release is required with custom filter ordering: 'Custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version' When the input is already a quality-filtered or reference-guided transcript set where non-coding fragments were removed by other means http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Removes transcript contigs from a de novo assembly whose predicted open reading frame (ORF) is too short, using community-default thresholds of 50 aa or 100 aa, as one of the three filter components (CD-HIT-EST, TPM, ORF length) explored in the Bellerophon pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/ece3.5571
skills.summary: Removes transcript contigs from a de novo assembly whose predicted open reading frame (ORF) is too short, using community-default thresholds of 50 aa or 100 aa, as one of the three filter components (CD-HIT-EST, TPM, ORF length) explored in the Bellerophon pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When maximizing TransRate score is the only goal: the CD-HIT-EST-only filter scored highest (0.319) and ORF-length filtering removed too many transcripts, so it is suboptimal for that objective When the current Bellerophon release is required with custom filter ordering: 'Custom order of filtering steps is disabled in this version' When the input is already a quality-filtered or reference-guided transcript set where non-coding fragments were removed by other means

skills.description: Use when tumor scRNA-seq data (Seurat object with malignant epithelial cells pre-identified) must be assigned a cancer cell of origin using Census organ-specific CCLE-trained models for Liver, Pancreas, or Large_Intestine (colon).
skills.name: organ-specific-malignant-cell-model-application
skills.search_text: organ-specific-malignant-cell-model-application Use when tumor scRNA-seq data (Seurat object with malignant epithelial cells pre-identified) must be assigned a cancer cell of origin using Census organ-specific CCLE-trained models for Liver, Pancreas, or Large_Intestine (colon). The tissue organ has no Census cancer model — only Kidney, Large_Intestine, Liver, Lung, Mammary, Pancreas are available; other organs cannot be run with predict_cancer=T Malignant cells have not been pre-identified and the goal is general normal-tissue annotation — census_main without predict_cancer is the appropriate entry point The environment has Seurat v5 loaded — Census requires Seurat version 4 and will not run correctly http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply Census's organ-specific CCLE-trained cancer models to scRNA-seq tumor datasets to classify malignant epithelial cells and predict their likely cell of origin (e.g., hepatocellular vs cholangiocarcinoma in liver, ductal vs acinar-like states in pancreatic PDAC, enterocyte-lineage assignments in colon cancer). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Apply Census's organ-specific CCLE-trained cancer models to scRNA-seq tumor datasets to classify malignant epithelial cells and predict their likely cell of origin (e.g., hepatocellular vs cholangiocarcinoma in liver, ductal vs acinar-like states in pancreatic PDAC, enterocyte-lineage assignments in colon cancer).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tissue organ has no Census cancer model — only Kidney, Large_Intestine, Liver, Lung, Mammary, Pancreas are available; other organs cannot be run with predict_cancer=T Malignant cells have not been pre-identified and the goal is general normal-tissue annotation — census_main without predict_cancer is the appropriate entry point The environment has Seurat v5 loaded — Census requires Seurat version 4 and will not run correctly

skills.description: Use when quantifying how accurately a supervised single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet) transfers cell-type labels across iPSC cell lines in cortical organoid scRNA-seq datasets, or when reproducing reported accuracy and radial glia misclassification rates from Figures 6C-D, 6E and Table S11.
skills.name: organoid-cell-type-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: organoid-cell-type-accuracy-evaluation Use when quantifying how accurately a supervised single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet) transfers cell-type labels across iPSC cell lines in cortical organoid scRNA-seq datasets, or when reproducing reported accuracy and radial glia misclassification rates from Figures 6C-D, 6E and Table S11. Training and prediction data come from different species — the authors explicitly limited SIMS to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species The target dataset lacks matching gene features or was not processed with the same normalization pipeline (filtering, normalize_total, log1p, scale) as the training data No pre-existing annotations are available for the reference dataset, since SIMS is supervised and relies on prior expert annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates SIMS (TabNet-based) cross-cell-line label transfer on human cortical organoids by training on 11A-derived organoid annotations and scoring predictions on Velasco PGP1 and GM8330 organoids, quantifying overall accuracy and lineage-specific misclassification (radial glia called immature projection neurons). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Evaluates SIMS (TabNet-based) cross-cell-line label transfer on human cortical organoids by training on 11A-derived organoid annotations and scoring predictions on Velasco PGP1 and GM8330 organoids, quantifying overall accuracy and lineage-specific misclassification (radial glia called immature projection neurons).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Training and prediction data come from different species — the authors explicitly limited SIMS to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species The target dataset lacks matching gene features or was not processed with the same normalization pipeline (filtering, normalize_total, log1p, scale) as the training data No pre-existing annotations are available for the reference dataset, since SIMS is supervised and relies on prior expert annotations

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original identification method: paired-end FASTQ reads must be filtered with the original rules to define the baseline read set for overlap/consistency computation.
skills.name: original-spliseq-baseline-filtering-reimplementation
skills.search_text: original-spliseq-baseline-filtering-reimplementation Use when benchmarking a SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original identification method: paired-end FASTQ reads must be filtered with the original rules to define the baseline read set for overlap/consistency computation. Input is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcoded data — the last-6-base barcode match and three 8 nt barcode rules are SPLiT-seq specific and the fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data The goal is SCSit performance (runtime or tolerance) evaluation rather than baseline consistency comparison — other skills cover the -t 4 runtime assessment and >1 mismatch/indel tolerance testing Reads have already been processed through SCSit only and no original-method baseline read set is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reimplements the original SPLiT-seq read-identification baseline (barcode last-6-base match, UMI quality, and 8 nt barcode mismatch filters) so SCSit's identified reads can be compared against the original method per sample, yielding 96-97% consistency measurements across five SPLiT-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Reimplements the original SPLiT-seq read-identification baseline (barcode last-6-base match, UMI quality, and 8 nt barcode mismatch filters) so SCSit's identified reads can be compared against the original method per sample, yielding 96-97% consistency measurements across five SPLiT-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not SPLiT-seq combinatorial-barcoded data — the last-6-base barcode match and three 8 nt barcode rules are SPLiT-seq specific and the fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed only for SPLiT-seq data The goal is SCSit performance (runtime or tolerance) evaluation rather than baseline consistency comparison — other skills cover the -t 4 runtime assessment and >1 mismatch/indel tolerance testing Reads have already been processed through SCSit only and no original-method baseline read set is required

skills.description: Use when you need simulated OU-process expression data with known Redundant/Unique deletion class labels (e.g., to train or benchmark CLOUDe classifiers) for Nk observations per class across m conditions, bounded by empirical expression ranges.
skills.name: ornstein-uhlenbeck-expression-simulation
skills.search_text: ornstein-uhlenbeck-expression-simulation Use when you need simulated OU-process expression data with known Redundant/Unique deletion class labels (e.g., to train or benchmark CLOUDe classifiers) for Nk observations per class across m conditions, bounded by empirical expression ranges. The input is real expression data with unknown true deletion classes — simulation provides synthetic labels; use the CLOUDeClassify* functions on empirical data instead You only need to apply pre-trained classifiers or predictors to an existing test set — CLOUDeClassifyNN/XGB/RF/SVM take existing feature files and skip data generation The target evolutionary scenario requires a distinct ancestral optimum (theta0 differing from theta1 and theta2), which needs separately simulated data rather than the standard class-balanced generation http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Simulates class-balanced Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) expression-evolution training and test data for gene deletion events using CLOUDe's GenerateTrainingData(), producing labeled 'Redundant'/'Unique' observations whose expression ranges are bounded by an empirical dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Simulates class-balanced Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) expression-evolution training and test data for gene deletion events using CLOUDe's GenerateTrainingData(), producing labeled 'Redundant'/'Unique' observations whose expression ranges are bounded by an empirical dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real expression data with unknown true deletion classes — simulation provides synthetic labels; use the CLOUDeClassify* functions on empirical data instead You only need to apply pre-trained classifiers or predictors to an existing test set — CLOUDeClassifyNN/XGB/RF/SVM take existing feature files and skip data generation The target evolutionary scenario requires a distinct ancestral optimum (theta0 differing from theta1 and theta2), which needs separately simulated data rather than the standard class-balanced generation

skills.description: Use when a Mpath landmark graph (landmark coordinates and connecting edges) and cell-to-landmark transition assignments exist and individual cells must be placed in pseudo-temporal order along developmental trajectories between neighbouring landmarks.
skills.name: orthogonal-projection-onto-landmark-edges
skills.search_text: orthogonal-projection-onto-landmark-edges Use when a Mpath landmark graph (landmark coordinates and connecting edges) and cell-to-landmark transition assignments exist and individual cells must be placed in pseudo-temporal order along developmental trajectories between neighbouring landmarks. Development process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — the article states Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets where specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to this setting You need a global diffusion-pseudotime value per cell rather than a per-edge ordering concatenated along landmarks; this skill orders cells only along Mpath landmark edges http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Final step of the Mpath framework: cells transitioning between pairs of adjacent landmark states are orthogonally projected onto the straight edge connecting the landmark pair, and sorted by projection coordinate to produce a pseudo-temporal ordering of single cells along each developmental trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Final step of the Mpath framework: cells transitioning between pairs of adjacent landmark states are orthogonally projected onto the straight edge connecting the landmark pair, and sorted by projection coordinate to produce a pseudo-temporal ordering of single cells along each developmental trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development process starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — the article states Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets where specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to this setting You need a global diffusion-pseudotime value per cell rather than a per-edge ordering concatenated along landmarks; this skill orders cells only along Mpath landmark edges

skills.description: Use when you have OrthoFinder (or eggNOG/PLAZA/orthomcl) orthogroup results for a query species (e.g. Danio rerio) and need per-orthogroup gene ages (LCA classes) or continuity scores of species representation.
skills.name: orthogroup-lca-annotation
skills.search_text: orthogroup-lca-annotation Use when you have OrthoFinder (or eggNOG/PLAZA/orthomcl) orthogroup results for a query species (e.g. Danio rerio) and need per-orthogroup gene ages (LCA classes) or continuity scores of species representation. Your orthogroups come from raw OrthoFinder/eggNOG output without a defined query species — the LCA assignment is target-species specific and needs qlin/of2orthomap context You only need TEI or gene age-weighted expression on scRNA objects (use the downstream Scanpy-based TEI step, not this annotation skill) Input is already a computed orthomap (gene ages per orthogroup) — skip directly to the continuity/TEI analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates each orthologous group with its lowest common ancestor (LCA) as the gene age class for a query species using oggmap's of2orthomap logic on OrthoFinder results, and optionally derives a per-orthogroup continuity score of species completeness along the LCA-to-focal-species path. This grounds evolutionary age assignment for downstream scRNA analyses such as the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Annotates each orthologous group with its lowest common ancestor (LCA) as the gene age class for a query species using oggmap's of2orthomap logic on OrthoFinder results, and optionally derives a per-orthogroup continuity score of species completeness along the LCA-to-focal-species path. This grounds evolutionary age assignment for downstream scRNA analyses such as the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your orthogroups come from raw OrthoFinder/eggNOG output without a defined query species — the LCA assignment is target-species specific and needs qlin/of2orthomap context You only need TEI or gene age-weighted expression on scRNA objects (use the downstream Scanpy-based TEI step, not this annotation skill) Input is already a computed orthomap (gene ages per orthogroup) — skip directly to the continuity/TEI analysis

skills.description: Use when building a KO/protein ortholog reference from hundreds of eukaryote proteomes to support read-to-ortholog mapping for non-model species RNA-seq, instead of per-species transcript assembly and annotation transfer.
skills.name: ortholog-database-construction
skills.search_text: ortholog-database-construction Use when building a KO/protein ortholog reference from hundreds of eukaryote proteomes to support read-to-ortholog mapping for non-model species RNA-seq, instead of per-species transcript assembly and annotation transfer. When the species of interest already has a well-annotated reference transcriptome/genome — direct gene-level quantification (e.g., Kallisto against GRCz11) is preferable When taxonomically diverse comparisons require gene-level identity: reads from the same gene may map to similar but different orthologs across species When the target function is absent from the KO system (e.g., vitellogenin) — ortholog-group-based mapping cannot recover it http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Constructs a high-resolution protein ortholog database (EcoOmicsDB) by downloading all protein-coding sequences from KEGG for 687 eukaryotic organisms and binning ~12.8 million proteins into ortholog groups with OrthoFinder, enabling annotation of RNA-seq data from species without a reference transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Constructs a high-resolution protein ortholog database (EcoOmicsDB) by downloading all protein-coding sequences from KEGG for 687 eukaryotic organisms and binning ~12.8 million proteins into ortholog groups with OrthoFinder, enabling annotation of RNA-seq data from species without a reference transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the species of interest already has a well-annotated reference transcriptome/genome — direct gene-level quantification (e.g., Kallisto against GRCz11) is preferable When taxonomically diverse comparisons require gene-level identity: reads from the same gene may map to similar but different orthologs across species When the target function is absent from the KO system (e.g., vitellogenin) — ortholog-group-based mapping cannot recover it

skills.description: Use when matching cell types across a species pair requires gene/gene correspondences and a simple sequence-alignment-based ortholog map (e.g., BLAST one-to-one matches) is acceptable, or when benchmarking against embedding-based gene matching.
skills.name: ortholog-gene-matching-with-blast
skills.search_text: ortholog-gene-matching-with-blast Use when matching cell types across a species pair requires gene/gene correspondences and a simple sequence-alignment-based ortholog map (e.g., BLAST one-to-one matches) is acceptable, or when benchmarking against embedding-based gene matching. When higher-quality gene matches are needed — the article reports ProtBERT-based gene matching gives better cell type matches than BLAST within TACTiCS When input data is single-species, since ortholog matching only applies to cross-species comparisons When trained TACTiCS models and precomputed protein embeddings are already available, making sequence alignment unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Establishes cross-species one-to-one orthologous gene correspondences using BLAST alignments of protein sequences, providing the gene-matching layer needed for baseline cross-species cell type matching pipelines such as Seurat and as a comparison point against ProtBERT embedding-based gene matching in TACTiCS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Establishes cross-species one-to-one orthologous gene correspondences using BLAST alignments of protein sequences, providing the gene-matching layer needed for baseline cross-species cell type matching pipelines such as Seurat and as a comparison point against ProtBERT embedding-based gene matching in TACTiCS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When higher-quality gene matches are needed — the article reports ProtBERT-based gene matching gives better cell type matches than BLAST within TACTiCS When input data is single-species, since ortholog matching only applies to cross-species comparisons When trained TACTiCS models and precomputed protein embeddings are already available, making sequence alignment unnecessary

skills.description: Use when building or extending a protein ortholog database for non-model eukaryotic species (e.g., species lacking a reference transcriptome) so reads can be quantified against ortholog groups instead of transcript IDs.
skills.name: ortholog-group-clustering
skills.search_text: ortholog-group-clustering Use when building or extending a protein ortholog database for non-model eukaryotic species (e.g., species lacking a reference transcriptome) so reads can be quantified against ortholog groups instead of transcript IDs. The species already has a well-annotated reference genome/transcriptome and a standard gene-level quantification pipeline (e.g., Kallisto against GRCz11) is sufficient — KO/ortholog coverage is limited (only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes carry KOs), so ortholog-based analysis is mainly for non-model species. The input is already a count table or gene list keyed to known IDs — use the downstream statistical/enrichment modules instead of rebuilding ortholog groups. A taxonomically narrow sub-group database would be a mismatch for the sample (e.g., mapping protist reads against the 'fishes' database), which risks missing key functional groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Binning protein-coding sequences from hundreds of eukaryotic species into ortholog groups with OrthoFinder, as used to construct the EcoOmicsDB ortholog database (666,067 groups from 12,828,537 KEGG proteins across 687 species) that underpins KO-level RNA-seq analysis of non-model species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Binning protein-coding sequences from hundreds of eukaryotic species into ortholog groups with OrthoFinder, as used to construct the EcoOmicsDB ortholog database (666,067 groups from 12,828,537 KEGG proteins across 687 species) that underpins KO-level RNA-seq analysis of non-model species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species already has a well-annotated reference genome/transcriptome and a standard gene-level quantification pipeline (e.g., Kallisto against GRCz11) is sufficient — KO/ortholog coverage is limited (only 76.16% of human and 61.40% of zebrafish protein-coding genes carry KOs), so ortholog-based analysis is mainly for non-model species. The input is already a count table or gene list keyed to known IDs — use the downstream statistical/enrichment modules instead of rebuilding ortholog groups. A taxonomically narrow sub-group database would be a mismatch for the sample (e.g., mapping protist reads against the 'fishes' database), which risks missing key functional groups.

skills.description: Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple species for integration and you must define homologous gene groups (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) before concatenating counts into a shared feature matrix.
skills.name: ortholog-group-construction-o2o-he-sh
skills.search_text: ortholog-group-construction-o2o-he-sh Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple species for integration and you must define homologous gene groups (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) before concatenating counts into a shared feature matrix. The input is already a homologous-gene-aligned or integrated feature matrix rather than per-species raw counts The goal is species-specific gene analysis where dropping unshared genes (in the non-UINMF variants) is not acceptable and UINMF is not used Species lack curated sequence-based gene orthology in ENSEMBL, making orthology-based feature construction unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the cross-species gene feature space for the BENGAL benchmarking pipeline by grouping genes into one-to-one (O2O), one-to-many in-paralog (HE), and many-to-many out-paralog/co-ortholog (SH) orthology classes from ENSEMBL v106 via biomaRt, then subsetting and concatenating raw count matrices per homology class, optionally appending unshared features for LIGER UINMF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Constructs the cross-species gene feature space for the BENGAL benchmarking pipeline by grouping genes into one-to-one (O2O), one-to-many in-paralog (HE), and many-to-many out-paralog/co-ortholog (SH) orthology classes from ENSEMBL v106 via biomaRt, then subsetting and concatenating raw count matrices per homology class, optionally appending unshared features for LIGER UINMF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a homologous-gene-aligned or integrated feature matrix rather than per-species raw counts The goal is species-specific gene analysis where dropping unshared genes (in the non-UINMF variants) is not acceptable and UINMF is not used Species lack curated sequence-based gene orthology in ENSEMBL, making orthology-based feature construction unreliable

skills.description: Use when differential expression has been called on ortholog-group IDs (e.g. via Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst for species lacking a reference transcriptome) and you must validate whether the significant DEG list is inflated by reads from one gene mapping to different ortholog IDs in different species.
skills.name: ortholog-group-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: ortholog-group-differential-expression-analysis Use when differential expression has been called on ortholog-group IDs (e.g. via Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst for species lacking a reference transcriptome) and you must validate whether the significant DEG list is inflated by reads from one gene mapping to different ortholog IDs in different species. Input is already gene-level (not ortholog-level) DE results from a species with a well-annotated reference transcriptome — cross-species ortholog duplication is not the relevant concern You intend to use the default stricter cutoff (FDR < 0.05 and |log fold change| > 1.5) when reproducing the salamander study, which explicitly used FDR-adjusted p < 0.1 The taxonomic subgroup database was chosen improperly (e.g. reads mapped to the wrong phylum's database), since key functional groups may be missed and duplication audit would be meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential expression analysis performed at KEGG ortholog (KO) group level for non-model species, followed by an audit of how many significant hits are duplicated ortholog pairs (reads from the same gene mapping to similar but distinct orthologs across species). This skill tests whether ortholog-level DEG counts are inflated, e.g. confirming that duplicated DEGs account for only ~3% of significant salamander results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Differential expression analysis performed at KEGG ortholog (KO) group level for non-model species, followed by an audit of how many significant hits are duplicated ortholog pairs (reads from the same gene mapping to similar but distinct orthologs across species). This skill tests whether ortholog-level DEG counts are inflated, e.g. confirming that duplicated DEGs account for only ~3% of significant salamander results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already gene-level (not ortholog-level) DE results from a species with a well-annotated reference transcriptome — cross-species ortholog duplication is not the relevant concern You intend to use the default stricter cutoff (FDR < 0.05 and |log fold change| > 1.5) when reproducing the salamander study, which explicitly used FDR-adjusted p < 0.1 The taxonomic subgroup database was chosen improperly (e.g. reads mapped to the wrong phylum's database), since key functional groups may be missed and duplication audit would be meaningless

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets from different plant species must be integrated onto a shared UMAP/embedding while keeping cell identities consistent and detecting species-specific or conserved (e.g. meristem) cell types.
skills.name: orthologous-gene-anchoring
skills.search_text: orthologous-gene-anchoring Use when scRNA-seq datasets from different plant species must be integrated onto a shared UMAP/embedding while keeping cell identities consistent and detecting species-specific or conserved (e.g. meristem) cell types. Input is single-species scRNA-seq data — ordinary scPlant/Seurat processing (readData, QCfun, RunSeurat) is the right path, not crossSpecies_integrate Species pairs lack one-to-one orthologous genes sufficient for anchoring, so the ortholog map cannot support CCA/RPCA integration The goal is cell-type-specific gene regulatory network construction or trajectory inference within one species rather than cross-species integration http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cross-species single-cell integration that anchors one-to-one orthologous genes between plant species (e.g. Arabidopsis, rice, maize) so their scRNA-seq data can be co-embedded while preserving cell identity, as implemented in scPlant's crossSpecies_integrate built on Seurat's CCA/RPCA integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Cross-species single-cell integration that anchors one-to-one orthologous genes between plant species (e.g. Arabidopsis, rice, maize) so their scRNA-seq data can be co-embedded while preserving cell identity, as implemented in scPlant's crossSpecies_integrate built on Seurat's CCA/RPCA integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-species scRNA-seq data — ordinary scPlant/Seurat processing (readData, QCfun, RunSeurat) is the right path, not crossSpecies_integrate Species pairs lack one-to-one orthologous genes sufficient for anchoring, so the ortholog map cannot support CCA/RPCA integration The goal is cell-type-specific gene regulatory network construction or trajectory inference within one species rather than cross-species integration

skills.description: Use when a target species' genes need evolutionary age classes derived from precomputed or newly computed orthologous groups (OrthoFinder, eggNOG v6, PLAZA v5), e.g. to build an orthomap or count species gene-age coverage.
skills.name: orthologous-group-lca-gene-age-interpretation
skills.search_text: orthologous-group-lca-gene-age-interpretation Use when a target species' genes need evolutionary age classes derived from precomputed or newly computed orthologous groups (OrthoFinder, eggNOG v6, PLAZA v5), e.g. to build an orthomap or count species gene-age coverage. The orthologous groups must first be computed from protein/CDS FASTA — this skill consumes existing OrthoFinder/eggNOG/PLAZA orthogroup results, not raw sequence files. The goal is orthology inference itself (finding orthogroups/orthologs) rather than interpreting existing orthogroups as gene ages — use OrthoFinder directly instead. Taxonomic lineages are needed for species other than the query target and without orthogroup context — use NCBI taxonomy queries (ncbitax/qlin) alone. http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Interprets orthologous groups as gene ages by assigning the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of each orthogroup as a gene age class for a target species, using oggmap to extract an orthomap from OrthoFinder, eggNOG, or PLAZA orthology results. The resulting gene ages per orthogroup enable downstream analyses such as gene age-weighted expression (TEI) on scRNA data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Interprets orthologous groups as gene ages by assigning the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of each orthogroup as a gene age class for a target species, using oggmap to extract an orthomap from OrthoFinder, eggNOG, or PLAZA orthology results. The resulting gene ages per orthogroup enable downstream analyses such as gene age-weighted expression (TEI) on scRNA data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The orthologous groups must first be computed from protein/CDS FASTA — this skill consumes existing OrthoFinder/eggNOG/PLAZA orthogroup results, not raw sequence files. The goal is orthology inference itself (finding orthogroups/orthologs) rather than interpreting existing orthogroups as gene ages — use OrthoFinder directly instead. Taxonomic lineages are needed for species other than the query target and without orthogroup context — use NCBI taxonomy queries (ncbitax/qlin) alone.

skills.description: Use when the task requires quantifying species coverage of precomputed gene age / orthomap assignments in oggmap, e.g. verifying that oggmap covers 317 (Ensembl release-110), 1322 (eggNOG v6), and 98 dicots + 52 monocots (PLAZA v5) eukaryotic species.
skills.name: orthomap-gene-age-coverage-counting
skills.search_text: orthomap-gene-age-coverage-counting Use when the task requires quantifying species coverage of precomputed gene age / orthomap assignments in oggmap, e.g. verifying that oggmap covers 317 (Ensembl release-110), 1322 (eggNOG v6), and 98 dicots + 52 monocots (PLAZA v5) eukaryotic species. The goal is to generate a NEW orthomap for a single query species from your own OrthoFinder, eggNOG, or PLAZA results — use the oggmap subcommands (of2orthomap, plaza2orthomap) instead of counting shipped coverage files.
