skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq cell population appears homogeneous but you suspect hidden heterogeneity (e.g., compromised/doublet cells), and known covariates (patient identity, geometric library size) fail to explain the residual variation.
skills.name: outlier-cell-identification-from-sv1
skills.search_text: outlier-cell-identification-from-sv1 Use when a scRNA-seq cell population appears homogeneous but you suspect hidden heterogeneity (e.g., compromised/doublet cells), and known covariates (patient identity, geometric library size) fail to explain the residual variation. The goal is de novo cell-type clustering of a mixed population — IA-SVA here is for hidden factors within one ostensibly homogeneous cell type, not cell-type discovery A known factor (e.g., patient identity or library size) already fully explains the variation; PC1 highly correlated with geometric library size should be discarded rather than interpreted as biology The SV being examined is not significant by the permutation-based significance index; the paper cautions SI is not an empirical p-value and a stringent SI cut-off is recommended when many unknown factors are expected http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies hidden outlier cells within a seemingly homogeneous single-cell population by thresholding the first surrogate variable (SV1) inferred with IA-SVA, as demonstrated on 101 human alpha cells from the Lawlor islet dataset where 6 outlier cells were separated from 95 normal cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: Identifies hidden outlier cells within a seemingly homogeneous single-cell population by thresholding the first surrogate variable (SV1) inferred with IA-SVA, as demonstrated on 101 human alpha cells from the Lawlor islet dataset where 6 outlier cells were separated from 95 normal cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo cell-type clustering of a mixed population — IA-SVA here is for hidden factors within one ostensibly homogeneous cell type, not cell-type discovery A known factor (e.g., patient identity or library size) already fully explains the variation; PC1 highly correlated with geometric library size should be discarded rather than interpreted as biology The SV being examined is not significant by the permutation-based significance index; the paper cautions SI is not an empirical p-value and a stringent SI cut-off is recommended when many unknown factors are expected

skills.description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes with a senescence signature (e.g. SenePy hub scores) and you need to call individual senescent outlier cells and test whether their proportion shifts across groups such as donor age.
skills.name: outlier-cell-thresholding-gaussian-sigma
skills.search_text: outlier-cell-thresholding-gaussian-sigma Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes with a senescence signature (e.g. SenePy hub scores) and you need to call individual senescent outlier cells and test whether their proportion shifts across groups such as donor age. When you need calibrated per-cell senescence probabilities rather than a population-relative tail call: mu + 3 sigma is distribution-relative, so a hub-score shift in the whole population changes the threshold When the data are scaled (z-scored) — score_hub expects unscaled data; binarized default scoring makes normalization optional but scaling breaks it When comparing across hubs or datasets with very different cell numbers without care, since the 3-sigma cutoff and chi-square counts are sensitive to population size and score distribution shape http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A statistical procedure for identifying senescent 'outlier' cells from single-cell SenePy hub-score distributions: cells exceeding the population mean plus 3 standard deviations (mu + 3 sigma) are flagged, and age-dependent shifts in outlier proportions are tested with a chi-square test on the outlier/non-outlier contingency table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: A statistical procedure for identifying senescent 'outlier' cells from single-cell SenePy hub-score distributions: cells exceeding the population mean plus 3 standard deviations (mu + 3 sigma) are flagged, and age-dependent shifts in outlier proportions are tested with a chi-square test on the outlier/non-outlier contingency table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need calibrated per-cell senescence probabilities rather than a population-relative tail call: mu + 3 sigma is distribution-relative, so a hub-score shift in the whole population changes the threshold When the data are scaled (z-scored) — score_hub expects unscaled data; binarized default scoring makes normalization optional but scaling breaks it When comparing across hubs or datasets with very different cell numbers without care, since the 3-sigma cutoff and chi-square counts are sensitive to population size and score distribution shape

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression log fold changes after DCA denoising and isolated genes show extreme LFC outliers in the denoised data that were not present in raw data or bulk samples.
skills.name: outlier-log-fold-change-correction
skills.search_text: outlier-log-fold-change-correction Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression log fold changes after DCA denoising and isolated genes show extreme LFC outliers in the denoised data that were not present in raw data or bulk samples. The input log fold changes come from raw (non-denoised) single-cell data where the outlier arose from dropout rather than from denoising artifacts The comparison is between denoised data and a ground truth other than bulk samples, since the article notes defining ground truth for real data is challenging Denoising was performed with hyperparameters producing overimputation (e.g., too low-dimensional bottleneck layer), which may itself create distorted gene-level values A corrective step applied to differential expression log fold changes computed on DCA-denoised single-cell data, where individual genes (e.g., LEFTY1 in the Chu et al. H1 vs DEC data) show spurious outlier LFCs after denoising that would otherwise deflate correspondence with bulk LFCs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: A corrective step applied to differential expression log fold changes computed on DCA-denoised single-cell data, where individual genes (e.g., LEFTY1 in the Chu et al. H1 vs DEC data) show spurious outlier LFCs after denoising that would otherwise deflate correspondence with bulk LFCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input log fold changes come from raw (non-denoised) single-cell data where the outlier arose from dropout rather than from denoising artifacts The comparison is between denoised data and a ground truth other than bulk samples, since the article notes defining ground truth for real data is challenging Denoising was performed with hyperparameters producing overimputation (e.g., too low-dimensional bottleneck layer), which may itself create distorted gene-level values

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a replicate-aware count model (e.g., PAIRADISE paired model) is more robust than a naive pooled-read baseline under outlier contamination, or when tracing power-versus-number-of-replicates curves for differential splicing detection.
skills.name: outlier-replicate-perturbation-simulation
skills.search_text: outlier-replicate-perturbation-simulation Use when evaluating whether a replicate-aware count model (e.g., PAIRADISE paired model) is more robust than a naive pooled-read baseline under outlier contamination, or when tracing power-versus-number-of-replicates curves for differential splicing detection. When the goal is to run the PAIRADISE pipeline on real RNA-seq FASTQ data (personalization, mapping, annotation, counting) — this skill is a simulation-based robustness benchmark, not the data-processing pipeline. When there is no replicate structure to perturb (single-sample analysis): PAIRADISE's advantage comes from aggregating signals across multiple individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP, which is the setup being simulated. When the question is detecting ASAS events themselves rather than benchmarking detection methods under outlier contamination. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3300 A benchmarking simulation that injects an outlier replicate (one replicate PSI drawn from Uniform[0,1]) into simulated allele-specific splicing count data to show that PAIRADISE's paired replicate model is substantially more robust than a Fisher's exact test on pooled reads for differential AS detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: A benchmarking simulation that injects an outlier replicate (one replicate PSI drawn from Uniform[0,1]) into simulated allele-specific splicing count data to show that PAIRADISE's paired replicate model is substantially more robust than a Fisher's exact test on pooled reads for differential AS detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to run the PAIRADISE pipeline on real RNA-seq FASTQ data (personalization, mapping, annotation, counting) — this skill is a simulation-based robustness benchmark, not the data-processing pipeline. When there is no replicate structure to perturb (single-sample analysis): PAIRADISE's advantage comes from aggregating signals across multiple individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP, which is the setup being simulated. When the question is detecting ASAS events themselves rather than benchmarking detection methods under outlier contamination.

skills.description: Use when analyzing 10x Visium spatial spots from a tissue time course (e.g., myocardial infarction) to flag senescence-high outlier spots, test their colocalization with a spatial marker such as Col1a1 fibrosis, and quantify Moran's I spatial autocorrelation.
skills.name: outlier-spot-detection-in-time-course-spatial-data
skills.search_text: outlier-spot-detection-in-time-course-spatial-data Use when analyzing 10x Visium spatial spots from a tissue time course (e.g., myocardial infarction) to flag senescence-high outlier spots, test their colocalization with a spatial marker such as Col1a1 fibrosis, and quantify Moran's I spatial autocorrelation. Input is single-cell (not spatial) data — plain SenePy hub scoring per cell suffices without spot-level outlier detection or Moran's I Data are scaled (e.g., scanpy.pp.scale applied) — score_hub requires raw or normalized, non-scaled expression No spatial coordinates are available, so colocalization and Moran's I spatial autocorrelation cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect spatially coherent senescence-outlier spots in Visium spatial transcriptomics by scoring spots against cell-type-specific SenePy senescence hubs, aggregating into a composite senescence burden, and testing colocalization with fibrosis markers and spatial autocorrelation over a post-MI time course. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Detect spatially coherent senescence-outlier spots in Visium spatial transcriptomics by scoring spots against cell-type-specific SenePy senescence hubs, aggregating into a composite senescence burden, and testing colocalization with fibrosis markers and spatial autocorrelation over a post-MI time course.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (not spatial) data — plain SenePy hub scoring per cell suffices without spot-level outlier detection or Moran's I Data are scaled (e.g., scanpy.pp.scale applied) — score_hub requires raw or normalized, non-scaled expression No spatial coordinates are available, so colocalization and Moran's I spatial autocorrelation cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when SCISSOR has returned a ScissorOutput object with GSC$OS and LSC$OS outlyingness scores and you must identify and report which samples exceed the global/local shape-change cutoffs for a gene such as TP53.
skills.name: outlyingness-score-visualization
skills.search_text: outlyingness-score-visualization Use when SCISSOR has returned a ScissorOutput object with GSC$OS and LSC$OS outlyingness scores and you must identify and report which samples exceed the global/local shape-change cutoffs for a gene such as TP53. The Scissor() detection step has not yet been run — there are no outlyingness scores or cutoffs to visualize yet Samples with severe RNA degradation were not excluded first (e.g., the 70 severely degraded cases out of 522 TCGA HNSC), since degraded profiles would dominate the outlyingness plots The goal is mutation calling or junction-based isoform quantification rather than coverage-shape outlier screening, for which tools like DEXSeq, MISO, or rMATS are designed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualizes per-sample outlyingness scores from SCISSOR's global (GSC) and local (LSC) shape-change detection, using plot_ScissorOS with sample labels, against the derived significance cutoffs (e.g., 1e-04), to identify which samples deviate from the gene's coverage shape. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Visualizes per-sample outlyingness scores from SCISSOR's global (GSC) and local (LSC) shape-change detection, using plot_ScissorOS with sample labels, against the derived significance cutoffs (e.g., 1e-04), to identify which samples deviate from the gene's coverage shape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Scissor() detection step has not yet been run — there are no outlyingness scores or cutoffs to visualize yet Samples with severe RNA degradation were not excluded first (e.g., the 70 severely degraded cases out of 522 TCGA HNSC), since degraded profiles would dominate the outlyingness plots The goal is mutation calling or junction-based isoform quantification rather than coverage-shape outlier screening, for which tools like DEXSeq, MISO, or rMATS are designed

skills.description: Use when a high-resolution Leiden-clustered scRNA-seq AnnData is intentionally over-clustered and you must quantify how well a merging method discriminates significant from non-significant artificial over-cluster pairs via AUROC.
skills.name: over-clustered-annata-merging-benchmark
skills.search_text: over-clustered-annata-merging-benchmark Use when a high-resolution Leiden-clustered scRNA-seq AnnData is intentionally over-clustered and you must quantify how well a merging method discriminates significant from non-significant artificial over-cluster pairs via AUROC. The input clustering is not over-clustered — Cytocipher assumes high-resolution tentative Leiden labels so that non-significantly different clusters exist to merge The task is de novo clustering rather than testing/merging of existing tentative cluster labels The dataset lacks known cell-type labels, so AUROC of merged clusters against ground truth cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark cluster-merging of deliberately over-clustered single-cell AnnData (e.g. the 483152-cell Tabula Sapiens Atlas with high-resolution Leiden labels) using Cytocipher's significance testing, scoring performance as AUROC against known cell-type labels, and comparing against Sc-SHC and Giotto-based scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Benchmark cluster-merging of deliberately over-clustered single-cell AnnData (e.g. the 483152-cell Tabula Sapiens Atlas with high-resolution Leiden labels) using Cytocipher's significance testing, scoring performance as AUROC against known cell-type labels, and comparing against Sc-SHC and Giotto-based scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input clustering is not over-clustered — Cytocipher assumes high-resolution tentative Leiden labels so that non-significantly different clusters exist to merge The task is de novo clustering rather than testing/merging of existing tentative cluster labels The dataset lacks known cell-type labels, so AUROC of merged clusters against ground truth cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when transferring reference cell-type labels onto a large query single-cell dataset (AnnData) via marker-based cell-type scores, and you need robust consensus annotations by over-clustering across multiple MACA parameter settings rather than a single clustering run.
skills.name: over-clustering-ensemble-label-transfer
skills.search_text: over-clustering-ensemble-label-transfer Use when transferring reference cell-type labels onto a large query single-cell dataset (AnnData) via marker-based cell-type scores, and you need robust consensus annotations by over-clustering across multiple MACA parameter settings rather than a single clustering run. Query data contains cell types or subtypes absent from the reference — MASI alone cannot annotate unseen cell types; combine MASI with SCCAF to identify subtypes within major cell types. The input has not been converted to a cell-type score matrix (masi.gene2cell not yet run) — this skill operates on scores, not raw gene expression. Annotation accuracy is critical and the reference data quality/resolution is uncertain — annotation via MASI depends on reference quality, and the choice and resolution of the reference are critical to downstream analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A MASI-based label-transfer strategy that deliberately over-clusters cells with MACA across multiple clustering resolutions (3, 5, 7) and neighborhood sizes (5, 10, 15), then ensembles the resulting labels into stable major cell-type/lineage annotations, with large datasets split into N batches (default batch_size=50000) processed one batch per CPU core. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: A MASI-based label-transfer strategy that deliberately over-clusters cells with MACA across multiple clustering resolutions (3, 5, 7) and neighborhood sizes (5, 10, 15), then ensembles the resulting labels into stable major cell-type/lineage annotations, with large datasets split into N batches (default batch_size=50000) processed one batch per CPU core.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data contains cell types or subtypes absent from the reference — MASI alone cannot annotate unseen cell types; combine MASI with SCCAF to identify subtypes within major cell types. The input has not been converted to a cell-type score matrix (masi.gene2cell not yet run) — this skill operates on scores, not raw gene expression. Annotation accuracy is critical and the reference data quality/resolution is uncertain — annotation via MASI depends on reference quality, and the choice and resolution of the reference are critical to downstream analysis.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking single-cell batch correction methods (scCobra, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) on two same-condition samples and you need to detect over-correction by comparing DEG counts before vs. after correction.
skills.name: over-correction-assessment-via-deg-preservation
skills.search_text: over-correction-assessment-via-deg-preservation Use when benchmarking single-cell batch correction methods (scCobra, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) on two same-condition samples and you need to detect over-correction by comparing DEG counts before vs. after correction. The two samples come from different conditions (e.g. healthy vs. disease) — true biological differences would then produce legitimate DEGs, and DEG reduction would wrongly flag over-correction, which the article describes as ignoring 'the potential inherent difference associated with different batches'. Only one sample per condition is available, since the metric relies on a pairwise DE test between two same-condition samples. You need batch-correction metrics other than over-correction (e.g. bio-conservation scoring via the scIB pipeline with Leiden clustering at resolutions 0.1–2.0). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies batch-correction over-correction by counting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between two healthy samples from the same condition after applying each correction method; a well-behaved method (e.g. scCobra) should shrink raw DEG counts (470 for GSE149614 raw) toward few DEGs while over-correcting or under-correcting methods leave more (Harmony 40, scVI 66). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Quantifies batch-correction over-correction by counting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between two healthy samples from the same condition after applying each correction method; a well-behaved method (e.g. scCobra) should shrink raw DEG counts (470 for GSE149614 raw) toward few DEGs while over-correcting or under-correcting methods leave more (Harmony 40, scVI 66).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two samples come from different conditions (e.g. healthy vs. disease) — true biological differences would then produce legitimate DEGs, and DEG reduction would wrongly flag over-correction, which the article describes as ignoring 'the potential inherent difference associated with different batches'. Only one sample per condition is available, since the metric relies on a pairwise DE test between two same-condition samples. You need batch-correction metrics other than over-correction (e.g. bio-conservation scoring via the scIB pipeline with Leiden clustering at resolutions 0.1–2.0).

skills.description: Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition (multi-tissue) scRNA-seq datasets and you need to check the chosen method (JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI, etc.) for over-correction of true biological condition differences.
skills.name: over-correction-quantification-across-tissues
skills.search_text: over-correction-quantification-across-tissues Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition (multi-tissue) scRNA-seq datasets and you need to check the chosen method (JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI, etc.) for over-correction of true biological condition differences. The integration task involves a single tissue/condition where only batch effects (not biological variability) need removing — over-correction is not the relevant failure mode. You only need overall clustering performance (ARI/NMI vs. labels) rather than testing retention of across-condition biological signal. Input is raw expression data that has not yet been merged into a batch-labelled multi-sample object; preprocessing and merging must precede this quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies whether a single-cell batch-integration method removes within-tissue batch effects without erasing genuine across-tissue biological variability, using the pancreas-lung multi-donor benchmark from the JOINTLY paper (e.g., interferon-signalling module scores and 3529 pancreas-vs-lung endothelial DE genes retained). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Quantifies whether a single-cell batch-integration method removes within-tissue batch effects without erasing genuine across-tissue biological variability, using the pancreas-lung multi-donor benchmark from the JOINTLY paper (e.g., interferon-signalling module scores and 3529 pancreas-vs-lung endothelial DE genes retained).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The integration task involves a single tissue/condition where only batch effects (not biological variability) need removing — over-correction is not the relevant failure mode. You only need overall clustering performance (ARI/NMI vs. labels) rather than testing retention of across-condition biological signal. Input is raw expression data that has not yet been merged into a batch-labelled multi-sample object; preprocessing and merging must precede this quantification.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking single-cell batch-correction methods (scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) for over-correction risk on data containing a known biological difference between batches, e.g., an implanted perturbation in GSE149614 immune cells.
skills.name: over-correction-scoring-from-umap-embeddings
skills.search_text: over-correction-scoring-from-umap-embeddings Use when benchmarking single-cell batch-correction methods (scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) for over-correction risk on data containing a known biological difference between batches, e.g., an implanted perturbation in GSE149614 immune cells. When evaluating integration quality metrics other than over-correction (e.g., batch mixing or bio-conservation via the scIB Leiden-clustering pipeline at resolutions 0.1–2.0) When the dataset has no known or implanted biological difference between batches — over-correction cannot be detected without a signal that should be preserved When a distribution-free, embedding-independent over-correction measure is required; these scores are derived from 2D UMAP embeddings per the SCALEX methodology http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Quantify how much a batch-correction method erases genuine biological signal by computing an over-correction score from two-dimensional UMAP embeddings of integrated outputs, following the SCALEX methodology, on data where an implanted perturbation (e.g., 'Defense response to Virus' genes up-shifted in CD4+ T cells of the 10X batch) must be preserved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Quantify how much a batch-correction method erases genuine biological signal by computing an over-correction score from two-dimensional UMAP embeddings of integrated outputs, following the SCALEX methodology, on data where an implanted perturbation (e.g., 'Defense response to Virus' genes up-shifted in CD4+ T cells of the 10X batch) must be preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When evaluating integration quality metrics other than over-correction (e.g., batch mixing or bio-conservation via the scIB Leiden-clustering pipeline at resolutions 0.1–2.0) When the dataset has no known or implanted biological difference between batches — over-correction cannot be detected without a signal that should be preserved When a distribution-free, embedding-independent over-correction measure is required; these scores are derived from 2D UMAP embeddings per the SCALEX methodology

skills.description: Use when preparing multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics counts (e.g., mOB, Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) before fitting LDA in STdeconvolve, and noisy, low-variance genes must be filtered out.
skills.name: overdispersed-gene-feature-selection
skills.search_text: overdispersed-gene-feature-selection Use when preparing multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics counts (e.g., mOB, Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) before fitting LDA in STdeconvolve, and noisy, low-variance genes must be filtered out. The ST data is sub-cellular resolution or covers only a few pixels (e.g., tissue slivers), where overdispersed genes are insufficient for deconvolution Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack variability and overdispersion filtering yields no informative signal A pre-computed feature-selected gene set is already available and no re-filtering is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 STdeconvolve's unsupervised feature-selection step that retains significantly overdispersed genes — those with higher-than-expected expression variance across ST pixels — to prepare a pixel-by-gene count matrix for latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) deconvolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: STdeconvolve's unsupervised feature-selection step that retains significantly overdispersed genes — those with higher-than-expected expression variance across ST pixels — to prepare a pixel-by-gene count matrix for latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) deconvolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ST data is sub-cellular resolution or covers only a few pixels (e.g., tissue slivers), where overdispersed genes are insufficient for deconvolution Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack variability and overdispersion filtering yields no informative signal A pre-computed feature-selected gene set is already available and no re-filtering is needed

skills.description: Use when dimension-reducing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (SingleCellExperiment) whose counts are overdispersed and where log(x+1)+PCA pipelines underperform, or when benchmarking embeddings against ground-truth cell-type labels with ARI.
skills.name: overdispersion-adjusted-ca-variants
skills.search_text: overdispersion-adjusted-ca-variants Use when dimension-reducing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (SingleCellExperiment) whose counts are overdispersed and where log(x+1)+PCA pipelines underperform, or when benchmarking embeddings against ground-truth cell-type labels with ARI. When the goal is multi-table batch integration rather than single-table dimension reduction — corralm, not the corral CA-variant benchmarking path, is the appropriate entry point When the input is already log-transformed 'logcounts' intended for a PCA pipeline — CA operates on raw counts via chi-squared residuals and should not be applied to log-transformed matrices When ground-truth cell labels are independently validated complex-tissue annotations are required — the SCMixology/Zhengmix benchmarks are simple pseudo-cell mixtures without independently validated labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies the corral R/Bioconductor package's five CA adaptations for overdispersed scRNA-seq counts (Freeman-Tukey residuals, square-root/Anscombe/Freeman-Tukey variance-stabilizing transformations, and power deflation with alpha = 0.9), and benchmarks their cell-population recovery via ARI against standard CA and glmPCA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Applies the corral R/Bioconductor package's five CA adaptations for overdispersed scRNA-seq counts (Freeman-Tukey residuals, square-root/Anscombe/Freeman-Tukey variance-stabilizing transformations, and power deflation with alpha = 0.9), and benchmarks their cell-population recovery via ARI against standard CA and glmPCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is multi-table batch integration rather than single-table dimension reduction — corralm, not the corral CA-variant benchmarking path, is the appropriate entry point When the input is already log-transformed 'logcounts' intended for a PCA pipeline — CA operates on raw counts via chi-squared residuals and should not be applied to log-transformed matrices When ground-truth cell labels are independently validated complex-tissue annotations are required — the SCMixology/Zhengmix benchmarks are simple pseudo-cell mixtures without independently validated labels

skills.description: Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a Seurat object and likely doublets must be removed before artificial-doublet simulation for training.
skills.name: overkill-doublet-removal-prefiltering
skills.search_text: overkill-doublet-removal-prefiltering Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a Seurat object and likely doublets must be removed before artificial-doublet simulation for training. Data already contains experimental doublet labels (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) — those methods require special operations and costs but directly label doublets, making computational prefiltering redundant Running downstream boosting with additional methods on seu.robj / overkilled.robj — that is the 'addmethods' stage, not the initial overkill prefilter Runtime is critical: Chord (including overkill) is not time-optimal because it integrates results of multiple methods http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Chord's 'overkill' preliminary filtering stage that removes the most likely doublets from a droplet scRNA-seq dataset using its three built-in detectors (scds cxds, scds bcds, and DoubletFinder) before artificial doublets are simulated for training the GBM/AdaBoost classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Chord's 'overkill' preliminary filtering stage that removes the most likely doublets from a droplet scRNA-seq dataset using its three built-in detectors (scds cxds, scds bcds, and DoubletFinder) before artificial doublets are simulated for training the GBM/AdaBoost classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already contains experimental doublet labels (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) — those methods require special operations and costs but directly label doublets, making computational prefiltering redundant Running downstream boosting with additional methods on seu.robj / overkilled.robj — that is the 'addmethods' stage, not the initial overkill prefilter Runtime is critical: Chord (including overkill) is not time-optimal because it integrates results of multiple methods

skills.description: Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a droplet-based scRNA-seq sample (e.g. a Seurat object) and you need the overkilled training data — doublets filtered out and simulated doublets generated from remaining cells — before GBM integration of method scores.
skills.name: overkill-simulated-doublet-training-set-construction
skills.search_text: overkill-simulated-doublet-training-set-construction Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a droplet-based scRNA-seq sample (e.g. a Seurat object) and you need the overkilled training data — doublets filtered out and simulated doublets generated from remaining cells — before GBM integration of method scores. Time-critical analyses — Chord requires integration of multiple methods' results, so it is not optimal in terms of time efficiency Data where doublets are already experimentally labeled (e.g. cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet), making computational overkill unnecessary Existing scRNA-seq datasets where you only want to run one lightweight detector rather than retrain an ensemble on simulated doublets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 The Chord 'overkill' step: built-in methods (scds, DoubletFinder) first evaluate the real data, the top fraction of doublet-like cells is removed, and artificial doublets are then simulated from the remaining cells to form the training set for the GBM/AdaBoost ensemble classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: The Chord 'overkill' step: built-in methods (scds, DoubletFinder) first evaluate the real data, the top fraction of doublet-like cells is removed, and artificial doublets are then simulated from the remaining cells to form the training set for the GBM/AdaBoost ensemble classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Time-critical analyses — Chord requires integration of multiple methods' results, so it is not optimal in terms of time efficiency Data where doublets are already experimentally labeled (e.g. cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet), making computational overkill unnecessary Existing scRNA-seq datasets where you only want to run one lightweight detector rather than retrain an ensemble on simulated doublets

skills.description: Use when you have feature sets selected by a method (e.g., G-PC, CEM-PC, mrmr, ReliefF, F) over multiple runs on randomly sampled data and need to measure how reproducible the selected gene/feature sets are across runs.
skills.name: overlap-over-union-statistic-computation
skills.search_text: overlap-over-union-statistic-computation Use when you have feature sets selected by a method (e.g., G-PC, CEM-PC, mrmr, ReliefF, F) over multiple runs on randomly sampled data and need to measure how reproducible the selected gene/feature sets are across runs. Only a single feature set exists (no repeated runs over resampled data), so no pairwise overlap statistics can be computed The goal is discriminative performance (classification accuracy or deconvolution error) rather than selection reproducibility Feature sets come from datasets with non-matching feature spaces (different gene identifiers), making set overlap meaningless Quantifies the reproducibility (stability) of marker-selection procedures by computing pairwise overlap-over-union statistics between feature sets selected across repeated runs on randomly resampled data, then aggregating them into a per-method stability index. Used in Hasanaj et al. (Cell Reports Methods, 2022) to show G-PC retains ~60-70% of genes across runs while CEM-PC is the least stable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Quantifies the reproducibility (stability) of marker-selection procedures by computing pairwise overlap-over-union statistics between feature sets selected across repeated runs on randomly resampled data, then aggregating them into a per-method stability index. Used in Hasanaj et al. (Cell Reports Methods, 2022) to show G-PC retains ~60-70% of genes across runs while CEM-PC is the least stable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single feature set exists (no repeated runs over resampled data), so no pairwise overlap statistics can be computed The goal is discriminative performance (classification accuracy or deconvolution error) rather than selection reproducibility Feature sets come from datasets with non-matching feature spaces (different gene identifiers), making set overlap meaningless

skills.description: Decision support for judging per-HTO demultiplexing quality after fitting demuxmix regression mixture models: needed when you must rank HTOs by how well their negative and positive droplet populations separate before accepting classifications.
skills.name: overlap-score-computation-from-mixture-components
skills.search_text: overlap-score-computation-from-mixture-components Decision support for judging per-HTO demultiplexing quality after fitting demuxmix regression mixture models: needed when you must rank HTOs by how well their negative and positive droplet populations separate before accepting classifications. The HTO mixture models have not yet been fitted — the overlap score requires the fitted negative and positive components of the DemuxmixResult, not raw HTO counts alone You need per-droplet classification decisions or error probabilities — this skill yields a per-HTO separability metric, not assignments for individual droplets The data are not oligonucleotide-barcoded (HTO-labeled) scRNA-seq droplets — the negative/positive component structure is specific to demuxmix's HTO mixture models http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Computes the overlap score (ovs) for each hashtag oligonucleotide (HTO) as the shared probability mass of the negative and positive components of the fitted demuxmix mixture model, a per-HTO data-quality metric quantifying how separable the two droplet classes are. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Computes the overlap score (ovs) for each hashtag oligonucleotide (HTO) as the shared probability mass of the negative and positive components of the fitted demuxmix mixture model, a per-HTO data-quality metric quantifying how separable the two droplet classes are.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The HTO mixture models have not yet been fitted — the overlap score requires the fitted negative and positive components of the DemuxmixResult, not raw HTO counts alone You need per-droplet classification decisions or error probabilities — this skill yields a per-HTO separability metric, not assignments for individual droplets The data are not oligonucleotide-barcoded (HTO-labeled) scRNA-seq droplets — the negative/positive component structure is specific to demuxmix's HTO mixture models

skills.search_text: overlap-score-computation-hto-datasets Use when you need a numeric, per-dataset quality metric for HTO demultiplexing data — e.g., to compare newly published GEO HTO datasets against benchmarks or simulated low-quality levels before choosing a demultiplexing method. skills.summary: Quantify the quality of hashtag oligonucleotide (HTO) count matrices by fitting demuxmix's negative binomial regression mixture models and computing the overlap score (ovs) between fitted components, enabling comparison of real datasets against benchmark or simulated quality levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is RNA gene-by-droplet count data without an accompanying HTO count matrix — the overlap score is defined on HTO counts only You need cell-to-sample assignments (demultiplexing calls) rather than a dataset-level quality metric — use demuxmix's classification instead of computing ovs The HTO data has already been demultiplexed and filtered, since ovs is computed from fitted mixture components on the raw HTO counts

skills.description: Use when preprocessing a real scRNA-seq BAM file for count-matrix training and reads overlapping annotated genes must be assigned to mutually exclusive genomic features.
skills.name: overlapping-gene-supergene-aggregation
skills.search_text: overlapping-gene-supergene-aggregation Use when preprocessing a real scRNA-seq BAM file for count-matrix training and reads overlapping annotated genes must be assigned to mutually exclusive genomic features. Input is an scATAC-seq BAM for peak-based segmentation — use Utility.scATAC_CreateFeatureSets and Utility.CallPeak (MACS3) instead. The goal is isoform-level ground truths (isoform abundance or alternative splicing events), which scReadSim explicitly does not generate. Input already consists of non-overlapping feature regions and no supergene merging is needed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 scReadSim's scRNA-seq genome-segmentation step partitions the reference genome into gene (foreground) and inter-gene (background) BED regions, aggregating overlapping genes into non-overlapping supergenes so counts can be unambiguously assigned. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: scReadSim's scRNA-seq genome-segmentation step partitions the reference genome into gene (foreground) and inter-gene (background) BED regions, aggregating overlapping genes into non-overlapping supergenes so counts can be unambiguously assigned.

When merging only a handful of input signatures (e.g. one tissue's Lung hubs), where a manual overlap_threshold is more appropriate than the permutation-based threshold When you need cell-type- or tissue-specific signatures rather than genes universal across all 97 cell types When the input is already a universal signature list (e.g. universal_signatures/Universal_mouse.txt), which contains genes but no importance weights http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies genes statistically overrepresented across a collection of SenePy cell-type senescence signatures by merging hubs with a permutation-based occurrence threshold, retaining genes significant at FDR p-value < 0.01 to form universal mouse (635 genes) and human (734 genes) panels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7

skills.description: Use when multiple DEG detection method outputs (per-gene p-value vectors) are available and a machine-learning integration of DEG calls is needed, rather than a simple vote threshold cut-off.
skills.name: p-value-integration-across-deg-methods
skills.search_text: p-value-integration-across-deg-methods Use when multiple DEG detection method outputs (per-gene p-value vectors) are available and a machine-learning integration of DEG calls is needed, rather than a simple vote threshold cut-off. A minimum vote threshold cut-off is sufficient 'where possible' — the article recommends the simple threshold as the default suggestion when it works Only a single DEG method's p-values are available, so no multi-method p-value vector can be assembled as classifier features No labelled simulation or ground-truth data exist to train the classifier for the organism/tissue in question http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains a Naive Bayes classifier in the ExpHunter Suite that integrates per-gene p-value vectors from multiple DEG detection methods (e.g. DESeq2, NOISeq, limma) into robust DEG calls. The model is trained on simulated RNA-seq data with DEG/non-DEG ground-truth labels and validated on a spike-in dataset by F-measure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Trains a Naive Bayes classifier in the ExpHunter Suite that integrates per-gene p-value vectors from multiple DEG detection methods (e.g. DESeq2, NOISeq, limma) into robust DEG calls. The model is trained on simulated RNA-seq data with DEG/non-DEG ground-truth labels and validated on a spike-in dataset by F-measure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A minimum vote threshold cut-off is sufficient 'where possible' — the article recommends the simple threshold as the default suggestion when it works Only a single DEG method's p-values are available, so no multi-method p-value vector can be assembled as classifier features No labelled simulation or ground-truth data exist to train the classifier for the organism/tissue in question

skills.description: Use when you need robust DEG detection from RNA-seq count matrices and no single DE method can be assumed appropriate, since methods 'behave quite differently depending on the properties of the data'.
skills.name: p-value-integration-combination
skills.search_text: p-value-integration-combination Use when you need robust DEG detection from RNA-seq count matrices and no single DE method can be assumed appropriate, since methods 'behave quite differently depending on the properties of the data'. When a single method's assumptions are known to fit the experimental design and the goal is interpretability of one method's statistics rather than robust consensus calling When extrapolating the optimal vote threshold (2 for spike-in data) to other organisms, tissues, or experimental designs — the authors are 'hesitant to extrapolate these findings to a more general rule' http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combines DEG calls from multiple differential expression methods (DESeq2, edgeR, limma, NOISeq) by integrating their p-values within the DEgenes Hunter pipeline, producing a combined-FDR ranking that is more robust than any single method across simulated datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Combines DEG calls from multiple differential expression methods (DESeq2, edgeR, limma, NOISeq) by integrating their p-values within the DEgenes Hunter pipeline, producing a combined-FDR ranking that is more robust than any single method across simulated datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single method's assumptions are known to fit the experimental design and the goal is interpretability of one method's statistics rather than robust consensus calling When extrapolating the optimal vote threshold (2 for spike-in data) to other organisms, tissues, or experimental designs — the authors are 'hesitant to extrapolate these findings to a more general rule'

skills.description: Use when combining two independent differential-expression p-values (sender ligand, receiver receptor) into one LR-pair significance and needing a multiple-testing-adjusted p-value to filter candidate ligand-receptor associations.

skills.search_text: p-value-multiple-testing-adjustment Use when combining two independent differential-expression p-values (sender ligand, receiver receptor) into one LR-pair significance and needing a multiple-testing-adjusted p-value to filter candidate ligand-receptor associations. When LR-pair significance should incorporate pathway activity in receiver cells (CommPath's downstream filterLR step) rather than expression-based statistical identification alone When the input is not cluster-level differential-expression results but, e.g., already aggregated interaction counts or pathway-level statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A statistical skill from CommPath that combines ligand and receptor differential-expression p-values into a single LR-pair significance (P_lr,AB = 1 − (1−P_l,A)(1−P_r,B)) and reports an adjusted P value for multiple testing, enabling statistically grounded prioritization of ligand-receptor associations between cell clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: A statistical skill from CommPath that combines ligand and receptor differential-expression p-values into a single LR-pair significance (P_lr,AB = 1 − (1−P_l,A)(1−P_r,B)) and reports an adjusted P value for multiple testing, enabling statistically grounded prioritization of ligand-receptor associations between cell clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When LR-pair significance should incorporate pathway activity in receiver cells (CommPath's downstream filterLR step) rather than expression-based statistical identification alone When the input is not cluster-level differential-expression results but, e.g., already aggregated interaction counts or pathway-level statistics

skills.description: Use when you need to compare per-gene p-value rankings produced by two versions or variants of a feature-scanning method across multiple datasets, to quantify whether a methodological change (e.g., binary detection vs continuous activity) preserves DEG predictions.
skills.name: p-value-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: p-value-rank-correlation-analysis Use when you need to compare per-gene p-value rankings produced by two versions or variants of a feature-scanning method across multiple datasets, to quantify whether a methodological change (e.g., binary detection vs continuous activity) preserves DEG predictions. You need comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons cannot be easily conducted and are planned future work. Your goal is spatial DEG testing where SPARK-X-class speed is required — the article notes singleCellHaystack has 'relatively longer runtimes' than SPARK-X despite better sensitivity. You rely on hierarchical clustering of genes — the Python implementation lacks the cluster_genes hierarchical clustering method (beta-stage missing feature). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies agreement between two per-feature significance-testing variants (here, binary v0.3.4 vs continuous v1.0.0+ singleCellHaystack) by computing Spearman rank correlation between their log p-values across all genes in each dataset, and benchmarks wall-clock runtimes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between two per-feature significance-testing variants (here, binary v0.3.4 vs continuous v1.0.0+ singleCellHaystack) by computing Spearman rank correlation between their log p-values across all genes in each dataset, and benchmarks wall-clock runtimes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need comparisons between multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons cannot be easily conducted and are planned future work. Your goal is spatial DEG testing where SPARK-X-class speed is required — the article notes singleCellHaystack has 'relatively longer runtimes' than SPARK-X despite better sensitivity. You rely on hierarchical clustering of genes — the Python implementation lacks the cluster_genes hierarchical clustering method (beta-stage missing feature).

skills.description: Use when two DEG-prediction methods have been run on the same scRNA-seq dataset and you need per-gene p-value tables and top-N rank-overlap counts to quantify agreement.
skills.name: p-value-scatterplot-data-generation
skills.search_text: p-value-scatterplot-data-generation Use when two DEG-prediction methods have been run on the same scRNA-seq dataset and you need per-gene p-value tables and top-N rank-overlap counts to quantify agreement. The current implementation of singleCellHaystack requires binary detection data as input, so it is the wrong choice if you need continuous expression levels (e.g., normalized read counts) as the basis for the comparison singleCellHaystack is a clustering-independent method; do not use this comparison workflow when you need DEGs defined strictly relative to pre-existing cell cluster labels rather than non-random positioning in a multidimensional space http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compiles per-gene significance values from two DEG prediction approaches — singleCellHaystack (Kullback-Leibler divergence) and Seurat FindAllMarkers (Wilcoxon rank-sum) — into a table suitable for a p-value scatterplot, and quantifies rank-overlap of their top-ranked genes on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Compiles per-gene significance values from two DEG prediction approaches — singleCellHaystack (Kullback-Leibler divergence) and Seurat FindAllMarkers (Wilcoxon rank-sum) — into a table suitable for a p-value scatterplot, and quantifies rank-overlap of their top-ranked genes on the Tabula Muris bone marrow dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The current implementation of singleCellHaystack requires binary detection data as input, so it is the wrong choice if you need continuous expression levels (e.g., normalized read counts) as the basis for the comparison singleCellHaystack is a clustering-independent method; do not use this comparison workflow when you need DEGs defined strictly relative to pre-existing cell cluster labels rather than non-random positioning in a multidimensional space

skills.description: Use when two SVG/DEG detection methods have been run on the same spatial dataset and you must verify and report which features agree or show discrepant ranks and p-values between them.

skills.search_text: p-value-significance-verification Use when two SVG/DEG detection methods have been run on the same spatial dataset and you must verify and report which features agree or show discrepant ranks and p-values between them. skills.summary: Cross-check per-gene p-values and ranks produced by two spatially-variable-gene methods (singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X) on the same count matrix and 2D spatial coordinates, quantifying where the methods agree (e.g. Gm42418 as top SVG) and where they diverge (e.g. Gm10925: rank 13 by singleCellHaystack, p=2.7e-39, vs rank 105 by SPARK-X, p=0.013).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one method's output is available — the skill requires matched ranked feature lists and p-values from both singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X on the same data. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is short-read RNA-seq data — dsRID and this depth analysis are designed for PacBio long-read RNA-seq Input is already a feature table such as dsRID_data.tsv or dsRID_whole.tsv (BAM input is required for the training/extraction steps) Goal is simply to predict dsRNA regions at full sequencing depth without assessing depth sufficiency — use the standard dsRID workflow instead

skills.description: Use when simulating or implementing a DNA-based data storage encode path that must convert an arbitrary binary file into addressable packets and base-sequences prior to inner-code DNA strand synthesis, e.g. when building or validating a FrameD-style pipeline.
skills.name: packet-base-sequence-file-segmentation
skills.search_text: packet-base-sequence-file-segmentation Use when simulating or implementing a DNA-based data storage encode path that must convert an arbitrary binary file into addressable packets and base-sequences prior to inner-code DNA strand synthesis, e.g. when building or validating a FrameD-style pipeline. The input is already a set of sequenced DNA reads or FASTQ strands — segmentation applies on the encode side; for those inputs the decode path (clustering, MSA, inner-code reversal) is the relevant skill. The goal is to model channel errors (e.g. nanopore synthesis/sequencing/basecalling errors) rather than to segment and encode a file — a simulator such as DNArSim is the appropriate tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Segmentation stage of the FrameD DNA storage pipeline in which an input file is decomposed into packets and then into base-sequences before indexing and inner encoding to DNA strands.
