The reads are already genome-aligned, e.g., scReadSim's synthetic output is a BAM file already aligned to the reference genome The goal is count-level comparison using gene-by-cell UMI count matrices, which requires no read alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aligns synthetic paired-end reads (e.g., minnow's two FASTQ files) to the same mm10 reference genome used for real scRNA-seq data, so synthetic coverage can be directly compared with already-aligned real BAM files in genomic windows. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Aligns synthetic paired-end reads (e.g., minnow's two FASTQ files) to the same mm10 reference genome used for real scRNA-seq data, so synthetic coverage can be directly compared with already-aligned real BAM files in genomic windows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads are already genome-aligned, e.g., scReadSim's synthetic output is a BAM file already aligned to the reference genome The goal is count-level comparison using gene-by-cell UMI count matrices, which requires no read alignment

skills.description: Use when a multi-sample sequencing workflow must ingest raw FASTQ inputs from a sample sheet into per-read-group QC and trimming steps, distinguishing paired-end (R1/R2) from single-end files for DNA-seq and RNA-seq.
skills.name: paired-end-read-group-organization
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-group-organization Use when a multi-sample sequencing workflow must ingest raw FASTQ inputs from a sample sheet into per-read-group QC and trimming steps, distinguishing paired-end (R1/R2) from single-end files for DNA-seq and RNA-seq. Input reads are already trimmed/filtered (no adapter or quality preprocessing needed) — re-running fastp trimming adds no value and risks over-trimming Data are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio) — fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina NovaSeq, MGI); the fastp README directs long-read users to fastplong The goal is downstream alignment or variant calling itself — this skill only covers the pre-processing stage before HLA genotyping, yara filtering, and variant calling http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Organizes raw sequencing reads into per-(sample, seqtype, group) read groups and runs per-file quality control (FastQC) and trimming (fastp) as the first stage of the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, keeping single-end and paired-end file conventions separate. This ensures every downstream HLA genotyping and variant-calling step consumes consistently named, quality-filtered gzipped FASTQ files. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Organizes raw sequencing reads into per-(sample, seqtype, group) read groups and runs per-file quality control (FastQC) and trimming (fastp) as the first stage of the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, keeping single-end and paired-end file conventions separate. This ensures every downstream HLA genotyping and variant-calling step consumes consistently named, quality-filtered gzipped FASTQ files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already trimmed/filtered (no adapter or quality preprocessing needed) — re-running fastp trimming adds no value and risks over-trimming Data are long reads (Nanopore, PacBio) — fastp is designed for short reads (Illumina NovaSeq, MGI); the fastp README directs long-read users to fastplong The goal is downstream alignment or variant calling itself — this skill only covers the pre-processing stage before HLA genotyping, yara filtering, and variant calling

skills.description: Use when processing paired-end, 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g. Microwell-seq FASTQ from Mouse Cell Atlas / Human Cell Landscape) where reads must overlap and be merged to recover the full insert containing the 3' cleavage site.
skills.name: paired-end-read-overlap-assembly
skills.search_text: paired-end-read-overlap-assembly Use when processing paired-end, 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g. Microwell-seq FASTQ from Mouse Cell Atlas / Human Cell Landscape) where reads must overlap and be merged to recover the full insert containing the 3' cleavage site. Input is 10x Genomics 3'-end tag data: most reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, so overlap assembly cannot support exact de novo CS mapping (quantification against a known CS annotation, e.g. scUTRquant, is the correct approach instead). Read pairs from short-insert protocols with no overlap cannot be merged, so overlap assembly would fail or produce partial inserts lacking the cleavage site. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstruct full insert sequences carrying mRNA 3'-end information by merging overlapping paired-end Microwell-seq reads (e.g. with PEAR) before downstream cleavage-site mapping. This is essential for MWS-style data where only full-span reads preserve the position of the cleavage site. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Reconstruct full insert sequences carrying mRNA 3'-end information by merging overlapping paired-end Microwell-seq reads (e.g. with PEAR) before downstream cleavage-site mapping. This is essential for MWS-style data where only full-span reads preserve the position of the cleavage site.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10x Genomics 3'-end tag data: most reads do not span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites, so overlap assembly cannot support exact de novo CS mapping (quantification against a known CS annotation, e.g. scUTRquant, is the correct approach instead). Read pairs from short-insert protocols with no overlap cannot be merged, so overlap assembly would fail or produce partial inserts lacking the cleavage site.

skills.description: Use when performing a targeted fusion search on paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data by anchoring a gene of interest, and reads must be aligned to both the target gene transcript fasta and a whole-genome reference.
skills.name: paired-end-rna-seq-alignment
skills.search_text: paired-end-rna-seq-alignment Use when performing a targeted fusion search on paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data by anchoring a gene of interest, and reads must be aligned to both the target gene transcript fasta and a whole-genome reference. Input is single-end RNA-seq data, whole-genome sequencing, or whole-exome sequencing — Anchored-fusion only supports paired-end RNA-seq The fusion of interest does not include the user-provided target (anchored) gene — such fusions will not be detected An untargeted, de novo fusion discovery across all possible fusion partners is required — the anchored search is limited to the user-specified gene http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Maps paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ reads to an anchored target gene and to the whole genome using BWA-MEM plus samtools, the alignment backbone of the Anchored-fusion targeted fusion search; it recovers multi-mapping and chimeric read pairs that de novo fusion detectors typically discard. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Maps paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ reads to an anchored target gene and to the whole genome using BWA-MEM plus samtools, the alignment backbone of the Anchored-fusion targeted fusion search; it recovers multi-mapping and chimeric read pairs that de novo fusion detectors typically discard.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq data, whole-genome sequencing, or whole-exome sequencing — Anchored-fusion only supports paired-end RNA-seq The fusion of interest does not include the user-provided target (anchored) gene — such fusions will not be detected An untargeted, de novo fusion discovery across all possible fusion partners is required — the anchored search is limited to the user-specified gene

skills.description: Use when building an evaluation read set with definitive splicing ground truth from paired-end 10X scRNA-seq data (e.g., mouse/human scRNA-seq) to benchmark splicing-status predictors via AUC.
skills.name: paired-end-splicing-label-derivation
skills.search_text: paired-end-splicing-label-derivation Use when building an evaluation read set with definitive splicing ground truth from paired-end 10X scRNA-seq data (e.g., mouse/human scRNA-seq) to benchmark splicing-status predictors via AUC. Single-end libraries: the labeling rules depend on read 1's exon-containment pattern to label the read-2 mate, so a paired-end alignment is required. The goal is prediction rather than ground-truth construction: for probabilistic splicing-status prediction run the Forseti model (forseti_predictor) instead of deriving labels. Reads that do not map uniquely to the genome (multiple NH values) — the labeling pipeline explicitly filters them out, so they cannot receive definitive labels. Derives definitive ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels for scRNA-seq reads by exploiting paired-end alignment structure: the exon-containment pattern of read 1 determines the splicing status assigned to its read-2 mate. This creates an evaluation read set whose labels are treated as ground truth for computing ROC/AUC against Forseti's probabilistic predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Derives definitive ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels for scRNA-seq reads by exploiting paired-end alignment structure: the exon-containment pattern of read 1 determines the splicing status assigned to its read-2 mate. This creates an evaluation read set whose labels are treated as ground truth for computing ROC/AUC against Forseti's probabilistic predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-end libraries: the labeling rules depend on read 1's exon-containment pattern to label the read-2 mate, so a paired-end alignment is required. The goal is prediction rather than ground-truth construction: for probabilistic splicing-status prediction run the Forseti model (forseti_predictor) instead of deriving labels. Reads that do not map uniquely to the genome (multiple NH values) — the labeling pipeline explicitly filters them out, so they cannot receive definitive labels.

skills.description: Use when comparing a new causal-inference or prediction model against baseline configurations on the same candidate peak-gene pairs, and you need per-configuration retrieval AUROCs plus significance statistics for the differences.
skills.name: paired-model-comparison-significance-testing
skills.search_text: paired-model-comparison-significance-testing Use when comparing a new causal-inference or prediction model against baseline configurations on the same candidate peak-gene pairs, and you need per-configuration retrieval AUROCs plus significance statistics for the differences. The candidate sets differ between the proposed model and the baselines, making AUROC comparisons on eQTL retrieval non-comparable There is no external ground-truth validation resource (such as eQTL Catalogue significant associations) to define retrieval positives The goal is method development rather than ablation: comparing configurations of the same model on training performance rather than causal-link retrieval accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Rigorous ablation methodology for comparing a graph-neural-network Granger method (GrID-Net) against matched baseline configurations (linear Granger on the full SHARE-seq DAG and on individual cortex, medulla, and IRS branches) by scoring each on eQTL-retrieval AUROC and computing significance statistics for the AUROC differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Rigorous ablation methodology for comparing a graph-neural-network Granger method (GrID-Net) against matched baseline configurations (linear Granger on the full SHARE-seq DAG and on individual cortex, medulla, and IRS branches) by scoring each on eQTL-retrieval AUROC and computing significance statistics for the AUROC differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate sets differ between the proposed model and the baselines, making AUROC comparisons on eQTL retrieval non-comparable There is no external ground-truth validation resource (such as eQTL Catalogue significant associations) to define retrieval positives The goal is method development rather than ablation: comparing configurations of the same model on training performance rather than causal-link retrieval accuracy

skills.description: Use when you have raw paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices (AnnData objects) that must be normalized and feature-processed before training or evaluating a scButterfly cross-modality translation model.
skills.name: paired-multiomics-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: paired-multiomics-data-preprocessing Use when you have raw paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices (AnnData objects) that must be normalized and feature-processed before training or evaluating a scButterfly cross-modality translation model. Input is already normalized or feature-processed — scButterfly expects the raw count matrix as load_data input The task is training the model or running augmentation (scButterfly-T/scButterfly-C), not the preceding preprocessing stage Data is unpaired single-modality data intended for diagonal training scenarios, where different setup is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Load and preprocess paired single-modality scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices for scButterfly cross-modality translation, using the package's RNA_data_preprocessing and ATAC_data_preprocessing routines on raw AnnData count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Load and preprocess paired single-modality scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices for scButterfly cross-modality translation, using the package's RNA_data_preprocessing and ATAC_data_preprocessing routines on raw AnnData count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or feature-processed — scButterfly expects the raw count matrix as load_data input The task is training the model or running augmentation (scButterfly-T/scButterfly-C), not the preceding preprocessing stage Data is unpaired single-modality data intended for diagonal training scenarios, where different setup is needed

skills.description: Use when you need qualitative visual confirmation that translated single-cell profiles (predicted scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq from a cross-modality translator) cluster by cell type and match true labeled profiles.
skills.name: paired-multiomics-tnse-visualization
skills.search_text: paired-multiomics-tnse-visualization Use when you need qualitative visual confirmation that translated single-cell profiles (predicted scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq from a cross-modality translator) cluster by cell type and match true labeled profiles. Input is raw un-translated single-modality data where no cross-modality translation quality needs assessment Quantitative clustering indices (e.g., ARI/NMI from calculate_cluster_index) already suffice and no qualitative figure is required Very small cell sets (e.g., a down-sampled fold with only tens of cells) where t-SNE embeddings are unstable and misleading http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Renders t-SNE plots of scButterfly-translated single-cell profiles (e.g., predicted scATAC from scRNA or vice versa) colored by cell-type labels, providing qualitative validation that translated cross-modality data preserves cellular heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Renders t-SNE plots of scButterfly-translated single-cell profiles (e.g., predicted scATAC from scRNA or vice versa) colored by cell-type labels, providing qualitative validation that translated cross-modality data preserves cellular heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw un-translated single-modality data where no cross-modality translation quality needs assessment Quantitative clustering indices (e.g., ARI/NMI from calculate_cluster_index) already suffice and no qualitative figure is required Very small cell sets (e.g., a down-sampled fold with only tens of cells) where t-SNE embeddings are unstable and misleading

skills.description: Use when two configurations of the same method (e.g. weighted vs unweighted decoupleR runs) yield paired scores over identical dataset/regulator combinations and a directional significance claim must be tested nonparametrically.
skills.name: paired-nonparametric-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: paired-nonparametric-hypothesis-testing Use when two configurations of the same method (e.g. weighted vs unweighted decoupleR runs) yield paired scores over identical dataset/regulator combinations and a directional significance claim must be tested nonparametrically. Samples are unpaired or come from independent runs — the signed-rank test requires matched pairs of the same evaluation units (dataset/regulator combinations). You are comparing entirely different methods against each other rather than the same method with vs without weights — that is a different benchmark question in decoupleRBench. Paired differences are plausibly normal — a paired t-test would be the more appropriate parametric choice. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies a one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (R stats::wilcox.test) to per-method paired performance deltas, e.g. decoupleR perturbed-regulator recovery scores computed with interaction weights versus without, to establish that weight-leveraging methods perform significantly better (P < 2.2e-16, Supplementary Fig. S4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Applies a one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (R stats::wilcox.test) to per-method paired performance deltas, e.g. decoupleR perturbed-regulator recovery scores computed with interaction weights versus without, to establish that weight-leveraging methods perform significantly better (P < 2.2e-16, Supplementary Fig. S4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are unpaired or come from independent runs — the signed-rank test requires matched pairs of the same evaluation units (dataset/regulator combinations). You are comparing entirely different methods against each other rather than the same method with vs without weights — that is a different benchmark question in decoupleRBench. Paired differences are plausibly normal — a paired t-test would be the more appropriate parametric choice.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq count data provide per-allele exon inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC) with incLen/skpLen effective lengths for individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP, and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR <= 10%.
skills.name: paired-replicate-differential-splicing-testing
skills.search_text: paired-replicate-differential-splicing-testing Use when RNA-seq count data provide per-allele exon inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC) with incLen/skpLen effective lengths for individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP, and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR <= 10%. No heterozygous SNP exists outside the alternative exon but close enough to the AS event to be detected on the same RNA-seq read — PAIRADISE cannot assign reads allele-specifically SNPs are located within or too distant from alternative exons in short-read RNA-seq data — they cannot be analyzed The task is standard group-level differential splicing (e.g., case-control across conditions) rather than allele-specific comparison within the identical cellular environment of individuals http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply the PAIRADISE paired statistical model to inclusion/skipping junction counts (IJC/SJC) from reference and alternative alleles to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS), aggregating signals across paired replicates or individuals instead of testing one sample at a time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Apply the PAIRADISE paired statistical model to inclusion/skipping junction counts (IJC/SJC) from reference and alternative alleles to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS), aggregating signals across paired replicates or individuals instead of testing one sample at a time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No heterozygous SNP exists outside the alternative exon but close enough to the AS event to be detected on the same RNA-seq read — PAIRADISE cannot assign reads allele-specifically SNPs are located within or too distant from alternative exons in short-read RNA-seq data — they cannot be analyzed The task is standard group-level differential splicing (e.g., case-control across conditions) rather than allele-specific comparison within the identical cellular environment of individuals

skills.description: Use when per-event allele-specific inclusion/skipping counts (IJC/SJC for REF and ALT alleles) are available for multiple individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP and you need a combined ASAS p-value via a paired-replicate LRT on δi = 0.
skills.name: paired-replicate-likelihood-ratio-testing
skills.search_text: paired-replicate-likelihood-ratio-testing Use when per-event allele-specific inclusion/skipping counts (IJC/SJC for REF and ALT alleles) are available for multiple individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP and you need a combined ASAS p-value via a paired-replicate LRT on δi = 0. The heterozygous SNP is inside the alternative exon or too distant to co-occur on the same short RNA-seq read — the event cannot be allele-assigned for this test You need to test the causal SNP itself within the exon or nearby intronic splicing regions — PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs outside the alternative exon Input is genotype–phenotype sQTL association data rather than paired REF/ALT allele counts per individual — the within-individual paired allelic model does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 The PAIRADISE hierarchical paired-replicate model: binomial read-count likelihoods plus logit-normal isoform ratios where both alleles of an individual share the subject effect alpha_ik; after integrating it out, the two alleles' logit exon inclusion levels follow a bivariate normal with mean [μi, μi+δi], and significance comes from a likelihood-ratio test of δi = 0 (chi-squared, 1 df). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: The PAIRADISE hierarchical paired-replicate model: binomial read-count likelihoods plus logit-normal isoform ratios where both alleles of an individual share the subject effect alpha_ik; after integrating it out, the two alleles' logit exon inclusion levels follow a bivariate normal with mean [μi, μi+δi], and significance comes from a likelihood-ratio test of δi = 0 (chi-squared, 1 df).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The heterozygous SNP is inside the alternative exon or too distant to co-occur on the same short RNA-seq read — the event cannot be allele-assigned for this test You need to test the causal SNP itself within the exon or nearby intronic splicing regions — PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs outside the alternative exon Input is genotype–phenotype sQTL association data rather than paired REF/ALT allele counts per individual — the within-individual paired allelic model does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have per-allele exon inclusion (IJC) and skipping (SJC) counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) from replicate RNA-seq samples sharing a heterozygous SNP, and need to test for differential splicing between alleles across replicates.
skills.name: paired-replicate-statistical-model-fitting
skills.search_text: paired-replicate-statistical-model-fitting Use when you have per-allele exon inclusion (IJC) and skipping (SJC) counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) from replicate RNA-seq samples sharing a heterozygous SNP, and need to test for differential splicing between alleles across replicates. SNPs are located within the alternative exon or too distant from it to be co-detected on the same short RNA-seq read — PAIRADISE requires a heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon but close enough for allele-specific read assignment Data are single-sample with no replicates or heterozygous-SNP-sharing individuals to aggregate — the paired-replicate model needs multiple paired observations for power Reads fail the uniqueness filter (not uniquely aligned to both haplotype-modified genomes at the same location) or multi-SNP reads with a majority-voting draw — these must be discarded before fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit the PAIRADISE paired statistical model (R with nloptr optimization, parallelized via doParallel/foreach) to per-allele exon inclusion/skipping counts to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) by aggregating signals across replicates/individuals, calling significant events at FDR <= 10% (Benjamini-Hochberg). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Fit the PAIRADISE paired statistical model (R with nloptr optimization, parallelized via doParallel/foreach) to per-allele exon inclusion/skipping counts to detect allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) by aggregating signals across replicates/individuals, calling significant events at FDR <= 10% (Benjamini-Hochberg).
skills.when_to_use_negative: SNPs are located within the alternative exon or too distant from it to be co-detected on the same short RNA-seq read — PAIRADISE requires a heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon but close enough for allele-specific read assignment Data are single-sample with no replicates or heterozygous-SNP-sharing individuals to aggregate — the paired-replicate model needs multiple paired observations for power Reads fail the uniqueness filter (not uniquely aligned to both haplotype-modified genomes at the same location) or multi-SNP reads with a majority-voting draw — these must be discarded before fitting

skills.description: Use when PDAC expression datasets contain patient-matched primary tumors, metastases, and/or derived cell lines (e.g., PACA-AU paired samples) and you need to compare signature scores across matched sample classes rather than across unrelated samples.
skills.name: paired-sample-matching-across-datasets
skills.search_text: paired-sample-matching-across-datasets Use when PDAC expression datasets contain patient-matched primary tumors, metastases, and/or derived cell lines (e.g., PACA-AU paired samples) and you need to compare signature scores across matched sample classes rather than across unrelated samples. When datasets have no patient-level pairing information in sampInfo — pdacR notes the 'inability to robustly merge datasets', so cross-platform matching without sample metadata is not defensible When the goal is cohort-level subtype classification (e.g., PurIST) rather than within-patient comparison of signature retention/loss When samples include low-purity or non-adenocarcinoma cases (e.g., the 32 non-PDAC TCGA-PAAD samples) that have not been filtered out, since these confound signature scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify matched samples (primary tumor, metastatic tumor, and derived cell line from the same patient) within and between the ICGC PACA-AU RNAseq and microarray expression sets using pdacR's parsed sampInfo metadata, enabling longitudinal/paired comparisons of gene-signature retention or loss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Identify matched samples (primary tumor, metastatic tumor, and derived cell line from the same patient) within and between the ICGC PACA-AU RNAseq and microarray expression sets using pdacR's parsed sampInfo metadata, enabling longitudinal/paired comparisons of gene-signature retention or loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When datasets have no patient-level pairing information in sampInfo — pdacR notes the 'inability to robustly merge datasets', so cross-platform matching without sample metadata is not defensible When the goal is cohort-level subtype classification (e.g., PurIST) rather than within-patient comparison of signature retention/loss When samples include low-purity or non-adenocarcinoma cases (e.g., the 32 non-PDAC TCGA-PAAD samples) that have not been filtered out, since these confound signature scoring

skills.description: Use when comparing a spatial subpopulation identification method against baselines (Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC, scCoGAPS) on simulated data with known ground-truth subcluster labels, using ARI as the metric.
skills.name: paired-scrnaseq-spatial-transcriptomics-benchmarking
skills.search_text: paired-scrnaseq-spatial-transcriptomics-benchmarking Use when comparing a spatial subpopulation identification method against baselines (Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC, scCoGAPS) on simulated data with known ground-truth subcluster labels, using ARI as the metric. The analysis target is real biological ST data without ground-truth cluster labels — ARI against truth cannot be computed and this benchmark design does not apply. The task is spatial-domain identification of ST data itself rather than spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data; the article notes scSpace 'focuses on the spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data whereas other methods target the spatial domain identification of ST data'. Spatially heterogeneous subcluster count exceeds 10 or the simulation design differs fundamentally (e.g., no spatial heterogeneity), making the 2-10 subcluster benchmark series inapplicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking skill for evaluating scSpace against clustering and spatial-domain methods on simulated paired scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets, scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against ground-truth spatially heterogeneous subclusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for evaluating scSpace against clustering and spatial-domain methods on simulated paired scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets, scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against ground-truth spatially heterogeneous subclusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is real biological ST data without ground-truth cluster labels — ARI against truth cannot be computed and this benchmark design does not apply. The task is spatial-domain identification of ST data itself rather than spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data; the article notes scSpace 'focuses on the spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data whereas other methods target the spatial domain identification of ST data'. Spatially heterogeneous subcluster count exceeds 10 or the simulation design differs fundamentally (e.g., no spatial heterogeneity), making the 2-10 subcluster benchmark series inapplicable.

skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell transcriptome and full-length TCR sequencing data (e.g. Smart-seq2 CD8 TILs) and need per-cell clonotype assignments to test clonal relatedness between transcriptional states.
skills.name: paired-scrnaseq-tcrseq-data-processing
skills.search_text: paired-scrnaseq-tcrseq-data-processing Use when you have paired single-cell transcriptome and full-length TCR sequencing data (e.g. Smart-seq2 CD8 TILs) and need per-cell clonotype assignments to test clonal relatedness between transcriptional states. Your data is droplet-based (10X 5'/3') without full-length TCR capture — TraCeR is designed for full-length TCR reconstruction from single-cell RNA-seq, and the paper contrasts plate-based smart-seq2 with droplet technologies You only need transcriptomic state annotation without clonal information — TILPRED/ProjecTILs alone suffices and TraCeR reconstruction is unnecessary You need cross-sample/cross-patient clonotype sharing — this skill groups clonotypes separately per mouse/within-host, which prevents cross-sample clonotype comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Reconstruct paired TCR alpha/beta sequences from full-length TCR single-cell RNA-seq reads with TraCeR, group cells sharing identical receptor sequences into per-mouse clonotypes, and link each clonotype to its transcriptomically assigned CD8 TIL state (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naive) via TILPRED. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Reconstruct paired TCR alpha/beta sequences from full-length TCR single-cell RNA-seq reads with TraCeR, group cells sharing identical receptor sequences into per-mouse clonotypes, and link each clonotype to its transcriptomically assigned CD8 TIL state (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naive) via TILPRED.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data is droplet-based (10X 5'/3') without full-length TCR capture — TraCeR is designed for full-length TCR reconstruction from single-cell RNA-seq, and the paper contrasts plate-based smart-seq2 with droplet technologies You only need transcriptomic state annotation without clonal information — TILPRED/ProjecTILs alone suffices and TraCeR reconstruction is unnecessary You need cross-sample/cross-patient clonotype sharing — this skill groups clonotypes separately per mouse/within-host, which prevents cross-sample clonotype comparison

skills.description: Use when the same tumor samples have signature-fitting estimates from two matched contexts (e.g., WES capture-restricted vs WGS SNV catalogs) and you must quantify per-sample systematic differences, such as exome-vs-WGS shifts for SBS9.
skills.name: paired-signature-estimate-statistical-comparison
skills.search_text: paired-signature-estimate-statistical-comparison Use when the same tumor samples have signature-fitting estimates from two matched contexts (e.g., WES capture-restricted vs WGS SNV catalogs) and you must quantify per-sample systematic differences, such as exome-vs-WGS shifts for SBS9. Mutation catalogs come from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases, where mutational burdens are too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting. Estimates are unpaired (no matched WES/WGS catalog for the same tumor), so a paired T-test on per-sample differences would be invalid. skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression data whose high dropout and noise make naive two-cell similarity unreliable, and a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix is needed as input to spectral clustering.
skills.name: pairwise-similarity-computation-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: pairwise-similarity-computation-scrna-seq Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression data whose high dropout and noise make naive two-cell similarity unreliable, and a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix is needed as input to spectral clustering. The analysis goal is direct clustering on raw expression features without similarity learning — spectral clustering on the learned similarity is the SSRE pathway Very large-scale datasets where the time cost is prohibitive; the authors note SSRE is 'relatively time-consuming in large-scale datasets' and parallel acceleration was not implemented Only a simple two-cell expression comparison is needed — SSRE's value comes from incorporating similar neighbors, not pairwise-only computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes cell-to-cell similarity for scRNA-seq clustering by combining a sparse-subspace self-expression matrix (learned via ADMM) with three classical pairwise similarities (Pearson correlation, Jaccard, and cosine), then enhancing the sparse similarity using KNN-based modified Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation. SSRE uses this enhanced similarity with spectral clustering to reveal cell-type block structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Computes cell-to-cell similarity for scRNA-seq clustering by combining a sparse-subspace self-expression matrix (learned via ADMM) with three classical pairwise similarities (Pearson correlation, Jaccard, and cosine), then enhancing the sparse similarity using KNN-based modified Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation. SSRE uses this enhanced similarity with spectral clustering to reveal cell-type block structure.

skills.search_text: palantir-cell-fate-probability-comparison Use when DICE has already assigned primed vs unprimed cells toward competing lineages and you must validate those assignments against Palantir fate probabilities (and, for SHARE-Seq data, matched scATAC-Seq chromVAR TF activity). When the goal is to separate tumor from stromal signals at single-cell resolution — the pdacR datasets are bulk analyses and cannot fully separate cellular populations When samples lack tissue-of-origin annotation (e.g. unfiltered TCGA-PAAD with non-PDAC cases), since the Wilcoxon comparison depends on correct sample tracks When merging scores across the microarray and RNAseq datasets, since cross-platform aggregation and batch correction are not supported http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Scores curated PDAC gene signatures (ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) per sample across the Moffitt 2015 microarray and RNAseq datasets and uses Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to attribute signature expression to tissue/cell types, revealing whether expression is tumor-cell-intrinsic or derived from normal pancreas compartments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Scores curated PDAC gene signatures (ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) per sample across the Moffitt 2015 microarray and RNAseq datasets and uses Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to attribute signature expression to tissue/cell types, revealing whether expression is tumor-cell-intrinsic or derived from normal pancreas compartments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to separate tumor from stromal signals at single-cell resolution — the pdacR datasets are bulk analyses and cannot fully separate cellular populations When samples lack tissue-of-origin annotation (e.g. unfiltered TCGA-PAAD with non-PDAC cases), since the Wilcoxon comparison depends on correct sample tracks When merging scores across the microarray and RNAseq datasets, since cross-platform aggregation and batch correction are not supported

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq of pancreatic endocrine development (e.g., E15.5 Bastidas-Ponce pancreas data) must have rare hormone-producing fates like delta cells and Beta-1/Beta-2 subtypes detected without manual cell-fate assignment.
skills.name: pancreatic-endocrine-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: pancreatic-endocrine-cell-type-annotation Use when scRNA-seq of pancreatic endocrine development (e.g., E15.5 Bastidas-Ponce pancreas data) must have rare hormone-producing fates like delta cells and Beta-1/Beta-2 subtypes detected without manual cell-fate assignment. The input lacks a gene-by-cell expression matrix with an AnnData PCA representation (adata.obsm['X_pca']), e.g., it is already a cluster-level feature table. The trajectory is disconnected and requires multiple explicit roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected with preserve_disconnected=True instead of the standard wrapper. Terminal states are already known and manually specified, making VIA's auto-detection (pseudotime_threshold_TS=30, too_big_factor=0.4) unnecessary. Automated detection and marker-based annotation of pancreatic endocrine lineages (Alpha, Beta-1, Beta-2, Delta, Epsilon) in E15.5 murine pancreas scRNA-seq by running VIA's lazy-teleporting random-walk trajectory inference with auto-detected terminal states, then assigning fates via marker genes (Sst, Hhex, Cd24a, Ins1, Ins2, Gcg). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Automated detection and marker-based annotation of pancreatic endocrine lineages (Alpha, Beta-1, Beta-2, Delta, Epsilon) in E15.5 murine pancreas scRNA-seq by running VIA's lazy-teleporting random-walk trajectory inference with auto-detected terminal states, then assigning fates via marker genes (Sst, Hhex, Cd24a, Ins1, Ins2, Gcg).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks a gene-by-cell expression matrix with an AnnData PCA representation (adata.obsm['X_pca']), e.g., it is already a cluster-level feature table. The trajectory is disconnected and requires multiple explicit roots — use via_wrapper_disconnected with preserve_disconnected=True instead of the standard wrapper. Terminal states are already known and manually specified, making VIA's auto-detection (pseudotime_threshold_TS=30, too_big_factor=0.4) unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when deconvolving bulk pancreatic islet RNA-seq (e.g., Fadista/GSE50244 read counts) into alpha, beta, delta, gamma, acinar and ductal proportions with a healthy-human-islet scRNA-seq reference (E-MTAB-5060) and testing proportion–phenotype associations such as beta cell proportion vs HbA1c.
skills.name: pancreatic-islet-cell-type-biology
skills.search_text: pancreatic-islet-cell-type-biology Use when deconvolving bulk pancreatic islet RNA-seq (e.g., Fadista/GSE50244 read counts) into alpha, beta, delta, gamma, acinar and ductal proportions with a healthy-human-islet scRNA-seq reference (E-MTAB-5060) and testing proportion–phenotype associations such as beta cell proportion vs HbA1c. When the bulk or single-cell input contains TPM-normalized values — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use raw read counts. When bulk samples come from conditions very different from the scRNA-seq reference (e.g., multi-condition bulk data) — MuSiC2 is the intended iterative alternative for such cases. When the goal is absolute cell type proportions rather than trends across subjects — under the method's assumptions only trends of cell type proportion change across subjects can be recovered. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the MuSiC deconvolution analysis in which bulk pancreatic islet RNA-seq from 89 Fadista et al. donors (GSE50244) is deconvolved using the Segerstolpe et al. scRNA-seq reference (E-MTAB-5060) and the estimated beta cell proportion is regressed on HbA1c, recovering the reported p-value of 0.00126. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Reproduces the MuSiC deconvolution analysis in which bulk pancreatic islet RNA-seq from 89 Fadista et al. donors (GSE50244) is deconvolved using the Segerstolpe et al. scRNA-seq reference (E-MTAB-5060) and the estimated beta cell proportion is regressed on HbA1c, recovering the reported p-value of 0.00126.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the bulk or single-cell input contains TPM-normalized values — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use raw read counts. When bulk samples come from conditions very different from the scRNA-seq reference (e.g., multi-condition bulk data) — MuSiC2 is the intended iterative alternative for such cases. When the goal is absolute cell type proportions rather than trends across subjects — under the method's assumptions only trends of cell type proportion change across subjects can be recovered.

skills.description: Use when simulating transcription factor overexpression in single-cell time-series scRNA-seq of pancreatic/β-cell differentiation, and you need day-resolved or starting-population-resolved fate-bias shifts toward β-, α-, or EC-cell outcomes.
skills.name: pancreatic-lineage-fate-outcome-analysis
skills.search_text: pancreatic-lineage-fate-outcome-analysis Use when simulating transcription factor overexpression in single-cell time-series scRNA-seq of pancreatic/β-cell differentiation, and you need day-resolved or starting-population-resolved fate-bias shifts toward β-, α-, or EC-cell outcomes. Your data's final time point is not at steady-state — PRESCIENT requires the last time point to be at steady-state, so temporal perturbation simulations would be invalid You need gene-level resolution of perturbation effects rather than fate-outcome shifts, since PRESCIENT transforms data into PCA space where information about individual genes is lost The perturbation targets are non-TFs such as signaling pathway effectors — the published screen was limited to TFs, so positive controls and expected-effect priors exist only for TFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Uses PRESCIENT in silico TF perturbation simulations on the Veres et al. 2019 in vitro β-cell differentiation time series to quantify how perturbation timing (day 0–6) and starting subpopulation (SOX2+, NKX6.1+, neurog3-early/mid/late) shift β-, α-, and EC-cell fate outcomes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Uses PRESCIENT in silico TF perturbation simulations on the Veres et al. 2019 in vitro β-cell differentiation time series to quantify how perturbation timing (day 0–6) and starting subpopulation (SOX2+, NKX6.1+, neurog3-early/mid/late) shift β-, α-, and EC-cell fate outcomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data's final time point is not at steady-state — PRESCIENT requires the last time point to be at steady-state, so temporal perturbation simulations would be invalid You need gene-level resolution of perturbation effects rather than fate-outcome shifts, since PRESCIENT transforms data into PCA space where information about individual genes is lost The perturbation targets are non-TFs such as signaling pathway effectors — the published screen was limited to TFs, so positive controls and expected-effect priors exist only for TFs

skills.description: Use when a fitted scKINETICS model (gene regulatory network matrix A plus per-cell transcriptional velocities) is available and TF-level regulator activity across a pancreatic lineage transition such as acinar-to-ductal metaplasia must be inferred.
skills.name: pancreatic-lineage-trajectory-interpretation
skills.search_text: pancreatic-lineage-trajectory-interpretation Use when a fitted scKINETICS model (gene regulatory network matrix A plus per-cell transcriptional velocities) is available and TF-level regulator activity across a pancreatic lineage transition such as acinar-to-ductal metaplasia must be inferred. Input is raw single-cell expression data without a fitted scKINETICS model — the knockout screen requires the GRN matrix A and per-cell velocities from a prior EM fit The analysis goal is TF activity from co-expression or motif enrichment alone (no velocity/dynamical model), where velocity-perturbation scoring is not applicable The dataset contains no pancreatic lineage transition (e.g., ADM) or phenotypic manifold along which to interpret cluster-specific activity patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify transcription-factor regulatory activity along a pancreatic acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) trajectory by simulating in silico TF knockouts in a fitted scKINETICS dynamical model and scoring per-cell velocity perturbations, recovering regulators (e.g., Ptf1a) whose influence is not apparent from expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Quantify transcription-factor regulatory activity along a pancreatic acinar-to-ductal metaplasia (ADM) trajectory by simulating in silico TF knockouts in a fitted scKINETICS dynamical model and scoring per-cell velocity perturbations, recovering regulators (e.g., Ptf1a) whose influence is not apparent from expression alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-cell expression data without a fitted scKINETICS model — the knockout screen requires the GRN matrix A and per-cell velocities from a prior EM fit The analysis goal is TF activity from co-expression or motif enrichment alone (no velocity/dynamical model), where velocity-perturbation scoring is not applicable The dataset contains no pancreatic lineage transition (e.g., ADM) or phenotypic manifold along which to interpret cluster-specific activity patterns

skills.search_text: parallel-outer-loop-benchmarking Use when timing nested CV fits of nestedcv (e.g. nestcv.train with random forest, nestcv.glmnet) on high-dimensional transcriptomic data and comparing serial (cv.cores=1) vs parallel (cv.cores=8) wall-clock times. When the goal is faster fitting rather than benchmarking — simply set cv.cores to the physical core count and run once When the model call does not support outer-loop parallelisation (cv.cores is available for nestcv.glmnet, nestcv.train, nestcv.SuperLearner and outercv, not all nestedcv functions) When the critical cost is inside inner CV folds or the model fit itself rather than the outer loop — parallelising outer folds alone will yield little gain http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks wall-clock speedup from parallelising the outer CV loop of nestedcv model fits (nestcv.train, nestcv.glmnet) via the cv.cores argument, which dispatches outer folds with mclapply from the parallel package. The paper reports up to 5.0x speedup for random forest nestcv.train and up to 2.5x for nestcv.glmnet on the R4RA dataset (10 x 10 default folds). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Benchmarks wall-clock speedup from parallelising the outer CV loop of nestedcv model fits (nestcv.train, nestcv.glmnet) via the cv.cores argument, which dispatches outer folds with mclapply from the parallel package. The paper reports up to 5.0x speedup for random forest nestcv.train and up to 2.5x for nestcv.glmnet on the R4RA dataset (10 x 10 default folds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is faster fitting rather than benchmarking — simply set cv.cores to the physical core count and run once When the model call does not support outer-loop parallelisation (cv.cores is available for nestcv.glmnet, nestcv.train, nestcv.SuperLearner and outercv, not all nestedcv functions) When the critical cost is inside inner CV folds or the model fit itself rather than the outer loop — parallelising outer folds alone will yield little gain

skills.description: Use when nested CV fitting (e.g. 10 x 10-fold nestcv.train or nestcv.glmnet) is too slow serially and you need to quantify how much wall-clock time cv.cores parallelisation saves on multi-core hardware.

skills.search_text: parallel-scaling-plateau-analysis Use when nested CV fitting (e.g. 10 x 10-fold nestcv.train or nestcv.glmnet) is too slow serially and you need to quantify how much wall-clock time cv.cores parallelisation saves on multi-core hardware. Single-core machines or CI runners: mclapply-based outer-loop parallelisation cannot yield speedup and timings would be misleading When the analysis goal is model accuracy or hyperparameter tuning rather than wall-clock performance benchmarking — cv.cores does not change fitted results Windows-only environments where you cannot use mclapply semantics; nestedcv falls back to parLapply and timing behaviour differs http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Benchmark the wall-clock speedup gained by parallelising the outer CV loop of nestedcv model fitting (nestcv.train, nestcv.glmnet) with the cv.cores argument, verifying that speedup plateaus near the number of physical cores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock speedup gained by parallelising the outer CV loop of nestedcv model fitting (nestcv.train, nestcv.glmnet) with the cv.cores argument, verifying that speedup plateaus near the number of physical cores.

skills.description: Use when a cell-by-gene expression matrix must be converted to a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix for >10^3 pathways across ≥10^5 cells and standard UCell/AddModuleScore would be too slow.
skills.name: parallel-scoring-of-pathway-gene-sets
skills.search_text: parallel-scoring-of-pathway-gene-sets Use when a cell-by-gene expression matrix must be converted to a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix for >10^3 pathways across ≥10^5 cells and standard UCell/AddModuleScore would be too slow. The input is already a PAS/feature matrix or pseudobulk-aggregated table rather than a cell-level expression matrix — scoring would be redundant. The study has fewer than 15 samples and the downstream goal is MOFA-based multicellular pathway module identification (scPAFA's downstream step requires ≥15 samples). Only a small number of pathways (<10^3) and a small dataset are involved, where existing tools like UCell or AddModuleScore suffice without the parallel implementation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Compute cell-level pathway activity scores (PAS) for large gene-set collections on large-scale scRNA-seq data using scPAFA's fast_ucell, a vectorized, multi-core Python reimplementation of the R UCell method based on within-cell expression rankings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Compute cell-level pathway activity scores (PAS) for large gene-set collections on large-scale scRNA-seq data using scPAFA's fast_ucell, a vectorized, multi-core Python reimplementation of the R UCell method based on within-cell expression rankings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a PAS/feature matrix or pseudobulk-aggregated table rather than a cell-level expression matrix — scoring would be redundant. The study has fewer than 15 samples and the downstream goal is MOFA-based multicellular pathway module identification (scPAFA's downstream step requires ≥15 samples). Only a small number of pathways (<10^3) and a small dataset are involved, where existing tools like UCell or AddModuleScore suffice without the parallel implementation.

skills.description: Use when validating that a knowledge-masked Transformer annotator (e.g., TOSICA on mPancreas, Supplementary Fig. 8) actually gains accuracy from curated .gmt masks rather than model capacity alone.
skills.name: parameter-matched-mask-ablation-study
skills.search_text: parameter-matched-mask-ablation-study Use when validating that a knowledge-masked Transformer annotator (e.g., TOSICA on mPancreas, Supplementary Fig. 8) actually gains accuracy from curated .gmt masks rather than model capacity alone. The goal is to run TOSICA for prediction/annotation of a new query with an already-trained model, not to interrogate whether the mask itself is responsible for accuracy The model's masks are not a controllable design parameter (e.g., unmasked, fully attention-based architectures) so no knowledge-vs-random comparison is possible The reference has no per-epoch validation split (30% of training) available, so convergence behavior cannot be measured http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 An ablation protocol testing whether a masked-attention annotator's accuracy truly depends on expert-knowledge masks, by training TOSICA on the same reference with knowledge-based gene-set masks and with parameter-matched random masks (1% and 5% reserved gene-to-token connections) and comparing epochs-to-convergence and converged validation accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: An ablation protocol testing whether a masked-attention annotator's accuracy truly depends on expert-knowledge masks, by training TOSICA on the same reference with knowledge-based gene-set masks and with parameter-matched random masks (1% and 5% reserved gene-to-token connections) and comparing epochs-to-convergence and converged validation accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to run TOSICA for prediction/annotation of a new query with an already-trained model, not to interrogate whether the mask itself is responsible for accuracy The model's masks are not a controllable design parameter (e.g., unmasked, fully attention-based architectures) so no knowledge-vs-random comparison is possible The reference has no per-epoch validation split (30% of training) available, so convergence behavior cannot be measured

skills.description: Use when scoring gene signatures on low-depth or downsampled single-cell data with UCell and you need to justify or reproduce a non-default maxRank setting, or to verify how missing signature genes affect scores under 'impute' vs 'skip'.

skills.search_text: parameter-sensitivity-comparison Use when scoring gene signatures on low-depth or downsampled single-cell data with UCell and you need to justify or reproduce a non-default maxRank setting, or to verify how missing signature genes affect scores under 'impute' vs 'skip'. Data are high-depth so the default maxRank=1500 cap is adequate and no parameter adjustment needs justification The task is generic gene signature scoring rather than reproducing or validating parameter choices of the UCell Seurat vignette Input is a raw expression matrix without a Seurat object and the goal is not to compare AddModuleScore_UCell runs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A reproducibility exercise that quantifies how UCell signature scores on the low-depth downsampled Zilionis lung immune dataset change when the maxRank cap (default 1500 vs adjusted 800-1000) or the missing_genes policy ('impute' vs 'skip') is varied, producing a per-cell comparison table of differing score columns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: A reproducibility exercise that quantifies how UCell signature scores on the low-depth downsampled Zilionis lung immune dataset change when the maxRank cap (default 1500 vs adjusted 800-1000) or the missing_genes policy ('impute' vs 'skip') is varied, producing a per-cell comparison table of differing score columns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are high-depth so the default maxRank=1500 cap is adequate and no parameter adjustment needs justification The task is generic gene signature scoring rather than reproducing or validating parameter choices of the UCell Seurat vignette Input is a raw expression matrix without a Seurat object and the goal is not to compare AddModuleScore_UCell runs

skills.description: Use when validating a clustering or similarity-learning pipeline whose defaults (e.g. penalty ratio rho/lambda) need empirical justification, by sweeping parameters on benchmark datasets and plotting performance stability curves.
skills.name: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis Use when validating a clustering or similarity-learning pipeline whose defaults (e.g. penalty ratio rho/lambda) need empirical justification, by sweeping parameters on benchmark datasets and plotting performance stability curves. The method has already been validated for parameter sensitivity and the default is known — re-running the sweep adds no information The task is benchmarking against competing methods rather than tuning/justifying the method's own penalty parameters Datasets lack ground-truth cell type labels, so NMI and ARI cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematically varies a method's key penalty parameters over a grid (e.g. SSRE's rho/lambda ratio over {2, 4, ..., 30}) on real scRNA-seq benchmarks, evaluates clustering quality (NMI, ARI) at each point, and identifies the stable interval supporting a default setting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Systematically varies a method's key penalty parameters over a grid (e.g. SSRE's rho/lambda ratio over {2, 4, ..., 30}) on real scRNA-seq benchmarks, evaluates clustering quality (NMI, ARI) at each point, and identifies the stable interval supporting a default setting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method has already been validated for parameter sensitivity and the default is known — re-running the sweep adds no information The task is benchmarking against competing methods rather than tuning/justifying the method's own penalty parameters Datasets lack ground-truth cell type labels, so NMI and ARI cannot be computed

skills.search_text: parameter-sweep-benchmarking Use when evaluating how technical or biological simulation parameters (e.g., capture efficiency alpha, variability sigma) affect the relative performance of multiple methods that need simulated gold standards for scoring. The task is a single fixed-parameter run rather than a sweep over simulation settings such as Sigma or alpha Real experimental data with verified gold standards are available, making simulation-based ground truth unnecessary The methods under comparison require UMI-based input; this workflow uses True2ObservedCounts with protocol='nonUMI' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark computational methods across a controlled parameter grid (e.g., SymSim's Sigma within-population variability and alpha capture efficiency) by simulating gold-standard datasets, running competing methods on each grid point, and scoring against simulated ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Benchmark computational methods across a controlled parameter grid (e.g., SymSim's Sigma within-population variability and alpha capture efficiency) by simulating gold-standard datasets, running competing methods on each grid point, and scoring against simulated ground truth.

skills.summary: Orchestrates FrameD fault-injection parameter sweeps by parsing a JSON configuration (encoder, decoder, fault distribution, copy distribution, and optional sweep), expanding it into one simulation job per parameter combination, and collecting the per-combination statistics for cross-configuration comparison.

skills.description: Use when a denoised expression matrix (e.g., the SERM autoencoder output So) must be summarized as a single parametric probability distribution before histogram-equalization imputation, and you need to choose among Gaussian, Rayleigh, and exponential families objectively.
skills.name: parametric-probability-density-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: parametric-probability-density-curve-fitting Use when a denoised expression matrix (e.g., the SERM autoencoder output So) must be summarized as a single parametric probability distribution before histogram-equalization imputation, and you need to choose among Gaussian, Rayleigh, and exponential families objectively. The data have not been denoised/reconstructed first — fitting PDFs to raw sparse scRNA-seq counts with dropouts will model the dropout artifact rather than the underlying expression distribution Small genomic datasets where the 2000-element autoencoder subset may yield an estimated distribution that diverges from the actual data distribution The goal is imputation by a non-parametric or deep generative model (e.g., scVI, MAGIC) rather than a parametric histogram-equalization pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits candidate probability density functions (Gaussian, Rayleigh, exponential) to the normalized histogram of autoencoder-reconstructed gene expression values, then selects the best-fitting distribution by minimum root mean square error. This is the distribution-learning stage of SERM (Fig. 1 steps 2–3) that supplies the parametric PDF used downstream for histogram-equalization imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Fits candidate probability density functions (Gaussian, Rayleigh, exponential) to the normalized histogram of autoencoder-reconstructed gene expression values, then selects the best-fitting distribution by minimum root mean square error. This is the distribution-learning stage of SERM (Fig. 1 steps 2–3) that supplies the parametric PDF used downstream for histogram-equalization imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have not been denoised/reconstructed first — fitting PDFs to raw sparse scRNA-seq counts with dropouts will model the dropout artifact rather than the underlying expression distribution Small genomic datasets where the 2000-element autoencoder subset may yield an estimated distribution that diverges from the actual data distribution The goal is imputation by a non-parametric or deep generative model (e.g., scVI, MAGIC) rather than a parametric histogram-equalization pipeline
