skills.name: pars-tuberalis-subtype-identification
skills.search_text: pars-tuberalis-subtype-identification Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (~tens of thousands of cells, e.g. ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain profiles from the Single Cell Portal) must be scanned for rare minor cell subpopulations that standard clustering would miss. Input is already a small pre-selected rare-cell set where density-based rareness scoring adds no value The goal is doublet detection — doublet rates (1–30%) do not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application there A comprehensive clustering of all cell types is required in a single pass; typical clustering techniques are time consuming and this skill targets minor subpopulations only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify novel rare-cell sub-types, such as the Hesx1+/Cyp2f2+ pars tuberalis sub-type, by scoring every cell for rareness with FiRE (LSH-based density estimation), thresholding scores via the IQR rule, and clustering the rare cells with dropClust to reveal minor cell types in the ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain scRNA-seq dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Identify novel rare-cell sub-types, such as the Hesx1+/Cyp2f2+ pars tuberalis sub-type, by scoring every cell for rareness with FiRE (LSH-based density estimation), thresholding scores via the IQR rule, and clustering the rare cells with dropClust to reveal minor cell types in the ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a small pre-selected rare-cell set where density-based rareness scoring adds no value The goal is doublet detection — doublet rates (1–30%) do not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application there A comprehensive clustering of all cell types is required in a single pass; typical clustering techniques are time consuming and this skill targets minor subpopulations only

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how accurately a splice-aware tool detects junctions between annotated splice sites that are absent from the reference annotation: simulate reads from full transcriptomes, derive a partial ground truth by removing held-out event transcripts, and score recall/precision.
skills.name: partial-annotation-benchmark-construction
skills.search_text: partial-annotation-benchmark-construction Use when you must quantify how accurately a splice-aware tool detects junctions between annotated splice sites that are absent from the reference annotation: simulate reads from full transcriptomes, derive a partial ground truth by removing held-out event transcripts, and score recall/precision. The reference annotation already contains the junctions of interest, so there are no held-out novel events to score against — a partial-annotation design would measure nothing. You need full-assembly evaluation (e.g. novel splice-site discovery from unaligned reads), not recall/precision on junction-spanning reads between annotated splice sites. Read lengths other than the indexed ones are used: fortuna indexes are read-length-specific (built separately with -rl 75 and -rl 100), so off-target read lengths would require new indexes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking scheme for novel splice-junction detection in which a 'partial' ground-truth annotation is created by withholding transcripts carrying AStalavista-identified exon skipping / alternative donor / alternative acceptor events, so those events serve as held-out truth against which tools (fortuna, STAR 1/2-pass, Whippet) are scored for recall and precision. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: A benchmarking scheme for novel splice-junction detection in which a 'partial' ground-truth annotation is created by withholding transcripts carrying AStalavista-identified exon skipping / alternative donor / alternative acceptor events, so those events serve as held-out truth against which tools (fortuna, STAR 1/2-pass, Whippet) are scored for recall and precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference annotation already contains the junctions of interest, so there are no held-out novel events to score against — a partial-annotation design would measure nothing. You need full-assembly evaluation (e.g. novel splice-site discovery from unaligned reads), not recall/precision on junction-spanning reads between annotated splice sites. Read lengths other than the indexed ones are used: fortuna indexes are read-length-specific (built separately with -rl 75 and -rl 100), so off-target read lengths would require new indexes.

skills.description: Use when implementing or validating a greedy feature-selection criterion (e.g., RRCT or an mRMR extension) that must account for feature interactions: candidate features need scoring via conditional relevance given the already-selected subset, not just marginal relevance and pairwise redundancy.
skills.name: partial-correlation-complementarity-assessment
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-complementarity-assessment Use when implementing or validating a greedy feature-selection criterion (e.g., RRCT or an mRMR extension) that must account for feature interactions: candidate features need scoring via conditional relevance given the already-selected subset, not just marginal relevance and pairwise redundancy. Features are already selected and only a classifier evaluation (e.g., misclassification rate via random forest over 1...min(M,30) subsets) is needed — this skill only scores features The selection criterion intentionally ignores interactions (e.g., plain mRMR_Spearman, which combines only relevance and redundancy without a complementarity term) The data matrix is not a standard X/y setup (no response vector), since relevance and conditional relevance are both defined against y http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies the complementarity (conditional relevance) term of the RRCT feature-selection criterion by computing rank partial correlations between each candidate feature and the response, controlling for the already-selected feature subset rp(fj,y|S), alongside the information-theoretic transformation of Spearman rank correlations used for relevance and redundancy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100471
skills.summary: Quantifies the complementarity (conditional relevance) term of the RRCT feature-selection criterion by computing rank partial correlations between each candidate feature and the response, controlling for the already-selected feature subset rp(fj,y|S), alongside the information-theoretic transformation of Spearman rank correlations used for relevance and redundancy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are already selected and only a classifier evaluation (e.g., misclassification rate via random forest over 1...min(M,30) subsets) is needed — this skill only scores features The selection criterion intentionally ignores interactions (e.g., plain mRMR_Spearman, which combines only relevance and redundancy without a complementarity term) The data matrix is not a standard X/y setup (no response vector), since relevance and conditional relevance are both defined against y

skills.description: Use when building a GGM-based co-expression network from a large single-cell expression matrix where weak co-expression signals and dropouts make ordinary Pearson correlation unreliable.
skills.name: partial-correlation-edge-thresholding
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-edge-thresholding Use when building a GGM-based co-expression network from a large single-cell expression matrix where weak co-expression signals and dropouts make ordinary Pearson correlation unreliable. The dataset is a bulk transcriptome dataset — the modified GGM workflow for bulk data is rgsGGM, not SingleCellGGM The cell number is small (SingleCellGGM recommends >5000 cells), or low-expression genes have not been filtered out first The goal is integrative multimodal analysis (e.g. ATAC-seq or proteomics); SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct a single-cell gene co-expression network by thresholding gene-pair partial correlation coefficients (pcors) computed by SingleCellGGM, retaining edges with pcor >= 0.03 between gene pairs co-expressed in at least 10 cells, and assessing edge significance with permutation-based FDR control. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Construct a single-cell gene co-expression network by thresholding gene-pair partial correlation coefficients (pcors) computed by SingleCellGGM, retaining edges with pcor >= 0.03 between gene pairs co-expressed in at least 10 cells, and assessing edge significance with permutation-based FDR control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is a bulk transcriptome dataset — the modified GGM workflow for bulk data is rgsGGM, not SingleCellGGM The cell number is small (SingleCellGGM recommends >5000 cells), or low-expression genes have not been filtered out first The goal is integrative multimodal analysis (e.g. ATAC-seq or proteomics); SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data

skills.description: Use when the goal is to construct a gene co-expression network from a raw single-cell expression matrix (e.g., MCA, >5000 cells) via GGM/pcor methods, and to identify gene expression programs (GEPs) from it.
skills.name: partial-correlation-network-inference-single-cell
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-network-inference-single-cell Use when the goal is to construct a gene co-expression network from a raw single-cell expression matrix (e.g., MCA, >5000 cells) via GGM/pcor methods, and to identify gene expression programs (GEPs) from it. The dataset is small-scale or has few cells (<5000 recommended by the README for SingleCellGGM) where existing pcor methods like ppcor/SILGGM were originally tested The goal requires integration of non-transcriptomic single-cell modalities (ATAC-seq, proteomics) — SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data Dropout-imputation or metacell-based co-expression approaches (MAGIC, scImpute, MetaCell, scCorr) are the intended analysis route rather than GGM/pcor network inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infers single-cell gene co-expression networks using partial correlation (pcor)-based graphical Gaussian model approaches — primarily SingleCellGGM, with ppcor and SILGGM as comparators — and evaluates the resulting GEPs by module counts, GO enrichment, and significance criteria. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Infers single-cell gene co-expression networks using partial correlation (pcor)-based graphical Gaussian model approaches — primarily SingleCellGGM, with ppcor and SILGGM as comparators — and evaluates the resulting GEPs by module counts, GO enrichment, and significance criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small-scale or has few cells (<5000 recommended by the README for SingleCellGGM) where existing pcor methods like ppcor/SILGGM were originally tested The goal requires integration of non-transcriptomic single-cell modalities (ATAC-seq, proteomics) — SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data Dropout-imputation or metacell-based co-expression approaches (MAGIC, scImpute, MetaCell, scCorr) are the intended analysis route rather than GGM/pcor network inference

skills.description: Use when building a gene co-expression network (GGM) from a large single-cell expression matrix (>5000 cells recommended) and you need pcor estimates with permutation-based FDR control to select significant gene pairs.
skills.name: partial-correlation-permutation-testing
skills.search_text: partial-correlation-permutation-testing Use when building a gene co-expression network (GGM) from a large single-cell expression matrix (>5000 cells recommended) and you need pcor estimates with permutation-based FDR control to select significant gene pairs. Datasets with fewer than ~5000 cells — the README recommends large cell numbers and the method was designed for large-scale transcriptomes You need multi-modal integration (ATAC-seq, single-cell proteomics) — SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data Small-scale datasets where simpler co-expression methods suffice — prior pcor methods like SILGGM and scLink were only tested on small datasets, whereas this skill targets large datasets such as MCA (61,637 cells) and Mouse Brain (292,495 cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistical inference of gene-gene partial correlations (pcors) from single-cell transcriptomes via SingleCellGGM, which samples gene pairs over ~20,000 iterations and uses permutation-based statistics to control the gene-pair false discovery rate before network construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Statistical inference of gene-gene partial correlations (pcors) from single-cell transcriptomes via SingleCellGGM, which samples gene pairs over ~20,000 iterations and uses permutation-based statistics to control the gene-pair false discovery rate before network construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with fewer than ~5000 cells — the README recommends large cell numbers and the method was designed for large-scale transcriptomes You need multi-modal integration (ATAC-seq, single-cell proteomics) — SingleCellGGM relies exclusively on transcriptome data Small-scale datasets where simpler co-expression methods suffice — prior pcor methods like SILGGM and scLink were only tested on small datasets, whereas this skill targets large datasets such as MCA (61,637 cells) and Mouse Brain (292,495 cells)

skills.description: Use when evaluating how accurately a supervised single-cell integration method predicts cell-type labels for unannotated cells, against a baseline like scANVI, under partial-annotation settings (10%, 20%, or 50% of cells missing labels).
skills.name: partial-label-prediction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: partial-label-prediction-benchmarking Use when evaluating how accurately a supervised single-cell integration method predicts cell-type labels for unannotated cells, against a baseline like scANVI, under partial-annotation settings (10%, 20%, or 50% of cells missing labels). The task is fully supervised integration where all cells are annotated (use scDREAMER-Sup in fully supervised mode instead of a partial-label benchmark) The goal is unsupervised batch integration without any cell-type annotations or label prediction (use unsupervised scDREAMER) The dataset lacks ground-truth cell-type labels, so macro F1 on held-out cells cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks semi-supervised cell-type label prediction by training scDREAMER-Sup and scANVI on the same partially annotated scRNA-seq dataset (10/20/50% labels masked) and comparing macro F1-scores on the held-out unlabeled cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43590-8
skills.summary: Benchmarks semi-supervised cell-type label prediction by training scDREAMER-Sup and scANVI on the same partially annotated scRNA-seq dataset (10/20/50% labels masked) and comparing macro F1-scores on the held-out unlabeled cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is fully supervised integration where all cells are annotated (use scDREAMER-Sup in fully supervised mode instead of a partial-label benchmark) The goal is unsupervised batch integration without any cell-type annotations or label prediction (use unsupervised scDREAMER) The dataset lacks ground-truth cell-type labels, so macro F1 on held-out cells cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when scRNAseq expression matrices contain unmeasured technical confounders (e.g. ERCC spike-ins available as controls), and a corrected matrix is needed for downstream clustering/analysis.
skills.name: partial-least-squares-control-gene-modeling
skills.search_text: partial-least-squares-control-gene-modeling Use when scRNAseq expression matrices contain unmeasured technical confounders (e.g. ERCC spike-ins available as controls), and a corrected matrix is needed for downstream clustering/analysis. You need direct estimates of biological factors u_i — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors themselves, due to model identifiability Downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction) — the paper states performance of scPLS in other analysis settings was not evaluated Data are counts that require a count-based model — extending the framework to count modeling is explicitly left as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply scPLS (single cell partial least squares) to infer and remove hidden technical confounding factors in scRNAseq data by jointly modeling a control gene set (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, then benchmark the corrected data with clustering (k-means, PCA, t-SNE, SC3) scored by adjusted Rand Index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Apply scPLS (single cell partial least squares) to infer and remove hidden technical confounding factors in scRNAseq data by jointly modeling a control gene set (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, then benchmark the corrected data with clustering (k-means, PCA, t-SNE, SC3) scored by adjusted Rand Index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need direct estimates of biological factors u_i — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors themselves, due to model identifiability Downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction) — the paper states performance of scPLS in other analysis settings was not evaluated Data are counts that require a count-based model — extending the framework to count modeling is explicitly left as future work

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression must be corrected for hidden confounders (e.g. cell cycle, batch/technical effects) and both control genes and target genes are available to inform factor inference.
skills.name: partial-least-squares-latent-factor-modeling
skills.search_text: partial-least-squares-latent-factor-modeling Use when scRNA-seq expression must be corrected for hidden confounders (e.g. cell cycle, batch/technical effects) and both control genes and target genes are available to inform factor inference. When the goal is direct inference of biological factors (u_i) — by model identifiability scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the biological factors When a count-based model of the raw data is required — the article leaves extension to count models as future work When control genes are unavailable and no all-genes (PCA/LMM-style) configuration is acceptable http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit scPLS, a partial least squares latent factor model that jointly models a control gene set and a target gene set in single cell RNA-seq data to infer hidden confounding factors, using the paper's PLS-based initializer and a naive/block-wise EM algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Fit scPLS, a partial least squares latent factor model that jointly models a control gene set and a target gene set in single cell RNA-seq data to infer hidden confounding factors, using the paper's PLS-based initializer and a naive/block-wise EM algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is direct inference of biological factors (u_i) — by model identifiability scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the biological factors When a count-based model of the raw data is required — the article leaves extension to count models as future work When control genes are unavailable and no all-genes (PCA/LMM-style) configuration is acceptable

skills.description: Use when a decomposition algorithm (e.g. JIVE) needs only the 1–10 singular components of a large dense matrix and full SVD is the runtime bottleneck.
skills.name: partial-svd-computation
skills.search_text: partial-svd-computation Use when a decomposition algorithm (e.g. JIVE) needs only the 1–10 singular components of a large dense matrix and full SVD is the runtime bottleneck. All singular values/vectors or the full rank decomposition are required, not just the leading 1–10 components. The matrix is small enough that base R svd runtime (~1.67 s at 1000×1000) is not a bottleneck. The data are sparse or too large for dense storage, where specialized sparse iterative solvers would be more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Benchmarks and applies RSpectra's partial SVD (svds) against base R's full svd to compute leading singular components, the core linear-algebra kernel behind JIVE's computational-efficiency boost. On 1000×1000 matrices it cuts runtime by 91–95% for 1–10 components. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Benchmarks and applies RSpectra's partial SVD (svds) against base R's full svd to compute leading singular components, the core linear-algebra kernel behind JIVE's computational-efficiency boost. On 1000×1000 matrices it cuts runtime by 91–95% for 1–10 components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All singular values/vectors or the full rank decomposition are required, not just the leading 1–10 components. The matrix is small enough that base R svd runtime (~1.67 s at 1000×1000) is not a bottleneck. The data are sparse or too large for dense storage, where specialized sparse iterative solvers would be more appropriate.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (Scanpy AnnData, .h5ad) must be decomposed into gene-age-stratified expression contributions — e.g. to test whether the youngest age classes (C. elegans classes 11–13) peak in early embryos.
skills.name: partial-tei-stratified-computation
skills.search_text: partial-tei-stratified-computation Use when scRNA-seq data (Scanpy AnnData, .h5ad) must be decomposed into gene-age-stratified expression contributions — e.g. to test whether the youngest age classes (C. elegans classes 11–13) peak in early embryos. The goal is a single global TEI trendline per cell without decomposing into age-class contributions — plain get_TEI suffices No orthomap/gene age annotations exist for the species and none can be extracted — gene ages are the prerequisite for stratification The input is bulk expression data rather than a Scanpy scRNA object; oggmap's TEI functions operate on Scanpy AnnData http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell/per-stage partial transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) profiles, where the expression-weighted contributions of individual gene age classes sum to the global TEI, using oggmap on Scanpy scRNA objects. This reveals which evolutionary age strata (e.g. youngest, species-specific classes) drive expression at each cell type or developmental stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Compute per-cell/per-stage partial transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) profiles, where the expression-weighted contributions of individual gene age classes sum to the global TEI, using oggmap on Scanpy scRNA objects. This reveals which evolutionary age strata (e.g. youngest, species-specific classes) drive expression at each cell type or developmental stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single global TEI trendline per cell without decomposing into age-class contributions — plain get_TEI suffices No orthomap/gene age annotations exist for the species and none can be extracted — gene ages are the prerequisite for stratification The input is bulk expression data rather than a Scanpy scRNA object; oggmap's TEI functions operate on Scanpy AnnData

skills.description: Use when a fitted subgroup tree (dipm/spmtree for continuous or survival outcomes) needs publication-ready visualization, and the default partykit terminal panels are insufficient because treatment-stratified distributions or survival curves must be shown per node.
skills.name: partykit-tree-plot-customization
skills.search_text: partykit-tree-plot-customization Use when a fitted subgroup tree (dipm/spmtree for continuous or survival outcomes) needs publication-ready visualization, and the default partykit terminal panels are insufficient because treatment-stratified distributions or survival curves must be shown per node. The tree is a plain rpart or party object from a non-dipm workflow — node_dipm is designed for dipm/spmtree objects returned by this package's fitting functions Only the DIPM depth importance scores or pruned subgroup structure are needed (use pmprune(tree) or the printed tree object instead of rendering plots) The analysis goal is fitting or pruning the tree rather than visualizing it — use dipm(), spmtree(), or pmprune() directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 This skill renders fitted precision-medicine trees (dipm or spmtree objects) as tree diagrams with custom terminal-node panels, using node_dipm from the dipm package as the panel function for partykit::plot. It produces per-node boxplots for continuous outcomes (e.g. anorexia) and survival curves for survival outcomes (e.g. GBSG2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: This skill renders fitted precision-medicine trees (dipm or spmtree objects) as tree diagrams with custom terminal-node panels, using node_dipm from the dipm package as the panel function for partykit::plot. It produces per-node boxplots for continuous outcomes (e.g. anorexia) and survival curves for survival outcomes (e.g. GBSG2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tree is a plain rpart or party object from a non-dipm workflow — node_dipm is designed for dipm/spmtree objects returned by this package's fitting functions Only the DIPM depth importance scores or pruned subgroup structure are needed (use pmprune(tree) or the printed tree object instead of rendering plots) The analysis goal is fitting or pruning the tree rather than visualizing it — use dipm(), spmtree(), or pmprune() directly

skills.description: Use when a DIPM tree (e.g. fitted to the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) or a pmprune-pruned version of it needs to be rendered for inspection, so subgroup splits and optimal treatment assignments at each node can be visually verified.
skills.name: partykit-tree-visualization
skills.search_text: partykit-tree-visualization Use when a DIPM tree (e.g. fitted to the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) or a pmprune-pruned version of it needs to be rendered for inspection, so subgroup splits and optimal treatment assignments at each node can be visually verified. The tree has not yet been fitted or pruned — plot() on a non-tree object from the dipm workflow will not render the DIPM node structure The goal is treatment-effect estimation or subgroup identification itself rather than visual inspection of an already-fitted DIPM tree; use dipm()/spmtree() instead partykit cannot be attached because its dependencies were not installed — the dipm package does not attach it automatically, so plotting will fail without an explicit library(partykit) call Visual inspection of a fitted (and optionally pmprune-simplified) DIPM classification tree by plotting the tree object with the partykit package, which the dipm package lists as a Dependency. skills.summary: Visual inspection of a fitted (and optionally pmprune-simplified) DIPM classification tree by plotting the tree object with the partykit package, which the dipm package lists as a Dependency. skills.when_to_use_negative: The tree has not yet been fitted or pruned — plot() on a non-tree object from the dipm workflow will not render the DIPM node structure The goal is treatment-effect estimation or subgroup identification itself rather than visual inspection of an already-fitted DIPM tree; use dipm()/spmtree() instead partykit cannot be attached because its dependencies were not installed — the dipm package does not attach it automatically, so plotting will fail without an explicit library(partykit) call

skills.description: Use when 10x cellranger output exists for infected-cell scRNAseq data and per-cell UMI counts for individual pathogen genes (not just total pathogen reads) are needed, e.g. for Fig. 3J-style aligner consistency or gene-level infection analysis.
skills.name: pathogen-gene-umi-quantification
skills.search_text: pathogen-gene-umi-quantification Use when 10x cellranger output exists for infected-cell scRNAseq data and per-cell UMI counts for individual pathogen genes (not just total pathogen reads) are needed, e.g. for Fig. 3J-style aligner consistency or gene-level infection analysis. No pathogen/viral GTF file is available — scPathoQuant will only produce total pathogen counts, since pathogen_genes_al_sort_counts.sam 'will not be produced if pathogen/viral gtf is not provided' Input is not 10x cellranger count output (e.g. bulk RNA-seq FASTQs or already-aggregated gene-count matrices) — scPathoQuant expects the cellranger output folder structure Goal is viral phylogenetic or clade analysis rather than gene-level quantification — use the mapped-read FASTQ (pathogen_al_mapped.fq.gz) instead of per-gene UMI counts Quantifies per-cell UMI counts mapping to individual pathogen genes (e.g. the ten annotated SARS-CoV-2 genes on GCF_009858895.2) using scPathoQuant, which runs htseq with --intersection-nonempty on reads aligned to the pathogen genome and integrates per-gene counts back into 10x cellranger outputs. Per-gene resolution also enables aligner-consistency checks such as correlating bbmap vs bowtie2 gene count vectors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Quantifies per-cell UMI counts mapping to individual pathogen genes (e.g. the ten annotated SARS-CoV-2 genes on GCF_009858895.2) using scPathoQuant, which runs htseq with --intersection-nonempty on reads aligned to the pathogen genome and integrates per-gene counts back into 10x cellranger outputs. Per-gene resolution also enables aligner-consistency checks such as correlating bbmap vs bowtie2 gene count vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No pathogen/viral GTF file is available — scPathoQuant will only produce total pathogen counts, since pathogen_genes_al_sort_counts.sam 'will not be produced if pathogen/viral gtf is not provided' Input is not 10x cellranger count output (e.g. bulk RNA-seq FASTQs or already-aggregated gene-count matrices) — scPathoQuant expects the cellranger output folder structure Goal is viral phylogenetic or clade analysis rather than gene-level quantification — use the mapped-read FASTQ (pathogen_al_mapped.fq.gz) instead of per-gene UMI counts

skills.description: Use when you have 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample where cellranger count has already aligned reads to the host genome, and you need per-cell viral/bacterial counts in a single command.
skills.name: pathogen-genome-read-alignment
skills.search_text: pathogen-genome-read-alignment Use when you have 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample where cellranger count has already aligned reads to the host genome, and you need per-cell viral/bacterial counts in a single command. skills.name: pathogen-specific-candidate-count-verification
skills.search_text: pathogen-specific-candidate-count-verification Use when reproducing or validating candidate gene counts from GWAS SNPs plus coexpression modules, e.g. after running cageminer on SoyFungiGCN data with defense guide genes and a 2 Mb SNP window. The goal is de novo network construction from raw RNA-seq rather than counting candidates from the pre-built SoyFungiGCN coexpression data The target organism or pathogen set differs from soybean and its five phytopathogenic fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi) Different SNP window sizes or scoring thresholds are intended, in which case counts cannot be compared to the published 188/56/11/8/3 values http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Verifies that the cageminer-based prioritization of soybean candidate resistance genes reproduces the per-pathogen high-confidence candidate counts (188/56/11/8/3) reported for F. virguliforme, F. graminearum, C. gregata, M. phaseolina, and P. pachyrhizi using the SoyFungiGCN package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Verifies that the cageminer-based prioritization of soybean candidate resistance genes reproduces the per-pathogen high-confidence candidate counts (188/56/11/8/3) reported for F. virguliforme, F. graminearum, C. gregata, M. phaseolina, and P. pachyrhizi using the SoyFungiGCN package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo network construction from raw RNA-seq rather than counting candidates from the pre-built SoyFungiGCN coexpression data The target organism or pathogen set differs from soybean and its five phytopathogenic fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi) Different SNP window sizes or scoring thresholds are intended, in which case counts cannot be compared to the published 188/56/11/8/3 values

skills.description: Use when validating Cancer-Finder (or similar) spot-level malignancy predictions on 10x Visium slides against pathologist annotations, e.g. reproducing the reported per-slide accuracy of 82.00–97.37% (Fig. 4b,c).
skills.name: pathologist-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: pathologist-annotation-accuracy-evaluation Use when validating Cancer-Finder (or similar) spot-level malignancy predictions on 10x Visium slides against pathologist annotations, e.g. reproducing the reported per-slide accuracy of 82.00–97.37% (Fig. 4b,c). Input is hematologic tumor data — the article states 'We do not therefore recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data'. Slides from cancer types not included in the ST training set — the 82.00–97.37% accuracy claim applies only to trained tissues. Analysis requires modeling spatial dependencies — 'Cancer-Finder overlooks the spatial relationships among spots in ST data'. Evaluates reference-free malignant-spot predictions on 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics slides by comparing binarized model calls to pathologist-derived malignant (1) / non-malignant (0) spot labels, computing per-slide accuracy as (TP+TN)/N and expecting values in the reported 82.00–97.37% range for trained cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Evaluates reference-free malignant-spot predictions on 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics slides by comparing binarized model calls to pathologist-derived malignant (1) / non-malignant (0) spot labels, computing per-slide accuracy as (TP+TN)/N and expecting values in the reported 82.00–97.37% range for trained cancer types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is hematologic tumor data — the article states 'We do not therefore recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data'. Slides from cancer types not included in the ST training set — the 82.00–97.37% accuracy claim applies only to trained tissues. Analysis requires modeling spatial dependencies — 'Cancer-Finder overlooks the spatial relationships among spots in ST data'.

skills.description: Use when you have tumor ST spot-level predictions (e.g., malignancy_probability, AUCell signature scores, image scores) plus pathologist-annotated malignant regions and need accuracy/balanced-accuracy benchmarking against expert labels or a competing classifier.
skills.name: pathologist-annotation-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: pathologist-annotation-benchmark-comparison Use when you have tumor ST spot-level predictions (e.g., malignancy_probability, AUCell signature scores, image scores) plus pathologist-annotated malignant regions and need accuracy/balanced-accuracy benchmarking against expert labels or a competing classifier. Input is scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates or pathology images — the multi-feature region clustering requires malignancy_probability, Malignant_up, and image_score; for non-spatial data use single-cell malignant-cell identification instead Cancer type has unknown or controversial origin (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — the tool's capabilities were not validated there Malignant cells have not been distinguished from basic cell types — the method relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types and applies only to cancerous lineages http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks model-predicted malignant regions in spatial transcriptomics against expert pathologist annotations by computing region-level accuracy and balanced accuracy, and against competing tools such as Cancer-Finder, following the scMalignantFinder eight-dataset evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Benchmarks model-predicted malignant regions in spatial transcriptomics against expert pathologist annotations by computing region-level accuracy and balanced accuracy, and against competing tools such as Cancer-Finder, following the scMalignantFinder eight-dataset evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates or pathology images — the multi-feature region clustering requires malignancy_probability, Malignant_up, and image_score; for non-spatial data use single-cell malignant-cell identification instead Cancer type has unknown or controversial origin (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — the tool's capabilities were not validated there Malignant cells have not been distinguished from basic cell types — the method relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types and applies only to cancerous lineages

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample cell-type/structure distributions from histopathology (e.g., .h5ad pathomics objects) and want an unsupervised disease progression ordering of samples plus associated morphometric changes.
skills.name: pathomics-trajectory-inference-with-eiplgraph
skills.search_text: pathomics-trajectory-inference-with-eiplgraph Use when you have per-sample cell-type/structure distributions from histopathology (e.g., .h5ad pathomics objects) and want an unsupervised disease progression ordering of samples plus associated morphometric changes. Data are single-cell gene expression rather than pathomics structure distributions — use the PILOT single-cell (e.g., myocardial infarction) workflow instead Samples were collected with distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which PILOT does not explicitly correct for You need patient labels supervised in advance — PILOT is designed for unsupervised sample-level analysis, unlike PhEMD/SCANCell/Multi-scale PHATE approaches that require labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reconstruct a patient-level disease progression trajectory from pathomics data by computing sample-level Wasserstein distances with PILOT, embedding them via diffusion maps, and fitting an EIPLGraph principal graph to rank samples along pseudotime. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Reconstruct a patient-level disease progression trajectory from pathomics data by computing sample-level Wasserstein distances with PILOT, embedding them via diffusion maps, and fitting an EIPLGraph principal graph to rank samples along pseudotime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell gene expression rather than pathomics structure distributions — use the PILOT single-cell (e.g., myocardial infarction) workflow instead Samples were collected with distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based), which PILOT does not explicitly correct for You need patient labels supervised in advance — PILOT is designed for unsupervised sample-level analysis, unlike PhEMD/SCANCell/Multi-scale PHATE approaches that require labels

skills.search_text: pathway-activation-heatmap-visualization Use when a CommPath object already contains scored pathways (scorePath) and differential activation results (diffAllPath), and you need to visualize the top differentially activated pathways per cluster as a heatmap PDF. skills.summary: Render the differentially activated signaling pathways per cell cluster from a CommPath analysis as a heatmap (pathHeatmap), so that top pathway activation differences (e.g., KEGG pathways scored by GSVA) can be inspected alongside the acti.path.dat significance statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Before pathway scores exist — the object lacks scorePath/diffAllPath results, so there is nothing differentially activated to display When the goal is to show LR pair counts or interaction intensities among clusters — use circosPlot (filter=FALSE or TRUE) instead of a pathway heatmap When pathways are only annotated (findLRpath) but not yet scored, since the heatmap reflects activation levels, not mere geneset overlap

skills.description: Use when single-cell or semi-profiled cohort data (annotated cells with condition labels, e.g., Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical) must be compared for pathway-level fidelity, or when pathway activation patterns are a downstream deliverable.
skills.name: pathway-activation-score-computation-single-cell
skills.search_text: pathway-activation-score-computation-single-cell Use when single-cell or semi-profiled cohort data (annotated cells with condition labels, e.g., Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical) must be compared for pathway-level fidelity, or when pathway activation patterns are a downstream deliverable. Input is bulk sequencing data without a single-cell reference — bulk deconvolution approaches (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS) are constrained to cell-type-level resolution and cannot produce single-cell-level pathway scores Data are from other modalities such as proteomics — the article states such extensions are future work, not yet implemented The cohort lacks a healthy baseline condition, since fold changes are defined relative to the healthy condition http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-cell pathway/gene-set activation scores (e.g., interferon) from single-cell data with SCANPY's tl.score_genes, aggregates them per cell type and disease condition as fold changes versus healthy, and uses the resulting score matrices to quantify agreement between semi-profiled and real-profiled cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Computes per-cell pathway/gene-set activation scores (e.g., interferon) from single-cell data with SCANPY's tl.score_genes, aggregates them per cell type and disease condition as fold changes versus healthy, and uses the resulting score matrices to quantify agreement between semi-profiled and real-profiled cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk sequencing data without a single-cell reference — bulk deconvolution approaches (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, DWLS, MuSiC, NNLS) are constrained to cell-type-level resolution and cannot produce single-cell-level pathway scores Data are from other modalities such as proteomics — the article states such extensions are future work, not yet implemented The cohort lacks a healthy baseline condition, since fold changes are defined relative to the healthy condition

skills.description: Use when a gene expression matrix (rows = samples, columns = Entrez gene IDs) must be converted into gene-set/pathway activity features for cancer subtype classification or to test robustness to incomplete gene annotation.
skills.name: pathway-activity-estimation-from-gene-expression
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-estimation-from-gene-expression Use when a gene expression matrix (rows = samples, columns = Entrez gene IDs) must be converted into gene-set/pathway activity features for cancer subtype classification or to test robustness to incomplete gene annotation. The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is developed for classification but not clustering Input is already a pathway/gene-set activity or deep-feature table rather than raw gene expression (spectra computation would be redundant) Only one sample is available with no reference expression profile for the same/similar cancer type and platform http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Compute DeepCC 'functional spectra' — pathway/gene-set activity scores that transform a gene expression profile into MSigDB gene-set space using tools like getFunctionalSpectra over MSigDB v7 (22,596 gene sets). This transformation is what makes the DeepCC classifier platform independent and robust to missing genes across platforms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Compute DeepCC 'functional spectra' — pathway/gene-set activity scores that transform a gene expression profile into MSigDB gene-set space using tools like getFunctionalSpectra over MSigDB v7 (22,596 gene sets). This transformation is what makes the DeepCC classifier platform independent and robust to missing genes across platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is developed for classification but not clustering Input is already a pathway/gene-set activity or deep-feature table rather than raw gene expression (spectra computation would be redundant) Only one sample is available with no reference expression profile for the same/similar cancer type and platform

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData-wrapped MIX-Seq drug treatment data) needs to be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by GMT gene sets, and per-cell pathway activity or differential pathway activity between conditions is the goal.
skills.name: pathway-activity-inference-at-single-cell-level
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-inference-at-single-cell-level Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData-wrapped MIX-Seq drug treatment data) needs to be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by GMT gene sets, and per-cell pathway activity or differential pathway activity between conditions is the goal. When predictive/generative performance is the priority rather than interpretability — VEGA's sparse, single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance and has limited generative capacity When prior gene module annotations (e.g., MSigDB) are incomplete or not context-specific and unannotated genes are expected to matter — the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge When the goal is de novo discovery of pathways or latent factors without a priori gene module definitions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers gene module/pathway activities (GMVs) per single cell using VEGA, a sparse VAE whose decoder wiring mirrors user-provided gene modules (e.g., MSigDB hallmark GMT files), enabling interpretable latent-space analysis of perturbation responses such as drug treatments in MIX-Seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Infers gene module/pathway activities (GMVs) per single cell using VEGA, a sparse VAE whose decoder wiring mirrors user-provided gene modules (e.g., MSigDB hallmark GMT files), enabling interpretable latent-space analysis of perturbation responses such as drug treatments in MIX-Seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When predictive/generative performance is the priority rather than interpretability — VEGA's sparse, single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance and has limited generative capacity When prior gene module annotations (e.g., MSigDB) are incomplete or not context-specific and unannotated genes are expected to matter — the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge When the goal is de novo discovery of pathways or latent factors without a priori gene module definitions

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify signaling pathway activity from normalized gene expression (DESeq2 size-factor/VST RNA-seq, microarray, single-cell) for perturbation recall, driver mutation, drug-sensitivity, or patient-survival association analyses.
skills.name: pathway-activity-inference-from-gene-expression
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-inference-from-gene-expression Use when you need to quantify signaling pathway activity from normalized gene expression (DESeq2 size-factor/VST RNA-seq, microarray, single-cell) for perturbation recall, driver mutation, drug-sensitivity, or patient-survival association analyses. When you need pathway activity for organisms/pathways without perturbation experiments — directed-path methods (e.g., Gene Ontology/Reactome abundance via GSVA) cover more pathways, but their expression level should not be interpreted as activity When a tissue-specific signature is available and the target is one specific tissue context — the consensus PROGENy signatures may be outperformed in narrow contexts When input is raw, un-normalized counts without size-factor normalization — DESeq2 normalization precedes scoring in the reference workflows http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer signaling pathway activity scores from gene expression using PROGENy's Pathway RespOnsive GENes (PRGs): 11 pathway signatures (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) derived from 208 ArrayExpress perturbation submissions (580 experiments), computed as weighted linear combinations of normalized expression via the progeny R/Bioconductor package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Infer signaling pathway activity scores from gene expression using PROGENy's Pathway RespOnsive GENes (PRGs): 11 pathway signatures (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) derived from 208 ArrayExpress perturbation submissions (580 experiments), computed as weighted linear combinations of normalized expression via the progeny R/Bioconductor package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need pathway activity for organisms/pathways without perturbation experiments — directed-path methods (e.g., Gene Ontology/Reactome abundance via GSVA) cover more pathways, but their expression level should not be interpreted as activity When a tissue-specific signature is available and the target is one specific tissue context — the consensus PROGENy signatures may be outperformed in narrow contexts When input is raw, un-normalized counts without size-factor normalization — DESeq2 normalization precedes scoring in the reference workflows

skills.description: Use when you need single-cell pathway activity scores (PAL) for a gene set in scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data without clustering, e.g., to fetch relevant cells or weight cells for spatial relevance tests.
skills.name: pathway-activity-likelihood-scoring
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-likelihood-scoring Use when you need single-cell pathway activity scores (PAL) for a gene set in scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data without clustering, e.g., to fetch relevant cells or weight cells for spatial relevance tests. Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' The goal is differential-density testing of gene sets in the MCA space alone (use compute.kld) rather than per-cell activity scoring/fetching of relevant cells Running on macOS with an M1 chip, where installation fails due to a CelliD/scuttle dependency issue http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Score per-cell pathway activity likelihood (PAL) with GSDensity by running random walk with restart (network propagation) on a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built in the MCA co-embedding, using pathway genes as seeds; optionally benchmarked against CelliD's MCA-based ranking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Score per-cell pathway activity likelihood (PAL) with GSDensity by running random walk with restart (network propagation) on a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built in the MCA co-embedding, using pathway genes as seeds; optionally benchmarked against CelliD's MCA-based ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' The goal is differential-density testing of gene sets in the MCA space alone (use compute.kld) rather than per-cell activity scoring/fetching of relevant cells Running on macOS with an M1 chip, where installation fails due to a CelliD/scuttle dependency issue

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively evaluate whether a pathway activity method outperforms alternatives (fGSEA, iDEA, GSVA, AUCell, Vision, ssGSEA) on controlled single-cell simulations with a known ground-truth perturbed pathway.
skills.name: pathway-activity-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-method-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively evaluate whether a pathway activity method outperforms alternatives (fGSEA, iDEA, GSVA, AUCell, Vision, ssGSEA) on controlled single-cell simulations with a known ground-truth perturbed pathway. The goal is biological discovery on real patient data (e.g. COVID-19 peripheral blood atlas comparisons) rather than controlled method evaluation with a known implanted pathway. The competing tools cannot be run on the identical simulated input — a fair sensitivity comparison requires all methods to see the same two-population sample pairs. Only a single simulation scenario is available; sensitivity (fraction of scenarios with detection) cannot be meaningfully estimated from one point. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmarking protocol for comparing the sensitivity of a single-cell pathway analysis method (here SCPA) against competitor tools on Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq datasets with an implanted 200-gene perturbed pathway, quantifying detection sensitivity per method per scenario. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for comparing the sensitivity of a single-cell pathway analysis method (here SCPA) against competitor tools on Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq datasets with an implanted 200-gene perturbed pathway, quantifying detection sensitivity per method per scenario.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological discovery on real patient data (e.g. COVID-19 peripheral blood atlas comparisons) rather than controlled method evaluation with a known implanted pathway. The competing tools cannot be run on the identical simulated input — a fair sensitivity comparison requires all methods to see the same two-population sample pairs. Only a single simulation scenario is available; sensitivity (fraction of scenarios with detection) cannot be meaningfully estimated from one point.

skills.description: Use when single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data must be scored per cell for pathway activity without clustering — e.g., to fetch cells active for a gene set (Hallmark G2M, GO BP terms) or to weight cells for spatial KDE testing.
skills.name: pathway-activity-network-propagation
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-network-propagation Use when single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data must be scored per cell for pathway activity without clustering — e.g., to fetch cells active for a gene set (Hallmark G2M, GO BP terms) or to weight cells for spatial KDE testing. Data are targeted-panel spatial assays with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' unless unmeasured genes are imputed, which is not implemented The gene set failed the coordination test (compute.kld adjusted p >= 0.05) — binarization should only be performed on gene sets that pass the coordination test Only relative pathway ranking speed on small cell numbers matters — AUCell was faster than GSDensity when the number of cells was small http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute per-cell pathway activity likelihood scores (PALs) with GSDensity by seeding a random-walk-with-restart on a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built from the MCA co-embedding, enabling cluster-free, pathway-centric classification of single cells (e.g., G2M-positive tumor cells) and spatial pathway relevance weighting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Compute per-cell pathway activity likelihood scores (PALs) with GSDensity by seeding a random-walk-with-restart on a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built from the MCA co-embedding, enabling cluster-free, pathway-centric classification of single cells (e.g., G2M-positive tumor cells) and spatial pathway relevance weighting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted-panel spatial assays with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' unless unmeasured genes are imputed, which is not implemented The gene set failed the coordination test (compute.kld adjusted p >= 0.05) — binarization should only be performed on gene sets that pass the coordination test Only relative pathway ranking speed on small cell numbers matters — AUCell was faster than GSDensity when the number of cells was small

skills.description: Use when you have a cpm-normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix with sample labels (e.g., CF vs healthy donors) and need to identify which gene sets show significantly shifted or over-dispersed activity between conditions.
skills.name: pathway-activity-quantification-from-rnaseq
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-quantification-from-rnaseq Use when you have a cpm-normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix with sample labels (e.g., CF vs healthy donors) and need to identify which gene sets show significantly shifted or over-dispersed activity between conditions. Data are not normalized — rRoma requires normalized input; the README warns 'rRoma works with normalized data' and cpm from edgeR was used for normalisation The goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than coordinated gene set/module activity quantification You need a complete statistical power assessment from a single small dataset — the authors state the CF case study 'would require us to include additional transcriptional dataset... and increase the statistical power of our analyses' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify gene set (module) activity from a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix using the rROMA R package, which computes PC1-based statistics (L1 overdispersion and Median Exp shift) against random gene set null distributions to detect shifted pathways, as demonstrated on the GSE176121 cystic fibrosis airway epithelial dataset with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Quantify gene set (module) activity from a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix using the rROMA R package, which computes PC1-based statistics (L1 overdispersion and Median Exp shift) against random gene set null distributions to detect shifted pathways, as demonstrated on the GSE176121 cystic fibrosis airway epithelial dataset with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not normalized — rRoma requires normalized input; the README warns 'rRoma works with normalized data' and cpm from edgeR was used for normalisation The goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than coordinated gene set/module activity quantification You need a complete statistical power assessment from a single small dataset — the authors state the CF case study 'would require us to include additional transcriptional dataset... and increase the statistical power of our analyses'

skills.description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of PAS scoring methods (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes) across datasets scaling from 10,000 cells to over 1.2 million cells.
skills.name: pathway-activity-score-computation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-score-computation-benchmarking Use when comparing computational efficiency of PAS scoring methods (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes) across datasets scaling from 10,000 cells to over 1.2 million cells. The goal is to produce PAS for biological interpretation (e.g. multicellular pathway modules via MOFA) rather than to measure computational performance The dataset has few cells (<10^3) or few pathways (<10^3), where runtime differences between methods are negligible and benchmarking adds no decision value Input is not a cell x gene expression matrix with a pathway gene-set dictionary, so no PAS scoring comparison can be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks the runtime and peak-memory cost of computing pathway activity scores (PAS) with scPAFA's fast_ucell and fast_score_genes against UCell, AUCell and Scanpy score_genes on large single-cell datasets with >10^3 pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks the runtime and peak-memory cost of computing pathway activity scores (PAS) with scPAFA's fast_ucell and fast_score_genes against UCell, AUCell and Scanpy score_genes on large single-cell datasets with >10^3 pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to produce PAS for biological interpretation (e.g. multicellular pathway modules via MOFA) rather than to measure computational performance The dataset has few cells (<10^3) or few pathways (<10^3), where runtime differences between methods are negligible and benchmarking adds no decision value Input is not a cell x gene expression matrix with a pathway gene-set dictionary, so no PAS scoring comparison can be constructed

skills.description: Use when you need to compare how well competing pathway activity scoring methods recover known cell types from scRNA-seq data, or to benchmark GSDensity against ssGSEA/GSVA/AUCell/VAM/scGSEA/CelliD on labeled or simulated datasets.
skills.name: pathway-activity-scoring-across-methods
skills.search_text: pathway-activity-scoring-across-methods Use when you need to compare how well competing pathway activity scoring methods recover known cell types from scRNA-seq data, or to benchmark GSDensity against ssGSEA/GSVA/AUCell/VAM/scGSEA/CelliD on labeled or simulated datasets. The data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is not suitable there and imputation of unmeasured genes would be needed The goal is only pathway scoring speed on one dataset rather than cell-type recovery benchmarking (a separate five-method speed comparison covers GSDensity, CelliD, AUCell, ssGSEA, VAM) No known cell-type labels or simulated ground truth exist, so recovery AUC/accuracy cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Benchmark gene set/pathway activity scoring methods (GSDensity, ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) for cell-type recovery on SERGIO-simulated and real scRNA-seq datasets, reproducing the GSDensity paper's Fig. 2f-i comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Benchmark gene set/pathway activity scoring methods (GSDensity, ssGSEA, GSVA, AUCell, VAM, scGSEA, CelliD) for cell-type recovery on SERGIO-simulated and real scRNA-seq datasets, reproducing the GSDensity paper's Fig. 2f-i comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are targeted gene panels with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is not suitable there and imputation of unmeasured genes would be needed The goal is only pathway scoring speed on one dataset rather than cell-type recovery benchmarking (a separate five-method speed comparison covers GSDensity, CelliD, AUCell, ssGSEA, VAM) No known cell-type labels or simulated ground truth exist, so recovery AUC/accuracy cannot be computed
