skills.name: pathway-and-disease-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-and-disease-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a list of genes carrying predicted Ψ sites (e.g. from a >0.99-precision transcriptome scan in Supplemental_table2.csv) and need to identify which molecular functions, pathways, or diseases are functionally over-represented. The input is raw uridine-centered RNA fragments or per-site predictions rather than a gene-level list suitable for over-representation analysis The analysis target is a non-human organism or non-protein-coding transcriptome — the paper's enrichment was run against the human protein-coding transcriptome background only Predicted Ψ sites below the >0.99 precision threshold are included, since the enrichment analysis was defined on the high-precision gene set http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Over-representation analysis of GO terms, pathways, and diseases for the 2441 human genes containing MU-PseUDeep-predicted pseudouridine (Ψ) sites, followed by GO semantic similarity network construction, to reveal that predicted Ψ-site genes are enriched in nucleotide/protein binding and neurodegeneration pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Over-representation analysis of GO terms, pathways, and diseases for the 2441 human genes containing MU-PseUDeep-predicted pseudouridine (Ψ) sites, followed by GO semantic similarity network construction, to reveal that predicted Ψ-site genes are enriched in nucleotide/protein binding and neurodegeneration pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw uridine-centered RNA fragments or per-site predictions rather than a gene-level list suitable for over-representation analysis The analysis target is a non-human organism or non-protein-coding transcriptome — the paper's enrichment was run against the human protein-coding transcriptome background only Predicted Ψ sites below the >0.99 precision threshold are included, since the enrichment analysis was defined on the high-precision gene set

skills.description: Use when a trained MOFA model on pseudobulk pathway activity scores (PAS) must be interpreted: identifying which latent factors are disease-related and which pathway-cell type pairs drive them.
skills.name: pathway-cell-type-module-interpretation
skills.search_text: pathway-cell-type-module-interpretation Use when a trained MOFA model on pseudobulk pathway activity scores (PAS) must be interpreted: identifying which latent factors are disease-related and which pathway-cell type pairs drive them. The trained model has fewer than 15 samples (not cells) — the MOFA requirement for multicellular pathway module identification is not met Input is a raw single-cell expression matrix rather than a trained factor model with pathway weights — compute PAS and train MOFA first (steps 1-3) A causal interpretation of pathway-cell type associations is required — scPAFA modules are data-driven associations only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Step-4 downstream analysis of a trained scPAFA/MOFA model that converts latent factors into disease-related multicellular pathway modules by statistically testing factor values against sample-level clinical metadata and dissecting high-weighted pathway-cell type pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Step-4 downstream analysis of a trained scPAFA/MOFA model that converts latent factors into disease-related multicellular pathway modules by statistically testing factor values against sample-level clinical metadata and dissecting high-weighted pathway-cell type pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trained model has fewer than 15 samples (not cells) — the MOFA requirement for multicellular pathway module identification is not met Input is a raw single-cell expression matrix rather than a trained factor model with pathway weights — compute PAS and train MOFA first (steps 1-3) A causal interpretation of pathway-cell type associations is required — scPAFA modules are data-driven associations only

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (Seurat object) must be screened to determine which curated gene sets (KEGG, BIOCARTA, GO:BP) are genuinely heterogeneous across cells prior to pathway activity scoring or binarization, without pre-clustering the cells.
skills.name: pathway-coordination-testing-kld
skills.search_text: pathway-coordination-testing-kld Use when scRNA-seq data (Seurat object) must be screened to determine which curated gene sets (KEGG, BIOCARTA, GO:BP) are genuinely heterogeneous across cells prior to pathway activity scoring or binarization, without pre-clustering the cells. Data are targeted gene-panel scRNA-seq with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is not suitable for such data The gene sets are intended to be used directly without testing; the article recommends binarization only on gene sets that pass the coordination test Input lacks whole-transcriptome coverage needed to estimate an all-gene background density in the MCA space http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether a curated gene set/pathway shows heterogeneous, coordinated activity among cells in single-cell RNA-seq data, by co-embedding cells and genes with MCA and comparing the pathway-gene density to the all-gene background density via KL-divergence permutation testing in GSDensity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Tests whether a curated gene set/pathway shows heterogeneous, coordinated activity among cells in single-cell RNA-seq data, by co-embedding cells and genes with MCA and comparing the pathway-gene density to the all-gene background density via KL-divergence permutation testing in GSDensity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted gene-panel scRNA-seq with limited numbers of genes — GSDensity is not suitable for such data The gene sets are intended to be used directly without testing; the article recommends binarization only on gene sets that pass the coordination test Input lacks whole-transcriptome coverage needed to estimate an all-gene background density in the MCA space

skills.description: Use when a table of enriched int-pairs from a cell-cell interaction analysis needs functional/pathway annotation of its ligand-receptor pairs, e.g. in InterCellar's function-verse.
skills.name: pathway-database-querying
skills.search_text: pathway-database-querying Use when a table of enriched int-pairs from a cell-cell interaction analysis needs functional/pathway annotation of its ligand-receptor pairs, e.g. in InterCellar's function-verse. Input is not pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow builds on CCI data generated by supported tools rather than raw scRNA-seq counts The goal is de novo pathway enrichment of a gene list rather than annotating specific interaction pairs in the function-verse http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Retrieves functional term-gene annotations from Gene Ontology (via biomaRt/Ensembl) and six pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome, Biocarta, PID:NCI-Nature, Panther, PharmGKB via graphite) so that predicted ligand-receptor interaction pairs from InterCellar's function-verse can be annotated with biological functions and pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Retrieves functional term-gene annotations from Gene Ontology (via biomaRt/Ensembl) and six pathway databases (KEGG, Reactome, Biocarta, PID:NCI-Nature, Panther, PharmGKB via graphite) so that predicted ligand-receptor interaction pairs from InterCellar's function-verse can be annotated with biological functions and pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow builds on CCI data generated by supported tools rather than raw scRNA-seq counts The goal is de novo pathway enrichment of a gene list rather than annotating specific interaction pairs in the function-verse

skills.description: Use when preparing pathway prior knowledge as input to scPAFA's fast_Ucell or fast_score_genes PAS computation, i.e., before Step1 'Calculate Pathway Activity Score'.
skills.name: pathway-dictionary-construction
skills.search_text: pathway-dictionary-construction Use when preparing pathway prior knowledge as input to scPAFA's fast_Ucell or fast_score_genes PAS computation, i.e., before Step1 'Calculate Pathway Activity Score'. The analysis goal is de novo gene module discovery without prior knowledge — scPAFA's pathway input is supervised: 'the selection of pathways is a supervised process, where using a redundant pathway set may increase the complexity of the results' Input is already an scPAFA-ready pathway dictionary of pathway name → gene list mappings The downstream tool does not accept gene-set dictionaries (e.g., methods requiring GMT pre-processing internally or sample-level expression matrices only) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Construct the Python pathway dictionary required by scPAFA: each item maps a pathway name (key) to a list of genes (values), built from public collections such as MsigDB or NCATS BioPlanet, or from a custom pathway set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Construct the Python pathway dictionary required by scPAFA: each item maps a pathway name (key) to a list of genes (values), built from public collections such as MsigDB or NCATS BioPlanet, or from a custom pathway set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is de novo gene module discovery without prior knowledge — scPAFA's pathway input is supervised: 'the selection of pathways is a supervised process, where using a redundant pathway set may increase the complexity of the results' Input is already an scPAFA-ready pathway dictionary of pathway name → gene list mappings The downstream tool does not accept gene-set dictionaries (e.g., methods requiring GMT pre-processing internally or sample-level expression matrices only)

skills.description: Use when you have trained a topic model (e.g. 100-topic scETM) on scRNA-seq data and need to show the learned topics correspond to known human gene pathways or disease gene sets via gene set enrichment analysis.
skills.name: pathway-disease-association-interpretation
skills.search_text: pathway-disease-association-interpretation Use when you have trained a topic model (e.g. 100-topic scETM) on scRNA-seq data and need to show the learned topics correspond to known human gene pathways or disease gene sets via gene set enrichment analysis. When you need de novo pathway discovery rather than testing topics against curated gene sets such as MSigDB or PsyGeNET When the model output is a cell embedding (e.g. delta/theta) and no gene-by-topic embedding matrices (rho, alpha) are available, since per-topic gene scores cannot be computed When gene sets of interest contain 5 or fewer genes, which are filtered out by the pathway-size cutoff http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Interprets scETM-learned topics by ranking genes per topic (gene embedding rho combined with topic embedding alpha) and running permutation-based GSEA against MSigDB Canonical Pathways, PsyGeNET, or similar gene sets to test whether topics map to biologically meaningful and disease-related pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Interprets scETM-learned topics by ranking genes per topic (gene embedding rho combined with topic embedding alpha) and running permutation-based GSEA against MSigDB Canonical Pathways, PsyGeNET, or similar gene sets to test whether topics map to biologically meaningful and disease-related pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need de novo pathway discovery rather than testing topics against curated gene sets such as MSigDB or PsyGeNET When the model output is a cell embedding (e.g. delta/theta) and no gene-by-topic embedding matrices (rho, alpha) are available, since per-topic gene scores cannot be computed When gene sets of interest contain 5 or fewer genes, which are filtered out by the pathway-size cutoff

skills.description: Use when you have gene subnetworks/modules partitioned from a gene regulatory network (e.g., SCING GRN modules via Leiden) and need biological annotation or disease-relevant pathway interpretation for each module.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-annotation-of-gene-modules
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-annotation-of-gene-modules Use when you have gene subnetworks/modules partitioned from a gene regulatory network (e.g., SCING GRN modules via Leiden) and need biological annotation or disease-relevant pathway interpretation for each module. Input is an unpartitioned GRN or raw expression matrix — the Leiden module partitioning (ModuleBasedDimensionalityReduction) must be run first to obtain per-module gene sets You need de novo motif/TFBS enrichment — SCING's companion steps prune edges via TFBS and conditional mutual information; this skill only queries curated pathway knowledge bases via enrichR Spatial-resolved pathway mapping is required — SCING does not explicitly utilize spatial information during network construction, so enrichment is on module gene sets, not spatial coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates gene modules (Leiden subnetworks from a SCING-inferred GRN) with biological pathways by running enrichment analysis of each module's gene set against knowledge bases such as GO Biological Process, DisGeNET, Reactome, BioCarta, and KEGG using enrichR in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Annotates gene modules (Leiden subnetworks from a SCING-inferred GRN) with biological pathways by running enrichment analysis of each module's gene set against knowledge bases such as GO Biological Process, DisGeNET, Reactome, BioCarta, and KEGG using enrichR in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an unpartitioned GRN or raw expression matrix — the Leiden module partitioning (ModuleBasedDimensionalityReduction) must be run first to obtain per-module gene sets You need de novo motif/TFBS enrichment — SCING's companion steps prune edges via TFBS and conditional mutual information; this skill only queries curated pathway knowledge bases via enrichR Spatial-resolved pathway mapping is required — SCING does not explicitly utilize spatial information during network construction, so enrichment is on module gene sets, not spatial coordinates

skills.description: Use when a CCC decomposition factor's loadings (e.g., Factor 4 from the context x interaction x sender x receiver tensor built on GSE96583/EH2259 IFN-beta PBMCs) must be biologically interpreted via pathway enrichment dotplots such as JAK-STAT across STIM vs CTRL contexts.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-dotplot-visualization
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-dotplot-visualization Use when a CCC decomposition factor's loadings (e.g., Factor 4 from the context x interaction x sender x receiver tensor built on GSE96583/EH2259 IFN-beta PBMCs) must be biologically interpreted via pathway enrichment dotplots such as JAK-STAT across STIM vs CTRL contexts. The per-sample ligand-receptor scoring or tensor assembly has not yet been done — there are no factor loadings to enrich, so build the tensor and decompose it first (rank 7 here). The goal is quantifying pathway activity in the original expression matrix rather than interpreting CCC factor loadings from a multi-context decomposition. The question concerns long-distance endocrine signalling or other signalling not represented by gene expression, which scRNA-seq-based CCC inference cannot capture. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Visualise pathway enrichment of cell-cell communication (CCC) tensor factor loadings as dotplots — e.g., the JAK-STAT enrichment dotplot for Factor 4 of the rank-7 tensor-cell2cell decomposition that separates IFN-beta-stimulated (STIM) from control (CTRL) PBMC contexts in the LIANA x tensor-cell2cell workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Visualise pathway enrichment of cell-cell communication (CCC) tensor factor loadings as dotplots — e.g., the JAK-STAT enrichment dotplot for Factor 4 of the rank-7 tensor-cell2cell decomposition that separates IFN-beta-stimulated (STIM) from control (CTRL) PBMC contexts in the LIANA x tensor-cell2cell workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The per-sample ligand-receptor scoring or tensor assembly has not yet been done — there are no factor loadings to enrich, so build the tensor and decompose it first (rank 7 here). The goal is quantifying pathway activity in the original expression matrix rather than interpreting CCC factor loadings from a multi-context decomposition. The question concerns long-distance endocrine signalling or other signalling not represented by gene expression, which scRNA-seq-based CCC inference cannot capture.

skills.description: Use when a gene-level p-value table (gene, pvalue) and a pathway database (e.g., GO BP terms of size 50-500) must be converted into coherent pathway-level enrichment scores that account for redundant/overlapping gene sets.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-estimation
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-estimation Use when a gene-level p-value table (gene, pvalue) and a pathway database (e.g., GO BP terms of size 50-500) must be converted into coherent pathway-level enrichment scores that account for redundant/overlapping gene sets. The input is already a pathway-level enrichment result and only visualization is needed (use enrichplot directly rather than re-fitting pareg). The pathway database has negligible overlap/redundancy between terms, so network regularization on inter-pathway dependencies adds no modeling benefit. No gene-to-pathway mapping or similarity matrix is available, leaving no term_network for the regularized regression. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Estimate pathway enrichment scores by regressing gene-level differential-expression p-values with pareg, a regularized generalized linear model that directly incorporates inter-pathway dependencies (e.g., Jaccard similarity) via network regularization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Estimate pathway enrichment scores by regressing gene-level differential-expression p-values with pareg, a regularized generalized linear model that directly incorporates inter-pathway dependencies (e.g., Jaccard similarity) via network regularization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a pathway-level enrichment result and only visualization is needed (use enrichplot directly rather than re-fitting pareg). The pathway database has negligible overlap/redundancy between terms, so network regularization on inter-pathway dependencies adds no modeling benefit. No gene-to-pathway mapping or similarity matrix is available, leaving no term_network for the regularized regression.

skills.description: Use when a pathway enrichment analysis must account for redundancy/dependencies between gene sets (e.g. large GO/KEGG/Reactome databases), or when benchmarking enrichment robustness to noise on synthetic pathway data.
skills.name: pathway-enrichment-regularized-regression-modeling
skills.search_text: pathway-enrichment-regularized-regression-modeling Use when a pathway enrichment analysis must account for redundancy/dependencies between gene sets (e.g. large GO/KEGG/Reactome databases), or when benchmarking enrichment robustness to noise on synthetic pathway data. When genesets are small and largely non-redundant so inter-pathway dependencies add little regularization signal When the analysis is plain over-representation analysis without per-gene p-values — pareg regresses differential expression p-values and requires them as input When no pathway similarity structure (term_network) is available and only the no-penalty pareg_noterms baseline is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply pareg, a regularized generalized linear model that incorporates inter-pathway dependencies (e.g. Jaccard similarity) via LASSO and network fusion penalties, to estimate coherent pathway enrichment scores; validated on synthetic benchmarks by sweeping network_param (η) and comparing PR-AUC across regularization variants. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Apply pareg, a regularized generalized linear model that incorporates inter-pathway dependencies (e.g. Jaccard similarity) via LASSO and network fusion penalties, to estimate coherent pathway enrichment scores; validated on synthetic benchmarks by sweeping network_param (η) and comparing PR-AUC across regularization variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When genesets are small and largely non-redundant so inter-pathway dependencies add little regularization signal When the analysis is plain over-representation analysis without per-gene p-values — pareg regresses differential expression p-values and requires them as input When no pathway similarity structure (term_network) is available and only the no-penalty pareg_noterms baseline is needed

skills.description: Use when a KEGG metabolic pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g. the four-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340) and read-count data must be aggregated per node to identify the dominant enzyme.
skills.name: pathway-flux-interpretation-from-dominant-genes
skills.search_text: pathway-flux-interpretation-from-dominant-genes Use when a KEGG metabolic pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g. the four-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340) and read-count data must be aggregated per node to identify the dominant enzyme. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP When only a single gene maps to each reaction node — node expansion and count-based prioritization add nothing When enzyme-level (isoform) activity resolution is required — KEGG does not provide curated isoform-level enzyme activity, so analysis is limited to the gene level http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Prioritize the enzyme most likely responsible for a reaction in multi-gene KEGG pathway nodes by assuming reaction activity mainly depends on the gene with the highest RNA-seq read count, then collapse all homologous genes in the node into a single aggregated measurement for differential-expression interpretation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Prioritize the enzyme most likely responsible for a reaction in multi-gene KEGG pathway nodes by assuming reaction activity mainly depends on the gene with the highest RNA-seq read count, then collapse all homologous genes in the node into a single aggregated measurement for differential-expression interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored and are excluded from FunHoP When only a single gene maps to each reaction node — node expansion and count-based prioritization add nothing When enzyme-level (isoform) activity resolution is required — KEGG does not provide curated isoform-level enzyme activity, so analysis is limited to the gene level

skills.description: Use when initializing p-scETM with trainable_gene_emb_dim set to zero, or whenever a known gene-set matrix must be size-filtered before being used as a fixed gene embedding in topic models.
skills.name: pathway-gene-matrix-filtering
skills.search_text: pathway-gene-matrix-filtering Use when initializing p-scETM with trainable_gene_emb_dim set to zero, or whenever a known gene-set matrix must be size-filtered before being used as a fixed gene embedding in topic models. When trainable_gene_emb_dim is set to a positive value, since all scRNA-seq genes are kept and no pathway-fixed gene embedding is required When the analysis is standard unregularized scETM clustering with freely learned gene embeddings ρ rather than pathway-informed topics http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Filters a pathways-by-genes binary matrix downloaded from the pathDIP4 pathway database so that only pathways containing more than 5 genes are retained, preparing the fixed gene embedding matrix ρ used by p-scETM to learn pathway-topic associations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Filters a pathways-by-genes binary matrix downloaded from the pathDIP4 pathway database so that only pathways containing more than 5 genes are retained, preparing the fixed gene embedding matrix ρ used by p-scETM to learn pathway-topic associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When trainable_gene_emb_dim is set to a positive value, since all scRNA-seq genes are kept and no pathway-fixed gene embedding is required When the analysis is standard unregularized scETM clustering with freely learned gene embeddings ρ rather than pathway-informed topics

skills.description: Use when preparing pathway gene sets (MSigDB collections, csv, or gmt files) as input to SCPA or another pathway-analysis method that expects a structured pathway table mapping pathway names to gene sets.
skills.name: pathway-geneset-formatting
skills.search_text: pathway-geneset-formatting Use when preparing pathway gene sets (MSigDB collections, csv, or gmt files) as input to SCPA or another pathway-analysis method that expects a structured pathway table mapping pathway names to gene sets. The input is already a formatted pathway table compatible with compare_pathways (no reformatting needed) The analysis goal is gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level distribution comparison, since SCPA gene sets are irrelevant there http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Format curated pathway gene sets (MSigDB Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome/GO/regulatory sets via msigdbr or csv/gmt files) into the gene-set table structure required by SCPA's compare_pathways function for single-cell pathway perturbation analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Format curated pathway gene sets (MSigDB Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome/GO/regulatory sets via msigdbr or csv/gmt files) into the gene-set table structure required by SCPA's compare_pathways function for single-cell pathway perturbation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a formatted pathway table compatible with compare_pathways (no reformatting needed) The analysis goal is gene-level differential expression rather than pathway-level distribution comparison, since SCPA gene sets are irrelevant there

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset will be analyzed with VEGA or another annotation-informed latent variable model and a GMT file of gene module membership (Reactome, MSigDB, GO, PANTHER) must be loaded to define the decoder wiring.
skills.name: pathway-gmt-gene-module-loading
skills.search_text: pathway-gmt-gene-module-loading Use when a single-cell dataset will be analyzed with VEGA or another annotation-informed latent variable model and a GMT file of gene module membership (Reactome, MSigDB, GO, PANTHER) must be loaded to define the decoder wiring. No GMT/gene annotation file is available and modules must be learned de novo rather than hard-wired from prior knowledge The gene module annotations are suspected to be incomplete or not context-specific for the dataset, since VEGA's hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge The input is raw count data not yet filtered/normalized — preprocessing must precede VEGA training, and membership loading alone does not address this http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Parse a GMT-format gene set file (e.g., Reactome pathways or MSigDB gene sets) and convert it into the gene module membership matrix that hard-wires VEGA's sparse linear decoder, connecting genes to gene module variables (GMVs) in the latent space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Parse a GMT-format gene set file (e.g., Reactome pathways or MSigDB gene sets) and convert it into the gene module membership matrix that hard-wires VEGA's sparse linear decoder, connecting genes to gene module variables (GMVs) in the latent space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No GMT/gene annotation file is available and modules must be learned de novo rather than hard-wired from prior knowledge The gene module annotations are suspected to be incomplete or not context-specific for the dataset, since VEGA's hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge The input is raw count data not yet filtered/normalized — preprocessing must precede VEGA training, and membership loading alone does not address this

skills.description: Use when a pareg fit (or an enrichment result convertible via as_enrichplot_object) must be inspected for inter-pathway structure — clustered groups of related terms — rather than only a top-N term ranking.
skills.name: pathway-network-visualization
skills.search_text: pathway-network-visualization Use when a pareg fit (or an enrichment result convertible via as_enrichplot_object) must be inspected for inter-pathway structure — clustered groups of related terms — rather than only a top-N term ranking. When only a flat top-N ranked term table is needed and no inter-pathway structure is of interest — a ranked dataframe by desc(abs(enrichment)) suffices without the network view. When the pathway database or the enriched term set is so small or sparse that no term pairs share genes (all similarities near zero), the network collapses to isolated nodes and adds no insight. When working with an enrichment result not produced by pareg and not convertible via as_enrichplot_object — the plot(fit, ...) path expects a pareg fit object. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Render pareg enrichment fits as a pathway network view, where nodes are enriched GO terms and edges are drawn between terms whose similarity (e.g. Jaccard) exceeds a threshold, to expose clustered pathway groups rather than an unstructured ranked list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Render pareg enrichment fits as a pathway network view, where nodes are enriched GO terms and edges are drawn between terms whose similarity (e.g. Jaccard) exceeds a threshold, to expose clustered pathway groups rather than an unstructured ranked list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a flat top-N ranked term table is needed and no inter-pathway structure is of interest — a ranked dataframe by desc(abs(enrichment)) suffices without the network view. When the pathway database or the enriched term set is so small or sparse that no term pairs share genes (all similarities near zero), the network collapses to isolated nodes and adds no insight. When working with an enrichment result not produced by pareg and not convertible via as_enrichplot_object — the plot(fit, ...) path expects a pareg fit object.

skills.description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes carry multiple gene names (functional homologs/OR groups) and Cytoscape/KEGGScape shows only the first gene, hiding candidate enzymes for a reaction.
skills.name: pathway-node-expansion
skills.search_text: pathway-node-expansion Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes carry multiple gene names (functional homologs/OR groups) and Cytoscape/KEGGScape shows only the first gene, hiding candidate enzymes for a reaction. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' whose reactions use 'link' entries instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or coloured in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP When the goal is collapsed, single-value node expression rather than per-gene visibility — FunHoP's aggregation step collapses all homologs in a node into one RNA-seq read-count measurement Non-human or non-metabolic KEGG pathways — the current FunHoP version supports only human metabolic pathways (with glycan exceptions) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Expands KEGG KGML pathway XML nodes containing multiple functional homologs so that every responsible gene is rendered in Cytoscape via KEGGScape, instead of only the first listed gene, by rewriting the KGML with ElementTree and reusing KEGG's protein-complex group-node solution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Expands KEGG KGML pathway XML nodes containing multiple functional homologs so that every responsible gene is rendered in Cytoscape via KEGGScape, instead of only the first listed gene, by rewriting the KGML with ElementTree and reusing KEGG's protein-complex group-node solution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' whose reactions use 'link' entries instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or coloured in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP When the goal is collapsed, single-value node expression rather than per-gene visibility — FunHoP's aggregation step collapses all homologs in a node into one RNA-seq read-count measurement Non-human or non-metabolic KEGG pathways — the current FunHoP version supports only human metabolic pathways (with glycan exceptions)

skills.description: Use when a DMC list from Illumina 450K/EPIC differential methylation analysis must be mapped to genes and tested for enriched biological pathways across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways.
skills.name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
skills.search_text: pathway-over-representation-analysis Use when a DMC list from Illumina 450K/EPIC differential methylation analysis must be mapped to genes and tested for enriched biological pathways across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways. The input is raw IDAT or normalized beta values rather than a DMC list — use methylation preprocessing/differential modules instead (beta tables feed MDS/PCA modules, not pathway enrichment) Intersections of multiple gene/region sets need visualization (e.g. Venn/UpSet) — use a dedicated tool such as Intervene rather than methylR's enrichment module http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Performs over-representation and gene-set enrichment analysis of differentially methylated CpG (DMC)-derived gene lists against KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways databases within methylR's Shiny GUI, downstream of functional (GO) analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad184

skills.description: Use when you have a matrix of perturbation gene-expression experiments and a PROGENy model, and need to test that inferred pathway activations are specific to the experimentally perturbed pathway even when that experiment is held out of model building.
skills.name: pathway-perturbation-association-testing
skills.search_text: pathway-perturbation-association-testing Use when you have a matrix of perturbation gene-expression experiments and a PROGENy model, and need to test that inferred pathway activations are specific to the experimentally perturbed pathway even when that experiment is held out of model building. Input data are not gene-expression perturbation experiments (e.g. methylation or proteomics) — PROGENy footprints were derived from ArrayExpress perturbation transcriptomics. Pathway scores are already computed and the task is only a generic correlation analysis without any experiment being held out — leave-one-out rebuilding would be pointless. Species outside human or mouse, since PROGENy signatures cover only human and mouse. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Leave-one-out validation of PROGENy pathway activity inference: for each perturbation experiment, the multivariate regression model is rebuilt with that experiment excluded, pathway scores are computed with the progeny R package, and statistical association p-values between pathway scores and perturbation conditions are assembled to test whether the model recovers the perturbed pathway it never saw. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Leave-one-out validation of PROGENy pathway activity inference: for each perturbation experiment, the multivariate regression model is rebuilt with that experiment excluded, pathway scores are computed with the progeny R package, and statistical association p-values between pathway scores and perturbation conditions are assembled to test whether the model recovers the perturbed pathway it never saw.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not gene-expression perturbation experiments (e.g. methylation or proteomics) — PROGENy footprints were derived from ArrayExpress perturbation transcriptomics. Pathway scores are already computed and the task is only a generic correlation analysis without any experiment being held out — leave-one-out rebuilding would be pointless. Species outside human or mouse, since PROGENy signatures cover only human and mouse.

skills.summary: Stratifies cell lines into quartiles of a PROGENy pathway score (e.g. MAPK) within driver-mutation groups (BRAF/KRAS/NRAS mutant vs wild-type, tracking TP53) and computes fold-changes of median drug IC50 between the pathway-active top quartile and remaining lines, to test whether pathway activity adds stratification beyond mutation status alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-sample pathway activity table with no gene-expression data to score The question is mutation-status association with drug response alone, without pathway-activity stratification Samples lack matched drug sensitivity measurements, so no IC50 fold-change can be computed

skills.search_text: pathway-topic-association-analysis Use when scRNA-seq AnnData matrices (HP, AD, MDD) with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' need direct, functionally meaningful pathway-topic interpretations without sacrificing clustering performance relative to unregularized scETM. skills.description: Use when you have per-cluster differential expression from multiple diseased scRNA-seq samples (PDX or patient) plus a tissue-specific LINCS L1000 drug reference, and you need patient-level drug recommendations and cross-cohort overlap of significant drugs.
skills.name: patient-level-drug-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: patient-level-drug-overlap-analysis Use when you have per-cluster differential expression from multiple diseased scRNA-seq samples (PDX or patient) plus a tissue-specific LINCS L1000 drug reference, and you need patient-level drug recommendations and cross-cohort overlap of significant drugs. Input is bulk-cell expression with no cell clusters or per-cluster DE lists — ASGARD's DrugScore requires multi-cluster input and bulk methods (CLUE, DrInsight) are the comparators, not the target No normal/reference tissue controls are obtainable for the disease — the article flags that substitutes must be found before patient-level scoring is meaningful Goal is single-cluster drug ranking rather than patient-level aggregation and cross-cohort overlap — GetDrug/TopDrug alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 ASGARD-based analysis that aggregates per-cluster drug rankings into a multi-cluster, patient-level DrugScore and then intersects the resulting significant drug lists across independent patient/PDX cohorts (e.g., metastatic TNBC PDX models vs. TNBC patient scRNA-seq) to identify convergent repurposing candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36637-3
skills.summary: ASGARD-based analysis that aggregates per-cluster drug rankings into a multi-cluster, patient-level DrugScore and then intersects the resulting significant drug lists across independent patient/PDX cohorts (e.g., metastatic TNBC PDX models vs. TNBC patient scRNA-seq) to identify convergent repurposing candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk-cell expression with no cell clusters or per-cluster DE lists — ASGARD's DrugScore requires multi-cluster input and bulk methods (CLUE, DrInsight) are the comparators, not the target No normal/reference tissue controls are obtainable for the disease — the article flags that substitutes must be found before patient-level scoring is meaningful Goal is single-cluster drug ranking rather than patient-level aggregation and cross-cohort overlap — GetDrug/TopDrug alone suffices

skills.description: Use when fitting a scCODA Dirichlet-Multinomial model to cell-type count data and a covariate matrix must be constructed from a formula (e.g. 'x_0') with a specified or automatically selected reference cell type.
skills.name: patsy-design-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: patsy-design-matrix-construction Use when fitting a scCODA Dirichlet-Multinomial model to cell-type count data and a covariate matrix must be constructed from a formula (e.g. 'x_0') with a specified or automatically selected reference cell type. The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data without cell-type cluster assignments — scCODA requires pre-specified, statistically sound cell-type definitions The counts are not compositional cell-type proportions (e.g. a feature/abundance table from metagenomics with a different modeling goal) Only a single covariate-free dataset with no condition annotation exists, so no patsy formula can be specified Builds the covariate (design) matrix for the scCODA compositional model by parsing a patsy-style formula applied to a compositional anndata object, while fixing the reference cell type whose effects are constrained to zero so all cell-type shifts are interpreted relative to it. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Builds the covariate (design) matrix for the scCODA compositional model by parsing a patsy-style formula applied to a compositional anndata object, while fixing the reference cell type whose effects are constrained to zero so all cell-type shifts are interpreted relative to it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data without cell-type cluster assignments — scCODA requires pre-specified, statistically sound cell-type definitions The counts are not compositional cell-type proportions (e.g. a feature/abundance table from metagenomics with a different modeling goal) Only a single covariate-free dataset with no condition annotation exists, so no patsy formula can be specified

skills.description: Use when evaluating a decomposition or clustering method (e.g., ACTIONet, cNMF, cLDA, cICA, Louvain) on synthetic scRNA-seq benchmarks with planted patterns, to measure pattern-recovery purity against generative ground truth.
skills.name: pattern-recovery-purity-evaluation
skills.search_text: pattern-recovery-purity-evaluation Use when evaluating a decomposition or clustering method (e.g., ACTIONet, cNMF, cLDA, cICA, Louvain) on synthetic scRNA-seq benchmarks with planted patterns, to measure pattern-recovery purity against generative ground truth. Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without planted ground-truth patterns — purity against generative truth is undefined; use annotation or marker-based validation instead. The goal is novel pattern discovery rather than method benchmarking — the multiresolution decomposition itself (reduce_kernel + run_ACTIONet) is the appropriate skill, not the recovery-purity evaluation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark protocol for quantifying how well a single-cell decomposition or clustering method recovers planted identity and activity patterns from synthetic scRNA-seq data, by matching recovered patterns to generative ground truth and computing pattern-recovery purity across instances and noise levels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for quantifying how well a single-cell decomposition or clustering method recovers planted identity and activity patterns from synthetic scRNA-seq data, by matching recovered patterns to generative ground truth and computing pattern-recovery purity across instances and noise levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without planted ground-truth patterns — purity against generative truth is undefined; use annotation or marker-based validation instead. The goal is novel pattern discovery rather than method benchmarking — the multiresolution decomposition itself (reduce_kernel + run_ACTIONet) is the appropriate skill, not the recovery-purity evaluation.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether gene set scores computed on sparsified/downsampled single-cell data remain discriminative between cell types, or when comparing smoothed vs non-smoothed scoring robustness.
skills.name: pbmc3k-cell-type-discrimination
skills.search_text: pbmc3k-cell-type-discrimination Use when evaluating whether gene set scores computed on sparsified/downsampled single-cell data remain discriminative between cell types, or when comparing smoothed vs non-smoothed scoring robustness. The data are bulk RNA-seq or already pseudobulked — the smoothing rationale addresses single-cell sparsity and technical noise, which bulk data do not exhibit. The goal is cell-type clustering or annotation itself rather than robustness testing of gene set scores; the workflow assumes pre-assigned Louvain groups and known B-cell labels. The AnnData lacks a neighborhood graph or grouping column (groupby='louvain') and cannot support nearest neighbor graph construction within groups. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarking workflow that quantifies how nearest neighbor graph smoothing (gssnng) makes single-cell gene set scores robust to count-matrix downsampling, using AUC of the 'B cells naive' signature to discriminate B cells from other PBMC types in the processed pbmc3k dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Benchmarking workflow that quantifies how nearest neighbor graph smoothing (gssnng) makes single-cell gene set scores robust to count-matrix downsampling, using AUC of the 'B cells naive' signature to discriminate B cells from other PBMC types in the processed pbmc3k dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk RNA-seq or already pseudobulked — the smoothing rationale addresses single-cell sparsity and technical noise, which bulk data do not exhibit. The goal is cell-type clustering or annotation itself rather than robustness testing of gene set scores; the workflow assumes pre-assigned Louvain groups and known B-cell labels. The AnnData lacks a neighborhood graph or grouping column (groupby='louvain') and cannot support nearest neighbor graph construction within groups.
