skills.name: pbmc3k-scrnaseq-data-processing
skills.search_text: pbmc3k-scrnaseq-data-processing Use when a QC-filtered PBMC3k-style scRNA-seq count matrix must be processed in SCALA/Seurat through normalization, dimensionality reduction, Louvain clustering, and per-cluster marker-gene testing with Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2. Input is scATAC-seq data — SCALA uses a separate scATAC-seq pipeline (e.g., LSI dimensionality reduction, ArchR-based BMMC workflow), not the PBMC3k scRNA-seq processing route Input is a bulk RNA-seq or precomputed feature table rather than per-cell scRNA-seq counts; cluster-level one-vs-all Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2 testing does not apply Dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA version — the article recommends the desktop version as some steps cannot be completed online http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces SCALA's scRNA-seq processing pipeline on the PBMC3k dataset: QC filtering, normalization and scaling, variable-feature detection, SVD cross-validated PCA, Seurat SNN-graph Louvain clustering, and per-cluster marker identification with the Wilcoxon rank sum test (plus MAST/DESeq2 alternatives). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Reproduces SCALA's scRNA-seq processing pipeline on the PBMC3k dataset: QC filtering, normalization and scaling, variable-feature detection, SVD cross-validated PCA, Seurat SNN-graph Louvain clustering, and per-cluster marker identification with the Wilcoxon rank sum test (plus MAST/DESeq2 alternatives).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scATAC-seq data — SCALA uses a separate scATAC-seq pipeline (e.g., LSI dimensionality reduction, ArchR-based BMMC workflow), not the PBMC3k scRNA-seq processing route Input is a bulk RNA-seq or precomputed feature table rather than per-cell scRNA-seq counts; cluster-level one-vs-all Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2 testing does not apply Dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA version — the article recommends the desktop version as some steps cannot be completed online

skills.description: Use when assessing sensitivity of trajectory inference / terminal-state detection to the dimensionality of the input PC representation, e.g. scATAC-seq (ChromVAR k-mer or TF-motif z-scores) swept across ~10–100 PCs to compare fate-detection F1 stability.
skills.name: pc-count-robustness-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pc-count-robustness-benchmarking Use when assessing sensitivity of trajectory inference / terminal-state detection to the dimensionality of the input PC representation, e.g. scATAC-seq (ChromVAR k-mer or TF-motif z-scores) swept across ~10–100 PCs to compare fate-detection F1 stability. Input is raw scATAC-seq fragment/count data rather than preprocessed TF-motif or k-mer z-score matrices with precomputed PC projections The goal is topology benchmarking on simulated toy data (e.g. dynverse/dyntoy 4-leaf or disconnected simulations) rather than PC-count sensitivity on real scATAC-seq data The comparison focuses on scalability/runtime (e.g. the 1.3-million-cell MOCA atlas) rather than fate-detection accuracy as a function of dimensionality http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmarks how terminal-state and lineage detection accuracy of trajectory inference methods (VIA vs SlingShot, Palantir, STREAM, Monocle3) degrades as the number of input principal components increases, using scATAC-seq hematopoiesis data preprocessed with TF-motif and k-mer z-score protocols. It demonstrates VIA's F1-score robustness beyond ~50 PCs where baselines degrade. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks how terminal-state and lineage detection accuracy of trajectory inference methods (VIA vs SlingShot, Palantir, STREAM, Monocle3) degrades as the number of input principal components increases, using scATAC-seq hematopoiesis data preprocessed with TF-motif and k-mer z-score protocols. It demonstrates VIA's F1-score robustness beyond ~50 PCs where baselines degrade.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scATAC-seq fragment/count data rather than preprocessed TF-motif or k-mer z-score matrices with precomputed PC projections The goal is topology benchmarking on simulated toy data (e.g. dynverse/dyntoy 4-leaf or disconnected simulations) rather than PC-count sensitivity on real scATAC-seq data The comparison focuses on scalability/runtime (e.g. the 1.3-million-cell MOCA atlas) rather than fate-detection accuracy as a function of dimensionality

skills.description: Use when evaluating how well an automatic dimension-selection criterion (RMT-based, elbow, or 95%-variance) preserves the local neighborhood structure of a scRNA-seq embedding, or when comparing PC counts across downsampled data.
skills.name: pc-count-selection-comparison
skills.search_text: pc-count-selection-comparison Use when evaluating how well an automatic dimension-selection criterion (RMT-based, elbow, or 95%-variance) preserves the local neighborhood structure of a scRNA-seq embedding, or when comparing PC counts across downsampled data. The input is already a low-dimensional embedding or feature table — no PCA/PC selection is needed The dataset is shallowly sequenced such that no deep-sequenced reference exists to build the ground-truth kNN graph The goal is clustering or cell-type annotation performance rather than local-structure (kNN-overlap) preservation Benchmark strategy from the scLENS paper for comparing how different PC-selection strategies (scLENS's RMT-based automatic selection, elbow method, 95% variance criterion) preserve local structure of scRNA-seq embeddings under downsampling, using normalized kNN-overlap scores against a reference graph. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: Benchmark strategy from the scLENS paper for comparing how different PC-selection strategies (scLENS's RMT-based automatic selection, elbow method, 95% variance criterion) preserve local structure of scRNA-seq embeddings under downsampling, using normalized kNN-overlap scores against a reference graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a low-dimensional embedding or feature table — no PCA/PC selection is needed The dataset is shallowly sequenced such that no deep-sequenced reference exists to build the ground-truth kNN graph The goal is clustering or cell-type annotation performance rather than local-structure (kNN-overlap) preservation

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized gene expression matrix (samples as columns, genes as rows) plus a module/GMT list (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK) and need sample-level module activity scores with statistical shift/overdispersion significance.
skills.name: pc1-based-geneset-shift-overdispersion-testing
skills.search_text: pc1-based-geneset-shift-overdispersion-testing Use when you have a normalized gene expression matrix (samples as columns, genes as rows) plus a module/GMT list (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK) and need sample-level module activity scores with statistical shift/overdispersion significance. Input data is raw, unnormalized counts and cannot be normalized first — rRoma explicitly works only with normalized data Datasets contain missing values that have not been imputed — the README recommends using datasets with missing values already imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback The goal is differential expression per gene rather than coordinated gene set (module) activity estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify gene set activity by computing PC1 over a gene set's expression and test whether the gene set is 'shifted' (median of sample projections) or 'over-dispersed' (L1 variance) versus random gene set nulls, using the rROMA R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Quantify gene set activity by computing PC1 over a gene set's expression and test whether the gene set is 'shifted' (median of sample projections) or 'over-dispersed' (L1 variance) versus random gene set nulls, using the rROMA R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is raw, unnormalized counts and cannot be normalized first — rRoma explicitly works only with normalized data Datasets contain missing values that have not been imputed — the README recommends using datasets with missing values already imputed rather than relying on the mice fallback The goal is differential expression per gene rather than coordinated gene set (module) activity estimation

skills.description: Use when you need sample-wise pathway/module activity scores and significance from a normalized gene expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) and a collection of gene sets (GMT/MSigDB Hallmark), to find shifted or over-dispersed modules between conditions.
skills.name: pc1-module-activity-quantification
skills.search_text: pc1-module-activity-quantification Use when you need sample-wise pathway/module activity scores and significance from a normalized gene expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) and a collection of gene sets (GMT/MSigDB Hallmark), to find shifted or over-dispersed modules between conditions. Input is raw, unnormalized count data — rRoma explicitly requires normalized matrices (cpm, vst, etc.) Expression matrix still contains many missing values that were not imputed — the README recommends using datasets with missing values already imputed The goal is differential gene expression per gene rather than coordinated module/sample-wise activity — a DE tool (edgeR/DESeq2) is the wrong lens here http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Quantify gene set (module) activity from normalized omics matrices by computing the first principal component (PC1) of the genes in each set with rROMA, an R implementation of ROMA, and testing shifted vs over-dispersed modules against a random gene set null. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Quantify gene set (module) activity from normalized omics matrices by computing the first principal component (PC1) of the genes in each set with rROMA, an R implementation of ROMA, and testing shifted vs over-dispersed modules against a random gene set null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unnormalized count data — rRoma explicitly requires normalized matrices (cpm, vst, etc.) Expression matrix still contains many missing values that were not imputed — the README recommends using datasets with missing values already imputed The goal is differential gene expression per gene rather than coordinated module/sample-wise activity — a DE tool (edgeR/DESeq2) is the wrong lens here

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix and gene sets (e.g., MSigDB GMT) and need sample-wise module activity scores with statistical significance distinguishing shifted vs overdispersed gene sets.
skills.name: pc1-variance-geneset-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: pc1-variance-geneset-activity-scoring Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix and gene sets (e.g., MSigDB GMT) and need sample-wise module activity scores with statistical significance distinguishing shifted vs overdispersed gene sets. The expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma works with normalized data — apply cpm/edgeR, vst/DESeq2, or another normalization first) The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than coordinated module activity scoring The dataset contains many missing values that have not been imputed — rROMA recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed (mice imputation is a fallback) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Quantify gene set (module) activity from a normalized omics expression matrix by computing PC1 via SVD (irlba) for each gene set, deriving the L1 statistic (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median sample projection on PC1), and testing significance against null distributions from random gene sets of matched size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Quantify gene set (module) activity from a normalized omics expression matrix by computing PC1 via SVD (irlba) for each gene set, deriving the L1 statistic (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median sample projection on PC1), and testing significance against null distributions from random gene sets of matched size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is not normalized (rRoma works with normalized data — apply cpm/edgeR, vst/DESeq2, or another normalization first) The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than coordinated module activity scoring The dataset contains many missing values that have not been imputed — rROMA recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed (mice imputation is a fallback)

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate that imputation or preprocessing improves cell-subpopulation separation in scRNA-seq count matrices, by comparing PCA-based cluster compactness of raw vs imputed data against a known ground-truth clustering.
skills.name: pca-based-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: pca-based-clustering-evaluation Use when you need to demonstrate that imputation or preprocessing improves cell-subpopulation separation in scRNA-seq count matrices, by comparing PCA-based cluster compactness of raw vs imputed data against a known ground-truth clustering. When cell-type labels are unknown and no ground-truth clustering exists to define within-cluster sum-of-squares — cluster compactness cannot be computed without labels When the goal is imputation itself rather than evaluation of its effect on clustering; use scimpute() directly instead of this evaluation wrapper When data dimensionality or nonlinearity makes two PCs a poor summary (e.g., trajectories needing time-series analysis rather than subpopulation separation) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify how well cell subpopulations separate in scRNA-seq count matrices by projecting raw and scImpute-imputed data onto the first two principal components and comparing within-cluster sum-of-squares, as done in the scImpute paper's simulated three-cell-type benchmark (within-cluster SS 94 after imputation vs 2646 for raw data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Quantify how well cell subpopulations separate in scRNA-seq count matrices by projecting raw and scImpute-imputed data onto the first two principal components and comparing within-cluster sum-of-squares, as done in the scImpute paper's simulated three-cell-type benchmark (within-cluster SS 94 after imputation vs 2646 for raw data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell-type labels are unknown and no ground-truth clustering exists to define within-cluster sum-of-squares — cluster compactness cannot be computed without labels When the goal is imputation itself rather than evaluation of its effect on clustering; use scimpute() directly instead of this evaluation wrapper When data dimensionality or nonlinearity makes two PCs a poor summary (e.g., trajectories needing time-series analysis rather than subpopulation separation)

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq pipeline must decide how many top-ranked feature genes (DUBStepR-ordered) to retain before PCA and clustering, and cell type annotations may not exist for tuning that number.
skills.name: pca-cell-embedding-feature-set-sweep
skills.search_text: pca-cell-embedding-feature-set-sweep Use when an scRNA-seq pipeline must decide how many top-ranked feature genes (DUBStepR-ordered) to retain before PCA and clustering, and cell type annotations may not exist for tuning that number. Input is already a fixed feature table or expression matrix with a predetermined feature count — no size sweep is needed Data has not been QC'd and normalized (low-quality cells discarded, reads log-normalized) as required before DUBStepR feature ordering Goal is general benchmarking of feature selection methods rather than choosing a feature set size for one DUBStepR-ordered ranking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Sweeps increasing DUBStepR-ordered feature set sizes, embedding cells in PCA space at each size to compute label-free (Density Index) and label-based (Silhouette Index) clustering-quality curves, so the optimal feature set size can be chosen without cell type labels. Grounded in the DUBStepR Nature Communications 2021 workflow (Seurat/DUBStepR, k = 10, num.pcs = 20). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Sweeps increasing DUBStepR-ordered feature set sizes, embedding cells in PCA space at each size to compute label-free (Density Index) and label-based (Silhouette Index) clustering-quality curves, so the optimal feature set size can be chosen without cell type labels. Grounded in the DUBStepR Nature Communications 2021 workflow (Seurat/DUBStepR, k = 10, num.pcs = 20).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fixed feature table or expression matrix with a predetermined feature count — no size sweep is needed Data has not been QC'd and normalized (low-quality cells discarded, reads log-normalized) as required before DUBStepR feature ordering Goal is general benchmarking of feature selection methods rather than choosing a feature set size for one DUBStepR-ordered ranking

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a denoising method preserved or recovered celltype structure in scRNA-seq data with known labels, by comparing PCA embeddings of denoised vs. ground-truth matrices.
skills.name: pca-celltype-visualization
skills.search_text: pca-celltype-visualization Use when evaluating whether a denoising method preserved or recovered celltype structure in scRNA-seq data with known labels, by comparing PCA embeddings of denoised vs. ground-truth matrices. When no ground-truth celltype labels exist (e.g., fully unsampled real data), since recovery cannot be visually or quantitatively judged — the article notes evaluating denoising is difficult because defining a ground truth for real data is challenging When the analysis goal is differential expression or trajectory inference rather than assessing celltype structure recovery after denoising http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run PCA on ground-truth, DCA-denoised, and baseline-denoised scRNA-seq count matrices and plot cells colored by known celltype labels to visually verify that a denoiser (e.g., DCA with ZINB loss) recovers the original celltype structure that an MSE-based autoencoder fails to recover in dropout data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Run PCA on ground-truth, DCA-denoised, and baseline-denoised scRNA-seq count matrices and plot cells colored by known celltype labels to visually verify that a denoiser (e.g., DCA with ZINB loss) recovers the original celltype structure that an MSE-based autoencoder fails to recover in dropout data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ground-truth celltype labels exist (e.g., fully unsampled real data), since recovery cannot be visually or quantitatively judged — the article notes evaluating denoising is difficult because defining a ground truth for real data is challenging When the analysis goal is differential expression or trajectory inference rather than assessing celltype structure recovery after denoising

skills.description: Use when you have clustered simulated (or ground-truthed) feature profiles with k-means/k-medoids and need an unsupervised confirmation that cluster assignments reflect the known simulation design before computing incorrect-assignment rates.
skills.name: pca-clustering-validation
skills.search_text: pca-clustering-validation Use when you have clustered simulated (or ground-truthed) feature profiles with k-means/k-medoids and need an unsupervised confirmation that cluster assignments reflect the known simulation design before computing incorrect-assignment rates. The data are real experimental samples with no simulated ground-truth design — PCA alignment with 'simulation settings' is then not meaningful Raw, untransformed count matrices — the log(x+1) transformation (and per-cell-type aggregation or CPM > 1 filtering) is a prerequisite in this workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A validation technique from the MOSim simulator paper: after clustering simulated multi-omics feature profiles (k-means or k-medoids), run PCA on the log(x+1)-transformed profiles to confirm that the cluster structure aligns with the simulation settings (e.g., simulated temporal patterns or cell-type/DE-group labels). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: A validation technique from the MOSim simulator paper: after clustering simulated multi-omics feature profiles (k-means or k-medoids), run PCA on the log(x+1)-transformed profiles to confirm that the cluster structure aligns with the simulation settings (e.g., simulated temporal patterns or cell-type/DE-group labels).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real experimental samples with no simulated ground-truth design — PCA alignment with 'simulation settings' is then not meaningful Raw, untransformed count matrices — the log(x+1) transformation (and per-cell-type aggregation or CPM > 1 filtering) is a prerequisite in this workflow

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a periodicity- or trajectory-based gene ranking against a linear PCA baseline on the same scRNA-seq matrix, e.g., to test whether circular pseudo-time captures cell-cycle biology better than principal components.
skills.name: pca-component-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: pca-component-gene-ranking Use when benchmarking a periodicity- or trajectory-based gene ranking against a linear PCA baseline on the same scRNA-seq matrix, e.g., to test whether circular pseudo-time captures cell-cycle biology better than principal components. Input data is not variance-normalized: PCA loadings on raw or uncentered counts are dominated by highly expressed genes, invalidating the ranking as a fair baseline (the article specifies scaled, centered log2(x+1) data). The biology of interest is not periodic/circular (e.g., simple linear differentiation trajectories): linear PCA may be an adequate representation and the comparison against a circular manifold is not informative. The goal is cell-cycle phase scoring from marker genes (e.g., Cyclone-style phase prediction) rather than ab-initio gene ranking — Cyclum's README instead recommends refine_labels for integrating external phase labels. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Rank genes by their loadings on principal components (PC1, PC2) computed on preprocessed scRNA-seq data, then use these ranked lists as linear-manifold baselines against which ab-initio circular rankings (e.g., Cyclum) are compared via GSEA enrichment of the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Rank genes by their loadings on principal components (PC1, PC2) computed on preprocessed scRNA-seq data, then use these ranked lists as linear-manifold baselines against which ab-initio circular rankings (e.g., Cyclum) are compared via GSEA enrichment of the GO:0007049 cell-cycle gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not variance-normalized: PCA loadings on raw or uncentered counts are dominated by highly expressed genes, invalidating the ranking as a fair baseline (the article specifies scaled, centered log2(x+1) data). The biology of interest is not periodic/circular (e.g., simple linear differentiation trajectories): linear PCA may be an adequate representation and the comparison against a circular manifold is not informative. The goal is cell-cycle phase scoring from marker genes (e.g., Cyclone-style phase prediction) rather than ab-initio gene ranking — Cyclum's README instead recommends refine_labels for integrating external phase labels.

skills.description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix needs dimension reduction before distance- or similarity-based steps such as scImpute's outlier-cell detection via nearest-neighbor distances.
skills.name: pca-dimension-reduction-of-count-matrices
skills.search_text: pca-dimension-reduction-of-count-matrices Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix needs dimension reduction before distance- or similarity-based steps such as scImpute's outlier-cell detection via nearest-neighbor distances. The count matrix has already been dimension-reduced or normalized into a feature/embedding table — PCA on the raw whole-genome count matrix is what scImpute recommends, since a gene filtering step is acceptable only if most genes are present The goal is imputation of dropout values without the outlier-detection pre-step, and a different distance definition (not nearest-neighbor in PC space) is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reduce a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) to its leading principal components within the scImpute workflow, retaining PCs that jointly explain a set fraction of total variance so that cell-cell distances — e.g., nearest-neighbor distances used for outlier detection — are computed in a denoised low-dimensional space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Reduce a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) to its leading principal components within the scImpute workflow, retaining PCs that jointly explain a set fraction of total variance so that cell-cell distances — e.g., nearest-neighbor distances used for outlier detection — are computed in a denoised low-dimensional space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The count matrix has already been dimension-reduced or normalized into a feature/embedding table — PCA on the raw whole-genome count matrix is what scImpute recommends, since a gene filtering step is acceptable only if most genes are present The goal is imputation of dropout values without the outlier-detection pre-step, and a different distance definition (not nearest-neighbor in PC space) is required

skills.description: Use when you have a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GSE45719, 268 mouse embryo cells) and need low-dimensional coordinates for downstream spectral clustering or comparison of imputation methods.
skills.name: pca-dimension-reduction-of-scrna-counts
skills.search_text: pca-dimension-reduction-of-scrna-counts Use when you have a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GSE45719, 268 mouse embryo cells) and need low-dimensional coordinates for downstream spectral clustering or comparison of imputation methods. Data are bulk RNA-seq profiles, where the goal is cell-to-cell transcriptomic variation rather than clustering of individual cells The downstream method requires more than two latent dimensions and the two-PC projection loses subpopulation structure needed by the analysis The count matrix has already been embedded (e.g. by ZIFA or other dimension-reduction model), making a second PCA step redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Project single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (raw or imputed by scImpute/MAGIC/SAVER) onto the first two principal components so that cell subpopulations can be clustered and benchmarked. This is the standard post-imputation dimension-reduction step in the scImpute mouse embryo evaluation workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Project single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (raw or imputed by scImpute/MAGIC/SAVER) onto the first two principal components so that cell subpopulations can be clustered and benchmarked. This is the standard post-imputation dimension-reduction step in the scImpute mouse embryo evaluation workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq profiles, where the goal is cell-to-cell transcriptomic variation rather than clustering of individual cells The downstream method requires more than two latent dimensions and the two-PC projection loses subpopulation structure needed by the analysis The count matrix has already been embedded (e.g. by ZIFA or other dimension-reduction model), making a second PCA step redundant

skills.description: Use when evaluating imputation or preprocessing effects on single-cell clustering: after obtaining a gene-by-cell matrix (raw or imputed), reduce it with 50-component PCA prior to k-means clustering and ARI computation.
skills.name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when evaluating imputation or preprocessing effects on single-cell clustering: after obtaining a gene-by-cell matrix (raw or imputed), reduce it with 50-component PCA prior to k-means clustering and ARI computation. When the analysis goal is dimensionality reduction for visualization of already-normalized feature tables rather than a controlled ARI comparison between raw and imputed data. When the dataset is small enough that full PCA is unnecessary or when a different embedding (e.g. for trajectory inference) is the target — this skill is specific to the 50-component PCA feeding k-means in the paper's benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reduces high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression matrices (raw or imputed, e.g. the Goolam E-MTAB-3321 CPM data) to 50 principal components before k-means clustering, so that clustering ARI against known cell-type labels can be computed on a denoised low-dimensional representation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Reduces high-dimensional scRNA-seq expression matrices (raw or imputed, e.g. the Goolam E-MTAB-3321 CPM data) to 50 principal components before k-means clustering, so that clustering ARI against known cell-type labels can be computed on a denoised low-dimensional representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is dimensionality reduction for visualization of already-normalized feature tables rather than a controlled ARI comparison between raw and imputed data. When the dataset is small enough that full PCA is unnecessary or when a different embedding (e.g. for trajectory inference) is the target — this skill is specific to the 50-component PCA feeding k-means in the paper's benchmark.

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-by-ontology-type score matrix (e.g. pred_Y_all from OnClassModel.Predict) or another high-dimensional per-cell feature table and need a low-dimensional embedding for clustering-quality benchmarks such as silhouette analysis.
skills.name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a cell-by-ontology-type score matrix (e.g. pred_Y_all from OnClassModel.Predict) or another high-dimensional per-cell feature table and need a low-dimensional embedding for clustering-quality benchmarks such as silhouette analysis. The goal is expression-based batch correction/integration itself — use Scanorama directly rather than PCA on OnClass scores Input is raw count expression data without OnClass predicted annotations — PCA on expression alone does not leverage Cell Ontology type scores Only two or three datasets are being compared and no cell type labels are available, since silhouette computation and the significance test require ground-truth labels Reduces high-dimensional per-cell feature matrices to a low-dimensional embedding via PCA — in this workflow, applied to the OnClass cell-by-Cell-Ontology-type score matrix (pred_Y_all) to produce an embedding whose cluster separation by cell type is scored with the silhouette coefficient and compared against Scanorama expression integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Reduces high-dimensional per-cell feature matrices to a low-dimensional embedding via PCA — in this workflow, applied to the OnClass cell-by-Cell-Ontology-type score matrix (pred_Y_all) to produce an embedding whose cluster separation by cell type is scored with the silhouette coefficient and compared against Scanorama expression integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is expression-based batch correction/integration itself — use Scanorama directly rather than PCA on OnClass scores Input is raw count expression data without OnClass predicted annotations — PCA on expression alone does not leverage Cell Ontology type scores Only two or three datasets are being compared and no cell type labels are available, since silhouette computation and the significance test require ground-truth labels

skills.description: Use when a raw single-cell counts matrix (csv/rds/h5, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be reduced to a lower-dimensional gene space before cell clustering or neural-network cell-type annotation in a cancer TME scRNA-seq pipeline.
skills.name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-for-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction-for-scrna-seq Use when a raw single-cell counts matrix (csv/rds/h5, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be reduced to a lower-dimensional gene space before cell clustering or neural-network cell-type annotation in a cancer TME scRNA-seq pipeline. skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) must be embedded into a low-dimensional PC score space so per-PC mixed models can be fit for downstream cell-type distance estimation or inference.

skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction-of-sc-rna-seq-counts Use when a high-dimensional normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) must be embedded into a low-dimensional PC score space so per-PC mixed models can be fit for downstream cell-type distance estimation or inference. The data are raw counts — the article notes scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts and recommends normalization (e.g. scTransform) first The cell population has been over-clustered — the article shows condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances, leading scDist to false negatives The goal is differential abundance rather than differential state — abundance-only tools (DA-seq, Milo, Meld) do not use expression-space PC projections http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Project a normalized single-cell RNA-seq count matrix onto top-K PCA loadings (computed via truncated SVD) to obtain low-dimensional PC scores that serve as a plug-in estimator for the projection matrix U in scDist's per-cell-type distance estimation, enabling computationally efficient mixed-model inference per PC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Project a normalized single-cell RNA-seq count matrix onto top-K PCA loadings (computed via truncated SVD) to obtain low-dimensional PC scores that serve as a plug-in estimator for the projection matrix U in scDist's per-cell-type distance estimation, enabling computationally efficient mixed-model inference per PC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw counts — the article notes scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts and recommends normalization (e.g. scTransform) first The cell population has been over-clustered — the article shows condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances, leading scDist to false negatives The goal is differential abundance rather than differential state — abundance-only tools (DA-seq, Milo, Meld) do not use expression-space PC projections

skills.name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-preprocessing
skills.search_text: pca-dimensionality-reduction-preprocessing Use when raw Tabula Muris FACS scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 00_facs_raw_data/FACS/{Tissue}-counts.csv from the Figshare deposit) must be converted into a numeric 50-PC feature matrix as input to embedding methods such as EMBEDR. Input is scATAC-seq data — the paper uses a different filter set for that modality (TSS enrichment, cells with <=200 peaks, peaks in <=10 cells), not the FACS gene/read-count thresholds Data is already normalized or already dimensionally reduced (e.g. an existing PCA or embedding matrix) — reapplying the raw-count filter/normalize/scale steps would distort the representation The dataset is non-normalized or not a Tabula Muris FACS count matrix and you intend to chain it directly into EMBEDR's null-generation process, which the paper notes has not been extended to non-normalized datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A scRNA-seq preprocessing pipeline that converts raw Tabula Muris FACS counts (e.g. Diaphragm-counts.csv) into a cell-by-50-principal-component matrix via quality filtering, library-size normalization with log transform, highly-variable-gene selection with centering/scaling, and scikit-learn PCA retaining 50 components. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: A scRNA-seq preprocessing pipeline that converts raw Tabula Muris FACS counts (e.g. Diaphragm-counts.csv) into a cell-by-50-principal-component matrix via quality filtering, library-size normalization with log transform, highly-variable-gene selection with centering/scaling, and scikit-learn PCA retaining 50 components.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scATAC-seq data — the paper uses a different filter set for that modality (TSS enrichment, cells with <=200 peaks, peaks in <=10 cells), not the FACS gene/read-count thresholds Data is already normalized or already dimensionally reduced (e.g. an existing PCA or embedding matrix) — reapplying the raw-count filter/normalize/scale steps would distort the representation The dataset is non-normalized or not a Tabula Muris FACS count matrix and you intend to chain it directly into EMBEDR's null-generation process, which the paper notes has not been extended to non-normalized datasets

This embedding feeds approximate nearest-neighbor graph construction (faiss) for Leiden clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not yet been QC-filtered and normalized (CPM 1e5 + log1p + scaling); applying PCA directly on raw counts will be dominated by library size Data is scATAC-seq peak/bin matrices where a gene activity score conversion (e.g., BinToGene) or topic modeling (cisTopic) is the article's stated alternative The goal is differential expression or functional enrichment rather than building a latent representation for clustering

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify residual batch effects after correction (e.g. ComBat on two-technical-replicate mESC data) in a linear PC space, or to build the PCA baseline needed for a sensitivity comparison against a nonlinear embedding such as BEENE.
skills.name: pca-embedding-batch-assessment
skills.search_text: pca-embedding-batch-assessment Use when you need to quantify residual batch effects after correction (e.g. ComBat on two-technical-replicate mESC data) in a linear PC space, or to build the PCA baseline needed for a sensitivity comparison against a nonlinear embedding such as BEENE. The goal is to remove/correct batch effects (e.g. running ComBat itself) rather than estimate their extent — this skill assesses mixing in an embedding downstream of correction The data have no batch variable (single batch) — kBET and iLISI require batch labels to compute rejection rates and local inverse Simpson indices The embedding under evaluation is already a nonlinear BEENE embedding — this skill defines the PCA baseline space for comparison, not the nonlinear embedding generation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes a PCA embedding of RNA-seq/single-cell data (raw or ComBat-corrected, e.g. mESC technical replicates) and quantifies residual batch effects with kBET rejection rate and iLISI. This PCA space serves as the linear baseline against which the BEENE paper shows nonlinear embeddings are more sensitive to sophisticated batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Computes a PCA embedding of RNA-seq/single-cell data (raw or ComBat-corrected, e.g. mESC technical replicates) and quantifies residual batch effects with kBET rejection rate and iLISI. This PCA space serves as the linear baseline against which the BEENE paper shows nonlinear embeddings are more sensitive to sophisticated batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to remove/correct batch effects (e.g. running ComBat itself) rather than estimate their extent — this skill assesses mixing in an embedding downstream of correction The data have no batch variable (single batch) — kBET and iLISI require batch labels to compute rejection rates and local inverse Simpson indices The embedding under evaluation is already a nonlinear BEENE embedding — this skill defines the PCA baseline space for comparison, not the nonlinear embedding generation step

skills.search_text: pca-embedding-of-trajectory-data Use when pseudotime has been inferred with redPATH's consensus Hamiltonian path algorithm and you need to detect and visualize whether the developmental trajectory is linear or branched. When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this labeling-free approach 'may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly' When the goal is simultaneous integrative analysis of proliferation and differentiation rather than trajectory visualization — the article states integrative models are preferred and the current visualization is limited When cell type labels are required as input — this approach was designed so that 'cell type labeling is not required here' http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 redPATH's trajectory visualization approach: combine multiple asymmetric Hamiltonian path solutions from the redpath() call into an N-by-N cell transition probability matrix, then apply PCA to embed cells in a low-dimensional space that exposes linear or branched developmental trends. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: redPATH's trajectory visualization approach: combine multiple asymmetric Hamiltonian path solutions from the redpath() call into an N-by-N cell transition probability matrix, then apply PCA to embed cells in a low-dimensional space that exposes linear or branched developmental trends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When pseudotime results perform poorly — the article notes this labeling-free approach 'may fail when the pseudotime results perform poorly' When the goal is simultaneous integrative analysis of proliferation and differentiation rather than trajectory visualization — the article states integrative models are preferred and the current visualization is limited When cell type labels are required as input — this approach was designed so that 'cell type labeling is not required here'

skills.description: Use when running DIEM on 10X droplet-based snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq) count data and you need to initialize k cell-type clusters via PCA and k-means before run_em debris-score estimation and call_targets filtering.
skills.name: pca-kmeans-cell-type-initialization
skills.search_text: pca-kmeans-cell-type-initialization Use when running DIEM on 10X droplet-based snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq) count data and you need to initialize k cell-type clusters via PCA and k-means before run_em debris-score estimation and call_targets filtering. It is motivated by zero-inflated negative binomial modeling that accounts for dropouts and over-dispersion, where plain PCA can distort the developmental signal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5

Input is already a dimensionality-reduced embedding or a normalized log-expression matrix prepared with a different scheme than the imputation pipeline — inconsistent normalization (e.g., skipping CPM + log10 with bias 1.01) invalidates cross-method comparison The downstream goal is differential expression or pseudotime rather than assessing cell-to-cell relationship recovery — the discussion notes no single imputation method wins across all downstream analyses The dataset has no cell type labels or clustering available, so the cell-to-cell correlation against labeled types cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Projects raw and imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., Bfimpute outputs on the Chu et al. 2016 human-ESC dataset) into PCA space and computes cell-to-cell correlations against labeled cell types to judge whether imputation recovers cell-to-cell relationships, reproducing the S1I-S1J comparison pattern. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133

skills.search_text: pca-vs-nonlinear-embedding-batch-benchmarking Use when quantifying batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq data where PCA-space metrics may miss nonlinear batch structure — e.g., comparing uncorrected vs. ComBat/Harmony-corrected data with kBET and iLISI. When the goal is batch correction itself rather than quantifying/estimating batch effect extent — BEENE estimates effects, it does not remove them When the embedding input is a high-dimensional dataset with thousands of features and no dimensionality reduction has been applied — hyperparameter guidance differs (e.g., lambda1=0.001, lambda2=5, lambda3=5 rather than 1/2/1) When a pure-Python kBET implementation is required — kBET is R-only and must be reached via rpy2 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Benchmarks batch-effect quantification on a PCA embedding versus a BEENE nonlinear autoencoder embedding, evaluating kBET rejection rates and iLISI before and after correction (e.g., ComBat, Harmony) to test whether a nonlinear embedding reflects batch effects more sensitively than PC space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Benchmarks batch-effect quantification on a PCA embedding versus a BEENE nonlinear autoencoder embedding, evaluating kBET rejection rates and iLISI before and after correction (e.g., ComBat, Harmony) to test whether a nonlinear embedding reflects batch effects more sensitively than PC space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch correction itself rather than quantifying/estimating batch effect extent — BEENE estimates effects, it does not remove them When the embedding input is a high-dimensional dataset with thousands of features and no dimensionality reduction has been applied — hyperparameter guidance differs (e.g., lambda1=0.001, lambda2=5, lambda3=5 rather than 1/2/1) When a pure-Python kBET implementation is required — kBET is R-only and must be reached via rpy2

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices show within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle activity that obscures clustering of cell types, and you need a correction before downstream clustering.
skills.name: pcabased-cellcycle-component-removal
skills.search_text: pcabased-cellcycle-component-removal Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices show within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle activity that obscures clustering of cell types, and you need a correction before downstream clustering. Data has very low cell-cycle activity — for glioblastoma data, where cell-cycle activity is known to be at a very low level, the paper uses a smaller cutoff CΔ = 2, so the default cutoff=3 is inappropriate there The dominant unwanted effect is not the cell cycle (e.g. batch/technical replicate effects) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and does not remove other confounding effects The cell-cycle effect influences too few control genes (below ~8% of control genes), where it may not be captured by the principal components and will be missed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 PCA-based identification and removal of cell-cycle principal components from single-cell RNA-Seq data using ccRemover, which bootstrap-tests whether each leading PC is enriched in cell-cycle annotated genes before removing it, preserving other biological signals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: PCA-based identification and removal of cell-cycle principal components from single-cell RNA-Seq data using ccRemover, which bootstrap-tests whether each leading PC is enriched in cell-cycle annotated genes before removing it, preserving other biological signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has very low cell-cycle activity — for glioblastoma data, where cell-cycle activity is known to be at a very low level, the paper uses a smaller cutoff CΔ = 2, so the default cutoff=3 is inappropriate there The dominant unwanted effect is not the cell cycle (e.g. batch/technical replicate effects) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and does not remove other confounding effects The cell-cycle effect influences too few control genes (below ~8% of control genes), where it may not be captured by the principal components and will be missed

When no independent whole-genome copy-number cohort (e.g., PCAWG) is available for the tumor types of interest, so coincidence cannot be tested When ecDNA calls have not yet been generated and gene-overlap annotation has not been performed upstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Intersect ecDNA-amplified genes with PCAWG copy-number-gain calls and statistically test their coincidence, providing orthogonal whole-genome validation that ATAC-Seq-derived ecDNA calls carry amplified oncogenes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0
skills.summary: Intersect ecDNA-amplified genes with PCAWG copy-number-gain calls and statistically test their coincidence, providing orthogonal whole-genome validation that ATAC-Seq-derived ecDNA calls carry amplified oncogenes.

skills.description: Use when scoring candidate gene fusions from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data for technical artifact likelihood, or when validating PCAWG fusion calls by assigning an artifact probability and filtering at a 0.5 cutoff.
skills.name: pcawg-fusion-artifact-score-validation
skills.search_text: pcawg-fusion-artifact-score-validation Use when scoring candidate gene fusions from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data for technical artifact likelihood, or when validating PCAWG fusion calls by assigning an artifact probability and filtering at a 0.5 cutoff. Input reads are 10X scRNA-seq data — scFusion and this artifact-scoring workflow target Smart-Seq data only FASTQ files are named *_1.fq — the scFusion pipeline requires the *.fastq extension and will not accept *_1.fq The mappability filter file is unavailable and a fully unfiltered candidate set is desired — omitting the UCSC file silently disables the mappability filter rather than erroring Train and validate a bi-directional LSTM (TensorFlow/Keras) artifact-scoring model, built on scFusion candidate fusion features, that distinguishes technical chimeric artifacts from real fusions, then apply it to PCAWG fusion calls to filter artifacts. Validation benchmarks on six public scRNA-seq datasets target a median ROC AUC of 0.884 and PR AUPR of 0.913. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Train and validate a bi-directional LSTM (TensorFlow/Keras) artifact-scoring model, built on scFusion candidate fusion features, that distinguishes technical chimeric artifacts from real fusions, then apply it to PCAWG fusion calls to filter artifacts. Validation benchmarks on six public scRNA-seq datasets target a median ROC AUC of 0.884 and PR AUPR of 0.913.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are 10X scRNA-seq data — scFusion and this artifact-scoring workflow target Smart-Seq data only FASTQ files are named *_1.fq — the scFusion pipeline requires the *.fastq extension and will not accept *_1.fq The mappability filter file is unavailable and a fully unfiltered candidate set is desired — omitting the UCSC file silently disables the mappability filter rather than erroring

skills.description: Use when you have a true counts matrix from SimulateTrueCounts and need observed counts that reflect a specific scRNA-seq protocol (non-UMI vs UMI), or when testing whether simulated data reproduce protocol-specific artifacts like gene length bias.
skills.name: pcr-amplification-and-fragmentation-simulation
skills.search_text: pcr-amplification-and-fragmentation-simulation Use when you have a true counts matrix from SimulateTrueCounts and need observed counts that reflect a specific scRNA-seq protocol (non-UMI vs UMI), or when testing whether simulated data reproduce protocol-specific artifacts like gene length bias. You only need true (latent) transcript counts without technical noise — use SimulateTrueCounts alone You need to model batch effects — use DivideBatches on the output of True2ObservedCounts instead, as the library-preparation pipeline itself omits reverse transcription and library cleanup steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Use SymSim's True2ObservedCounts function to convert simulated true transcript counts into observed non-UMI read counts or UMI counts, explicitly modeling capture efficiency, PCR amplification (with gene length bias via lenslope and nbins), fragmentation, and sequencing depth. This reproduces protocol-specific technical artifacts such as the gene length bias seen in full-length scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Use SymSim's True2ObservedCounts function to convert simulated true transcript counts into observed non-UMI read counts or UMI counts, explicitly modeling capture efficiency, PCR amplification (with gene length bias via lenslope and nbins), fragmentation, and sequencing depth. This reproduces protocol-specific technical artifacts such as the gene length bias seen in full-length scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need true (latent) transcript counts without technical noise — use SimulateTrueCounts alone You need to model batch effects — use DivideBatches on the output of True2ObservedCounts instead, as the library-preparation pipeline itself omits reverse transcription and library cleanup steps

skills.description: Use when quantifying isoform expression from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore reads where PCR amplification scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate UMIs under high sequencing error.
skills.name: pcr-amplification-fold-quantification
skills.search_text: pcr-amplification-fold-quantification Use when quantifying isoform expression from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore reads where PCR amplification scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate UMIs under high sequencing error. When input reads are short Illumina reads with low per-base error, where UMI collapse by fixed edit distance suffices and the r-based pruning tail assumption is unnecessary When UMI sequences are whitelist-anchored like cell barcodes; UMIs are shorter and randomly generated, so the skill's error model (estimated from 12mer adapter Needleman-Wunsch scores) assumes no UMI whitelist is available When the goal is consensus alignment correction or isoform discovery rather than correcting amplification-scattered UMI counts — the pipeline handles those in separate steps Adaptive UMI cluster-size pruning in Longcell that corrects PCR amplification scattering in Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification by removing error-driven small clusters from the left tail of each within-isoform cluster-size distribution, with stability validated against GC-dependent amplification folds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Adaptive UMI cluster-size pruning in Longcell that corrects PCR amplification scattering in Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification by removing error-driven small clusters from the left tail of each within-isoform cluster-size distribution, with stability validated against GC-dependent amplification folds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When input reads are short Illumina reads with low per-base error, where UMI collapse by fixed edit distance suffices and the r-based pruning tail assumption is unnecessary When UMI sequences are whitelist-anchored like cell barcodes; UMIs are shorter and randomly generated, so the skill's error model (estimated from 12mer adapter Needleman-Wunsch scores) assumes no UMI whitelist is available When the goal is consensus alignment correction or isoform discovery rather than correcting amplification-scattered UMI counts — the pipeline handles those in separate steps

skills.description: Use when converting aligned 10x droplet scRNA-seq reads (Read1/cDNA insert aligned with STAR, MAPQ=255) into a per-cell UMI count matrix and PCR duplicates must be removed before counting.
skills.name: pcr-duplicate-marking-by-barcode-umi-gene
skills.search_text: pcr-duplicate-marking-by-barcode-umi-gene Use when converting aligned 10x droplet scRNA-seq reads (Read1/cDNA insert aligned with STAR, MAPQ=255) into a per-cell UMI count matrix and PCR duplicates must be removed before counting. Input is already a gene-cell UMI count matrix or feature table — duplicate marking has already been applied upstream by Cell Ranger Sequencing data are not from a 10x/GemCode droplet 3' assay with cell barcode + UMI read structure (e.g. full-length plate-based scRNA-seq without UMIs) Downstream analysis such as SNV calling or chimerism inference where read-level rather than molecule-level information is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Marks and removes PCR duplicates from 10x Genomics single-cell 3' reads by collapsing reads sharing the same (cell barcode, UMI, gene ID) tuple, so that only confidently mapped, non-duplicate reads with valid barcodes and UMIs contribute to the gene-barcode count matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Marks and removes PCR duplicates from 10x Genomics single-cell 3' reads by collapsing reads sharing the same (cell barcode, UMI, gene ID) tuple, so that only confidently mapped, non-duplicate reads with valid barcodes and UMIs contribute to the gene-barcode count matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-cell UMI count matrix or feature table — duplicate marking has already been applied upstream by Cell Ranger Sequencing data are not from a 10x/GemCode droplet 3' assay with cell barcode + UMI read structure (e.g. full-length plate-based scRNA-seq without UMIs) Downstream analysis such as SNV calling or chimerism inference where read-level rather than molecule-level information is required

skills.description: Use when building or validating a dataset inventory table from pdacR's parsed .rds objects (e.g. verifying Table 1's 13-dataset compendium), or when auditing sample/feature counts and Used flags for PDAC transcriptomic datasets before analysis.

skills.search_text: pdac-dataset-inventory-curation Use when building or validating a dataset inventory table from pdacR's parsed .rds objects (e.g. verifying Table 1's 13-dataset compendium), or when auditing sample/feature counts and Used flags for PDAC transcriptomic datasets before analysis. You need single-cell analyses — the scRNA atlas (rmoffitt/scOh) is distributed separately and its computational burden is 'beyond the scope of a responsive GUI'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the pdacR Table 1 compendium inventory by programmatically extracting platform type, sample description, sample/feature counts, and Used flags from the thirteen parsed PDAC datasets stored in the pdacR R package, with the known TCGA-PAAD whitelist correction (150 of 182 samples histologically confirmed PDAC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Reproduces the pdacR Table 1 compendium inventory by programmatically extracting platform type, sample description, sample/feature counts, and Used flags from the thirteen parsed PDAC datasets stored in the pdacR R package, with the known TCGA-PAAD whitelist correction (150 of 182 samples histologically confirmed PDAC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You intend to merge or aggregate datasets across the microarray and bulk RNA-seq platforms — the article states aggregation was removed because 'aggregation introduced more problems than it solved' and cross-platform merging is not robust. skills.description: Use when loading a public PDAC bulk expression dataset (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) from pdacR and the analysis requires only histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma samples; triggered by sample counts exceeding the whitelisted PDAC set or known contamination by non-PDAC tumors.
skills.name: pdac-dataset-sample-filtering
skills.search_text: pdac-dataset-sample-filtering Use when loading a public PDAC bulk expression dataset (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) from pdacR and the analysis requires only histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma samples; triggered by sample counts exceeding the whitelisted PDAC set or known contamination by non-PDAC tumors. The dataset has already been curated to histologically confirmed PDAC samples only (no non-PDAC labels remain in any sample track). The goal is to analyze non-adenocarcinoma samples present in the original repository data rather than tumor-cell-specific signatures. Analysis targets single-cell data (e.g. the rmoffitt/scOh atlas), which is outside pdacR's bulk-dataset filtering workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies the pdacR 'Filter samples by' mechanism to remove non-adenocarcinoma and low-purity cases from public PDAC transcriptomic datasets before downstream subtyping or signature analysis. This is essential because, e.g., TCGA-PAAD ships 182 mRNA samples of which only 150 are histologically confirmed PDAC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Applies the pdacR 'Filter samples by' mechanism to remove non-adenocarcinoma and low-purity cases from public PDAC transcriptomic datasets before downstream subtyping or signature analysis. This is essential because, e.g., TCGA-PAAD ships 182 mRNA samples of which only 150 are histologically confirmed PDAC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has already been curated to histologically confirmed PDAC samples only (no non-PDAC labels remain in any sample track). The goal is to analyze non-adenocarcinoma samples present in the original repository data rather than tumor-cell-specific signatures. Analysis targets single-cell data (e.g. the rmoffitt/scOh atlas), which is outside pdacR's bulk-dataset filtering workflow.

skills.description: Use when a bulk PDAC expression matrix (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) needs sample-level subtype calls under one or more of the Moffitt, Collisson, or Bailey schemas, or when comparing subtype assignments across these classification systems.
skills.name: pdac-subtype-classification
skills.search_text: pdac-subtype-classification Use when a bulk PDAC expression matrix (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) needs sample-level subtype calls under one or more of the Moffitt, Collisson, or Bailey schemas, or when comparing subtype assignments across these classification systems. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use the rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas instead; bulk signatures assume tumor/TME mixture of bulk samples The expression cohort contains non-PDAC samples (e.g. the 32 non-whitelist TCGA-PAAD samples) — these must be removed first or subtype calls and signature specificity are compromised Goal is single-sample clinical subtyping rather than cluster-based cohort analysis — the PurIST classifier in pdacR is the dedicated single-sample classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Classifies PDAC bulk tumor expression samples into the Moffitt basal-like/classical, Collisson classical/QM, and Bailey progenitor/squamous subtypes using curated SYMBOL-level gene signatures from the pdacR package, and quantifies cross-schema concordance (expected ~60% overlap between analogous subtype calls). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Classifies PDAC bulk tumor expression samples into the Moffitt basal-like/classical, Collisson classical/QM, and Bailey progenitor/squamous subtypes using curated SYMBOL-level gene signatures from the pdacR package, and quantifies cross-schema concordance (expected ~60% overlap between analogous subtype calls).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data — use the rmoffitt/scOh single-cell atlas instead; bulk signatures assume tumor/TME mixture of bulk samples The expression cohort contains non-PDAC samples (e.g. the 32 non-whitelist TCGA-PAAD samples) — these must be removed first or subtype calls and signature specificity are compromised Goal is single-sample clinical subtyping rather than cluster-based cohort analysis — the PurIST classifier in pdacR is the dedicated single-sample classifier

skills.description: Use when a PDAC transcriptomic analysis needs to check whether a subtype gene signature (Collisson Exocrine, Bailey ADEX, etc.) actually tracks tumor cellularity rather than tumor-intrinsic biology, using pdacR datasets with purity or VAF metadata.
skills.name: pdac-subtype-geneset-interpretation
skills.search_text: pdac-subtype-geneset-interpretation Use when a PDAC transcriptomic analysis needs to check whether a subtype gene signature (Collisson Exocrine, Bailey ADEX, etc.) actually tracks tumor cellularity rather than tumor-intrinsic biology, using pdacR datasets with purity or VAF metadata. The analysis goal is tumor-intrinsic subtype classification (e.g. PurIST) rather than testing whether a signature tracks sample purity/cellularity The dataset is single-cell RNA-seq (use the rmoffitt/scOh atlas instead); the article notes bulk datasets 'are limited in our ability to fully separate cellular populations' Samples have not been filtered to histologically confirmed PDAC (e.g. the 32 non-PDAC TCGA-PAAD samples), which would confound the signature-purity association http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores a curated PDAC subtype gene signature (e.g. Collisson Exocrine or Bailey ADEX) per sample in pdacR datasets and tests its Spearman correlation with a tumor purity/cellularity proxy (ABSOLUTE purity or predicted mean VAF), establishing whether the signature marks low-purity, non-tumor-heavy bulk samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Scores a curated PDAC subtype gene signature (e.g. Collisson Exocrine or Bailey ADEX) per sample in pdacR datasets and tests its Spearman correlation with a tumor purity/cellularity proxy (ABSOLUTE purity or predicted mean VAF), establishing whether the signature marks low-purity, non-tumor-heavy bulk samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is tumor-intrinsic subtype classification (e.g. PurIST) rather than testing whether a signature tracks sample purity/cellularity The dataset is single-cell RNA-seq (use the rmoffitt/scOh atlas instead); the article notes bulk datasets 'are limited in our ability to fully separate cellular populations' Samples have not been filtered to histologically confirmed PDAC (e.g. the 32 non-PDAC TCGA-PAAD samples), which would confound the signature-purity association

skills.description: Use when comparing curated PDAC subtype signatures across matched/paired samples (primary vs metastatic vs cell line) or platforms (RNAseq vs microarray) to quantify signature retention or loss.
skills.name: pdac-subtype-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: pdac-subtype-signature-scoring Use when comparing curated PDAC subtype signatures across matched/paired samples (primary vs metastatic vs cell line) or platforms (RNAseq vs microarray) to quantify signature retention or loss. When the goal is assigning individual tumors to a subtype rather than scoring signature retention/loss across paired samples — use the PurIST single-sample classifier instead When the input is single-cell data: pdacR datasets are bulk transcriptomics and the companion scOh atlas (rmoffitt/scOh) is a separate resource without a gene-set scoring web interface When trying to merge or batch-correct across many platforms: the article notes the inability to robustly merge datasets across platforms and compositions, so comparisons are done within each platform separately http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores PDAC subtype gene signatures (e.g., Bailey ADEX, Bailey Immunogenic, Collisson Exocrine) by per-sample z-scoring of signature genes and computing mean-centered gene set scores, to test whether signatures are retained or lost across paired primary tumors, metastases, and derived cell lines in the pdacR-curated PACA-AU datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Scores PDAC subtype gene signatures (e.g., Bailey ADEX, Bailey Immunogenic, Collisson Exocrine) by per-sample z-scoring of signature genes and computing mean-centered gene set scores, to test whether signatures are retained or lost across paired primary tumors, metastases, and derived cell lines in the pdacR-curated PACA-AU datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is assigning individual tumors to a subtype rather than scoring signature retention/loss across paired samples — use the PurIST single-sample classifier instead When the input is single-cell data: pdacR datasets are bulk transcriptomics and the companion scOh atlas (rmoffitt/scOh) is a separate resource without a gene-set scoring web interface When trying to merge or batch-correct across many platforms: the article notes the inability to robustly merge datasets across platforms and compositions, so comparisons are done within each platform separately
