skills.name: pdx-model-identifier-mapping
skills.search_text: pdx-model-identifier-mapping Use when pre-clinical CRC cohorts (PDX or cell line) have CMS predictions from CMScaller and independently annotated drug-response labels that must be joined on sample/model identifiers before testing subtype-response associations. Sample is a metastatic CRC biopsy or other tissue with a different human stromal component than primary CRCs — CMScaller predictions feeding the mapping are not recommended for such samples Gene expression dataset is very small (fewer than ~40 samples), where centering/scaling of inputs introduces prediction uncertainty in the CMS labels being mapped The data are single-cell RNA-sequencing, which is exceedingly noisy and outside CMScaller's intended scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps pre-clinical colorectal cancer model identifiers (PDX and cell line sample IDs) to their CMScaller CMS class labels and external drug-response annotations via ID joins, enabling contingency-table analyses of CMS2 vs non-CMS2 response to cetuximab across cohorts such as Gao PDXs, Isella GSE76402, and Medle/Binter cell lines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Maps pre-clinical colorectal cancer model identifiers (PDX and cell line sample IDs) to their CMScaller CMS class labels and external drug-response annotations via ID joins, enabling contingency-table analyses of CMS2 vs non-CMS2 response to cetuximab across cohorts such as Gao PDXs, Isella GSE76402, and Medle/Binter cell lines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample is a metastatic CRC biopsy or other tissue with a different human stromal component than primary CRCs — CMScaller predictions feeding the mapping are not recommended for such samples Gene expression dataset is very small (fewer than ~40 samples), where centering/scaling of inputs introduces prediction uncertainty in the CMS labels being mapped The data are single-cell RNA-sequencing, which is exceedingly noisy and outside CMScaller's intended scope

skills.description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq multiomic AnnData objects before GrID-Net-style causal inference, to define the bounded set of peak-gene pairs that will be scored.
skills.name: peak-gene-candidate-pair-filtering
skills.search_text: peak-gene-candidate-pair-filtering Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq multiomic AnnData objects before GrID-Net-style causal inference, to define the bounded set of peak-gene pairs that will be scored. The AnnData objects lack TSS or peak-coordinate annotations in adata.var, so genomic distance cannot be computed The goal is all-vs-all gene regulatory inference without genomic proximity constraints (pair filtering by 1 Mb TSS distance would be inappropriate) The data are not paired multimodal single-cell measurements of the same cells (e.g. bulk ATAC + bulk RNA) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Assemble and filter the candidate peak-gene pair universe for causal regulatory inference from single-cell multimodal RNA+ATAC data, by removing genes expressed in <1% of cells, peaks accessible in <0.1% of cells, and restricting pairs to peaks within 1 Mb (250 kb for 10x Multiome) of a gene's TSS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Assemble and filter the candidate peak-gene pair universe for causal regulatory inference from single-cell multimodal RNA+ATAC data, by removing genes expressed in <1% of cells, peaks accessible in <0.1% of cells, and restricting pairs to peaks within 1 Mb (250 kb for 10x Multiome) of a gene's TSS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData objects lack TSS or peak-coordinate annotations in adata.var, so genomic distance cannot be computed The goal is all-vs-all gene regulatory inference without genomic proximity constraints (pair filtering by 1 Mb TSS distance would be inappropriate) The data are not paired multimodal single-cell measurements of the same cells (e.g. bulk ATAC + bulk RNA)

skills.description: Use when you have GrID-Net peak-gene results plus correlation-method rankings and want to show that causally-prioritized pairs are biologically distinct, e.g., enriched for poised enhancers.
skills.name: peak-gene-pair-differential-prioritization
skills.search_text: peak-gene-pair-differential-prioritization Use when you have GrID-Net peak-gene results plus correlation-method rankings and want to show that causally-prioritized pairs are biologically distinct, e.g., enriched for poised enhancers. No matched ChIP-seq (H3K4me1/H3K27ac) data exists for the relevant cell type, so enhancer-state annotation cannot be performed The goal is causal link discovery itself rather than benchmarking GrID-Net against correlation methods The dataset is not a dynamic process with pseudotemporal context — GrID-Net requires multiomic data from a dynamic process such as differentiation to build the cell-state DAG http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identifies peak-gene pairs differentially prioritized by GrID-Net's Granger causal inference relative to correlation-based baseline methods, then tests whether GrID-Net-specific pairs carry chromatin-priming signatures (poised H3K4me1-only vs active H3K4me1+H3K27ac enhancers). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Identifies peak-gene pairs differentially prioritized by GrID-Net's Granger causal inference relative to correlation-based baseline methods, then tests whether GrID-Net-specific pairs carry chromatin-priming signatures (poised H3K4me1-only vs active H3K4me1+H3K27ac enhancers).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched ChIP-seq (H3K4me1/H3K27ac) data exists for the relevant cell type, so enhancer-state annotation cannot be performed The goal is causal link discovery itself rather than benchmarking GrID-Net against correlation methods The dataset is not a dynamic process with pseudotemporal context — GrID-Net requires multiomic data from a dynamic process such as differentiation to build the cell-state DAG

skills.description: Use when comparing computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as cell counts scale, or when you need to extrapolate MaCroDNA runtime to datasets larger than the measured ones.
skills.name: peak-memory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: peak-memory-benchmarking Use when comparing computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as cell counts scale, or when you need to extrapolate MaCroDNA runtime to datasets larger than the measured ones. You need assignment accuracy or clonal-prevalence evaluation rather than computational-cost scaling — use the cell-to-clone accuracy benchmark instead The dataset has no per-patient structure or ground truth clusters (e.g. the BE dataset), so intNMF-based sampling of comparable cell counts is not possible Your method is not invoked via a single dominating solve step (MaCroDNA's Gurobi MIP dominates timing), so wall-clock timing around the whole call will not attribute cost correctly Benchmark wall-clock runtime and peak memory of MaCroDNA against clonealign and Seurat as input size scales, by sampling the CRC scDNA/scRNA data at fractions lambda = 0.5–1.0, timing each Gurobi-driven cell2cell_assignment() call, and extrapolating runtime with a linear regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Benchmark wall-clock runtime and peak memory of MaCroDNA against clonealign and Seurat as input size scales, by sampling the CRC scDNA/scRNA data at fractions lambda = 0.5–1.0, timing each Gurobi-driven cell2cell_assignment() call, and extrapolating runtime with a linear regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need assignment accuracy or clonal-prevalence evaluation rather than computational-cost scaling — use the cell-to-clone accuracy benchmark instead The dataset has no per-patient structure or ground truth clusters (e.g. the BE dataset), so intNMF-based sampling of comparable cell counts is not possible Your method is not invoked via a single dominating solve step (MaCroDNA's Gurobi MIP dominates timing), so wall-clock timing around the whole call will not attribute cost correctly

skills.description: Use when two alternative matrix-decomposition or joint-dimensionality-reduction implementations must be compared for computational efficiency on the same scenario, and runtime, memory, and rank-selection agreement are the metrics of interest.
skills.name: peak-memory-profiling-of-decomposition-runs
skills.search_text: peak-memory-profiling-of-decomposition-runs Use when two alternative matrix-decomposition or joint-dimensionality-reduction implementations must be compared for computational efficiency on the same scenario, and runtime, memory, and rank-selection agreement are the metrics of interest. The goal is statistical accuracy or batch-effect correction quality rather than computational cost — use downstream benchmarking against tools like Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, or ComBat-seq instead The implementations cannot be run on identical input data, making runtime and memory measurements incomparable The analysis targets small datasets where JIVE's original implementation is tractable, so profiling overhead adds little value http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks matrix-decomposition implementations (e.g., AJIVE from the Python mvdr library vs the R r.jive jive() function) on identical multi-view input by recording wall-clock runtime, peak memory usage, and the selected joint rank, enabling head-to-head computational comparisons such as the reported ~18 s / 601 MB vs ~2 h / 1180 MB result. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Benchmarks matrix-decomposition implementations (e.g., AJIVE from the Python mvdr library vs the R r.jive jive() function) on identical multi-view input by recording wall-clock runtime, peak memory usage, and the selected joint rank, enabling head-to-head computational comparisons such as the reported ~18 s / 601 MB vs ~2 h / 1180 MB result.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is statistical accuracy or batch-effect correction quality rather than computational cost — use downstream benchmarking against tools like Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, or ComBat-seq instead The implementations cannot be run on identical input data, making runtime and memory measurements incomparable The analysis targets small datasets where JIVE's original implementation is tractable, so profiling overhead adds little value

skills.description: Use when benchmarking manifold alignment or single-cell integration methods for scalability, specifically to compare peak memory demand and runtime across multiple methods on the same datasets.
skills.name: peak-memory-usage-measurement
skills.search_text: peak-memory-usage-measurement Use when benchmarking manifold alignment or single-cell integration methods for scalability, specifically to compare peak memory demand and runtime across multiple methods on the same datasets. The goal is to assess alignment quality (e.g. label transfer accuracy or topology preservation) rather than computational cost — use the alignment benchmarking workflow instead. Datasets lack overlapping-free single-modality structure or are not the pre-processed PBMC/BM inputs, making runtime/memory comparisons against the paper's baselines not directly interpretable. Profiles peak memory usage (and total runtime) of manifold alignment methods — scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT — across the Full PBMC, Partial PBMC, and BM single-cell datasets to reproduce the computational resource comparison in Supplementary Table S1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Profiles peak memory usage (and total runtime) of manifold alignment methods — scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT — across the Full PBMC, Partial PBMC, and BM single-cell datasets to reproduce the computational resource comparison in Supplementary Table S1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to assess alignment quality (e.g. label transfer accuracy or topology preservation) rather than computational cost — use the alignment benchmarking workflow instead. Datasets lack overlapping-free single-modality structure or are not the pre-processed PBMC/BM inputs, making runtime/memory comparisons against the paper's baselines not directly interpretable.

skills.description: Use when integrating scATAC (peaks) with transcriptomic modalities (scRNA/smFISH) in scConfluence: chromatin peaks must first be converted to gene activity scores to build the cross-modality common features matrix before computing the correlation-based cost matrix.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-activity-conversion
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-activity-conversion Use when integrating scATAC (peaks) with transcriptomic modalities (scRNA/smFISH) in scConfluence: chromatin peaks must first be converted to gene activity scores to build the cross-modality common features matrix before computing the correlation-based cost matrix. When the modality pair has no weakly connected features (e.g., electrophysiology vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on cross-modality feature connections When the scATAC data is already provided as gene activity scores (e.g., the Open problems Multiome dataset, where gene activities were already computed by the authors with Signac) When doing paired/multiomic integration on the same cells; scConfluence targets unpaired (diagonal) integration http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Converts scATAC chromatin peak measurements into gene-level activity scores (e.g., with Signac) so that scATAC cells can be compared on shared gene features with scRNA/smFISH cells, enabling scConfluence's cross-modality common features matrix Y and correlation-based biological cost matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Converts scATAC chromatin peak measurements into gene-level activity scores (e.g., with Signac) so that scATAC cells can be compared on shared gene features with scRNA/smFISH cells, enabling scConfluence's cross-modality common features matrix Y and correlation-based biological cost matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the modality pair has no weakly connected features (e.g., electrophysiology vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on cross-modality feature connections When the scATAC data is already provided as gene activity scores (e.g., the Open problems Multiome dataset, where gene activities were already computed by the authors with Signac) When doing paired/multiomic integration on the same cells; scConfluence targets unpaired (diagonal) integration

skills.description: Use when building an enhancer-based GRN from paired snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq co-embedded cells and you need to restrict candidate genes to those both variable along pseudotime and linkable to at least one peak.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-association-filtering
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-association-filtering Use when building an enhancer-based GRN from paired snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq co-embedded cells and you need to restrict candidate genes to those both variable along pseudotime and linkable to at least one peak. Cells are unpaired or not co-embedded (no CCA/Harmony coembedding), since gene–peak association requires paired RNA/ATAC cells No pseudotime trajectory has been defined — variation-along-pseudotime filtering is meaningless on unordered clusters You need genome-wide enhancer–promoter links rather than trajectory-specific candidate genes for GRN seeding http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 scMEGA-style filtering that links candidate genes to at least one accessible ATAC peak and retains only genes whose expression varies along pseudotime, producing the trajectory-relevant enhancer–gene set used as GRN input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: scMEGA-style filtering that links candidate genes to at least one accessible ATAC peak and retains only genes whose expression varies along pseudotime, producing the trajectory-relevant enhancer–gene set used as GRN input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are unpaired or not co-embedded (no CCA/Harmony coembedding), since gene–peak association requires paired RNA/ATAC cells No pseudotime trajectory has been defined — variation-along-pseudotime filtering is meaningless on unordered clusters You need genome-wide enhancer–promoter links rather than trajectory-specific candidate genes for GRN seeding

skills.description: Use when building an enhancer-based gene regulatory network from single-cell multiome data, where candidate TF–gene pairs must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif binding in linked peaks.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-linkage-integration
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-linkage-integration Use when building an enhancer-based gene regulatory network from single-cell multiome data, where candidate TF–gene pairs must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif binding in linked peaks. Inputs lack a peak-to-gene link table or motif occurrence matrix — correlation-only TF–gene inference cannot satisfy the enhancer-based retention rule The goal is cell-level TF activity scoring rather than network assembly — RunChromVAR deviation scores alone are the appropriate earlier step http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Assembles scMEGA's enhancer-based GRN (eGRN) by intersecting peak-to-gene links with a TF–gene correlation table and a motif-matching matrix: a TF–gene edge is retained only when the gene has at least one linked enhancer and that enhancer is bound by the TF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Assembles scMEGA's enhancer-based GRN (eGRN) by intersecting peak-to-gene links with a TF–gene correlation table and a motif-matching matrix: a TF–gene edge is retained only when the gene has at least one linked enhancer and that enhancer is bound by the TF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inputs lack a peak-to-gene link table or motif occurrence matrix — correlation-only TF–gene inference cannot satisfy the enhancer-based retention rule The goal is cell-level TF activity scoring rather than network assembly — RunChromVAR deviation scores alone are the appropriate earlier step

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC multiome) cells ordered along a trajectory and need enhancer-to-promoter links to constrain TF-gene edges in an eGRN.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-linking-from-multiome-data
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-linking-from-multiome-data Use when you have paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC multiome) cells ordered along a trajectory and need enhancer-to-promoter links to constrain TF-gene edges in an eGRN. Input is unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq from separate cells without a cell-pairing step (PairCells/CreatePairedObject) — linking along a shared trajectory first requires paired or pseudo-paired modalities You only have scRNA-seq or only scATAC-seq data — no peak accessibility/gene expression pairing is possible The goal is bulk or non-trajectory GRN inference where enhancer-to-promoter links along pseudotime are not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Correlates peak accessibility (scATAC-seq) with gene expression (scRNA-seq) along a pseudotime trajectory in single-cell multiome data to define enhancer-to-promoter (peak-to-gene) links that support enhancer-based gene regulatory network inference with scMEGA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Correlates peak accessibility (scATAC-seq) with gene expression (scRNA-seq) along a pseudotime trajectory in single-cell multiome data to define enhancer-to-promoter (peak-to-gene) links that support enhancer-based gene regulatory network inference with scMEGA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq from separate cells without a cell-pairing step (PairCells/CreatePairedObject) — linking along a shared trajectory first requires paired or pseudo-paired modalities You only have scRNA-seq or only scATAC-seq data — no peak accessibility/gene expression pairing is possible The goal is bulk or non-trajectory GRN inference where enhancer-to-promoter links along pseudotime are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have scATAC-seq data (e.g. Cusanovich 2018 Spleen, GSE111586) plus a TF motif catalogue and need to filter out non-relevant TFs and build a per-target-gene candidate TF pool (base GRN parquet) for downstream logic-gate GRN inference.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-regulatory-linking
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-regulatory-linking Use when you have scATAC-seq data (e.g. Cusanovich 2018 Spleen, GSE111586) plus a TF motif catalogue and need to filter out non-relevant TFs and build a per-target-gene candidate TF pool (base GRN parquet) for downstream logic-gate GRN inference. scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs — do not use this base-GRN pipeline for large-scale inference from scratch without external hints No scATAC-seq or motif data are available for the tissue/cell-type context — the base GRN cannot be built and scGATE should be run with base_GRN = NA The goal is pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or modeling temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle this You expect to decode Boolean logic among more than 5 TFs per target — overfitting is a major concern and this candidate-pool construction supports subsets of up to k=5 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs a scATAC-seq-derived base gene regulatory network: accessible chromatin peaks passing co-accessibility and TSS-proximity criteria are scanned for TF DNA binding motifs and linked to nearby target genes, producing a peak-based TF–gene candidate table (parquet) that scGATE consumes as its refined candidate TF pool per target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Reconstructs a scATAC-seq-derived base gene regulatory network: accessible chromatin peaks passing co-accessibility and TSS-proximity criteria are scanned for TF DNA binding motifs and linked to nearby target genes, producing a peak-based TF–gene candidate table (parquet) that scGATE consumes as its refined candidate TF pool per target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs — do not use this base-GRN pipeline for large-scale inference from scratch without external hints No scATAC-seq or motif data are available for the tissue/cell-type context — the base GRN cannot be built and scGATE should be run with base_GRN = NA The goal is pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories or modeling temporal delays — scGATE does not yet handle this You expect to decode Boolean logic among more than 5 TFs per target — overfitting is a major concern and this candidate-pool construction supports subsets of up to k=5

skills.description: Use when MACS-called peaks from a 10x Chromium-like BAM must be filtered to gene-associated candidates — same strand as a gene and within a maximum distance — before designating 3' UTRs.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-strand-distance-matching
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-strand-distance-matching Use when MACS-called peaks from a 10x Chromium-like BAM must be filtered to gene-associated candidates — same strand as a gene and within a maximum distance — before designating 3' UTRs. The BAM comes from a protocol where signal is not concentrated at the distal ends of 3' or 5' UTRs, so strand/distance-matched peaks will not correspond to UTR ends. The goal is de novo peak calling or general ChIP/RIP peak analysis rather than annotating 3' UTRs against a canonical GFF/GTF. Pre-existing 3' UTR annotations are already complete and must neither be extended nor overridden by new peak-based calls. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Filter stage of peaks2utr in which MACS3-called broad peaks of significant read coverage are matched to gene models (GFF/GTF) on the same strand within a user-defined maximum distance; only passing peaks are designated novel 3' UTRs and truncated at SPAT pile-up truncation points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Filter stage of peaks2utr in which MACS3-called broad peaks of significant read coverage are matched to gene models (GFF/GTF) on the same strand within a user-defined maximum distance; only passing peaks are designated novel 3' UTRs and truncated at SPAT pile-up truncation points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM comes from a protocol where signal is not concentrated at the distal ends of 3' or 5' UTRs, so strand/distance-matched peaks will not correspond to UTR ends. The goal is de novo peak calling or general ChIP/RIP peak analysis rather than annotating 3' UTRs against a canonical GFF/GTF. Pre-existing 3' UTR annotations are already complete and must neither be extended nor overridden by new peak-based calls.

skills.description: Use when simulated RNA-seq data carry known theoretical circRNA isoform abundances and you must score how faithfully a quantifier (CircAST FPKM/TPM) recovers per-locus relative isoform fractions across conditions, or benchmark it against junction-read counting.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-abundance-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-abundance-accuracy-assessment Use when simulated RNA-seq data carry known theoretical circRNA isoform abundances and you must score how faithfully a quantifier (CircAST FPKM/TPM) recovers per-locus relative isoform fractions across conditions, or benchmark it against junction-read counting. The dataset is real RNA-seq without simulated ground truth - no theoretical isoform abundances exist to correlate against, so the Pearson-based accuracy check cannot be performed. The circRNA locus has a single isoform - relative isoform fractions are trivially 1.0 and Pearson correlation across conditions is meaningless. The target loci are intronic or intergenic circRNAs, which CircAST's exon-annotated pipeline may miss, invalidating the comparison to theoretical values. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Benchmarking skill that scores circRNA isoform quantification accuracy by computing per-locus Pearson correlations between theoretical (simulated ground-truth) and CircAST-estimated relative abundances (TPM/FPKM) across simulated conditions, then comparing against raw junction-read-count correlations. CircAST's reported accuracy range on the 4-loci, 8-condition simulation is 0.849-0.993. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that scores circRNA isoform quantification accuracy by computing per-locus Pearson correlations between theoretical (simulated ground-truth) and CircAST-estimated relative abundances (TPM/FPKM) across simulated conditions, then comparing against raw junction-read-count correlations. CircAST's reported accuracy range on the 4-loci, 8-condition simulation is 0.849-0.993.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real RNA-seq without simulated ground truth - no theoretical isoform abundances exist to correlate against, so the Pearson-based accuracy check cannot be performed. The circRNA locus has a single isoform - relative isoform fractions are trivially 1.0 and Pearson correlation across conditions is meaningless. The target loci are intronic or intergenic circRNAs, which CircAST's exon-annotated pipeline may miss, invalidating the comparison to theoretical values.

skills.description: Use when two features from a sequencing or microarray expression data frame (e.g., RNASEH2A vs PCNA in logTCGA40) need in-depth pairwise correlation with regression fit, correlation coefficient, and density/histogram visualization.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-analysis Use when two features from a sequencing or microarray expression data frame (e.g., RNASEH2A vs PCNA in logTCGA40) need in-depth pairwise correlation with regression fit, correlation coefficient, and density/histogram visualization. The goal is correlating one prime feature against many features rather than a single pair — use primefeature_corr instead The goal is a multiple pairwise correlation matrix with clustering/heatmap — use pairwise_corr (e.g., visorder='hclust', clustno=2) instead Input data are raw read counts with PCR artifacts and heteroskedasticity and have not yet been transformed — apply data_transform (log2, z-score) first http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 In-depth pairwise correlation analysis of two features (e.g., genes) using the FeatureCorr::pair_scatter function, which fits a linear regression and computes a correlation coefficient (e.g., Pearson) while visualizing the scatter with marginal histograms and smooth density. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: In-depth pairwise correlation analysis of two features (e.g., genes) using the FeatureCorr::pair_scatter function, which fits a linear regression and computes a correlation coefficient (e.g., Pearson) while visualizing the scatter with marginal histograms and smooth density.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is correlating one prime feature against many features rather than a single pair — use primefeature_corr instead The goal is a multiple pairwise correlation matrix with clustering/heatmap — use pairwise_corr (e.g., visorder='hclust', clustno=2) instead Input data are raw read counts with PCR artifacts and heteroskedasticity and have not yet been transformed — apply data_transform (log2, z-score) first

skills.summary: Quantifies linear relationships between benchmark dataset characteristics (dataset size, cell type count, entropy, DKL between reference and query) and cell type annotation accuracy using Pearson correlation coefficients (PCC) computed with scipy.stats.pearsonr in Python.

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell activity vectors for multiple ORIGINS2 biological-process PPINs (e.g. 18 BP edge sets) from a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and need to characterize cross-BP relationships such as anti-correlation between immune and replication programs.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-bp-activities
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-bp-activities Use when you have per-cell activity vectors for multiple ORIGINS2 biological-process PPINs (e.g. 18 BP edge sets) from a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and need to characterize cross-BP relationships such as anti-correlation between immune and replication programs. Input is a raw (unnormalized) count matrix — the activity() function expects a normalized expression matrix. You need cell-type annotation of individual cells rather than relationships among biological processes; the ORIGINS2 activity/UMAP annotation workflow is the appropriate skill instead. Only one BP edge set is available — Pearson correlation across BP activities requires at least two per-BP activity profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes pairwise Pearson correlation matrices among per-cell ORIGINS2 PPIN activity profiles of biological processes (BPs) in a scRNA-seq sample, to reveal whether BPs cluster into correlated or anti-correlated groups (e.g. inflammatory/immune vs replication/differentiation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Computes pairwise Pearson correlation matrices among per-cell ORIGINS2 PPIN activity profiles of biological processes (BPs) in a scRNA-seq sample, to reveal whether BPs cluster into correlated or anti-correlated groups (e.g. inflammatory/immune vs replication/differentiation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw (unnormalized) count matrix — the activity() function expects a normalized expression matrix. Input is a raw SNV or gene expression matrix that has not been reduced by SSrGE — the correlation distance should be computed on LASSO-selected eeSNV features, not noisy GE or unfiltered SNVs Cells lack the primary (PDX-pRCC) subgroup needed to root the MST at the primary-to-metastasis origin The goal is subpopulation classification accuracy rather than trajectory/pseudo-time reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes a pairwise Pearson correlation matrix between single cells on their eeSNV feature vectors and converts it to a correlation distance (e.g., 1 − r), serving as the cell-to-cell dissimilarity input for Monocle-style minimum spanning tree pseudo-time reconstruction of the Kim primary-to-metastasis (PDX-pRCC → Pt-mRCC → PDX-mRCC) trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Computes a pairwise Pearson correlation matrix between single cells on their eeSNV feature vectors and converts it to a correlation distance (e.g., 1 − r), serving as the cell-to-cell dissimilarity input for Monocle-style minimum spanning tree pseudo-time reconstruction of the Kim primary-to-metastasis (PDX-pRCC → Pt-mRCC → PDX-mRCC) trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw SNV or gene expression matrix that has not been reduced by SSrGE — the correlation distance should be computed on LASSO-selected eeSNV features, not noisy GE or unfiltered SNVs Cells lack the primary (PDX-pRCC) subgroup needed to root the MST at the primary-to-metastasis origin The goal is subpopulation classification accuracy rather than trajectory/pseudo-time reconstruction

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-distance-preservation-analysis Use when evaluating whether a 2D embedding of high-dimensional single-cell (CyTOF/scRNA-seq) data retains global inter-cluster geometry, using manually annotated cell-population labels and centroid distance concordance. When only local neighbourhood preservation matters — the PCC of centroid distances measures global inter-cluster structure, not fine-grained local structure When no manually annotated cell populations are available, since centroid distances require labelled clusters For evaluating label transfer or classification accuracy directly — the paper complements this with SVM classification accuracy and phenograph ARI, which this skill does not compute http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies how well a dimensionality-reduction embedding (e.g. ivis or t-SNE) preserves global inter-cluster structure by correlating Euclidean distance matrices of manually annotated cell-population centroids in original vs. embedding space using a Mantel test with Pearson's product-moment correlation coefficient (PCC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Quantifies how well a dimensionality-reduction embedding (e.g. ivis or t-SNE) preserves global inter-cluster structure by correlating Euclidean distance matrices of manually annotated cell-population centroids in original vs. embedding space using a Mantel test with Pearson's product-moment correlation coefficient (PCC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only local neighbourhood preservation matters — the PCC of centroid distances measures global inter-cluster structure, not fine-grained local structure When no manually annotated cell populations are available, since centroid distances require labelled clusters For evaluating label transfer or classification accuracy directly — the paper complements this with SVM classification accuracy and phenograph ARI, which this skill does not compute

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-feature-transformation Use when preparing a scRNA-seq expression matrix (CSV) plus class labels for graph-embedding visualization with GraphDDP/graph_embed, after class filtering, normalization, and feature selection. The goal is dimensionality reduction or pseudotime ordering with tools like TSCAN, Monocle2, or SPRING rather than supervised force-based graph embedding The input is already a correlation or similarity matrix over cells; applying the transformation again would double-transform Class labels are unavailable — the pipeline (class filtering and one-vs-all SVM-SGD RFE) requires a discrete label per instance Pre-processing step in the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed pipeline that converts the feature-selected, per-cell normalized expression matrix into a Pearson correlation-coefficient matrix, mapping each cell to an R^n correlation vector used as input to the force-based graph layout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Pre-processing step in the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed pipeline that converts the feature-selected, per-cell normalized expression matrix into a Pearson correlation-coefficient matrix, mapping each cell to an R^n correlation vector used as input to the force-based graph layout.

skills.description: Use when you have scPagwas per-cell gPAS scores for a GWAS trait and a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, and need to derive a ranked trait-relevant gene set (e.g., top 1,000 genes) for downstream enrichment or gene-set comparisons.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-gene-ranking Use when you have scPagwas per-cell gPAS scores for a GWAS trait and a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, and need to derive a ranked trait-relevant gene set (e.g., top 1,000 genes) for downstream enrichment or gene-set comparisons. When no per-cell gPAS scores exist yet — the correlation requires scPagwas's pathway-based polygenic regression output, not raw GWAS summary statistics When the goal is cell-type-level association (TRS/cell-type inference) rather than gene-level prioritization When genes must be linked to variants by functionally informed mapping — scPagwas annotates SNPs to genes only by proximal distance with a 20 kb window http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Prioritize trait-relevant genes from scPagwas output by computing the Pearson correlation (PCC) of each gene's single-cell expression with the summed per-cell genetic pathway association scores (gPASsum), then selecting the top 1,000 genes per trait as the trait-relevant gene set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Prioritize trait-relevant genes from scPagwas output by computing the Pearson correlation (PCC) of each gene's single-cell expression with the summed per-cell genetic pathway association scores (gPASsum), then selecting the top 1,000 genes per trait as the trait-relevant gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no per-cell gPAS scores exist yet — the correlation requires scPagwas's pathway-based polygenic regression output, not raw GWAS summary statistics When the goal is cell-type-level association (TRS/cell-type inference) rather than gene-level prioritization When genes must be linked to variants by functionally informed mapping — scPagwas annotates SNPs to genes only by proximal distance with a 20 kb window

skills.description: Use when imputing dropout-affected zero entries in an scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must choose which genes from a pre-defined gene subspace serve as regression predictors for a target gene.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-gene-selection
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-gene-selection Use when imputing dropout-affected zero entries in an scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must choose which genes from a pre-defined gene subspace serve as regression predictors for a target gene. The entry is not flagged as imputable — under-representation-test-significant (trustworthy) zeros must be left untouched; scISR only alters entries identified by hypothesis testing as dropout-affected. The target gene has no assigned subspace or the subspace contains fewer than 10 candidate training genes with measurable Pearson correlation, so the top-10 selection is not well-defined. You need a whole-matrix smoothing/denoising imputation: scISR deliberately imputes only identified dropout zeros rather than all zero-valued entries, including true zeros. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predictor-selection step from scISR's subspace-regression imputation module: within a gene's assigned subspace, compute Pearson correlation between the target gene y and each candidate training gene x_i and keep the 10 most correlated genes as predictors for the linear model used to estimate dropout-affected zero entries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Predictor-selection step from scISR's subspace-regression imputation module: within a gene's assigned subspace, compute Pearson correlation between the target gene y and each candidate training gene x_i and keep the 10 most correlated genes as predictors for the linear model used to estimate dropout-affected zero entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The entry is not flagged as imputable — under-representation-test-significant (trustworthy) zeros must be left untouched; scISR only alters entries identified by hypothesis testing as dropout-affected. The target gene has no assigned subspace or the subspace contains fewer than 10 candidate training genes with measurable Pearson correlation, so the top-10 selection is not well-defined. You need a whole-matrix smoothing/denoising imputation: scISR deliberately imputes only identified dropout zeros rather than all zero-valued entries, including true zeros.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a cell-specific network inference method against dyngen's per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks and you need a simple correlation-differencing baseline (SSN) using Pearson correlation as the base estimator.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-grn-estimation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-grn-estimation Use when benchmarking a cell-specific network inference method against dyngen's per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks and you need a simple correlation-differencing baseline (SSN) using Pearson correlation as the base estimator. The task requires method discovery or high benchmark performance rather than a simple negative-control baseline — SSN performed poorly because its subtract-one-cell correlation differences are mostly noise. The data lack per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks, so AUROC/AUPR against a known CSN cannot be computed. The analysis goal is RNA velocity or trajectory alignment benchmarking, the other dyngen applications. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A cell-specific gene regulatory network (CSNI) baseline that scores every TF–gene pair per cell using a leave-one-out differencing of Pearson correlation matrices (the SSN approach), evaluated against dyngen's cell-specific ground-truth GRNs on the 42-dataset benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: A cell-specific gene regulatory network (CSNI) baseline that scores every TF–gene pair per cell using a leave-one-out differencing of Pearson correlation matrices (the SSN approach), evaluated against dyngen's cell-specific ground-truth GRNs on the 42-dataset benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires method discovery or high benchmark performance rather than a simple negative-control baseline — SSN performed poorly because its subtract-one-cell correlation differences are mostly noise. The data lack per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks, so AUROC/AUPR against a known CSN cannot be computed. The analysis goal is RNA velocity or trajectory alignment benchmarking, the other dyngen applications.

skills.description: Use when you have deep features from a trained DeepCC model and need to test whether features self-organize into biological groups (e.g., three groups mapping to CMS1 MSI, CMS3 metabolic, CMS4 EMT).
skills.name: pearson-correlation-hierarchical-clustering
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-hierarchical-clustering Use when you have deep features from a trained DeepCC model and need to test whether features self-organize into biological groups (e.g., three groups mapping to CMS1 MSI, CMS3 metabolic, CMS4 EMT). Input is raw gene expression or functional spectra rather than deep features extracted from a trained DeepCC ANN — the grouping structure exists in learned-feature space, not in the raw pathway-activity table Goal is classifying new patient samples rather than interpreting model internals (use get_DeepCC_label for prediction; DeepCC is a classification framework, not for clustering of cancer patients) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 An interpretability workflow from the DeepCC paper: compute the absolute Pearson correlation matrix among the ten deep features extracted from the last hidden layer of a trained DeepCC ANN, hierarchically cluster that matrix, and annotate the resulting feature groups against subtype-relevant biology (MSI, metabolic dysregulation, EMT) to show the network learned CMS-subtype characteristics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: An interpretability workflow from the DeepCC paper: compute the absolute Pearson correlation matrix among the ten deep features extracted from the last hidden layer of a trained DeepCC ANN, hierarchically cluster that matrix, and annotate the resulting feature groups against subtype-relevant biology (MSI, metabolic dysregulation, EMT) to show the network learned CMS-subtype characteristics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression or functional spectra rather than deep features extracted from a trained DeepCC ANN — the grouping structure exists in learned-feature space, not in the raw pathway-activity table Goal is classifying new patient samples rather than interpreting model internals (use get_DeepCC_label for prediction; DeepCC is a classification framework, not for clustering of cancer patients)

skills.description: Use when comparing gene imputation methods on paired observed/reference matrices (e.g. SERM vs MAGIC, SAVER, scVI on the cellular taxonomy dataset) and you need a quantitative accuracy score per sampling efficiency.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-imputation-evaluation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-imputation-evaluation Use when comparing gene imputation methods on paired observed/reference matrices (e.g. SERM vs MAGIC, SAVER, scVI on the cellular taxonomy dataset) and you need a quantitative accuracy score per sampling efficiency. When no dropout-free reference matrix is available — the Pearson evaluation requires paired reference and imputed data and cannot be run on experimental data with unknown ground truth When the goal is evaluating downstream biological utility (e.g. clustering accuracy, NMI, AR, Hubert indices) rather than raw expression recovery accuracy When evaluating methods on very small genomic datasets, where the reference constructed from only high-expression cells and genes may not represent the true distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods by computing per-cell Pearson correlation coefficients between imputed and dropout-free reference expression vectors, then aggregating into percent improvement over observed data across sampling efficiencies (0.1%–10%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods by computing per-cell Pearson correlation coefficients between imputed and dropout-free reference expression vectors, then aggregating into percent improvement over observed data across sampling efficiencies (0.1%–10%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no dropout-free reference matrix is available — the Pearson evaluation requires paired reference and imputed data and cannot be run on experimental data with unknown ground truth When the goal is evaluating downstream biological utility (e.g. clustering accuracy, NMI, AR, Hubert indices) rather than raw expression recovery accuracy When evaluating methods on very small genomic datasets, where the reference constructed from only high-expression cells and genes may not represent the true distribution

skills.name: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation Use when validating that a per-cell background/noise estimate (µ1) captures shared variance with isotype controls in CITE-seq ADT data, or when quantifying concordance of fitted parameters between alternative mixture-component definitions (k=2 vs k=3). Datasets without isotype control antibody measurements — caveats for such datasets are deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note Analyzing normalized/denoised dsb output values — correlations must be computed on step-I ambient-corrected values before technical-component removal Background droplets are not well-defined — dsb normalized values are sensitive to how background barcodes are defined and a reasonable subset requires care http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Compute a Pearson correlation matrix across single cells between the per-cell fitted background protein mean (µ1 from a k=2 Gaussian mixture), isotype control antibodies, their mean, and protein library size, to validate the shared-variance technical noise estimate underlying the dsb technical component (λ). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Compute a Pearson correlation matrix across single cells between the per-cell fitted background protein mean (µ1 from a k=2 Gaussian mixture), isotype control antibodies, their mean, and protein library size, to validate the shared-variance technical noise estimate underlying the dsb technical component (λ).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets without isotype control antibody measurements — caveats for such datasets are deferred to the dsb Supplementary Note Analyzing normalized/denoised dsb output values — correlations must be computed on step-I ambient-corrected values before technical-component removal Background droplets are not well-defined — dsb normalized values are sensitive to how background barcodes are defined and a reasonable subset requires care

skills.description: Use when a supervised cell annotation pipeline must decide between model architectures based on cross-cell-type similarity, or when a K x K cell-type correlation matrix from averaged scRNA-seq expression profiles is required.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation Use when a supervised cell annotation pipeline must decide between model architectures based on cross-cell-type similarity, or when a K x K cell-type correlation matrix from averaged scRNA-seq expression profiles is required. The new sample contains cell types that do not exist in the reference/training data (NeuCA is designed for exhaustively known cell types) Input is raw unnormalized counts without cell type labels — correlation profiles cannot be computed per type without labels The goal is to identify unknown/rare or malignant cells rather than assign known labels; pre-filter with tools like inferCNV or copyKAT first instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute a Pearson correlation matrix across K cell types from their mean gene expression profiles, used by NeuCA to gate its annotation strategy between a feed-forward neural network and a cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network at a threshold of tau = 0.95. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Compute a Pearson correlation matrix across K cell types from their mean gene expression profiles, used by NeuCA to gate its annotation strategy between a feed-forward neural network and a cell lineage-based hierarchical neural network at a threshold of tau = 0.95.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The new sample contains cell types that do not exist in the reference/training data (NeuCA is designed for exhaustively known cell types) Input is raw unnormalized counts without cell type labels — correlation profiles cannot be computed per type without labels The goal is to identify unknown/rare or malignant cells rather than assign known labels; pre-filter with tools like inferCNV or copyKAT first instead

skills.description: Use when multiple gene-set activity scoring methods (e.g. ORIGINS2 network activity, AUCell, mean expression) have been run on the same gene sets and you need to quantify their agreement with Pearson correlations and summary means.

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-method-comparison Use when multiple gene-set activity scoring methods (e.g. ORIGINS2 network activity, AUCell, mean expression) have been run on the same gene sets and you need to quantify their agreement with Pearson correlations and summary means. You need per-cell normalized activity (normalization=TRUE) rather than raw edge-sum activity for cross-method comparison on equal footing Your gene sets are not shared across all methods being compared, since Pearson correlations must be computed over the same BP sets You want cell-type label assignment itself rather than agreement/benchmarking of scoring methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark ORIGINS2 PPIN activity scores against AUCell and mean-expression (Average) scoring by computing pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients across biological-process gene sets, as done for 17 BPs on a TNBC single-cell sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Benchmark ORIGINS2 PPIN activity scores against AUCell and mean-expression (Average) scoring by computing pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients across biological-process gene sets, as done for 17 BPs on a TNBC single-cell sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-cell normalized activity (normalization=TRUE) rather than raw edge-sum activity for cross-method comparison on equal footing Your gene sets are not shared across all methods being compared, since Pearson correlations must be computed over the same BP sets You want cell-type label assignment itself rather than agreement/benchmarking of scoring methods

skills.description: Use when two raw gene-barcode count matrices produced by different scRNA-seq pipelines on the same FASTQ dataset must be compared numerically to validate that an alternative pipeline reproduces native-pipeline output.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-of-count-matrices
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-count-matrices Use when two raw gene-barcode count matrices produced by different scRNA-seq pipelines on the same FASTQ dataset must be compared numerically to validate that an alternative pipeline reproduces native-pipeline output. Input matrices come from different datasets, references, or read sets — the correlation is only meaningful for paired pipelines run on identical FASTQ input (e.g. same GRCh38 chr21-mapped reads) The goal is to compare dimensionality-reduced or normalized expression matrices rather than raw UMI count GBMs 5' scRNA-seq data from technologies other than Chromium, which UniverSC does not support at the time of writing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies agreement between two single-cell gene-barcode matrices (GBMs), e.g. one from UniverSC and one from a platform-specific pipeline such as Cell Ranger, dropSeqPipe, CogentAP, or zUMIs, by Pearson-correlating paired per-gene UMI counts. This is the benchmarking approach used to show UniverSC GBMs match native pipelines (r = 1 for Chromium/Cell Ranger 3.0.2, r >= 0.94 for the other three platforms). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between two single-cell gene-barcode matrices (GBMs), e.g. one from UniverSC and one from a platform-specific pipeline such as Cell Ranger, dropSeqPipe, CogentAP, or zUMIs, by Pearson-correlating paired per-gene UMI counts. This is the benchmarking approach used to show UniverSC GBMs match native pipelines (r = 1 for Chromium/Cell Ranger 3.0.2, r >= 0.94 for the other three platforms).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices come from different datasets, references, or read sets — the correlation is only meaningful for paired pipelines run on identical FASTQ input (e.g. same GRCh38 chr21-mapped reads) The goal is to compare dimensionality-reduced or normalized expression matrices rather than raw UMI count GBMs 5' scRNA-seq data from technologies other than Chromium, which UniverSC does not support at the time of writing

skills.description: Use when a CITE-seq (or ASAP-seq/TEA-seq) ADT dataset has both a raw empty-droplet matrix and a cell-containing matrix, and you need to verify that empty-droplet counts faithfully capture the ambient antibody background before using them for dsb step I correction.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-of-per-protein-background-levels
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-per-protein-background-levels Use when a CITE-seq (or ASAP-seq/TEA-seq) ADT dataset has both a raw empty-droplet matrix and a cell-containing matrix, and you need to verify that empty-droplet counts faithfully capture the ambient antibody background before using them for dsb step I correction. When the dataset provides no empty-droplet (background) matrix — dsb documentation notes defining a reasonable subset of barcodes as background droplets still requires care, and the 'no empty drops' vignette should be used instead For RNA expression matrices — this skill applies to antibody-derived tag (ADT) protein counts, not mRNA counts To validate the cell-level denoising (dsb step II) — this skill only checks the ambient/background correspondence, not the Gaussian-mixture or technical-component correction http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Quantifies the correspondence between ambient antibody levels in cell-free (empty) droplets and unstained/cell-containing droplets by correlating per-protein mean log10(count+1) values across the 87-antibody CITE-seq panel, validating that empty-droplet ADT counts estimate the ambient noise each antibody contributes to cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Quantifies the correspondence between ambient antibody levels in cell-free (empty) droplets and unstained/cell-containing droplets by correlating per-protein mean log10(count+1) values across the 87-antibody CITE-seq panel, validating that empty-droplet ADT counts estimate the ambient noise each antibody contributes to cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset provides no empty-droplet (background) matrix — dsb documentation notes defining a reasonable subset of barcodes as background droplets still requires care, and the 'no empty drops' vignette should be used instead For RNA expression matrices — this skill applies to antibody-derived tag (ADT) protein counts, not mRNA counts To validate the cell-level denoising (dsb step II) — this skill only checks the ambient/background correspondence, not the Gaussian-mixture or technical-component correction

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-perturbation-ranking-profiles Use when comparing perturbation effect ranking lists produced under alternative MUSIC preprocessing settings (imputation on/off, Cell_filtering on/off) to measure ranking-list similarity and identify which strategy shifts the ranking most. skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-umi-counts Use when two aligned gene-barcode matrices (same barcodes, zero-padded genes) from different processing pipelines must be quantitatively compared at the UMI-count level to assess processing concordance. skills.description: Use when building gene co-expression networks from RNA-Seq expression matrices where Pearson-correlation edges must be filtered for statistical significance before fusing with other similarity-based networks (e.g., Euclidean-distance networks).
skills.name: pearson-correlation-permutation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-permutation-significance-testing Use when building gene co-expression networks from RNA-Seq expression matrices where Pearson-correlation edges must be filtered for statistical significance before fusing with other similarity-based networks (e.g., Euclidean-distance networks). The input is a Euclidean-distance co-expression network — that network is filtered by 99th-percentile edge-weight thresholding, not by the permutation test Edges have already been filtered and a fused network exists — the next step is the disparity filter backbone extraction, not this significance test Only a single similarity measure is being used with no need for edge-count parity across networks, where a simpler correlation cutoff may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A statistical edge-filtering procedure for Pearson-correlation gene co-expression networks: a permutation test on randomly shuffled TCGA expression data detects a significant correlation threshold, and a p-value percentile cut further prunes edges so edge counts are fairly homogeneous across similarity measures (e.g., matched to the 99th-percentile-filtered Euclidean-distance network). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: A statistical edge-filtering procedure for Pearson-correlation gene co-expression networks: a permutation test on randomly shuffled TCGA expression data detects a significant correlation threshold, and a p-value percentile cut further prunes edges so edge counts are fairly homogeneous across similarity measures (e.g., matched to the 99th-percentile-filtered Euclidean-distance network).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a Euclidean-distance co-expression network — that network is filtered by 99th-percentile edge-weight thresholding, not by the permutation test Edges have already been filtered and a fused network exists — the next step is the disparity filter backbone extraction, not this significance test Only a single similarity measure is being used with no need for edge-count parity across networks, where a simpler correlation cutoff may suffice

skills.name: pearson-correlation-protein-network-inference
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-protein-network-inference Use when you need a plain co-expression/PCC baseline network on a protein-by-condition matrix (tsv/csv, e.g. HPA 566,109-cell scRNA-seq or PRIDE bulk proteomics) to benchmark against a learned method like FAVA. The goal is the highest-quality network itself, not a baseline — the article shows FAVA's latent-space correlations outperform plain co-expression 'by a wide margin' (>90% precision, >5000 true positives with <500 false positives on HPA vs KEGG). The input is already a dense, low-dimensional latent representation — at that point simple correlation is exactly FAVA's contribution; applying PCC on the original high-dimensional data is what fails. The matrix is small and dense with no sparseness/redundancy concerns, where the runtime and accuracy disadvantages of brute-force PCC are less relevant. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers protein functional association networks via plain Pearson correlation (PCC) on gene/protein-by-condition matrices, serving as the classical co-expression baseline that FAVA is benchmarked against on Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Infers protein functional association networks via plain Pearson correlation (PCC) on gene/protein-by-condition matrices, serving as the classical co-expression baseline that FAVA is benchmarked against on Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics data.

The input is already a dense, low-dimensional latent representation — at that point simple correlation is exactly FAVA's contribution; applying PCC on the original high-dimensional data is what fails. The matrix is small and dense with no sparseness/redundancy concerns, where the runtime and accuracy disadvantages of brute-force PCC are less relevant.

skills.description: Use when validating that clustering features (e.g., Spearman correlation features from sscClust) remain robust to subsampling fluctuations across multiple subsampling rates of an scRNA-seq dataset.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-scatter-visualization
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-scatter-visualization Use when validating that clustering features (e.g., Spearman correlation features from sscClust) remain robust to subsampling fluctuations across multiple subsampling rates of an scRNA-seq dataset. The goal is to measure subsampling bias itself (e.g., comparing accuracy degradation across fractions) rather than to verify robustness via near-zero correlation Only a single subsampling rate is available, so no silhouette-vs-rate correlation can be computed The dataset lacks true cell-type labels, since silhouette values must be computed against known labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A robustness-diagnostic visualization in which per-cell silhouette values (X axis) from Spearman-correlation-based SSCC features are plotted against cell-subsampling rates (Y axis, 10%–50%) as scatter plots, with a Pearson correlation coefficient computed per dataset. Near-zero correlations indicate the engineered features stay consistent with true cluster labels regardless of the subsampled cell fraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: A robustness-diagnostic visualization in which per-cell silhouette values (X axis) from Spearman-correlation-based SSCC features are plotted against cell-subsampling rates (Y axis, 10%–50%) as scatter plots, with a Pearson correlation coefficient computed per dataset. Near-zero correlations indicate the engineered features stay consistent with true cluster labels regardless of the subsampled cell fraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure subsampling bias itself (e.g., comparing accuracy degradation across fractions) rather than to verify robustness via near-zero correlation Only a single subsampling rate is available, so no silhouette-vs-rate correlation can be computed The dataset lacks true cell-type labels, since silhouette values must be computed against known labels

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify and significance-test the association between two per-cell score vectors (e.g., AXL-high vs MITF-high program scores in scRNA-seq) and compare that association before vs after confounder correction.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-significance-testing Use when you need to quantify and significance-test the association between two per-cell score vectors (e.g., AXL-high vs MITF-high program scores in scRNA-seq) and compare that association before vs after confounder correction. The score vectors are not paired per cell (correlation requires matched cells across the two vectors) You need monotonic-but-nonlinear association — use Spearman/Kendall rather than Pearson, which the paper's P-value is not defined for Input matrices are not on the recommended scale (unscaled/uncentered/linear-transformed), which changes average-expression program scores and hence R http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute and significance-test Pearson correlations between per-cell gene-program scores (e.g., AXL and MITF in Mel78 melanoma cells) on uncorrected and cell-cycle-corrected expression matrices, to quantify how a confounder correction (Cyclum) changes the relationship between programs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Compute and significance-test Pearson correlations between per-cell gene-program scores (e.g., AXL and MITF in Mel78 melanoma cells) on uncorrected and cell-cycle-corrected expression matrices, to quantify how a confounder correction (Cyclum) changes the relationship between programs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The score vectors are not paired per cell (correlation requires matched cells across the two vectors) You need monotonic-but-nonlinear association — use Spearman/Kendall rather than Pearson, which the paper's P-value is not defined for Input matrices are not on the recommended scale (unscaled/uncentered/linear-transformed), which changes average-expression program scores and hence R

skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-similarity-assessment Use when validating that computationally inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data reproduces the ground-truth cohort structure, by correlating per-condition cell-type proportion vectors and pathway activation scores between two cohorts. When the goal is to capture variability within cell types — aggregate proportion correlations operate at cell-type-level resolution and cannot attest to single-cell-level agreement When the two cohorts cannot be merged on a shared condition axis (e.g., mismatched severity labels), since correlations are computed per condition When data have not passed semi-profiling QC (library size normalization, log1p, highly variable gene selection), as raw counts will distort proportion and pathway-score estimates http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies similarity between semi-profiled and real-profiled single-cell cohorts by computing per-condition Pearson correlations of cell-type proportions (via scipy.stats.pearsonr) and of IFN pathway activation scores, writing the metrics to similarity_metrics.csv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
