skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to capture variability within cell types — aggregate proportion correlations operate at cell-type-level resolution and cannot attest to single-cell-level agreement When the two cohorts cannot be merged on a shared condition axis (e.g., mismatched severity labels), since correlations are computed per condition When data have not passed semi-profiling QC (library size normalization, log1p, highly variable gene selection), as raw counts will distort proportion and pathway-score estimates

skills.description: Use when a model has a stochastic component (e.g. random GAN initialization) and you must test whether an internal loss reliably predicts external alignment quality across repeated runs, via per-run Pearson correlations between loss and metric trajectories.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-stability-analysis
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-stability-analysis Use when a model has a stochastic component (e.g. random GAN initialization) and you must test whether an internal loss reliably predicts external alignment quality across repeated runs, via per-run Pearson correlations between loss and metric trajectories. You have only a single training run with no repeated random initializations — there is no trajectory distribution to correlate across runs. Your goal is benchmarking scTopoGAN against UnionCom or MMD-MA rather than assessing initialization stability — use the UnionCom.py / manifold_align_mmd_pytorch.py / scTopoGAN_results.py scripts instead. Your input modalities share overlapping features or cells — the article motivates scTopoGAN for non-overlapping single-modality datasets; methods relying on overlaps are the established route there. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies run-to-run stability of a stochastic manifold-alignment model by correlating, per run, the trajectory of the topological loss (Eq. 2) with Celltype and Subcelltype label-matching score trajectories across repeated random initializations. In the scTopoGAN study this showed GANs with low topological loss align the ATAC source manifold to the RNA target manifold better (Pearson r ≈ −0.73 and −0.67 across 40 runs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Quantifies run-to-run stability of a stochastic manifold-alignment model by correlating, per run, the trajectory of the topological loss (Eq. 2) with Celltype and Subcelltype label-matching score trajectories across repeated random initializations. In the scTopoGAN study this showed GANs with low topological loss align the ATAC source manifold to the RNA target manifold better (Pearson r ≈ −0.73 and −0.67 across 40 runs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single training run with no repeated random initializations — there is no trajectory distribution to correlate across runs. Your goal is benchmarking scTopoGAN against UnionCom or MMD-MA rather than assessing initialization stability — use the UnionCom.py / manifold_align_mmd_pytorch.py / scTopoGAN_results.py scripts instead. Your input modalities share overlapping features or cells — the article motivates scTopoGAN for non-overlapping single-modality datasets; methods relying on overlaps are the established route there.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing NeuCA's annotation route when a labelled training scRNA-seq matrix is available: compute cross-cell-type correlations and check whether any off-diagonal element reaches tau = 0.95.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-strategy-selection
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-strategy-selection Decision support for choosing NeuCA's annotation route when a labelled training scRNA-seq matrix is available: compute cross-cell-type correlations and check whether any off-diagonal element reaches tau = 0.95. Cell types in the new sample include unknown/novel or malignant populations not present in the training reference — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types already exist in the training data; identify such cells first (e.g. inferCNV or copyKAT) before applying this gate Fewer than two cell types in the training labels — the off-diagonal correlation comparison over P is undefined Only the test matrix is available with no labelled training data — supervised gating (and NeuCA itself) requires known labels to compute the averaged profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 NeuCA's data-driven gate that computes a Pearson correlation matrix across cell types from averaged gene expression profiles of the labelled training scRNA-seq data and selects the annotation route: a single feed-forward neural network when all off-diagonal correlations are below tau = 0.95, otherwise a marker-guided hierarchical (cell lineage tree) network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: NeuCA's data-driven gate that computes a Pearson correlation matrix across cell types from averaged gene expression profiles of the labelled training scRNA-seq data and selects the annotation route: a single feed-forward neural network when all off-diagonal correlations are below tau = 0.95, otherwise a marker-guided hierarchical (cell lineage tree) network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types in the new sample include unknown/novel or malignant populations not present in the training reference — NeuCA is designed for settings where all cell types already exist in the training data; identify such cells first (e.g. inferCNV or copyKAT) before applying this gate Fewer than two cell types in the training labels — the off-diagonal correlation comparison over P is undefined Only the test matrix is available with no labelled training data — supervised gating (and NeuCA itself) requires known labels to compute the averaged profiles

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell TCR-contribution scores from a trained mvTCR model plus TCRdist similarities per specificity group, and you must validate that TCR contribution quantitatively tracks TCR sequence similarity across epitope groups.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-validation
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-validation Use when you have per-cell TCR-contribution scores from a trained mvTCR model plus TCRdist similarities per specificity group, and you must validate that TCR contribution quantitatively tracks TCR sequence similarity across epitope groups. Your embedding does not separate joint and TCR-unimodal views (e.g. you only have a clonotype-level integration), since angular distance between modalities is undefined Data lack antigen specificity annotations and TCR sequences usable for Scirpy's TCRdist computation Only CDR3-based TCR representation with partially missing paired data is available, which the authors note was insufficiently addressed (mvTCR was applied mainly to fully paired data) Validation procedure for the TCR-Contribution analysis in mvTCR: average the per-cell TCR-contribution scores (angular distance between joint and TCR-unimodal embeddings) per antigen specificity, then test whether these averages track TCRdist-based sequence similarity via a Pearson correlation (reported r = 0.64 on the 10x dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Validation procedure for the TCR-Contribution analysis in mvTCR: average the per-cell TCR-contribution scores (angular distance between joint and TCR-unimodal embeddings) per antigen specificity, then test whether these averages track TCRdist-based sequence similarity via a Pearson correlation (reported r = 0.64 on the 10x dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your embedding does not separate joint and TCR-unimodal views (e.g. you only have a clonotype-level integration), since angular distance between modalities is undefined Data lack antigen specificity annotations and TCR sequences usable for Scirpy's TCRdist computation Only CDR3-based TCR representation with partially missing paired data is available, which the authors note was insufficiently addressed (mvTCR was applied mainly to fully paired data)

skills.description: Use when you need to decide, cell by cell, whether a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) faithfully preserves pre-embedding neighborhood structure, or when optimizing hyperparameters like t-SNE perplexity by minimizing dubious embeddings.
skills.name: pearson-neighborhood-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: pearson-neighborhood-similarity-scoring Use when you need to decide, cell by cell, whether a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) faithfully preserves pre-embedding neighborhood structure, or when optimizing hyperparameters like t-SNE perplexity by minimizing dubious embeddings. You only need a global embedding-quality metric or cluster-level assessment — scDEED's score is strictly per-cell and neighborhood-based, and methods like EMBEDR or DynamicViz serve different purposes (EMBEDR tests against chance, DynamicViz only measures stability) The embedding hyperparameter already appears optimal or the number of dubious cells shows a complex trend with increasing hyperparameter value, suggesting complex cell topology where interpretation of the 2D plot requires caution Input is raw counts with no Seurat preprocessing pipeline possible — the score requires a PCA pre-embedding space built from scale.data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes a per-cell reliability score as the Pearson correlation between a cell's ordered pre-embedding neighbor distances (e.g., K-dimensional PCA space) and its 2D t-SNE/UMAP neighbor distances, as implemented in scDEED's Cell.Similarity step. Comparing these scores against a gene-permutation null distribution separates dubious from trustworthy 2D embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Computes a per-cell reliability score as the Pearson correlation between a cell's ordered pre-embedding neighbor distances (e.g., K-dimensional PCA space) and its 2D t-SNE/UMAP neighbor distances, as implemented in scDEED's Cell.Similarity step. Comparing these scores against a gene-permutation null distribution separates dubious from trustworthy 2D embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a global embedding-quality metric or cluster-level assessment — scDEED's score is strictly per-cell and neighborhood-based, and methods like EMBEDR or DynamicViz serve different purposes (EMBEDR tests against chance, DynamicViz only measures stability) The embedding hyperparameter already appears optimal or the number of dubious cells shows a complex trend with increasing hyperparameter value, suggesting complex cell topology where interpretation of the 2D plot requires caution Input is raw counts with no Seurat preprocessing pipeline possible — the score requires a PCA pre-embedding space built from scale.data

skills.description: Use when you have a raw scRNAseq count matrix and need the chi-squared residual matrix for CA dimension reduction, or when verifying a re-implementation of the corral_preproc count-to-residual pre-processing stage element-wise.
skills.name: pearson-residual-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: pearson-residual-matrix-computation Use when you have a raw scRNAseq count matrix and need the chi-squared residual matrix for CA dimension reduction, or when verifying a re-implementation of the corral_preproc count-to-residual pre-processing stage element-wise. The downstream analysis already requires a variance-stabilized or power-deflated residual variant (e.g. Freeman–Tukey residuals, square-root/Anscombe VST, or signed power deflation) rather than the plain standardized Pearson residuals. The goal is batch/multi-table integration across samples — corralm, not the single-table residual pre-processing, is the appropriate entry point. The pipeline expects the conventional log(x + 1) 'logcounts' transformation followed by PCA instead of CA on chi-squared residuals. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the standardized Pearson residual matrix (observed minus expected over sqrt of expected, with expectations from row and column marginals) from an scRNAseq count matrix as the chi-squared residual stage that precedes SVD in correspondence analysis (CA), replacing the log(x+1) + PCA transformation used in typical single-cell workflows. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Computes the standardized Pearson residual matrix (observed minus expected over sqrt of expected, with expectations from row and column marginals) from an scRNAseq count matrix as the chi-squared residual stage that precedes SVD in correspondence analysis (CA), replacing the log(x+1) + PCA transformation used in typical single-cell workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream analysis already requires a variance-stabilized or power-deflated residual variant (e.g. Freeman–Tukey residuals, square-root/Anscombe VST, or signed power deflation) rather than the plain standardized Pearson residuals. The goal is batch/multi-table integration across samples — corralm, not the single-table residual pre-processing, is the appropriate entry point. The pipeline expects the conventional log(x + 1) 'logcounts' transformation followed by PCA instead of CA on chi-squared residuals.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq samples come from related individuals (family/pedigree cohort) and you want to model pairwise genetic relatedness as a covariance random effect, or to compare kinship vs non-kinship model fit via per-gene AIC.
skills.name: pedigree-kinship-matrix-preparation
skills.search_text: pedigree-kinship-matrix-preparation Use when RNA-seq samples come from related individuals (family/pedigree cohort) and you want to model pairwise genetic relatedness as a covariance random effect, or to compare kinship vs non-kinship model fit via per-gene AIC. Samples are unrelated or no genetic relatedness/pedigree data exist — the lme random effect without kin, or an unpaired lm, is the appropriate model Input is raw sequence data or an unnormalized count matrix lacking the per-sample library structure (patientID/libraryID) that kmFit's paired design requires You only need standard unpaired DEG detection — limma unpaired or kimma's lm model suffices and matches kimma's performance for that design http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepare a pairwise genetic kinship matrix (e.g., kimma's example.kin) and format it so it can be passed as a covariance random effect to a linear mixed effects RNA-seq model via kimma's kmFit, which routes kinship to lme4qtl::relmatLmer. This enables testing whether relatedness among samples impacts model fit and differential expression detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Prepare a pairwise genetic kinship matrix (e.g., kimma's example.kin) and format it so it can be passed as a covariance random effect to a linear mixed effects RNA-seq model via kimma's kmFit, which routes kinship to lme4qtl::relmatLmer. This enables testing whether relatedness among samples impacts model fit and differential expression detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are unrelated or no genetic relatedness/pedigree data exist — the lme random effect without kin, or an unpaired lm, is the appropriate model Input is raw sequence data or an unnormalized count matrix lacking the per-sample library structure (patientID/libraryID) that kmFit's paired design requires You only need standard unpaired DEG detection — limma unpaired or kimma's lm model suffices and matches kimma's performance for that design

skills.description: Use when predicting overall survival (time + censoring indicator) from thousands of genetic features per patient — e.g., Z-scored mRNA entries or mutated-gene matrices — and you need penalized Cox models with cross-validated prediction power.
skills.name: penalized-cox-regression-survival-modeling
skills.search_text: penalized-cox-regression-survival-modeling Use when predicting overall survival (time + censoring indicator) from thousands of genetic features per patient — e.g., Z-scored mRNA entries or mutated-gene matrices — and you need penalized Cox models with cross-validated prediction power. The outcome is binary rather than a survival time + censoring indicator — use the logistic regression variants (ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso logistic) instead The feature count approaches ~100,000 and no FDR screening is applied — the article states penalized regression models fall short at that magnitude and recommends including FDR first-step screening The data are low-dimensional (few candidate predictors) — an unpenalized standard Cox regression is the appropriate tool, not penalized variants with cross-validated tuning http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Fits Ridge, Lasso, and adaptive Lasso penalized Cox regression models to high-dimensional genomic covariates (e.g., TCGA ovarian HGSC mRNA or somatic mutation matrices) with an optional Benjamini-Hochberg FDR first-step screening and 5-fold cross-validated C-index estimation, via the HDMAC R/Shiny platform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60791-z
skills.summary: Fits Ridge, Lasso, and adaptive Lasso penalized Cox regression models to high-dimensional genomic covariates (e.g., TCGA ovarian HGSC mRNA or somatic mutation matrices) with an optional Benjamini-Hochberg FDR first-step screening and 5-fold cross-validated C-index estimation, via the HDMAC R/Shiny platform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The outcome is binary rather than a survival time + censoring indicator — use the logistic regression variants (ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso logistic) instead The feature count approaches ~100,000 and no FDR screening is applied — the article states penalized regression models fall short at that magnitude and recommends including FDR first-step screening The data are low-dimensional (few candidate predictors) — an unpenalized standard Cox regression is the appropriate tool, not penalized variants with cross-validated tuning

skills.name: penalized-lda-topic-model-fitting
skills.search_text: penalized-lda-topic-model-fitting Use when the goal is to decompose a scRNA-seq count matrix into latent topics whose topic-word probabilities and per-cell topic proportions yield biologically interpretable structure, via the penalized LDA model adapted from natural language processing. The input is not scRNA-seq count data structured as genes-by-cells (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already-clustered/annotated cell type tables) The analysis goal requires supervised cell-type classification rather than unsupervised latent topic discovery The user needs topic assignments for text documents (natural language processing LDA) rather than gene expression counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit a penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) model to single-cell RNA-seq count matrices using the pLDA R package, treating genes as words, cells as documents, and latent biological functions as topics to obtain interpretable topic-word distributions and per-cell topic proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-021-09304-8

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not scRNA-seq count data structured as genes-by-cells (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already-clustered/annotated cell type tables) The analysis goal requires supervised cell-type classification rather than unsupervised latent topic discovery The user needs topic assignments for text documents (natural language processing LDA) rather than gene expression counts

skills.description: Use when you have a robust correlation/covariance matrix from single-cell gene expression data and need to distinguish direct gene-gene associations from indirect ones via a sparse concentration matrix estimate.
skills.name: penalized-likelihood-estimation
skills.search_text: penalized-likelihood-estimation Use when you have a robust correlation/covariance matrix from single-cell gene expression data and need to distinguish direct gene-gene associations from indirect ones via a sparse concentration matrix estimate. The goal is a raw pairwise co-expression summary rather than conditional (direct) dependencies — use sclink_cor alone instead of the network step. The gene list is very large; the article suggests first dividing genes into major modules based on scLink's correlation and applying scLink separately per module. The input is bulk-RNA-seq-like or already densely measured data, where bulk network methods may suffice; imputed single-cell data can also still be too sparse for reliable graphical model fitting. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs sparse gene co-expression networks from single-cell expression data by maximizing a data-adaptively penalized Gaussian graphical model likelihood (weighted graphical lasso solved with QUIC), as implemented in scLink's sclink_net. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Reconstructs sparse gene co-expression networks from single-cell expression data by maximizing a data-adaptively penalized Gaussian graphical model likelihood (weighted graphical lasso solved with QUIC), as implemented in scLink's sclink_net.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a raw pairwise co-expression summary rather than conditional (direct) dependencies — use sclink_cor alone instead of the network step. The gene list is very large; the article suggests first dividing genes into major modules based on scLink's correlation and applying scLink separately per module. The input is bulk-RNA-seq-like or already densely measured data, where bulk network methods may suffice; imputed single-cell data can also still be too sparse for reliable graphical model fitting.

skills.search_text: penalized-regression-competitor-evaluation Use when evaluating a high-dimensional regression method (e.g. SuffPCR) against feature-selecting penalized competitors on transcriptomic data where correlated features and small selected-feature counts matter. The goal is method development or new theory, not head-to-head benchmarking of feature-selecting sparse regression methods on real datasets Data are not high-dimensional regression/classification tasks with correlated omics features — e.g. low-dimensional data where OLS suffices Only a single train/test split is available, so validation-fold lambda selection at the 40/30/30 protocol cannot be implemented reproducibly http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks SuffPCR (row-sparse PCA + OLS/logistic regression) against feature-selecting sparse regression alternatives (SPC, Lasso, Elastic Net, SPCA, DSPCA) on high-dimensional microarray datasets using a shared 40/30/30 train/validation/test splitting and validation-fold lambda-selection protocol, to compare average test MSE and number of selected features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Benchmarks SuffPCR (row-sparse PCA + OLS/logistic regression) against feature-selecting sparse regression alternatives (SPC, Lasso, Elastic Net, SPCA, DSPCA) on high-dimensional microarray datasets using a shared 40/30/30 train/validation/test splitting and validation-fold lambda-selection protocol, to compare average test MSE and number of selected features.

skills.search_text: penalized-spline-additive-model-edge-weighting Use when you need data-driven weights for every directed edge of an input igraph network from RNA-seq-style expression data, as the first phase of CAT tree reconstruction in SEMtree(); trigger: fully connected or candidate digraph plus an n x p expression matrix. When the goal is SEM perturbation testing on an existing graph (SEMrun node/edge perturbation or SEMace), not data-driven edge scoring for tree reconstruction When edges are undirected and must remain undirected (e.g., active subnetwork modules before CAT conversion) — the fits model directed i->j relationships When relationships are known to be linear and a simpler linear SEM edge weighting (e.g., Fisher r-to-z on correlations) suffices; penalized splines target nonlinear additive dependence http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Scores each directed edge i->j of a graph by fitting a bivariate additive regression y_j ~ s(y_i) with penalized regression splines (mgcv::gam) and converting the fitted smooth's association strength into an edge weight (e.g., negated so stronger dependence = lower cost), feeding the weighted digraph into causal additive tree (CAT) recovery via Chu–Liu–Edmonds in SEMtree(). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377

skills.description: Use when mutant peptides of length 8–11 aa derived from called SNVs, INDELs, or gene fusions must be scored for peptide-MHC binding and immunogenicity against patient HLA alleles to shortlist candidate neoantigens.
skills.name: peptide-mhc-binding-immunogenicity-prediction
skills.search_text: peptide-mhc-binding-immunogenicity-prediction Use when mutant peptides of length 8–11 aa derived from called SNVs, INDELs, or gene fusions must be scored for peptide-MHC binding and immunogenicity against patient HLA alleles to shortlist candidate neoantigens. The task is TCR-pMHC binding prediction or TCR sequencing analysis — the article explicitly states this is not yet part of the pipeline and is planned for future updates. Peptides are shorter than 8 or longer than 11 amino acids — only peptides of length 8–11 covering the mutations are extracted and predicted. The user wants generic MHC binding affinity without immunogenicity — TSNAD v2.0 deliberately replaced NetMHCpan with DeepHLApan, which considers both binding and immunogenicity. Predicts peptide-MHC binding and immunogenicity of candidate mutant peptides using DeepHLApan v1.1, which jointly scores binding and immunogenicity, and then applies score and rank thresholds to designate potential and high-confidence neoantigens. This is the neoantigen-selection core of the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, replacing NetMHCpan. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Predicts peptide-MHC binding and immunogenicity of candidate mutant peptides using DeepHLApan v1.1, which jointly scores binding and immunogenicity, and then applies score and rank thresholds to designate potential and high-confidence neoantigens. This is the neoantigen-selection core of the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, replacing NetMHCpan.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is TCR-pMHC binding prediction or TCR sequencing analysis — the article explicitly states this is not yet part of the pipeline and is planned for future updates. Peptides are shorter than 8 or longer than 11 amino acids — only peptides of length 8–11 covering the mutations are extracted and predicted. The user wants generic MHC binding affinity without immunogenicity — TSNAD v2.0 deliberately replaced NetMHCpan with DeepHLApan, which considers both binding and immunogenicity.

skills.name: peptide-physicochemical-feature-calculation
skills.search_text: peptide-physicochemical-feature-calculation Use when encoding transcript sequences for coding-potential prediction and putative peptide sequences translated from ORFs need to be converted into peptide-related numerical features (MW, pI, Gravy, instability index) for a classifier. Input consists of raw nucleotide transcripts without any ORF/peptide information (e.g. the study notes future work requires collecting sORF-translated peptide sequences that are not yet available) Input is already a numeric feature table — re-computing peptide descriptors from scratch would be redundant Non-Standard genetic-code organisms, since Orfipy is configured with Standard Code transl_table=1 (ATG/TTG/CTG starts, TAA/TAG/TGA stops) http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Computes peptide-related physicochemical features (molecular weight, theoretical isoelectric point, Gravy hydrophilicity, instability index) from ORF-derived putative peptide sequences, which LncCat fuses with codon-, GC-, sequence- and ORF-attention features into the 599-dimensional vector fed to CatBoost for lncRNA vs. PCT classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools (e.g. EasyCellType vs Garnett, scPred, SingleR) on simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels and you need per-cell accuracy tables.
skills.name: per-cell-annotation-accuracy-computation
skills.search_text: per-cell-annotation-accuracy-computation Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools (e.g. EasyCellType vs Garnett, scPred, SingleR) on simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels and you need per-cell accuracy tables. The dataset is real tissue data without simulated ground-truth cell-type labels — per-cell accuracy against truth cannot be computed and only plausibility or expert review applies The goal is annotation itself (e.g. querying marker lists against CellMarker via EasyCellType) rather than evaluating annotation accuracy Accuracy has already been aggregated at the cluster level and per-cell resolution is not required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes per-cell annotation accuracy for single-cell RNA-seq cell-type annotation tools by comparing each predicted cell label against simulated ground-truth labels, as done in the EasyCellType paper's PBMC simulation benchmark for Supplementary Figure S5. This enables head-to-head accuracy comparison across tools, tool variants, and dataset sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Computes per-cell annotation accuracy for single-cell RNA-seq cell-type annotation tools by comparing each predicted cell label against simulated ground-truth labels, as done in the EasyCellType paper's PBMC simulation benchmark for Supplementary Figure S5. This enables head-to-head accuracy comparison across tools, tool variants, and dataset sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real tissue data without simulated ground-truth cell-type labels — per-cell accuracy against truth cannot be computed and only plausibility or expert review applies The goal is annotation itself (e.g. querying marker lists against CellMarker via EasyCellType) rather than evaluating annotation accuracy Accuracy has already been aggregated at the cluster level and per-cell resolution is not required

skills.summary: Reconstructs Cellenium's standardized cell typing step by running CellO's pretrained Cell Ontology classifier on a prepared AnnData study (e.g. the blood_covid demo study) and exporting one standardized annotation per cell to cell_annotations.csv.

skills.search_text: per-cell-bam-processing Use when starting from per-cell (barcode-split) BAM files from a 10x or non-10x scRNA-seq experiment and you need a per-cell normalized gene body coverage vector for SkewC quality/skewness analysis. BAM files are not yet split per cell — run 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh first (10x Genomics outputs a single barcoded BAM that must be split by cell barcode) You plan to run RSeQC's geneBody_coverage.py instead — then BAM index files are required and the geneBodyCoverage.pl speed/behavior described here does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Computes normalized gene body coverage for each single cell in the SkewC scRNA-seq workflow by running geneBodyCoverage.pl (a ~10x faster Perl imitation of RSeQC's geneBody_coverage.py) over per-cell BAM files, producing per-cell 100-value coverage vectors aggregated into coverage.r. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.102038

skills.description: Use when evaluating a single-cell long-read isoform quantification method against a matched gold-standard count matrix, e.g. Nanopore output vs PacBio IsoSeq truth for the same Jurkat 5' cDNA library.
skills.name: per-cell-correlation-evaluation-against-reference-matrix
skills.search_text: per-cell-correlation-evaluation-against-reference-matrix Use when evaluating a single-cell long-read isoform quantification method against a matched gold-standard count matrix, e.g. Nanopore output vs PacBio IsoSeq truth for the same Jurkat 5' cDNA library. No library-matched gold-standard quantification exists for the same sample — per-cell correlations against an unrelated matrix are not interpretable The goal is discovering isoform switching or splicing heterogeneity (use Longcell's analysis modules like getIsoform or genesSitesPhi instead of benchmarking) The method's isoform identifiers cannot be joined to the truth matrix by isoform, so the full join yields an empty or near-empty row set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill that scores single-cell isoform quantification methods by fully joining each method's cell-by-isoform count matrix to a library-matched PacBio IsoSeq gold-standard matrix and computing per-cell Spearman correlations. It quantifies accuracy gains, e.g. Longcell's mean 0.43 vs an 8.72% improvement over Sicelore2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that scores single-cell isoform quantification methods by fully joining each method's cell-by-isoform count matrix to a library-matched PacBio IsoSeq gold-standard matrix and computing per-cell Spearman correlations. It quantifies accuracy gains, e.g. Longcell's mean 0.43 vs an 8.72% improvement over Sicelore2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No library-matched gold-standard quantification exists for the same sample — per-cell correlations against an unrelated matrix are not interpretable The goal is discovering isoform switching or splicing heterogeneity (use Longcell's analysis modules like getIsoform or genesSitesPhi instead of benchmarking) The method's isoform identifiers cannot be joined to the truth matrix by isoform, so the full join yields an empty or near-empty row set

VarTrix does not perform variant calling — do not use it to discover novel variants from scRNA-seq; input must be a pre-called variant set (e.g. from eWGS) Multi-allelic sites are ignored by VarTrix (rows retained but values empty), so this skill is wrong for multi-allelic loci Not appropriate for detecting CNAs — use copyCat on paired tumor/normal coverage instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Quantify somatic SNV evidence per cell in 10x Genomics Chromium scRNA-seq data by parsing CB-tagged barcodes and UMI/read counts, producing a per-cell genotype matrix from which scVAF, Mutant Cell Fraction (MCF), and Mutant Cell Detection Rate can be computed against eWGS and bulk RNA-seq VAFs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1

skills.name: per-cell-informativeness-scoring
skills.search_text: per-cell-informativeness-scoring Use when a cell-typed .h5ad single-cell dataset is too large for ML/DL training and you need a per-cell importance score before sketching, or want to rank ambiguous/atypical cells by OOB accuracy. Cells lack cell-type labels — the OOB accuracy score requires supervised labels Y The goal is distance- or distribution-preserving subsampling without labels (e.g. GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler designs) — DV ranking is supervised and OOB-based You already have a feature/importance table and need only type-level size allocation or within-type selection (steps 2–3 of the scValue pipeline), not per-cell scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Scores every cell in a labeled scRNA-seq dataset with a 'data value' (DV) equal to its out-of-bag (OOB) prediction accuracy from a random forest, quantifying per-cell informativeness for downstream subsampling or filtering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279

skills.description: Use when you need a local, per-cell quality measure for a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) — e.g. to feed EMBEDR p-value estimation, compare DR algorithms, or tune perplexity/n_neighbors.
skills.name: per-cell-kl-divergence-quantification
skills.search_text: per-cell-kl-divergence-quantification Use when you need a local, per-cell quality measure for a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) — e.g. to feed EMBEDR p-value estimation, compare DR algorithms, or tune perplexity/n_neighbors. Your dataset is not normalized — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets, so per-cell DKL against such nulls is not supported You only need a single global DR quality score rather than local, per-cell error estimates or per-sample p-values You want theoretical/parametric p-values — null distributions here are purely empirical, bounded by the number of nulls embedded http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes EMBEDR's empirical embedding statistic (EES): a per-cell Kullback-Leibler divergence between each cell's high-dimensional affinity distribution and its low-dimensional affinity distribution, quantifying how well each cell's local neighborhood is preserved by a t-SNE or UMAP embedding of real or null (marginal-resampled) data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Computes EMBEDR's empirical embedding statistic (EES): a per-cell Kullback-Leibler divergence between each cell's high-dimensional affinity distribution and its low-dimensional affinity distribution, quantifying how well each cell's local neighborhood is preserved by a t-SNE or UMAP embedding of real or null (marginal-resampled) data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your dataset is not normalized — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets, so per-cell DKL against such nulls is not supported You only need a single global DR quality score rather than local, per-cell error estimates or per-sample p-values You want theoretical/parametric p-values — null distributions here are purely empirical, bounded by the number of nulls embedded

skills.description: Use when an EMBEDR perplexity (or n_neighbors) sweep has been fit on scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data and you want per-sample optimal scales, or a sample-wise optimal embedding, instead of a single global hyperparameter.
skills.name: per-cell-optimal-neighborhood-scale-selection
skills.search_text: per-cell-optimal-neighborhood-scale-selection Use when an EMBEDR perplexity (or n_neighbors) sweep has been fit on scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data and you want per-sample optimal scales, or a sample-wise optimal embedding, instead of a single global hyperparameter. No EMBEDR sweep has been fit yet — the optimal perplexity can only be selected from values used in the sweep, so the skill requires a completed sweep first The goal is a single globally optimal hyperparameter rather than a per-cell heterogeneous neighborhood-scale embedding (use the sweep boxplot/lineplot summaries instead) The dataset is not normalized — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Selects, for each cell/sample individually, the hyperparameter (perplexity for t-SNE) whose EMBEDR p-value is lowest, then uses those per-cell optimal scales to build a 'cell-wise optimal' embedding whose neighborhood size varies across the data. This reveals characteristic neighborhood scales per cell rather than forcing one global hyperparameter. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Selects, for each cell/sample individually, the hyperparameter (perplexity for t-SNE) whose EMBEDR p-value is lowest, then uses those per-cell optimal scales to build a 'cell-wise optimal' embedding whose neighborhood size varies across the data. This reveals characteristic neighborhood scales per cell rather than forcing one global hyperparameter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No EMBEDR sweep has been fit yet — the optimal perplexity can only be selected from values used in the sweep, so the skill requires a completed sweep first The goal is a single globally optimal hyperparameter rather than a per-cell heterogeneous neighborhood-scale embedding (use the sweep boxplot/lineplot summaries instead) The dataset is not normalized — the article notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets

skills.description: Use when you have 10x scRNA-seq data from an infected sample for which cellranger count has already run against the host genome, and you need per-cell pathogen read and UMI counts appended to the 10x matrices for downstream single-cell analysis.
skills.name: per-cell-pathogen-umi-quantification
skills.search_text: per-cell-pathogen-umi-quantification Use when you have 10x scRNA-seq data from an infected sample for which cellranger count has already run against the host genome, and you need per-cell pathogen read and UMI counts appended to the 10x matrices for downstream single-cell analysis. Input is raw FASTQ with no cellranger count output — scPathoQuant consumes the 10x output folder generated by cellranger count, not unprocessed reads Host and pathogen alignment is already complete (e.g. cellranger run against a combined GRCh38 + SARS-CoV-2 reference) — a second SPQ pass adds remapping redundancy The goal is de novo viral genome assembly or clade calling rather than per-cell quantification — scPathoQuant only emits pathogen_al_mapped.fq.gz as a starting point for such downstream analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scPathoQuant takes host-unaligned reads from cellranger count 10x output, remaps them to a pathogen reference (default bbmap, alternative bowtie2), quantifies per-cell total pathogen reads and gene-level UMI counts with htseq, and writes the pathogen counts back into filtered_feature_bc_matrix/raw_feature_bc_matrix so Seurat can consume them. It replaces running a second CellRanger pass with a combined host+pathogen reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: scPathoQuant takes host-unaligned reads from cellranger count 10x output, remaps them to a pathogen reference (default bbmap, alternative bowtie2), quantifies per-cell total pathogen reads and gene-level UMI counts with htseq, and writes the pathogen counts back into filtered_feature_bc_matrix/raw_feature_bc_matrix so Seurat can consume them. It replaces running a second CellRanger pass with a combined host+pathogen reference.
