skills.description: Use when two cellranger count runs on identical reads must be compared by per-cell QC summary statistics to quantify the effect of swapping the reference annotation (e.g. canonical vs. peaks2utr-augmented GFF3).
skills.name: per-cell-qc-metrics-extraction
skills.search_text: per-cell-qc-metrics-extraction Use when two cellranger count runs on identical reads must be compared by per-cell QC summary statistics to quantify the effect of swapping the reference annotation (e.g. canonical vs. peaks2utr-augmented GFF3). There is only a single Cell Ranger run with no second reference/condition to compare against The BAM reads are not from a 3'-enriched single-cell protocol — peaks2utr favours BAM files from runs like 10x Chromium where signal is concentrated at UTR distal ends The per-cell metrics table already exists (e.g. the cellranger_per_cell_metrics_comparison.csv has been produced) and only downstream interpretation is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts and compares per-cell quality metrics (median genes per cell, median UMIs per cell) from paired Cell Ranger 6.1.1 runs — one against a canonical reference, one against a peaks2utr-augmented reference — to quantify how 3' UTR annotation changes alter T. brucei 10x Chromium scRNA-seq capture efficiency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Extracts and compares per-cell quality metrics (median genes per cell, median UMIs per cell) from paired Cell Ranger 6.1.1 runs — one against a canonical reference, one against a peaks2utr-augmented reference — to quantify how 3' UTR annotation changes alter T. brucei 10x Chromium scRNA-seq capture efficiency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is only a single Cell Ranger run with no second reference/condition to compare against The BAM reads are not from a 3'-enriched single-cell protocol — peaks2utr favours BAM files from runs like 10x Chromium where signal is concentrated at UTR distal ends The per-cell metrics table already exists (e.g. the cellranger_per_cell_metrics_comparison.csv has been produced) and only downstream interpretation is needed

skills.description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A + per-cell velocities) and need TF-level, per-cell activity scores to identify regulators whose influence varies across clusters, e.g. acinar vs transitioning vs duct-like populations.
skills.name: per-cell-regulator-activity-comparison-across-clusters
skills.search_text: per-cell-regulator-activity-comparison-across-clusters Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A + per-cell velocities) and need TF-level, per-cell activity scores to identify regulators whose influence varies across clusters, e.g. acinar vs transitioning vs duct-like populations. No fitted scKINETICS model is available — the GRN matrix A and original velocities must first be produced by model fitting (EM estimation), so this skill cannot run on raw expression data alone The question is differential gene expression between clusters rather than regulator influence — activity scores measure regulatory impact via velocity perturbation, not expression abundance (e.g. Ptf1a scores are high despite low expression) You need perturbation effects on cell fate/phenotype trajectories rather than per-cell regulator activity scores from velocity ablation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Quantifies each transcription factor's regulatory influence at single-cell resolution by in silico knockout: zeroing the TF's column in the learned GRN, recomputing scKINETICS velocities, and scoring perturbation effects as per-cell cosine distance between original and perturbed velocity vectors, then comparing activity patterns across cell clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Quantifies each transcription factor's regulatory influence at single-cell resolution by in silico knockout: zeroing the TF's column in the learned GRN, recomputing scKINETICS velocities, and scoring perturbation effects as per-cell cosine distance between original and perturbed velocity vectors, then comparing activity patterns across cell clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No fitted scKINETICS model is available — the GRN matrix A and original velocities must first be produced by model fitting (EM estimation), so this skill cannot run on raw expression data alone The question is differential gene expression between clusters rather than regulator influence — activity scores measure regulatory impact via velocity perturbation, not expression abundance (e.g. Ptf1a scores are high despite low expression) You need perturbation effects on cell fate/phenotype trajectories rather than per-cell regulator activity scores from velocity ablation

skills.description: Use when per-cell annotation or disease scores (e.g., LHSC_per_cell_score, Neoplastic_monocyte_per_cell_score) are stored in a Seurat object's metadata and you need to compare their spatial/UMAP distributions across biological conditions such as healthy vs AML or diagnosis vs relapse.
skills.name: per-cell-signature-score-visualization
skills.search_text: per-cell-signature-score-visualization Use when per-cell annotation or disease scores (e.g., LHSC_per_cell_score, Neoplastic_monocyte_per_cell_score) are stored in a Seurat object's metadata and you need to compare their spatial/UMAP distributions across biological conditions such as healthy vs AML or diagnosis vs relapse. Input data are raw counts without per-cell signature scores in meta.data — run accordion_disease() scoring first rather than visualizing counts directly The goal is cluster-level annotation (accordion_per_cluster) rather than continuous per-cell score comparison across conditions; use DimPlot instead The dataset is spatial omics or a non-Seurat feature table where FeaturePlot/UMAP splitting by condition is not applicable Visualize per-cell disease-signature scores (e.g., LHSC and Neoplastic Monocyte scores computed by the Cell Marker Accordion accordion_disease function) on a Seurat object using FeaturePlot split by condition (healthy vs AML), with quantile-based color cutoffs to expose aberrant-cell enrichment patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Visualize per-cell disease-signature scores (e.g., LHSC and Neoplastic Monocyte scores computed by the Cell Marker Accordion accordion_disease function) on a Seurat object using FeaturePlot split by condition (healthy vs AML), with quantile-based color cutoffs to expose aberrant-cell enrichment patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw counts without per-cell signature scores in meta.data — run accordion_disease() scoring first rather than visualizing counts directly The goal is cluster-level annotation (accordion_per_cluster) rather than continuous per-cell score comparison across conditions; use DimPlot instead The dataset is spatial omics or a non-Seurat feature table where FeaturePlot/UMAP splitting by condition is not applicable

skills.description: Use when an AnnData scRNA-seq object and a gene-age orthomap (e.g. from OrthoFinder/oggmap) are available and you need gene age-weighted expression summaries such as per-cell or per-stage TEI to test developmental hourglass patterns.
skills.name: per-cell-tei-computation
skills.search_text: per-cell-tei-computation Use when an AnnData scRNA-seq object and a gene-age orthomap (e.g. from OrthoFinder/oggmap) are available and you need gene age-weighted expression summaries such as per-cell or per-stage TEI to test developmental hourglass patterns. The input is already a gene age-weighted expression matrix or a computed TEI vector — re-running get_tei would double-weight the data No orthomap (gene ages per orthogroup) exists for the query species and generating one (OrthoFinder/oggmap extraction) has not been done — compute the orthomap first The goal is orthogroup/gene-age extraction itself (cds2aa, of2orthomap, gtf2t2g) rather than linking ages to expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute a per-cell transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) by weighting gene expression in an scRNA-seq object (AnnData/Scanpy) with gene age classes from an oggmap orthomap, then aggregate stage/cell-type-level TEI profiles to detect evolutionary hourglass patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Compute a per-cell transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) by weighting gene expression in an scRNA-seq object (AnnData/Scanpy) with gene age classes from an oggmap orthomap, then aggregate stage/cell-type-level TEI profiles to detect evolutionary hourglass patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene age-weighted expression matrix or a computed TEI vector — re-running get_tei would double-weight the data No orthomap (gene ages per orthogroup) exists for the query species and generating one (OrthoFinder/oggmap extraction) has not been done — compute the orthomap first The goal is orthogroup/gene-age extraction itself (cds2aa, of2orthomap, gtf2t2g) rather than linking ages to expression data

skills.description: Use when you have cell-type label predictions for query datasets mapped onto a pre-trained reference (e.g., scCobra KNN label transfer on GSE114297/GSE85247/GSE83312 pancreas queries) and need a per-cell-type accuracy breakdown, such as reproducing the Fig. 6b-e ACC heatmap.
skills.name: per-cell-type-accuracy-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-accuracy-heatmap-visualization Use when you have cell-type label predictions for query datasets mapped onto a pre-trained reference (e.g., scCobra KNN label transfer on GSE114297/GSE85247/GSE83312 pancreas queries) and need a per-cell-type accuracy breakdown, such as reproducing the Fig. 6b-e ACC heatmap. Reference and query datasets do not originate from the same tissue type or do not contain similar cell types, making per-cell-type accuracy comparison unreliable Predictions come from a method that retrained on the query data rather than online label transfer with a frozen encoder, so the comparison to Fig. 6b-e is not meaningful Input is raw counts without the paper's preprocessing (cells < 200 genes filtered, genes < 3 cells filtered, mito fraction > 5% removed, log1p normalization), since accuracy values will not match the published heatmap http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Renders a per-cell-type accuracy (ACC) heatmap that breaks down label-transfer performance of annotated query cells (e.g., scCobra online label transfer onto a pancreas reference atlas) by reference cell type, exposing which cell types the pre-trained KNN classifier annotates well versus poorly. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Renders a per-cell-type accuracy (ACC) heatmap that breaks down label-transfer performance of annotated query cells (e.g., scCobra online label transfer onto a pancreas reference atlas) by reference cell type, exposing which cell types the pre-trained KNN classifier annotates well versus poorly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference and query datasets do not originate from the same tissue type or do not contain similar cell types, making per-cell-type accuracy comparison unreliable Predictions come from a method that retrained on the query data rather than online label transfer with a frozen encoder, so the comparison to Fig. 6b-e is not meaningful Input is raw counts without the paper's preprocessing (cells < 200 genes filtered, genes < 3 cells filtered, mito fraction > 5% removed, log1p normalization), since accuracy values will not match the published heatmap

skills.description: Use when you have a pretrained Miscell latent feature matrix (e.g. from PBMC scRNA-seq) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well those features separate 7 cell types via a linear probe.
skills.name: per-cell-type-auroc-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-auroc-evaluation Use when you have a pretrained Miscell latent feature matrix (e.g. from PBMC scRNA-seq) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well those features separate 7 cell types via a linear probe. The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so the linear probe on latent features would not be reliable on small datasets The data contain uncorrected batch effects: Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods, so latent features (and hence classifier metrics) would be confounded Input is raw gene expression rather than Miscell latent features; this skill evaluates the learned representation, so features must first be extracted with the pretrained model http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates the cell-type information content of Miscell latent features by training a single-layer linear classifier (scikit-learn logistic regression) on the latent representation of 43,095 PBMCs and computing one-vs-rest AUROC and accuracy for each of the 7 PBMC cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Evaluates the cell-type information content of Miscell latent features by training a single-layer linear classifier (scikit-learn logistic regression) on the latent representation of 43,095 PBMCs and computing one-vs-rest AUROC and accuracy for each of the 7 PBMC cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small: Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, so the linear probe on latent features would not be reliable on small datasets The data contain uncorrected batch effects: Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods, so latent features (and hence classifier metrics) would be confounded Input is raw gene expression rather than Miscell latent features; this skill evaluates the learned representation, so features must first be extracted with the pretrained model

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells carry per-cell activity scores (from ORIGINS2 activity()) plus known cell-type labels, and you need density distributions per type to compare biological programs across clusters.
skills.name: per-cell-type-density-estimation
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-density-estimation Use when scRNA-seq cells carry per-cell activity scores (from ORIGINS2 activity()) plus known cell-type labels, and you need density distributions per type to compare biological programs across clusters. Cells lack per-cell type annotations, so no per-type stratification of the activity distribution can be formed The goal is annotating unlabeled cells from scratch via PPIN activity rather than comparing densities across already-assigned types The expression matrix is raw counts rather than the normalized expression matrix activity() expects http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate and plot per-cell-type probability densities of computed PPIN activity scores (e.g., GO:0030154 cell differentiation) so that distributions can be compared across annotated cell populations (L1, L2, basal) in a scRNA-seq sample, optionally overlaid on a precomputed UMAP embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Estimate and plot per-cell-type probability densities of computed PPIN activity scores (e.g., GO:0030154 cell differentiation) so that distributions can be compared across annotated cell populations (L1, L2, basal) in a scRNA-seq sample, optionally overlaid on a precomputed UMAP embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack per-cell type annotations, so no per-type stratification of the activity distribution can be formed The goal is annotating unlabeled cells from scratch via PPIN activity rather than comparing densities across already-assigned types The expression matrix is raw counts rather than the normalized expression matrix activity() expects

skills.description: Use when Chord (or another doublet caller) has output predicted doublet barcodes for annotated scRNA-seq samples and you need per-sample doublet rates and per-cell-type doublet proportions to identify doublet-enriched populations.
skills.name: per-cell-type-doublet-proportion-quantification
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-doublet-proportion-quantification Use when Chord (or another doublet caller) has output predicted doublet barcodes for annotated scRNA-seq samples and you need per-sample doublet rates and per-cell-type doublet proportions to identify doublet-enriched populations. When the dataset has experimental doublet labels (e.g., cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet calls) — direct experimental annotation is preferable to summarizing computational Chord calls. When cell-type annotations are absent or untrusted — cross-tabulating doublets against unvalidated annotations yields misleading per-type proportions. When the goal is doublet detection itself rather than downstream summarization — use the chord() detection workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Cross-tabulates Chord-predicted doublet barcodes against cell-type annotations and per-sample totals to quantify doublet burden per cell type and per sample, revealing which populations (e.g., myeloid vs fibroblasts) are enriched for doublets in real-world scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Cross-tabulates Chord-predicted doublet barcodes against cell-type annotations and per-sample totals to quantify doublet burden per cell type and per sample, revealing which populations (e.g., myeloid vs fibroblasts) are enriched for doublets in real-world scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset has experimental doublet labels (e.g., cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet calls) — direct experimental annotation is preferable to summarizing computational Chord calls. When cell-type annotations are absent or untrusted — cross-tabulating doublets against unvalidated annotations yields misleading per-type proportions. When the goal is doublet detection itself rather than downstream summarization — use the chord() detection workflow instead.

skills.description: Use when you have PacBio/ONT single-cell long-read fastq.gz files plus a barcode-to-cell-type assignment table (e.g. from Seurat short-read analysis) and need per-cell-type isoform, TSS, or polyA counts.
skills.name: per-cell-type-isoform-quantification
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-isoform-quantification Use when you have PacBio/ONT single-cell long-read fastq.gz files plus a barcode-to-cell-type assignment table (e.g. from Seurat short-read analysis) and need per-cell-type isoform, TSS, or polyA counts. Input reads lack single-cell barcodes or a barcode-to-celltype assignment file — the quantification depends on assigning every long read to a cell type via deconvolved barcodes You only need gene-level expression counts, not isoform/TSS/polyA resolution — short-read quantification pipelines are more appropriate Differential exon-level splicing tests are the sole goal and isoform-level testing is unnecessary (note the paper found isoform tests perform better for DIE, but ExonQuant exists for that narrower need) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify isoform, TSS, and polyA-site usage per cell type from ScISOrSeq long reads by chaining scisorseqr barcode deconvolution, STARlong/Minimap2 alignment, full-length spliced-read filtering, and IsoQuant, producing cell-type-resolved isoform count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Quantify isoform, TSS, and polyA-site usage per cell type from ScISOrSeq long reads by chaining scisorseqr barcode deconvolution, STARlong/Minimap2 alignment, full-length spliced-read filtering, and IsoQuant, producing cell-type-resolved isoform count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads lack single-cell barcodes or a barcode-to-celltype assignment file — the quantification depends on assigning every long read to a cell type via deconvolved barcodes You only need gene-level expression counts, not isoform/TSS/polyA resolution — short-read quantification pipelines are more appropriate Differential exon-level splicing tests are the sole goal and isoform-level testing is unnecessary (note the paper found isoform tests perform better for DIE, but ExonQuant exists for that narrower need)

skills.description: Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq reference matrix (cells × genes with cell-type annotations) and need cell-type-level mean expression vectors to feed the E-test ΔS gene-selection statistic or a multinomial MLE classifier.
skills.name: per-cell-type-mean-expression-computation
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-mean-expression-computation Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq reference matrix (cells × genes with cell-type annotations) and need cell-type-level mean expression vectors to feed the E-test ΔS gene-selection statistic or a multinomial MLE classifier. The expression matrix has no cell-type labels — the E-test ΔS statistic requires annotated groups to compute per-type means. Data are raw UMI counts or raw TPM that have not been log-normalized; the multinomial parameter estimation with Laplace smoothing assumes normalized values. The goal is unsupervised dimensionality reduction (e.g. HVG detection without labels) rather than supervised gene selection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the per-cell-type mean expression vector for every gene in a labeled single-cell training matrix (e.g., the 70% reference split of GSE104276); these means are the foundation of SciBet's E-test ΔS statistic and its multinomial likelihood classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Computes the per-cell-type mean expression vector for every gene in a labeled single-cell training matrix (e.g., the 70% reference split of GSE104276); these means are the foundation of SciBet's E-test ΔS statistic and its multinomial likelihood classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has no cell-type labels — the E-test ΔS statistic requires annotated groups to compute per-type means. Data are raw UMI counts or raw TPM that have not been log-normalized; the multinomial parameter estimation with Laplace smoothing assumes normalized values. The goal is unsupervised dimensionality reduction (e.g. HVG detection without labels) rather than supervised gene selection.

skills.description: Use when a gene metagene or embedding-derived gene program must be validated as cell-type-independent by comparing per-cell scaled expression of its member genes between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control) within each annotated cell type.
skills.name: per-cell-type-scaled-expression-differential-analysis
skills.search_text: per-cell-type-scaled-expression-differential-analysis Use when a gene metagene or embedding-derived gene program must be validated as cell-type-independent by comparing per-cell scaled expression of its member genes between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control) within each annotated cell type. When the goal is batch correction or cell type annotation rather than validating a metagene's cell-type independence — use CellEmbedding batch_correct or phenotype_probability instead. When genes must be distinguished as activated versus repressed — GeneVector's mutual information is agnostic to the direction of statistical dependency, so scaled-expression contrasts cannot establish repression. When the input is not an AnnData object with raw counts in .X and existing cell type annotations; the within-cell-type comparison requires an obs-level cell type key. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Confirms that a GeneVector-derived metagene (e.g., the IFIT1-containing ISG program in interferon beta-stimulated PBMCs) is elevated across every annotated cell type by computing mean scaled expression per cell in stimulated versus control conditions within each cell type, avoiding the cell-type confounding seen in PCA and LDVAE loadings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Confirms that a GeneVector-derived metagene (e.g., the IFIT1-containing ISG program in interferon beta-stimulated PBMCs) is elevated across every annotated cell type by computing mean scaled expression per cell in stimulated versus control conditions within each cell type, avoiding the cell-type confounding seen in PCA and LDVAE loadings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch correction or cell type annotation rather than validating a metagene's cell-type independence — use CellEmbedding batch_correct or phenotype_probability instead. When genes must be distinguished as activated versus repressed — GeneVector's mutual information is agnostic to the direction of statistical dependency, so scaled-expression contrasts cannot establish repression. When the input is not an AnnData object with raw counts in .X and existing cell type annotations; the within-cell-type comparison requires an obs-level cell type key.

skills.description: Use when two 10x scRNA-seq libraries must be compared for equal per-cell capture depth (genes/UMIs per cell), e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs, after matching mean reads per cell by downsampling.
skills.name: per-cell-umi-count-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: per-cell-umi-count-statistical-testing Use when two 10x scRNA-seq libraries must be compared for equal per-cell capture depth (genes/UMIs per cell), e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs, after matching mean reads per cell by downsampling. The gene-barcode matrices were generated under unequal mean reads per cell — downsample first, otherwise the count comparison is confounded by depth The question is about expression levels rather than detection depth/sensitivity — per-cell UMI testing does not address differential expression Input is already an aggregated per-sample summary (e.g. median counts) — the t-test requires per-cell values http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistically compares per-cell detection depth (number of detected genes and UMI counts per cell) between two scRNA-seq preparations, e.g. fresh versus cryopreserved PBMCs, using two-sided t-tests after read downsampling, to test whether sample handling compromises counting sensitivity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Statistically compares per-cell detection depth (number of detected genes and UMI counts per cell) between two scRNA-seq preparations, e.g. fresh versus cryopreserved PBMCs, using two-sided t-tests after read downsampling, to test whether sample handling compromises counting sensitivity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene-barcode matrices were generated under unequal mean reads per cell — downsample first, otherwise the count comparison is confounded by depth The question is about expression levels rather than detection depth/sensitivity — per-cell UMI testing does not address differential expression Input is already an aggregated per-sample summary (e.g. median counts) — the t-test requires per-cell values

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample pathogen_al_counts.csv files from scPathoQuant runs over a multi-virus reference (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 + metapneumovirus) and need to aggregate per-cell counts into a per-virus infected-cell and read-abundance table.
skills.name: per-cell-viral-read-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-cell-viral-read-count-aggregation Use when you have per-sample pathogen_al_counts.csv files from scPathoQuant runs over a multi-virus reference (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 + metapneumovirus) and need to aggregate per-cell counts into a per-virus infected-cell and read-abundance table. The input is not 10x scRNAseq data already processed with cellranger count (scPathoQuant expects the cellranger output folder as -10x input). You need pathogen gene-level quantification rather than total pathogen reads per cell — that requires supplying a pathogen gtf alongside the fasta. The reference folder would contain more than 2 fasta entries, which exceeds the documented scPathoQuant multi-virus configuration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Aggregates scPathoQuant pathogen_al_counts.csv outputs (total pathogen reads per cell per sample) into a per-patient, per-virus detection table listing infected-cell counts and read abundance for each pathogen, exploiting scPathoQuant's ability to differentiate multiple viruses in a single 10x scRNAseq sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Aggregates scPathoQuant pathogen_al_counts.csv outputs (total pathogen reads per cell per sample) into a per-patient, per-virus detection table listing infected-cell counts and read abundance for each pathogen, exploiting scPathoQuant's ability to differentiate multiple viruses in a single 10x scRNAseq sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not 10x scRNAseq data already processed with cellranger count (scPathoQuant expects the cellranger output folder as -10x input). You need pathogen gene-level quantification rather than total pathogen reads per cell — that requires supplying a pathogen gtf alongside the fasta. The reference folder would contain more than 2 fasta entries, which exceeds the documented scPathoQuant multi-virus configuration.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an annotation or classification model whose improvement is concentrated in minority classes, and aggregate metrics would hide the rare-class gains.
skills.name: per-class-f1-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-class-f1-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking an annotation or classification model whose improvement is concentrated in minority classes, and aggregate metrics would hide the rare-class gains. When the goal is overall annotation accuracy on balanced cell types — macro aggregates or accuracy suffice and per-class breakdown adds little When no ground-truth labels exist for the query data, since per-class F1 and correct-assignment counts cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Evaluates cell-type annotation performance by computing correct-assignment counts and per-class F1 scores, specifically to quantify whether a model variant (e.g., SMOTE oversampling in SELINA) rescues rare cell-type annotation that is masked by overall accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Evaluates cell-type annotation performance by computing correct-assignment counts and per-class F1 scores, specifically to quantify whether a model variant (e.g., SMOTE oversampling in SELINA) rescues rare cell-type annotation that is masked by overall accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is overall annotation accuracy on balanced cell types — macro aggregates or accuracy suffice and per-class breakdown adds little When no ground-truth labels exist for the query data, since per-class F1 and correct-assignment counts cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when you have predicted cell-type annotations from a tool like Census plus reference labels for the same cells and need per-class F1 scores, or need to test annotation robustness across embedding parameter grids.
skills.name: per-class-f1-score-computation
skills.search_text: per-class-f1-score-computation Use when you have predicted cell-type annotations from a tool like Census plus reference labels for the same cells and need per-class F1 scores, or need to test annotation robustness across embedding parameter grids. There is no ground-truth reference annotation for the dataset, so no F1 can be computed against a reference The question is overall annotation accuracy across a benchmark of many tissues rather than robustness of per-class scores to embedding parameters Input predictions are probabilistic scores rather than discrete cell-type labels without an additional argmax/thresholding step Computes per-cell-type F1 scores by comparing an automated annotation method's predictions (e.g., Census cell-type calls from UMAP-embedded scRNA-seq data) against reference labels, and tests whether scores are stable across conditions (e.g., UMAP n.neighbors and min.dist settings) with Kruskal-Wallis tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Computes per-cell-type F1 scores by comparing an automated annotation method's predictions (e.g., Census cell-type calls from UMAP-embedded scRNA-seq data) against reference labels, and tests whether scores are stable across conditions (e.g., UMAP n.neighbors and min.dist settings) with Kruskal-Wallis tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no ground-truth reference annotation for the dataset, so no F1 can be computed against a reference The question is overall annotation accuracy across a benchmark of many tissues rather than robustness of per-class scores to embedding parameters Input predictions are probabilistic scores rather than discrete cell-type labels without an additional argmax/thresholding step

skills.description: Use when a multiclass or hierarchical cell-type classifier must be validated against labelled ground truth and reported per cell type, e.g. fivefold cross-validation on the pan-cancer training reference or the blood/stroma/cancer benchmark of Fig. 2c.
skills.name: per-class-f1-score-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-class-f1-score-evaluation Use when a multiclass or hierarchical cell-type classifier must be validated against labelled ground truth and reported per cell type, e.g. fivefold cross-validation on the pan-cancer training reference or the blood/stroma/cancer benchmark of Fig. 2c. No per-cell ground-truth labels exist for the sample — F1 cannot be computed without held-out truth, so this applies only to stratified CV folds or externally validated biopsies Input is a normal tissue sample — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present and should not be used in normal tissue applications Data are pooled across patients — inter-patient cancer-cell effects interfere with scATOMIC's cancer signature scoring and classification confidence, invalidating per-biopsy benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates a cell-type classifier by computing per-class precision, recall, and F1 against per-cell ground-truth labels, as used to benchmark scATOMIC's pan-cancer TME annotations (median fivefold CV F1 0.90–0.99) against six comparator annotators. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: Evaluates a cell-type classifier by computing per-class precision, recall, and F1 against per-cell ground-truth labels, as used to benchmark scATOMIC's pan-cancer TME annotations (median fivefold CV F1 0.90–0.99) against six comparator annotators.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No per-cell ground-truth labels exist for the sample — F1 cannot be computed without held-out truth, so this applies only to stratified CV folds or externally validated biopsies Input is a normal tissue sample — the default scATOMIC model assumes at least some cancer cells are present and should not be used in normal tissue applications Data are pooled across patients — inter-patient cancer-cell effects interfere with scATOMIC's cancer signature scoring and classification confidence, invalidating per-biopsy benchmarking

skills.description: Use when comparing classifiers trained on different gene feature spaces over the five PAM50 subtypes, and you need per-class (subtype) recalls, macro-averaged recall, and precision on a held-out test split rather than aggregate accuracy alone.
skills.name: per-class-recall-performance-benchmarking
skills.search_text: per-class-recall-performance-benchmarking Use when comparing classifiers trained on different gene feature spaces over the five PAM50 subtypes, and you need per-class (subtype) recalls, macro-averaged recall, and precision on a held-out test split rather than aggregate accuracy alone. You only need a single aggregate accuracy number and class balance is not a concern — overall accuracy suffices and per-class recalls add unnecessary computation. Labels are not the five PAM50 intrinsic subtypes (e.g. microarray AWCA classifications of GSE4922/GSE1456) — the reported recall checkpoints (Her2-Enriched 93%, macro-recall 0.94) are specific to the TCGA RNA-seq subtype setting. The published subtype labels were themselves generated by PAM50 on the same gene panel — the article warns such accuracies are biased, so per-class recall benchmarking against PAM50-derived labels will overestimate Her2-enriched/Normal-like performance. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark a regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) breast-cancer intrinsic subtyping model not only by overall accuracy on a held-out TCGA test split, but by per-subtype recall (Luminal A, Luminal B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like), macro-averaged recall, and precision across competing feature spaces (filters and limmaN signatures). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Benchmark a regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) breast-cancer intrinsic subtyping model not only by overall accuracy on a held-out TCGA test split, but by per-subtype recall (Luminal A, Luminal B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like), macro-averaged recall, and precision across competing feature spaces (filters and limmaN signatures).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single aggregate accuracy number and class balance is not a concern — overall accuracy suffices and per-class recalls add unnecessary computation. Labels are not the five PAM50 intrinsic subtypes (e.g. microarray AWCA classifications of GSE4922/GSE1456) — the reported recall checkpoints (Her2-Enriched 93%, macro-recall 0.94) are specific to the TCGA RNA-seq subtype setting. The published subtype labels were themselves generated by PAM50 on the same gene panel — the article warns such accuracies are biased, so per-class recall benchmarking against PAM50-derived labels will overestimate Her2-enriched/Normal-like performance.

skills.description: Use when a CMS prediction (or any 4-class sample-subtype assignment) must be validated sample-by-sample against original reference labels on a held-out cohort and per-class sensitivity/specificity are required, not just a single accuracy figure.
skills.name: per-class-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
skills.search_text: per-class-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation Use when a CMS prediction (or any 4-class sample-subtype assignment) must be validated sample-by-sample against original reference labels on a held-out cohort and per-class sensitivity/specificity are required, not just a single accuracy figure. Input samples are metastatic CRC biopsies or otherwise have a different human stromal component than primary CRCs — CMScaller is not recommended for such samples in its current implementation Dataset contains fewer than approximately forty samples — the required centering/scaling inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty for small datasets Input is single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and not what the classifier was optimized for http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates a nearest-template-prediction CMS classifier against reference labels on a held-out test set (TCGA pCRC, n = 143) by computing overall accuracy with a 95% confidence interval plus class-wise sensitivity and specificity for CMS1–CMS4, mirroring the CMScaller benchmark (accuracy 0.83; CMS3 sensitivity 0.71; CMS4 specificity 0.91). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Evaluates a nearest-template-prediction CMS classifier against reference labels on a held-out test set (TCGA pCRC, n = 143) by computing overall accuracy with a 95% confidence interval plus class-wise sensitivity and specificity for CMS1–CMS4, mirroring the CMScaller benchmark (accuracy 0.83; CMS3 sensitivity 0.71; CMS4 specificity 0.91).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are metastatic CRC biopsies or otherwise have a different human stromal component than primary CRCs — CMScaller is not recommended for such samples in its current implementation Dataset contains fewer than approximately forty samples — the required centering/scaling inescapably introduces prediction uncertainty for small datasets Input is single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and not what the classifier was optimized for

skills.description: Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB output) for two or more conditions and want to identify cell clusters whose total interaction counts differ strikingly between conditions.
skills.name: per-cluster-interaction-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-cluster-interaction-count-aggregation Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB output) for two or more conditions and want to identify cell clusters whose total interaction counts differ strikingly between conditions. Input is raw scRNA-seq data or cluster assignments without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow starts from CCI data, not expression matrices The CCI data comes from a prediction tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) The question concerns which genes or pathways drive the interactions — this belongs to the gene-verse or function-verse, not per-cluster count aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 Aggregate predicted ligand-receptor interaction counts per cell cluster in InterCellar's cluster-verse, classifying each interaction as autocrine or paracrine, then render a back-to-back barplot to compare per-cluster totals between conditions (e.g., critical vs. moderate COVID-19). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02986-2
skills.summary: Aggregate predicted ligand-receptor interaction counts per cell cluster in InterCellar's cluster-verse, classifying each interaction as autocrine or paracrine, then render a back-to-back barplot to compare per-cluster totals between conditions (e.g., critical vs. moderate COVID-19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scRNA-seq data or cluster assignments without pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions — InterCellar's workflow starts from CCI data, not expression matrices The CCI data comes from a prediction tool outside InterCellar's supported input set (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) The question concerns which genes or pathways drive the interactions — this belongs to the gene-verse or function-verse, not per-cluster count aggregation

skills.description: Use when analyzing a preprocessed Seurat object (e.g., Tyser 2021, 1195 cells) and the goal is cluster-specific binary markers — genes expressed exclusively in one cell population — rather than graded average-expression DE.
skills.name: per-cluster-marker-ranking-by-ncdi
skills.search_text: per-cluster-marker-ranking-by-ncdi Use when analyzing a preprocessed Seurat object (e.g., Tyser 2021, 1195 cells) and the goal is cluster-specific binary markers — genes expressed exclusively in one cell population — rather than graded average-expression DE. The goal is standard average-expression differential expression between clusters rather than identification of binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) exclusively expressed in one population The analysis requires accounting for variation across biological replicates — CDI is a known exception to replicate-aware DE methods The gene space has not been restricted to expressed genes; running CDI on the full feature space is computationally intensive http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements the co-dependency index (CDI) differential expression approach from scMiko/scPipeline to identify binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) — genes exclusively expressed in one cell population — and ranks the top marker(s) per cluster by the normalized nCDI score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Implements the co-dependency index (CDI) differential expression approach from scMiko/scPipeline to identify binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) — genes exclusively expressed in one cell population — and ranks the top marker(s) per cluster by the normalized nCDI score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard average-expression differential expression between clusters rather than identification of binary differentially-expressed genes (bDEGs) exclusively expressed in one population The analysis requires accounting for variation across biological replicates — CDI is a known exception to replicate-aware DE methods The gene space has not been restricted to expressed genes; running CDI on the full feature space is computationally intensive

skills.search_text: per-cluster-metric-aggregation Use when a per-cell metric must be summarized per annotated cluster and globally to compare methods, e.g. local velocity inconsistency via mean cosine distance to k=30 neighbors across velocity methods. Cluster annotations are missing or unreliable, since per-cluster aggregation would inherit annotation errors The metric being aggregated is not per-cell (e.g., dataset-level summary statistics), making cluster-wise averaging meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates a per-cell quality metric (e.g., cosine distance between a cell's velocity vector and its k=30 neighbors' velocities) within annotated clusters and across the dataset, enabling method-level comparison of velocity consistency for scKINETICS versus baselines like scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Aggregates a per-cell quality metric (e.g., cosine distance between a cell's velocity vector and its k=30 neighbors' velocities) within annotated clusters and across the dataset, enabling method-level comparison of velocity consistency for scKINETICS versus baselines like scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cluster annotations are missing or unreliable, since per-cluster aggregation would inherit annotation errors The metric being aggregated is not per-cell (e.g., dataset-level summary statistics), making cluster-wise averaging meaningless

skills.description: Use when mapping a query single-cell dataset onto a Symphony reference and you need to detect query cell populations (clusters) that are absent from the reference, e.g. after holding out or ablating a cell type.
skills.name: per-cluster-metric-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-cluster-metric-aggregation Use when mapping a query single-cell dataset onto a Symphony reference and you need to detect query cell populations (clusters) that are absent from the reference, e.g. after holding out or ablating a cell type. When the novel query population is very similar to an existing reference population — the paper states these metrics 'may be less informative in cases where the novel population is very similar to an existing reference population' When the goal is de novo discovery of novel cell types rather than flagging non-mapping populations — Symphony 'does not entirely supplant the need for users interested in novel cell type discovery to conduct de novo analyses of the query alone' When the query already has full cell-type coverage in the reference (no held-out/ablated types), since detection of missing types is the target task Aggregate Symphony's per-cell Mahalanobis-distance-based mapping metrics into per-cluster metrics (calcPerClusterMappingMetric) to flag query clusters that represent cell types missing from the reference, benchmarking detection with AUCs for held-out types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Aggregate Symphony's per-cell Mahalanobis-distance-based mapping metrics into per-cluster metrics (calcPerClusterMappingMetric) to flag query clusters that represent cell types missing from the reference, benchmarking detection with AUCs for held-out types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the novel query population is very similar to an existing reference population — the paper states these metrics 'may be less informative in cases where the novel population is very similar to an existing reference population' When the goal is de novo discovery of novel cell types rather than flagging non-mapping populations — Symphony 'does not entirely supplant the need for users interested in novel cell type discovery to conduct de novo analyses of the query alone' When the query already has full cell-type coverage in the reference (no held-out/ablated types), since detection of missing types is the target task

skills.description: Use when a cell-by-cell-type score matrix (e.g. ScType es.max output on a clustered Seurat object) must be collapsed into one label per cluster, with a minimum-score threshold to flag unannotated clusters.
skills.name: per-cluster-score-aggregation-and-thresholding
skills.search_text: per-cluster-score-aggregation-and-thresholding Use when a cell-by-cell-type score matrix (e.g. ScType es.max output on a clustered Seurat object) must be collapsed into one label per cluster, with a minimum-score threshold to flag unannotated clusters. The input is raw counts or unclustered cells — aggregation requires a prior FindClusters clustering and an es.max score matrix You need cell-level (not cluster-level) annotations or per-cell confidence values rather than a single label per cluster http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Aggregates ScType cell-type scores (es.max) per Seurat cluster by row sums, selects the top-scoring cell type per cluster with dplyr::top_n(n = 1, wt = scores), and labels low-confidence clusters as 'Unknown' when the aggregated score falls below ncells/4. This converts the cell-by-cell-type score matrix into discrete cluster-level annotations with an explicit confidence cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Aggregates ScType cell-type scores (es.max) per Seurat cluster by row sums, selects the top-scoring cell type per cluster with dplyr::top_n(n = 1, wt = scores), and labels low-confidence clusters as 'Unknown' when the aggregated score falls below ncells/4. This converts the cell-by-cell-type score matrix into discrete cluster-level annotations with an explicit confidence cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw counts or unclustered cells — aggregation requires a prior FindClusters clustering and an es.max score matrix You need cell-level (not cluster-level) annotations or per-cell confidence values rather than a single label per cluster

skills.description: Use when multiple segmentation configurations (e.g., loss-weight ablations) have been run and per-run metric values must be collected, tabulated, and compared against reference trends.
skills.name: per-configuration-result-tabulation
skills.search_text: per-configuration-result-tabulation Use when multiple segmentation configurations (e.g., loss-weight ablations) have been run and per-run metric values must be collected, tabulated, and compared against reference trends. Only a single segmentation configuration was run, so there is no cross-configuration ordering to tabulate or compare The task is benchmarking BIDCell against external methods (e.g., Cellpose, Baysor) rather than comparing internal loss-ablation configurations Assembles segmentation metric values (purity F1, captured transcripts, Chromium correlation) from each BIDCell ablation configuration into a single tabular file (ablation_metrics.csv) and verifies that the relative ordering of configurations reproduces the degradation trends reported in Supplementary Figs. 4-5. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Assembles segmentation metric values (purity F1, captured transcripts, Chromium correlation) from each BIDCell ablation configuration into a single tabular file (ablation_metrics.csv) and verifies that the relative ordering of configurations reproduces the degradation trends reported in Supplementary Figs. 4-5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single segmentation configuration was run, so there is no cross-configuration ordering to tabulate or compare The task is benchmarking BIDCell against external methods (e.g., Cellpose, Baysor) rather than comparing internal loss-ablation configurations

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell malignant-cell predictions from a scRNA-seq annotation model across many datasets and need to compare dataset-level malignant fractions against reference percentages (e.g., CancerSCEM database values).
skills.name: per-dataset-malignant-fraction-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-dataset-malignant-fraction-aggregation Use when you have per-cell malignant-cell predictions from a scRNA-seq annotation model across many datasets and need to compare dataset-level malignant fractions against reference percentages (e.g., CancerSCEM database values). Input data are from hematologic tumors — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data Single-cell datasets with no reference malignant-cell percentage available (e.g., unannotated cohorts), since the skill's validation step requires database-reported fractions Spatial transcriptomics spots where spatial relationships among spots matter — Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships in ST data http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates per-cell malignant/non-malignant predictions from Cancer-Finder into per-dataset malignant cell percentages across 152 CancerSCEM scRNA-seq datasets, then validates the predicted percentages against the database-reported percentages via a two-tailed Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Aggregates per-cell malignant/non-malignant predictions from Cancer-Finder into per-dataset malignant cell percentages across 152 CancerSCEM scRNA-seq datasets, then validates the predicted percentages against the database-reported percentages via a two-tailed Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are from hematologic tumors — the article explicitly does not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumor data Single-cell datasets with no reference malignant-cell percentage available (e.g., unannotated cohorts), since the skill's validation step requires database-reported fractions Spatial transcriptomics spots where spatial relationships among spots matter — Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships in ST data

skills.description: Use when precomputing scTab data augmentation: per-cell-type, per-donor mean expression centroids must be derived from a size-factor-normalized, log1p CxG matrix to build donor-difference augmentation vectors.
skills.name: per-donor-per-celltype-centroid-computation
skills.search_text: per-donor-per-celltype-centroid-computation Use when precomputing scTab data augmentation: per-cell-type, per-donor mean expression centroids must be derived from a size-factor-normalized, log1p CxG matrix to build donor-difference augmentation vectors. Input is raw-count or unnormalized data — centroids would mix library-size effects instead of reflecting size-factor-normalized (10,000 counts), log1p expression. The analysis needs per-cell resolution or within-group variance; per-(cell type, donor) means discard single-cell heterogeneity. Augmentation vectors are already precomputed (augmentation_vectors.parquet exists) and only sampling of stored vectors during training is required. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes mean gene-expression centroids per (cell type, donor) pair from a size-factor-normalized (10,000 counts) and log1p-transformed scRNA-seq cell-by-gene matrix; these group means are the basis from which scTab derives donor-difference augmentation vectors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Computes mean gene-expression centroids per (cell type, donor) pair from a size-factor-normalized (10,000 counts) and log1p-transformed scRNA-seq cell-by-gene matrix; these group means are the basis from which scTab derives donor-difference augmentation vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw-count or unnormalized data — centroids would mix library-size effects instead of reflecting size-factor-normalized (10,000 counts), log1p expression. The analysis needs per-cell resolution or within-group variance; per-(cell type, donor) means discard single-cell heterogeneity. Augmentation vectors are already precomputed (augmentation_vectors.parquet exists) and only sampling of stored vectors during training is required.

skills.search_text: per-factor-gene-count-aggregation Use when a workflow must reproduce or audit the composition statistics of the E.PATH database — e.g. count unique gene sets, annotated modules, or genes assigned to each environmental factor from gs_genes/gs_info and annotations files. skills.summary: Aggregates gene-set membership data from the E.PATH curated database into per-environmental-factor gene counts (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) and validates them against the paper's reported totals (18,015 diet, 13,259 infection, 3,841 smoking, 644 toxic-chemical genes; 25,789 unique genes overall).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is running enrichment on a user gene list (use E.PAGE's process_input_text/process_input_seurat and compute, not count aggregation) The database contains environmental factors beyond the four curated in this study (cigarette smoking, diet, infections, toxic chemicals) — the counts and match flags only apply to these categories Input is raw differential-expression data (e.g. GEO/MSigDB C7 downloads) that has not yet been curated into gene-set membership files

skills.description: Use when fitting NBGMMs with the nebula R package on multi-subject single-cell counts and you must decide, per gene, whether NEBULA-LN estimates suffice or NEBULA-HL re-estimation (full or partial, fixing phi) is required.
skills.name: per-gene-algorithm-dispatch-thresholding
skills.search_text: per-gene-algorithm-dispatch-thresholding Use when fitting NBGMMs with the nebula R package on multi-subject single-cell counts and you must decide, per gene, whether NEBULA-LN estimates suffice or NEBULA-HL re-estimation (full or partial, fixing phi) is required. Data with fewer than 30 cells per subject across the board — every gene routes to NEBULA-HL regardless, so the threshold dispatch is trivially unnecessary Genes whose NEBULA-LN fit has not yet been obtained (no sigma2_hat/phi_hat/c_hat available) — run nebula first; the dispatch operates on fitted LN outputs, not raw counts alone Genes with convergence code <= -20 or estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 — these should be removed or interpreted cautiously rather than mechanically refit with NEBULA-HL http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Routes each gene between NEBULA-LN (fast large-sample approximation) and NEBULA-HL (h-likelihood refit) using cells-per-subject (CPS) and estimated overdispersion thresholds, reserving the slower NEBULA-HL refit only for genes whose LN estimates are unreliable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Routes each gene between NEBULA-LN (fast large-sample approximation) and NEBULA-HL (h-likelihood refit) using cells-per-subject (CPS) and estimated overdispersion thresholds, reserving the slower NEBULA-HL refit only for genes whose LN estimates are unreliable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with fewer than 30 cells per subject across the board — every gene routes to NEBULA-HL regardless, so the threshold dispatch is trivially unnecessary Genes whose NEBULA-LN fit has not yet been obtained (no sigma2_hat/phi_hat/c_hat available) — run nebula first; the dispatch operates on fitted LN outputs, not raw counts alone Genes with convergence code <= -20 or estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 — these should be removed or interpreted cautiously rather than mechanically refit with NEBULA-HL

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq count data include paired samples or repeated measures from the same donor/patient (e.g. a patientID variable) and per-gene differential expression with random effects and fit metrics like AIC is needed.
skills.name: per-gene-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: per-gene-differential-expression-testing Use when RNA-seq count data include paired samples or repeated measures from the same donor/patient (e.g. a patientID variable) and per-gene differential expression with random effects and fit metrics like AIC is needed. Samples are unpaired / independent groups with no donor or patient repeated-measure structure — a simple fixed-effect linear model (kimma's lm run) or limma unpaired would suffice The analysis goal is genotyping/association testing rather than RNA-seq differential expression — kmFit_eQTL, not the per-gene DE mixed model, is the relevant kimma entry point Kinship/covariance structure among related individuals is not of interest and no kinship matrix is available — although kimma still supports plain random effects via lme4::lmer, the kinship-specific value of the package is not engaged http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit a per-gene linear mixed effects model to RNA-seq counts using kimma's kmFit (backed by lme4::lmer) to detect differentially expressed genes in paired/repeated-measure designs, reporting fixed-effect estimates, standard errors, P-values, and fit metrics (AIC/BIC) for each gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Fit a per-gene linear mixed effects model to RNA-seq counts using kimma's kmFit (backed by lme4::lmer) to detect differentially expressed genes in paired/repeated-measure designs, reporting fixed-effect estimates, standard errors, P-values, and fit metrics (AIC/BIC) for each gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are unpaired / independent groups with no donor or patient repeated-measure structure — a simple fixed-effect linear model (kimma's lm run) or limma unpaired would suffice The analysis goal is genotyping/association testing rather than RNA-seq differential expression — kmFit_eQTL, not the per-gene DE mixed model, is the relevant kimma entry point Kinship/covariance structure among related individuals is not of interest and no kinship matrix is available — although kimma still supports plain random effects via lme4::lmer, the kinship-specific value of the package is not engaged

skills.description: Use when raw pre-processed COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation records must be converted into the paper's 37 ratio-metric, entropy and frequency features per gene/transcript for driver-gene classification.
skills.name: per-gene-feature-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: per-gene-feature-matrix-construction Use when raw pre-processed COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation records must be converted into the paper's 37 ratio-metric, entropy and frequency features per gene/transcript for driver-gene classification. The processed feature matrix already exists (RamanLab/IdentifyTSGOG/data/FeatureMat/FeatureMat.tsv) and the goal is model training or prediction, not feature construction The input mutation dataset lacks the COSMIC mutation type annotations needed for the categorisation (e.g. the Tokheim et al. data, for which missense and frameshift entropy and frequency could not be calculated) The goal is background-mutation-rate-based driver detection (e.g. MutSigCV-style), which this feature-matrix approach deliberately avoids Regenerates the 37-feature per-gene/transcript matrix from pre-processed COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data using cTaG's categorisation of 11 COSMIC mutation types plus compound/LOF/damaging/benign classes, PolyPhen2-based HiFI/MiFI/LoFI missense binning, and entropy/frequency formulas. This matrix is the training input for the cTaG random-forest TSG/OG classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Regenerates the 37-feature per-gene/transcript matrix from pre-processed COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data using cTaG's categorisation of 11 COSMIC mutation types plus compound/LOF/damaging/benign classes, PolyPhen2-based HiFI/MiFI/LoFI missense binning, and entropy/frequency formulas. This matrix is the training input for the cTaG random-forest TSG/OG classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The processed feature matrix already exists (RamanLab/IdentifyTSGOG/data/FeatureMat/FeatureMat.tsv) and the goal is model training or prediction, not feature construction The input mutation dataset lacks the COSMIC mutation type annotations needed for the categorisation (e.g. the Tokheim et al. data, for which missense and frameshift entropy and frequency could not be calculated) The goal is background-mutation-rate-based driver detection (e.g. MutSigCV-style), which this feature-matrix approach deliberately avoids

skills.description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model must be interpreted to identify which genes drive cell type classification, e.g. reproducing Figure 2 gene rankings for testis and PBMC cell types.
skills.name: per-gene-importance-aggregation-per-cell-type
skills.search_text: per-gene-importance-aggregation-per-cell-type Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model must be interpreted to identify which genes drive cell type classification, e.g. reproducing Figure 2 gene rankings for testis and PBMC cell types. skills.search_text: per-spot-module-expression-scoring Use when you have a merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN divided into leiden subnetworks and need quantitative module activity scores per spatial spot or cell to support regional-specificity tests, clustering, or phenotype/plaque correlation analyses. skills.when_to_use_negative: When no gene modules/subnetworks have been defined yet — AUCell scoring requires a merged SCING GRN already partitioned with leiden; network construction and edge pruning must come first. skills.description: Use when testing many overlapping gene sets from summary-statistics-based enrichment (e.g., iDEA on scRNA-seq DE z-scores) and you need calibrated FDR estimates rather than naive p-value thresholds that ignore gene set non-independence.

skills.search_text: permutation-based-fdr-estimation Use when testing many overlapping gene sets from summary-statistics-based enrichment (e.g., iDEA on scRNA-seq DE z-scores) and you need calibrated FDR estimates rather than naive p-value thresholds that ignore gene set non-independence.
