skills.name: permutation-null-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: permutation-null-distribution-analysis Use when testing whether two transcriptome region sets (e.g., m6A RNA methylation sites and stop codon regions) colocalize more than expected by chance, especially when region-to-isoform association is ambiguous. When the analysis target is the genome rather than the transcriptome (existing genome-based tools like LOLA or GenomeRunner suffice and RgnTX's transcriptome null model is unnecessary) When only two static feature tables need interval overlap counting without a statistical significance assessment When regions have unambiguous isoform association AND a simple genome-based permutation is acceptable — RgnTX's isoform-aware machinery adds cost without benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Generates empirical null distributions of overlaps between transcriptome region sets using RgnTX permutation tests, enabling colocalization assessment of elements (e.g., m6A sites vs stop codons) that accounts for isoform heterogeneity and isoform ambiguity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Generates empirical null distributions of overlaps between transcriptome region sets using RgnTX permutation tests, enabling colocalization assessment of elements (e.g., m6A sites vs stop codons) that accounts for isoform heterogeneity and isoform ambiguity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis target is the genome rather than the transcriptome (existing genome-based tools like LOLA or GenomeRunner suffice and RgnTX's transcriptome null model is unnecessary) When only two static feature tables need interval overlap counting without a statistical significance assessment When regions have unambiguous isoform association AND a simple genome-based permutation is acceptable — RgnTX's isoform-aware machinery adds cost without benefit

skills.description: Use when you must demonstrate that an observed cell-to-cell similarity/distance metric (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity) exceeds random expectation, by comparing it against a label-permuted null and a competing baseline metric (e.g., Euclidean distance on HVG+PCA coordinates).
skills.name: permutation-null-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-null-hypothesis-testing Use when you must demonstrate that an observed cell-to-cell similarity/distance metric (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity) exceeds random expectation, by comparing it against a label-permuted null and a competing baseline metric (e.g., Euclidean distance on HVG+PCA coordinates). The input lacks cell-type labels or a marker panel that can assign per-cell labels, since the permutation null requires shuffling labels repeatedly. The data has not been reduced into a cell-similarity space (no archetypal/kernel embedding or PCA coordinates), because the test compares metric values rather than raw counts. The goal is a parametric significance test (e.g., t-test or ANOVA on metric values) rather than an empirical label-shuffled null of deviation from random expectation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds label-permutation null models to test whether ACTIONet's Jensen-Shannon-divergence (JSD)-based cell similarity separates same-type cells more strongly than random expectation — and more strongly than a Seurat-style HVG + PCA + Euclidean-distance baseline — as reported in Fig. 4e of the ACTIONet paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Builds label-permutation null models to test whether ACTIONet's Jensen-Shannon-divergence (JSD)-based cell similarity separates same-type cells more strongly than random expectation — and more strongly than a Seurat-style HVG + PCA + Euclidean-distance baseline — as reported in Fig. 4e of the ACTIONet paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks cell-type labels or a marker panel that can assign per-cell labels, since the permutation null requires shuffling labels repeatedly. The data has not been reduced into a cell-similarity space (no archetypal/kernel embedding or PCA coordinates), because the test compares metric values rather than raw counts. The goal is a parametric significance test (e.g., t-test or ANOVA on metric values) rather than an empirical label-shuffled null of deviation from random expectation.

skills.description: Use when detected network modules (e.g. fRNC global/local RNCs from ESCA TCGA data) must be validated against a random null to confirm their scores significantly exceed chance at the detection FDR threshold (1e-5).
skills.name: permutation-null-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-null-significance-testing Use when detected network modules (e.g. fRNC global/local RNCs from ESCA TCGA data) must be validated against a random null to confirm their scores significantly exceed chance at the detection FDR threshold (1e-5). Modules were not detected with fRNC's runmodule scoring scheme, so random node sets cannot be scored comparably The analysis goal is differential expression testing rather than module robustness against random node sets Computational budget cannot accommodate 100,000 random node-set score evaluations http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Assesses whether detected RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) modules are significantly more robust than random by building an empirical null distribution from 100,000 randomly sampled node sets matched to each module's size, then computing a one-sided empirical p-value for the module's observed summary score. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Assesses whether detected RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) modules are significantly more robust than random by building an empirical null distribution from 100,000 randomly sampled node sets matched to each module's size, then computing a one-sided empirical p-value for the module's observed summary score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modules were not detected with fRNC's runmodule scoring scheme, so random node sets cannot be scored comparably The analysis goal is differential expression testing rather than module robustness against random node sets Computational budget cannot accommodate 100,000 random node-set score evaluations

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether colocalization between two transcriptome region sets (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A sites and stop codon regions) is statistically significant, via a permutation-derived null distribution, p-value, z-score and shifted z-score.
skills.name: permutation-null-zscore-statistics
skills.search_text: permutation-null-zscore-statistics Use when you need to quantify whether colocalization between two transcriptome region sets (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A sites and stop codon regions) is statistically significant, via a permutation-derived null distribution, p-value, z-score and shifted z-score. When regions have unambiguous transcript isoform association and you need the plain permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick null model rather than the TxIA (isoform ambiguity) randomization. When you need an exact-test colocalization statistic (binomial, Fisher's exact, chi-square as in GREAT/LOLA/GenomeRunner) rather than a permutation-based null distribution. When the analysis background is the whole genome rather than transcriptome space — genome-based nulls produce significantly different overlap distributions from transcriptome-based nulls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes permutation-test statistics (p-value, z-score, shifted z-score, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value) for transcriptome colocalization analysis by comparing an observed overlap count against the null distribution of random overlaps generated by RgnTX's transcriptome-aware randomization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Computes permutation-test statistics (p-value, z-score, shifted z-score, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value) for transcriptome colocalization analysis by comparing an observed overlap count against the null distribution of random overlaps generated by RgnTX's transcriptome-aware randomization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When regions have unambiguous transcript isoform association and you need the plain permTestTx/permTestTx_customPick null model rather than the TxIA (isoform ambiguity) randomization. When you need an exact-test colocalization statistic (binomial, Fisher's exact, chi-square as in GREAT/LOLA/GenomeRunner) rather than a permutation-based null distribution. When the analysis background is the whole genome rather than transcriptome space — genome-based nulls produce significantly different overlap distributions from transcriptome-based nulls.

skills.description: Use when a permutation test from RgnTX (permTestTx, permTestTx_customPick, or permTestTxIA_customPick) has produced a null overlap distribution and you need to plot observed vs. random overlaps, p-values, or z-scores for a transcriptome colocalization result.
skills.name: permutation-result-visualization
skills.search_text: permutation-result-visualization Use when a permutation test from RgnTX (permTestTx, permTestTx_customPick, or permTestTxIA_customPick) has produced a null overlap distribution and you need to plot observed vs. random overlaps, p-values, or z-scores for a transcriptome colocalization result. When the colocalization question is genome-based only and isoform ambiguity/transcriptome shuffling is irrelevant — genome-based tools like regioneR or BEDTools are the appropriate comparison points. When no permutation test has been run yet — visualization requires an existing results object with a random overlap null distribution. When regions have clear isoform association and you need IA-mode accounting — use overlapCountsTx rather than overlapCountsTxIA as the evaluation function context. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Visualize RgnTX permutation test results by plotting the observed colocalization overlap of a region set (e.g., m7G sites against 5'UTR or CDS) relative to the transcriptome-wide shuffling null distribution, supporting summary-statistics plots like Fig. S2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Visualize RgnTX permutation test results by plotting the observed colocalization overlap of a region set (e.g., m7G sites against 5'UTR or CDS) relative to the transcriptome-wide shuffling null distribution, supporting summary-statistics plots like Fig. S2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the colocalization question is genome-based only and isoform ambiguity/transcriptome shuffling is irrelevant — genome-based tools like regioneR or BEDTools are the appropriate comparison points. When no permutation test has been run yet — visualization requires an existing results object with a random overlap null distribution. When regions have clear isoform association and you need IA-mode accounting — use overlapCountsTx rather than overlapCountsTxIA as the evaluation function context.

skills.description: Use when a NeuronChat run on scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics must identify which sender–receiver communication links are significant (p < 0.05) before aggregating networks, ranking interactions, or comparing conditions.
skills.name: permutation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-significance-testing Use when a NeuronChat run on scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics must identify which sender–receiver communication links are significant (p < 0.05) before aggregating networks, ranking interactions, or comparing conditions. Input is a spatial dataset where the goal is spatial proximity enrichment — that uses its own 1000-permutation label-permutation of cell/spot labels (cell_proximity_enrichment_score_single/multiple), not the M=100 group-label permutation in run_NeuronChat. The analysis goal is method benchmarking (AUROC/AUPRC against retrograde-tracing ground truth) without significance filtering context — the shuffled-label ablation of task_003 is a different permutation design (shuffling subclass labels to test topology dependence, not to assign link significance). Expression data has not been preprocessed (normalized to 10,000 scale with pseudocount 1 and log-transformed) and genes expressed in <25% of cells have not been filtered — running the permutation test on raw counts invalidates the Tukey-trimean ensemble averages. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assess the statistical significance of NeuronChat-inferred intercellular communication strengths by permuting cell-group labels and recomputing ligand-target communication, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg correction so only p < 0.05 links are retained. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Assess the statistical significance of NeuronChat-inferred intercellular communication strengths by permuting cell-group labels and recomputing ligand-target communication, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg correction so only p < 0.05 links are retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a spatial dataset where the goal is spatial proximity enrichment — that uses its own 1000-permutation label-permutation of cell/spot labels (cell_proximity_enrichment_score_single/multiple), not the M=100 group-label permutation in run_NeuronChat. The analysis goal is method benchmarking (AUROC/AUPRC against retrograde-tracing ground truth) without significance filtering context — the shuffled-label ablation of task_003 is a different permutation design (shuffling subclass labels to test topology dependence, not to assign link significance). Expression data has not been preprocessed (normalized to 10,000 scale with pseudocount 1 and log-transformed) and genes expressed in <25% of cells have not been filtered — running the permutation test on raw counts invalidates the Tukey-trimean ensemble averages.

skills.description: Use when you must attach an empirical significance level to an entropy- or potency-derived statistic — e.g. testing whether a bulk-sample signalling entropy (SR) significantly exceeds a matched single-cell SR distribution — without assuming a parametric null.
skills.name: permutation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-significance-testing Use when you must attach an empirical significance level to an entropy- or potency-derived statistic — e.g. testing whether a bulk-sample signalling entropy (SR) significantly exceeds a matched single-cell SR distribution — without assuming a parametric null. The observed statistic falls outside the single-cell reference range entirely (e.g. AML population SR=0.88 > max single-cell SR=0.82), where an exceedance comparison rather than resampling within the reference is the appropriate argument The statistic is a bulk-average profile with no regulated heterogeneity, which the control shows is correctly non-significant (P≈0.30) — do not force significance interpretation Entropies are transcriptomic entropies not based on network information (e.g. as in StemID/SLICE); the SCENT-network-based SR framework underpinning this test would not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3572 Assess statistical significance of signalling-entropy-based quantities (e.g. the MRH z-score of a bulk sample's deviation from a matched single-cell SR distribution) by empirical/permutation P-values, complemented by combined Fisher tests and negative controls, as done in the SCENT-based regulated heterogeneity analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Assess statistical significance of signalling-entropy-based quantities (e.g. the MRH z-score of a bulk sample's deviation from a matched single-cell SR distribution) by empirical/permutation P-values, complemented by combined Fisher tests and negative controls, as done in the SCENT-based regulated heterogeneity analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The observed statistic falls outside the single-cell reference range entirely (e.g. AML population SR=0.88 > max single-cell SR=0.82), where an exceedance comparison rather than resampling within the reference is the appropriate argument The statistic is a bulk-average profile with no regulated heterogeneity, which the control shows is correctly non-significant (P≈0.30) — do not force significance interpretation Entropies are transcriptomic entropies not based on network information (e.g. as in StemID/SLICE); the SCENT-network-based SR framework underpinning this test would not apply

skills.description: Use when inferred ligand-receptor communication networks from scRNA-seq (NeuronChat objects) must be filtered for statistical significance, or when assessing stability of significant-link calls across permutation counts.
skills.name: permutation-significance-testing-of-communication-links
skills.search_text: permutation-significance-testing-of-communication-links Use when inferred ligand-receptor communication networks from scRNA-seq (NeuronChat objects) must be filtered for statistical significance, or when assessing stability of significant-link calls across permutation counts. The goal is cell-cell communication based on short-range autocrine/paracrine signaling with protein-only ligand-receptor databases — NeuronChatDB is neural-specific and built for long-distance neurotransmitter signaling. Spatially resolved data requires distance-constrained filtering; use spatial proximity enrichment scores (cell/spot label permutation, 1000 permutations) rather than only group-label permutation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Determines which inferred neuron-neuron communication links are statistically significant by randomly permuting cell-group labels, recomputing communication strength, correcting p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg, and zeroing non-significant links (p >= 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Determines which inferred neuron-neuron communication links are statistically significant by randomly permuting cell-group labels, recomputing communication strength, correcting p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg, and zeroing non-significant links (p >= 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-cell communication based on short-range autocrine/paracrine signaling with protein-only ligand-receptor databases — NeuronChatDB is neural-specific and built for long-distance neurotransmitter signaling. Spatially resolved data requires distance-constrained filtering; use spatial proximity enrichment scores (cell/spot label permutation, 1000 permutations) rather than only group-label permutation.

skills.description: Use when running NeuronChat's run_NeuronChat permutation test and you must verify that significance calls at a modest M (e.g., 100) are stable and consistent with a large-M reference run (e.g., 1000).
skills.name: permutation-stability-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: permutation-stability-comparison-analysis Use when running NeuronChat's run_NeuronChat permutation test and you must verify that significance calls at a modest M (e.g., 100) are stable and consistent with a large-M reference run (e.g., 1000). You only need the aggregated communication network (net_aggregation over interaction pairs) and not validated significance calls — a single default run suffices without the M=1000 reference. You are analyzing spatial proximity enrichment, which uses its own label-permutation scheme (cell_proximity_enrichment_score with 1000 permutations by default) rather than link-significance permutations. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assesses how many permutations (M) are needed for reliable NeuronChat link-significance calls by comparing significant-link sets from a low-permutation run (e.g., M=100) against a high-permutation run (e.g., M=1000) after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Assesses how many permutations (M) are needed for reliable NeuronChat link-significance calls by comparing significant-link sets from a low-permutation run (e.g., M=100) against a high-permutation run (e.g., M=1000) after Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the aggregated communication network (net_aggregation over interaction pairs) and not validated significance calls — a single default run suffices without the M=1000 reference. You are analyzing spatial proximity enrichment, which uses its own label-permutation scheme (cell_proximity_enrichment_score with 1000 permutations by default) rather than link-significance permutations.

skills.description: Use when filtering inferred ligand-receptor interactions in scRNA-seq cell-cell communication analysis, i.e., after computing communication probabilities and needing a nonparametric null model to call interactions significant at p < 0.05.
skills.name: permutation-test-group-label-shuffling
skills.search_text: permutation-test-group-label-shuffling Use when filtering inferred ligand-receptor interactions in scRNA-seq cell-cell communication analysis, i.e., after computing communication probabilities and needing a nonparametric null model to call interactions significant at p < 0.05. When the goal is differential expression or pathway enrichment testing rather than filtering pairwise cell-cell communication probabilities — the permutation applies specifically to cell group labels in the communication probability model When communication probabilities have not yet been computed; the null model must use the same mass-action model parameters (type, trim, population.size, Kh, n) as the forward calculation When analyzing spatially resolved communication at single-cell resolution without discrete group labels to permute — use Spatial CellChat approaches instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 CellChat's permutation-based significance test for ligand-receptor interactions: cell group labels are randomly shuffled 100 times to recompute communication probabilities under the null, retaining interactions with p < 0.05. This is the statistical filter that turns mass-action probability scores into a validated interaction set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: CellChat's permutation-based significance test for ligand-receptor interactions: cell group labels are randomly shuffled 100 times to recompute communication probabilities under the null, retaining interactions with p < 0.05. This is the statistical filter that turns mass-action probability scores into a validated interaction set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential expression or pathway enrichment testing rather than filtering pairwise cell-cell communication probabilities — the permutation applies specifically to cell group labels in the communication probability model When communication probabilities have not yet been computed; the null model must use the same mass-action model parameters (type, trim, population.size, Kh, n) as the forward calculation When analyzing spatially resolved communication at single-cell resolution without discrete group labels to permute — use Spatial CellChat approaches instead

skills.description: Use when you have a CellChat object with overexpressed signaling genes across cell groups and need to determine which predicted ligand-receptor interactions are statistically significant rather than chance-level.
skills.name: permutation-testing-of-cell-group-interactions
skills.search_text: permutation-testing-of-cell-group-interactions Use when you have a CellChat object with overexpressed signaling genes across cell groups and need to determine which predicted ligand-receptor interactions are statistically significant rather than chance-level. When the input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell-resolution inference — use Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) instead, since v1/v2 permutation testing was developed for discrete cell groups in scRNA-seq When ground-truth validation of communication networks is required — the article notes systematic evaluation is impossible due to lack of ground truth, so the permutation test only controls label-randomization error, not biological accuracy When proteomics-level ligand-receptor evidence is needed — mRNA levels are used to approximate protein levels, so a significant interaction is not direct evidence of protein-level signaling http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Identify statistically significant ligand-receptor interactions between cell groups or cell states by randomly permuting cell group labels and recomputing communication probabilities, keeping interactions with p < 0.05. This is CellChat's null-model approach for filtering inferred cell-cell communication networks in scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Identify statistically significant ligand-receptor interactions between cell groups or cell states by randomly permuting cell group labels and recomputing communication probabilities, keeping interactions with p < 0.05. This is CellChat's null-model approach for filtering inferred cell-cell communication networks in scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is spatial transcriptomics data requiring single-cell-resolution inference — use Spatial CellChat (CellChat v3) instead, since v1/v2 permutation testing was developed for discrete cell groups in scRNA-seq When ground-truth validation of communication networks is required — the article notes systematic evaluation is impossible due to lack of ground truth, so the permutation test only controls label-randomization error, not biological accuracy When proteomics-level ligand-receptor evidence is needed — mRNA levels are used to approximate protein levels, so a significant interaction is not direct evidence of protein-level signaling

skills.description: Use when single-cell time-course data has CellTag lineage barcodes and a fate label (e.g. Capybara-assigned iEP conversion), and you must split cells at an intermediate time point into clone groups enriched or depleted for successful fate conversion.
skills.name: permutation-testing-of-clonal-state-enrichment
skills.search_text: permutation-testing-of-clonal-state-enrichment Use when single-cell time-course data has CellTag lineage barcodes and a fate label (e.g. Capybara-assigned iEP conversion), and you must split cells at an intermediate time point into clone groups enriched or depleted for successful fate conversion. The dataset lacks clonal lineage barcodes (no CellTag integration), so fate can only be inferred from state, not clonally validated Only terminal (fully converted) cells are available with no intermediate time point whose cells need fate labeling The goal is generic differential expression between states rather than linking early state to outcome via clonal membership http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A statistical procedure that uses a randomized (permutation) test of CellTag clone membership among cells with a known fate outcome to partition intermediate-state cells into fate-enriched and fate-depleted groups, enabling clonal linking of early GRN state to reprogramming outcome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: A statistical procedure that uses a randomized (permutation) test of CellTag clone membership among cells with a known fate outcome to partition intermediate-state cells into fate-enriched and fate-depleted groups, enabling clonal linking of early GRN state to reprogramming outcome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks clonal lineage barcodes (no CellTag integration), so fate can only be inferred from state, not clonally validated Only terminal (fully converted) cells are available with no intermediate time point whose cells need fate labeling The goal is generic differential expression between states rather than linking early state to outcome via clonal membership

skills.description: Use when deconvolving multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data with STdeconvolve and an appropriate number of cell types K must be set a priori for the LDA model.
skills.name: perplexity-based-k-selection
skills.search_text: perplexity-based-k-selection Use when deconvolving multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data with STdeconvolve and an appropriate number of cell types K must be set a priori for the LDA model. Input is sub-cellular pixel-resolution ST data — STdeconvolve is not best suited for such resolutions Genes show no variability across pixels because cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform, so deconvolution is expected to fail regardless of K A curated single-cell RNA-seq reference exists and a supervised method (RCTD, SPOTlight, spatialDWLS) is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Data-driven selection of the number of cell types K in STdeconvolve by fitting latent Dirichlet allocation models over a grid of candidate K values (topicmodels backend), recording perplexity for each K, and choosing the K with minimal perplexity that avoids rare, low-proportion topics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Data-driven selection of the number of cell types K in STdeconvolve by fitting latent Dirichlet allocation models over a grid of candidate K values (topicmodels backend), recording perplexity for each K, and choosing the K with minimal perplexity that avoids rare, low-proportion topics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is sub-cellular pixel-resolution ST data — STdeconvolve is not best suited for such resolutions Genes show no variability across pixels because cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform, so deconvolution is expected to fail regardless of K A curated single-cell RNA-seq reference exists and a supervised method (RCTD, SPOTlight, spatialDWLS) is preferred

skills.description: Use when a scorecard run on antibiotic-exposed bacterial biofilm transcriptomics (e.g. VAN comparisons yielding Q3 down-regulated SAUSA300 entries) needs gene-level functional interpretation as persistence or survival strategies.
skills.name: persister-cell-gene-annotation
skills.search_text: persister-cell-gene-annotation Use when a scorecard run on antibiotic-exposed bacterial biofilm transcriptomics (e.g. VAN comparisons yielding Q3 down-regulated SAUSA300 entries) needs gene-level functional interpretation as persistence or survival strategies. Differential expression has not yet been filtered through the scorecard with statistical-significance-aware quadrants — typical four-way or volcano plots alone do not provide the occurrence reports this annotation step consumes The input transcriptome lacks gene IDs or locus tags in a dedicated column (gene_name parameter cannot map entries to known genes) The goal is raw expression quantification rather than data-driven extraction of extreme or moderate fold-change variations across multiple experimental conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate genes surfaced by the Scorecard library (e.g. SAUSA300 loci from Dataset 1 transposon-sequencing comparisons under VAN, LZD, CPT, DEL) as candidate persister-cell or biofilm-survival factors by linking scorecard quadrant/occurrence reports to known mechanisms such as altered penicillin-protein binding affinity, cell wall thickening, efflux pumps, and enzymatic drug inactivation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Annotate genes surfaced by the Scorecard library (e.g. SAUSA300 loci from Dataset 1 transposon-sequencing comparisons under VAN, LZD, CPT, DEL) as candidate persister-cell or biofilm-survival factors by linking scorecard quadrant/occurrence reports to known mechanisms such as altered penicillin-protein binding affinity, cell wall thickening, efflux pumps, and enzymatic drug inactivation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Differential expression has not yet been filtered through the scorecard with statistical-significance-aware quadrants — typical four-way or volcano plots alone do not provide the occurrence reports this annotation step consumes The input transcriptome lacks gene IDs or locus tags in a dedicated column (gene_name parameter cannot map entries to known genes) The goal is raw expression quantification rather than data-driven extraction of extreme or moderate fold-change variations across multiple experimental conditions

skills.description: Use when the goal is to find driver nodes/genes specific to individual patients from matched tumor-normal RNA-seq matrices (e.g., TCGA), and to assess patient-level tumor heterogeneity via driver-gene recurrence frequencies.
skills.name: personalized-differential-coexpression-analysis
skills.search_text: personalized-differential-coexpression-analysis Use when the goal is to find driver nodes/genes specific to individual patients from matched tumor-normal RNA-seq matrices (e.g., TCGA), and to assess patient-level tumor heterogeneity via driver-gene recurrence frequencies. When a single population-level driver-gene list is sufficient — use the global WMDS.net dominating set on the pooled differential network instead of per-patient SSNs When input is already a ranked driver-gene list or a feature table rather than raw tumor/normal expression matrices — WMDS.net requires expression matrices to recompute co-expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Builds patient-specific differential co-expression networks and identifies personalized driver genes by solving a weighted minimum dominating set (WMDS.net) on each network, then quantifies recurrence frequency of driver genes across patients within each cancer type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Builds patient-specific differential co-expression networks and identifies personalized driver genes by solving a weighted minimum dominating set (WMDS.net) on each network, then quantifies recurrence frequency of driver genes across patients within each cancer type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single population-level driver-gene list is sufficient — use the global WMDS.net dominating set on the pooled differential network instead of per-patient SSNs When input is already a ranked driver-gene list or a feature table rather than raw tumor/normal expression matrices — WMDS.net requires expression matrices to recompute co-expression

skills.description: Use when detecting allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) from RNA-seq fastq data and reads must be assigned to alleles via alignment to haplotype-modified personal genomes rather than a generic reference.
skills.name: personalized-genome-alignment-with-star
skills.search_text: personalized-genome-alignment-with-star Use when detecting allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) from RNA-seq fastq data and reads must be assigned to alleles via alignment to haplotype-modified personal genomes rather than a generic reference. skills.name: perturbation-zero-expression-rate-quantification
skills.search_text: perturbation-zero-expression-rate-quantification Use when auditing MUSIC-style single-cell CRISPR screening pipelines: before or after the perturbation-filtering step, to identify which perturbations (e. The goal is off-target or sgRNA knockout-efficiency evaluation rather than assessing the perturbation-level zero-expression filter (MUSIC handles those via CRISPRseek and separate sgRNA evaluation steps). The perturbation target gene is nonzero in at least some cells in every dataset, so the filter removes nothing and the with-/without-filter comparison is moot. Input data is fastq or raw 10X output that has not yet been converted to MUSIC's expression_profile.txt / perturb_information.txt format via Input_preprocess() or Input_preprocess_10X(). Quantifies, for each of the 326 knockout/knockdown perturbations across 14 datasets, the zero_rate statistic — the fraction of cells in which the targeted gene has zero expression — and evaluates whether MUSIC's rule of dropping perturbations whose targeted gene is zero in all cells materially changes the perturbation effect rankings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x

skills.description: Use when preparing RNA-seq FASTQ input for viRNAtrap or similar viral-read detection: TCGA BAM files must be stripped of human (hg19) alignments and phiX phage contaminant reads before viral prediction.
skills.name: phage-contaminant-removal
skills.search_text: phage-contaminant-removal Use when preparing RNA-seq FASTQ input for viRNAtrap or similar viral-read detection: TCGA BAM files must be stripped of human (hg19) alignments and phiX phage contaminant reads before viral prediction. Input FASTQ files already represent fully unmapped reads that still contain phiX-aligned reads would need this filter, but reads already reduced to *_unmapped.fastq after both hg19 and phiX filtering should not be re-filtered Reads from non-human organisms: viRNAtrap models are trained on human vs viral sequences, so this hg19/phiX removal pipeline is not appropriate for samples from other host species Single-read (unpaired) data processed as separate files per sample would violate viRNAtrap's one-file-per-sample assumption if not merged appropriately Pre-processing step from the viRNAtrap TCGA workflow that removes phiX phage contamination: TCGA RNA-seq reads are first unmapped from hg19, then remaining read pairs are aligned against the phiX (NC_001422) reference with Bowtie2 and read pairs unmapped to both references are extracted as the *_unmapped.fastq input files. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Pre-processing step from the viRNAtrap TCGA workflow that removes phiX phage contamination: TCGA RNA-seq reads are first unmapped from hg19, then remaining read pairs are aligned against the phiX (NC_001422) reference with Bowtie2 and read pairs unmapped to both references are extracted as the *_unmapped.fastq input files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input FASTQ files already represent fully unmapped reads that still contain phiX-aligned reads would need this filter, but reads already reduced to *_unmapped.fastq after both hg19 and phiX filtering should not be re-filtered Reads from non-human organisms: viRNAtrap models are trained on human vs viral sequences, so this hg19/phiX removal pipeline is not appropriate for samples from other host species Single-read (unpaired) data processed as separate files per sample would violate viRNAtrap's one-file-per-sample assumption if not merged appropriately

skills.search_text: phase-i-dlt-rate-estimation Use when dose-escalation decisions in a phase I/II trial require per-dose DLT probability estimates that are guaranteed monotonically non-decreasing across dose levels, from raw cohort DLT counts. The goal is joint toxicity-efficacy (bivariate) estimation in stage 2 of TSNP rather than univariate per-dose DLT rates Response/toxicity outcomes are not binary and quickly observable — the TSNP design cannot be directly applied when the response outcome requires long follow-up time Only one dose level has data, so no ordering constraint across doses can be violated and pooling is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes per-dose dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate estimates in the TSNP phase I/II design by applying the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA) to observed per-dose toxicity proportions, yielding isotonic estimates that satisfy the monotonic increasing order constraint on toxicity rates and are equivalent to the constrained MLEs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Computes per-dose dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate estimates in the TSNP phase I/II design by applying the pool-adjacent-violators algorithm (PAVA) to observed per-dose toxicity proportions, yielding isotonic estimates that satisfy the monotonic increasing order constraint on toxicity rates and are equivalent to the constrained MLEs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is joint toxicity-efficacy (bivariate) estimation in stage 2 of TSNP rather than univariate per-dose DLT rates Response/toxicity outcomes are not binary and quickly observable — the TSNP design cannot be directly applied when the response outcome requires long follow-up time Only one dose level has data, so no ordering constraint across doses can be violated and pooling is unnecessary

skills.search_text: phase-i-ii-dose-finding-simulation Use when simulating a phase I/II trial with binary toxicity and efficacy outcomes to identify an optimal biological dose (OBD) for immunotherapy, or when benchmarking dose-finding designs on OBD selection and patient-allocation percentages. The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is only appropriate for binary, quickly observable response outcomes The trial targets an MTD-only phase I objective rather than joint toxicity-efficacy OBD selection for immunotherapy The goal is dose- combination finding — extension of TSNP to drug-combination trials is future work, not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3305 Reproduce and evaluate the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II dose-finding design for immunotherapy via Monte Carlo simulation in R, comparing OBD selection percentages against Bayesian parametric comparators (Thall-Cook P1, Yin et al. P2) and U-BOIN. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Reproduce and evaluate the TSNP two-stage nonparametric phase I/II dose-finding design for immunotherapy via Monte Carlo simulation in R, comparing OBD selection percentages against Bayesian parametric comparators (Thall-Cook P1, Yin et al. P2) and U-BOIN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is only appropriate for binary, quickly observable response outcomes The trial targets an MTD-only phase I objective rather than joint toxicity-efficacy OBD selection for immunotherapy The goal is dose- combination finding — extension of TSNP to drug-combination trials is future work, not yet implemented

skills.summary: Runs Monte Carlo simulations of the two-stage nonparametric (TSNP) phase I/II dose-finding design across maximum sample sizes (N=40, 50, 60) to evaluate correct optimal biological dose (OBD) selection percentages per scenario and identify the smallest N meeting performance criteria.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess or is not binary and quickly observable — the TSNP design is explicitly limited to binary, shortly observable responses The trial involves drug combinations — extension of TSNP to drug-combination trials is stated as future work, not yet implemented You only need a single-N operating characteristics run with no sample-size sensitivity comparison — the N=40/50/60 replication loop is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when reproducing or executing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial with the TSNP design — e.g., a hypothetical trial with J=5 doses, phi=0.3, max sample size 30, m=6 — to obtain per-dose utilities and a final OBD.
skills.name: phase-i-ii-trial-design-implementation
skills.search_text: phase-i-ii-trial-design-implementation Use when reproducing or executing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial with the TSNP design — e.g., a hypothetical trial with J=5 doses, phi=0.3, max sample size 30, m=6 — to obtain per-dose utilities and a final OBD. The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is limited to binary, quickly observable response outcomes The trial is a drug-combination dose-finding study — extension of TSNP to combination trials is future work and not yet supported The goal is conventional MTD-targeting phase I dosing rather than OBD selection balancing toxicity and efficacy via a utility function http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Implements the two-stage nonparametric (TSNP) phase I/II clinical trial design for identifying the optimal biological dose (OBD) of immunotherapy, using the R code from github.com/yongzang2020/TSNP. Stage 1 explores the toxicity profile via isotonic (PAVA) estimates and Fisher's exact admissibility tests; stage 2 selects the OBD by maximizing a utility function U(pi-hat_jkl, omega_kl) over the admissible set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/pst.2075
skills.summary: Implements the two-stage nonparametric (TSNP) phase I/II clinical trial design for identifying the optimal biological dose (OBD) of immunotherapy, using the R code from github.com/yongzang2020/TSNP. Stage 1 explores the toxicity profile via isotonic (PAVA) estimates and Fisher's exact admissibility tests; stage 2 selects the OBD by maximizing a utility function U(pi-hat_jkl, omega_kl) over the admissible set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response outcome requires long follow-up to assess — the design is limited to binary, quickly observable response outcomes The trial is a drug-combination dose-finding study — extension of TSNP to combination trials is future work and not yet supported The goal is conventional MTD-targeting phase I dosing rather than OBD selection balancing toxicity and efficacy via a utility function

skills.description: Use when validating RNA velocity or TF-based gene dynamics fits: after running scVelo/TFvelo on scRNA-seq (e.g., E15.5 mouse pancreas), check phase portraits of -fitted genes for the clockwise TF–target traversal that evidences regulation.
skills.name: phase-portrait-co-expression-interpretation
skills.search_text: phase-portrait-co-expression-interpretation Use when validating RNA velocity or TF-based gene dynamics fits: after running scVelo/TFvelo on scRNA-seq (e.g., E15.5 mouse pancreas), check phase portraits of -fitted genes for the clockwise TF–target traversal that evidences regulation. Genes for which TFvelo cannot fit the dynamics well (Fig. S14) — the phase portrait will not show a coherent clockwise curve and offers no validation signal Datasets lacking identifiable candidate TFs in ENCODE/ChEA, where a TF representation axis cannot be constructed for the target gene Large-scale datasets where TFvelo's low time efficiency relative to scVelo makes full portrait-fitting runs impractical without parallelizing over more CPUs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Qualitative validation of TF-based gene dynamics by inspecting phase portraits between TF representation (or unspliced/spliced counts) and the target gene, where a correctly modeled regulatory relationship manifests as a desired clockwise co-expression curve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Qualitative validation of TF-based gene dynamics by inspecting phase portraits between TF representation (or unspliced/spliced counts) and the target gene, where a correctly modeled regulatory relationship manifests as a desired clockwise co-expression curve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes for which TFvelo cannot fit the dynamics well (Fig. S14) — the phase portrait will not show a coherent clockwise curve and offers no validation signal Datasets lacking identifiable candidate TFs in ENCODE/ChEA, where a TF representation axis cannot be constructed for the target gene Large-scale datasets where TFvelo's low time efficiency relative to scVelo makes full portrait-fitting runs impractical without parallelizing over more CPUs

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data with both spliced and unspliced count layers (AnnData) to infer RNA velocity and cell-fate trajectories on multi-branching differentiation without labeling metadata.
skills.name: phase-portrait-fitting-of-spliced-unspliced-rna
skills.search_text: phase-portrait-fitting-of-spliced-unspliced-rna Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data with both spliced and unspliced count layers (AnnData) to infer RNA velocity and cell-fate trajectories on multi-branching differentiation without labeling metadata. Data lacks an unspliced mRNA layer (e.g., standard 10x output without intronic counting) — phase-portrait fitting requires un/spliced pairs Metabolic-labeling information (e.g., scEU-seq pulse-chase labels) is available and should be exploited directly rather than inferred Goal is evaluation against ground-truth cluster edges without defined cluster_edges/label annotations for utv.evaluate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit UniTVelo's joint dynamic model to spliced and unspliced mRNA phase portraits, estimating per-gene velocities and a unified latent time without metabolic-labeling knowledge, using an RBF-based transcription rate over Python 3/TensorFlow 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7
skills.summary: Fit UniTVelo's joint dynamic model to spliced and unspliced mRNA phase portraits, estimating per-gene velocities and a unified latent time without metabolic-labeling knowledge, using an RBF-based transcription rate over Python 3/TensorFlow 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks an unspliced mRNA layer (e.g., standard 10x output without intronic counting) — phase-portrait fitting requires un/spliced pairs Metabolic-labeling information (e.g., scEU-seq pulse-chase labels) is available and should be exploited directly rather than inferred Goal is evaluation against ground-truth cluster edges without defined cluster_edges/label annotations for utv.evaluate

Datasets lacking unspliced/spliced counts where the un/spliced-based baselines (scVelo, Dynamo, UniTVelo, cellDancer) cannot run at all, breaking the common-gene comparison When the goal is velocity vector accuracy downstream (CBDir/ICCoh trajectory metrics) rather than gene-level phase portrait fitting quality Very large-scale datasets where TFvelo's runtime is prohibitive compared to scVelo http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates RNA velocity methods by measuring how well each method fits gene dynamics on phase portraits, quantified via intra-class and inter-class distance metrics across methods and genes. skills.search_text: phase-portrait-fitting-visualization Use when you need to validate that a gene-regulation-based RNA velocity method fits gene dynamics correctly by inspecting phase portraits (TF representation vs. target) and UMAP pseudotime/streamplots, especially on multi-omics or scRNA-seq datasets. skills.description: Use when small-RNA sequencing reads (19–25 nt) should be scanned for phased siRNA-producing loci (PHAS genes) against a reference transcriptome, genome, or full-length transcriptome, especially to recover phasiRNAs that only the phase score method detects.
skills.name: phase-score-based-phasing-analysis
skills.search_text: phase-score-based-phasing-analysis Use when small-RNA sequencing reads (19–25 nt) should be scanned for phased siRNA-producing loci (PHAS genes) against a reference transcriptome, genome, or full-length transcriptome, especially to recover phasiRNAs that only the phase score method detects. The question is whether predicted PHAS loci pass the hypergeometric pvalue cutoff alone — with -dp y, only-P-method results are discarded, so phase-score-only hits will not survive integration. Input is degradome data or initiator/target prediction (use 'phasiHunter target/initiator' or 'phasiHunter deg' instead of the phase module). Reads outside the 19–25 nt window or with abundance below the CPM cutoff of 1 — preprocess filtering will remove them before phasing is meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Predict phasiRNAs and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data using PhasiHunter's phase score method (with optional hypergeometric-test confirmation) against transcriptome, genome, or full-length-transcriptome references. Phase scoring captures phased 21-nt (or 24-nt) siRNA accumulation patterns that hypergeometric testing alone can miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Predict phasiRNAs and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data using PhasiHunter's phase score method (with optional hypergeometric-test confirmation) against transcriptome, genome, or full-length-transcriptome references. Phase scoring captures phased 21-nt (or 24-nt) siRNA accumulation patterns that hypergeometric testing alone can miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is whether predicted PHAS loci pass the hypergeometric pvalue cutoff alone — with -dp y, only-P-method results are discarded, so phase-score-only hits will not survive integration. Input is degradome data or initiator/target prediction (use 'phasiHunter target/initiator' or 'phasiHunter deg' instead of the phase module). Reads outside the 19–25 nt window or with abundance below the CPM cutoff of 1 — preprocess filtering will remove them before phasing is meaningful.

skills.description: Use when detecting phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters/PHAS loci from sRNA-seq reads mapped to a transcriptome or genome and you need a combined phase-score + hypergeometric detection with bidirectional search.
skills.name: phase-score-calculation
skills.search_text: phase-score-calculation Use when detecting phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters/PHAS loci from sRNA-seq reads mapped to a transcriptome or genome and you need a combined phase-score + hypergeometric detection with bidirectional search. When only one algorithm is desired — use -me h (hypergeometric only) or -me p (phase score only) instead of the combined default, e.g. if downstream analysis discards only-P-method results (-dp y). When the input sRNA reads are untrimmed raw FASTQ — the phase module expects preprocessed map files and filtered FASTA produced by the `phasiHunter preprocess` step (trim adaptor, normalization, length/abundance filter, mapping). PhasiHunter's PHAS loci detection runs two complementary phasiRNA prediction algorithms — a phase score method and a hypergeometric distribution-based method — with forward and reverse search to maximize PHAS loci detection sensitivity and prediction integrity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: PhasiHunter's PHAS loci detection runs two complementary phasiRNA prediction algorithms — a phase score method and a hypergeometric distribution-based method — with forward and reverse search to maximize PHAS loci detection sensitivity and prediction integrity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one algorithm is desired — use -me h (hypergeometric only) or -me p (phase score only) instead of the combined default, e.g. if downstream analysis discards only-P-method results (-dp y). When the input sRNA reads are untrimmed raw FASTQ — the phase module expects preprocessed map files and filtered FASTA produced by the `phasiHunter preprocess` step (trim adaptor, normalization, length/abundance filter, mapping).

skills.description: Use when benchmarking allele-specific CNA callers on scWGS data requires ground-truth simulations that preserve haplotype structure and phasing accuracy, e.g., testing sensitivity to 200 kb–5 Mb CNAs under controlled phase-switch error rates.
skills.name: phased-genotype-error-simulation
skills.search_text: phased-genotype-error-simulation Use when benchmarking allele-specific CNA callers on scWGS data requires ground-truth simulations that preserve haplotype structure and phasing accuracy, e.g., testing sensitivity to 200 kb–5 Mb CNAs under controlled phase-switch error rates. Input is real tumor scWGS data whose clonal haplotype structure should be inferred, not simulated — SDX models synthetic diploid chrX only The caller under test does not use BAF or phasing information; the 1% phase-switch error injection targets phasing-aware methods specifically A benchmark requires realistic female XX or autosome diploid simulation — SDX pools male haploid X chromosomes and this construction does not generalize directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A simulation strategy for building synthetic diploid X (SDX) scWGS benchmark data by pooling reads from two male haploid X chromosomes (OligoA and OligoB1), inserting allele-specific CNAs, and injecting phase-switch errors at a controlled 1% rate so BAF/phasing-based CNA callers are challenged realistically. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: A simulation strategy for building synthetic diploid X (SDX) scWGS benchmark data by pooling reads from two male haploid X chromosomes (OligoA and OligoB1), inserting allele-specific CNAs, and injecting phase-switch errors at a controlled 1% rate so BAF/phasing-based CNA callers are challenged realistically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real tumor scWGS data whose clonal haplotype structure should be inferred, not simulated — SDX models synthetic diploid chrX only The caller under test does not use BAF or phasing information; the 1% phase-switch error injection targets phasing-aware methods specifically A benchmark requires realistic female XX or autosome diploid simulation — SDX pools male haploid X chromosomes and this construction does not generalize directly

skills.description: Use when scWGS analysis requires allele-specific copy-number states or BAF-based validation, and you have single-cell BAMs plus a matched bulk WGS sample per individual to source and phase gHETs.
skills.name: phased-heterozygous-snp-baf-estimation
skills.search_text: phased-heterozygous-snp-baf-estimation Use when scWGS analysis requires allele-specific copy-number states or BAF-based validation, and you have single-cell BAMs plus a matched bulk WGS sample per individual to source and phase gHETs. Analysis targets sex chromosomes: SCAN2 and the phased-gHET workflow support only diploid human autosomes 1–22 (female X in principle) Only gHETs with bulk VAF outside 0.1–0.9 are available (no properly phased, heterozygous anchor sites), making BAF estimation unreliable No matched bulk WGS exists for the individual, so gHETs cannot be called and phased against a germline reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Establishes a set of bulk-phased germline heterozygous SNPs (gHETs) and derives B-allele frequencies (BAF) at those sites so that allele-specific copy-number callers like HiScanner (and validation of BAF-agnostic callers like Ginkgo) can use allelic imbalance evidence from single-cell WGS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Establishes a set of bulk-phased germline heterozygous SNPs (gHETs) and derives B-allele frequencies (BAF) at those sites so that allele-specific copy-number callers like HiScanner (and validation of BAF-agnostic callers like Ginkgo) can use allelic imbalance evidence from single-cell WGS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis targets sex chromosomes: SCAN2 and the phased-gHET workflow support only diploid human autosomes 1–22 (female X in principle) Only gHETs with bulk VAF outside 0.1–0.9 are available (no properly phased, heterozygous anchor sites), making BAF estimation unreliable No matched bulk WGS exists for the individual, so gHETs cannot be called and phased against a germline reference

skills.description: Use when phasiRNA prediction (phase module) outputs exist from mappings to more than one reference sequence — e.g. a cDNA map and a gDNA map — and clusters in different coordinate systems must be reconciled into one unified PHAS locus set.
skills.name: phased-sirna-loci-deduplication-and-merging
skills.search_text: phased-sirna-loci-deduplication-and-merging Use when phasiRNA prediction (phase module) outputs exist from mappings to more than one reference sequence — e.g. a cDNA map and a gDNA map — and clusters in different coordinate systems must be reconciled into one unified PHAS locus set. You have prediction results from only a single reference sequence — no cross-reference coordinate transform or merging is needed. You are still in the prediction stage (raw sRNA data preprocessing or the phase module); this skill operates only on phase module outputs (phase_o.txt / phase_a.txt), not on .map or FASTQ inputs. You need initiator or degradome target verification (the 'target'/'initiator' modules) rather than locus consolidation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS locus prediction results produced separately on different reference sequences (transcriptome, genome, full-length transcriptome) by a coordinate-system transform implemented with bedtools and python3 dictionaries, then deduplicates, merges, annotates, and classifies phasiRNA clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS locus prediction results produced separately on different reference sequences (transcriptome, genome, full-length transcriptome) by a coordinate-system transform implemented with bedtools and python3 dictionaries, then deduplicates, merges, annotates, and classifies phasiRNA clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have prediction results from only a single reference sequence — no cross-reference coordinate transform or merging is needed. You are still in the prediction stage (raw sRNA data preprocessing or the phase module); this skill operates only on phase module outputs (phase_o.txt / phase_a.txt), not on .map or FASTQ inputs. You need initiator or degradome target verification (the 'target'/'initiator' modules) rather than locus consolidation.

skills.description: Use when sRNA-seq reads (19–25 nt, e.g. rice SRR5049781) must be scanned for phased 21-nt siRNA stacks and PHAS loci, especially when genome- and transcriptome-based predictions should be combined to catch alternative-splicing or novel unannotated loci.
skills.name: phased-sirna-loci-prediction
skills.search_text: phased-sirna-loci-prediction Use when sRNA-seq reads (19–25 nt, e.g. rice SRR5049781) must be scanned for phased 21-nt siRNA stacks and PHAS loci, especially when genome- and transcriptome-based predictions should be combined to catch alternative-splicing or novel unannotated loci. skills.summary: Predict phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data using PhasiHunter's dual-algorithm approach (hypergeometric test plus phase score) run against multiple reference sequences (genome, transcriptome, full-length transcriptome), then integrate the reference-based results with GFF3 annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is degradome data or miRNA target verification — use the separate target/initiator modules instead of the phase module. Only a single reference (genome alone) is available and no transcriptome/flnc integration or annotation-based locus naming is needed — the multi-reference value-add (alternative-splicing and novel-locus detection) is lost. skills.description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of phasiRNA/phased siRNA prediction tools, or when deciding whether PhasiHunter's parallel (-j) mode is needed for large genome-based 21-nt phasiRNA prediction workloads.

skills.search_text: phased-sirna-prediction-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing computational efficiency of phasiRNA/phased siRNA prediction tools, or when deciding whether PhasiHunter's parallel (-j) mode is needed for large genome-based 21-nt phasiRNA prediction workloads.
