skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads are already mapped to a reference (transcriptome and/or genome) and you need to call 21-nt or 24-nt phased siRNA loci and integrate multi-reference predictions into gene-level PHAS sets.
skills.name: phasirna-cluster-integration
skills.search_text: phasirna-cluster-integration Use when small RNA-seq reads are already mapped to a reference (transcriptome and/or genome) and you need to call 21-nt or 24-nt phased siRNA loci and integrate multi-reference predictions into gene-level PHAS sets. Input reads are raw FASTQ that have not been adapter-trimmed, normalized, length-filtered (19–25 nt), or bowtie-mapped — run the preprocess module first The analysis requires phasiRNA trigger/initiator miRNA identification or degradome target validation — use the target/initiator/deg modules instead No GFF3 annotation is available for the reference genome, since the integration module requires -an annotation to consolidate loci http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predict phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters and PHAS loci from small RNA-seq mapping data using PhasiHunter's phase module (hypergeometric and phase-score methods), then consolidate results across reference sequences with the integration module against a GFF3 annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Predict phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters and PHAS loci from small RNA-seq mapping data using PhasiHunter's phase module (hypergeometric and phase-score methods), then consolidate results across reference sequences with the integration module against a GFF3 annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are raw FASTQ that have not been adapter-trimmed, normalized, length-filtered (19–25 nt), or bowtie-mapped — run the preprocess module first The analysis requires phasiRNA trigger/initiator miRNA identification or degradome target validation — use the target/initiator/deg modules instead No GFF3 annotation is available for the reference genome, since the integration module requires -an annotation to consolidate loci

skills.description: Use when separate PhasiHunter phase runs on gDNA and cDNA (or full-length transcriptome) references have produced phase_o.txt and phase_a.txt outputs and the clusters must be merged into a single genome-annotated result set.
skills.name: phasirna-cluster-integration-across-reference-sequences
skills.search_text: phasirna-cluster-integration-across-reference-sequences Use when separate PhasiHunter phase runs on gDNA and cDNA (or full-length transcriptome) references have produced phase_o.txt and phase_a.txt outputs and the clusters must be merged into a single genome-annotated result set. You have only run PhasiHunter's phase module against a single reference sequence and need no cross-reference merging or coordinate transform — the phase module outputs are already the final per-reference result. You need to predict phasiRNAs or PHAS loci themselves rather than merge/annotate existing phase predictions — use the phase module with its -me h|p|b method selection instead. Your input is raw sRNA-seq FASTQ data not yet preprocessed or phased — the integration module requires phase_o.txt/phase_a.txt from completed phase runs, not raw reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS loci and all-siRNA cluster predictions that PhasiHunter's phase module produced separately against multiple reference sequences (genome/gDNA, transcriptome/cDNA, full-length transcriptome) by transforming coordinates with bedtools and a python3 dictionary, then deduplicating, merging, annotating, and classifying the clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Integrates phasiRNA/PHAS loci and all-siRNA cluster predictions that PhasiHunter's phase module produced separately against multiple reference sequences (genome/gDNA, transcriptome/cDNA, full-length transcriptome) by transforming coordinates with bedtools and a python3 dictionary, then deduplicating, merging, annotating, and classifying the clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only run PhasiHunter's phase module against a single reference sequence and need no cross-reference merging or coordinate transform — the phase module outputs are already the final per-reference result. You need to predict phasiRNAs or PHAS loci themselves rather than merge/annotate existing phase predictions — use the phase module with its -me h|p|b method selection instead. Your input is raw sRNA-seq FASTQ data not yet preprocessed or phased — the integration module requires phase_o.txt/phase_a.txt from completed phase runs, not raw reads.

skills.description: Use when sRNA-seq libraries (e.g. 19–25 nt reads) need phased siRNA/PHAS locus prediction against one or more reference sequences (transcriptome and/or genome), or when comparing reference-based phasiRNA predictions.
skills.name: phasirna-phas-loci-prediction
skills.search_text: phasirna-phas-loci-prediction Use when sRNA-seq libraries (e.g. 19–25 nt reads) need phased siRNA/PHAS locus prediction against one or more reference sequences (transcriptome and/or genome), or when comparing reference-based phasiRNA predictions. Input is already a per-library Bowtie map file — use the phase module directly rather than re-preprocessing. The goal is microRNA discovery or miRNA target prediction with no interest in phasing/PHAS loci — this skill is specific to phased siRNA cluster mining. Reads fall outside the 19–25 nt sRNA window; the preprocess length cutoffs (-mi 19, -ma 25) would discard the data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predict phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data using PhasiHunter's dual prediction algorithms (hypergeometric test and phase score) across transcriptome and genome reference sequences, with downstream integration to consolidate results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Predict phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data using PhasiHunter's dual prediction algorithms (hypergeometric test and phase score) across transcriptome and genome reference sequences, with downstream integration to consolidate results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-library Bowtie map file — use the phase module directly rather than re-preprocessing. The goal is microRNA discovery or miRNA target prediction with no interest in phasing/PHAS loci — this skill is specific to phased siRNA cluster mining. Reads fall outside the 19–25 nt sRNA window; the preprocess length cutoffs (-mi 19, -ma 25) would discard the data.

skills.description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a Seurat object carrying Louvain cluster assignments and PCA/UMAP reductions) needs a diffusion-based, trajectory-friendly embedding to support Slingshot trajectory inference and pseudotime visualization.
skills.name: phate-diffusion-embedding
skills.search_text: phate-diffusion-embedding Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a Seurat object carrying Louvain cluster assignments and PCA/UMAP reductions) needs a diffusion-based, trajectory-friendly embedding to support Slingshot trajectory inference and pseudotime visualization. Input is scATAC-seq data analyzed through SCALA's ArchR-based workflow, where dimensionality reduction is performed with LSI rather than a PHATE expression embedding. The dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA web server, where some steps cannot be completed — prefer the desktop version. The goal is cluster annotation or marker identification (e.g., CIPR, presto) rather than trajectory or pseudotime analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes a PHATE diffusion embedding of scRNA-seq cells with the GitHub version of phateR on a patched Seurat object, producing a diffusion-based, trajectory-friendly reduced-dimension space that SCALA uses for Slingshot trajectory inference and pseudotime visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Computes a PHATE diffusion embedding of scRNA-seq cells with the GitHub version of phateR on a patched Seurat object, producing a diffusion-based, trajectory-friendly reduced-dimension space that SCALA uses for Slingshot trajectory inference and pseudotime visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scATAC-seq data analyzed through SCALA's ArchR-based workflow, where dimensionality reduction is performed with LSI rather than a PHATE expression embedding. The dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA web server, where some steps cannot be completed — prefer the desktop version. The goal is cluster annotation or marker identification (e.g., CIPR, presto) rather than trajectory or pseudotime analysis.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking sample-level single-cell distance methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., .h5ad patient cohorts) and you need the PhEMD baseline with its required Monocle 2 preprocessing and measured runtime.
skills.name: phemd-pipeline-execution-with-monocle-preprocessing
skills.search_text: phemd-pipeline-execution-with-monocle-preprocessing Use when benchmarking sample-level single-cell distance methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., .h5ad patient cohorts) and you need the PhEMD baseline with its required Monocle 2 preprocessing and measured runtime. When the goal is unsupervised sample-level analysis rather than benchmarking: the paper notes the latter methods 'require labels of patients for their analysis and cannot be used in the unsupervised analysis' When you only need patient-level distances and runtime matters — PILOT via POT's emd2 completed the 1.26M-cell Lupus dataset in 58.12 s vs PhEMD's 16.50 min When the data are already aggregated per sample (pseudo-bulk proportions); the pseudo-bulk baseline applies directly instead of the full PhEMD pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Executes PhEMD end-to-end as a competing sample-level baseline: Monocle 2 performs normalization, dimension reduction, and cell clustering, after which PhEMD computes earth moving distances (EMD) between specimens. Used in the PILOT paper to benchmark wall-clock runtime against PILOT and a pseudo-bulk baseline on the ~1.26M-cell Lupus PBMC dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Executes PhEMD end-to-end as a competing sample-level baseline: Monocle 2 performs normalization, dimension reduction, and cell clustering, after which PhEMD computes earth moving distances (EMD) between specimens. Used in the PILOT paper to benchmark wall-clock runtime against PILOT and a pseudo-bulk baseline on the ~1.26M-cell Lupus PBMC dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is unsupervised sample-level analysis rather than benchmarking: the paper notes the latter methods 'require labels of patients for their analysis and cannot be used in the unsupervised analysis' When you only need patient-level distances and runtime matters — PILOT via POT's emd2 completed the 1.26M-cell Lupus dataset in 58.12 s vs PhEMD's 16.50 min When the data are already aggregated per sample (pseudo-bulk proportions); the pseudo-bulk baseline applies directly instead of the full PhEMD pipeline

skills.description: Use when 2D embeddings of preprocessed CyTOF data (arcsinh X/5, MinMaxScaler to [0,1]) must be partitioned into cell populations and quantitatively compared to manual gating labels via ARI, e.g. benchmarking dimensionality-reduction quality on BMMC/Samusik.
skills.name: phenograph-clustering-ari-assessment
skills.search_text: phenograph-clustering-ari-assessment Use when 2D embeddings of preprocessed CyTOF data (arcsinh X/5, MinMaxScaler to [0,1]) must be partitioned into cell populations and quantitatively compared to manual gating labels via ARI, e.g. benchmarking dimensionality-reduction quality on BMMC/Samusik. The dataset has no manually gated cell-population labels, so ARI cannot be computed — use unsupervised metrics or the Mantel-test PCC on centroid distances instead The data are raw FCS files that have not yet been arcsinh-transformed and MinMax-scaled; clustering unscaled cytometry intensities is out of scope for this workflow The goal is to assess preservation of global inter-cluster geometry rather than cluster recoverability — the paper uses the Mantel test with Pearson correlation for that question http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Cluster 2D single-cell embeddings (e.g. ivis or t-SNE embeddings of CyTOF data) with PhenoGraph and score agreement against manually gated cell-population labels using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), as done in the Szubert et al. 2019 ivis benchmark on the BMMC (Levine-32-dim) and Samusik CyTOF datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Cluster 2D single-cell embeddings (e.g. ivis or t-SNE embeddings of CyTOF data) with PhenoGraph and score agreement against manually gated cell-population labels using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), as done in the Szubert et al. 2019 ivis benchmark on the BMMC (Levine-32-dim) and Samusik CyTOF datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no manually gated cell-population labels, so ARI cannot be computed — use unsupervised metrics or the Mantel-test PCC on centroid distances instead The data are raw FCS files that have not yet been arcsinh-transformed and MinMax-scaled; clustering unscaled cytometry intensities is out of scope for this workflow The goal is to assess preservation of global inter-cluster geometry rather than cluster recoverability — the paper uses the Mantel test with Pearson correlation for that question

skills.description: Use when you must select a small global feature/gene set that jointly distinguishes every pair of phenotypes (e.g., cell type × tissue combinations) from a phenotype × gene score matrix, where per-group DE genes overlap and pairwise discrimination matters.
skills.name: phenotype-cover-marker-selection
skills.search_text: phenotype-cover-marker-selection Use when you must select a small global feature/gene set that jointly distinguishes every pair of phenotypes (e.g., cell type × tissue combinations) from a phenotype × gene score matrix, where per-group DE genes overlap and pairwise discrimination matters. When only a small number of distinct groups exist with non-overlapping differentially expressed genes — standard per-group DE marker selection suffices (the paper targets many groups with overlapping DE genes). When you need an optimal (not approximate) solution — G-PC is a greedy approximation and does not provide an optimal solution. When input is raw scRNA-seq counts without a phenotype × feature score matrix — the matrix must be constructed (and log-transformed) first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies the phenotype-cover (PC) formulation — equivalent to the NP-complete multiset multicover problem — to select a global set of biomarkers that discriminates every phenotype pair in a phenotype × feature score matrix. Provides two polynomial-time approximators, G-PC (extended greedy set cover) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy method), with CEM-PC finalizing the marker set from features whose probability score exceeds 0.98 after convergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Applies the phenotype-cover (PC) formulation — equivalent to the NP-complete multiset multicover problem — to select a global set of biomarkers that discriminates every phenotype pair in a phenotype × feature score matrix. Provides two polynomial-time approximators, G-PC (extended greedy set cover) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy method), with CEM-PC finalizing the marker set from features whose probability score exceeds 0.98 after convergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a small number of distinct groups exist with non-overlapping differentially expressed genes — standard per-group DE marker selection suffices (the paper targets many groups with overlapping DE genes). When you need an optimal (not approximate) solution — G-PC is a greedy approximation and does not provide an optimal solution. When input is raw scRNA-seq counts without a phenotype × feature score matrix — the matrix must be constructed (and log-transformed) first.

skills.description: Use when marker selection must produce a single global feature set that discriminates between many overlapping phenotypes (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or HCA scRNA-seq data), not just per-group DE genes.
skills.name: phenotype-cover-optimization
skills.search_text: phenotype-cover-optimization Use when marker selection must produce a single global feature set that discriminates between many overlapping phenotypes (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or HCA scRNA-seq data), not just per-group DE genes. The goal is per-group differentially expressed genes rather than a single global marker set discriminating between many overlapping phenotypes (e.g., a small number of distinct major cell types) An optimal (not approximate) solution to the covering problem is required — G-PC provides no optimality guarantee The input is already a curated marker list or a feature table unrelated to phenotype-pair discrimination http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Formulates discriminative marker selection as the phenotype cover (PC) problem — finding the smallest feature set such that every phenotype pair is covered — and solves it via the G-PC (greedy) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy) polynomial-time approximations from Hasanaj et al. 2022. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Formulates discriminative marker selection as the phenotype cover (PC) problem — finding the smallest feature set such that every phenotype pair is covered — and solves it via the G-PC (greedy) and CEM-PC (cross-entropy) polynomial-time approximations from Hasanaj et al. 2022.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-group differentially expressed genes rather than a single global marker set discriminating between many overlapping phenotypes (e.g., a small number of distinct major cell types) An optimal (not approximate) solution to the covering problem is required — G-PC provides no optimality guarantee The input is already a curated marker list or a feature table unrelated to phenotype-pair discrimination

skills.description: Use when you need to select a global biomarker set that discriminates every phenotype pair in a phenotype x feature score matrix, or when scoring a gene set by the phenotype-pair coverage it attains (e.g., CEM-PC with I=500 iterations, Rs=1000 elite samples).
skills.name: phenotype-pair-coverage-scoring
skills.search_text: phenotype-pair-coverage-scoring Use when you need to select a global biomarker set that discriminates every phenotype pair in a phenotype x feature score matrix, or when scoring a gene set by the phenotype-pair coverage it attains (e.g., CEM-PC with I=500 iterations, Rs=1000 elite samples). You need per-class one-vs-rest markers only, not a global set that discriminates every phenotype pair — ordinary DE analysis may suffice when there is a small number of distinct groups You need the provably optimal cover: PC is NP-complete via multiset multicover, and CEM-PC (like G-PC) provides an approximation, not an optimal solution Input is raw counts without log transformation — the README notes X may need log-transforming when working with raw counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Score a candidate marker gene set by the phenotype-pair coverage it attains over a phenotype x gene score matrix (e.g., IPF scRNA-seq), as formulated in the phenotype cover (PC) / multiset multicover problem. This coverage-rewarding, size-penalizing score drives both the CEM-PC cross-entropy solver and final marker-set extraction (features with probability score > 0.98). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Score a candidate marker gene set by the phenotype-pair coverage it attains over a phenotype x gene score matrix (e.g., IPF scRNA-seq), as formulated in the phenotype cover (PC) / multiset multicover problem. This coverage-rewarding, size-penalizing score drives both the CEM-PC cross-entropy solver and final marker-set extraction (features with probability score > 0.98).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-class one-vs-rest markers only, not a global set that discriminates every phenotype pair — ordinary DE analysis may suffice when there is a small number of distinct groups You need the provably optimal cover: PC is NP-complete via multiset multicover, and CEM-PC (like G-PC) provides an approximation, not an optimal solution Input is raw counts without log transformation — the README notes X may need log-transforming when working with raw counts

skills.description: Use when you have cell embeddings (GRN module AUCell scores or batch-corrected PCs) plus cell-level phenotype labels and need a quantitative readout of biological signal retention, e.g., reproducing Figure S6-style embedding comparisons.
skills.name: phenotype-prediction-f1-scoring
skills.search_text: phenotype-prediction-f1-scoring Use when you have cell embeddings (GRN module AUCell scores or batch-corrected PCs) plus cell-level phenotype labels and need a quantitative readout of biological signal retention, e.g., reproducing Figure S6-style embedding comparisons. Input is a raw count matrix without any embedding or corrected representation — build embeddings first (e.g., SCING AUCell module scores) before scoring phenotypes. The goal is measuring batch mixing alone rather than biological signal retention — the neighborhood score (Equation 1) sweep is the more direct metric. Data has no meaningful cell-level phenotype labels (diagnosis, sex, stage); F1 of phenotype prediction would be undefined or uninformative. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how well a cell embedding (e.g., SCING GRN module AUCell scores) retains biological information by predicting a cell-level phenotype annotation (diagnosis, sex, tangle/plaque stage) and scoring it with the phenotype F1 score (Equation 2), enabling comparison against batch-correction baselines like FastMNN, Harmony, and Seurat. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Quantifies how well a cell embedding (e.g., SCING GRN module AUCell scores) retains biological information by predicting a cell-level phenotype annotation (diagnosis, sex, tangle/plaque stage) and scoring it with the phenotype F1 score (Equation 2), enabling comparison against batch-correction baselines like FastMNN, Harmony, and Seurat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix without any embedding or corrected representation — build embeddings first (e.g., SCING AUCell module scores) before scoring phenotypes. The goal is measuring batch mixing alone rather than biological signal retention — the neighborhood score (Equation 1) sweep is the more direct metric. Data has no meaningful cell-level phenotype labels (diagnosis, sex, stage); F1 of phenotype prediction would be undefined or uninformative.

skills.description: Use when fitting scKINETICS to single-cell transcriptomic data and a prior constraining cells' future states along the phenotypic manifold is needed to regularize the EM-learned gene regulatory network and velocities.
skills.name: phenotypic-manifold-constraint-sampling
skills.search_text: phenotypic-manifold-constraint-sampling Use when fitting scKINETICS to single-cell transcriptomic data and a prior constraining cells' future states along the phenotypic manifold is needed to regularize the EM-learned gene regulatory network and velocities. When no phenotypic ordering or manifold structure is apparent in the data (e.g., dissociated cells lacking a trajectory axis) — the constraint prior would impose spurious future-state restrictions. When the goal is purely an ATAC-seq-derived epigenetic prior — scKINETICS treats epigenetic masks and manifold constraints as separate, distinct priors. When the expression matrix lacks per-cell cluster labels needed to seed the manifold per phenograph cluster. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates a phenotypic manifold constraint on cells' future states — one of the biologically motivated priors in scKINETICS — by seeding DBSCAN clusters on the phenotypic manifold and sampling from truncated normals to initialize the EM fit of per-cluster regulatory dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Estimates a phenotypic manifold constraint on cells' future states — one of the biologically motivated priors in scKINETICS — by seeding DBSCAN clusters on the phenotypic manifold and sampling from truncated normals to initialize the EM fit of per-cluster regulatory dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no phenotypic ordering or manifold structure is apparent in the data (e.g., dissociated cells lacking a trajectory axis) — the constraint prior would impose spurious future-state restrictions. When the goal is purely an ATAC-seq-derived epigenetic prior — scKINETICS treats epigenetic masks and manifold constraints as separate, distinct priors. When the expression matrix lacks per-cell cluster labels needed to seed the manifold per phenograph cluster.

skills.description: Use when evaluating which decoupleR methods recover perturbed kinases (regulators) from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when comparing phospho-proteomics method rankings against transcriptomics rankings.
skills.name: phosphoproteomics-perturbation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: phosphoproteomics-perturbation-benchmarking Use when evaluating which decoupleR methods recover perturbed kinases (regulators) from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when comparing phospho-proteomics method rankings against transcriptomics rankings. The goal is to benchmark methods on transcriptomic perturbation experiments (RNA) rather than phospho-proteomics — use run_rna_bench.R instead You only need to run inference on a single dataset with one chosen method rather than evaluate/benchmark multiple methods across perturbation experiments Your prior knowledge network is not a kinase-substrate resource and the perturbation targets are transcription factors, not kinases http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark decoupleR statistical methods for inferring kinase activities from phospho-proteomics perturbation experiments using the decoupleRBench package and the Hernandez-Armenta et al. 2017 collection, ranking 11 methods plus the consensus score by sensitivity of perturbed-kinase recovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Benchmark decoupleR statistical methods for inferring kinase activities from phospho-proteomics perturbation experiments using the decoupleRBench package and the Hernandez-Armenta et al. 2017 collection, ranking 11 methods plus the consensus score by sensitivity of perturbed-kinase recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark methods on transcriptomic perturbation experiments (RNA) rather than phospho-proteomics — use run_rna_bench.R instead You only need to run inference on a single dataset with one chosen method rather than evaluate/benchmark multiple methods across perturbation experiments Your prior knowledge network is not a kinase-substrate resource and the perturbation targets are transcription factors, not kinases

skills.description: Use when you have matched single-cell expression data and a reconstructed lineage tree and need to test whether user-defined gene signatures are heritable, i.e. associated with phylogenetic structure.
skills.name: phylogenetic-autocorrelation-analysis
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-autocorrelation-analysis Use when you have matched single-cell expression data and a reconstructed lineage tree and need to test whether user-defined gene signatures are heritable, i.e. associated with phylogenetic structure. You want de novo modules rather than testing user-defined signatures — use Hotspot-based module detection instead No lineage/phylogeny is available or the tree covers cells absent from the expression matrix — Geary's C on cophenetic distances requires matched cells on a tree You only need phylogeny visualization with annotation overlays (iTOL, CeLaVi) without joint expression-lineage statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies whether gene signature scores vary consistently among nearby cells on a single-cell phylogeny by computing Geary's C phylogenetic autocorrelation statistics (reported as C' = 1 - C) on a KNN graph built from cophenetic distances, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR against randomly generated signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Quantifies whether gene signature scores vary consistently among nearby cells on a single-cell phylogeny by computing Geary's C phylogenetic autocorrelation statistics (reported as C' = 1 - C) on a KNN graph built from cophenetic distances, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR against randomly generated signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want de novo modules rather than testing user-defined signatures — use Hotspot-based module detection instead No lineage/phylogeny is available or the tree covers cells absent from the expression matrix — Geary's C on cophenetic distances requires matched cells on a tree You only need phylogeny visualization with annotation overlays (iTOL, CeLaVi) without joint expression-lineage statistics

skills.description: Use when OrthoFinder rooted gene trees and an of2orthomap-derived orthomap (with LCA gene age classes) are available for a focal species such as Danio rerio, and you need per-orthogroup completeness along the lineage to flag low-continuity, HGT-suspect orthogroups.
skills.name: phylogenetic-node-completeness-scoring
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-node-completeness-scoring Use when OrthoFinder rooted gene trees and an of2orthomap-derived orthomap (with LCA gene age classes) are available for a focal species such as Danio rerio, and you need per-orthogroup completeness along the lineage to flag low-continuity, HGT-suspect orthogroups. OrthoFinder was run without gene tree inference (orthogroup membership only) — there are no internal tree nodes to walk, so continuity cannot be computed The goal is simply assigning gene ages (LCA classes) per gene or calculating TEI from scRNA objects — those are handled by of2orthomap and the Scanpy-based TEI workflow, not node-completeness scoring The orthogroup is single-species or the focal species gene is absent from the tree — no LCA-to-focal path exists to score http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Computes an optional per-orthogroup continuity score from oggmap/OrthoFinder output, quantifying species completeness at each tree node along the LCA-to-focal-species path so that intermediate nodes lacking detectable orthologs (candidate horizontal gene transfer) are exposed. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Computes an optional per-orthogroup continuity score from oggmap/OrthoFinder output, quantifying species completeness at each tree node along the LCA-to-focal-species path so that intermediate nodes lacking detectable orthologs (candidate horizontal gene transfer) are exposed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: OrthoFinder was run without gene tree inference (orthogroup membership only) — there are no internal tree nodes to walk, so continuity cannot be computed The goal is simply assigning gene ages (LCA classes) per gene or calculating TEI from scRNA objects — those are handled by of2orthomap and the Scanpy-based TEI workflow, not node-completeness scoring The orthogroup is single-species or the focal species gene is absent from the tree — no LCA-to-focal path exists to score

skills.description: Use when you have small RNA-seq reads that failed to map to the human genome (e.g. STAR *_Aligned_UnMapped.bam) and need microbial species-level read counts per taxon.
skills.name: phylogenetic-taxon-read-counting
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-taxon-read-counting Use when you have small RNA-seq reads that failed to map to the human genome (e.g. STAR *_Aligned_UnMapped.bam) and need microbial species-level read counts per taxon. Reads already mapped to the human genome — those go to the Annotation module, not the Microbe module You need shotgun metagenomic abundance profiling with per-sample relative abundance normalization rather than small RNA fragment microbial read counts Your target taxon is outside the four supported taxons (archaea, bacteria, fungi, viruses) http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Aggregate BLAST hits of human-unmapped small RNA-seq reads against the UCSC nt database into per-taxon read counts across the four supported microbial taxons (archaea, bacteria, fungi, viruses), using the phylogenetic tree to list all potential taxa because of interspecies homology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Aggregate BLAST hits of human-unmapped small RNA-seq reads against the UCSC nt database into per-taxon read counts across the four supported microbial taxons (archaea, bacteria, fungi, viruses), using the phylogenetic tree to list all potential taxa because of interspecies homology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads already mapped to the human genome — those go to the Annotation module, not the Microbe module You need shotgun metagenomic abundance profiling with per-sample relative abundance normalization rather than small RNA fragment microbial read counts Your target taxon is outside the four supported taxons (archaea, bacteria, fungi, viruses)

skills.description: Use when simulating single-cell RNA-seq data for multiple discrete populations or continuous trajectories whose relationships should follow a lineage/phylogenetic tree, and you need to validate that the simulated heterogeneity (Sigma) preserves tree structure in low-dimensional embeddings.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-based-population-modeling
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-based-population-modeling Use when simulating single-cell RNA-seq data for multiple discrete populations or continuous trajectories whose relationships should follow a lineage/phylogenetic tree, and you need to validate that the simulated heterogeneity (Sigma) preserves tree structure in low-dimensional embeddings. Simulating a single homogeneous population — SymSim handles this with one-population EVF type and no tree input is needed You need observed counts with library-preparation and sequencing effects rather than true transcript counts — True2ObservedCounts must then be applied on top, which this tree-modeling skill does not cover The populations are unrelated / no lineage or tree relationship should be imposed on the cell groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate discrete or continuous cell populations whose relationship is defined by a phylogenetic tree using SymSim's SimulateTrueCounts with extrinsic variability factors (EVFs) evolving along the tree (e.g. Brownian motion), then verify that tSNE plots of log2(true_counts+1) reflect the input tree structure as the within-population variability parameter Sigma varies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Simulate discrete or continuous cell populations whose relationship is defined by a phylogenetic tree using SymSim's SimulateTrueCounts with extrinsic variability factors (EVFs) evolving along the tree (e.g. Brownian motion), then verify that tSNE plots of log2(true_counts+1) reflect the input tree structure as the within-population variability parameter Sigma varies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Simulating a single homogeneous population — SymSim handles this with one-population EVF type and no tree input is needed You need observed counts with library-preparation and sequencing effects rather than true transcript counts — True2ObservedCounts must then be applied on top, which this tree-modeling skill does not cover The populations are unrelated / no lineage or tree relationship should be imposed on the cell groups

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (Newick/phylo with cells as leaves) and need to partition tip cells into a fixed number of subpopulations that each correspond to a clade of the reconstructed phylogeny.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-breadth-first-clustering
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-breadth-first-clustering Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (Newick/phylo with cells as leaves) and need to partition tip cells into a fixed number of subpopulations that each correspond to a clade of the reconstructed phylogeny. You need expression-driven (transcriptional) clusters rather than lineage/clade-defined subpopulations — this skill partitions by tree topology, not expression similarity The tree has not had unifurcations collapsed; running on a tree with single-child internal nodes breaks the assumption that every internal node branches properly You need continuous lineage metrics such as relative fitness, which the article notes 'are not directly supported within our software' http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters cells on a single-cell phylogeny (ape phylo object) by a breadth-first search over internal nodes, collecting the leaves beneath selected nodes into exactly `target` (default 10) phylogenetically coherent subpopulation labels such as VISION_Clusters_Tree / meta$DepthClusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Clusters cells on a single-cell phylogeny (ape phylo object) by a breadth-first search over internal nodes, collecting the leaves beneath selected nodes into exactly `target` (default 10) phylogenetically coherent subpopulation labels such as VISION_Clusters_Tree / meta$DepthClusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need expression-driven (transcriptional) clusters rather than lineage/clade-defined subpopulations — this skill partitions by tree topology, not expression similarity The tree has not had unifurcations collapsed; running on a tree with single-child internal nodes breaks the assumption that every internal node branches properly You need continuous lineage metrics such as relative fitness, which the article notes 'are not directly supported within our software'

skills.description: Use when a reconstructed lineage or phylogenetic tree (e.g., Newick format from LinRace) must be partitioned at a specified depth and tip-level annotations (e.g., 34 cell types over 9707 mouse embryo cells) summarized per subtree in R.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-manipulation-in-r
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-manipulation-in-r Use when a reconstructed lineage or phylogenetic tree (e.g., Newick format from LinRace) must be partitioned at a specified depth and tip-level annotations (e.g., 34 cell types over 9707 mouse embryo cells) summarized per subtree in R. This enables downstream analyses such as checking whether barcode-reconstructed subtrees are consistent with transcriptome-derived cell type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3

This enables downstream analyses such as checking whether barcode-reconstructed subtrees are consistent with transcriptome-derived cell type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to evaluate tree reconstruction accuracy itself (use Nye similarity or Robinson-Foulds distance against a ground-truth tree instead of subtree composition analysis) The cell annotations are missing or not mappable to tree tip labels, so per-subtree cell-type tabulation is impossible Your goal is comparing alternative reconstruction methods (e.g., LinRace vs DCLEAR vs Cassiopeia) on topology, not analyzing composition of a single tree

skills.description: Use when several lineage or phylogenetic trees have been reconstructed from the same cell set (e.g., competing lineage-reconstruction methods) and you need to compare their local resolution via maximum root-to-tip depth and internal-node counts.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-topology-comparison
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-topology-comparison Use when several lineage or phylogenetic trees have been reconstructed from the same cell set (e.g., competing lineage-reconstruction methods) and you need to compare their local resolution via maximum root-to-tip depth and internal-node counts. When edge lengths carry biological meaning and must be preserved (this skill discards edge lengths to compare topology only) When trees cover different cell sets — node and depth counts are not comparable across different tips When accuracy against a ground-truth tree is needed — use distance metrics like normalized Robinson-Foulds (RF.dist) instead of local-resolution counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Compares reconstructed lineage/phylogenetic trees from multiple methods on local-resolution metrics — maximum root-to-tip depth and number of internal nodes — to quantify how much hierarchical structure each reconstruction recovers, as done for LinRace vs Cassiopeia, LinTIMaT, and DCLEAR on the scGESTALT zebrafish ZF1-F3 sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Compares reconstructed lineage/phylogenetic trees from multiple methods on local-resolution metrics — maximum root-to-tip depth and number of internal nodes — to quantify how much hierarchical structure each reconstruction recovers, as done for LinRace vs Cassiopeia, LinTIMaT, and DCLEAR on the scGESTALT zebrafish ZF1-F3 sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When edge lengths carry biological meaning and must be preserved (this skill discards edge lengths to compare topology only) When trees cover different cell sets — node and depth counts are not comparable across different tips When accuracy against a ground-truth tree is needed — use distance metrics like normalized Robinson-Foulds (RF.dist) instead of local-resolution counts

skills.description: Use when a single-cell lineage-tracing dataset has a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 lineage trees from Cassiopeia) that must be interactively browsed, selected, and overlaid with UMAP/tSNE projections and metadata in a shareable web report.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-visualization
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-visualization Use when a single-cell lineage-tracing dataset has a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 lineage trees from Cassiopeia) that must be interactively browsed, selected, and overlaid with UMAP/tSNE projections and metadata in a shareable web report. Only a static, publication-figure tree is needed — iTOL is a web-server tool for uploading tree structures and annotation files for interactive viewing without an R analysis session No lineage/phylogenetic data are available and only scRNA-seq expression interpretation is required — plain VISION handles signature enrichment without a tree The tree exceeds the tested scale (~4,000 leaves), where low-latency selections and subtree collapsing were validated Render single-cell lineage phylogenies as an interactive radial or linear tree display embedded in a shareable web-based report (via PhyloVision's PhyloPlot.js on the VISION front-end), supporting low-latency cell selections and subtree collapsing for exploratory lineage-expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Render single-cell lineage phylogenies as an interactive radial or linear tree display embedded in a shareable web-based report (via PhyloVision's PhyloPlot.js on the VISION front-end), supporting low-latency cell selections and subtree collapsing for exploratory lineage-expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a static, publication-figure tree is needed — iTOL is a web-server tool for uploading tree structures and annotation files for interactive viewing without an R analysis session No lineage/phylogenetic data are available and only scRNA-seq expression interpretation is required — plain VISION handles signature enrichment without a tree The tree exceeds the tested scale (~4,000 leaves), where low-latency selections and subtree collapsing were validated

skills.description: Use when a single-cell phylogeny and an expression matrix must be reconciled before lineage-aware analysis — e.g., cells present in one modality but not the other, unifurcations in the tree, or raw UMI counts needing normalization.
skills.name: phylogeny-preprocessing-and-pruning
skills.search_text: phylogeny-preprocessing-and-pruning Use when a single-cell phylogeny and an expression matrix must be reconciled before lineage-aware analysis — e.g., cells present in one modality but not the other, unifurcations in the tree, or raw UMI counts needing normalization. The input is already a normalized, filtered expression matrix paired with a binary tree free of unifurcations whose leaves exactly match the cell barcodes The analysis goal is pure tree visualization without joining expression data (iTOL/CeLaVi-style overlays suffice) The tree leaves do not correspond to individual cells (e.g., a species-level phylogeny) — the barcode-matching preprocessing is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prepare a single-cell phylogeny (e.g., a Cassiopeia-reconstructed tumor tree from Quinn et al. 2021 clone CP007) and its matched scRNA-seq data for downstream PhyloVision/Hotspot analysis by pruning to shared cells, collapsing unifurcations, library-size normalizing counts, and selecting informative genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Prepare a single-cell phylogeny (e.g., a Cassiopeia-reconstructed tumor tree from Quinn et al. 2021 clone CP007) and its matched scRNA-seq data for downstream PhyloVision/Hotspot analysis by pruning to shared cells, collapsing unifurcations, library-size normalizing counts, and selecting informative genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized, filtered expression matrix paired with a binary tree free of unifurcations whose leaves exactly match the cell barcodes The analysis goal is pure tree visualization without joining expression data (iTOL/CeLaVi-style overlays suffice) The tree leaves do not correspond to individual cells (e.g., a species-level phylogeny) — the barcode-matching preprocessing is meaningless

skills.description: Use when you have mapped RNA-seq reads (BAM) and need a genome-wide BAF/allelic-shift profile at germline SNP sites to support CNV or LOH inference, without a matched DNA variant call set.
skills.name: pileup-based-snv-allele-frequency-extraction
skills.search_text: pileup-based-snv-allele-frequency-extraction Use when you have mapped RNA-seq reads (BAM) and need a genome-wide BAF/allelic-shift profile at germline SNP sites to support CNV or LOH inference, without a matched DNA variant call set. Data are 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) with sparse variants near gene 3' ends, degrading the BAF shift signal You need heterozygous genotype calls for downstream variant-level analyses rather than genome-wide BAF shift profiles for CNV correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signal directly from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract's two-step pileup pipeline, without requiring a pre-called heterozygous variant set. skills.summary: Generates a genome-wide B-allele frequency (BAF) shift signal directly from mapped RNA-seq reads using BAFExtract's two-step pileup pipeline, without requiring a pre-called heterozygous variant set. skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are 3'-only sequencing (e.g. DropSeq) with sparse variants near gene 3' ends, degrading the BAF shift signal You need heterozygous genotype calls for downstream variant-level analyses rather than genome-wide BAF shift profiles for CNV correction

skills.search_text: plaza-dicot-monocot-species-partitioning Use when reproducing or updating species-coverage counts for precomputed gene age class assignments, specifically when the PLAZA source must be split into dicot vs monocot species blocks alongside Ensembl and eggNOG counts. The goal is to build a de novo orthomap for a single query species (use plaza2orthomap/of2orthomap extraction, not coverage counting). The input is already an aggregated coverage table or the species partition (dicot/monocot) is already annotated — recomputing partitions would be redundant. The source data is not PLAZA (e.g. OrthoFinder or orthomcl output), where this dicot/monocot partitioning does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Enumerate the eukaryotic species with precomputed LCA-derived gene age assignments from PLAZA gene family data via oggmap, and partition them into dicot and monocot lineages so per-source coverage counts (PLAZA v5: 98 dicots + 52 monocots) can be aggregated with Ensembl and eggNOG blocks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Enumerate the eukaryotic species with precomputed LCA-derived gene age assignments from PLAZA gene family data via oggmap, and partition them into dicot and monocot lineages so per-source coverage counts (PLAZA v5: 98 dicots + 52 monocots) can be aggregated with Ensembl and eggNOG blocks.

skills.name: plink-ld-reference-processing
skills.search_text: plink-ld-reference-processing Use when training eQTL weights from summary-level data (OTTERS-style TWAS Stage I) and you must supply a PLINK 1.9 .bed/.bim/.fam LD reference panel plus gene annotation to drive LD clumping and per-gene extraction. The analysis already has individual-level reference genotype-expression data (e.g. GTEx V6/V8), where FUSION-style individual-level training is the more direct choice The reference panel genotype build or ancestry does not match the eQTL summary statistics or the selected lassosum LD blocks (e.g. hg38 genotypes with hg19 blocks) The trait association test is already done and you only need Stage II TWAS testing, which consumes the trained weights rather than rebuilding the LD reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Prepare and extract a PLINK-binary LD reference panel and per-gene LD blocks so that OTTERS Stage I can clump cis-eQTLs (r2=0.99) and train eQTL weights with P+T, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS. PLINK 1.9 and TABIX are integrated into OTTERS to slice the reference per target gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Prepare and extract a PLINK-binary LD reference panel and per-gene LD blocks so that OTTERS Stage I can clump cis-eQTLs (r2=0.99) and train eQTL weights with P+T, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS. PLINK 1.9 and TABIX are integrated into OTTERS to slice the reference per target gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis already has individual-level reference genotype-expression data (e.g. GTEx V6/V8), where FUSION-style individual-level training is the more direct choice The reference panel genotype build or ancestry does not match the eQTL summary statistics or the selected lassosum LD blocks (e.g. hg38 genotypes with hg19 blocks) The trait association test is already done and you only need Stage II TWAS testing, which consumes the trained weights rather than rebuilding the LD reference

skills.description: Use when validating RNA-seq-derived CNV calls against matched DNA-seq absolute copy-number ground truth in single cells, so absolute copy numbers must be expressed relative to ploidy before computing TPR/FPR.
skills.name: ploidy-relative-copy-number-conversion
skills.search_text: ploidy-relative-copy-number-conversion Use when validating RNA-seq-derived CNV calls against matched DNA-seq absolute copy-number ground truth in single cells, so absolute copy numbers must be expressed relative to ploidy before computing TPR/FPR. Ground truth is already relative copy number or a binary loss/gain label — no ploidy conversion is needed No matched DNA copy-number data exist (e.g., MM135 10x cells, where exact ground truth CNV calls are unknown); rely on tool concordance instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts absolute DNA copy-number ground truth (e.g., from DR-Seq simultaneous RNA/DNA measurements) into relative copy numbers via a ploidy formula, enabling direct comparison against RNA-seq-based CNV calls from CaSpER. This normalization is required because CaSpER reports relative (loss/heterozygous-loss/gain) states rather than absolute copy counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Converts absolute DNA copy-number ground truth (e.g., from DR-Seq simultaneous RNA/DNA measurements) into relative copy numbers via a ploidy formula, enabling direct comparison against RNA-seq-based CNV calls from CaSpER. This normalization is required because CaSpER reports relative (loss/heterozygous-loss/gain) states rather than absolute copy counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground truth is already relative copy number or a binary loss/gain label — no ploidy conversion is needed No matched DNA copy-number data exist (e.g., MM135 10x cells, where exact ground truth CNV calls are unknown); rely on tool concordance instead

skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is normal/non-cancer tissue: scATOMIC's default model assumes at least some cancer cells are present, so ploidy-agreement validation is inappropriate (use the normal_tissue parameter instead) The goal is to determine a cancer's tissue of origin rather than validate malignant-cell calls — CNV inference cannot provide the cancer's tissue of origin The dataset is already a curated cell-type annotation table with no raw counts to re-run CopyKAT CNV inference on

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq profiles (e.g. hESC vs progenitor/differentiated populations) must be ranked or classified by differentiation potency without marker genes, feature selection, or training labels.
skills.name: pluripotency-discrimination-assessment
skills.search_text: pluripotency-discrimination-assessment Use when single-cell RNA-Seq profiles (e.g. hESC vs progenitor/differentiated populations) must be ranked or classified by differentiation potency without marker genes, feature selection, or training labels. The task is pseudo-time ordering or trajectory inference with tools such as Monocle or MPath, which the paper notes cannot readily obtain this network-entropy potency insight. No matched PPI/connectome network is available for the expression matrix, since SR's discrimination depends on network-constrained expression patterns (reshuffling over the network abolishes it). The analysis requires potency estimates derived from prior biological knowledge such as marker expression or timepoint, which SCENT is explicitly designed to avoid. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the normalized signalling entropy rate (SR) per single cell with the SCENT R package by integrating an scRNA-Seq expression matrix with a PPI connectome, then tests whether SR alone discriminates pluripotent from non-pluripotent cells (Chu et al.: Spearman 0.91, ROC AUC 0.96) without feature selection or training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Computes the normalized signalling entropy rate (SR) per single cell with the SCENT R package by integrating an scRNA-Seq expression matrix with a PPI connectome, then tests whether SR alone discriminates pluripotent from non-pluripotent cells (Chu et al.: Spearman 0.91, ROC AUC 0.96) without feature selection or training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is pseudo-time ordering or trajectory inference with tools such as Monocle or MPath, which the paper notes cannot readily obtain this network-entropy potency insight. No matched PPI/connectome network is available for the expression matrix, since SR's discrimination depends on network-constrained expression patterns (reshuffling over the network abolishes it). The analysis requires potency estimates derived from prior biological knowledge such as marker expression or timepoint, which SCENT is explicitly designed to avoid.

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime and memory footprint of pluripotency/potency scoring tools (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on scRNA-seq count matrices from breast, colon, hematopoietic, or lung datasets.

skills.search_text: pluripotency-score-computation-across-tools Use when comparing runtime and memory footprint of pluripotency/potency scoring tools (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on scRNA-seq count matrices from breast, colon, hematopoietic, or lung datasets. The goal is biological accuracy of pluripotency ranking rather than computational efficiency — the Table 1 benchmark only measures runtime and RAM, not score agreement with known biology The input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or single-cell ATAC-seq) — ORIGINS' activity() expects a gene-by-cell expression matrix You need PPINs for biological processes other than differentiation — the extended ORIGINS2 package, not ORIGINS, provides 18 process-specific PPINs and custom PPIN construction http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce the computational benchmark from Senra et al. (2022) comparing ORIGINS' differentiation activity score against LandSCENT (SR) and CytoTRACE across four GEO scRNA-seq datasets, recording elapsed runtime and extra RAM per tool per dataset (Table 1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Reproduce the computational benchmark from Senra et al. (2022) comparing ORIGINS' differentiation activity score against LandSCENT (SR) and CytoTRACE across four GEO scRNA-seq datasets, recording elapsed runtime and extra RAM per tool per dataset (Table 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological accuracy of pluripotency ranking rather than computational efficiency — the Table 1 benchmark only measures runtime and RAM, not score agreement with known biology The input is not a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or single-cell ATAC-seq) — ORIGINS' activity() expects a gene-by-cell expression matrix You need PPINs for biological processes other than differentiation — the extended ORIGINS2 package, not ORIGINS, provides 18 process-specific PPINs and custom PPIN construction

skills.search_text: pmhc-binding-immunogenicity-scoring Use when 8–11-aa mutant peptides extracted from annotated tumor SNV/INDEL calls must be paired with OptiType-derived HLA alleles and ranked by pMHC binding plus immunogenicity to prioritize neoantigens. No patient HLA typing is available (DeepHLApan in TSNAD requires OptiType-derived HLA alleles as input) The task requires TCR-pMHC interaction prediction — the article states no TCR-pMHC binding prediction model is included and this is future work Peptides outside the 8–11 amino acid range or non-MHC-I binding scoring is needed, since the extraction step covers only lengths 8 to 11 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_3306 Scores candidate peptide-MHC (pMHC) pairs for both binding affinity and immunogenicity using DeepHLApan 1.1 inside TSNAD v2.0, replacing the binding-only NetMHCpan step; this dual scoring significantly reduced false positives in neoantigen prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016

skills.search_text: pmhc-specificity-cluster-purity-analysis Use when comparing embeddings (TCR-only, RNA-only, Harmony-corrected, multimodal mvTCR) of paired scRNA/TCR-seq data by how compactly and purely they cluster cells sharing a pMHC specificity annotation. Benchmarks clustering quality against the published NMI ranking (TCR 0.408, RNA 0.456, Harmony 0.212, mvTCR 0.535).

skills.name: pod5-raw-signal-processing
skills.search_text: pod5-raw-signal-processing Use when raw ONT dRNA pod5 or fast5 signal files must be basecalled in a single step that simultaneously calls canonical (A,C,G,U) and modified bases (I, m6A, m1A, m5C, Psi), avoiding re-squiggling and separate modification models. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled FASTQ/BAM data without raw ionic signals — NanoSpeech requires raw pod5/fast5 signal input The analysis needs modification probabilities requiring post-processing with ModKit-style tools — NanoSpeech calls modified bases directly during basecalling without such steps Only DNA nanopore reads are present — the pipeline is designed for direct RNA sequencing data from ONT chemistries (SQK-RNA002, SQK-RNA004)

skills.description: Use when you have high-confidence candidate genes linked to a binary resistance trait (e.g. GWAS-derived resistant vs susceptible accessions) and need an ordered, score-based ranking to pick a small validation set such as a top-10 per pathogen.
skills.name: point-biserial-correlation-scoring
skills.search_text: point-biserial-correlation-scoring Use when you have high-confidence candidate genes linked to a binary resistance trait (e.g. GWAS-derived resistant vs susceptible accessions) and need an ordered, score-based ranking to pick a small validation set such as a top-10 per pathogen. When your association variable is continuous-continuous rather than binary-vs-continuous — a point-biserial correlation is specific to a dichotomous trait such as resistant/susceptible accession status. When genes lack hub or transcription-factor annotations in the SoyFungiGCN hubs dataset, the kappa multiplier degenerates to 1 and ranking power is reduced. When the goal is coexpression network construction or module enrichment (mod_enrich) rather than prioritizing/ranking an existing candidate gene set. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks prioritized soybean candidate resistance genes by scoring each gene as the product of its point-biserial correlation with the resistance-associated trait and a kappa multiplier derived from hub and transcription-factor status, then selecting the top 10 genes per fungal pathogen. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Ranks prioritized soybean candidate resistance genes by scoring each gene as the product of its point-biserial correlation with the resistance-associated trait and a kappa multiplier derived from hub and transcription-factor status, then selecting the top 10 genes per fungal pathogen.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When your association variable is continuous-continuous rather than binary-vs-continuous — a point-biserial correlation is specific to a dichotomous trait such as resistant/susceptible accession status. When genes lack hub or transcription-factor annotations in the SoyFungiGCN hubs dataset, the kappa multiplier degenerates to 1 and ranking power is reduced. When the goal is coexpression network construction or module enrichment (mod_enrich) rather than prioritizing/ranking an existing candidate gene set.

skills.description: Use when two paired single-cell modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of the same granulocyte cells) have been mapped between domains by scMMGAN, CycleGAN, or CMAE and you must verify that predictions retain point-wise correspondence with ground truth rather than only matching the marginal.
skills.name: point-wise-correlation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: point-wise-correlation-benchmarking Use when two paired single-cell modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of the same granulocyte cells) have been mapped between domains by scMMGAN, CycleGAN, or CMAE and you must verify that predictions retain point-wise correspondence with ground truth rather than only matching the marginal. Only unpaired modalities with no ground-truth measurements of the target modality — point-wise correlation cannot be computed without per-cell paired truth You only need distribution-level agreement between generated and true populations; MMD alone suffices and point-wise correlation would conflate alignment quality with correspondence The mapping has not yet been trained/converged — GAN training is unstable and the model can deteriorate from effective to ineffective across iterations, invalidating the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark for judging whether cross-modal single-cell mappings (e.g., ATAC-seq to RNA-seq) preserve point-wise correspondence: after generating predictions with scMMGAN, CycleGAN, and CMAE, compute the correlation between each predicted value and the ground-truth measurement of the target modality. A high point-wise correlation (scMMGAN r≈0.336 on the granulocyte pair) distinguishes geometry-preserving mappings from distribution-matching ones that are essentially uncorrelated with the truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Benchmark for judging whether cross-modal single-cell mappings (e.g., ATAC-seq to RNA-seq) preserve point-wise correspondence: after generating predictions with scMMGAN, CycleGAN, and CMAE, compute the correlation between each predicted value and the ground-truth measurement of the target modality. A high point-wise correlation (scMMGAN r≈0.336 on the granulocyte pair) distinguishes geometry-preserving mappings from distribution-matching ones that are essentially uncorrelated with the truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only unpaired modalities with no ground-truth measurements of the target modality — point-wise correlation cannot be computed without per-cell paired truth You only need distribution-level agreement between generated and true populations; MMD alone suffices and point-wise correlation would conflate alignment quality with correspondence The mapping has not yet been trained/converged — GAN training is unstable and the model can deteriorate from effective to ineffective across iterations, invalidating the comparison

skills.description: Use when fitting a latent-space model to raw scRNA-seq count matrices with per-cell time labels, so the generative likelihood matches integer counts (Poisson) rather than Gaussian assumptions on log-transformed data.
skills.name: poisson-count-likelihood-modeling
skills.search_text: poisson-count-likelihood-modeling Use when fitting a latent-space model to raw scRNA-seq count matrices with per-cell time labels, so the generative likelihood matches integer counts (Poisson) rather than Gaussian assumptions on log-transformed data. The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern The goal is a purely Gaussian latent-variable model on log-transformed data (e.g. scaling log(X+1) then t-SNE/diffusion maps) rather than count-based likelihood fitting You need immediate biological interpretation of cell clusters without additional pathway analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prototype-based Bayesian generative modeling of temporal single-cell RNA-seq counts: read counts are generated from prototype metagenes under a Poisson likelihood with Gamma priors on rates and an RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior over prototype positions, fit by variational EM as implemented in the TCM R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05112-9
skills.summary: Prototype-based Bayesian generative modeling of temporal single-cell RNA-seq counts: read counts are generated from prototype metagenes under a Poisson likelihood with Gamma priors on rates and an RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior over prototype positions, fit by variational EM as implemented in the TCM R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern The goal is a purely Gaussian latent-variable model on log-transformed data (e.g. scaling log(X+1) then t-SNE/diffusion maps) rather than count-based likelihood fitting You need immediate biological interpretation of cell clusters without additional pathway analysis

skills.description: Use when benchmarking type-I error control of scRNA-seq co-expression methods: you need null count matrices where genes are not co-expressed, in both constant-depth and depth-confounded variants.
skills.name: poisson-count-resampling-simulation
skills.search_text: poisson-count-resampling-simulation Use when benchmarking type-I error control of scRNA-seq co-expression methods: you need null count matrices where genes are not co-expressed, in both constant-depth and depth-confounded variants. The goal is estimating real co-expression from observed data rather than simulating null data — use CS-CORE/CSCORE directly on observed counts instead The null must preserve gene-gene dependence structure (e.g. for power or module-recovery simulations); permutation destroys co-expression by design Input is normalized/log-transformed expression rather than raw UMI integer counts, since the Poisson resampling model operates on raw counts and depths t_i http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates null scRNA-seq UMI count matrices with no true gene co-expression by per-cell sequencing-depth normalization, per-gene permutation of normalized expression across cells, and Poisson resampling of counts under either constant or observed (varying) sequencing depths. skills.summary: Generates null scRNA-seq UMI count matrices with no true gene co-expression by per-cell sequencing-depth normalization, per-gene permutation of normalized expression across cells, and Poisson resampling of counts under either constant or observed (varying) sequencing depths. This provides the null data needed to benchmark false-positive rates of co-expression methods such as CS-CORE.
