skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the purity/homogeneity of an scRNA-seq cell cluster by fitting a per-gene entropy model on a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix and computing a ROGUE score.
skills.name: poisson-gamma-negative-binomial-statistics
skills.search_text: poisson-gamma-negative-binomial-statistics Use when you need to quantify the purity/homogeneity of an scRNA-seq cell cluster by fitting a per-gene entropy model on a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix and computing a ROGUE score. You need to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the paper notes this is not yet supported and proposed as future work The data are low-quality or continuous such that the recommended 0.9 purity threshold does not apply without recalibrating against global ROGUE values The goal is rare cell-type detection/clustering rather than purity assessment — tools like GiniClust or RaceID3 address clustering, not entropy-based purity scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements the S–E (shifted entropy) model of the ROGUE framework: single-gene sample entropy is computed under a Poisson-Gamma/negative-binomial model (S = ln E(X) + a), a LOESS fit of ln E(X) yields per-gene entropy-reduction residuals (ds), and these aggregate into the purity statistic ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Implements the S–E (shifted entropy) model of the ROGUE framework: single-gene sample entropy is computed under a Poisson-Gamma/negative-binomial model (S = ln E(X) + a), a LOESS fit of ln E(X) yields per-gene entropy-reduction residuals (ds), and these aggregate into the purity statistic ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms — the paper notes this is not yet supported and proposed as future work The data are low-quality or continuous such that the recommended 0.9 purity threshold does not apply without recalibrating against global ROGUE values The goal is rare cell-type detection/clustering rather than purity assessment — tools like GiniClust or RaceID3 address clustering, not entropy-based purity scoring

skills.description: Use when benchmarking co-expression detection methods on simulated scRNA-seq data that must preserve real co-expression structure — e.g., generating p x n UMI count matrices from a known sparse co-expression matrix to compute precision-recall curves and wall-clock runtimes per method.
skills.name: poisson-measurement-model-simulation
skills.search_text: poisson-measurement-model-simulation Use when benchmarking co-expression detection methods on simulated scRNA-seq data that must preserve real co-expression structure — e.g., generating p x n UMI count matrices from a known sparse co-expression matrix to compute precision-recall curves and wall-clock runtimes per method. The input is observed real scRNA-seq data and the goal is co-expression inference rather than method benchmarking — run CS-CORE directly on the data instead of simulating. The count model must differ from Poisson (e.g., negative binomial) — the article explicitly defers adaptation of x_ij|z_ij to other distributions such as the negative binomial to future work. Input is normalized/transformed expression (not raw UMI counts) — the measurement model is defined on nonnegative-integer UMI counts confounded by sequencing depth and measurement error. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count data under the CS-CORE latent-variable Poisson measurement model x_ij|z_ij ~ Poisson(s_i * z_ij), using a ground-truth sparse co-expression network estimated from real data, to benchmark co-expression methods via precision-recall and running-time comparisons. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Simulates synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count data under the CS-CORE latent-variable Poisson measurement model x_ij|z_ij ~ Poisson(s_i * z_ij), using a ground-truth sparse co-expression network estimated from real data, to benchmark co-expression methods via precision-recall and running-time comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is observed real scRNA-seq data and the goal is co-expression inference rather than method benchmarking — run CS-CORE directly on the data instead of simulating. The count model must differ from Poisson (e.g., negative binomial) — the article explicitly defers adaptation of x_ij|z_ij to other distributions such as the negative binomial to future work. Input is normalized/transformed expression (not raw UMI counts) — the measurement model is defined on nonnegative-integer UMI counts confounded by sequencing depth and measurement error.

skills.description: Use when bulk HiChIP enhancer-promoter loop counts must be deconvolved into subpopulation-specific profiles using scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles from the same population, and a principled model-based alternative to the plug-in baseline is acceptable despite ~24 h runtime.
skills.name: poisson-model-hichip-deconvolution
skills.search_text: poisson-model-hichip-deconvolution Use when bulk HiChIP enhancer-promoter loop counts must be deconvolved into subpopulation-specific profiles using scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles from the same population, and a principled model-based alternative to the plug-in baseline is acceptable despite ~24 h runtime. When runtime matters (e.g. quick exploratory analysis): the Poisson MAP inference takes ~24 h versus ~3 min for the simple plug-in method, with only slightly better PCC When scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles cannot be treated as known (no reliable cluster labels / subpopulation profiles P1, P2 available) When the goal is not HiChIP deconvolution but plain coupled clustering of single cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A Poisson model-based MAP inference approach for deconvolving bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loop counts into subpopulation-specific profiles within DC3, treating single-cell expression/accessibility profiles as known and iteratively estimating latent multinomial loop-count variables. It offers better interpretation and slightly better simulation performance than the simple plug-in method, at much higher time cost (24 h vs 3 min). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: A Poisson model-based MAP inference approach for deconvolving bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loop counts into subpopulation-specific profiles within DC3, treating single-cell expression/accessibility profiles as known and iteratively estimating latent multinomial loop-count variables. It offers better interpretation and slightly better simulation performance than the simple plug-in method, at much higher time cost (24 h vs 3 min).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When runtime matters (e.g. quick exploratory analysis): the Poisson MAP inference takes ~24 h versus ~3 min for the simple plug-in method, with only slightly better PCC When scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles cannot be treated as known (no reliable cluster labels / subpopulation profiles P1, P2 available) When the goal is not HiChIP deconvolution but plain coupled clustering of single cells

skills.description: Use when you have candidate 3' end cleavage site coordinates from 3'-tag scRNA-seq (e.g., Microwell-seq) and need to label them against GENCODE 3' ends, PolyASite 2.0 clusters, and internal-priming risk.
skills.name: polya-cluster-overlap-annotation
skills.search_text: polya-cluster-overlap-annotation Use when you have candidate 3' end cleavage site coordinates from 3'-tag scRNA-seq (e.g., Microwell-seq) and need to label them against GENCODE 3' ends, PolyASite 2.0 clusters, and internal-priming risk. Input is 10x Genomics data where reads do not span the mRNA 3' end cleavage site, preventing exact de novo CS mapping and thus reliable overlap-based classification The goal is quantifying 3'UTR isoform abundance from scRNA-seq counts rather than building or extending a cleavage site annotation catalog (use scUTRquant quantification instead) Candidate sites have not yet passed quality control for internal priming — classification must not be run before the cleanUpdTSeq filtering step http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classifies candidate mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) called from Microwell-seq (MWS) data by coordinate-based overlap with GENCODE-annotated 3' ends and PolyASite 2.0 poly(A) clusters, after removing internal-priming artifacts with cleanUpdTSeq, to build the validated/supported/likely CS catalog. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Classifies candidate mRNA 3' end cleavage sites (CS) called from Microwell-seq (MWS) data by coordinate-based overlap with GENCODE-annotated 3' ends and PolyASite 2.0 poly(A) clusters, after removing internal-priming artifacts with cleanUpdTSeq, to build the validated/supported/likely CS catalog.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10x Genomics data where reads do not span the mRNA 3' end cleavage site, preventing exact de novo CS mapping and thus reliable overlap-based classification The goal is quantifying 3'UTR isoform abundance from scRNA-seq counts rather than building or extending a cleavage site annotation catalog (use scUTRquant quantification instead) Candidate sites have not yet passed quality control for internal priming — classification must not be run before the cleanUpdTSeq filtering step

skills.description: Use when you need to predict the splicing status (spliced, unspliced, or ambiguous 'A') of individual scRNA-seq reads, especially reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference and filtered to unique genome mappings.
skills.name: polya-priming-window-scoring
skills.search_text: polya-priming-window-scoring Use when you need to predict the splicing status (spliced, unspliced, or ambiguous 'A') of individual scRNA-seq reads, especially reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference and filtered to unique genome mappings. You only need gene- or transcript-level abundance quantification rather than per-read splicing status — a standard pseudoaligner/quantifier is the wrong tool. The reads are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell scRNA-seq; the binding affinity and fragment length models were trained on scRNA-seq priming behavior. No spliceu (spliced + unspliced augmented) reference or trained model pickles are available and you cannot build/train them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Score putative priming windows for oligo(dT) primers in scRNA-seq reads using Forseti's trained binding affinity MLP (mlp_pa6with1mm.pkl) together with a cubic-spline fragment length distribution model, to probabilistically assign a splicing status to reads aligned to a spliceu reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Score putative priming windows for oligo(dT) primers in scRNA-seq reads using Forseti's trained binding affinity MLP (mlp_pa6with1mm.pkl) together with a cubic-spline fragment length distribution model, to probabilistically assign a splicing status to reads aligned to a spliceu reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need gene- or transcript-level abundance quantification rather than per-read splicing status — a standard pseudoaligner/quantifier is the wrong tool. The reads are bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell scRNA-seq; the binding affinity and fragment length models were trained on scRNA-seq priming behavior. No spliceu (spliced + unspliced augmented) reference or trained model pickles are available and you cannot build/train them.

skills.description: Use when evaluating predicted polyA-site bins from an aptardi output GTF (or a StringTie/Ensembl baseline transcriptome) against curated polyA-site databases such as PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3, or PolyA-Seq tissue-specific ground truth.
skills.name: polya-site-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: polya-site-benchmark-comparison Use when evaluating predicted polyA-site bins from an aptardi output GTF (or a StringTie/Ensembl baseline transcriptome) against curated polyA-site databases such as PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3, or PolyA-Seq tissue-specific ground truth. Direct 3′-end sequencing data (e.g., PolyA-Seq) is available for the sample itself — aptardi is designed to predict sites from RNA-Seq plus DNA sequence when 3′-sequencing data are not available The analysis targets coding APA in upstream exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream events cannot be benchmarked with this skill Only a priori annotated polyA sites are needed (e.g., MISO/QAPA/PARQ workflows) — there is no de novo prediction to validate against databases http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmarks predicted polyadenylation (polyA) sites from an aptardi-modified or assembler transcriptome against ground-truth references (PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3, Derti et al. PolyA-Seq) using BEDtools interval intersections, yielding precision/recall metrics and counts of unannotated tissue-specific sites. It establishes whether a machine-learning polyA predictor meaningfully extends the 3′-end content of a StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Benchmarks predicted polyadenylation (polyA) sites from an aptardi-modified or assembler transcriptome against ground-truth references (PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3, Derti et al. PolyA-Seq) using BEDtools interval intersections, yielding precision/recall metrics and counts of unannotated tissue-specific sites. It establishes whether a machine-learning polyA predictor meaningfully extends the 3′-end content of a StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Direct 3′-end sequencing data (e.g., PolyA-Seq) is available for the sample itself — aptardi is designed to predict sites from RNA-Seq plus DNA sequence when 3′-sequencing data are not available The analysis targets coding APA in upstream exons — aptardi only evaluates 3' terminal exons, so upstream events cannot be benchmarked with this skill Only a priori annotated polyA sites are needed (e.g., MISO/QAPA/PARQ workflows) — there is no de novo prediction to validate against databases

skills.description: Use when a sequence-based polyA/IPA site predictor must be independently validated on external polyA databases (GENCODE, PolyA_DB 3, PolyASite 2.0) rather than on random splits of its own training annotations.
skills.name: polya-site-benchmark-dataset-curation
skills.search_text: polya-site-benchmark-dataset-curation Use when a sequence-based polyA/IPA site predictor must be independently validated on external polyA databases (GENCODE, PolyA_DB 3, PolyASite 2.0) rather than on random splits of its own training annotations. When the goal is read-based IPA detection from RNA-seq alignments — that is the InPACT read module's role, not sequence-module benchmarking When the predictor was trained on or exposed to sites overlapping the external test databases, since the exclusion of training-overlapping sites is essential to this skill's validity When no independent external polyA annotation is available and only a random split of the training data is possible — leakage-free cross-database evaluation cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs held-out polyA site benchmark test sets from GENCODE, PolyA_DB 3, and PolyASite 2.0 annotations (excluding sites overlapping the training data) and uses them to score a trained InPACT CNN sequence module by AUROC. This establishes an independent, non-overlapping evaluation of sequence-based polyA site prediction against external ground-truth databases. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Constructs held-out polyA site benchmark test sets from GENCODE, PolyA_DB 3, and PolyASite 2.0 annotations (excluding sites overlapping the training data) and uses them to score a trained InPACT CNN sequence module by AUROC. This establishes an independent, non-overlapping evaluation of sequence-based polyA site prediction against external ground-truth databases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is read-based IPA detection from RNA-seq alignments — that is the InPACT read module's role, not sequence-module benchmarking When the predictor was trained on or exposed to sites overlapping the external test databases, since the exclusion of training-overlapping sites is essential to this skill's validity When no independent external polyA annotation is available and only a random split of the training data is possible — leakage-free cross-database evaluation cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when comparing predicted transcript 3'-end/polyA site calls from multiple tools (e.g., aptardi vs TAPAS vs APARENT) against a PolyA-Seq gold standard and quantitative accuracy metrics are needed.
skills.name: polya-site-benchmarking-against-polyaseq-gold-standard
skills.search_text: polya-site-benchmarking-against-polyaseq-gold-standard Use when comparing predicted transcript 3'-end/polyA site calls from multiple tools (e.g., aptardi vs TAPAS vs APARENT) against a PolyA-Seq gold standard and quantitative accuracy metrics are needed. No gold-standard polyA site coordinates (e.g., PolyA-Seq) are available for the sample or species being analyzed, so accuracy cannot be scored The question is differential APA or 3' UTR usage between conditions rather than benchmarking 3'-end prediction accuracy Input transcripts fall outside the 3' terminal exon scope aptardi analyzes (upstream exons are not analyzed, so coding APA cannot be evaluated) http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark predicted transcript 3'-ends (from aptardi, TAPAS, APARENT, or an original StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome) against true PolyA-Seq sites on the HBR data set, counting correct termini (within 100 bases), PPV, and unique true-site counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Benchmark predicted transcript 3'-ends (from aptardi, TAPAS, APARENT, or an original StringTie/Ensembl transcriptome) against true PolyA-Seq sites on the HBR data set, counting correct termini (within 100 bases), PPV, and unique true-site counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No gold-standard polyA site coordinates (e.g., PolyA-Seq) are available for the sample or species being analyzed, so accuracy cannot be scored The question is differential APA or 3' UTR usage between conditions rather than benchmarking 3'-end prediction accuracy Input transcripts fall outside the 3' terminal exon scope aptardi analyzes (upstream exons are not analyzed, so coding APA cannot be evaluated)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking IPA site callers against GEO-deposited 3'-end sequencing ground truth whose polyA site coordinates were produced on an older assembly and must be converted to GRCh38 before interval matching.
skills.name: polya-site-coordinate-liftover
skills.search_text: polya-site-coordinate-liftover Use when benchmarking IPA site callers against GEO-deposited 3'-end sequencing ground truth whose polyA site coordinates were produced on an older assembly and must be converted to GRCh38 before interval matching. Ground-truth polyA site coordinates are already in GRCh38 coordinates — liftOver is unnecessary and could shift valid sites The comparison target is Iso-seq polyA sites, which are extracted directly from the isoform annotation rather than lifted Benchmarking quantification accuracy (e.g., |ΔPAU| on Polyester-simulated data) rather than site-coordinate accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Lifts polyadenylation site coordinates from ground-truth resources (A-seq, 3P-seq, polyA-seq) to the GRCh38 assembly with liftOver so that IPA tool predictions can be benchmarked on a consistent reference genome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Lifts polyadenylation site coordinates from ground-truth resources (A-seq, 3P-seq, polyA-seq) to the GRCh38 assembly with liftOver so that IPA tool predictions can be benchmarked on a consistent reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth polyA site coordinates are already in GRCh38 coordinates — liftOver is unnecessary and could shift valid sites The comparison target is Iso-seq polyA sites, which are extracted directly from the isoform annotation rather than lifted Benchmarking quantification accuracy (e.g., |ΔPAU| on Polyester-simulated data) rather than site-coordinate accuracy

skills.description: Use when you need simulated paired-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with known ground-truth splicing status—especially reads that are ambiguous ('A', compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts)—to evaluate a splicing-status or read-origin prediction model.
skills.name: polya-site-fragment-read-simulation
skills.search_text: polya-site-fragment-read-simulation Use when you need simulated paired-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with known ground-truth splicing status—especially reads that are ambiguous ('A', compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts)—to evaluate a splicing-status or read-origin prediction model. When the goal is real-data quantification of spliced/unspliced/ambiguous counts from experimental FASTQs rather than ground-truth-labeled simulated reads When the downstream predictor is not evaluated against known splicing-status labels—simulation ground truth provides no benefit there When only a single-end or non-polyA-primed protocol is used, since the uniform polyA-site and fragment-length sampling assumptions would not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simulate paired-end scRNA-seq read sets from a spliceu (spliced + unspliced) augmented reference by uniformly sampling polyA priming sites, drawing fragment lengths from an empirical fragment length distribution, and adding Illumina sequencing errors, once with and once without the fundamental-ambiguity-permitting step, to benchmark splicing-status predictors like Forseti. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Simulate paired-end scRNA-seq read sets from a spliceu (spliced + unspliced) augmented reference by uniformly sampling polyA priming sites, drawing fragment lengths from an empirical fragment length distribution, and adding Illumina sequencing errors, once with and once without the fundamental-ambiguity-permitting step, to benchmark splicing-status predictors like Forseti.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is real-data quantification of spliced/unspliced/ambiguous counts from experimental FASTQs rather than ground-truth-labeled simulated reads When the downstream predictor is not evaluated against known splicing-status labels—simulation ground truth provides no benefit there When only a single-end or non-polyA-primed protocol is used, since the uniform polyA-site and fragment-length sampling assumptions would not apply

skills.description: Use when you have a PACdataset of poly(A) sites with per-cell or per-sample counts plus BAM alignments and genome annotation, and need to visually inspect proximal vs distal pA usage for a specific gene.
skills.name: polya-site-genome-track-visualization
skills.search_text: polya-site-genome-track-visualization Use when you have a PACdataset of poly(A) sites with per-cell or per-sample counts plus BAM alignments and genome annotation, and need to visually inspect proximal vs distal pA usage for a specific gene. You need quantitative differential APA statistics (e.g., RUD scores or APA markers) rather than a visual coverage/usage inspection — use vizStats or vizAPAmarkers instead Your poly(A) sites have not yet been identified or converted into a PACdataset (e.g., raw Sierra or scAPAtrap output still needs readPACds conversion) No genome annotation is available, since the gene model track requires an annoHub built from TxDb or GTF http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates a genome-browser-like multi-track plot (gene model, poly(A) sites, single-cell counts, BAM read coverage) for a gene of interest using the vizAPA vizTracks module on R/ggbio, to visually inspect poly(A) site usage across cell types or samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae099
skills.summary: Generates a genome-browser-like multi-track plot (gene model, poly(A) sites, single-cell counts, BAM read coverage) for a gene of interest using the vizAPA vizTracks module on R/ggbio, to visually inspect poly(A) site usage across cell types or samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need quantitative differential APA statistics (e.g., RUD scores or APA markers) rather than a visual coverage/usage inspection — use vizStats or vizAPAmarkers instead Your poly(A) sites have not yet been identified or converted into a PACdataset (e.g., raw Sierra or scAPAtrap output still needs readPACds conversion) No genome annotation is available, since the gene model track requires an annoHub built from TxDb or GTF

skills.description: Use when raw spatially barcoded ST FASTQ reads (barcodes/UMIs in read 1) must be turned into a poly(A) site-by-spot matrix and per-spot APA usage ratios (RUD) before imputation or layer-level APA analysis.
skills.name: polya-site-quantification-in-spatial-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: polya-site-quantification-in-spatial-transcriptomics Use when raw spatially barcoded ST FASTQ reads (barcodes/UMIs in read 1) must be turned into a poly(A) site-by-spot matrix and per-spot APA usage ratios (RUD) before imputation or layer-level APA analysis. The spatial assay is image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) rather than spatially barcoded ST — the paper notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra. A poly(A) site matrix (PACdataset) already exists — skip to imputation (imputeAPAIndex) and spatial clustering instead of re-running site identification. The goal is DEAPA/LSAPA/SVAPA gene calling from an already-imputed RUD matrix — use findContrastAPA/findAllMarkers/findSVAPA rather than raw site quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A preprocessing-and-quantification skill that converts raw spatially barcoded ST reads (e.g., MOB ST data, SRA SRR3382373) into a poly(A) site-by-spot count matrix via scAPAtrap, then computes per-spot APA usage ratios (RUD) with stAPAminer's computeAPAIndex. It is the entry point of the stAPAminer pipeline before KNN imputation and spatial APA gene detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: A preprocessing-and-quantification skill that converts raw spatially barcoded ST reads (e.g., MOB ST data, SRA SRR3382373) into a poly(A) site-by-spot count matrix via scAPAtrap, then computes per-spot APA usage ratios (RUD) with stAPAminer's computeAPAIndex. It is the entry point of the stAPAminer pipeline before KNN imputation and spatial APA gene detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial assay is image-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) rather than spatially barcoded ST — the paper notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra. A poly(A) site matrix (PACdataset) already exists — skip to imputation (imputeAPAIndex) and spatial clustering instead of re-running site identification. The goal is DEAPA/LSAPA/SVAPA gene calling from an already-imputed RUD matrix — use findContrastAPA/findAllMarkers/findSVAPA rather than raw site quantification.

skills.description: Use when a PACdataset contains multiple poly(A) sites per gene (3'UTR APA) and per-gene/per-cell RUD scores are needed to quantify 3'UTR shortening or lengthening across cells or cell types.
skills.name: polya-site-rud-index-computation
skills.search_text: polya-site-rud-index-computation Use when a PACdataset contains multiple poly(A) sites per gene (3'UTR APA) and per-gene/per-cell RUD scores are needed to quantify 3'UTR shortening or lengthening across cells or cell types. The PACdataset contains genes with only a single poly(A) site — RUD requires at least a proximal–distal pA pair, so get3UTRAPAds/get3UTRAPApd must exclude them first. The goal is genome-browser-style visualization of raw poly(A) site usage per site (vizTracks/vizStats) rather than a gene-level shortening index. The pA sites are not annotated to 3'UTR features (e.g., intronic or intergenic pAs without prior annotatePAC/ext3UTRPACds). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-gene, per-cell Relative Usage of Distal poly(A) site (RUD) indices from a PACdataset of poly(A) site counts, quantifying 3'UTR shortening/lengthening at single-cell resolution. This is the core quantitative step in vizAPA for turning proximal–distal site usage ratios into a cell-level APA score overlayable on UMAP embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae099
skills.summary: Compute per-gene, per-cell Relative Usage of Distal poly(A) site (RUD) indices from a PACdataset of poly(A) site counts, quantifying 3'UTR shortening/lengthening at single-cell resolution. This is the core quantitative step in vizAPA for turning proximal–distal site usage ratios into a cell-level APA score overlayable on UMAP embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The PACdataset contains genes with only a single poly(A) site — RUD requires at least a proximal–distal pA pair, so get3UTRAPAds/get3UTRAPApd must exclude them first. The goal is genome-browser-style visualization of raw poly(A) site usage per site (vizTracks/vizStats) rather than a gene-level shortening index. The pA sites are not annotated to 3'UTR features (e.g., intronic or intergenic pAs without prior annotatePAC/ext3UTRPACds).

skills.description: Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) reads are annotated with polyA sites against a reference such as the polyasite.unibas.ch atlas or FANTOM CAGE peaks (mm10), and the goal is to find genes whose 3' end site choice differs between biological groups.
skills.name: polya-site-usage-analysis
skills.search_text: polya-site-usage-analysis Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) reads are annotated with polyA sites against a reference such as the polyasite.unibas.ch atlas or FANTOM CAGE peaks (mm10), and the goal is to find genes whose 3' end site choice differs between biological groups. Input is a bulk short-read RNA-seq quantification without full-length read polyA-site annotation — the chi-square framework needs per-read 3' end assignments against a polyA-site atlas The goal is cell-type-resolved hierarchical DIE testing (is.hier = TRUE tree traversal) rather than a pairwise bulk-condition polyA comparison Genes with fewer than minNumReads = 25 reads per condition — the chi-square test is underpowered and these genes are filtered out http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies per-gene polyadenylation (polyA) site usage from long-read ScISOrSeq data and tests for differential polyA-site usage between conditions (e.g., hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex) using gene-wise n x 2 chi-square tests with FDR and delta-PI thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Quantifies per-gene polyadenylation (polyA) site usage from long-read ScISOrSeq data and tests for differential polyA-site usage between conditions (e.g., hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex) using gene-wise n x 2 chi-square tests with FDR and delta-PI thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a bulk short-read RNA-seq quantification without full-length read polyA-site annotation — the chi-square framework needs per-read 3' end assignments against a polyA-site atlas The goal is cell-type-resolved hierarchical DIE testing (is.hier = TRUE tree traversal) rather than a pairwise bulk-condition polyA comparison Genes with fewer than minNumReads = 25 reads per condition — the chi-square test is underpowered and these genes are filtered out

skills.description: Use when a strand-split BAM of aligned reads must be interrogated for reads with soft-clipped polyA/polyT tails to build truncation-point tallies that localize precise 3' UTR end bases.
skills.name: polya-tail-motif-screening
skills.search_text: polya-tail-motif-screening Use when a strand-split BAM of aligned reads must be interrogated for reads with soft-clipped polyA/polyT tails to build truncation-point tallies that localize precise 3' UTR end bases. The BAM contains long-read or full-length transcript alignments without soft-clipping — polyA tails will be embedded in aligned sequence rather than clipped, so the truncation-point signal will be absent or misleading You only need broad regions of UTR enrichment — MACS peak calling on the BAM is the upstream step for that, and this skill addresses the finer end-base localization stage The library chemistry does not enrich signal at transcript distal ends (not a 10x Chromium-like run), so soft-clipped polyA reads are too sparse to form piled-up truncation points http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Screens aligned sequencing reads in a BAM file for soft-clipped bases carrying a polyA-tail (or reverse-strand polyT stretch) of a configured minimum length, tallying each qualifying read's final aligned end base as a 'truncation point' for downstream 3' UTR end determination, as implemented in the SPAT stage of peaks2utr. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Screens aligned sequencing reads in a BAM file for soft-clipped bases carrying a polyA-tail (or reverse-strand polyT stretch) of a configured minimum length, tallying each qualifying read's final aligned end base as a 'truncation point' for downstream 3' UTR end determination, as implemented in the SPAT stage of peaks2utr.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM contains long-read or full-length transcript alignments without soft-clipping — polyA tails will be embedded in aligned sequence rather than clipped, so the truncation-point signal will be absent or misleading You only need broad regions of UTR enrichment — MACS peak calling on the BAM is the upstream step for that, and this skill addresses the finer end-base localization stage The library chemistry does not enrich signal at transcript distal ends (not a 10x Chromium-like run), so soft-clipped polyA reads are too sparse to form piled-up truncation points

skills.name: polyadenylation-site-prediction
skills.search_text: polyadenylation-site-prediction Use when a sample-specific transcriptome (e.g. StringTie GTF) needs accurate 3'-end/polyA site annotation from genome-aligned RNA-Seq plus genome FASTA, and downstream APA or quantitation analyses require refined transcript termini. When the goal is detecting coding APA within upstream exons — aptardi evaluates only the 3' terminal exons of input transcripts and does not analyze upstream exons or intron junctions. When input transcriptomes require de novo transcript structure discovery from RNA-Seq alone — aptardi requires an initial transcriptome (GTF/GFF) and refines 3'-ends rather than assembling transcripts. When only DNA sequence is available — aptardi requires both sample RNA-Seq coverage and DNA sequence; DNA-sequence-only predictors cannot capture sample-specific expression. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Predict sample-specific polyadenylation (polyA) sites by combining RNA-Seq coverage with DNA sequence features using aptardi, a supervised machine-learning tool that refines transcript 3'-ends into a modified GTF transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Predict sample-specific polyadenylation (polyA) sites by combining RNA-Seq coverage with DNA sequence features using aptardi, a supervised machine-learning tool that refines transcript 3'-ends into a modified GTF transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is detecting coding APA within upstream exons — aptardi evaluates only the 3' terminal exons of input transcripts and does not analyze upstream exons or intron junctions. When input transcriptomes require de novo transcript structure discovery from RNA-Seq alone — aptardi requires an initial transcriptome (GTF/GFF) and refines 3'-ends rather than assembling transcripts. When only DNA sequence is available — aptardi requires both sample RNA-Seq coverage and DNA sequence; DNA-sequence-only predictors cannot capture sample-specific expression.

skills.name: polygenic-score-model-fitting
skills.search_text: polygenic-score-model-fitting Use when TWAS Stage I eQTL weights must be trained from summary-level eQTL summary statistics (with CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N columns) because individual-level genotype-expression reference data are unavailable or too small (e.g., GTEx V6 n=338 vs eQTLGen n=31,684). The goal involves trans-eQTL effects or cross-population TWAS — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects and available summary-level eQTL references are mainly European, limiting transferability Individual-level reference genotype-expression data of adequate size already exist for the tissue, making direct individual-level training (e.g., FUSION-style) applicable instead No ancestry-matched LD reference panel is available for the eQTL summary statistics (PRS-CS requires the reference panel to match the GWAS/eQTL sample ancestry, not the target sample) http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train GReX/TWAS Stage I eQTL imputation weights from summary-level eQTL statistics (e.g., eQTLGen whole blood, n=31,684) by repurposing polygenic risk score methods — P+T with LD clumping, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS — inside the OTTERS framework, avoiding dependence on small individual-level expression references. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Train GReX/TWAS Stage I eQTL imputation weights from summary-level eQTL statistics (e.g., eQTLGen whole blood, n=31,684) by repurposing polygenic risk score methods — P+T with LD clumping, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS — inside the OTTERS framework, avoiding dependence on small individual-level expression references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal involves trans-eQTL effects or cross-population TWAS — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects and available summary-level eQTL references are mainly European, limiting transferability Individual-level reference genotype-expression data of adequate size already exist for the tissue, making direct individual-level training (e.g., FUSION-style) applicable instead No ancestry-matched LD reference panel is available for the eQTL summary statistics (PRS-CS requires the reference panel to match the GWAS/eQTL sample ancestry, not the target sample)

skills.search_text: polygenic-score-thresholding-with-ld-clumping Use when only summary-level eQTL reference data (e.g., eQTLGen-style p-values + beta coefficients per gene) are available and individual-level genotype/expression cannot be used to fit GReX imputation weights. skills.name: polyphen2-functional-impact-binning
skills.search_text: polyphen2-functional-impact-binning Use when building mutation-type feature matrices from COSMIC somatic mutation data where missense variants must be stratified by predicted functional impact (HiFI/MiFI/LoFI) before computing per-gene ratio-metric, entropy and frequency features for driver-gene classification. The input is already a processed feature table (e.g. the released FeatureMat.tsv from RamanLab/IdentifyTSGOG) — binning is only needed when regenerating features from raw mutation records Working with datasets that lack the fields needed to compute missense entropy/frequency features (as happened with the Tokheim et al. comparison data) The analysis requires background-mutation-rate-based driver detection rather than mutation-type-profile features (the cTaG feature approach is explicitly not a MutSigCV-style mutation-rate method) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Stratifies missense mutations from COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data into predicted functional-impact classes (HiFI/MiFI/LoFI) using PolyPhen2-based scores. These binned classes feed the cTaG 37-feature per-gene/transcript matrix (ratio-metric plus entropy and frequency features) used to classify tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) and oncogenes (OGs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Stratifies missense mutations from COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data into predicted functional-impact classes (HiFI/MiFI/LoFI) using PolyPhen2-based scores. These binned classes feed the cTaG 37-feature per-gene/transcript matrix (ratio-metric plus entropy and frequency features) used to classify tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) and oncogenes (OGs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table (e.g. the released FeatureMat.tsv from RamanLab/IdentifyTSGOG) — binning is only needed when regenerating features from raw mutation records Working with datasets that lack the fields needed to compute missense entropy/frequency features (as happened with the Tokheim et al. comparison data) The analysis requires background-mutation-rate-based driver detection rather than mutation-type-profile features (the cTaG feature approach is explicitly not a MutSigCV-style mutation-rate method)

skills.description: Use when predicting miRNA activity from scRNA-seq data where single-cell profiles are too sparse for a pretrained bulk-trained model, and you want to contrast pooled-cluster predictions with per-cell predictions.
skills.name: pooled-versus-single-cell-prediction-strategy
skills.search_text: pooled-versus-single-cell-prediction-strategy Use when predicting miRNA activity from scRNA-seq data where single-cell profiles are too sparse for a pretrained bulk-trained model, and you want to contrast pooled-cluster predictions with per-cell predictions. The input is already bulk (non-sparse) RNA-seq data — pooling is unnecessary; apply the miRSCAPE model directly in bulk mode The application sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the model's training cohort, where the article expects 'a more substantive loss in performance' — retraining on detected genes may be needed instead The analysis goal is miRNA target activity from putative-target lists alone without a trained model — use the target-only control approach (e.g. miReact) rather than pooled miRSCAPE http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 A two-mode miRNA-inference strategy from the miRSCAPE paper: pool cells within a scRNA-seq cluster to obtain a non-sparse transcriptomic profile before applying pretrained miRSCAPE models, and separately apply the same models per single cell, then compare induced-vs-uninduced log-fold changes against a target-only control (miReact). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: A two-mode miRNA-inference strategy from the miRSCAPE paper: pool cells within a scRNA-seq cluster to obtain a non-sparse transcriptomic profile before applying pretrained miRSCAPE models, and separately apply the same models per single cell, then compare induced-vs-uninduced log-fold changes against a target-only control (miReact).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already bulk (non-sparse) RNA-seq data — pooling is unnecessary; apply the miRSCAPE model directly in bulk mode The application sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the model's training cohort, where the article expects 'a more substantive loss in performance' — retraining on detected genes may be needed instead The analysis goal is miRNA target activity from putative-target lists alone without a trained model — use the target-only control approach (e.g. miReact) rather than pooled miRSCAPE

Input is raw FASTQ or an unnormalized barcode counts table — normalize counts first (upstream BARtab/bartools steps) The goal is lineage reconstruction from single-cell expressed barcodes (use lineage reconstruction tools such as Cassiopeia or LinRace, not population-level PCA) Samples have no replicate or treatment structure, so PCA separation cannot be interpreted against a biological grouping http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Principal component analysis (prcomp) on log-normalized population-level barcode counts tables to assess whether clonal composition separates samples by treatment, time course, or condition, as demonstrated for DMSO, IBET-151, and AraC in the bartools dose-escalation workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or an unnormalized barcode counts table — normalize counts first (upstream BARtab/bartools steps) The goal is lineage reconstruction from single-cell expressed barcodes (use lineage reconstruction tools such as Cassiopeia or LinRace, not population-level PCA) Samples have no replicate or treatment structure, so PCA separation cannot be interpreted against a biological grouping

skills.description: Use when a PAIRADISE results table of significant ASAS events (FDR <= 10%) must be tested for LD-based enrichment against GWAS catalog SNPs and quantified per dataset (e.g., GM12878, Geuvadis CEU/FIN/GBR/TSI/YRI).
skills.name: population-genetic-allele-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: population-genetic-allele-frequency-analysis Use when a PAIRADISE results table of significant ASAS events (FDR <= 10%) must be tested for LD-based enrichment against GWAS catalog SNPs and quantified per dataset (e.g., GM12878, Geuvadis CEU/FIN/GBR/TSI/YRI). You need the causal splicing variant itself: PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs — 'the causal SNPs could be located within the alternative exons or nearby intronic regions and are not tested by PAIRADISE' The ASAS event lacks a heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon on the same RNA-seq read; such events cannot be detected and thus cannot enter the LD overlap analysis You want direct positional overlap rather than LD-proxy overlap; r2 > 0.8 linking via 1000 Genomes phase 3 is intrinsic to this enrichment design http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether significant ASAS SNPs identified by PAIRADISE are enriched for linkage disequilibrium (r2 > 0.8) with GWAS-catalog trait/disease-associated SNPs relative to a random ±1,000 bp control null, and tallies the number of ASAS events linked to GWAS SNPs per population dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Tests whether significant ASAS SNPs identified by PAIRADISE are enriched for linkage disequilibrium (r2 > 0.8) with GWAS-catalog trait/disease-associated SNPs relative to a random ±1,000 bp control null, and tallies the number of ASAS events linked to GWAS SNPs per population dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the causal splicing variant itself: PAIRADISE only tests tagging SNPs — 'the causal SNPs could be located within the alternative exons or nearby intronic regions and are not tested by PAIRADISE' The ASAS event lacks a heterozygous SNP outside the alternative exon on the same RNA-seq read; such events cannot be detected and thus cannot enter the LD overlap analysis You want direct positional overlap rather than LD-proxy overlap; r2 > 0.8 linking via 1000 Genomes phase 3 is intrinsic to this enrichment design

skills.description: Use when you have a raw barcode counts matrix (e.g. from BARtab output on SPLINTR/GEO data) and need to remove low-quality samples and low-abundance barcodes before downstream barcoding analysis.
skills.name: population-level-barcode-count-table-filtering
skills.search_text: population-level-barcode-count-table-filtering Use when you have a raw barcode counts matrix (e.g. from BARtab output on SPLINTR/GEO data) and need to remove low-quality samples and low-abundance barcodes before downstream barcoding analysis. Input is still raw FASTQ or per-read barcode extractions rather than a tabulated counts matrix — run the BARtab pipeline first The analysis is single-cell or spatial barcode data, where per-cell UMI-based filters (e.g. umi_count_filter, umi_fraction_filter) rather than bulk per-sample thresholds apply A stricter barcode filter stringency is required by the study design — the <10 reads in <4 samples rule is explicitly low-stringency http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters a population-level cellular barcoding counts table (barcodes x samples) with bartools-style QC: a sample-level read-count outlier removal (5th-percentile total reads) followed by a per-barcode low-abundance filter, as demonstrated on the SPLINTR dose-escalation dataset from GSE246611 to yield 1,680 high-confidence barcodes across 41 samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Filters a population-level cellular barcoding counts table (barcodes x samples) with bartools-style QC: a sample-level read-count outlier removal (5th-percentile total reads) followed by a per-barcode low-abundance filter, as demonstrated on the SPLINTR dose-escalation dataset from GSE246611 to yield 1,680 high-confidence barcodes across 41 samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ or per-read barcode extractions rather than a tabulated counts matrix — run the BARtab pipeline first The analysis is single-cell or spatial barcode data, where per-cell UMI-based filters (e.g. umi_count_filter, umi_fraction_filter) rather than bulk per-sample thresholds apply A stricter barcode filter stringency is required by the study design — the <10 reads in <4 samples rule is explicitly low-stringency

skills.search_text: position-specific-gapped-kmer-descriptor-grouping Use when a combined feature table mixes several descriptor families (e.g., position-specific gapped k-mer and position-specific k-mer modes plus GC-content) and you need per-group Random Forest feature selection rather than ranking all features jointly. skills.name: position-specific-gapped-kmer-feature-ablation
skills.search_text: position-specific-gapped-kmer-feature-ablation Use when benchmarking which subsets of position-specific (gapped) k-mer feature blocks contribute to classifier performance on 41-nt RNA sequences, e.g. reproducing a Table 3-style ablation with Accuracy/Precision/Sensitivity/Specificity/F1/MCC. Input is already a reduced/selected feature table from a different feature family (e.g. k-mer frequency features from a prior study) rather than position-specific blocks generated from raw 41-nt sequences The goal is benchmarking against an external predictor (e.g. iRNA5hmC) or evaluating on the independent test set, rather than internal feature-mode ablation Sequences are not 41 nt — the position-specific matching against consecutive-residue-groups and the webserver protocol assume 41-nt RNA sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduces the iRNA5hmC-PS feature ablation: evaluating all 15 non-empty combinations of the four position-specific feature modes (A = Ps-k-mer, B = PsM(G)D, C = PsD(G)M, D = PsM(G)M(G)M) plus GC-content under 10-times 5-fold cross-validation with default scikit-learn Logistic Regression, after group-wise feature-importance selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: Reproduces the iRNA5hmC-PS feature ablation: evaluating all 15 non-empty combinations of the four position-specific feature modes (A = Ps-k-mer, B = PsM(G)D, C = PsD(G)M, D = PsM(G)M(G)M) plus GC-content under 10-times 5-fold cross-validation with default scikit-learn Logistic Regression, after group-wise feature-importance selection.
