skills.description: Use when building machine-learning inputs for m5C site prediction from labeled 41-nt RNA sequence segments (e.g., A. thaliana or M. musculus benchmarks) and you need positional, compositional, and physicochemical feature encodings fused into one matrix.
skills.name: position-specific-propensity-sequence-encoding
skills.search_text: position-specific-propensity-sequence-encoding Use when building machine-learning inputs for m5C site prediction from labeled 41-nt RNA sequence segments (e.g., A. thaliana or M. musculus benchmarks) and you need positional, compositional, and physicochemical feature encodings fused into one matrix. Input sequences are not 41-bp segments centered on a candidate m5C site, or come from a species other than Arabidopsis or Mouse — the article notes it is necessary to set up species-specific models Input is already a numeric feature table; this skill operates on raw nucleotide sequences Only sequence-motif visualization is needed (Two Sample Logo analysis) rather than quantitative feature encoding for classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Encodes 41-bp RNA segments centered on candidate m5C sites using position-specific propensity (PSP) together with k-mer (k=1,2,3), PCPseDNC, and PseEIIP encodings, then fuses them into a single input matrix for the Staem5 stacked-ensemble m5C predictor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Encodes 41-bp RNA segments centered on candidate m5C sites using position-specific propensity (PSP) together with k-mer (k=1,2,3), PCPseDNC, and PseEIIP encodings, then fuses them into a single input matrix for the Staem5 stacked-ensemble m5C predictor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are not 41-bp segments centered on a candidate m5C site, or come from a species other than Arabidopsis or Mouse — the article notes it is necessary to set up species-specific models Input is already a numeric feature table; this skill operates on raw nucleotide sequences Only sequence-motif visualization is needed (Two Sample Logo analysis) rather than quantitative feature encoding for classification

skills.description: Use when scoring nucleotide sequences against a PWM for motif detection and the scoring must be normalized to the GC fraction of the user-supplied sequence to avoid GC-bias in motif hits.
skills.name: position-weight-matrix-log-odds-scoring
skills.search_text: position-weight-matrix-log-odds-scoring Use when scoring nucleotide sequences against a PWM for motif detection and the scoring must be normalized to the GC fraction of the user-supplied sequence to avoid GC-bias in motif hits. When searching for arbitrary user-defined motifs that are not represented in the ElemeNT 2023 PWM table — although ElemeNT 2023 can search any user-defined motif, the GC-normalized log-odds scoring described here is grounded in its PWM-based motif search. When a background model other than a simple GC-fraction model is required (e.g. Markov-order-1 backgrounds), since this skill's normalization uses only P(G)=P(C)=GC/2 and P(A)=P(T)=(1-GC)/2. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Computes GC-content-normalized log2 log-odds scores from a PWM by dividing each position-nucleotide probability by a GC-dependent background model (P(G)=P(C)=GC/2, P(A)=P(T)=(1-GC)/2), as implemented in ElemeNT 2023 for core promoter element detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae110
skills.summary: Computes GC-content-normalized log2 log-odds scores from a PWM by dividing each position-nucleotide probability by a GC-dependent background model (P(G)=P(C)=GC/2, P(A)=P(T)=(1-GC)/2), as implemented in ElemeNT 2023 for core promoter element detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When searching for arbitrary user-defined motifs that are not represented in the ElemeNT 2023 PWM table — although ElemeNT 2023 can search any user-defined motif, the GC-normalized log-odds scoring described here is grounded in its PWM-based motif search. When a background model other than a simple GC-fraction model is required (e.g. Markov-order-1 backgrounds), since this skill's normalization uses only P(G)=P(C)=GC/2 and P(A)=P(T)=(1-GC)/2.

skills.description: Use when clusters of closely related cell subtypes (e.g. naive vs effector T cells, immature B vs plasma cells) collapse to near-equal scores under positive-only markers, and negative marker evidence is needed to resolve them.
skills.name: positive-negative-marker-scoring
skills.search_text: positive-negative-marker-scoring Use when clusters of closely related cell subtypes (e.g. naive vs effector T cells, immature B vs plasma cells) collapse to near-equal scores under positive-only markers, and negative marker evidence is needed to resolve them. When cell types of interest differ by well-separated positive markers alone and no negative markers are available — ScType's annotation depends on marker specificity across both clusters and cell types, and negative markers are still relatively few compared to positive markers When input is not raw scRNA-seq data but an already annotated or reference-labeled dataset — supervised methods like CaSTLe or ACTINN that train on labeled references are the appropriate choice When the marker database lacks entries for the tissue of interest (tissues with fewer than 5 cell types were excluded from the ScType database) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute ScType cell-type scores by combining positive and negative marker gene sets, where negative markers (genes providing evidence against a cell type) suppress incorrect assignments. This is the core scoring mechanism that lets ScType distinguish closely related subtypes, e.g. naive vs effector T cells separated by CCR7/SELL as negative markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28803-w
skills.summary: Compute ScType cell-type scores by combining positive and negative marker gene sets, where negative markers (genes providing evidence against a cell type) suppress incorrect assignments. This is the core scoring mechanism that lets ScType distinguish closely related subtypes, e.g. naive vs effector T cells separated by CCR7/SELL as negative markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell types of interest differ by well-separated positive markers alone and no negative markers are available — ScType's annotation depends on marker specificity across both clusters and cell types, and negative markers are still relatively few compared to positive markers When input is not raw scRNA-seq data but an already annotated or reference-labeled dataset — supervised methods like CaSTLe or ACTINN that train on labeled references are the appropriate choice When the marker database lacks entries for the tissue of interest (tissues with fewer than 5 cell types were excluded from the ScType database)

skills.description: Use when building benchmark datasets for a tissue- or species-specific site-prediction model and you need equal positive and negative sequence counts in both training and testing partitions to avoid class-imbalance bias.
skills.name: positive-negative-sample-balancing
skills.search_text: positive-negative-sample-balancing Use when building benchmark datasets for a tissue- or species-specific site-prediction model and you need equal positive and negative sequence counts in both training and testing partitions to avoid class-imbalance bias. Your task allows class imbalance and you plan to use weighted loss or resampling during model training instead — this skill hard-balances at dataset construction time. The input sequences have not yet been deduplicated; balancing should follow CD-HIT filtering at <80% similarity, not precede it. You are working outside the m6A tissue-prediction setting (e.g., whole-transcript classification) where segment-centered 41-nt positive/negative labeling does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Construct class-balanced RNA benchmark datasets by pairing each positive (m6A-containing) 41-nt segment with an equal count of negative (m6A-free) segments, then splitting into training and testing sets with matched positive/negative counts per tissue. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Construct class-balanced RNA benchmark datasets by pairing each positive (m6A-containing) 41-nt segment with an equal count of negative (m6A-free) segments, then splitting into training and testing sets with matched positive/negative counts per tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your task allows class imbalance and you plan to use weighted loss or resampling during model training instead — this skill hard-balances at dataset construction time. The input sequences have not yet been deduplicated; balancing should follow CD-HIT filtering at <80% similarity, not precede it. You are working outside the m6A tissue-prediction setting (e.g., whole-transcript classification) where segment-centered 41-nt positive/negative labeling does not apply.

skills.description: Use when you have two balanced sets of centered, fixed-length nucleotide fragments (e.g., 5,298 vs 5,298 A. thaliana; 4,563 vs 4,563 M. musculus) and need to test whether the positive class shows position-specific residue enrichment or motifs relative to the negative class.
skills.name: positive-negative-set-contrast-analysis
skills.search_text: positive-negative-set-contrast-analysis Use when you have two balanced sets of centered, fixed-length nucleotide fragments (e.g., 5,298 vs 5,298 A. thaliana; 4,563 vs 4,563 M. musculus) and need to test whether the positive class shows position-specific residue enrichment or motifs relative to the negative class. You need a predictive model of m5C sites rather than a descriptive motif contrast (use the Staem5 stacked-ensemble predictor instead) Positive and negative fragment sets are not balanced or fragments are not aligned to a common centered reference position, so per-position contrasts are confounded The analysis goal is feature-based classification performance (e.g., F-score feature selection, SVM/XGBoost evaluation), not visual nucleotide preference inspection http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Contrasts nucleotide preferences between balanced positive (m5C-containing) and negative (non-m5C) 41-bp RNA fragments using the Two Sample Logo approach, rendering per-position two-sample sequence logos to reveal whether m5C sites carry distinctive flanking motifs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Contrasts nucleotide preferences between balanced positive (m5C-containing) and negative (non-m5C) 41-bp RNA fragments using the Two Sample Logo approach, rendering per-position two-sample sequence logos to reveal whether m5C sites carry distinctive flanking motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a predictive model of m5C sites rather than a descriptive motif contrast (use the Staem5 stacked-ensemble predictor instead) Positive and negative fragment sets are not balanced or fragments are not aligned to a common centered reference position, so per-position contrasts are confounded The analysis goal is feature-based classification performance (e.g., F-score feature selection, SVM/XGBoost evaluation), not visual nucleotide preference inspection

skills.description: Use when you have a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq and need to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets, including recovering genuine cells with total counts below a fixed cutoff.
skills.name: positive-unlabeled-learning-classification
skills.search_text: positive-unlabeled-learning-classification Use when you have a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq and need to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets, including recovering genuine cells with total counts below a fixed cutoff. When cell-containing droplets with very low total counts may be abundant and the assumption that low-count barcodes are cell-free does not hold without manually adjusting the T threshold When the goal is to correct ambient RNA contamination in gene expression estimates — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected expression profiles; use a tool such as SoupX instead When the input is already a filtered cell-by-gene matrix or a feature table, since EmptyNN requires the raw unfiltered droplet matrix to construct sets P and U http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Train a neural network with positive-unlabeled (PU) learning to classify droplets as cell-free or cell-containing from a raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrix, using confidently cell-free barcodes (set P) as positives for the negative class and the ambiguous remainder (set U) as unlabeled data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Train a neural network with positive-unlabeled (PU) learning to classify droplets as cell-free or cell-containing from a raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrix, using confidently cell-free barcodes (set P) as positives for the negative class and the ambiguous remainder (set U) as unlabeled data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell-containing droplets with very low total counts may be abundant and the assumption that low-count barcodes are cell-free does not hold without manually adjusting the T threshold When the goal is to correct ambient RNA contamination in gene expression estimates — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected expression profiles; use a tool such as SoupX instead When the input is already a filtered cell-by-gene matrix or a feature table, since EmptyNN requires the raw unfiltered droplet matrix to construct sets P and U

skills.description: Use when given a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq and you need to classify barcodes as cell-free vs cell-containing, or recover cell-containing droplets below common count cutoffs.
skills.name: positive-unlabeled-neural-network-cell-calling
skills.search_text: positive-unlabeled-neural-network-cell-calling Use when given a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq and you need to classify barcodes as cell-free vs cell-containing, or recover cell-containing droplets below common count cutoffs. The input is already a filtered cell-by-gene matrix or a processed Seurat/AnnData object — EmptyNN requires the raw unfiltered count matrix including empty droplets The goal is correcting ambient RNA contamination in retained cells' expression profiles — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression; use SoupX downstream The dataset contains many genuine cell-containing droplets with very low total counts near T — the low-count-means-cell-free assumption may mislabel them and T must be manually adjusted http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Cell-calling skill based on EmptyNN, which trains a neural network with positive-unlabeled (PU) learning to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets in raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrices, removing empty droplets while recovering low-count cells lost by threshold-based methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Cell-calling skill based on EmptyNN, which trains a neural network with positive-unlabeled (PU) learning to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets in raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrices, removing empty droplets while recovering low-count cells lost by threshold-based methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered cell-by-gene matrix or a processed Seurat/AnnData object — EmptyNN requires the raw unfiltered count matrix including empty droplets The goal is correcting ambient RNA contamination in retained cells' expression profiles — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected gene expression; use SoupX downstream The dataset contains many genuine cell-containing droplets with very low total counts near T — the low-count-means-cell-free assumption may mislabel them and T must be manually adjusted

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) and you must assign each retained barcode to a positive (cell-free) or unlabeled (mixed cell-containing/cell-free) set before PU-learning-based cell calling.
skills.name: positive-unlabeled-set-partitioning
skills.search_text: positive-unlabeled-set-partitioning Use when starting from a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) and you must assign each retained barcode to a positive (cell-free) or unlabeled (mixed cell-containing/cell-free) set before PU-learning-based cell calling. The dataset is expected to contain genuine cell-containing droplets with very low total counts comparable to ambient-RNA barcodes; the low-count-implies-empty assumption of set P may not hold and the user must manually adjust T The input is already a filtered/processed feature table rather than a raw unfiltered count matrix; partitioning assumes the full barcode space including cell-free droplets The goal is ambient RNA correction of expression profiles rather than barcode partitioning; EmptyNN does not estimate corrected profiles and tools such as SoupX are needed Partitions raw droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into a positively labeled set P of bona fide cell-free droplets (total UMI counts below threshold T, default 100) and an unlabeled set U of remaining barcodes, the prerequisite step for EmptyNN's positive-unlabeled (PU) learning classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Partitions raw droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into a positively labeled set P of bona fide cell-free droplets (total UMI counts below threshold T, default 100) and an unlabeled set U of remaining barcodes, the prerequisite step for EmptyNN's positive-unlabeled (PU) learning classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is expected to contain genuine cell-containing droplets with very low total counts comparable to ambient-RNA barcodes; the low-count-implies-empty assumption of set P may not hold and the user must manually adjust T The input is already a filtered/processed feature table rather than a raw unfiltered count matrix; partitioning assumes the full barcode space including cell-free droplets The goal is ambient RNA correction of expression profiles rather than barcode partitioning; EmptyNN does not estimate corrected profiles and tools such as SoupX are needed

skills.description: Use when a dataset is too large to cluster directly (e.g. Levine15_32dim, 104,184 cells; Samusik16, 86,864 cells) and a KMD model has been fit on a subsample whose labels must be propagated to the unsampled objects.
skills.name: post-hoc-cluster-label-inference
skills.search_text: post-hoc-cluster-label-inference Use when a dataset is too large to cluster directly (e.g. Levine15_32dim, 104,184 cells; Samusik16, 86,864 cells) and a KMD model has been fit on a subsample whose labels must be propagated to the unsampled objects. The dataset is small enough to cluster directly without subsampling — the post hoc inferring step is only recommended for large datasets (sub_sample=True is 'reccomended on large dataset') Clusters of interest are very small and may be poorly represented in the subsample, since the sampling-based extension may miss clusters that are not sampled well A precomputed adjacency matrix or non-default affinity is required and incompatible with the subsample-then-infer flow without care http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Extends KMD clustering from a subsampled core to the full dataset: after fitting KMDClustering on a subsample (sub_sample=True), a post hoc inferring (predict) step labels all remaining objects against the core clusters. This is what makes KMD clustering scale to million-object biological datasets such as mass cytometry panels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Extends KMD clustering from a subsampled core to the full dataset: after fitting KMDClustering on a subsample (sub_sample=True), a post hoc inferring (predict) step labels all remaining objects against the core clusters. This is what makes KMD clustering scale to million-object biological datasets such as mass cytometry panels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough to cluster directly without subsampling — the post hoc inferring step is only recommended for large datasets (sub_sample=True is 'reccomended on large dataset') Clusters of interest are very small and may be poorly represented in the subsample, since the sampling-based extension may miss clusters that are not sampled well A precomputed adjacency matrix or non-default affinity is required and incompatible with the subsample-then-infer flow without care

skills.description: Use when you have tabulated control vs. perturbed cell counts per Louvain cluster (from any integration embedding or ICAT sslouvain assignments), a G-test has flagged clusters with significant treatment enrichment, and you need per-cluster direction of enrichment for a Fig 5C-style comparison.
skills.name: post-hoc-fishers-exact-testing
skills.search_text: post-hoc-fishers-exact-testing Use when you have tabulated control vs. perturbed cell counts per Louvain cluster (from any integration embedding or ICAT sslouvain assignments), a G-test has flagged clusters with significant treatment enrichment, and you need per-cluster direction of enrichment for a Fig 5C-style comparison. Cluster-level treatment enrichment has not yet been established by the G-test — Fisher's exact post hoc testing is only meaningful for clusters flagged as significant The question is differential gene expression or state identification itself — use ICAT's NCFS weighting and semi-supervised clustering rather than count-tabulation tests Data are not discrete cell-by-cluster assignment counts (e.g., continuous expression values), since Fisher's exact test requires a 2x2 contingency table http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Follow-up significance testing that resolves the direction (depletion vs. enrichment) of perturbed-cell clustering after a per-cluster G-test, used to show that ICAT — not Seurat, Scanorama, or Harmony — resolves the sm50/pks2 PMC responses to MK-886 in the GSE164240 dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Follow-up significance testing that resolves the direction (depletion vs. enrichment) of perturbed-cell clustering after a per-cluster G-test, used to show that ICAT — not Seurat, Scanorama, or Harmony — resolves the sm50/pks2 PMC responses to MK-886 in the GSE164240 dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cluster-level treatment enrichment has not yet been established by the G-test — Fisher's exact post hoc testing is only meaningful for clusters flagged as significant The question is differential gene expression or state identification itself — use ICAT's NCFS weighting and semi-supervised clustering rather than count-tabulation tests Data are not discrete cell-by-cluster assignment counts (e.g., continuous expression values), since Fisher's exact test requires a 2x2 contingency table

skills.description: Use when a single-sample scRNA-seq pipeline has already produced an integrated multi-sample SingleCellExperiment object (with HVGs and reduced dimensions) and you need post-integration clustering, cell-type annotation, and an HTML report.
skills.name: post-integration-single-cell-clustering
skills.search_text: post-integration-single-cell-clustering Use when a single-sample scRNA-seq pipeline has already produced an integrated multi-sample SingleCellExperiment object (with HVGs and reduced dimensions) and you need post-integration clustering, cell-type annotation, and an HTML report. Input is raw single-sample data that has not yet been integrated across samples — use the single-sample pipeline's second clustering stage instead The 01_integration stage has not completed, so no integrated object with computed integration methods exists to select from The goal is marker gene detection or differential expression between clusters rather than clustering/annotation itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 The scdrake 02_int_clustering stage reruns normalization, dimensionality reduction, graph-based clustering, and SingleR cell-type annotation on data already integrated across samples, producing a standalone HTML report. It lets the analyst pick one final integration method and derive clusters/annotations from the integrated embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad089
skills.summary: The scdrake 02_int_clustering stage reruns normalization, dimensionality reduction, graph-based clustering, and SingleR cell-type annotation on data already integrated across samples, producing a standalone HTML report. It lets the analyst pick one final integration method and derive clusters/annotations from the integrated embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw single-sample data that has not yet been integrated across samples — use the single-sample pipeline's second clustering stage instead The 01_integration stage has not completed, so no integrated object with computed integration methods exists to select from The goal is marker gene detection or differential expression between clusters rather than clustering/annotation itself

skills.description: Use when p-values are needed for variables selected by Lasso or adaptive Lasso penalized regression on high-dimensional genomic covariates, since standard software p-values are invalid after variable selection.
skills.name: post-selection-p-value-inference
skills.search_text: post-selection-p-value-inference Use when p-values are needed for variables selected by Lasso or adaptive Lasso penalized regression on high-dimensional genomic covariates, since standard software p-values are invalid after variable selection. The model was fit by ridge or ordinary (unpenalized) regression — selection-based p-value correction targets Lasso/adaptive Lasso selection events The p-values are needed for prediction assessment rather than variable-level inference — cross-validation prediction power is the HDMAC mechanism for that The number of variables is around a hundred thousand where penalized regression falls short — HDMAC recommends FDR screening first rather than relying on the penalized fit directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Computes valid conditional post-selection p-values for variables retained by Lasso and adaptive Lasso penalized regression (Cox and logistic variants) using the selectiveInference R package implementing Lee et al.'s algorithm, as provided by the HDMAC platform for high-dimensional TCGA genomic analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60791-z
skills.summary: Computes valid conditional post-selection p-values for variables retained by Lasso and adaptive Lasso penalized regression (Cox and logistic variants) using the selectiveInference R package implementing Lee et al.'s algorithm, as provided by the HDMAC platform for high-dimensional TCGA genomic analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model was fit by ridge or ordinary (unpenalized) regression — selection-based p-value correction targets Lasso/adaptive Lasso selection events The p-values are needed for prediction assessment rather than variable-level inference — cross-validation prediction power is the HDMAC mechanism for that The number of variables is around a hundred thousand where penalized regression falls short — HDMAC recommends FDR screening first rather than relying on the penalized fit directly

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-scaled scRNA-seq matrix with a shortlist of candidate TFs per target gene and need to infer which Boolean logic combination (e.g., TF1 AND NOT TF2) regulates each target without per-gate likelihood enumeration.
skills.name: posterior-assignment-of-regulatory-combinations
skills.search_text: posterior-assignment-of-regulatory-combinations Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-scaled scRNA-seq matrix with a shortlist of candidate TFs per target gene and need to infer which Boolean logic combination (e.g., TF1 AND NOT TF2) regulates each target without per-gate likelihood enumeration. When candidate TF lists are large and unrefined — scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with refined candidate regulatory TFs based on external hints, and >5 regulators risks overfitting. When the goal is a linear directed TF-target network without logic gates — use scGATE_edge() instead of the gate-inference mixture fit. When data are pseudotime-sorted single-cell profiles along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A Bayesian mixture-model step in scGATE that fits a zero-inflated density over enumerated Boolean TF combinations (AND/OR/XOR products of Hill-transformed expressions), estimates prior weights w_v with EM, and assigns each cell to its maximum-posterior combination — inferring the most probable logic gate a posteriori instead of computing a separate likelihood per rule. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: A Bayesian mixture-model step in scGATE that fits a zero-inflated density over enumerated Boolean TF combinations (AND/OR/XOR products of Hill-transformed expressions), estimates prior weights w_v with EM, and assigns each cell to its maximum-posterior combination — inferring the most probable logic gate a posteriori instead of computing a separate likelihood per rule.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When candidate TF lists are large and unrefined — scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with refined candidate regulatory TFs based on external hints, and >5 regulators risks overfitting. When the goal is a linear directed TF-target network without logic gates — use scGATE_edge() instead of the gate-inference mixture fit. When data are pseudotime-sorted single-cell profiles along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays.

skills.description: Use when FFC cluster labels and pval_list are available for single-cell data (PBMC CITE-seq, multiome, MCA) and you want to quantify ARI/purity gains from restricting evaluation to high-confidence (PEP < 0.1) labels.
skills.name: posterior-confidence-label-filtering
skills.search_text: posterior-confidence-label-filtering Use when FFC cluster labels and pval_list are available for single-cell data (PBMC CITE-seq, multiome, MCA) and you want to quantify ARI/purity gains from restricting evaluation to high-confidence (PEP < 0.1) labels. The data contains only one cluster — every point receives a single label type, so Monte Carlo validation cannot estimate meaningful uncertainty. Cluster labels come from a method other than FFC's validate()/pval() pipeline, so no per-cell posterior significance values exist to threshold at 0.1. The raw count matrix has not been embedded/dimension-reduced first — FFC is sensitive to high dimensionality and should be applied after nonlinear dimensionality reduction or PCA, not to raw features. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters single-cell cluster assignments to high-confidence cells using Forest Fire Clustering's non-parametric posterior significance values (PEP < 0.1), which the paper shows improves clustering ARI (e.g., >20% gain on PBMC benchmarks; 0.38→0.72 on the Mouse Cell Atlas). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Filters single-cell cluster assignments to high-confidence cells using Forest Fire Clustering's non-parametric posterior significance values (PEP < 0.1), which the paper shows improves clustering ARI (e.g., >20% gain on PBMC benchmarks; 0.38→0.72 on the Mouse Cell Atlas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data contains only one cluster — every point receives a single label type, so Monte Carlo validation cannot estimate meaningful uncertainty. Cluster labels come from a method other than FFC's validate()/pval() pipeline, so no per-cell posterior significance values exist to threshold at 0.1. The raw count matrix has not been embedded/dimension-reduced first — FFC is sensitive to high dimensionality and should be applied after nonlinear dimensionality reduction or PCA, not to raw features.

skills.description: Use when the goal is a treatment-subgroup analysis: a treatment/coding/interacting variable structure must be encoded via the types argument of dipm(), and a tree over baseline covariates (e.g. MASS::anorexia weight-change data) must be grown, split by depth-importance, and optionally pruned.

The goal is to inspect per-variable depth importance alone without growing a treatment-subgroup tree — compute node statistics only via node_dipm(obj) A forest-based node fit is not desired and an exhaustive classical split search is preferred — use spmtree() instead of dipm(), noting it exposes only nmin and maxdepth as structural tuning Pruning must alter optimal treatment assignments — pmprune only collapses terminal sister nodes with the same optimal treatment, so it is the wrong tool for cost/complexity pruning that changes recommendations Fits Depth Importance in Precision Medicine (DIPM) classification trees using the dipm R package, which implements the tree/forest method through R code that calls a C program, to identify subgroups where subjects perform especially well or poorly under a particular treatment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac041
skills.summary: Fits Depth Importance in Precision Medicine (DIPM) classification trees using the dipm R package, which implements the tree/forest method through R code that calls a C program, to identify subgroups where subjects perform especially well or poorly under a particular treatment.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare competing gene set enrichment methods on synthetic studies where the true positive pathways are known by construction, across a noise/similarity grid.

skills.summary: Benchmark enrichment methods by computing per-method precision-recall AUC against a simulated ground truth of active pathways, sweeping noise levels η and similarity factors ρ to expose robustness differences as done for pareg vs MGSA, FET, topGO, blitzGSEA, and a null model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real experimental studies with no ground truth for which pathways are truly active — PR-AUC against simulated truth is only meaningful on synthetic data where positives are sampled by construction Evaluating a single enrichment method in isolation without competitor baselines — this skill is specifically a comparative benchmarking design Datasets where pathway redundancy/inter-pathway dependencies are irrelevant — the (η, ρ) similarity sweep is the point of the benchmark

skills.description: Use when a GRN method's aggregate precision-recall curve looks acceptable and you need to check whether that summary hides poor edge-rank recovery for individual regulators in the gold standard.

skills.search_text: precision-recall-caveat-analysis Use when a GRN method's aggregate precision-recall curve looks acceptable and you need to check whether that summary hides poor edge-rank recovery for individual regulators in the gold standard. The input is raw single-cell expression data rather than a completed, aggregated ranked edge list — run SINGE GLG and SINGE Aggregate first The gold standard does not decompose into individual regulators with known targets, so regulator-specific edge ranks cannot be computed You need a single overall precision-recall number rather than a diagnosis of regulator-level performance caveats http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A regulator-specific evaluation that sorts gold-standard regulators by their outgoing edge count in the ESCAPE regulatory network and plots per-regulator distributions of predicted edge ranks, exposing regulators whose edge recovery is poor despite acceptable overall precision-recall performance of a GRN inference method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: A regulator-specific evaluation that sorts gold-standard regulators by their outgoing edge count in the ESCAPE regulatory network and plots per-regulator distributions of predicted edge ranks, exposing regulators whose edge recovery is poor despite acceptable overall precision-recall performance of a GRN inference method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw single-cell expression data rather than a completed, aggregated ranked edge list — run SINGE GLG and SINGE Aggregate first The gold standard does not decompose into individual regulators with known targets, so regulator-specific edge ranks cannot be computed You need a single overall precision-recall number rather than a diagnosis of regulator-level performance caveats

skills.description: Use when comparing variant-calling or classification tools against a known ground truth, and you need cutoff-independent metrics (AUPRC/AUROC) plus PR/ROC curves across simulation settings.

skills.search_text: precision-recall-curve-analysis Use when comparing variant-calling or classification tools against a known ground truth, and you need cutoff-independent metrics (AUPRC/AUROC) plus PR/ROC curves across simulation settings. No ground-truth labels exist for the called variants — PR/ROC against unknown truth is undefined; use clonal reconstruction validation instead. The tool only outputs binary calls with no tunable score cutoff, so a PR/ROC curve cannot be traced. Evaluating clustering or clone-assignment quality (e.g., vireoSNP assignments) rather than per-variant detection performance. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark variant-calling performance by sweeping a tool's score cutoff to trace precision-recall (PR) and ROC curves, then comparing AUPRC/AUROC against ground-truth clonal mtDNA variants — as done to show MQuad (AUPRC 0.976) outperforms mgatk and Monovar on simulated Smart-seq2-like data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Benchmark variant-calling performance by sweeping a tool's score cutoff to trace precision-recall (PR) and ROC curves, then comparing AUPRC/AUROC against ground-truth clonal mtDNA variants — as done to show MQuad (AUPRC 0.976) outperforms mgatk and Monovar on simulated Smart-seq2-like data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth labels exist for the called variants — PR/ROC against unknown truth is undefined; use clonal reconstruction validation instead. The tool only outputs binary calls with no tunable score cutoff, so a PR/ROC curve cannot be traced. Evaluating clustering or clone-assignment quality (e.g., vireoSNP assignments) rather than per-variant detection performance.

skills.summary: Computes cell type annotation accuracy as the fraction of correctly predicted cells for TOSICA's reference-query label transfer, benchmarked against 18 other annotators across six datasets (hArtery, hBone, hPancreas, mBrain, mPancreas, mAtlas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset has no ground-truth cell type labels (accuracy cannot be computed; use interpretability outputs like attention weights or gene2token_weights.csv instead) The query AnnData var_names are not consistent with, and in the same order as, the reference — predictions would be invalid and accuracy meaningless until subsetting is done The goal is unsupervised clustering or de novo annotation rather than label transfer from a reference dataset

skills.description: Use when classifying genomes (e.g., unknown-lifestyle Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia or Pseudomonas strains) with random-forest per-lifestyle probability outputs where an assignment cutoff must separate confident calls from uncertain ones.
skills.name: prediction-confidence-thresholding
skills.search_text: prediction-confidence-thresholding Use when classifying genomes (e.g., unknown-lifestyle Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia or Pseudomonas strains) with random-forest per-lifestyle probability outputs where an assignment cutoff must separate confident calls from uncertain ones. Genomes already carry literature-derived lifestyle labels — these are training/evaluation data, not prediction targets for thresholded assignment The goal is identifying lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs via >70% group presence and >2 log2 fold change) rather than assigning lifestyles to individual genomes The classifier is trained from scratch rather than being the article's trained model — the 0.8 cutoff and per-lifestyle binary forests are specific to bacLIFE's setup and must be re-justified http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns a predicted lifestyle to a genome only when the binary random forest (scikit-learn, n_estimators=50) adjudication confidence — the fraction of trees voting for a class — exceeds 0.8; genomes below the threshold stay 'unknown'. This prevents overconfident lifestyle calls in bacLIFE's lifestyle-prediction module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Assigns a predicted lifestyle to a genome only when the binary random forest (scikit-learn, n_estimators=50) adjudication confidence — the fraction of trees voting for a class — exceeds 0.8; genomes below the threshold stay 'unknown'. This prevents overconfident lifestyle calls in bacLIFE's lifestyle-prediction module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genomes already carry literature-derived lifestyle labels — these are training/evaluation data, not prediction targets for thresholded assignment The goal is identifying lifestyle-associated genes (pLAGs via >70% group presence and >2 log2 fold change) rather than assigning lifestyles to individual genomes The classifier is trained from scratch rather than being the article's trained model — the 0.8 cutoff and per-lifestyle binary forests are specific to bacLIFE's setup and must be re-justified

The Seurat object does not contain a UMAP dimensionality reduction — contours are computed in UMAP space, so the input must already include one The R session uses Seurat version 5 or another version — Census requires Seurat v4 to be loaded before the Census library Labels are already stabilized or the analysis goal is model training on a reference rather than annotation of a new dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Census's label-stabilizing step: compute MASS-based prediction contours for each candidate cell-type label in UMAP space, detect overlapping contours, adjudicate disputed cells, and iterate with UMAP SNN-cluster label propagation until contours no longer overlap or labels stop changing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Census's label-stabilizing step: compute MASS-based prediction contours for each candidate cell-type label in UMAP space, detect overlapping contours, adjudicate disputed cells, and iterate with UMAP SNN-cluster label propagation until contours no longer overlap or labels stop changing.

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate the accuracy and precision of regression-based parameter estimators by comparing predicted-minus-true error distributions across multiple model architectures on simulated data with known ground truth.
skills.name: prediction-error-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: prediction-error-distribution-analysis Use when you need to evaluate the accuracy and precision of regression-based parameter estimators by comparing predicted-minus-true error distributions across multiple model architectures on simulated data with known ground truth. Applied to empirical data where true parameter values are unknown — per-event error (predicted minus true) cannot be computed without simulated ground truth. Evaluating class prediction (redundant vs unique classification accuracy/power) rather than continuous parameter estimation — use the CLOUDeClassify* functions instead. The test data are unbalanced across classes, since precision comparisons by class require the balanced design described in the study. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies how precisely CLOUDe's four machine learning architectures (NN, XGB, RF, SVM) and an LRT baseline estimate the OU evolutionary parameters theta1, theta2, and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) by computing per-event prediction errors on balanced simulated test data, stratified by 'redundant' vs 'unique' class. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae002
skills.summary: Quantifies how precisely CLOUDe's four machine learning architectures (NN, XGB, RF, SVM) and an LRT baseline estimate the OU evolutionary parameters theta1, theta2, and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) by computing per-event prediction errors on balanced simulated test data, stratified by 'redundant' vs 'unique' class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Applied to empirical data where true parameter values are unknown — per-event error (predicted minus true) cannot be computed without simulated ground truth. Evaluating class prediction (redundant vs unique classification accuracy/power) rather than continuous parameter estimation — use the CLOUDeClassify* functions instead. The test data are unbalanced across classes, since precision comparisons by class require the balanced design described in the study.

skills.description: Use when converting LncCat/CatBoost prediction probabilities into binary lncRNA vs PCT labels, or when sweeping cutoffs (e.g. 0.1-0.9) to check that reported MCC/F1 benchmarks hold at the fixed 0.5 cutoff.
skills.name: prediction-score-cutoff-thresholding
skills.search_text: prediction-score-cutoff-thresholding Use when converting LncCat/CatBoost prediction probabilities into binary lncRNA vs PCT labels, or when sweeping cutoffs (e.g. 0.1-0.9) to check that reported MCC/F1 benchmarks hold at the fixed 0.5 cutoff. Input is already a binary lncRNA/PCT label file rather than continuous prediction scores — thresholding is not applicable. The goal is to compare whole coding-potential methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) rather than to re-derive LncCat's own binary calls from its scores. Evaluating on sORF test datasets where a different, unreported cutoff calibration may apply and the 0.5 baseline is not established. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Converts LncCat (CatBoost) prediction scores into binary lncRNA vs PCT calls by thresholding at a fixed cutoff of 0.5 (score >= 0.5 -> lncRNA, < 0.5 -> PCT), and supports cutoff sweeps to verify reported MCC/F1 benchmarks are tied to that fixed cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Converts LncCat (CatBoost) prediction scores into binary lncRNA vs PCT calls by thresholding at a fixed cutoff of 0.5 (score >= 0.5 -> lncRNA, < 0.5 -> PCT), and supports cutoff sweeps to verify reported MCC/F1 benchmarks are tied to that fixed cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a binary lncRNA/PCT label file rather than continuous prediction scores — thresholding is not applicable. The goal is to compare whole coding-potential methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) rather than to re-derive LncCat's own binary calls from its scores. Evaluating on sORF test datasets where a different, unreported cutoff calibration may apply and the 0.5 baseline is not established.

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or retraining a dual-branch 1D CNN for nucleotide-modification site prediction from one-hot encoded sequence plus secondary-structure matrices, or when the target model must report 661,118 trainable parameters.
skills.name: prelu-convolutional-layer-configuration
skills.search_text: prelu-convolutional-layer-configuration Use when reconstructing or retraining a dual-branch 1D CNN for nucleotide-modification site prediction from one-hot encoded sequence plus secondary-structure matrices, or when the target model must report 661,118 trainable parameters. Input is raw nucleotide sequence rather than a one-of-K encoded 51×4 / 51×6 matrix — the encoding step must happen first A single-modality model suffices — the paper showed the combined model's benefit comes from adding the secondary-structure branch; sequence-only CNNs are weaker (3–4% lower accuracy/F1) No source code or webserver exists for a competitor method (e.g. iPseU-CNN), so this architecture cannot be used for a direct head-to-head reconstruction of that tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configures the dual-input 1D CNN architecture of MU-PseUDeep in Keras/TensorFlow, where PReLU-activated convolutional branches process one-of-K encoded RNA sequence (51×4) and RNAshapes secondary-structure (51×6) matrices before concatenation into a 512-neuron softplus dense layer. Reproduces the paper's exact hyperparameters, including tuned kernel regularizers and dropout rates per layer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Configures the dual-input 1D CNN architecture of MU-PseUDeep in Keras/TensorFlow, where PReLU-activated convolutional branches process one-of-K encoded RNA sequence (51×4) and RNAshapes secondary-structure (51×6) matrices before concatenation into a 512-neuron softplus dense layer. Reproduces the paper's exact hyperparameters, including tuned kernel regularizers and dropout rates per layer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw nucleotide sequence rather than a one-of-K encoded 51×4 / 51×6 matrix — the encoding step must happen first A single-modality model suffices — the paper showed the combined model's benefit comes from adding the secondary-structure branch; sequence-only CNNs are weaker (3–4% lower accuracy/F1) No source code or webserver exists for a competitor method (e.g. iPseU-CNN), so this architecture cannot be used for a direct head-to-head reconstruction of that tool

skills.name: preprocessing-for-protein-imputation
skills.search_text: preprocessing-for-protein-imputation Use when you have raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts plus paired ADT (CITE-seq/REAP-seq) protein counts and need the normalized denoised expression matrix and relative protein abundance response vectors required to run or train cTP-net. Expression input is TPM or RPKM — cTP-net can only apply to count-based UMI expression input, and CITE-seq data with TPM/RPKM metrics has unknown prediction accuracy The scRNA-seq data is already SAVER-X denoised and LogNormalized — re-denoising or double-normalizing would distort the Λ estimates You need raw CITE-seq protein measurements rather than imputed ones — this skill prepares inputs for imputation, not direct measurement http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Prepares paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT data for cTP-net surface protein imputation by SAVER-X denoising of UMI counts, Seurat LogNormalize of the denoised matrix, and geometric-mean log-ratio transformation of protein counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Prepares paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT data for cTP-net surface protein imputation by SAVER-X denoising of UMI counts, Seurat LogNormalize of the denoised matrix, and geometric-mean log-ratio transformation of protein counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression input is TPM or RPKM — cTP-net can only apply to count-based UMI expression input, and CITE-seq data with TPM/RPKM metrics has unknown prediction accuracy The scRNA-seq data is already SAVER-X denoised and LogNormalized — re-denoising or double-normalizing would distort the Λ estimates You need raw CITE-seq protein measurements rather than imputed ones — this skill prepares inputs for imputation, not direct measurement

skills.description: Use when you have a weighted gene network or community of genes (e.g., a GRnnData network across the 26 benchmarked cell types or a Louvain community) and need to test whether its genes are enriched for TFs, cell-type markers, ENCODE targets, or GO molecular-function terms.

When the input is raw expression data rather than an already-inferred weighted gene network — build the network first (e.g., with scPRINT's attention-matrix extraction) before ranking genes When the gene set of interest is smaller than the retained-community window or lacks a ranked score (prerank requires a full ordered gene list as background) When seeking causal ground-truth validation — the article notes no perfect ground truths exist for gene network inference benchmarking, so enrichment is a consistency check, not causal proof http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Runs GSEA-style prerank enrichment (Enrichr/GSEA) on per-gene ranked scores derived from single-cell gene networks — e.g., eigenvector centrality or Target-Hub/Regulator-Hub edge-score sums — against TF, pangaloDB cell-type marker, ENCODE TF-target, and GO_MF_2023 gene sets to validate biological meaning of scPRINT, scGPT, GENIE3, DeepSEM, and Geneformer networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Runs GSEA-style prerank enrichment (Enrichr/GSEA) on per-gene ranked scores derived from single-cell gene networks — e.g., eigenvector centrality or Target-Hub/Regulator-Hub edge-score sums — against TF, pangaloDB cell-type marker, ENCODE TF-target, and GO_MF_2023 gene sets to validate biological meaning of scPRINT, scGPT, GENIE3, DeepSEM, and Geneformer networks.

The system of interest lacks relevant curated signature gene sets — the article notes the user would have to compile and curate customized gene sets, since only 75 hematopoiesis gene sets are provided The input is raw count matrices or unclustered cells — clusters must already be identified before pre-ranking marker genes Manual inspection of a handful of known marker genes on a single small dataset is sufficient and no gene-set enrichment framework is desired http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Objective cell type annotation for scRNA-seq clusters by pre-ranking cluster marker genes by log2 fold-change and running fast GSEA (fGSEA) against curated GMT gene sets, then visualizing normalized enrichment scores (NES) as a cluster-by-gene-set heatmap to assign identities and cell states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266

skills.search_text: preranked-gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when factor loadings from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition (e.g., 6 ASD factors) need functional interpretation by ranking LR pairs and testing enrichment of pathway-level LR gene sets. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a ranked list of LR pairs ordered by factor loadings (e.g., you only have raw expression counts without a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition) The pathway gene sets contain fewer than 15 LR pairs after intersecting with the ranked list, below the min set size cutoff The analysis targets a single context/sample rather than factor-specific loadings from a context-deconvolved communication tensor
