skills.name: pretrained-model-inference-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: pretrained-model-inference-scrnaseq Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (.h5ad) from progression-stage samples (normal mucosa, polyps, tumors) must be scored for malignancy with a pretrained classifier instead of retraining, and per-stage malignant-cell percentages are needed. When no basic cell-type annotation is available — the tool 'is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages, relying on the prerequisite identification of basic cell types' For cancers with unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — capabilities are untested there When the goal is de novo malignant-cell annotation without a pretrained model — this skill covers inference with the provided Zenodo model, not training a new classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Apply scMalignantFinder's pretrained classifier (model.joblib + ordered_feature.tsv from Zenodo record 17888140) to epithelial scRNA-seq expression matrices (.h5ad) to obtain per-cell Normal/Malignant predictions and malignancy probabilities, enabling quantification of malignancy trends across carcinogenesis stages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Apply scMalignantFinder's pretrained classifier (model.joblib + ordered_feature.tsv from Zenodo record 17888140) to epithelial scRNA-seq expression matrices (.h5ad) to obtain per-cell Normal/Malignant predictions and malignancy probabilities, enabling quantification of malignancy trends across carcinogenesis stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no basic cell-type annotation is available — the tool 'is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages, relying on the prerequisite identification of basic cell types' For cancers with unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — capabilities are untested there When the goal is de novo malignant-cell annotation without a pretrained model — this skill covers inference with the provided Zenodo model, not training a new classifier

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data lack miRNA measurements (poly(A) capture precludes miRNA profiling) and you need to infer miRNA expression per cluster or per cell using a model pretrained on paired bulk miRNA-mRNA cohorts such as TCGA, GTEx, or CCLE.
skills.name: pretrained-model-transfer-to-scrna-data
skills.search_text: pretrained-model-transfer-to-scrna-data Use when scRNA-seq data lack miRNA measurements (poly(A) capture precludes miRNA profiling) and you need to infer miRNA expression per cluster or per cell using a model pretrained on paired bulk miRNA-mRNA cohorts such as TCGA, GTEx, or CCLE. The application sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the model's training cohort (e.g. applying a CCLE-trained model to very different tissue), where performance loss is expected per Figure S9 Too few genes are detected in the single-cell data due to dropout, so a pre-trained model may fail and retraining on detected genes is required rather than transfer Paired miRNA-mRNA expression data already exist for the sample, making inference unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Apply a pretrained, bulk-trained machine learning model (miRSCAPE, xgboost-based) to single-cell RNA-seq data by pooling cells within clusters to overcome scRNA-seq sparsity, or by predicting per-cell in unpooled mode. Enables miRNA activity inference from mRNA-only scRNA-seq profiles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Apply a pretrained, bulk-trained machine learning model (miRSCAPE, xgboost-based) to single-cell RNA-seq data by pooling cells within clusters to overcome scRNA-seq sparsity, or by predicting per-cell in unpooled mode. Enables miRNA activity inference from mRNA-only scRNA-seq profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The application sample's cellular/tissue context differs substantially from the model's training cohort (e.g. applying a CCLE-trained model to very different tissue), where performance loss is expected per Figure S9 Too few genes are detected in the single-cell data due to dropout, so a pre-trained model may fail and retraining on detected genes is required rather than transfer Paired miRNA-mRNA expression data already exist for the sample, making inference unnecessary

skills.description: Use when new gene expression profiles (a batch data.frame with Entrez ID columns, or a single-sample profile) must be classified with an already-trained DeepCC model without retraining, e.g., assigning CMS labels to colorectal cancer samples.
skills.name: pretrained-neural-classifier-inference
skills.search_text: pretrained-neural-classifier-inference Use when new gene expression profiles (a batch data.frame with Entrez ID columns, or a single-sample profile) must be classified with an already-trained DeepCC model without retraining, e.g., assigning CMS labels to colorectal cancer samples. You need unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is developed for classification but not clustering of cancer patients. Input is already a functional-spectrum/enrichment feature matrix rather than raw gene expression profiles. No reference expression profile of the same or similar cancer type/platform is available for a single microarray sample and a customized reference cannot be generated — rescaling against the RNA-Seq TCGA reference may be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Applies a pre-trained DeepCC Keras classifier to new gene expression data by first computing functional spectra (MSigDB v7, 22,596 gene sets by default) and then emitting subtype labels (e.g., CMS for colorectal cancer) or class probabilities, including a single-sample mode with reference-profile rescaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Applies a pre-trained DeepCC Keras classifier to new gene expression data by first computing functional spectra (MSigDB v7, 22,596 gene sets by default) and then emitting subtype labels (e.g., CMS for colorectal cancer) or class probabilities, including a single-sample mode with reference-profile rescaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need unsupervised clustering of cancer patients — DeepCC is developed for classification but not clustering of cancer patients. Input is already a functional-spectrum/enrichment feature matrix rather than raw gene expression profiles. No reference expression profile of the same or similar cancer type/platform is available for a single microarray sample and a customized reference cannot be generated — rescaling against the RNA-Seq TCGA reference may be unreliable.

skills.description: Use when a test scRNA-seq expression matrix must be labeled against the Cell Ontology without retraining, especially when the query may contain cell types absent from any training annotations.
skills.name: pretrained-neural-model-inference
skills.search_text: pretrained-neural-model-inference Use when a test scRNA-seq expression matrix must be labeled against the Cell Ontology without retraining, especially when the query may contain cell types absent from any training annotations. You need to train a model on a new labeled dataset with custom annotations — use ProcessTrainFeature/Train instead of the pretrained checkpoint. Your analysis requires distinguishing topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot separate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Apply OnClass's provided pre-trained neural model to score test single-cell transcriptomes against the Cell Ontology, propagating confidence scores via random walk with restart so all Cell Ontology terms—including unseen ones—receive predictions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Apply OnClass's provided pre-trained neural model to score test single-cell transcriptomes against the Cell Ontology, propagating confidence scores via random walk with restart so all Cell Ontology terms—including unseen ones—receive predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train a model on a new labeled dataset with custom annotations — use ProcessTrainFeature/Train instead of the pretrained checkpoint. Your analysis requires distinguishing topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot separate.

skills.description: Use when a trained TACTiCS PyTorch model must be loaded from the Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.7582460) to extract cell embeddings for motor cortex scRNA-seq cells without retraining.
skills.name: pretrained-neural-network-model-loading
skills.search_text: pretrained-neural-network-model-loading Use when a trained TACTiCS PyTorch model must be loaded from the Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.7582460) to extract cell embeddings for motor cortex scRNA-seq cells without retraining. You need to train TACTiCS from scratch on a new species pair or dataset — follow the tutorial.ipynb training workflow (embed_proteins, calc_dist, `TACTiCS` class) instead of loading a deposited checkpoint. The task is creating protein-sequence embeddings or computing the gene similarity distance matrix (embed_proteins / calc_dist in genes.py) — model loading presupposes that matrix already exists. The input scRNA-seq data is not one of the deposited 50k motor cortex subsets the released models were trained on; checkpoints will not directly transfer to unrelated preprocessed datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Loads the pretrained TACTiCS neural-network checkpoints (the PyTorch `TACTiCS` class in `tactics.py`) from the Zenodo deposit to extract per-cell embeddings for human/mouse/marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq data. This reproduces the paper's embedding space for downstream cell-type cross-species alignment without retraining the network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Loads the pretrained TACTiCS neural-network checkpoints (the PyTorch `TACTiCS` class in `tactics.py`) from the Zenodo deposit to extract per-cell embeddings for human/mouse/marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq data. This reproduces the paper's embedding space for downstream cell-type cross-species alignment without retraining the network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train TACTiCS from scratch on a new species pair or dataset — follow the tutorial.ipynb training workflow (embed_proteins, calc_dist, `TACTiCS` class) instead of loading a deposited checkpoint. The task is creating protein-sequence embeddings or computing the gene similarity distance matrix (embed_proteins / calc_dist in genes.py) — model loading presupposes that matrix already exists. The input scRNA-seq data is not one of the deposited 50k motor cortex subsets the released models were trained on; checkpoints will not directly transfer to unrelated preprocessed datasets.

skills.description: Use when cell type labels must be predicted for raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. artificially dropout-masked validation datasets) using a pretrained disease/tissue-specific Pollock module, so F1 can be computed against annotated cell types.
skills.name: pretrained-pollock-module-inference
skills.search_text: pretrained-pollock-module-inference Use when cell type labels must be predicted for raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. artificially dropout-masked validation datasets) using a pretrained disease/tissue-specific Pollock module, so F1 can be computed against annotated cell types. The input matrix is normalized rather than raw counts — Pollock expects raw expression counts (.X for scanpy, @assays$RNA@counts for Seurat) You need to train a new classifier on your own annotated data instead of applying an existing pretrained module (use train mode, not this skill) The tissue/disease context has no matching pretrained module (modules are disease-specific, e.g. breast cancer, melanoma, pancreatic cancer) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs a pretrained Pollock VAE-plus-linear-classifier module in predict mode ('pollock predict') on scRNA-seq count data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger input) to assign cell type labels with per-cell probabilities. This skill powers the dropout-robustness benchmark where masked copies of validation datasets are classified and scored by macro-averaged F1 against annotated labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Runs a pretrained Pollock VAE-plus-linear-classifier module in predict mode ('pollock predict') on scRNA-seq count data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger input) to assign cell type labels with per-cell probabilities. This skill powers the dropout-robustness benchmark where masked copies of validation datasets are classified and scored by macro-averaged F1 against annotated labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is normalized rather than raw counts — Pollock expects raw expression counts (.X for scanpy, @assays$RNA@counts for Seurat) You need to train a new classifier on your own annotated data instead of applying an existing pretrained module (use train mode, not this skill) The tissue/disease context has no matching pretrained module (modules are disease-specific, e.g. breast cancer, melanoma, pancreatic cancer)

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix needs denoising, label prediction, embedding/batch correction, or gene network extraction without labeled training data, e.g. rare cell states where smoothing-based methods lose signal.
skills.name: pretrained-transformer-zero-shot-inference
skills.search_text: pretrained-transformer-zero-shot-inference Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix needs denoising, label prediction, embedding/batch correction, or gene network extraction without labeled training data, e.g. rare cell states where smoothing-based methods lose signal. Input is spatial omics data or cells with fewer than 200 expressed genes — scPRINT's pretraining filters explicitly drop these The task requires benchmarking against neighbor-aggregating methods where shared biological signal across abundant cell types is the target (MAGIC/KNNsmoothing2 with K=5–10 can match on bulk populations) No pretrained checkpoint covering the organism/gene vocabulary is available (scPRINT pretraining keeps only primary human or mouse cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply a large pretrained cell model (scPRINT, pre-trained on >50 million cellxgene cells) directly to single-cell RNA tasks — denoising, batch effect correction, cell label prediction, gene network inference — without task-specific fine-tuning. Because scPRINT denoises each cell independently, it is particularly strong on rare cell states where neighbor-aggregating methods fail. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Apply a large pretrained cell model (scPRINT, pre-trained on >50 million cellxgene cells) directly to single-cell RNA tasks — denoising, batch effect correction, cell label prediction, gene network inference — without task-specific fine-tuning. Because scPRINT denoises each cell independently, it is particularly strong on rare cell states where neighbor-aggregating methods fail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spatial omics data or cells with fewer than 200 expressed genes — scPRINT's pretraining filters explicitly drop these The task requires benchmarking against neighbor-aggregating methods where shared biological signal across abundant cell types is the target (MAGIC/KNNsmoothing2 with K=5–10 can match on bulk populations) No pretrained checkpoint covering the organism/gene vocabulary is available (scPRINT pretraining keeps only primary human or mouse cells)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-to-scDNA clone-assignment methods against ground-truth clone labels and you need to compare predicted vs. true clonal prevalence concordance across methods.
skills.name: prevalence-scatter-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: prevalence-scatter-plot-visualization Use when benchmarking scRNA-to-scDNA clone-assignment methods against ground-truth clone labels and you need to compare predicted vs. true clonal prevalence concordance across methods. No ground-truth clone labels exist for the dataset (e.g., the BE dataset), so true prevalences cannot be paired with predicted ones — use resampling/stability analyses instead Evaluating cell-to-cell (rather than cell-to-clone) assignments, where clonal prevalence is not defined Only a single method with no baseline or competitor is being assessed — a scatter against the diagonal adds little without comparison context http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Visualizes cell-to-clone integration quality by plotting true clonal prevalences against clonal prevalences predicted by each integration method (e.g., MaCroDNA, Seurat, clonealign) as per-method scatter points with a diagonal ideal-correlation reference line. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Visualizes cell-to-clone integration quality by plotting true clonal prevalences against clonal prevalences predicted by each integration method (e.g., MaCroDNA, Seurat, clonealign) as per-method scatter points with a diagonal ideal-correlation reference line.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth clone labels exist for the dataset (e.g., the BE dataset), so true prevalences cannot be paired with predicted ones — use resampling/stability analyses instead Evaluating cell-to-cell (rather than cell-to-clone) assignments, where clonal prevalence is not defined Only a single method with no baseline or competitor is being assessed — a scatter against the diagonal adds little without comparison context

skills.description: Use when you have a gene-symbol-indexed transcriptome of one cell population of interest and need to infer its emitted (outward) communication toward reference partner cell types via ICELLNET.
skills.name: primary-cell-atlas-reference-profiling
skills.search_text: primary-cell-atlas-reference-profiling Use when you have a gene-symbol-indexed transcriptome of one cell population of interest and need to infer its emitted (outward) communication toward reference partner cell types via ICELLNET. The input is already a computed cell-cell communication score table rather than a raw transcriptome of a single cell type of interest The analysis involves non-human transcriptomic data — the ICELLNET database is curated exclusively from human studies You need chemokine or immune-checkpoint interactions, which are not yet included in the ICELLNET database http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Profile a single cell type of interest (e.g., CAF-S1 vs CAF-S4 bulk RNA-seq) for outward cell-cell communication by connecting its transcriptome to the Human Primary Cell Atlas reference profiles using the ICELLNET scoring framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: Profile a single cell type of interest (e.g., CAF-S1 vs CAF-S4 bulk RNA-seq) for outward cell-cell communication by connecting its transcriptome to the Human Primary Cell Atlas reference profiles using the ICELLNET scoring framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a computed cell-cell communication score table rather than a raw transcriptome of a single cell type of interest The analysis involves non-human transcriptomic data — the ICELLNET database is curated exclusively from human studies You need chemokine or immune-checkpoint interactions, which are not yet included in the ICELLNET database

skills.description: Use when you need to observe the correlation of a single feature of interest against many features in an NGS or microarray expression table, obtaining per-feature coefficients and p-values plus a distribution plot.
skills.name: prime-feature-correlation-statistics
skills.search_text: prime-feature-correlation-statistics Use when you need to observe the correlation of a single feature of interest against many features in an NGS or microarray expression table, obtaining per-feature coefficients and p-values plus a distribution plot. When you need pairwise correlation among many features with clustering/heatmap output rather than one-vs-many — use FeatureCorr::pairwise_corr instead When a deep two-feature analysis with scatter, linear regression, and density plots is required — use FeatureCorr::pair_scatter instead When the input table has not been preprocessed/normalized; primefeature_corr expects a transformed data frame (e.g., log2, medianthres=1 filtered) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes correlation coefficients, distribution statistics, and a histogram of the correlation-coefficient distribution for one 'prime' feature (e.g., the RNASEH2A gene) against all other features in a transformed expression dataset, using the FeatureCorr R package's primefeature_corr function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: Computes correlation coefficients, distribution statistics, and a histogram of the correlation-coefficient distribution for one 'prime' feature (e.g., the RNASEH2A gene) against all other features in a transformed expression dataset, using the FeatureCorr R package's primefeature_corr function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need pairwise correlation among many features with clustering/heatmap output rather than one-vs-many — use FeatureCorr::pairwise_corr instead When a deep two-feature analysis with scatter, linear regression, and density plots is required — use FeatureCorr::pair_scatter instead When the input table has not been preprocessed/normalized; primefeature_corr expects a transformed data frame (e.g., log2, medianthres=1 filtered)

skills.description: Use when a multipotent cell population (e.g. MPPs or TACs) has been shown by CompDICE/CompPrimingPval to be significantly primed (empirical P < 0.05 from nMC >= 1000 randomizations) and top RF pairs are known, and you need per-cell primed-state assignments from scRNA-Seq alone.
skills.name: primed-cell-state-calling
skills.search_text: primed-cell-state-calling Use when a multipotent cell population (e.g. MPPs or TACs) has been shown by CompDICE/CompPrimingPval to be significantly primed (empirical P < 0.05 from nMC >= 1000 randomizations) and top RF pairs are known, and you need per-cell primed-state assignments from scRNA-Seq alone. The multipotent population has not first been shown to be significantly primed via CompPrimingPval against randomized null matrices — calling cells without this significance step is unsupported No candidate regulatory-factor pairs have been ranked by FindPrimingFactors (LOO perturbation and Spearman correlation), since FindPrimedCells requires the top RF pairs as input The goal is to detect bifurcation timing over pseudotime rather than call primed cells in a static snapshot population — DICE's binning (CreateDPTbin, minBins=7) workflow is a different skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Calls individual primed cells within a multipotent progenitor population using the DICE R package's FindPrimedCells function, based on co-expression of the top-ranked regulatory-factor pairs identified by leave-one-out DICE perturbation and Spearman correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Calls individual primed cells within a multipotent progenitor population using the DICE R package's FindPrimedCells function, based on co-expression of the top-ranked regulatory-factor pairs identified by leave-one-out DICE perturbation and Spearman correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The multipotent population has not first been shown to be significantly primed via CompPrimingPval against randomized null matrices — calling cells without this significance step is unsupported No candidate regulatory-factor pairs have been ranked by FindPrimingFactors (LOO perturbation and Spearman correlation), since FindPrimedCells requires the top RF pairs as input The goal is to detect bifurcation timing over pseudotime rather than call primed cells in a static snapshot population — DICE's binning (CreateDPTbin, minBins=7) workflow is a different skill

skills.description: Use when you have DICE-predicted primed cells and regulator TFs from scRNA-Seq plus a matched scATAC-Seq dataset for the same cell types, and need epigenomic confirmation that primed cells show higher accessibility/motif activity of the predicted TFs' targets.
skills.name: primed-cell-state-cross-modality-validation
skills.search_text: primed-cell-state-cross-modality-validation Use when you have DICE-predicted primed cells and regulator TFs from scRNA-Seq plus a matched scATAC-Seq dataset for the same cell types, and need epigenomic confirmation that primed cells show higher accessibility/motif activity of the predicted TFs' targets. No matched scATAC-Seq data exists for the same cell types (e.g. no SHARE-Seq or matched epigenomic dataset) — cross-modality validation is impossible and only the scRNA-Seq evidence stands The predicted priming regulator is not a transcription factor (e.g. UHRF1), since chromVAR motif activity cannot be computed for non-TF chromatin modifiers You need experimental/functional proof that the regulatory factors drive priming — this skill only provides computational epigenomic corroboration, not perturbation evidence http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validates scRNA-Seq-predicted primed cell states (e.g. GP and MEMP primed MPPs from DICE) in matched scATAC-Seq data by showing that chromVAR transcription factor activity of the predicted regulators (GATA1, KLF1 for MEMP; IRF8 for GP) is elevated in scATAC cells assigned as primed via summed marker-gene accessibility. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Validates scRNA-Seq-predicted primed cell states (e.g. GP and MEMP primed MPPs from DICE) in matched scATAC-Seq data by showing that chromVAR transcription factor activity of the predicted regulators (GATA1, KLF1 for MEMP; IRF8 for GP) is elevated in scATAC cells assigned as primed via summed marker-gene accessibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scATAC-Seq data exists for the same cell types (e.g. no SHARE-Seq or matched epigenomic dataset) — cross-modality validation is impossible and only the scRNA-Seq evidence stands The predicted priming regulator is not a transcription factor (e.g. UHRF1), since chromVAR motif activity cannot be computed for non-TF chromatin modifiers You need experimental/functional proof that the regulatory factors drive priming — this skill only provides computational epigenomic corroboration, not perturbation evidence

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has assigned primed states (e.g. via DICE FindPrimedCells) and matched scATAC-Seq profiles exist for the same or equivalent cells, and you must confirm that priming leaves an epigenomic signature.
skills.name: primed-state-cross-omic-validation
skills.search_text: primed-state-cross-omic-validation Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has assigned primed states (e.g. via DICE FindPrimedCells) and matched scATAC-Seq profiles exist for the same or equivalent cells, and you must confirm that priming leaves an epigenomic signature. No matched scATAC-Seq data exist for the cells or cell-types of interest — the article notes that SHARE-Seq-style joint profiles were unavailable for some studies, forcing an approximate assignment method The goal is to infer primed states de novo from scRNA-Seq rather than to validate already-assigned primed cells epigenomically (use DICE FindPrimedCells first) Experimental perturbation evidence is required for the regulatory factors — the study itself performed no experimental validation, only scATAC-Seq validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validate scRNA-Seq-inferred primed cell states and their regulatory factors in matched scATAC-Seq data by testing whether primed cells show higher chromatin accessibility/TF motif activity and lineage fate probability toward their assigned branch (e.g. SHARE-Seq hair-follicle TACs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Validate scRNA-Seq-inferred primed cell states and their regulatory factors in matched scATAC-Seq data by testing whether primed cells show higher chromatin accessibility/TF motif activity and lineage fate probability toward their assigned branch (e.g. SHARE-Seq hair-follicle TACs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scATAC-Seq data exist for the cells or cell-types of interest — the article notes that SHARE-Seq-style joint profiles were unavailable for some studies, forcing an approximate assignment method The goal is to infer primed states de novo from scRNA-Seq rather than to validate already-assigned primed cells epigenomically (use DICE FindPrimedCells first) Experimental perturbation evidence is required for the regulatory factors — the study itself performed no experimental validation, only scATAC-Seq validation

skills.description: Use when a normalized, log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrix must be decomposed into principal components to identify dominant directions of unwanted variation (e.g. cell-cycle effect) prior to removal or clustering.
skills.name: principal-component-analysis-implementation
skills.search_text: principal-component-analysis-implementation Use when a normalized, log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrix must be decomposed into principal components to identify dominant directions of unwanted variation (e.g. cell-cycle effect) prior to removal or clustering. The goal is to remove general hidden confounders (e.g. library-quality or batch effects) rather than the cell-cycle effect — scLVM-style latent-factor removal is the wrong target here since ccRemover is designed exclusively for the cell cycle The input matrix is not log-transformed and gene-centered, or no cell-cycle gene annotation (if_cc indicator) is available to define control vs cell-cycle gene sets Cell-cycle activity is known to be very low and the standard cutoff would miss it — the article uses a smaller cutoff C_delta = 2 for glioblastoma data instead of defaulting to C = 3 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Implements PCA on a log-transformed, gene-by-gene centered single-cell expression matrix to expose leading components of systematic variation, as in ccRemover where PCA on control genes XB yields loadings v1..v_ntop used to test for cell-cycle effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Implements PCA on a log-transformed, gene-by-gene centered single-cell expression matrix to expose leading components of systematic variation, as in ccRemover where PCA on control genes XB yields loadings v1..v_ntop used to test for cell-cycle effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to remove general hidden confounders (e.g. library-quality or batch effects) rather than the cell-cycle effect — scLVM-style latent-factor removal is the wrong target here since ccRemover is designed exclusively for the cell cycle The input matrix is not log-transformed and gene-centered, or no cell-cycle gene annotation (if_cc indicator) is available to define control vs cell-cycle gene sets Cell-cycle activity is known to be very low and the standard cutoff would miss it — the article uses a smaller cutoff C_delta = 2 for glioblastoma data instead of defaulting to C = 3

skills.description: Use when evaluating multiple spatial-domain clustering outputs (e.g., over alpha_options/beta_options/seed_options grids) and ground-truth labels are unavailable, so clustering quality must be ranked by a model-based score instead of ARI.
skills.name: principal-component-based-domain-scoring
skills.search_text: principal-component-based-domain-scoring Use when evaluating multiple spatial-domain clustering outputs (e.g., over alpha_options/beta_options/seed_options grids) and ground-truth labels are unavailable, so clustering quality must be ranked by a model-based score instead of ARI. Ground-truth annotations exist for the sample — use ARI directly rather than this proxy score Input is still a raw count matrix; the top-2000 HVG / PC preprocessing step (get_genex_data_from_10x_h5.R or get_genex_data_from_rds_ST_data.R) must run first Data is non-spatial (no spot neighborhood graph can be built), since the Potts-model prior term requires spatial coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes ScribbleDom's ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα)=q(y,Cα)∏p(yi|Ciα)p(Ciα) that scores each candidate spatial-domain clustering by combining Gaussian likelihood of gene-expression PCs, a Potts-model spatial prior, and a within-cluster PC variance penalty — enabling hyperparameter selection (alpha, beta, seed) without manual annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: Computes ScribbleDom's ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα)=q(y,Cα)∏p(yi|Ciα)p(Ciα) that scores each candidate spatial-domain clustering by combining Gaussian likelihood of gene-expression PCs, a Potts-model spatial prior, and a within-cluster PC variance penalty — enabling hyperparameter selection (alpha, beta, seed) without manual annotations.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression data (log-transformed, gene-centered) shows a suspected dominant systematic effect and you must test whether PCs are cell-cycle effects before removal, using annotated control vs cell-cycle gene sets.

skills.description: Use when approximate sequence search needs a significance cutoff on shared minimizers — e.g. a query read with a sequence-dependent number of (w,k)-minimizers must be judged against random minimizer sharing at a fixed confidence level.
skills.name: probabilistic-threshold-parameterization-for-sequence-search
skills.search_text: probabilistic-threshold-parameterization-for-sequence-search Use when approximate sequence search needs a significance cutoff on shared minimizers — e.g. a query read with a sequence-dependent number of (w,k)-minimizers must be judged against random minimizer sharing at a fixed confidence level. The query length and minimizer count are fixed and known a priori so a single hand-computed threshold suffices — the table machinery is for sequence-dependent per-read minimizer counts. The search does not use (w,k)-minimizer representation (e.g. full-text FM-index or k-mer-exact tools like COBS/Mantis without winnowing), where the Lemma 2 error model does not apply. You need a provenly exact threshold: the indirectly affected term P(Cn) is only estimable by sampling, so results carry Monte Carlo error. Reconstructs Raptor's probabilistic thresholding model (Equations 1–5 and Lemma 2) as a standalone generator of minimizer-sharing thresholds tau for (w,k)-minimizer queries, parameterized by window size w, k-mer size k, number of errors, and per-query minimizer count m. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Reconstructs Raptor's probabilistic thresholding model (Equations 1–5 and Lemma 2) as a standalone generator of minimizer-sharing thresholds tau for (w,k)-minimizer queries, parameterized by window size w, k-mer size k, number of errors, and per-query minimizer count m.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query length and minimizer count are fixed and known a priori so a single hand-computed threshold suffices — the table machinery is for sequence-dependent per-read minimizer counts. The search does not use (w,k)-minimizer representation (e.g. full-text FM-index or k-mer-exact tools like COBS/Mantis without winnowing), where the Lemma 2 error model does not apply. You need a provenly exact threshold: the indirectly affected term P(Cn) is only estimable by sampling, so results carry Monte Carlo error.

skills.search_text: profile-based-homology-search Use when building a reference database of endogenous retroviral sequences that must each be backed by detectable retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV) before downstream alignment of assembled contigs. When the goal is de novo viral discovery from raw RNAseq reads — use the viRNAtrap deep-learning pipeline instead; this skill only builds the reference HERV database When candidate sequences are already curated as intact retroviruses and only need classification against known viral genomes via blastn http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Constructs a curated database of potentially functional human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) by extracting HERVd-annotated loci from hg19, screening translated sequences against NCBI NR with blastx (E-value 1e-4), and building a MAFFT POL profile to retain only sequences carrying POL/RT, GAG, or ENV retroviral motifs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z

skills.description: Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (CPLM/ZICP) models to UMI or read-count scRNA-seq data and the index parameter p must be estimated rather than fixed, e.g. to compare gene-specific p across experimental protocols.
skills.name: profile-likelihood-index-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: profile-likelihood-index-parameter-optimization Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (CPLM/ZICP) models to UMI or read-count scRNA-seq data and the index parameter p must be estimated rather than fixed, e.g. to compare gene-specific p across experimental protocols. When zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes — the article notes Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' When p can be fixed a priori and only regression coefficients are needed — the full profile-likelihood optimization is unnecessary overhead When the goal is a simple ad-hoc normalization/transformation rather than model-based DE testing — the paper argues the offset-based Tweedie model 'bypass[es] the need for an adhoc normalization and/or transformation prior to DE testing' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Optimizes the Tweedie index (power) parameter p and dispersion phi for per-gene Compound Poisson Linear Models fitted to scRNA-seq counts, by profiling out regression coefficients and maximizing the Tweedie log-likelihood subject to phi > 0 and p in (1, 2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Optimizes the Tweedie index (power) parameter p and dispersion phi for per-gene Compound Poisson Linear Models fitted to scRNA-seq counts, by profiling out regression coefficients and maximizing the Tweedie log-likelihood subject to phi > 0 and p in (1, 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes — the article notes Tweedieverse 'is not architected for the situation when zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of the genes' When p can be fixed a priori and only regression coefficients are needed — the full profile-likelihood optimization is unnecessary overhead When the goal is a simple ad-hoc normalization/transformation rather than model-based DE testing — the paper argues the offset-based Tweedie model 'bypass[es] the need for an adhoc normalization and/or transformation prior to DE testing'

skills.description: Use when you need to infer signaling pathway activity (e.g. MAPK, PI3K, NFkB, TGFb, JAK-STAT) from bulk or single-cell gene expression, especially in perturbation experiments where pathway activity must be validated against controls or phospho-protein measurements.
skills.name: progeny-model-application
skills.search_text: progeny-model-application Use when you need to infer signaling pathway activity (e.g. MAPK, PI3K, NFkB, TGFb, JAK-STAT) from bulk or single-cell gene expression, especially in perturbation experiments where pathway activity must be validated against controls or phospho-protein measurements. The pathway of interest has no PROGENy signature — the resource covers only the 11 curated pathways (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) You need tissue-specific pathway activity in a well-characterized context — the article notes specific-tissue signatures may more closely reflect activation than the consensus PROGENy signatures You want to quantify the expression level (abundance) of pathway members rather than pathway activity — the article warns the expression level of a pathway should not be interpreted as its activity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Compute PROGENy pathway activity scores by taking weighted linear combinations of normalized gene expression using the Pathway RespOnsive GENes signatures, then compare perturbation conditions against controls to infer signaling pathway activity from transcriptomics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Compute PROGENy pathway activity scores by taking weighted linear combinations of normalized gene expression using the Pathway RespOnsive GENes signatures, then compare perturbation conditions against controls to infer signaling pathway activity from transcriptomics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathway of interest has no PROGENy signature — the resource covers only the 11 curated pathways (EGFR, Hypoxia, JAK-STAT, MAPK, NFkB, p53/DDR, PI3K, TGFb, Trail, VEGF/PDGF) You need tissue-specific pathway activity in a well-characterized context — the article notes specific-tissue signatures may more closely reflect activation than the consensus PROGENy signatures You want to quantify the expression level (abundance) of pathway members rather than pathway activity — the article warns the expression level of a pathway should not be interpreted as its activity

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples with survival and treatment-response metadata must be stratified by a published prognostic gene signature into survival-differentiated high/low risk groups.
skills.name: prognostic-risk-score-computation
skills.search_text: prognostic-risk-score-computation Use when bulk RNA-seq samples with survival and treatment-response metadata must be stratified by a published prognostic gene signature into survival-differentiated high/low risk groups. Input is single-cell or already-deconvolved cell-abundance data rather than a bulk RNA-seq matrix with human gene symbol rows No per-gene hazard ratios are available for the candidate signature, so the log10(HR)-weighted risk score cannot be computed Samples lack survival endpoints and treatment-response labels, making Kaplan-Meier and Wilcoxon validation impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute a per-sample prognostic risk score from a published 33-gene signature by summing log10(hazard ratio) weighted log2(x+1)-transformed expression, then validate it by median-split Kaplan-Meier survival separation and responder/non-responder comparison, as applied to GSE78220 anti-PD-1 melanoma data in the DCNet study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Compute a per-sample prognostic risk score from a published 33-gene signature by summing log10(hazard ratio) weighted log2(x+1)-transformed expression, then validate it by median-split Kaplan-Meier survival separation and responder/non-responder comparison, as applied to GSE78220 anti-PD-1 melanoma data in the DCNet study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or already-deconvolved cell-abundance data rather than a bulk RNA-seq matrix with human gene symbol rows No per-gene hazard ratios are available for the candidate signature, so the log10(HR)-weighted risk score cannot be computed Samples lack survival endpoints and treatment-response labels, making Kaplan-Meier and Wilcoxon validation impossible

skills.description: Use when a candidate gene signature identified from single-cell or spatial transcriptomics must be validated as a prognostic indicator in a bulk RNA-seq cohort with survival metadata (e.g., TCGA KIRC overall survival).
skills.name: prognostic-signature-benchmarking
skills.search_text: prognostic-signature-benchmarking Use when a candidate gene signature identified from single-cell or spatial transcriptomics must be validated as a prognostic indicator in a bulk RNA-seq cohort with survival metadata (e.g., TCGA KIRC overall survival). Input is single-cell or spatial data without matched bulk cohort survival metadata — the skill requires bulk RNA-seq plus overall-survival information per patient The cohort lacks enough patients in both median-split groups to support a meaningful log-rank comparison Evaluating hematologic tumor signatures via the upstream Cancer-Finder identification step — the article states it is not recommended for hematologic tumor data (survival validation itself is unaffected, but the signature source is) Evaluates whether a gene signature (here the 10-gene ccRCC interface signature: NDRG1, TAGLN, MALAT1, IGKC, IGHA1, IGHG4, IGLC2, IGHG3, SOD2, KRT19) predicts patient survival by scoring bulk RNA-seq cohorts with ssGSEA, median-splitting patients, and comparing Kaplan-Meier curves with a two-sided log-rank test, optionally benchmarking against competing signatures such as Hallmark EMT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a gene signature (here the 10-gene ccRCC interface signature: NDRG1, TAGLN, MALAT1, IGKC, IGHA1, IGHG4, IGLC2, IGHG3, SOD2, KRT19) predicts patient survival by scoring bulk RNA-seq cohorts with ssGSEA, median-splitting patients, and comparing Kaplan-Meier curves with a two-sided log-rank test, optionally benchmarking against competing signatures such as Hallmark EMT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or spatial data without matched bulk cohort survival metadata — the skill requires bulk RNA-seq plus overall-survival information per patient The cohort lacks enough patients in both median-split groups to support a meaningful log-rank comparison Evaluating hematologic tumor signatures via the upstream Cancer-Finder identification step — the article states it is not recommended for hematologic tumor data (survival validation itself is unaffected, but the signature source is)

skills.description: Use when stage-resolved epithelial scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., .h5ad per normal mucosa, polyp, tumor, CAG, IM, EGC stage) are available and the goal is to test whether predicted malignancy increases monotonically across carcinogenesis stages.
skills.name: progression-stage-stratified-analysis
skills.search_text: progression-stage-stratified-analysis Use when stage-resolved epithelial scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., .h5ad per normal mucosa, polyp, tumor, CAG, IM, EGC stage) are available and the goal is to test whether predicted malignancy increases monotonically across carcinogenesis stages. Input is normal (non-cancerous) tissue or a lineage that has not been identified as the cancerous epithelial lineage — the tool requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types and is restricted to cancerous lineages Cancers with unknown or controversial cell of origin, such as synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors, where capabilities are untested The goal is de novo malignant-cell discovery without pretrained features — alternative tools like ikarus, Cancer-Finder, or CopyKAT would be required instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Applies the pretrained scMalignantFinder classifier stage-by-stage across colorectal and gastric carcinogenesis scRNA-seq datasets (normal mucosa → polyps/CAG → IM → tumors/EGC) to quantify how the fraction of epithelial cells predicted 'Malignant' and their mean malignancy probability change with progression stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Applies the pretrained scMalignantFinder classifier stage-by-stage across colorectal and gastric carcinogenesis scRNA-seq datasets (normal mucosa → polyps/CAG → IM → tumors/EGC) to quantify how the fraction of epithelial cells predicted 'Malignant' and their mean malignancy probability change with progression stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is normal (non-cancerous) tissue or a lineage that has not been identified as the cancerous epithelial lineage — the tool requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types and is restricted to cancerous lineages Cancers with unknown or controversial cell of origin, such as synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors, where capabilities are untested The goal is de novo malignant-cell discovery without pretrained features — alternative tools like ikarus, Cancer-Finder, or CopyKAT would be required instead

skills.description: Decision support for choosing which combination of biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, Kinase) to embed in an SCA/SSCA latent space when single-knowledge spaces fail to reconstruct specific single-cell clusters.
skills.name: progressive-biological-knowledge-integration-analysis
skills.search_text: progressive-biological-knowledge-integration-analysis Decision support for choosing which combination of biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, Kinase) to embed in an SCA/SSCA latent space when single-knowledge spaces fail to reconstruct specific single-cell clusters. When the goal is cluster discovery itself rather than functional reconstruction of already-defined clusters — SCA reconstructs only specific clusters of a pre-existing clustering. When no pre-computed cluster assignments (e.g. clusters 1-5 of setA) are available to evaluate QCC/QCM against. When working with data where miRNAs must be directly quantified alongside mRNAs — it is currently not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuits cannot be directly measured. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Progressively combines biological knowledge groups (experimentally validated TF targets, miRNA targets, kinase targets, and cancer-related immune signatures) into single SSCA latent spaces (TF+miRNA, TF+miRNA+IS, TF+miRNA+IS+Kinase) and evaluates whether combined spaces improve cluster reconstruction (QCM/QCC) on the setA blood-cell scRNAseq dataset versus each knowledge group alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Progressively combines biological knowledge groups (experimentally validated TF targets, miRNA targets, kinase targets, and cancer-related immune signatures) into single SSCA latent spaces (TF+miRNA, TF+miRNA+IS, TF+miRNA+IS+Kinase) and evaluates whether combined spaces improve cluster reconstruction (QCM/QCC) on the setA blood-cell scRNAseq dataset versus each knowledge group alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cluster discovery itself rather than functional reconstruction of already-defined clusters — SCA reconstructs only specific clusters of a pre-existing clustering. When no pre-computed cluster assignments (e.g. clusters 1-5 of setA) are available to evaluate QCC/QCM against. When working with data where miRNAs must be directly quantified alongside mRNAs — it is currently not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuits cannot be directly measured.

skills.description: Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) must be merged into one hierarchical classifier, especially when some batches may lack cell populations and you need to assess whether the learned tree stays stable.
skills.name: progressive-learning-cell-annotation-across-batches
skills.search_text: progressive-learning-cell-annotation-across-batches Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) must be merged into one hierarchical classifier, especially when some batches may lack cell populations and you need to assess whether the learned tree stays stable. Datasets have not been aligned/batch-corrected first — scHPL is explicitly 'not a batch correction tool', so mistakes may stem from erroneous alignment rather than mismatches created by scHPL Cell populations violate the tree assumption, e.g. dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes, where a hierarchical tree is not adequate The goal is annotating a single pre-labeled reference against one query dataset with marker genes (methods like SCINA or Garnett assume marker-gene priors and are a different paradigm) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Progressively learn a hierarchical classification tree of cell identities across multiple annotated batches/datasets using scHPL, matching cell populations across batches and training a per-node classifier (linear SVM or one-class SVM) that can also flag unknown populations. Useful for combining datasets annotated at different resolutions and testing how batch composition affects tree stability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Progressively learn a hierarchical classification tree of cell identities across multiple annotated batches/datasets using scHPL, matching cell populations across batches and training a per-node classifier (linear SVM or one-class SVM) that can also flag unknown populations. Useful for combining datasets annotated at different resolutions and testing how batch composition affects tree stability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have not been aligned/batch-corrected first — scHPL is explicitly 'not a batch correction tool', so mistakes may stem from erroneous alignment rather than mismatches created by scHPL Cell populations violate the tree assumption, e.g. dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes, where a hierarchical tree is not adequate The goal is annotating a single pre-labeled reference against one query dataset with marker genes (methods like SCINA or Garnett assume marker-gene priors and are a different paradigm)

skills.description: Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., from different labs or protocols, such as Saunders, Zeisel, Tabula Muris brain data) must be combined into one consistent cell-population hierarchy, especially when annotation terminologies differ between studies.
skills.name: progressive-learning-tree-construction
skills.search_text: progressive-learning-tree-construction Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., from different labs or protocols, such as Saunders, Zeisel, Tabula Muris brain data) must be combined into one consistent cell-population hierarchy, especially when annotation terminologies differ between studies. Datasets are not yet batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL is not a batch correction tool and mismatches may result from erroneous alignment The cell populations violate a hierarchical relationship, e.g., dedifferentiation like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A standardized constant terminology across datasets is assumed available and simple name-based matching would suffice (scHPL's value is discovering relationships names cannot) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Construct a hierarchical classification tree of cell identities by progressively learning relationships between cell populations across multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets with scHPL, adding datasets sequentially so that populations are matched across studies and merged into a shared hierarchy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Construct a hierarchical classification tree of cell identities by progressively learning relationships between cell populations across multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets with scHPL, adding datasets sequentially so that populations are matched across studies and merged into a shared hierarchy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not yet batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL is not a batch correction tool and mismatches may result from erroneous alignment The cell populations violate a hierarchical relationship, e.g., dedifferentiation like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A standardized constant terminology across datasets is assumed available and simple name-based matching would suffice (scHPL's value is discovering relationships names cannot)

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate how faithfully a method projects held-out scRNA-seq data onto a reference atlas and how accurately it transfers cell-state labels, relative to alternative mapping tools.
skills.name: projection-accuracy-metrics-evaluation
skills.search_text: projection-accuracy-metrics-evaluation Use when you need to quantitatively validate how faithfully a method projects held-out scRNA-seq data onto a reference atlas and how accurately it transfers cell-state labels, relative to alternative mapping tools. The goal is annotating a genuinely new query dataset rather than benchmarking projection fidelity — use Run.ProjecTILs label transfer directly instead of cross-validation scoring. The query contains cell states absent from the reference (e.g. γδ T cells, under-represented CD4+ TILs), where projection-accuracy metrics against reference coordinates are not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks a reference-mapping method by leave-half-samples-out cross-validation on a reference TIL atlas, scoring projection accuracy (fraction of cells landing within one UMAP unit / five PCA units of original coordinates) and classification accuracy of cell-state labels against competing methods such as Azimuth/Seurat 4 and scmap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks a reference-mapping method by leave-half-samples-out cross-validation on a reference TIL atlas, scoring projection accuracy (fraction of cells landing within one UMAP unit / five PCA units of original coordinates) and classification accuracy of cell-state labels against competing methods such as Azimuth/Seurat 4 and scmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotating a genuinely new query dataset rather than benchmarking projection fidelity — use Run.ProjecTILs label transfer directly instead of cross-validation scoring. The query contains cell states absent from the reference (e.g. γδ T cells, under-represented CD4+ TILs), where projection-accuracy metrics against reference coordinates are not meaningful.

skills.description: Use when a cohort of base-level RNA-seq pileup matrices at one gene must be screened unsupervised for samples with anomalous coverage shapes (splicing, intron retention, deletions, ATS/ATT) rather than differential expression.
skills.name: projection-pursuit-outlier-scoring
skills.search_text: projection-pursuit-outlier-scoring Use when a cohort of base-level RNA-seq pileup matrices at one gene must be screened unsupervised for samples with anomalous coverage shapes (splicing, intron retention, deletions, ATS/ATT) rather than differential expression. The question is differential expression of known transcripts or junction-level isoform quantification — methods like DEXSeq, SpliceTrap, MISO, rMATS, or DiffSplice target that; SCISSOR targets base-level shape anomalies. The cohort is small (fewer than ~30 samples); empirically 30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully to date. Input is already a compressed expression/feature count table — SCISSOR requires intact, uncompressed base-level pileup data to retain shape information. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 SCISSOR's two-step statistical procedure that scores sample outliers in base-level RNA-seq coverage by exploring all possible low-dimensional projections (global shape change detection) and then searching the residual space after subtracting a gene-shape model (local shape change detection). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: SCISSOR's two-step statistical procedure that scores sample outliers in base-level RNA-seq coverage by exploring all possible low-dimensional projections (global shape change detection) and then searching the residual space after subtracting a gene-shape model (local shape change detection).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is differential expression of known transcripts or junction-level isoform quantification — methods like DEXSeq, SpliceTrap, MISO, rMATS, or DiffSplice target that; SCISSOR targets base-level shape anomalies. The cohort is small (fewer than ~30 samples); empirically 30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully to date. Input is already a compressed expression/feature count table — SCISSOR requires intact, uncompressed base-level pileup data to retain shape information.

skills.description: Use when single-cell marker-intensity data from multiplexed imaging (e.g. CyCIF) must be scored per cell for proliferation vs. cell-cycle arrest, to derive the fraction of a cell type (e.g. SOX10+ tumor cells) with MPI = 1.
skills.name: proliferation-index-piecewise-scoring
skills.search_text: proliferation-index-piecewise-scoring Use when single-cell marker-intensity data from multiplexed imaging (e.g. CyCIF) must be scored per cell for proliferation vs. cell-cycle arrest, to derive the fraction of a cell type (e.g. SOX10+ tumor cells) with MPI = 1. Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery that has not yet been converted to single-cell data — run MCMICRO (or equivalent) first, since 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells' Goal is spatial region assignment (immune-isolated vs. immune-rich subregions, tumor isolation index) rather than per-cell proliferation scoring — use assignPointsToRegions/getRegionComposition instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Computes a multivariate proliferation index (MPI) per cell with SpatialCells' getMPI, combining gated mitosis/proliferation markers (PHH3, Ki67, PCNA, MCM2) and cell-cycle arrest markers (p21, p27) into a piecewise {-1, 0, 1} label. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Computes a multivariate proliferation index (MPI) per cell with SpatialCells' getMPI, combining gated mitosis/proliferation markers (PHH3, Ki67, PCNA, MCM2) and cell-cycle arrest markers (p21, p27) into a piecewise {-1, 0, 1} label.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery that has not yet been converted to single-cell data — run MCMICRO (or equivalent) first, since 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells' Goal is spatial region assignment (immune-isolated vs. immune-rich subregions, tumor isolation index) rather than per-cell proliferation scoring — use assignPointsToRegions/getRegionComposition instead

skills.description: Use when modeling cell fate bias from time-series scRNA-seq data (e.g., day-2/4/6 lineage-tracing points) and empirical or gene-expression-derived growth rates are available to weight the learned differentiation landscape.
skills.name: proliferation-weight-incorporation-in-fate-modeling
skills.search_text: proliferation-weight-incorporation-in-fate-modeling Use when modeling cell fate bias from time-series scRNA-seq data (e.g., day-2/4/6 lineage-tracing points) and empirical or gene-expression-derived growth rates are available to weight the learned differentiation landscape. The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state — PRESCIENT requires this constraint for training No proliferation estimates are obtainable (empirical or expression-derived) and only the no-growth model can be fit, since the improvement depends on growth-rate quality The analysis goal is per-gene interpretation rather than fate-bias prediction — information about individual genes is lost in the PCA transformation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Incorporate empirically measured or expression-derived cell proliferation rates as growth weights into PRESCIENT's potential-energy model to improve clonal fate-bias prediction on longitudinal scRNA-seq data such as the Weinreb hematopoiesis lineage-tracing dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Incorporate empirically measured or expression-derived cell proliferation rates as growth weights into PRESCIENT's potential-energy model to improve clonal fate-bias prediction on longitudinal scRNA-seq data such as the Weinreb hematopoiesis lineage-tracing dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset's final time point is not at steady-state — PRESCIENT requires this constraint for training No proliferation estimates are obtainable (empirical or expression-derived) and only the no-growth model can be fit, since the improvement depends on growth-rate quality The analysis goal is per-gene interpretation rather than fate-bias prediction — information about individual genes is lost in the PCA transformation

skills.description: Use when you need promoter-restricted TF motif activity from scRNA-seq data — e.g. reproducing ISMARA-like motif dynamics or correlating a TF's motif activity with its own mRNA across a cell cycle trajectory.
skills.name: promoter-binding-site-mapping
skills.search_text: promoter-binding-site-mapping Use when you need promoter-restricted TF motif activity from scRNA-seq data — e.g. reproducing ISMARA-like motif dynamics or correlating a TF's motif activity with its own mRNA across a cell cycle trajectory. The dataset lacks unspliced read counts (no scVelo 'Mu' layer), since the linear model is fit on unspliced counts No genome-mapped binding-site annotations (GFF) are available for the organism, so promoter windows cannot be defined Cells are not ordered along a dynamic process (e.g. no cell_cycle_theta), so motif-activity dynamics cannot be correlated with expression http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Maps transcription factor binding motifs to promoters by restricting motif-predicted binding sites (e.g. Swiss Regulon Motevo GFF annotations) to TSS +/- 1 kb windows, then quantifying motif activity from scRNA-seq unspliced counts so promoter-level motif activity can be correlated with TF mRNA dynamics (e.g. Ybx1 across the cell cycle). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Maps transcription factor binding motifs to promoters by restricting motif-predicted binding sites (e.g. Swiss Regulon Motevo GFF annotations) to TSS +/- 1 kb windows, then quantifying motif activity from scRNA-seq unspliced counts so promoter-level motif activity can be correlated with TF mRNA dynamics (e.g. Ybx1 across the cell cycle).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks unspliced read counts (no scVelo 'Mu' layer), since the linear model is fit on unspliced counts No genome-mapped binding-site annotations (GFF) are available for the organism, so promoter windows cannot be defined Cells are not ordered along a dynamic process (e.g. no cell_cycle_theta), so motif-activity dynamics cannot be correlated with expression

skills.description: Use when running FateCompass or an ISMARA-style linear model of gene regulation on scRNA-seq and you must build/load the TF binding-site matrix and align it to expressed genes in an adata object.
skills.name: promoter-binding-site-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: promoter-binding-site-matrix-processing Use when running FateCompass or an ISMARA-style linear model of gene regulation on scRNA-seq and you must build/load the TF binding-site matrix and align it to expressed genes in an adata object. Your regulatory sites come from distal enhancers or long-range interactions (e.g. scATAC-seq maps) — FateCompass only considers binding sites in promoter regions You want a dynamic model of TF activity over time and already have validated motif activities (the matrix alone does not model dynamics; it feeds the linear model) Input gene identifiers in the binding-site matrix cannot be mapped to the adata gene names — alignment will silently drop genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepares and validates the TF binding-site matrix — the FateCompass input whose columns are TFs/motifs and whose rows are expressed genes with promoter binding sites — so it aligns with a pre-processed adata object before TF activities are inferred with the linear model of gene regulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Prepares and validates the TF binding-site matrix — the FateCompass input whose columns are TFs/motifs and whose rows are expressed genes with promoter binding sites — so it aligns with a pre-processed adata object before TF activities are inferred with the linear model of gene regulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your regulatory sites come from distal enhancers or long-range interactions (e.g. scATAC-seq maps) — FateCompass only considers binding sites in promoter regions You want a dynamic model of TF activity over time and already have validated motif activities (the matrix alone does not model dynamics; it feeds the linear model) Input gene identifiers in the binding-site matrix cannot be mapped to the adata gene names — alignment will silently drop genes

skills.description: Use when csRNA-seq (or TSS-seq) peaks have been called (e.g. with HOMER findPeaks on GSE221852 Drosophila embryo or GSE135498 K562/BMDM data) and ±100 bp TSS-centered sequences are needed as FASTA input for ElemeNT 2023 element detection.
skills.name: promoter-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: promoter-sequence-extraction Use when csRNA-seq (or TSS-seq) peaks have been called (e.g. with HOMER findPeaks on GSE221852 Drosophila embryo or GSE135498 K562/BMDM data) and ±100 bp TSS-centered sequences are needed as FASTA input for ElemeNT 2023 element detection. Input is already a FASTA file of candidate promoter sequences — ElemeNT 2023 can be run directly without re-extraction. The goal is element detection outside a core promoter context (e.g. generic DNA-binding site search); ElemeNT 2023 itself can search user-defined motifs, so full TSS-centered extraction is not required. The input is already an expanded, gene-symbol-level LR pair table — re-expansion and ortholog mapping would duplicate records or break identifiers The goal is per-dataset inference of significant LR associations from scRNA-seq expression (use CommPath's findLRpairs on a CommPath object instead of rebuilding the reference database) The analysis requires pathway-level filtering of LR interactions (findLRpath/filterLR), which operates downstream of the reference database rather than on the raw CellPhoneDB/FANTOM5 sources http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constructs CommPath's curated ligand-receptor reference database by parsing CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 resources and expanding heteromeric protein complexes into individual (ligand, receptor) gene-pair interactions, mapped to official gene symbols per supported species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.10.028
skills.summary: Constructs CommPath's curated ligand-receptor reference database by parsing CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 resources and expanding heteromeric protein complexes into individual (ligand, receptor) gene-pair interactions, mapped to official gene symbols per supported species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an expanded, gene-symbol-level LR pair table — re-expansion and ortholog mapping would duplicate records or break identifiers The goal is per-dataset inference of significant LR associations from scRNA-seq expression (use CommPath's findLRpairs on a CommPath object instead of rebuilding the reference database) The analysis requires pathway-level filtering of LR interactions (findLRpath/filterLR), which operates downstream of the reference database rather than on the raw CellPhoneDB/FANTOM5 sources

skills.description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway files are loaded in Cytoscape via KEGGScape and nodes whose name strings contain more than one gene (functional homolog or OR-group nodes) display only the first gene, hiding the others.
skills.name: protein-complex-group-modeling
skills.search_text: protein-complex-group-modeling Use when KEGG KGML pathway files are loaded in Cytoscape via KEGGScape and nodes whose name strings contain more than one gene (functional homolog or OR-group nodes) display only the first gene, hiding the others. Glycan-related KEGG pathways (mostly category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism') that use 'line' link nodes instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded even if they contain multiple genes and cannot be coloured in Cytoscape Pathways where only the first listed gene per node is an acceptable rendering, i.e. when no functional homolog (OR-group) expansion is needed When the goal is collapsing multi-gene nodes into a single expression value rather than expanding and displaying every gene (that is FunHoP's count-aggregation step, a separate concern) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Expands KEGG KGML pathway nodes that contain multiple functional homologs by parsing the KGML XML with ElementTree and regrouping every hidden gene into a common 'group' node, reusing KEGG's protein-complex (AND-group) representation so Cytoscape/KEGGScape renders all responsible genes instead of only the first listed one. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: Expands KEGG KGML pathway nodes that contain multiple functional homologs by parsing the KGML XML with ElementTree and regrouping every hidden gene into a common 'group' node, reusing KEGG's protein-complex (AND-group) representation so Cytoscape/KEGGScape renders all responsible genes instead of only the first listed one.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Glycan-related KEGG pathways (mostly category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism') that use 'line' link nodes instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded even if they contain multiple genes and cannot be coloured in Cytoscape Pathways where only the first listed gene per node is an acceptable rendering, i.e. when no functional homolog (OR-group) expansion is needed When the goal is collapsing multi-gene nodes into a single expression value rather than expanding and displaying every gene (that is FunHoP's count-aggregation step, a separate concern)

skills.search_text: protein-embedding-distance-rank-statistics Use when two species' protein sequences and ProtBERT embeddings are available and you need to quantify how embedding-based gene matches agree with BLAST -hit assignments and ranks (e.g., for TACTiCS gene-similarity input validation).
