skills.summary: Benchmark gene-matching by ProtBERT protein-embedding distances against BLAST sequence-alignment best hits across species (human vs mouse motor cortex datasets), quantifying top-1 agreement, rank agreement, and expression-correlation arbitration of discordant genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a gene similarity distance matrix and only need to run/evaluate TACTiCS cell-type matching — supply the matrix directly to the TACTiCS class instead Your goal is TACTiCS cell-type classification or transfer-learning label propagation across species — this skill covers only the gene-matching benchmark, not the downstream neural network or transfer steps Genes lack a one-to-one BLAST ortholog match between the species — the 94%/13,935-gene statistics apply only to one-to-one human–mouse matches

skills.description: Use when preparing cross-species single-cell comparisons that need a gene similarity distance matrix derived from protein sequence embeddings rather than sequence alignment tools like BLAST.
skills.name: protein-embedding-gene-matching
skills.search_text: protein-embedding-gene-matching Use when preparing cross-species single-cell comparisons that need a gene similarity distance matrix derived from protein sequence embeddings rather than sequence alignment tools like BLAST. The analysis is a single-species scRNA-seq analysis with no need for cross-species gene orthology or a gene similarity distance matrix A downstream method other than TACTiCS requires BLAST-style alignment scores instead of embedding-based distances, and the comparison target explicitly benchmarks BLAST-based gene matching Precomputed protein embeddings for the species pair are already available in the Zenodo deposit, making regeneration redundant (though reuse is preferred over recompute) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Match genes across two species by embedding their protein sequences with a natural language processing model (transformers-based, e.g. ProtBERT) and computing a gene similarity distance matrix, which TACTiCS uses to align cross-species cell types. This NLP-based gene matching yields better cell type matches than BLAST within TACTiCS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Match genes across two species by embedding their protein sequences with a natural language processing model (transformers-based, e.g. ProtBERT) and computing a gene similarity distance matrix, which TACTiCS uses to align cross-species cell types. This NLP-based gene matching yields better cell type matches than BLAST within TACTiCS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is a single-species scRNA-seq analysis with no need for cross-species gene orthology or a gene similarity distance matrix A downstream method other than TACTiCS requires BLAST-style alignment scores instead of embedding-based distances, and the comparison target explicitly benchmarks BLAST-based gene matching Precomputed protein embeddings for the species pair are already available in the Zenodo deposit, making regeneration redundant (though reuse is preferred over recompute)

skills.description: Use when you have raw cell and empty-droplet ADT UMI matrices (e.g., Cell Ranger filtered/raw barcodes from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) and need the log(pseudocount=10) transform required before dsb step I ambient standardization.
skills.name: protein-expression-matrix-log-transformation
skills.search_text: protein-expression-matrix-log-transformation Use when you have raw cell and empty-droplet ADT UMI matrices (e.g., Cell Ranger filtered/raw barcodes from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) and need the log(pseudocount=10) transform required before dsb step I ambient standardization. The ADT matrix is already dsb-normalized, CLR-normalized, or otherwise log/scaled transformed — re-transforming would double-apply the pseudocount The input is mRNA/RNA UMI data rather than antibody-derived-tag protein counts; dsb normalization is designed for ADT noise structure (ambient antibody + cell-intrinsic technical noise) No background/empty droplets exist and you need a plug-in transform without considering dsb's alternative no-empty-drops workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Log-transforms raw ADT/protein UMI count matrices from droplet-based CITE-seq data with pseudocount 10, the prerequisite step for dsb ambient-noise standardization, which subsequently rescales cells by per-protein empty-droplet mean (mu_N) and SD (sigma_N). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Log-transforms raw ADT/protein UMI count matrices from droplet-based CITE-seq data with pseudocount 10, the prerequisite step for dsb ambient-noise standardization, which subsequently rescales cells by per-protein empty-droplet mean (mu_N) and SD (sigma_N).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ADT matrix is already dsb-normalized, CLR-normalized, or otherwise log/scaled transformed — re-transforming would double-apply the pseudocount The input is mRNA/RNA UMI data rather than antibody-derived-tag protein counts; dsb normalization is designed for ADT noise structure (ambient antibody + cell-intrinsic technical noise) No background/empty droplets exist and you need a plug-in transform without considering dsb's alternative no-empty-drops workflow

skills.description: Use when a mosaic integration layout leaves feature entities (e.g., genes or proteins) unconnected by any shared data matrix, so scMoMaT would otherwise receive None placeholders for a modality in some batches.
skills.name: protein-gene-mapping-count-projection
skills.search_text: protein-gene-mapping-count-projection Use when a mosaic integration layout leaves feature entities (e.g., genes or proteins) unconnected by any shared data matrix, so scMoMaT would otherwise receive None placeholders for a modality in some batches. When every feature entity is already connected by jointly profiled data matrices and no None placeholders remain in the counts dictionary When the protein panel lacks a valid 1:1 gene counterpart for a protein (the projection relies on 1:1 mapping only) When the goal is cross-modality feature relationship learning itself — the paper defers feature representations to future work rather than providing this http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Generates pseudo-count matrices for mosaic integration: a pseudo-scRNA-seq gene-activity matrix from scATAC-seq peaks (Seurat/LIGER-like procedure) and pseudo-protein counts from scRNA-seq via a 1:1 protein-gene mapping, filling the None placeholders in scMoMaT's counts dictionary when a batch lacks a modality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2
skills.summary: Generates pseudo-count matrices for mosaic integration: a pseudo-scRNA-seq gene-activity matrix from scATAC-seq peaks (Seurat/LIGER-like procedure) and pseudo-protein counts from scRNA-seq via a 1:1 protein-gene mapping, filling the None placeholders in scMoMaT's counts dictionary when a batch lacks a modality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When every feature entity is already connected by jointly profiled data matrices and no None placeholders remain in the counts dictionary When the protein panel lacks a valid 1:1 gene counterpart for a protein (the projection relies on 1:1 mapping only) When the goal is cross-modality feature relationship learning itself — the paper defers feature representations to future work rather than providing this

skills.description: Use when a SCANet co-expression module or GRN (e.g. M11 monocyte network or M4 ISC hub network at correlation ≥ 0.8) must be converted to UniProt identifiers before drug–target interaction queries.
skills.name: protein-identifier-mapping-uniprot
skills.search_text: protein-identifier-mapping-uniprot Use when a SCANet co-expression module or GRN (e.g. M11 monocyte network or M4 ISC hub network at correlation ≥ 0.8) must be converted to UniProt identifiers before drug–target interaction queries. The analysis goal is upstream network inference (co-expression modules, hub detection, GRN reconstruction) rather than drug repurposing — identifier mapping to UniProt is only the entry point of the drug–target query step. The input scRNA-seq data are not from human tissue; Drugst.One links the human interactome to drug–target databases, so non-human gene identifiers are out of scope. Genes are already provided as UniProt IDs and no drug–target interaction query (NeDRex/DrugBank/DrugCentral/ChEMBL/DGIdb) is planned, making the mapping step redundant. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps gene symbols from a SCANet-derived co-expression module (GCN or GRN) to a primary common protein identifier — UniProt ID, plus Entrez/Ensembl — via the Drugst.One package, as the prerequisite step for querying drug–target interaction databases and extracting repurposing candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Maps gene symbols from a SCANet-derived co-expression module (GCN or GRN) to a primary common protein identifier — UniProt ID, plus Entrez/Ensembl — via the Drugst.One package, as the prerequisite step for querying drug–target interaction databases and extracting repurposing candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is upstream network inference (co-expression modules, hub detection, GRN reconstruction) rather than drug repurposing — identifier mapping to UniProt is only the entry point of the drug–target query step. The input scRNA-seq data are not from human tissue; Drugst.One links the human interactome to drug–target databases, so non-human gene identifiers are out of scope. Genes are already provided as UniProt IDs and no drug–target interaction query (NeDRex/DrugBank/DrugCentral/ChEMBL/DGIdb) is planned, making the mapping step redundant.

skills.description: Use when Step 1 of DELVE must be reproduced on a preprocessed .h5ad single-cell object (e.g., 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features) to identify temporally co-expressed dynamic feature modules and the dynamic seed.
skills.name: protein-imaging-feature-dynamic-seed-recovery
skills.search_text: protein-imaging-feature-dynamic-seed-recovery Use when Step 1 of DELVE must be reproduced on a preprocessed .h5ad single-cell object (e.g., 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features) to identify temporally co-expressed dynamic feature modules and the dynamic seed. The goal is benchmarking DELVE against twelve alternative feature selection methods — use the delve_benchmark package (fs class with run_delve_fs, laplacian_score_fs, etc.) instead of reconstructing Step 1 manually Supervised feature selection is acceptable because manual annotations (e.g., cell types) are available; DELVE targets unsupervised settings where such labels are unavailable The input is raw or unnormalized data — this skill presumes a preprocessed .h5ad object such as those distributed on the Zenodo repository http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reconstructs Step 1 of DELVE (dynamic seed selection) on imaging-derived single-cell features: it builds a k-NN neighborhood graph, sketches prototypical neighborhoods with Kernel Herding, clusters features by their average pairwise change in expression, and applies a variance-based permutation test to recover the dynamically-expressed seed module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs Step 1 of DELVE (dynamic seed selection) on imaging-derived single-cell features: it builds a k-NN neighborhood graph, sketches prototypical neighborhoods with Kernel Herding, clusters features by their average pairwise change in expression, and applies a variance-based permutation test to recover the dynamically-expressed seed module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking DELVE against twelve alternative feature selection methods — use the delve_benchmark package (fs class with run_delve_fs, laplacian_score_fs, etc.) instead of reconstructing Step 1 manually Supervised feature selection is acceptable because manual annotations (e.g., cell types) are available; DELVE targets unsupervised settings where such labels are unavailable The input is raw or unnormalized data — this skill presumes a preprocessed .h5ad object such as those distributed on the Zenodo repository

skills.description: Use when analyzing single-cell protein immunofluorescence imaging measurements (stored as .h5ad, e.g. adata_RPE.h5ad) where the full feature panel includes noisy/irrelevant measurements and the goal is to identify features tied to cell cycle progression or other trajectories without labels.
skills.name: protein-immunofluorescence-imaging-analysis
skills.search_text: protein-immunofluorescence-imaging-analysis Use when analyzing single-cell protein immunofluorescence imaging measurements (stored as .h5ad, e.g. adata_RPE.h5ad) where the full feature panel includes noisy/irrelevant measurements and the goal is to identify features tied to cell cycle progression or other trajectories without labels. The input is already a curated, noise-free feature table where all measurements are known to be trajectory-relevant — unsupervised selection adds little over direct modeling. Supervised annotations are available and inexpensive, and the goal is pure prediction rather than discovering an unsupervised feature subset. The data are bulk measurements or lack per-cell resolution, since the methods rely on single-cell cell-similarity graphs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Unsupervised feature selection and trajectory analysis on iterative protein immunofluorescence imaging data (e.g. the RPE 4i cell-cycle dataset of 2759 cells x 241 imaging features), using DELVE to pick trajectory-preserving features from noisy measurement panels and evaluating them against cell-cycle phase and age annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Unsupervised feature selection and trajectory analysis on iterative protein immunofluorescence imaging data (e.g. the RPE 4i cell-cycle dataset of 2759 cells x 241 imaging features), using DELVE to pick trajectory-preserving features from noisy measurement panels and evaluating them against cell-cycle phase and age annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated, noise-free feature table where all measurements are known to be trajectory-relevant — unsupervised selection adds little over direct modeling. Supervised annotations are available and inexpensive, and the goal is pure prediction rather than discovering an unsupervised feature subset. The data are bulk measurements or lack per-cell resolution, since the methods rely on single-cell cell-similarity graphs.

skills.description: Use when you have ranked protein-pair interaction predictions from one or more network-inference methods on scRNA-seq datasets and need a reference-standard comparison against KEGG Release 95 or BioGRID Release 4.4.217.
skills.name: protein-interaction-benchmarking-against-kegg-biogrid
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-benchmarking-against-kegg-biogrid Use when you have ranked protein-pair interaction predictions from one or more network-inference methods on scRNA-seq datasets and need a reference-standard comparison against KEGG Release 95 or BioGRID Release 4.4.217. Predictions are not a ranked interaction list (e.g., already an adjacency matrix with no ranking to truncate) Ground-truth evaluation should avoid curated databases because the goal is to measure literature bias rather than replicate it (the paper emphasizes existing networks are heavily biased by data availability) The dataset cannot be processed by a competing method (e.g., scLink could not process the large PBMC dataset), so ratios are not comparable across methods http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Benchmark ranked protein-protein interaction lists (e.g., from FAVA, scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) by truncating each to the top 10000 interactions and scoring them against KEGG and BioGRID reference networks as ground truth via true-positive/false-positive counts and TP/FP ratios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Benchmark ranked protein-protein interaction lists (e.g., from FAVA, scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) by truncating each to the top 10000 interactions and scoring them against KEGG and BioGRID reference networks as ground truth via true-positive/false-positive counts and TP/FP ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predictions are not a ranked interaction list (e.g., already an adjacency matrix with no ranking to truncate) Ground-truth evaluation should avoid curated databases because the goal is to measure literature bias rather than replicate it (the paper emphasizes existing networks are heavily biased by data availability) The dataset cannot be processed by a competing method (e.g., scLink could not process the large PBMC dataset), so ratios are not comparable across methods

skills.description: Use when inferring ligand-receptor communication between two scRNA-seq cell clusters (e.g., vCAFs to malignant ICC cells) and you must remove biologically unlikely or low-confidence protein pairs before ranking by interaction power.
skills.name: protein-interaction-credibility-and-action-mode-filtering
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-credibility-and-action-mode-filtering Use when inferring ligand-receptor communication between two scRNA-seq cell clusters (e.g., vCAFs to malignant ICC cells) and you must remove biologically unlikely or low-confidence protein pairs before ranking by interaction power. The input is not scRNA-seq cluster-level expression but a precomputed interaction network or feature table — InterCellDB filtering requires gene expression per cluster plus protein localization annotations. The biological question concerns interactions other than ligand-receptor binding (e.g., receptor-receptor or vesicle-cell types the database also encodes) and 'binding' action mode between released factors and membrane receptors does not apply. Only predicted (neither experiment validated nor pathway curated) protein interactions are acceptable as evidence for the claim being made. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A filtering strategy from InterCellDB that narrows candidate ligand-receptor gene pairs by interaction credibility (experiment validated or pathway curated STRING subsets, score >= 400 / medium confidence) and action mode/effect ('binding' with extracellular ligand to plasma-membrane receptor), then confirms significance via a cell-label permutation test (N = 100, p < 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: A filtering strategy from InterCellDB that narrows candidate ligand-receptor gene pairs by interaction credibility (experiment validated or pathway curated STRING subsets, score >= 400 / medium confidence) and action mode/effect ('binding' with extracellular ligand to plasma-membrane receptor), then confirms significance via a cell-label permutation test (N = 100, p < 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not scRNA-seq cluster-level expression but a precomputed interaction network or feature table — InterCellDB filtering requires gene expression per cluster plus protein localization annotations. The biological question concerns interactions other than ligand-receptor binding (e.g., receptor-receptor or vesicle-cell types the database also encodes) and 'binding' action mode between released factors and membrane receptors does not apply. Only predicted (neither experiment validated nor pathway curated) protein interactions are acceptable as evidence for the claim being made.

skills.description: Use when building or subsetting a cell–cell interaction database from STRING/COMPARTMENTS/UniProt annotations, or when filtering candidate ligand–receptor and protein–protein pairs by localization, evidence source, action mode, or effect before intercellular analysis.
skills.name: protein-interaction-database-filtering
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-database-filtering Use when building or subsetting a cell–cell interaction database from STRING/COMPARTMENTS/UniProt annotations, or when filtering candidate ligand–receptor and protein–protein pairs by localization, evidence source, action mode, or effect before intercellular analysis. The goal is de novo prediction of protein–protein interactions from sequence or structure — this skill only partitions and filters STRING-derived interaction evidence, it does not predict new pairs Only ligand–receptor pairs are needed and receptor–receptor, extracellular matrix–receptor, or vesicle–cell interaction types must be excluded — InterCellDB's user-defined scope deliberately covers these broader interaction types The input is already a curated, tool-specific ligand–receptor list (e.g. CellPhoneDB's built-in database) that requires no localization or action-mode subsetting http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Construct and partition a protein–protein interaction database (STRING v11) into experiment validated, pathway curated, and predicted sub-libraries, then filter biologically unlikely interactions using COMPARTMENTS subcellular localization, credibility scores, and action mode/effect annotations for user-defined intercellular communication analysis with InterCellDB. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202200045
skills.summary: Construct and partition a protein–protein interaction database (STRING v11) into experiment validated, pathway curated, and predicted sub-libraries, then filter biologically unlikely interactions using COMPARTMENTS subcellular localization, credibility scores, and action mode/effect annotations for user-defined intercellular communication analysis with InterCellDB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo prediction of protein–protein interactions from sequence or structure — this skill only partitions and filters STRING-derived interaction evidence, it does not predict new pairs Only ligand–receptor pairs are needed and receptor–receptor, extracellular matrix–receptor, or vesicle–cell interaction types must be excluded — InterCellDB's user-defined scope deliberately covers these broader interaction types The input is already a curated, tool-specific ligand–receptor list (e.g. CellPhoneDB's built-in database) that requires no localization or action-mode subsetting

skills.description: Use when you have gene sets (gene programs/modules) from scRNA-seq analysis and want to validate them functionally by testing enrichment of STRING PPI interactions, or when benchmarking methods like SSN vs ICA/NMF.
skills.name: protein-interaction-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-enrichment-testing Use when you have gene sets (gene programs/modules) from scRNA-seq analysis and want to validate them functionally by testing enrichment of STRING PPI interactions, or when benchmarking methods like SSN vs ICA/NMF. Gene sets are already validated curated pathway signatures rather than de novo discovered programs — enrichment testing against STRING adds no benchmarking value The goal is cell-type annotation rather than unsupervised gene program discovery/functional validation — use the Miko scoring pipeline instead Single-cell data has not been feature-selected or clustered into gene modules — there are no defined gene sets to test for PPI enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether discovered single-cell gene programs (e.g., from SSN, ICA, or NMF) are enriched for known protein-protein interactions from STRING, providing a functional-validation metric that complements GO-term recovery when benchmarking gene program discovery methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Tests whether discovered single-cell gene programs (e.g., from SSN, ICA, or NMF) are enriched for known protein-protein interactions from STRING, providing a functional-validation metric that complements GO-term recovery when benchmarking gene program discovery methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene sets are already validated curated pathway signatures rather than de novo discovered programs — enrichment testing against STRING adds no benchmarking value The goal is cell-type annotation rather than unsupervised gene program discovery/functional validation — use the Miko scoring pipeline instead Single-cell data has not been feature-selected or clustered into gene modules — there are no defined gene sets to test for PPI enrichment

skills.description: Use when scoring snapshot scRNA-Seq cells for differentiation potency or identifying cancer stem-cell-like phenotypes (e.g. cancer vs non-malignant cells in Tirosh melanoma) without prior marker knowledge or timepoints.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-based-potency-scoring
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-based-potency-scoring Use when scoring snapshot scRNA-Seq cells for differentiation potency or identifying cancer stem-cell-like phenotypes (e.g. cancer vs non-malignant cells in Tirosh melanoma) without prior marker knowledge or timepoints. When the input is already a feature table, cluster assignment, or pseudo-time trajectory rather than a raw gene x cell count matrix When marker genes or experimental timepoints are reliably available and the question is ordering cells along a known differentiation axis (SCENT's value is not requiring such priors) When the goal is transcriptome-entropy-only analysis without network context — the article argues network-based signalling entropy outperforms StemID/SLICE-style measures http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates single-cell differentiation potency by computing signalling promiscuity (entropy) of each cell's transcriptome in the context of a protein interaction network, using the SCENT package, without feature selection or training. It captures a subtle positive correlation between transcriptome and connectome that entropy-only methods (StemID, SLICE) miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Estimates single-cell differentiation potency by computing signalling promiscuity (entropy) of each cell's transcriptome in the context of a protein interaction network, using the SCENT package, without feature selection or training. It captures a subtle positive correlation between transcriptome and connectome that entropy-only methods (StemID, SLICE) miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a feature table, cluster assignment, or pseudo-time trajectory rather than a raw gene x cell count matrix When marker genes or experimental timepoints are reliably available and the question is ordering cells along a known differentiation axis (SCENT's value is not requiring such priors) When the goal is transcriptome-entropy-only analysis without network context — the article argues network-based signalling entropy outperforms StemID/SLICE-style measures

skills.description: Use when quantifying network disruption from an isoform switching event: STRING interaction partners must be filtered to high-quality edges (combined score > 900) before classifying which physical interactions are lost.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering Use when quantifying network disruption from an isoform switching event: STRING interaction partners must be filtered to high-quality edges (combined score > 900) before classifying which physical interactions are lost. The disease or isoform switching event is not covered by CanIsoNet (its 31 disease types cover 27 PCAWG cancer types plus OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and Behcet's RNA-Seq datasets) — the dMDT entry will not exist to filter against You need de novo prediction of protein-protein interactions rather than confidence filtering of existing STRING edges You are analyzing interactions at the gene level where isoform domain composition differences are irrelevant http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filters a protein interaction network to high-confidence edges — in the CanIsoNet workflow, STRING edges with combined score > 900 — before assessing which physical, domain-mediated interactions are lost by an isoform switching event (dMDT). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Filters a protein interaction network to high-confidence edges — in the CanIsoNet workflow, STRING edges with combined score > 900 — before assessing which physical, domain-mediated interactions are lost by an isoform switching event (dMDT).

skills.name: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering Use when a FAVA (favapy) predicted protein association network must be reduced to high-confidence edges before counting or validating interactions, e.g. against STRING, hu.MAP, or the IDG Tdark list. When the goal is to generate the network itself from raw scRNA-seq/proteomics matrices rather than threshold and validate an already-predicted network When a confidence threshold other than the article's ≥70% Pearson correlation cut-off is required, since the counts (4210 interactions, 2747 absent from STRING, 1284 shared hu.MAP edges) are specific to that cutoff When the reference comparison target is not a curated protein interaction database (STRING, hu.MAP) or the IDG dark-protein list http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Filter the FAVA-predicted functional association network (built from Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics data) at a ≥70% Pearson correlation confidence cut-off using favapy's pairs_after_cutoff, then validate the retained edges against STRING v11.5 and hu.MAP 2.0 for the IDG Tdark understudied-protein analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Filter the FAVA-predicted functional association network (built from Human Protein Atlas scRNA-seq and PRIDE proteomics data) at a ≥70% Pearson correlation confidence cut-off using favapy's pairs_after_cutoff, then validate the retained edges against STRING v11.5 and hu.MAP 2.0 for the IDG Tdark understudied-protein analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to generate the network itself from raw scRNA-seq/proteomics matrices rather than threshold and validate an already-predicted network When a confidence threshold other than the article's ≥70% Pearson correlation cut-off is required, since the counts (4210 interactions, 2747 absent from STRING, 1284 shared hu.MAP edges) are specific to that cutoff When the reference comparison target is not a curated protein interaction database (STRING, hu.MAP) or the IDG dark-protein list

skills.description: Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process (e.g. GO:0008283 cell proliferation) and need an adjacency-edge PPIN to compute per-cell network activity on scRNA-seq expression data with ORIGINS2.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-construction-from-gene-lists
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-construction-from-gene-lists Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process (e.g. GO:0008283 cell proliferation) and need an adjacency-edge PPIN to compute per-cell network activity on scRNA-seq expression data with ORIGINS2. The biological process of interest is already covered by one of the 18 preloaded BP adjacency edge sets in ORIGINS2 (e.g. cell_cycle_edges, differentiation_edges) — use those directly instead of building a custom network. You need normalized per-cell activity values rather than a network — the construction step only produces edges; normalization is controlled later by the logical normalization parameter of activity(). http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a custom PPIN for any biological process of interest by intersecting a supplied gene ID list (genes_bp) with the complete human PPIN adjacency list (full_human_ppin) using ORIGINS2's build_ppin function in R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Constructs a custom PPIN for any biological process of interest by intersecting a supplied gene ID list (genes_bp) with the complete human PPIN adjacency list (full_human_ppin) using ORIGINS2's build_ppin function in R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process of interest is already covered by one of the 18 preloaded BP adjacency edge sets in ORIGINS2 (e.g. cell_cycle_edges, differentiation_edges) — use those directly instead of building a custom network. You need normalized per-cell activity values rather than a network — the construction step only produces edges; normalization is controlled later by the logical normalization parameter of activity().

skills.description: Use when you have cell-cluster-annotated scRNA-seq data (human or mouse) and need to identify, score, and rank ligand-receptor interactions between sender and receiver populations, as in SCALA's ligand-receptor analysis mode.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-prioritization
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-prioritization Use when you have cell-cluster-annotated scRNA-seq data (human or mouse) and need to identify, score, and rank ligand-receptor interactions between sender and receiver populations, as in SCALA's ligand-receptor analysis mode. The input dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — SCALA and nichenetr currently support only human and mouse analysis Clusters are not yet annotated / no sender-receiver population pair has been defined — ligand-receptor scoring requires annotated cell populations as input The goal is basic exploratory single-cell analysis (QC, normalization, clustering) rather than intercellular communication inference between defined populations http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs SCALA's ligand-receptor analysis layer, which employs the nichenetr (NicheNet) R package to score interactions between annotated cell populations and rank ligand-receptor pairs by a 'prior interaction potential' score derived from a protein-protein interaction model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Reconstructs SCALA's ligand-receptor analysis layer, which employs the nichenetr (NicheNet) R package to score interactions between annotated cell populations and rank ligand-receptor pairs by a 'prior interaction potential' score derived from a protein-protein interaction model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — SCALA and nichenetr currently support only human and mouse analysis Clusters are not yet annotated / no sender-receiver population pair has been defined — ligand-receptor scoring requires annotated cell populations as input The goal is basic exploratory single-cell analysis (QC, normalization, clustering) rather than intercellular communication inference between defined populations

skills.description: Use when quantifying a protein's relative connectivity in the human STRING interaction network, or when scoring how isoform switching events disrupt protein-protein interactions in disease RNA-seq data.
skills.name: protein-interaction-network-scoring
skills.search_text: protein-interaction-network-scoring Use when quantifying a protein's relative connectivity in the human STRING interaction network, or when scoring how isoform switching events disrupt protein-protein interactions in disease RNA-seq data. The question concerns differential gene or transcript expression alone (e.g. raw DE analysis) with no need to place events on an interaction network The target proteome is not covered by the human STRING network used by CanIsoNet (which annotates 31 human disease types from PCAWG and four RNA-Seq datasets) Input data is already a curated interaction-impact results table conforming to the CanIsoNet schema — no rescoring is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Scores proteins and isoform-switching events within the human STRING protein-protein interaction network — e.g. the weighted network density score (HSPH1 = 78%) and the pathogenic impact of dMDT isoform switching events on their interactions, as implemented by CanIsoNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Scores proteins and isoform-switching events within the human STRING protein-protein interaction network — e.g. the weighted network density score (HSPH1 = 78%) and the pathogenic impact of dMDT isoform switching events on their interactions, as implemented by CanIsoNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns differential gene or transcript expression alone (e.g. raw DE analysis) with no need to place events on an interaction network The target proteome is not covered by the human STRING network used by CanIsoNet (which annotates 31 human disease types from PCAWG and four RNA-Seq datasets) Input data is already a curated interaction-impact results table conforming to the CanIsoNet schema — no rescoring is needed

skills.description: Use when matched mRNA, miRNA and protein expression data from tumor and normal samples are available and the goal is to identify RBP-ncRNA circuits in which ncRNAs modulate RBP function at the protein level.
skills.name: protein-level-network-module-detection
skills.search_text: protein-level-network-module-detection Use when matched mRNA, miRNA and protein expression data from tumor and normal samples are available and the goal is to identify RBP-ncRNA circuits in which ncRNAs modulate RBP function at the protein level. Only transcript-level data (no matched protein expression) is available — use the transcription-level workflow (interStringency type='transcription') instead The goal is a locally seeded module around a user-defined node — use runmodule(method='local', maxsize=..., seletN=...) rather than the global search http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect a maximum-scoring RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) where RBPs are represented at the protein level, using the fRNC R package on matched mRNA, miRNA and protein expression data (e.g. 852 tumor / 18 normal BRCA samples from TCGA/TCPA). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Detect a maximum-scoring RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) where RBPs are represented at the protein level, using the fRNC R package on matched mRNA, miRNA and protein expression data (e.g. 852 tumor / 18 normal BRCA samples from TCGA/TCPA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only transcript-level data (no matched protein expression) is available — use the transcription-level workflow (interStringency type='transcription') instead The goal is a locally seeded module around a user-defined node — use runmodule(method='local', maxsize=..., seletN=...) rather than the global search

skills.description: Use when constructing or curating a ligand–receptor prior database for cell–cell communication inference and you must restrict candidate pairs to biophysically plausible secreted/membrane proteins using GO compartment annotations.
skills.name: protein-localization-based-interaction-filtering
skills.search_text: protein-localization-based-interaction-filtering Use when constructing or curating a ligand–receptor prior database for cell–cell communication inference and you must restrict candidate pairs to biophysically plausible secreted/membrane proteins using GO compartment annotations. The user supplies their own curated L-R gene list — dsCellNet supports supplementary user-provided L-R genes instead of relying on the default localization-filtered database The analysis requires receptor localization beyond the plasma membrane (e.g. intracellular/nuclear receptors), which this GO:0005886-based filter drops by design Inferring interactions in a single stationary snapshot without needing a localization-filtered prior — though the filter still applies inside dsCellNet, other methods' pair lists may be used directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Builds and filters a multi-species ligand–receptor database by subcellular localization: merge published L-R sources (Ramilowski 2015, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR), then keep only pairs whose ligand is secreted or plasma-membrane and whose receptor is plasma-membrane, yielding dsCellNet's default list of 5,744 interactions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Builds and filters a multi-species ligand–receptor database by subcellular localization: merge published L-R sources (Ramilowski 2015, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR), then keep only pairs whose ligand is secreted or plasma-membrane and whose receptor is plasma-membrane, yielding dsCellNet's default list of 5,744 interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The user supplies their own curated L-R gene list — dsCellNet supports supplementary user-provided L-R genes instead of relying on the default localization-filtered database The analysis requires receptor localization beyond the plasma membrane (e.g. intracellular/nuclear receptors), which this GO:0005886-based filter drops by design Inferring interactions in a single stationary snapshot without needing a localization-filtered prior — though the filter still applies inside dsCellNet, other methods' pair lists may be used directly

skills.description: Use when you have a multimodal CITE-seq h5ad with normalized protein counts and protein-derived PCs, and need to validate clustering-free protein marker predictions against Seurat-style Wilcoxon/t-test baselines.
skills.name: protein-marker-concordance-verification
skills.search_text: protein-marker-concordance-verification Use when you have a multimodal CITE-seq h5ad with normalized protein counts and protein-derived PCs, and need to validate clustering-free protein marker predictions against Seurat-style Wilcoxon/t-test baselines. The goal is a multi-condition comparison (e.g. wild-type vs knockout): the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' with singleCellHaystack Results must feed directly into a cluster-oriented analysis: the discussion notes singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analyses The feature space is spatial transcriptomics where SPARK-X's faster runtime is preferred and sensitivity trade-offs are acceptable http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Verifies that singleCellHaystack's clustering-independent prediction of differentially active proteins on a CITE-seq PBMC atlas (normalized 228-protein matrix + 50 protein-based PCs) agrees with cluster-based differential expression baselines (Wilcoxon rank-sum and t-test), and pinpoints proteins whose rankings diverge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Verifies that singleCellHaystack's clustering-independent prediction of differentially active proteins on a CITE-seq PBMC atlas (normalized 228-protein matrix + 50 protein-based PCs) agrees with cluster-based differential expression baselines (Wilcoxon rank-sum and t-test), and pinpoints proteins whose rankings diverge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a multi-condition comparison (e.g. wild-type vs knockout): the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' with singleCellHaystack Results must feed directly into a cluster-oriented analysis: the discussion notes singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analyses The feature space is spatial transcriptomics where SPARK-X's faster runtime is preferred and sensitivity trade-offs are acceptable

skills.description: Use when a weighted protein association network edge list (e.g. from a favapy run) must be partitioned into functional clusters with MCL and the resulting cluster count and size distribution must be validated against published numbers before enrichment analysis.
skills.name: protein-network-cluster-size-distribution-verification
skills.search_text: protein-network-cluster-size-distribution-verification Use when a weighted protein association network edge list (e.g. from a favapy run) must be partitioned into functional clusters with MCL and the resulting cluster count and size distribution must be validated against published numbers before enrichment analysis. The network has not yet been generated by the upstream favapy run — clustering an unvalidated or differently filtered edge list will not reproduce the 341/130 reference numbers. The goal is enrichment on all clusters regardless of size — this skill restricts downstream enrichment to clusters with five or more nodes. The clustering target is a co-expression network from raw scRNA-seq rather than a FAVA-inferred protein association network in latent-space correlation form. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Verifies MCL graph clustering of the combined FAVA protein association network by reproducing the reported 341 clusters (inflation 1.5) and the 130 clusters with five or more nodes, then running Cytoscape stringApp 2.0 enrichment on those clusters across seven annotation categories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: Verifies MCL graph clustering of the combined FAVA protein association network by reproducing the reported 341 clusters (inflation 1.5) and the 130 clusters with five or more nodes, then running Cytoscape stringApp 2.0 enrichment on those clusters across seven annotation categories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network has not yet been generated by the upstream favapy run — clustering an unvalidated or differently filtered edge list will not reproduce the 341/130 reference numbers. The goal is enrichment on all clusters regardless of size — this skill restricts downstream enrichment to clusters with five or more nodes. The clustering target is a co-expression network from raw scRNA-seq rather than a FAVA-inferred protein association network in latent-space correlation form.

skills.description: Use when building an LncDC-style lncRNA-vs-mRNA feature matrix and protein-level descriptors (e.g. ProtParam properties from translated ORFs) must be added to sequence and secondary-structure features.
skills.name: protein-physicochemical-feature-computation
skills.search_text: protein-physicochemical-feature-computation Use when building an LncDC-style lncRNA-vs-mRNA feature matrix and protein-level descriptors (e.g. ProtParam properties from translated ORFs) must be added to sequence and secondary-structure features. The input is already a computed feature matrix (e.g. a populated 57-column csv) — PF computation belongs only to the raw-feature extraction stage Only secondary structure features (SSFs) are being added via the -r flag; PFs are computed independently of the ViennaRNA/RNAfold SSF path Input records lack a mappable mRNA/CDS pair, since the CDS-matched ORF definition drives the translated ORFs used for ProtParam features http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Computes protein features (PFs) in LncDC by translating each transcript's ORFs and deriving ProtParam physicochemical properties, one of the three feature families (SIFs, SSFs, PFs) fed to the XGBoost lncRNA/mRNA classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Computes protein features (PFs) in LncDC by translating each transcript's ORFs and deriving ProtParam physicochemical properties, one of the three feature families (SIFs, SSFs, PFs) fed to the XGBoost lncRNA/mRNA classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a computed feature matrix (e.g. a populated 57-column csv) — PF computation belongs only to the raw-feature extraction stage Only secondary structure features (SSFs) are being added via the -r flag; PFs are computed independently of the ViennaRNA/RNAfold SSF path Input records lack a mappable mRNA/CDS pair, since the CDS-matched ORF definition drives the translated ORFs used for ProtParam features

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cTP-net surface-protein imputation on holdout CITE-seq cells and you need to isolate the contribution of SAVER-X denoising versus other preprocessing or training parameter choices, measured as correlation retraction.
skills.name: protein-prediction-correlation-comparison
skills.search_text: protein-prediction-correlation-comparison Use when benchmarking cTP-net surface-protein imputation on holdout CITE-seq cells and you need to isolate the contribution of SAVER-X denoising versus other preprocessing or training parameter choices, measured as correlation retraction. Expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g. TPM/RPKM), since cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input You only need a routine cTP-net imputation run — this skill is an ablation comparison requiring both a denoised baseline and a retrained raw-input model on matched validation cells Cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage, which was not tested in the paper's benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 An ablation-comparison skill for cTP-net: quantify how much per-protein Pearson correlation between predicted and measured surface protein abundance drops when SAVER-X denoising is replaced by raw LogNormalize RNA input, and compare that retraction (~0.02) against other parameter tweaks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: An ablation-comparison skill for cTP-net: quantify how much per-protein Pearson correlation between predicted and measured surface protein abundance drops when SAVER-X denoising is replaced by raw LogNormalize RNA input, and compare that retraction (~0.02) against other parameter tweaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g. TPM/RPKM), since cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input You only need a routine cTP-net imputation run — this skill is an ablation comparison requiring both a denoised baseline and a retrained raw-input model on matched validation cells Cells are not of the hematopoietic lineage, which was not tested in the paper's benchmarks

skills.description: Use when you have a small, validated gene list (ideally with gene symbols) and need to test whether its members form a non-random interaction network and which KEGG pathways are enriched, as done for shared broiler ASE genes.
skills.name: protein-protein-interaction-network-enrichment
skills.search_text: protein-protein-interaction-network-enrichment Use when you have a small, validated gene list (ideally with gene symbols) and need to test whether its members form a non-random interaction network and which KEGG pathways are enriched, as done for shared broiler ASE genes. The gene list is not validated (e.g., the three-tissue overlap has not been confirmed at the expected 20.1% / 1715 shared genes), so network results would be uninterpretable Genes lack assigned symbols and cannot be reliably mapped to STRING identifiers The question is SNP-level ASE overlap rather than gene-level functional enrichment (the study found only 3.7% of ASE SNPs shared across tissues, versus 20.1% of ASE genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Build a STRING protein-protein interaction network from a curated list of genes with symbols and extract KEGG pathway enrichments to identify shared functional biology (e.g., ribosome/translation pathways) among candidate genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Build a STRING protein-protein interaction network from a curated list of genes with symbols and extract KEGG pathway enrichments to identify shared functional biology (e.g., ribosome/translation pathways) among candidate genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene list is not validated (e.g., the three-tissue overlap has not been confirmed at the expected 20.1% / 1715 shared genes), so network results would be uninterpretable Genes lack assigned symbols and cannot be reliably mapped to STRING identifiers The question is SNP-level ASE overlap rather than gene-level functional enrichment (the study found only 3.7% of ASE SNPs shared across tissues, versus 20.1% of ASE genes)

skills.description: Use when you need a PPIN edge list restricted to a specific biological process or custom gene list, to feed into PPIN activity scoring of scRNA-seq expression matrices.
skills.name: protein-protein-interaction-network-subsetting
skills.search_text: protein-protein-interaction-network-subsetting Use when you need a PPIN edge list restricted to a specific biological process or custom gene list, to feed into PPIN activity scoring of scRNA-seq expression matrices. The biological process of interest already has a pre-built PPIN loaded in ORIGINS2 (18 BP are included, e.g. differentiation_edges, cell_cycle_edges, dna_repair_edges) — use those directly instead of rebuilding. You need the complete human interactome rather than a process-specific subnetwork — use full_human_ppin directly. The input is a normalized expression matrix needing activity scoring rather than a gene list needing an edge set — use the activity() function instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs a custom protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) for an arbitrary biological process or user-supplied gene list by subsetting edges of the bundled full human PPIN (full_human_ppin) in the ORIGINS2 R package, using the build_ppin function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Constructs a custom protein-protein interaction network (PPIN) for an arbitrary biological process or user-supplied gene list by subsetting edges of the bundled full human PPIN (full_human_ppin) in the ORIGINS2 R package, using the build_ppin function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The biological process of interest already has a pre-built PPIN loaded in ORIGINS2 (18 BP are included, e.g. differentiation_edges, cell_cycle_edges, dna_repair_edges) — use those directly instead of rebuilding. You need the complete human interactome rather than a process-specific subnetwork — use full_human_ppin directly. The input is a normalized expression matrix needing activity scoring rather than a gene list needing an edge set — use the activity() function instead.

skills.description: Use when you have a list of predicted candidate regulators (e.g. 73 CRIT NMF-cluster candidates) and a gold-standard regulator list (gold_regulators.xlsx), and need to quantify physical-interaction enrichment between the two sets.
skills.name: protein-protein-interaction-overlap-testing
skills.search_text: protein-protein-interaction-overlap-testing Use when you have a list of predicted candidate regulators (e.g. 73 CRIT NMF-cluster candidates) and a gold-standard regulator list (gold_regulators.xlsx), and need to quantify physical-interaction enrichment between the two sets. The goal is co-expression or shared-transcription-factor association testing — these use the MSigDB Cancer Gene Co-expression Modules and TRANSFAC Curated Transcription Factor Targets datasets instead of the Pathway Commons PPI dataset The input is raw omics data (TCGA/MiOncoCirc/RNAct files) rather than an already-computed candidate regulator list from NMF clustering No gold-standard regulator list is available to define the reference set against which overlap is tested http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Tests whether predicted circRNA regulators are functionally connected to gold-standard regulators through protein-protein interactions by intersecting candidate and gold gene sets in the Harmonizome Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions dataset and assessing overlap significance with 10,000 random-sampling permutations at FDR < 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Tests whether predicted circRNA regulators are functionally connected to gold-standard regulators through protein-protein interactions by intersecting candidate and gold gene sets in the Harmonizome Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions dataset and assessing overlap significance with 10,000 random-sampling permutations at FDR < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is co-expression or shared-transcription-factor association testing — these use the MSigDB Cancer Gene Co-expression Modules and TRANSFAC Curated Transcription Factor Targets datasets instead of the Pathway Commons PPI dataset The input is raw omics data (TCGA/MiOncoCirc/RNAct files) rather than an already-computed candidate regulator list from NMF clustering No gold-standard regulator list is available to define the reference set against which overlap is tested

skills.description: Use when you have Prokka-predicted protein FASTAs from many quality-filtered genomes and need function-based gene clusters plus a genome-by-cluster absence/presence matrix for comparative genomics or feature-based ML.
skills.name: protein-sequence-clustering
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-clustering Use when you have Prokka-predicted protein FASTAs from many quality-filtered genomes and need function-based gene clusters plus a genome-by-cluster absence/presence matrix for comparative genomics or feature-based ML. Genomes have not been quality-filtered or redundancy-reduced — bacLIFE clusters only high-quality (>90% completeness, <5% contamination) non-redundant genomes You need ortholog-level one-to-one grouping rather than similar-function clusters; the authors benchmarked against OrthoFinder defaults and chose MCL inflation 3.0 for EC-number consistency/granularity instead Input is raw reads or unannotated contigs — Prokka gene prediction must be run first to obtain protein sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Two-stage functional clustering of pooled predicted proteins — MMseqs2 linclust pre-clustering followed by MCL graph clustering on a diamond bitscore network — to build gene-family absence/presence matrices for downstream lifestyle prediction in bacLIFE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Two-stage functional clustering of pooled predicted proteins — MMseqs2 linclust pre-clustering followed by MCL graph clustering on a diamond bitscore network — to build gene-family absence/presence matrices for downstream lifestyle prediction in bacLIFE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genomes have not been quality-filtered or redundancy-reduced — bacLIFE clusters only high-quality (>90% completeness, <5% contamination) non-redundant genomes You need ortholog-level one-to-one grouping rather than similar-function clusters; the authors benchmarked against OrthoFinder defaults and chose MCL inflation 3.0 for EC-number consistency/granularity instead Input is raw reads or unannotated contigs — Prokka gene prediction must be run first to obtain protein sequences

skills.description: Use when aligning genes across species (e.g. human vs mouse scRNA-seq) by protein sequence similarity and you need embedding-based gene matches or a gene distance matrix for TACTiCS, as an alternative to BLAST -hit matching.
skills.name: protein-sequence-embedding
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-embedding Use when aligning genes across species (e.g. human vs mouse scRNA-seq) by protein sequence similarity and you need embedding-based gene matches or a gene distance matrix for TACTiCS, as an alternative to BLAST -hit matching. Genes are being matched within a single species only — TACTiCS gene matching exists to align orthologs across species Only gene names/symbols are available without protein sequences — `embed_proteins` requires protein sequences as input A BLAST best-hit gene match set is already accepted for the analysis — though note the paper shows BLAST matches reduce TACTiCS ADS and recall relative to ProtBERT matches http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generate fixed-length protein sequence embeddings (e.g. ProtBERT via the transformers package) with TACTiCS's `embed_proteins` in genes.py, then convert them into a gene similarity distance matrix with `calc_dist` to serve as the gene-matching input for cross-species cell type matching. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Generate fixed-length protein sequence embeddings (e.g. ProtBERT via the transformers package) with TACTiCS's `embed_proteins` in genes.py, then convert them into a gene similarity distance matrix with `calc_dist` to serve as the gene-matching input for cross-species cell type matching.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes are being matched within a single species only — TACTiCS gene matching exists to align orthologs across species Only gene names/symbols are available without protein sequences — `embed_proteins` requires protein sequences as input A BLAST best-hit gene match set is already accepted for the analysis — though note the paper shows BLAST matches reduce TACTiCS ADS and recall relative to ProtBERT matches

skills.description: Use when integrating modalities measured on different feature spaces (e.g., scRNA-seq vs surface proteins or smFISH) and you need a common gene-level feature matrix to compute cross-modality cell distances.
skills.name: protein-to-coding-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: protein-to-coding-gene-mapping Use when integrating modalities measured on different feature spaces (e.g., scRNA-seq vs surface proteins or smFISH) and you need a common gene-level feature matrix to compute cross-modality cell distances. When the modalities already share the same native feature space (e.g., two scRNA-seq datasets), no protein-to-gene conversion is needed When no cross-modality feature connections exist at all (e.g., electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities When the goal is paired multimodal integration (matched cells across modalities) rather than diagonal integration of unpaired samples Converts measured surface-protein features (e.g., CITE-seq/CyTOF antibodies, smFISH targets) into their coding genes so protein-based modalities can be expressed on a gene feature space shared with scRNA-seq, enabling cross-modality cell-to-cell comparison in scConfluence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Converts measured surface-protein features (e.g., CITE-seq/CyTOF antibodies, smFISH targets) into their coding genes so protein-based modalities can be expressed on a gene feature space shared with scRNA-seq, enabling cross-modality cell-to-cell comparison in scConfluence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the modalities already share the same native feature space (e.g., two scRNA-seq datasets), no protein-to-gene conversion is needed When no cross-modality feature connections exist at all (e.g., electrophysiology measurements vs gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities When the goal is paired multimodal integration (matched cells across modalities) rather than diagonal integration of unpaired samples

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized proteomic expression matrix (proteins x samples) and want to identify significantly shifted or overdispersed pathways and stratify samples into clusters based on their module activity profiles.

skills.summary: Aggregate single cells into pseudo-bulk profiles (per cell type within each sample, or per sample-by-condition combination) as implemented in scMerge2, to reduce atlas-scale collections (~5 million cells, 1298 samples) to a tractable pseudo-replicate structure before batch-effect estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is joint integration across modalities (e.g. combining scRNA-seq and CyTOF features); the paper's integration was performed within each modality only, with multi-modal incorporation deferred to future work When the study is small enough that per-cell processing is tractable and pseudo-bulk compression offers no scalability benefit When no reliable cell-type annotations exist, since the pseudo-bulk grouping depends on annotated cell types per sample

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known per-cell type labels and need pseudo-bulk mixtures with ground-truth proportions to benchmark deconvolution performance of competing marker sets or signature matrices.
skills.name: pseudo-bulk-mixture-simulation
skills.search_text: pseudo-bulk-mixture-simulation Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known per-cell type labels and need pseudo-bulk mixtures with ground-truth proportions to benchmark deconvolution performance of competing marker sets or signature matrices. You need individual-cell-level classification accuracy rather than bulk mixture proportion estimation — the logistic-regression left-out evaluation workflow is the appropriate alternative. You lack cell-type labels for the single cells, since ground-truth proportions for the mixtures cannot be recorded. You want truly in vivo bulk RNA-seq validation rather than simulated mixtures — pseudo-bulk averaging of single cells is only an approximation of real bulk tissue profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates bulk RNA-seq mixtures from scRNA-seq data by averaging expression across single cells in test sets, then evaluates marker sets via CIBERSORT (linear nu-SVR) deconvolution against known cell-type proportions using Jensen-Shannon divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Simulates bulk RNA-seq mixtures from scRNA-seq data by averaging expression across single cells in test sets, then evaluates marker sets via CIBERSORT (linear nu-SVR) deconvolution against known cell-type proportions using Jensen-Shannon divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need individual-cell-level classification accuracy rather than bulk mixture proportion estimation — the logistic-regression left-out evaluation workflow is the appropriate alternative. You lack cell-type labels for the single cells, since ground-truth proportions for the mixtures cannot be recorded. You want truly in vivo bulk RNA-seq validation rather than simulated mixtures — pseudo-bulk averaging of single cells is only an approximation of real bulk tissue profiles.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq alignments and a set of TAR/uTAR intervals and need aggregate (pseudo-bulk) expression per region, e.g., to rank uTARs by total coverage and compare against cell-type-defining PC loadings.
skills.name: pseudo-bulk-read-coverage-quantification
skills.search_text: pseudo-bulk-read-coverage-quantification Use when you have scRNA-seq alignments and a set of TAR/uTAR intervals and need aggregate (pseudo-bulk) expression per region, e.g., to rank uTARs by total coverage and compare against cell-type-defining PC loadings. You need per-cell expression patterns or differential expression across clusters — use the single-cell TAR expression matrix and Seurat workflow instead; pseudo-bulk coverage discards cell-level structure. The alignment contains multi-mapped reads and you have not applied the uniquely-mapped filter (-q 255); coverage counts will be inflated. TAR/uTAR intervals do not yet exist — groHMM must first run to identify TARs from the alignments (see the calcHMMrefFlat/groHMM workflow). http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies total expression level of transcriptionally active regions (TARs), especially unannotated TARs (uTARs), by merging uniquely mapped scRNA-seq reads per experiment and computing region-level read coverage. In this paper it is used to test whether highly expressed uTARs are the same ones that best define cell types via PCA loadings (they are not: r2 = 4.0e-3). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Quantifies total expression level of transcriptionally active regions (TARs), especially unannotated TARs (uTARs), by merging uniquely mapped scRNA-seq reads per experiment and computing region-level read coverage. In this paper it is used to test whether highly expressed uTARs are the same ones that best define cell types via PCA loadings (they are not: r2 = 4.0e-3).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need per-cell expression patterns or differential expression across clusters — use the single-cell TAR expression matrix and Seurat workflow instead; pseudo-bulk coverage discards cell-level structure. The alignment contains multi-mapped reads and you have not applied the uniquely-mapped filter (-q 255); coverage counts will be inflated. TAR/uTAR intervals do not yet exist — groHMM must first run to identify TARs from the alignments (see the calcHMMrefFlat/groHMM workflow).

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters are annotated via one-against-all marker gene tests (e.g. Seurat Wilcoxon) and you need to flag markers upregulated in multiple clusters that could cause incorrect or inconsistent cell type annotation.
skills.name: pseudo-marker-gene-detection
skills.search_text: pseudo-marker-gene-detection Use when scRNA-seq clusters are annotated via one-against-all marker gene tests (e.g. Seurat Wilcoxon) and you need to flag markers upregulated in multiple clusters that could cause incorrect or inconsistent cell type annotation. Cluster annotation already uses paired-comparison or evidence-based scoring approaches (e.g. scCATCH itself) that exclude genes upregulated in more than one cluster by design The dataset has only two clusters, so 'upregulated in at least two clusters' cannot be evaluated meaningfully The CellMatch reference database lacks coverage for the tissue of interest, since scCATCH performance majorly depends on the reference database and a limited reference can itself cause incorrect annotation independent of pseudo markers http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects pseudo marker genes — genes significantly upregulated in at least two clusters rather than one — that arise from Seurat-style one-against-all cluster marker identification in scRNA-seq data, and quantifies how they impair cell type annotation consistency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Detects pseudo marker genes — genes significantly upregulated in at least two clusters rather than one — that arise from Seurat-style one-against-all cluster marker identification in scRNA-seq data, and quantifies how they impair cell type annotation consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cluster annotation already uses paired-comparison or evidence-based scoring approaches (e.g. scCATCH itself) that exclude genes upregulated in more than one cluster by design The dataset has only two clusters, so 'upregulated in at least two clusters' cannot be evaluated meaningfully The CellMatch reference database lacks coverage for the tissue of interest, since scCATCH performance majorly depends on the reference database and a limited reference can itself cause incorrect annotation independent of pseudo markers

skills.search_text: pseudo-replicate-assignment-with-phenotypes Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell collections (e.g. millions of cells across many donors/studies) where batch effects must be removed without confounding biological differences between phenotypes or severity groups. skills.summary: A key scMerge2 innovation in which pseudo-replicates are assigned within phenotype/condition groups after building pseudo-bulk profiles per annotated cell type per sample, enabling condition-aware atlas-scale integration of multi-sample single-cell data.

skills.search_text: pseudo-replicate-bootstrapping-benchmarking Use when evaluating or running Scanpro on unreplicated single-cell proportion data (no samples_col), or when determining how many pseudo-replicates (5-8 vs 8+) to use in bootstrapped differential composition analysis. skills.search_text: pseudobulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-data Use when you have a cell-level PAS matrix from scPAFA ('fast_Ucell' or 'fast_score_genes') plus cell-level metadata and need sample-level input for MOFA-based multicellular pathway module discovery. The analysis requires single-cell resolution — pseudobulk integration of the PAS matrix leads to information loss since the PAS of multiple cells is aggregated. The input is already a sample-level feature table (aggregation would be redundant; proceed directly to MOFA training). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Step 2 of the scPAFA workflow: reformat the cell-level pathway activity score (PAS) matrix into a long-table-like pandas dataframe via pseudobulk aggregation per sample/donor and cell type, with sample/donor, cell type, and technical batch metadata, producing the input required by mofapy2 for MOFA model training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Step 2 of the scPAFA workflow: reformat the cell-level pathway activity score (PAS) matrix into a long-table-like pandas dataframe via pseudobulk aggregation per sample/donor and cell type, with sample/donor, cell type, and technical batch metadata, producing the input required by mofapy2 for MOFA model training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study has fewer than 15 samples (not cells) — scPAFA requires at least 15 samples to use the MOFA model for identifying multicellular pathway modules. skills.description: Use when benchmarking perturbation metrics for single-cell differential state analysis, or when you need a gene-count baseline (nDEG) to contrast against cell-count-confounded measures on datasets with variable cells per cell type.
skills.name: pseudobulk-differential-expression-counting
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-differential-expression-counting Use when benchmarking perturbation metrics for single-cell differential state analysis, or when you need a gene-count baseline (nDEG) to contrast against cell-count-confounded measures on datasets with variable cells per cell type. As a primary perturbation metric when cells per cell type vary substantially — nDEG is highly confounded by cell count in the 100–10,000 cell resampling of the COVID-19 dataset When computational efficiency matters at scale — the gene-wise pseudobulk testing was over 60x slower than scDist's PC-based mixed-model distance When a statistically rigorous distance with per-cell-type uncertainty is needed rather than a raw count of significant genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A baseline transcriptomic-perturbation metric that aggregates single-cell counts per sample and cell type (pseudobulk), performs gene-wise differential testing, and counts significant DEGs (nDEG). skills.summary: A baseline transcriptomic-perturbation metric that aggregates single-cell counts per sample and cell type (pseudobulk), performs gene-wise differential testing, and counts significant DEGs (nDEG). skills.when_to_use_negative: As a primary perturbation metric when cells per cell type vary substantially — nDEG is highly confounded by cell count in the 100–10,000 cell resampling of the COVID-19 dataset When computational efficiency matters at scale — the gene-wise pseudobulk testing was over 60x slower than scDist's PC-based mixed-model distance When a statistically rigorous distance with per-cell-type uncertainty is needed rather than a raw count of significant genes
