skills.name: pseudobulk-probability-projection-to-cells
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-probability-projection-to-cells Use when trajectory inference was performed on VDJ pseudobulks (e.g. miloR neighbourhoods from the Suo et al. fetal immune atlas data) and you need per-cell pseudotime and CD4/CD8 branch probabilities to score predicted cell fates against annotated labels. The trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing) and cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains, so branch probabilities to project are undefined The dataset topology is not bifurcation or linear — destiny-based diffusion map inference underpinning the probabilities is unsuitable Input is already per-cell pseudotime/fate data and no pseudobulk aggregation was performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branch/fate probabilities computed on the VDJ feature space via diffusion maps and absorbing Markov chains) back to individual cells using dandelionR's projectPseudotimeToCell, enabling cell-level fate scoring in the ab T-cell DP-to-CD4/CD8 analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branch/fate probabilities computed on the VDJ feature space via diffusion maps and absorbing Markov chains) back to individual cells using dandelionR's projectPseudotimeToCell, enabling cell-level fate scoring in the ab T-cell DP-to-CD4/CD8 analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing) and cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains, so branch probabilities to project are undefined The dataset topology is not bifurcation or linear — destiny-based diffusion map inference underpinning the probabilities is unsuitable Input is already per-cell pseudotime/fate data and no pseudobulk aggregation was performed

skills.description: Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads against real reads at the read-sequence level, or when benchmarking a read simulator's ability to mimic pseudo-bulk coverage patterns across genomic windows.
skills.name: pseudobulk-read-coverage-window-binning
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-read-coverage-window-binning Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads against real reads at the read-sequence level, or when benchmarking a read simulator's ability to mimic pseudo-bulk coverage patterns across genomic windows. Evaluating count-level fidelity of a simulator that outputs only a gene-by-cell count matrix and no reads — use count-matrix correlations instead Benchmarking isoform-level or alternative-splicing ground truths — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI ground truths only Comparing simulators when reads are aligned to different reference genomes — correlations are only comparable on the same reference (mm10) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A read-level fidelity assessment for synthetic scRNA-seq data: real and simulated BAM/aligned reads are binned per chromosome (e.g., 1000-bp windows on chr1), per-window coverage is summed, and Spearman/Pearson correlations quantify how well a simulator (scReadSim vs minnow) reproduces real read-coverage structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: A read-level fidelity assessment for synthetic scRNA-seq data: real and simulated BAM/aligned reads are binned per chromosome (e.g., 1000-bp windows on chr1), per-window coverage is summed, and Spearman/Pearson correlations quantify how well a simulator (scReadSim vs minnow) reproduces real read-coverage structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating count-level fidelity of a simulator that outputs only a gene-by-cell count matrix and no reads — use count-matrix correlations instead Benchmarking isoform-level or alternative-splicing ground truths — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI ground truths only Comparing simulators when reads are aligned to different reference genomes — correlations are only comparable on the same reference (mm10)

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or simulated tissue samples must be collapsed into pseudobulk profiles and deconvolved against a sketch-derived single-cell reference, with per-sample cell-type proportion estimates compared to known true proportions.
skills.name: pseudobulk-sample-aggregation
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-sample-aggregation Use when bulk RNA-seq or simulated tissue samples must be collapsed into pseudobulk profiles and deconvolved against a sketch-derived single-cell reference, with per-sample cell-type proportion estimates compared to known true proportions. Downstream questions require cell-level resolution (e.g. cell-type annotation, label transfer) — pseudobulk aggregation collapses cells per sample and only supports bulk proportion estimation No ground-truth cell-type proportions are available for the bulk samples, since Pearson/RMSE/MAE scoring against true proportions is the core of the benchmark The single-cell reference lacks cell-type annotations (cell_type_key), making it unusable to build the annotated reference matrix MuSiC requires http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates individual single-cell or simulated bulk tissue samples into pseudobulk expression profiles so that a reference single-cell matrix (e.g. a scValue sketch of the T&ILC A29/A31 donors) can be used with MuSiC to infer cell-type proportions, which are then scored against ground truth via Pearson correlation, RMSE, and MAE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Aggregates individual single-cell or simulated bulk tissue samples into pseudobulk expression profiles so that a reference single-cell matrix (e.g. a scValue sketch of the T&ILC A29/A31 donors) can be used with MuSiC to infer cell-type proportions, which are then scored against ground truth via Pearson correlation, RMSE, and MAE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Downstream questions require cell-level resolution (e.g. cell-type annotation, label transfer) — pseudobulk aggregation collapses cells per sample and only supports bulk proportion estimation No ground-truth cell-type proportions are available for the bulk samples, since Pearson/RMSE/MAE scoring against true proportions is the core of the benchmark The single-cell reference lacks cell-type annotations (cell_type_key), making it unusable to build the annotated reference matrix MuSiC requires

skills.description: Use when you need QC of a curated scRNA-seq time-course against a matched bulk RNA-seq reference — e.g. testing pseudo-bulk profiles of embryo stages against low-input bulk profiles before downstream analysis.
skills.name: pseudobulk-vs-bulk-rnaseq-correlation-validation
skills.search_text: pseudobulk-vs-bulk-rnaseq-correlation-validation Use when you need QC of a curated scRNA-seq time-course against a matched bulk RNA-seq reference — e.g. testing pseudo-bulk profiles of embryo stages against low-input bulk profiles before downstream analysis. The input is already a validated bulk-only expression matrix with no single-cell data to aggregate into pseudo-bulk profiles There is no matched bulk RNA-seq reference for the same stages, so agreement cannot be assessed The goal is cell-type-resolved communication inference (e.g. CellChat/CellPhoneDB) rather than dataset-level QC http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates curated single-cell RNA-seq data quality by computing stage-level pseudo-bulk expression profiles and checking agreement with matching low-input bulk RNA-seq profiles via Pearson correlation, complemented by kBET batch-mixing assessment. Used in TimeTalk to confirm scRNA-seq (GSE38495, GSE45719) faithfully represents embryo development stages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Validates curated single-cell RNA-seq data quality by computing stage-level pseudo-bulk expression profiles and checking agreement with matching low-input bulk RNA-seq profiles via Pearson correlation, complemented by kBET batch-mixing assessment. Used in TimeTalk to confirm scRNA-seq (GSE38495, GSE45719) faithfully represents embryo development stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a validated bulk-only expression matrix with no single-cell data to aggregate into pseudo-bulk profiles There is no matched bulk RNA-seq reference for the same stages, so agreement cannot be assessed The goal is cell-type-resolved communication inference (e.g. CellChat/CellPhoneDB) rather than dataset-level QC

skills.description: Use when converting per-sample single-cell cluster count vectors into probability distributions over clusters as input for optimal transport (Wasserstein/EMD) sample-level analysis, especially when some clusters are absent in individual samples.
skills.name: pseudocount-regularization-of-sample-compositions
skills.search_text: pseudocount-regularization-of-sample-compositions Use when converting per-sample single-cell cluster count vectors into probability distributions over clusters as input for optimal transport (Wasserstein/EMD) sample-level analysis, especially when some clusters are absent in individual samples. Input is already a normalized sample x cluster probability/composition table that feeds directly into the Wasserstein distance computation — re-applying pseudo-counts would double-regularize. The goal is per-cell or per-cluster analysis rather than sample-level distributions; this skill only regularizes sample-level cluster compositions. Data are pathomics tissue structures with a different clustering representation where the count-multinomial assumption does not hold (check whether the hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial model is appropriate for the structure counts). http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Robustly estimates each sample's cell-cluster probability distribution via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate, where a Dirichlet prior adds pseudo cell counts weighted by the global cell distribution of all samples. This yields strictly positive per-sample cluster probabilities p_lk that feed PILOT's Wasserstein-distance computation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Robustly estimates each sample's cell-cluster probability distribution via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate, where a Dirichlet prior adds pseudo cell counts weighted by the global cell distribution of all samples. This yields strictly positive per-sample cluster probabilities p_lk that feed PILOT's Wasserstein-distance computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized sample x cluster probability/composition table that feeds directly into the Wasserstein distance computation — re-applying pseudo-counts would double-regularize. The goal is per-cell or per-cluster analysis rather than sample-level distributions; this skill only regularizes sample-level cluster compositions. Data are pathomics tissue structures with a different clustering representation where the count-multinomial assumption does not hold (check whether the hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial model is appropriate for the structure counts).

skills.description: Use when converting 41 bp RNA m5C sequence segments into numerical features via dinucleotide physicochemical properties, e.g. to reproduce Staem5's PCPseDNC feature block before fusing with PSP, k-mer, and PseEIIP encodings.
skills.name: pseudodinucleotide-physicochemical-encoding
skills.search_text: pseudodinucleotide-physicochemical-encoding Use when converting 41 bp RNA m5C sequence segments into numerical features via dinucleotide physicochemical properties, e.g. to reproduce Staem5's PCPseDNC feature block before fusing with PSP, k-mer, and PseEIIP encodings. Input is already a numeric feature matrix (encoding has already been performed) The task requires feature blocks other than dinucleotide physicochemical composition, e.g. only PSP or only PseEIIP features are needed Sequences are not RNA m5C segment data of the expected 41 bp window length http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Compute parallel correlation pseudo dinucleotide composition (PCPseDNC) features from RNA sequence segments, encoding 38 dinucleotide physicochemical properties. In Staem5 this is one of four feature blocks (PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) fused into the model input matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Compute parallel correlation pseudo dinucleotide composition (PCPseDNC) features from RNA sequence segments, encoding 38 dinucleotide physicochemical properties. In Staem5 this is one of four feature blocks (PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) fused into the model input matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature matrix (encoding has already been performed) The task requires feature blocks other than dinucleotide physicochemical composition, e.g. only PSP or only PseEIIP features are needed Sequences are not RNA m5C segment data of the expected 41 bp window length

skills.description: Use when solving a matrix factorization W=(RΣ)+A where the GRN adjacency matrix R (m×m) times the singular matrix Σ of the expression matrix A (m×n) is not invertible, so W must be recovered via the pseudoinverse.
skills.name: pseudoinverse-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: pseudoinverse-matrix-computation Use when solving a matrix factorization W=(RΣ)+A where the GRN adjacency matrix R (m×m) times the singular matrix Σ of the expression matrix A (m×n) is not invertible, so W must be recovered via the pseudoinverse. Equation 5 is applicable only when the number of cells equals the number of genes and RΣ is invertible — but in that case the pseudoinverse shortcut is unnecessary; the pseudoinverse route (Equation 6) is what handles the general case GRN quality is poor or unknown, since the accuracy of the GRN can affect the results of cell-cell communication for MDIC3 The analysis requires interpreting specific ligand-receptor pairs directly from the decomposition alone; MDIC3 needs a separate L-R extraction step (readLRDB/LR_exp against e.g. CellChatDB Human_LR.txt) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the product RΣ to solve the right submatrix W=(RΣ)+A in MDIC3, yielding an n×n cell-cell communication adjacency matrix from an m×n single-cell expression matrix. This step is required because RΣ is generally non-invertible when the number of cells and genes differ. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Computes the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the product RΣ to solve the right submatrix W=(RΣ)+A in MDIC3, yielding an n×n cell-cell communication adjacency matrix from an m×n single-cell expression matrix. This step is required because RΣ is generally non-invertible when the number of cells and genes differ.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Equation 5 is applicable only when the number of cells equals the number of genes and RΣ is invertible — but in that case the pseudoinverse shortcut is unnecessary; the pseudoinverse route (Equation 6) is what handles the general case GRN quality is poor or unknown, since the accuracy of the GRN can affect the results of cell-cell communication for MDIC3 The analysis requires interpreting specific ligand-receptor pairs directly from the decomposition alone; MDIC3 needs a separate L-R extraction step (readLRDB/LR_exp against e.g. CellChatDB Human_LR.txt)

skills.description: Use when Lamian XDE test results (per-gene fdr.overall from lamian_test/lamian_test_h5, e.g. sex tested at testvar=2 with batch columns adjusted) are available and significant genes must be grouped into pseudotemporal pattern clusters and plotted.
skills.name: pseudotemporal-gene-clustering-and-visualization
skills.search_text: pseudotemporal-gene-clustering-and-visualization Use when Lamian XDE test results (per-gene fdr.overall from lamian_test/lamian_test_h5, e.g. sex tested at testvar=2 with batch columns adjusted) are available and significant genes must be grouped into pseudotemporal pattern clusters and plotted. No genes pass the XDE significance cutoff (FDR.overall < 0.05), so there are no differential pseudotemporal patterns to cluster or plot. The question is differential topology or cell-density change (XCD) rather than gene-expression change along pseudotime; clusterGene/plotXDEHm operate on XDE gene results, not abundance or topology tests. The trajectory was built with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot, which Lamian's modules 1 and 2 do not support. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Clusters Lamian XDE genes passing FDR.overall < 0.05 by their covariate-specific fitted pseudotemporal expression patterns (clusterGene, e.g. k=14) and visualizes original, population-fitted, and covariate-group-difference profiles along pseudotime with plotXDEHm and plotClusterMeanAndDiff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Clusters Lamian XDE genes passing FDR.overall < 0.05 by their covariate-specific fitted pseudotemporal expression patterns (clusterGene, e.g. k=14) and visualizes original, population-fitted, and covariate-group-difference profiles along pseudotime with plotXDEHm and plotClusterMeanAndDiff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No genes pass the XDE significance cutoff (FDR.overall < 0.05), so there are no differential pseudotemporal patterns to cluster or plot. The question is differential topology or cell-density change (XCD) rather than gene-expression change along pseudotime; clusterGene/plotXDEHm operate on XDE gene results, not abundance or topology tests. The trajectory was built with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot, which Lamian's modules 1 and 2 do not support.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth pseudotime, e.g. quantifying pseudotime accuracy via Kendall rank correlation.
skills.name: pseudotime-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: pseudotime-accuracy-evaluation Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth pseudotime, e.g. quantifying pseudotime accuracy via Kendall rank correlation. Real scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., hematopoiesis, dentate gyrus, pancreatic endocrinogenesis, forebrain) where no simulated ground-truth pseudotime exists for Kendall correlation When the goal is trajectory topology or direction assignment rather than pseudotime ordering accuracy along paths Datasets where estimated RNA velocity is unreliable, since performance of all RNA velocity-based methods is affected by velocity inference accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark pseudotime inference accuracy by computing Kendall rank correlation between each trajectory inference method's inferred pseudotime and simulated ground-truth pseudotime on tree-structured datasets, comparing CellPath against Slingshot, VeTra, and CellRank. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Benchmark pseudotime inference accuracy by computing Kendall rank correlation between each trajectory inference method's inferred pseudotime and simulated ground-truth pseudotime on tree-structured datasets, comparing CellPath against Slingshot, VeTra, and CellRank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., hematopoiesis, dentate gyrus, pancreatic endocrinogenesis, forebrain) where no simulated ground-truth pseudotime exists for Kendall correlation When the goal is trajectory topology or direction assignment rather than pseudotime ordering accuracy along paths Datasets where estimated RNA velocity is unreliable, since performance of all RNA velocity-based methods is affected by velocity inference accuracy

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from two or more conditions (e.g., mock vs TGF-β treatment) must be compared along a shared developmental trajectory, and you need to test differential topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or condition-specific gene expression along lineages.
skills.name: pseudotime-based-condition-testing
skills.search_text: pseudotime-based-condition-testing Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from two or more conditions (e.g., mock vs TGF-β treatment) must be compared along a shared developmental trajectory, and you need to test differential topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or condition-specific gene expression along lineages. Cells are in a steady-state system with no dynamic transition, where cluster-based differential abundance methods (e.g., milo, DAseq) are appropriate Batch and condition are inherently confounded and cannot be separated, invalidating cross-condition trajectory comparison You lack per-cell condition labels or a reduced-dimension representation suitable for trajectory inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A three-step condiments workflow that tests whether single-cell dynamic processes differ between conditions by leveraging trajectory structure: differential topology (topologyTest), differential progression and fate selection along lineages (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression along lineages (tradeSeq conditionTest). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: A three-step condiments workflow that tests whether single-cell dynamic processes differ between conditions by leveraging trajectory structure: differential topology (topologyTest), differential progression and fate selection along lineages (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression along lineages (tradeSeq conditionTest).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are in a steady-state system with no dynamic transition, where cluster-based differential abundance methods (e.g., milo, DAseq) are appropriate Batch and condition are inherently confounded and cannot be separated, invalidating cross-condition trajectory comparison You lack per-cell condition labels or a reduced-dimension representation suitable for trajectory inference

skills.description: Use when time-series scRNA-seq data already have (or need) Monocle3 pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance changes significantly along pseudotime.
skills.name: pseudotime-based-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: pseudotime-based-differential-expression-testing Use when time-series scRNA-seq data already have (or need) Monocle3 pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance changes significantly along pseudotime. The data are not time-series scRNA-seq and no temporal/pseudotime ordering of cells is relevant to the biological question. Only static differential expression between labeled conditions is needed — standard DE tools apply, since scTITANS tests variation along pseudotime rather than between groups. Trajectory reconstruction itself is not feasible: the paper shows Monocle3 failed on some topologies (e.g. only Mpath reconstructed the eight CMP branches), so pseudotime inputs may be unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 scTITANS converts Monocle3-derived pseudotime into a time-dependent covariate statistical test, fitting per-gene and per-subcluster curves along pseudotime and calling differential genes/subclusters via F-statistics with bootstrap q-values at FDR 0.01. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: scTITANS converts Monocle3-derived pseudotime into a time-dependent covariate statistical test, fitting per-gene and per-subcluster curves along pseudotime and calling differential genes/subclusters via F-statistics with bootstrap q-values at FDR 0.01.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not time-series scRNA-seq and no temporal/pseudotime ordering of cells is relevant to the biological question. Only static differential expression between labeled conditions is needed — standard DE tools apply, since scTITANS tests variation along pseudotime rather than between groups. Trajectory reconstruction itself is not feasible: the paper shows Monocle3 failed on some topologies (e.g. only Mpath reconstructed the eight CMP branches), so pseudotime inputs may be unreliable.

skills.description: Use when pseudotime orderings from redPATH and baseline methods must be quantitatively compared on the same filtered expression matrix against known cell type/stage labels using CI, BI, KC, and POS scores.
skills.name: pseudotime-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: pseudotime-benchmark-evaluation Use when pseudotime orderings from redPATH and baseline methods must be quantitatively compared on the same filtered expression matrix against known cell type/stage labels using CI, BI, KC, and POS scores. The expression matrix has not yet been reduced to GO development-related genes and dispersion-filtered, since comparisons must run on identical filtered matrices The goal is single-method pseudotime inference rather than head-to-head benchmarking against baselines with known cell type labels The dataset lacks known cell type/stage labels, making CI/BI/KC/POS evaluation against ground truth impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark redPATH against SCORPIUS, TSCAN, Monocle2, and DPT on single-cell RNA-seq datasets by computing CI, BI, KC, and POS metrics from inferred pseudotemporal orderings against known cell type labels, and reproduce reported scores (e.g., redPATH CI 0.868, BI 0.973, KC 0.832 on the 56-cell G0-removed NSC-Llorens dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Benchmark redPATH against SCORPIUS, TSCAN, Monocle2, and DPT on single-cell RNA-seq datasets by computing CI, BI, KC, and POS metrics from inferred pseudotemporal orderings against known cell type labels, and reproduce reported scores (e.g., redPATH CI 0.868, BI 0.973, KC 0.832 on the 56-cell G0-removed NSC-Llorens dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has not yet been reduced to GO development-related genes and dispersion-filtered, since comparisons must run on identical filtered matrices The goal is single-method pseudotime inference rather than head-to-head benchmarking against baselines with known cell type labels The dataset lacks known cell type/stage labels, making CI/BI/KC/POS evaluation against ground truth impossible

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has a known number of branches and cell-type ordering (e.g., CMP GSE72857 with eight branches, HSMM with two, MEF with three) and you must choose which TI method to trust before pseudotime-based downstream analysis.
skills.name: pseudotime-benchmarking-on-real-datasets
skills.search_text: pseudotime-benchmarking-on-real-datasets Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has a known number of branches and cell-type ordering (e.g., CMP GSE72857 with eight branches, HSMM with two, MEF with three) and you must choose which TI method to trust before pseudotime-based downstream analysis. The dataset has no independently known branch structure or cell-type ordering to benchmark against, so per-method comparison is meaningless A single TI method is already fixed downstream (scTITANS uses Monocle3 for pseudotime) and no method-selection decision is needed The input is bulk time-series data rather than single-cell RNA-seq, where trajectory inference per cell is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark ten trajectory inference (TI) methods (Monocle, Monocle2, Monocle3, TSCAN, SLICER, GPfates, Slingshot, Destiny, Mpath, STEMNET) on scRNA-seq datasets with known branching topology to select the method whose reconstructed branches best match the reference cell-type ordering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.07.016
skills.summary: Benchmark ten trajectory inference (TI) methods (Monocle, Monocle2, Monocle3, TSCAN, SLICER, GPfates, Slingshot, Destiny, Mpath, STEMNET) on scRNA-seq datasets with known branching topology to select the method whose reconstructed branches best match the reference cell-type ordering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no independently known branch structure or cell-type ordering to benchmark against, so per-method comparison is meaningless A single TI method is already fixed downstream (scTITANS uses Monocle3 for pseudotime) and no method-selection decision is needed The input is bulk time-series data rather than single-cell RNA-seq, where trajectory inference per cell is not applicable

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has a cell pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g., monocle3) and the goal is to identify which MSigDB KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways are coordinated and active at successive developmental stages.
skills.name: pseudotime-binned-pal-averaging
skills.search_text: pseudotime-binned-pal-averaging Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has a cell pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g., monocle3) and the goal is to identify which MSigDB KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways are coordinated and active at successive developmental stages. Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Cells lack a meaningful trajectory/pseudotime ordering (static or spatially organized samples) — use spatially relevant pathway identification (compute.spatial.kld) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trajectory-coupled GSDensity analysis that averages per-cell pathway activity levels (PALs) across equal-width pseudotime bins and clusters the fitted PAL-vs-pseudotime curves, revealing curated pathways active at specific stages of development (e.g., E17.5 mouse cortex grouped into 8 k-medoids clusters). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Trajectory-coupled GSDensity analysis that averages per-cell pathway activity levels (PALs) across equal-width pseudotime bins and clusters the fitted PAL-vs-pseudotime curves, revealing curated pathways active at specific stages of development (e.g., E17.5 mouse cortex grouped into 8 k-medoids clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Cells lack a meaningful trajectory/pseudotime ordering (static or spatially organized samples) — use spatially relevant pathway identification (compute.spatial.kld) instead

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells from a new condition (e.g., Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-knockout GMPs) must be projected onto an existing wild-type branching trajectory to read off branch-level fate allocation.
skills.name: pseudotime-branch-visualization
skills.search_text: pseudotime-branch-visualization Use when scRNA-seq cells from a new condition (e.g., Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-knockout GMPs) must be projected onto an existing wild-type branching trajectory to read off branch-level fate allocation. The query cells have totally different fates from any present in the reference structure — the mapping procedure may not be optimal in that case. You need to learn a new trajectory from scratch rather than project cells onto an existing one — use STREAM's trajectory reconstruction workflow instead of the mapping feature. The data are cyclic or disconnected graph topologies — the paper notes STREAM requires further improvement to properly describe these more general structures. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize and quantify how single cells (e.g., genetically perturbed GMPs) distribute over the branching structure of a precomputed STREAM elastic-principal-graph trajectory, using STREAM's mapping feature to project new cells onto the fixed reference graph instead of re-fitting the trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Visualize and quantify how single cells (e.g., genetically perturbed GMPs) distribute over the branching structure of a precomputed STREAM elastic-principal-graph trajectory, using STREAM's mapping feature to project new cells onto the fixed reference graph instead of re-fitting the trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query cells have totally different fates from any present in the reference structure — the mapping procedure may not be optimal in that case. You need to learn a new trajectory from scratch rather than project cells onto an existing one — use STREAM's trajectory reconstruction workflow instead of the mapping feature. The data are cyclic or disconnected graph topologies — the paper notes STREAM requires further improvement to properly describe these more general structures.

skills.description: Use when you have run CellPath's all_in_one() on scRNA-seq data with scVelo-computed velocities and need per-cell pseudotime and branching assignments to identify lineage paths (e.g., α/β/δ endocrine fates) or run path-level differential expression.
skills.name: pseudotime-branching-assignment
skills.search_text: pseudotime-branching-assignment Use when you have run CellPath's all_in_one() on scRNA-seq data with scVelo-computed velocities and need per-cell pseudotime and branching assignments to identify lineage paths (e.g., α/β/δ endocrine fates) or run path-level differential expression. The goal is cluster-level trajectory topology only with no need for per-cell pseudotime — Directed-PAGA-style cluster graphs may suffice and CellPath's high-resolution output would be overly complex. RNA velocity estimates are unavailable or expected to be unreliable, since CellPath's performance is limited by the accuracy of RNA velocity inference. skills.description: Use when a hyperbolic scPhere embedding of a time-course single-cell dataset (e.g., C. elegans embryo GSE126954, 86,024 cells) must be checked for whether latent geometry encodes progression time as a pseudotime signal.

skills.search_text: pseudotime-correlation-analysis Use when a hyperbolic scPhere embedding of a time-course single-cell dataset (e.g., C. elegans embryo GSE126954, 86,024 cells) must be checked for whether latent geometry encodes progression time as a pseudotime signal. skills.description: Use when comparing trajectory-inference algorithms that each output a pseudotime ordering of the same scRNA-seq cells and you need a quantitative, gene-centric smoothness metric to rank them.

skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a trajectory reconstructed between two chosen cell states (e.g. from a rare or transitory subpopulation) rather than to score an already-computed ordering — Monocle 2 and other linear/branch-limited methods are unsuited to that task per the paper. skills.description: Use when single-cell data from multiple conditions has been embedded (e.g., Dim1/Dim2 reduced-dimension coordinates with cluster and condition labels) and you must decide whether to fit one common trajectory or test for differential topology and differential progression between conditions.
skills.name: pseudotime-lineage-fitting
skills.search_text: pseudotime-lineage-fitting Use when single-cell data from multiple conditions has been embedded (e.g., Dim1/Dim2 reduced-dimension coordinates with cluster and condition labels) and you must decide whether to fit one common trajectory or test for differential topology and differential progression between conditions. Cells are in steady state with no dynamic/trajectory structure, where cluster-based differential abundance methods are more appropriate than trajectory fitting. The trajectory inference method does not allow specification of an underlying skeleton structure, since topologyTest requires a mapping between trajectories across condition-label permutations (only e.g. slingshot, TSCAN work). The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages, which is handled downstream by fitGAM and conditionTest rather than trajectory-level topology/progression tests. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit a common trajectory on a low-dimensional embedding with slingshot using cluster labels, extract per-lineage pseudotimes, and use condiments' topologyTest and progressionTest to decide whether one common trajectory suffices or whether conditions differ in topology or progression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Fit a common trajectory on a low-dimensional embedding with slingshot using cluster labels, extract per-lineage pseudotimes, and use condiments' topologyTest and progressionTest to decide whether one common trajectory suffices or whether conditions differ in topology or progression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are in steady state with no dynamic/trajectory structure, where cluster-based differential abundance methods are more appropriate than trajectory fitting. The trajectory inference method does not allow specification of an underlying skeleton structure, since topologyTest requires a mapping between trajectories across condition-label permutations (only e.g. slingshot, TSCAN work). The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages, which is handled downstream by fitGAM and conditionTest rather than trajectory-level topology/progression tests.

When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is itself faulty — the authors note trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case (e.g. spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset) When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable, which the authors explicitly do not recommend for Cytopath trajectory inference When the dataset has no per-cell elapsed-time or ordering ground truth to correlate pseudotime against http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates RNA velocity-based pseudotime (Cytopath) as a proxy for the cell's internal clock by correlating it with a known external time label — stimulation duration (0–120 min) in the scNT-seq mouse cortical neuron dataset — and benchmarking it against the Cytopath-Euclidean ablation that removes velocity information. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Validates RNA velocity-based pseudotime (Cytopath) as a proxy for the cell's internal clock by correlating it with a known external time label — stimulation duration (0–120 min) in the scNT-seq mouse cortical neuron dataset — and benchmarking it against the Cytopath-Euclidean ablation that removes velocity information.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation is itself faulty — the authors note trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case (e.g. spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset) When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable, which the authors explicitly do not recommend for Cytopath trajectory inference When the dataset has no per-cell elapsed-time or ordering ground truth to correlate pseudotime against

skills.description: Use when single-cell flow cytometry data of radially symmetric multicellular spheroids have been ordered in pseudotime and marker profiles (Ki-67, p27, DNA, RNA) must be recovered versus distance from the spheroid surface.
skills.name: pseudotime-to-spatial-scale-transformation
skills.search_text: pseudotime-to-spatial-scale-transformation Use when single-cell flow cytometry data of radially symmetric multicellular spheroids have been ordered in pseudotime and marker profiles (Ki-67, p27, DNA, RNA) must be recovered versus distance from the spheroid surface. When no theoretically or empirically justified true-scale distribution can be constructed, e.g. stem cell differentiation, where target cell densities and death/division rates at every stage are unknown When the pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is unreliable, since MAPiT inherits errors in cell order When the biological system lacks radial symmetry or a known cell-density profile that can serve as the transformation target http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 MAPiT is a measure-preserving transformation (MATLAB implementation: jointDensityPseudotimeY.m, preMAPiT.m, MAPiT.m) that converts pseudotime trajectories from Wanderlust or Diffusion Maps into real spatial scales, e.g. distance from the spheroid surface, using prior knowledge of the true-scale cell-density distribution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-60400-z
skills.summary: MAPiT is a measure-preserving transformation (MATLAB implementation: jointDensityPseudotimeY.m, preMAPiT.m, MAPiT.m) that converts pseudotime trajectories from Wanderlust or Diffusion Maps into real spatial scales, e.g. distance from the spheroid surface, using prior knowledge of the true-scale cell-density distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no theoretically or empirically justified true-scale distribution can be constructed, e.g. stem cell differentiation, where target cell densities and death/division rates at every stage are unknown When the pseudotime ordering from the trajectory inference algorithm is unreliable, since MAPiT inherits errors in cell order When the biological system lacks radial symmetry or a known cell-density profile that can serve as the transformation target

skills.description: Use when in silico TF perturbation simulations (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) must be quantified as scores by comparing simulated transitions to the pseudotime differentiation gradient.
skills.name: pseudotime-to-vector-field-conversion
skills.search_text: pseudotime-to-vector-field-conversion Use when in silico TF perturbation simulations (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) must be quantified as scores by comparing simulated transitions to the pseudotime differentiation gradient. The dataset lacks a pseudotime ordering or a low-dimensional embedding, so no reference gradient vector field can be constructed. The perturbed TF is not covered by the base GRN (e.g., not present in the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas base GRN), making the simulated transition field meaningless. The goal is cell-type classification or identity-continuum measurement (use Capybara instead) rather than perturbation-effect scoring via vector-field inner products. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts CellOracle pseudotime-derived cell-state transitions into a 2D grid-based gradient vector field on the low-dimensional embedding so that simulated TF-perturbation transitions can be compared against reference differentiation vectors via per-grid-point inner products (perturbation scores). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Converts CellOracle pseudotime-derived cell-state transitions into a 2D grid-based gradient vector field on the low-dimensional embedding so that simulated TF-perturbation transitions can be compared against reference differentiation vectors via per-grid-point inner products (perturbation scores).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks a pseudotime ordering or a low-dimensional embedding, so no reference gradient vector field can be constructed. The perturbed TF is not covered by the base GRN (e.g., not present in the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas base GRN), making the simulated transition field meaningless. The goal is cell-type classification or identity-continuum measurement (use Capybara instead) rather than perturbation-effect scoring via vector-field inner products.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have a pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g. monocle3 on GSE153162 E17.5 mouse cortex) and the goal is to find which pathway gene sets are active at each developmental stage and how their activity curves cluster over pseudotime.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-analysis Use when scRNA-seq cells have a pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g. monocle3 on GSE153162 E17.5 mouse cortex) and the goal is to find which pathway gene sets are active at each developmental stage and how their activity curves cluster over pseudotime. Data are spatial transcriptomics with no trajectory ordering; use the weighted-KDE spatial relevance workflow (compute.spatial.kld) instead of pseudotime binning Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes; GSDensity is not suitable for such data and imputation is suggested but not implemented Only pathway-level enrichment of a predefined cluster is needed without developmental ordering; a simpler coordination test (compute.kld alone) suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Combine monocle3 pseudotime ordering of single-cell data with GSDensity pathway activity levels (PALs) to identify curated KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways active at successive stages of mouse brain development, grouping fitted PAL-vs-pseudotime curves into stage-pattern clusters via k-medoids. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Combine monocle3 pseudotime ordering of single-cell data with GSDensity pathway activity levels (PALs) to identify curated KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways active at successive stages of mouse brain development, grouping fitted PAL-vs-pseudotime curves into stage-pattern clusters via k-medoids.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are spatial transcriptomics with no trajectory ordering; use the weighted-KDE spatial relevance workflow (compute.spatial.kld) instead of pseudotime binning Input is targeted gene-panel data with limited numbers of genes; GSDensity is not suitable for such data and imputation is suggested but not implemented Only pathway-level enrichment of a predefined cluster is needed without developmental ordering; a simpler coordination test (compute.kld alone) suffices

skills.description: Use when a splicing-free velocity or trajectory method must be validated against a multi-omics baseline: compare pseudotime ordering, streamplot direction, and gene phase-portrait dynamics on a shared dataset.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-benchmarking Use when a splicing-free velocity or trajectory method must be validated against a multi-omics baseline: compare pseudotime ordering, streamplot direction, and gene phase-portrait dynamics on a shared dataset. The dataset has reliable spliced/unspliced counts and splicing-based models (scVelo/velocyto) are appropriate — TFvelo's benchmarking here targets datasets lacking splicing information Large-scale datasets where TFvelo's lower time efficiency versus scVelo is prohibitive Genes known to be poorly modeled — TFvelo cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a RNA-velocity/trajectory method (e.g., TFvelo, RNA-only) against a multi-omics baseline (MultiVelo) by comparing inferred pseudotime ordering, stream direction on UMAP, and per-gene phase-portrait fits on example genes such as AHI1, NTRK2, and GRIN2B. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Benchmark a RNA-velocity/trajectory method (e.g., TFvelo, RNA-only) against a multi-omics baseline (MultiVelo) by comparing inferred pseudotime ordering, stream direction on UMAP, and per-gene phase-portrait fits on example genes such as AHI1, NTRK2, and GRIN2B.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has reliable spliced/unspliced counts and splicing-based models (scVelo/velocyto) are appropriate — TFvelo's benchmarking here targets datasets lacking splicing information Large-scale datasets where TFvelo's lower time efficiency versus scVelo is prohibitive Genes known to be poorly modeled — TFvelo cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14)

skills.description: Use when comparing two single-cell cohorts (e.g., AI-generated/semi-profiled vs. real-profiled) to verify that developmental or disease-progression trajectories are preserved, via Monocle3 pseudotime computed on shared UMAP coordinates.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-correlation
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-correlation Use when comparing two single-cell cohorts (e.g., AI-generated/semi-profiled vs. real-profiled) to verify that developmental or disease-progression trajectories are preserved, via Monocle3 pseudotime computed on shared UMAP coordinates. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed cell-type-level deconvolution result — no single-cell resolution means pseudotime cannot be computed (bulk methods are limited to cell-type-level resolution) The two cohorts lack a shared UMAP embedding or comparable cell-type structure, so identical root placement is impossible You need cell-cell interaction strength comparison or gene-set enrichment fidelity — those are separate analyses (CellChat correlation, GSEApy RRHO), not pseudotime correlation Validates that a semi-profiled single-cell cohort (generated by scSemiProfiler) reproduces the pseudotime trajectories of the real-profiled cohort by running Monocle3 on shared UMAP coordinates and correlating grid-averaged pseudotime values. This is one of the downstream-fidelity checks from the COVID-19 cohort study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Validates that a semi-profiled single-cell cohort (generated by scSemiProfiler) reproduces the pseudotime trajectories of the real-profiled cohort by running Monocle3 on shared UMAP coordinates and correlating grid-averaged pseudotime values. This is one of the downstream-fidelity checks from the COVID-19 cohort study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed cell-type-level deconvolution result — no single-cell resolution means pseudotime cannot be computed (bulk methods are limited to cell-type-level resolution) The two cohorts lack a shared UMAP embedding or comparable cell-type structure, so identical root placement is impossible You need cell-cell interaction strength comparison or gene-set enrichment fidelity — those are separate analyses (CellChat correlation, GSEApy RRHO), not pseudotime correlation

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous biological transition (e.g. naive CD4+ T cell activation through intermediate populations at 0 h, 12 h, 24 h) and you need pathway dynamics along the trajectory rather than a two-group comparison.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous biological transition (e.g. naive CD4+ T cell activation through intermediate populations at 0 h, 12 h, 24 h) and you need pathway dynamics along the trajectory rather than a two-group comparison. The question is a simple two-population comparison (e.g. 0 h resting vs 12 h intermediate cells) — a classical two-sample compare_pathways call is the appropriate design, as used as the internal control in the pseudotime analysis Cells form discrete, unrelated clusters with no continuous transition — ordering them on pseudotime milestones would be unjustified Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated feature table — trajectory inference needs per-cell expression distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer a pseudotime trajectory from single-cell RNA-seq data using dyno (ti_slingshot), bin cells onto trajectory milestones, and feed the milestone populations into SCPA's multisample compare_pathways to quantify pathway activity across differentiation or activation transitions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Infer a pseudotime trajectory from single-cell RNA-seq data using dyno (ti_slingshot), bin cells onto trajectory milestones, and feed the milestone populations into SCPA's multisample compare_pathways to quantify pathway activity across differentiation or activation transitions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is a simple two-population comparison (e.g. 0 h resting vs 12 h intermediate cells) — a classical two-sample compare_pathways call is the appropriate design, as used as the internal control in the pseudotime analysis Cells form discrete, unrelated clusters with no continuous transition — ordering them on pseudotime milestones would be unjustified Input is bulk RNA-seq or an already-aggregated feature table — trajectory inference needs per-cell expression distributions

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous state-transition process (e.g., acinar-to-ductal transdifferentiation) and you need a pseudotime-anchored reference direction to benchmark velocity vectors against, as in the ADM-axis concordance task.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous state-transition process (e.g., acinar-to-ductal transdifferentiation) and you need a pseudotime-anchored reference direction to benchmark velocity vectors against, as in the ADM-axis concordance task. Data represent discrete, disconnected cell populations with no continuous transdifferentiation axis — diffusion-map pseudotime anchoring will be meaningless You need regulatory network or velocity inference itself; this skill supplies the manifold reference, while tools like scKINETICS fit the per-cell velocities and GRN http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer per-cell pseudotime along a transdifferentiation manifold (e.g., acinar-to-ductal metaplasia in GSE207943 acute pancreatitis scRNA-seq) with Palantir, then convert the trajectory into per-cell reference directions used to evaluate or constrain RNA velocity methods such as scKINETICS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Infer per-cell pseudotime along a transdifferentiation manifold (e.g., acinar-to-ductal metaplasia in GSE207943 acute pancreatitis scRNA-seq) with Palantir, then convert the trajectory into per-cell reference directions used to evaluate or constrain RNA velocity methods such as scKINETICS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data represent discrete, disconnected cell populations with no continuous transdifferentiation axis — diffusion-map pseudotime anchoring will be meaningless You need regulatory network or velocity inference itself; this skill supplies the manifold reference, while tools like scKINETICS fit the per-cell velocities and GRN

skills.description: Use when a single-cell multi-omic dataset has been co-embedded, batch-corrected (RunHarmony) and sub-clustered, and the goal is to order clusters along a differentiation continuum (e.g. progenitors to myofibroblasts) for GRN inference.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when a single-cell multi-omic dataset has been co-embedded, batch-corrected (RunHarmony) and sub-clustered, and the goal is to order clusters along a differentiation continuum (e.g. progenitors to myofibroblasts) for GRN inference. Cells do not lie on a differentiation/transition continuum (e.g. static, unrelated populations) — the user-supplied cluster ordering would be arbitrary and the trajectory meaningless. Modalities have not been co-embedded and batch-corrected (CoembedData + RunHarmony), so snRNA and snATAC cells cannot be jointly ordered or paired with PairCells. No meaningful sub-clusters with significant group differences (CompareCellProp) exist to serve as trajectory nodes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Fits a supervised pseudotime trajectory over a co-embedded snRNA/snATAC Seurat object using scMEGA's ArchR-based AddTrajectory, ordering predefined cell clusters from a progenitor state (SCARA5+ fibroblasts) to a terminal state (POSTN/COL1A1+ myofibroblasts) so that trajectory-dependent genes and TFs can be selected downstream. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Fits a supervised pseudotime trajectory over a co-embedded snRNA/snATAC Seurat object using scMEGA's ArchR-based AddTrajectory, ordering predefined cell clusters from a progenitor state (SCARA5+ fibroblasts) to a terminal state (POSTN/COL1A1+ myofibroblasts) so that trajectory-dependent genes and TFs can be selected downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells do not lie on a differentiation/transition continuum (e.g. static, unrelated populations) — the user-supplied cluster ordering would be arbitrary and the trajectory meaningless. Modalities have not been co-embedded and batch-corrected (CoembedData + RunHarmony), so snRNA and snATAC cells cannot be jointly ordered or paired with PairCells. No meaningful sub-clusters with significant group differences (CompareCellProp) exist to serve as trajectory nodes.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data from two or more conditions must be placed on a common trajectory to ask whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data from two or more conditions must be placed on a common trajectory to ask whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages. The system is at steady state with no dynamic process — clustering plus differential abundance methods (milo, DAseq) is the appropriate approach instead Only one condition is present, so there is no between-condition comparison for topologyTest, progressionTest, or fateSelectionTest The goal is differential abundance without any trajectory structure, where cluster-based methods suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A three-step condiments workflow for inferring and testing cell trajectories across multiple conditions: differential topology (topologyTest), trajectory-level abundance changes (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression along lineages (conditionTest), applied here to the fibrosis ILD scRNA-Seq case study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: A three-step condiments workflow for inferring and testing cell trajectories across multiple conditions: differential topology (topologyTest), trajectory-level abundance changes (progressionTest, fateSelectionTest), and gene-level differential expression along lineages (conditionTest), applied here to the fibrosis ILD scRNA-Seq case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The system is at steady state with no dynamic process — clustering plus differential abundance methods (milo, DAseq) is the appropriate approach instead Only one condition is present, so there is no between-condition comparison for topologyTest, progressionTest, or fateSelectionTest The goal is differential abundance without any trajectory structure, where cluster-based methods suffice

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell counts with known developmental/staged time labels (e.g., Chu GSE75748, Scialdone GSE74994, Petropoulos E-MTAB-3929) and need to test whether imputation recovers true temporal cell order.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when you have single-cell counts with known developmental/staged time labels (e.g., Chu GSE75748, Scialdone GSE74994, Petropoulos E-MTAB-3929) and need to test whether imputation recovers true temporal cell order. The dataset has no external time/stage labels or biological ordering against which POS and Kendall's correlation can be computed The goal is clustering, DE analysis, or visualization rather than temporal ordering — the article notes prior imputation methods improve these analyses differently You need a single universally best imputation method: the article's discussion warns 'There is no consensus about which imputation method is the best' and performance varies by dataset and downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark whether imputation improves pseudotime ordering of developmental scRNA-seq cells by inferring trajectories with TSCAN and Monocle on raw versus imputed matrices (Bfimpute, scImpute, DrImpute) and scoring orderings against true developmental time with POS and Kendall's rank correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Benchmark whether imputation improves pseudotime ordering of developmental scRNA-seq cells by inferring trajectories with TSCAN and Monocle on raw versus imputed matrices (Bfimpute, scImpute, DrImpute) and scoring orderings against true developmental time with POS and Kendall's rank correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no external time/stage labels or biological ordering against which POS and Kendall's correlation can be computed The goal is clustering, DE analysis, or visualization rather than temporal ordering — the article notes prior imputation methods improve these analyses differently You need a single universally best imputation method: the article's discussion warns 'There is no consensus about which imputation method is the best' and performance varies by dataset and downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when dropout-affected scRNA-seq data has been imputed (e.g., with SERM vs. MAGIC) and the goal is to verify that developmental trajectories and state transitions are recovered, not just gene values.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when dropout-affected scRNA-seq data has been imputed (e.g., with SERM vs. MAGIC) and the goal is to verify that developmental trajectories and state transitions are recovered, not just gene values. Input matrices have no ground-truth stage labels or known developmental ordering, so pseudotime recovery cannot be validated against reference trajectory structure Small genomic datasets where SERM's estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution, leading to inaccurate imputation values and misleading trajectories Batch-effect-critical settings, since batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply TSCAN and Slingshot pseudotime inference to reference, dropout-affected observed, and imputed scRNA-seq matrices (zebrafish development, EB differentiation), then visualize with PHATE to test whether SERM-based imputation preserves continuous developmental trajectories and state transitions without manifold distortion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Apply TSCAN and Slingshot pseudotime inference to reference, dropout-affected observed, and imputed scRNA-seq matrices (zebrafish development, EB differentiation), then visualize with PHATE to test whether SERM-based imputation preserves continuous developmental trajectories and state transitions without manifold distortion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrices have no ground-truth stage labels or known developmental ordering, so pseudotime recovery cannot be validated against reference trajectory structure Small genomic datasets where SERM's estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution, leading to inaccurate imputation values and misleading trajectories Batch-effect-critical settings, since batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. GSE81682 mouse HSPC from Nestorowa et al., 2016) must be ordered along a pseudotime trajectory with slingshot and visualized as group-wise colour groups in CellexalVR.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-slingshot
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-slingshot Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. GSE81682 mouse HSPC from Nestorowa et al., 2016) must be ordered along a pseudotime trajectory with slingshot and visualized as group-wise colour groups in CellexalVR. The analysis goal is differential expression between predefined groups rather than trajectory ordering along a hand-traced path The dataset has no biologically meaningful start/stop clusters, so slingshot pseudotime would be uninterpretable Input is not single-cell expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already-computed pseudotime values) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs slingshot-based pseudotime trajectory inference on selected cells partitioned into four clusters, orders cells by pseudotime, splits them into ten colour groups, and generates a hierarchically clustered heatmap of correlated genes — the in-session trajectory workflow of CellexalVR's cellexalvrR backend. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Runs slingshot-based pseudotime trajectory inference on selected cells partitioned into four clusters, orders cells by pseudotime, splits them into ten colour groups, and generates a hierarchically clustered heatmap of correlated genes — the in-session trajectory workflow of CellexalVR's cellexalvrR backend.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential expression between predefined groups rather than trajectory ordering along a hand-traced path The dataset has no biologically meaningful start/stop clusters, so slingshot pseudotime would be uninterpretable Input is not single-cell expression data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or already-computed pseudotime values)

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether pseudotime-based approaches such as TSCAN can identify differentiation pathways on single-cell RNA-seq data given the same number of clusters as a class-informed method, or when comparing trajectory inference to visualization baselines.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-visualization
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-visualization Use when evaluating whether pseudotime-based approaches such as TSCAN can identify differentiation pathways on single-cell RNA-seq data given the same number of clusters as a class-informed method, or when comparing trajectory inference to visualization baselines. When the goal is a class-informed visualization integrating prior cluster assignments — GraphDDP's force-based layout with -c class_confidence is the appropriate tool instead When only a dimensionality-reduction baseline (t-SNE, PCA, MDS) is needed without trajectory inference When quantitative benchmarking metrics are required — the paper reports only qualitative, expert-review validation for these baselines http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run TSCAN cluster-based minimum-spanning-tree pseudotime inference as a baseline against graph-embedding visualizations like GraphDDP, overlaying the inferred pseudotime on intestinal epithelial and myeloid progenitor single-cell data to test whether trajectory-only methods recover differentiation pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Run TSCAN cluster-based minimum-spanning-tree pseudotime inference as a baseline against graph-embedding visualizations like GraphDDP, overlaying the inferred pseudotime on intestinal epithelial and myeloid progenitor single-cell data to test whether trajectory-only methods recover differentiation pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a class-informed visualization integrating prior cluster assignments — GraphDDP's force-based layout with -c class_confidence is the appropriate tool instead When only a dimensionality-reduction baseline (t-SNE, PCA, MDS) is needed without trajectory inference When quantitative benchmarking metrics are required — the paper reports only qualitative, expert-review validation for these baselines

skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-with-scfates Use when you have SiFT-filtered AnnData expression (e.g. local spatial signal removed via a coordinate-based kernel) and need to order cells along a trajectory and split genes into early/late pseudotime groups. skills.summary: Runs pseudotime/trajectory inference with scFates on SiFT-filtered single-cell expression data (e.g. the APAP liver-regeneration ST slides) and partitions genes into early and late pseudotime groups for downstream figure assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input data still contains the local spatial-neighborhood signal (no SiFT filtering with a coordinate-based kernel has been applied), since the migratory subpopulation and its trajectory are otherwise obscured When the analysis goal is marker discovery or clustering itself rather than trajectory ordering — use scanpy rank_genes_groups and joint Leiden clustering instead

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells form continuous pseudotemporal trajectories (e.g. E14.5 embryonic skin dermal/epidermal states) and you need cell-state-specific ligand-receptor signaling rather than cluster-level communication.
skills.name: pseudotime-trajectory-signaling-analysis
skills.search_text: pseudotime-trajectory-signaling-analysis Use when scRNA-seq cells form continuous pseudotemporal trajectories (e.g. E14.5 embryonic skin dermal/epidermal states) and you need cell-state-specific ligand-receptor signaling rather than cluster-level communication. Cells do not form continuous trajectories or pseudotime ordering is unavailable — standard cluster-to-cluster CellChat analysis suffices. Input lacks cell-group labels or has not passed QC — CellChat requires prior cell clustering and quality-filtered expression data. The goal is spatially-resolved communication; this label-free workflow does not model spatial proximity (use SpatialCellChat instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infer ligand-receptor communication along continuous cell-state pseudotime trajectories (not just discrete clusters) using CellChat, e.g. predicting 88 significant interactions across 22 signaling pathways along E14.5 embryonic mouse skin dermal/epidermal trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Infer ligand-receptor communication along continuous cell-state pseudotime trajectories (not just discrete clusters) using CellChat, e.g. predicting 88 significant interactions across 22 signaling pathways along E14.5 embryonic mouse skin dermal/epidermal trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells do not form continuous trajectories or pseudotime ordering is unavailable — standard cluster-to-cluster CellChat analysis suffices. skills.search_text: qphate-embedding-biomarker-thresholding Use when transferring single-cell atlas latent structure (e.g., the stage-4 Human Colon Cancer Atlas c295) onto bulk RNA patient profiles to create binary biomarkers for survival/differential-treatment-effect testing, and standard PHATE or NMF-derived biomarkers lack statistical significance. When the reference and target datasets require batch-effect correction or alignment — the study explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets, so raw transferred coordinates may be confounded. When only classical dimensionality reduction suffices — the article reports classical NMF and PHATE biomarkers produced no statistically significant differential treatment effects, but if no differential effect is biologically expected, this added machinery is unnecessary. When single-cell data are not available as an atlas reference — the method depends on inferring latent variables from an scRNAseq atlas before deconvolution onto bulk profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Constructs binary patient biomarkers from q-diffused PHATE (qPHATE) embeddings: atlas-inferred qPHATE coordinates are transferred onto patient bulk RNA by linear deconvolution and thresholded along their principal component, yielding latent-variable biomarkers with sufficient differential treatment-effect signal to reach FDR-corrected significance in the CALGB/SWOG 80405 mCRC trial where classical PHATE embeddings fail. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Constructs binary patient biomarkers from q-diffused PHATE (qPHATE) embeddings: atlas-inferred qPHATE coordinates are transferred onto patient bulk RNA by linear deconvolution and thresholded along their principal component, yielding latent-variable biomarkers with sufficient differential treatment-effect signal to reach FDR-corrected significance in the CALGB/SWOG 80405 mCRC trial where classical PHATE embeddings fail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the reference and target datasets require batch-effect correction or alignment — the study explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate datasets, so raw transferred coordinates may be confounded. When only classical dimensionality reduction suffices — the article reports classical NMF and PHATE biomarkers produced no statistically significant differential treatment effects, but if no differential effect is biologically expected, this added machinery is unnecessary. When single-cell data are not available as an atlas reference — the method depends on inferring latent variables from an scRNAseq atlas before deconvolution onto bulk profiles.
