skills.summary: Reproduces the article's comparison of random forest vs logistic regression classifiers used as the base learner inside an active learning loop for single-cell annotation, quantifying RF's relative F1 improvement over LR under random initial training-set selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the initial training set is guaranteed to contain all cell types (e.g. marker-informed or adaptive-reweighting selection), since the RF-vs-LR advantage was established specifically under random initial selection of 20 cells When the goal is cell selection/subsampling itself (adaptive reweighting, self-training) rather than comparing classifier backends within an active learning loop When data are not log-normalized single-cell expression matrices with ground-truth labels; CyTOF-style or other feature tables without cell type annotations are out of scope for this comparison

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-type replicability (e.g., neuron vs non-neuron AUROC) with random gene sets and you need to test how set size (100 vs 800 genes) or cross-validation variability bins influence MetaNeighbor performance.
skills.name: random-gene-set-size-sampling
skills.search_text: random-gene-set-size-sampling Use when benchmarking cell-type replicability (e.g., neuron vs non-neuron AUROC) with random gene sets and you need to test how set size (100 vs 800 genes) or cross-validation variability bins influence MetaNeighbor performance. When the analysis goal is cross-dataset matching without known cell-type labels — unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes (top-quartile variable genes) is the appropriate mode instead. When gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — MetaNeighbor requires matching names and multi-gene sets to run. When the question is identifying candidate marker genes for replicable subtypes rather than characterizing gene-set-size effects on AUROC. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Skill for quantifying how gene set size and expression variability affect MetaNeighbor AUROC by sampling random gene sets (e.g., 100 sets of 100 genes vs 800 genes) from the mn_data/GOmouse R environment and running supervised MetaNeighbor with leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Skill for quantifying how gene set size and expression variability affect MetaNeighbor AUROC by sampling random gene sets (e.g., 100 sets of 100 genes vs 800 genes) from the mn_data/GOmouse R environment and running supervised MetaNeighbor with leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is cross-dataset matching without known cell-type labels — unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes (top-quartile variable genes) is the appropriate mode instead. When gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — MetaNeighbor requires matching names and multi-gene sets to run. When the question is identifying candidate marker genes for replicable subtypes rather than characterizing gene-set-size effects on AUROC.

skills.description: Use when quantifying pathway/module activity from a normalized gene expression matrix and you need empirical p-values for PC1-based activity statistics (L1, Median Exp) that distinguish shifted from overdispersed gene sets.
skills.name: random-geneset-null-distribution-sampling
skills.search_text: random-geneset-null-distribution-sampling Use when quantifying pathway/module activity from a normalized gene expression matrix and you need empirical p-values for PC1-based activity statistics (L1, Median Exp) that distinguish shifted from overdispersed gene sets. The expression matrix is raw/unnormalized — rRoma works with normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) The dataset contains many missing values that have not been imputed (imputation via the mice low-rank PCA procedure is recommended beforehand) The analysis goal is gene-level differential expression rather than gene-set/module activity scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Assess statistical significance of gene set activity (as implemented in rROMA) by generating null distributions of L1 (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median sample projection on PC1) statistics from randomly generated gene sets of matched size, then classifying modules as shifted or overdispersed by empirical ppv p-values (BH-corrected) with a 0.05 threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: Assess statistical significance of gene set activity (as implemented in rROMA) by generating null distributions of L1 (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median sample projection on PC1) statistics from randomly generated gene sets of matched size, then classifying modules as shifted or overdispersed by empirical ppv p-values (BH-corrected) with a 0.05 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw/unnormalized — rRoma works with normalized data (e.g. cpm from edgeR or vst from DESeq2) The dataset contains many missing values that have not been imputed (imputation via the mice low-rank PCA procedure is recommended beforehand) The analysis goal is gene-level differential expression rather than gene-set/module activity scoring

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a marker-selection method (e.g., scGeneFit on CBMC scRNA-seq) and a size-matched random-gene baseline is needed to show that reported classification error reflects informed marker choice rather than panel size.
skills.name: random-marker-set-sampling
skills.search_text: random-marker-set-sampling Use when benchmarking a marker-selection method (e.g., scGeneFit on CBMC scRNA-seq) and a size-matched random-gene baseline is needed to show that reported classification error reflects informed marker choice rather than panel size. The goal is to select genuinely informative markers for cell type discrimination — a random panel has no optimization rationale and high error by design Labels are not categorical cell types (e.g., trajectory time points or spatial locations), since the kNN label-classification baseline assumes a flat label partition Input is already a reduced feature table or a fixed curated panel — there is no gene universe from which to sample a matched-size random set http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Baseline procedure from the scGeneFit paper (Nature Communications, 2021) that samples a marker set of random genes matched in size to the method-selected panel, so that discriminatory power (via k-nearest-neighbor label classification in the reduced marker space) can be compared against jointly optimized and curated marker sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Baseline procedure from the scGeneFit paper (Nature Communications, 2021) that samples a marker set of random genes matched in size to the method-selected panel, so that discriminatory power (via k-nearest-neighbor label classification in the reduced marker space) can be compared against jointly optimized and curated marker sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to select genuinely informative markers for cell type discrimination — a random panel has no optimization rationale and high error by design Labels are not categorical cell types (e.g., trajectory time points or spatial locations), since the kNN label-classification baseline assumes a flat label partition Input is already a reduced feature table or a fixed curated panel — there is no gene universe from which to sample a matched-size random set

skills.description: Use when denoising a sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (e.g. 95%-sparse scRNA-seq) and you need to decide which eigenvectors/gene sets reflect signal versus sparsity artifacts.
skills.name: random-matrix-eigenvector-localization-analysis
skills.search_text: random-matrix-eigenvector-localization-analysis Use when denoising a sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (e.g. 95%-sparse scRNA-seq) and you need to decide which eigenvectors/gene sets reflect signal versus sparsity artifacts. Input is dense/low-sparsity data where sparsity-induced eigenvector localization is not a concern (the method targets ~95%-sparse single-cell matrices). You need imputation or zero-inflated modeling (e.g. MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI/DCA) rather than RMT-based feature selection and denoising. The dataset is too small for a meaningful covariance spectrum, so Tracy-Widom/Marchenko-Pastur universality comparisons are unreliable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Analyzes eigenvalue/eigenvector spectra of a single-cell expression matrix via random matrix theory (RMT), using eigenvector localization as a phase-transition marker to separate noise, sparsity-induced spurious signal (~3%), and true biological signal (~2%) from the ~95% RMT-compatible bulk. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Analyzes eigenvalue/eigenvector spectra of a single-cell expression matrix via random matrix theory (RMT), using eigenvector localization as a phase-transition marker to separate noise, sparsity-induced spurious signal (~3%), and true biological signal (~2%) from the ~95% RMT-compatible bulk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is dense/low-sparsity data where sparsity-induced eigenvector localization is not a concern (the method targets ~95%-sparse single-cell matrices). You need imputation or zero-inflated modeling (e.g. MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI/DCA) rather than RMT-based feature selection and denoising. The dataset is too small for a meaningful covariance spectrum, so Tracy-Widom/Marchenko-Pastur universality comparisons are unreliable.

skills.description: Use when you need a reproducible, size-controlled workload to benchmark linear-algebra implementations (SVD variants, matrix multiplication, core-count scaling) before applying them to real data.
skills.name: random-matrix-simulation
skills.search_text: random-matrix-simulation Use when you need a reproducible, size-controlled workload to benchmark linear-algebra implementations (SVD variants, matrix multiplication, core-count scaling) before applying them to real data. The goal is to time methods on real empirical data (e.g., actual scRNA-seq count matrices or TCGA BRCA_data) rather than on controlled synthetic workloads The matrices are much smaller than 1000×1000, where iterative partial SVD overhead can dominate and the reported speedup regime (90%+) will not hold The analysis requires matrices with realistic structure (sparsity, zero inflation, batch effects) — iid standard-normal entries deliberately strip all such structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generate synthetic 1000×1000 standard-normal matrices in R (with a fixed seed) as controlled benchmark inputs for timing linear-algebra routines such as base svd, RSpectra svds, %*%, and OpenMP-parallel RcppEigen/RcppArmadillo backends. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Generate synthetic 1000×1000 standard-normal matrices in R (with a fixed seed) as controlled benchmark inputs for timing linear-algebra routines such as base svd, RSpectra svds, %*%, and OpenMP-parallel RcppEigen/RcppArmadillo backends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to time methods on real empirical data (e.g., actual scRNA-seq count matrices or TCGA BRCA_data) rather than on controlled synthetic workloads The matrices are much smaller than 1000×1000, where iterative partial SVD overhead can dominate and the reported speedup regime (90%+) will not hold The analysis requires matrices with realistic structure (sparsity, zero inflation, batch effects) — iid standard-normal entries deliberately strip all such structure

skills.description: Use when analyzing sparse scRNA-seq count data and a data-driven signal/noise cutoff on PCA-like dimensions is needed instead of subjective elbow-inspection of eigenvalues.
skills.name: random-matrix-theory-noise-filtering
skills.search_text: random-matrix-theory-noise-filtering Use when analyzing sparse scRNA-seq count data and a data-driven signal/noise cutoff on PCA-like dimensions is needed instead of subjective elbow-inspection of eigenvalues. Input data has already been feature-selected to highly variable genes — the article warns this compromises local structure in low-variance genes and would bias the RMT eigenvalue spectrum Data has been imputed — the article notes imputation can bias data and generate false signals that RMT filtering cannot distinguish from true biology Only a small random-matrix-like synthetic matrix without a meaningful MP regime is available — the MP/TW fit assumes a large noise eigenvalue spectrum to fit against http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A data-driven noise-filtering step from scLENS that classifies eigenvalues of the cell-to-cell similarity matrix G = XX^T/N as noise or biological signal by fitting the Marchenko-Pastur distribution and applying a Tracy-Widom threshold, eliminating manual signal-dimension tuning. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: A data-driven noise-filtering step from scLENS that classifies eigenvalues of the cell-to-cell similarity matrix G = XX^T/N as noise or biological signal by fitting the Marchenko-Pastur distribution and applying a Tracy-Widom threshold, eliminating manual signal-dimension tuning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has already been feature-selected to highly variable genes — the article warns this compromises local structure in low-variance genes and would bias the RMT eigenvalue spectrum Data has been imputed — the article notes imputation can bias data and generate false signals that RMT filtering cannot distinguish from true biology Only a small random-matrix-like synthetic matrix without a meaningful MP regime is available — the MP/TW fit assumes a large noise eigenvalue spectrum to fit against

skills.description: Use when a discrete assignment problem (e.g., mapping cell clusters to palette colors) must be solved by minimizing a Frobenius-norm graph-matching objective, and local search alone risks poor local minima.
skills.name: random-restart-optimization
skills.search_text: random-restart-optimization Use when a discrete assignment problem (e.g., mapping cell clusters to palette colors) must be solved by minimizing a Frobenius-norm graph-matching objective, and local search alone risks poor local minima. When the user has manually fixed or specified colors for particular cell types and only wants the remaining types optimized — use Spaco's manual color-fixing option instead of unconstrained restarts When the goal is palette selection or palette extraction from an image rather than assignment of an already-selected palette to clusters http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 A coarse-to-fine stochastic optimization strategy for the cluster-color assignment step of Spaco: random permutation restarts over the CI-graph/CD-graph matching objective, followed by pairwise color-swap refinement, to find a one-to-one cluster-to-color mapping that maximizes color contrast between interlaced cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: A coarse-to-fine stochastic optimization strategy for the cluster-color assignment step of Spaco: random permutation restarts over the CI-graph/CD-graph matching objective, followed by pairwise color-swap refinement, to find a one-to-one cluster-to-color mapping that maximizes color contrast between interlaced cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the user has manually fixed or specified colors for particular cell types and only wants the remaining types optimized — use Spaco's manual color-fixing option instead of unconstrained restarts When the goal is palette selection or palette extraction from an image rather than assignment of an already-selected palette to clusters

skills.description: Use when judging whether an observed overlap between a candidate regulator list and a reference set (e.g. gold circRNA regulators in a Harmonizome interaction or co-expression dataset) exceeds chance, via random-sampling permutations.
skills.name: random-sampling-permutation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: random-sampling-permutation-significance-testing Use when judging whether an observed overlap between a candidate regulator list and a reference set (e.g. gold circRNA regulators in a Harmonizome interaction or co-expression dataset) exceeds chance, via random-sampling permutations. When the candidate feature matrix has not yet been built and NMF clustering has not produced a candidate list — run the CRIT pipeline (GET_*.R scripts, NMF.R) first. When the question is direct circRNA-RBP binding rather than indirect association (PPI, co-expression, shared TFs) — use CLIP database validation instead. When no sensible background set (all genes or the 1344-RBP list) can be defined for the reference data, as the permutation null is undefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Assess whether observed overlaps between the 73 CRIT-predicted candidate circRNA regulators and gold-standard regulators in Harmonizome datasets (Pathway Commons PPI, MSigDB co-expression, TRANSFAC TF targets) are significant, by comparing to 10,000 random-sampling permutations against appropriate gene or RBP backgrounds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Assess whether observed overlaps between the 73 CRIT-predicted candidate circRNA regulators and gold-standard regulators in Harmonizome datasets (Pathway Commons PPI, MSigDB co-expression, TRANSFAC TF targets) are significant, by comparing to 10,000 random-sampling permutations against appropriate gene or RBP backgrounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the candidate feature matrix has not yet been built and NMF clustering has not produced a candidate list — run the CRIT pipeline (GET_*.R scripts, NMF.R) first. When the question is direct circRNA-RBP binding rather than indirect association (PPI, co-expression, shared TFs) — use CLIP database validation instead. When no sensible background set (all genes or the 1344-RBP list) can be defined for the reference data, as the permutation null is undefined.

skills.description: Use when the method being benchmarked involves stochastic steps (random clustering, random subsampling) and you need seed-averaged scores or robustness estimates across parameter sweeps.
skills.name: random-seed-replicate-aggregation
skills.search_text: random-seed-replicate-aggregation Use when the method being benchmarked involves stochastic steps (random clustering, random subsampling) and you need seed-averaged scores or robustness estimates across parameter sweeps. The pipeline is fully deterministic (no random clustering or sampling steps), so seed replicates would be identical and add no information. Trajectories are disconnected or contain cycles, since Totem cannot generate them and the sweep's scoring step would be invalid. The dataset has extremely rare plus extremely prevalent cell types simultaneously, where k-medoids fails regardless of seed and aggregation would average over structurally broken clusterings. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Run a stochastic analysis (e.g., Totem's CLARA k-medoids clustering) repeatedly with different random seeds and aggregate the results across replicates to separate method robustness from seed-level noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Run a stochastic analysis (e.g., Totem's CLARA k-medoids clustering) repeatedly with different random seeds and aggregate the results across replicates to separate method robustness from seed-level noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline is fully deterministic (no random clustering or sampling steps), so seed replicates would be identical and add no information. Trajectories are disconnected or contain cycles, since Totem cannot generate them and the sweep's scoring step would be invalid. The dataset has extremely rare plus extremely prevalent cell types simultaneously, where k-medoids fails regardless of seed and aggregation would average over structurally broken clusterings.

skills.description: Use when comparing model variants (multimodal vs unimodal) on a prediction task with specificity annotation and you need statistically robust mean performance across random splits rather than a single train/test result.
skills.name: random-split-cross-validation-aggregation
skills.search_text: random-split-cross-validation-aggregation Use when comparing model variants (multimodal vs unimodal) on a prediction task with specificity annotation and you need statistically robust mean performance across random splits rather than a single train/test result. The dataset lacks specificity annotation — use tutorials/02_training_analysis.ipynb (training/analysis with cell type and clonotype annotation) instead of the prediction setup You need a single deterministic train/test estimate rather than a variance-aware multi-split comparison, e.g. for quick debugging on the 15-minute subsampled tutorial dataset Input data is not paired TCR + transcriptome multimodal single-cell data (e.g. BCR/SHM datasets, which the paper notes lack large-scale specificity-annotated benchmarks) Benchmarking protocol that trains a model (e.g. mvTCR and unimodal TCR/RNA baselines) across five random data splits, evaluates kNN antigen-specificity prediction on each held-out split, and aggregates mean F1-Scores for comparison against published values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol that trains a model (e.g. mvTCR and unimodal TCR/RNA baselines) across five random data splits, evaluates kNN antigen-specificity prediction on each held-out split, and aggregates mean F1-Scores for comparison against published values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks specificity annotation — use tutorials/02_training_analysis.ipynb (training/analysis with cell type and clonotype annotation) instead of the prediction setup You need a single deterministic train/test estimate rather than a variance-aware multi-split comparison, e.g. for quick debugging on the 15-minute subsampled tutorial dataset Input data is not paired TCR + transcriptome multimodal single-cell data (e.g. BCR/SHM datasets, which the paper notes lack large-scale specificity-annotated benchmarks)

skills.description: Use when you must demonstrate that a supervised single-cell drug-response predictor's performance is not an artifact of a single train/test split, by measuring metric variation across repeated random stratified samplings of labeled scRNA-seq cells.
skills.name: random-subsampling-stability-assessment
skills.search_text: random-subsampling-stability-assessment Use when you must demonstrate that a supervised single-cell drug-response predictor's performance is not an artifact of a single train/test split, by measuring metric variation across repeated random stratified samplings of labeled scRNA-seq cells. When the goal is a single best point estimate of prediction accuracy on one fixed train/test split rather than quantifying split-to-split stability When the scRNA-seq data lack binary sensitivity/resistance labels (sens_label), since stratified sampling and label-based metrics cannot be computed When the task is de novo drug-response prediction on new cell types rather than robustness assessment of the already-benchmarked six scDEAL datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3306 A robustness-testing skill that quantifies the stability of scDEAL's single-cell drug-response predictions by repeating 80% stratified random subsampling 20 times on the six benchmark scRNA-seq datasets and reporting metric variation (e.g. standard deviation) across repeats. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: A robustness-testing skill that quantifies the stability of scDEAL's single-cell drug-response predictions by repeating 80% stratified random subsampling 20 times on the six benchmark scRNA-seq datasets and reporting metric variation (e.g. standard deviation) across repeats.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single best point estimate of prediction accuracy on one fixed train/test split rather than quantifying split-to-split stability When the scRNA-seq data lack binary sensitivity/resistance labels (sens_label), since stratified sampling and label-based metrics cannot be computed When the task is de novo drug-response prediction on new cell types rather than robustness assessment of the already-benchmarked six scDEAL datasets

skills.description: Use when constructing a cell-cell relationship graph from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix: after building the unweighted KNN graph, to compute transition probabilities and the PPMI-weighted adjacency.
skills.name: random-surfing-transition-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: random-surfing-transition-matrix-computation Use when constructing a cell-cell relationship graph from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix: after building the unweighted KNN graph, to compute transition probabilities and the PPMI-weighted adjacency. Input is a raw count matrix or has not been normalized and filtered to highly variable genes — the paper's pipeline normalizes the scRNA-seq matrix and selects the top d highly variable genes before graph construction A weighted cell-cell relationship graph is already available — random surfing is designed to enrich an unweighted KNN graph, not to re-weight existing edge weights The downstream model does not use graph convolution over the cell-PPMI graph (e.g., non-graph clustering like DEC or DCA) — the PPMI graph is specific to scMGCA-style aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs a random surfing algorithm over the unweighted k-NN cell graph to obtain a transition matrix capturing vertex-to-vertex transition probabilities, which is then converted into the positive pointwise mutual information (PPMI) cell-PPMI graph used by scMGCA to aggregate neighboring cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: Runs a random surfing algorithm over the unweighted k-NN cell graph to obtain a transition matrix capturing vertex-to-vertex transition probabilities, which is then converted into the positive pointwise mutual information (PPMI) cell-PPMI graph used by scMGCA to aggregate neighboring cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix or has not been normalized and filtered to highly variable genes — the paper's pipeline normalizes the scRNA-seq matrix and selects the top d highly variable genes before graph construction A weighted cell-cell relationship graph is already available — random surfing is designed to enrich an unweighted KNN graph, not to re-weight existing edge weights The downstream model does not use graph convolution over the cell-PPMI graph (e.g., non-graph clustering like DEC or DCA) — the PPMI graph is specific to scMGCA-style aggregation

skills.description: Use when you must judge whether a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g., a LinRace subtree for cells sharing an identical barcode but from different clones) carries real topological signal, by comparing its distance to a reference against random trees over the same tip set.
skills.name: random-tree-null-distribution-testing
skills.search_text: random-tree-null-distribution-testing Use when you must judge whether a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g., a LinRace subtree for cells sharing an identical barcode but from different clones) carries real topological signal, by comparing its distance to a reference against random trees over the same tip set. The reference tree has no cells that need collapsing (all leaves uniquely resolvable) — compare directly with RF.dist or NyeSimilarity normalization instead of a random-tree null Only one or a few random trees are feasible to generate — the null distribution is too sparse to support the 'lower than every random tree' criterion http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Validates a lineage-tree reconstruction by computing a tree-distance metric (here, CID — common intervals distance) between the reconstructed tree and a reference tree, and comparing it against the null distribution obtained from 100 randomly generated trees over the same tips. A reconstructed tree is considered informative only if its distance to the reference falls below every (or nearly all) random-tree distances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Validates a lineage-tree reconstruction by computing a tree-distance metric (here, CID — common intervals distance) between the reconstructed tree and a reference tree, and comparing it against the null distribution obtained from 100 randomly generated trees over the same tips. A reconstructed tree is considered informative only if its distance to the reference falls below every (or nearly all) random-tree distances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference tree has no cells that need collapsing (all leaves uniquely resolvable) — compare directly with RF.dist or NyeSimilarity normalization instead of a random-tree null Only one or a few random trees are feasible to generate — the null distribution is too sparse to support the 'lower than every random tree' criterion

skills.description: Use when comparing two sketching/sampling methods across multiple single-cell datasets and sketch sizes, where robust Hausdorff distance to the full dataset quantifies representativeness and stochastic trials must be aggregated.
skills.name: random-trial-aggregation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: random-trial-aggregation-across-datasets Use when comparing two sketching/sampling methods across multiple single-cell datasets and sketch sizes, where robust Hausdorff distance to the full dataset quantifies representativeness and stochastic trials must be aggregated. skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol that repeats Sphetcher spherical sketching and Hie et al. geometric sketching over 10 random trials per dataset and sketch size (1%, 4%, 10%), computes robust Hausdorff distances of each sketch to the full data, and aggregates results into comparison tables and plots across six single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single sketch for downstream analysis (e.g., clustering with Louvain or trajectory inference with Monocle 2) rather than a method-vs-method accuracy benchmark You want to evaluate fairness-constrained sketching with prior class labels and l_min representatives per class — that is a separate optimization mode of Sphetcher, not this comparison protocol Your dataset is small enough that sketching is unnecessary; the paper motivates this for datasets whose size exceeds the capability of current computational analysis methods

skills.description: Use when reconstructing pseudotime/directionality on a PARC cluster graph for single-cell trajectory data (e.g., mESC CyTOF cell-cycle), where a root cluster is known and hitting-time-based ordering is needed.
skills.name: random-walk-hitting-time-computation
skills.search_text: random-walk-hitting-time-computation Use when reconstructing pseudotime/directionality on a PARC cluster graph for single-cell trajectory data (e.g., mESC CyTOF cell-cycle), where a root cluster is known and hitting-time-based ordering is needed. Data lacks a defensible root/start population, since hitting times are computed from a specified root cluster The goal is a fully data-driven tree/fate analysis without cluster-level abstraction — VIA's cluster-graph hitting times assume PARC clustering granularity is appropriate Trajectory topology requires higher-order memory effects beyond the first-order lazy-teleporting walk (StaVia/Via 2.0's memory walks address this) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes single-cell pseudotime and graph directionality on the PARC cluster graph via the theoretical expected hitting times of a lazy-teleporting random walk (VIA stage 1, Eqs. 1-8), followed by lazy-teleporting MCMC refinement on the forward-biased graph (VIA stage 2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Computes single-cell pseudotime and graph directionality on the PARC cluster graph via the theoretical expected hitting times of a lazy-teleporting random walk (VIA stage 1, Eqs. 1-8), followed by lazy-teleporting MCMC refinement on the forward-biased graph (VIA stage 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks a defensible root/start population, since hitting times are computed from a specified root cluster The goal is a fully data-driven tree/fate analysis without cluster-level abstraction — VIA's cluster-graph hitting times assume PARC clustering granularity is appropriate Trajectory topology requires higher-order memory effects beyond the first-order lazy-teleporting walk (StaVia/Via 2.0's memory walks address this)

skills.description: Use when scoring per-cell pathway activity in normalized scRNA-seq data (e.g. Seurat objects) to fetch the cells most relevant to a curated gene set (GO, Hallmarks, KEGG, BIOCARTA) without clustering.
skills.name: random-walk-restart-label-propagation
skills.search_text: random-walk-restart-label-propagation Use when scoring per-cell pathway activity in normalized scRNA-seq data (e.g. Seurat objects) to fetch the cells most relevant to a curated gene set (GO, Hallmarks, KEGG, BIOCARTA) without clustering. Data are targeted-gene panels with limited gene numbers; GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' The gene set fails the coordination (KLD) test — binarization is recommended only for coordinated gene sets A fast score for a small cell number is needed, where AUCell is faster than GSDensity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 GSDensity's single-cell pathway activity scoring step: after MCA co-embedding of cells and genes and nearest-neighbor graph construction, pathway genes are used as seeds for random walk with restart (RWR) on the cell-gene graph, yielding per-cell pathway activity (label propagation) probabilities that can be binarized to fetch the most relevant cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: GSDensity's single-cell pathway activity scoring step: after MCA co-embedding of cells and genes and nearest-neighbor graph construction, pathway genes are used as seeds for random walk with restart (RWR) on the cell-gene graph, yielding per-cell pathway activity (label propagation) probabilities that can be binarized to fetch the most relevant cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted-gene panels with limited gene numbers; GSDensity is 'not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' The gene set fails the coordination (KLD) test — binarization is recommended only for coordinated gene sets A fast score for a small cell number is needed, where AUCell is faster than GSDensity

skills.search_text: random-walk-restart-pathway-activity-scoring Use when a gene set's spatial/density relevance has been established (compute.kld p.adj < 0.05) and per-cell pathway activity scores or positive/negative cell labels are needed for downstream spatial or classification analysis. Data are targeted-panel spatial transcriptomics with limited gene numbers — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Gene sets that failed the coordination pre-filter (compute.kld adjusted p >= 0.05), since over 98% of non-coordinated gene sets yield spurious binarizations Non-spatial single-cell clustering workflows where only cluster-level enrichment is needed and per-cell labels are not required http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 GSDensity's single-cell pathway activity scoring step: a random walk with restart (RWR) is propagated over a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built in the MCA latent space, using pathway genes as seeds, to yield per-cell pathway relevance probabilities without clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: GSDensity's single-cell pathway activity scoring step: a random walk with restart (RWR) is propagated over a nearest-neighbor cell-gene graph built in the MCA latent space, using pathway genes as seeds, to yield per-cell pathway relevance probabilities without clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are targeted-panel spatial transcriptomics with limited gene numbers — the article states GSDensity 'is not suitable for targeted gene data having limited numbers of genes' Gene sets that failed the coordination pre-filter (compute.kld adjusted p >= 0.05), since over 98% of non-coordinated gene sets yield spurious binarizations Non-spatial single-cell clustering workflows where only cluster-level enrichment is needed and per-cell labels are not required

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a lazy-teleporting random-walk/MCMC stage improves pseudotime accuracy on time-series single-cell (e.g., CyTOF) data against ablated variants and TI baselines.
skills.name: random-walk-trajectory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: random-walk-trajectory-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a lazy-teleporting random-walk/MCMC stage improves pseudotime accuracy on time-series single-cell (e.g., CyTOF) data against ablated variants and TI baselines. The input lacks annotated time/day labels, since the validation metric is a Pearson correlation of inferred pseudotime against annotated sampling days The goal is simulating synthetic toy trajectories for prototyping TI methods — use dyntoy/dyngen-style generators instead of this CyTOF benchmark The dataset is tree-only scRNA-seq where baselines like Slingshot/STREAM are already adequate and the lazy-teleporting MCMC ablation question is not of interest Benchmark lazy-teleporting random-walk trajectory inference (VIA) against ablation and TI baselines (Slingshot, Palantir, STREAM, PAGA) by correlating inferred pseudotime with annotated time labels on the mESC CyTOF dataset (~90K cells, 28 antibody markers), demonstrating the MCMC stage's contribution to pseudotime accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Benchmark lazy-teleporting random-walk trajectory inference (VIA) against ablation and TI baselines (Slingshot, Palantir, STREAM, PAGA) by correlating inferred pseudotime with annotated time labels on the mESC CyTOF dataset (~90K cells, 28 antibody markers), demonstrating the MCMC stage's contribution to pseudotime accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks annotated time/day labels, since the validation metric is a Pearson correlation of inferred pseudotime against annotated sampling days The goal is simulating synthetic toy trajectories for prototyping TI methods — use dyntoy/dyngen-style generators instead of this CyTOF benchmark The dataset is tree-only scRNA-seq where baselines like Slingshot/STREAM are already adequate and the lazy-teleporting MCMC ablation question is not of interest

skills.description: Use when you have a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix and need to model cell-fate transition dynamics as a Markov random walk before attractor/coarse-graining analysis.
skills.name: random-walk-transition-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: random-walk-transition-matrix-construction Use when you have a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix and need to model cell-fate transition dynamics as a Markov random walk before attractor/coarse-graining analysis. The input is not a pre-processed expression matrix but raw counts or already-clustered/feature-summarized data lacking per-cell gene expression The dataset has very few cells where high-resolution identification of transition cells is unreliable (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset required special care) The goal is static clustering or pseudo-time ordering alone (e.g., DPT/Slingshot/Monocle) without any stochastic dynamical modeling of transitions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs the cell-cell scale random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) from a pre-processed single-cell gene expression matrix using a Gaussian-like affinity kernel with degree normalization, as the first step of MuTrans's multiscale stochastic dynamics framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Constructs the cell-cell scale random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) from a pre-processed single-cell gene expression matrix using a Gaussian-like affinity kernel with degree normalization, as the first step of MuTrans's multiscale stochastic dynamics framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a pre-processed expression matrix but raw counts or already-clustered/feature-summarized data lacking per-cell gene expression The dataset has very few cells where high-resolution identification of transition cells is unreliable (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset required special care) The goal is static clustering or pseudo-time ordering alone (e.g., DPT/Slingshot/Monocle) without any stochastic dynamical modeling of transitions

skills.description: Use when single-cell snapshot transcriptome data must be decomposed into stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells, e.g. Pro-B to Pre-B differentiation, EMT, or Langevin simulation wells, with basin count guided by the EPI eigen-gap.
skills.name: random-walk-transition-probability-matrix-coarse-graining
skills.search_text: random-walk-transition-probability-matrix-coarse-graining Use when single-cell snapshot transcriptome data must be decomposed into stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells, e.g. Pro-B to Pre-B differentiation, EMT, or Langevin simulation wells, with basin count guided by the EPI eigen-gap. Datasets where cell counts are too small for high-resolution transition-cell identification (e.g. the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 data required special care per the discussion) Systems where non-stationary effects from cell cycle or proliferation dominate and must be explicitly modeled — MuTrans does not account for these The goal is static clustering with hard state assignments (e.g. SC3/SIMLR-style), which enforce distinct states and erase transient cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 MuTrans core multi-scale procedure that learns a cell-cell random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) via a Gaussian-like affinity kernel, coarse-grains it to cluster-cluster scale dynamics to recover attractor basins and inter-basin transition probabilities, and optimizes a soft cell-cluster membership matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: MuTrans core multi-scale procedure that learns a cell-cell random walk transition probability matrix (rwTPM) via a Gaussian-like affinity kernel, coarse-grains it to cluster-cluster scale dynamics to recover attractor basins and inter-basin transition probabilities, and optimizes a soft cell-cluster membership matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets where cell counts are too small for high-resolution transition-cell identification (e.g. the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 data required special care per the discussion) Systems where non-stationary effects from cell cycle or proliferation dominate and must be explicitly modeled — MuTrans does not account for these The goal is static clustering with hard state assignments (e.g. SC3/SIMLR-style), which enforce distinct states and erase transient cells

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed N×D single-cell expression matrix must be converted into per-cell stationary diffusion distributions over a k-nearest-neighbor graph as a precursor to pseudotime ordering or BKFD dimensionality reduction.
skills.name: random-walk-with-restart-diffusion
skills.search_text: random-walk-with-restart-diffusion Use when a pre-processed N×D single-cell expression matrix must be converted into per-cell stationary diffusion distributions over a k-nearest-neighbor graph as a precursor to pseudotime ordering or BKFD dimensionality reduction. The input is raw, unprocessed counts — the article requires pre-processing into a gene expression matrix X (N×D) before transition-matrix construction The analysis goal is Scanpy DPT specifically and you intend to reproduce DPT exactly — RWR here is the more general algorithm of which DPT is the p=1 special case; using p=0.9 gives DTFLOW's setting, not DPT You need a principled, dataset-specific parameter selection — the article notes parameter values (Gaussian kernel width, k, restart probability 1-p) may vary from dataset to dataset and defers optimal selection to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a per-cell stationary diffusion distribution by running random walk with restart (RWR) over a kNN-derived Markov transition matrix, as implemented in DTFLOW's get_diffusionRWR(p) with restart probability 1-p and default p=0.9. This step is the diffusion-propagation core of DTFLOW pseudotime inference and the generalization of which diffusion pseudotime (DPT, Scanpy) is the p=1 special case. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Builds a per-cell stationary diffusion distribution by running random walk with restart (RWR) over a kNN-derived Markov transition matrix, as implemented in DTFLOW's get_diffusionRWR(p) with restart probability 1-p and default p=0.9. This step is the diffusion-propagation core of DTFLOW pseudotime inference and the generalization of which diffusion pseudotime (DPT, Scanpy) is the p=1 special case.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unprocessed counts — the article requires pre-processing into a gene expression matrix X (N×D) before transition-matrix construction The analysis goal is Scanpy DPT specifically and you intend to reproduce DPT exactly — RWR here is the more general algorithm of which DPT is the p=1 special case; using p=0.9 gives DTFLOW's setting, not DPT You need a principled, dataset-specific parameter selection — the article notes parameter values (Gaussian kernel width, k, restart probability 1-p) may vary from dataset to dataset and defers optimal selection to future work

skills.description: Use when classifying scRNA-seq cells to Cell Ontology terms — including unseen cell types with no annotated training cells — or when cell type embeddings and cell-by-gene expression matrices must share one low-dimensional space.
skills.name: random-walk-with-restart-embedding
skills.search_text: random-walk-with-restart-embedding Use when classifying scRNA-seq cells to Cell Ontology terms — including unseen cell types with no annotated training cells — or when cell type embeddings and cell-by-gene expression matrices must share one low-dimensional space. The task is plain cell type classification with a fixed label set and no need to annotate unseen ontology terms — a standard classifier without ontology embedding suffices You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot resolve The ontology is missing the cell types or cell states of interest, since the Cell Ontology was not developed specifically for scRNA-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0089 Embeds Cell Ontology cell types into a shared low-dimensional space by running random walk with restart (clusDCA-style, restart probabilities 0.5-0.8) on the ontology 'is_a' graph followed by SVD, so that single-cell transcriptomes can be projected into the same space for ontology-aware classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Embeds Cell Ontology cell types into a shared low-dimensional space by running random walk with restart (clusDCA-style, restart probabilities 0.5-0.8) on the ontology 'is_a' graph followed by SVD, so that single-cell transcriptomes can be projected into the same space for ontology-aware classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is plain cell type classification with a fixed label set and no need to annotate unseen ontology terms — a standard classifier without ontology embedding suffices You need to distinguish topologically identical unseen cell types (siblings with the same parents in the Cell Ontology graph), which OnClass cannot resolve The ontology is missing the cell types or cell states of interest, since the Cell Ontology was not developed specifically for scRNA-seq

skills.description: Use when a large normalized single-cell expression matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) needs a rank-k SVD, or when the low-rank parameter k must be selected automatically from the top-100 singular-value spectrum.
skills.name: randomized-svd-computation
skills.search_text: randomized-svd-computation Use when a large normalized single-cell expression matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) needs a rank-k SVD, or when the low-rank parameter k must be selected automatically from the top-100 singular-value spectrum. The input matrix is not normalized (raw counts) — library/log normalization should precede the SVD so the spectrum reflects the modeled expression scale The goal is a full-rank or exact SVD of a small matrix; randomized SVD is designed for fast rank-k approximation of large matrices Imputation methods that do not rely on low-rank structure (e.g. DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) are required instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the rank-k randomized singular value decomposition of a large scRNA-seq expression matrix, as the computational core of ALRA's low-rank approximation and its automatic rank selection (choose_k) based on singular-value spacings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Computes the rank-k randomized singular value decomposition of a large scRNA-seq expression matrix, as the computational core of ALRA's low-rank approximation and its automatic rank selection (choose_k) based on singular-value spacings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is not normalized (raw counts) — library/log normalization should precede the SVD so the spectrum reflects the modeled expression scale The goal is a full-rank or exact SVD of a small matrix; randomized SVD is designed for fast rank-k approximation of large matrices Imputation methods that do not rely on low-rank structure (e.g. DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) are required instead

skills.name: rank-based-gene-set-scoring
skills.search_text: rank-based-gene-set-scoring Use when input is a scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) count matrix and per-cell gene set activity scores are needed using rank-based scorers such as ssGSEA, singscore, RBO, or summed_up ranks, especially where sparsity/noise motivates neighbor-graph smoothing first. When the goal is differential activity at the group/sample level rather than per-cell scores — aggregated pseudobulk methods may be preferable When gene sets are defined by up/down directionality but the .gmt file does not encode _UP/_DN nomenclature — ranked scorers will treat all genes as up since genesets default to up When counts are already normalized bulk expression profiles, where the sparsity-driven smoothing of the nearest neighbor graph adds little http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores single-cell gene expression against gene sets using rank-based single-sample methods (singscore, ssGSEA, rank_biased_overlap, summed_up with ranked=True), optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed counts from gssnng, to quantify per-cell gene set activity in Scanpy AnnData objects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Scores single-cell gene expression against gene sets using rank-based single-sample methods (singscore, ssGSEA, rank_biased_overlap, summed_up with ranked=True), optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed counts from gssnng, to quantify per-cell gene set activity in Scanpy AnnData objects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential activity at the group/sample level rather than per-cell scores — aggregated pseudobulk methods may be preferable When gene sets are defined by up/down directionality but the .gmt file does not encode _UP/_DN nomenclature — ranked scorers will treat all genes as up since genesets default to up When counts are already normalized bulk expression profiles, where the sparsity-driven smoothing of the nearest neighbor graph adds little

skills.description: Use when you need rapid per-cell pathway activity scores on large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g., >100k cells, >10^3 pathways) and existing tools like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow.
skills.name: rank-based-gene-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: rank-based-gene-signature-scoring Use when you need rapid per-cell pathway activity scores on large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g., >100k cells, >10^3 pathways) and existing tools like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow. Input is already aggregated (pseudobulk or bulk expression) rather than per-cell scRNA-seq — PAS computation on single cells is the premise of this skill; pseudobulk integration happens later and loses information The downstream goal is disease-related multicellular pathway module discovery with fewer than 15 samples — this skill only produces the PAS matrix (Step 1); MOFA-based module identification requires ≥15 samples Expression data has already been scored — re-scoring an existing PAS matrix with fast_ucell is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell pathway activity scores (PAS) from a single-cell gene expression matrix using rank-based gene-set scoring, via scPAFA's fast_ucell (UCell reimplementation) or fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore/Scanpy score_genes reimplementation), designed for million-cell-scale scRNA-seq with >10^3 pathways. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Compute per-cell pathway activity scores (PAS) from a single-cell gene expression matrix using rank-based gene-set scoring, via scPAFA's fast_ucell (UCell reimplementation) or fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore/Scanpy score_genes reimplementation), designed for million-cell-scale scRNA-seq with >10^3 pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aggregated (pseudobulk or bulk expression) rather than per-cell scRNA-seq — PAS computation on single cells is the premise of this skill; pseudobulk integration happens later and loses information The downstream goal is disease-related multicellular pathway module discovery with fewer than 15 samples — this skill only produces the PAS matrix (Step 1); MOFA-based module identification requires ≥15 samples Expression data has already been scored — re-scoring an existing PAS matrix with fast_ucell is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when scoring cell-type or biological-process gene signatures on a gene-vs-cell scRNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or SingleCellExperiment, and you need scores that are unaffected by dataset composition.
skills.name: rank-based-mann-whitney-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: rank-based-mann-whitney-enrichment-scoring Use when scoring cell-type or biological-process gene signatures on a gene-vs-cell scRNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or SingleCellExperiment, and you need scores that are unaffected by dataset composition. The input is not single-cell expression data ranked per cell (e.g. already aggregated bulk or feature tables), where rank-capping at rmax=1500 is meaningless You need dataset-level normalization that depends on the full dataset composition — UCell scores deliberately depend only on relative expression within individual cells Signatures contain mostly genes absent from the reference, where 'impute' handling (setting absent genes to rmax+1) can distort scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Score gene signatures in single-cell data using UCell, which computes a normalized Mann-Whitney U statistic (equivalent to AUC) on per-cell gene expression ranks, making scores robust to dataset size and composition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: Score gene signatures in single-cell data using UCell, which computes a normalized Mann-Whitney U statistic (equivalent to AUC) on per-cell gene expression ranks, making scores robust to dataset size and composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not single-cell expression data ranked per cell (e.g. already aggregated bulk or feature tables), where rank-capping at rmax=1500 is meaningless You need dataset-level normalization that depends on the full dataset composition — UCell scores deliberately depend only on relative expression within individual cells Signatures contain mostly genes absent from the reference, where 'impute' handling (setting absent genes to rmax+1) can distort scores

skills.description: Use when multiple bifurcation-capable trajectory inference methods (e.g., STREAM/ElPiGraph, Monocle2) have been run on a branching single-cell dataset and you need an objective, marker-gene-anchored measure of pseudotime accuracy to rank the methods.
skills.name: rank-based-vs-distance-based-pseudotime-comparison
skills.search_text: rank-based-vs-distance-based-pseudotime-comparison Use when multiple bifurcation-capable trajectory inference methods (e.g., STREAM/ElPiGraph, Monocle2) have been run on a branching single-cell dataset and you need an objective, marker-gene-anchored measure of pseudotime accuracy to rank the methods. Data with cyclic or disconnected graph topologies — the paper notes further improvement is necessary for STREAM to properly describe these more general structures, so bifurcation-anchored pseudotime accuracy is not meaningful When no prior-knowledge marker genes are available to anchor pseudotime evaluation, since the whole comparison depends on correlating with ENO3/MEF2C/MYH2-like markers When only one trajectory method was run — the skill is a cross-method accuracy comparison, not a single-method pseudotime computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks trajectory-inference methods on the Trapnell HSMM myoblast dataset by correlating each method's rank-based and distance-based pseudotime with myogenic marker genes (ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2), using Pearson/Spearman/Kendall coefficients to reproduce the STREAM paper's Fig. 5c-d accuracy comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Benchmarks trajectory-inference methods on the Trapnell HSMM myoblast dataset by correlating each method's rank-based and distance-based pseudotime with myogenic marker genes (ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2), using Pearson/Spearman/Kendall coefficients to reproduce the STREAM paper's Fig. 5c-d accuracy comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data with cyclic or disconnected graph topologies — the paper notes further improvement is necessary for STREAM to properly describe these more general structures, so bifurcation-anchored pseudotime accuracy is not meaningful When no prior-knowledge marker genes are available to anchor pseudotime evaluation, since the whole comparison depends on correlating with ENO3/MEF2C/MYH2-like markers When only one trajectory method was run — the skill is a cross-method accuracy comparison, not a single-method pseudotime computation

skills.name: rank-biased-overlap-scoring
skills.search_text: rank-biased-overlap-scoring Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq cells (Scanpy AnnData h5ad) for membership in a gene set using a rank-based statistic, e.g. testing whether an _UP/_DN signature separates two cell states such as injured vs control endothelial cells. Data is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated pseudobulk, where the nearest-neighbor smoothing of gssnng is unnecessary The chosen scoring statistic is one gssnng recommends for unranked data (e.g. mean_z, robust_std), which conflict with ranked=True The goal is pathway activity inference from a model/resource (Decoupler/Omnipath style) rather than scoring a user-supplied .gmt signature http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks per-cell gene expression and applies the rank_biased_overlap (RBO) scorer from gssnng — a weighted average of agreement between sorted ranks and a gene set — to estimate gene set activity per single cell, optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Ranks per-cell gene expression and applies the rank_biased_overlap (RBO) scorer from gssnng — a weighted average of agreement between sorted ranks and a gene set — to estimate gene set activity per single cell, optionally on nearest-neighbor-smoothed counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is bulk RNA-seq or already aggregated pseudobulk, where the nearest-neighbor smoothing of gssnng is unnecessary The chosen scoring statistic is one gssnng recommends for unranked data (e.g. mean_z, robust_std), which conflict with ranked=True The goal is pathway activity inference from a model/resource (Decoupler/Omnipath style) rather than scoring a user-supplied .gmt signature

skills.description: Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices where thousands of zero-expression genes per cell would dominate per-cell gene rankings, and scores must be robust to dataset size and composition.
skills.name: rank-capping-zero-inflation-tail-correction
skills.search_text: rank-capping-zero-inflation-tail-correction Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices where thousands of zero-expression genes per cell would dominate per-cell gene rankings, and scores must be robust to dataset size and composition. Input is already a scored feature table or enrichment score matrix — rank capping applies to raw expression matrices only The analysis requires scores sensitive to dataset composition or absolute expression levels (e.g. comparing cells across deliberately different expression scales) Using Seurat's AddModuleScore-style binning is intended instead, since UCell's rank-based approach is specifically an alternative whose scores depend only on per-cell relative ranks http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 UCell's sparsity-handling mechanism: per-cell gene expression ranks are computed (via data.table frank) and capped at a maxRank parameter (default 1500), setting all genes ranked above rmax to rmax+1 so the uninformative zero-expression tail does not distort Mann-Whitney U-based signature scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: UCell's sparsity-handling mechanism: per-cell gene expression ranks are computed (via data.table frank) and capped at a maxRank parameter (default 1500), setting all genes ranked above rmax to rmax+1 so the uninformative zero-expression tail does not distort Mann-Whitney U-based signature scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a scored feature table or enrichment score matrix — rank capping applies to raw expression matrices only The analysis requires scores sensitive to dataset composition or absolute expression levels (e.g. comparing cells across deliberately different expression scales) Using Seurat's AddModuleScore-style binning is intended instead, since UCell's rank-based approach is specifically an alternative whose scores depend only on per-cell relative ranks

skills.description: Use when you have a raw single-cell expression matrix and need to learn cell-to-cell similarities robust to noise, outliers and dropouts, rather than using a fixed distance metric.
skills.name: rank-constrained-matrix-optimization
skills.search_text: rank-constrained-matrix-optimization Use when you have a raw single-cell expression matrix and need to learn cell-to-cell similarities robust to noise, outliers and dropouts, rather than using a fixed distance metric. The dataset is already a cell-to-cell similarity or feature table rather than an expression matrix A supervised analysis with pre-selected gene subsets of known function is required — SIMLR is unsupervised and supports de novo discovery only The goal is simply applying a standard dimension reduction method (e.g. PCA, t-SNE) to data whose statistical characteristics already fit standard assumptions http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Reconstructs SIMLR's optimization loop, which combines multiple Gaussian kernels into a learned sample-to-sample similarity matrix for single-cell RNA-seq data under a rank constraint, solved by a simple iterative procedure. skills.name: rank-correlation-feature-scoring
skills.search_text: rank-correlation-feature-scoring Use when a data matrix and response are given and features must be scored for relevance and redundancy with a fast, robust criterion — especially for fat datasets (e.g. 100x500, 1000x500) or mixed-type variables. Features are already pre-selected or the goal is wrapper/embedding selection rather than filter-based scoring of the full feature set The analysis requires wrapper-based or causal-discovery methods (e.g. the IAMB-style algorithms from CausalExplorer) rather than a fast filter criterion Rank correlation is inappropriate for the data structure, e.g. when feature-response association is purely conditional and not captured by marginal rank statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantify feature-response association and feature-pair redundancy using Spearman rank correlation coefficients transformed into information theoretic quantities, as done in the RRCT feature-selection algorithm. This provides a fast, robust alternative to mutual information estimation via histograms or density estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100471
skills.summary: Quantify feature-response association and feature-pair redundancy using Spearman rank correlation coefficients transformed into information theoretic quantities, as done in the RRCT feature-selection algorithm. This provides a fast, robust alternative to mutual information estimation via histograms or density estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features are already pre-selected or the goal is wrapper/embedding selection rather than filter-based scoring of the full feature set The analysis requires wrapper-based or causal-discovery methods (e.g. the IAMB-style algorithms from CausalExplorer) rather than a fast filter criterion Rank correlation is inappropriate for the data structure, e.g. when feature-response association is purely conditional and not captured by marginal rank statistics

skills.description: Use when evaluating a differential expression detection method against simulated data where true per-gene log fold changes (logFC_theoretical from getDEgenes) are known and ranking quality, not just binary detection, must be quantified.

skills.search_text: rank-correlation-pvalue-assessment Use when evaluating a differential expression detection method against simulated data where true per-gene log fold changes (logFC_theoretical from getDEgenes) are known and ranking quality, not just binary detection, must be quantified. skills.summary: Benchmarking metric that scores differential expression methods by the negative Spearman correlation between method-predicted p-values and gold-standard true log fold changes, complementing AUROC on the SymSim-simulated observed counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No gold-standard true log fold changes are available (e.g. real experimental data without a simulated ground truth) The task is clustering or trajectory inference benchmarking rather than differential expression detection Only a binary DE/non-DE verdict is needed and ranking of non-DE genes by effect size is irrelevant (AUROC alone suffices)
