skills.description: Use when combining interaction scores from multiple CCC methods with incomparable magnitudes and differing interaction coverage into a single consensus ranking, e.g. as the preprocessing stage before Robust Rank Aggregation in LIANA.
skills.name: rank-normalisation-and-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: rank-normalisation-and-missing-value-imputation Use when combining interaction scores from multiple CCC methods with incomparable magnitudes and differing interaction coverage into a single consensus ranking, e.g. as the preprocessing stage before Robust Rank Aggregation in LIANA. Scores are already on a comparable scale and every method reports the same interaction universe — direct averaging may be appropriate instead of ranking The goal is to compare the individual methods rather than merge them; LIANA was designed to expose each method separately before any consensus Methods infer intracellular processes (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk native workflow, SoptSC) that are not directly comparable as interaction scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares heterogeneous ligand-receptor interaction scores (e.g. CellPhoneDB truncated mean, NATMI mean-expression edge weight, SingleCellSignalR LRscore, CellChat probability, Cytotalk crosstalk score) for consensus aggregation in LIANA by orienting scores so smaller values denote stronger interactions, converting them to ranks over the union universe of interactions, and imputing interactions missing from a method with the maximum (worst) rank. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Prepares heterogeneous ligand-receptor interaction scores (e.g. CellPhoneDB truncated mean, NATMI mean-expression edge weight, SingleCellSignalR LRscore, CellChat probability, Cytotalk crosstalk score) for consensus aggregation in LIANA by orienting scores so smaller values denote stronger interactions, converting them to ranks over the union universe of interactions, and imputing interactions missing from a method with the maximum (worst) rank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are already on a comparable scale and every method reports the same interaction universe — direct averaging may be appropriate instead of ranking The goal is to compare the individual methods rather than merge them; LIANA was designed to expose each method separately before any consensus Methods infer intracellular processes (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk native workflow, SoptSC) that are not directly comparable as interaction scores

skills.description: Use when you must benchmark or stress-test CCC inference methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, Connectome, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, Cytotalk) for sensitivity to noisy cell data or corrupted ligand-receptor prior-knowledge resources.
skills.name: rank-overlap-analysis-of-ligand-receptor-interactions
skills.search_text: rank-overlap-analysis-of-ligand-receptor-interactions Use when you must benchmark or stress-test CCC inference methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, Connectome, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, Cytotalk) for sensitivity to noisy cell data or corrupted ligand-receptor prior-knowledge resources. The CCC method infers intracellular processes (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC) — the paper states these are 'not directly comparable' with ligand-receptor methods The goal is absolute accuracy against a biological ground truth — no gold standard for CCC is available, so only perturbation-stability (overlap) can be assessed Evaluating agreement with independent modalities (spatial colocalisation, cytokine activities, receptor protein abundance) rather than ranking stability under noise http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies the robustness of cell-cell communication (CCC) inference methods by re-ranking ligand-receptor interactions on perturbed inputs (cell subsampling, cell-type label reshuffling, resource interaction replacement) and computing the overlap of top-250 ranked interactions against the unperturbed ranking, as done in the LIANA benchmark (Dimitrov et al., Nat Commun 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Quantifies the robustness of cell-cell communication (CCC) inference methods by re-ranking ligand-receptor interactions on perturbed inputs (cell subsampling, cell-type label reshuffling, resource interaction replacement) and computing the overlap of top-250 ranked interactions against the unperturbed ranking, as done in the LIANA benchmark (Dimitrov et al., Nat Commun 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CCC method infers intracellular processes (e.g. NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC) — the paper states these are 'not directly comparable' with ligand-receptor methods The goal is absolute accuracy against a biological ground truth — no gold standard for CCC is available, so only perturbation-stability (overlap) can be assessed Evaluating agreement with independent modalities (spatial colocalisation, cytokine activities, receptor protein abundance) rather than ranking stability under noise

skills.description: Use when tuning the LinQ-View ADT purity score's rank hyperparameter, or when evaluating how a cluster-scoring metric's parameter behaves across datasets with different surface-protein (ADT) feature counts.
skills.name: rank-parameter-sweep-evaluation
skills.search_text: rank-parameter-sweep-evaluation Use when tuning the LinQ-View ADT purity score's rank hyperparameter, or when evaluating how a cluster-scoring metric's parameter behaves across datasets with different surface-protein (ADT) feature counts. Massive datasets such as 170K cells with 228 ADT features, where LinQ-View (and its purity scoring) failed while Seurat 4 succeeded CITE-seq datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g., >=50), since LinQ-View is documented as best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) Analyses that need per-cluster transcriptional entropy rather than surface-protein purity — the ROGUE score targets cluster uniformity in scRNA-seq, not the ADT modality rank sweep Sweeps the adjustable 'rank' parameter (1-5) of the LinQ-View ADT purity score across CITE-seq datasets with different numbers of ADT features to identify the rank range that best quantifies cluster variation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Sweeps the adjustable 'rank' parameter (1-5) of the LinQ-View ADT purity score across CITE-seq datasets with different numbers of ADT features to identify the rank range that best quantifies cluster variation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Massive datasets such as 170K cells with 228 ADT features, where LinQ-View (and its purity scoring) failed while Seurat 4 succeeded CITE-seq datasets with a large number of ADT features (e.g., >=50), since LinQ-View is documented as best suited for large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50) Analyses that need per-cluster transcriptional entropy rather than surface-protein purity — the ROGUE score targets cluster uniformity in scRNA-seq, not the ADT modality rank sweep

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether a cell-type perturbation metric keeps stable rankings under varying cells-per-cell-type subsampling, or when demonstrating cell-count confounding of differential-expression-count metrics.
skills.name: rank-preservation-analysis
skills.search_text: rank-preservation-analysis Use when benchmarking whether a cell-type perturbation metric keeps stable rankings under varying cells-per-cell-type subsampling, or when demonstrating cell-count confounding of differential-expression-count metrics. Input data has not been normalized (scDist cannot be applied directly to raw counts; scTransform Pearson residual normalization is recommended) The goal is differential abundance of cell-type proportions rather than differential-state perturbation magnitude (use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead) Cells are heavily over-clustered or annotations are unreliable, since condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill that tests whether a cell-type perturbation metric (e.g., scDist distance) preserves its cell-type rankings across subsampled data sizes, while contrasting it against a confounded baseline (nDEG counts vs. cells per cell type) on resampled COVID-19 single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that tests whether a cell-type perturbation metric (e.g., scDist distance) preserves its cell-type rankings across subsampled data sizes, while contrasting it against a confounded baseline (nDEG counts vs. cells per cell type) on resampled COVID-19 single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been normalized (scDist cannot be applied directly to raw counts; scTransform Pearson residual normalization is recommended) The goal is differential abundance of cell-type proportions rather than differential-state perturbation magnitude (use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead) Cells are heavily over-clustered or annotations are unreliable, since condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward bias in estimated distances

skills.description: Use when a 4D-communication tensor (cell types x LR pairs x contexts x cell types) has been built with cell2cell and the number of latent communication factors must be chosen before running non-negative tensor component analysis.
skills.name: rank-selection-by-reconstruction-error
skills.search_text: rank-selection-by-reconstruction-error Use when a 4D-communication tensor (cell types x LR pairs x contexts x cell types) has been built with cell2cell and the number of latent communication factors must be chosen before running non-negative tensor component analysis. The tensor contains missing values across contexts — the article notes the implemented tensor decomposition algorithm is not optimized for missing values, so rank selection on an incomplete tensor may be biased Communication scores have not yet been computed per context; rank selection requires an assembled 4D tensor, not raw single-cell expression data A single-context cell-cell communication analysis is the goal — this skill applies to multi-context (e.g., 12 time-point) tensors, not one-sample deconvolution http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Select the number of tensor factors for Tensor-cell2cell decomposition by scanning component ranks and choosing the rank that minimizes the normalized reconstruction error of the 4D-communication tensor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Select the number of tensor factors for Tensor-cell2cell decomposition by scanning component ranks and choosing the rank that minimizes the normalized reconstruction error of the 4D-communication tensor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tensor contains missing values across contexts — the article notes the implemented tensor decomposition algorithm is not optimized for missing values, so rank selection on an incomplete tensor may be biased Communication scores have not yet been computed per context; rank selection requires an assembled 4D tensor, not raw single-cell expression data A single-context cell-cell communication analysis is the goal — this skill applies to multi-context (e.g., 12 time-point) tensors, not one-sample deconvolution

skills.description: Use when two independent sets of scores must be compared for a significant shift — e.g. donor-pair NMI values from MuDCoD vs. PisCES at one time point — and a nonparametric test on unpaired samples is appropriate.
skills.name: rank-sum-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: rank-sum-statistical-testing Use when two independent sets of scores must be compared for a significant shift — e.g. donor-pair NMI values from MuDCoD vs. PisCES at one time point — and a nonparametric test on unpaired samples is appropriate. When the score samples are paired (same donor pair scored under both methods with matching rank structure) — a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test would be the correct variant, not the unpaired rank-sum test used here. When the outcome is a continuous measurement across many observations rather than a small set of similarity scores per donor pair, where a parametric or permutational test may offer more power. When no baseline comparison exists (e.g. evaluating a single method's accuracy against ground truth) — ARI against true labels is the article's suggested alternative. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies the Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney) nonparametric test to compare distributions of donor-pair NMI scores between two community-detection methods (MuDCoD vs. PisCES) at a fixed time point, e.g. day-52 of the Jerber-2021 dopaminergic differentiation dataset, yielding a significance p-value for method superiority. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Applies the Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney) nonparametric test to compare distributions of donor-pair NMI scores between two community-detection methods (MuDCoD vs. PisCES) at a fixed time point, e.g. day-52 of the Jerber-2021 dopaminergic differentiation dataset, yielding a significance p-value for method superiority.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the score samples are paired (same donor pair scored under both methods with matching rank structure) — a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test would be the correct variant, not the unpaired rank-sum test used here. When the outcome is a continuous measurement across many observations rather than a small set of similarity scores per donor pair, where a parametric or permutational test may offer more power. When no baseline comparison exists (e.g. evaluating a single method's accuracy against ground truth) — ARI against true labels is the article's suggested alternative.

skills.description: Use when you have a labeled feature matrix (e.g. scRNA-seq expression with phenotype labels) and need a per-feature numeric score to produce a full descending feature ranking, as a baseline filter before or alongside marker-set methods like GreedyPC.
skills.name: ranked-feature-table-generation
skills.search_text: ranked-feature-table-generation Use when you have a labeled feature matrix (e.g. scRNA-seq expression with phenotype labels) and need a per-feature numeric score to produce a full descending feature ranking, as a baseline filter before or alongside marker-set methods like GreedyPC. The goal is a small globally discriminative marker set covering all phenotype pairs — use the phenotype cover algorithms (GreedyPC or CEM-PC) instead of a per-feature ranking filter No phenotype labels are available, since ReliefF requires contrasting same-class neighbors against different-label samples Input is already a ranked or selected feature list rather than a raw feature-by-sample matrix Generates a per-feature ranked table (e.g. relieff_faiss_ranked_features.csv) by computing a numeric importance score for every feature — in the marker-selection study, ReliefF weights over the Mouse Cortex (Zeisel et al.) scRNA-seq matrix using 30 faiss approximate-nearest-neighbor hits versus different-phenotype misses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Generates a per-feature ranked table (e.g. relieff_faiss_ranked_features.csv) by computing a numeric importance score for every feature — in the marker-selection study, ReliefF weights over the Mouse Cortex (Zeisel et al.) scRNA-seq matrix using 30 faiss approximate-nearest-neighbor hits versus different-phenotype misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a small globally discriminative marker set covering all phenotype pairs — use the phenotype cover algorithms (GreedyPC or CEM-PC) instead of a per-feature ranking filter No phenotype labels are available, since ReliefF requires contrasting same-class neighbors against different-label samples Input is already a ranked or selected feature list rather than a raw feature-by-sample matrix

skills.description: Use when scTenifoldNet's diffRegulation output (genes ranked by differential regulation distance with BH-adjusted p-values) is available and the goal is to identify enriched biological processes from that ranked list.
skills.name: ranked-gene-list-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: ranked-gene-list-enrichment-analysis Use when scTenifoldNet's diffRegulation output (genes ranked by differential regulation distance with BH-adjusted p-values) is available and the goal is to identify enriched biological processes from that ranked list. The two samples are highly dissimilar (e.g., different cell types) rather than two populations of cells of the same type — the article notes scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples. The analysis goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than differential transcriptional regulation; a DE tool, not comparative GRN analysis plus enrichment, is the right choice. The input is already a curated gene set or enrichment-ready table with no gene-level ranking statistic; re-ranking through the GRN pipeline is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Interprets scTenifoldNet's ranked differential-regulation output by running gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on genes ordered by their differential regulation distance, to recover biological programs such as opioid signaling, GPCR signaling, and reduced cytosolic calcium among differentially regulated genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Interprets scTenifoldNet's ranked differential-regulation output by running gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on genes ordered by their differential regulation distance, to recover biological programs such as opioid signaling, GPCR signaling, and reduced cytosolic calcium among differentially regulated genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two samples are highly dissimilar (e.g., different cell types) rather than two populations of cells of the same type — the article notes scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples. The analysis goal is differential expression of individual genes rather than differential transcriptional regulation; a DE tool, not comparative GRN analysis plus enrichment, is the right choice. The input is already a curated gene set or enrichment-ready table with no gene-level ranking statistic; re-ranking through the GRN pipeline is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when simulated or controlled datasets have a known ground-truth set of condition-associated key genes and you must quantify how accurately competing gene-ranking methods recover them.
skills.name: ranked-list-correlation-against-ground-truth
skills.search_text: ranked-list-correlation-against-ground-truth Use when simulated or controlled datasets have a known ground-truth set of condition-associated key genes and you must quantify how accurately competing gene-ranking methods recover them. Real datasets without a known ground-truth set of condition-associated key genes — AUPRC/Early Precision cannot be computed against truth Single-condition or single-batch datasets where batch and condition effects cannot be disentangled (scDisInFact needs multi-batch multi-condition input) Tasks other than gene-ranking evaluation, e.g., perturbation prediction or batch effect removal quality assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark protocol for condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection: rank genes with competing methods (scDisInFact gene scores, scINSIGHT membership variance, Wilcoxon rank-sum) and score each ranked list against known ground-truth CKG sets using AUPRC, Early Precision, and Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection: rank genes with competing methods (scDisInFact gene scores, scINSIGHT membership variance, Wilcoxon rank-sum) and score each ranked list against known ground-truth CKG sets using AUPRC, Early Precision, and Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real datasets without a known ground-truth set of condition-associated key genes — AUPRC/Early Precision cannot be computed against truth Single-condition or single-batch datasets where batch and condition effects cannot be disentangled (scDisInFact needs multi-batch multi-condition input) Tasks other than gene-ranking evaluation, e.g., perturbation prediction or batch effect removal quality assessment

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked, per-cell-type marker list (e.g., MASI's cell_markers dict from marker_identification) and need to weight markers by rank before summing marker expression into cell-type scores.
skills.name: ranked-list-linear-discounting
skills.search_text: ranked-list-linear-discounting Use when you have a ranked, per-cell-type marker list (e.g., MASI's cell_markers dict from marker_identification) and need to weight markers by rank before summing marker expression into cell-type scores. Input markers are not ranked per cell type (e.g., only a flat marker set) — the discount scheme requires an explicit rank order per cell type Only a single marker per cell type is available — with N=1 the 100%-to-50% endpoints are degenerate and weighting has no effect http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies MASI's linear marker-weighing scheme, in which the 1st marker in a cell type's ranked marker list contributes 100% of its expression to the cell-type score and the Nth marker contributes 50%, with intermediate markers discounted linearly. This weighting is the bridge from robust-rank-aggregated marker lists to MASI's cell-type score matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Applies MASI's linear marker-weighing scheme, in which the 1st marker in a cell type's ranked marker list contributes 100% of its expression to the cell-type score and the Nth marker contributes 50%, with intermediate markers discounted linearly. This weighting is the bridge from robust-rank-aggregated marker lists to MASI's cell-type score matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input markers are not ranked per cell type (e.g., only a flat marker set) — the discount scheme requires an explicit rank order per cell type Only a single marker per cell type is available — with N=1 the 100%-to-50% endpoints are degenerate and weighting has no effect

skills.description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (thousands to tens of thousands of cells, e.g. 68k PBMC or 4491-cell intestinal crypt) must be scanned for minor cell populations that bulk clustering toolkits like Seurat or Scater miss.
skills.name: rare-cell-cluster-identification
skills.search_text: rare-cell-cluster-identification Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (thousands to tens of thousands of cells, e.g. 68k PBMC or 4491-cell intestinal crypt) must be scanned for minor cell populations that bulk clustering toolkits like Seurat or Scater miss. The goal is comprehensive characterisation of major cell types, for which toolkits like Seurat or Scater are the appropriate choice The input is not a cell-by-gene expression profile (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables, bulk RNA-seq, or flow cytometry data) RaceID-scale per-cell clustering is required on modest-size data where full clustering is computationally feasible — though note RaceID's unrealistic runtime on thousands of cells is exactly what GapClust avoids http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect rare cell populations in large scRNA-seq datasets using GapClust, which exploits the gap between a minor cluster and its neighbouring abundant cluster via a second-order derivative type distance score on nearest-neighbour distances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Detect rare cell populations in large scRNA-seq datasets using GapClust, which exploits the gap between a minor cluster and its neighbouring abundant cluster via a second-order derivative type distance score on nearest-neighbour distances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comprehensive characterisation of major cell types, for which toolkits like Seurat or Scater are the appropriate choice The input is not a cell-by-gene expression profile (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables, bulk RNA-seq, or flow cytometry data) RaceID-scale per-cell clustering is required on modest-size data where full clustering is computationally feasible — though note RaceID's unrealistic runtime on thousands of cells is exactly what GapClust avoids

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering comparison must determine whether any method can separate known rare subclusters, and when external metrics (ARI/NMI) and internal metrics (per-cell silhouette) should be reported against a Louvain resolution sweep.
skills.name: rare-cell-cluster-separation-assessment
skills.search_text: rare-cell-cluster-separation-assessment Use when a scRNA-seq clustering comparison must determine whether any method can separate known rare subclusters, and when external metrics (ARI/NMI) and internal metrics (per-cell silhouette) should be reported against a Louvain resolution sweep. Input is real data without ground-truth labels — ARI/NMI cannot be computed and the comparison must rely on internal metrics or annotation only The goal is de novo rare-cell discovery in a single broad cluster (use SCISSORS reclustering directly) rather than benchmarking separation quality across methods The dataset has no rare or low-abundance subpopulations, where the silhouette/reclustering framework provides no advantage over standard Louvain http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark clustering methods on a simulated scRNA-seq dataset containing rare, closely placed clusters by computing silhouette scores (cluster::silhouette in PCA space), ARI, and NMI against ground truth, and sweeping Seurat Louvain resolutions to show whether higher resolution improves separation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Benchmark clustering methods on a simulated scRNA-seq dataset containing rare, closely placed clusters by computing silhouette scores (cluster::silhouette in PCA space), ARI, and NMI against ground truth, and sweeping Seurat Louvain resolutions to show whether higher resolution improves separation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real data without ground-truth labels — ARI/NMI cannot be computed and the comparison must rely on internal metrics or annotation only The goal is de novo rare-cell discovery in a single broad cluster (use SCISSORS reclustering directly) rather than benchmarking separation quality across methods The dataset has no rare or low-abundance subpopulations, where the silhouette/reclustering framework provides no advantage over standard Louvain

skills.description: Use when a new rare-cell or subcluster clustering method must be validated for label-recall ity on simulated scRNA-seq data with known ground-truth cell-type labels, comparing ARI/NMI/silhouette against clustering baselines.
skills.name: rare-cell-clustering-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: rare-cell-clustering-method-benchmarking Use when a new rare-cell or subcluster clustering method must be validated for label-recall ity on simulated scRNA-seq data with known ground-truth cell-type labels, comparing ARI/NMI/silhouette against clustering baselines. Data has no ground-truth labels and no simulation basis is possible — ARI/NMI label recapture cannot be computed, so only internal metrics remain The question is which clustering resolution a single method should use on one real dataset (use MultiK/getClusters-style resolution selection instead of cross-method benchmarking) Inputs are not per-cell scRNA-seq count matrices from a Seurat-standard pipeline (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables or bulk expression) — the silhouette-on-PCA comparison is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a rare-cell clustering method (SCISSORS) against Seurat/Louvain, GiniClust3, CellSIUS, k-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN, and Leiden on simulated scRNA-seq data with ground-truth labels, scoring each method by ARI, NMI, and median per-cell silhouette on cosine distance over PCA embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Benchmark a rare-cell clustering method (SCISSORS) against Seurat/Louvain, GiniClust3, CellSIUS, k-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN, and Leiden on simulated scRNA-seq data with ground-truth labels, scoring each method by ARI, NMI, and median per-cell silhouette on cosine distance over PCA embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has no ground-truth labels and no simulation basis is possible — ARI/NMI label recapture cannot be computed, so only internal metrics remain The question is which clustering resolution a single method should use on one real dataset (use MultiK/getClusters-style resolution selection instead of cross-method benchmarking) Inputs are not per-cell scRNA-seq count matrices from a Seurat-standard pipeline (e.g. already-aggregated feature tables or bulk expression) — the silhouette-on-PCA comparison is undefined

skills.description: Use when you already have per-cell rareness scores (FiRE) and IQR-thresholded rare cells (e.g. 727 cells from ~20k Arc-ME profiles) and need to partition them into minor sub-clusters for marker-based annotation.
skills.name: rare-cell-clustering-with-dropclust
skills.search_text: rare-cell-clustering-with-dropclust Use when you already have per-cell rareness scores (FiRE) and IQR-thresholded rare cells (e.g. 727 cells from ~20k Arc-ME profiles) and need to partition them into minor sub-clusters for marker-based annotation. You need to detect rare cells from the full dataset first — that is the FiRE scoring/thresholding step, not clustering; FiRE scores must exist before clustering the subset. Your goal is to identify or remove technical outliers/doublets — dropClust gives outliers no special treatment and they get submerged into minor cell clusters, and FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. The cell population you care about is abundant, not rare — a typical clustering technique cannot comprehensively chart minor cell types in one pass, and dropClust on the full ~20k profiles would not isolate the minor subpopulations this skill targets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cluster the small set of FiRE-detected rare cells (e.g. the 727 rare cells from the ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain scRNA-seq dataset) into minor subpopulations using dropClust, which applies no special handling of outliers, to resolve novel minor cell types such as the Hesx1+/Cyp2f2+ pars tuberalis sub-type (cluster R10). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Cluster the small set of FiRE-detected rare cells (e.g. the 727 rare cells from the ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain scRNA-seq dataset) into minor subpopulations using dropClust, which applies no special handling of outliers, to resolve novel minor cell types such as the Hesx1+/Cyp2f2+ pars tuberalis sub-type (cluster R10).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect rare cells from the full dataset first — that is the FiRE scoring/thresholding step, not clustering; FiRE scores must exist before clustering the subset. Your goal is to identify or remove technical outliers/doublets — dropClust gives outliers no special treatment and they get submerged into minor cell clusters, and FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. The cell population you care about is abundant, not rare — a typical clustering technique cannot comprehensively chart minor cell types in one pass, and dropClust on the full ~20k profiles would not isolate the minor subpopulations this skill targets.

skills.search_text: rare-cell-detection-benchmarking Use when comparing rare-cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq data, or when quantifying how few differentially expressed genes a detector needs and how runtimes scale to tens of thousands of profiles. The goal is doublet detection rather than rare-cell detection — FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types, and doublet rates (1%–30%) do not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness The analysis requires binary-only outputs to be avoided, i.e. when graded rareness scores per cell are needed for downstream ranking rather than the binary calls RaceID/GiniClust provide The dataset is a feature/summary table (e.g. already-clustered or dimensionality-reduced) rather than a cell x gene expression profile matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) on simulated and real scRNA-seq data by measuring AUC-ROC sensitivity to the number of DE genes and single-core runtime scaling from 1k to ~68k cells. This reproduces the FiRE paper's evaluation strategy and provides decision support for choosing a rare-entity finder. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Benchmark rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) on simulated and real scRNA-seq data by measuring AUC-ROC sensitivity to the number of DE genes and single-core runtime scaling from 1k to ~68k cells. This reproduces the FiRE paper's evaluation strategy and provides decision support for choosing a rare-entity finder.

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell rareness scores from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (tens of thousands of cells) and clustering-based rare cell tools (RaceID, GiniClust) are too slow or memory inefficient.
skills.name: rare-cell-identification
skills.search_text: rare-cell-identification Use when you need per-cell rareness scores from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (tens of thousands of cells) and clustering-based rare cell tools (RaceID, GiniClust) are too slow or memory inefficient. When the goal is to separate technical outliers from genuine minor cell types — FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. When doublet detection is required — doublet rates vary between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness. When input is already cluster labels or a small dataset where established tools like RaceID or GiniClust suffice; FiRE's advantage is scaling to tens of thousands of profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Implements FiRE (Finder of Rare Entities) rareness scoring: sketch each cell's expression profile into M=50-bit locality-sensitive hash codes with L=100 estimators and use bucket populousness to assign a per-cell rareness score without clustering. Enables rare cell detection on ultra-large scRNA-seq data in seconds (e.g. ~31 s for ~68k profiles). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Implements FiRE (Finder of Rare Entities) rareness scoring: sketch each cell's expression profile into M=50-bit locality-sensitive hash codes with L=100 estimators and use bucket populousness to assign a per-cell rareness score without clustering. Enables rare cell detection on ultra-large scRNA-seq data in seconds (e.g. ~31 s for ~68k profiles).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to separate technical outliers from genuine minor cell types — FiRE does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. When doublet detection is required — doublet rates vary between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness. When input is already cluster labels or a small dataset where established tools like RaceID or GiniClust suffice; FiRE's advantage is scaling to tens of thousands of profiles.

skills.name: rare-cell-population-detection
skills.search_text: rare-cell-population-detection Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset is too large for downstream analysis (e.g., >200k cells) and a rare cell population must be recovered without uniform subsampling that overlooks rare states. When the dataset is small enough that clustering or trajectory tools (e.g., SC3, Louvain) can run directly on the full data without sketching When the task requires systematic evaluation of the interplay between the sketching distance metric and downstream preprocessing, which the authors explicitly did not address When rare-population recovery depends on prior categorical knowledge beyond proof-of-principle fairness sketching, since the authors note additional experiments are required http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Recover rare cell populations (e.g., inflammatory macrophages) from massive scRNA-seq datasets by sketching a representative cell subset with Sphetcher's spherical thresholding, then clustering the sketch with Louvain and quantifying marker-gene enrichment by AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126

skills.description: Use when a broadly-defined scRNA-seq cluster is suspected heterogeneous (e.g. a stromal/mesenchymal cluster that may hide CAF subtypes, or immune clusters hiding fine-grained subtypes) and rare, low-abundance subpopulations must be recovered from Seurat-processed data.
skills.name: rare-cell-population-identification
skills.search_text: rare-cell-population-identification Use when a broadly-defined scRNA-seq cluster is suspected heterogeneous (e.g. a stromal/mesenchymal cluster that may hide CAF subtypes, or immune clusters hiding fine-grained subtypes) and rare, low-abundance subpopulations must be recovered from Seurat-processed data. Broad clusters already have high median silhouette scores (homogeneous) — reclustering there adds noise, since SCISSORS targets clusters with low median silhouette scores. Input is not single-cell RNA-seq data requiring subclustering (e.g. an already fine-grained cell-type-annotated dataset or a bulk/feature table) — SCISSORS is designed for subcluster discovery within broadly-defined scRNA-seq clusters. The question is de novo clustering of an unclustered dataset rather than recovering rare subpopulations hidden inside existing broad clusters — existing methods focused on the optimal number of robust clusters are the wrong framing here, but so is treating SCISSORS as a general first-pass clustering tool. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 SCISSORS-based skill for recovering extremely low-abundance cell populations by splitting heterogeneous broad clusters via silhouette-scored, semi-supervised iterative reclustering wrapped around Seurat. It enables identification of rare subtypes (e.g. 23-cell apCAF populations) that standard unsupervised clustering misses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: SCISSORS-based skill for recovering extremely low-abundance cell populations by splitting heterogeneous broad clusters via silhouette-scored, semi-supervised iterative reclustering wrapped around Seurat. It enables identification of rare subtypes (e.g. 23-cell apCAF populations) that standard unsupervised clustering misses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Broad clusters already have high median silhouette scores (homogeneous) — reclustering there adds noise, since SCISSORS targets clusters with low median silhouette scores. Input is not single-cell RNA-seq data requiring subclustering (e.g. an already fine-grained cell-type-annotated dataset or a bulk/feature table) — SCISSORS is designed for subcluster discovery within broadly-defined scRNA-seq clusters. The question is de novo clustering of an unclustered dataset rather than recovering rare subpopulations hidden inside existing broad clusters — existing methods focused on the optimal number of robust clusters are the wrong framing here, but so is treating SCISSORS as a general first-pass clustering tool.

skills.description: Use when clustering an already-annotated single-cell subset (e.g. SingleR-annotated T/NK cells from RA patient PBMCs) and the goal is to resolve rare subtypes and doublets and report their cluster frequencies.
skills.name: rare-cell-subtype-frequency-quantification
skills.search_text: rare-cell-subtype-frequency-quantification Use when clustering an already-annotated single-cell subset (e.g. SingleR-annotated T/NK cells from RA patient PBMCs) and the goal is to resolve rare subtypes and doublets and report their cluster frequencies. Input is raw whole-PBMC data without an upstream cell-type annotation — deconvolve broad types first rather than applying this subtype-resolution workflow Cells are being assigned purely by reference-based annotation (e.g. SingleR) without clustering — platelet and RBC transcriptomes are absent from the reference panel, so rare doublets are mis-classified The dataset lacks disease-associated or rare subpopulations and a generic feature-selection pipeline would suffice Deconvolution of an annotated single-cell subset (e.g. SingleR-annotated T/NK cells from rheumatoid arthritis PBMCs) using DUBStepR correlation-based feature selection with DI optimization, to resolve discrete subtypes — including rare clusters like RBCs, proliferating cells, and platelet-T/NK doublets — and quantify their frequencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Deconvolution of an annotated single-cell subset (e.g. SingleR-annotated T/NK cells from rheumatoid arthritis PBMCs) using DUBStepR correlation-based feature selection with DI optimization, to resolve discrete subtypes — including rare clusters like RBCs, proliferating cells, and platelet-T/NK doublets — and quantify their frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw whole-PBMC data without an upstream cell-type annotation — deconvolve broad types first rather than applying this subtype-resolution workflow Cells are being assigned purely by reference-based annotation (e.g. SingleR) without clustering — platelet and RBC transcriptomes are absent from the reference panel, so rare doublets are mis-classified The dataset lacks disease-associated or rare subpopulations and a generic feature-selection pipeline would suffice

skills.name: rare-celltype-balancing-for-classification
skills.search_text: rare-celltype-balancing-for-classification Use when preparing a cell-by-gene reference matrix (e.g., SELINA xx_expr.txt with paired xx_meta.txt labels) for supervised cell-type annotation and some cell types are far outnumbered by majority types. The query dataset is being annotated with an already-trained SELINA model — balancing is applied to reference data before pre-training, not to query data Cell-type counts are already roughly balanced relative to Nmax, so no rare types fall below the rarity threshold Working with disease-mode data where diverse abnormal-cell expression profiles are expected and the paper recommends users train with their own data rather than relying on curated references http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Balances a reference scRNA-seq expression matrix before supervised training by oversampling rare cell types with SMOTE, so that minority cell types are not ignored during classifier modeling (as in SELINA's cell-type balancing step). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100577
skills.summary: Balances a reference scRNA-seq expression matrix before supervised training by oversampling rare cell types with SMOTE, so that minority cell types are not ignored during classifier modeling (as in SELINA's cell-type balancing step).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query dataset is being annotated with an already-trained SELINA model — balancing is applied to reference data before pre-training, not to query data Cell-type counts are already roughly balanced relative to Nmax, so no rare types fall below the rarity threshold Working with disease-mode data where diverse abnormal-cell expression profiles are expected and the paper recommends users train with their own data rather than relying on curated references

skills.description: Use when after cluster decomposition and merging in scCAD, you need to score each M-cluster's rarity from isolation-forest anomaly scores and decide which sub-clusters count as rare cell types.
skills.name: rare-cluster-threshold-classification
skills.search_text: rare-cluster-threshold-classification Use when after cluster decomposition and merging in scCAD, you need to score each M-cluster's rarity from isolation-forest anomaly scores and decide which sub-clusters count as rare cell types. You need anomaly scores on the full global expression profile rather than cluster-specific top-20 differential gene sets — scCAD's IS is defined relative to each M-cluster's candidate gene set Clusters have not yet been decomposed and merged (rare_h default 0.01, merge_h default 0.3); the independence score presupposes M-cluster assignments You want a quantitative rarity ranking rather than a binary rare/common classification at a fixed threshold http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies scCAD's M-clusters as rare or common by feeding each cluster's top-20 differential genes into an isolation forest, converting anomaly scores into an independence score (IS), and flagging clusters with IS above the default threshold I = 0.7. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9
skills.summary: Classifies scCAD's M-clusters as rare or common by feeding each cluster's top-20 differential genes into an isolation forest, converting anomaly scores into an independence score (IS), and flagging clusters with IS above the default threshold I = 0.7.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need anomaly scores on the full global expression profile rather than cluster-specific top-20 differential gene sets — scCAD's IS is defined relative to each M-cluster's candidate gene set Clusters have not yet been decomposed and merged (rare_h default 0.01, merge_h default 0.3); the independence score presupposes M-cluster assignments You want a quantitative rarity ranking rather than a binary rare/common classification at a fixed threshold

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result may hide rare cell types inside large clusters, and you need to recursively decompose oversized clusters (R*n threshold) and merge near-identical sub-clusters before rare-population scoring.
skills.name: rare-population-cluster-size-thresholding
skills.search_text: rare-population-cluster-size-thresholding Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result may hide rare cell types inside large clusters, and you need to recursively decompose oversized clusters (R*n threshold) and merge near-identical sub-clusters before rare-population scoring. Input is not raw/normalized single-cell expression data (e.g. already a feature table, marker matrix, or bulk expression profile) since decomposition requires per-cell expression vectors for PCA and cluster centers Clusters are already all below the R*n size threshold and rare populations are expected to be cleanly separated by one-time Louvain clustering, making recursive decomposition unnecessary The goal is differential expression testing between known groups rather than discovery of rare, previously unlabeled sub-populations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Iterative cluster decomposition and merging used by scCAD: initial Louvain I-clusters are recursively split while any cluster exceeds R*n cells, then decomposed D-clusters are merged via center-distance threshold THM to yield M-clusters prior to rare cluster detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9
skills.summary: Iterative cluster decomposition and merging used by scCAD: initial Louvain I-clusters are recursively split while any cluster exceeds R*n cells, then decomposed D-clusters are merged via center-distance threshold THM to yield M-clusters prior to rare cluster detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw/normalized single-cell expression data (e.g. already a feature table, marker matrix, or bulk expression profile) since decomposition requires per-cell expression vectors for PCA and cluster centers Clusters are already all below the R*n size threshold and rare populations are expected to be cleanly separated by one-time Louvain clustering, making recursive decomposition unnecessary The goal is differential expression testing between known groups rather than discovery of rare, previously unlabeled sub-populations

skills.description: Use when experimental-design questions ask how many cells (N) must be sequenced to detect a rare subpopulation (e.g., 5% or 10% of cells) and ARI-vs-N curves per method are needed.
skills.name: rare-population-detection-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: rare-population-detection-curve-visualization Use when experimental-design questions ask how many cells (N) must be sequenced to detect a rare subpopulation (e.g., 5% or 10% of cells) and ARI-vs-N curves per method are needed. The goal is trajectory inference benchmarking (dynwrap/dynmethods territory), not rare-population detection power curves. Data are real experimental counts without known ground-truth population labels, so adjusted Rand index against true labels cannot be computed. The simulation uses non-UMI protocols or continuous EVF trajectories rather than the discrete-population UMI setting this curve analysis was validated on. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Plots adjusted Rand index (ARI) as a function of total cell number N (and simulation parameters like Sigma, alpha, depth, and rare-population proportion Prop) for each clustering method, reproducing Fig. 5b–c rare-population detection curves from SymSim UMI-based simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Plots adjusted Rand index (ARI) as a function of total cell number N (and simulation parameters like Sigma, alpha, depth, and rare-population proportion Prop) for each clustering method, reproducing Fig. 5b–c rare-population detection curves from SymSim UMI-based simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is trajectory inference benchmarking (dynwrap/dynmethods territory), not rare-population detection power curves. Data are real experimental counts without known ground-truth population labels, so adjusted Rand index against true labels cannot be computed. The simulation uses non-UMI protocols or continuous EVF trajectories rather than the discrete-population UMI setting this curve analysis was validated on.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell detection tools across controlled rare-population sizes and DE strengths, or when deciding whether a detector (e.g. GapClust) retains accuracy as the planted minor cluster grows from 2 to 100 cells.
skills.name: rare-population-proportion-scaling
skills.search_text: rare-population-proportion-scaling Use when benchmarking rare-cell detection tools across controlled rare-population sizes and DE strengths, or when deciding whether a detector (e.g. GapClust) retains accuracy as the planted minor cluster grows from 2 to 100 cells. The goal is general clustering of major cell types — Seurat/Scater-style workflows are the article's designated tools for major populations, not this rare-cell proportion sweep You need to call a rare population in a single real dataset rather than benchmark detectors against simulated ground truth — run GapClust directly instead of the simulation sweep The rare population is not 'rare' relative to dataset size (planted sizes here stay ≤ 100 cells per simulated profile) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq count matrices in which the size of a planted rare population (2–100 cells) and its differential-expression level (de.prob 0.1–0.8) are systematically swept, so that rare-cell detectors can be benchmarked by F1 score across rare-population proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Generates Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq count matrices in which the size of a planted rare population (2–100 cells) and its differential-expression level (de.prob 0.1–0.8) are systematically swept, so that rare-cell detectors can be benchmarked by F1 score across rare-population proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general clustering of major cell types — Seurat/Scater-style workflows are the article's designated tools for major populations, not this rare-cell proportion sweep You need to call a rare population in a single real dataset rather than benchmark detectors against simulated ground truth — run GapClust directly instead of the simulation sweep The rare population is not 'rare' relative to dataset size (planted sizes here stay ≤ 100 cells per simulated profile)

skills.description: Use when you must determine how far MetaNeighbor AUROC performance degrades as a held-out cell type becomes rare (1-20% incidence) or only subtly different from the out-group, before trusting a replicability call.
skills.name: rarity-and-subtlety-parameter-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: rarity-and-subtlety-parameter-sweep-analysis Use when you must determine how far MetaNeighbor AUROC performance degrades as a held-out cell type becomes rare (1-20% incidence) or only subtly different from the out-group, before trusting a replicability call. Cell-type labels are unknown or ambiguous across datasets — use the unsupervised MetaNeighbor variant (variableGenes + MetaNeighborUS) instead of the supervised sweep Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — MetaNeighbor cannot run on such inputs The goal is discovering new subtypes rather than quantifying how robust identification of a known target type is under rarity/subtlety degradation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Empirically stress-tests MetaNeighbor's supervised neighbor-voting replicability framework by sweeping target cell-type incidence (rarity, 1-20%) and transcriptional subtlety (up to ~88-90%) using the GO:0022857 transporter-activity gene set versus matched random 20-gene controls, quantifying robustness via mean AUROC (e.g. ~0.71 at ~88% subtlety for excitatory neurons). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Empirically stress-tests MetaNeighbor's supervised neighbor-voting replicability framework by sweeping target cell-type incidence (rarity, 1-20%) and transcriptional subtlety (up to ~88-90%) using the GO:0022857 transporter-activity gene set versus matched random 20-gene controls, quantifying robustness via mean AUROC (e.g. ~0.71 at ~88% subtlety for excitatory neurons).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are unknown or ambiguous across datasets — use the unsupervised MetaNeighbor variant (variableGenes + MetaNeighborUS) instead of the supervised sweep Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix row names — MetaNeighbor cannot run on such inputs The goal is discovering new subtypes rather than quantifying how robust identification of a known target type is under rarity/subtlety degradation

skills.description: Use when input consists of paired, cell-by-event count matrices (inclusion/exclusion or spliced/unspliced reads) from multi-sample single-cell data and the goal is a harmonized latent embedding plus imputed ratio (e.g., logit PSI) values.
skills.name: ratio-mode-latent-variable-modeling-of-paired-counts
skills.search_text: ratio-mode-latent-variable-modeling-of-paired-counts Use when input consists of paired, cell-by-event count matrices (inclusion/exclusion or spliced/unspliced reads) from multi-sample single-cell data and the goal is a harmonized latent embedding plus imputed ratio (e.g., logit PSI) values. Input is a single count matrix (gene expression) rather than paired ratio-based measurements (inclusion/exclusion, spliced/unspliced) — use GEDI's standard single-measurement mode instead The goal requires nonlinear manifold learning — GEDI currently supports only linear manifold learning with an optional hyperellipsoid restriction Data are not multi-sample — inter-sample harmonization (the main benefit of this mode) has no counterpart to remove GEDI's ratio mode fits a Bayesian latent variable model to paired count matrices (e.g., exon inclusion raw_M1 / exclusion raw_M2 from Quantas) by modeling the log-ratio with a binomial data-generating distribution, enabling inter-sample harmonization and imputed logit(PSI) estimates for ratio-based single-cell modalities like alternative splicing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: GEDI's ratio mode fits a Bayesian latent variable model to paired count matrices (e.g., exon inclusion raw_M1 / exclusion raw_M2 from Quantas) by modeling the log-ratio with a binomial data-generating distribution, enabling inter-sample harmonization and imputed logit(PSI) estimates for ratio-based single-cell modalities like alternative splicing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single count matrix (gene expression) rather than paired ratio-based measurements (inclusion/exclusion, spliced/unspliced) — use GEDI's standard single-measurement mode instead The goal requires nonlinear manifold learning — GEDI currently supports only linear manifold learning with an optional hyperellipsoid restriction Data are not multi-sample — inter-sample harmonization (the main benefit of this mode) has no counterpart to remove

skills.search_text: raw-idat-test-data-ingestion Use when reproducing or smoke-testing the methylR pipeline on the authors' distributed test dataset, or when Illumina 450K/EPIC raw methylation data (IDAT) must be ingested into a locally running methylR container. You only need the accessory GUI demo inputs (Volcano, PCA/MDS, heatmap, pathway enrichment) — those are in the GitHub data/ directory, not testData.zip Your host is ARM64, which is explicitly not supported by methylR You need to analyze your own 450K/EPIC samples rather than reproduce the authors' test-data workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Obtains and loads methylR's Illumina methylation array test dataset (testData.zip from SourceForge) into the locally-run methylR Shiny/Docker container so that complete ChAMP or minfi analyses can be executed on raw data with a few mouse clicks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad184

skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the accessory GUI demo inputs (Volcano, PCA/MDS, heatmap, pathway enrichment) — those are in the GitHub data/ directory, not testData.zip Your host is ARM64, which is explicitly not supported by methylR You need to analyze your own 450K/EPIC samples rather than reproduce the authors' test-data workflow

skills.description: Use when implementing per-cell selection in a VR scatter/DR plot where datasets with tens of thousands of points (e.g., the >30k-cell mouse gastrulation GSE87038 coordinates) make per-point Unity colliders infeasible.
skills.name: raycast-collision-detection
skills.search_text: raycast-collision-detection Use when implementing per-cell selection in a VR scatter/DR plot where datasets with tens of thousands of points (e.g., the >30k-cell mouse gastrulation GSE87038 coordinates) make per-point Unity colliders infeasible. The DR plot is sparse (far fewer than tens of thousands of points), where attaching native Unity colliders per point would be simpler and sufficient The goal is data preparation or backend statistics (e.g., DE gene identification in cellexalvrR) rather than in-VR interaction/collision logic Working outside the Unity/C# VR environment (e.g., selecting cells in a 2D desktop plotting tool) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Engineer a purpose-built collision detection system (octree spatial indexing plus controller raycast traversal) in CellexalVR's C# codebase so that every cell in dense dimension-reduction plots containing >30k points remains individually selectable without lag. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251

skills.description: Use when fitting TCM to temporal single-cell RNA-seq data and you must configure the radial prototype landscape and the RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior over prototype positions before variational EM fitting.
skills.name: rbf-gaussian-process-prior-specification
skills.search_text: rbf-gaussian-process-prior-specification Use when fitting TCM to temporal single-cell RNA-seq data and you must configure the radial prototype landscape and the RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior over prototype positions before variational EM fitting. The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern (a stated requirement of TCM) No temporal/staged sampling exists — for non-temporal single-cell data a generic dimension-reduction method (t-SNE, diffusion map) is more appropriate You need immediate biological interpretation of cell clusters; the article notes pathway analysis must be conducted separately on TCM's latent space http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Specifies the generative-model prior structure of the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) algorithm: prototype metagenes laid out on an R×S radial landscape grid whose latent positions are governed by an RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior, coupled with Poisson read-count likelihoods and Gamma priors on rates, so temporal scRNA-seq cells are convolved onto one 2D latent space with early time points at the center and later ones at the periphery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05112-9
skills.summary: Specifies the generative-model prior structure of the TCM (Topographic Cell Map) algorithm: prototype metagenes laid out on an R×S radial landscape grid whose latent positions are governed by an RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior, coupled with Poisson read-count likelihoods and Gamma priors on rates, so temporal scRNA-seq cells are convolved onto one 2D latent space with early time points at the center and later ones at the periphery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern (a stated requirement of TCM) No temporal/staged sampling exists — for non-temporal single-cell data a generic dimension-reduction method (t-SNE, diffusion map) is more appropriate You need immediate biological interpretation of cell clusters; the article notes pathway analysis must be conducted separately on TCM's latent space

skills.description: Use when you have a catalog of splicing QTLs (e.g. from sQTLseekeR2 on GTEx) plus ENCODE eCLIP peak sets and want to identify which RBPs' binding sites are altered by sQTLs relative to non-sQTL variants.
skills.name: rbp-binding-site-disruption-analysis
skills.search_text: rbp-binding-site-disruption-analysis Use when you have a catalog of splicing QTLs (e.g. from sQTLseekeR2 on GTEx) plus ENCODE eCLIP peak sets and want to identify which RBPs' binding sites are altered by sQTLs relative to non-sQTL variants. You need cis-association mapping itself rather than downstream interpretation of an existing sQTL catalog — use sqtlseeker2-nf/sQTLseekeR2 directly for that step. Your variants do not overlap high-confidence eCLIP peaks (FDR < 0.01, FC >= 2) or the RBP has fewer than 30 top-5% sQTLs in its peaks — the paper restricted analysis to 32 such RBPs. You are evaluating protein-coding loss-of-function or splice-site variants — tools like LOFTEE address that complementary question, not RBP motif disruption. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the sQTL-downstream analysis from Garrido-Martín et al. testing whether splicing QTLs disrupt RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding sites more than splice-site motifs, by training gapped-kmer SVM (gkmSVM) models on ENCODE eCLIP peaks and comparing deltaSVM scores of sQTLs vs non-sQTLs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Reproduces the sQTL-downstream analysis from Garrido-Martín et al. testing whether splicing QTLs disrupt RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding sites more than splice-site motifs, by training gapped-kmer SVM (gkmSVM) models on ENCODE eCLIP peaks and comparing deltaSVM scores of sQTLs vs non-sQTLs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need cis-association mapping itself rather than downstream interpretation of an existing sQTL catalog — use sqtlseeker2-nf/sQTLseekeR2 directly for that step. Your variants do not overlap high-confidence eCLIP peaks (FDR < 0.01, FC >= 2) or the RBP has fewer than 30 top-5% sQTLs in its peaks — the paper restricted analysis to 32 such RBPs. You are evaluating protein-coding loss-of-function or splice-site variants — tools like LOFTEE address that complementary question, not RBP motif disruption.

skills.description: Use when an NMF (or other) clustering of candidate RBPs has produced cluster assignments and you must test whether any single cluster is significantly enriched for known gold-standard circRNA regulators before accepting the clustering strategy.
skills.name: rbp-candidate-validation-against-gold-standard
skills.search_text: rbp-candidate-validation-against-gold-standard Use when an NMF (or other) clustering of candidate RBPs has produced cluster assignments and you must test whether any single cluster is significantly enriched for known gold-standard circRNA regulators before accepting the clustering strategy. You have not yet generated NMF cluster assignments (NMFgroup_XXclusterYYrun.txt) from the CRIT feature matrix — run NMF.R first. Your candidate set is not RBPs or lacks a curated gold-standard regulator list to test enrichment against. You need de novo prediction of regulators rather than validation of an existing clustering against known regulators (use supervised-learning extensions, noted as unimplemented in the paper). http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates NMF-derived RBP clusters from the CRIT pipeline by Fisher's exact tests of cluster membership against gold-standard circRNA regulator lists, demonstrating that the clustering captures known regulators (cluster 23: 17/90 gold regulators, p=0.00012). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Validates NMF-derived RBP clusters from the CRIT pipeline by Fisher's exact tests of cluster membership against gold-standard circRNA regulator lists, demonstrating that the clustering captures known regulators (cluster 23: 17/90 gold regulators, p=0.00012).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet generated NMF cluster assignments (NMFgroup_XXclusterYYrun.txt) from the CRIT feature matrix — run NMF.R first. Your candidate set is not RBPs or lacks a curated gold-standard regulator list to test enrichment against. You need de novo prediction of regulators rather than validation of an existing clustering against known regulators (use supervised-learning extensions, noted as unimplemented in the paper).

skills.description: Use when a merged CRIT feature matrix plus NMF cluster membership labels are available and the goal is to rank features (e.g., Zg splicing similarity, Zp alteration proportion) that separate predicted circRNA regulators from other RBPs.
skills.name: rbp-cluster-comparison-statistics
skills.search_text: rbp-cluster-comparison-statistics Use when a merged CRIT feature matrix plus NMF cluster membership labels are available and the goal is to rank features (e.g., Zg splicing similarity, Zp alteration proportion) that separate predicted circRNA regulators from other RBPs. The goal is to predict/cluster circRNA regulators from raw multi-omics data rather than characterize an already-produced NMF cluster — use the full CRIT NMF.R pipeline instead Input is not a merged CRIT feature matrix (e.g., raw TCGA alteration files or MiOncoCirc FPKM tables that have not passed through the GET_*.R feature scripts) There is only one group (no cluster labels) so no two-sample comparison is defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A per-feature two-sample Welch t-test procedure in R that compares the 51 CRIT features (ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) between NMF-predicted circRNA-regulating RBPs (90 genes) and the remaining 916 RBPs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, to identify which feature categories distinguish authentic regulators. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: A per-feature two-sample Welch t-test procedure in R that compares the 51 CRIT features (ρm, Zp, Zs, Zg, C value) between NMF-predicted circRNA-regulating RBPs (90 genes) and the remaining 916 RBPs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, to identify which feature categories distinguish authentic regulators.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to predict/cluster circRNA regulators from raw multi-omics data rather than characterize an already-produced NMF cluster — use the full CRIT NMF.R pipeline instead Input is not a merged CRIT feature matrix (e.g., raw TCGA alteration files or MiOncoCirc FPKM tables that have not passed through the GET_*.R feature scripts) There is only one group (no cluster labels) so no two-sample comparison is defined

skills.description: Use when building the prior interaction graph needed to search RBP-ncRNA circuits (RNCs) from multi-omics differential expression scores, e.g. TCGA ESCA/BRCA or APP/PS1 mouse data scored with fRNC.
skills.name: rbp-ncrna-interaction-network-construction
skills.search_text: rbp-ncrna-interaction-network-construction Use when building the prior interaction graph needed to search RBP-ncRNA circuits (RNCs) from multi-omics differential expression scores, e.g. TCGA ESCA/BRCA or APP/PS1 mouse data scored with fRNC. You have no ENCORI/CLIP-seq or PARE-derived interaction data and only a user-supplied generic PPI or co-expression graph — fRNC's interStringency pipeline is specific to ENCORI RBP-ncRNA interactions. You need low-stringency interactions including non-experimental predictions — interStringency with stringency='high' restricts to CLIP experimental evidence count >= 3, discarding weaker support by design. The goal is differential expression itself rather than circuit detection — use the fRNC DEGs/edgeR step first; this skill only builds the interaction prior. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Construct a high-stringency RBP-ncRNA interaction network in the fRNC R package by extracting ENCORI (starBase) CLIP-seq/PARE-derived interactions with interStringency and standardizing node identifiers (Ensembl, miRBase MIMAT, circBase IDs) into a node_gene_ID/type/target_gene_ID edge list. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Construct a high-stringency RBP-ncRNA interaction network in the fRNC R package by extracting ENCORI (starBase) CLIP-seq/PARE-derived interactions with interStringency and standardizing node identifiers (Ensembl, miRBase MIMAT, circBase IDs) into a node_gene_ID/type/target_gene_ID edge list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no ENCORI/CLIP-seq or PARE-derived interaction data and only a user-supplied generic PPI or co-expression graph — fRNC's interStringency pipeline is specific to ENCORI RBP-ncRNA interactions. You need low-stringency interactions including non-experimental predictions — interStringency with stringency='high' restricts to CLIP experimental evidence count >= 3, discarding weaker support by design. The goal is differential expression itself rather than circuit detection — use the fRNC DEGs/edgeR step first; this skill only builds the interaction prior.

skills.description: Use when detected RNC modules (global or local, e.g. from runmodule with FDR = 1e-5) need permutation-based validation of whether their summary scores exceed what random node sets of the same size would achieve.
skills.name: rbp-ncrna-network-module-scoring
skills.search_text: rbp-ncrna-network-module-scoring Use when detected RNC modules (global or local, e.g. from runmodule with FDR = 1e-5) need permutation-based validation of whether their summary scores exceed what random node sets of the same size would achieve. The modules have not yet been detected by fRNC runmodule — build the null against existing observed scores, not before module detection The scoring scheme (gene2weight or network) differs from that used during module search — the null must use the identical scoring to be a valid comparison The goal is functional/GO enrichment of modules rather than statistical robustness of module scores — permutation of node sets does not assess enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Assess the statistical significance of detected RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) modules by building an empirical null distribution of module scores from 100,000 randomly sampled node sets of matching size, and computing one-sided empirical p-values against the observed scores. This confirms that fRNC-detected modules score significantly higher than random node sets under the same scoring scheme. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.03.035
skills.summary: Assess the statistical significance of detected RBP-ncRNA circuit (RNC) modules by building an empirical null distribution of module scores from 100,000 randomly sampled node sets of matching size, and computing one-sided empirical p-values against the observed scores. This confirms that fRNC-detected modules score significantly higher than random node sets under the same scoring scheme.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modules have not yet been detected by fRNC runmodule — build the null against existing observed scores, not before module detection The scoring scheme (gene2weight or network) differs from that used during module search — the null must use the identical scoring to be a valid comparison The goal is functional/GO enrichment of modules rather than statistical robustness of module scores — permutation of node sets does not assess enrichment

skills.description: Use when both an RDR_Xdata and a BAF_merge_Xdata from XClone runs on the same cells/genes exist and per-cell haplotype-aware copy-number states (including copy-neutral LOH) are needed.
skills.name: rdr-baf-cna-state-combination
skills.search_text: rdr-baf-cna-state-combination Use when both an RDR_Xdata and a BAF_merge_Xdata from XClone runs on the same cells/genes exist and per-cell haplotype-aware copy-number states (including copy-neutral LOH) are needed. Only one signal type is available (e.g., no BAF/allele data): combine cannot run and RDR alone will miss copy-neutral LOH. The goal is bulk or pseudo-bulk clonal CNA calling (e.g., Numbat-style); XClone combine is designed for per-cell resolution from scRNA-seq counts. The dataset contains no identifiable normal/reference cell type, so ref_celltype cannot be set and baseline normalization is undefined. The goal is pseudo-bulk or single-cell DNA-seq CNA calling (e.g. ACT, CHISEL), which does not rely on scRNA-seq read-depth ratios. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalizes the gene-by-cell scRNA-seq read-depth matrix against a user-specified reference cell type (e.g. 'N' non-tumour cells) before XClone's negative-binomial RDR modeling, so copy-number states are expressed as ratios relative to baseline ploidy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Normalizes the gene-by-cell scRNA-seq read-depth matrix against a user-specified reference cell type (e.g. 'N' non-tumour cells) before XClone's negative-binomial RDR modeling, so copy-number states are expressed as ratios relative to baseline ploidy.

skills.description: Use when converting a gene-by-sample RNA-seq expression matrix into reaction-level upper/lower bounds for Human-GEM FBA, i.e., capping each of the 13,082 reaction fluxes by its GPR-derived normalized MRAS with a nutrient medium constraint.

skills.summary: Benchmark scPathoQuant per-cell pathogen read counts against comparator tools (ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, Venus) by correlating read abundance and checking expected count offsets, as done for HIV-infected donor 2 cells in Fig. 5B-D.

skills.search_text: read-barcode-assignment-sc-rnaseq Use when you have FASTQ or FASTA single-cell reads (e.g. 10x Chromium or Visium libraries, noisy long-read scRNA-seq) and need to identify cellular barcodes and UMIs and assign reads to them. Barcodes have already been extracted and corrected and the input is a count matrix or cell-by-gene table rather than raw reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assign single-cell reads (short or long) to cellular barcodes using Flexiplex, either in known-barcode mode with chemistry presets (e.g. 10x3v3) or in barcode discovery mode followed by whitelist filtering and empty-droplet removal via flexiplex-filter. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae102

skills.name: read-coverage-peak-calling
skills.search_text: read-coverage-peak-calling Use when a BAM of aligned 3'-end-enriched reads (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) must be scanned for broad coverage peaks to serve as candidate 3' UTRs against an existing GFF3/GTF gene model. skills.search_text: read-depth-binning-at-100kb-resolution Use when preparing high-coverage (>20x) single-cell WGS BAMs for CNA detection or tool benchmarking at small variant sizes (200 kb–5 Mb), where a fixed 100 kb bin resolution harmonizes read depth across callers. skills.name: read-depth-segmentation
skills.search_text: read-depth-segmentation Use when segmenting high-coverage (>20x) PTA-amplified single-cell WGS read-depth profiles into CNAs at 200 kb–5 Mb scales, especially when allele-specific calls and comparison against BAF-agnostic RDR-only callers are needed. skills.search_text: read-group-barcoded-bam-splitting Use when a BAM of aligned sequencing reads (e.g. from 10x Chromium single-cell runs) must be split by SAM FLAG reverse-strand bit and RG tag into per-strand, per-read-group BAMs before peak calling or coverage analysis. skills.description: Use when performing allele-specific read assignment for ASAS analysis: you have phased per-chromosome VCFs, gzipped FASTQ reads, hg19.fa, and need to label each uniquely aligned read with haplotype 1, 2, or 'discarded'.
skills.name: read-haplotype-assignment-majority-voting
skills.search_text: read-haplotype-assignment-majority-voting Use when performing allele-specific read assignment for ASAS analysis: you have phased per-chromosome VCFs, gzipped FASTQ reads, hg19.fa, and need to label each uniquely aligned read with haplotype 1, 2, or 'discarded'. You only need gene/transcript quantification without allele-specific resolution — a single-genome STAR alignment is cheaper than dual haplotype-genome mapping The heterozygous SNP of interest lies within, or too far from, the alternative exon so that no read can cover both SNP and splice event — PAIRADISE cannot analyze these SNPs with short reads Your SNVs are putative RNA editing sites rather than germline heterozygous variants — PAIRADISE handles these separately via the RADAR-based --rnaedit flag, not via haplotype personalization http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 PAIRADISE-style assignment of RNA-seq reads to haplotype 1 or 2 after aligning to haplotype-modified personal genomes: reads are retained only if they map uniquely to both personal genome versions at the same location, then assigned by majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs, with draws and ambiguous reads discarded. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: PAIRADISE-style assignment of RNA-seq reads to haplotype 1 or 2 after aligning to haplotype-modified personal genomes: reads are retained only if they map uniquely to both personal genome versions at the same location, then assigned by majority voting over covered heterozygous SNPs, with draws and ambiguous reads discarded.
