skills.name: region-specific-gene-identification
skills.search_text: region-specific-gene-identification Use when a reconstructed single-cell spatial landscape is available and the goal is to find genes determining spatial location or restricted to specific regions (e.g., cortical layers L1-L6, hepatic lobule zones) rather than merely mapping cells. Before a spatially aware embedding exists — STEM's SDG identification requires the trained model's adjacency-embedding-gene pathfinding, so plain differential expression on non-spatial SC data is the wrong substitute When the goal is deconvolving spot composition into fixed cell-type fractions rather than linking SC and ST at single-cell resolution — the article notes deconvolution cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify genes whose expression is spatially restricted to specific tissue regions by following STEM's spatial adjacency-embedding-gene pathfinding to extract spatially dominant genes (SDGs), and validate region-specificity against known layer/region marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Identify genes whose expression is spatially restricted to specific tissue regions by following STEM's spatial adjacency-embedding-gene pathfinding to extract spatially dominant genes (SDGs), and validate region-specificity against known layer/region marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Before a spatially aware embedding exists — STEM's SDG identification requires the trained model's adjacency-embedding-gene pathfinding, so plain differential expression on non-spatial SC data is the wrong substitute When the goal is deconvolving spot composition into fixed cell-type fractions rather than linking SC and ST at single-cell resolution — the article notes deconvolution cannot link SC and ST at the single-cell level

skills.description: Use when you need to determine whether specific focal or arm-level CNV events (e.g., an oncogene amplicon or a chromosome arm deletion) are recovered by CaSpER at particular expression smoothing scales in bulk or single-cell RNA-seq.
skills.name: region-targeted-cnv-call-extraction
skills.search_text: region-targeted-cnv-call-extraction Use when you need to determine whether specific focal or arm-level CNV events (e.g., an oncogene amplicon or a chromosome arm deletion) are recovered by CaSpER at particular expression smoothing scales in bulk or single-cell RNA-seq. When the goal is a genome-wide unsupervised CNV catalog rather than interrogation of predefined target regions — use full CaSpER summarization (extractSegmentSummary, extractLargeScaleEvents) instead When only DNA-seq (e.g., SNV array or WGS) data are available and no RNA-seq expression or BAF shift signal exists, since CaSpER relies on RNA-seq expression and BAF profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extracts gene-level and segment-level CNV calls from CaSpER per-scale final.objects for specific genomic regions (e.g., PDGFRA at 4q12, chromosome 22q arm), tabulating how each expression smoothing scale and BAF scale pairwise comparison classifies each region as amp/del/neutral. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Extracts gene-level and segment-level CNV calls from CaSpER per-scale final.objects for specific genomic regions (e.g., PDGFRA at 4q12, chromosome 22q arm), tabulating how each expression smoothing scale and BAF scale pairwise comparison classifies each region as amp/del/neutral.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a genome-wide unsupervised CNV catalog rather than interrogation of predefined target regions — use full CaSpER summarization (extractSegmentSummary, extractLargeScaleEvents) instead When only DNA-seq (e.g., SNV array or WGS) data are available and no RNA-seq expression or BAF shift signal exists, since CaSpER relies on RNA-seq expression and BAF profiles

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics spot-level module scores (e.g., AUCell scores per Visium spot) need testing for regional specificity across annotated anatomical subregions or correlation with spatially mapped phenotypes such as plaque burden or age.
skills.name: regional-specificity-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: regional-specificity-statistical-testing Use when spatial transcriptomics spot-level module scores (e.g., AUCell scores per Visium spot) need testing for regional specificity across annotated anatomical subregions or correlation with spatially mapped phenotypes such as plaque burden or age. The GRN has not yet been built and leiden-partitioned into modules (SCING BuildNetwork and leiden partitioning must precede AUCell scoring and testing) Spot-level spatial annotations or phenotype measures (e.g., plaque staining) are unavailable, since regional specificity and correlation tests require them Single-cell (non-spatial) data with no anatomical region or spatial phenotype annotations, where regional specificity testing is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Statistically tests whether SCING GRN module expression scores differ across annotated brain subregions and whether they correlate with phenotypes (amyloid beta plaque burden, age) in mouse AD Visium spatial transcriptomics, using t-tests/ANOVA plus Pearson correlations against permutation nulls with Bonferroni correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Statistically tests whether SCING GRN module expression scores differ across annotated brain subregions and whether they correlate with phenotypes (amyloid beta plaque burden, age) in mouse AD Visium spatial transcriptomics, using t-tests/ANOVA plus Pearson correlations against permutation nulls with Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GRN has not yet been built and leiden-partitioned into modules (SCING BuildNetwork and leiden partitioning must precede AUCell scoring and testing) Spot-level spatial annotations or phenotype measures (e.g., plaque staining) are unavailable, since regional specificity and correlation tests require them Single-cell (non-spatial) data with no anatomical region or spatial phenotype annotations, where regional specificity testing is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have DNase-seq (or other genome-wide regulatory) measurements and matched gene expression matrices for tens of cell types and need cell-type-general predictive models of regulatory element activity.
skills.name: regression-model-training-on-multi-cell-type-genomic-data
skills.search_text: regression-model-training-on-multi-cell-type-genomic-data Use when you have DNase-seq (or other genome-wide regulatory) measurements and matched gene expression matrices for tens of cell types and need cell-type-general predictive models of regulatory element activity. You need to discover new DHS locations in a new sample — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs, it only predicts within loci present in the model The response and predictors are low-dimensional — big data regression with cluster-level models is designed for ultra-high-dimensional predictors (transcriptome) and responses (regulome) Gene expression platform differs from all available training models and no matched training data exist to build a new model http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train big-data regression models (BIRD) that predict genome-wide DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) from whole-transcriptome gene expression across many cell types, using ENCODE DNase-seq and exon array/RNA-seq training matrices and evaluating on held-out cell types via cross-locus (rL) and cross-cell-type (rC) correlations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-01188-x
skills.summary: Train big-data regression models (BIRD) that predict genome-wide DNase I hypersensitivity (DH) from whole-transcriptome gene expression across many cell types, using ENCODE DNase-seq and exon array/RNA-seq training matrices and evaluating on held-out cell types via cross-locus (rL) and cross-cell-type (rC) correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to discover new DHS locations in a new sample — BIRD will not discover new locations of DHSs, it only predicts within loci present in the model The response and predictors are low-dimensional — big data regression with cluster-level models is designed for ultra-high-dimensional predictors (transcriptome) and responses (regulome) Gene expression platform differs from all available training models and no matched training data exist to build a new model

skills.description: Use when per-gene CTMM results (cell type-specificity and mean-difference measures) must be compared against gene-level annotations such as enhancer domain score, enhancer count, LOEUF, or pLI to ask whether interindividual variance tracks genome features differently than mean-based cell.
skills.name: regression-statistics-table-reporting
skills.search_text: regression-statistics-table-reporting Use when per-gene CTMM results (cell type-specificity and mean-difference measures) must be compared against gene-level annotations such as enhancer domain score, enhancer count, LOEUF, or pLI to ask whether interindividual variance tracks genome features differently than mean-based cell. The goal is to fit the CTMM mixed model itself or generate pseudobulk (OP/CTP) inputs — this skill only consumes per-gene CTMM output; use the ctmm package (op/ctp modules) instead Gene-level annotations such as LOEUF or EDS are unavailable, since all four annotations must be decile-binned for the regression design You need per-gene resolution rather than decile-level summaries — the 10-bin aggregation discards within-decile variation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Method for relating per-gene CTMM cell type-specificity and cell type mean-difference measures to genome-structure/conservation annotations (EDS, enhancer count, LOEUF, pLI) by decile binning genes and fitting per-decile OLS regressions, then reporting coefficients, standard errors, and p-values as a TSV summary table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Method for relating per-gene CTMM cell type-specificity and cell type mean-difference measures to genome-structure/conservation annotations (EDS, enhancer count, LOEUF, pLI) by decile binning genes and fitting per-decile OLS regressions, then reporting coefficients, standard errors, and p-values as a TSV summary table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to fit the CTMM mixed model itself or generate pseudobulk (OP/CTP) inputs — this skill only consumes per-gene CTMM output; use the ctmm package (op/ctp modules) instead Gene-level annotations such as LOEUF or EDS are unavailable, since all four annotations must be decile-binned for the regression design You need per-gene resolution rather than decile-level summaries — the 10-bin aggregation discards within-decile variation

skills.description: Use when you must attribute performance contributions of individual regularization penalties in a regularized regression model, or determine how the network regularization parameter η affects enrichment performance under varying noise conditions.
skills.name: regularization-parameter-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: regularization-parameter-sweep-analysis Use when you must attribute performance contributions of individual regularization penalties in a regularized regression model, or determine how the network regularization parameter η affects enrichment performance under varying noise conditions. The goal is a single biological enrichment analysis on real differential expression data rather than a controlled ablation of regularization terms — use a plain pareg fit instead. No ground-truth active pathways (true positives) are available, so precision-recall AUC cannot be computed against known positives. The model under study does not expose distinct regularization terms (e.g. an unregularized ORA/GSEA method) that could be toggled independently. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Systematically sweeps pareg's regularization configurations (none, LASSO-only, network-only, network+LASSO) and the network regularization parameter η over a grid (e.g. 0.25 and 0.75), scoring each fit by precision-recall AUC against known active pathways to quantify how each penalty term contributes to performance at different noise levels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: Systematically sweeps pareg's regularization configurations (none, LASSO-only, network-only, network+LASSO) and the network regularization parameter η over a grid (e.g. 0.25 and 0.75), scoring each fit by precision-recall AUC against known active pathways to quantify how each penalty term contributes to performance at different noise levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single biological enrichment analysis on real differential expression data rather than a controlled ablation of regularization terms — use a plain pareg fit instead. No ground-truth active pathways (true positives) are available, so precision-recall AUC cannot be computed against known positives. The model under study does not expose distinct regularization terms (e.g. an unregularized ORA/GSEA method) that could be toggled independently.

skills.description: Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available and the goal is to test whether a bulk population's signalling entropy is significantly higher than expected from its constituent single cells.
skills.name: regulated-heterogeneity-z-score-computation
skills.search_text: regulated-heterogeneity-z-score-computation Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available and the goal is to test whether a bulk population's signalling entropy is significantly higher than expected from its constituent single cells. No matched single-cell data exist for the bulk sample, so no single-cell SR reference distribution can be built The goal is ordering cells in pseudo-time or ranking differentiation potency of individual cells rather than testing bulk-vs-single-cell entropy deviation Genes cannot be mapped onto the interaction network required by SCENT's entropy computation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes a measure of regulated heterogeneity (MRH) z-score by standardizing the signalling entropy (SR) of a matched bulk RNA-Seq sample against the single-cell SCENT SR distribution, testing whether bulk entropy exceeds what one random single cell would give — evidence of regulated single-cell expression heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Computes a measure of regulated heterogeneity (MRH) z-score by standardizing the signalling entropy (SR) of a matched bulk RNA-Seq sample against the single-cell SCENT SR distribution, testing whether bulk entropy exceeds what one random single cell would give — evidence of regulated single-cell expression heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched single-cell data exist for the bulk sample, so no single-cell SR reference distribution can be built The goal is ordering cells in pseudo-time or ranking differentiation potency of individual cells rather than testing bulk-vs-single-cell entropy deviation Genes cannot be mapped onto the interaction network required by SCENT's entropy computation

skills.description: Use when a count table or expression matrix must be summarized into per-regulator (TF/kinase) activity scores via signed, weighted prior-knowledge networks, or when multiple inference methods must be combined into a consensus.
skills.name: regulator-activity-inference
skills.search_text: regulator-activity-inference Use when a count table or expression matrix must be summarized into per-regulator (TF/kinase) activity scores via signed, weighted prior-knowledge networks, or when multiple inference methods must be combined into a consensus. The task is pathway enrichment scoring unrelated to signed regulator activities over a prior-knowledge network. No prior-knowledge resource is available or the resource lacks mode-of-regulation/interaction weights that the decoupleR methods require. Only a single method's output is needed and no benchmarking, consensus aggregation, or robustness analysis is in scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer transcription factor and kinase regulatory activities from omics data using decoupleR's ensemble of statistical methods (e.g. ULM, MLV, consensus scoring) applied over prior-knowledge networks such as DoRothEA and OmniPath. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Infer transcription factor and kinase regulatory activities from omics data using decoupleR's ensemble of statistical methods (e.g. ULM, MLV, consensus scoring) applied over prior-knowledge networks such as DoRothEA and OmniPath.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is pathway enrichment scoring unrelated to signed regulator activities over a prior-knowledge network. No prior-knowledge resource is available or the resource lacks mode-of-regulation/interaction weights that the decoupleR methods require. Only a single method's output is needed and no benchmarking, consensus aggregation, or robustness analysis is in scope.

skills.description: Use when you have activity score matrices (regulators × methods) from decoupleRBench runs and need to reproduce manuscript-level agreement statistics such as median Spearman correlations, Jaccard overlap, or Wilcoxon weight tests.
skills.name: regulator-activity-score-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: regulator-activity-score-matrix-analysis Use when you have activity score matrices (regulators × methods) from decoupleRBench runs and need to reproduce manuscript-level agreement statistics such as median Spearman correlations, Jaccard overlap, or Wilcoxon weight tests. Input is raw count tables or metadata rather than already-inferred activity score matrices — build those first with decoupleRBench (run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R). You need AUROC/AUPRC benchmark evaluation itself rather than post-hoc agreement or weights comparisons — use the decoupleRBench evaluation pipeline with its downsampling strategy instead. The goal is to evaluate a new method's predictive performance rather than characterize agreement among the 11 existing decoupleR methods. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Analyze per-method regulator activity score matrices produced by decoupleR perturbation benchmarks (transcriptomics and phospho-proteomics) to quantify cross-method agreement and weighted vs. unweighted mode-of-regulation effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Analyze per-method regulator activity score matrices produced by decoupleR perturbation benchmarks (transcriptomics and phospho-proteomics) to quantify cross-method agreement and weighted vs. unweighted mode-of-regulation effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count tables or metadata rather than already-inferred activity score matrices — build those first with decoupleRBench (run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R). You need AUROC/AUPRC benchmark evaluation itself rather than post-hoc agreement or weights comparisons — use the decoupleRBench evaluation pipeline with its downsampling strategy instead. The goal is to evaluate a new method's predictive performance rather than characterize agreement among the 11 existing decoupleR methods.

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq and regulatory omics count matrices plus a ground-truth regulator–gene interaction list and need to quantify how strongly each modelled interaction manifests as a correlation.
skills.name: regulator-gene-lagged-correlation-computation
skills.search_text: regulator-gene-lagged-correlation-computation Use when you have bulk RNA-seq and regulatory omics count matrices plus a ground-truth regulator–gene interaction list and need to quantify how strongly each modelled interaction manifests as a correlation. Data are single-cell — the article specifies Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell gene-regulator validation rather than lagged Pearson's correlations Interactions were not simulated and no ground-truth regulator–gene list exists — the null random-pair background and class labels cannot be constructed Goal is validating temporal/co-expression patterns of gene profiles — the article instead uses k-means clustering of simulated feature profiles for that purpose http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-pair correlations between regulator features (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks) and target genes on simulated or real bulk multi-omics counts, including lagged correlations up to lag 2, to validate that modelled activator/repressor interactions are detectable. Serves as the ground-truth validation step for regulatory interactions generated by the bulk MOSim simulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Compute per-pair correlations between regulator features (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks) and target genes on simulated or real bulk multi-omics counts, including lagged correlations up to lag 2, to validate that modelled activator/repressor interactions are detectable. Serves as the ground-truth validation step for regulatory interactions generated by the bulk MOSim simulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell — the article specifies Kendall's Tb correlation for single-cell gene-regulator validation rather than lagged Pearson's correlations Interactions were not simulated and no ground-truth regulator–gene list exists — the null random-pair background and class labels cannot be constructed Goal is validating temporal/co-expression patterns of gene profiles — the article instead uses k-means clustering of simulated feature profiles for that purpose

skills.description: Use when preparing SINGE inputs for pseudotemporal single-cell expression data and only a subset of genes (e.g., transcription factors) should be considered as candidate regulators rather than all genes in gene_list.mat.
skills.name: regulator-list-construction-in-mat-files
skills.search_text: regulator-list-construction-in-mat-files Use when preparing SINGE inputs for pseudotemporal single-cell expression data and only a subset of genes (e.g., transcription factors) should be considered as candidate regulators rather than all genes in gene_list.mat. The analysis goal is to infer edges from every gene as a potential regulator — omitting regix lets SINGE search the full gene list The expression data are not ordered by pseudotime (no ptime array), since SINGE requires pseudotemporal ordering for Granger regression Regulator identities cannot be justified (e.g., no known transcription factor list), as an arbitrary subset will bias the ranked interaction list http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a candidate regulator subset for SINGE by earmarking a subset of the gene list as regulators and passing their row indices as the optional regix array inside the input .mat file, restricting network inference to regulator-target edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Constructs a candidate regulator subset for SINGE by earmarking a subset of the gene list as regulators and passing their row indices as the optional regix array inside the input .mat file, restricting network inference to regulator-target edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is to infer edges from every gene as a potential regulator — omitting regix lets SINGE search the full gene list The expression data are not ordered by pseudotime (no ptime array), since SINGE requires pseudotemporal ordering for Granger regression Regulator identities cannot be justified (e.g., no known transcription factor list), as an arbitrary subset will bias the ranked interaction list

skills.description: Use when evaluating which activity-inference methods recover perturbed regulators from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when reproducing the decoupleR phospho-proteomics method ranking.
skills.name: regulator-recovery-sensitivity-evaluation
skills.search_text: regulator-recovery-sensitivity-evaluation Use when evaluating which activity-inference methods recover perturbed regulators from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when reproducing the decoupleR phospho-proteomics method ranking. The goal is transcriptomic (RNA) perturbation benchmarking — run Rscript R/process/run_rna_bench.R instead of the phospho-proteomics benchmark The task is the noise or scalability analysis rather than the main perturbation benchmark (run_php_noise.R / get_simmulated_data.R are separate scripts) Input is single-dataset activity inference without perturbation ground truth — there is no response vector to compute AUROC/AUPRC against http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark procedure that ranks decoupleR statistical methods by their ability to recover perturbed regulators (kinases) from phospho-proteomics perturbation experiments, using decoupleRBench with sensitivity-focused evaluation. Reproduces the paper's finding that consensus, multivariate linear model (mlm) and ULM are the top three methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Benchmark procedure that ranks decoupleR statistical methods by their ability to recover perturbed regulators (kinases) from phospho-proteomics perturbation experiments, using decoupleRBench with sensitivity-focused evaluation. Reproduces the paper's finding that consensus, multivariate linear model (mlm) and ULM are the top three methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is transcriptomic (RNA) perturbation benchmarking — run Rscript R/process/run_rna_bench.R instead of the phospho-proteomics benchmark The task is the noise or scalability analysis rather than the main perturbation benchmark (run_php_noise.R / get_simmulated_data.R are separate scripts) Input is single-dataset activity inference without perturbation ground truth — there is no response vector to compute AUROC/AUPRC against

skills.description: Use when overall precision-recall evaluation of a GRN method looks acceptable and you need to check whether performance is uneven across individual regulators, using a gold standard with per-regulator target sets.
skills.name: regulator-specific-prediction-evaluation
skills.search_text: regulator-specific-prediction-evaluation Use when overall precision-recall evaluation of a GRN method looks acceptable and you need to check whether performance is uneven across individual regulators, using a gold standard with per-regulator target sets. You only need an overall precision-recall comparison of GRN methods and are not concerned with per-regulator variability The gold standard does not identify individual regulators and their target genes, so outgoing edge counts per regulator cannot be computed You have raw expression data and have not yet run the full SINGE pipeline (SINGE GLG then SINGE Aggregate) to obtain ranked edges http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A regulator-specific evaluation that disaggregates GRN inference precision-recall performance by individual regulator. It sorts evaluated regulators (e.g., the 12 ESCAPE gold-standard regulators) by their outgoing gold-standard edge count and plots per-regulator distributions of predicted edge ranks to expose poor per-regulator performance hidden by overall metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: A regulator-specific evaluation that disaggregates GRN inference precision-recall performance by individual regulator. It sorts evaluated regulators (e.g., the 12 ESCAPE gold-standard regulators) by their outgoing gold-standard edge count and plots per-regulator distributions of predicted edge ranks to expose poor per-regulator performance hidden by overall metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need an overall precision-recall comparison of GRN methods and are not concerned with per-regulator variability The gold standard does not identify individual regulators and their target genes, so outgoing edge counts per regulator cannot be computed You have raw expression data and have not yet run the full SINGE pipeline (SINGE GLG then SINGE Aggregate) to obtain ranked edges

skills.description: Use when single-cell trajectory progressions and a reconstructed GRN edge list are available and you need to identify transcriptional regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions at the network level.
skills.name: regulator-target-interaction-analysis
skills.search_text: regulator-target-interaction-analysis Use when single-cell trajectory progressions and a reconstructed GRN edge list are available and you need to identify transcriptional regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions at the network level. The analysis goal is trajectory reconstruction itself (subpopulation identification, flow-network paths) rather than scoring regulators — CellRouter's trajectory and GRN-scoring steps are separate workflow stages No reconstructed gene regulatory network exists for the dataset; the score requires predicted target genes per regulator, not expression data alone The goal is general single-cell analysis with diffusion pseudotime (e.g. the theislab/scAnalysisTutorial approach), which does not use GRN-based regulator scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CellRouter's GRN score ranks transcriptional regulators of cell-state transitions by combining each regulator's activation status (Spearman correlation with trajectory progression), the mean correlation of its predicted target genes, and its number of regulated targets in a reconstructed gene regulatory network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: CellRouter's GRN score ranks transcriptional regulators of cell-state transitions by combining each regulator's activation status (Spearman correlation with trajectory progression), the mean correlation of its predicted target genes, and its number of regulated targets in a reconstructed gene regulatory network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is trajectory reconstruction itself (subpopulation identification, flow-network paths) rather than scoring regulators — CellRouter's trajectory and GRN-scoring steps are separate workflow stages No reconstructed gene regulatory network exists for the dataset; the score requires predicted target genes per regulator, not expression data alone The goal is general single-cell analysis with diffusion pseudotime (e.g. the theislab/scAnalysisTutorial approach), which does not use GRN-based regulator scoring

skills.description: Use when simulating bulk multi-omics regulatory layers with MOSim and you must decide how a regulator's simulated count/time profile relates to the expression pattern of its assigned target genes.
skills.name: regulator-target-profile-matching
skills.search_text: regulator-target-profile-matching Use when simulating bulk multi-omics regulatory layers with MOSim and you must decide how a regulator's simulated count/time profile relates to the expression pattern of its assigned target genes. The input is real experimental regulator data (e.g., measured ChIP-seq or Methyl-seq counts) rather than a simulation task — this skill only constructs synthetic regulator profiles coupled to simulated gene expression. Simulating single-cell data with sc_mosim, where regulatory layers are restricted to scATAC-seq and TFs and count generation relies on SPARSim single-cell functionality rather than the bulk activator/repressor mirroring mechanism. Modeling omics layers like proteomics or metabolomics, which the paper explicitly does not cover. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 In MOSim's bulk simulation workflow, regulatory omics layers (ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, miRNA-seq, Methyl-seq, TFs) receive count profiles derived from the genes they regulate: activator regulators mirror the temporal DEG profile of their targets, while repressors follow the opposite pattern, coupling regulator abundance to gene expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: In MOSim's bulk simulation workflow, regulatory omics layers (ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, miRNA-seq, Methyl-seq, TFs) receive count profiles derived from the genes they regulate: activator regulators mirror the temporal DEG profile of their targets, while repressors follow the opposite pattern, coupling regulator abundance to gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real experimental regulator data (e.g., measured ChIP-seq or Methyl-seq counts) rather than a simulation task — this skill only constructs synthetic regulator profiles coupled to simulated gene expression. Simulating single-cell data with sc_mosim, where regulatory layers are restricted to scATAC-seq and TFs and count generation relies on SPARSim single-cell functionality rather than the bulk activator/repressor mirroring mechanism. Modeling omics layers like proteomics or metabolomics, which the paper explicitly does not cover.

skills.description: Use when you have BoostDiff output from two conditions (e.g., salt-stress target vs. SMM baseline) and need to rank regulator-to-target edges by aggregating weighted DVI across the boosted differential trees into a VIM table.
skills.name: regulator-variable-importance-ranking
skills.search_text: regulator-variable-importance-ranking Use when you have BoostDiff output from two conditions (e.g., salt-stress target vs. SMM baseline) and need to rank regulator-to-target edges by aggregating weighted DVI across the boosted differential trees into a VIM table. The two expression matrices do not share the same set of features, or data comes from a single condition — BoostDiff's differential trees require two conditions compared simultaneously with the first column named 'Gene'. The goal is differential expression per gene rather than ranking regulatory context; BoostDiff complements standard differential expression analyses but does not replace them. Dataset scale matches the Crohn's disease dataset (GSE126124), which the authors state is too large for a single machine and needs a high-performance computing cluster. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Rank candidate regulators of each target gene by aggregating BoostDiff's differential variance improvement (DVI) across its 50-tree modified AdaBoost ensemble into per-target-gene variable importance (VIM) scores. These weighted importances are what turn the boosted differential trees into the final differential gene regulatory network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Rank candidate regulators of each target gene by aggregating BoostDiff's differential variance improvement (DVI) across its 50-tree modified AdaBoost ensemble into per-target-gene variable importance (VIM) scores. These weighted importances are what turn the boosted differential trees into the final differential gene regulatory network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two expression matrices do not share the same set of features, or data comes from a single condition — BoostDiff's differential trees require two conditions compared simultaneously with the first column named 'Gene'. The goal is differential expression per gene rather than ranking regulatory context; BoostDiff complements standard differential expression analyses but does not replace them. Dataset scale matches the Crohn's disease dataset (GSE126124), which the authors state is too large for a single machine and needs a high-performance computing cluster.

skills.description: Use when you have fine-mapped credible-set variants (e.g., CAFEH pip/alpha per SNP) and want to test whether they are enriched in active promoters/enhancers relative to a matched background, as in Figure 3D.
skills.name: regulatory-element-annotation-overlap
skills.search_text: regulatory-element-annotation-overlap Use when you have fine-mapped credible-set variants (e.g., CAFEH pip/alpha per SNP) and want to test whether they are enriched in active promoters/enhancers relative to a matched background, as in Figure 3D. Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants may not show eQTL effects and cannot be assessed with this eQTL-based regulatory overlap approach When studies have large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences), fine-mapped credible sets may be unreliable before annotation overlap is meaningful Colocalization does not necessarily suggest mediation — do not interpret regulatory enrichment alone as proof of a causal variant-to-gene pathway (horizontal pleiotropy is possible) http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Assess whether fine-mapped eQTL causal variants are functionally plausible by intersecting CAFEH credible-set variants with Roadmap Epigenomics chromHMM active regulatory elements and testing enrichment against a matched lead-eQTL background using Fisher's exact test per tissue. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Assess whether fine-mapped eQTL causal variants are functionally plausible by intersecting CAFEH credible-set variants with Roadmap Epigenomics chromHMM active regulatory elements and testing enrichment against a matched lead-eQTL background using Fisher's exact test per tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants may not show eQTL effects and cannot be assessed with this eQTL-based regulatory overlap approach When studies have large LD differences (e.g., ancestry differences), fine-mapped credible sets may be unreliable before annotation overlap is meaningful Colocalization does not necessarily suggest mediation — do not interpret regulatory enrichment alone as proof of a causal variant-to-gene pathway (horizontal pleiotropy is possible)

skills.description: Use when you have bootstrapped COSLIR coefficient matrices plus first-moment vectors (mu1, mu2) from two consecutive time points and need to rank directed gene-gregulatory interactions by influence.
skills.name: regulatory-interaction-rescaling
skills.search_text: regulatory-interaction-rescaling Use when you have bootstrapped COSLIR coefficient matrices plus first-moment vectors (mu1, mu2) from two consecutive time points and need to rank directed gene-gregulatory interactions by influence. You need GRNs that maintain a single cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition — COSLIR targets sparse transition-driving networks from TSCS data Only a single time point / cell stage is available, so no consecutive-stage means (mu1, mu2) exist to compute the denominator |(mu1)_i − (mu2)_i| Expression values are not summarized as first and second moments per time point (e.g., raw unaggregated counts without time stamps) http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Rescales each bootstrapped COSLIR regression coefficient (edge weight) by the target gene's mean abundance and the regulator's absolute mean change across a two-stage transition — (A~)_ij = (|Â|)_ij · |μ̂_1|_j / |(μ̂_1)_i − (μ̂_2)_i| — so influential directed regulatory interactions can be ranked for early-precision evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Rescales each bootstrapped COSLIR regression coefficient (edge weight) by the target gene's mean abundance and the regulator's absolute mean change across a two-stage transition — (A~)_ij = (|Â|)_ij · |μ̂_1|_j / |(μ̂_1)_i − (μ̂_2)_i| — so influential directed regulatory interactions can be ranked for early-precision evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need GRNs that maintain a single cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition — COSLIR targets sparse transition-driving networks from TSCS data Only a single time point / cell stage is available, so no consecutive-stage means (mu1, mu2) exist to compute the denominator |(mu1)_i − (mu2)_i| Expression values are not summarized as first and second moments per time point (e.g., raw unaggregated counts without time stamps)

skills.description: Use when you need to test robustness of scKINETICS velocity/network outputs by sweeping sigma over an initiating grid or perturbing nonzero A^ coexpression-prior elements with Gaussian noise while holding all other inputs fixed.
skills.name: regulatory-network-em-refitting
skills.search_text: regulatory-network-em-refitting Use when you need to test robustness of scKINETICS velocity/network outputs by sweeping sigma over an initiating grid or perturbing nonzero A^ coexpression-prior elements with Gaussian noise while holding all other inputs fixed. You are fitting scKINETICS for the first time to derive velocities/networks rather than stress-testing an existing reference fit You are benchmarking scKINETICS against other velocity methods rather than assessing its internal robustness to sigma and prior perturbation No epigenetic/coexpression priors or manifold constraint are defined, so there is no A^ to perturb and no sigma to sweep Refits the scKINETICS expectation-maximization model across perturbations — sweeping the manifold-constraint width sigma and adding Gaussian noise to the coexpression prior A^ — to quantify how sensitive inferred per-cell velocities and the governing gene regulatory network are to prior/parameter choices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Refits the scKINETICS expectation-maximization model across perturbations — sweeping the manifold-constraint width sigma and adding Gaussian noise to the coexpression prior A^ — to quantify how sensitive inferred per-cell velocities and the governing gene regulatory network are to prior/parameter choices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are fitting scKINETICS for the first time to derive velocities/networks rather than stress-testing an existing reference fit You are benchmarking scKINETICS against other velocity methods rather than assessing its internal robustness to sigma and prior perturbation No epigenetic/coexpression priors or manifold constraint are defined, so there is no A^ to perturb and no sigma to sweep

skills.description: Use when a fitted GRN matrix A (e.g. from scKINETICS EM fitting) must be validated for recovery accuracy by simulating noisy expression trajectories from random start cells and refitting the model.
skills.name: regulatory-network-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: regulatory-network-trajectory-simulation Use when a fitted GRN matrix A (e.g. from scKINETICS EM fitting) must be validated for recovery accuracy by simulating noisy expression trajectories from random start cells and refitting the model. Input is real single-cell expression data with no ground-truth network — there is no true A to correlate against, so recovery accuracy cannot be assessed The goal is to fit a GRN on real data rather than to benchmark recovery of an already-fitted A matrix The underlying dynamics are strongly nonlinear and cannot be approximated by the linear model x(t)=e^{At}x(0) used in this benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates an inferred gene regulatory network by propagating simulated expression states through the fitted linear dynamics x(t)=e^{At}x(0) with added Gaussian noise, refitting the model, and measuring recovery of the true A matrix — the simulation-based benchmark used by scKINETICS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Validates an inferred gene regulatory network by propagating simulated expression states through the fitted linear dynamics x(t)=e^{At}x(0) with added Gaussian noise, refitting the model, and measuring recovery of the true A matrix — the simulation-based benchmark used by scKINETICS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real single-cell expression data with no ground-truth network — there is no true A to correlate against, so recovery accuracy cannot be assessed The goal is to fit a GRN on real data rather than to benchmark recovery of an already-fitted A matrix The underlying dynamics are strongly nonlinear and cannot be approximated by the linear model x(t)=e^{At}x(0) used in this benchmark

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch single-cell multimodal (RNA+ATAC) dataset is being used to infer regulatory potential and TF motif enrichments, and technical/batch effects may confound motif-gene associations you want to compare between corrected and uncorrected models.
skills.name: regulatory-potential-model-technical-effect-augmentation
skills.search_text: regulatory-potential-model-technical-effect-augmentation Use when a multi-batch single-cell multimodal (RNA+ATAC) dataset is being used to infer regulatory potential and TF motif enrichments, and technical/batch effects may confound motif-gene associations you want to compare between corrected and uncorrected models. Data are unimodal or lack scATAC-seq accessibility peaks, so no regulatory potential model over accessible peaks near TSS-annotated genes can be trained. Data come from a single batch with no technical-effect structure, so fixing CODAL technical effects as a non-trainable component is unnecessary. The question is generic batch correction of embeddings rather than testing whether technical-effect disentanglement changes downstream regulatory/motif inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains MIRA regulatory potential models on multimodal single-cell data with CODAL technical effects fixed as an additive, non-trainable component of the negative binomial generative distribution, then uses probabilistic in silico deletion over JASPAR PWMs to test whether batch-effect disentanglement changes detected TF motif enrichments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Trains MIRA regulatory potential models on multimodal single-cell data with CODAL technical effects fixed as an additive, non-trainable component of the negative binomial generative distribution, then uses probabilistic in silico deletion over JASPAR PWMs to test whether batch-effect disentanglement changes detected TF motif enrichments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unimodal or lack scATAC-seq accessibility peaks, so no regulatory potential model over accessible peaks near TSS-annotated genes can be trained. Data come from a single batch with no technical-effect structure, so fixing CODAL technical effects as a non-trainable component is unnecessary. The question is generic batch correction of embeddings rather than testing whether technical-effect disentanglement changes downstream regulatory/motif inference.

skills.description: Use when you have an annotated plant (e.g., Arabidopsis TAIR10) scRNA-seq Seurat object and need to infer cell-type-specific regulons/GRNs and identify top regulon TFs per cluster.
skills.name: regulon-activity-score-computation-aucell
skills.search_text: regulon-activity-score-computation-aucell Use when you have an annotated plant (e.g., Arabidopsis TAIR10) scRNA-seq Seurat object and need to infer cell-type-specific regulons/GRNs and identify top regulon TFs per cluster. The organism has no precomputed cisTarget database and no genome/gff3 available to build one (though custom databases can be built via aertslab/create_cisTarget_databases) The goal is bulk deconvolution, trajectory inference, or cross-species integration rather than GRN/regulon inference — use scPlant's decomposeBulk, RunMonocle2/3, RunSlingshot or crossSpecies_integrate instead Input is raw unprocessed counts without prior QC/clustering/annotation — run scPlant's readData, QCfun and RunSeurat first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Compute cell-type-specific regulon activity scores from an annotated plant single-cell atlas using pySCENIC's AUCell within the scPlant pipeline, ranking regulon TFs (e.g., RSS-based) per cell cluster to recover cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Compute cell-type-specific regulon activity scores from an annotated plant single-cell atlas using pySCENIC's AUCell within the scPlant pipeline, ranking regulon TFs (e.g., RSS-based) per cell cluster to recover cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has no precomputed cisTarget database and no genome/gff3 available to build one (though custom databases can be built via aertslab/create_cisTarget_databases) The goal is bulk deconvolution, trajectory inference, or cross-species integration rather than GRN/regulon inference — use scPlant's decomposeBulk, RunMonocle2/3, RunSlingshot or crossSpecies_integrate instead Input is raw unprocessed counts without prior QC/clustering/annotation — run scPlant's readData, QCfun and RunSeurat first

skills.description: Use when MINI-EX or SCENIC regulons have been inferred on a plant single-cell atlas and you need to rank top regulons per cluster, render enrichment heatmaps, and quantify cross-tool regulon consistency.
skills.name: regulon-enrichment-visualization
skills.search_text: regulon-enrichment-visualization Use when MINI-EX or SCENIC regulons have been inferred on a plant single-cell atlas and you need to rank top regulons per cluster, render enrichment heatmaps, and quantify cross-tool regulon consistency. Input is raw count data that has not been pre-processed with the scPlant auxiliary script (MINIEX_preprocess.R) and no regulons have yet been inferred The organism is not covered by available cisTarget/TF-motif resources — MINI-EX targets scRNA-seq gene regulatory network inference in plants You need a single-tool regulon list without cross-tool validation or enrichment visualization (use topRegulons_MINIEX alone rather than the full comparison workflow) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Visualize and cross-validate cell-type-specific regulons inferred from plant scRNA-seq data by inspecting MINI-EX pipeline results with scPlant functions (enrich_exp_hmp, topRegulons_MINIEX, BordaRank_MINIEX) and quantifying agreement with SCENIC via Jaccard similarity of top regulons per cell cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Visualize and cross-validate cell-type-specific regulons inferred from plant scRNA-seq data by inspecting MINI-EX pipeline results with scPlant functions (enrich_exp_hmp, topRegulons_MINIEX, BordaRank_MINIEX) and quantifying agreement with SCENIC via Jaccard similarity of top regulons per cell cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count data that has not been pre-processed with the scPlant auxiliary script (MINIEX_preprocess.R) and no regulons have yet been inferred The organism is not covered by available cisTarget/TF-motif resources — MINI-EX targets scRNA-seq gene regulatory network inference in plants You need a single-tool regulon list without cross-tool validation or enrichment visualization (use topRegulons_MINIEX alone rather than the full comparison workflow)

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-lineage-specific GRN plus identified driver regulators (e.g., from CEFCON's driver_regulators() step) and need gene modules and per-cell module activity matrices for downstream enrichment or clustering benchmarks.
skills.name: regulon-like-gene-module-detection
skills.search_text: regulon-like-gene-module-detection Use when you have a cell-lineage-specific GRN plus identified driver regulators (e.g., from CEFCON's driver_regulators() step) and need gene modules and per-cell module activity matrices for downstream enrichment or clustering benchmarks. You only have raw scRNA-seq data and no constructed lineage-specific GRN or identified driver regulators — the GRN-construction and driver-regulator steps of CEFCON must run first. You need regulons restricted to transcription factors only and must match the classic SCENIC definition rather than CEFCON's extended non-TF-inclusive modules. Your trajectory contains multiple fate branches with bifurcations, since CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Detect regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) involving driver regulators identified by CEFCON, including non-TF genes and both out-degree and in-degree module types, and score their per-cell activity with AUCell. This extends regulon detection beyond SCENIC-style TF-only regulons to capture more biologically meaningful modules in cell-lineage-specific GRNs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Detect regulon-like gene modules (RGMs) involving driver regulators identified by CEFCON, including non-TF genes and both out-degree and in-degree module types, and score their per-cell activity with AUCell. This extends regulon detection beyond SCENIC-style TF-only regulons to capture more biologically meaningful modules in cell-lineage-specific GRNs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw scRNA-seq data and no constructed lineage-specific GRN or identified driver regulators — the GRN-construction and driver-regulator steps of CEFCON must run first. You need regulons restricted to transcription factors only and must match the classic SCENIC definition rather than CEFCON's extended non-TF-inclusive modules. Your trajectory contains multiple fate branches with bifurcations, since CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time.

skills.description: Use when a differential network (e.g. from BoostDiff on salt/heat/ethanol stress vs. control) needs biological validation: check whether top hub genes belong to a known regulon such as SigB.
skills.name: regulon-membership-validation
skills.search_text: regulon-membership-validation Use when a differential network (e.g. from BoostDiff on salt/heat/ethanol stress vs. control) needs biological validation: check whether top hub genes belong to a known regulon such as SigB. The condition under study has no curated transcription-factor regulon against which hub genes can be checked — the validation relies on prior regulon knowledge and cannot be applied blind. The network is still the raw BoostDiff output before filter_network filtering (p=3, n_top_edges=150) — unfiltered edges include genes where BoostDiff did not find a more predictive model for the target condition, so hub ranking would be misleading. The goal is differential expression testing rather than network-structure validation — standard differential expression analysis is a complementary but distinct check. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates a condition-specific differential network by checking whether its top-ranked hub genes are members of a known transcription-factor regulon (here, the B. subtilis SigB stress-response regulon), turning biological prior knowledge into a correctness signal for network inference methods like BoostDiff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Validates a condition-specific differential network by checking whether its top-ranked hub genes are members of a known transcription-factor regulon (here, the B. subtilis SigB stress-response regulon), turning biological prior knowledge into a correctness signal for network inference methods like BoostDiff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The condition under study has no curated transcription-factor regulon against which hub genes can be checked — the validation relies on prior regulon knowledge and cannot be applied blind. The network is still the raw BoostDiff output before filter_network filtering (p=3, n_top_edges=150) — unfiltered edges include genes where BoostDiff did not find a more predictive model for the target condition, so hub ranking would be misleading. The goal is differential expression testing rather than network-structure validation — standard differential expression analysis is a complementary but distinct check.

skills.description: Use when an inferred GRN (e.g. from Augusta's mutual-information step) needs to be grouped into TF-specific regulons before promoter-based motif discovery, and small regulons must be pruned.
skills.name: regulon-partitioning-from-inferred-grn
skills.search_text: regulon-partitioning-from-inferred-grn Use when an inferred GRN (e.g. from Augusta's mutual-information step) needs to be grouped into TF-specific regulons before promoter-based motif discovery, and small regulons must be pruned. No GenBank-annotated genome is available for the organism, since refinement steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome Only a curated-database-driven refinement is desired (e.g. when running Augusta.GRN_to_BN with add_dbs_info and no motif-based refinement is needed) The GRN is not gene-regulatory (e.g. a protein-protein interaction network), so TF-target regulons cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Partitions Augusta's inferred GRN into per-transcription-factor regulons and filters out TFs with fewer than five target genes, preparing regulons whose promoters can be scanned for de novo TFBMs via MEME Suite. This threshold-based grouping is the first step of the GRN refinement stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Partitions Augusta's inferred GRN into per-transcription-factor regulons and filters out TFs with fewer than five target genes, preparing regulons whose promoters can be scanned for de novo TFBMs via MEME Suite. This threshold-based grouping is the first step of the GRN refinement stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No GenBank-annotated genome is available for the organism, since refinement steps cannot be performed without additional knowledge of a genome Only a curated-database-driven refinement is desired (e.g. when running Augusta.GRN_to_BN with add_dbs_info and no motif-based refinement is needed) The GRN is not gene-regulatory (e.g. a protein-protein interaction network), so TF-target regulons cannot be defined

Your goal is general cell-type annotation or deconvolution rather than gene regulatory network / regulon inference Your organism has no available cisTarget database and you cannot construct one (e.g., no genome/gff3 or motif collection from JASPAR/PlantTFDB) Input is bulk RNA-seq data — scPlant's regulon module targets single-cell atlases; bulk data is handled by other modules such as decomposeBulk http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers and ranks cell-type-specific regulons from plant scRNA-seq data using pySCENIC with species-specific cisTarget databases, then scores regulon specificity per cluster (RAS/RSS) to identify the characteristic regulon TF for a cell type (e.g., PIF5 for photosynthetic cells in the Arabidopsis root atlas). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how a hierarchical classifier rejects cells from unseen populations held out of training, e.g. comparing one-class SVM vs linear SVM rejection fractions across tree nodes.

skills.search_text: rejection-fraction-heatmap-visualization Use when benchmarking how a hierarchical classifier rejects cells from unseen populations held out of training, e.g. comparing one-class SVM vs linear SVM rejection fractions across tree nodes. Datasets are not yet aligned — since scHPL is not a batch correction tool, rejection fractions computed on unaligned data are not interpretable; align first with scVI or scArches All cell populations in the test set are present in the training data, so there are no unseen populations whose rejection behavior needs to be visualized Compiles per-node rejection rates from scHPL's hierarchical classifier into a table and renders a Fig. 3E-style heatmap comparing how the linear SVM and one-class SVM reject cells from unseen (held-out) cell populations such as 'Group 3'. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Compiles per-node rejection rates from scHPL's hierarchical classifier into a table and renders a Fig. 3E-style heatmap comparing how the linear SVM and one-class SVM reject cells from unseen (held-out) cell populations such as 'Group 3'.

skills.description: Use when training a reference-based identifier (MarkerCount_Ref) on a pre-annotated reference dataset whose taxonomy does not cover the test cells, and you need non-parametric per-cell-type thresholds tm on normalized marker counts for unknown-population rejection.
skills.name: rejection-threshold-calibration
skills.search_text: rejection-threshold-calibration Use when training a reference-based identifier (MarkerCount_Ref) on a pre-annotated reference dataset whose taxonomy does not cover the test cells, and you need non-parametric per-cell-type thresholds tm on normalized marker counts for unknown-population rejection. The reference taxonomy already contains the cell types present in the test data (no unknown populations to reject), so rejection thresholds trade off sensitivity without benefit You are running marker-based mode (MarkerCount or HiCAT) with pre-existing marker lists and no pre-annotated reference from which to learn thresholds Cell populations are not well clustered, since cluster-basis reassignment after thresholding relies on within-cluster gene expression similarity http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calibrates MarkerCount's conservative rejection thresholds on normalized marker counts so that cells from populations absent from the reference taxonomy (e.g., tumor cells when training on blood references) are left unassigned (CUA) instead of erroneously assigned, followed by cluster-basis reassignment to limit unnecessarily unassigned cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.06.010
skills.summary: Calibrates MarkerCount's conservative rejection thresholds on normalized marker counts so that cells from populations absent from the reference taxonomy (e.g., tumor cells when training on blood references) are left unassigned (CUA) instead of erroneously assigned, followed by cluster-basis reassignment to limit unnecessarily unassigned cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference taxonomy already contains the cell types present in the test data (no unknown populations to reject), so rejection thresholds trade off sensitivity without benefit You are running marker-based mode (MarkerCount or HiCAT) with pre-existing marker lists and no pre-annotated reference from which to learn thresholds Cell populations are not well clustered, since cluster-basis reassignment after thresholding relies on within-cluster gene expression similarity

skills.description: Use when calibrating the unassigned-cells portion threshold that triggers cluster-basis reassignment in a marker-count-based scRNA-seq cell type identifier, and you need empirical justification for the chosen cutoff.

skills.description: Use when a gene expression matrix (Pandas DataFrame, genes × samples) must be screened for stable endogenous reference genes by replicating ERgene's inverse internal-reference calculation rather than treating the library as a black box.
skills.name: relative-correction-factor-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: relative-correction-factor-matrix-computation Use when a gene expression matrix (Pandas DataFrame, genes × samples) must be screened for stable endogenous reference genes by replicating ERgene's inverse internal-reference calculation rather than treating the library as a black box. The goal is gene expression normalization of data by an already-identified reference gene — use Ergene.Normalizationdata(Data, Ergname) instead of re-deriving the F1/F2 matrices The dataset is very small and shallow reference-gene screening via the ERgene library directly (FindERG) is sufficient, making a reimplementation unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reimplements the inverse-of-internal-reference screening at the core of the ERgene Python library: per-sample relative correction factor matrices F1 and F2 are built, their difference ΔF is computed, and per-gene variance of ΔF ranks candidate endogenous reference genes (top 20 returned). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-75586-5
skills.summary: Reimplements the inverse-of-internal-reference screening at the core of the ERgene Python library: per-sample relative correction factor matrices F1 and F2 are built, their difference ΔF is computed, and per-gene variance of ΔF ranks candidate endogenous reference genes (top 20 returned).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene expression normalization of data by an already-identified reference gene — use Ergene.Normalizationdata(Data, Ergname) instead of re-deriving the F1/F2 matrices The dataset is very small and shallow reference-gene screening via the ERgene library directly (FindERG) is sufficient, making a reimplementation unnecessary

When the goal is a minimal discriminative marker set covering all phenotype pairs rather than a per-feature relevance ranking — use phenotype-cover (G-PC/CEM-PC) instead When features must be evaluated jointly for redundancy (ReliefF scores each feature independently of other selected features) Computes ReliefF neighbor-based per-feature weights on a labeled scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., the MC mouse cortex dataset from Zeisel et al.), using faiss approximate nearest neighbors with k=30 to produce a ranked feature list usable as a baseline marker-selection method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a minimal discriminative marker set covering all phenotype pairs rather than a per-feature relevance ranking — use phenotype-cover (G-PC/CEM-PC) instead When features must be evaluated jointly for redundancy (ReliefF scores each feature independently of other selected features)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple donors has been aggregated into cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP), ctnu, and cell type proportions P, and the goal is to partition interindividual expression variance into cell type-shared (hom2) vs cell type-specific (V) components and test genes for.

Cohorts with fewer than ~50 individuals — 'CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50' Individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells or rare cell types, since CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian even after pseudobulking, where the Gaussian approximation fails http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Models (CTMM) to cell type-specific pseudobulk scRNA-seq data using REML optimization, and run jackknife-based Wald tests to detect genes with cell type-specific interindividual variance (e.g. 2310/11,526 genes in the OneK1K PBMC cohort). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fit Cell Type-specific linear Mixed Models (CTMM) to cell type-specific pseudobulk scRNA-seq data using REML optimization, and run jackknife-based Wald tests to detect genes with cell type-specific interindividual variance (e.g. 2310/11,526 genes in the OneK1K PBMC cohort).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cohorts with fewer than ~50 individuals — 'CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50' Individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells or rare cell types, since CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Lowly-expressed genes that are severely non-Gaussian even after pseudobulking, where the Gaussian approximation fails

Sample size is below ~50 individuals, where the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable Rare cell types with <=10 cells per individual-cell type pair, since CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Genes with very low expression, which are severely non-Gaussian and violate the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fit the CTMM Free model to cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data with restricted maximum likelihood (REML), using jackknife-based Wald tests to detect cell type-specific interindividual variance differentiation (V) and mean expression differentiation (ct_beta) per gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fit the CTMM Free model to cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) scRNA-seq data with restricted maximum likelihood (REML), using jackknife-based Wald tests to detect cell type-specific interindividual variance differentiation (V) and mean expression differentiation (ct_beta) per gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample size is below ~50 individuals, where the Free test is slightly inflated and CTMM is not reliable Rare cell types with <=10 cells per individual-cell type pair, since CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Genes with very low expression, which are severely non-Gaussian and violate the Gaussian pseudobulk approximation

skills.description: Use when you have paired transcriptome-only and ClonoCluster hybrid cluster assignments plus a count matrix, and need genes whose expression predicts cell reassignment (reorganization markers) between cluster pairs for downstream GO enrichment.
skills.name: reorganization-marker-auc-scoring
skills.search_text: reorganization-marker-auc-scoring Use when you have paired transcriptome-only and ClonoCluster hybrid cluster assignments plus a count matrix, and need genes whose expression predicts cell reassignment (reorganization markers) between cluster pairs for downstream GO enrichment. You only have one clustering scheme with no paired transcriptome-only vs hybrid α assignments — use standard cluster marker analysis with Find_Markers_ROC instead No clone barcode data exist, so hybrid clusters cannot be generated and rearrangement between clusterings is undefined The goal is cluster-level marker identification at a single clustering level (covered by *_auc_linclust.txt AUCs), not genes predicting switches between clusterings http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores every gene by reorg-AUC — how well its expression predicts whether a cell switches affiliation from a transcriptome-only cluster to a particular ClonoCluster hybrid α cluster — using the Find_Markers_ROC wrapper around ROCR, then retains genes with reorg-AUC > 0.80 as reorganization markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: Scores every gene by reorg-AUC — how well its expression predicts whether a cell switches affiliation from a transcriptome-only cluster to a particular ClonoCluster hybrid α cluster — using the Find_Markers_ROC wrapper around ROCR, then retains genes with reorg-AUC > 0.80 as reorganization markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have one clustering scheme with no paired transcriptome-only vs hybrid α assignments — use standard cluster marker analysis with Find_Markers_ROC instead No clone barcode data exist, so hybrid clusters cannot be generated and rearrangement between clusterings is undefined The goal is cluster-level marker identification at a single clustering level (covered by *_auc_linclust.txt AUCs), not genes predicting switches between clusterings

Input is raw unfiltered scRNA-seq counts — the re-parameterized Bayesian stage expects the non-negative, filtered representation produced by the first-module kernel autoencoder The goal is only gene/component filtering; insignificant genes or components are removed by the first module's encoder weight distribution, not by latent perturbation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Samples multiple realizations of the latent vector z via the re-parameterization trick inside scDHA's second module (a stacked Bayesian autoencoder built on the VAE), so the compressed 15-dimensional space is repeatedly perturbed to learn a more generalized representation and reduce neural-network overfitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Samples multiple realizations of the latent vector z via the re-parameterization trick inside scDHA's second module (a stacked Bayesian autoencoder built on the VAE), so the compressed 15-dimensional space is repeatedly perturbed to learn a more generalized representation and reduce neural-network overfitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unfiltered scRNA-seq counts — the re-parameterized Bayesian stage expects the non-negative, filtered representation produced by the first-module kernel autoencoder The goal is only gene/component filtering; insignificant genes or components are removed by the first module's encoder weight distribution, not by latent perturbation

skills.description: Use when a stochastic deep-clustering pipeline (e.g., scDCC with random initialization) yields run-to-run variability and you must quantify whether a modification (e.g., adding pairwise constraints) consistently improves a downstream metric such as cluster-specificity scores of marker genes.
skills.name: repeated-clustering-run-aggregation
skills.search_text: repeated-clustering-run-aggregation Use when a stochastic deep-clustering pipeline (e.g., scDCC with random initialization) yields run-to-run variability and you must quantify whether a modification (e.g., adding pairwise constraints) consistently improves a downstream metric such as cluster-specificity scores of marker genes. When the clustering algorithm is deterministic or you only have a single clustering run — the paired across-run aggregation and signed-rank test require multiple independent repeats. When you need to compare more than two conditions (with vs. without constraints) — the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test as applied here is strictly paired and two-condition. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregate stochastic clustering results by running a clustering algorithm (scDCC) repeatedly with and without pairwise constraints, computing per-gene cluster-specificity scores (DESeq2 Wald statistics) per repeat, averaging across repeats, and testing paired differences with a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to determine whether constraints systematically improve marker-gene specificity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3
skills.summary: Aggregate stochastic clustering results by running a clustering algorithm (scDCC) repeatedly with and without pairwise constraints, computing per-gene cluster-specificity scores (DESeq2 Wald statistics) per repeat, averaging across repeats, and testing paired differences with a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test to determine whether constraints systematically improve marker-gene specificity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the clustering algorithm is deterministic or you only have a single clustering run — the paired across-run aggregation and signed-rank test require multiple independent repeats. When you need to compare more than two conditions (with vs. without constraints) — the one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test as applied here is strictly paired and two-condition.

skills.description: Use when a new feature set (e.g. PSG k-mer, position-specific k-mer, GC-content) must be compared against baselines on a labeled sequence dataset, requiring averaged cross-validation metrics and ROC/PR curves rather than a single train/test split.
skills.name: repeated-cross-validation-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: repeated-cross-validation-model-evaluation Use when a new feature set (e.g. PSG k-mer, position-specific k-mer, GC-content) must be compared against baselines on a labeled sequence dataset, requiring averaged cross-validation metrics and ROC/PR curves rather than a single train/test split. The goal is independent-set generalization: the article reports independent-test results (Table 6) separately from cross-validation (Table 5), so use a held-out test evaluation instead. You want to test whether position-specific features combine with k-mer frequency features in one model — the authors note these do not work well together and defer combination to a feature-subspace ensemble approach. Input is a raw sequence file only — feature extraction must first be run (Feature Generation.ipynb) before cross-validation can be executed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A protocol for rigorously benchmarking sequence-based machine learning classifiers (LR, SVM, GNB) by repeated 5-fold cross-validation, as used in iRNA5hmC-PS to report Accuracy, Precision, Sensitivity, Specificity, F1, MCC, AUROC, and AUPR on the RNA 5hmC benchmark dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: A protocol for rigorously benchmarking sequence-based machine learning classifiers (LR, SVM, GNB) by repeated 5-fold cross-validation, as used in iRNA5hmC-PS to report Accuracy, Precision, Sensitivity, Specificity, F1, MCC, AUROC, and AUPR on the RNA 5hmC benchmark dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is independent-set generalization: the article reports independent-test results (Table 6) separately from cross-validation (Table 5), so use a held-out test evaluation instead. You want to test whether position-specific features combine with k-mer frequency features in one model — the authors note these do not work well together and defer combination to a feature-subspace ensemble approach. Input is a raw sequence file only — feature extraction must first be run (Feature Generation.ipynb) before cross-validation can be executed.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify computational time requirements of a scRNA-seq trajectory-inference workflow (e.g., Escort) across dataset sizes such as 1000 vs 3000 cells, and report reproducible per-step runtime statistics.
skills.name: repeated-measure-runtime-aggregation
skills.search_text: repeated-measure-runtime-aggregation Use when you need to quantify computational time requirements of a scRNA-seq trajectory-inference workflow (e.g., Escort) across dataset sizes such as 1000 vs 3000 cells, and report reproducible per-step runtime statistics. When the goal is accuracy or trajectory-quality evaluation rather than runtime measurement — Escort's scoring system (negative infinity to two, scores > 0 recommended) addresses suitability, not speed. When the trajectory method does not use two-dimensional representations, since Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches using two-dimensional representations. When timing end-to-end pipelines with variable numbers of embeddings — this skill times Steps 2-3 for a single embedding, so multi-embedding sweeps need per-embedding aggregation instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark the computational cost of Escort's trajectory-inference workflow by timing Step 1 (trajectory suitability testing) independently of any embedding and Steps 2-3 (embedding evaluation plus trajectory fitting) per single embedding, repeating each scenario five times and reporting mean and SD runtime in minutes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Benchmark the computational cost of Escort's trajectory-inference workflow by timing Step 1 (trajectory suitability testing) independently of any embedding and Steps 2-3 (embedding evaluation plus trajectory fitting) per single embedding, repeating each scenario five times and reporting mean and SD runtime in minutes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accuracy or trajectory-quality evaluation rather than runtime measurement — Escort's scoring system (negative infinity to two, scores > 0 recommended) addresses suitability, not speed. When the trajectory method does not use two-dimensional representations, since Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches using two-dimensional representations. When timing end-to-end pipelines with variable numbers of embeddings — this skill times Steps 2-3 for a single embedding, so multi-embedding sweeps need per-embedding aggregation instead.
