skills.name: rna-seq-gene-id-mapping
skills.search_text: rna-seq-gene-id-mapping Use when the input expression matrix is a .csv counts file with Ensembl gene IDs as row names and TCGA-style sample IDs as columns, and downstream GSVA, integration, or correlation analysis requires gene-symbol-keyed TPM data. The expression matrix already uses gene symbols (e.g. the TPM matrix in Figure19 format) — no Ensembl-to-symbol mapping is needed before integration You need gene-level differential expression (DEG) counts analysis with edgeR, which operates on the counts matrix, not the TPM/log2-transformed values The transcriptome is non-human: ARMT relies on Bioconductor human resources such as org.Hs.eg.db, so Ensembl-to-symbol mapping is not supported for other organisms in this tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Converts a raw RNA-seq counts matrix with Ensembl gene IDs into a log2(TPM+1) matrix keyed by gene symbols, the format ARMT requires for downstream GSVA score calculation. This ID conversion is embedded in ARMT's Normalization&GSVA step so that counts matrices can be joined with genesets and clinical data on gene symbols. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Converts a raw RNA-seq counts matrix with Ensembl gene IDs into a log2(TPM+1) matrix keyed by gene symbols, the format ARMT requires for downstream GSVA score calculation. This ID conversion is embedded in ARMT's Normalization&GSVA step so that counts matrices can be joined with genesets and clinical data on gene symbols.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix already uses gene symbols (e.g. the TPM matrix in Figure19 format) — no Ensembl-to-symbol mapping is needed before integration You need gene-level differential expression (DEG) counts analysis with edgeR, which operates on the counts matrix, not the TPM/log2-transformed values The transcriptome is non-human: ARMT relies on Bioconductor human resources such as org.Hs.eg.db, so Ensembl-to-symbol mapping is not supported for other organisms in this tool

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq differential expression data contain paired or repeated samples from the same donor (e.g., pre/post or within-patient designs) and you need per-gene mixed-model P-values plus AIC/BIC fit metrics.
skills.name: rna-seq-linear-mixed-effects-modeling
skills.search_text: rna-seq-linear-mixed-effects-modeling Use when RNA-seq differential expression data contain paired or repeated samples from the same donor (e.g., pre/post or within-patient designs) and you need per-gene mixed-model P-values plus AIC/BIC fit metrics. The design is unpaired or has no repeated measures per donor — a plain linear model (kimma_lm / limma-style) or a paired-specific competitor like dream may be simpler and the paper benchmarks kimma against limma unpaired and dream paired models rather than claiming superiority in all settings The goal is genotype–expression association rather than differential expression — use kimma's dedicated kmFit_eQTL entry point instead of kmFit with run_lme You need kinship-adjusted relatedness modeling with the kinship covariance (kimma_lmerel path) rather than a simple donor random intercept — the generic run_lme path does not incorporate kin http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit per-gene linear mixed effects models to RNA-seq counts with kimma's kmFit (backed by lme4::lmer under REML) to handle paired/repeated-measure designs via a patientID random intercept, returning fixed-effect estimates, standard errors, P-values, and fit metrics (AIC/BIC) for each gene. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Fit per-gene linear mixed effects models to RNA-seq counts with kimma's kmFit (backed by lme4::lmer under REML) to handle paired/repeated-measure designs via a patientID random intercept, returning fixed-effect estimates, standard errors, P-values, and fit metrics (AIC/BIC) for each gene.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The design is unpaired or has no repeated measures per donor — a plain linear model (kimma_lm / limma-style) or a paired-specific competitor like dream may be simpler and the paper benchmarks kimma against limma unpaired and dream paired models rather than claiming superiority in all settings The goal is genotype–expression association rather than differential expression — use kimma's dedicated kmFit_eQTL entry point instead of kmFit with run_lme You need kinship-adjusted relatedness modeling with the kinship covariance (kimma_lmerel path) rather than a simple donor random intercept — the generic run_lme path does not incorporate kin

skills.description: Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq differential expression analysis whose original authors identified an outlier sample via QA/QC, or when PCA/box-plot diagnostics reveal a mislabeled or poorly separated sample before fitting a DE model.
skills.name: rna-seq-outlier-sample-exclusion
skills.search_text: rna-seq-outlier-sample-exclusion Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq differential expression analysis whose original authors identified an outlier sample via QA/QC, or when PCA/box-plot diagnostics reveal a mislabeled or poorly separated sample before fitting a DE model. The original publication did not flag any outlier sample and QC plots show clean separation by the metadata of interest — excluding samples would break reproducibility Input is already a normalized expression matrix from a microarray rather than RNA-seq counts (use the array workflow with 'mean' summary and no count filter instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify and exclude outlier RNA-seq samples flagged by QA/QC diagnostics (box plots, PCA) before differential expression analysis, so that downstream DEG counts reflect the same sample set as a reference publication. In the ExpressAnalyst salamander case study, this meant dropping SRR7499350 from the SRR7499348–SRR7499365 range prior to limma DE analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Identify and exclude outlier RNA-seq samples flagged by QA/QC diagnostics (box plots, PCA) before differential expression analysis, so that downstream DEG counts reflect the same sample set as a reference publication. In the ExpressAnalyst salamander case study, this meant dropping SRR7499350 from the SRR7499348–SRR7499365 range prior to limma DE analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The original publication did not flag any outlier sample and QC plots show clean separation by the metadata of interest — excluding samples would break reproducibility Input is already a normalized expression matrix from a microarray rather than RNA-seq counts (use the array workflow with 'mean' summary and no count filter instead)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA full-length assembly or isoform quantification method against known ground truth, requiring simulated paired-end reads with controlled depth, read length, and per-condition isoform abundances.
skills.name: rna-seq-paired-end-read-simulation
skills.search_text: rna-seq-paired-end-read-simulation Use when benchmarking a circRNA full-length assembly or isoform quantification method against known ground truth, requiring simulated paired-end reads with controlled depth, read length, and per-condition isoform abundances. The goal is real-data circRNA discovery on RNase R-treated RNA-seq rather than controlled benchmarking against known truth Circular transcripts of interest are intronic or intergenic, which the CircAST pipeline (and hence this hg19-annotation-based simulation design) cannot model Only single-end or non-paired-end data are available, since the design and CircAST itself assume paired-end SAM/BAM alignments from tophat2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Generates simulated paired-end RNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth transcript abundances to benchmark circRNA assembly and relative quantification, as done in the CircAST study with 2923 Hs68-derived circular transcripts and a 4-loci (NOLC1, PAFAH1B2, DHPS, EXOSC10), 10-isoform, 8-condition panel. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Generates simulated paired-end RNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth transcript abundances to benchmark circRNA assembly and relative quantification, as done in the CircAST study with 2923 Hs68-derived circular transcripts and a 4-loci (NOLC1, PAFAH1B2, DHPS, EXOSC10), 10-isoform, 8-condition panel.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-data circRNA discovery on RNase R-treated RNA-seq rather than controlled benchmarking against known truth Circular transcripts of interest are intronic or intergenic, which the CircAST pipeline (and hence this hg19-annotation-based simulation design) cannot model Only single-end or non-paired-end data are available, since the design and CircAST itself assume paired-end SAM/BAM alignments from tophat2

skills.description: Use when a list of publicly reported splice-site mutation calls (e.g. TCGA HNSC MAF-style calls for TP53) must be cross-checked against SCISSOR shape-change outliers to flag likely mis-annotated calls.
skills.name: rna-seq-pileup-shape-change-interpretation
skills.search_text: rna-seq-pileup-shape-change-interpretation Use when a list of publicly reported splice-site mutation calls (e.g. TCGA HNSC MAF-style calls for TP53) must be cross-checked against SCISSOR shape-change outliers to flag likely mis-annotated calls. The goal is de novo shape-change detection from BAM/pileup data rather than interpretation of existing SCISSOR results against mutation calls (run Scissor via build_pileup/get_Ranges instead). The mutation calls are not splice-site annotated, or the gene/analysis cohort differs from the TP53 TCGA HNSC results object, so the GSC/LSC sample overlap is undefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduce the SCISSOR-based discordance assessment of TP53 splice-site mutation calls in TCGA HNSC, checking which repository-annotated splice-site mutations coincide with statistically significant global (GSC) or local (LSC) shape changes in the base-level RNA-seq coverage shape. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Reproduce the SCISSOR-based discordance assessment of TP53 splice-site mutation calls in TCGA HNSC, checking which repository-annotated splice-site mutations coincide with statistically significant global (GSC) or local (LSC) shape changes in the base-level RNA-seq coverage shape.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo shape-change detection from BAM/pileup data rather than interpretation of existing SCISSOR results against mutation calls (run Scissor via build_pileup/get_Ranges instead). The mutation calls are not splice-site annotated, or the gene/analysis cohort differs from the TP53 TCGA HNSC results object, so the GSC/LSC sample overlap is undefined.

skills.description: Use when sorted RNAseq BAM files must be converted into position-by-position variant/invariant nucleotide frequency tables (REDItools outTables, bgzip+tabix indexed) to feed REDInet or other RNA editing classifiers.
skills.name: rna-seq-pileup-table-preparation
skills.search_text: rna-seq-pileup-table-preparation Use when sorted RNAseq BAM files must be converted into position-by-position variant/invariant nucleotide frequency tables (REDItools outTables, bgzip+tabix indexed) to feed REDInet or other RNA editing classifiers. Sites are already provided as a REDItools outTable or a curated ground-truth site list — skip pileup generation and run REDInet inference directly on the tabix-indexed table Analysis targets non-A-to-G events or non-human species — REDItoolDnaRna.py low-stringency settings and REDInet's A-to-G filtering (MinAG, MinAGfreq) are tuned for human A-to-I editing detection Only variant sites without flanking nucleotide frequencies are needed — the low-stringency settings deliberately retrieve complete 101-base intervals and are unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates RNAseq pileup outTables from sorted BAM files using REDItools (v1/v3) under low-stringency settings so that complete 101-base windows are retrievable for REDInet predictions, then bgzip-compresses and tabix-indexes the outTables for downstream inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf107
skills.summary: Generates RNAseq pileup outTables from sorted BAM files using REDItools (v1/v3) under low-stringency settings so that complete 101-base windows are retrievable for REDInet predictions, then bgzip-compresses and tabix-indexes the outTables for downstream inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sites are already provided as a REDItools outTable or a curated ground-truth site list — skip pileup generation and run REDInet inference directly on the tabix-indexed table Analysis targets non-A-to-G events or non-human species — REDItoolDnaRna.py low-stringency settings and REDInet's A-to-G filtering (MinAG, MinAGfreq) are tuned for human A-to-I editing detection Only variant sites without flanking nucleotide frequencies are needed — the low-stringency settings deliberately retrieve complete 101-base intervals and are unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when expression data (microarray, bulk or single-cell RNA-seq, e.g. TCGA-like sample-by-gene matrices) has a non-normal, bimodal, or multimodal feature distribution and must be Z-score normalized before correlation analysis.
skills.name: rna-seq-preprocessing-and-normalization
skills.search_text: rna-seq-preprocessing-and-normalization Use when expression data (microarray, bulk or single-cell RNA-seq, e.g. TCGA-like sample-by-gene matrices) has a non-normal, bimodal, or multimodal feature distribution and must be Z-score normalized before correlation analysis. Sequencing count data dominated by PCR artifacts or heteroskedasticity (high variation in features with high signal or read count) — the article states log2 transformation is most frequently used there instead of z-score. Single-cell data with non-viable cells and low abundance genes that first require read count filtration — the article notes this limitation precedes transformation. Data already normalized/centered, where a further z-score pass would be redundant before correlation analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Z-score transformation of non-normal or multimodal expression data (e.g., microarray and single-cell RNA-seq) using the FeatureCorr::data_transform function in R, with distribution visualizations of both original and transformed data to assess the transformation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: Z-score transformation of non-normal or multimodal expression data (e.g., microarray and single-cell RNA-seq) using the FeatureCorr::data_transform function in R, with distribution visualizations of both original and transformed data to assess the transformation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequencing count data dominated by PCR artifacts or heteroskedasticity (high variation in features with high signal or read count) — the article states log2 transformation is most frequently used there instead of z-score. Single-cell data with non-viable cells and low abundance genes that first require read count filtration — the article notes this limitation precedes transformation. Data already normalized/centered, where a further z-score pass would be redundant before correlation analysis.

skills.description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs from chicken (or other species) must be spliced-aligned for downstream per-sample variant calling (g.vcf/HaplotypeCaller) or allele-specific expression analysis.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-alignment
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-alignment Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs from chicken (or other species) must be spliced-aligned for downstream per-sample variant calling (g.vcf/HaplotypeCaller) or allele-specific expression analysis. Input data are already aligned BAM files — the next step in this workflow is duplicate marking with Picard 2.8.1 and GATK 3.7 processing, not re-alignment The goal is ASE detection from an existing multi-sample VCF — use VADT (github.com/mjtiv/VADT) directly rather than re-aligning reads Reads are small-RNA or single-end libraries where spliced two-pass alignment of paired reads against a full genome build is not appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Align paired-end broiler RNA-seq reads with STAR 2.5.2b in two-pass mode against the Gallus_gallus_5.0 build, then mark duplicates with Picard 2.8.1, producing aligned BAMs ready for GATK HaplotypeCaller variant calling and ASE analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Align paired-end broiler RNA-seq reads with STAR 2.5.2b in two-pass mode against the Gallus_gallus_5.0 build, then mark duplicates with Picard 2.8.1, producing aligned BAMs ready for GATK HaplotypeCaller variant calling and ASE analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already aligned BAM files — the next step in this workflow is duplicate marking with Picard 2.8.1 and GATK 3.7 processing, not re-alignment The goal is ASE detection from an existing multi-sample VCF — use VADT (github.com/mjtiv/VADT) directly rather than re-aligning reads Reads are small-RNA or single-end libraries where spliced two-pass alignment of paired reads against a full genome build is not appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have raw FASTQ reads (paired-end, e.g., first-strand Illumina libraries) and need a sorted, genome-aligned BAM as input to downstream transcriptome reconstruction (StringTie) or aptardi polyA-site prediction.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-alignment
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-alignment Use when you have raw FASTQ reads (paired-end, e.g., first-strand Illumina libraries) and need a sorted, genome-aligned BAM as input to downstream transcriptome reconstruction (StringTie) or aptardi polyA-site prediction. The input is already a genome-aligned sorted BAM from a previous run — re-aligning adds nothing downstream The goal is quantifying expression against a fixed transcriptome only (no transcript reconstruction or 3'-end refinement planned) — a direct quantification workflow such as Salmon/RSEM on an existing GTF is more appropriate The reads are unstranded and/or from a non-mammalian species outside the scope tested (the paper notes aptardi performed modestly worse on the unstranded, cross-species BNLx/SHR data and that engineered DNA features may not apply outside mammals) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Splice-aware alignment of RNA-Seq reads to a reference genome with HISAT2 in transcriptome-assembly mode (e.g., --rna-strandness RF --dta), followed by SAMtools sorting, producing the sorted BAM that StringTie reconstruction and aptardi polyA prediction consume. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Splice-aware alignment of RNA-Seq reads to a reference genome with HISAT2 in transcriptome-assembly mode (e.g., --rna-strandness RF --dta), followed by SAMtools sorting, producing the sorted BAM that StringTie reconstruction and aptardi polyA prediction consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a genome-aligned sorted BAM from a previous run — re-aligning adds nothing downstream The goal is quantifying expression against a fixed transcriptome only (no transcript reconstruction or 3'-end refinement planned) — a direct quantification workflow such as Salmon/RSEM on an existing GTF is more appropriate The reads are unstranded and/or from a non-mammalian species outside the scope tested (the paper notes aptardi performed modestly worse on the unstranded, cross-species BNLx/SHR data and that engineered DNA features may not apply outside mammals)

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854 droplet-prepared mouse epithelial libraries) must be converted into a per-gene exonic read-pair count matrix for each demultiplexed sample combination.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-alignment-gene-counting
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-alignment-gene-counting Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854 droplet-prepared mouse epithelial libraries) must be converted into a per-gene exonic read-pair count matrix for each demultiplexed sample combination. Input is already a gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. the Nestorowa et al. GSE81682 count matrices obtained directly from the authors) — skip alignment and proceed to downstream modelling The dataset is human or another non-mouse organism, since the reference described here is specifically the mm10 mouse genome The goal is 10x Genomics molecule-level deconvolution, where the molecule-information-file based exclusion in MarioniLab/DropletUtils is the appropriate route instead of raw read-pair counting http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Align single-cell RNA-seq reads to the mouse mm10 genome and count exonic read pairs per gene per sample/barcode combination, producing the gene-by-sample count matrix needed for downstream analyses such as barcode-swapping regression in the Griffiths/Richard 2018 pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Align single-cell RNA-seq reads to the mouse mm10 genome and count exonic read pairs per gene per sample/barcode combination, producing the gene-by-sample count matrix needed for downstream analyses such as barcode-swapping regression in the Griffiths/Richard 2018 pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. the Nestorowa et al. GSE81682 count matrices obtained directly from the authors) — skip alignment and proceed to downstream modelling The dataset is human or another non-mouse organism, since the reference described here is specifically the mm10 mouse genome The goal is 10x Genomics molecule-level deconvolution, where the molecule-information-file based exclusion in MarioniLab/DropletUtils is the appropriate route instead of raw read-pair counting

skills.description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a mapping-derived signal (e.g. a shift, bias, or clustering pattern) is algorithm-independent by repeating the same alignment on identical input FASTQ with multiple aligners and comparing downstream distributions.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-alignment-multi-aligner
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-alignment-multi-aligner Use when you need to demonstrate that a mapping-derived signal (e.g. a shift, bias, or clustering pattern) is algorithm-independent by repeating the same alignment on identical input FASTQ with multiple aligners and comparing downstream distributions. The question is about alignment quality or sensitivity of a single aligner rather than testing whether a pattern persists across aligners — a single-alignment benchmark suffices. The data are paired-end or spliced RNA-Seq where intron-aware alignment is required; the article's STAR run explicitly specifies no introns for its single-end P. patens UMI data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align the same quality-filtered, UMI-clipped FASTQ reads to a genomic reference with three independent aligners (STAR with no introns, GSNAP, and HISAT2) to test whether an observed pattern — here the UMI-read mapping shift artefact in P. patens single-cell RNA-Seq — is an artefact of one alignment algorithm or persists across aligners. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-31064-7
skills.summary: Align the same quality-filtered, UMI-clipped FASTQ reads to a genomic reference with three independent aligners (STAR with no introns, GSNAP, and HISAT2) to test whether an observed pattern — here the UMI-read mapping shift artefact in P. patens single-cell RNA-Seq — is an artefact of one alignment algorithm or persists across aligners.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about alignment quality or sensitivity of a single aligner rather than testing whether a pattern persists across aligners — a single-alignment benchmark suffices. The data are paired-end or spliced RNA-Seq where intron-aware alignment is required; the article's STAR run explicitly specifies no introns for its single-end P. patens UMI data.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing labeled SPLiT-seq FASTQ reads (e.g., SCSit output with combinatorial barcodes and UMI) need to be aligned to mm10, hg19, or a combined mm10-hg19 reference to compare mapped-read yields.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-alignment-star
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-alignment-star Use when preprocessing labeled SPLiT-seq FASTQ reads (e.g., SCSit output with combinatorial barcodes and UMI) need to be aligned to mm10, hg19, or a combined mm10-hg19 reference to compare mapped-read yields. Input is not SPLiT-seq pair-end FASTQ data with combinatorial barcodes and UMI (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or other single-cell platforms). The reference genome is neither mm10 nor hg19 nor a combined mm10-hg19 build. The goal is only to identify barcodes/UMIs (preprocessing) rather than to measure mapped-read yield. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align SPLiT-seq identified reads (from SCSit or the original method) to the combined mm10-hg19 genome (or mm10 alone) with STAR, and record uniquely mapped read counts to quantify how much more data SCSit retains. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Align SPLiT-seq identified reads (from SCSit or the original method) to the combined mm10-hg19 genome (or mm10 alone) with STAR, and record uniquely mapped read counts to quantify how much more data SCSit retains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not SPLiT-seq pair-end FASTQ data with combinatorial barcodes and UMI (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or other single-cell platforms). The reference genome is neither mm10 nor hg19 nor a combined mm10-hg19 build. The goal is only to identify barcodes/UMIs (preprocessing) rather than to measure mapped-read yield.

skills.description: Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g., the 4-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340 or the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564) and you need one node-level read count and regulation value instead of per-gene ambiguity.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-count-aggregation-per-node
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-count-aggregation-per-node Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g., the 4-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340 or the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564) and you need one node-level read count and regulation value instead of per-gene ambiguity. Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP Analysis is restricted to human metabolic KEGG pathways at the gene level; KEGG provides no curated isoform-level enzyme activity, so isoform-resolution questions are out of scope When you only need per-gene (not node-level) regulation — the standard expanded network already shows every homolog individually http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 FunHoP-style aggregation that collapses all genes within a multi-gene KEGG pathway node into a single node-level measurement by summing RNA-seq read counts (adjusted for gene length), assuming reaction activity depends mainly on the highest-read homolog. This makes node-level differential expression and network coloring biologically interpretable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.03.003
skills.summary: FunHoP-style aggregation that collapses all genes within a multi-gene KEGG pathway node into a single node-level measurement by summing RNA-seq read counts (adjusted for gene length), assuming reaction activity depends mainly on the highest-read homolog. This makes node-level differential expression and network coloring biologically interpretable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pathways from KEGG category 1.7 'Glycan biosynthesis and metabolism' that use 'links' instead of nodes — these cannot be expanded or colored in Cytoscape and are excluded from FunHoP Analysis is restricted to human metabolic KEGG pathways at the gene level; KEGG provides no curated isoform-level enzyme activity, so isoform-resolution questions are out of scope When you only need per-gene (not node-level) regulation — the standard expanded network already shows every homolog individually

skills.description: Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detection sensitivity (or similar read-count-dependent callers) across decreasing sequencing depths from a single deeply sequenced paired-end FASTQ sample.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-depth-subsampling
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-depth-subsampling Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detection sensitivity (or similar read-count-dependent callers) across decreasing sequencing depths from a single deeply sequenced paired-end FASTQ sample. Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome data — subsampled reads cannot support paired-end fusion anchoring The goal is to detect fusion genes not involving a user-provided target gene; anchored methods only return fusions containing the anchored gene The original FASTQ depth is already too shallow for 7 halvings to leave meaningful read counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Generates progressive sequencing-depth dilution series from paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data by repeated random halving of read pairs, to benchmark caller sensitivity as depth is reduced below ~1 million reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Generates progressive sequencing-depth dilution series from paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data by repeated random halving of read pairs, to benchmark caller sensitivity as depth is reduced below ~1 million reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome data — subsampled reads cannot support paired-end fusion anchoring The goal is to detect fusion genes not involving a user-provided target gene; anchored methods only return fusions containing the anchored gene The original FASTQ depth is already too shallow for 7 halvings to leave meaningful read counts

skills.description: Use when training or fairly benchmarking fixed-length read classifiers (e.g., viRNAtrap vs DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, Seq2Seq) and you need viral and human transcripts converted into comparable 48 bp fragments with shared train/test splits.
skills.name: rna-seq-read-fragmentation
skills.search_text: rna-seq-read-fragmentation Use when training or fairly benchmarking fixed-length read classifiers (e.g., viRNAtrap vs DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, Seq2Seq) and you need viral and human transcripts converted into comparable 48 bp fragments with shared train/test splits.
