skills.search_text: rna-seq-tpm-expression-retrieval Use when building a soybean–fungal infection expression dataset (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi) from public TPM estimates to feed coexpression or differential analyses. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) requiring alignment or quantification rather than pre-computed TPM estimates The analysis targets non-infection soybean tissues or pathogens outside the five fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi), so the 150-sample infection subset and its noise threshold do not apply A different expression unit (e.g., raw counts for DESeq2-style modeling) is required, since this skill relies on TPM estimates from the Soybean Expression Atlas http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves TPM expression estimates from the Soybean Expression Atlas plus supplementary infection RNA-seq sample data, subsets them to soybean–fungal infection samples, and applies a median-TPM noise filter to assemble a filtered gene expression matrix for coexpression/network analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Retrieves TPM expression estimates from the Soybean Expression Atlas plus supplementary infection RNA-seq sample data, subsets them to soybean–fungal infection samples, and applies a median-TPM noise filter to assemble a filtered gene expression matrix for coexpression/network analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) requiring alignment or quantification rather than pre-computed TPM estimates The analysis targets non-infection soybean tissues or pathogens outside the five fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi), so the 150-sample infection subset and its noise threshold do not apply A different expression unit (e.g., raw counts for DESeq2-style modeling) is required, since this skill relies on TPM estimates from the Soybean Expression Atlas

skills.description: Use when you have splice-aware BAM alignments of RNA-seq reads from one or more aligners (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) mapped to a reference genome and need to assemble transcripts, especially lowly expressed ones missed by single-aligner assemblers.
skills.name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
skills.search_text: rna-seq-transcript-assembly Use when you have splice-aware BAM alignments of RNA-seq reads from one or more aligners (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) mapped to a reference genome and need to assemble transcripts, especially lowly expressed ones missed by single-aligner assemblers. Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets You need annotation-guided assembly using known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies Input alignments come from aligners other than Hisat(2) or Star — the current Tiglon version only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Genome-guided transcriptome reconstruction via Tiglon's label-based dynamic path-extension program: build a labeled splice graph from multiple aligners' BAM mappings (Hisat2, Star), then traverse it with dynamic programming to recover transcript-representing paths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Genome-guided transcriptome reconstruction via Tiglon's label-based dynamic path-extension program: build a labeled splice graph from multiple aligners' BAM mappings (Hisat2, Star), then traverse it with dynamic programming to recover transcript-representing paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets You need annotation-guided assembly using known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies Input alignments come from aligners other than Hisat(2) or Star — the current Tiglon version only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-Seq FASTQ samples (e.g., 180 TARGET osteosarcoma tumors plus 9 normal bone controls) must be converted into a consensus transcript candidate set prior to novel lncRNA detection.
skills.name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
skills.search_text: rna-seq-transcript-assembly Use when raw RNA-Seq FASTQ samples (e.g., 180 TARGET osteosarcoma tumors plus 9 normal bone controls) must be converted into a consensus transcript candidate set prior to novel lncRNA detection. Input is already an assembled transcriptome (GTF/GFF) or a FASTA of candidate transcript sequences — go directly to classification with LncDC Only a single aligner/assembler combination is available, since the reliability argument rests on consensus between STAR+Cufflinks and HISAT2+StringTie routes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstruct transcript assemblies from RNA-Seq reads via two independent aligner/assembler routes (STAR+Cufflinks and HISAT2+StringTie) and retain only candidates whose chromosome positions agree between routes, yielding a high-confidence candidate set for downstream lncRNA classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Reconstruct transcript assemblies from RNA-Seq reads via two independent aligner/assembler routes (STAR+Cufflinks and HISAT2+StringTie) and retain only candidates whose chromosome positions agree between routes, yielding a high-confidence candidate set for downstream lncRNA classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an assembled transcriptome (GTF/GFF) or a FASTA of candidate transcript sequences — go directly to classification with LncDC Only a single aligner/assembler combination is available, since the reliability argument rests on consensus between STAR+Cufflinks and HISAT2+StringTie routes

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENA (disease and control samples) must be converted to per-sample isoform-level TPM abundances as input for isoform switching / dMDT calling in the CanIsoNet workflow.
skills.name: rna-seq-transcript-quantification
skills.search_text: rna-seq-transcript-quantification Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENA (disease and control samples) must be converted to per-sample isoform-level TPM abundances as input for isoform switching / dMDT calling in the CanIsoNet workflow. Input is already a quantified gene-level count/TPM matrix with no isoform resolution — dMDT isoform switching requires transcript-level abundances The dataset is one of the already-processed conditions (27 PCAWG cancer types plus OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) browsable directly at caniso.net The analysis goal is network impact scoring only (the CanIsoNet/STRING step) without new RNA-seq quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify transcript/isoform-level abundances (TPM) for every sample in a disease RNA-seq study with Kallisto against the human reference transcriptome, producing the per-sample isoform expression values that the CanIsoNet dMDT isoform-switching pipeline requires. This is the expression-measurement step that converts raw FASTQ reads into isoform usage statistics comparable across disease and control samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Quantify transcript/isoform-level abundances (TPM) for every sample in a disease RNA-seq study with Kallisto against the human reference transcriptome, producing the per-sample isoform expression values that the CanIsoNet dMDT isoform-switching pipeline requires. This is the expression-measurement step that converts raw FASTQ reads into isoform usage statistics comparable across disease and control samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quantified gene-level count/TPM matrix with no isoform resolution — dMDT isoform switching requires transcript-level abundances The dataset is one of the already-processed conditions (27 PCAWG cancer types plus OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's) browsable directly at caniso.net The analysis goal is network impact scoring only (the CanIsoNet/STRING step) without new RNA-seq quantification

skills.description: Use when classifying binary treatment response (e.g. rituximab responders vs non-responders in the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 cohort) from transcriptomic matrices where predictors vastly outnumber samples (P >> n) and an honest out-of-sample AUC is required.
skills.name: rna-seq-treatment-response-classification
skills.search_text: rna-seq-treatment-response-classification Use when classifying binary treatment response (e.g. rituximab responders vs non-responders in the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 cohort) from transcriptomic matrices where predictors vastly outnumber samples (P >> n) and an honest out-of-sample AUC is required. The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split, or predictors are few relative to samples — the article motivates nested CV specifically for small-n, P >> n biomedical data You only need hyperparameter tuning, not an unbiased performance estimate — plain cv.glmnet inner CV suffices and is faster Predictors include factors/character variables not yet encoded — one_hot() conversion is needed before passing a matrix to glmnet http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds an unbiased classifier of treatment response from high-dimensional RNA-seq expression data using nested cross-validation (nestcv.glmnet) with an embedded univariate t-test feature filter, so that filtering and hyperparameter tuning never leak into the outer test folds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048
skills.summary: Builds an unbiased classifier of treatment response from high-dimensional RNA-seq expression data using nested cross-validation (nestcv.glmnet) with an embedded univariate t-test feature filter, so that filtering and hyperparameter tuning never leak into the outer test folds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is large enough for a conventional 2/3-1/3 train/test split, or predictors are few relative to samples — the article motivates nested CV specifically for small-n, P >> n biomedical data You only need hyperparameter tuning, not an unbiased performance estimate — plain cv.glmnet inner CV suffices and is faster Predictors include factors/character variables not yet encoded — one_hot() conversion is needed before passing a matrix to glmnet

skills.description: Use when raw RNA sequences (fixed length, e.g. 41 nt FASTA or CSV) must be converted into position-specific k-mer/gapped k-mer binary feature vectors for ML-based modification-site prediction.
skills.name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-feature-extraction Use when raw RNA sequences (fixed length, e.g. 41 nt FASTA or CSV) must be converted into position-specific k-mer/gapped k-mer binary feature vectors for ML-based modification-site prediction. Input is already a feature table (e.g. All_Features_Dataset.csv exists) — proceed directly to model training/feature selection instead Sequences vary in length or exceed 41 nt without re-defining the position-specific matching window, since the descriptor counts depend on the 41-nt coordinate grid The goal is frequency-based k-mer features or combination with existing frequency-based descriptors — the authors found position-specific features do not work well in conjunction with frequency-based counterparts http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes 41-nt RNA sequences into position-specific gapped k-mer (PSG k-mer), position-specific k-mer, and GC-content features — 19,877 numerical features per sequence in total — as used by iRNA5hmC-PS for 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) site prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.10.032
skills.summary: Encodes 41-nt RNA sequences into position-specific gapped k-mer (PSG k-mer), position-specific k-mer, and GC-content features — 19,877 numerical features per sequence in total — as used by iRNA5hmC-PS for 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) site prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table (e.g. All_Features_Dataset.csv exists) — proceed directly to model training/feature selection instead Sequences vary in length or exceed 41 nt without re-defining the position-specific matching window, since the descriptor counts depend on the 41-nt coordinate grid The goal is frequency-based k-mer features or combination with existing frequency-based descriptors — the authors found position-specific features do not work well in conjunction with frequency-based counterparts

skills.description: Use when raw RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format must be converted into the numeric feature set (SIFs, SS k-mer scores, ORF, protein features) that LncDC's XGBoost model consumes for lncRNA prediction, or when reproducing its SSF ablation experiments.
skills.name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-feature-extraction Use when raw RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format must be converted into the numeric feature set (SIFs, SS k-mer scores, ORF, protein features) that LncDC's XGBoost model consumes for lncRNA prediction, or when reproducing its SSF ablation experiments. Input is already a numeric feature table rather than raw transcript FASTA sequences — no sequence feature extraction is needed Secondary structure features are required but ViennaRNA is not installed (RNAfold is only available when the optional dependency is present) Only full-model default human prediction on well-annotated data is needed and runtime matters — skip -r since RNAfold is time-consuming and SSF gains are marginal http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Extract sequence-derived features (sequence intrinsic features/SIFs, hexamer scores, flexible ORF features, and secondary structure features/SSFs via ViennaRNA k-mer tables) from RNA FASTA transcripts to feed LncDC's XGBoost lncRNA-vs-mRNA classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Extract sequence-derived features (sequence intrinsic features/SIFs, hexamer scores, flexible ORF features, and secondary structure features/SSFs via ViennaRNA k-mer tables) from RNA FASTA transcripts to feed LncDC's XGBoost lncRNA-vs-mRNA classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table rather than raw transcript FASTA sequences — no sequence feature extraction is needed Secondary structure features are required but ViennaRNA is not installed (RNAfold is only available when the optional dependency is present) Only full-model default human prediction on well-annotated data is needed and runtime matters — skip -r since RNAfold is time-consuming and SSF gains are marginal

skills.description: Use when building train/test splits of RNA fragments (e.g., 51-nt pseudouridine-site windows) where homologous sequences across folds would inflate prediction accuracy through leakage.
skills.name: rna-sequence-identity-reduction
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-identity-reduction Use when building train/test splits of RNA fragments (e.g., 51-nt pseudouridine-site windows) where homologous sequences across folds would inflate prediction accuracy through leakage. Input is already a single de-duplicated benchmark where train/test homology filtering was applied previously The comparison targets methods evaluated without identity reduction (e.g., iPseU-CNN, for which no source code or webserver was available for direct comparison) Working with non-RNA sequences where cd-hit-est word-length 4 defaults are inappropriate (use the protein or DNA cd-hit variants instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 De-replicates RNA sequence benchmark sets so that training and test fragments share no high-identity homologs, using cd-hit-est-2d (threshold 0.8, word length 4), Needleman-Wunsch global alignment (>60% identity removal), and cd-hit-est within-set clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: De-replicates RNA sequence benchmark sets so that training and test fragments share no high-identity homologs, using cd-hit-est-2d (threshold 0.8, word length 4), Needleman-Wunsch global alignment (>60% identity removal), and cd-hit-est within-set clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a single de-duplicated benchmark where train/test homology filtering was applied previously The comparison targets methods evaluated without identity reduction (e.g., iPseU-CNN, for which no source code or webserver was available for direct comparison) Working with non-RNA sequences where cd-hit-est word-length 4 defaults are inappropriate (use the protein or DNA cd-hit variants instead)

skills.description: Use when raw RNA sequence segments (e.g., 41-nt tissue-specific m6A positive/negative samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature matrices before feeding a CNN or other fixed-input neural network model.
skills.name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding Use when raw RNA sequence segments (e.g., 41-nt tissue-specific m6A positive/negative samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature matrices before feeding a CNN or other fixed-input neural network model. Input is already a numeric feature matrix or embedding (e.g., Gene2Vec-style vectors) rather than raw nucleotide sequences Sequences are not the fixed 41-nt m6A segments used by im6A-TS-CNN, since the 4 x 41 = 164-dimension assumption no longer holds without re-padding or re-trimming A sequence-aware model (e.g., RNN/transformer) that can consume raw nucleotide tokens directly is chosen, making one-hot flattening unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Encodes RNA nucleotide sequences as 4-dimensional one-hot vectors (A=(1,0,0,0), U=(0,1,0,0), C=(0,0,1,0), G=(0,0,0,1)) so each 41-nt m6A segment becomes a 164-dimensional feature vector suitable for CNN-based m6A site identification as used in im6A-TS-CNN. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Encodes RNA nucleotide sequences as 4-dimensional one-hot vectors (A=(1,0,0,0), U=(0,1,0,0), C=(0,0,1,0), G=(0,0,0,1)) so each 41-nt m6A segment becomes a 164-dimensional feature vector suitable for CNN-based m6A site identification as used in im6A-TS-CNN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature matrix or embedding (e.g., Gene2Vec-style vectors) rather than raw nucleotide sequences Sequences are not the fixed 41-nt m6A segments used by im6A-TS-CNN, since the 4 x 41 = 164-dimension assumption no longer holds without re-padding or re-trimming A sequence-aware model (e.g., RNN/transformer) that can consume raw nucleotide tokens directly is chosen, making one-hot flattening unnecessary

skills.description: Use when preparing Ψ-centered 51-bp RNA fragments (sequence plus RNAshapes dot-bracket structure) from RMBase v2.0 as fixed-size one-of-K binary matrices to feed paired 1D CNN inputs like MU-PseUDeep.
skills.name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding
skills.search_text: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding Use when preparing Ψ-centered 51-bp RNA fragments (sequence plus RNAshapes dot-bracket structure) from RMBase v2.0 as fixed-size one-of-K binary matrices to feed paired 1D CNN inputs like MU-PseUDeep. Fragments are not 51-bp and uridine-centered (e.g., variable-length windows or non-Ψ modifications) — the fixed 51 × 4 and 51 × 6 matrices would not apply Input is already a derived feature vector (e.g., the pseudo-nucleotide composition features used by iRNA-PseU or PPUS SVMs) rather than raw fragment sequence and structure You need to handle class imbalance alone — one-of-K encoding does not address imbalance; negatives must still be bootstrapped into N bins sized to the positive class http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 One-of-K (one-hot) encoding of 51-bp Ψ-centered RNA fragments into 51 × 4 nucleotide binary matrices and RNAshapes dot-bracket secondary structure into 51 × 6 binary matrices, producing the fixed-width dual inputs that MU-PseUDeep's paired 1D CNNs require for pseudouridine site prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: One-of-K (one-hot) encoding of 51-bp Ψ-centered RNA fragments into 51 × 4 nucleotide binary matrices and RNAshapes dot-bracket secondary structure into 51 × 6 binary matrices, producing the fixed-width dual inputs that MU-PseUDeep's paired 1D CNNs require for pseudouridine site prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fragments are not 51-bp and uridine-centered (e.g., variable-length windows or non-Ψ modifications) — the fixed 51 × 4 and 51 × 6 matrices would not apply Input is already a derived feature vector (e.g., the pseudo-nucleotide composition features used by iRNA-PseU or PPUS SVMs) rather than raw fragment sequence and structure You need to handle class imbalance alone — one-of-K encoding does not address imbalance; negatives must still be bootstrapped into N bins sized to the positive class

skills.description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) or dot-bracket FASTA format plus a tab-delimited per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file, and you need BPC/entropy plots and structure-count heatmap/histogram outputs.
skills.name: rna-structural-content-figure-generation
skills.search_text: rna-structural-content-figure-generation Use when you have an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) or dot-bracket FASTA format plus a tab-delimited per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file, and you need BPC/entropy plots and structure-count heatmap/histogram outputs. The secondary structure file is neither CT format nor dot-bracket FASTA (the two scripts dispatch only on these two input types). No per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list is available — both scripts require the structure file to be paired with a shannon.txt entropy file. The goal is interactive exploration rather than command-line figure generation — the README suggests the Rmd notebook via RStudio as the alternate access mode. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate RSCanner's RNA structural-content figures (BPC line plot, smoothed Shannon entropy plot, structure-counts histogram, and heatmap) by routing a secondary-structure file in CT or dot-bracket format, paired with a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list, to the correct R script. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Generate RSCanner's RNA structural-content figures (BPC line plot, smoothed Shannon entropy plot, structure-counts histogram, and heatmap) by routing a secondary-structure file in CT or dot-bracket format, paired with a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list, to the correct R script.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The secondary structure file is neither CT format nor dot-bracket FASTA (the two scripts dispatch only on these two input types). No per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list is available — both scripts require the structure file to be paired with a shannon.txt entropy file. The goal is interactive exploration rather than command-line figure generation — the README suggests the Rmd notebook via RStudio as the alternate access mode.

skills.description: Use when you have per-window BPC values and smoothed Shannon entropy values for an RNA (e.g., from HCV_Jc1 CT/dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt) and must designate structure counts under RSCanner's dual-threshold filtering.
skills.name: rna-structure-basepair-content-filtering
skills.search_text: rna-structure-basepair-content-filtering Use when you have per-window BPC values and smoothed Shannon entropy values for an RNA (e.g., from HCV_Jc1 CT/dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt) and must designate structure counts under RSCanner's dual-threshold filtering. You only have raw dot-bracket/CT structure or Shannon entropy input and have not yet run RSCanner's sliding-window BPC and entropy smoothing step — run RSCanner first to generate bpc_data.csv and smoothed_Shannon_data.csv. The goal is the heatmap of % structure content per bin (ordered_structure_table.csv), not the per-nucleotide structure counts filter and its histogram. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies RSCanner's structure counts filter, classifying each nucleotide of an RNA transcript as a structure count where its base pair content (BPC) exceeds a percentile cutoff and its smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a percentile cutoff (both default = 50th percentile), then saves the surviving positions and plots their frequency distribution as a histogram. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Applies RSCanner's structure counts filter, classifying each nucleotide of an RNA transcript as a structure count where its base pair content (BPC) exceeds a percentile cutoff and its smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a percentile cutoff (both default = 50th percentile), then saves the surviving positions and plots their frequency distribution as a histogram.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw dot-bracket/CT structure or Shannon entropy input and have not yet run RSCanner's sliding-window BPC and entropy smoothing step — run RSCanner first to generate bpc_data.csv and smoothed_Shannon_data.csv. The goal is the heatmap of % structure content per bin (ordered_structure_table.csv), not the per-nucleotide structure counts filter and its histogram.

skills.description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure (CT or dot-bracket format) plus a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file and need per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots (e.g. reproducing Supplementary Fig. S2A/B for HCV_Jc1).
skills.name: rna-structure-lineplot-visualization
skills.search_text: rna-structure-lineplot-visualization Use when you have an RNA secondary structure (CT or dot-bracket format) plus a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file and need per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots (e.g. reproducing Supplementary Fig. S2A/B for HCV_Jc1). No positional Shannon entropy file (calculated from base pairing probabilities) is available — RSCanner_CT_shannon.R / RSCanner_dotbracket_shannon.R require both a structure file and a shannon.txt input Input is not a secondary structure in CT or dot-bracket (FASTA) format (e.g. raw sequencing data, 3D coordinates, or alignment files) The goal is the structure-counts frequency distribution (heatmap/histogram) rather than per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Per-nucleotide line-plot visualization of RNA secondary-structure content: base-pairing content (BPC) and smoothed Shannon entropy computed over a centered 51 nt sliding window (as in RSCanner), rendered as ggplot2 line plots with dashed global-median reference lines and exported as CSV data tables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Per-nucleotide line-plot visualization of RNA secondary-structure content: base-pairing content (BPC) and smoothed Shannon entropy computed over a centered 51 nt sliding window (as in RSCanner), rendered as ggplot2 line plots with dashed global-median reference lines and exported as CSV data tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No positional Shannon entropy file (calculated from base pairing probabilities) is available — RSCanner_CT_shannon.R / RSCanner_dotbracket_shannon.R require both a structure file and a shannon.txt input Input is not a secondary structure in CT or dot-bracket (FASTA) format (e.g. raw sequencing data, 3D coordinates, or alignment files) The goal is the structure-counts frequency distribution (heatmap/histogram) rather than per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots

skills.description: Use when building training and test FASTA sets of mRNA, their CDS, and lncRNA transcripts from curated annotations (e.g., NCBI RefSeq or GENCODE) to train or benchmark lncRNA identification models.
skills.name: rna-transcript-dataset-construction
skills.search_text: rna-transcript-dataset-construction Use when building training and test FASTA sets of mRNA, their CDS, and lncRNA transcripts from curated annotations (e.g., NCBI RefSeq or GENCODE) to train or benchmark lncRNA identification models. Raw RNA-Seq reads rather than assembled transcript FASTA — LncDC's predictor takes RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format, not FASTQ read data Feature tables or precomputed k-mer matrices — this skill constructs the raw transcript-level FASTA inputs that precede feature extraction Organisms with too few well-annotated lncRNAs to build a local training set — the README recommends instead reusing models trained on evolutionary close model organisms (Zebrafish, Yeast, Soybean, D. melanogaster, etc.) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Assembles curated mRNA, CDS, and lncRNA transcript FASTA sets (e.g., M-Train/M-Test mouse sets) from manual gene annotations so they can be fed to LncDC's lncDC-train.py and lncDC.py for model training and coding-potential benchmarking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Assembles curated mRNA, CDS, and lncRNA transcript FASTA sets (e.g., M-Train/M-Test mouse sets) from manual gene annotations so they can be fed to LncDC's lncDC-train.py and lncDC.py for model training and coding-potential benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw RNA-Seq reads rather than assembled transcript FASTA — LncDC's predictor takes RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format, not FASTQ read data Feature tables or precomputed k-mer matrices — this skill constructs the raw transcript-level FASTA inputs that precede feature extraction Organisms with too few well-annotated lncRNAs to build a local training set — the README recommends instead reusing models trained on evolutionary close model organisms (Zebrafish, Yeast, Soybean, D. melanogaster, etc.)

skills.description: Use when you have an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers, scvelo RNA velocity, and an ensemble of DTW-aligned simulated trajectories, and need per-cell scores, pseudotime, and cell fate probabilities.
skills.name: rna-velocity-alignment-score-computation
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-alignment-score-computation Use when you have an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers, scvelo RNA velocity, and an ensemble of DTW-aligned simulated trajectories, and need per-cell scores, pseudotime, and cell fate probabilities. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable from the RNA velocity field — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cytopath trajectory inference in this case The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty (e.g. spurious root/terminal states as in the erythroid gastrulation dataset or with time-dependent degradation rates), since downstream alignment scores inherit the error http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute Cytopath's cell-to-trajectory alignment scores that evaluate each cell's static expression and RNA velocity similarity against consensus trajectory steps, then use the maximum-scoring assignment to derive per-trajectory pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation potential. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Compute Cytopath's cell-to-trajectory alignment scores that evaluate each cell's static expression and RNA velocity similarity against consensus trajectory steps, then use the maximum-scoring assignment to derive per-trajectory pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation potential.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable from the RNA velocity field — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cytopath trajectory inference in this case The underlying RNA velocity estimation is faulty (e.g. spurious root/terminal states as in the erythroid gastrulation dataset or with time-dependent degradation rates), since downstream alignment scores inherit the error

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark an RNA-velocity- or manifold-based cell-cycle method (scVelo dynamical, Cyclum, Cyclone, Revelio, DeepCycle) on mESC or human fibroblast h5ad data and quantify agreement of inferred trajectories with annotated phases or DeepCycle's cell_cycle_theta.
skills.name: rna-velocity-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-baseline-comparison Use when you need to benchmark an RNA-velocity- or manifold-based cell-cycle method (scVelo dynamical, Cyclum, Cyclone, Revelio, DeepCycle) on mESC or human fibroblast h5ad data and quantify agreement of inferred trajectories with annotated phases or DeepCycle's cell_cycle_theta. No cycling genes are detectable in the dataset (e.g. insufficient sequencing depth per cell) — the results will not be reliable per the README The input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments, since all baselines operate on Mu/Ms moments The goal is phase assignment from gene-marker signatures only, which the paper states 'lacks generalizability' across cellular models http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking procedure that reproduces the head-to-head comparison of DeepCycle against scVelo's extended dynamical model, Cyclum, Cyclone and Revelio on cell-cycle scRNA-seq datasets, testing whether each method fits single-gene unspliced-spliced dynamics and recovers the correct latent-time/cell-cycle trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that reproduces the head-to-head comparison of DeepCycle against scVelo's extended dynamical model, Cyclum, Cyclone and Revelio on cell-cycle scRNA-seq datasets, testing whether each method fits single-gene unspliced-spliced dynamics and recovers the correct latent-time/cell-cycle trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cycling genes are detectable in the dataset (e.g. insufficient sequencing depth per cell) — the results will not be reliable per the README The input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments, since all baselines operate on Mu/Ms moments The goal is phase assignment from gene-marker signatures only, which the paper states 'lacks generalizability' across cellular models

skills.description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on real datasets with known trajectory directions, or when quantitative CBDir/ICCoh benchmark scores are needed to validate velocity estimates.
skills.name: rna-velocity-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on real datasets with known trajectory directions, or when quantitative CBDir/ICCoh benchmark scores are needed to validate velocity estimates. Data lacks unspliced/spliced layers — RNA velocity (both LatentVelo and scVelo) requires AnnData objects with spliced and unspliced count layers The goal is synthetic-data or batch-correction benchmarking rather than real-dataset trajectory direction evaluation — those use separate benchmark subdirectories in the LatentVelo repo Datasets contain sparse cell clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — velocity scores may remain accurate but inferred latent trajectories can start from incorrect initial states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark RNA velocity methods (LatentVelo vs scVelo stochastic/dynamical) across developmental h5ad datasets using cross-boundary directedness (CBDir) and inner-cluster coherence (ICCoh) scores from the scIB benchmark suite, aggregating results into comparison tables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Benchmark RNA velocity methods (LatentVelo vs scVelo stochastic/dynamical) across developmental h5ad datasets using cross-boundary directedness (CBDir) and inner-cluster coherence (ICCoh) scores from the scIB benchmark suite, aggregating results into comparison tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks unspliced/spliced layers — RNA velocity (both LatentVelo and scVelo) requires AnnData objects with spliced and unspliced count layers The goal is synthetic-data or batch-correction benchmarking rather than real-dataset trajectory direction evaluation — those use separate benchmark subdirectories in the LatentVelo repo Datasets contain sparse cell clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories — velocity scores may remain accurate but inferred latent trajectories can start from incorrect initial states

skills.description: Use when a TFvelo run has completed (rc.h5ad output exists) and you need to extract -fitted genes, test KEGG pathway enrichment among them, and verify the sign consistency of top-weighted TFs on specific pathway gene sets.
skills.name: rna-velocity-best-fitted-gene-selection
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-best-fitted-gene-selection Use when a TFvelo run has completed (rc.h5ad output exists) and you need to extract -fitted genes, test KEGG pathway enrichment among them, and verify the sign consistency of top-weighted TFs on specific pathway gene sets. The dataset lacks suitable TF expression data or you have not decompressed the ENCODE TF-target database (ENCODE.zip) after downloading the package The analysis goal is splicing-based velocity (unspliced/spliced counts with scVelo dynamics) rather than TF-regulation-based dynamics; TFvelo is also slower than scVelo, a weakness for large-scale datasets You need a fitted model for every gene — TFvelo still cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14), so genes not selected as best-fitted should not be force-analyzed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the best-fitted genes from a TFvelo RNA velocity run (stored in 'TFvelo_pancreas/rc.h5ad'), whose TF weight matrix is then used for KEGG over-representation enrichment and verification of TF weight-sign signatures (e.g. REST negative, HMGN3 positive on insulin secretion pathway genes in pancreas). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Selects the best-fitted genes from a TFvelo RNA velocity run (stored in 'TFvelo_pancreas/rc.h5ad'), whose TF weight matrix is then used for KEGG over-representation enrichment and verification of TF weight-sign signatures (e.g. REST negative, HMGN3 positive on insulin secretion pathway genes in pancreas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks suitable TF expression data or you have not decompressed the ENCODE TF-target database (ENCODE.zip) after downloading the package The analysis goal is splicing-based velocity (unspliced/spliced counts with scVelo dynamics) rather than TF-regulation-based dynamics; TFvelo is also slower than scVelo, a weakness for large-scale datasets You need a fitted model for every gene — TFvelo still cannot fit the dynamics of some genes well (Fig. S14), so genes not selected as best-fitted should not be force-analyzed

skills.description: Use when comparing unsupervised feature-selection methods on a differentiation trajectory and you have spliced/unspliced counts so ScVelo's dynamical model can produce a likelihood-ranked gene set.
skills.name: rna-velocity-dynamical-model-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-dynamical-model-gene-ranking Use when comparing unsupervised feature-selection methods on a differentiation trajectory and you have spliced/unspliced counts so ScVelo's dynamical model can produce a likelihood-ranked gene set. The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced count layers, which the ScVelo dynamical model requires The goal is not a method comparison but a single self-contained ranking, since this skill's value in the source workflow is as a velocity-based baseline against DELVE and HVG (top 500) feature sets Features are proteins from iterative immunofluorescence imaging, where spliced/unspliced RNA layers and velocity dynamics are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Ranks genes for a trajectory analysis using the RNA velocity dynamical model from ScVelo, producing a likelihood-based gene ranking that serves as a velocity-based feature-selection baseline. In the DELVE Nature Communications 2024 study it is benchmarked against DELVE and HVG selection on the hESC-to-definitive-endoderm differentiation dataset by counting lineage-specific transcription factors recovered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Ranks genes for a trajectory analysis using the RNA velocity dynamical model from ScVelo, producing a likelihood-based gene ranking that serves as a velocity-based feature-selection baseline. In the DELVE Nature Communications 2024 study it is benchmarked against DELVE and HVG selection on the hESC-to-definitive-endoderm differentiation dataset by counting lineage-specific transcription factors recovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks spliced/unspliced count layers, which the ScVelo dynamical model requires The goal is not a method comparison but a single self-contained ranking, since this skill's value in the source workflow is as a velocity-based baseline against DELVE and HVG (top 500) feature sets Features are proteins from iterative immunofluorescence imaging, where spliced/unspliced RNA layers and velocity dynamics are unavailable

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced counts (e.g. SMART-Seq2 U2OS cell cycle data) must be converted into velocity vectors and a cell-to-cell transition matrix to support directionality-aware trajectory reconstruction.
skills.name: rna-velocity-estimation
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-estimation Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced counts (e.g. SMART-Seq2 U2OS cell cycle data) must be converted into velocity vectors and a cell-to-cell transition matrix to support directionality-aware trajectory reconstruction. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or unrepresentative of true transcriptional dynamics (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this setting (e.g. fuzzy root cell probability in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) When the data lack spliced/unspliced count information required for velocity estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate RNA velocity fields (spliced/unspliced dynamics) from single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with scvelo, producing the velocity-informed transition probability matrix that Cytopath requires for simulation-based trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Estimate RNA velocity fields (spliced/unspliced dynamics) from single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with scvelo, producing the velocity-informed transition probability matrix that Cytopath requires for simulation-based trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty or unrepresentative of true transcriptional dynamics (e.g. time-dependent degradation rates), the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this setting (e.g. fuzzy root cell probability in the hepatocyte zonation dataset) When the data lack spliced/unspliced count information required for velocity estimation

skills.description: Use when you have spliced/unspliced count matrices (AnnData/h5ad) from differentiation datasets such as pancreas, dentate gyrus, retina, hindbrain, erythroid or bone marrow, and need directed cell transitions, latent time, or CBDir benchmarking against scVelo.
skills.name: rna-velocity-estimation
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-estimation Use when you have spliced/unspliced count matrices (AnnData/h5ad) from differentiation datasets such as pancreas, dentate gyrus, retina, hindbrain, erythroid or bone marrow, and need directed cell transitions, latent time, or CBDir benchmarking against scVelo. Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers (e.g., only normalized counts or a feature table) — velocity estimation requires unspliced reads Dataset exceeds ~50,000 cells on a GPU with 12GB memory and sub-sampling is not acceptable, since accuracy impact of sub-sampling is not yet evaluated You need unsupervised selection of dynamically informed genes for projecting cell transitions — the authors state this remains an open challenge http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate RNA velocity and inferred trajectory direction on single-cell spliced/unspliced data with UniTVelo, a TensorFlow 2 framework that models spliced/unspliced dynamics with radial-basis-function transcription rates and either a unified latent time across the transcriptome (FIT_OPTION='1') or gene-specific time (FIT_OPTION='2'), benchmarked against scVelo's stochastic and dynamical modes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7
skills.summary: Estimate RNA velocity and inferred trajectory direction on single-cell spliced/unspliced data with UniTVelo, a TensorFlow 2 framework that models spliced/unspliced dynamics with radial-basis-function transcription rates and either a unified latent time across the transcriptome (FIT_OPTION='1') or gene-specific time (FIT_OPTION='2'), benchmarked against scVelo's stochastic and dynamical modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers (e.g., only normalized counts or a feature table) — velocity estimation requires unspliced reads Dataset exceeds ~50,000 cells on a GPU with 12GB memory and sub-sampling is not acceptable, since accuracy impact of sub-sampling is not yet evaluated You need unsupervised selection of dynamically informed genes for projecting cell transitions — the authors state this remains an open challenge

skills.description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced count layers is available and the goal is to visualize predicted transcriptional trajectories as animated arrows/particles in a 3D embedding (e.g., PHATE/UMAP) inside CellexalVR.
skills.name: rna-velocity-estimation-spliced-unspliced
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-estimation-spliced-unspliced Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced count layers is available and the goal is to visualize predicted transcriptional trajectories as animated arrows/particles in a 3D embedding (e.g., PHATE/UMAP) inside CellexalVR. The input data lacks unspliced transcript counts, so spliced/unspliced velocity estimation cannot be performed The goal is static visualization of cell clusters rather than animated RNA velocity trajectories The target platform is not CellexalVR and cannot consume cellexalvrR-exported input files http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-cell RNA velocity from spliced/unspliced transcript counts (scvelo velocity graph) and exports paired origin/destination 3D coordinates so CellexalVR can render animated RNA velocity trajectories, as demonstrated on the Liver Cell Atlas PHATE reduction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Computes per-cell RNA velocity from spliced/unspliced transcript counts (scvelo velocity graph) and exports paired origin/destination 3D coordinates so CellexalVR can render animated RNA velocity trajectories, as demonstrated on the Liver Cell Atlas PHATE reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data lacks unspliced transcript counts, so spliced/unspliced velocity estimation cannot be performed The goal is static visualization of cell clusters rather than animated RNA velocity trajectories The target platform is not CellexalVR and cannot consume cellexalvrR-exported input files

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed AnnData with cell-type 'clusters' annotations and a scVelo RNA velocity field is available and you need per-cell fate probabilities or end-fate frequencies toward terminal states (e.g., E15.5 endocrine α, β, ε fates), or to benchmark against CellRank.
skills.name: rna-velocity-fate-probability-inference
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-fate-probability-inference Use when a pre-processed AnnData with cell-type 'clusters' annotations and a scVelo RNA velocity field is available and you need per-cell fate probabilities or end-fate frequencies toward terminal states (e.g., E15.5 endocrine α, β, ε fates), or to benchmark against CellRank. RNA velocity profiles are not robust for the dataset — the differentiation-potential mode requires prior biological knowledge that is difficult to provide in some cases, such as cancer studies The adata lacks cell-type 'clusters' annotations or defined terminal populations, which FateCompass requires as input The goal is TF activity estimation or differential motif activity (tf_activities.m, bootstrapping.m, differential_motif_activity_analysis.m) — those are downstream FateCompass steps, not RNA-velocity fate-probability inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers per-cell fate probabilities and end-fate frequencies by directing a discrete Markov chain on a k=10-neighbor UMAP-space graph of the Bastidas-Ponce E15.5 mouse pancreas data (3,696 cells) with scVelo RNA velocity, then sampling 2,000 stochastic differentiation trajectories from progenitors to terminal endocrine fates (α ~12.4%, β ~77%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Infers per-cell fate probabilities and end-fate frequencies by directing a discrete Markov chain on a k=10-neighbor UMAP-space graph of the Bastidas-Ponce E15.5 mouse pancreas data (3,696 cells) with scVelo RNA velocity, then sampling 2,000 stochastic differentiation trajectories from progenitors to terminal endocrine fates (α ~12.4%, β ~77%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: RNA velocity profiles are not robust for the dataset — the differentiation-potential mode requires prior biological knowledge that is difficult to provide in some cases, such as cancer studies The adata lacks cell-type 'clusters' annotations or defined terminal populations, which FateCompass requires as input The goal is TF activity estimation or differential motif activity (tf_activities.m, bootstrapping.m, differential_motif_activity_analysis.m) — those are downstream FateCompass steps, not RNA-velocity fate-probability inference

skills.description: Use when single-cell spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and you need velocity fields, latent trajectories, batch-corrected dynamics embeddings, or fate separation across multiple lineages where steady-state RNA velocity assumptions fail.
skills.name: rna-velocity-inference
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-inference Use when single-cell spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and you need velocity fields, latent trajectories, batch-corrected dynamics embeddings, or fate separation across multiple lineages where steady-state RNA velocity assumptions fail. Data lacks unspliced/spliced count layers (LatentVelo requires AnnData with both layers), e.g., only a processed expression matrix Goal is cell-type annotation or de novo clustering rather than dynamics — scANVI/scTour-style tools or clustering is more appropriate Dataset contains sparse cell clusters with few transient cells connecting trajectories, where inferred trajectories may incorrectly start from disconnected clusters (e.g., microglia in dentate gyrus) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer RNA velocity and cell developmental trajectories using LatentVelo, a variational autoencoder that embeds spliced/unspliced counts into a dynamics-based latent space and models differentiation with neural ODEs, including a latent regulatory state (zr) for lineage-dependent dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Infer RNA velocity and cell developmental trajectories using LatentVelo, a variational autoencoder that embeds spliced/unspliced counts into a dynamics-based latent space and models differentiation with neural ODEs, including a latent regulatory state (zr) for lineage-dependent dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks unspliced/spliced count layers (LatentVelo requires AnnData with both layers), e.g., only a processed expression matrix Goal is cell-type annotation or de novo clustering rather than dynamics — scANVI/scTour-style tools or clustering is more appropriate Dataset contains sparse cell clusters with few transient cells connecting trajectories, where inferred trajectories may incorrectly start from disconnected clusters (e.g., microglia in dentate gyrus)

skills.description: Use when preparing a kallisto/bustools index for RNA velocity or splicing-aware scRNA-seq quantification, so that pseudoalignment can separate spliced (cDNA) reads from unspliced (intronic) reads.
skills.name: rna-velocity-intron-transcript-extraction
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-intron-transcript-extraction Use when preparing a kallisto/bustools index for RNA velocity or splicing-aware scRNA-seq quantification, so that pseudoalignment can separate spliced (cDNA) reads from unspliced (intronic) reads. If the goal is only gene-level quantification without splicing dynamics or RNA velocity — a plain cDNA transcriptome index suffices and intron extraction is unnecessary overhead. If the genome is not available as a BSgenome object and cannot be converted; the protocol notes the required genome may not exist as a BSgenome object and users need to convert a customized genome. If alignment to a whole genome with splice-aware alignment (e.g. STAR-based) is required instead of transcriptome pseudoalignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Builds a kallisto pseudoalignment index that distinguishes spliced from unspliced reads by using BUSpaRse::get_velocity_files to extract intronic intervals from a GTF annotation (e.g. TAIR10) against a genome (BSgenome.Athaliana.TAIR.TAIR9), concatenating cDNA and intron sequences, and indexing the combined FASTA for scKB. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101729
skills.summary: Builds a kallisto pseudoalignment index that distinguishes spliced from unspliced reads by using BUSpaRse::get_velocity_files to extract intronic intervals from a GTF annotation (e.g. TAIR10) against a genome (BSgenome.Athaliana.TAIR.TAIR9), concatenating cDNA and intron sequences, and indexing the combined FASTA for scKB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is only gene-level quantification without splicing dynamics or RNA velocity — a plain cDNA transcriptome index suffices and intron extraction is unnecessary overhead. If the genome is not available as a BSgenome object and cannot be converted; the protocol notes the required genome may not exist as a BSgenome object and users need to convert a customized genome. If alignment to a whole genome with splice-aware alignment (e.g. STAR-based) is required instead of transcriptome pseudoalignment.

skills.description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and the goal is RNA velocity on multi-lineage, time-dependent, or multi-batch data where strict steady-state assumptions of Velocyto/scVelo fail, or when batch-integrated velocities and latent trajectories are needed.
skills.name: rna-velocity-latent-dynamics-modeling
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-latent-dynamics-modeling Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and the goal is RNA velocity on multi-lineage, time-dependent, or multi-batch data where strict steady-state assumptions of Velocyto/scVelo fail, or when batch-integrated velocities and latent trajectories are needed. Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers — LatentVelo requires AnnData with both count layers Cells form sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, or disconnected clusters (e.g., microglia in dentate gyrus) that absorb the assumed single initial state Stochastic dynamics or normalization must be explicitly modeled — these challenges are not addressed by the current latent ODE formulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate RNA velocity in a learned latent space using LatentVelo, which embeds cells with a variational autoencoder and models differentiation dynamics with neural ordinary differential equations, enabling batch correction, cell-type-annotated modeling, and latent trajectory inference on multi-lineage single-cell datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Estimate RNA velocity in a learned latent space using LatentVelo, which embeds cells with a variational autoencoder and models differentiation dynamics with neural ordinary differential equations, enabling batch correction, cell-type-annotated modeling, and latent trajectory inference on multi-lineage single-cell datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks spliced/unspliced layers — LatentVelo requires AnnData with both count layers Cells form sparse clusters with few observed transient cells connecting trajectories, or disconnected clusters (e.g., microglia in dentate gyrus) that absorb the assumed single initial state Stochastic dynamics or normalization must be explicitly modeled — these challenges are not addressed by the current latent ODE formulation

skills.description: Use when multi-batch single-cell transcriptomic data captures a continuous biological process (e.g., erythroid differentiation) and cells must be ordered in pseudo-time to validate that learned latent factors show distinct temporal profiles.
skills.name: rna-velocity-latent-time-inference
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-latent-time-inference Use when multi-batch single-cell transcriptomic data captures a continuous biological process (e.g., erythroid differentiation) and cells must be ordered in pseudo-time to validate that learned latent factors show distinct temporal profiles. When the goal is discrete cell-type clustering rather than continuous temporal dynamics — use JOINTLY's FindNeighbors/FindClusters (dims 1:15, res = 0.05) workflow instead of latent-time binning When data are complex multi-condition, multi-sample datasets where samples do not share the same axes of variation — the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY over consensus PCA, and latent-time interpretation presumes a continuous axis When no spliced/unspliced layers exist, since RNA-velocity latent time cannot be computed by scVelo http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers RNA-velocity-based latent time with scVelo on multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., 9815 mouse gastrulation erythropoiesis cells across three batches) to order cells along continuous differentiation, providing a continuous temporal axis against which interpretable JOINTLY factor activities can be profiled. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Infers RNA-velocity-based latent time with scVelo on multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., 9815 mouse gastrulation erythropoiesis cells across three batches) to order cells along continuous differentiation, providing a continuous temporal axis against which interpretable JOINTLY factor activities can be profiled.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is discrete cell-type clustering rather than continuous temporal dynamics — use JOINTLY's FindNeighbors/FindClusters (dims 1:15, res = 0.05) workflow instead of latent-time binning When data are complex multi-condition, multi-sample datasets where samples do not share the same axes of variation — the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY over consensus PCA, and latent-time interpretation presumes a continuous axis When no spliced/unspliced layers exist, since RNA-velocity latent time cannot be computed by scVelo

skills.description: Use when preparing an scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. adata_mESC.h5ad from Zenodo) that lacks imputed 'Ms'/'Mu' layers, as a mandatory step before running DeepCycle or any unspliced-spliced RNA velocity analysis.
skills.name: rna-velocity-moments-preprocessing
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-moments-preprocessing Use when preparing an scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. adata_mESC.h5ad from Zenodo) that lacks imputed 'Ms'/'Mu' layers, as a mandatory step before running DeepCycle or any unspliced-spliced RNA velocity analysis. The AnnData already contains imputed 'Ms' and 'Mu' layers (re-running moments would be redundant) The dataset has no velocyto-derived spliced/unspliced count layers, so moments imputation cannot be computed The downstream analysis does not rely on unspliced-spliced RNA velocity dynamics (e.g. standard expression clustering or marker analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocessing skill that runs scvelo's pp.moments on a velocyto-annotated AnnData to generate the imputed spliced ('Ms') and unspliced ('Mu') expression layers that DeepCycle requires as input for cell-cycle transcriptional phase inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Preprocessing skill that runs scvelo's pp.moments on a velocyto-annotated AnnData to generate the imputed spliced ('Ms') and unspliced ('Mu') expression layers that DeepCycle requires as input for cell-cycle transcriptional phase inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData already contains imputed 'Ms' and 'Mu' layers (re-running moments would be redundant) The dataset has no velocyto-derived spliced/unspliced count layers, so moments imputation cannot be computed The downstream analysis does not rely on unspliced-spliced RNA velocity dynamics (e.g. standard expression clustering or marker analysis)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data has pre-computed RNA velocity (scvelo/velocyto), root and terminal cell states are identifiable or supplied, and per-lineage pseudotime must be inferred and validated against a known cell type ordering.
skills.name: rna-velocity-pseudotime-estimation
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-pseudotime-estimation Use when scRNA-seq data has pre-computed RNA velocity (scvelo/velocyto), root and terminal cell states are identifiable or supplied, and per-lineage pseudotime must be inferred and validated against a known cell type ordering. When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — spurious root/terminal inference was observed on the erythroid gastrulation dataset and on scvelo-simulated data with time-dependent degradation rates When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (authors explicitly do not recommend trajectory inference with Cytopath in this case), e.g. fuzzy root probabilities in the hepatocyte zonation dataset When a method with topology-specific assumptions is required instead of independent per-trajectory modelling — Cytopath places no tree/cycle constraints, and Slingshot/Monocle3 are the baselines for tree-like/graph topologies http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate per-cell pseudotime by defining a Markov chain model from RNA velocity, simulating an ensemble of differentiation trajectories (Cytopath), aligning them via dynamic time warping, and assigning cells to trajectory steps; pseudotime quality is judged by Spearman correlation with known cell type ordering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Estimate per-cell pseudotime by defining a Markov chain model from RNA velocity, simulating an ensemble of differentiation trajectories (Cytopath), aligning them via dynamic time warping, and assigning cells to trajectory steps; pseudotime quality is judged by Spearman correlation with known cell type ordering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — spurious root/terminal inference was observed on the erythroid gastrulation dataset and on scvelo-simulated data with time-dependent degradation rates When root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (authors explicitly do not recommend trajectory inference with Cytopath in this case), e.g. fuzzy root probabilities in the hepatocyte zonation dataset When a method with topology-specific assumptions is required instead of independent per-trajectory modelling — Cytopath places no tree/cycle constraints, and Slingshot/Monocle3 are the baselines for tree-like/graph topologies

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq AnnData object with spliced counts and scVelo-derived RNA velocity must be denoised into meta-cell-level smoothed velocities as input for trajectory inference.
skills.name: rna-velocity-smoothing
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-smoothing Use when an scRNA-seq AnnData object with spliced counts and scVelo-derived RNA velocity must be denoised into meta-cell-level smoothed velocities as input for trajectory inference. The goal is cell-level rather than meta-cell-level velocities, or no RNA velocity (spliced/unspliced) information is available for the dataset The task is downstream of smoothing (kNN graph construction, path finding, or pseudotime assignment) — use the later CellPath steps such as all_in_one instead Single-cell counts are extremely sparse for direct velocity estimation and no unspliced reads exist; scVelo velocity inference itself may be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CellPath's first pipeline step: cluster single cells into meta-cells and fit a Gaussian-RBF kernel regression regressing meta-cell-aggregated RNA velocity on averaged spliced expression, yielding noise-reduced per-meta-cell smoothed velocity vectors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: CellPath's first pipeline step: cluster single cells into meta-cells and fit a Gaussian-RBF kernel regression regressing meta-cell-aggregated RNA velocity on averaged spliced expression, yielding noise-reduced per-meta-cell smoothed velocity vectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell-level rather than meta-cell-level velocities, or no RNA velocity (spliced/unspliced) information is available for the dataset The task is downstream of smoothing (kNN graph construction, path finding, or pseudotime assignment) — use the later CellPath steps such as all_in_one instead Single-cell counts are extremely sparse for direct velocity estimation and no unspliced reads exist; scVelo velocity inference itself may be unreliable

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData object (with spliced/unspliced counts) needs trajectory inference: recovering parallel branches, within-population sub-flows, and cell pseudotime that direction-free TI methods (e.g., Slingshot) or velocity tools that lack path output (e.g., CellRank) cannot resolve.
skills.name: rna-velocity-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: rna-velocity-trajectory-inference Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData object (with spliced/unspliced counts) needs trajectory inference: recovering parallel branches, within-population sub-flows, and cell pseudotime that direction-free TI methods (e.g., Slingshot) or velocity tools that lack path output (e.g., CellRank) cannot resolve. The task requires only initial/terminal states or probabilistic fate maps without explicit trajectories — CellRank may suffice since CellPath is designed to output paths and pseudotime Only cluster-level trajectory resolution is needed and a compact backbone graph is acceptable — Directed-PAGA provides this without meta-cell construction No spliced/unspliced or velocity information is available and direction inference cannot be supported, since CellPath relies on RNA velocity to orient trajectories http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Infer multiple high-resolution cell trajectories and per-cell pseudotime by integrating scRNA-seq count matrices with RNA velocity matrices using CellPath, which constructs meta-cells, builds kNN graphs, and greedily selects major trajectories without constraints on trajectory topology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Infer multiple high-resolution cell trajectories and per-cell pseudotime by integrating scRNA-seq count matrices with RNA velocity matrices using CellPath, which constructs meta-cells, builds kNN graphs, and greedily selects major trajectories without constraints on trajectory topology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires only initial/terminal states or probabilistic fate maps without explicit trajectories — CellRank may suffice since CellPath is designed to output paths and pseudotime Only cluster-level trajectory resolution is needed and a compact backbone graph is acceptable — Directed-PAGA provides this without meta-cell construction No spliced/unspliced or velocity information is available and direction inference cannot be supported, since CellPath relies on RNA velocity to orient trajectories

skills.summary: Constructs a cell-to-cell transition probability matrix from RNA velocity fields (processed with scvelo) of spliced/unspliced single-cell RNA-seq data, which serves as the Markov chain model backbone for Cytopath's simulation-based trajectory inference.

skills.description: Use when a cells-by-variants VAF matrix from scRNA-seq variant calling contains NA/missing entries and you need to quantify how much missingness is attributable to type I drop-out before lineage reconstruction or quality assessment.
skills.name: rnaseq-dropout-characterization
skills.search_text: rnaseq-dropout-characterization Use when a cells-by-variants VAF matrix from scRNA-seq variant calling contains NA/missing entries and you need to quantify how much missingness is attributable to type I drop-out before lineage reconstruction or quality assessment. Input is not a single-cell VAF/variant matrix — e.g. bulk somatic variant calls or gene expression counts with no per-variant missingness structure. The goal is to impute or correct drop-outs via lineage-aware modeling (use SClineager's run_sclineager instead) rather than to characterize their prevalence. Missingness in the matrix encodes true homozygous reference calls rather than unobserved/low-coverage positions; counting all NAs would then overstate type I drop-out. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies type I expressional drop-out (missing variant observations from low expression / shallow coverage) in single-cell variant allele frequency matrices, per variant, per cell, and overall. This characterizes the magnitude of missingness that motivates coverage-aware lineage inference methods such as SClineager. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108589
skills.summary: Quantifies type I expressional drop-out (missing variant observations from low expression / shallow coverage) in single-cell variant allele frequency matrices, per variant, per cell, and overall. This characterizes the magnitude of missingness that motivates coverage-aware lineage inference methods such as SClineager.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a single-cell VAF/variant matrix — e.g. bulk somatic variant calls or gene expression counts with no per-variant missingness structure. The goal is to impute or correct drop-outs via lineage-aware modeling (use SClineager's run_sclineager instead) rather than to characterize their prevalence. Missingness in the matrix encodes true homozygous reference calls rather than unobserved/low-coverage positions; counting all NAs would then overstate type I drop-out.

skills.search_text: rnaseq-expression-median-cutoff-filtering Use when starting from a raw RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. >16,000 genes from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-11611) and low-abundance genes must be dropped by a median-expression cut-off before fitting models such as nestcv.glmnet. Supervised feature selection is intended — filtering on the whole dataset creates bias when determining model accuracy (Vabalas et al, 2019); use nestedcv filter functions inside the outer loop instead. The input is already a reduced feature table or the model is not high-dimensional (P >> n), where a median-abundance cutoff is unnecessary. The data are not RNA-seq expression measurements (e.g. Sonar, BostonHousing2, iris predictors), where abundance-based gene filtering does not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pre-processing skill that removes low-abundance genes from an RNA-seq expression matrix by applying a median-expression cut-off across samples, as done in the nestedcv vignette on the R4RA rheumatoid arthritis RNA-seq dataset (E-MTAB-11611) before nested cross-validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad048

skills.search_text: rnaseq-index-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a pre-filter such as Raptor can replace or complement an exact index like Mantis for membership queries of transcripts/reads against thousands of SRA RNA-Seq experiments, with resource and FPR metrics. skills.summary: Benchmarks approximate sequence-search indices (Raptor binning directories vs Mantis) on a large human RNA-Seq experiment collection, comparing construction time/RAM/space and query speed, memory, and false-positive rate for transcript membership searches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input collection is a small set of genomes or a clustered RefSeq dataset with few bins — the paper's limiting factors are 'uneven bin sizes as well as a high number of bins', so tiny collections do not exercise the pre-filter's advantages Edit-distance-tolerant full-text alignment results are required rather than approximate set-membership pre-filtering — Raptor is a pre-filter, not a mapper like DREAM-Yara The index was built with an older Raptor release and queried with version 2.0.0 — indices are not cross-version compatible
