skills.name: rnaseq-time-series-network-benchmarking
skills.search_text: rnaseq-time-series-network-benchmarking Use when comparing gene regulatory network inference methods on a time-series RNA-Seq dataset with a known gold-standard GRN, requiring sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and runtime metrics per tool. The goal is single-cell RNA-Seq network inference — tools like Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, and Arboreto are designed for scRNA-Seq, and this benchmark targets bulk whole-genome time-series data No gold standard or annotated genome is available — refinement steps require additional knowledge of a genome (promoter sequences, GenBank annotation) and validation requires known positive/negative interactions The task is Boolean Network inference/model simulation rather than comparative GRN inference benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark workflow for evaluating GRN inference tools (Augusta with/without TFBM/database refinement, GENIE3, TDAracne, KBoost) on a whole-genome RNA-Seq time-series dataset, scoring predictions against a gold standard with a multiclass (positive/negative/absent) confusion matrix plus runtime measurement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2024.01.013
skills.summary: Benchmark workflow for evaluating GRN inference tools (Augusta with/without TFBM/database refinement, GENIE3, TDAracne, KBoost) on a whole-genome RNA-Seq time-series dataset, scoring predictions against a gold standard with a multiclass (positive/negative/absent) confusion matrix plus runtime measurement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-cell RNA-Seq network inference — tools like Inferelator 3.0, GRNBoost2, and Arboreto are designed for scRNA-Seq, and this benchmark targets bulk whole-genome time-series data No gold standard or annotated genome is available — refinement steps require additional knowledge of a genome (promoter sequences, GenBank annotation) and validation requires known positive/negative interactions The task is Boolean Network inference/model simulation rather than comparative GRN inference benchmarking

skills.description: Use when a sorted, genome-aligned RNA-Seq BAM (e.g. HISAT2 + SAMtools) and a StringTie-reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need de novo polyA site prediction and 3' end refinement without direct 3'-end sequencing.
skills.name: rnaseq-transcript-3prime-end-refinement
skills.search_text: rnaseq-transcript-3prime-end-refinement Use when a sorted, genome-aligned RNA-Seq BAM (e.g. HISAT2 + SAMtools) and a StringTie-reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need de novo polyA site prediction and 3' end refinement without direct 3'-end sequencing. Goal is detecting coding (upstream-exon) alternative polyadenylation: aptardi evaluates only 3' terminal exons, eliminating the possibility of identifying coding APA. The pre-built 100-base-bin model must be reused but predictions at finer resolution than 100 bases are required, since aptardi annotates the 3'-most base of a positive 100-base bin. The analysis targets taxa outside mammals: the manually engineered DNA sequence features may not apply outside of mammals. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 Refines transcript 3'-ends and identifies expressed polyadenylation (polyA) sites in a sample-specific transcriptome using aptardi, a supervised machine-learning approach that combines RNA-Seq read coverage with DNA sequence. Outputs a modified GTF/GFF that adds aptardi transcripts on top of the unmodified input transcriptome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Refines transcript 3'-ends and identifies expressed polyadenylation (polyA) sites in a sample-specific transcriptome using aptardi, a supervised machine-learning approach that combines RNA-Seq read coverage with DNA sequence. Outputs a modified GTF/GFF that adds aptardi transcripts on top of the unmodified input transcriptome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is detecting coding (upstream-exon) alternative polyadenylation: aptardi evaluates only 3' terminal exons, eliminating the possibility of identifying coding APA. The pre-built 100-base-bin model must be reused but predictions at finer resolution than 100 bases are required, since aptardi annotates the 3'-most base of a positive 100-base bin. The analysis targets taxa outside mammals: the manually engineered DNA sequence features may not apply outside of mammals.

skills.description: Use when a GTF transcriptome (e.g., from StringTie plus aptardi) contains many candidate transcript isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and needs expression-based filtering before quantitation and differential analysis.
skills.name: rnaseq-transcript-quantitation-and-count-filtering
skills.search_text: rnaseq-transcript-quantitation-and-count-filtering Use when a GTF transcriptome (e.g., from StringTie plus aptardi) contains many candidate transcript isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and needs expression-based filtering before quantitation and differential analysis. When working with a single sample or few samples where the 2/3-samples rule is undefined — a simple expression threshold may be more appropriate, and the cutoff depends on the dataset. When the input transcriptome is already curated and lacks many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons — the README's redundancy rationale for filtering does not apply. When the goal is differential 3' UTR usage analysis requiring all aptardi-added transcripts retained without count-based removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantitate a transcriptome (e.g., an aptardi-modified GTF) with RSEM and then generate a high-quality transcriptome by removing transcripts without at least 1 count in 2/3 of samples. This filtering step removes redundant/false-positive aptardi transcripts before downstream differential expression analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Quantitate a transcriptome (e.g., an aptardi-modified GTF) with RSEM and then generate a high-quality transcriptome by removing transcripts without at least 1 count in 2/3 of samples. This filtering step removes redundant/false-positive aptardi transcripts before downstream differential expression analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When working with a single sample or few samples where the 2/3-samples rule is undefined — a simple expression threshold may be more appropriate, and the cutoff depends on the dataset. When the input transcriptome is already curated and lacks many isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons — the README's redundancy rationale for filtering does not apply. When the goal is differential 3' UTR usage analysis requiring all aptardi-added transcripts retained without count-based removal.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq-derived VCFs need validation against genotype array data (e.g., Axiom SNP array VCF from GSE131764) to confirm variant-calling fidelity before ASE or downstream analyses.
skills.name: rnaseq-variant-call-validation
skills.search_text: rnaseq-variant-call-validation Use when RNA-seq-derived VCFs need validation against genotype array data (e.g., Axiom SNP array VCF from GSE131764) to confirm variant-calling fidelity before ASE or downstream analyses. Input variant calls were not produced by GATK HaplotypeCaller — the README warns VCFs from other callers may have format incompatibilities with Compare_VCF_Files/VADT There is no independent genotyping dataset overlapping the RNA-seq samples, so no self-by-self vs random-pairing contrast can be computed The goal is ASE detection itself rather than variant-call QC — use VADT's binomial test pipeline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validate RNA-seq variant calls (from GATK HaplotypeCaller, g.vcf workflow) by comparing per-sample genotypes against an independent genotyping platform (Axiom 600K chicken array VCF) using Compare_VCF_Files, reporting self-by-self vs randomly-paired concordance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Validate RNA-seq variant calls (from GATK HaplotypeCaller, g.vcf workflow) by comparing per-sample genotypes against an independent genotyping platform (Axiom 600K chicken array VCF) using Compare_VCF_Files, reporting self-by-self vs randomly-paired concordance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input variant calls were not produced by GATK HaplotypeCaller — the README warns VCFs from other callers may have format incompatibilities with Compare_VCF_Files/VADT There is no independent genotyping dataset overlapping the RNA-seq samples, so no self-by-self vs random-pairing contrast can be computed The goal is ASE detection itself rather than variant-call QC — use VADT's binomial test pipeline instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating inferred lineage/cell division trees (e.g., from LinRace, DCLEAR, Cassiopeia, Startle, LinTIMaT, or NJ-on-Hamming baselines) against a known ground-truth tree across simulation conditions such as mutation rate or dropout.
skills.name: robinson-foulds-tree-distance-comparison
skills.search_text: robinson-foulds-tree-distance-comparison Use when evaluating inferred lineage/cell division trees (e.g., from LinRace, DCLEAR, Cassiopeia, Startle, LinTIMaT, or NJ-on-Hamming baselines) against a known ground-truth tree across simulation conditions such as mutation rate or dropout. No ground-truth or reference tree is available (e.g., purely exploratory real-data trees like the zebrafish scGESTALT ZF1-F3 reconstruction) — use Nye similarity between method pairs or qualitative subtree inspection instead of RF-vs-truth scoring Trees being compared have different leaf sets (cell label mismatch) — RF.dist requires corresponding taxa, so relabel/intersect leaves first You need branch-length-aware or ancestral-state agreement measures; RF/Nye/CID capture only topology split agreement, not inferred ancestral cell states http://edamontology.org/topic_3293 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark lineage-reconstruction methods by scoring each inferred cell division tree against the ground-truth tree using normalized Robinson-Foulds distance (ape::RF.dist, normalize=TRUE), complemented by normalized Nye similarity (TreeDist::NyeSimilarity) and CID, as done in the LinRace paper to compare LinRace against DCLEAR, Cassiopeia, LinTIMaT, Startle, and a barcode-only NJ baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Benchmark lineage-reconstruction methods by scoring each inferred cell division tree against the ground-truth tree using normalized Robinson-Foulds distance (ape::RF.dist, normalize=TRUE), complemented by normalized Nye similarity (TreeDist::NyeSimilarity) and CID, as done in the LinRace paper to compare LinRace against DCLEAR, Cassiopeia, LinTIMaT, Startle, and a barcode-only NJ baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth or reference tree is available (e.g., purely exploratory real-data trees like the zebrafish scGESTALT ZF1-F3 reconstruction) — use Nye similarity between method pairs or qualitative subtree inspection instead of RF-vs-truth scoring Trees being compared have different leaf sets (cell label mismatch) — RF.dist requires corresponding taxa, so relabel/intersect leaves first You need branch-length-aware or ancestral-state agreement measures; RF/Nye/CID capture only topology split agreement, not inferred ancestral cell states

skills.description: Use when a sample-level trajectory (pseudotime from Wasserstein distances + diffusion maps + EIPLGraph) has been estimated on single-cell data (AnnData .h5ad) and you must rank which cell populations and genes change significantly along that trajectory.
skills.name: robust-huber-regression-cell-proportion-testing
skills.search_text: robust-huber-regression-cell-proportion-testing Use when a sample-level trajectory (pseudotime from Wasserstein distances + diffusion maps + EIPLGraph) has been estimated on single-cell data (AnnData .h5ad) and you must rank which cell populations and genes change significantly along that trajectory. Input is already an aggregated feature/marker table — this skill requires raw cell-level AnnData with sample and cluster labels to recompute proportions and fits The goal is comparing two samples pairwise or differential expression between discrete disease groups rather than testing features along an ordered progression trajectory Data are pathomics/structure-level without cell-cluster proportion annotations, so cell_importance's per-cluster proportion fits are undefined without adaptation PILOT's statistical layer for interpreting disease-progression trajectories: step-wise Huber regression (linear, quadratic, linear-quadratic terms) fits each cell cluster's proportion (and each gene's expression) against EIPLGraph pseudotime, and Wald statistics test whether fitted curves differ between a target cluster and all other clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: PILOT's statistical layer for interpreting disease-progression trajectories: step-wise Huber regression (linear, quadratic, linear-quadratic terms) fits each cell cluster's proportion (and each gene's expression) against EIPLGraph pseudotime, and Wald statistics test whether fitted curves differ between a target cluster and all other clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated feature/marker table — this skill requires raw cell-level AnnData with sample and cluster labels to recompute proportions and fits The goal is comparing two samples pairwise or differential expression between discrete disease groups rather than testing features along an ordered progression trajectory Data are pathomics/structure-level without cell-cluster proportion annotations, so cell_importance's per-cluster proportion fits are undefined without adaptation

skills.description: Use when building a final ranked marker list per cell type from reference scRNA-seq data where individual DE tests vary in their ability to predict cell types and a single consensus ranking is needed.
skills.name: robust-rank-aggregation-of-marker-lists
skills.search_text: robust-rank-aggregation-of-marker-lists Use when building a final ranked marker list per cell type from reference scRNA-seq data where individual DE tests vary in their ability to predict cell types and a single consensus ranking is needed. The reference AnnData lacks cell-type labels ('cell_type'), since per-cluster DE ranking cannot be computed The query data contains cell types unseen in the reference — MASI (and thus its aggregated markers) cannot annotate unseen types and must be combined with SCCAF for subtype discovery You already have a validated, curated marker gene list per cell type and do not need to re-derive rankings from DE tests http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a consensus ranked cell-type marker list by aggregating the outputs of multiple differential expression tests with robust rank aggregation (RRA), with an alternative Lancaster p-value combination (marker_identification_LC), as used in MASI to build reference markers for label transfer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Constructs a consensus ranked cell-type marker list by aggregating the outputs of multiple differential expression tests with robust rank aggregation (RRA), with an alternative Lancaster p-value combination (marker_identification_LC), as used in MASI to build reference markers for label transfer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference AnnData lacks cell-type labels ('cell_type'), since per-cluster DE ranking cannot be computed The query data contains cell types unseen in the reference — MASI (and thus its aggregated markers) cannot annotate unseen types and must be combined with SCCAF for subtype discovery You already have a validated, curated marker gene list per cell type and do not need to re-derive rankings from DE tests

skills.description: Use when testing whether a gene-gene correlation differs between phenotypic subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) in normalized RNA-seq count data, and per-link differential p-values are needed.
skills.name: robust-regression-interaction-testing
skills.search_text: robust-regression-interaction-testing Use when testing whether a gene-gene correlation differs between phenotypic subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) in normalized RNA-seq count data, and per-link differential p-values are needed. When comparing more than two groups with the robust-regression path — switch to the one-way ANOVA variant instead When the input is raw (unnormalized) count data or multi-omic assays — the successor multiDEGGs package with get_diffNetworks is the maintained route When metadata and count matrix columns/rows are not sample-aligned (identical(colnames, rownames) fails) — correct alignment first http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Assess the differential significance of each gene-gene link across sample subgroups by fitting robust linear regression with a Gene*Group interaction term (one-way ANOVA when >2 groups) and extracting the F-test p-value on the interaction, as implemented in the DEGGs package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad192
skills.summary: Assess the differential significance of each gene-gene link across sample subgroups by fitting robust linear regression with a Gene*Group interaction term (one-way ANOVA when >2 groups) and extracting the F-test p-value on the interaction, as implemented in the DEGGs package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing more than two groups with the robust-regression path — switch to the one-way ANOVA variant instead When the input is raw (unnormalized) count data or multi-omic assays — the successor multiDEGGs package with get_diffNetworks is the maintained route When metadata and count matrix columns/rows are not sample-aligned (identical(colnames, rownames) fails) — correct alignment first

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more independent 10X replicates (e.g., matrix.mtx/gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) must be resolved into high-resolution cell subpopulations with a shuffled-data false-discovery control, and reproducible clusters must be matched across replicates.
skills.name: robust-subpopulation-identification-across-replicates
skills.search_text: robust-subpopulation-identification-across-replicates Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more independent 10X replicates (e.g., matrix.mtx/gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) must be resolved into high-resolution cell subpopulations with a shuffled-data false-discovery control, and reproducible clusters must be matched across replicates. Input is not raw 10X scRNA-seq count data (e.g., already clustered feature tables or bulk RNA-seq) — read.data expects 10X format and the pipeline performs its own quality filtering Only a single replicate with no plan to assess cross-replicate cluster reproducibility via correlation — the robustness/similarity step requires multiple independently clustered datasets Compute environment without slurm or at least 8G of memory when running parallel shuffled-data simulations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify robust cell subpopulations from scRNA-seq data with the robustSingleCell pipeline, controlling false discovery of clusters by repeating Phenograph clustering over shuffled data, then integrating replicate datasets (e.g., LCMV1/LCMV2) via cross-replicate cluster correlation similarity analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: Identify robust cell subpopulations from scRNA-seq data with the robustSingleCell pipeline, controlling false discovery of clusters by repeating Phenograph clustering over shuffled data, then integrating replicate datasets (e.g., LCMV1/LCMV2) via cross-replicate cluster correlation similarity analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw 10X scRNA-seq count data (e.g., already clustered feature tables or bulk RNA-seq) — read.data expects 10X format and the pipeline performs its own quality filtering Only a single replicate with no plan to assess cross-replicate cluster reproducibility via correlation — the robustness/similarity step requires multiple independently clustered datasets Compute environment without slurm or at least 8G of memory when running parallel shuffled-data simulations

skills.description: Use when stress-testing a trajectory-alignment method's robustness: synthetic single-cell trajectory pairs are available and the goal is to measure how alignment distance and conservation scores change as noise standard deviation increases.
skills.name: robustness-benchmark-visualization
skills.search_text: robustness-benchmark-visualization Use when stress-testing a trajectory-alignment method's robustness: synthetic single-cell trajectory pairs are available and the goal is to measure how alignment distance and conservation scores change as noise standard deviation increases. The input datasets have different global topological structures — the paper reports CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in that benchmarking setting, so noise-robustness curves would not transfer. The trajectory data contain complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs rather than trees, which CAPITAL in its present form cannot handle. The goal is data integration of cell subpopulations (e.g., Scanorama/Seurat-style anchor transformation) rather than scoring trajectory-tree alignment robustness. http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 A benchmarking skill that quantifies how CAPITAL's trajectory-tree alignment quality degrades under graded Gaussian noise on synthetic single-cell trajectory pairs, using the normalized alignment distance and ATC score as robustness metrics (Fig. 3a-b). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that quantifies how CAPITAL's trajectory-tree alignment quality degrades under graded Gaussian noise on synthetic single-cell trajectory pairs, using the normalized alignment distance and ATC score as robustness metrics (Fig. 3a-b).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input datasets have different global topological structures — the paper reports CAPITAL's alignment accuracy degraded in that benchmarking setting, so noise-robustness curves would not transfer. The trajectory data contain complex graphs such as cycles or disconnected graphs rather than trees, which CAPITAL in its present form cannot handle. The goal is data integration of cell subpopulations (e.g., Scanorama/Seurat-style anchor transformation) rather than scoring trajectory-tree alignment robustness.

skills.description: Use when a GRN-inference or network-based method consumes a prior gene interaction network and you must quantify how much method performance degrades when that prior is partially randomized or noisy.
skills.name: robustness-sensitivity-analysis-of-prior-knowledge-networks
skills.search_text: robustness-sensitivity-analysis-of-prior-knowledge-networks Use when a GRN-inference or network-based method consumes a prior gene interaction network and you must quantify how much method performance degrades when that prior is partially randomized or noisy. The prior network is not required by the method, or method performance cannot be reduced to a scalar metric comparable across perturbed and unperturbed runs The goal is to test sensitivity to input scRNA-seq data or hyperparameters rather than to perturbations of the prior interaction network itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how sensitive a downstream method's performance (e.g., CEFCON's GRN AUPRC) is to perturbations of its input prior gene interaction network, by randomly shuffling a fixed fraction (e.g., 20%) of edges and comparing performance against the unperturbed baseline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Quantifies how sensitive a downstream method's performance (e.g., CEFCON's GRN AUPRC) is to perturbations of its input prior gene interaction network, by randomly shuffling a fixed fraction (e.g., 20%) of edges and comparing performance against the unperturbed baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The prior network is not required by the method, or method performance cannot be reduced to a scalar metric comparable across perturbed and unperturbed runs The goal is to test sensitivity to input scRNA-seq data or hyperparameters rather than to perturbations of the prior interaction network itself

skills.description: Use when you have a continuous per-cell score (e.g. signalling entropy rate) and binary or continuous ground-truth labels (pluripotent vs progenitor, or a pluripotency score) and need to quantify discriminative performance.
skills.name: roc-and-correlation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: roc-and-correlation-benchmarking Use when you have a continuous per-cell score (e.g. signalling entropy rate) and binary or continuous ground-truth labels (pluripotent vs progenitor, or a pluripotency score) and need to quantify discriminative performance. The input is already a feature/engineered table and no per-cell score needs external validation — benchmarking is redundant. Cells lack ground-truth labels or pluripotency annotations, making ROC and correlation against truth impossible. The goal is pseudo-temporal ordering of cells within a lineage rather than benchmarking discriminative accuracy of a potency score. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark a per-cell potency score such as signalling entropy (SCENT SR) against ground-truth class labels by computing Spearman correlation with a pluripotency score and ROC AUC for pluripotent-vs-non-pluripotent discrimination. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Benchmark a per-cell potency score such as signalling entropy (SCENT SR) against ground-truth class labels by computing Spearman correlation with a pluripotency score and ROC AUC for pluripotent-vs-non-pluripotent discrimination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/engineered table and no per-cell score needs external validation — benchmarking is redundant. Cells lack ground-truth labels or pluripotency annotations, making ROC and correlation against truth impossible. The goal is pseudo-temporal ordering of cells within a lineage rather than benchmarking discriminative accuracy of a potency score.

skills.description: Use when ranking competing statistical detection methods on simulated count data with known positives, by comparing ROC AUC and TPR at a fixed 5% FPR across methods.
skills.name: roc-auc-and-tpr-method-comparison
skills.search_text: roc-auc-and-tpr-method-comparison Use when ranking competing statistical detection methods on simulated count data with known positives, by comparing ROC AUC and TPR at a fixed 5% FPR across methods. Real RNA-seq data without simulated ground truth — ROC AUC and TPR at 5% FPR require known positive ASAS events, which real datasets lack Replicate numbers or variance settings far from the benchmark conditions — the reported ranking (AUC 84% vs 74%/68%/63%/60%) was established specifically for M=3 replicates and low variance Competing methods that do not emit per-event p values or scores that can be thresholded into an ROC curve http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking method that ranks ASAS/differential-splicing detection approaches by simulating exon-skipping count data (5,000 events, M=3 replicates) and comparing ROC AUC and true positive rate at a fixed 5% FPR across PAIRADISE and four competing statistical tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: A benchmarking method that ranks ASAS/differential-splicing detection approaches by simulating exon-skipping count data (5,000 events, M=3 replicates) and comparing ROC AUC and true positive rate at a fixed 5% FPR across PAIRADISE and four competing statistical tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real RNA-seq data without simulated ground truth — ROC AUC and TPR at 5% FPR require known positive ASAS events, which real datasets lack Replicate numbers or variance settings far from the benchmark conditions — the reported ranking (AUC 84% vs 74%/68%/63%/60%) was established specifically for M=3 replicates and low variance Competing methods that do not emit per-event p values or scores that can be thresholded into an ROC curve

skills.description: Use when simulated single-cell datasets with ground-truth covariate-pseudotime interaction labels are available and you must compare interaction-detection accuracy (AUC) of PhenoPath vs DE-based methods across varying fractions of interacting genes.
skills.name: roc-auc-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: roc-auc-benchmark-evaluation Use when simulated single-cell datasets with ground-truth covariate-pseudotime interaction labels are available and you must compare interaction-detection accuracy (AUC) of PhenoPath vs DE-based methods across varying fractions of interacting genes. Input is real experimental data without simulated ground-truth interaction labels — no ROC/AUC can be computed The analysis goal is pseudotime/covariate inference itself rather than benchmarking detection accuracy of competing methods Features are assumed to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks PhenoPath's covariate-trajectory interaction detection against differential-expression workflows (limma-voom, DESeq2, MAST, Monocle 2) by ranking genes per method and computing ROC curves/AUC on simulated data with known interaction labels, reproducing Fig 1f. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks PhenoPath's covariate-trajectory interaction detection against differential-expression workflows (limma-voom, DESeq2, MAST, Monocle 2) by ranking genes per method and computing ROC curves/AUC on simulated data with known interaction labels, reproducing Fig 1f.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental data without simulated ground-truth interaction labels — no ROC/AUC can be computed The analysis goal is pseudotime/covariate inference itself rather than benchmarking detection accuracy of competing methods Features are assumed to evolve nonlinearly with pseudotime, since PhenoPath assumes features evolve linearly with respect to pseudotime

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a splicing-status predictor (e.g., Forseti splice_prob) with ROC AUC against trivial baselines on scRNA-seq reads carrying ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels.
skills.name: roc-auc-computation
skills.search_text: roc-auc-computation Use when benchmarking a splicing-status predictor (e.g., Forseti splice_prob) with ROC AUC against trivial baselines on scRNA-seq reads carrying ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels. When the goal is to run or evaluate Forseti's own prediction model rather than compare it against trivial predictors — use the forseti_predictor workflow and the forseti-experiments Nextflow evaluation step instead When reads lack ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels (e.g., ambiguous 'A' reads with no verified status), since AUC cannot be computed without labels When probability calibration rather than ranking quality is the question — AUC is rank-based and cannot assess calibration of splice_prob values http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute ROC AUC for splicing-status prediction of scRNA-seq reads on a labeled evaluation set of uniquely mapped reads, including the trivial 'All spliced', 'All unspliced', and 'All random' baselines that floor at AUC = 0.5 (as in Forseti's Fig. 3 comparison). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Compute ROC AUC for splicing-status prediction of scRNA-seq reads on a labeled evaluation set of uniquely mapped reads, including the trivial 'All spliced', 'All unspliced', and 'All random' baselines that floor at AUC = 0.5 (as in Forseti's Fig. 3 comparison).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to run or evaluate Forseti's own prediction model rather than compare it against trivial predictors — use the forseti_predictor workflow and the forseti-experiments Nextflow evaluation step instead When reads lack ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels (e.g., ambiguous 'A' reads with no verified status), since AUC cannot be computed without labels When probability calibration rather than ranking quality is the question — AUC is rank-based and cannot assess calibration of splice_prob values

skills.description: Reference for quantifying and comparing CNA-detection accuracy of scRNA-seq copy-number callers via ROC-AUC against single-cell DNA-seq ground truth, as done for XClone on the 4416-cell 2R astrocytoma minor clone.
skills.name: roc-auc-computation-for-copy-number-detection
skills.search_text: roc-auc-computation-for-copy-number-detection Reference for quantifying and comparing CNA-detection accuracy of scRNA-seq copy-number callers via ROC-AUC against single-cell DNA-seq ground truth, as done for XClone on the 4416-cell 2R astrocytoma minor clone. The input is bulk DNA-seq or bulk RNA-seq copy-number data rather than single-cell transcriptomic matrices with allelic AD/DP information No single-cell DNA ground truth (e.g. scOne-seq clone profile) is available, so ROC-AUC scoring cannot be performed The dataset lacks heterozygous SNP coverage, making the BAF module and allele-specific benchmarks inapplicable (RDR-only evaluation would be required) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking protocol that scores per-cell copy gain/loss calls from XClone (RDR+BAF modules) and competing CNA callers (CaSpER, Numbat, InferCNV, CopyKAT) against scOne-seq single-cell DNA copy-number profiles, then computes ROC-AUC per method on the astrocytoma 2R clone 1 snRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol that scores per-cell copy gain/loss calls from XClone (RDR+BAF modules) and competing CNA callers (CaSpER, Numbat, InferCNV, CopyKAT) against scOne-seq single-cell DNA copy-number profiles, then computes ROC-AUC per method on the astrocytoma 2R clone 1 snRNA-seq data.

skills.search_text: roi-boundary-zero-padding Use when per-ROI histogram-equalized imputation patches (from SERM's sliding-window stage) must be merged into a single expression matrix with globally consistent expression values. The expression matrix is too small to divide into N >= 4 ROIs, so there are no patch seams to reconcile via resampling The data are not a sparse scRNA-seq count/expression matrix requiring SERM-style patch-wise imputation (e.g. already a dense feature table) Only a single-ROI imputation was performed, in which case no cross-patch consistency step is needed Final consistency step of the SERM imputation pipeline: all per-ROI imputed patches are merged via bilinear resampling, where each interior element is the sample average of its four diagonal neighbors and matrix-edge elements use zero padding (s_hat_i0 = s_hat_0j = s_hat_i(q+1) = s_hat_(n+1)j = 0). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w

skills.description: Use when you have a sparse, dropout-affected scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a fitted PDF from a prior distribution-learning step, and you need to impute missing values by analytically enforcing self-consistency via ROI-based histogram equalization.
skills.name: roi-selection-histogram-equalization
skills.search_text: roi-selection-histogram-equalization Use when you have a sparse, dropout-affected scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a fitted PDF from a prior distribution-learning step, and you need to impute missing values by analytically enforcing self-consistency via ROI-based histogram equalization. The dataset is small: SERM learns the distribution from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations. You need explicit batch-effect correction: batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation (only a z-score integration of batches is applied downstream). You only have raw unfiltered counts and no fitted distribution from the modeling stage — the equalization transform T_Si(k) requires the fitted PDF's decay parameter λ. http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 SERM's fixed imputation stage: divide the dropout-affected scRNA-seq expression matrix into overlapping rectangular ROIs and impute each window by adaptive histogram equalization whose target CDF is the parametric distribution (Gaussian, Rayleigh, or exponential with decay parameter λ) fitted in the modeling stage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: SERM's fixed imputation stage: divide the dropout-affected scRNA-seq expression matrix into overlapping rectangular ROIs and impute each window by adaptive histogram equalization whose target CDF is the parametric distribution (Gaussian, Rayleigh, or exponential with decay parameter λ) fitted in the modeling stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small: SERM learns the distribution from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual data distribution and yield inaccurate imputations. You need explicit batch-effect correction: batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation (only a z-score integration of batches is applied downstream). You only have raw unfiltered counts and no fitted distribution from the modeling stage — the equalization transform T_Si(k) requires the fitted PDF's decay parameter λ.

skills.search_text: root-terminal-state-probability-thresholding Use when a scvelo-processed AnnData object with a velocity field must be decomposed into root and terminal cell sets before simulating Markov-chain differentiation trajectories with Cytopath, and no prior root/terminal annotations are supplied. The goal is integration/correction in a joint latent representation (e.g., scVI-style) rather than correction at the gene expression level No reliable prior knowledge is available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs and normalizes a cell-cell similarity kernel so each row sums to 1, making it a probabilistic operator that can project a gene expression count matrix onto a biological signal for SiFT-style filtering (X~ = X − K·X). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Constructs and normalizes a cell-cell similarity kernel so each row sums to 1, making it a probabilistic operator that can project a gene expression count matrix onto a biological signal for SiFT-style filtering (X~ = X − K·X).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is integration/correction in a joint latent representation (e.g., scVI-style) rather than correction at the gene expression level No reliable prior knowledge is available to define the cell-cell similarity kernel — an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal

skills.description: Use when beginning a UniBic/runibic biclustering run on a continuous expression matrix: the input matrix must first be converted to an index matrix where each row lists column indexes sorted by that row's increasing values.
skills.name: row-wise-column-rank-ordering
skills.search_text: row-wise-column-rank-ordering Use when beginning a UniBic/runibic biclustering run on a continuous expression matrix: the input matrix must first be converted to an index matrix where each row lists column indexes sorted by that row's increasing values. The input is already discrete or already a rank/index matrix (BCUnibicD operates on discretized data; re-sorting would not add information). The goal is downstream bicluster seeding (pairwiseLCS/calculateLCS) or expansion (cluster) — those consume the index matrix rather than produce it. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute the UniBic index matrix: for each row of the input expression matrix, reorder column indexes by increasing entry value. This is Step 1 (Index Matrix Creation) of the UniBic pipeline and the substrate on which its row-pair LCS seeding operates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep23466
skills.summary: Compute the UniBic index matrix: for each row of the input expression matrix, reorder column indexes by increasing entry value. This is Step 1 (Index Matrix Creation) of the UniBic pipeline and the substrate on which its row-pair LCS seeding operates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already discrete or already a rank/index matrix (BCUnibicD operates on discretized data; re-sorting would not add information). The goal is downstream bicluster seeding (pairwiseLCS/calculateLCS) or expansion (cluster) — those consume the index matrix rather than produce it.

skills.description: Use when integrating multiple single-cell RNA-seq samples with STACAS/Seurat and you must remove anchors whose pairwise rPCA distance or inconsistent cell type labels make them unreliable before scoring anchors and building the integration guide tree.
skills.name: rpca-distance-based-anchor-filtering
skills.search_text: rpca-distance-based-anchor-filtering Use when integrating multiple single-cell RNA-seq samples with STACAS/Seurat and you must remove anchors whose pairwise rPCA distance or inconsistent cell type labels make them unreliable before scoring anchors and building the integration guide tree. Input is a single dataset with no batch structure to correct, so there are no cross-sample anchors to filter The integration method does not use anchor-based correspondence (e.g., scVI/scANVI latent-space correction), where rPCA anchor filtering has no analogue Cell type annotations are entirely absent and unsupervised integration is desired — while STACAS is described as robust to missing labels, semi-supervised anchor confidence filtering relies on prior cell type information http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filters integration anchors between scRNA-seq datasets by pairwise rPCA distance using STACAS's FilterAnchors.STACAS, retaining only reliable cross-sample cell correspondences that then drive anchor scoring and guide-tree-based integration order. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Filters integration anchors between scRNA-seq datasets by pairwise rPCA distance using STACAS's FilterAnchors.STACAS, retaining only reliable cross-sample cell correspondences that then drive anchor scoring and guide-tree-based integration order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single dataset with no batch structure to correct, so there are no cross-sample anchors to filter The integration method does not use anchor-based correspondence (e.g., scVI/scANVI latent-space correction), where rPCA anchor filtering has no analogue Cell type annotations are entirely absent and unsupervised integration is desired — while STACAS is described as robust to missing labels, semi-supervised anchor confidence filtering relies on prior cell type information

skills.description: Use when you have scMM latent representations of multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA + surface protein counts stored as RNA_count.mtx/Protein_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) and need high-resolution, interpretable cluster assignments for downstream heatmap visualization.
skills.name: rphenograph-graph-based-single-cell-clustering
skills.search_text: rphenograph-graph-based-single-cell-clustering Use when you have scMM latent representations of multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA + surface protein counts stored as RNA_count.mtx/Protein_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) and need high-resolution, interpretable cluster assignments for downstream heatmap visualization. Input is raw count matrices without an scMM-trained latent representation — cluster on the latent space, not directly on counts Data are single-modality or non-CITE-seq formats whose folder layout (RNA-seq/CITE-seq/ATAC-seq with gene.tsv/protein.tsv/peak.tsv) does not match the scMM expected structure without reorganization The goal is low-level coarse annotation rather than the high-resolution fine-grained partition the scMM paper targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Clusters cells in the scMM joint transcriptome–surface-protein latent space using Rphenograph (k-nearest-neighbor graph + Louvain community detection) to recover the paper's high-resolution ~54-cluster partition on PBMC CITE-seq data, enabling cluster-level interpretability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count matrices without an scMM-trained latent representation — cluster on the latent space, not directly on counts Data are single-modality or non-CITE-seq formats whose folder layout (RNA-seq/CITE-seq/ATAC-seq with gene.tsv/protein.tsv/peak.tsv) does not match the scMM expected structure without reorganization The goal is low-level coarse annotation rather than the high-resolution fine-grained partition the scMM paper targets

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers on scReadSim synthetic reads and you need to compare read enrichment of called peaks vs ground-truth peaks (or non-peaks) in a length-normalized way via RPKM distributions.
skills.name: rpkm-read-coverage-normalization
skills.search_text: rpkm-read-coverage-normalization Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers on scReadSim synthetic reads and you need to compare read enrichment of called peaks vs ground-truth peaks (or non-peaks) in a length-normalized way via RPKM distributions. The task is isoform-level or alternative-splicing benchmarking — the article states the current scReadSim provides gene-level ground truths only and is not recommended for such tools Peak sets are already length- and depth-normalized (e.g., RPKM/CPM columns exist) — re-normalizing would double-correct No ground-truth peak/non-peak intervals are available, so the called-vs-ground-truth RPKM mean-difference comparison cannot be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Length- and library-size-normalized read coverage (RPKM) computation for comparing called peak sets against scReadSim-designed ground-truth peaks/non-peaks in the scATAC-seq peak-calling benchmark. It enables the mean-difference RPKM comparison (Fig. 4) that distinguishes top performers (HMMRATAC, MACS3) from weak ones (SEACR). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Length- and library-size-normalized read coverage (RPKM) computation for comparing called peak sets against scReadSim-designed ground-truth peaks/non-peaks in the scATAC-seq peak-calling benchmark. It enables the mean-difference RPKM comparison (Fig. 4) that distinguishes top performers (HMMRATAC, MACS3) from weak ones (SEACR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is isoform-level or alternative-splicing benchmarking — the article states the current scReadSim provides gene-level ground truths only and is not recommended for such tools Peak sets are already length- and depth-normalized (e.g., RPKM/CPM columns exist) — re-normalizing would double-correct No ground-truth peak/non-peak intervals are available, so the called-vs-ground-truth RPKM mean-difference comparison cannot be constructed

skills.description: Use when per-sample tncRNA subclass counts (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH, tRNA halves) must be expressed in a library-size-independent unit or reconciled against the paper's species-level totals.
skills.name: rpm-normalization-counting
skills.search_text: rpm-normalization-counting Use when per-sample tncRNA subclass counts (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH, tRNA halves) must be expressed in a library-size-independent unit or reconciled against the paper's species-level totals. Reads have not yet been classified as tncRNAs mapping exclusively to the artificial chromosomes (masked tRNA plus 50 nt leader/trailer) — normalization must not include ambiguous non-tRNA assignments Paired-end or long-read data instead of the single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ inputs the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline was built for http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Normalizes plant tncRNA abundances to Reads Per Million (RPM = reads mapped to progenitor tRNA ÷ PMF, where PMF = total mapped reads/10^6) and aggregates per-sample tncRNA counts into per-species, per-subtype summary tables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Normalizes plant tncRNA abundances to Reads Per Million (RPM = reads mapped to progenitor tRNA ÷ PMF, where PMF = total mapped reads/10^6) and aggregates per-sample tncRNA counts into per-species, per-subtype summary tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads have not yet been classified as tncRNAs mapping exclusively to the artificial chromosomes (masked tRNA plus 50 nt leader/trailer) — normalization must not include ambiguous non-tRNA assignments Paired-end or long-read data instead of the single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ inputs the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline was built for

skills.search_text: rrho-marker-overlap-analysis Use when two single-cell cohorts of the same biological system must be compared at the level of per-cell-type differential marker rankings and downstream enrichment results, to verify that a computational surrogate (e.g., scSemiProfiler output) reproduces ground-truth analyses. When the goal is quantitative assessment of the semi-profiling pipeline itself (active learning selection, VAE-GAN inference) rather than downstream analysis fidelity comparison When only one dataset is available and no paired semi-profiled/real-profiled comparison can be made When cell types have not been annotated in both datasets, since marker ranking and RRHO require matched per-cell-type gene rankings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies agreement between cell-type marker/signature gene sets derived from two single-cell datasets (e.g., semi-profiled vs. real-profiled COVID-19 cohorts) using rank-rank hypergeometric overlap (RRHO) plots and GO/Reactome enrichment overlap statistics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1

skills.description: Use when candidate RBPs have no physical interaction with gold circRNA regulators (e.g., the 16 non-physically-associated candidates from CRIT) and motif-level functional connection must be established from circRNA sequences.
skills.name: rrna-binding-protein-sequence-analysis
skills.search_text: rrna-binding-protein-sequence-analysis Use when candidate RBPs have no physical interaction with gold circRNA regulators (e.g., the 16 non-physically-associated candidates from CRIT) and motif-level functional connection must be established from circRNA sequences. The candidate RBP already has physical-interaction evidence with a gold regulator via Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions — motif similarity adds no new independence argument. No circRNA sequence set can be linked to the candidate RBP (no circRNA annotations align to its RNAct RNA targets), leaving MEME with no input sequences. The goal is the NMF-based regulator identification itself (CRIT features Zp, Zs, Zg, rho_m, C value) rather than post-hoc validation of already-predicted candidates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A motif-similarity validation skill from the CRIT circRNA-regulator pipeline: it performs de novo motif discovery (MEME) on circRNA sequences linked to candidate RBPs and compares the discovered motifs against gold-regulator motifs with TOMTOM, providing binding-motif evidence for candidate regulators that lack physical interaction evidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: A motif-similarity validation skill from the CRIT circRNA-regulator pipeline: it performs de novo motif discovery (MEME) on circRNA sequences linked to candidate RBPs and compares the discovered motifs against gold-regulator motifs with TOMTOM, providing binding-motif evidence for candidate regulators that lack physical interaction evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate RBP already has physical-interaction evidence with a gold regulator via Pathway Commons Protein-Protein Interactions — motif similarity adds no new independence argument. No circRNA sequence set can be linked to the candidate RBP (no circRNA annotations align to its RNAct RNA targets), leaving MEME with no input sequences. The goal is the NMF-based regulator identification itself (CRIT features Zp, Zs, Zg, rho_m, C value) rather than post-hoc validation of already-predicted candidates.

skills.description: Use when raw Ribo-seq FastQ reads have been adapter-trimmed and length-filtered, and abundant rRNA/tRNA contamination must be depleted before HISAT2/Bowtie2 alignment and htseq-count CDS quantification.
skills.name: rrna-contaminant-read-depletion
skills.search_text: rrna-contaminant-read-depletion Use when raw Ribo-seq FastQ reads have been adapter-trimmed and length-filtered, and abundant rRNA/tRNA contamination must be depleted before HISAT2/Bowtie2 alignment and htseq-count CDS quantification. Input reads are already rRNA-depleted (e.g. delivered post-filtering) and only alignment/counting remains No contaminant reference FASTA for the organism of study can be built or obtained, since Bowtie2 needs a matched rRNA/tRNA reference The dataset is not ribosome-profiling data but ordinary RNA-seq, where Ribo-seq-specific RPF handling (25-35 nt selection, P-site offset tools) is out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Removes contaminating reads (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) from ribosome-profiling samples by aligning trimmed reads against a contaminant reference FASTA with Bowtie2 within the RiboDoc pipeline, so that only non-contaminant footprints proceed to genome/transcriptome alignment and CDS counting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: Removes contaminating reads (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) from ribosome-profiling samples by aligning trimmed reads against a contaminant reference FASTA with Bowtie2 within the RiboDoc pipeline, so that only non-contaminant footprints proceed to genome/transcriptome alignment and CDS counting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already rRNA-depleted (e.g. delivered post-filtering) and only alignment/counting remains No contaminant reference FASTA for the organism of study can be built or obtained, since Bowtie2 needs a matched rRNA/tRNA reference The dataset is not ribosome-profiling data but ordinary RNA-seq, where Ribo-seq-specific RPF handling (25-35 nt selection, P-site offset tools) is out of scope

skills.description: Use when a controlled benchmark of transcriptome assemblers is needed and a ground-truth transcriptome (e.g., hg38 NCBI RefSeq) must be paired with realistic simulated reads.
skills.name: rsem-transcriptome-read-simulation
skills.search_text: rsem-transcriptome-read-simulation Use when a controlled benchmark of transcriptome assemblers is needed and a ground-truth transcriptome (e.g., hg38 NCBI RefSeq) must be paired with realistic simulated reads. Data are long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT) — this simulation workflow was built for 100-bp paired-end short reads The benchmark requires measuring performance on real biological variation rather than a ground-truth-controlled simulation from RefSeq The assembly must be annotation-guided or use known transcript annotations, which the current Tiglon version does not support Generate a paired-end RNA-seq simulation with RSEM in which the simulation-model parameters are learned from a real human RNA-seq sample (SRR7536920), producing ~52 million 100-bp paired-end reads from the hg38 NCBI RefSeq transcriptome for assembler benchmarking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Generate a paired-end RNA-seq simulation with RSEM in which the simulation-model parameters are learned from a real human RNA-seq sample (SRR7536920), producing ~52 million 100-bp paired-end reads from the hg38 NCBI RefSeq transcriptome for assembler benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT) — this simulation workflow was built for 100-bp paired-end short reads The benchmark requires measuring performance on real biological variation rather than a ground-truth-controlled simulation from RefSeq The assembly must be annotation-guided or use known transcript annotations, which the current Tiglon version does not support

skills.description: Use when computing gene body coverage across many split per-cell scRNA-seq BAM files with RSeQC-equivalent output at ~10-fold lower cost, or when benchmarking geneBodyCoverage.pl vs geneBody_coverage.py on the same BAM/BED.
skills.name: rseqc-tool-execution
skills.search_text: rseqc-tool-execution Use when computing gene body coverage across many split per-cell scRNA-seq BAM files with RSeQC-equivalent output at ~10-fold lower cost, or when benchmarking geneBodyCoverage.pl vs geneBody_coverage.py on the same BAM/BED. BAM files are not yet split by cell barcode — run 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh first, otherwise the coverage is not per-cell Species has no bundled norRNAtRNA reference (SkewC provides only hg38_Gencode_V28 and mm10_Gencode_VM18 BED files) The task demands bit-identical results to RSeQC — the outputs 'differ a bit' (negligible, but not identical) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Executes SkewC's geneBodyCoverage.pl — a Perl script written to imitate RSeQC's geneBody_coverage.py — on split per-cell scRNA-seq BAM files, using reference indexing to cut gene body coverage runtime by about 10 folds (~9 min per 1 GB BAM). It also covers benchmarking the Perl reimplementation against RSeQC for runtime and output equivalence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.102038
skills.summary: Executes SkewC's geneBodyCoverage.pl — a Perl script written to imitate RSeQC's geneBody_coverage.py — on split per-cell scRNA-seq BAM files, using reference indexing to cut gene body coverage runtime by about 10 folds (~9 min per 1 GB BAM). It also covers benchmarking the Perl reimplementation against RSeQC for runtime and output equivalence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: BAM files are not yet split by cell barcode — run 0_split10XbyBarcode.sh first, otherwise the coverage is not per-cell Species has no bundled norRNAtRNA reference (SkewC provides only hg38_Gencode_V28 and mm10_Gencode_VM18 BED files) The task demands bit-identical results to RSeQC — the outputs 'differ a bit' (negligible, but not identical)

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or adapting IA-SVA to estimate a surrogate variable for a hidden factor (e.g., patient or cell-type heterogeneity) from single-cell read counts after adjusting for known covariates such as patient_id and geo_lib_size.
skills.name: rsq-based-gene-weighting-for-factor-estimation
skills.search_text: rsq-based-gene-weighting-for-factor-estimation Use when reconstructing or adapting IA-SVA to estimate a surrogate variable for a hidden factor (e.g., patient or cell-type heterogeneity) from single-cell read counts after adjusting for known covariates such as patient_id and geo_lib_size. Input is already normalized/transformed expression or a feature table rather than raw read counts, since the procedure regresses log-transformed read counts on the design matrix The goal is orthogonal factor decomposition only (e.g., plain PCA/SVA); IA-SVA specifically targets hidden factors that may be correlated with known covariates No permutation-based significance test is desired or feasible, since the R-squared weighting step is gated on PC1 significance testing with permuted columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A core mechanism of IA-SVA in which per-gene R-squared values from regressing residualized read counts on PC1 are used to build a weighted matrix Y'' = Y * W, whose second SVD yields the surrogate variable for a hidden factor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: A core mechanism of IA-SVA in which per-gene R-squared values from regressing residualized read counts on PC1 are used to build a weighted matrix Y'' = Y * W, whose second SVD yields the surrogate variable for a hidden factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/transformed expression or a feature table rather than raw read counts, since the procedure regresses log-transformed read counts on the design matrix The goal is orthogonal factor decomposition only (e.g., plain PCA/SVA); IA-SVA specifically targets hidden factors that may be correlated with known covariates No permutation-based significance test is desired or feasible, since the R-squared weighting step is gated on PC1 significance testing with permuted columns

skills.description: Use when only GWAS/eQTL summary statistics are available (no individual-level genotypes/phenotypes) and joint fine-mapping plus colocalization across multiple traits or tissues is needed, provided a reference LD matrix and sample sizes can be supplied.
skills.name: rss-likelihood-summary-statistics-modeling
skills.search_text: rss-likelihood-summary-statistics-modeling Use when only GWAS/eQTL summary statistics are available (no individual-level genotypes/phenotypes) and joint fine-mapping plus colocalization across multiple traits or tissues is needed, provided a reference LD matrix and sample sizes can be supplied. Individual-level genotypes and phenotypes are available — use CAFEH-G genotype mode (--mode genotype) instead, which does not require an LD matrix reference The effect size matrix contains missing data — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets and does not handle missing entries LD differs substantially between studies (e.g., due to ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so such heterogeneity can bias colocalization and fine-mapping inference http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Constructs an RSS-based likelihood from a reference LD matrix together with z-scores (or effect sizes and standard errors) plus sample sizes, so that CAFEH's spike-and-slab variational model (CAFEH-S) can jointly fine-map and colocalize signals across traits using summary statistics instead of individual-level genotypes and phenotypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Constructs an RSS-based likelihood from a reference LD matrix together with z-scores (or effect sizes and standard errors) plus sample sizes, so that CAFEH's spike-and-slab variational model (CAFEH-S) can jointly fine-map and colocalize signals across traits using summary statistics instead of individual-level genotypes and phenotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual-level genotypes and phenotypes are available — use CAFEH-G genotype mode (--mode genotype) instead, which does not require an LD matrix reference The effect size matrix contains missing data — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets and does not handle missing entries LD differs substantially between studies (e.g., due to ancestry differences) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix, so such heterogeneity can bias colocalization and fine-mapping inference

skills.description: Use when a single-cell dataset lacks biological replicates and Scanpro's bootstrapping produces ~100 iterations of per-cluster regression statistics that must be pooled into a single robust result per cell type.
skills.name: rubins-rule-multiple-imputation-pooling
skills.search_text: rubins-rule-multiple-imputation-pooling Use when a single-cell dataset lacks biological replicates and Scanpro's bootstrapping produces ~100 iterations of per-cluster regression statistics that must be pooled into a single robust result per cell type. The dataset already has biological replicates for all conditions — run the standard replicated Scanpro analysis instead, since bootstrapping is designed for non-replicated data (omit samples_col or set it to None to trigger bootstrapping only when unreplicated) Rare cell types below ~2% of all cells dominate the analysis — bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types and small clusters produce unstable results, so filter them out with n_min trimming rather than pooling their statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pool per-iteration beta coefficients and p-values from Scanpro's bootstrapped pseudo-replication analysis of unreplicated single-cell datasets using Rubin's multiple-imputation rule for coefficients and the median of adjusted p-values per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Pool per-iteration beta coefficients and p-values from Scanpro's bootstrapped pseudo-replication analysis of unreplicated single-cell datasets using Rubin's multiple-imputation rule for coefficients and the median of adjusted p-values per cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has biological replicates for all conditions — run the standard replicated Scanpro analysis instead, since bootstrapping is designed for non-replicated data (omit samples_col or set it to None to trigger bootstrapping only when unreplicated) Rare cell types below ~2% of all cells dominate the analysis — bootstrapping has limited benefits for rare cell types and small clusters produce unstable results, so filter them out with n_min trimming rather than pooling their statistics

skills.search_text: run-length-array-compression Use when indexing many datasets with per-dataset Bloom filters whose nested merges along a comb tree must be stored compactly, and per-dataset membership must be recoverable from run-length aggregation values. The collection has fewer than two datasets, so no nested series of merged Bloom filters exists to aggregate The number of indexed files exceeds the integer width chosen for aggregation values (e.g. >256 files with -e 8); the wrong width silently truncates membership counts Exact (non-approximate) dataset membership listing is required, since Bloom filters introduce a false-positive rate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes the nested series of Bloom filters (Rt⊆…⊆R1) found along a PAC comb-tree branch as an Aggregated Bloom filter: a t×b stacked matrix M plus an integer array V of size b where V[i] stores the length of the run of 1s in row i, so t Bloom filters of size b collapse to b integers of log t bits each. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225

skills.when_to_use_negative: The collection has fewer than two datasets, so no nested series of merged Bloom filters exists to aggregate The number of indexed files exceeds the integer width chosen for aggregation values (e.g. >256 files with -e 8); the wrong width silently truncates membership counts Exact (non-approximate) dataset membership listing is required, since Bloom filters introduce a false-positive rate

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify runtime and peak-memory costs of PAS computation (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes) vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes, or SCPA on datasets scaling from 10,000 up to 1,263,676 cells with 1383–14,300 pathways.
skills.name: runtime-and-memory-profiling
skills.search_text: runtime-and-memory-profiling Use when you need to quantify runtime and peak-memory costs of PAS computation (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes) vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes, or SCPA on datasets scaling from 10,000 up to 1,263,676 cells with 1383–14,300 pathways. skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is correctness or biological quality of results (e.g., whether a method preserves cell-type effects), not computational runtime You have time for only a single untimed run — one-shot timings without repetitions (here 100 per configuration) are too noisy to support speedup claims The operation has no meaningful single-threaded baseline to compare against, so percentage speedup is undefined

skills.search_text: sam-file-umi-position-extraction Use when UMI-containing FASTQ reads have been aligned to a genomic reference (e.g. STAR with no introns) yielding a sorted SAM file, and you need each UMI's complete list of genomic mapping positions to measure mapping-shift distances between reads sharing a UMI. skills.search_text: sample-covariance-matrix-estimation Use when the input is a sparsity-filtered cell-gene expression matrix and the goal is to expose its eigenvalue density for comparison against random matrix theory universality (Marchenko-Pastur) predictions. The expression matrix has not yet been sparsity-filtered — spurious eigenvector localization from sparsity (~3% of information per the paper) would contaminate the Wishart spectrum and bias the MP fit The goal is to extract true biological signal (only ~2% of information); this step characterizes the random-matrix noise bulk, not the low-rank signal departures from MP support The input is already a covariance matrix or a small matrix where Marchenko-Pastur universality assumptions are inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute the sample covariance (Wishart) matrix of a sparsity-filtered single-cell expression matrix and its eigenvalue spectrum, so that the random-matrix (noise) component of the data can be identified by fitting a Marchenko-Pastur distribution via gradient descent. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Compute the sample covariance (Wishart) matrix of a sparsity-filtered single-cell expression matrix and its eigenvalue spectrum, so that the random-matrix (noise) component of the data can be identified by fitting a Marchenko-Pastur distribution via gradient descent.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has not yet been sparsity-filtered — spurious eigenvector localization from sparsity (~3% of information per the paper) would contaminate the Wishart spectrum and bias the MP fit The goal is to extract true biological signal (only ~2% of information); this step characterizes the random-matrix noise bulk, not the low-rank signal departures from MP support The input is already a covariance matrix or a small matrix where Marchenko-Pastur universality assumptions are inappropriate

skills.search_text: sample-size-inverse-estimation Use when planning scCODA differential abundance experiments and you must know how many biological replicates are needed to detect a compositional shift of a given log-fold change, especially for rare vs abundant cell types. The experiment has many replicates per condition and no sample-size planning question — scCODA itself is already designed to handle the low-replicate regime, and no inversion is needed. The goal is detecting heterogeneity in response between individual samples or donors — scCODA does not model response variability within a condition, so sample-size curves for the joint model will not capture that. Effect of a covariate is expected to be non-log-linear with cell abundance — scCODA assumes a log-linear relationship, so the power estimates would be mis-specified. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates the number of case-control samples scCODA needs to detect a compositional change of a given log2 effect size, by fitting power curves on synthetic Dirichlet-multinomial data and inverting a quasibinomial GLM to solve for the sample size reaching a power of 0.8. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6

skills.search_text: sankey-diagram-visualization Use when you have per-cell predicted labels from a classifier (e.g., SciBet Bet predictions) plus known true labels and need to visualize label-to-label correspondence, such as cross-species mapping results. There is no label-to-label correspondence to display (e.g., unsupervised clustering output without reference annotations) — a Sankey flow between predicted and true labels is undefined. The task requires a per-gene statistic visualization (e.g., ΔS entropy rankings from SelectGene) rather than per-cell label flows. Query cells are not annotated with known labels, so no reference side of the flow diagram exists; a simple prediction bar chart would be appropriate instead. Render a Sankey (alluvial) diagram linking predicted cell-type labels to known reference labels, as used to display SciBet's cross-species mapping of human pancreas cells classified with the mouse Tabula Muris model (~92% correct mapping, Fig. 3b). It turns per-cell classification output into a flow diagram whose ribbon widths encode the number of cells assigned to each predicted-versus-true label pair. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
