skills.search_text: sc-rna-seq-preprocessing-filtering-logtransformation Use when preparing raw or lightly processed scRNA-Seq count matrices (e.g. GEO downloads like GSE59739 CPM or GSE102962 TPM) before NMF dictionary learning, knowledge transfer, or downstream clustering such as SC3. The input is already cell- and gene-filtered and log-transformed — the scRNA scripts allow turning off these steps to avoid double-filtering or re-logging data Datasets share only a small set of transcripts, since after intersecting gene sets 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable' and the approach is deferred to future work A batch-effect-removal or imputation pre-processing (Seurat CCA or MAGIC) is the goal — these are separate additional pre-processing steps applied on top, not replacements for the three base steps http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Standard three-step pre-processing of scRNA-Seq count matrices (cell filter, gene filter, log-transformation after adding a pseudo-count of 1) used in Mieth et al. 2019 to prepare source and target datasets before NMF-based transfer learning and SC3 clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Standard three-step pre-processing of scRNA-Seq count matrices (cell filter, gene filter, log-transformation after adding a pseudo-count of 1) used in Mieth et al. 2019 to prepare source and target datasets before NMF-based transfer learning and SC3 clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already cell- and gene-filtered and log-transformed — the scRNA scripts allow turning off these steps to avoid double-filtering or re-logging data Datasets share only a small set of transcripts, since after intersecting gene sets 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable' and the approach is deferred to future work A batch-effect-removal or imputation pre-processing (Seurat CCA or MAGIC) is the goal — these are separate additional pre-processing steps applied on top, not replacements for the three base steps

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers contains a proliferative subpopulation (e.g. Leiden cluster 0 in human fibroblasts) and the goal is to resolve the G1-to-G0 exit path and its marker genes.
skills.name: sc-rna-seq-subpopulation-mapping
skills.search_text: sc-rna-seq-subpopulation-mapping Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers contains a proliferative subpopulation (e.g. Leiden cluster 0 in human fibroblasts) and the goal is to resolve the G1-to-G0 exit path and its marker genes. If the dataset contains no cycling genes after filtering — the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed. If the input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments — DeepCycle requires imputed Mu/Ms moments. If the biological question does not concern cell-cycle dynamics or phase assignment, e.g. static differential expression between unrelated cell types. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Map a single-cell RNA-seq subpopulation (Leiden cluster) along a continuous cell-cycle trajectory with DeepCycle to identify genes and transcription factors underlying the branching point where human fibroblasts exit the cell cycle into a nonproliferative (G0-like) state. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30545-8
skills.summary: Map a single-cell RNA-seq subpopulation (Leiden cluster) along a continuous cell-cycle trajectory with DeepCycle to identify genes and transcription factors underlying the branching point where human fibroblasts exit the cell cycle into a nonproliferative (G0-like) state.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the dataset contains no cycling genes after filtering — the results will not be reliable and deeper sequencing may be needed. If the input Anndata lacks spliced/unspliced layers or has not been preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments — DeepCycle requires imputed Mu/Ms moments. If the biological question does not concern cell-cycle dynamics or phase assignment, e.g. static differential expression between unrelated cell types.

skills.description: Use when processing raw scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. 10X human PBMC, Tabula Muris, lemur lung, mole rat spleen, sea urchin embryo) and you need to measure how many uniquely mapped reads fall outside current gene annotations (uTARs) to assess annotation completeness.
skills.name: sc-rna-seq-unique-read-fraction-quantification
skills.search_text: sc-rna-seq-unique-read-fraction-quantification Use when processing raw scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. 10X human PBMC, Tabula Muris, lemur lung, mole rat spleen, sea urchin embryo) and you need to measure how many uniquely mapped reads fall outside current gene annotations (uTARs) to assess annotation completeness. Reads are already aligned with cellranger count — use the from_cellranger workflow variant instead of from_fastqs The goal is differential expression or homology annotation of uTARs rather than quantifying annotation-incompleteness read fractions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies the fraction of unique scRNA-seq reads assigned to unannotated transcriptionally active regions (uTARs) per organism, using the TAR-scRNA-seq Snakemake workflow to expose incompleteness of genome annotations across human, mouse, gray mouse lemur, naked mole rat, and purple sea urchin datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Quantifies the fraction of unique scRNA-seq reads assigned to unannotated transcriptionally active regions (uTARs) per organism, using the TAR-scRNA-seq Snakemake workflow to expose incompleteness of genome annotations across human, mouse, gray mouse lemur, naked mole rat, and purple sea urchin datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already aligned with cellranger count — use the from_cellranger workflow variant instead of from_fastqs The goal is differential expression or homology annotation of uTARs rather than quantifying annotation-incompleteness read fractions

skills.description: Use when a processed Seurat object carries broad clusters (or SCISSORS-revealed subclusters) that need cell-type labels, and you want markers specific to the target cluster rather than generic upregulated genes.
skills.name: sc-rnaseq-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: sc-rnaseq-cluster-annotation Use when a processed Seurat object carries broad clusters (or SCISSORS-revealed subclusters) that need cell-type labels, and you want markers specific to the target cluster rather than generic upregulated genes. Clusters already have trusted labels and the goal is only to visualize known canonical markers rather than re-derive a specificity-filtered marker set. The Seurat object is unprocessed (no NormalizeData / ScaleData / RunPCA) or has no cluster annotations yet — preprocessing and reclustering must come first. The goal is to discover rare subclusters within a heterogeneous cluster — use the SCISSORS silhouette-scoring and semi-supervised reclustering module, not the marker-gene module. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotate clusters or subclusters in a Seurat scRNA-seq analysis by identifying marker genes of high specificity to the cell type: build a candidate list with Wilcoxon rank-sum testing against background clusters, then filter out any gene highly expressed in non-target clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Annotate clusters or subclusters in a Seurat scRNA-seq analysis by identifying marker genes of high specificity to the cell type: build a candidate list with Wilcoxon rank-sum testing against background clusters, then filter out any gene highly expressed in non-target clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters already have trusted labels and the goal is only to visualize known canonical markers rather than re-derive a specificity-filtered marker set. The Seurat object is unprocessed (no NormalizeData / ScaleData / RunPCA) or has no cluster annotations yet — preprocessing and reclustering must come first. The goal is to discover rare subclusters within a heterogeneous cluster — use the SCISSORS silhouette-scoring and semi-supervised reclustering module, not the marker-gene module.

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized single-cell (or spatially resolved) transcriptomics matrix with cell group labels and want to infer neuron-neuron communication networks, especially neurotransmitter signaling absent from protein-only ligand-receptor databases.
skills.name: sc-rnaseq-communication-inference
skills.search_text: sc-rnaseq-communication-inference Use when you have a normalized single-cell (or spatially resolved) transcriptomics matrix with cell group labels and want to infer neuron-neuron communication networks, especially neurotransmitter signaling absent from protein-only ligand-receptor databases. Your signaling question concerns short-range autocrine/paracrine protein signaling only; NeuronChat is designed for long-distance neurotransmitter-based neuron-neuron communication and NeuronChatDB may not cover non-neural interactions You lack cell group labels — the method requires pre-defined cell groups/clusters as input to createNeuronChat Only protein-level interaction databases (OmniPath, STRING) are needed for non-neural cell types; NeuronChatDB is neural-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Infer neural-specific cell-cell communication networks from scRNA-seq data using NeuronChat, which models neurotransmitter-based signaling via the curated NeuronChatDB (373 interactions; 190 human, 183 mouse) and aggregates per-interaction link strengths into an intercellular network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36800-w
skills.summary: Infer neural-specific cell-cell communication networks from scRNA-seq data using NeuronChat, which models neurotransmitter-based signaling via the curated NeuronChatDB (373 interactions; 190 human, 183 mouse) and aggregates per-interaction link strengths into an intercellular network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your signaling question concerns short-range autocrine/paracrine protein signaling only; NeuronChat is designed for long-distance neurotransmitter-based neuron-neuron communication and NeuronChatDB may not cover non-neural interactions You lack cell group labels — the method requires pre-defined cell groups/clusters as input to createNeuronChat Only protein-level interaction databases (OmniPath, STRING) are needed for non-neural cell types; NeuronChatDB is neural-specific

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., counts_dt from splatSimulate, or the 3005-cell mouse cortex/hippocampus matrix) must be depth-normalized and log2-transformed before running endr, UMAP, or t-SNE.
skills.name: sc-rnaseq-library-size-normalization
skills.search_text: sc-rnaseq-library-size-normalization Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., counts_dt from splatSimulate, or the 3005-cell mouse cortex/hippocampus matrix) must be depth-normalized and log2-transformed before running endr, UMAP, or t-SNE. The input is already a log-normalized matrix (dat_log), a similarity matrix, or a 2D embedding — re-normalizing would corrupt values meant for endr/UMAP/t-SNE The downstream task requires raw counts (e.g., count-based modeling in Splatter params) rather than log-normalized expression You only need feature-gene selection; normalization here does not replace the separate top-variable-gene filter (1000 genes real / 500 simulated) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Median library-size normalization followed by log2(x+1) transformation of a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix, producing the log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix (dat_log) that EDGE's endr pipeline, UMAP, and t-SNE consume. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Median library-size normalization followed by log2(x+1) transformation of a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix, producing the log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix (dat_log) that EDGE's endr pipeline, UMAP, and t-SNE consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a log-normalized matrix (dat_log), a similarity matrix, or a 2D embedding — re-normalizing would corrupt values meant for endr/UMAP/t-SNE The downstream task requires raw counts (e.g., count-based modeling in Splatter params) rather than log-normalized expression You only need feature-gene selection; normalization here does not replace the separate top-variable-gene filter (1000 genes real / 500 simulated)

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE149614 HCC01T/HCC03N .h5ad or similar) require QC, normalization, and HVG selection before batch correction or DEG analysis.
skills.name: sc-rnaseq-quality-control-and-normalization
skills.search_text: sc-rnaseq-quality-control-and-normalization Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE149614 HCC01T/HCC03N .h5ad or similar) require QC, normalization, and HVG selection before batch correction or DEG analysis. Input is already normalized/log1p-transformed — re-normalizing a scaled matrix would double-transform the data The goal is multi-omic scATAC-seq processing, which requires a different route (e.g., conversion to a gene activity matrix via MAESTRO in this paper's pipeline) Analysis requires retaining low-mito or low-gene cells (e.g., plate-based datasets where the 5% mito and 200-gene cutoffs would over-filter) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Preprocessing skill for raw scRNA-seq count matrices: cell/gene QC filtering, count-depth normalization to 10,000 per cell with log1p stabilization, and highly variable gene selection, preparing data for downstream batch correction such as scCobra. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Preprocessing skill for raw scRNA-seq count matrices: cell/gene QC filtering, count-depth normalization to 10,000 per cell with log1p stabilization, and highly variable gene selection, preparing data for downstream batch correction such as scCobra.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/log1p-transformed — re-normalizing a scaled matrix would double-transform the data The goal is multi-omic scATAC-seq processing, which requires a different route (e.g., conversion to a gene activity matrix via MAESTRO in this paper's pipeline) Analysis requires retaining low-mito or low-gene cells (e.g., plate-based datasets where the 5% mito and 200-gene cutoffs would over-filter)

skills.description: Use when you have SC count matrix plus ST counts with spot spatial coordinates and cell-type labels, and need single-cell spatial mapping, pseudo-spatial adjacency, or colocalization of cell types (e.g., TSKs vs endothelial cells in hSCC).
skills.name: sc-st-embedding-transfer-learning
skills.search_text: sc-st-embedding-transfer-learning Use when you have SC count matrix plus ST counts with spot spatial coordinates and cell-type labels, and need single-cell spatial mapping, pseudo-spatial adjacency, or colocalization of cell types (e.g., TSKs vs endothelial cells in hSCC). The goal is classic spot deconvolution where a spot is modeled as a mixture of a fixed number of cell types — STEM instead transfers spatial information to individual cells SC and ST data come from different donors (even in the same disease state) — the paper states this remains untested future work The ST data lack spot spatial coordinates, so the Gaussian spatial-variance term and coordinate mapping cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train STEM's SOmodel, a deep transfer learning model, to encode single-cell RNA-seq (SC) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) counts into a shared spatially aware embedding space, then derive SC–ST mapping matrices and single-cell pseudo-spatial coordinates. It eliminates the domain gap (batch/technical bias, dropout) between SC and ST data without requiring spot deconvolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Train STEM's SOmodel, a deep transfer learning model, to encode single-cell RNA-seq (SC) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) counts into a shared spatially aware embedding space, then derive SC–ST mapping matrices and single-cell pseudo-spatial coordinates. It eliminates the domain gap (batch/technical bias, dropout) between SC and ST data without requiring spot deconvolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is classic spot deconvolution where a spot is modeled as a mixture of a fixed number of cell types — STEM instead transfers spatial information to individual cells SC and ST data come from different donors (even in the same disease state) — the paper states this remains untested future work The ST data lack spot spatial coordinates, so the Gaussian spatial-variance term and coordinate mapping cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when you have normalized SC and ST datasets and need to map every single cell to a spatial coordinate on ST spots — e.g. to build a single-cell level spatial transcriptomic landscape or run cell-type-specific spatial DE along a tissue axis.
skills.name: sc-st-mapping-matrix-inference
skills.search_text: sc-st-mapping-matrix-inference Use when you have normalized SC and ST datasets and need to map every single cell to a spatial coordinate on ST spots — e.g. to build a single-cell level spatial transcriptomic landscape or run cell-type-specific spatial DE along a tissue axis. When the goal is spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types — STEM's single-cell mapping is explicitly positioned against deconvolution approaches that treat a spot as a fixed mixture. When SC and ST data come from different donors or disease states — the article notes this remains untested future work (the mouse liver application relied on same-region, similar cell-type-proportion data). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers SC-ST and ST-SC mapping matrices by encoding single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data into STEM's unified spatially aware embedding space, then taking softmax of embedding dot products so each row sums to 1. This assigns single cells spatial coordinates and transfers spot-level spatial information (e.g. zonation scores) to individual cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Infers SC-ST and ST-SC mapping matrices by encoding single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data into STEM's unified spatially aware embedding space, then taking softmax of embedding dot products so each row sums to 1. This assigns single cells spatial coordinates and transfers spot-level spatial information (e.g. zonation scores) to individual cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types — STEM's single-cell mapping is explicitly positioned against deconvolution approaches that treat a spot as a fixed mixture. When SC and ST data come from different donors or disease states — the article notes this remains untested future work (the mouse liver application relied on same-region, similar cell-type-proportion data).

skills.description: Use when you need simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks with known ground truth — e.g., testing whether a trajectory-suitability check correctly flags trajectory-free simulations (homogeneous cells) while not falsely flagging linear-trajectory simulations.
skills.name: scaffold-simulation-dataset-generation
skills.search_text: scaffold-simulation-dataset-generation Use when you need simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks with known ground truth — e.g., testing whether a trajectory-suitability check correctly flags trajectory-free simulations (homogeneous cells) while not falsely flagging linear-trajectory simulations. Real experimental datasets with unknown ground truth — simulation is only needed when trajectory truth must be known to validate flag accuracy; for real data use Escort directly on the dataset (e.g., GSE190616). Benchmarks requiring non-linear (bifurcating/tree) trajectory topologies — the documented simulation conditions here cover only homogeneous (0% dynamic) and linear (20% dynamic genes) trajectories. If you only need ready-made benchmarks — the article notes six publicly available simulated datasets [45] that can be used instead of generating new ones. Generate synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with the Scaffold R package (v0.2.0) from a human pancreas single-cell RNA-seq reference, spanning known ground-truth conditions (homogeneous, 0% dynamic genes vs. linear trajectory, 20% dynamic genes) so that downstream tools like Escort's Step 1 suitability checks can be validated against known truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Generate synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with the Scaffold R package (v0.2.0) from a human pancreas single-cell RNA-seq reference, spanning known ground-truth conditions (homogeneous, 0% dynamic genes vs. linear trajectory, 20% dynamic genes) so that downstream tools like Escort's Step 1 suitability checks can be validated against known truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real experimental datasets with unknown ground truth — simulation is only needed when trajectory truth must be known to validate flag accuracy; for real data use Escort directly on the dataset (e.g., GSE190616). Benchmarks requiring non-linear (bifurcating/tree) trajectory topologies — the documented simulation conditions here cover only homogeneous (0% dynamic) and linear (20% dynamic genes) trajectories. If you only need ready-made benchmarks — the article notes six publicly available simulated datasets [45] that can be used instead of generating new ones.

skills.name: scalability-analysis-of-clustering-pipelines
skills.search_text: scalability-analysis-of-clustering-pipelines Use when quantifying how a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method's runtime and peak memory grow with cell count — e.g. comparing a correlation-based method against correlation-free baselines at 10k/100k/1M-cell scales. The question concerns clustering accuracy (e.g. silhouette index, ARI against cell-type annotations), not computational scaling — use the accuracy benchmarking skill instead The dataset is small (e.g. the 10X pbmc_1k_v2 PBMC dataset, ~1k cells), where memory/time scaling cannot be meaningfully profiled across orders of magnitude Only one feature selection method is of interest and no correlation-free baselines will be run, since the benchmark's value is the comparative scaling contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark how a single-cell feature selection/clustering pipeline's wall-clock runtime and peak memory scale with cell count, as done for DUBStepR on the Cao et al. mouse organogenesis scRNA-seq dataset (GSE119945), where memory grew 6.4x from 100k to 1M cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Benchmark how a single-cell feature selection/clustering pipeline's wall-clock runtime and peak memory scale with cell count, as done for DUBStepR on the Cao et al. mouse organogenesis scRNA-seq dataset (GSE119945), where memory grew 6.4x from 100k to 1M cells.

skills.description: Use when comparing how clustering/batch-correction methods scale with many batches and tens of thousands of cells, or when a candidate method must be ruled in/out on computing time or memory (e.g. a 32 GB limit).
skills.name: scalability-benchmarking-of-clustering-methods
skills.search_text: scalability-benchmarking-of-clustering-methods Use when comparing how clustering/batch-correction methods scale with many batches and tens of thousands of cells, or when a candidate method must be ruled in/out on computing time or memory (e.g. a 32 GB limit). The question is clustering accuracy (ARI against reference cell-type labels) rather than runtime or memory scaling — use the ARI evaluation workflow instead The dataset has no batch structure (e.g. a single batch like the paul15 myeloid progenitor data), so batch-count scaling cannot be exercised Working memory is far below 32 GB and BERMUDA must be run anyway — its recorded peak memory exceeds 32 GB, so it cannot complete and will break the benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime and peak memory footprint of scRNA-seq clustering and batch-correction methods (DESC, MNN/Seurat 3.0, scVI, BERMUDA, scanorama) on a fixed batch-structured subsample (e.g. 30 batches, 30,000 cells of the macaque retina dataset), to establish which methods scale to large atlas-like studies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime and peak memory footprint of scRNA-seq clustering and batch-correction methods (DESC, MNN/Seurat 3.0, scVI, BERMUDA, scanorama) on a fixed batch-structured subsample (e.g. 30 batches, 30,000 cells of the macaque retina dataset), to establish which methods scale to large atlas-like studies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is clustering accuracy (ARI against reference cell-type labels) rather than runtime or memory scaling — use the ARI evaluation workflow instead The dataset has no batch structure (e.g. a single batch like the paul15 myeloid progenitor data), so batch-count scaling cannot be exercised Working memory is far below 32 GB and BERMUDA must be run anyway — its recorded peak memory exceeds 32 GB, so it cannot complete and will break the benchmark

skills.description: Use when you need to show a tool's runtime scales acceptably with dataset size — e.g., colorizing single-cell-resolution SRT datasets of 1k–100,000 cells within a bounded time budget.
skills.name: scalability-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: scalability-curve-visualization Use when you need to show a tool's runtime scales acceptably with dataset size — e.g., colorizing single-cell-resolution SRT datasets of 1k–100,000 cells within a bounded time budget. The goal is to compare colorization quality or visual clarity rather than runtime — use qualitative benchmarking on real SRT datasets (STARmap, Stereo-seq, seqFISH, IMC) instead The tool under test has no simulated-data generator and you only have small real samples — runtime scaling on few small inputs does not support a scaling-curve claim http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of a pipeline (here, the Spaco colorization pipeline) across simulated datasets of increasing size, record per-size timings, and plot a runtime-versus-scale curve to validate that the method stays practical (e.g., Spaco colorizes up to 100,000 cells in under 30 seconds). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of a pipeline (here, the Spaco colorization pipeline) across simulated datasets of increasing size, record per-size timings, and plot a runtime-versus-scale curve to validate that the method stays practical (e.g., Spaco colorizes up to 100,000 cells in under 30 seconds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare colorization quality or visual clarity rather than runtime — use qualitative benchmarking on real SRT datasets (STARmap, Stereo-seq, seqFISH, IMC) instead The tool under test has no simulated-data generator and you only have small real samples — runtime scaling on few small inputs does not support a scaling-curve claim

skills.description: Use when comparing execution-speed scaling of two implementations of an omics method across large simulated datasets, where runtime must be normalized per sample and per regulator.
skills.name: scalability-performance-evaluation-omics-methods
skills.search_text: scalability-performance-evaluation-omics-methods Use when comparing execution-speed scaling of two implementations of an omics method across large simulated datasets, where runtime must be normalized per sample and per regulator. skills.summary: Benchmarks the runtime scalability of omics inference methods (decoupleR's R vs Python implementations) by timing each method on simulated large-scale matrices and normalizing to ms per sample and regulator.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is method accuracy (AUROC/AUPRC against perturbation ground truth) rather than runtime — use the decoupleRBench perturbation benchmark pipeline instead. skills.search_text: scale-free-network-soft-thresholding Use when you need unsupervised gene program/module discovery from scRNA-seq data and want to benchmark against or replace factorization methods like ICA or NMF, starting from an annotated Seurat object. The input is already a gene-module/factor list from another method and only functional annotation is needed — use getAnnotationPathways scoring directly rather than re-running SSN. Cluster stability cannot be assessed (e.g. single-replicate datasets), where the paper notes the related resolution-optimization methods are limited by cluster stability and reproducibility. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Unsupervised gene program discovery via a scale-free transformed shared nearest neighbor (SSN) network: Pearson co-expression graph built on selected network features, driven toward a scale-free topology, clustered into gene modules, and pruned of low-connectivity genes. Implemented in scMiko (runSSN/pruneSSN) and shown to recover more GO terms and STRING PPI enrichment than ICA and NMF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Unsupervised gene program discovery via a scale-free transformed shared nearest neighbor (SSN) network: Pearson co-expression graph built on selected network features, driven toward a scale-free topology, clustered into gene modules, and pruned of low-connectivity genes. Implemented in scMiko (runSSN/pruneSSN) and shown to recover more GO terms and STRING PPI enrichment than ICA and NMF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene-module/factor list from another method and only functional annotation is needed — use getAnnotationPathways scoring directly rather than re-running SSN. Cluster stability cannot be assessed (e.g. single-replicate datasets), where the paper notes the related resolution-optimization methods are limited by cluster stability and reproducibility.

skills.description: Use when a gene co-expression network or module has been inferred (e.g. via SCANet/BioNERO WGCNA) and you need to validate that its graph topology is biologically plausible before selecting hubs or downstream modules.
skills.name: scale-free-topology-assessment
skills.search_text: scale-free-topology-assessment Use when a gene co-expression network or module has been inferred (e.g. via SCANet/BioNERO WGCNA) and you need to validate that its graph topology is biologically plausible before selecting hubs or downstream modules. The input is a transcriptional regulatory network (GRN) rather than a co-expression module — SCANet derives GRNs from GCNs via RcisTarget TF-motif validation, and the scale-free check applies to the co-expression module graph. The network was inferred by a method whose node degree distribution is not expected to be scale-free (e.g. COTAN, scLink, or fcoex outputs), not by the modified-WGCNA/BioNERO route described here. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A validation step in SCANet's modified-WGCNA co-expression workflow that checks whether an inferred gene co-expression module's graph fits the scale-free topology characteristic of real-world biological networks, supporting hub-gene identification and module QC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: A validation step in SCANet's modified-WGCNA co-expression workflow that checks whether an inferred gene co-expression module's graph fits the scale-free topology characteristic of real-world biological networks, supporting hub-gene identification and module QC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a transcriptional regulatory network (GRN) rather than a co-expression module — SCANet derives GRNs from GCNs via RcisTarget TF-motif validation, and the scale-free check applies to the co-expression module graph. The network was inferred by a method whose node degree distribution is not expected to be scale-free (e.g. COTAN, scLink, or fcoex outputs), not by the modified-WGCNA/BioNERO route described here.

skills.description: Use when you have a constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression network (adjacency or edge list) and need to validate that its degree distribution approximately follows a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis.
skills.name: scale-free-topology-fitting
skills.search_text: scale-free-topology-fitting Use when you have a constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression network (adjacency or edge list) and need to validate that its degree distribution approximately follows a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis. Input is still raw TCGA expression matrices (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor / TCGA_BLCAnormal) rather than a constructed co-expression network — network construction must happen first The goal is to rank key nodes / driver genes in the network — that is WMDS.net's controllability (intlinprog) step, not topology validation The network is small or sparse such that a degree-frequency histogram is too discontinuous for a meaningful log-log regression http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Assesses whether a differential co-expression network approximates a scale-free topology by fitting log2(degree frequency) versus log2(degree) with linear regression and reporting the R-square, following the Zhang and Horvath criterion (R2 > 0.80) used to validate the 14 TCGA cancer-type networks in WMDS.net. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Assesses whether a differential co-expression network approximates a scale-free topology by fitting log2(degree frequency) versus log2(degree) with linear regression and reporting the R-square, following the Zhang and Horvath criterion (R2 > 0.80) used to validate the 14 TCGA cancer-type networks in WMDS.net.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw TCGA expression matrices (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor / TCGA_BLCAnormal) rather than a constructed co-expression network — network construction must happen first The goal is to rank key nodes / driver genes in the network — that is WMDS.net's controllability (intlinprog) step, not topology validation The network is small or sparse such that a degree-frequency histogram is too discontinuous for a meaningful log-log regression

skills.description: Use when raw CT values or normalized expression matrices for multiple candidate reference genes (internal controls) are available and a single optimally weighted virtual reference gene is needed for ΔΔCT normalization.
skills.name: scale-invariant-aggregation-optimization
skills.search_text: scale-invariant-aggregation-optimization Use when raw CT values or normalized expression matrices for multiple candidate reference genes (internal controls) are available and a single optimally weighted virtual reference gene is needed for ΔΔCT normalization. Aggregating more than 5 reference genes with geom(sd) — the article reports no expected benefit compared to the regular geometric mean in that regime Stability measures other than SD/CV are required and the InterOptCuda executable is not installed in PATH (Genorm/NormFinder cannot be computed) The input is already a single aggregated reference value or a target-gene expression table with no multiple reference genes to weight http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Computes optimal aggregation weights for combining multiple qPCR reference genes into a single virtual reference gene via weighted arithmetic or geometric means, minimizing SD or CV (the four InterOpt methods: geom(sd), geom(cv), arith(sd), arith(cv)). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107945
skills.summary: Computes optimal aggregation weights for combining multiple qPCR reference genes into a single virtual reference gene via weighted arithmetic or geometric means, minimizing SD or CV (the four InterOpt methods: geom(sd), geom(cv), arith(sd), arith(cv)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Aggregating more than 5 reference genes with geom(sd) — the article reports no expected benefit compared to the regular geometric mean in that regime Stability measures other than SD/CV are required and the InterOptCuda executable is not installed in PATH (Genorm/NormFinder cannot be computed) The input is already a single aggregated reference value or a target-gene expression table with no multiple reference genes to weight

skills.description: Use when validating whether predictive entropy from classifiers trained on labeled cells can flag cells whose ground truth labels were corrupted, e.g. simulating annotation mistakes before self-training cell selection.
skills.name: scaled-entropy-distribution-comparison
skills.search_text: scaled-entropy-distribution-comparison Use when validating whether predictive entropy from classifiers trained on labeled cells can flag cells whose ground truth labels were corrupted, e.g. simulating annotation mistakes before self-training cell selection. Labels have not been (and cannot be) corrupted or audited, so there is no mislabel status to compare against — use standard uncertainty-based active learning selection instead Input is already class posterior probabilities or entropies rather than expression count data — no need to retrain classifiers The goal is cluster-based subsampling for balanced training sets (LEADER adaptive reweighting), not mislabel detection by entropy http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Detects mislabeled cells in a self-training set by computing predictive entropy from random forest and logistic regression classifiers trained on a label-corrupted training sample, scaling entropies for cross-cohort comparability, and comparing entropy distributions of corrupted vs correctly labeled cells (Fig. 5D-style analysis). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Detects mislabeled cells in a self-training set by computing predictive entropy from random forest and logistic regression classifiers trained on a label-corrupted training sample, scaling entropies for cross-cohort comparability, and comparing entropy distributions of corrupted vs correctly labeled cells (Fig. 5D-style analysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels have not been (and cannot be) corrupted or audited, so there is no mislabel status to compare against — use standard uncertainty-based active learning selection instead Input is already class posterior probabilities or entropies rather than expression count data — no need to retrain classifiers The goal is cluster-based subsampling for balanced training sets (LEADER adaptive reweighting), not mislabel detection by entropy

skills.description: Use when you need to visually validate temporal expression patterns of differentially expressed genes and their linked regulators (activators vs repressors) across omics layers from simulated or real multi-omics count data.
skills.name: scaled-expression-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: scaled-expression-heatmap-visualization Use when you need to visually validate temporal expression patterns of differentially expressed genes and their linked regulators (activators vs repressors) across omics layers from simulated or real multi-omics count data. The goal is single-cell data visualization — MOSim's sc_mosim validation uses Kendall's Tb correlation and k-medoids/Silhouette clustering instead, not this bulk heatmap workflow Input data are raw counts that need simulation or differential analysis first rather than already-selected DEGs with linked regulators for visualization The omics layers of interest are proteomics or metabolomics — MOSim does not support these layers http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Renders heatmaps of log(x+1)-transformed, row-wise z-scored group-mean expression profiles for selected genes/regulators across multi-omic layers (RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, TF), enabling visual validation of simulated activator/repressor regulatory patterns in multilayer GRN simulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Renders heatmaps of log(x+1)-transformed, row-wise z-scored group-mean expression profiles for selected genes/regulators across multi-omic layers (RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, TF), enabling visual validation of simulated activator/repressor regulatory patterns in multilayer GRN simulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-cell data visualization — MOSim's sc_mosim validation uses Kendall's Tb correlation and k-medoids/Silhouette clustering instead, not this bulk heatmap workflow Input data are raw counts that need simulation or differential analysis first rather than already-selected DEGs with linked regulators for visualization The omics layers of interest are proteomics or metabolomics — MOSim does not support these layers

skills.description: Use when you need to score or compare batch integration of multiple embedding methods (e.g., corralm vs. PCA+Harmony) on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, such as the SCMixology 10X/Celseq2/Dropseq CellBench dataset.
skills.name: scaled-variance-batch-mixing-assessment
skills.search_text: scaled-variance-batch-mixing-assessment Use when you need to score or compare batch integration of multiple embedding methods (e.g., corralm vs. PCA+Harmony) on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, such as the SCMixology 10X/Celseq2/Dropseq CellBench dataset. The data are a single batch/table with no cross-batch structure to mix — corral (single-table CA) and no SV mixing assessment is needed The goal is cluster recovery or cell-type annotation accuracy rather than batch integration — the article evaluates that separately with ARI, and ARI may even penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations Embeddings are not aligned across batches (e.g., raw per-batch PCA), since SV would measure meaningless mixing on incomparable coordinate systems http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies batch integration quality of single-cell embeddings with the scaled variance (SV) batch-mixing metric, where SV close to 1 indicates successful cross-batch mixing. In Hsu & Culhane (2023) it was used to show that corralm and Harmony-on-corralm embeddings outperform Harmony on PCA embeddings for the SCMixology three-platform dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Quantifies batch integration quality of single-cell embeddings with the scaled variance (SV) batch-mixing metric, where SV close to 1 indicates successful cross-batch mixing. In Hsu & Culhane (2023) it was used to show that corralm and Harmony-on-corralm embeddings outperform Harmony on PCA embeddings for the SCMixology three-platform dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are a single batch/table with no cross-batch structure to mix — corral (single-table CA) and no SV mixing assessment is needed The goal is cluster recovery or cell-type annotation accuracy rather than batch integration — the article evaluates that separately with ARI, and ARI may even penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations Embeddings are not aligned across batches (e.g., raw per-batch PCA), since SV would measure meaningless mixing on incomparable coordinate systems

skills.description: Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNA-seq methods: multiple tools must be run on size-graded subsamples of one dataset (e.g. the 68k PBMC set) and runtime/peak-memory curves plotted against cell number.
skills.name: scaling-analysis-cell-count-vs-runtime
skills.search_text: scaling-analysis-cell-count-vs-runtime Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNA-seq methods: multiple tools must be run on size-graded subsamples of one dataset (e.g. the 68k PBMC set) and runtime/peak-memory curves plotted against cell number. The goal is rare-cell detection accuracy (e.g. F1 score) rather than computational cost — use a detection-accuracy benchmarking skill instead The dataset cannot be subsampled across a size range, so no scaling relationship can be estimated Only a single tool is of interest — scalability curves require comparing multiple methods on identical data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill that measures wall-clock running time and peak RAM of five rare-cell detection tools (RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS, FiRE, GapClust) across 16 subsampled scRNA-seq datasets scaled from ~1,000 to ~68,000 cells, to characterize computational scalability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that measures wall-clock running time and peak RAM of five rare-cell detection tools (RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS, FiRE, GapClust) across 16 subsampled scRNA-seq datasets scaled from ~1,000 to ~68,000 cells, to characterize computational scalability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is rare-cell detection accuracy (e.g. F1 score) rather than computational cost — use a detection-accuracy benchmarking skill instead The dataset cannot be subsampled across a size range, so no scaling relationship can be estimated Only a single tool is of interest — scalability curves require comparing multiple methods on identical data

skills.description: Use when reproducing an integration pipeline at atlas scale and you must verify the reported computational efficiency (runtime and memory scaling) against baselines such as scJoint and Seurat.
skills.name: scaling-benchmark-measurement
skills.search_text: scaling-benchmark-measurement Use when reproducing an integration pipeline at atlas scale and you must verify the reported computational efficiency (runtime and memory scaling) against baselines such as scJoint and Seurat. When the goal is only label-transfer accuracy (F1) or embedding quality and no efficiency/scaling claim needs verification — use the label-transfer evaluation skill instead. When the dataset is small paired multi-omics data (e.g., the 4,644 CITE-seq / 4,506 ASAP-seq PBMC cells from GSE156478), where atlas-scale scaling benchmarks are not the claim under test. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Measures wall-clock time and peak memory of a multi-omics integration method (e.g., scBridge) over atlas-scale inputs (~102,103 mouse atlas cells) to verify the linear-time/constant-memory scaling profile reported in the paper's Fig. 3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Measures wall-clock time and peak memory of a multi-omics integration method (e.g., scBridge) over atlas-scale inputs (~102,103 mouse atlas cells) to verify the linear-time/constant-memory scaling profile reported in the paper's Fig. 3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only label-transfer accuracy (F1) or embedding quality and no efficiency/scaling claim needs verification — use the label-transfer evaluation skill instead. When the dataset is small paired multi-omics data (e.g., the 4,644 CITE-seq / 4,506 ASAP-seq PBMC cells from GSE156478), where atlas-scale scaling benchmarks are not the claim under test.

skills.description: Use when training and test scRNA-seq datasets come from different studies, platforms, or gene panels (e.g., Lemur 4 vs. Lemur 1, Muris FACS vs. Lemur 2) and batch effects may obscure cross-dataset cell type annotation with OnClass.
skills.name: scanorama-batch-correction
skills.search_text: scanorama-batch-correction Use when training and test scRNA-seq datasets come from different studies, platforms, or gene panels (e.g., Lemur 4 vs. Lemur 1, Muris FACS vs. Lemur 2) and batch effects may obscure cross-dataset cell type annotation with OnClass. Train and test cells come from the same dataset or sequencing run — batch correction could remove real biological signal The test set contains a very large number of unseen cell types relative to the reference, a setting the OnClass authors flag as one where batch-effect correction methods are not yet developed Features are already integrated or normalized across datasets (e.g., prior Scanpy external.pp.scanorama_integrate was applied) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Optionally apply Scanorama batch correction between training and test gene expression panels (e.g., Lemur/Muris single-cell datasets) before OnClass training and prediction, so that platform/dataset effects do not confound cross-dataset cell type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Optionally apply Scanorama batch correction between training and test gene expression panels (e.g., Lemur/Muris single-cell datasets) before OnClass training and prediction, so that platform/dataset effects do not confound cross-dataset cell type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Train and test cells come from the same dataset or sequencing run — batch correction could remove real biological signal The test set contains a very large number of unseen cell types relative to the reference, a setting the OnClass authors flag as one where batch-effect correction methods are not yet developed Features are already integrated or normalized across datasets (e.g., prior Scanpy external.pp.scanorama_integrate was applied)

skills.description: Use when a multi-dataset scRNA-seq collection must be integrated purely from expression profiles as a batch-correction/integration baseline — e.g., to test whether annotation-score embeddings cluster cells by cell type better than expression-level integration.
skills.name: scanorama-expression-integration
skills.search_text: scanorama-expression-integration Use when a multi-dataset scRNA-seq collection must be integrated purely from expression profiles as a batch-correction/integration baseline — e.g., to test whether annotation-score embeddings cluster cells by cell type better than expression-level integration. The goal is annotation-based integration rather than expression-based integration — the OnClass paper shows ontology-score PCA embeddings cluster cells by type better than Scanorama (P < 7e-293), so Scanorama is the wrong primary method when label-quality clustering is the objective Data has not undergone noise reduction — Scanorama is designed to run downstream of imputation/highly-variable gene filtering, not as a first processing step Only a single dataset is present — Scanorama's mutual-NN matching requires multiple datasets/batches to integrate http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Integrates heterogeneous scRNA-seq datasets based on expression profiles using Scanorama, producing a low-dimensional integrated embedding (here with scan_dim = 10) that serves as the expression-based baseline against which Cell Ontology annotation-based integration (OnClass score embeddings) is compared via silhouette coefficients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Integrates heterogeneous scRNA-seq datasets based on expression profiles using Scanorama, producing a low-dimensional integrated embedding (here with scan_dim = 10) that serves as the expression-based baseline against which Cell Ontology annotation-based integration (OnClass score embeddings) is compared via silhouette coefficients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation-based integration rather than expression-based integration — the OnClass paper shows ontology-score PCA embeddings cluster cells by type better than Scanorama (P < 7e-293), so Scanorama is the wrong primary method when label-quality clustering is the objective Data has not undergone noise reduction — Scanorama is designed to run downstream of imputation/highly-variable gene filtering, not as a first processing step Only a single dataset is present — Scanorama's mutual-NN matching requires multiple datasets/batches to integrate

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has continuous nuisance covariate scores (e.g., cell cycle or sex scores) that must be regressed out as a pre-processing baseline before clustering or trajectory analysis.
skills.name: scanpy-covariate-regression
skills.search_text: scanpy-covariate-regression Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has continuous nuisance covariate scores (e.g., cell cycle or sex scores) that must be regressed out as a pre-processing baseline before clustering or trajectory analysis. When the goal is to preserve maximum biological signal at gene-expression level — regress_out retained only 30% of genes of interest in corrected HVGs versus 40% for SiFT knn-kernel filtering When correction is needed only in latent space rather than on gene expression — scVI performs correction at the level of a joint latent representation When no reliable marker gene lists or covariate scores exist to define the nuisance signal to regress http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Baseline approach for removing unwanted variation (e.g., cell cycle, sex) from single-cell RNA-seq data by regressing covariate scores out of gene expression with Scanpy's regress_out, evaluated here as a comparison baseline against SiFT and scVI on Drosophila wing disc data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Baseline approach for removing unwanted variation (e.g., cell cycle, sex) from single-cell RNA-seq data by regressing covariate scores out of gene expression with Scanpy's regress_out, evaluated here as a comparison baseline against SiFT and scVI on Drosophila wing disc data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to preserve maximum biological signal at gene-expression level — regress_out retained only 30% of genes of interest in corrected HVGs versus 40% for SiFT knn-kernel filtering When correction is needed only in latent space rather than on gene expression — scVI performs correction at the level of a joint latent representation When no reliable marker gene lists or covariate scores exist to define the nuisance signal to regress

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be preprocessed for Cancer-Finder inference — e.g. applying the model at scale to external scRNA-seq datasets such as the 152 CancerSCEM databases.
skills.name: scanpy-expression-normalization
skills.search_text: scanpy-expression-normalization Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be preprocessed for Cancer-Finder inference — e.g. applying the model at scale to external scRNA-seq datasets such as the 152 CancerSCEM databases. The input data is hematologic tumor scRNA-seq, where the article does not recommend Cancer-Finder The input is spatial transcriptomics (ST) data, which requires Cancer-Finder models retrained on spatial transcriptomic datasets rather than the scRNA-seq checkpoint The matrix is already normalized/log-transformed under a compatible scheme — re-normalizing with pp.normalize_total + log1p would double-transform the values http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalize raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices with SCANPY's pp.normalize_total followed by log1p (global-scaling, log-transformed normalization) so they conform to the input distribution expected by the Cancer-Finder pre-trained model before running inference with infer.py. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Normalize raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices with SCANPY's pp.normalize_total followed by log1p (global-scaling, log-transformed normalization) so they conform to the input distribution expected by the Cancer-Finder pre-trained model before running inference with infer.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data is hematologic tumor scRNA-seq, where the article does not recommend Cancer-Finder The input is spatial transcriptomics (ST) data, which requires Cancer-Finder models retrained on spatial transcriptomic datasets rather than the scRNA-seq checkpoint The matrix is already normalized/log-transformed under a compatible scheme — re-normalizing with pp.normalize_total + log1p would double-transform the values

skills.description: Use when re-implementing or auditing SenePy's score_hub on an AnnData object and you need a scanpy.score_genes-equivalent configuration (binarize=False, importance=False) as a ground-truth comparison for per-cell signature scores.
skills.name: scanpy-gene-scoring-equivalence
skills.search_text: scanpy-gene-scoring-equivalence Use when re-implementing or auditing SenePy's score_hub on an AnnData object and you need a scanpy.score_genes-equivalent configuration (binarize=False, importance=False) as a ground-truth comparison for per-cell signature scores. When the goal is the default SenePy senescence score itself — binarize=True and importance weighting should stay enabled, not be disabled to mimic scanpy When the AnnData contains scaled (z-scored) expression — score_hub explicitly requires non-scaled data When scoring against a gene set with no SenePy hub or importance weights (e.g. SenMayo gene lists), where plain scanpy.score_genes is the appropriate tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Cross-validate the SenePy score_hub senescence-scoring implementation against scanpy.score_genes by running SenePy with binarize=False and importance=False, which reproduces default scanpy gene-scoring behavior and provides a reference point for verifying re-implementations of per-cell signature scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Cross-validate the SenePy score_hub senescence-scoring implementation against scanpy.score_genes by running SenePy with binarize=False and importance=False, which reproduces default scanpy gene-scoring behavior and provides a reference point for verifying re-implementations of per-cell signature scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the default SenePy senescence score itself — binarize=True and importance weighting should stay enabled, not be disabled to mimic scanpy When the AnnData contains scaled (z-scored) expression — score_hub explicitly requires non-scaled data When scoring against a gene set with no SenePy hub or importance weights (e.g. SenMayo gene lists), where plain scanpy.score_genes is the appropriate tool

skills.name: scanpy-hvg-marker-selection
skills.search_text: scanpy-hvg-marker-selection Use when benchmarking unsupervised marker selection for single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., reconstructing the full transcriptome from k=50 markers on CITE-seq, Mouse Brain, Paul, or Zeisel datasets — and a Scanpy HVG baseline is needed to compare against MarkerMap, RandomBaseline, or PERSIST. skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices (AnnData) from scRNA-seq datasets need normalization to comparable expression scales prior to cell-type scoring, marker identification, or label transfer.
skills.name: scanpy-lognormalization-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scanpy-lognormalization-preprocessing Use when raw UMI count matrices (AnnData) from scRNA-seq datasets need normalization to comparable expression scales prior to cell-type scoring, marker identification, or label transfer. Input data is already normalized or provided as log(CPM + 1) or other normalized expression values rather than raw counts The downstream tool requires a different normalization convention, e.g. scNym which expects log(CPM + 1) with natural logarithm The analysis requires highly variable gene selection before integration — MASI deliberately skips HVG selection because only marker genes are used http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocess raw single-cell RNA-seq counts with LogNormalization — divide each cell's counts by its total, scale by 10,000, and log-transform — using Scanpy before marker-based integration with MASI. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Preprocess raw single-cell RNA-seq counts with LogNormalization — divide each cell's counts by its total, scale by 10,000, and log-transform — using Scanpy before marker-based integration with MASI.

skills.description: Use when raw count matrices (e.g., CSV count tables for SC or ST data) must be normalized, log-transformed, and QC-metric'd before feeding a mapping/integration model, or when a median-genes dropout rate is needed.
skills.name: scanpy-normalization-qc-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scanpy-normalization-qc-preprocessing Use when raw count matrices (e.g., CSV count tables for SC or ST data) must be normalized, log-transformed, and QC-metric'd before feeding a mapping/integration model, or when a median-genes dropout rate is needed.
