No base GRN from external hints (scATAC-seq/motifs) is available — read_base_GRN() is not needed and scGATE can be run with base_GRN left empty (NA), though the README notes scGATE_gate() is more suitable for small networks or when a base GRN is available The task is large-scale de novo GRN inference across thousands of genes without a refined candidate TF list — the article states scGATE is currently applicable to a rather small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Parses a base gene regulatory network (GRN) derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF DNA binding motifs — supplied as a .parquet dataframe (e.g. Cusanovich2018_Spleen_peak_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) — using arrow::read_parquet() and scGATE's read_base_GRN() summarization, so the refined candidate TF–target pairs can be passed as the base_GRN argument to scGATE_edge()/scGATE_logic() for context-specific network inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Parses a base gene regulatory network (GRN) derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF DNA binding motifs — supplied as a .parquet dataframe (e.g. Cusanovich2018_Spleen_peak_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) — using arrow::read_parquet() and scGATE's read_base_GRN() summarization, so the refined candidate TF–target pairs can be passed as the base_GRN argument to scGATE_edge()/scGATE_logic() for context-specific network inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No base GRN from external hints (scATAC-seq/motifs) is available — read_base_GRN() is not needed and scGATE can be run with base_GRN left empty (NA), though the README notes scGATE_gate() is more suitable for small networks or when a base GRN is available The task is large-scale de novo GRN inference across thousands of genes without a refined candidate TF list — the article states scGATE is currently applicable to a rather small (<200) subset of genes with a refined list of candidate regulatory TFs

skills.description: Use when validating DICE-predicted primed cell states and their candidate regulatory factors (e.g. Runx2, Zfhx3, Foxo3, Lmo7) in matched scATAC-Seq profiles, by testing whether motif-derived TF activity is higher in primed versus unprimed cells.
skills.name: scatac-seq-chromvar-tf-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-chromvar-tf-activity-scoring Use when validating DICE-predicted primed cell states and their candidate regulatory factors (e.g. Runx2, Zfhx3, Foxo3, Lmo7) in matched scATAC-Seq profiles, by testing whether motif-derived TF activity is higher in primed versus unprimed cells. No matched scATAC-Seq data exist for the cell population — the article notes SHARE-Seq profiles were unavailable for one study, forcing approximate assignment of primed states in separate scATAC-Seq populations The goal is to cluster cells or call peaks from raw scATAC-Seq rather than score predefined candidate TF motifs; chromVAR is used here for motif-activity annotation, not cluster identification Candidate regulatory factors have no known binding motifs, since chromVAR deviation scores require motif annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 Computes transcription factor activity scores from peak-level scATAC-Seq data with chromVAR, using TF binding motifs, to validate primed states (e.g. HS- and IRS-primed TACs) predicted from scRNA-Seq data alone by DICE in matched single-cell multiome data (SHARE-Seq). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Computes transcription factor activity scores from peak-level scATAC-Seq data with chromVAR, using TF binding motifs, to validate primed states (e.g. HS- and IRS-primed TACs) predicted from scRNA-Seq data alone by DICE in matched single-cell multiome data (SHARE-Seq).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scATAC-Seq data exist for the cell population — the article notes SHARE-Seq profiles were unavailable for one study, forcing approximate assignment of primed states in separate scATAC-Seq populations The goal is to cluster cells or call peaks from raw scATAC-Seq rather than score predefined candidate TF motifs; chromVAR is used here for motif-activity annotation, not cluster identification Candidate regulatory factors have no known binding motifs, since chromVAR deviation scores require motif annotations

skills.description: Use when starting an scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC dataset) and low-quality cells, doublets, and high-dimensional tile/peak matrices must be filtered and reduced before clustering.
skills.name: scatac-seq-fragment-quality-control
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-fragment-quality-control Use when starting an scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC dataset) and low-quality cells, doublets, and high-dimensional tile/peak matrices must be filtered and reduced before clustering. Input is already a filtered, dimensionality-reduced scATAC-seq embedding or peak-count matrix with cell QC previously applied Data are scRNA-seq rather than scATAC-seq — SCALA's RNA module uses PCA (e.g. 25 PCs for the SF dataset), not fragment QC and LSI on 500-bp tiles Non-human, non-mouse datasets — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse for both modalities http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Performs cell-level quality control on scATAC-seq fragment data (TSS enrichment and unique nuclear fragment counts) within SCALA's ArchR-based pipeline, and reduces dimensionality of filtered chromatin accessibility data using latent semantic indexing (LSI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Performs cell-level quality control on scATAC-seq fragment data (TSS enrichment and unique nuclear fragment counts) within SCALA's ArchR-based pipeline, and reduces dimensionality of filtered chromatin accessibility data using latent semantic indexing (LSI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered, dimensionality-reduced scATAC-seq embedding or peak-count matrix with cell QC previously applied Data are scRNA-seq rather than scATAC-seq — SCALA's RNA module uses PCA (e.g. 25 PCs for the SF dataset), not fragment QC and LSI on 500-bp tiles Non-human, non-mouse datasets — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse for both modalities

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq-derived cell assignments or marker gene lists must be validated against matched scATAC-Seq data by testing whether target genes of lineage regulators (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8) show higher chromatin accessibility in the predicted cells.
skills.name: scatac-seq-gene-accessibility-quantification
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-gene-accessibility-quantification Use when scRNA-Seq-derived cell assignments or marker gene lists must be validated against matched scATAC-Seq data by testing whether target genes of lineage regulators (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8) show higher chromatin accessibility in the predicted cells. No matched scATAC-Seq data for the same cell types is available — the vignette notes that joint SHARE-Seq profiles were not available for the liver hematopoiesis study, and this validation approach requires separate ATAC profiles of the same cell types The query factor is not a transcription factor (e.g. UHRF1): it has no motif and hence no chromVAR TF activity, so only target-gene accessibility sums apply The goal is peak-level or cluster-level ATAC analysis rather than gene-level accessibility validation of predicted primed cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Quantify per-cell gene-level chromatin accessibility from scATAC-Seq peak data (peaks 3kb upstream plus gene body, log-normalized with Seurat) to validate scRNA-Seq-derived primed states, using marker-gene accessibility sums and chromVAR TF motif activity as validation readouts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Quantify per-cell gene-level chromatin accessibility from scATAC-Seq peak data (peaks 3kb upstream plus gene body, log-normalized with Seurat) to validate scRNA-Seq-derived primed states, using marker-gene accessibility sums and chromVAR TF motif activity as validation readouts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scATAC-Seq data for the same cell types is available — the vignette notes that joint SHARE-Seq profiles were not available for the liver hematopoiesis study, and this validation approach requires separate ATAC profiles of the same cell types The query factor is not a transcription factor (e.g. UHRF1): it has no motif and hence no chromVAR TF activity, so only target-gene accessibility sums apply The goal is peak-level or cluster-level ATAC analysis rather than gene-level accessibility validation of predicted primed cells

skills.description: Use when the input is scATAC-seq data and pseudo-space reconstruction is needed but no spatial ATAC-seq reference is available, requiring conversion to a gene activity matrix (via Signac) so ST data can serve as the spatial reference in scSpace.
skills.name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-inference
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-gene-activity-inference Use when the input is scATAC-seq data and pseudo-space reconstruction is needed but no spatial ATAC-seq reference is available, requiring conversion to a gene activity matrix (via Signac) so ST data can serve as the spatial reference in scSpace. Input is already a gene-expression matrix (scRNA-seq or ST) — no gene activity conversion via Signac is needed before scSpace An appropriate spatial ATAC-seq reference exists for the tissue — direct spatial ATAC-seq referencing is preferable to substituting an ST reference The tissue has low spatial coherence or weak correspondence with the chosen ST reference — scSpace should be applied cautiously in such cases http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts scATAC-seq data (e.g., mouse cortex ISSAAC-seq) into a gene-by-cell gene activity matrix using Signac so that the data becomes compatible with scSpace, which uses spatial transcriptomics (ST) data as a reference to reconstruct the pseudo-space of single cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Converts scATAC-seq data (e.g., mouse cortex ISSAAC-seq) into a gene-by-cell gene activity matrix using Signac so that the data becomes compatible with scSpace, which uses spatial transcriptomics (ST) data as a reference to reconstruct the pseudo-space of single cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-expression matrix (scRNA-seq or ST) — no gene activity conversion via Signac is needed before scSpace An appropriate spatial ATAC-seq reference exists for the tissue — direct spatial ATAC-seq referencing is preferable to substituting an ST reference The tissue has low spatial coherence or weak correspondence with the chosen ST reference — scSpace should be applied cautiously in such cases

skills.description: Use when input is a scATAC-seq dataset converted to a cell-by-gene activity score matrix and the goal is cell clustering and marker-gene identification via differential expression of the resulting clusters.
skills.name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-analysis Use when input is a scATAC-seq dataset converted to a cell-by-gene activity score matrix and the goal is cell clustering and marker-gene identification via differential expression of the resulting clusters. Input is a raw scATAC-seq cell-by-bin/peak matrix not yet converted to gene activity scores — use a converter such as BinToGene or cisTopic topic modeling first. Data are already annotated single-cell gene expression with reference labels available for supervised transfer — scanpy Ingest or SingleR label transfer is more appropriate than unsupervised cluster-then-DE annotation. Protein/imaging data (CODEX, CITE-seq) — Cellar's protein workflows such as STvEA mapping, not gene-activity DE analysis, apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Analyze scATAC-seq cell-by-gene activity score matrices (e.g., PBMC 10k converted to gene activity scores) by CPM/log1p normalization, randomized-SVD PCA, faiss approximate-neighbor Leiden clustering, and diffxpy Welch's t-test DE to recover known cell-type markers such as the NK-cell marker KLRD1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Analyze scATAC-seq cell-by-gene activity score matrices (e.g., PBMC 10k converted to gene activity scores) by CPM/log1p normalization, randomized-SVD PCA, faiss approximate-neighbor Leiden clustering, and diffxpy Welch's t-test DE to recover known cell-type markers such as the NK-cell marker KLRD1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw scATAC-seq cell-by-bin/peak matrix not yet converted to gene activity scores — use a converter such as BinToGene or cisTopic topic modeling first. Data are already annotated single-cell gene expression with reference labels available for supervised transfer — scanpy Ingest or SingleR label transfer is more appropriate than unsupervised cluster-then-DE annotation. Protein/imaging data (CODEX, CITE-seq) — Cellar's protein workflows such as STvEA mapping, not gene-activity DE analysis, apply.

skills.description: Use when integrating paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data (e.g. the 10X Genomics PBMC multi-omic dataset) with tools that operate on gene-by-cell matrices rather than peak matrices.
skills.name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-conversion
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-conversion Use when integrating paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data (e.g. the 10X Genomics PBMC multi-omic dataset) with tools that operate on gene-by-cell matrices rather than peak matrices. The integration modality is CITE-seq protein data, which contains only a few hundred features and makes identifying shared features between modalities difficult You need chromatin accessibility information at peak/region resolution rather than gene-level summaries — the conversion to a gene activity matrix may lead to information loss The input is a single scRNA-seq dataset with only sequencing-platform batch effects and no second modality http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts an scATAC-seq open chromatin peak matrix into a gene activity matrix using the MAESTRO package so that ATAC data can be treated as an expression-like batch and integrated with scRNA-seq data by methods such as scCobra, scVI, and Seurat. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Converts an scATAC-seq open chromatin peak matrix into a gene activity matrix using the MAESTRO package so that ATAC data can be treated as an expression-like batch and integrated with scRNA-seq data by methods such as scCobra, scVI, and Seurat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The integration modality is CITE-seq protein data, which contains only a few hundred features and makes identifying shared features between modalities difficult You need chromatin accessibility information at peak/region resolution rather than gene-level summaries — the conversion to a gene activity matrix may lead to information loss The input is a single scRNA-seq dataset with only sequencing-platform batch effects and no second modality

skills.description: Use when a scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be reduced to an informative peak subset before clustering or trajectory inference, and standard HVF selection is suspected to obscure cell type structure.
skills.name: scatac-seq-peak-accessibility-processing
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-peak-accessibility-processing Use when a scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be reduced to an informative peak subset before clustering or trajectory inference, and standard HVF selection is suspected to obscure cell type structure. The input is already a reduced or curated feature set, so correlation-based reselection adds no information. The analysis is supervised cell-type classification (e.g., SingleR-style annotation against a reference) rather than unsupervised feature selection for clustering or trajectory inference. The data modality is bulk ATAC-seq or other non-single-cell accessibility data where the cell-level correlation structure DUBStepR relies on is absent. Applies DUBStepR correlation-based feature selection to single-cell ATAC-seq peak-by-cell accessibility matrices (e.g., Buenrostro et al. human bone marrow, GSE96583), adapting the gene-based algorithm to peaks, and evaluates selected peaks by whether downstream Monocle 3 trajectories recover known differentiation topology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Applies DUBStepR correlation-based feature selection to single-cell ATAC-seq peak-by-cell accessibility matrices (e.g., Buenrostro et al. human bone marrow, GSE96583), adapting the gene-based algorithm to peaks, and evaluates selected peaks by whether downstream Monocle 3 trajectories recover known differentiation topology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced or curated feature set, so correlation-based reselection adds no information. The analysis is supervised cell-type classification (e.g., SingleR-style annotation against a reference) rather than unsupervised feature selection for clustering or trajectory inference. The data modality is bulk ATAC-seq or other non-single-cell accessibility data where the cell-level correlation structure DUBStepR relies on is absent.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers against a known set of ground-truth peaks (e.g. scReadSim synthetic BAM from the sci-ATAC-seq dataset), or when choosing a peak caller for single-cell ATAC data.
skills.name: scatac-seq-peak-calling-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-peak-calling-benchmarking Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers against a known set of ground-truth peaks (e.g. scReadSim synthetic BAM from the sci-ATAC-seq dataset), or when choosing a peak caller for single-cell ATAC data. Benchmarking scRNA-seq UMI deduplication tools — use the scReadSim synthetic UMI count matrix ground truth instead The tool under test is an isoform-level or alternative-splicing method — scReadSim currently provides only gene-level/peak-level ground truths, not isoform abundance Input data lacks ground-truth peaks/non-peaks (real data without designed truth) — recall/precision/F1 cannot be computed, only qualitative cross-tool overlap http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarks scATAC-seq peak-calling tools (MACS3, HOMER, SEACR, HMMRATAC) on scReadSim synthetic reads whose designed ground-truth peaks and non-peaks allow exact recall, precision, and F1 computation. HMMRATAC and MACS3 emerge as top performers in the scReadSim benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks scATAC-seq peak-calling tools (MACS3, HOMER, SEACR, HMMRATAC) on scReadSim synthetic reads whose designed ground-truth peaks and non-peaks allow exact recall, precision, and F1 computation. HMMRATAC and MACS3 emerge as top performers in the scReadSim benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking scRNA-seq UMI deduplication tools — use the scReadSim synthetic UMI count matrix ground truth instead The tool under test is an isoform-level or alternative-splicing method — scReadSim currently provides only gene-level/peak-level ground truths, not isoform abundance Input data lacks ground-truth peaks/non-peaks (real data without designed truth) — recall/precision/F1 cannot be computed, only qualitative cross-tool overlap

skills.description: Use when analyzing 10x scATAC-seq (or multi-omics) data and you want clustering/benchmarking feature matrices that combine accessible-chromatin peaks with locus-specific TE counts from MATES, alongside TE-only and multi-mapping-TE-only perspectives.
skills.name: scatac-seq-peak-plus-te-feature-construction
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-peak-plus-te-feature-construction Use when analyzing 10x scATAC-seq (or multi-omics) data and you want clustering/benchmarking feature matrices that combine accessible-chromatin peaks with locus-specific TE counts from MATES, alongside TE-only and multi-mapping-TE-only perspectives. Input is already a processed cell-by-feature count matrix — this skill covers quantification from aligned BAMs, not downstream re-clustering of existing matrices Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where MATES' 2001 bp coverage vector gives inaccurate multi-mapping rates TE copies lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions (e.g., highly identical HERVK isoforms), where locus-specific allocation is unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Builds combined Peak+TE cell-by-feature matrices for 10x scATAC-seq data, where MATES-quantified locus-specific transposable element counts are appended to standard ATAC peak counts so downstream clustering can leverage both open-chromatin peaks and TE loci. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Builds combined Peak+TE cell-by-feature matrices for 10x scATAC-seq data, where MATES-quantified locus-specific transposable element counts are appended to standard ATAC peak counts so downstream clustering can leverage both open-chromatin peaks and TE loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed cell-by-feature count matrix — this skill covers quantification from aligned BAMs, not downstream re-clustering of existing matrices Quantifying long autonomously expressed TEs such as L1HS spanning several thousand bases, where MATES' 2001 bp coverage vector gives inaccurate multi-mapping rates TE copies lacking uniquely mappable flanking regions (e.g., highly identical HERVK isoforms), where locus-specific allocation is unreliable

skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq BAM files (e.g. FACS-purified mouse cell samples) should be characterized by TE open-chromatin content alone, to test whether TE accessibility recovers known cell identities or reveals TE-specific openness.
skills.name: scatac-seq-te-accessibility-quantification
skills.search_text: scatac-seq-te-accessibility-quantification Use when scATAC-seq BAM files (e.g. FACS-purified mouse cell samples) should be characterized by TE open-chromatin content alone, to test whether TE accessibility recovers known cell identities or reveals TE-specific openness. The input is single-cell RNA-seq data quantifying TE expression rather than chromatin accessibility — use scTE with scTE_build indices instead of scTEATAC. The analysis requires standard peak-based ATAC-seq calls or gene-level accessibility rather than TE-mapped reads. A genome assembly or RepeatMasker annotation for which no rmsk goldenPath download exists has not been prepared as a custom TE BED. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Quantify per-cell chromatin accessibility of transposable elements from scATAC-seq BAM files using scTEATAC, then use the resulting cell-by-TE accessibility matrix alone to discriminate cell types and identify cell-type-specific open TEs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Quantify per-cell chromatin accessibility of transposable elements from scATAC-seq BAM files using scTEATAC, then use the resulting cell-by-TE accessibility matrix alone to discriminate cell types and identify cell-type-specific open TEs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell RNA-seq data quantifying TE expression rather than chromatin accessibility — use scTE with scTE_build indices instead of scTEATAC. The analysis requires standard peak-based ATAC-seq calls or gene-level accessibility rather than TE-mapped reads. A genome assembly or RepeatMasker annotation for which no rmsk goldenPath download exists has not been prepared as a custom TE BED.

skills.description: Use when preparing scATAC-seq data (binary cell-by-bin accessibility matrix) to feed into cross-modality integration (e.g., with scRNA-seq via uniPort's coupled-VAE) alongside log-normalized gene expression.
skills.name: scatac-tfidf-lsi-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scatac-tfidf-lsi-preprocessing Use when preparing scATAC-seq data (binary cell-by-bin accessibility matrix) to feed into cross-modality integration (e.g., with scRNA-seq via uniPort's coupled-VAE) alongside log-normalized gene expression. When the ATAC data will be summarized as gene activity scores computed by an external tool (e.g., SnapATAC) instead of processed from the peak matrix — the paper notes uniPort's scATAC integration is based on gene activity scores and tested alternatives When data lacks a peak/bin-level accessibility matrix (e.g., only pre-LSI embeddings or chromatin summary stats are available) When memory is severely constrained and save_OT=True dense OT plans are requested downstream — the paper warns dense T storage needs substantial memory http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Preprocess single-cell ATAC-seq data for multi-omics integration by applying TF-IDF weighting to a binary cell-by-peak/bin accessibility matrix followed by latent semantic indexing (LSI) dimensionality reduction, as implemented in uniPort's TFIDF_LSI function. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Preprocess single-cell ATAC-seq data for multi-omics integration by applying TF-IDF weighting to a binary cell-by-peak/bin accessibility matrix followed by latent semantic indexing (LSI) dimensionality reduction, as implemented in uniPort's TFIDF_LSI function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the ATAC data will be summarized as gene activity scores computed by an external tool (e.g., SnapATAC) instead of processed from the peak matrix — the paper notes uniPort's scATAC integration is based on gene activity scores and tested alternatives When data lacks a peak/bin-level accessibility matrix (e.g., only pre-LSI embeddings or chromatin summary stats are available) When memory is severely constrained and save_OT=True dense OT plans are requested downstream — the paper warns dense T storage needs substantial memory

skills.description: Use when analyzing scATAC/SNARE-seq chromatin accessibility as a cell-by-peak matrix (e.g. ~31,758 cells x 575,265 peaks) and you need unsupervised topics and clusters in the chromatin modality before assigning cell types.
skills.name: scatc-topic-modeling-on-scatc-seq-chromatin-accessibility
skills.search_text: scatc-topic-modeling-on-scatc-seq-chromatin-accessibility Use when analyzing scATAC/SNARE-seq chromatin accessibility as a cell-by-peak matrix (e.g. ~31,758 cells x 575,265 peaks) and you need unsupervised topics and clusters in the chromatin modality before assigning cell types. The input is already a gene-expression matrix with no chromatin-accessibility (cell-by-peak) modality — cisTopic topic modeling over peaks does not apply; use expression-based dimensionality reduction instead. The scATAC data was converted to a gene activity score matrix (e.g. via BinToGene against GENCODE v35) and expression tools are intended — topic modeling on raw peaks is unnecessary. Cell barcodes are not shared between the ATAC and RNA modalities, so cell-ID-based label transfer of cluster assignments is impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Run cisTopic probabilistic topic modeling on a single-cell multiome (SNARE-seq) chromatin-accessibility cell-by-peak matrix to discover cis-regulatory topics, then cluster the cell-by-topic matrix to derive joint-modality cell clusters. This is the Cellar approach for extracting structure from sparse scATAC data so labels can be transferred to the paired expression modality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29744-0
skills.summary: Run cisTopic probabilistic topic modeling on a single-cell multiome (SNARE-seq) chromatin-accessibility cell-by-peak matrix to discover cis-regulatory topics, then cluster the cell-by-topic matrix to derive joint-modality cell clusters. This is the Cellar approach for extracting structure from sparse scATAC data so labels can be transferred to the paired expression modality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene-expression matrix with no chromatin-accessibility (cell-by-peak) modality — cisTopic topic modeling over peaks does not apply; use expression-based dimensionality reduction instead. The scATAC data was converted to a gene activity score matrix (e.g. via BinToGene against GENCODE v35) and expression tools are intended — topic modeling on raw peaks is unnecessary. Cell barcodes are not shared between the ATAC and RNA modalities, so cell-ID-based label transfer of cluster assignments is impossible.

skills.description: Use when comparing a per-cell quality metric (e.g. silhouette coefficient against true cluster labels) between an original data representation and alternative feature constructions, and a scatter/diagonal visualization with a fraction-above-diagonal summary is needed.
skills.name: scatter-plot-figure-generation
skills.search_text: scatter-plot-figure-generation Use when comparing a per-cell quality metric (e.g. silhouette coefficient against true cluster labels) between an original data representation and alternative feature constructions, and a scatter/diagonal visualization with a fraction-above-diagonal summary is needed. The per-cell values to compare are not paired (no original-vs-alternative metric for the same cells), so a scatter-vs-diagonal interpretation is meaningless The goal is clustering itself or accuracy benchmarking of clustering algorithms (e.g. SSCC vs SC3 ARI comparison) rather than visualizing per-cell silhouette accordance Only aggregate summary statistics are available — the skill requires per-cell silhouette values to draw scatter panels http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assembles per-cell scatter panels comparing silhouette values of original scRNA-seq expression profiles against silhouette values of engineered feature representations (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman, autoencoder) into a Figure 2-style composite plot, quantifying the fraction of cells above the diagonal. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: Assembles per-cell scatter panels comparing silhouette values of original scRNA-seq expression profiles against silhouette values of engineered feature representations (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman, autoencoder) into a Figure 2-style composite plot, quantifying the fraction of cells above the diagonal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The per-cell values to compare are not paired (no original-vs-alternative metric for the same cells), so a scatter-vs-diagonal interpretation is meaningless The goal is clustering itself or accuracy benchmarking of clustering algorithms (e.g. SSCC vs SC3 ARI comparison) rather than visualizing per-cell silhouette accordance Only aggregate summary statistics are available — the skill requires per-cell silhouette values to draw scatter panels

skills.description: Use when two independent feature-ranking metrics (e.g., expression magnitude vs. variance-based loadings) must be compared to decide whether they identify the same significant features, and you need quadrant counts plus a correlation statistic as evidence.
skills.name: scatter-quadrant-threshold-visualization
skills.search_text: scatter-quadrant-threshold-visualization Use when two independent feature-ranking metrics (e.g., expression magnitude vs. variance-based loadings) must be compared to decide whether they identify the same significant features, and you need quadrant counts plus a correlation statistic as evidence. Input is already a ranked or filtered feature list without raw per-feature metric values — thresholds and quadrant counts cannot be recomputed The two metrics are not computed on the same feature universe (e.g., aTARs vs. uTARs), making quadrant overlap meaningless The goal is differential expression testing of TARs across clusters rather than comparing two continuous feature-ranking metrics http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Build a thresholded scatter plot comparing two ranking metrics for genomic features (here, uTAR pseudo-bulk read coverage vs. summed absolute Seurat PC loadings across the first 5 PCs), count features in each quadrant, and quantify agreement via Pearson correlation. skills.summary: SpatialScope's third step: a conditional score-based generative model trained on the snRNA-seq reference infers posterior-mean single-cell, transcriptome-wide expression at each segmented nucleus by annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling, upgrading spot-level Visium data to single-cell resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ST platform already provides single-cell, whole-transcriptome resolution, or the goal is only spot-level cell-type proportion estimation — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD suffice Only a few hundred predefined genes are measured with no scRNA-seq reference to train the score-based generative model Platform effects between the ST data and the single-cell reference cannot be appropriately corrected — the article warns decomposition results 'would not be satisfactory' in that case

skills.description: Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq V2) must be decomposed to single-cell resolution using a paired scRNA-seq reference, or when image-based ST data need transcriptome-wide expression inference.
skills.name: score-based-generative-decomposition-pipeline
skills.search_text: score-based-generative-decomposition-pipeline Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq V2) must be decomposed to single-cell resolution using a paired scRNA-seq reference, or when image-based ST data need transcriptome-wide expression inference. Only spot-level cell-type proportions are needed without single-cell resolution — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD suffice and are cheaper No paired histological/nuclear image is available and the platform is not Slide-seq, so nucleus segmentation and cell-count estimation cannot be performed reliably A gene panel of only a few hundred measured genes is the target output rather than transcriptome-wide inference — image-based ST (MERFISH/seqFISH) may already suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Three-step SpatialScope workflow — nucleus segmentation, cell type identification with Potts smoothness, and gene expression decomposition via a conditional score-based generative model with annealed Langevin dynamics sampling — that resolves spot-level spatial transcriptomics data to single-cell, transcriptome-wide resolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Three-step SpatialScope workflow — nucleus segmentation, cell type identification with Potts smoothness, and gene expression decomposition via a conditional score-based generative model with annealed Langevin dynamics sampling — that resolves spot-level spatial transcriptomics data to single-cell, transcriptome-wide resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only spot-level cell-type proportions are needed without single-cell resolution — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD suffice and are cheaper No paired histological/nuclear image is available and the platform is not Slide-seq, so nucleus segmentation and cell-count estimation cannot be performed reliably A gene panel of only a few hundred measured genes is the target output rather than transcriptome-wide inference — image-based ST (MERFISH/seqFISH) may already suffice

skills.description: Use when you have nucleus-segmented or singlet/doublet-classified spatial transcriptomics spots plus a labeled scRNA-seq reference and need transcriptome-wide per-cell expression beyond spot-level resolution.
skills.name: score-based-generative-decomposition-spatial-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: score-based-generative-decomposition-spatial-transcriptomics Use when you have nucleus-segmented or singlet/doublet-classified spatial transcriptomics spots plus a labeled scRNA-seq reference and need transcriptome-wide per-cell expression beyond spot-level resolution. You only need spot-level cell-type proportions rather than per-cell expression — simpler deconvolution tools (RCTD, Cell2location, CARD) suffice, and the generative training/decomposition cost (hours or days) is unnecessary You lack a labeled scRNA-seq reference or cannot correct platform effects between reference and ST data — the article warns results 'would not be satisfactory if the platform effects are not appropriately corrected' No histological image or equivalent (e.g., DAPI) is available and cell counts per spot cannot be estimated, complicating the per-cell decomposition http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition step: a score-based conditional generative model learned from a labeled scRNA-seq reference is combined with annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling to infer transcriptome-wide, single-cell-resolution expression for every nucleus/cell segmented from Visium or Slide-seq spots, after cross-platform batch correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition step: a score-based conditional generative model learned from a labeled scRNA-seq reference is combined with annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling to infer transcriptome-wide, single-cell-resolution expression for every nucleus/cell segmented from Visium or Slide-seq spots, after cross-platform batch correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need spot-level cell-type proportions rather than per-cell expression — simpler deconvolution tools (RCTD, Cell2location, CARD) suffice, and the generative training/decomposition cost (hours or days) is unnecessary You lack a labeled scRNA-seq reference or cannot correct platform effects between reference and ST data — the article warns results 'would not be satisfactory if the platform effects are not appropriately corrected' No histological image or equivalent (e.g., DAPI) is available and cell counts per spot cannot be estimated, complicating the per-cell decomposition

skills.description: Use when seq-based ST data (Slide-seq V2, Visium) has dropout or sparse gene expression and a paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference is available, and you need to recover/impute whole-transcriptome expression and benchmark the correction.
skills.name: score-based-generative-dropout-correction
skills.search_text: score-based-generative-dropout-correction Use when seq-based ST data (Slide-seq V2, Visium) has dropout or sparse gene expression and a paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference is available, and you need to recover/impute whole-transcriptome expression and benchmark the correction. When the ST data are image-based (e.g., MERFISH) already at single-cell resolution — the article's stated use case here is enhancing seq-based data like Slide-seq V2, not image-based panels When no paired single-cell reference atlas is available for the tissue, since the score model is trained on cell-type-specific expression from the reference When the goal is cell-type proportion estimation only (use deconvolution tools such as RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD) rather than transcriptome-wide expression recovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Corrects simulated technical dropouts in spatial transcriptomics (e.g., Slide-seq V2 cerebellum) by running SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition, which uses a conditional score-based generative model trained on a paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference and annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling, then benchmarks the corrected expression against Tangram using MAE and PCC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Corrects simulated technical dropouts in spatial transcriptomics (e.g., Slide-seq V2 cerebellum) by running SpatialScope's gene expression decomposition, which uses a conditional score-based generative model trained on a paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference and annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling, then benchmarks the corrected expression against Tangram using MAE and PCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the ST data are image-based (e.g., MERFISH) already at single-cell resolution — the article's stated use case here is enhancing seq-based data like Slide-seq V2, not image-based panels When no paired single-cell reference atlas is available for the tissue, since the score model is trained on cell-type-specific expression from the reference When the goal is cell-type proportion estimation only (use deconvolution tools such as RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD) rather than transcriptome-wide expression recovery

skills.description: Use when you need a trained conditional score network from a single-cell RNA-seq reference before running SpatialScope's Langevin-dynamics posterior sampling for gene expression decomposition or imputation.
skills.name: score-based-generative-model-training
skills.search_text: score-based-generative-model-training Use when you need a trained conditional score network from a single-cell RNA-seq reference before running SpatialScope's Langevin-dynamics posterior sampling for gene expression decomposition or imputation. When only cell-type proportions per spot are needed and single-cell resolution is unnecessary — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, CARD, or spatialDWLS estimate proportions without a generative model When no paired scRNA-seq reference is available, since the score network must approximate the expression distribution of labeled cell types from reference data When a quick alignment of existing reference cells to spots suffices — alignment-based methods such as Tangram or CytoSPACE assign cells rather than sampling from a learned distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains SpatialScope's conditional score-based generative network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k) on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Ref_Heart_sanger_D2.h5ad) via denoising score matching, so the learned score function can later drive annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling for spot decomposition and gene imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Trains SpatialScope's conditional score-based generative network s_theta(x, sigma_l, mu_k) on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Ref_Heart_sanger_D2.h5ad) via denoising score matching, so the learned score function can later drive annealed Langevin dynamics posterior sampling for spot decomposition and gene imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only cell-type proportions per spot are needed and single-cell resolution is unnecessary — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, CARD, or spatialDWLS estimate proportions without a generative model When no paired scRNA-seq reference is available, since the score network must approximate the expression distribution of labeled cell types from reference data When a quick alignment of existing reference cells to spots suffices — alignment-based methods such as Tangram or CytoSPACE assign cells rather than sampling from a learned distribution

skills.description: Use when many candidate clusterings exist for a trajectory-inference benchmark and you must compare selection criteria (e.g. connectivity+VRC vs ASW vs VRC vs random) by how trajectory quality degrades over the top-n ranked candidates.
skills.name: score-curve-aggregation-across-clusterings
skills.search_text: score-curve-aggregation-across-clusterings Use when many candidate clusterings exist for a trajectory-inference benchmark and you must compare selection criteria (e.g. connectivity+VRC vs ASW vs VRC vs random) by how trajectory quality degrades over the top-n ranked candidates. The dataset has extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types simultaneously, where k-medoids does not work properly and clusterings must be merged manually before ranking is meaningful The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles, which Totem cannot generate The trajectory is multi-root (converging), since dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime and scores based on pseudotime are unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Benchmarks clustering-selection criteria for Totem trajectory inference by ranking 10,000 k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings per criterion, inferring MST trajectories from the top-n clusterings with Slingshot, and aggregating maximum/mean dynverse overall scores as score-versus-n curves to compare Totem cell connectivity+VRC against ASW, VRC-alone, and random ranking. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Benchmarks clustering-selection criteria for Totem trajectory inference by ranking 10,000 k-medoids (CLARA) clusterings per criterion, inferring MST trajectories from the top-n clusterings with Slingshot, and aggregating maximum/mean dynverse overall scores as score-versus-n curves to compare Totem cell connectivity+VRC against ASW, VRC-alone, and random ranking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types simultaneously, where k-medoids does not work properly and clusterings must be merged manually before ranking is meaningful The expected trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles, which Totem cannot generate The trajectory is multi-root (converging), since dynplot will not generate the correct pseudotime and scores based on pseudotime are unreliable

skills.description: Use when you have a phenotype x feature score matrix M (e.g., from a scRNA-seq dataset like Tabula Muris, mouse cortex, or HCA) and need every phenotype pair (i,j) distinguished at least K times by selected markers.
skills.name: score-matrix-integer-rounding
skills.search_text: score-matrix-integer-rounding Use when you have a phenotype x feature score matrix M (e.g., from a scRNA-seq dataset like Tabula Muris, mouse cortex, or HCA) and need every phenotype pair (i,j) distinguished at least K times by selected markers. The feature-selection goal is all-relevant (identifying every feature related to the target) rather than a minimal set that discriminates every phenotype pair — mRMR-style or all-relevance methods fit better Raw count data has not been log-transformed and normalized first, which the README notes is needed when working with raw counts There is only a small number of distinct groups with non-overlapping differential genes, where ordinary per-group DE marker selection suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reduction step in the phenotype cover (PC) marker-selection framework in which a real-valued phenotype x feature score matrix M is rounded to integer multiplicities so the PC problem becomes multiset multicover and greedy selection (G-PC) can be applied. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Reduction step in the phenotype cover (PC) marker-selection framework in which a real-valued phenotype x feature score matrix M is rounded to integer multiplicities so the PC problem becomes multiset multicover and greedy selection (G-PC) can be applied.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature-selection goal is all-relevant (identifying every feature related to the target) rather than a minimal set that discriminates every phenotype pair — mRMR-style or all-relevance methods fit better Raw count data has not been log-transformed and normalized first, which the README notes is needed when working with raw counts There is only a small number of distinct groups with non-overlapping differential genes, where ordinary per-group DE marker selection suffices

skills.description: Use when scorecard_functions.scorecard(df,param_dict) has already generated the four single-quadrant assignments and plots and you need the assembled full scorecard image per pairwise comparison, e.g. VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs control.
skills.name: scorecard-plot-reconstruction
skills.search_text: scorecard-plot-reconstruction Use when scorecard_functions.scorecard(df,param_dict) has already generated the four single-quadrant assignments and plots and you need the assembled full scorecard image per pairwise comparison, e.g. VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs control. The 'multiplication factor' is set to 1, which produces a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard, so quadrant reconstruction of scorecard regions does not apply No individual quadrant outputs have been generated yet — reconstruct_scorecard must be called only after scorecard(df,param_dict) has processed all four quadrants The dataset lacks pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV; the scorecard does not compute differential expression itself (e.g. dataset 1 fold-changes were pre-computed via TRANSIT resampling with beta-geometric normalization) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Rebuilds the complete scorecard figure from the four individually computed quadrant plots using scorecard_functions.reconstruct_scorecard, producing the full multi-region visualization plus JSON outcome files in save_dir after scorecard() has processed each quadrant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Rebuilds the complete scorecard figure from the four individually computed quadrant plots using scorecard_functions.reconstruct_scorecard, producing the full multi-region visualization plus JSON outcome files in save_dir after scorecard() has processed each quadrant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The 'multiplication factor' is set to 1, which produces a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard, so quadrant reconstruction of scorecard regions does not apply No individual quadrant outputs have been generated yet — reconstruct_scorecard must be called only after scorecard(df,param_dict) has processed all four quadrants The dataset lacks pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV; the scorecard does not compute differential expression itself (e.g. dataset 1 fold-changes were pre-computed via TRANSIT resampling with beta-geometric normalization)

skills.description: Use when a CSV contains per-gene log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons (e.g. VAN/LZD/CPT antibiotics, AGXX vs silver coatings) and you need data-driven identification of extreme or moderately changing genes without preselecting them.
skills.name: scorecard-quadrant-classification
skills.search_text: scorecard-quadrant-classification Use when a CSV contains per-gene log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons (e.g. VAN/LZD/CPT antibiotics, AGXX vs silver coatings) and you need data-driven identification of extreme or moderately changing genes without preselecting them. The dataset has raw counts or TPMs only — scorecard requires pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV, as stated in the README You only need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering or extreme-region detection (set 'multiplication factor' to 1; the added quadrant machinery is unnecessary) Input is a single-condition experiment with no pairwise treatment/control comparisons to contrast (the scorecard compares two treatments against a control per call) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Applies the Python scorecard_functions library to classify genes from pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns into significance-filtered quadrants (regions of interest) of a four-way scorecard plot, per pairwise experimental comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Applies the Python scorecard_functions library to classify genes from pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns into significance-filtered quadrants (regions of interest) of a four-way scorecard plot, per pairwise experimental comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has raw counts or TPMs only — scorecard requires pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns in the CSV, as stated in the README You only need a standard four-way plot without significance filtering or extreme-region detection (set 'multiplication factor' to 1; the added quadrant machinery is unnecessary) Input is a single-condition experiment with no pairwise treatment/control comparisons to contrast (the scorecard compares two treatments against a control per call)

skills.description: Use when a CSV holds pre-computed log2 fold-change and padj columns for pairwise condition comparisons and you need to identify statistically significant extreme gene regulation (down- or up-regulated) per quadrant across multiple antibiotic or treatment contrasts.
skills.name: scorecard-region-of-interest-gene-assignment
skills.search_text: scorecard-region-of-interest-gene-assignment Use when a CSV holds pre-computed log2 fold-change and padj columns for pairwise condition comparisons and you need to identify statistically significant extreme gene regulation (down- or up-regulated) per quadrant across multiple antibiotic or treatment contrasts. The input lacks pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the scorecard requires these as CSV columns and does not compute differential expression itself Setting multiplication factor to 1 is requested — this produces a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard region-of-interest structure Only a single condition pair is available with no interest in multi-comparison pattern synthesis — volcano plots or standard four-way plots are the simpler choices, and the scorecard's value is merging information across multiple comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Assign genes from pairwise differential-expression comparisons (log2 fold change plus adjusted p-values) to quadrant/region-of-interest zones of a scorecard using the Python scorecard_functions library, exposing extreme or moderate regulation patterns across multiple experimental conditions (e.g., VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs untreated controls in S. aureus dataset 1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00284-025-04435-3
skills.summary: Assign genes from pairwise differential-expression comparisons (log2 fold change plus adjusted p-values) to quadrant/region-of-interest zones of a scorecard using the Python scorecard_functions library, exposing extreme or moderate regulation patterns across multiple experimental conditions (e.g., VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs untreated controls in S. aureus dataset 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input lacks pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns — the scorecard requires these as CSV columns and does not compute differential expression itself Setting multiplication factor to 1 is requested — this produces a standard four-way plot rather than the scorecard region-of-interest structure Only a single condition pair is available with no interest in multi-comparison pattern synthesis — volcano plots or standard four-way plots are the simpler choices, and the scorecard's value is merging information across multiple comparisons

skills.description: Use when a user has a completed cellranger count output for 10x scRNAseq data and wants pathogen (viral or bacterial) reads aligned, quantified per cell, and appended to the filtered/raw feature-barcode matrices without leaving the host pipeline.
skills.name: scpathoquant-cli-parameterization
skills.search_text: scpathoquant-cli-parameterization Use when a user has a completed cellranger count output for 10x scRNAseq data and wants pathogen (viral or bacterial) reads aligned, quantified per cell, and appended to the filtered/raw feature-barcode matrices without leaving the host pipeline. The sequencing data are not 10x scRNAseq cellranger outputs — scPathoQuant is built specifically around 10x files (features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz, possorted_genome_bam.bam). Reads have already been aligned to the pathogen genome and quantified by another tool (e.g. ViralTrack, Venus, PathogenTrack); re-running SPQ would duplicate the integration step. Only host-cell transcriptomic analysis is needed with no pathogen genome reference available — the -p2genome fasta is mandatory. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Configures and launches the scPathoQuant Python package with its CLI parameters (-10x, -op, -p, -p2genome, -align, aligner-specific params, --tmp_removal) to align host-unaligned reads to a pathogen genome and integrate pathogen UMI counts back into 10x cellranger output in a single command. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Configures and launches the scPathoQuant Python package with its CLI parameters (-10x, -op, -p, -p2genome, -align, aligner-specific params, --tmp_removal) to align host-unaligned reads to a pathogen genome and integrate pathogen UMI counts back into 10x cellranger output in a single command.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing data are not 10x scRNAseq cellranger outputs — scPathoQuant is built specifically around 10x files (features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz, possorted_genome_bam.bam). Reads have already been aligned to the pathogen genome and quantified by another tool (e.g. ViralTrack, Venus, PathogenTrack); re-running SPQ would duplicate the integration step. Only host-cell transcriptomic analysis is needed with no pathogen genome reference available — the -p2genome fasta is mandatory.

skills.description: Use when very large scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., 35,699-cell RGC or 599,926-cell HCL droplet data) need low-dimensional embeddings that preserve global hierarchical structure, or when mapping new batches/patients batch-invariantly.
skills.name: scphere-model-training-and-inference
skills.search_text: scphere-model-training-and-inference Use when very large scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., 35,699-cell RGC or 599,926-cell HCL droplet data) need low-dimensional embeddings that preserve global hierarchical structure, or when mapping new batches/patients batch-invariantly. Data already consists of normalized embeddings or a feature table rather than raw UMI counts — scPhere models negative-binomial count observations directly The goal is local neighborhood visualization only, where t-SNE/UMAP already suffice and no batch correction or global hierarchical structure preservation is required Analyses requiring tools unavailable in hyperbolic space, such as efficient k-NN search, which the article notes are lacking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train and apply scPhere, a deep generative VAE that embeds scRNA-seq UMI count matrices into low-dimensional hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher) or hyperbolic latent spaces, avoiding the cell crowding of normal-prior VAEs and preserving hierarchical global structure better than t-SNE or UMAP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Train and apply scPhere, a deep generative VAE that embeds scRNA-seq UMI count matrices into low-dimensional hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher) or hyperbolic latent spaces, avoiding the cell crowding of normal-prior VAEs and preserving hierarchical global structure better than t-SNE or UMAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data already consists of normalized embeddings or a feature table rather than raw UMI counts — scPhere models negative-binomial count observations directly The goal is local neighborhood visualization only, where t-SNE/UMAP already suffice and no batch correction or global hierarchical structure preservation is required Analyses requiring tools unavailable in hyperbolic space, such as efficient k-NN search, which the article notes are lacking

skills.description: Use when a benchmark dataset has known ground-truth cell-type labels and per-cell supervised annotation accuracy must be quantified against other tools (e.g., EasyCellType, Garnett, SingleR).
skills.name: scpred-eigengene-classifier-training
skills.search_text: scpred-eigengene-classifier-training Use when a benchmark dataset has known ground-truth cell-type labels and per-cell supervised annotation accuracy must be quantified against other tools (e.g., EasyCellType, Garnett, SingleR). No labeled reference cells are available — marker-list querying methods like EasyCellType (GSEA / modified Fisher's exact test) are the appropriate choice instead Input is only a differential-expression marker list to check against cell marker databases — that is EasyCellType's workflow, not scPred training The task is cluster-level rather than per-cell annotation accuracy — supervised per-cell classifiers will not directly produce that output http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Supervised cell-type annotation skill that trains scPred's eigengene-based machine-learning classifier on a labeled reference subset (3500 sampled cells per simulated PBMC dataset) and scores per-cell prediction accuracy in both prediction and no-rejection variants. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Supervised cell-type annotation skill that trains scPred's eigengene-based machine-learning classifier on a labeled reference subset (3500 sampled cells per simulated PBMC dataset) and scores per-cell prediction accuracy in both prediction and no-rejection variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No labeled reference cells are available — marker-list querying methods like EasyCellType (GSEA / modified Fisher's exact test) are the appropriate choice instead Input is only a differential-expression marker list to check against cell marker databases — that is EasyCellType's workflow, not scPred training The task is cluster-level rather than per-cell annotation accuracy — supervised per-cell classifiers will not directly produce that output

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SMARTer, Smart-Seq2, CEL-Seq2, inDrop data from GEO/ArrayExpress accessions like GSE81608 or E-MTAB-5061) need cell type clustering and cluster-specific key gene identification without knowing the number of cell types in advance.
skills.name: scqa-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: scqa-pipeline-execution Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SMARTer, Smart-Seq2, CEL-Seq2, inDrop data from GEO/ArrayExpress accessions like GSE81608 or E-MTAB-5061) need cell type clustering and cluster-specific key gene identification without knowing the number of cell types in advance. When the input is already a feature-reduced or pre-clustered representation (e.g., a dimensionality-reduced embedding), since scQA expects the filtered cells-by-genes matrix from pre.R When the number of cell types must be specified in advance or clusters must be constrained — scQA deliberately obviates a predetermined number of cell types When genes expressed outside the 2.5%–97.5% cell range carry the signal of interest — the pre.R filter removes them, and retaining only 2000 HVGs excluded some informative genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run the scQA dual-perspective (qualitative + quantitative) cell type identification pipeline on a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq count matrix: filter genes, select 2000 highly variable genes, build landmark-based binary and quantitative representations, and obtain cluster labels via label propagation. scQA identifies cell types without requiring a predetermined number of clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Run the scQA dual-perspective (qualitative + quantitative) cell type identification pipeline on a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq count matrix: filter genes, select 2000 highly variable genes, build landmark-based binary and quantitative representations, and obtain cluster labels via label propagation. scQA identifies cell types without requiring a predetermined number of clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is already a feature-reduced or pre-clustered representation (e.g., a dimensionality-reduced embedding), since scQA expects the filtered cells-by-genes matrix from pre.R When the number of cell types must be specified in advance or clusters must be constrained — scQA deliberately obviates a predetermined number of cell types When genes expressed outside the 2.5%–97.5% cell range carry the signal of interest — the pre.R filter removes them, and retaining only 2000 HVGs excluded some informative genes

skills.name: scran-count-normalization-and-cell-filtering
skills.search_text: scran-count-normalization-and-cell-filtering Use when a raw UMI count matrix (e.g., from Cell Ranger or Fluidigm C1 scRNA-seq) must be cleaned and normalized before trajectory inference, time-series differential expression, or cell-subcluster identification. skills.summary: Preprocessing pipeline from the scTITANS workflow that filters genes and cells from a raw UMI count matrix and normalizes it with scran's pool-and-deconvolute algorithm, producing a cleaned matrix ready for trajectory inference and time-dependent covariate analysis.

skills.description: Use when comparing batch mixing of two embedding spaces (e.g., BEENE vs PCA) on scRNA-seq data with batch labels and optionally biological labels, to test which space more sensitively detects batch effects via iLISI/kBET.
skills.name: scrna-batch-mixing-ilisi-quantification
skills.search_text: scrna-batch-mixing-ilisi-quantification Use when comparing batch mixing of two embedding spaces (e.g., BEENE vs PCA) on scRNA-seq data with batch labels and optionally biological labels, to test which space more sensitively detects batch effects via iLISI/kBET. The input embedding already comes from a batch-correction/integration method and the goal is post-correction mixing assessment — kBET's README advises that if rejection rate is 1 on corrected data you should additionally use silhouette width and PCA-based measures to gauge severity, not iLISI alone. The batch variable is undefined or the data has no replicate/study structure — iLISI measures mixing across a categorical batch variable and cannot be computed without one-hot-encoded batch labels. You only have Python and cannot install R (>= 4.1.0) with rpy2 (>= 3.4.0) — kBET has no Python implementation and is available only in R, so the kBET cross-check is not feasible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantify cell-type/batch mixing in single-cell RNA-seq embeddings by computing iLISI (inverse Simpson's index) per cell on a chosen embedding space (BEENE nonlinear embedding or PCA-50 baseline), optionally paired with R kBET rejection rates to cross-validate batch-effect detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Quantify cell-type/batch mixing in single-cell RNA-seq embeddings by computing iLISI (inverse Simpson's index) per cell on a chosen embedding space (BEENE nonlinear embedding or PCA-50 baseline), optionally paired with R kBET rejection rates to cross-validate batch-effect detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input embedding already comes from a batch-correction/integration method and the goal is post-correction mixing assessment — kBET's README advises that if rejection rate is 1 on corrected data you should additionally use silhouette width and PCA-based measures to gauge severity, not iLISI alone. The batch variable is undefined or the data has no replicate/study structure — iLISI measures mixing across a categorical batch variable and cannot be computed without one-hot-encoded batch labels. You only have Python and cannot install R (>= 4.1.0) with rpy2 (>= 3.4.0) — kBET has no Python implementation and is available only in R, so the kBET cross-check is not feasible.

skills.search_text: scrna-dataset-downsampling Use when benchmarking cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq count matrices and you need training sets of 500–10,000 cells and testing sets of 1,000–50,000 cells, or ~10,000-cell stratified subsets. Input data has not yet been quality-filtered (genes not expressed in any cells, cells with <200 genes, >20% mitochondrial expression, or unlabeled cells still present) — filtering must precede partitioning The analysis goal is marker-based (markersupervised) methods such as SCSA, SCINA or DigitalCellSorter that require a marker list rather than training/testing splits Data are bulk RNA-seq or already a precomputed feature/signature table with no per-cell labels to stratify on http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates stratified scRNA-seq training/testing subsets of controlled size with the caret R package's createDataPartition (and createFolds for five-fold cross-validation), enabling benchmarks where computation time and accuracy are measured as dataset size varies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Generates stratified scRNA-seq training/testing subsets of controlled size with the caret R package's createDataPartition (and createFolds for five-fold cross-validation), enabling benchmarks where computation time and accuracy are measured as dataset size varies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not yet been quality-filtered (genes not expressed in any cells, cells with <200 genes, >20% mitochondrial expression, or unlabeled cells still present) — filtering must precede partitioning The analysis goal is marker-based (markersupervised) methods such as SCSA, SCINA or DigitalCellSorter that require a marker list rather than training/testing splits Data are bulk RNA-seq or already a precomputed feature/signature table with no per-cell labels to stratify on

skills.description: Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction embeddings of small UMI count matrices to test whether a vMF/hyperspherical latent space avoids the origin-crowding seen with normal-prior VAEs and t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE.
skills.name: scrna-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scrna-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction embeddings of small UMI count matrices to test whether a vMF/hyperspherical latent space avoids the origin-crowding seen with normal-prior VAEs and t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE. Datasets are large with real multi-level batch factors (patient/disease/location) — use batch-aware scPhere with n_batch lists instead of the no-batch crowding benchmark The goal is trajectory/developmental analysis — use scPhere's hyperbolic (Lorentz/Poincaré, latent_dist='wn') mode rather than this spherical-vs-Euclidean crowding comparison Input is already an embedding or a feature table rather than a raw UMI count matrix — scPhere models negative-binomial gene expression counts directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark workflow comparing scPhere's hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher latent) VAE embeddings against a standard normal-prior (Euclidean) VAE and classical tools (t-SNE, UMAP, PHATE) on small scRNA-seq datasets, to test whether a spherical latent space resolves the cell-crowding problem at the origin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Benchmark workflow comparing scPhere's hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher latent) VAE embeddings against a standard normal-prior (Euclidean) VAE and classical tools (t-SNE, UMAP, PHATE) on small scRNA-seq datasets, to test whether a spherical latent space resolves the cell-crowding problem at the origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are large with real multi-level batch factors (patient/disease/location) — use batch-aware scPhere with n_batch lists instead of the no-batch crowding benchmark The goal is trajectory/developmental analysis — use scPhere's hyperbolic (Lorentz/Poincaré, latent_dist='wn') mode rather than this spherical-vs-Euclidean crowding comparison Input is already an embedding or a feature table rather than a raw UMI count matrix — scPhere models negative-binomial gene expression counts directly

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix contains excessive zero dropouts and the goal is expression-matrix completion that retains true (biologically silent) zeros rather than overwriting them.

skills.search_text: scrna-dropout-imputation Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix contains excessive zero dropouts and the goal is expression-matrix completion that retains true (biologically silent) zeros rather than overwriting them. Input is a bulk RNA-seq matrix or any fully observed (non-sparse) expression matrix — dropout imputation is only meaningful for sparse single-cell data The matrix has not been pre-processed (gene filtering, normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion selection); AutoImpute.py expects the pre-processed count matrix as input The goal is differential-expression testing rather than matrix completion prior to downstream clustering or variance analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Impute dropout events in sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices using AutoImpute, an overcomplete-autoencoder approach that preserves biologically silent true zeros. Evaluated against scImpute, drImpute, and MAGIC using matched bulk/single-cell Trapnell (GSE52529) data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Impute dropout events in sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices using AutoImpute, an overcomplete-autoencoder approach that preserves biologically silent true zeros. Evaluated against scImpute, drImpute, and MAGIC using matched bulk/single-cell Trapnell (GSE52529) data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a bulk RNA-seq matrix or any fully observed (non-sparse) expression matrix — dropout imputation is only meaningful for sparse single-cell data The matrix has not been pre-processed (gene filtering, normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion selection); AutoImpute.py expects the pre-processed count matrix as input The goal is differential-expression testing rather than matrix completion prior to downstream clustering or variance analysis
