skills.description: Use when query cells have been projected onto a ProjectSVR reference (ref.umap attached) and you must decide which cells to retain for label transfer or downstream tests, e.g. via mean.knn.dist < 1.6 or mapQ.p.adj < 0.1.
skills.name: scrna-mapping-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: scrna-mapping-quality-assessment Use when query cells have been projected onto a ProjectSVR reference (ref.umap attached) and you must decide which cells to retain for label transfer or downstream tests, e.g. via mean.knn.dist < 1.6 or mapQ.p.adj < 0.1. Query cells contain novel biological states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, so compare against unsupervised clustering instead of trusting map-quality filters alone The query was generated on a different platform than the reference (e.g. Smart-seq2 projected onto 10x data) — performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth, so cutoffs calibrated on matched-platform data may not transfer You need a per-cell mapping confidence metric for a non-ProjectSVR mapper (Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs) — this empirical k-NN null procedure is defined on the ProjectSVR projected UMAP embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assess whether query cells projected onto a pre-built ProjectSVR reference model were mapped reliably, using the mean k-NN distance in the projected UMAP space and BH-corrected empirical p-values (AddProjQual/MapQCPlot) before filtering to well-mapped cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Assess whether query cells projected onto a pre-built ProjectSVR reference model were mapped reliably, using the mean k-NN distance in the projected UMAP space and BH-corrected empirical p-values (AddProjQual/MapQCPlot) before filtering to well-mapped cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel biological states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading, so compare against unsupervised clustering instead of trusting map-quality filters alone The query was generated on a different platform than the reference (e.g. Smart-seq2 projected onto 10x data) — performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth, so cutoffs calibrated on matched-platform data may not transfer You need a per-cell mapping confidence metric for a non-ProjectSVR mapper (Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs) — this empirical k-NN null procedure is defined on the ProjectSVR projected UMAP embedding

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be collapsed into pooled, non-sparse per-cluster transcriptomic profiles before applying a predictor (e.g., miRNA inference) to each cell type.
skills.name: scrna-pseudobulk-cluster-aggregation
skills.search_text: scrna-pseudobulk-cluster-aggregation Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be collapsed into pooled, non-sparse per-cluster transcriptomic profiles before applying a predictor (e.g., miRNA inference) to each cell type. When per-cell resolution of miRNA activity is required — the article notes miReact's authors 'interpreted the predicted miRNA at the level of cell clusters', and pooling deliberately collapses single cells. When the sample context does not match the training cohort — the article warns accuracy is reduced 'when the cellular/tissue context of the application sample does not perfectly match those of the training cohort'. When genes are largely undetected due to dropout — the article states 'a pre-trained model may not work and miRSCAPE needs to be retrained using only the genes that are detected at a reasonable level'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Aggregates cells within each single-cell cluster into a non-sparse pseudo-bulk mRNA profile (via Seurat-object manipulation and bootstrapped cell pooling) so that downstream regression models such as miRSCAPE can be applied at the cell-type level rather than on sparse individual cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Aggregates cells within each single-cell cluster into a non-sparse pseudo-bulk mRNA profile (via Seurat-object manipulation and bootstrapped cell pooling) so that downstream regression models such as miRSCAPE can be applied at the cell-type level rather than on sparse individual cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When per-cell resolution of miRNA activity is required — the article notes miReact's authors 'interpreted the predicted miRNA at the level of cell clusters', and pooling deliberately collapses single cells. When the sample context does not match the training cohort — the article warns accuracy is reduced 'when the cellular/tissue context of the application sample does not perfectly match those of the training cohort'. When genes are largely undetected due to dropout — the article states 'a pre-trained model may not work and miRSCAPE needs to be retrained using only the genes that are detected at a reasonable level'.

skills.description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics dataset (Visium, Slide-seq V2, MERFISH) must be integrated with a cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference and a generative model of single-cell expression distributions is needed for cell type identification or gene expression imputation/decomposition.
skills.name: scrna-reference-distribution-learning
skills.search_text: scrna-reference-distribution-learning Use when a spatial transcriptomics dataset (Visium, Slide-seq V2, MERFISH) must be integrated with a cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference and a generative model of single-cell expression distributions is needed for cell type identification or gene expression imputation/decomposition. The goal is only spot-level cell-type proportion estimates, not single-cell-resolution decomposition or whole-transcriptome imputation — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD are cheaper and sufficient. No cell-type-annotated single-cell reference is available for the tissue of interest, since the model is trained directly on reference expression distributions. Training turnaround is unacceptable: the paper notes deep generative model training is measured in hours or days, and pretrained checkpoints may not exist for your reference. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a conditional score-based deep generative model on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g., the mouse MOp droplet snRNA-seq atlas, 26,431 cells, 20 cell types) so its learned score function sθ(x, σl, μk) can later support posterior sampling of transcriptome-wide expression for spatial transcriptomics via SpatialScope. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Train a conditional score-based deep generative model on a cell-type-labeled scRNA-seq reference (e.g., the mouse MOp droplet snRNA-seq atlas, 26,431 cells, 20 cell types) so its learned score function sθ(x, σl, μk) can later support posterior sampling of transcriptome-wide expression for spatial transcriptomics via SpatialScope.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only spot-level cell-type proportion estimates, not single-cell-resolution decomposition or whole-transcriptome imputation — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, or CARD are cheaper and sufficient. No cell-type-annotated single-cell reference is available for the tissue of interest, since the model is trained directly on reference expression distributions. Training turnaround is unacceptable: the paper notes deep generative model training is measured in hours or days, and pretrained checkpoints may not exist for your reference.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression matrix (E) and scATAC-seq openness matrix (O) come from separate samples of the same mixed cell population, and clustering should be informed across datatypes — optionally with bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loops.
skills.name: scrna-scatac-joint-clustering-analysis
skills.search_text: scrna-scatac-joint-clustering-analysis Use when scRNA-seq expression matrix (E) and scATAC-seq openness matrix (O) come from separate samples of the same mixed cell population, and clustering should be informed across datatypes — optionally with bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loops. The single-cell samples are not from the same heterogeneous cell population (no shared subpopulations to couple across scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq). Only bulk HiChIP deconvolution is needed without any single-cell data — DC3 requires the E and O matrices. Single-cell data types are jointly profiled in the same cells (e.g. sci-CAR), which DC3's cost function does not yet incorporate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Coupled clustering of scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples from the same heterogeneous cell population using DC3, which jointly analyzes the two single-cell matrices together with bulk HiChIP loop counts to assign single cells to subpopulations more accurately than per-datatype NMF. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12547-1
skills.summary: Coupled clustering of scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq samples from the same heterogeneous cell population using DC3, which jointly analyzes the two single-cell matrices together with bulk HiChIP loop counts to assign single cells to subpopulations more accurately than per-datatype NMF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The single-cell samples are not from the same heterogeneous cell population (no shared subpopulations to couple across scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq). Only bulk HiChIP deconvolution is needed without any single-cell data — DC3 requires the E and O matrices. Single-cell data types are jointly profiled in the same cells (e.g. sci-CAR), which DC3's cost function does not yet incorporate.

skills.description: Use when paired or separate scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices with time-stage/fate annotations must be integrated and used to reconstruct a bifurcating trajectory and detect terminal cell fates.
skills.name: scrna-scatac-multimodal-integration
skills.search_text: scrna-scatac-multimodal-integration Use when paired or separate scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices with time-stage/fate annotations must be integrated and used to reconstruct a bifurcating trajectory and detect terminal cell fates. Data consists of a single modality with a simple tree-like topology where established methods (e.g., Slingshot, STREAM) suffice without integration. Only normalized expression/feature matrices are available without raw per-modality count matrices or fate annotations to score terminal-state recovery. The goal is generic Seurat integration quality assessment rather than downstream trajectory inference and fate detection. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Normalize and Seurat-anchor-integrate paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cardiac progenitor datasets (Jia et al., 197 RNA cells and 695 ATAC cells), then feed individual-modality and integrated PCA embeddings into VIA to recover the bifurcating Isl1+ cardiomyocyte and endothelial fates that baseline TI methods merge or fragment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Normalize and Seurat-anchor-integrate paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cardiac progenitor datasets (Jia et al., 197 RNA cells and 695 ATAC cells), then feed individual-modality and integrated PCA embeddings into VIA to recover the bifurcating Isl1+ cardiomyocyte and endothelial fates that baseline TI methods merge or fragment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data consists of a single modality with a simple tree-like topology where established methods (e.g., Slingshot, STREAM) suffice without integration. Only normalized expression/feature matrices are available without raw per-modality count matrices or fate annotations to score terminal-state recovery. The goal is generic Seurat integration quality assessment rather than downstream trajectory inference and fate detection.

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-3utr-isoform-quantification Use when raw 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (FASTQ/BAM from 10x Genomics or Microwell-seq chemistry) must be converted into sparse gene-level and 3'UTR isoform count matrices for APA/UTR-length analysis. Data are full-length transcripts that span mRNA 3' end cleavage sites and support exact de novo cleavage-site mapping rather than UTRome-based pseudoalignment Only gene-level expression is needed — standard gene-count quantification without isoform resolution is simpler and sufficient The library is a bulk RNA-seq or non-3'-end-tag protocol incompatible with the kallisto-bustools 3'-end tag workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify gene and 3'UTR isoform expression simultaneously from 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10x Genomics, Microwell-seq) by pseudoaligning reads with kallisto bus against a prebuilt UTRome index of truncated transcript (txcutr) targets, via the Snakemake-based scUTRquant pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Quantify gene and 3'UTR isoform expression simultaneously from 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10x Genomics, Microwell-seq) by pseudoaligning reads with kallisto bus against a prebuilt UTRome index of truncated transcript (txcutr) targets, via the Snakemake-based scUTRquant pipeline.

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-batch-effect-correction Use when a Scanpy AnnData object with raw scRNA-seq counts plus per-cell batch labels shows cells separating by batch rather than by cell type (e.g. skewed cell types across batches, nested batch effects, or >10 batches), and an unsupervised integrated embedding is needed. skills.search_text: scrna-seq-batch-effect-correction Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., three cell lines across CEL-seq2, 10x Chromium, Drop-seq) has unknown cell types and batch effects must be corrected while clustering cells and benchmarking ARI against alternative integration methods. skills.summary: Fit BUSseq, an interpretable Bayesian hierarchical model, to simultaneously correct batch effects, cluster unknown cell types, impute dropout-caused missing data, and detect differentially expressed genes in multi-batch scRNA-seq count data, and benchmark the clustering against competing integration methods (LIGER, MNN, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat, ZINB-WaVE, CellAssign) via adjusted Rand index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — no batch-correction method, including BUSseq, is applicable Input is already normalized or batch-corrected expression data; BUSseq requires raw read counts to model count nature, overdispersion, dropouts, and cell-specific size factors The goal is bulk-sample batch adjustment, where ComBat or SVA are the classic appropriate tools rather than a single-cell hierarchical model

skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to integrate more than two datasets — BATMAN's current implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is only possible 'in principle') The goal is batch correction of a real biological dataset rather than a controlled simulation-based benchmark with ground-truth batch structure You need to distinguish cell subtypes hidden by batch effects with deep transfer learning (e.g., BERMUDA-style analysis) rather than benchmark matching-based correction

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-batch-integration-benchmarking Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches or species (e.g., human–mouse atlas data up to ~1M cells) and you need to compare integration methods' batch mixing, cell-type conservation, and runtime. skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cell-type-classification-benchmarking Use when you need to compare malignant-vs-non-malignant cell prediction performance of an ensemble k-NN classifier against established cell-annotation tools on the same single-cell test datasets. skills.summary: Benchmark PreCanCell's malignant/non-malignant cell classification against CHETAH, SciBet, SCINA, scmap-cell, scmap-cluster, SingleR, and ikarus on shared scRNA-seq test sets using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, and AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — PreCanCell is limited to annotating cancer vs non-cancer cells The input is raw unnormalized counts — PreCanCell_data() expects an already library-depth-normalized expression matrix (e.g., TPM or CPM) You need reproducible version-pinned comparisons without accession IDs — the article provides no versions for PreCanCell or the seven comparators and no accession IDs for several named test datasets

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells must be labeled against the Cell Ontology controlled vocabulary, especially when the query or test set may contain cell type terms absent from the training labels.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cell-type-prediction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cell-type-prediction Use when scRNA-seq cells must be labeled against the Cell Ontology controlled vocabulary, especially when the query or test set may contain cell type terms absent from the training labels. Input is raw unprocessed count data that has not yet passed ProcessTrainFeature/ProcessTestFeature alignment to the pretrained model's gene space The goal is marker gene identification for ontology terms rather than per-cell annotation scores Free-text annotations must be mapped to Cell Ontology terms — that requires the NLP/Char-level LSTM mapping step, not the graph propagation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Predict cell type annotations for single-cell RNA-seq data with OnClass, propagating confidence scores over the Cell Ontology graph via random walk with restart so that all ontology terms—including unseen terms with no annotated training cells—receive per-cell scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Predict cell type annotations for single-cell RNA-seq data with OnClass, propagating confidence scores over the Cell Ontology graph via random walk with restart so that all ontology terms—including unseen terms with no annotated training cells—receive per-cell scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed count data that has not yet passed ProcessTrainFeature/ProcessTestFeature alignment to the pretrained model's gene space The goal is marker gene identification for ontology terms rather than per-cell annotation scores Free-text annotations must be mapped to Cell Ontology terms — that requires the NLP/Char-level LSTM mapping step, not the graph propagation step

skills.description: Use when FASTQ files from a UMI-based 3' scRNA-seq platform (e.g., Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, SmartSeq3) must be processed with a single unified pipeline and the platform-specific chemistry is unknown or should be auto-detected.
skills.name: scrna-seq-chemistry-configuration
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-chemistry-configuration Use when FASTQ files from a UMI-based 3' scRNA-seq platform (e.g., Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, SmartSeq3) must be processed with a single unified pipeline and the platform-specific chemistry is unknown or should be auto-detected. The data are 5' scRNA-seq from a technology other than Chromium — the article states such technologies are not supported at the time of writing The input is not UMI-based scRNA-seq data — UniverSC supports only UMI-based platforms Cell Ranger's own chemistry/whitelisting behavior must be bypassed entirely, since UniverSC calls Cell Ranger as an external dependency and inherits its processing model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure UniverSC (v1.2.7) to automatically determine the correct UMI-based 3' scRNA-seq chemistry for a FASTQ dataset, wrapping Cell Ranger 3.0.2 so that one pipeline can process Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, and SmartSeq3 data identically. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Configure UniverSC (v1.2.7) to automatically determine the correct UMI-based 3' scRNA-seq chemistry for a FASTQ dataset, wrapping Cell Ranger 3.0.2 so that one pipeline can process Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, and SmartSeq3 data identically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are 5' scRNA-seq from a technology other than Chromium — the article states such technologies are not supported at the time of writing The input is not UMI-based scRNA-seq data — UniverSC supports only UMI-based platforms Cell Ranger's own chemistry/whitelisting behavior must be bypassed entirely, since UniverSC calls Cell Ranger as an external dependency and inherits its processing model

skills.description: Use when annotating cell types for scRNA-seq clusters and marker genes must be identified by one-against-one paired cluster comparison with explicit fold-change, significance, and percent-expression thresholds.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cluster-annotation-criteria
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cluster-annotation-criteria Use when annotating cell types for scRNA-seq clusters and marker genes must be identified by one-against-one paired cluster comparison with explicit fold-change, significance, and percent-expression thresholds. Input is not cluster-level scRNA-seq data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, a feature table without per-cell cluster assignments, or pre-computed marker lists) A one-against-all differential expression strategy is explicitly desired, since scCATCH's rationale is to avoid pseudo marker genes from one-against-all comparisons The species or tissue is not covered by CellMatch (human or mouse references); the article notes that a limited reference database can lead to incorrect annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A skill for identifying potential marker genes per cluster in scRNA-seq data using scCATCH's one-against-one paired-cluster comparison, retaining genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster (log10 fold change >= 0.25, Wilcoxon p < 0.05, expressed in >= 25% of cells) to avoid pseudo marker genes and support accurate automatic cell type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: A skill for identifying potential marker genes per cluster in scRNA-seq data using scCATCH's one-against-one paired-cluster comparison, retaining genes significantly upregulated in only one cluster (log10 fold change >= 0.25, Wilcoxon p < 0.05, expressed in >= 25% of cells) to avoid pseudo marker genes and support accurate automatic cell type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not cluster-level scRNA-seq data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, a feature table without per-cell cluster assignments, or pre-computed marker lists) A one-against-all differential expression strategy is explicitly desired, since scCATCH's rationale is to avoid pseudo marker genes from one-against-all comparisons The species or tissue is not covered by CellMatch (human or mouse references); the article notes that a limited reference database can lead to incorrect annotation

skills.description: Decision support for whether visually distinct scRNA-seq clusters in a scDEED-optimized t-SNE embedding should be unified into one cluster — e.g. five Hydra neuron ectodermal subtypes or CAR-T clusters 3/4/9/11.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cluster-assignment-analysis
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cluster-assignment-analysis Decision support for whether visually distinct scRNA-seq clusters in a scDEED-optimized t-SNE embedding should be unified into one cluster — e.g. five Hydra neuron ectodermal subtypes or CAR-T clusters 3/4/9/11. The input is raw count data without defined cluster labels — scDEED/Seurat preprocessing (NormalizeData, ScaleData, RunPCA, clustering) must be run first The question is whether the 2D embedding itself is dubious or hyperparameters need tuning — use the scDEED optimization skill, not ROGUE purity comparison Cluster identity is already validated by external biology (e.g. marker genes); ROGUE merging tests would not change the conclusion http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantitatively test whether single-cell clusters identified in a 2D embedding (t-SNE/UMAP) should be merged or kept separate by computing the ROGUE cluster-purity metric on each cluster and on merged combinations, using Seurat cluster labels as input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Quantitatively test whether single-cell clusters identified in a 2D embedding (t-SNE/UMAP) should be merged or kept separate by computing the ROGUE cluster-purity metric on each cluster and on merged combinations, using Seurat cluster labels as input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw count data without defined cluster labels — scDEED/Seurat preprocessing (NormalizeData, ScaleData, RunPCA, clustering) must be run first The question is whether the 2D embedding itself is dubious or hyperparameters need tuning — use the scDEED optimization skill, not ROGUE purity comparison Cluster identity is already validated by external biology (e.g. marker genes); ROGUE merging tests would not change the conclusion

skills.description: Use when you need to determine the minimum number of cells per cluster (here >=20) at which automated cell-type annotations remain statistically indistinguishable from full-dataset annotations, or when auditing annotation robustness on sparse clusters of a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cluster-downsampling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cluster-downsampling Use when you need to determine the minimum number of cells per cluster (here >=20) at which automated cell-type annotations remain statistically indistinguishable from full-dataset annotations, or when auditing annotation robustness on sparse clusters of a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction. Every cluster already has >=500 cells, so down-sampling cannot reveal any annotation sensitivity that was not already tested The Seurat object lacks a UMAP reduction or cluster annotations, so the Census label-stabilizing step and cluster-based down-sampling cannot be performed The goal is cell-of-origin inference on a full cancer dataset rather than quantifying annotation robustness to sample size http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A sensitivity-analysis skill that quantifies how many cells per UMAP cluster are needed for reliable Census cell-type annotations, by iteratively down-sampling the Peng et al. 2019 pancreatic cancer scRNA-seq dataset from 5 to 500 cells per cluster, re-annotating with the pretrained Census model, and testing F1-score differences with a Kruskal-Wallis test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill that quantifies how many cells per UMAP cluster are needed for reliable Census cell-type annotations, by iteratively down-sampling the Peng et al. 2019 pancreatic cancer scRNA-seq dataset from 5 to 500 cells per cluster, re-annotating with the pretrained Census model, and testing F1-score differences with a Kruskal-Wallis test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Every cluster already has >=500 cells, so down-sampling cannot reveal any annotation sensitivity that was not already tested The Seurat object lacks a UMAP reduction or cluster annotations, so the Census label-stabilizing step and cluster-based down-sampling cannot be performed The goal is cell-of-origin inference on a full cancer dataset rather than quantifying annotation robustness to sample size

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-annotation tool's accuracy is limited by its bundled reference database, or when testing whether substituting an external taxonomy reference (e.g., CellMatch) improves cluster-label consistency on benchmark datasets.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cluster-label-consistency-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cluster-label-consistency-evaluation Use when evaluating whether a cell-annotation tool's accuracy is limited by its bundled reference database, or when testing whether substituting an external taxonomy reference (e.g., CellMatch) improves cluster-label consistency on benchmark datasets. The goal is to evaluate scCATCH's own evidence-based scoring (findmarkergene/findcelltype) rather than to ablate the reference database used by a cell-based annotator such as SingleR or CellAssign. The input dataset has no benchmark/truth labels against which cluster-level annotation consistency can be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 A benchmarking procedure that quantifies how the choice of reference database affects cell type annotation accuracy, by running an annotator such as SingleR on the same benchmark scRNA-seq datasets with its default references and then with the CellMatch reference (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) and comparing per-cluster agreement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that quantifies how the choice of reference database affects cell type annotation accuracy, by running an annotator such as SingleR on the same benchmark scRNA-seq datasets with its default references and then with the CellMatch reference (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) and comparing per-cluster agreement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate scCATCH's own evidence-based scoring (findmarkergene/findcelltype) rather than to ablate the reference database used by a cell-based annotator such as SingleR or CellAssign. The input dataset has no benchmark/truth labels against which cluster-level annotation consistency can be computed.

skills.description: Use when a pretrained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (Miscell) has produced cell clusters and you need ranked, cluster-specific marker genes via attribution rather than differential-expression tests.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cluster-marker-validation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cluster-marker-validation Use when a pretrained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (Miscell) has produced cell clusters and you need ranked, cluster-specific marker genes via attribution rather than differential-expression tests. The marker genes of interest may lie outside the highly variable gene set, since Miscell's attribution-based identification is limited to HVGs The dataset is small, because Miscell (like deep neural network methods generally) demands a large sample size to obtain good performance The input data have batch effects that have not been corrected, since Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify cluster-specific marker genes from a trained Miscell self-supervised encoder by freezing its weights, attaching a 1-layer linear classifier, and applying integrated-gradients attribution to rank each gene's influence per cell cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Identify cluster-specific marker genes from a trained Miscell self-supervised encoder by freezing its weights, attaching a 1-layer linear classifier, and applying integrated-gradients attribution to rank each gene's influence per cell cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The marker genes of interest may lie outside the highly variable gene set, since Miscell's attribution-based identification is limited to HVGs The dataset is small, because Miscell (like deep neural network methods generally) demands a large sample size to obtain good performance The input data have batch effects that have not been corrected, since Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Tabula Muris bone marrow) needs cluster-based marker discovery, or when benchmarking a clustering-independent DEG method (singleCellHaystack) against the standard cluster-then-test Wilcoxon pipeline.
skills.name: scrna-seq-clustering-based-deg-prediction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-clustering-based-deg-prediction Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Tabula Muris bone marrow) needs cluster-based marker discovery, or when benchmarking a clustering-independent DEG method (singleCellHaystack) against the standard cluster-then-test Wilcoxon pipeline. When the goal is DEG prediction itself and the number of biologically relevant clusters is unclear — the article warns that 'the definition of cell clusters is often not straightforward' and singleCellHaystack was built for this case. When a p-value on the DEG list must be strictly calibrated — clustering-based (and haystack) p-values are inflated by double use of gene expression data for clustering and testing. When genes must be ranked by expression level, not detection: both approaches discussed here rely on detection/zero-count handling, and singleCellHaystack requires binary detection data as input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Baseline clustering-based DEG prediction workflow for scRNA-seq: cluster cells (e.g., Seurat FindClusters) and call per-cluster markers with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (FindAllMarkers). It serves as the comparison standard against clustering-independent methods like singleCellHaystack, whose top-100 bone marrow DEGs overlap it in only 3 genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Baseline clustering-based DEG prediction workflow for scRNA-seq: cluster cells (e.g., Seurat FindClusters) and call per-cluster markers with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (FindAllMarkers). It serves as the comparison standard against clustering-independent methods like singleCellHaystack, whose top-100 bone marrow DEGs overlap it in only 3 genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is DEG prediction itself and the number of biologically relevant clusters is unclear — the article warns that 'the definition of cell clusters is often not straightforward' and singleCellHaystack was built for this case. When a p-value on the DEG list must be strictly calibrated — clustering-based (and haystack) p-values are inflated by double use of gene expression data for clustering and testing. When genes must be ranked by expression level, not detection: both approaches discussed here rely on detection/zero-count handling, and singleCellHaystack requires binary detection data as input.

skills.description: Use when partial cell type annotations (e.g., scGate multi-classifier output) cover only a subset of cells in an integrated TIL map and complete labels are needed before a second semi-supervised STACAS integration round.
skills.name: scrna-seq-clustering-based-label-refinement
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-clustering-based-label-refinement Use when partial cell type annotations (e.g., scGate multi-classifier output) cover only a subset of cells in an integrated TIL map and complete labels are needed before a second semi-supervised STACAS integration round. When cell type annotations are already complete and trustworthy for every cell — re-clustering and transfer can inject noise rather than refine When no intermediate integrated embedding exists (labels transferred in uncorrected space will follow batch structure, not biology) When the cell type of interest is present in only one dataset, where CiLISI-type evaluation and cross-sample label transfer are not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Refine partial scGate-derived cell type labels by clustering an intermediate semi-supervised STACAS integrated embedding and propagating labels to unannotated cells with annotate.by.neighbors, producing the refined labels used as prior information for the second ssSTACAS round. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Refine partial scGate-derived cell type labels by clustering an intermediate semi-supervised STACAS integrated embedding and propagating labels to unannotated cells with annotate.by.neighbors, producing the refined labels used as prior information for the second ssSTACAS round.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell type annotations are already complete and trustworthy for every cell — re-clustering and transfer can inject noise rather than refine When no intermediate integrated embedding exists (labels transferred in uncorrected space will follow batch structure, not biology) When the cell type of interest is present in only one dataset, where CiLISI-type evaluation and cross-sample label transfer are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when cell embeddings from a scRNA-seq integration or clustering model (AnnData with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' obs columns) must be quantitatively benchmarked via ARI/NMI clustering scores and kBET batch-mixing acceptance rates.
skills.name: scrna-seq-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-clustering-evaluation Use when cell embeddings from a scRNA-seq integration or clustering model (AnnData with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' obs columns) must be quantitatively benchmarked via ARI/NMI clustering scores and kBET batch-mixing acceptance rates. Input lacks ground-truth cell type annotations ('cell_types' column), so ARI/NMI against reference labels cannot be computed The task is supervised cell-type classification or label transfer rather than unsupervised clustering evaluation of learned embeddings Only a single batch is present and no batch-effect correction is needed, making kBET batch-mixing assessment uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluate unsupervised clustering quality of single-cell embeddings (e.g. scETM's 'delta' cell embeddings) by computing ARI and NMI against ground-truth 'cell_types' labels, and batch mixing via kBET acceptance rates, as done in the scETM benchmark against seven baselines (scVI, scVI-LD, Seurat, scVAE-GM, Scanorama, Harmony, LIGER). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Evaluate unsupervised clustering quality of single-cell embeddings (e.g. scETM's 'delta' cell embeddings) by computing ARI and NMI against ground-truth 'cell_types' labels, and batch mixing via kBET acceptance rates, as done in the scETM benchmark against seven baselines (scVI, scVI-LD, Seurat, scVAE-GM, Scanorama, Harmony, LIGER).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks ground-truth cell type annotations ('cell_types' column), so ARI/NMI against reference labels cannot be computed The task is supervised cell-type classification or label transfer rather than unsupervised clustering evaluation of learned embeddings Only a single batch is present and no batch-effect correction is needed, making kBET batch-mixing assessment uninformative

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate scRNA-seq imputation/clustering models by clustering their learned cell embeddings and scoring agreement against true cell labels supplied in a h5 expression matrix (e.g., Adam, Romanov).
skills.name: scrna-seq-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-clustering-evaluation Use when you need to evaluate scRNA-seq imputation/clustering models by clustering their learned cell embeddings and scoring agreement against true cell labels supplied in a h5 expression matrix (e.g., Adam, Romanov). The h5 input lacks true cell labels, so no clustering agreement metrics against ground truth can be computed The goal is gene imputation quality assessment or gene expression pattern enhancement (e.g., in Alzheimer's disease datasets) rather than clustering-based performance evaluation The data are not scRNA-seq dropout-affected count matrices; scGCL and its ZINB-based evaluation target single-cell RNA-seq data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cluster the learned cell embeddings produced by scGCL (or its ablation variants) and compute clustering agreement metrics against the true cell labels stored in the h5 expression file, to quantify imputation/clustering performance and assemble ablation comparisons such as Table 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Cluster the learned cell embeddings produced by scGCL (or its ablation variants) and compute clustering agreement metrics against the true cell labels stored in the h5 expression file, to quantify imputation/clustering performance and assemble ablation comparisons such as Table 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The h5 input lacks true cell labels, so no clustering agreement metrics against ground truth can be computed The goal is gene imputation quality assessment or gene expression pattern enhancement (e.g., in Alzheimer's disease datasets) rather than clustering-based performance evaluation The data are not scRNA-seq dropout-affected count matrices; scGCL and its ZINB-based evaluation target single-cell RNA-seq data

skills.description: Use when raw or unclustered scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Genomics counts from mouse skin wound samples GSM3453535-GSM3453538) must be QC-filtered and assigned to cell groups before ligand-receptor communication inference.
skills.name: scrna-seq-clustering-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-clustering-preprocessing Use when raw or unclustered scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Genomics counts from mouse skin wound samples GSM3453535-GSM3453538) must be QC-filtered and assigned to cell groups before ligand-receptor communication inference. Input is already a clustered CellChat object or Seurat object with defined cell identities — clustering is complete and re-running QC could discard legitimate cell groups Data are spatial transcriptomics or pseudotime/continuous-state trajectories where discrete Louvain clustering is not the appropriate representation for communication inference Only a benchmark of inference tools on existing labels is needed — this skill covers preprocessing, not the communication inference itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quality control, filtering, and cell clustering of scRNA-seq datasets so that discrete cell groups exist as a prerequisite for cell-cell communication inference with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Quality control, filtering, and cell clustering of scRNA-seq datasets so that discrete cell groups exist as a prerequisite for cell-cell communication inference with CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK and SingleCellSignalR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a clustered CellChat object or Seurat object with defined cell identities — clustering is complete and re-running QC could discard legitimate cell groups Data are spatial transcriptomics or pseudotime/continuous-state trajectories where discrete Louvain clustering is not the appropriate representation for communication inference Only a benchmark of inference tools on existing labels is needed — this skill covers preprocessing, not the communication inference itself

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth CNA labels to benchmark copy-number callers on single-cell RNA-seq, by simulating known events (e.g. allele-specific chr3 loss) in a seeded tumor dataset.
skills.name: scrna-seq-cna-simulation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-cna-simulation Use when you need ground-truth CNA labels to benchmark copy-number callers on single-cell RNA-seq, by simulating known events (e.g. allele-specific chr3 loss) in a seeded tumor dataset. The dataset already has clonal ground truth from matched scDNA-seq — benchmark directly on it instead of simulating The analysis goal is biological CNA detection on a real tumor sample, not caller benchmarking The comparison targets RDR-only CNA events where allelic imbalance carries no signal (e.g. copy-neutral events cannot be resolved by inferCNV/CopyKAT) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark allele-specific copy-number callers (XClone, Numbat, inferCNV) on simulated scRNA-seq data generated with scCNASimulator, which injects known CNA events (e.g. allele-specific chr3 copy loss in two subclones) into a real seed dataset such as GX109-T1c to create ground-truth labels for AUROC evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Benchmark allele-specific copy-number callers (XClone, Numbat, inferCNV) on simulated scRNA-seq data generated with scCNASimulator, which injects known CNA events (e.g. allele-specific chr3 copy loss in two subclones) into a real seed dataset such as GX109-T1c to create ground-truth labels for AUROC evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has clonal ground truth from matched scDNA-seq — benchmark directly on it instead of simulating The analysis goal is biological CNA detection on a real tumor sample, not caller benchmarking The comparison targets RDR-only CNA events where allelic imbalance carries no signal (e.g. copy-neutral events cannot be resolved by inferCNV/CopyKAT)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (expression matrix plus cell-type labels) must be analyzed for intercellular communication, especially for non-human species or when results should not be constrained by known L-R databases.
skills.name: scrna-seq-communication-matrix-inference
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-communication-matrix-inference Use when scRNA-seq data (expression matrix plus cell-type labels) must be analyzed for intercellular communication, especially for non-human species or when results should not be constrained by known L-R databases. When the analysis goal requires strictly literature-curated L-R coexpression-based inference in humans, where tools like CellChat, CellPhoneDB, or iTALK are the established alternatives When each cell type contains fewer than ~10 cells, as the README warns users to input single-cell gene expression data containing at least 10 cells When a time-course/time-series design is required for direct regulation inference — Equation 2's approach is limited by the requirement for time-series data, which MDIC3 circumvents but does not replace http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infer cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq data with MDIC3, which factorizes the gene-by-cell expression matrix via a gene regulatory network (GNIPLR) and two-sided matrix decomposition (R, Σ, W), yielding sender-receiver communication strengths independent of predefined ligand-receptor pairs and applicable to any species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Infer cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq data with MDIC3, which factorizes the gene-by-cell expression matrix via a gene regulatory network (GNIPLR) and two-sided matrix decomposition (R, Σ, W), yielding sender-receiver communication strengths independent of predefined ligand-receptor pairs and applicable to any species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal requires strictly literature-curated L-R coexpression-based inference in humans, where tools like CellChat, CellPhoneDB, or iTALK are the established alternatives When each cell type contains fewer than ~10 cells, as the README warns users to input single-cell gene expression data containing at least 10 cells When a time-course/time-series design is required for direct regulation inference — Equation 2's approach is limited by the requirement for time-series data, which MDIC3 circumvents but does not replace

skills.description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression data with barcode lineage annotations (e.g., GEO GSE74923) and need to test whether related cells are transcriptionally more similar than random pairs.
skills.name: scrna-seq-correlation-distance-computation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-correlation-distance-computation Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression data with barcode lineage annotations (e.g., GEO GSE74923) and need to test whether related cells are transcriptionally more similar than random pairs. The cell population contains only distantly related cells, since GEMLI performs less robustly in such populations and correlation-distance contrasts may lack closely related pairs The dataset lacks barcode lineage annotations, in which case lineages must first be predicted (e.g., with GEMLI predict_lineages) rather than assumed Lineages span long time spans (weeks or months); memory-based inference covers only about 1-5 cell divisions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies gene-expression memory by computing whole-transcriptome Pearson correlation distances (1 - Pearson r) between lineage-related cell pairs and comparing them to equal-sized samples of random unrelated pairs from normalized scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Quantifies gene-expression memory by computing whole-transcriptome Pearson correlation distances (1 - Pearson r) between lineage-related cell pairs and comparing them to equal-sized samples of random unrelated pairs from normalized scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell population contains only distantly related cells, since GEMLI performs less robustly in such populations and correlation-distance contrasts may lack closely related pairs The dataset lacks barcode lineage annotations, in which case lineages must first be predicted (e.g., with GEMLI predict_lineages) rather than assumed Lineages span long time spans (weeks or months); memory-based inference covers only about 1-5 cell divisions

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset needs to be reduced from many individual cells to metacells (e.g. ~100-fold cell reduction on large atlases), or when metacell-level DE/DA/PCA must be weighted by metacell size to match single-cell reference results.

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-count-aggregation-to-metacells Use when a scRNA-seq dataset needs to be reduced from many individual cells to metacells (e.g. ~100-fold cell reduction on large atlases), or when metacell-level DE/DA/PCA must be weighted by metacell size to match single-cell reference results. When the biological question requires per-cell resolution (metacells are not cell types; multiple metacells can share the same state, and inter-cell heterogeneity is averaged out within each metacell). When metacells fail QC (low purity — the most abundant cell type does not dominate the metacell), since aggregation would mix biological states. When metacell-level DE/DA results must be reported without applying metacell size weights — unweighted aggregation-based comparisons produce type I/II errors relative to the single-cell reference. skills.search_text: scrna-seq-data-clustering Use when clustering a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. tens of thousands of cells, such as the Pollen dataset or 68,578-cell blood cell dataset) and standard k-means or PCA-based clustering is too slow or inaccurate. skills.summary: Clustering of single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices using the SSCC (Spearman subsampling-clustering-classification) framework implemented in the sscClust R package, which combines subsampling, Spearman-correlation ('iCor') feature projection, and classification to improve clustering accuracy, robustness, and scalability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced feature space or embedding (e.g. a precomputed PCA or SIMLR similarity) rather than a raw expression matrix Dataset is small enough that full-data clustering with SC3 or k-means is already fast and accurate, so the subsampling-classification machinery adds unnecessary complexity The goal is de novo estimation of the number of clusters rather than clustering with a user-specified k (ssc.run takes k.batch as input)

skills.description: Use when a normalized, log1p-transformed scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Klein dataset, top 5000 HVGs) contains dropouts and a denoised, complete cell-by-gene expression matrix is needed for downstream clustering.
skills.name: scrna-seq-data-imputation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-data-imputation Use when a normalized, log1p-transformed scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Klein dataset, top 5000 HVGs) contains dropouts and a denoised, complete cell-by-gene expression matrix is needed for downstream clustering. The goal is dimensionality reduction rather than imputation — use the 68K PBMC workflow (filter_genes_dispersion, n_top_genes=1000, then save obsm['X_ae_tpgg']) instead The input is raw unnormalized counts that have not been converted to semi-continuous form (normalize_per_cell + log1p) — the TPGG model expects that normalized representation The dataset's gene-expression distribution assumptions differ (e.g. not positive, right-skewed continuous positive part) and a different imputation model is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Impute dropout events in semi-continuous normalized scRNA-seq data with AE-TPGG, an autoencoder based on a two-part-generalized-gamma (GG) distribution, by computing the TPGG mean from the fitted alpha, beta, gamma, and pi parameter matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s11704-022-2011-y
skills.summary: Impute dropout events in semi-continuous normalized scRNA-seq data with AE-TPGG, an autoencoder based on a two-part-generalized-gamma (GG) distribution, by computing the TPGG mean from the fitted alpha, beta, gamma, and pi parameter matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is dimensionality reduction rather than imputation — use the 68K PBMC workflow (filter_genes_dispersion, n_top_genes=1000, then save obsm['X_ae_tpgg']) instead The input is raw unnormalized counts that have not been converted to semi-continuous form (normalize_per_cell + log1p) — the TPGG model expects that normalized representation The dataset's gene-expression distribution assumptions differ (e.g. not positive, right-skewed continuous positive part) and a different imputation model is preferred

skills.description: Use when a reproduction or benchmark needs the exact processed single-cell RNA-seq data and precomputed UMAP/tSNE embeddings cited in a paper, and the paper's data-availability section names a GEO accession (e.g. GSE87038, GSE129788).
skills.name: scrna-seq-dataset-acquisition-geo
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dataset-acquisition-geo Use when a reproduction or benchmark needs the exact processed single-cell RNA-seq data and precomputed UMAP/tSNE embeddings cited in a paper, and the paper's data-availability section names a GEO accession (e.g. GSE87038, GSE129788). You need raw sequencing data (FASTQ) or reprocessing from reads — the paper only traces processed matrices and precomputed embeddings via GEO, not a reprocessing pipeline. The dataset of interest is not deposited under a GEO accession (e.g. only on another archive); forcing a GEO lookup will fail. You only need to visualize data in CellexalVR itself rather than reproduce the 2D-vs-3D entropy analysis — then the cellexalvrR data-preparation workflow is the right entry point instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Locate and download publicly deposited scRNA-seq datasets — expression matrices plus precomputed UMAP/tSNE cell-coordinate embeddings — from their GEO accessions (e.g. GSE87038 for mouse gastrulation) so that downstream analyses like the entropy-based 2D-vs-3D overlap comparison can be reproduced. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Locate and download publicly deposited scRNA-seq datasets — expression matrices plus precomputed UMAP/tSNE cell-coordinate embeddings — from their GEO accessions (e.g. GSE87038 for mouse gastrulation) so that downstream analyses like the entropy-based 2D-vs-3D overlap comparison can be reproduced.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need raw sequencing data (FASTQ) or reprocessing from reads — the paper only traces processed matrices and precomputed embeddings via GEO, not a reprocessing pipeline.
