You only need to visualize data in CellexalVR itself rather than reproduce the 2D-vs-3D entropy analysis — then the cellexalvrR data-preparation workflow is the right entry point instead.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how a single-cell method's CPU time and memory scale with dataset size, requiring size-stratified subsets drawn from a large atlas such as MOCA (10k to 900k cells).
skills.name: scrna-seq-dataset-downsampling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dataset-downsampling Use when benchmarking how a single-cell method's CPU time and memory scale with dataset size, requiring size-stratified subsets drawn from a large atlas such as MOCA (10k to 900k cells). The goal is a biological or quality comparison (e.g. metacell purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than computational cost — downsampling changes cell composition and is not a like-for-like biological control. The dataset is already small enough that all candidate methods run tractably, so size scaling is not the question. The input is not single-cell count data (e.g. a precomputed feature table or bulk data), where cell-count stratification is not meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepare size-stratified single-cell RNA-seq subsets (e.g. MOCA 10k–900k cells) so that the computational cost of metacell construction tools (MC2, SuperCell, SEACells) at a fixed graining level can be benchmarked for CPU time and peak memory scaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Prepare size-stratified single-cell RNA-seq subsets (e.g. MOCA 10k–900k cells) so that the computational cost of metacell construction tools (MC2, SuperCell, SEACells) at a fixed graining level can be benchmarked for CPU time and peak memory scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a biological or quality comparison (e.g. metacell purity, compactness, separation, INV) rather than computational cost — downsampling changes cell composition and is not a like-for-like biological control. The dataset is already small enough that all candidate methods run tractably, so size scaling is not the question. The input is not single-cell count data (e.g. a precomputed feature table or bulk data), where cell-count stratification is not meaningful.

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data must be prepared for deep clustering with scBGEDA, requiring gene filtering and selection of highly variable genes before running SDDA.py and BC.m.
skills.name: scrna-seq-dataset-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dataset-preprocessing Use when raw scRNA-seq count data must be prepared for deep clustering with scBGEDA, requiring gene filtering and selection of highly variable genes before running SDDA.py and BC.m. Input is already preprocessed, denoised, or a low-dimensional latent embedding — re-running preprocess.py would not add information and could distort downstream ZINB/denoising reconstruction. The analysis goal is not scBGEDA-based clustering (e.g. a non-autoencoder pipeline with its own preprocessing), since this module is specifically the first module of scBGEDA. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Preprocessing module of scBGEDA that filters scRNA-seq count matrices and selects highly variable genes (e.g. --highly_genes 2000) to prepare denoised inputs for the dual denoising autoencoder and bipartite graph ensemble clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Preprocessing module of scBGEDA that filters scRNA-seq count matrices and selects highly variable genes (e.g. --highly_genes 2000) to prepare denoised inputs for the dual denoising autoencoder and bipartite graph ensemble clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already preprocessed, denoised, or a low-dimensional latent embedding — re-running preprocess.py would not add information and could distort downstream ZINB/denoising reconstruction. The analysis goal is not scBGEDA-based clustering (e.g. a non-autoencoder pipeline with its own preprocessing), since this module is specifically the first module of scBGEDA.

skills.description: Use when raw or published scRNA-seq count/TPM matrices must be normalized before clustering: values exceed 100, low-level expressed genes are present, and downstream feature selection needs a comparable scale.
skills.name: scrna-seq-dataset-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dataset-preprocessing Use when raw or published scRNA-seq count/TPM matrices must be normalized before clustering: values exceed 100, low-level expressed genes are present, and downstream feature selection needs a comparable scale. Input is already log-normalized with all expression values ≤ 100 and low-expression genes already filtered — reapplying log2 would distort the data Analysis goal is full-length transcript/trajectory quantification rather than producing a matrix for ensemble feature selection and meta-clustering Input is single-cell ATAC or other non-gene-expression data where the 2% cell-detection gene filter is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocess published scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. the fourteen GSE/E-MTAB datasets used by scEFSC) by log2 rescaling and low-expression gene filtering so they are suitable for downstream ensemble feature selection and clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.04.023
skills.summary: Preprocess published scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. the fourteen GSE/E-MTAB datasets used by scEFSC) by log2 rescaling and low-expression gene filtering so they are suitable for downstream ensemble feature selection and clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already log-normalized with all expression values ≤ 100 and low-expression genes already filtered — reapplying log2 would distort the data Analysis goal is full-length transcript/trajectory quantification rather than producing a matrix for ensemble feature selection and meta-clustering Input is single-cell ATAC or other non-gene-expression data where the 2% cell-detection gene filter is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell or doublet detection methods on scRNA-seq data and controlled, labeled datasets with known rare-cell abundances are needed as inputs.
skills.name: scrna-seq-dataset-subsampling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dataset-subsampling Use when benchmarking rare-cell or doublet detection methods on scRNA-seq data and controlled, labeled datasets with known rare-cell abundances are needed as inputs. The goal is applying GapClust to a real, unmodified dataset to discover rare cells rather than evaluating methods on controlled benchmarks The input dataset lacks labeled cell populations (e.g., CD14+ monocytes, NK cells, B cells) needed to plant and score rare cells against ground truth A homogeneous background population is not appropriate — e.g., when realistic multi-cell-type composition is required for the benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Construct controlled single-cell benchmark datasets by subsampling the 68k PBMC dataset, planting known numbers of CD14+ monocytes into homogeneous NK/B-cell populations to create rare-cell and doublet detection benchmarks with ground-truth labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Construct controlled single-cell benchmark datasets by subsampling the 68k PBMC dataset, planting known numbers of CD14+ monocytes into homogeneous NK/B-cell populations to create rare-cell and doublet detection benchmarks with ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is applying GapClust to a real, unmodified dataset to discover rare cells rather than evaluating methods on controlled benchmarks The input dataset lacks labeled cell populations (e.g., CD14+ monocytes, NK cells, B cells) needed to plant and score rare cells against ground truth A homogeneous background population is not appropriate — e.g., when realistic multi-cell-type composition is required for the benchmark

skills.description: Use when pooled scRNA-seq libraries were labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides and each droplet in an (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrix must be assigned to its sample of origin (including multiplet detection), with uncertain droplets discarded via error probabilities.
skills.name: scrna-seq-demultiplexing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-demultiplexing Use when pooled scRNA-seq libraries were labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides and each droplet in an (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrix must be assigned to its sample of origin (including multiplet detection), with uncertain droplets discarded via error probabilities. The library contains no sequenced hashtag oligonucleotides — without an (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrix there is nothing for the negative binomial mixture models to fit. Input is already a per-droplet sample-assignment table; this skill performs the probabilistic assignment step itself, not downstream integration of already-demultiplexed cells. Sample-of-origin must be inferred from genotype/SNP data rather than oligonucleotide barcodes — the paper's scope is demultiplexing pooled cells labeled with sample-specific barcode oligonucleotides. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Demultiplex pooled, hashtag-oligonucleotide (HTO)-barcoded single-cell RNA-seq by fitting per-HTO negative binomial mixture models (naive and genes-detected regression variants) to the (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and classifying each droplet to its sample of origin or a multiplet by posterior probability, discarding droplets below the acceptance threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Demultiplex pooled, hashtag-oligonucleotide (HTO)-barcoded single-cell RNA-seq by fitting per-HTO negative binomial mixture models (naive and genes-detected regression variants) to the (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and classifying each droplet to its sample of origin or a multiplet by posterior probability, discarding droplets below the acceptance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library contains no sequenced hashtag oligonucleotides — without an (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrix there is nothing for the negative binomial mixture models to fit. Input is already a per-droplet sample-assignment table; this skill performs the probabilistic assignment step itself, not downstream integration of already-demultiplexed cells. Sample-of-origin must be inferred from genotype/SNP data rather than oligonucleotide barcodes — the paper's scope is demultiplexing pooled cells labeled with sample-specific barcode oligonucleotides.

skills.description: Use when a CITE-seq or multimodal dataset provides protein-level sub-population labels (e.g., CD56bright/CD56dim NK cells from CD16/CD56 ADTs) and you must quantify whether denoised RNA better matches that protein structure than raw counts.
skills.name: scrna-seq-denoising-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-denoising-benchmark-evaluation Use when a CITE-seq or multimodal dataset provides protein-level sub-population labels (e.g., CD56bright/CD56dim NK cells from CD16/CD56 ADTs) and you must quantify whether denoised RNA better matches that protein structure than raw counts. The dataset lacks a paired protein/multimodal measurement, so no independent ground-truth labels exist against which to compute silhouette agreement The question is about imputation of specific missing values rather than whether denoising recovers sub-population structure; the article notes the non-trivial distinction between true (celltype-specific) and false (dropout) zeros makes classical imputation evaluation unsuitable The RNA matrix has already been heavily filtered or transformed (e.g., normalized, log-transformed) in ways incompatible with DCA's raw-count negative binomial input assumption http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmark skill for judging whether scRNA-seq denoising (e.g., DCA deep count autoencoder with NB/ZINB loss) recovers biological structure, using CITE-seq antibody-derived tag (ADT) protein labels as ground truth and quantifying agreement via silhouette coefficients on marker genes such as NCAM1/FCGR3A. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: A benchmark skill for judging whether scRNA-seq denoising (e.g., DCA deep count autoencoder with NB/ZINB loss) recovers biological structure, using CITE-seq antibody-derived tag (ADT) protein labels as ground truth and quantifying agreement via silhouette coefficients on marker genes such as NCAM1/FCGR3A.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks a paired protein/multimodal measurement, so no independent ground-truth labels exist against which to compute silhouette agreement The question is about imputation of specific missing values rather than whether denoising recovers sub-population structure; the article notes the non-trivial distinction between true (celltype-specific) and false (dropout) zeros makes classical imputation evaluation unsuitable The RNA matrix has already been heavily filtered or transformed (e.g., normalized, log-transformed) in ways incompatible with DCA's raw-count negative binomial input assumption

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., mESC-SMARTer / ola_mES_2i.RData) must be normalized and log-transformed to log2(TPM+1) before reCAT clustering, scoring, or marker-gene distribution plots.
skills.name: scrna-seq-deseq-normalization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-deseq-normalization Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., mESC-SMARTer / ola_mES_2i.RData) must be normalized and log-transformed to log2(TPM+1) before reCAT clustering, scoring, or marker-gene distribution plots. Input is already a reCAT test_exp matrix that is log2(TPM+1) normalized — re-normalizing would distort values. The goal is stage scoring/ordering (get_ordIndex, get_score, get_hmm_order) on already-preprocessed data rather than producing the normalized matrix itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Normalize single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with DESeq size-factor normalization and the reCAT log2(TPM+1) convention before cell cycle analyses such as marker-gene violin plots, clustering, and HMM-based cell cycle staging. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Normalize single-cell RNA-seq count matrices with DESeq size-factor normalization and the reCAT log2(TPM+1) convention before cell cycle analyses such as marker-gene violin plots, clustering, and HMM-based cell cycle staging.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reCAT test_exp matrix that is log2(TPM+1) normalized — re-normalizing would distort values. The goal is stage scoring/ordering (get_ordIndex, get_score, get_hmm_order) on already-preprocessed data rather than producing the normalized matrix itself.

skills.description: Use when analyzing how L-R pair expression changes across ordered developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis) and you need to assign pairs to temporal clusters and identify peak time points.
skills.name: scrna-seq-developmental-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-developmental-trajectory-analysis Use when analyzing how L-R pair expression changes across ordered developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis) and you need to assign pairs to temporal clusters and identify peak time points. The data are a single stationary condition without a developmental time series — use standard single-time-point cell-cell communication inference instead (e.g., singlenet step). You need per-time-point interaction networks rather than temporal grouping of L-R pair expression profiles — the DTW/comparednet steps are the appropriate dsCellNet stages. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Groups developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pairs into temporal clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, refining key time points (e.g., E12.5, E15.5, E17.5) and mediator connections in the dsCellNet corticogenesis workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Groups developmental-series expression profiles of ligand-receptor pairs into temporal clusters using Mfuzz fuzzy c-means, refining key time points (e.g., E12.5, E15.5, E17.5) and mediator connections in the dsCellNet corticogenesis workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are a single stationary condition without a developmental time series — use standard single-time-point cell-cell communication inference instead (e.g., singlenet step). You need per-time-point interaction networks rather than temporal grouping of L-R pair expression profiles — the DTW/comparednet steps are the appropriate dsCellNet stages.

skills.description: Use when a cell-by-gene expression matrix has cells labeled by clone/copy-state (e.g., XClone Clone_ID annotation) and the goal is to test whether DEGs between clones are enriched in LOH regions, as in TNBC1.
skills.name: scrna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-differential-expression-analysis Use when a cell-by-gene expression matrix has cells labeled by clone/copy-state (e.g., XClone Clone_ID annotation) and the goal is to test whether DEGs between clones are enriched in LOH regions, as in TNBC1. CNA inference has not yet been run and no per-region LOH/CNA-state annotation exists — run XClone (RDR + BAF modules) first, since this skill depends on the CNA-state stratification The analysis goal is detecting copy-neutral LOH itself from scRNA-seq — use XClone directly, as methods like InferCNV and CopyKAT cannot detect copy-neutral LOH Data are from single-cell DNA-seq pipelines (e.g., ACT, CHISEL) rather than gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrices, so there are no expression values to test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between clonal populations in an XClone-annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., Clone 1 vs Normal and Clone 2 vs Normal in the TNBC1 triple-negative breast cancer sample), and links DEG burden to genomic region state (copy-neutral LOH vs non-LOH) detected by XClone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between clonal populations in an XClone-annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., Clone 1 vs Normal and Clone 2 vs Normal in the TNBC1 triple-negative breast cancer sample), and links DEG burden to genomic region state (copy-neutral LOH vs non-LOH) detected by XClone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CNA inference has not yet been run and no per-region LOH/CNA-state annotation exists — run XClone (RDR + BAF modules) first, since this skill depends on the CNA-state stratification The analysis goal is detecting copy-neutral LOH itself from scRNA-seq — use XClone directly, as methods like InferCNV and CopyKAT cannot detect copy-neutral LOH Data are from single-cell DNA-seq pipelines (e.g., ACT, CHISEL) rather than gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrices, so there are no expression values to test

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data comes with predicted cluster labels (e.g. from scBGEDA on datasets like QS_Heart) and the goal is to assign cell-type identities by testing differential expression per cluster against published marker genes.
skills.name: scrna-seq-differential-expression-testing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-differential-expression-testing Use when scRNA-seq expression data comes with predicted cluster labels (e.g. from scBGEDA on datasets like QS_Heart) and the goal is to assign cell-type identities by testing differential expression per cluster against published marker genes. Input cells have no cluster labels yet — clustering (e.g. scBGEDA's three-module pipeline: preprocess.py, SDDA.py, BC.m) must be run first before marker testing is meaningful. The data is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table rather than single-cell expression with per-cell labels — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test in scanpy requires per-cell expression grouped by cluster. No curated marker reference (e.g. CellMark) is available for the tissue or organism, since cell-type annotation depends on matching DEGs to published markers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify cell-type marker genes from scRNA-seq cluster assignments by running the Wilcoxon rank-sum test per cluster in scanpy (rank_genes_groups, method='wilcoxon'), retaining the top 20 DEGs per cluster at P<0.05, and annotating clusters by matching nominated markers to the CellMark curated marker database. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Identify cell-type marker genes from scRNA-seq cluster assignments by running the Wilcoxon rank-sum test per cluster in scanpy (rank_genes_groups, method='wilcoxon'), retaining the top 20 DEGs per cluster at P<0.05, and annotating clusters by matching nominated markers to the CellMark curated marker database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input cells have no cluster labels yet — clustering (e.g. scBGEDA's three-module pipeline: preprocess.py, SDDA.py, BC.m) must be run first before marker testing is meaningful. The data is bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed feature table rather than single-cell expression with per-cell labels — the Wilcoxon rank-sum test in scanpy requires per-cell expression grouped by cluster. No curated marker reference (e.g. CellMark) is available for the tissue or organism, since cell-type annotation depends on matching DEGs to published markers.

skills.description: Use when you have a log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrix (cells x genes) and need a 2D embedding that reveals rare cell populations more cleanly than t-SNE or UMAP.
skills.name: scrna-seq-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a log2-transformed scRNA-seq matrix (cells x genes) and need a 2D embedding that reveals rare cell populations more cleanly than t-SNE or UMAP. When the input is not an expression matrix but an already-computed feature table or embedding — EDGE expects log-normalized gene expression as input When the analysis goal is only global/hierarchical structure recovery and no rare cell types or feature genes are of interest — t-SNE preserves local structure but can lose global geometry, and EDGE's advantage is specifically rare-type separation When memory is severely constrained and very large hash table sizes or many weak learners would be required — the README warns 'large memory will be required' http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Two-dimensional embedding of log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices via EDGE, which estimates an initial spectral embedding from a similarity matrix built by weak learners and refines it with stochastic gradient descent to separate rare cell types while enabling feature gene extraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Two-dimensional embedding of log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices via EDGE, which estimates an initial spectral embedding from a similarity matrix built by weak learners and refines it with stochastic gradient descent to separate rare cell types while enabling feature gene extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is not an expression matrix but an already-computed feature table or embedding — EDGE expects log-normalized gene expression as input When the analysis goal is only global/hierarchical structure recovery and no rare cell types or feature genes are of interest — t-SNE preserves local structure but can lose global geometry, and EDGE's advantage is specifically rare-type separation When memory is severely constrained and very large hash table sizes or many weak learners would be required — the README warns 'large memory will be required'

skills.description: Use when many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) have overlapping DE genes and per-group markers fail, and a smallest global feature set distinguishing every phenotype pair is needed.
skills.name: scrna-seq-discriminative-gene-set-selection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-discriminative-gene-set-selection Use when many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) have overlapping DE genes and per-group markers fail, and a smallest global feature set distinguishing every phenotype pair is needed. Only a small number of distinct groups (e.g., major cell types) with non-overlapping DE genes — standard per-group marker selection suffices. The goal is an all-relevant feature ranking rather than a minimal discriminative cover (mRMR/Boruta-style methods are the wrong contrast here). skills.search_text: scrna-seq-embedding-generation Use when a sxRNA-seq dataset contains multiple batches/samples (batch.var present) and the goal is a batch-corrected embedding for joint clustering, cell-type annotation, or benchmarking against integration methods such as scVI or Harmony. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is causal network construction or obtaining directions of gene associations — the article states c-CSN is not designed for causal gene association networks and directions cannot be obtained The input is not single-cell expression data, e.g. bulk RNA-seq with no per-cell resolution for building cell-specific networks Runtime is severely constrained, since the conditional testing incurs a G-fold computational cost increase with no parallel scheme provided

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-gene-filtering Use when scRNA-seq counts from multiple subjects (e.g., iPSC dopaminergic differentiation time points) must be converted into per-donor gene co-expression adjacency matrices as input for MuDCoD or similar personalized dynamic community detection. The input is already a set of adjacency matrices or a co-expression network — the filtering step is only needed upstream of community detection. The goal is gene centrality analysis rather than producing networks for MuDCoD — the article explicitly stops before Dozer's 'Section 4: Gene Centrality Analysis'. Data are not population-scale scRNA-seq from multiple subjects; Dozer is designed for subject-specific co-expression networks with phenotypic subject information. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Filter genes and construct personalized weighted gene co-expression networks from population-scale scRNA-seq using Dozer, selecting top 3000 highly variable genes with Scanpy and SCTransform normalization, then thresholding each network at its top-5% edges to produce n-by-n adjacency matrices for multi-subject dynamic community detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a set of adjacency matrices or a co-expression network — the filtering step is only needed upstream of community detection. Data are not population-scale scRNA-seq from multiple subjects; Dozer is designed for subject-specific co-expression networks with phenotypic subject information.
