Input has not passed Input_preprocess()/Cell_qc(), so the ablation arms cannot share a common quality-controlled starting point The dataset is not a pooled CRISPR knockout screening dataset with per-cell sgRNA assignments (e.g. plain scRNA-seq without perturbation labels), since Rank_overall perturbation rankings cannot be produced You only need SAVER imputation itself as a final result rather than a sensitivity comparison — in that case call Data_imputation directly without the ablation design http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 An ablation skill that re-runs the MUSIC single-cell CRISPR screening pipeline with SAVER imputation and cell filtering toggled on/off, quantifying how each preprocessing strategy shifts the final perturbation effect ranking (average pairwise ranking similarity ≈ 0.6 across 14 datasets, with the combined skip being the most disruptive). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10216-x
skills.summary: An ablation skill that re-runs the MUSIC single-cell CRISPR screening pipeline with SAVER imputation and cell filtering toggled on/off, quantifying how each preprocessing strategy shifts the final perturbation effect ranking (average pairwise ranking similarity ≈ 0.6 across 14 datasets, with the combined skip being the most disruptive).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has not passed Input_preprocess()/Cell_qc(), so the ablation arms cannot share a common quality-controlled starting point The dataset is not a pooled CRISPR knockout screening dataset with per-cell sgRNA assignments (e.g. plain scRNA-seq without perturbation labels), since Rank_overall perturbation rankings cannot be produced You only need SAVER imputation itself as a final result rather than a sensitivity comparison — in that case call Data_imputation directly without the ablation design

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether an scRNA-Seq imputation method recovers cell-type structure or differential expression signal from dropout/NB-noise matrices, against AutoClass and control methods on known-truth data.
skills.name: scrna-seq-imputation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-imputation-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether an scRNA-Seq imputation method recovers cell-type structure or differential expression signal from dropout/NB-noise matrices, against AutoClass and control methods on known-truth data. Input data has no ground-truth labels or paired true counts, so ASW against known cell types or median DE t-statistics over truly DE genes cannot be computed The goal is applying one imputation method to new data rather than comparing multiple imputation methods head-to-head under controlled noise Data is not single-cell RNA-Seq count data (e.g., bulk RNA-Seq or proteomics), where the dropout/NB-noise simulation and imputation benchmark design do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A benchmarking workflow for comparing AutoClass against control imputation methods (DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC, regular autoencoder) on simulated Splatter datasets and the Tian et al. sc_mixology cell-mixture data, scoring recovery by average silhouette width (ASW) on t-SNE embeddings and median DE t-statistics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow for comparing AutoClass against control imputation methods (DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC, regular autoencoder) on simulated Splatter datasets and the Tian et al. sc_mixology cell-mixture data, scoring recovery by average silhouette width (ASW) on t-SNE embeddings and median DE t-statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has no ground-truth labels or paired true counts, so ASW against known cell types or median DE t-statistics over truly DE genes cannot be computed The goal is applying one imputation method to new data rather than comparing multiple imputation methods head-to-head under controlled noise Data is not single-cell RNA-Seq count data (e.g., bulk RNA-Seq or proteomics), where the dropout/NB-noise simulation and imputation benchmark design do not apply

skills.description: Use when multiple sxRNA-seq batches/samples must be jointly clustered with batch effects removed while retaining interpretable gene-module factors, e.g. to annotate cell types or compare integration performance against scVI, Harmony, or LIGER.
skills.name: scrna-seq-joint-clustering-across-batches
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-joint-clustering-across-batches Use when multiple sxRNA-seq batches/samples must be jointly clustered with batch effects removed while retaining interpretable gene-module factors, e.g. to annotate cell types or compare integration performance against scVI, Harmony, or LIGER. When the goal requires standard, non-interpretable integration-only embeddings without gene-module interpretation, or when comparing against methods where task-specific performance matters — no method is always the best across all tasks, so verify on your specific task. When datasets are complex multi-condition, multi-sample samples that do not share the same axes of variation — the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than the consensus PCA default. For smoothed/imputed expression values beyond visualization — the README advises using MAGIC-like batch-aware smoothed values from the H/F matrices with caution and only for visualization purposes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Perform interpretable joint clustering of scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets across batches using JOINTLY, a hybrid linear and non-linear kernel-based joint NMF method, followed by Seurat clustering and ARI/NMI evaluation against cell type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Perform interpretable joint clustering of scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets across batches using JOINTLY, a hybrid linear and non-linear kernel-based joint NMF method, followed by Seurat clustering and ARI/NMI evaluation against cell type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal requires standard, non-interpretable integration-only embeddings without gene-module interpretation, or when comparing against methods where task-specific performance matters — no method is always the best across all tasks, so verify on your specific task. When datasets are complex multi-condition, multi-sample samples that do not share the same axes of variation — the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than the consensus PCA default. For smoothed/imputed expression values beyond visualization — the README advises using MAGIC-like batch-aware smoothed values from the H/F matrices with caution and only for visualization purposes.

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed source scRNA-Seq matrix X_src comes with ground-truth cluster labels y_src and those annotations should steer NMF dictionary learning before transferring knowledge to an unlabeled target dataset.
skills.name: scrna-seq-label-one-hot-initialization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-label-one-hot-initialization Use when a pre-processed source scRNA-Seq matrix X_src comes with ground-truth cluster labels y_src and those annotations should steer NMF dictionary learning before transferring knowledge to an unlabeled target dataset. The source dataset has no ground-truth cell-type annotations — the scRNA framework then generates labels via NMF clustering instead of one-hot initialization You need to cluster the target dataset itself rather than learn a source dictionary — use the target-side knowledge-transfer step (learning W_trg given fixed H_src) instead The source and target gene spaces barely overlap — the paper notes information loss is inevitable since only genes present in both datasets can be used http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Initializes the source-data matrix W_src of the elastic-net-regularized NMF in the scRNA transfer-learning pipeline with a one-hot encoding of already-known source cell-type cluster labels, so the learned dictionary H_src (g genes x k clusters) is anchored to the annotated reference cell types rather than discovered from scratch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Initializes the source-data matrix W_src of the elastic-net-regularized NMF in the scRNA transfer-learning pipeline with a one-hot encoding of already-known source cell-type cluster labels, so the learned dictionary H_src (g genes x k clusters) is anchored to the annotated reference cell types rather than discovered from scratch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The source dataset has no ground-truth cell-type annotations — the scRNA framework then generates labels via NMF clustering instead of one-hot initialization You need to cluster the target dataset itself rather than learn a source dictionary — use the target-side knowledge-transfer step (learning W_trg given fixed H_src) instead The source and target gene spaces barely overlap — the paper notes information loss is inevitable since only genes present in both datasets can be used

skills.description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq datasets from different labs or protocols using labeled reference datasets, especially when annotations are at different resolutions and unknown cell populations must be rejected or discovered.
skills.name: scrna-seq-label-prediction-with-rejection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-label-prediction-with-rejection Use when annotating scRNA-seq datasets from different labs or protocols using labeled reference datasets, especially when annotations are at different resolutions and unknown cell populations must be rejected or discovered. Datasets are not batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL explicitly requires alignment beforehand and does not perform batch correction itself Cell populations do not follow a hierarchical (tree-like) relationship, e.g., dedifferentiation states such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A complete reference atlas with standardized nomenclature already resolves the annotation task — simpler name-based or marker-based annotation may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Use scHPL, a hierarchical progressive learning method, to annotate cells in single-cell RNA-seq data by constructing a classification tree across multiple datasets and training per-node classifiers (linear SVM, kNN, or one-class SVM) so that unseen populations can be rejected and new cell populations discovered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Use scHPL, a hierarchical progressive learning method, to annotate cells in single-cell RNA-seq data by constructing a classification tree across multiple datasets and training per-node classifiers (linear SVM, kNN, or one-class SVM) so that unseen populations can be rejected and new cell populations discovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL explicitly requires alignment beforehand and does not perform batch correction itself Cell populations do not follow a hierarchical (tree-like) relationship, e.g., dedifferentiation states such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes A complete reference atlas with standardized nomenclature already resolves the annotation task — simpler name-based or marker-based annotation may suffice

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain dropout events and you need a nonlinear low-dimensional (2D) cell representation for visualization, lineage re-establishment, or downstream gene-marker discovery via correlation with latent features.
skills.name: scrna-seq-latent-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-latent-feature-extraction Use when scRNA-seq data contain dropout events and you need a nonlinear low-dimensional (2D) cell representation for visualization, lineage re-establishment, or downstream gene-marker discovery via correlation with latent features. Input is not scRNA-seq with dropout events but a bulk RNA-seq or already-reduced feature table — VASC's Gumbel-based dropout modeling and dimension reduction are specific to noisy single-cell data You need a fixed, deterministic embedding in a single run — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation requiring repeated runs You have no basis for choosing the latent dimension and cannot fix the co-variance matrix for very small sample sizes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Extract low-dimensional latent features from single-cell RNA-seq data using VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models dropout events, then correlate gene expression against the 2D latent features to identify candidate marker genes (e.g. associated with human pre-implantation embryo development). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.08.003
skills.summary: Extract low-dimensional latent features from single-cell RNA-seq data using VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models dropout events, then correlate gene expression against the 2D latent features to identify candidate marker genes (e.g. associated with human pre-implantation embryo development).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not scRNA-seq with dropout events but a bulk RNA-seq or already-reduced feature table — VASC's Gumbel-based dropout modeling and dimension reduction are specific to noisy single-cell data You need a fixed, deterministic embedding in a single run — stochastic optimization introduces run-to-run variation requiring repeated runs You have no basis for choosing the latent dimension and cannot fix the co-variance matrix for very small sample sizes

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., .npz of HVG features, AnnData) need cell-type-invariant latent representations for clustering, and deep generative baselines like scVI are too costly or hard to optimize.
skills.name: scrna-seq-latent-feature-learning
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-latent-feature-learning Use when scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., .npz of HVG features, AnnData) need cell-type-invariant latent representations for clustering, and deep generative baselines like scVI are too costly or hard to optimize. Datasets are small — Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, like other deep neural network methods. Data contain batch effects that have not been corrected — Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods; users must correct for batch effects before running it. The goal is marker gene discovery outside highly variable genes — Miscell's cluster-specific marker identification is limited to HVGs and may miss markers outside them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Learn latent cell representations from sparse, noisy single-cell RNA-seq data using Miscell, a self-supervised contrastive deep learning approach (DenseNet encoder, MoCo-style), and use the learned features for clustering and downstream embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Learn latent cell representations from sparse, noisy single-cell RNA-seq data using Miscell, a self-supervised contrastive deep learning approach (DenseNet encoder, MoCo-style), and use the learned features for clustering and downstream embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are small — Miscell demands a large sample size to obtain good performance, like other deep neural network methods. Data contain batch effects that have not been corrected — Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods; users must correct for batch effects before running it. The goal is marker gene discovery outside highly variable genes — Miscell's cluster-specific marker identification is limited to HVGs and may miss markers outside them.

skills.description: Use when target scRNA-seq latent representations have confirmed bimodal E-score distributions (via bimodality coefficient or Hartigan's dip test) and cells must be split into known vs unknown groups without a manual threshold.
skills.name: scrna-seq-latent-representation-scoring
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-latent-representation-scoring Use when target scRNA-seq latent representations have confirmed bimodal E-score distributions (via bimodality coefficient or Hartigan's dip test) and cells must be split into known vs unknown groups without a manual threshold. Bimodality tests (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test) find no bimodal structure — then scEMAIL defines the known group as all target cells and skips thresholding Raw source data are available and can be aligned with target data — the source-free, threshold-free design is not needed A priori known, manually specified thresholds are acceptable and user supervision is available http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Score target-cell latent representations in scEMAIL with an expert ensemble E-score (entropy, confidence, consistency) and partition cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups using an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold, enabling automatic novel cell-type perception without a user-selected cutoff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Score target-cell latent representations in scEMAIL with an expert ensemble E-score (entropy, confidence, consistency) and partition cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups using an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold, enabling automatic novel cell-type perception without a user-selected cutoff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bimodality tests (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test) find no bimodal structure — then scEMAIL defines the known group as all target cells and skips thresholding Raw source data are available and can be aligned with target data — the source-free, threshold-free design is not needed A priori known, manually specified thresholds are acceptable and user supervision is available

skills.description: Use when preparing raw count matrices from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets (e.g. 10X neuron_9k and nuclei_900) as input to scID or similar methods that require library-depth-normalized, non-log-transformed data.
skills.name: scrna-seq-library-depth-normalization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-library-depth-normalization Use when preparing raw count matrices from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets (e.g. 10X neuron_9k and nuclei_900) as input to scID or similar methods that require library-depth-normalized, non-log-transformed data. Data are already log-transformed — scID requires non-log-transformed values, so log-normalized matrices must not be fed in directly The goal is cross-dataset integration by batch correction rather than reference-based cell assignment — the article notes batch-correction methods risk over-correction and losing biological variance Neither the reference nor the target is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies library-depth (TPM or CPM) column normalization to scRNA-seq count matrices so they meet scID's input requirement of depth-normalized, non-log-transformed expression, using scID's counts_to_cpm helper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Applies library-depth (TPM or CPM) column normalization to scRNA-seq count matrices so they meet scID's input requirement of depth-normalized, non-log-transformed expression, using scID's counts_to_cpm helper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already log-transformed — scID requires non-log-transformed values, so log-normalized matrices must not be fed in directly The goal is cross-dataset integration by batch correction rather than reference-based cell assignment — the article notes batch-correction methods risk over-correction and losing biological variance Neither the reference nor the target is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID is not a recommended approach in that case

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g. Tabula Muris Spleen-10X_P4_7 ExpressionData.csv) must be normalized and rescaled to the (0,1) interval before feeding scRNA_seq_preprocessing output into scGATE_edge()/scGATE_logic() network inference.
skills.name: scrna-seq-library-size-normalization-and-rescaling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-library-size-normalization-and-rescaling Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g. Tabula Muris Spleen-10X_P4_7 ExpressionData.csv) must be normalized and rescaled to the (0,1) interval before feeding scRNA_seq_preprocessing output into scGATE_edge()/scGATE_logic() network inference. Input matrix is already normalized or is not raw UMI counts (set library_size_normalization="False" or skip; double-normalizing distorts the (0,1) rescaling) Goal is large-scale GRN inference from scratch on many genes without a refined TF candidate list — the article notes scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with refined candidate TFs Data are pseudotime-sorted single-cell profiles along differentiation trajectories, which scGATE does not yet handle http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 scGATE-specific preprocessing of raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells in rows, genes in columns) that performs library size normalization followed by min-max rescaling into the (0,1) interval, optionally restricted to a supplied TF list, so expression profiles are ready for Hill-function-based logic-gate inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: scGATE-specific preprocessing of raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells in rows, genes in columns) that performs library size normalization followed by min-max rescaling into the (0,1) interval, optionally restricted to a supplied TF list, so expression profiles are ready for Hill-function-based logic-gate inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input matrix is already normalized or is not raw UMI counts (set library_size_normalization="False" or skip; double-normalizing distorts the (0,1) rescaling) Goal is large-scale GRN inference from scratch on many genes without a refined TF candidate list — the article notes scGATE is applicable only to a small (<200) subset of genes with refined candidate TFs Data are pseudotime-sorted single-cell profiles along differentiation trajectories, which scGATE does not yet handle

skills.description: Use when starting from raw cell-by-gene FACS scRNA-seq counts (Tabula Muris Figshare CSVs) that must be filtered, normalized by library size, log-transformed, and reduced to 50 principal components before embedding evaluation.
skills.name: scrna-seq-library-size-normalization-log-transform
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-library-size-normalization-log-transform Use when starting from raw cell-by-gene FACS scRNA-seq counts (Tabula Muris Figshare CSVs) that must be filtered, normalized by library size, log-transformed, and reduced to 50 principal components before embedding evaluation. Input is a scATAC-seq counts-by-peaks matrix (the 10x PBMC data in this paper instead uses TSS-enrichment filtering and peak/cell count cutoffs like >=200 peaks and >10 cells per peak) The dataset is not normalized or the goal is quality analysis of an entire unnormalized pipeline — the paper notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets Data are already preprocessed (e.g. an existing PCA or embedding) and only require the DR-quality assessment step rather than re-normalization http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocess raw Tabula Muris FACS scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. Diaphragm-counts.csv) by quality filtering, per-cell library-size normalization, log-transformation, and HVG selection/scaling to prepare a PCA-ready matrix (50 PCs) for downstream dimensionality-reduction quality assessment with EMBEDR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Preprocess raw Tabula Muris FACS scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. Diaphragm-counts.csv) by quality filtering, per-cell library-size normalization, log-transformation, and HVG selection/scaling to prepare a PCA-ready matrix (50 PCs) for downstream dimensionality-reduction quality assessment with EMBEDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a scATAC-seq counts-by-peaks matrix (the 10x PBMC data in this paper instead uses TSS-enrichment filtering and peak/cell count cutoffs like >=200 peaks and >10 cells per peak) The dataset is not normalized or the goal is quality analysis of an entire unnormalized pipeline — the paper notes EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets Data are already preprocessed (e.g. an existing PCA or embedding) and only require the DR-quality assessment step rather than re-normalization

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data lacks lineage labels but you need cell lineage relationships, e.g., to study heritable gene expression, symmetric vs asymmetric cell fate decisions, or DEGs at cell fate switches.
skills.name: scrna-seq-lineage-inference
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-lineage-inference Use when scRNA-seq data lacks lineage labels but you need cell lineage relationships, e.g., to study heritable gene expression, symmetric vs asymmetric cell fate decisions, or DEGs at cell fate switches. Cell populations contain only distantly related cells — GEMLI performs less robustly there Long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months is needed — GEMLI is limited to lineages over about 1–5 cell divisions Lineages with large variability in growth rates, which may decrease GEMLI's performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Predict small to medium-sized cell lineages (cells sharing a common ancestor over ~1–5 divisions) from scRNA-seq data alone using GEMLI, which leverages genes with stable, heritable expression (gene expression memory) through repeated iterative clustering — no barcode or genetic lineage tracing required. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Predict small to medium-sized cell lineages (cells sharing a common ancestor over ~1–5 divisions) from scRNA-seq data alone using GEMLI, which leverages genes with stable, heritable expression (gene expression memory) through repeated iterative clustering — no barcode or genetic lineage tracing required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell populations contain only distantly related cells — GEMLI performs less robustly there Long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months is needed — GEMLI is limited to lineages over about 1–5 cell divisions Lineages with large variability in growth rates, which may decrease GEMLI's performance

skills.description: Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (CSV or JLD2 with rows=cells, columns=genes) before dimensionality reduction, especially for sparse data where conventional log normalization would distort signals via unequal cell vector lengths.
skills.name: scrna-seq-log-l2-normalization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-log-l2-normalization Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (CSV or JLD2 with rows=cells, columns=genes) before dimensionality reduction, especially for sparse data where conventional log normalization would distort signals via unequal cell vector lengths. The data are already normalized or already a feature/gene-selected table — re-normalizing would not address the log-normalization distortion scLENS targets The goal is to repair dropout zeros before analysis — scLENS deliberately avoids imputation, which can bias data and generate false signals The data are not single-cell count matrices (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial statistics) where the cell-vector-length distortion mechanism does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 scLENS's two-step preprocessing for scRNA-seq count matrices: log normalization with a scaling factor of 1, followed by L2 normalization that uniformizes cell vector lengths. This combination addresses the false variability that conventional log normalization introduces by amplifying gaps between zero and non-zero values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: scLENS's two-step preprocessing for scRNA-seq count matrices: log normalization with a scaling factor of 1, followed by L2 normalization that uniformizes cell vector lengths. This combination addresses the false variability that conventional log normalization introduces by amplifying gaps between zero and non-zero values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already normalized or already a feature/gene-selected table — re-normalizing would not address the log-normalization distortion scLENS targets The goal is to repair dropout zeros before analysis — scLENS deliberately avoids imputation, which can bias data and generate false signals The data are not single-cell count matrices (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or spatial statistics) where the cell-vector-length distortion mechanism does not apply

skills.description: Use when raw SeqFISH/scRNA-seq count matrices must be converted to AnnData h5ad with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']] and log-normalized (scran) before contrastive model training or spatial reconstruction benchmarking.
skills.name: scrna-seq-log-normalization-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-log-normalization-preprocessing Use when raw SeqFISH/scRNA-seq count matrices must be converted to AnnData h5ad with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']] and log-normalized (scran) before contrastive model training or spatial reconstruction benchmarking. The input is already a log-normalized AnnData object compatible with the CellContrast train/eval pipeline — re-normalizing could distort the scran-scaled values used by the published benchmark. The data are sequencing-based spot-level ST (e.g. 10X Visium) rather than single-cell-resolution imaging data — different predefined parameters (parameters_spot.json vs parameters_singleCell.json) and considerations apply. The goal is deconvolution or gene imputation on ST spots rather than preparing expression profiles for SC spatial relationship reconstruction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Preprocess single-cell and spatial transcriptomics count matrices into log-normalized AnnData objects (scran-based log-normalization) so that CellContrast contrastive training and SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction operate on comparable expression scales. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Preprocess single-cell and spatial transcriptomics count matrices into log-normalized AnnData objects (scran-based log-normalization) so that CellContrast contrastive training and SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction operate on comparable expression scales.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a log-normalized AnnData object compatible with the CellContrast train/eval pipeline — re-normalizing could distort the scran-scaled values used by the published benchmark. The data are sequencing-based spot-level ST (e.g. 10X Visium) rather than single-cell-resolution imaging data — different predefined parameters (parameters_spot.json vs parameters_singleCell.json) and considerations apply. The goal is deconvolution or gene imputation on ST spots rather than preparing expression profiles for SC spatial relationship reconstruction.

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (genes × cells) is about to be fed into ccRemover or PCA-based factor analysis, and the paper's protocol requires log-scaling and gene-wise centering first.
skills.name: scrna-seq-log-transformation-and-gene-centering
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-log-transformation-and-gene-centering Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (genes × cells) is about to be fed into ccRemover or PCA-based factor analysis, and the paper's protocol requires log-scaling and gene-wise centering first. Data are already normalized on a log scale and gene-centered (e.g. re-processing a corrected matrix like ccRemover's xhat output) The downstream method does not operate on PCA of the expression matrix and does not require gene-wise centering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Pre-processing step for scRNA-Seq expression matrices in which data are log-transformed and centered on a gene-by-gene basis prior to cell-cycle effect removal with ccRemover, so that principal components capture comparable variance scales across genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Pre-processing step for scRNA-Seq expression matrices in which data are log-transformed and centered on a gene-by-gene basis prior to cell-cycle effect removal with ccRemover, so that principal components capture comparable variance scales across genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already normalized on a log scale and gene-centered (e.g. re-processing a corrected matrix like ccRemover's xhat output) The downstream method does not operate on PCA of the expression matrix and does not require gene-wise centering

skills.description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq count matrices (mESC, melanoma Mel78-88, hESC 10X Chromium) as input to Cyclum's circular-manifold autoencoder or comparators like reCAT, Seurat, or ccRemover.
skills.name: scrna-seq-log2-variance-scaling-preprocessing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-log2-variance-scaling-preprocessing Use when preparing scRNA-seq count matrices (mESC, melanoma Mel78-88, hESC 10X Chromium) as input to Cyclum's circular-manifold autoencoder or comparators like reCAT, Seurat, or ccRemover. Input is already a normalized/feature-scaled expression matrix rather than raw counts — re-applying log2 and variance scaling would distort the data The downstream method requires its own normalization scheme (e.g., methods outside the Cyclum/reCAT comparison set that specify different transforms) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocessing convention recommended by the Cyclum authors for scRNA-seq expression matrices: a log2(x+1) transform followed by scaling to variance = 1 and centering to mean = 1, so the sinusoidal autoencoder operates on comparable gene scales. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15295-9
skills.summary: Preprocessing convention recommended by the Cyclum authors for scRNA-seq expression matrices: a log2(x+1) transform followed by scaling to variance = 1 and centering to mean = 1, so the sinusoidal autoencoder operates on comparable gene scales.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized/feature-scaled expression matrix rather than raw counts — re-applying log2 and variance scaling would distort the data The downstream method requires its own normalization scheme (e.g., methods outside the Cyclum/reCAT comparison set that specify different transforms)

skills.description: Use when annotating patient-derived cancer scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data to label malignant cells within an already-identified cancerous lineage and to obtain a continuous malignancy probability per cell or spot.
skills.name: scrna-seq-malignant-cell-classification
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-malignant-cell-classification Use when annotating patient-derived cancer scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data to label malignant cells within an already-identified cancerous lineage and to obtain a continuous malignancy probability per cell or spot. The dataset has not been pre-annotated for basic cell types — the tool relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types and is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages only, not to distinguish malignant cells from all other non-malignant cell types The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the article states capabilities require further testing Input is normal (non-cancer) tissue data where no malignant cells are expected and no prior lineage annotation has been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classifies malignant versus normal cells in cancer scRNA-seq (and spatial transcriptomics) data using scMalignantFinder, a machine-learning classifier trained on a signature-calibrated training set with a union of DEG features, returning a per-cell 'Normal'/'Malignant' prediction plus a malignancy_probability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Classifies malignant versus normal cells in cancer scRNA-seq (and spatial transcriptomics) data using scMalignantFinder, a machine-learning classifier trained on a signature-calibrated training set with a union of DEG features, returning a per-cell 'Normal'/'Malignant' prediction plus a malignancy_probability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has not been pre-annotated for basic cell types — the tool relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types and is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages only, not to distinguish malignant cells from all other non-malignant cell types The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the article states capabilities require further testing Input is normal (non-cancer) tissue data where no malignant cells are expected and no prior lineage annotation has been performed

skills.description: Use when building malignant-vs-normal cell classifier features from a signature-calibrated training set and you need per-dataset DEG testing (Seurat FindAllMarkers) followed by a cross-dataset union.
skills.name: scrna-seq-malignant-vs-epithelial-deg-testing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-malignant-vs-epithelial-deg-testing Use when building malignant-vs-normal cell classifier features from a signature-calibrated training set and you need per-dataset DEG testing (Seurat FindAllMarkers) followed by a cross-dataset union. A pre-built feature list already exists (e.g. the deposited ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt at Zenodo record 17888140) — reuse it instead of re-running DEG testing Cells have not yet been annotated into basic cell types, so no malignant vs normal epithelial comparator exists — scMalignantFinder relies on the prerequisite identification of basic cell types within cancerous lineages The comparison of interest is malignant vs all other non-malignant cells rather than vs originating normal epithelial cells — this skill's calibration and comparator are specifically normal epithelial cells http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives the scMalignantFinder model feature set by running per-dataset differential expression between malignant and normal epithelial cells and taking the union of up- and downregulated DEGs, yielding a 2707-gene feature list (1656 up, 1051 down). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Derives the scMalignantFinder model feature set by running per-dataset differential expression between malignant and normal epithelial cells and taking the union of up- and downregulated DEGs, yielding a 2707-gene feature list (1656 up, 1051 down).
skills.when_to_use_negative: A pre-built feature list already exists (e.g. the deposited ordered_feature.tsv or combined_tumor_up_down_degs.txt at Zenodo record 17888140) — reuse it instead of re-running DEG testing Cells have not yet been annotated into basic cell types, so no malignant vs normal epithelial comparator exists — scMalignantFinder relies on the prerequisite identification of basic cell types within cancerous lineages The comparison of interest is malignant vs all other non-malignant cells rather than vs originating normal epithelial cells — this skill's calibration and comparator are specifically normal epithelial cells

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether a clustering solution (e.g., scDCC with pairwise constraints vs. unconstrained) improves marker-gene cluster specificity in an scRNA-seq dataset, via paired per-gene specificity scores and a one-sided Wilcoxon test.
skills.name: scrna-seq-marker-gene-cluster-assignment-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-marker-gene-cluster-assignment-evaluation Use when you need to quantify whether a clustering solution (e.g., scDCC with pairwise constraints vs. unconstrained) improves marker-gene cluster specificity in an scRNA-seq dataset, via paired per-gene specificity scores and a one-sided Wilcoxon test. The goal is cell type assignment from predefined marker-gene sets (e.g., CellAssign or SCINA-style annotation) rather than evaluating cluster specificity of a fitted clustering solution. You are clustering an unrestricted dataset without a set of uniquely assigned marker genes to score specificity against. You only have a single clustering per condition and cannot form the ten paired repeats required for the paired signed-rank comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates whether constrained clustering (scDCC) improves cluster specificity of uniquely assigned marker genes in the human liver scRNA-seq dataset by comparing DESeq2 Wald-statistic-based specificity scores with vs. without pairwise constraints using a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (reported p = 0.00024). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22008-3
skills.summary: Evaluates whether constrained clustering (scDCC) improves cluster specificity of uniquely assigned marker genes in the human liver scRNA-seq dataset by comparing DESeq2 Wald-statistic-based specificity scores with vs. without pairwise constraints using a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (reported p = 0.00024).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cell type assignment from predefined marker-gene sets (e.g., CellAssign or SCINA-style annotation) rather than evaluating cluster specificity of a fitted clustering solution. You are clustering an unrestricted dataset without a set of uniquely assigned marker genes to score specificity against. You only have a single clustering per condition and cannot form the ten paired repeats required for the paired signed-rank comparison.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with cellular labels and a selected marker-gene panel (e.g., scGeneFit's 15-marker CBMC panel) and need to verify whether the reduced marker space preserves cell type distinctions via t-SNE.
skills.name: scrna-seq-marker-projection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-marker-projection Use when you have scRNA-seq data with cellular labels and a selected marker-gene panel (e.g., scGeneFit's 15-marker CBMC panel) and need to verify whether the reduced marker space preserves cell type distinctions via t-SNE. The goal is to select the marker panel itself rather than visualize an existing one — use scGeneFit's marker selection instead of a projection task The cell type classes are not linearly separable in the marker space or the analysis requires nonlinear dimension reduction — the article notes scGeneFit assumes linear separability and had not yet implemented nonlinear methods Labels are continuous manifold quantities (e.g., trajectory pseudotime or spatial location) rather than categorical cell type labels — the article states categorical labeling is a current limitation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Visualizes single-cell RNA-seq data in a low-dimensional marker-gene space by subsetting the full expression matrix to an scGeneFit-selected marker panel (e.g., 15 markers for the 13-population CBMC dataset) and embedding the cells with t-SNE to check that cell type distinctions are preserved. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: Visualizes single-cell RNA-seq data in a low-dimensional marker-gene space by subsetting the full expression matrix to an scGeneFit-selected marker panel (e.g., 15 markers for the 13-population CBMC dataset) and embedding the cells with t-SNE to check that cell type distinctions are preserved.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to select the marker panel itself rather than visualize an existing one — use scGeneFit's marker selection instead of a projection task The cell type classes are not linearly separable in the marker space or the analysis requires nonlinear dimension reduction — the article notes scGeneFit assumes linear separability and had not yet implemented nonlinear methods Labels are continuous manifold quantities (e.g., trajectory pseudotime or spatial location) rather than categorical cell type labels — the article states categorical labeling is a current limitation

skills.description: Use when fitting CTMM to pseudobulk scRNA-seq (OP or CTP) and per-observation measurement noise variances (nu, ctnu) must be supplied as model inputs.
skills.name: scrna-seq-measurement-noise-estimation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-measurement-noise-estimation Use when fitting CTMM to pseudobulk scRNA-seq (OP or CTP) and per-observation measurement noise variances (nu, ctnu) must be supplied as model inputs. Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells: CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Genes are very lowly expressed and severely non-Gaussian: the Gaussian approximation requires more cells than the ct_cut=10 threshold Sample sizes are below ~50 individuals: CTMM is not reliable in that regime and the Free test is slightly inflated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-individual and per-individual-cell-type measurement noise variances (nu and ctnu) from single-cell RNA-seq data so that CTMM linear mixed models can account for pseudobulk sampling noise when partitioning interindividual variance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Compute per-individual and per-individual-cell-type measurement noise variances (nu and ctnu) from single-cell RNA-seq data so that CTMM linear mixed models can account for pseudobulk sampling noise when partitioning interindividual variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual-cell type pairs have <=10 cells: CTMM requires >10 cells per pair and is limited to common cell types Genes are very lowly expressed and severely non-Gaussian: the Gaussian approximation requires more cells than the ct_cut=10 threshold Sample sizes are below ~50 individuals: CTMM is not reliable in that regime and the Free test is slightly inflated

skills.description: Use when adapting a pre-trained source classifier to target scRNA-seq cells without source data and you need globally retrieved, weighted neighbors (bidirectional/unidirectional/extensional) as self-supervised affinity constraints.
skills.name: scrna-seq-memory-bank-management
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-memory-bank-management Use when adapting a pre-trained source classifier to target scRNA-seq cells without source data and you need globally retrieved, weighted neighbors (bidirectional/unidirectional/extensional) as self-supervised affinity constraints. When raw source data are available, since explicit feature alignment methods (e.g., transfer learning with source access) are then applicable and this source-free bank-based approach is unnecessary. When no pre-trained source model exists to produce soft label bank S and latent representation bank R — the banks depend on the source classifier's outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Builds offline memory banks of latent representations and soft predicted labels from target scRNA-seq cells, enabling efficient global retrieval of multi-order neighbors that impose local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation in scEMAIL. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Builds offline memory banks of latent representations and soft predicted labels from target scRNA-seq cells, enabling efficient global retrieval of multi-order neighbors that impose local affinity constraints during source-free model adaptation in scEMAIL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When raw source data are available, since explicit feature alignment methods (e.g., transfer learning with source access) are then applicable and this source-free bank-based approach is unnecessary. When no pre-trained source model exists to produce soft label bank S and latent representation bank R — the banks depend on the source classifier's outputs.

skills.description: Use when evaluating which automatic scRNA-seq cell-type identification method (eager, lazy, or marker-based supervised) performs on a manually annotated dataset, measured by accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and speed.
skills.name: scrna-seq-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-method-benchmarking Use when evaluating which automatic scRNA-seq cell-type identification method (eager, lazy, or marker-based supervised) performs on a manually annotated dataset, measured by accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and speed. The dataset lacks manually annotated cell-type labels and no marker lists are available, so neither reference-based nor marker-based training is possible The goal is de novo cell discovery or clustering rather than benchmarking of supervised annotation methods Input is already a per-method summary table of metrics — the cross-validation evaluation has already been performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark automatic single-cell RNA-seq cell-type identification methods via five-fold stratified cross-validation self-projection, comparing prediction accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and running time across tissues using the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Benchmark automatic single-cell RNA-seq cell-type identification methods via five-fold stratified cross-validation self-projection, comparing prediction accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate and running time across tissues using the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks manually annotated cell-type labels and no marker lists are available, so neither reference-based nor marker-based training is possible The goal is de novo cell discovery or clustering rather than benchmarking of supervised annotation methods Input is already a per-method summary table of metrics — the cross-validation evaluation has already been performed

skills.description: Use when calling AutomaticCellTypeIdentification on count-matrix inputs and you must route a named method (e.g. Seurat, scmap-cell, SCSA) to the correct wrapper with the correct argument order.
skills.name: scrna-seq-method-category-dispatch
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-method-category-dispatch Use when calling AutomaticCellTypeIdentification on count-matrix inputs and you must route a named method (e.g. Seurat, scmap-cell, SCSA) to the correct wrapper with the correct argument order. No training labels AND no marker lists are available (method is unsupervised; these wrappers only cover supervised categories) Input is already a marker list but the target method is eager or lazy supervised — those wrappers require the full training expression matrix and labels, not markers The goal is to benchmark method accuracy (accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate) rather than to route and execute a single named method http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Dispatches scRNA-seq cell-type identification methods to one of three wrapper interfaces in the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package — eagersupervised, lazysupervised, and markersupervised — each with a distinct argument signature matched to the method's learning category. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Dispatches scRNA-seq cell-type identification methods to one of three wrapper interfaces in the AutomaticCellTypeIdentification R package — eagersupervised, lazysupervised, and markersupervised — each with a distinct argument signature matched to the method's learning category.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No training labels AND no marker lists are available (method is unsupervised; these wrappers only cover supervised categories) Input is already a marker list but the target method is eager or lazy supervised — those wrappers require the full training expression matrix and labels, not markers The goal is to benchmark method accuracy (accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate) rather than to route and execute a single named method

skills.description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix is about to be fed into scDHA's non-negative kernel autoencoder or any model that expects per-cell expression profiles scaled to [0, 1] with non-negative values.
skills.name: scrna-seq-minmax-cell-normalization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-minmax-cell-normalization Use when a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix is about to be fed into scDHA's non-negative kernel autoencoder or any model that expects per-cell expression profiles scaled to [0, 1] with non-negative values. Data is already normalized or is a feature-level table (e.g. gene statistics, not a cell-by-gene matrix) Downstream method explicitly requires library-size normalization or z-scored values (e.g. tools like SC3/Scanpy pipelines that assume different preprocessing) rather than [0,1]-bounded, non-negative input The matrix contains negative values (e.g. imputed or log-difference data), where non-negativity required by the kernel autoencoder would be violated by construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalizes each cell's scRNA-seq expression profile by min-max scaling to the [0, 1] range (optionally after log2(data + 1) transformation), preparing the count matrix for scDHA's non-negative kernel autoencoder gene-filtering module, which assumes non-negative, bounded inputs to produce a part-based representation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Normalizes each cell's scRNA-seq expression profile by min-max scaling to the [0, 1] range (optionally after log2(data + 1) transformation), preparing the count matrix for scDHA's non-negative kernel autoencoder gene-filtering module, which assumes non-negative, bounded inputs to produce a part-based representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already normalized or is a feature-level table (e.g. gene statistics, not a cell-by-gene matrix) Downstream method explicitly requires library-size normalization or z-scored values (e.g. tools like SC3/Scanpy pipelines that assume different preprocessing) rather than [0,1]-bounded, non-negative input The matrix contains negative values (e.g. imputed or log-difference data), where non-negativity required by the kernel autoencoder would be violated by construction

skills.description: Use when you need to predict miRNA expression or activity from scRNA-seq clusters or bulk RNA-seq profiles lacking miRNA measurements, e.g. Seurat objects from HCL, TCGA, CCLE, or induced-miRNA experiments.
skills.name: scrna-seq-mirna-activity-inference
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-mirna-activity-inference Use when you need to predict miRNA expression or activity from scRNA-seq clusters or bulk RNA-seq profiles lacking miRNA measurements, e.g. Seurat objects from HCL, TCGA, CCLE, or induced-miRNA experiments. You already have directly measured miRNA expression for the samples — miRSCAPE is designed for profiles where mature miRNAs are not captured by poly(A)-based scRNA-seq protocols. Single-cell data is too sparse and cannot be pooled by cluster — the article warns that given the large dropout rate, a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes may be required. The application sample's cellular/tissue context is very different from the training cohort — a substantive loss in performance is expected (Figure S9), so a context-matched model should be trained instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train or apply miRSCAPE, an XGBoost-based machine learning model, to infer miRNA expression/activity from genome-wide mRNA profiles of single-cell clusters, compensating for the inability of poly(A)-based scRNA-seq protocols to capture mature miRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Train or apply miRSCAPE, an XGBoost-based machine learning model, to infer miRNA expression/activity from genome-wide mRNA profiles of single-cell clusters, compensating for the inability of poly(A)-based scRNA-seq protocols to capture mature miRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have directly measured miRNA expression for the samples — miRSCAPE is designed for profiles where mature miRNAs are not captured by poly(A)-based scRNA-seq protocols. Single-cell data is too sparse and cannot be pooled by cluster — the article warns that given the large dropout rate, a pre-trained model may not work and retraining on detected genes may be required. The application sample's cellular/tissue context is very different from the training cohort — a substantive loss in performance is expected (Figure S9), so a context-matched model should be trained instead.

skills.description: Use when building a reference T cell atlas (e.g., murine TIL or LCMV viral CD8 T cell atlas) from multiple public scRNA-seq studies whose samples, protocols, and batches differ and must be aligned before annotation or query projection.
skills.name: scrna-seq-multi-study-dataset-integration
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-multi-study-dataset-integration Use when building a reference T cell atlas (e.g., murine TIL or LCMV viral CD8 T cell atlas) from multiple public scRNA-seq studies whose samples, protocols, and batches differ and must be aligned before annotation or query projection. skills.summary: Integration of heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq datasets from multiple individuals, tissues, batches, and technologies into a common reference atlas space using STACAS, the semi-supervised integration tool from the Carmona lab, as implemented within the ProjecTILs reference-atlas workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single homogeneous dataset with no batch or study effects — no cross-study integration is needed The goal is projecting a new query dataset onto an already-built reference atlas — use Run.ProjecTILs / make.projection instead of rebuilding the reference The data are not scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or flow cytometry) — STACAS integration of single-cell transcriptomes does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need per-cell activity scores for biological processes such as cell differentiation, proliferation, or immune response.

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-network-activity-scoring Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need per-cell activity scores for biological processes such as cell differentiation, proliferation, or immune response. The expression matrix is raw counts rather than a normalized expression matrix, since activity() expects normalized values You need pathway scores for a biological process with no bundled edge set and lack a gene ID list plus the full_human_ppin to build a custom PPIN The analysis goal is cell-type clustering from the transcriptome rather than scoring predefined biological-process network activity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes per-cell activity of protein-protein interaction networks (PPIN) associated with biological processes from normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices using the ORIGINS2 R package, enabling pathway-level scoring and cell annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2023.102179
skills.summary: Computes per-cell activity of protein-protein interaction networks (PPIN) associated with biological processes from normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices using the ORIGINS2 R package, enabling pathway-level scoring and cell annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is raw counts rather than a normalized expression matrix, since activity() expects normalized values You need pathway scores for a biological process with no bundled edge set and lack a gene ID list plus the full_human_ppin to build a custom PPIN The analysis goal is cell-type clustering from the transcriptome rather than scoring predefined biological-process network activity

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation method against controls: you need a noisy count matrix with known ground-truth expression and cell labels, or a real dataset (e.g., Tian et al. 305-cell mixture) degraded with dropout or negative binomial noise.
skills.name: scrna-seq-noise-simulation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-noise-simulation Use when benchmarking a scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation method against controls: you need a noisy count matrix with known ground-truth expression and cell labels, or a real dataset (e.g., Tian et al. 305-cell mixture) degraded with dropout or negative binomial noise. skills.summary: Simulates controlled noise (dropout, uniform, Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, negative binomial) onto scRNA-Seq count matrices — via Splatter-simulated truth or real datasets like the Tian et al. sc_mixology cell mixtures — to benchmark whether denoising methods (AutoClass vs. DCA, SAVER, scImpute, MAGIC) recover true expression and cell-type structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already clean, imputed, or normalized expression data with no noise layer added — there is no ground-truth/noisy pair to evaluate recovery against The goal is biological discovery on real data rather than method benchmarking — injecting simulated noise would distort genuine signal You lack known cell-type labels or a true count matrix, so ASW/MSE-based recovery cannot be validated

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., from Tabula Muris, 'Qx Limb Muscle', or PDAC datasets) must be normalized and reduced to highly variable genes prior to training a graph convolutional autoencoder such as scMGCA.
skills.name: scrna-seq-normalization-hvg-selection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-normalization-hvg-selection Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., from Tabula Muris, 'Qx Limb Muscle', or PDAC datasets) must be normalized and reduced to highly variable genes prior to training a graph convolutional autoencoder such as scMGCA. Input is already a normalized, HVG-filtered expression matrix (e.g., a denoised output from DCA or scVI) — re-filtering and re-normalizing can discard signal The analysis goal is marker-gene annotation or differential expression with Seurat/SCANPY on pre-clustered data rather than building an autoencoder input Bulk RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data, where the single-cell dropout-reduction rationale for filtering all-zero genes does not apply in the same way http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocess scRNA-seq count matrices by filtering out genes not expressed in cells, normalizing the gene expression matrix, and selecting highly variable genes before feeding them into the scMGCA graph-embedding autoencoder. skills.summary: Preprocess scRNA-seq count matrices by filtering out genes not expressed in cells, normalizing the gene expression matrix, and selecting highly variable genes before feeding them into the scMGCA graph-embedding autoencoder. This step reduces the impact of high dropout rates and retains only high-information genes for downstream clustering and genomic interpretation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized, HVG-filtered expression matrix (e.g., a denoised output from DCA or scVI) — re-filtering and re-normalizing can discard signal The analysis goal is marker-gene annotation or differential expression with Seurat/SCANPY on pre-clustered data rather than building an autoencoder input Bulk RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data, where the single-cell dropout-reduction rationale for filtering all-zero genes does not apply in the same way

skills.description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq data under open or open-partial settings where target-private cell types may exist, raw source data are unavailable, and no prior threshold for 'unknown' detection is known.
skills.name: scrna-seq-novel-cell-type-detection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-novel-cell-type-detection Use when annotating target scRNA-seq data under open or open-partial settings where target-private cell types may exist, raw source data are unavailable, and no prior threshold for 'unknown' detection is known. Target data are known to contain no novel cell types (closed or partial label-overlap setting) — bimodality testing and threshold partitioning are unnecessary Raw labeled source data are available and the user prefers explicit source-target feature alignment methods (e.g. scArches) rather than source-free adaptation Only per-cluster annotations without cell-level uncertainty are needed — the E-score requires per-cell classifier probability outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detects novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data without source data or manual thresholds by testing the expert-ensemble E-score distribution for bimodality (bimodality coefficient + Hartigan's dip test) and, if bimodal, partitioning cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups via an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Detects novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data without source data or manual thresholds by testing the expert-ensemble E-score distribution for bimodality (bimodality coefficient + Hartigan's dip test) and, if bimodal, partitioning cells into 'known' and 'unknown' groups via an adaptive manifold-mixup threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target data are known to contain no novel cell types (closed or partial label-overlap setting) — bimodality testing and threshold partitioning are unnecessary Raw labeled source data are available and the user prefers explicit source-target feature alignment methods (e.g. scArches) rather than source-free adaptation Only per-cluster annotations without cell-level uncertainty are needed — the E-score requires per-cell classifier probability outputs

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) is being imputed with scImpute and aberrant cells should be flagged and excluded before dropout imputation.
skills.name: scrna-seq-outlier-cell-detection
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-outlier-cell-detection Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) is being imputed with scImpute and aberrant cells should be flagged and excluded before dropout imputation. The input is already normalized, dimension-reduced, or a feature/cell-type table rather than a raw whole-genome count matrix — scImpute recommends applying it on the whole-genome count matrix with most genes present The goal is general-purpose outlier detection independent of dropout imputation — this rule is coupled to scImpute's imputation pipeline and serves to exclude outlier cells from imputation The number of cells is extremely large without a prior cell filtering step — computational efficiency is limited in that setting per the article's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Detects outlier cells in a raw scRNA-seq count matrix using scImpute's PCA-based nearest-neighbor distance rule, so that aberrant cells are excluded from dropout imputation rather than distorting it. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Detects outlier cells in a raw scRNA-seq count matrix using scImpute's PCA-based nearest-neighbor distance rule, so that aberrant cells are excluded from dropout imputation rather than distorting it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already normalized, dimension-reduced, or a feature/cell-type table rather than a raw whole-genome count matrix — scImpute recommends applying it on the whole-genome count matrix with most genes present The goal is general-purpose outlier detection independent of dropout imputation — this rule is coupled to scImpute's imputation pipeline and serves to exclude outlier cells from imputation The number of cells is extremely large without a prior cell filtering step — computational efficiency is limited in that setting per the article's discussion

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-per-cell-quality-metric-computation Use when tall-format (melted) scRNA-seq expression data has been loaded as a Spark DataFrame and per-cell/per-gene quality summaries are needed before applying data_filter() thresholds. skills.summary: Compute Spark-distributed per-cell (Θ1) and per-gene (Θ2) quality summary matrices from melted tall-format scRNA-seq data in scSPARKL, producing the QC metrics (e.g., percent ERCC, percent mitochondrial, dropout rate) that downstream cell/gene filtering thresholds depend on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has not yet been melted to tall format — scSPARKL requires data melting as the preceding step The goal is already-filtered data; this skill only derives quality summaries — filtering itself is delegated to data_filter() You need a quality-control implementation in Seurat, Scanpy, or scater rather than a Spark-native one — scSPARKL targets in-memory-limitation scenarios where those pipelines are constrained by RAM

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-per-gene-dropout-summarization Use when you need per-gene quality metrics (cells expressing > 0, dropout count/percentage, mean/total expression) from tall-format scRNA-seq data to drive gene-level filtering in a Spark-based pipeline. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a wide gene-by-cell matrix that has not been melted to tall format; the skill expects the tall/melted representation produced by the scSPARKL data-melting step You need per-cell quality metrics (ERCC percentage, mitochondrial percentage, total genes expressed) — use the Θ1 per-cell QC summary instead You are running an in-memory pipeline such as Seurat or Scanpy on a small dataset; the Spark-distributed approach is intended for large-scale scRNA-seq data

skills.description: Use when designing a benchmark where a cell population is artificially sparsified to test whether trajectory or clustering outcomes depend on sampling density, before attempting generative restoration.
skills.name: scrna-seq-population-downsampling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-population-downsampling Use when designing a benchmark where a cell population is artificially sparsified to test whether trajectory or clustering outcomes depend on sampling density, before attempting generative restoration. The population is already too sparse to yield a meaningful downsampled subset or a stable original trajectory reference The goal is conditional generation of specific cell types from multi-type data — use cscGAN conditioning rather than plain downsampling plus unconditional scGAN The analysis goal does not involve testing sampling-density sensitivity (e.g. simple marker gene detection on the full population) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Deliberately reduces a well-sampled scRNA-seq cell population (e.g. the 150-cell node-4 erythrocyte cluster from GSE72857 mouse bone marrow) to a sparse subset (e.g. 13 cells) to create a controlled test case for evaluating whether generative augmentation (scGAN) can restore downstream analyses such as PAGA pseudo-time trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Deliberately reduces a well-sampled scRNA-seq cell population (e.g. the 150-cell node-4 erythrocyte cluster from GSE72857 mouse bone marrow) to a sparse subset (e.g. 13 cells) to create a controlled test case for evaluating whether generative augmentation (scGAN) can restore downstream analyses such as PAGA pseudo-time trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The population is already too sparse to yield a meaningful downsampled subset or a stable original trajectory reference The goal is conditional generation of specific cell types from multi-type data — use cscGAN conditioning rather than plain downsampling plus unconditional scGAN The analysis goal does not involve testing sampling-density sensitivity (e.g. simple marker gene detection on the full population)

skills.search_text: scrna-seq-prediction-probability-extraction Use when a trained TOSICA Transformer model has annotated query scRNA-seq cells (e.g., monocyte subtypes in pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating myeloid data) and per-cell Prediction, Probability, and gene-set attention values must be exported for validation or enrichment testing. skills.summary: Extract TOSICA's per-cell predicted labels, softmax probabilities, and the attention matrix from the AnnData returned by TOSICA.pre(), assembling them into a single tosica_predictions.csv table for downstream cell-type and tissue-enrichment analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need cluster labels from an unsupervised workflow (Leiden/Seurat clustering) rather than reference-based label transfer with interpretability — TOSICA.pre requires a trained model and aligned reference genes. The query AnnData gene names/order do not match ref_adata.var_names and cannot be subset to match — predictions would be invalid. The input is already a feature/attention table rather than raw cell-by-gene expression; this skill operates on AnnData objects consumed by TOSICA.pre.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to detect rare cell populations in a scRNA-seq count matrix (thousands to ~68k+ profiles) and no annotated clusters exist yet; FiRE gives a per-cell continuous rareness score in seconds where RaceID/GiniClust scale poorly.
skills.name: scrna-seq-rare-cell-scoring
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-rare-cell-scoring Use when the goal is to detect rare cell populations in a scRNA-seq count matrix (thousands to ~68k+ profiles) and no annotated clusters exist yet; FiRE gives a per-cell continuous rareness score in seconds where RaceID/GiniClust scale poorly. The task is doublet detection: doublet rate varies between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application to doublet detection. You need to separate technical outliers from genuine minor cell-type cells: FiRE, in principle, does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. The input is already a cluster label table or feature summary rather than a cells-by-genes expression matrix — FiRE requires per-cell expression profiles to estimate bucket populousness. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assign a FiRE rareness score to every individual scRNA-seq expression profile using an LSH Sketch-based density estimator (L=100 estimators, M=50-bit hash codes, H=1017881 bins), then dichotomize cells into rare vs non-rare with the interquartile-range threshold rule — without clustering as an intermediate step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Assign a FiRE rareness score to every individual scRNA-seq expression profile using an LSH Sketch-based density estimator (L=100 estimators, M=50-bit hash codes, H=1017881 bins), then dichotomize cells into rare vs non-rare with the interquartile-range threshold rule — without clustering as an intermediate step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is doublet detection: doublet rate varies between 1% and 30%, a range that does not necessarily comply with the notion of cell rareness, limiting FiRE's application to doublet detection. You need to separate technical outliers from genuine minor cell-type cells: FiRE, in principle, does not discriminate between an outlier and cells representing minor cell types. The input is already a cluster label table or feature summary rather than a cells-by-genes expression matrix — FiRE requires per-cell expression profiles to estimate bucket populousness.

skills.description: Use when comparing scalability of clustering or cluster-merging methods on scRNA-seq data: you need wall-clock runtime on a fixed, small, cell-type-labelled subset to contrast with AUROC performance on the full dataset.
skills.name: scrna-seq-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing scalability of clustering or cluster-merging methods on scRNA-seq data: you need wall-clock runtime on a fixed, small, cell-type-labelled subset to contrast with AUROC performance on the full dataset. The analysis goal is statistical significance of cluster differences rather than method benchmarking — run cc.tl.merge_clusters directly instead of timing comparisons. The dataset is already small enough that all methods run interactively; runtime contrast is only meaningful where the expensive method measurably scales poorly (e.g. 178.80 s for 500 cells implies prohibitive cost at 483152 cells). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Times competing single-cell clustering/merging methods on identical cell subsets (e.g. Sc-SHC vs Cytocipher's merge_clusters on a 500-cell, 12-cell-type Tabula Sapiens subset) to quantify runtime scaling differences alongside accuracy benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435

skills.description: Use when you need to link scRNA-seq cells to spatial coordinates/positions via optimal transport — e.g., mapping 1297 Drosophila embryo cells onto 3039 seqFISH/in situ spatial positions from geometry.txt and dge_normalized.txt/bdtnp.txt inputs.
skills.name: scrna-seq-spatial-mapping
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-spatial-mapping Use when you need to link scRNA-seq cells to spatial coordinates/positions via optimal transport — e.g., mapping 1297 Drosophila embryo cells onto 3039 seqFISH/in situ spatial positions from geometry.txt and dge_normalized.txt/bdtnp.txt inputs. You only need spatial gene-expression prediction at positions without a cell-to-position coupling map. The dataset is so large that pairwise structured transport becomes computationally intractable even with landmark approximations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Maps n single cells from scRNA-seq data to m spatial positions (e.g., Drosophila embryo scRNA-seq vs. in situ hybridization from Synapse syn15665609) by solving an unbalanced, structured optimal transport problem with SpaOTsc, yielding an optimal transport plan γ* that connects the two datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Maps n single cells from scRNA-seq data to m spatial positions (e.g., Drosophila embryo scRNA-seq vs. in situ hybridization from Synapse syn15665609) by solving an unbalanced, structured optimal transport problem with SpaOTsc, yielding an optimal transport plan γ* that connects the two datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already spatially resolved single-cell measurements with coordinates per cell — SpaOTsc can be applied directly but the cell↔position mapping step is unnecessary.
