skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq reads labeled 'ambiguous' (compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts) need a probabilistic spliced/unspliced resolution, e.g. PBMC1k-style reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference.
skills.name: scrna-seq-splicing-status-prediction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-splicing-status-prediction Use when scRNA-seq reads labeled 'ambiguous' (compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts) need a probabilistic spliced/unspliced resolution, e.g. PBMC1k-style reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference. Reads already carry reliable spliced/unspliced labels (i.e. not from single-cell data with ambiguous counts) — Forseti is designed for scRNA-seq reads compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts Single-end reads or alignments without transcriptomic coordinates — Forseti scores putative fragments that associate each alignment with proximate priming sites, requiring toTranscriptome BAM output from STAR Long-read or non-10X data where oligo(dT) priming assumptions and the 10X whitelist (e.g. 3M-february-2018.txt) do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Apply Forseti, a mechanistic predictive model, to probabilistically assign a splicing status (spliced, unspliced, or ambiguous) to scRNA-seq reads by scoring putative fragments against proximate oligo(dT) priming sites using a trained binding-affinity MLP and a cubic-spline fragment-length distribution model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Apply Forseti, a mechanistic predictive model, to probabilistically assign a splicing status (spliced, unspliced, or ambiguous) to scRNA-seq reads by scoring putative fragments against proximate oligo(dT) priming sites using a trained binding-affinity MLP and a cubic-spline fragment-length distribution model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads already carry reliable spliced/unspliced labels (i.e. not from single-cell data with ambiguous counts) — Forseti is designed for scRNA-seq reads compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts Single-end reads or alignments without transcriptomic coordinates — Forseti scores putative fragments that associate each alignment with proximate priming sites, requiring toTranscriptome BAM output from STAR Long-read or non-10X data where oligo(dT) priming assumptions and the 10X whitelist (e.g. 3M-february-2018.txt) do not apply

skills.description: Use when a time-course or staged single-cell RNA-Seq dataset spans a known or suspected lineage bifurcation (e.g., retinal progenitors splitting into neuronal vs epithelial fates) and the exact transition/tipping stage must be resolved.
skills.name: scrna-seq-stage-wise-dice-dynamics
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-stage-wise-dice-dynamics Use when a time-course or staged single-cell RNA-Seq dataset spans a known or suspected lineage bifurcation (e.g., retinal progenitors splitting into neuronal vs epithelial fates) and the exact transition/tipping stage must be resolved. The goal is generic trajectory/pseudotime inference or cell clustering rather than localizing a bifurcation point between competing lineages — trajectory algorithms like Palantir serve that purpose and cannot resolve the transition timing. No candidate lineage-specific regulatory factors can be defined (no differential expression between terminal branches), so there is no TF covariation signal for DICE to quantify. The population is a single continuous lineage with no competing downstream fates, so no priming/bifurcation dynamic exists to detect. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes distance covariance entropy (DICE) over successive developmental stages or pseudotime bins of a scRNA-Seq time-course to pinpoint the timing of a lineage bifurcation. It outperforms variance-based and trajectory-inference approaches because it tracks covariation entropy of lineage-specific regulatory factors rather than individual gene variance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Computes distance covariance entropy (DICE) over successive developmental stages or pseudotime bins of a scRNA-Seq time-course to pinpoint the timing of a lineage bifurcation. It outperforms variance-based and trajectory-inference approaches because it tracks covariation entropy of lineage-specific regulatory factors rather than individual gene variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is generic trajectory/pseudotime inference or cell clustering rather than localizing a bifurcation point between competing lineages — trajectory algorithms like Palantir serve that purpose and cannot resolve the transition timing. No candidate lineage-specific regulatory factors can be defined (no differential expression between terminal branches), so there is no TF covariation signal for DICE to quantify. The population is a single continuous lineage with no competing downstream fates, so no priming/bifurcation dynamic exists to detect.

skills.description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix must be ranked by pluripotency/stemness to identify stem or progenitor cells, e.g. to pick trajectory-inference origins or to check whether a potency method recovers a known cellular hierarchy (HSC > MPP > GMP, stem vs TA).
skills.name: scrna-seq-stemness-scoring
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-stemness-scoring Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix must be ranked by pluripotency/stemness to identify stem or progenitor cells, e.g. to pick trajectory-inference origins or to check whether a potency method recovers a known cellular hierarchy (HSC > MPP > GMP, stem vs TA). When the goal is PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — use the extended ORIGINS2 package (build_ppin with full_human_ppin) or PyOrigins instead, since base ORIGINS ships only the differentiation PPIN. When only a pre-computed feature table or per-cell annotation is available with no gene-by-cell expression matrix — activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges) requires the expression matrix itself. When the biological question is whether a stemness method correctly recovers the classical hierarchy (e.g. HSC-first ordering): the paper's findings show all methods failed this on the colon and hematopoietic benchmarks (TA cells and GMP scored highest), so results should not be assumed to equal true stem-cell identity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores from scRNA-seq count matrices using the ORIGINS differentiation-activity function (activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges)) and benchmark them against LandSCENT and CytoTRACE, as done in the Senra et al. 2022 MethodsX workflow on breast (GSE113197), colon (GSE125970), hematopoietic (GSE117498) and lung (GSE161383) datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Compute per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores from scRNA-seq count matrices using the ORIGINS differentiation-activity function (activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges)) and benchmark them against LandSCENT and CytoTRACE, as done in the Senra et al. 2022 MethodsX workflow on breast (GSE113197), colon (GSE125970), hematopoietic (GSE117498) and lung (GSE161383) datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is PPIN activity for a biological process other than differentiation — use the extended ORIGINS2 package (build_ppin with full_human_ppin) or PyOrigins instead, since base ORIGINS ships only the differentiation PPIN. When only a pre-computed feature table or per-cell annotation is available with no gene-by-cell expression matrix — activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges) requires the expression matrix itself. When the biological question is whether a stemness method correctly recovers the classical hierarchy (e.g. HSC-first ordering): the paper's findings show all methods failed this on the colon and hematopoietic benchmarks (TA cells and GMP scored highest), so results should not be assumed to equal true stem-cell identity.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type identification methods on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a fair, repeated train/test comparison of accuracy across datasets is needed.
skills.name: scrna-seq-stratified-cross-validation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-stratified-cross-validation Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type identification methods on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a fair, repeated train/test comparison of accuracy across datasets is needed. The task is de novo cell-type discovery or clustering rather than evaluating supervised classifiers against pre-annotated labels Input is a single dataset without ground-truth cell-type labels, so stratified train/test splits against reference labels are impossible You need to evaluate false-positive control on cell types absent from the reference (the null-dataset confidence-score workflow), which this within-reference CV setup does not address http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A repeated stratified hold-out (70/30) cross-validation benchmark for comparing supervised single-cell RNA-seq cell-type classifiers (SciBet, scmap, Seurat v3) across 14 datasets, using E-test feature selection (top 500 ΔS genes) and accuracy/balanced-accuracy as the metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: A repeated stratified hold-out (70/30) cross-validation benchmark for comparing supervised single-cell RNA-seq cell-type classifiers (SciBet, scmap, Seurat v3) across 14 datasets, using E-test feature selection (top 500 ΔS genes) and accuracy/balanced-accuracy as the metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is de novo cell-type discovery or clustering rather than evaluating supervised classifiers against pre-annotated labels Input is a single dataset without ground-truth cell-type labels, so stratified train/test splits against reference labels are impossible You need to evaluate false-positive control on cell types absent from the reference (the null-dataset confidence-score workflow), which this within-reference CV setup does not address

skills.name: scrna-seq-study-data-preparation
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-study-data-preparation Use when importing new scRNA-seq (RNA-, ATAC-, or CITE-seq) studies into Cellenium, i.e. when raw/normalized single-cell data must be converted to annotated H5AD files with semantically organized study metadata. skills.name: scrna-seq-subclone-clustering-tsne-visualization
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-subclone-clustering-tsne-visualization Use when deposited scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., drug-sensitive vs. resistant HMCL pairs like U266P vs U266VR) must be clustered into subclones and screened for drug-target gene enrichment to prioritize combination therapies. The goal is in silico secDrug prediction from pharmacogenomics data via the greedy set cover algorithm, not single-cell target-gene enrichment screening. The input is bulk RNA-seq or CyTOF proteomics data rather than single-cell transcriptomic count matrices requiring clustering and t-SNE embedding. The candidate drug combination's target genes are not known or mappable onto the scRNA-seq feature space, so enrichment cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that preprocesses and clusters myeloma cell-line scRNA-seq count matrices with Seurat, embeds subclones via t-SNE, and maps LINCS-derived drug-target genes (HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 for 17-AAG, NAMPT for FK866) onto subclonal clusters to rank secDrug combination candidates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41408-022-00636-2
skills.summary: A single-cell RNA-seq screening skill that preprocesses and clusters myeloma cell-line scRNA-seq count matrices with Seurat, embeds subclones via t-SNE, and maps LINCS-derived drug-target genes (HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 for 17-AAG, NAMPT for FK866) onto subclonal clusters to rank secDrug combination candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is in silico secDrug prediction from pharmacogenomics data via the greedy set cover algorithm, not single-cell target-gene enrichment screening. The input is bulk RNA-seq or CyTOF proteomics data rather than single-cell transcriptomic count matrices requiring clustering and t-SNE embedding. The candidate drug combination's target genes are not known or mappable onto the scRNA-seq feature space, so enrichment cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the wall-clock runtime of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, scImpute, SAVER) as a function of cell count, requiring random subsets of a large filtered expression matrix.
skills.name: scrna-seq-subset-sampling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-subset-sampling Use when benchmarking the wall-clock runtime of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, scImpute, SAVER) as a function of cell count, requiring random subsets of a large filtered expression matrix. The goal is imputation accuracy rather than runtime scaling — subsets would confound accuracy comparisons that should use the full annotated dataset The input matrix is already small (e.g., under ~10,000 cells), where subsetting adds no meaningful runtime-scaling information Genes have not yet been filtered (mean expression >= 0.00003 and non-zero in >= 4 cells checks not applied), so runtime reflects unfiltered noise genes http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Sampling random cell subsets (e.g., 5,000–50,000 cells) from a large filtered scRNA-seq expression matrix, such as the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex dataset, to benchmark how imputation method runtime scales with cell count. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Sampling random cell subsets (e.g., 5,000–50,000 cells) from a large filtered scRNA-seq expression matrix, such as the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex dataset, to benchmark how imputation method runtime scales with cell count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is imputation accuracy rather than runtime scaling — subsets would confound accuracy comparisons that should use the full annotated dataset The input matrix is already small (e.g., under ~10,000 cells), where subsetting adds no meaningful runtime-scaling information Genes have not yet been filtered (mean expression >= 0.00003 and non-zero in >= 4 cells checks not applied), so runtime reflects unfiltered noise genes

skills.description: Use when you have metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq rpeLabeling.h5ad with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices plus a labeling-time vector) and need paired time-point inputs for RNAForecaster.
skills.name: scrna-seq-temporal-data-handling
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-temporal-data-handling Use when you have metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq rpeLabeling.h5ad with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices plus a labeling-time vector) and need paired time-point inputs for RNAForecaster. Input is standard scRNA-seq without paired time-point measurements of the same cell, since 'This sort of data is not available when using standard scRNA-seq protocols' Data lacks separate labeled/unlabeled count matrices or a defined labeling time, so degradation cannot be estimated in real time The goal is ordering cells along a trajectory rather than forecasting future expression states with a neural ODE http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts metabolic labeling scRNA-seq counts (e.g., scEU-seq labeled/unlabeled/total matrices) into paired time-point expression matrices suitable for training RNAForecaster neural ODEs, by reconstructing a t=0 expression estimate that includes degraded transcripts using per-gene degradation rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100793
skills.summary: Converts metabolic labeling scRNA-seq counts (e.g., scEU-seq labeled/unlabeled/total matrices) into paired time-point expression matrices suitable for training RNAForecaster neural ODEs, by reconstructing a t=0 expression estimate that includes degraded transcripts using per-gene degradation rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is standard scRNA-seq without paired time-point measurements of the same cell, since 'This sort of data is not available when using standard scRNA-seq protocols' Data lacks separate labeled/unlabeled count matrices or a defined labeling time, so degradation cannot be estimated in real time The goal is ordering cells along a trajectory rather than forecasting future expression states with a neural ODE

skills.description: Use when scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform quantification from scRNA-seq must be validated against bulk 3'-seq reference TPMs (e.g., ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391 HSC or PolyASite-annotated ESC bulk data) to establish concordance.
skills.name: scrna-seq-to-bulk-3prime-seq-concordance
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-to-bulk-3prime-seq-concordance Use when scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform quantification from scRNA-seq must be validated against bulk 3'-seq reference TPMs (e.g., ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391 HSC or PolyASite-annotated ESC bulk data) to establish concordance. Input is already a bulk 3'-seq or bulk RNA-seq abundance table with no single-cell UMI matrix to pseudobulk The scRNA-seq library is not 3'-end tag-based (e.g., full-length protocols), since scUTRquant targets 3'-end tag data like 10x Genomics and Microwell-seq The goal is de novo cleavage-site mapping rather than validating pre-defined UTRome isoform quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Validation skill that benchmarks scUTRquant-derived 3'UTR isoform counts from single-cell RNA-seq against bulk 3' end sequencing (the gold standard) by computing Spearman correlations of per-sample TPMs in matched cell types such as FACS-sorted HSCs and ESCs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Validation skill that benchmarks scUTRquant-derived 3'UTR isoform counts from single-cell RNA-seq against bulk 3' end sequencing (the gold standard) by computing Spearman correlations of per-sample TPMs in matched cell types such as FACS-sorted HSCs and ESCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a bulk 3'-seq or bulk RNA-seq abundance table with no single-cell UMI matrix to pseudobulk The scRNA-seq library is not 3'-end tag-based (e.g., full-length protocols), since scUTRquant targets 3'-end tag data like 10x Genomics and Microwell-seq The goal is de novo cleavage-site mapping rather than validating pre-defined UTRome isoform quantification

skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq (annotated source, h5ad with obs['CellType']) and scATAC-seq (unlabeled target) data to transfer cell-type labels, e.g. SNARE-seq or mouse-atlas benchmarks.
skills.name: scrna-seq-to-scatac-seq-label-transfer
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-to-scatac-seq-label-transfer Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq (annotated source, h5ad with obs['CellType']) and scATAC-seq (unlabeled target) data to transfer cell-type labels, e.g. SNARE-seq or mouse-atlas benchmarks. Paired multi-omics data with per-cell pairing information — scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration using cross-omics pairing instead Data with expected novel cell types not present in the scRNA-seq annotations — use scBridge's --novel_type mode with structure preservation loss rather than plain label transfer Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq matrices not converted to a gene activity matrix — first transform with a tool such as Signac http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transfer cell-type annotations from an annotated scRNA-seq source to an unlabeled scATAC-seq target using scBridge's heterogeneous transfer learning, which exploits cell heterogeneity by iteratively selecting reliable scATAC-seq cells via a Gaussian Mixture reliability model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41795-5
skills.summary: Transfer cell-type annotations from an annotated scRNA-seq source to an unlabeled scATAC-seq target using scBridge's heterogeneous transfer learning, which exploits cell heterogeneity by iteratively selecting reliable scATAC-seq cells via a Gaussian Mixture reliability model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Paired multi-omics data with per-cell pairing information — scAI or MOFA+ perform joint integration using cross-omics pairing instead Data with expected novel cell types not present in the scRNA-seq annotations — use scBridge's --novel_type mode with structure preservation loss rather than plain label transfer Peak-by-cell scATAC-seq matrices not converted to a gene activity matrix — first transform with a tool such as Signac

The dataset lacks original study cell annotations, so no 'consistent'/'inconsistent'/'unknown' labels or test-set ground truth can be defined The target cell types are tissue-specific (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) outside scWizard's TME reference of 7 major types and 47 subtypes Only the scWizard built-in reference (113,976 cells across 13 cancer types) is needed for inference without any benchmarking or retraining http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepare labeled cancer scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., T/NK_BRCA, T/NK_KIRC, Mye_PAAD, LYM from Table S1) by splitting each into training and testing sets so that cell-annotation models such as scWizard's hierarchical deep neural network and the ACTINN/SingleR/SingleCellNet/SCSA/CellAssign baselines can be trained and evaluated on identical data partitions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks original study cell annotations, so no 'consistent'/'inconsistent'/'unknown' labels or test-set ground truth can be defined The target cell types are tissue-specific (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) outside scWizard's TME reference of 7 major types and 47 subtypes Only the scWizard built-in reference (113,976 cells across 13 cancer types) is needed for inference without any benchmarking or retraining

skills.description: Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal epithelial training set from labeled scRNA-seq datasets where the raw 'Malignant'/'Tumor' annotations may be noisy and need refinement via cancer signature activity.
skills.name: scrna-seq-training-dataset-construction
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-training-dataset-construction Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal epithelial training set from labeled scRNA-seq datasets where the raw 'Malignant'/'Tumor' annotations may be noisy and need refinement via cancer signature activity. Your goal is malignant-cell prediction on new data, not training-set curation — use the pretrained model.joblib predict step instead of rebuilding the training set. The dataset lacks reliable basic cell-type/epithelial annotations, since the baseline is defined on 'Normal'-annotated epithelial cells and the tool relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types. The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the curated signatures' transcriptional patterns have not been validated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a signature-calibrated scRNA-seq training set for malignant-cell classifiers by scoring nine curated pan-cancer gene signatures (AUCell) on originally annotated malignant cells and removing cells inconsistent with normal-epithelial baseline signature activity. In scMalignantFinder this yielded a calibrated set of 416,774 cells (134,053 malignant, 282,721 normal epithelial). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Constructs a signature-calibrated scRNA-seq training set for malignant-cell classifiers by scoring nine curated pan-cancer gene signatures (AUCell) on originally annotated malignant cells and removing cells inconsistent with normal-epithelial baseline signature activity. In scMalignantFinder this yielded a calibrated set of 416,774 cells (134,053 malignant, 282,721 normal epithelial).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is malignant-cell prediction on new data, not training-set curation — use the pretrained model.joblib predict step instead of rebuilding the training set. The dataset lacks reliable basic cell-type/epithelial annotations, since the baseline is defined on 'Normal'-annotated epithelial cells and the tool relies on prerequisite identification of basic cell types. The cancer type has unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma or certain brain tumors), where the curated signatures' transcriptional patterns have not been validated.

skills.description: Use when a pre-trained source classifier's soft probability outputs exist for scRNA-seq target cells and you need a per-cell uncertainty score to detect which cells belong to known cell types versus novel types.
skills.name: scrna-seq-uncertainty-measurement
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-uncertainty-measurement Use when a pre-trained source classifier's soft probability outputs exist for scRNA-seq target cells and you need a per-cell uncertainty score to detect which cells belong to known cell types versus novel types. No pre-trained source model with a main classifier and two auxiliary classifiers is available — the E-score is defined only from those three probability outputs You already have confirmed cell-type labels for all target cells and only need final annotation, not uncertainty estimation or novel-type detection Downstream analysis requires distinguishing known from unknown cells without following through with bimodality testing and the manifold-mixup adaptive threshold, for which the E-score alone is only an intermediate signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes per-cell E-scores for scRNA-seq target data by combining three complementary uncertainty indices — entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) — derived from a pre-trained source model's main and auxiliary classifier probability vectors, as implemented in scEMAIL. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Computes per-cell E-scores for scRNA-seq target data by combining three complementary uncertainty indices — entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) — derived from a pre-trained source model's main and auxiliary classifier probability vectors, as implemented in scEMAIL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No pre-trained source model with a main classifier and two auxiliary classifiers is available — the E-score is defined only from those three probability outputs You already have confirmed cell-type labels for all target cells and only need final annotation, not uncertainty estimation or novel-type detection Downstream analysis requires distinguishing known from unknown cells without following through with bimodality testing and the manifold-mixup adaptive threshold, for which the E-score alone is only an intermediate signal

skills.description: Use when a UMI count matrix (cells x genes) needs low-dimensional embedding for visualization, batch correction across multiple batch factors (e.g., 30 patients x 3 health statuses x 2 locations), or mapping of held-out individuals.
skills.name: scrna-seq-variational-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-variational-autoencoder-training Use when a UMI count matrix (cells x genes) needs low-dimensional embedding for visualization, batch correction across multiple batch factors (e.g., 30 patients x 3 health statuses x 2 locations), or mapping of held-out individuals. The goal is imputing missing counts or removing ambient RNA contamination — the article states further studies are required to validate scPhere for these tasks The data are already embedded or reduced (e.g., a precomputed embedding or feature table) rather than raw UMI counts An efficient k-NN search in hyperbolic space is required as the primary deliverable — the article notes there are not yet many tools to process data distributed in the hyperbolic space, such as efficient k-NN search tools http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Train the scPhere variational autoencoder to embed scRNA-seq UMI count matrices into hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher) or hyperbolic (wrapped normal) latent spaces, handling multilevel batch vectors and optional batch-invariant mapping of new patients. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Train the scPhere variational autoencoder to embed scRNA-seq UMI count matrices into hyperspherical (von Mises–Fisher) or hyperbolic (wrapped normal) latent spaces, handling multilevel batch vectors and optional batch-invariant mapping of new patients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is imputing missing counts or removing ambient RNA contamination — the article states further studies are required to validate scPhere for these tasks The data are already embedded or reduced (e.g., a precomputed embedding or feature table) rather than raw UMI counts An efficient k-NN search in hyperbolic space is required as the primary deliverable — the article notes there are not yet many tools to process data distributed in the hyperbolic space, such as efficient k-NN search tools

skills.description: Use when a Yan (or similar scRNA-seq) expression matrix and SSRE-inferred cluster labels are available and the goal is validating that the clustering supports downstream DEG detection via Kruskal-Wallis testing.
skills.name: scrna-seq-yan-dataset-processing
skills.search_text: scrna-seq-yan-dataset-processing Use when a Yan (or similar scRNA-seq) expression matrix and SSRE-inferred cluster labels are available and the goal is validating that the clustering supports downstream DEG detection via Kruskal-Wallis testing. skills.description: Use when a scRNAseq expression matrix shows unwanted variation (e.g. ERCC spike-in confounding or cell-cycle effects) and downstream clustering must recover known biological groupings from corrected data.
skills.name: scrnaseq-confounding-factor-correction
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-confounding-factor-correction Use when a scRNAseq expression matrix shows unwanted variation (e.g. ERCC spike-in confounding or cell-cycle effects) and downstream clustering must recover known biological groupings from corrected data. You need to directly infer the biological factors themselves (u_i): scPLS can only infer the biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, because of model identifiability You require a count-based model of raw scRNAseq counts: extending the framework to modeling count data is left as future work in the paper Your downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction): the paper's evaluation of correction methods covers clustering only and notes performance in other settings was not evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infer and remove hidden confounding factors (technical or cell-cycle effects) from scRNAseq expression matrices using scPLS, which jointly models a control gene set (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, implemented in the Citrus R/C++ toolkit with a block-wise EM algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Infer and remove hidden confounding factors (technical or cell-cycle effects) from scRNAseq expression matrices using scPLS, which jointly models a control gene set (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) and a target gene set via partial least squares regression, implemented in the Citrus R/C++ toolkit with a block-wise EM algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to directly infer the biological factors themselves (u_i): scPLS can only infer the biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, because of model identifiability You require a count-based model of raw scRNAseq counts: extending the framework to modeling count data is left as future work in the paper Your downstream analysis is not clustering (e.g. differential expression, lineage reconstruction): the paper's evaluation of correction methods covers clustering only and notes performance in other settings was not evaluated

skills.search_text: scrnaseq-count-matrix-simulation Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq gene-by-cell count matrix to validate penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) topic modeling, or to sanity-check topic-word probability estimation on data with known latent structure. The input is already an unstructured document corpus (plain-text bags of words) — the pLDA adaptation here is specific to scRNA-seq counts with genes as words and cells as documents The goal is clustering cells by existing annotations rather than estimating latent topics — pLDA's topics are meant to be interpretable with biological functions, not predefined labels You cannot build the package vignettes (build_vignettes=TRUE fails), since the simulation example is only accessible via browseVignettes('pLDA') http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduce the pLDA package's simulation example, which generates a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix where genes are words, cells are documents, and latent topics represent biological functions, then fit the penalized LDA model to it. This provides a controlled testbed for validating topic-word and cell-topic estimation before applying pLDA to real scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-021-09304-8
skills.summary: Reproduce the pLDA package's simulation example, which generates a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix where genes are words, cells are documents, and latent topics represent biological functions, then fit the penalized LDA model to it. This provides a controlled testbed for validating topic-word and cell-topic estimation before applying pLDA to real scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an unstructured document corpus (plain-text bags of words) — the pLDA adaptation here is specific to scRNA-seq counts with genes as words and cells as documents The goal is clustering cells by existing annotations rather than estimating latent topics — pLDA's topics are meant to be interpretable with biological functions, not predefined labels You cannot build the package vignettes (build_vignettes=TRUE fails), since the simulation example is only accessible via browseVignettes('pLDA')

skills.description: Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq benchmark dataset with known cell-type labels and controllable cluster sizes (e.g., a rare population <5% of cells) to evaluate clustering accuracy and robustness.
skills.name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-simulation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-count-matrix-simulation Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq benchmark dataset with known cell-type labels and controllable cluster sizes (e.g., a rare population <5% of cells) to evaluate clustering accuracy and robustness. The goal is to benchmark on real experimental data where biological variability, not controllable cluster sizes, is the test condition. The input is already a labeled synthetic count matrix — re-simulation adds no information and risks duplicating the benchmark. The analysis requires unnormalized continuous expression values rather than integer count matrices, since scDesign2 simulates raw counts. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth cell-type labels by fitting the scDesign2 generative model to a real reference dataset, enabling controlled benchmarking of clustering methods such as scAce. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad546
skills.summary: Generate synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth cell-type labels by fitting the scDesign2 generative model to a real reference dataset, enabling controlled benchmarking of clustering methods such as scAce.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark on real experimental data where biological variability, not controllable cluster sizes, is the test condition. The input is already a labeled synthetic count matrix — re-simulation adds no information and risks duplicating the benchmark. The analysis requires unnormalized continuous expression values rather than integer count matrices, since scDesign2 simulates raw counts.

skills.description: Use when an evaluation needs synthetic scRNA-Seq count data with known ground-truth cell-cluster labels — e.g. benchmarking clustering or transfer-learning pipelines where ARI can only be computed if true labels exist.
skills.name: scrnaseq-count-simulation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-count-simulation Use when an evaluation needs synthetic scRNA-Seq count data with known ground-truth cell-cluster labels — e.g. benchmarking clustering or transfer-learning pipelines where ARI can only be computed if true labels exist. Real scRNA-Seq datasets (e.g. Hockley, Usoskin, Tasic GEO data) are the analysis input — simulation parameters are for synthetic benchmarks, not for modifying real counts You need to transfer knowledge into an existing target dataset (NMF dictionary transfer, W'trg binarization, theta mixing) rather than generate synthetic data from scratch Running on Windows — the scRNA command-line scripts are available for MacOS and Linux only http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Generates synthetic scRNA-Seq count-level datasets with known ground-truth cluster labels using the scRNA package (cmd_generate_data.py / scRNA-generate-data.sh), producing hierarchical cluster structure (e.g. 8 sub-clusters from 5 top-level clusters) over ~10,000 genes in ~1800 cells for benchmarking clustering and transfer-learning methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: Generates synthetic scRNA-Seq count-level datasets with known ground-truth cluster labels using the scRNA package (cmd_generate_data.py / scRNA-generate-data.sh), producing hierarchical cluster structure (e.g. 8 sub-clusters from 5 top-level clusters) over ~10,000 genes in ~1800 cells for benchmarking clustering and transfer-learning methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scRNA-Seq datasets (e.g. Hockley, Usoskin, Tasic GEO data) are the analysis input — simulation parameters are for synthetic benchmarks, not for modifying real counts You need to transfer knowledge into an existing target dataset (NMF dictionary transfer, W'trg binarization, theta mixing) rather than generate synthetic data from scratch Running on Windows — the scRNA command-line scripts are available for MacOS and Linux only

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a cell-cycle or latent-factor removal method on scRNA-Seq data where ground-truth effect assignments (which PCs are cell-cycle, which genes are cell-type) must be known exactly.
skills.name: scrnaseq-count-simulation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-count-simulation Use when benchmarking a cell-cycle or latent-factor removal method on scRNA-Seq data where ground-truth effect assignments (which PCs are cell-cycle, which genes are cell-type) must be known exactly. The goal is to remove a cell-cycle effect from a real scRNA-Seq dataset (e.g. T helper, mESC, glioblastoma data) rather than to benchmark a removal method against known ground truth The confounder of interest is not cell-cycle and cell-type structure (e.g. batch or technical replicates), since the planted effect model covers only these two components Cell-cycle activity is very low in the target setting (e.g. glioblastoma, where the paper uses a smaller cutoff C_delta = 2), so the default simulation and cutoff=3 parameters would not reflect the analysis conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates a synthetic scRNA-Seq matrix X with a planted cell-cycle effect on annotated genes and a separate cell-type effect (50 cells x 2,000 genes, 400 cell-cycle genes, six cell-type-by-cell-cycle-stage groups), enabling controlled benchmarking of correction methods such as ccRemover and scLVM against known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic scRNA-Seq matrix X with a planted cell-cycle effect on annotated genes and a separate cell-type effect (50 cells x 2,000 genes, 400 cell-cycle genes, six cell-type-by-cell-cycle-stage groups), enabling controlled benchmarking of correction methods such as ccRemover and scLVM against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to remove a cell-cycle effect from a real scRNA-Seq dataset (e.g. T helper, mESC, glioblastoma data) rather than to benchmark a removal method against known ground truth The confounder of interest is not cell-cycle and cell-type structure (e.g. batch or technical replicates), since the planted effect model covers only these two components Cell-cycle activity is very low in the target setting (e.g. glioblastoma, where the paper uses a smaller cutoff C_delta = 2), so the default simulation and cutoff=3 parameters would not reflect the analysis conditions

skills.description: Use when several labeled scRNA-seq studies of the same tissue exist and you need to quantify how annotation accuracy transfers between studies/platforms (inter-study annotation) across competing classifiers.
skills.name: scrnaseq-cross-platform-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-cross-platform-benchmark-evaluation Use when several labeled scRNA-seq studies of the same tissue exist and you need to quantify how annotation accuracy transfers between studies/platforms (inter-study annotation) across competing classifiers. Cell types in the test sample may be novel or not present in the reference data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest, so only unsupervised clustering is viable The test data still contains unknown/rare or malignant cells that need prior identification (e.g., inferCNV/copyKAT) rather than exhaustive label assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A benchmarking protocol for comparing supervised scRNA-seq cell annotation methods (NeuCA, scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) across datasets from different studies/platforms, using one dataset as training reference and the others as independent tests with published labels as ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol for comparing supervised scRNA-seq cell annotation methods (NeuCA, scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) across datasets from different studies/platforms, using one dataset as training reference and the others as independent tests with published labels as ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types in the test sample may be novel or not present in the reference data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the training data No labeled training data exist for the tissue of interest, so only unsupervised clustering is viable The test data still contains unknown/rare or malignant cells that need prior identification (e.g., inferCNV/copyKAT) rather than exhaustive label assignment

skills.name: scrnaseq-data-formatting
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-data-formatting Use when raw scRNA-seq data (e.g. GEO accession GSE116753 or similar) must be reshaped into MDIC3's exp.txt/metadata.txt input format before GRN inference with GNIPLR and communication scoring. Data is already in MDIC3's exp.txt/metadata.txt format and validated — no reformatting needed Analysis targets cell-cell communication methods with other input requirements (e.g. CellChat expects R objects/CellChatDB, not exp.txt) The expression file lacks cell-type labels in metadata, since MDIC3 requires existing cell classification labels to run http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Formats scRNA-seq expression matrices and cell-type metadata into the exact *.txt layouts MDIC3 requires (rows = genes, columns = cells; cells in metadata matching the expression header), so cell-cell communication inference can run downstream. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Formats scRNA-seq expression matrices and cell-type metadata into the exact *.txt layouts MDIC3 requires (rows = genes, columns = cells; cells in metadata matching the expression header), so cell-cell communication inference can run downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is already in MDIC3's exp.txt/metadata.txt format and validated — no reformatting needed Analysis targets cell-cell communication methods with other input requirements (e.g. CellChat expects R objects/CellChatDB, not exp.txt) The expression file lacks cell-type labels in metadata, since MDIC3 requires existing cell classification labels to run

The analysis goal is single-time-point cell–cell communication without developmental series information — other methods (CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR) may suffice Input data lacks cell-type labels or time-point information needed by dsCellNet's three-file input interface http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prepare scRNA-seq input files (expression matrix, cell-type labels, and time-point information) in the three-file layout required by dsCellNet's datainput interface so developmental-series cell–cell interaction networks can be inferred. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Prepare scRNA-seq input files (expression matrix, cell-type labels, and time-point information) in the three-file layout required by dsCellNet's datainput interface so developmental-series cell–cell interaction networks can be inferred.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is single-time-point cell–cell communication without developmental series information — other methods (CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR) may suffice Input data lacks cell-type labels or time-point information needed by dsCellNet's three-file input interface

skills.description: Use when several scRNA-seq datasets with expression matrices, dataset-of-origin labels, and cell-type labels must be combined to test whether cell types (e.g. neurons vs non-neuronal cells) replicate across studies via AUROC.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dataset-harmonization
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dataset-harmonization Use when several scRNA-seq datasets with expression matrices, dataset-of-origin labels, and cell-type labels must be combined to test whether cell types (e.g. neurons vs non-neuronal cells) replicate across studies via AUROC. Cell-type labels are ambiguous or uninformative across datasets — the supervised MetaNeighbor requires known corresponding types; use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes HVGs instead You only have a single dataset and no cross-dataset replication question — neighbor voting with leave-one-dataset-out folds is meaningless without at least two studies Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix — the method will fail; harmonize identifiers first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Harmonizes multiple scRNA-seq datasets into a single SummarizedExperiment object with study_id and cell_type metadata so that MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting framework can quantify cross-dataset cell-type replicability via mean AUROC scores over leave-one-dataset-out folds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Harmonizes multiple scRNA-seq datasets into a single SummarizedExperiment object with study_id and cell_type metadata so that MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting framework can quantify cross-dataset cell-type replicability via mean AUROC scores over leave-one-dataset-out folds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are ambiguous or uninformative across datasets — the supervised MetaNeighbor requires known corresponding types; use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS with variableGenes HVGs instead You only have a single dataset and no cross-dataset replication question — neighbor voting with leave-one-dataset-out folds is meaningless without at least two studies Gene sets contain fewer than two genes or gene names do not match the expression matrix — the method will fail; harmonize identifiers first

skills.description: Use when a benchmark or method comparison requires raw scRNA-seq count matrices with ground-truth cell labels and the paper lists source repositories (GEO/SCP accession numbers, e.g. Table 1 of the scDHA article) to fetch them.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dataset-retrieval-geo-scp
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dataset-retrieval-geo-scp Use when a benchmark or method comparison requires raw scRNA-seq count matrices with ground-truth cell labels and the paper lists source repositories (GEO/SCP accession numbers, e.g. Table 1 of the scDHA article) to fetch them. The task is clustering a single user-provided dataset that is already locally available — no retrieval step is needed. The analysis needs datasets without published cell-type labels, since ARI benchmarking against known labels is impossible. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieve scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with known cell-type labels from GEO/SCP using accession numbers, as required to reproduce the 34-dataset clustering benchmark (ARI comparison) from the scDHA paper (Nature Communications, 2021). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Retrieve scRNA-seq benchmark datasets with known cell-type labels from GEO/SCP using accession numbers, as required to reproduce the 34-dataset clustering benchmark (ARI comparison) from the scDHA paper (Nature Communications, 2021).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is clustering a single user-provided dataset that is already locally available — no retrieval step is needed. The analysis needs datasets without published cell-type labels, since ARI benchmarking against known labels is impossible.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking PAS/scoring tools on million-cell-level scRNA-seq data where full-dataset computation is impractical, and a fixed-size random cell subset (e.g., 100k cells from the >1.2M-cell lupus atlas) suffices for validation.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting Use when benchmarking PAS/scoring tools on million-cell-level scRNA-seq data where full-dataset computation is impractical, and a fixed-size random cell subset (e.g., 100k cells from the >1.2M-cell lupus atlas) suffices for validation. The downstream goal is full-scale multicellular pathway module discovery with MOFA — that requires all samples/cells and studies with at least 15 samples, not a 100k-cell benchmark subset The dataset is already small enough that direct full-data tool comparison or scoring is computationally feasible The analysis depends on precise population composition where a random subsample could distort rare-cell-type representation (ranking-based fast_ucell PAS is composition-insensitive, but cell-type proportions are not) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Draws fixed-size cell subsets (e.g., 100,000 cells) from million-cell-scale scRNA-seq atlases such as the >1.2M-cell lupus PBMC atlas and CRC tumor datasets, so that method-comparison benchmarks like the fast_ucell-vs-AUCell PAS cosine-similarity validation can run in tractable time. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Draws fixed-size cell subsets (e.g., 100,000 cells) from million-cell-scale scRNA-seq atlases such as the >1.2M-cell lupus PBMC atlas and CRC tumor datasets, so that method-comparison benchmarks like the fast_ucell-vs-AUCell PAS cosine-similarity validation can run in tractable time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream goal is full-scale multicellular pathway module discovery with MOFA — that requires all samples/cells and studies with at least 15 samples, not a 100k-cell benchmark subset The dataset is already small enough that direct full-data tool comparison or scoring is computationally feasible The analysis depends on precise population composition where a random subsample could distort rare-cell-type representation (ranking-based fast_ucell PAS is composition-insensitive, but cell-type proportions are not)

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. a whole-tumor immune atlas) must be narrowed to a biologically relevant population (immune cells) and a fixed number of cells (e.g. 5000) before per-cell scoring.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting-and-downsampling
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting-and-downsampling Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. a whole-tumor immune atlas) must be narrowed to a biologically relevant population (immune cells) and a fixed number of cells (e.g. 5000) before per-cell scoring. The dataset is already a cell x gene score/feature table or small enough that subsetting would discard informative heterogeneity The analysis requires scores on the full population, since per-cell UCell scores are robust to dataset composition and do not require downsampling for correctness The input lacks cell-type annotations, making a biologically meaningful (e.g. immune-cell) subset impossible to define http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prepare a scRNA-seq object for signature scoring by loading the Zilionis et al. (2019) NSCLC immune-cell dataset via the scRNAseq package, subsetting it to immune cells, and downsampling to 5000 cells so that downstream UCell scoring is tractable and results are reproducible. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: Prepare a scRNA-seq object for signature scoring by loading the Zilionis et al. (2019) NSCLC immune-cell dataset via the scRNAseq package, subsetting it to immune cells, and downsampling to 5000 cells so that downstream UCell scoring is tractable and results are reproducible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already a cell x gene score/feature table or small enough that subsetting would discard informative heterogeneity The analysis requires scores on the full population, since per-cell UCell scores are robust to dataset composition and do not require downsampling for correctness The input lacks cell-type annotations, making a biologically meaningful (e.g. immune-cell) subset impossible to define

skills.description: Use when processing droplet-based scRNA-seq data (Seurat/SingleCellExperiment objects) that lacks experimental doublet labels (no cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet), and doublets must be called computationally per sample before downstream clustering or trajectory analyses.
skills.name: scrnaseq-doublet-detection-ensemble-analysis
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-doublet-detection-ensemble-analysis Use when processing droplet-based scRNA-seq data (Seurat/SingleCellExperiment objects) that lacks experimental doublet labels (no cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet), and doublets must be called computationally per sample before downstream clustering or trajectory analyses. When experimental doublet labels are available (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) — these directly label doublets and Chord's computational inference is unnecessary When runtime is critical — Chord must integrate results of multiple methods, so it is 'not optimal in terms of time efficiency' When the input is not a droplet-based scRNA-seq dataset with co-encapsulated-cell artefacts — doublet removal addresses a droplet-microfluidics-specific problem http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect and remove doublets in droplet scRNA-seq data using Chord, an ensemble machine learning method that integrates multiple doublet detection tools (scds, DoubletFinder) via GBM/AdaBoost, with an 'overkill' step that removes consensus doublets before simulating a training set. Validated on NSCLC tumour samples where it estimated per-sample doublet rates of 3.81–4.74%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Detect and remove doublets in droplet scRNA-seq data using Chord, an ensemble machine learning method that integrates multiple doublet detection tools (scds, DoubletFinder) via GBM/AdaBoost, with an 'overkill' step that removes consensus doublets before simulating a training set. Validated on NSCLC tumour samples where it estimated per-sample doublet rates of 3.81–4.74%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When experimental doublet labels are available (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) — these directly label doublets and Chord's computational inference is unnecessary When runtime is critical — Chord must integrate results of multiple methods, so it is 'not optimal in terms of time efficiency' When the input is not a droplet-based scRNA-seq dataset with co-encapsulated-cell artefacts — doublet removal addresses a droplet-microfluidics-specific problem

skills.description: Use when benchmarking gene-imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices (h5 format) under controlled synthetic dropout, e.g. to verify a method recovers masked non-zero entries better than baselines.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dropout-masking
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dropout-masking Use when benchmarking gene-imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices (h5 format) under controlled synthetic dropout, e.g. to verify a method recovers masked non-zero entries better than baselines. Data is bulk RNA-seq or single-cell data without excessive dropouts, where masking zero-valued (biological) entries would create artificial non-zero targets the methods are not designed to impute Goal is downstream clustering or cell-type labeling rather than quantitative imputation benchmarking (scGCL supports a separate 'task' argument for node/clustering/similarity) Raw counts have not passed quality-control filtering (>1% non-zero expression for genes and cells) and size-factor log normalization plus top-2048 HVG selection via scanpy, so masking would be applied to an unprocessed matrix inconsistent with the published protocol http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Simulates scRNA-seq dropout by randomly masking non-zero expression entries at 10%, 30% and 50% rates (scVI-style strategy), retaining true values as ground truth so that imputation methods like scGCL, AutoClass, GraphSCI and MAGIC can be quantitatively compared on masked-entry recovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Simulates scRNA-seq dropout by randomly masking non-zero expression entries at 10%, 30% and 50% rates (scVI-style strategy), retaining true values as ground truth so that imputation methods like scGCL, AutoClass, GraphSCI and MAGIC can be quantitatively compared on masked-entry recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is bulk RNA-seq or single-cell data without excessive dropouts, where masking zero-valued (biological) entries would create artificial non-zero targets the methods are not designed to impute Goal is downstream clustering or cell-type labeling rather than quantitative imputation benchmarking (scGCL supports a separate 'task' argument for node/clustering/similarity) Raw counts have not passed quality-control filtering (>1% non-zero expression for genes and cells) and size-factor log normalization plus top-2048 HVG selection via scanpy, so masking would be applied to an unprocessed matrix inconsistent with the published protocol

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an scRNA-seq imputation method on controlled dropout recovery — i.e., you have complete pre-processed count matrices and need to quantify NMSE/RMSE/MAE recovery at artificially masked non-zero values.
skills.name: scrnaseq-dropout-masking-simulation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-dropout-masking-simulation Use when benchmarking an scRNA-seq imputation method on controlled dropout recovery — i.e., you have complete pre-processed count matrices and need to quantify NMSE/RMSE/MAE recovery at artificially masked non-zero values. When the goal is biological downstream analysis (clustering, cell-type separability) rather than controlled reconstruction-error benchmarking When comparing against drImpute with error metrics — its gene-filtering preprocessing changes matrix dimensions, making RMSE/MAE/NMSE at masked locations incomparable When input matrices are not pre-processed/log-transformed or lack a complete reference matrix to score masked entries against http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A masked-matrix recovery benchmark for scRNA-seq imputation: artificially mute 10–50% of non-zero expression values in pre-processed log-transformed count matrices, impute with AutoImpute and baselines (MAGIC, scImpute), and score recovery with NMSE, RMSE, and MAE at the masked locations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: A masked-matrix recovery benchmark for scRNA-seq imputation: artificially mute 10–50% of non-zero expression values in pre-processed log-transformed count matrices, impute with AutoImpute and baselines (MAGIC, scImpute), and score recovery with NMSE, RMSE, and MAE at the masked locations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is biological downstream analysis (clustering, cell-type separability) rather than controlled reconstruction-error benchmarking When comparing against drImpute with error metrics — its gene-filtering preprocessing changes matrix dimensions, making RMSE/MAE/NMSE at masked locations incomparable When input matrices are not pre-processed/log-transformed or lack a complete reference matrix to score masked entries against

skills.description: Use when fitting trajectories (e.g., Slingshot, Monocle3) on scRNA-seq data and you must decide among candidate embeddings from feature selection (number of highly variable genes) and dimension reduction choices, or need to know if a trajectory is appropriate at all.
skills.name: scrnaseq-embedding-suitability-evaluation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-embedding-suitability-evaluation Use when fitting trajectories (e.g., Slingshot, Monocle3) on scRNA-seq data and you must decide among candidate embeddings from feature selection (number of highly variable genes) and dimension reduction choices, or need to know if a trajectory is appropriate at all. The trajectory inference method of interest does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations, so methods outside this restriction require further evaluation None of the evaluated embeddings is suitable — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices being evaluated You need RNA velocity-derived dimension reductions — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort (future work) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A data-driven skill for evaluating whether a scRNA-seq dataset and its candidate embeddings (feature selection, dimension reduction, hyperparameter choices) are suitable for trajectory inference, using the Escort framework's standardized benchmark score range from negative infinity to two where embeddings scoring >0 are recommended. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: A data-driven skill for evaluating whether a scRNA-seq dataset and its candidate embeddings (feature selection, dimension reduction, hyperparameter choices) are suitable for trajectory inference, using the Escort framework's standardized benchmark score range from negative infinity to two where embeddings scoring >0 are recommended.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory inference method of interest does not rely on a two-dimensional representation — Escort only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations, so methods outside this restriction require further evaluation None of the evaluated embeddings is suitable — Escort is not guaranteed to identify a recommended embedding among the choices being evaluated You need RNA velocity-derived dimension reductions — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort (future work)

skills.description: Use when implementing or validating an entropy-based cluster purity score for scRNA-seq clusters, i.e. computing single-gene sample entropy, LOESS-derived ds residuals, and aggregating them into ROGUE.
skills.name: scrnaseq-entropy-model-implementation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-entropy-model-implementation Use when implementing or validating an entropy-based cluster purity score for scRNA-seq clusters, i.e. computing single-gene sample entropy, LOESS-derived ds residuals, and aggregating them into ROGUE. Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not yet support this (proposed future work) Data are log2-transformed or otherwise not raw counts — the model assumes count-level expression for the Poisson-Gamma entropy computation Low-quality or continuous data where the default 0.9 purity threshold must instead be determined from global ROGUE values per the discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implementation of the S-E (expression entropy) model underlying the ROGUE statistic, converting per-gene entropy reduction (ds) into a quantitative cluster-purity score for scRNA-seq cell populations (ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K)). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Implementation of the S-E (expression entropy) model underlying the ROGUE statistic, converting per-gene entropy reduction (ds) into a quantitative cluster-purity score for scRNA-seq cell populations (ROGUE = 1 - sum(ds)/(sum(ds) + K)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assessing purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the article states current ROGUE does not yet support this (proposed future work) Data are log2-transformed or otherwise not raw counts — the model assumes count-level expression for the Poisson-Gamma entropy computation Low-quality or continuous data where the default 0.9 purity threshold must instead be determined from global ROGUE values per the discussion

skills.search_text: scrnaseq-expression-matrix-permutation Use when you must verify that a matrix-imputation pipeline (e.g., SERM) is invariant to the arrangement of cells and genes — i.e., row/column permutations of a scRNA-seq count matrix yield near-identical Pearson correlations to the reference. skills.description: Use when a scRNAseq counts table with cell-cluster assignments (e.g. setA, clusters 1-5) must be functionally annotated by reconstructing clusters in an encoded space derived from validated target/signature sets rather than gene expression alone.
skills.name: scrnaseq-latent-space-construction-from-target-sets
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-latent-space-construction-from-target-sets Use when a scRNAseq counts table with cell-cluster assignments (e.g. setA, clusters 1-5) must be functionally annotated by reconstructing clusters in an encoded space derived from validated target/signature sets rather than gene expression alone. The input is raw FASTQ or an unclustered counts table — clustering must be done first (e.g. via rCASC) before SCA can reconstruct defined subpopulations. The goal is generic dimensionality reduction or visualization of cells rather than testing which biological knowledge group functionally drives a specific cluster's aggregation. The dataset is miRNA+mRNA co-measurement — miRNAs cannot currently be quantified together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuits cannot be directly measured. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Build sparsely-connected autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) latent spaces for single-cell RNAseq from experimentally validated biological knowledge sets (TF targets, miRNA targets, kinase targets, cancer-related immune signatures), progressively combining groups so cluster-specific functional features drive cell aggregation, and score reconstruction quality with QCM/QCC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Build sparsely-connected autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) latent spaces for single-cell RNAseq from experimentally validated biological knowledge sets (TF targets, miRNA targets, kinase targets, cancer-related immune signatures), progressively combining groups so cluster-specific functional features drive cell aggregation, and score reconstruction quality with QCM/QCC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ or an unclustered counts table — clustering must be done first (e.g. via rCASC) before SCA can reconstruct defined subpopulations. skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq count matrices (UMI or read counts) across cells with varying sequencing depth, and a Tweedie/GLM-style model requires a library-size offset log(S) instead of pre-normalizing counts.
skills.name: scrnaseq-library-size-offset-normalization
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-library-size-offset-normalization Use when analyzing scRNA-seq count matrices (UMI or read counts) across cells with varying sequencing depth, and a Tweedie/GLM-style model requires a library-size offset log(S) instead of pre-normalizing counts. Input is already normalized or log-transformed expression data — adding a log(S) offset would double-correct for sequencing depth; the article's approach explicitly bypasses ad hoc normalization/transformation prior to DE testing. Data lack per-cell library size information (e.g., pre-aggregated pseudobulk or metacell matrices) and the log link model log(μ)=Xβ+log(S) cannot be specified. Zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes, a situation the authors state Tweedieverse is not architected for. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalizes single-cell RNA-seq expression data for sequencing depth by estimating cell-specific library sizes with the SCRAN R/Bioconductor package and incorporating them as an additive offset (log(S)) in per-gene Tweedie models (CPLM/ZICP), bypassing ad hoc normalization or transformation prior to differential expression testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1002/sim.9430
skills.summary: Normalizes single-cell RNA-seq expression data for sequencing depth by estimating cell-specific library sizes with the SCRAN R/Bioconductor package and incorporating them as an additive offset (log(S)) in per-gene Tweedie models (CPLM/ZICP), bypassing ad hoc normalization or transformation prior to differential expression testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized or log-transformed expression data — adding a log(S) offset would double-correct for sequencing depth; the article's approach explicitly bypasses ad hoc normalization/transformation prior to DE testing. Data lack per-cell library size information (e.g., pre-aggregated pseudobulk or metacell matrices) and the log link model log(μ)=Xβ+log(S) cannot be specified. Zero-inflation is a property specific only to a subset of genes, a situation the authors state Tweedieverse is not architected for.

skills.search_text: scrnaseq-normalized-expression-processing Use when constructing ligand-receptor communication edges from a normalised single-cell expression matrix and need an explicit, reproducible definition of gene 'expression' per cell type before edge extraction. Input is bulk transcriptomics or proteomic data where per-cell detection rates are not defined Heteromeric complex-mediated interactions are required, since NATMI does not model them Spatially resolved communication inference is the goal, as NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Applies NATMI's gene-expression filtering convention to single-cell data: a ligand/receptor counts as expressed in a cell type only if detected in more than 20% of that type's cells and its mean expression exceeds 10 counts-per-million (CPM), yielding a per-cell-type detection/expression table used to gate cell-to-cell communication edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Applies NATMI's gene-expression filtering convention to single-cell data: a ligand/receptor counts as expressed in a cell type only if detected in more than 20% of that type's cells and its mean expression exceeds 10 counts-per-million (CPM), yielding a per-cell-type detection/expression table used to gate cell-to-cell communication edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk transcriptomics or proteomic data where per-cell detection rates are not defined Heteromeric complex-mediated interactions are required, since NATMI does not model them Spatially resolved communication inference is the goal, as NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data

skills.description: Use when the input is a barcoded scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. GEO accession GSE99915) needing a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix plus cell-ID-to-barcode-ID lineage annotations before lineage inference or memory-gene analysis.
skills.name: scrnaseq-normalized-matrix-qc-processing
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-normalized-matrix-qc-processing Use when the input is a barcoded scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. GEO accession GSE99915) needing a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix plus cell-ID-to-barcode-ID lineage annotations before lineage inference or memory-gene analysis. The cells are only distantly related — GEMLI performs less robustly in populations containing only distant relatives, so the lineage-annotated matrix would not support reliable downstream inference The dataset already ships a QC'd, normalized expression matrix with matching barcode-based lineage annotations — reprocessing from BAM would duplicate the step The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months — expression-memory-based processing only resolves lineages over about 1–5 cell divisions http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Load and prepare a quality-controlled, normalized single-cell RNA-seq gene expression matrix together with cell-to-lineage annotations (e.g. barcode IDs), so that lineage-aware downstream analyses such as GEMLI memory-gene calling can be run. It converts raw CellRanger/CellTag outputs into the cell-by-gene matrix and annotation tables the analysis consumes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Load and prepare a quality-controlled, normalized single-cell RNA-seq gene expression matrix together with cell-to-lineage annotations (e.g. barcode IDs), so that lineage-aware downstream analyses such as GEMLI memory-gene calling can be run. It converts raw CellRanger/CellTag outputs into the cell-by-gene matrix and annotation tables the analysis consumes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cells are only distantly related — GEMLI performs less robustly in populations containing only distant relatives, so the lineage-annotated matrix would not support reliable downstream inference The dataset already ships a QC'd, normalized expression matrix with matching barcode-based lineage annotations — reprocessing from BAM would duplicate the step The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months — expression-memory-based processing only resolves lineages over about 1–5 cell divisions

skills.search_text: scrnaseq-preprocessing-quality-control Use when raw scRNA-seq count data must be filtered (min/max genes per cell, min cells per gene, mitochondrial percentage, HVG dispersion) before single-cell drug-response prediction with scDEAL. Input is already a QC-filtered or processed AnnData (.h5ad) object from a prior scDEAL run — re-filtering would drop cells/genes against the benchmark settings Data are bulk RNA-seq cell-line profiles (ALL_expression.csv / ALL_label_binary_wf.csv) used to train bulkmodel.py, which do not undergo per-cell scRNA-seq QC Highly variable gene selection must keep all genes (var_genes_disp = None) because the study selects all genes for that dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality-control and preprocessing of drug-treated scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. GSE117872, GSE112274, GSE140440, GSE149383, GSE110894) ahead of scDEAL transfer learning, using Scanpy-based gene/cell/mt-content filters and highly-variable-gene selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34277-7
skills.summary: Quality-control and preprocessing of drug-treated scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. GSE117872, GSE112274, GSE140440, GSE149383, GSE110894) ahead of scDEAL transfer learning, using Scanpy-based gene/cell/mt-content filters and highly-variable-gene selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a QC-filtered or processed AnnData (.h5ad) object from a prior scDEAL run — re-filtering would drop cells/genes against the benchmark settings Data are bulk RNA-seq cell-line profiles (ALL_expression.csv / ALL_label_binary_wf.csv) used to train bulkmodel.py, which do not undergo per-cell scRNA-seq QC Highly variable gene selection must keep all genes (var_genes_disp = None) because the study selects all genes for that dataset

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether denoising or imputation of scRNA-seq data preserves biological structure, by comparing principal component subspaces of original vs. perturbed/imputed matrices.
