skills.search_text: scrnaseq-principal-component-analysis Use when evaluating whether denoising or imputation of scRNA-seq data preserves biological structure, by comparing principal component subspaces of original vs. perturbed/imputed matrices. When the goal is imputation itself rather than evaluating signal preservation of an imputation method When input matrices are not cell-by-gene normalized expression matrices (e.g., already a reduced-dimension embedding or feature table) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute principal components of scRNA-seq expression matrices and quantify how well an imputation method (e.g., ALRA) preserves the biological signal, by measuring the subspace angle between the top-k signal PCs of original vs. downsampled data before and after imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Compute principal components of scRNA-seq expression matrices and quantify how well an imputation method (e.g., ALRA) preserves the biological signal, by measuring the subspace angle between the top-k signal PCs of original vs. downsampled data before and after imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is imputation itself rather than evaluating signal preservation of an imputation method When input matrices are not cell-by-gene normalized expression matrices (e.g., already a reduced-dimension embedding or feature table)

skills.description: Use when a sample-level trajectory (PILOT diffusion-map embedding + EIPLGraph pseudotime, e.g. from myocardial_infarction.h5ad) already exists and you must rank cell populations changing along progression and identify cluster-specific genes via Wald tests.
skills.name: scrnaseq-pseudotime-gene-expression-modeling
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-pseudotime-gene-expression-modeling Use when a sample-level trajectory (PILOT diffusion-map embedding + EIPLGraph pseudotime, e.g. from myocardial_infarction.h5ad) already exists and you must rank cell populations changing along progression and identify cluster-specific genes via Wald tests. You only need the patient-level distances or trajectory itself — use PILOT's wasserstein_distance/trajectory steps, not the regression/Wald-testing skill The input is a pathomics (histology structures) dataset without gene expression; genes_importance and gene_cluster_differentiation are not applicable to morphometric features Samples mix technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — PILOT assumes samples were collected uniformly, so trajectory-fitted changes may reflect batch rather than biology http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit step-wise Huber regression models (linear, quadratic, linear-quadratic) of cell-cluster proportions and gene expression along a PILOT-estimated disease-trajectory pseudotime, then use Wald statistics to find genes whose fitted curves differ in a target cluster versus all others. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Fit step-wise Huber regression models (linear, quadratic, linear-quadratic) of cell-cluster proportions and gene expression along a PILOT-estimated disease-trajectory pseudotime, then use Wald statistics to find genes whose fitted curves differ in a target cluster versus all others.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the patient-level distances or trajectory itself — use PILOT's wasserstein_distance/trajectory steps, not the regression/Wald-testing skill The input is a pathomics (histology structures) dataset without gene expression; genes_importance and gene_cluster_differentiation are not applicable to morphometric features Samples mix technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — PILOT assumes samples were collected uniformly, so trajectory-fitted changes may reflect batch rather than biology

skills.description: Use when a raw counts matrix or Seurat object (csv/rds/h5 or 10X folder) enters a scRNA-seq workflow and cells must be filtered for quality before annotation, clustering, or gene-set scoring.
skills.name: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering Use when a raw counts matrix or Seurat object (csv/rds/h5 or 10X folder) enters a scRNA-seq workflow and cells must be filtered for quality before annotation, clustering, or gene-set scoring. Input is already a QC-passed, filtered expression matrix and re-filtering would remove valid cells (e.g., datasets with naturally low gene counts or high mitochondrial content by biology) Tissue-specific subtypes or cellular states are the analysis target — scWizard QC plus its annotation may leave such cells in an 'Unknown cluster' (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) The goal is not scRNA-seq cell-level QC but, e.g., batch-effect assessment or copy-number inference, which are separate scWizard modules ('Batch processing', 'inferCNV') http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quality control step for single-cell RNA-seq data that filters low-quality cells using scWizard's default thresholds (<200 detected genes, >10,000 detected genes, or >5% mitochondrial read fraction) before downstream analyses such as cell annotation or GSVA scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Quality control step for single-cell RNA-seq data that filters low-quality cells using scWizard's default thresholds (<200 detected genes, >10,000 detected genes, or >5% mitochondrial read fraction) before downstream analyses such as cell annotation or GSVA scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a QC-passed, filtered expression matrix and re-filtering would remove valid cells (e.g., datasets with naturally low gene counts or high mitochondrial content by biology) Tissue-specific subtypes or cellular states are the analysis target — scWizard QC plus its annotation may leave such cells in an 'Unknown cluster' (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers) The goal is not scRNA-seq cell-level QC but, e.g., batch-effect assessment or copy-number inference, which are separate scWizard modules ('Batch processing', 'inferCNV')

skills.description: Use when preprocessing 10X Genomics scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO samples GSM3453537/GSM3453538) before building a CellChat object, and cells must be filtered by UMI count, gene count, and mitochondrial fraction thresholds.
skills.name: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering Use when preprocessing 10X Genomics scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO samples GSM3453537/GSM3453538) before building a CellChat object, and cells must be filtered by UMI count, gene count, and mitochondrial fraction thresholds. The input is already a filtered/normalized expression matrix or a pre-built CellChat object, not raw cell-by-gene counts. The tissue or dataset has different expected mitochondrial or capture characteristics such that the embryonic-skin thresholds (UMI 2500–50000, genes >= 1000, mito < 20%) are biologically inappropriate. The goal is spatially resolved or proteomic data QC rather than scRNA-seq droplet data filtering. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies the embryonic mouse skin scRNA-seq QC filters used before CellChat cell-cell communication inference — UMI count 2500–50000, number of genes >= 1000, and mitochondrial count fraction < 20% — so that downstream communication probabilities are computed on reliably captured cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Applies the embryonic mouse skin scRNA-seq QC filters used before CellChat cell-cell communication inference — UMI count 2500–50000, number of genes >= 1000, and mitochondrial count fraction < 20% — so that downstream communication probabilities are computed on reliably captured cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered/normalized expression matrix or a pre-built CellChat object, not raw cell-by-gene counts. The tissue or dataset has different expected mitochondrial or capture characteristics such that the embryonic-skin thresholds (UMI 2500–50000, genes >= 1000, mito < 20%) are biologically inappropriate. The goal is spatially resolved or proteomic data QC rather than scRNA-seq droplet data filtering.

skills.description: Use when planning scRNA-seq experiments from small pilot data: you need to test whether generative models trained on sub-sampled pilot datasets can produce synthetic data whose clustering, cell-type proportions, and per-gene distributions match a larger ground-truth dataset.
skills.name: scrnaseq-random-subsampling-pilot-design
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-random-subsampling-pilot-design Use when planning scRNA-seq experiments from small pilot data: you need to test whether generative models trained on sub-sampled pilot datasets can produce synthetic data whose clustering, cell-type proportions, and per-gene distributions match a larger ground-truth dataset. Datasets with batch effects you intend to correct: the study examined all models without batch-correction capabilities, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects Pilot samples that are not representative of the target population (changed experimental settings), since extrapolation from small to larger datasets assumes representativeness Goals requiring detection of rare cell types from very small pilots: all approaches overrepresented highly abundant cell types and missed less abundant ones http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A pilot-study design skill for scRNA-seq: random sub-samples (384–2304 cells, 30 repetitions per size) are drawn from a larger ground-truth dataset (PBMC4k, Segerstolpe) to train deep generative models (scDBM, scVI posterior/prior) that extrapolate synthetic data back to the original study size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: A pilot-study design skill for scRNA-seq: random sub-samples (384–2304 cells, 30 repetitions per size) are drawn from a larger ground-truth dataset (PBMC4k, Segerstolpe) to train deep generative models (scDBM, scVI posterior/prior) that extrapolate synthetic data back to the original study size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with batch effects you intend to correct: the study examined all models without batch-correction capabilities, and scDBMs currently cannot learn batch effects Pilot samples that are not representative of the target population (changed experimental settings), since extrapolation from small to larger datasets assumes representativeness Goals requiring detection of rare cell types from very small pilots: all approaches overrepresented highly abundant cell types and missed less abundant ones

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (.sra/.fastq, e.g., from the Kim dataset) must be mapped to HUMAN reference (read_length 100) to produce BAMs feeding featureCounts and GATK-based SNV calling.
skills.name: scrnaseq-read-alignment-star
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-read-alignment-star Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (.sra/.fastq, e.g., from the Kim dataset) must be mapped to HUMAN reference (read_length 100) to produce BAMs feeding featureCounts and GATK-based SNV calling. Input is already an aligned BAM or a per-cell snv_filtered.vcf / matrix_counts.txt — skip directly to feature_counts or process_snv Data is bulk RNA-seq or coupled single-cell DNA-seq; the pipeline here targets scRNA-seq raw reads, and SSrGE notes it 'may miss some driver mutations due to the incomplete DNA coverage of scRNA-seq reads' Reads whose length differs substantially from the indexed read_length (100) — rebuild the STAR index with the matching read_length first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Align single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ/SRA reads to a reference genome (e.g., hg19) using STAR as implemented in the SSrGE docker pipeline (opoirion/ssrge), as the step between SRA extraction and per-cell gene count matrix / SNV calling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Align single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ/SRA reads to a reference genome (e.g., hg19) using STAR as implemented in the SSrGE docker pipeline (opoirion/ssrge), as the step between SRA extraction and per-cell gene count matrix / SNV calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aligned BAM or a per-cell snv_filtered.vcf / matrix_counts.txt — skip directly to feature_counts or process_snv Data is bulk RNA-seq or coupled single-cell DNA-seq; the pipeline here targets scRNA-seq raw reads, and SSrGE notes it 'may miss some driver mutations due to the incomplete DNA coverage of scRNA-seq reads' Reads whose length differs substantially from the indexed read_length (100) — rebuild the STAR index with the matching read_length first

skills.description: Use when a study needs synthetic scRNA-seq reads (BAM/FASTQ) that mimic real data at both read-sequence and read-count levels, e.g., benchmarking UMI deduplication tools or comparing read-coverage fidelity against simulators like minnow.
skills.name: scrnaseq-read-simulation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-read-simulation Use when a study needs synthetic scRNA-seq reads (BAM/FASTQ) that mimic real data at both read-sequence and read-count levels, e.g., benchmarking UMI deduplication tools or comparing read-coverage fidelity against simulators like minnow. Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI count ground truths only, not isoform-level ground truths Count-level-only simulations where reads are unnecessary — scDesign2/scDesign3 alone suffice and are faster Multi-sample or multi-condition studies requiring simultaneous simulation from pooled inputs — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simulate realistic single-cell RNA-seq sequencing reads with scReadSim by training scDesign2 on real UMI count matrices and generating synthetic paired-end reads (BAM/FASTQ) with ground-truth gene-by-cell UMI counts, enabling read-level benchmarking that count-only simulators cannot support. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Simulate realistic single-cell RNA-seq sequencing reads with scReadSim by training scDesign2 on real UMI count matrices and generating synthetic paired-end reads (BAM/FASTQ) with ground-truth gene-by-cell UMI counts, enabling read-level benchmarking that count-only simulators cannot support.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI count ground truths only, not isoform-level ground truths Count-level-only simulations where reads are unnecessary — scDesign2/scDesign3 alone suffice and are faster Multi-sample or multi-condition studies requiring simultaneous simulation from pooled inputs — one BAM file per sample/condition must be supplied separately

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium spots with multi-cell content, or Slide-seq singlet/doublet spots) must be assigned cell-type labels using a paired, cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference, and accuracy must be benchmarked per slice vs. jointly across slices.
skills.name: scrnaseq-reference-based-deconvolution
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-reference-based-deconvolution Use when spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium spots with multi-cell content, or Slide-seq singlet/doublet spots) must be assigned cell-type labels using a paired, cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference, and accuracy must be benchmarked per slice vs. jointly across slices. When the goal is only spot-level cell-type proportions without single-cell-resolution labels — simple deconvolution (Cell2location, CARD, spatialDWLS) suffices and the benchmark here targets single-cell label accuracy When no cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue, since all compared methods are reference-based When the task is gene expression imputation rather than cell type labeling — gene imputation methods (Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE) were reported insufficiently accurate for label inference here http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Method for labeling spatial transcriptomics spots or single cells with cell types by leveraging a labeled scRNA-seq reference, comparing deconvolution/labeling approaches (RCTD, SpatialScope, Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD) by single-cell-level error rate against ground-truth labels on simulated multi-slice Visium benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Method for labeling spatial transcriptomics spots or single cells with cell types by leveraging a labeled scRNA-seq reference, comparing deconvolution/labeling approaches (RCTD, SpatialScope, Tangram, CytoSPACE, StarDist+RCTD) by single-cell-level error rate against ground-truth labels on simulated multi-slice Visium benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only spot-level cell-type proportions without single-cell-resolution labels — simple deconvolution (Cell2location, CARD, spatialDWLS) suffices and the benchmark here targets single-cell label accuracy When no cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue, since all compared methods are reference-based When the task is gene expression imputation rather than cell type labeling — gene imputation methods (Tangram, gimVI, SpaGE) were reported insufficiently accurate for label inference here

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from a complex tissue and a matching scRNA-seq reference with cell type annotations, and need cell type proportion estimates without pre-selected marker genes.
skills.name: scrnaseq-reference-based-proportion-estimation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-reference-based-proportion-estimation Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from a complex tissue and a matching scRNA-seq reference with cell type annotations, and need cell type proportion estimates without pre-selected marker genes. Input bulk data are TPM-normalized rather than raw read counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input The bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions where at least one condition differs from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2 instead Estimates of cell type specific total RNA abundance are unavailable and only RPKM data exist, with no way to provide cell size/RNA-content corrections http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using a multi-subject single-cell RNA-seq reference with MuSiC's weighted non-negative least squares, which weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency instead of relying on pre-selected marker genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using a multi-subject single-cell RNA-seq reference with MuSiC's weighted non-negative least squares, which weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency instead of relying on pre-selected marker genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input bulk data are TPM-normalized rather than raw read counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input The bulk samples come from multiple clinical conditions where at least one condition differs from the scRNA-seq reference — use MuSiC2 instead Estimates of cell type specific total RNA abundance are unavailable and only RPKM data exist, with no way to provide cell size/RNA-content corrections

skills.description: Use when a seq-based ST dataset (e.g., 10X Visium spots) needs per-spot cell type proportions estimated from a matched scRNA-seq reference, or when cell-type composition must be obtained before Splane spatial-domain identification.
skills.name: scrnaseq-reference-based-spot-deconvolution
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-reference-based-spot-deconvolution Use when a seq-based ST dataset (e.g., 10X Visium spots) needs per-spot cell type proportions estimated from a matched scRNA-seq reference, or when cell-type composition must be obtained before Splane spatial-domain identification. Input is single-cell-resolution in-situ ST data where deconvolution of spot mixtures is unnecessary (Spoint targets spot-based seq technologies such as 10X Visium) The goal is spatial-domain identification or 3D alignment directly — use Splane or Scube instead; Spoint is only the prerequisite deconvolution step for seq-based ST data No annotated scRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue, since Spoint is reference-based and depends on the single-cell reference for training http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Deconvolute cell-type composition per spot on single spatial-transcriptomics slices by embedding a multiple-layer perceptron with a probabilistic model (Spoint, the SPACEL deconvolution module) trained on a scRNA-seq reference, enabling downstream Splane spatial-domain identification on seq-based ST data such as 10X Visium. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Deconvolute cell-type composition per spot on single spatial-transcriptomics slices by embedding a multiple-layer perceptron with a probabilistic model (Spoint, the SPACEL deconvolution module) trained on a scRNA-seq reference, enabling downstream Splane spatial-domain identification on seq-based ST data such as 10X Visium.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell-resolution in-situ ST data where deconvolution of spot mixtures is unnecessary (Spoint targets spot-based seq technologies such as 10X Visium) The goal is spatial-domain identification or 3D alignment directly — use Splane or Scube instead; Spoint is only the prerequisite deconvolution step for seq-based ST data No annotated scRNA-seq reference exists for the tissue, since Spoint is reference-based and depends on the single-cell reference for training

skills.description: Use when deciding whether an available scRNA-seq reference (e.g., one missing key cell types like neurons, or an atlas from a different tissue such as mouse brain) is fit for reference-based deconvolution of multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data.
skills.name: scrnaseq-reference-curation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-reference-curation Use when deciding whether an available scRNA-seq reference (e.g., one missing key cell types like neurons, or an atlas from a different tissue such as mouse brain) is fit for reference-based deconvolution of multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data. A suitable scRNA-seq reference covering all cell types in the ST tissue is available — in that case supervised methods perform comparably to STdeconvolve and no curation stress test is needed The ST data are sub-cellular pixel-resolution, where STdeconvolve and this benchmark design are not well suited Cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels so overdispersed-gene feature selection yields no signal, undermining the reference-free baseline the comparison relies on http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmark-driven approach for judging whether a candidate scRNA-seq reference is suitable for supervised ST deconvolution, by testing supervised methods (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) against the reference-free baseline STdeconvolve on simulated pixels with known ground truth and quantifying RMSE inflation with Diebold-Mariano tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: A benchmark-driven approach for judging whether a candidate scRNA-seq reference is suitable for supervised ST deconvolution, by testing supervised methods (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) against the reference-free baseline STdeconvolve on simulated pixels with known ground truth and quantifying RMSE inflation with Diebold-Mariano tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A suitable scRNA-seq reference covering all cell types in the ST tissue is available — in that case supervised methods perform comparably to STdeconvolve and no curation stress test is needed The ST data are sub-cellular pixel-resolution, where STdeconvolve and this benchmark design are not well suited Cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels so overdispersed-gene feature selection yields no signal, undermining the reference-free baseline the comparison relies on

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq (or spatial MERFISH) dataset must be annotated by transferring labels from a matched reference scRNA-seq atlas sharing the same tissue, especially when batch effects separate the two datasets.
skills.name: scrnaseq-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-reference-mapping Use when a query scRNA-seq (or spatial MERFISH) dataset must be annotated by transferring labels from a matched reference scRNA-seq atlas sharing the same tissue, especially when batch effects separate the two datasets. Reference and query datasets originate from different tissues or contain dissimilar cell types — the article states label transfer requires same-tissue or similar cell-type composition for optimal performance The modality pair has few shared features (e.g. CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features), making shared-feature selection and model optimization impractical The goal is de novo clustering of a single batch without any reference atlas — over-correction-free integration machinery is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Map query single-cell data onto a reference atlas using scCobra's contrastive cell embeddings with domain adaptation, enabling online label transfer across batch-affected datasets without retraining. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07692-x
skills.summary: Map query single-cell data onto a reference atlas using scCobra's contrastive cell embeddings with domain adaptation, enabling online label transfer across batch-affected datasets without retraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference and query datasets originate from different tissues or contain dissimilar cell types — the article states label transfer requires same-tissue or similar cell-type composition for optimal performance The modality pair has few shared features (e.g. CITE-seq protein data with only a few hundred features), making shared-feature selection and model optimization impractical The goal is de novo clustering of a single batch without any reference atlas — over-correction-free integration machinery is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when comparing computational scalability of rare-cell identification methods on scRNA-seq data, or when judging whether a method can process datasets in the tens-of-thousands-of-cells range.
skills.name: scrnaseq-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-runtime-benchmarking Use when comparing computational scalability of rare-cell identification methods on scRNA-seq data, or when judging whether a method can process datasets in the tens-of-thousands-of-cells range. The goal is accuracy of rare-cell detection (precision/recall) rather than runtime scalability — this skill measures execution time only The dataset is small (hundreds of cells) where scalability differences between methods are negligible The candidate method cannot be run single-core or in a controlled environment, making wall-clock comparisons unfair http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking protocol that measures single-core wall-clock execution times of rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) as scRNA-seq input size scales from 1k to ~68k expression profiles, demonstrating FiRE's dramatic speed advantage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: A benchmarking protocol that measures single-core wall-clock execution times of rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) as scRNA-seq input size scales from 1k to ~68k expression profiles, demonstrating FiRE's dramatic speed advantage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy of rare-cell detection (precision/recall) rather than runtime scalability — this skill measures execution time only The dataset is small (hundreds of cells) where scalability differences between methods are negligible The candidate method cannot be run single-core or in a controlled environment, making wall-clock comparisons unfair

skills.description: Use when you need to visually compare cell-type or developmental-stage separation produced by different learned cell-to-cell similarity matrices on scRNA-seq data, e.g. benchmarking SSRE against Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR on the Goolam or Yan datasets.
skills.name: scrnaseq-similarity-matrix-visualization
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-similarity-matrix-visualization Use when you need to visually compare cell-type or developmental-stage separation produced by different learned cell-to-cell similarity matrices on scRNA-seq data, e.g. benchmarking SSRE against Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR on the Goolam or Yan datasets. The goal is quantitative clustering accuracy (NMI/ARI/Purity) rather than visual separation comparison — use the SSRE clustering evaluation instead of the visualization extension Data are not scRNA-seq similarity matrices but already-embedded 2D coordinates or a feature table requiring only standard t-SNE Datasets are large-scale, where SSRE is known to be relatively time-consuming and parallel computing would be required http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce the SSRE paper's Figure 3-style visualization by embedding cell-to-cell similarity matrices learned by competing methods (native t-SNE, Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, SSRE) into 2D with a modified t-SNE for scRNA-seq data, then comparing how clearly developmental stage/cell-type groups separate across methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Reproduce the SSRE paper's Figure 3-style visualization by embedding cell-to-cell similarity matrices learned by competing methods (native t-SNE, Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, SSRE) into 2D with a modified t-SNE for scRNA-seq data, then comparing how clearly developmental stage/cell-type groups separate across methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantitative clustering accuracy (NMI/ARI/Purity) rather than visual separation comparison — use the SSRE clustering evaluation instead of the visualization extension Data are not scRNA-seq similarity matrices but already-embedded 2D coordinates or a feature table requiring only standard t-SNE Datasets are large-scale, where SSRE is known to be relatively time-consuming and parallel computing would be required

skills.description: Use when validating or benchmarking a cluster-merging / cluster-significance method (e.g. Cytocipher cluster-merge) on simulated scRNA-seq data where the true subcluster structure is known and an AUROC against ground-truth labels is the target metric.
skills.name: scrnaseq-simulation-with-ground-truth-subclusters
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-simulation-with-ground-truth-subclusters Use when validating or benchmarking a cluster-merging / cluster-significance method (e.g. Cytocipher cluster-merge) on simulated scRNA-seq data where the true subcluster structure is known and an AUROC against ground-truth labels is the target metric. Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without any ground-truth subcluster labels — ROC/AUROC against the three-way artificial subclusters cannot be computed. The Leiden labels are not over-clustered (low resolution) — the README recommends high Leiden resolution so there is substantial over-clustering for Cytocipher to merge. The data is raw counts without log-cpm normalisation and tentative cluster labels — the expected input is an AnnData processed via the scanpy standard workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmark cluster-merge discrimination on simulated scRNA-seq data where groups are defined by unique gene combinations and each group carries a three-way artificial subcluster ground truth, scoring cluster-pair significance via ROC/AUROC across multiple enrichment-scoring approaches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Benchmark cluster-merge discrimination on simulated scRNA-seq data where groups are defined by unique gene combinations and each group carries a three-way artificial subcluster ground truth, scoring cluster-pair significance via ROC/AUROC across multiple enrichment-scoring approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data without any ground-truth subcluster labels — ROC/AUROC against the three-way artificial subclusters cannot be computed. The Leiden labels are not over-clustered (low resolution) — the README recommends high Leiden resolution so there is substantial over-clustering for Cytocipher to merge. The data is raw counts without log-cpm normalisation and tentative cluster labels — the expected input is an AnnData processed via the scanpy standard workflow.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data are available and gene-level DE effect sizes (beta coefficients and their variances) must be generated as input for iDEA's joint DE and gene set enrichment analysis.
skills.name: scrnaseq-summary-statistics-construction
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-summary-statistics-construction Use when scRNA-seq count data are available and gene-level DE effect sizes (beta coefficients and their variances) must be generated as input for iDEA's joint DE and gene set enrichment analysis. When only individual-level count data are available and a full joint model of raw scRNA-seq counts is required rather than summary-statistic integration. When the downstream analysis needs DE calls with individual-level modeling assumptions rather than effect-size borrowing across genes (iDEA makes no explicit modeling assumptions on individual-level data). When gene sets have coverage rate below min_precent_annot = 0.0025 or fewer than min_degene = 5 detected DE genes — they are filtered out by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Produce gene-level differential expression summary statistics (beta coefficient and its variance) from scRNA-seq data using standalone DE tools (MAST, edgeR with ZINB-WaVE weighting, zingeR), formatted for downstream integration by iDEA. iDEA consumes only these summary statistics, avoiding explicit modeling of individual-level scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Produce gene-level differential expression summary statistics (beta coefficient and its variance) from scRNA-seq data using standalone DE tools (MAST, edgeR with ZINB-WaVE weighting, zingeR), formatted for downstream integration by iDEA. iDEA consumes only these summary statistics, avoiding explicit modeling of individual-level scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only individual-level count data are available and a full joint model of raw scRNA-seq counts is required rather than summary-statistic integration. When the downstream analysis needs DE calls with individual-level modeling assumptions rather than effect-size borrowing across genes (iDEA makes no explicit modeling assumptions on individual-level data). When gene sets have coverage rate below min_precent_annot = 0.0025 or fewer than min_degene = 5 detected DE genes — they are filtered out by design.

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset with collection time-point labels needs a balanced subsample before trajectory inference, especially to exclude cells whose pseudotime disagrees with their collection time point.
skills.name: scrnaseq-time-series-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-time-series-trajectory-inference Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset with collection time-point labels needs a balanced subsample before trajectory inference, especially to exclude cells whose pseudotime disagrees with their collection time point. The input is already a small or pre-filtered dataset where uniform subsampling would not risk overlooking rare cell states or unbalanced time-point representation The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's model — the article notes compatibility was only shown for Louvain community detection and Monocle 2 No prior categorical information (cell type, collection time point) exists and fair sampling per class is not needed; use Sphetcher's two-argument mode instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A fairness-constrained single-cell sketching workflow: Sphetcher selects a representative sketch of cells from an scRNA-seq expression matrix while enforcing a minimum number of representatives (l_min) per collection time-point class, and the sketch feeds Monocle 2 trajectory inference on the HSMM human skeletal muscle myoblast differentiation data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: A fairness-constrained single-cell sketching workflow: Sphetcher selects a representative sketch of cells from an scRNA-seq expression matrix while enforcing a minimum number of representatives (l_min) per collection time-point class, and the sketch feeds Monocle 2 trajectory inference on the HSMM human skeletal muscle myoblast differentiation data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small or pre-filtered dataset where uniform subsampling would not risk overlooking rare cell states or unbalanced time-point representation The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's model — the article notes compatibility was only shown for Louvain community detection and Monocle 2 No prior categorical information (cell type, collection time point) exists and fair sampling per class is not needed; use Sphetcher's two-argument mode instead

skills.description: Use when clustering a small scRNA-Seq target dataset (e.g. rare cell types, 300–600 cells) for which a large, well-annotated source dataset from a related tissue or context exists.
skills.name: scrnaseq-transfer-learning-clustering
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-transfer-learning-clustering Use when clustering a small scRNA-Seq target dataset (e.g. rare cell types, 300–600 cells) for which a large, well-annotated source dataset from a related tissue or context exists. Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — the article notes 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only the set of genes present in both datasets can be used' No large, well-annotated source dataset exists for the tissue or disease context of interest Downstream analysis other than clustering is the goal — the article explicitly states other downstream methods besides SC3 are an open research direction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 NMF-based transfer learning method that modifies a small scRNA-Seq target dataset with information from a large well-annotated source dataset before downstream clustering, to improve clustering of small disease- or tissue-specific datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-56911-z
skills.summary: NMF-based transfer learning method that modifies a small scRNA-Seq target dataset with information from a large well-annotated source dataset before downstream clustering, to improve clustering of small disease- or tissue-specific datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Source and target share only a small set of transcripts — the article notes 'a loss of (probably) vital information is inevitable since only the set of genes present in both datasets can be used' No large, well-annotated source dataset exists for the tissue or disease context of interest Downstream analysis other than clustering is the goal — the article explicitly states other downstream methods besides SC3 are an open research direction

skills.description: Use when preparing per-cell-group average expression of ligands, receptors, and cofactors from scRNA-seq data before inferring cell-cell communication probabilities with CellChat or a reimplementation of its mass-action model.
skills.name: scrnaseq-trimean-expression-aggregation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-trimean-expression-aggregation Use when preparing per-cell-group average expression of ligands, receptors, and cofactors from scRNA-seq data before inferring cell-cell communication probabilities with CellChat or a reimplementation of its mass-action model. Input is spatial transcriptomics data needing single-cell-resolution communication (use CellChat v3/SpatialCellChat instead) Only differential expression of signaling genes is needed rather than group-level averaged expression feeding interaction inference Cell grouping or clustering is not yet established — CellChat and related tools require pre-defined cell groups as a prerequisite http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Computes the statistically robust ensemble-average expression of signaling genes per cell group using the trimean (mean of quartiles), with geometric-mean aggregation for multi-subunit ligand/receptor complexes from CellChatDB, as the input layer for CellChat's mass-action communication probability model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Computes the statistically robust ensemble-average expression of signaling genes per cell group using the trimean (mean of quartiles), with geometric-mean aggregation for multi-subunit ligand/receptor complexes from CellChatDB, as the input layer for CellChat's mass-action communication probability model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spatial transcriptomics data needing single-cell-resolution communication (use CellChat v3/SpatialCellChat instead) Only differential expression of signaling genes is needed rather than group-level averaged expression feeding interaction inference Cell grouping or clustering is not yet established — CellChat and related tools require pre-defined cell groups as a prerequisite

skills.description: Use when you have a multi-sample scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. patient biopsies with cell-type annotations, PCA embedding, patient and disease-status columns) and need sample-level distances to detect disease-associated patient subgroups without patient labels.
skills.name: scrnaseq-wasserstein-distance-computation
skills.search_text: scrnaseq-wasserstein-distance-computation Use when you have a multi-sample scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. patient biopsies with cell-type annotations, PCA embedding, patient and disease-status columns) and need sample-level distances to detect disease-associated patient subgroups without patient labels. When patients already carry labels required by competing approaches (PhEMD, SCANCell, Multi-scale PHATE) and a supervised comparison suffices — PILOT's value here is unsupervised sample-level analysis When samples were collected non-uniformly across distinct technologies (single nucleus vs. single cell) or isolation methods (droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge When the goal is per-cell rather than per-sample comparison — this skill operates on sample-level cluster distributions, not individual cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute Wasserstein (earth mover's) distances between individual single-cell samples with PILOT's optimal-transport machinery (emd2 from the POT library) so that samples—not cells—become the unit of unsupervised analysis. This yields a sample-by-sample distance matrix W that feeds Leiden clustering or trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Compute Wasserstein (earth mover's) distances between individual single-cell samples with PILOT's optimal-transport machinery (emd2 from the POT library) so that samples—not cells—become the unit of unsupervised analysis. This yields a sample-by-sample distance matrix W that feeds Leiden clustering or trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When patients already carry labels required by competing approaches (PhEMD, SCANCell, Multi-scale PHATE) and a supervised comparison suffices — PILOT's value here is unsupervised sample-level analysis When samples were collected non-uniformly across distinct technologies (single nucleus vs. single cell) or isolation methods (droplet vs. well based), which the authors flag as an open challenge When the goal is per-cell rather than per-sample comparison — this skill operates on sample-level cluster distributions, not individual cells

skills.description: Use when a single-cell transcriptomics dataset ships with pre-computed dimensionality reductions and manual cell-type annotations, and you must show whether a new embedding or clustering method beats those baselines on unsupervised cell-type recovery.
skills.name: scrtcna-dimensionality-reduction-baseline-comparison
skills.search_text: scrtcna-dimensionality-reduction-baseline-comparison Use when a single-cell transcriptomics dataset ships with pre-computed dimensionality reductions and manual cell-type annotations, and you must show whether a new embedding or clustering method beats those baselines on unsupervised cell-type recovery. Datasets requiring batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate batches — the source study explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction, so baseline comparisons under strong batch structure are out of scope Samples with tens of thousands or more cells — the benchmark deliberately restricted to tissues with fewer than 10,000 sampled cells, and q-diffused kernel evaluation across all cell pairs takes 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix Analyses that need directly interpretable nonlinear structure — the authors note q-diffusion's nonlinearities are less directly interpretable than those of dimensionality-reduction embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark protocol for comparing an experimental single-cell embedding/clustering method (here, q-diffusion with Leiden) against the dimensionality reductions supplied with a dataset (e.g., scVI in Tabula Sapiens) and neighborhood-graph baselines (Seurat, Monocle, Scanpy, SC3), scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against manual cell-type annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for comparing an experimental single-cell embedding/clustering method (here, q-diffusion with Leiden) against the dimensionality reductions supplied with a dataset (e.g., scVI in Tabula Sapiens) and neighborhood-graph baselines (Seurat, Monocle, Scanpy, SC3), scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against manual cell-type annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets requiring batch-effect correction or alignment of disparate batches — the source study explicitly did not consider batch-effect correction, so baseline comparisons under strong batch structure are out of scope Samples with tens of thousands or more cells — the benchmark deliberately restricted to tissues with fewer than 10,000 sampled cells, and q-diffused kernel evaluation across all cell pairs takes 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix Analyses that need directly interpretable nonlinear structure — the authors note q-diffusion's nonlinearities are less directly interpretable than those of dimensionality-reduction embeddings

skills.description: Use when scTE differential TE calls (e.g. ≥2-fold change, FDR < 0.05 between ESCs and MEFs) need robustness checks against TE annotation mode, especially to test whether intronic TE reads drive specificity.
skills.name: scte-mode-comparison-validation
skills.search_text: scte-mode-comparison-validation Use when scTE differential TE calls (e.g. ≥2-fold change, FDR < 0.05 between ESCs and MEFs) need robustness checks against TE annotation mode, especially to test whether intronic TE reads drive specificity. Input is already an aggregated TE count or DE results table — the skill requires re-running scTE from raw BAM/SAM alignments in two modes The analysis aims to assign reads overlapping TE-in-exon/UTR regions to both genes and TEs — that requires the inclusive mode (-m inclusive), not the exclusive/nointron comparison Data are single-cell ATAC-seq; TE accessibility should use scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build rather than scTE count modes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 A validation skill for scTE-based TE differential expression: re-run scTE in a second annotation mode (nointron vs default exclusive) and quantify how many significant DE TEs retain cell-type specificity, testing whether findings depend on intronic reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: A validation skill for scTE-based TE differential expression: re-run scTE in a second annotation mode (nointron vs default exclusive) and quantify how many significant DE TEs retain cell-type specificity, testing whether findings depend on intronic reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an aggregated TE count or DE results table — the skill requires re-running scTE from raw BAM/SAM alignments in two modes The analysis aims to assign reads overlapping TE-in-exon/UTR regions to both genes and TEs — that requires the inclusive mode (-m inclusive), not the exclusive/nointron comparison Data are single-cell ATAC-seq; TE accessibility should use scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build rather than scTE count modes

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices from one or more plant samples (e.g. Arabidopsis, Oryza sativa, Zea mays roots) must be variance-stabilized and normalized with SCTransform prior to PCA/UMAP, clustering, or CCA/RPCA-based cross-species integration.
skills.name: sctransform-normalization
skills.search_text: sctransform-normalization Use when raw single-cell count matrices from one or more plant samples (e.g. Arabidopsis, Oryza sativa, Zea mays roots) must be variance-stabilized and normalized with SCTransform prior to PCA/UMAP, clustering, or CCA/RPCA-based cross-species integration. Input is already an SCT-normalized or integrated Seurat object — re-normalizing would distort the corrected counts. The analysis target is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution or gene regulatory network construction, where the scPlant pipeline uses other modules rather than SCTransform normalization. Data are non-plant single-cell datasets where scPlant's plant-specific ortholog/genome resources (TAIR10, Oryza sativa V7.0, Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0) do not provide anchors. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalize single-plant scRNA-seq expression matrices with SCTransform (as implemented via the Seurat package inside scPlant) before embedding and cross-species integration, e.g. as the per-dataset normalization step of scPlant::crossSpecies_integrate on Arabidopsis, rice, and maize root data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Normalize single-plant scRNA-seq expression matrices with SCTransform (as implemented via the Seurat package inside scPlant) before embedding and cross-species integration, e.g. as the per-dataset normalization step of scPlant::crossSpecies_integrate on Arabidopsis, rice, and maize root data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an SCT-normalized or integrated Seurat object — re-normalizing would distort the corrected counts. The analysis target is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution or gene regulatory network construction, where the scPlant pipeline uses other modules rather than SCTransform normalization. Data are non-plant single-cell datasets where scPlant's plant-specific ortholog/genome resources (TAIR10, Oryza sativa V7.0, Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0) do not provide anchors.

skills.description: Use when multiple scRNAseq samples (e.g., a time series such as GSE223109) must be normalized and integrated before joint clustering, and per-sample SCTransform normalization plus a shared integration feature set is needed to remove batch effects.
skills.name: sctransform-sample-integration
skills.search_text: sctransform-sample-integration Use when multiple scRNAseq samples (e.g., a time series such as GSE223109) must be normalized and integrated before joint clustering, and per-sample SCTransform normalization plus a shared integration feature set is needed to remove batch effects. You have only a single sample with no batch effects to correct — SCTransform alone suffices without SelectIntegrationFeatures-based integration. Input is already a normalized/integrated expression matrix or pseudobulk table rather than raw CellRanger output requiring per-sample SCTransform normalization. Prediction of circadian time from an already-integrated pseudobulk sample is the goal — that is tauFisher's train/test pipeline, not sample integration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalize each single-cell RNAseq sample independently with Seurat's SCTransform, then batch-integrate samples using 3250 SelectIntegrationFeatures so that downstream PCA/Louvain clustering reflects biology rather than sample-specific technical effects. Used in the tauFisher paper to build an integrated mouse dermis scRNAseq time series (GSE223109, MM10) for cell-type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: Normalize each single-cell RNAseq sample independently with Seurat's SCTransform, then batch-integrate samples using 3250 SelectIntegrationFeatures so that downstream PCA/Louvain clustering reflects biology rather than sample-specific technical effects. Used in the tauFisher paper to build an integrated mouse dermis scRNAseq time series (GSE223109, MM10) for cell-type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single sample with no batch effects to correct — SCTransform alone suffices without SelectIntegrationFeatures-based integration. Input is already a normalized/integrated expression matrix or pseudobulk table rather than raw CellRanger output requiring per-sample SCTransform normalization. Prediction of circadian time from an already-integrated pseudobulk sample is the goal — that is tauFisher's train/test pipeline, not sample integration.

skills.description: Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) with cell-type labels must be subsampled for a downstream ML/DL task (annotation, label transfer, deconvolution) and cell-level informativeness should guide which cells enter the sketch.
skills.name: scvalue-rf-oob-data-value-computation
skills.search_text: scvalue-rf-oob-data-value-computation Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) with cell-type labels must be subsampled for a downstream ML/DL task (annotation, label transfer, deconvolution) and cell-level informativeness should guide which cells enter the sketch. The dataset is small enough that no subsampling is needed, or the analysis goal is uniform/distribution-preserving sketching (GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler) rather than value-based selection for ML/DL tasks Input lacks cell-type labels in .obs, since DV computation is supervised (random forest OOB estimates per cell type) The input is already a reduced feature table or the target task is not a learning task (e.g. pure visualization of the full atlas) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute a per-cell 'data value' (DV) score for an scRNA-seq dataset using out-of-bag (OOB) estimates from a random forest classifier, via the scValue Python package. Higher-DV cells are more helpful for distinguishing their cell type and are prioritized during subsampling (sketching). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Compute a per-cell 'data value' (DV) score for an scRNA-seq dataset using out-of-bag (OOB) estimates from a random forest classifier, via the scValue Python package. Higher-DV cells are more helpful for distinguishing their cell type and are prioritized during subsampling (sketching).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that no subsampling is needed, or the analysis goal is uniform/distribution-preserving sketching (GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, scSampler) rather than value-based selection for ML/DL tasks Input lacks cell-type labels in .obs, since DV computation is supervised (random forest OOB estimates per cell type) The input is already a reduced feature table or the target task is not a learning task (e.g. pure visualization of the full atlas)

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires traditional linear RNA velocity baselines — e.g., comparing against LatentVelo on dyngen synthetic AnnData (spliced/unspliced layers) or real scRNA-seq with spliced and unspliced counts.
skills.name: scvelo-dynamical-and-stochastic-velocity-estimation
skills.search_text: scvelo-dynamical-and-stochastic-velocity-estimation Use when a benchmark requires traditional linear RNA velocity baselines — e.g., comparing against LatentVelo on dyngen synthetic AnnData (spliced/unspliced layers) or real scRNA-seq with spliced and unspliced counts. The data lacks unspliced (or spliced) count layers — scVelo's dynamical and stochastic models both rely on the unspliced-to-spliced relationship The goal is batch-corrected or lineage-aware velocity; the article shows traditional linear methods fail with multiple lineages, transcriptional boosts, lineage-dependent kinetics, and weak unspliced signals, and LatentVelo is designed for those settings Comparing against LatentVelo outputs on its latent AnnData, where velocities use vkey='spliced_velocity' and must not be overwritten by scVelo-computed velocities http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run scVelo in its dynamical and stochastic modes to produce baseline RNA velocity estimates that can be benchmarked against latent-space methods such as LatentVelo on synthetic and real datasets, using metrics like cosine similarity, CBDir, and ICCoh. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100581
skills.summary: Run scVelo in its dynamical and stochastic modes to produce baseline RNA velocity estimates that can be benchmarked against latent-space methods such as LatentVelo on synthetic and real datasets, using metrics like cosine similarity, CBDir, and ICCoh.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lacks unspliced (or spliced) count layers — scVelo's dynamical and stochastic models both rely on the unspliced-to-spliced relationship The goal is batch-corrected or lineage-aware velocity; the article shows traditional linear methods fail with multiple lineages, transcriptional boosts, lineage-dependent kinetics, and weak unspliced signals, and LatentVelo is designed for those settings Comparing against LatentVelo outputs on its latent AnnData, where velocities use vkey='spliced_velocity' and must not be overwritten by scVelo-computed velocities

skills.description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData from a hematopoietic or erythroid differentiation dataset yields suspicious or reversed velocity directions from scVelo, and a benchmark against a unified-time method is needed.
skills.name: scvelo-dynamical-model-benchmarking
skills.search_text: scvelo-dynamical-model-benchmarking Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData from a hematopoietic or erythroid differentiation dataset yields suspicious or reversed velocity directions from scVelo, and a benchmark against a unified-time method is needed. Datasets without spliced/unspliced count layers or velocity genes identified, since both scVelo dynamical mode and UniTVelo require them Scenarios where the scVelo dynamical trajectory direction is already correct and matches expected biology — no benchmark/correction step is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Benchmark scVelo's likelihood-based 'dynamical' mode against UniTVelo's unified latent time on erythroid haematopoiesis datasets containing MURK genes, where scVelo returns distorted or reversed maturation trajectory directions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34188-7
skills.summary: Benchmark scVelo's likelihood-based 'dynamical' mode against UniTVelo's unified latent time on erythroid haematopoiesis datasets containing MURK genes, where scVelo returns distorted or reversed maturation trajectory directions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets without spliced/unspliced count layers or velocity genes identified, since both scVelo dynamical mode and UniTVelo require them Scenarios where the scVelo dynamical trajectory direction is already correct and matches expected biology — no benchmark/correction step is needed

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain quantifiable continuous nuisance covariates (e.g., cell-cycle or sex scores) and a latent-space batch-correction baseline is needed to compare against gene-level filtering methods.
skills.name: scvi-continuous-covariate-correction
skills.search_text: scvi-continuous-covariate-correction Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain quantifiable continuous nuisance covariates (e.g., cell-cycle or sex scores) and a latent-space batch-correction baseline is needed to compare against gene-level filtering methods. When correction must occur at the gene expression level (e.g., downstream tools require corrected genes or properly log-transformed expression) — scVI corrects only in a joint latent representation When nuisance variation cannot be encoded as continuous per-cell covariate scores When no integration metrics appropriate to the application are available to evaluate whether unwanted variation was actually removed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Trains an scVI variational autoencoder with continuous covariates (e.g., cell-cycle and sex scores) to remove unwanted biological variation in a joint latent representation, serving as a deep-learning baseline for gene-level filtering methods like SiFT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Trains an scVI variational autoencoder with continuous covariates (e.g., cell-cycle and sex scores) to remove unwanted biological variation in a joint latent representation, serving as a deep-learning baseline for gene-level filtering methods like SiFT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When correction must occur at the gene expression level (e.g., downstream tools require corrected genes or properly log-transformed expression) — scVI corrects only in a joint latent representation When nuisance variation cannot be encoded as continuous per-cell covariate scores When no integration metrics appropriate to the application are available to evaluate whether unwanted variation was actually removed

skills.description: Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq observations with a trained VAE (scVI) but you want generation independent of the original observations, i.e., sampling directly from the prior of the latent space rather than the posterior.
skills.name: scvi-prior-sampling-implementation
skills.search_text: scvi-prior-sampling-implementation Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq observations with a trained VAE (scVI) but you want generation independent of the original observations, i.e., sampling directly from the prior of the latent space rather than the posterior. You need the standard scVI generative variant that conditions generation on copies of original observations via the posterior p(z|x) rather than the prior. Your trained model lacks a learned library-size mean (l_mu) or does not use a gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder, so prior sampling with Normal(l_mu, 1) library sizes is not well-defined. Your goal is batch correction: the paper examined all models without using potentially available batch correction capabilities and explicitly omitted batch-correction methods from its scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs the scVI prior-sampling generative variant from Treppner et al. (2021), in which latent z is drawn from Normal(0, 1) and library sizes from Normal(l_mu, 1) instead of the standard posterior sampling p(z|x), and synthetic UMI counts are produced via scVI's gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs the scVI prior-sampling generative variant from Treppner et al. (2021), in which latent z is drawn from Normal(0, 1) and library sizes from Normal(l_mu, 1) instead of the standard posterior sampling p(z|x), and synthetic UMI counts are produced via scVI's gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the standard scVI generative variant that conditions generation on copies of original observations via the posterior p(z|x) rather than the prior. Your trained model lacks a learned library-size mean (l_mu) or does not use a gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) decoder, so prior sampling with Normal(l_mu, 1) library sizes is not well-defined. Your goal is batch correction: the paper examined all models without using potentially available batch correction capabilities and explicitly omitted batch-correction methods from its scope.

skills.description: Use when you have trained a VEGA model with gene-module-informed latent posteriors and need to call gene modules significantly differentially active between two cell groups via a Bayes Factor.
skills.name: scvi-tools-style-differential-testing-implementation
skills.search_text: scvi-tools-style-differential-testing-implementation Use when you have trained a VEGA model with gene-module-informed latent posteriors and need to call gene modules significantly differentially active between two cell groups via a Bayes Factor. The latent variables are not tied to user-provided gene modules (e.g. an unconstrained VAE/scVI latent space with no GMT annotation), so there is no GMV posterior to contrast You only need dataset-wide module activation scores rather than a two-group statistical contrast — VEGA's single-cell GMV activity inference suffices without the Bayes Factor test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements VEGA's Bayesian differential gene module variable (GMV) activity test — a Monte Carlo Bayes Factor procedure contrasting latent GMV activity posteriors between two cell groups — packaged as a reusable module following the scvi-tools-inspired differential testing design. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Implements VEGA's Bayesian differential gene module variable (GMV) activity test — a Monte Carlo Bayes Factor procedure contrasting latent GMV activity posteriors between two cell groups — packaged as a reusable module following the scvi-tools-inspired differential testing design.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The latent variables are not tied to user-provided gene modules (e.g. an unconstrained VAE/scVI latent space with no GMT annotation), so there is no GMV posterior to contrast You only need dataset-wide module activation scores rather than a two-group statistical contrast — VEGA's single-cell GMV activity inference suffices without the Bayes Factor test

skills.description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. tens of thousands of cells) must be scanned for rare cell clusters without clustering the whole dataset, and clusters must be ranked by a gap-based distance score (skewness > 2).
skills.name: second-order-derivative-gap-distance-scoring
skills.search_text: second-order-derivative-gap-distance-scoring Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. tens of thousands of cells) must be scanned for rare cell clusters without clustering the whole dataset, and clusters must be ranked by a gap-based distance score (skewness > 2). When the task is comprehensive characterisation of major cell types — use mainstream toolkits such as Seurat or Scater, as GapClust targets only rare populations When the input is already a clustered/annotated cell-type table rather than a raw expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 GapClust's core statistic: score candidate rare clusters by a second-order derivative type distance score that exploits the inter-cluster gap, ranking minor clusters by skewness so that cells in a rare cluster whose nearest out-of-cluster neighbours are far away stand out. It underpins ultra-fast rare cell detection in large scRNA-seq datasets such as the 68k PBMC dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: GapClust's core statistic: score candidate rare clusters by a second-order derivative type distance score that exploits the inter-cluster gap, ranking minor clusters by skewness so that cells in a rare cluster whose nearest out-of-cluster neighbours are far away stand out. It underpins ultra-fast rare cell detection in large scRNA-seq datasets such as the 68k PBMC dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is comprehensive characterisation of major cell types — use mainstream toolkits such as Seurat or Scater, as GapClust targets only rare populations When the input is already a clustered/annotated cell-type table rather than a raw expression matrix

skills.description: Use when you have a precomputed cell-to-neighbour distance matrix for a scRNA-seq dataset and need to derive ∆D/∆∆D statistics and per-k skewness to identify candidate rare cluster sizes.
skills.name: second-order-derivative-statistic-computation
skills.search_text: second-order-derivative-statistic-computation Use when you have a precomputed cell-to-neighbour distance matrix for a scRNA-seq dataset and need to derive ∆D/∆∆D statistics and per-k skewness to identify candidate rare cluster sizes. Input is raw expression counts without a precomputed neighbour-distance matrix — run the upstream distance-computation step first The goal is to characterise major/abundant cell types — GapClust's ∆∆D statistic is designed to exploit the gap around minor clusters only http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes the second-order derivative distance statistics (∆∆D) over sorted nearest-neighbour distances and aggregates their per-k skewness so GapClust can flag candidate rare-cluster sizes k when skewness > 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Computes the second-order derivative distance statistics (∆∆D) over sorted nearest-neighbour distances and aggregates their per-k skewness so GapClust can flag candidate rare-cluster sizes k when skewness > 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw expression counts without a precomputed neighbour-distance matrix — run the upstream distance-computation step first The goal is to characterise major/abundant cell types — GapClust's ∆∆D statistic is designed to exploit the gap around minor clusters only

skills.description: Use when a comparative-genomics pipeline needs BGC-level absence/presence features across many bacterial genomes — e.g. annotating .gbk files with Prokka then mining secondary metabolites with antiSMASH and BiG-SCAPE before lifestyle association.
skills.name: secondary-metabolite-class-profiling
skills.search_text: secondary-metabolite-class-profiling Use when a comparative-genomics pipeline needs BGC-level absence/presence features across many bacterial genomes — e.g. annotating .gbk files with Prokka then mining secondary metabolites with antiSMASH and BiG-SCAPE before lifestyle association. The input is already a binary feature matrix (e.g. a gene-cluster absence/presence table) ready for lifestyle prediction or machine learning — the BGC mining step would be redundant. Genomes have not passed quality filtering (CheckM >90% completeness, <5% contamination) or redundancy reduction at 0.99 Mash-estimated ANI — antiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE would be run on low-quality or near-duplicate assemblies. The goal is lifestyle prediction itself (random-forest classifier with >0.8 confidence threshold) rather than secondary-metabolite profiling — use the lifestyle-prediction module instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs the bacLIFE secondary-metabolite analysis in which BGCs predicted per genome by antiSMASH are clustered into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs) with BiG-SCAPE at a 0.70 distance cutoff, yielding a binary GCF absence/presence matrix and per-genome BGC-class tallies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46302-y
skills.summary: Reconstructs the bacLIFE secondary-metabolite analysis in which BGCs predicted per genome by antiSMASH are clustered into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs) with BiG-SCAPE at a 0.70 distance cutoff, yielding a binary GCF absence/presence matrix and per-genome BGC-class tallies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a binary feature matrix (e.g. a gene-cluster absence/presence table) ready for lifestyle prediction or machine learning — the BGC mining step would be redundant. Genomes have not passed quality filtering (CheckM >90% completeness, <5% contamination) or redundancy reduction at 0.99 Mash-estimated ANI — antiSMASH/BiG-SCAPE would be run on low-quality or near-duplicate assemblies. The goal is lifestyle prediction itself (random-forest classifier with >0.8 confidence threshold) rather than secondary-metabolite profiling — use the lifestyle-prediction module instead.

skills.summary: Ablation protocol for the LncDC lncRNA classifier that quantifies the contribution of the 6 selected secondary structure features (SSFs) by comparing full-model prediction (SIF+PF+SSF) against a SIF+PF-only model and an SSF-only model on the human H-Test FASTA dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo lncRNA prediction on new RNA-Seq assemblies rather than evaluating which features drive the classifier's performance You need to train new models from your own mRNA/CDS/lncRNA FASTA data (use the lncDC-train.py workflow instead of running the prebuilt ablation) The comparison targets a non-human organism without prebuilt SS k-mer tables, since self-training with -r requires time-consuming RNAfold secondary structure calculation

skills.search_text: secondary-structure-kmer-feature-generation Use when training or predicting with LncDC with secondary structure features enabled (the '-r' flag), so RNAfold foldings must be converted into ss k-mer score tables at k=1..k=5. If secondary structure features are not wanted, train without '-r' — output is then only the hexamer table and SIF+PF model files (XGB_model_SIF_PF.pkl) If ViennaRNA is not installed and cannot be installed, since RNAfold is required to compute the foldings the ss k-mer tables depend on If the input is already a computed feature matrix — this skill only generates ss k-mer tables from transcript FASTA sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Generates sequence-and-secondary-structure (SASS) k-mer score features for RNA transcripts by folding each transcript with RNAfold (ViennaRNA) and scoring k-mers (k=1 to 5) against training-derived ss k-mer tables, which improves LncDC's lncRNA vs mRNA classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-22082-7
skills.summary: Generates sequence-and-secondary-structure (SASS) k-mer score features for RNA transcripts by folding each transcript with RNAfold (ViennaRNA) and scoring k-mers (k=1 to 5) against training-derived ss k-mer tables, which improves LncDC's lncRNA vs mRNA classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If secondary structure features are not wanted, train without '-r' — output is then only the hexamer table and SIF+PF model files (XGB_model_SIF_PF.pkl) If ViennaRNA is not installed and cannot be installed, since RNAfold is required to compute the foldings the ss k-mer tables depend on If the input is already a computed feature matrix — this skill only generates ss k-mer tables from transcript FASTA sequences

skills.search_text: seed-controlled-in-silico-dataset-generation Use when a benchmark needs multiple simulated single-cell datasets with known ground truth (trajectory, progression times, cell-specific GRNs) across diverse backbone topologies and reproducible seeds. The analysis requires real biological data rather than synthetic data with known ground truth (dyngen simulations assume well-mixed, independent cells and do not capture inter-cellular dependencies). The target method needs simulator features dyngen does not provide, e.g. benchmarking of clustering or differential-expression methods for which protocol-specific simulators such as Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim were designed. Only a single arbitrary topology is needed without controlled backbone variety or seed-level reproducibility — a simpler one-off simulation suffices. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate reproducible simulated single-cell datasets with dyngen by enumerating predefined trajectory backbones, instantiating each backbone into a model, and running generate_dataset() over fixed random seeds so every dataset carries its transcriptomic count matrix plus ground-truth trajectory and cellwise gene regulatory network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Generate reproducible simulated single-cell datasets with dyngen by enumerating predefined trajectory backbones, instantiating each backbone into a model, and running generate_dataset() over fixed random seeds so every dataset carries its transcriptomic count matrix plus ground-truth trajectory and cellwise gene regulatory network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires real biological data rather than synthetic data with known ground truth (dyngen simulations assume well-mixed, independent cells and do not capture inter-cellular dependencies). The target method needs simulator features dyngen does not provide, e.g. benchmarking of clustering or differential-expression methods for which protocol-specific simulators such as Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim were designed. Only a single arbitrary topology is needed without controlled backbone variety or seed-level reproducibility — a simpler one-off simulation suffices.
