skills.search_text: senescence-signature-importance-weighting Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes with a SenePy senescence hub signature and you want per-gene contributions scaled by hub-network connectivity rather than treating all signature genes equally. When you deliberately want scanpy.score_genes-equivalent behavior (equal gene weighting on continuous, normalized, log-transformed expression) — then pass binarize=False, importance=False instead. When using the Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt universal signature files, which carry no importance weights; obtain weighted genes from merge_hubs instead. When the AnnData matrix has been scaled (z-scored), which violates score_hub's input expectation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Weights each gene in a SenePy cellular senescence signature by its number of connections in the hub gene network, so that highly connected hub genes contribute more to per-cell senescence scores. This is the default behavior of senePy's score_hub and distinguishes SenePy scoring from plain scanpy.score_genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Weights each gene in a SenePy cellular senescence signature by its number of connections in the hub gene network, so that highly connected hub genes contribute more to per-cell senescence scores. This is the default behavior of senePy's score_hub and distinguishes SenePy scoring from plain scanpy.score_genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you deliberately want scanpy.score_genes-equivalent behavior (equal gene weighting on continuous, normalized, log-transformed expression) — then pass binarize=False, importance=False instead. When using the Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt universal signature files, which carry no importance weights; obtain weighted genes from merge_hubs instead. When the AnnData matrix has been scaled (z-scored), which violates score_hub's input expectation.

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics spots or single-cell transcriptomes must be scored for senescence using cell-type-specific hub signatures (e.g., mapping senescence burden onto Visium sections or with fibrosis markers like Col1a1).
skills.name: senescence-signature-scoring-of-spatial-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: senescence-signature-scoring-of-spatial-transcriptomics Use when spatial transcriptomics spots or single-cell transcriptomes must be scored for senescence using cell-type-specific hub signatures (e.g., mapping senescence burden onto Visium sections or with fibrosis markers like Col1a1). The AnnData expression matrix is already scaled — score_hub's default binarization assumes raw or normalized (optionally log-transformed) data, not scaled data The goal is scoring with plain scanpy.score_genes behavior — you would pass binarize=False, importance=False after normalize_total and log1p, which changes the method rather than applying this skill's default weighted-binarized scoring You only need a universal signature without importance weights — the README warns universal signatures have no importance weights; use merge_hubs if weights are needed, or a different approach http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Scores spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g., 10x Visium) for cellular senescence using SenePy's cell-type-specific weighted senescence hub signatures, then aggregates per-hub scores into a composite senescence burden for downstream spatial colocalization and autocorrelation analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Scores spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g., 10x Visium) for cellular senescence using SenePy's cell-type-specific weighted senescence hub signatures, then aggregates per-hub scores into a composite senescence burden for downstream spatial colocalization and autocorrelation analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The AnnData expression matrix is already scaled — score_hub's default binarization assumes raw or normalized (optionally log-transformed) data, not scaled data The goal is scoring with plain scanpy.score_genes behavior — you would pass binarize=False, importance=False after normalize_total and log1p, which changes the method rather than applying this skill's default weighted-binarized scoring You only need a universal signature without importance weights — the README warns universal signatures have no importance weights; use merge_hubs if weights are needed, or a different approach

skills.description: Use when you have CCIVR Table.csv output containing cis-NAT pairs with expression profiling columns (fold_change, padj) and need to tabulate pair counts per expression combination to find inversely correlated (down-up) pairs.
skills.name: sense-antisense-expression-combination-annotation
skills.search_text: sense-antisense-expression-combination-annotation Use when you have CCIVR Table.csv output containing cis-NAT pairs with expression profiling columns (fold_change, padj) and need to tabulate pair counts per expression combination to find inversely correlated (down-up) pairs. Input lacks RNA-seq expression profiling columns (fold_change, padj) — CCIVR can extract cis-NATs structurally, but expression-combination classification is impossible without expression data Analysis requires de novo transcriptome assembly or strand-specific error-rate modeling rather than annotation-based cis-NAT extraction (use NATpipe or NASTI-seq instead) Gene annotation (structure and strand direction) accuracy in the source database is questionable, since CCIVR prediction quality depends entirely on it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Classifies cis-NAT pairs extracted by CCIVR into expression-combination categories (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT) using the fold_change and padj columns of the CCIVR output table, enabling identification of inversely correlated sense-antisense pairs such as BCAR3-AS1/BCAR3 and GPX2/CHURC1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Classifies cis-NAT pairs extracted by CCIVR into expression-combination categories (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per structural type (EB, FO, HH, TT) using the fold_change and padj columns of the CCIVR output table, enabling identification of inversely correlated sense-antisense pairs such as BCAR3-AS1/BCAR3 and GPX2/CHURC1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks RNA-seq expression profiling columns (fold_change, padj) — CCIVR can extract cis-NATs structurally, but expression-combination classification is impossible without expression data Analysis requires de novo transcriptome assembly or strand-specific error-rate modeling rather than annotation-based cis-NAT extraction (use NATpipe or NASTI-seq instead) Gene annotation (structure and strand direction) accuracy in the source database is questionable, since CCIVR prediction quality depends entirely on it

skills.search_text: sensitivity-ppv-benchmark-evaluation Use when quantifying the detection limit of a genotype/chimerism assignment method — e.g. how low a minor donor fraction SNV-based assignment can detect in single-cell UMI count data. Input is a gene expression feature matrix rather than allele-level SNV UMI counts — this skill benchmarks genotype assignment, not expression deconvolution SNVs have not passed the genotype-assignment filters (>=2 cell barcodes, SNV Qual >=30, base Qual >=1); unfiltered calls will inflate error rates The goal is calling chimerism in a real clinical sample rather than establishing a detection limit via synthetic/in silico mixtures http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark the SNV-based single-cell genotype-assignment method by constructing in silico donor mixtures, running Gibbs-sampled K=1/K=2 model comparisons, and tabulating minor-genotype detection sensitivity and positive predictive value across mixing ratios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Benchmark the SNV-based single-cell genotype-assignment method by constructing in silico donor mixtures, running Gibbs-sampled K=1/K=2 model comparisons, and tabulating minor-genotype detection sensitivity and positive predictive value across mixing ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene expression feature matrix rather than allele-level SNV UMI counts — this skill benchmarks genotype assignment, not expression deconvolution SNVs have not passed the genotype-assignment filters (>=2 cell barcodes, SNV Qual >=30, base Qual >=1); unfiltered calls will inflate error rates The goal is calling chimerism in a real clinical sample rather than establishing a detection limit via synthetic/in silico mixtures

skills.name: sensitivity-specificity-computation
skills.search_text: sensitivity-specificity-computation Use when reproducing or validating malignant-cell-identification benchmarks on labeled scRNA-seq test sets (e.g., test_cancerCellLine.h5ad and test_TabulaSapiens.h5ad) where ground-truth malignant/normal labels exist and method sensitivity/specificity must be quantified. The dataset lacks ground-truth malignant/normal labels, so sensitivity and specificity cannot be computed — use unsupervised evaluation instead. The goal is patient-derived tumor annotation rather than the gold-standard cell-line/non-cancer-donor benchmark; the article notes scMalignantFinder is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages only. Analyzing cancers with unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors), where the tool's capabilities are explicitly untested. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark protocol for computing sensitivity and specificity of malignant-cell classifiers against gold-standard scRNA-seq labels (cancer cell lines vs. non-cancer donor epithelium) and comparing the reproduced values with reported benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks ground-truth malignant/normal labels, so sensitivity and specificity cannot be computed — use unsupervised evaluation instead. The goal is patient-derived tumor annotation rather than the gold-standard cell-line/non-cancer-donor benchmark; the article notes scMalignantFinder is designed to identify malignant cells from cancerous lineages only. Analyzing cancers with unknown or controversial origins (e.g., synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors), where the tool's capabilities are explicitly untested.

skills.description: Use when protein or lncRNA sequences of variable length must be transformed into fixed-length CNN-compatible inputs for lncRNA-protein interaction prediction or similar sequence-pair classification.
skills.name: sequence-copy-padding-encoding
skills.search_text: sequence-copy-padding-encoding Use when protein or lncRNA sequences of variable length must be transformed into fixed-length CNN-compatible inputs for lncRNA-protein interaction prediction or similar sequence-pair classification. All experimental sequences already fall within the fixed length range and can be encoded directly without the copy-padding/cropping step. The goal is predicting a new lncRNA-protein pair (Run_LPI_CNNCP_model(Y_crop_LPI=False, N_crop_LPI=False, Independent=True)) rather than encoding sequences for cross-validation training/evaluation. A non-CNN classifier is used, since the copy-padding trick exists specifically to satisfy the fixed-size input requirements of the convolutional neural network. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encodes variable-length protein/RNA sequences for convolutional neural network input by applying the LPI-CNNCP copy-padding trick followed by high-order one-hot encoding, producing fixed-length, image-like, non-independent inputs that satisfy CNN dimensionality requirements. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ab.2020.113767
skills.summary: Encodes variable-length protein/RNA sequences for convolutional neural network input by applying the LPI-CNNCP copy-padding trick followed by high-order one-hot encoding, producing fixed-length, image-like, non-independent inputs that satisfy CNN dimensionality requirements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All experimental sequences already fall within the fixed length range and can be encoded directly without the copy-padding/cropping step. The goal is predicting a new lncRNA-protein pair (Run_LPI_CNNCP_model(Y_crop_LPI=False, N_crop_LPI=False, Independent=True)) rather than encoding sequences for cross-validation training/evaluation. A non-CNN classifier is used, since the copy-padding trick exists specifically to satisfy the fixed-size input requirements of the convolutional neural network.

skills.description: Use when measuring how query time/throughput on a large sequence-database index changes with index configuration (e.g., zero/one/two Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) across query batches of similar, dissimilar, and random sequences.
skills.name: sequence-database-query-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sequence-database-query-benchmarking Use when measuring how query time/throughput on a large sequence-database index changes with index configuration (e.g., zero/one/two Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) across query batches of similar, dissimilar, and random sequences. The analysis goal is exact sequence alignment or full similarity search rather than approximate membership queries listing datasets that may contain a sequence (BLAST-like search is out of PAC's scope). The index structures under comparison are not AMQ/Bloom-filter based (e.g., benchmarking HowDeSBT/Cobs requires their own CLIs, not PAC's -l/-q interface). Only one query batch is available, so no similar-vs-dissimilar contrast can be made and Bloom filter acceleration cannot be meaningfully evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmarks query throughput of an AMQ index (PAC, built with Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) over collections of genome/transcriptome datasets, comparing index configurations across query batches of varying similarity. Grounded in the PAC paper's ablation showing several-fold speedups on dissimilar batches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Benchmarks query throughput of an AMQ index (PAC, built with Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) over collections of genome/transcriptome datasets, comparing index configurations across query batches of varying similarity. Grounded in the PAC paper's ablation showing several-fold speedups on dissimilar batches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is exact sequence alignment or full similarity search rather than approximate membership queries listing datasets that may contain a sequence (BLAST-like search is out of PAC's scope). The index structures under comparison are not AMQ/Bloom-filter based (e.g., benchmarking HowDeSBT/Cobs requires their own CLIs, not PAC's -l/-q interface). Only one query batch is available, so no similar-vs-dissimilar contrast can be made and Bloom filter acceleration cannot be meaningfully evaluated.

skills.description: Use when you need to determine which of thousands of indexed FASTA/FASTQ datasets contain a query sequence, and how many k-mers the query shares with each dataset.
skills.name: sequence-dataset-query-scoring
skills.search_text: sequence-dataset-query-scoring Use when you need to determine which of thousands of indexed FASTA/FASTQ datasets contain a query sequence, and how many k-mers the query shares with each dataset. You need exact alignment-level search results or full sequence alignment scores — PAC is an approximate membership query (AMQ) structure that lists candidate datasets, not a BLAST replacement for alignment The target collection has fewer datasets than could be searched directly with BLAST-like methods against a small number of genomes, where index construction overhead is not justified The query calls for positions or locations of matches within datasets — PAC only reports which datasets contain the sequence and shared k-mer counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run queries against a PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb tree) index so that each query sequence returns an n-sized bit vector of per-dataset hits plus a score vector counting shared k-mers with each indexed dataset, enabling approximate membership screening of a sequence against thousands of files. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Run queries against a PAC (Partitioned Aggregated Bloom Comb tree) index so that each query sequence returns an n-sized bit vector of per-dataset hits plus a score vector counting shared k-mers with each indexed dataset, enabling approximate membership screening of a sequence against thousands of files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need exact alignment-level search results or full sequence alignment scores — PAC is an approximate membership query (AMQ) structure that lists candidate datasets, not a BLAST replacement for alignment The target collection has fewer datasets than could be searched directly with BLAST-like methods against a small number of genomes, where index construction overhead is not justified The query calls for positions or locations of matches within datasets — PAC only reports which datasets contain the sequence and shared k-mer counts

skills.description: Use when building RNA modification (m5C) predictors that need fused informatic sequence profiles from raw FASTA-like training sequences before classifier training or F-score feature selection.
skills.name: sequence-feature-encoding-pseudonucleotide-composition
skills.search_text: sequence-feature-encoding-pseudonucleotide-composition Use when building RNA modification (m5C) predictors that need fused informatic sequence profiles from raw FASTA-like training sequences before classifier training or F-score feature selection. Input is already a numeric feature table — encoding would be redundant The goal is cross-species prediction with a single general model — the paper found species-specific models are necessary ('it could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction') Predicting m5C in species other than A. thaliana or M. musculus, since only 'Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse' are accepted by the released predictor http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Encode RNA sequences into numeric feature vectors using four complementary schemes — position-specific propensity (PSP), k-mer (k=1,2,3), parallel correlation pseudo dinucleotide composition (PCPseDNC), and electron-ion interaction pseudo potentials of trinucleotide (PseEIIP) — as the fused input representation for the Staem5 m5C site prediction model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Encode RNA sequences into numeric feature vectors using four complementary schemes — position-specific propensity (PSP), k-mer (k=1,2,3), parallel correlation pseudo dinucleotide composition (PCPseDNC), and electron-ion interaction pseudo potentials of trinucleotide (PseEIIP) — as the fused input representation for the Staem5 m5C site prediction model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table — encoding would be redundant The goal is cross-species prediction with a single general model — the paper found species-specific models are necessary ('it could be difficult to develop a general model for cross-species prediction') Predicting m5C in species other than A. thaliana or M. musculus, since only 'Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse' are accepted by the released predictor

skills.name: sequence-fragment-alignment-and-centering
skills.search_text: sequence-fragment-alignment-and-centering Use when you need to test whether m5C-containing fragments show distinctive sequence motifs vs non-m5C fragments by comparing per-position nucleotide enrichment across cytosine-centered, equal-length flanking sequences. Fragments are variable-length or lack a shared anchor, so no cytosine-centered coordinate frame (e.g., -18 to -1 upstream indexing) can be defined across sequences The goal is m5C site prediction rather than motif characterization — in that case use the Staem5 predictor (m5C_predict.py) instead of descriptive logo analysis Input is already a per-position feature table or encoded features (PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP); alignment/centering has already been done http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns m5C-positive and m5C-negative RNA fragments (e.g., the 41-bp Staem5 training windows for A. thaliana and M. musculus) with the candidate cytosine centered, so per-position nucleotide frequency differences can be computed and rendered as two-sample logos. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Aligns m5C-positive and m5C-negative RNA fragments (e.g., the 41-bp Staem5 training windows for A. thaliana and M. musculus) with the candidate cytosine centered, so per-position nucleotide frequency differences can be computed and rendered as two-sample logos.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Fragments are variable-length or lack a shared anchor, so no cytosine-centered coordinate frame (e.g., -18 to -1 upstream indexing) can be defined across sequences The goal is m5C site prediction rather than motif characterization — in that case use the Staem5 predictor (m5C_predict.py) instead of descriptive logo analysis Input is already a per-position feature table or encoded features (PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP); alignment/centering has already been done

skills.description: Use when reads in UMI libraries show mapping shifts and you need to test whether cluster size correlates with sequence complexity, e.g. computing Shannon Entropy and Mutual Information per UMI-read cluster in run_171108.
skills.name: sequence-information-theory-analysis
skills.search_text: sequence-information-theory-analysis Use when reads in UMI libraries show mapping shifts and you need to test whether cluster size correlates with sequence complexity, e.g. computing Shannon Entropy and Mutual Information per UMI-read cluster in run_171108. Input data lack UMI information entirely — in the absence of UMI the mapping shift artefact is undetectable and cluster-size stratification cannot be built The goal is to conclusively attribute mapping shifts to PCR stutter — the article warns that shifts can occur with reads of normal or high entropy, so entropy metrics alone cannot establish mechanism The data set is very small — the article notes that possibly larger data sets are needed to observe meaningful trends in these metrics and in visible repeat content http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Computes Shannon Entropy over nucleotide sequences and Mutual Information between base positions of modal reads in UMI-read clusters, then tests whether these information-theory metrics vary systematically with UMI-read cluster size using one-way ANOVA, to characterize low-entropy/tandem-repeat tendencies of reads exhibiting the UMI mapping shift artefact. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-31064-7
skills.summary: Computes Shannon Entropy over nucleotide sequences and Mutual Information between base positions of modal reads in UMI-read clusters, then tests whether these information-theory metrics vary systematically with UMI-read cluster size using one-way ANOVA, to characterize low-entropy/tandem-repeat tendencies of reads exhibiting the UMI mapping shift artefact.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lack UMI information entirely — in the absence of UMI the mapping shift artefact is undetectable and cluster-size stratification cannot be built The goal is to conclusively attribute mapping shifts to PCR stutter — the article warns that shifts can occur with reads of normal or high entropy, so entropy metrics alone cannot establish mechanism The data set is very small — the article notes that possibly larger data sets are needed to observe meaningful trends in these metrics and in visible repeat content

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be turned into fixed-length autoregressive token sequences for tGPT: rank genes by descending expression, tokenize, and pad/truncate to 64 or 128 tokens.
skills.name: sequence-padding-truncation
skills.search_text: sequence-padding-truncation Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be turned into fixed-length autoregressive token sequences for tGPT: rank genes by descending expression, tokenize, and pad/truncate to 64 or 128 tokens. Input is already a feature/embedding table or tokenized sequences — re-ranking and re-tokenizing would discard or corrupt existing representations. You need actual expression magnitudes or fold changes: tGPT uses only gene expression rankings, so 'the fold changes among genes are neglected and this can affect biological interpretation.' Analysis targets low-expressing genes: 'tGPT uses only the top-expressing genes; therefore, it may miss the information that is specifically represented within the low-expressing genes.' http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Converts per-cell ranked gene-symbol sequences into fixed-length token sequences for tGPT by replacing '-'/'.' with underscores, wrapping with [<s>, G1, ..., <e>] special tokens, and padding/truncating to a max_len of 64 (62 genes) or 128 (126 genes) with HuggingFace PreTrainedTokenizerFast. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Converts per-cell ranked gene-symbol sequences into fixed-length token sequences for tGPT by replacing '-'/'.' with underscores, wrapping with [<s>, G1, ..., <e>] special tokens, and padding/truncating to a max_len of 64 (62 genes) or 128 (126 genes) with HuggingFace PreTrainedTokenizerFast.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/embedding table or tokenized sequences — re-ranking and re-tokenizing would discard or corrupt existing representations. You need actual expression magnitudes or fold changes: tGPT uses only gene expression rankings, so 'the fold changes among genes are neglected and this can affect biological interpretation.' Analysis targets low-expressing genes: 'tGPT uses only the top-expressing genes; therefore, it may miss the information that is specifically represented within the low-expressing genes.'

skills.description: Use when a set of sequencing reads must be searched against a pre-built Raptor IBF/MIBF index over 64 or 1,024 bins, and run time, memory, and bin-assignment accuracy must be measured per index size.
skills.name: sequence-read-query-execution
skills.search_text: sequence-read-query-execution Use when a set of sequencing reads must be searched against a pre-built Raptor IBF/MIBF index over 64 or 1,024 bins, and run time, memory, and bin-assignment accuracy must be measured per index size. The target index was built with an older Raptor version, since indices built with an older version cannot be used with version 2.0.0 The reference sequences have highly uneven bin sizes or very many bins, which Raptor explicitly identifies as its main limiting factor http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Executes approximate sequence search of large query sets (e.g. 2^20 NGS reads) against Raptor binning-directory indices built from interleaved Bloom filters (IBF/MIBF), recording search time, peak RAM, and false-positive bin assignments across index configurations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Executes approximate sequence search of large query sets (e.g. 2^20 NGS reads) against Raptor binning-directory indices built from interleaved Bloom filters (IBF/MIBF), recording search time, peak RAM, and false-positive bin assignments across index configurations.

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing approximate sequence search tools (Raptor, COBS, Mantis) over large binned nucleotide collections and you need construction time, search speed, RAM/disk, and specificity measurements.
skills.name: sequence-search-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sequence-search-benchmarking Use when evaluating or comparing approximate sequence search tools (Raptor, COBS, Mantis) over large binned nucleotide collections and you need construction time, search speed, RAM/disk, and specificity measurements. When your goal is a single-tool deployment rather than a head-to-head speed/memory/FP comparison of Raptor, COBS, and Mantis When the input is a real, unevenly sized collection with a very high number of bins — Raptor's own discussion flags uneven bin sizes and high bin counts as its main limiting factors, so a benchmark on the artificial dataset would not represent that regime When edit-distance-tolerant search against un-binned, small references is needed — full-text/FM-index approaches may be more appropriate than pre-filter benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking of approximate nucleotide sequence search tools (Raptor, COBS, Mantis) on binned reference collections, recording index construction time, search time, memory/disk usage, and false positives so pre-filter performance can be compared fairly. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102782
skills.summary: Benchmarking of approximate nucleotide sequence search tools (Raptor, COBS, Mantis) on binned reference collections, recording index construction time, search time, memory/disk usage, and false positives so pre-filter performance can be compared fairly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When your goal is a single-tool deployment rather than a head-to-head speed/memory/FP comparison of Raptor, COBS, and Mantis When the input is a real, unevenly sized collection with a very high number of bins — Raptor's own discussion flags uneven bin sizes and high bin counts as its main limiting factors, so a benchmark on the artificial dataset would not represent that regime When edit-distance-tolerant search against un-binned, small references is needed — full-text/FM-index approaches may be more appropriate than pre-filter benchmarks

skills.description: Use when curating RNA/DNA sequence benchmark sets for ML training and testing where redundant sequences could cause overfitting, and a similarity cutoff (e.g. <80%) must be enforced per dataset.
skills.name: sequence-similarity-clustering
skills.search_text: sequence-similarity-clustering Use when curating RNA/DNA sequence benchmark sets for ML training and testing where redundant sequences could cause overfitting, and a similarity cutoff (e.g. <80%) must be enforced per dataset. Input sequences are already known to be non-redundant or were previously CD-HIT-processed at the target cutoff — re-clustering wastes time and may over-prune. The downstream task tolerates high sequence redundancy (e.g. per-read variant calling on native transcripts) rather than benchmark curation for a supervised classifier. http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Deduplicate nucleotide sequence benchmark datasets by clustering sequences with CD-HIT so that pairwise sequence similarity stays below a specified cutoff (here <80%), preventing redundant near-identical sequences from inflating classifier performance in tissue-specific m6A prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Deduplicate nucleotide sequence benchmark datasets by clustering sequences with CD-HIT so that pairwise sequence similarity stays below a specified cutoff (here <80%), preventing redundant near-identical sequences from inflating classifier performance in tissue-specific m6A prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are already known to be non-redundant or were previously CD-HIT-processed at the target cutoff — re-clustering wastes time and may over-prune. The downstream task tolerates high sequence redundancy (e.g. per-read variant calling on native transcripts) rather than benchmark curation for a supervised classifier.

skills.description: Use when you have a uniform-format list of miRNA/precursor candidates (output from miRNATranslate in iwa-miRNA's Galaxy framework) and need to prioritize true positives before manual curation.
skills.name: sequence-structure-expression-feature-based-mirna-selection
skills.search_text: sequence-structure-expression-feature-based-mirna-selection Use when you have a uniform-format list of miRNA/precursor candidates (output from miRNATranslate in iwa-miRNA's Galaxy framework) and need to prioritize true positives before manual curation. sRNA-Seq data are from a species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA cannot handle such data in the current version Candidate miRNAs must be discovered from reads that do not map to the reference genome — these reads are ignored by the current version The goal is downstream enrichment analysis (GO annotation, miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparative analysis of already selected miRNAs — these are out of scope for the MiRNA Selection module http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 The MiRNA Selection module of iwa-miRNA screens an aggregated list of annotated and newly predicted miRNA precursors using two parallel mechanisms — a high-throughput (HT) criteria filter and a one-class SVM classifier built on sequence, structure (MFE/AMFE), and expression features from sRNA-Seq data — each run with default parameters to label promising candidates (e.g., Ara-Set1 and Ara-Set2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: The MiRNA Selection module of iwa-miRNA screens an aggregated list of annotated and newly predicted miRNA precursors using two parallel mechanisms — a high-throughput (HT) criteria filter and a one-class SVM classifier built on sequence, structure (MFE/AMFE), and expression features from sRNA-Seq data — each run with default parameters to label promising candidates (e.g., Ara-Set1 and Ara-Set2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: sRNA-Seq data are from a species without a reference genome — iwa-miRNA cannot handle such data in the current version Candidate miRNAs must be discovered from reads that do not map to the reference genome — these reads are ignored by the current version The goal is downstream enrichment analysis (GO annotation, miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparative analysis of already selected miRNAs — these are out of scope for the MiRNA Selection module

skills.description: Use when input is raw (untransformed) NGS/RNA-seq expression data (e.g., TCGA, GTEx count-style feature tables) showing high variance in high-read-count features, and a preprocessing/normalization choice must be made before correlation analysis.
skills.name: sequencing-artifact-heteroskedasticity-assessment
skills.search_text: sequencing-artifact-heteroskedasticity-assessment Use when input is raw (untransformed) NGS/RNA-seq expression data (e.g., TCGA, GTEx count-style feature tables) showing high variance in high-read-count features, and a preprocessing/normalization choice must be made before correlation analysis. Data are already log2-transformed (e.g., the packaged logTCGA40 object) — re-transforming would distort the values Data derive from microarray experiments where log2 is not the indicated transformation among the package's three options (log2, z-score) Input is single-cell count data requiring prior read count filtration for non-viable cells and low-abundance genes before transformation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Applies log2 transformation (via FeatureCorr::data_transform) to sequencing-derived expression data to reduce PCR artifacts and heteroskedasticity — high variation in features with high signal or read count — and verifies the effect with before/after distribution plots. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100144
skills.summary: Applies log2 transformation (via FeatureCorr::data_transform) to sequencing-derived expression data to reduce PCR artifacts and heteroskedasticity — high variation in features with high signal or read count — and verifies the effect with before/after distribution plots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already log2-transformed (e.g., the packaged logTCGA40 object) — re-transforming would distort the values Data derive from microarray experiments where log2 is not the indicated transformation among the package's three options (log2, z-score) Input is single-cell count data requiring prior read count filtration for non-viable cells and low-abundance genes before transformation

skills.search_text: sequencing-cost-estimation Use when a semi-profiling workflow needs a defensible dollar figure for sequencing only representative samples versus the whole cohort, or when judging whether the 1/10–1/3 cost-savings target of scSemiProfiler was achieved. skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-fold-change-simulation Use when validating that a single-cell cluster-purity metric (e.g., ROGUE) is insensitive to sequencing-depth fold changes between replicates or to variation in cell number, by simulating replicate mixtures and comparing ROGUE/S against silhouette. The goal is to compare clustering algorithms (e.g., GiniClust, GiniClust2, RaceID3) rather than to validate the robustness of a purity metric to technical depth differences The data are integrated cell populations from different protocols and platforms — the article explicitly notes ROGUE does not yet assess purity of such integrated populations (proposed future work) The input is already a real experimental dataset where the 0.9 purity threshold or a data-derived global ROGUE threshold should be applied directly instead of running simulations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulate two-replicate pure single-cell populations with 2- to 100-fold sequencing-depth differences and cell-number down-sampling, then verify with the ROGUE entropy statistic that the purity metric stays robust (~0.99-1) while a conventional metric like silhouette varies (0.25-0.75). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3

skills.name: sequencing-depth-perturbation-analysis
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-perturbation-analysis Use when a single-cell velocity model's outputs must be shown stable under technical noise, specifically when perturbing raw count matrices by downsampling to reduced sequencing-depth proportions. Input is not raw counts (e.g., normalized or dimensionality-reduced data), since downsampling to a percentage of total counts requires raw integer UMI counts The scKINETICS mask or parameters would be re-optimized per trial, which confounds the depth perturbation with model refitting and invalidates the comparison The goal is biological, not technical, perturbation analysis — downsampling only simulates reduced sequencing depth, not real biological variation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A robustness test for scKINETICS velocity estimates that randomly downsamples raw single-cell counts to simulate reduced transcript capture depth, refits the model, and quantifies cosine deviation of perturbed velocities from the original fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A robustness test for scKINETICS velocity estimates that randomly downsamples raw single-cell counts to simulate reduced transcript capture depth, refits the model, and quantifies cosine deviation of perturbed velocities from the original fit.

skills.description: Use when a large single-cell dataset with deposited predefined cell labels is available and you need to quantify whether per-cell UMI counts (sequencing depth) bias the accuracy of an automatic annotation tool such as deCS.correlation().
skills.name: sequencing-depth-stratified-recall-evaluation
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-stratified-recall-evaluation Use when a large single-cell dataset with deposited predefined cell labels is available and you need to quantify whether per-cell UMI counts (sequencing depth) bias the accuracy of an automatic annotation tool such as deCS.correlation(). The query dataset lacks deposited predefined cell labels, so recall cannot be computed and only annotation output is possible Cell type annotation is intended at cluster level rather than single-cell resolution, since this skill evaluates per-cell depth effects The tissue or cell types of interest are not represented in the available reference panels (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF), which the article notes may bias annotation results http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates how sequencing depth affects automatic cell type annotation accuracy by splitting scRNA-seq cells into low/median/high UMI-count groups and computing annotation recall against predefined labels. The deCS paper applied this to 63,103 bronchoalveolar immune cells (BICs) from COVID-19 patients to show low-depth cells are annotated only slightly less accurately. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001

skills.description: Use when evaluating how an estimator (e.g., allelic proportion or expression estimates) performs at reduced sequencing depth, by simulating low-coverage data via random per-cell read down-sampling from full-depth counts.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-variance-simulation
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-variance-simulation Use when evaluating how an estimator (e.g., allelic proportion or expression estimates) performs at reduced sequencing depth, by simulating low-coverage data via random per-cell read down-sampling from full-depth counts. The input data is already low-coverage — down-sampling would discard information without serving an evaluation purpose The goal is differential-expression or burst-kinetics testing rather than estimation-precision (MSE) evaluation of allelic proportions UMI-based counts are the target (e.g., Larsson et al. data), since down-sampling reads rather than molecules distorts UMI count semantics http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates low-coverage scRNA-Seq data by random down-sampling of full-depth allele-specific read counts (1% of reads per cell) so that estimator precision — e.g., MSE of allelic proportions under partial pooling — can be evaluated against known full-depth values, as done in scBASE for 122 CAST×B6 blastocyst cells (~147,538 reads/cell). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Generates low-coverage scRNA-Seq data by random down-sampling of full-depth allele-specific read counts (1% of reads per cell) so that estimator precision — e.g., MSE of allelic proportions under partial pooling — can be evaluated against known full-depth values, as done in scBASE for 122 CAST×B6 blastocyst cells (~147,538 reads/cell).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data is already low-coverage — down-sampling would discard information without serving an evaluation purpose The goal is differential-expression or burst-kinetics testing rather than estimation-precision (MSE) evaluation of allelic proportions UMI-based counts are the target (e.g., Larsson et al. data), since down-sampling reads rather than molecules distorts UMI count semantics

skills.description: Use when benchmarking isoform quantification methods (e.g. Longcell, Sicelore2, FLAMES, wf-single-cell, IsoQuant) on simulated Nanopore reads where per-read error processes must be modeled at controlled low/middle/high quality regimes with a ground-truth cell-by-isoform matrix for scoring.
skills.name: sequencing-error-markov-chain-modeling
skills.search_text: sequencing-error-markov-chain-modeling Use when benchmarking isoform quantification methods (e.g. Longcell, Sicelore2, FLAMES, wf-single-cell, IsoQuant) on simulated Nanopore reads where per-read error processes must be modeled at controlled low/middle/high quality regimes with a ground-truth cell-by-isoform matrix for scoring. Input is real Nanopore FASTQ data rather than a simulation — the gold-standard-correlation scoring this error model enables does not apply Short-read (Illumina) data, where error profiles and 10x 5'-attached full-length-read structure differ from the Nanopore four-state chain modeled here Evaluating biological splicing variation (e.g. isoform switching mechanisms) rather than computational-method accuracy under controlled error regimes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation approach from the Longcell paper that models Nanopore sequencing as a four-state Markov chain (correct/insertion/deletion/wrong-base) at low, middle, and high quality transition matrices, layered onto simulated full-length transcripts so that single-cell isoform quantification methods can be benchmarked against a known gold-standard expression matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: A simulation approach from the Longcell paper that models Nanopore sequencing as a four-state Markov chain (correct/insertion/deletion/wrong-base) at low, middle, and high quality transition matrices, layered onto simulated full-length transcripts so that single-cell isoform quantification methods can be benchmarked against a known gold-standard expression matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real Nanopore FASTQ data rather than a simulation — the gold-standard-correlation scoring this error model enables does not apply Short-read (Illumina) data, where error profiles and 10x 5'-attached full-length-read structure differ from the Nanopore four-state chain modeled here Evaluating biological splicing variation (e.g. isoform switching mechanisms) rather than computational-method accuracy under controlled error regimes

skills.description: Use when benchmarking or validating UMI recovery/collapse methods (e.g., Longcell iterative clustering vs DBSCAN eps=2) where you need error-laden simulated reads with known ground-truth UMI counts across amplification levels.
skills.name: sequencing-error-read-simulation
skills.search_text: sequencing-error-read-simulation Use when benchmarking or validating UMI recovery/collapse methods (e.g., Longcell iterative clustering vs DBSCAN eps=2) where you need error-laden simulated reads with known ground-truth UMI counts across amplification levels. Input is real Nanopore sequencing data with no ground-truth UMI counts — simulation-based validation is unnecessary and ground truth cannot be verified The downstream method collapses UMIs by whitelist-based cell-barcode-style matching rather than clustering, where error-tolerance behavior is already known Sequencing error is negligible (e.g., short-read Illumina UMI protocols), since inflation under high error is the phenomenon being modeled http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates simulated UMI-bearing read samples (e.g., adapter 10-mers) with Nanopore-like sequencing errors across PCR amplification folds from 2x to 50x, retaining ground-truth UMI counts, so that UMI-collapse/clustering methods can be benchmarked for count inflation under high error rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Generates simulated UMI-bearing read samples (e.g., adapter 10-mers) with Nanopore-like sequencing errors across PCR amplification folds from 2x to 50x, retaining ground-truth UMI counts, so that UMI-collapse/clustering methods can be benchmarked for count inflation under high error rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real Nanopore sequencing data with no ground-truth UMI counts — simulation-based validation is unnecessary and ground truth cannot be verified The downstream method collapses UMIs by whitelist-based cell-barcode-style matching rather than clustering, where error-tolerance behavior is already known Sequencing error is negligible (e.g., short-read Illumina UMI protocols), since inflation under high error is the phenomenon being modeled

skills.description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries have been sequenced on both a patterned-flowcell instrument (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) and a non-patterned control (HiSeq 2500), and you need to quantify or rule out excess inter-sample cell-barcode sharing.
skills.name: sequencing-instrument-swapping-control-comparison
skills.search_text: sequencing-instrument-swapping-control-comparison Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries have been sequenced on both a patterned-flowcell instrument (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) and a non-patterned control (HiSeq 2500), and you need to quantify or rule out excess inter-sample cell-barcode sharing. Data derive from plate-based scRNA-seq (e.g. Smart-seq2) where sample identity is carried by well plate barcodes rather than 10x cell barcodes; use the regression-gradient swapping-fraction estimation instead Only a single sequencing instrument is available, so no HiSeq 2500 negative-control comparison can be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A control-comparison design for detecting barcode swapping artefacts in 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq by testing whether multiplexed samples sequenced on patterned-flowcell instruments (HiSeq 4000) share more cell barcodes than expected by chance, using the same libraries sequenced on HiSeq 2500 as a negative control. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: A control-comparison design for detecting barcode swapping artefacts in 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq by testing whether multiplexed samples sequenced on patterned-flowcell instruments (HiSeq 4000) share more cell barcodes than expected by chance, using the same libraries sequenced on HiSeq 2500 as a negative control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data derive from plate-based scRNA-seq (e.g. Smart-seq2) where sample identity is carried by well plate barcodes rather than 10x cell barcodes; use the regression-gradient swapping-fraction estimation instead Only a single sequencing instrument is available, so no HiSeq 2500 negative-control comparison can be constructed

skills.description: Use when building simulated single-cell sequencing benchmarks that must preserve haplotype structure and amplification artifacts while challenging BAF/phasing-based CNA callers with realistic noise.
skills.name: sequencing-noise-modeling
skills.search_text: sequencing-noise-modeling Use when building simulated single-cell sequencing benchmarks that must preserve haplotype structure and amplification artifacts while challenging BAF/phasing-based CNA callers with realistic noise. The target is detecting real somatic CNAs in experimental scWGS data rather than benchmarking caller sensitivity on known ground truth The simulated cells should reflect clonal CNAs shared across a population of cells — SDX embeds non-clonal, single-cell allele-specific CNAs in haploid-pooled reads Sex chromosomes are out of scope: SCAN2, a dependency in the HiScanner pipeline, explicitly does not support sex chromosomes, and the simulation strategy relies on male haploid X pooling http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Construct realistic simulated scWGS benchmarks by embedding stochastic sequencing noise (Poisson read-depth sampling) and phasing imperfections (phase-switch errors at a controlled 1% rate) into pooled haploid read data, so that allele-specific CNA callers like HiScanner are evaluated under realistic error conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Construct realistic simulated scWGS benchmarks by embedding stochastic sequencing noise (Poisson read-depth sampling) and phasing imperfections (phase-switch errors at a controlled 1% rate) into pooled haploid read data, so that allele-specific CNA callers like HiScanner are evaluated under realistic error conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target is detecting real somatic CNAs in experimental scWGS data rather than benchmarking caller sensitivity on known ground truth The simulated cells should reflect clonal CNAs shared across a population of cells — SDX embeds non-clonal, single-cell allele-specific CNAs in haploid-pooled reads Sex chromosomes are out of scope: SCAN2, a dependency in the HiScanner pipeline, explicitly does not support sex chromosomes, and the simulation strategy relies on male haploid X pooling

skills.description: Use when a barcode-swapping fraction has been estimated on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need a same-libraries control on a non-patterned instrument (HiSeq 2500) to attribute swapping to the sequencer rather than the libraries.
skills.name: sequencing-platform-swap-control-analysis
skills.search_text: sequencing-platform-swap-control-analysis Use when a barcode-swapping fraction has been estimated on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need a same-libraries control on a non-patterned instrument (HiSeq 2500) to attribute swapping to the sequencer rather than the libraries. The libraries were prepared for or sequenced only on non-patterned flow-cell instruments where swapping is expected to be at background — the control adds no discriminating information The analysis goal is demultiplexing or molecule-level de-swapping in 10x Genomics data (use the DropletUtils cell/molecule exclusion algorithm instead of the regression control) Sample-index combinations are unique dual indexes where impossible combinations cannot arise, so the impossible-combination regression cannot be fitted http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A control procedure that quantifies the barcode-swapped read fraction attributable to a specific sequencing platform by repeating the impossible-combination regression on the same libraries sequenced on an alternative instrument (e.g. HiSeq 2500 vs HiSeq 4000), isolating patterned-flow-cell-specific swapping from library-preparation effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: A control procedure that quantifies the barcode-swapped read fraction attributable to a specific sequencing platform by repeating the impossible-combination regression on the same libraries sequenced on an alternative instrument (e.g. HiSeq 2500 vs HiSeq 4000), isolating patterned-flow-cell-specific swapping from library-preparation effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The libraries were prepared for or sequenced only on non-patterned flow-cell instruments where swapping is expected to be at background — the control adds no discriminating information The analysis goal is demultiplexing or molecule-level de-swapping in 10x Genomics data (use the DropletUtils cell/molecule exclusion algorithm instead of the regression control) Sample-index combinations are unique dual indexes where impossible combinations cannot arise, so the impossible-combination regression cannot be fitted

skills.description: Use when a cell type classifier trained on 10x 3'/5' scRNA-seq must be evaluated on cells from other sequencing protocols (STRT-seq, Smart-seq2, BD Rhapsody Targeted mRNA) to quantify protocol-specific generalization loss.
skills.name: sequencing-protocol-stratified-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sequencing-protocol-stratified-benchmarking Use when a cell type classifier trained on 10x 3'/5' scRNA-seq must be evaluated on cells from other sequencing protocols (STRT-seq, Smart-seq2, BD Rhapsody Targeted mRNA) to quantify protocol-specific generalization loss. When the goal is in-distribution benchmarking on holdout 10X data only (the donor-based split), not cross-protocol transfer When author cell type labels are free-text and not mappable to Cell Ontology terms, since the ontology-aware correctness rule (exact match or subtype via child-node lookup) cannot be applied When a protocol group has too few cells to yield a stable macro F1 estimate — the paper's benchmark excluded uncommon assay technologies due to data availability http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark out-of-distribution protocol transfer of a cross-tissue cell type annotation model (scTab/TabNet) by grouping donor-holdout test cells by sequencing assay and computing macro F1 per protocol group. It exposes degradation from 10X-trained inference (~0.8 macro F1) to non-10X protocols (~0.4) as reported in Supp. Fig. 7b. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Benchmark out-of-distribution protocol transfer of a cross-tissue cell type annotation model (scTab/TabNet) by grouping donor-holdout test cells by sequencing assay and computing macro F1 per protocol group. It exposes degradation from 10X-trained inference (~0.8 macro F1) to non-10X protocols (~0.4) as reported in Supp. Fig. 7b.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is in-distribution benchmarking on holdout 10X data only (the donor-based split), not cross-protocol transfer When author cell type labels are free-text and not mappable to Cell Ontology terms, since the ontology-aware correctness rule (exact match or subtype via child-node lookup) cannot be applied When a protocol group has too few cells to yield a stable macro F1 estimate — the paper's benchmark excluded uncommon assay technologies due to data availability

skills.name: sequencing-read-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: sequencing-read-quality-assessment Use when starting a sequencing analysis (DNA-seq or RNA-seq) from raw FASTQ data and the downstream pipeline needs quality-checked, adapter-free, length- and quality-filtered reads before alignment or genotyping. skills.summary: First stage of the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow: assess raw FASTQ quality with FastQC and trim reads with fastp (adapter removal, sliding-window quality trimming, length filtering) before HLA genotyping and variant calling.

skills.search_text: sequencing-read-region-property-checking Use when a seqspec specification (YAML) file for a genomics assay library must be schema-validated before use in preprocessing, or when auditing a curated library of assay specs for missing required Region fields. skills.name: sequencing-read-structure-interpretation
skills.search_text: sequencing-read-structure-interpretation Use when you need to know where a genomics assay encodes its cell barcodes, UMIs, or cDNA across R1/R2 reads and Illumina indices — e.g. before preprocessing with cellatlas/kb, or when a spec must be annotated or validated. The input is already a preprocessed cell-by-feature count matrix (matrix.mtx with barcodes.txt/genes.txt) — structure interpretation is upstream of that and `mx inspect`/`mx filter` apply instead The goal is actual quantification/preprocessing (alignment, barcode correction, UMI counting) — use cellatlas with kb-python rather than spec inspection The assay has no seqspec YAML in the repository's specs/ directory, so no machine-readable library structure is available to render Interprets the machine-readable seqspec YAML of a genomics assay to determine which library elements (cell barcodes, UMIs, cDNA) are encoded in which sequencing read or Illumina index region, rendering per-feature nucleotide lengths. skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a preprocessed cell-by-feature count matrix (matrix.mtx with barcodes.txt/genes.txt) — structure interpretation is upstream of that and `mx inspect`/`mx filter` apply instead The goal is actual quantification/preprocessing (alignment, barcode correction, UMI counting) — use cellatlas with kb-python rather than spec inspection The assay has no seqspec YAML in the repository's specs/ directory, so no machine-readable library structure is available to render

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how deeply the gRNA library was sequenced in a CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen and determine the read depth (e.g. 34%, 59%, 92% saturation) required for reliable gRNA-to-cell assignment.
skills.name: sequencing-saturation-accuracy-benchmarking
skills.search_text: sequencing-saturation-accuracy-benchmarking Use when you need to quantify how deeply the gRNA library was sequenced in a CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen and determine the read depth (e.g. 34%, 59%, 92% saturation) required for reliable gRNA-to-cell assignment. You want to detect CRISPR-Cas9 editing effects in the transcriptome data — that requires GiRAFR's separate editing-effect analysis mode, not the gRNA_mutation downsampling benchmark. You want to identify mutant gRNAs in the full library at a single operating point without assessing depth-dependence — the standard GiRAFR gRNA_mutation pipeline without downsampling suffices. The question is which mutation types or locations are tolerable vs damaging — the article explicitly declares this fine-grained appraisal beyond its scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks how gRNA library sequencing saturation affects single-cell CRISPR screen annotation quality by downsampling the gRNA alignment BAM to fixed fractions, re-running the GiRAFR gRNA_mutation pipeline per level, and plotting annotation accuracy against unique gRNA UMIs recovered per cell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks how gRNA library sequencing saturation affects single-cell CRISPR screen annotation quality by downsampling the gRNA alignment BAM to fixed fractions, re-running the GiRAFR gRNA_mutation pipeline per level, and plotting annotation accuracy against unique gRNA UMIs recovered per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to detect CRISPR-Cas9 editing effects in the transcriptome data — that requires GiRAFR's separate editing-effect analysis mode, not the gRNA_mutation downsampling benchmark. The question is which mutation types or locations are tolerable vs damaging — the article explicitly declares this fine-grained appraisal beyond its scope.

skills.search_text: sequencing-substitution-error-introduction Use when scReadSim has produced synthetic scRNA-seq reads and you need realistic sequencing-error profiles added before benchmarking read-level tools such as UMI deduplication or alignment. skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation classifiers across multiple scRNA-seq datasets generated by different sequencing technologies, to compare accuracy, computational efficiency, and model complexity per method per dataset.

skills.search_text: sequencing-technology-cross-platform-classification-evaluation Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation classifiers across multiple scRNA-seq datasets generated by different sequencing technologies, to compare accuracy, computational efficiency, and model complexity per method per dataset. skills.description: Use when integrating many single-cell RNA-seq datasets (e.g., hundreds of samples, hundreds of thousands of cells) with partial cell type annotations, where batch effects must be corrected while preserving cell-type-specific biology.
skills.name: sequential-batch-correction-with-sample-tree
skills.search_text: sequential-batch-correction-with-sample-tree Use when integrating many single-cell RNA-seq datasets (e.g., hundreds of samples, hundreds of thousands of cells) with partial cell type annotations, where batch effects must be corrected while preserving cell-type-specific biology. skills.search_text: seurat-dataset-alignment-for-label-transfer Use when combining annotated scRNA-seq datasets generated by different labs or sequencing protocols (e.g., Saunders, Zeisel, Tabula Muris) into one classification tree, and per-cell label prediction must transfer across batch-corrected data. scHPL is not a batch correction tool — do not use it in place of Seurat/scVI/scArches integration; datasets must already be aligned before matching cell populations When a new dataset is added, the alignment must be rerun and scHPL rerun with it — avoid this skill if frequent dataset addition without re-alignment is required When cell populations genuinely violate hierarchical relationships (e.g., dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes), a tree-based classifier is inadequate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different labs/protocols into a common feature space (e.g., Seurat-aligned AnnData with the integrated matrix in .X and labels/batch as metadata) before hierarchical progressive-learning label transfer with scHPL, since scHPL matches cell populations across datasets and is not itself a batch correction tool. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Align single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different labs/protocols into a common feature space (e.g., Seurat-aligned AnnData with the integrated matrix in .X and labels/batch as metadata) before hierarchical progressive-learning label transfer with scHPL, since scHPL matches cell populations across datasets and is not itself a batch correction tool.
skills.when_to_use_negative: scHPL is not a batch correction tool — do not use it in place of Seurat/scVI/scArches integration; datasets must already be aligned before matching cell populations When a new dataset is added, the alignment must be rerun and scHPL rerun with it — avoid this skill if frequent dataset addition without re-alignment is required When cell populations genuinely violate hierarchical relationships (e.g., dedifferentiation such as beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes), a tree-based classifier is inadequate

skills.description: Use when investigating why one-against-all differential expression produces pseudo marker genes shared across clusters, or when benchmarking cluster-marker-based annotation accuracy against manually assigned cell type labels on scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: seurat-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: seurat-differential-expression-analysis Use when investigating why one-against-all differential expression produces pseudo marker genes shared across clusters, or when benchmarking cluster-marker-based annotation accuracy against manually assigned cell type labels on scRNA-seq data. When the goal is accurate cell type annotation rather than diagnosing marker gene identification failure — scCATCH's evidence-based scoring is the alternative being benchmarked against When clusters are defined by paired (one-against-one) comparisons, since pseudo marker genes arise specifically from one-against-all methods When the dataset is not clustered — inadequate clustering (too many or few cells per cluster) introduces errors into cell type annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduce Seurat's one-against-all Wilcoxon rank-sum marker gene identification on the Gierahn PBMC dataset to demonstrate how pseudo marker genes (genes upregulated in multiple clusters, e.g. CCL22, SWAP70, KLRF1) arise and degrade cell type annotation consistency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Reproduce Seurat's one-against-all Wilcoxon rank-sum marker gene identification on the Gierahn PBMC dataset to demonstrate how pseudo marker genes (genes upregulated in multiple clusters, e.g. CCL22, SWAP70, KLRF1) arise and degrade cell type annotation consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is accurate cell type annotation rather than diagnosing marker gene identification failure — scCATCH's evidence-based scoring is the alternative being benchmarked against When clusters are defined by paired (one-against-one) comparisons, since pseudo marker genes arise specifically from one-against-all methods When the dataset is not clustered — inadequate clustering (too many or few cells per cluster) introduces errors into cell type annotation

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a raw gene expression matrix (GEM) that has not been transformed by c-CSN — run the c-CSN/CNDM construction skill first, since this skill operates on network degree data The goal is constructing or interpreting the gene-gene association network itself (e.g., direct vs. indirect associations or NFE-based differentiation potency) rather than cell-level dimension reduction and clustering
