skills.name: seurat-dimensionality-reduction-processing
skills.search_text: seurat-dimensionality-reduction-processing Use when raw single-cell counts need to be converted into a Seurat object with normalized, scaled data, variable features, PCA, and a t-SNE or UMAP 2D embedding — e.g. before detecting dubious embeddings or optimizing hyperparameters with scDEED. Input is already a processed Seurat object with the required PCA and 2D reduction — re-running the full pipeline would discard prior normalization choices The desired embedding method is not t-SNE or UMAP via Seurat (scDEED supports these natively; other methods require adapting the pipeline) Data are not single-cell expression counts (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or feature tables), where the Seurat single-cell normalization workflow does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Build and process a Seurat object through the standard scRNA-seq dimensionality-reduction pipeline (CreateSeuratObject, NormalizeData, ScaleData, FindVariableFeatures, RunPCA, then RunTSNE or RunUMAP) so that a pre-embedding space (PCA) and a 2D embedding are available for downstream evaluation, e.g. with scDEED. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Build and process a Seurat object through the standard scRNA-seq dimensionality-reduction pipeline (CreateSeuratObject, NormalizeData, ScaleData, FindVariableFeatures, RunPCA, then RunTSNE or RunUMAP) so that a pre-embedding space (PCA) and a 2D embedding are available for downstream evaluation, e.g. with scDEED.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed Seurat object with the required PCA and 2D reduction — re-running the full pipeline would discard prior normalization choices The desired embedding method is not t-SNE or UMAP via Seurat (scDEED supports these natively; other methods require adapting the pipeline) Data are not single-cell expression counts (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or feature tables), where the Seurat single-cell normalization workflow does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have a Seurat object with cell-level metadata (e.g. 'milestone' bins along a pseudotime trajectory, stimulation time points, or cell-type labels) and need per-population expression matrices to feed into SCPA multisample pathway comparison.
skills.name: seurat-expression-matrix-extraction
skills.search_text: seurat-expression-matrix-extraction Use when you have a Seurat object with cell-level metadata (e.g. 'milestone' bins along a pseudotime trajectory, stimulation time points, or cell-type labels) and need per-population expression matrices to feed into SCPA multisample pathway comparison. Input is a SingleCellExperiment object rather than a Seurat object — use `sce_extract()` / `compare_sce()` instead You already have manually subsetted expression matrices; SCPA accepts these directly in compare_pathways() without seurat_extract You want to run the comparison directly on the full Seurat object without pre-extracting matrices — use `compare_seurat()` instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extract condition- or population-specific expression matrices from a Seurat object using SCPA's `seurat_extract()`, which subsets cells by metadata columns (e.g. timepoint, milestone, cell type) and returns raw or pseudocount-adjusted matrices ready for downstream `compare_pathways()` analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Extract condition- or population-specific expression matrices from a Seurat object using SCPA's `seurat_extract()`, which subsets cells by metadata columns (e.g. timepoint, milestone, cell type) and returns raw or pseudocount-adjusted matrices ready for downstream `compare_pathways()` analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a SingleCellExperiment object rather than a Seurat object — use `sce_extract()` / `compare_sce()` instead You already have manually subsetted expression matrices; SCPA accepts these directly in compare_pathways() without seurat_extract You want to run the comparison directly on the full Seurat object without pre-extracting matrices — use `compare_seurat()` instead

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DEG-prediction methods on artificial single-cell datasets with known/planted DEGs, and you need Seurat FindAllMarkers results — both with default filtering and unfiltered — as a cluster-based comparison baseline.
skills.name: seurat-findallmarkers-filtering-configuration
skills.search_text: seurat-findallmarkers-filtering-configuration Use when benchmarking DEG-prediction methods on artificial single-cell datasets with known/planted DEGs, and you need Seurat FindAllMarkers results — both with default filtering and unfiltered — as a cluster-based comparison baseline. When the goal is DEG prediction without relying on cell clustering — the source study showed singleCellHaystack achieves higher accuracy on artificial datasets and FindAllMarkers depends on cluster definitions that are 'often not straightforward' When input is not a scRNA-seq expression/detection matrix with cell-level metadata, since FindAllMarkers requires clustered Seurat objects rather than a pre-ranked feature table or generic feature matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure and run Seurat's FindAllMarkers, with and without its default filtering, as a clustering-based DEG-prediction baseline whose gene rankings are scored by AUC against planted DEGs when benchmarking methods like singleCellHaystack on artificial scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Configure and run Seurat's FindAllMarkers, with and without its default filtering, as a clustering-based DEG-prediction baseline whose gene rankings are scored by AUC against planted DEGs when benchmarking methods like singleCellHaystack on artificial scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is DEG prediction without relying on cell clustering — the source study showed singleCellHaystack achieves higher accuracy on artificial datasets and FindAllMarkers depends on cluster definitions that are 'often not straightforward' When input is not a scRNA-seq expression/detection matrix with cell-level metadata, since FindAllMarkers requires clustered Seurat objects rather than a pre-ranked feature table or generic feature matrix

skills.description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices with malignant/non-malignant cell annotations from multiple cancer datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) and need a consensus marker gene feature set for cell-type classification.
skills.name: seurat-findmarkers-workflow
skills.search_text: seurat-findmarkers-workflow Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices with malignant/non-malignant cell annotations from multiple cancer datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) and need a consensus marker gene feature set for cell-type classification. You already have a preprocessed, gene-matched, scaled feature matrix ready for classification — use PreCanCell_data() and PreCanCell_classifier() instead of re-deriving DEGs Your goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — this workflow only distinguishes cancer vs non-cancer cells You have only a single dataset — the TMG/NMG sets require intersection across all five training datasets and may not generalize from one cancer type http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A differential expression workflow using Seurat's FindMarkers() (Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Bonferroni correction) to identify genes consistently upregulated in malignant versus non-malignant cells across five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets, yielding tumor marker gene (TMG) and non-malignant marker gene (NMG) feature sets (73 TMGs, 186 NMGs) for the PreCanCell classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: A differential expression workflow using Seurat's FindMarkers() (Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Bonferroni correction) to identify genes consistently upregulated in malignant versus non-malignant cells across five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets, yielding tumor marker gene (TMG) and non-malignant marker gene (NMG) feature sets (73 TMGs, 186 NMGs) for the PreCanCell classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a preprocessed, gene-matched, scaled feature matrix ready for classification — use PreCanCell_data() and PreCanCell_classifier() instead of re-deriving DEGs Your goal is annotating non-cancer cell subpopulations (immune, stromal, epithelial) — this workflow only distinguishes cancer vs non-cancer cells You have only a single dataset — the TMG/NMG sets require intersection across all five training datasets and may not generalize from one cancer type

skills.description: Use when a pooled multi-sample scRNA-seq experiment has a cell-hashing (HTO) assay stored in a Seurat object and cells must be assigned singlet/doublet/negative hashtag identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes where cutoff calling dominates negative assignment.
skills.name: seurat-hto-assay-processing
skills.search_text: seurat-hto-assay-processing Use when a pooled multi-sample scRNA-seq experiment has a cell-hashing (HTO) assay stored in a Seurat object and cells must be assigned singlet/doublet/negative hashtag identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes where cutoff calling dominates negative assignment. Input samples lack a hashtag/HTO assay entirely (e.g. SNP-only demultiplexing inputs with no cell hashing staining). The goal is genetic-variant (SNP-based) demultiplexing from transcriptome data — that requires genotype clustering methods (demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo), not HTO assay processing. The Seurat object does not contain an assay named 'HTO'; HTOClassification and PlotHTO require assay = 'HTO'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepare and process a Seurat object's HTO assay (hashtag oligo counts) for cell-hashing demultiplexing, including loading the 'HTO' assay, running HTOreader's HTOClassification with CLR or log normalization and automatic or manually specified cutoffs, and inspecting cutoff quality with PlotHTO. This is the prerequisite step for any hashtag-based singlet/doublet/negative calling in the hybrid demultiplexing workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Prepare and process a Seurat object's HTO assay (hashtag oligo counts) for cell-hashing demultiplexing, including loading the 'HTO' assay, running HTOreader's HTOClassification with CLR or log normalization and automatic or manually specified cutoffs, and inspecting cutoff quality with PlotHTO. This is the prerequisite step for any hashtag-based singlet/doublet/negative calling in the hybrid demultiplexing workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples lack a hashtag/HTO assay entirely (e.g. SNP-only demultiplexing inputs with no cell hashing staining). The goal is genetic-variant (SNP-based) demultiplexing from transcriptome data — that requires genotype clustering methods (demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo), not HTO assay processing. The Seurat object does not contain an assay named 'HTO'; HTOClassification and PlotHTO require assay = 'HTO'.

skills.description: Use when a cell-hashing CITE-seq experiment yields a hashtag oligo count matrix (e.g. from CITE-seq-Count) and cells must be assigned to hashed samples with doublet/negative calls, as in gExcite's hashing deconvolution step.
skills.name: seurat-htodemux-singlet-doublet-negative-calling
skills.search_text: seurat-htodemux-singlet-doublet-negative-calling Use when a cell-hashing CITE-seq experiment yields a hashtag oligo count matrix (e.g. from CITE-seq-Count) and cells must be assigned to hashed samples with doublet/negative calls, as in gExcite's hashing deconvolution step. Input is single-cell gene expression or CITE-seq data without hashtag oligo counts — there are no HTOs to deconvolve Samples were not multiplexed via cell hashing (one FASTQ/sample, no hashtag library), so no demultiplexing is needed An existing per-cell sample-assignment table (e.g. hashed_sample_assignments.csv) is already available — reuse it instead of re-running demultiplexing http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Seurat-based demultiplexing of cell-hashing data as implemented in gExcite: hashtag oligo (HTO) counts are normalized per cell and HTODemux-style thresholding classifies each cell as a singlet assigned to a hashed sample, a doublet, or a negative. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: Seurat-based demultiplexing of cell-hashing data as implemented in gExcite: hashtag oligo (HTO) counts are normalized per cell and HTODemux-style thresholding classifies each cell as a singlet assigned to a hashed sample, a doublet, or a negative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell gene expression or CITE-seq data without hashtag oligo counts — there are no HTOs to deconvolve Samples were not multiplexed via cell hashing (one FASTQ/sample, no hashtag library), so no demultiplexing is needed An existing per-cell sample-assignment table (e.g. hashed_sample_assignments.csv) is already available — reuse it instead of re-running demultiplexing

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from two scRNA-seq batches (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 and Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 pancreas data) must be normalized to log-counts before batch correction or before computing Euclidean distances between cells in gene space.
skills.name: seurat-log-count-preprocessing
skills.search_text: seurat-log-count-preprocessing Use when raw UMI count matrices from two scRNA-seq batches (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 and Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 pancreas data) must be normalized to log-counts before batch correction or before computing Euclidean distances between cells in gene space. The input matrices are already log-normalized by a different pipeline and cross-method comparability would be broken by re-normalizing only one arm The downstream method requires raw counts or its own internal normalization (e.g., some deep-learning integrators), making Seurat log-counts an inappropriate common space Only one dataset is present — this skill exists to harmonize two batches prior to integration http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Standardize each input scRNA-seq count matrix with Seurat V3.0 pre-processing to produce log-count matrices that serve as the common input space for BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama integration runs, ensuring all methods operate on identically normalized expression values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Standardize each input scRNA-seq count matrix with Seurat V3.0 pre-processing to produce log-count matrices that serve as the common input space for BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama integration runs, ensuring all methods operate on identically normalized expression values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrices are already log-normalized by a different pipeline and cross-method comparability would be broken by re-normalizing only one arm The downstream method requires raw counts or its own internal normalization (e.g., some deep-learning integrators), making Seurat log-counts an inappropriate common space Only one dataset is present — this skill exists to harmonize two batches prior to integration

skills.description: Use when preparing UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., HCA MantonCB1/MantonBM1 or CITE-seq PBMC) as input to cTP-net protein imputation, after SAVER-X denoising and before running the pre-trained 24-protein model.
skills.name: seurat-lognormalize-preprocessing
skills.search_text: seurat-lognormalize-preprocessing Use when preparing UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., HCA MantonCB1/MantonBM1 or CITE-seq PBMC) as input to cTP-net protein imputation, after SAVER-X denoising and before running the pre-trained 24-protein model. Input expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g., TPM or RPKM) — the article notes such prediction accuracy is unknown and that 'cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based).' Raw (undenoised) counts fed directly to imputation — SAVER-X denoising is strongly recommended, and skipping it degrades correlation by 0.02. Cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the article states imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried on non-hematopoietic cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Seurat default LogNormalize transformation of SAVER-X-denoised scRNA-seq counts to prepare the normalized expression matrix that serves as input to cTP-net surface protein imputation, with feature-space alignment to the pre-trained protein panel via the cTPnet package's preprocess/postprocess functions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Seurat default LogNormalize transformation of SAVER-X-denoised scRNA-seq counts to prepare the normalized expression matrix that serves as input to cTP-net surface protein imputation, with feature-space alignment to the pre-trained protein panel via the cTPnet package's preprocess/postprocess functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g., TPM or RPKM) — the article notes such prediction accuracy is unknown and that 'cTP-net can only apply to count-based expression input (UMI-based).' Raw (undenoised) counts fed directly to imputation — SAVER-X denoising is strongly recommended, and skipping it degrades correlation by 0.02. Cells outside the hematopoietic lineage — the article states imputation of these immune-related markers was not tried on non-hematopoietic cells.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking clustering methods on UMI-based simulated scRNA-seq data — especially detecting a rare subpopulation — and you need a graph-based baseline to compare against k-means on PCA/scVI latent spaces and SIMLR.
skills.name: seurat-louvain-graph-clustering
skills.search_text: seurat-louvain-graph-clustering Use when benchmarking clustering methods on UMI-based simulated scRNA-seq data — especially detecting a rare subpopulation — and you need a graph-based baseline to compare against k-means on PCA/scVI latent spaces and SIMLR. The task is trajectory inference rather than discrete-population clustering — the paper handles trajectories with dynwrap/dynmethods, not this benchmark Input data are non-UMI read counts; the benchmark described targets UMI-protocol simulations (True2ObservedCounts protocol='UMI') http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies Seurat's Louvain graph-based clustering to SymSim-simulated UMI count matrices as one of several clustering baselines (alongside PCA/k-means, scVI/k-means, and SIMLR) for benchmarking rare-population detection, scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against the true population labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Applies Seurat's Louvain graph-based clustering to SymSim-simulated UMI count matrices as one of several clustering baselines (alongside PCA/k-means, scVI/k-means, and SIMLR) for benchmarking rare-population detection, scored by adjusted Rand index (ARI) against the true population labels.

skills.search_text: seurat-louvain-leiden-clustering Use when benchmarking a new scRNA-seq clustering framework (e.g., DeepCCI) against baselines, and you need Seurat Louvain/Leiden results on the same labeled datasets to compute comparative ARI/NMI scores. skills.name: seurat-marker-detection-findallmarkers
skills.search_text: seurat-marker-detection-findallmarkers Use when you have a gene+TE (or feature-by-cell) expression matrix with cluster identities and need per-cluster marker TEs/genes with log2FC and adjusted P-values, or when benchmarking a quantification method's marker-recovery rate against known cluster labels. skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed count matrix plus manually annotated cell-type labels and need top positive marker genes per cell type to run marker-supervised methods (SCSA, MarkerCount, SCINA) or evaluate marker-based identification.
skills.name: seurat-marker-gene-selection
skills.search_text: seurat-marker-gene-selection Use when you have a preprocessed count matrix plus manually annotated cell-type labels and need top positive marker genes per cell type to run marker-supervised methods (SCSA, MarkerCount, SCINA) or evaluate marker-based identification. No manually annotated labels exist for the training cells — FindAllMarkers requires labels set as 'active.ident'; use eager- or lazy-learning methods instead. Markers are already available from marker resource centers (PanglaoDB, CellMarker, CancerSEA) and no dataset-derived markers are needed. The goal is prediction from reference data rather than marker-based identification — use eagersupervised or lazysupervised interfaces of AutomaticCellTypeIdentification instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Derives cell-type-specific marker genes from a count matrix with manually annotated labels using the Seurat pipeline (NormalizeData followed by FindAllMarkers with only.pos=TRUE), seeding marker-learning cell-type identification methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.10.027
skills.summary: Derives cell-type-specific marker genes from a count matrix with manually annotated labels using the Seurat pipeline (NormalizeData followed by FindAllMarkers with only.pos=TRUE), seeding marker-learning cell-type identification methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No manually annotated labels exist for the training cells — FindAllMarkers requires labels set as 'active.ident'; use eager- or lazy-learning methods instead. Markers are already available from marker resource centers (PanglaoDB, CellMarker, CancerSEA) and no dataset-derived markers are needed. The goal is prediction from reference data rather than marker-based identification — use eagersupervised or lazysupervised interfaces of AutomaticCellTypeIdentification instead.

skills.search_text: seurat-multimodal-reference-mapping Use when a STARsolo-derived DGE has spatial barcodes too sparse (few UMIs each, e.g. SeqScope ~1M barcodes/mm2) for direct clustering, and cell-type labels must be transferred from a reference onto grid-collapsed spatial segments. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is subcellular-resolution analysis — sliding-window segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10um), so MSSW-based clustering is not feasible at subcellular scale Input is already a per-cell or per-spot dataset with sufficient UMI depth (e.g. standard VISIUM), where direct per-barcode clustering without grid collapsing suffices No suitable reference dataset exists for Seurat reference mapping, since Step C3's annotation step depends on transferring labels from a reference

skills.description: Use when the input is a raw single-cell count matrix (e.g. from GEO accessions like GSE124395 or GSE63473, or 10x filtered_gene_bc_matrices) and you need normalized, clustered, UMAP-embedded cells as input to marker-based cell-type annotation.

skills.search_text: seurat-normalization-and-clustering Use when the input is a raw single-cell count matrix (e.g. from GEO accessions like GSE124395 or GSE63473, or 10x filtered_gene_bc_matrices) and you need normalized, clustered, UMAP-embedded cells as input to marker-based cell-type annotation. skills.summary: Standard Seurat v4 pre-processing that turns a raw scRNA-seq count matrix into a clustered, UMAP-embedded Seurat object whose per-cluster scaled expression feeds downstream ScType cell-type scoring. skills.search_text: seurat-object-cluster-processing Use when you have a Seurat object with graph-based clustering already performed and need to extract a cluster-specific differential expression gene list for enrichment analysis with E.PAGE. skills.search_text: seurat-object-construction-from-spatial-dge Use when a DGE plus spatial coordinates at ultra-high resolution (e.g. Seq-Scope, >1M barcodes/mm2 with very low UMI per barcode) must be aggregated into grid-level Seurat objects before dimension reduction and clustering. Input is not a collapsed spatial DGE with coordinates (e.g. already a clustered Seurat object or a feature table) — no re-aggregation is needed Target spatial segments would be smaller than subcellular compartments (~10um); the article notes subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible at that scale Working with data already at cellular resolution (e.g. standard VISIUM spots) where collapsing barcodes into grids provides no benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs Seurat objects for cell-type clustering from a STARsolo digital expression matrix (DGE) with spatial coordinates by collapsing spatial barcodes into square grids — either non-overlapping bins (Step C1) or multi-scale sliding-window overlapping bins (Step C2) — as done in STtools for Seq-Scope/Slide-seq/VISIUM data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Constructs Seurat objects for cell-type clustering from a STARsolo digital expression matrix (DGE) with spatial coordinates by collapsing spatial barcodes into square grids — either non-overlapping bins (Step C1) or multi-scale sliding-window overlapping bins (Step C2) — as done in STtools for Seq-Scope/Slide-seq/VISIUM data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a collapsed spatial DGE with coordinates (e.g. already a clustered Seurat object or a feature table) — no re-aggregation is needed Target spatial segments would be smaller than subcellular compartments (~10um); the article notes subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible at that scale Working with data already at cellular resolution (e.g. standard VISIUM spots) where collapsing barcodes into grids provides no benefit

skills.search_text: seurat-pca-clustering-pipeline Use when you have a log-normalized single-cell Seurat object with a biologically informed feature set (e.g., DUBStepR optimal features) and need PCA-based graph clustering to resolve discrete cell subtypes. The input is raw unnormalized counts — log-normalization and DUBStepR feature selection must precede PCA/clustering. You only need the feature selection step itself (gene-gene correlation range scoring, stepwise regression) — that is the DUBStepR method, not this clustering pipeline. You need cell-level quality control or annotation against a reference — those are separate steps (QC discarding low-quality cells; SingleR reference-based labeling). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Seurat-based downstream clustering workflow that takes DUBStepR-selected variable features, scales all genes, runs PCA, builds a neighbor graph, clusters cells, and projects UMAP so subtypes (e.g., the 10 T/NK subtypes in RA PBMCs) can be annotated by marker expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Seurat-based downstream clustering workflow that takes DUBStepR-selected variable features, scales all genes, runs PCA, builds a neighbor graph, clusters cells, and projects UMAP so subtypes (e.g., the 10 T/NK subtypes in RA PBMCs) can be annotated by marker expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw unnormalized counts — log-normalization and DUBStepR feature selection must precede PCA/clustering. skills.description: Use when per-nucleotide structure calls must be derived from RSCanner sliding-window BPC and median Shannon entropy values, e.g. to select low-entropy/high-BPC positions from a CT or dot-bracket structure scan of HCV_Jc1 or any long RNA.
skills.name: shannon-entropy-filtering
skills.search_text: shannon-entropy-filtering Use when per-nucleotide structure calls must be derived from RSCanner sliding-window BPC and median Shannon entropy values, e.g. to select low-entropy/high-BPC positions from a CT or dot-bracket structure scan of HCV_Jc1 or any long RNA. No positional Shannon entropy file (shannon.txt) is available — the filter requires per-nucleotide entropy values in addition to the structure file, so RSCanner cannot compute smoothed entropy from the CT/dot-bracket input alone. The goal is de novo RNA structure prediction rather than filtering an existing structure — RSCanner takes a pre-computed secondary structure (CT or dot-bracket) and entropy, and does not fold or infer structure. An absolute (non-percentile) entropy threshold is required — the cutoffs are percentiles of the transcript's own distributions, not fixed entropy values, so the filter is not calibrated across independent transcripts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Filters nucleotide positions by keeping only those whose smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a user-defined percentile cutoff while base pair content (BPC) exceeds its percentile cutoff — the structure-count computation step of RSCanner used to isolate ordered, stable regions of an RNA secondary structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Filters nucleotide positions by keeping only those whose smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a user-defined percentile cutoff while base pair content (BPC) exceeds its percentile cutoff — the structure-count computation step of RSCanner used to isolate ordered, stable regions of an RNA secondary structure.

skills.description: Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (from a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt file) and need to binarize positions into 'structure counts' using percentile cutoffs before building heatmap/histogram summaries.
skills.name: shannon-entropy-percentile-thresholding
skills.search_text: shannon-entropy-percentile-thresholding Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (from a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt file) and need to binarize positions into 'structure counts' using percentile cutoffs before building heatmap/histogram summaries. The structure file is not in CT or dot-bracket (FASTA) format, or no positional shannon.txt is available — RSCanner's two scripts require exactly these input types. You need absolute (absolute-threshold) structural stability calls rather than relative percentile-based labels within one transcript; the default 50th-percentile cutoffs are transcript-relative. The goal is raw per-window BPC or entropy profiling (bpcplot.tiff / smoothed_Shannonplot.tiff) rather than binarized structure-count classification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 RSCanner's two-criterion filtering step that designates individual nucleotides as 'structure counts': positions are kept only when smoothed BPC exceeds a percentile cutoff (default 50th) AND smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a percentile cutoff (default 50th), flagging nucleotides that are both heavily base-paired and structurally stable (low entropy). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: RSCanner's two-criterion filtering step that designates individual nucleotides as 'structure counts': positions are kept only when smoothed BPC exceeds a percentile cutoff (default 50th) AND smoothed Shannon entropy falls below a percentile cutoff (default 50th), flagging nucleotides that are both heavily base-paired and structurally stable (low entropy).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The structure file is not in CT or dot-bracket (FASTA) format, or no positional shannon.txt is available — RSCanner's two scripts require exactly these input types. You need absolute (absolute-threshold) structural stability calls rather than relative percentile-based labels within one transcript; the default 50th-percentile cutoffs are transcript-relative. skills.description: Use when quantifying gene set activity from a normalized expression matrix and needing to statistically distinguish coordinated-variance (overdispersed) from mean-shift (shifted) pathway activation in omics data.
skills.name: shift-vs-overdispersion-module-classification
skills.search_text: shift-vs-overdispersion-module-classification Use when quantifying gene set activity from a normalized expression matrix and needing to statistically distinguish coordinated-variance (overdispersed) from mean-shift (shifted) pathway activation in omics data. The input expression matrix is raw/unnormalized — rRoma works with normalized data (e.g. cpm or vst) before classification The goal is differential-expression-per-gene testing rather than gene-set/module-level activity quantification The gene set sizes are so heterogeneous that shared null distributions (ApproxSample log-spaced grid) would be a poor approximation and full per-size nulls are required http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 rROMA's empirical significance procedure that classifies each gene set as either 'shifted' (samples displaced along PC1, tested via Median Exp) or 'overdispersed' (coordinated variance, tested via L1 % variance explained), using null distributions from randomly generated gene sets of matched size and BH-corrected ppv q-values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x
skills.summary: rROMA's empirical significance procedure that classifies each gene set as either 'shifted' (samples displaced along PC1, tested via Median Exp) or 'overdispersed' (coordinated variance, tested via L1 % variance explained), using null distributions from randomly generated gene sets of matched size and BH-corrected ppv q-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input expression matrix is raw/unnormalized — rRoma works with normalized data (e.g. cpm or vst) before classification The goal is differential-expression-per-gene testing rather than gene-set/module-level activity quantification The gene set sizes are so heterogeneous that shared null distributions (ApproxSample log-spaced grid) would be a poor approximation and full per-size nulls are required

skills.search_text: shm-mutation-enumeration-in-ighv Use when a de novo assembled Ig transcript (FASTA) needs its top germline IGHV gene, percent identity, SHM count, and mutated/unmutated (mCLL/uCLL) call determined from RNA-seq data. The goal is only partial-IGHV repertoire inference from a portion of the IGHV gene segment — CRIS's SHM classification is concordant because it uses the entire reconstructed IGHV gene segment The input reads are not aligned to the hg38 (GRCh38) genome build and coordinate-sorted/indexed as CRIS requires Only non-human or non-B-cell RNA-seq data without Ig gene loci reads is available http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 Enumerates somatic hypermutations (SHMs) and classifies IGHV mutation status from RNA-seq by aligning assembled Ig-transcript contigs to the top germline IGHV hit with IgBLAST, then calling mCLL (<98% identity) versus uCLL (>=98% identity). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021

skills.description: Use when assembling isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads (read clouds per barcode) and a per-barcode subgraph contains short low-coverage edges interrupting otherwise continuous isoform paths.
skills.name: short-edge-gap-closing
skills.search_text: short-edge-gap-closing Use when assembling isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads (read clouds per barcode) and a per-barcode subgraph contains short low-coverage edges interrupting otherwise continuous isoform paths. Input is standard unbarcoded RNA-seq without read clouds — use the rnaSPAdes transcriptome assembler pipeline instead of per-barcode subgraph simplification Gaps are too long to be bridged by short-read linked-read data — hybrid gap closure with PacBio CLR or Oxford Nanopore reads is the appropriate approach Goal is to correct the shared assembly graph itself — an edge erroneous for one barcode's isoform may be correct for another's, so edits must never be applied to the base graph http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 cloudrnaSPAdes' gap-closing step: within each barcode-specific subgraph extracted from a shared assembly graph, edges are joined across short low-coverage edges to produce continuous isoform paths, without modifying the shared graph. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad781
skills.summary: cloudrnaSPAdes' gap-closing step: within each barcode-specific subgraph extracted from a shared assembly graph, edges are joined across short low-coverage edges to produce continuous isoform paths, without modifying the shared graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is standard unbarcoded RNA-seq without read clouds — use the rnaSPAdes transcriptome assembler pipeline instead of per-barcode subgraph simplification Gaps are too long to be bridged by short-read linked-read data — hybrid gap closure with PacBio CLR or Oxford Nanopore reads is the appropriate approach Goal is to correct the shared assembly graph itself — an edge erroneous for one barcode's isoform may be correct for another's, so edits must never be applied to the base graph

Input is already an aligned BAM or a processed gene-cell count matrix — alignment would be redundant Data were generated by a non-droplet scRNA-seq protocol whose read structure does not place the cDNA insert in Read1 Mouse or other non-human samples without the matching reference genome (mm10 for mouse, hg19 for human) prepared http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns the cDNA-insert read (Read1) from 10x Genomics droplet single-cell 3' sequencing reads to a reference genome (hg19 for human, mm10 for mouse) with STAR, keeping only confidently mapped alignments (MAPQ=255) as a prerequisite for gene-barcode UMI counting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049

skills.description: Use when barcode-bearing reads have been extracted and trimmed and must be assigned to a known synthetic barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR barcodes in FASTA) to produce per-barcode alignment counts.
skills.name: short-read-alignment-to-barcode-reference
skills.search_text: short-read-alignment-to-barcode-reference Use when barcode-bearing reads have been extracted and trimmed and must be assigned to a known synthetic barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR barcodes in FASTA) to produce per-barcode alignment counts. No barcode reference library exists for the barcode design — use the reference-free mode instead of bowtie1 alignment. Input reads are raw, untrimmed FASTQ: constant regions must be removed with cutadapt first or alignments will not span the full barcode and FILTER_ALIGNMENTS will reject them. Downstream analysis needs clone/cell annotation rather than bulk barcode counts — continue to UMI error correction and PARSE_BARCODES_SC instead of stopping at the counts table. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Aligns quality-filtered, constant-region-trimmed sequencing reads against a known synthetic barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR_mCHERRY_V2_barcode_reference_library.fasta) using bowtie1 within the BARtab pipeline, then filters alignments so each read is assigned to a single lineage barcode for downstream quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Aligns quality-filtered, constant-region-trimmed sequencing reads against a known synthetic barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR_mCHERRY_V2_barcode_reference_library.fasta) using bowtie1 within the BARtab pipeline, then filters alignments so each read is assigned to a single lineage barcode for downstream quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No barcode reference library exists for the barcode design — use the reference-free mode instead of bowtie1 alignment. Input reads are raw, untrimmed FASTQ: constant regions must be removed with cutadapt first or alignments will not span the full barcode and FILTER_ALIGNMENTS will reject them. Downstream analysis needs clone/cell annotation rather than bulk barcode counts — continue to UMI error correction and PARSE_BARCODES_SC instead of stopping at the counts table.

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., LCMV1/LCMV2 10X CD44+ T cell matrices with selected PCs) and you must pick a clustering resolution without over-discovering spurious clusters.
skills.name: shuffled-data-null-false-discovery-control
skills.search_text: shuffled-data-null-false-discovery-control Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., LCMV1/LCMV2 10X CD44+ T cell matrices with selected PCs) and you must pick a clustering resolution without over-discovering spurious clusters. The data have not passed quality filtering, variable-gene selection, and confounder correction — the shuffle-based control assumes the read.data/get.variable.genes/add.confounder.variables steps are complete You only need a single fixed-resolution clustering and have no need to control false discovery (e.g., exploratory plots), since running repeated shuffled analyses is computationally expensive The biological question calls for cross-dataset cluster similarity/integration rather than per-replicate clustering resolution selection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A false-discovery control for scRNA-seq clustering (robustSingleCell) in which Phenograph clustering is run over a range of KNN-ratio resolutions on both the original data and repeatedly shuffled data, and the resolution is accepted only when original-to-shuffled modularity fold change (mdlrty/mean.shfl) exceeds 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: A false-discovery control for scRNA-seq clustering (robustSingleCell) in which Phenograph clustering is run over a range of KNN-ratio resolutions on both the original data and repeatedly shuffled data, and the resolution is accepted only when original-to-shuffled modularity fold change (mdlrty/mean.shfl) exceeds 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have not passed quality filtering, variable-gene selection, and confounder correction — the shuffle-based control assumes the read.data/get.variable.genes/add.confounder.variables steps are complete You only need a single fixed-resolution clustering and have no need to control false discovery (e.g., exploratory plots), since running repeated shuffled analyses is computationally expensive The biological question calls for cross-dataset cluster similarity/integration rather than per-replicate clustering resolution selection

skills.description: Use when implementing or reproducing ivis's dimensionality-reduction model, i.e. when a scalable neural embedding that preserves local (KNN) and global structure must be trained with a triplet loss on high-dimensional single-cell or general tabular data.
skills.name: siamese-network-architecture-construction
skills.search_text: siamese-network-architecture-construction Use when implementing or reproducing ivis's dimensionality-reduction model, i.e. when a scalable neural embedding that preserves local (KNN) and global structure must be trained with a triplet loss on high-dimensional single-cell or general tabular data. The task requires purely non-parametric embedding without a mapping for new points — ivis's value is the parametric transform; if no out-of-sample embedding is needed and only pairwise similarity preservation matters, alternatives may suffice Labels are available and supervised classification is the goal — although ivis supports supervised mode, this skill covers the unsupervised triplet-based siamese construction only The dataset is tiny and low-dimensional where simpler methods (e.g. on the iris-scale toy data) do not need a neural siamese network and Annoy ANN indexing overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs the ivis siamese neural network: three identical Keras replicates of a 'szubert' base network (dense 128-neuron SELU layers with LeCun normal init, plus a linear-activation embedding layer of embedding_dims size) with shared weights, trained on triplets sampled via approximate nearest-neighbour identification (Annoy random projection trees). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0
skills.summary: Constructs the ivis siamese neural network: three identical Keras replicates of a 'szubert' base network (dense 128-neuron SELU layers with LeCun normal init, plus a linear-activation embedding layer of embedding_dims size) with shared weights, trained on triplets sampled via approximate nearest-neighbour identification (Annoy random projection trees).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires purely non-parametric embedding without a mapping for new points — ivis's value is the parametric transform; if no out-of-sample embedding is needed and only pairwise similarity preservation matters, alternatives may suffice Labels are available and supervised classification is the goal — although ivis supports supervised mode, this skill covers the unsupervised triplet-based siamese construction only The dataset is tiny and low-dimensional where simpler methods (e.g. on the iris-scale toy data) do not need a neural siamese network and Annoy ANN indexing overhead

skills.search_text: siamese-network-dimensionality-reduction Use when visualizing or embedding high-dimensional single-cell expression data (CyTOF/scRNA-seq matrices) while needing to preserve global inter-cluster distances, or when new cells must be mapped into an existing embedding. skills.description: Use when an RMT-based noise-filtering pass (e.g., on ZhengMix PBMC or similar sparse scRNA-seq data) has flagged candidate signal dimensions and you need a data-driven threshold to keep only robust, biologically meaningful signals before UMAP embedding.
skills.name: signal-robustness-perturbation-testing
skills.search_text: signal-robustness-perturbation-testing Use when an RMT-based noise-filtering pass (e.g., on ZhengMix PBMC or similar sparse scRNA-seq data) has flagged candidate signal dimensions and you need a data-driven threshold to keep only robust, biologically meaningful signals before UMAP embedding. Input data has not been preprocessed with log normalization plus L2 normalization — signal distortion from conventional log normalization alone (e.g., 84 signals on ZhengMix) invalidates the robustness comparison baseline The goal is imputation of dropout zeros rather than signal filtering — the robustness test removes dropout-driven signals without imputing values The dataset is too large for full eigenvalue decomposition of the cell-to-cell similarity matrix, which requires significant memory resources http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 scLENS's signal robustness test filters low-quality signal dimensions identified by RMT-based noise filtering by checking each signal's stability against sparse perturbations of the scRNA-seq data, enabling data-driven, imputation-free removal of signals arising from stochastic dropout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: scLENS's signal robustness test filters low-quality signal dimensions identified by RMT-based noise filtering by checking each signal's stability against sparse perturbations of the scRNA-seq data, enabling data-driven, imputation-free removal of signals arising from stochastic dropout.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has not been preprocessed with log normalization plus L2 normalization — signal distortion from conventional log normalization alone (e.g., 84 signals on ZhengMix) invalidates the robustness comparison baseline The goal is imputation of dropout zeros rather than signal filtering — the robustness test removes dropout-driven signals without imputing values The dataset is too large for full eigenvalue decomposition of the cell-to-cell similarity matrix, which requires significant memory resources

skills.summary: Subdivides a filtered cell-cell connectome into per-signaling-family (per-mode) sub-networks and ranks cell types by sending vs. receiving centrality, using Connectome's Centrality function with Kleinberg hub/authority scores on cumulative edgeweights.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq-derived Boolean regulatory rules exist for a pathway topology (GRAPHML or KEGG) and the goal is to map individual cells to characteristic signaling states (attractors) of that pathway.
skills.name: signaling-pathway-network-simulation
skills.search_text: signaling-pathway-network-simulation Use when scRNA-seq-derived Boolean regulatory rules exist for a pathway topology (GRAPHML or KEGG) and the goal is to map individual cells to characteristic signaling states (attractors) of that pathway. No Boolean regulatory rules have been inferred yet for the pathway — run scBONITA rule inference (Step 1–2 of the pipeline) first The analysis goal is differential gene expression or conventional over-representation analysis (ORA) rather than dynamic modeling — the paper showed ORA was inefficacious here, but this skill addresses dynamic signaling states, not DE testing Data are too large for available RAM — the README recommends >10G RAM and a SLURM system rather than a desktop for attractor analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Simulates scBONITA-learned Boolean regulatory rules for a signaling pathway (e.g., KEGG or GRAPHML topology) from each sequenced cell's binarized state until steady-state attractors are reached, then assigns each cell to its closest attractor by Hamming distance. This enables pathway-based characterization of cellular signaling states not apparent from gene expression alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq profiles must be ordered by differentiation potency without markers or timepoints — e.g. snapshot data of complex tissues, high-dropout datasets, or identifying cancer stem-cell/drug-resistant phenotypes.
skills.name: signalling-entropy-potency-estimation
skills.search_text: signalling-entropy-potency-estimation Use when scRNA-seq profiles must be ordered by differentiation potency without markers or timepoints — e.g. snapshot data of complex tissues, high-dropout datasets, or identifying cancer stem-cell/drug-resistant phenotypes. When prior biological knowledge such as marker expression or timepoint labels is reliable and preferred — SCENT is intended for cases where such knowledge is unavailable or dropouts preclude marker use When the goal is trajectory/pseudo-time inference by clustering or branch analysis — the article notes the insight is 'not readily obtainable using other algorithms such as Monocle or MPath', but conversely Monocle/MPath-style tools serve different purposes When only transcriptomic (non-network) entropy is required — StemID/SLICE-style measures differ because they do not use network information and are less accurate here http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates the differentiation potency of individual cells by computing signalling entropy (SR): the signalling promiscuity of a cell's transcriptome integrated with a protein-protein interaction (connectome) network, implemented in the SCENT R package. Requires no feature selection, marker genes, timepoint labels, or prior biological knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Estimates the differentiation potency of individual cells by computing signalling entropy (SR): the signalling promiscuity of a cell's transcriptome integrated with a protein-protein interaction (connectome) network, implemented in the SCENT R package. Requires no feature selection, marker genes, timepoint labels, or prior biological knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When prior biological knowledge such as marker expression or timepoint labels is reliable and preferred — SCENT is intended for cases where such knowledge is unavailable or dropouts preclude marker use When the goal is trajectory/pseudo-time inference by clustering or branch analysis — the article notes the insight is 'not readily obtainable using other algorithms such as Monocle or MPath', but conversely Monocle/MPath-style tools serve different purposes When only transcriptomic (non-network) entropy is required — StemID/SLICE-style measures differ because they do not use network information and are less accurate here

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell expression data with SCENT signalling entropy (SR) values and want to test or use the CCAT connectome-correlation score as a fast proxy for SR/differentiation potency.
skills.name: signalling-entropy-vs-connectome-agreement-analysis
skills.search_text: signalling-entropy-vs-connectome-agreement-analysis Use when you have single-cell expression data with SCENT signalling entropy (SR) values and want to test or use the CCAT connectome-correlation score as a fast proxy for SR/differentiation potency. You need the full signalling entropy (SR) estimate itself with its network information, not a fast proxy — CCAT is a correlation-based surrogate for SR Other entropy-based measures such as StemID or SLICE would be used instead when transcriptomic entropy without network information is desired Your goal is pseudo-time ordering with algorithms like Monocle or MPath rather than potency estimation via SCENT/CCAT http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes the CCAT (connectome-transcriptome Pearson correlation) score for every single cell using the SCENT package and validates it as a proxy for full signalling entropy (SR) by fitting a linear regression and reporting the coefficient of determination, which reaches R2=0.96 on the Chu et al. dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Computes the CCAT (connectome-transcriptome Pearson correlation) score for every single cell using the SCENT package and validates it as a proxy for full signalling entropy (SR) by fitting a linear regression and reporting the coefficient of determination, which reaches R2=0.96 on the Chu et al. dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the full signalling entropy (SR) estimate itself with its network information, not a fast proxy — CCAT is a correlation-based surrogate for SR Other entropy-based measures such as StemID or SLICE would be used instead when transcriptomic entropy without network information is desired Your goal is pseudo-time ordering with algorithms like Monocle or MPath rather than potency estimation via SCENT/CCAT

skills.name: signature-matrix-construction-from-marker-genes
skills.search_text: signature-matrix-construction-from-marker-genes Use when you have a curated marker gene set (e.g., from G-PC/phenotype-cover, RankCorr, or scGeneFit) plus a scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels, and you need to assess how well those markers support deconvolution of bulk or pseudo-bulk mixtures. When the input is already bulk data without single-cell reference profiles to build a signature matrix When the goal is marker selection itself rather than evaluating a marker set — use GreedyPC/CEMPC selection first When you need an optimal (not approximate) marker set — G-PC does not provide an optimal solution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a genes × cell types signature matrix from a selected marker gene set by averaging per-cell-type expression profiles, then uses it as the basis for pseudo-bulk deconvolution with CIBERSORT (linear ν-SVR) evaluated by Jensen-Shannon divergence between predicted and true cell-type proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332

skills.description: Use when fitting reference mutational signatures to individual cancer samples (especially hematological malignancies with low-burden or overlapping processes like SBS9/AID) and you need a specific presence/absence call rather than a point estimate.
skills.name: signature-presence-calling-from-nonzero-ci
skills.search_text: signature-presence-calling-from-nonzero-ci Use when fitting reference mutational signatures to individual cancer samples (especially hematological malignancies with low-burden or overlapping processes like SBS9/AID) and you need a specific presence/absence call rather than a point estimate. Data from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases — mutational burden is too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting Catalogs of fewer than ~500 mutations, where fitting accuracy (sensitivity/specificity of error suppression) is no longer optimal Whole-exome data where the expected signature profile in coding versus non-coding regions differs substantially from the genome-wide reference, and flat signatures may be falsely removed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Calls a mutational signature 'present' in individual hematological cancer samples by fitting a curated COSMIC v3.1 reference with mmsig (EM-based fitting with dynamic cosine-similarity error suppression) and requiring a non-zero 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the signature's contribution. Used here to detect nc-AID (SBS9) in IGHV-unmutated CLL WGS samples previously thought to lack this process. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-01938-0
skills.summary: Calls a mutational signature 'present' in individual hematological cancer samples by fitting a curated COSMIC v3.1 reference with mmsig (EM-based fitting with dynamic cosine-similarity error suppression) and requiring a non-zero 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the signature's contribution. Used here to detect nc-AID (SBS9) in IGHV-unmutated CLL WGS samples previously thought to lack this process.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data from targeted capture panels covering only a few megabases — mutational burden is too low for meaningful individual-patient signature fitting Catalogs of fewer than ~500 mutations, where fitting accuracy (sensitivity/specificity of error suppression) is no longer optimal Whole-exome data where the expected signature profile in coding versus non-coding regions differs substantially from the genome-wide reference, and flat signatures may be falsely removed

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (expression matrix plus spot coordinates) should be scanned for spatially clustered TME gene signatures — e.g. detecting TLSs or tumor capsules — in R with scCancer2.
skills.name: signature-score-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: signature-score-enrichment-analysis Use when spatial transcriptomics data (expression matrix plus spot coordinates) should be scanned for spatially clustered TME gene signatures — e.g. detecting TLSs or tumor capsules — in R with scCancer2. Input is bulk or single-cell (non-spatial) scRNA-seq data with no spot coordinates — the spatial autocorrelation tests require a spatial map You need cell-level TME subtype annotation rather than spatial structure localization — scCancer2's predCellType / runCellSubtypeClassify modules cover that task instead The gene signatures of interest have no expected spatial pattern (e.g. housekeeping signatures), since a global Moran's I below 0.5 short-circuits the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-spot enrichment scores for gene signatures across a spatial transcriptomics map in scCancer2, then tests each signature for spatial structure using Global Moran's I (threshold > 0.5) and localizes significant structures with Local Moran's I. This is the mechanism scCancer2 uses to detect and position TME features such as TLSs and tumor capsules. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Computes per-spot enrichment scores for gene signatures across a spatial transcriptomics map in scCancer2, then tests each signature for spatial structure using Global Moran's I (threshold > 0.5) and localizes significant structures with Local Moran's I. This is the mechanism scCancer2 uses to detect and position TME features such as TLSs and tumor capsules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk or single-cell (non-spatial) scRNA-seq data with no spot coordinates — the spatial autocorrelation tests require a spatial map You need cell-level TME subtype annotation rather than spatial structure localization — scCancer2's predCellType / runCellSubtypeClassify modules cover that task instead The gene signatures of interest have no expected spatial pattern (e.g. housekeeping signatures), since a global Moran's I below 0.5 short-circuits the analysis

skills.search_text: signed-power-deflation-transform Use when scRNAseq count data are overdispersed relative to Poisson expectations and you need to deflate a CA chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman-Tukey) before SVD in a corral preprocessing stage. When the goal is batch integration of multiple tables rather than single-table preprocessing — corralm, not the corral preprocessing stage, is the appropriate path When the pipeline already uses log(x + 1) transformation followed by PCA — this skill specifically replaces that with CA on a chi-squared residual matrix, so mixing them is inappropriate When counts are not overdispersed and standard CA on plain Pearson residuals suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A power-deflation adaptation of correspondence analysis for scRNAseq counts: the chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman-Tukey, or a variance-stabilizing transform) is raised element-wise to a power α with signs preserved, smoothing the residual matrix prior to SVD to address overdispersion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: A power-deflation adaptation of correspondence analysis for scRNAseq counts: the chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman-Tukey, or a variance-stabilizing transform) is raised element-wise to a power α with signs preserved, smoothing the residual matrix prior to SVD to address overdispersion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch integration of multiple tables rather than single-table preprocessing — corralm, not the corral preprocessing stage, is the appropriate path When the pipeline already uses log(x + 1) transformation followed by PCA — this skill specifically replaces that with CA on a chi-squared residual matrix, so mixing them is inappropriate When counts are not overdispersed and standard CA on plain Pearson residuals suffices

skills.description: Use when a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix has multiple labeled subtypes and the goal is to flag genes that are silent specifically in one subtype (SDG) rather than subtype-enriched marker genes.
skills.name: silent-gene-identification-across-subtypes
skills.search_text: silent-gene-identification-across-subtypes Use when a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix has multiple labeled subtypes and the goal is to flag genes that are silent specifically in one subtype (SDG) rather than subtype-enriched marker genes. The goal is detecting subtype-enriched marker genes (MG) — use the standard COT ideal-MG reference vector, not the XOR-based SDG statistic The input matrix is not batch-corrected; COT's input should be batch-corrected before computing subtype means and cosines There are only K=2 subtypes, since the SDG bound 1/(K-1) degenerates to 1 and the statistic is uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Identifies subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) — genes silent in exactly one subtype but expressed in all others — by replacing COT's ideal-MG reference vector with an XOR-based reference (0 in one subtype, 1 in all others) and computing a bounded cosine statistic (1/(K-1) < t_COT(i) < 1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac037
skills.summary: Identifies subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) — genes silent in exactly one subtype but expressed in all others — by replacing COT's ideal-MG reference vector with an XOR-based reference (0 in one subtype, 1 in all others) and computing a bounded cosine statistic (1/(K-1) < t_COT(i) < 1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting subtype-enriched marker genes (MG) — use the standard COT ideal-MG reference vector, not the XOR-based SDG statistic The input matrix is not batch-corrected; COT's input should be batch-corrected before computing subtype means and cosines There are only K=2 subtypes, since the SDG bound 1/(K-1) degenerates to 1 and the statistic is uninformative

skills.search_text: silhouette-based-cluster-heterogeneity-evaluation Use when a Seurat object has broad Louvain clusters that may mask rare cell types, and you need a quantitative criterion (per-cell silhouette score distributions) to decide which clusters are heterogeneous enough to recluster. skills.name: silhouette-based-cluster-number-selection
skills.search_text: silhouette-based-cluster-number-selection Use when performing unsupervised clustering of single-cell expression data and you need a quantitative, unbiased criterion (silhouette score) to pick K instead of fixing cluster resolution ad hoc. Input contains mixed lymphocyte populations (Treg, CD4T, NKT cells) — filter to CD8 T cells first (e.g. TILPRED's filterCD8T) or silhouette values will be dominated by coarse cell-type separation Input is bulk RNA-seq or flow cytometry data, where per-cell silhouette scoring on a single-cell neighborhood graph is not applicable A curated reference atlas projection (e.g. ProjecTILs) is preferred over de novo clustering, e.g. when mapping query cells onto a stable annotated reference http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects the optimal number of transcriptomic cell states K by computing silhouette coefficients across candidate clustering resolutions and choosing the K before the sharp drop — here K=4 for CD8 TILs from B16 melanoma scRNA-seq (GSE116390, >3500 smart-seq2 cells from seven tumor-bearing mice). transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Selects the optimal number of transcriptomic cell states K by computing silhouette coefficients across candidate clustering resolutions and choosing the K before the sharp drop — here K=4 for CD8 TILs from B16 melanoma scRNA-seq (GSE116390, >3500 smart-seq2 cells from seven tumor-bearing mice).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input contains mixed lymphocyte populations (Treg, CD4T, NKT cells) — filter to CD8 T cells first (e.g. TILPRED's filterCD8T) or silhouette values will be dominated by coarse cell-type separation Input is bulk RNA-seq or flow cytometry data, where per-cell silhouette scoring on a single-cell neighborhood graph is not applicable A curated reference atlas projection (e.g. ProjecTILs) is preferred over de novo clustering, e.g. when mapping query cells onto a stable annotated reference

skills.description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction or batch-integration methods for scRNA-seq (e.g., corralm vs PCA vs Seurat on multi-batch data) and you need a quantitative cell-type-preservation vs batch-mixing trade-off metric on cell embeddings.
skills.name: silhouette-based-clustering-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-based-clustering-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing dimension-reduction or batch-integration methods for scRNA-seq (e.g., corralm vs PCA vs Seurat on multi-batch data) and you need a quantitative cell-type-preservation vs batch-mixing trade-off metric on cell embeddings. When the evaluation goal is label-transfer or ARI-based clustering accuracy against a reference — the article notes ARI may penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations or rare cell types relative to reference labels When the input is raw counts rather than reduced-dimension embeddings and no dimension reduction has been run — silhouette must be computed on the method's embedding (e.g., 8 PCs/CA dimensions), not the expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates dimension-reduction and batch-integration embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq by computing average silhouette width (ASW) with cell-type labels and batch labels, trading off ASW_celltype against 1 - ASW_batch on the first 8 dimensions of each method's embedding. In the Hsu & Culhane corral paper this is how corralm with Freeman–Tukey residuals (alone and with Harmony/MNN) is compared against multibatch PCA and the Seurat routine on the Baron, Lawlor, and Muraro pancreas datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Evaluates dimension-reduction and batch-integration embeddings for single-cell RNA-seq by computing average silhouette width (ASW) with cell-type labels and batch labels, trading off ASW_celltype against 1 - ASW_batch on the first 8 dimensions of each method's embedding. In the Hsu & Culhane corral paper this is how corralm with Freeman–Tukey residuals (alone and with Harmony/MNN) is compared against multibatch PCA and the Seurat routine on the Baron, Lawlor, and Muraro pancreas datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the evaluation goal is label-transfer or ARI-based clustering accuracy against a reference — the article notes ARI may penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations or rare cell types relative to reference labels When the input is raw counts rather than reduced-dimension embeddings and no dimension reduction has been run — silhouette must be computed on the method's embedding (e.g., 8 PCs/CA dimensions), not the expression matrix

skills.description: Use when comparing imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., Bfimpute vs scImpute/DrImpute/PBLR outputs) on datasets with known cell type labels and you need silhouette-based clustering quality metrics.
skills.name: silhouette-based-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-based-clustering-evaluation Use when comparing imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., Bfimpute vs scImpute/DrImpute/PBLR outputs) on datasets with known cell type labels and you need silhouette-based clustering quality metrics. Datasets lack reliable true cell type labels and clustering must be inferred instead (Bfimpute would need ccluster = c(7,"Spectrum") or a custom clustering function rather than labeled mode) The goal is only imputation itself, not benchmarking clustering/cell-to-cell relationship recovery across methods Input counts are already normalized — set normalized=TRUE, otherwise CPM plus log10 bias 1.01 will be re-applied inappropriately http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods by computing silhouette scores against true cell type labels and same/different-cell-type Pearson correlations on each imputed expression matrix, as done for Bfimpute vs scImpute, DrImpute, PBLR, ALRA, and mcImpute. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq imputation methods by computing silhouette scores against true cell type labels and same/different-cell-type Pearson correlations on each imputed expression matrix, as done for Bfimpute vs scImpute, DrImpute, PBLR, ALRA, and mcImpute.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lack reliable true cell type labels and clustering must be inferred instead (Bfimpute would need ccluster = c(7,"Spectrum") or a custom clustering function rather than labeled mode) The goal is only imputation itself, not benchmarking clustering/cell-to-cell relationship recovery across methods Input counts are already normalized — set normalized=TRUE, otherwise CPM plus log10 bias 1.01 will be re-applied inappropriately

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether an engineered/derived cell feature representation (e.g., Spearman or Pearson correlation, cosine, Euclidean, autoencoder features) improves consistency with known cell-type labels in scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: silhouette-based-clustering-validation
skills.search_text: silhouette-based-clustering-validation Use when you need to quantify whether an engineered/derived cell feature representation (e.g., Spearman or Pearson correlation, cosine, Euclidean, autoencoder features) improves consistency with known cell-type labels in scRNA-seq data. No ground-truth cell-type labels are available — silhouette against true labels cannot be computed The goal is clustering accuracy itself (e.g., ARI against labels) rather than assessing whether a derived feature space better aligns with labels than the original expression profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates scRNA-seq feature construction/extraction methods by computing silhouette coefficients of cell features against true cluster labels and comparing them per cell to those of the original expression profiles, as done in the SSCC paper's Figure 2 across five benchmark datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: Validates scRNA-seq feature construction/extraction methods by computing silhouette coefficients of cell features against true cluster labels and comparing them per cell to those of the original expression profiles, as done in the SSCC paper's Figure 2 across five benchmark datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth cell-type labels are available — silhouette against true labels cannot be computed The goal is clustering accuracy itself (e.g., ARI against labels) rather than assessing whether a derived feature space better aligns with labels than the original expression profiles

skills.description: Use when comparing two clusterings of the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 5% vs 10% cell subsamples processed by SCC or SSCC) and you need a numeric measure of clustering consistency and per-cell cluster quality.
skills.name: silhouette-cluster-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-quality-assessment Use when comparing two clusterings of the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 5% vs 10% cell subsamples processed by SCC or SSCC) and you need a numeric measure of clustering consistency and per-cell cluster quality. You need an external ground-truth-based accuracy metric (e.g., ARI against known cell types) rather than internal consistency between two subsampling schemes The dataset is small enough that full-data clustering is feasible and subsampling bias is not a concern, making the consistency comparison moot http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify clustering quality and cross-scheme consistency for single-cell RNA-seq clusterings using silhouette statistics, comparing clusterings produced under different subsampling schemes (e.g., 5% vs 10% of cells) in the SSCC vs SCC framework of sscClust. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: Quantify clustering quality and cross-scheme consistency for single-cell RNA-seq clusterings using silhouette statistics, comparing clusterings produced under different subsampling schemes (e.g., 5% vs 10% of cells) in the SSCC vs SCC framework of sscClust.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need an external ground-truth-based accuracy metric (e.g., ARI against known cell types) rather than internal consistency between two subsampling schemes The dataset is small enough that full-data clustering is feasible and subsampling bias is not a concern, making the consistency comparison moot

skills.description: Use when you have annotated single-cell expression matrices (e.g. Jurkat-293T with CD3D/XIST marker annotations, Zeisel with nine major classes) in raw vs. imputed versions and need to assess whether imputation improves cell-type subpopulation separability.
skills.name: silhouette-cluster-separability-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-separability-evaluation Use when you have annotated single-cell expression matrices (e.g. Jurkat-293T with CD3D/XIST marker annotations, Zeisel with nine major classes) in raw vs. imputed versions and need to assess whether imputation improves cell-type subpopulation separability. Cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable — silhouette scoring requires pre-defined clusters per cell and cannot be computed from unannotated data The goal is expression-value recovery accuracy (masked matrix recovery) rather than visual/quantitative separability; use the paper's subsampling recovery evaluation instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify cell-type separability in scRNA-seq data by projecting log-transformed expression matrices into 2D PCA space and computing the average silhouette index per imputation condition, as used in the AutoImpute paper to show that AutoImpute groups same cell-types together with improved separability (Fig. 5, Supplementary Table S4). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Quantify cell-type separability in scRNA-seq data by projecting log-transformed expression matrices into 2D PCA space and computing the average silhouette index per imputation condition, as used in the AutoImpute paper to show that AutoImpute groups same cell-types together with improved separability (Fig. 5, Supplementary Table S4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable — silhouette scoring requires pre-defined clusters per cell and cannot be computed from unannotated data The goal is expression-value recovery accuracy (masked matrix recovery) rather than visual/quantitative separability; use the paper's subsampling recovery evaluation instead

skills.description: Use when comparing single-cell denoising or feature-selection methods and a ground-truth cell-phenotype labeling exists, so cluster separation can be quantified as mean silhouette score per method and latent dimension.
skills.name: silhouette-cluster-separation-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-separation-evaluation Use when comparing single-cell denoising or feature-selection methods and a ground-truth cell-phenotype labeling exists, so cluster separation can be quantified as mean silhouette score per method and latent dimension. No known phenotype or cluster labels exist for the cells — silhouette requires predefined groupings and cannot be computed from labels alone Cells have not yet been embedded into a reduced latent space (silhouette is computed on embedded coordinates, not the raw sparse count matrix) The goal is to discover novel clusters rather than evaluate recovery of known marked cell populations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates whether a denoising or dimensionality-reduction method preserves known cell phenotypes by computing the mean silhouette coefficient of phenotype clusters in the reduced latent space, as used to benchmark RMT-based denoising against MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI, DCA, Seurat, top-HVG, and raw baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Evaluates whether a denoising or dimensionality-reduction method preserves known cell phenotypes by computing the mean silhouette coefficient of phenotype clusters in the reduced latent space, as used to benchmark RMT-based denoising against MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI, DCA, Seurat, top-HVG, and raw baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No known phenotype or cluster labels exist for the cells — silhouette requires predefined groupings and cannot be computed from labels alone Cells have not yet been embedded into a reduced latent space (silhouette is computed on embedded coordinates, not the raw sparse count matrix) The goal is to discover novel clusters rather than evaluate recovery of known marked cell populations

skills.description: Use when comparing manifold projection methods (topoAE, VAE, AE, UMAP) on single-cell modalities and you need a class-separation metric for each low-dimensional embedding, alongside KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 density scores.
