skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-separation-evaluation Use when comparing manifold projection methods (topoAE, VAE, AE, UMAP) on single-cell modalities and you need a class-separation metric for each low-dimensional embedding, alongside KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 density scores. When the goal is alignment of two modalities into a shared latent space (use scTopoGAN's run_scTopoGAN instead of per-modality projection evaluation) When only density preservation matters and no cell-class labels are available — Silhouette cannot be computed without class structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes Silhouette scores on low-dimensional (e.g., 8-dimensional) single-cell embeddings to quantify cell-class separation, complementing KL divergence-based density-preservation metrics in the scTopoGAN topoAE vs. VAE/AE/UMAP benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Computes Silhouette scores on low-dimensional (e.g., 8-dimensional) single-cell embeddings to quantify cell-class separation, complementing KL divergence-based density-preservation metrics in the scTopoGAN topoAE vs. VAE/AE/UMAP benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is alignment of two modalities into a shared latent space (use scTopoGAN's run_scTopoGAN instead of per-modality projection evaluation) When only density preservation matters and no cell-class labels are available — Silhouette cannot be computed without class structure

skills.description: Use when running hsslda::runHSS feature selection on single-cell marker data (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers) and you want subset scoring based on cluster cohesion vs. separation of a priori class labels rather than euclidean distance.
skills.name: silhouette-cluster-separation-metric
skills.search_text: silhouette-cluster-separation-metric Use when running hsslda::runHSS feature selection on single-cell marker data (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers) and you want subset scoring based on cluster cohesion vs. separation of a priori class labels rather than euclidean distance. Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — HSS-LDA is a supervised method and inappropriate in these situations Feature space exceeds ~100 dimensions, where HSS (and thus silhouette-scored subset search) is not feasible Silhouette/pixel-based metrics cannot be used because their dependencies (e.g., cluster, entropy) are unavailable and the default euclidean metric is preferred http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Uses the silhouette width (cluster package) as a separation metric to score candidate feature subsets during hybrid subset selection (HSS) for HSS-LDA, guiding which markers are retained for the LDA visualization of single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Uses the silhouette width (cluster package) as a separation metric to score candidate feature subsets during hybrid subset selection (HSS) for HSS-LDA, guiding which markers are retained for the LDA visualization of single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — HSS-LDA is a supervised method and inappropriate in these situations Feature space exceeds ~100 dimensions, where HSS (and thus silhouette-scored subset search) is not feasible Silhouette/pixel-based metrics cannot be used because their dependencies (e.g., cluster, entropy) are unavailable and the default euclidean metric is preferred

skills.search_text: silhouette-clustering-agreement-scoring Use when simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g. Splatter two- or six-group, 200 genes, 2000 cells, with dropout) has ground-truth celltype labels and you must numerically judge whether a denoiser (DCA ZINB vs MSE autoencoder) recovers celltype structure. skills.summary: Quantifies how well a denoised scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. DCA vs MSE-autoencoder output vs no-dropout ground truth) recovers simulated celltype structure using silhouette scores and clustering-agreement metrics such as ARI against ground-truth labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real experimental scRNA-seq data with no simulated ground-truth celltype labels — the article notes the definition of a ground truth can be challenging for real data, so ARI against known labels cannot be computed Evaluating imputation accuracy at zero-entry level rather than celltype structure recovery — silhouette/ARI do not measure per-cell-gene overimputation Datasets where cells and genes with zero expression were not removed and library-size normalization has not been applied consistently across compared matrices

skills.search_text: silhouette-coefficient-cluster-evaluation Use when comparing two cell embeddings (e.g., OnClass pred_Y_all score-PCA vs Scanorama-integrated expression) on labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a per-dataset, statistically testable measure of cluster separation by cell type. Cells lack ground-truth cell type labels — silhouette in this workflow is computed against cell type labels, so unlabeled embeddings cannot be scored this way You only have a single embedding and no baseline (e.g., the Scanorama expression embedding) — the skill is designed for head-to-head comparison and a two-sided significance test Your goal is annotation accuracy (correct cell type assignment) rather than evaluating whether an embedding separates cells by cell type http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantify how well cell type labels separate in a low-dimensional single-cell embedding by computing the silhouette coefficient per dataset, as used to show OnClass Cell-Ontology score embeddings integrate the 26 scRNA-seq datasets better than Scanorama expression-based integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25725-x
skills.summary: Quantify how well cell type labels separate in a low-dimensional single-cell embedding by computing the silhouette coefficient per dataset, as used to show OnClass Cell-Ontology score embeddings integrate the 26 scRNA-seq datasets better than Scanorama expression-based integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack ground-truth cell type labels — silhouette in this workflow is computed against cell type labels, so unlabeled embeddings cannot be scored this way You only have a single embedding and no baseline (e.g., the Scanorama expression embedding) — the skill is designed for head-to-head comparison and a two-sided significance test Your goal is annotation accuracy (correct cell type assignment) rather than evaluating whether an embedding separates cells by cell type

skills.search_text: silhouette-coefficient-computation Use when you have 2D UMAP coordinates plus cell-type labels from gene-annotation-based KNN/Seurat clustering and want to test whether an alternative feature space (e.g., uTAR reads outside gene annotations) clusters cell types comparably to annotated gene expression. Input is raw read counts or a gene-by-cell expression matrix rather than an existing 2D embedding with cluster labels — silhouette is computed on the UMAP coordinates, not raw profiles You want to detect differentially expressed uTARs or annotate them by sequence homology — use the TAR-scRNA-seq differential-expression and homology steps instead No cell-type labels exist for the dataset — silhouette requires pre-defined clusters to score http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute silhouette coefficients on 2D UMAP embeddings for each scRNA-seq feature space (annotated gene expression, aTARs, uTARs) to quantify how well cell-type clusters are separated, following Fig. 2b of the TAR-scRNA-seq paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Compute silhouette coefficients on 2D UMAP embeddings for each scRNA-seq feature space (annotated gene expression, aTARs, uTARs) to quantify how well cell-type clusters are separated, following Fig. 2b of the TAR-scRNA-seq paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read counts or a gene-by-cell expression matrix rather than an existing 2D embedding with cluster labels — silhouette is computed on the UMAP coordinates, not raw profiles You want to detect differentially expressed uTARs or annotate them by sequence homology — use the TAR-scRNA-seq differential-expression and homology steps instead No cell-type labels exist for the dataset — silhouette requires pre-defined clusters to score

skills.search_text: silhouette-coefficient-evaluation Use when benchmarking a cluster-purity or clustering-quality metric (e.g., ROGUE) against silhouette coefficients on simulated or real scRNA-seq populations, especially to test robustness to sequencing-depth or cell-number differences. Input is already a filtered/normalized feature table or the goal is simply to pick the optimal number of clusters — the article notes silhouette and similar approaches 'are not comparable among datasets and have poor interpretability of cluster purity' The aim is to detect rare cell types rather than assess cluster purity — dedicated tools like GiniClust or RaceID3 are designed for that task Data are low-quality or continuous where the recommended 0.9 ROGUE purity threshold may not apply and thresholds must be set from global ROGUE values http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates single-cell cluster separation by computing silhouette coefficients on gene-expression matrices and, as in the ROGUE paper (Nat Commun 2020), pairing silhouette values with the entropy-based ROGUE metric to benchmark how cluster-purity statistics behave on simulated replicate mixtures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Evaluates single-cell cluster separation by computing silhouette coefficients on gene-expression matrices and, as in the ROGUE paper (Nat Commun 2020), pairing silhouette values with the entropy-based ROGUE metric to benchmark how cluster-purity statistics behave on simulated replicate mixtures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered/normalized feature table or the goal is simply to pick the optimal number of clusters — the article notes silhouette and similar approaches 'are not comparable among datasets and have poor interpretability of cluster purity' The aim is to detect rare cell types rather than assess cluster purity — dedicated tools like GiniClust or RaceID3 are designed for that task Data are low-quality or continuous where the recommended 0.9 ROGUE purity threshold may not apply and thresholds must be set from global ROGUE values

skills.name: silhouette-evaluation-of-embeddings
skills.search_text: silhouette-evaluation-of-embeddings Use when comparing 2D embeddings of scRNA-seq data for rare cell type separation, where a silhouette index computed over 100+ replicated runs (e.g., EDGE mean 0.851 vs UMAP 0.801 vs t-SNE 0.838 on PBMC) is needed as an objective metric. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a 2D cell embedding derived from a normalized count matrix (dat_log) — silhouette on unnormalized or raw counts does not benchmark embedding quality The dataset lacks labeled rare cell type annotations, since the silhouette index must be computed per rare cell type (e.g., Jurkat cells, dendritic cells, megakaryocytes) You need feature gene identification rather than embedding quality assessment — use EDGE's endr feature gene output instead

skills.name: silhouette-index-cluster-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-index-cluster-evaluation Use when comparing 2D embeddings (e.g., EDGE, t-SNE, UMAP) of labeled single-cell RNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, replication-averaged measure of how compactly and separately each cell type is projected. The input is raw counts that have not been library-size normalized and log2(x+1) transformed — silhouette rankings are only comparable when all methods embed the same normalized matrix The cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable, since silhouette must be computed against known groups Only a single embedding per method exists without replication, since Monte Carlo tolerance on the reported means (e.g., 0.621 vs 0.501) cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates how well a low-dimensional embedding preserves cell-type structure by computing the silhouette index of each cell type in the 2D embedding, averaged over many replications. Used in the EDGE paper to rank EDGE, UMAP, and t-SNE on the 3005-cell mouse cortex/hippocampus dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Evaluates how well a low-dimensional embedding preserves cell-type structure by computing the silhouette index of each cell type in the 2D embedding, averaged over many replications. Used in the EDGE paper to rank EDGE, UMAP, and t-SNE on the 3005-cell mouse cortex/hippocampus dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw counts that have not been library-size normalized and log2(x+1) transformed — silhouette rankings are only comparable when all methods embed the same normalized matrix The cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable, since silhouette must be computed against known groups Only a single embedding per method exists without replication, since Monte Carlo tolerance on the reported means (e.g., 0.621 vs 0.501) cannot be assessed

skills.description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction or visualization methods for scRNA-seq data and you need a label-referenced metric of cell-type separation for each 2D embedding.
skills.name: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation Use when comparing dimension-reduction or visualization methods for scRNA-seq data and you need a label-referenced metric of cell-type separation for each 2D embedding. The input is not a 2D embedding or dimension-reduction output — silhouette evaluation here is defined on visualization embeddings, not on raw high-dimensional count matrices No ground-truth cell-type labels are available, since the silhouette index must be computed with true labels as the cluster reference The goal is pseudotime or trajectory benchmarking (use scDHA.pt / Monocle-style evaluation instead of silhouette index) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Evaluates the quality of low-dimensional single-cell embeddings (e.g. 2D visualization embeddings from scDHA.vis, PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, SCANPY) by computing the silhouette index against ground-truth cell-type labels, and comparing methods statistically across benchmark datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Evaluates the quality of low-dimensional single-cell embeddings (e.g. 2D visualization embeddings from scDHA.vis, PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, SCANPY) by computing the silhouette index against ground-truth cell-type labels, and comparing methods statistically across benchmark datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a 2D embedding or dimension-reduction output — silhouette evaluation here is defined on visualization embeddings, not on raw high-dimensional count matrices No ground-truth cell-type labels are available, since the silhouette index must be computed with true labels as the cluster reference The goal is pseudotime or trajectory benchmarking (use scDHA.pt / Monocle-style evaluation instead of silhouette index)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method and you need a label-based quantitative score of cluster separation across feature set sizes (e.g., 50-4000 genes).
skills.name: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method and you need a label-based quantitative score of cluster separation across feature set sizes (e.g., 50-4000 genes). No independent cell type annotations are available — the silhouette index requires known labels and cannot be computed purely unsupervised You need a label-free proxy for choosing feature set size — use the Density Index instead, which the paper validated as concordant with SI in 5 of 7 datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluates feature selection and clustering quality in scRNA-seq pipelines by computing the mean scaled silhouette index of cell clusters in PCA space against known cell type labels, as used in the DUBStepR benchmark across 7 datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Evaluates feature selection and clustering quality in scRNA-seq pipelines by computing the mean scaled silhouette index of cell clusters in PCA space against known cell type labels, as used in the DUBStepR benchmark across 7 datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent cell type annotations are available — the silhouette index requires known labels and cannot be computed purely unsupervised You need a label-free proxy for choosing feature set size — use the Density Index instead, which the paper validated as concordant with SI in 5 of 7 datasets

skills.description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or VAE embeddings of scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and you need a quantitative, per-method separation metric to supplement visual checks for crowding or overlap.
skills.name: silhouette-score-cell-type-evaluation
skills.search_text: silhouette-score-cell-type-evaluation Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or VAE embeddings of scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and you need a quantitative, per-method separation metric to supplement visual checks for crowding or overlap. Cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable — Silhouette scores require ground-truth labels and are meaningless on unlabeled embeddings Datasets are the large multi-patient IBD/colon mucosa benchmarks where the paper's evaluation focus is batch correction and reference mapping, not the small-dataset crowding benchmark You need a hyperbolic (wn latent_dist) embedding evaluation for developmental trajectory structure rather than discrete cell-type separation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantitatively evaluates how well a low-dimensional embedding (e.g., scPhere vMF spherical vs. normal-prior Euclidean VAE vs. t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE) separates known cell types by computing Silhouette scores of cell-type labels on each embedding, as done in the scPhere paper's Supplementary Figs. 1–3 benchmark on small scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Quantitatively evaluates how well a low-dimensional embedding (e.g., scPhere vMF spherical vs. normal-prior Euclidean VAE vs. t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE) separates known cell types by computing Silhouette scores of cell-type labels on each embedding, as done in the scPhere paper's Supplementary Figs. 1–3 benchmark on small scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are unavailable or unreliable — Silhouette scores require ground-truth labels and are meaningless on unlabeled embeddings Datasets are the large multi-patient IBD/colon mucosa benchmarks where the paper's evaluation focus is batch correction and reference mapping, not the small-dataset crowding benchmark You need a hyperbolic (wn latent_dist) embedding evaluation for developmental trajectory structure rather than discrete cell-type separation

skills.search_text: silhouette-score-clustering-evaluation Use when you need to quantitatively compare clustering performance of DR methods (e.g., scLENS vs Seurat/Scanpy PCs) on single-cell datasets with known ground-truth labels across varying sparsity or TGC variability. skills.description: Use when comparing cross-platform scRNA-seq integration quality — e.g. after Seurat integration of platform-specific gene-by-barcode matrices (GBMs) with a reference GBM — by scoring cluster separation alongside kBET.
skills.name: silhouette-score-computation
skills.search_text: silhouette-score-computation Use when comparing cross-platform scRNA-seq integration quality — e.g. after Seurat integration of platform-specific gene-by-barcode matrices (GBMs) with a reference GBM — by scoring cluster separation alongside kBET. Input is raw FASTQ or an unprocessed/unharmonised GBM — clusters must come from a completed Seurat integration of matched gene/barcode matrices before a Silhouette score is meaningful The question is upstream processing fidelity (e.g. FASTQ-to-count accuracy) rather than cross-platform integration quality — Silhouette alone does not measure read/UMI correctness Only one integration exists with no comparison candidate (e.g. no zUMIs counterpart), since the skill's value is the directional UniverSC-vs-platform-specific comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the Silhouette score (R package cluster, v2.1.3) to quantify the distinctness of clusters in a Seurat-integrated single-cell dataset, used here to judge whether SmartSeq2 mouse primary cell data processed by UniverSC integrates better with a Chromium reference than the same data processed by zUMIs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Computes the Silhouette score (R package cluster, v2.1.3) to quantify the distinctness of clusters in a Seurat-integrated single-cell dataset, used here to judge whether SmartSeq2 mouse primary cell data processed by UniverSC integrates better with a Chromium reference than the same data processed by zUMIs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or an unprocessed/unharmonised GBM — clusters must come from a completed Seurat integration of matched gene/barcode matrices before a Silhouette score is meaningful The question is upstream processing fidelity (e.g. FASTQ-to-count accuracy) rather than cross-platform integration quality — Silhouette alone does not measure read/UMI correctness Only one integration exists with no comparison candidate (e.g. no zUMIs counterpart), since the skill's value is the directional UniverSC-vs-platform-specific comparison

skills.description: Use when a patient/specimen-level distance matrix (Wasserstein/EMD between cell-cluster distributions) has been computed and you need an unsupervised quality metric of that matrix, or when benchmarking distance methods with ARI/Silhouette/AUCPR/Spearman metrics.
skills.name: silhouette-score-distance-matrix-validation
skills.search_text: silhouette-score-distance-matrix-validation Use when a patient/specimen-level distance matrix (Wasserstein/EMD between cell-cluster distributions) has been computed and you need an unsupervised quality metric of that matrix, or when benchmarking distance methods with ARI/Silhouette/AUCPR/Spearman metrics. Input is raw per-cell expression or structure-level features rather than an already-computed sample-by-sample distance matrix — cluster distributions must be built first (e.g., via Seurat for pathomics structures or Monocle 2 for PhEMD input) You need to correct for technical artifacts or batch effects: the paper notes PILOT 'does not explicitly correct for such potential technical artefacts', and Silhouette on W will reflect any technology/isolation-method confounding rather than fix it Comparing datasets with non-uniform tissue collection or mixed technologies (single-nucleus vs. single-cell, droplet vs. well-based), which the authors state is still an open challenge http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute the Silhouette score of a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., the Wasserstein distance matrix W produced by PILOT via POT's emd2) to validate that the patient-level distances reflect coherent sample groupings before downstream clustering and trajectory analysis, and to compare methods in the 12-dataset PILOT benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Compute the Silhouette score of a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., the Wasserstein distance matrix W produced by PILOT via POT's emd2) to validate that the patient-level distances reflect coherent sample groupings before downstream clustering and trajectory analysis, and to compare methods in the 12-dataset PILOT benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw per-cell expression or structure-level features rather than an already-computed sample-by-sample distance matrix — cluster distributions must be built first (e.g., via Seurat for pathomics structures or Monocle 2 for PhEMD input) You need to correct for technical artifacts or batch effects: the paper notes PILOT 'does not explicitly correct for such potential technical artefacts', and Silhouette on W will reflect any technology/isolation-method confounding rather than fix it Comparing datasets with non-uniform tissue collection or mixed technologies (single-nucleus vs. single-cell, droplet vs. well-based), which the authors state is still an open challenge

skills.search_text: silhouette-score-evaluation Use when a Seurat/SCISSORS clustering must be assessed for heterogeneity, when comparing clusterings across methods with violin plots of per-cell silhouettes, or when deciding which broad clusters to recluster for rare subpopulations. When only an external agreement metric is needed (ARI/NMI against known labels) and no assessment of within-cluster heterogeneity or reclustering targets is intended When the input is raw counts or a feature table that has not been normalized and reduced to PCA space — silhouette scores are only meaningful on the embedding (dims from RunPCA) When clusters are already known to be homogeneous fine-grained subclusters (e.g. a validated 148-cell rare subcluster) — silhouette evaluation targets broad, heterogeneous parent clusters http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Per-cell silhouette scoring of scRNA-seq clusterings in PCA (or cosine-distance) space to quantify cluster heterogeneity, compare candidate clusterings (SCISSORS vs Seurat vs SAFE vs GiniClust3), and flag broad clusters that warrant semi-supervised reclustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad449
skills.summary: Per-cell silhouette scoring of scRNA-seq clusterings in PCA (or cosine-distance) space to quantify cluster heterogeneity, compare candidate clusterings (SCISSORS vs Seurat vs SAFE vs GiniClust3), and flag broad clusters that warrant semi-supervised reclustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only an external agreement metric is needed (ARI/NMI against known labels) and no assessment of within-cluster heterogeneity or reclustering targets is intended When the input is raw counts or a feature table that has not been normalized and reduced to PCA space — silhouette scores are only meaningful on the embedding (dims from RunPCA) When clusters are already known to be homogeneous fine-grained subclusters (e.g. a validated 148-cell rare subcluster) — silhouette evaluation targets broad, heterogeneous parent clusters

skills.search_text: silhouette-score-evaluation-of-cell-type-clustering Use when comparing scRNA-seq integration/annotation pipelines (e.g., 16 MASI variants of raw vs. PlinerScore matrices, marker vs. HVG features) and you need a numeric, statistically testable measure of whether cell-type structure is resolved. When the question is annotation correctness against ground-truth labels (accuracy/F1) rather than unsupervised cluster geometry — the article benchmarks MASI on integration, annotation, and speed as separate axes When batch mixing alone is the target and cell-type separation is not scored — batch entropy mixing should be interpreted jointly with silhouette, not in isolation When the reference data quality or cell-type resolution is not matched to the query — MASI annotation is dependent on reference quality, so silhouette scores on poor annotations are not interpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantitatively score how well cell-type annotations form compact, well-separated clusters by computing the cell-type silhouette score (paired with batch entropy mixing) per pipeline per dataset, then test significance with paired t-tests. Used in the MASI benchmark to rank 16 feature/score pipelines across 6 batch-involved scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04820-3
skills.summary: Quantitatively score how well cell-type annotations form compact, well-separated clusters by computing the cell-type silhouette score (paired with batch entropy mixing) per pipeline per dataset, then test significance with paired t-tests. Used in the MASI benchmark to rank 16 feature/score pipelines across 6 batch-involved scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is annotation correctness against ground-truth labels (accuracy/F1) rather than unsupervised cluster geometry — the article benchmarks MASI on integration, annotation, and speed as separate axes When batch mixing alone is the target and cell-type separation is not scored — batch entropy mixing should be interpreted jointly with silhouette, not in isolation When the reference data quality or cell-type resolution is not matched to the query — MASI annotation is dependent on reference quality, so silhouette scores on poor annotations are not interpretable

skills.name: silhouette-score-heterogeneity-assessment
skills.search_text: silhouette-score-heterogeneity-assessment Use when you have preprocessed bulk RNA-seq data for a cohort (e.g., < 100 samples) and need to decide how many representative clusters exist so that all representatives can be selected in one batch instead of multi-round active learning. You plan to iteratively improve inference over multiple sequencing rounds — use scSemiProfiler's active learning module instead of the one-shot global mode You want per-target-sample single-cell deconvolution from bulk data plus a single-cell reference — that is the bulk deconvolution (single-cell level) pipeline, not heterogeneity assessment for representative selection http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 A step within scSemiProfiler's global mode that assesses cohort heterogeneity using Silhouette scores and bulk-data visualization to determine the appropriate number of representative clusters before K-Means selection. It enables all representatives to be chosen in a single round from the initial bulk-data analysis, avoiding multi-round active learning and associated batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1

skills.description: Use when evaluating a batch-corrected/embedded Seurat object (e.g. STACAS output) to determine whether cell type structure survives integration, or when demonstrating that batch-mixing metrics like iLISI reward overcorrected embeddings.

skills.search_text: silhouette-width-celltype-assessment Use when evaluating a batch-corrected/embedded Seurat object (e.g. STACAS output) to determine whether cell type structure survives integration, or when demonstrating that batch-mixing metrics like iLISI reward overcorrected embeddings. Cell type annotations are absent — CiLISI and similar metrics require cell type labels Cell types are present in only one dataset — CiLISI cannot be calculated for them Datasets have highly unequal cell numbers or lopsided cell proportions across batches — LISI/CiLISI are suboptimal and robust batch-mixing metrics are still lacking http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill that scores integrated scRNA-seq embeddings with cell type-aware metrics — average silhouette width (ASW), CiLISI, and normalized cLISI from the scIntegrationMetrics R package — to test whether an integration (e.g. STACAS) preserves biological variance while correcting batch effects, as opposed to overcorrecting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z

skills.description: Use when you have external cluster labels (e.g., from a different modality or a GMM fit) and need to quantify how well-separated those clusters are in an expression matrix, such as testing whether denoising recovers structure lost to dropout.
skills.name: silhouette-width-cluster-label-validation
skills.search_text: silhouette-width-cluster-label-validation Use when you have external cluster labels (e.g., from a different modality or a GMM fit) and need to quantify how well-separated those clusters are in an expression matrix, such as testing whether denoising recovers structure lost to dropout. You have no pre-defined cluster labels and are still discovering clusters — silhouette here only scores externally supplied labels, it does not determine them. The denoised output may suffer overimputation (e.g., inadequate hyperparameters such as too low-dimensional a bottleneck), which can inflate silhouette widths by artificially sharpening structure rather than recovering true biology. The features underlying the labels are absent from the expression matrix you are scoring against (e.g., NCAM1/FCGR3A not measured). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validate that cluster labels (e.g., protein- or RNA-derived cell types) are consistent with a given expression space by computing average silhouette widths, as in the DCA paper where CD56bright/CD56dim NK sub-population labels were scored against protein, original RNA, and DCA-denoised RNA expression of NCAM1/FCGR3A. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2

skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no pre-defined cluster labels and are still discovering clusters — silhouette here only scores externally supplied labels, it does not determine them. skills.description: Use when a labeled two-population scRNA-seq mixture is available and you need a controlled simulation of rare-population abundance (e.g. 0.5–5%) to benchmark rare-cell detection tools with F1 scores.
skills.name: simulated-cell-mixture-dilution
skills.search_text: simulated-cell-mixture-dilution Use when a labeled two-population scRNA-seq mixture is available and you need a controlled simulation of rare-population abundance (e.g. 0.5–5%) to benchmark rare-cell detection tools with F1 scores. The dataset has more than two labeled cell types or no ground-truth rare-population annotation, so controlled dilution and F1 computation are not possible. The goal is detecting novel, unannotated rare cell types in real tissue data rather than benchmarking known-population recovery (FiRE itself does not discriminate outliers from minor cell types). Input is a small mixture where the rare population fraction is already fixed and dilution simulation would leave too few rare cells for stable F1 estimates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark rare-cell detection methods by bioinformatically diluting an annotated rare cell population (e.g. Jurkat) into an abundant background (e.g. 293T) at controlled fractions (0.5%, 2.5%, 5%) and comparing method performance via F1 score against the ground-truth rare labels, as done for FiRE vs LOF, RaceID and GiniClust. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Benchmark rare-cell detection methods by bioinformatically diluting an annotated rare cell population (e.g. Jurkat) into an abundant background (e.g. 293T) at controlled fractions (0.5%, 2.5%, 5%) and comparing method performance via F1 score against the ground-truth rare labels, as done for FiRE vs LOF, RaceID and GiniClust.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has more than two labeled cell types or no ground-truth rare-population annotation, so controlled dilution and F1 computation are not possible. skills.search_text: simulated-doublet-training-set-labeling Use when fitting an ensemble doublet classifier (Chord GBM/AdaBoost) that requires labeled training data built from simulated doublets scored by existing detection tools rather than experimental ground truth. Ground-truth doublet labels are available experimentally (e.g., cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet); simulated-doublet labels are unnecessary and the ensemble training approach adds cost without benefit. skills.summary: Benchmark the CCSF cMAP embedding against PCA (and Leiden) baselines for clustering Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq data, using k-means with the CCSF-learned class count and scoring with adjusted Rand index and clustering accuracy. skills.summary: Generates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices from negative-binomial (NB) and zero-inflated negative-binomial (ZINB) generative models so that feature-selection methods such as the S-E entropy model, HVG, Gini, M3Drop, SCTransform, Fano factor, and RaceID3 can be compared with ground-truth informative genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real (non-simulated) scRNA-seq data where the goal is selecting variable genes on actual expression matrices rather than benchmarking against known ground truth The question is assessing purity of already-defined cell clusters (use ROGUE's CalculateRogue/Entropy on a real cluster, not the NB/ZINB simulation benchmark) The data are not raw UMI count matrices from NB/ZINB-like generative processes (e.g. log-transformed qPCR-style data)

skills.summary: Generate artificial count-level scRNA-Seq datasets with known ground-truth cell labels using the nicococo/scRNA package's scRNA-generate-data.sh / cmd_generate_data.py, in the paper's benchmark configuration (10,000 genes, 1,800 cells, 100 sets per overlap setting). These simulated datasets provide the controlled ground truth against which transfer-learning clustering and KTA/ARI agreement are evaluated.

skills.search_text: simulated-scrnaseq-ground-truth-validation Use when evaluating or comparing clustering methods on scRNA-seq data where simulated ground-truth cluster labels exist, especially to test whether a method resolves rare subpopulations placed close together. skills.description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference or RNA-velocity-based methods against known ground truth, or when replicated simulated datasets (e.g., 785 cells x 600 genes cycle-tree) are needed to quantify pseudotime accuracy.
skills.name: simulated-scrnaseq-trajectory-generation
skills.search_text: simulated-scrnaseq-trajectory-generation Use when benchmarking trajectory inference or RNA-velocity-based methods against known ground truth, or when replicated simulated datasets (e.g., 785 cells x 600 genes cycle-tree) are needed to quantify pseudotime accuracy. The goal is inference on real scRNA-seq data without a ground-truth trajectory — simulation is only for controlled benchmarking, and the article notes all velocity-based methods are affected by noise in estimated RNA velocity. The analysis requires realistic dataset complexity (batch effects, dropouts, real topology uncertainty) that the simple cycle-tree simulation with fixed 785x600 dimensions does not capture. Evaluating methods whose output is cluster-level only (e.g., Directed-PAGA), which cannot produce the high-resolution per-cell pseudotime needed for per-path Kendall correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth trajectories (e.g., VeloSim cycle-tree topologies with spliced/unspliced counts and pseudotime) so that trajectory inference methods such as CellPath can be benchmarked against baselines using Kendall rank correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Generate simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth trajectories (e.g., VeloSim cycle-tree topologies with spliced/unspliced counts and pseudotime) so that trajectory inference methods such as CellPath can be benchmarked against baselines using Kendall rank correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inference on real scRNA-seq data without a ground-truth trajectory — simulation is only for controlled benchmarking, and the article notes all velocity-based methods are affected by noise in estimated RNA velocity. The analysis requires realistic dataset complexity (batch effects, dropouts, real topology uncertainty) that the simple cycle-tree simulation with fixed 785x600 dimensions does not capture. Evaluating methods whose output is cluster-level only (e.g., Directed-PAGA), which cannot produce the high-resolution per-cell pseudotime needed for per-path Kendall correlation.

skills.description: Use when you have a trained generative scRNA-seq simulator's output (.h5ad) plus the original reference dataset and need to verify that developmental trajectories, transitional states, and pseudotime ordering were preserved before downstream use.
skills.name: simulated-vs-experimental-trajectory-benchmarking
skills.search_text: simulated-vs-experimental-trajectory-benchmarking Use when you have a trained generative scRNA-seq simulator's output (.h5ad) plus the original reference dataset and need to verify that developmental trajectories, transitional states, and pseudotime ordering were preserved before downstream use. The model was trained on a completely new dataset or one with significantly different numbers of genes and TFs — hyperparameters may need re-tuning via a validation set before trajectory fidelity can be expected You want to evaluate numeric GRN inference benchmarking (AUROC of inferred edges against ground truth) rather than trajectory/trajectory-structure preservation — use the --benchmark_grn evaluation instead The simulation goal is unnormalized raw count generation — GRouNdGAN only generates library-size normalized expression values across the considered genes and TFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Qualitative-quantitative benchmarking skill that checks whether GRouNdGAN-simulated single-cell RNA-seq data preserves the cell trajectories and pseudo-time ordering of an experimental reference (e.g., BoneMarrow hematopoiesis) by jointly embedding both datasets in scanpy and comparing PAGA structure, diffusion pseudotime, and lineage marker gene activation order. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48516-6
skills.summary: Qualitative-quantitative benchmarking skill that checks whether GRouNdGAN-simulated single-cell RNA-seq data preserves the cell trajectories and pseudo-time ordering of an experimental reference (e.g., BoneMarrow hematopoiesis) by jointly embedding both datasets in scanpy and comparing PAGA structure, diffusion pseudotime, and lineage marker gene activation order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model was trained on a completely new dataset or one with significantly different numbers of genes and TFs — hyperparameters may need re-tuning via a validation set before trajectory fidelity can be expected You want to evaluate numeric GRN inference benchmarking (AUROC of inferred edges against ground truth) rather than trajectory/trajectory-structure preservation — use the --benchmark_grn evaluation instead The simulation goal is unnormalized raw count generation — GRouNdGAN only generates library-size normalized expression values across the considered genes and TFs

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method (e.g. AutoClass vs DCA) against a known ground truth, or when testing robustness to hyperparameters such as bottleneck size, pre-clustering number K, or classifier weight.
skills.name: simulation-based-benchmark-evaluation-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: simulation-based-benchmark-evaluation-scrnaseq Use when benchmarking an scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method (e.g. AutoClass vs DCA) against a known ground truth, or when testing robustness to hyperparameters such as bottleneck size, pre-clustering number K, or classifier weight. Input is real scRNA-Seq data without simulated ground truth — ASW/ARI against known groups and MSE/dropout0/true0 against true counts require true labels and true expression values The goal is biological discovery (e.g. differential expression on a real dataset like Baron) rather than method benchmarking or robustness testing The candidate method cannot be retrained programmatically across a hyperparameter grid (no Python/TensorFlow >=2.0 interface) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Evaluate scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation methods on simulated ground-truth data (Splatter Dataset 1: 1000 genes, 500 cells, six groups) by sweeping method hyperparameters and scoring clustering (ASW, ARI), reconstruction (MSE), and zero-recovery (dropout0/true0 ratio) metrics against true counts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Evaluate scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation methods on simulated ground-truth data (Splatter Dataset 1: 1000 genes, 500 cells, six groups) by sweeping method hyperparameters and scoring clustering (ASW, ARI), reconstruction (MSE), and zero-recovery (dropout0/true0 ratio) metrics against true counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-Seq data without simulated ground truth — ASW/ARI against known groups and MSE/dropout0/true0 against true counts require true labels and true expression values The goal is biological discovery (e.g. differential expression on a real dataset like Baron) rather than method benchmarking or robustness testing The candidate method cannot be retrained programmatically across a hyperparameter grid (no Python/TensorFlow >=2.0 interface)

skills.description: Use when you need to compare precision and sensitivity of single-cell CNA callers against simulated ground-truth events (200 kb–5 Mb single-copy losses/gains) on high-coverage scWGS benchmark data.
skills.name: simulation-based-cna-caller-benchmarking
skills.search_text: simulation-based-cna-caller-benchmarking Use when you need to compare precision and sensitivity of single-cell CNA callers against simulated ground-truth events (200 kb–5 Mb single-copy losses/gains) on high-coverage scWGS benchmark data. The task is calling clonal, megabase-scale CNAs in low-coverage (<0.05x) scWGS cancer data — CHISEL and the other comparators were designed for that regime, not for high-resolution benchmarking of small non-clonal events Input is real (non-simulated) data without a ground-truth CNA event list — precision/sensitivity against truth cannot be computed; use qualitative comparison instead Only bulk WGS is available with no single-cell BAMs — none of the five single-cell callers can be run http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce the precision/sensitivity benchmark of HiScanner versus Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN, and CHISEL for detecting simulated non-clonal CNAs (200 kb–5 Mb) on high-coverage (~30x) SDX single-cell WGS data, computing TP/FP/FN counts and per-size, per-type metrics from harmonized allele-specific CNA calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Reproduce the precision/sensitivity benchmark of HiScanner versus Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN, and CHISEL for detecting simulated non-clonal CNAs (200 kb–5 Mb) on high-coverage (~30x) SDX single-cell WGS data, computing TP/FP/FN counts and per-size, per-type metrics from harmonized allele-specific CNA calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is calling clonal, megabase-scale CNAs in low-coverage (<0.05x) scWGS cancer data — CHISEL and the other comparators were designed for that regime, not for high-resolution benchmarking of small non-clonal events Input is real (non-simulated) data without a ground-truth CNA event list — precision/sensitivity against truth cannot be computed; use qualitative comparison instead Only bulk WGS is available with no single-cell BAMs — none of the five single-cell callers can be run

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing DE method power on single-cell RNA-seq data where simulated ground truth (known DE genes, coverage rate, tau1/tau0 parameters) is available, or when reproducing iDEA power-gain results.
skills.name: simulation-based-de-power-evaluation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-de-power-evaluation Use when evaluating or comparing DE method power on single-cell RNA-seq data where simulated ground truth (known DE genes, coverage rate, tau1/tau0 parameters) is available, or when reproducing iDEA power-gain results. Only real scRNA-seq data with no known DE ground truth is available — empirical power cannot be computed without simulated or validated DE genes. The goal is gene set enrichment (GSE) power or FDR calibration rather than gene-level differential expression power. Input data is bulk RNA-seq or non-count data incompatible with the MAST/edgeR/zingeR summary-statistic pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark differential expression power on scRNA-seq simulations with known DE genes, comparing standalone DE methods (MAST, edgeR, zingeR) against iDEA-augmented aggregation of their summary statistics, at a fixed true FDR of 5%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Benchmark differential expression power on scRNA-seq simulations with known DE genes, comparing standalone DE methods (MAST, edgeR, zingeR) against iDEA-augmented aggregation of their summary statistics, at a fixed true FDR of 5%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only real scRNA-seq data with no known DE ground truth is available — empirical power cannot be computed without simulated or validated DE genes. The goal is gene set enrichment (GSE) power or FDR calibration rather than gene-level differential expression power. Input data is bulk RNA-seq or non-count data incompatible with the MAST/edgeR/zingeR summary-statistic pipeline.

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a scalable algorithmic variant (e.g. chunked E-step with Chunk=TRUE, chunk.size=500 or 1000) reproduces the accuracy of a reference implementation while reducing runtime, or when benchmarking confounding-factor inference on simulated scRNAseq grids.
skills.name: simulation-based-estimation-error-evaluation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-estimation-error-evaluation Use when evaluating whether a scalable algorithmic variant (e.g. chunked E-step with Chunk=TRUE, chunk.size=500 or 1000) reproduces the accuracy of a reference implementation while reducing runtime, or when benchmarking confounding-factor inference on simulated scRNAseq grids. Downstream-analysis evaluation beyond confounding-effect estimation — the paper notes the 'best' confounding removal method depends on the downstream question and only clustering-type settings were evaluated When the goal is inference of biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, due to model identifiability When a count-based error model is required — the paper's framework does not model count data, which is left as future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark the accuracy and CPU cost of an inference method (here scPLS confounding-effect estimation via naive vs. block-wise chunked EM) on simulated scRNAseq data across a grid of cell/gene counts, recording estimation error of the inferred confounding effects and elapsed CPU time for comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy and CPU cost of an inference method (here scPLS confounding-effect estimation via naive vs. block-wise chunked EM) on simulated scRNAseq data across a grid of cell/gene counts, recording estimation error of the inferred confounding effects and elapsed CPU time for comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Downstream-analysis evaluation beyond confounding-effect estimation — the paper notes the 'best' confounding removal method depends on the downstream question and only clustering-type settings were evaluated When the goal is inference of biological factors u_i themselves — scPLS can only infer biological effects (Lambda_u u_i), not the factors, due to model identifiability When a count-based error model is required — the paper's framework does not model count data, which is left as future work

skills.description: Use when you need to verify that a Bayesian-FDR intrinsic/differential gene selection procedure recovers known true DE genes in simulation and yields biologically interpretable enriched pathways on real data.
skills.name: simulation-based-gene-recovery-validation
skills.search_text: simulation-based-gene-recovery-validation Use when you need to verify that a Bayesian-FDR intrinsic/differential gene selection procedure recovers known true DE genes in simulation and yields biologically interpretable enriched pathways on real data. Input is raw count data that has not yet been fitted with BUSseq_MCMC — the indicator probabilities xi_gk required for FDR ranking do not exist before model fitting The analysis goal is batch-effect correction or cell-type clustering rather than validating differential gene detection — use corrected_read_counts or cell-type clustering steps instead The experimental design is completely confounded (each batch measures disjoint cell types) — the paper states no method is applicable in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates a spike-and-slab Bayesian-FDR intrinsic gene detection procedure by running it on simulated scRNA-seq data with planted differentially expressed genes, checking recovery of the 500 true intrinsic genes at approximately 2% true FDR under a 5% Bayesian FDR cutoff, and on real data by confirming biologically meaningful KEGG enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Validates a spike-and-slab Bayesian-FDR intrinsic gene detection procedure by running it on simulated scRNA-seq data with planted differentially expressed genes, checking recovery of the 500 true intrinsic genes at approximately 2% true FDR under a 5% Bayesian FDR cutoff, and on real data by confirming biologically meaningful KEGG enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count data that has not yet been fitted with BUSseq_MCMC — the indicator probabilities xi_gk required for FDR ranking do not exist before model fitting The analysis goal is batch-effect correction or cell-type clustering rather than validating differential gene detection — use corrected_read_counts or cell-type clustering steps instead The experimental design is completely confounded (each batch measures disjoint cell types) — the paper states no method is applicable in that setting

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS with Pearson, SSN, pySCENIC) and synthetic ground truth is required because real single-cell data lacks a known regulatory network reference.
skills.name: simulation-based-grn-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: simulation-based-grn-method-benchmarking Use when evaluating or comparing cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS with Pearson, SSN, pySCENIC) and synthetic ground truth is required because real single-cell data lacks a known regulatory network reference. The goal is benchmarking RNA velocity or trajectory/alignment methods rather than cell-specific regulatory network inference — those use dyngen's other evaluation protocols (velocity vectors, ABWAP alignment scores). PANDA is the intended method, since dyngen datasets provide no motif data and PANDA requires motif-tf-gene inputs. The analysis claims absolute performance on real biological data — the article only supports quantitative CSNI evaluation against synthetic ground truth. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods against dyngen's fully known ground-truth cellwise regulatory networks, scoring predictions per cell with mean AUROC and mean AUPR over simulated datasets (e.g. the 42 dyngen datasets from 14 backbones with three seeds each). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) methods against dyngen's fully known ground-truth cellwise regulatory networks, scoring predictions per cell with mean AUROC and mean AUPR over simulated datasets (e.g. the 42 dyngen datasets from 14 backbones with three seeds each).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is benchmarking RNA velocity or trajectory/alignment methods rather than cell-specific regulatory network inference — those use dyngen's other evaluation protocols (velocity vectors, ABWAP alignment scores). PANDA is the intended method, since dyngen datasets provide no motif data and PANDA requires motif-tf-gene inputs. The analysis claims absolute performance on real biological data — the article only supports quantitative CSNI evaluation against synthetic ground truth.

skills.description: Use when comparing cell-type deconvolution or clustering methods on spatial transcriptomics data where ground truth is unavailable in real tissue, by simulating multi-cellular pixels with known cell-type proportions and evaluating RMSE of estimated proportions.
skills.name: simulation-based-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: simulation-based-method-benchmarking Use when comparing cell-type deconvolution or clustering methods on spatial transcriptomics data where ground truth is unavailable in real tissue, by simulating multi-cellular pixels with known cell-type proportions and evaluating RMSE of estimated proportions. Real datasets lacking simulated ground truth — per-pixel RMSE against true proportions cannot be computed Sub-cellular resolution ST data, where the paper notes STdeconvolve may not be best suited and new methods will be needed Datasets where cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels — the paper reports STdeconvolve may fail to deconvolve when genes lack variability across pixels http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a deconvolution method against competing approaches (e.g., regular transcriptional clustering and BayesSpace resolution-enhanced clustering) on simulated multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data with known ground-truth cell-type proportions, quantifying per-pixel RMSE and testing significance with the Diebold-Mariano test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a deconvolution method against competing approaches (e.g., regular transcriptional clustering and BayesSpace resolution-enhanced clustering) on simulated multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data with known ground-truth cell-type proportions, quantifying per-pixel RMSE and testing significance with the Diebold-Mariano test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real datasets lacking simulated ground truth — per-pixel RMSE against true proportions cannot be computed Sub-cellular resolution ST data, where the paper notes STdeconvolve may not be best suited and new methods will be needed Datasets where cell-type proportions are homogeneous across pixels — the paper reports STdeconvolve may fail to deconvolve when genes lack variability across pixels

skills.description: Use when you need to rank or validate differential abundance testing methods against ground truth on synthetic compositional count data, e.g. at low replicate numbers where FDR control is critical.
skills.name: simulation-based-method-comparison
skills.search_text: simulation-based-method-comparison Use when you need to rank or validate differential abundance testing methods against ground truth on synthetic compositional count data, e.g. at low replicate numbers where FDR control is critical. Ground-truth differential effects are unknown (real patient data), so MCC and average precision against simulated truth cannot be computed The goal is interpreting credible cell-type shifts in a single biological dataset (use credible_effects and summary() directly rather than benchmarking) The benchmark goal is not differential compositional testing, e.g. gene-level or clustering benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmark differential compositional analysis methods (scCODA vs. ANCOM-BC, ANCOM, ALDEx2, ALR t-test, Beta-Binomial, t-test, scDC, Dirichlet-multinomial) on synthetic case-control single-cell count data with known ground-truth effects, scoring each method by Matthews correlation coefficient, ROC AUC, and average precision. It exists because without simulated truth, false-discovery control and detection power of compositional tests cannot be fairly quantified. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Benchmark differential compositional analysis methods (scCODA vs. ANCOM-BC, ANCOM, ALDEx2, ALR t-test, Beta-Binomial, t-test, scDC, Dirichlet-multinomial) on synthetic case-control single-cell count data with known ground-truth effects, scoring each method by Matthews correlation coefficient, ROC AUC, and average precision. It exists because without simulated truth, false-discovery control and detection power of compositional tests cannot be fairly quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ground-truth differential effects are unknown (real patient data), so MCC and average precision against simulated truth cannot be computed The goal is interpreting credible cell-type shifts in a single biological dataset (use credible_effects and summary() directly rather than benchmarking) The benchmark goal is not differential compositional testing, e.g. gene-level or clustering benchmarks

skills.description: Use when evaluating a CNA caller's sensitivity/precision across variant sizes and coverages, or choosing bin size and depth for scWGS analysis using simulated data with known truth events.

Used to identify the parameter combination with the best precision-sensitivity trade-off, which for HiScanner was 100 kb bins at 30×. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Benchmark a single-cell CNA caller by grid-searching bin size (50/100/500 kb) and sequencing depth (0.5×/10×/30×) on simulated scWGS data, matching called segments against truth events to compute precision and sensitivity per CNA type and size class. Used to identify the parameter combination with the best precision-sensitivity trade-off, which for HiScanner was 100 kb bins at 30×.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are real biological samples without simulated truth events — precision/sensitivity cannot be computed without ground truth The analysis goal is CNA discovery in a new dataset rather than method benchmarking or parameter selection

skills.description: Use when a new distance-estimation or differential-state method must be checked for accuracy and calibration: simulated data with known per-cell-type true distances are available or can be generated (here via scDist::simData with nct=10, N1=N2=5).
skills.name: simulation-based-method-validation-against-ground-truth
skills.search_text: simulation-based-method-validation-against-ground-truth Use when a new distance-estimation or differential-state method must be checked for accuracy and calibration: simulated data with known per-cell-type true distances are available or can be generated (here via scDist::simData with nct=10, N1=N2=5). Data are over-clustered: the article shows over-clustering makes scDist produce false negatives, with median distance decaying toward 0 as cluster number increases, so simulated-validation conclusions will not transfer You need a cluster-free differential-state test: the article states designing a cluster-free extension of scDist is future work, so validation against clustered simulation ground truth cannot certify such a setting Only raw (unnormalized) counts are available: scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts, so the simulation must supply normalized data (scTransform Pearson residuals recommended) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validate scDist's distance inference by generating a fully simulated single-cell dataset with known ground-truth between-condition distances (simData), running the full PC-projection plus mixed-model pipeline, and comparing estimated distances and p-values against D.true per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Validate scDist's distance inference by generating a fully simulated single-cell dataset with known ground-truth between-condition distances (simData), running the full PC-projection plus mixed-model pipeline, and comparing estimated distances and p-values against D.true per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are over-clustered: the article shows over-clustering makes scDist produce false negatives, with median distance decaying toward 0 as cluster number increases, so simulated-validation conclusions will not transfer You need a cluster-free differential-state test: the article states designing a cluster-free extension of scDist is future work, so validation against clustered simulation ground truth cannot certify such a setting Only raw (unnormalized) counts are available: scDist cannot currently be applied directly to raw counts, so the simulation must supply normalized data (scTransform Pearson residuals recommended)

skills.description: Use when evaluating a circRNA full-length assembly/quantification tool against simulated paired-end FASTQ reads with known ground-truth circular isoforms, to characterize how sequencing depth or read length affects assembly sensitivity, precision, and F1.
skills.name: simulation-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: simulation-benchmark-comparison Use when evaluating a circRNA full-length assembly/quantification tool against simulated paired-end FASTQ reads with known ground-truth circular isoforms, to characterize how sequencing depth or read length affects assembly sensitivity, precision, and F1. Input is real experimental RNA-seq data without ground-truth circular isoform sequences — sensitivity/precision cannot be computed as in this simulation benchmark Data are not RNase R-treated: the article states CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, so simulated/real benchmarks must model rRNA-depleted, RNase R-treated conditions The goal is circRNA detection (back-splice site identification) rather than full-length isoform assembly — use upstream detectors like CIRI2 or CIRCexplorer2 instead of benchmarking CircAST assembly output http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark full-length circRNA transcript assembly (CircAST with the EMPC algorithm) on simulated paired-end RNA-seq datasets, comparing assembled isoforms against simulation ground truth to compute sensitivity, precision, and F1 across sequencing depths and read lengths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Benchmark full-length circRNA transcript assembly (CircAST with the EMPC algorithm) on simulated paired-end RNA-seq datasets, comparing assembled isoforms against simulation ground truth to compute sensitivity, precision, and F1 across sequencing depths and read lengths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental RNA-seq data without ground-truth circular isoform sequences — sensitivity/precision cannot be computed as in this simulation benchmark Data are not RNase R-treated: the article states CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, so simulated/real benchmarks must model rRNA-depleted, RNase R-treated conditions The goal is circRNA detection (back-splice site identification) rather than full-length isoform assembly — use upstream detectors like CIRI2 or CIRCexplorer2 instead of benchmarking CircAST assembly output

skills.description: Use when evaluating assembly/quantification accuracy on simulated data where performance may depend on structural complexity (e.g., overlapping genomic regions among circRNAs), requiring metrics stratified by a complexity bin such as RI 1-4 vs RI > 4.
skills.name: simulation-benchmark-stratification
skills.search_text: simulation-benchmark-stratification Use when evaluating assembly/quantification accuracy on simulated data where performance may depend on structural complexity (e.g., overlapping genomic regions among circRNAs), requiring metrics stratified by a complexity bin such as RI 1-4 vs RI > 4. Data are real experimental reads without simulated ground-truth transcripts — sensitivity/precision against truth cannot be computed Each BSJ site is isolated (no overlapping genomic regions among circRNAs), so all sites fall in a single RI bin and stratification is uninformative Goal is circRNA detection (BSJ identification) rather than full-length isoform assembly and quantification evaluation http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratifies benchmark results on simulated circRNA data by a computed overlap metric — the relation index (RI), the cardinality of the equivalence class of overlapping back-splice junction (BSJ) sites — to quantify how locus complexity degrades CircAST's assembly precision, sensitivity, and quantification accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Stratifies benchmark results on simulated circRNA data by a computed overlap metric — the relation index (RI), the cardinality of the equivalence class of overlapping back-splice junction (BSJ) sites — to quantify how locus complexity degrades CircAST's assembly precision, sensitivity, and quantification accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real experimental reads without simulated ground-truth transcripts — sensitivity/precision against truth cannot be computed Each BSJ site is isolated (no overlapping genomic regions among circRNAs), so all sites fall in a single RI bin and stratification is uninformative Goal is circRNA detection (BSJ identification) rather than full-length isoform assembly and quantification evaluation

skills.description: Use when you need controlled simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks to quantify how varying batch-effect and cell-type effect strengths (plus balanced vs unbalanced cell-type proportions) affect batch-correction tool performance.
skills.name: simulation-condition-grid-configuration
skills.search_text: simulation-condition-grid-configuration Use when you need controlled simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks to quantify how varying batch-effect and cell-type effect strengths (plus balanced vs unbalanced cell-type proportions) affect batch-correction tool performance. Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data rather than a simulation scenario — use batch-correction methods (e.g. scJIVE, Harmony) directly instead of generating synthetic conditions The analysis question does not involve systematically varying batch/cell-type effect strengths, so a single fixed Splatter condition would suffice rather than the full 100-condition grid http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Configures a systematic grid of in silico scRNA-seq benchmark conditions using the Splatter R package (Splat model), varying cell-type effect and batch effect location parameters over {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} crossed with balanced/unbalanced cell-type proportions to yield 100 simulation conditions for evaluating batch-effect correction methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae134
skills.summary: Configures a systematic grid of in silico scRNA-seq benchmark conditions using the Splatter R package (Splat model), varying cell-type effect and batch effect location parameters over {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1} crossed with balanced/unbalanced cell-type proportions to yield 100 simulation conditions for evaluating batch-effect correction methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental scRNA-seq data rather than a simulation scenario — use batch-correction methods (e.g. scJIVE, Harmony) directly instead of generating synthetic conditions The analysis question does not involve systematically varying batch/cell-type effect strengths, so a single fixed Splatter condition would suffice rather than the full 100-condition grid

skills.description: Use when benchmarking enrichment methods (pareg, MGSA, FET, topGO, blitzGSEA) on simulated differential-expression studies where robustness to noise must be quantified at a fixed recall target.

skills.search_text: simulation-noise-parameter-tuning Use when benchmarking enrichment methods (pareg, MGSA, FET, topGO, blitzGSEA) on simulated differential-expression studies where robustness to noise must be quantified at a fixed recall target. The goal is enriching a real experimental study rather than measuring a method's robustness to synthetic noise Ground-truth active pathways are unavailable — precision-recall interpolation at fixed recall requires known true positives The pathway database lacks enough redundancy/clustering for similarity_sample to define a meaningful activation set http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A synthetic-benchmark design for evaluating pathway enrichment methods under controlled noise: activate pathways via similarity sampling, inject noise by setting η (e.g. η=0.25) and ρ (ρ=0.5), then score methods on precision-recall curves to obtain median precision at fixed recall (80%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad522
skills.summary: A synthetic-benchmark design for evaluating pathway enrichment methods under controlled noise: activate pathways via similarity sampling, inject noise by setting η (e.g. η=0.25) and ρ (ρ=0.5), then score methods on precision-recall curves to obtain median precision at fixed recall (80%).
