skills.name: simulation-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-estimation Use when you need sensitivity benchmarks for a pathway or gene-set method on synthetic scRNA-seq data with a known implanted target pathway, and ground-truth recovery can be scored per scenario. The question is real-data pathway analysis (e.g. comparing COVID-19 vs healthy peripheral blood) rather than synthetic benchmarking with a known implanted pathway The input is already a scored comparison of pathway activity with no simulation component and only needs interpretation (qval as primary statistic, fold change/enrichment as secondary) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Estimate simulation parameters from a reference single-cell dataset with Splatter's splatEstimate() and generate controlled two-population simulations (~17,000 background genes plus an implanted 200-gene perturbed pathway) to benchmark pathway analysis tools such as SCPA against fGSEA, GSVA, AUCell and others. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Estimate simulation parameters from a reference single-cell dataset with Splatter's splatEstimate() and generate controlled two-population simulations (~17,000 background genes plus an implanted 200-gene perturbed pathway) to benchmark pathway analysis tools such as SCPA against fGSEA, GSVA, AUCell and others.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is real-data pathway analysis (e.g. comparing COVID-19 vs healthy peripheral blood) rather than synthetic benchmarking with a known implanted pathway The input is already a scored comparison of pathway activity with no simulation component and only needs interpretation (qval as primary statistic, fold change/enrichment as secondary)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking normalization or differential-expression methods on scRNA-seq requires simulated datasets with known ground-truth logFC whose mean/variance/library-size structure matches real UMI count data.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-fitting-from-umi-counts
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-fitting-from-umi-counts Use when benchmarking normalization or differential-expression methods on scRNA-seq requires simulated datasets with known ground-truth logFC whose mean/variance/library-size structure matches real UMI count data. Analyzing real (non-simulated) scRNA-seq data without ground-truth logFC — there is no reference against which to compute regression bias and R2. Full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq platforms — the article only focused on UMI-based datasets and notes full-length platforms may need revalidation of nonlinear covariates. The goal is biological discovery or differential expression calling itself rather than quantifying method accuracy against a known effect-size ground truth. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits SymSim and Splatter simulation parameters to the empirical count distributions of real UMI scRNA-seq data (e.g., QC-filtered Perturb-seq) to generate two-group differential-expression datasets with known ground-truth logFC, enabling bias and variance (R²) benchmarking of normalization/DE methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Fits SymSim and Splatter simulation parameters to the empirical count distributions of real UMI scRNA-seq data (e.g., QC-filtered Perturb-seq) to generate two-group differential-expression datasets with known ground-truth logFC, enabling bias and variance (R²) benchmarking of normalization/DE methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing real (non-simulated) scRNA-seq data without ground-truth logFC — there is no reference against which to compute regression bias and R2. Full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq platforms — the article only focused on UMI-based datasets and notes full-length platforms may need revalidation of nonlinear covariates. The goal is biological discovery or differential expression calling itself rather than quantifying method accuracy against a known effect-size ground truth.

skills.description: Use when a simulation must be calibrated to a specific real scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Zeisel UMI cortex counts) so downstream benchmarks or experimental-design curves reflect realistic depth, dropout, and variability.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-fitting-to-real-data
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-fitting-to-real-data Use when a simulation must be calibrated to a specific real scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Zeisel UMI cortex counts) so downstream benchmarks or experimental-design curves reflect realistic depth, dropout, and variability. The analysis goal is purely theoretical and does not need calibration to any real dataset (e.g., a closed-form binomial bound on detecting a rare population) The real dataset's protocol or statistics have no counterpart in the pre-computed simulated grid (BestMatchParams relies on grid-search database coverage) Fitting kinetic parameters when cells are not dividable into clusters sharing the same kinetic parameters http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit SymSim simulation parameters (Sigma, capture efficiency alpha, sequencing depth, and kinetic kon/koff/s parameters) so that simulated datasets reproduce the statistical properties of a given real scRNA-seq dataset, via BestMatchParams grid-search matching or MCMC kinetic fitting with RJAGS. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Fit SymSim simulation parameters (Sigma, capture efficiency alpha, sequencing depth, and kinetic kon/koff/s parameters) so that simulated datasets reproduce the statistical properties of a given real scRNA-seq dataset, via BestMatchParams grid-search matching or MCMC kinetic fitting with RJAGS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is purely theoretical and does not need calibration to any real dataset (e.g., a closed-form binomial bound on detecting a rare population) The real dataset's protocol or statistics have no counterpart in the pre-computed simulated grid (BestMatchParams relies on grid-search database coverage) Fitting kinetic parameters when cells are not dividable into clusters sharing the same kinetic parameters

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA assembly or isoform-quantification method against known ground truth, or when validating that regenerated simulation datasets match a published design (depths, read lengths, loci, conditions).
skills.name: simulation-parameter-series-design
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-series-design Use when benchmarking a circRNA assembly or isoform-quantification method against known ground truth, or when validating that regenerated simulation datasets match a published design (depths, read lengths, loci, conditions). The goal is empirical benchmarking on real RNA-seq data rather than controlled simulation with known ground-truth abundances The target circular transcripts are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts, so simulated panels must be built on annotated exonic loci http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Designs controlled simulation panels of circular RNA sequencing data — depth series, read-length series, and multi-locus/multi-condition isoform panels with assigned ground-truth abundances — to benchmark full-length assembly and relative quantification of circRNA isoform expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Designs controlled simulation panels of circular RNA sequencing data — depth series, read-length series, and multi-locus/multi-condition isoform panels with assigned ground-truth abundances — to benchmark full-length assembly and relative quantification of circRNA isoform expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is empirical benchmarking on real RNA-seq data rather than controlled simulation with known ground-truth abundances The target circular transcripts are intronic or intergenic — the CircAST pipeline quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts, so simulated panels must be built on annotated exonic loci

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a method whose performance may depend on simulation settings (e.g. differential-expression level, rarity of a cell population) and multiple synthetic datasets with ground-truth labels are needed across a parameter grid.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-sweep
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-sweep Use when benchmarking a method whose performance may depend on simulation settings (e.g. differential-expression level, rarity of a cell population) and multiple synthetic datasets with ground-truth labels are needed across a parameter grid. The input is real experimental data without ground-truth labels — a parameter sweep over simulated profiles provides no benchmarking signal there; use biological validation (e.g. known marker genes) instead. The method under test is insensitive to simulation parameters and a single simulated dataset suffices — the sweep's cost is not justified. The simulation tool cannot encode the factor being swept (e.g. no differential-expression parameter analogous to Splatter's de.prob), so the grid would not vary the relevant difficulty axis. http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematically varies simulation parameters (e.g. Splatter de.prob from 0.1 to 0.8 and rare population size from 2 to 100 cells) to generate a grid of synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with known ground truth, enabling robust benchmarking of rare-cell detectors such as GapClust, RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS and FiRE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Systematically varies simulation parameters (e.g. Splatter de.prob from 0.1 to 0.8 and rare population size from 2 to 100 cells) to generate a grid of synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with known ground truth, enabling robust benchmarking of rare-cell detectors such as GapClust, RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS and FiRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real experimental data without ground-truth labels — a parameter sweep over simulated profiles provides no benchmarking signal there; use biological validation (e.g. known marker genes) instead. The method under test is insensitive to simulation parameters and a single simulated dataset suffices — the sweep's cost is not justified. The simulation tool cannot encode the factor being swept (e.g. no differential-expression parameter analogous to Splatter's de.prob), so the grid would not vary the relevant difficulty axis.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking lineage reconstruction quality against simulation parameters, e.g., sweeping mutation rate or dropout settings on TedSim-simulated barcode data with a known ground-truth tree.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-sweep
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-sweep Use when benchmarking lineage reconstruction quality against simulation parameters, e.g., sweeping mutation rate or dropout settings on TedSim-simulated barcode data with a known ground-truth tree. Input is real experimental barcode data with no ground-truth tree — Qr/Qh cannot be computed against a known lineage Goal is to evaluate expression-integrated methods like LinRace's NJ_asym_Dif accuracy itself rather than how barcode data quality varies with simulation parameters http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Systematically vary TedSim simulation parameters (mutation rate mu, dropout probability p_d, ncells, N_char) to generate benchmark datasets with ground-truth lineage trees, and record how downstream metrics such as reconstruction potential (Qr) and homoplasy edge ratio (Qh) respond. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Systematically vary TedSim simulation parameters (mutation rate mu, dropout probability p_d, ncells, N_char) to generate benchmark datasets with ground-truth lineage trees, and record how downstream metrics such as reconstruction potential (Qr) and homoplasy edge ratio (Qh) respond.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real experimental barcode data with no ground-truth tree — Qr/Qh cannot be computed against a known lineage Goal is to evaluate expression-integrated methods like LinRace's NJ_asym_Dif accuracy itself rather than how barcode data quality varies with simulation parameters

skills.description: Use when validating a perturbation-effect estimator on synthetic scCRISPR-seq benchmarks: construct two-cluster data with known cluster proportions and per-gRNA responses, sweep bias-generating parameters (d, r), run many seeded replicates, and score estimation loss.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-sweep-analysis
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-sweep-analysis Use when validating a perturbation-effect estimator on synthetic scCRISPR-seq benchmarks: construct two-cluster data with known cluster proportions and per-gRNA responses, sweep bias-generating parameters (d, r), run many seeded replicates, and score estimation loss. Real scCRISPR-seq data without ground-truth responses — OC against known truth cannot be computed, so the sweep loses its validation power; use application-style runs (run_scDecouple) instead. Systems violating scDecouple's assumptions, e.g. tumor/disease tissues where the Gaussian mixture assumption may not hold, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection. When the goal is perturbation-response estimation on a single dataset rather than characterizing estimator behavior as bias magnitude changes — no parameter sweep is needed. Benchmark scDecouple's EM-based response estimator against a naive observed-change (fold-change) baseline on synthetic two-cluster scCRISPR-seq simulations, sweeping the infected-proportion-bias parameters (cluster distance d, ratio change r) and scoring overall correlation (OC) against ground-truth cellular responses on PC 1 and PC 2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Benchmark scDecouple's EM-based response estimator against a naive observed-change (fold-change) baseline on synthetic two-cluster scCRISPR-seq simulations, sweeping the infected-proportion-bias parameters (cluster distance d, ratio change r) and scoring overall correlation (OC) against ground-truth cellular responses on PC 1 and PC 2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scCRISPR-seq data without ground-truth responses — OC against known truth cannot be computed, so the sweep loses its validation power; use application-style runs (run_scDecouple) instead. Systems violating scDecouple's assumptions, e.g. tumor/disease tissues where the Gaussian mixture assumption may not hold, or when rare cell types are completely absent from infection. When the goal is perturbation-response estimation on a single dataset rather than characterizing estimator behavior as bias magnitude changes — no parameter sweep is needed.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking community detection (or similar inference) methods on simulated multi-subject dynamic networks and you need to isolate the effect of information-sharing levels (r_subject, r_time) and time horizon T on accuracy.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-sweep-design
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-sweep-design Use when benchmarking community detection (or similar inference) methods on simulated multi-subject dynamic networks and you need to isolate the effect of information-sharing levels (r_subject, r_time) and time horizon T on accuracy. The goal is applied community detection on real scRNA-seq-derived co-expression networks rather than controlled benchmarking — then use Dozer-filtered networks directly instead of a synthetic sweep. The simulation axes of interest are not information-sharing levels or time horizon; other MuSDynamicDCBM parameters (n, k, p_in/p_out) should be fixed, not swept, if the claim under test concerns r_time/r_subject/T. Only a single network configuration is needed (no comparison across parameter levels) — a one-shot MuSDynamicDCBM simulation suffices rather than a full sweep. http://edamontology.org/topic_3316 Designs and executes controlled parameter sweeps over a simulated multi-subject dynamic network benchmark (MuSDynamicDCBM), varying r_subject, r_time, and time horizon T with fixed graph topology parameters and ~100 replicates per configuration, to measure how a detection method's accuracy (ARI) responds to each parameter. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad592
skills.summary: Designs and executes controlled parameter sweeps over a simulated multi-subject dynamic network benchmark (MuSDynamicDCBM), varying r_subject, r_time, and time horizon T with fixed graph topology parameters and ~100 replicates per configuration, to measure how a detection method's accuracy (ARI) responds to each parameter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is applied community detection on real scRNA-seq-derived co-expression networks rather than controlled benchmarking — then use Dozer-filtered networks directly instead of a synthetic sweep. The simulation axes of interest are not information-sharing levels or time horizon; other MuSDynamicDCBM parameters (n, k, p_in/p_out) should be fixed, not swept, if the claim under test concerns r_time/r_subject/T. Only a single network configuration is needed (no comparison across parameter levels) — a one-shot MuSDynamicDCBM simulation suffices rather than a full sweep.

skills.description: Use when simulated single-cell count data (e.g. from dyngen's SSA simulation) must be shown to match the technical characteristics of a real transcript-count dataset before using it for benchmarking.
skills.name: simulation-reference-dataset-comparison
skills.search_text: simulation-reference-dataset-comparison Use when simulated single-cell count data (e.g. from dyngen's SSA simulation) must be shown to match the technical characteristics of a real transcript-count dataset before using it for benchmarking. The input data are already real single-cell measurements, so no protocol emulation or reference-dataset calibration is needed The goal is benchmarking downstream methods (trajectory inference, RNA velocity, network inference) on existing simulations rather than validating the realism of the simulated count distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates dyngen's simulated single-cell count matrices against real reference single-cell RNA-seq datasets by emulating profiling protocols (library sizes drawn from a reference transcript-count distribution, capture rates from N(1, 0.05), multinomial molecule drawing) and checking that characteristic omics features (library size, fraction zeros, mean-variance) match the reference as assessed by countsimQC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Validates dyngen's simulated single-cell count matrices against real reference single-cell RNA-seq datasets by emulating profiling protocols (library sizes drawn from a reference transcript-count distribution, capture rates from N(1, 0.05), multinomial molecule drawing) and checking that characteristic omics features (library size, fraction zeros, mean-variance) match the reference as assessed by countsimQC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already real single-cell measurements, so no protocol emulation or reference-dataset calibration is needed The goal is benchmarking downstream methods (trajectory inference, RNA velocity, network inference) on existing simulations rather than validating the realism of the simulated count distribution

skills.description: Use when you have DS analysis result tables from multiple differential methods (e.g., pbDS/edgeR/limma vs. mmDS) run over simulation replicates per DS category, and need to quantify and visualize which genes are jointly vs. uniquely detected at FDR < 0.05.
skills.name: simulation-replicate-method-concordance
skills.search_text: simulation-replicate-method-concordance Use when you have DS analysis result tables from multiple differential methods (e.g., pbDS/edgeR/limma vs. mmDS) run over simulation replicates per DS category, and need to quantify and visualize which genes are jointly vs. uniquely detected at FDR < 0.05. You are analyzing real experimental data (e.g., the LPS-treated mouse cortex snRNA-seq application) rather than simulation replicates with known ground truth — method-unique hits cannot be classified as true/false discoveries without a truth set. You need to rank or compare methods by sensitivity/FDR/computational cost rather than characterize agreement among top-ranked detections. Only a single method (or a single aggregation-based method) was run — no between-method intersections can be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assesses between-method concordance of differential state (DS) detections across simulation replicates by intersecting method-wise significant hits (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) from muscat's pseudobulk (pbDS) and mixed-model (mmDS) engines and visualizing overlaps as an UpSet plot, distinguishing true from isolated, often false, discoveries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Assesses between-method concordance of differential state (DS) detections across simulation replicates by intersecting method-wise significant hits (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) from muscat's pseudobulk (pbDS) and mixed-model (mmDS) engines and visualizing overlaps as an UpSet plot, distinguishing true from isolated, often false, discoveries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You are analyzing real experimental data (e.g., the LPS-treated mouse cortex snRNA-seq application) rather than simulation replicates with known ground truth — method-unique hits cannot be classified as true/false discoveries without a truth set. You need to rank or compare methods by sensitivity/FDR/computational cost rather than characterize agreement among top-ranked detections. Only a single method (or a single aggregation-based method) was run — no between-method intersections can be computed.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) analysis methods and you need synthetic multi-sample scRNA-seq data whose properties are anchored to a real reference SingleCellExperiment.
skills.name: simulation-scenario-configuration
skills.search_text: simulation-scenario-configuration Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) analysis methods and you need synthetic multi-sample scRNA-seq data whose properties are anchored to a real reference SingleCellExperiment. The goal is DS testing on real experimental data rather than method benchmarking — use muscat's pbDS/mmDS on the actual data instead The simulation must accommodate an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the article notes the framework does not yet support these extensions You need scenarios such as different percentages of DM mixtures that the paper did not test http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure and run muscat's reference-anchored simulation framework (simData) to generate synthetic multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq count data with embedded differential-state genes, used to benchmark DS analysis methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Configure and run muscat's reference-anchored simulation framework (simData) to generate synthetic multi-sample, multi-group, multi-subpopulation scRNA-seq count data with embedded differential-state genes, used to benchmark DS analysis methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is DS testing on real experimental data rather than method benchmarking — use muscat's pbDS/mmDS on the actual data instead The simulation must accommodate an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the article notes the framework does not yet support these extensions You need scenarios such as different percentages of DM mixtures that the paper did not test

skills.description: Use when validating that a TWAS or gene-based test controls type I error before applying it to real GWAS data, or when designing simulation grids over p_causal and h_e2 for null or power calibrations.
skills.name: simulation-scenario-parameterization
skills.search_text: simulation-scenario-parameterization Use when validating that a TWAS or gene-based test controls type I error before applying it to real GWAS data, or when designing simulation grids over p_causal and h_e2 for null or power calibrations. The goal is power comparison under alternative (causal) architectures rather than null calibration — effects must then be injected instead of simulating pure noise The reference LD panel does not match the ancestry/population of the data being tested, violating the calibration premise http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Define null-simulation scenarios (causal-variant proportion, heritability, number of phenotypes/replicates) and derive empirical type I error rates at fixed p-value thresholds to assess whether a gene-based association test such as the OTTERS ACAT-O omnibus TWAS is well calibrated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Define null-simulation scenarios (causal-variant proportion, heritability, number of phenotypes/replicates) and derive empirical type I error rates at fixed p-value thresholds to assess whether a gene-based association test such as the OTTERS ACAT-O omnibus TWAS is well calibrated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is power comparison under alternative (causal) architectures rather than null calibration — effects must then be injected instead of simulating pure noise The reference LD panel does not match the ancestry/population of the data being tested, violating the calibration premise

skills.description: Use when fitting gene dynamics models from scRNA-seq expression data lacking splicing information, by optimizing sine-profile kinetic parameters per target gene via a generalized EM algorithm over TF weights and latent times.
skills.name: sine-profile-dynamics-parameter-optimization
skills.search_text: sine-profile-dynamics-parameter-optimization Use when fitting gene dynamics models from scRNA-seq expression data lacking splicing information, by optimizing sine-profile kinetic parameters per target gene via a generalized EM algorithm over TF weights and latent times. The dataset already has reliable spliced/unspliced counts and scVelo's dynamical EM model is preferred — TFvelo is slower than scVelo, a weakness for large-scale datasets You need per-gene phase portraits for genes whose dynamics TFvelo cannot fit well — the paper notes some genes remain poorly fitted (Fig. S14) A nonlinear TF-weight estimator is required — only the bounded linear model (lsq_linear) is implemented; the paper notes more complex models may replace it but none are provided http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fits per-gene RNA dynamics in TFvelo by optimizing sine-profile parameters (alpha, beta, theta, gamma) together with TF weights within a generalized EM loop, assigning each cell a latent time on the model curve. It replaces the splicing-based dynamical model of scVelo with a TF-expression-based model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Fits per-gene RNA dynamics in TFvelo by optimizing sine-profile parameters (alpha, beta, theta, gamma) together with TF weights within a generalized EM loop, assigning each cell a latent time on the model curve. It replaces the splicing-based dynamical model of scVelo with a TF-expression-based model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has reliable spliced/unspliced counts and scVelo's dynamical EM model is preferred — TFvelo is slower than scVelo, a weakness for large-scale datasets You need per-gene phase portraits for genes whose dynamics TFvelo cannot fit well — the paper notes some genes remain poorly fitted (Fig. S14) A nonlinear TF-weight estimator is required — only the bounded linear model (lsq_linear) is implemented; the paper notes more complex models may replace it but none are provided

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed 4i/protein imaging single-cell dataset (.h5ad, e.g. RPE 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features) must be loaded and subsampled into representative neighborhoods before feature-module discovery.
skills.name: single-cell-4i-data-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-4i-data-preprocessing Use when a preprocessed 4i/protein imaging single-cell dataset (.h5ad, e.g. RPE 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features) must be loaded and subsampled into representative neighborhoods before feature-module discovery. The input is raw image tiles or unsegmented fluorescence stacks rather than a preprocessed cell x feature .h5ad matrix The goal is supervised feature selection using pre-existing cell-type annotations rather than unsupervised trajectory-preserving selection Only a cell-similarity graph over the full noisy dataset is needed without neighborhood sketching; similarity-based methods can fail when noisy features outweigh informative ones Load, validate, and distribution-aware subsample preprocessed iterative immunofluorescence (4i) single-cell datasets (.h5ad, cells x imaging-derived features) so that downstream DELVE module discovery operates on representative cellular neighborhoods. This skill grounds feature selection in the RPE 4i cell cycle benchmark of the DELVE paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Load, validate, and distribution-aware subsample preprocessed iterative immunofluorescence (4i) single-cell datasets (.h5ad, cells x imaging-derived features) so that downstream DELVE module discovery operates on representative cellular neighborhoods. This skill grounds feature selection in the RPE 4i cell cycle benchmark of the DELVE paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw image tiles or unsegmented fluorescence stacks rather than a preprocessed cell x feature .h5ad matrix The goal is supervised feature selection using pre-existing cell-type annotations rather than unsupervised trajectory-preserving selection Only a cell-similarity graph over the full noisy dataset is needed without neighborhood sketching; similarity-based methods can fail when noisy features outweigh informative ones

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how many cells must be manually annotated to reach high annotation F1, comparing active learning classifiers/search strategies, or testing whether unlabeled novel cell types are flagged by predictive entropy.
skills.name: single-cell-active-learning-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-active-learning-simulation Use when benchmarking how many cells must be manually annotated to reach high annotation F1, comparing active learning classifiers/search strategies, or testing whether unlabeled novel cell types are flagged by predictive entropy. The goal is self-supervised label propagation without oracle labeling — use the self-training variant (label most confidently predicted cells by entropy) instead of active learning with ground-truth relabeling Expression data are raw counts, not log-normalized with variable features scaled — the classifiers require PCA on scaled, centered logcount data The dataset has no reliable ground truth labels to simulate the manual annotation oracle http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Simulates manual cell type annotation as an active learning loop on single-cell expression data: classifiers (random forest, logistic regression) trained on the first 20 PCs of scaled logcounts iteratively select the 10 unlabeled cells with highest predictive uncertainty for ground-truth labeling and retraining, using the leader benchmarking framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Simulates manual cell type annotation as an active learning loop on single-cell expression data: classifiers (random forest, logistic regression) trained on the first 20 PCs of scaled logcounts iteratively select the 10 unlabeled cells with highest predictive uncertainty for ground-truth labeling and retraining, using the leader benchmarking framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is self-supervised label propagation without oracle labeling — use the self-training variant (label most confidently predicted cells by entropy) instead of active learning with ground-truth relabeling Expression data are raw counts, not log-normalized with variable features scaled — the classifiers require PCA on scaled, centered logcount data The dataset has no reliable ground truth labels to simulate the manual annotation oracle

skills.description: Use when verifying that a database-side aggregation of single-cell expression data (e.g. per gene and cell type averages from a sparse PostgreSQL table) matches values computed directly from the original AnnData (H5AD) expression matrix.

skills.search_text: single-cell-aggregation-consistency-checking Use when verifying that a database-side aggregation of single-cell expression data (e.g. per gene and cell type averages from a sparse PostgreSQL table) matches values computed directly from the original AnnData (H5AD) expression matrix. Input data has not been imported into a database in gene-centric sparse form — computing averages only in Python from AnnData does not exercise the database aggregation path The analysis goal is interactive visual exploration (UMAP, violin plots, coexpression) rather than validating aggregation correctness — use the Cellenium webapp instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs Cellenium's gene-centric sparse storage of single-cell expression data in PostgreSQL and validates database-side gene/cell-type aggregation against recomputed averages from the source AnnData matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad349
skills.summary: Reconstructs Cellenium's gene-centric sparse storage of single-cell expression data in PostgreSQL and validates database-side gene/cell-type aggregation against recomputed averages from the source AnnData matrix.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a CAST×B6-style F1 hybrid must be converted into maternal/paternal allelic count matrices (e.g., 122 blastocyst cells, 8,290 genes) that feed bursting or ASE-state models, and multi-mapping reads would otherwise be discarded.
skills.name: single-cell-allelic-count-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-allelic-count-processing Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a CAST×B6-style F1 hybrid must be converted into maternal/paternal allelic count matrices (e.g., 122 blastocyst cells, 8,290 genes) that feed bursting or ASE-state models, and multi-mapping reads would otherwise be discarded. Input is already a processed barcode counts/annotation table — this skill starts from raw single-cell amplicon FASTQ Data are population-level (bulk) barcode sequencing with no cell barcodes — use the BARtab bulk mode workflow instead Study uses evolving barcode methods (e.g. Cas9-based recorders), which BARtab and bartools do not officially support http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract, error-correct, and tabulate expressed synthetic lineage barcodes per cell from single-cell amplicon sequencing FASTQ using the BARtab Nextflow pipeline (with fastp, umi-tools, cutadapt, bowtie1), producing a per-cell barcode annotation table comparable to FateMap-style outputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Extract, error-correct, and tabulate expressed synthetic lineage barcodes per cell from single-cell amplicon sequencing FASTQ using the BARtab Nextflow pipeline (with fastp, umi-tools, cutadapt, bowtie1), producing a per-cell barcode annotation table comparable to FateMap-style outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed barcode counts/annotation table — this skill starts from raw single-cell amplicon FASTQ Data are population-level (bulk) barcode sequencing with no cell barcodes — use the BARtab bulk mode workflow instead Study uses evolving barcode methods (e.g. Cas9-based recorders), which BARtab and bartools do not officially support

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw, unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (mtx or h5, e.g. neurons_900_raw.h5) and you need to define the P/U barcode sets that EmptyNN requires before training its classifier.

skills.search_text: single-cell-barcode-quality-control Use when starting from a raw, unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (mtx or h5, e.g. neurons_900_raw.h5) and you need to define the P/U barcode sets that EmptyNN requires before training its classifier. You need ambient RNA-corrected gene expression profiles — EmptyNN does not estimate corrected expression; use SoupX downstream instead You need to remove low-quality cells with a high fraction of mitochondrial reads — these may pass the initial filtering and must be removed in downstream analysis The data are not from a droplet-based scRNA-seq experiment with cell-free droplets in the raw matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Partition droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into a positive set P of bona fide cell-free droplets (total UMI counts below threshold T, default 100) and an unlabeled set U, after excluding barcodes with total counts of 10 or fewer. This positive/unlabeled labeling is the prerequisite input for EmptyNN's PU-learning classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Partition droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into a positive set P of bona fide cell-free droplets (total UMI counts below threshold T, default 100) and an unlabeled set U, after excluding barcodes with total counts of 10 or fewer. This positive/unlabeled labeling is the prerequisite input for EmptyNN's PU-learning classifier.

skills.search_text: single-cell-barcode-table-processing Use when you have barcoded single-cell profiles with a table of unique cell IDs and assigned barcodes, and you want clonal relationships to inform clustering (alpha) or UMAP embeddings (Warp Factor s in 0-10). skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack lineage barcode assignments (no 'rn'/'Barcode' table), so only transcriptome-only clustering is possible Input is full-lineage tracing data (CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing or imaging-based family trees) rather than single-cell barcodes; the paper did not address these, though ClonoCluster could be adapted to weight by phylogenetic distance

skills.search_text: single-cell-batch-correction-benchmarking Use when comparing how well batch-effect correction methods mix datasets with overlapping cell types while preserving cell-type resolution, e.g. reproducing Cell BLAST Fig. 2a-style integration benchmarks. skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets lack overlapping cell types across batches, so neither alignment-score mixing nor MAP cell-type resolution can be meaningfully computed Cell type or batch labels are absent, making the supervised mixing and precision metrics undefined The goal is integration for downstream annotation of a single query set rather than systematic method benchmarking

skills.search_text: single-cell-batch-effect-correction Use when raw read-count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches show batch separation (e.g., in t-SNE colored by batch) and the goal is corrected counts plus cell-type clustering without a priori subtype labels. The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — the article states no method is applicable in that case The data require bulk-level batch correction with known subtype labels a priori, where ComBat or SVA are designed instead Input is not raw read-count data (e.g., already-normalized or corrected matrices), since BUSseq models counts, overdispersion, dropout, and cell-specific sequencing depth directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate batch-effect-corrected scRNA-seq count data by fitting the BUSseq Bayesian hierarchical model and applying its quantile-matching procedure, so corrected values can be analyzed as if all cells were sequenced in a single batch. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Generate batch-effect-corrected scRNA-seq count data by fitting the BUSseq Bayesian hierarchical model and applying its quantile-matching procedure, so corrected values can be analyzed as if all cells were sequenced in a single batch.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g., batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4) — the article states no method is applicable in that case The data require bulk-level batch correction with known subtype labels a priori, where ComBat or SVA are designed instead Input is not raw read-count data (e.g., already-normalized or corrected matrices), since BUSseq models counts, overdispersion, dropout, and cell-specific sequencing depth directly

skills.search_text: single-cell-batch-effect-correction Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple scRNA-seq protocols or batches must be integrated for clustering, and batch mixing must be quantified (e.g., ASW) against baselines such as DESC, Harmony, MNN, scVI or Scanorama. skills.when_to_use_negative: The data come from a single protocol/batch so no batch merging is needed — plain clustering (e.g., scMGCA on a single dataset) suffices without the batch-correction comparison The input is raw counts from a single dataset where the goal is denoising rather than batch integration (DCA/ZINB autoencoders are the appropriate choice) Cell-type annotation is the goal on an already-integrated dataset (e.g., the PDAC workflow with marker-gene annotation), not batch-effect removal

skills.search_text: single-cell-batch-effect-embedding-training Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple batches requires a nonlinear lower-dimensional embedding that explicitly models batch effects for downstream batch-effect assessment metrics like iLISI or kBET. When the goal is batch correction/removal rather than batch-effect detection and estimation — BEENE generates an embedding for assessing batch effects, not corrected expression data When a simple linear embedding suffices: the article positions BEENE for sophisticated non-linear batch effects that PC-space methods fail to capture When biological predictor labels are required for the bio branch of the loss but none exist — the bio weight λ3 must be set to 0 with bio variables passed as None, otherwise training will fail http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Trains a BEENE deep nonlinear autoencoder that simultaneously learns batch and biological variables from RNA-seq data, producing a 50-dimensional embedding more robust and sensitive than PCA embedding for detecting and quantifying batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad479
skills.summary: Trains a BEENE deep nonlinear autoencoder that simultaneously learns batch and biological variables from RNA-seq data, producing a 50-dimensional embedding more robust and sensitive than PCA embedding for detecting and quantifying batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is batch correction/removal rather than batch-effect detection and estimation — BEENE generates an embedding for assessing batch effects, not corrected expression data When a simple linear embedding suffices: the article positions BEENE for sophisticated non-linear batch effects that PC-space methods fail to capture When biological predictor labels are required for the bio branch of the loss but none exist — the bio weight λ3 must be set to 0 with bio variables passed as None, otherwise training will fail

Sample is normal (non-cancer) tissue rather than a tumour biopsy — scATOMIC's default model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter workflow instead Analysis is run on a merged multi-patient cohort — inter-patient cancer cell-specific effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring module and classification confidence Goal is to classify non-malignant immune or stromal subtypes — scATOMIC's terminal cancer-signature module applies only to cells predicted as cancer http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 scATOMIC's cancer signature scoring and cell-differentiating module: after terminal-layer annotation, cancer-type-specific up-/down-regulated gene programs (OncoDB-derived) are scored per cell with Seurat AddModuleScore, and clusters enriched for normal cells are iteratively dropped to distinguish malignant from non-malignant tissue-specific cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37353-8
skills.summary: scATOMIC's cancer signature scoring and cell-differentiating module: after terminal-layer annotation, cancer-type-specific up-/down-regulated gene programs (OncoDB-derived) are scored per cell with Seurat AddModuleScore, and clusters enriched for normal cells are iteratively dropped to distinguish malignant from non-malignant tissue-specific cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample is normal (non-cancer) tissue rather than a tumour biopsy — scATOMIC's default model assumes at least some cancer cells are present; use the normal_tissue parameter workflow instead Analysis is run on a merged multi-patient cohort — inter-patient cancer cell-specific effects interfere with the cancer signature scoring module and classification confidence Goal is to classify non-malignant immune or stromal subtypes — scATOMIC's terminal cancer-signature module applies only to cells predicted as cancer

skills.description: Use when the input is time-course or pseudotime-ordered single-cell RNA-seq without definitive cell types (e.g. pre-blastocyst embryos) and the goal is to infer causal ligand-receptor communication and its link to temporal TF programs.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-communication-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-communication-inference Use when the input is time-course or pseudotime-ordered single-cell RNA-seq without definitive cell types (e.g. pre-blastocyst embryos) and the goal is to infer causal ligand-receptor communication and its link to temporal TF programs. The question is communication between well-defined cell types in a formed tissue — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that; TimeTalk targets settings where definitive cell types do not yet exist (e.g. pre-blastocyst embryos) The communication of interest is maternal-embryo interaction or non-LR-mediated (e.g. extracellular vesicle) signaling — TimeTalk's autocrine ligand-receptor assumption excludes these The data lack any temporal ordering or trajectory, since the method depends on temporal series information and interpolation of LR/TF activity profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 TimeTalk-style inference of ligand-receptor cell-cell communication from time-course single-cell RNA-seq: it uses trajectory-derived temporal information, co-variation scoring of LR pairs (SCC/PCC cutoffs), and Granger causal tests against temporal TF clusters to identify development-linked eLRs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: TimeTalk-style inference of ligand-receptor cell-cell communication from time-course single-cell RNA-seq: it uses trajectory-derived temporal information, co-variation scoring of LR pairs (SCC/PCC cutoffs), and Granger causal tests against temporal TF clusters to identify development-linked eLRs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is communication between well-defined cell types in a formed tissue — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that; TimeTalk targets settings where definitive cell types do not yet exist (e.g. pre-blastocyst embryos) The communication of interest is maternal-embryo interaction or non-LR-mediated (e.g. extracellular vesicle) signaling — TimeTalk's autocrine ligand-receptor assumption excludes these The data lack any temporal ordering or trajectory, since the method depends on temporal series information and interpolation of LR/TF activity profiles

skills.description: Use when you need to determine how many pseudo-replicates Scanpro's bootstrapping should use for an unreplicated single-cell dataset, given an estimate of total cells per condition.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-count-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-count-simulation Use when you need to determine how many pseudo-replicates Scanpro's bootstrapping should use for an unreplicated single-cell dataset, given an estimate of total cells per condition. The dataset already has biological replicates for all conditions — run standard Scanpro with samples_col instead of bootstrapping simulation The cell type of interest is rare (<2% of all cells), where benchmarking showed bootstrapping has limited benefits The goal is differential expression, not differential cell-type proportion analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a proportion-analysis bootstrapping method by simulating single-cell replicate datasets across a range of total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells) and testing how the optimal number of pseudo-replicates (2–14) shifts with dataset size, scored by auROC and accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: Benchmark a proportion-analysis bootstrapping method by simulating single-cell replicate datasets across a range of total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells) and testing how the optimal number of pseudo-replicates (2–14) shifts with dataset size, scored by auROC and accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset already has biological replicates for all conditions — run standard Scanpro with samples_col instead of bootstrapping simulation The cell type of interest is rare (<2% of all cells), where benchmarking showed bootstrapping has limited benefits The goal is differential expression, not differential cell-type proportion analysis

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., the 145-cell Llorens-Bobadilla neural stem cell data) contains quiescent G0-like cells that standard cell-cycle analysis does not detect and must be removed before pseudotime inference.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-cycle-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-cycle-scoring Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., the 145-cell Llorens-Bobadilla neural stem cell data) contains quiescent G0-like cells that standard cell-cycle analysis does not detect and must be removed before pseudotime inference. When the goal is to retain cell-cycle signal for trajectory reconstruction — redPATH instead contrasts this approach with the traditional strategy of removing cycling genes to remove cell cycle effects When pseudotime results already perform poorly, since redPATH notes downstream cell-type-label-free approaches may fail when pseudotime performs poorly and G0 filtering is a preprocessing step feeding redPATH When data lack per-cell cycle-phase scores (no reCAT/Cyclebase-annotated scores), since k-means and ANOVA operate on the six mean_scores columns http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies quiescent (G0-like) cells in single-cell RNA-seq data by clustering reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) with k-means and flagging the cluster that is significantly lowest across all six scores via pairwise ANOVA, as implemented in redPATH's optional G0 detection module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: Identifies quiescent (G0-like) cells in single-cell RNA-seq data by clustering reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) with k-means and flagging the cluster that is significantly lowest across all six scores via pairwise ANOVA, as implemented in redPATH's optional G0 detection module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to retain cell-cycle signal for trajectory reconstruction — redPATH instead contrasts this approach with the traditional strategy of removing cycling genes to remove cell cycle effects When pseudotime results already perform poorly, since redPATH notes downstream cell-type-label-free approaches may fail when pseudotime performs poorly and G0 filtering is a preprocessing step feeding redPATH When data lack per-cell cycle-phase scores (no reCAT/Cyclebase-annotated scores), since k-means and ANOVA operate on the six mean_scores columns

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (Seurat object) needs fully automated cell-type labels, or when cancer datasets need malignant cell identification and cell-of-origin inference, without manual marker curation.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-annotation Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (Seurat object) needs fully automated cell-type labels, or when cancer datasets need malignant cell identification and cell-of-origin inference, without manual marker curation. The input is not a scRNA-seq dataset processed into a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction (Census's label stabilization requires UMAP clusters and prediction contours). The tissue organ falls outside the 24 supported organs and no custom reference model can be trained (pretrained organ and cancer models cover a fixed list). The task requires the shortest runtime over annotation quality — scType had shorter run times than Census in the 44-tissue benchmark. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Automated hierarchical cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq data with Census, which applies gradient-boosted decision tree models organized along a cell-type hierarchy, followed by label stabilization in UMAP space; the pretrained Tabula Sapiens + CCLE model classifies 175 cell-types from 24 organs and can flag malignant cells and their cell of origin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Automated hierarchical cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq data with Census, which applies gradient-boosted decision tree models organized along a cell-type hierarchy, followed by label stabilization in UMAP space; the pretrained Tabula Sapiens + CCLE model classifies 175 cell-types from 24 organs and can flag malignant cells and their cell of origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a scRNA-seq dataset processed into a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction (Census's label stabilization requires UMAP clusters and prediction contours). The tissue organ falls outside the 24 supported organs and no custom reference model can be trained (pretrained organ and cancer models cover a fixed list). The task requires the shortest runtime over annotation quality — scType had shorter run times than Census in the 44-tissue benchmark.

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed, clustered Seurat object from plant single-cell data needs cell-type labels without manual curation, especially when a reference atlas (e.g., PRJNA517021, PRJNA706435) or a marker gene data frame is available.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-annotation Use when a pre-processed, clustered Seurat object from plant single-cell data needs cell-type labels without manual curation, especially when a reference atlas (e.g., PRJNA517021, PRJNA706435) or a marker gene data frame is available. No reference atlas and no curated marker gene list exist for the organism/tissue, leaving the automatic strategies without supervision The input is raw count data that has not been processed through the scPlant/Seurat QC-and-clustering pipeline (QCfun, RunSeurat), since the annotation functions expect a processed Seurat object The goal is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution rather than single-cell labeling — scPlant handles that via decomposeBulk, not these annotation wrappers http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Automated cell-type annotation for plant scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets using scPlant's wrapper functions built on SingleR, Garnett, scCATCH, CellAssign, and CellFunTopic, with reference cell maps or curated marker gene databases as supervision. Enables label transfer across datasets and even across species (e.g., wheat annotated with rice references). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Automated cell-type annotation for plant scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq datasets using scPlant's wrapper functions built on SingleR, Garnett, scCATCH, CellAssign, and CellFunTopic, with reference cell maps or curated marker gene databases as supervision. Enables label transfer across datasets and even across species (e.g., wheat annotated with rice references).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference atlas and no curated marker gene list exist for the organism/tissue, leaving the automatic strategies without supervision The input is raw count data that has not been processed through the scPlant/Seurat QC-and-clustering pipeline (QCfun, RunSeurat), since the annotation functions expect a processed Seurat object The goal is bulk RNA-seq deconvolution rather than single-cell labeling — scPlant handles that via decomposeBulk, not these annotation wrappers

skills.description: Use when raw source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target data may contain novel cell types requiring source-free annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation-transfer
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-annotation-transfer Use when raw source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target data may contain novel cell types requiring source-free annotation. Raw source data are available and explicit source-target feature alignment is possible (other transfer methods may suffice without scEMAIL's source-free constraint) A subjective/user-defined threshold for novel cell detection is acceptable and the task is simple clustering rather than label transfer from a trained source model The target data are not single-cell count data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq), where the ZINB count model and per-cell E-score machinery do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Source-free transfer learning annotation of single-cell target data using scEMAIL: only pre-trained source model weights (ZINB autoencoder encoder h, main classifier c, two auxiliary classifiers c1/c2) are shared, and target cells are annotated with automatic detection of novel cell types via an expert ensemble E-score, bimodality tests, manifold-mixup thresholding, and multi-order local affinity constraints. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Source-free transfer learning annotation of single-cell target data using scEMAIL: only pre-trained source model weights (ZINB autoencoder encoder h, main classifier c, two auxiliary classifiers c1/c2) are shared, and target cells are annotated with automatic detection of novel cell types via an expert ensemble E-score, bimodality tests, manifold-mixup thresholding, and multi-order local affinity constraints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw source data are available and explicit source-target feature alignment is possible (other transfer methods may suffice without scEMAIL's source-free constraint) A subjective/user-defined threshold for novel cell detection is acceptable and the task is simple clustering rather than label transfer from a trained source model The target data are not single-cell count data (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or bulk ATAC-seq), where the ZINB count model and per-cell E-score machinery do not apply

skills.description: Use when you have raw (unnormalized) single-cell count data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger output) and annotated cell type labels to train on, or a pretrained Pollock module to assign cell type labels to new cells.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-classification Use when you have raw (unnormalized) single-cell count data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger output) and annotated cell type labels to train on, or a pretrained Pollock module to assign cell type labels to new cells. Input expression matrix is normalized/log-transformed — Pollock requires raw unnormalized counts (e.g. the tutorial keeps a separate counts_adata copy before sc.pp.normalize_total/log1p). Goal is differential expression, clustering, or other unsupervised analysis rather than supervised cell type label assignment with an annotated reference or pretrained module. You need classification of organisms/cell types outside the available pretrained cancer/PBMC modules and have no annotated training data to train a new module. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Classify single-cell types/states using Pollock, a VAE-based deep learning method with a linear classification head, via its train/predict CLI or pretrained modules covering scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, and snATAC-seq (gene activity) cancer datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Classify single-cell types/states using Pollock, a VAE-based deep learning method with a linear classification head, via its train/predict CLI or pretrained modules covering scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, and snATAC-seq (gene activity) cancer datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression matrix is normalized/log-transformed — Pollock requires raw unnormalized counts (e.g. the tutorial keeps a separate counts_adata copy before sc.pp.normalize_total/log1p). Goal is differential expression, clustering, or other unsupervised analysis rather than supervised cell type label assignment with an annotated reference or pretrained module. You need classification of organisms/cell types outside the available pretrained cancer/PBMC modules and have no annotated training data to train a new module.

skills.description: Use when you have a trained Pollock VAE classification module (e.g. scRNAseq_brca_panimmune) plus raw-count .h5ad/.RDS cells and need the interpretability scores identifying which genes drive each predicted cell state.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-interpretability-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-interpretability-scoring Use when you have a trained Pollock VAE classification module (e.g. scRNAseq_brca_panimmune) plus raw-count .h5ad/.RDS cells and need the interpretability scores identifying which genes drive each predicted cell state. Input expression matrices are normalized rather than raw counts — explain mode requires unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts You need cell type prediction itself rather than explanation — use Pollock predict mode instead Very large numbers of cells to explain without downsampling — the README warns of excessive runtimes for large cell counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Ranks the genes that drive Pollock's cell state predictions (driver working genes, DWGs) by applying Captum Integrated Gradients feature attributions in Pollock's explain mode against a sampled background, yielding per-cell-state ranked gene tables used to confirm recovery of known markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Ranks the genes that drive Pollock's cell state predictions (driver working genes, DWGs) by applying Captum Integrated Gradients feature attributions in Pollock's explain mode against a sampled background, yielding per-cell-state ranked gene tables used to confirm recovery of known markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression matrices are normalized rather than raw counts — explain mode requires unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts You need cell type prediction itself rather than explanation — use Pollock predict mode instead Very large numbers of cells to explain without downsampling — the README warns of excessive runtimes for large cell counts

skills.description: Use when a query AnnData needs cell type labels transferred from an annotated reference (e.g. resolving monocyte subtypes in pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating myeloid data), and you want interpretable, pathway-token-based predictions with per-cell probabilities.
skills.name: single-cell-cell-type-label-transfer
skills.search_text: single-cell-cell-type-label-transfer Use when a query AnnData needs cell type labels transferred from an annotated reference (e.g. resolving monocyte subtypes in pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating myeloid data), and you want interpretable, pathway-token-based predictions with per-cell probabilities. The reference and query AnnData var_names differ in order or membership and you cannot subset the query — the README warns predictions require identical, ordered genes. You need an unsupervised discovery of entirely novel cell types with no labeled reference — this skill transfers labels from a reference dataset rather than de novo annotating clusters. Your goal is dimensionality-reduced latent embeddings for visualization rather than interpretable label transfer — TOSICA deliberately avoids dimensionality reduction to keep attention traceable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transfer cell type annotations from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset to a query dataset using TOSICA, a Transformer-based multi-head self-attention model whose attention layers are masked by biologically relevant pathway/regulon tokens (e.g. Reactome, GO_bp, immune, TF .gmt gene sets), yielding predictions, probabilities, and an interpretable attention matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Transfer cell type annotations from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset to a query dataset using TOSICA, a Transformer-based multi-head self-attention model whose attention layers are masked by biologically relevant pathway/regulon tokens (e.g. Reactome, GO_bp, immune, TF .gmt gene sets), yielding predictions, probabilities, and an interpretable attention matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference and query AnnData var_names differ in order or membership and you cannot subset the query — the README warns predictions require identical, ordered genes. You need an unsupervised discovery of entirely novel cell types with no labeled reference — this skill transfers labels from a reference dataset rather than de novo annotating clusters. Your goal is dimensionality-reduced latent embeddings for visualization rather than interpretable label transfer — TOSICA deliberately avoids dimensionality reduction to keep attention traceable.

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts of T cells (or other cell types with a pre-built reference map) must be annotated with reference-defined cell states, e.g. assigning tumor-specific CD8 TILs to Tex/Tpex/EM states on the murine TIL atlas.
skills.name: single-cell-cellstate-label-transfer
skills.search_text: single-cell-cellstate-label-transfer Use when raw scRNA-seq counts of T cells (or other cell types with a pre-built reference map) must be annotated with reference-defined cell states, e.g. assigning tumor-specific CD8 TILs to Tex/Tpex/EM states on the murine TIL atlas. The query contains γδ T cells or CD4+ TIL states that are under-represented or not represented at all in the reference atlases The goal is de novo unsupervised discovery of entirely novel cell types for which no appropriate reference map exists rather than assignment to reference-defined states A different normalization strategy is preferred but raw counts cannot be placed in the Seurat 'data' layer with skip.normalize=TRUE http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reference-based cell state label transfer for scRNA-seq: ProjecTILs projects query cells (e.g. tetramer+ CD8 TILs) into a stable annotated reference atlas PCA/UMAP space and transfers subtype labels (e.g. Tex, Tpex, EM) via nearest-neighbor prediction without altering the reference structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Reference-based cell state label transfer for scRNA-seq: ProjecTILs projects query cells (e.g. tetramer+ CD8 TILs) into a stable annotated reference atlas PCA/UMAP space and transfers subtype labels (e.g. Tex, Tpex, EM) via nearest-neighbor prediction without altering the reference structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query contains γδ T cells or CD4+ TIL states that are under-represented or not represented at all in the reference atlases The goal is de novo unsupervised discovery of entirely novel cell types for which no appropriate reference map exists rather than assignment to reference-defined states A different normalization strategy is preferred but raw counts cannot be placed in the Seurat 'data' layer with skip.normalize=TRUE

Input is already an annotated feature table or cell-type label set rather than a gene-cell-barcode count matrix Cells of interest lack reference populations with adequate surface-marker or transcriptional coverage (e.g. erythrocyte precursors, where limited surface markers make assignment unreliable) A sample is a K=1 all-one-genotype call with mixture fraction below the ~4%-of-6,000-cells detection level, where genotype-stratified annotation is uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Annotate single-cell types by correlating each cell's log-transformed expression profile against reference populations in Seurat, as used on ~68k PBMCs and ~17,000 post-transplant BMMCs profiled with the 10x Genomics GemCode droplet platform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049

skills.search_text: single-cell-clonal-genotyping-from-transcriptomes Use when single-cell gene expression data carry linked per-cell mutation calls (GoT) that are noisy (false negatives from shallow sequencing, false positives from ambient RNA) and the goal is to reconcile genotype-based clone labels with transcriptional cell-type annotations. skills.search_text: single-cell-clonal-subset-comparison Use when single cells have already been assigned to clones/subclones (e.g., mtDNA subclones clone1.MT0 vs clone1.MT1) and the goal is to test whether those subclones are biologically distinct via DE genes and Hallmark pathway enrichment. Cells have not yet been assigned to clones — run the upstream mtDNA clonality pipeline (cellsnp-lite/MQuad/vireoSNP) first The question is identifying informative mtDNA variants or reconstructing clones, not testing expression differences between already-defined subclones Nuclear SNV or CNV lineage labels are the only clonal markers and mtDNA subclone structure is not of interest — the clone predictor in the GLM would not represent the intended contrast http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Establishes that clonally defined single-cell subpopulations (e.g., mtDNA-defined subclones from MQuad/vireoSNP) are transcriptionally and functionally distinct, by running an edgeR quasi-likelihood differential expression test between subclones followed by limma camera enrichment of MSigDB Hallmark gene sets on the resulting log2-fold-changes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0

skills.description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data carry integrated lineage barcodes (e.g. CellTag lentiviral captures from 10x Chromium runs) and you must group cells into clones for state-fate or clonal GRN analyses.
skills.name: single-cell-clone-calling-from-lineage-barcode-data
skills.search_text: single-cell-clone-calling-from-lineage-barcode-data Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data carry integrated lineage barcodes (e.g. CellTag lentiviral captures from 10x Chromium runs) and you must group cells into clones for state-fate or clonal GRN analyses. The dataset contains no lineage barcodes (plain scRNA-seq without CellTag or similar lineage capture) — clone calling is impossible and cell clustering should be used instead The goal is cell-type classification or fate-transition scoring of transcriptomes only — Capybara is the appropriate tool, not barcode-based clone calling The barcode library has not been allowlisted against the plasmid library — calling clones from unallowed barcodes will inflate clone counts http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Recover clonal lineages from single-cell lineage-tracing datasets by allowlisting lineage barcodes (e.g. CellTag lentiviral barcodes) and calling clones from integrated barcode data, producing clone labels per cell that link early cell states to fate outcomes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Recover clonal lineages from single-cell lineage-tracing datasets by allowlisting lineage barcodes (e.g. CellTag lentiviral barcodes) and calling clones from integrated barcode data, producing clone labels per cell that link early cell states to fate outcomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no lineage barcodes (plain scRNA-seq without CellTag or similar lineage capture) — clone calling is impossible and cell clustering should be used instead The goal is cell-type classification or fate-transition scoring of transcriptomes only — Capybara is the appropriate tool, not barcode-based clone calling The barcode library has not been allowlisted against the plasmid library — calling clones from unallowed barcodes will inflate clone counts

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed and clustered Seurat object or count matrix from scRNA-seq or imaging-based spatial data (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain) needs cell type labels per cluster or per cell, and marker-gene-based annotation with interpretable results is desired.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-annotation Use when a preprocessed and clustered Seurat object or count matrix from scRNA-seq or imaging-based spatial data (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain) needs cell type labels per cluster or per cell, and marker-gene-based annotation with interpretable results is desired. No marker-gene-independent comparison: the article notes no direct comparison with reference-based, non-marker annotation tools, so this skill is not the choice when a comprehensive reference atlas mapping is required Tissue not represented in the Accordion database (728 cell types across 212 human tissues plus mouse) — check list_tissues() first Aberrant/disease cell states require the disease_accordion_marker database, not the default healthy accordion_marker database http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Automatically annotate cell types in single-cell and spatial omics clusters using consistency-weighted markers from the Cell Marker Accordion database (accordion() function), validated to outperform other marker-based tools (e.g., >13% on MERFISH mouse brain; ~23% average). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Automatically annotate cell types in single-cell and spatial omics clusters using consistency-weighted markers from the Cell Marker Accordion database (accordion() function), validated to outperform other marker-based tools (e.g., >13% on MERFISH mouse brain; ~23% average).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No marker-gene-independent comparison: the article notes no direct comparison with reference-based, non-marker annotation tools, so this skill is not the choice when a comprehensive reference atlas mapping is required Tissue not represented in the Accordion database (728 cell types across 212 human tissues plus mouse) — check list_tissues() first Aberrant/disease cell states require the disease_accordion_marker database, not the default healthy accordion_marker database

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-assignment-counting Use when evaluating sequence-search or demultiplexing tools on single-cell FASTQ data by measuring how many cells in a known cluster are recovered via their barcodes after matching target sequences such as BCAS4-BCAS3, E1A, or a variant allele. skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been clustered into cell subtypes (e.g. CD163-high macrophage clusters identified by scNovel) and you need pathway-level (GO/GSEA) interpretation of condition-dependent differential expression per cluster.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-biomarker-ranking
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-biomarker-ranking Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been clustered into cell subtypes (e.g. CD163-high macrophage clusters identified by scNovel) and you need pathway-level (GO/GSEA) interpretation of condition-dependent differential expression per cluster. The single-cell data have not yet been clustered or novel subtypes identified — scNovel's detection step (barcode preprocessing, query-stage thresholding) must precede this ranking step. The goal is cell-type annotation or novel-cell detection rather than interpreting cluster biology through pathway enrichment. You have only bulk RNA-seq or pre-aggregated gene signatures without per-cell cluster structure — the skill depends on cluster-resolved ranked gene lists. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks genes within single-cell RNA-seq clusters by their differential expression statistic between conditions (here COVID-19 vs healthy macrophage clusters 3, 5, and 12 from GSE171524) and converts the ranked lists into GO and gene set enrichment results that reveal which biological pathways distinguish COVID from non-COVID cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Ranks genes within single-cell RNA-seq clusters by their differential expression statistic between conditions (here COVID-19 vs healthy macrophage clusters 3, 5, and 12 from GSE171524) and converts the ranked lists into GO and gene set enrichment results that reveal which biological pathways distinguish COVID from non-COVID cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The single-cell data have not yet been clustered or novel subtypes identified — scNovel's detection step (barcode preprocessing, query-stage thresholding) must precede this ranking step. The goal is cell-type annotation or novel-cell detection rather than interpreting cluster biology through pathway enrichment.
