skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset or 2D embedding must be screened before trajectory fitting — e.g., before Slingshot/Monocle3 — to flag disconnected clusters or homogeneous cells with no trajectory signal.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-connectivity-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-connectivity-analysis Use when a scRNA-seq dataset or 2D embedding must be screened before trajectory fitting — e.g., before Slingshot/Monocle3 — to flag disconnected clusters or homogeneous cells with no trajectory signal. The trajectory method under consideration does not use two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations. The embeddings derive from RNA velocity or other velocity-informed dimension reduction — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort (future work). The question is trajectory accuracy after fitting (choice of feature selection, dimension reduction, hyperparameters) rather than pre-fit suitability — that is Escort's later scoring steps, not this Step 1 check. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Escort's Step 1 suitability assessment determines whether a scRNA-seq dataset (or a given embedding) is appropriate for trajectory inference by detecting disconnected cell clusters and homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal, using Jaccard-based cluster connectivity and a PC1–HVG correlation permutation test. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Escort's Step 1 suitability assessment determines whether a scRNA-seq dataset (or a given embedding) is appropriate for trajectory inference by detecting disconnected cell clusters and homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal, using Jaccard-based cluster connectivity and a PC1–HVG correlation permutation test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory method under consideration does not use two-dimensional representations — Escort presently only considers trajectory inference approaches that use two-dimensional representations. The embeddings derive from RNA velocity or other velocity-informed dimension reduction — support for these is not yet implemented in Escort (future work). The question is trajectory accuracy after fitting (choice of feature selection, dimension reduction, hyperparameters) rather than pre-fit suitability — that is Escort's later scoring steps, not this Step 1 check.

skills.description: Use when starting PILOT-style sample-level analysis: you have a cell-by-cluster annotated .h5ad (e.g. clusters_col 'cell_subtype', sample_col 'sampleID') and need per-sample cluster probability distributions for Wasserstein distance computation.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-count-aggregation Use when starting PILOT-style sample-level analysis: you have a cell-by-cluster annotated .h5ad (e.g. clusters_col 'cell_subtype', sample_col 'sampleID') and need per-sample cluster probability distributions for Wasserstein distance computation. The input is already a per-sample feature/distribution table (e.g. pre-computed cluster proportions or pathomics structure counts) — no count aggregation or prior smoothing is needed. You need distances between individual cells or between clusters rather than between whole samples; PILOT's transport step operates on sample-level distributions, not single cells. Samples come from distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — the article flags cross-technology analysis as an unresolved open challenge for this representation. Aggregates per-sample cell-cluster count vectors from a clustered single-cell AnnData and converts them into robust per-sample probability distributions over clusters via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate. These distributions are the input PILOT feeds into its optimal-transport (Wasserstein) comparison of samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-023-00003-8
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample cell-cluster count vectors from a clustered single-cell AnnData and converts them into robust per-sample probability distributions over clusters via a hierarchical Dirichlet-multinomial MAP estimate. These distributions are the input PILOT feeds into its optimal-transport (Wasserstein) comparison of samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-sample feature/distribution table (e.g. pre-computed cluster proportions or pathomics structure counts) — no count aggregation or prior smoothing is needed. You need distances between individual cells or between clusters rather than between whole samples; PILOT's transport step operates on sample-level distributions, not single cells. Samples come from distinct technologies or isolation methods (single nucleus vs. single cell, droplet vs. well based) — the article flags cross-technology analysis as an unresolved open challenge for this representation.

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-count-validation Use when a published scRNA-seq result specifies an exact cell count and cluster number for a defined cell compartment (e.g., 44,799 T/NK cells in 32 clusters) and the goal is to independently reproduce and check those values in Seurat. The published result is not defined at the level of an annotated cell compartment (e.g., a whole-atlas clustering where subsetting is not part of the reported workflow) The task is cell-cell communication inference itself (LR-pair enrichment/visualization with scCrossTalk) rather than verifying the cell/cluster counts feeding into it The input is already a de novo clustering problem with no published reference cell/cluster counts to validate against http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A validation skill for reproducing reported single-cell subclustering results — subsetting an annotated cell compartment (here T/NK cells from 12 human liver transplant samples), re-running PCA/UMAP and graph-based clustering in Seurat, and confirming that cell counts (44,799 T/NK cells) and cluster numbers (32 distinctive clusters) match the published values before accepting the re-run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: A validation skill for reproducing reported single-cell subclustering results — subsetting an annotated cell compartment (here T/NK cells from 12 human liver transplant samples), re-running PCA/UMAP and graph-based clustering in Seurat, and confirming that cell counts (44,799 T/NK cells) and cluster numbers (32 distinctive clusters) match the published values before accepting the re-run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The published result is not defined at the level of an annotated cell compartment (e.g., a whole-atlas clustering where subsetting is not part of the reported workflow) The task is cell-cell communication inference itself (LR-pair enrichment/visualization with scCrossTalk) rather than verifying the cell/cluster counts feeding into it The input is already a de novo clustering problem with no published reference cell/cluster counts to validate against

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-count-verification Use when scRNA-seq data has been deliberately over-clustered with Leiden at high resolution (e.g. 3.5) and you need to verify how many significantly different clusters remain after Cytocipher merging and whether intermediate cell states were recovered. Input AnnData lacks tentative cluster labels or has been clustered at low Leiden resolution — Cytocipher expects high-resolution over-clustering so that non-significant clusters can be merged Data is not log-cpm normalised via the scanpy standard workflow (e.g. raw counts or a feature table) The goal is subpopulation discovery in a different biological context (e.g. CD8+ T cell subtypes in PBMC or prostate luminal epithelial subpopulations) rather than verification of cluster counts and intermediate states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Verifies the number of significantly different cell clusters produced by Cytocipher's cluster-merge on over-clustered scRNA-seq data, confirming that non-significant Leiden clusters are merged and that biologically meaningful intermediate cell states are retained. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Verifies the number of significantly different cell clusters produced by Cytocipher's cluster-merge on over-clustered scRNA-seq data, confirming that non-significant Leiden clusters are merged and that biologically meaningful intermediate cell states are retained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input AnnData lacks tentative cluster labels or has been clustered at low Leiden resolution — Cytocipher expects high-resolution over-clustering so that non-significant clusters can be merged Data is not log-cpm normalised via the scanpy standard workflow (e.g. raw counts or a feature table) The goal is subpopulation discovery in a different biological context (e.g. CD8+ T cell subtypes in PBMC or prostate luminal epithelial subpopulations) rather than verification of cluster counts and intermediate states

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-functional-annotation Use when a clustered scRNAseq counts matrix needs functional annotation — e.g. identifying which TFs, miRNAs, kinases, or immune signatures drive cell clusterization, or extracting minimal COMET marker gene panels (≤4 genes) for specific clusters. When only raw FASTQ files are available — pre-process with cellrangerCount/indropCounts first; this skill annotates clusters from an already-clustered counts matrix When the goal is general cluster discovery without functional interpretation — SCA is designed to reconstruct only the clusters supported by its encoding space, not to cluster all cells de novo When trying to measure TF-miRNA circuits directly — miRNAs cannot currently be quantified together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA latent spaces rely on inferred target sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functional mining of single-cell RNAseq clusters using a Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) whose latent space is built from experimentally validated data (TF targets, miRNA targets, kinase targets, cancer-related immune signatures), with COMET marker-panel extraction and QCC/QCM quality metrics, implemented as an rCASC module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6

The input lacks cluster labels — gene ranking requires pre-defined clusters; run clustering (e.g. scBGEDA) first The goal is quantifying gene influence on clusters via the model's learned latent representation (scBGEDA's built-in functional genomic analysis) rather than standard differential-expression ranking The dataset has no expectation of known cell-type composition, so CellMark-based annotation would be meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Ranks genes per cluster by differential expression using scanpy's Wilcoxon rank-sum test on an AnnData object built from predicted cluster labels (e.g. scBGEDA outputs), then matches top-ranked genes to curated marker databases to assign cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-label-aggregation Use when you have a latent cell embedding (e.g. from a dual denoising autoencoder) and K basic clusterings with varying k, and need a single consensus partition that is stable across random seeds and cluster counts. skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-label-mapping Use when synthetic single-cell observations must be assigned cluster identities for fidelity evaluation, and ground-truth cluster labels (e.g. from Seurat clustering on UMAP of PBMC4k or Segerstolpe data) exist only for the original cells. skills.summary: Transfers cluster labels from a ground-truth scRNA-seq dataset to synthetic observations by mapping each synthetic cell to its nearest original cell via Euclidean distance in UMAP space, enabling comparison of per-cluster cell counts between original and synthetic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When batch correction is required: the study examined all models without batch correction capabilities, and batch effects cannot currently be learned with scDBMs When ground-truth cluster labels for the original data cannot be trusted (e.g. no Seurat clustering available), since label transfer propagates the assumption that mapped synthetic cells land in correct clusters When the goal is annotating cells with known cell-type markers rather than evaluating synthetic-data fidelity against ground-truth clustering

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering method (e.g., SSRE) has produced cell type labels and you need to confirm the labels are biologically meaningful by recovering known marker genes via differential expression testing.

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-label-validation Use when a scRNA-seq clustering method (e.g., SSRE) has produced cell type labels and you need to confirm the labels are biologically meaningful by recovering known marker genes via differential expression testing. skills.summary: Validates computationally inferred single-cell cluster labels (e.g., SSRE-inferred labels on the Yan scRNA-seq dataset) by testing whether they support downstream differential expression analysis, using per-gene Kruskal-Wallis rank-sum tests with a P < 0.01 significance threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cluster labels have not yet been produced or cannot be aligned cell-by-cell to the expression matrix rows The goal is evaluating clustering accuracy against ground-truth labels (use NMI/Purity/ARI comparisons instead) The gene expression matrix is not raw/log-normalized count data suited to rank-based testing across cluster groups

skills.description: Use when CITE-seq data with normalized RNA and ADT matrices plus per-cell cluster assignments needs a quantitative per-cluster purity assessment in both transcriptome and surface protein modalities.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-level-statistics
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-level-statistics Use when CITE-seq data with normalized RNA and ADT matrices plus per-cell cluster assignments needs a quantitative per-cluster purity assessment in both transcriptome and surface protein modalities. Datasets with very large numbers of ADT features (e.g., 228 ADT features in 170K cells), where the paper shows LinQ-View fails and recommends Seurat 4 Datasets beyond LinQ-View's sweet spot of large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50), since pairwise distance memory/complexity grow quadratically with cell count http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes per-cluster purity scores for CITE-seq data by combining an entropy-based ROGUE transcriptome score (S_RNA) with a rank-adjusted ADT score (S_ADT) via the geometric mean S = sqrt(S_ADT*S_RNA), providing a quantitative metric for judging whether a cluster is a pure cell population in both modalities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: Computes per-cluster purity scores for CITE-seq data by combining an entropy-based ROGUE transcriptome score (S_RNA) with a rank-adjusted ADT score (S_ADT) via the geometric mean S = sqrt(S_ADT*S_RNA), providing a quantitative metric for judging whether a cluster is a pure cell population in both modalities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with very large numbers of ADT features (e.g., 228 ADT features in 170K cells), where the paper shows LinQ-View fails and recommends Seurat 4 Datasets beyond LinQ-View's sweet spot of large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50), since pairwise distance memory/complexity grow quadratically with cell count

skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-marker-identification Use when a Seurat/scMiko scRNA-seq object has author- or algorithm-defined cluster labels (e.g. 'sub_cluster') and you need cluster-specific DEGs, or want to benchmark CDI (binary DEG) markers against Wilcoxon markers for specificity. skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal requires DE methods that account for variation in biological replicates — the CDI approach, like existing scRNA-seq DE methods, fails to account for replicate-level variation Clusters come from a single-replicate dataset where spurious clusters from artifact genes cannot be distinguished from real biology Input is raw count data without cluster labels — cell-type annotation (e.g. Miko scoring or sc-type) must precede marker identification

skills.description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with FindClusters-defined clusters) needs cluster-level marker genes to feed downstream annotation tools such as deCS that accept either gene lists or z-scored expression profiles.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-marker-identification
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-marker-identification Use when a clustered scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with FindClusters-defined clusters) needs cluster-level marker genes to feed downstream annotation tools such as deCS that accept either gene lists or z-scored expression profiles. The query is already a precomputed marker list or z-scored expression matrix (e.g., pbmc_example.rda) — skip directly to deCS.correlation()/deCS.fisher() Cells are unclustered or the analysis is at single-cell rather than cluster level — deCS defines cell types at the cluster level and requires predefined clusters The target is novel/cancer cell type discovery — deCS is a mapping-based tool limited to its reference panels (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies cluster-specific marker genes from a clustered scRNA-seq object (e.g., Seurat PBMC 3k) using FindAllMarkers and derives both a top-10 marker gene list per cluster and a cluster-average z-scored marker expression matrix, the two query inputs required by deCS.correlation() and deCS.fisher() for cell type annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.04.001
skills.summary: Identifies cluster-specific marker genes from a clustered scRNA-seq object (e.g., Seurat PBMC 3k) using FindAllMarkers and derives both a top-10 marker gene list per cluster and a cluster-average z-scored marker expression matrix, the two query inputs required by deCS.correlation() and deCS.fisher() for cell type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query is already a precomputed marker list or z-scored expression matrix (e.g., pbmc_example.rda) — skip directly to deCS.correlation()/deCS.fisher() Cells are unclustered or the analysis is at single-cell rather than cluster level — deCS defines cell types at the cluster level and requires predefined clusters The target is novel/cancer cell type discovery — deCS is a mapping-based tool limited to its reference panels (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune, HCL, HCAF)

skills.description: Use when you have a count matrix plus cluster assignments (e.g., ClonoCluster hybrid clusters across alpha values) and need to quantify marker sensitivity/specificity via AUC or identify reorganization markers (reorg-AUC > 0.80).
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-marker-roc-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-marker-roc-analysis Use when you have a count matrix plus cluster assignments (e.g., ClonoCluster hybrid clusters across alpha values) and need to quantify marker sensitivity/specificity via AUC or identify reorganization markers (reorg-AUC > 0.80). The goal is differential expression testing with p-values rather than ROC-based marker classification accuracy — use a DE framework instead Cell IDs in the barcode table do not exactly match those in the count matrix — the analysis would mispair cells and barcodes No cluster assignments exist yet; hybrid clusters must first be generated by running clonocluster over the alpha range http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ROC/AUC-based marker analysis for single-cell clustering results, using the ClonoCluster Find_Markers_ROC wrapper around ROCR to compute AUCs for cluster markers (marker fidelity) and reorganization markers (genes whose expression predicts cluster rearrangement between transcriptome-only and hybrid clusters). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100247
skills.summary: ROC/AUC-based marker analysis for single-cell clustering results, using the ClonoCluster Find_Markers_ROC wrapper around ROCR to compute AUCs for cluster markers (marker fidelity) and reorganization markers (genes whose expression predicts cluster rearrangement between transcriptome-only and hybrid clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression testing with p-values rather than ROC-based marker classification accuracy — use a DE framework instead Cell IDs in the barcode table do not exactly match those in the count matrix — the analysis would mispair cells and barcodes No cluster assignments exist yet; hybrid clusters must first be generated by running clonocluster over the alpha range

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be converted into pooled, cluster-level transcriptomic profiles (rows = genes, columns = clusters) before predicting miRNA expression with miRSCAPE or a similar trained model.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-pooling-and-preparation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-pooling-and-preparation Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be converted into pooled, cluster-level transcriptomic profiles (rows = genes, columns = clusters) before predicting miRNA expression with miRSCAPE or a similar trained model. The input is already a dense bulk RNA-seq or miRNA expression matrix and only needs bulkTransform-style log normalization, not Seurat-object pooling The task requires single-cell-resolution miRNA inference without cluster pooling (e.g. following miReact, which interprets predicted miRNA at the level of cell clusters anyway, pooling is the intended resolution) The scRNA-seq data is not in a Seurat object and cannot be converted, since modifySeuratObject assumes Seurat object storage http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares Seurat-object scRNA-seq data for miRNA-expression inference by pooling cells within each cell-type cluster and formatting the pooled transcriptomic matrix, so the sparse single-cell profile becomes a dense sample-level input for the miRSCAPE xgboost model. It also covers bulkData-style transformation (bulkTransform) of the accompanying mRNA and miRNA matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Prepares Seurat-object scRNA-seq data for miRNA-expression inference by pooling cells within each cell-type cluster and formatting the pooled transcriptomic matrix, so the sparse single-cell profile becomes a dense sample-level input for the miRSCAPE xgboost model. It also covers bulkData-style transformation (bulkTransform) of the accompanying mRNA and miRNA matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a dense bulk RNA-seq or miRNA expression matrix and only needs bulkTransform-style log normalization, not Seurat-object pooling The task requires single-cell-resolution miRNA inference without cluster pooling (e.g. following miReact, which interprets predicted miRNA at the level of cell clusters anyway, pooling is the intended resolution) The scRNA-seq data is not in a Seurat object and cannot be converted, since modifySeuratObject assumes Seurat object storage

skills.description: Use when an scRNAseq or spatial transcriptomics counts table has been clustered (e.g., 9 SIMLR clusters on a Visium breast cancer section) and you need to determine which clusters the SCA autoencoder reconstructs for the majority of cells before downstream functional annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-reconstruction-quality-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-reconstruction-quality-metric-evaluation Use when an scRNAseq or spatial transcriptomics counts table has been clustered (e.g., 9 SIMLR clusters on a Visium breast cancer section) and you need to determine which clusters the SCA autoencoder reconstructs for the majority of cells before downstream functional annotation. Clusters were not defined beforehand — SCA requires pre-clustered cells; use a clustering tool (e.g., SIMLR in rCASC) first You only need bulk or pseudo-bulk autoencoding where per-cluster reconstruction quality is not meaningful Input is already a TF activity or feature table rather than a raw counts matrix accepted by SCA http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Evaluates which single-cell/spatial-transcriptomics clusters are meaningfully reconstructed by the rCASC Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) using the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics with a >0.5 threshold per cell. It decides which clusters are worth downstream TF-ranking (e.g., COMET) rather than blindly analyzing all clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Evaluates which single-cell/spatial-transcriptomics clusters are meaningfully reconstructed by the rCASC Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) using the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics with a >0.5 threshold per cell. It decides which clusters are worth downstream TF-ranking (e.g., COMET) rather than blindly analyzing all clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters were not defined beforehand — SCA requires pre-clustered cells; use a clustering tool (e.g., SIMLR in rCASC) first You only need bulk or pseudo-bulk autoencoding where per-cluster reconstruction quality is not meaningful Input is already a TF activity or feature table rather than a raw counts matrix accepted by SCA

skills.description: Use when you have a scATAC-seq-derived base GRN edge list plus a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas with the Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP data) and need per-cluster regulatory networks.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-specific-network-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-specific-network-inference Use when you have a scATAC-seq-derived base GRN edge list plus a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas with the Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP data) and need per-cluster regulatory networks. You only need the scATAC-seq base GRN itself (motif-level potential connections) and have no matched scRNA-seq expression to prune against — CellOracle's base GRN construction is the relevant skill instead The data lack defined cell clusters or trajectory states, so no cluster-specific context exists to condition the network on Your goal is cell type classification rather than network inference — Capybara (used for cell type classification in this paper) is the appropriate tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Converts a base GRN derived from scATAC-seq data into context-dependent, cluster-specific GRN configurations by pruning inactive TF-target edges against single-cell RNA-seq expression and refitting edge weights per cluster with CellOracle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Converts a base GRN derived from scATAC-seq data into context-dependent, cluster-specific GRN configurations by pruning inactive TF-target edges against single-cell RNA-seq expression and refitting edge weights per cluster with CellOracle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need the scATAC-seq base GRN itself (motif-level potential connections) and have no matched scRNA-seq expression to prune against — CellOracle's base GRN construction is the relevant skill instead The data lack defined cell clusters or trajectory states, so no cluster-specific context exists to condition the network on Your goal is cell type classification rather than network inference — Capybara (used for cell type classification in this paper) is the appropriate tool

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object carries ≥2 conflicting cell-cluster annotation columns (e.g. Leiden at different resolutions, Seurat3/Monocle3/ICGS2, cellHarmony label transfers, or RNA/ADT modality labels) and a single high-confidence reconciled assignment is needed.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-stability-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-stability-integration Use when an AnnData object carries ≥2 conflicting cell-cluster annotation columns (e.g. Leiden at different resolutions, Seurat3/Monocle3/ICGS2, cellHarmony label transfers, or RNA/ADT modality labels) and a single high-confidence reconciled assignment is needed. When a single well-justified clustering resolution already resolves all cell states of interest — scTriangulate addresses the case where no single resolution identifies the most discrete cell states across modalities When the goal is a joint latent-space or graph-based multimodal embedding (e.g. Seurat-WNN or TotalVI) rather than reconciling pre-computed cluster annotations at the decision level When cell populations still need to be named: population naming remains largely non-standardized and is an explicitly unmet challenge of this approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 A decision-level integration approach (scTriangulate) that mixes and matches conflicting single-cell clustering results from multiple algorithms, modalities, resolutions, and reference annotations using the Shapley Value from coalitional game theory plus cluster stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5/TFIDF10, SCCAF), rather than selecting an ensemble consensus. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: A decision-level integration approach (scTriangulate) that mixes and matches conflicting single-cell clustering results from multiple algorithms, modalities, resolutions, and reference annotations using the Shapley Value from coalitional game theory plus cluster stability metrics (reassign, TFIDF5/TFIDF10, SCCAF), rather than selecting an ensemble consensus.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a single well-justified clustering resolution already resolves all cell states of interest — scTriangulate addresses the case where no single resolution identifies the most discrete cell states across modalities When the goal is a joint latent-space or graph-based multimodal embedding (e.g. Seurat-WNN or TotalVI) rather than reconciling pre-computed cluster annotations at the decision level When cell populations still need to be named: population naming remains largely non-standardized and is an explicitly unmet challenge of this approach

skills.description: Use when single-cell profiles (e.g. CSV expression matrix plus discrete class labels) must be visualized in 2D while preserving both cluster structure and differentiation pathways, especially when t-SNE/PCA/MDS fail to reveal trajectories.
skills.name: single-cell-cluster-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-cluster-visualization Use when single-cell profiles (e.g. CSV expression matrix plus discrete class labels) must be visualized in 2D while preserving both cluster structure and differentiation pathways, especially when t-SNE/PCA/MDS fail to reveal trajectories. The analysis goal is pseudotime ordering alone (e.g. cluster-then-MST ordering) rather than a supervised 2D visualization — TSCAN is the better fit No discrete class/cluster labels are available, since the knn edge construction and class-confidence contraction both require a prior user-defined cluster assignment A quantitative comparison of dimensionality-reduction biases (e.g. variance explained by PCA) is needed; the article reports no quantitative metrics for GraphDDP vs t-SNE/PCA/MDS, only qualitative trajectory visibility http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Produce a supervised 2D visualization of single-cell data that integrates cluster membership and differentiation trajectories using GraphDDP's force-based (Kamada-Kawai) graph embedding of knn same-class edges and density-gradient k-shift edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Produce a supervised 2D visualization of single-cell data that integrates cluster membership and differentiation trajectories using GraphDDP's force-based (Kamada-Kawai) graph embedding of knn same-class edges and density-gradient k-shift edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is pseudotime ordering alone (e.g. cluster-then-MST ordering) rather than a supervised 2D visualization — TSCAN is the better fit No discrete class/cluster labels are available, since the knn edge construction and class-confidence contraction both require a prior user-defined cluster assignment A quantitative comparison of dimensionality-reduction biases (e.g. variance explained by PCA) is needed; the article reports no quantitative metrics for GraphDDP vs t-SNE/PCA/MDS, only qualitative trajectory visibility

skills.description: Use when you need to judge whether a single-cell clustering/joint-embedding method (e.g. CoupledNMF, Cell Ranger, Seurat V3) produces subpopulations consistent with external labels derived from FACS-sorted bulk signatures.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-accuracy-evaluation Use when you need to judge whether a single-cell clustering/joint-embedding method (e.g. CoupledNMF, Cell Ranger, Seurat V3) produces subpopulations consistent with external labels derived from FACS-sorted bulk signatures. Data come from multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg's approach does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition to be compared You lack external (bulk/FACS-derived) reference labels — silhouette significance against surrogate ground truth cannot be computed The goal is downstream differential regulatory network construction (use the sc_compreg workflow instead of the clustering-validation skill) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Validates single-cell clustering and joint embedding (CoupledNMF vs Cell Ranger vs Seurat V3 label transfer) on healthy donor BMMC scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq by scoring cluster assignments against surrogate ground truth from FACS-sorted bulk cell-type signatures, using silhouette index and sign rank tests. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Validates single-cell clustering and joint embedding (CoupledNMF vs Cell Ranger vs Seurat V3 label transfer) on healthy donor BMMC scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq by scoring cluster assignments against surrogate ground truth from FACS-sorted bulk cell-type signatures, using silhouette index and sign rank tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from multiple donors per condition — sc-compReg's approach does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition to be compared You lack external (bulk/FACS-derived) reference labels — silhouette significance against surrogate ground truth cannot be computed The goal is downstream differential regulatory network construction (use the sc_compreg workflow instead of the clustering-validation skill)

skills.description: Use when clustering raw UMI count matrices from droplet-based scRNA-seq (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium) generated for several individuals or donors, and naive pooling would cause batch effects or Cell Ranger aggregation downsampling would lose information.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-across-multiple-individuals
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-across-multiple-individuals Use when clustering raw UMI count matrices from droplet-based scRNA-seq (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium) generated for several individuals or donors, and naive pooling would cause batch effects or Cell Ranger aggregation downsampling would lose information. The dataset consists of a single individual (use the DIMMSC mode explicitly instead of multi-individual BAMM-SC). The goal is quantifying cell cycle or developmental stages — each cell is assumed to belong to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities only measure clustering uncertainty. The analysis requires identifying very rare cell types — filtering genes with excessive zeros and the supervised BAMMSC.predict strategy may miss rare clusters. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Cluster droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count data from multiple individuals simultaneously using BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model that accounts for data heterogeneity and batch effects (e.g., unbalanced sequencing depths) in a unified framework. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09639-3
skills.summary: Cluster droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count data from multiple individuals simultaneously using BAMM-SC, a Bayesian hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture model that accounts for data heterogeneity and batch effects (e.g., unbalanced sequencing depths) in a unified framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset consists of a single individual (use the DIMMSC mode explicitly instead of multi-individual BAMM-SC). The goal is quantifying cell cycle or developmental stages — each cell is assumed to belong to one distinct cluster and posterior probabilities only measure clustering uncertainty. The analysis requires identifying very rare cell types — filtering genes with excessive zeros and the supervised BAMMSC.predict strategy may miss rare clusters.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell perturbation dataset contains control cells plus one or more treatments and you need control-anchored, interpretable cell states — especially when standard integration workflows might erase perturbation-unique responses.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-across-treatments
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-across-treatments Use when a single-cell perturbation dataset contains control cells plus one or more treatments and you need control-anchored, interpretable cell states — especially when standard integration workflows might erase perturbation-unique responses. No control/untreated population exists to anchor the semi-supervised clustering — ICAT requires control-defined states as input The goal is batch correction or integration that removes perturbation effects, rather than resolving treatment-induced cell states (ICAT deliberately preserves perturbation-unique responses) Input is already aggregated (pseudobulk) or is a pre-labeled cell-type annotation table rather than per-cell counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Apply ICAT, which combines NCFS self-supervised gene weighting with control-guided semi-supervised Louvain clustering, to resolve cell states in single-cell perturbation data while keeping control labels fixed so treated cells join any state. The paper validates this on a sea urchin PMC SMART-Seq2 dataset where only ICAT recovers a perturbation-unique response that integration workflows miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad278
skills.summary: Apply ICAT, which combines NCFS self-supervised gene weighting with control-guided semi-supervised Louvain clustering, to resolve cell states in single-cell perturbation data while keeping control labels fixed so treated cells join any state. The paper validates this on a sea urchin PMC SMART-Seq2 dataset where only ICAT recovers a perturbation-unique response that integration workflows miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No control/untreated population exists to anchor the semi-supervised clustering — ICAT requires control-defined states as input The goal is batch correction or integration that removes perturbation effects, rather than resolving treatment-induced cell states (ICAT deliberately preserves perturbation-unique responses) Input is already aggregated (pseudobulk) or is a pre-labeled cell-type annotation table rather than per-cell counts

skills.description: Use when you have precomputed cell embeddings (e.g. SnapCCESS snapshots across ensemble sizes) for multimodal single-cell data and need to compare clustering algorithms against known cell-type labels using ARI and NMI.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-benchmarking Use when you have precomputed cell embeddings (e.g. SnapCCESS snapshots across ensemble sizes) for multimodal single-cell data and need to compare clustering algorithms against known cell-type labels using ARI and NMI. You only need a single clustering result on one embedding — a full algorithm/ensemble-size benchmark is overkill. No reference cell-type labels exist, so ARI/NMI against ground truth cannot be computed. The input is raw RNA/ADT count matrices rather than already-generated embeddings; generate SnapCCESS embeddings first. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Benchmarks how multiple clustering algorithms (k-means, CiteFuse spectral clustering, and SIMLR) perform when coupled with SnapCCESS embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data, tracking whether performance improves with ensemble size and comparing ARI/NMI against reference cell-type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Benchmarks how multiple clustering algorithms (k-means, CiteFuse spectral clustering, and SIMLR) perform when coupled with SnapCCESS embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data, tracking whether performance improves with ensemble size and comparing ARI/NMI against reference cell-type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single clustering result on one embedding — a full algorithm/ensemble-size benchmark is overkill. No reference cell-type labels exist, so ARI/NMI against ground truth cannot be computed. The input is raw RNA/ADT count matrices rather than already-generated embeddings; generate SnapCCESS embeddings first.

skills.description: Use when comparing clustering method performance on single-cell (mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) datasets with known cell-type labels, or when testing whether a clustering method stays accurate at large scale via subsampling.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-comparison Use when comparing clustering method performance on single-cell (mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) datasets with known cell-type labels, or when testing whether a clustering method stays accurate at large scale via subsampling.
