Clustering labels have not yet been generated — scQA's label propagation must run first (labels.txt does not exist) No published marker/DEG reference gene sets exist for the dataset's tissue, so overlap validation cannot be grounded Goal is cluster identification itself (e.g., estimating number of cell types) rather than annotating/validating existing clusters — use scQA's LC1/LC2/CC pipeline directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Validates biological significance of cluster-defining key genes (consensus landmarks) identified by scQA by overlapping them against cell-type marker genes, differentially expressed genes (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01), and hub genes from the dataset's original publication, plus GO-term enrichment checks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Validates biological significance of cluster-defining key genes (consensus landmarks) identified by scQA by overlapping them against cell-type marker genes, differentially expressed genes (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01), and hub genes from the dataset's original publication, plus GO-term enrichment checks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clustering labels have not yet been generated — scQA's label propagation must run first (labels.txt does not exist) No published marker/DEG reference gene sets exist for the dataset's tissue, so overlap validation cannot be grounded Goal is cluster identification itself (e.g., estimating number of cell types) rather than annotating/validating existing clusters — use scQA's LC1/LC2/CC pipeline directly

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify the robustness or reproducibility of clusters produced by repeated stochastic single-cell clustering runs (e.g., SCA runs in rCASC), or when implementing cluster-stability validation metrics with a 0.5 explainability threshold.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-robustness-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-robustness-quantification Use when you need to quantify the robustness or reproducibility of clusters produced by repeated stochastic single-cell clustering runs (e.g., SCA runs in rCASC), or when implementing cluster-stability validation metrics with a 0.5 explainability threshold. You have only a single clustering run — QCC and QCM are defined across multiple SCA runs and random run pairs, so a one-off clustering cannot be scored Your goal is to perform the clustering itself or to annotate cluster function (e.g., SSCA signatures of TFs, miRNAs, kinases) rather than to evaluate clustering robustness No reference/valuable cluster definition exists — QCC measures reconstruction of a specific reference cluster, so it is undefined without one http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implements the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics from the SCA/rCASC paper, which quantify how faithfully the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder reconstructs valuable cell clusters across repeated runs. QCC scores co-localization of reference-cluster cells across runs and QCM scores run-to-run cluster consistency, with QCC and QCM >= 0.5 defining a cluster explainable by SCA analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Implements the QCC (Quality Control of Cluster) and QCM (Quality Control of Model) metrics from the SCA/rCASC paper, which quantify how faithfully the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder reconstructs valuable cell clusters across repeated runs. QCC scores co-localization of reference-cluster cells across runs and QCM scores run-to-run cluster consistency, with QCC and QCM >= 0.5 defining a cluster explainable by SCA analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single clustering run — QCC and QCM are defined across multiple SCA runs and random run pairs, so a one-off clustering cannot be scored Your goal is to perform the clustering itself or to annotate cluster function (e.g., SSCA signatures of TFs, miRNAs, kinases) rather than to evaluate clustering robustness No reference/valuable cluster definition exists — QCC measures reconstruction of a specific reference cluster, so it is undefined without one

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a pseudo-time reconstruction (e.g. consensus-TSP vs arbitrary insertion or Oscope) on cell-cycle-labeled scRNA-seq data across a sweep of cluster numbers k, needing correlation-scores per k.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-sweep
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-sweep Use when benchmarking a pseudo-time reconstruction (e.g. consensus-TSP vs arbitrary insertion or Oscope) on cell-cycle-labeled scRNA-seq data across a sweep of cluster numbers k, needing correlation-scores per k. Data is not unsynchronized scRNA-seq with reliable cell-cycle phase labels — the correlation-score against stage labels cannot be computed Goal is a single ordering rather than benchmarking performance across cluster numbers; a single get_ordIndex call without the k sweep suffices Comparing pseudo-time methods on data lacking the two-wave G1/G2 cyclic structure reCAT assumes (phases forming a cycle with monotonic transcriptome change) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sweeps the number of single-cell clusters k in the reCAT consensus-TSP pipeline, recomputing the cell ordering at each k and benchmarking the resulting pseudo time-series against baselines via a PCC-based correlation-score, as done for the mESC-SMARTer comparison (Fig. 2c). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-00039-z
skills.summary: Sweeps the number of single-cell clusters k in the reCAT consensus-TSP pipeline, recomputing the cell ordering at each k and benchmarking the resulting pseudo time-series against baselines via a PCC-based correlation-score, as done for the mESC-SMARTer comparison (Fig. 2c).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not unsynchronized scRNA-seq with reliable cell-cycle phase labels — the correlation-score against stage labels cannot be computed Goal is a single ordering rather than benchmarking performance across cluster numbers; a single get_ordIndex call without the k sweep suffices Comparing pseudo-time methods on data lacking the two-wave G1/G2 cyclic structure reCAT assumes (phases forming a cycle with monotonic transcriptome change)

skills.description: Use when scRNAseq counts (e.g. setA, 10XGenomics UMI tables) have pre-computed cell clusters and the goal is to discover which biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, kinase targets) drives clusterization, or to test whether combining knowledge groups improves cluster reconstruction.
skills.name: single-cell-clustermining-with-autoencoder
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustermining-with-autoencoder Use when scRNAseq counts (e.g. setA, 10XGenomics UMI tables) have pre-computed cell clusters and the goal is to discover which biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, kinase targets) drives clusterization, or to test whether combining knowledge groups improves cluster reconstruction. When no pre-existing cluster assignments exist and de novo clustering itself is the goal — SCA queries already-defined cell subpopulations rather than performing the clustering When the aim is to measure miRNA expression directly — the article notes it is not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuits cannot be directly measured; miRNA effects are inferred via miRNA target-gene latent spaces When the input is raw FASTQ rather than a counts table — preprocessing (cellrangerCount, indropCounts, filterZeros, lorenzFilter) is a separate upstream workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Functional mining of single-cell RNAseq clusters using the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) within rCASC: encoded latent spaces built from experimentally validated TF, miRNA, kinase targets and immune signatures reconstruct only clusters where the encoding is key to cell aggregation, scored by QCM and QCC metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-020-00162-6
skills.summary: Functional mining of single-cell RNAseq clusters using the Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA/SSCA) within rCASC: encoded latent spaces built from experimentally validated TF, miRNA, kinase targets and immune signatures reconstruct only clusters where the encoding is key to cell aggregation, scored by QCM and QCC metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no pre-existing cluster assignments exist and de novo clustering itself is the goal — SCA queries already-defined cell subpopulations rather than performing the clustering When the aim is to measure miRNA expression directly — the article notes it is not possible to quantify miRNAs together with mRNAs at single-cell level, so TF-miRNA circuits cannot be directly measured; miRNA effects are inferred via miRNA target-gene latent spaces When the input is raw FASTQ rather than a counts table — preprocessing (cellrangerCount, indropCounts, filterZeros, lorenzFilter) is a separate upstream workflow

skills.description: Use when analyzing PTA-amplified or low-coverage scWGS BAM files to call allele-specific CNAs, especially at small size scales (200 kb–5 Mb), or when comparing single-cell CNA callers on simulated or brain/meningioma datasets.
skills.name: single-cell-cna-calling
skills.search_text: single-cell-cna-calling Use when analyzing PTA-amplified or low-coverage scWGS BAM files to call allele-specific CNAs, especially at small size scales (200 kb–5 Mb), or when comparing single-cell CNA callers on simulated or brain/meningioma datasets. Input is germline genotyping or sex chromosomes — SCAN2/HiScanner analysis is restricted to diploid autosomes 1–22 The task is bulk-tumor CNA calling — BAF is a standard feature of bulk methods such as ASCAT and Battenberg; single-cell callers like HiScanner are tailored to scWGS profiles Only clonal CNAs at megabase scale in low-coverage cancer cells are needed — existing low-coverage callers (CHISEL, Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN) may suffice, though HiScanner is designed to extend resolution below 5 Mb http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect allele-specific copy number alterations (CNAs) in single-cell whole-genome sequencing (scWGS) data by combining read-depth ratios (RDR), B-allele frequencies (BAF), and reference-based phasing, as implemented in HiScanner, and benchmarked against BAF-agnostic callers like Ginkgo. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Detect allele-specific copy number alterations (CNAs) in single-cell whole-genome sequencing (scWGS) data by combining read-depth ratios (RDR), B-allele frequencies (BAF), and reference-based phasing, as implemented in HiScanner, and benchmarked against BAF-agnostic callers like Ginkgo.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is germline genotyping or sex chromosomes — SCAN2/HiScanner analysis is restricted to diploid autosomes 1–22 The task is bulk-tumor CNA calling — BAF is a standard feature of bulk methods such as ASCAT and Battenberg; single-cell callers like HiScanner are tailored to scWGS profiles Only clonal CNAs at megabase scale in low-coverage cancer cells are needed — existing low-coverage callers (CHISEL, Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN) may suffice, though HiScanner is designed to extend resolution below 5 Mb

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (10x Genomics droplet-based or Smart-seq2) from a tumour sample must be profiled for allele-specific CNAs (copy gain, copy loss, copy-neutral LOH) and subclones reconstructed from sparse, low-coverage data.
skills.name: single-cell-cna-detection-from-scrna
skills.search_text: single-cell-cna-detection-from-scrna Use when scRNA-seq data (10x Genomics droplet-based or Smart-seq2) from a tumour sample must be profiled for allele-specific CNAs (copy gain, copy loss, copy-neutral LOH) and subclones reconstructed from sparse, low-coverage data. The input is single-cell DNA-seq rather than scRNA-seq — tools such as ACT or CHISEL are designed for that modality instead. Only copy-number magnitude is needed and copy-neutral LOH detection is out of scope: InferCNV or CopyKAT, which ignore allelic information, may suffice. High-coverage data make per-SNP allelic signals reliable enough without aggregation; the smoothing/haplotyping machinery is aimed at extremely low per-variant coverage. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Detect allele-specific copy number alterations (CNAs) and reconstruct tumour clonal substructure from sparse single-cell RNA-seq data by combining read-depth ratio (RDR) and B-allele frequency (BAF) modules in XClone, with HMM smoothing along genome coordinates and KNN smoothing across the cell-neighborhood graph. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Detect allele-specific copy number alterations (CNAs) and reconstruct tumour clonal substructure from sparse single-cell RNA-seq data by combining read-depth ratio (RDR) and B-allele frequency (BAF) modules in XClone, with HMM smoothing along genome coordinates and KNN smoothing across the cell-neighborhood graph.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell DNA-seq rather than scRNA-seq — tools such as ACT or CHISEL are designed for that modality instead. Only copy-number magnitude is needed and copy-neutral LOH detection is out of scope: InferCNV or CopyKAT, which ignore allelic information, may suffice. High-coverage data make per-SNP allelic signals reliable enough without aggregation; the smoothing/haplotyping machinery is aimed at extremely low per-variant coverage.

skills.description: Use when preparing single-cell WGS (e.g., PTA- or MDA-amplified) data for CNA calling and an assay-specific minimum bin size must be chosen from measured allelic dropout, or when verifying that single-cell CNA calls pass QC thresholds (mappability, MAPQ, VAF filters).
skills.name: single-cell-cnv-analysis-quality-control
skills.search_text: single-cell-cnv-analysis-quality-control Use when preparing single-cell WGS (e.g., PTA- or MDA-amplified) data for CNA calling and an assay-specific minimum bin size must be chosen from measured allelic dropout, or when verifying that single-cell CNA calls pass QC thresholds (mappability, MAPQ, VAF filters). When the goal is CNA calling in bulk tumor data — tools like ASCAT and Battenberg already handle BAF there and no single-cell ADO calibration applies When input cells are expected aneuploid (e.g., tumor cells): the HMM must be trained on copy-neutral control cells, so aneuploid cells would corrupt the dropout-size distribution When the amplification chemistry has already been characterized and a bin size fixed — re-running ADO calibration on unrelated cells adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Quality-control workflow for single-cell CNV analysis that calibrates assay-specific allelic dropout (ADO) via a two-state HMM on phased BAF at germline heterozygous SNPs (gHETs), deriving the smallest permissible bin size that balances CNA detection resolution against amplification noise before running the HiScanner copy-number caller. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Quality-control workflow for single-cell CNV analysis that calibrates assay-specific allelic dropout (ADO) via a two-state HMM on phased BAF at germline heterozygous SNPs (gHETs), deriving the smallest permissible bin size that balances CNA detection resolution against amplification noise before running the HiScanner copy-number caller.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is CNA calling in bulk tumor data — tools like ASCAT and Battenberg already handle BAF there and no single-cell ADO calibration applies When input cells are expected aneuploid (e.g., tumor cells): the HMM must be trained on copy-neutral control cells, so aneuploid cells would corrupt the dropout-size distribution When the amplification chemistry has already been characterized and a bin size fixed — re-running ADO calibration on unrelated cells adds no information

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (e.g., 430-cell GBM dataset) to call large-scale CNVs per cell, identify mutually exclusive/co-occurring CNV subclones within a patient, and derive a CNV-based clonal phylogenetic tree.
skills.name: single-cell-cnv-calling-from-rnaseq
skills.search_text: single-cell-cnv-calling-from-rnaseq Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (e.g., 430-cell GBM dataset) to call large-scale CNVs per cell, identify mutually exclusive/co-occurring CNV subclones within a patient, and derive a CNV-based clonal phylogenetic tree. Input is already a DNA-seq copy-number call set or feature table — CaSpER is designed for CNV inference from RNA-seq signal, not re-analysis of existing CNV calls 3′-only sequencing data (e.g., DropSeq/10x-style) where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted because variants are measured only near 3′ ends of genes — pooled BAF signal may be too sparse Bulk RNA-seq cohort-level focal CNV discovery without single-cell resolution needs — the bulk variant of this skill applies instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Infer single-cell copy-number variant (CNV) architecture — including mutually exclusive subclones and clonal trees — from scRNA-seq expression data by integrating multiscale-smoothed expression signal with patient-pooled BAF allele-shift signal using CaSpER. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Infer single-cell copy-number variant (CNV) architecture — including mutually exclusive subclones and clonal trees — from scRNA-seq expression data by integrating multiscale-smoothed expression signal with patient-pooled BAF allele-shift signal using CaSpER.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a DNA-seq copy-number call set or feature table — CaSpER is designed for CNV inference from RNA-seq signal, not re-analysis of existing CNV calls 3′-only sequencing data (e.g., DropSeq/10x-style) where BAF shift signal is adversely impacted because variants are measured only near 3′ ends of genes — pooled BAF signal may be too sparse Bulk RNA-seq cohort-level focal CNV discovery without single-cell resolution needs — the bulk variant of this skill applies instead

skills.description: Use when a cohort's bulk sequencing data (e.g., preprocessed COVID-19 cohort bulk RNA-seq from the scSemiProfiler example_data folder) must yield all representative samples in one batch, and multi-round active learning is impractical or would introduce batch effects.
skills.name: single-cell-cohort-representative-sampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-cohort-representative-sampling Use when a cohort's bulk sequencing data (e.g., preprocessed COVID-19 cohort bulk RNA-seq from the scSemiProfiler example_data folder) must yield all representative samples in one batch, and multi-round active learning is impractical or would introduce batch effects. You need iterative, inference-driven representative selection to improve single-cell inference — use scSemiProfiler's Active Learning module instead of global mode The cohort has 100 or more samples, where the 'sample size minus one PCs' rule described for smaller cohorts no longer applies You only have single-target bulk data for one sample — use the bulk deconvolution (single-cell level) pipeline with a single-cell reference instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Selects representative samples from a bulk RNA-seq cohort in a single round using scSemiProfiler's global mode, so that only a small set of samples needs real single-cell sequencing for semi-profiling. For the COVID-19 cohort, global mode selected 28 representatives. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Selects representative samples from a bulk RNA-seq cohort in a single round using scSemiProfiler's global mode, so that only a small set of samples needs real single-cell sequencing for semi-profiling. For the COVID-19 cohort, global mode selected 28 representatives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need iterative, inference-driven representative selection to improve single-cell inference — use scSemiProfiler's Active Learning module instead of global mode The cohort has 100 or more samples, where the 'sample size minus one PCs' rule described for smaller cohorts no longer applies You only have single-target bulk data for one sample — use the bulk deconvolution (single-cell level) pipeline with a single-cell reference instead

skills.description: Use when you have a seqspec YAML for a combinatorial-indexing single-cell assay and need to identify where the cell barcode is encoded (e.g. Illumina index regions) before preprocessing FASTQs.
skills.name: single-cell-combinatorial-indexing-assay-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-combinatorial-indexing-assay-annotation Use when you have a seqspec YAML for a combinatorial-indexing single-cell assay and need to identify where the cell barcode is encoded (e.g. Illumina index regions) before preprocessing FASTQs. Input is already a cell-by-feature count matrix or barcode list rather than an assay library specification (use mx filter/inspect or bustools instead) The goal is downstream preprocessing — barcode error correction and UMI counting are performed with bustools, not by spec annotation The assay has no seqspec YAML in the IGVF/seqspec specs/ directory and you cannot author one; annotation cannot proceed from FASTQs alone http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates the library structure of combinatorial-indexing single-cell assays (e.g. sci-CAR-seq, Cao et al. 2018) with the seqspec machine-readable specification, locating which library region encodes the cell barcode. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae168
skills.summary: Annotates the library structure of combinatorial-indexing single-cell assays (e.g. sci-CAR-seq, Cao et al. 2018) with the seqspec machine-readable specification, locating which library region encodes the cell barcode.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-by-feature count matrix or barcode list rather than an assay library specification (use mx filter/inspect or bustools instead) The goal is downstream preprocessing — barcode error correction and UMI counting are performed with bustools, not by spec annotation The assay has no seqspec YAML in the IGVF/seqspec specs/ directory and you cannot author one; annotation cannot proceed from FASTQs alone

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data (genes x cells) plus cell-type labels need unsupervised cell-cell communication inference without relying on predefined L-R pairs, e.g., non-human species or benchmarking against CellChat/CellPhoneDB/iTALK.
skills.name: single-cell-communication-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-communication-inference Use when scRNA-seq expression data (genes x cells) plus cell-type labels need unsupervised cell-cell communication inference without relying on predefined L-R pairs, e.g., non-human species or benchmarking against CellChat/CellPhoneDB/iTALK. When the analysis goal strictly requires literature-curated ligand-receptor interpretation only (e.g., an established human L-R focused workflow with CellChat/CellPhoneDB/iTALK defaults) rather than species-agnostic, GRN-based inference. When input lacks existing cell classification labels, since MDIC3 infers communication networks from individual cells to cell types 'based on existing cell classification labels'. When the GRN cannot be trusted or computed: the article notes 'the accuracy of the GRN can affect the results of cell-cell communication for MDIC3', so a poor-quality GRN invalidates the decomposition. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Infer cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq data using MDIC3, which factorizes the expression matrix A into R*Sigma*W with the GRN adjacency matrix (from GNIPLR) as R and solves W=(R*Sigma)+A as a weighted directed cell-cell communication adjacency matrix, independent of prior ligand-receptor knowledge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100911
skills.summary: Infer cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq data using MDIC3, which factorizes the expression matrix A into R*Sigma*W with the GRN adjacency matrix (from GNIPLR) as R and solves W=(R*Sigma)+A as a weighted directed cell-cell communication adjacency matrix, independent of prior ligand-receptor knowledge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal strictly requires literature-curated ligand-receptor interpretation only (e.g., an established human L-R focused workflow with CellChat/CellPhoneDB/iTALK defaults) rather than species-agnostic, GRN-based inference. When input lacks existing cell classification labels, since MDIC3 infers communication networks from individual cells to cell types 'based on existing cell classification labels'. When the GRN cannot be trusted or computed: the article notes 'the accuracy of the GRN can affect the results of cell-cell communication for MDIC3', so a poor-quality GRN invalidates the decomposition.

skills.description: Use when building or visualizing a cell-to-cell communication network from single-cell expression data plus cell-type labels and you must decide which ligand–receptor edges pass detection (e.g. >20% of cells), specificity, and expression cutoffs before drawing.
skills.name: single-cell-communication-network-thresholding
skills.search_text: single-cell-communication-network-thresholding Use when building or visualizing a cell-to-cell communication network from single-cell expression data plus cell-type labels and you must decide which ligand–receptor edges pass detection (e.g. >20% of cells), specificity, and expression cutoffs before drawing. Input is spatial transcriptomics data — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data The analysis requires modelling heteromeric ligand/receptor complexes, co-receptor requirements, or downstream signalling consequences — NATMI does not model these (use tools like CellPhoneDB/NicheNet instead) Estimates of ligand–receptor binding kinetics are required — NATMI provides none http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Applies NATMI's expression, detection, and specificity cutoffs when constructing and drawing ligand–receptor-mediated cell-to-cell communication networks, so that only edges supported by co-expressed ligand–receptor pairs in defined cell types are retained. This mirrors the manuscript's Tabula Muris workflow (detection threshold 0.2, specificity/expression thresholds 0) used to identify highly communicating cell pairs and communities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Applies NATMI's expression, detection, and specificity cutoffs when constructing and drawing ligand–receptor-mediated cell-to-cell communication networks, so that only edges supported by co-expressed ligand–receptor pairs in defined cell types are retained. This mirrors the manuscript's Tabula Muris workflow (detection threshold 0.2, specificity/expression thresholds 0) used to identify highly communicating cell pairs and communities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is spatial transcriptomics data — NATMI has not been specifically designed for spatial data The analysis requires modelling heteromeric ligand/receptor complexes, co-receptor requirements, or downstream signalling consequences — NATMI does not model these (use tools like CellPhoneDB/NicheNet instead) Estimates of ligand–receptor binding kinetics are required — NATMI provides none

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression, cell-type labels, and (optionally) time-point annotations and need to infer and compare cell-cell interaction networks, especially to test how L-R aggregation schemes affect interaction recovery.
skills.name: single-cell-communication-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-communication-quantification Use when you have scRNA-seq expression, cell-type labels, and (optionally) time-point annotations and need to infer and compare cell-cell interaction networks, especially to test how L-R aggregation schemes affect interaction recovery. Data lacks reliable cell-type labels or protein-localization information is irrelevant (e.g., purely intracellular gene programs) — the localization-aware scoring is the method's core rationale Analysis goal is temporal dynamics across developmental series rather than a single-time-point interaction map — use dsCellNet's developcorrelation/DTW workflow instead of singlenet alone The L-R pairs of interest are absent from the default 5,744-pair database and no supplementary L-R list is supplied — the default list size can cause missed interactions (e.g., MG–Neurons) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quantifies ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell interactions from single-cell RNA-seq using dsCellNet, which scores membrane- and secreted-ligand interactions separately against protein localization, rather than a single product-of-sum or product-of-mean aggregation of L-R expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: Quantifies ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell interactions from single-cell RNA-seq using dsCellNet, which scores membrane- and secreted-ligand interactions separately against protein localization, rather than a single product-of-sum or product-of-mean aggregation of L-R expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks reliable cell-type labels or protein-localization information is irrelevant (e.g., purely intracellular gene programs) — the localization-aware scoring is the method's core rationale Analysis goal is temporal dynamics across developmental series rather than a single-time-point interaction map — use dsCellNet's developcorrelation/DTW workflow instead of singlenet alone The L-R pairs of interest are absent from the default 5,744-pair database and no supplementary L-R list is supplied — the default list size can cause missed interactions (e.g., MG–Neurons)

skills.description: Use when you have a patient-partitioned scRNA-seq object with cell-type annotations and want community-aware metabolic fluxes per cell type (e.g. glucose uptake across myeloid, B, T, epithelial cells) rather than per-cell or bulk fluxes.
skills.name: single-cell-community-flux-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-community-flux-modeling Use when you have a patient-partitioned scRNA-seq object with cell-type annotations and want community-aware metabolic fluxes per cell type (e.g. glucose uptake across myeloid, B, T, epithelial cells) rather than per-cell or bulk fluxes. Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than annotated single-cell data — use METAFlux::compute_flux instead of compute_sc_flux Data lacks cell-type annotations or patient/TME grouping needed to define the community and its fractions Per-single-cell flux estimates are required — METAFlux calculates fluxes at the cell cluster/type level, not per individual cell http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Model a tumor microenvironment as a multi-cell-type metabolic community with METAFlux: aggregate scRNA-seq expression per cell type per patient, compute MRAS against the 13,082-reaction Human-GEM, and run FBA over the whole TME to obtain per-cell-type reaction fluxes (e.g. glucose uptake via HMR_9034). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Model a tumor microenvironment as a multi-cell-type metabolic community with METAFlux: aggregate scRNA-seq expression per cell type per patient, compute MRAS against the 13,082-reaction Human-GEM, and run FBA over the whole TME to obtain per-cell-type reaction fluxes (e.g. glucose uptake via HMR_9034).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq rather than annotated single-cell data — use METAFlux::compute_flux instead of compute_sc_flux Data lacks cell-type annotations or patient/TME grouping needed to define the community and its fractions Per-single-cell flux estimates are required — METAFlux calculates fluxes at the cell cluster/type level, not per individual cell

skills.description: Use when you have four single-cell datasets (one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions/populations) and need to identify subpopulation-specific differential regulatory relations between transcription factors and target genes.
skills.name: single-cell-comparative-regulatory-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-comparative-regulatory-analysis Use when you have four single-cell datasets (one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions/populations) and need to identify subpopulation-specific differential regulatory relations between transcription factors and target genes. You only have a single condition/sample — sc_compreg tests differential regulation between two linked subpopulations, not regulation within one sample More than one donor per condition — the method does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition (extension noted as pending in the discussion) Expression/accessibility matrices are not log2-transformed and have not been preprocessed into PeakName_intersect.txt / peak_gene_prior_intersect.bed via sc_compreg_process_data_.sh http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Implements the sc-compReg workflow for comparing gene regulatory networks between two conditions from paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data, constructing a cell-specific transcription factor regulatory potential (TFRP) index and testing differential TF-TG regulation across linked subpopulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: Implements the sc-compReg workflow for comparing gene regulatory networks between two conditions from paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data, constructing a cell-specific transcription factor regulatory potential (TFRP) index and testing differential TF-TG regulation across linked subpopulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single condition/sample — sc_compreg tests differential regulation between two linked subpopulations, not regulation within one sample More than one donor per condition — the method does not yet accommodate multiple donors under each condition (extension noted as pending in the discussion) Expression/accessibility matrices are not log2-transformed and have not been preprocessed into PeakName_intersect.txt / peak_gene_prior_intersect.bed via sc_compreg_process_data_.sh

skills.description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes on rows, cells on columns) and need to remove the normal-cell expression baseline so that cell-specific copy number signal can be segmented, without manually identifying reference cell clusters as inferCNV requires.
skills.name: single-cell-copy-number-baseline-subtraction
skills.search_text: single-cell-copy-number-baseline-subtraction Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes on rows, cells on columns) and need to remove the normal-cell expression baseline so that cell-specific copy number signal can be segmented, without manually identifying reference cell clusters as inferCNV requires. The tumor type has minimal copy number alterations (e.g., leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — the aneuploidy-based baseline/CNV approach may not be suited in this case You already have a trusted reference profile or matched normal cells and only need clonal structure with a fixed reference — pass norm_cells with FIXED_NORMAL_CELLS=TRUE rather than re-estimating a baseline http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Estimates a copy number baseline from confidently normal cells in a scRNA-seq count matrix (median expression of cells passing yaGST significance thresholds, P < 1e-10 and NES > 1.0) and subtracts it to produce the relative expression matrix that SCEVAN smooths and segments for clonal CNV detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Estimates a copy number baseline from confidently normal cells in a scRNA-seq count matrix (median expression of cells passing yaGST significance thresholds, P < 1e-10 and NES > 1.0) and subtracts it to produce the relative expression matrix that SCEVAN smooths and segments for clonal CNV detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tumor type has minimal copy number alterations (e.g., leukemia, pediatric cancers, Ependymomas) — the aneuploidy-based baseline/CNV approach may not be suited in this case You already have a trusted reference profile or matched normal cells and only need clonal structure with a fixed reference — pass norm_cells with FIXED_NORMAL_CELLS=TRUE rather than re-estimating a baseline

skills.description: Use when calling allele-specific somatic CNAs from paired single-cell + matched bulk WGS BAMs (PTA-amplified, ~20-30x scWGS), when small (200 kb-5 Mb) or subclonal CNAs must be resolved, or when benchmarking single-cell CNA callers.
skills.name: single-cell-copy-number-calling
skills.search_text: single-cell-copy-number-calling Use when calling allele-specific somatic CNAs from paired single-cell + matched bulk WGS BAMs (PTA-amplified, ~20-30x scWGS), when small (200 kb-5 Mb) or subclonal CNAs must be resolved, or when benchmarking single-cell CNA callers. Data are low-coverage (<0.05x per cell) single-cell cancer datasets from DLP+ or 10x Genomics platforms — CHISEL/Alleloscope-style callers designed for clonal CNAs are the intended setting, while HiScanner exploits high-coverage (>20x) scWGS Input lacks a matched bulk sample or phased germline heterozygous SNPs — the BAF/phasing steps require phased gHETs and bulk VAF 0.1-0.9 Calling germline variants or working on sex chromosomes — SCAN2 excludes mutations with any bulk read support and only diploid autosomes (1-22) are supported http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 A high-resolution, allele-specific somatic CNA calling workflow for single-cell WGS that combines read depth (RDR), B-allele frequency (BAF), and reference-based haplotype phasing via HiScanner, benchmarked against Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN, and CHISEL on PTA-amplified high-coverage scWGS data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: A high-resolution, allele-specific somatic CNA calling workflow for single-cell WGS that combines read depth (RDR), B-allele frequency (BAF), and reference-based haplotype phasing via HiScanner, benchmarked against Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN, and CHISEL on PTA-amplified high-coverage scWGS data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are low-coverage (<0.05x per cell) single-cell cancer datasets from DLP+ or 10x Genomics platforms — CHISEL/Alleloscope-style callers designed for clonal CNAs are the intended setting, while HiScanner exploits high-coverage (>20x) scWGS Input lacks a matched bulk sample or phased germline heterozygous SNPs — the BAF/phasing steps require phased gHETs and bulk VAF 0.1-0.9 Calling germline variants or working on sex chromosomes — SCAN2 excludes mutations with any bulk read support and only diploid autosomes (1-22) are supported

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from tumor biopsies (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) must be automatically segregated into malignant and non-malignant cells and subcloned by copy-number architecture without a manually identified reference-cell cluster.
skills.name: single-cell-copy-number-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-copy-number-inference Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from tumor biopsies (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) must be automatically segregated into malignant and non-malignant cells and subcloned by copy-number architecture without a manually identified reference-cell cluster. Tumors expected to have minimal genomic alterations (leukemias, pediatric cancers, ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based inference is unsuitable Samples where cell-type annotation already exists and only expression analysis is needed (input is already a classified/annotated feature table) Tasks requiring matched-tumor/normal bulk segmentation only (use DNAcopy or CNVkit on bulk data rather than single-cell inference) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers per-cell malignant vs non-malignant labels and clonal copy-number substructure directly from raw scRNA-seq count matrices using SCEVAN's variational pipeline, without manually defined normal-cell references. Rationale: aneuploidy-driven expression profiles allow joint segmentation and classification that outperforms CopyKAT (F1 0.90 vs 0.63 across 106 samples). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36790-9
skills.summary: Infers per-cell malignant vs non-malignant labels and clonal copy-number substructure directly from raw scRNA-seq count matrices using SCEVAN's variational pipeline, without manually defined normal-cell references. Rationale: aneuploidy-driven expression profiles allow joint segmentation and classification that outperforms CopyKAT (F1 0.90 vs 0.63 across 106 samples).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tumors expected to have minimal genomic alterations (leukemias, pediatric cancers, ependymomas) where aneuploidy-based inference is unsuitable Samples where cell-type annotation already exists and only expression analysis is needed (input is already a classified/annotated feature table) Tasks requiring matched-tumor/normal bulk segmentation only (use DNAcopy or CNVkit on bulk data rather than single-cell inference)

skills.description: Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment objects contain sparse gene and 3'UTR isoform count matrices at single-cell resolution and counts must be summed per cell type before pairwise differential testing.
skills.name: single-cell-count-aggregation-by-cell-type
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-aggregation-by-cell-type Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment objects contain sparse gene and 3'UTR isoform count matrices at single-cell resolution and counts must be summed per cell type before pairwise differential testing. Cells lack cell-type annotations and exclude_unannotated_cells cannot resolve them, so no valid pseudobulk groups can be formed The analysis target is single-cell-level variability rather than cell-type-level comparisons, where pseudobulk aggregation would obscure per-cell signal Genes of interest are single-UTR genes, since the pipeline restricts to multi-UTR genes co-expressed in both members of the cell-type pair http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aggregates per-cell gene-level and 3'UTR isoform (multi-UTR) counts from scUTRquant-generated SingleCellExperiment objects into per-cell-type pseudobulk matrices so that pairwise cell-type statistical tests (Welch t-test DGE, scUTRboot WUI tests) can be run. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Aggregates per-cell gene-level and 3'UTR isoform (multi-UTR) counts from scUTRquant-generated SingleCellExperiment objects into per-cell-type pseudobulk matrices so that pairwise cell-type statistical tests (Welch t-test DGE, scUTRboot WUI tests) can be run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack cell-type annotations and exclude_unannotated_cells cannot resolve them, so no valid pseudobulk groups can be formed The analysis target is single-cell-level variability rather than cell-type-level comparisons, where pseudobulk aggregation would obscure per-cell signal Genes of interest are single-UTR genes, since the pipeline restricts to multi-UTR genes co-expressed in both members of the cell-type pair

skills.description: Use when benchmarking co-expression inference methods (e.g., CS-CORE vs Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) against a known true network, or when evaluating whether estimation bias harms downstream clustering/PCA via simulations with controlled n, p, and cluster structure.
skills.name: single-cell-count-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-data-simulation Use when benchmarking co-expression inference methods (e.g., CS-CORE vs Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) against a known true network, or when evaluating whether estimation bias harms downstream clustering/PCA via simulations with controlled n, p, and cluster structure. Analyzing a real scRNA-seq dataset where no ground-truth co-expression network exists — simulation is a benchmarking device, not an analysis pipeline step You require realistic overdispersion in the count-generating distribution — the model here is Poisson-only; the authors note negative binomial adaptation is deferred to future work The question concerns differential expression or cell-type annotation rather than co-expression estimation accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count data with known ground-truth co-expression structure using a latent-variable Poisson measurement model, enabling controlled benchmarks of co-expression estimation, clustering, and PCA recovery methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Generates synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count data with known ground-truth co-expression structure using a latent-variable Poisson measurement model, enabling controlled benchmarks of co-expression estimation, clustering, and PCA recovery methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing a real scRNA-seq dataset where no ground-truth co-expression network exists — simulation is a benchmarking device, not an analysis pipeline step You require realistic overdispersion in the count-generating distribution — the model here is Poisson-only; the authors note negative binomial adaptation is deferred to future work The question concerns differential expression or cell-type annotation rather than co-expression estimation accuracy

skills.description: Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts must be denoised/imputed prior to kinetic parameter estimation (kon, koff, s) with the RJAGS Gibbs sampler, or when scVI/MAGIC imputation is needed to meet modeling assumptions.
skills.name: single-cell-count-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-imputation Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts must be denoised/imputed prior to kinetic parameter estimation (kon, koff, s) with the RJAGS Gibbs sampler, or when scVI/MAGIC imputation is needed to meet modeling assumptions. The dataset is small (<~hundreds of cells): the paper notes scVI is only applicable to large datasets, so for the 130-cell non-UMI Th17 dataset MAGIC alone is appropriate The downstream task does not require imputed values (e.g., analyses explicitly designed for raw counts), since imputation alters count distributions before fitting Cells have not been clustered, violating the assumption that all cells share the same kinetic parameters for per-cluster fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Imputes raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., the Zeisel UMI cortex dataset of 3005 cells) with scVI and MAGIC before fitting two-state kinetic parameters (kon, koff, s) used by SymSim, since raw counts are unsuitable for MCMC-based kinetic fitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Imputes raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., the Zeisel UMI cortex dataset of 3005 cells) with scVI and MAGIC before fitting two-state kinetic parameters (kon, koff, s) used by SymSim, since raw counts are unsuitable for MCMC-based kinetic fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small (<~hundreds of cells): the paper notes scVI is only applicable to large datasets, so for the 130-cell non-UMI Th17 dataset MAGIC alone is appropriate The downstream task does not require imputed values (e.g., analyses explicitly designed for raw counts), since imputation alters count distributions before fitting Cells have not been clustered, violating the assumption that all cells share the same kinetic parameters for per-cluster fitting

skills.description: Use when an alternative scRNA-seq quantification workflow must be benchmarked against a standard pipeline like Cell Ranger by comparing gene-level UMI count matrices across the same cells and genes.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-correlation-analysis Use when an alternative scRNA-seq quantification workflow must be benchmarked against a standard pipeline like Cell Ranger by comparing gene-level UMI count matrices across the same cells and genes. The two count matrices quantify different feature sets (e.g. 3'UTR isoforms vs genes) or different cells, so shared-identifier alignment is impossible The goal is differential expression or 3'UTR length analysis rather than quantification-pipeline benchmarking Data are full-length or non-3'-end tag-based libraries that scUTRquant does not support http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates that a custom scRNA-seq quantification pipeline (scUTRquant on a truncated UTRome) produces gene counts concordant with a reference pipeline (Cell Ranger) by computing per-cell and per-gene Spearman rank correlations on raw UMI count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Validates that a custom scRNA-seq quantification pipeline (scUTRquant on a truncated UTRome) produces gene counts concordant with a reference pipeline (Cell Ranger) by computing per-cell and per-gene Spearman rank correlations on raw UMI count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two count matrices quantify different feature sets (e.g. 3'UTR isoforms vs genes) or different cells, so shared-identifier alignment is impossible The goal is differential expression or 3'UTR length analysis rather than quantification-pipeline benchmarking Data are full-length or non-3'-end tag-based libraries that scUTRquant does not support

skills.description: Use when you need to test stability of a fitted single-cell dynamical model (e.g. scKINETICS velocities) against technical noise in transcript capture by perturbing raw counts at reduced sequencing depths and refitting.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-downsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-downsampling Use when you need to test stability of a fitted single-cell dynamical model (e.g. scKINETICS velocities) against technical noise in transcript capture by perturbing raw counts at reduced sequencing depths and refitting. When the question is biological variation across samples or conditions rather than technical robustness of a single fit to sequencing depth. When you intend to vary the regulatory mask or model parameters along with the counts — this protocol requires those to stay fixed so only the count perturbation differs. When the input is not raw counts (e.g. already normalized or feature-selected matrices), since downsampling must operate on raw count totals to simulate capture-rate loss. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A robustness-testing skill that simulates reduced sequencing depth by randomly downsampling raw single-cell count matrices to several percentages of total counts (e.g. 15 trials per proportion) and refitting a fixed-configuration model — here scKINETICS velocity — to quantify how perturbed estimates deviate from the original fit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A robustness-testing skill that simulates reduced sequencing depth by randomly downsampling raw single-cell count matrices to several percentages of total counts (e.g. 15 trials per proportion) and refitting a fixed-configuration model — here scKINETICS velocity — to quantify how perturbed estimates deviate from the original fit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is biological variation across samples or conditions rather than technical robustness of a single fit to sequencing depth. When you intend to vary the regulatory mask or model parameters along with the counts — this protocol requires those to stay fixed so only the count perturbation differs. When the input is not raw counts (e.g. already normalized or feature-selected matrices), since downsampling must operate on raw count totals to simulate capture-rate loss.

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be converted into descending expression-ranked gene-symbol sequences for autoregressive transformer models like tGPT.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-gene-filtering
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-gene-filtering Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be converted into descending expression-ranked gene-symbol sequences for autoregressive transformer models like tGPT. Analysis requires absolute expression levels or fold changes among genes — tGPT input uses rankings only and neglects fold changes Downstream analysis depends on low-expressing genes, which are dropped when retaining only top-expressing genes A feature/embedding table already exists and no tokenization into gene-ranking sequences is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocess single-cell count matrices (e.g., HCL, GSE134355) by discarding mitochondrial, ribosomal, and non-protein-coding genes against a 20,706 protein-coding gene reference list, then rank each cell's gene symbols by descending expression to produce the token sequences tGPT consumes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Preprocess single-cell count matrices (e.g., HCL, GSE134355) by discarding mitochondrial, ribosomal, and non-protein-coding genes against a 20,706 protein-coding gene reference list, then rank each cell's gene symbols by descending expression to produce the token sequences tGPT consumes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis requires absolute expression levels or fold changes among genes — tGPT input uses rankings only and neglects fold changes Downstream analysis depends on low-expressing genes, which are dropped when retaining only top-expressing genes A feature/embedding table already exists and no tokenization into gene-ranking sequences is needed

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ files (or Cell Ranger BAMs convertible via bamtofastq) from any UMI-based scRNA-seq platform must be processed into gene-by-barcode matrices under one uniform pipeline, e.g. for cross-platform integration benchmarks.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-generation Use when raw FASTQ files (or Cell Ranger BAMs convertible via bamtofastq) from any UMI-based scRNA-seq platform must be processed into gene-by-barcode matrices under one uniform pipeline, e.g. for cross-platform integration benchmarks. Input data comes from 5' scRNA-seq technologies other than Chromium, which UniverSC does not support Data are already processed gene-by-barcode matrices and the goal is integration or clustering rather than raw count generation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate gene-by-barcode count (GBM) matrices from single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ data using UniverSC, a Cell Ranger-wrapping pipeline that supports any UMI-based platform (Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, SmartSeq2/3) with automatic chemistry determination and a single processing configuration across platforms. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Generate gene-by-barcode count (GBM) matrices from single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ data using UniverSC, a Cell Ranger-wrapping pipeline that supports any UMI-based platform (Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, SmartSeq2/3) with automatic chemistry determination and a single processing configuration across platforms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data comes from 5' scRNA-seq technologies other than Chromium, which UniverSC does not support Data are already processed gene-by-barcode matrices and the goal is integration or clustering rather than raw count generation

skills.description: Use when pooled scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq droplets have been labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides and you need to load HTO and RNA count matrices, derive per-droplet detected-gene totals, and check HTO-vs-gene correlations before demultiplexing.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when pooled scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq droplets have been labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides and you need to load HTO and RNA count matrices, derive per-droplet detected-gene totals, and check HTO-vs-gene correlations before demultiplexing. Input is already demultiplexed cell assignments or a demuxmix classification output rather than raw HTO/RNA count matrices The experiment uses no hashtag oligonucleotide labeling (e.g. genotype-based or lipid-tag demultiplexing), so no HTO count matrix exists to correlate with detected genes Only full transcription profiles (not count summaries) are available and per-droplet detected-gene totals cannot be computed for the regression covariate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Prepare (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrices and (genes x droplets) RNA count matrices from hashtag-oligonucleotide-labeled, pooled single-cell experiments, and compute per-droplet covariates such as the total number of detected genes so they can be passed to demuxmix regression mixture models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Prepare (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrices and (genes x droplets) RNA count matrices from hashtag-oligonucleotide-labeled, pooled single-cell experiments, and compute per-droplet covariates such as the total number of detected genes so they can be passed to demuxmix regression mixture models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already demultiplexed cell assignments or a demuxmix classification output rather than raw HTO/RNA count matrices The experiment uses no hashtag oligonucleotide labeling (e.g. genotype-based or lipid-tag demultiplexing), so no HTO count matrix exists to correlate with detected genes Only full transcription profiles (not count summaries) are available and per-droplet detected-gene totals cannot be computed for the regression covariate

skills.description: Use when raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices (cells in rows, genes in columns, CSV or similar) must be normalized and rescaled before scGATE inference, or when base GRN .parquet files need read_base_GRN() summarization.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices (cells in rows, genes in columns, CSV or similar) must be normalized and rescaled before scGATE inference, or when base GRN .parquet files need read_base_GRN() summarization. Data are already library-size normalized and rescaled — re-running normalization on pre-normalized deposits can distort values; set library_size_normalization = 'False' The goal is genome-wide large-scale GRN inference — scGATE preprocessing is designed for small (<200) gene subsets with a refined candidate TF list Input is pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocess single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. mouse haematopoiesis or Tabula Muris CSV counts) with scGATE's scRNA_seq_preprocessing(), performing library size normalization and rescaling into the (0,1) interval so downstream logic-gate inference receives suitable continuous input. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae180
skills.summary: Preprocess single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. mouse haematopoiesis or Tabula Muris CSV counts) with scGATE's scRNA_seq_preprocessing(), performing library size normalization and rescaling into the (0,1) interval so downstream logic-gate inference receives suitable continuous input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already library-size normalized and rescaled — re-running normalization on pre-normalized deposits can distort values; set library_size_normalization = 'False' The goal is genome-wide large-scale GRN inference — scGATE preprocessing is designed for small (<200) gene subsets with a refined candidate TF list Input is pseudotime-sorted single-cell data along differentiation trajectories — scGATE does not yet handle temporal ordering or delays

skills.description: Use when a raw single-cell gene expression count matrix must be preprocessed to remove an annotated unwanted signal (batch, cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, healthy-reference trajectory) before downstream analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when a raw single-cell gene expression count matrix must be preprocessed to remove an annotated unwanted signal (batch, cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, healthy-reference trajectory) before downstream analysis. When no prior knowledge is available to define a meaningful cell–cell similarity kernel — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal. When the downstream task requires properly log-transformed expression data, since SiFT modifies gene expression so the data are no longer properly log-transformed. When batch-effect correction at the level of a joint latent representation suffices (e.g., via scVI, Harmony, or bbknn), rather than correction at the gene expression level. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Kernel-based preprocessing of single-cell gene expression count matrices in which the counts are projected onto a cell–cell similarity kernel (P = K·X) and the projection is subtracted to filter an unwanted or known biological signal, with a pseudocount correction restoring a valid expression scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Kernel-based preprocessing of single-cell gene expression count matrices in which the counts are projected onto a cell–cell similarity kernel (P = K·X) and the projection is subtracted to filter an unwanted or known biological signal, with a pseudocount correction restoring a valid expression scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no prior knowledge is available to define a meaningful cell–cell similarity kernel — SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the kernel, and an inaccurate or coarse-grained mapping may lead to a loss of signal. When the downstream task requires properly log-transformed expression data, since SiFT modifies gene expression so the data are no longer properly log-transformed. When batch-effect correction at the level of a joint latent representation suffices (e.g., via scVI, Harmony, or bbknn), rather than correction at the gene expression level.

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNAseq count matrix must be pre-processed into standardized residuals prior to SVD/CA — e.g., to address overdispersion of counts instead of applying log(x+1) followed by PCA.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when a raw scRNAseq count matrix must be pre-processed into standardized residuals prior to SVD/CA — e.g., to address overdispersion of counts instead of applying log(x+1) followed by PCA. Input is already log-transformed 'logcounts' destined for PCA — this skill instead replaces that log(x+1) + PCA route with a residual-based CA pre-processing stage The goal is multi-table batch integration rather than single-table pre-processing — use corralm instead Input data are microarray or bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell count data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Transforms a scRNAseq count matrix into a chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman–Tukey, optionally with square-root/Anscombe/Freeman–Tukey variance-stabilizing transforms and sign-preserving power deflation α) as the pre-processing stage before CA-based dimension reduction, replacing the distortive log(x+1) transform. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Transforms a scRNAseq count matrix into a chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman–Tukey, optionally with square-root/Anscombe/Freeman–Tukey variance-stabilizing transforms and sign-preserving power deflation α) as the pre-processing stage before CA-based dimension reduction, replacing the distortive log(x+1) transform.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already log-transformed 'logcounts' destined for PCA — this skill instead replaces that log(x+1) + PCA route with a residual-based CA pre-processing stage The goal is multi-table batch integration rather than single-table pre-processing — use corralm instead Input data are microarray or bulk RNA-seq rather than single-cell count data

skills.description: Use when raw per-individual UMI count matrices from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq need gene filtering, top-1000 HVG selection, and marker-based approximated ground-truth cell-type labels before clustering benchmarking.
skills.name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing Use when raw per-individual UMI count matrices from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq need gene filtering, top-1000 HVG selection, and marker-based approximated ground-truth cell-type labels before clustering benchmarking. skills.summary: Standardizes single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., MCalla et al. and Yan E-GEOD-36552 hESC/mESC datasets) so that multiple gene network inference methods — scPRINT, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer v2, GENIE3 — can be benchmarked against the same ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold standards with method-appropriate normalization per method.

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth scRNA-seq count data with known celltype labels and an applied dropout model to quantify whether a denoiser (DCA vs. an MSE autoencoder) recovers the true cell structure.

skills.search_text: single-cell-count-simulation Use when you need ground-truth scRNA-seq count data with known celltype labels and an applied dropout model to quantify whether a denoiser (DCA vs. an MSE autoencoder) recovers the true cell structure. Real scRNA-seq data where the true expression state (ground truth) is unknown — the article notes 'evaluation of denoising is difficult because the definition of a ground truth can be challenging for real data'. Benchmarks requiring hyperparameter-optimized denoisers — the authors state hyperparameters were not fine-tuned for any of the manuscript analyses, so default settings are the reproducible baseline, not a tuned configuration. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking skill that generates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with controlled dropout (e.g. two-group and six-group Splatter simulations of 200 genes x 2000 cells) so that denoisers such as DCA can be evaluated against a known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill that generates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with controlled dropout (e.g. two-group and six-group Splatter simulations of 200 genes x 2000 cells) so that denoisers such as DCA can be evaluated against a known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scRNA-seq data where the true expression state (ground truth) is unknown — the article notes 'evaluation of denoising is difficult because the definition of a ground truth can be challenging for real data'. Benchmarks requiring hyperparameter-optimized denoisers — the authors state hyperparameters were not fine-tuned for any of the manuscript analyses, so default settings are the reproducible baseline, not a tuned configuration.

skills.search_text: single-cell-crispr-screening-perturbation-ranking Use when you need to validate that a single-cell CRISPR screening pipeline's perturbation-effect ranking (e.g., MUSIC's Rank_overall) is stable under control-cell label noise, or to reproduce the reported robustness figures before trusting downstream ranking-driven conclusions. skills.summary: A robustness test for MUSIC's overall perturbation effect rankings: randomly relabel a fraction (e.g., 20%) of control cells as a held-out test perturbation, re-rank perturbations with Rank_overall, and quantify ranking stability via disturbance rate and Pearson correlation across repeated random relabelings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want an absolute perturbation-effect estimate or functional topic annotation, not a stability/reproducibility check on existing rankings Your dataset lacks a blank-control cell population (no 'CTRL' label), since the test relabels control cells as a held-out group Perturbations fall below MUSIC's minimal cell threshold (fewer than 30 perturbed cells), which MUSIC excludes from analysis anyway
