skills.search_text: single-cell-dataset-alignment Use when multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets must be combined to learn a hierarchical classification tree, and batch effects are expected between the datasets (e.g., different PBMC studies measured on different platforms). When only a single dataset is analyzed and no cross-dataset population matching is needed When the goal is batch correction itself rather than preprocessing for hierarchical classifier training — scHPL (and this alignment step as framed here) is not a batch correction tool When datasets cannot be assumed to share cell populations or a roughly consistent annotation terminology across studies http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align multiple annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets into a shared feature space before hierarchical classifier training, because scHPL is not a batch correction tool and requires batch-effect-corrected inputs for reliable cell population matching across datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Align multiple annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets into a shared feature space before hierarchical classifier training, because scHPL is not a batch correction tool and requires batch-effect-corrected inputs for reliable cell population matching across datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single dataset is analyzed and no cross-dataset population matching is needed When the goal is batch correction itself rather than preprocessing for hierarchical classifier training — scHPL (and this alignment step as framed here) is not a batch correction tool When datasets cannot be assumed to share cell populations or a roughly consistent annotation terminology across studies

skills.description: Use when a cell can belong to multiple inferred trajectories and you need to quantify whether its inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths, benchmarked per dataset.
skills.name: single-cell-dataset-benchmark-table-construction
skills.search_text: single-cell-dataset-benchmark-table-construction Use when a cell can belong to multiple inferred trajectories and you need to quantify whether its inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths, benchmarked per dataset. Cells assigned to only a single trajectory path — Diffpst is undefined since it requires deviation across multiple assigned paths Trajectory outputs from methods that do not emit per-path cell pseudotime and branching assignments (e.g., Directed-PAGA infers only cluster-level trajectories) Datasets not processed through CellPath, where percentile pseudotime positions per path cannot be extracted from cellpath_obj.pseudo_order http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify per-dataset pseudotime consistency for cells assigned to multiple CellPath trajectories by computing Diffpst (mean absolute deviation of within-path percentile pseudotime positions), binning deviations into four categories, and tabulating per-dataset proportions (e.g., forebrain ~10.2% in the large-deviation bin, Figure S4G). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Quantify per-dataset pseudotime consistency for cells assigned to multiple CellPath trajectories by computing Diffpst (mean absolute deviation of within-path percentile pseudotime positions), binning deviations into four categories, and tabulating per-dataset proportions (e.g., forebrain ~10.2% in the large-deviation bin, Figure S4G).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells assigned to only a single trajectory path — Diffpst is undefined since it requires deviation across multiple assigned paths Trajectory outputs from methods that do not emit per-path cell pseudotime and branching assignments (e.g., Directed-PAGA infers only cluster-level trajectories) Datasets not processed through CellPath, where percentile pseudotime positions per path cannot be extracted from cellpath_obj.pseudo_order

skills.description: Use when benchmarking the scalability of a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g. Symphony/Harmony) and you need matched downsampled expression/metadata subsets at multiple cell counts as controlled inputs.
skills.name: single-cell-dataset-downsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-dataset-downsampling Use when benchmarking the scalability of a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g. Symphony/Harmony) and you need matched downsampled expression/metadata subsets at multiple cell counts as controlled inputs. When the analysis goal is discovery of novel cell types in the query — downsampling to fit a reference benchmark discards cells and Symphony itself does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone When evaluating mapping accuracy rather than runtime — downsampled subsets may no longer cover all reference cell types, violating Symphony's Condition I requiring comprehensive cell type coverage http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Systematically subset a single-cell expression matrix and its cell metadata to a ladder of cell counts (e.g. 20K–500K reference cells; 1K–100K query cells) so that runtime and scalability of reference-building vs. query-mapping pipelines can be measured on comparable inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Systematically subset a single-cell expression matrix and its cell metadata to a ladder of cell counts (e.g. 20K–500K reference cells; 1K–100K query cells) so that runtime and scalability of reference-building vs. query-mapping pipelines can be measured on comparable inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is discovery of novel cell types in the query — downsampling to fit a reference benchmark discards cells and Symphony itself does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone When evaluating mapping accuracy rather than runtime — downsampled subsets may no longer cover all reference cell types, violating Symphony's Condition I requiring comprehensive cell type coverage

skills.description: Use when a single-cell count matrix needs a biologically interpretable, cell-type-separating embedding: e.g., the MCA dataset must be embedded via the 137 marker GEPs and benchmarked against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA using Davies-Bouldin and Calinski-Harabasz scores.
skills.name: single-cell-dataset-label-matching
skills.search_text: single-cell-dataset-label-matching Use when a single-cell count matrix needs a biologically interpretable, cell-type-separating embedding: e.g., the MCA dataset must be embedded via the 137 marker GEPs and benchmarked against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA using Davies-Bouldin and Calinski-Harabasz scores. The input is already an embedding or feature-reduced table rather than a raw gene count matrix — average_by_gep expects a gene count matrix with gene names as row names. Gene identifiers of the dataset do not match the GEP table format (e.g., Ensembl IDs when only the symbol-version GEP file is available, or vice versa), since gene-name matching is required for averaging. The goal is discovering novel cell-type structure rather than matching cells to the known GEP/cell-type vocabulary of the reference dataset; the article notes that label transfer is constrained by the cell-type coverage of the source dataset, leaving uncovered cells annotated as 'unknown'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reduces single-cell transcriptome dimensionality by averaging gene expression over marker gene expression programs (GEPs) — e.g., the 137 MCA GEPs identified by SingleCellGGM — so cell-type identity is directly encoded in the embedding, enabling comparison and label matching across datasets against methods like PCA, scDHA, and scMGCA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100813
skills.summary: Reduces single-cell transcriptome dimensionality by averaging gene expression over marker gene expression programs (GEPs) — e.g., the 137 MCA GEPs identified by SingleCellGGM — so cell-type identity is directly encoded in the embedding, enabling comparison and label matching across datasets against methods like PCA, scDHA, and scMGCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an embedding or feature-reduced table rather than a raw gene count matrix — average_by_gep expects a gene count matrix with gene names as row names. Gene identifiers of the dataset do not match the GEP table format (e.g., Ensembl IDs when only the symbol-version GEP file is available, or vice versa), since gene-name matching is required for averaging. The goal is discovering novel cell-type structure rather than matching cells to the known GEP/cell-type vocabulary of the reference dataset; the article notes that label transfer is constrained by the cell-type coverage of the source dataset, leaving uncovered cells annotated as 'unknown'.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking execution time of single-cell methods across growing sample sizes: subset a raw cell-by-gene count matrix at fixed increments and record single-core wall-clock time and failures per method per size.
skills.name: single-cell-dataset-subset-sampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-dataset-subset-sampling Use when benchmarking execution time of single-cell methods across growing sample sizes: subset a raw cell-by-gene count matrix at fixed increments and record single-core wall-clock time and failures per method per size. The goal is rare-cell detection accuracy on a single fixed dataset, not runtime scaling — use FiRE scoring directly with IQR thresholding (th = q3 + 1.5*iqr) instead of subsetting The dataset is small (hundreds to ~1k cells) where scaling differences between methods are not meaningful Input is already a per-method runtime table and only needs comparison, not re-subsetting of raw data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs nested cell-count subsets (1k, 5k, 10k, ... up to full ~68k profiles) from a scRNA-seq expression matrix and times each method on every subset to produce a runtime-scaling comparison table. Used to quantify how algorithms like FiRE, LOF, RaceID and GiniClust scale with sample size. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Constructs nested cell-count subsets (1k, 5k, 10k, ... up to full ~68k profiles) from a scRNA-seq expression matrix and times each method on every subset to produce a runtime-scaling comparison table. Used to quantify how algorithms like FiRE, LOF, RaceID and GiniClust scale with sample size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is rare-cell detection accuracy on a single fixed dataset, not runtime scaling — use FiRE scoring directly with IQR thresholding (th = q3 + 1.5*iqr) instead of subsetting The dataset is small (hundreds to ~1k cells) where scaling differences between methods are not meaningful Input is already a per-method runtime table and only needs comparison, not re-subsetting of raw data

skills.description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare DEG prediction methods on single-cell RNA-seq data with known ground truth — i.e., artificial datasets with planted DEGs where AUC and elapsed runtime per method per dataset size can be tabulated.
skills.name: single-cell-deg-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-deg-method-benchmarking Use when you need to quantitatively compare DEG prediction methods on single-cell RNA-seq data with known ground truth — i.e., artificial datasets with planted DEGs where AUC and elapsed runtime per method per dataset size can be tabulated. The dataset is real data without known ground-truth DEGs — AUC against planted labels cannot be computed, so this benchmarking design does not apply. The goal is spatial DEG discovery on actual tissue coordinates (e.g., 10x Genomics Visium) rather than method comparison on artificial benchmarks. Gene expression is only available as continuous normalized counts and cannot be binarized into detection data, since singleCellHaystack requires binary detection input. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark the accuracy (AUC of DEG detection ROC via ROCR) and runtime of singleCellHaystack against DEsingle, EMDomics, scDD, edgeR, monocle 2, and Seurat FindAllMarkers on artificial scRNA-seq datasets with planted DEGs, reproducing the Vandenbon & Diez benchmark table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: Benchmark the accuracy (AUC of DEG detection ROC via ROCR) and runtime of singleCellHaystack against DEsingle, EMDomics, scDD, edgeR, monocle 2, and Seurat FindAllMarkers on artificial scRNA-seq datasets with planted DEGs, reproducing the Vandenbon & Diez benchmark table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is real data without known ground-truth DEGs — AUC against planted labels cannot be computed, so this benchmarking design does not apply. The goal is spatial DEG discovery on actual tissue coordinates (e.g., 10x Genomics Visium) rather than method comparison on artificial benchmarks. Gene expression is only available as continuous normalized counts and cannot be binarized into detection data, since singleCellHaystack requires binary detection input.

skills.description: Use when preparing an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix plus per-droplet detected-gene counts for regression mixture model demultiplexing, and initial class labels or outlier flags are needed before model fitting.
skills.name: single-cell-demultiplexing-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-demultiplexing-preprocessing Use when preparing an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix plus per-droplet detected-gene counts for regression mixture model demultiplexing, and initial class labels or outlier flags are needed before model fitting. Input lacks an HTO count matrix (e.g. only gene-by-droplet RNA counts), so no per-HTO labeling exists to cluster Goal is the final probabilistic demultiplexing/classification itself rather than initialization and QC of its inputs Droplets have already been classified and the task is to discard uncertain assignments using error probabilities http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocessing step for HTO-based demultiplexing as implemented in demuxmix: per-HTO k-means (k = 2) clustering of log-transformed HTO counts to obtain initial positive/negative class labels, plus Q3 + 1.5*IQR outlier flagging on HTO counts and detected genes to exclude noisy droplets from model fitting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Preprocessing step for HTO-based demultiplexing as implemented in demuxmix: per-HTO k-means (k = 2) clustering of log-transformed HTO counts to obtain initial positive/negative class labels, plus Q3 + 1.5*IQR outlier flagging on HTO counts and detected genes to exclude noisy droplets from model fitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks an HTO count matrix (e.g. only gene-by-droplet RNA counts), so no per-HTO labeling exists to cluster Goal is the final probabilistic demultiplexing/classification itself rather than initialization and QC of its inputs Droplets have already been classified and the task is to discard uncertain assignments using error probabilities

skills.description: Use when a sparse single-cell expression matrix with known cell-phenotype labels (e.g., 95% sparse PBMC or mouse cortex data) must be denoised and you need to verify whether RMT feature selection outperforms MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI, DCA, Seurat, or HVG baselines.
skills.name: single-cell-denoising-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-denoising-method-benchmarking Use when a sparse single-cell expression matrix with known cell-phenotype labels (e.g., 95% sparse PBMC or mouse cortex data) must be denoised and you need to verify whether RMT feature selection outperforms MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI, DCA, Seurat, or HVG baselines. Input is bulk RNA-seq or already a denoised/imputed feature table — the RMT decomposition assumes a highly sparse raw single-cell matrix (about 95% sparsity) as noise plus low-rank signal No ground-truth phenotype labels or known cell populations exist, since the benchmark is scored by silhouette of marked phenotypes rather than intrinsic metrics Only one denoising method is of interest without comparison baselines — the skill is a comparative benchmark across at least the RMT, imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning families http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark the RMT-based denoising pipeline (Randomly) against imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning baselines on sparse single-cell expression matrices by measuring mean silhouette scores of known phenotype clusters across latent-space dimensions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100035
skills.summary: Benchmark the RMT-based denoising pipeline (Randomly) against imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning baselines on sparse single-cell expression matrices by measuring mean silhouette scores of known phenotype clusters across latent-space dimensions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or already a denoised/imputed feature table — the RMT decomposition assumes a highly sparse raw single-cell matrix (about 95% sparsity) as noise plus low-rank signal No ground-truth phenotype labels or known cell populations exist, since the benchmark is scored by silhouette of marked phenotypes rather than intrinsic metrics Only one denoising method is of interest without comparison baselines — the skill is a comparative benchmark across at least the RMT, imputation, zero-inflated, and deep-learning families

skills.description: Use when filtering ligand-receptor pairs in single-cell expression data so a gene counts as 'expressed' in a cell type only if detected in more than 20% of its cells (NATMI --detectionThreshold default 0.2).
skills.name: single-cell-detection-rate-thresholding
skills.search_text: single-cell-detection-rate-thresholding Use when filtering ligand-receptor pairs in single-cell expression data so a gene counts as 'expressed' in a cell type only if detected in more than 20% of its cells (NATMI --detectionThreshold default 0.2). Input is bulk expression or proteomic data where per-cell detection rates cannot be computed Data are not normalised to counts per million (raw counts would make the 10 CPM expressionThreshold meaningless) Analysis requires modelling heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model them, so pair-level thresholding is insufficient http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Defines ligand/receptor 'expression' in a cell type for NATMI by requiring detection (non-zero counts) in >20% of that cell type's cells, optionally combined with an expression-level threshold of 10 CPM, before predicting cell-to-cell communication edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Defines ligand/receptor 'expression' in a cell type for NATMI by requiring detection (non-zero counts) in >20% of that cell type's cells, optionally combined with an expression-level threshold of 10 CPM, before predicting cell-to-cell communication edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk expression or proteomic data where per-cell detection rates cannot be computed Data are not normalised to counts per million (raw counts would make the 10 CPM expressionThreshold meaningless) Analysis requires modelling heteromeric complexes — NATMI does not model them, so pair-level thresholding is insufficient

skills.description: Use when you have unpaired single-cell modality pairs (e.g. scRNA-scATAC, scRNA-protein, scRNA-smFISH, scRNA-morphology) from the same biological condition and need a shared cell embedding without converting features across modalities.
skills.name: single-cell-diagonal-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-diagonal-integration Use when you have unpaired single-cell modality pairs (e.g. scRNA-scATAC, scRNA-protein, scRNA-smFISH, scRNA-morphology) from the same biological condition and need a shared cell embedding without converting features across modalities. No cross-modality feature connections are available for the modality pair — the paper notes scConfluence 'relies on connections between features of different modalities... as for example when integrating electrophysiology measurements with gene expression' Data are paired multimodal measurements of the same cells; the paper states integration of paired with unpaired multimodal data 'is not yet addressed by scConfluence' The primary goal involves very rare cell populations, since rare populations are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches and this remains challenging for scConfluence and all state-of-the-art methods http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Integrates unpaired single-cell multimodal data (diagonal integration) using scConfluence, which combines uncoupled autoencoders with regularized Inverse Optimal Transport (rIOT) on weakly connected features to learn a shared low-dimensional latent space across modalities such as scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, surface protein, smFISH, and neuronal morphology images. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Integrates unpaired single-cell multimodal data (diagonal integration) using scConfluence, which combines uncoupled autoencoders with regularized Inverse Optimal Transport (rIOT) on weakly connected features to learn a shared low-dimensional latent space across modalities such as scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, surface protein, smFISH, and neuronal morphology images.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cross-modality feature connections are available for the modality pair — the paper notes scConfluence 'relies on connections between features of different modalities... as for example when integrating electrophysiology measurements with gene expression' Data are paired multimodal measurements of the same cells; the paper states integration of paired with unpaired multimodal data 'is not yet addressed by scConfluence' The primary goal involves very rare cell populations, since rare populations are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches and this remains challenging for scConfluence and all state-of-the-art methods

skills.description: Use when two annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets processed in SingCellaR (e.g., eFL and FL HSPC objects with existing UMAP embeddings and cell-type labels) must be compared for cell-subpopulation abundance shifts, and per-cell DA scores plus a DA UMAP figure are the desired outputs.
skills.name: single-cell-differential-abundance-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-abundance-analysis Use when two annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets processed in SingCellaR (e.g., eFL and FL HSPC objects with existing UMAP embeddings and cell-type labels) must be compared for cell-subpopulation abundance shifts, and per-cell DA scores plus a DA UMAP figure are the desired outputs. The datasets have not been clustered, annotated, and embedded (no UMAP) in SingCellaR — run the upstream clustering/annotation workflow first. The goal is differential gene expression rather than differential cell-subpopulation abundance — use identifyDifferentialGenes directly instead. More than two conditions must be compared simultaneously — this skill covers a pairwise two-object comparison (e.g., eFL vs FL). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Performs pairwise differential abundance (DAseq) testing between two processed SingCellaR objects (e.g., early fetal liver vs fetal liver HSPCs), computes DA log2FC scores per subpopulation, projects them onto the UMAP embedding, and renders a labeled DA UMAP figure (eFL_vs_FL.pdf). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Performs pairwise differential abundance (DAseq) testing between two processed SingCellaR objects (e.g., early fetal liver vs fetal liver HSPCs), computes DA log2FC scores per subpopulation, projects them onto the UMAP embedding, and renders a labeled DA UMAP figure (eFL_vs_FL.pdf).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The datasets have not been clustered, annotated, and embedded (no UMAP) in SingCellaR — run the upstream clustering/annotation workflow first. The goal is differential gene expression rather than differential cell-subpopulation abundance — use identifyDifferentialGenes directly instead. More than two conditions must be compared simultaneously — this skill covers a pairwise two-object comparison (e.g., eFL vs FL).

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or trajectory data in h5ad/Seurat form with an embedding or coordinate space (PCA, pseudotime, 1D-3D spatial) and need clustering-independent detection of features with non-random activity patterns.
skills.name: single-cell-differential-activity-prediction
skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-activity-prediction Use when you have scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or trajectory data in h5ad/Seurat form with an embedding or coordinate space (PCA, pseudotime, 1D-3D spatial) and need clustering-independent detection of features with non-random activity patterns. Comparing multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' and multi-condition methods are future work Analyses that need DEG results integrated into a cluster-oriented scRNA-seq workflow — results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' compared to cluster-based approaches Spatial transcriptomics where runtime is the overriding constraint — SPARK-X is faster, though singleCellHaystack offers better sensitivity http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Predict differentially active features (DEGs, spatial DEGs, accessible chromatin, pathway activities) in single-cell or spatial genomics data using singleCellHaystack v1.0+, which models continuous activity levels with cross-validated splines and Kullback-Leibler divergence instead of cluster comparisons or hard binary detection thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Predict differentially active features (DEGs, spatial DEGs, accessible chromatin, pathway activities) in single-cell or spatial genomics data using singleCellHaystack v1.0+, which models continuous activity levels with cross-validated splines and Kullback-Leibler divergence instead of cluster comparisons or hard binary detection thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Comparing multiple conditions (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' and multi-condition methods are future work Analyses that need DEG results integrated into a cluster-oriented scRNA-seq workflow — results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' compared to cluster-based approaches Spatial transcriptomics where runtime is the overriding constraint — SPARK-X is faster, though singleCellHaystack offers better sensitivity

skills.description: Use when you have partitioned droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into cell-calling groups (e.g. All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, EmptyNN-removed) and need to test whether a cell-caller's retained barcodes are transcriptionally similar to confirmed cells.
skills.name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis Use when you have partitioned droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into cell-calling groups (e.g. All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, EmptyNN-removed) and need to test whether a cell-caller's retained barcodes are transcriptionally similar to confirmed cells. Input is already filtered/normalized expression (e.g. a Seurat object with a subset of cells) — the contrasts require the raw unfiltered matrix so barcodes below the 200-count threshold can be partitioned Goal is cell-type annotation of recovered clusters via marker genes rather than validating cell-calling agreement between barcode groups — the downsampling design here is specific to comparing EmptyNN-retained vs EmptyNN-removed groups No cell-calling labels (e.g. nn.keep vector) exist for the barcodes, so the three group partition cannot be constructed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Differential expression analysis in Seurat comparing barcodes retained by a cell-calling method (All-retained) against barcodes removed (EmptyNN-removed) or specifically recovered (EmptyNN-retained), after downsampling UMI counts and cells to remove group-size and depth bias, to validate that recovered barcodes resemble genuine cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Differential expression analysis in Seurat comparing barcodes retained by a cell-calling method (All-retained) against barcodes removed (EmptyNN-removed) or specifically recovered (EmptyNN-retained), after downsampling UMI counts and cells to remove group-size and depth bias, to validate that recovered barcodes resemble genuine cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already filtered/normalized expression (e.g. a Seurat object with a subset of cells) — the contrasts require the raw unfiltered matrix so barcodes below the 200-count threshold can be partitioned Goal is cell-type annotation of recovered clusters via marker genes rather than validating cell-calling agreement between barcode groups — the downsampling design here is specific to comparing EmptyNN-retained vs EmptyNN-removed groups No cell-calling labels (e.g. nn.keep vector) exist for the barcodes, so the three group partition cannot be constructed

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been partitioned by a binary event (e.g., presence/absence of a fusion such as TMPRSS2-ERG) and you must test association with treatment or differential gene expression to quantify the fusion's transcriptional impact per cell.
skills.name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis Use when scRNA-seq cells have been partitioned by a binary event (e.g., presence/absence of a fusion such as TMPRSS2-ERG) and you must test association with treatment or differential gene expression to quantify the fusion's transcriptional impact per cell. Data are bulk RNA-seq or droplet 10X data — scFusion and its per-cell grouping are built for Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ (*_1.fastq, *_2.fastq), not 10X or *_1.fq files No per-cell binary grouping exists (no fusion calls or treatment labels), so a 2x2 contingency/Fisher test framework cannot be defined Fusion is rare and the tumor is highly heterogeneous — detection power is limited and group sizes are too small for reliable testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistical comparison of gene expression between subpopulations of single cells — here, ERG expression in TMPRSS2-ERG fusion-positive vs fusion-negative prostate epithelial cells from a 922-cell scRNA-seq patient dataset — to quantify the transcriptional impact of a fusion at single-cell resolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Statistical comparison of gene expression between subpopulations of single cells — here, ERG expression in TMPRSS2-ERG fusion-positive vs fusion-negative prostate epithelial cells from a 922-cell scRNA-seq patient dataset — to quantify the transcriptional impact of a fusion at single-cell resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq or droplet 10X data — scFusion and its per-cell grouping are built for Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ (*_1.fastq, *_2.fastq), not 10X or *_1.fq files No per-cell binary grouping exists (no fusion calls or treatment labels), so a 2x2 contingency/Fisher test framework cannot be defined Fusion is rare and the tumor is highly heterogeneous — detection power is limited and group sizes are too small for reliable testing

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data or DE summary statistics (per-gene beta coefficient and variance) are available and gene-level differential expression calls between cell types or conditions are needed, especially when power or cross-method consistency is a concern.
skills.name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis Use when scRNA-seq count data or DE summary statistics (per-gene beta coefficient and variance) are available and gene-level differential expression calls between cell types or conditions are needed, especially when power or cross-method consistency is a concern. When the analysis goal is gene set enrichment rather than gene-level DE calls — use iDEA's GSE branch (iDEA.louis / iDEA.FDR) or fGSEA/GSEA/CAMERA instead When only individual-level scRNA-seq counts with no DE tool output exist and you need an off-the-shelf per-gene test without summarizing to beta/beta_var statistics for joint modeling When DE is performed on inferred cell types whose uncertainty must be propagated — the article notes this can yield inflated DE test statistics with artificially smaller standard errors http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Perform differential expression (DE) analysis on scRNA-seq data with MAST, SCDE, zingeR/zingeR-DESeq2, or edgeR with ZINB-WaVE weights, then optionally augment the per-gene evidence with iDEA's BMA aggregation to gain power by borrowing information across genes. This skill covers running the standalone DE tools, converting their outputs (beta and beta_var summary statistics) to iDEA input, and evaluating power/consistency of the resulting DE gene lists. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Perform differential expression (DE) analysis on scRNA-seq data with MAST, SCDE, zingeR/zingeR-DESeq2, or edgeR with ZINB-WaVE weights, then optionally augment the per-gene evidence with iDEA's BMA aggregation to gain power by borrowing information across genes. This skill covers running the standalone DE tools, converting their outputs (beta and beta_var summary statistics) to iDEA input, and evaluating power/consistency of the resulting DE gene lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is gene set enrichment rather than gene-level DE calls — use iDEA's GSE branch (iDEA.louis / iDEA.FDR) or fGSEA/GSEA/CAMERA instead When only individual-level scRNA-seq counts with no DE tool output exist and you need an off-the-shelf per-gene test without summarizing to beta/beta_var statistics for joint modeling When DE is performed on inferred cell types whose uncertainty must be propagated — the article notes this can yield inflated DE test statistics with artificially smaller standard errors

skills.search_text: single-cell-differential-expression-testing Use when you have a gene-by-cell expression matrix with cell type/cluster assignments and need to identify cell type-specific DE genes or TFs (e.g., Welch's t test p < 0.05) to feed signature or regulatory-network analysis. Cell types or clusters have not yet been defined — SINCERA requires cell type identification before DE testing, since specificity is computed per cell type against all others. Genes are non- or low-expressed and have not passed prefiltering (prefilterGenes / expr.minimum), so t tests would be run on mostly-zero profiles. The goal is differential expression between two predefined biological conditions rather than cell type specificity within one scRNA-seq dataset — a two-condition DE tool is more appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Test each gene's expression in one cell type against all other cells in a scRNA-seq dataset to flag cell type-specific differentially expressed genes and transcription factors (one-tailed Welch's t test, p < 0.05), as implemented in the SINCERA pipeline and echoed by dedicated scRNA-seq DE tools such as SAMstrt and SCDE. The resulting DE calls are the raw material for cell type-specific signature and driving-force analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Test each gene's expression in one cell type against all other cells in a scRNA-seq dataset to flag cell type-specific differentially expressed genes and transcription factors (one-tailed Welch's t test, p < 0.05), as implemented in the SINCERA pipeline and echoed by dedicated scRNA-seq DE tools such as SAMstrt and SCDE. The resulting DE calls are the raw material for cell type-specific signature and driving-force analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell types or clusters have not yet been defined — SINCERA requires cell type identification before DE testing, since specificity is computed per cell type against all others. Genes are non- or low-expressed and have not passed prefiltering (prefilterGenes / expr.minimum), so t tests would be run on mostly-zero profiles. The goal is differential expression between two predefined biological conditions rather than cell type specificity within one scRNA-seq dataset — a two-condition DE tool is more appropriate.

skills.search_text: single-cell-dimension-reduction Use when you have a temporal scRNA-seq gene-by-cell count matrix with a cell-by-time-point binary time table and need a 2D visualization that preserves developmental trajectories and resolves intra-time-point subpopulations. skills.summary: Reduces temporal single-cell expression count matrices to a 2D latent space using TCM (Topographic Cell Map), which preserves global developmental trajectories over time points while separating subpopulations within each time point, benchmarked against t-SNE, diffusion map, diffusion pseudotime, Wishbone, Monocle and TSCAN via percent of non-temporal variance explained.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq dataset lacks a complete time index, or the time index is not correlated with the underlying dynamic expression pattern The data are not temporal single-cell expression data and no time.table exists (e.g. a feature table or bulk omics matrix) You need immediate biological interpretation of cell clusters on the latent space — TCM requires further pathway analysis to elucidate the meaning of each trajectory

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (wide format, e.g. tens of thousands to millions of cells from 10x Genomics data) exceeds single-machine memory and you need Spark-native PCA cell embeddings compatible with downstream Parquet-based UMAP/t-SNE steps.
skills.name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction Use when a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (wide format, e.g. tens of thousands to millions of cells from 10x Genomics data) exceeds single-machine memory and you need Spark-native PCA cell embeddings compatible with downstream Parquet-based UMAP/t-SNE steps. Input is raw count data that has not passed scSPARKL QC/filtering (e.g. cells expressing < 10 genes, percent_mito > 5% not yet removed) and normalization — PCA here expects the normalized wide-format matrix Dataset fits comfortably in single-machine memory and you need a UMAP/t-SNE embedding instead — those steps in scSPARKL run as Python outside Spark, not via the Spark PCA routine You need a biologically benchmarked reduction validated against Seurat/Scanpy — the paper explicitly acknowledges 'No benchmarking against Seurat and Scanpy performed' http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 Distributed PCA-based dimensionality reduction for scRNA-seq data using scSPARKL, implemented exclusively in Spark MLlib so it scales beyond single-machine RAM on normalized wide-format expression matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: Distributed PCA-based dimensionality reduction for scRNA-seq data using scSPARKL, implemented exclusively in Spark MLlib so it scales beyond single-machine RAM on normalized wide-format expression matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count data that has not passed scSPARKL QC/filtering (e.g. cells expressing < 10 genes, percent_mito > 5% not yet removed) and normalization — PCA here expects the normalized wide-format matrix Dataset fits comfortably in single-machine memory and you need a UMAP/t-SNE embedding instead — those steps in scSPARKL run as Python outside Spark, not via the Spark PCA routine You need a biologically benchmarked reduction validated against Seurat/Scanpy — the paper explicitly acknowledges 'No benchmarking against Seurat and Scanpy performed'

skills.description: Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers, scRNA-seq PCs) come with a priori class labels such as cell type, cell-cycle phase, or experimental time point, and the goal is a supervised visualization whose axes separate those labels.
skills.name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers, scRNA-seq PCs) come with a priori class labels such as cell type, cell-cycle phase, or experimental time point, and the goal is a supervised visualization whose axes separate those labels. Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the approach is supervised and inappropriate in those situations. Data have more than ~100 dimensions and HSS feature selection is required (HSS is not feasible >100 dimensions); use LDA/sda on PCs instead. A large degree of heterogeneity exists within a given class (e.g., PBMCs labeled by time point) or the number of populations is very large — performance suffers. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Supervised dimensionality reduction of single-cell data using linear discriminant analysis (LDA) with feature selection by hybrid subset selection (HSS), implemented in the R package hsslda, to generate non-stochastic, interpretable axes that optimally separate a priori class labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Supervised dimensionality reduction of single-cell data using linear discriminant analysis (LDA) with feature selection by hybrid subset selection (HSS), implemented in the R package hsslda, to generate non-stochastic, interpretable axes that optimally separate a priori class labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the approach is supervised and inappropriate in those situations. Data have more than ~100 dimensions and HSS feature selection is required (HSS is not feasible >100 dimensions); use LDA/sda on PCs instead. A large degree of heterogeneity exists within a given class (e.g., PBMCs labeled by time point) or the number of populations is very large — performance suffers.

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., ZF1_F3_DrImpute) must be converted into cluster labels and state lineages that downstream lineage-tree methods like LinRace NJ_asym_Dif require as inputs.
skills.name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-and-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-and-clustering Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., ZF1_F3_DrImpute) must be converted into cluster labels and state lineages that downstream lineage-tree methods like LinRace NJ_asym_Dif require as inputs. Input is already a cluster label vector or state lineage set rather than a raw count/expression matrix — the reduction and clustering step is redundant. The system has synchronous, fast differentiation so ancestral cell states are absent from the current-day scRNA-seq data; k-means states would not capture intermediates. Data quality is too low (sparse lineage barcodes / poor expression coverage), as LinRace assumes high-diversity, high-coverage barcodes for reliable state assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Preprocesses paired single-cell gene expression data (e.g., zebrafish scGESTALT ZF1_F3_DrImpute counts) by scaling, PCA to 50 PCs, k-means clustering into 20 cell states, UMAP embedding (min_dist = 0.3), and Slingshot trajectory inference to derive state lineages used by LinRace. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Preprocesses paired single-cell gene expression data (e.g., zebrafish scGESTALT ZF1_F3_DrImpute counts) by scaling, PCA to 50 PCs, k-means clustering into 20 cell states, UMAP embedding (min_dist = 0.3), and Slingshot trajectory inference to derive state lineages used by LinRace.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cluster label vector or state lineage set rather than a raw count/expression matrix — the reduction and clustering step is redundant. The system has synchronous, fast differentiation so ancestral cell states are absent from the current-day scRNA-seq data; k-means states would not capture intermediates. Data quality is too low (sparse lineage barcodes / poor expression coverage), as LinRace assumes high-diversity, high-coverage barcodes for reliable state assignment.

skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking Use when assessing whether a dimensionality-reduction method can handle a million-plus-cell scRNA-seq dataset within practical runtime, by timing ivis against Barnes-Hut t-SNE with a 24-hour timeout. The dataset is small or moderate in size (e.g. the 4,645 x 23,686 Melanoma SCP11 dataset or the 70,000-observation MNIST dataset), where t-SNE finishes well within the timeout and a runtime-scaling benchmark is uninformative The goal is accuracy/structure-preservation comparison (e.g. Mantel-test PCC or SVM-classifier accuracy on subsamples) rather than runtime scalability http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmarking skill for comparing the runtime and scalability of the ivis siamese-network dimensionality-reduction algorithm against scikit-learn's Barnes-Hut t-SNE on very large single-cell datasets (e.g. the 1.3-million-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain scRNA-seq matrix), demonstrating ivis's linear scaling to millions of observations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-45301-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small or moderate in size (e.g. the 4,645 x 23,686 Melanoma SCP11 dataset or the 70,000-observation MNIST dataset), where t-SNE finishes well within the timeout and a runtime-scaling benchmark is uninformative The goal is accuracy/structure-preservation comparison (e.g. Mantel-test PCC or SVM-classifier accuracy on subsamples) rather than runtime scalability

skills.description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the Ind4 breast epithelium sample from GEO GSE113197, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be projected to low-dimensional space (PCA, then UMAP) before graph-based clustering and marker-based cell annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-embedding
skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-embedding Use when a QC-filtered, normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the Ind4 breast epithelium sample from GEO GSE113197, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be projected to low-dimensional space (PCA, then UMAP) before graph-based clustering and marker-based cell annotation. The input is already an embedding or trajectory result rather than a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix — re-embedding would double-reduce the data. The goal is computing differentiation activity scores with ORIGINS activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges), which consumes the expression matrix directly and does not require an embedding step. The data are not single-cell expression profiles (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or PPI edge lists such as differentiation_edges), where per-cell clustering in embedded space is meaningless. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 PCA followed by a neighbor-embedding (UMAP) on a normalized single-cell expression matrix, as performed in the GSE113197 (Ind4) breast epithelial workflow that goes from count matrix to cluster annotation and trajectory inference. The low-dimensional embedding is what makes graph-based clustering of epithelial subpopulations feasible. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: PCA followed by a neighbor-embedding (UMAP) on a normalized single-cell expression matrix, as performed in the GSE113197 (Ind4) breast epithelial workflow that goes from count matrix to cluster annotation and trajectory inference. The low-dimensional embedding is what makes graph-based clustering of epithelial subpopulations feasible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an embedding or trajectory result rather than a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix — re-embedding would double-reduce the data. The goal is computing differentiation activity scores with ORIGINS activity(expression_matrix, differentiation_edges), which consumes the expression matrix directly and does not require an embedding step. The data are not single-cell expression profiles (e.g., bulk RNA-seq or PPI edge lists such as differentiation_edges), where per-cell clustering in embedded space is meaningless.

skills.search_text: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-pca-lsi Use when you need a low-dimensional cell representation of a single-cell count matrix (scRNA counts, protein ADT, or scATAC peak matrix) to feed a kNN graph, integration method, or label-consistency metric like kNN agreement. skills.summary: Reduces per-modality single-cell matrices to low-dimensional representations (PCA for scRNA and protein, LSI for scATAC) so that downstream label-quality metrics such as kNN agreement, clustering, or integration can be computed on a denoised, comparable cell embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell-cell adjacency you need must come from the integrated scMoMaT cell factors themselves — use scmomat.post_process on the extracted cell factors instead of reducing raw modality matrices. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. precomputed dimensionality reduction in .obsm for MultiMAP) — apply the kNN graph directly rather than re-reducing. skills.description: Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset contains cells measured under multiple biological conditions and you need to jointly remove batch effect while preserving condition effect in latent factors.
skills.name: single-cell-disentangled-latent-model-training
skills.search_text: single-cell-disentangled-latent-model-training Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset contains cells measured under multiple biological conditions and you need to jointly remove batch effect while preserving condition effect in latent factors. Each batch of cells is measured under only one condition — the paper notes there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects in that setting. The task is single-condition scRNA-seq integration with only batch effects and no condition design (e.g. plain batch correction with scVI/BBKNN). Condition types are strongly correlated, requiring a combined condition type (e.g. stim1_stim2, ctrl1_stim2, stim1_ctrl2, ctrl1_ctrl2) rather than independent condition encodings. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Train scDisInFact, a conditional variational autoencoder that disentangles multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data into shared-bio factors, condition-specific unshared-bio factors, and batch factors, enabling batch effect removal, key gene detection, and perturbation prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Train scDisInFact, a conditional variational autoencoder that disentangles multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data into shared-bio factors, condition-specific unshared-bio factors, and batch factors, enabling batch effect removal, key gene detection, and perturbation prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch of cells is measured under only one condition — the paper notes there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects in that setting. The task is single-condition scRNA-seq integration with only batch effects and no condition design (e.g. plain batch correction with scVI/BBKNN). Condition types are strongly correlated, requiring a combined condition type (e.g. stim1_stim2, ctrl1_stim2, stim1_ctrl2, ctrl1_ctrl2) rather than independent condition encodings.

skills.search_text: single-cell-distance-metric-benchmarking Use when you need to validate that a proposed cell-to-cell similarity/distance measure captures same-cell-type affinity more strongly than a conventional pipeline baseline (e.g., HVG+PCA Euclidean distance), by quantifying deviation from a permutation null. skills.search_text: single-cell-distance-metric-computation Use when quantifying how closely inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data matches real-profiled ground truth, or when scoring per-sample inference difficulty Dsc to drive active-learning representative selection on a bulk+single-cell cohort. skills.search_text: single-cell-dna-rna-cell-assignment-stability-analysis Use when scRNA-seq and scDNA-seq cells from the same samples have been assigned with MaCroDNA but no paired ground truth exists, and you need statistical significance and stability of those assignments.
