skills.description: Use when you have independent single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression matrices from the same sample (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need to associate RNA cells to DNA cells or infer cell-to-clone assignments.
skills.name: single-cell-dna-rna-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-dna-rna-integration Use when you have independent single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression matrices from the same sample (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need to associate RNA cells to DNA cells or infer cell-to-clone assignments. You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — MaCroDNA, unlike clonealign, does not provide them; use only the step number in cell2cell_step as a confidence proxy. Your sample is highly homogeneous — matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples per the article's discussion. You have paired multi-omic measurements of the same cells (no cell association problem to solve) or no clone labels and only need cell-to-clone results. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Integrates scRNA-seq gene expression with scDNA-seq copy-number data by maximum weighted bipartite matching of per-gene Pearson correlations, using MaCroDNA (Gurobi MIP) to assign RNA cells to DNA cells or clones. Rationale: gene expression is assumed proportional to copy number, so correlated per-gene profiles identify the same cell across modalities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Integrates scRNA-seq gene expression with scDNA-seq copy-number data by maximum weighted bipartite matching of per-gene Pearson correlations, using MaCroDNA (Gurobi MIP) to assign RNA cells to DNA cells or clones. Rationale: gene expression is assumed proportional to copy number, so correlated per-gene profiles identify the same cell across modalities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — MaCroDNA, unlike clonealign, does not provide them; use only the step number in cell2cell_step as a confidence proxy. Your sample is highly homogeneous — matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples per the article's discussion. You have paired multi-omic measurements of the same cells (no cell association problem to solve) or no clone labels and only need cell-to-clone results.

skills.description: Use when training or evaluating cross-tissue cell type classifiers on multi-donor scRNA-seq corpora where test cells must come from donors never seen during training.
skills.name: single-cell-donor-based-data-splitting
skills.search_text: single-cell-donor-based-data-splitting Use when training or evaluating cross-tissue cell type classifiers on multi-donor scRNA-seq corpora where test cells must come from donors never seen during training. When the research question is within-donor performance (e.g., annotating new cells from the same donors), a cell-level random split is appropriate and a donor split would underestimate attainable accuracy. When the corpus lacks reliable donor/batch metadata or cell types are observed in fewer than 30 donors, held-out-donor generalization cannot be reliably quantified. When data is not primary (is_primary_data == False), donor-based splitting cannot prevent train/test label leakage from duplicated observations. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Splits a large single-cell RNA-seq corpus into train/val/test partitions by donor (batch) rather than by cell, so that classifier performance measures generalization to unseen donors. This is essential for honestly quantifying whether scaling gains come from donor diversity versus cell count. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5
skills.summary: Splits a large single-cell RNA-seq corpus into train/val/test partitions by donor (batch) rather than by cell, so that classifier performance measures generalization to unseen donors. This is essential for honestly quantifying whether scaling gains come from donor diversity versus cell count.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the research question is within-donor performance (e.g., annotating new cells from the same donors), a cell-level random split is appropriate and a donor split would underestimate attainable accuracy. When the corpus lacks reliable donor/batch metadata or cell types are observed in fewer than 30 donors, held-out-donor generalization cannot be reliably quantified. When data is not primary (is_primary_data == False), donor-based splitting cannot prevent train/test label leakage from duplicated observations.

skills.description: Use when droplet-based scRNA-seq data may contain heterotypic doublets that destabilize downstream clustering or trajectory inference, and single-method doublet scores vary across datasets — an ensemble (GBM-boosted) score is needed before filtering.
skills.name: single-cell-doublet-ensemble-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-doublet-ensemble-scoring Use when droplet-based scRNA-seq data may contain heterotypic doublets that destabilize downstream clustering or trajectory inference, and single-method doublet scores vary across datasets — an ensemble (GBM-boosted) score is needed before filtering. The dataset was already doublet-identified experimentally (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) and only inter-sample doublets need labelling — those techniques label doublets directly without computational scoring Ambient mRNA contamination is the dominant artifact rather than doublets — Chord does not incorporate ambient RNA removal steps and other pre-processing would be needed Input is not single-cell droplet data (e.g. a bulk or aggregated feature table) — simulating doublets from remaining cells is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores every cell in a droplet scRNA-seq dataset for doublets by integrating multiple detection methods (scds cxds/bcds, DoubletFinder, optionally Scrublet) with a GBM/AdaBoost ensemble, then removes the top-ranked cells (matching the estimated doublet rate, e.g. 20%) to produce a clean single-cell matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Scores every cell in a droplet scRNA-seq dataset for doublets by integrating multiple detection methods (scds cxds/bcds, DoubletFinder, optionally Scrublet) with a GBM/AdaBoost ensemble, then removes the top-ranked cells (matching the estimated doublet rate, e.g. 20%) to produce a clean single-cell matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset was already doublet-identified experimentally (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) and only inter-sample doublets need labelling — those techniques label doublets directly without computational scoring Ambient mRNA contamination is the dominant artifact rather than doublets — Chord does not incorporate ambient RNA removal steps and other pre-processing would be needed Input is not single-cell droplet data (e.g. a bulk or aggregated feature table) — simulating doublets from remaining cells is meaningless

skills.description: Use when a computationally inferred or semi-profiled single-cell cohort must be validated against a real-profiled cohort by comparing downstream outputs such as marker genes, GO enrichment, CellChat interaction matrices, and Monocle3 pseudotime.
skills.name: single-cell-downstream-fidelity-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-downstream-fidelity-evaluation Use when a computationally inferred or semi-profiled single-cell cohort must be validated against a real-profiled cohort by comparing downstream outputs such as marker genes, GO enrichment, CellChat interaction matrices, and Monocle3 pseudotime. The cohort being evaluated is real-profiled data with no AI-generated or semi-profiled counterpart, so there is no fidelity comparison to make Only bulk-level deconvolution accuracy (cell-type proportions) is needed — this skill evaluates true single-cell-resolution downstream analyses, not cell-type-fraction correlation The inferred cohort lacks a matched real-profiled ground truth on shared cells, making RRHO, CellChat, and pseudotime correlations undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking workflow for verifying that semi-profiled (AI-generated) single-cell cohorts reproduce downstream single-cell analyses — marker/RRHO overlap, GO/Reactome enrichment, cell-cell interactions, and pseudotime — at the fidelity levels achieved by scSemiProfiler on the COVID-19 cohort. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: A benchmarking workflow for verifying that semi-profiled (AI-generated) single-cell cohorts reproduce downstream single-cell analyses — marker/RRHO overlap, GO/Reactome enrichment, cell-cell interactions, and pseudotime — at the fidelity levels achieved by scSemiProfiler on the COVID-19 cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort being evaluated is real-profiled data with no AI-generated or semi-profiled counterpart, so there is no fidelity comparison to make Only bulk-level deconvolution accuracy (cell-type proportions) is needed — this skill evaluates true single-cell-resolution downstream analyses, not cell-type-fraction correlation The inferred cohort lacks a matched real-profiled ground truth on shared cells, making RRHO, CellChat, and pseudotime correlations undefined

skills.description: Use when reconstructing the decoder of the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder, or when a count-matrix generative loss must account for high-probability dropout events without assuming a zero-inflated negative binomial model.
skills.name: single-cell-dropout-event-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-dropout-event-modeling Use when reconstructing the decoder of the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder, or when a count-matrix generative loss must account for high-probability dropout events without assuming a zero-inflated negative binomial model. When the goal is explicit zero-inflated negative binomial modeling or zero-expansion imputation — the scMGCA decoder deliberately uses a multinomial distribution rather than a zero-inflated distribution (contrast DCA/scDeepCluster, which use ZINB losses) When the input is already log-normalized or non-count expression data — the multinomial likelihood requires a count matrix over the retained highly variable genes When genes expressed in zero cells have not been filtered out — the article states this filtering is the first step to reduce the impact of high dropout rates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 The scMGCA multinomial-based decoder models the scRNA-seq count matrix as following a multinomial distribution (rather than a zero-inflated distribution) and simulates dropout events with Bernoulli dropout variables on zero-count entries, so the autoencoder loss compensates for high dropout rates during clustering-oriented denoising. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: The scMGCA multinomial-based decoder models the scRNA-seq count matrix as following a multinomial distribution (rather than a zero-inflated distribution) and simulates dropout events with Bernoulli dropout variables on zero-count entries, so the autoencoder loss compensates for high dropout rates during clustering-oriented denoising.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is explicit zero-inflated negative binomial modeling or zero-expansion imputation — the scMGCA decoder deliberately uses a multinomial distribution rather than a zero-inflated distribution (contrast DCA/scDeepCluster, which use ZINB losses) When the input is already log-normalized or non-count expression data — the multinomial likelihood requires a count matrix over the retained highly variable genes When genes expressed in zero cells have not been filtered out — the article states this filtering is the first step to reduce the impact of high dropout rates

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive simulated or observed dropouts (e.g. 0.1%–10% sampling efficiency) and accurate imputation is needed before clustering, visualization, or pseudotime analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-dropout-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-dropout-imputation Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive simulated or observed dropouts (e.g. 0.1%–10% sampling efficiency) and accurate imputation is needed before clustering, visualization, or pseudotime analysis. Small genomic datasets: SERM learns the distribution from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual distribution and produce inaccurate imputation values Reference/observed pairs where dropouts were experimentally observed rather than simulated — the benchmark design (reference filtered to high-expression cells/genes, dropouts simulated) may not match such data Batch-level analyses requiring explicit batch-effect modeling — batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation (only z-score integration post hoc) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Recovers zeroed-out (dropout) gene expression values in sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices by learning the underlying data distribution (autoencoder + parametric PDF curve fitting) and imposing self-consistency via adaptive histogram equalization over sliding ROIs (SERM), yielding imputed matrices that improve downstream clustering and trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34595-w
skills.summary: Recovers zeroed-out (dropout) gene expression values in sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices by learning the underlying data distribution (autoencoder + parametric PDF curve fitting) and imposing self-consistency via adaptive histogram equalization over sliding ROIs (SERM), yielding imputed matrices that improve downstream clustering and trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Small genomic datasets: SERM learns the distribution from a small fraction of the data, so the estimated distribution may diverge from the actual distribution and produce inaccurate imputation values Reference/observed pairs where dropouts were experimentally observed rather than simulated — the benchmark design (reference filtered to high-expression cells/genes, dropouts simulated) may not match such data Batch-level analyses requiring explicit batch-effect modeling — batch effects are not considered explicitly in the SERM formulation (only z-score integration post hoc)

skills.description: Use when pre-training or adapting a single-cell classification model on raw scRNA-seq count matrices and a loss must capture the mean-dispersion-dropout structure (zero-inflation) of gene expression counts.
skills.name: single-cell-dropout-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-dropout-modeling Use when pre-training or adapting a single-cell classification model on raw scRNA-seq count matrices and a loss must capture the mean-dispersion-dropout structure (zero-inflation) of gene expression counts. Input data are not raw scRNA-seq counts (e.g. pre-normalized or log-transformed expression), since the ZINB likelihood assumes discrete count structure with dropout events The goal is purely unsupervised clustering without a source classification model, where the ZINB denoising loss of scEMAIL's source pre-training stage is not the driving component http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstruct the ZINB model-based denoising autoencoder that scEMAIL uses in source model pre-training and target adaptation, minimizing the ZINB negative log-likelihood to depict the global probabilistic structure of scRNA-seq count data, including its dropout (zero-inflation) component. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Reconstruct the ZINB model-based denoising autoencoder that scEMAIL uses in source model pre-training and target adaptation, minimizing the ZINB negative log-likelihood to depict the global probabilistic structure of scRNA-seq count data, including its dropout (zero-inflation) component.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not raw scRNA-seq counts (e.g. pre-normalized or log-transformed expression), since the ZINB likelihood assumes discrete count structure with dropout events The goal is purely unsupervised clustering without a source classification model, where the ZINB denoising loss of scEMAIL's source pre-training stage is not the driving component

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq raw count matrix contains dropout-driven false zeros and you need to estimate which gene-cell entries are affected by dropout before imputation, rather than altering all expression values.
skills.name: single-cell-dropout-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-dropout-probability-estimation Use when an scRNA-seq raw count matrix contains dropout-driven false zeros and you need to estimate which gene-cell entries are affected by dropout before imputation, rather than altering all expression values. If the goal is to impute every entry in the matrix regardless of dropout status — MAGIC and SAVER alter all gene expression levels including those unaffected by dropouts, which scImpute deliberately avoids If cell type labels or cluster structure are unknown and no reasonable Kcluster can be chosen, since the number of cell populations is left to the user without a definitive selection procedure If the raw data come from droplet-based protocols with severely high dropout rates, where imputation efficiency is noted as degrading Estimate per-gene, per-cell dropout probabilities in scRNA-seq data by fitting a two-component Gamma-Normal mixture model per gene within each cell subpopulation via expectation-maximization, as implemented in scImpute. Only entries whose posterior dropout probability exceeds a threshold (e.g. drop_thre = 0.5) are targeted for imputation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03405-7
skills.summary: Estimate per-gene, per-cell dropout probabilities in scRNA-seq data by fitting a two-component Gamma-Normal mixture model per gene within each cell subpopulation via expectation-maximization, as implemented in scImpute. Only entries whose posterior dropout probability exceeds a threshold (e.g. drop_thre = 0.5) are targeted for imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is to impute every entry in the matrix regardless of dropout status — MAGIC and SAVER alter all gene expression levels including those unaffected by dropouts, which scImpute deliberately avoids If cell type labels or cluster structure are unknown and no reasonable Kcluster can be chosen, since the number of cell populations is left to the user without a definitive selection procedure If the raw data come from droplet-based protocols with severely high dropout rates, where imputation efficiency is noted as degrading

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue (e.g., TNBC PDX models or patient samples like GSE123926/GSE161529) needs FDA-approved drug recommendations that account for multiple heterogeneous cell clusters.
skills.name: single-cell-drug-repositioning
skills.search_text: single-cell-drug-repositioning Use when scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue (e.g., TNBC PDX models or patient samples like GSE123926/GSE161529) needs FDA-approved drug recommendations that account for multiple heterogeneous cell clusters. Input is bulk RNA-seq or a feature table without single-cell resolution — ASGARD's drug score is defined across single-cell clusters and bulk-based methods like CLUE underperform in the benchmarks No suitable normal-tissue control exists for the disease — the article notes substitutes may be needed until normal tissue data are available No tissue-matched LINCS L1000 drug reference exists for the target disease — the reference is limited to 98 cell lines http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0208 http://edamontology.org/topic_0154 Apply the ASGARD pipeline (R package) to scRNA-seq data to recommend repurposed drugs by computing a per-patient multi-cluster DrugScore across all diseased cell clusters, addressing intratumoral cellular heterogeneity that bulk-cell methods miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36637-3
skills.summary: Apply the ASGARD pipeline (R package) to scRNA-seq data to recommend repurposed drugs by computing a per-patient multi-cluster DrugScore across all diseased cell clusters, addressing intratumoral cellular heterogeneity that bulk-cell methods miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or a feature table without single-cell resolution — ASGARD's drug score is defined across single-cell clusters and bulk-based methods like CLUE underperform in the benchmarks No suitable normal-tissue control exists for the disease — the article notes substitutes may be needed until normal tissue data are available No tissue-matched LINCS L1000 drug reference exists for the target disease — the reference is limited to 98 cell lines

skills.description: Use when you have untreated disease-state scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations, a known drug target gene (e.g. Smo for vismodegib, Ctsk for tanshinone IIA), and need to rank which cell types are most drug-responsive.
skills.name: single-cell-drug-response-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-drug-response-inference Use when you have untreated disease-state scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations, a known drug target gene (e.g. Smo for vismodegib, Ctsk for tanshinone IIA), and need to rank which cell types are most drug-responsive. The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank primarily focuses on inhibitor drugs, and agonist/multi-target extensions are preliminary only You require disease-treatment paired datasets and differential-expression-based inference rather than target-informed ranking of untreated samples The drug target is unknown and cannot be resolved via utile_database or candidate gene ranking in the cell-type-specific GRN http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply scRank's target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) approach to rank drug-responsive cell populations via in silico drug perturbation using untreated single-cell transcriptomic data, as described in Li et al., Cell Reports Medicine 2024. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Apply scRank's target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN) approach to rank drug-responsive cell populations via in silico drug perturbation using untreated single-cell transcriptomic data, as described in Li et al., Cell Reports Medicine 2024.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank primarily focuses on inhibitor drugs, and agonist/multi-target extensions are preliminary only You require disease-treatment paired datasets and differential-expression-based inference rather than target-informed ranking of untreated samples The drug target is unknown and cannot be resolved via utile_database or candidate gene ranking in the cell-type-specific GRN

skills.description: Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) and need cluster-wise drug sensitivity estimates (IC50) and cell-kill percentages for GDSC drugs.
skills.name: single-cell-drug-response-prediction
skills.search_text: single-cell-drug-response-prediction Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) and need cluster-wise drug sensitivity estimates (IC50) and cell-kill percentages for GDSC drugs. No Louvain clustering or AnnData object exists yet — run Single-Cell Data Analysis first to produce scanpyobj.h5ad The drug of interest was not experimentally screened in GDSC/PRISM — scDrug prediction is limited by experimentally screened compounds You need de novo prediction of drug sensitivity for unscreened compounds — this is explicitly not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3336 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predicts drug response per Louvain cell cluster from a Scanpy AnnData object by estimating IC50 with the CaDRReS-Sc GDSC pre-trained model and converting it into cell death percentages reported as drug kill efficacy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Predicts drug response per Louvain cell cluster from a Scanpy AnnData object by estimating IC50 with the CaDRReS-Sc GDSC pre-trained model and converting it into cell death percentages reported as drug kill efficacy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No Louvain clustering or AnnData object exists yet — run Single-Cell Data Analysis first to produce scanpyobj.h5ad The drug of interest was not experimentally screened in GDSC/PRISM — scDrug prediction is limited by experimentally screened compounds You need de novo prediction of drug sensitivity for unscreened compounds — this is explicitly not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be clustered and interpreted through topics — e.g. identifying topics differentially expressed between disease and control conditions or across cell types.
skills.name: single-cell-embedding-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-embedding-analysis Use when scRNA-seq count data must be clustered and interpreted through topics — e.g. identifying topics differentially expressed between disease and control conditions or across cell types. The goal is batch correction alone rather than topic-level interpretation — methods like Harmony or Scanorama target integration without topic structure The input is not single-cell count data in AnnData format (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature tables) Only one mini-batch of training is feasible and the model cannot reach the ~6k gradient updates recommended for convergence http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Trains the scETM generative topic model on scRNA-seq data and uses the learned cell topic mixtures, topic and gene embeddings to interpret topics via differential topic abundance tests (permutation + Bonferroni) and pathway enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Trains the scETM generative topic model on scRNA-seq data and uses the learned cell topic mixtures, topic and gene embeddings to interpret topics via differential topic abundance tests (permutation + Bonferroni) and pathway enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is batch correction alone rather than topic-level interpretation — methods like Harmony or Scanorama target integration without topic structure The input is not single-cell count data in AnnData format (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature tables) Only one mini-batch of training is feasible and the model cannot reach the ~6k gradient updates recommended for convergence

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a single-cell embedding method (e.g., DIRECTi, DCA, PCA, tSNE) preserves cell-type resolution in scRNA-seq latent space, by computing MAP of nearest-neighbor cell retrieval between query and reference datasets.
skills.name: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a single-cell embedding method (e.g., DIRECTi, DCA, PCA, tSNE) preserves cell-type resolution in scRNA-seq latent space, by computing MAP of nearest-neighbor cell retrieval between query and reference datasets. Datasets with fewer than 1000 cells, which may suffer from under-training of the over-parameterized DIRECTi model (3000 cells is generally sufficient) Mega-scale integration scenarios where highly skewed cell-type composition across batches risks over-correcting of batches Tasks where input is not cell-by-gene scRNA-seq data with reference annotations available for cell-querying http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmarks Cell BLAST's DIRECTi deep generative embeddings against DCA, PCA, and tSNE for cell-type resolution using mean average precision (MAP) on real-world scRNA-seq reference/query datasets in h5ad format, as in Supplementary Table 1/2 and Supplementary Fig. 3 of the Cell BLAST paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks Cell BLAST's DIRECTi deep generative embeddings against DCA, PCA, and tSNE for cell-type resolution using mean average precision (MAP) on real-world scRNA-seq reference/query datasets in h5ad format, as in Supplementary Table 1/2 and Supplementary Fig. 3 of the Cell BLAST paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with fewer than 1000 cells, which may suffer from under-training of the over-parameterized DIRECTi model (3000 cells is generally sufficient) Mega-scale integration scenarios where highly skewed cell-type composition across batches risks over-correcting of batches Tasks where input is not cell-by-gene scRNA-seq data with reference annotations available for cell-querying

skills.description: Use when comparing how well alternative low-dimensional embeddings of simulated scRNA-seq preserve cell-cell topological structure, evaluated as trajectory (pseudotime) recovery measured by Kendall correlation against a known ground truth.
skills.name: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking Use when comparing how well alternative low-dimensional embeddings of simulated scRNA-seq preserve cell-cell topological structure, evaluated as trajectory (pseudotime) recovery measured by Kendall correlation against a known ground truth. The input is empirical data with no simulated ground-truth trajectory ordering — Kendall-tau benchmarking against truth is undefined there The goal is clustering rather than trajectory recovery — the paper reports scGAE vs competitors differ in their clustering ranking, so tau on pseudotime would not answer the question A single method's embedding quality is already established and no competitor comparison is needed — building the full multi-method table adds no information http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks dimensionality-reduction methods for scRNA-seq by embedding the same simulated lineage datasets with scGAE and competitors (DCA, scVI, PHATE, SAUCIE, scGNN, ZINB-WaVE, Ivis), running diffusion pseudotime on each embedding, and scoring trajectory recovery by Kendall-tau correlation against the simulated ground-truth ordering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks dimensionality-reduction methods for scRNA-seq by embedding the same simulated lineage datasets with scGAE and competitors (DCA, scVI, PHATE, SAUCIE, scGNN, ZINB-WaVE, Ivis), running diffusion pseudotime on each embedding, and scoring trajectory recovery by Kendall-tau correlation against the simulated ground-truth ordering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is empirical data with no simulated ground-truth trajectory ordering — Kendall-tau benchmarking against truth is undefined there The goal is clustering rather than trajectory recovery — the paper reports scGAE vs competitors differ in their clustering ranking, so tau on pseudotime would not answer the question A single method's embedding quality is already established and no competitor comparison is needed — building the full multi-method table adds no information

skills.description: Use when inferring a tree-shaped trajectory from single-cell data and a diverse set of candidate clusterings is needed to construct minimum spanning trees and estimate cell connectivity, as in the Totem workflow.
skills.name: single-cell-embedding-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-embedding-clustering Use when inferring a tree-shaped trajectory from single-cell data and a diverse set of candidate clusterings is needed to construct minimum spanning trees and estimate cell connectivity, as in the Totem workflow. The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types, where k-medoids may fail and manual cluster merging is required instead The embedding is a high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components), where k-medoids may produce degenerate 1-2 cell clusters The analysis goal does not require an ensemble of dissimilar clusterings (e.g. a single trusted prior clustering is already available to guide the search) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a large ensemble of dissimilar clusterings by running the CLARA k-medoids algorithm many times (default 10,000 runs, k from 3 to 20) on a low-dimensional embedding of single-cell data, providing the clustering basis for downstream MST-based trajectory inference in Totem. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Generates a large ensemble of dissimilar clusterings by running the CLARA k-medoids algorithm many times (default 10,000 runs, k from 3 to 20) on a low-dimensional embedding of single-cell data, providing the clustering basis for downstream MST-based trajectory inference in Totem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset mixes extremely rare and extremely prevalent cell types, where k-medoids may fail and manual cluster merging is required instead The embedding is a high-dimensional PCA (e.g. 30 principal components), where k-medoids may produce degenerate 1-2 cell clusters The analysis goal does not require an ensemble of dissimilar clusterings (e.g. a single trusted prior clustering is already available to guide the search)

skills.description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) on integrated single-cell embeddings where ground-truth cell-type labels exist and you need quantitative clustering/bio-conservation and batch-mixing metrics.
skills.name: single-cell-embedding-clustering-accuracy-assessment
skills.search_text: single-cell-embedding-clustering-accuracy-assessment Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) on integrated single-cell embeddings where ground-truth cell-type labels exist and you need quantitative clustering/bio-conservation and batch-mixing metrics. The expression matrix is already log-normalized — in that case pass normalization=False to scCAD to avoid double-normalizing The task is downstream anomaly scoring of precomputed sub-clusters (isolation forest on top 20 differential genes, independence score threshold I=0.7) rather than preprocessing The input is not a cell-by-gene count matrix (e.g., a feature table or metadata sheet), which cannot be gene-filtered or PCA-embedded by this recipe http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocess raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., the 1%Jurkat.h5 example with 1540 293T + 16 Jurkat cells) by retaining genes expressed in at least three cells, log-normalizing with cell-specific size factors plus log2(x+1) transformation, and embedding via 40-PC PCA with a 15-nearest-neighbor Euclidean graph and Louvain clustering to produce initial I-clusters. This is the deterministic front-end that scCAD's rare cell detection depends on. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9

skills.name: single-cell-genotyping-from-bam-pileups
skills.search_text: single-cell-genotyping-from-bam-pileups Use when a list of somatic SNVs from paired tumor/normal eWGS must be detected per-cell in 10x 5' scRNA-seq BAMs (CB/UB_tag barcodes), producing per-sample mutant-cell counts. No pre-called somatic variant list exists — cb_sniffer/VarTrix assign previously defined variants, they do not call variants de novo (VarTrix 'does not perform variant calling') The goal is determining which cells are truly wild-type for a mutation — dropout makes this impossible; only mutant/unknown labels are supportable Multi-allelic sites are the target — VarTrix ignores all multi-allelic sites, leaving empty matrix values http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Genotype individual cells in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq BAM data at somatic SNVs pre-discovered by enhanced whole-genome sequencing (eWGS), using barcode-aware pileups to label each cell mutant or unknown and count mutant cells per sample. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Genotype individual cells in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq BAM data at somatic SNVs pre-discovered by enhanced whole-genome sequencing (eWGS), using barcode-aware pileups to label each cell mutant or unknown and count mutant cells per sample.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No pre-called somatic variant list exists — cb_sniffer/VarTrix assign previously defined variants, they do not call variants de novo (VarTrix 'does not perform variant calling') The goal is determining which cells are truly wild-type for a mutation — dropout makes this impossible; only mutant/unknown labels are supportable Multi-allelic sites are the target — VarTrix ignores all multi-allelic sites, leaving empty matrix values

skills.description: Use when clustering raw or preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices where preserving cell-cell topological relationships matters, e.g. datasets with rare cell types, small clusters, or >25,000 cells needing batched learning.
skills.name: single-cell-graph-embedding-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-graph-embedding-clustering Use when clustering raw or preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrices where preserving cell-cell topological relationships matters, e.g. datasets with rare cell types, small clusters, or >25,000 cells needing batched learning. Input is already a cell-feature embedding or cluster-label table — scMGCA requires the gene expression count matrix to build the cell-PPMI graph The goal is gene-level pathway enrichment without first obtaining a latent representation — use a standard GO/KEGG over-representation workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Cluster scRNA-seq cells by training scMGCA, a graph-embedding autoencoder that simultaneously learns cell-cell topology via a cell-PPMI graph and cluster assignments through a two-layer GCN encoder with a multinomial-based decoder and KL-divergence self-optimized clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36134-7
skills.summary: Cluster scRNA-seq cells by training scMGCA, a graph-embedding autoencoder that simultaneously learns cell-cell topology via a cell-PPMI graph and cluster assignments through a two-layer GCN encoder with a multinomial-based decoder and KL-divergence self-optimized clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-feature embedding or cluster-label table — scMGCA requires the gene expression count matrix to build the cell-PPMI graph The goal is gene-level pathway enrichment without first obtaining a latent representation — use a standard GO/KEGG over-representation workflow instead

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix plus prior cluster labels and need a 2D layout that shows cluster membership together with differentiation trajectories between clusters (e.g. stem-cell-centered lineages, branch points).
skills.name: single-cell-graph-embedding-layout
skills.search_text: single-cell-graph-embedding-layout Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix plus prior cluster labels and need a 2D layout that shows cluster membership together with differentiation trajectories between clusters (e.g. stem-cell-centered lineages, branch points). No prior cluster assignment exists — GraphDDP starts from a user-defined cluster label per instance; run a clustering step (e.g. RaceID2) first. You need quantitative pseudotime ordering or a rooted trajectory tree rather than a visual layout — use pseudotime tools like TSCAN or Monocle2 instead. The input is not an instance/feature matrix with discrete labels (e.g. already a feature table of summary statistics or unlabeled bulk data). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute a supervised 2D graph embedding of single-cell transcriptome data (GraphDDP/GraphEmbed) that integrates RaceID2/StemID-style cluster assignments with density-gradient differentiation trajectories, so lineage hierarchies and progenitor relations become visible in one layout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Compute a supervised 2D graph embedding of single-cell transcriptome data (GraphDDP/GraphEmbed) that integrates RaceID2/StemID-style cluster assignments with density-gradient differentiation trajectories, so lineage hierarchies and progenitor relations become visible in one layout.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior cluster assignment exists — GraphDDP starts from a user-defined cluster label per instance; run a clustering step (e.g. RaceID2) first. You need quantitative pseudotime ordering or a rooted trajectory tree rather than a visual layout — use pseudotime tools like TSCAN or Monocle2 instead. The input is not an instance/feature matrix with discrete labels (e.g. already a feature table of summary statistics or unlabeled bulk data).

skills.description: Use when building a lineage-specific GRN from a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., AnnData with a developmental trajectory) and a prior gene interaction network edgelist, as input to driver regulator or gene module analyses.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-construction
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-construction Use when building a lineage-specific GRN from a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., AnnData with a developmental trajectory) and a prior gene interaction network edgelist, as input to driver regulator or gene module analyses. When multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time When only scRNA-seq data are available without a prior gene interaction network, since CEFCON requires a prior network as input When modeling extrinsic factors (cell–cell communication, spatial location) or epigenetic regulation — CEFCON focuses on intracellular RNA-level factors http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Construct cell-lineage-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from scRNA-seq data and a prior gene interaction network using CEFCON's graph attention neural network under a contrastive learning framework, as described in Wang et al. 2023 (Nature Communications). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Construct cell-lineage-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from scRNA-seq data and a prior gene interaction network using CEFCON's graph attention neural network under a contrastive learning framework, as described in Wang et al. 2023 (Nature Communications).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON can only handle one cell lineage at a time When only scRNA-seq data are available without a prior gene interaction network, since CEFCON requires a prior network as input When modeling extrinsic factors (cell–cell communication, spatial location) or epigenetic regulation — CEFCON focuses on intracellular RNA-level factors

skills.description: Use when reconstructing gene regulatory networks from raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) and you need a GRN construction method with high specificity and sensitivity across a wide range of cell numbers (10 to 3,000 cells).
skills.name: single-cell-grn-construction-pc-regression
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-construction-pc-regression Use when reconstructing gene regulatory networks from raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) and you need a GRN construction method with high specificity and sensitivity across a wide range of cell numbers (10 to 3,000 cells). The goal is differential regulation testing or comparing two conditions end-to-end — use the full scTenifoldNet pipeline (tensorDecomposition, manifoldAlignment, dRegulation) instead of bare PC regression network construction The input is already normalized/processed rather than raw counts, unless you intentionally substitute custom preprocessing (scTenifoldNet's modular design permits this but the default expects raw counts) The samples being compared are highly dissimilar — scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Construct single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) from raw scRNA-seq count matrices using principal-component (PC) regression via scTenifoldNet's pcNet/makeNetworks functions, benchmarked to outperform Spearman correlation, mutual information, and GENIE3 in specificity (accuracy) and sensitivity (recall). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139
skills.summary: Construct single-cell gene regulatory networks (scGRNs) from raw scRNA-seq count matrices using principal-component (PC) regression via scTenifoldNet's pcNet/makeNetworks functions, benchmarked to outperform Spearman correlation, mutual information, and GENIE3 in specificity (accuracy) and sensitivity (recall).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential regulation testing or comparing two conditions end-to-end — use the full scTenifoldNet pipeline (tensorDecomposition, manifoldAlignment, dRegulation) instead of bare PC regression network construction The input is already normalized/processed rather than raw counts, unless you intentionally substitute custom preprocessing (scTenifoldNet's modular design permits this but the default expects raw counts) The samples being compared are highly dissimilar — scTenifoldNet is more suitable for comparing highly similar samples, such as two populations of cells of the same type

skills.description: Use when two gene regulatory network inference tools (e.g., MINI-EX and SCENIC) have been run on the same single-cell atlas and their cell-type-specific regulon outputs must be compared and validated.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-cross-tool-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-cross-tool-comparison Use when two gene regulatory network inference tools (e.g., MINI-EX and SCENIC) have been run on the same single-cell atlas and their cell-type-specific regulon outputs must be compared and validated. Only one GRN inference tool has been run and no second tool's regulon output exists for cross-comparison The input is bulk transcriptomic data rather than a cell-clustered single-cell atlas, since both MINI-EX and the comparison workflow require cell-type-specific regulons The organism's cisTarget databases or TF motif resources (e.g., from JASPAR or PlantTFDB) are unavailable, so regulons cannot be inferred for the species http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Reproduce the cross-tool comparison of cell-type-specific regulons inferred by MINI-EX and SCENIC on the Arabidopsis root single-cell atlas, quantifying agreement via Jaccard similarity of top regulons and confirming MINI-EX's higher signal-to-noise ratio of regulon enrichment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Reproduce the cross-tool comparison of cell-type-specific regulons inferred by MINI-EX and SCENIC on the Arabidopsis root single-cell atlas, quantifying agreement via Jaccard similarity of top regulons and confirming MINI-EX's higher signal-to-noise ratio of regulon enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one GRN inference tool has been run and no second tool's regulon output exists for cross-comparison The input is bulk transcriptomic data rather than a cell-clustered single-cell atlas, since both MINI-EX and the comparison workflow require cell-type-specific regulons The organism's cisTarget databases or TF motif resources (e.g., from JASPAR or PlantTFDB) are unavailable, so regulons cannot be inferred for the species

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a method's ranked driver regulator list recovers known cell-fate regulators (e.g., NANOG, SOX2, POU5F1) against GO ground-truth sets in scRNA-seq benchmarking.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-driver-ranking-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-driver-ranking-analysis Use when evaluating whether a method's ranked driver regulator list recovers known cell-fate regulators (e.g., NANOG, SOX2, POU5F1) against GO ground-truth sets in scRNA-seq benchmarking. The goal is GRN edge inference quality rather than driver regulator ranking — use GRN construction benchmarks instead The input dataset contains multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations that must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON handles only one cell lineage at a time http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Reproduce and benchmark CEFCON's driver regulator identification by computing top-k (k=1-20) precision of ranked driver lists from CEFCON and five baselines (VIPER, ANANSE, SCENIC, CellRouter, CellOracle) against GO term and literature-curated ground-truth gene sets on the mESC and hESC datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44103-3
skills.summary: Reproduce and benchmark CEFCON's driver regulator identification by computing top-k (k=1-20) precision of ranked driver lists from CEFCON and five baselines (VIPER, ANANSE, SCENIC, CellRouter, CellOracle) against GO term and literature-curated ground-truth gene sets on the mESC and hESC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is GRN edge inference quality rather than driver regulator ranking — use GRN construction benchmarks instead The input dataset contains multiple fate trajectories with bifurcations that must be processed simultaneously — CEFCON handles only one cell lineage at a time

skills.description: Use when the goal is to build a whole-transcriptome GRN from a scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, or spatial dataset and the analysis requires robust consensus edges, module detection, and downstream perturbation-prediction evaluation (AUROC, TPR at FPR 0.05).
skills.name: single-cell-grn-inference-and-ensemble-merging
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-inference-and-ensemble-merging Use when the goal is to build a whole-transcriptome GRN from a scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, or spatial dataset and the analysis requires robust consensus edges, module detection, and downstream perturbation-prediction evaluation (AUROC, TPR at FPR 0.05). The task requires explicitly causal or directional regulatory edges — the inferred links 'are not necessarily causal or directional' per the article's discussion The task requires leveraging spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING 'does not currently utilize the spatial information' despite GRNs showing spatial patterns The task requires integrating additional omics (scATAC-seq, scHi-C, ChIP-seq, cis/trans eQTL) — these modalities are deferred to future work in SCING http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers robust gene regulatory networks from full single-cell transcriptomes (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, spatial) using SCING's bagging-based consensus: supercells, ~100 gradient-boosted GRNs on subsamples, and edge pruning via conditional mutual information, benchmarkable against GRNBOOST2, PIDC, and ppcor on Perturb-seq perturbation-prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Infers robust gene regulatory networks from full single-cell transcriptomes (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, spatial) using SCING's bagging-based consensus: supercells, ~100 gradient-boosted GRNs on subsamples, and edge pruning via conditional mutual information, benchmarkable against GRNBOOST2, PIDC, and ppcor on Perturb-seq perturbation-prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires explicitly causal or directional regulatory edges — the inferred links 'are not necessarily causal or directional' per the article's discussion The task requires leveraging spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING 'does not currently utilize the spatial information' despite GRNs showing spatial patterns The task requires integrating additional omics (scATAC-seq, scHi-C, ChIP-seq, cis/trans eQTL) — these modalities are deferred to future work in SCING

skills.description: Use when you have pySCENIC/SCENIC GRN outputs from plant single-cell data and need to visualize which regulon TFs characterize specific cell clusters.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-network-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-network-visualization Use when you have pySCENIC/SCENIC GRN outputs from plant single-cell data and need to visualize which regulon TFs characterize specific cell clusters. Input is raw unprocessed scRNA-seq counts without prior Seurat clustering and cell-type annotation — GRN visualization requires an annotated object Data are from non-plant organisms with no species-specific cisTarget database available in the scPlant auxiliary bundle The goal is differential expression or trajectory inference rather than regulon/GRN interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Visualize cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) inferred with pySCENIC/SCENIC inside the scPlant R framework, using regulon activity matrices, regulon specificity scores, and TF-target links to identify cell-type-characterizing regulon TFs (e.g., PIF5 for photosynthetic cells in the Arabidopsis root atlas). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Visualize cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) inferred with pySCENIC/SCENIC inside the scPlant R framework, using regulon activity matrices, regulon specificity scores, and TF-target links to identify cell-type-characterizing regulon TFs (e.g., PIF5 for photosynthetic cells in the Arabidopsis root atlas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unprocessed scRNA-seq counts without prior Seurat clustering and cell-type annotation — GRN visualization requires an annotated object Data are from non-plant organisms with no species-specific cisTarget database available in the scPlant auxiliary bundle The goal is differential expression or trajectory inference rather than regulon/GRN interpretation

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data has been clustered into pseudotime/Monocle states, CellOracle GRNs are inferred per state, and you need to rank TFs by predicted effect of knockout on a fate-transition process.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-perturbation-score-aggregation
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-perturbation-score-aggregation Use when scRNA-seq data has been clustered into pseudotime/Monocle states, CellOracle GRNs are inferred per state, and you need to rank TFs by predicted effect of knockout on a fate-transition process. When the goal is to identify cis-regulatory elements or build the base GRN from epigenomic data (e.g. the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas base-GRN) rather than to score perturbation effects on an already-inferred GRN When the input lacks a biologically expected perturbation control (like the reprogramming transgene) with which to sanity-check the top of the ranking When no replicate structure exists — the ranking's reproducibility (Pearson r) cannot be assessed from a single sample http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Systematic in silico knockout simulation of active transcription factors using CellOracle on state-specific GRNs (Links), followed by aggregation of per-state perturbation scores into a single ranked TF list, with reproducibility checked between biological replicates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Systematic in silico knockout simulation of active transcription factors using CellOracle on state-specific GRNs (Links), followed by aggregation of per-state perturbation scores into a single ranked TF list, with reproducibility checked between biological replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify cis-regulatory elements or build the base GRN from epigenomic data (e.g. the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas base-GRN) rather than to score perturbation effects on an already-inferred GRN When the input lacks a biologically expected perturbation control (like the reprogramming transgene) with which to sanity-check the top of the ranking When no replicate structure exists — the ranking's reproducibility (Pearson r) cannot be assessed from a single sample

skills.description: Use when cluster-specific GRN Links objects must be scored and compared across a reprogramming or differentiation trajectory, and centrality/cartography structure (e.g., Hnf4α-Foxa1 edge strength, connector-hub detection) needs to be visualized.
skills.name: single-cell-grn-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-grn-visualization Use when cluster-specific GRN Links objects must be scored and compared across a reprogramming or differentiation trajectory, and centrality/cartography structure (e.g., Hnf4α-Foxa1 edge strength, connector-hub detection) needs to be visualized. You only have raw scRNA-seq counts and no inferred cluster-specific GRN Links objects — first run CellOracle GRN inference rather than network scoring/visualization The goal is in silico TF perturbation simulation (KO/overexpression) of gene expression rather than structural network characterization The network of interest is not a TF regulatory network with a meaningful weighted adjacency — igraph/rnetcarto centrality and cartography roles are not interpretable on arbitrary graphs http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Method for scoring, characterizing, and visualizing cluster-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) along a cell-fate trajectory using CellOracle's network_analysis module, computing per-cluster edge/network scores, degree and eigenvector centrality, and network cartography roles to identify connector hubs and regulatory reconfiguration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Method for scoring, characterizing, and visualizing cluster-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) along a cell-fate trajectory using CellOracle's network_analysis module, computing per-cluster edge/network scores, degree and eigenvector centrality, and network cartography roles to identify connector hubs and regulatory reconfiguration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw scRNA-seq counts and no inferred cluster-specific GRN Links objects — first run CellOracle GRN inference rather than network scoring/visualization The goal is in silico TF perturbation simulation (KO/overexpression) of gene expression rather than structural network characterization The network of interest is not a TF regulatory network with a meaningful weighted adjacency — igraph/rnetcarto centrality and cartography roles are not interpretable on arbitrary graphs

skills.description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells from a Perturb-seq/CROP-seq gRNA capture library and you need mutation-aware cell-to-guide assignment with adaptive UMI thresholds rather than fixed ad hoc cutoffs.
skills.name: single-cell-grna-assignment-threshold-tuning
skills.search_text: single-cell-grna-assignment-threshold-tuning Use when assigning gRNAs to cells from a Perturb-seq/CROP-seq gRNA capture library and you need mutation-aware cell-to-guide assignment with adaptive UMI thresholds rather than fixed ad hoc cutoffs. You only need to detect CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing effects in the transcriptome — use GiRAFR's separate editing-effect mode instead of cell assignment Cell-to-guide assignments already exist from a trusted, validated annotation and you are not re-profiling gRNA sequences or mutations The gRNA library has not been aligned to a custom cassette reference, so no consensus sequences or variant calls exist to feed assignment http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assign gRNAs to individual cells in single-cell CRISPR screens using a data-adaptive, per-guide UMI threshold fitted with a two-component mixed Gaussian model, so that low-UMI ambient signal is separated from endogenous gRNA expression and mutant gRNAs are treated on par with intact ones. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05351-7
skills.summary: Assign gRNAs to individual cells in single-cell CRISPR screens using a data-adaptive, per-guide UMI threshold fitted with a two-component mixed Gaussian model, so that low-UMI ambient signal is separated from endogenous gRNA expression and mutant gRNAs are treated on par with intact ones.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need to detect CRISPR-Cas9-induced DNA editing effects in the transcriptome — use GiRAFR's separate editing-effect mode instead of cell assignment Cell-to-guide assignments already exist from a trusted, validated annotation and you are not re-profiling gRNA sequences or mutations The gRNA library has not been aligned to a custom cassette reference, so no consensus sequences or variant calls exist to feed assignment

skills.description: Use when GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object are available and the goal is to rank trait-relevant genes and compare their functional enrichment to gene-scoring baselines.
skills.name: single-cell-gwas-gene-prioritization
skills.search_text: single-cell-gwas-gene-prioritization Use when GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object are available and the goal is to rank trait-relevant genes and compare their functional enrichment to gene-scoring baselines. The goal is causal inference — the paper states identification of statistical association between traits and cells 'does not imply causality' Functionally informed SNP-to-gene linking is required — default scPagwas annotates SNPs to genes solely by proximal distance within a 20 kb window Input is bulk rather than single-cell expression — the skill depends on per-cell expression correlated with per-cell gPAS scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prioritize trait-relevant genes by correlating per-gene single-cell expression with scPagwas genetic pathway-activation scores (gPAS), then benchmark the top 1,000 genes against MAGMA/TWAS/S-PrediXcan/S-MultiXcan gene sets using GO biological-process over-representation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Prioritize trait-relevant genes by correlating per-gene single-cell expression with scPagwas genetic pathway-activation scores (gPAS), then benchmark the top 1,000 genes against MAGMA/TWAS/S-PrediXcan/S-MultiXcan gene sets using GO biological-process over-representation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is causal inference — the paper states identification of statistical association between traits and cells 'does not imply causality' Functionally informed SNP-to-gene linking is required — default scPagwas annotates SNPs to genes solely by proximal distance within a 20 kb window Input is bulk rather than single-cell expression — the skill depends on per-cell expression correlated with per-cell gPAS scores

skills.description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics (e.g., IEU ID ieu-b-2 AD GWAS) plus a cell-annotated snRNA-seq Seurat object (e.g., Grubman entorhinal cortex, 11,786 cells) and need trait-relevant cell types and single cells.
skills.name: single-cell-gwas-polygenic-regression-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-gwas-polygenic-regression-analysis Use when you have GWAS summary statistics (e.g., IEU ID ieu-b-2 AD GWAS) plus a cell-annotated snRNA-seq Seurat object (e.g., Grubman entorhinal cortex, 11,786 cells) and need trait-relevant cell types and single cells. You only have a pre-computed feature/gene-set table without per-cell expression or individual-level GWAS summary statistics — scPagwas requires both raw inputs You need causal inference for cell-trait associations — the article explicitly notes statistical association between traits and individual cells does not imply causality Your biological question depends on non-canonical or non-KEGG pathway definitions — the method is restricted to canonical KEGG pathways (5-300 genes) http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply scPagwas, a pathway-based polygenic regression method, to integrate GWAS summary statistics with pathway-activity-transformed scRNA-seq data to identify trait-relevant cell types and individual cells, as demonstrated for Alzheimer's disease (OPCs and microglia, FDR < 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100383
skills.summary: Apply scPagwas, a pathway-based polygenic regression method, to integrate GWAS summary statistics with pathway-activity-transformed scRNA-seq data to identify trait-relevant cell types and individual cells, as demonstrated for Alzheimer's disease (OPCs and microglia, FDR < 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a pre-computed feature/gene-set table without per-cell expression or individual-level GWAS summary statistics — scPagwas requires both raw inputs You need causal inference for cell-trait associations — the article explicitly notes statistical association between traits and individual cells does not imply causality Your biological question depends on non-canonical or non-KEGG pathway definitions — the method is restricted to canonical KEGG pathways (5-300 genes)

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is available as an .h5ad file and you want TFvelo to fit TF-based gene dynamics, infer pseudotime/trajectory, and rank transcription factors on data lacking splicing information.
skills.name: single-cell-h5ad-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-h5ad-preprocessing Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is available as an .h5ad file and you want TFvelo to fit TF-based gene dynamics, infer pseudotime/trajectory, and rank transcription factors on data lacking splicing information. The input is not an .h5ad AnnData file — the loader branch reads exclusively via ad.read_h5ad(your_h5ad_file_path), so raw count matrices (e.g., 10x mtx or FASTQ-derived data) must be converted first. Very large-scale datasets where runtime matters — the paper notes TFvelo's time efficiency is lower than scVelo, which 'could be a weakness when being applied to the large-scale datasets'. The goal is only visualization without refitting — TFvelo_analysis_demo.py consumes rc.h5ad produced by TFvelo_run_demo.py, so skipping the fitting step breaks the downstream demo. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Adapts the TFvelo pipeline (an scVelo-framework, gene-regulation-inspired RNA velocity method) to a custom scRNA-seq dataset stored as an AnnData .h5ad file by adding a dataset loader into the preprocess() function of TFvelo_run_demo.py, then running model fitting and visualization with default hyperparameters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: Adapts the TFvelo pipeline (an scVelo-framework, gene-regulation-inspired RNA velocity method) to a custom scRNA-seq dataset stored as an AnnData .h5ad file by adding a dataset loader into the preprocess() function of TFvelo_run_demo.py, then running model fitting and visualization with default hyperparameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an .h5ad AnnData file — the loader branch reads exclusively via ad.read_h5ad(your_h5ad_file_path), so raw count matrices (e.g., 10x mtx or FASTQ-derived data) must be converted first. Very large-scale datasets where runtime matters — the paper notes TFvelo's time efficiency is lower than scVelo, which 'could be a weakness when being applied to the large-scale datasets'. The goal is only visualization without refitting — TFvelo_analysis_demo.py consumes rc.h5ad produced by TFvelo_run_demo.py, so skipping the fitting step breaks the downstream demo.

skills.description: Use when two or more cell groups have been defined in-session from single-cell expression data and a ranked marker-gene heatmap with per-gene Wilcoxon p-values and FDRs is required to compare groups.
skills.name: single-cell-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-heatmap-visualization Use when two or more cell groups have been defined in-session from single-cell expression data and a ranked marker-gene heatmap with per-gene Wilcoxon p-values and FDRs is required to compare groups. Only a single cell group is defined — the two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test requires at least two groups to compare The goal is pseudotime trajectory analysis rather than group comparison — CellexalVR handles that separately by partitioning selected cells into four clusters for a slingshot analysis Expression data has not yet been converted to CellexalVR input files via the cellexalvrR package (as_cellexalvrR / export2cellexalvr) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies differentially expressed genes between user-defined cell groups with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (implemented in C++ for speed), adjusts p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and renders the top 250 marker genes as a hierarchically clustered heatmap — the in-session heatmap workflow of CellexalVR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Identifies differentially expressed genes between user-defined cell groups with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (implemented in C++ for speed), adjusts p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and renders the top 250 marker genes as a hierarchically clustered heatmap — the in-session heatmap workflow of CellexalVR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single cell group is defined — the two-group Wilcoxon rank-sum test requires at least two groups to compare The goal is pseudotime trajectory analysis rather than group comparison — CellexalVR handles that separately by partitioning selected cells into four clusters for a slingshot analysis Expression data has not yet been converted to CellexalVR input files via the cellexalvrR package (as_cellexalvrR / export2cellexalvr)

skills.description: Use when preparing raw single-cell Hi-C count data (e.g. oocyte vs zygote cells) for scHiCDiff DCI testing and you need to filter low-contact cells and restrict contacts to a short genomic distance range.
skills.name: single-cell-hic-cell-quality-control
skills.search_text: single-cell-hic-cell-quality-control Use when preparing raw single-cell Hi-C count data (e.g. oocyte vs zygote cells) for scHiCDiff DCI testing and you need to filter low-contact cells and restrict contacts to a short genomic distance range. Input is already a QC-filtered, normalized count.table ready for scHiCDiff detection functions — re-filtering could discard valid cells Analysis targets long-range (>10 Mb) chromatin contacts; the 0-10 Mb distance restriction would remove the bin pairs of interest Bulk Hi-C contact matrices are supplied rather than single-cell data; the >5000 contacts-per-cell threshold is defined for single-cell libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quality-control filter for single-cell Hi-C datasets prior to differential chromatin interaction (DCI) detection: retain only cells with sufficient contact counts and restrict bin pairs to a defined genomic distance range. Applied to the Flyamer 2017 mouse oocyte vs zygote scHi-C data before running scHiCDiff. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Quality-control filter for single-cell Hi-C datasets prior to differential chromatin interaction (DCI) detection: retain only cells with sufficient contact counts and restrict bin pairs to a defined genomic distance range. Applied to the Flyamer 2017 mouse oocyte vs zygote scHi-C data before running scHiCDiff.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a QC-filtered, normalized count.table ready for scHiCDiff detection functions — re-filtering could discard valid cells Analysis targets long-range (>10 Mb) chromatin contacts; the 0-10 Mb distance restriction would remove the bin pairs of interest Bulk Hi-C contact matrices are supplied rather than single-cell data; the >5000 contacts-per-cell threshold is defined for single-cell libraries

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) plus a two-level condition factor and need per-bin-pair differential interaction statistics and BH-adjusted p-values.
skills.name: single-cell-hic-count-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-hic-count-matrix-analysis Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) plus a two-level condition factor and need per-bin-pair differential interaction statistics and BH-adjusted p-values. Input is a raw, unnormalized N*N scHi-C contact matrix — run the scHiCDiff.norm normalization step (Gaussian convolution imputation + scHiCNorm NB-hurdle) first. Comparing bulk Hi-C experiments rather than single-cell Hi-C: the ZINB model is specifically designed for single-cell zero inflation, though NB remains the common bulk-Hi-C assumption. More than two conditions per comparison: the detection functions take a factor of exactly two conditions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) between two cell conditions from a normalized single-cell Hi-C count matrix using scHiCDiff's four tests (KS, CVM, NB, ZINB likelihood-ratio tests) and extract their common DCI set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad625
skills.summary: Detect differential chromatin interactions (DCIs) between two cell conditions from a normalized single-cell Hi-C count matrix using scHiCDiff's four tests (KS, CVM, NB, ZINB likelihood-ratio tests) and extract their common DCI set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw, unnormalized N*N scHi-C contact matrix — run the scHiCDiff.norm normalization step (Gaussian convolution imputation + scHiCNorm NB-hurdle) first. Comparing bulk Hi-C experiments rather than single-cell Hi-C: the ZINB model is specifically designed for single-cell zero inflation, though NB remains the common bulk-Hi-C assumption. More than two conditions per comparison: the detection functions take a factor of exactly two conditions.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data appears homogeneous under known covariates (e.g., a single cell type within patients) but unexplained heterogeneity — such as doublets, cell-cycle stage, or outlier cells — is suspected and PCA/tSNE fails to separate it.
skills.name: single-cell-hidden-factor-detection
skills.search_text: single-cell-hidden-factor-detection Use when scRNA-seq count data appears homogeneous under known covariates (e.g., a single cell type within patients) but unexplained heterogeneity — such as doublets, cell-cycle stage, or outlier cells — is suspected and PCA/tSNE fails to separate it. When all sources of unwanted variation are already known and fully captured by the design matrix covariates (patient identity, geometric library size) — plain regression or SVA suffices When the goal is cell-type assignment across a mixed population where PCA or ZINB-WaVe may suffice; IA-SVA is designed for hidden factors correlated with known covariates within seemingly homogeneous cells When expecting many unknown factors without a stringent SI cut-off strategy — the article warns the SI is not an empirical p-value and users must select a stringent cut-off in that setting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects hidden sources of variation in single-cell RNA-seq data that are correlated with known covariates, using Iteratively Adjusted Surrogate Variable Analysis (IA-SVA). Unlike SVA/USVA, IA-SVA iteratively identifies genes associated with each hidden factor and uses a permutation-based significance index to decide how many surrogate variables to retain. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: Detects hidden sources of variation in single-cell RNA-seq data that are correlated with known covariates, using Iteratively Adjusted Surrogate Variable Analysis (IA-SVA). Unlike SVA/USVA, IA-SVA iteratively identifies genes associated with each hidden factor and uses a permutation-based significance index to decide how many surrogate variables to retain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all sources of unwanted variation are already known and fully captured by the design matrix covariates (patient identity, geometric library size) — plain regression or SVA suffices When the goal is cell-type assignment across a mixed population where PCA or ZINB-WaVe may suffice; IA-SVA is designed for hidden factors correlated with known covariates within seemingly homogeneous cells When expecting many unknown factors without a stringent SI cut-off strategy — the article warns the SI is not an empirical p-value and users must select a stringent cut-off in that setting

skills.name: single-cell-hierarchical-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-hierarchical-clustering Use when a preprocessed, z-score transformed expression matrix of cell type-selective genes is available and cells must be assigned to major cell type clusters within the SINCERA pipeline. Input is a raw count matrix that has not been filtered for low-quality cells, low-expression genes, or z-score normalized — the clustering expects the preprocessed SINCERA matrix The analysis goal is downstream of cell type definition, e.g. cell type-specific signature gene analysis or driving-force identification — this skill only assigns clusters Genes lack a defined expression-specificity threshold (no cluster.geneSelection / specificity.thresholdSelection output) — clustering on non-selective genes degrades cell type separation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assigns single cells to initial clusters in the SINCERA pipeline via hierarchical clustering (average linkage with Pearson's correlation distance) on z-scored cell type-selective genes, with consensus, tight, and ward-linkage alternatives and permutation-based cluster significance testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/978-1-4939-7710-9_15
skills.summary: Assigns single cells to initial clusters in the SINCERA pipeline via hierarchical clustering (average linkage with Pearson's correlation distance) on z-scored cell type-selective genes, with consensus, tight, and ward-linkage alternatives and permutation-based cluster significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix that has not been filtered for low-quality cells, low-expression genes, or z-score normalized — the clustering expects the preprocessed SINCERA matrix The analysis goal is downstream of cell type definition, e.g. cell type-specific signature gene analysis or driving-force identification — this skill only assigns clusters Genes lack a defined expression-specificity threshold (no cluster.geneSelection / specificity.thresholdSelection output) — clustering on non-selective genes degrades cell type separation
