skills.name: single-cell-hierarchical-count-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-hierarchical-count-modeling Use when a sparse droplet-based scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells, integer counts) has multi-subject structure (e. Data are bulk RNA-seq with small sample sizes — NEBULA is designed for large-scale multi-subject single-cell hierarchies, and existing bulk tools suffice Counts are already normalized/non-integer values (nebula requires integer count matrices) Genes are lowly expressed or have estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 — co-expression analysis has little statistical power for low-expression genes and results should be removed or interpreted cautiously http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit gene-wise negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) to multi-subject single-cell counts, decomposing overdispersion into subject-level (sigma^2) and cell-level (phi^-1) components using NEBULA-LN or NEBULA-HL. This enables differential and co-expression testing on droplet-based scRNA-seq data with thousands of cells grouped into tens of subjects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Fit gene-wise negative binomial gamma mixed models (NBGMM) to multi-subject single-cell counts, decomposing overdispersion into subject-level (sigma^2) and cell-level (phi^-1) components using NEBULA-LN or NEBULA-HL. This enables differential and co-expression testing on droplet-based scRNA-seq data with thousands of cells grouped into tens of subjects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq with small sample sizes — NEBULA is designed for large-scale multi-subject single-cell hierarchies, and existing bulk tools suffice Counts are already normalized/non-integer values (nebula requires integer count matrices) Genes are lowly expressed or have estimated cell-level overdispersion > 100 — co-expression analysis has little statistical power for low-expression genes and results should be removed or interpreted cautiously

skills.description: Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets must be merged into a single hierarchical cell-population tree, especially when annotations differ in resolution (e.g., AMB2016 vs AMB2018 visual cortex) and new populations may need to be discovered.
skills.name: single-cell-hierarchy-progressive-learning
skills.search_text: single-cell-hierarchy-progressive-learning Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets must be merged into a single hierarchical cell-population tree, especially when annotations differ in resolution (e.g., AMB2016 vs AMB2018 visual cortex) and new populations may need to be discovered. Datasets are not batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL explicitly is not a batch correction tool and advises aligning datasets before matching populations Cell populations do not follow a tree-structured relationship, e.g. dedifferentiation states like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes You only need flat cell-type label transfer from a fixed atlas without hierarchy learning or discovery of new populations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reconstruct and continuously update a hierarchical classification tree of cell populations across annotated scRNA-seq datasets using scHPL, which automatically matches populations across datasets, detects new subpopulations via one-class rejection, and trains a linear SVM, kNN, or one-class SVM at each node. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Reconstruct and continuously update a hierarchical classification tree of cell populations across annotated scRNA-seq datasets using scHPL, which automatically matches populations across datasets, detects new subpopulations via one-class rejection, and trains a linear SVM, kNN, or one-class SVM at each node.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not batch-corrected/aligned — scHPL explicitly is not a batch correction tool and advises aligning datasets before matching populations Cell populations do not follow a tree-structured relationship, e.g. dedifferentiation states like beta-to-alpha cell conversions in type 2 diabetes You only need flat cell-type label transfer from a fixed atlas without hierarchy learning or discovery of new populations

skills.description: Use when you have a cell hashing HTO count matrix (e.g. an 8-hashtag dataset such as Stoeckius-2018 GSE108313) and need to assign singlets, doublets and negatives per cell before comparing demultiplexing methods.
skills.name: single-cell-hto-count-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-hto-count-matrix-processing Use when you have a cell hashing HTO count matrix (e.g. an 8-hashtag dataset such as Stoeckius-2018 GSE108313) and need to assign singlets, doublets and negatives per cell before comparing demultiplexing methods. The samples lack a distinct genetic background or are the same donors across timepoints and you rely solely on SNP-based demultiplexing (e.g. demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo) — use hashing instead, or the hybrid strategy only if hashing is available. The input is already a cell×sample label table or post-demultiplexing output rather than a raw HTO count matrix — this skill operates on raw hashtag counts in a Seurat object. The dataset contains no hashtag/HTO assay (e.g. genetic demultiplexing-only experiments) — HTOreader's HTOClassification requires an HTO assay in the Seurat object. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Process single-cell HTO (hashtag oligo) count matrices for cell hashing demultiplexing by loading the HTO assay into a Seurat object and running HTOreader's HTOClassification with CLR (or log) normalization to assign per-cell hashtag identities. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae254
skills.summary: Process single-cell HTO (hashtag oligo) count matrices for cell hashing demultiplexing by loading the HTO assay into a Seurat object and running HTOreader's HTOClassification with CLR (or log) normalization to assign per-cell hashtag identities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The samples lack a distinct genetic background or are the same donors across timepoints and you rely solely on SNP-based demultiplexing (e.g. demuxlet, scSplit, Vireo) — use hashing instead, or the hybrid strategy only if hashing is available. The input is already a cell×sample label table or post-demultiplexing output rather than a raw HTO count matrix — this skill operates on raw hashtag counts in a Seurat object. The dataset contains no hashtag/HTO assay (e.g. genetic demultiplexing-only experiments) — HTOreader's HTOClassification requires an HTO assay in the Seurat object.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a reprogramming or fate-conversion experiment must be scored per cell for source (fibroblast) versus target (iEP) identity to compare conditions, e.g. testing whether adding Fos/Yap1 to a cocktail increases target identity scores.
skills.name: single-cell-identity-scoring-against-reference-profiles
skills.search_text: single-cell-identity-scoring-against-reference-profiles Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a reprogramming or fate-conversion experiment must be scored per cell for source (fibroblast) versus target (iEP) identity to compare conditions, e.g. testing whether adding Fos/Yap1 to a cocktail increases target identity scores. The data are not single-cell gene expression profiles, e.g. bulk RNA-seq or GRN edge lists — Capybara QP classification requires a genes x cells matrix The goal is to simulate perturbation effects on identity rather than score observed identity; use CellOracle's in silico KO/overexpression simulation instead No annotated reference profiles exist for the source and target cell states, so fibroblast/iEP scores cannot be anchored http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores individual cells for fibroblast versus induced endoderm progenitor (iEP) identity by classifying them against reference transcriptomic profiles with Capybara's quadratic-programming-based cell type classification, enabling quantitative comparison of identity across reprogramming cocktails (e.g. Hnf4α-Foxa1 with or without Fos/Yap1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Scores individual cells for fibroblast versus induced endoderm progenitor (iEP) identity by classifying them against reference transcriptomic profiles with Capybara's quadratic-programming-based cell type classification, enabling quantitative comparison of identity across reprogramming cocktails (e.g. Hnf4α-Foxa1 with or without Fos/Yap1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not single-cell gene expression profiles, e.g. bulk RNA-seq or GRN edge lists — Capybara QP classification requires a genes x cells matrix The goal is to simulate perturbation effects on identity rather than score observed identity; use CellOracle's in silico KO/overexpression simulation instead No annotated reference profiles exist for the source and target cell states, so fibroblast/iEP scores cannot be anchored

skills.description: Use when single-cell VDJ-seq data (SingleCellExperiment with TCR information) must be pseudobulked into a VDJ feature space of V/D/J gene usage counts per miloR neighbourhood for downstream trajectory analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-immune-repertoire-object-manipulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-immune-repertoire-object-manipulation Use when single-cell VDJ-seq data (SingleCellExperiment with TCR information) must be pseudobulked into a VDJ feature space of V/D/J gene usage counts per miloR neighbourhood for downstream trajectory analysis. Input is already a normalized feature table or pseudobulk matrix rather than a cell-level SingleCellExperiment/milo object with VDJ annotations The dataset lacks paired single-cell VDJ sequencing (e.g. Baccin et al./Bandyopadhyay et al. lack BCR sequencing) or has too few cells for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells) The target trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains downstream of the feature space http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Constructs and manipulates pseudobulked VDJ feature spaces in R by combining dandelionR, miloR, and SingleCellExperiment objects, converting single-cell immune receptor data into a continuous V/D/J gene-usage matrix suitable for trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Constructs and manipulates pseudobulked VDJ feature spaces in R by combining dandelionR, miloR, and SingleCellExperiment objects, converting single-cell immune receptor data into a continuous V/D/J gene-usage matrix suitable for trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized feature table or pseudobulk matrix rather than a cell-level SingleCellExperiment/milo object with VDJ annotations The dataset lacks paired single-cell VDJ sequencing (e.g. Baccin et al./Bandyopadhyay et al. lack BCR sequencing) or has too few cells for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. only 972 healthy B cells) The target trajectory is cyclic (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains downstream of the feature space

skills.description: Use when you need to compare scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising methods quantitatively — e.g. simulated counts with known true values and group labels across noise types such as dropout, uniform, Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, negative binomial.
skills.name: single-cell-imputation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-imputation-benchmarking Use when you need to compare scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising methods quantitatively — e.g. simulated counts with known true values and group labels across noise types such as dropout, uniform, Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, negative binomial. Input is real scRNA-Seq data with no simulated truth counts or known group labels — MSE against true values and ASW recovery of known labels cannot be computed Input is a single noise type only (e.g. dropouts alone) when the goal is to test distribution-agnostic cleaning across uniform, Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, and negative binomial noise The matrix is not a gene x cell count matrix from a scRNA-Seq experiment (e.g. bulk RNA-Seq or precomputed feature tables) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation methods by simulating noisy count matrices with Splatter, imputing them with AutoClassImpute and controls (DCA, MAGIC, scImpute, SAVER), and quantifying recovery via MSE against true counts and average silhouette width (ASW) against known group labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation methods by simulating noisy count matrices with Splatter, imputing them with AutoClassImpute and controls (DCA, MAGIC, scImpute, SAVER), and quantifying recovery via MSE against true counts and average silhouette width (ASW) against known group labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-Seq data with no simulated truth counts or known group labels — MSE against true values and ASW recovery of known labels cannot be computed Input is a single noise type only (e.g. dropouts alone) when the goal is to test distribution-agnostic cleaning across uniform, Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, and negative binomial noise The matrix is not a gene x cell count matrix from a scRNA-Seq experiment (e.g. bulk RNA-Seq or precomputed feature tables)

skills.summary: Benchmark how well five single-cell data integration methods (Supervised Harmony, Harmony, Seurat RPCA, Scanorama, Limma) mix batches and donors while conserving AUCell-derived cell types on HSPC data, using iLISI/cLISI scores and kBET acceptance rates computed inside SingCellaR.

skills.description: Use when input is a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell count matrix (e.g., sparse dgCMatrix) with sample/condition covariates, and you need an integrated latent embedding plus cluster-free DE or sample-variability deconvolution across conditions.
skills.name: single-cell-integration-latent-embedding-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-integration-latent-embedding-modeling Use when input is a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell count matrix (e.g., sparse dgCMatrix) with sample/condition covariates, and you need an integrated latent embedding plus cluster-free DE or sample-variability deconvolution across conditions. The manifold structure of interest is strongly non-linear — GEDI currently supports only linear manifold learning, with an optional hyperellipsoid restriction, and other parametric manifolds are future extensions. You only need standard pseudobulk DE per pre-defined cell type/cluster — a sequential normalization + integration + DESeq2 pseudobulk workflow suffices and the unified model is unnecessary. You need validated single-cell imputation specifically — GEDI's gene-level imputations have not been benchmarked against existing imputation methods. Fit GEDI, a Bayesian generative model, to multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell count matrices to jointly perform normalization, denoising, inter-sample harmonization, and interpretable latent embedding that supports cluster-free differential gene expression. It replaces sequential normalization-then-integration-then-DGE workflows that ignore the interplay between integration and differential expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50963-0
skills.summary: Fit GEDI, a Bayesian generative model, to multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell count matrices to jointly perform normalization, denoising, inter-sample harmonization, and interpretable latent embedding that supports cluster-free differential gene expression. It replaces sequential normalization-then-integration-then-DGE workflows that ignore the interplay between integration and differential expression.

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing how STACAS weights integration anchors and derives the guide tree that orders dataset integration, or when validating an independent implementation against Run.STACAS defaults.
skills.name: single-cell-integration-reproducibility-validation
skills.search_text: single-cell-integration-reproducibility-validation Use when reproducing or auditing how STACAS weights integration anchors and derives the guide tree that orders dataset integration, or when validating an independent implementation against Run.STACAS defaults. Input data lacks prior cell type annotations and the goal is fully unsupervised integration — STACAS's semi-supervised label-confidence filtering of anchors is central to this skill The task is only evaluating integration quality (e.g., computing CiLISI/ASW with scIntegrationMetrics) rather than reconstructing the anchor weighting and tree logic itself Datasets are technical replicates where simple unsupervised methods (Harmony, FastMNN) suffice and anchor-based semi-supervised correction adds unnecessary label dependence http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Reconstructs and validates STACAS's anchor scoring and integration guide tree: anchors are weighted from pairwise rPCA distances via a logistic score, combined with SNN scores (alpha = 0.8), filtered by label confidence, and summed into dataset-pair similarities that yield a ward.D2 hierarchical tree determining integration order. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Reconstructs and validates STACAS's anchor scoring and integration guide tree: anchors are weighted from pairwise rPCA distances via a logistic score, combined with SNN scores (alpha = 0.8), filtered by label confidence, and summed into dataset-pair similarities that yield a ward.D2 hierarchical tree determining integration order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks prior cell type annotations and the goal is fully unsupervised integration — STACAS's semi-supervised label-confidence filtering of anchors is central to this skill The task is only evaluating integration quality (e.g., computing CiLISI/ASW with scIntegrationMetrics) rather than reconstructing the anchor weighting and tree logic itself Datasets are technical replicates where simple unsupervised methods (Harmony, FastMNN) suffice and anchor-based semi-supervised correction adds unnecessary label dependence

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data across multiple batches has been fitted with BUSseq and you need the gene set that differentiates the discovered cell types at a controlled Bayesian FDR cutoff.
skills.name: single-cell-intrinsic-gene-detection
skills.search_text: single-cell-intrinsic-gene-detection Use when scRNA-seq count data across multiple batches has been fitted with BUSseq and you need the gene set that differentiates the discovered cell types at a controlled Bayesian FDR cutoff. The data has not been fitted with BUSseq (no posterior spike-and-slab indicator estimates exist) — differential expression methods for pre-normalized or bulk data like ComBat/SVA are a different setting The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g. batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4), where no method, including BUSseq, is applicable The goal is batch-effect-corrected expression matrices rather than gene selection — use corrected_read_counts() or imputed_read_counts() instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies intrinsic (differentially expressed) genes that differentiate cell types from a fitted BUSseq Bayesian hierarchical model, using the posterior indicator probabilities of the spike-and-slab prior on cell-type effects and controlling the Bayesian FDR (alpha = 0.05). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Identifies intrinsic (differentially expressed) genes that differentiate cell types from a fitted BUSseq Bayesian hierarchical model, using the posterior indicator probabilities of the spike-and-slab prior on cell-type effects and controlling the Bayesian FDR (alpha = 0.05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data has not been fitted with BUSseq (no posterior spike-and-slab indicator estimates exist) — differential expression methods for pre-normalized or bulk data like ComBat/SVA are a different setting The experimental design is completely confounded (e.g. batch 1 measures cell types 1 and 2, batch 2 measures cell types 3 and 4), where no method, including BUSseq, is applicable The goal is batch-effect-corrected expression matrices rather than gene selection — use corrected_read_counts() or imputed_read_counts() instead

skills.search_text: single-cell-junction-matrix-quality-filtering Use when a raw junction reads matrix (junc_matrix.csv / junc_mat.npy) has been integrated LeafCutter-style from single-cell SMART-seq BAM or SJ.out.tab files and must be quality-filtered before AS event grouping and probability computation. Input is already a quality-filtered AS probability matrix or a dense gene expression matrix rather than a raw junction reads matrix Bulk RNA-seq junction data intended for Leafcutter differential splicing analysis with known sample groups — SCASL's QC thresholds target sparse single-cell SMART-seq matrices AS analysis requiring known cell labels for differential splicing (e.g., BRIE, rMATS, MARVEL workflows), since this stage serves unsupervised SCASL clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 QC stage of the SCASL pipeline that filters the single-cell junction reads matrix (sites x cells) by expression support — minimum expressing cells per site and minimum expressing sites per cell — before grouping junctions into 5'/3' AS events and computing the AS probability matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: QC stage of the SCASL pipeline that filters the single-cell junction reads matrix (sites x cells) by expression support — minimum expressing cells per site and minimum expressing sites per cell — before grouping junctions into 5'/3' AS events and computing the AS probability matrix.

skills.description: Use when you have a wide-format normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with a PCA-reduced representation and need unbiased cell clustering, optimal-k selection, and cluster-pair differential expression ranking.
skills.name: single-cell-kmeans-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-kmeans-clustering Use when you have a wide-format normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with a PCA-reduced representation and need unbiased cell clustering, optimal-k selection, and cluster-pair differential expression ranking. Input is raw count data that has not passed scSPARKL's QC/filtering (percent_ercc > 10%, percent_mito > 5%, cells expressing < 10 genes, genes expressed in < 3 cells, dropout rate > 70%) and normalization You expect many non-convex or highly irregular clusters that K-means cannot capture You need multi-omics integration (CITE-seq, scATAC-seq, scBS-seq) — such Spark-based pipelines are not yet developed per the paper's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_3306 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 K-means clustering of PCA-reduced normalized single-cell expression data, with k selected via elbow (within-cluster sum of squares) and silhouette score analysis, followed by per-cluster-pair two-sample t-test DGE ranking. Grounded in scSPARKL's Spark/Parquet pipeline, which achieved ARI ≈ 0.90 on the Jurkat–293T cell mixture. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: K-means clustering of PCA-reduced normalized single-cell expression data, with k selected via elbow (within-cluster sum of squares) and silhouette score analysis, followed by per-cluster-pair two-sample t-test DGE ranking. Grounded in scSPARKL's Spark/Parquet pipeline, which achieved ARI ≈ 0.90 on the Jurkat–293T cell mixture.

skills.search_text: single-cell-knn-graph-clustering Use when quality-filtered 10X scRNA-seq data (matrix.mtx, gene.tsv, barcode.tsv) with selected PCs needs high-resolution T cell cluster discovery, and cluster assignments must be validated against a shuffled-data null to avoid spurious clusters. skills.name: single-cell-label-mapping-across-datasets
skills.search_text: single-cell-label-mapping-across-datasets Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset lacks cell labels but a reference dataset with known clusters exists, especially when batch effect or strong imbalance in cell numbers/library sizes makes integration-based or biomarker-based mapping unreliable. Neither the reference nor the target data is well clustered or contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types' in that case Input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID requires library-depth (TPM/CPM) normalized, not log-transformed, data There is no labeled reference dataset with known clusters to map against http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Map cells in an unannotated target scRNA-seq dataset to clusters of a labeled reference dataset using scID, a Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework that scores target cells on weighted cluster-specific gene signatures and assigns them via a finite mixture of Gaussians, robust to batch effect. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914

skills.description: Use when the task is cell-type clustering on raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. datasets like 'Adam') where deep-autoencoder latent representations must be learned and converted into consensus cell-type partitions evaluated by NMI/ARI.
skills.name: single-cell-latent-embedding-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-latent-embedding-clustering Use when the task is cell-type clustering on raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. datasets like 'Adam') where deep-autoencoder latent representations must be learned and converted into consensus cell-type partitions evaluated by NMI/ARI. The input is not single-cell transcriptome data or the goal is not cell-type clustering — scBGEDA is designed for scRNA-seq cell-type identification, not bulk RNA-seq or general feature tables. A single fixed clustering (rather than a graph-based consensus partition from an ensemble of basic clusterings) is required — BGEC.m is specifically a consensus/ensemble function. The task requires downstream marker-gene or functional genomic analysis without clustering — those are separate capabilities requiring the trained model's gene-influence quantification. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Clusters scRNA-seq cell types by first learning a compressed latent embedding with a single-cell dual denoising autoencoder (ZINB + denoising reconstruction loss), then deriving a consensus partition from that latent space via bipartite graph ensemble clustering (scBGEDA). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad075
skills.summary: Clusters scRNA-seq cell types by first learning a compressed latent embedding with a single-cell dual denoising autoencoder (ZINB + denoising reconstruction loss), then deriving a consensus partition from that latent space via bipartite graph ensemble clustering (scBGEDA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not single-cell transcriptome data or the goal is not cell-type clustering — scBGEDA is designed for scRNA-seq cell-type identification, not bulk RNA-seq or general feature tables. A single fixed clustering (rather than a graph-based consensus partition from an ensemble of basic clusterings) is required — BGEC.m is specifically a consensus/ensemble function. The task requires downstream marker-gene or functional genomic analysis without clustering — those are separate capabilities requiring the trained model's gene-influence quantification.

skills.name: single-cell-latent-representation-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-latent-representation-scoring Use when a source-free transfer learning pipeline needs per-cell uncertainty for target scRNA-seq cells from classifier outputs, e.g. to feed bimodality tests for novel cell-type detection in scEMAIL. The source model has not been trained yet — the score depends on the main classifier plus the two auxiliary classifiers taking features from h of the pre-trained source model You need hard cell-type labels rather than an uncertainty signal — E-scores only measure certainty and must be followed by bimodality tests and a manifold-mixup threshold to actually partition cells Raw source data are available and you can align features explicitly — the source-free E-score design targets the setting where source data are inaccessible during adaptation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes a per-cell expert-ensemble E-score from the soft probability vectors of a pre-trained source model's main classifier and two auxiliary classifiers over target-cell latent representations (z_it), combining normalized entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) to quantify how certain each target cell belongs to a known cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Computes a per-cell expert-ensemble E-score from the soft probability vectors of a pre-trained source model's main classifier and two auxiliary classifiers over target-cell latent representations (z_it), combining normalized entropy (EN), confidence (CF), and consistency (CS) to quantify how certain each target cell belongs to a known cell type.

skills.name: single-cell-latent-space-embedding
skills.search_text: single-cell-latent-space-embedding Use when you have a normalized single-cell transcriptomic dataset (Scanpy AnnData) plus prior biological knowledge in GMT format and want each latent dimension to correspond to a named gene module rather than an opaque factor. Raw (unnormalized) count data — VEGA was shown handling normalized expression profiles, and count support (e.g. via scVI-style likelihoods) was only discussed as a future direction When no prior gene module annotations are available or the existing annotation (e.g. MSigDB) is known to be incomplete or not context-specific, since the hard-coded decoder connections cannot correct wrong priors When strong generative/predictive performance is the primary goal rather than interpretability — VEGA's single-layer sparse decoder sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Embed a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq dataset into an interpretable latent space using VEGA, a VAE whose sparse linear decoder is wired one-to-one to user-provided gene module variables (GMVs) such as pathways, gene regulatory networks, or transcription factors, so each latent dimension maps directly to biological activity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0

skills.search_text: single-cell-ld-axes-visualization Use when cells from an unseen condition or subset must be visualized on axes learned from labeled training cells (e.g., projecting CD57high T cells onto CD57low-trained LD axes over day0–day5 TCR stimulation) to compare progression states. Class labels are unknown or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — the article states 'This supervised approach is inappropriate in situations in which labels are unknown, or in which an unbiased view of the data is preferable.' The biology is expected to be non-linear along the labeled classes — LDA 'does not capture non-linear relationships, which may limit its performance on some datasets.' There is large within-class heterogeneity or very many populations (e.g., heterogeneous PBMCs labeled by time point) — 'HSS-LDA may not perform well in situations in which a large degree of heterogeneity exists within a given class' and 'performance will suffer with an increasing number of populations.' http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Projects single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers) onto linear discriminant (LD) axes trained on labeled reference cells — using MASS::lda() or hsslda model scaling coefficients plus makeAxes() — to visualize unseen populations (such as CD57high senescent T cells) in the coordinate system of a training population (CD57low T cells) across experimental time points. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Projects single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers) onto linear discriminant (LD) axes trained on labeled reference cells — using MASS::lda() or hsslda model scaling coefficients plus makeAxes() — to visualize unseen populations (such as CD57high senescent T cells) in the coordinate system of a training population (CD57low T cells) across experimental time points.

skills.description: Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., iasva_counts_test.Rds) and you need to decide which principal components or library-size covariates capture technical depth variation before surrogate-variable analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-library-size-calculation
skills.search_text: single-cell-library-size-calculation Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., iasva_counts_test.Rds) and you need to decide which principal components or library-size covariates capture technical depth variation before surrogate-variable analysis. Input is already normalized/size-factor-corrected expression (e.g., SCnorm- or SCRAN-normalized values), where colSums(log(counts+1)) no longer represents sequencing depth Analysis goal is to detect hidden biological factors rather than to quantify/adjust for library-size-driven technical variation The matrix is too sparse/small for a meaningful PCA (e.g., lowly expressed genes retained without applying expression filters) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute the geometric library size (colSums of log-transformed counts) for a scRNA-seq cell matrix and quantify how strongly it dominates variability by correlating it with the first principal component (PC1) of the log-transformed matrix. In the IA-SVA workflow this established that PC1 on 101 Lawlor alpha cells was essentially library size (r = 0.99), justifying geometric library size as a known covariate. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-35365-9
skills.summary: Compute the geometric library size (colSums of log-transformed counts) for a scRNA-seq cell matrix and quantify how strongly it dominates variability by correlating it with the first principal component (PC1) of the log-transformed matrix. In the IA-SVA workflow this established that PC1 on 101 Lawlor alpha cells was essentially library size (r = 0.99), justifying geometric library size as a known covariate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/size-factor-corrected expression (e.g., SCnorm- or SCRAN-normalized values), where colSums(log(counts+1)) no longer represents sequencing depth Analysis goal is to detect hidden biological factors rather than to quantify/adjust for library-size-driven technical variation The matrix is too sparse/small for a meaningful PCA (e.g., lowly expressed genes retained without applying expression filters)

skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell lineage barcode (character matrix) and scRNA-seq expression data with per-cell type labels, and need to reconstruct and biologically validate a cell lineage tree by comparing barcode-defined subtrees against transcriptomic cell types.
skills.name: single-cell-lineage-barcode-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-lineage-barcode-analysis Use when you have paired single-cell lineage barcode (character matrix) and scRNA-seq expression data with per-cell type labels, and need to reconstruct and biologically validate a cell lineage tree by comparing barcode-defined subtrees against transcriptomic cell types. Lineage and expression data are unpaired (barcodes from different cells than the scRNA-seq profiles), since LinRace's asymmetric division model requires joint paired data The biological system has largely reversible cell state transitions, which LinRace's irreversible-transition assumption does not model The goal is de novo cell type annotation rather than lineage validation — this skill assumes cell type labels already exist Reconstruct a cell division tree from paired lineage barcode and gene expression data with LinRace, then validate it by cutting the tree at a fixed depth and tabulating annotated cell-type composition within each subtree. Partial mixing of cell types across subtrees indicates consistency between transcriptome similarity and barcode similarity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44173-3
skills.summary: Reconstruct a cell division tree from paired lineage barcode and gene expression data with LinRace, then validate it by cutting the tree at a fixed depth and tabulating annotated cell-type composition within each subtree. Partial mixing of cell types across subtrees indicates consistency between transcriptome similarity and barcode similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lineage and expression data are unpaired (barcodes from different cells than the scRNA-seq profiles), since LinRace's asymmetric division model requires joint paired data The biological system has largely reversible cell state transitions, which LinRace's irreversible-transition assumption does not model The goal is de novo cell type annotation rather than lineage validation — this skill assumes cell type labels already exist

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny (Newick/phylo object with cells as leaves) and need to group cells into a target number of clade-coherent subpopulations, e.g. to define tumor subclones or lineage labels for signature-scoring.
skills.name: single-cell-lineage-cluster-assignment
skills.search_text: single-cell-lineage-cluster-assignment Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny (Newick/phylo object with cells as leaves) and need to group cells into a target number of clade-coherent subpopulations, e.g. to define tumor subclones or lineage labels for signature-scoring. The input is a flat expression matrix or annotation table with no phylogenetic tree — clustering must instead use expression-based methods (e.g. UMAP/Hotspot modules) Clusters need not correspond to connected clades (e.g. purely transcriptional communities) — cophenetic merging will force lineage-coherent groups The tree has unresolved unifurcations and you cannot preprocess it — the algorithm assumes every internal node branches properly after collapse.singles http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Partition the tip cells of a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny into a fixed number of phylogenetically coherent subpopulation clusters using PhyloVision's Cluster-Phylogeny algorithm, a breadth-first search over internal nodes with cophenetic-distance-based merging. This yields a leaf-to-cluster assignment (VISION_Clusters_Tree) usable as lineage-aware metadata in downstream VISION/Hotspot analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Partition the tip cells of a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny into a fixed number of phylogenetically coherent subpopulation clusters using PhyloVision's Cluster-Phylogeny algorithm, a breadth-first search over internal nodes with cophenetic-distance-based merging. This yields a leaf-to-cluster assignment (VISION_Clusters_Tree) usable as lineage-aware metadata in downstream VISION/Hotspot analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a flat expression matrix or annotation table with no phylogenetic tree — clustering must instead use expression-based methods (e.g. UMAP/Hotspot modules) Clusters need not correspond to connected clades (e.g. purely transcriptional communities) — cophenetic merging will force lineage-coherent groups The tree has unresolved unifurcations and you cannot preprocess it — the algorithm assumes every internal node branches properly after collapse.singles

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential trajectory-topology or cell-proportion tests on multi-sample scRNA-seq data by artificially removing cells from a known lineage and checking false positive rate at 0% removal and power as removal increases.
skills.name: single-cell-lineage-subsampling-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-lineage-subsampling-simulation Use when benchmarking differential trajectory-topology or cell-proportion tests on multi-sample scRNA-seq data by artificially removing cells from a known lineage and checking false positive rate at 0% removal and power as removal increases. The analysis goal is detecting differential gene expression or cell density along pseudotime rather than topology/cell-proportion changes driven by lineage composition shifts. The trajectory is built with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these trajectory types (default is TSCAN). Only a single sample per condition is available, since the differential tests rely on cross-sample variability with multiple replicates. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Simulate lineage composition changes in multi-sample scRNA-seq data by subsampling a target lineage (e.g., myeloid cells) at graded removal percentages (0%–80%) across all or a subset of samples, then use Lamian's differential topology tests to benchmark type I error control and statistical power. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-42841-y
skills.summary: Simulate lineage composition changes in multi-sample scRNA-seq data by subsampling a target lineage (e.g., myeloid cells) at graded removal percentages (0%–80%) across all or a subset of samples, then use Lamian's differential topology tests to benchmark type I error control and statistical power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is detecting differential gene expression or cell density along pseudotime rather than topology/cell-proportion changes driven by lineage composition shifts. The trajectory is built with Monocle2, Monocle3, or Slingshot — Lamian modules 1 and 2 do not support these trajectory types (default is TSCAN). Only a single sample per condition is available, since the differential tests rely on cross-sample variability with multiple replicates.

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices must be transformed to a common sequencing-depth scale via log(1 + scaled expression) — e.g., for exploratory visualization, marker plots, or when reproducing benchmarks of how downstream co-expression estimators behave on log-normalized data.
skills.name: single-cell-log-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-log-normalization Use when raw UMI count matrices must be transformed to a common sequencing-depth scale via log(1 + scaled expression) — e.g., for exploratory visualization, marker plots, or when reproducing benchmarks of how downstream co-expression estimators behave on log-normalized data. When the downstream goal is statistically justified cell-type-specific co-expression inference — the article shows log-normalized correlations (e.g., locCSN = 0.61, propr = 0.50 for an independent pair) are inflated false positives; use CS-CORE on raw UMI counts instead When the measurement model should account for count distribution assumptions beyond Poisson — the article defers negative-binomial adaptations to future work, so log-normalization does not substitute for a count-level model http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transforms scRNA-seq UMI counts into log-normalized values, log(1 + scaled expression), where scaled expression is raw counts multiplied by sequencing-depth scale factors. In this paper's evaluations, applying co-expression methods (locCSN, Pearson, propr, Spearman, SpQN) on such log-normalized counts inflated false-positive co-expression even for truly independent gene pairs, motivating CS-CORE's model-based alternative. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40503-7
skills.summary: Transforms scRNA-seq UMI counts into log-normalized values, log(1 + scaled expression), where scaled expression is raw counts multiplied by sequencing-depth scale factors. In this paper's evaluations, applying co-expression methods (locCSN, Pearson, propr, Spearman, SpQN) on such log-normalized counts inflated false-positive co-expression even for truly independent gene pairs, motivating CS-CORE's model-based alternative.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the downstream goal is statistically justified cell-type-specific co-expression inference — the article shows log-normalized correlations (e.g., locCSN = 0.61, propr = 0.50 for an independent pair) are inflated false positives; use CS-CORE on raw UMI counts instead When the measurement model should account for count distribution assumptions beyond Poisson — the article defers negative-binomial adaptations to future work, so log-normalization does not substitute for a count-level model

skills.search_text: single-cell-log-normalization-preprocessing Use when preparing a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix (rows=cells, columns=genes, CSV/JLD2 from 10x data) for RMT-based signal/noise separation, where raw log normalization would inflate detected signals (e.g., 84 vs 42 signals on ZhengMix) due to non-uniform cell vector lengths. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized (e.g., Pearson residuals or count-based factor analysis outputs) — the paper notes these alternatives underperform relative to corrected log normalization and double-normalizing distorts signals The goal is feature selection of highly variable genes or zero imputation — the paper warns high-variance gene selection can compromise local structure in low-variance genes and imputation can bias data and generate false signals Data is not sparse single-cell count data — the preprocessing thresholds (200 genes/cell, 15 cells/gene) are tuned for scRNA-seq sparsity

skills.search_text: single-cell-log2-tpm-preprocessing Use when raw unsynchronized scRNA-seq expression (e.g. TPM values in ola_mES_2i.RData or youngMpp .RData) must be converted to log2(TPM+1) and restricted to the cycle base genes to build reCAT's standard test_exp input. skills.summary: reCAT's first-stage data preparation: transform unsynchronized single-cell expression values to log2(TPM+1) and filter to the cycle base genes so the matrix becomes the standard test_exp input for downstream get_ordIndex/get_score steps.

The analysis goal requires data-driven (semi-supervised) selection of cell cycle genes from the data rather than the preselected 378-gene set, which the authors themselves flag as a limitation. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential isoform expression at the whole-transcript level — the article reports 'Isoform tests for DIE show better performance than exon tests', so IsoQuant with typeOfTest='Iso' is preferred when isoform assignments are available When reads are short-read-only and not full-length spliced long reads, since inclusion/exclusion counts per cell require long-read exon traversals When cell-type labels are absent — ExonQuant groups by a groupingFactor (e.g. 'Celltype') that must already exist in the AllInfo file

skills.search_text: single-cell-long-read-splicing-analysis Use when long-read FASTQs (PacBio/ONT) from single cells assigned to cell types must be converted into a cell-type-specific alternative splicing/DIE analysis, or when bulk DIE events must be traced to one vs. multiple cell types. skills.description: Use when you have Hotspot-identified heritable gene modules (e.g., from phylogenetically autocorrelated genes in a lineage-traced tumor clone) and need a per-cell score for each module to overlay on phylogeny or expression projections.
skills.name: single-cell-module-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-module-scoring Use when you have Hotspot-identified heritable gene modules (e.g., from phylogenetically autocorrelated genes in a lineage-traced tumor clone) and need a per-cell score for each module to overlay on phylogeny or expression projections. Modules are user-defined signatures rather than de novo Hotspot modules — then plain VISION signature scoring without the Hotspot de novo module step is appropriate No cell similarity structure (phylogeny, spatial metric, or latent space) is available — Hotspot module identification underlying the scores cannot be computed Input expression is raw counts without library-size normalization for the scoring step http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Computes per-cell gene module scores for de novo Hotspot gene modules (learned from the intersection of phylogeny and expression data) using the signature-scoring procedure in VISION, so heritable expression programs can be visualized across cells in the PhyloVision report. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Computes per-cell gene module scores for de novo Hotspot gene modules (learned from the intersection of phylogeny and expression data) using the signature-scoring procedure in VISION, so heritable expression programs can be visualized across cells in the PhyloVision report.

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix and defined gene signatures (meta-modules or cell-cycle sets) and need per-cell module scores plus dominant-module calls to annotate clusters from an unsupervised clustering such as RCC.

skills.search_text: single-cell-module-scoring-ssgsea Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix and defined gene signatures (meta-modules or cell-cycle sets) and need per-cell module scores plus dominant-module calls to annotate clusters from an unsupervised clustering such as RCC. Input is bulk transcriptomic data where subtype discovery (rather than per-cell module scoring) is the goal — use RCC directly for bulk subtyping No predefined gene signatures are available — ssGSEA requires curated gene sets and cannot de novo discover cellular-state modules http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score every single cell against curated gene-set signatures (e.g. the six Neftel GBM meta-modules MES1/MES2/AC/OPC/NPC1/NPC2 plus G1S/G2M cell-cycle signatures) using ssGSEA, then assign each cell its dominant module and aggregate scores per cluster to annotate clusters biologically. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Score every single cell against curated gene-set signatures (e.g. the six Neftel GBM meta-modules MES1/MES2/AC/OPC/NPC1/NPC2 plus G1S/G2M cell-cycle signatures) using ssGSEA, then assign each cell its dominant module and aggregate scores per cluster to annotate clusters biologically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk transcriptomic data where subtype discovery (rather than per-cell module scoring) is the goal — use RCC directly for bulk subtyping No predefined gene signatures are available — ssGSEA requires curated gene sets and cannot de novo discover cellular-state modules

skills.description: Use when a dataset contains multiple single-cell batches that jointly profile different subsets of modalities (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, CITE-seq protein, chromVAR motifs), especially with unequal cell-type composition across batches.
skills.name: single-cell-mosaic-multiomics-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-mosaic-multiomics-integration Use when a dataset contains multiple single-cell batches that jointly profile different subsets of modalities (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, CITE-seq protein, chromVAR motifs), especially with unequal cell-type composition across batches. All batches jointly profile the same set of modalities (horizontal/diagonal/vertical integration only) — methods like LIGER, Seurat v3/v4, MultiVI, CoupleNMF, MMD-MA, scDART, or MultiMAP may be more appropriate Input consists of feature/bio-marker tables rather than raw per-cell count matrices that need to be stored in the counts dictionary format One jointly profiled batch already bridges all modalities and dictionary-learning bridge integration suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrate arbitrary numbers of single-cell multi-omics batches under the mosaic scenario (each batch profiles a different subset of modalities) using matrix tri-factorization with scMoMaT, producing a unified cell-factor embedding and cluster-specific multi-modal bio-markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36066-2

skills.when_to_use_negative: All batches jointly profile the same set of modalities (horizontal/diagonal/vertical integration only) — methods like LIGER, Seurat v3/v4, MultiVI, CoupleNMF, MMD-MA, scDART, or MultiMAP may be more appropriate Input consists of feature/bio-marker tables rather than raw per-cell count matrices that need to be stored in the counts dictionary format One jointly profiled batch already bridges all modalities and dictionary-learning bridge integration suffices

skills.name: single-cell-mtdna-read-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-mtdna-read-simulation Use when benchmarking mtDNA variant-calling tools against known ground-truth clonal variants in simulated Smart-seq2-like scRNA-seq data, or when generating simulated single-cell mtDNA BAMs with controlled clone counts, allele frequencies, and lineage trees. The goal is calling clonal variants on real single-cell data (e.g., Kim or fibroblast Smart-seq2 datasets) rather than benchmarking callers against a synthetic truth set The assay is scATAC-seq with NUMT-masked references, where mtDNA-specific callers like mgatk were primarily designed and simulation assumptions may not transfer Input data has already been genotyped into a SNP-by-cell AD/DP matrix and the task is clonal reconstruction (use vireoSNP downstream instead) In-silico simulation of single-cell mtDNA sequencing reads (NEAT-genReads + SomatoSim on hg19) to build ground-truth benchmark datasets for evaluating clonal mtDNA variant callers such as MQuad, mgatk, and Monovar by AUPRC/AUROC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: In-silico simulation of single-cell mtDNA sequencing reads (NEAT-genReads + SomatoSim on hg19) to build ground-truth benchmark datasets for evaluating clonal mtDNA variant callers such as MQuad, mgatk, and Monovar by AUPRC/AUROC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling clonal variants on real single-cell data (e.g., Kim or fibroblast Smart-seq2 datasets) rather than benchmarking callers against a synthetic truth set The assay is scATAC-seq with NUMT-masked references, where mtDNA-specific callers like mgatk were primarily designed and simulation assumptions may not transfer Input data has already been genotyped into a SNP-by-cell AD/DP matrix and the task is clonal reconstruction (use vireoSNP downstream instead)

skills.description: Use when concatenating multiple scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Baron, Lawlor, Muraro pancreas datasets) with batch and cell-type annotations and you need joint low-dimensional embeddings that both preserve cell-type separation and integrate batches for comparison against PCA-based pipelines.
skills.name: single-cell-multi-batch-dataset-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-multi-batch-dataset-integration Use when concatenating multiple scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Baron, Lawlor, Muraro pancreas datasets) with batch and cell-type annotations and you need joint low-dimensional embeddings that both preserve cell-type separation and integrate batches for comparison against PCA-based pipelines. Data are simple pseudo-cell mixtures or pools of distinct cell types (e.g., SCMixology, Zhengmix) where batch structure is by design simpler than real complex tissue — the paper notes these do not reflect real-world tissue complexity A single-table dimensionality reduction is needed without multi-batch alignment — use the corral function instead of corralm Cell-type ground-truth labels are unvalidated or the goal is to detect novel sub-populations/rare cell types — the paper notes ARI-style evaluation can penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations relative to reference labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrate multiple single-cell RNA-seq batches/datasets by running corralm multi-table correspondence analysis (preferably with Freeman–Tukey residuals) on concatenated count matrices, optionally followed by batch correction (Harmony or MNN) on the resulting cell embeddings, to preserve cell-type structure while removing batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Integrate multiple single-cell RNA-seq batches/datasets by running corralm multi-table correspondence analysis (preferably with Freeman–Tukey residuals) on concatenated count matrices, optionally followed by batch correction (Harmony or MNN) on the resulting cell embeddings, to preserve cell-type structure while removing batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are simple pseudo-cell mixtures or pools of distinct cell types (e.g., SCMixology, Zhengmix) where batch structure is by design simpler than real complex tissue — the paper notes these do not reflect real-world tissue complexity A single-table dimensionality reduction is needed without multi-batch alignment — use the corral function instead of corralm Cell-type ground-truth labels are unvalidated or the goal is to detect novel sub-populations/rare cell types — the paper notes ARI-style evaluation can penalize methods that better distinguish sub-populations relative to reference labels

skills.description: Use when paired transcriptome and surface protein (CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT) data are available for training and the goal is to impute relative surface protein abundances from UMI-based scRNA-seq counts alone.
skills.name: single-cell-multi-omic-model-fitting
skills.search_text: single-cell-multi-omic-model-fitting Use when paired transcriptome and surface protein (CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT) data are available for training and the goal is to impute relative surface protein abundances from UMI-based scRNA-seq counts alone. Input expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g. TPM/RPKM) — cTP-net can only apply to count-based UMI expression input, and prediction accuracy on TPM/RPKM is unknown. You need imputation of non-hematopoietic or out-of-panel proteins — generalization outside the hematopoietic lineage was not tested, and the 100-protein model was still in training. You only need cell-type clustering/annotation from transcriptome alone with no protein imputation target. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit a multiple-branch deep neural network (MB-DNN) that maps a SAVER-X-denoised, LogNormalize-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix to the geometric-mean log-ratio (relative abundance) transformed surface protein counts, imputing protein abundances for single cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Fit a multiple-branch deep neural network (MB-DNN) that maps a SAVER-X-denoised, LogNormalize-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix to the geometric-mean log-ratio (relative abundance) transformed surface protein counts, imputing protein abundances for single cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data is not UMI-based count data (e.g. TPM/RPKM) — cTP-net can only apply to count-based UMI expression input, and prediction accuracy on TPM/RPKM is unknown. You need imputation of non-hematopoietic or out-of-panel proteins — generalization outside the hematopoietic lineage was not tested, and the 100-protein model was still in training. You only need cell-type clustering/annotation from transcriptome alone with no protein imputation target.

skills.description: Use when paired single-cell modality matrices (e.g. DBIT-seq transcriptomic/proteomic or granulocyte scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq count matrices) must be preprocessed before training scMMGAN or its CycleGAN/CMAE baselines.
skills.name: single-cell-multi-omics-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-multi-omics-preprocessing Use when paired single-cell modality matrices (e.g. DBIT-seq transcriptomic/proteomic or granulocyte scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq count matrices) must be preprocessed before training scMMGAN or its CycleGAN/CMAE baselines. Input data is already a preprocessed feature table in the desired scale (e.g. columns already mostly within [-10, 10]) — reapplying scaling and PCA would distort the geometry used by the correspondence loss The task requires raw count-level interpretation (e.g. differential expression on original gene counts) before mapping, since PCA reduction to 50 components discards per-gene resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Prepares paired single-cell multi-omic datasets (e.g. scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq or spatial transcriptomics/proteomics) for scMMGAN training by applying MAGIC dropout correction, per-dimension zero-centering and unit scaling, and reduction to 50 principal components, so that each input column is mostly in the interval [-10, 10]. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Prepares paired single-cell multi-omic datasets (e.g. scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq or spatial transcriptomics/proteomics) for scMMGAN training by applying MAGIC dropout correction, per-dimension zero-centering and unit scaling, and reduction to 50 principal components, so that each input column is mostly in the interval [-10, 10].
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already a preprocessed feature table in the desired scale (e.g. columns already mostly within [-10, 10]) — reapplying scaling and PCA would distort the geometry used by the correspondence loss The task requires raw count-level interpretation (e.g. differential expression on original gene counts) before mapping, since PCA reduction to 50 components discards per-gene resolution

skills.description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq count tables (batches, samples, or platforms) sharing a common gene feature space must be integrated into a joint low-dimensional embedding, especially when PCA+Harmony shows poor batch mixing.
skills.name: single-cell-multi-table-correspondence-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-multi-table-correspondence-analysis Use when multiple scRNA-seq count tables (batches, samples, or platforms) sharing a common gene feature space must be integrated into a joint low-dimensional embedding, especially when PCA+Harmony shows poor batch mixing. When there is only a single count table with no batches to integrate — use corral (single-table CA for dimensionality reduction) instead of corralm When the batches do not share a comparable gene feature space and cannot be restricted to an intersecting gene set When the goal is independent cluster-accuracy benchmarking (ARI) on complex tissues — the article notes ground-truth datasets like SCMixology are simple pseudo-cell mixtures with unvalidated annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply corralm, the multi-table correspondence analysis routine from the corral R/Bioconductor package, to align and batch-integrate SingleCellExperiment scRNA-seq tables (e.g., the SCMixology 10X/Celseq2/Dropseq batches) as a CA-based substitute for PCA embeddings in batch-correction pipelines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-26434-1
skills.summary: Apply corralm, the multi-table correspondence analysis routine from the corral R/Bioconductor package, to align and batch-integrate SingleCellExperiment scRNA-seq tables (e.g., the SCMixology 10X/Celseq2/Dropseq batches) as a CA-based substitute for PCA embeddings in batch-correction pipelines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there is only a single count table with no batches to integrate — use corral (single-table CA for dimensionality reduction) instead of corralm When the batches do not share a comparable gene feature space and cannot be restricted to an intersecting gene set When the goal is independent cluster-accuracy benchmarking (ARI) on complex tissues — the article notes ground-truth datasets like SCMixology are simple pseudo-cell mixtures with unvalidated annotations

skills.description: Use when you have multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-Seq, Multiome, TEA-Seq) with multiple conflicting annotation sets from Leiden clustering at different resolutions, and need a reconciled per-cell population assignment.
skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-clustering-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-clustering-integration Use when you have multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-Seq, Multiome, TEA-Seq) with multiple conflicting annotation sets from Leiden clustering at different resolutions, and need a reconciled per-cell population assignment. When only one modality with a single resolution clustering exists and no conflicting annotations need reconciliation When more than 15 annotation sets are provided and runtime matters — scTriangulate substitutes Shapley selection with combined rank-based selection When you need integration of multiple samples of the same modality or across technologies — the article notes this support is planned but not yet available http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 A decision-level strategy for reconciling conflicting single-cell clustering solutions across modalities (RNA, ATAC, ADT), algorithms, and resolutions using scTriangulate's Shapley-value coalitional framework plus stability metrics, benchmarked against Seurat-WNN, TotalVI, and ensemble clustering (MCLA, HGPA, HBGF). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: A decision-level strategy for reconciling conflicting single-cell clustering solutions across modalities (RNA, ATAC, ADT), algorithms, and resolutions using scTriangulate's Shapley-value coalitional framework plus stability metrics, benchmarked against Seurat-WNN, TotalVI, and ensemble clustering (MCLA, HGPA, HBGF).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one modality with a single resolution clustering exists and no conflicting annotations need reconciliation When more than 15 annotation sets are provided and runtime matters — scTriangulate substitutes Shapley selection with combined rank-based selection When you need integration of multiple samples of the same modality or across technologies — the article notes this support is planned but not yet available

skills.description: Use when two single-cell omics matrices (e.g., snRNA-seq counts and snATAC-seq peak counts from the same study but unpaired barcodes, such as 10x Multiome PBMC data) must be co-embedded and cross-modal cell pairing is needed.
skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-data-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-data-integration Use when two single-cell omics matrices (e.g., snRNA-seq counts and snATAC-seq peak counts from the same study but unpaired barcodes, such as 10x Multiome PBMC data) must be co-embedded and cross-modal cell pairing is needed. The dataset is already intrinsically paired (same barcode in both modalities), so cross-modal cell matching is unnecessary — proceed directly to paired-object analysis. Input is a single-modality dataset with no second omics layer to integrate. The goal is enhancer-to-promoter linking or GRN inference itself (AddMotifs/RunChromVAR) rather than modality integration and cell pairing. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 Integrate single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq modalities by projecting both into a common low-dimensional space via Seurat's CCA method (wrapped in scMEGA's CoembedData), optionally batch-correcting with Harmony, and pairing cells across modalities with PairCells. This is the foundational co-embedding step of the scMEGA end-to-end multi-omics analysis workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Integrate single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq modalities by projecting both into a common low-dimensional space via Seurat's CCA method (wrapped in scMEGA's CoembedData), optionally batch-correcting with Harmony, and pairing cells across modalities with PairCells. This is the foundational co-embedding step of the scMEGA end-to-end multi-omics analysis workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is already intrinsically paired (same barcode in both modalities), so cross-modal cell matching is unnecessary — proceed directly to paired-object analysis. Input is a single-modality dataset with no second omics layer to integrate. The goal is enhancer-to-promoter linking or GRN inference itself (AddMotifs/RunChromVAR) rather than modality integration and cell pairing.

skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-data-preprocessing Use when raw single-cell datasets with paired TCR sequences and gene expression must be annotated (cell type, tissue, cancer source) and filtered before training mvTCR or building a multi-study reference atlas. skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-deep-clustering Use when you need to jointly cluster RNA+ADT (CITE-seq) data and assess whether a learned latent space separates cell types while removing batch effects across batches. Single-modal scRNA-seq data without an ADT/second modality, where single-modal methods like IDEC, Tscan, or SC3 are the appropriate baselines When you need automatic estimation of the number of clusters — scMDC requires the user to specify K after pretraining Data already reduced to a low-dimensional embedding, where clustering should be applied directly rather than relearning a joint latent space http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Runs the scMDC multimodal deep clustering model (PyTorch) on multi-batch CITE-seq datasets such as BMNC and SLN111, exports its latent embedding and predicted cluster labels, and visualizes them with Scanpy t-SNE to show cell-type separation and batch mixing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35031-9
skills.summary: Runs the scMDC multimodal deep clustering model (PyTorch) on multi-batch CITE-seq datasets such as BMNC and SLN111, exports its latent embedding and predicted cluster labels, and visualizes them with Scanpy t-SNE to show cell-type separation and batch mixing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-modal scRNA-seq data without an ADT/second modality, where single-modal methods like IDEC, Tscan, or SC3 are the appropriate baselines When you need automatic estimation of the number of clusters — scMDC requires the user to specify K after pretraining Data already reduced to a low-dimensional embedding, where clustering should be applied directly rather than relearning a joint latent space

skills.description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq data (RNA gene counts CSV + raw protein ADT counts CSV, rows = cells, columns = genes/proteins) and need joint cell embeddings or want to quantify complementary, modality-specific information across cells.
skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-embedding-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-embedding-analysis Use when you have paired CITE-seq data (RNA gene counts CSV + raw protein ADT counts CSV, rows = cells, columns = genes/proteins) and need joint cell embeddings or want to quantify complementary, modality-specific information across cells. Input is a single-modality dataset (RNA-only or protein-only) with no paired ADT counts — scME requires both modalities The goal is a fused/consensus clustering only and modality-specific complementary information should be discarded — the article notes most integration methods do this instead Data is not paired CITE-seq RNA/protein counts in the CSV layout scME expects (rows = cells, columns = genes/proteins, cell ids in column 0) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate joint single-cell multiomics embeddings with scME, a dual-modality factor model that combines RNA gene counts and raw protein ADT counts from CITE-seq data, then use the embeddings to quantify shared vs complementary (modality-inconsistent) information across cell pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad337
skills.summary: Generate joint single-cell multiomics embeddings with scME, a dual-modality factor model that combines RNA gene counts and raw protein ADT counts from CITE-seq data, then use the embeddings to quantify shared vs complementary (modality-inconsistent) information across cell pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-modality dataset (RNA-only or protein-only) with no paired ADT counts — scME requires both modalities The goal is a fused/consensus clustering only and modality-specific complementary information should be discarded — the article notes most integration methods do this instead Data is not paired CITE-seq RNA/protein counts in the CSV layout scME expects (rows = cells, columns = genes/proteins, cell ids in column 0)

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq data and need to quantify whether a multimodal latent embedding improves downstream prediction (antigen specificity, binding avidity from pMHC multimer counts) or cluster identification relative to unimodal baselines.

skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-embedding-evaluation Use when you have paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq data and need to quantify whether a multimodal latent embedding improves downstream prediction (antigen specificity, binding avidity from pMHC multimer counts) or cluster identification relative to unimodal baselines. skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are unpaired or missing one modality (e.g. gene expression without α-/β-CDR3) — the authors note mvTCR was applied mainly to fully paired data and handling of partially missing data remains insufficiently addressed The input is already a reduced embedding or feature table and you only need classification/clustering — training a new multi-view VAE is unnecessary No specificity/avidity or cell-type/clonotype annotations exist to train or evaluate prediction heads (tutorials 02/03 require such annotation)
