skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-trajectory-branch-subsetting
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-trajectory-branch-subsetting Use when a single-cell multimodal dataset forms a tree-like or branching differentiation trajectory and you need to ablate topology — testing whether full-trajectory DAG inference or individual branch sub-DAGs explain the observed locus-gene signal. The dataset is not a dynamic branching process — GrID-Net relies on multiomic single-cell data from matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process, such as differentiation, to provide pseudotemporal context You only need a single global locus-gene ranking and have no need to compare topology configurations; run gridnet.run_gridnet on the full DAG directly Cells lack lineage annotations and cannot be partitioned into biologically meaningful branches, making a branch-wise ablation undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Subset a single-cell multimodal trajectory (e.g., SHARE-seq mouse skin differentiation) into biological lineages/branches, build a separate cell-state DAG per branch with the same construction settings as the full trajectory, and score each branch-specific Granger-causal configuration against the full-DAG GrID-Net result to isolate the contribution of the DAG topology. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Subset a single-cell multimodal trajectory (e.g., SHARE-seq mouse skin differentiation) into biological lineages/branches, build a separate cell-state DAG per branch with the same construction settings as the full trajectory, and score each branch-specific Granger-causal configuration against the full-DAG GrID-Net result to isolate the contribution of the DAG topology.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is not a dynamic branching process — GrID-Net relies on multiomic single-cell data from matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process, such as differentiation, to provide pseudotemporal context You only need a single global locus-gene ranking and have no need to compare topology configurations; run gridnet.run_gridnet on the full DAG directly Cells lack lineage annotations and cannot be partitioned into biologically meaningful branches, making a branch-wise ablation undefined

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell transcriptome count data (RNA_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) from a CITE-seq experiment and need to predict paired surface protein abundances from a pretrained multimodal VAE, then quantify prediction accuracy against measured protein counts.
skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-vae-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-vae-inference Use when you have single-cell transcriptome count data (RNA_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) from a CITE-seq experiment and need to predict paired surface protein abundances from a pretrained multimodal VAE, then quantify prediction accuracy against measured protein counts. Input is single-modality data with no measured protein counts available to validate predictions against (Jaccard index benchmarking requires measured top-expressing cell sets) You need to train a model from scratch rather than apply a pretrained one — use the scMM training workflow with paired multimodal input instead Data are chromatin accessibility rather than CITE-seq transcriptome/protein pairs (would require the ATAC-seq folder layout and peak.tsv features) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Applies the pretrained scMM mixture-of-experts multimodal VAE to perform crossmodal generation on CITE-seq data — e.g. predicting surface protein abundance of BMNC cells from transcriptome-only input — and benchmarks predictions against measured values using the Jaccard index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Applies the pretrained scMM mixture-of-experts multimodal VAE to perform crossmodal generation on CITE-seq data — e.g. predicting surface protein abundance of BMNC cells from transcriptome-only input — and benchmarks predictions against measured values using the Jaccard index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-modality data with no measured protein counts available to validate predictions against (Jaccard index benchmarking requires measured top-expressing cell sets) You need to train a model from scratch rather than apply a pretrained one — use the scMM training workflow with paired multimodal input instead Data are chromatin accessibility rather than CITE-seq transcriptome/protein pairs (would require the ATAC-seq folder layout and peak.tsv features)

skills.description: Use when a droplet-based single-cell dataset contains matched mRNA and antibody-derived tag (ADT) measurements and you need a joint cell clustering whose dependence on protein normalization (e.g., dsb vs. CLR) must be evaluated.
skills.name: single-cell-multimodal-wnn-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-multimodal-wnn-clustering Use when a droplet-based single-cell dataset contains matched mRNA and antibody-derived tag (ADT) measurements and you need a joint cell clustering whose dependence on protein normalization (e.g., dsb vs. CLR) must be evaluated. The dataset is transcript-only scRNA-seq with no ADT/protein modality — WNN multimodal integration is unnecessary; plain RNA PCA/clustering suffices. You have not yet normalized the protein data: comparing unnormalized ADT counts within WNN conflates ambient and cell-to-cell noise rather than testing normalization effects. Isotype control antibodies and empty droplets are unavailable and no fallback normalization strategy has been chosen — dsb's technical component and background estimation require careful redefinition (see Supplementary Note). http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Jointly cluster CITE-seq cells by combining mRNA and normalized protein (ADT) data with Seurat weighted nearest neighbors (WNN), as used in the dsb paper to compare dsb- versus CLR-normalized protein inputs within the same RNA space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Jointly cluster CITE-seq cells by combining mRNA and normalized protein (ADT) data with Seurat weighted nearest neighbors (WNN), as used in the dsb paper to compare dsb- versus CLR-normalized protein inputs within the same RNA space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is transcript-only scRNA-seq with no ADT/protein modality — WNN multimodal integration is unnecessary; plain RNA PCA/clustering suffices. You have not yet normalized the protein data: comparing unnormalized ADT counts within WNN conflates ambient and cell-to-cell noise rather than testing normalization effects. Isotype control antibodies and empty droplets are unavailable and no fallback normalization strategy has been chosen — dsb's technical component and background estimation require careful redefinition (see Supplementary Note).

skills.description: Use when raw paired RNA-seq + ATAC-seq single-cell multimodal counts (e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq, sci-CAR) must be normalized and filtered before peak-gene link analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-multiome-count-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiome-count-preprocessing Use when raw paired RNA-seq + ATAC-seq single-cell multimodal counts (e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq, sci-CAR) must be normalized and filtered before peak-gene link analysis. The input data are already normalized, log-transformed, or feature-filtered — re-running preprocess_multimodal would double-transform the counts Only one modality is available (single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq alone), since the function requires paired RNA and ATAC AnnData objects The goal is correlation-free pseudotime or trajectory analysis without peak-gene Granger inference, where alternate preprocessing conventions may be preferable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Normalizes paired single-cell multiome count matrices (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) with count normalization followed by log(1+x) transformation, then filters genes expressed in fewer than 1% of cells and peaks accessible in fewer than 0.1% of cells. This prepares AnnData objects for GrID-Net's multimodal integration, DAG construction, and Granger causal peak-gene inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Normalizes paired single-cell multiome count matrices (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) with count normalization followed by log(1+x) transformation, then filters genes expressed in fewer than 1% of cells and peaks accessible in fewer than 0.1% of cells. This prepares AnnData objects for GrID-Net's multimodal integration, DAG construction, and Granger causal peak-gene inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are already normalized, log-transformed, or feature-filtered — re-running preprocess_multimodal would double-transform the counts Only one modality is available (single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq alone), since the function requires paired RNA and ATAC AnnData objects The goal is correlation-free pseudotime or trajectory analysis without peak-gene Granger inference, where alternate preprocessing conventions may be preferable

skills.description: Use when you need held-out likelihood evaluation of batch-wise single-cell models (e.g., MIRA RP models on the 13-batch NEURIPS 10x Multiome bone marrow data) and must split cells per batch into train/test sets.
skills.name: single-cell-multiome-data-partitioning
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiome-data-partitioning Use when you need held-out likelihood evaluation of batch-wise single-cell models (e.g., MIRA RP models on the 13-batch NEURIPS 10x Multiome bone marrow data) and must split cells per batch into train/test sets. The analysis goal is batch correction or latent-space integration rather than held-out likelihood model comparison — use CODAL/MIRA joint modeling directly instead The dataset has a single batch, so per-batch stratified train/test partitioning has no batch structure to preserve Input is already a model output (topic compositions or embeddings); partitioning applies to cell-level count data with batch labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Partitions single-cell multiome cells from each sequencing batch into training and held-out test sets (4:1 ratio) so that generative models such as MIRA regulatory potential models can be compared by held-out log-likelihood across batches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39494-2
skills.summary: Partitions single-cell multiome cells from each sequencing batch into training and held-out test sets (4:1 ratio) so that generative models such as MIRA regulatory potential models can be compared by held-out log-likelihood across batches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is batch correction or latent-space integration rather than held-out likelihood model comparison — use CODAL/MIRA joint modeling directly instead The dataset has a single batch, so per-batch stratified train/test partitioning has no batch structure to preserve Input is already a model output (topic compositions or embeddings); partitioning applies to cell-level count data with batch labels

skills.description: Use when you have four single-cell data sets (one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions, e.g. CLL donor vs healthy control) and need to identify and compare condition-specific subpopulations and their regulatory programs.
skills.name: single-cell-multiome-subpopulation-linking
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiome-subpopulation-linking Use when you have four single-cell data sets (one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions, e.g. CLL donor vs healthy control) and need to identify and compare condition-specific subpopulations and their regulatory programs. You have multiple donors per condition — the method currently accommodates one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq per condition and does not yet support multiple donors Your data are single-condition or lack paired expression/accessibility from both conditions, since the comparative model requires four data sets from two populations You want to incorporate bulk HiChIP data into the analysis — sc-compReg does not yet support this (extension planned) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A comparative single-cell workflow (sc-compReg) that performs coupled clustering and joint embedding of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data from two conditions, links subpopulations of the same cell type across conditions, and constructs differential regulatory networks to identify condition-specific hub regulators such as TOX2 in CLL-specific B cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25089-2
skills.summary: A comparative single-cell workflow (sc-compReg) that performs coupled clustering and joint embedding of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data from two conditions, links subpopulations of the same cell type across conditions, and constructs differential regulatory networks to identify condition-specific hub regulators such as TOX2 in CLL-specific B cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have multiple donors per condition — the method currently accommodates one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq per condition and does not yet support multiple donors Your data are single-condition or lack paired expression/accessibility from both conditions, since the comparative model requires four data sets from two populations You want to incorporate bulk HiChIP data into the analysis — sc-compReg does not yet support this (extension planned)

skills.description: Use when you have aligned single-cell embeddings from multiple alignment methods (e.g. scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA) on paired-modality datasets (RNA/ATAC PBMC, RNA/ADT BM) and must rank them on clustering and cross-modality prediction performance.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomic-alignment-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomic-alignment-benchmark-evaluation Use when you have aligned single-cell embeddings from multiple alignment methods (e.g. scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA) on paired-modality datasets (RNA/ATAC PBMC, RNA/ADT BM) and must rank them on clustering and cross-modality prediction performance. The data has overlapping cells or features between modalities — standard integration methods that exploit overlaps apply, and the unsupervised alignment benchmark setting here is for non-overlapping modalities. You only need the per-modality low-dimensional representations themselves (the TopoAE-vs-Autoencoder/VAE/UMAP benchmark via TopoAE_benchmark.py), not a comparison of full alignment methods on downstream tasks. Inputs are raw or unaligned single-cell matrices rather than method-produced aligned embeddings — run the alignment step (e.g. run_scTopoGAN) first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Benchmark evaluation of unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment methods (scTopoGAN, topoAE, Autoencoder, VAE, UMAP, UnionCom, MMD-MA) by scoring their aligned embeddings on two downstream tasks: Leiden clustering agreement with known cell labels (Adjusted Rand Index) and 50-nearest-neighbor weighted-regression cross-modality prediction scored by median Spearman correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad171
skills.summary: Benchmark evaluation of unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment methods (scTopoGAN, topoAE, Autoencoder, VAE, UMAP, UnionCom, MMD-MA) by scoring their aligned embeddings on two downstream tasks: Leiden clustering agreement with known cell labels (Adjusted Rand Index) and 50-nearest-neighbor weighted-regression cross-modality prediction scored by median Spearman correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data has overlapping cells or features between modalities — standard integration methods that exploit overlaps apply, and the unsupervised alignment benchmark setting here is for non-overlapping modalities. You only need the per-modality low-dimensional representations themselves (the TopoAE-vs-Autoencoder/VAE/UMAP benchmark via TopoAE_benchmark.py), not a comparison of full alignment methods on downstream tasks. Inputs are raw or unaligned single-cell matrices rather than method-produced aligned embeddings — run the alignment step (e.g. run_scTopoGAN) first.

skills.description: Use when you have two independent single-cell datasets from the same sample — scDNA-seq copy-number profiles and scRNA-seq expression profiles — restricted to a shared gene set, and need a one-to-one cell correspondence or RNA-cell-to-DNA-clone mapping.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomic-cell-assignment
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomic-cell-assignment Use when you have two independent single-cell datasets from the same sample — scDNA-seq copy-number profiles and scRNA-seq expression profiles — restricted to a shared gene set, and need a one-to-one cell correspondence or RNA-cell-to-DNA-clone mapping. You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — unlike statistical methods such as clonealign, MaCroDNA does not provide them The sample is biologically homogeneous — the paper notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples, a biologically driven issue You have paired multi-omic measurements of the same cells (e.g. scTrio-seq with known correspondence) — no computational association is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers cell-to-cell and cell-to-clone correspondence between scRNA-seq (gene expression) and scDNA-seq (copy number) data using MaCroDNA's maximum weighted bipartite matching over per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients, solved as a Gurobi binary mixed-integer program (with a sequential heuristic when RNA cells outnumber DNA cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44014-3
skills.summary: Infers cell-to-cell and cell-to-clone correspondence between scRNA-seq (gene expression) and scDNA-seq (copy number) data using MaCroDNA's maximum weighted bipartite matching over per-gene Pearson correlation coefficients, solved as a Gurobi binary mixed-integer program (with a sequential heuristic when RNA cells outnumber DNA cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need probabilistic confidence measures for assignments — unlike statistical methods such as clonealign, MaCroDNA does not provide them The sample is biologically homogeneous — the paper notes matching cells is distinctively challenging in homogeneous samples, a biologically driven issue You have paired multi-omic measurements of the same cells (e.g. scTrio-seq with known correspondence) — no computational association is needed

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has predicted primed cells and candidate regulatory factors (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8 in fetal liver MPPs) and matched scATAC-Seq data from the same cell types is available for epigenomic validation.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomic-data-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomic-data-integration Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has predicted primed cells and candidate regulatory factors (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8 in fetal liver MPPs) and matched scATAC-Seq data from the same cell types is available for epigenomic validation. No matched scATAC-Seq data exists for the cell types under study (e.g. the Ranzoni study lacked SHARE-Seq joint profiles, forcing this indirect validation) The candidate regulator is not a transcription factor with a motif (e.g. UHRF1), so no chromVAR motif activity can be computed for it The scRNA-Seq result is a cluster/trajectory annotation without defined marker genes, since the ATAC-side cell assignment depends on summing accessibility over lineage marker genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Validates scRNA-Seq-derived primed states and their regulatory factors by projecting them onto matched scATAC-Seq data: transfer RNA-derived cell assignments and marker genes to a gene-level accessibility matrix, then test chromVAR TF motif activity differences between primed cell groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105709
skills.summary: Validates scRNA-Seq-derived primed states and their regulatory factors by projecting them onto matched scATAC-Seq data: transfer RNA-derived cell assignments and marker genes to a gene-level accessibility matrix, then test chromVAR TF motif activity differences between primed cell groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scATAC-Seq data exists for the cell types under study (e.g. the Ranzoni study lacked SHARE-Seq joint profiles, forcing this indirect validation) The candidate regulator is not a transcription factor with a motif (e.g. UHRF1), so no chromVAR motif activity can be computed for it The scRNA-Seq result is a cluster/trajectory annotation without defined marker genes, since the ATAC-side cell assignment depends on summing accessibility over lineage marker genes

skills.description: Use when you have paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data from a dynamic single-cell process and need to rank candidate chromatin peak-gene regulatory links by causal strength rather than correlation.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomic-peak-gene-linking
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomic-peak-gene-linking Use when you have paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data from a dynamic single-cell process and need to rank candidate chromatin peak-gene regulatory links by causal strength rather than correlation. Data lack pseudotemporal context: the method relies on multiomic single-cell data from matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process such as differentiation or disease; static or non-dynamic snapshots are out of scope. Only one modality is available (RNA-seq or ATAC-seq alone) — the wrapper requires paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq for the same cells. The goal is total-order Granger causality on regular time series rather than causal inference on a partially ordered DAG of cell states. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Infers causal noncoding peak-gene links from paired single-cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data by generalizing Granger causality to DAGs: GrID-Net trains lagged message-passing GNN forecasting models (reduced vs. full) and scores each candidate peak-gene pair with a one-tailed F-test on forecasting improvement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Infers causal noncoding peak-gene links from paired single-cell ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data by generalizing Granger causality to DAGs: GrID-Net trains lagged message-passing GNN forecasting models (reduced vs. full) and scores each candidate peak-gene pair with a one-tailed F-test on forecasting improvement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack pseudotemporal context: the method relies on multiomic single-cell data from matching tissue undergoing a dynamic process such as differentiation or disease; static or non-dynamic snapshots are out of scope. Only one modality is available (RNA-seq or ATAC-seq alone) — the wrapper requires paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq for the same cells. The goal is total-order Granger causality on regular time series rather than causal inference on a partially ordered DAG of cell states.

skills.description: Use when raw unprocessed RNA-seq and ATAC-seq AnnData objects from a paired single-cell multimodal assay must be normalized and filtered to define valid candidate peak-gene pairs for downstream GrID-Net or pseudotime analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomic-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomic-preprocessing Use when raw unprocessed RNA-seq and ATAC-seq AnnData objects from a paired single-cell multimodal assay must be normalized and filtered to define valid candidate peak-gene pairs for downstream GrID-Net or pseudotime analysis. Data are already normalized and only a single modality (e.g., scRNA-seq alone) is available — pseudotime-oriented causal inference requires paired RNA+ATAC observations of the same cells The goal is linking variants to genes without single-cell multimodal data, since preprocessing and candidate-pair assembly presuppose peak coordinates and TSS annotations The dataset is static or lacks a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation), as the method relies on pseudotemporal context for the cell-state DAG http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Preprocess paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq multimodal data (e.g., 10x Multiome human corticogenesis) with count normalization, log(1+x) transformation, and expression/accessibility filtering before causal peak-gene link inference with GrID-Net. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-61337-5
skills.summary: Preprocess paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq multimodal data (e.g., 10x Multiome human corticogenesis) with count normalization, log(1+x) transformation, and expression/accessibility filtering before causal peak-gene link inference with GrID-Net.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already normalized and only a single modality (e.g., scRNA-seq alone) is available — pseudotime-oriented causal inference requires paired RNA+ATAC observations of the same cells The goal is linking variants to genes without single-cell multimodal data, since preprocessing and candidate-pair assembly presuppose peak coordinates and TSS annotations The dataset is static or lacks a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation), as the method relies on pseudotemporal context for the cell-state DAG

skills.description: Use when raw or minimally processed CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq h5 count matrices need per-modality normalization (mRNA vs. ADT/ATAC) before feeding a deep clustering model such as scMDC.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomics-count-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomics-count-preprocessing Use when raw or minimally processed CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq h5 count matrices need per-modality normalization (mRNA vs. ADT/ATAC) before feeding a deep clustering model such as scMDC. The downstream method expects already-scaled, variable-feature-selected inputs (e.g., a Seurat WNN workflow) rather than the size-factor/log-transformed matrices scMDC expects Input is a joint embedding or latent representation rather than raw per-modality count data The modality combination is not supported by the pipeline (e.g., methylation or spatial data not among the paper's CITE-seq/SMAGE-seq modalities) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Preprocess paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/SMAGE-seq count matrices (h5 inputs with X1=RNA, X2=ADT/ATAC, Y=labels) separately per modality using Scanpy — filtering zero-count features, size-factor normalizing, and log transforming — so the data are ready for deep multimodal clustering with scMDC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35031-9
skills.summary: Preprocess paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/SMAGE-seq count matrices (h5 inputs with X1=RNA, X2=ADT/ATAC, Y=labels) separately per modality using Scanpy — filtering zero-count features, size-factor normalizing, and log transforming — so the data are ready for deep multimodal clustering with scMDC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream method expects already-scaled, variable-feature-selected inputs (e.g., a Seurat WNN workflow) rather than the size-factor/log-transformed matrices scMDC expects Input is a joint embedding or latent representation rather than raw per-modality count data The modality combination is not supported by the pipeline (e.g., methylation or spatial data not among the paper's CITE-seq/SMAGE-seq modalities)

skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics count matrices (e.g. RNA + surface protein CITE-seq, or RNA + ATAC peaks) and need joint dimensionality reduction, cross-modal prediction, or interpretable latent dimensions.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomics-data-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomics-data-integration Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics count matrices (e.g. RNA + surface protein CITE-seq, or RNA + ATAC peaks) and need joint dimensionality reduction, cross-modal prediction, or interpretable latent dimensions. Data modalities are unpaired (not measured in the same cells) — the mixture-of-experts joint representation requires aligned paired counts Input is already a reduced feature/embedding table rather than raw integer counts — scMM models raw count data per modality with modality-specific distributions Only a single modality is available — cross-modal generation and multimodal joint representation require at least two modalities http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Integrate paired single-cell multiomics data (transcriptome & surface proteins via CITE-seq, or transcriptome & chromatin accessibility) with scMM, a mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder that models raw count data per modality with modality-specific probability distributions to extract interpretable joint representations and enable cross-modal generation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100071
skills.summary: Integrate paired single-cell multiomics data (transcriptome & surface proteins via CITE-seq, or transcriptome & chromatin accessibility) with scMM, a mixture-of-experts multimodal variational autoencoder that models raw count data per modality with modality-specific probability distributions to extract interpretable joint representations and enable cross-modal generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data modalities are unpaired (not measured in the same cells) — the mixture-of-experts joint representation requires aligned paired counts Input is already a reduced feature/embedding table rather than raw integer counts — scMM models raw count data per modality with modality-specific distributions Only a single modality is available — cross-modal generation and multimodal joint representation require at least two modalities

skills.description: Use when benchmarking CITE-seq clustering methods (scMDC vs. TotalVI, Seurat V4 WNN, SC3, scDCC, BREM-SC, CiteFuse, Specter) requires controlled mRNA+ADT data with ground-truth labels, or for linear-runtime scalability tests.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomics-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomics-data-simulation Use when benchmarking CITE-seq clustering methods (scMDC vs. TotalVI, Seurat V4 WNN, SC3, scDCC, BREM-SC, CiteFuse, Specter) requires controlled mRNA+ADT data with ground-truth labels, or for linear-runtime scalability tests. The data are real, already-annotated CITE-seq datasets (e.g. GSE128639 BMNC, 10X PBMC, GSE150599 SLN) — use the real-data benchmarking workflow rather than simulation. Only a single modality (scRNA-seq alone) needs simulation; the paired mRNA/ADT h5 structure (X1/X2/Y) and multimodal preprocessing are not required. Only CPU hardware is available and validated results are mandatory — the study's simulated experiments were all run on an Nvidia Tesla P100 (16 G) GPU and CPU reproduction is unvalidated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates synthetic paired mRNA/ADT CITE-seq datasets with SymSim across clustering-signal, dropout-rate, and batch-effect regimes (plus 1,000–100,000-cell scalability series), exporting h5 files (X1=RNA, X2=ADT, Y=ground-truth labels) that serve as controlled benchmarks for evaluating scMDC-style multimodal clustering performance and runtime scaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35031-9
skills.summary: Generates synthetic paired mRNA/ADT CITE-seq datasets with SymSim across clustering-signal, dropout-rate, and batch-effect regimes (plus 1,000–100,000-cell scalability series), exporting h5 files (X1=RNA, X2=ADT, Y=ground-truth labels) that serve as controlled benchmarks for evaluating scMDC-style multimodal clustering performance and runtime scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are real, already-annotated CITE-seq datasets (e.g. GSE128639 BMNC, 10X PBMC, GSE150599 SLN) — use the real-data benchmarking workflow rather than simulation. Only a single modality (scRNA-seq alone) needs simulation; the paired mRNA/ADT h5 structure (X1/X2/Y) and multimodal preprocessing are not required. Only CPU hardware is available and validated results are mandatory — the study's simulated experiments were all run on an Nvidia Tesla P100 (16 G) GPU and CPU reproduction is unvalidated.

skills.description: Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (RNA and ATAC or CITE-seq) in mtx format with gene/peak/barcode annotation files and need joint representations or crossmodal prediction between modalities.
skills.name: single-cell-multiomics-generative-model-training
skills.search_text: single-cell-multiomics-generative-model-training Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (RNA and ATAC or CITE-seq) in mtx format with gene/peak/barcode annotation files and need joint representations or crossmodal prediction between modalities. skills.name: single-cell-overdispersion-decomposition
skills.search_text: single-cell-overdispersion-decomposition Use when fitting per-gene mixed models to multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts and you need to separate between-subject from within-subject overdispersion, or test whether covariates (e.g., age, sex, AD status) explain subject-level variation. The data are bulk RNA-seq or have no multi-subject (multi-donor) structure — the subject-level/cell-level overdispersion decomposition requires hierarchical multi-subject sampling. You only need differential expression p-values, not the variance-component estimates (σ², ϕ⁻¹); standard DE tools may suffice. Genes fail QC outright (convergence code ≤ -20, cell-level overdispersion >100, or subject-level overdispersion >1 when testing subject-level variables) — these estimates are unreliable and should be excluded rather than interpreted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Decomposes gene-specific overdispersion in multi-subject single-cell data into subject-level (σ²) and cell-level (ϕ⁻¹) components using NEBULA's negative binomial gamma mixed model (NBGMM), then quantifies how much covariate adjustment explains each component. Applied here to ROSMAP frontal cortex snRNA-seq across six major brain cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-021-02146-6
skills.summary: Decomposes gene-specific overdispersion in multi-subject single-cell data into subject-level (σ²) and cell-level (ϕ⁻¹) components using NEBULA's negative binomial gamma mixed model (NBGMM), then quantifies how much covariate adjustment explains each component. Applied here to ROSMAP frontal cortex snRNA-seq across six major brain cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk RNA-seq or have no multi-subject (multi-donor) structure — the subject-level/cell-level overdispersion decomposition requires hierarchical multi-subject sampling. Genes fail QC outright (convergence code ≤ -20, cell-level overdispersion >100, or subject-level overdispersion >1 when testing subject-level variables) — these estimates are unreliable and should be excluded rather than interpreted.

skills.description: Use when comparing the computational cost (CPU/wall-clock time) of pathogen quantification tools—scPathoQuant, ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, Venus—on an identical 10x scRNAseq sample to rank them from fastest to slowest.

The goal is comparing quantification accuracy or sensitivity rather than computational runtime — this skill measures only CPU/wall-clock cost The input is not a 10x cellranger output sample with an accompanying pathogen reference genome folder, since the four tools must run on the identical input for timing to be comparable A single tool's runtime is needed on its own data; timing comparisons require all four tools (ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, Venus, scPathoQuant) run under identical thread allocation on the same sample http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmark the CPU time of scPathoQuant's quantification step against ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, and Venus on the same 10x scRNAseq sample (HIV infected donor 2) to reproduce the reported runtime ranking from the scPathoQuant paper (Fig. 5E). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae145
skills.summary: Benchmark the CPU time of scPathoQuant's quantification step against ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, and Venus on the same 10x scRNAseq sample (HIV infected donor 2) to reproduce the reported runtime ranking from the scPathoQuant paper (Fig. 5E).

The question is differential gene expression or gene-set over-representation only, with no interest in distributional change of pathway gene expression Input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated feature tables rather than single-cell-level expression with population metadata Only one population/sample is available, since SCPA compares pathway distributions across at least two conditions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Compare pathway activity between two or more single-cell populations using SCPA, which defines pathway activity as a change in the multivariate distribution of a pathway's genes (qval) rather than gene-set enrichment. skills.description: Use when you must compute PAS for a large pathway collection (>10^3 gene sets) across a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 100k+ cells, million-cell atlases) and existing scorers like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow or memory-hungry.
skills.name: single-cell-pathway-activity-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-pathway-activity-scoring Use when you must compute PAS for a large pathway collection (>10^3 gene sets) across a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 100k+ cells, million-cell atlases) and existing scorers like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow or memory-hungry. When the goal is cross-condition differential pathway testing where SCPA's downsampling (500/1000/2000 cells) design is acceptable and PAS per cell is not needed — SCPA may suffice, though scPAFA was 1.3x–103.9x faster. When you already have a cell-by-pathway score matrix (e.g., from a prior fast_Ucell run) — re-running scoring wastes computation; proceed directly to pseudobulk processing and MOFA training. When the expression matrix already contains PAS columns or when pathway sets are highly redundant — pathway selection is a supervised process and a redundant set increases result complexity. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes cell-level pathway activity scores (PAS) for large-scale scRNA-seq data using scPAFA's fast_Ucell (a Python reimplementation of UCell) or fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore/Scanpy score_genes equivalent), converting a cell-gene expression matrix into a cell-pathway PAS matrix at million-cell scale. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Computes cell-level pathway activity scores (PAS) for large-scale scRNA-seq data using scPAFA's fast_Ucell (a Python reimplementation of UCell) or fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore/Scanpy score_genes equivalent), converting a cell-gene expression matrix into a cell-pathway PAS matrix at million-cell scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is cross-condition differential pathway testing where SCPA's downsampling (500/1000/2000 cells) design is acceptable and PAS per cell is not needed — SCPA may suffice, though scPAFA was 1.3x–103.9x faster. When you already have a cell-by-pathway score matrix (e.g., from a prior fast_Ucell run) — re-running scoring wastes computation; proceed directly to pseudobulk processing and MOFA training. When the expression matrix already contains PAS columns or when pathway sets are highly redundant — pathway selection is a supervised process and a redundant set increases result complexity.

skills.description: Use when comparing pathway activity between scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. resting vs 24h-activated naive CD4+ T cells) and you need distribution-level perturbation signals, not gene-set over-representation.
skills.name: single-cell-pathway-distribution-testing
skills.search_text: single-cell-pathway-distribution-testing Use when comparing pathway activity between scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. resting vs 24h-activated naive CD4+ T cells) and you need distribution-level perturbation signals, not gene-set over-representation. Your question is strictly gene-set over-representation/enrichment testing, not multivariate distributional change in gene expression You have no per-cell expression data — SCPA requires total normalized count matrices, not precomputed bulk or aggregate profiles You need a two-sample-only statistic and rely on fold change as the primary readout; SCPA's fold change/enrichment is secondary and is not produced for multisample (>2) comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detect pathway perturbations in single-cell RNA-seq using SCPA, a graph-based nonparametric framework that defines pathway activity as a change in the multivariate distribution of a pathway's genes across two or more conditions, yielding pval/adjusted pval/qval statistics rather than enrichment scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111697
skills.summary: Detect pathway perturbations in single-cell RNA-seq using SCPA, a graph-based nonparametric framework that defines pathway activity as a change in the multivariate distribution of a pathway's genes across two or more conditions, yielding pval/adjusted pval/qval statistics rather than enrichment scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your question is strictly gene-set over-representation/enrichment testing, not multivariate distributional change in gene expression You have no per-cell expression data — SCPA requires total normalized count matrices, not precomputed bulk or aggregate profiles You need a two-sample-only statistic and rely on fold change as the primary readout; SCPA's fold change/enrichment is secondary and is not produced for multisample (>2) comparisons

skills.description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, log2(TPM+1)-style), cell-level metadata with 1/0 condition labels, a contrast file, and you need to identify which signaling pathways are dysregulated per cell type across conditions.
skills.name: single-cell-pathway-dysregulation-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-pathway-dysregulation-analysis Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, log2(TPM+1)-style), cell-level metadata with 1/0 condition labels, a contrast file, and you need to identify which signaling pathways are dysregulated per cell type across conditions. When the goal is differential gene expression or conventional ORA on DE genes — the article shows conventional ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes (migration-related pathways were not enriched among DE genes), so scBONITA-PA is the intended approach, but plain DE analysis is not this skill. When no condition contrast (pairs of cell-wise condition labels) can be defined — pathway analysis requires a contrast file comparing two conditions. When running on a desktop without adequate resources — rule inference and attractor analysis on large scRNA-seq datasets require in excess of 10G RAM. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 Apply scBONITA pathway analysis (scBONITA-PA) to identify KEGG signaling pathways dysregulated between conditions (e.g., pre- vs post-HIV infection, AS+ vs AS- PLWH) in specific single-cell subpopulations such as cytotoxic T cells and monocytes, using inferred Boolean rules rather than conventional over-representation analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Apply scBONITA pathway analysis (scBONITA-PA) to identify KEGG signaling pathways dysregulated between conditions (e.g., pre- vs post-HIV infection, AS+ vs AS- PLWH) in specific single-cell subpopulations such as cytotoxic T cells and monocytes, using inferred Boolean rules rather than conventional over-representation analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential gene expression or conventional ORA on DE genes — the article shows conventional ORA was inefficacious at identifying coherent molecular processes (migration-related pathways were not enriched among DE genes), so scBONITA-PA is the intended approach, but plain DE analysis is not this skill. When no condition contrast (pairs of cell-wise condition labels) can be defined — pathway analysis requires a contrast file comparing two conditions. skills.search_text: single-cell-pathway-perturbation-analysis Use when comparing pathway activity across multiple conditions, time points, or pseudotime phases in scRNA-seq data — especially when enrichment-based methods miss pathways with distributional shifts but little fold change. skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been quality-controlled and cell-annotated and you need to quantify a signaling pathway (e.g., angiogenesis) per cell, rank cell types by score, and highlight pathway-high subpopulations in the tumor microenvironment.

skills.search_text: single-cell-pathway-score-visualization Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been quality-controlled and cell-annotated and you need to quantify a signaling pathway (e.g., angiogenesis) per cell, rank cell types by score, and highlight pathway-high subpopulations in the tumor microenvironment. skills.summary: Compute per-cell pathway activity scores (e.g., angiogenesis) on a QC-passed single-cell RNA-seq dataset using the GSVA module in scWizard with MSigDB gene sets or a user-supplied GMT file, then aggregate and visualize scores by cell type to flag pathway-high populations, as demonstrated in the scWizard ICC case study.

skills.description: Use when two (or more) scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need a common low-dimensional embedding before batch-correction or integration comparison, and cells must be represented as points in N-dimensional space for distance-weighted matching.

skills.search_text: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when two (or more) scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need a common low-dimensional embedding before batch-correction or integration comparison, and cells must be represented as points in N-dimensional space for distance-weighted matching. skills.name: single-cell-perturbation-benchmark-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-perturbation-benchmark-analysis Use when comparing drug-responsive cell-type prioritization methods on scRNA-seq perturbation data where ground-truth target cell types are known and paired pre/post-treatment baselines must be evaluated against untreated-only inference. The goal is single-method application rather than cross-method benchmarking — just run the scRank pipeline (CreateScRank -> Constr_net -> rank_celltype) without comparator methods The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank's inhibitor-focused tpGRN model and its agonist/multi-target extensions are only preliminary (Figures S14, S17) No known ground-truth target cell types exist for the datasets, since the averaged-rank validation metric requires target-cell-type ranks http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks scRank's untreated-only target-perturbed GRN approach against paired-condition cell-type prioritization baselines (Augur, Wilcoxon, MAST, bimod, DESeq2) on simulated and real drug-perturbation scRNA-seq datasets with known target cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Benchmarks scRank's untreated-only target-perturbed GRN approach against paired-condition cell-type prioritization baselines (Augur, Wilcoxon, MAST, bimod, DESeq2) on simulated and real drug-perturbation scRNA-seq datasets with known target cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-method application rather than cross-method benchmarking — just run the scRank pipeline (CreateScRank -> Constr_net -> rank_celltype) without comparator methods The drug acts as an agonist or has multiple targets — scRank's inhibitor-focused tpGRN model and its agonist/multi-target extensions are only preliminary (Figures S14, S17) No known ground-truth target cell types exist for the datasets, since the averaged-rank validation metric requires target-cell-type ranks

skills.description: Use when comparing perturbed vs control single-cell RNA-seq cells and asking which pre-annotated gene modules/pathways (GMT-defined GMVs) are significantly differentially active, with module-level significance and a GSEA cross-check.
skills.name: single-cell-perturbation-differential-testing
skills.search_text: single-cell-perturbation-differential-testing Use when comparing perturbed vs control single-cell RNA-seq cells and asking which pre-annotated gene modules/pathways (GMT-defined GMVs) are significantly differentially active, with module-level significance and a GSEA cross-check. You have no prior gene-module annotation (GMT file) — VEGA's interpretable latent space and GMV testing require user-provided gene modules. The question is gene-level differential expression rather than module/pathway-level activity — use a standard DE tool instead of the VEGA BF test. The dataset is not count/normalized single-cell expression prepared per VEGA's preprocessing recommendations (article notes count-data handling as a limitation; SFig. 8). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Bayesian differential gene module activity testing with VEGA on single-cell perturbation data: computes log_e(Bayes Factors) for each gene module variable (GMV) between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control Kang PBMC innate immune cells) and benchmarks module calls against GSEA FDR values. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Bayesian differential gene module activity testing with VEGA on single-cell perturbation data: computes log_e(Bayes Factors) for each gene module variable (GMV) between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control Kang PBMC innate immune cells) and benchmarks module calls against GSEA FDR values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no prior gene-module annotation (GMT file) — VEGA's interpretable latent space and GMV testing require user-provided gene modules. The question is gene-level differential expression rather than module/pathway-level activity — use a standard DE tool instead of the VEGA BF test. The dataset is not count/normalized single-cell expression prepared per VEGA's preprocessing recommendations (article notes count-data handling as a limitation; SFig. 8).

skills.description: Use when a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3-batch COVID-19 atlas with age and disease severity condition types) requires predicting counts toward a held-out condition/batch combination, in-sample or out-of-sample.
skills.name: single-cell-perturbation-prediction
skills.search_text: single-cell-perturbation-prediction Use when a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3-batch COVID-19 atlas with age and disease severity condition types) requires predicting counts toward a held-out condition/batch combination, in-sample or out-of-sample. Each batch is measured under only one condition, so there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects Highly correlated condition types without combining them first — the article recommends creating a combined condition type (e.g., stim1_stim2, ctrl1_stim2) and training on it instead Single-batch, single-condition datasets where perturbation prediction across batches is not the goal — task-specific methods suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predicts gene expression responses to unseen biological conditions in multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data using scDisInFact, which disentangles shared-bio factors, condition-specific unshared-bio factors, and batch effect, and benchmarks against scGen and scPreGAN. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45227-w
skills.summary: Predicts gene expression responses to unseen biological conditions in multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq data using scDisInFact, which disentangles shared-bio factors, condition-specific unshared-bio factors, and batch effect, and benchmarks against scGen and scPreGAN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Each batch is measured under only one condition, so there is not enough information to fully disentangle batch and condition effects Highly correlated condition types without combining them first — the article recommends creating a combined condition type (e.g., stim1_stim2, ctrl1_stim2) and training on it instead Single-batch, single-condition datasets where perturbation prediction across batches is not the goal — task-specific methods suffice

skills.description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data (cell-by-gene matrices Y = perturbation group, Z = control group) where differing infected-cell cluster proportions between perturbation and control groups make fold-change perturbation effects unreliable and per-gRNA cellular response must be estimated.
skills.name: single-cell-perturbation-response-decoupling
skills.search_text: single-cell-perturbation-response-decoupling Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data (cell-by-gene matrices Y = perturbation group, Z = control group) where differing infected-cell cluster proportions between perturbation and control groups make fold-change perturbation effects unreliable and per-gRNA cellular response must be estimated. Disease tissues or intricate systems such as tumors where the Gaussian mixture assumption for expression distributions may not hold Extreme cases where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, so the same-cluster assumption between NT and perturbation groups fails Datasets with strong heterogeneity where cellular responses differ across cell clusters — scDecouple assumes similar responses across clusters and suits cells with moderate heterogeneity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Applies scDecouple's GMM-EM decoupling core to separate true cellular response of each gRNA from infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq, by fitting shared-K Gaussian mixture models to control and perturbation groups in selected PC space and running maximum-likelihood estimation of cluster proportions (lambda), response coefficients (beta), and precisions (M). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae011
skills.summary: Applies scDecouple's GMM-EM decoupling core to separate true cellular response of each gRNA from infected proportion bias in scCRISPR-seq, by fitting shared-K Gaussian mixture models to control and perturbation groups in selected PC space and running maximum-likelihood estimation of cluster proportions (lambda), response coefficients (beta), and precisions (M).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Disease tissues or intricate systems such as tumors where the Gaussian mixture assumption for expression distributions may not hold Extreme cases where some rare cell types are completely absent from infection, so the same-cluster assumption between NT and perturbation groups fails Datasets with strong heterogeneity where cellular responses differ across cell clusters — scDecouple assumes similar responses across clusters and suits cells with moderate heterogeneity

skills.description: Use when you have a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus per-cell categorical metadata (e.g., clone, site, or state labels from GEO metadata) and want a per-cell numeric score of how plastic (mixed) the ancestral context of each category is along the lineage.
skills.name: single-cell-plasticity-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-plasticity-quantification Use when you have a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus per-cell categorical metadata (e.g., clone, site, or state labels from GEO metadata) and want a per-cell numeric score of how plastic (mixed) the ancestral context of each category is along the lineage. The metadata of interest is continuous/numeric rather than categorical — Fitch-Hartigan small parsimony requires discrete character states The goal is to quantify relative fitness from the phylogeny — the article explicitly notes such approaches 'are not directly supported within our software' The tree leaves do not correspond one-to-one with metadata rows (e.g., mixed species or unmatched cell barcodes), since scores are assigned per leaf via sampleID http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 Quantifies per-cell 'plasticity' of user-provided categorical meta-data on a single-cell phylogeny, as implemented in the PhyloVision phyloAnalyze pipeline: Fitch-Hartigan small-parsimony scores computed on subtrees, edge-normalized, and averaged along root-to-leaf paths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100200
skills.summary: Quantifies per-cell 'plasticity' of user-provided categorical meta-data on a single-cell phylogeny, as implemented in the PhyloVision phyloAnalyze pipeline: Fitch-Hartigan small-parsimony scores computed on subtrees, edge-normalized, and averaged along root-to-leaf paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The metadata of interest is continuous/numeric rather than categorical — Fitch-Hartigan small parsimony requires discrete character states The goal is to quantify relative fitness from the phylogeny — the article explicitly notes such approaches 'are not directly supported within our software' The tree leaves do not correspond one-to-one with metadata rows (e.g., mixed species or unmatched cell barcodes), since scores are assigned per leaf via sampleID

skills.description: Use when you need per-cell stemness/pluripotency scores from a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) to identify stem/progenitor cells as trajectory origins, or to compare ORIGINS, LandSCENT, and CytoTRACE scores.
skills.name: single-cell-pluripotency-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-pluripotency-quantification Use when you need per-cell stemness/pluripotency scores from a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) to identify stem/progenitor cells as trajectory origins, or to compare ORIGINS, LandSCENT, and CytoTRACE scores. ORIGINS assumes the input matrix is a normalized expression matrix with genes as rows and cells as columns; a raw count matrix or a cell-by-gene matrix is the wrong input orientation/format The task is annotating cells by arbitrary biological processes other than differentiation — use ORIGINS2 or build a custom PPIN with build_ppin() instead of the differentiation network Only a Python environment is available without R — use PyOrigins rather than expecting the R activity() workflow verbatim http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Quantify per-cell pluripotency/stemness from scRNA-seq expression matrices using ORIGINS (differentiation PPIN activity), benchmarked against LandSCENT SR and CytoTRACE scores on four healthy human datasets (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Quantify per-cell pluripotency/stemness from scRNA-seq expression matrices using ORIGINS (differentiation PPIN activity), benchmarked against LandSCENT SR and CytoTRACE scores on four healthy human datasets (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383).
skills.when_to_use_negative: ORIGINS assumes the input matrix is a normalized expression matrix with genes as rows and cells as columns; a raw count matrix or a cell-by-gene matrix is the wrong input orientation/format The task is annotating cells by arbitrary biological processes other than differentiation — use ORIGINS2 or build a custom PPIN with build_ppin() instead of the differentiation network Only a Python environment is available without R — use PyOrigins rather than expecting the R activity() workflow verbatim

skills.name: single-cell-polya-expression-track-rendering
skills.search_text: single-cell-polya-expression-track-rendering Use when you need a per-gene genome-browser view (e.g., Fig. 1C) showing where poly(A) sites sit in a gene's 3'UTR and how single-cell pA counts and bulk BAM coverage change across sample groups such as SC/RS/ES. The goal is group-level statistics of pA usage (violin/box/bubble/dot plots) rather than a per-gene genomic view — use vizStats instead The input is raw Sierra MEX output or a scAPAtrap RDA that has not yet been converted into a PACdataset via readPACds/createPACdataset You need APA-marker detection or UMAP embedding of APA profiles — vizAPAmarkers or vizUMAP are the appropriate modules http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Render a genome-browser-like multi-track plot of a single gene's poly(A) site usage with vizAPA::vizTracks, layering the gene model, PACdataset pA positions, per-cell expression grouped by cell type, and BAM read-coverage tracks for one or more biological conditions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae099

skills.description: Use when you hold a scRNA-seq reference atlas with a cell-to-type identity file (e.g., the CCI distribution's data_ref/ cell-type and identity files for healthy BMMCs) and must report or verify the percentage composition of each annotated population.
skills.name: single-cell-population-frequency-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-population-frequency-quantification Use when you hold a scRNA-seq reference atlas with a cell-to-type identity file (e.g., the CCI distribution's data_ref/ cell-type and identity files for healthy BMMCs) and must report or verify the percentage composition of each annotated population. The single-cell dataset has no cell-type annotation or identity file, so cells cannot be assigned to the 17 hematopoietic populations before tabulation The goal is projecting leukemia subclusters onto the reference via CCI scores (BF probability) rather than summarizing the reference's own population composition Input is already a computed frequency or feature table rather than per-cell identity assignments Quantifies the relative abundance (counts and percentages) of annotated cell populations in a single-cell RNA-seq reference atlas, such as the healthy BMMC atlas of 18,751 cells from 4 healthy donors annotated into 17 hematopoietic populations, so that computed composition can be validated against paper-reported frequencies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41421-020-00223-4
skills.summary: Quantifies the relative abundance (counts and percentages) of annotated cell populations in a single-cell RNA-seq reference atlas, such as the healthy BMMC atlas of 18,751 cells from 4 healthy donors annotated into 17 hematopoietic populations, so that computed composition can be validated against paper-reported frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The single-cell dataset has no cell-type annotation or identity file, so cells cannot be assigned to the 17 hematopoietic populations before tabulation The goal is projecting leukemia subclusters onto the reference via CCI scores (BF probability) rather than summarizing the reference's own population composition Input is already a computed frequency or feature table rather than per-cell identity assignments

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether a hierarchical single-cell classifier detects truly novel populations: hold out a known population (e.g. 'Group 3' with four AMB nodes at tree layers 2 and 3) and measure the fraction of its cells rejected as unseen under alternative node classifiers.
skills.name: single-cell-population-rejection-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-population-rejection-evaluation Use when you need to test whether a hierarchical single-cell classifier detects truly novel populations: hold out a known population (e.g. 'Group 3' with four AMB nodes at tree layers 2 and 3) and measure the fraction of its cells rejected as unseen under alternative node classifiers. Datasets are not aligned: scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so running this rejection evaluation without prior alignment (e.g. scVI or scArches) is inappropriate The goal is classification accuracy on populations present in training rather than rejection of unseen populations — for accuracy comparisons use the classifiers' standard performance metrics instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark how well classifier variants within scHPL (linear SVM vs one-class SVM) reject cells from unseen cell populations held out from training, quantifying rejection rates and rendering per-node rejection fractions as a Fig. 3E-style heatmap. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23196-8
skills.summary: Benchmark how well classifier variants within scHPL (linear SVM vs one-class SVM) reject cells from unseen cell populations held out from training, quantifying rejection rates and rendering per-node rejection fractions as a Fig. 3E-style heatmap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are not aligned: scHPL is not a batch correction tool, so running this rejection evaluation without prior alignment (e.g. scVI or scArches) is inappropriate The goal is classification accuracy on populations present in training rather than rejection of unseen populations — for accuracy comparisons use the classifiers' standard performance metrics instead

skills.search_text: single-cell-population-separation-assessment Use when a trained deep learning model (Keras model JSON + weight bin, e.g. tmpMod./tmpWeight.bin) has classified single-cell gene expression data (e.g. Zheng sorted, Pancreas, CellBench) and you need to visually assess whether learned representations separate cell populations. You need hidden outputs from a branch of a branching model — layerUMAP cannot capture these; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead You want quantitative per-cell classification metrics rather than visual representation assessment — use the model's saved predictions (predicting.py) instead Input is raw sequence or expression data not yet passed through a trained model — no hidden-layer representations exist to visualize http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Visualize the last hidden-layer representations learned by a deep learning cell-type classifier (e.g. RFCN) in two-dimensional UMAP space using layerUMAP, coloring cells by known cell-type labels, and assess how UMAP parameters (n_neighbors, min_dist) and distance metrics affect separation of cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105530
