skills.when_to_use_negative: You need hidden outputs from a branch of a branching model — layerUMAP cannot capture these; capture them manually via Jupyter Notebook instead You want quantitative per-cell classification metrics rather than visual representation assessment — use the model's saved predictions (predicting.py) instead Input is raw sequence or expression data not yet passed through a trained model — no hidden-layer representations exist to visualize

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) need preprocessing and initial Louvain clustering prior to rare cell-type detection, e.g., as stage 1 of the scCAD cluster-decomposition workflow.
skills.name: single-cell-preprocessing-and-louvain-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-preprocessing-and-louvain-clustering Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) need preprocessing and initial Louvain clustering prior to rare cell-type detection, e.g., as stage 1 of the scCAD cluster-decomposition workflow. Input is already a normalized/feature-selected expression matrix or a precomputed cluster assignment — re-filtering at 3 cells and re-normalizing would double-transform the data The goal is rare-type scoring alone with an existing trusted partition; then only scCAD's decomposition and isolation-forest steps are needed, not re-clustering Data are bulk RNA-seq or spatial-resolved assays without single-cell count structure (cells x genes with sparse expression) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Standard scRNA-seq preprocessing and graph-based initial clustering as defined by scCAD: retain genes expressed in at least three cells, log-normalize with cell-specific size factors, project onto 40 PCs, build a k=15 KNN graph, and run Louvain to obtain initial (I-)clusters that serve as the starting point for downstream cluster decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51891-9
skills.summary: Standard scRNA-seq preprocessing and graph-based initial clustering as defined by scCAD: retain genes expressed in at least three cells, log-normalize with cell-specific size factors, project onto 40 PCs, build a k=15 KNN graph, and run Louvain to obtain initial (I-)clusters that serve as the starting point for downstream cluster decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized/feature-selected expression matrix or a precomputed cluster assignment — re-filtering at 3 cells and re-normalizing would double-transform the data The goal is rare-type scoring alone with an existing trusted partition; then only scCAD's decomposition and isolation-forest steps are needed, not re-clustering Data are bulk RNA-seq or spatial-resolved assays without single-cell count structure (cells x genes with sparse expression)

skills.description: Use when raw CITE-seq count matrices (transcriptome + surface-protein/ADT) from 10x Genomics or similar must be cleaned and prepared — e.g. pbmc_1k_protein_v3-style datasets — before pairwise-distance fusion and Louvain clustering in LinQ-View.
skills.name: single-cell-preprocessing-qc
skills.search_text: single-cell-preprocessing-qc Use when raw CITE-seq count matrices (transcriptome + surface-protein/ADT) from 10x Genomics or similar must be cleaned and prepared — e.g. pbmc_1k_protein_v3-style datasets — before pairwise-distance fusion and Louvain clustering in LinQ-View. Massive datasets (e.g. ~170K cells with 228 ADT features): LinQ-View failed there while Seurat 4 succeeded; the article recommends Seurat 4 for massive CITE-seq data with many ADT features. Datasets with large numbers of ADT features: the article states LinQ-View is best suited to large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50). Input is already a preprocessed/normalized Seurat object with QC complete — re-applying these thresholds would discard cells redundantly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 LinQ-View-style preprocessing and quality control for CITE-seq data: cell-level QC (gene and mitochondrial thresholds), normalization/scaling of both transcriptome and ADT modalities, HVG identification, and PCA ahead of joint multimodal clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100056
skills.summary: LinQ-View-style preprocessing and quality control for CITE-seq data: cell-level QC (gene and mitochondrial thresholds), normalization/scaling of both transcriptome and ADT modalities, HVG identification, and PCA ahead of joint multimodal clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Massive datasets (e.g. ~170K cells with 228 ADT features): LinQ-View failed there while Seurat 4 succeeded; the article recommends Seurat 4 for massive CITE-seq data with many ADT features. Datasets with large numbers of ADT features: the article states LinQ-View is best suited to large datasets with a limited number of ADT features (<50). Input is already a preprocessed/normalized Seurat object with QC complete — re-applying these thresholds would discard cells redundantly.

skills.description: Use when a trained SIMS model must emit per-cell classification confidences, or when novel/unseen cell types in the target AnnData should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a forced label.
skills.name: single-cell-probability-calibration
skills.search_text: single-cell-probability-calibration Use when a trained SIMS model must emit per-cell classification confidences, or when novel/unseen cell types in the target AnnData should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a forced label. The target dataset contains only cell types seen during training and no confidence gating is needed — direct predict()/label transfer suffices without calibration The model has not yet been trained or no validation split exists — temperature scaling requires held-out logits to fit the temperature parameter Cross-species label transfer is the goal — the paper states SIMS has only been validated within the same species, so 'unknown' flagging behavior across species is untested http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Post-hoc temperature scaling of a trained SIMS/TabNet single-cell classifier to convert raw logits into calibrated per-class probabilities, with a user-adjustable confidence threshold that flags low-confidence cells as 'unknown'. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Post-hoc temperature scaling of a trained SIMS/TabNet single-cell classifier to convert raw logits into calibrated per-class probabilities, with a user-adjustable confidence threshold that flags low-confidence cells as 'unknown'.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target dataset contains only cell types seen during training and no confidence gating is needed — direct predict()/label transfer suffices without calibration The model has not yet been trained or no validation split exists — temperature scaling requires held-out logits to fit the temperature parameter Cross-species label transfer is the goal — the paper states SIMS has only been validated within the same species, so 'unknown' flagging behavior across species is untested

skills.description: Use when query cells have been projected into a reference atlas embedding (e.g., via ProjectSVR's ProjectNewdata with a ref.umap reduction) and you must determine which mapped cells are well-placed versus low-quality outliers before downstream label transfer.
skills.name: single-cell-projection-outlier-detection
skills.search_text: single-cell-projection-outlier-detection Use when query cells have been projected into a reference atlas embedding (e.g., via ProjectSVR's ProjectNewdata with a ref.umap reduction) and you must determine which mapped cells are well-placed versus low-quality outliers before downstream label transfer. Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading and low mapQ may reflect novelty rather than technical failure; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first You have not yet projected the query into the reference UMAP space — the metric requires projected coordinates, not raw counts or an unprojected Seurat object Projecting across platforms (e.g., Smart-seq2 to 10x) where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions — interpret mapQ cautiously rather than as a clean outlier signal http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assesses the quality of query-cell projections onto a reference atlas UMAP using ProjectSVR's mean k-NN distance metric, with empirical p-values estimated from a null distribution of randomly sampled cells and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, to flag low-quality or outlier mapped cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Assesses the quality of query-cell projections onto a reference atlas UMAP using ProjectSVR's mean k-NN distance metric, with empirical p-values estimated from a null distribution of randomly sampled cells and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, to flag low-quality or outlier mapped cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel cell states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading and low mapQ may reflect novelty rather than technical failure; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first You have not yet projected the query into the reference UMAP space — the metric requires projected coordinates, not raw counts or an unprojected Seurat object Projecting across platforms (e.g., Smart-seq2 to 10x) where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions — interpret mapQ cautiously rather than as a clean outlier signal

skills.description: Use when benchmarking false-positive control of cell-type proportion analysis: null datasets with unchanged cluster proportions are simulated and accuracy (fraction of unchanged clusters correctly called non-significant) is scored per replicate or pseudo-replicate count.
skills.name: single-cell-proportion-null-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-proportion-null-simulation Use when benchmarking false-positive control of cell-type proportion analysis: null datasets with unchanged cluster proportions are simulated and accuracy (fraction of unchanged clusters correctly called non-significant) is scored per replicate or pseudo-replicate count. Clusters supported by less than 2% of all cells are present — the benchmarking found such rare clusters produce unstable results, so null-accuracy estimates for them are unreliable The goal is detecting real proportion changes rather than measuring false-positive control — use the proportion-change simulation workflow instead of the null simulation Input data is already summarized as a cell-type-by-sample count table outside AnnData — this skill assumes AnnData objects with sample/cluster/condition metadata columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A null-simulation benchmarking procedure that quantifies how well Scanpro controls false positives in differential proportion analysis, on both genuinely replicated single-cell data and pseudo-replicated data generated by its iteration-based bootstrapping. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-66381-7
skills.summary: A null-simulation benchmarking procedure that quantifies how well Scanpro controls false positives in differential proportion analysis, on both genuinely replicated single-cell data and pseudo-replicated data generated by its iteration-based bootstrapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters supported by less than 2% of all cells are present — the benchmarking found such rare clusters produce unstable results, so null-accuracy estimates for them are unreliable The goal is detecting real proportion changes rather than measuring false-positive control — use the proportion-change simulation workflow instead of the null simulation Input data is already summarized as a cell-type-by-sample count table outside AnnData — this skill assumes AnnData objects with sample/cluster/condition metadata columns

skills.description: Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq experiments show antibody-specific background from unbound antibodies, and both a cell protein matrix and an empty-droplet protein matrix are available.
skills.name: single-cell-protein-ambient-noise-correction
skills.search_text: single-cell-protein-ambient-noise-correction Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq experiments show antibody-specific background from unbound antibodies, and both a cell protein matrix and an empty-droplet protein matrix are available. No empty droplets are available in the experiment (use the dsb 'no_empty_drops' variant instead) Input is already normalized protein data (e.g. CLR-normalized or previously dsb-rescaled values), where re-standardization against empty droplets would be invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Denoises droplet-based single-cell protein (ADT) data by removing ambient, unbound-antibody background noise: protein counts in empty droplets estimate the expected ambient background per antibody, and each cell's log-transformed counts are standardized by that background's mean and standard deviation (dsb step I). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29356-8
skills.summary: Denoises droplet-based single-cell protein (ADT) data by removing ambient, unbound-antibody background noise: protein counts in empty droplets estimate the expected ambient background per antibody, and each cell's log-transformed counts are standardized by that background's mean and standard deviation (dsb step I).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No empty droplets are available in the experiment (use the dsb 'no_empty_drops' variant instead) Input is already normalized protein data (e.g. CLR-normalized or previously dsb-rescaled values), where re-standardization against empty droplets would be invalid

skills.description: Use when processing preprocessed single-cell proteomic imaging (4i) .h5ad datasets (e.g., PDAC cell lines or RPE with 241–253 imaging features) to select features that preserve cell cycle phases or cellular trajectories prior to trajectory inference.
skills.name: single-cell-proteomic-imaging-data-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-proteomic-imaging-data-processing Use when processing preprocessed single-cell proteomic imaging (4i) .h5ad datasets (e.g., PDAC cell lines or RPE with 241–253 imaging features) to select features that preserve cell cycle phases or cellular trajectories prior to trajectory inference. Input is already a curated feature set or the analysis goal is supervised feature selection with available manual annotations rather than unsupervised trajectory preservation Data are not single-cell profiles (e.g., bulk omics or imaging data without per-cell feature matrices), since the method relies on a cell-similarity graph over single-cell measurements http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Load and preprocess single-cell protein iterative immunofluorescence (4i) datasets as .h5ad AnnData objects and perform trajectory-preserving unsupervised feature selection (DELVE and benchmarked alternatives) so that downstream cell-type and cell-cycle trajectory analyses are not distorted by noisy or irrelevant imaging-derived features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Load and preprocess single-cell protein iterative immunofluorescence (4i) datasets as .h5ad AnnData objects and perform trajectory-preserving unsupervised feature selection (DELVE and benchmarked alternatives) so that downstream cell-type and cell-cycle trajectory analyses are not distorted by noisy or irrelevant imaging-derived features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature set or the analysis goal is supervised feature selection with available manual annotations rather than unsupervised trajectory preservation Data are not single-cell profiles (e.g., bulk omics or imaging data without per-cell feature matrices), since the method relies on a cell-similarity graph over single-cell measurements

skills.description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and ST data (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and need to map single cells into spatial coordinates or identify spatially variated cell subpopulations that traditional single-cell pipelines miss.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudo-space-reconstruction
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudo-space-reconstruction Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and ST data (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and need to map single cells into spatial coordinates or identify spatially variated cell subpopulations that traditional single-cell pipelines miss. Tissues with low spatial coherence, such as Patients 5 and 9 of SCC evaluated in the paper — the paper states scSpace should be applied cautiously there No appropriate spatial reference is available for the tissue (e.g. spatial ATAC-seq data was unavailable for the scATAC-seq attempt in the paper) Spatial domain identification of the ST data itself is the goal — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC which target ST spatial domains http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct spatial associations of single cells within scRNA-seq data by integrating a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference: scSpace uses transfer component analysis (TCA) to extract shared latent features, an MLP to project cells into a pseudo-space, and space-informed clustering to identify spatially heterogeneous subpopulations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Reconstruct spatial associations of single cells within scRNA-seq data by integrating a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference: scSpace uses transfer component analysis (TCA) to extract shared latent features, an MLP to project cells into a pseudo-space, and space-informed clustering to identify spatially heterogeneous subpopulations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Tissues with low spatial coherence, such as Patients 5 and 9 of SCC evaluated in the paper — the paper states scSpace should be applied cautiously there No appropriate spatial reference is available for the tissue (e.g. spatial ATAC-seq data was unavailable for the scATAC-seq attempt in the paper) Spatial domain identification of the ST data itself is the goal — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC which target ST spatial domains

skills.description: Use when a cell-to-landmark trajectory graph already exists and individual cells must be sequenced along developmental paths between adjacent landmark states to recover a pseudo-time axis.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudo-temporal-ordering
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudo-temporal-ordering Use when a cell-to-landmark trajectory graph already exists and individual cells must be sequenced along developmental paths between adjacent landmark states to recover a pseudo-time axis. The trajectory graph itself has not been built yet — this ordering is the final step and depends on upstream landmark construction and cell-to-landmark transition assignments Development starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath explicitly does not yet support this case The goal is estimating landmark state transitions from neighbourhood counts rather than ordering cells along already-defined edges Places individual single-cell RNA-seq cells in pseudo-temporal order along the multi-branching developmental trajectories constructed by Mpath, by ordering transitioning cells between neighbouring landmark states along each graph edge. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Places individual single-cell RNA-seq cells in pseudo-temporal order along the multi-branching developmental trajectories constructed by Mpath, by ordering transitioning cells between neighbouring landmark states along each graph edge.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectory graph itself has not been built yet — this ordering is the final step and depends on upstream landmark construction and cell-to-landmark transition assignments Development starts from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath explicitly does not yet support this case The goal is estimating landmark state transitions from neighbourhood counts rather than ordering cells along already-defined edges

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix captures cells from ordered developmental stages and the goal is to infer cell ordering (pseudo-time) and quantify it against known capture/stage time.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudo-time-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudo-time-inference Use when a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix captures cells from ordered developmental stages and the goal is to infer cell ordering (pseudo-time) and quantify it against known capture/stage time. The dataset lacks any ordered biological process (stages/capture times) against which a trajectory can be meaningfully evaluated Only a single trajectory-inference result is needed without low-dimensional embedding and scDHA's clustering/classification pipeline Input is already a low-dimensional embedding from another framework where scDHA's noise-detachment autoencoder step is not part of the validated workflow Reconstruct ordered developmental trajectories from scRNA-seq data by embedding cells in scDHA's low-dimensional space (non-negative kernel autoencoder + stacked Bayesian self-learning module) and applying scDHA.pt, benchmarking R-squared against Monocle, TSCAN, Slingshot, and SCANPY. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Reconstruct ordered developmental trajectories from scRNA-seq data by embedding cells in scDHA's low-dimensional space (non-negative kernel autoencoder + stacked Bayesian self-learning module) and applying scDHA.pt, benchmarking R-squared against Monocle, TSCAN, Slingshot, and SCANPY.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks any ordered biological process (stages/capture times) against which a trajectory can be meaningfully evaluated Only a single trajectory-inference result is needed without low-dimensional embedding and scDHA's clustering/classification pipeline Input is already a low-dimensional embedding from another framework where scDHA's noise-detachment autoencoder step is not part of the validated workflow

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. H5ad/HDF5/loom) must be converted into pseudo-bulk representative cells per cell type/sub-cluster before gene co-expression network inference with SCANet/WGCNA.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudobulk-aggregation
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudobulk-aggregation Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. H5ad/HDF5/loom) must be converted into pseudo-bulk representative cells per cell type/sub-cluster before gene co-expression network inference with SCANet/WGCNA. Input is already bulk or pseudo-bulk expression data with no per-cell counts to aggregate The goal is downstream TF–TG GRN reconstruction (GRNBoost2/RcisTarget) or drug-repurposing prediction rather than the upstream pseudo-bulk pre-processing step Data are raw unprocessed single-cell counts still requiring QC, normalization, and cell-type annotation before aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates single-cell scRNA-seq read counts into pseudo-bulk representative cells by averaging gene expression within N sub-clusters of each cell type, reducing data dimensionality before co-expression network (GCN) inference with modified WGCNA in SCANet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Aggregates single-cell scRNA-seq read counts into pseudo-bulk representative cells by averaging gene expression within N sub-clusters of each cell type, reducing data dimensionality before co-expression network (GCN) inference with modified WGCNA in SCANet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already bulk or pseudo-bulk expression data with no per-cell counts to aggregate The goal is downstream TF–TG GRN reconstruction (GRNBoost2/RcisTarget) or drug-repurposing prediction rather than the upstream pseudo-bulk pre-processing step Data are raw unprocessed single-cell counts still requiring QC, normalization, and cell-type annotation before aggregation

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether different scRNA-seq DS methods (edgeR/DESeq2/limma-voom pseudobulk vs MAST/dream mixed models) agree on top-ranked detections at FDR < 0.05, or when benchmarking muscat's pbDS/mmDS engines on simulated multi-sample data.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudobulk-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudobulk-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether different scRNA-seq DS methods (edgeR/DESeq2/limma-voom pseudobulk vs MAST/dream mixed models) agree on top-ranked detections at FDR < 0.05, or when benchmarking muscat's pbDS/mmDS engines on simulated multi-sample data. The data are already aggregated pseudobulk bulk-level counts without the cell-level sample_id/group_id/cluster_id metadata needed by muscat The goal is per-method power/FDR calibration against a known ground truth rather than between-method concordance of top-ranked detections Only a single sample per condition is available, so sample-level pseudobulk inference and replicate-wise set intersection are not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarking skill for differential state (DS) analysis of multi-sample multi-group scRNA-seq data: compare pseudobulk (pbDS) and cell-level mixed-model (mmDS) engines across simulation replicates by intersecting FDR<0.05 significant gene sets and assessing between-method concordance (e.g., UpSet plots as in the muscat Fig. 3 concordance analysis). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for differential state (DS) analysis of multi-sample multi-group scRNA-seq data: compare pseudobulk (pbDS) and cell-level mixed-model (mmDS) engines across simulation replicates by intersecting FDR<0.05 significant gene sets and assessing between-method concordance (e.g., UpSet plots as in the muscat Fig. 3 concordance analysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already aggregated pseudobulk bulk-level counts without the cell-level sample_id/group_id/cluster_id metadata needed by muscat The goal is per-method power/FDR calibration against a known ground truth rather than between-method concordance of top-ranked detections Only a single sample per condition is available, so sample-level pseudobulk inference and replicate-wise set intersection are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when you have raw scRNAseq count matrices with circadian (or other periodic) time labels and need bulk-like profiles so a predictor trained on bulk RNAseq or microarray data can score the samples.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudobulk-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudobulk-count-aggregation Use when you have raw scRNAseq count matrices with circadian (or other periodic) time labels and need bulk-like profiles so a predictor trained on bulk RNAseq or microarray data can score the samples. You need circadian time predictions for individual cells: tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and thus cannot predict circadian time at a single-cell level The single-cell data are not raw counts (e.g. already SCTransform-normalized/integrated matrices), since the aggregation step requires summing raw counts per gene across all cells Your test samples are diseased or circadian-disturbed and only a healthy-donor training time series exists; tauFisher trained on healthy data cannot provide diseased-sample timescales http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates raw single-cell RNAseq counts by summing per gene across all cells at each circadian time point to build pseudobulk samples, enabling bulk-trained circadian time predictors like tauFisher to be applied to single-cell data despite scRNAseq dropout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48041-6
skills.summary: Aggregates raw single-cell RNAseq counts by summing per gene across all cells at each circadian time point to build pseudobulk samples, enabling bulk-trained circadian time predictors like tauFisher to be applied to single-cell data despite scRNAseq dropout.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need circadian time predictions for individual cells: tauFisher cannot overcome the high sequencing dropout rate in scRNAseq and thus cannot predict circadian time at a single-cell level The single-cell data are not raw counts (e.g. already SCTransform-normalized/integrated matrices), since the aggregation step requires summing raw counts per gene across all cells Your test samples are diseased or circadian-disturbed and only a healthy-donor training time series exists; tauFisher trained on healthy data cannot provide diseased-sample timescales

skills.description: Use when individual-cell type pairs in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data have <=10 cells so ctp/ctnu entries were set to missing, and CTMM fitting requires a complete expression and noise-variance matrix.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudobulk-missingness-masking
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudobulk-missingness-masking Use when individual-cell type pairs in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data have <=10 cells so ctp/ctnu entries were set to missing, and CTMM fitting requires a complete expression and noise-variance matrix. All individual-cell type pairs already have >10 cells so no ctp/ctnu entries are missing — imputation is unnecessary. Only a small subset of genes is of interest — the benchmark supporting transcriptome-wide softImpute was computed across all genes, so gene-subset imputation lacks this validation. Sample size is below ~50 individuals — CTMM itself is unreliable there regardless of imputation quality. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Impute missing cell type-specific pseudobulk (ctp) and cell type-specific noise variance (ctnu) entries for individual-cell type pairs with too few cells using transcriptome-wide matrix completion (softImpute, called from Python via rpy2), which benchmarked best before fitting CTMM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Impute missing cell type-specific pseudobulk (ctp) and cell type-specific noise variance (ctnu) entries for individual-cell type pairs with too few cells using transcriptome-wide matrix completion (softImpute, called from Python via rpy2), which benchmarked best before fitting CTMM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All individual-cell type pairs already have >10 cells so no ctp/ctnu entries are missing — imputation is unnecessary. Only a small subset of genes is of interest — the benchmark supporting transcriptome-wide softImpute was computed across all genes, so gene-subset imputation lacks this validation. Sample size is below ~50 individuals — CTMM itself is unreliable there regardless of imputation quality.

skills.description: Use when pseudotime and branch probabilities were computed at the pseudobulk (neighbourhood) level via vdjPseudobulk and must be mapped back to individual cells in a miloR SingleCellExperiment, especially when some cells are unassigned to any neighbourhood.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudobulk-value-projection
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudobulk-value-projection Use when pseudotime and branch probabilities were computed at the pseudobulk (neighbourhood) level via vdjPseudobulk and must be mapped back to individual cells in a miloR SingleCellExperiment, especially when some cells are unassigned to any neighbourhood. Values are already at single-cell resolution (no pseudobulk milo object exists) — projecting again would double-aggregate. The trajectory has a cyclic topology (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which dandelionR's absorbing Markov chain pseudotime cannot represent. The dataset has too few cells for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. only ~972 cells), leaving most cells without a neighbourhood assignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branching probabilities such as 'CD8+T' and 'CD4+T') from a miloR pseudobulk object back to individual cells using dandelionR::projectPseudotimeToCell, removing cells that belong to no neighbourhood. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Projects pseudobulk-level trajectory results (pseudotime and branching probabilities such as 'CD8+T' and 'CD4+T') from a miloR pseudobulk object back to individual cells using dandelionR::projectPseudotimeToCell, removing cells that belong to no neighbourhood.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Values are already at single-cell resolution (no pseudobulk milo object exists) — projecting again would double-aggregate. The trajectory has a cyclic topology (e.g. B cell receptor editing), which dandelionR's absorbing Markov chain pseudotime cannot represent. The dataset has too few cells for miloR neighbourhood construction (e.g. only ~972 cells), leaving most cells without a neighbourhood assignment.

skills.description: Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (e.g. h5ad count matrices) lacks direction information and you need high-resolution, multi-branch trajectories plus per-cell pseudotime, especially with intricate topologies like parallel differentiation routes.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-assignment
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-assignment Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (e.g. h5ad count matrices) lacks direction information and you need high-resolution, multi-branch trajectories plus per-cell pseudotime, especially with intricate topologies like parallel differentiation routes. When time-resolved (time-course) data already provides direction so velocity inference is unnecessary When only a single pre-defined linear topology is expected and cluster-level tools like PAGA/Slingshot suffice When RNA velocity estimates are unreliable for the tissue (all velocity-based TI performance is limited by velocity inference accuracy) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assign cell-level pseudotime and branching/trajectory labels by integrating scRNA-seq expression with RNA velocity via CellPath: meta-cells are built with leiden clustering, a symmetric k-nn meta-cell graph is searched for candidate paths, a greedy algorithm selects major trajectories, and first-order pseudotime reconstruction maps cells onto paths. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100095
skills.summary: Assign cell-level pseudotime and branching/trajectory labels by integrating scRNA-seq expression with RNA velocity via CellPath: meta-cells are built with leiden clustering, a symmetric k-nn meta-cell graph is searched for candidate paths, a greedy algorithm selects major trajectories, and first-order pseudotime reconstruction maps cells onto paths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When time-resolved (time-course) data already provides direction so velocity inference is unnecessary When only a single pre-defined linear topology is expected and cluster-level tools like PAGA/Slingshot suffice When RNA velocity estimates are unreliable for the tissue (all velocity-based TI performance is limited by velocity inference accuracy)

skills.description: Use when a processed AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo RNA velocity plus Cytopath consensus trajectory steps are available and per-cell pseudotime and cell fate probabilities must be quantified.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-estimation Use when a processed AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo RNA velocity plus Cytopath consensus trajectory steps are available and per-cell pseudotime and cell fate probabilities must be quantified. The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty (e.g., spurious root/terminal states as seen in the erythroid gastrulation dataset); the authors do not expect trajectory inference to be meaningful in this case. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probability without discernible pattern as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset); the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath here. Input lacks velocity information — static expression profiles alone are ambiguous with respect to directionality of cell state transitions, undermining root/terminal assignment and pseudotime ordering. http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns each cell to inferred trajectory steps of Cytopath's consensus trajectories via alignment scores combining static expression and RNA velocity similarity, then derives per-cell pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation potential (Shannon entropy of fate vector). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Assigns each cell to inferred trajectory steps of Cytopath's consensus trajectories via alignment scores combining static expression and RNA velocity similarity, then derives per-cell pseudotime, fate probabilities, and differentiation potential (Shannon entropy of fate vector).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty (e.g., spurious root/terminal states as seen in the erythroid gastrulation dataset); the authors do not expect trajectory inference to be meaningful in this case. Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable (e.g., fuzzy root cell probability without discernible pattern as in the hepatocyte zonation dataset); the authors do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath here. Input lacks velocity information — static expression profiles alone are ambiguous with respect to directionality of cell state transitions, undermining root/terminal assignment and pseudotime ordering.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix from a cross-sectional cohort must be ordered along a one-dimensional biological progression without capture times, especially when covariates (stimulus, mutation, drug) may perturb the trajectory.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-inference Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix from a cross-sectional cohort must be ordered along a one-dimensional biological progression without capture times, especially when covariates (stimulus, mutation, drug) may perturb the trajectory. Features must evolve linearly with pseudotime — when strong nonlinear gene-pseudotime dynamics are expected, PhenoPath's linear assumption may be inappropriate When physical capture-time information is available and should be used directly for ordering (e.g. DeLorean-style capture-time models) rather than inferred When data require complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath cannot handle http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Infers per-cell pseudotimes (latent pathway scores) from single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices, here via PhenoPath, a Bayesian hybrid regression-latent variable model that can additionally modulate trajectories by covariates such as LPS/PAM stimulation status, using coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: Infers per-cell pseudotimes (latent pathway scores) from single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices, here via PhenoPath, a Bayesian hybrid regression-latent variable model that can additionally modulate trajectories by covariates such as LPS/PAM stimulation status, using coordinate ascent mean-field variational inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Features must evolve linearly with pseudotime — when strong nonlinear gene-pseudotime dynamics are expected, PhenoPath's linear assumption may be inappropriate When physical capture-time information is available and should be used directly for ordering (e.g. DeLorean-style capture-time models) rather than inferred When data require complex mixtures of continuous and discrete covariates in high-dimensional settings, which current PhenoPath cannot handle

skills.description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (cells × genes) must be ordered along a developmental trajectory, visualized in 2D, or split into branching differentiation paths.

skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-inference Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (cells × genes) must be ordered along a developmental trajectory, visualized in 2D, or split into branching differentiation paths. skills.summary: Infers single-cell pseudotime trajectories using DTFLOW: a kNN Markov graph, random walk with restart diffusion, Bhattacharyya kernel feature decomposition (BKFD) for 2D embedding, and root-distance pseudotime, optionally with RSKG branch detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one bifurcation event must be found and a simpler branch detector suffices — RSKG is aimed at multi-branching processes with multiple bifurcation points When the input is raw sequencing data rather than a pre-processed gene expression matrix — the article requires 'A. skills.description: Use when single cells have a sparse binary/eeSNV feature matrix with subgroup labels and the goal is a continuous genotype-based ordering (primary-to-metastasis trajectory) plus detection of subgroup-specific branches.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-ordering
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-ordering Use when single cells have a sparse binary/eeSNV feature matrix with subgroup labels and the goal is a continuous genotype-based ordering (primary-to-metastasis trajectory) plus detection of subgroup-specific branches. Input is already a gene-expression feature table rather than eeSNV/SNV-derived features — the article reports eeSNVs, not transcript abundance, achieve better subpopulation separation Cells lack subgroup labels or a known primary/root population, so the tree cannot be rooted for directional pseudo-time Goal is clustering alone without a continuous trajectory; a subpopulation classifier on eeSNVs is the simpler choice http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Monocle-style minimum spanning tree (MST) pseudo-time reconstruction computed on eeSNV features (the SSrGE-transformed matrix) to order single cells continuously, e.g., from primary (PDX-pRCC) to metastasized (Pt-mRCC, PDX-mRCC) tumors in the Kim dataset, while exposing intra-group ramification heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Monocle-style minimum spanning tree (MST) pseudo-time reconstruction computed on eeSNV features (the SSrGE-transformed matrix) to order single cells continuously, e.g., from primary (PDX-pRCC) to metastasized (Pt-mRCC, PDX-mRCC) tumors in the Kim dataset, while exposing intra-group ramification heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-expression feature table rather than eeSNV/SNV-derived features — the article reports eeSNVs, not transcript abundance, achieve better subpopulation separation Cells lack subgroup labels or a known primary/root population, so the tree cannot be rooted for directional pseudo-time Goal is clustering alone without a continuous trajectory; a subpopulation classifier on eeSNVs is the simpler choice

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple processing batches (e.g. the 10,878-cell human monocyte dataset) must be ordered along pseudotime without batch effects confounding the trajectory.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple processing batches (e.g. the 10,878-cell human monocyte dataset) must be ordered along pseudotime without batch effects confounding the trajectory. Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC's iterative self-learning may then fail to remove batch effects The analysis goal is purely discrete cell-type clustering with no temporal ordering, where soft-clustering probabilities alone suffice The user wants batch correction order-dependent pairwise methods (CCA, MNN, Seurat 3.0, Scanorama) rather than DESC's simultaneous all-batch embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstruct pseudotemporal cell trajectories by feeding the DESC low-dimensional embedding (X_Embeded_z in adata.obsm) into Monocle3, leveraging DESC's soft clustering probabilities that reveal pseudotemporal structure while removing batch effects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Reconstruct pseudotemporal cell trajectories by feeding the DESC low-dimensional embedding (X_Embeded_z in adata.obsm) into Monocle3, leveraging DESC's soft clustering probabilities that reveal pseudotemporal structure while removing batch effects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Technical differences across batches are larger than true biological variations — DESC's iterative self-learning may then fail to remove batch effects The analysis goal is purely discrete cell-type clustering with no temporal ordering, where soft-clustering probabilities alone suffice The user wants batch correction order-dependent pairwise methods (CCA, MNN, Seurat 3.0, Scanorama) rather than DESC's simultaneous all-batch embedding

skills.description: Use when you have a single-cell scRNA-seq count matrix with a differentiation hierarchy (e.g., basal-to-differentiated epithelium) and need to root a trajectory objectively by pluripotency scores rather than a priori marker assumptions.
skills.name: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when you have a single-cell scRNA-seq count matrix with a differentiation hierarchy (e.g., basal-to-differentiated epithelium) and need to root a trajectory objectively by pluripotency scores rather than a priori marker assumptions. The goal is only pluripotency/cell-annotation scoring (use ORIGINS/ORIGINS2 activity scores alone) and no trajectory or lineage structure is needed. The input is not a single-cell count matrix with an expected differentiation hierarchy (e.g., a bulk transcriptome or fully differentiated-only sample), so root selection by activity scores is not meaningful. A biologically validated root is already available and only the pseudotime computation is required; ORIGINS-based rooting adds an unnecessary step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run pseudotime trajectory inference on scRNA-seq data using ORIGINS-derived differentiation PPI network activity to select stem/progenitor cells as the trajectory root, then infer lineages (e.g., Slingshot) that branch from the root cluster into terminal cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Run pseudotime trajectory inference on scRNA-seq data using ORIGINS-derived differentiation PPI network activity to select stem/progenitor cells as the trajectory root, then infer lineages (e.g., Slingshot) that branch from the root cluster into terminal cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only pluripotency/cell-annotation scoring (use ORIGINS/ORIGINS2 activity scores alone) and no trajectory or lineage structure is needed. The input is not a single-cell count matrix with an expected differentiation hierarchy (e.g., a bulk transcriptome or fully differentiated-only sample), so root selection by activity scores is not meaningful. skills.description: Use when annotating unlabeled scRNA-seq query cells against a curated reference with known cell types, especially across datasets with batch effects, and when negative queries (cell types absent from the reference) must be rejected.
skills.name: single-cell-query-based-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-query-based-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating unlabeled scRNA-seq query cells against a curated reference with known cell types, especially across datasets with batch effects, and when negative queries (cell types absent from the reference) must be rejected. Query datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells — the over-parameterized DIRECTi model may be under-trained (3000 cells is generally sufficient) Mega-scale reference integration with highly skewed cell-type composition, which may cause over-correcting of batches Tasks needing a continuous latent embedding for exploratory dimensionality reduction rather than annotation transfer via cell querying http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Transfer cell-type annotations from curated scRNA-seq reference datasets to unlabeled query cells by searching references with Cell BLAST, which fits a DIRECTi generative model and ranks hits by distance between posterior distributions rather than cosine or LSH Hamming distance. Benchmarked with mean balanced accuracy over positive and negative queries, it outperformed scmap and CellFishing.jl, especially in rejecting negative queries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Transfer cell-type annotations from curated scRNA-seq reference datasets to unlabeled query cells by searching references with Cell BLAST, which fits a DIRECTi generative model and ranks hits by distance between posterior distributions rather than cosine or LSH Hamming distance. Benchmarked with mean balanced accuracy over positive and negative queries, it outperformed scmap and CellFishing.jl, especially in rejecting negative queries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query datasets with fewer than ~1000 cells — the over-parameterized DIRECTi model may be under-trained (3000 cells is generally sufficient) Mega-scale reference integration with highly skewed cell-type composition, which may cause over-correcting of batches Tasks needing a continuous latent embedding for exploratory dimensionality reduction rather than annotation transfer via cell querying

skills.search_text: single-cell-rare-cluster-reclustering Use when a Seurat object contains a broadly-defined cluster suspected to be heterogeneous (low median silhouette scores) and rare subpopulations of very low abundance may be masked by standard unsupervised clustering. skills.search_text: single-cell-read-splicing-status-prediction Use when single-cell RNA-seq reads aligned to a transcriptome need their spliced/unspliced status predicted, or when multi-gene mapped reads must be resolved to a single gene of origin. Reads are not single-cell scRNA-seq alignments against a spliceu augmented reference (the model scores oligo(dT) priming sites and fragment lengths specific to scRNA-seq). Reads that map uniquely to a single gene with no multi-gene ambiguity — splicing status prediction is the model's focus, and multi-gene rescue requires tied best genes. You need to distinguish fundamentally ambiguous reads arising from polyA tail priming within the terminal exon versus exon-derived cDNA fragments — Forseti as a mechanistic model cannot separate these two sources. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Apply Forseti, a mechanistic model combining a trained oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP and a cubic-spline fragment length distribution, to probabilistically assign splicing status and gene origin to scRNA-seq reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Apply Forseti, a mechanistic model combining a trained oligo(dT) binding-affinity MLP and a cubic-spline fragment length distribution, to probabilistically assign splicing status and gene origin to scRNA-seq reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not single-cell scRNA-seq alignments against a spliceu augmented reference (the model scores oligo(dT) priming sites and fragment lengths specific to scRNA-seq).
