skills.name: single-cell-reference-atlas-projection
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-atlas-projection Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (10x format or Seurat objects) must be interpreted in the stable coordinate system of a curated reference atlas, or when cell subtype composition of a query condition must be quantified and compared. The query population is not represented in the reference atlas — e.g., gamma-delta T cells are not represented at all, and CD4+ TILs are under-represented in the reference atlases The goal is de novo clustering of a heterogeneous dataset rather than interpreting query cells in a fixed reference coordinate system Only a label per cell is needed and re-embedding in the reference space is unnecessary — use the ProjecTILs.classifier mode instead of full projection, or a label-transfer-only tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Projects new scRNA-seq query data into the PCA/UMAP space of a curated reference single-cell atlas (e.g., the murine TIL or viral CD8 T cell atlases) with ProjecTILs, preserving the reference coordinate system, and transfers cell state labels via nearest-neighbor prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23324-4
skills.summary: Projects new scRNA-seq query data into the PCA/UMAP space of a curated reference single-cell atlas (e.g., the murine TIL or viral CD8 T cell atlases) with ProjecTILs, preserving the reference coordinate system, and transfers cell state labels via nearest-neighbor prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query population is not represented in the reference atlas — e.g., gamma-delta T cells are not represented at all, and CD4+ TILs are under-represented in the reference atlases The goal is de novo clustering of a heterogeneous dataset rather than interpreting query cells in a fixed reference coordinate system Only a label per cell is needed and re-embedding in the reference space is unnecessary — use the ProjecTILs.classifier mode instead of full projection, or a label-transfer-only tool

skills.description: Use when evaluating a segmentation method's cell-gene matrix for expression purity or cross-cell contamination, e.g. measuring B cells expressing T-cell markers (CD4, CD8A, CD8B, CD3D, CD3E) in Xenium breast cancer data.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-based-purity-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-based-purity-scoring Use when evaluating a segmentation method's cell-gene matrix for expression purity or cross-cell contamination, e.g. measuring B cells expressing T-cell markers (CD4, CD8A, CD8B, CD3D, CD3E) in Xenium breast cancer data. The input is raw imaging or transcript coordinates rather than an already-generated cell-gene expression matrix — run BIDCell's pipeline (make_cell_gene_mat) first No matched single-cell reference or marker definition files exist for the tissue, since the purity F1 scores depend on cell-type-specific top/bottom 10 percentile markers http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies segmentation purity and neighbour contamination by scoring BIDCell-segmented cells against a single-cell reference (TISCH-BRCA sc_breast.csv) using positive/negative marker F1 scores and distance-stratified expression of negative markers in B cells (Fig. 3a-e). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Quantifies segmentation purity and neighbour contamination by scoring BIDCell-segmented cells against a single-cell reference (TISCH-BRCA sc_breast.csv) using positive/negative marker F1 scores and distance-stratified expression of negative markers in B cells (Fig. 3a-e).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw imaging or transcript coordinates rather than an already-generated cell-gene expression matrix — run BIDCell's pipeline (make_cell_gene_mat) first No matched single-cell reference or marker definition files exist for the tissue, since the purity F1 scores depend on cell-type-specific top/bottom 10 percentile markers

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending the cross-platform generalisability benchmark of BIDCell on CosMx or MERSCOPE data, or when single-cell reference data are needed to guide biologically-informed segmentation and assess B-cell/T-cell marker contamination.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-based-segmentation-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-based-segmentation-annotation Use when reproducing or extending the cross-platform generalisability benchmark of BIDCell on CosMx or MERSCOPE data, or when single-cell reference data are needed to guide biologically-informed segmentation and assess B-cell/T-cell marker contamination. Input is Xenium breast cancer data — the dedicated Xenium workflow and xenium_example_config.yaml path should be used instead of the CosMx/MERSCOPE path Data come from a platform with no matching single-cell reference (reference csv must contain average expressions for genes in the spatial dataset) The goal is nuclei-only segmentation without cell-body delineation or biological loss terms — thresholding or pretrained models such as Cellpose or Mesmer may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Run the BIDCell pipeline with a public single-cell reference and positive/negative marker files to segment cells on non-Xenium SST platforms (NanoString CosMx lung, Vizgen MERSCOPE melanoma) and validate the segmentation via cell-type contamination and entropy-versus-CV metrics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Run the BIDCell pipeline with a public single-cell reference and positive/negative marker files to segment cells on non-Xenium SST platforms (NanoString CosMx lung, Vizgen MERSCOPE melanoma) and validate the segmentation via cell-type contamination and entropy-versus-CV metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Xenium breast cancer data — the dedicated Xenium workflow and xenium_example_config.yaml path should be used instead of the CosMx/MERSCOPE path Data come from a platform with no matching single-cell reference (reference csv must contain average expressions for genes in the spatial dataset) The goal is nuclei-only segmentation without cell-body delineation or biological loss terms — thresholding or pretrained models such as Cellpose or Mesmer may suffice

skills.description: Use when segmenting subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium breast cancer) with BIDCell and a single-cell reference plus marker files are needed to pre-annotate cells for biologically-informed training or cross-replicate cell type proportion comparison.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-cell-type-annotation Use when segmenting subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium breast cancer) with BIDCell and a single-cell reference plus marker files are needed to pre-annotate cells for biologically-informed training or cross-replicate cell type proportion comparison. The spatial dataset is from a tissue with no matching single-cell reference — the reference csv must cover the tissue/cell types of the spatial data (e.g. do not apply the breast cancer reference to brain tissue) Only nuclear segmentation is needed without cell type information — the marker-driven loss terms are optional inputs, not required to produce the *_connected.tif mask alone Reference genes do not overlap the spatial panel — the reference csv must contain average expressions for genes present in the spatial transcriptomic dataset (fewer than 1,000 genes suffice for segmentation) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Annotates predicted cells from BIDCell spatial transcriptomics segmentation with cell types using a single-cell sequencing reference (average expression per cell type) plus positive/negative marker gene lists, which feed BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions and the preannotate step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Annotates predicted cells from BIDCell spatial transcriptomics segmentation with cell types using a single-cell sequencing reference (average expression per cell type) plus positive/negative marker gene lists, which feed BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions and the preannotate step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The spatial dataset is from a tissue with no matching single-cell reference — the reference csv must cover the tissue/cell types of the spatial data (e.g. do not apply the breast cancer reference to brain tissue) Only nuclear segmentation is needed without cell type information — the marker-driven loss terms are optional inputs, not required to produce the *_connected.tif mask alone Reference genes do not overlap the spatial panel — the reference csv must contain average expressions for genes present in the spatial transcriptomic dataset (fewer than 1,000 genes suffice for segmentation)

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq ExpressionSet data must be deconvolved into cell type proportions and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (ExpressionSet or SingleCellExperiment) with cell type and subject annotations is available.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-deconvolution
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-deconvolution Use when bulk RNA-seq ExpressionSet data must be deconvolved into cell type proportions and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (ExpressionSet or SingleCellExperiment) with cell type and subject annotations is available. Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use read counts (RPKM only if cell-type-specific total RNA abundance estimates are provided) Only a single-subject scRNA-seq reference is available — MuSiC relies on cross-subject scRNA-seq to capture subject-to-subject variation in cell-type-specific expression The goal is absolute cell type proportions under unsatisfied efficiency assumptions — only the fraction of RNA molecules from each cell type, or trends of proportion change across subjects, can be recovered http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using cross-subject scRNA-seq references with MuSiC, a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) method that weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency instead of pre-selected markers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq data using cross-subject scRNA-seq references with MuSiC, a weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) method that weights genes by cross-subject and cross-cell consistency instead of pre-selected markers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input bulk data are TPM-normalized — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input; use read counts (RPKM only if cell-type-specific total RNA abundance estimates are provided) Only a single-subject scRNA-seq reference is available — MuSiC relies on cross-subject scRNA-seq to capture subject-to-subject variation in cell-type-specific expression The goal is absolute cell type proportions under unsatisfied efficiency assumptions — only the fraction of RNA molecules from each cell type, or trends of proportion change across subjects, can be recovered

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object, e.g. .qs/.rds) must be placed into a published reference atlas space for cell-type label transfer, cross-protocol batch-effect correction, pseudotime projection, or group composition comparison.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-mapping Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object, e.g. .qs/.rds) must be placed into a published reference atlas space for cell-type label transfer, cross-protocol batch-effect correction, pseudotime projection, or group composition comparison. Query cells contain novel states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first. Mapping across dissimilar platforms (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x), where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth. The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with integration-dependent mappers — but note ProjectSVR is specifically designed to avoid this dependency; do not substitute Seurat/scArches/Symphony/ProjecTILs for the continuous-state pseudotime use case (regression, not classification). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Project query single-cell RNA-seq data onto a pre-built reference atlas using ProjectSVR, which trains ensemble support vector regression models to predict reference UMAP embeddings from AUCell/UCell gene set activity scores, decoupling mapping from any specific integration method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf586
skills.summary: Project query single-cell RNA-seq data onto a pre-built reference atlas using ProjectSVR, which trains ensemble support vector regression models to predict reference UMAP embeddings from AUCell/UCell gene set activity scores, decoupling mapping from any specific integration method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells contain novel states absent from the reference — fixed-model projections may be misleading; compare unsupervised clustering to mapping results first. Mapping across dissimilar platforms (e.g. Smart-seq2 to 10x), where performance declines due to differing UMI distributions and sequencing depth. The reference atlas was built with a data-tailored integration strategy incompatible with integration-dependent mappers — but note ProjectSVR is specifically designed to avoid this dependency; do not substitute Seurat/scArches/Symphony/ProjecTILs for the continuous-state pseudotime use case (regression, not classification).

skills.description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a new 10x technology or donor) must be placed into an existing integrated reference embedding for label transfer, without re-running de novo integration on all raw cells.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-mapping Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a new 10x technology or donor) must be placed into an existing integrated reference embedding for label transfer, without re-running de novo integration on all raw cells. When the goal is novel cell type discovery — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone When the query contains populations very similar to an existing reference population — mapping metrics may be less informative about novelty When the reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage (Condition I), which limits equivalence with de novo Harmony integration http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Build a compressed, integrated single-cell reference atlas with Symphony (variable-gene selection, PCA, Harmony, reference compression) and map held-out query cells into the stable harmonized embedding to transfer annotations within seconds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Build a compressed, integrated single-cell reference atlas with Symphony (variable-gene selection, PCA, Harmony, reference compression) and map held-out query cells into the stable harmonized embedding to transfer annotations within seconds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is novel cell type discovery — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone When the query contains populations very similar to an existing reference population — mapping metrics may be less informative about novelty When the reference lacks comprehensive cell type coverage (Condition I), which limits equivalence with de novo Harmony integration

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing a malignancy-classifier gene panel by intersecting pan-cancer bulk RNA-seq DE genes (e.g. TCGA edgeR top-5000 lists) with high-variance genes from an integrated scRNA-seq matrix, and subsetting that matrix into a classifier-ready reference.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-matrix-subsetting
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-matrix-subsetting Use when building or reproducing a malignancy-classifier gene panel by intersecting pan-cancer bulk RNA-seq DE genes (e.g. TCGA edgeR top-5000 lists) with high-variance genes from an integrated scRNA-seq matrix, and subsetting that matrix into a classifier-ready reference. The input is already a trained feature panel or the downstream classifier's genes-scRNA-tcga-sorted.txt already exists with the expected 2,756 genes — no reconstruction is needed. The goal is generic variable-feature selection within a single scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Seurat FindVariableFeatures alone) rather than a bulk+single-cell integrated malignancy reference. A confident internal scRNA-seq reference with labeled malignant and non-malignant cells is available, making the TCGA-bulk-derived reference unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs scCancer2's bulk+single-cell feature-selection pipeline that builds the gene panel (GbulkDE ∪ GscHV, 2,756 genes) for the malignant-cell XGBoost reference matrix of 466,468 cells. It bridges pan-cancer TCGA bulk differential expression with single-cell high-variance features so the classifier works when no internal confident reference cells exist. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Reconstructs scCancer2's bulk+single-cell feature-selection pipeline that builds the gene panel (GbulkDE ∪ GscHV, 2,756 genes) for the malignant-cell XGBoost reference matrix of 466,468 cells. It bridges pan-cancer TCGA bulk differential expression with single-cell high-variance features so the classifier works when no internal confident reference cells exist.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a trained feature panel or the downstream classifier's genes-scRNA-tcga-sorted.txt already exists with the expected 2,756 genes — no reconstruction is needed. The goal is generic variable-feature selection within a single scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Seurat FindVariableFeatures alone) rather than a bulk+single-cell integrated malignancy reference. A confident internal scRNA-seq reference with labeled malignant and non-malignant cells is available, making the TCGA-bulk-derived reference unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you have scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq counts with cell-type and individual labels from the same tissue as your bulk RNA-seq samples and need a reference profile for cell-type proportion estimation (decomposition).
skills.name: single-cell-reference-profile-generation
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-profile-generation Use when you have scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq counts with cell-type and individual labels from the same tissue as your bulk RNA-seq samples and need a reference profile for cell-type proportion estimation (decomposition). When no reference profile is available (no single-cell data for the tissue) — use the marker-based BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition path instead, which estimates relative abundances from marker genes only When the labeled single-cell data come from a different tissue or its cell composition does not match the expected physiological composition (README scope statement) When single-cell measurements have known severe bias, e.g. severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest — the article advises caution since estimates will reflect the single-cell technology's proportions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a cell-type reference expression profile by averaging per-individual read-count abundances within each cell type from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data (GenerateSCReference), as the first stage of Bisque's reference-based decomposition, where the reference is combined with learned gene-specific bulk transformations before NNLS regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Builds a cell-type reference expression profile by averaging per-individual read-count abundances within each cell type from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data (GenerateSCReference), as the first stage of Bisque's reference-based decomposition, where the reference is combined with learned gene-specific bulk transformations before NNLS regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no reference profile is available (no single-cell data for the tissue) — use the marker-based BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition path instead, which estimates relative abundances from marker genes only When the labeled single-cell data come from a different tissue or its cell composition does not match the expected physiological composition (README scope statement) When single-cell measurements have known severe bias, e.g. severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest — the article advises caution since estimates will reflect the single-cell technology's proportions

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from complex tissue (e.g., 89 Fadista pancreatic islet donors) and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (e.g., E-MTAB-5060 Segerstolpe data), and need cell type proportions to test trait associations.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from complex tissue (e.g., 89 Fadista pancreatic islet donors) and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (e.g., E-MTAB-5060 Segerstolpe data), and need cell type proportions to test trait associations. Bulk expression input is TPM/normalized values without raw counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input Target cell types are extremely rare or highly collinear without a cluster-aware strategy — MuSiC's basic W-NNLS struggles with collinearity among closely related cell types The scRNA-seq reference is a single-subject library without pre-selected markers — the cross-subject MuSiC weighting cannot be exploited and existing marker-gene pitfalls apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq samples by MuSiC weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution against a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, enabling association analyses of cell composition with clinical phenotypes such as HbA1c in pancreatic islet data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Estimates cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq samples by MuSiC weighted non-negative least squares (W-NNLS) deconvolution against a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, enabling association analyses of cell composition with clinical phenotypes such as HbA1c in pancreatic islet data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bulk expression input is TPM/normalized values without raw counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input Target cell types are extremely rare or highly collinear without a cluster-aware strategy — MuSiC's basic W-NNLS struggles with collinearity among closely related cell types The scRNA-seq reference is a single-subject library without pre-selected markers — the cross-subject MuSiC weighting cannot be exploited and existing marker-gene pitfalls apply

skills.description: Use when you have a bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., 124-sample COVID-19 pseudobulk) plus a single-cell reference (annotated representative samples or public dataset) and need cell-type proportions comparable against ground truth.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation Use when you have a bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., 124-sample COVID-19 pseudobulk) plus a single-cell reference (annotated representative samples or public dataset) and need cell-type proportions comparable against ground truth. No single-cell reference exists — the article notes scSemiProfiler performs single-cell level deconvolution only 'provided there is a single-cell reference' The goal is true single-cell-resolution inference of within-cell-type variability, not cell-type-level proportion estimation, and no generative inference is feasible Input data are already single-cell profiles rather than bulk/pseudobulk measurements http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimates cell-type proportions from bulk/pseudobulk RNA-seq cohorts using single-cell references — either via scSemiProfiler's deep-generative single-cell-level deconvolution or by benchmarking against established deconvolution methods (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, Scaden, TAPE, EPIC, NNLS, MuSiC). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-50150-1
skills.summary: Estimates cell-type proportions from bulk/pseudobulk RNA-seq cohorts using single-cell references — either via scSemiProfiler's deep-generative single-cell-level deconvolution or by benchmarking against established deconvolution methods (CIBERSORTx, Bisque, Scaden, TAPE, EPIC, NNLS, MuSiC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No single-cell reference exists — the article notes scSemiProfiler performs single-cell level deconvolution only 'provided there is a single-cell reference' The goal is true single-cell-resolution inference of within-cell-type variability, not cell-type-level proportion estimation, and no generative inference is feasible Input data are already single-cell profiles rather than bulk/pseudobulk measurements

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-querying/annotation method remains tractable as the reference dataset grows to hundreds of thousands of cells, by timing queries across a range of subsampled reference sizes.
skills.name: single-cell-reference-subsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-reference-subsampling Use when evaluating whether a cell-querying/annotation method remains tractable as the reference dataset grows to hundreds of thousands of cells, by timing queries across a range of subsampled reference sizes. The question is about annotation accuracy rather than computational scalability — accuracy benchmarking is evaluated separately in the article The reference dataset is small (< 1,000 cells): the article notes small-sized datasets with fewer than 1000 cells may suffer from under-training issues of the over-parameterized DIRECTi model Reference cells are already embedded/searched via an index and no comparative timing across methods is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark how cell-querying methods (Cell BLAST/DIRECTi, scmap, CellFishing.jl) scale by subsampling a 1.3M mouse brain scRNA-seq reference from 1,000 to 1,000,000 cells and recording wall-clock querying time against the Marques query dataset, reproducing the Fig. 2d scalability comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17281-7
skills.summary: Benchmark how cell-querying methods (Cell BLAST/DIRECTi, scmap, CellFishing.jl) scale by subsampling a 1.3M mouse brain scRNA-seq reference from 1,000 to 1,000,000 cells and recording wall-clock querying time against the Marques query dataset, reproducing the Fig. 2d scalability comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about annotation accuracy rather than computational scalability — accuracy benchmarking is evaluated separately in the article The reference dataset is small (< 1,000 cells): the article notes small-sized datasets with fewer than 1000 cells may suffer from under-training issues of the over-parameterized DIRECTi model Reference cells are already embedded/searched via an index and no comparative timing across methods is needed

skills.description: Use when evaluating how well CSNI methods (e.g. pySCENIC, LIONESS, SSN) recover cell-specific regulatory interactions, and simulated single-cell data with known cellwise ground-truth GRNs is available for quantitative AUROC/AUPR evaluation.
skills.name: single-cell-regulatory-network-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-regulatory-network-inference Use when evaluating how well CSNI methods (e.g. pySCENIC, LIONESS, SSN) recover cell-specific regulatory interactions, and simulated single-cell data with known cellwise ground-truth GRNs is available for quantitative AUROC/AUPR evaluation. The data lack ground-truth cellwise regulatory interactions (e.g. dyngen does not generate motif data, so motif-analysis filtering steps cannot be applied) The analysis goal is bulk or population-level GRN inference rather than per-cell (cell-specific) regulatory networks You need to evaluate trajectory, RNA velocity, or trajectory alignment methods — these use dyngen's other ground-truth layers and different evaluation metrics such as ABWAP http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark cell-specific network inference (CSNI) methods by reconstructing per-cell gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics and scoring them against dyngen's ground-truth cellwise regulatory networks using mean AUROC and AUPR over 42 simulated datasets (14 backbones x 3 seeds). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-specific network inference (CSNI) methods by reconstructing per-cell gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics and scoring them against dyngen's ground-truth cellwise regulatory networks using mean AUROC and AUPR over 42 simulated datasets (14 backbones x 3 seeds).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data lack ground-truth cellwise regulatory interactions (e.g. dyngen does not generate motif data, so motif-analysis filtering steps cannot be applied) The analysis goal is bulk or population-level GRN inference rather than per-cell (cell-specific) regulatory networks You need to evaluate trajectory, RNA velocity, or trajectory alignment methods — these use dyngen's other ground-truth layers and different evaluation metrics such as ABWAP

skills.description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq time courses of TF-mediated reprogramming (e.g., 10x Chromium data with Monocle-annotated trajectory states) to identify and rank regulators of successful fate conversion.
skills.name: single-cell-reprogramming-data-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-reprogramming-data-analysis Use when analyzing scRNA-seq time courses of TF-mediated reprogramming (e.g., 10x Chromium data with Monocle-annotated trajectory states) to identify and rank regulators of successful fate conversion. Input is bulk RNA-seq or lacks single-cell resolution — CellOracle GRN inference and state-specific perturbation simulation require single-cell transcriptome (+ epigenome) data The question is discrete cell-type labeling rather than trajectory-based GRN reconfiguration and perturbation ranking — use Capybara-style classification instead No known reprogramming cocktail exists for validation, since the ranking should be sanity-checked against transgene components (Hnf4α-Foxa1 at rank 1) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproducible single-cell analysis of direct lineage reprogramming (e.g., MEF-to-iEP conversion) that infers state-specific gene regulatory networks with CellOracle and simulates TF perturbations to rank candidate regulators of cell identity conversion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Reproducible single-cell analysis of direct lineage reprogramming (e.g., MEF-to-iEP conversion) that infers state-specific gene regulatory networks with CellOracle and simulates TF perturbations to rank candidate regulators of cell identity conversion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or lacks single-cell resolution — CellOracle GRN inference and state-specific perturbation simulation require single-cell transcriptome (+ epigenome) data The question is discrete cell-type labeling rather than trajectory-based GRN reconfiguration and perturbation ranking — use Capybara-style classification instead No known reprogramming cocktail exists for validation, since the ranking should be sanity-checked against transgene components (Hnf4α-Foxa1 at rank 1)

skills.description: Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts (e.g., CITE-seq/REAP-seq RNA matrices, cTPnet_demo 4000-cell demo) must be denoised before protein imputation or other downstream modeling.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-count-denoising
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-count-denoising Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts (e.g., CITE-seq/REAP-seq RNA matrices, cTPnet_demo 4000-cell demo) must be denoised before protein imputation or other downstream modeling. Expression data are already TPM- or RPKM-normalized or otherwise non-UMI — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) input, and accuracy on TPM/RPKM CITE-seq data is untested The matrix has already been denoised/normalized (e.g., an existing LogNormalize'd Seurat object) and only needs downstream imputation The goal is protein imputation itself rather than the denoising/normalization preprocessing stage http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Denoises raw UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices with SAVER-X (default parameters) to obtain more accurate transcript relative-abundance estimates, as the recommended first step of the cTP-net surface-protein-imputation pipeline before Seurat LogNormalize. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14391-0
skills.summary: Denoises raw UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices with SAVER-X (default parameters) to obtain more accurate transcript relative-abundance estimates, as the recommended first step of the cTP-net surface-protein-imputation pipeline before Seurat LogNormalize.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are already TPM- or RPKM-normalized or otherwise non-UMI — cTP-net can only apply to count-based (UMI) input, and accuracy on TPM/RPKM CITE-seq data is untested The matrix has already been denoised/normalized (e.g., an existing LogNormalize'd Seurat object) and only needs downstream imputation The goal is protein imputation itself rather than the denoising/normalization preprocessing stage

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq UMI counts (e.g. 10x h5/h5ad matrices from GEO like GSE117825 or Synapse syn26320732) must be converted into log CPTT-normalized AnnData before scTriangulate integration.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-count-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-count-normalization Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq UMI counts (e.g. 10x h5/h5ad matrices from GEO like GSE117825 or Synapse syn26320732) must be converted into log CPTT-normalized AnnData before scTriangulate integration. Input data is already normalized log CPTT or you only have ADT/ATAC modalities, where the article prescribes CLR normalization instead of RNA CPTT You are performing data-level multimodal integration (Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) that requires a joint latent space rather than decision-level annotation integration on normalized counts AnnData already contains adata.raw — per the README this must be removed first, so normalization alone is insufficient until adata.raw is deleted http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Normalize raw single-cell RNA UMI count matrices to logarithmic counts per ten thousand (log CPTT) within AnnData so that subsequent scTriangulate stability scoring, clustering, and mix-and-match integration operate on a comparable scale. scTriangulate assumes adata.X is properly normalized before computing TFIDF/reassign scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Normalize raw single-cell RNA UMI count matrices to logarithmic counts per ten thousand (log CPTT) within AnnData so that subsequent scTriangulate stability scoring, clustering, and mix-and-match integration operate on a comparable scale. scTriangulate assumes adata.X is properly normalized before computing TFIDF/reassign scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already normalized log CPTT or you only have ADT/ATAC modalities, where the article prescribes CLR normalization instead of RNA CPTT You are performing data-level multimodal integration (Seurat-WNN, TotalVI) that requires a joint latent space rather than decision-level annotation integration on normalized counts AnnData already contains adata.raw — per the README this must be removed first, so normalization alone is insufficient until adata.raw is deleted

skills.description: Use when evaluating how well a denoising method recovers true expression profiles from severely downsampled scRNA-seq data (70% transcript removal), particularly for rare cell states like pericytes, microfold cells, or microglial cells.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-denoising-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-denoising-benchmarking Use when evaluating how well a denoising method recovers true expression profiles from severely downsampled scRNA-seq data (70% transcript removal), particularly for rare cell states like pericytes, microfold cells, or microglial cells. Input is already full-depth data with no downsampled baseline — without 70% transcript removal there is no controlled correlation-increase target to compute. Goal is gene network (GRN) inference from single-cell data rather than benchmarking expression-profile denoising. Data are spatial omics or non-primary/non-human/non-mouse cells — the scPRINT preprocessing scope keeps only primary cells from humans or mice and drops spatial omics datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces scPRINT's zero-shot denoising benchmark: downsample scRNA-seq test profiles (70% transcript removal via zero-inflated Poisson), denoise with pretrained scPRINT, MAGIC (Scanpy), and KNNsmoothing2, and rank methods by Spearman correlation increase to true profiles, especially on rare cell states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-58699-1
skills.summary: Reproduces scPRINT's zero-shot denoising benchmark: downsample scRNA-seq test profiles (70% transcript removal via zero-inflated Poisson), denoise with pretrained scPRINT, MAGIC (Scanpy), and KNNsmoothing2, and rank methods by Spearman correlation increase to true profiles, especially on rare cell states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already full-depth data with no downsampled baseline — without 70% transcript removal there is no controlled correlation-increase target to compute. Goal is gene network (GRN) inference from single-cell data rather than benchmarking expression-profile denoising. Data are spatial omics or non-primary/non-human/non-mouse cells — the scPRINT preprocessing scope keeps only primary cells from humans or mice and drops spatial omics datasets.

skills.description: Use when you have labeled cell-by-gene single-cell RNA-seq matrices (AnnData .h5ad or CSV) with a 'class_label' annotation and need automated label transfer to unlabeled cells, especially with many cell types or imbalanced labels.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-expression-classification
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-expression-classification Use when you have labeled cell-by-gene single-cell RNA-seq matrices (AnnData .h5ad or CSV) with a 'class_label' annotation and need automated label transfer to unlabeled cells, especially with many cell types or imbalanced labels. Prediction across species is desired — the authors 'limited our work to samples within the same species' because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species No pre-existing cell-type annotations are available for training, since SIMS is supervised and relies on labels derived from normalization, clustering, and expert annotation Metadata such as sequencing technology or cell line must be integrated into the model — this is a proposed future direction and is not implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains SIMS, a TabNet-based deep-learning classifier implemented in PyTorch Lightning, to transfer cell-type labels from annotated single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData .h5ad) to unlabeled cells, with accuracy/F1 evaluation and attention-based explainability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Trains SIMS, a TabNet-based deep-learning classifier implemented in PyTorch Lightning, to transfer cell-type labels from annotated single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData .h5ad) to unlabeled cells, with accuracy/F1 evaluation and attention-based explainability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prediction across species is desired — the authors 'limited our work to samples within the same species' because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species No pre-existing cell-type annotations are available for training, since SIMS is supervised and relies on labels derived from normalization, clustering, and expert annotation Metadata such as sequencing technology or cell line must be integrated into the model — this is a proposed future direction and is not implemented

skills.description: Use when you need to transfer cell-type annotations from a labeled single-cell RNA-seq reference (e.g., .h5ad AnnData with a 'class_label' column) to unlabeled query cells, even across datasets with different gene panels or cell lines.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-label-transfer
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-label-transfer Use when you need to transfer cell-type annotations from a labeled single-cell RNA-seq reference (e.g., .h5ad AnnData with a 'class_label' column) to unlabeled query cells, even across datasets with different gene panels or cell lines. Query cells come from a different species than the training reference — the authors limited validation to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species No pre-existing annotations are available for any reference dataset — SIMS is supervised and relies on pre-existing annotations (clustering, differential expression, expert annotation) The input is not a cell x gene expression matrix (e.g., gene x cell) — SIMS requires cells as rows since training samples are individual-cell transcriptomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train and apply SIMS, a TabNet-based deep-learning pipeline implemented in PyTorch Lightning, to transfer cell-type labels across single-cell RNA-seq datasets, including benchmarks against scANVI, Seurat, scNym, SingleR, and SciBet and cross-cell-line/organoid prediction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2024.100581
skills.summary: Train and apply SIMS, a TabNet-based deep-learning pipeline implemented in PyTorch Lightning, to transfer cell-type labels across single-cell RNA-seq datasets, including benchmarks against scANVI, Seurat, scNym, SingleR, and SciBet and cross-cell-line/organoid prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query cells come from a different species than the training reference — the authors limited validation to samples within the same species because neuronal subtypes diverge significantly between species No pre-existing annotations are available for any reference dataset — SIMS is supervised and relies on pre-existing annotations (clustering, differential expression, expert annotation) The input is not a cell x gene expression matrix (e.g., gene x cell) — SIMS requires cells as rows since training samples are individual-cell transcriptomes

skills.description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq reference (e.g., Allen Institute cortical taxonomy or Whole_miniatlas_meta.csv BRCA annotations) must be projected onto a 10x Visium slice to resolve per-spot cell-type composition and localize structures like TLS or cortical layers.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-reference-mapping Use when an annotated scRNA-seq reference (e.g., Allen Institute cortical taxonomy or Whole_miniatlas_meta.csv BRCA annotations) must be projected onto a 10x Visium slice to resolve per-spot cell-type composition and localize structures like TLS or cortical layers. Datasets are profiled from the same cells (vertical integration) or share no genes (diagonal integration) — use up.Run with mode='v' or mode='d' instead of the horizontal default When computing memory cannot hold the dense global OT matrix T — the paper warns capacity 'should be ascertained before using this option' (save_OT) Input is raw spatial data needing normalization/annotation itself without a matched annotated scRNA reference available http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Map an annotated single-cell RNA-seq reference onto spatial transcriptomics (10x Visium) data via uniPort's coupled-VAE plus Minibatch unbalanced optimal transport, using the global OT plan — rather than the latent space — to transfer cell-type labels and deconvolute per-spot cell-type proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Map an annotated single-cell RNA-seq reference onto spatial transcriptomics (10x Visium) data via uniPort's coupled-VAE plus Minibatch unbalanced optimal transport, using the global OT plan — rather than the latent space — to transfer cell-type labels and deconvolute per-spot cell-type proportions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets are profiled from the same cells (vertical integration) or share no genes (diagonal integration) — use up.Run with mode='v' or mode='d' instead of the horizontal default When computing memory cannot hold the dense global OT matrix T — the paper warns capacity 'should be ascertained before using this option' (save_OT) Input is raw spatial data needing normalization/annotation itself without a matched annotated scRNA reference available

skills.description: Use when a cell-type or cell-state classifier trained on scRNA-seq data (.h5ad anndata, e.g. PBMCs-BS top-3,500 scaLR features) must be scored on a held-out test set, or when benchmarking prediction accuracy across annotation pipelines.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-accuracy-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-accuracy-evaluation Use when a cell-type or cell-state classifier trained on scRNA-seq data (.h5ad anndata, e.g. PBMCs-BS top-3,500 scaLR features) must be scored on a held-out test set, or when benchmarking prediction accuracy across annotation pipelines. The goal is biomarker ranking rather than classification accuracy — several comparison tools (scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) cannot extract top features, limiting comparability of feature importance Data has not been preprocessed into the expected anndata format (log1p-normalized adata.X, cell metadata in obs with target column) — scaLR's performance may vary based on input data format Evaluating differential gene expression or DGE biomarker analysis (Pseudo bulk / LMEM), which is a separate downstream module http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Evaluates a trained single-cell classifier (e.g. scaLR DNN on top-3,500 features) on a held-out test set using precision, recall, f1-score, and accuracy, and aggregates per-pipeline accuracy alongside wall-clock time and peak memory into a comparison table (e.g. pipeline_comparison_metrics.csv reproducing Table 3 of scaLR). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: Evaluates a trained single-cell classifier (e.g. scaLR DNN on top-3,500 features) on a held-out test set using precision, recall, f1-score, and accuracy, and aggregates per-pipeline accuracy alongside wall-clock time and peak memory into a comparison table (e.g. pipeline_comparison_metrics.csv reproducing Table 3 of scaLR).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biomarker ranking rather than classification accuracy — several comparison tools (scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) cannot extract top features, limiting comparability of feature importance Data has not been preprocessed into the expected anndata format (log1p-normalized adata.X, cell metadata in obs with target column) — scaLR's performance may vary based on input data format Evaluating differential gene expression or DGE biomarker analysis (Pseudo bulk / LMEM), which is a separate downstream module

skills.description: Use when input is full-length scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g., SMART-seq2, such as the E-MTAB-9801 human fetal bone marrow dataset) and per-cell sorted BAM alignments free of PCR duplicates are needed for downstream isoform/IPA analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-alignment-and-pcr-duplicate-removal
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-alignment-and-pcr-duplicate-removal Use when input is full-length scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g., SMART-seq2, such as the E-MTAB-9801 human fetal bone marrow dataset) and per-cell sorted BAM alignments free of PCR duplicates are needed for downstream isoform/IPA analysis. Input is 10x Genomics or other UMI-based droplet scRNA-seq — duplicate marking should rely on UMIs (e.g., alevin-fry) rather than samtools rmdup positional duplicate removal The goal is only gene-level expression quantification from bulk RNA-seq, where duplicate removal choices differ and IPA identification is not required Reads are already aligned and duplicate-marked BAMs are provided as input — re-aligning and re-running rmdup could remove legitimate reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Preprocessing skill for full-length single-cell RNA-seq (SMART-seq2): align each cell's reads to the GRCh38 reference with HISAT2 and remove PCR duplicates with samtools rmdup, producing coordinate-sorted BAMs suitable for IPA site identification with InPACT. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46875-8
skills.summary: Preprocessing skill for full-length single-cell RNA-seq (SMART-seq2): align each cell's reads to the GRCh38 reference with HISAT2 and remove PCR duplicates with samtools rmdup, producing coordinate-sorted BAMs suitable for IPA site identification with InPACT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is 10x Genomics or other UMI-based droplet scRNA-seq — duplicate marking should rely on UMIs (e.g., alevin-fry) rather than samtools rmdup positional duplicate removal The goal is only gene-level expression quantification from bulk RNA-seq, where duplicate removal choices differ and IPA identification is not required Reads are already aligned and duplicate-marked BAMs are provided as input — re-aligning and re-running rmdup could remove legitimate reads

skills.description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq samples or datasets need batch correction and integration, and prior (even partial or noisy) cell type annotations are available to preserve biological variance.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-anchor-based-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-anchor-based-integration Use when multiple scRNA-seq samples or datasets need batch correction and integration, and prior (even partial or noisy) cell type annotations are available to preserve biological variance. Input consists of a single dataset with no batches to correct — anchor-based integration is unnecessary No cell type information is available and unbiased batch mixing (e.g., of technical replicates only) is the sole goal — cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics/integration may suffice, though STACAS remains robust to missing labels Cell types of interest are present in only one dataset, making alignment and evaluation (e.g., CiLISI) uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Semi-supervised, anchor-based batch-effect correction of scRNA-seq datasets using STACAS, which leverages prior cell type labels to preserve biological variability while integrating multiple samples into a common embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45240-z
skills.summary: Semi-supervised, anchor-based batch-effect correction of scRNA-seq datasets using STACAS, which leverages prior cell type labels to preserve biological variability while integrating multiple samples into a common embedding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of a single dataset with no batches to correct — anchor-based integration is unnecessary No cell type information is available and unbiased batch mixing (e.g., of technical replicates only) is the sole goal — cell type-agnostic batch mixing metrics/integration may suffice, though STACAS remains robust to missing labels Cell types of interest are present in only one dataset, making alignment and evaluation (e.g., CiLISI) uninformative

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with simulated ground-truth labels, or when deciding between EasyCellType-style marker-database querying and supervised tools like scPred or SingleR.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-annotation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-annotation-benchmarking Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with simulated ground-truth labels, or when deciding between EasyCellType-style marker-database querying and supervised tools like scPred or SingleR. Input is real data without ground-truth labels — accuracy cannot be computed, so a quantitative benchmark is not the right framing The goal is a single dataset's annotation rather than a method comparison — run EasyCellType or SingleR directly instead of building a benchmark harness Input is already an annotation output (predicted labels table); this skill starts from count matrices, not post-hoc label reconciliation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill for comparing cell-type annotation tools on scRNA-seq data: simulate PBMC datasets with known ground-truth labels, run supervised tools (Garnett, scPred, SingleR) and marker-based tools (EasyCellType's GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test soft/hard classifiers), and score per-cell annotation accuracy. It exists to quantify when marker-database querying is comparable to supervised reference-based annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for comparing cell-type annotation tools on scRNA-seq data: simulate PBMC datasets with known ground-truth labels, run supervised tools (Garnett, scPred, SingleR) and marker-based tools (EasyCellType's GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test soft/hard classifiers), and score per-cell annotation accuracy. It exists to quantify when marker-database querying is comparable to supervised reference-based annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real data without ground-truth labels — accuracy cannot be computed, so a quantitative benchmark is not the right framing The goal is a single dataset's annotation rather than a method comparison — run EasyCellType or SingleR directly instead of building a benchmark harness Input is already an annotation output (predicted labels table); this skill starts from count matrices, not post-hoc label reconciliation

skills.description: Use when comparing wall-clock runtime or novel-cell-detection performance of scRNA-seq annotation tools as dataset size grows from ~1k to million-scale cells, e.g. showing whether a tool scales efficiently versus scmap-cluster/scPred.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-benchmarking Use when comparing wall-clock runtime or novel-cell-detection performance of scRNA-seq annotation tools as dataset size grows from ~1k to million-scale cells, e.g. showing whether a tool scales efficiently versus scmap-cluster/scPred. The goal is annotation accuracy on a single small dataset without a runtime or scaling comparison across dataset sizes The datasets lack labeled reference sets, since scPred and scmap-cluster require labeled references for the comparison splits Data are not single-cell transcriptomic count matrices (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature tables) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking runtime and detection performance of single-cell novel-cell discovery tools (scNovel, scmap-cluster, scPred) across datasets spanning ~1k cells (Darmanis) to the million-scale TM atlas, after Scanpy preprocessing (normalize_total to 1e4 + log1p). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Benchmarking runtime and detection performance of single-cell novel-cell discovery tools (scNovel, scmap-cluster, scPred) across datasets spanning ~1k cells (Darmanis) to the million-scale TM atlas, after Scanpy preprocessing (normalize_total to 1e4 + log1p).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is annotation accuracy on a single small dataset without a runtime or scaling comparison across dataset sizes The datasets lack labeled reference sets, since scPred and scmap-cluster require labeled references for the comparison splits Data are not single-cell transcriptomic count matrices (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or pre-computed feature tables)

skills.description: Use when comparing the wall-clock runtime of cell-cell interaction inference methods (dsCellNet, NATMI, CellPhoneDB, SingleCellSignalR) on identically sized scRNA-seq inputs, and the original dataset cell count differs from or exceeds the target benchmark size.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-subsampling-replicates
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-subsampling-replicates Use when comparing the wall-clock runtime of cell-cell interaction inference methods (dsCellNet, NATMI, CellPhoneDB, SingleCellSignalR) on identically sized scRNA-seq inputs, and the original dataset cell count differs from or exceeds the target benchmark size. When the analysis goal is biological inference of dynamic cell-cell interactions rather than runtime benchmarking — use the full un-subsampled dataset through the full dsCellNet pipeline (preparepairs, singlenet, developcorrelation) instead When the dataset already contains the target benchmark cell count or fewer cells, so subsampling would discard data rather than equalize inputs When comparing methods on accuracy or interaction sensitivity (e.g. detection of EC interactions or autocrine signaling) rather than computational speed A benchmarking skill for fairly timing cell-cell communication tools on single-cell RNA-seq data by randomly subsampling cells to a fixed count (e.g. 10,000 cells from the 11,670-cell E15.5 mouse embryonic cerebral cortex dataset GSE153164), generating independent replicate subsamples with a fixed seed, and wrapping each method's core call in a wall-clock timer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.07.047
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for fairly timing cell-cell communication tools on single-cell RNA-seq data by randomly subsampling cells to a fixed count (e.g. 10,000 cells from the 11,670-cell E15.5 mouse embryonic cerebral cortex dataset GSE153164), generating independent replicate subsamples with a fixed seed, and wrapping each method's core call in a wall-clock timer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is biological inference of dynamic cell-cell interactions rather than runtime benchmarking — use the full un-subsampled dataset through the full dsCellNet pipeline (preparepairs, singlenet, developcorrelation) instead When the dataset already contains the target benchmark cell count or fewer cells, so subsampling would discard data rather than equalize inputs When comparing methods on accuracy or interaction sensitivity (e.g. detection of EC interactions or autocrine signaling) rather than computational speed

skills.description: Use when raw or normalized scRNA-seq/spatial count data (Seurat object or count matrix) needs automated cell type labels, and marker-based annotation with interpretable top marker genes per cluster is required.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation Use when raw or normalized scRNA-seq/spatial count data (Seurat object or count matrix) needs automated cell type labels, and marker-based annotation with interpretable top marker genes per cluster is required. The annotation target requires non-marker-based reference mapping or direct comparison with such tools — the article explicitly did not compare with annotation tools that do not rely on marker genes No high-quality ground truth is needed and a reference-based method is preferred; the article notes non-marker-based methods require comprehensive reference datasets and are susceptible to technical variation The tissue of interest is absent from the built-in Accordion database and no user-provided signature is available (check with list_tissues() first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Automated cell type annotation of single-cell and spatial omics data using the Cell Marker Accordion, which exploits a curated database of consistency-weighted marker genes (specificity score SPs and evidence consistency score ECs) to annotate clusters or cells with interpretable outputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Automated cell type annotation of single-cell and spatial omics data using the Cell Marker Accordion, which exploits a curated database of consistency-weighted marker genes (specificity score SPs and evidence consistency score ECs) to annotate clusters or cells with interpretable outputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The annotation target requires non-marker-based reference mapping or direct comparison with such tools — the article explicitly did not compare with annotation tools that do not rely on marker genes No high-quality ground truth is needed and a reference-based method is preferred; the article notes non-marker-based methods require comprehensive reference datasets and are susceptible to technical variation The tissue of interest is absent from the built-in Accordion database and no user-provided signature is available (check with list_tissues() first)

skills.description: Use when annotating newly sequenced scRNA-seq cells or clusters against labeled reference data (e.g., human pancreas, PBMC, Tabula Muris), or when benchmarking cross-platform classification against Seurat v3 and scmap.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating newly sequenced scRNA-seq cells or clusters against labeled reference data (e.g., human pancreas, PBMC, Tabula Muris), or when benchmarking cross-platform classification against Seurat v3 and scmap. The query cells belong to cell types absent from the labeled reference and no null-dataset confidence-score control (conf_score with cutoffs 0.001–0.5) has been set up — unrepresented types cannot be identified by the plain Bet classifier Input is not single-cell transcriptomic data with a labeled reference (e.g., bulk RNA-seq, proteomics, or already-computed feature/annotation tables) A fully unsupervised clustering/annotation workflow is desired, since SciBet is a supervised classifier requiring pre-annotated training labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A supervised single-cell RNA-seq cell type annotation skill based on SciBet, a multinomial maximum-likelihood classifier that ranks informative genes by the ΔS statistic and assigns cell identities with order-of-magnitude speed advantage. It supports cross-validation against Seurat v3 and scmap benchmarks on pancreas and PBMC datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: A supervised single-cell RNA-seq cell type annotation skill based on SciBet, a multinomial maximum-likelihood classifier that ranks informative genes by the ΔS statistic and assigns cell identities with order-of-magnitude speed advantage. It supports cross-validation against Seurat v3 and scmap benchmarks on pancreas and PBMC datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query cells belong to cell types absent from the labeled reference and no null-dataset confidence-score control (conf_score with cutoffs 0.001–0.5) has been set up — unrepresented types cannot be identified by the plain Bet classifier Input is not single-cell transcriptomic data with a labeled reference (e.g., bulk RNA-seq, proteomics, or already-computed feature/annotation tables) A fully unsupervised clustering/annotation workflow is desired, since SciBet is a supervised classifier requiring pre-annotated training labels

skills.description: Use when annotating human single-cell RNA-seq cells with standardized, ontology-grounded cell type labels without supplying marker genes or a user-labeled training set, especially when uncertain cells should be placed at ancestral ontology nodes.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating human single-cell RNA-seq cells with standardized, ontology-grounded cell type labels without supplying marker genes or a user-labeled training set, especially when uncertain cells should be placed at ancestral ontology nodes. The data are non-human (e.g. mouse); CellO's training set covers only human primary samples and mouse training would require curated SRA training data not yet available The user already has a curated marker gene set or a labeled reference specific to their tissue, where a flat classifier against that reference may suffice Cell type labels for lineages absent from CellO's bulk RNA-seq training set are required at leaf-level specificity; CellO can only place such cells at ancestral ontology nodes (e.g. acinar cells annotated as glandular epithelial cells) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Hierarchical cell type classification of human scRNA-seq data against the Cell Ontology using CellO, a supervised tool pre-trained on human primary cell bulk RNA-seq data from the SRA, benchmarked against scMatch, SingleR, and 1NN baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101913
skills.summary: Hierarchical cell type classification of human scRNA-seq data against the Cell Ontology using CellO, a supervised tool pre-trained on human primary cell bulk RNA-seq data from the SRA, benchmarked against scMatch, SingleR, and 1NN baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are non-human (e.g. mouse); CellO's training set covers only human primary samples and mouse training would require curated SRA training data not yet available The user already has a curated marker gene set or a labeled reference specific to their tissue, where a flat classifier against that reference may suffice Cell type labels for lineages absent from CellO's bulk RNA-seq training set are required at leaf-level specificity; CellO can only place such cells at ancestral ontology nodes (e.g. acinar cells annotated as glandular epithelial cells)

skills.description: Use when annotating cells from cancer scRNA-seq data (counts matrix, Seurat object, h5, or 10X folder) into tumor microenvironment major cell types and subtypes, or when benchmarking annotation accuracy against original study labels.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating cells from cancer scRNA-seq data (counts matrix, Seurat object, h5, or 10X folder) into tumor microenvironment major cell types and subtypes, or when benchmarking annotation accuracy against original study labels. skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI counts (e.g., UC mucosa cells) need denoised/imputed expression values via the scPhere decoder, and when dropouts must be reduced without introducing false-positive expression of marker genes.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-count-imputation Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI counts (e.g., UC mucosa cells) need denoised/imputed expression values via the scPhere decoder, and when dropouts must be reduced without introducing false-positive expression of marker genes. The article's discussion explicitly flags imputation of missing counts and ambient-RNA removal as requiring further validation, so do not treat scPhere decoder outputs as a validated general-purpose imputation or ambient-RNA-correction tool beyond demonstrated denoising cases. Input is not raw UMI counts (e.g., already log-normalized or TPM data) — the model is built for UMI count matrices with a negative-binomial observation distribution ('nb'). No trained scPhere model exists for the tissue/batch structure at hand; training a model just for ad hoc imputation without checking the batch-invariant setting is not supported by the demonstrated workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Denoise/impute UMI count matrices by passing cell count vectors through a trained batch-invariant scPhere decoder (negative-binomial observation model, observation_dist='nb'), producing mean imputed expression per cell and gene; validated on UC CD8+ T cells where the CD8A–CD8B Pearson correlation rises from ~0.27 (raw counts) to ~0.81 (imputed) without inducing false-positive CD4 expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22851-4
skills.summary: Denoise/impute UMI count matrices by passing cell count vectors through a trained batch-invariant scPhere decoder (negative-binomial observation model, observation_dist='nb'), producing mean imputed expression per cell and gene; validated on UC CD8+ T cells where the CD8A–CD8B Pearson correlation rises from ~0.27 (raw counts) to ~0.81 (imputed) without inducing false-positive CD4 expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article's discussion explicitly flags imputation of missing counts and ambient-RNA removal as requiring further validation, so do not treat scPhere decoder outputs as a validated general-purpose imputation or ambient-RNA-correction tool beyond demonstrated denoising cases. Input is not raw UMI counts (e.g., already log-normalized or TPM data) — the model is built for UMI count matrices with a negative-binomial observation distribution ('nb'). No trained scPhere model exists for the tissue/batch structure at hand; training a model just for ad hoc imputation without checking the batch-invariant setting is not supported by the demonstrated workflow.
