skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-covariate-modeling Use when an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and the total number of genes detected per droplet are both available, and more accurate probabilistic droplet assignment is needed than a naive HTO-only model provides. No per-droplet detected-gene counts are available and only HTO counts exist — the naive demuxmix variant is the appropriate (if weaker) option The data contain no hashtag-oligocode labels at all and cells cannot be distinguished by oligonucleotide barcodes Droplets have already been demultiplexed and only downstream per-sample analysis is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Improves HTO-based demultiplexing of single-cell RNA-seq droplets by fitting demuxmix's negative binomial regression mixture model with the per-droplet number of detected genes as a covariate, exploiting the positive association between RNA content and HTO counts to explain variance and sharpen assignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad481
skills.summary: Improves HTO-based demultiplexing of single-cell RNA-seq droplets by fitting demuxmix's negative binomial regression mixture model with the per-droplet number of detected genes as a covariate, exploiting the positive association between RNA content and HTO counts to explain variance and sharpen assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No per-droplet detected-gene counts are available and only HTO counts exist — the naive demuxmix variant is the appropriate (if weaker) option The data contain no hashtag-oligocode labels at all and cells cannot be distinguished by oligonucleotide barcodes Droplets have already been demultiplexed and only downstream per-sample analysis is needed

skills.description: Use when cell-type labels must be compared across two or more scRNA-seq studies with matching labels (e.g., excitatory vs inhibitory neurons), and you need quantitative AUROC evidence of cross-study replicability.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-harmonization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-harmonization Use when cell-type labels must be compared across two or more scRNA-seq studies with matching labels (e.g., excitatory vs inhibitory neurons), and you need quantitative AUROC evidence of cross-study replicability. Cell-type labels are ambiguous or absent across datasets — use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS variant instead of the supervised framework Only one dataset is present — leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation requires at least two studies to compare Genes in the gene sets do not match the expression matrix row names, or gene sets contain fewer than two genes — MetaNeighbor will not run correctly http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Harmonize multiple scRNA-seq studies into a shared cell-type label space and quantify cross-dataset replicability with MetaNeighbor's supervised neighbor-voting AUROC framework (e.g., 2809 excitatory vs 1162 inhibitory cortical neurons across four studies, mean AUROC ~0.69 ± 0.1). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Harmonize multiple scRNA-seq studies into a shared cell-type label space and quantify cross-dataset replicability with MetaNeighbor's supervised neighbor-voting AUROC framework (e.g., 2809 excitatory vs 1162 inhibitory cortical neurons across four studies, mean AUROC ~0.69 ± 0.1).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type labels are ambiguous or absent across datasets — use the unsupervised MetaNeighborUS variant instead of the supervised framework Only one dataset is present — leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation requires at least two studies to compare Genes in the gene sets do not match the expression matrix row names, or gene sets contain fewer than two genes — MetaNeighbor will not run correctly

skills.description: Use when evaluating a cluster-purity metric (e.g., ROGUE) against sequencing-depth differences or cell-number variation, by generating simulated replicate scRNA-seq mixtures with known ground-truth purity.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation Use when evaluating a cluster-purity metric (e.g., ROGUE) against sequencing-depth differences or cell-number variation, by generating simulated replicate scRNA-seq mixtures with known ground-truth purity. Input consists of real, already-annotated cell clusters rather than simulated populations with known ground-truth purity — use ROGUE directly via CalculateRogue instead of simulating The goal is to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms, which the paper states ROGUE does not yet support (proposed future work) The task is clustering or rare cell-type detection (e.g., GiniClust, RaceID3) rather than benchmarking a purity metric http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simulate two-replicate pure single-cell populations with controlled sequencing-depth fold changes (2–100x) and varying cell numbers to benchmark whether the ROGUE entropy-based purity metric remains robust to technical factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: Simulate two-replicate pure single-cell populations with controlled sequencing-depth fold changes (2–100x) and varying cell numbers to benchmark whether the ROGUE entropy-based purity metric remains robust to technical factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of real, already-annotated cell clusters rather than simulated populations with known ground-truth purity — use ROGUE directly via CalculateRogue instead of simulating The goal is to assess purity of integrated cell populations from different protocols/platforms, which the paper states ROGUE does not yet support (proposed future work) The task is clustering or rare cell-type detection (e.g., GiniClust, RaceID3) rather than benchmarking a purity metric

skills.description: Use when you must benchmark cross-timepoint cell annotation methods under controlled scenarios (shifted compositions, disappearing or emerging cell types) with ground-truth labels and Monte Carlo replicates.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation Use when you must benchmark cross-timepoint cell annotation methods under controlled scenarios (shifted compositions, disappearing or emerging cell types) with ground-truth labels and Monte Carlo replicates. Input is a single-timepoint (cross-sectional) scRNA-seq dataset with no t0/t1 structure to simulate or borrow information across The goal is real-data evaluation without ground truth — CASi's own limitation is that a dramatically different later timepoint (or a transcriptomically similar novel cell) breaks the neural network/novel-cell detection You only need novel-cell-type detection or tDEG identification on real data rather than a controlled annotation benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates simulated longitudinal (t0/t1) single-cell RNA-seq datasets from a real PBMC pool of sorted cells to benchmark cross-timepoint cell annotation methods (e.g., CASi vs. scmap, CHETAH, scPred) by accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-58566-x
skills.summary: Generates simulated longitudinal (t0/t1) single-cell RNA-seq datasets from a real PBMC pool of sorted cells to benchmark cross-timepoint cell annotation methods (e.g., CASi vs. scmap, CHETAH, scPred) by accuracy and adjusted Rand index (ARI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-timepoint (cross-sectional) scRNA-seq dataset with no t0/t1 structure to simulate or borrow information across The goal is real-data evaluation without ground truth — CASi's own limitation is that a dramatically different later timepoint (or a transcriptomically similar novel cell) breaks the neural network/novel-cell detection You only need novel-cell-type detection or tDEG identification on real data rather than a controlled annotation benchmark

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction or clustering tools requires ground-truth labels plus controlled sparsity and CV of TGC, e.g. testing robustness to >90% zeros and dropout-driven variability.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction or clustering tools requires ground-truth labels plus controlled sparsity and CV of TGC, e.g. testing robustness to >90% zeros and dropout-driven variability. Real scRNA-seq data already has trusted expert labels and known sparsity — analyze it directly instead of simulating. The goal is biological discovery on the dataset itself rather than method benchmarking; simulation adds no information about the underlying biology. The data is not UMI/count-based scRNA-seq (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, spatial protein assays) that the scDesign2 count model was not trained to mimic. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate ground-truth-labeled synthetic scRNA-seq count data by training the scDesign2 (v1.0.0) simulator on a reference immune cell dataset, then subsample to build stratified benchmark cohorts spanning gradients of sparsity and CV of total gene counts (TGC). This enables quantitative DR-tool comparison (SIL/ECS) when no real data with trusted cell-type labels exists. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: Generate ground-truth-labeled synthetic scRNA-seq count data by training the scDesign2 (v1.0.0) simulator on a reference immune cell dataset, then subsample to build stratified benchmark cohorts spanning gradients of sparsity and CV of total gene counts (TGC). This enables quantitative DR-tool comparison (SIL/ECS) when no real data with trusted cell-type labels exists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Real scRNA-seq data already has trusted expert labels and known sparsity — analyze it directly instead of simulating. The goal is biological discovery on the dataset itself rather than method benchmarking; simulation adds no information about the underlying biology. The data is not UMI/count-based scRNA-seq (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, spatial protein assays) that the scDesign2 count model was not trained to mimic.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking spatial subpopulation or spatial-domain methods against a known truth: simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST data with ground-truth subcluster labels are needed for ARI-style evaluation.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation Use when benchmarking spatial subpopulation or spatial-domain methods against a known truth: simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST data with ground-truth subcluster labels are needed for ARI-style evaluation. The analysis goal is biological discovery on real tissue data rather than controlled benchmarking with known ground truth The method under test cannot consume paired single-cell and spatial transcriptomics inputs with fixed ground-truth subcluster assignments Evaluation requires metrics other than agreement with known subclusters (e.g. trajectory inference quality), for which ARI against simulated subclusters is not informative http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generating synthetic paired scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics datasets with Splatter, with known ground-truth spatially heterogeneous subcluster labels, to benchmark clustering and spatial-domain identification methods such as scSpace. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Generating synthetic paired scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics datasets with Splatter, with known ground-truth spatially heterogeneous subcluster labels, to benchmark clustering and spatial-domain identification methods such as scSpace.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is biological discovery on real tissue data rather than controlled benchmarking with known ground truth The method under test cannot consume paired single-cell and spatial transcriptomics inputs with fixed ground-truth subcluster assignments Evaluation requires metrics other than agreement with known subclusters (e.g. trajectory inference quality), for which ARI against simulated subclusters is not informative

skills.description: Use when benchmarking scalability of a single-cell method: you have a cell x gene expression matrix (e.g., PBMC Multiome from the Human Blood Atlas) and need runtime vs. cell-number measurements on nested subsamples.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsampling Use when benchmarking scalability of a single-cell method: you have a cell x gene expression matrix (e.g., PBMC Multiome from the Human Blood Atlas) and need runtime vs. cell-number measurements on nested subsamples. The goal is accuracy/performance benchmarking of GRN inference rather than runtime scaling — use the method's accuracy evaluation workflow instead Data are true longitudinal time series or already pseudo-time-ordered trajectories; this skill targets time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data where cells at different times come from independent batches http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generates subsampled versions of a single-cell expression matrix at a series of increasing cell counts and times a method (here, the Python version of COSLIR) on each to characterize how running time scales with the number of cells, as done to reproduce the near-flat runtime curve of Fig. 5C. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Generates subsampled versions of a single-cell expression matrix at a series of increasing cell counts and times a method (here, the Python version of COSLIR) on each to characterize how running time scales with the number of cells, as done to reproduce the near-flat runtime curve of Fig. 5C.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy/performance benchmarking of GRN inference rather than runtime scaling — use the method's accuracy evaluation workflow instead Data are true longitudinal time series or already pseudo-time-ordered trajectories; this skill targets time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data where cells at different times come from independent batches

skills.description: Use when building synthetic rare-cell detection benchmarks by subsampling known cell types from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix, or when probing how few DE genes preserve rare-cell identity.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsetting
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsetting Use when building synthetic rare-cell detection benchmarks by subsampling known cell types from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix, or when probing how few DE genes preserve rare-cell identity. The goal is identifying novel rare populations in a real, unlabelled dataset rather than benchmarking a detector on controlled synthetic mixtures The dataset is too small to support an abundant population of ~500 cells plus a genuinely rare subpopulation Cell-type identities or marker genes are unknown, since the subsetting depends on picking defined populations (CD19+ B cells, CD14+ monocytes) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Subsample cell populations from a large scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., 500 CD19+ B cells plus 2, 5, or 10 CD14+ monocytes drawn from the 68k PBMC dataset) to construct synthetic rare-cell benchmarks, optionally with DE gene replacement, for evaluating rare-cell detectors like GapClust. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8
skills.summary: Subsample cell populations from a large scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., 500 CD19+ B cells plus 2, 5, or 10 CD14+ monocytes drawn from the 68k PBMC dataset) to construct synthetic rare-cell benchmarks, optionally with DE gene replacement, for evaluating rare-cell detectors like GapClust.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is identifying novel rare populations in a real, unlabelled dataset rather than benchmarking a detector on controlled synthetic mixtures The dataset is too small to support an abundant population of ~500 cells plus a genuinely rare subpopulation Cell-type identities or marker genes are unknown, since the subsetting depends on picking defined populations (CD19+ B cells, CD14+ monocytes)

skills.description: Use when two raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need batch integration in gene space, with quality judged by mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN metrics.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-integration
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-integration Use when two raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need batch integration in gene space, with quality judged by mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN metrics. More than two datasets need integrating — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is only possible 'in principle') Extra-large datasets where exact blossom-based matching is too slow is fine (use -greedy), but the skill does not cover dimensionality-reduction-based integration (e.g. ZIFA) or simulation-based workflows (Splatter) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Batch-correct and integrate two single-cell RNA-seq datasets using BATMAN, which builds a bipartite graph over representative anchor cells, finds a minimum-weight one-to-one matching (exact blossom-based or greedy ratio-2 approximation), and applies local shifting vectors in high-dimensional gene space. Rationale: it removes batch effects while preserving local cell-to-cell structure, outperforming MNN-based methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Batch-correct and integrate two single-cell RNA-seq datasets using BATMAN, which builds a bipartite graph over representative anchor cells, finds a minimum-weight one-to-one matching (exact blossom-based or greedy ratio-2 approximation), and applies local shifting vectors in high-dimensional gene space. Rationale: it removes batch effects while preserving local cell-to-cell structure, outperforming MNN-based methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: More than two datasets need integrating — the current BATMAN implementation works only with two datasets (multi-dataset integration is only possible 'in principle') Extra-large datasets where exact blossom-based matching is too slow is fine (use -greedy), but the skill does not cover dimensionality-reduction-based integration (e.g. ZIFA) or simulation-based workflows (Splatter)

skills.description: Use when two library-depth-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. TPM/CPM gene-by-cell data frames) exist, one with known reference clusters, and target cells must be assigned to equivalent reference cell types, especially with batch effect or imbalanced cell numbers/library sizes.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-mapping
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-mapping Use when two library-depth-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. TPM/CPM gene-by-cell data frames) exist, one with known reference clusters, and target cells must be assigned to equivalent reference cell types, especially with batch effect or imbalanced cell numbers/library sizes. When neither dataset is well clustered and contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types' in this case When the input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID is compatible only with library-depth normalization (TPM/CPM), not log-transformed data When the goal is explicit batch correction/integration of the datasets themselves rather than label transfer: scID identifies equivalent cells without assumptions about technical and biological variation and does not impute or over-correct expression http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to reference clusters using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, which extracts cluster-specific gene signatures, weights them by discriminative power, and assigns equivalent target cells via a finite mixture of Gaussians — robust to batch effect without explicit data integration. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100914
skills.summary: Map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to reference clusters using scID's Fisher's Linear Discriminant Analysis-like framework, which extracts cluster-specific gene signatures, weights them by discriminative power, and assigns equivalent target cells via a finite mixture of Gaussians — robust to batch effect without explicit data integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When neither dataset is well clustered and contains good gene signatures — the article states scID 'is not a recommended approach for identification of equivalent cell types' in this case When the input expression matrices are log-transformed — scID is compatible only with library-depth normalization (TPM/CPM), not log-transformed data When the goal is explicit batch correction/integration of the datasets themselves rather than label transfer: scID identifies equivalent cells without assumptions about technical and biological variation and does not impute or over-correct expression

skills.description: Use when training a FAVA VAE (or similar latent-space model) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need to demonstrate the model generalizes to unseen cells rather than memorizing the training set.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-splitting
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-splitting Use when training a FAVA VAE (or similar latent-space model) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need to demonstrate the model generalizes to unseen cells rather than memorizing the training set. When the goal is producing the final FAVA functional association network from all available cells — the full dataset should be used, not a split When input data are bulk omics, proteomics-only, or already aggregated condition-level data rather than single-cell scRNA-seq When generalization can be tested on an external independent dataset; a random within-dataset split only checks memorization of the same cell population A train/test generalization (overfitting) check for FAVA: partition single-cell scRNA-seq data (e.g. GSE75748) into a 67% training and 33% test split, train the VAE on training cells only, and verify that latent-space correlations and KEGG-based network benchmark performance are similar across both splits. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: A train/test generalization (overfitting) check for FAVA: partition single-cell scRNA-seq data (e.g. GSE75748) into a 67% training and 33% test split, train the VAE on training cells only, and verify that latent-space correlations and KEGG-based network benchmark performance are similar across both splits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is producing the final FAVA functional association network from all available cells — the full dataset should be used, not a split When input data are bulk omics, proteomics-only, or already aggregated condition-level data rather than single-cell scRNA-seq When generalization can be tested on an external independent dataset; a random within-dataset split only checks memorization of the same cell population

skills.description: Use when comparing cell type matching methods (e.g., TACTiCS vs SAMap) whose reference performances were computed on differently sized datasets, and you need equal-sized per-species subsets to control for dataset size effects.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-subsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-subsampling Use when comparing cell type matching methods (e.g., TACTiCS vs SAMap) whose reference performances were computed on differently sized datasets, and you need equal-sized per-species subsets to control for dataset size effects. When the analysis goal is absolute best performance rather than a size-controlled method comparison — the full unprocessed datasets should be used instead When subsampling would drop any included cell type below the minimum of 50 cells per type, violating the preserved-proportions constraint http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Subsample scRNA-seq datasets to equal-sized (e.g., 50k cells per species) subsets that preserve cell type proportions with a minimum of 50 cells per included type, enabling fair cross-method comparisons controlled for dataset size differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad248
skills.summary: Subsample scRNA-seq datasets to equal-sized (e.g., 50k cells per species) subsets that preserve cell type proportions with a minimum of 50 cells per included type, enabling fair cross-method comparisons controlled for dataset size differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is absolute best performance rather than a size-controlled method comparison — the full unprocessed datasets should be used instead When subsampling would drop any included cell type below the minimum of 50 cells per type, violating the preserved-proportions constraint

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data have already been embedded by a pre-trained graph autoencoder and cell-level cluster labels are needed, with simultaneous learning of embedding and cluster assignment.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-deep-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-deep-clustering Use when scRNA-seq count data have already been embedded by a pre-trained graph autoencoder and cell-level cluster labels are needed, with simultaneous learning of embedding and cluster assignment. Only a 2D visualization embedding is needed — the article notes the graph autoencoder cannot directly embed into 2D and instead uses an intermediate dimension plus tSNE, not the clustering stage The model has not been pre-trained on reconstruction loss L_r — centroids are obtained by Louvain clustering of the pre-trained embedded data, so skipping pre-training gives no valid initialization Trajectory inference is the goal rather than discrete clustering — scGAE and scGNN perform similarly on trajectory inference, so this skill's advantage is specifically clustering performance http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Refines a pre-trained scGAE graph autoencoder into a clustering-friendly latent embedding via DEC-style alter-training: Student's-t soft assignment Q to Louvain-initialized centroids, a DEC target distribution P, and joint minimization of L = L_r + gamma*L_c with gamma = 2.5. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Refines a pre-trained scGAE graph autoencoder into a clustering-friendly latent embedding via DEC-style alter-training: Student's-t soft assignment Q to Louvain-initialized centroids, a DEC target distribution P, and joint minimization of L = L_r + gamma*L_c with gamma = 2.5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a 2D visualization embedding is needed — the article notes the graph autoencoder cannot directly embed into 2D and instead uses an intermediate dimension plus tSNE, not the clustering stage The model has not been pre-trained on reconstruction loss L_r — centroids are obtained by Louvain clustering of the pre-trained embedded data, so skipping pre-training gives no valid initialization Trajectory inference is the goal rather than discrete clustering — scGAE and scGNN perform similarly on trajectory inference, so this skill's advantage is specifically clustering performance

skills.description: Use when two or more single-cell groups (e.g., cells assigned to mtDNA variants/clones by MQuad+vireoSNP) need to be compared transcriptomically to report up-/down-regulated genes with adjusted p-value cutoffs.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis Use when two or more single-cell groups (e.g., cells assigned to mtDNA variants/clones by MQuad+vireoSNP) need to be compared transcriptomically to report up-/down-regulated genes with adjusted p-value cutoffs. The goal is discovering which mtDNA variants discriminate clones, not testing transcriptional consequences — use MQuad on cellsnp-lite AD/DP matrices instead of differential expression on the expression matrix. The comparison groups are defined by a single confounded variable (e.g., clone assignment perfectly co-segregates with batch or donor), so DE calls would not be attributable to the clone. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Detects transcriptional differences between single-cell-defined subclones (here, mtDNA-defined clones T0 vs T1 in the TNBC1 10x scRNA-seq dataset) by running Seurat FindMarkers with the DESeq2 two-sided Wald test and summarizing results as a table of log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values plus a volcano plot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28845-0
skills.summary: Detects transcriptional differences between single-cell-defined subclones (here, mtDNA-defined clones T0 vs T1 in the TNBC1 10x scRNA-seq dataset) by running Seurat FindMarkers with the DESeq2 two-sided Wald test and summarizing results as a table of log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values plus a volcano plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovering which mtDNA variants discriminate clones, not testing transcriptional consequences — use MQuad on cellsnp-lite AD/DP matrices instead of differential expression on the expression matrix. The comparison groups are defined by a single confounded variable (e.g., clone assignment perfectly co-segregates with batch or donor), so DE calls would not be attributable to the clone.

skills.description: Use when noisy scRNA-seq count matrices (with high dropout) need unsupervised dimension reduction to 2D for cell-type visualization, k-means clustering benchmarks, or lineage/pseudo-time recovery.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dimension-reduction
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dimension-reduction Use when noisy scRNA-seq count matrices (with high dropout) need unsupervised dimension reduction to 2D for cell-type visualization, k-means clustering benchmarks, or lineage/pseudo-time recovery. The goal is traditional bulk RNA-seq analysis or the data are already a low-dimensional feature table rather than a raw scRNA-seq count matrix Optimal latent dimension must be determined strictly without any prior knowledge, since 'the determination of the optimal dimension is a tricky task if prior knowledge is limited' Compute budget cannot tolerate several hours of single-GPU model learning for datasets with several thousand cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3315 Apply VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models scRNA-seq dropout events with the Gumbel distribution, to learn a 2D nonlinear latent representation of single-cell RNA-seq data for visualization, clustering (NMI/ARI), and developmental trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.08.003
skills.summary: Apply VASC, a deep variational autoencoder that models scRNA-seq dropout events with the Gumbel distribution, to learn a 2D nonlinear latent representation of single-cell RNA-seq data for visualization, clustering (NMI/ARI), and developmental trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is traditional bulk RNA-seq analysis or the data are already a low-dimensional feature table rather than a raw scRNA-seq count matrix Optimal latent dimension must be determined strictly without any prior knowledge, since 'the determination of the optimal dimension is a tricky task if prior knowledge is limited' Compute budget cannot tolerate several hours of single-GPU model learning for datasets with several thousand cells

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS marrow counts) needs 2D embedding with t-SNE/UMAP and a statistically grounded, per-cell assessment of whether the visible structure is real rather than stochastic.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dimensionality-reduction-embedding
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dimensionality-reduction-embedding Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS marrow counts) needs 2D embedding with t-SNE/UMAP and a statistically grounded, per-cell assessment of whether the visible structure is real rather than stochastic. The data are not single-cell count matrices — EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets, so whole-pipeline quality analyses of arbitrary feature tables are out of scope. Only a single global quality estimate is needed rather than local, per-cell error estimates against a null hypothesis. The downstream task requires strictly 'nearest' neighbors rather than approximate ones (use vantage-point trees instead of Annoy-based FIt-SNE nearest neighbors when subtle detail is required). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Embed scRNA-seq count data (e.g., ~4,800 Tabula Muris bone marrow cells) in 2D with t-SNE (FIt-SNE/openTSNE) and UMAP, and use EMBEDR's marginal-resampling nulls to assign per-cell p-values that quantify which parts of the embedding reflect real structure versus algorithm-induced noise. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Embed scRNA-seq count data (e.g., ~4,800 Tabula Muris bone marrow cells) in 2D with t-SNE (FIt-SNE/openTSNE) and UMAP, and use EMBEDR's marginal-resampling nulls to assign per-cell p-values that quantify which parts of the embedding reflect real structure versus algorithm-induced noise.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not single-cell count matrices — EMBEDR's null-generation process has not been extended to non-normalized datasets, so whole-pipeline quality analyses of arbitrary feature tables are out of scope. Only a single global quality estimate is needed rather than local, per-cell error estimates against a null hypothesis. The downstream task requires strictly 'nearest' neighbors rather than approximate ones (use vantage-point trees instead of Annoy-based FIt-SNE nearest neighbors when subtle detail is required).

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-type perturbation statistic (e.g., nDEG from pseudobulk DE testing or scDist distance) remains stable under varying numbers of cells per cell type in scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-downsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-downsampling Use when evaluating whether a cell-type perturbation statistic (e.g., nDEG from pseudobulk DE testing or scDist distance) remains stable under varying numbers of cells per cell type in scRNA-seq data. The goal is to compare cell-type abundance/proportion changes between conditions rather than transcriptomic perturbation magnitude (differential abundance tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the relevant class). The input data are raw counts — scDist's model assumes normalized expression (Pearson residuals recommended), and applying it directly to counts is deferred to a future version. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill that systematically resamples cells per cell type across a size grid (e.g., 100 to 10,000 cells) in single-cell RNA-seq data to expose methods whose statistics are confounded by cell count, contrasting nDEG (number of differentially expressed genes) with the scDist between-condition distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that systematically resamples cells per cell type across a size grid (e.g., 100 to 10,000 cells) in single-cell RNA-seq data to expose methods whose statistics are confounded by cell count, contrasting nDEG (number of differentially expressed genes) with the scDist between-condition distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare cell-type abundance/proportion changes between conditions rather than transcriptomic perturbation magnitude (differential abundance tools like DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the relevant class). The input data are raw counts — scDist's model assumes normalized expression (Pearson residuals recommended), and applying it directly to counts is deferred to a future version.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and downstream tasks such as cell clustering, t-SNE visualization, differential expression, or pseudotime/trajectory inference are degraded by zero inflation.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-dropout-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-dropout-imputation Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and downstream tasks such as cell clustering, t-SNE visualization, differential expression, or pseudotime/trajectory inference are degraded by zero inflation. The input matrix is already normalized and log-transformed without setting normalized = TRUE, risking double normalization (Bfimpute will redo CPM + log10 bias 1.01 otherwise) No benchmark or labeled/ordered data exists and only point estimates of individual gene activity are needed, since the article notes prior imputation methods are less effective at recovering cell-to-cell relationships but no single method is best for every criterion A dataset far outside the benchmarked regimes (simulated 5-8 cell types with 20,000 genes and 500-800 cells; Chu, Scialdone, Petropoulos) is used without tuning, since generalizability beyond these datasets is unconfirmed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Impute dropout events in scRNA-seq count matrices using Bfimpute, a Bayesian factorization method that reconstructs latent gene (G) and cell (C) matrices via MCMC, optionally within spectral clusters and with gene/cell side information (e.g., bulk RNA-seq), to improve clustering and pseudotime analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Impute dropout events in scRNA-seq count matrices using Bfimpute, a Bayesian factorization method that reconstructs latent gene (G) and cell (C) matrices via MCMC, optionally within spectral clusters and with gene/cell side information (e.g., bulk RNA-seq), to improve clustering and pseudotime analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input matrix is already normalized and log-transformed without setting normalized = TRUE, risking double normalization (Bfimpute will redo CPM + log10 bias 1.01 otherwise) No benchmark or labeled/ordered data exists and only point estimates of individual gene activity are needed, since the article notes prior imputation methods are less effective at recovering cell-to-cell relationships but no single method is best for every criterion A dataset far outside the benchmarked regimes (simulated 5-8 cell types with 20,000 genes and 500-800 cells; Chu, Scialdone, Petropoulos) is used without tuning, since generalizability beyond these datasets is unconfirmed

skills.description: Use when you have a merged, quantile-normalized single-cell expression matrix from a temporal biological process (e.g. mouse pre-implantation stages, oocyte to late blastocyst) and need pseudotime ordering that reflects developmental progression.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-embryo-trajectory-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-embryo-trajectory-analysis Use when you have a merged, quantile-normalized single-cell expression matrix from a temporal biological process (e.g. mouse pre-implantation stages, oocyte to late blastocyst) and need pseudotime ordering that reflects developmental progression. Goal is ligand-receptor-to-TF causal inference between defined cell types (e.g. EPI vs PE) — use the full TimeTalk RunTimeTalk workflow instead of trajectory ordering alone Cells come from a process without temporal/developmental structure (definitive cell types, no stage ordering) — pseudotime from DDRTree would not reflect true progression Workflow requires monocle3 (e.g. RunMonocle3 on a Seurat object with minimal_branch_len) rather than the monocle2 DDRTree pipeline used here http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs a developmental pseudotime trajectory from curated pre-implantation mouse embryo scRNA-seq data using monocle2: differential gene selection (qval = 0.01), DDRTree dimension reduction, and orderCells ordering of cells from oocyte to late blastocyst. This validates that merged, quantile-normalized single-cell data recapitulate early embryo development. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Reconstructs a developmental pseudotime trajectory from curated pre-implantation mouse embryo scRNA-seq data using monocle2: differential gene selection (qval = 0.01), DDRTree dimension reduction, and orderCells ordering of cells from oocyte to late blastocyst. This validates that merged, quantile-normalized single-cell data recapitulate early embryo development.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is ligand-receptor-to-TF causal inference between defined cell types (e.g. EPI vs PE) — use the full TimeTalk RunTimeTalk workflow instead of trajectory ordering alone Cells come from a process without temporal/developmental structure (definitive cell types, no stage ordering) — pseudotime from DDRTree would not reflect true progression Workflow requires monocle3 (e.g. RunMonocle3 on a Seurat object with minimal_branch_len) rather than the monocle2 DDRTree pipeline used here

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., Smart-Seq2 SCC EMT) needs attractor decomposition into multiple stable/hybrid states and quantification of transition flux through intermediate cell states between epithelial and mesenchymal attractors.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-emt-lineage-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-emt-lineage-inference Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., Smart-Seq2 SCC EMT) needs attractor decomposition into multiple stable/hybrid states and quantification of transition flux through intermediate cell states between epithelial and mesenchymal attractors. Datasets with too few cells for high-resolution transition-cell identification — the article notes small datasets like the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 data require special care to confirm transition-cell analysis Analyses that require modeling non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics, which MuTrans does not currently consider Systems violating the steady-state/detailed-balance assumptions where coarse-grained transition probabilities may not follow Kramers' reaction rate theory http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies MuTrans multiscale stochastic dynamics to reconstruct attractor basins and infer E→ICS→M cell lineage transition paths on the Smart-Seq2 squamous cell carcinoma EMT dataset, quantifying the fraction of E-to-M transition flux routed through intermediate cell states (ICS). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Applies MuTrans multiscale stochastic dynamics to reconstruct attractor basins and infer E→ICS→M cell lineage transition paths on the Smart-Seq2 squamous cell carcinoma EMT dataset, quantifying the fraction of E-to-M transition flux routed through intermediate cell states (ICS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets with too few cells for high-resolution transition-cell identification — the article notes small datasets like the myelopoiesis Fluidigm C1 data require special care to confirm transition-cell analysis Analyses that require modeling non-stationary effects such as cell cycle or cell proliferation dynamics, which MuTrans does not currently consider Systems violating the steady-state/detailed-balance assumptions where coarse-grained transition probabilities may not follow Kramers' reaction rate theory

skills.description: Use when you need to determine whether an scRNA-seq cluster is a pure cell population, e.g. assessing purity loss from batch effects such as aggregating control and IFN-beta stimulated PBMCs or cells from multiple unrelated individuals (Kang et al., GSE96583).
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-entropy-modeling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-entropy-modeling Use when you need to determine whether an scRNA-seq cluster is a pure cell population, e.g. assessing purity loss from batch effects such as aggregating control and IFN-beta stimulated PBMCs or cells from multiple unrelated individuals (Kang et al., GSE96583). Assessing purity of cell populations integrated across different protocols and platforms — the paper states ROGUE does not yet support this and proposes it as future work Low-quality or continuous datasets where the recommended 0.9 purity threshold is unsuitable — the paper notes the threshold should instead be derived from global ROGUE values Clustering tasks aimed at detecting rare cell types, which are the purpose of GiniClust/GiniClust2/RaceID rather than purity quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 An entropy-based modeling workflow using the ROGUE statistic (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy) to quantify the purity/homogeneity of single-cell RNA-seq clusters, implemented in the open-source R package ROGUE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16904-3
skills.summary: An entropy-based modeling workflow using the ROGUE statistic (Ratio of Global Unshifted Entropy) to quantify the purity/homogeneity of single-cell RNA-seq clusters, implemented in the open-source R package ROGUE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Assessing purity of cell populations integrated across different protocols and platforms — the paper states ROGUE does not yet support this and proposes it as future work Low-quality or continuous datasets where the recommended 0.9 purity threshold is unsuitable — the paper notes the threshold should instead be derived from global ROGUE values Clustering tasks aimed at detecting rare cell types, which are the purpose of GiniClust/GiniClust2/RaceID rather than purity quantification

skills.description: Use when a quantitative, rank-trend-based low-dimensional gene representation is needed from normalized scRNA-seq data, i.e., when binning continuous expression values into discrete levels to group quasi-trend-preserved genes.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-binning-discretization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-binning-discretization Use when a quantitative, rank-trend-based low-dimensional gene representation is needed from normalized scRNA-seq data, i.e., when binning continuous expression values into discrete levels to group quasi-trend-preserved genes. Input is not normalized to [0,1]: equal-width binning of [0,1] is meaningless on raw counts or differently scaled matrices The goal is qualitative (binary) landmark construction — use LC1 binarization instead of quantitative k-bin discretization The input already contains discrete/categorical expression levels and only requires clustering rather than re-discretization http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Discretize normalized single-cell RNA-seq expression values by dividing the [0,1] range into k equal bins (scQA uses k=6, tunable via the 'binning' parameter) and replacing each value with its bin index, forming matrix D' that enables grouping of quasi-trend-preserved genes by the number of bins they utilize for quantitative landmark construction (LC2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Discretize normalized single-cell RNA-seq expression values by dividing the [0,1] range into k equal bins (scQA uses k=6, tunable via the 'binning' parameter) and replacing each value with its bin index, forming matrix D' that enables grouping of quasi-trend-preserved genes by the number of bins they utilize for quantitative landmark construction (LC2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not normalized to [0,1]: equal-width binning of [0,1] is meaningless on raw counts or differently scaled matrices The goal is qualitative (binary) landmark construction — use LC1 binarization instead of quantitative k-bin discretization The input already contains discrete/categorical expression levels and only requires clustering rather than re-discretization

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type labels and need to compute, rank, or compare expression-based ligand-receptor interaction scores across CCC methods and prior-knowledge resources.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-scoring Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type labels and need to compute, rank, or compare expression-based ligand-receptor interaction scores across CCC methods and prior-knowledge resources. The method of interest additionally infers intracellular processes (e.g., NicheNet, SoptSC, full Cytotalk) — these are not directly comparable to expression-based ligand-receptor scoring The biological question concerns long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq gene expression within the dataset does not capture Only raw unprocessed counts without cell-type annotation are available, since sender-receiver scoring requires cell-type-labelled expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Score candidate ligand-receptor interactions from single-cell RNA-seq expression data using method-specific formulas (CellChat probability, CellPhoneDB truncated mean, Connectome weight_norm, NATMI mean-expression edge weight, SingleCellSignalR LRscore, iTALK logFC Mean, Cytotalk Crosstalk score) decoupled from their default prior-knowledge resources, to quantify and compare predicted cell-cell communication. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Score candidate ligand-receptor interactions from single-cell RNA-seq expression data using method-specific formulas (CellChat probability, CellPhoneDB truncated mean, Connectome weight_norm, NATMI mean-expression edge weight, SingleCellSignalR LRscore, iTALK logFC Mean, Cytotalk Crosstalk score) decoupled from their default prior-knowledge resources, to quantify and compare predicted cell-cell communication.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method of interest additionally infers intracellular processes (e.g., NicheNet, SoptSC, full Cytotalk) — these are not directly comparable to expression-based ligand-receptor scoring The biological question concerns long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq gene expression within the dataset does not capture Only raw unprocessed counts without cell-type annotation are available, since sender-receiver scoring requires cell-type-labelled expression data

skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-feature-representation-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-feature-representation-comparison Use when benchmarking whether feature construction/extraction methods improve the accordance between engineered cell features and true cluster labels in scRNA-seq data, measured via silhouette values against original data. No true cell-type labels are available for the dataset, since silhouette coefficients must be computed against true cluster labels The goal is to compare clustering algorithms themselves (e.g. SC3 vs. Seurat vs. SIMLR accuracy/runtime) rather than feature construction methods within one clustering framework Input is already a reduced/feature-space representation; this skill constructs and compares representations from original expression profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces the SSCC paper's Figure 2 analysis, which compares alternative feature representations of scRNA-seq data (Euclidean-, cosine-, Pearson-, Spearman-correlation-based, and autoencoder-derived features) against the original expression profiles by computing silhouette coefficients against true cell-type labels on five benchmark datasets (Kolodziejczyk, Pollen, Usoskin, Zeisel, Zheng). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: Reproduces the SSCC paper's Figure 2 analysis, which compares alternative feature representations of scRNA-seq data (Euclidean-, cosine-, Pearson-, Spearman-correlation-based, and autoencoder-derived features) against the original expression profiles by computing silhouette coefficients against true cell-type labels on five benchmark datasets (Kolodziejczyk, Pollen, Usoskin, Zeisel, Zheng).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No true cell-type labels are available for the dataset, since silhouette coefficients must be computed against true cluster labels The goal is to compare clustering algorithms themselves (e.g. SC3 vs. Seurat vs. SIMLR accuracy/runtime) rather than feature construction methods within one clustering framework Input is already a reduced/feature-space representation; this skill constructs and compares representations from original expression profiles

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-gene-detection-rate-filtering Use when a raw single-cell read count matrix is highly zero-inflated (e.g. ~70% zeros) and must be filtered to well-detected genes prior to normalization, correlation estimation, or network inference with scLink. Input is already a normalized or imputed expression matrix rather than a raw count matrix (filtering should precede sclink_norm) Bulk RNA-seq or other non-single-cell data where zero inflation from non-detection is not the dominant feature A gene explicitly of biological interest falls below the detection-rate cutoff and should be force-included via a user-set threshold instead of dropped http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pre-processes sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices by keeping only genes detected in a minimum fraction of cells (e.g. >=10%), reducing all-zero-heavy features before scLink's Gamma-Normal mixture modeling and robust co-expression estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Pre-processes sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices by keeping only genes detected in a minimum fraction of cells (e.g. >=10%), reducing all-zero-heavy features before scLink's Gamma-Normal mixture modeling and robust co-expression estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized or imputed expression matrix rather than a raw count matrix (filtering should precede sclink_norm) Bulk RNA-seq or other non-single-cell data where zero inflation from non-detection is not the dominant feature A gene explicitly of biological interest falls below the detection-rate cutoff and should be force-included via a user-set threshold instead of dropped

skills.description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from a droplet-based scRNA-seq experiment (e.g. 10x cellranger filtered_bc_matrix or gene-by-cell tables) need QC, normalization, scaling and variable-feature detection prior to PCA/clustering.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-global-scaling-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-global-scaling-normalization Use when raw UMI count matrices from a droplet-based scRNA-seq experiment (e.g. 10x cellranger filtered_bc_matrix or gene-by-cell tables) need QC, normalization, scaling and variable-feature detection prior to PCA/clustering. Input is already normalized/scaled or an HVG feature table rather than raw UMI counts Data are scATAC-seq epigenomes (e.g. BMMCs) — use the LSI-based SCALA module instead Non-human/non-mouse datasets — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs the SCALA/Seurat scRNA-seq preprocessing module for the PBMC3k dataset: QC filtering on genes detected, UMI counts and mitochondrial percentage, followed by global-scaling normalization (counts per barcode scaled to 10,000 and log-transformed), z-score scaling, and VST-based highly variable feature detection that identified 1535 variable genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Reconstructs the SCALA/Seurat scRNA-seq preprocessing module for the PBMC3k dataset: QC filtering on genes detected, UMI counts and mitochondrial percentage, followed by global-scaling normalization (counts per barcode scaled to 10,000 and log-transformed), z-score scaling, and VST-based highly variable feature detection that identified 1535 variable genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/scaled or an HVG feature table rather than raw UMI counts Data are scATAC-seq epigenomes (e.g. BMMCs) — use the LSI-based SCALA module instead Non-human/non-mouse datasets — SCALA currently supports only human and mouse

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-hidden-layer-representation-extraction Use when a trained DL model (e.g., RFCN on the Zheng sorted scRNA-seq dataset) exists and you need its last hidden layer outputs projected into a 2D UMAP space to inspect cell-population separation by known cell-type labels. This makes learned high-level cell-type representations visually inspectable and enables parameter-sensitivity analysis of the embedding. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105530
skills.summary: Extracts the last hidden layer representations of a trained deep learning classifier (e.g., the RFCN model) on single-cell gene expression data using autoBioSeqpy, then embeds them in 2D with layerUMAP/UMAP. skills.description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq expression matrix has a large fraction of false zeros (dropout) and downstream analyses such as cell-cell distance or correlation computation are degraded by undetected transcripts.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq expression matrix has a large fraction of false zeros (dropout) and downstream analyses such as cell-cell distance or correlation computation are degraded by undetected transcripts. When all zeros should be treated as missing data and filled everywhere — methods like MAGIC/DCA output a matrix where every gene is expressed in every cell, whereas ALRA preserves biological zeros When the input is not an scRNA-seq-like non-negative, low-rank expression matrix with many zeros — ALRA's thresholding relies on true biological zeros being symmetrically distributed around zero after SVD When the matrix orientation is genes x rows — ALRA requires cells as rows and genes as columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Zero-preserving imputation of scRNA-seq count matrices using ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation), which computes a rank-k randomized SVD approximation and thresholds per-gene entries to complete technical (dropout) zeros while keeping true biological zeros at zero. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Zero-preserving imputation of scRNA-seq count matrices using ALRA (Adaptively thresholded Low-Rank Approximation), which computes a rank-k randomized SVD approximation and thresholds per-gene entries to complete technical (dropout) zeros while keeping true biological zeros at zero.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When all zeros should be treated as missing data and filled everywhere — methods like MAGIC/DCA output a matrix where every gene is expressed in every cell, whereas ALRA preserves biological zeros When the input is not an scRNA-seq-like non-negative, low-rank expression matrix with many zeros — ALRA's thresholding relies on true biological zeros being symmetrically distributed around zero after SVD When the matrix orientation is genes x rows — ALRA requires cells as rows and genes as columns

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix is highly sparse (>80% or even 95% zeros) and true expression levels behind excess zeros must be recovered computationally, treating all zeros as missing values.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix is highly sparse (>80% or even 95% zeros) and true expression levels behind excess zeros must be recovered computationally, treating all zeros as missing values. When zeros may be biological (true zero expression): LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes zeros with a nonzero value, without distinguishing biological from technical zeros When TensorFlow 2 is the required/available framework: LATE is not compatible with TensorFlow 2 and needs a TF 1.x (1.0–1.4) virtual environment When the input is not raw read counts but already imputed, normalized, or a feature/summary table http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Impute dropout zeros in highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10x Genomics h5/csv/tsv inputs) by training an autoencoder (LATE) with random initialization on nonzero values, producing a log10(count+1)-scale imputed hd5 matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Impute dropout zeros in highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10x Genomics h5/csv/tsv inputs) by training an autoencoder (LATE) with random initialization on nonzero values, producing a log10(count+1)-scale imputed hd5 matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When zeros may be biological (true zero expression): LATE assumes all zeros are missing values and always imputes zeros with a nonzero value, without distinguishing biological from technical zeros When TensorFlow 2 is the required/available framework: LATE is not compatible with TensorFlow 2 and needs a TF 1.x (1.0–1.4) virtual environment When the input is not raw read counts but already imputed, normalized, or a feature/summary table

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-label-noise-injection Use when you must quantify sensitivity of marker gene selection or cell-type classifiers to mislabeled training cells in scRNA-seq data (e.g. .h5ad AnnData with a group_by annotation column), at controlled corruption percentages for k selected markers. You need to assess robustness of a fully unsupervised clustering or marker method to label noise — unsupervised MarkerMap does not depend on input labels, so the corruption has no effect and the experiment is uninformative for it beyond confirming a flat curve Your data lack cell-type annotations (no group_by labels in adata.obs); uniform label corruption requires labels to corrupt You are evaluating marker stability with respect to sample size or k rather than annotation quality — use the standard benchmark over a range of k values instead of label_error http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking procedure that injects uniformly random label noise into single-cell RNA-seq training labels (label_error benchmark) to measure how robustly marker selection methods (MarkerMap variants, LassoNet-type baselines, RankCorr, COSG, RandomBaseline) select informative gene sets as annotation quality degrades. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: A benchmarking procedure that injects uniformly random label noise into single-cell RNA-seq training labels (label_error benchmark) to measure how robustly marker selection methods (MarkerMap variants, LassoNet-type baselines, RankCorr, COSG, RandomBaseline) select informative gene sets as annotation quality degrades.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to assess robustness of a fully unsupervised clustering or marker method to label noise — unsupervised MarkerMap does not depend on input labels, so the corruption has no effect and the experiment is uninformative for it beyond confirming a flat curve Your data lack cell-type annotations (no group_by labels in adata.obs); uniform label corruption requires labels to corrupt You are evaluating marker stability with respect to sample size or k rather than annotation quality — use the standard benchmark over a range of k values instead of label_error

skills.description: Decision support for choosing between RAW, TC, TMM, or FQ normalization before scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (PCA, ZIFA, ZINB-WaVE), when the analysis goal is to quantify how normalization choice affects clustering quality.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-library-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-library-normalization Decision support for choosing between RAW, TC, TMM, or FQ normalization before scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (PCA, ZIFA, ZINB-WaVE), when the analysis goal is to quantify how normalization choice affects clustering quality. The counts are already normalized (e.g., TC-scaled or log-transformed) — re-applying library normalization is redundant and the comparison design assumes RAW as one arm The downstream model is ZINB-WaVE with a column of ones in the gene-level covariate matrix — the paper shows its cell-level intercept acts as a global-scaling normalization factor, so no prior normalization is needed The data are bulk RNA-seq where a standard edgeR TMM differential-expression workflow suffices without a single-cell low-dimensional benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs comparable normalization variants (RAW, TC, TMM, FQ) of scRNA-seq count matrices and benchmarks their effect on downstream low-dimensional representations, testing whether ZINB-WaVE's built-in global-scaling intercept removes the need for a preliminary normalization step. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Constructs comparable normalization variants (RAW, TC, TMM, FQ) of scRNA-seq count matrices and benchmarks their effect on downstream low-dimensional representations, testing whether ZINB-WaVE's built-in global-scaling intercept removes the need for a preliminary normalization step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The counts are already normalized (e.g., TC-scaled or log-transformed) — re-applying library normalization is redundant and the comparison design assumes RAW as one arm The downstream model is ZINB-WaVE with a column of ones in the gene-level covariate matrix — the paper shows its cell-level intercept acts as a global-scaling normalization factor, so no prior normalization is needed The data are bulk RNA-seq where a standard edgeR TMM differential-expression workflow suffices without a single-cell low-dimensional benchmark

skills.description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) that must be scaled by cell library size and log-transformed before embedding, similarity search, or feature gene selection.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-log-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-log-normalization Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) that must be scaled by cell library size and log-transformed before embedding, similarity search, or feature gene selection. Input is already log-normalized or is a feature/summary table rather than raw counts — re-normalizing would distort expression values. The downstream method expects raw counts or applies its own internal size-factor normalization. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Library-size normalization to the median total count followed by log2(x+1) transformation of a scRNA-seq count matrix, producing a cells-by-genes log-normalized matrix suitable for downstream methods such as EDGE dimensionality reduction and feature gene extraction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Library-size normalization to the median total count followed by log2(x+1) transformation of a scRNA-seq count matrix, producing a cells-by-genes log-normalized matrix suitable for downstream methods such as EDGE dimensionality reduction and feature gene extraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already log-normalized or is a feature/summary table rather than raw counts — re-normalizing would distort expression values. The downstream method expects raw counts or applies its own internal size-factor normalization.

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData dataset needs a small panel of marker genes (e.g., k=50 or fewer than 10% of genes) that maximize cell type classification accuracy, as in spatial transcriptomics panel design or marker benchmarking studies.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData dataset needs a small panel of marker genes (e.g., k=50 or fewer than 10% of genes) that maximize cell type classification accuracy, as in spatial transcriptomics panel design or marker benchmarking studies. Input is not cell-by-gene scRNA-seq expression with cell type labels (the method relies on supervised classification signal) The goal is differential expression per se rather than selecting a minimal k-marker set for cell type prediction — Scanpy DE tests or COSG target that directly Data is extremely high-dimensional with no ability to densify adata.X — sparse matrices must first be converted via adata.X.toarray() http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects minimal, cell-type-informative gene marker sets from scRNA-seq data using MarkerMap, a generative VAE-based model with supervised/mixed/unsupervised modes controlled by loss_tradeoff, and benchmarks the resulting k markers against baselines (LassoNet, SMaSH, COSG, PERSIST, RankCorr, RandomBaseline) via nearest-neighbor and Random Forest classification accuracy and weighted F1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: Selects minimal, cell-type-informative gene marker sets from scRNA-seq data using MarkerMap, a generative VAE-based model with supervised/mixed/unsupervised modes controlled by loss_tradeoff, and benchmarks the resulting k markers against baselines (LassoNet, SMaSH, COSG, PERSIST, RankCorr, RandomBaseline) via nearest-neighbor and Random Forest classification accuracy and weighted F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not cell-by-gene scRNA-seq expression with cell type labels (the method relies on supervised classification signal) The goal is differential expression per se rather than selecting a minimal k-marker set for cell type prediction — Scanpy DE tests or COSG target that directly Data is extremely high-dimensional with no ability to densify adata.X — sparse matrices must first be converted via adata.X.toarray()

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain many cell types/tissues with overlapping DE genes and you need one global marker set that discriminates every phenotype pair (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or human cell atlas datasets).
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection Use when scRNA-seq data contain many cell types/tissues with overlapping DE genes and you need one global marker set that discriminates every phenotype pair (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or human cell atlas datasets). The goal is per-cell-type markers for a small number of distinct groups with non-overlapping DE genes — standard differential expression suffices You need the provably optimal minimum marker set — G-PC is a polynomial-time approximation and does not provide an optimal solution The target variable is numeric or the task is generic ML feature selection without phenotype-pair coverage requirements (use mRMR or all-relevant methods instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects a global, discriminative set of markers from single-cell RNA-seq data by formulating marker selection as the phenotype cover (PC) problem — equivalent to NP-complete multiset multicover — and approximating it with GreedyPC (extended greedy set cover) or CEMPC (cross-entropy method) from the phenotype-cover package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Selects a global, discriminative set of markers from single-cell RNA-seq data by formulating marker selection as the phenotype cover (PC) problem — equivalent to NP-complete multiset multicover — and approximating it with GreedyPC (extended greedy set cover) or CEMPC (cross-entropy method) from the phenotype-cover package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is per-cell-type markers for a small number of distinct groups with non-overlapping DE genes — standard differential expression suffices You need the provably optimal minimum marker set — G-PC is a polynomial-time approximation and does not provide an optimal solution The target variable is numeric or the task is generic ML feature selection without phenotype-pair coverage requirements (use mRMR or all-relevant methods instead)

skills.description: Use when an scRNA-seq expression matrix is normalized but unscaled and will feed a non-negative-kernel autoencoder or neural-network feature-selection/dimensionality-reduction step that requires bounded, non-negative input values.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-minmax-rescaling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-minmax-rescaling Use when an scRNA-seq expression matrix is normalized but unscaled and will feed a non-negative-kernel autoencoder or neural-network feature-selection/dimensionality-reduction step that requires bounded, non-negative input values. Data is not yet normalized — scCAN's workflow assumes an already-normalized matrix; rescaling raw counts directly would misrepresent expression levels The downstream method is not a non-negative/NN-constrained model (e.g. PCA-based tools like CIDR or SEURAT that accept unbounded standardized values) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Rescale an already-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) so each gene's values fall in the 0–1 range via min-max scaling, as the first step of the scCAN pipeline before non-negative-kernel autoencoder feature selection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Rescale an already-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) so each gene's values fall in the 0–1 range via min-max scaling, as the first step of the scCAN pipeline before non-negative-kernel autoencoder feature selection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is not yet normalized — scCAN's workflow assumes an already-normalized matrix; rescaling raw counts directly would misrepresent expression levels The downstream method is not a non-negative/NN-constrained model (e.g. PCA-based tools like CIDR or SEURAT that accept unbounded standardized values)
