skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-multi-dataset-integration Use when several independently generated scRNA-seq datasets (different labs, platforms, or batches) must be merged so cells group by biological cell type rather than by study of origin. Analyzing a single dataset with no batch/study structure to correct — plain ACTIONet without the Harmony-kernel reduction suffices When the goal is differential-state or activity analysis within one condition rather than cross-study integration and label harmonization When input is already a reduced/embedded feature representation rather than raw gene-by-cell counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrate multiple independent scRNA-seq studies into a joint analysis using ACTIONet's Harmony-kernel batch-corrected reduction, then transfer cell-type labels across datasets via network-based label propagation and consolidate them into consensus gene signatures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Integrate multiple independent scRNA-seq studies into a joint analysis using ACTIONet's Harmony-kernel batch-corrected reduction, then transfer cell-type labels across datasets via network-based label propagation and consolidate them into consensus gene signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing a single dataset with no batch/study structure to correct — plain ACTIONet without the Harmony-kernel reduction suffices When the goal is differential-state or activity analysis within one condition rather than cross-study integration and label harmonization When input is already a reduced/embedded feature representation rather than raw gene-by-cell counts

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices must be normalized before association testing (DE, co-expression, or CRISPR screen) and unbiased, uniformly distributed null P values across gene expression levels are required.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices must be normalized before association testing (DE, co-expression, or CRISPR screen) and unbiased, uniformly distributed null P values across gene expression levels are required. Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq data — the study only focused on UMI-based datasets, and nonlinear covariates may need revalidation on full-length platforms The goal is hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations, not linear DE/co-expression/CRISPR screen inference An integrative analysis spanning multiple datasets requires batch-effect correction, which Normalisr does not address http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalizes raw scRNA-seq UMI read counts with the Normalisr normalization module (lcpm, normcov, scaling_factor, compute_var, normvar) so that nonlinear library-size confounders are removed at both mean and variance levels, yielding unbiased P values for downstream differential expression, co-expression, and CRISPR screen testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26682-1
skills.summary: Normalizes raw scRNA-seq UMI read counts with the Normalisr normalization module (lcpm, normcov, scaling_factor, compute_var, normvar) so that nonlinear library-size confounders are removed at both mean and variance levels, yielding unbiased P values for downstream differential expression, co-expression, and CRISPR screen testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is full-length (non-UMI) scRNA-seq data — the study only focused on UMI-based datasets, and nonlinear covariates may need revalidation on full-length platforms The goal is hypothesis testing of arbitrary nonlinear associations, not linear DE/co-expression/CRISPR screen inference An integrative analysis spanning multiple datasets requires batch-effect correction, which Normalisr does not address

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows strong within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle genes (e.g. cells cluster by cell-cycle stage instead of cell type) and you need a corrected matrix before clustering.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows strong within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle genes (e.g. cells cluster by cell-cycle stage instead of cell type) and you need a corrected matrix before clustering. The dataset is known to have very low cell-cycle activity (e.g. the Patel et al. glioblastoma data), where the default CΔ cutoff of 3 is too strict and a lower cutoff (CΔ = 2) must be used instead of the default call The dominant unwanted variation is not the cell cycle (e.g. batch or other confounders) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and will not remove these other effects The goal is to remove any leading factor regardless of its annotation (the scLVM approach) rather than to test whether each factor is cell-cycle-driven; blind factor removal risks deleting the biological signal of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A pre-processing workflow for single-cell RNA-Seq matrices that identifies leading principal components driven by annotated cell-cycle genes (using a bootstrap t-statistic) and removes them, while preserving other biological signals such as the TH2 substructure in differentiating T-helper cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/srep33892
skills.summary: A pre-processing workflow for single-cell RNA-Seq matrices that identifies leading principal components driven by annotated cell-cycle genes (using a bootstrap t-statistic) and removes them, while preserving other biological signals such as the TH2 substructure in differentiating T-helper cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is known to have very low cell-cycle activity (e.g. the Patel et al. glioblastoma data), where the default CΔ cutoff of 3 is too strict and a lower cutoff (CΔ = 2) must be used instead of the default call The dominant unwanted variation is not the cell cycle (e.g. batch or other confounders) — ccRemover is designed for removing the cell-cycle effect exclusively and will not remove these other effects The goal is to remove any leading factor regardless of its annotation (the scLVM approach) rather than to test whether each factor is cell-cycle-driven; blind factor removal risks deleting the biological signal of interest

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g. CD34_sc from MetacellAnalysisToolkit) must be normalized and embedded prior to building metacells or computing QC metrics like purity, compactness, or separation.

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-dimensionality-reduction Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g. CD34_sc from MetacellAnalysisToolkit) must be normalized and embedded prior to building metacells or computing QC metrics like purity, compactness, or separation. Input is already normalized and embedded (e.g. a processed .h5ad or Seurat object with PCA/UMAP already computed) — re-running would change the latent space and invalidate prior metacell memberships Data are scATAC-seq, where SEACells uses an LSI/SVD embedding (X_svd) rather than the scRNA-seq PCA pipeline described here http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Preprocess single-cell RNA-seq data with Seurat (LogNormalize normalization, variable feature selection, scaling, PCA, UMAP) to obtain the latent embedding required before metacell construction and QC in the MetacellAnalysisToolkit workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s44320-024-00045-6
skills.summary: Preprocess single-cell RNA-seq data with Seurat (LogNormalize normalization, variable feature selection, scaling, PCA, UMAP) to obtain the latent embedding required before metacell construction and QC in the MetacellAnalysisToolkit workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized and embedded (e.g. a processed .h5ad or Seurat object with PCA/UMAP already computed) — re-running would change the latent space and invalidate prior metacell memberships Data are scATAC-seq, where SEACells uses an LSI/SVD embedding (X_svd) rather than the scRNA-seq PCA pipeline described here

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-scaling Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object has already been through a coarse doublet-removal (overkill) step and you need normalized, scaled, PCA-embedded data to build k-means clusters for artificial doublet simulation. skills.summary: Preprocess a prefiltered Seurat object (NormalizeData, FindVariableFeatures, ScaleData, PCA on PC1-30) so its cell embeddings can be partitioned by k-means (k=20) to simulate artificial doublets for Chord's GBM ensemble training set.

skills.description: Use when a raw Seurat object of single-cell RNA-seq data must be prepared for Connectome's CreateConnectome — i.e. before ligand-receptor z-score calculation on the panc8, ifnb, or similar annotated scRNA-seq objects.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-scaling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-scaling Use when a raw Seurat object of single-cell RNA-seq data must be prepared for Connectome's CreateConnectome — i.e. before ligand-receptor z-score calculation on the panc8, ifnb, or similar annotated scRNA-seq objects. Input is already normalized/scaled or is a feature table rather than a raw Seurat scRNA-seq object — re-normalizing would distort z-score-based edge weights. The goal is downstream network visualization only (NetworkPlot, CircosPlot) on an already-built connectome — no re-normalization is needed. Cell type identities or clusters are not yet annotated on the Seurat object; Connectome defines nodes from the active identity slot. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Normalize and scale single-cell RNA-seq expression data in Seurat before connectomic ligand-receptor mapping: NormalizeData on the raw counts, subsetting to ligand/receptor genes from a ground-truth database (e.g. ncomms8866_human from FANTOM5/Ramilowski 2015), and ScaleData on those genes so that edge z-scores in CreateConnectome are computed on comparable expression distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-07959-x
skills.summary: Normalize and scale single-cell RNA-seq expression data in Seurat before connectomic ligand-receptor mapping: NormalizeData on the raw counts, subsetting to ligand/receptor genes from a ground-truth database (e.g. ncomms8866_human from FANTOM5/Ramilowski 2015), and ScaleData on those genes so that edge z-scores in CreateConnectome are computed on comparable expression distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized/scaled or is a feature table rather than a raw Seurat scRNA-seq object — re-normalizing would distort z-score-based edge weights. The goal is downstream network visualization only (NetworkPlot, CircosPlot) on an already-built connectome — no re-normalization is needed. Cell type identities or clusters are not yet annotated on the Seurat object; Connectome defines nodes from the active identity slot.

skills.description: Use when you have two or more independently pre-processed SingCellaR objects from biological replicates and need a single integrated object for downstream clustering, UMAP visualization, and cell-type annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-object-merging
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-object-merging Use when you have two or more independently pre-processed SingCellaR objects from biological replicates and need a single integrated object for downstream clustering, UMAP visualization, and cell-type annotation. You have only a single pre-processed object — use the standard per-sample workflow with get_variable_genes_by_fitting_GLM_model instead of the integrative variant Your objects are in Seurat or SingleCellExperiment format and cannot be converted — SingCellaR still lacks automatic object transformation to interact with packages such as Seurat You have not yet performed per-replicate preprocessing and QC — merging raw, unfiltered objects is outside this skill's scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Merges pre-processed SingCellaR objects from biological replicates (e.g., early fetal liver samples eFL_1 and eFL_2) into a single combined object, then re-applies QC, normalization, regression, variable gene selection, PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering so cells cluster by major cell type rather than by sample of origin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2022.101266
skills.summary: Merges pre-processed SingCellaR objects from biological replicates (e.g., early fetal liver samples eFL_1 and eFL_2) into a single combined object, then re-applies QC, normalization, regression, variable gene selection, PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering so cells cluster by major cell type rather than by sample of origin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single pre-processed object — use the standard per-sample workflow with get_variable_genes_by_fitting_GLM_model instead of the integrative variant Your objects are in Seurat or SingleCellExperiment format and cannot be converted — SingCellaR still lacks automatic object transformation to interact with packages such as Seurat You have not yet performed per-replicate preprocessing and QC — merging raw, unfiltered objects is outside this skill's scope

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a differential-state method (e.g., Augur) inflates false positives as patient-level variability (tau^2) grows, by simulating null scRNA-seq data with beta=0 and comparing against scDist's calibrated p-values.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-perturbation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-perturbation-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a differential-state method (e.g., Augur) inflates false positives as patient-level variability (tau^2) grows, by simulating null scRNA-seq data with beta=0 and comparing against scDist's calibrated p-values. When conditions truly differ (beta != 0), the null calibration check is not informative and power rather than false-positive control should be evaluated When data are raw counts: scDist requires normalized input (scTransform Pearson residuals recommended) and cannot yet be applied directly to counts When performing differential abundance (proportion changes) rather than differential state: DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate tools, not this benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark workflow for comparing perturbed-cell-type detection methods (Augur AUC-based vs. scDist mixed-effects distance) under null-simulated scRNA-seq conditions, quantifying false positives driven by individual-to-individual variability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Benchmark workflow for comparing perturbed-cell-type detection methods (Augur AUC-based vs. scDist mixed-effects distance) under null-simulated scRNA-seq conditions, quantifying false positives driven by individual-to-individual variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When conditions truly differ (beta != 0), the null calibration check is not informative and power rather than false-positive control should be evaluated When data are raw counts: scDist requires normalized input (scTransform Pearson residuals recommended) and cannot yet be applied directly to counts When performing differential abundance (proportion changes) rather than differential state: DA-seq, Milo, or Meld are the appropriate tools, not this benchmark

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g. cancer scRNA-seq from 10X or RDS) must be quality-filtered, normalized, and scaled before cell-type annotation, malignancy prediction, or feeding an XGBoost model in scCancer2.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g. cancer scRNA-seq from 10X or RDS) must be quality-filtered, normalized, and scaled before cell-type annotation, malignancy prediction, or feeding an XGBoost model in scCancer2. The input is already a normalized and scaled Seurat object or feature table rather than raw counts. The data are bulk RNA-seq (e.g. the TCGA training matrix side of scCancer2) rather than single-cell counts requiring per-cell QC. The analysis is spatial transcriptomics, which scCancer2 handles with a separate module rather than this scRNA-seq preprocessing path. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Standard Seurat-based preprocessing of tumor scRNA-seq count matrices used by scCancer2: quality filtering (min.genes=200, min.cells=3), mito.percent computation, LogNormalize at scale factor 10000, vst variable-feature selection up to 5000 features, and scaling with regression on nCount_RNA and mito.percent so the matrix can be aligned to a fixed gene list for downstream classifiers. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Standard Seurat-based preprocessing of tumor scRNA-seq count matrices used by scCancer2: quality filtering (min.genes=200, min.cells=3), mito.percent computation, LogNormalize at scale factor 10000, vst variable-feature selection up to 5000 features, and scaling with regression on nCount_RNA and mito.percent so the matrix can be aligned to a fixed gene list for downstream classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized and scaled Seurat object or feature table rather than raw counts. The data are bulk RNA-seq (e.g. the TCGA training matrix side of scCancer2) rather than single-cell counts requiring per-cell QC. The analysis is spatial transcriptomics, which scCancer2 handles with a separate module rather than this scRNA-seq preprocessing path.

skills.description: Use when preparing single-cell count matrices (e.g., capital.dataset.setty19, velten17, paul15) for branched pseudotime trajectory inference or trajectory-tree alignment, where denoised, dimension-reduced expression is required.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing Use when preparing single-cell count matrices (e.g., capital.dataset.setty19, velten17, paul15) for branched pseudotime trajectory inference or trajectory-tree alignment, where denoised, dimension-reduced expression is required. If the goal is batch integration of multiple datasets — the article notes anchor/integration approaches (Scanorama, Seurat) use mutual nearest neighbors whereas CAPITAL computes Spearman's correlation for alignment, and integration can wrongly match cell subpopulations If trajectories are expected to contain cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL handles only trajectory trees computed from the preprocessed data If the input is already denoised/embedded and compatible with capital.tl.trajectory_tree, re-running preprocessing may generate an undesirably different cluster structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Standardizes raw scRNA-seq count data for trajectory-tree alignment by running CAPITAL's MAGIC denoising, PCA, and k-NN preprocessing on each dataset (e.g., Setty19 human CD34+ bone marrow, Velten17, Paul15) before pseudotime and tree inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Standardizes raw scRNA-seq count data for trajectory-tree alignment by running CAPITAL's MAGIC denoising, PCA, and k-NN preprocessing on each dataset (e.g., Setty19 human CD34+ bone marrow, Velten17, Paul15) before pseudotime and tree inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is batch integration of multiple datasets — the article notes anchor/integration approaches (Scanorama, Seurat) use mutual nearest neighbors whereas CAPITAL computes Spearman's correlation for alignment, and integration can wrongly match cell subpopulations If trajectories are expected to contain cycles or disconnected graphs — CAPITAL handles only trajectory trees computed from the preprocessed data If the input is already denoised/embedded and compatible with capital.tl.trajectory_tree, re-running preprocessing may generate an undesirably different cluster structure

skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already spatial transcriptomics spots (Visium/MERSCOPE/MERFISH/Xenium) serving as the training side of the CeLEry pipeline — this normalization targets the dissociated scRNA-seq test data The downstream method requires raw integer counts or library-size-only normalization (e.g. differential expression testing), since gene-level z-scoring destroys the count scale The gene space cannot be matched to the pretrained model (few or no overlapping non-DE genes), so gene-level standardization on the shared set is not meaningful

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-control-filtering Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (.csv or .parquet) need QC summarization and low-quality cell/gene removal as a preprocessing step before normalization, HVG selection, and clustering. Input is already normalized or filtered data where re-filtering would drop valid cells/genes (data_filter() expects raw count-derived quality summaries) Data are not single-cell transcriptomic counts — the cutoffs (genes per cell, dropout rate, percent_ercc/percent_mito) are meaningless for bulk RNA-seq or other data types Input files are formats other than .csv or .parquet; the current scSPARKL pipeline only accepts those two formats http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality control and cell/gene filtering stage of the scSPARKL pipeline: Spark-parallel routines generate per-cell and per-gene quality summaries from melted tall-format scRNA-seq count data, then apply the `data_filter()` function to remove unwanted cells and genes using configurable cutoffs before normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a reference-based cell type annotator can flag unseen cell types as 'Unknown': remove one cell type from the training reference and check predictions on held-out cells of that type.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-reference-subsetting
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-reference-subsetting Use when evaluating whether a reference-based cell type annotator can flag unseen cell types as 'Unknown': remove one cell type from the training reference and check predictions on held-out cells of that type. The goal is standard annotation of query cells whose types are all represented in the reference — subsetting would only remove training signal and degrade accuracy. The analysis is unsupervised clustering or de novo discovery without any reference dataset, since this skill presupposes a labeled training reference. The query and reference gene spaces cannot be reconciled — TOSICA requires query_adata = query_adata[:,ref_adata.var_names], so mismatched var_names must be fixed before this workflow is meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Deliberately delete a high-abundance cell type (e.g. alpha cells from the hPancreas reference AnnData) before training an annotator so that held-out cells of the deleted type can be used to test whether the tool abstains ('Unknown') instead of force-labeling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-35923-4
skills.summary: Deliberately delete a high-abundance cell type (e.g. alpha cells from the hPancreas reference AnnData) before training an annotator so that held-out cells of the deleted type can be used to test whether the tool abstains ('Unknown') instead of force-labeling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard annotation of query cells whose types are all represented in the reference — subsetting would only remove training signal and degrade accuracy. The analysis is unsupervised clustering or de novo discovery without any reference dataset, since this skill presupposes a labeled training reference. The query and reference gene spaces cannot be reconciled — TOSICA requires query_adata = query_adata[:,ref_adata.var_names], so mismatched var_names must be fixed before this workflow is meaningful.

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation Use when a new or existing rare-cell detection method needs quantitative benchmarking against competitors, and no real dataset with validated rare-cell ground-truth labels of controlled size and differential-expression level is available. When real experimental data with externally validated rare-cell identities (e.g. tuft cells in the intestine dataset marked by Dclk1/Trpm5) is available — biological realism matters more than controlled ground truth When the goal is to characterize detection limits only in one regime — a single Splatter setting is insufficient; the sweep over population size and de.prob is what makes conclusions general When the tool under test requires major cell types to be pre-specified and simulation scenarios cannot encode that annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate ground-truth single-cell RNA-seq benchmark data with Splatter by planting rare cell populations across controlled simulation parameters (rare population size 2–100 cells, de.prob 0.1–0.8), enabling rigorous F1-score comparison of rare-cell detection methods such as GapClust, RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS and FiRE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24489-8

skills.description: Use when benchmarking how many DE genes are needed for a method (e.g. FiRE) to detect a rare cell subpopulation (~5% of cells) in simulated scRNA-seq data, or when building AUC-ROC sensitivity curves over DE-gene counts.
skills.name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation Use when benchmarking how many DE genes are needed for a method (e.g. FiRE) to detect a rare cell subpopulation (~5% of cells) in simulated scRNA-seq data, or when building AUC-ROC sensitivity curves over DE-gene counts. The goal is clustering or typing all major cell populations rather than detecting a rare minor subpopulation. Input is real single-cell data with known labels; the skill specifically targets splatter-simulated two-group data for controlled sensitivity sweeps. The rare population differs from the major population by only 1-19 DE genes and detection is expected to fail — FiRE struggled below ~20 DE genes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Sensitivity-evaluation skill for rare-cell detection: simulate two-group single-cell expression data with the splatter R package (a 5% rare population among 500 cells x 5000 genes), vary the number of differentially expressed (DE) genes distinguishing the minor group, and score each simulation with FiRE to build an AUC-ROC versus DE-gene-count curve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Sensitivity-evaluation skill for rare-cell detection: simulate two-group single-cell expression data with the splatter R package (a 5% rare population among 500 cells x 5000 genes), vary the number of differentially expressed (DE) genes distinguishing the minor group, and score each simulation with FiRE to build an AUC-ROC versus DE-gene-count curve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering or typing all major cell populations rather than detecting a rare minor subpopulation. Input is real single-cell data with known labels; the skill specifically targets splatter-simulated two-group data for controlled sensitivity sweeps. The rare population differs from the major population by only 1-19 DE genes and detection is expected to fail — FiRE struggled below ~20 DE genes.

skills.summary: Embedding single-cell RNA-seq data into a 2D UMAP space via a scanpy/scvelo neighborhood graph, used in the Cytocipher workflow to visualize over-clustered (Leiden resolution 3.5) cells and the merged significantly different clusters.

skills.search_text: single-cell-rna-spatial-data-integration Use when integrating scRNA-seq reference data with spatial transcriptomics (e.g., STARmap, MERFISH, 10x Visium) to obtain shared latent embeddings or deconvolve spatial spot cell-type proportions via an optimal transport plan. Cells are paired/profiled from the same cells and you only need vertical integration without OT-plan deconvolution The datasets share no genes and you need diagonal integration with dataset-specific modeling only Memory cannot hold the dense global OT plan matrix — skip save_OT or use embedding-based label transfer instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrates heterogeneous single-cell datasets (scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics) by combining a coupled variational autoencoder with Minibatch Unbalanced Optimal Transport (Minibatch-UOT) in the uniPort framework, enabling joint embedding and OT-plan-based spatial deconvolution of spot cell-type proportions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Integrates heterogeneous single-cell datasets (scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics) by combining a coupled variational autoencoder with Minibatch Unbalanced Optimal Transport (Minibatch-UOT) in the uniPort framework, enabling joint embedding and OT-plan-based spatial deconvolution of spot cell-type proportions.

skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-age-binned-aggregation Use when you have an aggregated multi-tissue, multi-age single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object and need to algorithmically derive cell-type-specific signatures of an age-associated cellular state (e.g., senescence) from age-dynamic expression changes. The goal is scoring existing cells for senescence with already-published signatures — use load_hubs + score_hub instead of re-deriving hubs You need a universal pan-tissue signature only — call merge_hubs over hubs.metadata with calculate_thresh rather than re-running the full derivation Your dataset lacks an age/time axis, so age-dynamic differential expression scores (Equations 4-6) cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Derives cell-type-specific cellular senescence (CS) signatures by aggregating single-cell RNA-seq cells by tissue, cell type, and 10-year age bins, computing age-dynamic differential expression scores (paper's Equations 4-6), and building gene-gene co-expression hub networks from those scores. skills.description: Use when clustering raw or normalized scRNA-seq count/expression matrices (rows = cells, columns = genes) with tens of thousands of genes or millions of cells, especially when the number of cell types is unknown and rare cell types may be present.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-autoencoder-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-autoencoder-clustering Use when clustering raw or normalized scRNA-seq count/expression matrices (rows = cells, columns = genes) with tens of thousands of genes or millions of cells, especially when the number of cell types is unknown and rare cell types may be present. Input is not a gene-by-cell expression matrix (e.g. already-reduced embeddings, feature tables, or metadata only) — scCAN expects expression values and performs its own min-max scaling and log2(data+1) transformation Supervised cell-type annotation is the goal and reference labels already exist — scCAN is unsupervised and estimates cluster number via eigengap, not against labels Datasets with ambiguous/dropped cell labels that should be removed first (e.g. 'zothers', 'dropped', 'not applicable', 'Not available') without prior label cleanup http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data using scCAN, which compresses the expression matrix through a non-negative-kernel autoencoder (min-max scaled to 0-1, top 5000 genes) and a stacked variational autoencoder (latent dimension d=15), then partitions cells via similarity-network fusion and eigengap-based spectral clustering. Suited to large, noisy scRNA-seq datasets where accurate cell-type separation and automatic estimation of the number of clusters are required. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-14218-6
skills.summary: Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data using scCAN, which compresses the expression matrix through a non-negative-kernel autoencoder (min-max scaled to 0-1, top 5000 genes) and a stacked variational autoencoder (latent dimension d=15), then partitions cells via similarity-network fusion and eigengap-based spectral clustering. skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-dimensionality-reduction Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GSE84133 Baron pancreas) and need a low-dimensional embedding that preserves inter-population centroid distances and developmental trajectory structure rather than only local neighbor structure. When only a cheap 2D visualization of local neighborhoods is needed and inter-population topological structure is not a concern — plain t-SNE suffices and scGAE adds graph-building and training overhead When the goal is direct 2D embedding: the graph autoencoder cannot embed complex data structure directly into two dimensions; it yields an intermediate dimension that still requires t-SNE for visualization When a matching K for the KNN graph cannot be justified — the optimal K varies among datasets and parts of a dataset and is not resolved by the method http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply scGAE, a single-cell graph autoencoder, to reduce scRNA-seq count matrices to a low-dimensional (e.g., 20-D) embedding that preserves the topological/inter-cluster structure among cell populations, outperforming t-SNE, scVI, DCA, PHATE and other deep-learning methods on trajectory and cluster-distance preservation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Apply scGAE, a single-cell graph autoencoder, to reduce scRNA-seq count matrices to a low-dimensional (e.g., 20-D) embedding that preserves the topological/inter-cluster structure among cell populations, outperforming t-SNE, scVI, DCA, PHATE and other deep-learning methods on trajectory and cluster-distance preservation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a cheap 2D visualization of local neighborhoods is needed and inter-population topological structure is not a concern — plain t-SNE suffices and scGAE adds graph-building and training overhead When the goal is direct 2D embedding: the graph autoencoder cannot embed complex data structure directly into two dimensions; it yields an intermediate dimension that still requires t-SNE for visualization When a matching K for the KNN graph cannot be justified — the optimal K varies among datasets and parts of a dataset and is not resolved by the method

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix plus per-cell metadata (condition, patient, cluster/cell-type label) with replicates, and you need a statistically rigorous per-cell-type distance between condition means rather than a differential-abundance or classifier-based.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-distance-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-distance-estimation Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix plus per-cell metadata (condition, patient, cluster/cell-type label) with replicates, and you need a statistically rigorous per-cell-type distance between condition means rather than a differential-abundance or classifier-based. Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to counts; normalize first The question is differential abundance (changing cell proportions) — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead of differential-state distance estimation Clustering/annotation is unreliable or heavily over-clustered — condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward-biased distances, producing false negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimate transcriptomic perturbation distances between conditions for predefined cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data using scDist, which fits per-principal-component linear mixed-effects models (lme4, Satterthwaite df via lmerTest) to correct for individual-to-individual and technical variability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51649-3
skills.summary: Estimate transcriptomic perturbation distances between conditions for predefined cell types in single-cell RNA-seq data using scDist, which fits per-principal-component linear mixed-effects models (lme4, Satterthwaite df via lmerTest) to correct for individual-to-individual and technical variability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw (unnormalized) counts — scDist cannot currently be applied directly to counts; normalize first The question is differential abundance (changing cell proportions) — use DA-seq, Milo, or Meld instead of differential-state distance estimation Clustering/annotation is unreliable or heavily over-clustered — condition-specific effects can cause over-clustering and downward-biased distances, producing false negatives

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq doublet analysis needs to boost Chord beyond its three built-in tools by appending scores from any external doublet detector to the saved chord() objects and re-running the ensemble.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-doublet-detection
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-doublet-detection Use when a scRNA-seq doublet analysis needs to boost Chord beyond its three built-in tools by appending scores from any external doublet detector to the saved chord() objects and re-running the ensemble. When the goal is a single-method doublet detection without ensemble aggregation — Chord's GBM integration adds runtime overhead and is not optimal in time efficiency When no prior chord() run has been completed, since the port requires the exported seu.robj, sce.robj, and score CSV files When experimental doublet labeling (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) is already available, which labels doublets directly rather than computationally Integrate external doublet detection methods (e.g. Python-based Scrublet or DoubletDetection) into Chord's ensemble GBM model through its expandable port, producing an enhanced Chord Plus (ChordP) version that refits the GBM over built-in plus external method scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Integrate external doublet detection methods (e.g. Python-based Scrublet or DoubletDetection) into Chord's ensemble GBM model through its expandable port, producing an enhanced Chord Plus (ChordP) version that refits the GBM over built-in plus external method scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single-method doublet detection without ensemble aggregation — Chord's GBM integration adds runtime overhead and is not optimal in time efficiency When no prior chord() run has been completed, since the port requires the exported seu.robj, sce.robj, and score CSV files When experimental doublet labeling (cell hashing, MULTI-seq, demuxlet) is already available, which labels doublets directly rather than computationally

skills.description: Use when benchmarking computational performance (runtime, peak memory) of a scoring method across dataset sizes and you need controlled, identically sized single-cell expression matrices rather than testing only on the full million-cell atlas.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-downsampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-downsampling Use when benchmarking computational performance (runtime, peak memory) of a scoring method across dataset sizes and you need controlled, identically sized single-cell expression matrices rather than testing only on the full million-cell atlas. The goal is biological discovery (multicellular pathway modules via MOFA), not performance measurement — downsampling cells would discard signal; the paper notes downsampling strategies (e.g. SCPA's default 500 cells per condition) may lose information on large datasets The study has fewer samples than scPAFA's requirement of at least 15 samples (not cells) for MOFA-based module identification — downsampling cells does not address the sample-count constraint The input is already a small dataset at the target size, making downsampling a no-op http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate downsampled versions of single-cell gene expression matrices spanning a range of cell counts (e.g. 10,000 to 1,263,676 cells from the lupus atlas) so that runtime and peak-memory scaling of pathway activity scoring methods can be benchmarked on identically sized inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: Generate downsampled versions of single-cell gene expression matrices spanning a range of cell counts (e.g. 10,000 to 1,263,676 cells from the lupus atlas) so that runtime and peak-memory scaling of pathway activity scoring methods can be benchmarked on identically sized inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological discovery (multicellular pathway modules via MOFA), not performance measurement — downsampling cells would discard signal; the paper notes downsampling strategies (e.g. SCPA's default 500 cells per condition) may lose information on large datasets The study has fewer samples than scPAFA's requirement of at least 15 samples (not cells) for MOFA-based module identification — downsampling cells does not address the sample-count constraint The input is already a small dataset at the target size, making downsampling a no-op

skills.description: Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x top-1000 high-dispersion genes) contains dropout zeros that impair downstream clustering, expression recovery, or variance stabilization analyses.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-imputation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-imputation Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x top-1000 high-dispersion genes) contains dropout zeros that impair downstream clustering, expression recovery, or variance stabilization analyses. The expression matrix is already dense/imputed — further autoencoder imputation would distort true zeros in biologically silent genes Data have not been pre-processed (log2 transform, library-size normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion gene selection) — AutoImpute.py expects a pre-processed count matrix The analysis goal is a very small dataset where overfitting by an overcomplete (2000-unit) hidden layer is a concern and the paper's matrix-factorization or nuclear-norm baselines may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Impute dropouts in sparse single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices using AutoImpute, a three-layer fully-connected overcomplete autoencoder trained on observed (non-zero) entries only. Treats imputation as a collaborative-filtering/matrix-completion problem so missing values are filled with minimal modification to biologically silent genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-34688-x
skills.summary: Impute dropouts in sparse single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices using AutoImpute, a three-layer fully-connected overcomplete autoencoder trained on observed (non-zero) entries only. Treats imputation as a collaborative-filtering/matrix-completion problem so missing values are filled with minimal modification to biologically silent genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix is already dense/imputed — further autoencoder imputation would distort true zeros in biologically silent genes Data have not been pre-processed (log2 transform, library-size normalization, top-1000 high-dispersion gene selection) — AutoImpute.py expects a pre-processed count matrix The analysis goal is a very small dataset where overfitting by an overcomplete (2000-unit) hidden layer is a concern and the paper's matrix-factorization or nuclear-norm baselines may suffice

skills.description: Use when assessing robustness of bulk deconvolution (MuSiC) to zero-inflation in the single-cell reference: apply a dropout grid to a scRNA-seq ExpressionSet, re-estimate proportions with music_prop, and score against real proportions.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation Use when assessing robustness of bulk deconvolution (MuSiC) to zero-inflation in the single-cell reference: apply a dropout grid to a scRNA-seq ExpressionSet, re-estimate proportions with music_prop, and score against real proportions. Bulk and single-cell data are matched count data with no reference sparsity concern — dropout simulation adds artificial bias rather than information Expression values are TPM/RPKM rather than counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input, and dropout models calibrated on counts would not apply The goal is absolute cell type proportions rather than robustness assessment — under the model assumptions only trends across subjects are recoverable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarking protocol that artificially zero-inflates a single-cell RNA-seq reference (via the Jia et al. dropout scheme) and tests whether MuSiC's cell type deconvolution stays accurate as dropout increases, reproducing the paper's Supplementary Note 5 result that MuSiC remains accurate at ~30% dropout. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-08023-x
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol that artificially zero-inflates a single-cell RNA-seq reference (via the Jia et al. dropout scheme) and tests whether MuSiC's cell type deconvolution stays accurate as dropout increases, reproducing the paper's Supplementary Note 5 result that MuSiC remains accurate at ~30% dropout.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Bulk and single-cell data are matched count data with no reference sparsity concern — dropout simulation adds artificial bias rather than information Expression values are TPM/RPKM rather than counts — cell type proportions cannot be estimated with TPM as the input, and dropout models calibrated on counts would not apply The goal is absolute cell type proportions rather than robustness assessment — under the model assumptions only trends across subjects are recoverable

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method against a known ground truth, or reproducing ablations (e.g., classifier-necessity test) that require paired dropout and dropout-free count matrices with known cell-group labels.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation Use when benchmarking a scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method against a known ground truth, or reproducing ablations (e.g., classifier-necessity test) that require paired dropout and dropout-free count matrices with known cell-group labels. The analysis goal is real biological data with unknown ground truth (e.g., the Baron dataset) where no simulated dropout-free reference exists The benchmark targets batch-effect or cell-cycle noise correction rather than dropout imputation, since Splatter dropouts simulate only one noise type http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Simulate scRNA-Seq data with controlled dropout using Splatter (e.g., Dataset 1: 1000 genes, 500 cells in six groups, paired dropout and true count matrices) to create a ground-truth benchmark for evaluating imputation and denoising methods such as AutoClass. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Simulate scRNA-Seq data with controlled dropout using Splatter (e.g., Dataset 1: 1000 genes, 500 cells in six groups, paired dropout and true count matrices) to create a ground-truth benchmark for evaluating imputation and denoising methods such as AutoClass.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is real biological data with unknown ground truth (e.g., the Baron dataset) where no simulated dropout-free reference exists The benchmark targets batch-effect or cell-cycle noise correction rather than dropout imputation, since Splatter dropouts simulate only one noise type

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object with log-cpm normalized counts and over-clustered (high-resolution) Leiden labels needs statistically grounded merging of non-significantly different cell populations.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-enrichment-scoring Use when an AnnData object with log-cpm normalized counts and over-clustered (high-resolution) Leiden labels needs statistically grounded merging of non-significantly different cell populations. Input AnnData has not been log-cpm normalized and clustered with Leiden labels — the code-score requires normalized expression and tentative cluster groupings Goal is standard additive enrichment scoring (e.g. per-gene-set sum/mean) rather than joint-probability-based co-expression code scoring across cluster marker sets Only a single, well-supported clustering exists with no over-clustering — Cytocipher is designed to merge non-significantly different clusters from high-resolution over-clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Cytocipher's code-scoring quantitatively scores gene set co-expression per cell as the log of the inverse joint probability of expressing each marker gene at >= the level observed in that cell, producing a cell-by-cluster enrichment score matrix used to test which Leiden clusters are significantly different. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad435
skills.summary: Cytocipher's code-scoring quantitatively scores gene set co-expression per cell as the log of the inverse joint probability of expressing each marker gene at >= the level observed in that cell, producing a cell-by-cluster enrichment score matrix used to test which Leiden clusters are significantly different.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input AnnData has not been log-cpm normalized and clustered with Leiden labels — the code-score requires normalized expression and tentative cluster groupings Goal is standard additive enrichment scoring (e.g. per-gene-set sum/mean) rather than joint-probability-based co-expression code scoring across cluster marker sets Only a single, well-supported clustering exists with no over-clustering — Cytocipher is designed to merge non-significantly different clusters from high-resolution over-clustering

skills.description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., the Mouse cortex MC/Zeisel et al. dataset) with phenotype labels and need a per-gene score to rank all features before selecting a discriminative marker set.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-ranking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-ranking Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., the Mouse cortex MC/Zeisel et al. dataset) with phenotype labels and need a per-gene score to rank all features before selecting a discriminative marker set. Goal is a minimal subset of features that collectively distinguishes every phenotype pair (phenotype cover problem) — use GreedyPC or CEMPC from phenotype-cover instead of a per-feature ranking Input is already a ranked or selected feature list, or a phenotype x feature score matrix M ready for cover optimization The target variable is numeric regression rather than categorical phenotype labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Ranks individual genes of a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix by their per-feature discriminative scores, here via ReliefF neighbor-based feature weighting with faiss approximate nearest neighbors. Provides a ranked feature list that serves as input to marker-set methods such as the phenotype cover (PC) formulation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100332
skills.summary: Ranks individual genes of a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix by their per-feature discriminative scores, here via ReliefF neighbor-based feature weighting with faiss approximate nearest neighbors. Provides a ranked feature list that serves as input to marker-set methods such as the phenotype cover (PC) formulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is a minimal subset of features that collectively distinguishes every phenotype pair (phenotype cover problem) — use GreedyPC or CEMPC from phenotype-cover instead of a per-feature ranking Input is already a ranked or selected feature list, or a phenotype x feature score matrix M ready for cover optimization The target variable is numeric regression rather than categorical phenotype labels

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X pbmc_1k_v2 counts) and you need an optimal, non-redundant feature gene set to improve cluster separation and DE-gene detection before PCA/clustering.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-selection
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-selection Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X pbmc_1k_v2 counts) and you need an optimal, non-redundant feature gene set to improve cluster separation and DE-gene detection before PCA/clustering. The input is already a curated feature/marker gene table rather than a raw or normalized single-cell count matrix The analysis goal is differential expression testing or cell type annotation of existing clusters, not feature selection for unsupervised clustering Genes have not been filtered for detectability (no min.cells cutoff applied), which would let poorly measured genes corrupt the GGC matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects informative genes for single-cell RNA-seq clustering using DUBStepR, a correlation-based feature selection method that ranks genes by gene-gene correlation (GGC) structure, derives a minimally redundant seed set via stepwise regression, and expands it to the Density Index-optimal feature set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Selects informative genes for single-cell RNA-seq clustering using DUBStepR, a correlation-based feature selection method that ranks genes by gene-gene correlation (GGC) structure, derives a minimally redundant seed set via stepwise regression, and expands it to the Density Index-optimal feature set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a curated feature/marker gene table rather than a raw or normalized single-cell count matrix The analysis goal is differential expression testing or cell type annotation of existing clusters, not feature selection for unsupervised clustering Genes have not been filtered for detectability (no min.cells cutoff applied), which would let poorly measured genes corrupt the GGC matrix

skills.description: Use when evaluating fusion gene detection performance on single-cell RNA-seq data with low sequencing depth, e.g. reproducing HVLD AUC values on K562 or multiple-myeloma scRNA-seq cohorts against competing models.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-benchmarking Use when evaluating fusion gene detection performance on single-cell RNA-seq data with low sequencing depth, e.g. reproducing HVLD AUC values on K562 or multiple-myeloma scRNA-seq cohorts against competing models. Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion only works on paired-end RNA-seq data The analysis targets fusion genes not including the user-provided anchored target gene — these will not be detected The input dataset is too small to retrain the filter — use the default model parameters provided on GitHub instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Retrains and benchmarks the HVLD deep learning filter of Anchored-fusion on scRNA-seq datasets (K562 SRA:SRP291312 and multiple myeloma SRA:SRP158590) to distinguish true from artificial fusion reads, comparing AUC against competing models such as scFusion. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100733
skills.summary: Retrains and benchmarks the HVLD deep learning filter of Anchored-fusion on scRNA-seq datasets (K562 SRA:SRP291312 and multiple myeloma SRA:SRP158590) to distinguish true from artificial fusion reads, comparing AUC against competing models such as scFusion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end RNA-seq, whole-genome, or whole-exome sequencing data — Anchored-fusion only works on paired-end RNA-seq data The analysis targets fusion genes not including the user-provided anchored target gene — these will not be detected The input dataset is too small to retrain the filter — use the default model parameters provided on GitHub instead

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing fusion detection methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when quantifying how deep-learning/statistical filtering affects scFusion's precision and F-score.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-simulation Use when evaluating or comparing fusion detection methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when quantifying how deep-learning/statistical filtering affects scFusion's precision and F-score. Input is real 10X Genomics scRNA-seq data — scFusion is built for Smart-Seq data rather than 10X FASTQ files are named *_1.fq, which the scFusion pipeline does not accept No simulation ground truth is available, so precision/recall/F-score against known fusions cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Benchmark single-cell gene fusion callers by simulating Smart-Seq paired-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with spiked artificial chimeric fusion reads, then score precision, recall, and F-score against the simulation ground truth to compare scFusion against bulk methods (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, EricScript). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell gene fusion callers by simulating Smart-Seq paired-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with spiked artificial chimeric fusion reads, then score precision, recall, and F-score against the simulation ground truth to compare scFusion against bulk methods (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, EricScript).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real 10X Genomics scRNA-seq data — scFusion is built for Smart-Seq data rather than 10X FASTQ files are named *_1.fq, which the scFusion pipeline does not accept No simulation ground truth is available, so precision/recall/F-score against known fusions cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices (e.g., simulated Splatter data, Villani PBMC, Baron pancreatic islet) suffer from dropouts, noise, or batch effects and you need distribution-agnostic imputation/denoising with downstream clustering or batch-merging evaluation.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-imputation-with-autoclass
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-imputation-with-autoclass Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices (e.g., simulated Splatter data, Villani PBMC, Baron pancreatic islet) suffer from dropouts, noise, or batch effects and you need distribution-agnostic imputation/denoising with downstream clustering or batch-merging evaluation. Data analysis targets a specific parametric denoising model you know fits the data and distribution assumptions are acceptable (existing methods like DCA's ZINB or SAVER's negative binomial exist, but AutoClass's advantage is being distribution-agnostic — the paper does not claim superiority when exact distribution assumptions hold). The input is not a scRNA-Seq count matrix (e.g., bulk RNA-Seq, protein abundance) — the method was developed and benchmarked only on scRNA-Seq data. Only the abstract-level claim about robustness to hyperparameters matters and you cannot run TensorFlow >=2.0 — AutoClass will not execute without the stated dependency stack. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A skill for cleaning single-cell RNA-Seq data using AutoClass, a composite deep neural network that integrates an autoencoder and a classifier to remove dropouts, profiling noise, and batch effects without distribution assumptions. It outperforms state-of-the-art imputation methods such as DCA, SAVER, scImpute, and MAGIC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: A skill for cleaning single-cell RNA-Seq data using AutoClass, a composite deep neural network that integrates an autoencoder and a classifier to remove dropouts, profiling noise, and batch effects without distribution assumptions. It outperforms state-of-the-art imputation methods such as DCA, SAVER, scImpute, and MAGIC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data analysis targets a specific parametric denoising model you know fits the data and distribution assumptions are acceptable (existing methods like DCA's ZINB or SAVER's negative binomial exist, but AutoClass's advantage is being distribution-agnostic — the paper does not claim superiority when exact distribution assumptions hold). The input is not a scRNA-Seq count matrix (e.g., bulk RNA-Seq, protein abundance) — the method was developed and benchmarked only on scRNA-Seq data. Only the abstract-level claim about robustness to hyperparameters matters and you cannot run TensorFlow >=2.0 — AutoClass will not execute without the stated dependency stack.

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq, thousands of cells) contains extreme-depth cells or very sparse genes that would distort downstream imputation or Gini-distribution comparisons.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-library-size-filtering
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-library-size-filtering Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq, thousands of cells) contains extreme-depth cells or very sparse genes that would distort downstream imputation or Gini-distribution comparisons. The input is already normalized and QC-filtered (e.g. a Seurat object post-QC) — re-filtering by the same cutoffs would double-correct library sizes The dataset is not droplet-based scRNA-seq; bulk RNA-seq has far fewer zeros and does not need this depth-based cell filtering Cell-type identification or clustering is the goal and deliberately retaining very small or large library-size cells is part of the analysis plan http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality-control procedure for droplet-based scRNA-seq matrices that removes poor-quality cells by library-size cutoffs (keep cells with total counts between 500 and 20,000) and low-abundance genes (mean expression >= 0.1), plus GAPDH-percentile outlier removal, before imputation or normalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Quality-control procedure for droplet-based scRNA-seq matrices that removes poor-quality cells by library-size cutoffs (keep cells with total counts between 500 and 20,000) and low-abundance genes (mean expression >= 0.1), plus GAPDH-percentile outlier removal, before imputation or normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already normalized and QC-filtered (e.g. a Seurat object post-QC) — re-filtering by the same cutoffs would double-correct library sizes The dataset is not droplet-based scRNA-seq; bulk RNA-seq has far fewer zeros and does not need this depth-based cell filtering Cell-type identification or clustering is the goal and deliberately retaining very small or large library-size cells is part of the analysis plan

skills.description: Use when raw or low-level-normalized scRNA-seq count/TPM matrices feed an ensemble clustering or feature-selection pipeline and need normalization plus removal of low-level expressed genes.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-log2-preprocessing-and-gene-filtering
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-log2-preprocessing-and-gene-filtering Use when raw or low-level-normalized scRNA-seq count/TPM matrices feed an ensemble clustering or feature-selection pipeline and need normalization plus removal of low-level expressed genes. Data are single-cell ATAC-seq, proteomics, or bulk RNA-seq — the <2% cell-detection threshold is calibrated for scRNA-seq gene dropout structure The matrix is already log2-normalized with low-detection genes removed; re-applying the transformation and filter would double-normalize and discard no additional genes A supervised feature selection or differential-expression-driven gene filter is required — this is an unsupervised pre-filter http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pre-processing step from scEFSC that log2-normalizes an n × d scRNA-seq expression matrix (rescaling with log2 only when expression values exceed 100) and removes genes detected in fewer than 2% of cells, yielding a denoised matrix ready for downstream feature selection and clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.04.023
skills.summary: Pre-processing step from scEFSC that log2-normalizes an n × d scRNA-seq expression matrix (rescaling with log2 only when expression values exceed 100) and removes genes detected in fewer than 2% of cells, yielding a denoised matrix ready for downstream feature selection and clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-cell ATAC-seq, proteomics, or bulk RNA-seq — the <2% cell-detection threshold is calibrated for scRNA-seq gene dropout structure The matrix is already log2-normalized with low-detection genes removed; re-applying the transformation and filter would double-normalize and discard no additional genes A supervised feature selection or differential-expression-driven gene filter is required — this is an unsupervised pre-filter

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell direct gene-gene association networks, or when cell-specific hub genes/module structure (e.g., Gokce neural-differentiation hubs) need to be identified.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-network-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-network-analysis Use when a scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell direct gene-gene association networks, or when cell-specific hub genes/module structure (e.g., Gokce neural-differentiation hubs) need to be identified. The goal is a causal gene association network or directed edges — c-CSN is explicitly not designed to construct causal networks and cannot obtain directions of gene associations Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated expression with no single-cell resolution — c-CSN constructs one network per cell and requires per-cell data Only indirect-correction-free co-expression is needed at population level rather than cell-specific direct associations (ordinary CSN may suffice, though it overestimates associations) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) from scRNA-seq gene expression matrices using c-CSN, which tests direct gene-gene associations per cell by eliminating indirect associations, then supports downstream analyses such as hub-gene identification of differentiation modules (e.g., ONECUT1, ASCL1, NAR6A1 in the Gokce dataset). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Constructs a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) from scRNA-seq gene expression matrices using c-CSN, which tests direct gene-gene associations per cell by eliminating indirect associations, then supports downstream analyses such as hub-gene identification of differentiation modules (e.g., ONECUT1, ASCL1, NAR6A1 in the Gokce dataset).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a causal gene association network or directed edges — c-CSN is explicitly not designed to construct causal networks and cannot obtain directions of gene associations Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated expression with no single-cell resolution — c-CSN constructs one network per cell and requires per-cell data Only indirect-correction-free co-expression is needed at population level rather than cell-specific direct associations (ordinary CSN may suffice, though it overestimates associations)

skills.description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix must be converted to a comparable expression scale before gene selection or cell type classification, and the protocol (full-length vs UMI) dictates TPM+log1p or size-factor-10,000 normalization.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-normalization
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-normalization Use when an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix must be converted to a comparable expression scale before gene selection or cell type classification, and the protocol (full-length vs UMI) dictates TPM+log1p or size-factor-10,000 normalization. Input is already log-normalized or provided as a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM-log values) — re-normalizing would distort likelihood-based classification Bulk RNA-seq or other non-single-cell count data where per-cell size-factor normalization semantics do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Technology-dependent preprocessing of scRNA-seq matrices as defined in the SciBet paper: full-length read data are TPM-normalized, pseudo-value one added, and log-transformed, while UMI data use Seurat v3-style size-factor 10,000, add-one, log normalization before any feature selection or classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Technology-dependent preprocessing of scRNA-seq matrices as defined in the SciBet paper: full-length read data are TPM-normalized, pseudo-value one added, and log-transformed, while UMI data use Seurat v3-style size-factor 10,000, add-one, log normalization before any feature selection or classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already log-normalized or provided as a normalized expression matrix (e.g. TPM-log values) — re-normalizing would distort likelihood-based classification Bulk RNA-seq or other non-single-cell count data where per-cell size-factor normalization semantics do not apply

skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-normalization-handling Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices must be converted to a comparable feature space (sf-log1p) before training or evaluating cell type classifiers such as scTab, TabNet, XGBoost, MLP, or linear baselines. skills.summary: Size-factor normalize each single-cell RNA-seq cell to 10,000 counts followed by log1p transformation, as used to preprocess the 22,189,056-cell CELLxGENE corpus before training and benchmarking scTab and all reference classifiers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already preprocessed sf-log1p data, such as the released merlin_cxg_2023_05_15_sf-log1p store — re-normalizing would double-transform the values Analysis requires raw counts or alternative normalization (e.g. scran, SCTransform) or integration of non-transcriptomic modalities, which scTab does not yet cover Working with assays outside the corpus' sequencing protocols or gene spaces other than the 19,331 protein-coding gene subset

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether gene set enrichment methods (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) produce well-calibrated null p-values on zero-inflated scRNA-seq-like data, or when studying how gene set size / coverage rate affects calibration.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-null-gene-set-simulation
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-null-gene-set-simulation Use when benchmarking whether gene set enrichment methods (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) produce well-calibrated null p-values on zero-inflated scRNA-seq-like data, or when studying how gene set size / coverage rate affects calibration. The goal is to detect real enrichment or DE signal — this skill simulates explicit null data with no embedded signal and cannot measure power or ranking of true positives. Data are bulk RNA-seq without zero inflation — the zero-inflated negative-binomial simulation framework is designed for scRNA-seq dropout characteristics. Assessment of sensitivity to gene set overlap/non-independence among tested gene sets is the target; this null simulation varies coverage rate for synthetic sets instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulate zero-inflated negative-binomial scRNA-seq count matrices under an explicit null (no DE signal, null tau0=-2, tau1=0), construct synthetic gene sets at controlled coverage rates, and use the resulting null gene-set p-values to assess p-value calibration (via lambda_gc and QQ plots) of competitive gene set enrichment methods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15298-6
skills.summary: Simulate zero-inflated negative-binomial scRNA-seq count matrices under an explicit null (no DE signal, null tau0=-2, tau1=0), construct synthetic gene sets at controlled coverage rates, and use the resulting null gene-set p-values to assess p-value calibration (via lambda_gc and QQ plots) of competitive gene set enrichment methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to detect real enrichment or DE signal — this skill simulates explicit null data with no embedded signal and cannot measure power or ranking of true positives. Data are bulk RNA-seq without zero inflation — the zero-inflated negative-binomial simulation framework is designed for scRNA-seq dropout characteristics. Assessment of sensitivity to gene set overlap/non-independence among tested gene sets is the target; this null simulation varies coverage rate for synthetic sets instead.

skills.description: Use when a normalized and scaled gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. PBMC3k with VST-derived variable features) needs PCA followed by t-SNE/UMAP 2D embeddings in a Seurat/SCALA workflow.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-pca-dimensionality-reduction
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-pca-dimensionality-reduction Use when a normalized and scaled gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. PBMC3k with VST-derived variable features) needs PCA followed by t-SNE/UMAP 2D embeddings in a Seurat/SCALA workflow. Input is raw count data that has not been normalized and scaled — run upstream normalization/scaling and variable-feature detection first The modality is scATAC-seq — SCALA uses LSI dimensionality reduction for that modality, not PCA on gene expression Datasets larger than 50,000 cells in the SCALA online (web-server) version, where some steps cannot be completed; prefer the desktop version http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reconstructs SCALA's scRNA-seq dimensionality-reduction layer: PCA on the scaled variable-feature matrix (Seurat, PBMC3k), selection of informative PCs via SVD cross-validation, and t-SNE/UMAP embeddings of the top PCs for 2D visualization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Reconstructs SCALA's scRNA-seq dimensionality-reduction layer: PCA on the scaled variable-feature matrix (Seurat, PBMC3k), selection of informative PCs via SVD cross-validation, and t-SNE/UMAP embeddings of the top PCs for 2D visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count data that has not been normalized and scaled — run upstream normalization/scaling and variable-feature detection first The modality is scATAC-seq — SCALA uses LSI dimensionality reduction for that modality, not PCA on gene expression Datasets larger than 50,000 cells in the SCALA online (web-server) version, where some steps cannot be completed; prefer the desktop version

skills.description: Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq datasets against original count matrices to quantify per-gene distribution fidelity and to expose failures such as unreproduced bimodal gene distributions.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-per-gene-descriptive-statistics
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-per-gene-descriptive-statistics Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq datasets against original count matrices to quantify per-gene distribution fidelity and to expose failures such as unreproduced bimodal gene distributions. When the goal is clustering-quality assessment (ARI, Davies–Bouldin index, cluster proportions) rather than per-gene distribution fidelity — use the corresponding clustering evaluation skill instead. When the input data are already aggregated summary statistics rather than per-cell count matrices, since medians, IQRs, CVs, and zero-count proportions must be recomputed per gene. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Evaluates how faithfully synthetic scRNA-seq data reproduces per-gene univariate expression distributions by comparing medians, interquantile ranges, coefficients of variation, and proportion of zero counts between original and synthetic count matrices, and visualizing failures such as bimodal genes (e.g., CD74 in PBMC4k). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-88875-4
skills.summary: Evaluates how faithfully synthetic scRNA-seq data reproduces per-gene univariate expression distributions by comparing medians, interquantile ranges, coefficients of variation, and proportion of zero counts between original and synthetic count matrices, and visualizing failures such as bimodal genes (e.g., CD74 in PBMC4k).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is clustering-quality assessment (ARI, Davies–Bouldin index, cluster proportions) rather than per-gene distribution fidelity — use the corresponding clustering evaluation skill instead. When the input data are already aggregated summary statistics rather than per-cell count matrices, since medians, IQRs, CVs, and zero-count proportions must be recomputed per gene.

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell posterior samples of a circular (24 h) quantity such as circadian phase from a Bayesian single-cell method and need to verify that credible-interval uncertainty quantifications are well-calibrated against known true phases or sample-collection times.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-posterior-coverage-assessment
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-posterior-coverage-assessment Use when you have per-cell posterior samples of a circular (24 h) quantity such as circadian phase from a Bayesian single-cell method and need to verify that credible-interval uncertainty quantifications are well-calibrated against known true phases or sample-collection times. The method under evaluation provides only point estimates of phase and no posterior samples or uncertainty quantifications — existing unsupervised phase inference methods 'do not quantify estimation uncertainty', leaving nothing to calibrate. The quantity of interest is not circular/periodic (e.g., linear measurements); the HDR interval construction here assumes a 24 h circular phase where intervals wrap around midnight. No ground-truth phases are available (e.g., unsynchronized samples with no collection-time reference), so empirical coverage cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A calibration-assessment skill that converts approximate posterior phase samples from a Bayesian single-cell method (e.g., Tempo) into Highest-Density-Region credible intervals and checks whether their empirical coverage matches nominal confidence levels for a circadian 24 h phase quantity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34185-w
skills.summary: A calibration-assessment skill that converts approximate posterior phase samples from a Bayesian single-cell method (e.g., Tempo) into Highest-Density-Region credible intervals and checks whether their empirical coverage matches nominal confidence levels for a circadian 24 h phase quantity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The method under evaluation provides only point estimates of phase and no posterior samples or uncertainty quantifications — existing unsupervised phase inference methods 'do not quantify estimation uncertainty', leaving nothing to calibrate. The quantity of interest is not circular/periodic (e.g., linear measurements); the HDR interval construction here assumes a 24 h circular phase where intervals wrap around midnight. No ground-truth phases are available (e.g., unsynchronized samples with no collection-time reference), so empirical coverage cannot be computed.

skills.summary: Prepare droplet-based single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Chromium mouse aorta light-dark and Droin et al. hepatocyte time-course datasets) as anndata objects inside the Tempo conda environment so that circadian phase-inference methods can be benchmarked against known sampling-time references.
