skills.description: Use when raw 10x scRNA-seq FASTQ files (with optional CITE-seq ADT and hashing data) must be converted to a filtered, clustered, cell-type-annotated expression matrix via a reproducible end-to-end workflow.
skills.name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing Use when raw 10x scRNA-seq FASTQ files (with optional CITE-seq ADT and hashing data) must be converted to a filtered, clustered, cell-type-annotated expression matrix via a reproducible end-to-end workflow. The goal is antibody/ADT (CITE-seq) or hashing deconvolution analysis only — use the dedicated gExcite ADT and hashing modules instead of the GEX preprocessing layer. Data is already a filtered, processed count matrix from cellranger/STARsolo with QC done — start the pipeline after the resource-intensive cellranger steps rather than re-running from raw reads. Analysis must run on macOS or other non-Linux Unix systems — gExcite is compatible with and tested on Linux only. STARsolo is required instead of cellranger — that route is a scAmpi snakefile variant (snakefile_basic_starsolo.smk), not the default gExcite workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reproducible Snakemake-embedded preprocessing of single-cell gene expression data as implemented in gExcite/scAmpi: cellranger count from raw FASTQ, QC with empty-droplet and ambient-RNA filtering, normalisation, clustering and cell type classification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad329
skills.summary: Reproducible Snakemake-embedded preprocessing of single-cell gene expression data as implemented in gExcite/scAmpi: cellranger count from raw FASTQ, QC with empty-droplet and ambient-RNA filtering, normalisation, clustering and cell type classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is antibody/ADT (CITE-seq) or hashing deconvolution analysis only — use the dedicated gExcite ADT and hashing modules instead of the GEX preprocessing layer. Data is already a filtered, processed count matrix from cellranger/STARsolo with QC done — start the pipeline after the resource-intensive cellranger steps rather than re-running from raw reads. Analysis must run on macOS or other non-Linux Unix systems — gExcite is compatible with and tested on Linux only. STARsolo is required instead of cellranger — that route is a scAmpi snakefile variant (snakefile_basic_starsolo.smk), not the default gExcite workflow.

skills.summary: Standard Seurat-based preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and cell-type annotation of scRNA-seq data from human liver transplantation samples, used to identify EAD-associated immune populations (MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils) and prepare inputs for scCrossTalk cell-cell communication inference.

skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing-normalization Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq counts must be prepared as a log-normalized (genes x cells) matrix for full-dimensionality kernel methods (e.g. q-diffusion) that require no feature selection or dimensionality reduction. When the analysis pipeline requires feature selection, dimensionality reduction, or marker-gene identification — q-diffusion depends on the full gene library and those steps discard the interactions it captures When input is already a log-normalized expression matrix (e.g. an atlas reference's supplied dimensionality reduction such as scVI) — re-normalizing or re-reducing it is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Log-normalize a raw (genes x cells) scRNAseq count matrix — without feature selection or dimensionality reduction — to prepare full-dimensionality inputs for q-diffused kernel construction, using QDiffusion.jl's `preprocess_cell_counts`. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Log-normalize a raw (genes x cells) scRNAseq count matrix — without feature selection or dimensionality reduction — to prepare full-dimensionality inputs for q-diffused kernel construction, using QDiffusion.jl's `preprocess_cell_counts`.

The goal is inferring ligand-receptor cell-cell communication (e.g. enriching CellTalkDB LR pairs with scCrossTalk's Z-test) rather than scoring per-sample cell composition Single-cell data lack cell type annotations, so the three niche populations (MAIT, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK, S100A12+ neutrophils) cannot be identified Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated data where per-cell population percentages cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate each liver transplant scRNA-seq sample with derived metadata — percentages of MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, and S100A12+ neutrophils, their sum as an EAD-associated immune niche score, plus donor, stage (cold preservation vs 2-hour portal reperfusion), and EAD status — producing a 12-row per-sample table for group comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.eng.2023.12.004
skills.summary: Annotate each liver transplant scRNA-seq sample with derived metadata — percentages of MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, and S100A12+ neutrophils, their sum as an EAD-associated immune niche score, plus donor, stage (cold preservation vs 2-hour portal reperfusion), and EAD status — producing a 12-row per-sample table for group comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is inferring ligand-receptor cell-cell communication (e.g. enriching CellTalkDB LR pairs with scCrossTalk's Z-test) rather than scoring per-sample cell composition Single-cell data lack cell type annotations, so the three niche populations (MAIT, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK, S100A12+ neutrophils) cannot be identified Input is bulk RNA-seq or aggregated data where per-cell population percentages cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when constructing simulated single-cell scWGS benchmark data that must preserve allele-specific haplotype structure, controlled phase-switch error rates, and real WGA artifacts — e.g., before evaluating BAF/phasing-based CNA callers on ground-truth events spanning 200 kb to 5 Mb.
skills.name: single-cell-scngs-read-extraction
skills.search_text: single-cell-scngs-read-extraction Use when constructing simulated single-cell scWGS benchmark data that must preserve allele-specific haplotype structure, controlled phase-switch error rates, and real WGA artifacts — e.g., before evaluating BAF/phasing-based CNA callers on ground-truth events spanning 200 kb to 5 Mb. The goal is calling allele-specific CNAs on real single-cell data rather than generating simulated ground truth — use HiScanner directly instead Input BAMs are from a female donor or from autosomes without haploid allele separation, since the SDX trick relies on pooling two male haploid X chromosomes The caller under test operates on pre-binned read-depth tracks only, since read-level pooling cannot affect its allele-specific behavior http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A read-level simulation technique (SDX) that extracts chromosome X reads from single-cell scWGS BAM files of two male haploid donors using samtools, then pools, excises, or duplicates reads to embed allele-specific CNAs while preserving haplotype structure and scWGS amplification artifacts for benchmarking callers like HiScanner. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: A read-level simulation technique (SDX) that extracts chromosome X reads from single-cell scWGS BAM files of two male haploid donors using samtools, then pools, excises, or duplicates reads to embed allele-specific CNAs while preserving haplotype structure and scWGS amplification artifacts for benchmarking callers like HiScanner.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling allele-specific CNAs on real single-cell data rather than generating simulated ground truth — use HiScanner directly instead Input BAMs are from a female donor or from autosomes without haploid allele separation, since the SDX trick relies on pooling two male haploid X chromosomes The caller under test operates on pre-binned read-depth tracks only, since read-level pooling cannot affect its allele-specific behavior

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-state decomposition or clustering method recovers known planted identity and activity patterns from synthetic scRNA-seq data with planted ground truth.
skills.name: single-cell-scrnaseq-synthetic-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-scrnaseq-synthetic-benchmarking Use when evaluating whether a cell-state decomposition or clustering method recovers known planted identity and activity patterns from synthetic scRNA-seq data with planted ground truth. Input is real scRNA-seq data with no planted ground-truth patterns — purity against planted patterns cannot be computed The goal is a single-analysis cell annotation or integration run rather than method benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark pattern-recovery fidelity of single-cell decomposition methods on synthetic scRNA-seq data by matching recovered identity and activity patterns to planted generative patterns, as done for ACTIONet against cNMF, cLDA, cICA, and Louvain baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18416-6
skills.summary: Benchmark pattern-recovery fidelity of single-cell decomposition methods on synthetic scRNA-seq data by matching recovered identity and activity patterns to planted generative patterns, as done for ACTIONet against cNMF, cLDA, cICA, and Louvain baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-seq data with no planted ground-truth patterns — purity against planted patterns cannot be computed The goal is a single-analysis cell annotation or integration run rather than method benchmarking

skills.description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes (AnnData, normalized but unscaled) for cellular senescence with cell-type-specific signatures, e.g., quantifying senescent-cell burden across ages or disease conditions.
skills.name: single-cell-senescence-signature-scoring
skills.search_text: single-cell-senescence-signature-scoring Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes (AnnData, normalized but unscaled) for cellular senescence with cell-type-specific signatures, e.g., quantifying senescent-cell burden across ages or disease conditions. Data are scaled (e.g., scanpy sc.pp.scale applied) — score_hub requires unscaled values since it binarizes by default The goal is a plain scanpy-style gene-set score without background correction — then use score_hub(binarize=False, importance=False) after normalize_total/log1p, or scanpy.score_genes directly; the SenePy defaults would change the meaning of the score Studying senescence in bulk transcriptomes or spatial data without single-cell AnnData input — SenePy scoring requires a single-cell expression object http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scores individual cells for senescence using SenePy's cell-type-specific hub signatures: load hubs with load_hubs, extract genes via get_genes, then run score_hub with binarization and hub-network importance weighting to produce per-cell senescence scores and identify senescent outlier cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Scores individual cells for senescence using SenePy's cell-type-specific hub signatures: load hubs with load_hubs, extract genes via get_genes, then run score_hub with binarization and hub-network importance weighting to produce per-cell senescence scores and identify senescent outlier cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are scaled (e.g., scanpy sc.pp.scale applied) — score_hub requires unscaled values since it binarizes by default The goal is a plain scanpy-style gene-set score without background correction — then use score_hub(binarize=False, importance=False) after normalize_total/log1p, or scanpy.score_genes directly; the SenePy defaults would change the meaning of the score Studying senescence in bulk transcriptomes or spatial data without single-cell AnnData input — SenePy scoring requires a single-cell expression object

skills.description: Use when starting from raw or unprocessed scRNA-seq data — Seurat objects, .rds count matrices, or paired count/metadata files — that must be loaded, normalized, and clustered before cell-type annotation with the scMiko/Miko scoring pipeline.
skills.name: single-cell-seurat-object-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-seurat-object-processing Use when starting from raw or unprocessed scRNA-seq data — Seurat objects, .rds count matrices, or paired count/metadata files — that must be loaded, normalized, and clustered before cell-type annotation with the scMiko/Miko scoring pipeline. Input is already a processed, scored Seurat object that only needs annotation steps (e.g., sigScore/post-hoc coherence filtering) — skip to the scoring modules instead Data lives in a non-R/Scanpy-native format (e.g., .h5ad) that cannot be directly read with readRDS() without conversion to Seurat structure The analysis goal is gene program discovery on an already-annotated atlas where re-clustering would destroy the author-curated labels used for benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Load and preprocess single-cell RNA-seq data as Seurat objects (e.g., .rds files like so_tyser2021_220621.rds or paired count/matrix files like ps_count_matrix.rds + ps_meta_data.rds) using scMiko and the modular scPipeline Rmarkdown workflows, so downstream steps (clustering, Miko scoring, SSN analysis) operate on a consistent Seurat scaffold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-04093-2
skills.summary: Load and preprocess single-cell RNA-seq data as Seurat objects (e.g., .rds files like so_tyser2021_220621.rds or paired count/matrix files like ps_count_matrix.rds + ps_meta_data.rds) using scMiko and the modular scPipeline Rmarkdown workflows, so downstream steps (clustering, Miko scoring, SSN analysis) operate on a consistent Seurat scaffold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed, scored Seurat object that only needs annotation steps (e.g., sigScore/post-hoc coherence filtering) — skip to the scoring modules instead Data lives in a non-R/Scanpy-native format (e.g., .h5ad) that cannot be directly read with readRDS() without conversion to Seurat structure The analysis goal is gene program discovery on an already-annotated atlas where re-clustering would destroy the author-curated labels used for benchmarking

skills.description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices need potency ordering of single cells (e.g. pluripotent vs multipotent vs differentiated, developmental stage ordering, cancer-vs-microenvironment contrast) without prior marker or timepoint knowledge.
skills.name: single-cell-signalling-entropy-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-signalling-entropy-estimation Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices need potency ordering of single cells (e.g. pluripotent vs multipotent vs differentiated, developmental stage ordering, cancer-vs-microenvironment contrast) without prior marker or timepoint knowledge. When the goal is pseudo-temporal trajectory inference from well-established differentiation hierarchies where algorithms such as Monocle or MPath are the intended choice When only transcriptomic entropies without network information (as used in StemID or SLICE) are required, since SCENT specifically relies on the interaction network context When prior marker expression or timepoint information is already available and sufficient, as SCENT is designed for settings lacking such biological knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Estimate the differentiation potency of individual single-cell RNA-Seq profiles by computing signalling entropy (SR) — the signalling promiscuity of a cell's transcriptome in the context of a protein interaction network — using the SCENT algorithm, without feature selection or training. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms15599
skills.summary: Estimate the differentiation potency of individual single-cell RNA-Seq profiles by computing signalling entropy (SR) — the signalling promiscuity of a cell's transcriptome in the context of a protein interaction network — using the SCENT algorithm, without feature selection or training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is pseudo-temporal trajectory inference from well-established differentiation hierarchies where algorithms such as Monocle or MPath are the intended choice When only transcriptomic entropies without network information (as used in StemID or SLICE) are required, since SCENT specifically relies on the interaction network context When prior marker expression or timepoint information is already available and sufficient, as SCENT is designed for settings lacking such biological knowledge

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (AnnData object) must be scored or annotated for cellular senescence per cell type, or when literature-curated in vivo senescence gene signatures (e.g. Lung-fibroblast hubs) need to be extracted, searched, or merged.
skills.name: single-cell-signature-annotation
skills.search_text: single-cell-signature-annotation Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (AnnData object) must be scored or annotated for cellular senescence per cell type, or when literature-curated in vivo senescence gene signatures (e.g. Lung-fibroblast hubs) need to be extracted, searched, or merged. The data are already scaled — score_hub's default binarization and importance weighting assume raw or normalized (not scaled) expression; mimic scanpy.score_genes instead by setting binarize=False, importance=False after normalize_total and log1p. The goal is de novo discovery of senescence signatures from raw single-cell data rather than applying the published signatures — that requires the upstream GAD-scoring and co-positivity network workflow, not SenePy scoring. The input is bulk transcriptomic or non-single-cell data, since the signatures and scoring were developed and validated on single-cell transcriptomes. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Annotate single-cell transcriptomic data with cell-type-specific senescence signatures using the SenePy database (75 mouse and 65 human signatures from 97 unique cell types), scoring cells via weighted hub gene signatures stored in AnnData/scanpy-compatible objects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-57047-7
skills.summary: Annotate single-cell transcriptomic data with cell-type-specific senescence signatures using the SenePy database (75 mouse and 65 human signatures from 97 unique cell types), scoring cells via weighted hub gene signatures stored in AnnData/scanpy-compatible objects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already scaled — score_hub's default binarization and importance weighting assume raw or normalized (not scaled) expression; mimic scanpy.score_genes instead by setting binarize=False, importance=False after normalize_total and log1p. The goal is de novo discovery of senescence signatures from raw single-cell data rather than applying the published signatures — that requires the upstream GAD-scoring and co-positivity network workflow, not SenePy scoring. The input is bulk transcriptomic or non-single-cell data, since the signatures and scoring were developed and validated on single-cell transcriptomes.

skills.description: Use when a raw gene/protein expression CSV matrix (e.g. prot_expression.csv) plus class labels (target.csv) must be transformed before building the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed similarity graph.
skills.name: single-cell-similarity-matrix-transformation
skills.search_text: single-cell-similarity-matrix-transformation Use when a raw gene/protein expression CSV matrix (e.g. prot_expression.csv) plus class labels (target.csv) must be transformed before building the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed similarity graph. The input is already a normalized or correlation-transformed matrix (e.g. a precomputed similarity matrix), since re-applying --normalization or --correlation_transformation would distort the intended scale. The analysis goal is pseudotime reconstruction with tree-based methods (e.g. TSCAN's cluster-based MST) rather than building the GraphDDP knn/k-shift edge graph, where these matrix filters are not defined. A class has fewer than --min_threshold (default 5) instances, which the filter step is designed to exclude rather than transform. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Preprocesses the raw single-cell expression CSV matrix with GraphEmbed's --normalization (convert data matrix to normalized matrix) and --correlation_transformation (convert data matrix to correlation coefficient matrix) toggles so that subsequent cosine-similarity density estimates and knn/k-shift edge construction operate on comparable, scale-free profiles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05988-7
skills.summary: Preprocesses the raw single-cell expression CSV matrix with GraphEmbed's --normalization (convert data matrix to normalized matrix) and --correlation_transformation (convert data matrix to correlation coefficient matrix) toggles so that subsequent cosine-similarity density estimates and knn/k-shift edge construction operate on comparable, scale-free profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized or correlation-transformed matrix (e.g. a precomputed similarity matrix), since re-applying --normalization or --correlation_transformation would distort the intended scale. The analysis goal is pseudotime reconstruction with tree-based methods (e.g. TSCAN's cluster-based MST) rather than building the GraphDDP knn/k-shift edge graph, where these matrix filters are not defined. A class has fewer than --min_threshold (default 5) instances, which the filter step is designed to exclude rather than transform.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) methods requires simulated multi-sample scRNA-seq data that faithfully mimic a reference dataset's characteristics (mean-dropout, mean-variance, sample-to-sample variability).
skills.name: single-cell-simulation-anchored-to-reference-dataset
skills.search_text: single-cell-simulation-anchored-to-reference-dataset Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) methods requires simulated multi-sample scRNA-seq data that faithfully mimic a reference dataset's characteristics (mean-dropout, mean-variance, sample-to-sample variability). The analysis target is differential state inference on real experimental data rather than method benchmarking via simulation. The simulation must accommodate an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the authors note the framework does not yet support these extensions. Reference data are bulk RNA-seq or lack per-cell sample/group/cluster metadata required to anchor simData. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generates faithful multi-sample multi-group scRNA-seq simulations using muscat's simData, anchored to a reference SingleCellExperiment (e.g., Kang PBMC control samples via ExperimentHub EH2259), and verifies fidelity with countsimQC by comparing mean-dropout and mean-variance relationships plus pseudobulk dispersion-mean trends. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19894-4
skills.summary: Generates faithful multi-sample multi-group scRNA-seq simulations using muscat's simData, anchored to a reference SingleCellExperiment (e.g., Kang PBMC control samples via ExperimentHub EH2259), and verifies fidelity with countsimQC by comparing mean-dropout and mean-variance relationships plus pseudobulk dispersion-mean trends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is differential state inference on real experimental data rather than method benchmarking via simulation. The simulation must accommodate an arbitrary number of groups or hierarchical-type genes — the authors note the framework does not yet support these extensions. Reference data are bulk RNA-seq or lack per-cell sample/group/cluster metadata required to anchor simData.

skills.description: Use when comparing annotation accuracy of marker-database-based cell-type annotation methods on data with known ground-truth labels (e.g. a simulated PBMC dataset), or when deciding which marker database (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) to trust for easyct-based annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-simulation-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-simulation-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing annotation accuracy of marker-database-based cell-type annotation methods on data with known ground-truth labels (e.g. a simulated PBMC dataset), or when deciding which marker database (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) to trust for easyct-based annotation. Input is real scRNA-seq data without known ground-truth cluster labels — accuracy cannot be scored against simulated cell-type labels The goal is annotating a new dataset rather than benchmarking — directly run easyct on the marker list instead of running the full six-run database comparison Simple list-overlap annotation is sufficient — note the article's warning that 'simply overlapping the two lists without considering gene ranking might lead to unreliable results', so ranked-input methods are preferred over naive overlap benchmarks http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark cell-type annotation accuracy by running EasyCellType's easyct GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test against multiple marker databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) on a simulated 2400-cell PBMC dataset with known cluster-level ground-truth labels, then scoring per-database accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad029
skills.summary: Benchmark cell-type annotation accuracy by running EasyCellType's easyct GSEA and modified Fisher's exact test against multiple marker databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) on a simulated 2400-cell PBMC dataset with known cluster-level ground-truth labels, then scoring per-database accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is real scRNA-seq data without known ground-truth cluster labels — accuracy cannot be scored against simulated cell-type labels The goal is annotating a new dataset rather than benchmarking — directly run easyct on the marker list instead of running the full six-run database comparison Simple list-overlap annotation is sufficient — note the article's warning that 'simply overlapping the two lists without considering gene ranking might lead to unreliable results', so ranked-input methods are preferred over naive overlap benchmarks

skills.description: Use when a computational method for trajectory inference, trajectory alignment, RNA velocity, or cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) must be evaluated quantitatively against fully known ground truth.
skills.name: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking Use when a computational method for trajectory inference, trajectory alignment, RNA velocity, or cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) must be evaluated quantitatively against fully known ground truth. You need to evaluate methods on real biological data without ground truth — dyngen's value is completely known synthetic ground truth, not realism You need to simulate only the technical protocol (e.g. benchmarking clustering or differential expression) with existing simulators like Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim You require ODE-based bulk dynamics — dyngen targets low-molecule single-cell regimes where ODE simulators are ill-suited Benchmark single-cell computational methods using dyngen, a multi-modal simulation engine that provides completely known ground truth (cell state, reaction propensities, and cellwise regulatory networks) so methods can be evaluated quantitatively on 42 synthetic datasets built from 14 predefined backbones across three seeds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Benchmark single-cell computational methods using dyngen, a multi-modal simulation engine that provides completely known ground truth (cell state, reaction propensities, and cellwise regulatory networks) so methods can be evaluated quantitatively on 42 synthetic datasets built from 14 predefined backbones across three seeds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to evaluate methods on real biological data without ground truth — dyngen's value is completely known synthetic ground truth, not realism You need to simulate only the technical protocol (e.g. benchmarking clustering or differential expression) with existing simulators like Splatter, powsimR, PROSSTT, or SymSim You require ODE-based bulk dynamics — dyngen targets low-molecule single-cell regimes where ODE simulators are ill-suited

skills.description: Use when comparing interaction-detection performance of a new trajectory method against DE-based alternatives on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth interaction labels, as in Fig 1f.
skills.name: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking Use when comparing interaction-detection performance of a new trajectory method against DE-based alternatives on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth interaction labels, as in Fig 1f. Data are real (non-simulated) expression with no ground-truth interaction labels — ROC/AUC benchmarking against truth is not possible The goal is trajectory (pseudotime) ordering accuracy rather than covariate-trajectory interaction detection Input is already a feature table of ranked interaction statistics rather than raw/normalized cell-by-gene expression http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A benchmarking skill for evaluating how well a pseudotime/covariate-interaction method (PhenoPath) recovers covariate-trajectory interactions relative to differential-expression workflows (limma-voom, DESeq2, MAST, Monocle 2) on simulated single-cell data, quantified by ROC AUC across increasing fractions of interacting genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-04696-6
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for evaluating how well a pseudotime/covariate-interaction method (PhenoPath) recovers covariate-trajectory interactions relative to differential-expression workflows (limma-voom, DESeq2, MAST, Monocle 2) on simulated single-cell data, quantified by ROC AUC across increasing fractions of interacting genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are real (non-simulated) expression with no ground-truth interaction labels — ROC/AUC benchmarking against truth is not possible The goal is trajectory (pseudotime) ordering accuracy rather than covariate-trajectory interaction detection Input is already a feature table of ranked interaction statistics rather than raw/normalized cell-by-gene expression

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix is too large for downstream tools (clustering, trajectory inference) and an evenly covering cell subsample is needed, e.g. hundreds of thousands to millions of cells in CSV form.
skills.name: single-cell-sketch-sampling
skills.search_text: single-cell-sketch-sampling Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix is too large for downstream tools (clustering, trajectory inference) and an evenly covering cell subsample is needed, e.g. hundreds of thousands to millions of cells in CSV form. The input is already a small subsample or a pre-clustered/sampled dataset (e.g. clustering-then-sampling output as in dropClust); sketching is designed for full massive datasets The task requires a systematic study of how the sketching distance metric interacts with preprocessing of downstream algorithms — the paper states this interplay was not systematically addressed The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's underlying model — the paper only validated compatibility with Louvain community detection and Monocle 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Compute a 'spherical sketch' of a massive single-cell RNA-seq dataset with Sphetcher, which uses spherical thresholding (set cover) to pick a small representative subset of cells that evenly covers the transcriptomic space, enabling tractable downstream clustering and recovery of rare cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101126
skills.summary: Compute a 'spherical sketch' of a massive single-cell RNA-seq dataset with Sphetcher, which uses spherical thresholding (set cover) to pick a small representative subset of cells that evenly covers the transcriptomic space, enabling tractable downstream clustering and recovery of rare cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a small subsample or a pre-clustered/sampled dataset (e.g. clustering-then-sampling output as in dropClust); sketching is designed for full massive datasets The task requires a systematic study of how the sketching distance metric interacts with preprocessing of downstream algorithms — the paper states this interplay was not systematically addressed The downstream algorithm's assumptions are incompatible with Sphetcher's underlying model — the paper only validated compatibility with Louvain community detection and Monocle 2

skills.description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, scaled scRNA-seq object with variable features and PCA coordinates must be converted into a cell-to-cell SNN graph to enable graph-based (Louvain) clustering and downstream marker identification.
skills.name: single-cell-snn-graph-construction
skills.search_text: single-cell-snn-graph-construction Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, scaled scRNA-seq object with variable features and PCA coordinates must be converted into a cell-to-cell SNN graph to enable graph-based (Louvain) clustering and downstream marker identification. Input is raw count data that has not passed QC, normalization, scaling, and PCA — the graph must be built on scaled PCA coordinates, not raw expression Input is scATAC-seq data analyzed via LSI dimensionality reduction (SCALA uses LSI for the epigenomic modality, not PCA-based SNN on gene expression) The goal is only cluster annotation/label transfer (e.g., CIPR) rather than de novo graph-based partitioning of cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a shared-nearest-neighbour (SNN) graph over single-cell transcriptomes in the informative PCA space (e.g., 25 PCs of PBMC3k) using Seurat, as SCALA does, so that graph-based Louvain partitioning can identify distinct cell populations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Builds a shared-nearest-neighbour (SNN) graph over single-cell transcriptomes in the informative PCA space (e.g., 25 PCs of PBMC3k) using Seurat, as SCALA does, so that graph-based Louvain partitioning can identify distinct cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count data that has not passed QC, normalization, scaling, and PCA — the graph must be built on scaled PCA coordinates, not raw expression Input is scATAC-seq data analyzed via LSI dimensionality reduction (SCALA uses LSI for the epigenomic modality, not PCA-based SNN on gene expression) The goal is only cluster annotation/label transfer (e.g., CIPR) rather than de novo graph-based partitioning of cells

skills.description: Use when you have a 10x possorted_genome BAM plus barcodes.tsv from a multi-person cell mixture and need per-cell SNP genotypes to genetically separate contributors into individual-specific clusters.
skills.name: single-cell-snp-genotyping
skills.search_text: single-cell-snp-genotyping Use when you have a 10x possorted_genome BAM plus barcodes.tsv from a multi-person cell mixture and need per-cell SNP genotypes to genetically separate contributors into individual-specific clusters. The sample is single-source (no mixture) — standard genotyping/quantification suffices and cluster separation is unnecessary. Only dead/fixed cells are available — the 10x scRNA-seq platform used here 'requires live cells for successful genetic separation', so the input BAM cannot be produced. The goal is DNA profiling from bulk mixture traces (no single-cell data) — this skill operates on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs, not bulk forensic DNA profiles. http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Genotypes individual cells from a 10x single-cell RNA-seq mixture by calling SNPs with haplotype-based freebayes against a reference genome, filtering by depth/quality, and merging cells into per-cell genotype profiles that enable clustering of contributors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Genotypes individual cells from a 10x single-cell RNA-seq mixture by calling SNPs with haplotype-based freebayes against a reference genome, filtering by depth/quality, and merging cells into per-cell genotype profiles that enable clustering of contributors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample is single-source (no mixture) — standard genotyping/quantification suffices and cluster separation is unnecessary. Only dead/fixed cells are available — the 10x scRNA-seq platform used here 'requires live cells for successful genetic separation', so the input BAM cannot be produced. The goal is DNA profiling from bulk mixture traces (no single-cell data) — this skill operates on 10x scRNA-seq BAMs, not bulk forensic DNA profiles.

skills.description: Use when starting from raw scRNA-seq reads (GEO SRA/FASTQ) and you need per-cell SNV calls and gene count matrices as SSrGE inputs, e.g. to build eeSNV features for cancer subpopulation identification.
skills.name: single-cell-snv-calling
skills.search_text: single-cell-snv-calling Use when starting from raw scRNA-seq reads (GEO SRA/FASTQ) and you need per-cell SNV calls and gene count matrices as SSrGE inputs, e.g. to build eeSNV features for cancer subpopulation identification. You already have per-cell VCFs or an SNV matrix and want to fit SSrGE LASSO models or rank eeSNVs — this skill only produces the SNV/count inputs, not the modeling. The goal is exhaustive variant discovery from matched DNA-seq; the paper warns SSrGE may miss some driver mutations due to incomplete DNA coverage of scRNA-seq reads. skills.description: Use when a query SC dataset (e.g., .h5ad) lacks coordinates but a matched ST reference (SeqFISH/Visium-like) with truth x/y locations and overlapping genes is available, and spatially-aware downstream analyses such as co-localization or CCC are needed.

skills.search_text: single-cell-spatial-location-reconstruction Use when a query SC dataset (e.g., .h5ad) lacks coordinates but a matched ST reference (SeqFISH/Visium-like) with truth x/y locations and overlapping genes is available, and spatially-aware downstream analyses such as co-localization or CCC are needed. Tissue has a high level of repeating elements, which challenges spatial reconstruction of SC cells. The input already has truth cell locations or is itself an ST dataset — evaluation modules (neighbor hit, JSD, Spearman) should be used instead of inference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct spatial locations of single-cell RNA-seq (SC) cells from a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference using CellContrast's contrastive encoder, then benchmark or complement the reconstruction with CeLEry and SageNet for downstream cell-type co-localization analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Reconstruct spatial locations of single-cell RNA-seq (SC) cells from a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference using CellContrast's contrastive encoder, then benchmark or complement the reconstruction with CeLEry and SageNet for downstream cell-type co-localization analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query SC data and ST reference have a large gap (different tissues/conditions): forcing SC assignment to resemble ST can introduce bias, and all methods show a performance drop in global reconstruction.
