skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single study is available and no qualitative cross-study comparison of marker expression is required The study data has not been processed into H5AD files with cell annotations and precalculated differential expression results (raw counts or FASTQ inputs are out of scope for this skill) A quantitative, batch-corrected cross-study integration of expression values is needed — Cellenium's marker search is explicitly a qualitative comparison of gene expression across studies

skills.description: Use when a coarse cell-type annotation (e.g., 'dermal condensate') must be resolved into finer transcriptional states, and downstream tools like CellChat require state-resolved cell groups as input.
skills.name: single-cell-subclustering-louvain
skills.search_text: single-cell-subclustering-louvain Use when a coarse cell-type annotation (e.g., 'dermal condensate') must be resolved into finer transcriptional states, and downstream tools like CellChat require state-resolved cell groups as input. The input cell type has abundance <= 5% of the dataset — Louvain subclustering on rare populations is underpowered and not supported by the article's workflow Contaminated or doublet-containing groups have not yet been removed (e.g., CD3D+ T cells within FIB, or immune cells lacking DC markers), as these distort community structure The analysis goal is de novo clustering of the full dataset rather than resolving states within an already-annotated compartment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Subclusters a defined single-cell compartment (e.g., dermal cells in E14.5 embryonic skin) using Louvain community detection restricted to cell types with abundance > 5%, then annotates resulting states (placode, pre-DC, DC1, DC2) from canonical markers prior to cell-cell communication analysis with CellChat. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: Subclusters a defined single-cell compartment (e.g., dermal cells in E14.5 embryonic skin) using Louvain community detection restricted to cell types with abundance > 5%, then annotates resulting states (placode, pre-DC, DC1, DC2) from canonical markers prior to cell-cell communication analysis with CellChat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input cell type has abundance <= 5% of the dataset — Louvain subclustering on rare populations is underpowered and not supported by the article's workflow Contaminated or doublet-containing groups have not yet been removed (e.g., CD3D+ T cells within FIB, or immune cells lacking DC markers), as these distort community structure The analysis goal is de novo clustering of the full dataset rather than resolving states within an already-annotated compartment

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells need to be grouped into subpopulations using either SNV-based features (eeSNVs from SSrGE) or raw gene-expression matrices, and when cluster quality must be benchmarked against known labels with AMI over bootstrap runs.
skills.name: single-cell-subpopulation-clustering
skills.search_text: single-cell-subpopulation-clustering Use when scRNA-seq cells need to be grouped into subpopulations using either SNV-based features (eeSNVs from SSrGE) or raw gene-expression matrices, and when cluster quality must be benchmarked against known labels with AMI over bootstrap runs. The input is already a reduced/dimensionality-reduced feature table (e.g., pre-computed PCA components or a curated eeSNV matrix) — clustering can proceed directly without re-running the SSrGE feature derivation. The dataset is one of the four non-cancer scRNA-seq datasets (GSE79457, GSE81903, GSE71485, GSE80232) where the eeSNV-over-GE advantage was not the evaluated claim. No reference subpopulation labels are available — AMI cannot be computed, and the 30-run bootstrap evaluation design is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data into cancer cell subpopulations by comparing eeSNV-derived features against full gene-expression (GE) matrices across five clustering strategies (PCA/FA + K-means, PCA/FA + agglomerative WARD, and SIMLR), evaluated by adjusted mutual information (AMI) against known subpopulation labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data into cancer cell subpopulations by comparing eeSNV-derived features against full gene-expression (GE) matrices across five clustering strategies (PCA/FA + K-means, PCA/FA + agglomerative WARD, and SIMLR), evaluated by adjusted mutual information (AMI) against known subpopulation labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced/dimensionality-reduced feature table (e.g., pre-computed PCA components or a curated eeSNV matrix) — clustering can proceed directly without re-running the SSrGE feature derivation. The dataset is one of the four non-cancer scRNA-seq datasets (GSE79457, GSE81903, GSE71485, GSE80232) where the eeSNV-over-GE advantage was not the evaluated claim. No reference subpopulation labels are available — AMI cannot be computed, and the 30-run bootstrap evaluation design is not applicable.

skills.description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-level metadata (cell type, patient outcome) must be narrowed to one cell type before co-expression network inference, e.g. isolating classical monocytes from PBMCs.
skills.name: single-cell-subpopulation-selection
skills.search_text: single-cell-subpopulation-selection Use when a processed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-level metadata (cell type, patient outcome) must be narrowed to one cell type before co-expression network inference, e.g. isolating classical monocytes from PBMCs. Input is already bulk or pseudo-bulk expression data with no per-cell labels to subset The analysis goal is cell-type discovery/clustering itself rather than selecting a known annotated sub-population for downstream module detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects a specific cell sub-population (e.g. classical monocytes) from processed scRNA-seq data and divides it into N sub-clusters, averaging expression per sub-cluster to build pseudo-bulk representatives for downstream network inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad644
skills.summary: Selects a specific cell sub-population (e.g. classical monocytes) from processed scRNA-seq data and divides it into N sub-clusters, averaging expression per sub-cluster to build pseudo-bulk representatives for downstream network inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already bulk or pseudo-bulk expression data with no per-cell labels to subset The analysis goal is cell-type discovery/clustering itself rather than selecting a known annotated sub-population for downstream module detection

skills.description: Use when comparing sketching/subsampling methods on large scRNA-seq datasets (tens of thousands to millions of cells) with metrics like runtime, Gini coefficient, Hausdorff distance, or downstream deconvolution/annotation accuracy.
skills.name: single-cell-subsampling-method-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-subsampling-method-benchmarking Use when comparing sketching/subsampling methods on large scRNA-seq datasets (tens of thousands to millions of cells) with metrics like runtime, Gini coefficient, Hausdorff distance, or downstream deconvolution/annotation accuracy. The dataset is small enough to analyse in full — sketching trades fidelity for efficiency and full-data performance is the reference baseline The evaluation target is a purely distributional property other than cell-type balance and feature-distribution fidelity (e.g. spatial or trajectory structure), which the time/Gini/Hausdorff triad does not capture Cell-type labels (cell_type_key) are absent or unreliable, since scValue's DV-weighted per-type allocation and the Gini coefficient both require them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark scRNA-seq subsampling (sketching) methods — scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler — by generating 10% sketches, ranking them on computation time, Gini coefficient of cell-type proportions, and Hausdorff distance, and optionally validating sketches in downstream tasks such as MuSiC bulk deconvolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf279
skills.summary: Benchmark scRNA-seq subsampling (sketching) methods — scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler — by generating 10% sketches, ranking them on computation time, Gini coefficient of cell-type proportions, and Hausdorff distance, and optionally validating sketches in downstream tasks such as MuSiC bulk deconvolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough to analyse in full — sketching trades fidelity for efficiency and full-data performance is the reference baseline The evaluation target is a purely distributional property other than cell-type balance and feature-distribution fidelity (e.g. spatial or trajectory structure), which the time/Gini/Hausdorff triad does not capture Cell-type labels (cell_type_key) are absent or unreliable, since scValue's DV-weighted per-type allocation and the Gini coefficient both require them

skills.description: Use when benchmarking deep-learning cell annotation on tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq data, specifically to test whether major-type prediction followed by Seurat subclustering improves T/NK or myeloid subtype accuracy over direct per-cell annotation.
skills.name: single-cell-subtype-annotation-evaluation
skills.search_text: single-cell-subtype-annotation-evaluation Use when benchmarking deep-learning cell annotation on tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq data, specifically to test whether major-type prediction followed by Seurat subclustering improves T/NK or myeloid subtype accuracy over direct per-cell annotation. Input data is unlabeled or lacks original study cell labels — the 'consistent/inconsistent/unknown' accuracy evaluation against ground truth cannot be computed The goal is annotating tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers), which scWizard may not identify and will assign to the Unknown cluster http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reproduces scWizard's two-step (annotate-after-clustering) versus direct per-cell subtype annotation benchmark on T/NK and myeloid scRNA-seq test sets, quantifying accuracy gains from Seurat subclustering before subtype assignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.08.028
skills.summary: Reproduces scWizard's two-step (annotate-after-clustering) versus direct per-cell subtype annotation benchmark on T/NK and myeloid scRNA-seq test sets, quantifying accuracy gains from Seurat subclustering before subtype assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is unlabeled or lacks original study cell labels — the 'consistent/inconsistent/unknown' accuracy evaluation against ground truth cannot be computed The goal is annotating tissue-specific cell types (e.g., alveolar cells in lung cancers), which scWizard may not identify and will assign to the Unknown cluster

skills.description: Use when building a GRN from large single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g. snRNA-seq count matrices from a specific cell type like microglia or whole visium data) where full-transcriptome GRN inference is computationally intractable and per-cell sparsity must be reduced.
skills.name: single-cell-supercell-construction
skills.search_text: single-cell-supercell-construction Use when building a GRN from large single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g. snRNA-seq count matrices from a specific cell type like microglia or whole visium data) where full-transcriptome GRN inference is computationally intractable and per-cell sparsity must be reduced. The input is already aggregated (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed pseudobulk table) and has no per-cell heterogeneity to consolidate Spatial transcriptomics data where the analysis goal requires explicitly using spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING does not utilize spatial information in GRN construction The goal is a GRN over a small pre-selected panel of a few thousand genes where direct per-cell inference is already tractable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Aggregates transcriptionally similar single cells into supercells as the first stage of the SCING gene regulatory network inference pipeline, reducing sparsity and noise before GRN construction from snRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Aggregates transcriptionally similar single cells into supercells as the first stage of the SCING gene regulatory network inference pipeline, reducing sparsity and noise before GRN construction from snRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already aggregated (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or a precomputed pseudobulk table) and has no per-cell heterogeneity to consolidate Spatial transcriptomics data where the analysis goal requires explicitly using spatial coordinates during network construction — SCING does not utilize spatial information in GRN construction The goal is a GRN over a small pre-selected panel of a few thousand genes where direct per-cell inference is already tractable

skills.description: Use when a continuous positive separation/threshold parameter (Delta) must be tuned so that same-label samples stay closer than different-label samples in a reduced marker subspace, with accuracy on a held-out test split as the objective.
skills.name: single-cell-synthetic-spectra-handling
skills.search_text: single-cell-synthetic-spectra-handling Use when a continuous positive separation/threshold parameter (Delta) must be tuned so that same-label samples stay closer than different-label samples in a reduced marker subspace, with accuracy on a held-out test split as the objective. The parameter to tune is discrete or combinatorial (e.g., choosing which genes constitute the marker set), where the article frames the selection as 'a combinatorially difficult' problem rather than a continuous annealing search Cell labels are continuous trajectories or spatial locations rather than categorical labels, since the method's underlying assumption is that 'cell type classes are linearly separable' under categorical labeling No LP solver or evaluation backend exists to score candidate Delta values, since the objective must be evaluated through the solver A hyperparameter-search skill that reconstructs the target separation parameter (Delta) of a constrained marker-selection problem (scGeneFit-style label-aware compressive classification) by treating classifier accuracy, evaluated through a linear-program solver, as a black-box objective over Delta > 0 and optimizing it with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21453-4
skills.summary: A hyperparameter-search skill that reconstructs the target separation parameter (Delta) of a constrained marker-selection problem (scGeneFit-style label-aware compressive classification) by treating classifier accuracy, evaluated through a linear-program solver, as a black-box objective over Delta > 0 and optimizing it with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The parameter to tune is discrete or combinatorial (e.g., choosing which genes constitute the marker set), where the article frames the selection as 'a combinatorially difficult' problem rather than a continuous annealing search Cell labels are continuous trajectories or spatial locations rather than categorical labels, since the method's underlying assumption is that 'cell type classes are linearly separable' under categorical labeling No LP solver or evaluation backend exists to score candidate Delta values, since the objective must be evaluated through the solver

skills.description: Use when you have 10x-style scRNA-seq BAM files (Cell Ranger CB:Z/UB:Z or STARsolo CR:Z/UR:Z tags) and need per-cell TE expression counts to study TE heterogeneity during development, reprogramming, or differentiation.
skills.name: single-cell-te-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-te-expression-quantification Use when you have 10x-style scRNA-seq BAM files (Cell Ranger CB:Z/UB:Z or STARsolo CR:Z/UR:Z tags) and need per-cell TE expression counts to study TE heterogeneity during development, reprogramming, or differentiation. Input is already a gene or TE feature count matrix — scTE requires raw BAM/SAM alignments as input The analysis goal is chromatin accessibility of TEs rather than expression — scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build on scATAC-seq BAMs is the appropriate variant Filtered/selected alignment files are the only available input — the README highly recommends unfiltered alignment files http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Quantify transposable element (TE) expression in single-cell RNA-seq data using the scTE pipeline, which counts TE-derived reads per cell from aligned BAM/SAM files and yields a cell-by-TE matrix (e.g. .h5ad) for detecting lineage-specific TE dynamics. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21808-x
skills.summary: Quantify transposable element (TE) expression in single-cell RNA-seq data using the scTE pipeline, which counts TE-derived reads per cell from aligned BAM/SAM files and yields a cell-by-TE matrix (e.g. .h5ad) for detecting lineage-specific TE dynamics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene or TE feature count matrix — scTE requires raw BAM/SAM alignments as input The analysis goal is chromatin accessibility of TEs rather than expression — scTEATAC/scTEATAC_build on scATAC-seq BAMs is the appropriate variant Filtered/selected alignment files are the only available input — the README highly recommends unfiltered alignment files

skills.description: Use when single-cell short-read data (10X scRNA, Smart-seq2 scRNA, scATAC-seq, Visium, multi-omics) requires TE quantification where multi-mapping reads from repetitive TEs must be accurately assigned to specific loci rather than collapsed to subfamily level.
skills.name: single-cell-te-quantification
skills.search_text: single-cell-te-quantification Use when single-cell short-read data (10X scRNA, Smart-seq2 scRNA, scATAC-seq, Visium, multi-omics) requires TE quantification where multi-mapping reads from repetitive TEs must be accurately assigned to specific loci rather than collapsed to subfamily level. Data lacks sufficient multi-mapping TE reads — use MATES simple mode / version >=0.1.8 fallback instead of full locus-specific inference Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements like L1HS spanning several thousand bases — flanking-context-based multi-mapping estimation is inaccurate for TEs longer than 2001 bp Only bulk-level TE quantification is needed — bulk tools such as TEtranscripts or Telescope are designed for non-single-cell inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Quantify transposable element (TE) expression/accessibility at locus-specific resolution in single-cell sequencing data using MATES, a deep neural network that probabilistically allocates multi-mapping reads to individual TE loci based on flanking unique-read coverage context, improving over subfamily-level methods like scTE and SoloTE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-53114-7
skills.summary: Quantify transposable element (TE) expression/accessibility at locus-specific resolution in single-cell sequencing data using MATES, a deep neural network that probabilistically allocates multi-mapping reads to individual TE loci based on flanking unique-read coverage context, improving over subfamily-level methods like scTE and SoloTE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks sufficient multi-mapping TE reads — use MATES simple mode / version >=0.1.8 fallback instead of full locus-specific inference Target TEs are long autonomously expressed elements like L1HS spanning several thousand bases — flanking-context-based multi-mapping estimation is inaccurate for TEs longer than 2001 bp Only bulk-level TE quantification is needed — bulk tools such as TEtranscripts or Telescope are designed for non-single-cell inputs

skills.description: Use when multi-batch single-cell data has a continuous per-cell time axis (e.g. scVelo latent time) and you need to test whether learned interpretable factors (JOINTLY modules) show stage-specific or monotonic temporal activity.
skills.name: single-cell-temporal-binning-factor-profiling
skills.search_text: single-cell-temporal-binning-factor-profiling Use when multi-batch single-cell data has a continuous per-cell time axis (e.g. scVelo latent time) and you need to test whether learned interpretable factors (JOINTLY modules) show stage-specific or monotonic temporal activity. The input cells lack a continuous per-cell time ordering (no pseudotime/latent time), so ordered binning along differentiation cannot be defined. The analysis goal is batch-effect removal or clustering performance benchmarking (ARI/NMI) rather than temporal profiling of interpretable factors. The dataset is a static reference atlas task (e.g. WATLAS-style annotation/deconvolution) where stage-specific factor dynamics are not the question. Orders single cells along an external continuous axis (e.g. scVelo RNA-velocity latent time), bins cells into ordered intervals, and computes mean activity of interpretable JOINTLY factors per bin to build factor temporal profiles (Fig. 4I-K). Used to show that JOINTLY's factors recover continuous temporal dynamics during mouse gastrulation erythropoiesis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Orders single cells along an external continuous axis (e.g. scVelo RNA-velocity latent time), bins cells into ordered intervals, and computes mean activity of interpretable JOINTLY factors per bin to build factor temporal profiles (Fig. 4I-K). Used to show that JOINTLY's factors recover continuous temporal dynamics during mouse gastrulation erythropoiesis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input cells lack a continuous per-cell time ordering (no pseudotime/latent time), so ordered binning along differentiation cannot be defined. The analysis goal is batch-effect removal or clustering performance benchmarking (ARI/NMI) rather than temporal profiling of interpretable factors. The dataset is a static reference atlas task (e.g. WATLAS-style annotation/deconvolution) where stage-specific factor dynamics are not the question.

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell GEO datasets (e.g. GSE81861 CRC, GSE72056 melanoma, GSE86146 embryonic) must be converted into bulk-aggregated expression matrices to validate cell-abundance inference or run bulk deconvolution baselines.
skills.name: single-cell-to-bulk-aggregation
skills.search_text: single-cell-to-bulk-aggregation Use when raw single-cell GEO datasets (e.g. GSE81861 CRC, GSE72056 melanoma, GSE86146 embryonic) must be converted into bulk-aggregated expression matrices to validate cell-abundance inference or run bulk deconvolution baselines. The input is already bulk RNA-seq (e.g. TCGA samples downloaded from GDC) — no aggregation is needed, only the log2(x+1) transform The downstream method expects single-cell-level granularity rather than sample-level pseudo-bulk profiles The analysis is the DCNet training pipeline itself on TCGA data, where the article instead splits samples 80/20 into train/test sets rather than aggregating single cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates single-cell RNA-seq profiles into pseudo-bulk expression matrices (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) so that bulk deconvolution methods such as DCNet, CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, and xCell can be benchmarked against known true cell abundances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Aggregates single-cell RNA-seq profiles into pseudo-bulk expression matrices (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) so that bulk deconvolution methods such as DCNet, CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, and xCell can be benchmarked against known true cell abundances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already bulk RNA-seq (e.g. TCGA samples downloaded from GDC) — no aggregation is needed, only the log2(x+1) transform The downstream method expects single-cell-level granularity rather than sample-level pseudo-bulk profiles The analysis is the DCNet training pipeline itself on TCGA data, where the article instead splits samples 80/20 into train/test sets rather than aggregating single cells

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression counts from a large cohort plus snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data from a subset of the same tissue (e.g., DLPFC), and need estimated cell-type proportions for phenotype association testing.
skills.name: single-cell-to-bulk-decomposition
skills.search_text: single-cell-to-bulk-decomposition Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression counts from a large cohort plus snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data from a subset of the same tissue (e.g., DLPFC), and need estimated cell-type proportions for phenotype association testing. Only known marker genes are available and cross-cell-type comparison of absolute proportions is required — BisqueMarker estimates relative differences in abundances that cannot be compared across cell types. Very few individuals have single-cell data, making the reference profile and gene-specific transformations unreliable. Input is already cell-type-level single-cell data with no bulk cohort to decompose. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Reference-based decomposition of bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions using Bisque, which integrates scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference profiles with gene-specific bulk expression transformations; includes a marker-based fallback (BisqueMarker) when no reference is available. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Reference-based decomposition of bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions using Bisque, which integrates scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference profiles with gene-specific bulk expression transformations; includes a marker-based fallback (BisqueMarker) when no reference is available.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only known marker genes are available and cross-cell-type comparison of absolute proportions is required — BisqueMarker estimates relative differences in abundances that cannot be compared across cell types. Very few individuals have single-cell data, making the reference profile and gene-specific transformations unreliable. Input is already cell-type-level single-cell data with no bulk cohort to decompose.

skills.description: Use when you have a Miscell encoder trained on single-cell RNA-seq and a bulk tumor expression cohort (e.g., Mariathasan ICB or TCGA pan-cancer) whose clinical outcomes you want to link to latent features.
skills.name: single-cell-to-bulk-transfer-learning
skills.search_text: single-cell-to-bulk-transfer-learning Use when you have a Miscell encoder trained on single-cell RNA-seq and a bulk tumor expression cohort (e.g., Mariathasan ICB or TCGA pan-cancer) whose clinical outcomes you want to link to latent features. Small datasets: Miscell, analogous to deep neural network methods, demands a large sample size to obtain good performance Data with uncorrected batch effects: Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods, so batch correction must be a preprocessing step before projection If the goal is explainable clinical markers: the clinically significant latent features extracted by Miscell lack explainability and the biological mechanisms remain unknown Transfer latent features learned by Miscell's self-supervised encoder (contrastive learning on single-cell transcriptomes) to bulk tumor RNA-seq data, then test the 64 latent features for clinical associations such as ICB therapy response and overall survival. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Transfer latent features learned by Miscell's self-supervised encoder (contrastive learning on single-cell transcriptomes) to bulk tumor RNA-seq data, then test the 64 latent features for clinical associations such as ICB therapy response and overall survival.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Small datasets: Miscell, analogous to deep neural network methods, demands a large sample size to obtain good performance Data with uncorrected batch effects: Miscell does not internally include any batch-correction methods, so batch correction must be a preprocessing step before projection If the goal is explainable clinical markers: the clinically significant latent features extracted by Miscell lack explainability and the biological mechanisms remain unknown

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell expression data must be collapsed to cell-type-level sender/receiver scores per ligand-receptor pair before assembling communication tensors across multiple samples or contexts.
skills.name: single-cell-to-cell-type-aggregation-nonzero-fraction
skills.search_text: single-cell-to-cell-type-aggregation-nonzero-fraction Use when raw single-cell expression data must be collapsed to cell-type-level sender/receiver scores per ligand-receptor pair before assembling communication tensors across multiple samples or contexts. Data are already aggregated to pseudo-bulk or cell-type-level expression, so a second single-cell aggregation step is unnecessary The analysis targets a single sample/context with no need to build a context-aware tensor; a single-context CCC tool alone may suffice Cell types are not shared across all samples and retaining rare context-specific cell types is a priority, since the standard workflow drops unshared cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Aggregates single-cell ligand/receptor expression scores into cell-type-level communication scores using a non-zero fraction strategy implemented in cell2cell.preprocessing, as a prerequisite step for building 3D/4D communication tensors in the Tensor-cell2cell pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31369-2
skills.summary: Aggregates single-cell ligand/receptor expression scores into cell-type-level communication scores using a non-zero fraction strategy implemented in cell2cell.preprocessing, as a prerequisite step for building 3D/4D communication tensors in the Tensor-cell2cell pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already aggregated to pseudo-bulk or cell-type-level expression, so a second single-cell aggregation step is unnecessary The analysis targets a single sample/context with no need to build a context-aware tensor; a single-context CCC tool alone may suffice Cell types are not shared across all samples and retaining rare context-specific cell types is a priority, since the standard workflow drops unshared cell types

skills.description: Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERFISH) must be deconvolved to single-cell resolution by mapping each SC profile onto ST spots, after both datasets share a trained embedding space.
skills.name: single-cell-to-spot-mapping-matrix-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-to-spot-mapping-matrix-inference Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERFISH) must be deconvolved to single-cell resolution by mapping each SC profile onto ST spots, after both datasets share a trained embedding space. ST data is already at single-cell resolution, so no SC-to-spot assignment is needed SC and ST data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work Only spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types is required (deconvolution methods handle this; STEM's mapping matrix targets single-cell level assignment) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infers the cell-to-spot (SC-ST) mapping matrix `netsc2st` from STEM's spatially aware embeddings by applying softmax over the inner product of SC and ST embeddings, assigning each single cell a probability distribution over ST spots. This is the step that converts spot-level spatial information into single-cell spatial coordinates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Infers the cell-to-spot (SC-ST) mapping matrix `netsc2st` from STEM's spatially aware embeddings by applying softmax over the inner product of SC and ST embeddings, assigning each single cell a probability distribution over ST spots. This is the step that converts spot-level spatial information into single-cell spatial coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ST data is already at single-cell resolution, so no SC-to-spot assignment is needed SC and ST data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM across donors in the same disease state remains untested future work Only spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types is required (deconvolution methods handle this; STEM's mapping matrix targets single-cell level assignment)

skills.description: Use when you need to integrate and cluster large-scale scRNA-seq datasets while obtaining interpretable topic-pathway associations from a cells-by-genes AnnData matrix with batch annotations.
skills.name: single-cell-topic-model-training
skills.search_text: single-cell-topic-model-training Use when you need to integrate and cluster large-scale scRNA-seq datasets while obtaining interpretable topic-pathway associations from a cells-by-genes AnnData matrix with batch annotations. Your input is not a raw or normalized cells-by-genes count matrix in AnnData format but an already-embedded or feature-summarized table You need to correct for multiple categorical batch variables or continuous/numerical batch variables (e.g., subject age); scETM currently handles only a single categorical batch variable You need multi-omic integration (scRNA-seq with protein or scATAC-seq); this is not yet implemented in scETM http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train a scETM (single-cell Embedded Topic Model) generative topic model on cells-by-genes scRNA-seq AnnData matrices to learn interpretable cell, gene, and topic embeddings, optionally with pathway-fixed gene embeddings (p-scETM). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25534-2
skills.summary: Train a scETM (single-cell Embedded Topic Model) generative topic model on cells-by-genes scRNA-seq AnnData matrices to learn interpretable cell, gene, and topic embeddings, optionally with pathway-fixed gene embeddings (p-scETM).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is not a raw or normalized cells-by-genes count matrix in AnnData format but an already-embedded or feature-summarized table You need to correct for multiple categorical batch variables or continuous/numerical batch variables (e.g., subject age); scETM currently handles only a single categorical batch variable You need multi-omic integration (scRNA-seq with protein or scATAC-seq); this is not yet implemented in scETM

skills.description: Use when you have a clustering of single cells (from CLARA k-medoids) plus a low-dimensional cell embedding and need an acyclic tree-shaped trajectory topology connecting the clusters.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-backbone-construction
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-backbone-construction Use when you have a clustering of single cells (from CLARA k-medoids) plus a low-dimensional cell embedding and need an acyclic tree-shaped trajectory topology connecting the clusters. The desired trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles, since the MST backbone is a connected acyclic tree The trajectory has multiple roots (converging topology) and correct pseudotime is required — dynplot will not generate correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories and a manual work-around is needed Clustering input comes from a high-dimensional PCA embedding (e.g. 30 principal components) — k-medoids may produce 1-2 cell clusters, destabilizing the cluster vertices before MST construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs the per-clustering trajectory backbone as a minimum spanning tree over cluster vertices (placed at cluster centroids), using Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like between-cluster distances and the ape R package, as Totem does for each of its many CLARA k-medoids clustering results. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad515
skills.summary: Constructs the per-clustering trajectory backbone as a minimum spanning tree over cluster vertices (placed at cluster centroids), using Slingshot's covariance-based Mahalanobis-like between-cluster distances and the ape R package, as Totem does for each of its many CLARA k-medoids clustering results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The desired trajectory is disconnected or contains cycles — Totem cannot generate disconnected trajectories or trajectories that have cycles, since the MST backbone is a connected acyclic tree The trajectory has multiple roots (converging topology) and correct pseudotime is required — dynplot will not generate correct pseudotime for multi-root trajectories and a manual work-around is needed Clustering input comes from a high-dimensional PCA embedding (e.g. 30 principal components) — k-medoids may produce 1-2 cell clusters, destabilizing the cluster vertices before MST construction

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data span a developmental time course without definitive cell types (e.g., early embryo pre-blastocyst stages), and the goal is to find development-related ligand-receptor pairs whose expression co-varies or causally regulates TF activity along pseudotime.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-cell-cell-communication-analysis
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-cell-cell-communication-analysis Use when scRNA-seq data span a developmental time course without definitive cell types (e.g., early embryo pre-blastocyst stages), and the goal is to find development-related ligand-receptor pairs whose expression co-varies or causally regulates TF activity along pseudotime. Communication is between well-defined, given cell types at steady state — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting, whereas TimeTalk targets temporal/autocrine dynamics without definitive cell types The communication of interest is not ligand-receptor mediated (e.g. extracellular-vesicle-mediated signaling), which the current TimeTalk framework does not account for The question concerns maternal-embryo interactions: the autocrine hypothesis of eLR screening precludes that analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identify co-varying ligand-receptor pairs and infer causal LR-to-TF communication from time-course single-cell RNA-seq by ordering cells along a trajectory (pseudotime), interpolating expression series, and testing temporal correlations and Granger causality. Embodied by the TimeTalk R package for early embryo development data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: Identify co-varying ligand-receptor pairs and infer causal LR-to-TF communication from time-course single-cell RNA-seq by ordering cells along a trajectory (pseudotime), interpolating expression series, and testing temporal correlations and Granger causality. Embodied by the TimeTalk R package for early embryo development data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Communication is between well-defined, given cell types at steady state — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting, whereas TimeTalk targets temporal/autocrine dynamics without definitive cell types The communication of interest is not ligand-receptor mediated (e.g. extracellular-vesicle-mediated signaling), which the current TimeTalk framework does not account for The question concerns maternal-embryo interactions: the autocrine hypothesis of eLR screening precludes that analysis

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq anndata object with 'clusters' annotations and an scVelo RNA velocity field must be turned into a directed differentiation trajectory with per-population fate probabilities and terminal-state visualizations.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-data-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-data-visualization Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq anndata object with 'clusters' annotations and an scVelo RNA velocity field must be turned into a directed differentiation trajectory with per-population fate probabilities and terminal-state visualizations. The input is bulk RNA-seq or lacks cell-type ('clusters') annotations and an RNA velocity field, since neither CellRank's velocity kernel nor FateCompass's velocity-driven Markov chain can be built The goal is time- and lineage-specific transcription-factor activity estimation (the FateCompass linear-model/TF-dynamics workflow) rather than trajectory and terminal-fate visualization Only smooth pseudotime ordering is needed without directed, velocity-informed transition probabilities toward terminal states http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize single-cell differentiation trajectories and terminal-fate assignments by combining RNA-velocity-driven transition probabilities (FateCompass / CellRank) with cell-type annotations, as applied to the E15.5 mouse pancreas endocrine differentiation dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100512
skills.summary: Visualize single-cell differentiation trajectories and terminal-fate assignments by combining RNA-velocity-driven transition probabilities (FateCompass / CellRank) with cell-type annotations, as applied to the E15.5 mouse pancreas endocrine differentiation dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq or lacks cell-type ('clusters') annotations and an RNA velocity field, since neither CellRank's velocity kernel nor FateCompass's velocity-driven Markov chain can be built The goal is time- and lineage-specific transcription-factor activity estimation (the FateCompass linear-model/TF-dynamics workflow) rather than trajectory and terminal-fate visualization Only smooth pseudotime ordering is needed without directed, velocity-informed transition probabilities toward terminal states

skills.description: Use when you need a low-dimensional (d=2 or 3) manifold embedding and plot of single cells for trajectory visualization, starting from a preprocessed N cells × D genes expression matrix and the DTFLOW API.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-embedding-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-embedding-visualization Use when you need a low-dimensional (d=2 or 3) manifold embedding and plot of single cells for trajectory visualization, starting from a preprocessed N cells × D genes expression matrix and the DTFLOW API. The input is already a reduced feature table (e.g. approximate principal components) or an existing embedding rather than the N×D gene expression matrix — BKFD must derive its diffusion distributions from the expression data itself. You need node-specific restart behavior for a heterogeneous graph — the paper notes BKFD uses the same restart probability for all nodes, which may limit the effectiveness of the random walk. A valid bkfd_embedding.csv already exists and the task only needs downstream pseudotime (get_dtflow_times) or branch detection (get_branches(Num)) rather than regenerating the embedding. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Transforms each single cell into a random-walk-with-restart (RWR) diffusion distribution over the k=10 kNN Markov graph, measures cell-cell similarity with the Bhattacharyya kernel (G_ij = sqrt(<s_i, s_j>)), and SVD-decomposes log(G) into a d=2 or 3 dimensional BKFD embedding for pseudotime trajectory visualization in DTFLOW. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Transforms each single cell into a random-walk-with-restart (RWR) diffusion distribution over the k=10 kNN Markov graph, measures cell-cell similarity with the Bhattacharyya kernel (G_ij = sqrt(<s_i, s_j>)), and SVD-decomposes log(G) into a d=2 or 3 dimensional BKFD embedding for pseudotime trajectory visualization in DTFLOW.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a reduced feature table (e.g. approximate principal components) or an existing embedding rather than the N×D gene expression matrix — BKFD must derive its diffusion distributions from the expression data itself. You need node-specific restart behavior for a heterogeneous graph — the paper notes BKFD uses the same restart probability for all nodes, which may limit the effectiveness of the random walk. A valid bkfd_embedding.csv already exists and the task only needs downstream pseudotime (get_dtflow_times) or branch detection (get_branches(Num)) rather than regenerating the embedding.

skills.description: Use when time-series scRNA-seq data with time-point labels and cell type annotations is available and the goal is to predict cell fate bias — the probability a cell enters a particular fate given its initial state — including under simulated perturbations.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-fate-probability-estimation
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-fate-probability-estimation Use when time-series scRNA-seq data with time-point labels and cell type annotations is available and the goal is to predict cell fate bias — the probability a cell enters a particular fate given its initial state — including under simulated perturbations. The final time point of the dataset cannot be assumed to be at steady-state, violating the model's constraint The question concerns individual-gene resolution in a static snapshot rather than trajectories — information about individual genes is lost when data are transformed into PCA space The goal is causal validation of fate associations rather than in silico prediction; association of genes with fates does not imply causality and perturbation work in the paper was limited to TFs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fit a PRESCIENT generative model to longitudinal scRNA-seq data to learn an underlying differentiation landscape, then simulate trajectories from arbitrary initial cell states to estimate fate probabilities for downstream fates (e.g. alpha-, beta-, EC-cell in Veres et al. in vitro beta-cell differentiation). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-23518-w
skills.summary: Fit a PRESCIENT generative model to longitudinal scRNA-seq data to learn an underlying differentiation landscape, then simulate trajectories from arbitrary initial cell states to estimate fate probabilities for downstream fates (e.g. alpha-, beta-, EC-cell in Veres et al. in vitro beta-cell differentiation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The final time point of the dataset cannot be assumed to be at steady-state, violating the model's constraint The question concerns individual-gene resolution in a static snapshot rather than trajectories — information about individual genes is lost when data are transformed into PCA space The goal is causal validation of fate associations rather than in silico prediction; association of genes with fates does not imply causality and perturbation work in the paper was limited to TFs

skills.description: Use when a slingshot SingleCellExperiment/trajectory object exists with per-cell lineage curve weights across ≥2 conditions and the goal is to test whether condition shifts the proportions of cells committed to each lineage.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-fate-selection-testing
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-fate-selection-testing Use when a slingshot SingleCellExperiment/trajectory object exists with per-cell lineage curve weights across ≥2 conditions and the goal is to test whether condition shifts the proportions of cells committed to each lineage. The question is differential progression (pseudotime shifts along the same lineage) — use progressionTest instead of fateSelectionTest. Trajectory topology itself may differ between conditions — run topologyTest (Step 1) first, since a common trajectory is a prerequisite for Step 2 tests. The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages — use fitGAM plus conditionTest (Step 3). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assess differential fate selection — whether cells in different conditions differentiate in varying proportions between lineages — by testing the null hypothesis that lineage-weight (lineage-membership probability) distributions are equal between conditions, using the fateSelectionTest from the condiments workflow (Step 2b). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Assess differential fate selection — whether cells in different conditions differentiate in varying proportions between lineages — by testing the null hypothesis that lineage-weight (lineage-membership probability) distributions are equal between conditions, using the fateSelectionTest from the condiments workflow (Step 2b).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is differential progression (pseudotime shifts along the same lineage) — use progressionTest instead of fateSelectionTest. Trajectory topology itself may differ between conditions — run topologyTest (Step 1) first, since a common trajectory is a prerequisite for Step 2 tests. The goal is gene-level differential expression along lineages — use fitGAM plus conditionTest (Step 3).

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell RNA velocity vectors (spliced/unspliced-derived) that must be exported alongside 3D DR coordinates so CellexalVR can visualize trajectories as animated arrows/particles.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-file-formatting
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-file-formatting Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell RNA velocity vectors (spliced/unspliced-derived) that must be exported alongside 3D DR coordinates so CellexalVR can visualize trajectories as animated arrows/particles. The goal is a standard gene expression graph export without RNA velocity — plain DR coordinates suffice and no destination-coordinate table is needed Data is not destined for CellexalVR — other visualization platforms use different input file formats Only 2D embeddings are available — velocity visualization in CellexalVR expects 3D (x, y, z) coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Formats per-cell origin/destination coordinate pairs (e.g. from scvelo RNA velocity) into 7-column .mds trajectory files via the cellexalvrR export pipeline so CellexalVR can render animated RNA velocity trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103251
skills.summary: Formats per-cell origin/destination coordinate pairs (e.g. from scvelo RNA velocity) into 7-column .mds trajectory files via the cellexalvrR export pipeline so CellexalVR can render animated RNA velocity trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a standard gene expression graph export without RNA velocity — plain DR coordinates suffice and no destination-coordinate table is needed Data is not destined for CellexalVR — other visualization platforms use different input file formats Only 2D embeddings are available — velocity visualization in CellexalVR expects 3D (x, y, z) coordinates

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how an in silico TF perturbation (e.g., Gata1 KO) shifts simulated cell-state transitions relative to the reference differentiation gradient in a scRNA-seq trajectory dataset.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-gradient-visualization
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-gradient-visualization Use when you need to quantify how an in silico TF perturbation (e.g., Gata1 KO) shifts simulated cell-state transitions relative to the reference differentiation gradient in a scRNA-seq trajectory dataset. The goal is discrete cell-type classification rather than vector-field-based perturbation scoring — Capybara measures cell identity as a continuum and is a different approach No pseudotime or reference differentiation trajectory is available to serve as the reference gradient for inner-product scoring The GRN has not been inferred/loaded yet; perturbation simulation requires an Oracle object built from a base GRN first http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Visualizes single-cell trajectory dynamics by converting cell transitions into 2D grid-based gradient vector fields on a low-dimensional embedding, and scores TF perturbations by taking the inner product of simulated perturbation vectors against the pseudotime-derived differentiation gradient in CellOracle. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.stemcr.2022.11.010
skills.summary: Visualizes single-cell trajectory dynamics by converting cell transitions into 2D grid-based gradient vector fields on a low-dimensional embedding, and scores TF perturbations by taking the inner product of simulated perturbation vectors against the pseudotime-derived differentiation gradient in CellOracle.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discrete cell-type classification rather than vector-field-based perturbation scoring — Capybara measures cell identity as a continuum and is a different approach No pseudotime or reference differentiation trajectory is available to serve as the reference gradient for inner-product scoring The GRN has not been inferred/loaded yet; perturbation simulation requires an Oracle object built from a base GRN first

skills.description: Use when single-cell transcriptomic data from two or more conditions must be compared along a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation, EMT), and you need to decide whether a common trajectory suffices or conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or gene expression.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-inference Use when single-cell transcriptomic data from two or more conditions must be compared along a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation, EMT), and you need to decide whether a common trajectory suffices or conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or gene expression. Cells are in a steady-state system with no trajectory/continuum — use cluster-based differential abundance (e.g., milo, DAseq, MAST/scde) instead, since assessing condition imbalance per cluster ignores trajectory structure only when dynamics are absent The chosen trajectory inference method cannot accept a specified underlying skeleton — topologyTest requires a maintained mapping across condition-label permutations and works only with methods like slingshot or TSCAN Batch and condition are confounded such that condition-label permutation tests would be uninterpretable; the article notes some confounding is inherent and unresolvable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A three-step condiments-based workflow for inferring and interpreting single-cell developmental trajectories across multiple conditions: testing differential topology, differential progression/fate selection, and gene-level condition-specific expression along lineages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: A three-step condiments-based workflow for inferring and interpreting single-cell developmental trajectories across multiple conditions: testing differential topology, differential progression/fate selection, and gene-level condition-specific expression along lineages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are in a steady-state system with no trajectory/continuum — use cluster-based differential abundance (e.g., milo, DAseq, MAST/scde) instead, since assessing condition imbalance per cluster ignores trajectory structure only when dynamics are absent The chosen trajectory inference method cannot accept a specified underlying skeleton — topologyTest requires a maintained mapping across condition-label permutations and works only with methods like slingshot or TSCAN Batch and condition are confounded such that condition-label permutation tests would be uninterpretable; the article notes some confounding is inherent and unresolvable

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC/imaging) data must be ordered along pseudotime and cell fates/terminal states auto-detected — e.g. rare delta cells in E15.5 pancreatic endocrinogenesis or dendritic subtypes in CD34+ hematopoiesis.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC/imaging) data must be ordered along pseudotime and cell fates/terminal states auto-detected — e.g. rare delta cells in E15.5 pancreatic endocrinogenesis or dendritic subtypes in CD34+ hematopoiesis. The topology is already known and user-defined terminal/fate assignment is desired — VIA's value here is automatic, unsupervised fate detection without manual cell-fate assignment The input is not single-cell level data (e.g. bulk time-course without per-cell resolution), since VIA's cluster-graph and random-walk machinery operate on single-cell graphs Extensive pre-dimensionality reduction or subsampling is planned that would destroy global connectivity — VIA is designed to scale to >10^6 cells without it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct single-cell developmental trajectories and automatically detect terminal states and rare lineages using VIA, a graph-based trajectory-inference (TI) algorithm that clusters cells with PARC, computes pseudotime, and infers lineage probabilities via lazy-teleporting random walks with MCMC refinement. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25773-3
skills.summary: Reconstruct single-cell developmental trajectories and automatically detect terminal states and rare lineages using VIA, a graph-based trajectory-inference (TI) algorithm that clusters cells with PARC, computes pseudotime, and infers lineage probabilities via lazy-teleporting random walks with MCMC refinement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The topology is already known and user-defined terminal/fate assignment is desired — VIA's value here is automatic, unsupervised fate detection without manual cell-fate assignment The input is not single-cell level data (e.g. bulk time-course without per-cell resolution), since VIA's cluster-graph and random-walk machinery operate on single-cell graphs Extensive pre-dimensionality reduction or subsampling is planned that would destroy global connectivity — VIA is designed to scale to >10^6 cells without it

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a differentiating progenitor population must be ordered into a multi-branching trajectory with landmark states, without a priori temporal ordering of subsets, to detect branching fate decisions.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-inference Use when scRNA-seq data from a differentiating progenitor population must be ordered into a multi-branching trajectory with landmark states, without a priori temporal ordering of subsets, to detect branching fate decisions. Developmental processes start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous datasets in which specific subset information is not known — Mpath depends on signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction The input is already a trajectory or pseudotime ordering and the goal is only gene-wave detection rather than trajectory reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs multi-branching single-cell developmental trajectories using neighborhood-based cell state transitions, as implemented in the Mpath R package, to reveal progenitor progression and fate commitment from scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: Constructs multi-branching single-cell developmental trajectories using neighborhood-based cell state transitions, as implemented in the Mpath R package, to reveal progenitor progression and fate commitment from scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Developmental processes start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support this (planned future extension) Highly heterogeneous datasets in which specific subset information is not known — Mpath depends on signature genes of differentiated cell types and FACS-sorted terminal subsets for fate prediction The input is already a trajectory or pseudotime ordering and the goal is only gene-wave detection rather than trajectory reconstruction

skills.description: Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data spans multiple cell states (e.g., HSC-to-neutrophil/erythroid differentiation) and you need multi-state, transition-centered trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations without knowing branch counts a priori.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-inference-with-flow-networks
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-inference-with-flow-networks Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data spans multiple cell states (e.g., HSC-to-neutrophil/erythroid differentiation) and you need multi-state, transition-centered trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations without knowing branch counts a priori. The analysis goal is a single linear pseudotime ordering or one predefined branch point — linear tools (Waterfall, Monocle 1) or Wishbone may suffice and CellRouter's flow-network machinery is unnecessary overhead. Data are single-cell chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, or mass cytometry — the article only envisions these applications as future work and does not demonstrate them. You need validated functional enrichment or functional characterization of genes along trajectories for engineering engraftable cells — the manuscript explicitly defers this beyond its scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstruct multi-state, branched single-cell trajectories by applying CellRouter's flow network algorithm to subpopulation structure identified on a k-nearest-neighbor graph (cccd/igraph), then score transition-specific gene dynamics along each trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Reconstruct multi-state, branched single-cell trajectories by applying CellRouter's flow network algorithm to subpopulation structure identified on a k-nearest-neighbor graph (cccd/igraph), then score transition-specific gene dynamics along each trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a single linear pseudotime ordering or one predefined branch point — linear tools (Waterfall, Monocle 1) or Wishbone may suffice and CellRouter's flow-network machinery is unnecessary overhead. Data are single-cell chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, or mass cytometry — the article only envisions these applications as future work and does not demonstrate them. You need validated functional enrichment or functional characterization of genes along trajectories for engineering engraftable cells — the manuscript explicitly defers this beyond its scope.

skills.description: Use when new or perturbed cells (e.g. Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-KO GMP scRNA-seq count matrices) must be assigned to branches of an existing wild-type reference trajectory to quantify fate-biased allocation.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-mapping
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-mapping Use when new or perturbed cells (e.g. Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-KO GMP scRNA-seq count matrices) must be assigned to branches of an existing wild-type reference trajectory to quantify fate-biased allocation. When the new cells have totally different fates compared to the ones present in the reference structure — the article states the mapping procedure may not be optimal in that case When no reference trajectory exists and the goal is to reconstruct a trajectory de novo from a single pooled dataset (use the STREAM reconstruction/bifurcation workflow instead) When the expected topology is cyclic or disconnected — the article notes STREAM is not yet adapted to properly describe these more general structures http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Project new (e.g. genetically perturbed) single-cell populations onto a previously learned STREAM elastic principal graph without pooling cells or re-fitting the trajectory, using STREAM's mapping feature with MLLE-based neighborhood weights. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-09670-4
skills.summary: Project new (e.g. genetically perturbed) single-cell populations onto a previously learned STREAM elastic principal graph without pooling cells or re-fitting the trajectory, using STREAM's mapping feature with MLLE-based neighborhood weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the new cells have totally different fates compared to the ones present in the reference structure — the article states the mapping procedure may not be optimal in that case When no reference trajectory exists and the goal is to reconstruct a trajectory de novo from a single pooled dataset (use the STREAM reconstruction/bifurcation workflow instead) When the expected topology is cyclic or disconnected — the article notes STREAM is not yet adapted to properly describe these more general structures

skills.description: Use when comparing RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference (Cytopath) against topology-constrained baselines on a scRNA-seq dataset with pre-computed velocity and known root/terminal cell states and a known cell type ordering.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-method-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-method-comparison Use when comparing RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference (Cytopath) against topology-constrained baselines on a scRNA-seq dataset with pre-computed velocity and known root/terminal cell states and a known cell type ordering. The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case (e.g. spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset) Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this situation The differentiation topology violates the method's assumptions, e.g. tree-constrained methods like Slingshot on convergent/circular topologies such as the neonatal mouse inner ear dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark Cytopath against baseline trajectory inference methods (Slingshot, PAGA with velocity-pseudotime directionality, Monocle3, VeTra, Cellpath) on the 18,140-cell developing mouse hippocampus dataset, quantifying pseudotime quality via Spearman correlation with known cell type ordering across repeated runs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2022.100359
skills.summary: Benchmark Cytopath against baseline trajectory inference methods (Slingshot, PAGA with velocity-pseudotime directionality, Monocle3, VeTra, Cellpath) on the 18,140-cell developing mouse hippocampus dataset, quantifying pseudotime quality via Spearman correlation with known cell type ordering across repeated runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying RNA velocity estimation itself is faulty — the authors state trajectory inference with Cytopath is not meaningful in that case (e.g. spurious root/terminal inference on the erythroid gastrulation dataset) Root and terminal cell states are not clearly identifiable — the authors explicitly do not recommend performing trajectory inference with Cytopath in this situation The differentiation topology violates the method's assumptions, e.g. tree-constrained methods like Slingshot on convergent/circular topologies such as the neonatal mouse inner ear dataset

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple stable and transitional cell states and the goal is to reconstruct trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations (e.g., HSPC-to-erythroid/GMP, B-cell/mono-DC-to-HSPC reprogramming) that linear or single-branch tools cannot resolve.
skills.name: single-cell-trajectory-reconstruction
skills.search_text: single-cell-trajectory-reconstruction Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple stable and transitional cell states and the goal is to reconstruct trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations (e.g., HSPC-to-erythroid/GMP, B-cell/mono-DC-to-HSPC reprogramming) that linear or single-branch tools cannot resolve. skills.summary: Computes a per-cell trait relevance score (TRS) from scPagwas-prioritized trait-relevant genes using Seurat's AddModuleScore with expression-bin-matched control gene sets, then assesses single-cell significance by a Monte Carlo test against the empirical distribution of control TRSs. This background correction guards against expression sparsity, technical noise, and cell-level confounders.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is bulk cell-type enrichment from GWAS summary statistics alone without per-cell scoring — methods such as LDSC-SEG or EPIC apply instead Only trait-relevant gene prioritization is needed; the gPAS/Pearson-correlation step suffices and Monte Carlo TRS testing is unnecessary overhead The scRNA-seq data is unnormalized or lacks a 'RNA' assay, since AddModuleScore-based TRS computation assumes a normalized Seurat object

skills.search_text: single-cell-umap-dimensionality-reduction Use when running gExcite's CITE-seq/ADT analysis layer on paired GEX+ADT (e.g. 10x hashed PBMC) data and you need cell-level similarity embeddings from one or both modalities, or joint BremSC clustering inputs. skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 highly variable genes) must be modeled with per-gene negative-binomial dispersion, specifically to estimate or refresh the inverse dispersion parameter θ during deep generative model training.

skills.search_text: single-cell-umi-count-modeling Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 highly variable genes) must be modeled with per-gene negative-binomial dispersion, specifically to estimate or refresh the inverse dispersion parameter θ during deep generative model training. Input is normalized, log-transformed, or otherwise non-integer expression data — the negative-binomial likelihood in scDBM models raw UMI counts only Data contain batch effects that need correction — the paper states 'Currently, batch effects cannot be learned with scDBMs' and all models were examined without batch correction capabilities The goal is a quantitatively benchmarked dispersion estimator — the paper describes the Fisher scoring module but does not separately benchmark it http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Model scRNA-seq UMI counts with a negative-binomial likelihood (variance μ + μ²/θ) inside the scDBM deep Boltzmann machine, estimating the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ via a regularized Fisher scoring algorithm with a λ/θ² penalty. skills.summary: Model scRNA-seq UMI counts with a negative-binomial likelihood (variance μ + μ²/θ) inside the scDBM deep Boltzmann machine, estimating the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ via a regularized Fisher scoring algorithm with a λ/θ² penalty.
