skills.search_text: single-cell-variant-allele-frequency-inference Use when you have per-cell mutation VAF and coverage matrices from scRNA-seq variant calling that suffer from low coverage and allelic bias, and the goal is inferring corrected genotypes/VAFs or cell lineages. Input is bulk sequencing data without per-cell mutation/coverage matrices — the Bayesian model operates on single-cell variant calling where expressional drop-outs occur You only have transcriptome-level clustering goals with no genetic markers (variants/VAFs) — SClineager performs genetics-based, not expression-based, lineage tracing Input is unprocessed 10x fastq data — reads must first be split per cell (scSplitter) and variant-called (QBRC Somatic Pipeline) before SClineager can be applied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Applies the SClineager Bayesian hierarchical model (R package, MCMC sampling via sclineager_internal/run_sclineager) to infer true cell genotypes and variant allele frequencies (VAFs) from scRNA-seq-derived variant calling, explicitly modeling both expressional drop-outs: low coverage and allelic bias. This enables genetics-based lineage tracing of single cells from existing single-cell sequencing data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108589
skills.summary: Applies the SClineager Bayesian hierarchical model (R package, MCMC sampling via sclineager_internal/run_sclineager) to infer true cell genotypes and variant allele frequencies (VAFs) from scRNA-seq-derived variant calling, explicitly modeling both expressional drop-outs: low coverage and allelic bias. This enables genetics-based lineage tracing of single cells from existing single-cell sequencing data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk sequencing data without per-cell mutation/coverage matrices — the Bayesian model operates on single-cell variant calling where expressional drop-outs occur You only have transcriptome-level clustering goals with no genetic markers (variants/VAFs) — SClineager performs genetics-based, not expression-based, lineage tracing Input is unprocessed 10x fastq data — reads must first be split per cell (scSplitter) and variant-called (QBRC Somatic Pipeline) before SClineager can be applied

skills.description: Use when you have eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs and 10x Chromium BAMs from cells known to be wild-type (e.g., healthy donor bone marrow), and need to estimate per-site false-positive rates of scRNA-seq mutation calling.
skills.name: single-cell-variant-calling-with-molecular-barcodes
skills.search_text: single-cell-variant-calling-with-molecular-barcodes Use when you have eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs and 10x Chromium BAMs from cells known to be wild-type (e.g., healthy donor bone marrow), and need to estimate per-site false-positive rates of scRNA-seq mutation calling. The cells of interest harbor the somatic mutations being tested — this skill is specifically for negative-control cells (healthy donor / wild-type) to measure FPR, not for genotyping tumor cells. Input BAMs lack Chromium cell-barcode and UM (UB_tag) tags, e.g., plate-based full-length cDNA data from Fluidigm C1/SMART-seq, since duplicate collapsing relies on 10x molecular barcodes. You need de novo variant discovery rather than targeted detection of pre-called somatic SNVs — cb_sniffer (like VarTrix) does not perform variant calling. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 A validation skill for estimating the site-specific false-positive rate of scRNA-seq mutation calling by running the cb_sniffer variant-detection workflow on healthy donor bone marrow cells that should not harbor the tested somatic SNVs. It quantifies per-site FPR across ~8057 normal cells using Chromium molecular barcode (UB_tag) duplicate collapsing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: A validation skill for estimating the site-specific false-positive rate of scRNA-seq mutation calling by running the cb_sniffer variant-detection workflow on healthy donor bone marrow cells that should not harbor the tested somatic SNVs. It quantifies per-site FPR across ~8057 normal cells using Chromium molecular barcode (UB_tag) duplicate collapsing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cells of interest harbor the somatic mutations being tested — this skill is specifically for negative-control cells (healthy donor / wild-type) to measure FPR, not for genotyping tumor cells. Input BAMs lack Chromium cell-barcode and UM (UB_tag) tags, e.g., plate-based full-length cDNA data from Fluidigm C1/SMART-seq, since duplicate collapsing relies on 10x molecular barcodes. You need de novo variant discovery rather than targeted detection of pre-called somatic SNVs — cb_sniffer (like VarTrix) does not perform variant calling.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq somatic SNV read counts (Rs, Xs) and bulk WES counts (Rb, Xb) must be subsetted to mutations with estimable bursting kinetics before running Canopy2 tree inference.
skills.name: single-cell-variant-read-count-processing
skills.search_text: single-cell-variant-read-count-processing Use when scRNA-seq somatic SNV read counts (Rs, Xs) and bulk WES counts (Rb, Xb) must be subsetted to mutations with estimable bursting kinetics before running Canopy2 tree inference. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than count matrices — run the somatic/germline variant calling pre-processing pipeline from the Zenodo repository first The goal is clonal-tree inference itself (get_trees/get_best_tree/BIC selection) rather than preparing the read-count inputs for it Working with methods that do not consume mutation-specific bursting-kinetics estimates, such as Cardelino with a guide clonal tree Filters and assembles the mutation-by-cell (Rs, Xs) and mutation-by-bulk (Rb, Xb) read count matrices required by Canopy2, retaining only mutations with estimable bursting kinetics and pairing them with mutation-specific gene activation/deactivation rates (alpha, beta). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Filters and assembles the mutation-by-cell (Rs, Xs) and mutation-by-bulk (Rb, Xb) read count matrices required by Canopy2, retaining only mutations with estimable bursting kinetics and pairing them with mutation-specific gene activation/deactivation rates (alpha, beta).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than count matrices — run the somatic/germline variant calling pre-processing pipeline from the Zenodo repository first The goal is clonal-tree inference itself (get_trees/get_best_tree/BIC selection) rather than preparing the read-count inputs for it Working with methods that do not consume mutation-specific bursting-kinetics estimates, such as Cardelino with a guide clonal tree

skills.description: Use when raw scVDJ-seq contigs (e.g. AIRR/contig formats) must be merged with a SingleCellExperiment GEX object and cells without complete, productive TCR information filtered out before pseudobulking or trajectory analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-vdj-preprocessing
skills.search_text: single-cell-vdj-preprocessing Use when raw scVDJ-seq contigs (e.g. AIRR/contig formats) must be merged with a SingleCellExperiment GEX object and cells without complete, productive TCR information filtered out before pseudobulking or trajectory analysis. The dataset lacks paired single-cell VDJ/immune-receptor sequencing (e.g. Baccin et al. / Baccin-type bone marrow data with no BCR sequencing) — filtering on VDJ chain status is impossible or meaningless. Input has already been through setupVdjPseudobulk or equivalent Dandelion filtering and only contains productive, unambiguous VDJ chains. The goal is trajectory analysis on cyclic processes (e.g. B cell receptor editing) that cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains — preprocessing alone does not address the downstream topology limitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Preprocess paired single-cell VDJ-seq and gene-expression data by filtering non-productive immune receptors and ambiguous VDJ chain status (via dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk), yielding a filtered SingleCellExperiment with complete TCR information for downstream VDJ-feature-space trajectory analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.06.047
skills.summary: Preprocess paired single-cell VDJ-seq and gene-expression data by filtering non-productive immune receptors and ambiguous VDJ chain status (via dandelionR::setupVdjPseudobulk), yielding a filtered SingleCellExperiment with complete TCR information for downstream VDJ-feature-space trajectory analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks paired single-cell VDJ/immune-receptor sequencing (e.g. Baccin et al. / Baccin-type bone marrow data with no BCR sequencing) — filtering on VDJ chain status is impossible or meaningless. Input has already been through setupVdjPseudobulk or equivalent Dandelion filtering and only contains productive, unambiguous VDJ chains. The goal is trajectory analysis on cyclic processes (e.g. B cell receptor editing) that cannot be represented by absorbing Markov chains — preprocessing alone does not address the downstream topology limitation.

skills.description: Use when you have velocity matrices from two or more RNA velocity methods plus per-cell cluster annotations and need a quantitative, dataset-wide comparison of velocity field quality via local neighbor consistency.
skills.name: single-cell-velocity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-velocity-benchmarking Use when you have velocity matrices from two or more RNA velocity methods plus per-cell cluster annotations and need a quantitative, dataset-wide comparison of velocity field quality via local neighbor consistency. You only have a single velocity method's output — there is no baseline to benchmark against and no relative comparison can be made. You want to evaluate velocity accuracy against known ground-truth trajectories or pseudotime rather than internal consistency of the velocity field. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Benchmarks single-cell RNA velocity methods by quantifying local consistency of inferred velocity vectors: for each cell, the mean cosine distance between its velocity and those of its k=30 nearest neighbors is computed per method (e.g., scKINETICS vs. scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo), with lower values indicating a smoother, more concordant velocity field. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-cell RNA velocity methods by quantifying local consistency of inferred velocity vectors: for each cell, the mean cosine distance between its velocity and those of its k=30 nearest neighbors is computed per method (e.g., scKINETICS vs. scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo), with lower values indicating a smoother, more concordant velocity field.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single velocity method's output — there is no baseline to benchmark against and no relative comparison can be made. You want to evaluate velocity accuracy against known ground-truth trajectories or pseudotime rather than internal consistency of the velocity field.

skills.description: Use when scPathoQuant has been run twice on the same cellranger output with -align bbmap and -align bowtie2, and you need to test whether per-gene pathogen UMI quantifications are aligner-independent per sample.
skills.name: single-cell-viral-count-comparison
skills.search_text: single-cell-viral-count-comparison Use when scPathoQuant has been run twice on the same cellranger output with -align bbmap and -align bowtie2, and you need to test whether per-gene pathogen UMI quantifications are aligner-independent per sample. skills.summary: Quantifies consistency of per-gene viral UMI counts between the two scPathoQuant aligner options (bbmap default vs bowtie2) by correlating per-gene counts — e.g. the ten annotated SARS-CoV-2 genes from the GCF_009858895.2 reference — across single-cell samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pathogen GTF was not supplied to scPathoQuant — pathogen_genes_al_sort_counts.sam (per-gene htseq output) is not produced in that case, so only whole-pathogen counts (pathogen_al_counts.csv) exist and gene-level comparison is impossible The goal is benchmarking scPathoQuant against external tools (ViralTrack, Venus, PathogenTrack) rather than internal bbmap-vs-bowtie2 consistency Input is a single pathogen-level count table (pathogen_al_counts.csv) without gene resolution — correlate whole-pathogen copy numbers instead

skills.name: single-core-compute-profiling
skills.search_text: single-core-compute-profiling Use when comparing the computational scalability of imputation pipelines on large single-cell expression matrices (tens of thousands of cells) and needing a runtime-vs-cell-count profile under controlled single-core execution. The goal is imputation accuracy rather than computational benchmarking — accuracy comparisons require ground-truth validation, not timing runs Only a small dataset (under ~5000 cells) is available, so runtime scaling differences between methods cannot be resolved Parallel or multi-core execution is required — this skill's timings are only comparable under strict single-core restriction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, SAVER, scImpute) on random cell subsets of the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex matrix, each restricted to a single core, to characterize how runtime scales with cell count. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock runtime of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, SAVER, scImpute) on random cell subsets of the Hrvatin et al. mouse visual cortex matrix, each restricted to a single core, to characterize how runtime scales with cell count.

skills.description: Use when comparing runtime scalability of scRNA-seq rare-cell detection algorithms as input cell count grows from ~1k to tens of thousands of expression profiles, under single-core execution.
skills.name: single-core-execution-time-profiling
skills.search_text: single-core-execution-time-profiling Use when comparing runtime scalability of scRNA-seq rare-cell detection algorithms as input cell count grows from ~1k to tens of thousands of expression profiles, under single-core execution. The analysis goal is rare-cell detection accuracy (recall/precision) rather than runtime scaling — FiRE also returns rareness scores, but this skill only measures execution time Data is already small (fewer than a few thousand cells), where runtime differences among methods are not the bottleneck Multi-core or parallel timing is required — the benchmark protocol is explicitly single-core http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmarks single-core wall-clock execution time of rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) across nested cell-count subsets of a scRNA-seq dataset, from 1k up to ~68k profiles, to expose runtime scaling differences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07234-6
skills.summary: Benchmarks single-core wall-clock execution time of rare-cell detection methods (FiRE, LOF, RaceID, GiniClust) across nested cell-count subsets of a scRNA-seq dataset, from 1k up to ~68k profiles, to expose runtime scaling differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is rare-cell detection accuracy (recall/precision) rather than runtime scaling — FiRE also returns rareness scores, but this skill only measures execution time Data is already small (fewer than a few thousand cells), where runtime differences among methods are not the bottleneck Multi-core or parallel timing is required — the benchmark protocol is explicitly single-core

skills.description: Use when validating a scalability claim such as 'runtime scales linearly with the number of spatial locations': timing a method across a grid of downsampled dataset sizes (e.g. 200–3639 Visium spots, 1000–53208 Slide-seqV2 beads) on one processor core.
skills.name: single-core-performance-profiling
skills.search_text: single-core-performance-profiling Use when validating a scalability claim such as 'runtime scales linearly with the number of spatial locations': timing a method across a grid of downsampled dataset sizes (e.g. 200–3639 Visium spots, 1000–53208 Slide-seqV2 beads) on one processor core. When benchmarking multi-core or cluster performance — the paper's own non-single-core numbers (several hours on 10 processor cores on a high-performance compute cluster) reflect parallelized runs and are not comparable to single-thread scaling measurements When the goal is identifying spatially variable genes rather than characterizing computational scaling — use the standard nnSVG SVG-ranking workflow instead When profiling runtime as a function of gene count rather than spatial locations — note that runtime also depends on the number of genes, which confounds location-scaling measurements if the gene set varies Benchmarks the runtime of a method (here, nnSVG's gene-specific nearest-neighbor Gaussian process fitting) as a function of dataset size — downsampled numbers of spatial locations — executed on a single processor core and repeated 10 times per gene to obtain stable timing measurements, in order to verify the claimed linear scaling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z
skills.summary: Benchmarks the runtime of a method (here, nnSVG's gene-specific nearest-neighbor Gaussian process fitting) as a function of dataset size — downsampled numbers of spatial locations — executed on a single processor core and repeated 10 times per gene to obtain stable timing measurements, in order to verify the claimed linear scaling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When benchmarking multi-core or cluster performance — the paper's own non-single-core numbers (several hours on 10 processor cores on a high-performance compute cluster) reflect parallelized runs and are not comparable to single-thread scaling measurements When the goal is identifying spatially variable genes rather than characterizing computational scaling — use the standard nnSVG SVG-ranking workflow instead When profiling runtime as a function of gene count rather than spatial locations — note that runtime also depends on the number of genes, which confounds location-scaling measurements if the gene set varies

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires measuring and comparing classification/annotation runtime of single-cell label-transfer tools as dataset size scales, and elapsed wall-clock time and throughput are the primary metrics.
skills.name: single-cpu-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: single-cpu-runtime-profiling Use when a benchmark requires measuring and comparing classification/annotation runtime of single-cell label-transfer tools as dataset size scales, and elapsed wall-clock time and throughput are the primary metrics. The question under test is prediction accuracy or false positive rate rather than runtime — use the stratified 7:3 hold-out validation skill instead (50 repeats) rather than timing runs Input datasets are real experimental datasets with annotation labels rather than the simulated scaling matrices; timing comparisons across heterogeneous references confound dataset difficulty with speed Compute resources are multi-core or GPU-based and cannot be pinned to a single CPU, breaking the like-for-like runtime comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks the wall-clock classification runtime and throughput (cells per second) of single-cell annotation methods — SciBet vs. scmap and Seurat v3 — on simulated scRNA-seq datasets of increasing size (1,000 to 50,000 cells), under fixed single-CPU conditions, to demonstrate SciBet's order-of-magnitude speed advantage (~100,000 cells per second). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks the wall-clock classification runtime and throughput (cells per second) of single-cell annotation methods — SciBet vs. scmap and Seurat v3 — on simulated scRNA-seq datasets of increasing size (1,000 to 50,000 cells), under fixed single-CPU conditions, to demonstrate SciBet's order-of-magnitude speed advantage (~100,000 cells per second).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question under test is prediction accuracy or false positive rate rather than runtime — use the stratified 7:3 hold-out validation skill instead (50 repeats) rather than timing runs Input datasets are real experimental datasets with annotation labels rather than the simulated scaling matrices; timing comparisons across heterogeneous references confound dataset difficulty with speed Compute resources are multi-core or GPU-based and cannot be pinned to a single CPU, breaking the like-for-like runtime comparison

skills.description: Use when you need to detect, inspect and quantify known or novel isoforms for one gene at a time from long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Nanopore BAM), without prior knowledge of splice sites, and reproduce reported isoform counts.
skills.name: single-gene-splicing-analysis
skills.search_text: single-gene-splicing-analysis Use when you need to detect, inspect and quantify known or novel isoforms for one gene at a time from long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Nanopore BAM), without prior knowledge of splice sites, and reproduce reported isoform counts. The goal is whole-transcriptome de novo discovery across many samples rather than close inspection of one gene at a time — wf-transcriptomes (bambu/SQANTI3) is designed for that reference-guided multi-sample workflow. Input reads are short-read sequencing data or you already have an annotation with exon coordinates and splice sites, which VIsoQLR is not designed to require or exploit. Only abundant isoforms matter and manual curation is unnecessary — the default 2% threshold may suffice and lowering the threshold trades sensitivity for more (possibly noisy) isoforms. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Reproduce per-gene isoform detection and quantification with VIsoQLR on long-read sequencing data by mapping reads with GMAP, defining consensus exon coordinates (CECs) at a chosen read threshold (e.g. 3%), and extracting isoform read counts/abundances for single loci such as PAX6 and TP53. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Reproduce per-gene isoform detection and quantification with VIsoQLR on long-read sequencing data by mapping reads with GMAP, defining consensus exon coordinates (CECs) at a chosen read threshold (e.g. 3%), and extracting isoform read counts/abundances for single loci such as PAX6 and TP53.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is whole-transcriptome de novo discovery across many samples rather than close inspection of one gene at a time — wf-transcriptomes (bambu/SQANTI3) is designed for that reference-guided multi-sample workflow. Input reads are short-read sequencing data or you already have an annotation with exon coordinates and splice sites, which VIsoQLR is not designed to require or exploit. Only abundant isoforms matter and manual curation is unnecessary — the default 2% threshold may suffice and lowering the threshold trades sensitivity for more (possibly noisy) isoforms.

skills.description: Use when you must perform feature selection for scRNA-seq classification under low resources: an .h5ad/anndata gene-expression matrix is too large to train one model on all features, so per-subset weight scoring is needed to pick top-K genes.
skills.name: single-layer-neural-network-weight-scoring
skills.search_text: single-layer-neural-network-weight-scoring Use when you must perform feature selection for scRNA-seq classification under low resources: an .h5ad/anndata gene-expression matrix is too large to train one model on all features, so per-subset weight scoring is needed to pick top-K genes. You need feature attributions from a multi-layer model — use SHAP (shap_scorer) instead, since linear weight scoring only interprets the single-layer network's coefficients You need class-wise (per-class) top features rather than a global top-K ranking — use the classwise_abs or ClasswisePromoters selector instead of abs_mean The comparison tool you are using (e.g. scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) does not expose feature importances — weight-based top-K extraction is not applicable there http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 scaLR's feature-extraction mechanism: train a single-layer network (SequentialModel with weights_init_zero: True) on each feature subset, aggregate the class-wise weight matrices, and score every feature by the mean of absolute weights (LinearScorer + abs_mean selector) to rank and retain top-K features. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf243
skills.summary: scaLR's feature-extraction mechanism: train a single-layer network (SequentialModel with weights_init_zero: True) on each feature subset, aggregate the class-wise weight matrices, and score every feature by the mean of absolute weights (LinearScorer + abs_mean selector) to rank and retain top-K features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need feature attributions from a multi-layer model — use SHAP (shap_scorer) instead, since linear weight scoring only interprets the single-layer network's coefficients You need class-wise (per-class) top features rather than a global top-K ranking — use the classwise_abs or ClasswisePromoters selector instead of abs_mean The comparison tool you are using (e.g. scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, CellPLM) does not expose feature importances — weight-based top-K extraction is not applicable there

skills.description: Use when a 10X raw droplet count matrix (e.g. raw_feature_bc_matrix from fresh mouse brain nuclei) shows extranuclear RNA contamination and you must decide which droplets to keep versus remove as background.

skills.search_text: single-nucleus-rnaseq-ambient-rna-classification Use when a 10X raw droplet count matrix (e.g. raw_feature_bc_matrix from fresh mouse brain nuclei) shows extranuclear RNA contamination and you must decide which droplets to keep versus remove as background. Input is already a filtered expression matrix with low-quality droplets removed — classification needs the raw droplet count matrix. The data are scRNA-seq with little difference between background and cell profiles (e.g. PBMC scRNA-seq), where debris-score correlation with extranuclear contamination was less successful; use call_targets with clusters = 'debris' instead of a score threshold. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered expression matrix with low-quality droplets removed — classification needs the raw droplet count matrix. The data are scRNA-seq with little difference between background and cell profiles (e.g. PBMC scRNA-seq), where debris-score correlation with extranuclear contamination was less successful; use call_targets with clusters = 'debris' instead of a score threshold. skills.description: Use when you have a snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics) count matrix for a specific cell type — e.g. human prefrontal cortex microglia — and need a directed GRN covering the full transcriptome rather than a small pre-selected gene set.
skills.name: single-nucleus-rnaseq-data-processing
skills.search_text: single-nucleus-rnaseq-data-processing Use when you have a snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics) count matrix for a specific cell type — e.g. human prefrontal cortex microglia — and need a directed GRN covering the full transcriptome rather than a small pre-selected gene set. You need causal, directional regulatory mechanisms — the article's discussion notes 'the links between genes are not necessarily causal or directional'. You want spatial information explicitly used in network construction — SCING 'does not currently utilize the spatial information during network construction' even for spatial transcriptomics inputs. Your dataset is small or you only have a pre-selected set of a few thousand genes and cells; SCING is designed for full transcriptomes of large datasets, where its supercell and bagging strategy pays off. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Process single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) count matrices into robust gene regulatory networks using SCING, which combines supercell construction, bagging of 100 subsample GRNs via gradient boosting regressors, and conditional mutual information edge pruning to handle sparsity and cell-to-cell heterogeneity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107124
skills.summary: Process single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) count matrices into robust gene regulatory networks using SCING, which combines supercell construction, bagging of 100 subsample GRNs via gradient boosting regressors, and conditional mutual information edge pruning to handle sparsity and cell-to-cell heterogeneity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need causal, directional regulatory mechanisms — the article's discussion notes 'the links between genes are not necessarily causal or directional'. You want spatial information explicitly used in network construction — SCING 'does not currently utilize the spatial information during network construction' even for spatial transcriptomics inputs. Your dataset is small or you only have a pre-selected set of a few thousand genes and cells; SCING is designed for full transcriptomes of large datasets, where its supercell and bagging strategy pays off.

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples must be decomposed into cell-type proportions and a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference with cellType and SubjectName labels is available for some individuals (e.g., the 8 paired DLPFC individuals), especially under known single-cell vs. bulk technical variation.
skills.name: single-nucleus-rnaseq-decomposition
skills.search_text: single-nucleus-rnaseq-decomposition Use when bulk RNA-seq samples must be decomposed into cell-type proportions and a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference with cellType and SubjectName labels is available for some individuals (e.g., the 8 paired DLPFC individuals), especially under known single-cell vs. bulk technical variation. No reference expression profile is available (no single-cell data) — use BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition (BisqueMarker) with known marker genes instead, noting it yields relative abundances not comparable across cell types. There is known significant bias in the single-cell measurements, such as severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest, since Bisque's estimates reflect proportions as reported by the single-cell technology used for the reference. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates cell-type proportions in bulk RNA-seq using a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference via BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition, which learns gene-specific bulk expression transformations (SupervisedTransformBulk) to correct for technical differences between single-nucleus and bulk chemistries. This is the reference-based mode of Bisque, benchmarked on the DLPFC dataset against CIBERSORT, BSEQ-sc, and MuSiC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15816-6
skills.summary: Estimates cell-type proportions in bulk RNA-seq using a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference via BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition, which learns gene-specific bulk expression transformations (SupervisedTransformBulk) to correct for technical differences between single-nucleus and bulk chemistries. This is the reference-based mode of Bisque, benchmarked on the DLPFC dataset against CIBERSORT, BSEQ-sc, and MuSiC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reference expression profile is available (no single-cell data) — use BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition (BisqueMarker) with known marker genes instead, noting it yields relative abundances not comparable across cell types. There is known significant bias in the single-cell measurements, such as severe underrepresentation of a cell type of interest, since Bisque's estimates reflect proportions as reported by the single-cell technology used for the reference.

skills.description: Use when converting a bulk RNA-seq gene x sample matrix (human gene symbols as row names, non-negative normalized values) into sample-normalized reaction activity scores (MRAS) that feed METAFlux's compute_flux step.
skills.name: single-sample-transcriptomic-normalization
skills.search_text: single-sample-transcriptomic-normalization Use when converting a bulk RNA-seq gene x sample matrix (human gene symbols as row names, non-negative normalized values) into sample-normalized reaction activity scores (MRAS) that feed METAFlux's compute_flux step. skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a flux or reaction score matrix — apply compute_flux directly instead of recomputing MRAS Input is single-cell data — use the calculate_avg_exp / compute_sc_flux community workflow rather than bulk single-sample MRAS normalization The expression matrix contains raw counts or negative entries (e.g. from batch correction) — normalize/transform first, since MRAS expects non-negative normalized values

skills.description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq counts (h5ad AnnData) must be scored against a two-part UP/DN .gmt signature with a ranked, single-sample method, especially when sparsity blurs signal and neighbor-graph smoothing is an option.
skills.name: singlesample-gsea-scoring
skills.search_text: singlesample-gsea-scoring Use when per-cell scRNA-seq counts (h5ad AnnData) must be scored against a two-part UP/DN .gmt signature with a ranked, single-sample method, especially when sparsity blurs signal and neighbor-graph smoothing is an option. The input is already aggregated bulk expression — the nearest-neighbor smoothing and per-cell ranked scoring target sparse single-cell data (mini-pseudobulk profiles per cell). You need an unranked score such as mean_z, robust_std, average_score, median_score, or summed_up, which the README recommends for raw counts rather than rank-ordered data. There is no meaningful grouping structure to build the neighbor graph within (groupby), e.g. too few cells per group to support recompute_neighbors. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores single cells with ssGSEA, a single-sample GSEA method operating on per-cell ranked expression, inside gssnng's score_cells.with_gene_sets workflow (method_params={'omega': 0.75}). Applied to nearest-neighbor-graph smoothed Scanpy AnnData, mini-pseudobulk profiles raise spinal-injury endothelial AUC discrimination from 0.69 (unsmoothed) to 0.8 (smoothed). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Scores single cells with ssGSEA, a single-sample GSEA method operating on per-cell ranked expression, inside gssnng's score_cells.with_gene_sets workflow (method_params={'omega': 0.75}). Applied to nearest-neighbor-graph smoothed Scanpy AnnData, mini-pseudobulk profiles raise spinal-injury endothelial AUC discrimination from 0.69 (unsmoothed) to 0.8 (smoothed).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already aggregated bulk expression — the nearest-neighbor smoothing and per-cell ranked scoring target sparse single-cell data (mini-pseudobulk profiles per cell). You need an unranked score such as mean_z, robust_std, average_score, median_score, or summed_up, which the README recommends for raw counts rather than rank-ordered data. There is no meaningful grouping structure to build the neighbor graph within (groupby), e.g. too few cells per group to support recompute_neighbors.

skills.description: Use when processing Slide-seq (or other sub-cellular-spot, image-free) ST data where no nucleus segmentation is possible and each spot's cell count must be estimated before cell-type mapping or gene decomposition.
skills.name: singlet-doublet-classification-slideseq-spots
skills.search_text: singlet-doublet-classification-slideseq-spots Use when processing Slide-seq (or other sub-cellular-spot, image-free) ST data where no nucleus segmentation is possible and each spot's cell count must be estimated before cell-type mapping or gene decomposition. Image-based ST data (Visium, MERFISH) with a paired histology or DAPI image — use true nucleus segmentation instead, since Step 1 nucleus segmentation serves as the building block when images are available. Spots larger than ~two nuclei (e.g., Visium's 55 μm spots often contain multiple cells), where the at-most-two-cells assumption is invalid and full deconvolution methods like Cell2location or CARD are more appropriate. Unlabeled or unpaired scRNA-seq references, since RCTD requires cell-type-labeled reference profiles with platform-effect normalization. Replaces image-based nucleus segmentation for Spot-based ST platforms lacking histology (Slide-seq V2 10 μm spots) with an RCTD-inspired singlet/doublet classification, deciding whether one or two cells co-exist per spot so downstream cell type identification and gene expression decomposition can proceed at single-cell resolution. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Replaces image-based nucleus segmentation for Spot-based ST platforms lacking histology (Slide-seq V2 10 μm spots) with an RCTD-inspired singlet/doublet classification, deciding whether one or two cells co-exist per spot so downstream cell type identification and gene expression decomposition can proceed at single-cell resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Image-based ST data (Visium, MERFISH) with a paired histology or DAPI image — use true nucleus segmentation instead, since Step 1 nucleus segmentation serves as the building block when images are available. Spots larger than ~two nuclei (e.g., Visium's 55 μm spots often contain multiple cells), where the at-most-two-cells assumption is invalid and full deconvolution methods like Cell2location or CARD are more appropriate. Unlabeled or unpaired scRNA-seq references, since RCTD requires cell-type-labeled reference profiles with platform-effect normalization.

skills.description: Use when a slingshot trajectory object (sds) with multiple lineages is available and you need each cell's lineage-membership probabilities as input to condiments' fateSelectionTest for differential fate selection.
skills.name: slingshot-curve-weight-extraction
skills.search_text: slingshot-curve-weight-extraction Use when a slingshot trajectory object (sds) with multiple lineages is available and you need each cell's lineage-membership probabilities as input to condiments' fateSelectionTest for differential fate selection. The question is whether the trajectory topology itself differs between conditions — run the topologyTest (Step 1) instead. The question is whether cells progress at different rates along the same lineage (pseudotime distribution differences) — use progressionTest (Step 2a) rather than fate selection. No trajectory has been inferred yet (raw counts without a fitted slingshot object) — curve weights do not exist until slingshot lineages are fitted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Extracts per-cell lineage-membership probabilities (curve weights) from a fitted slingshot trajectory so they can be fed to the condiments fateSelectionTest, which tests whether lineage weight distributions differ between conditions (Step 2b, differential fate selection). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44823-0
skills.summary: Extracts per-cell lineage-membership probabilities (curve weights) from a fitted slingshot trajectory so they can be fed to the condiments fateSelectionTest, which tests whether lineage weight distributions differ between conditions (Step 2b, differential fate selection).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is whether the trajectory topology itself differs between conditions — run the topologyTest (Step 1) instead. The question is whether cells progress at different rates along the same lineage (pseudotime distribution differences) — use progressionTest (Step 2a) rather than fate selection. No trajectory has been inferred yet (raw counts without a fitted slingshot object) — curve weights do not exist until slingshot lineages are fitted.

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq matrix plus cell cluster labels must be ordered along a continuous differentiation dynamic — after an embedding choice (dimension reduction + HVG selection) has been evaluated, e.g. by Escort scoring > 0.
skills.name: slingshot-pseudotime-trajectory-fitting
skills.search_text: slingshot-pseudotime-trajectory-fitting Use when a normalized scRNA-seq matrix plus cell cluster labels must be ordered along a continuous differentiation dynamic — after an embedding choice (dimension reduction + HVG selection) has been evaluated, e.g. by Escort scoring > 0. The candidate embedding is disconnected — Escort classifies disconnected embeddings as immediately not recommended for trajectory inference Escort's first-step assessment indicates no trajectory signal exists (disconnected clusters or homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal), so fitting any pseudotime trajectory is inappropriate The trajectory method requires higher-dimensional or non-2D representations (e.g., RNA velocity-derived reductions) — Escort/Skills here only consider two-dimensional representations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits Slingshot lineage trajectories and pseudotime on a pre-evaluated low-dimensional embedding of single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., the Escort-recommended embedding), using cluster labels as the skeleton. In the hypertrophic chondrocyte case study (GSE190616), this recovered two biologically meaningful lineages where the original paper's embedding gave three, only one of which was interpretable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae216
skills.summary: Fits Slingshot lineage trajectories and pseudotime on a pre-evaluated low-dimensional embedding of single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., the Escort-recommended embedding), using cluster labels as the skeleton. In the hypertrophic chondrocyte case study (GSE190616), this recovered two biologically meaningful lineages where the original paper's embedding gave three, only one of which was interpretable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate embedding is disconnected — Escort classifies disconnected embeddings as immediately not recommended for trajectory inference Escort's first-step assessment indicates no trajectory signal exists (disconnected clusters or homogeneous cells lacking trajectory signal), so fitting any pseudotime trajectory is inappropriate The trajectory method requires higher-dimensional or non-2D representations (e.g., RNA velocity-derived reductions) — Escort/Skills here only consider two-dimensional representations

skills.description: Use when single-cell data is expected to follow a continuous developmental or bifurcating trajectory and you need lineage/pseudotime inference, or when validating that filtering steps (e.g. doublet removal) did not distort branch structure.
skills.name: slingshot-trajectory-reconstruction
skills.search_text: slingshot-trajectory-reconstruction Use when single-cell data is expected to follow a continuous developmental or bifurcating trajectory and you need lineage/pseudotime inference, or when validating that filtering steps (e.g. doublet removal) did not distort branch structure. Data has no expected continuous or bifurcating developmental structure (e.g. discrete immune cell types) — cluster-based MST lineage inference would impose a pseudo-trajectory Input is already a completed trajectory/pseudotime object and the goal is only downstream differential expression along it The question is doublet-detection accuracy itself (AUC/precision) rather than downstream trajectory integrity — score-based benchmarks are more direct http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct developmental trajectories and pseudotime from scRNA-seq data with Slingshot's cluster-based minimum spanning tree lineage inference, and use the resulting branch structure as a sensitive readout of data quality — e.g. detecting whether doublet removal preserved a bifurcating trajectory or introduced spurious branches. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-022-03476-9
skills.summary: Reconstruct developmental trajectories and pseudotime from scRNA-seq data with Slingshot's cluster-based minimum spanning tree lineage inference, and use the resulting branch structure as a sensitive readout of data quality — e.g. detecting whether doublet removal preserved a bifurcating trajectory or introduced spurious branches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has no expected continuous or bifurcating developmental structure (e.g. discrete immune cell types) — cluster-based MST lineage inference would impose a pseudo-trajectory Input is already a completed trajectory/pseudotime object and the goal is only downstream differential expression along it The question is doublet-detection accuracy itself (AUC/precision) rather than downstream trajectory integrity — score-based benchmarks are more direct

skills.description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data contains multiple branching developmental lineages with unknown endpoints, and you need to reconstruct trajectories unsupervised from a reduced-dimension representation rather than supervised from known progenitor/terminal markers.
skills.name: slingshot-unsupervised-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
skills.search_text: slingshot-unsupervised-pseudotime-trajectory-inference Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data contains multiple branching developmental lineages with unknown endpoints, and you need to reconstruct trajectories unsupervised from a reduced-dimension representation rather than supervised from known progenitor/terminal markers. When a supervised trajectory is appropriate (known root cluster and expected endpoints can be given to Slingshot directly) — unsupervised mode is only needed when endpoints are unknown When the low-dimensional representation is derived from unwanted technical variation that is not accounted for: 'there is no guarantee that the low-dimensional signal extracted by ZINB-WaVE is biologically relevant', so trajectory inference on such factors can be misleading When a PCA-based representation is relied on without verification — in the olfactory epithelium contrast, unsupervised PCA-based inference misses the mSUS endpoint http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run Slingshot in unsupervised mode on a low-dimensional representation (here, the first 50 ZINB-WaVE factors) with cluster labels from RSEC to infer minimum spanning tree lineage structure and identify terminal (endpoint) clusters, without supplying a known root or trajectory beforehand. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02554-5
skills.summary: Run Slingshot in unsupervised mode on a low-dimensional representation (here, the first 50 ZINB-WaVE factors) with cluster labels from RSEC to infer minimum spanning tree lineage structure and identify terminal (endpoint) clusters, without supplying a known root or trajectory beforehand.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a supervised trajectory is appropriate (known root cluster and expected endpoints can be given to Slingshot directly) — unsupervised mode is only needed when endpoints are unknown When the low-dimensional representation is derived from unwanted technical variation that is not accounted for: 'there is no guarantee that the low-dimensional signal extracted by ZINB-WaVE is biologically relevant', so trajectory inference on such factors can be misleading When a PCA-based representation is relied on without verification — in the olfactory epithelium contrast, unsupervised PCA-based inference misses the mSUS endpoint

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether an lncRNA/coding-potential classifier handles transcripts with small ORFs, by benchmarking it against established methods on the species-specific sORF test sets from the LncCat study.
skills.name: small-orf-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: small-orf-benchmark-evaluation Use when you need to test whether an lncRNA/coding-potential classifier handles transcripts with small ORFs, by benchmarking it against established methods on the species-specific sORF test sets from the LncCat study. Input transcripts contain long ORFs only — use the five-species long-ORF benchmark datasets instead, where LncCat's improvements are 1.90%–21.50% rather than sORF-specific The target species lacks sufficient annotation to build a species model (the article notes species may lack annotations, making it impossible to build models for all species) The task is functional annotation of sORF-translated peptides — the study explicitly defers collecting sORF peptide sequences to future work http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Benchmark protocol for evaluating whether lncRNA identification methods underperform on transcripts with small ORFs (sORFs), by running LncCat and eight comparison methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) on human-, mouse-, and zebrafish-sORF test datasets and computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.02.012
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol for evaluating whether lncRNA identification methods underperform on transcripts with small ORFs (sORFs), by running LncCat and eight comparison methods (CPAT, CNCI, PLEK, CPC2, LncFinder, CPPred, mRNN, RNAsamba) on human-, mouse-, and zebrafish-sORF test datasets and computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input transcripts contain long ORFs only — use the five-species long-ORF benchmark datasets instead, where LncCat's improvements are 1.90%–21.50% rather than sORF-specific The target species lacks sufficient annotation to build a species model (the article notes species may lack annotations, making it impossible to build models for all species) The task is functional annotation of sORF-translated peptides — the study explicitly defers collecting sORF peptide sequences to future work

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq reads must be assigned to features by ordered precedence — e.g. separating canonical miRNAs from 5'-shifted isomiRs or partial-overlap fragments — rather than counted by simple overlap.
skills.name: small-rna-hierarchical-classification-rules
skills.search_text: small-rna-hierarchical-classification-rules Use when small RNA-seq reads must be assigned to features by ordered precedence — e.g. separating canonical miRNAs from 5'-shifted isomiRs or partial-overlap fragments — rather than counted by simple overlap. Input is already a feature count table — no rule-based assignment of reads is needed Genome- or transcript-level alignment quantification without variant/class discrimination is sufficient (tiny-count does this too, but the rule CSV hierarchy is unnecessary) Annotations are discontinuous features with multi-valued Parent tags, which the README notes are not yet supported http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Configure tiny-count selection rules to hierarchically classify small RNA-seq reads into distinct small RNA classes and variants (e.g. canonical miRNAs vs isomiRs) with single-nucleotide precision, using ordered rule rows in a selection-rules CSV. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: Configure tiny-count selection rules to hierarchically classify small RNA-seq reads into distinct small RNA classes and variants (e.g. canonical miRNAs vs isomiRs) with single-nucleotide precision, using ordered rule rows in a selection-rules CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature count table — no rule-based assignment of reads is needed Genome- or transcript-level alignment quantification without variant/class discrimination is sufficient (tiny-count does this too, but the rule CSV hierarchy is unnecessary) Annotations are discontinuous features with multi-valued Parent tags, which the README notes are not yet supported

skills.description: Use when assigning demultiplexed small RNA-seq reads (FASTQ) to features from GFF3/GFF2/GTF annotations, especially when loci produce multiple small RNA classes (piRNA vs siRNA) or when miRNA/isomiR variants must be distinguished by single-nucleotide precision.
skills.name: small-rna-read-assignment
skills.search_text: small-rna-read-assignment Use when assigning demultiplexed small RNA-seq reads (FASTQ) to features from GFF3/GFF2/GTF annotations, especially when loci produce multiple small RNA classes (piRNA vs siRNA) or when miRNA/isomiR variants must be distinguished by single-nucleotide precision. FASTQ input is not demultiplexed — the README requires 'Files must be demultiplexed' before tiny-count can process it Feature annotation lacks the required column 9 ID/gene_id/Parent tags or uses multi-valued Parent tags, which tiny-count does not yet support The task is differential expression analysis of already-computed count matrices rather than read-level feature assignment — that is a downstream tinyRNA step Assign and quantify small RNA-seq reads to reference features using tiny-count's interval-overlap machinery (a custom Cython StepVector replacing HTSeq's, with ~30% average runtime reduction on the read-assignment workload), resolving distinct small RNA classes such as piRNAs and siRNAs from the same locus with single-nucleotide precision. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: Assign and quantify small RNA-seq reads to reference features using tiny-count's interval-overlap machinery (a custom Cython StepVector replacing HTSeq's, with ~30% average runtime reduction on the read-assignment workload), resolving distinct small RNA classes such as piRNAs and siRNAs from the same locus with single-nucleotide precision.
skills.when_to_use_negative: FASTQ input is not demultiplexed — the README requires 'Files must be demultiplexed' before tiny-count can process it Feature annotation lacks the required column 9 ID/gene_id/Parent tags or uses multi-valued Parent tags, which tiny-count does not yet support The task is differential expression analysis of already-computed count matrices rather than read-level feature assignment — that is a downstream tinyRNA step

skills.description: Use when STAR-aligned BAM files from small RNA-seq (e.g. hg38-mapped qualified reads) need to be converted into per-molecule read counts for six small RNA classes, or when deciding whether a read mapping to multiple loci/RNA types should be counted once or per RNA.
skills.name: small-rna-read-count-quantification
skills.search_text: small-rna-read-count-quantification Use when STAR-aligned BAM files from small RNA-seq (e.g. hg38-mapped qualified reads) need to be converted into per-molecule read counts for six small RNA classes, or when deciding whether a read mapping to multiple loci/RNA types should be counted once or per RNA. The reads were not mapped to the human genome — those qualified unmapped reads belong to the Microbe module (BLAST against the UCSC nt database), not Annotation. The goal is raw adapter-trimmed/quality-filtered read production or genome alignment — use the QC (-qc) and Alignment (-aln) modules upstream first. Differential expression or count-matrix aggregation across samples is needed directly — use the Function module (-fun -fd / -fm) on the annotation count outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantify small RNA molecules from human genome-mapped small RNA-seq reads by annotating them against multiple pre-built reference databases (miRBase, piRNABank/piRBase/piRNACluster, gtRNAdb, GENCODE release 27, circBase) and outputting per-RNA-type read count tables. This is the core COMPSRA Annotation module behavior for profiling miRNA, piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA and circRNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Quantify small RNA molecules from human genome-mapped small RNA-seq reads by annotating them against multiple pre-built reference databases (miRBase, piRNABank/piRBase/piRNACluster, gtRNAdb, GENCODE release 27, circBase) and outputting per-RNA-type read count tables. This is the core COMPSRA Annotation module behavior for profiling miRNA, piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA and circRNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reads were not mapped to the human genome — those qualified unmapped reads belong to the Microbe module (BLAST against the UCSC nt database), not Annotation. The goal is raw adapter-trimmed/quality-filtered read production or genome alignment — use the QC (-qc) and Alignment (-aln) modules upstream first. Differential expression or count-matrix aggregation across samples is needed directly — use the Function module (-fun -fd / -fm) on the annotation count outputs.

skills.description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ/FASTQ files (e.g. SRR5049781) must be adapter-trimmed, normalized, length-filtered, and mapped to a reference before phasiRNA phase prediction with PhasiHunter.
skills.name: small-rna-read-preprocessing-and-mapping
skills.search_text: small-rna-read-preprocessing-and-mapping Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ/FASTQ files (e.g. SRR5049781) must be adapter-trimmed, normalized, length-filtered, and mapped to a reference before phasiRNA phase prediction with PhasiHunter. Input is already a processed .map file or phase-module output — rerunning preprocessing would double-filter reads Reads fall outside the 19-25 nt window after trimming, or the goal is long-RNA/mRNA alignment rather than sRNA mapping with up to 10 hits http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Preprocess raw small RNA-seq reads with PhasiHunter's preprocess module (adapter trimming via Trim_galore, normalization, length/abundance filtering, Bowtie mapping) to produce the .map files required for phasiRNA/PHAS loci prediction against cdna, gdna, or flnc references. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Preprocess raw small RNA-seq reads with PhasiHunter's preprocess module (adapter trimming via Trim_galore, normalization, length/abundance filtering, Bowtie mapping) to produce the .map files required for phasiRNA/PHAS loci prediction against cdna, gdna, or flnc references.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed .map file or phase-module output — rerunning preprocessing would double-filter reads Reads fall outside the 19-25 nt window after trimming, or the goal is long-RNA/mRNA alignment rather than sRNA mapping with up to 10 hits

skills.description: Use when you have STAR-aligned BAM files from human small RNA-seq data (e.g. hg38/hg19) and need to classify reads into miRNA, piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA and circRNA classes with per-molecule counts.
skills.name: small-rna-reference-annotation
skills.search_text: small-rna-reference-annotation Use when you have STAR-aligned BAM files from human small RNA-seq data (e.g. hg38/hg19) and need to classify reads into miRNA, piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA and circRNA classes with per-molecule counts. Input reads are not yet mapped to a reference genome — COMPSRA's Annotation module expects the STAR Alignment module's BAM output, not raw FASTQ You need single-assignment (one RNA type per read) classification — COMPSRA deliberately provides all possible annotations and assigns counts to each overlapping small RNA Target organism is non-human and non-rat without pre-built databases — prebuilt small RNA databases cover human hg19/hg38 (and miRNA for Rattus norvegicus rno5/rno6 as of v1.0.1) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Annotate human genome-mapped small RNA-seq reads against multiple pre-built small RNA reference databases (miRBase, piRNABank/piRBase/piRNACluster, gtRNAdb, GENCODE, circBase) within COMPSRA's Annotation module, producing per-RNA-type read count tables rather than forcing a single RNA-type assignment per read. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Annotate human genome-mapped small RNA-seq reads against multiple pre-built small RNA reference databases (miRBase, piRNABank/piRBase/piRNACluster, gtRNAdb, GENCODE, circBase) within COMPSRA's Annotation module, producing per-RNA-type read count tables rather than forcing a single RNA-type assignment per read.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not yet mapped to a reference genome — COMPSRA's Annotation module expects the STAR Alignment module's BAM output, not raw FASTQ You need single-assignment (one RNA type per read) classification — COMPSRA deliberately provides all possible annotations and assigns counts to each overlapping small RNA Target organism is non-human and non-rat without pre-built databases — prebuilt small RNA databases cover human hg19/hg38 (and miRNA for Rattus norvegicus rno5/rno6 as of v1.0.1)

skills.description: Use when you have SRA accession numbers or FASTQ files of small RNA sequencing datasets and a reference genome plus annotation for a plant species, and you need to predict miRNA precursors and select credible candidates genome-wide.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-mirna-prediction
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-mirna-prediction Use when you have SRA accession numbers or FASTQ files of small RNA sequencing datasets and a reference genome plus annotation for a plant species, and you need to predict miRNA precursors and select credible candidates genome-wide. The species has no reference genome — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences and ignores reads that do not map to the reference The goal is downstream enrichment analysis (e.g., GO annotation or miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparative analysis of the selected miRNAs — the framework has limited downstream analysis capability Only a single small dataset with prior confident annotation exists and no genome-wide candidate selection is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Predict plant miRNA precursors from sRNA-Seq datasets using the miRNAPredict tool of the Galaxy-based iwa-miRNA framework, then merge predictions with database-annotated precursors (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) via miRNATranslate and select promising candidates with high-throughput criteria and a one-class SVM in miRNASelection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Predict plant miRNA precursors from sRNA-Seq datasets using the miRNAPredict tool of the Galaxy-based iwa-miRNA framework, then merge predictions with database-annotated precursors (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) via miRNATranslate and select promising candidates with high-throughput criteria and a one-class SVM in miRNASelection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The species has no reference genome — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences and ignores reads that do not map to the reference The goal is downstream enrichment analysis (e.g., GO annotation or miRNA set enrichment) or cross-species comparative analysis of the selected miRNAs — the framework has limited downstream analysis capability Only a single small dataset with prior confident annotation exists and no genome-wide candidate selection is needed

skills.description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., 50 nt serum reads) must be processed end-to-end into per-sample RNA-type count profiles, including case-vs-control differential expression on RNAs <200 nt.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-pipeline-execution Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., 50 nt serum reads) must be processed end-to-end into per-sample RNA-type count profiles, including case-vs-control differential expression on RNAs <200 nt. Input is already an annotated count matrix or feature table — use the Function module alone (-fun -fm) rather than re-running QC/Alignment/Annotation Reads are long (>200 nt) RNA-seq data; COMPSRA targets small RNAs (<200 nt) and its QC trimming and small RNA reference databases assume short reads No local Java/STAR environment and only a web workflow is acceptable — the authors note web-based tools like exceRpt require uploading original sequencing files, which is un-workable for big data; COMPSRA is a stand-alone alternative requiring local installation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Execute the COMPSRA v1.0 stand-alone Java pipeline for small RNA-seq data, running its five modules (Quality Control, Alignment, Annotation, Microbe, Function) to identify and quantify miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA and fragmental microbial RNA from FASTQ inputs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Execute the COMPSRA v1.0 stand-alone Java pipeline for small RNA-seq data, running its five modules (Quality Control, Alignment, Annotation, Microbe, Function) to identify and quantify miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA and fragmental microbial RNA from FASTQ inputs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an annotated count matrix or feature table — use the Function module alone (-fun -fm) rather than re-running QC/Alignment/Annotation Reads are long (>200 nt) RNA-seq data; COMPSRA targets small RNAs (<200 nt) and its QC trimming and small RNA reference databases assume short reads No local Java/STAR environment and only a web workflow is acceptable — the authors note web-based tools like exceRpt require uploading original sequencing files, which is un-workable for big data; COMPSRA is a stand-alone alternative requiring local installation

skills.description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ files (demultiplexed, optionally .gz) must be reduced to unique sequences with counts before genomic alignment and feature counting in the tinyRNA workflow, or when adapter-derived degenerate bases need trimming.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-preprocessing
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-preprocessing Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ files (demultiplexed, optionally .gz) must be reduced to unique sequences with counts before genomic alignment and feature counting in the tinyRNA workflow, or when adapter-derived degenerate bases need trimming. Input reads are already collapsed (each FASTA record already carries a count field) — re-collapsing would misattribute counts Input is a count matrix or feature table rather than raw sequencing reads Analysis is not small RNA-seq within the tinyRNA context and requires per-read identities downstream of counting http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Collapses demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads into unique-sequence FASTA records whose identifiers embed per-sequence occurrence counts (FASTX-Toolkit collapse convention), producing collapsed.fa that feeds the tinyRNA alignment and counting steps while drastically reducing resource demands. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad065
skills.summary: Collapses demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads into unique-sequence FASTA records whose identifiers embed per-sequence occurrence counts (FASTX-Toolkit collapse convention), producing collapsed.fa that feeds the tinyRNA alignment and counting steps while drastically reducing resource demands.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already collapsed (each FASTA record already carries a count field) — re-collapsing would misattribute counts Input is a count matrix or feature table rather than raw sequencing reads Analysis is not small RNA-seq within the tinyRNA context and requires per-read identities downstream of counting

skills.description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. 50 nt reads from serum small RNA kits like NEXTflex) need adapter removal, ligation-base trimming, and low-quality read filtering before genome alignment or small RNA annotation.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-quality-control
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-quality-control Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. 50 nt reads from serum small RNA kits like NEXTflex) need adapter removal, ligation-base trimming, and low-quality read filtering before genome alignment or small RNA annotation. Input is not raw small RNA-seq FASTQ (e.g. already aligned BAM/SAM files should go straight to the Annotation module) The library kit does not leave randomized bases at ligation junctions or uses a different adapter than TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG Reads are longer than 200 nt and not small RNAs — COMPSRA targets small RNAs (<200 nt) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quality-control routine for small RNA-seq FASTQ data as implemented in the COMPSRA QC module: trims the 3' adapter and randomized ligation bases, applies Phred-score-based read/head/tail filtering, and groups qualified reads by length interval before downstream alignment and annotation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Quality-control routine for small RNA-seq FASTQ data as implemented in the COMPSRA QC module: trims the 3' adapter and randomized ligation bases, applies Phred-score-based read/head/tail filtering, and groups qualified reads by length interval before downstream alignment and annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw small RNA-seq FASTQ (e.g. already aligned BAM/SAM files should go straight to the Annotation module) The library kit does not leave randomized bases at ligation junctions or uses a different adapter than TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG Reads are longer than 200 nt and not small RNAs — COMPSRA targets small RNAs (<200 nt)

skills.description: Use when quality- and adapter-trimmed single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be uniquely aligned to a customized genome index to identify small RNA loci (e.g., tncRNAs) while avoiding ambiguous multi-mapping to repetitive regions.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-read-alignment
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-read-alignment Use when quality- and adapter-trimmed single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be uniquely aligned to a customized genome index to identify small RNA loci (e.g., tncRNAs) while avoiding ambiguous multi-mapping to repetitive regions. Reads are paired-end or not quality-filtered and adapter-trimmed (e.g., not processed with Trim Galore v0.6.6) — the pipeline expects processed single-end small RNA reads Genome FASTA headers do not follow the '>chr[Num]', '>chrMt', '>chrPt' convention required by the tncRNA-Toolkit for nuclear/organellar separation The goal is to map reads to the native genome without masking tRNA regions — unmasked mapping would inflate ambiguous non-tRNA assignments the pipeline explicitly avoids http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 A Bowtie1-based short-read alignment strategy for mapping quality-filtered plant sRNA-seq reads to an artificial genome (masked tRNA regions plus 50 nt leader/trailer as artificial chromosomes) so tRNA-derived reads can be uniquely and error-tolerantly assigned for tncRNA discovery. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: A Bowtie1-based short-read alignment strategy for mapping quality-filtered plant sRNA-seq reads to an artificial genome (masked tRNA regions plus 50 nt leader/trailer as artificial chromosomes) so tRNA-derived reads can be uniquely and error-tolerantly assigned for tncRNA discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are paired-end or not quality-filtered and adapter-trimmed (e.g., not processed with Trim Galore v0.6.6) — the pipeline expects processed single-end small RNA reads Genome FASTA headers do not follow the '>chr[Num]', '>chrMt', '>chrPt' convention required by the tncRNA-Toolkit for nuclear/organellar separation The goal is to map reads to the native genome without masking tRNA regions — unmasked mapping would inflate ambiguous non-tRNA assignments the pipeline explicitly avoids

skills.description: Use when processing single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads (14–50 nt) from plant samples and you need to classify them into tRF/tRNA-half subtypes and reconcile per-species totals against published reference counts.
skills.name: small-rna-seq-read-classification-summarization
skills.search_text: small-rna-seq-read-classification-summarization Use when processing single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads (14–50 nt) from plant samples and you need to classify them into tRF/tRNA-half subtypes and reconcile per-species totals against published reference counts. Reads are paired-end or from non-plant species — the toolkit and its bowtie/HAMR settings were designed for single-end plant sRNA-seq The input is already a classified/annotated tncRNA count table — only the summarization step (pandas aggregation into species_tncRNA_summary.csv) is needed, not reclassification Reads contain tRNA post-transcriptional modifications that block alignment — the paper notes conventional RNA-seq modification biases; tRNA-seq would be required instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classifies quality-filtered small RNA-seq reads into tRNA-derived non-coding RNA (tncRNA) subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) using the tncRNA Toolkit, then aggregates per-sample classification output into per-species counts of unique reads and loci with pandas. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Classifies quality-filtered small RNA-seq reads into tRNA-derived non-coding RNA (tncRNA) subtypes (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) using the tncRNA Toolkit, then aggregates per-sample classification output into per-species counts of unique reads and loci with pandas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are paired-end or from non-plant species — the toolkit and its bowtie/HAMR settings were designed for single-end plant sRNA-seq The input is already a classified/annotated tncRNA count table — only the summarization step (pandas aggregation into species_tncRNA_summary.csv) is needed, not reclassification Reads contain tRNA post-transcriptional modifications that block alignment — the paper notes conventional RNA-seq modification biases; tRNA-seq would be required instead

skills.search_text: small-rna-target-prediction Use when you have a set of conserved plant small RNAs (e.g. tRF-5/tRF-3 series 18–25 nt) and need to predict their putative mRNA targets and test whether targets are enriched in specific biological processes. skills.description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq with smFISH spatial data to impute and validate spatial expression patterns for genes measured in one modality but not the other, or to benchmark diagonal integration methods on held-out spatial gene predictions.
skills.name: smfish-gene-imputation-evaluation
skills.search_text: smfish-gene-imputation-evaluation Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq with smFISH spatial data to impute and validate spatial expression patterns for genes measured in one modality but not the other, or to benchmark diagonal integration methods on held-out spatial gene predictions. Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections (e.g. electrophysiology vs gene expression), which scConfluence's rIOT cost matrix requires The task is paired/matched multiomic integration rather than diagonal (unpaired) integration, which scConfluence does not address Data contain very rare cell populations that are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches, degrading rIOT alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Reproduces the scConfluence scRNA-smFISH diagonal integration of the mouse somatosensory cortex, imputes spatial expression for genes absent from the smFISH panel (Scgn, Synpr, Olah), and evaluates imputation quality against five baselines via Spearman correlations on 11 held-out smFISH gene groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Reproduces the scConfluence scRNA-smFISH diagonal integration of the mouse somatosensory cortex, imputes spatial expression for genes absent from the smFISH panel (Scgn, Synpr, Olah), and evaluates imputation quality against five baselines via Spearman correlations on 11 held-out smFISH gene groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Modalities lack cross-modality feature connections (e.g. electrophysiology vs gene expression), which scConfluence's rIOT cost matrix requires The task is paired/matched multiomic integration rather than diagonal (unpaired) integration, which scConfluence does not address Data contain very rare cell populations that are unlikely to be co-sampled in mini-batches, degrading rIOT alignment

skills.search_text: smoke-test-training-on-citeseq-data Use when implementing or reconstructing the MarkerMap marker-selection module and you need to verify it trains end-to-end on a real scRNA-seq/CITE-seq AnnData object and returns exactly k marker indices. You only need marker-selection benchmarks against other methods (RankCorr, PERSIST, COSG) rather than a reconstruction-fidelity smoke test of the module itself. The data is spatial transcriptomics or non-count expression — this smoke test targets the CITE-seq AnnData pipeline described in the article. You need a method with no training loop (e.g. RandomBaseline, which simply selects k markers at random). http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A minimal end-to-end training harness for the MarkerMap VAE-based marker selector on the CITE-seq dataset (CITEseq.h5ad), verifying that the model instantiates, trains, and returns exactly k markers via differentiable Gumbel-Softmax sampling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00339-3
skills.summary: A minimal end-to-end training harness for the MarkerMap VAE-based marker selector on the CITE-seq dataset (CITEseq.h5ad), verifying that the model instantiates, trains, and returns exactly k markers via differentiable Gumbel-Softmax sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need marker-selection benchmarks against other methods (RankCorr, PERSIST, COSG) rather than a reconstruction-fidelity smoke test of the module itself. The data is spatial transcriptomics or non-count expression — this smoke test targets the CITE-seq AnnData pipeline described in the article.
