skills.search_text: smote-class-imbalance-oversampling Use when preparing disease/stress and control tab-separated expression matrices for BoostDiff and one condition has far fewer samples than the other (below the recommended ~30 per condition or below BoostDiff's min_samples=15 default). When both conditions already have ≥30 samples each — the README recommends this as sufficient input, and SMOTE would only add synthetic noise When the number of samples per condition would fall below BoostDiff's min_samples default of 15 even after oversampling is deemed inappropriate for very low-count conditions, or when applying single-sample/single-replicate pilot data where synthetic interpolation is unreliable When the differential network inference method is not tree-based (e.g. correlation-only network inference), since class balance mainly matters for bootstrapped, sample-resampling learners like BoostDiff's n_subsamples=20 ensemble http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Balances two-condition expression matrices by oversampling the minority class with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) so BoostDiff receives ≥30–48 samples per condition (e.g. B. subtilis stress vs control from GSE27219), since the AdaBoost ensemble of differential trees requires sufficient samples in each class. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbae034
skills.summary: Balances two-condition expression matrices by oversampling the minority class with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) so BoostDiff receives ≥30–48 samples per condition (e.g. B. subtilis stress vs control from GSE27219), since the AdaBoost ensemble of differential trees requires sufficient samples in each class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When both conditions already have ≥30 samples each — the README recommends this as sufficient input, and SMOTE would only add synthetic noise When the number of samples per condition would fall below BoostDiff's min_samples default of 15 even after oversampling is deemed inappropriate for very low-count conditions, or when applying single-sample/single-replicate pilot data where synthetic interpolation is unreliable When the differential network inference method is not tree-based (e.g. correlation-only network inference), since class balance mainly matters for bootstrapped, sample-resampling learners like BoostDiff's n_subsamples=20 ensemble

skills.description: Use when raw 10x 3'-end FASTQ/BAM scRNA-seq inputs must be quantified for 3'UTR isoforms via the scUTRquant Snakemake pipeline, requiring a config.yaml with target, tech, strand, whitelist, and min_umis settings plus a sample_sheet.csv.
skills.name: snakemake-pipeline-configuration
skills.search_text: snakemake-pipeline-configuration Use when raw 10x 3'-end FASTQ/BAM scRNA-seq inputs must be quantified for 3'UTR isoforms via the scUTRquant Snakemake pipeline, requiring a config.yaml with target, tech, strand, whitelist, and min_umis settings plus a sample_sheet.csv. The input is already a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix (e.g. a Cell Ranger filtered HDF5), not raw FASTQ/BAM reads needing pseudoalignment The data are full-length or 5'-end scRNA-seq libraries rather than 3'-end tag-based libraries, since scUTRquant is built for 3'-end tag data De novo mapping of mRNA 3' end cleavage sites is needed — most 10x reads do not span cleavage sites, and cleavage-site calling is handled by separate UTRome pipelines (hcl-utrome, mca-utrome) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure and run the scUTRquant Snakemake pipeline (Conda or Singularity mode) by assembling a config.yaml and sample_sheet.csv so that kallisto bus pseudoaligns 10x 3'-end reads against a prebuilt UTRome index and bustools corrects barcodes, producing SingleCellExperiment count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Configure and run the scUTRquant Snakemake pipeline (Conda or Singularity mode) by assembling a config.yaml and sample_sheet.csv so that kallisto bus pseudoaligns 10x 3'-end reads against a prebuilt UTRome index and bustools corrects barcodes, producing SingleCellExperiment count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix (e.g. a Cell Ranger filtered HDF5), not raw FASTQ/BAM reads needing pseudoalignment The data are full-length or 5'-end scRNA-seq libraries rather than 3'-end tag-based libraries, since scUTRquant is built for 3'-end tag data De novo mapping of mRNA 3' end cleavage sites is needed — most 10x reads do not span cleavage sites, and cleavage-site calling is handled by separate UTRome pipelines (hcl-utrome, mca-utrome)

skills.description: Use when a multi-person 10X scRNA-seq mixture (possorted_genome_bam + barcodes.tsv) must be separated into per-contributor cell clusters and genotyped VCFs via a reproducible Snakemake pipeline.
skills.name: snakemake-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: snakemake-pipeline-execution Use when a multi-person 10X scRNA-seq mixture (possorted_genome_bam + barcodes.tsv) must be separated into per-contributor cell clusters and genotyped VCFs via a reproducible Snakemake pipeline. Input is not 10X scRNA-seq output (possorted_genome_bam + barcodes.tsv) — e.g., bulk sequencing, VCFs, or other single-cell formats will not match the Snakefile inputs. The biological mixture contains non-living or fixed cells — the 10X platform used by this pipeline requires live cells for successful genetic separation. The goal is de novo SNP calling alone without cell-level mixture deconvolution — a standalone variant caller (e.g., freebayes directly) is the wrong-level tool here since this skill targets per-contributor cell clustering. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Executes the de-goulash Snakemake workflow inside the geniderasmusmc/de-goulash Docker image to deconvolve 10X scRNA-seq mixtures via two iterations of FreeBayes SNP calling, cell merging, and UMAP/k-means clustering, followed by a separate Snakefile_analysis step for identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Executes the de-goulash Snakemake workflow inside the geniderasmusmc/de-goulash Docker image to deconvolve 10X scRNA-seq mixtures via two iterations of FreeBayes SNP calling, cell merging, and UMAP/k-means clustering, followed by a separate Snakefile_analysis step for identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not 10X scRNA-seq output (possorted_genome_bam + barcodes.tsv) — e.g., bulk sequencing, VCFs, or other single-cell formats will not match the Snakefile inputs. The biological mixture contains non-living or fixed cells — the 10X platform used by this pipeline requires live cells for successful genetic separation. The goal is de novo SNP calling alone without cell-level mixture deconvolution — a standalone variant caller (e.g., freebayes directly) is the wrong-level tool here since this skill targets per-contributor cell clustering.

skills.search_text: snakemake-workflow-configuration Use when you need to run the circlehunter ecDNA-calling pipeline on one or more ATAC-Seq samples (simulated, cell-line, or negative-control) via its Snakemake workflow and YAML configuration. The analysis goal is WGS-based ecDNA detection requiring copy-number input (e.g., AmpliconArchitect, JaBbA, LINX), not ATAC-Seq-based ecDNA calling Input is single-cell ATAC-Seq data — the article notes its application to single-cell ATAC-Seq has yet to be explored You only need gene set enrichment analysis (GSEApy), which is a separate tool not part of this Snakemake ecDNA workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure and execute the circlehunter Snakemake pipeline, which identifies ecDNA from ATAC-Seq data, by installing the conda/mamba environment and driving the workflow from a YAML sample config file. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0
skills.summary: Configure and execute the circlehunter Snakemake pipeline, which identifies ecDNA from ATAC-Seq data, by installing the conda/mamba environment and driving the workflow from a YAML sample config file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is WGS-based ecDNA detection requiring copy-number input (e.g., AmpliconArchitect, JaBbA, LINX), not ATAC-Seq-based ecDNA calling Input is single-cell ATAC-Seq data — the article notes its application to single-cell ATAC-Seq has yet to be explored You only need gene set enrichment analysis (GSEApy), which is a separate tool not part of this Snakemake ecDNA workflow

skills.description: Use when the goal is to run neoantigen prediction end-to-end from raw FASTQ (WES and/or RNA-seq) and produce per-sample predicted neoepitope output tables under results/<sample>/prioritization/.

skills.search_text: snakemake-workflow-configuration-and-execution Use when the goal is to run neoantigen prediction end-to-end from raw FASTQ (WES and/or RNA-seq) and produce per-sample predicted neoepitope output tables under results/<sample>/prioritization/. Input is already a list of variants or VCFs and only the IEDB/netMHCpan epitope prediction step is needed — the full raw-data workflow is unnecessary Reads are long reads (PacBio/Nanopore); fastp and the short-read alignment stack are designed for Illumina short reads (NovaSeq/MGI) No conda/mamba or Snakemake ≥9.0.0 environment is available, since installation depends on environment.yml and the Snakemake engine Configure and execute the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow (requires snakemake ≥9.0.0) so that raw WES/RNA-seq FASTQ data is processed end-to-end — from fastp pre-processing through HLA typing, variant calling, and IEDB epitope prediction — into per-sample neoepitope tables. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Configure and execute the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow (requires snakemake ≥9.0.0) so that raw WES/RNA-seq FASTQ data is processed end-to-end — from fastp pre-processing through HLA typing, variant calling, and IEDB epitope prediction — into per-sample neoepitope tables.

skills.description: Use when SnapCCESS variational-autoencoder embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA/ADT) have already been generated and the goal is to partition cells into clusters and quantify clustering quality against known cell-type labels.
skills.name: snapccess-embedding-partitioning
skills.search_text: snapccess-embedding-partitioning Use when SnapCCESS variational-autoencoder embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA/ADT) have already been generated and the goal is to partition cells into clusters and quantify clustering quality against known cell-type labels. Raw multimodal count matrices have not yet been converted into SnapCCESS ensemble embeddings — run the embedding-generation skill first Single-modality data with no cell-type reference labels available, since ARI/NMI evaluation against reference labels cannot be performed The task is choosing optimal hyperparameters for generating embeddings — the tutorial explicitly does not recommend best parameters and defers to the paper http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Couples SnapCCESS-generated multimodal single-cell embeddings with downstream clustering algorithms (k-means, CiteFuse spectral clustering, SIMLR) to generate consensus cell clusters, and evaluates them against reference cell-type labels using ARI and NMI across ensemble sizes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad382
skills.summary: Couples SnapCCESS-generated multimodal single-cell embeddings with downstream clustering algorithms (k-means, CiteFuse spectral clustering, SIMLR) to generate consensus cell clusters, and evaluates them against reference cell-type labels using ARI and NMI across ensemble sizes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw multimodal count matrices have not yet been converted into SnapCCESS ensemble embeddings — run the embedding-generation skill first Single-modality data with no cell-type reference labels available, since ARI/NMI evaluation against reference labels cannot be performed The task is choosing optimal hyperparameters for generating embeddings — the tutorial explicitly does not recommend best parameters and defers to the paper

skills.description: Use when classifying snATAC-seq nuclei with Pollock: convert accessibility to gene activity, then train or apply the snATACseq_generalized or disease-specific BRCA/CCRCC/GBM modules.
skills.name: snatac-gene-activity-representation
skills.search_text: snatac-gene-activity-representation Use when classifying snATAC-seq nuclei with Pollock: convert accessibility to gene activity, then train or apply the snATACseq_generalized or disease-specific BRCA/CCRCC/GBM modules. Input is a peak-by-cell or fragment-file snATAC-seq matrix that has not been converted to gene activity — Pollock's snATAC-seq modules expect the gene activity representation Input is scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq — use the corresponding scRNAseq_* or snRNAseq_* pretrained modules instead of the snATAC-seq gene activity modules The goal is a disease-specific model for BRCA, CCRCC or GBM with no cross-cancer generalization benchmark — training a merged generalized module adds unnecessary complexity Represents single-nucleus ATAC-seq data as a gene activity matrix so Pollock's VAE classifiers can predict cell types in the same feature space as scRNA-seq, enabling training of generalized pan-cancer snATAC-seq modules (BRCA, CCRCC, GBM) and benchmarking them against disease-specific models. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Represents single-nucleus ATAC-seq data as a gene activity matrix so Pollock's VAE classifiers can predict cell types in the same feature space as scRNA-seq, enabling training of generalized pan-cancer snATAC-seq modules (BRCA, CCRCC, GBM) and benchmarking them against disease-specific models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a peak-by-cell or fragment-file snATAC-seq matrix that has not been converted to gene activity — Pollock's snATAC-seq modules expect the gene activity representation Input is scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq — use the corresponding scRNAseq_* or snRNAseq_* pretrained modules instead of the snATAC-seq gene activity modules The goal is a disease-specific model for BRCA, CCRCC or GBM with no cross-cancer generalization benchmark — training a merged generalized module adds unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when a pooled snATAC-seq candidate enhancer BED (e.g. 286,777 heart enhancers) has per-cell-type activity columns and you need cell-type-resolved enhancer–gene links with a generalized ABC score.
skills.name: snatac-seq-cell-type-activity-matrix-handling
skills.search_text: snatac-seq-cell-type-activity-matrix-handling Use when a pooled snATAC-seq candidate enhancer BED (e.g. 286,777 heart enhancers) has per-cell-type activity columns and you need cell-type-resolved enhancer–gene links with a generalized ABC score. When the goal is TF affinity computation and per-gene TF score summarisation rather than enhancer–gene ABC-scored interactions (use STARE's TF-affinity part instead of the separate ABC-scoring mode). When enhancer activity comes from bulk assays rather than per-cell-type snATAC-seq accessibility columns — the cell-type-resolved setup with one -n activity column per cell type would not apply. When genome build or Hi-C reference differs from the Fulco et al. hg19 average matrix and its matching enhancer coordinates — coordinate system must be consistent across BED, GTF and contact files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Run cell-type-specific enhancer–gene interaction scoring on a pooled single-nucleus ATAC-seq candidate enhancer set by supplying each cell type's accessibility column as the enhancer activity input to the generalized (adapted) ABC model in STARE, then quantify how many gABC-scored interactions arise per cell type and how much they overlap across cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad062
skills.summary: Run cell-type-specific enhancer–gene interaction scoring on a pooled single-nucleus ATAC-seq candidate enhancer set by supplying each cell type's accessibility column as the enhancer activity input to the generalized (adapted) ABC model in STARE, then quantify how many gABC-scored interactions arise per cell type and how much they overlap across cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is TF affinity computation and per-gene TF score summarisation rather than enhancer–gene ABC-scored interactions (use STARE's TF-affinity part instead of the separate ABC-scoring mode). When enhancer activity comes from bulk assays rather than per-cell-type snATAC-seq accessibility columns — the cell-type-resolved setup with one -n activity column per cell type would not apply. When genome build or Hi-C reference differs from the Fulco et al. hg19 average matrix and its matching enhancer coordinates — coordinate system must be consistent across BED, GTF and contact files.

skills.description: Use when the input is snATAC-seq data expressed as gene activity (not peak calls) and the goal is cell type classification or benchmarking against Pollock's snATACseq pretrained modules.
skills.name: snatac-seq-gene-activity-classification
skills.search_text: snatac-seq-gene-activity-classification Use when the input is snATAC-seq data expressed as gene activity (not peak calls) and the goal is cell type classification or benchmarking against Pollock's snATACseq pretrained modules. Input is single-cell peak-level accessibility (fragment files, peak matrices) rather than gene activity — the snATACseq modules are trained with snATAC-seq data represented as gene activity Input expression matrix is already normalized/log-transformed — the CLI requires raw, unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts Input is scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq — use the scRNAseq_* or snRNAseq_* pretrained modules instead of the snATACseq gene activity modules http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train or apply Pollock's VAE-based cell type classifiers on snATAC-seq data represented as gene activity, using the disease-specific snATACseq modules and the snATAC-seq gene activity benchmarking datasets from Zenodo record 5895221. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac028
skills.summary: Train or apply Pollock's VAE-based cell type classifiers on snATAC-seq data represented as gene activity, using the disease-specific snATACseq modules and the snATAC-seq gene activity benchmarking datasets from Zenodo record 5895221.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell peak-level accessibility (fragment files, peak matrices) rather than gene activity — the snATACseq modules are trained with snATAC-seq data represented as gene activity Input expression matrix is already normalized/log-transformed — the CLI requires raw, unnormalized counts in .X or @assays$RNA@counts Input is scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq — use the scRNAseq_* or snRNAseq_* pretrained modules instead of the snATACseq gene activity modules

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object must be prepared with an SNN graph and UMAP embedding as the spatial substrate for Census's cluster-and-contour label stabilization before hierarchical annotation.
skills.name: snn-graph-construction
skills.search_text: snn-graph-construction Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object must be prepared with an SNN graph and UMAP embedding as the spatial substrate for Census's cluster-and-contour label stabilization before hierarchical annotation. The input object has not yet been normalized, scaled, and PCA-reduced — RunUMAP/FindNeighbors on unprocessed counts will not yield a meaningful SNN graph The environment has Seurat v5 installed and the workflow requires Census, since Census explicitly requires Seurat version 4 loaded first The task is plain clustering/visualization with no downstream Census label-stabilization — the contour/propagation loop is not needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Constructs a shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph and UMAP embedding from a processed Seurat object so that Census's label-stabilizing algorithm can propagate confident binary predictions within UMAP SNN clusters and compute MASS-based prediction contours. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad714
skills.summary: Constructs a shared nearest-neighbor (SNN) graph and UMAP embedding from a processed Seurat object so that Census's label-stabilizing algorithm can propagate confident binary predictions within UMAP SNN clusters and compute MASS-based prediction contours.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input object has not yet been normalized, scaled, and PCA-reduced — RunUMAP/FindNeighbors on unprocessed counts will not yield a meaningful SNN graph The environment has Seurat v5 installed and the workflow requires Census, since Census explicitly requires Seurat version 4 loaded first The task is plain clustering/visualization with no downstream Census label-stabilization — the contour/propagation loop is not needed

skills.description: Use when a CellChat object with an inferred communication probability network is available and you need to identify coordinated outgoing/incoming signaling patterns among cell groups or classify signaling pathways into functional groups.
skills.name: snn-graph-manifold-learning
skills.search_text: snn-graph-manifold-learning Use when a CellChat object with an inferred communication probability network is available and you need to identify coordinated outgoing/incoming signaling patterns among cell groups or classify signaling pathways into functional groups. The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data without cell clustering or an inferred communication probability network — CellChat requires cell clustering and computeCommunProb results first. The goal is differential abundance or cell-state annotation rather than pattern recognition over an already-inferred intercellular communication network. Only a single ligand-receptor interaction pair is of interest — the SNN/NMF manifold machinery is designed for network- and pathway-level patterns, not individual interactions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 CellChat's manifold-learning approach that builds a shared-nearest-neighbor (SNN) similarity network over cell groups or signaling pathways, smooths the similarity matrix, embeds it with UMAP, and performs NMF to recover outgoing/incoming communication patterns and functional pathway groups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9
skills.summary: CellChat's manifold-learning approach that builds a shared-nearest-neighbor (SNN) similarity network over cell groups or signaling pathways, smooths the similarity matrix, embeds it with UMAP, and performs NMF to recover outgoing/incoming communication patterns and functional pathway groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data without cell clustering or an inferred communication probability network — CellChat requires cell clustering and computeCommunProb results first. The goal is differential abundance or cell-state annotation rather than pattern recognition over an already-inferred intercellular communication network. Only a single ligand-receptor interaction pair is of interest — the SNN/NMF manifold machinery is designed for network- and pathway-level patterns, not individual interactions.

skills.description: Use when you have a 10x scRNA-seq BAM (possorted_genome_bam.bam) plus barcodes.tsv from a multi-person mixture and need to assign each cell to its contributing individual based on genotype SNPs.
skills.name: snp-based-cell-clustering
skills.search_text: snp-based-cell-clustering Use when you have a 10x scRNA-seq BAM (possorted_genome_bam.bam) plus barcodes.tsv from a multi-person mixture and need to assign each cell to its contributing individual based on genotype SNPs. Cells are not live (the 10x Genomics scRNA-seq platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation) Mixture contains fewer than ~150 cells without deeper sequencing — this has not been empirically confirmed Biological mixtures other than blood — transferability to other tissue types is not yet demonstrated http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Two-iteration SNP-genotyping-and-clustering workflow (de-goulash) that separates cells from multi-person scRNA-seq mixtures by contributor: first using mtDNA-SNPs (freebayes over MT regions), then genome-wide SNPs, followed by UMAP-based clustering of cells into per-individual clusters. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: Two-iteration SNP-genotyping-and-clustering workflow (de-goulash) that separates cells from multi-person scRNA-seq mixtures by contributor: first using mtDNA-SNPs (freebayes over MT regions), then genome-wide SNPs, followed by UMAP-based clustering of cells into per-individual clusters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells are not live (the 10x Genomics scRNA-seq platform requires live cells for successful genetic separation) Mixture contains fewer than ~150 cells without deeper sequencing — this has not been empirically confirmed Biological mixtures other than blood — transferability to other tissue types is not yet demonstrated

skills.description: Use when 10x scRNA-seq BAM + barcodes.tsv from a multi-person mixture must be separated into per-individual cell clusters and each cluster genotyped/identified (sex, ancestry, LR-based ID) for forensic purposes.
skills.name: snp-based-mixture-deconvolution
skills.search_text: snp-based-mixture-deconvolution Use when 10x scRNA-seq BAM + barcodes.tsv from a multi-person mixture must be separated into per-individual cell clusters and each cluster genotyped/identified (sex, ancestry, LR-based ID) for forensic purposes. The mixture contains non-living or fixed cells — the 10X Genomics scRNA-seq platform used here requires live cells for successful genetic separation. Mixtures of more than nine individuals or fewer than ~150 cells with deeper sequencing were only hypothesized, not empirically confirmed — treat results as speculative beyond the validated 2–9 person blood mixtures. Input is bulk (not single-cell) DNA profiling data — this skill depends on per-cell SNP extraction from 10x scRNA-seq BAM/barcodes files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 De-goulash deconvolves multi-person biological mixtures (2–9 blood contributors, ratios up to 1:60) by calling SNPs per cell from 10x scRNA-seq data, clustering cells by contributing individual, and performing forensic characterization and individual identification against a WES/1000G reference. Rationale: separating the mixture by contributor first converts downstream DNA analysis to a single-source problem. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04557-z
skills.summary: De-goulash deconvolves multi-person biological mixtures (2–9 blood contributors, ratios up to 1:60) by calling SNPs per cell from 10x scRNA-seq data, clustering cells by contributing individual, and performing forensic characterization and individual identification against a WES/1000G reference. Rationale: separating the mixture by contributor first converts downstream DNA analysis to a single-source problem.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mixture contains non-living or fixed cells — the 10X Genomics scRNA-seq platform used here requires live cells for successful genetic separation. Mixtures of more than nine individuals or fewer than ~150 cells with deeper sequencing were only hypothesized, not empirically confirmed — treat results as speculative beyond the validated 2–9 person blood mixtures. Input is bulk (not single-cell) DNA profiling data — this skill depends on per-cell SNP extraction from 10x scRNA-seq BAM/barcodes files.

skills.description: Use when curated SNP positions are given on the Gmax_a1.v1 assembly but downstream analyses (e.g., gene proximity or coexpression module assignment) require Gmax_a2.v1 coordinates, and Soybase VCFs exist for both assemblies.
skills.name: snp-coordinate-liftover-between-genome-assemblies
skills.search_text: snp-coordinate-liftover-between-genome-assemblies Use when curated SNP positions are given on the Gmax_a1.v1 assembly but downstream analyses (e.g., gene proximity or coexpression module assignment) require Gmax_a2.v1 coordinates, and Soybase VCFs exist for both assemblies. The input SNP coordinates are already reported on the target assembly (Gmax_a2.v1) and no conversion is needed. VCF files are not available for both assemblies (a1.v1 and a2.v1), so allele-concordance anchoring cannot be performed. The goal is exploring the soybean-fungal-pathogen coexpression network via SoyFungiGCN rather than harmonizing SNP coordinates. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A procedure for converting manually curated resistance-associated SNP coordinates from an older soybean genome assembly (Gmax_a1.v1) to a newer one (Gmax_a2.v1), using the paired Soybase .vcf files for both assemblies to anchor each site by chromosome, position, and REF/ALT allele concordance, yielding a unified SNP coordinate set for downstream candidate gene analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: A procedure for converting manually curated resistance-associated SNP coordinates from an older soybean genome assembly (Gmax_a1.v1) to a newer one (Gmax_a2.v1), using the paired Soybase .vcf files for both assemblies to anchor each site by chromosome, position, and REF/ALT allele concordance, yielding a unified SNP coordinate set for downstream candidate gene analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input SNP coordinates are already reported on the target assembly (Gmax_a2.v1) and no conversion is needed. VCF files are not available for both assemblies (a1.v1 and a2.v1), so allele-concordance anchoring cannot be performed. The goal is exploring the soybean-fungal-pathogen coexpression network via SoyFungiGCN rather than harmonizing SNP coordinates.

skills.description: Use when re-running or reproducing the VADT filtering stage on per-tissue RNA-seq VCF files and you need to confirm the number of informative biallelic SNPs matches the published per-tissue counts before downstream ASE testing.
skills.name: snp-count-validation-against-published-results
skills.search_text: snp-count-validation-against-published-results Use when re-running or reproducing the VADT filtering stage on per-tissue RNA-seq VCF files and you need to confirm the number of informative biallelic SNPs matches the published per-tissue counts before downstream ASE testing. The goal is to call ASE itself rather than validate filtering counts — the downstream binomial test, Fisher's-method meta-analysis, and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (cutoff 0.05) stages of VADT are a separate skill Input VCFs were produced by a caller other than GATK HaplotypeCaller — the VADT README warns VCFs from other programs 'could potentially have some bugs' Variants are multiallelic or indels — they are removed by VADT's filters and cannot contribute to the informative SNP tally http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Validates a per-tissue ASE filtering pipeline by tallying the informative biallelic SNPs that survive VADT's variant- and sample-level filters and comparing the counts to the study's reported values (148,860 breast muscle, 217,628 abdominal fat, 155,875 liver; ~174,000 average). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Validates a per-tissue ASE filtering pipeline by tallying the informative biallelic SNPs that survive VADT's variant- and sample-level filters and comparing the counts to the study's reported values (148,860 breast muscle, 217,628 abdominal fat, 155,875 liver; ~174,000 average).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to call ASE itself rather than validate filtering counts — the downstream binomial test, Fisher's-method meta-analysis, and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (cutoff 0.05) stages of VADT are a separate skill Input VCFs were produced by a caller other than GATK HaplotypeCaller — the VADT README warns VCFs from other programs 'could potentially have some bugs' Variants are multiallelic or indels — they are removed by VADT's filters and cannot contribute to the informative SNP tally

skills.description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or extend runtime benchmarks of SNP pattern miners — i.e. measuring how running time scales with number of samples n and SNPs per gene l across HOGImine (k=1, k=2), SiNIMin, and FastCMH.
skills.name: snp-dataset-subsampling
skills.search_text: snp-dataset-subsampling Use when the goal is to reproduce or extend runtime benchmarks of SNP pattern miners — i.e. measuring how running time scales with number of samples n and SNPs per gene l across HOGImine (k=1, k=2), SiNIMin, and FastCMH. The goal is biological discovery rather than runtime benchmarking — then run HOGImine on the full dataset with permutations (p > 0) instead of timing subsampled runs The pattern output of the two tools is the deliverable; subsampling only controls (n, l) for scaling experiments and does not by itself validate statistical power Data uses additive encoding or requires covariate conditioning — subsample construction must then respect the FastCMH covariate file format (cov.txt) and the SiNIMin mapping/edge files http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runtime benchmarking skill for SNP meta-marker mining: subsample a biobank (e.g. the athaliana avrRpm1 dataset) to vary sample count n and SNPs-per-gene l, then time HOGImine, SiNIMin, and FastCMH on identical inputs to reproduce the Figure 4 speedup comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Runtime benchmarking skill for SNP meta-marker mining: subsample a biobank (e.g. the athaliana avrRpm1 dataset) to vary sample count n and SNPs-per-gene l, then time HOGImine, SiNIMin, and FastCMH on identical inputs to reproduce the Figure 4 speedup comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is biological discovery rather than runtime benchmarking — then run HOGImine on the full dataset with permutations (p > 0) instead of timing subsampled runs The pattern output of the two tools is the deliverable; subsampling only controls (n, l) for scaling experiments and does not by itself validate statistical power Data uses additive encoding or requires covariate conditioning — subsample construction must then respect the FastCMH covariate file format (cov.txt) and the SiNIMin mapping/edge files

skills.description: Use when you have RNA-seq expression counts, SNP genotype data, a SNP-to-gene map, and sample metadata (including patientID) and need to test whether genotype effects on gene expression differ by infection condition.
skills.name: snp-gene-pair-interaction-testing
skills.search_text: snp-gene-pair-interaction-testing Use when you have RNA-seq expression counts, SNP genotype data, a SNP-to-gene map, and sample metadata (including patientID) and need to test whether genotype effects on gene expression differ by infection condition. You only need standard differential expression without SNP–gene interaction testing — plain kmFit (kimma_lm, kimma_lme, kimma_lmerel) is the appropriate entry point. No genotype data or SNP-to-gene map is available, so no eQTL model can be specified. Samples are unrelated and no kinship matrix exists; the kinship-covariance mixed model rationale does not apply (a simpler lm-style eQTL approach may suffice). http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Test expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) by fitting each SNP–gene pair with kimma's kmFit_eQTL as a linear mixed model containing a genotype-by-condition interaction term and a kinship covariance random effect, then calling significance at FDR < 0.05 via summarise_kmFit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad279
skills.summary: Test expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) by fitting each SNP–gene pair with kimma's kmFit_eQTL as a linear mixed model containing a genotype-by-condition interaction term and a kinship covariance random effect, then calling significance at FDR < 0.05 via summarise_kmFit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need standard differential expression without SNP–gene interaction testing — plain kmFit (kimma_lm, kimma_lme, kimma_lmerel) is the appropriate entry point. No genotype data or SNP-to-gene map is available, so no eQTL model can be specified. Samples are unrelated and no kinship matrix exists; the kinship-covariance mixed model rationale does not apply (a simpler lm-style eQTL approach may suffice).

skills.description: Use when you need to rank germplasm accessions by resistance-allele burden against a pathogen from VCF genotype data plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes, e.g. to reproduce top-5 resistant accession tables for C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, or P.
skills.name: snp-genotype-dosage-scoring
skills.search_text: snp-genotype-dosage-scoring Use when you need to rank germplasm accessions by resistance-allele burden against a pathogen from VCF genotype data plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes, e.g. to reproduce top-5 resistant accession tables for C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, or P. No VCF genotype data for the germplasm accessions is available (allelic dosages cannot be computed) No curated resistance-SNP effect-size table exists for the target pathogen (e.g., F. graminearum SNPs are absent from SoySNP50k, so prediction yields a no-call) Goal is phenotypic resistance assessment from disease-assay data rather than allele-count-based genotype scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Scores soybean USDA germplasm accessions for fungal-pathogen resistance by converting VCF genotype calls into allele dosages (S in {0,1,2}) at curated resistance SNP loci, weighting each dosage by pathogen-specific SNP effect sizes, normalizing by the maximum theoretical potential (sum of |effect sizes| x 2), and ranking accessions per pathogen. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Scores soybean USDA germplasm accessions for fungal-pathogen resistance by converting VCF genotype calls into allele dosages (S in {0,1,2}) at curated resistance SNP loci, weighting each dosage by pathogen-specific SNP effect sizes, normalizing by the maximum theoretical potential (sum of |effect sizes| x 2), and ranking accessions per pathogen.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No VCF genotype data for the germplasm accessions is available (allelic dosages cannot be computed) No curated resistance-SNP effect-size table exists for the target pathogen (e.g., F. graminearum SNPs are absent from SoySNP50k, so prediction yields a no-call) Goal is phenotypic resistance assessment from disease-assay data rather than allele-count-based genotype scoring

skills.description: Use when allele-specific expression analysis of F1 hybrid (e.g., CAST×B6) scRNA-Seq data requires a personalized diploid reference built from known strain SNPs/indels, so reads can align to both parental transcriptomes and multi-reads can be enumerated for EM-based weighted allocation.
skills.name: snp-informed-genome-reconstruction
skills.search_text: snp-informed-genome-reconstruction Use when allele-specific expression analysis of F1 hybrid (e.g., CAST×B6) scRNA-Seq data requires a personalized diploid reference built from known strain SNPs/indels, so reads can align to both parental transcriptomes and multi-reads can be enumerated for EM-based weighted allocation. The reference genome already matches the sample's strain (no strain-specific variants need incorporation) and a single-genome index suffices The dataset lacks phase-known parental strain variant calls, so a diploid transcriptome cannot be constructed The downstream analysis discards multi-reads entirely by design (unique-reads counting), for which a strain-informed diploid index is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstructs a strain-specific (e.g., CAST) genome by incorporating known SNPs and short indels into a reference genome with g2gtools, then builds a bowtie (v1.0.0) index of the phase-known diploid transcriptome. This enables allele-aware alignment of single-cell RNA-Seq reads from F1 hybrid (CAST×B6) cells so that both unique and multi-mapping reads can be assigned to parental alleles. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13099-0
skills.summary: Reconstructs a strain-specific (e.g., CAST) genome by incorporating known SNPs and short indels into a reference genome with g2gtools, then builds a bowtie (v1.0.0) index of the phase-known diploid transcriptome. This enables allele-aware alignment of single-cell RNA-Seq reads from F1 hybrid (CAST×B6) cells so that both unique and multi-mapping reads can be assigned to parental alleles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference genome already matches the sample's strain (no strain-specific variants need incorporation) and a single-genome index suffices The dataset lacks phase-known parental strain variant calls, so a diploid transcriptome cannot be constructed The downstream analysis discards multi-reads entirely by design (unique-reads counting), for which a strain-informed diploid index is unnecessary

skills.description: Use when you have a significant sQTL catalog (sqtlseeker2-nf FDR < 0.05) and need a variant control set to test whether sQTLs are enriched in splice sites, chromatin marks, or GWAS LD hits.
skills.name: snp-null-set-matching-maf-and-location-bin
skills.search_text: snp-null-set-matching-maf-and-location-bin Use when you have a significant sQTL catalog (sqtlseeker2-nf FDR < 0.05) and need a variant control set to test whether sQTLs are enriched in splice sites, chromatin marks, or GWAS LD hits. When testing enrichment of eQTLs or other QTL classes without an equivalent matched null scheme — the matching bins are defined on the sQTL within-gene location distribution When variants cannot be intersected with the annotation tracks in a common genome build, since GENCODE v19 and the enrichment tracks assume consistent coordinates When a model-based functional enrichment framework (e.g. fgwas on GWAS summary statistics with >= ~20 independent loci) is already appropriate — the matched-null contingency approach is a simpler catalog-level alternative http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates MAF- and within-gene-location-bin-matched non-sQTL null variant sets so functional enrichment of sQTLs (splice sites, H3K36me3, GWAS LD hits) can be tested with Fisher's exact tests rather than against unmatched genome-wide SNPs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Generates MAF- and within-gene-location-bin-matched non-sQTL null variant sets so functional enrichment of sQTLs (splice sites, H3K36me3, GWAS LD hits) can be tested with Fisher's exact tests rather than against unmatched genome-wide SNPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing enrichment of eQTLs or other QTL classes without an equivalent matched null scheme — the matching bins are defined on the sQTL within-gene location distribution When variants cannot be intersected with the annotation tracks in a common genome build, since GENCODE v19 and the enrichment tracks assume consistent coordinates When a model-based functional enrichment framework (e.g. fgwas on GWAS summary statistics with >= ~20 independent loci) is already appropriate — the matched-null contingency approach is a simpler catalog-level alternative

skills.description: Use when per-tissue significant ASE SNP coordinate sets are available and the goal is to convert SNP-level ASE calls into gene-level ASE calls, or to quantify cross-tissue overlap at the gene rather than SNP level.
skills.name: snp-to-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: snp-to-gene-mapping Use when per-tissue significant ASE SNP coordinate sets are available and the goal is to convert SNP-level ASE calls into gene-level ASE calls, or to quantify cross-tissue overlap at the gene rather than SNP level. When only SNP-level overlap statistics are needed and gene-level aggregation is not the goal — Bedtools coordinate intersection alone suffices When SNPs cannot be confidently assigned to genes (e.g., intergenic SNPs lacking VEP consequence annotation), since aggregation to ASE genes would be unreliable For cross-build comparisons — the paper notes mapping issues with muscle tissue samples likely due to the current genome build, and repeated the analysis with the Gallus_gallus_6.0 GTF http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps tissue-specific significant ASE SNPs (detected by VADT meta-analysis) to their associated genes using Ensembl VEP consequence annotations, then aggregates SNP-level overlaps to the gene level to reveal higher cross-tissue concordance (20.1% shared ASE genes vs 3.7% shared ASE SNPs). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Maps tissue-specific significant ASE SNPs (detected by VADT meta-analysis) to their associated genes using Ensembl VEP consequence annotations, then aggregates SNP-level overlaps to the gene level to reveal higher cross-tissue concordance (20.1% shared ASE genes vs 3.7% shared ASE SNPs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only SNP-level overlap statistics are needed and gene-level aggregation is not the goal — Bedtools coordinate intersection alone suffices When SNPs cannot be confidently assigned to genes (e.g., intergenic SNPs lacking VEP consequence annotation), since aggregation to ASE genes would be unreliable For cross-build comparisons — the paper notes mapping issues with muscle tissue samples likely due to the current genome build, and repeated the analysis with the Gallus_gallus_6.0 GTF

skills.description: Use when starting a scRank analysis from raw snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq count matrices plus cell-type metadata, and you need a ScRank S4 object encoding species, cell-type labels, and a known drug-target gene before network reconstruction.
skills.name: snrna-seq-data-loading-and-object-construction
skills.search_text: snrna-seq-data-loading-and-object-construction Use when starting a scRank analysis from raw snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq count matrices plus cell-type metadata, and you need a ScRank S4 object encoding species, cell-type labels, and a known drug-target gene before network reconstruction. Data is bulk RNA-seq or lacks per-cell cell-type labels — scRank needs cell-type-resolved single-cell expression to build cell-type-specific GRNs The drug target gene is unknown or multi-target without tailored methodology — scRank models perturbation of a single target gene node, and multi-target extension is only preliminary (Figure S17) A ranked drug-responsive cell type is already available and the task is downstream modularization or visualization (use init_mod/plot_net/plot_dim instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Load single-nucleus RNA-seq count matrices with cell-type metadata (e.g., the untreated MDD dorsolateral prefrontal cortex dataset GSE144136) into a Seurat object and wrap it in an scRank S4 object via CreateScRank, specifying species, cell-type label column, drug target gene, and perturbation type. This is the mandatory entry point for the scRank target-perturbed GRN pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Load single-nucleus RNA-seq count matrices with cell-type metadata (e.g., the untreated MDD dorsolateral prefrontal cortex dataset GSE144136) into a Seurat object and wrap it in an scRank S4 object via CreateScRank, specifying species, cell-type label column, drug target gene, and perturbation type. This is the mandatory entry point for the scRank target-perturbed GRN pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is bulk RNA-seq or lacks per-cell cell-type labels — scRank needs cell-type-resolved single-cell expression to build cell-type-specific GRNs The drug target gene is unknown or multi-target without tailored methodology — scRank models perturbation of a single target gene node, and multi-target extension is only preliminary (Figure S17) A ranked drug-responsive cell type is already available and the task is downstream modularization or visualization (use init_mod/plot_net/plot_dim instead)

skills.description: Use when raw 10X droplet snRNA-seq data (e.g. CellRanger output from fresh/frozen nuclei preparations) contains ambient extranuclear RNA contamination and droplets must be classified as nuclear vs background before downstream clustering or cell-type calling.
skills.name: snrna-seq-droplet-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: snrna-seq-droplet-quality-assessment Use when raw 10X droplet snRNA-seq data (e.g. CellRanger output from fresh/frozen nuclei preparations) contains ambient extranuclear RNA contamination and droplets must be classified as nuclear vs background before downstream clustering or cell-type calling. Data are clean single-cell (scRNA-seq) droplet data where background/cell profiles differ little — DIEM's debris-score correlation with extranuclear contamination was less successful on PBMC scRNA-seq; prefer call_targets(clusters = "debris") instead of the score threshold There are few or no genes enriched in the background distribution — the debris score will likely be inaccurate since scoring relies on estimating debris-enriched genes Comparing debris scores across independent samples for integration — scores are normalized within-sample and cannot be assumed to be on the same scale if extranuclear RNA distributions differ http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assesses and filters droplets in droplet-based single-nucleus RNA-seq data by estimating per-droplet debris (ambient extranuclear RNA) contamination scores with the semi-supervised EM classifier DIEM, then calling nuclear (target) droplets. Replaces hard read/UMI/gene cutoffs, which lose nuclear droplets and retain debris, with a likelihood-based multinomial expression model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Assesses and filters droplets in droplet-based single-nucleus RNA-seq data by estimating per-droplet debris (ambient extranuclear RNA) contamination scores with the semi-supervised EM classifier DIEM, then calling nuclear (target) droplets. Replaces hard read/UMI/gene cutoffs, which lose nuclear droplets and retain debris, with a likelihood-based multinomial expression model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are clean single-cell (scRNA-seq) droplet data where background/cell profiles differ little — DIEM's debris-score correlation with extranuclear contamination was less successful on PBMC scRNA-seq; prefer call_targets(clusters = "debris") instead of the score threshold There are few or no genes enriched in the background distribution — the debris score will likely be inaccurate since scoring relies on estimating debris-enriched genes Comparing debris scores across independent samples for integration — scores are normalized within-sample and cannot be assumed to be on the same scale if extranuclear RNA distributions differ

skills.description: Use when processing raw 10X droplet snRNA-seq counts and you need a per-droplet contamination metric (percent-spliced reads) plus an experiment-specific nuclear/background midpoint threshold to validate or calibrate debris filtering.
skills.name: snrna-seq-nuclear-contamination-quantification
skills.search_text: snrna-seq-nuclear-contamination-quantification Use when processing raw 10X droplet snRNA-seq counts and you need a per-droplet contamination metric (percent-spliced reads) plus an experiment-specific nuclear/background midpoint threshold to validate or calibrate debris filtering. Input is single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) rather than nuclei: the paper notes the percent-spliced vs debris-score correlation 'was less successful in the PBMC single-cell RNA-seq data' because background and cell type profiles differ less You only have a filtered CellRanger matrix or pre-filtered droplet set — background droplets needed for the bimodal fit must come from the raw_feature_bc_matrix The goal is to compute DIEM's multinomial debris score from expression profiles rather than the splicing-based contamination metric used here for validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Quantifies extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in droplet-based snRNA-seq using the percent of reads that are spliced (mitochondrial genes excluded), and estimates a sample-specific midpoint from the bimodal percent-spliced distribution to separate nuclear droplets from background droplets, validating DIEM-style debris scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Quantifies extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in droplet-based snRNA-seq using the percent of reads that are spliced (mitochondrial genes excluded), and estimates a sample-specific midpoint from the bimodal percent-spliced distribution to separate nuclear droplets from background droplets, validating DIEM-style debris scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) rather than nuclei: the paper notes the percent-spliced vs debris-score correlation 'was less successful in the PBMC single-cell RNA-seq data' because background and cell type profiles differ less You only have a filtered CellRanger matrix or pre-filtered droplet set — background droplets needed for the bimodal fit must come from the raw_feature_bc_matrix The goal is to compute DIEM's multinomial debris score from expression profiles rather than the splicing-based contamination metric used here for validation

skills.description: Use when you need to convert raw snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq alignments (BAM/CRAM) into XClone-ready RDR and AD/DP AnnData objects for allele-specific CNA detection on a tumour dataset such as the 2R astrocytoma snRNA-seq sample.
skills.name: snrna-seq-rdr-baf-input-construction
skills.search_text: snrna-seq-rdr-baf-input-construction Use when you need to convert raw snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq alignments (BAM/CRAM) into XClone-ready RDR and AD/DP AnnData objects for allele-specific CNA detection on a tumour dataset such as the 2R astrocytoma snRNA-seq sample. The data are bulk DNA-seq or single-cell DNA-seq profiles — XClone models raw read/UMI counts from scRNA-seq, and scDNA CNA tools like ACT or CHISEL are the appropriate family. Only a normalised expression matrix is available and the allele-specific AD/DP matrices cannot be generated from source BAM/CRAM files, since XClone's BAF module cannot run from RDR alone in allele-specific applications. The goal is CNA calling in the absence of allelic information only for methods like InferCNV/CopyKAT that never consume AD/DP inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Constructs the three XClone input matrices from single-nucleus RNA-seq data — a cell-by-gene total read-depth matrix (RDR) and allele-specific AD/DP matrices (BAF) — wrapped into AnnData objects with hg38 gene/barcode annotation, so the XClone RDR, BAF, and combine modules can detect allele-specific CNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51026-0
skills.summary: Constructs the three XClone input matrices from single-nucleus RNA-seq data — a cell-by-gene total read-depth matrix (RDR) and allele-specific AD/DP matrices (BAF) — wrapped into AnnData objects with hg38 gene/barcode annotation, so the XClone RDR, BAF, and combine modules can detect allele-specific CNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are bulk DNA-seq or single-cell DNA-seq profiles — XClone models raw read/UMI counts from scRNA-seq, and scDNA CNA tools like ACT or CHISEL are the appropriate family. Only a normalised expression matrix is available and the allele-specific AD/DP matrices cannot be generated from source BAM/CRAM files, since XClone's BAF module cannot run from RDR alone in allele-specific applications. The goal is CNA calling in the absence of allelic information only for methods like InferCNV/CopyKAT that never consume AD/DP inputs.

skills.description: Use when annotating cell types in multi-batch snRNA-seq (e.g., nine VAT donors from SCP1376) where JOINTLY integration yields interpretable gene modules that must be scored per cell and compared to marker genes for cluster labeling.
skills.name: snrnaseq-cell-type-annotation
skills.search_text: snrnaseq-cell-type-annotation Use when annotating cell types in multi-batch snRNA-seq (e.g., nine VAT donors from SCP1376) where JOINTLY integration yields interpretable gene modules that must be scored per cell and compared to marker genes for cluster labeling. If the input is a single-sample dataset with no batch/donor structure, joint integration and batch-aware modules add no value — use standard marker-based annotation instead If cell type labels are already assigned and the task is only differential expression or pathway analysis, re-clustering and module-score-based annotation is unnecessary For datasets where samples do not share axes of variation (complex multi-condition, multi-sample data), the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than the consensus PCA path http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotate cell types in single-nucleus RNA-seq data by clustering on a JOINTLY co-embedding and using JOINTLY's interpretable gene modules, whose genes are more cell-type-specific than traditional marker genes, to guide and validate cluster-to-cell-type assignment. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44279-8
skills.summary: Annotate cell types in single-nucleus RNA-seq data by clustering on a JOINTLY co-embedding and using JOINTLY's interpretable gene modules, whose genes are more cell-type-specific than traditional marker genes, to guide and validate cluster-to-cell-type assignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the input is a single-sample dataset with no batch/donor structure, joint integration and batch-aware modules add no value — use standard marker-based annotation instead If cell type labels are already assigned and the task is only differential expression or pathway analysis, re-clustering and module-score-based annotation is unnecessary For datasets where samples do not share axes of variation (complex multi-condition, multi-sample data), the article advises regular PCA in JOINTLY rather than the consensus PCA path

skills.description: Use when DIEM debris scores have been computed for a droplet-based snRNA-seq sample and you must verify that the score actually quantifies extranuclear (ambient/spliced) RNA contamination rather than just count depth.
skills.name: snrnaseq-debris-score-interpretation
skills.search_text: snrnaseq-debris-score-interpretation Use when DIEM debris scores have been computed for a droplet-based snRNA-seq sample and you must verify that the score actually quantifies extranuclear (ambient/spliced) RNA contamination rather than just count depth. Input is single-cell (not single-nucleus) RNA-seq data such as PBMCs — the paper reports this contamination tracking was 'less successful in the PBMC single-cell RNA-seq data' because background and cell type profiles differ less The sample has few or no genes increased in the background/debris distribution, so debris scores would be inaccurate regardless of correlation testing You intend to compare absolute debris score values across multiple independent samples — scores are within-sample normalized and not comparable, so a cross-sample correlation of raw scores is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates the biological meaning of DIEM's per-droplet debris score by correlating it with an independent measure of extranuclear RNA contamination — the percent of reads that are spliced — per droplet in snRNA-seq data (mean Pearson R = 0.89 across 8 snRNA-seq experiments). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5
skills.summary: Validates the biological meaning of DIEM's per-droplet debris score by correlating it with an independent measure of extranuclear RNA contamination — the percent of reads that are spliced — per droplet in snRNA-seq data (mean Pearson R = 0.89 across 8 snRNA-seq experiments).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (not single-nucleus) RNA-seq data such as PBMCs — the paper reports this contamination tracking was 'less successful in the PBMC single-cell RNA-seq data' because background and cell type profiles differ less The sample has few or no genes increased in the background/debris distribution, so debris scores would be inaccurate regardless of correlation testing You intend to compare absolute debris score values across multiple independent samples — scores are within-sample normalized and not comparable, so a cross-sample correlation of raw scores is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when post-transplant bone marrow (BMMC) or donor-mix scRNA-seq data are available as a Cell Ranger genome BAM, and you need per-cell host/donor genotype calls and mixture fractions from de novo SNVs.
skills.name: snv-based-chimerism-genotype-assignment
skills.search_text: snv-based-chimerism-genotype-assignment Use when post-transplant bone marrow (BMMC) or donor-mix scRNA-seq data are available as a Cell Ranger genome BAM, and you need per-cell host/donor genotype calls and mixture fractions from de novo SNVs. Input lacks per-cell allele UMI structure (e.g. bulk sequencing or pre-aggregated VCFs) — the method needs single-cell SNV fractions to fit genotype mixtures. Clinical chimerism reporting is required — the method is described as proof-of-principle ('in the near future'), not yet clinically validated. The variant of interest involves indels or structural variation — SNVs are called with indels ignored. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 De novo SNV-based Bayesian genotype assignment to determine host/donor chimerism at single-cell resolution from scRNA-seq allele UMI counts, without prior genotype knowledge, by fitting K=1 vs K=2 genotype mixtures with a Gibbs sampler. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: De novo SNV-based Bayesian genotype assignment to determine host/donor chimerism at single-cell resolution from scRNA-seq allele UMI counts, without prior genotype knowledge, by fitting K=1 vs K=2 genotype mixtures with a Gibbs sampler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks per-cell allele UMI structure (e.g. bulk sequencing or pre-aggregated VCFs) — the method needs single-cell SNV fractions to fit genotype mixtures. Clinical chimerism reporting is required — the method is described as proof-of-principle ('in the near future'), not yet clinically validated. The variant of interest involves indels or structural variation — SNVs are called with indels ignored.

skills.description: Use when single-cell CNA clone assignments need orthogonal validation: paired single-cell + bulk WGS exists, somatic SNVs have been called (e.g. SCAN2/Mutect2), and an ARI between CNA- and SNV-based clusterings is the acceptance metric.
skills.name: snv-based-clonal-structure-validation
skills.search_text: snv-based-clonal-structure-validation Use when single-cell CNA clone assignments need orthogonal validation: paired single-cell + bulk WGS exists, somatic SNVs have been called (e.g. SCAN2/Mutect2), and an ARI between CNA- and SNV-based clusterings is the acceptance metric. No matched bulk sample is available — SCAN2 excludes any mutation candidate with any supporting reads in matched bulk, so somatic SNV calls cannot be produced Analysis targets sex chromosomes — SCAN2 should only be applied to diploid autosomes 1-22 Cells lack sufficient SNV burden (e.g. non-cancerous neurons/oligodendrocytes with only small mosaic CNAs) so mutation-genotype clustering is uninformative http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Independently cluster single tumor cells by somatic point-mutation genotype (SECEDO on Mutect2 PASS SNVs from SCAN2 calls) and compare against CNA-derived clone assignments using the Adjusted Rand Index, as done for 179 serial meningioma cells (ARI 0.83). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Independently cluster single tumor cells by somatic point-mutation genotype (SECEDO on Mutect2 PASS SNVs from SCAN2 calls) and compare against CNA-derived clone assignments using the Adjusted Rand Index, as done for 179 serial meningioma cells (ARI 0.83).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched bulk sample is available — SCAN2 excludes any mutation candidate with any supporting reads in matched bulk, so somatic SNV calls cannot be produced Analysis targets sex chromosomes — SCAN2 should only be applied to diploid autosomes 1-22 Cells lack sufficient SNV burden (e.g. non-cancerous neurons/oligodendrocytes with only small mosaic CNAs) so mutation-genotype clustering is uninformative

skills.description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (e.g. SRA files from a GEO study like the Kim dataset) need SNV genotyping per single cell, and no matched DNA-seq is available.
skills.name: snv-calling-from-scrnaseq-reads
skills.search_text: snv-calling-from-scrnaseq-reads Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (e.g. SRA files from a GEO study like the Kim dataset) need SNV genotyping per single cell, and no matched DNA-seq is available. Input is already an SNV matrix or VCF set — use the SSrGE modeling step directly instead of re-calling SNVs from reads Coupled DNA-seq data from the same single cells is available — DNA-seq-based variant calling gives more complete coverage than scRNA-seq reads Target variants lie outside exonic/covered regions — the pipeline may miss driver mutations due to incomplete DNA coverage of scRNA-seq reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 A GATK-based SNV calling pipeline, distributed in the opoirion/ssrge docker image, that identifies single nucleotide variants directly from scRNA-seq raw reads (SRA/FASTQ) by aligning to hg19 with STAR and calling SNVs from the aligned BAMs, benchmarked against artificially seeded ground-truth variants. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: A GATK-based SNV calling pipeline, distributed in the opoirion/ssrge docker image, that identifies single nucleotide variants directly from scRNA-seq raw reads (SRA/FASTQ) by aligning to hg19 with STAR and calling SNVs from the aligned BAMs, benchmarked against artificially seeded ground-truth variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an SNV matrix or VCF set — use the SSrGE modeling step directly instead of re-calling SNVs from reads Coupled DNA-seq data from the same single cells is available — DNA-seq-based variant calling gives more complete coverage than scRNA-seq reads Target variants lie outside exonic/covered regions — the pipeline may miss driver mutations due to incomplete DNA coverage of scRNA-seq reads

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-genotype or mixed-species sample (e.g. Jurkat/293T mixtures or transplant host/donor chimerism) must be deconvolved at single-cell resolution using sequence variation rather than gene expression markers.
skills.name: snv-calling-from-single-cell-rnaseq
skills.search_text: snv-calling-from-single-cell-rnaseq Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-genotype or mixed-species sample (e.g. Jurkat/293T mixtures or transplant host/donor chimerism) must be deconvolved at single-cell resolution using sequence variation rather than gene expression markers. The goal is differential gene expression or cell-type clustering based on transcript abundance rather than genotype assignment — use marker-based approaches (e.g. Seurat) instead The mixture fraction is below the detection level of the method (~4% of 6,000 cells in in silico mixing experiments); K=1 selection would only indicate the minor genotype is undetectable Input data lack per-cell UMI counts or the sample is homogeneous with no expected sequence variation between cell populations http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2885 A method for calling and using single nucleotide variants directly from scRNA-seq transcriptome data (via Freebayes on the Cell Ranger genome BAM) to assign individual cells to their genotype of origin without prior knowledge of cell-specific markers or genotypes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: A method for calling and using single nucleotide variants directly from scRNA-seq transcriptome data (via Freebayes on the Cell Ranger genome BAM) to assign individual cells to their genotype of origin without prior knowledge of cell-specific markers or genotypes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential gene expression or cell-type clustering based on transcript abundance rather than genotype assignment — use marker-based approaches (e.g. Seurat) instead The mixture fraction is below the detection level of the method (~4% of 6,000 cells in in silico mixing experiments); K=1 selection would only indicate the minor genotype is undetectable Input data lack per-cell UMI counts or the sample is homogeneous with no expected sequence variation between cell populations

skills.description: Use when raw breast cancer (GSE75688, SRP067248) or glioblastoma (EGAS00001001880) bulk WES and single-cell/bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files must be converted into QC-filtered somatic SNV read count matrices for Canopy2 input.
skills.name: snv-callset-qc-filtering
skills.search_text: snv-callset-qc-filtering Use when raw breast cancer (GSE75688, SRP067248) or glioblastoma (EGAS00001001880) bulk WES and single-cell/bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files must be converted into QC-filtered somatic SNV read count matrices for Canopy2 input. The read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) already exist, e.g. as the packaged GBM10_preproc/GBM10_postproc datasets — proceed directly to Canopy2 inference The goal is germline heterozygous locus calling in single-cell data — the authors ship a separate germline variant calling pipeline for that purpose The data are not matched bulk DNA WES plus scRNA-seq from the same samples, since force-calling and 0/0-normal QC depend on paired normal/bulk DNA data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Pre-processing QC pipeline that converts raw bulk WES and scRNA-seq FASTQ data into a finalized somatic SNV callset and the alternative/total read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) required by Canopy2, via Mutect2 variant calling followed by stringent filtering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: Pre-processing QC pipeline that converts raw bulk WES and scRNA-seq FASTQ data into a finalized somatic SNV callset and the alternative/total read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) required by Canopy2, via Mutect2 variant calling followed by stringent filtering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) already exist, e.g. as the packaged GBM10_preproc/GBM10_postproc datasets — proceed directly to Canopy2 inference The goal is germline heterozygous locus calling in single-cell data — the authors ship a separate germline variant calling pipeline for that purpose The data are not matched bulk DNA WES plus scRNA-seq from the same samples, since force-calling and 0/0-normal QC depend on paired normal/bulk DNA data

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a tumor sample needs per-cell tumor/normal labels and copy-number-based calling is unavailable or unreliable (e.g., normal-karyotype AML lacking CNAs), or when validating CNA-based calls against SNV/expression evidence.
skills.name: snv-expression-signature-cell-calling
skills.search_text: snv-expression-signature-cell-calling Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a tumor sample needs per-cell tumor/normal labels and copy-number-based calling is unavailable or unreliable (e.g., normal-karyotype AML lacking CNAs), or when validating CNA-based calls against SNV/expression evidence. When the goal is to determine whether a cell is truly wild-type for a mutation — dropout makes true wild-type status indeterminable from scRNA-seq. When the tumor has rich copy-number aberrations and a CNA-based classifier alone is sufficient; CNAs are rare in AML but this skill's value is greatest where CNAs are absent or incomplete. When the variant is germline or not somatic/within a CNV event — VarTrix assignment is only useful for somatic variants or variants within CNV events. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Classifies individual cells as tumor (AML) or normal by combining detection of tumor-specific expressed SNVs in scRNA-seq data with an expression-signature-based label, benchmarked against CNA-based (CONICSmat) classification. Grounded in the Petti et al. 2019 AML single-cell genotyping approach. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Classifies individual cells as tumor (AML) or normal by combining detection of tumor-specific expressed SNVs in scRNA-seq data with an expression-signature-based label, benchmarked against CNA-based (CONICSmat) classification. Grounded in the Petti et al. 2019 AML single-cell genotyping approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to determine whether a cell is truly wild-type for a mutation — dropout makes true wild-type status indeterminable from scRNA-seq. When the tumor has rich copy-number aberrations and a CNA-based classifier alone is sufficient; CNAs are rare in AML but this skill's value is greatest where CNAs are absent or incomplete. When the variant is germline or not somatic/within a CNV event — VarTrix assignment is only useful for somatic variants or variants within CNV events.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-cell or chimerism sample requires per-cell genotype assignment from transcriptome SNVs, especially when no distinguishing marker genes exist or marker-based calls need orthogonal validation.
skills.name: snv-fraction-cell-genotype-classification
skills.search_text: snv-fraction-cell-genotype-classification Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-cell or chimerism sample requires per-cell genotype assignment from transcriptome SNVs, especially when no distinguishing marker genes exist or marker-based calls need orthogonal validation. Input is a 5'/3' gene-expression feature matrix without an accompanying aligned genome BAM, since SNVs must be called from aligned transcriptome reads The sample is a single pure genotype, where marker-based classification already suffices and no genotype-informative SNV set exists Analysis goals require detecting chimerism below the method's detection level (~4% of 6,000 cells), where the K=1 model will be selected http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classifies individual cells in mixed scRNA-seq samples (e.g., Jurkat/293T, host/donor chimerism) by scoring genotype-enriched SNVs called directly from the transcriptome with Freebayes on the Cell Ranger genome BAM, independent of marker gene expression. Provides a de novo alternative to marker-based cell assignment plus a multiplet-rate estimator. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Classifies individual cells in mixed scRNA-seq samples (e.g., Jurkat/293T, host/donor chimerism) by scoring genotype-enriched SNVs called directly from the transcriptome with Freebayes on the Cell Ranger genome BAM, independent of marker gene expression. Provides a de novo alternative to marker-based cell assignment plus a multiplet-rate estimator.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a 5'/3' gene-expression feature matrix without an accompanying aligned genome BAM, since SNVs must be called from aligned transcriptome reads The sample is a single pure genotype, where marker-based classification already suffices and no genotype-informative SNV set exists Analysis goals require detecting chimerism below the method's detection level (~4% of 6,000 cells), where the K=1 model will be selected

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell SNV calls (e.g. .vcf-derived binary matrix) coupled with single-cell gene expression counts and need SNV-derived features that link genotype to expression phenotypes.
skills.name: snv-gene-expression-linkage
skills.search_text: snv-gene-expression-linkage Use when you have per-cell SNV calls (e.g. .vcf-derived binary matrix) coupled with single-cell gene expression counts and need SNV-derived features that link genotype to expression phenotypes. Input is already a reduced feature table or the SNVs and expression come from different cells — SSrGE requires coupled DNA/RNA data from the same single cells The goal is de novo SNV calling from raw reads — use the SSrGE SNV_calling/download modules or QuASAR first; this skill starts from already-called SNVs All candidate SNV features are highly correlated — LASSO may arbitrarily select only one of highly correlated SNV features corresponding to gene expression http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit LASSO-regularized sparse linear models (SSrGE) regressing gene expression on binary SNV matrices from scRNA-seq to derive effective, expressed SNVs (eeSNVs), whose accumulated coefficients rank SNVs and genes for subpopulation identification and genotype-phenotype linkage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Fit LASSO-regularized sparse linear models (SSrGE) regressing gene expression on binary SNV matrices from scRNA-seq to derive effective, expressed SNVs (eeSNVs), whose accumulated coefficients rank SNVs and genes for subpopulation identification and genotype-phenotype linkage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced feature table or the SNVs and expression come from different cells — SSrGE requires coupled DNA/RNA data from the same single cells The goal is de novo SNV calling from raw reads — use the SSrGE SNV_calling/download modules or QuASAR first; this skill starts from already-called SNVs All candidate SNV features are highly correlated — LASSO may arbitrarily select only one of highly correlated SNV features corresponding to gene expression

skills.description: Use when you have a binary SNV matrix (n_cells x n_SNVs) and a gene expression matrix (n_cells x n_genes) from the same single cells and need to infer which eeSNVs are associated with expression of particular genes.
skills.name: snv-gene-linkage-modeling-with-lasso
skills.search_text: snv-gene-linkage-modeling-with-lasso Use when you have a binary SNV matrix (n_cells x n_SNVs) and a gene expression matrix (n_cells x n_genes) from the same single cells and need to infer which eeSNVs are associated with expression of particular genes. You only have gene expression without SNV calls from the same single cells — SSrGE requires the coupled SNV matrix as features Input is already a ranked feature table or you need generic dimension reduction unrelated to SNV-gene linkage; LASSO may arbitrarily select one of highly correlated SNV features Raw reads without preprocessing — SNVs must first be identified from scRNA-seq raw reads via the SNV-calling pipeline before fitting http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Fit sparse LASSO linear models (via the SSrGE Python package) that link filtered, effective, and expressed SNVs (eeSNVs) from single-cell RNA-seq data to gene expression profiles, enabling eeSNV/gene ranking and genotype-phenotype linkage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Fit sparse LASSO linear models (via the SSrGE Python package) that link filtered, effective, and expressed SNVs (eeSNVs) from single-cell RNA-seq data to gene expression profiles, enabling eeSNV/gene ranking and genotype-phenotype linkage.
