skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have gene expression without SNV calls from the same single cells — SSrGE requires the coupled SNV matrix as features Input is already a ranked feature table or you need generic dimension reduction unrelated to SNV-gene linkage; LASSO may arbitrarily select one of highly correlated SNV features Raw reads without preprocessing — SNVs must first be identified from scRNA-seq raw reads via the SNV-calling pipeline before fitting

skills.description: Use when tumor WES/WGS and matched RNA-seq alignments must be converted into somatic SNV and short-indel VCFs as candidate neoantigen sources, with per-read-group parallel calling and Mutect2-learned filtering.
skills.name: snv-short-indel-variant-calling
skills.search_text: snv-short-indel-variant-calling Use when tumor WES/WGS and matched RNA-seq alignments must be converted into somatic SNV and short-indel VCFs as candidate neoantigen sources, with per-read-group parallel calling and Mutect2-learned filtering. The variant source of interest is a long indel — ScanNeo2 routes those to the transIndel module (build remapped BAM with redefined CIGARs, then detect_long_indel_ti_call), not Mutect2. The goal is alternative-splicing, exitron-splicing, or gene-fusion neoantigens — those require the SplAdder, ScanExitron, or Arriba modules respectively, not the SNV/short-indel module. Input is already a called VCF of somatic variants — this skill starts from raw aligned BAMs and would redo calling unnecessarily. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 The SNV/short-indel calling module of the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, which uses GATK Mutect2 on BWA-aligned DNA- and RNA-seq BAMs to produce somatic SNV and short-indel VCFs that feed downstream neoantigen extraction. It complements ScanNeo2's other variant sources (alternative splicing, exitron-splicing, gene fusions, long indels). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: The SNV/short-indel calling module of the ScanNeo2 Snakemake workflow, which uses GATK Mutect2 on BWA-aligned DNA- and RNA-seq BAMs to produce somatic SNV and short-indel VCFs that feed downstream neoantigen extraction. It complements ScanNeo2's other variant sources (alternative splicing, exitron-splicing, gene fusions, long indels).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The variant source of interest is a long indel — ScanNeo2 routes those to the transIndel module (build remapped BAM with redefined CIGARs, then detect_long_indel_ti_call), not Mutect2. The goal is alternative-splicing, exitron-splicing, or gene-fusion neoantigens — those require the SplAdder, ScanExitron, or Arriba modules respectively, not the SNV/short-indel module. Input is already a called VCF of somatic variants — this skill starts from raw aligned BAMs and would redo calling unnecessarily.

skills.description: Use when a single-cell expression dataset has been coarse-grained into K attractor basins (e.g., K_cluster from Eigen-Peak Index or Louvain/Leiden priors) and cells must be assigned fractional membership across basins to distinguish stable from transition cells.
skills.name: soft-clustering-membership-analysis
skills.search_text: soft-clustering-membership-analysis Use when a single-cell expression dataset has been coarse-grained into K attractor basins (e.g., K_cluster from Eigen-Peak Index or Louvain/Leiden priors) and cells must be assigned fractional membership across basins to distinguish stable from transition cells. The dataset has too few cells for high-resolution identification of transition cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset, where the article says special care is needed) The goal is hard clustering into discrete cell states, where high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR are more appropriate since they enforce distinct states Input is raw unprocessed reads rather than a pre-processed expression matrix loadable by MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Optimize and use the soft cell-cluster membership matrix rho*(x) from MuTrans's multiscale rwTPM learning to place each cell continuously within attractor basins, enabling downstream transition cell score (TCS) and transition entropy computation on the cell-fate dynamical manifold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25548-w
skills.summary: Optimize and use the soft cell-cluster membership matrix rho*(x) from MuTrans's multiscale rwTPM learning to place each cell continuously within attractor basins, enabling downstream transition cell score (TCS) and transition entropy computation on the cell-fate dynamical manifold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has too few cells for high-resolution identification of transition cells (e.g., the myelopoiesis dataset, where the article says special care is needed) The goal is hard clustering into discrete cell states, where high-accuracy methods like SC3 or SIMLR are more appropriate since they enforce distinct states Input is raw unprocessed reads rather than a pre-processed expression matrix loadable by MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with DESC and you need per-cell cluster assignment probabilities to identify high-confidence cells or reveal pseudotemporal structure.
skills.name: soft-clustering-probability-assignment
skills.search_text: soft-clustering-probability-assignment Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with DESC and you need per-cell cluster assignment probabilities to identify high-confidence cells or reveal pseudotemporal structure. When hard cluster labels alone suffice and no confidence measure or pseudotemporal interpretation of assignments is needed When batch effects are larger than true biological variation — DESC's self-learning removes batch effects only 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' When a reference-based or supervised annotation is required instead of unsupervised clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assign each cell cluster-specific probabilities via DESC's soft clustering, in which soft assignments Q from a Student's t kernel are iteratively refined against an auxiliary target distribution P by minimizing KL divergence, yielding biologically interpretable confidence values for cluster membership. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15851-3
skills.summary: Assign each cell cluster-specific probabilities via DESC's soft clustering, in which soft assignments Q from a Student's t kernel are iteratively refined against an auxiliary target distribution P by minimizing KL divergence, yielding biologically interpretable confidence values for cluster membership.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When hard cluster labels alone suffice and no confidence measure or pseudotemporal interpretation of assignments is needed When batch effects are larger than true biological variation — DESC's self-learning removes batch effects only 'as long as technical differences across batches are smaller than true biological variations' When a reference-based or supervised annotation is required instead of unsupervised clustering

skills.description: Use when constructing a weighted gene co-expression network from a bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex+hippocampus or 38-sample 3xTg-AD hippocampus datasets) and a soft-thresholding power must be chosen before adjacency and module detection.
skills.name: soft-thresholding-power-selection
skills.search_text: soft-thresholding-power-selection Use when constructing a weighted gene co-expression network from a bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex+hippocampus or 38-sample 3xTg-AD hippocampus datasets) and a soft-thresholding power must be chosen before adjacency and module detection. Input is a normalized single-gene differential expression table with no sample-level correlation structure to model — PyWGCNA's network construction (and thus power selection) is not applicable The goal is only functional enrichment or PPI analysis of an already-defined gene list — use the functional_enrichment_analysis or protein_protein_interaction tutorials instead of re-deriving a network Data are single-cell expression profiles, where the bulk RNA-seq co-expression module framework described here does not directly apply http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Selects the soft-thresholding power (pickSoftThreshold) that best brings gene-gene correlation adjacency matrices to approximate scale-free topology before TOM-based module detection in PyWGCNA. This step determines the weighting exponent that defines the WGCNA network and directly affects the number and size of co-expression modules recovered. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad415
skills.summary: Selects the soft-thresholding power (pickSoftThreshold) that best brings gene-gene correlation adjacency matrices to approximate scale-free topology before TOM-based module detection in PyWGCNA. This step determines the weighting exponent that defines the WGCNA network and directly affects the number and size of co-expression modules recovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a normalized single-gene differential expression table with no sample-level correlation structure to model — PyWGCNA's network construction (and thus power selection) is not applicable The goal is only functional enrichment or PPI analysis of an already-defined gene list — use the functional_enrichment_analysis or protein_protein_interaction tutorials instead of re-deriving a network Data are single-cell expression profiles, where the bulk RNA-seq co-expression module framework described here does not directly apply

skills.description: Use when cells must be labeled into known types from curated marker gene lists (e.g. CD3D/TRAC for T cells, CD79A/MZB1 for B/Plasma, LYZ/CST3 for Myeloid) after training GeneVector gene embeddings on an AnnData object.
skills.name: softmax-pseudo-probability-cell-labeling
skills.search_text: softmax-pseudo-probability-cell-labeling Use when cells must be labeled into known types from curated marker gene lists (e.g. CD3D/TRAC for T cells, CD79A/MZB1 for B/Plasma, LYZ/CST3 for Myeloid) after training GeneVector gene embeddings on an AnnData object. Input is not raw single-cell expression in AnnData .X (e.g. already a feature table, bulk RNA-seq, or pre-normalized embeddings) — GeneVectorDataset requires raw counts. No validated marker gene sets exist for the target cell types — the method depends entirely on curated marker lists, not de novo clustering. Cell types differ at finer granularity than the marker sets distinguish (e.g. CD4 vs CD8 T cell subtypes in the TICA three-type scheme) — use metagene clustering or reference-mapping tools instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assigns cell type labels by computing SoftMax pseudo-probabilities from curated marker gene sets over GeneVector cell embeddings, then taking the argmax per cell. Used in the TICA workflow to classify T, B/Plasma, and Myeloid cells against CellTypist-derived reference annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39985-2
skills.summary: Assigns cell type labels by computing SoftMax pseudo-probabilities from curated marker gene sets over GeneVector cell embeddings, then taking the argmax per cell. Used in the TICA workflow to classify T, B/Plasma, and Myeloid cells against CellTypist-derived reference annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw single-cell expression in AnnData .X (e.g. already a feature table, bulk RNA-seq, or pre-normalized embeddings) — GeneVectorDataset requires raw counts. No validated marker gene sets exist for the target cell types — the method depends entirely on curated marker lists, not de novo clustering. Cell types differ at finer granularity than the marker sets distinguish (e.g. CD4 vs CD8 T cell subtypes in the TICA three-type scheme) — use metagene clustering or reference-mapping tools instead.

skills.description: Use when running Cancer-Finder inference on 10x Visium spot matrices (or scRNA-seq cells) and you need to convert raw softmax probabilities into binary malignant/non-malignant labels for accuracy evaluation.
skills.name: softmax-thresholded-binary-classification
skills.search_text: softmax-thresholded-binary-classification Use when running Cancer-Finder inference on 10x Visium spot matrices (or scRNA-seq cells) and you need to convert raw softmax probabilities into binary malignant/non-malignant labels for accuracy evaluation. Hematologic tumor data — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumors Data that has not been normalized with log-transformed global scaling — raw UMI counts fed to the classifier violate the expected input distribution Analyses requiring spatial-neighborhood context — Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships among spots, so tasks depending on spot adjacency are out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Binarize Cancer-Finder's per-spot/per-cell malignant probabilities by applying a softmax score threshold (default 0.5 for 10x Visium ST data) via infer.py, converting continuous model output into malignant (1) vs non-malignant (0) calls. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Binarize Cancer-Finder's per-spot/per-cell malignant probabilities by applying a softmax score threshold (default 0.5 for 10x Visium ST data) via infer.py, converting continuous model output into malignant (1) vs non-malignant (0) calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Hematologic tumor data — the authors explicitly do not recommend Cancer-Finder for hematologic tumors Data that has not been normalized with log-transformed global scaling — raw UMI counts fed to the classifier violate the expected input distribution Analyses requiring spatial-neighborhood context — Cancer-Finder overlooks spatial relationships among spots, so tasks depending on spot adjacency are out of scope

skills.description: Use when you have CLL RNA-seq BAMs aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted and indexed, and need to call IGHV somatic hypermutation status (mCLL vs uCLL) or benchmark those calls against Sanger-based clinical labels.
skills.name: somatic-hypermutation-status-classification
skills.search_text: somatic-hypermutation-status-classification Use when you have CLL RNA-seq BAMs aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), coordinate-sorted and indexed, and need to call IGHV somatic hypermutation status (mCLL vs uCLL) or benchmark those calls against Sanger-based clinical labels. Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), or are not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS requires this specific setup The goal is to reconstruct T-cell receptor repertoires or non-IGHV loci; CRIS targets the immunoglobulin heavy chain variable region Libraries have fewer than 25M reads per sample or are neither ribodepleted nor polyA-selected http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Classify CLL samples as IGHV-mutated (mCLL) or unmutated (uCLL) by reconstructing full-length immunoglobulin heavy-chain variable region transcripts from RNA-seq with the CRIS pipeline and measuring percent identity to the top germline IGHV hit, enabling concordance checks against clinical PCR-Sanger labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbab021
skills.summary: Classify CLL samples as IGHV-mutated (mCLL) or unmutated (uCLL) by reconstructing full-length immunoglobulin heavy-chain variable region transcripts from RNA-seq with the CRIS pipeline and measuring percent identity to the top germline IGHV hit, enabling concordance checks against clinical PCR-Sanger labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAMs are not aligned to hg38 (GRCh38), or are not coordinate-sorted and indexed — CRIS requires this specific setup The goal is to reconstruct T-cell receptor repertoires or non-IGHV loci; CRIS targets the immunoglobulin heavy chain variable region Libraries have fewer than 25M reads per sample or are neither ribodepleted nor polyA-selected

skills.description: Use when you have a gene set defined by ecDNA amplification (e.g., 251 genes on circlehunter ecDNA calls) and need to test whether somatic mutations are over-represented in that set versus a background.
skills.name: somatic-mutation-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: somatic-mutation-enrichment-testing Use when you have a gene set defined by ecDNA amplification (e.g., 251 genes on circlehunter ecDNA calls) and need to test whether somatic mutations are over-represented in that set versus a background. When testing continuous signals such as copy number, expression, or CRISPR gene effect rather than binary/over-represented mutation membership — those used separate statistical tests (P = 8.754e-16, 2.047e-8, 8.408e-5) instead of over-representation When ecDNA calls have not yet been annotated to genes (the 251-gene amplified set must exist first; upstream task_005 circlehunter output is a prerequisite) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 An over-representation analysis that tests whether genes carried on circlehunter-predicted ecDNAs are enriched for somatic mutations, implemented with GSEApy and yielding P = 4.986e-2 for the 251 ecDNA-amplified genes (37 known oncogenes). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-023-00476-0
skills.summary: An over-representation analysis that tests whether genes carried on circlehunter-predicted ecDNAs are enriched for somatic mutations, implemented with GSEApy and yielding P = 4.986e-2 for the 251 ecDNA-amplified genes (37 known oncogenes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When testing continuous signals such as copy number, expression, or CRISPR gene effect rather than binary/over-represented mutation membership — those used separate statistical tests (P = 8.754e-16, 2.047e-8, 8.408e-5) instead of over-representation When ecDNA calls have not yet been annotated to genes (the 251-gene amplified set must exist first; upstream task_005 circlehunter output is a prerequisite)

skills.description: Use when raw somatic coding mutation data (e.g., COSMIC v79) must be converted into a gene-by-feature matrix for driver-gene classification, and feature definitions (ratio-metrics, entropy, frequency) need to be reproduced.
skills.name: somatic-mutation-feature-engineering
skills.search_text: somatic-mutation-feature-engineering Use when raw somatic coding mutation data (e.g., COSMIC v79) must be converted into a gene-by-feature matrix for driver-gene classification, and feature definitions (ratio-metrics, entropy, frequency) need to be reproduced. The input is already a gene-by-feature matrix (e.g., the deposited FeatureMat.tsv) — use it directly for modelling instead of re-engineering features The downstream method relies on background mutation rate modelling (e.g., MutSigCV-style) rather than mutation-type feature profiles — cTaG's features deliberately avoid mutation-rate bias Mutations come from a source without COSMIC-style mutation type annotations or PolyPhen2 impact predictions, so the 11 categories and HiFI/MiFI/LoFI bins cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Generates a per-gene 37-feature matrix from COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data using ratio-metric features plus entropy and frequency formulas over 11 COSMIC mutation-type categories (with compound, LOF, damaging, benign, and PolyPhen2-binned missense classes), as used to train the cTaG TSG/OG classifier. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Generates a per-gene 37-feature matrix from COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation data using ratio-metric features plus entropy and frequency formulas over 11 COSMIC mutation-type categories (with compound, LOF, damaging, benign, and PolyPhen2-binned missense classes), as used to train the cTaG TSG/OG classifier.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene-by-feature matrix (e.g., the deposited FeatureMat.tsv) — use it directly for modelling instead of re-engineering features The downstream method relies on background mutation rate modelling (e.g., MutSigCV-style) rather than mutation-type feature profiles — cTaG's features deliberately avoid mutation-rate bias Mutations come from a source without COSMIC-style mutation type annotations or PolyPhen2 impact predictions, so the 11 categories and HiFI/MiFI/LoFI bins cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when you have COSMIC somatic coding mutation data and need to classify genes into TSG/OG categories from mutation-type features, or to predict new driver genes among unlabelled genes.
skills.name: somatic-mutation-feature-matrix-modeling
skills.search_text: somatic-mutation-feature-matrix-modeling Use when you have COSMIC somatic coding mutation data and need to classify genes into TSG/OG categories from mutation-type features, or to predict new driver genes among unlabelled genes. The goal is mutation-rate-based driver discovery (e.g. MutSigCV-style background mutation rate modelling) rather than mutation-type feature classification Input is tissue-specific data for a tissue with 1000 or fewer samples (the analysis only used tissues with >1000 samples, e.g. breast, kidney, large_intestine) No somatic mutation annotations are available (e.g. expression or methylation data), since entropy and ratio-metric features cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Build pan-cancer random-forest classifiers (cTaG) on a 37-feature ratio-metric/entropy feature matrix derived from COSMIC somatic mutation data to classify genes as TSGs or OGs, using CGC labels and stable-hyper-parameter estimation to avoid overfitting the small training set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Build pan-cancer random-forest classifiers (cTaG) on a 37-feature ratio-metric/entropy feature matrix derived from COSMIC somatic mutation data to classify genes as TSGs or OGs, using CGC labels and stable-hyper-parameter estimation to avoid overfitting the small training set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is mutation-rate-based driver discovery (e.g. MutSigCV-style background mutation rate modelling) rather than mutation-type feature classification Input is tissue-specific data for a tissue with 1000 or fewer samples (the analysis only used tissues with >1000 samples, e.g. breast, kidney, large_intestine) No somatic mutation annotations are available (e.g. expression or methylation data), since entropy and ratio-metric features cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when starting from raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation records and you need to exclude hyper-mutated samples (>2000 mutations) or restrict to primary tissues with >1000 samples before driver-gene modeling.
skills.name: somatic-mutation-sample-filtering
skills.search_text: somatic-mutation-sample-filtering Use when starting from raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation records and you need to exclude hyper-mutated samples (>2000 mutations) or restrict to primary tissues with >1000 samples before driver-gene modeling. Input is already a pre-processed feature matrix (e.g. data/FeatureMat/FeatureMat.tsv) — filtering applies to raw COSMIC mutation records only Studying a rare cancer type or cohort with fewer than 1000 samples per tissue, where the tissue-size cutoff would exclude the data entirely (use the pan-cancer model instead) Analyses that intentionally include hyper-mutated samples, e.g. studies of mutator phenotypes, since the <2000-mutation cutoff removes them by design Filter raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation data to samples with fewer than 2000 mutations and, for tissue-specific driver-gene analysis, retain only primary tissues with greater than 1000 samples before building per-tissue feature matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04015-y
skills.summary: Filter raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation data to samples with fewer than 2000 mutations and, for tissue-specific driver-gene analysis, retain only primary tissues with greater than 1000 samples before building per-tissue feature matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a pre-processed feature matrix (e.g. data/FeatureMat/FeatureMat.tsv) — filtering applies to raw COSMIC mutation records only Studying a rare cancer type or cohort with fewer than 1000 samples per tissue, where the tissue-size cutoff would exclude the data entirely (use the pan-cancer model instead) Analyses that intentionally include hyper-mutated samples, e.g. studies of mutator phenotypes, since the <2000-mutation cutoff removes them by design

skills.description: Use when you have a tumor-normal pair of cleaned, aligned, recalibrated BAM files and need to detect somatic SNVs as well as INDELs for downstream neoantigen or mutation analysis.
skills.name: somatic-snv-indel-calling
skills.search_text: somatic-snv-indel-calling Use when you have a tumor-normal pair of cleaned, aligned, recalibrated BAM files and need to detect somatic SNVs as well as INDELs for downstream neoantigen or mutation analysis. Input is raw FASTQ without a matched normal sample — tumor-only calling is outside the tumor-normal design described here Sequencing depth is below the stated minimums (15x WGS / 50x WES), where calls would not be reliable You only need germline variant calling — Mutect2 in this pipeline is used for somatic SNVs/INDELs from tumor-normal pairs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calls somatic SNVs and INDELs from tumor-normal WES/WGS pairs using the Mutect2 module of GATK v4.2.0.0, as implemented in the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, writing results to a VCF (somatic_snvs_indels.vcf). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Calls somatic SNVs and INDELs from tumor-normal WES/WGS pairs using the Mutect2 module of GATK v4.2.0.0, as implemented in the TSNAD v2.0 pipeline, writing results to a VCF (somatic_snvs_indels.vcf).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ without a matched normal sample — tumor-only calling is outside the tumor-normal design described here Sequencing depth is below the stated minimums (15x WGS / 50x WES), where calls would not be reliable You only need germline variant calling — Mutect2 in this pipeline is used for somatic SNVs/INDELs from tumor-normal pairs

skills.description: Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes plus TCGA somatic SNV calls and need to classify genes as rarely- vs frequently-mutated per cancer type, e.g. to validate a driver-discovery method against CGC.
skills.name: somatic-snv-mutation-frequency-calculation
skills.search_text: somatic-snv-mutation-frequency-calculation Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes plus TCGA somatic SNV calls and need to classify genes as rarely- vs frequently-mutated per cancer type, e.g. to validate a driver-discovery method against CGC. Input is raw TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices (tumor/normal) — that is the input to WMDS.net driver-node discovery, not to this mutation-frequency characterization step Goal is to discover driver genes de novo; this skill only characterizes the mutation frequency of an existing predicted-driver list and does not rank or predict drivers Only germline variants or variant calls without non-synonymous consequence annotation are available, since the frequency is defined specifically over non-synonymous somatic SNVs http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the fraction of TCGA tumor samples carrying non-synonymous somatic SNVs in each WMDS.net-predicted driver gene per cancer type, then splits CGC-overlapping predicted drivers into low-frequency (<0.05) versus high-frequency (>0.05) classes to demonstrate that WMDS.net recovers rarely-mutated driver genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Computes the fraction of TCGA tumor samples carrying non-synonymous somatic SNVs in each WMDS.net-predicted driver gene per cancer type, then splits CGC-overlapping predicted drivers into low-frequency (<0.05) versus high-frequency (>0.05) classes to demonstrate that WMDS.net recovers rarely-mutated driver genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices (tumor/normal) — that is the input to WMDS.net driver-node discovery, not to this mutation-frequency characterization step Goal is to discover driver genes de novo; this skill only characterizes the mutation frequency of an existing predicted-driver list and does not rank or predict drivers Only germline variants or variant calls without non-synonymous consequence annotation are available, since the frequency is defined specifically over non-synonymous somatic SNVs

skills.description: Use when per-cell genotype matrices for somatic SNVs (from cb_sniffer or VarTrix on 10x Chromium data) exist and you need to estimate subclonal frequencies and check sensitivity against bulk VAFs.
skills.name: somatic-snv-subclonal-frequency-analysis
skills.search_text: somatic-snv-subclonal-frequency-analysis Use when per-cell genotype matrices for somatic SNVs (from cb_sniffer or VarTrix on 10x Chromium data) exist and you need to estimate subclonal frequencies and check sensitivity against bulk VAFs. When the goal is de novo variant discovery — cb_sniffer and VarTrix only genotype pre-called variants (VarTrix explicitly 'does not perform variant calling'); somatic SNVs must come from eWGS of paired tumor/normal When determining true wild-type genotype per cell is required — dropout makes it impossible to confirm a cell is truly wild-type for a given mutation When multi-allelic sites are of interest — VarTrix ignores all multi-allelic sites, leaving them empty in the output matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies subclonal somatic SNV burden from 10x scRNA-seq genotype matrices by computing read-based (scVAF) and cell-based (MCF, MCDR) metrics, then validating them against eWGS and bulk RNA-seq VAFs via Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Quantifies subclonal somatic SNV burden from 10x scRNA-seq genotype matrices by computing read-based (scVAF) and cell-based (MCF, MCDR) metrics, then validating them against eWGS and bulk RNA-seq VAFs via Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo variant discovery — cb_sniffer and VarTrix only genotype pre-called variants (VarTrix explicitly 'does not perform variant calling'); somatic SNVs must come from eWGS of paired tumor/normal When determining true wild-type genotype per cell is required — dropout makes it impossible to confirm a cell is truly wild-type for a given mutation When multi-allelic sites are of interest — VarTrix ignores all multi-allelic sites, leaving them empty in the output matrix

skills.description: Use when you have a panel of eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs from paired tumor/normal sequencing and need to show the variant-detection approach does not falsely call them in cells known not to harbor them (healthy donor scRNA-seq).
skills.name: somatic-snv-validation-across-donor-cohorts
skills.search_text: somatic-snv-validation-across-donor-cohorts Use when you have a panel of eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs from paired tumor/normal sequencing and need to show the variant-detection approach does not falsely call them in cells known not to harbor them (healthy donor scRNA-seq). The goal is to genotype AML/tumor cells to find cells harboring the mutation — this skill estimates the false-positive rate in cells that do not harbor the tested variants (healthy donor controls). The scRNA-seq data lacks Chromium UB/CB tags (i.e., is not 10x 3'/5' Chromium output), since cb_sniffer and the UB_tag duplicate-collapsing strategy are specific to 10x Cellranger BAMs. You need to identify arbitrary de novo mutations from the RNA data itself — this skill only tests previously discovered somatic SNVs, as noise from reverse transcription gives a high false-positive rate for de novo calling. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A negative-control validation skill that applies an scRNA-seq somatic SNV detection workflow (eWGS-discovered variants + cb_sniffer on 10x Chromium BAMs) to healthy donor cells to estimate the per-site false-positive rate. The article found zero false positives across 8057 healthy bone marrow cells from four donors, with a maximum per-site FPR of 0.39%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: A negative-control validation skill that applies an scRNA-seq somatic SNV detection workflow (eWGS-discovered variants + cb_sniffer on 10x Chromium BAMs) to healthy donor cells to estimate the per-site false-positive rate. The article found zero false positives across 8057 healthy bone marrow cells from four donors, with a maximum per-site FPR of 0.39%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to genotype AML/tumor cells to find cells harboring the mutation — this skill estimates the false-positive rate in cells that do not harbor the tested variants (healthy donor controls). The scRNA-seq data lacks Chromium UB/CB tags (i.e., is not 10x 3'/5' Chromium output), since cb_sniffer and the UB_tag duplicate-collapsing strategy are specific to 10x Cellranger BAMs. You need to identify arbitrary de novo mutations from the RNA data itself — this skill only tests previously discovered somatic SNVs, as noise from reverse transcription gives a high false-positive rate for de novo calling.

skills.description: Use when raw bulk DNA WES and paired scRNA-seq or bulk RNA-seq FASTQ data must be turned into mutation-by-sample read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) of QC-filtered somatic SNVs for downstream clonal tree inference.
skills.name: somatic-snv-variant-calling
skills.search_text: somatic-snv-variant-calling Use when raw bulk DNA WES and paired scRNA-seq or bulk RNA-seq FASTQ data must be turned into mutation-by-sample read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) of QC-filtered somatic SNVs for downstream clonal tree inference. Input is already a finalized read count matrix (Rs/Xs/Rb/Xb) or an R object like GBM10_postproc — go straight to Canopy2 inference instead Only germline heterozygous loci are needed for estimating gene activation/deactivation rates — use the separately provided germline variant calling pipeline scripts No matched bulk DNA WES data are available, since Rb/Xb matrices require bulk whole exome sequencing http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A pre-processing pipeline that converts raw bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq/bulk RNA-seq FASTQ data into the alternative and total read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) of stringently QC-filtered somatic SNVs required as input to Canopy2 tumor phylogeny inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s12561-024-09466-1
skills.summary: A pre-processing pipeline that converts raw bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq/bulk RNA-seq FASTQ data into the alternative and total read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) of stringently QC-filtered somatic SNVs required as input to Canopy2 tumor phylogeny inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a finalized read count matrix (Rs/Xs/Rb/Xb) or an R object like GBM10_postproc — go straight to Canopy2 inference instead Only germline heterozygous loci are needed for estimating gene activation/deactivation rates — use the separately provided germline variant calling pipeline scripts No matched bulk DNA WES data are available, since Rb/Xb matrices require bulk whole exome sequencing

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq reads must be classified per cell as mutant or unknown for pre-called somatic SNVs, and one must reason about why wild-type calls are impossible.
skills.name: somatic-variant-cell-labeling-with-dropout-awareness
skills.search_text: somatic-variant-cell-labeling-with-dropout-awareness Use when single-cell RNA-seq reads must be classified per cell as mutant or unknown for pre-called somatic SNVs, and one must reason about why wild-type calls are impossible. VarTrix is the better choice when one needs a maintained tool producing Cell Ranger-format genome matrices (sparse matrix of variant x cell) rather than cb_sniffer's barcode calls De novo variant discovery from the scRNA-seq reads themselves — reverse transcription noise gives a high false-positive rate; pre-called eWGS somatic SNVs are required Scenarios requiring definitive wild-type genotype calls per cell — dropout makes wild-type status indeterminable, so cells can only be labeled mutant or unknown http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Labels individual cells in 10x scRNA-seq data as mutant or unknown (rather than wild-type) for eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs, using barcode/UMI-aware pileups, while explicitly treating transcript and allelic dropout as an unavoidable sensitivity limit. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-11591-1
skills.summary: Labels individual cells in 10x scRNA-seq data as mutant or unknown (rather than wild-type) for eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs, using barcode/UMI-aware pileups, while explicitly treating transcript and allelic dropout as an unavoidable sensitivity limit.
skills.when_to_use_negative: VarTrix is the better choice when one needs a maintained tool producing Cell Ranger-format genome matrices (sparse matrix of variant x cell) rather than cb_sniffer's barcode calls De novo variant discovery from the scRNA-seq reads themselves — reverse transcription noise gives a high false-positive rate; pre-called eWGS somatic SNVs are required Scenarios requiring definitive wild-type genotype calls per cell — dropout makes wild-type status indeterminable, so cells can only be labeled mutant or unknown

skills.description: Use when you have somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g., GATK Mutect2 VCFs from tumor-normal WES/WGS) and HLA typing, and need amino-acid-level variant annotation plus peptide-MHC binding/immunogenicity scoring for neoantigen prediction.
skills.name: somatic-variant-effect-annotation
skills.search_text: somatic-variant-effect-annotation Use when you have somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g., GATK Mutect2 VCFs from tumor-normal WES/WGS) and HLA typing, and need amino-acid-level variant annotation plus peptide-MHC binding/immunogenicity scoring for neoantigen prediction. Input is raw reads without prior somatic mutation calling — Mutect2 SNV/INDEL calling must run first in Module 1 No HLA typing is available — DeepHLApan scoring requires HLA alleles from OptiType The goal is TCR-pMHC binding prediction — the article explicitly notes no TCR-pMHC interaction model is included in TSNAD v2.0 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates tumor somatic SNV/INDEL calls with Variant Effect Predictor (VEP 104) to obtain amino-acid-level mutation information, then extracts 8–11-mer mutant peptides and scores peptide-MHC pairs with DeepHLApan 1.1 for neoantigen prediction as implemented in TSNAD v2.0. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Annotates tumor somatic SNV/INDEL calls with Variant Effect Predictor (VEP 104) to obtain amino-acid-level mutation information, then extracts 8–11-mer mutant peptides and scores peptide-MHC pairs with DeepHLApan 1.1 for neoantigen prediction as implemented in TSNAD v2.0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw reads without prior somatic mutation calling — Mutect2 SNV/INDEL calling must run first in Module 1 No HLA typing is available — DeepHLApan scoring requires HLA alleles from OptiType The goal is TCR-pMHC binding prediction — the article explicitly notes no TCR-pMHC interaction model is included in TSNAD v2.0

skills.description: Use when labeled source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage constraints) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target cells must be annotated including detection of novel cell types.
skills.name: source-free-transfer-learning-model-adaptation
skills.search_text: source-free-transfer-learning-model-adaptation Use when labeled source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage constraints) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target cells must be annotated including detection of novel cell types. Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g., scArches-style architectural surgery on source and target) is feasible and preferred All target cell types are known a priori and a subjective/manual threshold for novel-type detection is acceptable with simpler transfer tools (scmap, Seurat v3, ItClust) Input is not single-cell omics data with a trained source classifier (the ZINB autoencoder and co-training classifiers presuppose scRNA-seq-like count structure) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Adapts a pre-trained single-cell annotation model to a target scRNA-seq dataset using only shared pre-trained model weights (no raw source data), combining a ZINB denoising loss with multi-order local affinity constraints to mitigate batch effect and annotate novel cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Adapts a pre-trained single-cell annotation model to a target scRNA-seq dataset using only shared pre-trained model weights (no raw source data), combining a ZINB denoising loss with multi-order local affinity constraints to mitigate batch effect and annotate novel cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw source data are available and explicit feature alignment (e.g., scArches-style architectural surgery on source and target) is feasible and preferred All target cell types are known a priori and a subjective/manual threshold for novel-type detection is acceptable with simpler transfer tools (scmap, Seurat v3, ItClust) Input is not single-cell omics data with a trained source classifier (the ZINB autoencoder and co-training classifiers presuppose scRNA-seq-like count structure)

skills.description: Use when comparing perturbation strength of several extracted directed subnetworks (e.g., seven CAT modules) by testing source-to-sink path significance on case/control RNA-seq data and assembling a comparative table of ACEs%, combined path P-values, and DEG counts.
skills.name: source-sink-path-significance-testing
skills.search_text: source-sink-path-significance-testing Use when comparing perturbation strength of several extracted directed subnetworks (e.g., seven CAT modules) by testing source-to-sink path significance on case/control RNA-seq data and assembling a comparative table of ACEs%, combined path P-values, and DEG counts. Input expression data have not been nonparanormal-transformed and violate SEM normality assumptions The graph is not a directed subnetwork with identifiable source and sink nodes (e.g., an undirected active module before Chu-Liu-Edmonds tree conversion) The goal is differential node or edge perturbation of a single fixed model (use SEMrun fit=1/fit=2) rather than source-sink path-level ACE testing across multiple candidate subnetworks http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Quantifies subnetwork perturbation by testing Average Causal Effects (ACEs) over all source-to-sink directed paths with SEMace(), counting significant paths (>2 nodes) as percentages and combining path P-values (Bonferroni) into PVAL(E), enabling ranking of candidate CAT subnetworks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Quantifies subnetwork perturbation by testing Average Causal Effects (ACEs) over all source-to-sink directed paths with SEMace(), counting significant paths (>2 nodes) as percentages and combining path P-values (Bonferroni) into PVAL(E), enabling ranking of candidate CAT subnetworks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression data have not been nonparanormal-transformed and violate SEM normality assumptions The graph is not a directed subnetwork with identifiable source and sink nodes (e.g., an undirected active module before Chu-Liu-Edmonds tree conversion) The goal is differential node or edge perturbation of a single fixed model (use SEMrun fit=1/fit=2) rather than source-sink path-level ACE testing across multiple candidate subnetworks

skills.description: Use when you have a filtered soybean RNA-seq expression matrix spanning multiple fungal-pathogen stress conditions and need to build an unsigned coexpression network whose gene-module structure supports GWAS-guided candidate resistance gene prioritization.
skills.name: soybean-fungal-stress-transcriptomics
skills.search_text: soybean-fungal-stress-transcriptomics Use when you have a filtered soybean RNA-seq expression matrix spanning multiple fungal-pathogen stress conditions and need to build an unsigned coexpression network whose gene-module structure supports GWAS-guided candidate resistance gene prioritization. When the goal is a signed coexpression network that preserves correlation sign, since this skill explicitly assembles an unsigned network on absolute Pearson correlations When the input is GWAS SNP summary data without RNA-seq expression; this skill only covers the transcriptomic/coexpression half of the paper's integration strategy When the expression data come from a single condition or non-soybean species, since the network was built specifically from five fungal-pathogen stress conditions in soybean http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs an unsigned soybean gene coexpression network from RNA-seq data of tissues infected with five phytopathogenic fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi), using BioNERO preprocessing and the SoyFungiGCN R package to enable downstream candidate resistance gene mining. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-03864-x
skills.summary: Reconstructs an unsigned soybean gene coexpression network from RNA-seq data of tissues infected with five phytopathogenic fungi (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi), using BioNERO preprocessing and the SoyFungiGCN R package to enable downstream candidate resistance gene mining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a signed coexpression network that preserves correlation sign, since this skill explicitly assembles an unsigned network on absolute Pearson correlations When the input is GWAS SNP summary data without RNA-seq expression; this skill only covers the transcriptomic/coexpression half of the paper's integration strategy When the expression data come from a single condition or non-soybean species, since the network was built specifically from five fungal-pathogen stress conditions in soybean

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells must be partitioned into subpopulations reflecting spatial variation, and a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) is available to reconstruct a pseudo-space.

skills.search_text: space-informed-cell-clustering Use when scRNA-seq cells must be partitioned into subpopulations reflecting spatial variation, and a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) is available to reconstruct a pseudo-space. The task is spatial domain identification of ST data itself — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC which target ST spatial domains The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC), where the article advises applying scSpace cautiously No appropriate spatial reference exists or the reference is mismatched to the tissue architecture (e.g., dACC vs DLPFC, where dACC is agranular and lacks cortical layer 4) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data in a reconstructed pseudo-space by jointly embedding gene expression and spatial weight, as implemented in scSpace, to resolve spatially heterogeneous cell subpopulations that traditional transcriptome-only pipelines miss. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Clusters single-cell RNA-seq data in a reconstructed pseudo-space by jointly embedding gene expression and spatial weight, as implemented in scSpace, to resolve spatially heterogeneous cell subpopulations that traditional transcriptome-only pipelines miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is spatial domain identification of ST data itself — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, unlike SpaGCN, BayesSpace, or DR-SC which target ST spatial domains The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., Patients 5 and 9 of SCC), where the article advises applying scSpace cautiously No appropriate spatial reference exists or the reference is mismatched to the tissue architecture (e.g., dACC vs DLPFC, where dACC is agranular and lacks cortical layer 4)

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been assigned pseudo-space coordinates from a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and the goal is to detect spatially variated subpopulations that traditional transcriptome-only clustering misses.
skills.name: space-informed-clustering-of-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: space-informed-clustering-of-scrna-seq Use when scRNA-seq cells have been assigned pseudo-space coordinates from a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and the goal is to detect spatially variated subpopulations that traditional transcriptome-only clustering misses. Input is ST data rather than scRNA-seq — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, whereas SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC target spatial domain identification of ST data The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9) — reconstruction accuracy is compromised and scSpace should be applied cautiously No appropriate spatial reference exists for the target tissue's architecture (e.g., using a DLPFC reference for agranular dACC lacking layer 4) without prior assessment http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Identify spatially heterogeneous cell subpopulations in scRNA-seq data by jointly embedding gene expression with spatial weights derived from pseudo-space coordinates projected via scSpace's TCA + MLP pipeline, then clustering with Leiden. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Identify spatially heterogeneous cell subpopulations in scRNA-seq data by jointly embedding gene expression with spatial weights derived from pseudo-space coordinates projected via scSpace's TCA + MLP pipeline, then clustering with Leiden.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is ST data rather than scRNA-seq — scSpace targets spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data, whereas SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC target spatial domain identification of ST data The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9) — reconstruction accuracy is compromised and scSpace should be applied cautiously No appropriate spatial reference exists for the target tissue's architecture (e.g., using a DLPFC reference for agranular dACC lacking layer 4) without prior assessment

skills.description: Use when loading a raw wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) into Apache Spark and column headers contain periods, commas, or spaces that would break Spark schema compatibility.
skills.name: spark-dataframe-column-sanitization
skills.search_text: spark-dataframe-column-sanitization Use when loading a raw wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) into Apache Spark and column headers contain periods, commas, or spaces that would break Spark schema compatibility. Input is already a tall-format or Parquet file that has previously passed through scSPARKL Stage-1 preprocessing (pipeline accepts .csv and .parquet inputs post-preprocessing) Column headers are already Spark-compatible (no periods, commas, or spaces) and would be left unchanged by the replacement The analysis pipeline is an in-memory tool such as Seurat or Scanpy that does not rely on Spark schema resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Sanitizes wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix column names (replacing periods, commas, and spaces with underscores) so the Spark DataFrame schema is Spark-compatible before Stage-1 preprocessing in scSPARKL. Clean column names are a prerequisite for the wide-to-tall melt and Parquet write that make scRNA-seq data efficient on commodity hardware. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-025-12897-5
skills.summary: Sanitizes wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix column names (replacing periods, commas, and spaces with underscores) so the Spark DataFrame schema is Spark-compatible before Stage-1 preprocessing in scSPARKL. Clean column names are a prerequisite for the wide-to-tall melt and Parquet write that make scRNA-seq data efficient on commodity hardware.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a tall-format or Parquet file that has previously passed through scSPARKL Stage-1 preprocessing (pipeline accepts .csv and .parquet inputs post-preprocessing) Column headers are already Spark-compatible (no periods, commas, or spaces) and would be left unchanged by the replacement The analysis pipeline is an in-memory tool such as Seurat or Scanpy that does not rely on Spark schema resolution

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count data has been melted to tall format in Spark and low-quality cells/genes must be filtered in parallel before normalization and HVG selection.
skills.name: spark-distributed-gene-filtering

skills.description: Use when you need per-gene spatially variable gene (SVG) rankings from spatial transcriptomics data — e.g., a Slide-seqV2 gene-by-bead puck matrix with 2D coordinates — to benchmark against singleCellHaystack's ranks.
skills.name: spark-x-spatial-statistics-execution
skills.search_text: spark-x-spatial-statistics-execution Use when you need per-gene spatially variable gene (SVG) rankings from spatial transcriptomics data — e.g., a Slide-seqV2 gene-by-bead puck matrix with 2D coordinates — to benchmark against singleCellHaystack's ranks. The dataset lacks physical spatial coordinates (e.g., pbmc3k scRNA-seq, PCA latent spaces, or 1D trajectories) — SPARK-X targets spatial inputs, while singleCellHaystack handles 1D trajectories and higher-dimensional latent spaces. Maximum sensitivity to strongly patterned genes matters more than runtime: the hippocampus benchmark showed SPARK-X ranking Plp1 1139th and Mal 1543rd where singleCellHaystack ranked them 20th and 55th. The goal is multi-condition comparison (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) rather than ranking spatial variability within a single tissue section. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Executes SPARK-X to produce per-gene spatially variable gene (SVG) ranks from a gene-by-bead expression matrix with 2D puck coordinates (e.g., Slide-seqV2 mouse hippocampus), serving as the fast spatial ranking baseline that the article benchmarks against singleCellHaystack's more sensitive differential-activity approach. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Executes SPARK-X to produce per-gene spatially variable gene (SVG) ranks from a gene-by-bead expression matrix with 2D puck coordinates (e.g., Slide-seqV2 mouse hippocampus), serving as the fast spatial ranking baseline that the article benchmarks against singleCellHaystack's more sensitive differential-activity approach.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset lacks physical spatial coordinates (e.g., pbmc3k scRNA-seq, PCA latent spaces, or 1D trajectories) — SPARK-X targets spatial inputs, while singleCellHaystack handles 1D trajectories and higher-dimensional latent spaces. Maximum sensitivity to strongly patterned genes matters more than runtime: the hippocampus benchmark showed SPARK-X ranking Plp1 1139th and Mal 1543rd where singleCellHaystack ranked them 20th and 55th. The goal is multi-condition comparison (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) rather than ranking spatial variability within a single tissue section.

skills.description: Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq expression matrix (normalized HVGs, one row per cell) must be converted into a cell-cell graph for graph-based learning, and the adjacency needs to be persisted in sparse .npz format.
skills.name: sparse-adjacency-matrix-serialization
skills.search_text: sparse-adjacency-matrix-serialization Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq expression matrix (normalized HVGs, one row per cell) must be converted into a cell-cell graph for graph-based learning, and the adjacency needs to be persisted in sparse .npz format. Input is raw unnormalized scRNA-seq counts — the cell graph should be built on the normalized HVG matrix from upstream pre-processing, not raw values. The downstream method does not operate on a cell-cell graph (e.g. non-graph imputation or clustering methods), so serializing a kNN adjacency adds no value. Cells must not be connected by symmetric mutual-neighbor edges — an asymmetric directed kNN structure is required instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Assembles the kNN cell graph (one node per cell, edges to the k=15 cosine-nearest neighbors, symmetrized) as a torch-geometric adjacency matrix and saves it as a sparse .npz file (adjacency_matrix.npz) so downstream graph contrastive learning can consume it. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad098
skills.summary: Assembles the kNN cell graph (one node per cell, edges to the k=15 cosine-nearest neighbors, symmetrized) as a torch-geometric adjacency matrix and saves it as a sparse .npz file (adjacency_matrix.npz) so downstream graph contrastive learning can consume it.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unnormalized scRNA-seq counts — the cell graph should be built on the normalized HVG matrix from upstream pre-processing, not raw values. The downstream method does not operate on a cell-cell graph (e.g. non-graph imputation or clustering methods), so serializing a kNN adjacency adds no value. Cells must not be connected by symmetric mutual-neighbor edges — an asymmetric directed kNN structure is required instead.

The matrices are already symmetric undirected adjacency weights (e.g., previously symmetrized Wx/Wy or an undirected igraph graph converted back to a matrix) The input is a raw counts matrix or normalized expression matrix rather than a denoised network adjacency matrix — symmetrization applies to the GRN layer, not the expression layer The downstream analysis is a directed-network method (e.g., directed regulatory-edge inference) where edge directionality is meaningful and should not be collapsed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_2258 Symmetrize the two denoised single-cell gene regulatory networks (sparse dgCMatrix objects X and Y from CP tensor decomposition) into symmetric weight matrices Wx and Wy over the same gene set, so they can be assembled into the joint Laplacian used for nonlinear manifold alignment in scTenifoldNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100139

skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrices are already symmetric undirected adjacency weights (e.g., previously symmetrized Wx/Wy or an undirected igraph graph converted back to a matrix) The input is a raw counts matrix or normalized expression matrix rather than a denoised network adjacency matrix — symmetrization applies to the GRN layer, not the expression layer The downstream analysis is a directed-network method (e.g., directed regulatory-edge inference) where edge directionality is meaningful and should not be collapsed

skills.description: Use when only summary-level eQTL statistics plus an LD reference panel are available (no individual-level expression genotypes) and per-gene GReX imputation weights are needed for downstream TWAS Stage II testing.
skills.name: sparse-and-bayesian-polygenic-model-training
skills.search_text: sparse-and-bayesian-polygenic-model-training Use when only summary-level eQTL statistics plus an LD reference panel are available (no individual-level expression genotypes) and per-gene GReX imputation weights are needed for downstream TWAS Stage II testing. Individual-level reference expression and genotype data are available — FUSION/PrediXcan-style individual-level training is the conventional alternative. The goal is trans-eQTL weight estimation — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects. Reference eQTL summary data are from a non-European population — available summary statistics are mainly from individuals of European descent, limiting cross-population transferability. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 OTTERS Stage I: train cis-eQTL weights per gene from summary-level eQTL statistics and a PLINK-binary LD reference panel by adapting four PRS methods — P+T with LD clumping (P0.001, P0.05), frequentist lassosum (fdrtool pseudo-validation), Bayesian SDPR (Dirichlet Process Regression), and Bayesian continuous-shrinkage PRS-CS — because eQTL effect sizes are effectively SNP effect sizes from a reference 'GWAS' of gene expression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: OTTERS Stage I: train cis-eQTL weights per gene from summary-level eQTL statistics and a PLINK-binary LD reference panel by adapting four PRS methods — P+T with LD clumping (P0.001, P0.05), frequentist lassosum (fdrtool pseudo-validation), Bayesian SDPR (Dirichlet Process Regression), and Bayesian continuous-shrinkage PRS-CS — because eQTL effect sizes are effectively SNP effect sizes from a reference 'GWAS' of gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual-level reference expression and genotype data are available — FUSION/PrediXcan-style individual-level training is the conventional alternative. The goal is trans-eQTL weight estimation — OTTERS currently considers only cis-eQTL effects. Reference eQTL summary data are from a non-European population — available summary statistics are mainly from individuals of European descent, limiting cross-population transferability.

The input is not tabular per-cell gene expression (e.g. raw sequencing reads or image data) — scTab's architecture is specific to tabular data A different cell type annotation model is needed, e.g. transformer-based scGPT or CIForm, which the paper benchmarks as alternatives rather than using this TabNet formulation Many decision steps or multi-step feature selection are required — the scTab specification uses a single decision step http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Implements the scTab cell type classifier's TabNet-derived architecture: feature transformer blocks with batch norm, skip connections and GLU activations, plus a feature attention mask computed with 1.5-entmax (replacing sparsemax) over a 19,331-protein-coding-gene input space to sparsely select informative genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51059-5

skills.name: sparse-binary-matrix-perturbation
skills.search_text: sparse-binary-matrix-perturbation Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix contains RMT-detected signal dimensions possibly inflated by stochastic dropout events, and a data-driven, imputation-free criterion is needed to decide which signal eigenvectors to keep. When the goal is denoising via imputation — scLENS deliberately avoids imputation because imputation can bias data and generate false signals When the data are not sparse scRNA-seq counts (the perturbation sparsity calibration assumes high dropout; zeros can exceed 90%) When a manual signal-noise threshold is acceptable and RMT/robustness automation is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A signal robustness test from scLENS that perturbs the raw count matrix by adding a binary random matrix with sparsity ≥0.97, then retains signals whose eigenvectors remain highly aligned with perturbed-data eigenvectors — filtering low-quality dropout-driven signals without imputation or altering the original data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3

skills.description: Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation has been severely downsampled (e.g. 150 erythrocyte cells reduced to 13) and you need to restore the original cell count so trajectory or graph analyses recover their structure.
skills.name: sparse-cell-population-augmentation
skills.search_text: sparse-cell-population-augmentation Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation has been severely downsampled (e.g. 150 erythrocyte cells reduced to 13) and you need to restore the original cell count so trajectory or graph analyses recover their structure. The population is not sparse — augmentation is aimed at sparse cell populations; well-sampled populations do not need synthetic cells and the article only demonstrates gains from augmenting sparse populations The goal requires condition-specific generation of defined cell types from multi-type data — that is the cscGAN use case, whereas this skill uses the non-conditional scGAN on an extracted single cluster You need to condition generation on side information other than cell type (e.g. case/control samples), which the authors explicitly leave untested for future work http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Augment a downsampled or sparse scRNA-seq cell population by training a single-cell GAN (scGAN) on the retained cells, generating replacement cells with the trained model, and re-appending them to restore the original population size and downstream graph structure (e.g., a PAGA pseudo-time trajectory). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Augment a downsampled or sparse scRNA-seq cell population by training a single-cell GAN (scGAN) on the retained cells, generating replacement cells with the trained model, and re-appending them to restore the original population size and downstream graph structure (e.g., a PAGA pseudo-time trajectory).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The population is not sparse — augmentation is aimed at sparse cell populations; well-sampled populations do not need synthetic cells and the article only demonstrates gains from augmenting sparse populations The goal requires condition-specific generation of defined cell types from multi-type data — that is the cscGAN use case, whereas this skill uses the non-conditional scGAN on an extracted single cluster You need to condition generation on side information other than cell type (e.g. case/control samples), which the authors explicitly leave untested for future work

skills.search_text: sparse-co-expression-edge-extraction Use when single-cell gene expression data has been normalized (library size 10^6), genes filtered to ~500 candidates, and a sparse gene co-expression network must distinguish direct from indirect gene associations via a Gaussian graphical model. Goal is to assign direction or edge type to interactions: the article states scLink's edges 'do not have directions' and it is not feasible to distinguish regulatory, co-regulatory, and functionally coordinated edge types using only gene expression data Gene set is very large (p too big to optimize jointly): the article recommends first dividing genes into major modules based on scLink's correlation and applying scLink separately to each module Data are bulk rather than single-cell: imputed single-cell data may still be much sparser than bulk data, so bulk-data network methods (and this skill's assumptions) may not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs scLink's data-adaptive penalized-likelihood network inference: maximizing a log-determinant Gaussian graphical model objective (Eq. 8) with QUIC over a lambda grid, then selecting the sparse network by minimum BIC and extracting the concentration matrix and nonzero edges. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Reconstructs scLink's data-adaptive penalized-likelihood network inference: maximizing a log-determinant Gaussian graphical model objective (Eq. 8) with QUIC over a lambda grid, then selecting the sparse network by minimum BIC and extracting the concentration matrix and nonzero edges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is to assign direction or edge type to interactions: the article states scLink's edges 'do not have directions' and it is not feasible to distinguish regulatory, co-regulatory, and functionally coordinated edge types using only gene expression data Gene set is very large (p too big to optimize jointly): the article recommends first dividing genes into major modules based on scLink's correlation and applying scLink separately to each module Data are bulk rather than single-cell: imputed single-cell data may still be much sparser than bulk data, so bulk-data network methods (and this skill's assumptions) may not transfer

skills.description: Use when processing 10x molecule information files from libraries multiplexed on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need barcode-swap-corrected per-sample sparse gene-by-cell count matrices.

skills.search_text: sparse-count-matrix-construction Use when processing 10x molecule information files from libraries multiplexed on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need barcode-swap-corrected per-sample sparse gene-by-cell count matrices. Data come from non-patterned-flowcell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500), where the paper's control showed barcode swapping is not the dominant artefact and cell exclusion of shared barcodes would unnecessarily discard cell libraries Input is a plate-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Smart-seq2 plates); the molecule-exclusion approach is specific to 10x droplet molecule information files Input is already a cleaned or count-matrix feature table rather than raw molecule-level information, since the key (UMI, cell barcode, aligned gene) grouping requires molecule-level records http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs cleaned per-sample sparse count matrices for multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq by assigning each molecule (UMI / cell barcode / aligned gene combination) to its sample-of-origin and excluding swapped molecules, as implemented in DropletUtils' swappedDrops. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Constructs cleaned per-sample sparse count matrices for multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq by assigning each molecule (UMI / cell barcode / aligned gene combination) to its sample-of-origin and excluding swapped molecules, as implemented in DropletUtils' swappedDrops.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data come from non-patterned-flowcell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500), where the paper's control showed barcode swapping is not the dominant artefact and cell exclusion of shared barcodes would unnecessarily discard cell libraries Input is a plate-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Smart-seq2 plates); the molecule-exclusion approach is specific to 10x droplet molecule information files Input is already a cleaned or count-matrix feature table rather than raw molecule-level information, since the key (UMI, cell barcode, aligned gene) grouping requires molecule-level records

skills.name: sparse-decoder-variational-autoencoder-training
skills.search_text: sparse-decoder-variational-autoencoder-training Use when you need an interpretable latent space for scRNA-seq where each latent dimension corresponds to a pathway, TF regulon, or cell-type gene set, and you must infer gene module activities per cell (in-sample and out-of-sample). You need a model that can correct or refine incomplete or non-context-specific prior knowledge (e.g., MSigDB gene sets) at training time — VEGA's hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for this You need raw count modeling or strong generative/predictive performance — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder limits generative capacity and sacrifices predictive performance for interpretability Input is not single-cell expression data with available gene module annotations (a GMT file is required to wire the decoder) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train VEGA, a variational autoencoder whose decoder is a sparse linear layer hard-wired to user-provided gene modules (e.g., Reactome pathways from a GMT file), so each latent dimension directly encodes a biological gene module activity (GMV) on single-cell RNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0

skills.description: Use when analyzing sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices where Pearson/Spearman correlations are unreliable due to excessive zeros, and you need a sparse gene co-expression network or comparison of networks across conditions/time points.
skills.name: sparse-gene-coexpression-network-inference
skills.search_text: sparse-gene-coexpression-network-inference Use when analyzing sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices where Pearson/Spearman correlations are unreliable due to excessive zeros, and you need a sparse gene co-expression network or comparison of networks across conditions/time points. When the goal is to determine edge direction or distinguish regulatory, co-regulatory, and functionally coordinated edge types — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies and expression data alone cannot resolve these. When imputation-first strategies are mandatory for the analysis design: imputed data may still be much sparser than bulk data, and imputation can be time-consuming depending on cell number. When analyzing very large gene sets without pre-filtering — gene filtering by detection rate or mean expression, or module-based subdivision, is recommended before applying scLink. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Infer sparse, undirected gene co-expression networks from sparse single-cell RNA-seq count data using scLink, which combines a robust correlation estimator with a penalized Gaussian graphical model and BIC-based regularization selection. It enables differential network comparison across conditions and time-course co-expression change detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Infer sparse, undirected gene co-expression networks from sparse single-cell RNA-seq count data using scLink, which combines a robust correlation estimator with a penalized Gaussian graphical model and BIC-based regularization selection. It enables differential network comparison across conditions and time-course co-expression change detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to determine edge direction or distinguish regulatory, co-regulatory, and functionally coordinated edge types — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies and expression data alone cannot resolve these. When imputation-first strategies are mandatory for the analysis design: imputed data may still be much sparser than bulk data, and imputation can be time-consuming depending on cell number. When analyzing very large gene sets without pre-filtering — gene filtering by detection rate or mean expression, or module-based subdivision, is recommended before applying scLink.
