skills.name: sparse-graph-convolution-implementation
skills.search_text: sparse-graph-convolution-implementation Use when you have a directed gene regulatory network (e.g. DawnNet edge list) plus a gene feature matrix and must compute directed graph convolution outputs while keeping all adjacency matrices sparse. The network is undirected or edge direction/regulation information is absent — DGCN's second-order in-/out-degree proximity matrices require directed edges The goal is node-level gene feature learning that must weigh multi-omics features over topology; DGMP augments DGCN with an MLP branch precisely because DGCN alone biases toward topological features Input is already a dense precomputed embedding rather than a sparse graph — sparse graph libraries add overhead with no benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reconstructs the DGCN module from DGMP, which applies three sparse proximity convolutions (first-order ZF and second-order in-/out-degree Zin, Zout) over a directed gene regulatory network, per Equations (1)-(2): Z = σ(ÂXΘ). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.11.004
skills.summary: Reconstructs the DGCN module from DGMP, which applies three sparse proximity convolutions (first-order ZF and second-order in-/out-degree Zin, Zout) over a directed gene regulatory network, per Equations (1)-(2): Z = σ(ÂXΘ).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network is undirected or edge direction/regulation information is absent — DGCN's second-order in-/out-degree proximity matrices require directed edges The goal is node-level gene feature learning that must weigh multi-omics features over topology; DGMP augments DGCN with an MLP branch precisely because DGCN alone biases toward topological features Input is already a dense precomputed embedding rather than a sparse graph — sparse graph libraries add overhead with no benefit

skills.description: Use when fitting scLink to a filtered single-cell expression matrix and you must pick the regularization strength (lda) for the sparse co-expression network objectively, e.g. via BIC rather than a hand-tuned edge cutoff.
skills.name: sparse-graphical-model-selection-via-bic
skills.search_text: sparse-graphical-model-selection-via-bic Use when fitting scLink to a filtered single-cell expression matrix and you must pick the regularization strength (lda) for the sparse co-expression network objectively, e.g. via BIC rather than a hand-tuned edge cutoff. When the analysis goal is a plain similarity network from reliable bulk expression data — Pearson or Spearman correlation does not require model selection at all When gene expression data are heavily zero-inflated and unfiltered without prior normalization/gene filtering, since BIC selection on unprocessed scRNA-seq counts is unreliable When edge directionality is required — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies and cannot distinguish regulatory from co-regulatory edges http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects scLink's sparse Gaussian graphical-model network over a candidate penalty (lambda) grid by choosing the model with minimum BIC, optionally capping edges at a fraction of all possible edges. This makes network sparsity data-adaptive rather than fixed by an arbitrary threshold. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.11.006
skills.summary: Selects scLink's sparse Gaussian graphical-model network over a candidate penalty (lambda) grid by choosing the model with minimum BIC, optionally capping edges at a fraction of all possible edges. This makes network sparsity data-adaptive rather than fixed by an arbitrary threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is a plain similarity network from reliable bulk expression data — Pearson or Spearman correlation does not require model selection at all When gene expression data are heavily zero-inflated and unfiltered without prior normalization/gene filtering, since BIC selection on unprocessed scRNA-seq counts is unreliable When edge directionality is required — scLink edges are undirected statistical dependencies and cannot distinguish regulatory from co-regulatory edges

skills.description: Use when you have time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell qPCR or RNA-seq expression data from consecutive time points and need a stable, sparse, signed, directed gene regulatory network despite imprecision in estimating sample mean and covariance.
skills.name: sparse-grn-structure-filtering
skills.search_text: sparse-grn-structure-filtering Use when you have time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell qPCR or RNA-seq expression data from consecutive time points and need a stable, sparse, signed, directed gene regulatory network despite imprecision in estimating sample mean and covariance. The goal is a network maintaining the current cell state at a single time point/stage rather than the mechanism driving a transition along the cell lineage (the article notes such GRNs are dense rather than sparse). You do not have at least two consecutive time points of TSCS data — COSLIR relies exclusively on the first and second moments of samples between two consecutive time points. A single un-bootstrapped COSLIR fit is acceptable and the extra bootstrap/ensemble runtime is not warranted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stabilizes COSLIR's estimator of the gene-gene interaction matrix by bootstrapping the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression, then retaining only non-zero entries that survive both a confidence threshold and a clipping threshold, yielding the final sparse directed GRN with signs and weights. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Stabilizes COSLIR's estimator of the gene-gene interaction matrix by bootstrapping the covariance-restricted sparse linear regression, then retaining only non-zero entries that survive both a confidence threshold and a clipping threshold, yielding the final sparse directed GRN with signs and weights.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a network maintaining the current cell state at a single time point/stage rather than the mechanism driving a transition along the cell lineage (the article notes such GRNs are dense rather than sparse). You do not have at least two consecutive time points of TSCS data — COSLIR relies exclusively on the first and second moments of samples between two consecutive time points. A single un-bootstrapped COSLIR fit is acceptable and the extra bootstrap/ensemble runtime is not warranted.

skills.description: Use when a sparse k-mer abundance matrix derived from scRNA-seq raw reads (BAM/FASTA via jellyfish) must be converted into reference-free CKG features because the reference genome is incomplete or insufficient.
skills.name: sparse-kmer-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: sparse-kmer-matrix-processing Use when a sparse k-mer abundance matrix derived from scRNA-seq raw reads (BAM/FASTA via jellyfish) must be converted into reference-free CKG features because the reference genome is incomplete or insufficient. The input is already a gene expression feature table or an existing cell-by-feature matrix rather than a k-mer abundance matrix. A complete reference genome is available and standard alignment-based gene-level feature extraction is sufficient, since this skill targets the reference-free case. The CKG look-up table already exists and the task is the downstream cell matrix generation step (transforming k-mer abundance into CKG expression). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Processes the sparse k-mer abundance matrix built from scRNA-seq raw reads (jellyfish k-mer files) into compressed k-mer groups (CKGs) by selecting informative k-mers and simhashing their abundance vectors into locality-sensitive fingerprints, without alignment to a reference genome. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.102855
skills.summary: Processes the sparse k-mer abundance matrix built from scRNA-seq raw reads (jellyfish k-mer files) into compressed k-mer groups (CKGs) by selecting informative k-mers and simhashing their abundance vectors into locality-sensitive fingerprints, without alignment to a reference genome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a gene expression feature table or an existing cell-by-feature matrix rather than a k-mer abundance matrix. A complete reference genome is available and standard alignment-based gene-level feature extraction is sufficient, since this skill targets the reference-free case. The CKG look-up table already exists and the task is the downstream cell matrix generation step (transforming k-mer abundance into CKG expression).

skills.description: Use when you have TSCS single-cell expression data (qPCR or RNA-seq) at two or more consecutive time points and need to reconstruct a directed, signed, sparse GRN driving a cell-state transition without constructing pseudo-time trajectories.
skills.name: sparse-linear-regression-matrix-recovery
skills.search_text: sparse-linear-regression-matrix-recovery Use when you have TSCS single-cell expression data (qPCR or RNA-seq) at two or more consecutive time points and need to reconstruct a directed, signed, sparse GRN driving a cell-state transition without constructing pseudo-time trajectories. You have true longitudinal time-series data with linkage across time points for the same cells, rather than time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) data The goal is to infer a network that maintains the current cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition Only a single cell stage/time point is available, so no two consecutive time-point moments can be supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Recover a sparse directed interaction matrix (e.g., a gene regulatory network transition matrix A_t) from time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data using COSLIR (COvariance restricted Sparse LInear Regression), which relies exclusively on the first and second moments of samples between two consecutive time points, bypassing pseudo-time inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-024-62850-1
skills.summary: Recover a sparse directed interaction matrix (e.g., a gene regulatory network transition matrix A_t) from time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data using COSLIR (COvariance restricted Sparse LInear Regression), which relies exclusively on the first and second moments of samples between two consecutive time points, bypassing pseudo-time inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have true longitudinal time-series data with linkage across time points for the same cells, rather than time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) data The goal is to infer a network that maintains the current cell stage rather than the mechanism driving a cell-state transition Only a single cell stage/time point is available, so no two consecutive time-point moments can be supplied

skills.description: Use when building an interpretable VAE decoder whose latent variables must correspond one-to-one to user-supplied gene modules (GMT membership) rather than to free-form latent dimensions.
skills.name: sparse-masked-decoder-construction
skills.search_text: sparse-masked-decoder-construction Use when building an interpretable VAE decoder whose latent variables must correspond one-to-one to user-supplied gene modules (GMT membership) rather than to free-form latent dimensions. The goal is a maximally accurate generative model rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance and has limited generative capacity The prior gene modules are incomplete or context-specific corrections are needed, since the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge The data are raw counts that require a count likelihood (VEGA was designed for normalized expression profiles; adapting it to counts follows the scVI rationale) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Constructs VEGA's single-layer sparse linear decoder by wiring a binary gene-membership mask (built from GMT gene-module files) so each latent gene-module variable (GMV) connects only to its annotated genes, with nonnegative weights and appended fully connected hidden nodes for unannotated genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26017-0
skills.summary: Constructs VEGA's single-layer sparse linear decoder by wiring a binary gene-membership mask (built from GMT gene-module files) so each latent gene-module variable (GMV) connects only to its annotated genes, with nonnegative weights and appended fully connected hidden nodes for unannotated genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a maximally accurate generative model rather than an interpretable latent space — VEGA's sparse single-layer decoder sacrifices predictive performance and has limited generative capacity The prior gene modules are incomplete or context-specific corrections are needed, since the hard-coded decoder connections leave no room for correcting prior knowledge The data are raw counts that require a count likelihood (VEGA was designed for normalized expression profiles; adapting it to counts follows the scVI rationale)

skills.description: Use when running RMT-based dimensionality reduction (e.g. scLENS) on whole-gene scRNA-seq matrices where eigenvalue computation exhausts CPU/GPU memory, and median-scaling with sparse storage is an acceptable trade-off.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-memory-optimization
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-memory-optimization Use when running RMT-based dimensionality reduction (e.g. scLENS) on whole-gene scRNA-seq matrices where eigenvalue computation exhausts CPU/GPU memory, and median-scaling with sparse storage is an acceptable trade-off. When the input matrix is already dense/small enough to fit in memory — the ~1.7x speedup and memory savings do not justify modifying the pipeline When downstream analysis requires exact z-score-normalized gene values, since median scaling changes the scaling statistic When feature selection of highly variable genes has already been applied (gene subsetting), rather than whole-gene matrices where memory is the bottleneck http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reduces the memory footprint and runtime of scLENS-style single-cell pipelines by replacing z-score gene scaling with median scaling during log normalization and preserving sparsity via SparseArrays.jl, so large scRNA-seq count matrices fit on commodity CPU/GPU hardware. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47884-3
skills.summary: Reduces the memory footprint and runtime of scLENS-style single-cell pipelines by replacing z-score gene scaling with median scaling during log normalization and preserving sparsity via SparseArrays.jl, so large scRNA-seq count matrices fit on commodity CPU/GPU hardware.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input matrix is already dense/small enough to fit in memory — the ~1.7x speedup and memory savings do not justify modifying the pipeline When downstream analysis requires exact z-score-normalized gene values, since median scaling changes the scaling statistic When feature selection of highly variable genes has already been applied (gene subsetting), rather than whole-gene matrices where memory is the bottleneck

skills.description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be turned into bounded, normalized encoder input for scButterfly's dual-aligned VAE — binarize, filter rare peaks, TF-IDF, then scale to [0,1].
skills.name: sparse-matrix-minmax-scaling
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-minmax-scaling Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be turned into bounded, normalized encoder input for scButterfly's dual-aligned VAE — binarize, filter rare peaks, TF-IDF, then scale to [0,1]. Preprocessing the scRNA-seq modality — use data_processing.RNA_data_preprocessing instead; ADT data uses data_processing.CLR_transform The matrix has already been binarized/TF-IDF-transformed by a prior scButterfly run — reapplying would double-transform the features Converting predicted ATAC profiles back to approximate raw counts — use data_processing.inverse_TFIDF, not re-scaling http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Final scaling step of scButterfly's ATAC-specific preprocessing (data_processing.ATAC_data_preprocessing): after binarization, 0.5% peak-frequency filtering, and TF-IDF transformation of a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix, values are min-max scaled to [0,1] so the matrix is compatible with the variational autoencoder's ATAC encoder. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47418-x
skills.summary: Final scaling step of scButterfly's ATAC-specific preprocessing (data_processing.ATAC_data_preprocessing): after binarization, 0.5% peak-frequency filtering, and TF-IDF transformation of a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix, values are min-max scaled to [0,1] so the matrix is compatible with the variational autoencoder's ATAC encoder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Preprocessing the scRNA-seq modality — use data_processing.RNA_data_preprocessing instead; ADT data uses data_processing.CLR_transform The matrix has already been binarized/TF-IDF-transformed by a prior scButterfly run — reapplying would double-transform the features Converting predicted ATAC profiles back to approximate raw counts — use data_processing.inverse_TFIDF, not re-scaling

skills.description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq count data (e.g. a Scanpy AnnData h5ad) are sparse and noisy and a per-cell mini-pseudobulk profile is needed before gene set scoring with methods like ssGSEA, singscore, or mean_z.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-multiplication
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-multiplication Use when per-cell scRNA-seq count data (e.g. a Scanpy AnnData h5ad) are sparse and noisy and a per-cell mini-pseudobulk profile is needed before gene set scoring with methods like ssGSEA, singscore, or mean_z. The input is bulk RNA-seq data with no cell-to-cell neighborhood graph — smoothing was designed to remedy sparsity and technical noise specific to single-cell measures The AnnData has no precomputed KNN graph in adata.obsp and neighbors cannot be recomputed within the defined groups The analysis requires scores on raw per-cell counts (smooth_mode='off') rather than neighborhood-smoothed profiles Computes the smoothed single-cell expression matrix M = A·X by multiplying a KNN graph matrix (binary adjacency or distance-weighted connectivities) against the count matrix X using scipy sparse operations, yielding neighbor-averaged mini-pseudobulk profiles that counteract sparsity and technical noise prior to gene set scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad150
skills.summary: Computes the smoothed single-cell expression matrix M = A·X by multiplying a KNN graph matrix (binary adjacency or distance-weighted connectivities) against the count matrix X using scipy sparse operations, yielding neighbor-averaged mini-pseudobulk profiles that counteract sparsity and technical noise prior to gene set scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk RNA-seq data with no cell-to-cell neighborhood graph — smoothing was designed to remedy sparsity and technical noise specific to single-cell measures The AnnData has no precomputed KNN graph in adata.obsp and neighbors cannot be recomputed within the defined groups The analysis requires scores on raw per-cell counts (smooth_mode='off') rather than neighborhood-smoothed profiles

skills.description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods like LATE/TRANSLATE: you hold a ground-truth matrix (e.g., example.hd5, 10,000 genes x 10,000 cells) and need a masked input with a controlled 10% nonzero rate.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-random-sampling
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-random-sampling Use when benchmarking imputation methods like LATE/TRANSLATE: you hold a ground-truth matrix (e.g., example.hd5, 10,000 genes x 10,000 cells) and need a masked input with a controlled 10% nonzero rate. The dataset has no ground truth (as in the mouse brain example_mouse_brain_10x.h5 case, where the ground truth is set to the input itself), so masking would destroy real signal with no way to score recovery The goal is to distinguish biological zeros from technical zeros — this masking assumes injected zeros are technical and LATE/TRANSLATE impute all zeros as missing values The input is already the masked benchmark file (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) supplied by the authors' data deposit http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates a synthetic sparse scRNA-seq benchmark input by randomly masking 90% of the entries of a ground-truth read-count matrix (e.g., example.hd5) to zero, creating excess 'technical zeros' whose recovery can be scored against the retained ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-019-0192-7
skills.summary: Generates a synthetic sparse scRNA-seq benchmark input by randomly masking 90% of the entries of a ground-truth read-count matrix (e.g., example.hd5) to zero, creating excess 'technical zeros' whose recovery can be scored against the retained ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground truth (as in the mouse brain example_mouse_brain_10x.h5 case, where the ground truth is set to the input itself), so masking would destroy real signal with no way to score recovery The goal is to distinguish biological zeros from technical zeros — this masking assumes injected zeros are technical and LATE/TRANSLATE impute all zeros as missing values The input is already the masked benchmark file (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) supplied by the authors' data deposit

skills.description: Use when converting a large-scale sparse single-cell expression matrix into a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix via within-cell rank statistics (UCell-style), but the dense rank matrix would exceed memory.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-rank-truncation
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-rank-truncation Use when converting a large-scale sparse single-cell expression matrix into a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix via within-cell rank statistics (UCell-style), but the dense rank matrix would exceed memory. The dataset is small enough that the dense within-cell rank matrix fits in memory without chunking or truncation Using scPAFA's fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore-style scoring) instead of fast_ucell, since that pathway does not require within-cell expression ranking The analysis requires cross-condition differential statistics (SCPA-style) rather than per-cell pathway activity scoring A memory-bounded technique used inside scPAFA's fast_ucell to rank gene expression within each cell (capped at r_max=2000) on 100,000-cell chunks and then truncate the dense within-cell rank matrix back to sparse form, enabling scalable cell-level pathway activity scoring. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-07238-7
skills.summary: A memory-bounded technique used inside scPAFA's fast_ucell to rank gene expression within each cell (capped at r_max=2000) on 100,000-cell chunks and then truncate the dense within-cell rank matrix back to sparse form, enabling scalable cell-level pathway activity scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough that the dense within-cell rank matrix fits in memory without chunking or truncation Using scPAFA's fast_score_genes (AddModuleScore-style scoring) instead of fast_ucell, since that pathway does not require within-cell expression ranking The analysis requires cross-condition differential statistics (SCPA-style) rather than per-cell pathway activity scoring

skills.description: Use when fitting regression or classification models on high-dimensional, correlated omics data (e.g. transcriptomic microarrays with n << p) where sparse feature selection and strong prediction MSE are both required.
skills.name: sparse-pcr-model-fitting
skills.search_text: sparse-pcr-model-fitting Use when fitting regression or classification models on high-dimensional, correlated omics data (e.g. transcriptomic microarrays with n << p) where sparse feature selection and strong prediction MSE are both required. The response-generating signal is not sparse in the features or does not lie near a low-dimensional principal subspace, since SuffPCR assumes a sparse subspace model and performs nearly optimally only when model assumptions are satisfied You need a one-off exploratory PCA of the expression matrix without a regression target — row-sparse PCA here is a means to sufficient PCR, not general dimension reduction http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits sufficient principal component regression (SuffPCR) for high-dimensional omics regression/classification by first estimating row-sparse principal components and then fitting OLS or logistic regression on the recovered subspace, so predictions depend on only a small subset of genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Fits sufficient principal component regression (SuffPCR) for high-dimensional omics regression/classification by first estimating row-sparse principal components and then fitting OLS or logistic regression on the recovered subspace, so predictions depend on only a small subset of genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The response-generating signal is not sparse in the features or does not lie near a low-dimensional principal subspace, since SuffPCR assumes a sparse subspace model and performs nearly optimally only when model assumptions are satisfied You need a one-off exploratory PCA of the expression matrix without a regression target — row-sparse PCA here is a means to sufficient PCR, not general dimension reduction

skills.description: Use when regressing (or classifying) a phenotype on high-dimensional, correlated transcriptomic features where marginal-correlation screening is unreliable and you need both accurate prediction and feature-sparse, gene-level interpretability.
skills.name: sparse-principal-component-regression
skills.search_text: sparse-principal-component-regression Use when regressing (or classifying) a phenotype on high-dimensional, correlated transcriptomic features where marginal-correlation screening is unreliable and you need both accurate prediction and feature-sparse, gene-level interpretability. Low-dimensional or independent-feature settings where standard sparse linear models (Lasso, Elastic Net, SPC) already satisfy the marginal-correlation screening assumption When the full dense principal component subspace (non-sparse PCR) is desired and no feature-level interpretability is needed When a pre-existing feature/signature table is already given and no subspace estimation is required http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Fit SuffPCR: a two-stage estimator that first recovers a row-sparse principal component subspace via sparse PCA (Fantope projection with ADMM and hard-threshold row selection), then fits OLS or logistic regression on the recovered subspace, so predictions depend on only a small subset of genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac033
skills.summary: Fit SuffPCR: a two-stage estimator that first recovers a row-sparse principal component subspace via sparse PCA (Fantope projection with ADMM and hard-threshold row selection), then fits OLS or logistic regression on the recovered subspace, so predictions depend on only a small subset of genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Low-dimensional or independent-feature settings where standard sparse linear models (Lasso, Elastic Net, SPC) already satisfy the marginal-correlation screening assumption When the full dense principal component subspace (non-sparse PCR) is desired and no feature-level interpretability is needed When a pre-existing feature/signature table is already given and no subspace estimation is required

skills.description: Use when you already have extracted gene communities (e.g. 'IC_'+tumor+'.csv' files for KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) and need a sparse, smaller gene signature per community for a classification task.
skills.name: sparse-regression-coefficient-extraction
skills.search_text: sparse-regression-coefficient-extraction Use when you already have extracted gene communities (e.g. 'IC_'+tumor+'.csv' files for KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) and need a sparse, smaller gene signature per community for a classification task. The goal is the differential expression baseline (DESeq2 DE genes), not sparse selection from pre-extracted co-expression communities No gene communities have been extracted yet — the LASSO step operates on IC communities produced upstream via Gephi modularity, not on the full expression matrix The task is gene set enrichment, PubMed literature, or DrugBank actionability evaluation of IC genes, which does not require LASSO re-selection http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Selects representative ICL genes from each per-cancer-type IC gene community by fitting a LASSO regression on the community's TCGA RNA-Seq/miRNA-Seq expression matrix and keeping genes with non-zero L1-shrunk coefficients, for downstream normal/cancer classification with Random Forest. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Selects representative ICL genes from each per-cancer-type IC gene community by fitting a LASSO regression on the community's TCGA RNA-Seq/miRNA-Seq expression matrix and keeping genes with non-zero L1-shrunk coefficients, for downstream normal/cancer classification with Random Forest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is the differential expression baseline (DESeq2 DE genes), not sparse selection from pre-extracted co-expression communities No gene communities have been extracted yet — the LASSO step operates on IC communities produced upstream via Gephi modularity, not on the full expression matrix The task is gene set enrichment, PubMed literature, or DrugBank actionability evaluation of IC genes, which does not require LASSO re-selection

skills.description: Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrices (sparse matrix or SingleCellExperiment) and per-cell rank-based, dataset-composition-independent scores are required, or when reproducing ScoreSignatures_UCell numerically.
skills.name: sparse-single-cell-matrix-handling
skills.search_text: sparse-single-cell-matrix-handling Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrices (sparse matrix or SingleCellExperiment) and per-cell rank-based, dataset-composition-independent scores are required, or when reproducing ScoreSignatures_UCell numerically. When a dataset-composition-dependent but statistically averaged score is acceptable — note Seurat's AddModuleScore bins genes by average expression and gives inconsistent results for the same cell depending on dataset composition, but is a different method, not a reproduction target here When input is not a gene-by-cell expression matrix (e.g. already-computed signature scores or a feature table) — reranking is meaningless When comparing against UCell versions < 2.7.6 while using the new U_max = n*maxRank - n(n+1)/2 normalization, which will systematically shift scores for large gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs UCell's rank-based gene signature scoring: per-cell gene ranks computed with data.table::frank are capped at maxRank (1500 by default) to handle sparse zero-expression tails, then a Mann-Whitney U statistic is normalized to a [0,1] score per cell. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.06.043
skills.summary: Reconstructs UCell's rank-based gene signature scoring: per-cell gene ranks computed with data.table::frank are capped at maxRank (1500 by default) to handle sparse zero-expression tails, then a Mann-Whitney U statistic is normalized to a [0,1] score per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a dataset-composition-dependent but statistically averaged score is acceptable — note Seurat's AddModuleScore bins genes by average expression and gives inconsistent results for the same cell depending on dataset composition, but is a different method, not a reproduction target here When input is not a gene-by-cell expression matrix (e.g. already-computed signature scores or a feature table) — reranking is meaningless When comparing against UCell versions < 2.7.6 while using the new U_max = n*maxRank - n(n+1)/2 normalization, which will systematically shift scores for large gene sets

skills.description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq analysis needs a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix for spectral clustering of cell types, especially with high-noise, high-dropout data where pairwise-only similarities are unreliable.
skills.name: sparse-subspace-optimization-admm
skills.search_text: sparse-subspace-optimization-admm Use when a single-cell RNA-seq analysis needs a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix for spectral clustering of cell types, especially with high-noise, high-dropout data where pairwise-only similarities are unreliable. The input is already a high-quality, dense cell-to-cell similarity/affinity matrix that does not suffer from dropout-induced sparsity. The goal is raw gene-expression feature extraction rather than similarity learning for cell-type clustering (e.g. input is an unclustered feature table for differential analysis). Very large-scale datasets where the time cost is prohibitive and parallel acceleration is unavailable — the article notes SSRE is relatively time-consuming on large-scale data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Solve SSRE's sparse subspace representation of scRNA-seq cell-to-cell similarity by expressing each cell as a sparse linear combination of other cells (Equations 1-3) via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), then enhance the resulting sparse similarity with KNN-based Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation and three classical pairwise similarities into the final matrix Esim_sparse. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Solve SSRE's sparse subspace representation of scRNA-seq cell-to-cell similarity by expressing each cell as a sparse linear combination of other cells (Equations 1-3) via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), then enhance the resulting sparse similarity with KNN-based Weighted Adamic/Adar imputation and three classical pairwise similarities into the final matrix Esim_sparse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a high-quality, dense cell-to-cell similarity/affinity matrix that does not suffer from dropout-induced sparsity. Data have no spatial coordinates (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or dissociated scRNA-seq), so no inverse-square distance weights between spots can be computed You need de novo structure discovery without predefined gene signatures — this skill tests clustering of specific signatures' enrichment scores, not unsupervised spatial domain segmentation Only a handful of spots are available, making global autocorrelation statistics unstable http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Two-stage spatial autocorrelation testing from scCancer2: Global Moran's I (with inverse-square distance weights) flags gene signatures as spatially clustered (GMI > 0.5), then Local Moran's I localizes hotspot/coldspot structures such as TLSs and tumor capsules in spatial transcriptomics data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Two-stage spatial autocorrelation testing from scCancer2: Global Moran's I (with inverse-square distance weights) flags gene signatures as spatially clustered (GMI > 0.5), then Local Moran's I localizes hotspot/coldspot structures such as TLSs and tumor capsules in spatial transcriptomics data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data have no spatial coordinates (e.g. bulk RNA-seq or dissociated scRNA-seq), so no inverse-square distance weights between spots can be computed You need de novo structure discovery without predefined gene signatures — this skill tests clustering of specific signatures' enrichment scores, not unsupervised spatial domain segmentation Only a handful of spots are available, making global autocorrelation statistics unstable

skills.description: Use when you have mapped single cells to spatial coordinates on a ST section (e.g. via STEM's all_coord) and need to identify genes differentially expressed along a spatial axis within one cell type, or fit spatial expression curves for landmark markers.
skills.name: spatial-axis-differential-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: spatial-axis-differential-expression-analysis Use when you have mapped single cells to spatial coordinates on a ST section (e.g. via STEM's all_coord) and need to identify genes differentially expressed along a spatial axis within one cell type, or fit spatial expression curves for landmark markers. When the goal is spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types rather than single-cell spatial variation — the article notes deconvolution 'cannot link the SC and ST at the single cell level' When SC and ST data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM to SC and ST from different donors in the same disease state 'remains untested future work' http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Performs cell-type-specific differential expression and expression-curve fitting along a spatial axis (e.g. the hepatic lobule PV-CV zonation axis) after transferring spatial coordinates from ST spots to single cells via STEM's SC-ST mapping matrix. This recovers regionally expressed genes within a cell type that deconvolution approaches cannot resolve. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Performs cell-type-specific differential expression and expression-curve fitting along a spatial axis (e.g. the hepatic lobule PV-CV zonation axis) after transferring spatial coordinates from ST spots to single cells via STEM's SC-ST mapping matrix. This recovers regionally expressed genes within a cell type that deconvolution approaches cannot resolve.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is spot-level deconvolution into a fixed number of cell types rather than single-cell spatial variation — the article notes deconvolution 'cannot link the SC and ST at the single cell level' When SC and ST data come from different donors or different disease states — the article states applying STEM to SC and ST from different donors in the same disease state 'remains untested future work'

skills.description: Use when a STARsolo digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates has too few UMIs per spatial barcode for direct cell-type clustering (Seq-Scope, Slide-seq), and you need binned Seurat objects at super-cellular resolution.
skills.name: spatial-barcode-grid-aggregation
skills.search_text: spatial-barcode-grid-aggregation Use when a STARsolo digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates has too few UMIs per spatial barcode for direct cell-type clustering (Seq-Scope, Slide-seq), and you need binned Seurat objects at super-cellular resolution. The input is raw FASTQ or an unaligned barcode file — aggregation requires a post-STARsolo DGE from Step A3 (preprocessing/alignment steps A1–A3 come first). Subcellular-resolution analysis is the goal — spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so MSSW cannot resolve subcellular structure. Each spatial barcode already has sufficient UMI depth for direct cell-type clustering (e.g. standard VISIUM-resolution data where aggregation adds little). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 STtools' two-track aggregation strategy that collapses sparse per-spatial-barcode DGEs into simple non-overlapping square grids (Step C1) and multi-scale sliding-window overlapping grids (Step C2) so that cell-type clustering becomes feasible on ultra-high-resolution platforms like Seq-Scope, Slide-seq, and VISIUM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: STtools' two-track aggregation strategy that collapses sparse per-spatial-barcode DGEs into simple non-overlapping square grids (Step C1) and multi-scale sliding-window overlapping grids (Step C2) so that cell-type clustering becomes feasible on ultra-high-resolution platforms like Seq-Scope, Slide-seq, and VISIUM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ or an unaligned barcode file — aggregation requires a post-STARsolo DGE from Step A3 (preprocessing/alignment steps A1–A3 come first). Subcellular-resolution analysis is the goal — spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so MSSW cannot resolve subcellular structure. Each spatial barcode already has sufficient UMI depth for direct cell-type clustering (e.g. standard VISIUM-resolution data where aggregation adds little).

skills.description: Use when spatially resolved data (Cell2location-deconvolved Visium spots or multiplexed single-cell imaging such as CyCIF/MCMICRO output) must be partitioned into communities with explicit boundaries and per-point region labels.
skills.name: spatial-boundary-delineation
skills.search_text: spatial-boundary-delineation Use when spatially resolved data (Cell2location-deconvolved Visium spots or multiplexed single-cell imaging such as CyCIF/MCMICRO output) must be partitioned into communities with explicit boundaries and per-point region labels. Input is a raw multi-channel whole-slide image without single-cell segmentation — preprocess with MCMICRO first, since 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells' Goal is general neighborhood graph construction/analysis rather than explicit region delineation — Squidpy is the cited toolkit for that purpose A HALO-style manual annotation workflow is preferred — SpatialCells is positioned as a replacement for approaches where spatial analysis 'often demands manual annotation' http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Delineates spatial regions (e.g., germinal centers in a Visium lymph node sample, tumor/immune subregions in CyCIF melanoma) by clustering spots/cells on deconvolved cell-type composition and computing explicit region boundaries with SpatialCells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Delineates spatial regions (e.g., germinal centers in a Visium lymph node sample, tumor/immune subregions in CyCIF melanoma) by clustering spots/cells on deconvolved cell-type composition and computing explicit region boundaries with SpatialCells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw multi-channel whole-slide image without single-cell segmentation — preprocess with MCMICRO first, since 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells' Goal is general neighborhood graph construction/analysis rather than explicit region delineation — Squidpy is the cited toolkit for that purpose A HALO-style manual annotation workflow is preferred — SpatialCells is positioned as a replacement for approaches where spatial analysis 'often demands manual annotation'

skills.description: Use when you have LDA-derived per-pixel cell-type proportions (theta) and pixel positions from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and need to inspect where each inferred cell type localizes spatially, e.
skills.name: spatial-cell-type-proportion-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-cell-type-proportion-visualization Use when you have LDA-derived per-pixel cell-type proportions (theta) and pixel positions from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and need to inspect where each inferred cell type localizes spatially, e. Input ST data is at sub-cellular pixel resolution — the paper states STdeconvolve may not be best suited for such data Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack spatial variability, or the tissue is a thin structure covering only a few pixels — deconvolution and hence spatial proportion maps are unreliable A suitable scRNA-seq reference exists and a reference-based method (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) is preferred for supervised deconvolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Visualize per-pixel cell-type proportions from STdeconvolve's reference-free LDA deconvolution overlaid on spatial transcriptomics pixel coordinates, enabling assessment of spatial organization of inferred cell types such as granule cell layer or rostral migratory stream populations in the mouse main olfactory bulb (mOB) ST data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Visualize per-pixel cell-type proportions from STdeconvolve's reference-free LDA deconvolution overlaid on spatial transcriptomics pixel coordinates, enabling assessment of spatial organization of inferred cell types such as granule cell layer or rostral migratory stream populations in the mouse main olfactory bulb (mOB) ST data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input ST data is at sub-cellular pixel resolution — the paper states STdeconvolve may not be best suited for such data Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so genes lack spatial variability, or the tissue is a thin structure covering only a few pixels — deconvolution and hence spatial proportion maps are unreliable A suitable scRNA-seq reference exists and a reference-based method (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) is preferred for supervised deconvolution

skills.description: Use when an SAW-processed spatial dataset (e.g., Stereo-seq with outUnMappedFq=1) carries expressed synthetic lineage barcodes and per-spot clone territories must be annotated and overlapped with matched bulk (GEO) and single-cell barcode annotations.
skills.name: spatial-clone-territory-mapping
skills.search_text: spatial-clone-territory-mapping Use when an SAW-processed spatial dataset (e.g., Stereo-seq with outUnMappedFq=1) carries expressed synthetic lineage barcodes and per-spot clone territories must be annotated and overlapped with matched bulk (GEO) and single-cell barcode annotations. The dataset is population-level (bulk) barcode sequencing only — use the BARtab bulk/paired-bulk workflow instead of spot-level annotation. The spatial platform is not SAW-based (e.g., 10x Visium) or the barcode construct lacks known flanking constant regions and a reference FASTA, so cutadapt constants and bowtie1 reference alignment cannot be specified. Barcode reads need PCR-chimera removal or UMI error correction (e.g., starcode-umi) as part of the count step — the spatial SAM-counting module used here intentionally omits these steps. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract SPLINTR lineage barcodes from Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics reads (SAW unmapped FASTQ) with BARtab's single-cell workflow, assign a dominant clone to each spatial spot, and map the spatial territories of the top-10 lineage barcodes for cross-validation against matched population-level and single-cell-level datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Extract SPLINTR lineage barcodes from Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics reads (SAW unmapped FASTQ) with BARtab's single-cell workflow, assign a dominant clone to each spatial spot, and map the spatial territories of the top-10 lineage barcodes for cross-validation against matched population-level and single-cell-level datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is population-level (bulk) barcode sequencing only — use the BARtab bulk/paired-bulk workflow instead of spot-level annotation. The spatial platform is not SAW-based (e.g., 10x Visium) or the barcode construct lacks known flanking constant regions and a reference FASTA, so cutadapt constants and bowtie1 reference alignment cannot be specified. Barcode reads need PCR-chimera removal or UMI error correction (e.g., starcode-umi) as part of the count step — the spatial SAM-counting module used here intentionally omits these steps.

skills.description: Use when a Seq-Scope, Slide-seq, or VISIUM spatial transcriptomics dataset has been clustered in Seurat (Step C3) and you need to visualize cell-type cluster identities across tissue coordinates, or to qualitatively compare MSSW versus simple-aggregation map resolution.
skills.name: spatial-cluster-map-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-cluster-map-visualization Use when a Seq-Scope, Slide-seq, or VISIUM spatial transcriptomics dataset has been clustered in Seurat (Step C3) and you need to visualize cell-type cluster identities across tissue coordinates, or to qualitatively compare MSSW versus simple-aggregation map resolution. Attempting subcellular-resolution spatial clustering maps: MSSW spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible When input is raw FASTQ or an uncollapsed spatial DGE — Steps A1–A3 and C1/C2 must run first before Step V2 can plot clusters When quantitative cluster-metric comparison is needed — the paper's validation is qualitative visual inspection of side-by-side maps, not a numerical resolution metric http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate UMAP embeddings and spatial cluster maps from STtools' Seurat objects (Step V2) to render cell-type identities across tissue coordinates, enabling side-by-side comparison of simple square-grid aggregation versus multiscale sliding window (MSSW) cluster maps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Generate UMAP embeddings and spatial cluster maps from STtools' Seurat objects (Step V2) to render cell-type identities across tissue coordinates, enabling side-by-side comparison of simple square-grid aggregation versus multiscale sliding window (MSSW) cluster maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Attempting subcellular-resolution spatial clustering maps: MSSW spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible When input is raw FASTQ or an uncollapsed spatial DGE — Steps A1–A3 and C1/C2 must run first before Step V2 can plot clusters When quantitative cluster-metric comparison is needed — the paper's validation is qualitative visual inspection of side-by-side maps, not a numerical resolution metric

skills.description: Use when an imputed APA index (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data (spots × poly(A) sites) needs to be partitioned into tissue layers, e.g., MOB sections, before layer-wise DEAPA or LSAPA tests.
skills.name: spatial-clustering-of-st-spots
skills.search_text: spatial-clustering-of-st-spots Use when an imputed APA index (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data (spots × poly(A) sites) needs to be partitioned into tissue layers, e.g., MOB sections, before layer-wise DEAPA or LSAPA tests. Input is raw poly(A)-site counts (APA.RDA) rather than a quantified and imputed APA-index matrix — quantification and KNN imputation must precede clustering Data are single-cell RNA-seq without spatial barcodes or coordinates — spots cannot be mapped to tissue layers and APA sites cannot be identified with scAPAtrap/Sierra from such data Image-based ST platforms (e.g., MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cluster spatially barcoded ST spots by their imputed APA usage (RUD) profiles using stAPAminer's Seurat-based clustering (makeStCluster), then assign clusters to morphological layers (GCL, GL, ONL, OPL, MCL) so APA usage can be compared across MOB anatomy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Cluster spatially barcoded ST spots by their imputed APA usage (RUD) profiles using stAPAminer's Seurat-based clustering (makeStCluster), then assign clusters to morphological layers (GCL, GL, ONL, OPL, MCL) so APA usage can be compared across MOB anatomy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw poly(A)-site counts (APA.RDA) rather than a quantified and imputed APA-index matrix — quantification and KNN imputation must precede clustering Data are single-cell RNA-seq without spatial barcodes or coordinates — spots cannot be mapped to tissue layers and APA sites cannot be identified with scAPAtrap/Sierra from such data Image-based ST platforms (e.g., MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools

skills.description: Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium slides of murine brain cortex or triple-negative breast cancer) must be converted into colocalized vs non-colocalized cell-type pairs to validate ligand-receptor predictions.
skills.name: spatial-colocalization-zscore-estimation
skills.search_text: spatial-colocalization-zscore-estimation Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium slides of murine brain cortex or triple-negative breast cancer) must be converted into colocalized vs non-colocalized cell-type pairs to validate ligand-receptor predictions. Input is single-cell (non-spatial) data only, with no spot-level deconvolution available — spatial colocalization z-scores cannot be computed and Squidpy adjacency on seqFISH/merFISH is the alternative. The goal is intracellular signalling inference (NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC), which the paper notes is not directly comparable to ligand-receptor methods benchmarked against spatial colocalization. The study concerns long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq gene expression does not capture. Quantifies whether cell types spatially co-occur by computing pairwise cell-type colocalization z-scores from SPOTlight deconvolved 10x Visium spot proportions, flagging colocalized pairs at z-score >= 1.645 (one-sided 95% threshold), to test agreement of prioritized CCC interactions with spatial adjacency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Quantifies whether cell types spatially co-occur by computing pairwise cell-type colocalization z-scores from SPOTlight deconvolved 10x Visium spot proportions, flagging colocalized pairs at z-score >= 1.645 (one-sided 95% threshold), to test agreement of prioritized CCC interactions with spatial adjacency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (non-spatial) data only, with no spot-level deconvolution available — spatial colocalization z-scores cannot be computed and Squidpy adjacency on seqFISH/merFISH is the alternative. The goal is intracellular signalling inference (NicheNet, Cytotalk, SoptSC), which the paper notes is not directly comparable to ligand-receptor methods benchmarked against spatial colocalization. The study concerns long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq gene expression does not capture.

skills.name: spatial-community-clustering
skills.search_text: spatial-community-clustering Use when single-cell x/y coordinates and marker intensities (e.g., MCMICRO-processed CyCIF data) are available and marker-positive populations must be grouped into spatial communities to delineate tumor boundaries and nested regions. Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery that has not yet been segmented into single cells — run MCMICRO first, since its output is the input of SpatialCells Marker gates have not been set (spatialcells.prep.setGates/setGates) — without thresholded marker labels there is no marker-defined cell population to cluster Analysis goal is graph-based neighborhood analysis without region delineation (e.g., Squidpy specializes in neighborhood graph construction and analysis) Clusters marker-defined cells (e.g., SOX10+ tumor cells from CyCIF multiplexed imaging) into spatial communities using SpatialCells' spatial module, providing the community structure from which region boundaries are derived for region-based TME analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Clusters marker-defined cells (e.g., SOX10+ tumor cells from CyCIF multiplexed imaging) into spatial communities using SpatialCells' spatial module, providing the community structure from which region boundaries are derived for region-based TME analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery that has not yet been segmented into single cells — run MCMICRO first, since its output is the input of SpatialCells Marker gates have not been set (spatialcells.prep.setGates/setGates) — without thresholded marker labels there is no marker-defined cell population to cluster Analysis goal is graph-based neighborhood analysis without region delineation (e.g., Squidpy specializes in neighborhood graph construction and analysis)

skills.description: Use when you have an expression matrix (e.g. a Visium AnnData/h5ad) with 2D spatial coordinates and want to rank all genes by non-random spatial activity, or compare SVG calls across methods like singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X.
skills.name: spatial-coordinate-based-feature-screening
skills.search_text: spatial-coordinate-based-feature-screening Use when you have an expression matrix (e.g. a Visium AnnData/h5ad) with 2D spatial coordinates and want to rank all genes by non-random spatial activity, or compare SVG calls across methods like singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X. The goal is differential expression between defined sample conditions (e.g. wild-type vs knockout) — the paper notes multi-condition comparisons cannot easily be conducted with singleCellHaystack. Runtime-critical large spatial screens where speed dominates sensitivity — the discussion notes singleCellHaystack has 'relatively longer runtimes compared to SPARK-X for spatial transcriptomics', though it is more sensitive. Analysis pipelines that are cluster-oriented, since singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-based scRNA-seq analyses. http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Screen all genes/features for spatially variable activity directly from 2D (or 3D) spatial coordinates using singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence approach, which detects non-random positioning of feature activity without clustering, and benchmark sensitivity against faster methods such as SPARK-X. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Screen all genes/features for spatially variable activity directly from 2D (or 3D) spatial coordinates using singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence approach, which detects non-random positioning of feature activity without clustering, and benchmark sensitivity against faster methods such as SPARK-X.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression between defined sample conditions (e.g. wild-type vs knockout) — the paper notes multi-condition comparisons cannot easily be conducted with singleCellHaystack. Runtime-critical large spatial screens where speed dominates sensitivity — the discussion notes singleCellHaystack has 'relatively longer runtimes compared to SPARK-X for spatial transcriptomics', though it is more sensitive. Analysis pipelines that are cluster-oriented, since singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-based scRNA-seq analyses.

skills.description: Use when an imaging-based spatial dataset (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain sections with per-cell x/y coordinates) needs anatomical registration to a reference atlas (Allen CCF 2020) to validate cell type annotations spatially.
skills.name: spatial-coordinate-mapping-to-brain-atlas
skills.search_text: spatial-coordinate-mapping-to-brain-atlas Use when an imaging-based spatial dataset (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain sections with per-cell x/y coordinates) needs anatomical registration to a reference atlas (Allen CCF 2020) to validate cell type annotations spatially. Input is non-spatial scRNA-seq data with no per-cell coordinates — no atlas registration is possible Tissue is not brain or the coordinates are not in the coordinate space of Allen CCF 2020 NIfTI reference images The dataset already carries authoritative anatomical region labels, making re-registration redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Registers imaging-based spatial transcriptomics cell coordinates (e.g., MERFISH coronal brain sections) onto the Allen CCF 2020 brain atlas via NIfTI images, providing anatomical ground truth against which predicted cell type annotations are spatially validated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60900-4
skills.summary: Registers imaging-based spatial transcriptomics cell coordinates (e.g., MERFISH coronal brain sections) onto the Allen CCF 2020 brain atlas via NIfTI images, providing anatomical ground truth against which predicted cell type annotations are spatially validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is non-spatial scRNA-seq data with no per-cell coordinates — no atlas registration is possible Tissue is not brain or the coordinates are not in the coordinate space of Allen CCF 2020 NIfTI reference images The dataset already carries authoritative anatomical region labels, making re-registration redundant

skills.name: spatial-coordinate-plotting
skills.search_text: spatial-coordinate-plotting Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics gene expression matrix plus per-cell spatial coordinates and need a 2D scatter/heatmap of one gene's expression across specified cell types to validate predicted cell–cell communication. The goal is constructing the cell–cell communication network itself — use the CPPLS-MLP CPPLS regression workflow (2023_01_*.RMD scripts) rather than its downstream plotting validation step Input data lack per-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., dissociated single-cell or bulk RNA-seq), since the visualization is inherently a 2D spatial coordinate plot A quantitative, statistically tested validation of communication-associated genes is required — the article's visualization is a qualitative confirmation, not a statistical test http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Renders the 2D spatial positions of cells from spatial transcriptomics datasets (Seq-Scope, seqFISH+) colored by a specific gene's expression level, to visually validate cell–cell communication predictions (e.g., GPX1 in B.cell_IgA/fibroblasts, CPLX1 in L5/L6 eNeurons) made by CPPLS-MLP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Renders the 2D spatial positions of cells from spatial transcriptomics datasets (Seq-Scope, seqFISH+) colored by a specific gene's expression level, to visually validate cell–cell communication predictions (e.g., GPX1 in B.cell_IgA/fibroblasts, CPLX1 in L5/L6 eNeurons) made by CPPLS-MLP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is constructing the cell–cell communication network itself — use the CPPLS-MLP CPPLS regression workflow (2023_01_*.RMD scripts) rather than its downstream plotting validation step Input data lack per-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., dissociated single-cell or bulk RNA-seq), since the visualization is inherently a 2D spatial coordinate plot A quantitative, statistically tested validation of communication-associated genes is required — the article's visualization is a qualitative confirmation, not a statistical test

skills.description: Use when visualizing single-cell spatial omics data (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl brain, STARmap, seqFISH, IMC datasets) and default color assignments from Seurat, Scanpy, Giotto, Squidpy, matplotlib, or ggplot2 produce perceptual ambiguity between neighboring, biologically distinct cell types.
skills.name: spatial-data-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-data-visualization Use when visualizing single-cell spatial omics data (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl brain, STARmap, seqFISH, IMC datasets) and default color assignments from Seurat, Scanpy, Giotto, Squidpy, matplotlib, or ggplot2 produce perceptual ambiguity between neighboring, biologically distinct cell types. Data is non-spatial (no spatial coordinates) — Spaco's DOI/CI-graph modeling relies on spatial interlacement between cell types Coloring hundreds of clusters or requiring strict CVD-supporting colorization — visual contrast obtainable through color space is limited in these cases per the paper's discussion User requires color differences to follow literature conventions rather than spatial distribution — Spaco enforces correspondence between color differences and spatial distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Spatially aware colorization of cellular-resolution spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) data using Spaco, which constructs a Degree of Interlacement (DOI)-weighted cluster interlacement graph to assign perceptually contrasting colors to adjacent cell types, with adaptive palette selection (including image-guided palette extraction) and CVD-supporting palettes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Spatially aware colorization of cellular-resolution spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) data using Spaco, which constructs a Degree of Interlacement (DOI)-weighted cluster interlacement graph to assign perceptually contrasting colors to adjacent cell types, with adaptive palette selection (including image-guided palette extraction) and CVD-supporting palettes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is non-spatial (no spatial coordinates) — Spaco's DOI/CI-graph modeling relies on spatial interlacement between cell types Coloring hundreds of clusters or requiring strict CVD-supporting colorization — visual contrast obtainable through color space is limited in these cases per the paper's discussion User requires color differences to follow literature conventions rather than spatial distribution — Spaco enforces correspondence between color differences and spatial distribution

skills.description: Use when you have a segmented cell-by-gene matrix from subcellular spatial data (e.g. Xenium) plus cell-type labels, and you need to test whether cell boundaries leak transcripts between adjacent cells.
skills.name: spatial-distance-stratified-marker-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: spatial-distance-stratified-marker-expression-analysis Use when you have a segmented cell-by-gene matrix from subcellular spatial data (e.g. Xenium) plus cell-type labels, and you need to test whether cell boundaries leak transcripts between adjacent cells. Input is raw Xenium transcripts or DAPI images rather than a segmentation-derived cell-by-gene matrix — run the BIDCell pipeline (preprocess/train/predict/make_cell_gene_mat) first. The tissue lacks adjacent, spatially intermingled cell types (e.g. no T cells near B cells), so distance-to-nearest-neighbour stratification is uninformative. The goal is nuclear-shape or boundary-quality assessment (e.g. CellSPA morphological categories) rather than transcript-level contamination between neighbours. Quantifies neighbour contamination in a segmentation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. BIDCell output on Xenium-BreastCancer1) by stratifying cells of one type (B cells) by distance to the nearest cell of another type (T cells) and computing the percentage expressing cross-lineage markers (CD4, CD8A, CD8B, CD3D, CD3E), mirroring Fig. 3e of the BIDCell paper. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44560-w
skills.summary: Quantifies neighbour contamination in a segmentation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. BIDCell output on Xenium-BreastCancer1) by stratifying cells of one type (B cells) by distance to the nearest cell of another type (T cells) and computing the percentage expressing cross-lineage markers (CD4, CD8A, CD8B, CD3D, CD3E), mirroring Fig. 3e of the BIDCell paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Xenium transcripts or DAPI images rather than a segmentation-derived cell-by-gene matrix — run the BIDCell pipeline (preprocess/train/predict/make_cell_gene_mat) first. The tissue lacks adjacent, spatially intermingled cell types (e.g. no T cells near B cells), so distance-to-nearest-neighbour stratification is uninformative. The goal is nuclear-shape or boundary-quality assessment (e.g. CellSPA morphological categories) rather than transcript-level contamination between neighbours.

skills.search_text: spatial-domain-clustering-model-selection Use when multiple spatial-domain clusterings (e.g. across alpha_options 0.05–0.95) must be ranked without ground-truth labels or manual ARI computation, to pick the optimal model configuration. Ground-truth domain annotations are available and ARI can be computed directly, making the annotation-free goodness score unnecessary The clustering output has already been fixed (no alpha_options or hyperparameter sweep to rank), so there is no model-selection decision to make Data has not been preprocessed yet (no PCs from top 2000 highly variable genes and no spot coordinates in preprocessed_data_folder) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes ScribbleDom's ARI-independent goodness score v(y,Cα)=q(y,Cα)∏p(yi|Ciα)p(Ciα) over candidate clusterings so the best hyperparameter setting (e.g. alpha_options) can be selected without manual annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
