skills.description: Use when running ScribbleDom training on Visium or ST spatial transcriptomics samples (e.g. bcdc_ffpe, melanoma, human DLPFC) with either expert manual_scribble.csv or Mclust-generated automated scribbles, and you need to tune the scribble-dropout rate beta.
skills.name: spatial-domain-detection-semi-supervised-training
skills.search_text: spatial-domain-detection-semi-supervised-training Use when running ScribbleDom training on Visium or ST spatial transcriptomics samples (e.g. bcdc_ffpe, melanoma, human DLPFC) with either expert manual_scribble.csv or Mclust-generated automated scribbles, and you need to tune the scribble-dropout rate beta. Input is not spatial transcriptomics spot data (Visium or ST platform) — the pipeline expects tissue_positions_list.csv, scalefactors_json.json, and filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 or sample .rds No scribble source is available and a fully supervised expert workflow is required — without manual_scribble.csv you get only AutoScribbleDom results The goal is domain detection on single-cell (non-spatial) data without histology images or spot coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Train the ScribbleDom semi-supervised convolutional network to identify spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data, using Scribble Dropout (rate beta, swept 0.25–0.4) to counter residual noise in automatically generated scribbles, with alpha swept 0.05–0.95 via grid search. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: Train the ScribbleDom semi-supervised convolutional network to identify spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data, using Scribble Dropout (rate beta, swept 0.25–0.4) to counter residual noise in automatically generated scribbles, with alpha swept 0.05–0.95 via grid search.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not spatial transcriptomics spot data (Visium or ST platform) — the pipeline expects tissue_positions_list.csv, scalefactors_json.json, and filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 or sample .rds No scribble source is available and a fully supervised expert workflow is required — without manual_scribble.csv you get only AutoScribbleDom results The goal is domain detection on single-cell (non-spatial) data without histology images or spot coordinates

skills.description: Use when you must quantify whether scSpace's space-informed clustering outperforms existing clustering or spatial-domain identification methods on data where ground-truth subcluster labels (e.g., Splatter simulations) are available.
skills.name: spatial-domain-identification-baseline-evaluation
skills.search_text: spatial-domain-identification-baseline-evaluation Use when you must quantify whether scSpace's space-informed clustering outperforms existing clustering or spatial-domain identification methods on data where ground-truth subcluster labels (e.g., Splatter simulations) are available. The goal is spatial-domain identification of ST data itself — the article stresses scSpace 'focuses on the spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data whereas other methods target the spatial domain identification of ST data', so baselines like SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC are not directly comparable in that setting No ground-truth subcluster labels exist (e.g., purely biological datasets), making ARI-based benchmarking against reference labels impossible The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), where scSpace and its benchmark interpretation should be applied cautiously http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark scSpace against clustering baselines (Louvain/Leiden, K-means, hierarchical clustering) and spatial-domain methods (SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC) using adjusted Rand index (ARI) on simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST datasets with ground-truth subcluster labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38121-4
skills.summary: Benchmark scSpace against clustering baselines (Louvain/Leiden, K-means, hierarchical clustering) and spatial-domain methods (SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC) using adjusted Rand index (ARI) on simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST datasets with ground-truth subcluster labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is spatial-domain identification of ST data itself — the article stresses scSpace 'focuses on the spatial analysis of scRNA-seq data whereas other methods target the spatial domain identification of ST data', so baselines like SpaGCN/BayesSpace/DR-SC are not directly comparable in that setting No ground-truth subcluster labels exist (e.g., purely biological datasets), making ARI-based benchmarking against reference labels impossible The tissue has low spatial coherence (e.g., SCC Patients 5 and 9 in the paper), where scSpace and its benchmark interpretation should be applied cautiously

skills.description: Use when you have several spatial transcriptomics slices (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) with Spoint-derived per-spot cell type proportions and need uniform spatial domain labels across slices, plus a quantitative joint-vs-single comparison.
skills.name: spatial-domain-identification-gcn
skills.search_text: spatial-domain-identification-gcn Use when you have several spatial transcriptomics slices (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) with Spoint-derived per-spot cell type proportions and need uniform spatial domain labels across slices, plus a quantitative joint-vs-single comparison. Input is a single ST slice with no plan for cross-slice comparison — the joint adversarial training has no batch-effect target to act on; use Splane-single instead For seq-based ST datasets like 10X Visium where cell type deconvolution has not been run — Splane depends on Spoint composition input and cannot be applied directly to raw expression A new slice is added to an already-trained dataset — SPACEL requires retraining the entire model from scratch, which may be computationally prohibitive http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Identify spatial domains that are transcriptomically and spatially coherent across multiple ST slices by training Splane's graph convolutional network with an adversarial learning algorithm on cell type composition input, and benchmark the joint model against per-slice (Splane-single) runs using Jaccard index, median ARI, and shifting distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Identify spatial domains that are transcriptomically and spatially coherent across multiple ST slices by training Splane's graph convolutional network with an adversarial learning algorithm on cell type composition input, and benchmark the joint model against per-slice (Splane-single) runs using Jaccard index, median ARI, and shifting distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single ST slice with no plan for cross-slice comparison — the joint adversarial training has no batch-effect target to act on; use Splane-single instead For seq-based ST datasets like 10X Visium where cell type deconvolution has not been run — Splane depends on Spoint composition input and cannot be applied directly to raw expression A new slice is added to an already-trained dataset — SPACEL requires retraining the entire model from scratch, which may be computationally prohibitive

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq data lacking spatial coordinates and a trained CeLEry spatial-domain model (e.g., LIBD DLPFC sections), and need to assign each cell to a tissue layer or spatial domain.
skills.name: spatial-domain-recovery-in-snrnaseq
skills.search_text: spatial-domain-recovery-in-snrnaseq Use when you have single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq data lacking spatial coordinates and a trained CeLEry spatial-domain model (e.g., LIBD DLPFC sections), and need to assign each cell to a tissue layer or spatial domain. The query data are single-cell-resolution ST platform data with small targeted gene panels (MERFISH/MERSCOPE/Xenium-style panels) — CeLEry is suboptimal on small gene panels and awaits transcriptome-wide single-cell-resolution ST Cells already carry spatial coordinates or the goal is 2D coordinate recovery rather than categorical spatial domain / layer assignment No trained spatial-domain model exists for the relevant tissue and no ST training sections are available to train one http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Recover the spatial domain (e.g., cortical layer L1-L6/WM) of dissociated snRNA-seq cells by applying a pretrained CeLEry supervised deep neural network that learned gene-expression-to-location relationships from spatial transcriptomics training sections, with per-cell uncertainty estimates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Recover the spatial domain (e.g., cortical layer L1-L6/WM) of dissociated snRNA-seq cells by applying a pretrained CeLEry supervised deep neural network that learned gene-expression-to-location relationships from spatial transcriptomics training sections, with per-cell uncertainty estimates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data are single-cell-resolution ST platform data with small targeted gene panels (MERFISH/MERSCOPE/Xenium-style panels) — CeLEry is suboptimal on small gene panels and awaits transcriptome-wide single-cell-resolution ST Cells already carry spatial coordinates or the goal is 2D coordinate recovery rather than categorical spatial domain / layer assignment No trained spatial-domain model exists for the relevant tissue and no ST training sections are available to train one

skills.description: Use when you need to render gene expression as 2D spatial maps keyed to spot/cell coordinates — e.g. visually validating CeLEry-predicted 2D coordinates against known spatial gradients (ERBB2, ESR1, GATA3) or inspecting VAE-generated ST replicates against originals.
skills.name: spatial-expression-map-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-expression-map-visualization Use when you need to render gene expression as 2D spatial maps keyed to spot/cell coordinates — e.g. visually validating CeLEry-predicted 2D coordinates against known spatial gradients (ERBB2, ESR1, GATA3) or inspecting VAE-generated ST replicates against originals. The query data has no spatial anchoring — plain scRNA-seq cells without recovered 2D coordinates cannot be placed into a spatial map The goal is quantitative benchmarking (pairwise-distance correlations, median Euclidean distances) rather than visual inspection of recovered gradients The training ST data is a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel, where CeLEry itself is suboptimal and maps may not reflect reliable gradients http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Renders gene expression as 2D spatial maps arranged by spot/cell coordinates — used with CeLEry to plot recovered marker-gene gradients (ERBB2, ESR1, GATA3) in predicted-coordinate space and to compare VAE-generated ST replicates against original expression maps as PNG figures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Renders gene expression as 2D spatial maps arranged by spot/cell coordinates — used with CeLEry to plot recovered marker-gene gradients (ERBB2, ESR1, GATA3) in predicted-coordinate space and to compare VAE-generated ST replicates against original expression maps as PNG figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query data has no spatial anchoring — plain scRNA-seq cells without recovered 2D coordinates cannot be placed into a spatial map The goal is quantitative benchmarking (pairwise-distance correlations, median Euclidean distances) rather than visual inspection of recovered gradients The training ST data is a single-cell-resolution platform with a small gene panel, where CeLEry itself is suboptimal and maps may not reflect reliable gradients

skills.description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from ultra-high-resolution ST platforms (Seq-Scope <1μm, Slide-seq 10μm, VISIUM 100μm) must be converted into a spatially annotated DGE with millions of spatial barcodes per mm².
skills.name: spatial-expression-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: spatial-expression-matrix-processing Use when raw FASTQ reads from ultra-high-resolution ST platforms (Seq-Scope <1μm, Slide-seq 10μm, VISIUM 100μm) must be converted into a spatially annotated DGE with millions of spatial barcodes per mm². Input is already a DGE with spatial coordinates (externally supplied matrix) — skip alignment steps A1–A3 and go directly to visualization or clustering Data are single-cell RNA-seq without spatial barcodes — STARsolo spatial whitelisting and coordinate extraction do not apply Subcellular-resolution inference via the MSSW (sliding window) strategy is requested — spatial segments must exceed ~10μm, larger than subcellular compartments, so MSSW subcellular analysis is not feasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Process raw Seq-Scope/Slide-seq/VISIUM FASTQ data into spatially annotated digital expression matrices (DGE) with STtools, using STARsolo alignment against a STAR genome index and retaining per-barcode spatial coordinates for downstream ultra-high-resolution analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Process raw Seq-Scope/Slide-seq/VISIUM FASTQ data into spatially annotated digital expression matrices (DGE) with STtools, using STARsolo alignment against a STAR genome index and retaining per-barcode spatial coordinates for downstream ultra-high-resolution analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a DGE with spatial coordinates (externally supplied matrix) — skip alignment steps A1–A3 and go directly to visualization or clustering Data are single-cell RNA-seq without spatial barcodes — STARsolo spatial whitelisting and coordinate extraction do not apply Subcellular-resolution inference via the MSSW (sliding window) strategy is requested — spatial segments must exceed ~10μm, larger than subcellular compartments, so MSSW subcellular analysis is not feasible

skills.description: Use when a sparse APA usage (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data must be imputed using spot–spot distances derived from a scaled gene-spot expression profile (e.g., count.csv + APA.RDA inputs).
skills.name: spatial-expression-matrix-scaling
skills.search_text: spatial-expression-matrix-scaling Use when a sparse APA usage (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data must be imputed using spot–spot distances derived from a scaled gene-spot expression profile (e.g., count.csv + APA.RDA inputs). The APA usage matrix is already dense/imputed — re-imputation with KNN would overwrite valid RUD values Data are not spatially barcoded ST (e.g., MERFISH/seqFISH), since APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra No gene expression profile is available alongside the poly(A) site matrix, because the spot–spot distance ranking depends entirely on expression similarity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Scales the gene-spot expression count matrix of spatially barcoded ST data to derive a spot–spot distance ranking matrix, which stAPAminer then uses to drive KNN-based imputation of the sparse APA usage (RUD) matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Scales the gene-spot expression count matrix of spatially barcoded ST data to derive a spot–spot distance ranking matrix, which stAPAminer then uses to drive KNN-based imputation of the sparse APA usage (RUD) matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The APA usage matrix is already dense/imputed — re-imputation with KNN would overwrite valid RUD values Data are not spatially barcoded ST (e.g., MERFISH/seqFISH), since APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra No gene expression profile is available alongside the poly(A) site matrix, because the spot–spot distance ranking depends entirely on expression similarity

skills.description: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Genomics Visium spots with GetTissueCoordinates) and need to identify spatially patterned genes without first defining spot clusters.
skills.name: spatial-feature-plot-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-feature-plot-visualization Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Genomics Visium spots with GetTissueCoordinates) and need to identify spatially patterned genes without first defining spot clusters. Your input space is an embedding such as t-SNE/UMAP/PCA from a non-spatial single-cell experiment rather than actual physical tissue coordinates — use the 2D/PCA workflow variants instead You need continuous expression levels (not binary detected/not-detected) to drive the analysis — the current implementation only accepts binary detection data with a hard threshold Genes are expressed in very few spots (fewer than 10 non-zero counts) and are not biologically relevant — they should be filtered out before running to save computation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A clustering-independent spatial DEG workflow that runs singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence-based haystack() on the real 2D tissue coordinates of 10x Visium spots (rather than an embedding) plus a normalized, detection-binarized expression matrix, to find genes spatially regulated across tissue structures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17900-3
skills.summary: A clustering-independent spatial DEG workflow that runs singleCellHaystack's Kullback-Leibler divergence-based haystack() on the real 2D tissue coordinates of 10x Visium spots (rather than an embedding) plus a normalized, detection-binarized expression matrix, to find genes spatially regulated across tissue structures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input space is an embedding such as t-SNE/UMAP/PCA from a non-spatial single-cell experiment rather than actual physical tissue coordinates — use the 2D/PCA workflow variants instead You need continuous expression levels (not binary detected/not-detected) to drive the analysis — the current implementation only accepts binary detection data with a hard threshold Genes are expressed in very few spots (fewer than 10 non-zero counts) and are not biologically relevant — they should be filtered out before running to save computation

skills.description: Use when TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize directly and you need to map a regulome-level activity (aggregated GRN target genes) onto heart tissue sections to localize fibrotic regulatory programs.
skills.name: spatial-feature-plotting-in-heart-tissue-sections
skills.search_text: spatial-feature-plotting-in-heart-tissue-sections Use when TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize directly and you need to map a regulome-level activity (aggregated GRN target genes) onto heart tissue sections to localize fibrotic regulatory programs. Direct TF expression in the spatial object is sufficiently dense to plot without regulome aggregation — plotting individual genes would suffice. The spatial data is not myocardial/fibrotic tissue or lacks a normalized spatial assay and spatial coordinates in a Seurat object. No inferred GRN edge list (e.g. df.grn2/final_grn.Rds) exists, so no target-gene sets are available to aggregate into regulome scores. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Overlay aggregated TF regulome scores (e.g. NR3C2, RUNX1 target-gene mean expression) onto the spatial coordinates of the Kuppe et al. 2022 human myocardial infarction spatial transcriptomics object using scMEGA's GRNSpatialPlot, since direct TF expression is too sparse in spatial spots. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad003
skills.summary: Overlay aggregated TF regulome scores (e.g. NR3C2, RUNX1 target-gene mean expression) onto the spatial coordinates of the Kuppe et al. 2022 human myocardial infarction spatial transcriptomics object using scMEGA's GRNSpatialPlot, since direct TF expression is too sparse in spatial spots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Direct TF expression in the spatial object is sufficiently dense to plot without regulome aggregation — plotting individual genes would suffice. The spatial data is not myocardial/fibrotic tissue or lacks a normalized spatial assay and spatial coordinates in a Seurat object. No inferred GRN edge list (e.g. df.grn2/final_grn.Rds) exists, so no target-gene sets are available to aggregate into regulome scores.

skills.description: Use when a diagonal integration predicts expression for genes absent from one spatial modality (e.g. smFISH) and you need to inspect the imputed spatial patterns and quantify their agreement with held-out measurements.
skills.name: spatial-gene-expression-pattern-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-gene-expression-pattern-visualization Use when a diagonal integration predicts expression for genes absent from one spatial modality (e.g. smFISH) and you need to inspect the imputed spatial patterns and quantify their agreement with held-out measurements. The gene of interest is already measured in the smFISH experiment, so its spatial pattern can be read directly without imputation No cross-modality feature connections exist between modalities (e.g. integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities The data are paired single-cell multimodal measurements; scConfluence targets diagonal (unpaired) integration and does not jointly integrate paired with unpaired data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Visualize spatial expression patterns for genes predicted by scConfluence's cross-modality imputation — specifically genes measured in scRNA-seq but not in the smFISH assay (Scgn, Synpr, Olah) in the mouse somatosensory cortex — and benchmark imputation quality with average/median Spearman correlations against measured smFISH patterns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-51382-x
skills.summary: Visualize spatial expression patterns for genes predicted by scConfluence's cross-modality imputation — specifically genes measured in scRNA-seq but not in the smFISH assay (Scgn, Synpr, Olah) in the mouse somatosensory cortex — and benchmark imputation quality with average/median Spearman correlations against measured smFISH patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene of interest is already measured in the smFISH experiment, so its spatial pattern can be read directly without imputation No cross-modality feature connections exist between modalities (e.g. integrating electrophysiology with gene expression), since scConfluence relies on connections between features of different modalities The data are paired single-cell multimodal measurements; scConfluence targets diagonal (unpaired) integration and does not jointly integrate paired with unpaired data

skills.description: Use when you have paired non-spatial scRNA-seq data and spatial in situ/spatial transcriptomics measurements of a subset of genes (e.g., Drosophila embryo bdtnp.txt with geometry.txt) and need to predict spatial expression of unmeasured genes or benchmark reconstruction accuracy by LOOCV.
skills.name: spatial-gene-expression-prediction
skills.search_text: spatial-gene-expression-prediction Use when you have paired non-spatial scRNA-seq data and spatial in situ/spatial transcriptomics measurements of a subset of genes (e.g., Drosophila embryo bdtnp.txt with geometry.txt) and need to predict spatial expression of unmeasured genes or benchmark reconstruction accuracy by LOOCV. When the scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large — the article notes computation can become intractable; use landmark approximation or another method When the goal is to infer time-delayed cell-cell communication (ligand diffusion / intracellular cascade timing) — the approach does not consider time delay When the input already has full spatial transcriptomics per gene and no mapping from scRNA-seq is needed — direct spatial analysis pipelines are more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predicts spatial expression of genes at tissue positions by mapping scRNA-seq cells onto spatial measurement positions via SpaOTsc's structured/unbalanced optimal transport, then computing a transport-plan-weighted average of gene expression. This enables reconstruction and leave-one-out cross-validation of spatial gene expression when only a small set of genes has spatial measurements. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Predicts spatial expression of genes at tissue positions by mapping scRNA-seq cells onto spatial measurement positions via SpaOTsc's structured/unbalanced optimal transport, then computing a transport-plan-weighted average of gene expression. This enables reconstruction and leave-one-out cross-validation of spatial gene expression when only a small set of genes has spatial measurements.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the scRNA-seq dataset is excessively large — the article notes computation can become intractable; use landmark approximation or another method When the goal is to infer time-delayed cell-cell communication (ligand diffusion / intracellular cascade timing) — the approach does not consider time delay When the input already has full spatial transcriptomics per gene and no mapping from scRNA-seq is needed — direct spatial analysis pipelines are more appropriate

skills.description: Use when a predicted cell–cell communication pair (e.g., immature B cells–fibroblasts, L5–L6 eNeurons) needs spatial validation by overlaying a specific gene's expression on cell coordinates from spatial transcriptomics data.
skills.name: spatial-gene-expression-visualization
skills.search_text: spatial-gene-expression-visualization Use when a predicted cell–cell communication pair (e.g., immature B cells–fibroblasts, L5–L6 eNeurons) needs spatial validation by overlaying a specific gene's expression on cell coordinates from spatial transcriptomics data. The goal is to construct or score the cell–cell communication network itself rather than validate an already-predicted communication pair with a gene-expression overlay The input data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., bulk or non-spatial scRNA-seq), so no 2D spatial distribution can be plotted The candidate gene has zero expression across all cells of the target cell type, which the pipeline removes before downstream analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Two-dimensional spatial scatter/heatmap plots of a candidate communication-associated gene (e.g., GPX1 on Seq-Scope, CPLX1 on seqFISH+) colored by expression level in interacting cell types, used to visually validate cell–cell communication networks predicted by CPPLS-MLP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Two-dimensional spatial scatter/heatmap plots of a candidate communication-associated gene (e.g., GPX1 on Seq-Scope, CPLX1 on seqFISH+) colored by expression level in interacting cell types, used to visually validate cell–cell communication networks predicted by CPPLS-MLP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to construct or score the cell–cell communication network itself rather than validate an already-predicted communication pair with a gene-expression overlay The input data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., bulk or non-spatial scRNA-seq), so no 2D spatial distribution can be plotted The candidate gene has zero expression across all cells of the target cell type, which the pipeline removes before downstream analysis

skills.description: Use when non-spatial scRNA-seq data has been equipped with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix (e.g., via SpaOTsc optimal transport) and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell affects which gene in a neighbor cell across spatial ranges.

skills.search_text: spatial-gene-regulatory-inference Use when non-spatial scRNA-seq data has been equipped with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix (e.g., via SpaOTsc optimal transport) and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell affects which gene in a neighbor cell across spatial ranges. When no spatial measurements of a small set of genes are available to build the cell–cell distance matrix via optimal transport When the dataset is excessively large, since cell–cell distance inference over all cell pairs can become computationally intractable When studying time-resolved signaling where ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade time delays must be modeled — this approach does not consider time delay http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Constructs a spatial map of intercellular gene–gene regulatory information flow from scRNA-seq data by quantifying unique information (via partial information decomposition) between a source gene's η-neighborhood expression and a target gene, using SpaOTsc cell–cell distances. Applied to the Drosophila embryo to recover regulations such as Twist affecting Snail across ~25 µm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Constructs a spatial map of intercellular gene–gene regulatory information flow from scRNA-seq data by quantifying unique information (via partial information decomposition) between a source gene's η-neighborhood expression and a target gene, using SpaOTsc cell–cell distances. Applied to the Drosophila embryo to recover regulations such as Twist affecting Snail across ~25 µm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no spatial measurements of a small set of genes are available to build the cell–cell distance matrix via optimal transport When the dataset is excessively large, since cell–cell distance inference over all cell pairs can become computationally intractable When studying time-resolved signaling where ligand diffusion or intracellular cascade time delays must be modeled — this approach does not consider time delay

skills.description: Use when single-cell spatially resolved transcriptomics data (SRT) has been clustered and cell-type colors must be assigned so that spatially interlaced/adjacent clusters get maximally contrasting colors from a limited palette.
skills.name: spatial-interlacement-graph-analysis
skills.search_text: spatial-interlacement-graph-analysis Use when single-cell spatially resolved transcriptomics data (SRT) has been clustered and cell-type colors must be assigned so that spatially interlaced/adjacent clusters get maximally contrasting colors from a limited palette. Clusters are spatially isolated with no interlacement — the CI-graph carries little signal and default framework colorization (Seurat/Giotto/Scanpy/Squidpy via matplotlib or ggplot2) suffices User has fixed colors for specific cell types that must not be optimized, or literature-conventional colors must be preserved — Spaco enforces color-difference correspondence to spatial distribution rather than user preference http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs Spaco's cluster interlacement graph (CI-graph) from the Degree of Interlacement between cell-type pairs and solves its optimal one-to-one matching to the color-difference (CD-graph) target via coarse-to-fine stochastic permutation optimization, so heavily interlaced neighboring clusters receive more distinct colors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Constructs Spaco's cluster interlacement graph (CI-graph) from the Degree of Interlacement between cell-type pairs and solves its optimal one-to-one matching to the color-difference (CD-graph) target via coarse-to-fine stochastic permutation optimization, so heavily interlaced neighboring clusters receive more distinct colors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clusters are spatially isolated with no interlacement — the CI-graph carries little signal and default framework colorization (Seurat/Giotto/Scanpy/Squidpy via matplotlib or ggplot2) suffices User has fixed colors for specific cell types that must not be optimized, or literature-conventional colors must be preserved — Spaco enforces color-difference correspondence to spatial distribution rather than user preference

skills.description: Use when analyzing cellular-resolution SRT data (e.g., STARmap, seqFISH, Stereo-seq, IMC) to quantify how interlaced two cell-type clusters are, or to verify that DOI-guided colorization yields color differences proportional to spatial interlacement.
skills.name: spatial-interlacement-quantification
skills.search_text: spatial-interlacement-quantification Use when analyzing cellular-resolution SRT data (e.g., STARmap, seqFISH, Stereo-seq, IMC) to quantify how interlaced two cell-type clusters are, or to verify that DOI-guided colorization yields color differences proportional to spatial interlacement. Data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., bulk or non-spatial scRNA-seq) — the CI-graph and DOI require spatial interlacement between clusters Goal is to score batch correction or label agreement (e.g., ARI/NMI/LISI via scPOP) rather than spatial relationships between cell types A fixed color mapping is desired that respects literature conventions or user preferences rather than spatially driven color differences (a stated limitation of Spaco) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies the spatial relationship between cell-type pairs in single-cell spatial transcriptomics (SRT) data using Spaco's Degree of Interlacement (DOI) metric and cluster interlacement graph (CI-graph), and validates its contribution to color assignment by regressing realized pairwise color differences (CIEDE2000) on DOI scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2023.100915
skills.summary: Quantifies the spatial relationship between cell-type pairs in single-cell spatial transcriptomics (SRT) data using Spaco's Degree of Interlacement (DOI) metric and cluster interlacement graph (CI-graph), and validates its contribution to color assignment by regressing realized pairwise color differences (CIEDE2000) on DOI scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., bulk or non-spatial scRNA-seq) — the CI-graph and DOI require spatial interlacement between clusters Goal is to score batch correction or label agreement (e.g., ARI/NMI/LISI via scPOP) rather than spatial relationships between cell types A fixed color mapping is desired that respects literature conventions or user preferences rather than spatially driven color differences (a stated limitation of Spaco)

skills.description: Use when analyzing spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium stxBrain anterior1) to find GO/pathway gene sets whose activity is spatially organized across or within transcriptomic clusters, including high-order patterns missed by cluster-centric analysis.
skills.name: spatial-kde-density-weighting
skills.search_text: spatial-kde-density-weighting Use when analyzing spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium stxBrain anterior1) to find GO/pathway gene sets whose activity is spatially organized across or within transcriptomic clusters, including high-order patterns missed by cluster-centric analysis. Input is targeted gene data with limited numbers of genes (e.g., targeted panels) — GSDensity spatial analysis is only applicable to spatial whole transcriptomic data; imputation of unmeasured genes is suggested but not implemented The dataset has no spatial coordinate information (plain scRNA-seq) — use the density/coordination (compute.kld) and label propagation workflow instead Gene sets have not passed the coordination test — binarization/propagation downstream steps are recommended only on gene sets passing the KLD cutoff http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 GSDensity's weighted-KDE approach for identifying spatially relevant pathways: pathway activity scores from random-walk propagation are used as cell weights in a 2D KDE on spatial coordinates, and the weighted density is tested against an equal-weighted null via permutation-based KL divergence (compute.spatial.kld / compute.spatial.kld.df). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: GSDensity's weighted-KDE approach for identifying spatially relevant pathways: pathway activity scores from random-walk propagation are used as cell weights in a 2D KDE on spatial coordinates, and the weighted density is tested against an equal-weighted null via permutation-based KL divergence (compute.spatial.kld / compute.spatial.kld.df).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is targeted gene data with limited numbers of genes (e.g., targeted panels) — GSDensity spatial analysis is only applicable to spatial whole transcriptomic data; imputation of unmeasured genes is suggested but not implemented The dataset has no spatial coordinate information (plain scRNA-seq) — use the density/coordination (compute.kld) and label propagation workflow instead Gene sets have not passed the coordination test — binarization/propagation downstream steps are recommended only on gene sets passing the KLD cutoff

skills.description: Use when spatial transcriptomics slides come with per-cell spatial coordinates and the goal is to remove local spatial-neighborhood effects to reveal global cell subpopulations hidden by spatial autocorrelation.
skills.name: spatial-kernel-construction-from-coordinates
skills.search_text: spatial-kernel-construction-from-coordinates Use when spatial transcriptomics slides come with per-cell spatial coordinates and the goal is to remove local spatial-neighborhood effects to reveal global cell subpopulations hidden by spatial autocorrelation. When the goal is the opposite — enhancing or studying the spatial zonation/localization signal itself rather than removing it (e.g., the paper's circadian-zonation example filters spatial signal only to enhance the temporal circadian signal) When no per-cell spatial coordinates are available to define the similarity kernel, or when the signal of interest is batch rather than spatial (integration methods like bbknn, Harmony, or scVI are the paper's examples for that task) When downstream tasks require properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so the filtered data is no longer properly log-transformed http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 Constructs a cell-cell similarity kernel directly from spatial transcriptomics coordinates (e.g., a SiFT KnnKernel or distance kernel) so that the local spatial neighborhood signal can be projected out and filtered from expression data. In the APAP-induced liver regeneration dataset (GSE223561), this exposes global migratory subpopulations (ANXA2+ hepatocytes) otherwise obscured by local neighborhoods. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Constructs a cell-cell similarity kernel directly from spatial transcriptomics coordinates (e.g., a SiFT KnnKernel or distance kernel) so that the local spatial neighborhood signal can be projected out and filtered from expression data. In the APAP-induced liver regeneration dataset (GSE223561), this exposes global migratory subpopulations (ANXA2+ hepatocytes) otherwise obscured by local neighborhoods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is the opposite — enhancing or studying the spatial zonation/localization signal itself rather than removing it (e.g., the paper's circadian-zonation example filters spatial signal only to enhance the temporal circadian signal) When no per-cell spatial coordinates are available to define the similarity kernel, or when the signal of interest is batch rather than spatial (integration methods like bbknn, Harmony, or scVI are the paper's examples for that task) When downstream tasks require properly log-transformed expression — SiFT modifies gene expression so the filtered data is no longer properly log-transformed

skills.description: Use when you need to recover the spatial origin (e.g., cortical layer L1–L6) of individual cells from non-spatial scRNA-seq data by mapping them onto a spatially resolved dataset with layer annotations via optimal transport.
skills.name: spatial-layer-origin-assignment
skills.search_text: spatial-layer-origin-assignment Use when you need to recover the spatial origin (e.g., cortical layer L1–L6) of individual cells from non-spatial scRNA-seq data by mapping them onto a spatially resolved dataset with layer annotations via optimal transport. The scRNA-seq data already contains spatial coordinates or the spatial data lacks layer/region annotations to transport onto The spatial and transcriptomic datasets share too few genes to build a meaningful common space (direct correlation between the 1020 STARmap genes and scRNA-seq is noisy without the CCA step) The goal is de novo spatial transcriptomics analysis (e.g., Giotto pipelines) rather than mapping existing scRNA-seq cells onto spatial positions http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Assigns each cell in a non-spatial scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Allen Brain Atlas mouse visual cortex scRNA-seq) to a spatial region/layer (L1–L6) by combining SpaOTsc's structured/unbalanced optimal transport mapping with layer-annotated STARmap positions, and evaluates the assignment as multiclass micro F1. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Assigns each cell in a non-spatial scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Allen Brain Atlas mouse visual cortex scRNA-seq) to a spatial region/layer (L1–L6) by combining SpaOTsc's structured/unbalanced optimal transport mapping with layer-annotated STARmap positions, and evaluates the assignment as multiclass micro F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq data already contains spatial coordinates or the spatial data lacks layer/region annotations to transport onto The spatial and transcriptomic datasets share too few genes to build a meaningful common space (direct correlation between the 1020 STARmap genes and scRNA-seq is noisy without the CCA step) The goal is de novo spatial transcriptomics analysis (e.g., Giotto pipelines) rather than mapping existing scRNA-seq cells onto spatial positions

skills.description: Use when a supervised location-recovery model (e.g., CeLEry) must be compared against mapping baselines on the same spatial transcriptomics/scRNA-seq splits, using pairwise-distance Pearson correlation as the headline metric.
skills.name: spatial-mapping-baseline-benchmarking
skills.search_text: spatial-mapping-baseline-benchmarking Use when a supervised location-recovery model (e.g., CeLEry) must be compared against mapping baselines on the same spatial transcriptomics/scRNA-seq splits, using pairwise-distance Pearson correlation as the headline metric. The task is spatial domain/layer classification with categorical labels rather than continuous 2D coordinate recovery — CeLEry's output layer and metric differ (categorical output, differentially expressed genes via Scanpy). No spatial transcriptomics reference with known locations exists for training, since all compared methods require ST data to learn or infer the mapping. Single-cell-resolution platforms with small gene panels are the only option — CeLEry is reportedly suboptimal in that regime. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark a spatial location recovery method (CeLEry) against baseline spatial mapping methods — Tangram, spaOTsc, and novoSpaRc — on shared train/test splits, scoring recovery quality by the Pearson correlation between pairwise Euclidean-distance matrices of true and predicted 2D coordinates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Benchmark a spatial location recovery method (CeLEry) against baseline spatial mapping methods — Tangram, spaOTsc, and novoSpaRc — on shared train/test splits, scoring recovery quality by the Pearson correlation between pairwise Euclidean-distance matrices of true and predicted 2D coordinates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is spatial domain/layer classification with categorical labels rather than continuous 2D coordinate recovery — CeLEry's output layer and metric differ (categorical output, differentially expressed genes via Scanpy). No spatial transcriptomics reference with known locations exists for training, since all compared methods require ST data to learn or infer the mapping. Single-cell-resolution platforms with small gene panels are the only option — CeLEry is reportedly suboptimal in that regime.

skills.description: Use when STEM (or another SC-ST mapper) has assigned cells/labels to ST spots and you need to confirm localization of a rare cell type by testing marker-gene expression differences between localized and non-localized spots.
skills.name: spatial-marker-gene-expression-comparison
skills.search_text: spatial-marker-gene-expression-comparison Use when STEM (or another SC-ST mapper) has assigned cells/labels to ST spots and you need to confirm localization of a rare cell type by testing marker-gene expression differences between localized and non-localized spots. When no spatial localization of the cell type has been established yet — the comparison presupposes a prior SC-ST mapping that defines 'localized' vs. 'other' spots When the marker genes are not detectably expressed in the ST data (high dropout may preclude a meaningful spot-level comparison) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compares expression of marker genes between spatially localized and other spots in an ST dataset after SC-ST mapping, to validate whether a rare cell type (e.g. plasmacytoid dendritic cells) is genuinely enriched at its predicted spatial location. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05640-1
skills.summary: Compares expression of marker genes between spatially localized and other spots in an ST dataset after SC-ST mapping, to validate whether a rare cell type (e.g. plasmacytoid dendritic cells) is genuinely enriched at its predicted spatial location.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no spatial localization of the cell type has been established yet — the comparison presupposes a prior SC-ST mapping that defines 'localized' vs. 'other' spots When the marker genes are not detectably expressed in the ST data (high dropout may preclude a meaningful spot-level comparison)

skills.description: Use when an OT-plan or label-transfer deconvolution of a spatial slice (e.g., 10x Visium) yields per-spot cell-type proportions and you must confirm biological plausibility against layer anatomy and marker-gene expression before accepting the result.
skills.name: spatial-marker-gene-validation
skills.search_text: spatial-marker-gene-validation Use when an OT-plan or label-transfer deconvolution of a spatial slice (e.g., 10x Visium) yields per-spot cell-type proportions and you must confirm biological plausibility against layer anatomy and marker-gene expression before accepting the result. Input is raw counts or an unannotated reference — marker-gene alignment checks require a completed label transfer with cell-type assignments, not preprocessed data Tissue lacks known spatial anatomy or established marker genes, so the qualitative layer-structure and marker-alignment checks cannot be evaluated The dense OT plan could not be produced (save_OT=False or insufficient memory), since the validation validates deconvolution derived from the global OT matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates spatial transcriptomic deconvolution by checking that per-spot transferred cell-type proportions reconstruct known anatomical structure and spatially align with canonical marker genes (e.g., Olig1/Olig2 for oligodendrocytes, Atp1b2/Slc1a2 for astrocytes, Dcn/Osr1 for fibroblast-like cells) on the Visium slice. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-35094-8
skills.summary: Validates spatial transcriptomic deconvolution by checking that per-spot transferred cell-type proportions reconstruct known anatomical structure and spatially align with canonical marker genes (e.g., Olig1/Olig2 for oligodendrocytes, Atp1b2/Slc1a2 for astrocytes, Dcn/Osr1 for fibroblast-like cells) on the Visium slice.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or an unannotated reference — marker-gene alignment checks require a completed label transfer with cell-type assignments, not preprocessed data Tissue lacks known spatial anatomy or established marker genes, so the qualitative layer-structure and marker-alignment checks cannot be evaluated The dense OT plan could not be produced (save_OT=False or insufficient memory), since the validation validates deconvolution derived from the global OT matrix

skills.description: Use when cells with x/y coordinates from a rolled (Swiss-rolled) intestinal tissue image must be mapped onto an ordered, user-selected backbone so that along-line arc position and radial offset (wall thickness) are retained.
skills.name: spatial-nearest-neighbor-assignment
skills.search_text: spatial-nearest-neighbor-assignment Use when cells with x/y coordinates from a rolled (Swiss-rolled) intestinal tissue image must be mapped onto an ordered, user-selected backbone so that along-line arc position and radial offset (wall thickness) are retained. Input images provide no x/y per-cell coordinates (e.g. only bulk or spot-level data) — IntestLine processes 'basically any images providing xy-coordinates' The tissue image is not a rolled/Swiss-rolled intestinal preparation, so no spiral backbone from center outward can be defined Data are already an unrolled linear map or a feature/abundance table with no spatial coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_3399 Assigns individual cells from a CODEX-exported x/y coordinate table to user-selected base-layer (backbone) points on a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image using a directionally biased nearest-neighbor matching, preserving intestinal-wall thickness and each cell's serosa-luminal position in the linear map. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad140
skills.summary: Assigns individual cells from a CODEX-exported x/y coordinate table to user-selected base-layer (backbone) points on a Swiss-rolled intestinal tissue image using a directionally biased nearest-neighbor matching, preserving intestinal-wall thickness and each cell's serosa-luminal position in the linear map.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input images provide no x/y per-cell coordinates (e.g. only bulk or spot-level data) — IntestLine processes 'basically any images providing xy-coordinates' The tissue image is not a rolled/Swiss-rolled intestinal preparation, so no spiral backbone from center outward can be defined Data are already an unrolled linear map or a feature/abundance table with no spatial coordinates

skills.description: Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (CellContrast, SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on data with truth cell locations, e.g. SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections in AnnData .h5ad with .obs[['x','y']].
skills.name: spatial-neighbor-hit-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: spatial-neighbor-hit-benchmark-evaluation Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (CellContrast, SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on data with truth cell locations, e.g. SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections in AnnData .h5ad with .obs[['x','y']]. Query data lacks ground-truth cell locations in .obs[['x','y']] — neighbor hit, JSD, and Spearman metrics all require truth coordinates to score against The goal is producing spatially reconstructed SC coordinates for downstream use (co-localization, CCC) rather than benchmarking — use CellContrast `inference`/`reconstruct` instead Evaluation targets sequencing-based ST spots rather than single-cell-resolution imaging data — switch to parameters_spot. defaults, not the single-cell parameter file Benchmark spatial reconstruction methods for single-cell RNA-seq by scoring predicted cell neighborhoods against ground-truth coordinates using three metrics: average nearest neighbor hit (k=20 to 200), Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) of cell-type proportions, and Spearman's rank correlation of pairwise distances. This is the CellContrast paper's evaluation protocol for judging local and global spatial reconstruction quality. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Benchmark spatial reconstruction methods for single-cell RNA-seq by scoring predicted cell neighborhoods against ground-truth coordinates using three metrics: average nearest neighbor hit (k=20 to 200), Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) of cell-type proportions, and Spearman's rank correlation of pairwise distances. This is the CellContrast paper's evaluation protocol for judging local and global spatial reconstruction quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query data lacks ground-truth cell locations in .obs[['x','y']] — neighbor hit, JSD, and Spearman metrics all require truth coordinates to score against The goal is producing spatially reconstructed SC coordinates for downstream use (co-localization, CCC) rather than benchmarking — use CellContrast `inference`/`reconstruct` instead Evaluation targets sequencing-based ST spots rather than single-cell-resolution imaging data — switch to parameters_spot. defaults, not the single-cell parameter file

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope mouse colon) plus a cell type label vector and need neighbor-influence scores per cell type to feed CPPLS cell-cell communication modeling.
skills.name: spatial-neighbor-score-computation
skills.search_text: spatial-neighbor-score-computation Use when you have single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope mouse colon) plus a cell type label vector and need neighbor-influence scores per cell type to feed CPPLS cell-cell communication modeling. Data lacks single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., dissociated single-cell RNA-seq without spatial information) — neighbor scores cannot be computed from O The goal is ligand-receptor database-based communication inference rather than spatial-neighbor regression modeling in CPPLS-MLP http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes raw adjacent cell type scores from a spatial transcriptomics coordinate matrix and cell type labels, using log10(dist/dist0) distance transformation followed by per-cell-type z-score transformation, as the spatial-neighbor input to CPPLS regression modeling in CPPLS-MLP. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae198
skills.summary: Computes raw adjacent cell type scores from a spatial transcriptomics coordinate matrix and cell type labels, using log10(dist/dist0) distance transformation followed by per-cell-type z-score transformation, as the spatial-neighbor input to CPPLS regression modeling in CPPLS-MLP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lacks single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., dissociated single-cell RNA-seq without spatial information) — neighbor scores cannot be computed from O The goal is ligand-receptor database-based communication inference rather than spatial-neighbor regression modeling in CPPLS-MLP

skills.description: Use when expert scribbles are unavailable for Visium/ST spatial transcriptomics data and an automated scribble (mclust_backbone.csv) must be derived from an initial non-spatial Mclust clustering.
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-consensus-filtering-of-spot-labels
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-consensus-filtering-of-spot-labels Use when expert scribbles are unavailable for Visium/ST spatial transcriptomics data and an automated scribble (mclust_backbone.csv) must be derived from an initial non-spatial Mclust clustering. An expert-generated manual scribble (manual_scribble.csv) is available — then run with schema 'expert' instead of AutoScribbleDom's mclust schema The spatial platform is neither Visium nor ST, since the filter assumes a six-neighbor hexagonal or four-neighbor square spot lattice A fully labeled per-spot map is required — the filter intentionally clears labels on non-consensus spots, producing a partial scribble http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A consensus filter in the ScribbleDom/AutoScribbleDom pipeline that converts a non-spatial Mclust clustering into a spatially coherent automated scribble by retaining a spot's label only when it agrees with all of its lattice neighbors, then clearing labels elsewhere. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad594
skills.summary: A consensus filter in the ScribbleDom/AutoScribbleDom pipeline that converts a non-spatial Mclust clustering into a spatially coherent automated scribble by retaining a spot's label only when it agrees with all of its lattice neighbors, then clearing labels elsewhere.
skills.when_to_use_negative: An expert-generated manual scribble (manual_scribble.csv) is available — then run with schema 'expert' instead of AutoScribbleDom's mclust schema The spatial platform is neither Visium nor ST, since the filter assumes a six-neighbor hexagonal or four-neighbor square spot lattice A fully labeled per-spot map is required — the filter intentionally clears labels on non-consensus spots, producing a partial scribble

skills.description: Use when fitting spatial-domain clustering models (iSC.MEB, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, SpaGCN) on SRT sections and an explicit spatial adjacency/neighbor graph must be built from spot coordinates before model fitting.
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-graph-construction
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-graph-construction Use when fitting spatial-domain clustering models (iSC.MEB, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, SpaGCN) on SRT sections and an explicit spatial adjacency/neighbor graph must be built from spot coordinates before model fitting. Input is a non-spatial expression matrix with no spot/cell coordinate information — the neighbor graph cannot be defined. Data already contains a precomputed spatial adjacency graph compatible with the MRF model. Analysis is purely non-spatial single-cell clustering (e.g., standard Louvain on PCA), where a spatial graph adds the wrong prior. Constructs spatial adjacency matrices capturing spot/cell neighborhood structure from multi-sample spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., six-section mouse embryo seqFISH), providing the graph input required by hidden Markov random field clustering in iSC.MEB. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad019
skills.summary: Constructs spatial adjacency matrices capturing spot/cell neighborhood structure from multi-sample spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., six-section mouse embryo seqFISH), providing the graph input required by hidden Markov random field clustering in iSC.MEB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a non-spatial expression matrix with no spot/cell coordinate information — the neighbor graph cannot be defined. Data already contains a precomputed spatial adjacency graph compatible with the MRF model. Analysis is purely non-spatial single-cell clustering (e.g., standard Louvain on PCA), where a spatial graph adds the wrong prior.

skills.description: Use when annotating malignant vs non-malignant regions on spatial transcriptomics spots from spot-level malignancy probabilities and image features, and neighboring spots' labels need spatial-coherence refinement.
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-label-refinement
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-label-refinement Use when annotating malignant vs non-malignant regions on spatial transcriptomics spots from spot-level malignancy probabilities and image features, and neighboring spots' labels need spatial-coherence refinement. Data is single-cell scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates — spatial neighborhood refinement is undefined; use the single-cell malignant cell identification mode instead Cell-type annotation for all lineages is needed — scMalignantFinder identifies malignant cells only from cancerous lineages and requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types Cancer with unknown/controversial origin (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — the article states capabilities require further testing there http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Refines per-spot region labels in tumor spatial transcriptomics by combining three obs features (malignancy_probability, AUCell-based Malignant_up score, image_score) via hierarchical clustering and then smoothing cluster/region calls using a spatial neighborhood network (spatial_nn=True), as implemented in scMalignantFinder's spatial.region_identification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-025-07942-y
skills.summary: Refines per-spot region labels in tumor spatial transcriptomics by combining three obs features (malignancy_probability, AUCell-based Malignant_up score, image_score) via hierarchical clustering and then smoothing cluster/region calls using a spatial neighborhood network (spatial_nn=True), as implemented in scMalignantFinder's spatial.region_identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is single-cell scRNA-seq without spatial coordinates — spatial neighborhood refinement is undefined; use the single-cell malignant cell identification mode instead Cell-type annotation for all lineages is needed — scMalignantFinder identifies malignant cells only from cancerous lineages and requires prerequisite identification of basic cell types Cancer with unknown/controversial origin (e.g. synovial sarcoma, certain brain tumors) — the article states capabilities require further testing there

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been equipped with a SpaOTsc-derived spatial cell-cell distance matrix and you need to quantify at what spatial distance a known ligand explains downstream target gene expression (signaling range inference).
skills.name: spatial-neighborhood-ligand-expression-aggregation
skills.search_text: spatial-neighborhood-ligand-expression-aggregation Use when scRNA-seq cells have been equipped with a SpaOTsc-derived spatial cell-cell distance matrix and you need to quantify at what spatial distance a known ligand explains downstream target gene expression (signaling range inference). No spatial cell-cell distance matrix is available yet — the aggregation requires the SpaOTsc optimal-transport-derived cell-cell distance, so run transport_plan/cell_cell_distance first The signaling pathway's ligand/receptor/downstream genes are unknown — the approach relies on known genes involved in specific signaling The input is spatial transcriptomics data with native coordinates and only short-range signaling distances are needed — direct distance-based approaches may be more appropriate than transporting scRNA-seq into space http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates ligand expression within spatial cell-cell neighborhoods of varying radius η (computed from the SpaOTsc optimal-transport cell-cell distance matrix) to form radius-dependent ligand features L̃(η), which are then fed to a receptor-weighted random forest to infer the spatial range of a signaling pathway (e.g., ~100 µm for Wg and ~125 µm for Dpp in the Drosophila embryo). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15968-5
skills.summary: Aggregates ligand expression within spatial cell-cell neighborhoods of varying radius η (computed from the SpaOTsc optimal-transport cell-cell distance matrix) to form radius-dependent ligand features L̃(η), which are then fed to a receptor-weighted random forest to infer the spatial range of a signaling pathway (e.g., ~100 µm for Wg and ~125 µm for Dpp in the Drosophila embryo).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No spatial cell-cell distance matrix is available yet — the aggregation requires the SpaOTsc optimal-transport-derived cell-cell distance, so run transport_plan/cell_cell_distance first The signaling pathway's ligand/receptor/downstream genes are unknown — the approach relies on known genes involved in specific signaling The input is spatial transcriptomics data with native coordinates and only short-range signaling distances are needed — direct distance-based approaches may be more appropriate than transporting scRNA-seq into space

skills.description: Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10x Visium) that has matched H&E images, and per-spot cell counts plus per-cell spatial locations (cell_locations) are needed to resolve spot-level data (~55 μm spots) to single-cell resolution.
skills.name: spatial-nucleus-segmentation-he-images
skills.search_text: spatial-nucleus-segmentation-he-images Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10x Visium) that has matched H&E images, and per-spot cell counts plus per-cell spatial locations (cell_locations) are needed to resolve spot-level data (~55 μm spots) to single-cell resolution. Input is Slide-seq V2 data without histology images — SpatialScope replaces nucleus segmentation with singlet/doublet classification, assuming at most two cell types co-exist within a spot Input is image-based ST (e.g., MERFISH, seqFISH) that already resolves single cells — segmentation is redundant Only a single-channel nuclear image (e.g., DAPI) or no image is available — SpatialScope notes these circumstances complicate cell count estimation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Step 1 of the SpatialScope pipeline: run nucleus segmentation (StarDist, the SpatialScope default for H&E) on matched H&E histology images to quantify the number of cells per spatial transcriptomics spot and locate individual cells, providing the single-cell scaffold for downstream cell type identification and gene expression decomposition. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: Step 1 of the SpatialScope pipeline: run nucleus segmentation (StarDist, the SpatialScope default for H&E) on matched H&E histology images to quantify the number of cells per spatial transcriptomics spot and locate individual cells, providing the single-cell scaffold for downstream cell type identification and gene expression decomposition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Slide-seq V2 data without histology images — SpatialScope replaces nucleus segmentation with singlet/doublet classification, assuming at most two cell types co-exist within a spot Input is image-based ST (e.g., MERFISH, seqFISH) that already resolves single cells — segmentation is redundant Only a single-channel nuclear image (e.g., DAPI) or no image is available — SpatialScope notes these circumstances complicate cell count estimation

skills.description: Use when an AnnData object with cell spatial coordinates and cell-type labels needs to be visualized as a spatial map with a custom cluster-to-color mapping, e.g., after Spaco colorization.
skills.name: spatial-plot-rendering-scanpy
skills.search_text: spatial-plot-rendering-scanpy Use when an AnnData object with cell spatial coordinates and cell-type labels needs to be visualized as a spatial map with a custom cluster-to-color mapping, e.g., after Spaco colorization. skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-colorization Use when visualizing cell-type clusters from single-cell-resolution SRT data (STARmap, Stereo-seq, seqFISH, IMC) where default palettes (Scanpy/matplotlib) cause perceptual ambiguity between spatially adjacent or interlaced cell types. The input is bulk or non-spatial data where cell-type spatial adjacency is meaningless — Spaco's optimization is driven by spatial interlacement. Hundreds of clusters must be colored or strict CVD-supporting colorization is required — the article notes visual contrast obtainable through color space is limited in these cases. skills.description: Use when you have spatial scRNAseq data (e.g., MERFISH cell coordinates + log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix) and need to segment tissue into spatial regions by comparing neighborhoods as transcriptome distributions rather than single cells.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-rexel-parcellation
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-rexel-parcellation Use when you have spatial scRNAseq data (e.g., MERFISH cell coordinates + log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix) and need to segment tissue into spatial regions by comparing neighborhoods as transcriptome distributions rather than single cells. The data are non-spatial scRNAseq with no cell coordinates — par_spatially_cluster_mmd requires a (dims x cells) spatial coordinates matrix The goal is single-cell-level clustering rather than distributional comparison of tissue regions — the MMD/LDS approach compares rexels as transcriptome distributions, not individual cells Datasets are much larger than ~10,000 cells per tissue region; the paper's LDS setting (k=16, n_pixels=64) was tuned for small tissue samples Segments spatial scRNAseq tissue (e.g., human cortical MERFISH) into local neighborhoods ('rexels') via approximate Voronoi parcellization and compares them as distributions of transcriptomes using MMD distances under the q-diffused kernel, enabling local distributional segmentation (LDS). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-024-06104-w
skills.summary: Segments spatial scRNAseq tissue (e.g., human cortical MERFISH) into local neighborhoods ('rexels') via approximate Voronoi parcellization and compares them as distributions of transcriptomes using MMD distances under the q-diffused kernel, enabling local distributional segmentation (LDS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are non-spatial scRNAseq with no cell coordinates — par_spatially_cluster_mmd requires a (dims x cells) spatial coordinates matrix The goal is single-cell-level clustering rather than distributional comparison of tissue regions — the MMD/LDS approach compares rexels as transcriptome distributions, not individual cells Datasets are much larger than ~10,000 cells per tissue region; the paper's LDS setting (k=16, n_pixels=64) was tuned for small tissue samples

skills.description: Use when you have a digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope Velocyto-format DGE from STARsolo alignment) and need to visualize marker gene sets or subcellular spliced/unspliced read patterns at sub-micrometer resolution.

skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-rgb-visualization Use when you have a digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope Velocyto-format DGE from STARsolo alignment) and need to visualize marker gene sets or subcellular spliced/unspliced read patterns at sub-micrometer resolution. The analysis requires subcellular inference via sliding-window (MSSW) clustering — spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible The dataset lacks per-barcode spatial coordinates (e.g., only an already-binned or clustered feature table is available), since un-binned barcode-level rendering is essential to retain sub-micrometer resolution The data is lower-resolution platform data where existing tools suffice and the goal is UMAP/spatial clustering rather than RGB marker rendering (Step V2 covers UMAP, spatial clustering, and feature violin plots instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Render ultra-high-resolution RGB geneset plots and Step V1 subcellular (spliced/unspliced) plots from spatial transcriptomics data using STtools, preserving sub-micrometer barcode resolution (e.g., Seq-Scope at <1 μm²/pixel). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac061
skills.summary: Render ultra-high-resolution RGB geneset plots and Step V1 subcellular (spliced/unspliced) plots from spatial transcriptomics data using STtools, preserving sub-micrometer barcode resolution (e.g., Seq-Scope at <1 μm²/pixel).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires subcellular inference via sliding-window (MSSW) clustering — spatial segments must be larger than subcellular compartments (~10 μm), so subcellular analysis with MSSW is not feasible The dataset lacks per-barcode spatial coordinates (e.g., only an already-binned or clustered feature table is available), since un-binned barcode-level rendering is essential to retain sub-micrometer resolution The data is lower-resolution platform data where existing tools suffice and the goal is UMAP/spatial clustering rather than RGB marker rendering (Step V2 covers UMAP, spatial clustering, and feature violin plots instead)

skills.description: Use when separately measured single-cell domains (spatial RNA-seq and scRNA-seq, e.g. Chromium 10X from tumor xenografts) must be aligned so that mapped points retain per-sample correspondence to their inputs, not just distribution-level similarity.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-scrnaseq-mapping
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-scrnaseq-mapping Use when separately measured single-cell domains (spatial RNA-seq and scRNA-seq, e.g. Chromium 10X from tumor xenografts) must be aligned so that mapped points retain per-sample correspondence to their inputs, not just distribution-level similarity. When only distribution-level matching is needed and point-wise correspondence does not matter — a plain CycleGAN or CMAE alignment suffices and the correspondence loss is unnecessary overhead. When more than a few modalities must be aligned simultaneously: the number of generators grows quadratically with the number of input modalities, forcing small or separately trained networks. When the data have no meaningful diffusion geometry or no defensible choice of distance between data points, since the geometry-based loss is not completely plug-and-play. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Reproduces scMMGAN-based mapping between spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq domains (e.g., MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer xenograft samples), where a diffusion-geometry correspondence loss preserves point-wise correspondence while matching the target distribution, outperforming CycleGAN and CMAE baselines on per-sample MSE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100577
skills.summary: Reproduces scMMGAN-based mapping between spatial transcriptomics and scRNA-seq domains (e.g., MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer xenograft samples), where a diffusion-geometry correspondence loss preserves point-wise correspondence while matching the target distribution, outperforming CycleGAN and CMAE baselines on per-sample MSE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only distribution-level matching is needed and point-wise correspondence does not matter — a plain CycleGAN or CMAE alignment suffices and the correspondence loss is unnecessary overhead. When more than a few modalities must be aligned simultaneously: the number of generators grows quadratically with the number of input modalities, forcing small or separately trained networks. When the data have no meaningful diffusion geometry or no defensible choice of distance between data points, since the geometry-based loss is not completely plug-and-play.

skills.description: Use when validating a spatial-pathway or spatial-relevance method on ST data where no ground truth exists: simulate tissue patterns with SRTsim (or SERGIO-style scripts from the manuscript repo), plant known spatially relevant gene sets, and test whether the method separates them from random sets.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation Use when validating a spatial-pathway or spatial-relevance method on ST data where no ground truth exists: simulate tissue patterns with SRTsim (or SERGIO-style scripts from the manuscript repo), plant known spatially relevant gene sets, and test whether the method separates them from random sets. Data are already real ST tissue sections with known anatomical annotations — evaluate spatial relevance directly rather than simulating The data are targeted-gene ST panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity/simulation is not suitable and gene imputation would be needed first The benchmark target is scRNA-seq cell-pathway detection rather than spatial organization — use the SERGIO steady/dynamic simulation scripts instead of SRTsim spatial modes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark spatial-relevance detection by simulating spatial transcriptomics (ST) data with controlled spatial organization patterns (e.g., four SRTsim modes: hotspot, hotspot-with-gradient, streak, gradient) and embedding ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets alongside matched random gene sets, so that a method like GSDensity's delta-KLD separation can be validated against known ground truth. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-44206-x
skills.summary: Benchmark spatial-relevance detection by simulating spatial transcriptomics (ST) data with controlled spatial organization patterns (e.g., four SRTsim modes: hotspot, hotspot-with-gradient, streak, gradient) and embedding ground-truth spatially relevant gene sets alongside matched random gene sets, so that a method like GSDensity's delta-KLD separation can be validated against known ground truth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already real ST tissue sections with known anatomical annotations — evaluate spatial relevance directly rather than simulating The data are targeted-gene ST panels with limited gene numbers — GSDensity/simulation is not suitable and gene imputation would be needed first The benchmark target is scRNA-seq cell-pathway detection rather than spatial organization — use the SERGIO steady/dynamic simulation scripts instead of SRTsim spatial modes

skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-framework
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-framework Use when benchmarking or validating an SVG detection method's p-value calibration and sensitivity — e.g., measuring FPR at nominal 0.01/0.05/0.1 cutoffs, running coordinate-shuffle ablations, or building coordinate-permuted null simulations for spatially-resolved transcriptomics data. The goal is identifying SVGs in real experimental data rather than validating method calibration — run nnSVG directly on the dataset instead of building simulations The analysis targets spatial domain marker genes (mean-level changes between domains) — the framework addresses continuously varying SVGs, and the paper explicitly focuses 'on methods to identify SVGs, not spatial domain marker genes' The input data lack spatial coordinates or a defined spot layout, so coordinates cannot be permuted for null simulation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation-based validation framework for spatially variable gene (SVG) detection methods, in which 1000 genes (100 SVGs, 900 noise genes) parameterized from MOBP statistics are simulated over Visium DLPFC spot coordinates with varied length scale and expression strength, and false positive/true positive rates are measured against nominal thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z
