skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is identifying SVGs in real experimental data rather than validating method calibration — run nnSVG directly on the dataset instead of building simulations The analysis targets spatial domain marker genes (mean-level changes between domains) — the framework addresses continuously varying SVGs, and the paper explicitly focuses 'on methods to identify SVGs, not spatial domain marker genes' The input data lack spatial coordinates or a defined spot layout, so coordinates cannot be permuted for null simulation

skills.description: Use when you need ground-truth-controlled ST data to test whether a deconvolution method recovers known cell-type proportions or condition-specific gene-expression changes (e.g., age-associated macrophage Cd274/Clec4d up, Coro1a down) from pixel mixtures.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-from-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-from-scrnaseq Use when you need ground-truth-controlled ST data to test whether a deconvolution method recovers known cell-type proportions or condition-specific gene-expression changes (e.g., age-associated macrophage Cd274/Clec4d up, Coro1a down) from pixel mixtures. The ST data are sub-cellular resolution or tissue slivers covering only a few pixels, where LDA-based deconvolution assumptions fail Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so overdispersed-gene feature selection cannot distinguish cell types A suitable single-cell reference already exists and a reference-based method (RCTD, SPOTlight, spatialDWLS) is preferred for the actual analysis rather than benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Simulate multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) data by aggregating single cells from scRNA-seq conditions (e.g., aged vs young mouse mammary gland) into pseudo-pixel mixtures, so that reference-free deconvolution methods like STdeconvolve can be benchmarked on recovering known perturbation-driven, cell-type-specific expression changes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30033-z
skills.summary: Simulate multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) data by aggregating single cells from scRNA-seq conditions (e.g., aged vs young mouse mammary gland) into pseudo-pixel mixtures, so that reference-free deconvolution methods like STdeconvolve can be benchmarked on recovering known perturbation-driven, cell-type-specific expression changes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The ST data are sub-cellular resolution or tissue slivers covering only a few pixels, where LDA-based deconvolution assumptions fail Cell-type proportions are homogeneous/uniform across pixels so overdispersed-gene feature selection cannot distinguish cell types A suitable single-cell reference already exists and a reference-based method (RCTD, SPOTlight, spatialDWLS) is preferred for the actual analysis rather than benchmarking

skills.description: Use when validating that exon-level splicing changes (delta-PSI) found between brain regions in single-cell ScISOrSeq data reproduce in spatial transcriptomics data with ONT long-read alignments, e.g. HIPP vs PFC on a defined exon set.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-splicing-concordance
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-splicing-concordance Use when validating that exon-level splicing changes (delta-PSI) found between brain regions in single-cell ScISOrSeq data reproduce in spatial transcriptomics data with ONT long-read alignments, e.g. HIPP vs PFC on a defined exon set. The analysis goal is differential isoform expression testing itself (use scisorseqr DiffSplicingAnalysis with isoform tests, which outperform exon tests), rather than cross-platform concordance of already-derived delta-PSI values. Input is short-read-only spatial data without ONT (or PacBio) long-read alignments, since exon/isoform resolution cannot be derived from short reads alone. Only a handful of exons are available — the Bernoulli significance assessment (e.g. 85% of 40 exons, p <= 3.5e-06) requires a sufficiently large exon set. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Reproduce region-specific splicing differences measured by single-cell long-read sequencing at spatial resolution by correlating single-cell and spatial (10X Visium + ONT long-read) delta-PSI values per exon, as demonstrated for HIPP-vs-PFC comparisons in the postnatal day 7 mouse brain. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20343-5
skills.summary: Reproduce region-specific splicing differences measured by single-cell long-read sequencing at spatial resolution by correlating single-cell and spatial (10X Visium + ONT long-read) delta-PSI values per exon, as demonstrated for HIPP-vs-PFC comparisons in the postnatal day 7 mouse brain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is differential isoform expression testing itself (use scisorseqr DiffSplicingAnalysis with isoform tests, which outperform exon tests), rather than cross-platform concordance of already-derived delta-PSI values. Input is short-read-only spatial data without ONT (or PacBio) long-read alignments, since exon/isoform resolution cannot be derived from short reads alone. Only a handful of exons are available — the Bernoulli significance assessment (e.g. 85% of 40 exons, p <= 3.5e-06) requires a sufficiently large exon set.

skills.description: Use when you have a spot-level ratio matrix (e.g., RUD APA usage from stAPAminer) plus spot coordinates from spatially barcoded ST data (e.g., MOB) and need to cluster spots, embed them, and validate clusters against tissue layer annotations.
skills.name: spatial-transcriptomics-spot-clustering
skills.search_text: spatial-transcriptomics-spot-clustering Use when you have a spot-level ratio matrix (e.g., RUD APA usage from stAPAminer) plus spot coordinates from spatially barcoded ST data (e.g., MOB) and need to cluster spots, embed them, and validate clusters against tissue layer annotations. Input is raw sequencing data rather than a quantified poly(A) site matrix — the PA-extraction pipeline (umi_tools, STAR, scAPAtrap) must run first. Data are image-based ST (MERFISH/seqFISH) without spatial barcodes — the article states APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools. The goal is gene-level differential APA testing (DEAPA/LSAPA/SVAPA) rather than spot-level layer clustering and its validation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Graph-based clustering of spatial transcriptomics spots on an APA usage (RUD) matrix using stAPAminer/Seurat, followed by UMAP embedding and quantitative evaluation against morphological layer labels via adjusted Rand index and within-layer spot-spot Pearson correlations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003
skills.summary: Graph-based clustering of spatial transcriptomics spots on an APA usage (RUD) matrix using stAPAminer/Seurat, followed by UMAP embedding and quantitative evaluation against morphological layer labels via adjusted Rand index and within-layer spot-spot Pearson correlations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data rather than a quantified poly(A) site matrix — the PA-extraction pipeline (umi_tools, STAR, scAPAtrap) must run first. Data are image-based ST (MERFISH/seqFISH) without spatial barcodes — the article states APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with existing tools. The goal is gene-level differential APA testing (DEAPA/LSAPA/SVAPA) rather than spot-level layer clustering and its validation.

skills.description: Use when you have region-annotated single-cell data from multiplexed imaging (e.g., MCMICRO output) and need per-subregion fractions of marker-defined cell populations, such as Ki67+/SOX10+ or MITF+/SOX10+ fractions across tumor core, peripheral bands, or invasive-front subregions.
skills.name: spatial-tumor-microenvironment-fraction-analysis
skills.search_text: spatial-tumor-microenvironment-fraction-analysis Use when you have region-annotated single-cell data from multiplexed imaging (e.g., MCMICRO output) and need per-subregion fractions of marker-defined cell populations, such as Ki67+/SOX10+ or MITF+/SOX10+ fractions across tumor core, peripheral bands, or invasive-front subregions. Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery not yet converted to single-cell data — MCMICRO must run first, as 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells.' The analysis goal is neighborhood-graph or single-cell transcriptomics spatial analysis rather than region-based composition of marker-gated populations (Squidpy-style graph analysis is a different toolkit). The region of interest includes fragmented SOX10+ satellite areas whose inclusion would artificially inflate distance measurements — exclude them before computing region-based fractions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3382 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Computes region-resolved cell-composition fractions (e.g., Ki67+/SOX10+ proliferating tumor cells and MITF+/SOX10+ cells) within user-defined spatial subregions of a tumor using SpatialCells, on MCMICRO-derived multiplexed single-cell data. This enables quantitative comparison of marker enrichment across tumor subregions, as demonstrated on the MEL1 melanoma CyCIF sample (1,110,585 cells). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae189
skills.summary: Computes region-resolved cell-composition fractions (e.g., Ki67+/SOX10+ proliferating tumor cells and MITF+/SOX10+ cells) within user-defined spatial subregions of a tumor using SpatialCells, on MCMICRO-derived multiplexed single-cell data. This enables quantitative comparison of marker enrichment across tumor subregions, as demonstrated on the MEL1 melanoma CyCIF sample (1,110,585 cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multi-channel whole-slide imagery not yet converted to single-cell data — MCMICRO must run first, as 'The output of MCMICRO is the input of SpatialCells.' The analysis goal is neighborhood-graph or single-cell transcriptomics spatial analysis rather than region-based composition of marker-gated populations (Squidpy-style graph analysis is a different toolkit). The region of interest includes fragmented SOX10+ satellite areas whose inclusion would artificially inflate distance measurements — exclude them before computing region-based fractions.

skills.description: Use when comparing SVG calls from two methods (e.g., singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X) on the same 2D spatial coordinates and count matrix, to identify high-sensitivity hits one method ranks poorly and produce a merged rank/p-value comparison table.
skills.name: spatial-variable-gene-pvalue-interpretation
skills.search_text: spatial-variable-gene-pvalue-interpretation Use when comparing SVG calls from two methods (e.g., singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X) on the same 2D spatial coordinates and count matrix, to identify high-sensitivity hits one method ranks poorly and produce a merged rank/p-value comparison table. The goal is multi-condition comparison (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' with singleCellHaystack Results must feed a cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analysis — the article notes singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-based workflows Runtime is the binding constraint on large spatial data — SPARK-X alone is the faster method, though at lower sensitivity http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Run and cross-compare spatially variable gene (SVG) rankings from singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X on the same spatial transcriptomics dataset, then interpret rank and p-value discrepancies (e.g., Ttr at 58th, p=1.1e-105 in singleCellHaystack vs 11,881st, p=0.0087 in SPARK-X). singleCellHaystack is more sensitive but slower; SPARK-X is fastest. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-023-38965-2
skills.summary: Run and cross-compare spatially variable gene (SVG) rankings from singleCellHaystack and SPARK-X on the same spatial transcriptomics dataset, then interpret rank and p-value discrepancies (e.g., Ttr at 58th, p=1.1e-105 in singleCellHaystack vs 11,881st, p=0.0087 in SPARK-X). singleCellHaystack is more sensitive but slower; SPARK-X is fastest.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is multi-condition comparison (e.g., wild-type vs knockout) — the article states such comparisons 'cannot be easily conducted' with singleCellHaystack Results must feed a cluster-oriented scRNA-seq analysis — the article notes singleCellHaystack results are 'not as straightforward to incorporate' into cluster-based workflows Runtime is the binding constraint on large spatial data — SPARK-X alone is the faster method, though at lower sensitivity

skills.description: Use when single-cell liver data contains a spatial zonation signal that confounds reconstruction of a temporal (circadian/regeneration) trajectory, and prior knowledge of zonated genes or a cell-to-location spatial mapping is available to define the signal to remove.
skills.name: spatial-zonation-signal-filtering
skills.search_text: spatial-zonation-signal-filtering Use when single-cell liver data contains a spatial zonation signal that confounds reconstruction of a temporal (circadian/regeneration) trajectory, and prior knowledge of zonated genes or a cell-to-location spatial mapping is available to define the signal to remove. No prior knowledge of zonated genes and no spatial cell-to-location mapping exists, since SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel The downstream task requires properly log-transformed expression, because SiFT-filtered data are no longer properly log-transformed The signal of interest is the spatial zonation itself rather than a hidden temporal trajectory — filtering would remove the target signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Filter the spatial zonation signal from single-cell liver data with SiFT to enhance recovery of the underlying temporal circadian clock trajectory, using prior-knowledge zonated genes or a novoSpaRc spatial mapping to define the cell-cell similarity kernel. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-44757-7
skills.summary: Filter the spatial zonation signal from single-cell liver data with SiFT to enhance recovery of the underlying temporal circadian clock trajectory, using prior-knowledge zonated genes or a novoSpaRc spatial mapping to define the cell-cell similarity kernel.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No prior knowledge of zonated genes and no spatial cell-to-location mapping exists, since SiFT strongly relies on the prior knowledge used to define the cell-cell similarity kernel The downstream task requires properly log-transformed expression, because SiFT-filtered data are no longer properly log-transformed The signal of interest is the spatial zonation itself rather than a hidden temporal trajectory — filtering would remove the target signal

skills.description: Use when significant ligand-receptor interactions detected on spatially reconstructed SC data (spatialDM p ≤ 0.05) must be traced to specific cells and tissues, e.g. recovering the heart/liver cells carrying IGF2-IGF2R signals in the E9.5 mouse embryo scRNA-S1 sample.
skills.name: spatially-restrained-signaling-cell-extraction
skills.search_text: spatially-restrained-signaling-cell-extraction Use when significant ligand-receptor interactions detected on spatially reconstructed SC data (spatialDM p ≤ 0.05) must be traced to specific cells and tissues, e.g. recovering the heart/liver cells carrying IGF2-IGF2R signals in the E9.5 mouse embryo scRNA-S1 sample. When truth single-cell spatial locations are already available — apply spatialDM directly instead of reconstructing coordinates first When only gene-expression-based global interaction inference is needed without cell-level spatial localization (CellChat alone suffices) When the SC query has a large gap from the ST reference — forcing SC cells to resemble ST can introduce bias and MDS-based de novo mapping loses the reference's cell distribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Localizes ligand-receptor signaling events to individual cells by running spatially aware CCC detection (spatialDM) on CellContrast-reconstructed single-cell coordinates, then extracting the significant cells (with normalized expression and reconstructed x/y coordinates) for a target interaction such as IGF2-IGF2R. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Localizes ligand-receptor signaling events to individual cells by running spatially aware CCC detection (spatialDM) on CellContrast-reconstructed single-cell coordinates, then extracting the significant cells (with normalized expression and reconstructed x/y coordinates) for a target interaction such as IGF2-IGF2R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When truth single-cell spatial locations are already available — apply spatialDM directly instead of reconstructing coordinates first When only gene-expression-based global interaction inference is needed without cell-level spatial localization (CellChat alone suffices) When the SC query has a large gap from the ST reference — forcing SC cells to resemble ST can introduce bias and MDS-based de novo mapping loses the reference's cell distribution

skills.description: Use when integrating spot-level ST data (Visium or Slide-seq) with an scRNA-seq reference to resolve per-cell cell type labels with a spatial smoothness prior, e.g. producing CellTypeLabel_nu10.csv for downstream decomposition.
skills.name: spatially-smoothed-cell-type-identification-potts-model
skills.search_text: spatially-smoothed-cell-type-identification-potts-model Use when integrating spot-level ST data (Visium or Slide-seq) with an scRNA-seq reference to resolve per-cell cell type labels with a spatial smoothness prior, e.g. producing CellTypeLabel_nu10.csv for downstream decomposition. When only spot-level cell-type proportions are needed and no single-cell resolution is required — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, CARD or spatialDWLS estimate proportions per spot without resolving individual cells When a histological image is unavailable for Visium data and no alternative image (e.g. DAPI) can support nucleus segmentation, making per-spot cell counts unreliable When the biological context violates the Potts assumption — e.g. tissues where neighboring cells are expected to be of different types http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 The SpatialScope cell type identification step assigns cell types to cells within each ST spot by combining a Poisson model with gene- and spot-specific batch effects and a Potts-model spatial smoothness prior (nu=10), so that spatially adjacent cells are encouraged to share cell type labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43629-w
skills.summary: The SpatialScope cell type identification step assigns cell types to cells within each ST spot by combining a Poisson model with gene- and spot-specific batch effects and a Potts-model spatial smoothness prior (nu=10), so that spatially adjacent cells are encouraged to share cell type labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only spot-level cell-type proportions are needed and no single-cell resolution is required — deconvolution methods like RCTD, Cell2location, CARD or spatialDWLS estimate proportions per spot without resolving individual cells When a histological image is unavailable for Visium data and no alternative image (e.g. DAPI) can support nucleus segmentation, making per-spot cell counts unreliable When the biological context violates the Potts assumption — e.g. tissues where neighboring cells are expected to be of different types

skills.description: Use when you have an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix or a gene-spot expression count matrix over ST spots and need to identify genes whose APA usage or expression varies spatially (adjusted P < 0.05).
skills.name: spatially-variable-gene-detection
skills.search_text: spatially-variable-gene-detection Use when you have an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix or a gene-spot expression count matrix over ST spots and need to identify genes whose APA usage or expression varies spatially (adjusted P < 0.05). skills.summary: Detects spatially variable (SV) signal from spatial transcriptomics data using SPARK, adapted by stAPAminer as findSVAPA to test the count-transformed imputed RUD (relative usage of distal poly(A) site) matrix and identify SVAPA genes in the MOB ST data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are imaging-based (MERFISH/seqFISH) without spatially barcoded reads, since APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra Your matrix is a ratio-type RUD matrix that cannot be reasonably transformed into a count matrix meeting SPARK's model assumptions You seek genes with layer-differential APA usage (use findContrastAPA/findAllMarkers for DEAPA/LSAPA, not findSVAPA)

skills.description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix with 2D (or 2-3D) spatial coordinates and need per-gene SVG rankings and p-values without pre-clustering cells or imposing a detection threshold.
skills.name: spatially-variable-gene-detection
skills.search_text: spatially-variable-gene-detection Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix with 2D (or 2-3D) spatial coordinates and need per-gene SVG rankings and p-values without pre-clustering cells or imposing a detection threshold. The goal is differential expression between labeled conditions (e.g. wild-type vs knockout) — the article states comparisons between multiple conditions cannot be easily conducted. skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-robustness-assessment Use when you need to measure how much adding or deleting a percentage of edges in a regulatory or kinase-substrate network changes downstream activity inference, and whether the change is statistically significant. Your goal is method performance benchmarking against perturbation ground truth (AUROC/AUPRC of perturbed vs unperturbed regulators) rather than network-noise robustness — use the decoupleRBench perturbation benchmark instead The prior knowledge network is unchanged and you only need to infer activities once — no perturbation-correlation assessment is applicable You are running the scalability analysis on simulated data rather than assessing robustness to edge noise http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies the robustness of biological activity estimates (TF or kinase activities inferred with decoupleR) to noise in prior knowledge networks by computing Spearman correlations between activities from perturbed (edge-added/edge-deleted) and original networks, followed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Quantifies the robustness of biological activity estimates (TF or kinase activities inferred with decoupleR) to noise in prior knowledge networks by computing Spearman correlations between activities from perturbed (edge-added/edge-deleted) and original networks, followed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is method performance benchmarking against perturbation ground truth (AUROC/AUPRC of perturbed vs unperturbed regulators) rather than network-noise robustness — use the decoupleRBench perturbation benchmark instead The prior knowledge network is unchanged and you only need to infer activities once — no perturbation-correlation assessment is applicable You are running the scalability analysis on simulated data rather than assessing robustness to edge noise

skills.description: Use when you have a reconstructed gene regulatory network (CLR/CellNet-style edge list) plus per-cell trajectory progression values from CellRouter and want to rank regulators driving or mediating specific cell-state transitions.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-trajectory-progression
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-trajectory-progression Use when you have a reconstructed gene regulatory network (CLR/CellNet-style edge list) plus per-cell trajectory progression values from CellRouter and want to rank regulators driving or mediating specific cell-state transitions. You have no reconstructed gene regulatory network linking regulators to predicted target genes — the multiplicative score requires regulator-target edges. You need trajectories between arbitrary cell states rather than regulator scores; CellRouter's flow-network trajectory reconstruction, not this scoring step, addresses trajectory detection. Trajectory progression values are unavailable (e.g., only raw counts without CellRouter trajectory inference) — correlations with progression cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Scores transcriptional regulators of cell-fate transitions in CellRouter by combining Spearman correlations of regulator expression and its predicted targets' expression with trajectory progression, multiplied by the number of regulated target genes (GRN(i,j) = c(i,j) * m(t,j) * n(j)). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03214-y
skills.summary: Scores transcriptional regulators of cell-fate transitions in CellRouter by combining Spearman correlations of regulator expression and its predicted targets' expression with trajectory progression, multiplied by the number of regulated target genes (GRN(i,j) = c(i,j) * m(t,j) * n(j)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no reconstructed gene regulatory network linking regulators to predicted target genes — the multiplicative score requires regulator-target edges. You need trajectories between arbitrary cell states rather than regulator scores; CellRouter's flow-network trajectory reconstruction, not this scoring step, addresses trajectory detection. Trajectory progression values are unavailable (e.g., only raw counts without CellRouter trajectory inference) — correlations with progression cannot be computed.

skills.description: Reference for initializing TF weight matrices when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics models, where candidate TFs (ENCODE/ChEA) need expression-correlation-based starting weights per target gene.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-weight-initialization
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-weight-initialization Reference for initializing TF weight matrices when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics models, where candidate TFs (ENCODE/ChEA) need expression-correlation-based starting weights per target gene. Target genes with no candidate TFs recovered from ENCODE/ChEA, since there are no TF-target pairs to correlate Datasets where expression correlation is a poor proxy for regulation and a different init_weight_method is warranted Running ScVelo's splicing-based EM instead, where TF weights are not part of the model at all http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 TFvelo initializes the per-gene transcription-factor weight matrix via Spearman correlation between TF and target gene expression (init_weight_method = Correlation), providing a regulation-informed starting point before the generalized EM refines weights by bounded lsq_linear regression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45661-w
skills.summary: TFvelo initializes the per-gene transcription-factor weight matrix via Spearman correlation between TF and target gene expression (init_weight_method = Correlation), providing a regulation-informed starting point before the generalized EM refines weights by bounded lsq_linear regression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target genes with no candidate TFs recovered from ENCODE/ChEA, since there are no TF-target pairs to correlate Datasets where expression correlation is a poor proxy for regulation and a different init_weight_method is warranted Running ScVelo's splicing-based EM instead, where TF weights are not part of the model at all

skills.description: Use when you have two single-cell trajectories (e.g. EPI and PE lineages from blastoid/blastocyst scRNA-seq ordered by monocle3), a ligand-receptor pair list, and RTN master-regulator results, and need to find co-varying LR–TF pairs prior to Granger causal testing.
skills.name: spearman-cross-correlation-lr-tf-covariation
skills.search_text: spearman-cross-correlation-lr-tf-covariation Use when you have two single-cell trajectories (e.g. EPI and PE lineages from blastoid/blastocyst scRNA-seq ordered by monocle3), a ligand-receptor pair list, and RTN master-regulator results, and need to find co-varying LR–TF pairs prior to Granger causal testing. Communication between already-defined, stable cell types without temporal/trajectory information — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting Analysis of non-ligand-receptor communication (e.g. extracellular-vesicle-mediated) — the current TimeTalk framework is designed for cell-cell communication mediated by ligand-receptor interactions Maternal-embryo interactions — the autocrine/inter-lineage hypothesis underlying LR screening precludes exploring maternal-embryo signaling http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A TimeTalk screening step that computes Spearman cross-correlations (SCC) between interpolated ligand and transcription-factor expression profiles from two aligned developmental trajectories, retaining LR–TF pairs with SCC ≥ 0.2 as co-varying candidates before Granger causality testing. It converts trajectory-based temporal information into a filtered candidate set of communication-linked regulatory pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05283-2
skills.summary: A TimeTalk screening step that computes Spearman cross-correlations (SCC) between interpolated ligand and transcription-factor expression profiles from two aligned developmental trajectories, retaining LR–TF pairs with SCC ≥ 0.2 as co-varying candidates before Granger causality testing. It converts trajectory-based temporal information into a filtered candidate set of communication-linked regulatory pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Communication between already-defined, stable cell types without temporal/trajectory information — CellPhoneDB or CellChat are designed for that setting Analysis of non-ligand-receptor communication (e.g. extracellular-vesicle-mediated) — the current TimeTalk framework is designed for cell-cell communication mediated by ligand-receptor interactions Maternal-embryo interactions — the autocrine/inter-lineage hypothesis underlying LR screening precludes exploring maternal-embryo signaling

skills.description: Use when you have simulated (or real) per-feature expression/accessibility profiles across multiple cell types and need to verify that features with shared simulated regulatory programs group into coherent profile clusters.
skills.name: spearman-distance-k-medoids-clustering
skills.search_text: spearman-distance-k-medoids-clustering Use when you have simulated (or real) per-feature expression/accessibility profiles across multiple cell types and need to verify that features with shared simulated regulatory programs group into coherent profile clusters. The data are raw per-cell counts that have not yet been aggregated to per-cell-type averages — the profile-level clustering assumes per-cell-type mean profiles Single-cell simulation output containing layers other than scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq — MOSim's sc_mosim currently supports only those two modalities You need clustering of temporal bulk profiles with time-course structure rather than across-cell-type profile structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Clusters feature expression profiles across cell types using Spearman's distance (1 − Spearman correlation) and partition-around-medoids (k-medoids) to validate that simulated multi-omics data reproduce the co-expression/co-accessibility patterns imposed by sc_mosim. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf110
skills.summary: Clusters feature expression profiles across cell types using Spearman's distance (1 − Spearman correlation) and partition-around-medoids (k-medoids) to validate that simulated multi-omics data reproduce the co-expression/co-accessibility patterns imposed by sc_mosim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are raw per-cell counts that have not yet been aggregated to per-cell-type averages — the profile-level clustering assumes per-cell-type mean profiles Single-cell simulation output containing layers other than scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq — MOSim's sc_mosim currently supports only those two modalities You need clustering of temporal bulk profiles with time-course structure rather than across-cell-type profile structure

skills.description: Use when validating inferred miRNA activity against measured single-cell or purified-cell-type miRNA profiles, by correlating predicted vs observed fold-differences between cell-type pairs across miRNAs.
skills.name: spearman-fold-difference-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-fold-difference-correlation-analysis Use when validating inferred miRNA activity against measured single-cell or purified-cell-type miRNA profiles, by correlating predicted vs observed fold-differences between cell-type pairs across miRNAs. When no measured miRNA expression for the cell types of interest is available — the observed side of the fold-difference comparison cannot be computed When the training context differs substantially from the application context (e.g. cross-species or unmatched tissue), since miRSCAPE accuracy is expected to drop, per Figure S9 and the hematopoietic mouse case (auROC = 0.67) When the goal is differential expression of mRNAs rather than validating inferred miRNA activity — this skill only assesses miRNA prediction concordance http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validation strategy for miRSCAPE that quantifies agreement between miRSCAPE-predicted miRNA expression and observed cell-type-specific miRNA profiles by computing Spearman rank correlations between predicted and observed inter-cell-type fold-differences across miRNAs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Validation strategy for miRSCAPE that quantifies agreement between miRSCAPE-predicted miRNA expression and observed cell-type-specific miRNA profiles by computing Spearman rank correlations between predicted and observed inter-cell-type fold-differences across miRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no measured miRNA expression for the cell types of interest is available — the observed side of the fold-difference comparison cannot be computed When the training context differs substantially from the application context (e.g. cross-species or unmatched tissue), since miRSCAPE accuracy is expected to drop, per Figure S9 and the hematopoietic mouse case (auROC = 0.67) When the goal is differential expression of mRNAs rather than validating inferred miRNA activity — this skill only assesses miRNA prediction concordance

skills.description: Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (e.g., CellContrast vs SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on test sections with truth locations, to quantify global distance-structure recovery alongside neighbor-hit and JSD metrics.
skills.name: spearman-global-distance-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-global-distance-correlation-analysis Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (e.g., CellContrast vs SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on test sections with truth locations, to quantify global distance-structure recovery alongside neighbor-hit and JSD metrics. When the goal is only local neighborhood accuracy (nearest-neighbor hit or JSD of cell-type proportions), not global distance-structure fidelity When the query section lacks truth locations in .obs[['x','y']], since the correlation requires true pairwise distances as reference When the method outputs only SC-ST spot assignments without SC-SC distances or coordinates usable to derive pairwise distances http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark metric that scores a spatial-reconstruction method by computing Spearman's rank correlation between predicted and true pairwise cell-cell distances for each query cell, capturing fidelity of global spatial structure rather than only local neighbor accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Benchmark metric that scores a spatial-reconstruction method by computing Spearman's rank correlation between predicted and true pairwise cell-cell distances for each query cell, capturing fidelity of global spatial structure rather than only local neighbor accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only local neighborhood accuracy (nearest-neighbor hit or JSD of cell-type proportions), not global distance-structure fidelity When the query section lacks truth locations in .obs[['x','y']], since the correlation requires true pairwise distances as reference When the method outputs only SC-ST spot assignments without SC-SC distances or coordinates usable to derive pairwise distances

skills.description: Use when comparing read-level coverage tracks of synthetic vs real scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data binned into genomic windows (e.g., 1000-bp bins on chr1) to quantify simulator fidelity.
skills.name: spearman-pearson-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-pearson-correlation-analysis Use when comparing read-level coverage tracks of synthetic vs real scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data binned into genomic windows (e.g., 1000-bp bins on chr1) to quantify simulator fidelity. Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI-count ground truths only, so coverage correlations do not validate isoform-level fidelity Data that is already a feature/count matrix without genomic coordinates — windowed read-coverage correlation requires aligned reads with chromosomal positions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes Spearman and Pearson correlations of per-window sequencing read coverage between real and synthetic datasets to quantify how faithfully a read simulator (e.g., scReadSim vs minnow) mimics real read-sequence-level coverage. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43162-w
skills.summary: Computes Spearman and Pearson correlations of per-window sequencing read coverage between real and synthetic datasets to quantify how faithfully a read simulator (e.g., scReadSim vs minnow) mimics real read-sequence-level coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking isoform abundance or alternative splicing tools — scReadSim provides gene-level UMI-count ground truths only, so coverage correlations do not validate isoform-level fidelity Data that is already a feature/count matrix without genomic coordinates — windowed read-coverage correlation requires aligned reads with chromosomal positions

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample gene-signature scores and a continuous per-sample metadata variable (purity/VAF) in a pdacR dataset and need a rank-based association with rho, p-value, and n.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation Use when you have per-sample gene-signature scores and a continuous per-sample metadata variable (purity/VAF) in a pdacR dataset and need a rank-based association with rho, p-value, and n. The comparison variable is categorical or the relationship is expected to be linear with Gaussian residuals where parametric correlation would be preferred The dataset has not been filtered to confirmed PDAC samples (e.g., using all 182 TCGA-PAAD samples instead of the 150 whitelisted ones), which the article warns can introduce non-specificity The goal is single-cell population separation, where bulk transcriptomic data cannot fully separate cellular populations http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Compute nonparametric Spearman rank correlations between PDAC gene-signature scores (e.g., Collisson Exocrine, Bailey ADEX) and sample purity proxies (predicted mean VAF or ABSOLUTE purity) using cor.test(method = 'spearman') in R on pdacR-parsed datasets, to test whether a signature predicts tumor cellularity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-04461-6
skills.summary: Compute nonparametric Spearman rank correlations between PDAC gene-signature scores (e.g., Collisson Exocrine, Bailey ADEX) and sample purity proxies (predicted mean VAF or ABSOLUTE purity) using cor.test(method = 'spearman') in R on pdacR-parsed datasets, to test whether a signature predicts tumor cellularity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison variable is categorical or the relationship is expected to be linear with Gaussian residuals where parametric correlation would be preferred The dataset has not been filtered to confirmed PDAC samples (e.g., using all 182 TCGA-PAAD samples instead of the 150 whitelisted ones), which the article warns can introduce non-specificity The goal is single-cell population separation, where bulk transcriptomic data cannot fully separate cellular populations

skills.description: Use when you have per-node scores (e.g., scBONITA node importance from rule inference on KEGG networks) plus graph-derived node statistics and need to test their association via Spearman rank correlation.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis Use when you have per-node scores (e.g., scBONITA node importance from rule inference on KEGG networks) plus graph-derived node statistics and need to test their association via Spearman rank correlation. When the goal is to validate that scores DO track network topology — this workflow is designed to demonstrate independence from centrality measures, not to predict topology from scores When node scores and network topology come from different, non-corresponding networks — the correlation must be computed per shared network When the data are paired per-cell measurements across two conditions; Pearson correlation of importance vectors (as done for cross-subpopulation comparison) is more appropriate than rank correlation http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Statistical test of whether scBONITA node importance scores are correlated with network-topology centrality measures (degree, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector, in-/out-degree) using Spearman rank correlation, to demonstrate that importance scores carry information distinct from network topology alone. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-022-00246-5
skills.summary: Statistical test of whether scBONITA node importance scores are correlated with network-topology centrality measures (degree, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector, in-/out-degree) using Spearman rank correlation, to demonstrate that importance scores carry information distinct from network topology alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to validate that scores DO track network topology — this workflow is designed to demonstrate independence from centrality measures, not to predict topology from scores When node scores and network topology come from different, non-corresponding networks — the correlation must be computed per shared network When the data are paired per-cell measurements across two conditions; Pearson correlation of importance vectors (as done for cross-subpopulation comparison) is more appropriate than rank correlation

skills.description: Use when comparing pseudotime (or any ranked) orderings between a full single-cell dataset and repeated random cell subsamples, to measure ordering robustness of trajectory-inference methods such as DTFLOW, Scanpy, or Monocle2.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis Use when comparing pseudotime (or any ranked) orderings between a full single-cell dataset and repeated random cell subsamples, to measure ordering robustness of trajectory-inference methods such as DTFLOW, Scanpy, or Monocle2. Input is raw gene expression or a single pseudotime ordering only — Spearman correlation requires two ranked orderings over the same cells to compare The goal is branch/topology detection or accuracy against known time stages — the paper uses Kendall rank correlation against time-stage labels for accuracy, not this subsampling robustness protocol Datasets other than the ME/MMP settings without a defined full-data reference ordering to correlate subsample orderings against http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies the stability of pseudotime orderings by computing Spearman rank correlations between cell orderings obtained on randomly subsampled data (90% of ME cells, 2500 of 2730 MMP cells) and the corresponding full-data orderings, aggregating mean, standard deviation, and variance per method. In the DTFLOW paper this robustness protocol distinguishes DTFLOW from Scanpy and Monocle2. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Quantifies the stability of pseudotime orderings by computing Spearman rank correlations between cell orderings obtained on randomly subsampled data (90% of ME cells, 2500 of 2730 MMP cells) and the corresponding full-data orderings, aggregating mean, standard deviation, and variance per method. In the DTFLOW paper this robustness protocol distinguishes DTFLOW from Scanpy and Monocle2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw gene expression or a single pseudotime ordering only — Spearman correlation requires two ranked orderings over the same cells to compare The goal is branch/topology detection or accuracy against known time stages — the paper uses Kendall rank correlation against time-stage labels for accuracy, not this subsampling robustness protocol Datasets other than the ME/MMP settings without a defined full-data reference ordering to correlate subsample orderings against

skills.description: Use when a multimodal single-cell dataset (e.g., CITE-seq RNA + ADT) is available and you need to test whether an imputation or transformation in one modality makes its pairwise cell distances more consistent with distances in the other modality.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis Use when a multimodal single-cell dataset (e.g., CITE-seq RNA + ADT) is available and you need to test whether an imputation or transformation in one modality makes its pairwise cell distances more consistent with distances in the other modality. When only one modality is present (no ADT/protein measurements) and there is no second distance structure to correlate against When the analysis goal is cluster/label agreement rather than concordance of pairwise cell-distance orderings — Spearman on distance vectors answers the latter, not the former When distance distributions are already on the same scale and a direct distance comparison (e.g., Procrustes or RMSE) is preferred over rank-based correlation http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Quantifies agreement between pairwise cell-distance structures computed in two feature spaces (e.g., imputed/log-normalized gene expression vs. ADT protein counts from CITE-seq) using the Spearman rank correlation. In the ALRA paper this is the metric demonstrating that ALRA imputation improves RNA-to-protein distance concordance on the CBMC dataset (Spearman ~0.36 raw → ~0.64 after ALRA). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between pairwise cell-distance structures computed in two feature spaces (e.g., imputed/log-normalized gene expression vs. ADT protein counts from CITE-seq) using the Spearman rank correlation. In the ALRA paper this is the metric demonstrating that ALRA imputation improves RNA-to-protein distance concordance on the CBMC dataset (Spearman ~0.36 raw → ~0.64 after ALRA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only one modality is present (no ADT/protein measurements) and there is no second distance structure to correlate against When the analysis goal is cluster/label agreement rather than concordance of pairwise cell-distance orderings — Spearman on distance vectors answers the latter, not the former When distance distributions are already on the same scale and a direct distance comparison (e.g., Procrustes or RMSE) is preferred over rank-based correlation

skills.description: Use when pseudobulk 3'UTR isoform counts from scRNA-seq samples (e.g., FACS-sorted HSCs or ESCs) need to be benchmarked against bulk 3' end sequencing TPMs via rank correlation.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis Use when pseudobulk 3'UTR isoform counts from scRNA-seq samples (e.g., FACS-sorted HSCs or ESCs) need to be benchmarked against bulk 3' end sequencing TPMs via rank correlation. Input is already a bulk 3'-seq feature table with no single-cell UMI matrix — there is nothing to pseudobulk or validate The goal is differential 3'UTR usage testing across perturbations rather than benchmarking against a bulk gold standard (use scUTRboot instead) Raw FASTQ data that still needs kallisto-bustools quantification — run the scUTRquant pipeline first to obtain '*.txs.Rds' outputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates scUTRquant-derived 3'UTR isoform quantification from scRNA-seq by computing Spearman rank correlations between pseudobulk UMI-derived TPMs and gold-standard bulk 3'-seq TPMs (HSC: ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391; ESC: PolyASite-annotated bulk data). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-48254-9
skills.summary: Validates scUTRquant-derived 3'UTR isoform quantification from scRNA-seq by computing Spearman rank correlations between pseudobulk UMI-derived TPMs and gold-standard bulk 3'-seq TPMs (HSC: ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391; ESC: PolyASite-annotated bulk data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a bulk 3'-seq feature table with no single-cell UMI matrix — there is nothing to pseudobulk or validate The goal is differential 3'UTR usage testing across perturbations rather than benchmarking against a bulk gold standard (use scUTRboot instead) Raw FASTQ data that still needs kallisto-bustools quantification — run the scUTRquant pipeline first to obtain '*.txs.Rds' outputs

skills.description: Use when you have ranked gene lists from two or more SVG/HVG identification methods on the same dataset and need to quantify rank agreement via Spearman correlations plus top-n (n = 10, 20, 50, 100, 200) overlap counts.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis Use when you have ranked gene lists from two or more SVG/HVG identification methods on the same dataset and need to quantify rank agreement via Spearman correlations plus top-n (n = 10, 20, 50, 100, 200) overlap counts. The goal is to identify or rank SVGs themselves on a new dataset rather than to compare existing rankings — run nnSVG (or a baseline) directly instead Only raw counts and spatial coordinates are available with no per-method ranked gene lists — the correlations require ranked outputs (e.g., nnSVG rank/LR_stat columns) from each method first Comparing methods across different tissues or spot sets, where gene rankings are not defined over a shared gene universe and set overlaps are not meaningful Quantify agreement between SVG gene rankings (e.g., nnSVG vs. HVGs, Moran's I, SPARK-X) using Spearman rank correlations and top-n set overlaps at n = 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 across datasets. This skill tests whether rankings from a new SVG method reproduce those of baseline methods rather than re-detecting SVGs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z
skills.summary: Quantify agreement between SVG gene rankings (e.g., nnSVG vs. HVGs, Moran's I, SPARK-X) using Spearman rank correlations and top-n set overlaps at n = 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 across datasets. This skill tests whether rankings from a new SVG method reproduce those of baseline methods rather than re-detecting SVGs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify or rank SVGs themselves on a new dataset rather than to compare existing rankings — run nnSVG (or a baseline) directly instead Only raw counts and spatial coordinates are available with no per-method ranked gene lists — the correlations require ranked outputs (e.g., nnSVG rank/LR_stat columns) from each method first Comparing methods across different tissues or spot sets, where gene rankings are not defined over a shared gene universe and set overlaps are not meaningful

skills.description: Use when a continuous or ordinal data matrix and response are given and you need fast, robust, nonparametric quantification of feature-response and feature-pair associations to feed a correlation-based filter (RRCT, mRMR_Spearman).
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-computation
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-computation Use when a continuous or ordinal data matrix and response are given and you need fast, robust, nonparametric quantification of feature-response and feature-pair associations to feed a correlation-based filter (RRCT, mRMR_Spearman). The analysis requires capturing non-monotonic or purely categorical associations that rank correlations cannot quantify (crude histogram-based mutual information is 'likely problematic', so a discrete-MI toolbox such as FEAST is a different choice, but not a fix for continuous inputs) The goal is to account for feature interactions/complementarity at selection time using Spearman correlations alone — mRMR_Spearman ignores the conditional-relevance term; use the full RRCT criterion instead Features are expected to be independent and redundant filtering provides no benefit (correlation-based redundancy penalties would discard useful features) Computes Spearman rank correlation coefficients between each feature and the response and between all feature pairs, then optionally applies the nonlinear information-theoretic transformation used by RRCT/mRMR_Spearman to derive relevance and redundancy terms. This is the fast, robust correlation backbone of the RRCT feature-selection framework (Tsanas, Patterns 2022). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100471
skills.summary: Computes Spearman rank correlation coefficients between each feature and the response and between all feature pairs, then optionally applies the nonlinear information-theoretic transformation used by RRCT/mRMR_Spearman to derive relevance and redundancy terms. This is the fast, robust correlation backbone of the RRCT feature-selection framework (Tsanas, Patterns 2022).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires capturing non-monotonic or purely categorical associations that rank correlations cannot quantify (crude histogram-based mutual information is 'likely problematic', so a discrete-MI toolbox such as FEAST is a different choice, but not a fix for continuous inputs) The goal is to account for feature interactions/complementarity at selection time using Spearman correlations alone — mRMR_Spearman ignores the conditional-relevance term; use the full RRCT criterion instead Features are expected to be independent and redundant filtering provides no benefit (correlation-based redundancy penalties would discard useful features)

skills.description: Use when paired CITE-seq data (ADT protein + RNA counts) is available and you need a ground-truth-based readout of whether scRNA-seq denoising improves protein-mRNA co-expression, e.g. CD3E detection vs CD3 protein.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-computation
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-computation Use when paired CITE-seq data (ADT protein + RNA counts) is available and you need a ground-truth-based readout of whether scRNA-seq denoising improves protein-mRNA co-expression, e.g. CD3E detection vs CD3 protein. No paired protein (ADT) measurements exist, so there is no external ground truth against which to rank-correlate the RNA signal The goal is gene-gene (rather than protein-mRNA) co-expression assessment, where rank correlation against an independent protein measurement is not applicable Data has already been size-factor normalized, since DCA in this benchmark runs on raw counts without normalization and the comparison must use the same counts basis http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Compute Spearman rank correlations between per-cell CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein measurements and matching mRNA levels, before and after DCA denoising, to validate that denoising improves protein-RNA co-expression agreement (Fig. 6 of Eraslan et al. 2019). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07931-2
skills.summary: Compute Spearman rank correlations between per-cell CITE-seq antibody-derived-tag (ADT) protein measurements and matching mRNA levels, before and after DCA denoising, to validate that denoising improves protein-RNA co-expression agreement (Fig. 6 of Eraslan et al. 2019).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No paired protein (ADT) measurements exist, so there is no external ground truth against which to rank-correlate the RNA signal The goal is gene-gene (rather than protein-mRNA) co-expression assessment, where rank correlation against an independent protein measurement is not applicable Data has already been size-factor normalized, since DCA in this benchmark runs on raw counts without normalization and the comparison must use the same counts basis

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices need a quantitative low-dimensional cell representation built by clustering genes with akin expression-rank trends, as in scQA's LC2 module.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-gene-clustering
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-gene-clustering Use when scRNA-seq count matrices need a quantitative low-dimensional cell representation built by clustering genes with akin expression-rank trends, as in scQA's LC2 module. If the goal is a binary (qualitative) low-dimensional representation based on dropout patterns — that is the separate LC1 module, not LC2. If input is not a cells-by-genes expression matrix without row/column names — the scQA executable requires this exact unlabeled matrix format. If the number of cell types is already fixed and a supervised or k-means-style assignment suffices; LC2 is an unsupervised gene-clustering step within scQA's pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Implementation of scQA's quantitative landmark constructor (LC2), which groups quasi-trend-preserved genes via Spearman rank correlation similarity graphs and iterative cluster-gene assignment to build a quantitative low-dimensional cell-landmark matrix (LM2/Q2). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.12.021
skills.summary: Implementation of scQA's quantitative landmark constructor (LC2), which groups quasi-trend-preserved genes via Spearman rank correlation similarity graphs and iterative cluster-gene assignment to build a quantitative low-dimensional cell-landmark matrix (LM2/Q2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: If the goal is a binary (qualitative) low-dimensional representation based on dropout patterns — that is the separate LC1 module, not LC2. If input is not a cells-by-genes expression matrix without row/column names — the scQA executable requires this exact unlabeled matrix format. If the number of cell types is already fixed and a supervised or k-means-style assignment suffices; LC2 is an unsupervised gene-clustering step within scQA's pipeline.

skills.description: Use when you need a cross-dataset cell-cell similarity network from scRNA-seq expression data for a gene set (e.g. GOmouse, HVGs) as the first step of MetaNeighbor neighbor voting or AUROC estimation.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-network-construction
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-network-construction Use when you need a cross-dataset cell-cell similarity network from scRNA-seq expression data for a gene set (e.g. GOmouse, HVGs) as the first step of MetaNeighbor neighbor voting or AUROC estimation. The gene set contains fewer than two genes, or gene set names do not match the gene names of the expression matrix (README lists these as critical requirements) You need an unsupervised marker gene ranking rather than a similarity network over cells Sample count is very large without parallelization, since the ranking step does not scale well in the R environment Constructs a cell-cell similarity network by computing Spearman rank correlations between all pairs of cells across scRNA-seq datasets based on a chosen gene set, then re-ranking and standardizing network values to lie between 0 and 1 for use in MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting predictor. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-03282-0
skills.summary: Constructs a cell-cell similarity network by computing Spearman rank correlations between all pairs of cells across scRNA-seq datasets based on a chosen gene set, then re-ranking and standardizing network values to lie between 0 and 1 for use in MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting predictor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The gene set contains fewer than two genes, or gene set names do not match the gene names of the expression matrix (README lists these as critical requirements) You need an unsupervised marker gene ranking rather than a similarity network over cells Sample count is very large without parallelization, since the ranking step does not scale well in the R environment

skills.description: Use when two alternative lineage groupings (e.g., GEMLI-predicted vs. ground-truth barcode lineages) must be compared at the level of gene-category enrichment rather than per-gene lists, to quantify recovery of memory gene GO-terms.
skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-of-enrichment-profiles
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-of-enrichment-profiles Use when two alternative lineage groupings (e.g., GEMLI-predicted vs. ground-truth barcode lineages) must be compared at the level of gene-category enrichment rather than per-gene lists, to quantify recovery of memory gene GO-terms. Cell populations contain only distantly related cells, where GEMLI lineage prediction (and hence the predicted-lineage enrichment profile) is expected to be less robust The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months; GEMLI's scope is limited to lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions You need per-lineage identity agreement rather than category-level (GO-term) agreement; a rank correlation of enrichment profiles does not verify cell-to-cell lineage assignments http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Validates that GEMLI-predicted lineages recover the same heritable (gene expression memory) gene categories as ground-truth barcode lineages by comparing GO biological process over-representation profiles with a Spearman rank correlation (target > 0.7, per Fig. 3a). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-47158-y
skills.summary: Validates that GEMLI-predicted lineages recover the same heritable (gene expression memory) gene categories as ground-truth barcode lineages by comparing GO biological process over-representation profiles with a Spearman rank correlation (target > 0.7, per Fig. 3a).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell populations contain only distantly related cells, where GEMLI lineage prediction (and hence the predicted-lineage enrichment profile) is expected to be less robust The goal is long-term lineage tracing over weeks or months; GEMLI's scope is limited to lineages over about 1-5 cell divisions You need per-lineage identity agreement rather than category-level (GO-term) agreement; a rank correlation of enrichment profiles does not verify cell-to-cell lineage assignments
