skills.name: spearman-rank-correlation-of-spatial-distances
skills.search_text: spearman-rank-correlation-of-spatial-distances Use when evaluating global spatial reconstruction quality of SC-to-ST mapped single-cell data — i.e., checking whether predicted pairwise cell-cell distances preserve the rank ordering of true coordinates in a query h5ad with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']]. You need local neighbor-level accuracy (use the average nearest neighbor hit over k = 20..200 or Jensen-Shannon distance of cell-type proportions instead) The query SC data has no truth coordinates for computing true pairwise distances, so the rank correlation cannot be validated The query data has a large gap from the ST reference, where forced SC-ST mapping can introduce bias — consider the MDS/de novo path, accepting that it loses the reference's cell distribution pre-knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes Spearman's rank correlation between predicted and true pairwise SC-SC distances after SC-ST spatial mapping, serving as the global spatial reconstruction metric in the CellContrast benchmark alongside nearest neighbor hit and Jensen-Shannon distance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Computes Spearman's rank correlation between predicted and true pairwise SC-SC distances after SC-ST spatial mapping, serving as the global spatial reconstruction metric in the CellContrast benchmark alongside nearest neighbor hit and Jensen-Shannon distance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need local neighbor-level accuracy (use the average nearest neighbor hit over k = 20..200 or Jensen-Shannon distance of cell-type proportions instead) The query SC data has no truth coordinates for computing true pairwise distances, so the rank correlation cannot be validated The query data has a large gap from the ST reference, where forced SC-ST mapping can introduce bias — consider the MDS/de novo path, accepting that it loses the reference's cell distribution pre-knowledge

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify how many species are covered by oggmap's precomputed gene age assignments across Ensembl, eggNOG, or PLAZA sources, or to verify reported coverage totals before relying on shipped orthomaps.
skills.name: species-coverage-summary-tabulation
skills.search_text: species-coverage-summary-tabulation Use when you need to quantify how many species are covered by oggmap's precomputed gene age assignments across Ensembl, eggNOG, or PLAZA sources, or to verify reported coverage totals before relying on shipped orthomaps. You need gene age assignments for a species not present in the shipped precomputed files — instead extract a fresh orthomap with of2orthomap or plaza2orthomap from OrthoFinder, eggNOG, orthomcl, or PLAZA results. Your goal is gene-age-weighted expression (TEI) analysis on scRNA data rather than coverage statistics — this tabulation skill does not touch Scanpy objects or expression data. The input is raw orthogroup output (OrthoFinder/eggNOG results) rather than oggmap's already-extracted gene age class files — use the appropriate orthomap extraction sub-command first. http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0621 Enumerate and tabulate the eukaryotic species coverage of oggmap's precomputed gene age class assignments by loading the shipped Ensembl release-110, eggNOG v6, and PLAZA v5 files, counting distinct species with at least one LCA-derived gene age assignment per source, and writing the per-source counts (317 Ensembl species; 1322 eggNOG species; 98 PLAZA dicots + 52 PLAZA monocots) to a summary table. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Enumerate and tabulate the eukaryotic species coverage of oggmap's precomputed gene age class assignments by loading the shipped Ensembl release-110, eggNOG v6, and PLAZA v5 files, counting distinct species with at least one LCA-derived gene age assignment per source, and writing the per-source counts (317 Ensembl species; 1322 eggNOG species; 98 PLAZA dicots + 52 PLAZA monocots) to a summary table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need gene age assignments for a species not present in the shipped precomputed files — instead extract a fresh orthomap with of2orthomap or plaza2orthomap from OrthoFinder, eggNOG, orthomcl, or PLAZA results. Your goal is gene-age-weighted expression (TEI) analysis on scRNA data rather than coverage statistics — this tabulation skill does not touch Scanpy objects or expression data. The input is raw orthogroup output (OrthoFinder/eggNOG results) rather than oggmap's already-extracted gene age class files — use the appropriate orthomap extraction sub-command first.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL tasks) and you need to test whether biology conservation, measured as ALCS from SCCAF self-projection, degrades with increasing species divergence time.
skills.name: species-divergence-time-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: species-divergence-time-correlation-analysis Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL tasks) and you need to test whether biology conservation, measured as ALCS from SCCAF self-projection, degrades with increasing species divergence time. The analysis involves only a single species (no cross-species divergence), so ALCS-versus-divergence-time trends cannot be defined Cell type annotations are uncurated or cross-species cell type homology is unknown — the paper states quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and confident known cell type homology The mapping of cell types across species is non-one-to-one; the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies how the accuracy loss of cell type self-projection (ALCS) changes as more distantly diverged species are integrated, regressing or plotting per-method ALCS against species divergence-time metadata across cross-species scRNA-seq integration tasks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Quantifies how the accuracy loss of cell type self-projection (ALCS) changes as more distantly diverged species are integrated, regressing or plotting per-method ALCS against species divergence-time metadata across cross-species scRNA-seq integration tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis involves only a single species (no cross-species divergence), so ALCS-versus-divergence-time trends cannot be defined Cell type annotations are uncurated or cross-species cell type homology is unknown — the paper states quantitative scoring assumes accurate annotations and confident known cell type homology The mapping of cell types across species is non-one-to-one; the benchmark is limited to one-to-one cell type mappings

skills.description: Use when you have integrated single-cell data from two or more species in a joint latent space (e.g., via scVI, scANVI or SeuratV4) and need to quantify species mixing versus biology conservation to compare integration strategies.
skills.name: species-mixing-metric-evaluation
skills.search_text: species-mixing-metric-evaluation Use when you have integrated single-cell data from two or more species in a joint latent space (e.g., via scVI, scANVI or SeuratV4) and need to quantify species mixing versus biology conservation to compare integration strategies. When cell type annotations are unreliable or literature cell type homology is unknown — the quantitative scoring system depends on these two assumptions When the goal is a non-one-to-one cell type mapping across species — the benchmark scoring uses one-to-one cell type mappings and valid non-one-to-one mappings were not assessed When evaluating whole-body atlas integration with challenging gene homology annotation, where SAMap-type approaches are more appropriate than flat homology-mapping scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Evaluates cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integration quality by scoring homology-mapping × algorithm combinations with 9 established integration metrics plus a biology conservation metric for maintenance of cell type distinguishability, as implemented in the BENGAL pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Evaluates cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integration quality by scoring homology-mapping × algorithm combinations with 9 established integration metrics plus a biology conservation metric for maintenance of cell type distinguishability, as implemented in the BENGAL pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When cell type annotations are unreliable or literature cell type homology is unknown — the quantitative scoring system depends on these two assumptions When the goal is a non-one-to-one cell type mapping across species — the benchmark scoring uses one-to-one cell type mappings and valid non-one-to-one mappings were not assessed When evaluating whole-body atlas integration with challenging gene homology annotation, where SAMap-type approaches are more appropriate than flat homology-mapping scores

skills.description: Use when evaluating how the number of species involved in a cross-species integration affects cell type distinguishability, e.g. detecting overcorrection of few-species cell types by nearest-neighbour methods via iso_F1 trends.
skills.name: species-scaling-trend-analysis
skills.search_text: species-scaling-trend-analysis Use when evaluating how the number of species involved in a cross-species integration affects cell type distinguishability, e.g. detecting overcorrection of few-species cell types by nearest-neighbour methods via iso_F1 trends. When the goal is to measure species mixing rather than biology conservation — iso_F1 addresses maintenance of cell type distinguishability, not how well species are mixed in the embedding When cell type annotations or known cell type homology are unreliable, since the metric depends on accurate annotations and confident one-to-one homology When the mapping across species is non-one-to-one or cell type correspondence needs hierarchical/complex description, which this flat-mapping-based metric does not cover http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes and plots how biology-conservation metrics, especially isolated-label F1 (iso_F1), change as more species are added to a cross-species scRNA-seq integration, using the BENGAL pipeline's 28 gene-homology-mapping x integration-algorithm strategies. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-41855-w
skills.summary: Computes and plots how biology-conservation metrics, especially isolated-label F1 (iso_F1), change as more species are added to a cross-species scRNA-seq integration, using the BENGAL pipeline's 28 gene-homology-mapping x integration-algorithm strategies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to measure species mixing rather than biology conservation — iso_F1 addresses maintenance of cell type distinguishability, not how well species are mixed in the embedding When cell type annotations or known cell type homology are unreliable, since the metric depends on accurate annotations and confident one-to-one homology When the mapping across species is non-one-to-one or cell type correspondence needs hierarchical/complex description, which this flat-mapping-based metric does not cover

skills.description: Use when building species- and tissue-stratified sequence benchmark sets from site-level modification calls, and redundancy must be removed before balanced train/test partitioning (e.g., CD-HIT <80% cutoff).
skills.name: species-tissue-dataset-organization
skills.search_text: species-tissue-dataset-organization Use when building species- and tissue-stratified sequence benchmark sets from site-level modification calls, and redundancy must be removed before balanced train/test partitioning (e.g., CD-HIT <80% cutoff). Sequences are already deduplicated or you are reusing the published Table 3 benchmark splits — re-running CD-HIT and re-splitting would break comparability with reported results Your modification sites come from antibody-based (m6A-seq/MeRIP) peak data rather than the antibody-independent endoribonuclease detection data, since single-nucleotide resolution of the site center is required for 41-nt segment labeling The task is single-species, single-tissue prediction with no need for tissue stratification — a generic sequence benchmark suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Curate balanced, tissue-specific RNA benchmark datasets (e.g., 11 species-tissue m6A sets spanning brain, liver, kidney, heart, and testis of human, mouse, and rat) by extracting 41-nt segments centered on candidate modification sites and deduplicating with CD-HIT below 80% sequence similarity before splitting into equal positive/negative training and testing subsets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.07.034
skills.summary: Curate balanced, tissue-specific RNA benchmark datasets (e.g., 11 species-tissue m6A sets spanning brain, liver, kidney, heart, and testis of human, mouse, and rat) by extracting 41-nt segments centered on candidate modification sites and deduplicating with CD-HIT below 80% sequence similarity before splitting into equal positive/negative training and testing subsets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are already deduplicated or you are reusing the published Table 3 benchmark splits — re-running CD-HIT and re-splitting would break comparability with reported results Your modification sites come from antibody-based (m6A-seq/MeRIP) peak data rather than the antibody-independent endoribonuclease detection data, since single-nucleotide resolution of the site center is required for 41-nt segment labeling The task is single-species, single-tissue prediction with no need for tissue stratification — a generic sequence benchmark suffices

skills.description: Use when you have a cell-level embedding score for >60k paired TCR/transcriptome cells (10x dataset) with specificity annotations (e.g., GILGFVFTL, GLCTLVAML, IVTDFSVIK, ELAGIGILTV) and want per-epitope summaries plus correlation with TCRdist similarity.
skills.name: specificity-stratified-aggregation
skills.search_text: specificity-stratified-aggregation Use when you have a cell-level embedding score for >60k paired TCR/transcriptome cells (10x dataset) with specificity annotations (e.g., GILGFVFTL, GLCTLVAML, IVTDFSVIK, ELAGIGILTV) and want per-epitope summaries plus correlation with TCRdist similarity. When no antigen-specificity annotation is available for the cells, since stratification and per-epitope aggregation cannot be performed When the question requires cell-level (not specificity-group-level) resolution — aggregation loses within-clonotype and within-epitope heterogeneity When data are unpaired or lack TCR sequences, since TCR-contribution scores and TCRdist similarity cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2830 Stratifies single-cell T cells by antigen specificity (epitope) and aggregates per-cell scores (e.g., mvTCR TCR-contribution, the angular distance between joint and TCR-unimodal embeddings) into per-specificity averages, then relates them to TCR sequence similarity (TCRdist) via Pearson correlation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49806-9
skills.summary: Stratifies single-cell T cells by antigen specificity (epitope) and aggregates per-cell scores (e.g., mvTCR TCR-contribution, the angular distance between joint and TCR-unimodal embeddings) into per-specificity averages, then relates them to TCR sequence similarity (TCRdist) via Pearson correlation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no antigen-specificity annotation is available for the cells, since stratification and per-epitope aggregation cannot be performed When the question requires cell-level (not specificity-group-level) resolution — aggregation loses within-clonotype and within-epitope heterogeneity When data are unpaired or lack TCR sequences, since TCR-contribution scores and TCRdist similarity cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when a NATMI ExtractEdges.py output folder of per-pair specificity/expression edge weights is available and the goal is to identify the top communicating cell-type pairs or communities (e.g. Fig. 5 Tabula Muris cardiac Nppa-Npr3).
skills.name: specificity-weighted-cell-pair-ranking
skills.search_text: specificity-weighted-cell-pair-ranking Use when a NATMI ExtractEdges.py output folder of per-pair specificity/expression edge weights is available and the goal is to identify the top communicating cell-type pairs or communities (e.g. Fig. 5 Tabula Muris cardiac Nppa-Npr3). When comparing two conditions and looking for differing edges — use NATMI's DiffEdges.py delta network analysis instead When spatial context or downstream signalling consequences are required — NATMI does not support spatial transcriptomics or downstream signalling prediction When heteromeric ligand-receptor complexes are essential to the question — NATMI does not model them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Aggregates NATMI ligand-receptor specificity edges between the same sending/receiving cell-type pair into summary edges whose weights are the sum of per-pair specificity weights, then ranks these cell-pair summary edges to identify the most highly communicating cellular communities and the ligand-receptor pairs driving them. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-18873-z
skills.summary: Aggregates NATMI ligand-receptor specificity edges between the same sending/receiving cell-type pair into summary edges whose weights are the sum of per-pair specificity weights, then ranks these cell-pair summary edges to identify the most highly communicating cellular communities and the ligand-receptor pairs driving them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When comparing two conditions and looking for differing edges — use NATMI's DiffEdges.py delta network analysis instead When spatial context or downstream signalling consequences are required — NATMI does not support spatial transcriptomics or downstream signalling prediction When heteromeric ligand-receptor complexes are essential to the question — NATMI does not model them

skills.description: Use when running Bfimpute on an unlabeled scRNA-seq count matrix and the number of cell types is known (e.g., k=7 for the Chu et al. 2016 dataset), so cells must be grouped before group-wise imputation.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-cell-grouping
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-cell-grouping Use when running Bfimpute on an unlabeled scRNA-seq count matrix and the number of cell types is known (e.g., k=7 for the Chu et al. 2016 dataset), so cells must be grouped before group-wise imputation. True cell type labels are already available — use ccluster="labeled" with the label parameter instead of spectral clustering, since the README notes labels 'gain more accuracy' The count matrix is already normalized and log-transformed — set normalized=TRUE rather than letting Bfimpute apply CPM and log10 (bias 1.01) again The number of cell types is unknown and cannot be estimated — the Spectrum/specc option requires a specific k to be supplied http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Group single-cell RNA-seq cells into cell-type clusters using spectral clustering (Spectrum or kernlab specc) so that Bfimpute can impute dropouts within each cell group, leveraging similar cells to strengthen cell-to-cell relationships. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2021.100133
skills.summary: Group single-cell RNA-seq cells into cell-type clusters using spectral clustering (Spectrum or kernlab specc) so that Bfimpute can impute dropouts within each cell group, leveraging similar cells to strengthen cell-to-cell relationships.
skills.when_to_use_negative: True cell type labels are already available — use ccluster="labeled" with the label parameter instead of spectral clustering, since the README notes labels 'gain more accuracy' The count matrix is already normalized and log-transformed — set normalized=TRUE rather than letting Bfimpute apply CPM and log10 (bias 1.01) again The number of cell types is unknown and cannot be estimated — the Spectrum/specc option requires a specific k to be supplied

When only a raw high-dimensional expression matrix is available and no similarity-learning step (sparse subspace representation or enhancement) has been performed — spectral clustering here presumes a learned affinity input For very large-scale scRNA-seq datasets where runtime matters — SSRE is described as relatively time-consuming on large-scale data When the goal is multi-omics integration or incorporation of gene-function/regulatory information — these are only proposed as future work, not implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run spectral clustering on a learned cell-to-cell similarity matrix (SSR sparse subspace representation or SSRE-enhanced similarity) to identify cell types from scRNA-seq data, and quantify clustering accuracy with NMI/ARI against ground-truth labels. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.09.004
skills.summary: Run spectral clustering on a learned cell-to-cell similarity matrix (SSR sparse subspace representation or SSRE-enhanced similarity) to identify cell types from scRNA-seq data, and quantify clustering accuracy with NMI/ARI against ground-truth labels.

skills.description: Use when you have 2D t-SNE or UMAP cell embeddings (original and hyperparameter-optimized) for scRNA-seq data with annotated cell type labels and need an objective cluster-vs-label agreement metric such as ARI.

skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-of-2d-embeddings Use when you have 2D t-SNE or UMAP cell embeddings (original and hyperparameter-optimized) for scRNA-seq data with annotated cell type labels and need an objective cluster-vs-label agreement metric such as ARI. Cells lack annotated cell type labels, so no external reference exists against which to compute the adjusted Rand index The goal is embedding-quality assessment alone (dubious vs trustworthy detection), which scDEED's reliability scores already provide without clustering Using a dimensionality reduction method other than t-SNE/UMAP in Seurat without adapting scDEED, since the package currently supports only those two http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantitatively scores 2D t-SNE/UMAP cell embeddings by applying spectral clustering to the embedding coordinates and computing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) of the resulting clusters against annotated cell types, so that scDEED-optimized embeddings can be compared with default-hyperparameter embeddings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45891-y
skills.summary: Quantitatively scores 2D t-SNE/UMAP cell embeddings by applying spectral clustering to the embedding coordinates and computing the adjusted Rand index (ARI) of the resulting clusters against annotated cell types, so that scDEED-optimized embeddings can be compared with default-hyperparameter embeddings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells lack annotated cell type labels, so no external reference exists against which to compute the adjusted Rand index The goal is embedding-quality assessment alone (dubious vs trustworthy detection), which scDEED's reliability scores already provide without clustering Using a dimensionality reduction method other than t-SNE/UMAP in Seurat without adapting scDEED, since the package currently supports only those two

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq junction/AS matrices are QC-filtered and imputed and the goal is unsupervised discovery of splicing-defined cell subpopulations that gene-expression clustering misses.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-of-as-matrices
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-of-as-matrices Use when single-cell RNA-seq junction/AS matrices are QC-filtered and imputed and the goal is unsupervised discovery of splicing-defined cell subpopulations that gene-expression clustering misses. The input is raw junction reads or an unfiltered/unimputed junction matrix — QC and iterative weighted KNN imputation must precede spectral clustering The goal is differential splicing analysis with known cell labels (use BRIE, Expedition, rMATS, or MARVEL instead); SCASL is designed for unsupervised clustering without predefined labels Very few cells or extremely sparse junction coverage make the demo caveat relevant — run-to-run stochasticity may dominate the clustering result http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 SCASL's spectral clustering step groups single cells by their imputed alternative splicing (AS) probability matrix, concatenated with an NA indicator matrix, revealing subpopulations (e.g., C3 vs C4 tumor-infiltrating Tregs) invisible to gene-expression-based clustering. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: SCASL's spectral clustering step groups single cells by their imputed alternative splicing (AS) probability matrix, concatenated with an NA indicator matrix, revealing subpopulations (e.g., C3 vs C4 tumor-infiltrating Tregs) invisible to gene-expression-based clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw junction reads or an unfiltered/unimputed junction matrix — QC and iterative weighted KNN imputation must precede spectral clustering The goal is differential splicing analysis with known cell labels (use BRIE, Expedition, rMATS, or MARVEL instead); SCASL is designed for unsupervised clustering without predefined labels Very few cells or extremely sparse junction coverage make the demo caveat relevant — run-to-run stochasticity may dominate the clustering result

skills.description: Use when you have GAN-generated single-cell expression profiles produced by mapping spatial transcriptomics data (x1) into the scRNA-seq domain, and you need to verify or derive spatially informed structure at single-cell resolution.
skills.name: spectral-clustering-of-generated-expression-profiles
skills.search_text: spectral-clustering-of-generated-expression-profiles Use when you have GAN-generated single-cell expression profiles produced by mapping spatial transcriptomics data (x1) into the scRNA-seq domain, and you need to verify or derive spatially informed structure at single-cell resolution. skills.search_text: spike-and-slab-credibility-assessment Use when scRNA-seq cell-type counts are available per sample (especially with few replicates, e.g. 4 healthy / 3 moderate / 6 severe COVID-19 BALF donors) and you need differential abundance calls that control false discoveries under compositionality. Cell-type clustering/annotation is not yet statistically sound — scCODA requires pre-specified cell-type definitions and inherits errors from poor clustering You need to detect donor-level heterogeneity or response variability within a condition — scCODA does not model response variability within a condition The relationship between covariates and cell abundance is strongly non-log-linear, which may mis-specify scCODA's log-linear model http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Use scCODA's Bayesian Dirichlet-multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to call credible cell-type compositional shifts, interpreting all effects relative to a chosen reference cell type and controlling false discoveries via the FDR threshold on the Final Parameter column. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27150-6
skills.summary: Use scCODA's Bayesian Dirichlet-multinomial model with a Logit-normal spike-and-slab prior to call credible cell-type compositional shifts, interpreting all effects relative to a chosen reference cell type and controlling false discoveries via the FDR threshold on the Final Parameter column.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cell-type clustering/annotation is not yet statistically sound — scCODA requires pre-specified cell-type definitions and inherits errors from poor clustering You need to detect donor-level heterogeneity or response variability within a condition — scCODA does not model response variability within a condition The relationship between covariates and cell abundance is strongly non-log-linear, which may mis-specify scCODA's log-linear model

skills.description: Use when a fitted BUSseq model is available and the goal is to detect intrinsic genes that differentiate cell types at a controlled Bayesian false discovery rate (e.g., alpha = 0.05) from posterior indicator probabilities.
skills.name: spike-and-slab-posterior-indicator-estimation
skills.search_text: spike-and-slab-posterior-indicator-estimation Use when a fitted BUSseq model is available and the goal is to detect intrinsic genes that differentiate cell types at a controlled Bayesian false discovery rate (e.g., alpha = 0.05) from posterior indicator probabilities. Input is raw count matrices that have not yet been fitted by BUSseq_MCMC (no posterior indicator probabilities exist yet); first run the MCMC and BIC-based K selection. The goal is batch-effect correction, imputation, or clustering rather than differential-expression gene detection; use corrected_read_counts() or imputed_read_counts() instead. The experimental design is completely confounded (each batch measures disjoint cell types), where the article states no method is applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstructs BUSseq's Bayesian-FDR procedure for identifying intrinsic (differentially expressed) genes, using posterior estimates of spike-and-slab indicator probabilities on cell-type effects and ranking genes by cumulative indicator mass under an FDR cutoff of 0.05. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-16905-2
skills.summary: Reconstructs BUSseq's Bayesian-FDR procedure for identifying intrinsic (differentially expressed) genes, using posterior estimates of spike-and-slab indicator probabilities on cell-type effects and ranking genes by cumulative indicator mass under an FDR cutoff of 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw count matrices that have not yet been fitted by BUSseq_MCMC (no posterior indicator probabilities exist yet); first run the MCMC and BIC-based K selection. The goal is batch-effect correction, imputation, or clustering rather than differential-expression gene detection; use corrected_read_counts() or imputed_read_counts() instead. The experimental design is completely confounded (each batch measures disjoint cell types), where the article states no method is applicable.

skills.description: Use when a synthetic RNA-seq dataset with known ground truth (e.g. External RNA Controls Consortium spike-in transcripts) is available and you need to quantify which DEG method or combination maximizes F-measure and logFC accuracy.
skills.name: spike-in-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: spike-in-benchmark-evaluation Use when a synthetic RNA-seq dataset with known ground truth (e.g. External RNA Controls Consortium spike-in transcripts) is available and you need to quantify which DEG method or combination maximizes F-measure and logFC accuracy. The input is a real biological dataset with no ground truth (e.g. the Lafora or PMM2-CDG disease experiments) — no spike-in labels exist, so F-measure cannot be computed You only need a single DEG method's calls and do not intend to compare methods or combination strategies against a benchmark The expression data is not RNA-seq count data from DEgenes Hunter (e.g. already-normalized feature tables from proteomics or microarrays) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks individual DEG detection methods (DESeq2, limma, NOISeq) and their combination strategies (vote-threshold, combined-FDR, Naïve Bayes classifier) against known spike-in transcript ground truth, computing F-measure and logFC correlation per method as in the ExpHunter Suite evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Benchmarks individual DEG detection methods (DESeq2, limma, NOISeq) and their combination strategies (vote-threshold, combined-FDR, Naïve Bayes classifier) against known spike-in transcript ground truth, computing F-measure and logFC correlation per method as in the ExpHunter Suite evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a real biological dataset with no ground truth (e.g. the Lafora or PMM2-CDG disease experiments) — no spike-in labels exist, so F-measure cannot be computed You only need a single DEG method's calls and do not intend to compare methods or combination strategies against a benchmark The expression data is not RNA-seq count data from DEgenes Hunter (e.g. already-normalized feature tables from proteomics or microarrays)

skills.description: Use when evaluating a single-cell fusion detection pipeline against a spike-in ground truth, to quantify sensitivity (e.g., 27/27 spike-ins recovered) and false discovery via bulk chimeric-read support fractions.
skills.name: spike-in-benchmark-fusion-recovery-analysis
skills.search_text: spike-in-benchmark-fusion-recovery-analysis Use when evaluating a single-cell fusion detection pipeline against a spike-in ground truth, to quantify sensitivity (e.g., 27/27 spike-ins recovered) and false discovery via bulk chimeric-read support fractions. Data are bulk RNA-seq or 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ files There is no ground-truth fusion set (e.g., no spike-ins or known fusions) to evaluate recovery against FASTQ names use *_1.fq extension, which the scFusion pipeline explicitly does not allow http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Benchmark a single-cell fusion caller by verifying recovery of known PCAWG spike-in fusions across 729 Smart-Seq single cells and comparing the caller's fusion counts and bulk-support fractions against four bulk RNA-seq fusion methods (as in Fig 5 of the scFusion paper). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-28661-6
skills.summary: Benchmark a single-cell fusion caller by verifying recovery of known PCAWG spike-in fusions across 729 Smart-Seq single cells and comparing the caller's fusion counts and bulk-support fractions against four bulk RNA-seq fusion methods (as in Fig 5 of the scFusion paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk RNA-seq or 10X droplet scRNA-seq rather than Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ files There is no ground-truth fusion set (e.g., no spike-ins or known fusions) to evaluate recovery against FASTQ names use *_1.fq extension, which the scFusion pipeline explicitly does not allow

skills.description: Use when a trained multi-method DEG integration model (e.g. Naïve Bayes over per-gene p-value vectors) must be benchmarked on independent data with ground-truth DEG/non-DEG labels, such as spike-in experiments.
skills.name: spike-in-classifier-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: spike-in-classifier-performance-evaluation Use when a trained multi-method DEG integration model (e.g. Naïve Bayes over per-gene p-value vectors) must be benchmarked on independent data with ground-truth DEG/non-DEG labels, such as spike-in experiments. The dataset has no ground-truth DEG/non-DEG labels (e.g. the Lafora disease or PMM2-CDG real datasets) — performance cannot be scored without known truth. The classifier was not trained on simulations matched to your dataset's characteristics — the paper trained the Naïve Bayes model specifically on simulations based on the Lafora disease dataset, so its votes may not transfer to other organisms, tissues, or experimental designs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluates a machine-learning DEG-combination classifier (the ExpHunter Suite Naïve Bayes model trained on simulated p-value vectors) by applying it to a spike-in RNA-seq dataset with known truth labels and computing its F-measure against single methods and vote-threshold combinations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-94343-w
skills.summary: Evaluates a machine-learning DEG-combination classifier (the ExpHunter Suite Naïve Bayes model trained on simulated p-value vectors) by applying it to a spike-in RNA-seq dataset with known truth labels and computing its F-measure against single methods and vote-threshold combinations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no ground-truth DEG/non-DEG labels (e.g. the Lafora disease or PMM2-CDG real datasets) — performance cannot be scored without known truth. The classifier was not trained on simulations matched to your dataset's characteristics — the paper trained the Naïve Bayes model specifically on simulations based on the Lafora disease dataset, so its votes may not transfer to other organisms, tissues, or experimental designs.

skills.description: Use when an scRNAseq dataset contains ERCC spike-in measurements that must be filtered and designated as the control-gene set before applying control-based confounding-removal methods like scPLS, RUV, or scLVM.
skills.name: spike-in-control-gene-selection
skills.search_text: spike-in-control-gene-selection Use when an scRNAseq dataset contains ERCC spike-in measurements that must be filtered and designated as the control-gene set before applying control-based confounding-removal methods like scPLS, RUV, or scLVM. The dataset contains no external spike-in transcripts, so all-gene-based methods (PCA, LMM) must be used instead of control-based ones Spike-ins are too sparsely or inconsistently detected across the homogeneous cell subset to form a reliable control set after filtering The goal is to infer biological factors u_i rather than remove technical confounding — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the factors themselves http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects external RNA spike-in transcripts (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) as the control gene set used by confounding-removal methods such as scPLS, RUV, and scLVM. This skill mirrors the mESC analysis in Chen & Zhou (2017), where 32 filtered ERCC spike-ins served as controls for inferring technical confounding factors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-13665-w
skills.summary: Selects external RNA spike-in transcripts (e.g. ERCC spike-ins) as the control gene set used by confounding-removal methods such as scPLS, RUV, and scLVM. This skill mirrors the mESC analysis in Chen & Zhou (2017), where 32 filtered ERCC spike-ins served as controls for inferring technical confounding factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains no external spike-in transcripts, so all-gene-based methods (PCA, LMM) must be used instead of control-based ones Spike-ins are too sparsely or inconsistently detected across the homogeneous cell subset to form a reliable control set after filtering The goal is to infer biological factors u_i rather than remove technical confounding — scPLS can only infer biological effects, not the factors themselves

skills.description: Use when validating droplet-based scRNA-seq sensitivity with ERCC synthetic spike-ins: FASTQ reads from spike-in-only GEMs must be aligned to the ERCC reference (not a genome) to count UMIs per ERCC transcript.
skills.name: spike-in-read-alignment-to-ercc-reference
skills.search_text: spike-in-read-alignment-to-ercc-reference Use when validating droplet-based scRNA-seq sensitivity with ERCC synthetic spike-ins: FASTQ reads from spike-in-only GEMs must be aligned to the ERCC reference (not a genome) to count UMIs per ERCC transcript. Input FASTQs are from cellular samples and must be quantified against hg19/mm10 gene references with the full Cell Ranger pipeline — ERCC-only alignment would discard the transcriptome signal. The goal is absolute ERCC molecule quantification or spike-in normalization of expression levels, not assessment of the droplet platform's conversion efficiency and UMI-to-molecule correlation. Read2/Read1 structure differs from the 3' counting chemistry described here (e.g. earlier libraries with 5 nt UMI and 5 bp Read2) without adjusting barcode/UMI extraction accordingly. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Aligns scRNA-seq Read1 (cDNA insert) reads from ERCC spike-in GEM runs to the ERCC synthetic RNA reference so that UMI counts per ERCC transcript can be recovered and conversion efficiency quantified. This is how the Zheng et al. droplet 3' counting system's sensitivity (6.7–8.1% conversion, r=0.96) was validated. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms14049
skills.summary: Aligns scRNA-seq Read1 (cDNA insert) reads from ERCC spike-in GEM runs to the ERCC synthetic RNA reference so that UMI counts per ERCC transcript can be recovered and conversion efficiency quantified. This is how the Zheng et al. droplet 3' counting system's sensitivity (6.7–8.1% conversion, r=0.96) was validated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input FASTQs are from cellular samples and must be quantified against hg19/mm10 gene references with the full Cell Ranger pipeline — ERCC-only alignment would discard the transcriptome signal. The goal is absolute ERCC molecule quantification or spike-in normalization of expression levels, not assessment of the droplet platform's conversion efficiency and UMI-to-molecule correlation. Read2/Read1 structure differs from the 3' counting chemistry described here (e.g. earlier libraries with 5 nt UMI and 5 bp Read2) without adjusting barcode/UMI extraction accordingly.

skills.description: Use when simulated scRNA-seq data with known differentially expressed (feature) genes and a rare/common two-cell-type structure is needed to benchmark feature gene detection or dimensionality reduction methods.
skills.name: splat-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: splat-parameter-configuration Use when simulated scRNA-seq data with known differentially expressed (feature) genes and a rare/common two-cell-type structure is needed to benchmark feature gene detection or dimensionality reduction methods. The analysis target is real scRNA-seq data where no ground-truth DE gene labels exist — Splatter simulation provides synthetic truth, not empirical validation More than two cell types or continuous trajectories are needed — the 'groups' method configured here yields exactly two groups (rare and common) A fixed dataset size different from the small-scale regime (hundreds of genes, hundreds to 1000 cells) is required and parameter re-tuning is out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Configure Splatter's newSplatParams/splatSimulate(method='groups') to generate two-group scRNA-seq count matrices with a rare and a common cell type, used as ground-truth input for benchmarking EDGE feature gene detection. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Configure Splatter's newSplatParams/splatSimulate(method='groups') to generate two-group scRNA-seq count matrices with a rare and a common cell type, used as ground-truth input for benchmarking EDGE feature gene detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is real scRNA-seq data where no ground-truth DE gene labels exist — Splatter simulation provides synthetic truth, not empirical validation More than two cell types or continuous trajectories are needed — the 'groups' method configured here yields exactly two groups (rare and common) A fixed dataset size different from the small-scale regime (hundreds of genes, hundreds to 1000 cells) is required and parameter re-tuning is out of scope

skills.description: Use when you need controlled, simulated two-batch scRNA-seq count matrices to benchmark batch-effect correction tools, and you must reproduce a specific effect design (large batch shift, elevated dropout, unequal batch sizes, small batch effects, or multi-cell-type structure).
skills.name: splatter-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: splatter-parameter-configuration Use when you need controlled, simulated two-batch scRNA-seq count matrices to benchmark batch-effect correction tools, and you must reproduce a specific effect design (large batch shift, elevated dropout, unequal batch sizes, small batch effects, or multi-cell-type structure). The goal is real-data integration, not controlled simulation — Splatter output cannot substitute for real pancreatic (Muraro CEL-Seq2 / Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2) or 10X PBMC datasets used in the paper's real-data experiments You need to simulate more than two batches per dataset, since the benchmark design and BATMAN's implementation are restricted to two-dataset (pairwise) integration A simulator with a different generative model (e.g. zero-inflated or Gaussian) is required; Splatter here specifically uses the gamma-Poisson model http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Configures the Splatter simulator to generate paired-batch scRNA-seq count data under a gamma-Poisson model for benchmarking batch-integration methods, replicating the BATMAN paper's five scenarios (LB, LB-DR, LB-UB, SB, LB-CT) with 1,000 genes per dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.101185
skills.summary: Configures the Splatter simulator to generate paired-batch scRNA-seq count data under a gamma-Poisson model for benchmarking batch-integration methods, replicating the BATMAN paper's five scenarios (LB, LB-DR, LB-UB, SB, LB-CT) with 1,000 genes per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-data integration, not controlled simulation — Splatter output cannot substitute for real pancreatic (Muraro CEL-Seq2 / Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2) or 10X PBMC datasets used in the paper's real-data experiments You need to simulate more than two batches per dataset, since the benchmark design and BATMAN's implementation are restricted to two-dataset (pairwise) integration A simulator with a different generative model (e.g. zero-inflated or Gaussian) is required; Splatter here specifically uses the gamma-Poisson model

skills.description: Use when regenerating the simulated scRNA-seq scenarios needed to benchmark scGAE, or when controlled-dropout synthetic single-cell count matrices of exactly 2000 cells x 5000 genes are required.
skills.name: splatter-parameterized-simulation
skills.search_text: splatter-parameterized-simulation Use when regenerating the simulated scRNA-seq scenarios needed to benchmark scGAE, or when controlled-dropout synthetic single-cell count matrices of exactly 2000 cells x 5000 genes are required. The goal is to run scGAE on empirical data (e.g. HSPCs HRA000084 or pancreatic cells GSE84133) rather than to regenerate the simulated benchmark scenarios A different cell/gene dimensionality than 2000 x 5000 is required, since the validated benchmark outputs are fixed at exactly 2000 cells x 5000 genes http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduce the five simulated scRNA-seq benchmark datasets (data1-data5) used to evaluate scGAE by generating 2000-cell x 5000-gene count matrices with the Splatter R package (data1, data3, data4) and PROSSTT Python (data2, data5), plus four zero-inflated scenario4 variants with controlled dropout rates. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: Reproduce the five simulated scRNA-seq benchmark datasets (data1-data5) used to evaluate scGAE by generating 2000-cell x 5000-gene count matrices with the Splatter R package (data1, data3, data4) and PROSSTT Python (data2, data5), plus four zero-inflated scenario4 variants with controlled dropout rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to run scGAE on empirical data (e.g. HSPCs HRA000084 or pancreatic cells GSE84133) rather than to regenerate the simulated benchmark scenarios A different cell/gene dimensionality than 2000 x 5000 is required, since the validated benchmark outputs are fixed at exactly 2000 cells x 5000 genes

skills.description: Use when a benchmark requires simulated scRNA-Seq counts with known ground truth (true counts before noise, DE gene labels, group assignments) so imputation quality can be scored against a reference.
skills.name: splatter-scrna-count-simulation
skills.search_text: splatter-scrna-count-simulation Use when a benchmark requires simulated scRNA-Seq counts with known ground truth (true counts before noise, DE gene labels, group assignments) so imputation quality can be scored against a reference. The analysis goal requires real biological scRNA-Seq data (e.g., the Baron dataset) where a simulator's generative assumptions would not reflect the actual tissue or protocol You already have paired true/observed count data from a controlled mixture experiment (e.g., the sc_mixology cell-line mixtures) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates single-cell RNA-Seq count matrices with known ground truth using Splatter — as in the AutoClass paper, which generated simulated datasets (e.g., 1000 genes × 500 cells) with true pre-noise counts, group structure, and differentially expressed gene labels — to benchmark denoising/imputation methods like AutoClass against SAVER, scImpute, and DCA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-29576-y
skills.summary: Simulates single-cell RNA-Seq count matrices with known ground truth using Splatter — as in the AutoClass paper, which generated simulated datasets (e.g., 1000 genes × 500 cells) with true pre-noise counts, group structure, and differentially expressed gene labels — to benchmark denoising/imputation methods like AutoClass against SAVER, scImpute, and DCA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal requires real biological scRNA-Seq data (e.g., the Baron dataset) where a simulator's generative assumptions would not reflect the actual tissue or protocol You already have paired true/observed count data from a controlled mixture experiment (e.g., the sc_mixology cell-line mixtures)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq data generation method (e.g. scGAN) against Splatter on the same real training cells, evaluating with MMD and random-forest discrimination AUC (RF-AUC).
skills.name: splatter-scrna-seq-simulation
skills.search_text: splatter-scrna-seq-simulation Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq data generation method (e.g. scGAN) against Splatter on the same real training cells, evaluating with MMD and random-forest discrimination AUC (RF-AUC). The goal is conditional, type-aware generation of specific subpopulations — use cscGAN rather than Splatter, which is unconditioned in this comparison Input data is not scRNA-seq count data in .h5/.h5ad form and has not been pre-processed/split alongside the scGAN training set, so a matched comparison is impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Simulates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with Splatter from the same training cells (e.g. Fresh 68k PBMCs Donor A) used to train scGAN, providing a state-of-the-art non-deep-learning baseline for judging the distributional fidelity (MMD) and realism (RF-AUC) of GAN-generated cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-14018-z
skills.summary: Simulates synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with Splatter from the same training cells (e.g. Fresh 68k PBMCs Donor A) used to train scGAN, providing a state-of-the-art non-deep-learning baseline for judging the distributional fidelity (MMD) and realism (RF-AUC) of GAN-generated cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is conditional, type-aware generation of specific subpopulations — use cscGAN rather than Splatter, which is unconditioned in this comparison Input data is not scRNA-seq count data in .h5/.h5ad form and has not been pre-processed/split alongside the scGAN training set, so a matched comparison is impossible

skills.description: Use when you need simulated single-cell RNA-seq data with continuous differentiation structure and known pseudotime to benchmark clustering, pseudotime, or label-uncertainty methods against a ground truth.
skills.name: splatter-scrnaseq-pathway-simulation
skills.search_text: splatter-scrnaseq-pathway-simulation Use when you need simulated single-cell RNA-seq data with continuous differentiation structure and known pseudotime to benchmark clustering, pseudotime, or label-uncertainty methods against a ground truth. Data contain only a single cluster — Monte Carlo internal validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty when every data point can only receive one label The goal is clustering quality benchmarking (purity/ARI/silhouette) rather than trajectory/transition analysis — use the paper's benchmark workflow instead You need expression values along pre-defined biological pathways rather than a continuous differentiation path — Splatter path simulations model pseudotime progression, not pathway activity http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate simulated scRNA-seq differentiation-path datasets with the R package Splatter so each cell carries a known pseudotime coordinate, enabling validation of trajectory-aware methods (e.g., Forest Fire Clustering label entropy) against ground-truth developmental progression. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-31107-8
skills.summary: Generate simulated scRNA-seq differentiation-path datasets with the R package Splatter so each cell carries a known pseudotime coordinate, enabling validation of trajectory-aware methods (e.g., Forest Fire Clustering label entropy) against ground-truth developmental progression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data contain only a single cluster — Monte Carlo internal validation cannot accurately estimate uncertainty when every data point can only receive one label The goal is clustering quality benchmarking (purity/ARI/silhouette) rather than trajectory/transition analysis — use the paper's benchmark workflow instead You need expression values along pre-defined biological pathways rather than a continuous differentiation path — Splatter path simulations model pseudotime progression, not pathway activity

skills.search_text: splatter-simulated-data-handling Use when a simulated single-cell RNA-seq benchmark is needed to evaluate EDGE or other embedding methods (t-SNE, UMAP), or when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix must be log-normalized before calling endr(). Input is already a log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix (e.g. dat_log.rds) — re-normalizing and re-transforming would distort the values The task requires real experimental scRNA-seq data rather than simulated benchmarks with known rare/common group proportions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Generate a Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq count matrix and preprocess it (median-based library-size normalization followed by log2(x+1) transformation) so it is in the cell-by-gene log matrix format required by EDGE's endr pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: Generate a Splatter-simulated scRNA-seq count matrix and preprocess it (median-based library-size normalization followed by log2(x+1) transformation) so it is in the cell-by-gene log matrix format required by EDGE's endr pipeline.

skills.description: Use when a clustering benchmark requires a large simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth labels — e.g. stress-testing a method's scalability to ~1,000,000 cells when real annotated data of that size is unavailable.
skills.name: splatter-simulation-of-scrna-seq
skills.search_text: splatter-simulation-of-scrna-seq Use when a clustering benchmark requires a large simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth labels — e.g. stress-testing a method's scalability to ~1,000,000 cells when real annotated data of that size is unavailable. The benchmark target is real experimental data with expert-assigned ground truth (e.g. Levine_32dim mass cytometry from FlowRepository FR-FCM-ZZPH) rather than simulated transcriptomes. The simulation targets non-transcriptomic data types (e.g. mass cytometry marker panels), which Splatter's scRNA-seq count model does not represent. Small generic clustering toy benchmarks are needed — the paper used scikit-learn random sample generators (1,000 objects, seed=1) for those, not Splatter. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Generate large simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with Splatter, estimating simulation parameters from a real reference dataset (e.g. Zeisel15) and fixing a seed, to create million-scale benchmark data with known ground-truth cell labels for evaluating clustering scalability. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s42003-023-05480-z
skills.summary: Generate large simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with Splatter, estimating simulation parameters from a real reference dataset (e.g. Zeisel15) and fixing a seed, to create million-scale benchmark data with known ground-truth cell labels for evaluating clustering scalability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The benchmark target is real experimental data with expert-assigned ground truth (e.g. Levine_32dim mass cytometry from FlowRepository FR-FCM-ZZPH) rather than simulated transcriptomes. The simulation targets non-transcriptomic data types (e.g. mass cytometry marker panels), which Splatter's scRNA-seq count model does not represent. Small generic clustering toy benchmarks are needed — the paper used scikit-learn random sample generators (1,000 objects, seed=1) for those, not Splatter.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking feature selection or trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cluster labels, DE genes, and latent step pseudotime must be known and noise must be systematically varied via BCV.
skills.name: splatter-single-cell-rnaseq-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: splatter-single-cell-rnaseq-trajectory-simulation Use when benchmarking feature selection or trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cluster labels, DE genes, and latent step pseudotime must be known and noise must be systematically varied via BCV. Evaluating methods on real experimental scRNA-seq or imaging data, where no simulation ground truth (DE genes, latent step time) exists Benchmarking supervised feature selection that requires ground-truth annotations at training time if the simulation labels would leak into the selection step Studying branched or complex trajectories — this setup generates linear Splatter paths only http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with known ground truth (cell type labels, differentially expressed genes, latent step time) using the Splatter 'paths' model via the scprep SplatSimulate wrapper, to benchmark unsupervised feature selection methods for trajectory preservation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Generate simulated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with known ground truth (cell type labels, differentially expressed genes, latent step time) using the Splatter 'paths' model via the scprep SplatSimulate wrapper, to benchmark unsupervised feature selection methods for trajectory preservation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating methods on real experimental scRNA-seq or imaging data, where no simulation ground truth (DE genes, latent step time) exists Benchmarking supervised feature selection that requires ground-truth annotations at training time if the simulation labels would leak into the selection step Studying branched or complex trajectories — this setup generates linear Splatter paths only

skills.description: Use when you must quantify recall/precision of novel splice-junction detection against held-out AStalavista truth events, or compare align-and-count vs pseudoalignment runtime/memory on tens to hundreds of millions of RNA-seq reads.
skills.name: splice-aware-alignment-benchmarking
skills.search_text: splice-aware-alignment-benchmarking Use when you must quantify recall/precision of novel splice-junction detection against held-out AStalavista truth events, or compare align-and-count vs pseudoalignment runtime/memory on tens to hundreds of millions of RNA-seq reads. Goal is plain abundance quantification of annotated transcripts only — a vanilla kallisto run suffices without fortuna's novel-fragment guessing or benchmarking harness. Ground truth involves splice sites with no annotated basis (truly novel donor/acceptor pairs) — fortuna --quant alone guesses combinations of annotated splice sites, so a spliced aligner plus fortuna --refine is needed instead. Reads are already spliced-aligned to a genome BAM and you only want event annotation from existing alignments rather than a mapping-accuracy comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark protocol from the fortuna paper for measuring how accurately splice-aware mappers and pseudoaligners (fortuna, STAR 1/2-pass, Whippet) detect novel junctions between annotated splice sites, plus runtime and peak-memory scaling on up to ~291M real RNA-seq reads. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Benchmark protocol from the fortuna paper for measuring how accurately splice-aware mappers and pseudoaligners (fortuna, STAR 1/2-pass, Whippet) detect novel junctions between annotated splice sites, plus runtime and peak-memory scaling on up to ~291M real RNA-seq reads.

skills.description: Use when building or adapting a Snakemake neoantigen/variant pipeline that must align RNA-seq reads splice- and chimeric-aware (for fusions, exitrons, indels) and DNA-seq reads genome-wide, with defined STAR chimera parameters and per-branch BAM indexing.
skills.name: splice-aware-alignment-parameter-tuning
skills.search_text: splice-aware-alignment-parameter-tuning Use when building or adapting a Snakemake neoantigen/variant pipeline that must align RNA-seq reads splice- and chimeric-aware (for fusions, exitrons, indels) and DNA-seq reads genome-wide, with defined STAR chimera parameters and per-branch BAM indexing. Input is raw, unpreprocessed FASTQ with adapters/low-quality tails — run fastp pre-processing first. The downstream goal is HLA genotyping — ScanNeo2 instead filters reads with yara and aligns against HLA alleles with Optitype/HLA-HD, not the genome-alignment branch. Only short-read SNV/indel calling on DNA-seq is needed with no RNA-seq branch — a plain BWA-MEM alignment without the STAR chimeric configuration suffices. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Configure chimeric-aware STAR alignment for RNA-seq alongside BWA-MEM alignment for DNA-seq in the ScanNeo2 workflow, including a BWA realignment step for STAR-produced BAMs so downstream variant callers (transIndel, ScanExitron) see a BWA-style CIGAR. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad659
skills.summary: Configure chimeric-aware STAR alignment for RNA-seq alongside BWA-MEM alignment for DNA-seq in the ScanNeo2 workflow, including a BWA realignment step for STAR-produced BAMs so downstream variant callers (transIndel, ScanExitron) see a BWA-style CIGAR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unpreprocessed FASTQ with adapters/low-quality tails — run fastp pre-processing first. Only short-read SNV/indel calling on DNA-seq is needed with no RNA-seq branch — a plain BWA-MEM alignment without the STAR chimeric configuration suffices.

skills.search_text: splice-aware-multimapping-read-alignment Use when preprocessing scRNA-Seq reads (FASTQ) for transposable element expression analysis where TEs are repetitive and multi-mapping must be retained rather than filtered, e.g., building BAMs for SoloTE or benchmarking against ground truth. skills.summary: Align single-cell RNA-Seq reads with STAR configured to retain multi-mapping reads (up to 100 genomic loci), producing the BAM files from which SoloTE assigns locus-specific transposable element expression, with uniquely mapped reads reported at locus level and multi-mappers at family level.

skills.name: splice-aware-read-alignment
skills.search_text: splice-aware-read-alignment Use when preprocessing Nanopore single-cell or spatially barcoded long reads for isoform-level analysis and you need spliced alignments that respect known transcript junctions before UMI/barcode denoising and isoform counting. Input reads are short Illumina reads where splice-aware long-read alignment (minimap2 -ax splice) is not appropriate. The analysis goal is genome-level structural variant calling rather than transcript/isoform-level quantification. Reads are already denoised, UMI-collapsed, and aligned; re-aligning would duplicate work or break existing UMI-to-read linkages. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Align Nanopore long reads to GRCh38 with minimap2 in spliced alignment mode, using a Gencode v39 GTF-derived splice junction bed to guide junction detection and suppress ambiguous secondary alignments prior to isoform quantification. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60902-2
skills.summary: Align Nanopore long reads to GRCh38 with minimap2 in spliced alignment mode, using a Gencode v39 GTF-derived splice junction bed to guide junction detection and suppress ambiguous secondary alignments prior to isoform quantification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are short Illumina reads where splice-aware long-read alignment (minimap2 -ax splice) is not appropriate. The analysis goal is genome-level structural variant calling rather than transcript/isoform-level quantification. Reads are already denoised, UMI-collapsed, and aligned; re-aligning would duplicate work or break existing UMI-to-read linkages.

skills.description: Use when aligning rRNA-depleted ribosome-footprint reads (e.g. 25-35 nt RPFs) to a genome whose transcripts contain exon junctions, requiring splice-aware mapping followed by a less strict remapping of unaligned reads.
skills.name: splice-aware-ribosome-footprint-genome-alignment
skills.search_text: splice-aware-ribosome-footprint-genome-alignment Use when aligning rRNA-depleted ribosome-footprint reads (e.g. 25-35 nt RPFs) to a genome whose transcripts contain exon junctions, requiring splice-aware mapping followed by a less strict remapping of unaligned reads. Reads still contain contaminant rRNA/tRNA — run the Bowtie2 contaminant-depletion step first, as aligned contaminants would pollute the genome mapping Reads have not been adapter-trimmed and length-filtered to 25-35 nt with Cutadapt — unfiltered read-length distributions break the RPF assumptions of the BAM.25-35 output Aligning transcriptomes without exon junctions where splice-aware mapping is unnecessary and Bowtie2 alone suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 RiboDoc's double-mapping step: rRNA-depleted, 25-35 nt RPF FastQ reads are first aligned to the reference genome with HISAT2 in splice-aware mode to recover footprints spanning exon junctions, then reads left unaligned by HISAT2 are remapped against the same FASTA with Bowtie2 (v2.4.2) permitting at most 1 mismatch; merged, sorted and indexed SAM/BAM outputs are produced with samtools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: RiboDoc's double-mapping step: rRNA-depleted, 25-35 nt RPF FastQ reads are first aligned to the reference genome with HISAT2 in splice-aware mode to recover footprints spanning exon junctions, then reads left unaligned by HISAT2 are remapped against the same FASTA with Bowtie2 (v2.4.2) permitting at most 1 mismatch; merged, sorted and indexed SAM/BAM outputs are produced with samtools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads still contain contaminant rRNA/tRNA — run the Bowtie2 contaminant-depletion step first, as aligned contaminants would pollute the genome mapping Reads have not been adapter-trimmed and length-filtered to 25-35 nt with Cutadapt — unfiltered read-length distributions break the RPF assumptions of the BAM.25-35 output Aligning transcriptomes without exon junctions where splice-aware mapping is unnecessary and Bowtie2 alone suffices

skills.description: Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., SRA accessions like SRR307911) and you need genome-aligned BAMs that preserve splice junctions for transcriptome assembly, especially when integrating multiple aligner mappings.
skills.name: splice-aware-rna-seq-read-alignment
skills.search_text: splice-aware-rna-seq-read-alignment Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., SRA accessions like SRR307911) and you need genome-aligned BAMs that preserve splice junctions for transcriptome assembly, especially when integrating multiple aligner mappings. Input is already assembled transcript GTF output from an assembler — no re-alignment is needed; go straight to evaluation with Cuffcompare. The reads are long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT): the article notes the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets, and this skill targets short-read spliced alignment. Only quantification at the transcriptome level is required without genome-guided assembly — a pseudoaligner workflow would avoid genome alignment entirely. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Generate splice-aware RNA-seq alignments by mapping reads to a reference genome (e.g., GRCh38 or GRCm38) with two complementary splice-aware aligners, HISAT2 (with --dta) and STAR, producing coordinate-sorted BAM files that downstream assemblers such as Tiglon, StringTie2, and Scallop can consume. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Generate splice-aware RNA-seq alignments by mapping reads to a reference genome (e.g., GRCh38 or GRCm38) with two complementary splice-aware aligners, HISAT2 (with --dta) and STAR, producing coordinate-sorted BAM files that downstream assemblers such as Tiglon, StringTie2, and Scallop can consume.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already assembled transcript GTF output from an assembler — no re-alignment is needed; go straight to evaluation with Cuffcompare. The reads are long-read RNA-seq (PacBio or ONT): the article notes the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets, and this skill targets short-read spliced alignment. Only quantification at the transcriptome level is required without genome-guided assembly — a pseudoaligner workflow would avoid genome alignment entirely.

skills.search_text: splice-event-filter-evaluation Use when you have per-sample splice-junction read counts (e.g., STAR split-read *.csf.splicing.txt* outputs) plus known pathogenic mis-splicing events and need to benchmark read-count or singleton-based event filters. Your goal is MRSD score generation itself (required sequencing depth prediction) rather than evaluating splicing-event filters — use MRSDexplorer.py without the filter-evaluation framing Input is long-read, single-cell, or spatially resolved RNA-seq — the MRSD framework is validated only for bulk short-read poly-A enrichment RNA-seq with this specific pipeline You lack RNA-seq data on samples with known pathogenic mis-splicing events, so retention of pathogenic events cannot be measured http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reproduce the MRSD paper's evaluation of splice-junction read-count and singleton (NRC > 0.25) filters, quantifying how much artifactual singleton junction events are removed while retaining known pathogenic mis-splicing events detected in 21 patient RNA-seq samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2021.12.014

skills.description: Use when integrating BAM alignments from multiple splice-aware aligners (e.g., Hisat2 --dta and STAR) over a gene locus and you need an exon/junction graph whose edges carry aligner-capture labels and averaged read-support weights.
skills.name: splice-graph-construction-from-alignments
skills.search_text: splice-graph-construction-from-alignments Use when integrating BAM alignments from multiple splice-aware aligners (e.g., Hisat2 --dta and STAR) over a gene locus and you need an exon/junction graph whose edges carry aligner-capture labels and averaged read-support weights. Input is a single aligner's BAM and the goal is plain transcript assembly without multi-aligner integration — a single-aligner assembler workflow (e.g., StringTie2 or Scallop) is the wrong model here Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or ONT) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets You need annotation-guided assembly from known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Construct a labeled splice graph from RNA-seq alignments, in which each node is an exon and each edge is a splice junction, with junction edges labeled according to which aligners captured them (label 2 = captured by all aligners, label 1 = otherwise, with 2 refined into 2+ / 2- based on identical read support). This is the graph model Tiglon uses before its label-based dynamic path extension recovers transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Construct a labeled splice graph from RNA-seq alignments, in which each node is an exon and each edge is a splice junction, with junction edges labeled according to which aligners captured them (label 2 = captured by all aligners, label 1 = otherwise, with 2 refined into 2+ / 2- based on identical read support). This is the graph model Tiglon uses before its label-based dynamic path extension recovers transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single aligner's BAM and the goal is plain transcript assembly without multi-aligner integration — a single-aligner assembler workflow (e.g., StringTie2 or Scallop) is the wrong model here Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or ONT) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets You need annotation-guided assembly from known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies

skills.name: splice-graph-path-search-implementation
skills.search_text: splice-graph-path-search-implementation Use when you have a labeled splice graph built from integrated mappings of multiple aligners (labels 1, 2+, 2-) and need to extract transcript-representing paths, particularly to recover lowly expressed transcripts. Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets An annotation-guided assembly is required — Tiglon has no option to use known transcript annotations to guide assembly Only a single aligner's BAM is available from a non-supported mapper — Tiglon v.1.1 only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Reconstructs transcript-representing paths from Tiglon's labeled splice graph using a label-based dynamic path extension program, where junction edges labeled 1, 2+, or 2- guide seed selection and extension order. It converts multi-aligner splice-junction evidence (e.g., Hisat2 and Star BAM mappings) into assembled candidate transcripts in GTF format. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
