skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current Tiglon version is not compatible with long-read datasets An annotation-guided assembly is required — Tiglon has no option to use known transcript annotations to guide assembly Only a single aligner's BAM is available from a non-supported mapper — Tiglon v.1.1 only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star

skills.description: Use when RNase R-treated paired-end RNA-seq data have back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, or UROBORUS and you need full-length circRNA transcript sequences with FPKM/TPM isoform-level quantification.
skills.name: splice-graph-transcript-assembly
skills.search_text: splice-graph-transcript-assembly Use when RNase R-treated paired-end RNA-seq data have back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, or UROBORUS and you need full-length circRNA transcript sequences with FPKM/TPM isoform-level quantification. Samples are not RNase R-treated — CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, where residual linear mRNA would otherwise confound assembly Target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the pipeline assembles and quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts Input is raw unaligned FASTQ without prior TopHat2 alignment and BSJ detection by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS (or format-converted equivalents) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assemble full-length circular RNA isoform sequences and quantify their expression by constructing multiple splice graphs at each gene locus from back-spliced junction (BSJ) signatures, then allocating paired-end reads to isoforms with CircAST's EMPC/maximum-likelihood algorithm. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.03.004
skills.summary: Assemble full-length circular RNA isoform sequences and quantify their expression by constructing multiple splice graphs at each gene locus from back-spliced junction (BSJ) signatures, then allocating paired-end reads to isoforms with CircAST's EMPC/maximum-likelihood algorithm.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are not RNase R-treated — CircAST can be applied only to RNase R-treated samples, where residual linear mRNA would otherwise confound assembly Target circRNAs are intronic or intergenic — the pipeline assembles and quantifies only exon-annotated circular transcripts Input is raw unaligned FASTQ without prior TopHat2 alignment and BSJ detection by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS (or format-converted equivalents)

skills.description: Use when you need linear RNA expression estimates from ribo− RNA-seq that are directly comparable to circRNA expression at the same gene loci, e.g. to compute a CIRCscore from paired FPBcirc/FPBlinear values.
skills.name: splice-junction-linear-rna-normalization
skills.search_text: splice-junction-linear-rna-normalization Use when you need linear RNA expression estimates from ribo− RNA-seq that are directly comparable to circRNA expression at the same gene loci, e.g. to compute a CIRCscore from paired FPBcirc/FPBlinear values. Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted there, so SJ-based linear quantification and CIRCscore evaluation are inaccurate Input data is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, which depletes circRNAs and cannot support balanced circular-vs-linear comparison The goal is circRNA detection alone without a comparable linear expression background (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq by counting fragments mapped to canonical splicing junction (SJ) sites and normalizing them to FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases), so linear expression is on the same scale as circRNA BSJ-derived FPBcirc and the ratio CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear is meaningful. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.11.004
skills.summary: Quantifies linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq by counting fragments mapped to canonical splicing junction (SJ) sites and normalizing them to FPB (fragments per billion mapped bases), so linear expression is on the same scale as circRNA BSJ-derived FPBcirc and the ratio CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear is meaningful.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is poly(A)−/ribo− or RNase R-treated RNA-seq: polyadenylated linear RNAs are largely depleted there, so SJ-based linear quantification and CIRCscore evaluation are inaccurate Input data is poly(A)+ RNA-seq, which depletes circRNAs and cannot support balanced circular-vs-linear comparison The goal is circRNA detection alone without a comparable linear expression background (plain CIRCexplorer2 suffices)

skills.description: Use when starting from per-cell BAM files or STAR SJ.out.tab junction files from single-cell SMART-seq data and you need a cells-by-sites junction matrix plus a 5'/3' AS probability matrix before imputation or clustering.
skills.name: splice-junction-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: splice-junction-matrix-construction Use when starting from per-cell BAM files or STAR SJ.out.tab junction files from single-cell SMART-seq data and you need a cells-by-sites junction matrix plus a 5'/3' AS probability matrix before imputation or clustering. Input is droplet-based scRNA-seq where splicing coverage is extremely sparse — the article notes RNA splicing profiling is more costly under current practice and SMART-seq-style full-length data are the demonstrated use case Goal is differential splicing with known cell labels (tools like rMATS, BRIE18, or MARVEL are designed for that); SCASL junction matrix construction targets unsupervised de novo AS event discovery You already have the AS probability matrix (e.g. the TNBC-2 demo intermediates in data/junction) — skip directly to imputation/clustering steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Construct a LeafCutter-style splice junction reads matrix from single-cell SMART-seq BAM/junction files and convert it into an alternative splicing (AS) probability matrix, the foundational input for SCASL's imputation and spectral clustering stages. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46480-9
skills.summary: Construct a LeafCutter-style splice junction reads matrix from single-cell SMART-seq BAM/junction files and convert it into an alternative splicing (AS) probability matrix, the foundational input for SCASL's imputation and spectral clustering stages.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is droplet-based scRNA-seq where splicing coverage is extremely sparse — the article notes RNA splicing profiling is more costly under current practice and SMART-seq-style full-length data are the demonstrated use case Goal is differential splicing with known cell labels (tools like rMATS, BRIE18, or MARVEL are designed for that); SCASL junction matrix construction targets unsupervised de novo AS event discovery You already have the AS probability matrix (e.g. the TNBC-2 demo intermediates in data/junction) — skip directly to imputation/clustering steps

skills.description: Use when reconstructing fortuna's Step B fragment-set construction (F from F1:1 and Fmax) from a preprocessed GTF, or when verifying that a fragment set is correct (all fragments derivable from T) and complete (any length-l read is mappable).
skills.name: splice-site-combination-enumeration
skills.search_text: splice-site-combination-enumeration Use when reconstructing fortuna's Step B fragment-set construction (F from F1:1 and Fmax) from a preprocessed GTF, or when verifying that a fragment set is correct (all fragments derivable from T) and complete (any length-l read is mappable). The read sequences contain splice junctions absent from any annotation and you need de novo splice-site discovery — this skill only combines annotated splice sites; novel sites require fortuna's optional step of incorporating sites found by a spliced aligner on reads unmapped in step (D) You need full transcript-level quantification rather than counts of elementary splicing units (signature counts) from pseudoaligned fragments The annotation has not been segmented (no NodeId subexon space); running --index on a raw GTF would not produce valid signature names http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Enumerates feasible transcript signatures for fortuna by combining annotated donor and acceptor splice sites per gene, then builds the trimmed, merged transcript fragment set F from the annotated-fragment set F1:1 and the maximally permissive set Fmax so that every length-l read from a transcript in T can be pseudoaligned by kallisto. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Enumerates feasible transcript signatures for fortuna by combining annotated donor and acceptor splice sites per gene, then builds the trimmed, merged transcript fragment set F from the annotated-fragment set F1:1 and the maximally permissive set Fmax so that every length-l read from a transcript in T can be pseudoaligned by kallisto.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The read sequences contain splice junctions absent from any annotation and you need de novo splice-site discovery — this skill only combines annotated splice sites; novel sites require fortuna's optional step of incorporating sites found by a spliced aligner on reads unmapped in step (D) You need full transcript-level quantification rather than counts of elementary splicing units (signature counts) from pseudoaligned fragments The annotation has not been segmented (no NodeId subexon space); running --index on a raw GTF would not produce valid signature names

skills.description: Use when you have SCISSOR shape-change results plus a public mutation-call repository and need to check whether annotated splice-site mutations are supported by significant coverage-shape changes.
skills.name: splice-site-mutation-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: splice-site-mutation-annotation-matching Use when you have SCISSOR shape-change results plus a public mutation-call repository and need to check whether annotated splice-site mutations are supported by significant coverage-shape changes. Mutation calls are point mutations within coding regions rather than splice-site annotations, since the matching logic targets splice-site entries specifically The RNA-seq cohort is too small for SCISSOR to fit a reliable gene-shape model (empirically ~30 samples is the smallest considered successfully) Samples show severe RNA degradation across many genes, as these were empirically removed before shape-change detection http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 Cross-reference publicly reported splice-site mutation calls (e.g., TCGA HNSC TP53) against SCISSOR-detected global and local shape changes to quantify what fraction of annotated splice-site mutations have statistically significant RNA-structure support. This exposes discordant annotations that may be miscalled or lack read-level splicing evidence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Cross-reference publicly reported splice-site mutation calls (e.g., TCGA HNSC TP53) against SCISSOR-detected global and local shape changes to quantify what fraction of annotated splice-site mutations have statistically significant RNA-structure support. This exposes discordant annotations that may be miscalled or lack read-level splicing evidence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mutation calls are point mutations within coding regions rather than splice-site annotations, since the matching logic targets splice-site entries specifically The RNA-seq cohort is too small for SCISSOR to fit a reliable gene-shape model (empirically ~30 samples is the smallest considered successfully) Samples show severe RNA degradation across many genes, as these were empirically removed before shape-change detection

skills.description: Use when SCISSOR (or similar) has called sample-level RNA coverage shape changes and you need to determine which aberrations coincide with annotated mutations (e.g., splice sites, exon skipping, intron retention, in-frame indels) and which are novel.
skills.name: splice-site-mutation-interpretation
skills.search_text: splice-site-mutation-interpretation Use when SCISSOR (or similar) has called sample-level RNA coverage shape changes and you need to determine which aberrations coincide with annotated mutations (e.g., splice sites, exon skipping, intron retention, in-frame indels) and which are novel. You need complete mutation-to-phenotype concordance: only 59% of annotated splice-site mutations in the public HNSC repository showed a statistically significant shape change, so this skill cannot confirm every annotated mutation. The gene's RNA-seq coverage data has not been preprocessed by SCISSOR (pileup via build_pileup, ranges via get_Ranges, Scissor run); without shape-change calls there is nothing to cross-reference. The cohort is much smaller than ~30 samples, the smallest cohort the SCISSOR authors report analyzing successfully. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Cross-references RNA-seq shape changes detected by SCISSOR (global and local shape changes) against publicly reported mutation calls (MAF) to classify each aberration as a known mutation, most commonly splice-site, versus previously unrecognized. Validated on 50 TP53 shape changes (26 GSCs, 24 LSCs) in 452 TCGA HNSC samples, where 82% coincided with known mutations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3

skills.description: Use when testing whether cis genetic variants overlapping splice junction motifs alter donor/acceptor site strength, and whether the strength change scales with sQTL effect size (md).

The analysis goal is RNA-binding protein binding site disruption rather than splice site strength — the article notes many more variants modify RBP binding sites than splice site sequences Variants do not overlap annotated donor or acceptor splice site intervals after intersection, so no PWM scores can be computed for them Splicing phenotypes were quantified without sQTLseekeR2 output (e.g. annotation-free LeafCutter intron excision ratios), since the skill depends on all-tests.nominal.tsv and sqtls-${level}fdr.nominal.tsv files http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Score sQTL and non-sQTL variants overlapping annotated donor/acceptor splice sites with position weight matrices to quantify allele-specific splice site strength, testing whether sQTLs alter splice site strength more frequently (63% vs 49%, OR = 1.79) and more strongly than non-sQTL variants. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2

skills.search_text: spliced-read-alignment-with-uniquely-mapped-filtering Use when raw paired-end spatially barcoded ST reads (e.g., MOB ST, SRA: SRR3382373) must be mapped to a reference genome before poly(A) site discovery, and downstream tools require unambiguous mapping. Input is already an aligned BAM or a gene/poly(A)-site count matrix — alignment and uniquely-mapped filtering are already done The analysis requires multi-mapper retention (e.g., repetitive or paralogous regions where multimapping evidence matters), since this pipeline discards non-unique alignments Data are image-based spatial assays (MERFISH/seqFISH) — the article notes APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data with tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Aligns spatially barcoded ST sequencing reads (read 2) to the mouse GRCm38 genome with STAR and retains only uniquely mapped reads, producing the BAM input required by downstream poly(A) site identification with scAPAtrap in the stAPAminer MOB workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2023.01.003

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell-calling methods on single-nucleus RNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrices and you need a contamination-sensitive quality metric (spliced-read fraction) to compare retained barcodes across methods.
skills.name: spliced-read-fraction-statistical-comparison
skills.search_text: spliced-read-fraction-statistical-comparison Use when benchmarking cell-calling methods on single-nucleus RNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrices and you need a contamination-sensitive quality metric (spliced-read fraction) to compare retained barcodes across methods. The input is already a filtered feature-by-cell matrix or an h5ad with cell barcodes pre-called — cell calling must be run on the raw unfiltered matrix for the comparison to be valid The data are standard scRNA-seq (whole cells) rather than snRNA-seq — the spliced-read fraction is a cytoplasmic-contamination signal specific to nuclei; whole-cell data do not support this interpretation Only one cell-calling method is being used — the metric is a comparative benchmark across methods, not a standalone QC pass/fail filter http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies cytoplasmic contamination in snRNA-seq cell-calling by computing the fraction of spliced reads among retained nucleus-containing droplets per method (EmptyNN, Cell Ranger v.2, EmptyDrops, Cell Ranger v.3, CellBender) and statistically testing the differences; in the EmptyNN paper's adult mouse brain dataset, EmptyNN- versus Cell Ranger v.3-filtered nuclei showed a significantly lower spliced-read fraction (p = 3.29e-5). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2021.100311
skills.summary: Quantifies cytoplasmic contamination in snRNA-seq cell-calling by computing the fraction of spliced reads among retained nucleus-containing droplets per method (EmptyNN, Cell Ranger v.2, EmptyDrops, Cell Ranger v.3, CellBender) and statistically testing the differences; in the EmptyNN paper's adult mouse brain dataset, EmptyNN- versus Cell Ranger v.3-filtered nuclei showed a significantly lower spliced-read fraction (p = 3.29e-5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a filtered feature-by-cell matrix or an h5ad with cell barcodes pre-called — cell calling must be run on the raw unfiltered matrix for the comparison to be valid The data are standard scRNA-seq (whole cells) rather than snRNA-seq — the spliced-read fraction is a cytoplasmic-contamination signal specific to nuclei; whole-cell data do not support this interpretation Only one cell-calling method is being used — the metric is a comparative benchmark across methods, not a standalone QC pass/fail filter

skills.description: Use when a pseudoalignment-based quantification (fortuna --quant) left reads unmapped and a spliced aligner such as STAR has detected novel acceptor (AA) or donor (AD) splice sites in those reads that must be counted and annotated.
skills.name: spliced-read-realignment
skills.search_text: spliced-read-realignment Use when a pseudoalignment-based quantification (fortuna --quant) left reads unmapped and a spliced aligner such as STAR has detected novel acceptor (AA) or donor (AD) splice sites in those reads that must be counted and annotated. No spliced-aligner output on unmapped reads is available — the refine step requires a BAM of unmapped reads realigned by a tool such as STAR; without it, plain fortuna --quant already covers counting and novel-event annotation The goal is de novo transcript assembly or full-length alignment of all reads rather than incorporating a small set of novel splice sites into fortuna's signature counts The annotation has not been preprocessed with bin/processGTF.sh — unsegmented GTFs lack the NodeId subexons that cnt.tsv/alt.tsv and the refine step depend on http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Use fortuna's --refine mode to incorporate novel splice sites that a spliced aligner (e.g. STAR) detected in reads left unmapped by pseudoalignment, refining subexons/introns and re-deriving signature counts and novel-event annotations from the realigned BAM. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Use fortuna's --refine mode to incorporate novel splice sites that a spliced aligner (e.g. STAR) detected in reads left unmapped by pseudoalignment, refining subexons/introns and re-deriving signature counts and novel-event annotations from the realigned BAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No spliced-aligner output on unmapped reads is available — the refine step requires a BAM of unmapped reads realigned by a tool such as STAR; without it, plain fortuna --quant already covers counting and novel-event annotation The goal is de novo transcript assembly or full-length alignment of all reads rather than incorporating a small set of novel splice sites into fortuna's signature counts The annotation has not been preprocessed with bin/processGTF.sh — unsegmented GTFs lack the NodeId subexons that cnt.tsv/alt.tsv and the refine step depend on

skills.search_text: spliced-unspliced-umi-quantification-per-droplet Use when processing raw 10X snRNA-seq droplet data (e.g. CellRanger outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix) to quantify per-droplet contamination via percent-spliced reads and estimate the sample-specific nuclear/background midpoint. Input is single-cell (not single-nucleus) data such as PBMC scRNA-seq, where the correlation between debris scoring and percent reads spliced was less successful due to smaller differences between background and cell type profiles You need contamination scores comparable across independently processed samples — the paper explicitly warns the debris score may not be on the same scale across experiments, so midpoints must be estimated per sample rather than transferred Input is already filtered to cell barcodes; background droplets must be present (raw_feature_bc_matrix) for the bimodal distribution and midpoint to be estimable http://edamontology.org/topic_3523 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies extranuclear RNA contamination per 10X droplet in snRNA-seq by computing the percent of reads spliced (from spliced vs. unspliced UMI counts, excluding mitochondrial genes), then estimates a sample-specific midpoint separating the bimodal nuclear/background droplet distributions. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67513-5

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell (not single-nucleus) data such as PBMC scRNA-seq, where the correlation between debris scoring and percent reads spliced was less successful due to smaller differences between background and cell type profiles You need contamination scores comparable across independently processed samples — the paper explicitly warns the debris score may not be on the same scale across experiments, so midpoints must be estimated per sample rather than transferred Input is already filtered to cell barcodes; background droplets must be present (raw_feature_bc_matrix) for the bimodal distribution and midpoint to be estimable

skills.search_text: spliceu-augmented-transcriptome-alignment Use when scRNA-seq reads must be aligned to an augmented spliced+unspliced transcriptome so per-read splicing status can be predicted or evaluated, or when uniquely genome-mapped and fully exonic (ambiguous) read sets are needed. Standard gene-level UMI quantification on the native transcriptome (e.g., plain Cell Ranger-style counting) where the doubled spliced+unspliced reference adds cost without benefit When no matching genome FASTA and GTF are available to augment into a spliceu reference When the goal is only measuring gene/intron UMI counts via STAR --soloFeatures GeneFull without per-read splicing-status prediction http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Builds and aligns against a 'spliceu' augmented reference — where each transcript gets a spliced and an unspliced version — so scRNA-seq reads can be mapped in a way that supports per-read splicing-status prediction (e.g., by Forseti) and downstream AUC evaluation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Builds and aligns against a 'spliceu' augmented reference — where each transcript gets a spliced and an unspliced version — so scRNA-seq reads can be mapped in a way that supports per-read splicing-status prediction (e.g., by Forseti) and downstream AUC evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Standard gene-level UMI quantification on the native transcriptome (e.g., plain Cell Ranger-style counting) where the doubled spliced+unspliced reference adds cost without benefit When no matching genome FASTA and GTF are available to augment into a spliceu reference When the goal is only measuring gene/intron UMI counts via STAR --soloFeatures GeneFull without per-read splicing-status prediction

skills.description: Use when preparing a scRNA-seq splicing-status analysis (e.g., Forseti prediction) that requires reads to align to both spliced and unspliced transcript versions; triggered by having a genome .fasta and .gtf but no augmented spliceu index.
skills.name: spliceu-reference-construction
skills.search_text: spliceu-reference-construction Use when preparing a scRNA-seq splicing-status analysis (e.g., Forseti prediction) that requires reads to align to both spliced and unspliced transcript versions; triggered by having a genome .fasta and .gtf but no augmented spliceu index. You already have a pre-built spliceu reference (spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, t2g_3col.tsv) — rebuilding is unnecessary. Your analysis only needs standard spliced transcript quantification (e.g., GeneFull UMI counts alone) and does not require unspliced/ambiguous read disambiguation. You lack a genome FASTA and matching GTF for the same genome build, which are both required inputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Builds a spliceu (spliced + unspliced) augmented transcriptome reference from a genome FASTA and gene annotation GTF, so each transcript has both a spliced (exon concatenation) and an unspliced (genomic span of all exons) representation, enabling read compatibility with both spliced and unspliced transcripts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Builds a spliceu (spliced + unspliced) augmented transcriptome reference from a genome FASTA and gene annotation GTF, so each transcript has both a spliced (exon concatenation) and an unspliced (genomic span of all exons) representation, enabling read compatibility with both spliced and unspliced transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a pre-built spliceu reference (spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, t2g_3col.tsv) — rebuilding is unnecessary. Your analysis only needs standard spliced transcript quantification (e.g., GeneFull UMI counts alone) and does not require unspliced/ambiguous read disambiguation. You lack a genome FASTA and matching GTF for the same genome build, which are both required inputs.

skills.description: Use when starting from a raw genome FASTA plus matching GTF annotation and needing an expanded (splici) reference and mapper index for alevin-fry USA-mode single-cell quantification.
skills.name: splici-reference-generation
skills.search_text: splici-reference-generation Use when starting from a raw genome FASTA plus matching GTF annotation and needing an expanded (splici) reference and mapper index for alevin-fry USA-mode single-cell quantification. The expanded reference and piscem index already exist in the output directory — re-running would rebuild the index needlessly Quantification is to be run on reads already mapped (RAD files) — this skill covers only reference construction and indexing, not `simpleaf quant` Only a transcriptome FASTA (no genome FASTA + GTF) is available — roers requires a genome FASTA and a GTF/GFF3 annotation as input http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a spliced+intronic (splici) expanded transcriptome reference from a reference genome FASTA and GTF for alevin-fry/simpleaf single-cell quantification, then indexes it with piscem. Encapsulated by simpleaf as a single `index` command, with roers performing the splici construction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad614
skills.summary: Builds a spliced+intronic (splici) expanded transcriptome reference from a reference genome FASTA and GTF for alevin-fry/simpleaf single-cell quantification, then indexes it with piscem. Encapsulated by simpleaf as a single `index` command, with roers performing the splici construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expanded reference and piscem index already exist in the output directory — re-running would rebuild the index needlessly Quantification is to be run on reads already mapped (RAD files) — this skill covers only reference construction and indexing, not `simpleaf quant` Only a transcriptome FASTA (no genome FASTA + GTF) is available — roers requires a genome FASTA and a GTF/GFF3 annotation as input

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell velocity vectors from a new velocity method plus a pseudotime-defined state-transition axis, and need a fair head-to-head comparison against splicing-based methods like scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo.
skills.name: splicing-based-velocity-baseline-benchmarking
skills.search_text: splicing-based-velocity-baseline-benchmarking Use when you have per-cell velocity vectors from a new velocity method plus a pseudotime-defined state-transition axis, and need a fair head-to-head comparison against splicing-based methods like scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo. When no pseudotime-derived reference direction exists — cosine angles against an arbitrary axis are meaningless as a concordance metric. When the dataset lacks unspliced/spliced layer annotations required to fit splicing-based kinetics models like scVelo, VeloVAE, or UniTVelo. When evaluating regulator discovery or GRN quality rather than velocity direction concordance — this benchmark only scores angular alignment of per-cell velocities. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits splicing-kinetics RNA velocity baselines (scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on the same preprocessed scRNA-seq gene set used for an alternative velocity method, then scores all methods by cosine-angle concordance against a pseudotime-derived reference direction (e.g. the acinar-to-ductal metaplasia axis). This isolates whether the alternative method's priors produce directionally better velocities than standard splicing-based inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: Fits splicing-kinetics RNA velocity baselines (scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on the same preprocessed scRNA-seq gene set used for an alternative velocity method, then scores all methods by cosine-angle concordance against a pseudotime-derived reference direction (e.g. the acinar-to-ductal metaplasia axis). This isolates whether the alternative method's priors produce directionally better velocities than standard splicing-based inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no pseudotime-derived reference direction exists — cosine angles against an arbitrary axis are meaningless as a concordance metric. When the dataset lacks unspliced/spliced layer annotations required to fit splicing-based kinetics models like scVelo, VeloVAE, or UniTVelo. When evaluating regulator discovery or GRN quality rather than velocity direction concordance — this benchmark only scores angular alignment of per-cell velocities.

skills.description: Use when validating a splicing-status predictor for scRNA-seq reads: you need negative-control baselines (constant or random splice_prob) to demonstrate that model AUC reflects genuine prediction rather than chance.
skills.name: splicing-prediction-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: splicing-prediction-benchmark-evaluation Use when validating a splicing-status predictor for scRNA-seq reads: you need negative-control baselines (constant or random splice_prob) to demonstrate that model AUC reflects genuine prediction rather than chance. When you already have Forseti's own prediction scores and only want its reported AUC (0.92 simulated, 0.88 experimental) — this skill builds the negative-control baselines, not the model itself When the input reads lack ground-truth splicing-status labels (e.g. unannotated alignments); AUC cannot be computed without labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the trivial-baseline ROC comparison from the Forseti paper (Fig. 3), in which 'All spliced', 'All unspliced', and 'All random' predictors are evaluated on the same uniquely mapped PBMC1k scRNA-seq read set to confirm all attain AUC = 0.5. This establishes that no degenerate predictor approaches Forseti's reported performance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae207
skills.summary: Reproduces the trivial-baseline ROC comparison from the Forseti paper (Fig. 3), in which 'All spliced', 'All unspliced', and 'All random' predictors are evaluated on the same uniquely mapped PBMC1k scRNA-seq read set to confirm all attain AUC = 0.5. This establishes that no degenerate predictor approaches Forseti's reported performance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you already have Forseti's own prediction scores and only want its reported AUC (0.92 simulated, 0.88 experimental) — this skill builds the negative-control baselines, not the model itself When the input reads lack ground-truth splicing-status labels (e.g. unannotated alignments); AUC cannot be computed without labels

skills.search_text: splicing-qtl-enrichment-testing Use when you have an sQTL catalog (e.g. from sQTLseekeR2 on GTEx) plus RBP eCLIP peaks and want to test whether sQTLs change RBP binding motifs more than matched non-sQTL variants. Your goal is to test enrichment of sQTLs in splice-site sequences rather than RBP binding sites — the article treats these as distinct mechanism classes You lack eCLIP peaks for the RBP of interest, so no gkm-SVM model can be trained or scored Variants come from a univariate splicing QTL analysis not accounting for the multivariate nature of alternative splicing (no LeafCutter intron excision ratios), making the sQTL/non-sQTL stratification non-comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Tests whether splicing QTLs (sQTLs) disproportionately alter RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding sites relative to non-sQTL variants, by comparing |deltaSVM| scores from per-RBP gapped-kmer SVM models. Grounds the finding that more splicing variants modify RBP binding sites than splice-site sequences. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2

Grounds the finding that more splicing variants modify RBP binding sites than splice-site sequences.

skills.description: Use when you already hold fortuna signature-count output (cnt.tsv with '|' joined subexon IDs and counts) and need DEXSeq-compatible per-subexon counts for alternative splicing analysis.
skills.name: splicing-signature-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: splicing-signature-count-aggregation Use when you already hold fortuna signature-count output (cnt.tsv with '|' joined subexon IDs and counts) and need DEXSeq-compatible per-subexon counts for alternative splicing analysis. If you only have raw FASTQ reads and no fortuna signature counts — you must first run the fortuna pipeline (processGTF.sh, --index, pseudoalignment) to produce cnt.tsv. If you need kallisto TCCs or Yanagi bins rather than DEXSeq per-subexon counts — this aggregation targets DEXSeq-style counting units specifically. If your counts come from an align-and-count workflow rather than fortuna's pseudoalignment equivalence classes — the signature-to-subexon semantics differ. http://edamontology.org/topic_3320 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Converts fortuna's elementary splicing signature counts (pipe-separated subexon IDs with read counts, e.g. cnt.tsv) into DEXSeq-style per-subexon counts by aggregating each subexon's count as the sum of all mapping signatures that contain it, without reprocessing raw reads or alignments. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad419
skills.summary: Converts fortuna's elementary splicing signature counts (pipe-separated subexon IDs with read counts, e.g. cnt.tsv) into DEXSeq-style per-subexon counts by aggregating each subexon's count as the sum of all mapping signatures that contain it, without reprocessing raw reads or alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: If you only have raw FASTQ reads and no fortuna signature counts — you must first run the fortuna pipeline (processGTF.sh, --index, pseudoalignment) to produce cnt.tsv. If you need kallisto TCCs or Yanagi bins rather than DEXSeq per-subexon counts — this aggregation targets DEXSeq-style counting units specifically. If your counts come from an align-and-count workflow rather than fortuna's pseudoalignment equivalence classes — the signature-to-subexon semantics differ.

skills.description: Use when you need per-read splicing probabilities for single-cell RNA-seq alignments—especially reads labeled ambiguous ('A') by alevin-fry/STAR workflow logic—so that spliced/unspliced quantification or downstream velocity analyses can resolve fundamentally ambiguous reads.
skills.name: splicing-status-prediction-modeling
skills.search_text: splicing-status-prediction-modeling Use when you need per-read splicing probabilities for single-cell RNA-seq alignments—especially reads labeled ambiguous ('A') by alevin-fry/STAR workflow logic—so that spliced/unspliced quantification or downstream velocity analyses can resolve fundamentally ambiguous reads. skills.description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ to extract cell-type barcodes and UMI from Read2, especially when reads may contain insertions or deletions in the 8-nt barcode index regions.
skills.name: spliseq-read2-barcode-index-kmer-matching
skills.search_text: spliseq-read2-barcode-index-kmer-matching Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ to extract cell-type barcodes and UMI from Read2, especially when reads may contain insertions or deletions in the 8-nt barcode index regions. Data are not SPLiT-seq-style combinatorially barcoded paired-end reads (SCSit fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq only; other platforms are deferred to future updates). Barcodes are long enough for standard aligners — the paper notes BWA fails here only because the 8-bp barcodes are too short. You require tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel per read; SCSit's default is restricted and higher tolerance was evaluated but not adopted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs SCSit's k-mer sliding-window identification of the three combinatorial barcodes and UMI in each SPLiT-seq Read2, tolerating one mismatch and one indel via 8-nt segment matching and quad-to-decimal encoded barcode lookups. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Reconstructs SCSit's k-mer sliding-window identification of the three combinatorial barcodes and UMI in each SPLiT-seq Read2, tolerating one mismatch and one indel via 8-nt segment matching and quad-to-decimal encoded barcode lookups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not SPLiT-seq-style combinatorially barcoded paired-end reads (SCSit fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq only; other platforms are deferred to future updates). Barcodes are long enough for standard aligners — the paper notes BWA fails here only because the 8-bp barcodes are too short. You require tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel per read; SCSit's default is restricted and higher tolerance was evaluated but not adopted.

skills.description: Use when one or more seqspec spec.yaml files are available and the goal is to interpret a library's ordered sequence elements or to compare library structures across assays — e.g. checking which split-pool barcode rounds are shared between two modalities.

skills.search_text: split-pool-barcoding-layout-interpretation Use when one or more seqspec spec.yaml files are available and the goal is to interpret a library's ordered sequence elements or to compare library structures across assays — e.g. checking which split-pool barcode rounds are shared between two modalities. Input is already a processed cell-by-feature count matrix (mtx/h5ad) — use mx inspect/filter or cellatlas preprocessing instead, since library structure is no longer the object of analysis The goal is read preprocessing (alignment, barcode correction, UMI counting) rather than interpreting or comparing library structure — seqspec print describes the spec, it does not quantify reads No seqspec spec.yaml exists for the assay of interest; the Region Ordered Tree can only be rendered from a machine-readable specification http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Interprets and compares the library structures encoded in seqspec YAML specifications, particularly to reveal that assays from different protocols (e.g. SPLiT-seq RNA-only vs. SHARE-seq RNA+ATAC) can share near-identical split-pool barcoding layouts. seqspec renders each spec as a Region Ordered Tree whose annotated nucleotide lengths make the ordered sequence elements (barcodes, UMIs, linkers, biological features) directly comparable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae168

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed cell-by-feature count matrix (mtx/h5ad) — use mx inspect/filter or cellatlas preprocessing instead, since library structure is no longer the object of analysis The goal is read preprocessing (alignment, barcode correction, UMI counting) rather than interpreting or comparing library structure — seqspec print describes the spec, it does not quantify reads No seqspec spec.yaml exists for the assay of interest; the Region Ordered Tree can only be rendered from a machine-readable specification

skills.description: Use when preprocessing raw SPLiT-seq paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads to label each read's cellular origin by identifying combinatorial barcodes (three 8 nt rounds) and UMI, especially when the original method's filters would discard too many reads.

skills.search_text: split-seq-combinatorial-barcode-identification Use when preprocessing raw SPLiT-seq paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads to label each read's cellular origin by identifying combinatorial barcodes (three 8 nt rounds) and UMI, especially when the original method's filters would discard too many reads. Input data is not from SPLiT-seq combinatorial barcoding — SCSit's fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data, and support for other single-cell sequencing platforms is deferred to future updates The task is genome alignment of clean reads (use STAR against mm10 or combined mm10-hg19 after barcode identification, not SCSit) A permissive mismatch/indel tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel is desired for maximal read recovery — this costs 20–40% more runtime for only 4–5% more identified reads (Table S4) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identify three rounds of combinatorial cell barcodes and UMI in SPLiT-seq paired-end reads using SCSit, which tolerates one mismatch and one indel during barcode alignment and outputs labeled Read1/Read2 FASTQ pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: Identify three rounds of combinatorial cell barcodes and UMI in SPLiT-seq paired-end reads using SCSit, which tolerates one mismatch and one indel during barcode alignment and outputs labeled Read1/Read2 FASTQ pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not from SPLiT-seq combinatorial barcoding — SCSit's fault-tolerant and indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data, and support for other single-cell sequencing platforms is deferred to future updates The task is genome alignment of clean reads (use STAR against mm10 or combined mm10-hg19 after barcode identification, not SCSit) A permissive mismatch/indel tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel is desired for maximal read recovery — this costs 20–40% more runtime for only 4–5% more identified reads (Table S4)

skills.description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data (e.g., SAMN08567259–SAMN08567264) to identify combinatorial barcodes and UMI fault-tolerantly, and to compare STAR mapped-read counts against the original BLAST/BWA-based SPLiT-seq filtering.
skills.name: splitseq-read-barcoding-preprocessing
skills.search_text: splitseq-read-barcoding-preprocessing Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data (e.g., SAMN08567259–SAMN08567264) to identify combinatorial barcodes and UMI fault-tolerantly, and to compare STAR mapped-read counts against the original BLAST/BWA-based SPLiT-seq filtering. Input data is from other single-cell sequencing platforms (e.g., non-SPLiT-seq barcode chemistries) — the article states fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data and support for more platforms is deferred to future updates Barcodes are longer than 8 nt — the article notes BWA fails to exploit such short 8 bp barcodes and BLAST-based determination is slow; SCSit's k-mer/indicator design targets the 8 nt SPLiT-seq barcodes You need tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel by default — the article reports this increases identified reads only 4–5% while taking 20–40% more runtime, so it was not adopted http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A preprocessing skill for SPLiT-seq single-cell data in which SCSit, a multithreaded C program, fault-tolerantly identifies three 8 nt cell barcodes and UMI (one mismatch, one INDEL) from paired-end FASTQ reads, and the resulting labeled reads are aligned with STAR to a combined mm10-hg19 or mm10 genome to demonstrate roughly doubled mapped-read yield versus the original SPLiT-seq method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.021
skills.summary: A preprocessing skill for SPLiT-seq single-cell data in which SCSit, a multithreaded C program, fault-tolerantly identifies three 8 nt cell barcodes and UMI (one mismatch, one INDEL) from paired-end FASTQ reads, and the resulting labeled reads are aligned with STAR to a combined mm10-hg19 or mm10 genome to demonstrate roughly doubled mapped-read yield versus the original SPLiT-seq method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is from other single-cell sequencing platforms (e.g., non-SPLiT-seq barcode chemistries) — the article states fault-tolerant/indel alignment was proposed for SPLiT-seq data and support for more platforms is deferred to future updates Barcodes are longer than 8 nt — the article notes BWA fails to exploit such short 8 bp barcodes and BLAST-based determination is slow; SCSit's k-mer/indicator design targets the 8 nt SPLiT-seq barcodes You need tolerance beyond one mismatch and one indel by default — the article reports this increases identified reads only 4–5% while taking 20–40% more runtime, so it was not adopted

skills.search_text: spot-lattice-adjacency-construction-from-coordinates Use when generating automated scribbles via AutoScribbleDom and you need neighbor adjacency to label-spot consensus-filter an initial non-spatial Mclust clustering on Visium or ST platform data. skills.summary: A KNN-based imputation step from stAPAminer that recovers sparse APA usage (RUD) values in spatially barcoded ST data by inferring spot–spot distances from the scaled gene expression profile and borrowing APA usage from neighboring spots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a gene expression matrix needing no APA imputation — this skill only recovers sparse APA usage (RUD) entries Data are image-based ST such as MERFISH/seqFISH, since APA sites can only be identified from spatially barcoded ST data using tools like scAPAtrap or Sierra The RUD matrix is already complete with no missing entries to impute

skills.search_text: spurious-interaction-generation-from-variable-genes Use when stress-testing the robustness of CCC inference (e.g. CellChat, CellPhoneDB, SingleCellSignalR run via LIANA) to corruption of the prior-knowledge ligand-receptor resource rather than to noise in the expression data or cell-type labels. skills.summary: Generates spurious ligand-receptor interactions drawn from the 2000 most variable genes to replace 0–40% of a curated CCC resource's interactions, in both selective (rank-preserving) and non-selective modes. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the perturbation of interest is cell-level noise (subsampling 0–40% of cells or reshuffling 0–40% of cell-type labels) rather than prior-knowledge-resource corruption — this is a different ablation axis When the goal is to identify a definitively best CCC method or resource — the article states no gold standard exists and biological ground truth for CCC is largely unknown When genuine large-scale curation of ligand-receptor resources is the goal; spurious interactions simulate resource errors and are not biologically validated knowledge

skills.description: Use when a catalog of sQTLs (e.g. sqtlseeker2-nf nominal/permuted output at FDR < 0.05) exists and the goal is to identify which functional annotations — splice sites, histone marks, GWAS hits — are over-represented among sQTLs versus matched non-sQTLs.
skills.name: sqtl-catalog-functional-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: sqtl-catalog-functional-enrichment-analysis Use when a catalog of sQTLs (e.g. sqtlseeker2-nf nominal/permuted output at FDR < 0.05) exists and the goal is to identify which functional annotations — splice sites, histone marks, GWAS hits — are over-represented among sQTLs versus matched non-sQTLs. No matched non-sQTL null sets can be generated (e.g. the sQTL catalog lacks MAF and within-gene location metadata needed for +/-0.02 MAF matching). The goal is fine-mapping or co-localization of sQTL and eQTL effects — the article notes currently available co-localization methods are not directly applicable within the multivariate non-parametric sQTL framework. Input is a raw expression/genotype dataset rather than a mapped sQTL catalog; sQTL mapping via sqtlseeker2-nf must be run first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Tests whether sQTLs mapped with sQTLseekeR2/sqtlseeker2-nf are enriched in functional genome annotations (splice donor/acceptor sites, H3K36me3 marks, GWAS LD hits) relative to matched non-sQTL null variants, using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact tests with FDR correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Tests whether sQTLs mapped with sQTLseekeR2/sqtlseeker2-nf are enriched in functional genome annotations (splice donor/acceptor sites, H3K36me3 marks, GWAS LD hits) relative to matched non-sQTL null variants, using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact tests with FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched non-sQTL null sets can be generated (e.g. the sQTL catalog lacks MAF and within-gene location metadata needed for +/-0.02 MAF matching). The goal is fine-mapping or co-localization of sQTL and eQTL effects — the article notes currently available co-localization methods are not directly applicable within the multivariate non-parametric sQTL framework. Input is a raw expression/genotype dataset rather than a mapped sQTL catalog; sQTL mapping via sqtlseeker2-nf must be run first.

skills.description: Use when nominal sQTL test output (all-tests.nominal.tsv) and FDR-thresholded sQTL labels are available and the goal is to test whether sQTLs alter splice site strength more often/strongly than non-sQTLs, scaling with md effect size.
skills.name: sqtl-effect-size-stratified-analysis
skills.search_text: sqtl-effect-size-stratified-analysis Use when nominal sQTL test output (all-tests.nominal.tsv) and FDR-thresholded sQTL labels are available and the goal is to test whether sQTLs alter splice site strength more often/strongly than non-sQTLs, scaling with md effect size. The analysis target is RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding site disruption rather than splice site motifs — the paper reports many more variants modify RBP binding sites, which requires a different scoring workflow (e.g. the gkmSVM-based analysis). Variants of interest do not overlap annotated donor or acceptor splice site intervals — PWM splice site strength is undefined for them. Only permuted-pass or FDR-adjusted summaries are available without per-variant nominal tests (all-tests.nominal.tsv), since md effect size per variant is needed for stratification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Reproduce the paper's splice-site strength analysis: score reference and alternative alleles of splice-site-overlapping variants with position weight matrices, compare sQTLs (FDR ≤ 0.05) versus non-sQTLs, and stratify absolute strength change |PWM(alt) - PWM(ref)| by sQTL effect size (md) bins to test the Fig. 4a trend. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Reproduce the paper's splice-site strength analysis: score reference and alternative alleles of splice-site-overlapping variants with position weight matrices, compare sQTLs (FDR ≤ 0.05) versus non-sQTLs, and stratify absolute strength change |PWM(alt) - PWM(ref)| by sQTL effect size (md) bins to test the Fig. 4a trend.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding site disruption rather than splice site motifs — the paper reports many more variants modify RBP binding sites, which requires a different scoring workflow (e.g. the gkmSVM-based analysis). Variants of interest do not overlap annotated donor or acceptor splice site intervals — PWM splice site strength is undefined for them. Only permuted-pass or FDR-adjusted summaries are available without per-variant nominal tests (all-tests.nominal.tsv), since md effect size per variant is needed for stratification.

skills.name: sqtl-mapping-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: sqtl-mapping-pipeline-execution Use when you need to identify genetic variants associated with multivariate splicing phenotypes (intron excision ratios) from genotype and transcript expression data in a reproducible, containerized workflow. The phenotype of interest is gene expression level rather than splicing ratios — an eQTL pipeline, not this sQTL mapper, is the right tool You need to splice individual splicing events univariately or perform co-localization/fine-mapping, which are not directly applicable within this multivariate, non-parametric framework http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Execute the sQTLseekeR2-based Nextflow pipeline (sqtlseeker2-nf) to map splicing QTLs from genotype and transcript expression data, running a nominal cis-association pass followed by an optional permutation pass for empirical P-values and multiple-testing correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Execute the sQTLseekeR2-based Nextflow pipeline (sqtlseeker2-nf) to map splicing QTLs from genotype and transcript expression data, running a nominal cis-association pass followed by an optional permutation pass for empirical P-values and multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The phenotype of interest is gene expression level rather than splicing ratios — an eQTL pipeline, not this sQTL mapper, is the right tool You need to splice individual splicing events univariately or perform co-localization/fine-mapping, which are not directly applicable within this multivariate, non-parametric framework

skills.description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL catalogs (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) and need to measure to what extent sQTLs are shared across GTEx tissues, or whether a tissue group such as brain has a distinct sharing pattern.
skills.name: sqtls-effect-size-pearson-correlation
skills.search_text: sqtls-effect-size-pearson-correlation Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL catalogs (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) and need to measure to what extent sQTLs are shared across GTEx tissues, or whether a tissue group such as brain has a distinct sharing pattern. You only have eQTL (expression) effect sizes rather than sQTL splicing MD effect sizes — this measures splicing-QTL sharing, not eQTL sharing Variant-gene pairs are significant in only one of the two tissues being compared — correlations must be computed on pairs significant in both tissues You need formal co-localization or fine-mapping of causal variants; the article notes such methods are not directly applicable within this multivariate, non-parametric framework and paired effects could be two variants in LD Quantify cross-tissue sharing of sQTLs by computing pairwise Pearson correlations of MD (maximum difference in relative expression) effect sizes over variant-gene pairs significant in both tissues of each pair, then cluster tissues by the resulting correlation matrix. This reproduces the Garrido-Martín et al. (2021) finding that brain subregions form a distinct sharing cluster (within-group mean r ~0.80/0.78 vs ~0.64 between groups). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Quantify cross-tissue sharing of sQTLs by computing pairwise Pearson correlations of MD (maximum difference in relative expression) effect sizes over variant-gene pairs significant in both tissues of each pair, then cluster tissues by the resulting correlation matrix. This reproduces the Garrido-Martín et al. (2021) finding that brain subregions form a distinct sharing cluster (within-group mean r ~0.80/0.78 vs ~0.64 between groups).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have eQTL (expression) effect sizes rather than sQTL splicing MD effect sizes — this measures splicing-QTL sharing, not eQTL sharing Variant-gene pairs are significant in only one of the two tissues being compared — correlations must be computed on pairs significant in both tissues You need formal co-localization or fine-mapping of causal variants; the article notes such methods are not directly applicable within this multivariate, non-parametric framework and paired effects could be two variants in LD

skills.description: Use when you have sqtlseeker2-nf sQTL mapping output (nominal per-variant tests plus FDR-significant sQTL tables) and need binary sQTL/non-sQTL labels for downstream functional-enrichment comparisons such as splice-site PWM strength analysis.
skills.name: sqtls-fdr-threshold-classification
skills.search_text: sqtls-fdr-threshold-classification Use when you have sqtlseeker2-nf sQTL mapping output (nominal per-variant tests plus FDR-significant sQTL tables) and need binary sQTL/non-sQTL labels for downstream functional-enrichment comparisons such as splice-site PWM strength analysis. You only have nominal p-values without the FDR-selected sQTL table (sqtls-${level}fdr.nominal.tsv) — thresholding raw p-values is not the paper's multiple-testing scheme Your question concerns eQTL/eGene classification or gene expression, not splicing phenotypes; this skill only labels splicing QTLs from sQTLseekeR2 output http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Classify tested variants as sQTLs versus non-sQTLs by joining per-variant nominal tests from the sqtlseeker2-nf output (all-tests.nominal.tsv) with the FDR-selected sQTL labels in sqtls-${level}fdr.nominal.tsv (default FDR 0.05), so downstream analyses can contrast the two variant sets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20578-2
skills.summary: Classify tested variants as sQTLs versus non-sQTLs by joining per-variant nominal tests from the sqtlseeker2-nf output (all-tests.nominal.tsv) with the FDR-selected sQTL labels in sqtls-${level}fdr.nominal.tsv (default FDR 0.05), so downstream analyses can contrast the two variant sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have nominal p-values without the FDR-selected sQTL table (sqtls-${level}fdr.nominal.tsv) — thresholding raw p-values is not the paper's multiple-testing scheme Your question concerns eQTL/eGene classification or gene expression, not splicing phenotypes; this skill only labels splicing QTLs from sQTLseekeR2 output

skills.description: Use when you have spatially resolved single-cell or spot-level data (seqFISH, merFISH, 10x Visium) with cell-type labels and need to test whether prioritized CCC interactions are enriched between spatially adjacent cell types.
skills.name: squidpy-neighbourhood-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: squidpy-neighbourhood-enrichment-analysis Use when you have spatially resolved single-cell or spot-level data (seqFISH, merFISH, 10x Visium) with cell-type labels and need to test whether prioritized CCC interactions are enriched between spatially adjacent cell types. The data have no spatial coordinates or cell-type annotations (e.g., dissociated scRNA-seq alone), so adjacency cannot be assessed The goal is to prioritize or score ligand-receptor pairs themselves rather than to evaluate the spatial coherence of already-ranked CCC predictions Studying long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq/spatial gene expression does not capture http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Uses Squidpy's label-permutation neighbourhood enrichment on spatial transcriptomics data (seqFISH, merFISH, Visium) to identify statistically adjacent/colocalized cell-type pairs, then tests whether top-ranked LIANA ligand-receptor interactions are preferentially found between those pairs via odds ratios. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-30755-0
skills.summary: Uses Squidpy's label-permutation neighbourhood enrichment on spatial transcriptomics data (seqFISH, merFISH, Visium) to identify statistically adjacent/colocalized cell-type pairs, then tests whether top-ranked LIANA ligand-receptor interactions are preferentially found between those pairs via odds ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have no spatial coordinates or cell-type annotations (e.g., dissociated scRNA-seq alone), so adjacency cannot be assessed The goal is to prioritize or score ligand-receptor pairs themselves rather than to evaluate the spatial coherence of already-ranked CCC predictions Studying long-distance endocrine signalling, which scRNA-seq/spatial gene expression does not capture

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-seq data for a study must be fetched from NCBI SRA via SRR/ERR run accessions or a study accession (SRP) before quantification with tools like Seq2Fun 2.0.
skills.name: sra-fastq-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-fastq-data-retrieval Use when raw RNA-seq data for a study must be fetched from NCBI SRA via SRR/ERR run accessions or a study accession (SRP) before quantification with tools like Seq2Fun 2.0. Count tables (e.g., salamander_ortholog_counts.tsv) or processed FASTQ files are already available locally The study's data are not deposited in NCBI SRA or accessions are invalid/unreleased The analysis starts from an existing gene expression matrix rather than raw reads (the ExpressAnalystR gene-matrix workflow) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fetch raw paired-end FASTQ files from NCBI SRA by accession (e.g., SRR7499348–SRR7499365 salamander samples or SRP299836 zebrafish samples) as the entry point for downstream Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst RNA-seq quantification in non-model species. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-38785-y
skills.summary: Fetch raw paired-end FASTQ files from NCBI SRA by accession (e.g., SRR7499348–SRR7499365 salamander samples or SRP299836 zebrafish samples) as the entry point for downstream Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst RNA-seq quantification in non-model species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Count tables (e.g., salamander_ortholog_counts.tsv) or processed FASTQ files are already available locally The study's data are not deposited in NCBI SRA or accessions are invalid/unreleased The analysis starts from an existing gene expression matrix rather than raw reads (the ExpressAnalystR gene-matrix workflow)

skills.description: Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq analysis and raw reads must be fetched from SRA before trimming, alignment (STAR), and quantification (RSEM/DESeq2); triggered when a supplemental accession table lists the samples.
skills.name: sra-fastq-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-fastq-retrieval Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq analysis and raw reads must be fetched from SRA before trimming, alignment (STAR), and quantification (RSEM/DESeq2); triggered when a supplemental accession table lists the samples. The processed read alignments or gene-level count/TPM tables are already available, making raw FASTQ retrieval unnecessary The target data are genome annotations rather than sequencing reads — obtain those from Ensembl (GRCh38/hg38) instead of SRA http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Retrieve published RNA-seq FASTQ files from the SRA using the per-sample accession list compiled in the study's Supplemental Table S1, as the first step of reproducing the pESC vs aESC differential expression analysis with the GRCh38/hg38 reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Retrieve published RNA-seq FASTQ files from the SRA using the per-sample accession list compiled in the study's Supplemental Table S1, as the first step of reproducing the pESC vs aESC differential expression analysis with the GRCh38/hg38 reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The processed read alignments or gene-level count/TPM tables are already available, making raw FASTQ retrieval unnecessary The target data are genome annotations rather than sequencing reads — obtain those from Ensembl (GRCh38/hg38) instead of SRA

skills.description: Use when reproducing the UMI mapping-shift analysis or Table 1 cluster-size read fractions and raw FASTQ files for any of run_171108, run_170420, SCRB, La Manno, Yanai1, or Yanai2 are needed.
skills.name: sra-rnaseq-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: sra-rnaseq-data-retrieval Use when reproducing the UMI mapping-shift analysis or Table 1 cluster-size read fractions and raw FASTQ files for any of run_171108, run_170420, SCRB, La Manno, Yanai1, or Yanai2 are needed. The analysis does not involve UMI-containing libraries or the UMI-analysis pipeline, e.g. paired-end bulk RNA-Seq differential expression projects where the 5'-UMI clipping and single-end assumption do not apply. Input is already quality-filtered, UMI-clipped, or a sorted SAM/BAM file — the downstream steps (umi_counterizer.pl, umi_analyzer_uthash) expect raw FASTQ with the UMI still at the 5' end of each read. The target data set is not one of the article's six, and no 5'-UMI position/length is known for it, since fastq_umi_clipper requires an explicit clip_length and optional g_length (e.g. protocol-derived trailing GGG/GGGG from the Clontech SMARTer system). http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Retrieves raw single-end FASTQ reads for the six UMI-containing RNA-Seq data sets used in the Sena et al. 2018 UMI mapping-shift study (run_171108, run_170420, SCRB, La Manno, Yanai1, Yanai2) from their SRA accessions, so that UMI-read cluster distributions can be reproduced downstream. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-018-31064-7
skills.summary: Retrieves raw single-end FASTQ reads for the six UMI-containing RNA-Seq data sets used in the Sena et al. 2018 UMI mapping-shift study (run_171108, run_170420, SCRB, La Manno, Yanai1, Yanai2) from their SRA accessions, so that UMI-read cluster distributions can be reproduced downstream.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis does not involve UMI-containing libraries or the UMI-analysis pipeline, e.g. paired-end bulk RNA-Seq differential expression projects where the 5'-UMI clipping and single-end assumption do not apply. Input is already quality-filtered, UMI-clipped, or a sorted SAM/BAM file — the downstream steps (umi_counterizer.pl, umi_analyzer_uthash) expect raw FASTQ with the UMI still at the 5' end of each read. The target data set is not one of the article's six, and no 5'-UMI position/length is known for it, since fastq_umi_clipper requires an explicit clip_length and optional g_length (e.g. protocol-derived trailing GGG/GGGG from the Clontech SMARTer system).

skills.description: Use when running the PhasiHunter preprocess module to produce .map files from sRNA FASTQ data against transcriptome/genome references, or when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools with the Bowtie index/mapping step held constant.
skills.name: srna-read-mapping-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: srna-read-mapping-workflow-execution Use when running the PhasiHunter preprocess module to produce .map files from sRNA FASTQ data against transcriptome/genome references, or when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools with the Bowtie index/mapping step held constant. When the analysis goal is degradome-based target or initiator prediction (phasihunter deg / target modules) rather than sRNA mapping and runtime comparison When the raw FASTQ has already been trimmed, normalized, and filtered — use preprocess mode m (mapping only) or skip to the phase module instead of rerunning raw mode When per-tool end-to-end wall-clock times including index building are desired; this skill deliberately excludes the shared Bowtie indexing/mapping step from timing http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Executes the sRNA-seq read preprocessing/mapping stage of the PhasiHunter pipeline (adapter trimming, normalization, length/abundance filtering, Bowtie mapping) so that shared mapping artifacts (cdna/gdna .map files) can feed downstream phasiRNA prediction and be excluded from runtime benchmarking of PhasiHunter, unitas, PhaseTank, and PhasiRNAnalyzer. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad676
skills.summary: Executes the sRNA-seq read preprocessing/mapping stage of the PhasiHunter pipeline (adapter trimming, normalization, length/abundance filtering, Bowtie mapping) so that shared mapping artifacts (cdna/gdna .map files) can feed downstream phasiRNA prediction and be excluded from runtime benchmarking of PhasiHunter, unitas, PhaseTank, and PhasiRNAnalyzer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is degradome-based target or initiator prediction (phasihunter deg / target modules) rather than sRNA mapping and runtime comparison When the raw FASTQ has already been trimmed, normalized, and filtered — use preprocess mode m (mapping only) or skip to the phase module instead of rerunning raw mode When per-tool end-to-end wall-clock times including index building are desired; this skill deliberately excludes the shared Bowtie indexing/mapping step from timing

skills.search_text: srna-read-stack-visualization Use when you need to visually inspect read stacks, expression boxplots, and arm-selection events for candidate plant miRNAs (e.g., ath-MIR156b) to support manual curation decisions. You only need genome-wide candidate lists rather than per-candidate feature-level curation views (use MiRNA Compilation/MiRNA Selection outputs instead) sRNA-Seq data come from a species without a reference genome, since unmapped reads are ignored and cannot support the read-stack display http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Visualize the sRNA-Seq read support, arm expression patterns, and arm-selection events of each selected miRNA candidate as feature views rendered into per-miRNA interactive HTML report pages within the iwa-miRNA manualCuration module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
skills.summary: Visualize the sRNA-Seq read support, arm expression patterns, and arm-selection events of each selected miRNA candidate as feature views rendered into per-miRNA interactive HTML report pages within the iwa-miRNA manualCuration module.

skills.search_text: srnaseq-read-alignment-to-reference-genome Use when you have sRNA-Seq data (SRA accession numbers or FASTQ files) for a plant species WITH a reference genome and need to predict novel miRNA precursors from mapped reads. The species has no reference genome sequence — iwa-miRNA cannot handle sRNA-Seq data from species without genome sequences Most sequencing reads do not map to the reference genome — unmapped reads are ignored in the current version, so no candidates will be derived from them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Aligns small RNA sequencing reads to a formatted plant reference genome using GMAP (via the iwa-miRNA miRNAPredict module) to predict novel miRNA precursor candidates that are later merged with database-annotated precursors. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2021.02.010
