skills.description: Use when a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor or LINCS drug-induced profiles) must be transformed into per-sample FM activity scores at the pathway level as part of the GSFM four-quantifier (GSFM_Up/Down/ssGSEA/TF) active-matrix construction.
skills.name: ssgsea-pathway-enrichment-scoring
skills.search_text: ssgsea-pathway-enrichment-scoring Use when a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor or LINCS drug-induced profiles) must be transformed into per-sample FM activity scores at the pathway level as part of the GSFM four-quantifier (GSFM_Up/Down/ssGSEA/TF) active-matrix construction. The analysis only needs gene-level up/down regulation proportions, where GSFM_Up/GSFM_Down (Z-score |1.96| threshold) are sufficient and ssGSEA adds no information. Input is already a GSFM/FM active matrix — the ssGSEA quantifier operates on gene expression matrices, not on transformed module-level tables. No adequate gene set definitions are available for the disease under study; the paper notes that defining functional modules without prior knowledge is a key limitation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes per-sample pathway-level activity of the 50 cancer-related Hallmark functional modules (FMs) via a GSFM_ssGSEA quantifier that compares the empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs) of gene expression ranks inside versus outside each FM, contributing the pathway-level column of the GSFM active matrix. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.apsb.2024.08.017
skills.summary: Computes per-sample pathway-level activity of the 50 cancer-related Hallmark functional modules (FMs) via a GSFM_ssGSEA quantifier that compares the empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs) of gene expression ranks inside versus outside each FM, contributing the pathway-level column of the GSFM active matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs gene-level up/down regulation proportions, where GSFM_Up/GSFM_Down (Z-score |1.96| threshold) are sufficient and ssGSEA adds no information. Input is already a GSFM/FM active matrix — the ssGSEA quantifier operates on gene expression matrices, not on transformed module-level tables. No adequate gene set definitions are available for the disease under study; the paper notes that defining functional modules without prior knowledge is a key limitation.

skills.description: Use when you have fitted SSrGE on paired SNV (n_cells x n_SNVs binary) and gene-expression matrices and need a ranked gene list (with SNV ids) to select top-ranked eeSNV genes for subpopulation markers or pathway enrichment.
skills.name: ssrge-gene-ranking
skills.search_text: ssrge-gene-ranking Use when you have fitted SSrGE on paired SNV (n_cells x n_SNVs binary) and gene-expression matrices and need a ranked gene list (with SNV ids) to select top-ranked eeSNV genes for subpopulation markers or pathway enrichment. Input is a single unpaired matrix (SNV or expression alone) — SSrGE ranking requires both a coupled SNV matrix and a gene-expression matrix from the same cells The environment cannot run Python 2.7 with scikit-learn 0.18, which the package requires The goal is de novo SNV calling from raw reads rather than ranking already-called eeSNVs and genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Rank eeSNVs and the genes harboring them after fitting SSrGE sparse linear models, so that robust SNV-based genetic markers (e.g., top 100 ranked genes per scRNA-seq cancer dataset) can be identified and carried into downstream enrichment analyses such as DAVID KEGG pathway testing. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Rank eeSNVs and the genes harboring them after fitting SSrGE sparse linear models, so that robust SNV-based genetic markers (e.g., top 100 ranked genes per scRNA-seq cancer dataset) can be identified and carried into downstream enrichment analyses such as DAVID KEGG pathway testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single unpaired matrix (SNV or expression alone) — SSrGE ranking requires both a coupled SNV matrix and a gene-expression matrix from the same cells The environment cannot run Python 2.7 with scikit-learn 0.18, which the package requires The goal is de novo SNV calling from raw reads rather than ranking already-called eeSNVs and genes

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell SNV matrices and gene expression matrices from scRNA-seq (or coupled RRBS/RNA-seq) data and need to identify expressed SNVs (eeSNVs) associated with gene expression, with or without copy-number predictors.
skills.name: ssrge-linear-model-fitting-with-cnv-predictors
skills.search_text: ssrge-linear-model-fitting-with-cnv-predictors Use when you have per-cell SNV matrices and gene expression matrices from scRNA-seq (or coupled RRBS/RNA-seq) data and need to identify expressed SNVs (eeSNVs) associated with gene expression, with or without copy-number predictors. Input is already a reduced/ranked feature matrix — SSrGE is a feature selection step applied to raw SNV x cell and gene x cell matrices, not a downstream analysis tool SNVs are highly correlated and you need all of them retained — LASSO may arbitrarily select only one of highly correlated SNV features corresponding to a gene's expression The driver mutation has incomplete DNA coverage in the scRNA-seq reads — SSrGE may miss driver mutations entirely in that case http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0199 Fit SSrGE sparse linear models (LASSO by default, ElasticNet optional) linking binary eeSNV matrices (n_cells x n_SNVs) to gene expression matrices (n_cells x n_Genes), optionally including a CNV matrix (n_cells x n_genes) as an additional predictor to recover SNV-gene expression associations in single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-07170-5
skills.summary: Fit SSrGE sparse linear models (LASSO by default, ElasticNet optional) linking binary eeSNV matrices (n_cells x n_SNVs) to gene expression matrices (n_cells x n_Genes), optionally including a CNV matrix (n_cells x n_genes) as an additional predictor to recover SNV-gene expression associations in single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced/ranked feature matrix — SSrGE is a feature selection step applied to raw SNV x cell and gene x cell matrices, not a downstream analysis tool SNVs are highly correlated and you need all of them retained — LASSO may arbitrarily select only one of highly correlated SNV features corresponding to a gene's expression The driver mutation has incomplete DNA coverage in the scRNA-seq reads — SSrGE may miss driver mutations entirely in that case

skills.description: Use when SC cells lack coordinates but an ST reference (e.g. SeqFISH embryo ST h5ad with .obs[['x','y']]) exists, and reconstructed per-cell spatial locations are needed for downstream co-localization or cell-cell communication analyses.
skills.name: st-reference-contrastive-model-inference
skills.search_text: st-reference-contrastive-model-inference Use when SC cells lack coordinates but an ST reference (e.g. SeqFISH embryo ST h5ad with .obs[['x','y']]) exists, and reconstructed per-cell spatial locations are needed for downstream co-localization or cell-cell communication analyses. There is a large gap between the query SC data and the ST reference: forcing SC assignment to resemble the ST could introduce more bias, and MDS de novo mode loses the pre-knowledge of the reference's cell distribution The SC data already contains truth spatial coordinates (use them directly as reference patterns instead) Spot-based ST parameters are mistakenly used for imaging-based single-cell ST references — the predefined --single_cell parameter set must be adopted instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3934 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply a contrastively trained CellContrast encoder to spatially reconstruct single-cell RNA-seq (SC) cells by projecting their latent representations onto a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference with truth locations, or onto an MDS pseudo-space from SC-SC cosine-similarity distances. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2024.101022
skills.summary: Apply a contrastively trained CellContrast encoder to spatially reconstruct single-cell RNA-seq (SC) cells by projecting their latent representations onto a spatial transcriptomics (ST) reference with truth locations, or onto an MDS pseudo-space from SC-SC cosine-similarity distances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is a large gap between the query SC data and the ST reference: forcing SC assignment to resemble the ST could introduce more bias, and MDS de novo mode loses the pre-knowledge of the reference's cell distribution The SC data already contains truth spatial coordinates (use them directly as reference patterns instead) Spot-based ST parameters are mistakenly used for imaging-based single-cell ST references — the predefined --single_cell parameter set must be adopted instead

skills.description: Use when preparing a 10x Visium training reference for CeLEry 2D location recovery, e.g. the mouse posterior brain dataset, where spot-level resolution or a limited gene panel would limit spatial-location prediction accuracy.
skills.name: st-super-pixel-data-enhancement
skills.search_text: st-super-pixel-data-enhancement Use when preparing a 10x Visium training reference for CeLEry 2D location recovery, e.g. the mouse posterior brain dataset, where spot-level resolution or a limited gene panel would limit spatial-location prediction accuracy. The task is spatial domain recovery rather than 2D location recovery — then differentially expressed genes are selected with rank_genes_groups in Scanpy instead of spatially variable genes in spaGCN The input is scRNA-seq test data, which is consumed by the CeLEry model but should not be TESLA-enhanced Cells have low UMI counts or a small number of expressed genes — such cells are eliminated rather than enhanced http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0202 Enhance 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics data to super-pixel resolution with TESLA and select spatially variable genes (SpaGCN rank_genes_groups) so that downstream CeLEry location-recovery training uses a denser, higher-quality spatial reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39895-3
skills.summary: Enhance 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics data to super-pixel resolution with TESLA and select spatially variable genes (SpaGCN rank_genes_groups) so that downstream CeLEry location-recovery training uses a denser, higher-quality spatial reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is spatial domain recovery rather than 2D location recovery — then differentially expressed genes are selected with rank_genes_groups in Scanpy instead of spatially variable genes in spaGCN The input is scRNA-seq test data, which is consumed by the CeLEry model but should not be TESLA-enhanced Cells have low UMI counts or a small number of expressed genes — such cells are eliminated rather than enhanced

skills.description: Decision support for choosing how many reference genes to aggregate in qPCR normalization: when you need to compare SD-vs-k stability curves of a weighted (geom_sd_hybrid) versus unweighted (geom) virtual RG to find the crossover point.
skills.name: stability-curve-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: stability-curve-benchmark-comparison Decision support for choosing how many reference genes to aggregate in qPCR normalization: when you need to compare SD-vs-k stability curves of a weighted (geom_sd_hybrid) versus unweighted (geom) virtual RG to find the crossover point. When the experiment uses only 2-3 preselected internal controls (e.g. RNU48, hsa-miR-16-5p) — use calcWeight on raw CT values instead of iterating over combination sizes When the goal is to select the best combination within a fixed k rather than to determine how many reference genes to aggregate — the benchmarking pipeline per-k sweep is unnecessary When analyzing non-qPCR normalized expression data where raw CT-based weighting assumptions do not hold http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Benchmarks the geom(sd) weighted virtual reference gene against the usual (unweighted) geometric mean across increasing numbers of aggregated reference genes (k=2 to 20), quantifying where the weighting advantage disappears. This reproduces the InterOpt finding that geom(sd) is applicable to up to five or six reference genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107945
skills.summary: Benchmarks the geom(sd) weighted virtual reference gene against the usual (unweighted) geometric mean across increasing numbers of aggregated reference genes (k=2 to 20), quantifying where the weighting advantage disappears. This reproduces the InterOpt finding that geom(sd) is applicable to up to five or six reference genes.

skills.description: Use when you have a raw CT matrix (rows = internal controls, columns = samples) for a chosen reference-gene combination and need per-gene weights that minimize the SD or CV of the weighted mean instead of taking a simple unweighted average.
skills.name: stability-measure-minimization-sd-cv
skills.search_text: stability-measure-minimization-sd-cv Use when you have a raw CT matrix (rows = internal controls, columns = samples) for a chosen reference-gene combination and need per-gene weights that minimize the SD or CV of the weighted mean instead of taking a simple unweighted average. Aggregating more than 5 reference genes with geom(sd): the paper notes it 'does not have the expected benefits compared to the regular geometric mean' at that scale The goal is to select which genes to combine rather than to weight an already-chosen combination — use run_experiment-based combination scanning instead Data are already normalized high-throughput expression values when raw CT values are available for the geom(sd) method, since raw-CT-derived weights avoid gene-independent technical variation http://edamontology.org/topic_3519 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Computes optimal aggregation weights for combining multiple qPCR reference genes into a single virtual reference gene by minimizing the SD or CV of the weighted geometric or arithmetic mean, using the four InterOpt weighting methods (geom(sd), geom(cv), arith(sd), arith(cv)). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.107945
skills.summary: Computes optimal aggregation weights for combining multiple qPCR reference genes into a single virtual reference gene by minimizing the SD or CV of the weighted geometric or arithmetic mean, using the four InterOpt weighting methods (geom(sd), geom(cv), arith(sd), arith(cv)).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Aggregating more than 5 reference genes with geom(sd): the paper notes it 'does not have the expected benefits compared to the regular geometric mean' at that scale The goal is to select which genes to combine rather than to weight an already-chosen combination — use run_experiment-based combination scanning instead Data are already normalized high-throughput expression values when raw CT values are available for the geom(sd) method, since raw-CT-derived weights avoid gene-independent technical variation

skills.description: Use when inferring gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data (.mat with sparse X, ptime, optional regix/branches) where single regression runs are unstable and ensembling with modified Borda aggregation is needed.
skills.name: stability-selection-ensembling
skills.search_text: stability-selection-ensembling Use when inferring gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data (.mat with sparse X, ptime, optional regix/branches) where single regression runs are unstable and ensembling with modified Borda aggregation is needed. The dataset has no meaningful pseudotemporal ordering — the paper notes caveats about poor performance with uninformative pseudotimes. A single-network fit suffices and the ensemble/aggregation overhead (many GLG tests over lambda/kernel-width/lag grids and replicates) is unwarranted for a small dataset. The expression matrix has more than 1000 genes and no sparsity can be tolerated — lambda=0 must be avoided, so a non-sparse regression request is out of scope. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Runs SINGE's ensemble pipeline: many Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) tests over hyperparameter combinations and subsampled pseudotime replicates, then merges the ranked edge lists with a modified Borda count to produce a stable ranked regulator-target network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2022.110333
skills.summary: Runs SINGE's ensemble pipeline: many Generalized Lasso Granger (GLG) tests over hyperparameter combinations and subsampled pseudotime replicates, then merges the ranked edge lists with a modified Borda count to produce a stable ranked regulator-target network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no meaningful pseudotemporal ordering — the paper notes caveats about poor performance with uninformative pseudotimes. A single-network fit suffices and the ensemble/aggregation overhead (many GLG tests over lambda/kernel-width/lag grids and replicates) is unwarranted for a small dataset. The expression matrix has more than 1000 genes and no sparsity can be tolerated — lambda=0 must be avoided, so a non-sparse regression request is out of scope.

skills.description: Use when building a binary RNA-modification (e.g., m5C) predictor from balanced 41-bp sequence datasets where a single RF- or SVM-based model underperforms and ensemble stacking should be benchmarked.
skills.name: stacked-ensemble-model-training
skills.search_text: stacked-ensemble-model-training Use when building a binary RNA-modification (e.g., m5C) predictor from balanced 41-bp sequence datasets where a single RF- or SVM-based model underperforms and ensemble stacking should be benchmarked. Input is already a numeric feature table unrelated to sequence encoding, or the task requires a general cross-species model — the paper notes species-specific models are necessary and cross-species prediction is difficult The query sequences are not 41-bp segments centered on a candidate cytosine, or the target species is neither A. thaliana nor M. musculus (the shipped m5C_predict.py accepts only 'Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse') A simple single-classifier baseline (RF or SVM) is sufficient and the added stacking complexity is not justified by the accuracy comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains a stacked ensemble classifier (Staem5-style) for m5C site prediction by combining base classifiers (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM) with a logistic regression meta-classifier over fused sequence-encoding features, evaluated by 10-fold cross-validation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2021.10.012
skills.summary: Trains a stacked ensemble classifier (Staem5-style) for m5C site prediction by combining base classifiers (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM) with a logistic regression meta-classifier over fused sequence-encoding features, evaluated by 10-fold cross-validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table unrelated to sequence encoding, or the task requires a general cross-species model — the paper notes species-specific models are necessary and cross-species prediction is difficult The query sequences are not 41-bp segments centered on a candidate cytosine, or the target species is neither A. thaliana nor M. musculus (the shipped m5C_predict.py accepts only 'Arabidopsis' or 'Mouse') A simple single-classifier baseline (RF or SVM) is sufficient and the added stacking complexity is not justified by the accuracy comparison

skills.description: Use when a scRNA dataset (Scanpy AnnData) has a gene age class annotation (orthomap) and you need to show which evolutionary age classes drive the global TEI across stages or cell types — e.g. testing whether youngest, species-specific classes peak in early embryos.
skills.name: stacked-evolutionary-profile-visualization
skills.search_text: stacked-evolutionary-profile-visualization Use when a scRNA dataset (Scanpy AnnData) has a gene age class annotation (orthomap) and you need to show which evolutionary age classes drive the global TEI across stages or cell types — e.g. testing whether youngest, species-specific classes peak in early embryos. Input lacks a gene age classification (no orthomap) — the stratification is meaningless without per-gene age classes. Data are bulk transcriptomics or already aggregated to a gene-age-by-condition feature table — use a direct expression-profile plot instead of per-cell TEI stratification. The goal is species-level phylostratigraphy in R (e.g. mypromaps/PhyloStratum workflows) rather than the oggmap/Scanpy Python stack. http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3299 Visualize per-cell/stage contribution of each gene age class to the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) by computing stacked partial TEI strata with oggmap's get_pstrata, so that per-class partial TEI values sum to the global TEI and young age classes' embryonic peaks are directly visible. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad657
skills.summary: Visualize per-cell/stage contribution of each gene age class to the transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI) by computing stacked partial TEI strata with oggmap's get_pstrata, so that per-class partial TEI values sum to the global TEI and young age classes' embryonic peaks are directly visible.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a gene age classification (no orthomap) — the stratification is meaningless without per-gene age classes. Data are bulk transcriptomics or already aggregated to a gene-age-by-condition feature table — use a direct expression-profile plot instead of per-cell TEI stratification. The goal is species-level phylostratigraphy in R (e.g. mypromaps/PhyloStratum workflows) rather than the oggmap/Scanpy Python stack.

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span an ordered trajectory (e.g. iPSC-to-endoderm stages CT1–CT4) and you need to test whether adjacent-stage interindividual correlations of cell type-specific expression effects exceed those between more distant stages.
skills.name: stage-effect-correlation-matrix-analysis
skills.search_text: stage-effect-correlation-matrix-analysis Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span an ordered trajectory (e.g. iPSC-to-endoderm stages CT1–CT4) and you need to test whether adjacent-stage interindividual correlations of cell type-specific expression effects exceed those between more distant stages. Sample sizes below ~50 individuals — the article states CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50 Individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells — ctp/ctnu must be set to missing for such pairs, so the skill is limited to common cell types Cell types expressed as continuous trajectories that cannot be meaningfully discretized into pseudobulk stages, since CTMM assumes discrete cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits the CTMM Full model by REML on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data to partition interindividual covariance between differentiation stages, then converts the partitioned covariance into a stage-by-stage correlation matrix that recapitulates the overall differentiation trajectory. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-49242-9
skills.summary: Fits the CTMM Full model by REML on cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP) data to partition interindividual covariance between differentiation stages, then converts the partitioned covariance into a stage-by-stage correlation matrix that recapitulates the overall differentiation trajectory.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample sizes below ~50 individuals — the article states CTMM is not reliable for sample sizes below ~50 Individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells — ctp/ctnu must be set to missing for such pairs, so the skill is limited to common cell types Cell types expressed as continuous trajectories that cannot be meaningfully discretized into pseudobulk stages, since CTMM assumes discrete cell types

skills.search_text: standalone-platform-execution-with-matched-parameters Use when comparing a local stand-alone small RNA-seq pipeline against a web-based tool on identical FASTQ files and the comparison requires parameters matched to the reference tool for a fair tool-vs-tool evaluation. Data is too large to process locally but the goal is not tool comparison — the article notes web-based tools require uploading original sequencing files, which is unworkable for big data, so a stand-alone run is preferred for big data anyway The goal is microbial (archaea/bacteria/fungi/virus) profiling — that requires the optional Microbe module and BLAST databases (~3.5 hours average runtime), beyond the QC/Alignment/Annotation scope of this skill Only a differential expression analysis is needed on existing count matrices — use the Function module directly instead of re-running QC/Alignment/Annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Execute a stand-alone small RNA-seq platform (COMPSRA v1.0) on local FASTQ inputs with alignment, trimming, and annotation parameters explicitly matched to a comparison pipeline (exceRpt), enabling a fair head-to-head comparison of miRNA detection on 12 serum samples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Execute a stand-alone small RNA-seq platform (COMPSRA v1.0) on local FASTQ inputs with alignment, trimming, and annotation parameters explicitly matched to a comparison pipeline (exceRpt), enabling a fair head-to-head comparison of miRNA detection on 12 serum samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is too large to process locally but the goal is not tool comparison — the article notes web-based tools require uploading original sequencing files, which is unworkable for big data, so a stand-alone run is preferred for big data anyway The goal is microbial (archaea/bacteria/fungi/virus) profiling — that requires the optional Microbe module and BLAST databases (~3.5 hours average runtime), beyond the QC/Alignment/Annotation scope of this skill Only a differential expression analysis is needed on existing count matrices — use the Function module directly instead of re-running QC/Alignment/Annotation

skills.description: Use when a small RNA-seq FASTQ (adapter- and quality-trimmed by COMPSRA QC) must be mapped to hg19/hg38 to enable annotation of miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA and circRNA molecules with COMPSRA.
skills.name: star-alignment-of-short-rna-reads
skills.search_text: star-alignment-of-short-rna-reads Use when a small RNA-seq FASTQ (adapter- and quality-trimmed by COMPSRA QC) must be mapped to hg19/hg38 to enable annotation of miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA and circRNA molecules with COMPSRA. The input is raw small RNA-seq FASTQ that has not been adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered by COMPSRA's QC module (adapter TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG, -rb 4, -rh/-rt/-rr 20). The goal is microbial (archaea/bacteria/fungi/viruses) profiling only — that is the BLAST-based Microbe Module operating on reads that this alignment step could not map to hg19/hg38. The reads are long (>200 nt) transcript reads; COMPSRA/STAR here is configured for short (<200 nt) small RNA local end alignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Align quality-controlled small RNA-seq reads to the hg38 human reference genome with STAR, as the Alignment Module of the COMPSRA platform, producing the BAM file that feeds COMPSRA's Annotation Module and an unmapped-reads file that feeds the Microbe Module. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-61495-0
skills.summary: Align quality-controlled small RNA-seq reads to the hg38 human reference genome with STAR, as the Alignment Module of the COMPSRA platform, producing the BAM file that feeds COMPSRA's Annotation Module and an unmapped-reads file that feeds the Microbe Module.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw small RNA-seq FASTQ that has not been adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered by COMPSRA's QC module (adapter TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG, -rb 4, -rh/-rt/-rr 20). The goal is microbial (archaea/bacteria/fungi/viruses) profiling only — that is the BLAST-based Microbe Module operating on reads that this alignment step could not map to hg19/hg38. The reads are long (>200 nt) transcript reads; COMPSRA/STAR here is configured for short (<200 nt) small RNA local end alignment.

skills.description: Use when you have STAR alignment log files (Log.final.out) from multiple RNA-seq samples and need per-sample or per-group comparison of uniquely mapped, 'too short' unmapped, and chimeric read percentages to diagnose tissue- or condition-specific mapping problems.
skills.name: star-log-metric-extraction
skills.search_text: star-log-metric-extraction Use when you have STAR alignment log files (Log.final.out) from multiple RNA-seq samples and need per-sample or per-group comparison of uniquely mapped, 'too short' unmapped, and chimeric read percentages to diagnose tissue- or condition-specific mapping problems. Input is VCF/genotype data for ASE analysis — use VADT (binomial test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR) rather than STAR log parsing Reads were aligned with a non-STAR aligner whose log schema does not contain the 'too short' unmapped category, so the extracted metrics are not comparable Goal is gene-body coverage bias assessment from BAM files — that requires RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py on the alignments, not STAR log metrics alone http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extracts per-sample alignment quality metrics (uniquely mapped %, unmapped 'too short' %, chimeric %) from STAR two-pass Log.final.out files and compares them across tissue groups, as done for the 68-sample broiler RNA-seq dataset to expose muscle-specific mapping failures. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-83459-8
skills.summary: Extracts per-sample alignment quality metrics (uniquely mapped %, unmapped 'too short' %, chimeric %) from STAR two-pass Log.final.out files and compares them across tissue groups, as done for the 68-sample broiler RNA-seq dataset to expose muscle-specific mapping failures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is VCF/genotype data for ASE analysis — use VADT (binomial test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR) rather than STAR log parsing Reads were aligned with a non-STAR aligner whose log schema does not contain the 'too short' unmapped category, so the extracted metrics are not comparable Goal is gene-body coverage bias assessment from BAM files — that requires RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py on the alignments, not STAR log metrics alone

skills.summary: Aligns single-cell RNA-Seq reads to the mm10 (or other) genome with STAR using permissive multi-mapping parameters (--winAnchorMultimapNmax 100, --outFilterMultimapNmax 100, --outSAMmultNmax 1) so that reads from repetitive transposable elements are retained for locus-level TE quantification by SoloTE instead of being discarded.

skills.search_text: state-transition-topology-comparison Use when a reconstructed cell-state transition network (e.g. Mpath's MDP-CDP-preDC cascade) must be shown robust to clustering or graph-pruning parameter changes before downstream biological interpretation. Development processes that start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support these (planned future extension). Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets in which specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to such data. Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types or FACS-sorted terminal subsets, since Mpath's fate prediction depends on end-stage contrasts. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A sensitivity-analysis skill that tests whether Mpath's landmark clusters and neighborhood-based state transition network remain stable across parameter settings — diversity cuts (0.5, 0.6, 0.7) and dendrogram cut depths yielding 11–13 initial clusters — on the mouse DC progenitor single-cell RNA-seq data set. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/ncomms11988
skills.summary: A sensitivity-analysis skill that tests whether Mpath's landmark clusters and neighborhood-based state transition network remain stable across parameter settings — diversity cuts (0.5, 0.6, 0.7) and dendrogram cut depths yielding 11–13 initial clusters — on the mouse DC progenitor single-cell RNA-seq data set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Development processes that start from multiple independent progenitor cell types — Mpath does not yet support these (planned future extension). Highly heterogeneous single-cell data sets in which specific subset information is unknown — Mpath is not yet extended to such data. Analyses lacking signature genes of differentiated cell types or FACS-sorted terminal subsets, since Mpath's fate prediction depends on end-stage contrasts.

skills.description: Use when you have per-method regulator activity score matrices from multiple inference methods (e.g. decoupleR on transcriptomics or phospho-proteomics benchmarks) and need to quantify whether methods agree.
skills.name: statistical-agreement-reproducibility-checking
skills.search_text: statistical-agreement-reproducibility-checking Use when you have per-method regulator activity score matrices from multiple inference methods (e.g. decoupleR on transcriptomics or phospho-proteomics benchmarks) and need to quantify whether methods agree. The goal is to evaluate predictive accuracy (AUROC/AUPRC) of methods against known perturbations — use the decoupleRBench evaluation pipeline with downsampling instead of agreement statistics. Only a single inference method's activities are available; pairwise Spearman and Jaccard comparisons require at least two methods. Input is raw count data before activity inference — activities must first be computed via the decoupleR 'decouple' wrapper. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces cross-method agreement statistics from the decoupleR benchmarks by computing pairwise Spearman correlations and top-5% Jaccard indexes of inferred regulator activities across the 11 methods, validating against the published medians (Spearman 0.52 transcriptomics / 0.65 phospho-proteomics; Jaccard 0.23 / 0.21). transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbac016
skills.summary: Reproduces cross-method agreement statistics from the decoupleR benchmarks by computing pairwise Spearman correlations and top-5% Jaccard indexes of inferred regulator activities across the 11 methods, validating against the published medians (Spearman 0.52 transcriptomics / 0.65 phospho-proteomics; Jaccard 0.23 / 0.21).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate predictive accuracy (AUROC/AUPRC) of methods against known perturbations — use the decoupleRBench evaluation pipeline with downsampling instead of agreement statistics. Only a single inference method's activities are available; pairwise Spearman and Jaccard comparisons require at least two methods. Input is raw count data before activity inference — activities must first be computed via the decoupleR 'decouple' wrapper.

skills.description: Use when a per-cell uncertainty or score distribution (e.g. scEMAIL E-scores from entropy, confidence, consistency) must be tested for unimodality vs. bimodality to make a binary presence/absence decision about novel cell types.
skills.name: statistical-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: statistical-distribution-analysis Use when a per-cell uncertainty or score distribution (e.g. scEMAIL E-scores from entropy, confidence, consistency) must be tested for unimodality vs. bimodality to make a binary presence/absence decision about novel cell types. The target data are already labeled with known cell types and no novel-type detection is required (plain annotation under the closed setting suffices). You only have raw scRNA-seq counts without the pre-computed E-score uncertainty values — the expert ensemble (entropy, confidence, consistency) must be computed first. You need to partition cells into known/unknown groups after novelty is confirmed — that requires the subsequent adaptive manifold-mixup threshold step, not just the bimodality tests. Applies distribution-shape statistics — the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test — to an empirical uncertainty distribution (the scEMAIL expert ensemble E-score) to decide whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2022.12.008
skills.summary: Applies distribution-shape statistics — the bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test — to an empirical uncertainty distribution (the scEMAIL expert ensemble E-score) to decide whether novel cell types are present in target scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target data are already labeled with known cell types and no novel-type detection is required (plain annotation under the closed setting suffices). You only have raw scRNA-seq counts without the pre-computed E-score uncertainty values — the expert ensemble (entropy, confidence, consistency) must be computed first. You need to partition cells into known/unknown groups after novelty is confirmed — that requires the subsequent adaptive manifold-mixup threshold step, not just the bimodality tests.

skills.description: Use when you need to find simulation parameters that reproduce the statistical properties (gene CV/mean distributions, zero fraction, SD) of a real scRNA-seq dataset, for either UMI or non-UMI protocols.
skills.name: statistical-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: statistical-distribution-fitting Use when you need to find simulation parameters that reproduce the statistical properties (gene CV/mean distributions, zero fraction, SD) of a real scRNA-seq dataset, for either UMI or non-UMI protocols. The goal is forward simulation with known mechanistic parameters (use SimulateTrueCounts/True2ObservedCounts directly) rather than fitting parameters to an existing real dataset The input dataset is small and non-UMI such that generative-model alternatives are required; note scVI is only applicable to large datasets in the article's imputation context You need kinetic parameter estimation via MCMC (kon, koff, s with RJAGS Gibbs sampling, 2000 iterations) rather than grid-based best-match search http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit simulation parameters to real scRNA-seq data by grid-searching a database of SymSim-simulated datasets and matching statistical distributions (gene mean, CV, percent non-zero, SD), then validating the fit with Q-Q plots against identity lines and comparing against Splatter and powsimR fits. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-10500-w
skills.summary: Fit simulation parameters to real scRNA-seq data by grid-searching a database of SymSim-simulated datasets and matching statistical distributions (gene mean, CV, percent non-zero, SD), then validating the fit with Q-Q plots against identity lines and comparing against Splatter and powsimR fits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is forward simulation with known mechanistic parameters (use SimulateTrueCounts/True2ObservedCounts directly) rather than fitting parameters to an existing real dataset The input dataset is small and non-UMI such that generative-model alternatives are required; note scVI is only applicable to large datasets in the article's imputation context You need kinetic parameter estimation via MCMC (kon, koff, s with RJAGS Gibbs sampling, 2000 iterations) rather than grid-based best-match search

skills.description: Use when cross-replicate or cross-dataset scRNAseq clusters must be matched: after assess.cluster.similarity computes FC-vector correlations, to discard non-reproducible cluster pairs before building a meta-cluster map.
skills.name: statistical-filtering-of-cluster-pairs
skills.search_text: statistical-filtering-of-cluster-pairs Use when cross-replicate or cross-dataset scRNAseq clusters must be matched: after assess.cluster.similarity computes FC-vector correlations, to discard non-reproducible cluster pairs before building a meta-cluster map. Datasets have not yet been individually clustered and summarized — filtering requires precomputed per-dataset cluster analyses loaded via read.preclustered.datasets Only one replicate/dataset is available — cross-replicate correlation robustness cannot be assessed, so the min.sd threshold is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A robustSingleCell step that filters pairwise cross-dataset cluster similarities so only statistically robust, reproducible cluster matches are retained, using fold-change (FC) vector Pearson correlations across replicates and significance thresholds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.celrep.2019.10.131
skills.summary: A robustSingleCell step that filters pairwise cross-dataset cluster similarities so only statistically robust, reproducible cluster matches are retained, using fold-change (FC) vector Pearson correlations across replicates and significance thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Datasets have not yet been individually clustered and summarized — filtering requires precomputed per-dataset cluster analyses loaded via read.preclustered.datasets Only one replicate/dataset is available — cross-replicate correlation robustness cannot be assessed, so the min.sd threshold is undefined

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores and you need to flag and remove a quiescent/G0-like cell group (no prior algorithm existed for G0-like detection) before pseudotime reconstruction.
skills.name: statistical-hypothesis-testing-for-cluster-annotation
skills.search_text: statistical-hypothesis-testing-for-cluster-annotation Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores and you need to flag and remove a quiescent/G0-like cell group (no prior algorithm existed for G0-like detection) before pseudotime reconstruction. No cell-cycle scores are available and reCAT has not been run — the ANOVA test requires the six mean cell-cycle phase scores as input. You want to remove cell-cycle effects by simply dropping cycling genes (the traditional trajectory-inference route) rather than identifying quiescent G0-like cells. The dataset is not expected to contain a quiescent subpopulation and removing cells would distort the lineage being reconstructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A redPATH procedure that annotates a cell-cycle k-means cluster as G0-like (quiescent) by testing whether it is significantly lowest across all six mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) using pairwise ANOVA at P < 0.001, enabling removal of quiescent cells (89 removed in the Llorens NSC dataset) before trajectory inference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.06.014
skills.summary: A redPATH procedure that annotates a cell-cycle k-means cluster as G0-like (quiescent) by testing whether it is significantly lowest across all six mean cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) using pairwise ANOVA at P < 0.001, enabling removal of quiescent cells (89 removed in the Llorens NSC dataset) before trajectory inference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No cell-cycle scores are available and reCAT has not been run — the ANOVA test requires the six mean cell-cycle phase scores as input. You want to remove cell-cycle effects by simply dropping cycling genes (the traditional trajectory-inference route) rather than identifying quiescent G0-like cells. The dataset is not expected to contain a quiescent subpopulation and removing cells would distort the lineage being reconstructed.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether regression-based (linear + interaction term) differential gene–gene links are also recoverable by a non-linear dependence measure such as k-NN mutual information, on matched subgroup data.
skills.name: statistical-link-concordance-comparison
skills.search_text: statistical-link-concordance-comparison Use when you need to test whether regression-based (linear + interaction term) differential gene–gene links are also recoverable by a non-linear dependence measure such as k-NN mutual information, on matched subgroup data. The goal is only DEGGs' own linear-model output (regression with interaction term) and no non-linear comparison is wanted — the MI step adds no value Expression data has only one phenotype group or no subgroup_variable to stratify, so differential co-expression between subgroups cannot be defined Input data are not normalised counts compatible with generate_subnetworks' expected count/design matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3360 Benchmarks DEGGs' linear-model differential co-expression calls against a non-linear association test (mutual information) on the same gene–gene links from the TCGA-BRCA subnetworks, quantifying which links each statistical framework detects. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad192
skills.summary: Benchmarks DEGGs' linear-model differential co-expression calls against a non-linear association test (mutual information) on the same gene–gene links from the TCGA-BRCA subnetworks, quantifying which links each statistical framework detects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only DEGGs' own linear-model output (regression with interaction term) and no non-linear comparison is wanted — the MI step adds no value Expression data has only one phenotype group or no subgroup_variable to stratify, so differential co-expression between subgroups cannot be defined Input data are not normalised counts compatible with generate_subnetworks' expected count/design matrices

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether enlarging the class of discoverable meta-markers (higher-order gene interactions, k>=2) yields more significant patterns than single/low-order miners under the same FWER criterion.
skills.name: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods Use when you need to quantify whether enlarging the class of discoverable meta-markers (higher-order gene interactions, k>=2) yields more significant patterns than single/low-order miners under the same FWER criterion. Your goal is discovery on a single real dataset rather than a controlled power comparison against baselines — the benchmark design requires synthetic data with known association strength rho. Your marker data are additive-encoded (e.g. 0/1/2 dosages) for the FastCMH baseline: FastCMH expects L rows x n columns of strictly binary 0/1 features, so only the binary-encoded arm of the comparison is valid there. You cannot guarantee an identical FWER criterion across methods — comparing raw pattern counts when one method uses a default other than FWER 0.05 (SiNIMin default 0.05) invalidates the power comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks the statistical power of HOGImine (k>=2 higher-order genetic interaction mining) against SiNIMin and FastCMH by counting significant genetic meta-markers under FWER control at alpha=0.05 across a range of association strengths rho on synthetic binary-encoded genotype data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Benchmarks the statistical power of HOGImine (k>=2 higher-order genetic interaction mining) against SiNIMin and FastCMH by counting significant genetic meta-markers under FWER control at alpha=0.05 across a range of association strengths rho on synthetic binary-encoded genotype data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is discovery on a single real dataset rather than a controlled power comparison against baselines — the benchmark design requires synthetic data with known association strength rho. Your marker data are additive-encoded (e.g. 0/1/2 dosages) for the FastCMH baseline: FastCMH expects L rows x n columns of strictly binary 0/1 features, so only the binary-encoded arm of the comparison is valid there. You cannot guarantee an identical FWER criterion across methods — comparing raw pattern counts when one method uses a default other than FWER 0.05 (SiNIMin default 0.05) invalidates the power comparison.

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify whether modeling replicates confers robustness against a single outlier sample versus pooling counts, by tracing detection power as sample size increases under simulated data.
skills.name: statistical-power-curve-comparison
skills.search_text: statistical-power-curve-comparison Use when you need to quantify whether modeling replicates confers robustness against a single outlier sample versus pooling counts, by tracing detection power as sample size increases under simulated data. The goal is real-data ASAS detection from aligned RNA-seq reads rather than a controlled simulation benchmark — use the full PAIRADISE pipeline (personalization, mapping, counting) instead of the simulation harness. There are no replicates and no outlier concern; a single-sample allelic test suffices and the pooled comparison adds no information. The comparison method must handle overdispersion rather than the specific replicate-versus-pooling robustness question; Fisher's pooled test is only the paper's naive baseline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Benchmark the statistical power of a replicate-aware model (PAIRADISE) against a naive read-pooling alternative (Fisher's exact test on pooled reads) across increasing replicate numbers under an injected-outlier simulation, producing a power-versus-sample-size comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.07.005
skills.summary: Benchmark the statistical power of a replicate-aware model (PAIRADISE) against a naive read-pooling alternative (Fisher's exact test on pooled reads) across increasing replicate numbers under an injected-outlier simulation, producing a power-versus-sample-size comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is real-data ASAS detection from aligned RNA-seq reads rather than a controlled simulation benchmark — use the full PAIRADISE pipeline (personalization, mapping, counting) instead of the simulation harness. There are no replicates and no outlier concern; a single-sample allelic test suffices and the pooled comparison adds no information. The comparison method must handle overdispersion rather than the specific replicate-versus-pooling robustness question; Fisher's pooled test is only the paper's naive baseline.

skills.description: Use when a paper reports a significance p-value (e.g. Wilcoxon p = 1.2e-7) comparing score distributions over a labeled table, and you have the score table to verify it.
skills.name: statistical-pvalue-reproduction-from-score-tables
skills.search_text: statistical-pvalue-reproduction-from-score-tables Use when a paper reports a significance p-value (e.g. Wilcoxon p = 1.2e-7) comparing score distributions over a labeled table, and you have the score table to verify it. The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than a table of already-computed prediction scores — use the full TSNAD pipeline instead. The published statistic is paired or parametric (e.g. paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, t-test) rather than a rank-sum comparison of two labeled groups. The score table lacks ground-truth immunogenicity labels, so no two-group split for the rank-sum test can be defined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces published p-values by re-running Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on tabulated prediction scores split by ground-truth labels — here, TSNAD v2.0/DeepHLApan immunogenicity scores on 608 TESLA pMHC pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.016
skills.summary: Reproduces published p-values by re-running Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on tabulated prediction scores split by ground-truth labels — here, TSNAD v2.0/DeepHLApan immunogenicity scores on 608 TESLA pMHC pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than a table of already-computed prediction scores — use the full TSNAD pipeline instead. The published statistic is paired or parametric (e.g. paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, t-test) rather than a rank-sum comparison of two labeled groups. The score table lacks ground-truth immunogenicity labels, so no two-group split for the rank-sum test can be defined.

skills.description: Use when you have a per-dataset performance metric matrix (e.g., ARI) for a proposed method plus baselines over a fixed benchmark and must produce a paired significance-test table.
skills.name: statistical-results-table-generation
skills.search_text: statistical-results-table-generation Use when you have a per-dataset performance metric matrix (e.g., ARI) for a proposed method plus baselines over a fixed benchmark and must produce a paired significance-test table. The score matrix is incomplete — any missing ARI values per dataset break the paired test design across the same 15 datasets. You need unpaired or independent-sample testing; the benchmark uses matched datasets per method, so paired=TRUE is required. The comparison vectors come from a single method's output rather than a method-vs-method benchmark matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generates a consolidated statistical significance table by running paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests in R comparing CASCC's ARI scores against six baseline clustering methods (CIDR, RaceID3, SC3, Seurat V4, SIMLR, TSCAN) across the 15-dataset benchmark, mirroring the paper's Supplementary Table S4. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae283
skills.summary: Generates a consolidated statistical significance table by running paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests in R comparing CASCC's ARI scores against six baseline clustering methods (CIDR, RaceID3, SC3, Seurat V4, SIMLR, TSCAN) across the 15-dataset benchmark, mirroring the paper's Supplementary Table S4.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The score matrix is incomplete — any missing ARI values per dataset break the paired test design across the same 15 datasets. You need unpaired or independent-sample testing; the benchmark uses matched datasets per method, so paired=TRUE is required. The comparison vectors come from a single method's output rather than a method-vs-method benchmark matrix.

skills.description: Use when a new differential abundance method must be validated against established competitors on shared single-cell datasets, requiring comparable per-cell-type DA statistics and captured-cell-fraction metrics.
skills.name: statistical-significance-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: statistical-significance-comparison-across-methods Use when a new differential abundance method must be validated against established competitors on shared single-cell datasets, requiring comparable per-cell-type DA statistics and captured-cell-fraction metrics. When the goal is a single method's DA calls on one dataset without a head-to-head benchmark — no comparison baseline exists When datasets are not identically preprocessed across methods, since preprocessing differences would confound the significance comparison When the competitor of interest is miloDE — the authors explicitly did not benchmark against it and flag this as an open question http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Benchmark a new DA-testing method (e.g. ELVAR) head-to-head against clustering-free competitors (DA-seq, Milo) by running all methods on the same scRNA-Seq datasets and comparing DA z-statistic distributions and the fraction of condition-enriched cells captured, as done for aging, Covid-19 and colon cancer benchmarks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-39017-z
skills.summary: Benchmark a new DA-testing method (e.g. ELVAR) head-to-head against clustering-free competitors (DA-seq, Milo) by running all methods on the same scRNA-Seq datasets and comparing DA z-statistic distributions and the fraction of condition-enriched cells captured, as done for aging, Covid-19 and colon cancer benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single method's DA calls on one dataset without a head-to-head benchmark — no comparison baseline exists When datasets are not identically preprocessed across methods, since preprocessing differences would confound the significance comparison When the competitor of interest is miloDE — the authors explicitly did not benchmark against it and flag this as an open question

skills.description: Use when comparing method performance across multiple scRNA-seq benchmark datasets and you must show the winner's advantage is statistically significant, e.g. via one-sided Wilcoxon tests on per-dataset scores.
skills.name: statistical-significance-testing
skills.search_text: statistical-significance-testing Use when comparing method performance across multiple scRNA-seq benchmark datasets and you must show the winner's advantage is statistically significant, e.g. via one-sided Wilcoxon tests on per-dataset scores. Scores are unpaired (different datasets per method) — a paired Wilcoxon test would be invalid The evaluation goal is ranking embeddings visually rather than testing statistical significance of a score difference http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Apply one-sided paired significance tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and clustering-quality metrics (adjusted Rand index, silhouette index) to statistically validate that scDHA outperforms competing methods across benchmark scRNA-seq datasets. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21312-2
skills.summary: Apply one-sided paired significance tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and clustering-quality metrics (adjusted Rand index, silhouette index) to statistically validate that scDHA outperforms competing methods across benchmark scRNA-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Scores are unpaired (different datasets per method) — a paired Wilcoxon test would be invalid The evaluation goal is ranking embeddings visually rather than testing statistical significance of a score difference

skills.description: Use when comparing a proposed method's averaged detection/classification metrics (e.g. AUROC at C^novel=1-4) against baseline methods across benchmark datasets and you need to confirm the improvement is significant, not noise.
skills.name: statistical-significance-testing-ttest
skills.search_text: statistical-significance-testing-ttest Use when comparing a proposed method's averaged detection/classification metrics (e.g. AUROC at C^novel=1-4) against baseline methods across benchmark datasets and you need to confirm the improvement is significant, not noise. When you only have a single aggregated score per method with no per-dataset replicates — a t-test requires per-dataset metric vectors to test against When the goal is two-sided comparison of arbitrary methods rather than the one-tailed hypothesis that scNovel's novel rare cell detection advantage is real http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Runs a one-tailed t-test over per-dataset averaged performance metrics (AUROC, AUPR, FPR95) to assess whether scNovel's novel rare cell detection advantage over scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred and scLearn is statistically significant. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae112
skills.summary: Runs a one-tailed t-test over per-dataset averaged performance metrics (AUROC, AUPR, FPR95) to assess whether scNovel's novel rare cell detection advantage over scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, scPred and scLearn is statistically significant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only have a single aggregated score per method with no per-dataset replicates — a t-test requires per-dataset metric vectors to test against When the goal is two-sided comparison of arbitrary methods rather than the one-tailed hypothesis that scNovel's novel rare cell detection advantage is real

skills.description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, clustered scRNA-seq object (e.g., PBMC3k with Louvain labels) needs per-cluster marker genes ranked by log2 fold-change against all remaining cells.
skills.name: statistical-testing-with-wilcoxon-mast-deseq2
skills.search_text: statistical-testing-with-wilcoxon-mast-deseq2 Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, clustered scRNA-seq object (e.g., PBMC3k with Louvain labels) needs per-cluster marker genes ranked by log2 fold-change against all remaining cells. The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — the article states 'the analysis of only human and mouse datasets is currently supported' The dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA web server — users are advised to use the desktop version as some steps cannot be completed online The input already is a ranked marker table or lacks a normalized expression matrix and cluster labels — one-vs-rest differential testing cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies marker genes characterizing each Louvain cluster of a scRNA-seq dataset by testing each cluster's cells against all remaining cells using the Wilcoxon rank sum test (with MAST and DESeq2 as alternatives) as implemented in SCALA via Seurat, as demonstrated on the PBMC3k dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.10.032
skills.summary: Identifies marker genes characterizing each Louvain cluster of a scRNA-seq dataset by testing each cluster's cells against all remaining cells using the Wilcoxon rank sum test (with MAST and DESeq2 as alternatives) as implemented in SCALA via Seurat, as demonstrated on the PBMC3k dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is from an organism other than human or mouse — the article states 'the analysis of only human and mouse datasets is currently supported' The dataset exceeds 50,000 cells on the online SCALA web server — users are advised to use the desktop version as some steps cannot be completed online The input already is a ranked marker table or lacks a normalized expression matrix and cluster labels — one-vs-rest differential testing cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when a RiboSeq pipeline has produced normalized count matrices (e.g. HTSeq-count count_matrix_by_transcript_IDs.csv) and you must define significance cutoffs (p-val, logFC) to accept/reject differential expression calls against a reference condition.
skills.name: statistical-threshold-filtering-gene-expression
skills.search_text: statistical-threshold-filtering-gene-expression Use when a RiboSeq pipeline has produced normalized count matrices (e.g. HTSeq-count count_matrix_by_transcript_IDs.csv) and you must define significance cutoffs (p-val, logFC) to accept/reject differential expression calls against a reference condition. Input is raw FastQ reads or untrimmed alignments — the DESeq2 statistical step requires the HTSeq-count matrix that only exists after trimming (Cutadapt), contaminant removal (Bowtie2), alignment (Hisat2/Bowtie2) and counting upstream. The goal is P-site offset estimation or periodicity QC rather than differential expression calling — use the riboWaltz/TRiP module instead. Sample replicates have already been flagged as low-quality and removed; RiboDoc should be rerun first with only the required recalculated steps before re-thresholding results. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Calls differentially expressed genes or transcripts in RiboDoc's quantitative module by applying user-configured p-value (p-val, e.g. 0.01) and log2FoldChange (logFC, e.g. 0) thresholds to DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test results computed on ribosome-profiling count matrices. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.014
skills.summary: Calls differentially expressed genes or transcripts in RiboDoc's quantitative module by applying user-configured p-value (p-val, e.g. 0.01) and log2FoldChange (logFC, e.g. 0) thresholds to DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test results computed on ribosome-profiling count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FastQ reads or untrimmed alignments — the DESeq2 statistical step requires the HTSeq-count matrix that only exists after trimming (Cutadapt), contaminant removal (Bowtie2), alignment (Hisat2/Bowtie2) and counting upstream. The goal is P-site offset estimation or periodicity QC rather than differential expression calling — use the riboWaltz/TRiP module instead. Sample replicates have already been flagged as low-quality and removed; RiboDoc should be rerun first with only the required recalculated steps before re-thresholding results.

skills.description: Use when you have gene differential-expression P-values (seed genes) plus a reference interactome and need a minimal connected subnetwork capturing perturbed condition-specific signal for downstream enrichment scoring.
skills.name: steiner-tree-backbone-extraction
skills.search_text: steiner-tree-backbone-extraction Use when you have gene differential-expression P-values (seed genes) plus a reference interactome and need a minimal connected subnetwork capturing perturbed condition-specific signal for downstream enrichment scoring. When the network is already DAG-structured and you need directed causal paths or ACE estimation rather than an undirected minimal connecting subtree (use SEMace/SEMpath instead) When seeds are a small curated gene list with no quantitative P-values available for edge weighting When the goal is classification/scoring of samples rather than perturbation extraction — other SEMtree() methods may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Extracts a minimal perturbed backbone subnetwork via Kou's Steiner tree algorithm, connecting all seed (disease) genes at minimum edge cost on a group-difference-weighted KEGG interactome, as implemented by SEMtree() with type='ST' in the SEMgraph R package. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Extracts a minimal perturbed backbone subnetwork via Kou's Steiner tree algorithm, connecting all seed (disease) genes at minimum edge cost on a group-difference-weighted KEGG interactome, as implemented by SEMtree() with type='ST' in the SEMgraph R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the network is already DAG-structured and you need directed causal paths or ACE estimation rather than an undirected minimal connecting subtree (use SEMace/SEMpath instead) When seeds are a small curated gene list with no quantitative P-values available for edge weighting When the goal is classification/scoring of samples rather than perturbation extraction — other SEMtree() methods may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when you have seed/disease genes plus group-labeled RNA-seq data and need a data-driven directed subnetwork whose significant causal paths (Bonferroni-corrected ACE testing) explain disease perturbation.
skills.name: steiner-tree-subnetwork-analysis
skills.search_text: steiner-tree-subnetwork-analysis Use when you have seed/disease genes plus group-labeled RNA-seq data and need a data-driven directed subnetwork whose significant causal paths (Bonferroni-corrected ACE testing) explain disease perturbation. Input is a raw count matrix without group labels or seed genes — Steiner terminals cannot be defined and SEMace source2sink effects are not estimable The goal is whole-interactome structure learning rather than extracting a perturbed backbone around seed genes (SEMtree offers TAHC, EBC, WTC and DAG-based alternatives) Only undirected perturbation modules are needed without causal direction — the five active subnetwork detection methods output undirected edges and the Chu–Liu–Edmonds tree conversion step is what adds directionality http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Extract a perturbed backbone subnetwork as a Steiner tree (Kou's algorithm) from a weighted interactome using SEMtree(), then interrogate it with SEMace, SEMpath and SEMrun to find significant source-to-sink perturbation paths (e.g., ATG16L1 -> CCR5, 14 nodes/13 edges) in the GSE172114 COVID-19 dataset. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad377
skills.summary: Extract a perturbed backbone subnetwork as a Steiner tree (Kou's algorithm) from a weighted interactome using SEMtree(), then interrogate it with SEMace, SEMpath and SEMrun to find significant source-to-sink perturbation paths (e.g., ATG16L1 -> CCR5, 14 nodes/13 edges) in the GSE172114 COVID-19 dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw count matrix without group labels or seed genes — Steiner terminals cannot be defined and SEMace source2sink effects are not estimable The goal is whole-interactome structure learning rather than extracting a perturbed backbone around seed genes (SEMtree offers TAHC, EBC, WTC and DAG-based alternatives) Only undirected perturbation modules are needed without causal direction — the five active subnetwork detection methods output undirected edges and the Chu–Liu–Edmonds tree conversion step is what adds directionality

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type annotations and must verify that stemness/pluripotency scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) rank expected stem/progenitor types highly.
skills.name: stemness-score-benchmark-verification
skills.search_text: stemness-score-benchmark-verification Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type annotations and must verify that stemness/pluripotency scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) rank expected stem/progenitor types highly. Input is not a gene-by-cell expression matrix (e.g. already aggregated to a feature table or pseudobulk), since activity() requires each row as a gene and each column as a cell The goal is to compute PPIN activity for biological processes other than differentiation — use the extended ORIGINS2 package instead Data are not human single-cell samples; the differentiation PPIN and benchmarks (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383) are human-specific http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Verifies pluripotency/stemness scoring pipelines (ORIGINS differentiation activity, LandSCENT Signal Rank, CytoTRACE) on scRNA-seq data by reproducing per-cell-type mean score rankings, including the known failure case of HVF-derived ORIGINS activity networks. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.mex.2022.101778
skills.summary: Verifies pluripotency/stemness scoring pipelines (ORIGINS differentiation activity, LandSCENT Signal Rank, CytoTRACE) on scRNA-seq data by reproducing per-cell-type mean score rankings, including the known failure case of HVF-derived ORIGINS activity networks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a gene-by-cell expression matrix (e.g. already aggregated to a feature table or pseudobulk), since activity() requires each row as a gene and each column as a cell The goal is to compute PPIN activity for biological processes other than differentiation — use the extended ORIGINS2 package instead Data are not human single-cell samples; the differentiation PPIN and benchmarks (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383) are human-specific

skills.description: Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers) has a priori class labels (e.g., time points day0–day5) and you need to automatically tune the feature set input to LDA for visualization instead of manually picking markers.
skills.name: stepwise-feature-selection
skills.search_text: stepwise-feature-selection Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers) has a priori class labels (e.g., time points day0–day5) and you need to automatically tune the feature set input to LDA for visualization instead of manually picking markers. Labels are unknown, or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — HSS-LDA is a supervised approach Data has more than 100 dimensions, where HSS is not feasible A large degree of heterogeneity exists within a given class (e.g., PBMCs labeled by time point) or the number of populations is large — performance suffers http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Hybrid subset selection (HSS) combines forward and reverse stepwise selection to automatically identify a marker subset whose separation scores maximize class separation for LDA-based supervised dimensionality reduction of single-cell data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100536
skills.summary: Hybrid subset selection (HSS) combines forward and reverse stepwise selection to automatically identify a marker subset whose separation scores maximize class separation for LDA-based supervised dimensionality reduction of single-cell data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Labels are unknown, or an unbiased view of the data is preferable — HSS-LDA is a supervised approach Data has more than 100 dimensions, where HSS is not feasible A large degree of heterogeneity exists within a given class (e.g., PBMCs labeled by time point) or the number of populations is large — performance suffers

skills.description: Use when you have a computed GGC matrix from normalized scRNA-seq data and need a minimally redundant seed feature set for DUBStepR-style guilt-by-association feature expansion.
skills.name: stepwise-regression-gene-selection
skills.search_text: stepwise-regression-gene-selection Use when you have a computed GGC matrix from normalized scRNA-seq data and need a minimally redundant seed feature set for DUBStepR-style guilt-by-association feature expansion. The GGC matrix has not yet been computed — run the correlation-range z-score gene filtering (getCorrelationRange/getFilteredData) and getGGC() steps first You only need the final optimal feature set rather than the minimally redundant seed core — use getOptimalFeatureSet(), which expands the seed via guilt-by-association Input is raw counts without QC, normalization (logNormalize), or gene filtering — the stepwise regression assumes a filtered, normalized expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Runs DUBStepR's stepwise regression on a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix to iteratively regress out the gene explaining maximal residual variance, yielding an ordered, minimally redundant seed gene set whose size is set by the elbow point of the stepwise-regression scree plot. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: Runs DUBStepR's stepwise regression on a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix to iteratively regress out the gene explaining maximal residual variance, yielding an ordered, minimally redundant seed gene set whose size is set by the elbow point of the stepwise-regression scree plot.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The GGC matrix has not yet been computed — run the correlation-range z-score gene filtering (getCorrelationRange/getFilteredData) and getGGC() steps first You only need the final optimal feature set rather than the minimally redundant seed core — use getOptimalFeatureSet(), which expands the seed via guilt-by-association Input is raw counts without QC, normalization (logNormalize), or gene filtering — the stepwise regression assumes a filtered, normalized expression matrix

skills.description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data and you need a non-redundant seed set of well-correlated, cell-type-specific marker genes to drive feature selection (e.g., on a log-normalized 10X PBMC matrix in Seurat).
skills.name: stepwise-regression-seed-feature-identification
skills.search_text: stepwise-regression-seed-feature-identification Use when clustering scRNA-seq data and you need a non-redundant seed set of well-correlated, cell-type-specific marker genes to drive feature selection (e.g., on a log-normalized 10X PBMC matrix in Seurat). Input is already a curated feature/marker table — the stepwise regression assumes a full gene-by-cell expression matrix from which correlations are computed Genes have not been pre-filtered for mitochondrial, ribosomal, spike-in, and pseudogene content, which DUBStepR expects removed before GGC construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 DUBStepR's stepwise regression identifies a minimally redundant core seed feature set from a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix, after filtering genes by correlation range z-score; the seed set is then expanded by guilt-by-association and sized optimally via the Density Index. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26085-2
skills.summary: DUBStepR's stepwise regression identifies a minimally redundant core seed feature set from a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix, after filtering genes by correlation range z-score; the seed set is then expanded by guilt-by-association and sized optimally via the Density Index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated feature/marker table — the stepwise regression assumes a full gene-by-cell expression matrix from which correlations are computed Genes have not been pre-filtered for mitochondrial, ribosomal, spike-in, and pseudogene content, which DUBStepR expects removed before GGC construction

skills.description: Use when processing a SAW-generated unmapped FASTQ from a Stereo-seq sample to recover expressed lineage barcodes per spatial spot and map the spatial territories of abundant clones.
skills.name: stereoseq-spatial-barcode-extraction
skills.search_text: stereoseq-spatial-barcode-extraction Use when processing a SAW-generated unmapped FASTQ from a Stereo-seq sample to recover expressed lineage barcodes per spatial spot and map the spatial territories of abundant clones. Input is a standard population-level barcode amplicon FASTQ rather than spatial data — use the BARtab bulk workflow instead Input FASTQ is not the SAW unmapped read set (e.g. genome-mapped BAM with no barcode reads) and lacks the flanking constant regions needed for cutadapt constants=all trimming Barcodes are evolving/naturally variable barcodes that need lineage reconstruction (e.g. CRISPR barcodes handled by Cassiopeia or LinRace) rather than fixed synthetic barcodes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extracts and annotates SPLINTR synthetic lineage barcodes from Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics data produced by the SAW pipeline, using the BARtab Nextflow single-cell workflow to generate per-spot barcode counts and spatial clone-territory annotations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.crmeth.2024.100763
skills.summary: Extracts and annotates SPLINTR synthetic lineage barcodes from Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics data produced by the SAW pipeline, using the BARtab Nextflow single-cell workflow to generate per-spot barcode counts and spatial clone-territory annotations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a standard population-level barcode amplicon FASTQ rather than spatial data — use the BARtab bulk workflow instead Input FASTQ is not the SAW unmapped read set (e.g. genome-mapped BAM with no barcode reads) and lacks the flanking constant regions needed for cutadapt constants=all trimming Barcodes are evolving/naturally variable barcodes that need lineage reconstruction (e.g. CRISPR barcodes handled by Cassiopeia or LinRace) rather than fixed synthetic barcodes

skills.description: Use when raw nanopore dRNA signals (fast5/pod5 chunks, e.g. 3000-sample chunks, pA scale) must be preprocessed into spectrogram-like inputs for a speech-to-text-style transformer that calls canonical and modified bases.
skills.name: stft-spectrogram-conversion-of-ionic-currents
