skills.search_text: stft-spectrogram-conversion-of-ionic-currents Use when raw nanopore dRNA signals (fast5/pod5 chunks, e.g. 3000-sample chunks, pA scale) must be preprocessed into spectrogram-like inputs for a speech-to-text-style transformer that calls canonical and modified bases. Data are already basecalled reads (fasta/fastq/BAM) rather than raw current signals — re-squiggling or modification-detection post-processing (e.g. ModiKit) is the appropriate path instead Working with latest ONT chemistry reads for which ONT's Dorado modification-aware basecaller is available and supported Signal chunks are truncated or unpadded in a way inconsistent with the chunk length the model was trained on Converts padded picoampere-scale ionic current chunks from ONT direct RNA reads into time-frequency spectrograms via STFT so a transformer basecaller (NanoSpeech) can consume them like audio features for kmer basecalling over an expanded nucleotide vocabulary. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbaf709
skills.summary: Converts padded picoampere-scale ionic current chunks from ONT direct RNA reads into time-frequency spectrograms via STFT so a transformer basecaller (NanoSpeech) can consume them like audio features for kmer basecalling over an expanded nucleotide vocabulary.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already basecalled reads (fasta/fastq/BAM) rather than raw current signals — re-squiggling or modification-detection post-processing (e.g. ModiKit) is the appropriate path instead Working with latest ONT chemistry reads for which ONT's Dorado modification-aware basecaller is available and supported Signal chunks are truncated or unpadded in a way inconsistent with the chunk length the model was trained on

skills.description: Use when multiple transcriptomic conditions from one cell type under distinct stimuli/blocking treatments must be compared for ligand-receptor communication amplitude against a common reference panel.
skills.name: stimulus-condition-comparative-analysis
skills.search_text: stimulus-condition-comparative-analysis Use when multiple transcriptomic conditions from one cell type under distinct stimuli/blocking treatments must be compared for ligand-receptor communication amplitude against a common reference panel. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple populations in the same sample rather than bulk/stimulus-condition transcriptomes — use the ICELLNET scRNAseq tutorial workflow instead The goal is inference of downstream signaling effectors rather than ligand-receptor communication, since ICELLNET explicitly does not integrate downstream effectors Non-human transcriptomic data, since the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compares ICELLNET-derived cell-cell communication scores across stimulus perturbation conditions (e.g., Medium, LPS, LPS+aTNFR, LPS+aIL-10R on monocyte-derived dendritic cells) to identify which autocrine loop controls communication amplitude with partner cell types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21244-x
skills.summary: Compares ICELLNET-derived cell-cell communication scores across stimulus perturbation conditions (e.g., Medium, LPS, LPS+aTNFR, LPS+aIL-10R on monocyte-derived dendritic cells) to identify which autocrine loop controls communication amplitude with partner cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple populations in the same sample rather than bulk/stimulus-condition transcriptomes — use the ICELLNET scRNAseq tutorial workflow instead The goal is inference of downstream signaling effectors rather than ligand-receptor communication, since ICELLNET explicitly does not integrate downstream effectors Non-human transcriptomic data, since the ICELLNET ligand-receptor database is curated exclusively from human studies

skills.description: Use when evaluating a DNA storage pipeline design under simulated synthesis/sequencing noise: you need per-oligo copy counts and error draws (substitutions, deletions, decode failures) parameterized by a JSON fault configuration before decoding.
skills.name: stochastic-copy-and-error-model-sampling
skills.search_text: stochastic-copy-and-error-model-sampling Use when evaluating a DNA storage pipeline design under simulated synthesis/sequencing noise: you need per-oligo copy counts and error draws (substitutions, deletions, decode failures) parameterized by a JSON fault configuration before decoding. You already have real sequencing reads from a wet-lab experiment — this skill injects simulated faults, not measured errors You only need to encode/decode a file without evaluating error resilience — use FrameD's core encoding module directly without the fault-injection test bed Your scheduler is not IBM LSF and you cannot extend TcshJob/LSFJob in submit.py, and you cannot run via the provided Docker image or subshell background-job mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Simulates DNA storage noise by generating the configured number of stochastic copies per encoded oligo and sampling errors from a fault distribution (i.i.d. or a channel model with memory such as DNArSim), so fault-injection experiments can be evaluated across parameter sweeps. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: Simulates DNA storage noise by generating the configured number of stochastic copies per encoded oligo and sampling errors from a fault distribution (i.i.d. or a channel model with memory such as DNArSim), so fault-injection experiments can be evaluated across parameter sweeps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have real sequencing reads from a wet-lab experiment — this skill injects simulated faults, not measured errors You only need to encode/decode a file without evaluating error resilience — use FrameD's core encoding module directly without the fault-injection test bed Your scheduler is not IBM LSF and you cannot extend TcshJob/LSFJob in submit.py, and you cannot run via the provided Docker image or subshell background-job mode

skills.description: Use when a cell-cell similarity matrix (e.g., ensemble weak-learner similarity S from EDGE) must be converted into an optimized low-dimensional embedding for visualization or downstream clustering of scRNA-seq data.
skills.name: stochastic-gradient-descent-embedding-optimization
skills.search_text: stochastic-gradient-descent-embedding-optimization Use when a cell-cell similarity matrix (e.g., ensemble weak-learner similarity S from EDGE) must be converted into an optimized low-dimensional embedding for visualization or downstream clustering of scRNA-seq data. Input is raw counts or a similarity matrix has not yet been computed — the optimization stage requires the ensemble similarity matrix S from the weak-learner stage Goal is to identify feature/differentially expressed genes — that is EDGE's separate feature gene extraction output, not the embedding optimization stage EDGE estimates the initial low-dimensional embedding of cells via spectral embedding of the normalized Laplacian built from the ensemble similarity matrix, then optimizes that embedding by minimizing a cross-entropy loss with a two-stage stochastic gradient descent (SGD) using a decreasing step size and uniformly sampled negative examples. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19465-7
skills.summary: EDGE estimates the initial low-dimensional embedding of cells via spectral embedding of the normalized Laplacian built from the ensemble similarity matrix, then optimizes that embedding by minimizing a cross-entropy loss with a two-stage stochastic gradient descent (SGD) using a decreasing step size and uniformly sampled negative examples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw counts or a similarity matrix has not yet been computed — the optimization stage requires the ensemble similarity matrix S from the weak-learner stage Goal is to identify feature/differentially expressed genes — that is EDGE's separate feature gene extraction output, not the embedding optimization stage

skills.description: Use when a per-cell gene-gene network (e.g. from c-CSN) must be converted into a stochastic flow matrix and summarized into a single entropy-based potency score per cell, e.g. to order Wang NPC Day 0-30 or Yang E10/E17 differentiation stages.
skills.name: stochastic-network-edge-weight-normalization
skills.search_text: stochastic-network-edge-weight-normalization Use when a per-cell gene-gene network (e.g. from c-CSN) must be converted into a stochastic flow matrix and summarized into a single entropy-based potency score per cell, e.g. to order Wang NPC Day 0-30 or Yang E10/E17 differentiation stages. The goal is clustering or dimension reduction of cells — those use the CNDM (conditional network degree matrix) with PCA/t-SNE and K-means/SC3/SIMLR, not NFE on stochastic matrices. Input is raw (unnormalized) gene expression without an associated per-cell network; edge weights must be derived from a CSN/CCSN, not directly from the expression matrix. The analysis targets mature cells only with no progenitor comparison, since NFE resolves potency by contrasting entropy across differentiation stages. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Converts a cell-specific gene-gene network (CSN/CCSN) into a weighted stochastic matrix P whose rows sum to 1, then computes network flow entropy (NFE) = -sum(i,j) xi*pij*log(xi*pij) as a per-cell differentiation-potency score. Higher NFE identifies more potent (progenitor) cells along differentiation trajectories. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.05.005
skills.summary: Converts a cell-specific gene-gene network (CSN/CCSN) into a weighted stochastic matrix P whose rows sum to 1, then computes network flow entropy (NFE) = -sum(i,j) xi*pij*log(xi*pij) as a per-cell differentiation-potency score. Higher NFE identifies more potent (progenitor) cells along differentiation trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering or dimension reduction of cells — those use the CNDM (conditional network degree matrix) with PCA/t-SNE and K-means/SC3/SIMLR, not NFE on stochastic matrices. Input is raw (unnormalized) gene expression without an associated per-cell network; edge weights must be derived from a CSN/CCSN, not directly from the expression matrix. The analysis targets mature cells only with no progenitor comparison, since NFE resolves potency by contrasting entropy across differentiation stages.

skills.description: Use when a defined gene regulatory network must be turned into stochastic biochemical reactions to simulate single-cell, single-transcript resolution dynamics with known ground truth.
skills.name: stochastic-reaction-network-conversion
skills.search_text: stochastic-reaction-network-conversion Use when a defined gene regulatory network must be turned into stochastic biochemical reactions to simulate single-cell, single-transcript resolution dynamics with known ground truth. The goal is to emulate only the technical sequencing protocol rather than underlying biological dynamics — the article notes such simulators' applicability and reusability is limited Data are bulk high-molecule measurements where ODE-based simulation is adequate; SSA is motivated by low library sizes and high dropout of single-cell data Cells must be modeled as spatially arranged or interacting — dyngen assumes cells are well-mixed and independent http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Converts a gene regulatory network into a set of biochemical reactions (transcription, splicing, translation, degradation) and simulates single-cell molecule counts with Gillespie's stochastic simulation algorithm, as implemented in dyngen's simulation pipeline. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-24152-2
skills.summary: Converts a gene regulatory network into a set of biochemical reactions (transcription, splicing, translation, degradation) and simulates single-cell molecule counts with Gillespie's stochastic simulation algorithm, as implemented in dyngen's simulation pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to emulate only the technical sequencing protocol rather than underlying biological dynamics — the article notes such simulators' applicability and reusability is limited Data are bulk high-molecule measurements where ODE-based simulation is adequate; SSA is motivated by low library sizes and high dropout of single-cell data Cells must be modeled as spatially arranged or interacting — dyngen assumes cells are well-mixed and independent

skills.description: Use when assessing whether model outputs (e.g., scKINETICS per-cell transcriptional velocities) are stable under technical noise, by repeating a stochastic perturbation such as downsampling raw counts across multiple independent trials per proportion and aggregating deviation statistics.
skills.name: stochastic-trial-aggregation
skills.search_text: stochastic-trial-aggregation Use when assessing whether model outputs (e.g., scKINETICS per-cell transcriptional velocities) are stable under technical noise, by repeating a stochastic perturbation such as downsampling raw counts across multiple independent trials per proportion and aggregating deviation statistics. The input is already normalized or processed expression data — downsampling to simulate reduced sequencing depth requires raw integer counts The perturbation is intended to change the model itself (mask or parameters) rather than isolate the effect of the count perturbation The goal is to test biological, not technical, reproducibility — this skill only simulates technical transcript-capture noise via random count subsampling http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A robustness-testing pattern for model-based single-cell analyses: repeatedly perturb raw inputs (e.g., random downsampling of raw counts), refit the identical model (scKINETICS with fixed regulatory mask and parameters) on each trial, and aggregate a per-cell deviation metric (cosine deviation of velocities) across trials to quantify sensitivity to the perturbation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad267
skills.summary: A robustness-testing pattern for model-based single-cell analyses: repeatedly perturb raw inputs (e.g., random downsampling of raw counts), refit the identical model (scKINETICS with fixed regulatory mask and parameters) on each trial, and aggregate a per-cell deviation metric (cosine deviation of velocities) across trials to quantify sensitivity to the perturbation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already normalized or processed expression data — downsampling to simulate reduced sequencing depth requires raw integer counts The perturbation is intended to change the model itself (mask or parameters) rather than isolate the effect of the count perturbation The goal is to test biological, not technical, reproducibility — this skill only simulates technical transcript-capture noise via random count subsampling

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples require sample-specific metabolic flux estimates over a genome-scale model, and gene expression (MRAS) plus a nutrient medium must be translated into E-Flux style bounds for a QP-constrained FBA solve.
skills.name: stoichiometric-constraint-formulation
skills.search_text: stoichiometric-constraint-formulation Use when bulk RNA-seq samples require sample-specific metabolic flux estimates over a genome-scale model, and gene expression (MRAS) plus a nutrient medium must be translated into E-Flux style bounds for a QP-constrained FBA solve. Input is single-cell RNA-seq data requiring community/tumor-microenvironment-aware fluxes — use compute_sc_flux with cell-type fractions instead of the bulk QP formulation Only pathway-level reaction activity scores (MRAS) are needed and no steady-state stoichiometric constraint is required — calculate_reaction_score alone suffices No nutrient medium context is available or the analysis needs unlimited uptake conditions, since this formulation restricts uptake to medium-defined exchange reactions http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Formulate and solve a convex quadratic-programming FBA problem over the Human-GEM stoichiometric matrix (13,082 reactions, 8,378 metabolites) to estimate per-sample metabolic fluxes, as implemented in METAFlux's compute_flux step. The objective simultaneously maximizes the biomass_human reaction and minimizes the sum of squared fluxes (parsimonious-FBA style), subject to MRAS-derived and medium-defined exchange bounds. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40457-w
skills.summary: Formulate and solve a convex quadratic-programming FBA problem over the Human-GEM stoichiometric matrix (13,082 reactions, 8,378 metabolites) to estimate per-sample metabolic fluxes, as implemented in METAFlux's compute_flux step. The objective simultaneously maximizes the biomass_human reaction and minimizes the sum of squared fluxes (parsimonious-FBA style), subject to MRAS-derived and medium-defined exchange bounds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell RNA-seq data requiring community/tumor-microenvironment-aware fluxes — use compute_sc_flux with cell-type fractions instead of the bulk QP formulation Only pathway-level reaction activity scores (MRAS) are needed and no steady-state stoichiometric constraint is required — calculate_reaction_score alone suffices No nutrient medium context is available or the analysis needs unlimited uptake conditions, since this formulation restricts uptake to medium-defined exchange reactions

skills.description: Use when a permutation colocalization test needs transcriptome regions of interest (e.g. stop codons) that are not provided directly as a GRanges set and must be picked per-transcript from UCSC hg19 TxDb annotation for features with unknown isoform association.
skills.name: stop-codon-region-extraction-custompick
skills.search_text: stop-codon-region-extraction-custompick Use when a permutation colocalization test needs transcriptome regions of interest (e.g. stop codons) that are not provided directly as a GRanges set and must be picked per-transcript from UCSC hg19 TxDb annotation for features with unknown isoform association. RS2 is already available as an explicit region set — use permTestTx with a directly supplied RS2 instead of a customPick function. Each feature's specific isoform association is known — use permTestTx_customPick (non-IA) since the TxIA averaging over K isoforms is unnecessary. The question is genome-based colocalization without transcriptome context — genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, BEDTools) do not model transcriptome backgrounds and RgnTX's null distributions on mRNA space are significantly different from genomic backgrounds. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Uses RgnTX's getStopCodon customPick function to derive stop codon regions from the UCSC hg19 transcriptome annotation (TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene) as transcriptome regions of interest (ROI), for use in colocalization permutation tests such as permTestTxIA_customPick against miCLIP-seq m6A sites that carry isoform ambiguity. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.08.021
skills.summary: Uses RgnTX's getStopCodon customPick function to derive stop codon regions from the UCSC hg19 transcriptome annotation (TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene) as transcriptome regions of interest (ROI), for use in colocalization permutation tests such as permTestTxIA_customPick against miCLIP-seq m6A sites that carry isoform ambiguity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: RS2 is already available as an explicit region set — use permTestTx with a directly supplied RS2 instead of a customPick function. Each feature's specific isoform association is known — use permTestTx_customPick (non-IA) since the TxIA averaging over K isoforms is unnecessary. The question is genome-based colocalization without transcriptome context — genome-based tools (GREAT, LOLA, GenomeRunner, BEDTools) do not model transcriptome backgrounds and RgnTX's null distributions on mRNA space are significantly different from genomic backgrounds.

skills.description: Use when a pipeline consumes a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium output) and downstream analysis, such as truncation-point pileups or per-strand peak calling, requires reads to be separated by strand and read group before processing.
skills.name: strand-aware-read-partitioning
skills.search_text: strand-aware-read-partitioning Use when a pipeline consumes a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium output) and downstream analysis, such as truncation-point pileups or per-strand peak calling, requires reads to be separated by strand and read group before processing. The input is not a BAM of aligned reads but an already-processed feature table, GFF/GTF annotation, or normalized coverage track The downstream tool consumes a single unsplit BAM and performs its own strand or read-group handling internally The BAM lacks read-group (RG) tags or strand information, so no meaningful RG-level or strand-level partition can be made http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Partitions an input BAM of aligned sequencing reads into forward- and reverse-strand files and further subdivides each strand pile by read group (RG) tag, using pysam (the Python wrapper for htslib/SAMtools). This preprocessing stage prepares the read data that peaks2utr feeds to the SPAT algorithm and MACS peak calling. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Partitions an input BAM of aligned sequencing reads into forward- and reverse-strand files and further subdivides each strand pile by read group (RG) tag, using pysam (the Python wrapper for htslib/SAMtools). This preprocessing stage prepares the read data that peaks2utr feeds to the SPAT algorithm and MACS peak calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not a BAM of aligned reads but an already-processed feature table, GFF/GTF annotation, or normalized coverage track The downstream tool consumes a single unsplit BAM and performs its own strand or read-group handling internally The BAM lacks read-group (RG) tags or strand information, so no meaningful RG-level or strand-level partition can be made

skills.description: Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads where each encoded strand has multiple noisy copies, and you must aggregate copies toward a consensus before reversing the inner encoding.
skills.name: strand-clustering-minhash-edit-distance
skills.search_text: strand-clustering-minhash-edit-distance Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads where each encoded strand has multiple noisy copies, and you must aggregate copies toward a consensus before reversing the inner encoding. When the error model does not warrant it: MSA is 'not always beneficial' and its inclusion depends on the error rate and error types being injected — skip it for low-error or benign error profiles When the chosen decode strategy is consolidation after the inner code rather than pre-inner-code clustering (the alternative FrameD decode mode) When only a single copy per strand exists, so there is nothing to cluster or aggregate toward consensus http://edamontology.org/topic_0632 A decode-stage error-correction step in FrameD that groups the multiple noisy copies of each encoded strand generated by synthesis/sequencing via MinHash/edit-distance clustering, optionally followed by multiple sequence alignment (MSA, e.g. Muscle), before the inner code is reversed to produce a consensus sequence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad572
skills.summary: A decode-stage error-correction step in FrameD that groups the multiple noisy copies of each encoded strand generated by synthesis/sequencing via MinHash/edit-distance clustering, optionally followed by multiple sequence alignment (MSA, e.g. Muscle), before the inner code is reversed to produce a consensus sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the error model does not warrant it: MSA is 'not always beneficial' and its inclusion depends on the error rate and error types being injected — skip it for low-error or benign error profiles When the chosen decode strategy is consolidation after the inner code rather than pre-inner-code clustering (the alternative FrameD decode mode) When only a single copy per strand exists, so there is nothing to cluster or aggregate toward consensus

skills.description: Use when you have groHMM HMM bed features (chr*_HMM.bed) and a refFlat gene annotation, and need a per-TAR aTAR/uTAR label based on genomic start/stop overlap regardless of strand.
skills.name: strand-insensitive-tar-labeling
skills.search_text: strand-insensitive-tar-labeling Use when you have groHMM HMM bed features (chr*_HMM.bed) and a refFlat gene annotation, and need a per-TAR aTAR/uTAR label based on genomic start/stop overlap regardless of strand. Your downstream analysis requires antisense-overlapping TARs to be called uTARs — use the strand-aware variant described in the paper instead You do not yet have groHMM bed files (chr*_HMM.bed); the labeling rule operates on already-called TAR features, not raw reads or BAMs http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Labels each groHMM-derived TAR (chr*_HMM.bed feature) as aTAR or uTAR by testing genomic coordinate overlap against the refFlat gene annotation while deliberately ignoring strand, so antisense-overlapping TARs are still counted as annotated. This yields a binary annotation-overlap label used to separate annotated from unannotated (dark-matter) transcription in the TAR-scRNA-seq workflow. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Labels each groHMM-derived TAR (chr*_HMM.bed feature) as aTAR or uTAR by testing genomic coordinate overlap against the refFlat gene annotation while deliberately ignoring strand, so antisense-overlapping TARs are still counted as annotated. This yields a binary annotation-overlap label used to separate annotated from unannotated (dark-matter) transcription in the TAR-scRNA-seq workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your downstream analysis requires antisense-overlapping TARs to be called uTARs — use the strand-aware variant described in the paper instead You do not yet have groHMM bed files (chr*_HMM.bed); the labeling rule operates on already-called TAR features, not raw reads or BAMs

skills.description: Use when you have a CSV of gene annotations (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) from Ensembl, optionally with TPM/FPKM/fold_change/padj columns, and need to enumerate sense-antisense overlapping pairs with structural classification.
skills.name: strand-specific-cis-nat-pair-extraction
skills.search_text: strand-specific-cis-nat-pair-extraction Use when you have a CSV of gene annotations (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) from Ensembl, optionally with TPM/FPKM/fold_change/padj columns, and need to enumerate sense-antisense overlapping pairs with structural classification. Input is raw RNA-seq reads — CCIVR expects processed gene-level annotation and expression values; mapping/profiling must be done upstream with STAR/RSEM/DESeq2. You need strand-specific read-level assembly of antisense transcripts de novo (e.g. NATpipe-style) rather than annotation-based overlap extraction from known gene loci. Gene annotations in the source database are unreliable for strand direction or transcript structure — CCIVR's output accuracy depends entirely on deposited annotation accuracy. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Use CCIVR to comprehensively extract all cis-NAT (cis-natural antisense transcript) pairs from a genome annotation CSV, classifying each pair into four structural types (EB, FO, HH, TT) via plus-to-minus and minus-to-minus passes, and optionally fold in RNA-seq expression profiling to find inversely correlated (down-up) pairs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-19782-5
skills.summary: Use CCIVR to comprehensively extract all cis-NAT (cis-natural antisense transcript) pairs from a genome annotation CSV, classifying each pair into four structural types (EB, FO, HH, TT) via plus-to-minus and minus-to-minus passes, and optionally fold in RNA-seq expression profiling to find inversely correlated (down-up) pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA-seq reads — CCIVR expects processed gene-level annotation and expression values; mapping/profiling must be done upstream with STAR/RSEM/DESeq2. You need strand-specific read-level assembly of antisense transcripts de novo (e.g. NATpipe-style) rather than annotation-based overlap extraction from known gene loci. Gene annotations in the source database are unreliable for strand direction or transcript structure — CCIVR's output accuracy depends entirely on deposited annotation accuracy.

skills.description: Use when generating a per-cell count matrix over groHMM-defined TARs from strand-specific paired-end scRNA-seq alignments (e.g., Smart-seq2), where read orientation must be preserved for correct quantification.
skills.name: strand-specific-feature-counting
skills.search_text: strand-specific-feature-counting Use when generating a per-cell count matrix over groHMM-defined TARs from strand-specific paired-end scRNA-seq alignments (e.g., Smart-seq2), where read orientation must be preserved for correct quantification. Input is already a gene- or feature-level count table — counting is unnecessary; proceed directly to Seurat analysis Alignments are single-end or non-strand-specific — the -s 1 strandedness setting would misassign fragments The goal is annotation-dependent gene-level quantification from Cell Ranger output rather than TAR discovery beyond known annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Counts sequenced fragments per feature (groHMM-defined TARs) while preserving read strandedness, converting strand-specific single-cell alignments into a TAR expression matrix for downstream Seurat analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Counts sequenced fragments per feature (groHMM-defined TARs) while preserving read strandedness, converting strand-specific single-cell alignments into a TAR expression matrix for downstream Seurat analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene- or feature-level count table — counting is unnecessary; proceed directly to Seurat analysis Alignments are single-end or non-strand-specific — the -s 1 strandedness setting would misassign fragments The goal is annotation-dependent gene-level quantification from Cell Ranger output rather than TAR discovery beyond known annotations

skills.description: Use when you have a STAR-aligned scRNA-seq combined BAM and groHMM-predicted transcribed regions, and need per-region, strand-aware read counts to apply a retention cutoff for annotation-free TAR discovery.
skills.name: strand-specific-genomic-coverage-computation
skills.search_text: strand-specific-genomic-coverage-computation Use when you have a STAR-aligned scRNA-seq combined BAM and groHMM-predicted transcribed regions, and need per-region, strand-aware read counts to apply a retention cutoff for annotation-free TAR discovery. Input is already a gene-annotated expression matrix where annotation-free TAR discovery is unnecessary Coverage must be aggregated across strands (e.g. bulk strandedness-agnostic counting), since this method deliberately separates sense and antisense signals http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A method for computing strand-specific read coverage over predicted transcribed regions in scRNA-seq alignments, used to filter groHMM-predicted TARs by a retention threshold before writing annotation features to refFlat format. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: A method for computing strand-specific read coverage over predicted transcribed regions in scRNA-seq alignments, used to filter groHMM-predicted TARs by a retention threshold before writing annotation features to refFlat format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene-annotated expression matrix where annotation-free TAR discovery is unnecessary Coverage must be aggregated across strands (e.g. bulk strandedness-agnostic counting), since this method deliberately separates sense and antisense signals

skills.description: Use when aligned strand-specific reads in BAM format (e.g. 10x Chromium runs where signal concentrates at 3' UTR distal ends) must be converted into candidate intervals of significant coverage as the basis for annotating novel 3' UTRs.
skills.name: strand-specific-read-coverage-analysis
skills.search_text: strand-specific-read-coverage-analysis Use when aligned strand-specific reads in BAM format (e.g. 10x Chromium runs where signal concentrates at 3' UTR distal ends) must be converted into candidate intervals of significant coverage as the basis for annotating novel 3' UTRs. The goal is final 3' UTR annotation with precise end bases — peak calling alone only yields candidate coverage regions; the truncation-point refinement and criteria filtering stages are separate downstream tasks. The input BAM is not strand-specific or the reads cannot be reliably assigned to a strand — merging both strands would corrupt per-strand peak calls. The analysis target is narrow punctate peak detection (e.g. transcription-factor ChIP-seq) rather than broad extended coverage regions; peaks2utr's design favours 10x Chromium-style signal concentrated at UTR distal ends. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconstructs the first stage of the peaks2utr 3' UTR annotation pipeline: calling broad peaks of significant read coverage with MACS3 separately on the plus- and minus-strand BAM files, yielding per-strand broadPeak BED interval sets that feed downstream UTR designation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Reconstructs the first stage of the peaks2utr 3' UTR annotation pipeline: calling broad peaks of significant read coverage with MACS3 separately on the plus- and minus-strand BAM files, yielding per-strand broadPeak BED interval sets that feed downstream UTR designation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is final 3' UTR annotation with precise end bases — peak calling alone only yields candidate coverage regions; the truncation-point refinement and criteria filtering stages are separate downstream tasks. The input BAM is not strand-specific or the reads cannot be reliably assigned to a strand — merging both strands would corrupt per-strand peak calls. The analysis target is narrow punctate peak detection (e.g. transcription-factor ChIP-seq) rather than broad extended coverage regions; peaks2utr's design favours 10x Chromium-style signal concentrated at UTR distal ends.

skills.description: Use when a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium) contains soft-clipped bases with polyA-tails, and precise strand-specific UTR end-base coordinates are needed for downstream 3' UTR annotation.
skills.name: strand-specific-read-end-tallying
skills.search_text: strand-specific-read-end-tallying Use when a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium) contains soft-clipped bases with polyA-tails, and precise strand-specific UTR end-base coordinates are needed for downstream 3' UTR annotation. The BAM contains no soft-clipped reads or terminal poly(A)/poly(T) tails (e.g. non-3'-enriched data such as random-primed RNA-seq), since no truncation points can be tallied. The goal is peak calling or UTR annotation without read-level end evidence — MACS peak calling or the downstream peaks2utr annotation stage, not read-end tallying, is the appropriate step. Input is already a GFF/GTF annotation of UTRs; this skill consumes aligned reads, not annotation files. http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Tallies the genomic coordinate of the final aligned end base of every read containing soft-clipped bases and a poly(A)-tail of a given minimum length, per chromosome and strand, to produce truncation-point counts used to pinpoint the precise 3' UTR end base. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad112
skills.summary: Tallies the genomic coordinate of the final aligned end base of every read containing soft-clipped bases and a poly(A)-tail of a given minimum length, per chromosome and strand, to produce truncation-point counts used to pinpoint the precise 3' UTR end base.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The BAM contains no soft-clipped reads or terminal poly(A)/poly(T) tails (e.g. non-3'-enriched data such as random-primed RNA-seq), since no truncation points can be tallied. The goal is peak calling or UTR annotation without read-level end evidence — MACS peak calling or the downstream peaks2utr annotation stage, not read-end tallying, is the appropriate step. Input is already a GFF/GTF annotation of UTRs; this skill consumes aligned reads, not annotation files.

skills.description: Use when running Tiglon (or evaluating its assembly) on Hisat2- or STAR-aligned BAM files and you must set the -s orientation flag to match the library type (paired-end first/second/unstranded or single-end single_forward/single_reverse/single_unstranded).
skills.name: strand-specific-rnaseq-parameter-configuration
skills.search_text: strand-specific-rnaseq-parameter-configuration Use when running Tiglon (or evaluating its assembly) on Hisat2- or STAR-aligned BAM files and you must set the -s orientation flag to match the library type (paired-end first/second/unstranded or single-end single_forward/single_reverse/single_unstranded). Input alignments come from aligners other than Hisat(2)/STAR — the current Tiglon version only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star The RNA-seq data are long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current version is not compatible with long-read RNA-seq datasets You need annotation-guided assembly using known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Configure Tiglon's library-orientation and quality-filter parameters (-s strand flag plus default min_trans_length 500, min_average_frac 0.03, min_unbalance_frac 0.03, min_gap_length 200, min_trans_cov >0) so that BAM alignments from Hisat2/Star are assembled into GTF transcripts consistent with the sequencing library's strandedness. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104067
skills.summary: Configure Tiglon's library-orientation and quality-filter parameters (-s strand flag plus default min_trans_length 500, min_average_frac 0.03, min_unbalance_frac 0.03, min_gap_length 200, min_trans_cov >0) so that BAM alignments from Hisat2/Star are assembled into GTF transcripts consistent with the sequencing library's strandedness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments come from aligners other than Hisat(2)/STAR — the current Tiglon version only accepts BAM files generated by Hisat(2) and Star The RNA-seq data are long reads (PacBio or Oxford Nanopore) — the current version is not compatible with long-read RNA-seq datasets You need annotation-guided assembly using known transcript annotations — the current Tiglon version has no option for annotation-guided assemblies

skills.description: Use when you have raw paired-end RNA-Seq reads (e.g. firststrand Illumina libraries) destined for aptardi polyA-site prediction and need to produce a sorted BAM aligned with HISAT2 plus a StringTie-reconstructed input transcriptome.
skills.name: stranded-rnaseq-bam-preprocessing
skills.search_text: stranded-rnaseq-bam-preprocessing Use when you have raw paired-end RNA-Seq reads (e.g. firststrand Illumina libraries) destined for aptardi polyA-site prediction and need to produce a sorted BAM aligned with HISAT2 plus a StringTie-reconstructed input transcriptome. You already have a genome-aligned, sorted BAM and an assembled input transcriptome — proceed directly to running aptardi in Mode 1 You only need to build a custom aptardi model (Mode 2) from gold-standard polyA sites and have no sample reads to align http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares stranded paired-end RNA-Seq reads into a coordinate-sorted BAM and a reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) suitable as aptardi inputs, via FastQC/Cutadapt quality processing, HISAT2 alignment with explicit strandness, SAMtools sorting, and StringTie reconstruction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21894-x
skills.summary: Prepares stranded paired-end RNA-Seq reads into a coordinate-sorted BAM and a reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) suitable as aptardi inputs, via FastQC/Cutadapt quality processing, HISAT2 alignment with explicit strandness, SAMtools sorting, and StringTie reconstruction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a genome-aligned, sorted BAM and an assembled input transcriptome — proceed directly to running aptardi in Mode 1 You only need to build a custom aptardi model (Mode 2) from gold-standard polyA sites and have no sample reads to align

skills.description: Use when a per-call result table already exists (e.g., classified Ginkgo CNA calls in 65 PTA-amplified brain cells) and the analysis goal is summary fractions broken down by cell type and call-length bins, as in HiScanner Fig. 4d–j.
skills.name: stratified-fraction-aggregation-by-cell-type-and-length
skills.search_text: stratified-fraction-aggregation-by-cell-type-and-length Use when a per-call result table already exists (e.g., classified Ginkgo CNA calls in 65 PTA-amplified brain cells) and the analysis goal is summary fractions broken down by cell type and call-length bins, as in HiScanner Fig. 4d–j. Input is raw read-depth or BAF data and calls have not yet been segmented, classified, and filtered (e.g., bulk-overlapping calls not removed) — stratification is meaningless until per-call labels exist The comparison involves other single-cell callers such as HiScanner, CHISEL, SCOPE, or SCYN whose output formats and concordance definitions differ from the Ginkgo per-call table assumed here http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates per-call classification results (e.g., BAF-concordant vs BAF-discordant Ginkgo CNA calls) into discordance fractions stratified by cell type (neurons vs oligodendrocytes) and by call-length bins, reproducing the Fig. 4d–j breakdown used to expose Ginkgo's unsupported CNA calls in brain cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60446-5
skills.summary: Aggregates per-call classification results (e.g., BAF-concordant vs BAF-discordant Ginkgo CNA calls) into discordance fractions stratified by cell type (neurons vs oligodendrocytes) and by call-length bins, reproducing the Fig. 4d–j breakdown used to expose Ginkgo's unsupported CNA calls in brain cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read-depth or BAF data and calls have not yet been segmented, classified, and filtered (e.g., bulk-overlapping calls not removed) — stratification is meaningless until per-call labels exist The comparison involves other single-cell callers such as HiScanner, CHISEL, SCOPE, or SCYN whose output formats and concordance definitions differ from the Ginkgo per-call table assumed here

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a supervised cell-type classifier (e.g., SciBet vs scmap vs Seurat v3) on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a repeated, class-balanced hold-out estimate of classification accuracy is needed.
skills.name: stratified-holdout-cross-validation
skills.search_text: stratified-holdout-cross-validation Use when benchmarking a supervised cell-type classifier (e.g., SciBet vs scmap vs Seurat v3) on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a repeated, class-balanced hold-out estimate of classification accuracy is needed. The dataset has no trusted cell-type labels, so a supervised hold-out accuracy comparison is not meaningful You need a one-time train/test evaluation rather than a benchmark averaged over 50 repeated splits (e.g., a single deployment prediction) Evaluating prediction of cell types absent from the reference (negative/unrepresented cells), which uses the null-dataset confidence score C instead of plain held-out accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarking strategy from the SciBet paper: repeatedly split a labeled scRNA-seq dataset into stratified train/test sets at a 7:3 ratio (sklearn's train_test_split, sampling without replacement), retrain and classify on each split, and average accuracy over 50 repetitions for a robust per-dataset/per-method comparison. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Benchmarking strategy from the SciBet paper: repeatedly split a labeled scRNA-seq dataset into stratified train/test sets at a 7:3 ratio (sklearn's train_test_split, sampling without replacement), retrain and classify on each split, and average accuracy over 50 repetitions for a robust per-dataset/per-method comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset has no trusted cell-type labels, so a supervised hold-out accuracy comparison is not meaningful You need a one-time train/test evaluation rather than a benchmark averaged over 50 repeated splits (e.g., a single deployment prediction) Evaluating prediction of cell types absent from the reference (negative/unrepresented cells), which uses the null-dataset confidence score C instead of plain held-out accuracy

skills.description: Use when benchmarking cell type annotation or cell selection methods on labeled single-cell expression data and repeated, class-balanced performance estimates (e.g. balanced accuracy, F1) are needed to compare strategies fairly.
skills.name: stratified-train-test-splitting
skills.search_text: stratified-train-test-splitting Use when benchmarking cell type annotation or cell selection methods on labeled single-cell expression data and repeated, class-balanced performance estimates (e.g. balanced accuracy, F1) are needed to compare strategies fairly. Data lack reliable ground-truth cell type labels, since stratification depends on the existing annotation (the authors relied on labels derived from previous studies and did not perform manual annotation) The goal is a single train/test split evaluation rather than the ten-replicate benchmark design used to produce the paper's figures and uncertainty ranges Extremely rare cell types with fewer members than needed for proportional 50:50 representation, where stratified splits cannot preserve class balance in both partitions http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Randomly split each single-cell dataset into ten 50:50 train/test partitions while stratifying by cell type, providing the repeated evaluation framework used across the active learning, marker-initialization, and imbalance benchmarks of the Geuenich et al. 2024 study. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-45198-y
skills.summary: Randomly split each single-cell dataset into ten 50:50 train/test partitions while stratifying by cell type, providing the repeated evaluation framework used across the active learning, marker-initialization, and imbalance benchmarks of the Geuenich et al. 2024 study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data lack reliable ground-truth cell type labels, since stratification depends on the existing annotation (the authors relied on labels derived from previous studies and did not perform manual annotation) The goal is a single train/test split evaluation rather than the ten-replicate benchmark design used to produce the paper's figures and uncertainty ranges Extremely rare cell types with fewer members than needed for proportional 50:50 representation, where stratified splits cannot preserve class balance in both partitions

skills.description: Use when a small, imbalanced RNA-modification dataset (e.g., RMBase v2.0 Ψ sites vs. 10x negatives) must be split into training and test sets while preserving class ratios and removing homologous sequences that would inflate evaluation performance.
skills.name: stratified-train-test-splitting
skills.search_text: stratified-train-test-splitting Use when a small, imbalanced RNA-modification dataset (e.g., RMBase v2.0 Ψ sites vs. 10x negatives) must be split into training and test sets while preserving class ratios and removing homologous sequences that would inflate evaluation performance. When the dataset is already identity-filtered or when the goal is benchmarking on a fixed external test set rather than cross-validation When sequence homology between train and test is desired (e.g., evaluating memorization), since this pipeline explicitly removes >0.8 / >60% identity pairs When class labels are unavailable or highly multi-class with tiny per-class counts where stratification cannot preserve ratios http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Constructs leakage-controlled train/test partitions for imbalanced Ψ-site classification datasets by stratifying class ratios across 10 folds and then re-filtering each fold's train/test pair with sequence-identity tools (cd-hit-est-2d, Needleman-Wunsch, cd-hit-est). transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010
skills.summary: Constructs leakage-controlled train/test partitions for imbalanced Ψ-site classification datasets by stratifying class ratios across 10 folds and then re-filtering each fold's train/test pair with sequence-identity tools (cd-hit-est-2d, Needleman-Wunsch, cd-hit-est).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the dataset is already identity-filtered or when the goal is benchmarking on a fixed external test set rather than cross-validation When sequence homology between train and test is desired (e.g., evaluating memorization), since this pipeline explicitly removes >0.8 / >60% identity pairs When class labels are unavailable or highly multi-class with tiny per-class counts where stratification cannot preserve ratios

skills.description: Use when single-cell library read structure cannot be expressed as one fixed barcode/UMI offset — e.g. barcodes split across two segments like '1{b[16]u[12]b[4]x:}' — yet the underlying mapper only supports simple geometry.
skills.name: streaming-read-normalization-via-fifo
skills.search_text: streaming-read-normalization-via-fifo Use when single-cell library read structure cannot be expressed as one fixed barcode/UMI offset — e.g. barcodes split across two segments like '1{b[16]u[12]b[4]x:}' — yet the underlying mapper only supports simple geometry. The library geometry is already simple and fixed-position (e.g. a single contiguous 16 bp barcode plus 12 bp UMI expressible directly by the mapper's native --geometry flag) — normalize directly in the mapper instead You need persistent normalized FASTQ files on disk for QC or reuse — the FIFO design streams reads in memory and writes no intermediate files Reads are single-end with no read-2 mappable sequence to relay, so the read-pair geometry grammar's '2{r:}' component does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simpleaf technique that normalizes sequencing reads with complex fragment geometries (variable-length or floating-position barcodes, e.g. concatenated barcode segments) into a simple fixed-position format on the fly, and streams the normalized reads directly to the piscem mapper through programmatically managed FIFOs so no intermediate normalized FASTQ is written to disk. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad614
skills.summary: A simpleaf technique that normalizes sequencing reads with complex fragment geometries (variable-length or floating-position barcodes, e.g. concatenated barcode segments) into a simple fixed-position format on the fly, and streams the normalized reads directly to the piscem mapper through programmatically managed FIFOs so no intermediate normalized FASTQ is written to disk.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library geometry is already simple and fixed-position (e.g. a single contiguous 16 bp barcode plus 12 bp UMI expressible directly by the mapper's native --geometry flag) — normalize directly in the mapper instead You need persistent normalized FASTQ files on disk for QC or reuse — the FIFO design streams reads in memory and writes no intermediate files Reads are single-end with no read-2 mappable sequence to relay, so the read-pair geometry grammar's '2{r:}' component does not apply

skills.description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrices plus sample metadata for samples spanning distinct stress treatments, and an annotated single-cell reference atlas, and you need to quantify how cell-type composition changes across conditions.
skills.name: stress-condition-composition-comparison
skills.search_text: stress-condition-composition-comparison Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrices plus sample metadata for samples spanning distinct stress treatments, and an annotated single-cell reference atlas, and you need to quantify how cell-type composition changes across conditions. Input is already single-cell data or a cell-composition table rather than bulk RNA-seq profiles needing deconvolution No annotated single-cell reference atlas exists for the organism/tissue, so cluster-specific marker signatures cannot be built The goal is cell-type annotation of single-cell data or trajectory inference — these are separate scPlant modules (RunSeurat, RunMonocle2/3, RunSlingshot) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Deconvolves bulk RNA-seq samples collected under different stress conditions against a single-cell reference (e.g., the PRJNA517021 Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq atlas from Zhang et al., 2019) using scPlant's decomposeBulk, then compares estimated cell-type fractions per condition to identify composition shifts such as changes in vasculature and companion cells. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xplc.2023.100631
skills.summary: Deconvolves bulk RNA-seq samples collected under different stress conditions against a single-cell reference (e.g., the PRJNA517021 Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq atlas from Zhang et al., 2019) using scPlant's decomposeBulk, then compares estimated cell-type fractions per condition to identify composition shifts such as changes in vasculature and companion cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already single-cell data or a cell-composition table rather than bulk RNA-seq profiles needing deconvolution No annotated single-cell reference atlas exists for the organism/tissue, so cluster-specific marker signatures cannot be built The goal is cell-type annotation of single-cell data or trajectory inference — these are separate scPlant modules (RunSeurat, RunMonocle2/3, RunSlingshot)

skills.description: Use when preparing a count matrix of tncRNA expression for DESeq2 stress contrasts and you must pick which control/treatment samples qualify, ensuring ≥3 biological replicates per condition.
skills.name: stress-condition-replicate-sample-selection
skills.search_text: stress-condition-replicate-sample-selection Use when preparing a count matrix of tncRNA expression for DESeq2 stress contrasts and you must pick which control/treatment samples qualify, ensuring ≥3 biological replicates per condition. A stress contrast lacks at least three biological replicates in either the control or treatment condition — DESeq2 dispersion estimation will be unreliable, so the contrast should be excluded rather than forced. The goal is tncRNA discovery/identification rather than differential expression testing — sample replicate balance is not required, and the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline should be run on all samples. Input data are already aggregated or tissue-level matrices without per-replicate sample annotation (e.g. tissues with ≥10 samples used for t-SNE matrix generation) — replicate structure needed for the Wald test cannot be recovered. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0780 Selects sRNA-seq sample sets with at least three biological replicates per condition (control and stress) from the tncRNA sample listings (Supplementary sheet 3.1) so that DESeq2 differential expression of tncRNAs under abiotic and biotic stress is statistically reliable. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.09.021
skills.summary: Selects sRNA-seq sample sets with at least three biological replicates per condition (control and stress) from the tncRNA sample listings (Supplementary sheet 3.1) so that DESeq2 differential expression of tncRNAs under abiotic and biotic stress is statistically reliable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A stress contrast lacks at least three biological replicates in either the control or treatment condition — DESeq2 dispersion estimation will be unreliable, so the contrast should be excluded rather than forced. The goal is tncRNA discovery/identification rather than differential expression testing — sample replicate balance is not required, and the tncRNA Toolkit pipeline should be run on all samples. Input data are already aggregated or tissue-level matrices without per-replicate sample annotation (e.g. tissues with ≥10 samples used for t-SNE matrix generation) — replicate structure needed for the Wald test cannot be recovered.

skills.description: Use when validating that gene modules recovered from single-cell feature selection (e.g., DELVE dynamic vs. static modules on CD8+ T cell LCMV data) carry experimental evidence of co-regulation rather than noise.
skills.name: string-gene-association-network-construction
skills.search_text: string-gene-association-network-construction Use when validating that gene modules recovered from single-cell feature selection (e.g., DELVE dynamic vs. static modules on CD8+ T cell LCMV data) carry experimental evidence of co-regulation rather than noise. The input features are not grouped into modules (e.g., a flat ranked feature list) — the test is defined per-module with size-matched nulls Curated/experimental interaction evidence is unavailable for the organism or gene set (e.g., poorly annotated species), making the STRING experimental-score null uninformative The goal is de novo interaction prediction rather than statistical validation of co-regulation in already-defined gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds gene association networks from experimentally-derived STRING scores for each DELVE-identified feature module and tests whether modules (dynamic vs. static) show statistically significant co-regulation via a one-sided permutation test on average network degree. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46773-z
skills.summary: Builds gene association networks from experimentally-derived STRING scores for each DELVE-identified feature module and tests whether modules (dynamic vs. static) show statistically significant co-regulation via a one-sided permutation test on average network degree.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input features are not grouped into modules (e.g., a flat ranked feature list) — the test is defined per-module with size-matched nulls Curated/experimental interaction evidence is unavailable for the organism or gene set (e.g., poorly annotated species), making the STRING experimental-score null uninformative The goal is de novo interaction prediction rather than statistical validation of co-regulation in already-defined gene sets

skills.description: Use when quantifying how connected a protein is within the human STRING interaction network, or when reproducing/validating reported network density percentages (e.g. HSPH1 = 78% from Fig. 1C of Kahraman et al., Scientific Reports 2020).
skills.name: string-network-density-normalization
skills.search_text: string-network-density-normalization Use when quantifying how connected a protein is within the human STRING interaction network, or when reproducing/validating reported network density percentages (e.g. HSPH1 = 78% from Fig. 1C of Kahraman et al., Scientific Reports 2020). When the analysis goal is isoform switching detection or functional impact scoring (CanIsoNet's primary use case) rather than raw network connectivity quantification When the interaction network is not STRING (the weighted-sum normalization is defined on STRING combined interaction scores and calibrated against the full human STRING network maximum) When a percentile of node degree alone suffices — the density score uses interaction weights, not just edge counts http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Compute a per-protein network density score in the human STRING protein-protein interaction network by normalizing each protein's weighted interaction sum against the network-wide maximum, expressed as a percentile-like percentage. Used in CanIsoNet/Kahraman et al. 2020 to quantify how connected a gene (e.g. HSPH1, 78%) is relative to all other proteins. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Compute a per-protein network density score in the human STRING protein-protein interaction network by normalizing each protein's weighted interaction sum against the network-wide maximum, expressed as a percentile-like percentage. Used in CanIsoNet/Kahraman et al. 2020 to quantify how connected a gene (e.g. HSPH1, 78%) is relative to all other proteins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is isoform switching detection or functional impact scoring (CanIsoNet's primary use case) rather than raw network connectivity quantification When the interaction network is not STRING (the weighted-sum normalization is defined on STRING combined interaction scores and calibrated against the full human STRING network maximum) When a percentile of node degree alone suffices — the density score uses interaction weights, not just edge counts

skills.description: Use when you have disease isoform switching results (dMDT gene lists whose isoforms lose domains) and need to map those domain losses onto protein-protein interactions from STRING to identify disrupted edges.
skills.name: string-ppi-data-integration
skills.search_text: string-ppi-data-integration Use when you have disease isoform switching results (dMDT gene lists whose isoforms lose domains) and need to map those domain losses onto protein-protein interactions from STRING to identify disrupted edges. The goal is general PPI network analysis without isoform switching or domain-loss context — STRING alone suffices and the 3did DDI overlay adds nothing. Input lacks disease-specific dMDT gene lists (e.g., only variant-level or expression-level data without isoform-level domain loss), so no edges can be flagged as disrupted. You need isoform-specific PPIs measured directly (e.g., AP-MS) rather than domain-loss-inferred disruption of reference PPIs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 Integrates STRING (v10.0) protein-protein interactions with 3did (v 2020_05) Pfam domain-domain interaction pairs to overlay isoform-driven domain losses from disease RNA-seq dMDT gene lists onto the PPI network, producing annotated disease-specific isoform interaction networks as consumed by CanIsoNet. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad050
skills.summary: Integrates STRING (v10.0) protein-protein interactions with 3did (v 2020_05) Pfam domain-domain interaction pairs to overlay isoform-driven domain losses from disease RNA-seq dMDT gene lists onto the PPI network, producing annotated disease-specific isoform interaction networks as consumed by CanIsoNet.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is general PPI network analysis without isoform switching or domain-loss context — STRING alone suffices and the 3did DDI overlay adds nothing. Input lacks disease-specific dMDT gene lists (e.g., only variant-level or expression-level data without isoform-level domain loss), so no edges can be flagged as disrupted. You need isoform-specific PPIs measured directly (e.g., AP-MS) rather than domain-loss-inferred disruption of reference PPIs.

skills.description: Use when raw association scores (e.g. FAVA PCC scores from scRNA-seq or bulk proteomics data) need to be calibrated into interpretable confidence probabilities for network filtering at STRING-style confidence cutoffs.
skills.name: string-style-score-calibration-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: string-style-score-calibration-curve-fitting Use when raw association scores (e.g. FAVA PCC scores from scRNA-seq or bulk proteomics data) need to be calibrated into interpretable confidence probabilities for network filtering at STRING-style confidence cutoffs. When the network scores are already calibrated posterior probabilities (e.g. STRING scores) rather than raw PCC values — refitting would double-calibrate When no benchmark of known protein associations (e.g. KEGG) exists for the organism, since local precision cannot be estimated http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 A method for converting raw PCC-derived association scores from FAVA-scored networks into STRING-style posterior confidence probabilities by fitting a five-parameter calibration function against a benchmark of known pathway associations (KEGG), then combining per-data-type calibrated networks and extracting subnetworks at 15%, 40%, and 70% confidence cutoffs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae010
skills.summary: A method for converting raw PCC-derived association scores from FAVA-scored networks into STRING-style posterior confidence probabilities by fitting a five-parameter calibration function against a benchmark of known pathway associations (KEGG), then combining per-data-type calibrated networks and extracting subnetworks at 15%, 40%, and 70% confidence cutoffs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the network scores are already calibrated posterior probabilities (e.g. STRING scores) rather than raw PCC values — refitting would double-calibrate When no benchmark of known protein associations (e.g. KEGG) exists for the organism, since local precision cannot be estimated

skills.description: Use when benchmarking long-read isoform assemblers on GMAP-aligned PacBio/ONT BAM data against a known reference isoform set (e.g. 68 SIRV isoforms), where StringTie2 must serve as the transcriptome-based comparator.
skills.name: stringtie2-long-read-transcript-assembly
skills.search_text: stringtie2-long-read-transcript-assembly Use when benchmarking long-read isoform assemblers on GMAP-aligned PacBio/ONT BAM data against a known reference isoform set (e.g. 68 SIRV isoforms), where StringTie2 must serve as the transcriptome-based comparator. Your goal is interactive per-gene inspection and fine-tuning of splice sites — the article positions VIsoQLR for that, whereas StringTie2 is a non-interactive assembler comparator. Data are short reads without long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments — the '-L' long-read mode and this benchmark setting target long-read sequencing input. You need isoform detection counts with very high sensitivity to low-abundance transcripts below ~2% — StringTie2 underperformed here and the article notes most missing isoforms were below the 2% default read threshold. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces the paper's benchmark of StringTie2 as a transcriptome-based isoform assembler on GMAP-aligned PacBio long-read data: running StringTie2 in long-read mode ('-L') with '-f 0' on the SIRV benchmark, where it detected 12 (18%) of the 68 known SIRV isoforms versus VIsoQLR's 49 (72%) and FLAIR's 37 (54%). transcriptomics/v2 10.1007/s00439-023-02539-z
skills.summary: Reproduces the paper's benchmark of StringTie2 as a transcriptome-based isoform assembler on GMAP-aligned PacBio long-read data: running StringTie2 in long-read mode ('-L') with '-f 0' on the SIRV benchmark, where it detected 12 (18%) of the 68 known SIRV isoforms versus VIsoQLR's 49 (72%) and FLAIR's 37 (54%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is interactive per-gene inspection and fine-tuning of splice sites — the article positions VIsoQLR for that, whereas StringTie2 is a non-interactive assembler comparator. Data are short reads without long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments — the '-L' long-read mode and this benchmark setting target long-read sequencing input. You need isoform detection counts with very high sensitivity to low-abundance transcripts below ~2% — StringTie2 underperformed here and the article notes most missing isoforms were below the 2% default read threshold.

skills.description: Use when evaluating 2D ST slice alignment quality: you have spatial coordinate systems of consecutive slices (e.g., STARmap mouse brain) transformed by a tool like Scube and need a per-slice similarity score against a ground-truth 3D stack.
skills.name: structural-similarity-index-computation
skills.search_text: structural-similarity-index-computation Use when evaluating 2D ST slice alignment quality: you have spatial coordinate systems of consecutive slices (e.g., STARmap mouse brain) transformed by a tool like Scube and need a per-slice similarity score against a ground-truth 3D stack. Evaluating nonlinear alignment quality — the article states the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment, so SSIM-based comparisons of nonlinear transforms are out of scope Assessing cell type deconvolution or spatial domain identification quality (Spoint/Splane tasks), where SSIM is not the relevant metric Input slices have no ground-truth 3D stack reference available, making per-slice SSIM/PCC against truth impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes structural similarity index (SSIM, alongside Pearson correlation) per spatial-transcriptomics slice to quantify how faithfully an aligned/transformed slice reproduces the ground-truth 3D tissue stack. In the SPACEL benchmark it is the primary metric scoring Scube's 3D alignment against STAligner and PASTE. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-43220-3
skills.summary: Computes structural similarity index (SSIM, alongside Pearson correlation) per spatial-transcriptomics slice to quantify how faithfully an aligned/transformed slice reproduces the ground-truth 3D tissue stack. In the SPACEL benchmark it is the primary metric scoring Scube's 3D alignment against STAligner and PASTE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Evaluating nonlinear alignment quality — the article states the current version of Scube does not support nonlinear alignment, so SSIM-based comparisons of nonlinear transforms are out of scope Assessing cell type deconvolution or spatial domain identification quality (Spoint/Splane tasks), where SSIM is not the relevant metric Input slices have no ground-truth 3D stack reference available, making per-slice SSIM/PCC against truth impossible

skills.description: Use when you have per-window BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (e.g., from RSCanner's 51-nt centered sliding windows on a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a Shannon file) and need to flag highly-structured positions and quantify structure density per genomic bin.
skills.name: structure-count-percentile-thresholding
skills.search_text: structure-count-percentile-thresholding Use when you have per-window BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (e.g., from RSCanner's 51-nt centered sliding windows on a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a Shannon file) and need to flag highly-structured positions and quantify structure density per genomic bin. Input is raw probing data (e.g., SHAPE or DMS reactivities) rather than a precomputed secondary structure (CT or dot bracket) plus a Shannon entropy file — RSCanner requires these precomputed inputs. You need overlapping/windowed per-nucleotide structure values rather than the non-overlapping 100-nt binned % structure content summarized by ordered_structure_table.csv. The RNA is so short that 51-nt centered windows are mostly truncated, making 50th-percentile cutoffs unstable across the transcript. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0097 Computes per-nucleotide 'structure counts' by thresholding sliding-window base pair content (BPC) above a percentile cutoff and smoothed Shannon entropy below a percentile cutoff, then aggregates counts into non-overlapping bins of default 100 nt to yield % structure content along an RNA. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Computes per-nucleotide 'structure counts' by thresholding sliding-window base pair content (BPC) above a percentile cutoff and smoothed Shannon entropy below a percentile cutoff, then aggregates counts into non-overlapping bins of default 100 nt to yield % structure content along an RNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw probing data (e.g., SHAPE or DMS reactivities) rather than a precomputed secondary structure (CT or dot bracket) plus a Shannon entropy file — RSCanner requires these precomputed inputs. You need overlapping/windowed per-nucleotide structure values rather than the non-overlapping 100-nt binned % structure content summarized by ordered_structure_table.csv. The RNA is so short that 51-nt centered windows are mostly truncated, making 50th-percentile cutoffs unstable across the transcript.

skills.description: Use when per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values are already computed for an RNA (e.g. HCV_Jc1 from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus a shannon.txt), and positions must be labeled as structure counts under RSCanner's filtering rules.
skills.name: structure-counts-classification
skills.search_text: structure-counts-classification Use when per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values are already computed for an RNA (e.g. HCV_Jc1 from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus a shannon.txt), and positions must be labeled as structure counts under RSCanner's filtering rules. Only the raw .ct/dot-bracket structure file and raw shannon.txt are available — the sliding-window BPC and Shannon-entropy smoothing step must run first to produce bpc_data.csv and smoothed_Shannon_data.csv. The goal is the final heatmap/histogram visualization rather than the per-nucleotide classification itself — use the downstream frequency-distribution plotting step. The RNA is short or the user wants absolute (e.g. fixed BPC) thresholds rather than relative global percentile cutoffs — the default 50th-percentile rule is data-relative and may not match other filtering schemes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Classifies individual nucleotides of an RNA transcript as 'structure counts' by applying dual percentile cutoffs to sliding-window base pair content (BPC) and smoothed Shannon entropy values, then tabulating the passing positions in structure_counts.csv. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Classifies individual nucleotides of an RNA transcript as 'structure counts' by applying dual percentile cutoffs to sliding-window base pair content (BPC) and smoothed Shannon entropy values, then tabulating the passing positions in structure_counts.csv.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the raw .ct/dot-bracket structure file and raw shannon.txt are available — the sliding-window BPC and Shannon-entropy smoothing step must run first to produce bpc_data.csv and smoothed_Shannon_data.csv. The goal is the final heatmap/histogram visualization rather than the per-nucleotide classification itself — use the downstream frequency-distribution plotting step. The RNA is short or the user wants absolute (e.g. fixed BPC) thresholds rather than relative global percentile cutoffs — the default 50th-percentile rule is data-relative and may not match other filtering schemes.

skills.description: Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and Shannon entropy (e.g. from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus shannon.txt) and need to map where structure-dense regions fall along the transcript.
skills.name: structure-density-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: structure-density-heatmap-visualization Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and Shannon entropy (e.g. from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus shannon.txt) and need to map where structure-dense regions fall along the transcript. Input lacks a predicted secondary structure or per-nucleotide Shannon entropy — RSCanner requires both a .ct/.dot-bracket structure and a shannon.txt file, so it cannot scan raw sequences alone. You need 3D or base-resolution structure validation rather than a windowed 1D density map of structure content along the transcript. You need overlapped/stacked feature windows rather than fixed non-overlapping bins — RSCanner's heatmap bins use a default 100-nt non-overlapping window. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Visualize the density of RNA secondary structure across a long transcript by binning RSCanner structure counts (high BPC, low Shannon entropy positions) into fixed non-overlapping windows and rendering a final line plot with a 1D heatmap overlay, plus a ranked table of % structure content per bin. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad111
skills.summary: Visualize the density of RNA secondary structure across a long transcript by binning RSCanner structure counts (high BPC, low Shannon entropy positions) into fixed non-overlapping windows and rendering a final line plot with a 1D heatmap overlay, plus a ranked table of % structure content per bin.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks a predicted secondary structure or per-nucleotide Shannon entropy — RSCanner requires both a .ct/.dot-bracket structure and a shannon.txt file, so it cannot scan raw sequences alone. You need 3D or base-resolution structure validation rather than a windowed 1D density map of structure content along the transcript. You need overlapped/stacked feature windows rather than fixed non-overlapping bins — RSCanner's heatmap bins use a default 100-nt non-overlapping window.

skills.description: Use when a published article tabulates per-entity configuration values (e.g., per-technology cell barcode length, UMI length, and special-case flags) that must be reproduced as a structured, row-per-item table for downstream automation.
skills.name: structured-table-curation
skills.search_text: structured-table-curation Use when a published article tabulates per-entity configuration values (e.g., per-technology cell barcode length, UMI length, and special-case flags) that must be reproduced as a structured, row-per-item table for downstream automation. The input is narrative text describing parameters without a per-entity tabulation, so no row-per-technology table can be reliably built The target tool cannot detect input chemistry from pre-set parameters — UniverSC determines the appropriate 3' scRNA-seq chemistry automatically, so manual parameter lookup is unnecessary for supported chemistries The technology is a 5' scRNA-seq platform other than Chromium, which is outside UniverSC's supported scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Curates a published parameter catalogue—here, UniverSC's Table 1 of 40 pre-set single-cell technology processing settings—into a flat, machine-readable CSV with one row per item and validated columns. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34681-z
skills.summary: Curates a published parameter catalogue—here, UniverSC's Table 1 of 40 pre-set single-cell technology processing settings—into a flat, machine-readable CSV with one row per item and validated columns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is narrative text describing parameters without a per-entity tabulation, so no row-per-technology table can be reliably built The target tool cannot detect input chemistry from pre-set parameters — UniverSC determines the appropriate 3' scRNA-seq chemistry automatically, so manual parameter lookup is unnecessary for supported chemistries The technology is a 5' scRNA-seq platform other than Chromium, which is outside UniverSC's supported scope
