skills.description: Use when a per-cell, local assessment of embedding quality is needed: high-D Gaussian affinities (perplexity = 10% of samples) must be paired with Student-t affinities in 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings to compute per-cell KL divergences for data and null embeddings.
skills.name: student-t-embedding-affinity-computation
skills.search_text: student-t-embedding-affinity-computation Use when a per-cell, local assessment of embedding quality is needed: high-D Gaussian affinities (perplexity = 10% of samples) must be paired with Student-t affinities in 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings to compute per-cell KL divergences for data and null embeddings. When the goal is a single global embedding-quality score rather than local, per-cell error estimates — EMBEDR's design goal is explicitly per-cell estimates When only a low-dimensional embedding exists without the original high-dimensional data, since high-D Gaussian affinities cannot be computed When the input dataset is non-normalized — the null-generation process feeding the comparison has not been extended to non-normalized datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Computes the pairwise affinity structures that underlie EMBEDR's per-cell quality statistic (EES): Gaussian-kernel neighborhoods in the high-dimensional space and Student-t kernel affinities in each 2D embedding, which are compared per cell via Kullback-Leibler divergence. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2022.100443
skills.summary: Computes the pairwise affinity structures that underlie EMBEDR's per-cell quality statistic (EES): Gaussian-kernel neighborhoods in the high-dimensional space and Student-t kernel affinities in each 2D embedding, which are compared per cell via Kullback-Leibler divergence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single global embedding-quality score rather than local, per-cell error estimates — EMBEDR's design goal is explicitly per-cell estimates When only a low-dimensional embedding exists without the original high-dimensional data, since high-D Gaussian affinities cannot be computed When the input dataset is non-normalized — the null-generation process feeding the comparison has not been extended to non-normalized datasets

skills.description: Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) must be clustered without cell labels and the goal is an unsupervised, graph-aware embedding with soft cell-to-cluster assignments.
skills.name: student-t-soft-assignment-clustering
skills.search_text: student-t-soft-assignment-clustering Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) must be clustered without cell labels and the goal is an unsupervised, graph-aware embedding with soft cell-to-cluster assignments. Cells already carry trusted labels — the Interaction model path (Feature.py --label_mode True) is the appropriate branch instead Input is a raw count matrix not yet preprocessed — run preprocess.py first to generate the model feature file Goal is CCI inference rather than cell clustering — the cluster model alone does not predict interactions http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 DeepCCI's unsupervised cell-clustering step: an AE+GCN joint embedding is converted into soft cluster assignments Q via a Student's t-distribution kernel, refined against a target distribution P, and optimized end-to-end with KL-divergence losses to cluster single cells from scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad596
skills.summary: DeepCCI's unsupervised cell-clustering step: an AE+GCN joint embedding is converted into soft cluster assignments Q via a Student's t-distribution kernel, refined against a target distribution P, and optimized end-to-end with KL-divergence losses to cluster single cells from scRNA-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells already carry trusted labels — the Interaction model path (Feature.py --label_mode True) is the appropriate branch instead Input is a raw count matrix not yet preprocessed — run preprocess.py first to generate the model feature file Goal is CCI inference rather than cell clustering — the cluster model alone does not predict interactions

skills.description: Use when a pre-trained graph autoencoder embedding of scRNA-seq cells must be made clustering-friendly by jointly refining embeddings and cluster assignments via soft-assignment KL loss with Louvain-initialized centroids.
skills.name: students-t-soft-cluster-assignment
skills.search_text: students-t-soft-cluster-assignment Use when a pre-trained graph autoencoder embedding of scRNA-seq cells must be made clustering-friendly by jointly refining embeddings and cluster assignments via soft-assignment KL loss with Louvain-initialized centroids. Input is raw, un-preprocessed counts — the stage expects scTransform-preprocessed data and a pre-trained model, not raw matrices The goal is 2D visualization only — scGAE embeds to an intermediate dimension and uses t-SNE for 2D plots; direct 2D embedding by the graph autoencoder is not supported Only a first-pass embedding is needed without cluster labels — pre-training with model.train() alone suffices; clustering training is explicitly optional in the README http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 DEC-style alter-training stage for scGAE in which Student's-t soft cluster assignments (Q) and a sharpened target distribution (P) are learned jointly with graph-autoencoder reconstruction, yielding a clustering-friendly latent embedding from scRNA-seq data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-99003-7
skills.summary: DEC-style alter-training stage for scGAE in which Student's-t soft cluster assignments (Q) and a sharpened target distribution (P) are learned jointly with graph-autoencoder reconstruction, yielding a clustering-friendly latent embedding from scRNA-seq data.

skills.description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq from a heterogeneous tumor (multiple cells per patient/sample) should be decomposed into CNV-defined subclones, and mutually exclusive vs co-occurring CNV events plus a clonal tree are the target outputs.

skills.search_text: subclone-mutual-exclusivity-analysis Use when single-cell RNA-seq from a heterogeneous tumor (multiple cells per patient/sample) should be decomposed into CNV-defined subclones, and mutually exclusive vs co-occurring CNV events plus a clonal tree are the target outputs. Input is bulk RNA-seq or DNA data without single-cell resolution — clonal decomposition per cell is not possible; use bulk CaSpER workflows instead. Only 3'-end (e.g. DropSeq-style) scRNA-seq with sparse variants: BAF shift is measured only near 3' gene ends and signal may be too degraded for reliable subclonal LOH integration. A DNA- or SNV-based clonal inference tool (e.g. clonealign-style integration) is required — this skill infers clones from RNA-seq-derived CNVs and does not use high-quality heterozygous variant call sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Infers subclonal CNV architecture from single-cell RNA-seq using CaSpER's iterative HMM segmentation with patient-pooled BAF shift signal, then tests mutually exclusive and co-occurring CNV events (Fisher's exact test) and reconstructs a CNV-based clonal tree, as demonstrated on the 430-cell GBM dataset (MGH28/MGH30/MGH31). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13779-x
skills.summary: Infers subclonal CNV architecture from single-cell RNA-seq using CaSpER's iterative HMM segmentation with patient-pooled BAF shift signal, then tests mutually exclusive and co-occurring CNV events (Fisher's exact test) and reconstructs a CNV-based clonal tree, as demonstrated on the 430-cell GBM dataset (MGH28/MGH30/MGH31).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk RNA-seq or DNA data without single-cell resolution — clonal decomposition per cell is not possible; use bulk CaSpER workflows instead. Only 3'-end (e.g. DropSeq-style) scRNA-seq with sparse variants: BAF shift is measured only near 3' gene ends and signal may be too degraded for reliable subclonal LOH integration. skills.description: Use when analyzing multi-subject dynamic networks with MuDCoD where subjects fall into natural groups (e.g., healthy vs diseased), and the global β subject-smoothing term inappropriately pulls subjects toward an all-subject mean.
skills.name: subject-smoothing-regularization-modification
skills.search_text: subject-smoothing-regularization-modification Use when analyzing multi-subject dynamic networks with MuDCoD where subjects fall into natural groups (e.g., healthy vs diseased), and the global β subject-smoothing term inappropriately pulls subjects toward an all-subject mean. skills.search_text: subsampling-clustering-classification-pipeline Use when clustering large scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., tens of thousands of cells like the 49,300-cell Macosko retina matrix) where full O(n^2) clustering is infeasible, or when clustering consistency across subsampling ratios (e.g., 5% vs 10%) must be assessed. The dataset is small enough for full (non-subsampled) clustering, where ssc.run(subsampling=FALSE) applies and subsampling bias need not be managed The task requires supervised cell-type annotation from known labels rather than unsupervised clustering of a subsample with k-NN label propagation A clustering algorithm incompatible with the subsampling-classification decomposition is required (the paper benchmarks general algorithms, but SSCC's Spearman feature engineering is designed for its own framework) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A two-stage (SCC/SSCC) clustering pipeline for large-scale scRNA-seq data in which a random cell subsample is clustered (e.g., k-means) and remaining cells are assigned labels by k-NN classification; the SSCC variant adds Spearman-correlation-based feature engineering and random projection to reduce subsampling bias and improve accuracy, robustness, and consistency. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: A two-stage (SCC/SSCC) clustering pipeline for large-scale scRNA-seq data in which a random cell subsample is clustered (e.g., k-means) and remaining cells are assigned labels by k-NN classification; the SSCC variant adds Spearman-correlation-based feature engineering and random projection to reduce subsampling bias and improve accuracy, robustness, and consistency.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset is small enough for full (non-subsampled) clustering, where ssc.run(subsampling=FALSE) applies and subsampling bias need not be managed The task requires supervised cell-type annotation from known labels rather than unsupervised clustering of a subsample with k-NN label propagation A clustering algorithm incompatible with the subsampling-classification decomposition is required (the paper benchmarks general algorithms, but SSCC's Spearman feature engineering is designed for its own framework)

skills.description: Use when comparing the robustness of pseudotime inference methods (e.g., DTFLOW, Scanpy, Monocle2) on a single-cell dataset where orderings from random cell subsamples should be checked against the full-data ordering.
skills.name: subsampling-robustness-analysis
skills.search_text: subsampling-robustness-analysis Use when comparing the robustness of pseudotime inference methods (e.g., DTFLOW, Scanpy, Monocle2) on a single-cell dataset where orderings from random cell subsamples should be checked against the full-data ordering. The goal is accuracy against known time stages (e.g., Kendall rank correlation against developmental stages), not subsampling stability — use the paper's accuracy protocol instead The dataset has so few cells that removing 10% of cells would eliminate rare developmental states or branches Only a single fixed train/test split is needed rather than repeated random subsampling (e.g., the one-off 2500-cell MMP subsample without repetition) http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Assesses pseudotime-ordering stability of DTFLOW, Scanpy, and Monocle2 by repeatedly subsampling single-cell datasets (90% of ME cells 50 times; 2500 of 2730 MMP cells) and computing Spearman rank correlations of subsample orderings against full-data orderings, aggregated into mean, standard deviation, and variance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2020.08.003
skills.summary: Assesses pseudotime-ordering stability of DTFLOW, Scanpy, and Monocle2 by repeatedly subsampling single-cell datasets (90% of ME cells 50 times; 2500 of 2730 MMP cells) and computing Spearman rank correlations of subsample orderings against full-data orderings, aggregated into mean, standard deviation, and variance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is accuracy against known time stages (e.g., Kendall rank correlation against developmental stages), not subsampling stability — use the paper's accuracy protocol instead The dataset has so few cells that removing 10% of cells would eliminate rare developmental states or branches Only a single fixed train/test split is needed rather than repeated random subsampling (e.g., the one-off 2500-cell MMP subsample without repetition)

skills.description: Use when validating that features engineered from scRNA-seq data (e.g., Spearman-correlation features from sscClust) are robust to subsampling fluctuations before trusting a subsampling-based clustering strategy.
skills.name: subsampling-robustness-assessment
skills.search_text: subsampling-robustness-assessment Use when validating that features engineered from scRNA-seq data (e.g., Spearman-correlation features from sscClust) are robust to subsampling fluctuations before trusting a subsampling-based clustering strategy. When the goal is a single full-data clustering run rather than a robustness assessment across subsampling rates. When no ground-truth cell-type labels are available, since silhouette values must be computed against true labels. When evaluating subsampling bias of methods that do not use a subsampling-clustering-classification (SCC) strategy, as the rationale is specific to SCC-style biases. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A validation procedure from the SSCC paper that tests whether Spearman correlation-based engineered features remain consistent with true cell-type labels across cell-subsampling rates (10%–50%), using per-cell silhouette values against true labels as the robustness metric. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2018.10.003
skills.summary: A validation procedure from the SSCC paper that tests whether Spearman correlation-based engineered features remain consistent with true cell-type labels across cell-subsampling rates (10%–50%), using per-cell silhouette values against true labels as the robustness metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a single full-data clustering run rather than a robustness assessment across subsampling rates. When no ground-truth cell-type labels are available, since silhouette values must be computed against true labels. When evaluating subsampling bias of methods that do not use a subsampling-clustering-classification (SCC) strategy, as the rationale is specific to SCC-style biases.

skills.description: Use when comparing low-dimensional structure (top-k PCA subspaces) between an original scRNA-seq matrix and its downsampled or imputed version, to test whether imputation preserves the signal.
skills.name: subspace-angle-computation
skills.search_text: subspace-angle-computation Use when comparing low-dimensional structure (top-k PCA subspaces) between an original scRNA-seq matrix and its downsampled or imputed version, to test whether imputation preserves the signal. Input is not a pair/matched set of original vs. downsampled (or imputed) scRNA-seq expression matrices — the angle is only meaningful between comparable PC subspaces The number of signal PCs cannot be determined from the original dataset (e.g., no jackstraw p-values available), since the same k must be used across conditions The goal is imputation quality of individual entries (false-zero recovery) rather than preservation of global low-dimensional structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies preservation of biological signal in downsampled scRNA-seq data by computing the subspace angle between the top-k signal PCs of an original dataset and the PCs of the downsampled dataset, before and after ALRA imputation, for Baron, Chen, La Manno, and Zeisel et al. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Quantifies preservation of biological signal in downsampled scRNA-seq data by computing the subspace angle between the top-k signal PCs of an original dataset and the PCs of the downsampled dataset, before and after ALRA imputation, for Baron, Chen, La Manno, and Zeisel et al.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a pair/matched set of original vs. downsampled (or imputed) scRNA-seq expression matrices — the angle is only meaningful between comparable PC subspaces The number of signal PCs cannot be determined from the original dataset (e.g., no jackstraw p-values available), since the same k must be used across conditions The goal is imputation quality of individual entries (false-zero recovery) rather than preservation of global low-dimensional structure

skills.description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., CPM/TPM/FPKM values) contains zero entries suspected of being dropout events, and the goal is to improve downstream cell-type clustering (k-means ARI) before imputation-vulnerable analyses.
skills.name: subspace-regression-gene-imputation
skills.search_text: subspace-regression-gene-imputation Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., CPM/TPM/FPKM values) contains zero entries suspected of being dropout events, and the goal is to improve downstream cell-type clustering (k-means ARI) before imputation-vulnerable analyses. The input contains no zero-valued entries or zeros are known to be true biological zeros — scISR's testing module is designed to distinguish dropouts, but imputing genuine zeros risks introducing false signals The analysis goal requires imputing all zero entries uniformly (e.g., some model-based baselines) — scISR intentionally alters only entries flagged as dropout-affected by hyper-geometric testing Downstream analysis is robust to dropouts or uses methods that internally handle sparsity (e.g., certain count-model tools), where over-smoothing by imputation could remove meaningful cell-to-cell stochasticity http://edamontology.org/topic_3516 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies scISR (single-cell Imputation via Subspace Regression) to recover dropout-induced zero values in scRNA-seq count matrices: hyper-geometric over/under-representation testing (p < 0.01) segregates zeros into imputable vs. trustworthy sets, and a generalized linear regression built on the 10 most Pearson-correlated genes imputes the imputable entries. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-022-06500-4
skills.summary: Applies scISR (single-cell Imputation via Subspace Regression) to recover dropout-induced zero values in scRNA-seq count matrices: hyper-geometric over/under-representation testing (p < 0.01) segregates zeros into imputable vs. trustworthy sets, and a generalized linear regression built on the 10 most Pearson-correlated genes imputes the imputable entries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input contains no zero-valued entries or zeros are known to be true biological zeros — scISR's testing module is designed to distinguish dropouts, but imputing genuine zeros risks introducing false signals The analysis goal requires imputing all zero entries uniformly (e.g., some model-based baselines) — scISR intentionally alters only entries flagged as dropout-affected by hyper-geometric testing Downstream analysis is robust to dropouts or uses methods that internally handle sparsity (e.g., certain count-model tools), where over-smoothing by imputation could remove meaningful cell-to-cell stochasticity

skills.description: Use when a supervised RNA-seq subtype classifier (mLR with Lasso/L1 or Ridge/L2) has been fitted on a feature-selected gene space and you need CV accuracy, held-out test accuracy, and per-class recall/precision tables to compare feature spaces.
skills.name: subtype-classification-cross-validation-evaluation
skills.search_text: subtype-classification-cross-validation-evaluation Use when a supervised RNA-seq subtype classifier (mLR with Lasso/L1 or Ridge/L2) has been fitted on a feature-selected gene space and you need CV accuracy, held-out test accuracy, and per-class recall/precision tables to compare feature spaces. When no held-out test split or cross-validation scheme is available and only a single reference-based PAM50 call per sample exists — use the AWCA_PAM50_BC_subtyping code instead When the goal is unsupervised centroid-correlation subtyping rather than evaluation of a trained supervised mLR classifier When training labels were themselves produced by the PAM50 assay on the same gene panel — accuracy estimates are biased and the paper explicitly flags such performances as biased http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Estimates and verifies the generalization performance of regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) breast cancer intrinsic-subtype classifiers by combining cross-validation on a TCGA training split with held-out test evaluation, recording overall accuracy and per-subtype recalls. It operationalizes the paper's finding that ad-hoc gene selection on the global transcriptome improves mLR subtyping beyond the whole-transcriptome feature space. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Estimates and verifies the generalization performance of regularized multiclass logistic regression (mLR) breast cancer intrinsic-subtype classifiers by combining cross-validation on a TCGA training split with held-out test evaluation, recording overall accuracy and per-subtype recalls. It operationalizes the paper's finding that ad-hoc gene selection on the global transcriptome improves mLR subtyping beyond the whole-transcriptome feature space.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no held-out test split or cross-validation scheme is available and only a single reference-based PAM50 call per sample exists — use the AWCA_PAM50_BC_subtyping code instead When the goal is unsupervised centroid-correlation subtyping rather than evaluation of a trained supervised mLR classifier When training labels were themselves produced by the PAM50 assay on the same gene panel — accuracy estimates are biased and the paper explicitly flags such performances as biased

skills.description: Use when a trained subtype classifier (e.g., DeepCC labels from get_DeepCC_label) has been applied to validation cohorts with clinical metadata and you must show its clinical relevance equals or exceeds a benchmark system like PAM50.
skills.name: subtype-classifier-comparative-evaluation
skills.search_text: subtype-classifier-comparative-evaluation Use when a trained subtype classifier (e.g., DeepCC labels from get_DeepCC_label) has been applied to validation cohorts with clinical metadata and you must show its clinical relevance equals or exceeds a benchmark system like PAM50. The goal is de novo discovery of subtypes — DeepCC is a supervised classification framework 'not clustering of cancer patients', so a classifier-evaluation skill on predefined subtypes is inappropriate for unsupervised discovery The input is raw expression data without predicted subtype labels or clinical receptor/DFS metadata — receptor association and survival testing cannot be performed and the classifier must first be run (getFunctionalSpectra then get_DeepCC_label) There is no established benchmark (e.g., PAM50) available for the same samples, making a comparative evaluation impossible http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a newly predicted molecular subtype classification (e.g., DeepCC-derived labels) against an established standard (PAM50) by testing concordance with known receptor biology (ER/PR/HER2 via Fisher's exact tests) and clinical outcome separation (Kaplan-Meier DFS with log-rank tests) across independent validation cohorts. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41389-019-0157-8
skills.summary: Benchmark a newly predicted molecular subtype classification (e.g., DeepCC-derived labels) against an established standard (PAM50) by testing concordance with known receptor biology (ER/PR/HER2 via Fisher's exact tests) and clinical outcome separation (Kaplan-Meier DFS with log-rank tests) across independent validation cohorts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo discovery of subtypes — DeepCC is a supervised classification framework 'not clustering of cancer patients', so a classifier-evaluation skill on predefined subtypes is inappropriate for unsupervised discovery The input is raw expression data without predicted subtype labels or clinical receptor/DFS metadata — receptor association and survival testing cannot be performed and the classifier must first be run (getFunctionalSpectra then get_DeepCC_label) There is no established benchmark (e.g., PAM50) available for the same samples, making a comparative evaluation impossible

skills.description: Use when subtype calls produced by AWCA or mLR models on RNA-seq expression matrices (TCGA RSEM, GSE96058 FPKM, PanCA, GSE81538) must be scored against published PAM50 labels or against another caller's calls via concordance/accuracy.
skills.name: subtype-concordance-evaluation
skills.search_text: subtype-concordance-evaluation Use when subtype calls produced by AWCA or mLR models on RNA-seq expression matrices (TCGA RSEM, GSE96058 FPKM, PanCA, GSE81538) must be scored against published PAM50 labels or against another caller's calls via concordance/accuracy. Input is raw/unnormalized RNA-seq data — callers must be applied to expression matrices normalized the same way as the training cohorts (TCGA RSEM, GSE96058 FPKM) Data are Affymetrix microarray profiles (e.g. GSE4922, GSE1456) — AWCA-based classification there used log2-transformed microarray data, a distinct setting Subtype labels for the comparison were themselves not PAM50-derived — accuracy vs published PAM50 calls is acknowledged as biased toward PAM50-gene-based methods Evaluates breast cancer intrinsic-subtyping callers (AWCA-PAM50 and regularized multiclass logistic regression, mLR) by computing concordance and classification accuracy of their subtype calls against published PAM50 reference labels across internal and external RNA-seq cohorts (TCGA, GSE96058, PanCA, GSE81538). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Evaluates breast cancer intrinsic-subtyping callers (AWCA-PAM50 and regularized multiclass logistic regression, mLR) by computing concordance and classification accuracy of their subtype calls against published PAM50 reference labels across internal and external RNA-seq cohorts (TCGA, GSE96058, PanCA, GSE81538).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw/unnormalized RNA-seq data — callers must be applied to expression matrices normalized the same way as the training cohorts (TCGA RSEM, GSE96058 FPKM) Data are Affymetrix microarray profiles (e.g. GSE4922, GSE1456) — AWCA-based classification there used log2-transformed microarray data, a distinct setting Subtype labels for the comparison were themselves not PAM50-derived — accuracy vs published PAM50 calls is acknowledged as biased toward PAM50-gene-based methods

skills.description: Use when RCC (or another consensus clustering run) has produced cluster assignments on an expression matrix and you need per-cluster marker genes and signature-enrichment evidence to characterize novel subtypes.
skills.name: subtype-marker-identification
skills.search_text: subtype-marker-identification Use when RCC (or another consensus clustering run) has produced cluster assignments on an expression matrix and you need per-cluster marker genes and signature-enrichment evidence to characterize novel subtypes. When no cluster assignments exist yet — run RCC_clus first; geneMarkers and ssgsea operate on clustered output When subtypes are already known and only supervised classification is needed, rather than novel subtype discovery When clusters contain fewer samples than the minSample filter, making attribute comparison and survival analysis unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Derives and validates marker genes for novel subtypes discovered by Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) on bulk or single-cell transcriptomic data, using geneMarkers and ssgsea to assign distinct marker signatures and quantify signature enrichment (e.g., proneural geneSet) per cluster. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Derives and validates marker genes for novel subtypes discovered by Recursive Consensus Clustering (RCC) on bulk or single-cell transcriptomic data, using geneMarkers and ssgsea to assign distinct marker signatures and quantify signature enrichment (e.g., proneural geneSet) per cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no cluster assignments exist yet — run RCC_clus first; geneMarkers and ssgsea operate on clustered output When subtypes are already known and only supervised classification is needed, rather than novel subtype discovery When clusters contain fewer samples than the minSample filter, making attribute comparison and survival analysis unreliable

skills.description: Use when building subtype classification templates for pre-clinical CRC models (cell lines, organoids, PDXs) where microenvironment-derived gene signals must be excluded from the marker set.
skills.name: subtype-marker-selection
skills.search_text: subtype-marker-selection Use when building subtype classification templates for pre-clinical CRC models (cell lines, organoids, PDXs) where microenvironment-derived gene signals must be excluded from the marker set. Samples with a different human stromal component than primary CRCs, e.g. patient biopsies of metastatic CRC — CMScaller is explicitly not recommended in its current implementation for such samples. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and for which a dedicated classifier would be required. Highly selected datasets whose molecular distributions severely deviate from pCRC cohorts (e.g. metastatic samples), where caution is warranted. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Reconstructs CMScaller's cancer cell-intrinsic CMS marker filtering pipeline, which successively narrows primary CRC (pCRC) subtype-vs-rest differential expression hits by cell line expression variation and by expression loss upon xenotransplantation, so the final template reflects cancer-cell rather than stromal/immune signals. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-017-16747-x
skills.summary: Reconstructs CMScaller's cancer cell-intrinsic CMS marker filtering pipeline, which successively narrows primary CRC (pCRC) subtype-vs-rest differential expression hits by cell line expression variation and by expression loss upon xenotransplantation, so the final template reflects cancer-cell rather than stromal/immune signals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with a different human stromal component than primary CRCs, e.g. patient biopsies of metastatic CRC — CMScaller is explicitly not recommended in its current implementation for such samples. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data, which is exceedingly noisy and for which a dedicated classifier would be required. Highly selected datasets whose molecular distributions severely deviate from pCRC cohorts (e.g. metastatic samples), where caution is warranted.

skills.description: Use when reproducing a cross-dataset cell label similarity map (e.g., B cell subtypes across HCC, NSCLC, BRCA references) and checking whether recomputed Jaccard values reproduce a reported pattern from the scCancer2 paper.
skills.name: subtype-similarity-pattern-validation
skills.search_text: subtype-similarity-pattern-validation Use when reproducing a cross-dataset cell label similarity map (e.g., B cell subtypes across HCC, NSCLC, BRCA references) and checking whether recomputed Jaccard values reproduce a reported pattern from the scCancer2 paper. When the goal is de novo cell subtype annotation for a single dataset without any cross-dataset label comparison — use predCellType/runCellSubtypeClassify directly instead of the similarity-map validation workflow When the input is raw count data that has not been rough-labeled and fine-labeled by the scCancer2 classification pipeline — similarityCalculation requires integrated fine labels as input When comparing labels across datasets where the reference label sets are not preserved from published atlases (the method relies on fully preserving original labeling in cell atlases) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Validates cross-dataset cell-subtype label similarity patterns by recomputing Jaccard similarity matrices with scCancer2's similarityCalculation on integrated fine labels, and confirming specific label-vs-reference similarity values (e.g., HCC 'Lymphoid-B' naive vs memory B cell rows) match published figures such as Fig. 3A / Section 3.3. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae028
skills.summary: Validates cross-dataset cell-subtype label similarity patterns by recomputing Jaccard similarity matrices with scCancer2's similarityCalculation on integrated fine labels, and confirming specific label-vs-reference similarity values (e.g., HCC 'Lymphoid-B' naive vs memory B cell rows) match published figures such as Fig. 3A / Section 3.3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is de novo cell subtype annotation for a single dataset without any cross-dataset label comparison — use predCellType/runCellSubtypeClassify directly instead of the similarity-map validation workflow When the input is raw count data that has not been rough-labeled and fine-labeled by the scCancer2 classification pipeline — similarityCalculation requires integrated fine labels as input When comparing labels across datasets where the reference label sets are not preserved from published atlases (the method relies on fully preserving original labeling in cell atlases)

skills.description: Use when you need to cross-compare intrinsic breast cancer subtype callers (Prosigna, standard PAM50, AWCA-based PAM50) on the same RNA-seq profiles and visualize call concordance plus ROR prognostic agreement.
skills.name: subtyping-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: subtyping-comparison-visualization Use when you need to cross-compare intrinsic breast cancer subtype callers (Prosigna, standard PAM50, AWCA-based PAM50) on the same RNA-seq profiles and visualize call concordance plus ROR prognostic agreement. Input is a single-sample classification task rather than a cross-caller comparison — use AWCA_PAM50_BC_subtyping or mLR directly Expression data are microarray-based (e.g. Affymetrix GSE4922/GSE1456) and the goal is mLR signature validation rather than Prosigna-vs-PAM50 ROR comparison No survival endpoints are available, so the 10-year overall survival discrimination cannot be evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduce in-silico Prosigna subtyping and ROR scoring on TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq PAM50 profiles, compare Prosigna calls/ROR against standard and AWCA-based PAM50 ROR-C calls for 10-year overall survival discrimination, and render the agreement as Figure 3 (figure3_prosigna_vs_pam50.png). transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Reproduce in-silico Prosigna subtyping and ROR scoring on TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq PAM50 profiles, compare Prosigna calls/ROR against standard and AWCA-based PAM50 ROR-C calls for 10-year overall survival discrimination, and render the agreement as Figure 3 (figure3_prosigna_vs_pam50.png).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample classification task rather than a cross-caller comparison — use AWCA_PAM50_BC_subtyping or mLR directly Expression data are microarray-based (e.g. Affymetrix GSE4922/GSE1456) and the goal is mLR signature validation rather than Prosigna-vs-PAM50 ROR comparison No survival endpoints are available, so the 10-year overall survival discrimination cannot be evaluated

skills.search_text: summary-statistic-fine-mapping-with-allelic-heterogeneity Use when you have summary statistics (z-scores or betas+SEs) plus a reference LD matrix for multiple traits/tissues over the same variants, and need fine-mapping with colocalization where multiple causal alleles may mask tissue specificity. Loci whose disease effects are mediated by coding variants that may not show eQTL effects — CAFEH cannot explore these Studies with large LD differences (e.g., different ancestries) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix and inference may be biased Datasets with missing variants in the effect-size matrix — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Jointly fine-map and colocalize eQTL and GWAS signals across multiple traits/tissues using CAFEH from summary statistics, accounting for allelic heterogeneity by fitting multiple causal components per locus. Used here to quantify how tissue-specific eQTL components relate to GWAS causality across UK Biobank traits and GTEx v8 tissues. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Jointly fine-map and colocalize eQTL and GWAS signals across multiple traits/tissues using CAFEH from summary statistics, accounting for allelic heterogeneity by fitting multiple causal components per locus. Used here to quantify how tissue-specific eQTL components relate to GWAS causality across UK Biobank traits and GTEx v8 tissues.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose disease effects are mediated by coding variants that may not show eQTL effects — CAFEH cannot explore these Studies with large LD differences (e.g., different ancestries) — CAFEH relies on a single LD matrix and inference may be biased Datasets with missing variants in the effect-size matrix — CAFEH implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested datasets

skills.description: Use when OTTERS Stage II per-gene TWAS Z-scores from five training models must be rescaled via genomic control and converted to p values for downstream ACAT-O omnibus aggregation.
skills.name: summary-statistics-zscore-to-pvalue-conversion
skills.search_text: summary-statistics-zscore-to-pvalue-conversion Use when OTTERS Stage II per-gene TWAS Z-scores from five training models must be rescaled via genomic control and converted to p values for downstream ACAT-O omnibus aggregation. Input is already ACAT-O omnibus p values or single-method TWAS p values that do not require cross-method genomic-control harmonization. Reference GWAS summary statistics for a single gene need conversion to p values inside Stage I weight training (e.g. PRS-CS input) rather than Stage II TWAS omnibus preparation. Z-scores come from individual-level reference methods (e.g. FUSION/PrediXcan) whose association testing pipeline has its own calibration rather than OTTERS per-method genomic control. http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts per-gene TWAS Z-scores from OTTERS Stage II (testing.py) into two-sided normal p values and applies genomic control per training model (P0.001, P0.05, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS) so the median p value equals 0.5 before ACAT-O omnibus aggregation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36862-w
skills.summary: Converts per-gene TWAS Z-scores from OTTERS Stage II (testing.py) into two-sided normal p values and applies genomic control per training model (P0.001, P0.05, lassosum, SDPR, PRS-CS) so the median p value equals 0.5 before ACAT-O omnibus aggregation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already ACAT-O omnibus p values or single-method TWAS p values that do not require cross-method genomic-control harmonization. Reference GWAS summary statistics for a single gene need conversion to p values inside Stage I weight training (e.g. PRS-CS input) rather than Stage II TWAS omnibus preparation. Z-scores come from individual-level reference methods (e.g. FUSION/PrediXcan) whose association testing pipeline has its own calibration rather than OTTERS per-method genomic control.

skills.description: Use when building or querying a PAC index and you need k-mers grouped by minimizer into super-k-mers, split into 4^p partition files, and resolved via per-partition inverted Bloom filters.

skills.search_text: super-kmer-extraction Use when building or querying a PAC index and you need k-mers grouped by minimizer into super-k-mers, split into 4^p partition files, and resolved via per-partition inverted Bloom filters. The collection is small enough that BLAST-like exact search is routine — PAC only lists datasets that may contain the query (approximate membership), not alignments You need exact containment calls with no false positives — Bloom filter false positives are controlled only by sizing -b, not eliminated The input should retain k-mers seen only once — the -u option filters singletons, so counts relying on unique k-mers are incompatible http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Groups consecutive k-mers sharing a minimizer into super-k-mers and routes them into minimizer-defined partitions of a PAC index, so that querying successive k-mers of a super-k-mer resolves within one small per-partition inverted Bloom filter structure. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad225
skills.summary: Groups consecutive k-mers sharing a minimizer into super-k-mers and routes them into minimizer-defined partitions of a PAC index, so that querying successive k-mers of a super-k-mer resolves within one small per-partition inverted Bloom filter structure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The collection is small enough that BLAST-like exact search is routine — PAC only lists datasets that may contain the query (approximate membership), not alignments You need exact containment calls with no false positives — Bloom filter false positives are controlled only by sizing -b, not eliminated The input should retain k-mers seen only once — the -u option filters singletons, so counts relying on unique k-mers are incompatible

skills.description: Use when training scRNA-seq data with known cell labels are available and you must quantify whether a supervised annotation method (e.g. NeuCA) outperforms existing supervised or unsupervised alternatives under varying train/test splits or conditions.
skills.name: supervised-cell-label-benchmarking
skills.search_text: supervised-cell-label-benchmarking Use when training scRNA-seq data with known cell labels are available and you must quantify whether a supervised annotation method (e.g. NeuCA) outperforms existing supervised or unsupervised alternatives under varying train/test splits or conditions. Novel/unknown cell types may exist in the testing data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the reference/training data No training data with known labels exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised methods are then the only viable solution The goal is novelty detection of rare cells rather than exhaustive label assignment; identify rare/unknown cells first (e.g. inferCNV or copyKAT for malignant cells) before applying NeuCA http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark supervised cell label assignment (NeuCA and baselines such as scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) against unsupervised clustering (Seurat, SC3) on scRNA-seq data with known labels, using accurately assigned rate and adjusted Rand index (ARI) as metrics across training-size, testing-size, and cross-condition settings. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-04473-4
skills.summary: Benchmark supervised cell label assignment (NeuCA and baselines such as scmap-cluster, scmap-cell, CHETAH) against unsupervised clustering (Seurat, SC3) on scRNA-seq data with known labels, using accurately assigned rate and adjusted Rand index (ARI) as metrics across training-size, testing-size, and cross-condition settings.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Novel/unknown cell types may exist in the testing data — NeuCA assumes all cell types in the new sample already exist in the reference/training data No training data with known labels exist for the tissue of interest — unsupervised methods are then the only viable solution The goal is novelty detection of rare cells rather than exhaustive label assignment; identify rare/unknown cells first (e.g. inferCNV or copyKAT for malignant cells) before applying NeuCA

The goal is clustering or unsupervised annotation — the benchmark is specifically for supervised classifiers given annotated reference labels The task is model accuracy on real annotated atlases (e.g. Tabula Muris, MOCA) rather than runtime scaling on simulated count matrices Data require cross-species mapping (human-mouse HomoloGene conversion) or null-dataset false-positive control, which are separate SciBet capabilities not exercised here http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks supervised single-cell type classifiers (SciBet, scmap, Seurat v3) for classification speed and accuracy across dataset sizes, from 1,000 to 50,000 simulated cells, using the multinomial-MLE SciBet model as the reference method. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-15523-2
skills.summary: Benchmarks supervised single-cell type classifiers (SciBet, scmap, Seurat v3) for classification speed and accuracy across dataset sizes, from 1,000 to 50,000 simulated cells, using the multinomial-MLE SciBet model as the reference method.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is clustering or unsupervised annotation — the benchmark is specifically for supervised classifiers given annotated reference labels The task is model accuracy on real annotated atlases (e.g. Tabula Muris, MOCA) rather than runtime scaling on simulated count matrices Data require cross-species mapping (human-mouse HomoloGene conversion) or null-dataset false-positive control, which are separate SciBet capabilities not exercised here

skills.summary: Supervised cell-type label transfer in which a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. HBMP2-spleen-2) is projected into a reference dataset's PCA latent space (40 components, fit on HBMP3-spleen-CC3) using scanpy Ingest, transferring reference annotations to the query. skills.search_text: svd-based-pca-module-projection Use when a normalized gene expression matrix (genes as rows, samples as columns) must be reduced to per-gene-set activity scores with statistical significance, distinguishing shifted from overdispersed modules. The expression matrix is raw/unnormalized counts — rRoma explicitly requires normalized data (cpm, vst, or similar) before PCA projection. The goal is gene-level differential expression rather than coordinated gene set activity — a DE tool (edgeR/DESeq2) is the appropriate choice instead. Datasets contain many missing values that have not been imputed — the README recommends using datasets for which missing values have already been imputed rather than relying on the mice fill step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantify gene set (module) activity by computing the first principal component via SVD on the subset of a globally centered expression matrix corresponding to each module, then assess significance of L1 (% variance explained by PC1) and Median Exp (median sample projection on PC1) against random gene set nulls. This is the core rROMA procedure for representing module activity from transcriptomic or proteomic data. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-024-00331-x

skills.description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) contains a large fraction of zeros (e.g. >90% with droplet-based data) and you need a low-rank approximation to complete technical zeros before adaptive thresholding.
skills.name: svd-low-rank-approximation
skills.search_text: svd-low-rank-approximation Use when a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) contains a large fraction of zeros (e.g. >90% with droplet-based data) and you need a low-rank approximation to complete technical zeros before adaptive thresholding. The input is not an scRNA-seq expression matrix or the cells/genes orientation is transposed — ALRA explicitly requires cells as rows and genes as columns The data is not assumed to be non-negative and low-rank (e.g. already fully denoised or a different modality where low-rank structure does not hold) All zeros must be treated as missing data and every gene imputed as expressed (e.g. when using a MAGIC/DCA-style approach is desired instead of zero-preserving imputation) http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Compute a rank-k approximation of a scRNA-seq expression matrix via (randomized) SVD as the core denoising step of ALRA, exploiting the non-negativity and low-rank structure of expression data so that subsequent thresholding can impute technical (dropout) zeros while preserving biological zeros. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-27729-z
skills.summary: Compute a rank-k approximation of a scRNA-seq expression matrix via (randomized) SVD as the core denoising step of ALRA, exploiting the non-negativity and low-rank structure of expression data so that subsequent thresholding can impute technical (dropout) zeros while preserving biological zeros.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not an scRNA-seq expression matrix or the cells/genes orientation is transposed — ALRA explicitly requires cells as rows and genes as columns The data is not assumed to be non-negative and low-rank (e.g. already fully denoised or a different modality where low-rank structure does not hold) All zeros must be treated as missing data and every gene imputed as expressed (e.g. when using a MAGIC/DCA-style approach is desired instead of zero-preserving imputation)

skills.search_text: svd-pathway-activation-score-computation Use when a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix must be transformed into a pathway-by-cell activity matrix (pca_scCell_mat) prior to downstream association testing, or when quantifying how pathway-level aggregation reduces single-cell sparsity. skills.search_text: svm-phase-classification-and-age-regression Use when benchmarking feature selection methods on proteomic-imaging single-cell data with ground truth labels, to test whether a top-p feature subset (e.g. p=30) preserves biologically meaningful signals like cell cycle phase and continuous cell age. skills.search_text: swapped-read-fraction-regression-estimation Use when raw demultiplexed scRNA-seq FASTQs from patterned flow-cell machines (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) are available with per-sample index barcodes, and you need to quantify the fraction of barcode-swapped (mislabelled) reads or validate that swapping is machine-specific. The data come from non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500 alone) where swapping is expected to be near background, so the regression primarily serves as a control rather than a correction target Reads lack sample-index barcodes that permit assignment to impossible combinations (e.g. uniquely barcoded molecules or UMI-only designs), so no swapped-read counts per impossible combination can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Estimates the fraction of barcode-swapped reads in Illumina single-cell RNA-seq experiments by regressing observed swapped reads for each impossible sample-index combination against the reads available for swapping, and taking the gradient as the swapping fraction; serves both to quantify HiSeq 4000 swapping (~2.5%) and as a control on HiSeq 2500 runs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-018-05083-x
skills.summary: Estimates the fraction of barcode-swapped reads in Illumina single-cell RNA-seq experiments by regressing observed swapped reads for each impossible sample-index combination against the reads available for swapping, and taking the gradient as the swapping fraction; serves both to quantify HiSeq 4000 swapping (~2.5%) and as a control on HiSeq 2500 runs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data come from non-patterned flow-cell instruments (e.g. HiSeq 2500 alone) where swapping is expected to be near background, so the regression primarily serves as a control rather than a correction target Reads lack sample-index barcodes that permit assignment to impossible combinations (e.g. uniquely barcoded molecules or UMI-only designs), so no swapped-read counts per impossible combination can be computed

skills.search_text: symphony-query-mapping Use when an mRNA-only query dataset must be placed into an existing integrated reference atlas (e.g., a CITE-seq memory T-cell reference of ~395,373 cells) to transfer cell-type annotations or infer modalities absent from the query, such as surface proteins. The goal is discovery of novel cell types that failed to map — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone and mapping metrics may be less informative for a novel population very similar to an existing reference population Query and reference peak sets differ and no standardization exists (e.g., scATAC-seq feature selection), since the optimal feature-selection approach for mapping is not defined in that setting The input is already a feature/annotation table rather than raw single-cell expression data requiring projection into a reference embedding http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Builds a compressed Symphony reference from a Harmony-integrated single-cell atlas and maps mRNA-only query cells into the stable reference embedding within seconds, enabling transfer of reference-defined annotations such as per-cell surface protein inference from a multimodal CITE-seq reference. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-25957-x
skills.summary: Builds a compressed Symphony reference from a Harmony-integrated single-cell atlas and maps mRNA-only query cells into the stable reference embedding within seconds, enabling transfer of reference-defined annotations such as per-cell surface protein inference from a multimodal CITE-seq reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is discovery of novel cell types that failed to map — Symphony does not replace de novo analyses of the query alone and mapping metrics may be less informative for a novel population very similar to an existing reference population Query and reference peak sets differ and no standardization exists (e.g., scATAC-seq feature selection), since the optimal feature-selection approach for mapping is not defined in that setting The input is already a feature/annotation table rather than raw single-cell expression data requiring projection into a reference embedding

skills.name: symsim-parameter-configuration

skills.summary: Configure and run SymSim v0.0.0.9000 in R to simulate large-scale single-cell RNA-seq tree differentiation trajectories (10,000 cells, 20,000 genes, 4 cell types) with known ground-truth cell types and latent progression, providing controlled benchmarks for evaluating trajectory-preserving feature selection methods.

skills.description: Use when reproducing the scTriangulate benchmarking analyses that rely on alternative clustering results (ICGS2, Monocle3, Seurat3, curated annotations) from a prior study deposited only in Synapse, not regenerable from GEO raw counts.
skills.name: synapse-dataset-retrieval
skills.search_text: synapse-dataset-retrieval Use when reproducing the scTriangulate benchmarking analyses that rely on alternative clustering results (ICGS2, Monocle3, Seurat3, curated annotations) from a prior study deposited only in Synapse, not regenerable from GEO raw counts. When the target dataset is raw count matrix data available directly from GEO (e.g., GSE117825, GSM4949911) or the 10x Genomics website — download those from their native sources instead of Synapse. When the goal is fresh unsupervised clustering rather than reusing prior study annotations — no Synapse retrieval is needed; scTriangulate can generate Leiden annotations itself. When the accession refers to a different study's artifact — syn26320732 is the benchmarking annotations set, whereas syn26320337 is the reproducibility folder root; pulling the wrong one will misalign annotation columns. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieves pre-computed clustering annotations, UMAP coordinates, and intermediate outputs deposited in the Synapse database (accessions syn26320732 and the syn26320337 reproducibility folder) so that scTriangulate integration benchmarks can be reproduced without re-running upstream clustering tools. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36016-y
skills.summary: Retrieves pre-computed clustering annotations, UMAP coordinates, and intermediate outputs deposited in the Synapse database (accessions syn26320732 and the syn26320337 reproducibility folder) so that scTriangulate integration benchmarks can be reproduced without re-running upstream clustering tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the target dataset is raw count matrix data available directly from GEO (e.g., GSE117825, GSM4949911) or the 10x Genomics website — download those from their native sources instead of Synapse. When the goal is fresh unsupervised clustering rather than reusing prior study annotations — no Synapse retrieval is needed; scTriangulate can generate Leiden annotations itself. When the accession refers to a different study's artifact — syn26320732 is the benchmarking annotations set, whereas syn26320337 is the reproducibility folder root; pulling the wrong one will misalign annotation columns.

skills.name: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-evaluation
skills.search_text: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-evaluation Use when a gold-standard synthetic single-cell dataset with known ground-truth trajectory topology (e.g. two bifurcations) and true pseudotime is available, and multiple trajectory-inference methods must be compared on branching detection and pseudotime ordering. skills.summary: Evaluate trajectory-inference methods (e.g. STREAM versus ten competitors such as Monocle2, TSCAN, DPT, PHATE) on a gold-standard synthetic dataset with known branching structure, scoring bifurcation detection and pseudotime accuracy with rank- and distance-based correlation metrics. This mirrors the STREAM paper's Rizvi et al. synthetic benchmark with two bifurcations and three simulated time points.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground truth (known bifurcations or true pseudotime) exists, so accuracy cannot be computed against reference topology — use real-data qualitative comparison instead Only one method is being run without any comparison baseline; the skill is defined by cross-method comparison against a benchmark The dataset topology is not tree-like (e.g. cyclic or disconnected graphs), which STREAM's authors flag as unsupported territory

skills.description: Use when you need reproducible paired trajectory-tree datasets with known topology to benchmark branched pseudotime alignment methods, or to stress-test alignment robustness against topological and clustering disruptions.
skills.name: synthetic-benchmark-pair-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-benchmark-pair-generation Use when you need reproducible paired trajectory-tree datasets with known topology to benchmark branched pseudotime alignment methods, or to stress-test alignment robustness against topological and clustering disruptions. The trajectories of interest are not tree-shaped (e.g., contain cycles or disconnected graphs) — CAPITAL can deal only with trajectory trees, not complex graphs. You need real biological datasets rather than simulator-derived pairs — use the packaged paul15, setty19, or velten19 datasets instead. You only need linear (unbranched) trajectory alignment — DTW-based methods on single lineages suffice and branching-aware tree alignment is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Generate synthetic scRNA-seq count datasets with dyngen on a binary-tree backbone (three branches) and filter to trajectory-tree pairs (four-leaf cluster-derived MSTs) for benchmarking CAPITAL's tree-alignment accuracy under controlled topological and clustering perturbations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-33681-3
skills.summary: Generate synthetic scRNA-seq count datasets with dyngen on a binary-tree backbone (three branches) and filter to trajectory-tree pairs (four-leaf cluster-derived MSTs) for benchmarking CAPITAL's tree-alignment accuracy under controlled topological and clustering perturbations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The trajectories of interest are not tree-shaped (e.g., contain cycles or disconnected graphs) — CAPITAL can deal only with trajectory trees, not complex graphs. You need real biological datasets rather than simulator-derived pairs — use the packaged paul15, setty19, or velten19 datasets instead. You only need linear (unbranched) trajectory alignment — DTW-based methods on single lineages suffice and branching-aware tree alignment is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you need a controlled single-cell count dataset with known data-generating expression rates and batch-confounded cell states to test whether a batch-correction or disentanglement method recovers the truth.
skills.name: synthetic-differentiation-trajectory-simulation
skills.search_text: synthetic-differentiation-trajectory-simulation Use when you need a controlled single-cell count dataset with known data-generating expression rates and batch-confounded cell states to test whether a batch-correction or disentanglement method recovers the truth. The goal is to evaluate batch correction on real, uncontrolled data — the simulation's ground-truth rates exist only for synthetic trajectories and cannot be verified against real atlases. Cell populations are not well-defined or cannot be split into control and batch-confounded groups, since the simulation's rationale requires a control group present in both treatment and control batches.
