skills.summary: Quantifies whether reads outside gene annotations (uTARs) carry cell-type-specific structure by computing silhouette coefficients of aTAR-, uTAR-, and gene-expression-based clustering on 2D UMAP coordinates and comparing them per sample, reproducing Fig. 2b of the TAR-scRNA-seq paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned Cell Ranger output — run the TAR-scRNA-seq Snakemake workflows (from_fastqs / from_cellranger) and groHMM TAR calling first to obtain TAR expression matrices You need genome-wide TAR discovery or uTAR homology annotation rather than a quantitative comparison of clustering quality across feature spaces You lack cell-type labels — silhouette coefficients require a predefined partition; without Seurat cluster labels this comparison cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when building a TAR annotation for scRNA-seq in the absence of a quality gene annotation and you must remove low-support groHMM-predicted regions by an alignment-derived read-count cutoff.
skills.name: tar-feature-threshold-filtering
skills.search_text: tar-feature-threshold-filtering Use when building a TAR annotation for scRNA-seq in the absence of a quality gene annotation and you must remove low-support groHMM-predicted regions by an alignment-derived read-count cutoff. A high-quality gene annotation already exists and standard gene-level quantification (e.g. cellranger count) is sufficient — this step is for annotation-independent TAR discovery The goal is per-cell expression quantification — this stage discards cell barcodes and individual cell information by design Input is already a filtered feature list or expression matrix rather than an alignment from which a read-depth threshold can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Filters annotation-free groHMM-predicted transcribed regions down to biologically supported TARs by applying a retention cutoff of n = 1/10,000,000 of uniquely mapped reads, then exports the retained features in refFlat format (tar_annotations.refflat) for downstream single-cell TAR expression analysis. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-22496-3
skills.summary: Filters annotation-free groHMM-predicted transcribed regions down to biologically supported TARs by applying a retention cutoff of n = 1/10,000,000 of uniquely mapped reads, then exports the retained features in refFlat format (tar_annotations.refflat) for downstream single-cell TAR expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A high-quality gene annotation already exists and standard gene-level quantification (e.g. cellranger count) is sufficient — this step is for annotation-independent TAR discovery The goal is per-cell expression quantification — this stage discards cell barcodes and individual cell information by design Input is already a filtered feature list or expression matrix rather than an alignment from which a read-depth threshold can be computed

skills.description: Use when you need to rank which cell type in an untreated diseased single-cell dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, especially when no paired treated data is available.
skills.name: target-perturbed-grn-analysis
skills.search_text: target-perturbed-grn-analysis Use when you need to rank which cell type in an untreated diseased single-cell dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, especially when no paired treated data is available. The drug has no known or confidently assigned target gene and the mechanism of action is unknown (unless using scRank's target-prioritization mode). You require paired disease-vs-treated data analysis (DEG or separability methods like Augur, beyondcell, scDEAL) rather than untreated-only inference. The question concerns multi-target drug perturbation with intricate target-to-target interactions — only preliminary results exist and tailored methods are not yet developed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq data using scRank's target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN), which models an inhibitor's drug perturbation as deletion of the target gene node and scores the resulting network distortion per cell type. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq data using scRank's target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN), which models an inhibitor's drug perturbation as deletion of the target gene node and scores the resulting network distortion per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug has no known or confidently assigned target gene and the mechanism of action is unknown (unless using scRank's target-prioritization mode). You require paired disease-vs-treated data analysis (DEG or separability methods like Augur, beyondcell, scDEAL) rather than untreated-only inference. The question concerns multi-target drug perturbation with intricate target-to-target interactions — only preliminary results exist and tailored methods are not yet developed.

skills.description: Use when you have untreated diseased single-cell expression data plus a known drug target gene (e.g. SLC6A4 for fluoxetine) and need to rank which cell cluster is most drug-responsive without paired treated samples.
skills.name: target-perturbed-network-in-silico-perturbation
skills.search_text: target-perturbed-network-in-silico-perturbation Use when you have untreated diseased single-cell expression data plus a known drug target gene (e.g. SLC6A4 for fluoxetine) and need to rank which cell cluster is most drug-responsive without paired treated samples. The drug acts on multiple targets with target-to-target interactions: multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank No prior knowledge of a drug target gene exists and the drug mechanism of action is unknown without candidate targets to prioritize The goal requires disease-treatment paired datasets analysis of differential expression rather than inference from untreated samples — scRank is designed specifically for untreated diseased single-cell data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq by modeling an in silico drug perturbation as deletion (inhibitor) or activation (agonist) of the drug-target gene node within a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN), implemented in the R package scRank. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101568
skills.summary: Rank drug-responsive cell types from untreated scRNA-seq by modeling an in silico drug perturbation as deletion (inhibitor) or activation (agonist) of the drug-target gene node within a target-perturbed gene regulatory network (tpGRN), implemented in the R package scRank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The drug acts on multiple targets with target-to-target interactions: multi-target perturbation requires specifically tailored methodologies not yet developed in scRank No prior knowledge of a drug target gene exists and the drug mechanism of action is unknown without candidate targets to prioritize The goal requires disease-treatment paired datasets analysis of differential expression rather than inference from untreated samples — scRank is designed specifically for untreated diseased single-cell data

skills.description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics for a complex trait plus eQTL summary statistics for many tissues, a reference LD matrix, and you need to identify which tissue's regulatory effects explain a disease locus.
skills.name: target-tissue-prioritization-for-disease-loci
skills.search_text: target-tissue-prioritization-for-disease-loci Use when you have GWAS summary statistics for a complex trait plus eQTL summary statistics for many tissues, a reference LD matrix, and you need to identify which tissue's regulatory effects explain a disease locus. Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants with no eQTL signal — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences (e.g., different ancestries), since CAFEH relies on a single shared LD matrix Datasets with missing effect-size entries, because CAFEH does not handle missing data and implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested studies http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Prioritize the causal target tissue(s) of GWAS disease loci by jointly fine-mapping and colocalizing the trait's summary statistics with eQTL summary statistics across many tissues (e.g., 49 GTEx studies) using CAFEH-S, which leverages allelic heterogeneity instead of single-signal pairwise colocalization. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.ajhg.2022.01.002
skills.summary: Prioritize the causal target tissue(s) of GWAS disease loci by jointly fine-mapping and colocalizing the trait's summary statistics with eQTL summary statistics across many tissues (e.g., 49 GTEx studies) using CAFEH-S, which leverages allelic heterogeneity instead of single-signal pairwise colocalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loci whose effects are mediated via coding variants with no eQTL signal — these cannot be explored with CAFEH Studies with large LD differences (e.g., different ancestries), since CAFEH relies on a single shared LD matrix Datasets with missing effect-size entries, because CAFEH does not handle missing data and implicitly assumes causal variants are present in all tested studies

skills.description: Use when mining high-order genetic interaction patterns (binary or additive encoded SNPs within mapped gene intervals) with a CMH test and you must avoid enumerating the full pattern space while controlling FWER.
skills.name: tarone-fwer-pruning-threshold-updating
skills.search_text: tarone-fwer-pruning-threshold-updating Use when mining high-order genetic interaction patterns (binary or additive encoded SNPs within mapped gene intervals) with a CMH test and you must avoid enumerating the full pattern space while controlling FWER. When the analysis conditions on a single marker interval rather than higher-order gene interaction patterns — FastCMH/SiNIMin address significant interval search and are the wrong tool for the HOGImine pattern poset. When no prior gene-interaction network or gene-to-SNP interval mapping exists and an unrestricted enumeration is required without Tarone pruning over a biologically constrained poset. When the phenotype is not binary/case-control and a CMH test conditioned on covariate classes is not applicable. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Applies Tarone's method inside HOGImine's breadth-first pattern enumeration: untestable patterns whose minimum achievable p-value cannot fall below the current Tarone threshold are pruned, and the threshold is updated incrementally as new testable patterns are discovered, so family-wise error rate is controlled at the target level. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad273
skills.summary: Applies Tarone's method inside HOGImine's breadth-first pattern enumeration: untestable patterns whose minimum achievable p-value cannot fall below the current Tarone threshold are pruned, and the threshold is updated incrementally as new testable patterns are discovered, so family-wise error rate is controlled at the target level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis conditions on a single marker interval rather than higher-order gene interaction patterns — FastCMH/SiNIMin address significant interval search and are the wrong tool for the HOGImine pattern poset. When no prior gene-interaction network or gene-to-SNP interval mapping exists and an unrestricted enumeration is required without Tarone pruning over a biologically constrained poset. When the phenotype is not binary/case-control and a CMH test conditioned on covariate classes is not applicable.

skills.description: Use when you have TCGA alteration data (CNV, mutations) for RBPs and need to quantify alteration burden (Zp) or test whether predicted circRNA regulators differ from non-regulators in alteration features.
skills.name: tcga-alteration-feature-interpretation
skills.search_text: tcga-alteration-feature-interpretation Use when you have TCGA alteration data (CNV, mutations) for RBPs and need to quantify alteration burden (Zp) or test whether predicted circRNA regulators differ from non-regulators in alteration features. Input is already a computed Zp / Z-score feature table — skip recomputation and go directly to the group comparison The tissue set is not from TCGA cancer batches (e.g., non-cancer or neurodegenerative cohorts) — the dichotomized-alteration Z-score is calibrated to TCGA's 19 batches of 12 cancer types and CRIT's generalization elsewhere is untested You need RBP-circRNA binding evidence rather than alteration burden — use the C value feature from RNAct/catRAPID instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Compute and statistically interpret the CRIT Zp feature — the Z-score of gene alteration proportion derived from dichotomized TCGA data (19 batches, 12 cancer types) — and use it to test whether circRNA-regulating RBPs harbor more alterations than other RBPs. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.omtn.2022.10.015
skills.summary: Compute and statistically interpret the CRIT Zp feature — the Z-score of gene alteration proportion derived from dichotomized TCGA data (19 batches, 12 cancer types) — and use it to test whether circRNA-regulating RBPs harbor more alterations than other RBPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a computed Zp / Z-score feature table — skip recomputation and go directly to the group comparison The tissue set is not from TCGA cancer batches (e.g., non-cancer or neurodegenerative cohorts) — the dichotomized-alteration Z-score is calibrated to TCGA's 19 batches of 12 cancer types and CRIT's generalization elsewhere is untested You need RBP-circRNA binding evidence rather than alteration burden — use the C value feature from RNAct/catRAPID instead

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq-derived outlier samples (e.g. SCISSOR shape changes) must be validated against an external TCGA mutation repository by matching TCGA barcodes to label aberrations as known vs novel.
skills.name: tcga-barcode-sample-matching
skills.search_text: tcga-barcode-sample-matching Use when RNA-seq-derived outlier samples (e.g. SCISSOR shape changes) must be validated against an external TCGA mutation repository by matching TCGA barcodes to label aberrations as known vs novel. Input is a raw MAF or variant list with no RNA-based outlier calls — there are no shape-change samples to cross-reference The RNA-seq cohort and the mutation repository are unmatched (no shared TCGA barcodes), so barcode matching cannot be performed The goal is de novo mutation calling from sequencing data rather than annotation of RNA-detected aberrations against existing calls http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Cross-references SCISSOR-detected RNA shape-change samples (GSC/LSC sample IDs) against publicly reported TCGA mutation calls (MAF) by TCGA barcode to classify each detected aberration as a known mutation or a previously unrecognized aberration, e.g. reproducing the 82%/18% TP53 split in TCGA HNSC. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Cross-references SCISSOR-detected RNA shape-change samples (GSC/LSC sample IDs) against publicly reported TCGA mutation calls (MAF) by TCGA barcode to classify each detected aberration as a known mutation or a previously unrecognized aberration, e.g. reproducing the 82%/18% TP53 split in TCGA HNSC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw MAF or variant list with no RNA-based outlier calls — there are no shape-change samples to cross-reference The RNA-seq cohort and the mutation repository are unmatched (no shared TCGA barcodes), so barcode matching cannot be performed The goal is de novo mutation calling from sequencing data rather than annotation of RNA-detected aberrations against existing calls

skills.description: Use when validating whether a gene signature discovered in single-cell/spatial data (e.g. the Cancer-Finder 10-gene ccRCC signature) has prognostic value in an independent bulk RNA-seq cohort with survival metadata.
skills.name: tcga-bulk-rnaseq-cohort-stratification
skills.search_text: tcga-bulk-rnaseq-cohort-stratification Use when validating whether a gene signature discovered in single-cell/spatial data (e.g. the Cancer-Finder 10-gene ccRCC signature) has prognostic value in an independent bulk RNA-seq cohort with survival metadata. Cohort is a hematologic tumor or the signature was derived from hematologic malignancy data, where the source method is explicitly not recommended Patients lack matched survival metadata, so no Kaplan-Meier/log-rank outcome analysis is possible The gene signature is not measurable in the bulk RNA-seq panel (signature genes absent from the expression matrix) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Stratifies a TCGA bulk RNA-seq patient cohort (e.g. 530 KIRC ccRCC samples with overall-survival metadata) into high- vs low-signature groups by median-splitting per-patient ssGSEA scores of a gene signature, then tests prognostic separation with a two-sided log-rank Kaplan-Meier analysis to validate the signature as a prognostic indicator. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-024-46413-6
skills.summary: Stratifies a TCGA bulk RNA-seq patient cohort (e.g. 530 KIRC ccRCC samples with overall-survival metadata) into high- vs low-signature groups by median-splitting per-patient ssGSEA scores of a gene signature, then tests prognostic separation with a two-sided log-rank Kaplan-Meier analysis to validate the signature as a prognostic indicator.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cohort is a hematologic tumor or the signature was derived from hematologic malignancy data, where the source method is explicitly not recommended Patients lack matched survival metadata, so no Kaplan-Meier/log-rank outcome analysis is possible The gene signature is not measurable in the bulk RNA-seq panel (signature genes absent from the expression matrix)

skills.description: Use when you have constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression networks (e.g. from TCGA tumor/normal RNA-seq) and need to verify they approximately satisfy a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis.
skills.name: tcga-cancer-network-evaluation
skills.search_text: tcga-cancer-network-evaluation Use when you have constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression networks (e.g. from TCGA tumor/normal RNA-seq) and need to verify they approximately satisfy a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis. The network was not built from expression data and a scale-free degree distribution is not an expected property (e.g. a fixed hub/gene-interaction network like the Gene_Net hub network). The analysis goal is driver-node identification rather than network topology validation — use WMDS.net controllability ranking instead once the scale-free check has passed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Assessment of differential co-expression networks built from TCGA cancer RNA-seq (BLCA, BRCA, COAD, HNSC, KICH, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUAD, LUSC, PRAD, STAD, THCA, UCEC) by fitting log2(degree frequency) vs log2(degree) with linear regression and checking the R-square against the scale-free topology criterion R2 > 0.80. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Assessment of differential co-expression networks built from TCGA cancer RNA-seq (BLCA, BRCA, COAD, HNSC, KICH, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUAD, LUSC, PRAD, STAD, THCA, UCEC) by fitting log2(degree frequency) vs log2(degree) with linear regression and checking the R-square against the scale-free topology criterion R2 > 0.80.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The network was not built from expression data and a scale-free degree distribution is not an expected property (e.g. a fixed hub/gene-interaction network like the Gene_Net hub network). The analysis goal is driver-node identification rather than network topology validation — use WMDS.net controllability ranking instead once the scale-free check has passed.

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample viral detection calls from RNA-seq (e.g., viRNAtrap contigs classified via blastn) and need to quantify detection accuracy against TCGA clinical viral-status annotations for the same samples.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-annotation-matching Use when you have per-sample viral detection calls from RNA-seq (e.g., viRNAtrap contigs classified via blastn) and need to quantify detection accuracy against TCGA clinical viral-status annotations for the same samples. The sample set has no corresponding TCGA clinical viral-status annotations to serve as ground truth, so no TPR can be computed The goal is discovery of novel or divergent viruses rather than benchmarking detection of known cancer-associated viruses (HR-ɑHPV, HBV, HCV) already annotated in TCGA Input reads are total raw RNA-seq reads rather than unmapped reads, since viRNAtrap expects reads pre-filtered against hg19 and phiX http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0781 Validates computational virus-detection calls from viRNAtrap by matching per-sample viral detections against TCGA clinical annotations of known cancer-associated viruses (HR-ɑHPV in CESC/HNSC, HBV/HCV in LIHC) and computing a true positive rate that must exceed 95%. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Validates computational virus-detection calls from viRNAtrap by matching per-sample viral detections against TCGA clinical annotations of known cancer-associated viruses (HR-ɑHPV in CESC/HNSC, HBV/HCV in LIHC) and computing a true positive rate that must exceed 95%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample set has no corresponding TCGA clinical viral-status annotations to serve as ground truth, so no TPR can be computed The goal is discovery of novel or divergent viruses rather than benchmarking detection of known cancer-associated viruses (HR-ɑHPV, HBV, HCV) already annotated in TCGA Input reads are total raw RNA-seq reads rather than unmapped reads, since viRNAtrap expects reads pre-filtered against hg19 and phiX

skills.description: Use when cluster assignments for TCGA pan-cancer samples must be joined to clinical survival metadata to determine which cancer-type subtypes show significantly distinct survival (e.g., at p<0.01 by log-rank).
skills.name: tcga-clinical-data-integration
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-data-integration Use when cluster assignments for TCGA pan-cancer samples must be joined to clinical survival metadata to determine which cancer-type subtypes show significantly distinct survival (e.g., at p<0.01 by log-rank). Input is raw transcriptome expression data with no clinical survival metadata available — clustering (e.g., RCC_clus) must precede survival comparison The goal is novel subtype discovery rather than clinical validation of existing cluster assignments; use RCC clustering (RCC_clus, clusterAttr) instead Cluster/clinical sample sizes fall below the minSample threshold for the cancer-type/cluster groups, making log-rank tests underpowered http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates TCGA pan-cancer clinical information (survival times, cancer-type attribute) with cluster assignment files to test whether clustering-derived subtypes have significantly distinct Kaplan-Meier survival profiles, as done in the RCC pan-cancer benchmark against tSNE+k-means, hclust, Chen et al., and Hoadley et al. baselines. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-67016-3
skills.summary: Integrates TCGA pan-cancer clinical information (survival times, cancer-type attribute) with cluster assignment files to test whether clustering-derived subtypes have significantly distinct Kaplan-Meier survival profiles, as done in the RCC pan-cancer benchmark against tSNE+k-means, hclust, Chen et al., and Hoadley et al. baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw transcriptome expression data with no clinical survival metadata available — clustering (e.g., RCC_clus) must precede survival comparison The goal is novel subtype discovery rather than clinical validation of existing cluster assignments; use RCC clustering (RCC_clus, clusterAttr) instead Cluster/clinical sample sizes fall below the minSample threshold for the cancer-type/cluster groups, making log-rank tests underpowered

skills.description: Use when a tumor subpopulation gene signature (e.g., top DEGs from a Scanpy cluster like Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be validated against TCGA patient survival data to assess prognostic significance.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-data-integration
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-data-integration Use when a tumor subpopulation gene signature (e.g., top DEGs from a Scanpy cluster like Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be validated against TCGA patient survival data to assess prognostic significance. The scRNA-seq cluster profiles align poorly with the available TCGA bulk data (e.g., limited or treated patient cohorts), as the paper reports no tumor cluster reached p < 0.05 in such a case The question is drug response prediction (IC50/AUC from GDSC or PRISM) rather than prognostic survival validation of a cluster signature Integrates TCGA bulk RNA expression profiles and matching clinical survival data with a cluster-derived gene signature from single-cell analysis to test whether the signature stratifies patients into high- and low-survival groups via Kaplan-Meier analysis and hazard ratio estimation. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.055
skills.summary: Integrates TCGA bulk RNA expression profiles and matching clinical survival data with a cluster-derived gene signature from single-cell analysis to test whether the signature stratifies patients into high- and low-survival groups via Kaplan-Meier analysis and hazard ratio estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The scRNA-seq cluster profiles align poorly with the available TCGA bulk data (e.g., limited or treated patient cohorts), as the paper reports no tumor cluster reached p < 0.05 in such a case The question is drug response prediction (IC50/AUC from GDSC or PRISM) rather than prognostic survival validation of a cluster signature

skills.description: Use when bulk tumor expression features (e.g., 64-dim Miscell latent features) must be paired with TCGA clinical outcomes (OS time/status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) to test prognostic associations.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-metadata-harmonization
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-metadata-harmonization Use when bulk tumor expression features (e.g., 64-dim Miscell latent features) must be paired with TCGA clinical outcomes (OS time/status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) to test prognostic associations. Working with single-cell data alone and no bulk tumor samples with TCGA survival endpoints are available Latent feature values have not yet been extracted from bulk expression with the Miscell encoder — harmonization must wait until features exist The clinical table lacks required survival covariates (OS time/status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) needed for the adjusted Cox model Join TCGA pan-cancer clinical survival metadata (overall survival time and status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) to Miscell latent feature values computed for tumor samples, keyed by TCGA sample barcode, enabling Kaplan-Meier and covariate-adjusted Cox survival analyses. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2021.103200
skills.summary: Join TCGA pan-cancer clinical survival metadata (overall survival time and status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) to Miscell latent feature values computed for tumor samples, keyed by TCGA sample barcode, enabling Kaplan-Meier and covariate-adjusted Cox survival analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Working with single-cell data alone and no bulk tumor samples with TCGA survival endpoints are available Latent feature values have not yet been extracted from bulk expression with the Miscell encoder — harmonization must wait until features exist The clinical table lacks required survival covariates (OS time/status, Age, Sex, TNM stage) needed for the adjusted Cox model

skills.description: Use when TCGA expression data must be joined with per-patient survival metadata to test gene-level prognostic association (hazard ratios) and compare Concordance statistics between candidate gene sets such as IC genes and DE genes.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-metadata-integration
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-metadata-integration Use when TCGA expression data must be joined with per-patient survival metadata to test gene-level prognostic association (hazard ratios) and compare Concordance statistics between candidate gene sets such as IC genes and DE genes. When the goal is differential expression itself rather than survival association — DE genes here are only the baseline input from DESeq2 (adjusted p-value < 0.05, |log2FC| > 2.0) When no per-patient survival metadata (vital status, days to death/follow-up) is available for the TCGA samples When analyzing cancer types other than KIRC, LIHC, and PRAD, for which no IC gene lists are provided in the repository http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates TCGA gene expression matrices with patient clinical metadata (vital status, days to death, days to follow-up) to test, via Cox proportional-hazards models, whether fused-network IC genes are more strongly prognostic than DESeq2-derived differentially expressed genes across KIRC, LIHC, and PRAD. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41540-021-00175-9
skills.summary: Integrates TCGA gene expression matrices with patient clinical metadata (vital status, days to death, days to follow-up) to test, via Cox proportional-hazards models, whether fused-network IC genes are more strongly prognostic than DESeq2-derived differentially expressed genes across KIRC, LIHC, and PRAD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is differential expression itself rather than survival association — DE genes here are only the baseline input from DESeq2 (adjusted p-value < 0.05, |log2FC| > 2.0) When no per-patient survival metadata (vital status, days to death/follow-up) is available for the TCGA samples When analyzing cancer types other than KIRC, LIHC, and PRAD, for which no IC gene lists are provided in the repository

skills.description: Use when TCGA RNA-seq expression (RSEM-normalized, log2(x+1)) plus clinical OS/DSS data are available and you need to test whether a gene-set expression signature stratifies patient survival.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-survival-analysis
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-survival-analysis Use when TCGA RNA-seq expression (RSEM-normalized, log2(x+1)) plus clinical OS/DSS data are available and you need to test whether a gene-set expression signature stratifies patient survival. Input is single-cell data without TCGA clinical survival annotations — PreCanCell cell classification, not survival testing, is the right skill The gene signature is defined per-patient rather than as a per-sample mean expression score, so a median split is not meaningful Only normal (non-tumor) samples are available, since KM/log-rank stratification requires tumor cohorts with OS/DSS follow-up http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Reproduces the TCGA pan-cancer survival analysis from PreCanCell: tumor samples are split at the median expression level of the 73 tumor marker genes (TMGs) into low- and high-expression classes, Kaplan-Meier curves for overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS) are fit, and separation is tested by log-rank. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.07.009
skills.summary: Reproduces the TCGA pan-cancer survival analysis from PreCanCell: tumor samples are split at the median expression level of the 73 tumor marker genes (TMGs) into low- and high-expression classes, Kaplan-Meier curves for overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS) are fit, and separation is tested by log-rank.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell data without TCGA clinical survival annotations — PreCanCell cell classification, not survival testing, is the right skill The gene signature is defined per-patient rather than as a per-sample mean expression score, so a median split is not meaningful Only normal (non-tumor) samples are available, since KM/log-rank stratification requires tumor cohorts with OS/DSS follow-up

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample binary exposure labels (e.g., viral/HERV contig presence) for TCGA tumor samples and clinical overall survival data, and need to test whether the marker is associated with survival in specific cancer cohorts.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-survival-data-analysis
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-survival-data-analysis Use when you have per-sample binary exposure labels (e.g., viral/HERV contig presence) for TCGA tumor samples and clinical overall survival data, and need to test whether the marker is associated with survival in specific cancer cohorts. Exposure labels are continuous rather than a per-sample binary presence/absence call — dichotomization into HERV-positive/negative groups is the assumed design The analysis goal is de novo viral detection or contig assembly from RNAseq reads (that is viRNAtrap's role, upstream of this skill) Cancer types outside the cohorts with adequate survival follow-up, or clinical endpoints other than overall survival, without re-validating the survival model assumptions http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Associates per-sample molecular markers (here, HERV-K/HERV-H contig presence from viRNAtrap) with TCGA overall survival by dichotomizing patients into marker-positive and marker-negative groups, fitting Kaplan-Meier estimators, and testing differences with log-rank tests, plus hypergeometric enrichment of marker-positive samples among somatically mutated driver genes. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-36336-z
skills.summary: Associates per-sample molecular markers (here, HERV-K/HERV-H contig presence from viRNAtrap) with TCGA overall survival by dichotomizing patients into marker-positive and marker-negative groups, fitting Kaplan-Meier estimators, and testing differences with log-rank tests, plus hypergeometric enrichment of marker-positive samples among somatically mutated driver genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Exposure labels are continuous rather than a per-sample binary presence/absence call — dichotomization into HERV-positive/negative groups is the assumed design The analysis goal is de novo viral detection or contig assembly from RNAseq reads (that is viRNAtrap's role, upstream of this skill) Cancer types outside the cohorts with adequate survival follow-up, or clinical endpoints other than overall survival, without re-validating the survival model assumptions

Input is already a processed feature table with no per-sample clinical survival time/status to merge The hypothesis concerns differential expression rather than clinical association of gene-set scores (use ARMT's differential analysis module instead) Data are not TCGA and lack the sample-ID format ARMT uses to join clinical and expression data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 Merges TCGA clinical data (survival time/status) with GSVA scores, TPM expression and mutation profiles on common samples using ARMT's built-in TCGA clinical datasets, enabling downstream survival and Cox regression analysis of gene-set scores. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Merges TCGA clinical data (survival time/status) with GSVA scores, TPM expression and mutation profiles on common samples using ARMT's built-in TCGA clinical datasets, enabling downstream survival and Cox regression analysis of gene-set scores.

skills.description: Use when screening a cohort of base-level RNA-seq pileup data (e.g., TCGA BAM files) for samples with aberrant transcript shapes — splicing changes, intron retention, deletions — in a specific gene.
skills.name: tcga-cohort-shape-change-screening
skills.search_text: tcga-cohort-shape-change-screening Use when screening a cohort of base-level RNA-seq pileup data (e.g., TCGA BAM files) for samples with aberrant transcript shapes — splicing changes, intron retention, deletions — in a specific gene. The cohort contains many non-expressed samples for the target gene — SCISSOR's per-gene 'not expressed' filter excluded 5802 genes (~28%) from downstream analysis Cohort is very small — empirically ~30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully The question requires junction-spanning or transcript-model-based isoform quantification rather than unbiased base-level coverage shape analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Two-step SCISSOR screening of base-level RNA-seq coverage across a tumor cohort (e.g., 522 TCGA HNSC) to detect global and local shape changes in a target gene, at a significance cutoff of 1e-04. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-20593-3
skills.summary: Two-step SCISSOR screening of base-level RNA-seq coverage across a tumor cohort (e.g., 522 TCGA HNSC) to detect global and local shape changes in a target gene, at a significance cutoff of 1e-04.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort contains many non-expressed samples for the target gene — SCISSOR's per-gene 'not expressed' filter excluded 5802 genes (~28%) from downstream analysis Cohort is very small — empirically ~30 samples is the smallest cohort considered successfully The question requires junction-spanning or transcript-model-based isoform quantification rather than unbiased base-level coverage shape analysis

skills.description: Use when comparing cancer driver gene prediction tools on TCGA RNA-seq datasets against curated benchmark gene lists (CGC/COSMIC, NCG, PMH) using precision-recall F_beta scoring.
skills.name: tcga-dataset-performance-evaluation

Input is a single gene list without a curated benchmark (CGC/NCG/PMH) to score against — no TP/FP/FN can be defined. The aim is discovery of driver nodes rather than head-to-head benchmarking of prediction tools (use the WMDS.net network control workflow instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Evaluate driver gene prediction tools (e.g. WMDS.net, WMDS.netP and 11 comparison tools) across 14 TCGA cancer datasets by computing precision, recall and the F_beta measure (beta^2=0.2) against the CGC, NCG and PMH benchmark gene lists, then rank tools per benchmark. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Evaluate driver gene prediction tools (e.g. WMDS.net, WMDS.netP and 11 comparison tools) across 14 TCGA cancer datasets by computing precision, recall and the F_beta measure (beta^2=0.2) against the CGC, NCG and PMH benchmark gene lists, then rank tools per benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single gene list without a curated benchmark (CGC/NCG/PMH) to score against — no TP/FP/FN can be defined. The aim is discovery of driver nodes rather than head-to-head benchmarking of prediction tools (use the WMDS.net network control workflow instead).

skills.description: Use when classifying TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq samples with PAM50 and you must quantify how the reference subset (its size, ER+/ER− balance, or medoid recomputation) changes subtype-call concordance with published labels.
skills.name: tcga-expression-classification
skills.search_text: tcga-expression-classification Use when classifying TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq samples with PAM50 and you must quantify how the reference subset (its size, ER+/ER− balance, or medoid recomputation) changes subtype-call concordance with published labels. The goal is single-sample classification with no cohort available to build a reference — use the article's single-sample alternatives (AIMS, mLR) instead You only need one classification run and are not varying or diagnosing reference-subset composition The input is microarray data with no log2-transformation/calibration strategy specified — AWCA-based PAM50 was validated on Affymetrix log2-transformed data (e.g. GSE4922), not raw RNA-seq-style inputs http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Sensitivity analysis of PAM50 subtype calling on TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq: rebuild nearest-centroid references from ER+/ER−-controlled sample subsets and measure concordance against published TCGA PAM50 labels. Grounds the finding that reference-cohort composition (e.g. 262-sample 50/50 ER+/ER− subsets) is a dominant driver of classification reproducibility. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-020-70832-2
skills.summary: Sensitivity analysis of PAM50 subtype calling on TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq: rebuild nearest-centroid references from ER+/ER−-controlled sample subsets and measure concordance against published TCGA PAM50 labels. Grounds the finding that reference-cohort composition (e.g. 262-sample 50/50 ER+/ER− subsets) is a dominant driver of classification reproducibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is single-sample classification with no cohort available to build a reference — use the article's single-sample alternatives (AIMS, mLR) instead You only need one classification run and are not varying or diagnosing reference-subset composition The input is microarray data with no log2-transformation/calibration strategy specified — AWCA-based PAM50 was validated on Affymetrix log2-transformed data (e.g. GSE4922), not raw RNA-seq-style inputs

skills.description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., TCGA LUAD/LUSC from GDC) must be prepared as DCNet input: rows as human gene symbols, columns as samples, log2(x+1) transformed, with zero-expression and marker-gene filters applied.
skills.name: tcga-gene-expression-preprocessing
skills.search_text: tcga-gene-expression-preprocessing Use when a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., TCGA LUAD/LUSC from GDC) must be prepared as DCNet input: rows as human gene symbols, columns as samples, log2(x+1) transformed, with zero-expression and marker-gene filters applied. Input is already a cell-type abundance/feature table — deconvolution preprocessing is for raw bulk expression matrices Single-cell RNA-seq data that does not require bulk deconvolution input formatting or the paper's TCGA-oriented gene filters Analyses where retaining genes with zero expression in many samples is required (e.g., splice or mutation-focused studies), since the 1/3-zero filter removes them http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Preprocesses TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices for DCNet cell-landscape deconvolution: orienting the matrix as rows of human gene symbols and columns of samples, applying the log2(x+1) transformation, and filtering genes and CellMarker-derived marker genes so only detectable, informative features feed the neural network. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Preprocesses TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices for DCNet cell-landscape deconvolution: orienting the matrix as rows of human gene symbols and columns of samples, applying the log2(x+1) transformation, and filtering genes and CellMarker-derived marker genes so only detectable, informative features feed the neural network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-type abundance/feature table — deconvolution preprocessing is for raw bulk expression matrices Single-cell RNA-seq data that does not require bulk deconvolution input formatting or the paper's TCGA-oriented gene filters Analyses where retaining genes with zero expression in many samples is required (e.g., splice or mutation-focused studies), since the 1/3-zero filter removes them

skills.description: Use when training or evaluating miRSCAPE on bulk TCGA/GTex paired miRNA-mRNA matrices and you need pooled multi-cancer or tumor-vs-normal cross-validation accuracy comparisons.
skills.name: tcga-gtex-cohort-harmonization
skills.search_text: tcga-gtex-cohort-harmonization Use when training or evaluating miRSCAPE on bulk TCGA/GTex paired miRNA-mRNA matrices and you need pooled multi-cancer or tumor-vs-normal cross-validation accuracy comparisons. The input is already a single-cell/scRNA-seq dataset — use the modifySeuratObject (Seurat) preparation path instead, and note a pre-trained model may need retraining due to dropout. Only one tissue or a small cohort is available — tissue-specific models lose ~0.2 accuracy relative to the pooled 8,089-sample TCGA model, so pooling is the point of this skill. The application sample's tissue context does not match the training cohort — accuracy is expected to drop (see Figure S9), so retrain on a matching cohort. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Harmonizes and pools paired bulk miRNA–mRNA cohorts from TCGA (~5,000 tumor samples) and GTEx (~4,500 normal samples) so that miRSCAPE's XGBoost model can be trained and cross-validated on large multi-tissue cohorts, quantifying how tissue heterogeneity affects prediction accuracy. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.104962
skills.summary: Harmonizes and pools paired bulk miRNA–mRNA cohorts from TCGA (~5,000 tumor samples) and GTEx (~4,500 normal samples) so that miRSCAPE's XGBoost model can be trained and cross-validated on large multi-tissue cohorts, quantifying how tissue heterogeneity affects prediction accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a single-cell/scRNA-seq dataset — use the modifySeuratObject (Seurat) preparation path instead, and note a pre-trained model may need retraining due to dropout. Only one tissue or a small cohort is available — tissue-specific models lose ~0.2 accuracy relative to the pooled 8,089-sample TCGA model, so pooling is the point of this skill. The application sample's tissue context does not match the training cohort — accuracy is expected to drop (see Figure S9), so retrain on a matching cohort.

skills.description: Use when a TCGA-LUAD SNV dataset in MAF format must be obtained and staged so ARMT can merge mutation profiles with clinical, TPM and GSVA score data by common samples before differential mutation testing.
skills.name: tcga-luad-mutation-data-acquisition
skills.search_text: tcga-luad-mutation-data-acquisition Use when a TCGA-LUAD SNV dataset in MAF format must be obtained and staged so ARMT can merge mutation profiles with clinical, TPM and GSVA score data by common samples before differential mutation testing. Mutation data are not in a standard .maf format (ARMT requires the TCGA-style mutation annotation format) or come from a non-TCGA cohort without mappable sample IDs for integration The goal is differential expression or GSVA-score analysis of RNA-seq counts rather than SNV mutation significance testing (use ARMT's differential expression or GSVA differential modules instead) Sample-level integration is impossible because clinical, GSVA and mutation data do not share common sample identifiers Acquires the TCGA lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) mutation data in standard MAF format and stages it for integration with clinical, TPM and GSVA-score data inside ARMT, so that downstream differential mutation analysis (e.g. hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low) can be run with maftools-backed plotting. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.009
skills.summary: Acquires the TCGA lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) mutation data in standard MAF format and stages it for integration with clinical, TPM and GSVA-score data inside ARMT, so that downstream differential mutation analysis (e.g. hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low) can be run with maftools-backed plotting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Mutation data are not in a standard .maf format (ARMT requires the TCGA-style mutation annotation format) or come from a non-TCGA cohort without mappable sample IDs for integration The goal is differential expression or GSVA-score analysis of RNA-seq counts rather than SNV mutation significance testing (use ARMT's differential expression or GSVA differential modules instead) Sample-level integration is impossible because clinical, GSVA and mutation data do not share common sample identifiers

skills.description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples from two cancer subtypes (e.g., TCGA LUAD vs LUSC) have DCNet-inferred cell abundance matrices and the goal is to identify cell types significantly enriched or depleted between subtypes.

skills.search_text: tcga-lung-cancer-subtype-comparison Use when bulk RNA-seq samples from two cancer subtypes (e.g., TCGA LUAD vs LUSC) have DCNet-inferred cell abundance matrices and the goal is to identify cell types significantly enriched or depleted between subtypes. Samples lack subtype labels or span more than two groups — the workflow is a two-group (LUAD vs LUSC) contrast with directional fold changes, not a multi-class or unsupervised clustering analysis Abundances come from a different deconvolution method (CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) with a non-overlapping cell-type panel — cell-type names and fold-change interpretation would not match the DCNet 434-cell landscape The goal is per-gene differential expression rather than deconvolved cell-type abundance differences http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Differentially abundant cell-type analysis between TCGA lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) using DCNet-inferred cell landscapes, testing per-cell-type abundance differences with fold change and multiple-testing correction. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2022.2043662
skills.summary: Differentially abundant cell-type analysis between TCGA lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) using DCNet-inferred cell landscapes, testing per-cell-type abundance differences with fold change and multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples lack subtype labels or span more than two groups — the workflow is a two-group (LUAD vs LUSC) contrast with directional fold changes, not a multi-class or unsupervised clustering analysis Abundances come from a different deconvolution method (CIBERSORTx, EPIC, MCP-counter, quanTIseq, TIMER, xCell) with a non-overlapping cell-type panel — cell-type names and fold-change interpretation would not match the DCNet 434-cell landscape The goal is per-gene differential expression rather than deconvolved cell-type abundance differences

skills.description: Use when building an IMGP-based prognostic model from bulk TCGA melanoma (SKCM06) expression and survival data, and you want to test whether filtering candidate gene pairs by cell-cell interaction enrichment improves LASSO Cox feature selection.
skills.name: tcga-melanoma-cohort-prognostic-modeling
skills.search_text: tcga-melanoma-cohort-prognostic-modeling Use when building an IMGP-based prognostic model from bulk TCGA melanoma (SKCM06) expression and survival data, and you want to test whether filtering candidate gene pairs by cell-cell interaction enrichment improves LASSO Cox feature selection. The cohort is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to effectively identify prognostic gene pairs. The outcome of interest is therapy response rather than prognosis — the Response Module (TimiGP-Response) is the appropriate module. The input is already a deconvolved cell-type abundance table or single-cell data rather than bulk transcriptomic profiles with cell-type marker pairs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Builds an IMGP-based prognostic model on the TCGA SKCM06 metastatic melanoma cohort and demonstrates that LASSO Cox feature selection is more likely to retain immune marker gene pairs (IMGPs) derived from TimiGP-enriched cell-cell interactions (76% of 544 candidates) than pairs chosen solely for univariate prognostic significance. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101121
skills.summary: Builds an IMGP-based prognostic model on the TCGA SKCM06 metastatic melanoma cohort and demonstrates that LASSO Cox feature selection is more likely to retain immune marker gene pairs (IMGPs) derived from TimiGP-enriched cell-cell interactions (76% of 544 candidates) than pairs chosen solely for univariate prognostic significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cohort is small or lacks matched survival information — TimiGP requires a large gene expression dataset with matched survival information to effectively identify prognostic gene pairs. The outcome of interest is therapy response rather than prognosis — the Response Module (TimiGP-Response) is the appropriate module. The input is already a deconvolved cell-type abundance table or single-cell data rather than bulk transcriptomic profiles with cell-type marker pairs.

skills.summary: Preprocessing of TCGA mRNA expression data using Z-score thresholds to flag abnormal expression entries and retain informative genes for downstream penalized regression, as implemented in the HDMAC workflow.

skills.description: Use when you have tissue-matched TCGA expression, MAF mutation calls, and GISTIC copy-number calls and need to test whether driver alterations (e.g. EGFR amplification, BRAF/TP53/VHL mutations) activate their corresponding signaling pathways.
skills.name: tcga-multi-omics-data-integration
skills.search_text: tcga-multi-omics-data-integration Use when you have tissue-matched TCGA expression, MAF mutation calls, and GISTIC copy-number calls and need to test whether driver alterations (e.g. EGFR amplification, BRAF/TP53/VHL mutations) activate their corresponding signaling pathways. When the question requires phosphoprotein-level pathway activity rather than expression-inferred footprints, since PROGENy does not account for post-translational modifications directly When studying context-specific or tissue-specific pathway activation where tissue-derived signatures may better reflect activation than the consensus PROGENy signatures When the input is a single small sample set without driver alteration status — comparing against perturbation experiments or tissue-matched normals was required for some competing methods (SPIA, Pathifier), and pathway score interpretation needs sufficient sample size http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates TCGA multi-omics data (RNA-seq expression, MAF somatic mutation calls, GISTIC copy-number values) by computing PROGENy pathway activity scores per sample and testing their association with driver alterations within each tumor type, demonstrating that expression-inferred signaling footprints recover functional effects of known driver mutations. transcriptomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-017-02391-6
skills.summary: Integrates TCGA multi-omics data (RNA-seq expression, MAF somatic mutation calls, GISTIC copy-number values) by computing PROGENy pathway activity scores per sample and testing their association with driver alterations within each tumor type, demonstrating that expression-inferred signaling footprints recover functional effects of known driver mutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question requires phosphoprotein-level pathway activity rather than expression-inferred footprints, since PROGENy does not account for post-translational modifications directly When studying context-specific or tissue-specific pathway activation where tissue-derived signatures may better reflect activation than the consensus PROGENy signatures When the input is a single small sample set without driver alteration status — comparing against perturbation experiments or tissue-matched normals was required for some competing methods (SPIA, Pathifier), and pathway score interpretation needs sufficient sample size

skills.search_text: tcga-pancancer-association-testing Use when testing whether tGPT-derived attention-head features from bulk tumor transcriptomes are associated with genomic alteration events, prognosis, or survival outcomes in a pan-cancer cohort. Task is single-cell clustering or cell-lineage inference from scRNA-seq — use tGPT's embedding + Leiden/UMAP workflow instead of attention-head association testing Input is already a feature/embedding table — attention-head distributions must be re-recorded from the model, which requires ranked gene-symbol lines as input No clinical or molecular event annotations (TP53, HRD, genome doubling, TMB, survival) are available — the association regression cannot be run http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce tGPT attention-head association analyses on TCGA bulk tumor transcriptomes: compute per-head attention entropy/importance features and test them against molecular alteration events (TMB, TP53 mutation, HRD, genome doubling) and overall survival across 33 cancer types. transcriptomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2023.106536
skills.summary: Reproduce tGPT attention-head association analyses on TCGA bulk tumor transcriptomes: compute per-head attention entropy/importance features and test them against molecular alteration events (TMB, TP53 mutation, HRD, genome doubling) and overall survival across 33 cancer types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Task is single-cell clustering or cell-lineage inference from scRNA-seq — use tGPT's embedding + Leiden/UMAP workflow instead of attention-head association testing Input is already a feature/embedding table — attention-head distributions must be re-recorded from the model, which requires ranked gene-symbol lines as input No clinical or molecular event annotations (TP53, HRD, genome doubling, TMB, survival) are available — the association regression cannot be run

skills.description: Use when you have FPKM-normalized TCGA tumor and normal expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample ids) plus the DawnRank-derived Gene_Net reference network, and need significant condition-specific co-expression edges.
skills.name: tcga-rna-seq-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: tcga-rna-seq-matrix-processing Use when you have FPKM-normalized TCGA tumor and normal expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample ids) plus the DawnRank-derived Gene_Net reference network, and need significant condition-specific co-expression edges. The cancer type has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ statistic is no longer a good approximation of the standard normal, so P-values are unreliable Input is a single condition (only one expression matrix) — the ΔZ test fundamentally requires two physiological states with separate correlation estimates Gene pairs not connected in the Gene_Net reference network — correlations are computed only for pairs connected in the reference network, so testing arbitrary pairs is out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Builds a differential co-expression network from two TCGA RNA-seq conditions by Fisher Z-transforming Pearson correlations on the Gene_Net edge set and applying a ΔZ two-sample test. Produces significant differential edges (gene_i, gene_j, ΔZ, P-value) that feed WMDS.net's node-controllability model. transcriptomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad071
skills.summary: Builds a differential co-expression network from two TCGA RNA-seq conditions by Fisher Z-transforming Pearson correlations on the Gene_Net edge set and applying a ΔZ two-sample test. Produces significant differential edges (gene_i, gene_j, ΔZ, P-value) that feed WMDS.net's node-controllability model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cancer type has fewer than 15 normal samples — the ΔZ statistic is no longer a good approximation of the standard normal, so P-values are unreliable Input is a single condition (only one expression matrix) — the ΔZ test fundamentally requires two physiological states with separate correlation estimates Gene pairs not connected in the Gene_Net reference network — correlations are computed only for pairs connected in the reference network, so testing arbitrary pairs is out of scope

skills.search_text: tcr-clonotype-assignment-per-mouse Use when paired single-cell transcriptome plus full-length TCR sequencing of CD8 TILs (e.g. >3500 cells from seven tumor-bearing mice, GSE116390) must be grouped into clonotypes per mouse before comparing clonal overlap across transcriptomic states. Input is droplet-based (10X 5'/3') data without full-length TCR genes — TraCeR requires full-length TCR sequences and the study's clonotype reconstruction was done on plate-based smart-seq2 data Cells come from a pooled experiment without per-mouse/sample identity — clonotypes must be grouped separately for each mouse, so this skill cannot be applied Goal is bulk TCR repertoire analysis rather than linking single-cell transcriptomic states to clonotypes http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Assigns single CD8 TILs to TCR clonotypes by reconstructing paired full-length TCR alpha/beta sequences from single-cell RNA-seq with TraCeR, grouping cells sharing identical receptor sequences separately within each mouse, and pairing the resulting clonotype labels with transcriptomic states (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naive) predicted by TILPRED to quantify clonal relatedness (Morisita-Horn) between CD8 TIL states. transcriptomics/v2 10.1080/2162402x.2020.1737369
skills.summary: Assigns single CD8 TILs to TCR clonotypes by reconstructing paired full-length TCR alpha/beta sequences from single-cell RNA-seq with TraCeR, grouping cells sharing identical receptor sequences separately within each mouse, and pairing the resulting clonotype labels with transcriptomic states (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naive) predicted by TILPRED to quantify clonal relatedness (Morisita-Horn) between CD8 TIL states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is droplet-based (10X 5'/3') data without full-length TCR genes — TraCeR requires full-length TCR sequences and the study's clonotype reconstruction was done on plate-based smart-seq2 data Cells come from a pooled experiment without per-mouse/sample identity — clonotypes must be grouped separately for each mouse, so this skill cannot be applied Goal is bulk TCR repertoire analysis rather than linking single-cell transcriptomic states to clonotypes
